ramacharitamanas::3713.verse_hindi: एक (अविद्या) दुष्ट (दोषयुक्त) है और अत्यंत दुःखरूप है, जिसके वश होकर जीव संसार रूपी कुएँ में पड़ा हुआ है और एक (विद्या) जिसके वश में गुण है और जो जगत् की रचना करती है, वह प्रभु से ही प्रेरित होती है, उसके अपना बल कुछ भी नही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3713.english_translation: One is wicked and full of suffering; under its grip, the living being falls into the pit of worldly existence. The other, ruled by virtue, creates the world, yet it acts only when moved by the supreme being and has no power of its own.
ramacharitamanas::3713.translation_literal: एक (one) / दुष्ट (wicked) / अतिसय (extremely) / दुखरूपा (of the form of suffering) / जा (whose) / बस (control) / जीव (living being) / परा (fallen) / भवकूपा (into the pit of worldly existence) / एक (one) / रचइ (creates) / जग (the world) / गुन (virtue) / बस (under control) / जाकें (of whom) / प्रभु (the supreme being) / प्रेरित (moved) / नहिं (not) / निज (own) / बल (power) / ताकें (of that one)
ramacharitamanas::3713.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3713.essence: One force enslaves; the other works only when the supreme reality moves it.
ramacharitamanas::3713.simple_meaning: Two powers are being described: one traps the living being in suffering, while the other is constructive but has no independent power and works only by the supreme being's prompting.
ramacharitamanas::3713.simple_insight: You start seeing that not every force in life is truly self-directed — some things only seem powerful until you look closer.
ramacharitamanas::3713.detailed_meaning: Ram is teaching Lakshman how to see the world clearly. After naming ignorance and knowledge, he explains that one power traps beings in suffering, while the other builds the world but still depends on the supreme reality. The lesson is about seeing what truly has agency.
ramacharitamanas::3713.modern_relevance: You watch a habit take over your day, then call it "just how I am." This verse cuts through that excuse: some forces enslave, and even the constructive ones are not ultimate.
ramacharitamanas::3713.insight: It shifts you from treating appearances as autonomous to tracing every power back to its source.

ramacharitamanas::3714.verse_sanskrit: ग्यान मान जहँ एकउ नाहीं। देख ब्रह्म समान सब माहीं॥ कहिअ तात सो परम बिरागी। तृन सम सिद्धि तीनि गुन त्यागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3714.verse_hindi: ज्ञान वह है, जहाँ (जिसमें) मान आदि एक भी (दोष) नहीं है और जो सबसे समान रूप से ब्रह्म को देखता है। हे तात! उसी को परम वैराग्यवान् कहना चाहिए, जो सारी सिद्धियों को और तीनों गुणों को तिनके के समान त्याग चुका हो ॥ (जिसमें मान, दम्भ, हिंसा, क्षमाराहित्य, टेढ़ापन, आचार्य सेवा का अभाव, अपवित्रता, अस्थिरता, मन का निगृहीत न होना, इंद्रियों के विषय में आसक्ति, अहंकार, जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-व्याधिमय जगत् में सुख-बुद्धि, स्त्री-पुत्र-घर आदि में आसक्ति तथा ममता, इष्ट और अनिष्ट की प्राप्ति में हर्ष-शोक, भक्ति का अभाव, एकान्त में मन न लगना, विषयी मनुष्यों के संग में प्रेम- ये अठारह न हों और नित्य अध्यात्म (आत्मा) में स्थिति तथा तत्त्व ज्ञान के अर्थ (तत्त्वज्ञान के द्वारा जानने योग्य) परमात्मा का नित्य दर्शन हो, वही ज्ञान कहलाता है। देखिए गीता अध्याय 13/ 7 से 11)
ramacharitamanas::3714.english_translation: Knowledge is where not even a trace of pride remains, and where you see the supreme reality equally in all. O dear one, call that person truly detached who has cast aside all powers and the three qualities like straw.
ramacharitamanas::3714.translation_literal: ग्यान (knowledge) / मान (pride) / जहँ (where) / एकउ (even one) / नाहीं (not) / देख (see) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / समान (equally) / सब (all) / माहीं (in)॥ / कहिअ (call) / तात (dear one) / सो (that) / परम (supreme) / बिरागी (detached one) / तृन सम (like straw) / सिद्धि (powers) / तीनि गुन (three qualities) / त्यागी (having abandoned)
ramacharitamanas::3714.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3714.essence: Real knowledge ends pride and makes every being look equal.
ramacharitamanas::3714.simple_meaning: Real knowledge removes pride and lets you see the same divine reality in everyone. Real detachment means not clinging to powers, achievements, or the three qualities of nature.
ramacharitamanas::3714.simple_insight: You feel lighter when superiority drops away and everything stops looking separate.
ramacharitamanas::3714.detailed_meaning: In the forest teaching, the speaker continues defining clear seeing. After explaining illusion and confusion, the verse turns to the mark of real knowledge: no pride, equal vision, and freedom from clinging to powers or the three qualities. It is a test for true detachment.
ramacharitamanas::3714.modern_relevance: You meet someone who outranks you, and the old urge to compare flares up. This verse asks whether you can still see the same worth in both of you without needing to win the room.
ramacharitamanas::3714.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to equal vision, and from spiritual achievement to non-clinging.

ramacharitamanas::3715.verse_sanskrit: माया ईस न आपु कहुँ जान कहिअ सो जीव। बंध मोच्छ प्रद सर्बपर माया प्रेरक सीव ॥
ramacharitamanas::3715.verse_hindi: जो माया को, ईश्वर को और अपने स्वरूप को नहीं जानता, उसे जीव कहना चाहिए। जो (कर्मानुसार) बंधन और मोक्ष देने वाला, सबसे परे और माया का प्रेरक है, वह ईश्वर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3715.english_translation: One who does not know maya, the divine ruler, or the true self is called a living being. The one beyond all, who gives bondage and freedom and moves maya, is Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::3715.translation_literal: माया (illusion/veil of appearance) / ईस (the divine ruler) / न (not) / आपु (the true self) / कहुँ (to) / जान (know) / कहिअ (is called) / सो (that) / जीव (living being) / बंध (bondage) / मोच्छ (freedom) / प्रद (giver) / सर्बपर (beyond all) / माया (the veil of appearance) / प्रेरक (mover) / सीव (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::3715.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3715.essence: Freedom begins when you see beyond maya and know the true self.
ramacharitamanas::3715.simple_meaning: A person is trapped when they do not understand illusion, the divine ruler, or their own true nature. Real freedom comes from seeing what is beyond all change.
ramacharitamanas::3715.simple_insight: Confusion is not just ignorance of the world; it is forgetting who you are and what truly governs life.
ramacharitamanas::3715.detailed_meaning: In the forest teaching between the sages, Tulsidas sharpens the line between confusion and freedom. He says the one who cannot recognize maya, the divine ruler, or the true self remains bound, while the one beyond maya is the source of both bondage and release.
ramacharitamanas::3715.modern_relevance: You keep reacting to a message thread, a headline, and a private fear, all while forgetting the deeper question: who is actually seeing this? The verse pulls you back to first principles.
ramacharitamanas::3715.insight: It shifts attention from surface events to the awareness that interprets them.

ramacharitamanas::3716.verse_sanskrit: धर्म तें बिरति जोग तें ग्याना। ग्यान मोच्छप्रद बेद बखाना॥ जातें बेगि द्रवउँ मैं भाई। सो मम भगति भगत सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3716.verse_hindi: धर्म (के आचरण) से वैराग्य और योग से ज्ञान होता है तथा ज्ञान मोक्ष का देने वाला है- ऐसा वेदों ने वर्णन किया है। और हे भाई! जिससे मैं शीघ्र ही प्रसन्न होता हूँ, वह मेरी भक्ति है जो भक्तों को सुख देने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3716.english_translation: Renunciation comes from duty, and knowledge comes from yoga; the Vedas say knowledge gives freedom. And, brother, what makes me quickly pleased is my devotion, which gives joy to devotees.
ramacharitamanas::3716.translation_literal: धर्म (duty/right conduct) / तें (from) / बिरति (renunciation) / जोग (yoga) / तें (from) / ग्याना (knowledge) / ग्यान (knowledge) / मोच्छप्रद (freedom-giving) / बेद (the Vedas) / बखाना (describe) ॥ / जातें (by which) / बेगि (quickly) / द्रवउँ (I am pleased/moved) / मैं (I) / भाई (brother) / सो (that) / मम (my) / भगति (devotion) / भगत (devotees) / सुखदाई (joy-giving) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3716.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3716.essence: Devotion reaches Ram faster than any ladder of practice.
ramacharitamanas::3716.simple_meaning: Right conduct can lead to detachment, yoga can lead to knowledge, and knowledge can lead to freedom. But Ram says devotion is what delights him fastest and brings joy to devotees.
ramacharitamanas::3716.simple_insight: You do not have to become impressive to be close to Ram; sincere devotion is enough.
ramacharitamanas::3716.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the teaching turns from theory to heart. After explaining the ladder from duty to renunciation to knowledge, the speaker reveals a higher secret: Ram is won most quickly not by technique, but by loving devotion that comforts the devotee.
ramacharitamanas::3716.modern_relevance: You can spend months perfecting your practice, your routine, your arguments, your self-image — and still feel far away. Then one honest prayer, one unguarded act of love, changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::3716.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing spiritual status to offering simple, heartfelt devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3717.verse_sanskrit: सो सुतंत्र अवलंब न आना। तेहि आधीन ग्यान बिग्याना॥ भगति तात अनुपम सुखमूला। मिलइ जो संत होइँ अनुकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3717.verse_hindi: वह भक्ति स्वतंत्र है, उसको (ज्ञान-विज्ञान आदि किसी) दूसरे साधन का सहारा (अपेक्षा) नहीं है। ज्ञान और विज्ञान तो उसके अधीन हैं। हे तात! भक्ति अनुपम एवं सुख की मूल है और वह तभी मिलती है, जब संत अनुकूल (प्रसन्न) होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3717.english_translation: That devotion is independent and needs no other support. Knowledge and discernment are under its sway. O friend, devotion is the unmatched root of joy, and it comes only when the saints are pleased.
ramacharitamanas::3717.translation_literal: सो (that) / सुतंत्र (independent) / अवलंब (support) / न (not) / आना (other) / तेहि (its) / आधीन (under control) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिग्याना (discernment) / भगति (devotion) / तात (friend) / अनुपम (matchless) / सुखमूला (root of joy) / मिलइ (is obtained) / जो (which) / संत (saints) / होइँ (become) / अनुकूला (favourable)
ramacharitamanas::3717.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3717.essence: Devotion is not the reward of wisdom; wisdom serves devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3717.simple_meaning: Devotion does not depend on any other path. Even knowledge and discernment serve it, and it becomes possible when saints are pleased.
ramacharitamanas::3717.simple_insight: You do not have to earn your way into love with perfect understanding first.
ramacharitamanas::3717.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the teaching turns from theory to the heart of the path. After saying that knowledge leads to freedom, Tulsidas now elevates devotion above every other means: it is self-sufficient, and even wisdom serves it.
ramacharitamanas::3717.modern_relevance: You have read every book, rehearsed every answer, and still feel dry inside. This verse says the missing piece may not be more analysis, but a heart that can yield to devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3717.insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as a result of insight to seeing insight as subordinate to devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3718.verse_sanskrit: भगति कि साधन कहउँ बखानी। सुगम पंथ मोहि पावहिं प्रानी॥ प्रथमहिं बिप्र चरन अति प्रीती। निज निज कर्म निरत श्रुति रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3718.verse_hindi: अब मैं भक्ति के साधन विस्तार से कहता हूँ- यह सुगम मार्ग है, जिससे जीव मुझको सहज ही पा जाते हैं। पहले तो ब्राह्मणों के चरणों में अत्यंत प्रीति हो और वेद की रीति के अनुसार अपने-अपने (वर्णाश्रम के) कर्मों में लगा रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3718.english_translation: Now I will explain the means of bhakti. It is the easy path by which living beings can reach me with ease. First, there should be deep love for the feet of the learned, and one should remain engaged in one's own duties according to the Vedic order.
ramacharitamanas::3718.translation_literal: भगति (devotion) / कि (of) / साधन (means) / कहउँ (I tell) / बखानी (explaining) / सुगम (easy) / पंथ (path) / मोहि (me) / पावहिं (reach) / प्रानी (living beings) / प्रथमहिं (first) / बिप्र (learned ones / brahmins) / चरन (feet) / अति (very) / प्रीती (love) / निज निज (one's own) / कर्म (duties) / निरत (engaged) / श्रुति (Vedic) / रीती (order)
ramacharitamanas::3718.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3718.essence: The easiest way to reach Ram is to honor wisdom and keep your duties.
ramacharitamanas::3718.simple_meaning: Bhakti is presented as an easy path: love the learned, and stay faithful to your own duties. That combination makes reaching Ram natural and direct.
ramacharitamanas::3718.simple_insight: Devotion is not vague feeling; it becomes real through respect and steady conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3718.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is teaching how bhakti works. He says the path is simple: honor those who know, and remain steady in your rightful duties. This is the first practical doorway before deeper devotion unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::3718.modern_relevance: You admire a mentor, then still show up for your work, your family, and your promises. That mix of reverence and responsibility is what makes devotion livable.
ramacharitamanas::3718.insight: It shifts devotion from private emotion to a disciplined way of living.

ramacharitamanas::3719.verse_sanskrit: एहि कर फल पुनि बिषय बिरागा। तब मम धर्म उपज अनुरागा॥ श्रवनादिक नव भक्ति दृढ़ाहीं। मम लीला रति अति मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3719.verse_hindi: इसका फल, फिर विषयों से वैराग्य होगा। तब (वैराग्य होने पर) मेरे धर्म (भागवत धर्म) में प्रेम उत्पन्न होगा। तब श्रवण आदि नौ प्रकार की भक्तियाँ दृढ़ होंगी और मन में मेरी लीलाओं के प्रति अत्यंत प्रेम होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3719.english_translation: Its fruit is detachment from worldly objects. Then love for my dharma arises. Then the nine forms of devotion become firm, and the mind grows deeply fond of my divine plays.
ramacharitamanas::3719.translation_literal: एहि (of this) / कर (its) / फल (fruit) / पुनि (then) / बिषय (worldly objects) / बिरागा (detachment) / तब (then) / मम (my) / धर्म (dharma) / उपज (arises) / अनुरागा (love)॥ / श्रवनादिक (hearing and the rest) / नव (nine) / भक्ति (devotions) / दृढ़ाहीं (become firm) / मम (my) / लीला (divine plays) / रति (love) / अति (very) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3719.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3719.essence: Detachment makes devotion stable, and stable devotion makes Ram's presence sweet.
ramacharitamanas::3719.simple_meaning: When attachment to worldly things fades, love for Ram's way appears. Then listening, remembering, and the other forms of devotion become steady, and the mind begins to delight in his stories.
ramacharitamanas::3719.simple_insight: Letting go is not emptiness; it makes room for love to become steady and alive.
ramacharitamanas::3719.detailed_meaning: In this stretch of the forest teaching, the speaker explains how bhakti matures. First comes detachment from sense-objects, and from that ripens love for Ram's dharma. Only then do the nine forms of devotion become firm and the mind truly relish his divine play.
ramacharitamanas::3719.modern_relevance: You stop checking your phone for one more hit of distraction, and suddenly prayer, music, or quiet reflection feels natural again. The appetite for noise weakens first; deeper love can finally settle in.
ramacharitamanas::3719.insight: It shifts you from chasing stimulation to building a mind that can stay with devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3720.verse_sanskrit: संत चरन पंकज अति प्रेमा। मन क्रम बचन भजन दृढ़ नेमा॥ गुरु पितु मातु बंधु पति देवा। सब मोहि कहँ जानै दृढ़ सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3720.verse_hindi: जिसका संतों के चरणकमलों में अत्यंत प्रेम हो, मन, वचन और कर्म से भजन का दृढ़ नियम हो और जो मुझको ही गुरु, पिता, माता, भाई, पति और देवता सब कुछ जाने और सेवा में दृढ़ हो, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3720.english_translation: One who deeply loves the feet of saints, keeps firm devotion in mind, words, and deeds, and sees me alone as teacher, father, mother, brother, husband, and divine, serves with unwavering dedication.
ramacharitamanas::3720.translation_literal: संत (holy people) / चरन (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / अति (very) / प्रेमा (love) / मन (mind) / क्रम (actions) / बचन (words) / भजन (devotion) / दृढ़ (firm) / नेमा (vow) / गुरु (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / बंधु (brother) / पति (husband) / देवा (divine) / सब (all) / मोहि (me) / कहँ (as) / जानै (knows) / दृढ़ (firm) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::3720.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3720.essence: True devotion makes one presence enough for every role in life.
ramacharitamanas::3720.simple_meaning: Deep devotion shows itself as love for holy people, steady worship in thought, speech, and action, and seeing Ram as the one true refuge in every role of life.
ramacharitamanas::3720.simple_insight: Devotion stops being an idea when it reshapes your loyalties, habits, and relationships.
ramacharitamanas::3720.detailed_meaning: Ram is describing the marks of true bhakti: love for saintly feet, steady remembrance in mind, words, and actions, and a life that treats him as teacher, parent, sibling, spouse, and highest refuge. The next verse shows the emotional signs that follow.
ramacharitamanas::3720.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone for one person’s reply, but your real devotion shows up in what you repeatedly choose, protect, and serve. Love becomes visible in loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3720.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to a whole-life orientation of service and remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::3721.verse_sanskrit: मम गुन गावत पुलक सरीरा। गदगद गिरा नयन बह नीरा॥ काम आदि मद दंभ न जाकें। तात निरंतर बस मैं ताकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3721.verse_hindi: मेरा गुण गाते समय जिसका शरीर पुलकित हो जाए, वाणी गदगद हो जाए और नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बहने लगे और काम, मद और दम्भ आदि जिसमें न हों, हे भाई! मैं सदा उसके वश में रहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3721.english_translation: When someone sings my qualities, their body shivers with joy, their voice breaks with emotion, and tears flow from their eyes. One who has no desire, pride, or vanity—dear friend, I always remain under that person's control.
ramacharitamanas::3721.translation_literal: मम (my) / गुन (qualities) / गावत (singing) / पुलक (horripilation, joy-shiver) / सरीरा (body) / गदगद (choked with emotion) / गिरा (speech) / नयन (eyes) / बह (flow) / नीरा (water, tears) / काम (desire) / आदि (etc.) / मद (pride) / दंभ (vanity) / न (not) / जाकें (in whom) / तात (dear one) / निरंतर (constantly) / बस (under control) / मैं (I) / ताकें (of that one)
ramacharitamanas::3721.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3721.essence: When pride is gone, love can pull the divine close.
ramacharitamanas::3721.simple_meaning: True devotion shows itself in tears, trembling, and speech that breaks with feeling. When pride and selfish desire are absent, Ram says he comes under that person's sway.
ramacharitamanas::3721.simple_insight: Devotion is not performance; it is the softening that lets grace meet you.
ramacharitamanas::3721.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram explains the inner signs of real bhakti to the seekers around him. He is not praising ritual skill but a heart so sincere that it trembles, weeps, and forgets pride. That openness itself draws him close.
ramacharitamanas::3721.modern_relevance: You hear your favorite song in a crowded car and suddenly your eyes fill, your voice catches, and nothing in you feels guarded. That kind of unselfconscious love is what this verse points to.
ramacharitamanas::3721.insight: It shifts devotion from display to surrender, showing that humility makes the heart receptive.

ramacharitamanas::3722.verse_sanskrit: बचन कर्म मन मोरि गति भजनु करहिं निःकाम। तिन्ह के हृदय कमल महुँ करउँ सदा बिश्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3722.verse_hindi: जिनको कर्म, वचन और मन से मेरी ही गति है और जो निष्काम भाव से मेरा भजन करते हैं, उनके हृदय कमल में मैं सदा विश्राम किया करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3722.english_translation: Those whose mind, speech, and action move only toward me, and who worship me without desire for reward — I dwell forever in the lotus of their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3722.translation_literal: बचन (speech) / कर्म (action) / मन (mind) / मोरि (my) / गति (movement, direction) / भजनु (devotion, worship) / करहिं (they do) / निःकाम (without desire for reward) / तिन्ह के (of those) / हृदय (heart) / कमल महुँ (in the lotus) / करउँ (I do) / सदा (always) / बिश्राम (rest, dwell)
ramacharitamanas::3722.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3722.essence: Selfless devotion makes the heart Ram’s resting place.
ramacharitamanas::3722.simple_meaning: When your mind, speech, and actions are all directed toward Ram, and you worship without wanting a reward, Ram lives in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::3722.simple_insight: Pure devotion turns the heart into a home for the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3722.detailed_meaning: Ram is teaching the heart of bhakti in the forest, as Lakshman listens and the exile journey deepens. He says that when a devotee’s mind, words, and actions all move toward him without selfish desire, he stays in that person’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::3722.modern_relevance: You show up for someone with no hidden agenda, no need for applause, no secret scorekeeping. That kind of love makes room for something sacred to stay.
ramacharitamanas::3722.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to wholehearted alignment.

ramacharitamanas::3723.verse_sanskrit: भगति जोग सुनि अति सुख पावा। लछिमन प्रभु चरनन्हि सिरु नावा॥ एहि बिधि कछुक दिन बीती। कहत बिराग ग्यान गुन नीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3723.verse_hindi: इस भक्ति योग को सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने अत्यंत सुख पाया और उन्होंने प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया। इस प्रकार वैराग्य, ज्ञान, गुण और नीति कहते हुए कुछ दिन बीत गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3723.english_translation: Hearing this yoga of devotion, Lakshman felt immense joy and bowed his head at Lord Ram's feet. In this way, some days passed, with talks of detachment, wisdom, virtues, and conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3723.translation_literal: भगति जोग (the yoga of devotion) / सुनि (having heard) / अति (greatly) / सुख (joy) / पावा (he found) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / प्रभु (Lord) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) ॥ एहि बिधि (in this way) / कछुक दिन (some days) / बीती (passed) / कहत (speaking) / बिराग (detachment) / ग्यान (wisdom) / गुन (virtues) / नीती (conduct) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3723.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3723.essence: Devotion first moves the heart; then wisdom can be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3723.simple_meaning: Lakshman feels deep joy on hearing about devotion and bows to Ram. Then the days pass as they keep speaking about detachment, wisdom, virtues, and right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3723.simple_insight: Joy deepens when devotion is understood, not just performed.
ramacharitamanas::3723.detailed_meaning: In the forest at Panchavati, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are living quietly after exile. Lakshman hears the teaching on bhakti and responds with delight and reverence. The verse then marks time passing as the conversation turns to renunciation and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3723.modern_relevance: You finally hear a teaching that feels true, and your whole body relaxes. Then you keep circling the same questions with someone you trust, and the days become lighter.
ramacharitamanas::3723.insight: It shows how devotion can soften the heart before any argument or philosophy begins.

ramacharitamanas::3724.verse_sanskrit: सूपनखा रावन कै बहिनी। दुष्ट हृदय दारुन जस अहिनी॥ पंचबटी सो गइ एक बारा। देखि बिकल भइ जुगल कुमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3724.verse_hindi: शूर्पणखा नामक रावण की एक बहिन थी, जो नागिन के समान भयानक और दुष्ट हृदय की थी। वह एक बार पंचवटी में गई और दोनों राजकुमारों को देखकर विकल (काम से पीड़ित) हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3724.english_translation: Sūpanakhā was Rāvaṇa’s sister. Her heart was cruel and wicked, like a serpent’s. Once she went to Panchavati and, seeing the two princes, became agitated with desire.
ramacharitamanas::3724.translation_literal: सूपनखा (Surpanakha) / रावन (Ravana's) / कै (of) / बहिनी (sister) / दुष्ट (wicked) / हृदय (heart) / दारुन (fierce, cruel) / जस (like) / अहिनी (a serpent) / पंचबटी (Panchavati) / सो (there) / गइ (went) / एक (one) / बारा (time) / देखि (seeing) / बिकल (agitated) / भइ (became) / जुगल (pair of) / कुमारा (princes)
ramacharitamanas::3724.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3724.essence: Desire can enter wearing beauty and still carry danger.
ramacharitamanas::3724.simple_meaning: Surpanakha, Ravana’s sister, comes to Panchavati and becomes unsettled when she sees Ram and Lakshman. The verse introduces her as dangerous and driven by desire.
ramacharitamanas::3724.simple_insight: Not every attraction is harmless; some desires arrive already carrying harm.
ramacharitamanas::3724.detailed_meaning: In Panchavati, the forest peace is about to break. Surpanakha, Ravana’s sister, enters the scene with a violent, unstable nature and sees the two princes. This verse sets up the danger before the conflict begins.
ramacharitamanas::3724.modern_relevance: A stranger’s attention can feel flattering at first, then suddenly unsafe. This verse shows how quickly desire can turn into threat when it is unchecked.
ramacharitamanas::3724.insight: It prepares the mind to notice how desire can distort judgment before any action begins.

ramacharitamanas::3725.verse_sanskrit: भ्राता पिता पुत्र उरगारी। पुरुष मनोहर निरखत नारी॥ होइ बिकल सक मनहि न रोकी। जिमि रबिमनि द्रव रबिहि बिलोकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3725.verse_hindi: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! (शूर्पणखा- जैसी राक्षसी, धर्मज्ञान शून्य कामान्ध) स्त्री मनोहर पुरुष को देखकर, चाहे वह भाई, पिता, पुत्र ही हो, विकल हो जाती है और मन को नहीं रोक सकती। जैसे सूर्यकान्तमणि सूर्य को देखकर द्रवित हो जाती है (ज्वाला से पिघल जाती है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3725.english_translation: A woman, upon seeing a handsome man, becomes agitated even if he is a brother, father, or son. She cannot hold her mind steady, just as a sun-stone melts when it sees the sun.
ramacharitamanas::3725.translation_literal: भ्राता (brother) / पिता (father) / पुत्र (son) / उरगारी (snake-keeper; a woman) / पुरुष (man) / मनोहर (beautiful) / निरखत (seeing) / नारी (woman) / होइ (becomes) / बिकल (disturbed) / सक (can) / मनहि (mind) / न रोकी (cannot stop) / जिमि (just as) / रबिमनि (sun-stone) / द्रव (melts) / रबिहि (the sun) / बिलोकी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::3725.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3725.essence: Desire can seize the mind before reason gets a chance.
ramacharitamanas::3725.simple_meaning: Seeing beauty can stir desire so strongly that the mind loses steadiness and stops obeying reason.
ramacharitamanas::3725.simple_insight: It reminds you how quickly attraction can hijack your attention if you do not watch it.
ramacharitamanas::3725.detailed_meaning: In Kak Bhushundi's teaching to Garuda, the forest story turns into a warning about desire. He describes how a woman may lose steadiness simply by seeing an attractive man, setting up Surpanakha's approach to Ram and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3725.modern_relevance: You open a photo, tell yourself it is harmless, and five minutes later your attention has been pulled off course. The mind can slip into craving faster than pride can admit.
ramacharitamanas::3725.insight: It trains you to notice attraction as it begins, before it turns into action.

ramacharitamanas::3726.verse_sanskrit: रुचिर रूप धरि प्रभु पहिं जाई। बोली बचन बहुत मुसुकाई॥ तुम्ह सम पुरुष न मो सम नारी। यह सँजोग बिधि रचा बिचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3726.verse_hindi: वह सुन्दर रूप धरकर प्रभु के पास जाकर और बहुत मुस्कुराकर वचन बोली- न तो तुम्हारे समान कोई पुरुष है, न मेरे समान स्त्री। विधाता ने यह संयोग (जोड़ा) बहुत विचार कर रचा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3726.english_translation: She took a lovely form, went to the Lord, and spoke with a broad smile: “There is no man like you, and no woman like me. The creator has arranged this meeting with great thought.”
ramacharitamanas::3726.translation_literal: रुचिर (lovely) / रूप (form) / धरि (taking) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पहिं (to) / जाई (went) / बोली (spoke) / बचन (words) / बहुत (much) / मुसुकाई (smiling) / तुम्ह (you) / सम (like) / पुरुष (man) / न (not) / मो (me) / सम (like) / नारी (woman) / यह (this) / सँजोग (meeting) / बिधि (the creator) / रचा (arranged) / बिचारी (thoughtfully)
ramacharitamanas::3726.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3726.essence: False sweetness can disguise a dangerous intention.
ramacharitamanas::3726.simple_meaning: She approaches him in a beautiful form, smiles, and flatters him by saying their meeting must be fate.
ramacharitamanas::3726.simple_insight: Charm can hide danger when it speaks in the language of destiny.
ramacharitamanas::3726.detailed_meaning: In Panchavati, Shurpanakha has already seen Rama and Lakshmana and been stirred by desire. Now she returns in a flattering form, smiling and speaking sweetly to draw Rama in. The scene shows seduction beginning as disguise.
ramacharitamanas::3726.modern_relevance: Someone sends a polished message that feels too smooth to be real. The praise is flattering, but the intention underneath is not innocent.
ramacharitamanas::3726.insight: It shows how manipulation often begins with admiration, softness, and a story that makes desire feel ordained.

ramacharitamanas::3727.verse_sanskrit: मम अनुरूप पुरुष जग माहीं। देखेउँ खोजि लोक तिहु नाहीं॥ तातें अब लगि रहिउँ कुमारी। मनु माना कछु तुम्हहि निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3727.verse_hindi: मेरे योग्य पुरुष (वर) जगत् भर में नहीं है, मैंने तीनों लोकों को खोज देखा। इसी से मैं अब तक कुमारी (अविवाहित) रही। अब तुमको देखकर कुछ मन माना (चित्त ठहरा) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3727.english_translation: No man in the world matched me; I searched the three worlds and found none. That is why I remained unmarried until now. Seeing you, my mind has become steady.
ramacharitamanas::3727.translation_literal: मम (my) / अनुरूप (suitable, matching) / पुरुष (man) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / देखेउँ (I saw, I searched) / खोजि (searching) / लोक (worlds) / तिहु (three) / नाहीं (not) / तातें (therefore) / अब (now) / लगि (until) / रहिउँ (I remained) / कुमारी (unmarried maiden) / मनु (mind) / माना (became satisfied) / कछु (somewhat) / तुम्हहि (you) / निहारी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::3727.speaker: Shurpanakha
ramacharitamanas::3727.essence: Desire can make you mistake attraction for final certainty.
ramacharitamanas::3727.simple_meaning: She says she searched everywhere for a man equal to her and found none, so she stayed unmarried until seeing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3727.simple_insight: Desire can make the mind declare itself complete before it is truly clear.
ramacharitamanas::3727.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shurpanakha has already begun testing Ram and Lakshman with flattery and desire. She claims she searched the three worlds for a match and found none, then says her mind has finally settled after seeing him. The verse sets up her bold proposal and the danger that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3727.modern_relevance: You scroll through endless profiles, convinced no one measures up, until one person catches your eye and the whole story changes. Attraction can feel like certainty before it has any wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3727.insight: It shows how desire narrows judgment and turns attraction into a claim of destiny.

ramacharitamanas::3728.verse_sanskrit: सीतहि चितइ कही प्रभु बाता। अहइ कुआर मोर लघु भ्राता॥ गइ लछिमन रिपु भगिनी जानी। प्रभु बिलोकि बोले मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3728.verse_hindi: सीताजी की ओर देखकर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने यह बात कही कि मेरा छोटा भाई कुमार है। तब वह लक्ष्मणजी के पास गई। लक्ष्मणजी ने उसे शत्रु की बहिन समझकर और प्रभु की ओर देखकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3728.english_translation: Sita looked at him, and the Lord said, "My younger brother is unmarried." Then she went to Lakshman. Seeing her as the enemy's sister and looking at the Lord, Lakshman spoke gently.
ramacharitamanas::3728.translation_literal: सीतहि (to Sita) / चितइ (looking at) / कही (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बाता (words) / अहइ (is) / कुआर (unmarried) / मोर (my) / लघु भ्राता (younger brother) / गइ (went) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / रिपु (enemy) / भगिनी (sister) / जानी (knowing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बोले (spoke) / मृदु बानी (gentle words)
ramacharitamanas::3728.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3728.essence: Right speech can hold both caution and kindness.
ramacharitamanas::3728.simple_meaning: Ram points Sita toward Lakshman and says his younger brother is unmarried. Lakshman then speaks gently, treating her as the enemy's sister while still looking to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3728.simple_insight: Even in a tense moment, dignity and restraint can guide your words.
ramacharitamanas::3728.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita approaches Ram in the disguise of a seeker. Ram redirects her toward Lakshman, who is still bound by loyalty to his brother and alert to danger. The verse is a small bridge into the fuller exchange that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3728.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a charged moment and choose your words carefully, not to inflame the situation. That restraint can protect everyone involved.
ramacharitamanas::3728.insight: It shows how loyalty, caution, and courtesy can coexist in a difficult encounter.

ramacharitamanas::3729.verse_sanskrit: सुंदरि सुनु मैं उन्ह कर दासा। पराधीन नहिं तोर सुपासा॥ प्रभु समर्थ कोसलपुर राजा। जो कछु करहिं उनहि सब छाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3729.verse_hindi: हे सुंदरी! सुन, मैं तो उनका दास हूँ। मैं पराधीन हूँ, अतः तुम्हे सुभीता (सुख) न होगा। प्रभु समर्थ हैं, कोसलपुर के राजा है, वे जो कुछ करें, उन्हें सब फबता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3729.english_translation: O beautiful one, listen: I am their servant. I am under another's control, so I cannot help you. The Lord is powerful, the king of Kosala; whatever they do, all suits them.
ramacharitamanas::3729.translation_literal: सुंदरि (O beautiful one) / सुनु (listen) / मैं (I) / उन्ह (their) / का दासा (servant) / पराधीन (dependent on another) / नहिं (not) / तोर (your) / सुपासा (ease/help) ॥ / प्रभु (the Lord) / समर्थ (powerful) / कोसलपुर (of Kosala city) / राजा (king) / जो (whatever) / कछु (anything) / करहिं (they do) / उनहि (for them) / सब (all) / छाजा (fits well) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3729.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3729.essence: Serving rightly means refusing what your role cannot permit.
ramacharitamanas::3729.simple_meaning: Lakshman tells Surpanakha that he serves Ram and cannot act independently. Ram is the powerful king, and whatever he does is fitting.
ramacharitamanas::3729.simple_insight: Real service means your personal comfort no longer comes first.
ramacharitamanas::3729.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha presses Lakshman with desire. He answers by naming his place plainly: he belongs to Ram's service, not to his own wishes. In that moment, duty becomes a boundary.
ramacharitamanas::3729.modern_relevance: Someone asks you for a favor that would cross a line you already know. You feel the pressure to be agreeable, but your role, promise, or loyalty comes first.
ramacharitamanas::3729.insight: It teaches you to hold your service steady even when someone demands more than you can give.

ramacharitamanas::3730.verse_sanskrit: सेवक सुख चह मान भिखारी। ब्यसनी धन सुभ गति बिभिचारी॥ लोभी जसु चह चार गुमानी। नभ दुहि दूध चहत ए प्रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3730.verse_hindi: सेवक सुख चाहे, भिखारी सम्मान चाहे, व्यसनी (जिसे जुए, शराब आदि का व्यसन हो) धन और व्यभिचारी शुभ गति चाहे, लोभी यश चाहे और अभिमानी चारों फल- अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष चाहे, तो ये सब प्राणी आकाश को दुहकर दूध लेना चाहते हैं (अर्थात् असंभव बात को संभव करना चाहते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3730.english_translation: A servant may want comfort, a beggar may want respect, an addict may want wealth, an adulterer may want a good fate, the greedy may want fame, and the proud may want all four aims of life. They are trying to milk the sky for milk.
ramacharitamanas::3730.translation_literal: सेवक (servant) / सुख (comfort) / चह (wants) / मान (respect) / भिखारी (beggar) / ब्यसनी (addict) / धन (wealth) / सुभ गति (good fate) / बिभिचारी (adulterer) / लोभी (greedy) / जसु (fame) / चह (wants) / चार (four) / गुमानी (proud one) / नभ (sky) / दुहि (to milk) / दूध (milk) / चहत (wants) / ए (these) / प्रानी (creatures)
ramacharitamanas::3730.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3730.essence: Impossible desires collapse when your life contradicts your wishes.
ramacharitamanas::3730.simple_meaning: People often want blessings that their own habits make impossible. A servant wants comfort, a beggar wants respect, and a proud person wants all four aims of life.
ramacharitamanas::3730.simple_insight: It stings, but it clears the fog: you cannot keep the same habits and expect opposite results.
ramacharitamanas::3730.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram turns from quiet conversation to a hard truth about human desire. He points out how different people chase incompatible goals while living in ways that block them. The image of milking the sky exposes the absurdity.
ramacharitamanas::3730.modern_relevance: You want a calm mind, but you keep doom-scrolling past midnight. You want trust, but you keep feeding suspicion. The verse cuts through that self-contradiction.
ramacharitamanas::3730.insight: It pushes you to notice when your goals and habits are fighting each other.

ramacharitamanas::3731.verse_sanskrit: पुनि फिरि राम निकट सो आई। प्रभु लछिमन पहिं बहुरि पठाई॥ लछिमन कहा तोहि सो बरई। जो तृन तोरि लाज परिहरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3731.verse_hindi: वह लौटकर फिर श्री रामजी के पास आई, प्रभु ने उसे फिर लक्ष्मणजी के पास भेज दिया। लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- तुम्हें वही वरेगा, जो लज्जा को तृण तोड़कर (अर्थात् प्रतिज्ञा करके) त्याग देगा (अर्थात् जो निपट निर्लज्ज होगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3731.english_translation: She came back again to Ram, and the Lord sent her once more to Lakshman. Lakshman said, "You will choose only the one who casts off shame like a blade of grass."
ramacharitamanas::3731.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / फिरि (turning back) / राम (Ram) / निकट (near) / सो (she) / आई (came) / प्रभु (the Lord) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / पहिं (to) / बहुरि (again) / पठाई (sent) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / कहा (said) / तोहि (you) / सो (that one) / बरई (will choose) / जो (who) / तृन (grass) / तोरि (breaking) / लाज (shame) / परिहरई (gives up)
ramacharitamanas::3731.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3731.essence: Repeated disrespect meets a sharper boundary.
ramacharitamanas::3731.simple_meaning: She returns to Ram, and he sends her to Lakshman again. Lakshman answers sharply: only someone with no shame at all would accept her.
ramacharitamanas::3731.simple_insight: Not every offer deserves a softer reply. Sometimes a boundary must be clear and unadorned.
ramacharitamanas::3731.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha keeps pressing her claim after Ram refuses her. Ram sends her on to Lakshman, and Lakshman cuts through the situation with a harsh rejection. The scene escalates the insult that will soon drive the larger conflict.
ramacharitamanas::3731.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing past your first no, hoping the second time will be easier. You finally answer plainly, without apology, because the boundary itself matters.
ramacharitamanas::3731.insight: It shows that repeated intrusion can be met with direct refusal, not endless politeness.

ramacharitamanas::3732.verse_sanskrit: तब खिसिआनि राम पहिं गई। रूप भयंकर प्रगटत भई॥ सीतहि सभय देखि रघुराई। कहा अनुज सन सयन बुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3732.verse_hindi: तब वह खिसियायी हुई (क्रुद्ध होकर) श्री रामजी के पास गई और उसने अपना भयंकर रूप प्रकट किया। सीताजी को भयभीत देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने लक्ष्मण को इशारा देकर कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3732.english_translation: Then, angered, she went to Ram and revealed her terrible form. Seeing Sita frightened, Raghunath signaled to Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3732.translation_literal: तब (then) / खिसिआनि (angered) / राम पहिं (to Ram) / गई (went) / रूप (form) / भयंकर (terrible) / प्रगटत (revealing) / भई (became) / सीतहि (Sita) / सभय (frightened) / देखि (seeing) / रघुराई (Raghurai) / कहा (said/signaled) / अनुज सन (to the younger brother) / सयन बुझाई (by a sign/gesture)
ramacharitamanas::3732.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3732.essence: Anger can turn ugly, but calm awareness still sees the real danger.
ramacharitamanas::3732.simple_meaning: The woman returns in anger, shows a frightening form, and Ram notices Sita’s fear and signals Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3732.simple_insight: Fear can expose deception, but steady attention still sees what needs to be done.
ramacharitamanas::3732.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha has already been rejected and humiliated. She returns to Ram in fury, revealing her terrifying form. Sita is alarmed, and Ram calmly signals Lakshman, setting the next turn of the encounter in motion.
ramacharitamanas::3732.modern_relevance: Someone storms back into a room after being embarrassed, trying to regain control with intimidation. The calm person notices who is actually shaken and quietly lets the right response begin.
ramacharitamanas::3732.insight: It shifts attention from the aggressor’s performance to the vulnerable person who needs protection.

ramacharitamanas::3733.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन अति लाघवँ सो नाक कान बिनु कीन्हि। ताके कर रावन कहँ मनौ चुनौती दीन्हि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3733.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने बड़ी फुर्ती से उसको बिना नाक-कान की कर दिया। मानो उसके हाथ रावण को चुनौती दी हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3733.english_translation: Lakshman swiftly cut off her nose and ears, as if he had thrown Ravana a challenge.
ramacharitamanas::3733.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / अति (very) / लाघवँ (with speed and lightness) / सो (that one) / नाक (nose) / कान (ears) / बिनु (without) / कीन्हि (made) / ताके (for that) / कर (hand) / रावन (Ravana) / कहँ (to) / मनौ (as if) / चुनौती (challenge) / दीन्हि (gave)
ramacharitamanas::3733.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3733.essence: A swift retaliation turns mockery into a direct challenge.
ramacharitamanas::3733.simple_meaning: Lakshman quickly disfigures the woman by cutting off her nose and ears, and the line compares it to a challenge thrown at Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::3733.simple_insight: Some actions are not just punishment; they announce that a line has been crossed.
ramacharitamanas::3733.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha has mocked Sita and pressed herself on Ram. Lakshman reacts instantly and cuts off her nose and ears. The verse is a sharp narrative beat, not a teaching, and it sets up the outrage that drives the next scene.
ramacharitamanas::3733.modern_relevance: A heated argument can turn into a point of no return in seconds. One sharp response can escalate everything beyond repair.
ramacharitamanas::3733.insight: It shows how a single retaliatory act can transform insult into open conflict.

ramacharitamanas::3734.verse_sanskrit: नाक कान बिनु भइ बिकरारा। जनु स्रव सैल गेरु कै धारा॥ खर दूषन पहिं गइ बिलपाता। धिग धिग तव पौरुष बल भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3734.verse_hindi: बिना नाक-कान के वह विकराल हो गई। (उसके शरीर से रक्त इस प्रकार बहने लगा) मानो (काले) पर्वत से गेरू की धारा बह रही हो। वह विलाप करती हुई खर-दूषण के पास गई (और बोली-) हे भाई! तुम्हारे पौरुष (वीरता) को धिक्कार है, तुम्हारे बल को धिक्कार है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3734.english_translation: She became hideous without nose and ears, as if a stream of red ochre flowed from a black mountain. Wailing, she went to Khara and Dushana and cried, "Shame on your manhood, shame on your strength, brother!"
ramacharitamanas::3734.translation_literal: नाक (nose) / कान (ears) / बिनु (without) / भइ (became) / बिकरारा (terrible, hideous) / जनु (as if) / स्रव (streaming) / सैल (mountain) / गेरु (red ochre) / कै (of) / धारा (stream) / खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / पहिं (to) / गइ (went) / बिलपाता (wailing) / धिग धिग (shame, shame) / तव (your) / पौरुष (manliness, valor) / बल (strength) / भ्राता (brother)
ramacharitamanas::3734.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3734.essence: Humiliation, left unchecked, becomes the spark for revenge.
ramacharitamanas::3734.simple_meaning: After Lakshman maimed her, Surpanakha became terrifying to look at and ran crying to her brothers, insulting their courage and strength.
ramacharitamanas::3734.simple_insight: Humiliation can turn pain into rage and make the wounded person seek revenge.
ramacharitamanas::3734.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman has just disfigured Surpanakha for her aggression toward Sita. Shamed and bleeding, she rushes to Khara and Dushana, not to heal, but to stir their fury. This moment drives the conflict into open violence.
ramacharitamanas::3734.modern_relevance: A heated argument leaves someone humiliated, and instead of cooling down, they call a sibling or friend to rally support. Hurt quickly becomes escalation.
ramacharitamanas::3734.insight: It shows how wounded pride can convert private injury into collective retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::3735.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं पूछा सब कहेसि बुझाई। जातुधान सुनि सेन बनाई॥ धाए निसिचर निकर बरूथा। जनु सपच्छ कज्जल गिरि जूथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3735.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पूछा, तब शूर्पणखा ने सब समझाकर कहा। सब सुनकर राक्षसों ने सेना तैयार की। राक्षस समूह झुंड के झुंड दौड़े। मानो पंखधारी काजल के पर्वतों का झुंड हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3735.english_translation: She was questioned, and then she explained everything clearly. Hearing it, the demons formed their army. The demon hosts rushed forward in swarms, like flocks of winged black mountains.
ramacharitamanas::3735.translation_literal: तेहिं (by her) / पूछा (asked) / सब (everything) / कहेसि (she told) / बुझाई (clearly) / जातुधान (demons) / सुनि (hearing) / सेन (army) / बनाई (formed) / धाए (rushed) / निसिचर (night-demons) / निकर (multitude) / बरूथा (ranks) / जनु (as if) / सपच्छ (winged) / कज्जल (black) / गिरि (mountain) / जूथा (herds)
ramacharitamanas::3735.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3735.essence: Anger multiplies fast when a wound is handed to a crowd.
ramacharitamanas::3735.simple_meaning: After hearing Shurpanakha's report, the demons quickly gather their army and rush out in huge numbers.
ramacharitamanas::3735.simple_insight: Some wounds don't stay personal; they become a call to violence.
ramacharitamanas::3735.detailed_meaning: In the forest episode of Aranyakand, Shurpanakha has just been disfigured and returns to the demon side. She explains what happened, and the demon forces immediately assemble and charge forward. The verse is a bridge from insult to war.
ramacharitamanas::3735.modern_relevance: One angry message in a family group chat can turn private hurt into a full-blown fight before anyone has cooled down.
ramacharitamanas::3735.insight: It shows how quickly resentment spreads when pain is turned into retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::3736.verse_sanskrit: नाना बाहन नानाकारा। नानायुध धर घोर अपारा॥ सूपनखा आगें करि लीनी। असुभ रूप श्रुति नासा हीनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3736.verse_hindi: वे अनेकों प्रकार की सवारियों पर चढ़े हुए तथा अनेकों आकार (सूरतों) के हैं। वे अपार हैं और अनेकों प्रकार के असंख्य भयानक हथियार धारण किए हुए हैं। उन्होंने नाक-कान कटी हुई अमंगलरूपिणी शूर्पणखा को आगे कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3736.english_translation: They rode on many kinds of mounts, in many forms, carrying countless terrible weapons. They placed the disfigured, inauspicious Shurpanakha in front.
ramacharitamanas::3736.translation_literal: नाना (many kinds of) / बाहन (mounts) / नानाकारा (many forms) / नानायुध (many weapons) / धर (holding) / घोर (terrible) / अपारा (countless) / सूपनखा (Shurpanakha) / आगें (in front) / करि (having made) / लीनी (taken) / असुभ (inauspicious) / रूप (form) / श्रुति (ears) / नासा (nose) / हीनी (deprived)
ramacharitamanas::3736.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3736.essence: Power driven by hurt still marches toward ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3736.simple_meaning: The demon army arrives in many forms, on many mounts, with many weapons, and they put Shurpanakha at the front.
ramacharitamanas::3736.simple_insight: Chaos can look powerful, but it is still driven by anger and injury.
ramacharitamanas::3736.detailed_meaning: After Shurpanakha is mutilated, she returns to the demon ranks in Lanka and leads them toward revenge. The scene is still building toward battle; this verse mainly describes the army's terrifying appearance, not a teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3736.modern_relevance: A crowd gathers outside a house after one person has been humiliated, and the whole mood turns sharp and reckless. The force looks huge, but it is really just wounded outrage spreading.
ramacharitamanas::3736.insight: It shifts attention from the army's spectacle to the emotion driving it: revenge born from injury.

ramacharitamanas::3737.verse_sanskrit: असगुन अमित होहिं भयकारी। गनहिं न मृत्यु बिबस सब झारी॥ गर्जहिं तर्जहिं गगन उड़ाहीं। देखि कटकु भट अति हरषाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3737.verse_hindi: अनगिनत भयंकर अशकुन हो रहे हैं, परंतु मृत्यु के वश होने के कारण वे सब के सब उनको कुछ गिनते ही नहीं। गरजते हैं, ललकारते हैं और आकाश में उड़ते हैं। सेना देखकर योद्धा लोग बहुत ही हर्षित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3737.english_translation: Countless ominous signs appear, but the warriors, driven by death, pay them no mind. They roar, shout, and fly through the sky. Seeing the army, the fighters are filled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3737.translation_literal: असगुन (bad omens) / अमित (countless) / होहिं (are) / भयकारी (fear-inducing) / गनहिं (they count) / न (not) / मृत्यु (death) / बिबस (under compulsion) / सब (all) / झारी (in vain, uselessly) / गर्जहिं (they roar) / तर्जहिं (they threaten) / गगन (sky) / उड़ाहीं (they fly) / देखि (seeing) / कटकु (army) / भट (warriors) / अति (greatly) / हरषाहीं (rejoice)
ramacharitamanas::3737.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3737.essence: Fearful omens mean nothing to those already rushing toward ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3737.simple_meaning: Bad omens fill the sky, but the warriors ignore them and rush ahead, roaring and shouting. The sight of the army only makes them more excited.
ramacharitamanas::3737.simple_insight: When rage takes over, even warning signs stop mattering.
ramacharitamanas::3737.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s forces surge out after Shurpanakha’s report. The sky is filled with ominous signs, but the warriors, already under death’s grip, charge ahead in excitement. This is scene-setting before the confrontation with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3737.modern_relevance: You’ve seen a group get hyped in a group chat, ignoring every warning sign, and rush straight into a mess. Momentum can make danger feel like celebration.
ramacharitamanas::3737.insight: It shows how collective aggression can override caution and make destruction feel thrilling.

ramacharitamanas::3738.verse_sanskrit: कोउ कह जिअत धरहु द्वौ भाई। धरि मारहु तिय लेहु छड़ाई॥ धूरि पूरि नभ मंडल रहा। राम बोलाइ अनुज सन कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3738.verse_hindi: कोई कहता है दोनों भाइयों को जीता ही पकड़ लो, पकड़कर मार डालो और स्त्री को छीन लो। आकाशमण्डल धूल से भर गया। तब श्री रामजी ने लक्ष्मणजी को बुलाकर उनसे कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3738.english_translation: Some said, “Catch both brothers alive, kill them after capturing them, and take the woman away.” Dust filled the sky. Then Ram called Lakshman and said:
ramacharitamanas::3738.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / कह (said) / जिअत (alive) / धरहु (catch) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) / धरि (having caught) / मारहु (kill) / तिय (woman) / लेहु (take) / छड़ाई (away) / धूरि (dust) / पूरि (filled) / नभ (sky) / मंडल (sphere) / रहा (remained) / राम (Ram) / बोलाइ (calling) / अनुज (younger brother) / सन (to) / कहा (said)
ramacharitamanas::3738.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3738.essence: The crisis is now, and Ram answers with command.
ramacharitamanas::3738.simple_meaning: The scene turns chaotic as enemies shout orders to seize Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Dust fills the sky, and Ram turns to Lakshman to respond.
ramacharitamanas::3738.simple_insight: Some moments leave no room for reflection — only alertness, speed, and trust in the person beside you.
ramacharitamanas::3738.detailed_meaning: The forest ambush has fully erupted. Ravana's forces are shouting for Ram and Lakshman to be seized and Sita taken away, while dust chokes the sky. In that instant, Ram calls Lakshman aside and gives the next command.
ramacharitamanas::3738.modern_relevance: A crowded street suddenly turns tense, voices rise, and you have seconds to decide who to protect and where to move. Clarity matters more than panic.
ramacharitamanas::3738.insight: It shifts attention from fear to immediate protective action.

ramacharitamanas::3739.verse_sanskrit: लै जानकिहि जाहु गिरि कंदर। आवा निसिचर कटकु भयंकर॥ रहेहु सजग सुनि प्रभु कै बानी। चले सहित श्री सर धनु पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3739.verse_hindi: राक्षसों की भयानक सेना आ गई है। जानकीजी को लेकर तुम पर्वत की कंदरा में चले जाओ। सावधान रहना। प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए श्री सीताजी सहित चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3739.english_translation: The terrifying army of demons has arrived. Take Janaki to the mountain cave. Stay alert. Hearing Lord Ram's words, Lakshman went with bow and arrows in hand, along with Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3739.translation_literal: लै (taking) / जानकिहि (Janaki) / जाहु (go) / गिरि (mountain) / कंदर (cave) / आवा (has come) / निसिचर (demon) / कटकु (army) / भयंकर (terrifying) / रहेहु (stay) / सजग (alert) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (Lord) / कै (of) / बानी (words) / चले (went) / सहित (together with) / श्री (radiant) / सर (arrows) / धनु (bow) / पानी (in hand)
ramacharitamanas::3739.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3739.essence: Urgency becomes clear service when danger arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3739.simple_meaning: The enemy army has arrived, so Sita should be taken to safety while everyone stays alert. Lakshman obeys Ram at once and leaves with bow in hand.
ramacharitamanas::3739.simple_insight: Protect what is precious first; steady action matters more than panic.
ramacharitamanas::3739.detailed_meaning: The demon army has reached the scene in Aranyakand. Ram gives an urgent command: take Sita to a mountain cave and stay watchful. Lakshman instantly obeys, armed and ready, as the danger closes in.
ramacharitamanas::3739.modern_relevance: A storm alert flashes on your phone, and you move the children to the safest room before grabbing your keys. In a crisis, calm obedience protects more than fear does.
ramacharitamanas::3739.insight: It shifts attention from fear to immediate protective action.

ramacharitamanas::3740.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम रिपुदल चलि आवा। बिहसि कठिन कोदंड चढ़ावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3740.verse_hindi: शत्रुओं की सेना (समीप) चली आई है, यह देखकर श्री रामजी ने हँसकर कठिन धनुष को चढ़ाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3740.english_translation: Seeing the enemy army advance, Ram smiled and strung the mighty bow.
ramacharitamanas::3740.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / रिपुदल (enemy army) / चलि (advancing) / आवा (came) / बिहसि (smiling) / कठिन (mighty, hard) / कोदंड (bow) / चढ़ावा (strung, raised)
ramacharitamanas::3740.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3740.essence: Fear does not enter where readiness is already complete.
ramacharitamanas::3740.simple_meaning: Ram sees the enemy army approaching and calmly prepares his bow for battle.
ramacharitamanas::3740.simple_insight: Courage can be quiet. You do not have to panic to meet danger.
ramacharitamanas::3740.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the attacking force draws near and the scene tightens around Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Ram does not flinch; he smiles and lifts his great bow. The verse simply shows his fearless readiness before the fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::3740.modern_relevance: You hear the worst possible update just before a meeting, and your chest tightens. Then you breathe, straighten up, and handle the next step without drama.
ramacharitamanas::3740.insight: It shifts you from fear to composed readiness when pressure arrives.

ramacharitamanas::3741.verse_sanskrit: कोदंड कठिन चढ़ाइ सिर जट जूट बाँधत सोह क्यों। मरकत सयल पर लरत दामिनि कोटि सों जुग भुजग ज्यों॥ कटि कसि निषंग बिसाल भुज गहि चाप बिसिख सुधारि कै। चितवत मनहुँ मृगराज प्रभु गजराज घटा निहारि कै॥
ramacharitamanas::3741.verse_hindi: कठिन धनुष चढ़ाकर सिर पर जटा का जू़ड़ा बाँधते हुए प्रभु कैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, जैसे मरकतमणि (पन्ने) के पर्वत पर करोड़ों बिजलियों से दो साँप लड़ रहे हों। कमर में तरकस कसकर, विशाल भुजाओं में धनुष लेकर और बाण सुधारकर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी राक्षसों की ओर देख रहे हैं। मानों मतवाले हाथियों के समूह को (आता) देखकर सिंह (उनकी ओर) ताक रहा हो।
ramacharitamanas::3741.english_translation: How splendid the Lord looks, bow raised, matted hair tied on his head, like two serpents fighting on a mountain of emerald and lightning. With his quiver tightened at the waist, mighty arms holding the bow, arrows ready, he watches the enemy like a lion watching a herd of elephants.
ramacharitamanas::3741.translation_literal: कोदंड (great bow) / कठिन (hard, mighty) / चढ़ाइ (having raised) / सिर (head) / जट जूट (matted hair knot) / बाँधत (tying) / सोह (shines, looks beautiful) / क्यों (how) / मरकत (emerald) / सयल (mountain) / पर (on) / लरत (fighting) / दामिनि (lightning) / कोटि सों (like millions) / जुग (pair) / भुजग (serpents) / ज्यों (as) / कटि (waist) / कसि (tightening) / निषंग (quiver) / बिसाल (great, vast) / भुज (arms) / गहि (holding) / चाप (bow) / बिसिख (arrows) / सुधारि कै (having readied) / चितवत (watching) / मनहुँ (as if) / मृगराज (lion) / प्रभु (Lord) / गजराज (elephants) / घटा (herd) / निहारि कै (having looked at)
ramacharitamanas::3741.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3741.essence: True courage looks beautiful because it is completely prepared.
ramacharitamanas::3741.simple_meaning: Ram stands ready for battle, beautifully fierce and fully armed, watching the enemy with calm strength.
ramacharitamanas::3741.simple_insight: Strength can be beautiful when it is disciplined and fully awake.
ramacharitamanas::3741.detailed_meaning: The forest scene has turned tense: the enemy army is arriving, and Ram stands alone in the open, bow raised, hair tied, arrows ready. Tulsidas pauses on his form itself, turning preparation into a vision of royal courage.
ramacharitamanas::3741.modern_relevance: You tighten your helmet strap before walking into the room where the hard conversation waits. Your calm is not weakness; it is readiness.
ramacharitamanas::3741.insight: It shifts attention from fear to poised readiness under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3742.verse_sanskrit: आइ गए बगमेल धरहु धरहु धावत सुभट। जथा बिलोकि अकेल बाल रबिहि घेरत दनुज ॥
ramacharitamanas::3742.verse_hindi: 'पकड़ो-पकड़ो' पुकारते हुए राक्षस योद्धा बाग छोड़कर (बड़ी तेजी से) दौड़े हुए आए (और उन्होंने श्री रामजी को चारों ओर से घेर लिया), जैसे बालसूर्य (उदयकालीन सूर्य) को अकेला देखकर मन्देह नामक दैत्य घेर लेते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3742.english_translation: The warrior-raksasas rushed in, shouting, “Catch him! Catch him!” and surrounded the lone Ram like demons surrounding the young sun.
ramacharitamanas::3742.translation_literal: आइ गए (came) / बगमेल (raksasa warriors) / धरहु धरहु (catch him, catch him) / धावत (rushing) / सुभट (brave warriors) / जथा (like) / बिलोकि (seeing) / अकेल (alone) / बाल (young) / रबिहि (sun) / घेरत (surrounding) / दनुज (demons)
ramacharitamanas::3742.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3742.essence: Aloneness can still stand unshaken when danger closes in.
ramacharitamanas::3742.simple_meaning: The enemy warriors rushed toward Ram and surrounded him, just as demons would crowd around the rising sun.
ramacharitamanas::3742.simple_insight: The scene shows danger closing in fast, with Ram standing alone against many attackers.
ramacharitamanas::3742.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram stands alone as the raksasa warriors rush in shouting to seize him. The verse paints the pressure of the moment by comparing him to the young sun surrounded by demons, setting up the battle that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3742.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and realize every eye is on you at once. The pressure feels sudden, but the verse holds the image of standing alone without shrinking.
ramacharitamanas::3742.insight: It frames crisis as a moment of visible courage, not panic.

ramacharitamanas::3743.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु बिलोकि सर सकहिं न डारी। थकित भई रजनीचर धारी॥ सचिव बोलि बोले खर दूषन। यह कोउ नृपबालक नर भूषन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3743.verse_hindi: (सौंदर्य-माधुर्यनिधि) प्रभु श्री रामजी को देखकर राक्षसों की सेना थकित रह गई। वे उन पर बाण नहीं छोड़ सके। मंत्री को बुलाकर खर-दूषण ने कहा- यह राजकुमार कोई मनुष्यों का भूषण है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3743.english_translation: Seeing Ram, the demon army grew tired and could not shoot their arrows. Calling his minister, Khara-Dushana said, "This prince is truly an ornament of humankind."
ramacharitamanas::3743.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सर (arrows) / सकहिं (are able) / न (not) / डारी (to throw) / थकित (tired) / भई (became) / रजनीचर (night-walkers, demons) / धारी (army) // सचिव (minister) / बोलि (calling) / बोले (spoke) / खर दूषन (Khara-Dushana) / यह (this) / कोउ (some) / नृपबालक (prince-child) / नर (of humans) / भूषन (ornament) / ॥
ramacharitamanas::3743.speaker: Khara-Dushana
ramacharitamanas::3743.essence: True majesty can stop violence before it begins.
ramacharitamanas::3743.simple_meaning: Ram's presence leaves the demon army stunned and unable to attack. Even Khara-Dushana recognizes that this prince is extraordinary.
ramacharitamanas::3743.simple_insight: Sometimes strength is so complete that even enemies pause before it.
ramacharitamanas::3743.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Khara and Dushana’s army rushes toward Ram after seeing his beauty and power. But the sight of Ram unnerves them, and their attack falters. Khara-Dushana then turns to his minister and admits that this prince is no ordinary human.
ramacharitamanas::3743.modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready for conflict, but something about your calm changes the whole atmosphere. Even the people braced against you can feel your steadiness before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3743.insight: It shows how presence can disarm aggression before force is used.

ramacharitamanas::3744.verse_sanskrit: नाग असुर सुर नर मुनि जेते। देखे जिते हते हम केते॥ हम भरि जन्म सुनहु सब भाई। देखी नहिं असि सुंदरताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3744.verse_hindi: जितने भी नाग, असुर, देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि हैं, उनमें से हमने न जाने कितने ही देखे, जीते और मार डाले हैं। पर हे सब भाइयों! सुनो, हमने जन्मभर में ऐसी सुंदरता कहीं नहीं देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3744.english_translation: We have seen, defeated, and killed countless serpents, demons, gods, humans, and sages. But listen, brothers: in all our lives, we have never seen such beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3744.translation_literal: नाग (serpents) / असुर (beings of ego and shadow) / सुर (radiant beings) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / जेते (as many as) / देखे (seen) / जिते (conquered) / हते (killed) / हम (we) / केते (how many)॥ / हम (we) / भरि (throughout) / जन्म (lives) / सुनहु (listen) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers) / देखी (seen) / नहिं (not) / असि (such) / सुंदरताई (beauty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3744.speaker: Ravana's ministers
ramacharitamanas::3744.essence: Beauty can silence even the proudest enemies.
ramacharitamanas::3744.simple_meaning: Ravana's men boast that they have faced every kind of being and defeated many, yet they admit they have never seen beauty like Ram's.
ramacharitamanas::3744.simple_insight: Even pride can be forced into awe when it meets what it cannot diminish.
ramacharitamanas::3744.detailed_meaning: Ravana's ministers have surrounded Ram in the forest and are staring at him in disbelief. They are hardened by battle and accustomed to violence, yet Ram's beauty stops their attack and leaves them speaking in admiration.
ramacharitamanas::3744.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a room who makes your usual confidence feel small. The mind that came ready to dominate suddenly has to admit, 'I have never seen this before.'
ramacharitamanas::3744.insight: It shows how true greatness can disarm aggression before any weapon is used.

ramacharitamanas::3745.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि भगिनी कीन्हि कुरूपा। बध लायक नहिं पुरुष अनूपा॥ देहु तुरत निज नारि दुराई। जीअत भवन जाहु द्वौ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3745.verse_hindi: यद्यपि इन्होंने हमारी बहिन को कुरूप कर दिया तथापि ये अनुपम पुरुष वध करने योग्य नहीं हैं। 'छिपाई हुई अपनी स्त्री हमें तुरंत दे दो और दोनों भाई जीते जी घर लौट जाओ' ॥
ramacharitamanas::3745.english_translation: Although they have disfigured our sister, such an incomparable man is not fit to be killed. Hand over your hidden wife at once, and both brothers may return home alive.
ramacharitamanas::3745.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / भगिनी (sister) / कीन्हि (made) / कुरूपा (ugly/disfigured) / बध (killing) / लायक (fit) / नहिं (not) / पुरुष (man) / अनूपा (incomparable) ॥ देहु (give) / तुरत (at once) / निज (your own) / नारि (wife) / दुराई (hidden) / जीअत (alive) / भवन (home) / जाहु (go) / द्वौ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3745.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3745.essence: Pride can admire greatness and still refuse to yield.
ramacharitamanas::3745.simple_meaning: Ravana admits the brothers are extraordinary, but still demands Sita back and offers them safe return if they comply.
ramacharitamanas::3745.simple_insight: Even a hostile mind can recognize greatness and still choose coercion.
ramacharitamanas::3745.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking after seeing Ram and Lakshman up close. He cannot deny their nobility, but he still tries to save face by bargaining for Sita's return. The moment shows pride wrestling with fear, yet refusing surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3745.modern_relevance: A person can praise your talent in one breath and pressure you in the next. Recognition does not always mean respect; sometimes it is just strategy.
ramacharitamanas::3745.insight: It exposes how ego can speak in compliments while still demanding control.

ramacharitamanas::3746.verse_sanskrit: मोर कहा तुम्ह ताहि सुनावहु। तासु बचन सुनि आतुर आवहु॥ दूतन्ह कहा राम सन जाई। सुनत राम बोले मुसुकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3746.verse_hindi: मेरा यह कथन तुम लोग उसे सुनाओ और उसका वचन (उत्तर) सुनकर शीघ्र आओ। दूतों ने जाकर यह संदेश श्री रामचंद्रजी से कहा। उसे सुनते ही श्री रामचंद्रजी मुस्कुराकर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3746.english_translation: Tell him my words, and come back quickly after hearing his reply. The messengers carried the message to Ram, and hearing it, Ram smiled.
ramacharitamanas::3746.translation_literal: मोर (my) / कहा (said) / तुम्ह (you all) / ताहि (to him) / सुनावहु (make hear, tell) / तासु (his) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / आतुर (quickly, eagerly) / आवहु (come) / दूतन्ह (by the messengers) / कहा (said) / राम (Ram) / सन (to) / जाई (going) / सुनत (hearing) / राम (Ram) / बोले (spoke) / मुसुकाई (smiling)
ramacharitamanas::3746.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3746.essence: A steady heart does not lose itself when challenged.
ramacharitamanas::3746.simple_meaning: Ravana tells the messengers to carry his words and return quickly with the reply. When Ram hears the message, he smiles.
ramacharitamanas::3746.simple_insight: Even a hostile message can reveal calm strength when it meets a steady heart.
ramacharitamanas::3746.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still testing the situation after Sita's abduction. He sends his words through messengers, and they bring the message to Ram. Ram's smile shows composure before the coming clash, not fear or confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3746.modern_relevance: Someone sends a sharp email meant to provoke you, but you read it once and stay steady. Not every challenge deserves agitation; some only reveal how settled you are.
ramacharitamanas::3746.insight: It shows how calm presence can answer provocation before any battle begins.

ramacharitamanas::3747.verse_sanskrit: हम छत्री मृगया बन करहीं। तुम्ह से खल मृग खोजत फिरहीं॥ रिपु बलवंत देखि नहिं डरहीं। एक बार कालहु सन लरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3747.verse_hindi: हम क्षत्रिय हैं, वन में शिकार करते हैं और तुम्हारे सरीखे दुष्ट पशुओं को तो ढ़ूँढते ही फिरते हैं। हम बलवान् शत्रु देखकर नहीं डरते। (लड़ने को आवे तो) एक बार तो हम काल से भी लड़ सकते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3747.english_translation: We are warriors who hunt in the forest. We keep searching for wicked beasts like you. Seeing a strong enemy does not frighten us. If needed, we can even fight Death itself.
ramacharitamanas::3747.translation_literal: हम (we) / छत्री (warriors) / मृगया (hunting) / बन (forest) / करहीं (do) / तुम्ह (you) / से (like) / खल (wicked) / मृग (beasts) / खोजत (searching) / फिरहीं (keep roaming) / रिपु (enemy) / बलवंत (powerful) / देखि (seeing) / नहिं (not) / डरहीं (fear) / एक बार (once) / कालहु (even Death) / सन (with) / लरहीं (fight)
ramacharitamanas::3747.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3747.essence: Real courage stands firm even before death.
ramacharitamanas::3747.simple_meaning: Lakshman answers with fierce confidence: he and Ram are not afraid of powerful enemies and are ready for battle.
ramacharitamanas::3747.simple_insight: Courage is not the absence of danger; it is refusing to shrink before it.
ramacharitamanas::3747.detailed_meaning: In the forest, after the demon's taunts and threats, Lakshman answers with a warrior's pride. He refuses intimidation, declares his readiness for battle, and shows that Ram's camp does not back away from danger.
ramacharitamanas::3747.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, trying to make you look small. You don't have to match their volume, but you also don't have to fold.
ramacharitamanas::3747.insight: It strengthens the mind to face threat without flinching or self-doubt.

ramacharitamanas::3748.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि मनुज दनुज कुल घालक। मुनि पालक खल सालक बालक॥ जौं न होइ बल घर फिरि जाहू। समर बिमुख मैं हतउँ न काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3748.verse_hindi: यद्यपि हम मनुष्य हैं, परन्तु दैत्यकुल का नाश करने वाले और मुनियों की रक्षा करने वाले हैं, हम बालक हैं, परन्तु दुष्टों को दण्ड देने वाले। यदि बल न हो तो घर लौट जाओ। संग्राम में पीठ दिखाने वाले किसी को मैं नहीं मारता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3748.english_translation: Although we are human, we destroy the race of demons and protect the sages. Though we are boys, we punish the wicked. If you lack strength, go back home. I do not strike anyone who turns away from battle.
ramacharitamanas::3748.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / मनुज (human) / दनुज कुल (demon race) / घालक (destroyer) / मुनि पालक (protector of sages) / खल सालक (punisher of the wicked) / बालक (boy) / जौं (if) / न होइ (there is not) / बल (strength) / घर फिरि जाहू (go back home) / समर (battle) / बिमुख (turning away) / मैं (I) / हतउँ (strike) / न (not) / काहू (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::3748.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3748.essence: Strength protects the good and refuses to chase the fleeing.
ramacharitamanas::3748.simple_meaning: Ram says his side exists to protect sages and defeat evil. He challenges the enemy to leave if they cannot fight with strength.
ramacharitamanas::3748.simple_insight: Real courage does not beg for approval; it simply asks you to face the moment honestly.
ramacharitamanas::3748.detailed_meaning: In the forest confrontation after the demons are challenged, Ram answers with calm authority. He defines his role clearly: protect the righteous, punish the wicked, and never strike someone who runs from battle. The verse sharpens the conflict before the fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::3748.modern_relevance: A tense argument is already turning into a fight, and someone starts bluffing instead of speaking plainly. This verse cuts through the performance: either stand by what you came for, or step away.
ramacharitamanas::3748.insight: It shifts the mind from posturing to honest action under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3749.verse_sanskrit: रन चढ़ि करिअ कपट चतुराई। रिपु पर कृपा परम कदराई॥ दूतन्ह जाइ तुरत सब कहेऊ। सुनि खर दूषन उर अति दहेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3749.verse_hindi: रण में चढ़ आकर कपट-चतुराई करना और शत्रु पर कृपा करना (दया दिखाना) तो बड़ी भारी कायरता है। दूतों ने लौटकर तुरंत सब बातें कहीं, जिन्हें सुनकर खर-दूषण का हृदय अत्यंत जल उठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3749.english_translation: Charging into battle and then using deceitful cleverness, or showing mercy to an enemy, is great cowardice. The messengers quickly reported everything, and hearing it, Khara and Dushana burned with anger.
ramacharitamanas::3749.translation_literal: रन (battle) / चढ़ि (having mounted) / करिअ (to do) / कपट (deceit) / चतुराई (cleverness) / रिपु (enemy) / पर (upon) / कृपा (mercy) / परम (extreme) / कदराई (cowardice) / दूतन्ह (by the messengers) / जाइ (going) / तुरत (immediately) / सब (all) / कहेऊ (was told) / सुनि (hearing) / खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / उर (heart) / अति (greatly) / दहेऊ (burned)
ramacharitamanas::3749.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3749.essence: Deceit and false softness have no place once battle has begun.
ramacharitamanas::3749.simple_meaning: In battle, false cleverness and mercy toward an enemy are called cowardice. The messengers return at once, and Khara and Dushana burn with rage.
ramacharitamanas::3749.simple_insight: Some moments call for clarity, not softness or trickery.
ramacharitamanas::3749.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the messengers have just returned from meeting Ram and Lakshman. They report their fearless words to Khara and Dushana. This verse is part of the rising tension before the fight, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::3749.modern_relevance: You replay a tense text thread and realize the other person has already taken your hesitation as weakness. The moment has moved past diplomacy.
ramacharitamanas::3749.insight: It marks the shift from warning to confrontation, where delay only hardens the conflict.

ramacharitamanas::3750.verse_sanskrit: उर दहेउ कहेउ कि धरहु धाए बिकट भट रजनीचरा। सर चाप तोमर सक्ति सूल कृपान परिघ परसु धरा॥ प्रभु कीन्हि धनुष टकोर प्रथम कठोर घोर भयावहा। भए बधिर ब्याकुल जातुधान न ग्यान तेहि अवसर रहा॥
ramacharitamanas::3750.verse_hindi: (खर-दूषण का) हृदय जल उठा। तब उन्होंने कहा- पकड़ लो (कैद कर लो)। (यह सुनकर) भयानक राक्षस योद्धा बाण, धनुष, तोमर, शक्ति (साँग), शूल (बरछी), कृपाण (कटार), परिघ और फरसा धारण किए हुए दौड़ पड़े। प्रभु श्री रामजी ने पहले धनुष का बड़ा कठोर, घोर और भयानक टंकार किया, जिसे सुनकर राक्षस बहरे और व्याकुल हो गए। उस समय उन्हें कुछ भी होश न रहा।
ramacharitamanas::3750.english_translation: Their hearts burned. Then they shouted, "Seize him!" Fierce night-roaming warriors rushed forward with arrows, bows, tomars, spears, daggers, iron clubs, and axes in hand. Lord Ram struck his bow first with a hard, terrible, fearsome twang. The demons became deaf and bewildered, and at that moment they lost all sense.
ramacharitamanas::3750.translation_literal: उर (heart) / दहेउ (burned) / कहेउ (said) / कि (that) / धरहु (seize) / धाए (rushed) / बिकट (fierce) / भट (warriors) / रजनीचरा (night-roamers) / सर (arrows) / चाप (bows) / तोमर (tomars) / सक्ति (spears) / सूल (spikes) / कृपान (daggers) / परिघ (iron clubs) / परसु (axes) / धरा (held) / प्रभु (Lord) / कीन्हि (made) / धनुष (bow) / टकोर (struck/twang) / प्रथम (first) / कठोर (hard) / घोर (terrible) / भयावहा (fearsome) / भए (became) / बधिर (deaf) / ब्याकुल (bewildered) / जातुधान (demons) / न (not) / ग्यान (sense) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / रहा (remained)
ramacharitamanas::3750.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3750.essence: Presence can shake aggression before the first arrow flies.
ramacharitamanas::3750.simple_meaning: The enemy rushes in armed for attack, and Ram answers first with the sound of his bow. That single strike overwhelms them before the fight even fully begins.
ramacharitamanas::3750.simple_insight: Some victories begin by unsettling the other side before a blow is exchanged.
ramacharitamanas::3750.detailed_meaning: In the forest battle against Khara and Dushan, the night-roaming warriors charge with every weapon they have. Ram answers not with panic, but with one terrifying twang of his bow. The sound itself breaks their composure, and the clash begins with their confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3750.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room where everyone expects you to flinch. Instead, you speak once, clearly and firmly, and the whole mood shifts before the argument starts.
ramacharitamanas::3750.insight: It shifts attention from brute force to presence: composure can disarm aggression before direct conflict escalates.

ramacharitamanas::3751.verse_sanskrit: सावधान होइ धाए जानि सबल आराति। लागे बरषन राम पर अस्त्र सस्त्र बहुभाँति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3751.verse_hindi: फिर वे शत्रु को बलवान् जानकर सावधान होकर दौड़े और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के ऊपर बहुत प्रकार के अस्त्र-शस्त्र बरसाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3751.english_translation: Then, knowing Ram was strong, they became alert and rushed forward, hurling many kinds of weapons at Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3751.translation_literal: सावधान (alert) / होइ (having become) / धाए (rushed) / जानि (knowing) / सबल (strong) / आराति (the enemy) / लागे (they began) / बरषन (to rain down) / राम पर (on Ram) / अस्त्र सस्त्र (weapons and missiles) / बहुभाँति (in many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::3751.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3751.essence: Recognising strength, the enemy attacks harder.
ramacharitamanas::3751.simple_meaning: The enemy warriors, seeing Ram's strength, rushed in alert and attacked him with many kinds of weapons.
ramacharitamanas::3751.simple_insight: Pressure often reveals fear: once strength is clear, opposition becomes frantic.
ramacharitamanas::3751.detailed_meaning: In the battle against Khara and Dushana, their warriors realise Ram is no ordinary opponent. They rush forward in alarm and shower him with weapons, setting up the next exchange of force.
ramacharitamanas::3751.modern_relevance: A room turns tense the moment one person stops bluffing and stands firm. The noise that follows is often just panic wearing armour.
ramacharitamanas::3751.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to motion: this is a combat beat, not a teaching verse.

ramacharitamanas::3752.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह के आयुध तिल सम करि काटे रघुबीर। तानि सरासन श्रवन लगि पुनि छाँड़े निज तीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3752.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीरजी ने उनके हथियारों को तिल के समान (टुकड़े-टुकड़े) करके काट डाला। फिर धनुष को कान तक तानकर अपने तीर छोड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3752.english_translation: Raghubir cut their weapons into tiny pieces. Then he drew his bow to his ear and released his own arrows.
ramacharitamanas::3752.translation_literal: तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / आयुध (weapons) / तिल सम (like sesame seeds) / करि (making) / काटे (cut) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / तानि (drawing) / सरासन (the bow) / श्रवन लगि (up to the ear) / पुनि (again) / छाँड़े (released) / निज (his own) / तीर (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::3752.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3752.essence: True strength meets aggression without losing control.
ramacharitamanas::3752.simple_meaning: Rama quickly destroys the enemy's weapons and then answers with his own arrows.
ramacharitamanas::3752.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response is calm, precise force — not panic.
ramacharitamanas::3752.detailed_meaning: The forest battle has already begun. Khara and Dushana's warriors rush in and rain weapons on Rama. In this moment, Rama effortlessly shatters their arms and answers with disciplined archery, showing his overwhelming skill before the clash intensifies.
ramacharitamanas::3752.modern_relevance: A heated argument lands in your lap, and you do not freeze. You cut through the confusion, answer clearly, and keep control of your response.
ramacharitamanas::3752.insight: It shifts attention from being attacked to responding with skill and precision.

ramacharitamanas::3753.verse_sanskrit: तब चले बान कराल। फुंकरत जनु बहु ब्याल॥ कोपेउ समर श्रीराम। चले बिसिख निसित निकाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3753.verse_hindi: तब भयानक बाण ऐसे चले, मानो फुफकारते हुए बहुत से सर्प जा रहे हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी संग्राम में क्रुद्ध हुए और अत्यन्त तीक्ष्ण बाण चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3753.english_translation: Then terrible arrows flew, like many hissing serpents. Shri Ram grew fierce in battle and sent out razor-sharp arrows.
