ramacharitamanas::3753.translation_literal: तब (then) / चले (flew) / बान (arrows) / कराल (terrible) / फुंकरत (hissing) / जनु (as if) / बहु (many) / ब्याल (serpents) ॥ / कोपेउ (became fierce) / समर (battle) / श्रीराम (Shri Ram) / चले (sent forth) / बिसिख (arrows) / निसित (sharp) / निकाम (extremely) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3753.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3753.essence: The clash turns fiercer as Ram answers force with force.
ramacharitamanas::3753.simple_meaning: Terrible arrows flew like hissing snakes, and Ram answered the attack with fierce, razor-sharp arrows of his own.
ramacharitamanas::3753.simple_insight: Some moments call for strength, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3753.detailed_meaning: In the forest battle, Khara, Dushana, and Trishira press their attack on Ram. Their weapons fly like serpents, and Ram finally responds with fierce force. The verse heightens the combat before the enemies begin to break.
ramacharitamanas::3753.insight: It shows battle pressure rising into direct counterattack, not reflection or teaching.

ramacharitamanas::3754.verse_sanskrit: अवलोकि खरतर तीर। मुरि चले निसिचर बीर॥ भए क्रुद्ध तीनिउ भाइ। जो भागि रन ते जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3754.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त तीक्ष्ण बाणों को देखकर राक्षस वीर पीठ दिखाकर भाग चले। तब खर-दूषण और त्रिशिरा तीनों भाई क्रुद्ध होकर बोले- जो रण से भागकर जाएगा, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3754.english_translation: Seeing the fierce arrows, the demon warriors turned back and fled. Then the three brothers grew angry and said, 'Whoever runs from the battlefield...'
ramacharitamanas::3754.translation_literal: अवलोकि (seeing) / खरतर (very fierce) / तीर (arrows) / मुरि (turning back) / चले (went, fled) / निसिचर (night-dwellers, demons) / बीर (warriors) / भए (became) / क्रुद्ध (angry) / तीनिउ (all three) / भाइ (brothers) / जो (whoever) / भागि (fleeing) / रन (battlefield) / ते (from) / जाइ (goes)
ramacharitamanas::3754.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3754.essence: Pride lashes out when fear makes retreat unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::3754.simple_meaning: The demon warriors see Ram's deadly arrows and run away. Their three leaders get angry and vow that no one should flee the battle.
ramacharitamanas::3754.simple_insight: Fear can expose pride fast, and pride often answers fear with anger.
ramacharitamanas::3754.detailed_meaning: In the forest battle, Ram has already shattered the demons' weapons. Now his arrows drive their warriors back. Seeing this retreat, the three brothers—Khara, Dushana, and Trishira—burn with rage and try to force the army to stand its ground.
ramacharitamanas::3754.modern_relevance: A team meeting collapses after one hard question, and the loudest person in the room snaps at everyone for backing down. Panic often wears the mask of anger.
ramacharitamanas::3754.insight: It shows how wounded ego reacts when it cannot control the field.

ramacharitamanas::3755.verse_sanskrit: तेहि बधब हम निज पानि। फिरे मरन मन महुँ ठानि॥ आयुध अनेक प्रकार। सनमुख ते करहिं प्रहार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3755.verse_hindi: उसका हम अपने हाथों वध करेंगे। तब मन में मरना ठानकर भागते हुए राक्षस लौट पड़े और सामने होकर वे अनेकों प्रकार के हथियारों से श्री रामजी पर प्रहार करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3755.english_translation: We will kill him with our own hands. Then, resolved to die, the fleeing demons turned back and attacked him from the front with many kinds of weapons.
ramacharitamanas::3755.translation_literal: तेहि (him) / बधब (we will kill) / हम (we) / निज (own) / पानि (hands) / फिरे (turned back) / मरन (death) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / ठानि (having resolved) / आयुध (weapons) / अनेक प्रकार (many kinds) / सनमुख (facing front) / ते (from them) / करहिं (they do) / प्रहार (attack)
ramacharitamanas::3755.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3755.essence: Pride makes retreat look like courage.
ramacharitamanas::3755.simple_meaning: The demons, determined to die or kill, turn back and attack Ram head-on with every weapon they have.
ramacharitamanas::3755.simple_insight: Pride can make fear look like courage, but it only drives you toward ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3755.detailed_meaning: In the forest battle, Khara, Dooshana, and Trishira have already seen Ram's force. Instead of yielding, they harden themselves and rush back to fight face-to-face, using every weapon they can.
ramacharitamanas::3755.modern_relevance: A person knows the argument is already lost, but pride keeps them typing longer, sharper messages. They come back swinging, even though the damage is already clear.
ramacharitamanas::3755.insight: It shows how ego can turn retreat into reckless aggression.

ramacharitamanas::3756.verse_sanskrit: रिपु परम कोपे जानि। प्रभु धनुष सर संधानि॥ छाँड़े बिपुल नाराच। लगे कटन बिकट पिसाच ॥
ramacharitamanas::3756.verse_hindi: शत्रु को अत्यन्त कुपित जानकर प्रभु ने धनुष पर बाण चढ़ाकर बहुत से बाण छोड़े, जिनसे भयानक राक्षस कटने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3756.english_translation: Seeing the enemy furious, the Lord drew his bow and released many arrows, and the terrible demons began to fall apart.
ramacharitamanas::3756.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / परम (greatly) / कोपे (angry) / जानि (knowing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / धनुष (bow) / सर (arrow) / संधानि (having nocked) / छाँड़े (released) / बिपुल (many) / नाराच (arrows) / लगे (began) / कटन (to be cut down) / बिकट (terrible) / पिसाच (demons)
ramacharitamanas::3756.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3756.essence: Clear force meets fury without losing control.
ramacharitamanas::3756.simple_meaning: Ram sees the enemy's rage, nocks his bow, and sends out many arrows. The demons are cut down in battle.
ramacharitamanas::3756.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response to fury is calm, precise force.
ramacharitamanas::3756.detailed_meaning: In the Aranyakand battle, Khara, Dushan, and Trishira have rushed back in anger after earlier being driven away. Seeing their fury, Ram calmly draws his bow and unleashes a shower of arrows that begins breaking their assault.
ramacharitamanas::3756.modern_relevance: A tense meeting turns hostile, voices rise, and everyone expects you to match the heat. Instead, you stay clear, prepare your response, and answer with exactness.
ramacharitamanas::3756.insight: It shifts you from reactive anger to disciplined, targeted action.

ramacharitamanas::3757.verse_sanskrit: उर सीस भुज कर चरन। जहँ तहँ लगे महि परन॥ चिक्करत लागत बान। धर परत कुधर समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3757.verse_hindi: उनकी छाती, सिर, भुजा, हाथ और पैर जहाँ-तहाँ पृथ्वी पर गिरने लगे। बाण लगते ही वे हाथी की तरह चिंग्घाड़ते हैं। उनके पहाड़ के समान धड़ कट-कटकर गिर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3757.english_translation: Their chests, heads, arms, hands, and feet fell here and there upon the earth. Hit by arrows, they roared like elephants, and their mountain-like trunks kept crashing down.
ramacharitamanas::3757.translation_literal: उर (chest) / सीस (head) / भुज (arms) / कर (hands) / चरन (feet) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / लगे (fell) / महि परन (upon the earth) ॥ / चिक्करत (roaring) / लागत (struck) / बान (arrows) / धर (body/trunk) / परत (falling) / कुधर (mountain) / समान (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3757.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3757.essence: The attack is so fierce that bodies fall apart on impact.
ramacharitamanas::3757.simple_meaning: Arrows tear the demons apart, and their limbs and bodies fall across the ground.
ramacharitamanas::3757.simple_insight: Violence here is total and relentless; there is no room left for pride or resistance.
ramacharitamanas::3757.detailed_meaning: In the forest battle, Rama's arrows are cutting down the attacking demons. This verse lingers on the collapse of their bodies, showing the force of the assault rather than offering a teaching. It is part of the action, not a separate reflection.
ramacharitamanas::3757.modern_relevance: A crisis can leave everything in pieces before you can even make sense of it. Sometimes the moment is just impact, not meaning.
ramacharitamanas::3757.insight: It keeps the reader inside the momentum of the fight, not in commentary about it.

ramacharitamanas::3758.verse_sanskrit: भट कटत तन सत खंड। पुनि उठत करि पाषंड॥ नभ उड़त बहु भुज मुंड। बिनु मौलि धावत रुंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::3758.verse_hindi: योद्धाओं के शरीर कटकर सैकड़ों टुकड़े हो जाते हैं। वे फिर माया करके उठ खड़े होते हैं। आकाश में बहुत सी भुजाएँ और सिर उड़ रहे हैं तथा बिना सिर के धड़ दौड़ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3758.english_translation: Warriors are cut into hundreds of pieces, then rise again through illusion. Many arms and heads fly through the sky, and headless trunks run on.
ramacharitamanas::3758.translation_literal: भट (warriors) / कटत (being cut) / तन (body) / सत खंड (hundred pieces) / पुनि (again) / उठत (rising) / करि (doing) / पाषंड (illusion) / नभ (sky) / उड़त (flying) / बहु (many) / भुज (arms) / मुंड (heads) / बिनु (without) / मौलि (head) / धावत (running) / रुंड (trunk)
ramacharitamanas::3758.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3758.essence: Violence here multiplies itself into nightmare, not triumph.
ramacharitamanas::3758.simple_meaning: Bodies are sliced apart, but the fighters keep rising in a terrifying display of magical power. The sky fills with severed limbs and heads, and headless bodies keep charging.
ramacharitamanas::3758.simple_insight: The scene shows how violence can become grotesque and endless, with no clean victory in sight.
ramacharitamanas::3758.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram’s arrows are tearing through the enemy ranks. Even after being cut apart, the warriors seem to rise again by deceptive power, turning the fight into a horrifying spectacle of flying limbs and headless bodies.
ramacharitamanas::3758.modern_relevance: A conflict that should have ended keeps escalating, and every response seems to spawn a worse one. What began as a problem now feels like a nightmare that feeds on itself.
ramacharitamanas::3758.insight: It shifts the mind from heroic combat to the horror of destructive force that refuses to end.

ramacharitamanas::3759.verse_sanskrit: खग कंक काक सृगाल। कटकटहिं कठिन कराल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3759.verse_hindi: चील (या क्रौंच), कौए आदि पक्षी और सियार कठोर और भयंकर कट-कट शब्द कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3759.english_translation: Crows, hawks, and jackals were making harsh, dreadful clicking sounds.
ramacharitamanas::3759.translation_literal: खग (birds) / कंक (hawks or herons) / काक (crows) / सृगाल (jackals) / कटकटहिं (are clattering) / कठिन (harsh) / कराल (dreadful)
ramacharitamanas::3759.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3759.essence: Even the forest seems to shudder at the violence.
ramacharitamanas::3759.simple_meaning: Birds and jackals are making harsh, ominous noises as the battle rages around them.
ramacharitamanas::3759.simple_insight: The scene feels cursed and violent, with nature itself sounding alarmed.
ramacharitamanas::3759.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the forest battle, bodies are being shattered and the air is thick with terror. This line adds an ominous soundscape: crows, hawks, and jackals cry out as if the whole place is recoiling from the violence.
ramacharitamanas::3759.modern_relevance: You walk past a street after a crash, and even the silence feels disturbed. Some moments are so violent that the whole atmosphere seems to flinch.
ramacharitamanas::3759.insight: It sharpens the battlefield into a full sensory scene, showing how violence infects even the environment.

ramacharitamanas::3760.verse_sanskrit: कटकटहिं जंबुक भूत प्रेत पिसाच खर्पर संचहीं। बेताल बीर कपाल ताल बजाइ जोगिनि नंचहीं॥ रघुबीर बान प्रचंड खंडहिं भटन्ह के उर भुज सिरा। जहँ तहँ परहिं उठि लरहिं धर धरु धरु करहिं भयंकर गिरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3760.verse_hindi: सियार कटकटाते हैं, भूत, प्रेत और पिशाच खोपड़ियाँ बटोर रहे हैं (अथवा खप्पर भर रहे हैं)। वीर-वैताल खोपड़ियों पर ताल दे रहे हैं और योगिनियाँ नाच रही हैं। श्री रघुवीर के प्रचंड बाण योद्धाओं के वक्षःस्थल, भुजा और सिरों के टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर डालते हैं। उनके धड़ जहाँ-तहाँ गिर पड़ते हैं, फिर उठते और लड़ते हैं और 'पकड़ो-पकड़ो' का भयंकर शब्द करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3760.english_translation: Jackals, ghosts, wandering spirits, and goblins gather skulls. Fierce spirits beat skulls like drums, and witch-like beings dance. Lord Raghubir's fierce arrows cut warriors' chests, arms, and heads apart. Their bodies fall, rise again, and fight, shouting in terrible voices.
ramacharitamanas::3760.translation_literal: कटकटहिं (click and clack) / जंबुक (jackals) / भूत (spirits) / प्रेत (wandering spirits) / पिसाच (goblins) / खर्पर (skulls) / संचहीं (gather) / बेताल (fierce spirits) / बीर (warrior-like) / कपाल (skulls) / ताल (rhythm) / बजाइ (beating) / जोगिनि (witch-like beings) / नंचहीं (dance) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बान (arrows) / प्रचंड (fierce) / खंडहिं (cut apart) / भटन्ह (warriors) / के (of) / उर (chests) / भुज (arms) / सिरा (heads) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / परहिं (fall) / उठि (rising) / लरहिं (fight) / धर धरु (catch, catch) / करहिं (make) / भयंकर (terrible) / गिरा (voices)
ramacharitamanas::3760.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3760.essence: The battlefield has become a nightmare of endless, savage motion.
ramacharitamanas::3760.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so savage that it feels haunted. Arrows tear warriors apart, yet the fighting continues as bodies fall, rise, and clash again.
ramacharitamanas::3760.simple_insight: Some conflicts become so violent that they stop feeling human at all.
ramacharitamanas::3760.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the battlefield has turned grotesque and uncanny. Tulsidas piles image upon image to show the terror of combat: bodies split apart, strange beings gathering around the dead, and warriors still rising to fight. It is vivid war narration, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::3760.insight: It shows the war as chaos beyond ordinary description, with violence and horror overtaking the scene.

ramacharitamanas::3761.verse_sanskrit: अंतावरीं गहि उड़त गीध पिसाच कर गहि धावहीं। संग्राम पुर बासी मनहुँ बहु बाल गुड़ी उड़ावहीं॥ मारे पछारे उर बिदारे बिपुल भट कहँरत परे। अवलोकि निज दल बिकल भट तिसिरादि खर दूषन फिरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3761.verse_hindi: अंतड़ियों के एक छोर को पकड़कर गीध उड़ते हैं और उन्हीं का दूसरा छोर हाथ से पकड़कर पिशाच दौड़ते हैं, ऐसा मालूम होता है मानो संग्राम रूपी नगर के निवासी बहुत से बालक पतंग उड़ा रहे हों। अनेकों योद्धा मारे और पछाड़े गए बहुत से, जिनके हृदय विदीर्ण हो गए हैं, पड़े कराह रहे हैं। अपनी सेना को व्याकुल देखर त्रिशिरा और खर-दूषण आदि योद्धा श्री रामजी की ओर मुड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3761.english_translation: Ghouls and vultures clutch the intestines and fly, while other demons run with the other end in hand, as if the people of the battlefield city were flying kites. Many warriors are struck down, thrown down, and pierced through the chest, lying groaning. Seeing their own army in confusion, Trishira, Khara, and Dushana turn toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3761.translation_literal: अंतावरीं (the inner ends) / गहि (grasping) / उड़त (flying) / गीध (vultures) / पिसाच (ghouls) / कर (with hands) / गहि (grasping) / धावहीं (run) / संग्राम (battle) / पुर (city) / बासी (inhabitants) / मनहुँ (as if) / बहु (many) / बाल (children) / गुड़ी (kites) / उड़ावहीं (fly) / मारे (struck) / पछारे (thrown down) / उर (chest) / बिदारे (pierced) / बिपुल (many) / भट (warriors) / कहँरत (groaning) / परे (fallen) / अवलोकि (seeing) / निज (their own) / दल (army) / बिकल (disturbed) / भट (warriors) / तिसिरादि (Trishira and others) / खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / फिरे (turned)
ramacharitamanas::3761.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3761.essence: Panic in one army forces its leaders to face Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3761.simple_meaning: The battlefield has become a scene of chaos and slaughter. Seeing their army break apart, Trishira, Khara, and Dushana turn toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3761.simple_insight: Violence spreads confusion fast, and even proud fighters are forced to face what is stronger than them.
ramacharitamanas::3761.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the fight against the forest demons has turned savage. Bodies fall, the air fills with terror, and the enemy ranks lose control. Watching their side collapse, Trishira, Khara, and Dushana finally turn toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3761.modern_relevance: A group chat has turned into a pile-on, and the loudest voices suddenly go quiet when the facts land. Chaos can look powerful for a moment, but it always reveals who still stands.
ramacharitamanas::3761.insight: It shifts attention from battlefield spectacle to the collapse of ego under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3762.verse_sanskrit: सरसक्ति तोमर परसु सूल कृपान एकहि बारहीं। करि कोप श्री रघुबीर पर अगनित निसाचर डारहीं॥ प्रभु निमिष महुँ रिपु सर निवारि पचारि डारे सायका। दस दस बिसिख उर माझ मारे सकल निसिचर नायका ॥
ramacharitamanas::3762.verse_hindi: अनगिनत राक्षस क्रोध करके बाण, शक्ति, तोमर, फरसा, शूल और कृपाण एक ही बार में श्री रघुवीर पर छोड़ने लगे। प्रभु ने पल भर में शत्रुओं के बाणों को काटकर, ललकारकर उन पर अपने बाण छोड़े। सब राक्षस सेनापतियों के हृदय में दस-दस बाण मारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3762.english_translation: Countless demons, in rage, hurled arrows, shaktis, toors, axes, spears, and swords at Shri Raghubir all at once. In a moment, the Lord cut down the enemy arrows, charged forward, and loosed his own arrows. He struck ten arrows into the hearts of all the demon commanders.
ramacharitamanas::3762.translation_literal: सरसक्ति (with shaktis) / तोमर (toors) / परसु (axes) / सूल (spears) / कृपान (swords) / एकहि बारहीं (all at once) / करि कोप (in anger) / श्री रघुबीर (Shri Raghubir) पर (upon) / अगनित (countless) / निसाचर (demons) / डारहीं (hurled) / प्रभु (the Lord) / निमिष महुँ (in a moment) / रिपु (enemy) / सर (arrows) / निवारि (cutting off) / पचारि (charging) / डारे (sent) / सायका (arrows) / दस दस (ten each) / बिसिख (arrows) / उर माझ (into the heart) / मारे (struck) / सकल (all) / निसिचर (demons) / नायका (chiefs)
ramacharitamanas::3762.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3762.simple_meaning: The demons attack in a furious shower of weapons, and Ram instantly cuts through them and answers with his own arrows.
ramacharitamanas::3762.simple_insight: Raw force meets calm mastery, and panic loses to precision.
ramacharitamanas::3762.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has fully opened. Demon commanders hurl every weapon they have at Ram, hoping sheer violence will overwhelm him. Instead, he meets the attack in a single instant, breaks it apart, and strikes their leaders down.
ramacharitamanas::3762.modern_relevance: A meeting turns hostile and everyone starts talking over each other. You stay steady, hear the real issue, and answer only what matters.
ramacharitamanas::3762.insight: It shows how composure and skill can cut through chaos faster than aggression can spread it.

ramacharitamanas::3763.verse_sanskrit: महि परत उठि भट भिरत मरत न करत माया अति घनी। सुर डरत चौदह सहस प्रेत बिलोकि एक अवध धनी॥ सुर मुनि सभय प्रभु देखि मायानाथ अति कौतुक कर् यो। देखहिं परसपर राम करि संग्राम रिपु दल लरि मर् यो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3763.verse_hindi: योद्धा पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ते हैं, फिर उठकर भिड़ते हैं। मरते नहीं, बहुत प्रकार की अतिशय माया रचते हैं। देवता यह देखकर डरते हैं कि प्रेत (राक्षस) चौदह हजार हैं और अयोध्यानाथ श्री रामजी अकेले हैं। देवता और मुनियों को भयभीत देखकर माया के स्वामी प्रभु ने एक बड़ा कौतुक किया, जिससे शत्रुओं की सेना एक-दूसरे को राम रूप देखने लगी और आपस में ही युद्ध करके लड़ मरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3763.english_translation: Warriors fell to the ground, got up, and fought again. They did not die; they created many kinds of illusions. The gods grew afraid seeing fourteen thousand spirits against the lone Lord of Ayodhya. Seeing the gods and sages afraid, the Lord of illusion made a wondrous display: the enemy army began seeing Ram in one another and destroyed itself in battle.
ramacharitamanas::3763.translation_literal: महि (on the ground) / परत (falling) / उठि (rising) / भट (warriors) / भिरत (fighting) / मरत (dying) / न (not) / करत (doing) / माया (illusion) / अति घनी (very dense) / सुर (gods) / डरत (afraid) / चौदह सहस (fourteen thousand) / प्रेत (spirits) / बिलोकि (seeing) / एक (one) / अवध धनी (Lord of Ayodhya) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / सभय (fearful) / प्रभु (Lord) / देखि (seeing) / मायानाथ (master of illusion) / अति कौतुक (great wonder) / कर्यो (did) / देखहिं (they see) / परसपर (one another) / राम करि (as Ram) / संग्राम (battle) / रिपु दल (enemy army) / लरि (fighting) / मर्यो (died)
ramacharitamanas::3763.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3763.essence: Illusion can make an army destroy itself.
ramacharitamanas::3763.simple_meaning: The battle turns into a strange illusion. Ram's enemies see one another as Ram and end up destroying themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3763.simple_insight: Even chaos can be turned back on itself when higher power is at work.
ramacharitamanas::3763.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram faces an overwhelming army of demons. The battlefield becomes a place of illusion, fear, and supernatural force. The verse shows Ram's power making the enemy collapse into confusion, while gods and sages watch in awe.
ramacharitamanas::3763.modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a pile-on, and everyone starts reacting to their own projections. What looked like one threat becomes self-destruction once confusion takes over.
ramacharitamanas::3763.insight: It shows how delusion can make conflict collapse from within.

ramacharitamanas::3764.verse_sanskrit: राम राम कहि तनु तजहिं पावहिं पद निर्बान। करि उपाय रिपु मारे छन महुँ कृपानिधान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3764.verse_hindi: सब ('यही राम है, इसे मारो' इस प्रकार) राम-राम कहकर शरीर छोड़ते हैं और निर्वाण (मोक्ष) पद पाते हैं। कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने यह उपाय करके क्षण भर में शत्रुओं को मार डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3764.english_translation: Saying "Ram, Ram," they leave their bodies and attain the state of freedom. The compassionate Lord used this means and, in a moment, destroyed the enemies.
ramacharitamanas::3764.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / कहि (saying) / तनु (body) / तजहिं (leave) / पावहिं (attain) / पद (state) / निर्बान (freedom) / करि (having done) / उपाय (means) / रिपु (enemies) / मारे (killed) / छन (moment) / महुँ (in) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::3764.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3764.essence: Ram's name turns even death into release.
ramacharitamanas::3764.simple_meaning: Even enemies can be freed by remembering Ram. His compassion ends violence quickly and turns death into liberation.
ramacharitamanas::3764.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that even the darkest conflict can be touched by grace.
ramacharitamanas::3764.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle is raging and the demons are falling. Tulsidas pauses to say that even as they die, those who cry out Ram's name attain freedom. Ram acts as the merciful force that ends the war and lifts souls beyond it.
ramacharitamanas::3764.modern_relevance: A room full of anger can shift in one honest moment. Sometimes the same force that stops the harm also softens the heart of everyone caught inside it.
ramacharitamanas::3764.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing victory as destruction to seeing mercy as the highest victory.

ramacharitamanas::3765.verse_sanskrit: हरषित बरषहिं सुमन सुर बाजहिं गगन निसान। अस्तुति करि करि सब चले सोभित बिबिध बिमान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3765.verse_hindi: देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसाते हैं, आकाश में नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। फिर वे सब स्तुति कर-करके अनेकों विमानों पर सुशोभित हुए चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3765.english_translation: The radiant beings rejoice, shower flowers, and beat celestial drums in the sky. After praising again and again, they all depart in splendid flying chariots.
ramacharitamanas::3765.translation_literal: हरषित (rejoicing) / बरषहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (radiant beings) / बाजहिं (sound/beating) / गगन (sky) / निसान (drums) / अस्तुति (praise) / करि करि (having done repeatedly) / सब (all) / चले (departed) / सोभित (shining) / बिबिध (various) / बिमान (flying chariots)
ramacharitamanas::3765.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3765.essence: Righteous victory makes even the heavens rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::3765.simple_meaning: The radiant beings celebrate Ram's victory with flowers, drums, and praise before returning to their celestial homes.
ramacharitamanas::3765.simple_insight: Even the highest beings respond to righteous victory with joy and gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::3765.detailed_meaning: After the fierce battle scene, the radiant beings in the sky rejoice at Ram's success. They shower flowers, beat drums, praise him, and depart in their shining chariots. It is a celebratory bridge before the next moment of the story.
ramacharitamanas::3765.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after the hard presentation ends, and then the people who believed in you start clapping first. Some victories deserve witness, not just results.
ramacharitamanas::3765.insight: It shifts attention from combat to celebration, showing that rightful victory restores harmony beyond the battlefield.

ramacharitamanas::3766.verse_sanskrit: जब रघुनाथ समर रिपु जीते। सुर नर मुनि सब के भय बीते॥ तब लछिमन सीतहि लै आए। प्रभु पद परत हरषि उर लाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3766.verse_hindi: जब श्री रघुनाथजी ने युद्ध में शत्रुओं को जीत लिया तथा देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सबके भय नष्ट हो गए, तब लक्ष्मणजी सीताजी को ले आए। चरणों में पड़ते हुए उनको प्रभु ने प्रसन्नतापूर्वक उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3766.english_translation: When Raghunath defeated the enemy in battle and the fear of gods, humans, and sages had passed, Lakshman brought Sita back. As she fell at his feet, the Lord lifted her up joyfully and held her to his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3766.translation_literal: जब (when) रघुनाथ (Raghunath) समर (battle) रिपु (enemy) जीते (won) / सुर (radiant beings) नर (humans) मुनि (sages) सब (all) के (of) भय (fear) बीते (passed)॥ / तब (then) लछिमन (Lakshman) सीतहि (Sita) लै (taking) आए (brought)॥ / प्रभु (Lord) पद (feet) परत (falling) हरषि (joyfully) उर (heart) लाए (brought/held)॥
ramacharitamanas::3766.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3766.essence: Victory matters because it makes reunion possible.
ramacharitamanas::3766.simple_meaning: Ram defeats the enemies, fear leaves everyone, and Sita is brought back to him. He welcomes her with joy and embraces her at his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3766.simple_insight: Love returns after loss, and welcome matters as much as victory.
ramacharitamanas::3766.detailed_meaning: The battle has ended and Ravana's side is broken. Lakshman brings Sita back to Ram, and the reunion becomes the emotional reward of the war: fear is gone, justice has returned, and Ram receives her with open joy.
ramacharitamanas::3766.modern_relevance: After a long fight to fix what went wrong, you finally see the person you were trying to protect walk back through the door. The relief is bigger than the victory.
ramacharitamanas::3766.insight: It shifts attention from conquest itself to the restoration that conquest makes possible.

ramacharitamanas::3767.verse_sanskrit: सीता चितव स्याम मृदु गाता। परम प्रेम लोचन न अघाता॥ पंचबटीं बसि श्री रघुनायक। करत चरित सुर मुनि सुखदायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::3767.verse_hindi: सीताजी श्री रामजी के श्याम और कोमल शरीर को परम प्रेम के साथ देख रही हैं, नेत्र अघाते नहीं हैं। इस प्रकार पंचवटी में बसकर श्री रघुनाथजी देवताओं और मुनियों को सुख देने वाले चरित्र करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3767.english_translation: Sita gazes at Ram's dark, gentle form, and her eyes are never satisfied. Dwelling in Panchavati, Shri Raghunath begins the acts that delight the radiant beings and sages.
ramacharitamanas::3767.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / चितव (gazes) / स्याम (dark) / मृदु (gentle) / गाता (body) / परम (supreme) / प्रेम (love) / लोचन (eyes) / न (not) / अघाता (satisfied)॥ / पंचबटीं (in Panchavati) / बसि (dwelling) / श्री (revered) / रघुनायक (Lord of Raghu) / करत (doing) / चरित (deeds) / सुर (radiant beings) / मुनि (sages) / सुखदायक (giving joy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3767.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3767.essence: True love cannot look enough, and Ram's presence turns the forest holy.
ramacharitamanas::3767.simple_meaning: Sita cannot stop looking at Ram. After settling in Panchavati, Ram begins the deeds that bring joy to sages and radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::3767.simple_insight: Love keeps looking because it never feels finished.
ramacharitamanas::3767.detailed_meaning: In Panchavati, after the journey and reunion, Sita drinks in Ram's gentle form with eyes that cannot look away. The scene then widens: Ram settles into forest life and begins the deeds that make sages and radiant beings rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::3767.modern_relevance: You catch someone you love across a crowded room and forget everything else for a second. That steady looking is what devotion feels like before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::3767.insight: It shifts attention from possession to reverent seeing.

ramacharitamanas::3768.verse_sanskrit: धुआँ देखि खरदूषन केरा। जाइ सुपनखाँ रावन प्रेरा॥ बोली बचन क्रोध करि भारी। देस कोस कै सुरति बिसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3768.verse_hindi: खर-दूषण का विध्वंस देखकर शूर्पणखा ने जाकर रावण को भड़काया। वह बड़ा क्रोध करके वचन बोली- तूने देश और खजाने की सुधि ही भुला दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3768.english_translation: Seeing the destruction of Khara and Dushana, Shurpanakha went and provoked Ravana. Enraged, she said, "You have forgotten even your own land and treasury."
ramacharitamanas::3768.translation_literal: धुआँ (smoke) / देखि (seeing) / खरदूषन केरा (of Khara and Dushana) / जाइ (going) / सुपनखाँ (Shurpanakha) / रावन (Ravana) / प्रेरा (provoked) ॥ / बोली (spoke) / बचन (words) / क्रोध करि (with anger) / भारी (greatly) / देस (country/realm) / कोस (treasury) / कै (of) / सुरति (awareness) / बिसारी (forgot) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3768.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3768.essence: Anger makes a ruler forget what protects him.
ramacharitamanas::3768.simple_meaning: Shurpanakha sees her brothers destroyed and rushes to inflame Ravana with angry words, accusing him of neglecting his kingdom and wealth.
ramacharitamanas::3768.simple_insight: Anger can turn a loss into a larger disaster.
ramacharitamanas::3768.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Shurpanakha sees the smoke of Khara and Dushana's defeat and rushes to Ravana. Instead of warning him wisely, she stokes his rage and shame, setting the stage for his reckless response.
ramacharitamanas::3768.modern_relevance: You get one furious voice note after a bad day, and suddenly a small problem becomes a family war. Heat spreads faster than wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3768.insight: It shows how wounded pride can be weaponized, pushing someone already unstable toward worse choices.

ramacharitamanas::3769.verse_sanskrit: करसि पान सोवसि दिनु राती। सुधि नहिं तव सिर पर आराती॥ राज नीति बिनु धन बिनु धर्मा। हरिहि समर्पे बिनु सतकर्मा ॥ बिद्या बिनु बिबेक उपजाएँ। श्रम फल पढ़ें किएँ अरु पाएँ॥ संग तें जती कुमंत्र ते राजा। मान ते ग्यान पान तें लाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3769.verse_hindi: शराब पी लेता है और दिन-रात पड़ा सोता रहता है। तुझे खबर नहीं है कि शत्रु तेरे सिर पर खड़ा है? नीति के बिना राज्य और धर्म के बिना धन प्राप्त करने से, भगवान को समर्पण किए बिना उत्तम कर्म करने से और विवेक उत्पन्न किए बिना विद्या पढ़ने से परिणाम में श्रम ही हाथ लगता है। विषयों के संग से संन्यासी, बुरी सलाह से राजा, मान से ज्ञान, मदिरा पान से लज्जा,॥4-5॥
ramacharitamanas::3769.english_translation: You drink and sleep day and night. Do you not know that an enemy stands over your head? Without policy, a kingdom; without dharma, wealth; without offering yourself to the divine, good deeds; and without wisdom, study all end in wasted effort. From bad company, a renunciant falls; from bad counsel, a king; from pride, wisdom; from drink, shame.
ramacharitamanas::3769.translation_literal: करसि (you do) / पान (drinking) / सोवसि (you sleep) / दिनु राती (day and night) / सुधि (awareness) / नहिं (not) / तव (your) / सिर (head) / पर (upon) / आराती (enemy) / राज नीति (statecraft) / बिनु (without) / धन (wealth) / बिनु (without) / धर्मा (dharma) / हरिहि (to Hari) / समर्पे (offering) / बिनु (without) / सतकर्मा (good deeds) / बिद्या (learning) / बिनु (without) / बिबेक (discerning mind) / उपजाएँ (arises) / श्रम (effort) / फल (fruit) / पढ़ें (by studying) / किएँ (by doing) / अरु (and) / पाएँ (by obtaining) / संग (company) / तें (from) / जती (renunciant) / कुमंत्र (bad counsel) / ते (from) / राजा (king) / मान (pride) / ते (from) / ग्यान (wisdom) / पान (drinking) / तें (from) / लाजा (shame)
ramacharitamanas::3769.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3769.essence: Without wisdom and restraint, even success becomes waste.
ramacharitamanas::3769.simple_meaning: Blind habit, bad company, and pride ruin even noble efforts. Work, learning, wealth, and power only bear fruit when guided by wisdom and right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3769.simple_insight: It leaves you alert to what quietly corrupts your choices before you notice the damage.
ramacharitamanas::3769.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poet turns from scene to warning. Ravana’s world is already sliding toward ruin, and Tulsidas spells out the causes: sleep, intoxication, bad counsel, pride, and action without wisdom or surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3769.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling past midnight, telling yourself you will fix it tomorrow. But tiredness, bad inputs, and ego have already started shaping the day before it begins.
ramacharitamanas::3769.insight: It teaches you to check the quality of your mind, company, and motives before measuring results.

ramacharitamanas::3770.verse_sanskrit: प्रीति प्रनय बिनु मद ते गुनी। नासहिं बेगि नीति अस सुनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3770.verse_hindi: नम्रता के बिना (नम्रता न होने से) प्रीति और मद (अहंकार) से गुणवान शीघ्र ही नष्ट हो जाते हैं, इस प्रकार नीति मैंने सुनी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3770.english_translation: Without humility, even gifted people quickly perish through pride. This is the policy I have heard.
ramacharitamanas::3770.translation_literal: प्रीति (humility / affection) / प्रनय (affection, courtesy) / बिनु (without) / मद (pride) / ते (from) / गुनी (gifted people, the virtuous) / नासहिं (perish) / बेगि (quickly) / नीति (policy, practical wisdom) / अस (thus) / सुनी (heard)
ramacharitamanas::3770.speaker: Shurpanakha
ramacharitamanas::3770.essence: Talent collapses when pride replaces humility.
ramacharitamanas::3770.simple_meaning: Pride destroys even capable people. Humility is what keeps skill, goodness, and good judgment from collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::3770.simple_insight: You can be talented and still lose everything if ego starts steering.
ramacharitamanas::3770.detailed_meaning: After seeing the destruction of Khara and Dushana, Shurpanakha rushes to Ravana and warns him. She is trying to shame him into seeing his danger, saying that gifted people fall quickly when pride replaces humility.
ramacharitamanas::3770.modern_relevance: You get praised for one project, then start believing you’re untouchable. A few weeks later, the same overconfidence makes you careless, defensive, and easy to break.
ramacharitamanas::3770.insight: It shifts attention from raw ability to the attitude that either preserves or destroys it.

ramacharitamanas::3771.verse_sanskrit: रिपु रुज पावक पाप प्रभु अहि गनिअ न छोट करि। अस कहि बिबिध बिलाप करि लागी रोदन करन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3771.verse_hindi: शत्रु, रोग, अग्नि, पाप, स्वामी और सर्प को छोटा करके नहीं समझना चाहिए। ऐसा कहकर शूर्पणखा अनेक प्रकार से विलाप करके रोने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3771.english_translation: Never treat an enemy, disease, fire, sin, a ruler, or a serpent as small. Saying this, she wailed in many ways and began to cry.
ramacharitamanas::3771.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / रुज (disease) / पावक (fire) / पाप (sin) / प्रभु (master/ruler) / अहि (serpent) / गनिअ (should be counted) / न छोट करि (not as small) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / बिबिध (various) / बिलाप (lamentation) / करि (having done) / लागी (began) / रोदन (weeping) / करन (to do)
ramacharitamanas::3771.speaker: Surpanakha
ramacharitamanas::3771.essence: Small dangers become disasters when you refuse to respect them.
ramacharitamanas::3771.simple_meaning: Surpanakha warns that dangerous things should never be underestimated, then breaks into grief and tears.
ramacharitamanas::3771.simple_insight: Underestimating danger can turn a small mistake into a much larger wound.
ramacharitamanas::3771.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha has been wounded and humiliated after her reckless approach to Ram's camp. Before her full complaint reaches Ravana's court, she blurts out a hard warning: enemies, illness, fire, wrongdoing, rulers, and serpents are never small.
ramacharitamanas::3771.modern_relevance: You ignore a small warning sign in a relationship, a body ache, or a risky deal, and suddenly the damage is everywhere. She is naming the cost of contempt.
ramacharitamanas::3771.insight: It teaches you to respect danger early, before pride or carelessness turns it into crisis.

ramacharitamanas::3772.verse_sanskrit: सभा माझ परि ब्याकुल बहु प्रकार कह रोइ। तोहि जिअत दसकंधर मोरि कि असि गति होइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3772.verse_hindi: (रावण की) सभा के बीच वह व्याकुल होकर पड़ी हुई बहुत प्रकार से रो-रोकर कह रही है कि अरे दशग्रीव! तेरे जीते जी मेरी क्या ऐसी दशा होनी चाहिए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3772.english_translation: In the middle of the assembly, she lay there distraught, crying in many ways: 'While you live, O ten-headed one, how could such a fate be mine?'
ramacharitamanas::3772.translation_literal: सभा (assembly) / माझ (middle) / परि (having fallen) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / बहु प्रकार (in many ways) / कह (saying) / रोइ (weeping) / तोहि (you) / जिअत (while living) / दसकंधर (ten-headed one) / मोरि (my) / कि (what) / असि (such) / गति (fate, condition) / होइ (becomes)
ramacharitamanas::3772.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3772.essence: Humiliation speaks first when hurt has not yet settled.
ramacharitamanas::3772.simple_meaning: She collapses in Ravana's court and cries out in distress, blaming his living presence for her humiliation and suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3772.simple_insight: Pain can make a person lash out and turn shame into accusation.
ramacharitamanas::3772.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Surpanakha is still reeling from the earlier humiliation. Surrounded by the assembly, she cries and complains that as long as Ravana lives, how can such disgrace have happened to her? The scene pushes the story toward Ravana's reaction.
ramacharitamanas::3772.modern_relevance: You walk into a room already wounded, and your first words come out as blame. The hurt is real, but it is still speaking through you.
ramacharitamanas::3772.insight: It shows how humiliation turns into public complaint before clear thinking returns.

ramacharitamanas::3773.verse_sanskrit: सुनत सभासद उठे अकुलाई। समुझाई गहि बाँह उठाई॥ कह लंकेस कहसि निज बाता। केइँ तव नासा कान निपाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3773.verse_hindi: शूर्पणखा के वचन सुनते ही सभासद् अकुला उठे। उन्होंने शूर्पणखा की बाँह पकड़कर उसे उठाया और समझाया। लंकापति रावण ने कहा- अपनी बात तो बता, किसने तेरे नाक-कान काट लिए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3773.english_translation: When the courtiers heard this, they sprang up in agitation. They consoled her, took her by the arm, and lifted her up. Then the lord of Lanka said, “Tell your story. Who cut off your nose and ears?”
ramacharitamanas::3773.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / सभासद (courtiers) / उठे (rose) / अकुलाई (in agitation) / समुझाई (having consoled) / गहि (grasping) / बाँह (arm) / उठाई (lifted up) / कह (said) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / कहसि (you tell) / निज (your own) / बाता (story) / केइँ (who) / तव (your) / नासा (nose) / कान (ears) / निपाता (cut off)
ramacharitamanas::3773.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3773.essence: Shock in the court opens the door to the accusation.
ramacharitamanas::3773.simple_meaning: The courtiers rush to help the injured woman, and Ravana asks who mutilated her. It is a scene of shock, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3773.simple_insight: Some moments only move the story forward; they do not yet ask anything of you.
ramacharitamanas::3773.detailed_meaning: In Ravana’s court at Lanka, the wounded Surpanakha has just finished her desperate complaint. The courtiers rush to steady her, and Ravana, hearing the uproar, asks for the story behind her humiliation. This verse only sets the next turn of the plot.
ramacharitamanas::3773.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone blurts out a shocking complaint, and everyone turns to the person who can explain what happened next. The scene matters, but it is still only the opening of the response.
ramacharitamanas::3773.insight: It keeps attention on the immediate scene and prepares the listener for the accusation to follow.

ramacharitamanas::3774.verse_sanskrit: अवध नृपति दसरथ के जाए। पुरुष सिंघ बन खेलन आए॥ समुझि परी मोहि उन्ह कै करनी। रहित निसाचर करिहहिं धरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3774.verse_hindi: (वह बोली-) अयोध्या के राजा दशरथ के पुत्र, जो पुरुषों में सिंह के समान हैं, वन में शिकार खेलने आए हैं। मुझे उनकी करनी ऐसी समझ पड़ी है कि वे पृथ्वी को राक्षसों से रहित कर देंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3774.english_translation: She said, "The sons of King Dasharath of Ayodhya have come. They are lions among men, come to play in the forest. I understand their deed: they will rid the earth of demons."
ramacharitamanas::3774.translation_literal: अवध (Ayodhya) / नृपति (king) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / के (of) / जाए (sons) / पुरुष (men) / सिंघ (lions) / बन (forest) / खेलन (to play) / आए (came)॥ / समुझि (understanding) / परी (fell) / मोहि (to me) / उन्ह (their) / कै (of) / करनी (deed) / रहित (free from) / निसाचर (demons) / करिहहिं (will make) / धरनी (earth) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3774.speaker: Shurpanakha
ramacharitamanas::3774.essence: What looks like play can be the beginning of a complete clearing.
ramacharitamanas::3774.simple_meaning: Shurpanakha recognizes that Ram and Lakshman are not ordinary forest visitors. She sees that their arrival will end the rule of demons on earth.
ramacharitamanas::3774.simple_insight: Sometimes the deepest threat to evil is simply being seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3774.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shurpanakha has just met the two princes of Ayodhya. Even before knowing their full story, she senses their power and mission. Her words foreshadow that Ram's presence will transform the forest and destroy the demon order.
ramacharitamanas::3774.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a gathering and think they are just being polite, but their calm presence changes the whole room. Some people arrive quietly and still shift the direction of everything around them.
ramacharitamanas::3774.insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to the deeper force behind a person's actions.

ramacharitamanas::3775.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह कर भुजबल पाइ दसानन। अभय भए बिचरत मुनि कानन॥ देखत बालक काल समाना। परम धीर धन्वी गुन नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3775.verse_hindi: जिनकी भुजाओं का बल पाकर हे दशमुख! मुनि लोग वन में निर्भय होकर विचरने लगे हैं। वे देखने में तो बालक हैं, पर हैं काल के समान। वे परम धीर, श्रेष्ठ धनुर्धर और अनेकों गुणों से युक्त हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3775.english_translation: By the strength of their arms, the sages have become fearless in the forest, O Ravana. They look like boys, yet they are like Time itself: deeply steady, master archers, and filled with many virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3775.translation_literal: जिन्ह (whose) / कर (of the) / भुजबल (arm-strength) / पाइ (having obtained) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / अभय (fearless) / भए (became) / बिचरत (wandering) / मुनि (sages) / कानन (forest)॥ / देखत (looking) / बालक (boys/children) / काल (Time/Death) / समाना (like) / परम (supremely) / धीर (steady) / धन्वी (archer) / गुन (virtues) / नाना (many) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3775.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3775.essence: Real power can look young, calm, and unthreatening.
ramacharitamanas::3775.simple_meaning: Ravana admits that Ram and Lakshman have made the forest safe for sages. Though they look young, they are powerful, calm, skilled archers, and full of virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3775.simple_insight: True strength can look gentle, and real power makes others feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::3775.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana is already measuring the brothers who stand in his way. He sees that their presence has made sages fearless, and that their youth hides deadly strength, composure, and skill. This is Ravana's own uneasy recognition of the danger before him.
ramacharitamanas::3775.modern_relevance: You meet the quiet person in the room who says little, but everyone relaxes when they arrive. Their calm changes the atmosphere before they ever speak.
ramacharitamanas::3775.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to actual capacity, showing that steadiness can be more formidable than display.

ramacharitamanas::3776.verse_sanskrit: अतुलित बल प्रताप द्वौ भ्राता। खल बध रत सुर मुनि सुखदाता॥ सोभा धाम राम अस नामा। तिन्ह के संग नारि एक स्यामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3776.verse_hindi: दोनों भाइयों का बल और प्रताप अतुलनीय है। वे दुष्टों का वध करने में लगे हैं और देवता तथा मुनियों को सुख देने वाले हैं। वे शोभा के धाम हैं, 'राम' ऐसा उनका नाम है। उनके साथ एक तरुणी सुंदर स्त्री है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3776.english_translation: The two brothers have unmatched strength and glory. They are devoted to destroying the wicked and giving joy to the gods and sages. Ram is a name of beauty, and with them is a dark-hued woman.
ramacharitamanas::3776.translation_literal: अतुलित (unmatched) / बल (strength) / प्रताप (glory) / द्वौ (two) / भ्राता (brothers) / खल (wicked) / बध (killing) / रत (engaged) / सुर (deities) / मुनि (sages) / सुखदाता (givers of joy) / सोभा (beauty) / धाम (abode) / राम (Ram) / अस (such) / नामा (name) / तिन्ह (their) / के संग (with) / नारि (woman) / एक (one) / स्यामा (dark-hued)
ramacharitamanas::3776.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3776.essence: Power and beauty are being introduced, not yet explained.
ramacharitamanas::3776.simple_meaning: The two brothers are unmatched in strength and glory. They protect the good and punish the wicked, and a beautiful dark-hued woman is with them.
ramacharitamanas::3776.simple_insight: Great power is being described, but the scene is still moving forward. The meaning will unfold in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::3776.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the demoness is sizing up the two brothers she has just seen. She notices their unmatched power, their role as protectors, and the radiant woman beside them. This verse is part of her description, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::3776.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a room and instantly sense their presence before they speak. The real meaning comes only when they begin to act.
ramacharitamanas::3776.insight: It frames the characters before the encounter turns into action, so the verse functions as scene-setting rather than a complete teaching.

ramacharitamanas::3777.verse_sanskrit: रूप रासि बिधि नारि सँवारी। रति सत कोटि तासु बलिहारी॥ तासु अनुज काटे श्रुति नासा। सुनि तव भगिनि करहिं परिहासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3777.verse_hindi: विधाता ने उस स्त्री को ऐसी रूप की राशि बनाया है कि सौ करोड़ रति (कामदेव की स्त्री) उस पर निछावर हैं। उन्हीं के छोटे भाई ने मेरे नाक-कान काट डाले। मैं तेरी बहिन हूँ, यह सुनकर वे मेरी हँसी करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3777.english_translation: The creator shaped that woman as a treasury of beauty; a hundred million Ratis would offer themselves to her. Her younger brother cut off my nose and ears. When I said, "I am your sister," they mocked me.
ramacharitamanas::3777.translation_literal: रूप रासि (a treasury of beauty) / बिधि (the creator) / नारि (woman) / सँवारी (fashioned, adorned) / रति (Rati) / सत कोटि (hundred million) / तासु (to her) / बलिहारी (offering myself, devoted) / तासु (her) / अनुज (younger brother) / काटे (cut off) / श्रुति (nose and ears) / नासा (nose) / सुनि (hearing) / तव (your) / भगिनि (sister) / करहिं (they do) / परिहासा (mockery, laughter)
ramacharitamanas::3777.speaker: Surpanakha
ramacharitamanas::3777.essence: Wounded pride turns beauty into resentment.
ramacharitamanas::3777.simple_meaning: Surpanakha describes Sita’s beauty, then complains that Lakshman mutilated her and laughed when she claimed to be Ravana’s sister.
ramacharitamanas::3777.simple_insight: Pride wounded by rejection can turn quickly into revenge.
ramacharitamanas::3777.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha is recounting her humiliation after approaching Ram and Lakshman. She praises Sita’s beauty, then shifts to her own injury and mockery, setting the anger that will soon pull Ravana into the conflict.
ramacharitamanas::3777.modern_relevance: You felt dismissed in one sharp moment, and now every word sounds like an insult. Hurt can make a small rejection grow teeth.
ramacharitamanas::3777.insight: It shows how wounded vanity turns humiliation into a story of grievance and retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::3778.verse_sanskrit: खर दूषन सुनि लगे पुकारा। छन महुँ सकल कटक उन्ह मारा॥ खर दूषन तिसिरा कर घाता। सुनि दससीस जरे सब गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3778.verse_hindi: मेरी पुकार सुनकर खर-दूषण सहायता करने आए। पर उन्होंने क्षण भर में सारी सेना को मार डाला। खर-दूषन और त्रिशिरा का वध सुनकर रावण के सारे अंग जल उठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3778.english_translation: Hearing the call, Khara and Dushana rushed to help. In a moment, they were all slain. When Khara, Dushana, and Trishira were killed, Ravana's whole body burned with rage.
ramacharitamanas::3778.translation_literal: खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / सुनि (hearing) / लगे (began) / पुकारा (to call out) / छन महुँ (in a moment) / सकल (all) / कटक (army) / उन्ह (their) / मारा (were killed) / खर दूषन (Khara and Dushana) / तिसिरा (Trishira) / कर (of) / घाता (killing) / सुनि (hearing) / दससीस (Ravana, ten-headed one) / जरे (burned) / सब (all) / गाता (limbs/body)
ramacharitamanas::3778.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3778.essence: Revenge arrives fast, but defeat can arrive faster.
ramacharitamanas::3778.simple_meaning: Khara and Dushana rush to help after hearing the call, but Ram's side destroys their army immediately. Ravana burns with anger when he hears they have been killed.
ramacharitamanas::3778.simple_insight: Pride can turn one alarm into a bigger collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3778.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shurpanakha's cry brings Khara and Dushana charging in with their forces. But Ram and Lakshman cut them down almost at once. News of that defeat reaches Ravana, and his fury flares across his whole body.
ramacharitamanas::3778.modern_relevance: A friend texts, then three people pile into the argument thinking they can fix it. Before the group chat settles, the damage is already done.
ramacharitamanas::3778.insight: It shows how quickly rash retaliation can be overwhelmed, and how anger spreads when ego is wounded.

ramacharitamanas::3779.verse_sanskrit: सूपनखहि समुझाइ करि बल बोलेसि बहु भाँति। गयउ भवन अति सोचबस नीद परइ नहिं राति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3779.verse_hindi: उसने शूर्पणखा को समझाकर बहुत प्रकार से अपने बल का बखान किया, किन्तु (मन में) वह अत्यन्त चिंतावश होकर अपने महल में गया, उसे रात भर नींद नहीं पड़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3779.english_translation: After reassuring Surpanakha and boasting in many ways of his strength, he went back to his palace, overwhelmed with worry and unable to sleep all night.
ramacharitamanas::3779.translation_literal: सूपनखहि (to Surpanakha) / समुझाइ करि (having explained) / बल (strength) / बोलेसि (he spoke) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / गयउ (went) / भवन (to the palace) / अति (very) / सोचबस (overwhelmed with worry) / नीद (sleep) / परइ (falls) / नहिं (not) / राति (at night)
ramacharitamanas::3779.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3779.essence: Boasted strength collapses into sleepless fear.
ramacharitamanas::3779.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to calm Surpanakha by boasting about his power, but inside he is shaken and cannot sleep.
ramacharitamanas::3779.simple_insight: Pride can sound confident while fear keeps you awake.
ramacharitamanas::3779.detailed_meaning: After Surpanakha is humiliated, Ravana reassures her and talks up his own strength. But the moment he returns to his palace, worry takes over. The boast is public; the fear is private.
ramacharitamanas::3779.modern_relevance: You leave a tense family argument sounding firm and certain, then lie awake replaying every word. The outside voice says control; the inside mind knows better.
ramacharitamanas::3779.insight: It exposes the split between outward bravado and inward insecurity.

ramacharitamanas::3780.verse_sanskrit: सुर नर असुर नाग खग माहीं। मोरे अनुचर कहँ कोउ नाहीं॥ खर दूषन मोहि सम बलवंता। तिन्हहि को मारइ बिनु भगवंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3780.verse_hindi: (वह मन ही मन विचार करने लगा-) देवता, मनुष्य, असुर, नाग और पक्षियों में कोई ऐसा नहीं, जो मेरे सेवक को भी पा सके। खर-दूषण तो मेरे ही समान बलवान थे। उन्हें भगवान के सिवा और कौन मार सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3780.english_translation: Among gods, humans, demons, serpents, and birds, none can match me. Khara and Dushana were as strong as I am; only the divine could kill them.
ramacharitamanas::3780.translation_literal: सुर (radiant beings) / नर (humans) / असुर (beings of ego and shadow) / नाग (serpents) / खग (birds) / माहीं (among) / मोरे (my) / अनुचर (followers) / कहँ (for) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (not)॥ / खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / मोहि (me) / सम (equal to) / बलवंता (powerful) / तिन्हहि (them) / को (who) / मारइ (can kill) / बिनु (without) / भगवंता (the divine) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3780.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3780.essence: Pride makes you imagine yourself beyond correction.
ramacharitamanas::3780.simple_meaning: Ravana is measuring his own power against the world and concluding that only the divine can defeat him. The verse reveals his pride and blindness.
ramacharitamanas::3780.simple_insight: Confidence without self-awareness turns into delusion.
ramacharitamanas::3780.detailed_meaning: After Shurpanakha returns wounded, Ravana sits in Lanka replaying the news. He cannot accept that ordinary beings defeated Khara and Dushana, so he inflates himself into the strongest force in the world. That pride sets up his ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3780.modern_relevance: You reread the email that proved you wrong and still want to call it a fluke. Ravana's mistake is familiar: when ego feels threatened, it starts rewriting reality.
ramacharitamanas::3780.insight: It exposes how the sense of separate self builds a false image of invulnerability.

ramacharitamanas::3781.verse_sanskrit: सुर रंजन भंजन महि भारा। जौं भगवंत लीन्ह अवतारा॥ तौ मैं जाइ बैरु हठि करऊँ। प्रभु सर प्रान तजें भव तरऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3781.verse_hindi: देवताओं को आनंद देने वाले और पृथ्वी का भार हरण करने वाले भगवान ने ही यदि अवतार लिया है, तो मैं जाकर उनसे हठपूर्वक वैर करूँगा और प्रभु के बाण (के आघात) से प्राण छोड़कर भवसागर से तर जाऊँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3781.english_translation: If the divine has truly taken birth to delight the radiant beings and lift the earth's burden, then I will go and fight him stubbornly. By the Lord's arrow, I will give up my life and cross beyond the cycle of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3781.translation_literal: सुर (radiant beings) / रंजन (delighting) / भंजन (destroying) / महि (earth) / भारा (burden) / जौं (if) / भगवंत (the divine) / लीन्ह (took) / अवतारा (incarnation)॥ / तौ (then) / मैं (I) / जाइ (going) / बैरु (enmity) / हठि (stubbornly) / करऊँ (will do)॥ / प्रभु (Lord) / सर (arrow) / प्रान (life) / तजें (leaving) / भव (cycle of suffering) / तरऊँ (cross beyond)॥
ramacharitamanas::3781.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3781.essence: Pride can recognise truth and still choose ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3781.simple_meaning: Ravana recognizes that Ram has likely come for a divine purpose, yet his pride pushes him to oppose that truth anyway.
ramacharitamanas::3781.simple_insight: Seeing the truth is not enough if the ego insists on fighting it.
ramacharitamanas::3781.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking after hearing of the mysterious force rising against him. He senses that Ram may be the divine itself come to restore balance, but instead of yielding, he hardens into defiance. The verse reveals the mind of pride at the edge of ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3781.modern_relevance: You know you’re wrong, but your jaw tightens anyway and you double down in the meeting. The facts are clear; the ego just wants the last word.
ramacharitamanas::3781.insight: It shows how clear seeing can still be defeated by stubborn self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::3782.verse_sanskrit: होइहि भजनु न तामस देहा। मन क्रम बचन मंत्र दृढ़ एहा॥ जौं नररूप भूपसुत कोऊ। हरिहउँ नारि जीति रन दोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3782.verse_hindi: इस तामस शरीर से भजन तो होगा नहीं, अतएव मन, वचन और कर्म से यही दृढ़ निश्चय है। और यदि वे मनुष्य रूप कोई राजकुमार होंगे तो उन दोनों को रण में जीतकर उनकी स्त्री को हर लूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3782.english_translation: Devotion will not come from this tamasic body. My resolve is firm in mind, speech, and action: if they are human princes, I will defeat them both in battle and seize their woman.
ramacharitamanas::3782.translation_literal: होइहि (will happen) / भजनु (devotion) / न (not) / तामस (tamasic, dark) / देहा (body) / मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / मंत्र (resolve) / दृढ़ (firm) / एहा (this) / जौं (if) / नररूप (human form) / भूपसुत (king's son, prince) / कोऊ (someone) / हरिहउँ (I will seize) / नारि (woman) / जीति (having won) / रन (battle) / दोऊ (both)
ramacharitamanas::3782.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3782.essence: Ego turns uncertainty into a vow of violence.
ramacharitamanas::3782.simple_meaning: Ravana hardens himself for violence. He dismisses devotion and vows that if the opponents are human princes, he will defeat them and take their wife.
ramacharitamanas::3782.simple_insight: Pride can turn fear into a vow of destruction.
ramacharitamanas::3782.detailed_meaning: Ravana is alone with his thoughts after hearing that Ram may be an avatar. Instead of humility, he doubles down on ego and aggression. He rejects devotion, fixes his mind on violence, and decides to test the princes in battle.
ramacharitamanas::3782.modern_relevance: Someone hears a warning that they may be outmatched, and instead of pausing, they get more reckless, more defensive, and more determined to prove themselves right.
ramacharitamanas::3782.insight: It shows how wounded pride hardens into a destructive plan instead of self-correction.

ramacharitamanas::3783.verse_sanskrit: चला अकेल जान चढ़ि तहवाँ। बस मारीच सिंधु तट जहवाँ॥ इहाँ राम जसि जुगुति बनाई। सुनहु उमा सो कथा सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3783.verse_hindi: राक्षसों की भयानक सेना आ गई है। जानकीजी को लेकर तुम पर्वत की कंदरा में चले जाओ। सावधान रहना। प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए श्री सीताजी सहित चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3783.english_translation: Laxman went alone up there, to the shore where Maricha lived by the sea. Here Ram made a fitting plan, O Uma, and the story is delightful to hear.
ramacharitamanas::3783.translation_literal: चला (went) / अकेल (alone) / जान (having known) / चढ़ि (going up) / तहवाँ (there) / बस (dwelling) / मारीच (Maricha) / सिंधु (sea) / तट (shore) / जहवाँ (where) / इहाँ (here) / राम (Ram) / जसि (fitting) / जुगुति (plan, strategy) / बनाई (made) / सुनहु (listen) / उमा (Uma) / सो (that) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (beautiful, pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::3783.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3783.essence: The story moves forward through careful, unseen planning.
ramacharitamanas::3783.simple_meaning: Laxman goes alone to the place where Maricha lives, while Ram quietly makes the right plan. The verse is a bridge in the story, not a teaching by itself.
ramacharitamanas::3783.simple_insight: Sometimes the right move is quiet, precise, and already prepared.
ramacharitamanas::3783.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Ram is setting the trap that will draw Ravana into action. Laxman moves alone toward Maricha's dwelling by the sea, while Ram arranges the plan with calm intelligence. This is narrative setup, not the verse's main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3783.modern_relevance: You watch someone leave the room to handle the hard part while another person quietly puts the plan in place. The real work is already moving.
ramacharitamanas::3783.insight: It shows coordinated action in a larger strategy, with no standalone moral claim.

ramacharitamanas::3784.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन गए बनहिं जब लेन मूल फल कंद। जनकसुता सन बोले बिहसि कृपा सुख बृंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::3784.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी जब कंद-मूल-फल लेने के लिए वन में गए, तब (अकेले में) कृपा और सुख के समूह श्री रामचंद्रजी हँसकर जानकीजी से बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3784.english_translation: When Lakshman went into the forest to gather roots, fruits, and tubers, Janak's daughter, smiling, spoke to him with grace and delight.
ramacharitamanas::3784.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / गए (went) / बनहिं (into the forest) / जब (when) / लेन (to take) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / कंद (tubers) / जनकसुता (Janak's daughter) / सन (to) / बोले (spoke) / बिहसि (smiling) / कृपा (grace) / सुख (delight) / बृंद (group, abundance)
ramacharitamanas::3784.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3784.essence: Love can speak softly right before hardship begins.
ramacharitamanas::3784.simple_meaning: Lakshman goes to fetch forest food, and Ram speaks lovingly to Sita. It is a quiet moment before the deeper plan is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::3784.simple_insight: Even in danger, tenderness can stay alive.
ramacharitamanas::3784.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman leaves to gather food. With him away, Ram turns to Sita with a smile and gentle ease. This brief, intimate moment sits just before he reveals the plan for the coming crisis.
ramacharitamanas::3784.modern_relevance: You are making tea while the house is tense, and someone you love gives you a small smile before the hard conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::3784.insight: It shows how calm affection can prepare the heart for sacrifice.

ramacharitamanas::3785.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु प्रिया ब्रत रुचिर सुसीला। मैं कछु करबि ललित नरलीला॥ तुम्ह पावक महुँ करहु निवासा। जौ लगि करौं निसाचर नासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3785.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! हे सुंदर पतिव्रत धर्म का पालन करने वाली सुशीले! सुनो! मैं अब कुछ मनोहर मनुष्य लीला करूँगा, इसलिए जब तक मैं राक्षसों का नाश करूँ, तब तक तुम अग्नि में निवास करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3785.english_translation: Listen, dear one, pure and noble in vow. I will now enact a beautiful human play. Remain in the fire until I destroy the demons.
ramacharitamanas::3785.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / प्रिया (dear one) / ब्रत (vow) / रुचिर (beautiful) / सुसीला (well-mannered, noble) / मैं (I) / कछु (some) / करबि (will do) / ललित (beautiful) / नरलीला (human play) / तुम्ह (you) / पावक (fire) / महुँ (in) / करहु (do/remain) / निवासा (residence) / जौ (until) / लगि (for) / करौं (I do) / निसाचर (demons) / नासा (destruction)
ramacharitamanas::3785.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3785.essence: What looks like loss can be part of a greater protection.
ramacharitamanas::3785.simple_meaning: Ram asks Sita to stay in the fire while he carries out his human play and destroys the demons.
ramacharitamanas::3785.simple_insight: Love sometimes protects by waiting in pain, not by forcing a quick ending.
ramacharitamanas::3785.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has already sent Lakshman away to gather roots and fruit. Now he speaks privately to Sita before the great deception unfolds. He asks her to enter the fire while he completes the destruction of Ravana's forces and preserves her purity.
ramacharitamanas::3785.modern_relevance: You may have to endure a painful separation for a larger purpose, trusting that the hidden cost is not the final truth.
ramacharitamanas::3785.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate comfort to protecting what is sacred through difficult means.

ramacharitamanas::3786.verse_sanskrit: जबहिं राम सब कहा बखानी। प्रभु पद धरि हियँ अनल समानी॥ निज प्रतिबिंब राखि तहँ सीता। तैसइ सील रूप सुबिनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3786.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने ज्यों ही सब समझाकर कहा, त्यों ही श्री सीताजी प्रभु के चरणों को हृदय में धरकर अग्नि में समा गईं। सीताजी ने अपनी ही छाया मूर्ति वहाँ रख दी, जो उनके जैसे ही शील-स्वभाव और रूपवाली तथा वैसे ही विनम्र थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3786.english_translation: As soon as Ram had explained everything, Sita entered the fire, holding the Lord's feet in her heart. There he placed her reflection, a form just like her—gentle in character, beautiful in form, and equally modest.
ramacharitamanas::3786.translation_literal: जबहिं (as soon as) / राम (Ram) / सब (everything) / कहा (said) / बखानी (explained) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पद (feet) / धरि (placing) / हियँ (in the heart) / अनल (fire) / समानी (entered) / निज (own) / प्रतिबिंब (reflection) / राखि (placing) / तहँ (there) / सीता (Sita) / तैसइ (likewise) / सील (character) / रूप (form) / सुबिनीता (well-mannered, modest)
ramacharitamanas::3786.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3786.essence: Trust can carry you through fire while your true form remains untouched.
ramacharitamanas::3786.simple_meaning: Sita enters the fire only after Ram has explained the plan. A perfect double of her remains behind, so the world sees her as before.
ramacharitamanas::3786.simple_insight: Sometimes the hardest step is also the most faithful one.
ramacharitamanas::3786.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram has just revealed the hidden purpose of this moment to Sita. She trusts him completely and steps into the fire, while a reflected likeness of her stays behind. The scene prepares the deception that will protect her during Ravana's coming crime.
ramacharitamanas::3786.modern_relevance: You agree to a painful plan because you trust the person who asked you to do it. Later, everyone sees only the version of you that stayed behind.
ramacharitamanas::3786.insight: It shows how trust can carry someone through a terrifying transition without breaking their dignity.

ramacharitamanas::3787.verse_sanskrit: लछिमनहूँ यह मरमु न जाना। जो कछु चरित रचा भगवाना॥ दसमुख गयउ जहाँ मारीचा। नाइ माथ स्वारथ रत नीचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3787.verse_hindi: भगवान ने जो कुछ लीला रची, इस रहस्य को लक्ष्मणजी ने भी नहीं जाना। स्वार्थ परायण और नीच रावण वहाँ गया, जहाँ मारीच था और उसको सिर नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3787.english_translation: Even Lakshman did not understand this secret: whatever the divine had arranged as the play. Ravana, driven by selfishness, went to where Maricha was and bowed his head before him.
ramacharitamanas::3787.translation_literal: लछिमनहूँ (even Lakshman) / यह (this) / मरमु (secret) / न (not) / जाना (knew) / जो कछु (whatever) / चरित (play / deed) / रचा (arranged) / भगवाना (the divine)॥ / दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / गयउ (went) / जहाँ (where) / मारीचा (Maricha) / नाइ (bowing) / माथ (head) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / रत (absorbed) / नीचा (base one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3787.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3787.essence: Selfish desire makes you bow to what will harm you.
ramacharitamanas::3787.simple_meaning: Even Lakshman could not see the hidden design behind events. Ravana, trapped in selfishness, went to Maricha and bowed to him.
ramacharitamanas::3787.simple_insight: Self-interest makes a person bow to what will later destroy them.
ramacharitamanas::3787.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has just sent Sita into the fire’s protection and begun the deceptive play that will draw Ravana onward. Even Lakshman cannot see the full hidden design. Ravana, blinded by craving, walks straight toward Maricha and lowers his head.
ramacharitamanas::3787.modern_relevance: You keep chasing the person who flatters your worst impulse, thinking it will help. Later, you see you were already bowing to the very thing that would trap you.
ramacharitamanas::3787.insight: It shows how desire narrows vision and makes dangerous choices feel respectful or wise.

ramacharitamanas::3788.verse_sanskrit: नवनि नीच कै अति दुखदाई। जिमि अंकुस धनु उरग बिलाई॥ भयदायक खल कै प्रिय बानी। जिमि अकाल के कुसुम भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3788.verse_hindi: नीच का झुकना (नम्रता) भी अत्यन्त दुःखदायी होता है। जैसे अंकुश, धनुष, साँप और बिल्ली का झुकना। हे भवानी! दुष्ट की मीठी वाणी भी (उसी प्रकार) भय देने वाली होती है, जैसे बिना ऋतु के फूल! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3788.english_translation: A low person's bowing is deeply painful, like a goad, a bow, a snake, or a cat bending low. O Bhavani, a wicked person's sweet speech is equally fearsome, like flowers blooming out of season.
ramacharitamanas::3788.translation_literal: नवनि (bowing/bending) / नीच कै (of a low person) / अति दुखदाई (extremely painful) / जिमि (like) / अंकुस (goad) / धनु (bow) / उरग (snake) / बिलाई (cat) / भयदायक (fear-inducing) / खल कै (of a wicked person) / प्रिय बानी (pleasant speech) / जिमि (like) / अकाल के (out of season) / कुसुम (flowers) / भवानी (O Bhavani)
ramacharitamanas::3788.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3788.essence: Softness can be a mask for danger.
ramacharitamanas::3788.simple_meaning: A wicked person may look humble and speak sweetly, but that can hide danger. Outward softness does not always mean good intent.
ramacharitamanas::3788.simple_insight: You learn to notice charm without being lulled by it.
ramacharitamanas::3788.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has taken the form of a mendicant and approaches Sita's shelter through deceit. Tulsidas pauses to warn Parvati that a villain's humility and sweetness can be more dangerous than open force.
ramacharitamanas::3788.modern_relevance: Someone apologizes with the perfect tone after hurting you, but their pattern never changes. The smile is polished; the intention is not.
ramacharitamanas::3788.insight: It trains you to test appearance against character before trusting what sounds gentle.

ramacharitamanas::3789.verse_sanskrit: करि पूजा मारीच तब सादर पूछी बात। कवन हेतु मन ब्यग्र अति अकसर आयहु तात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3789.verse_hindi: तब मारीच ने उसकी पूजा करके आदरपूर्वक बात पूछी- हे तात! आपका मन किस कारण इतना अधिक व्यग्र है और आप अकेले आए हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3789.english_translation: Then Maricha honored him with worship and respectfully asked, "Dear uncle, what makes your mind so troubled, and why have you come alone?"
ramacharitamanas::3789.translation_literal: करि (having done) / पूजा (worship) / मारीच (Maricha) / तब (then) / सादर (respectfully) / पूछी (asked) / बात (question) / कवन (what) / हेतु (reason) / मन (mind) / ब्यग्र (restless) / अति (very) / अकसर (alone) / आयहु (have come) / तात (dear uncle)
ramacharitamanas::3789.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3789.essence: Polite words can open the door to harm.
ramacharitamanas::3789.simple_meaning: Maricha greets Ravana with respect and asks why he has come alone in such a troubled state.
ramacharitamanas::3789.simple_insight: Not every polite question is innocent; sometimes courtesy hides a dangerous turn.
ramacharitamanas::3789.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana reaches Maricha after the earlier signs of deception and unease. Maricha receives him politely and asks why he has come alone, setting up the next step in Ravana’s plot against Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3789.modern_relevance: A friend calls you late at night, unusually formal, and asks if you can talk privately. The politeness itself tells you something is already off.
ramacharitamanas::3789.insight: It frames the scene as a prelude to manipulation, not a teaching in itself.

ramacharitamanas::3790.verse_sanskrit: दसमुख सकल कथा तेहि आगें। कही सहित अभिमान अभागें॥ होहु कपट मृग तुम्ह छलकारी। जेहि बिधि हरि आनौं नृपनारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3790.verse_hindi: भाग्यहीन रावण ने सारी कथा अभिमान सहित उसके सामने कही (और फिर कहा-) तुम छल करने वाले कपटमृग बनो, जिस उपाय से मैं उस राजवधू को हर लाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3790.english_translation: Ravana told the whole story before him, with pride despite his ill fortune, and said, 'Become a deceitful deer, you trickster, by whatever means I may bring away the queen.'
ramacharitamanas::3790.translation_literal: दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / सकल (entire) / कथा (story) / तेहि (to him) / आगें (before) / कही (told) / सहित (with) / अभिमान (pride) / अभागें (unlucky, doomed one) / होहु (become) / कपट (deceitful) / मृग (deer) / तुम्ह (you) / छलकारी (trickster) / जेहि बिधि (by whatever means) / हरि (take away) / आनौं (I may bring) / नृपनारी (king's wife, queen)
ramacharitamanas::3790.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3790.essence: Pride can dress itself as strategy and still be the beginning of collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3790.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Maricha his plan and orders him to take the form of a deceptive deer so he can lure away Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3790.simple_insight: Pride can make a person recruit others into their own ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3790.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has reached Maricha with a secret plan. Still swollen with ego, he lays out the entire scheme and demands help in the abduction of Sita. This verse is a step inside the trap before Maricha warns him.
ramacharitamanas::3790.modern_relevance: A powerful person calls you with a flattering tone and a dangerous request. You can hear the charm, but the real story is the harm underneath it.
ramacharitamanas::3790.insight: It shows how ego speaks openly while hiding its own destruction.

ramacharitamanas::3791.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं पुनि कहा सुनहु दससीसा। ते नररूप चराचर ईसा॥ तासों तात बयरु नहिं कीजै। मारें मरिअ जिआएँ जीजै ॥
ramacharitamanas::3791.verse_hindi: तब उसने (मारीच ने) कहा- हे दशशीश! सुनिए। वे मनुष्य रूप में चराचर के ईश्वर हैं। हे तात! उनसे वैर न कीजिए। उन्हीं के मारने से मरना और उनके जिलाने से जीना होता है (सबका जीवन-मरण उन्हीं के अधीन है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3791.english_translation: Then he said again, "Listen, Ravana. Those are the Lord in human form, the ruler of all moving and unmoving beings. So do not make enmity with him, my friend. Death and life are in his hands: he kills, and he gives life."
ramacharitamanas::3791.translation_literal: तेहिं (then he) / पुनि (again) / कहा (said) / सुनहु (listen) / दससीसा (O ten-headed one) / ते (those) / नररूप (human form) / चराचर (moving and unmoving beings) / ईसा (Lord) / तासों (with them) / तात (my friend) / बयरु (enmity) / नहिं (not) / कीजै (do) / मारें (by killing) / मरिअ (one dies) / जिआएँ (by giving life) / जीजै (one lives)
ramacharitamanas::3791.speaker: Maricha
ramacharitamanas::3791.essence: Enmity collapses when you see the divine power already standing before you.
ramacharitamanas::3791.simple_meaning: Maricha warns Ravana not to make Ram his enemy. He says Ram is the Lord in human form, and life and death rest with him.
ramacharitamanas::3791.simple_insight: Pride fades when you remember who you are really facing.
ramacharitamanas::3791.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has come to Maricha for help in his plan to abduct Sita. Maricha, remembering Ram's power from an earlier encounter, tries to stop him by speaking plainly: this is no ordinary man, and enmity with him will destroy you.
ramacharitamanas::3791.modern_relevance: You are about to send that angry text, convinced you can win the argument. Then a quieter part of you remembers: this person may be carrying far more power than your ego wants to admit.
ramacharitamanas::3791.insight: It shifts the mind from reckless opposition to clear recognition of power and consequence.

ramacharitamanas::3792.verse_sanskrit: मुनि मख राखन गयउ कुमारा। बिनु फर सर रघुपति मोहि मारा॥ सत जोजन आयउँ छन माहीं। तिन्ह सन बयरु किएँ भल नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3792.verse_hindi: यही राजकुमार मुनि विश्वामित्र के यज्ञ की रक्षा के लिए गए थे। उस समय श्री रघुनाथजी ने बिना फल का बाण मुझे मारा था, जिससे मैं क्षणभर में सौ योजन पर आ गिरा। उनसे वैर करने में भलाई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3792.english_translation: The prince went to protect the sage's sacrifice. Raghupati struck me with a fruitless arrow, and in a moment I fell a hundred leagues away. It is not wise to bear enmity toward them.
ramacharitamanas::3792.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / मख (sacrifice) / राखन (to protect) / गयउ (went) / कुमारा (the prince) / बिनु (without) / फर (fruit) / सर (arrow) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / मोहि (me) / मारा (struck)॥ / सत (hundred) / जोजन (leagues) / आयउँ (I came) / छन (moment) / माहीं (in) / तिन्ह (them) / सन (with) / बयरु (enmity) / किएँ (doing) / भल (good) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::3792.speaker: Maricha
ramacharitamanas::3792.essence: Remembering your defeat can save you from repeating it.
ramacharitamanas::3792.simple_meaning: Maricha warns Ravana that Ram once sent him flying with a single arrow, so fighting Ram and Lakshman will only bring harm.
ramacharitamanas::3792.simple_insight: Pride looks smaller when you remember who has already humbled you.
ramacharitamanas::3792.detailed_meaning: Maricha is trying to save Ravana from disaster. He recalls the day Ram went with Lakshman to protect Vishwamitra's sacrifice and struck him so hard that he was hurled far away. That memory becomes a warning: do not pick a fight with them.
ramacharitamanas::3792.modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry message, even though the last one already blew up in your face. Memory is trying to protect you from repeating a wound.
ramacharitamanas::3792.insight: It shifts you from stubborn revenge to sober self-recognition before you escalate harm.

ramacharitamanas::3793.verse_sanskrit: भइ मम कीट भृंग की नाई। जहँ तहँ मैं देखउँ दोउ भाई॥ जौं नर तात तदपि अति सूरा। तिन्हहि बिरोधि न आइहि पूरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3793.verse_hindi: मेरी दशा तो भृंगी के कीड़े की सी हो गई है। अब मैं जहाँ-तहाँ श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाइयों को ही देखता हूँ। और हे तात! यदि वे मनुष्य हैं, तो भी बड़े शूरवीर हैं। उनसे विरोध करने में पूरा न पड़ेगा (सफलता नहीं मिलेगी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3793.english_translation: My condition has become like a worm in a wasp's nest. Everywhere I look, I see only the two brothers, Ram and Lakshman. And, father, if they are only men, they are still very mighty; no one can defeat them.
ramacharitamanas::3793.translation_literal: भइ (became) / मम (my) / कीट (worm) / भृंग (wasp) / की नाई (like) / जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / मैं (I) / देखउँ (see) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)॥ / जौं (if) / नर (men) / तात (father) / तदपि (even then) / अति (very) / सूरा (mighty) / तिन्हहि (them) / बिरोधि (opposing) / न (not) / आइहि (will come) / पूरा (complete, successful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3793.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3793.essence: Fear makes one danger seem to occupy your entire world.
ramacharitamanas::3793.simple_meaning: Ravana says fear has made Ram and Lakshman seem to fill his whole world. He admits they are formidable enough that fighting them may fail.
ramacharitamanas::3793.simple_insight: Fear narrows vision until one threat seems to occupy everything.
ramacharitamanas::3793.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is already shaken by reports of Ram's power. He tells Maricha that the brothers seem to appear everywhere in his mind, and he concedes that even if they are only men, they are too strong to oppose lightly.
ramacharitamanas::3793.modern_relevance: You replay one harsh conversation all night and start seeing that person in every room, every message, every silence. Anxiety makes a single fear feel larger than reality.
ramacharitamanas::3793.insight: It shows how fear distorts perception and makes resistance look impossible before the struggle even begins.

ramacharitamanas::3794.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं ताड़का सुबाहु हति खंडेउ हर कोदंड। खर दूषन तिसिरा बधेउ मनुज कि अस बरिबंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::3794.verse_hindi: जिसने ताड़का और सुबाहु को मारकर शिवजी का धनुष तोड़ दिया और खर, दूषण और त्रिशिरा का वध कर डाला, ऐसा प्रचंड बली भी कहीं मनुष्य हो सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3794.english_translation: Can a mere human be so mighty—one who killed Tadka and Subahu, broke Shiva's bow, and slew Khara, Dushana, and Trisira?
ramacharitamanas::3794.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / ताड़का (Tadka) / सुबाहु (Subahu) / हति (having killed) / खंडेउ (broke) / हर (Shiva's) / कोदंड (bow) / खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / तिसिरा (Trisira) / बधेउ (killed) / मनुज (human) / कि (can) / अस (such) / बरिबंड (mighty, huge) (one)
ramacharitamanas::3794.speaker: Ravana
