ramacharitamanas::3794.essence: Ram's power is so great that even his enemy cannot call him ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::3794.simple_meaning: Ravana is stunned by Ram's power and lists Ram's victories to question whether such a mighty being can be only human.
ramacharitamanas::3794.simple_insight: Even fear can become recognition when someone’s strength is too obvious to deny.
ramacharitamanas::3794.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just heard that the prince who broke Shiva's bow and destroyed powerful enemies has entered his world. In this moment of alarm, he cannot dismiss Ram as ordinary, yet his pride still keeps him from bowing.
ramacharitamanas::3794.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm competence leaves no room for doubt. Their presence makes your excuses feel small, even before they say a word.
ramacharitamanas::3794.insight: It frames Ram's greatness through an enemy's reluctant admiration, raising the stakes before Ravana's anger erupts.

ramacharitamanas::3795.verse_sanskrit: जाहु भवन कुल कुसल बिचारी। सुनत जरा दीन्हिसि बहु गारी॥ गुरु जिमि मूढ़ करसि मम बोधा। कहु जग मोहि समान को जोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3795.verse_hindi: अतः अपने कुल की कुशल विचारकर आप घर लौट जाइए। यह सुनकर रावण जल उठा और उसने बहुत सी गालियाँ दीं (दुर्वचन कहे)। (कहा-) अरे मूर्ख! तू गुरु की तरह मुझे ज्ञान सिखाता है? बता तो संसार में मेरे समान योद्धा कौन है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3795.english_translation: Therefore, considering the welfare of your own family, return home. Hearing this, Ravana burned with anger and hurled many abuses. 'Fool! You try to teach me like a guru? Tell me, who in the world is a warrior equal to me?'
ramacharitamanas::3795.translation_literal: जाहु (go) / भवन (home) / कुल (family) / कुसल (well-being) / बिचारी (considering) / सुनत (hearing) / जरा (burned) / दीन्हिसि (gave) / बहु (many) / गारी (abuses) / गुरु (teacher) / जिमि (like) / मूढ़ (fool) / करसि (you do) / मम (my) / बोधा (instruction) / कहु (tell) / जग (world) / मोहि (me) / समान (equal) / को (who) / जोधा (warrior)
ramacharitamanas::3795.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3795.essence: Pride cannot hear wisdom without turning defensive.
ramacharitamanas::3795.simple_meaning: Ravana rejects advice, insults the messenger, and boasts that no warrior equals him.
ramacharitamanas::3795.simple_insight: Pride makes honest counsel feel like an insult.
ramacharitamanas::3795.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Maricha is trying to warn Ravana away from disaster. Ravana does not listen. He hears caution as disrespect, lashes out with abuse, and inflates his own greatness instead of facing the danger before him.
ramacharitamanas::3795.modern_relevance: Someone points out a blind spot in your plan, and your first reaction is to defend yourself instead of listening. That instant flare of ego can ruin what careful seeing might have saved.
ramacharitamanas::3795.insight: It shows how ego blocks correction and turns guidance into a threat.

ramacharitamanas::3796.verse_sanskrit: तब मारीच हृदयँ अनुमाना। नवहि बिरोधें नहिं कल्याना॥ सस्त्री मर्मी प्रभु सठ धनी। बैद बंदि कबि भानस गुनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3796.verse_hindi: तब मारीच ने हृदय में अनुमान किया कि शस्त्री (शस्त्रधारी), मर्मी (भेद जानने वाला), समर्थ स्वामी, मूर्ख, धनवान, वैद्य, भाट, कवि और रसोइया- इन नौ व्यक्तियों से विरोध (वैर) करने में कल्याण (कुशल) नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3796.english_translation: Then Maricha reasoned in his heart that there is no good in opposing these nine: an armed man, one who knows your secrets, a powerful lord, a fool, a wealthy man, a physician, a bard, a poet, and a cook.
ramacharitamanas::3796.translation_literal: तब (then) / मारीच (Maricha) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अनुमाना (reasoned, inferred) / नवहि (with nine) / बिरोधें (in opposition) / नहिं (not) / कल्याना (good, welfare)॥ / सस्त्री (armed) / मर्मी (one who knows secrets/weak points) / प्रभु (lord, master) / सठ (fool) / धनी (wealthy man) / बैद (physician) / बंदि (bard) / कबि (poet) / भानस (cook) / गुनी (skilled, discerning)॥
ramacharitamanas::3796.speaker: Maricha
ramacharitamanas::3796.essence: Clear seeing can spare you from a fight that cannot be won.
ramacharitamanas::3796.simple_meaning: Maricha sees that opposing certain kinds of people is dangerous and pointless. He understands that some confrontations only lead to harm.
ramacharitamanas::3796.simple_insight: You save yourself by recognizing danger early, before pride turns caution into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3796.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has just been mocked and urged to go home. Maricha, watching the situation, quietly calculates the cost of resistance. He knows that fighting the wrong people brings no benefit, only disaster.
ramacharitamanas::3796.modern_relevance: You’re about to send the angry text, jump into the group argument, or challenge the person who already has leverage over you. A pause now can save you from a costly mistake.
ramacharitamanas::3796.insight: It teaches you to assess power, weakness, and risk before reacting.

ramacharitamanas::3797.verse_sanskrit: उभय भाँति देखा निज मरना। तब ताकिसि रघुनायक सरना॥ उतरु देत मोहि बधब अभागें। कस न मरौं रघुपति सर लागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3797.verse_hindi: जब मारीच ने दोनों प्रकार से अपना मरण देखा, तब उसने श्री रघुनाथजी की शरण तकी (अर्थात उनकी शरण जाने में ही कल्याण समझा)। (सोचा कि) उत्तर देते ही (नाहीं करते ही) यह अभागा मुझे मार डालेगा। फिर श्री रघुनाथजी के बाण लगने से ही क्यों न मरूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3797.english_translation: Seeing death either way, Maricha took refuge in Raghunath. "If I answer, this wicked one will kill me. Why not die by Raghupati's arrow?"
ramacharitamanas::3797.translation_literal: उभय भाँति (in both ways) / देखा (saw) / निज (own) / मरना (death) / तब (then) / ताकिसि (he sought) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / सरना (refuge)॥ / उतरु (answer) / देत (giving) / मोहि (me) / बधब (will kill) / अभागें (the unlucky one) / कस (why) / न (not) / मरौं (should I die) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / सर (arrow) / लागें (struck) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3797.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3797.essence: When escape is impossible, surrender becomes the wisest act.
ramacharitamanas::3797.simple_meaning: Maricha sees that either answer or silence will lead to death, so he chooses Ram's refuge instead of resisting.
ramacharitamanas::3797.simple_insight: Sometimes surrender is not weakness; it is the clearest response when every other move is trapped.
ramacharitamanas::3797.detailed_meaning: Maricha stands trapped between Ravana's threat and Ram's arrow. He sees no escape in either direction, so he turns mentally toward Ram's refuge. This moment shows fear collapsing into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3797.modern_relevance: You are cornered in a conversation where every reply makes things worse. The moment you stop trying to control the damage and choose the truest response, relief begins.
ramacharitamanas::3797.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to surrender when control is no longer possible.

ramacharitamanas::3798.verse_sanskrit: अस जियँ जानि दसानन संगा। चला राम पद प्रेम अभंगा॥ मन अति हरष जनाव न तेही। आजु देखिहउँ परम सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3798.verse_hindi: हृदय में ऐसा समझकर वह रावण के साथ चला। श्री रामजी के चरणों में उसका अखंड प्रेम है। उसके मन में इस बात का अत्यन्त हर्ष है कि आज मैं अपने परम स्नेही श्री रामजी को देखूँगा, किन्तु उसने यह हर्ष रावण को नहीं जनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3798.english_translation: Thinking this in his heart, he went with Ravana. His love for Ram's feet was unbroken. Joy surged in his mind at the thought, 'Today I will see my dearest Ram,' but he did not show that joy to Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::3798.translation_literal: अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / दसानन (Ravana) / संगा (with) / चला (went) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / प्रेम (love) / अभंगा (unbroken) ॥ / मन (mind) / अति (very) / हरष (joy) / जनाव (showed) / न (not) / तेही (that) / ॥ / आजु (today) / देखिहउँ (I will see) / परम (supreme) / सनेही (beloved) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3798.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3798.essence: Devotion can survive even while you walk through danger.
ramacharitamanas::3798.simple_meaning: He walks with Ravana, but his heart belongs to Ram. He hides his joy because he is about to see the one he loves most.
ramacharitamanas::3798.simple_insight: True devotion can stay private, steady, and untouched even in dangerous company.
ramacharitamanas::3798.detailed_meaning: Maricha has already seen that either choice leads to death. So he goes with Ravana, but inwardly he is fixed on Ram. Even while walking toward danger, he feels joy at the thought of seeing Ram again.
ramacharitamanas::3798.modern_relevance: You sit through a tense dinner with people who would mock what you love. Your face stays calm, but inside you hold on to what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3798.insight: It teaches you to keep your deepest allegiance inwardly intact, even when outward circumstances force you to play along.

ramacharitamanas::3799.verse_sanskrit: निज परम प्रीतम देखि लोचन सुफल करि सुख पाइहौं। श्रीसहित अनुज समेत कृपानिकेत पद मन लाइहौं॥ निर्बान दायक क्रोध जा कर भगति अबसहि बसकरी। निज पानि सर संधानि सो मोहि बधिहि सुखसागर हरी॥
ramacharitamanas::3799.verse_hindi: (वह मन ही मन सोचने लगा-) अपने परम प्रियतम को देखकर नेत्रों को सफल करके सुख पाऊँगा। जानकीजी सहित और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी समेत कृपानिधान श्री रामजी के चरणों में मन लगाऊँगा। जिनका क्रोध भी मोक्ष देने वाला है और जिनकी भक्ति उन अवश (किसी के वश में न होने वाले, स्वतंत्र भगवान) को भी वश में करने वाली है, अब वे ही आनंद के समुद्र श्री हरि अपने हाथों से बाण सन्धानकर मेरा वध करेंगे।
ramacharitamanas::3799.english_translation: Seeing my most beloved, I will make my eyes fruitful and find joy. With Sita and Lakshman beside him, I will place my mind at the feet of the compassionate Lord. His anger grants freedom, and his devotion can bring even the unconstrained under control. Now the blissful Lord Hari himself will draw the arrow and strike me down with his own hand.
ramacharitamanas::3799.translation_literal: निज (own) / परम (supreme) / प्रीतम (beloved) / देखि (seeing) / लोचन (eyes) / सुफल (fruitful) / करि (making) / सुख (joy) / पाइहौं (I will attain) / श्रीसहित (with Sita) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / कृपानिकेत (abode of compassion) / पद (feet) / मन (mind) / लाइहौं (I will place) / निर्बान (freedom) / दायक (giver) / क्रोध (anger) / जा कर (whose) / भगति (devotion) / अबसहि (even the unconstrained) / बसकरी (that which brings under control) / निज (own) / पानि (hand) / सर (arrow) / संधानि (drawing) / सो (that) / मोहि (me) / बधिहि (will strike) / सुखसागर (ocean of bliss) / हरी (Hari)
ramacharitamanas::3799.speaker: Maricha
ramacharitamanas::3799.essence: Ram’s nearness is so complete that even death becomes joy.
ramacharitamanas::3799.simple_meaning: Maricha thinks that seeing Ram will fulfill his eyes and bring joy. He also sees Ram as so loving and powerful that even being killed by him feels blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3799.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that even the end feels like grace.
ramacharitamanas::3799.detailed_meaning: Maricha has already seen two sides of death and chosen Ram’s refuge. Now, while walking with Ravana, he imagines the moment he will finally see Ram, Sita, and Lakshman, bow his mind at Ram’s feet, and be struck down by the very Lord whose anger liberates and whose devotion subdues all.
ramacharitamanas::3799.modern_relevance: You meet someone who once hurt you, and instead of replaying the wound, you feel strangely grateful just to be in their presence. This verse holds that impossible tenderness: even judgment from the beloved can feel like mercy.
ramacharitamanas::3799.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to reverent longing, where even punishment becomes a form of blessing.

ramacharitamanas::3800.verse_sanskrit: मम पाछें धर धावत धरें सरासन बान। फिरि फिरि प्रभुहि बिलोकिहउँ धन्य न मो सम आन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3800.verse_hindi: धनुष-बाण धारण किए मेरे पीछे-पीछे पृथ्वी पर (पकड़ने के लिए) दौड़ते हुए प्रभु को मैं फिर-फिरकर देखूँगा। मेरे समान धन्य दूसरा कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3800.english_translation: Holding bow and arrows, the Lord will run behind me on the ground. Again and again I will behold the Lord; no one is as blessed as I am.
ramacharitamanas::3800.translation_literal: मम (my) / पाछें (behind) / धर (holding) / धावत (running) / धरें (holding) / सरासन (bow and arrows) / बान (arrows) / फिरि फिरि (again and again) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकिहउँ (I will behold) / धन्य (blessed) / न (not) / मो (me) / सम (equal) / आन (other)
ramacharitamanas::3800.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3800.essence: Even being chased can feel blessed when the beloved is in sight.
ramacharitamanas::3800.simple_meaning: Ravana imagines Ram chasing him with bow and arrows, yet he feels fortunate because he will keep seeing Ram again and again.
ramacharitamanas::3800.simple_insight: Love can be so intense that even danger feels like a gift.
ramacharitamanas::3800.detailed_meaning: Ravana has come near the forest where Ram lives, and his mind is already caught in a strange devotion. He imagines Ram running after him with weapons, yet all he can feel is joy at the chance to behold Ram again and again.
ramacharitamanas::3800.modern_relevance: You are bracing for a hard conversation, but the other person matters so much that even the tension feels strangely precious.
ramacharitamanas::3800.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing encounter to valuing the chance to see what you love.

ramacharitamanas::3801.verse_sanskrit: तेहि बननिकट दसानन गयऊ। तब मारीच कपटमृग भयऊ॥ अति बिचित्र कछु बरनि न जाई। कनक देह मनि रचित बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3801.verse_hindi: जब रावण उस वन के (जिस वन में श्री रघुनाथजी रहते थे) निकट पहुँचा, तब मारीच कपटमृग बन गया! वह अत्यन्त ही विचित्र था, कुछ वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। सोने का शरीर मणियों से जड़कर बनाया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3801.english_translation: When Ravana reached the edge of that forest, Maricha became the deceitful deer. It was so strange that it cannot be described: its body was golden and set with jewels.
ramacharitamanas::3801.translation_literal: तेहि (that) / बननिकट (near the forest) / दसानन (Ravana) / गयऊ (went) / तब (then) / मारीच (Maricha) / कपटमृग (deceitful deer) / भयऊ (became) / अति (very) / बिचित्र (strange) / कछु (something) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be) / कनक (golden) / देह (body) / मनि (jewels) / रचित (adorned) / बनाई (made)
ramacharitamanas::3801.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3801.essence: A dazzling disguise can hide a dangerous intention.
ramacharitamanas::3801.simple_meaning: Ravana reached the forest edge, and Maricha took the form of a dazzling golden deer that was hard to describe.
ramacharitamanas::3801.simple_insight: Not every beautiful thing is safe to trust.
ramacharitamanas::3801.detailed_meaning: Ravana arrives near the forest where Ram lives, and Maricha transforms into a glittering golden deer to lure Sita. The verse is scene-setting: it prepares the trap that will pull the story toward abduction.
ramacharitamanas::3801.modern_relevance: A message arrives with perfect grammar, a polished logo, and exactly the promise you wanted. The shine is the point — and that is why you should look twice.
ramacharitamanas::3801.insight: It trains you to notice how beauty can be used as bait.

ramacharitamanas::3802.verse_sanskrit: सीता परम रुचिर मृग देखा। अंग अंग सुमनोहर बेषा॥ सुनहु देव रघुबीर कृपाला। एहि मृग कर अति सुंदर छाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3802.verse_hindi: सीताजी ने उस परम सुंदर हिरन को देखा, जिसके अंग-अंग की छटा अत्यन्त मनोहर थी। (वे कहने लगीं-) हे देव! हे कृपालु रघुवीर! सुनिए। इस मृग की छाल बहुत ही सुंदर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3802.english_translation: Sita saw that exceedingly beautiful deer, with every limb charming to the eye. She said, “Listen, O divine, compassionate Raghuvir. This deer’s hide is very beautiful.”
ramacharitamanas::3802.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / परम (supremely) / रुचिर (beautiful) / मृग (deer) / देखा (saw) / अंग (limb) / अंग (limb) / सुमनोहर (very pleasing) / बेषा (form, appearance) / सुनहु (listen) / देव (divine one) / रघुबीर (Raghu's hero, Ram) / कृपाला (compassionate) / एहि (this) / मृग (deer) / कर (of) / अति (very) / सुंदर (beautiful) / छाला (hide)
ramacharitamanas::3802.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3802.essence: What looks harmless can be the very thing that separates you from what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3802.simple_meaning: Sita is captivated by the beautiful deer and asks Ram to bring back its lovely hide.
ramacharitamanas::3802.simple_insight: Beauty can open the door to danger when desire slips past discernment.
ramacharitamanas::3802.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Panchavati, Maricha has taken the form of a dazzling deer to lure Ram away. Sita sees only beauty and asks Ram to get the deer’s skin, not yet seeing the trap hidden inside the charm.
ramacharitamanas::3802.modern_relevance: You click on something dazzling because it feels harmless and lovely. Only later do you realize the shine was the bait.
ramacharitamanas::3802.insight: It shows how attraction can override caution and pull attention toward a hidden snare.

ramacharitamanas::3803.verse_sanskrit: सत्यसंध प्रभु बधि करि एही। आनहु चर्म कहति बैदेही॥ तब रघुपति जानत सब कारन। उठे हरषि सुर काजु सँवारन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3803.verse_hindi: जानकीजी ने कहा- हे सत्यप्रतिज्ञ प्रभो! इसको मारकर इसका चमड़ा ला दीजिए। तब श्री रघुनाथजी (मारीच के कपटमृग बनने का) सब कारण जानते हुए भी, देवताओं का कार्य बनाने के लिए हर्षित होकर उठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3803.english_translation: Sita said, “O truthful Lord, kill this one and bring me its skin.” Then Raghupati, knowing all the reason, rose gladly to complete the gods’ task.
ramacharitamanas::3803.translation_literal: सत्यसंध (bound to truth) / प्रभु (Lord) / बधि करि (having killed) / एही (this one) / आनहु (bring) / चर्म (skin) / कहति (saying) / बैदेही (Sita)॥ / तब (then) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / जानत (knowing) / सब (all) / कारन (cause) / उठे (rose) / हरषि (joyfully) / सुर (gods) / काजु (task) / सँवारन (to accomplish)
ramacharitamanas::3803.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3803.essence: Knowing the trick, he still moves to fulfill the larger plan.
ramacharitamanas::3803.simple_meaning: Sita asks Ram to kill the deer and bring back its skin. Ram already knows the trick, yet he rises gladly to help the divine plan unfold.
ramacharitamanas::3803.simple_insight: Even when you see the trap, you may still step into it for a higher purpose.
ramacharitamanas::3803.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is enchanted by Maricha’s dazzling disguise and asks Ram to kill the deer. Ram understands the deception immediately, but he still rises with joy, because this moment is part of the larger cosmic drama moving toward Ravana’s defeat.
ramacharitamanas::3803.modern_relevance: You can spot the manipulation in the room and still choose the harder, wiser response because protecting what matters is more important than proving you were right.
ramacharitamanas::3803.insight: It shows that clear seeing does not always lead to refusal; sometimes it leads to purposeful action.

ramacharitamanas::3804.verse_sanskrit: मृग बिलोकि कटि परिकर बाँधा। करतल चाप रुचिर सर साँधा॥ प्रभु लछिमनहि कहा समुझाई। फिरत बिपिन निसिचर बहु भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3804.verse_hindi: हिरन को देखकर श्री रामजी ने कमर में फेंटा बाँधा और हाथ में धनुष लेकर उस पर सुंदर (दिव्य) बाण चढ़ाया। फिर प्रभु ने लक्ष्मणजी को समझाकर कहा- हे भाई! वन में बहुत से राक्षस फिरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3804.english_translation: Seeing the deer, Ram tied his waist cloth and fitted a beautiful arrow to his bow. Then the Lord explained to Lakshman, 'Brother, many demons roam this forest.'
ramacharitamanas::3804.translation_literal: मृग (deer) / बिलोकि (seeing) / कटि (waist) / परिकर (cloth-belt) / बाँधा (tied) / करतल (in his hand) / चाप (bow) / रुचिर (beautiful) / सर (arrow) / साँधा (fitted) / प्रभु (the Lord) / लछिमनहि (to Lakshman) / कहा (said) / समुझाई (explaining) / फिरत (roaming) / बिपिन (forest) / निसिचर (demons) / बहु (many) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::3804.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3804.essence: Beauty can hide danger, so steady readiness matters.
ramacharitamanas::3804.simple_meaning: Ram gets ready to shoot the deer and warns Lakshman that many dangerous beings roam the forest.
ramacharitamanas::3804.simple_insight: Stay alert when a situation seems innocent but carries hidden danger.
ramacharitamanas::3804.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the beautiful deer has already caught Sita's attention. Ram quickly arms himself and quietly warns Lakshman, because he sees the deeper threat behind the scene. This verse moves the story from attraction to danger.
ramacharitamanas::3804.modern_relevance: You spot the charming offer, but something feels off. Before you commit, you prepare, check the risk, and tell the person beside you to stay alert.
ramacharitamanas::3804.insight: It teaches you to read beneath appearances and respond before danger fully reveals itself.

ramacharitamanas::3805.verse_sanskrit: सीता केरि करेहु रखवारी। बुधि बिबेक बल समय बिचारी॥ प्रभुहि बिलोकि चला मृग भाजी। धाए रामु सरासन साजी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3805.verse_hindi: तुम बुद्धि और विवेक के द्वारा बल और समय का विचार करके सीताजी की रखवाली करना। प्रभु को देखकर मृग भाग चला। श्री रामचन्द्रजी भी धनुष चढ़ाकर उसके पीछे दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3805.english_translation: Guard Sita with wisdom, discernment, strength, and attention to the moment. Seeing the Lord, the deer ran; Ram also ran after it, bow ready.
ramacharitamanas::3805.translation_literal: सीता केरि (of Sita) / करेहु (do) / रखवारी (guarding) / बुधि (wisdom) / बिबेक (discernment) / बल (strength) / समय (time, occasion) / बिचारी (considering) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / चला (ran) / मृग (deer) / भाजी (fleeing) / धाए (ran) / रामु (Ram) / सरासन (with bow) / साजी (equipped, ready)
ramacharitamanas::3805.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3805.essence: Protection works only when wisdom, timing, and strength move together.
ramacharitamanas::3805.simple_meaning: Keep watch over Sita using wisdom, discernment, strength, and good timing. The deer sees Ram and runs; Ram immediately gives chase.
ramacharitamanas::3805.simple_insight: Real protection needs clear judgment, not just force.
ramacharitamanas::3805.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has already seen through the golden deer, and Lakshman is being told to stay alert and protect Sita. The moment matters because the chase is beginning, and the smallest lapse will open the door to Ravana's deception.
ramacharitamanas::3805.modern_relevance: You leave someone you love alone for just a minute, trusting the situation is harmless. Later you realise the danger was never loud — it was clever. This verse asks for alert care, not sleepy confidence.
ramacharitamanas::3805.insight: It teaches you to protect what matters by reading the moment clearly, not by reacting late.

ramacharitamanas::3806.verse_sanskrit: निगम नेति सिव ध्यान न पावा। मायामृग पाछें सो धावा॥ कबहुँ निकट पुनि दूरि पराई। कबहुँक प्रगटइ कबहुँ छपाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3806.verse_hindi: वेद जिनके विषय में 'नेति-नेति' कहकर रह जाते हैं और शिवजी भी जिन्हें ध्यान में नहीं पाते (अर्थात जो मन और वाणी से नितान्त परे हैं), वे ही श्री रामजी माया से बने हुए मृग के पीछे दौड़ रहे हैं। वह कभी निकट आ जाता है और फिर दूर भाग जाता है। कभी तो प्रकट हो जाता है और कभी छिप जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3806.english_translation: The Vedas stop at "not this, not this," and Shiva cannot reach it in meditation. Yet Ram chases the deer made of illusion. Sometimes it comes near, sometimes it goes far away; sometimes it appears, sometimes it hides.
ramacharitamanas::3806.translation_literal: निगम (the Vedas) / नेति (not this) / सिव (Shiva) / ध्यान (meditation) / न पावा (did not attain) / माया-मृग (the illusion-deer) / पाछें (after) / सो (he) / धावा (ran) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / निकट (near) / पुनि (again) / दूरि (far) / पराई (went away) / कबहुँक (sometimes) / प्रगटइ (appears) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / छपाई (hides)
ramacharitamanas::3806.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3806.essence: The infinite can still be drawn into a game of appearances.
ramacharitamanas::3806.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond all description, yet he is now chasing the illusion-deer that keeps appearing and disappearing.
ramacharitamanas::3806.simple_insight: Even the limitless can enter the smallest human drama without losing its greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3806.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has already seen through the deer’s strange nature, but the illusion keeps luring him forward. Tulsidas pauses the chase to show the paradox: the one beyond the Vedas and meditation is now running after a trick of appearance and concealment.
ramacharitamanas::3806.modern_relevance: You know that moment when you keep checking your phone because something keeps almost-appearing, then vanishing again. The mind stays hooked by what it cannot quite hold.
ramacharitamanas::3806.insight: It shifts attention from the object’s trickery to the mind’s attachment to what flickers.

ramacharitamanas::3807.verse_sanskrit: प्रगटत दुरत करत छल भूरी। एहि बिधि प्रभुहि गयउ लै दूरी॥ तब तकि राम कठिन सर मारा। धरनि परेउ करि घोर पुकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3807.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार प्रकट होता और छिपता हुआ तथा बहुतेरे छल करता हुआ वह प्रभु को दूर ले गया। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तक कर (निशाना साधकर) कठोर बाण मारा, (जिसके लगते ही) वह घोर शब्द करके पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3807.english_translation: Moving in and out of sight, he used many tricks to lead the Lord farther away. Then Ram aimed carefully and shot a fierce arrow; struck by it, he fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
ramacharitamanas::3807.translation_literal: प्रगटत (appearing) / दुरत (at a distance) / करत (doing) / छल (deceit) / भूरी (many, abundant) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / गयउ (went) / लै (taking) / दूरी (far away) / तब (then) / तकि (aiming) / राम (Ram) / कठिन (hard, forceful) / सर (arrow) / मारा (struck) / धरनि (earth) / परेउ (fell) / करि (making) / घोर (terrible) / पुकारा (cry)
ramacharitamanas::3807.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3807.essence: What keeps deceiving you can still be brought down.
ramacharitamanas::3807.simple_meaning: The deer kept luring Ram farther away by appearing, disappearing, and tricking him. Ram then shot it with a powerful arrow, and it fell down crying out loudly.
ramacharitamanas::3807.simple_insight: Deception can only run so far before reality catches up.
ramacharitamanas::3807.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the illusory deer keeps shifting shape and pulling Ram away from Lakshman and Sita. Ram finally sees through the trick, draws his bow, and strikes it down. This is the moment the diversion ends.
ramacharitamanas::3807.modern_relevance: A message keeps pinging, a tab keeps reopening, and you keep getting pulled away from what matters. Eventually, the distraction has to be named and cut off.
ramacharitamanas::3807.insight: It shifts attention from the lure of appearances to the need for decisive action.

ramacharitamanas::3808.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन कर प्रथमहिं लै नामा। पाछें सुमिरेसि मन महुँ रामा॥ प्रान तजत प्रगटेसि निज देहा। सुमिरेसि रामु समेत सनेहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3808.verse_hindi: पहले लक्ष्मणजी का नाम लेकर उसने पीछे मन में श्री रामजी का स्मरण किया। प्राण त्याग करते समय उसने अपना (राक्षसी) शरीर प्रकट किया और प्रेम सहित श्री रामजी का स्मरण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3808.english_translation: She first took Lakshman's name, then remembered Ram in her mind. As she gave up her life, she revealed her own body and remembered Ram with love.
ramacharitamanas::3808.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / कर (of) / प्रथमहिं (first) / लै (taking) / नामा (name) / पाछें (afterward) / सुमिरेसि (she remembered) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / रामा (Ram) ॥ प्रान (life-breath) / तजत (giving up) / प्रगटेसि (revealed) / निज (own) / देहा (body) ॥ सुमिरेसि (she remembered) / रामु (Ram) / समेत (together with) / सनेहा (love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3808.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3808.essence: What the heart remembers at the end reveals what it truly served.
ramacharitamanas::3808.simple_meaning: At the moment of death, she first called on Lakshman and then remembered Ram with love. Even in that final instant, devotion remained alive.
ramacharitamanas::3808.simple_insight: What you love most can stay with you even at the edge of life.
ramacharitamanas::3808.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the demoness who had deceived Ram is dying after being struck down. Even as her body falls away, her mind turns to Lakshman first and then to Ram. The scene reveals that the heart's final memory matters.
ramacharitamanas::3808.modern_relevance: A person can spend years chasing approval, then suddenly face a hospital room, a breakup, or a grave mistake. In that last raw moment, what the mind returns to shows what truly held it.
ramacharitamanas::3808.insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to the final inward attachment that shapes the heart.

ramacharitamanas::3809.verse_sanskrit: अंतर प्रेम तासु पहिचाना। मुनि दुर्लभ गति दीन्हि सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3809.verse_hindi: सुजान (सर्वज्ञ) श्री रामजी ने उसके हृदय के प्रेम को पहचानकर उसे वह गति (अपना परमपद) दी जो मुनियों को भी दुर्लभ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3809.english_translation: The all-knowing Lord recognized his hidden love and gave him the rare state that even sages find hard to attain.
ramacharitamanas::3809.translation_literal: अंतर (within) / प्रेम (love) / तासु (his) / पहिचाना (recognized) / मुनि (sages) / दुर्लभ (rare, hard to obtain) / गति (state, attainment) / दीन्हि (gave) / सुजाना (the all-knowing one)
ramacharitamanas::3809.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3809.essence: Hidden devotion can receive the highest grace.
ramacharitamanas::3809.simple_meaning: Ram recognized the warrior's hidden devotion and granted him a rare spiritual state beyond ordinary reach.
ramacharitamanas::3809.simple_insight: Quiet love matters more than display; what is sincere can be rewarded beyond expectation.
ramacharitamanas::3809.detailed_meaning: After the fallen enemy reveals his devotion at the moment of death, Ram sees the love hidden in his heart. In the forest battle, that inner feeling matters more than his outer form, and Ram grants him a rare state even sages struggle to attain.
ramacharitamanas::3809.modern_relevance: You do the right thing without anyone noticing, and it still changes you. A quiet act of loyalty, a private prayer, a hidden kindness — none of it is wasted.
ramacharitamanas::3809.insight: It shifts attention from outer identity to the sincerity beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::3810.verse_sanskrit: बिपुल सुमर सुर बरषहिं गावहिं प्रभु गुन गाथ। निज पद दीन्ह असुर कहुँ दीनबंधु रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3810.verse_hindi: देवता बहुत से फूल बरसा रहे हैं और प्रभु के गुणों की गाथाएँ (स्तुतियाँ) गा रहे हैं (कि) श्री रघुनाथजी ऐसे दीनबन्धु हैं कि उन्होंने असुर को भी अपना परम पद दे दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3810.english_translation: Many radiant beings shower flowers and sing the Lord's praise: Raghunath gave even an asura his highest state, because he is the friend of the humble.
ramacharitamanas::3810.translation_literal: बिपुल (many) / सुमर (flowers) / सुर (radiant beings) / बरषहिं (shower) / गावहिं (sing) / प्रभु (Lord) / गुन (qualities) / गाथ (song) / निज (own) / पद (state/abode) / दीन्ह (gave) / असुर (asura) / कहुँ (to) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::3810.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3810.essence: Ram's mercy can raise even an enemy into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3810.simple_meaning: Heavenly beings celebrate Ram because he gave even an asura a supreme state. Ram is the friend of the humble and the fallen.
ramacharitamanas::3810.simple_insight: You are never too far gone for grace to reach you.
ramacharitamanas::3810.detailed_meaning: After the asura dies with Ram on his lips, the story pauses in awe. Radiant beings shower flowers and sing because Ram sees the hidden devotion in a feared enemy and gives him the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::3810.modern_relevance: You write someone off after their worst mistake, but they surprise everyone with one honest act of remorse. This verse says mercy can see deeper than reputation.
ramacharitamanas::3810.insight: It shifts you from judging by outer identity to recognising inner turning and the possibility of transformation.

ramacharitamanas::3811.verse_sanskrit: खल बधि तुरत फिरे रघुबीरा। सोह चाप कर कटि तूनीरा॥ आरत गिरा सुनी जब सीता। कह लछिमन सन परम सभीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3811.verse_hindi: दुष्ट मारीच को मारकर श्री रघुवीर तुरंत लौट पड़े। हाथ में धनुष और कमर में तरकस शोभा दे रहा है। इधर जब सीताजी ने दुःखभरी वाणी (मरते समय मारीच की 'हा लक्ष्मण' की आवाज) सुनी तो वे बहुत ही भयभीत होकर लक्ष्मणजी से कहने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3811.english_translation: Having slain the wicked one, Raghuvira returned at once, with bow in hand and quiver at his waist. Then, hearing the sorrowful cry, Sita became deeply frightened and said to Lakshmana:
ramacharitamanas::3811.translation_literal: खल (wicked one) / बधि (having slain) / तुरत (at once) / फिरे (returned) / रघुबीरा (Raghuvira) / सोह (shone) / चाप (bow) / कर (in hand) / कटि (at the waist) / तूनीरा (quiver) । आरत (sorrowful) / गिरा (cry) / सुनी (having heard) / जब (when) / सीता (Sita) / कह (said) / लछिमन सन (to Lakshmana) / परम (very) / सभीता (frightened)
ramacharitamanas::3811.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3811.essence: A single cry can turn calm into fear.
ramacharitamanas::3811.simple_meaning: Ram returns after killing the demon, and Sita is startled by the cry she hears. She turns to Lakshmana in fear.
ramacharitamanas::3811.simple_insight: Fear can spread fast, even when the danger is already gone.
ramacharitamanas::3811.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has just killed Maricha and returned with his bow and quiver still shining. Sita hears the dying cry and, not knowing what happened, is suddenly frightened. The scene moves straight into her warning to Lakshmana.
ramacharitamanas::3811.modern_relevance: You hear a panicked voice from another room and your body tightens before you know why. Fear often arrives before facts do.
ramacharitamanas::3811.insight: It shows how quickly the mind reacts to alarming sound, even without understanding the full situation.

ramacharitamanas::3812.verse_sanskrit: जाहु बेगि संकट अति भ्राता। लछिमन बिहसि कहा सुनु माता॥ भृकुटि बिलास सृष्टि लय होई। सपनेहुँ संकट परइ कि सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3812.verse_hindi: तुम शीघ्र जाओ, तुम्हारे भाई बड़े संकट में हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर कहा- हे माता! सुनो, जिनके भ्रृकुटि विलास (भौं के इशारे) मात्र से सारी सृष्टि का लय (प्रलय) हो जाता है, वे श्री रामजी क्या कभी स्वप्न में भी संकट में पड़ सकते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3812.english_translation: Go quickly, brother, for your brother is in great danger. Lakshman smiled and said, "Listen, Mother: can those on whose brows the mere play of an eyebrow brings about the dissolution of creation ever be in danger, even in a dream?"
ramacharitamanas::3812.translation_literal: जाहु (go) / बेगि (quickly) / संकट (danger) / अति (very great) / भ्राता (brother) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / बिहसि (smiling) / कहा (said) / सुनु (listen) / माता (Mother) / भृकुटि (eyebrow) / बिलास (play) / सृष्टि (creation) / लय (dissolution) / होई (happens) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / संकट (danger) / परइ (falls) / कि (whether) / सोई (they)
ramacharitamanas::3812.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3812.essence: Ram's smallest gesture is greater than the danger itself.
ramacharitamanas::3812.simple_meaning: Lakshman reassures Sita that Ram cannot truly be threatened, because even the slightest movement of Ram's brow can dissolve creation itself.
ramacharitamanas::3812.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when you remember who holds the larger power.
ramacharitamanas::3812.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita senses danger and urges Lakshman to go at once. Lakshman answers with calm confidence, reminding her that Ram is not an ordinary man. His reply is less a boast than a devotional certainty about Ram's cosmic power.
ramacharitamanas::3812.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with bad news, and panic starts to rise before you even know the facts. This verse reminds you to breathe and remember what is actually bigger than the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3812.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate panic to trust in a reality larger than the threat.

ramacharitamanas::3813.verse_sanskrit: मरम बचन जब सीता बोला। हरि प्रेरित लछिमन मन डोला॥ बन दिसि देव सौंपि सब काहू। चले जहाँ रावन ससि राहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3813.verse_hindi: इस पर जब सीताजी कुछ मर्म वचन (हृदय में चुभने वाले वचन) कहने लगीं, तब भगवान की प्रेरणा से लक्ष्मणजी का मन भी चंचल हो उठा। वे श्री सीताजी को वन और दिशाओं के देवताओं को सौंपकर वहाँ चले, जहाँ रावण रूपी चन्द्रमा के लिए राहु रूप श्री रामजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3813.english_translation: When Sita spoke words that struck the heart, Lakshman's mind wavered under the divine's prompting. Entrusting Sita to the forest spirits and all directions, he went where Ravana was like Rahu to the moon.
ramacharitamanas::3813.translation_literal: मरम (heart-striking) / बचन (words) / जब (when) / सीता (Sita) / बोला (spoke) / हरि (the divine) / प्रेरित (prompted) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / मन (mind) / डोला (wavered) / बन (forest) / दिसि (directions) / देव (deities/spirits) / सौंपि (entrusting) / सब (all) / काहू (to whom) / चले (went) / जहाँ (where) / रावन (Ravana) / ससि (moon) / राहू (Rahu)
ramacharitamanas::3813.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3813.essence: A shaken mind can still obey what must be done.
ramacharitamanas::3813.simple_meaning: Sita’s painful words unsettle Lakshman, and he leaves at once, placing her under divine and forest protection before going to face Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::3813.simple_insight: Even a loyal heart can tremble, but duty still moves it forward.
ramacharitamanas::3813.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita’s anxious words cut deeply into Lakshman. Moved by the divine, he hands her care to the forest guardians and rushes off toward Ravana, setting up the danger that will follow.
ramacharitamanas::3813.modern_relevance: Your sibling says one sharp sentence, and your whole body tightens. You still lock the door, hand over the keys, and go do what cannot wait.
ramacharitamanas::3813.insight: It shows loyalty under pressure: feeling shaken does not cancel immediate action.

ramacharitamanas::3814.verse_sanskrit: सून बीच दसकंधर देखा। आवा निकट जती कें बेषा॥ जाकें डर सुर असुर डेराहीं। निसि न नीद दिन अन्न न खाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3814.verse_hindi: रावण सूना मौका देखकर यति (संन्यासी) के वेष में श्री सीताजी के समीप आया, जिसके डर से देवता और दैत्य तक इतना डरते हैं कि रात को नींद नहीं आती और दिन में (भरपेट) अन्न नहीं खाते- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3814.english_translation: Ravana saw the chance when no one was around and came near Sita disguised as a renunciant. Even the radiant beings and shadow beings fear him so much that they lose sleep at night and cannot eat fully by day.
ramacharitamanas::3814.translation_literal: सून (empty / unguarded) / बीच (in the midst) / दसकंधर (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / देखा (saw) / आवा (came) / निकट (near) / जती (renunciant) / कें (in the) / बेषा (disguise) ॥ / जाकें (whose) / डर (fear) / सुर (radiant beings) / असुर (shadow beings) / डेराहीं (are afraid) / निसि (at night) / न (not) / नीद (sleep) / दिन (by day) / अन्न (food) / न (not) / खाहीं (eat) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3814.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3814.simple_meaning: Ravana takes advantage of the empty moment and approaches Sita in the disguise of a renunciant. His terrifying power is so great that even the radiant and shadow beings are restless before him.
ramacharitamanas::3814.simple_insight: Unchecked power looks strongest when it hides itself.
ramacharitamanas::3814.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is momentarily unguarded. Ravana, wearing the dress of a renunciant, slips close to her. The verse is not teaching a principle yet; it is building the danger and deceit that make the next moment devastating.
ramacharitamanas::3814.modern_relevance: A person who seems harmless at the door may be carrying bad intent underneath. This verse feels like the instant your guard drops and you realise the threat was already inside the room.
ramacharitamanas::3814.insight: It shows how danger often enters through disguise, not force.

ramacharitamanas::3815.verse_sanskrit: सो दससीस स्वान की नाईं। इत उत चितइ चला भड़िहाईं॥ इमि कुपंथ पग देत खगेसा। रह न तेज तन बुधि बल लेसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3815.verse_hindi: वही दस सिर वाला रावण कुत्ते की तरह इधर-उधर ताकता हुआ भड़िहाई (चोरी) के लिए चला। (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! इस प्रकार कुमार्ग पर पैर रखते ही शरीर में तेज तथा बुद्धि एवं बल का लेश भी नहीं रह जाता ॥ सूना पाकर कुत्ता चुपके से बर्तन-भाँड़ों में मुँह डालकर कुछ चुरा ले जाता है। उसे 'भड़िहाई' कहते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::3815.english_translation: Ravana, the ten-headed one, moved like a dog, looking here and there for a chance to steal. Thus, O Garuda, when one sets foot on the wrong path, even a trace of brilliance, clear judgment, and strength does not remain in the body.
ramacharitamanas::3815.translation_literal: सो (that) / दससीस (ten-headed one) / स्वान (dog) / की नाईं (like) / इत उत (here and there) / चितइ (looking) / चला (went) / भड़िहाईं (for theft / sneaking) / इमि (thus) / कुपंथ (wrong path) / पग (foot) / देत (placing) / खगेसा (O lord of birds) / रह (remains) / न (not) / तेज (brilliance) / तन (in the body) / बुधि (discerning mind) / बल (strength) / लेसा (even a trace)
ramacharitamanas::3815.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::3815.essence: Wrong action quietly strips away the power to see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3815.simple_meaning: Ravana is described as sneaking around like a dog looking for theft. The deeper point is that choosing the wrong path quickly drains your brilliance, judgment, and strength.
ramacharitamanas::3815.simple_insight: You can feel the cost of a bad choice before the consequences fully arrive.
ramacharitamanas::3815.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has come near Sita in disguise, and Kak Bhushundi turns to Garuda to explain what this kind of desire does to a person. The moment someone steps onto a crooked path, inner power begins to collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3815.modern_relevance: You tell one small lie to cover another, then notice how quickly your confidence starts to thin out. The verse catches that exact moment when bad choices begin to hollow you from within.
ramacharitamanas::3815.insight: It shifts attention from the outward act to the inner damage that follows unethical movement.

ramacharitamanas::3816.verse_sanskrit: नाना बिधि करि कथा सुहाई। राजनीति भय प्रीति देखाई॥ कह सीता सुनु जती गोसाईं। बोलेहु बचन दुष्ट की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3816.verse_hindi: रावण ने अनेकों प्रकार की सुहावनी कथाएँ रचकर सीताजी को राजनीति, भय और प्रेम दिखलाया। सीताजी ने कहा- हे यति गोसाईं! सुनो, तुमने तो दुष्ट की तरह वचन कहे॥6।
ramacharitamanas::3816.english_translation: Ravana used many charming stories to show Sita politics, fear, and love. Sita said, “O ascetic and lord, listen: you have spoken like a wicked man.”
ramacharitamanas::3816.translation_literal: नाना बिधि (in many ways) / करि (having done) / कथा (stories) / सुहाई (pleasant) / राजनीति (statecraft) / भय (fear) / प्रीति (love) / देखाई (showed) / कह (said) / सीता (Sita) / सुनु (listen) / जती (ascetic) / गोसाईं (lord) / बोलेहु (you spoke) / बचन (words) / दुष्ट (wicked) / की नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::3816.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3816.essence: False sweetness cannot hide a crooked intent.
ramacharitamanas::3816.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to win Sita with polished words, fear, and false affection. Sita sees through it and calls out the wickedness behind his speech.
ramacharitamanas::3816.simple_insight: Charm can hide harm, but clear seeing cuts through it.
ramacharitamanas::3816.detailed_meaning: In the Ashoka grove, Ravana approaches Sita in disguise and tries every tactic—sweet talk, politics, fear, and pretended affection. Sita answers from steady discernment, naming his words for what they are before he drops the disguise.
ramacharitamanas::3816.modern_relevance: Someone floods your inbox with polite language, pressure, and flattery to get what they want. You feel the mismatch before you can explain it. Sita shows how to name manipulation without getting pulled in.
ramacharitamanas::3816.insight: It trains you to trust clear seeing over persuasive packaging.

ramacharitamanas::3817.verse_sanskrit: तब रावन निज रूप देखावा। भई सभय जब नाम सुनावा॥ कह सीता धरि धीरजु गाढ़ा। आइ गयउ प्रभु रहु खल ठाढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3817.verse_hindi: तब रावण ने अपना असली रूप दिखलाया और जब नाम सुनाया तब तो सीताजी भयभीत हो गईं। उन्होंने गहरा धीरज धरकर कहा- 'अरे दुष्ट! खड़ा तो रह, प्रभु आ गए' ॥
ramacharitamanas::3817.english_translation: Then Ravana showed his true form, and when he announced his name, Sita became afraid. Gathering deep courage, she said, 'O wicked one, stand still — the Lord has arrived.'
ramacharitamanas::3817.translation_literal: तब (then) / रावन (Ravana) / निज रूप (his own form) / देखावा (showed) / भई (became) / सभय (afraid) / जब (when) / नाम (name) / सुनावा (was announced) / कह (said) / सीता (Sita) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (courage / patience) / गाढ़ा (firm, deep) / आइ (has come) / गयउ (has gone / has arrived) / प्रभु (the Lord) / रहु (stay) / खल (wicked one) / ठाढ़ा (standing)
ramacharitamanas::3817.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3817.essence: Courage can stand its ground even while fear is present.
ramacharitamanas::3817.simple_meaning: Ravana reveals his true nature, but Sita keeps her courage. Even while afraid, she tells him to stand still because Ram has already arrived.
ramacharitamanas::3817.simple_insight: Fear does not have to become collapse. You can stay steady long enough for help to meet you.
ramacharitamanas::3817.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana drops his disguise and exposes himself. Sita feels fear, but she gathers herself and speaks with firm courage. This moment turns her waiting into active strength, even before Ram appears.
ramacharitamanas::3817.modern_relevance: A threatening email lands in your inbox and your stomach drops, but you take one breath before replying. That pause can keep fear from steering the whole day.
ramacharitamanas::3817.insight: It teaches you to steady yourself under pressure instead of reacting from panic.

ramacharitamanas::3818.verse_sanskrit: जिमि हरिबधुहि छुद्र सस चाहा। भएसि कालबस निसिचर नाहा॥ सुनत बचन दससीस रिसाना। मन महुँ चरन बंदि सुख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3818.verse_hindi: जैसे सिंह की स्त्री को तुच्छ खरगोश चाहे, वैसे ही अरे राक्षसराज! तू (मेरी चाह करके) काल के वश हुआ है। ये वचन सुनते ही रावण को क्रोध आ गया, परन्तु मन में उसने सीताजी के चरणों की वंदना करके सुख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3818.english_translation: Like a jackal coveting a lioness, you, lord of demons, have fallen under Time’s control. Hearing this, Ravana burned with anger, yet in his mind he bowed to Sita’s feet and found a strange peace.
ramacharitamanas::3818.translation_literal: जिमि (like) / हरिबधुहि (to the lioness) / छुद्र (small) / सस (jackal) / चाहा (desired) / भएसि (you became) / कालबस (under the control of Time) / निसिचर नाहा (lord of demons) ॥ / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (the words) / दससीस (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / रिसाना (became angry) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / सुख (peace) / माना (felt) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3818.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3818.essence: Courage can expose arrogance so completely that anger and reverence appear together.
ramacharitamanas::3818.simple_meaning: Sita compares Ravana’s desire for her to a jackal wanting a lioness, then says he is already trapped by Time. Ravana outwardly rages, but inwardly feels humbled before her.
ramacharitamanas::3818.simple_insight: False power can still be pierced by a single fearless truth.
ramacharitamanas::3818.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has dropped all pretence and tried to terrify Sita. She answers without flinching, naming his desire as absurd and his ruin as already sealed. Her words sting him so deeply that anger rises, yet her moral force still unsettles him.
ramacharitamanas::3818.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a heated text thread, trying to dominate with bluster. You answer once, cleanly, and their confidence cracks because they know you are not afraid.
ramacharitamanas::3818.insight: It shifts the mind from being intimidated by force to seeing through it instantly.

ramacharitamanas::3819.verse_sanskrit: क्रोधवंत तब रावन लीन्हिसि रथ बैठाइ। चला गगनपथ आतुर भयँ रथ हाँकि न जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3819.verse_hindi: फिर क्रोध में भरकर रावण ने सीताजी को रथ पर बैठा लिया और वह बड़ी उतावली के साथ आकाश मार्ग से चला, किन्तु डर के मारे उससे रथ हाँका नहीं जाता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3819.english_translation: Then, in rage, Ravana lifted Sita onto his chariot. He hurried through the sky-route, but fear made him unable to drive the chariot properly.
ramacharitamanas::3819.translation_literal: क्रोधवंत (filled with rage) / तब (then) / रावन (Ravana) / लीन्हिसि (lifted) / रथ (chariot) / बैठाइ (having seated) / चला (moved off) / गगनपथ (sky-path) / आतुर (hurried, agitated) / भयँ (with fear) / रथ (chariot) / हाँकि (driving) / न जाइ (could not)
ramacharitamanas::3819.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3819.essence: Rage can seize someone, but fear still drives the chariot.
ramacharitamanas::3819.simple_meaning: Ravana, driven by anger and fear, abducts Sita and rushes away, but his own fear makes him unstable even as he flees.
ramacharitamanas::3819.simple_insight: Panic can make even power feel clumsy and unsafe.
ramacharitamanas::3819.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has finally seized Sita and placed her on his chariot. He escapes through the sky in agitation, but the fear inside him is already undoing his triumph. This verse marks the tense moment of abduction before Sita's lament begins.
ramacharitamanas::3819.modern_relevance: You storm out after a cruel argument, heart racing, only to realise your anger has made every next step shaky.
ramacharitamanas::3819.insight: It shows how domination born of rage is never steady; fear rides inside it and weakens every move.

ramacharitamanas::3820.verse_sanskrit: हा जग एक बीर रघुराया। केहिं अपराध बिसारेहु दाया॥ आरति हरन सरन सुखदायक। हा रघुकुल सरोज दिननायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::3820.verse_hindi: (सीताजी विलाप कर रही थीं-) हा जगत के अद्वितीय वीर श्री रघुनाथजी! आपने किस अपराध से मुझ पर दया भुला दी। हे दुःखों के हरने वाले, हे शरणागत को सुख देने वाले, हा रघुकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3820.english_translation: Alas, O unique hero of the world, Raghunath! For what fault have you forgotten your mercy toward me? O remover of suffering, giver of comfort to those who seek refuge, alas, sun of the lotus-clan of Raghu!
ramacharitamanas::3820.translation_literal: हा (alas) / जग (world) / एक (one) / बीर (hero) / रघुराया (Raghunath) / केहिं (for what) / अपराध (fault) / बिसारेहु (have you forgotten) / दाया (mercy)॥ / आरति (suffering) / हरन (removing) / सरन (refuge) / सुखदायक (giver of comfort) / हा (alas) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / सरोज (lotus) / दिननायक (sun)
ramacharitamanas::3820.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3820.essence: Love in exile still calls the beloved by name.
ramacharitamanas::3820.simple_meaning: Sita cries out to Ram, asking why his mercy has been forgotten and pleading to the one who removes suffering and comforts those who take refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3820.simple_insight: Even in heartbreak, the heart reaches first for the one it trusts most.
ramacharitamanas::3820.detailed_meaning: Sita is alone in Lanka after Ravana has carried her away. In her grief, she calls on Ram as her protector and refuge, wondering why his compassion feels distant now. This is part of her anguished lament, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3820.modern_relevance: You sit awake after a cruel message, staring at the person you trusted most. The ache is not just loss — it is the question, why did your care disappear?
ramacharitamanas::3820.insight: It captures how suffering turns longing into direct appeal, not abstraction.

ramacharitamanas::3821.verse_sanskrit: हा लछिमन तुम्हार नहिं दोसा। सो फलु पायउँ कीन्हेउँ रोसा॥ बिबिध बिलाप करति बैदेही। भूरि कृपा प्रभु दूरि सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3821.verse_hindi: हा लक्ष्मण! तुम्हारा दोष नहीं है। मैंने क्रोध किया, उसका फल पाया। श्री जानकीजी बहुत प्रकार से विलाप कर रही हैं- (हाय!) प्रभु की कृपा तो बहुत है, परन्तु वे स्नेही प्रभु बहुत दूर रह गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3821.english_translation: Ha Lakshman, your fault is not here. I earned this result by my own anger. Janaki weeps in many ways: the Lord is full of grace, yet the loving Lord has gone far away.
ramacharitamanas::3821.translation_literal: हा (alas) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / तुम्हार (your) / नहिं (not) / दोसा (fault) / सो (that) / फलु (fruit/result) / पायउँ (I received) / कीन्हेउँ (I did) / रोसा (anger) / बिबिध (various) / बिलाप (lamentations) / करति (doing) / बैदेही (Vaidehi/Sita) / भूरि (abundant) / कृपा (grace) / प्रभु (Lord) / दूरि (far) / सनेही (loving one/beloved)
ramacharitamanas::3821.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3821.essence: Your own reaction can hurt you more than anyone else's fault.
ramacharitamanas::3821.simple_meaning: Sita says Lakshman is not at fault. Her own anger brought this suffering, and she laments that the loving Lord has gone far away.
ramacharitamanas::3821.simple_insight: Blame falls away, but the ache of separation remains.
ramacharitamanas::3821.detailed_meaning: After Ravana carries Sita away, she cries out in grief from the sky-bound chariot. She absolves Lakshman of blame, recognises her own anger as the cause of her pain, and laments Ram's distant absence as her deepest wound.
ramacharitamanas::3821.modern_relevance: After the argument, you replay every line and want someone to blame. Then you see it more clearly: your own reaction helped create the damage, and the person you most need feels far away.
ramacharitamanas::3821.insight: It shifts the mind from blame to responsibility, while naming separation as the real suffering.

ramacharitamanas::3822.verse_sanskrit: बिपति मोरि को प्रभुहि सुनावा। पुरोडास चह रासभ खावा॥ सीता कै बिलाप सुनि भारी। भए चराचर जीव दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3822.verse_hindi: प्रभु को मेरी यह विपत्ति कौन सुनावे? यज्ञ के अन्न को गदहा खाना चाहता है। सीताजी का भारी विलाप सुनकर जड़-चेतन सभी जीव दुःखी हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3822.english_translation: Who can tell the Lord of my distress? A donkey wants to eat the sacred offering. Hearing Sita's deep lament, all moving and unmoving beings became sorrowful.
ramacharitamanas::3822.translation_literal: बिपति (distress) / मोरि (my) / को (who) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / सुनावा (will tell) / पुरोडास (sacred offering) / चह (wants) / रासभ (donkey) / खावा (to eat)॥ / सीता (Sita's) / कै (of) / बिलाप (lament) / सुनि (hearing) / भारी (deep) / भए (became) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / जीव (beings) / दुखारी (grieved) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3822.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3822.essence: Grief so deep can make the whole world ache with you.
ramacharitamanas::3822.simple_meaning: Sita cries out in helpless grief, asking who can carry her suffering to Ram. Her sorrow is so deep that all living beings are moved by it.
ramacharitamanas::3822.simple_insight: Deep grief can make the whole world feel heavy with you.
ramacharitamanas::3822.detailed_meaning: In the forest after Sita's abduction, she is alone in anguish, calling out to Ram with no answer. Her cry is so intense that the poem says even the world around her, living and lifeless, feels her pain.
ramacharitamanas::3822.modern_relevance: You sit on the bathroom floor after a message that changes everything, unable to explain the hurt to anyone else. Some pain is so raw it seems to spill into the room.
ramacharitamanas::3822.insight: It shows how grief can become a shared atmosphere, not just a private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3823.verse_sanskrit: गीधराज सुनि आरत बानी। रघुकुलतिलक नारि पहिचानी॥ अधम निसाचर लीन्हें जाई। जिमि मलेछ बस कपिला गाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3823.verse_hindi: गृध्रराज जटायु ने सीताजी की दुःखभरी वाणी सुनकर पहचान लिया कि ये रघुकुल तिलक श्री रामचन्द्रजी की पत्नी हैं। (उसने देखा कि) नीच राक्षस इनको (बुरी तरह) लिए जा रहा है, जैसे कपिला गाय म्लेच्छ के पाले पड़ गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3823.english_translation: King of the birds Jatayu heard Sita’s anguished voice and recognized her as the wife of Ram, the ornament of Raghu’s line. The wicked demon was carrying her away, like a cow seized by an outcaste.
ramacharitamanas::3823.translation_literal: गीधराज (king of birds) / सुनि (hearing) / आरत (anguished) / बानी (voice) / रघुकुलतिलक (ornament of the Raghu line) / नारि (woman, wife) / पहिचानी (recognized)॥ / अधम (wicked) / निसाचर (night-walker, demon) / लीन्हें (having taken) / जाई (away) / जिमि (like) / मलेछ (outcaste) / बस (in the control of) / कपिला (cow) / गाई (cow) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3823.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3823.essence: Recognition of suffering becomes the first act of courage.
ramacharitamanas::3823.simple_meaning: Jatayu hears Sita’s cry, recognizes who she is, and sees Ravana carrying her away like a helpless cow seized by a cruel stranger.
ramacharitamanas::3823.simple_insight: Even a passing cry can awaken courage when your heart recognizes someone in danger.
ramacharitamanas::3823.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is being carried off while Ram and Lakshman are away. Jatayu hears her cry, identifies her as Ram’s wife, and instantly understands the injustice. This recognition leads directly to his brave intervention.
ramacharitamanas::3823.modern_relevance: You hear a frightened voice from the next room and know something is wrong before anyone explains. Recognition itself can become responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::3823.insight: It turns perception into duty: once suffering is recognized, action follows.

ramacharitamanas::3824.verse_sanskrit: सीते पुत्रि करसि जनि त्रासा। करिहउँ जातुधान कर नासा ॥ धावा क्रोधवंत खग कैसें। छूटइ पबि परबत कहुँ जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3824.verse_hindi: (वह बोला-) हे सीते पुत्री! भय मत कर। मैं इस राक्षस का नाश करूँगा। (यह कहकर) वह पक्षी क्रोध में भरकर ऐसे दौड़ा, जैसे पर्वत की ओर वज्र छूटता हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3824.english_translation: “O Sita, daughter, do not be afraid. I will destroy this demon.” Saying this, the bird rushed in anger, like a thunderbolt striking a mountain.
ramacharitamanas::3824.translation_literal: सीते (O Sita) / पुत्रि (daughter) / करसि (do) / जनि (do not) / त्रासा (fear) / करिहउँ (I will do) / जातुधान (demon) / कर (of the hand) / नासा (destruction) ॥ धावा (rushed) / क्रोधवंत (full of anger) / खग (bird) / कैसें (like) / छूटइ (is released) / पबि (thunderbolt) / परबत (mountain) / कहुँ (toward) / जैसें (as)
ramacharitamanas::3824.speaker: Jatayu
ramacharitamanas::3824.essence: Love rushes toward danger before fear can speak.
ramacharitamanas::3824.simple_meaning: Jatayu comforts Sita, promises to destroy Ravana, and charges at him with fierce courage.
ramacharitamanas::3824.simple_insight: Courage can be love in motion, even when the odds are hopeless.
ramacharitamanas::3824.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has been seized and cries out for help. Jatayu, the old vulture king, hears her and recognizes her as Ram's wife. He speaks tenderly, then flies at Ravana with furious resolve, becoming the first protector in her rescue.
ramacharitamanas::3824.modern_relevance: You hear a frightened voice from the next room and move before thinking. That instant of protective courage is what Jatayu becomes here.
ramacharitamanas::3824.insight: It shows how devotion turns concern into immediate action, without waiting for safety or advantage.

ramacharitamanas::3825.verse_sanskrit: रे रे दुष्ट ठाढ़ किन हो ही। निर्भय चलेसि न जानेहि मोही॥ आवत देखि कृतांत समाना। फिरि दसकंधर कर अनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3825.verse_hindi: (उसने ललकारकर कहा-) रे रे दुष्ट! खड़ा क्यों नहीं होता? निडर होकर चल दिया! मुझे तूने नहीं जाना? उसको यमराज के समान आता हुआ देखकर रावण घूमकर मन में अनुमान करने लगा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3825.english_translation: “Hey you villain, why do you stand there? You flew off fearless and still you do not know me!” Seeing him come like Death itself, Ravana turned and thought to himself.
ramacharitamanas::3825.translation_literal: रे रे (hey hey) / दुष्ट (wicked one) / ठाढ़ (standing) / किन (why) / हो ही (are you) / निर्भय (fearless) / चलेसि (you went) / न (not) / जानेहि (you know) / मोही (me)॥ / आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / कृतांत (Death) / समाना (like) / फिरि (turning) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / कर (of) / अनुमाना (thought/estimate)॥
ramacharitamanas::3825.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3825.essence: Ego shouts loudest right before fear takes over.
ramacharitamanas::3825.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the opponent for daring to come fearlessly, then realizes he is facing someone as terrible as death and begins to reassess.
ramacharitamanas::3825.simple_insight: Pride can vanish the moment real danger appears.
ramacharitamanas::3825.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sees Jatayu pressing forward in rage. The bird’s fearless advance shocks him enough to halt his arrogance for a moment. This is not a teaching verse, only a sharp turn in the chase before the battle continues.
ramacharitamanas::3825.modern_relevance: You swagger into a room sure you control it, then one hard look from the person across from you changes everything. Confidence built on ego collapses fast.
ramacharitamanas::3825.insight: It shows how arrogance turns into caution when confronted by something greater.

ramacharitamanas::3826.verse_sanskrit: की मैनाक कि खगपति होई। मम बल जान सहित पति सोई॥ जाना जरठ जटायू एहा। मम कर तीरथ छाँड़िहि देहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3826.verse_hindi: यह या तो मैनाक पर्वत है या पक्षियों का स्वामी गरुड़। पर वह (गरुड़) तो अपने स्वामी विष्णु सहित मेरे बल को जानता है! (कुछ पास आने पर) रावण ने उसे पहचान लिया (और बोला-) यह तो बूढ़ा जटायु है। यह मेरे हाथ रूपी तीर्थ में शरीर छोड़ेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3826.english_translation: Is this Mainaka, or the king of birds? But he knows my strength along with his master Vishnu. Ah, this is the old Jatayu. He will leave his body in my hands, like a pilgrim at a holy place.
ramacharitamanas::3826.translation_literal: की (or) / मैनाक (Mainaka) / कि (or) / खगपति (lord of birds) / होई (is) / मम (my) / बल (strength) / जान (knowing) / सहित (along with) / पति (master) / सोई (that one) ॥ / जाना (known) / जरठ (old) / जटायू (Jatayu) / एहा (this) / मम (my) / कर (hand) / तीरथ (holy place) / छाँड़िहि (will leave) / देहा (body) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3826.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3826.essence: Pride turns even danger into a joke until it meets resistance.
ramacharitamanas::3826.simple_meaning: Ravana briefly mistakes Jatayu for something harmless, then recognizes the old bird and boasts that Jatayu will die at his hands.
ramacharitamanas::3826.simple_insight: Pride makes him misread what stands before him, even in a life-or-death moment.
ramacharitamanas::3826.detailed_meaning: Ravana is carrying Sita through the forest when he spots Jatayu. For a moment he wonders if it is Mainaka or Garuda, then realizes it is the old vulture. The line is part of his arrogant sizing-up of an opponent before the clash.
ramacharitamanas::3826.modern_relevance: You spot someone in your way and instantly rank them as weak or irrelevant. That split-second contempt can blind you to the courage already standing there.
ramacharitamanas::3826.insight: It exposes the ego that assumes it can name and dismiss resistance before the fight begins.

ramacharitamanas::3827.verse_sanskrit: सुनत गीध क्रोधातुर धावा। कह सुनु रावन मोर सिखावा॥ तजि जानकिहि कुसल गृह जाहू। नाहिं त अस होइहि बहुबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3827.verse_hindi: यह सुनते ही गीध क्रोध में भरकर बड़े वेग से दौड़ा और बोला- रावण! मेरी सिखावन सुन। जानकीजी को छोड़कर कुशलपूर्वक अपने घर चला जा। नहीं तो हे बहुत भुजाओं वाले! ऐसा होगा कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3827.english_translation: Hearing this, Jatayu rushed forward in anger and said, 'Listen, Ravana, to my warning: leave Janaki and go home safely. Otherwise, O many-armed one, this will happen...'
ramacharitamanas::3827.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / गीध (the vulture Jatayu) / क्रोधातुर (filled with anger) / धावा (rushed) / कह (said) / सुनु (listen) / रावन (Ravana) / मोर (my) / सिखावा (warning) ॥ तजि (leaving) / जानकिहि (Janaki) / कुसल (safely) / गृह (home) / जाहू (go) ॥ नाहिं (otherwise) / त (then) / अस (such) / होइहि (will happen) / बहुबाहू (O many-armed one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3827.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3827.essence: Real courage speaks up before violence fully begins.
ramacharitamanas::3827.simple_meaning: Jatayu confronts Ravana in anger and warns him to leave Sita and go home safely.
ramacharitamanas::3827.simple_insight: Courage sometimes means stepping in before harm goes further.
ramacharitamanas::3827.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Jatayu sees Ravana carrying Sita away. The old vulture does not stay silent; he rushes at the abducting king and warns him to release her. This line is the opening challenge before the fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::3827.modern_relevance: You see someone being cornered in a parking lot and your body moves before your fear catches up. Jatayu is that instant of moral courage.
ramacharitamanas::3827.insight: It shows that protecting the vulnerable can begin with a direct warning, not only with force.

ramacharitamanas::3828.verse_sanskrit: राम रोष पावक अति घोरा। होइहि सकल सलभ कुल तोरा॥ उतरु न देत दसानन जोधा। तबहिं गीध धावा करि क्रोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3828.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के क्रोध रूपी अत्यन्त भयानक अग्नि में तेरा सारा वंश पतिंगा (होकर भस्म) हो जाएगा। योद्धा रावण कुछ उत्तर नहीं देता। तब गीध क्रोध करके दौड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3828.english_translation: In Ram's terrible fire of wrath, your whole lineage will be burned to ash. The warrior Ravana gives no answer. Then the vulture, enraged, rushed forward.
ramacharitamanas::3828.translation_literal: राम (Ram's) / रोष (wrath) / पावक (fire) / अति (very) / घोरा (terrible) । / होइहि (will become) / सकल (all) / सलभ (moths) / कुल (lineage) / तोरा (yours) ॥ / उतरु (answer) / न (not) / देत (gives) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / जोधा (warrior) । / तबहिं (then) / गीध (vulture) / धावा (rushed) / करि (doing) / क्रोधा (anger) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3828.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3828.essence: Ram's wrath exposes ego as something that cannot endure.
ramacharitamanas::3828.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that Ram's anger will destroy his entire lineage, but he stays silent. Jatayu then attacks in rage.
ramacharitamanas::3828.simple_insight: Pride goes silent when truth arrives, but courage still moves.
ramacharitamanas::3828.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Jatayu has confronted Ravana while Sita is being carried away. He warns Ravana that Ram's fury will destroy his whole line, but Ravana refuses to answer. This verse simply sets up Jatayu's attack.
ramacharitamanas::3828.modern_relevance: A bully keeps talking until someone names the cost clearly. Then the room goes quiet, and the person with courage steps in anyway.
ramacharitamanas::3828.insight: It frames Jatayu's charge as righteous fury against Ravana's arrogance, not a random fight.

ramacharitamanas::3829.verse_sanskrit: धरि कच बिरथ कीन्ह महि गिरा। सीतहि राखि गीध पुनि फिरा॥ चोचन्ह मारि बिदारेसि देही। दंड एक भइ मुरुछा तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3829.verse_hindi: उसने (रावण के) बाल पकड़कर उसे रथ के नीचे उतार लिया, रावण पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। गीध सीताजी को एक ओर बैठाकर फिर लौटा और चोंचों से मार-मारकर रावण के शरीर को विदीर्ण कर डाला। इससे उसे एक घड़ी के लिए मूर्च्छा हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3829.english_translation: He seized Ravana by the hair and threw him to the ground. The eagle set Sita aside and returned again, striking the body with its beak until Ravana lay stunned for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::3829.translation_literal: धरि (seizing) / कच (hair) / बिरथ (from the chariot) / कीन्ह (made) / महि (to the ground) / गिरा (fell) / सीतहि (Sita) / राखि (placing) / गीध (the eagle) / पुनि (again) / फिरा (returned) / चोचन्ह (with beaks) / मारि (striking) / बिदारेसि (rent apart) / देही (the body) / दंड (a moment) / एक (one) / भइ (became) / मुरुछा (fainting) / तेही (to him)
ramacharitamanas::3829.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3829.essence: Protecting the vulnerable can be stronger than brute force.
ramacharitamanas::3829.simple_meaning: Jatayu throws Ravana down, protects Sita, and attacks again until Ravana is stunned.
ramacharitamanas::3829.simple_insight: True courage keeps returning to protect what is vulnerable, even against overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::3829.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Jatayu has already challenged Ravana for carrying Sita away. Ravana fights back, but the old bird still shields her, knocks him down, and returns to strike again. The scene shows fearless protection in the middle of abduction.
ramacharitamanas::3829.modern_relevance: You step between a friend and someone bullying them, even when your voice shakes. Protection is not loudness; it is refusing to move aside.
ramacharitamanas::3829.insight: It shows that dharma can mean repeated, bodily resistance when someone vulnerable is under attack.

ramacharitamanas::3830.verse_sanskrit: तब सक्रोध निसिचर खिसिआना। काढ़ेसि परम कराल कृपाना॥ काटेसि पंख परा खग धरनी। सुमिरि राम करि अदभुत करनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3830.verse_hindi: तब खिसियाए हुए रावण ने क्रोधयुक्त होकर अत्यन्त भयानक कटार निकाली और उससे जटायु के पंख काट डाले। पक्षी (जटायु) श्री रामजी की अद्भुत लीला का स्मरण करके पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3830.english_translation: Then, angered and hostile, the demon king drew a terribly fierce dagger. He cut off the bird's wings, and Jatayu fell to the earth, remembering Ram's wondrous deed.
ramacharitamanas::3830.translation_literal: तब (then) / सक्रोध (with anger) / निसिचर (demon) / खिसिआना (angered, irritated) / काढ़ेसि (he drew out) / परम (extremely) / कराल (fierce, terrible) / कृपाना (dagger, sword) / काटेसि (he cut) / पंख (wings) / परा (fell) / खग (bird) / धरनी (to the earth) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम (Ram) / करि (doing) / अदभुत (wondrous) / करनी (deed, act)
ramacharitamanas::3830.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3830.essence: Anger cuts the body, but remembrance can remain unbroken.
ramacharitamanas::3830.simple_meaning: Ravana, furious, draws a terrible weapon and cuts Jatayu's wings. The wounded bird falls, holding Ram in mind.
ramacharitamanas::3830.simple_insight: Even in defeat, remembrance can stay steady.
ramacharitamanas::3830.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has tried to stop Ravana from carrying Sita away. Enraged, Ravana draws a fierce dagger and cripples the bird. As Jatayu falls, his mind remains on Ram's wondrous protection, making this a tragic action beat rather than a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::3830.modern_relevance: A person lashes out in anger during a breakup or family fight, saying the cruel thing they can never take back. The wound lands, but the one being hurt may still hold on to what is highest.
ramacharitamanas::3830.insight: It shows how violence springs from wounded pride, while steadfast remembrance can survive physical defeat.

ramacharitamanas::3831.verse_sanskrit: सीतहि जान चढ़ाइ बहोरी। चला उताइल त्रास न थोरी॥ करति बिलाप जाति नभ सीता। ब्याध बिबस जनु मृगी सभीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3831.verse_hindi: सीताजी को फिर रथ पर चढ़ाकर रावण बड़ी उतावली के साथ चला। उसे भय कम न था। सीताजी आकाश में विलाप करती हुई जा रही हैं। मानो व्याधे के वश में पड़ी हुई (जाल में फँसी हुई) कोई भयभीत हिरनी हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3831.english_translation: Ravana hurried on after lifting Sita back onto the chariot. Fear still did not leave him. Sita went through the sky, crying out, like a frightened doe caught by a hunter.
ramacharitamanas::3831.translation_literal: सीतहि (Sita) / जान (having) / चढ़ाइ (having lifted up) / बहोरी (again) / चला (he went) / उताइल (hurried) / त्रास (fear) / न थोरी (not little)॥ करति (doing) / बिलाप (lamentation) / जाति (going) / नभ (sky) / सीता (Sita) / ब्याध (hunter) / बिबस (helpless) / जनु (as if) / मृगी (doe) / सभीता (frightened)
ramacharitamanas::3831.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3831.essence: Cruelty runs faster when fear is driving it.
ramacharitamanas::3831.simple_meaning: Ravana rushed onward with Sita after forcing her back onto the chariot. Sita cried out helplessly as she was carried through the sky, like a frightened deer caught by a hunter.
ramacharitamanas::3831.simple_insight: Fear makes cruelty rush faster, not wiser.
ramacharitamanas::3831.detailed_meaning: After overpowering Jatayu, Ravana forces Sita back onto his chariot and speeds away through the sky. Sita cries in helpless grief, and Tulsidas compares her to a terrified deer trapped by a hunter. The scene deepens the violence of her abduction.
ramacharitamanas::3831.modern_relevance: A person keeps pushing forward after crossing a line, not slowing down but speeding up. The harm is already done, yet the panic only makes the damage harsher.
ramacharitamanas::3831.insight: It shows how fear and force can keep a person moving without any inner steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::3832.verse_sanskrit: गिरि पर बैठे कपिन्ह निहारी। कहि हरि नाम दीन्ह पट डारी॥ एहि बिधि सीतहि सो लै गयऊ। बन असोक महँ राखत भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3832.verse_hindi: पर्वत पर बैठे हुए बंदरों को देखकर सीताजी ने हरिनाम लेकर वस्त्र डाल दिया। इस प्रकार वह सीताजी को ले गया और उन्हें अशोक वन में जा रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3832.english_translation: Seeing the monkeys seated on the mountain, Sita uttered Hari's name and let her cloth fall. In this way he carried Sita away and placed her in the Ashoka grove.
ramacharitamanas::3832.translation_literal: गिरि (mountain) / पर (on) / बैठे (seated) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / निहारी (seeing) / कहि (saying) / हरि नाम (Hari's name) / दीन्ह (gave) / पट (cloth) / डारी (dropped) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / सीतहि (Sita) / सो (he) / लै (taking) / गयऊ (went) / बन (forest) / असोक (Ashoka) / महँ (in) / राखत (placing) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::3832.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3832.essence: Even in captivity, Sita answers with Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3832.simple_meaning: Sita sees the monkeys, calls on Ram, and drops her cloth as a sign. Ravana then carries her to the Ashoka grove.
ramacharitamanas::3832.simple_insight: Even in captivity, her trust stays alive.
ramacharitamanas::3832.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita sees Hanuman and the monkeys from the mountain and quietly signals with Ram's name. Ravana then takes her to the Ashoka grove, trying to contain her sorrow and resistance.
ramacharitamanas::3832.modern_relevance: You catch sight of one familiar face in a room where you feel utterly alone. A small sign of trust can still travel farther than fear.
ramacharitamanas::3832.insight: It shows how faith can be signaled quietly, even when direct action is impossible.

ramacharitamanas::3833.verse_sanskrit: हारि परा खल बहु बिधि भय अरु प्रीति देखाइ। तब असोक पादप तर राखिसि जतन कराइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3833.verse_hindi: सीताजी को बहुत प्रकार से भय और प्रीति दिखलाकर जब वह दुष्ट हार गया, तब उन्हें यत्न कराके (सब व्यवस्था ठीक कराके) अशोक वृक्ष के नीचे रख दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3833.english_translation: After showing Sita many kinds of fear and affection and finally being defeated, the wicked one had her carefully placed under the Ashoka tree.
ramacharitamanas::3833.translation_literal: हारि (having lost) / परा (fell) / खल (the wicked one) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / भय (fear) / अरु (and) / प्रीति (affection) / देखाइ (showing) / तब (then) / असोक पादप (Ashoka tree) / तर (under) / राखिसि (placed) / जतन कराइ (with care, having arrangements made)
ramacharitamanas::3833.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3833.essence: False tenderness is still a cage.
ramacharitamanas::3833.simple_meaning: Ravana used fear and false kindness, but after failing, he had Sita placed under the Ashoka tree with care.
ramacharitamanas::3833.simple_insight: Cruelty can wear many masks, but it still remains cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::3833.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has seized Sita and brought her to the Ashoka grove. After trying to control her through threat and false gentleness, he finally has her kept beneath the tree. The verse marks the grim settling of her captivity.
ramacharitamanas::3833.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with pressure, then suddenly softens their tone to make control feel like concern. You can feel the manipulation even when it arrives wrapped in care.
ramacharitamanas::3833.insight: It teaches you to see coercion clearly, even when it comes dressed as kindness.

ramacharitamanas::3834.verse_sanskrit: जेहि बिधि कपट कुरंग सँग धाइ चले श्रीराम। सो छबि सीता राखि उर रटति रहति हरिनाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3834.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार कपट मृग के साथ श्री रामजी दौड़ चले थे, उसी छवि को हृदय में रखकर वे हरिनाम (रामनाम) रटती रहती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3834.english_translation: Keeping the image of Shri Ram running after the deceptive deer in her heart, Sita keeps chanting Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3834.translation_literal: जेहि बिधि (in the way) / कपट (deceptive) / कुरंग (deer) / सँग (with) / धाइ (running) / चले (went) / श्रीराम (Shri Ram) / सो (that) / छबि (image) / सीता (Sita) / राखि (keeping) / उर (in the heart) / रटति रहति (keeps repeating) / हरिनाम (Ram's name)
ramacharitamanas::3834.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3834.essence: A single remembered act of love can keep devotion breathing.
ramacharitamanas::3834.simple_meaning: Sita remembers the moment Ram ran after the false deer, and that memory keeps her repeating Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3834.simple_insight: Love survives by remembering what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3834.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Sita is alone after Ravana's abduction. She steadies herself by holding one vivid memory: Ram running after the deceptive deer. That remembered scene becomes her refuge and keeps her chanting his name.
ramacharitamanas::3834.modern_relevance: You replay one moment of care from someone you love while sitting alone in a quiet room. That memory keeps you from collapsing into panic.
ramacharitamanas::3834.insight: It teaches you to anchor attention in a sustaining memory so devotion stays alive under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3835.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति अनुजहि आवत देखी। बाहिज चिंता कीन्हि बिसेषी॥ जनकसुता परिहरिहु अकेली। आयहु तात बचन मम पेली ॥
ramacharitamanas::3835.verse_hindi: (इधर) श्री रघुनाथजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को आते देखकर ब्राह्य रूप में बहुत चिंता की (और कहा-) हे भाई! तुमने जानकी को अकेली छोड़ दिया और मेरी आज्ञा का उल्लंघन कर यहाँ चले आए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3835.english_translation: Seeing his younger brother return, Raghupati showed great concern outwardly and said, 'Brother, you left Janaki alone and came here against my command.'
ramacharitamanas::3835.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / अनुजहि (the younger brother) / आवत (coming) / देखी (seeing) / बाहिज (outwardly) / चिंता (concern) / कीन्हि (did) / बिसेषी (especially) ॥ / जनकसुता (Janak's daughter, Sita) / परिहरिहु (you left behind) / अकेली (alone) / आयहु (you came) / तात (brother/dear one) / बचन (word/command) / मम (my) / पेली (pushed/violated) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3835.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3835.essence: Fear for someone you love can wear the mask of anger.
ramacharitamanas::3835.simple_meaning: Ram speaks as if he is upset that Lakshman left Sita alone and returned against his order.
ramacharitamanas::3835.simple_insight: Love can sound like reproach when fear for someone vulnerable is close to the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3835.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman has returned to Ram after leaving Sita alone. Ram immediately acts disturbed and rebukes him, not because he lacks love, but because Sita's safety now feels urgent. The verse pushes the story toward the terrible realization that something has gone wrong.
