ramacharitamanas::3835.modern_relevance: You hear footsteps at the door after leaving someone vulnerable alone, and your first words come out sharper than you meant. Fear often speaks before calm does.
ramacharitamanas::3835.insight: It shows how protective concern can appear as blame when danger feels near.

ramacharitamanas::3836.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर निकर फिरहिं बन माहीं। मम मन सीता आश्रम नाहीं॥ गहि पद कमल अनुज कर जोरी। कहेउ नाथ कछु मोहि न खोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3836.verse_hindi: राक्षसों के झुंड वन में फिरते रहते हैं। मेरे मन में ऐसा आता है कि सीता आश्रम में नहीं है। छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी ने श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों को पकड़कर हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे नाथ! मेरा कुछ भी दोष नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3836.english_translation: The demons keep roaming the forest, and my mind tells me Sita is not at the hermitage. Lakshman clasped Ram's lotus feet and, with joined hands, said, "Lord, I have done nothing wrong."
ramacharitamanas::3836.translation_literal: निसिचर (demons) / निकर (crowd) / फिरहिं (wander) / बन (forest) / माहीं (in) । / मम (my) / मन (mind) / सीता (Sita) / आश्रम (hermitage) / नाहीं (not) ॥ / गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / अनुज (younger brother) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) । / कहेउ (said) / नाथ (lord) / कछु (some) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / खोरी (fault) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3836.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3836.essence: Fear can make innocence feel like guilt.
ramacharitamanas::3836.simple_meaning: Ram senses danger in the forest and fears Sita is no longer safe at the hermitage. Lakshman falls at his feet and insists he has done no wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3836.simple_insight: Fear can make even love sound like accusation.
ramacharitamanas::3836.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has just sent Lakshman back toward Sita, and the mood has turned tense. Seeing demons roaming, Ram's mind fills with dread that Sita is not safe. Lakshman, shocked, falls at Ram's feet and protests his innocence.
ramacharitamanas::3836.modern_relevance: You get a text that sounds like something went wrong, and your stomach drops before you even know why. In fear, even loyal people start defending themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3836.insight: It shows how anxiety distorts trust and turns concern into suspicion.

ramacharitamanas::3837.verse_sanskrit: अनुज समेत गए प्रभु तहवाँ। गोदावरि तट आश्रम जहवाँ॥ आश्रम देखि जानकी हीना। भए बिकल जस प्राकृत दीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3837.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामजी वहाँ गए, जहाँ गोदावरी के तट पर उनका आश्रम था। आश्रम को जानकीजी से रहित देखकर श्री रामजी साधारण मनुष्य की भाँति व्याकुल और दीन (दुःखी) हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3837.english_translation: Ram went there with Lakshman, to the hermitage on the bank of the Godavari. Seeing the hermitage empty of Janaki, Ram became distraught and helpless like an ordinary sorrowful man.
ramacharitamanas::3837.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / गए (went) / प्रभु (Lord) / तहवाँ (there) / गोदावरि (Godavari) / तट (bank) / आश्रम (hermitage) / जहवाँ (where)॥ / आश्रम (hermitage) / देखि (seeing) / जानकी (Janaki) / हीना (deprived/without) / भए (became) / बिकल (distressed) / जस (like) / प्राकृत (ordinary) / दीना (wretched/sorrowful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3837.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3837.essence: Absence itself can bring even the steady heart to its knees.
ramacharitamanas::3837.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman reach the hermitage by the Godavari, but Sita is missing. Seeing the empty place, Ram is overwhelmed with grief like an ordinary person.
ramacharitamanas::3837.simple_insight: Even the strongest heart can break when love is suddenly absent.
ramacharitamanas::3837.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman return to the hermitage on the Godavari bank, expecting to find Sita there. Instead, they find only emptiness. That sight undoes Ram at once, and the verse pauses on his human grief before the search begins.
ramacharitamanas::3837.modern_relevance: You come home and notice the small things first: the untouched cup, the quiet room, the message that never came. In that instant, absence becomes unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::3837.insight: It shows how loss can strip away composure and leave only raw feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3838.verse_sanskrit: हा गुन खानि जानकी सीता। रूप सील ब्रत नेम पुनीता॥ लछिमन समुझाए बहु भाँति। पूछत चले लता तरु पाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3838.verse_hindi: (वे विलाप करने लगे-) हा गुणों की खान जानकी! हा रूप, शील, व्रत और नियमों में पवित्र सीते! लक्ष्मणजी ने बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। तब श्री रामजी लताओं और वृक्षों की पंक्तियों से पूछते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3838.english_translation: Alas, Janaki, mine of virtues! Alas, pure Sita, radiant in beauty, conduct, vows, and discipline! Lakshman tried to console him in many ways. Then Ram walked on, asking the creepers and trees.
ramacharitamanas::3838.translation_literal: हा (alas) / गुन (virtues) / खानि (mine) / जानकी (Janaki) / सीता (Sita) / रूप (beauty) / सील (conduct) / ब्रत (vows) / नेम (discipline) / पुनीता (pure) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / समुझाए (consoled) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / पूछत (asking) / चले (walked) / लता (creepers) / तरु (trees) / पाँती (rows)
ramacharitamanas::3838.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3838.essence: Longing does not stop the search.
ramacharitamanas::3838.simple_meaning: Ram grieves for Sita’s absence, praises her virtues, and keeps searching for her despite Lakshman’s efforts to comfort him.
ramacharitamanas::3838.simple_insight: Love can stay steady even when it is hurting badly.
ramacharitamanas::3838.detailed_meaning: In the forest near the empty hermitage, Ram has just seen the place where Sita lived. Her absence breaks him open. Lakshman tries to steady him, but Ram keeps moving through the trees, calling out in despair.
ramacharitamanas::3838.modern_relevance: You search an empty room after someone you love has left, still hoping for one more sign. Grief makes you ask the world itself where they went.
ramacharitamanas::3838.insight: It shows how love keeps looking even when reason knows there is no answer.

ramacharitamanas::3839.verse_sanskrit: हे खग मृग हे मधुकर श्रेनी। तुम्ह देखी सीता मृगनैनी॥ खंजन सुक कपोत मृग मीना। मधुप निकर कोकिला प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3839.verse_hindi: हे पक्षियों! हे पशुओं! हे भौंरों की पंक्तियों! तुमने कहीं मृगनयनी सीता को देखा है? खंजन, तोता, कबूतर, हिरन, मछली, भौंरों का समूह, प्रवीण कोयल, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3839.english_translation: O birds, O deer, O rows of bees, have you seen Sita, the doe-eyed one? Khanjan birds, parrots, pigeons, deer, fish, swarms of bees, and clever cuckoos...
ramacharitamanas::3839.translation_literal: हे (O) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer) / हे (O) / मधुकर (bees) / श्रेनी (rows, groups) / तुम्ह (you all) / देखी (seen) / सीता (Sita) / मृगनैनी (doe-eyed) ॥ / खंजन (khanjan birds) / सुक (parrots) / कपोत (pigeons) / मृग (deer) / मीना (fish) / मधुप (bees) / निकर (crowd, swarm) / कोकिला (cuckoos) / प्रबीना (clever, skilled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3839.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3839.essence: Longing makes every creature feel like a witness.
ramacharitamanas::3839.simple_meaning: Ram is so overwhelmed by Sita's absence that he asks birds, animals, and even bees whether they have seen her. The verse is a heartfelt cry of searching, not a teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3839.simple_insight: Love can make the whole world feel like a witness to your longing.
ramacharitamanas::3839.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has reached the empty hermitage and found Sita gone. Still grieving, he turns to birds, deer, bees, and other creatures as if they might answer. The verse deepens his search before the next images unfold.
ramacharitamanas::3839.modern_relevance: You keep asking everyone in the group chat if they saw the person who left your life without warning. Even strangers start to feel like possible witnesses to your missing piece.
ramacharitamanas::3839.insight: It turns private grief into a search that reaches outward, making the whole world part of the longing.

ramacharitamanas::3840.verse_sanskrit: कुंद कली दाड़िम दामिनी। कमल सरद ससि अहिभामिनी॥ बरुन पास मनोज धनु हंसा। गज केहरि निज सुनत प्रसंसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3840.verse_hindi: कुन्दकली, अनार, बिजली, कमल, शरद् का चंद्रमा और नागिनी, अरुण का पाश, कामदेव का धनुष, हंस, गज और सिंह- ये सब आज अपनी प्रशंसा सुन रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3840.english_translation: Kund blossoms, pomegranate, lightning, lotus, autumn moon, and the serpent-woman; Varuna's noose, Cupid's bow, swan, elephant, and lion — all are hearing their own praise.
ramacharitamanas::3840.translation_literal: कुंद कली (kund blossom) / दाड़िम (pomegranate) / दामिनी (lightning) / कमल (lotus) / सरद (autumn) / ससि (moon) / अहिभामिनी (serpent-woman) / बरुन (Varuna) / पास (noose) / मनोज (Cupid) / धनु (bow) / हंसा (swan) / गज (elephant) / केहरि (lion) / निज (their own) / सुनत (hearing) / प्रसंसा (praise)
ramacharitamanas::3840.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3840.essence: Sita's radiance makes every comparison bow.
ramacharitamanas::3840.simple_meaning: The poet piles up images of beauty and power to say that all of them are being outshone by Sita's radiance.
ramacharitamanas::3840.simple_insight: Sometimes praise is really a way of saying no comparison can hold.
ramacharitamanas::3840.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama and Lakshman are searching for Sita after Ravana's abduction. Tulsidas compares her beauty to flowers, moonlight, weapons, animals, and celestial forces, showing that even nature's finest images now seem to be listening to her praise.
ramacharitamanas::3840.modern_relevance: You see someone enter a room and every polished detail around them feels ordinary. The verse catches that rare feeling when one presence makes all other beauty look smaller.
ramacharitamanas::3840.insight: It shifts attention from the objects named to the one they cannot equal.

ramacharitamanas::3841.verse_sanskrit: श्री फल कनक कदलि हरषाहीं। नेकु न संक सकुच मन माहीं॥ सुनु जानकी तोहि बिनु आजू। हरषे सकल पाइ जनु राजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3841.verse_hindi: बेल, सुवर्ण और केला हर्षित हो रहे हैं। इनके मन में जरा भी शंका और संकोच नहीं है। हे जानकी! सुनो, तुम्हारे बिना ये सब आज ऐसे हर्षित हैं, मानो राज पा गए हों। (अर्थात् तुम्हारे अंगों के सामने ये सब तुच्छ, अपमानित और लज्जित थे। आज तुम्हें न देखकर ये अपनी शोभा के अभिमान में फूल रहे हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3841.english_translation: The bel, golden flower, and banana trees are rejoicing. There is not even a trace of doubt or shyness in their minds. O Janaki, without you today they are all delighted, as if they have won a kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::3841.translation_literal: श्री फल (bel fruit) / कनक (golden) / कदलि (banana) / हरषाहीं (are rejoicing) / नेकु (not even a little) / न (not) / संक (doubt) / सकुच (shyness) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सुनु (listen) / जानकी (Janaki) / तोहि बिनु (without you) / आजू (today) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सकल (all) / पाइ (having obtained) / जनु (as if) / राजू (a kingdom)
ramacharitamanas::3841.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3841.essence: Nature itself seems to miss Sita’s beauty and presence.
ramacharitamanas::3841.simple_meaning: The poet imagines plants and trees rejoicing at Sita's absence, as if they feel proud of their own beauty now that she is not there to outshine them.
ramacharitamanas::3841.simple_insight: Beauty can feel competitive, but the deeper ache here is Sita's absence, not the plants' pride.
ramacharitamanas::3841.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is searching for Sita after her abduction. Tulsidas turns the whole landscape into a witness to her beauty: even trees and flowers seem to feel relieved and proud without her. The verse is part of the sorrowful search, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3841.modern_relevance: You step into a room after someone radiant has left, and everything still looks bright — but the brightness feels empty. The scene is really about the ache of their absence.
ramacharitamanas::3841.insight: It turns the search for Sita into a living landscape of longing, not a lesson to apply.

ramacharitamanas::3842.verse_sanskrit: किमि सहि जात अनख तोहि पाहीं। प्रिया बेगि प्रगटसि कस नाहीं॥ एहि बिधि खोजत बिलपत स्वामी। मनहुँ महा बिरही अति कामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3842.verse_hindi: तुमसे यह अनख (स्पर्धा) कैसे सही जाती है? हे प्रिये! तुम शीघ्र ही प्रकट क्यों नहीं होती? इस प्रकार (अनन्त ब्रह्माण्डों के अथवा महामहिमामयी स्वरूपाशक्ति श्री सीताजी के) स्वामी श्री रामजी सीताजी को खोजते हुए (इस प्रकार) विलाप करते हैं, मानो कोई महाविरही और अत्यंत कामी पुरुष हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3842.english_translation: How can I bear this rivalry from you? Beloved, why do you not appear at once? In this way, the lord of Sita searches and cries out, like a great lover burning with longing.
ramacharitamanas::3842.translation_literal: किमि (how) / सहि (bearing) / जात (is borne) / अनख (rivalry, jealousy) / तोहि (from you) / पाहीं (toward, by) / प्रिया (beloved) / बेगि (quickly) / प्रगटसि (you appear) / कस (why) / नाहीं (not) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / खोजत (searching) / बिलपत (crying out, lamenting) / स्वामी (lord) / मनहुँ (as if) / महा (great) / बिरही (one burning in separation) / अति (very) / कामी (filled with longing)
ramacharitamanas::3842.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3842.essence: Even the lord of Sita is shown as helpless in love.
ramacharitamanas::3842.simple_meaning: Ram searches for Sita in deep longing and cries out for her to appear. His grief is so intense it looks like the pain of a lover separated from the one he loves most.
ramacharitamanas::3842.simple_insight: Love can make even the strongest heart ache openly.
ramacharitamanas::3842.detailed_meaning: In the forest search for Sita, Ram is no longer the calm prince alone; he is a separated lover calling out in pain. The verse lingers on his longing, showing how devotion and love can make divine greatness feel heartbreakingly human.
ramacharitamanas::3842.modern_relevance: You have called, texted, waited, and still no reply comes. The silence starts to feel physical, and you understand how longing can make even dignity tremble.
ramacharitamanas::3842.insight: It shifts the mind from heroic distance to vulnerable devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3843.verse_sanskrit: पूरकनाम राम सुख रासी। मनुजचरित कर अज अबिनासी॥ आगें परा गीधपति देखा। सुमिरत राम चरन जिन्ह रेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3843.verse_hindi: पूर्णकाम, आनंद की राशि, अजन्मा और अविनाशी श्री रामजी मनुष्यों के चरित्र कर रहे हैं। आगे (जाने पर) उन्होंने गृध्रपति जटायु को पड़ा देखा। वह श्री रामजी के चरणों का स्मरण कर रहा था, जिनमें (ध्वजा, कुलिश आदि की) रेखाएँ (चिह्न) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3843.english_translation: Ram, the source of complete fulfillment and bliss, the unborn and imperishable, was acting out the life of a human. Ahead, he saw Jatayu, lord of the vultures, lying fallen, remembering the footprints of Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3843.translation_literal: पूरकनाम (full of fulfillment) / राम (Ram) / सुख रासी (treasure of bliss) / मनुजचरित (human conduct) / कर (doing) / अज (unborn) / अबिनासी (imperishable)॥ आगें (ahead) / परा (fell) / गीधपति (lord of vultures) / देखा (saw) / सुमिरत (remembering) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / जिन्ह (whose) / रेखा (marks) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3843.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3843.essence: The imperishable one walks as a human and is found by devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3843.simple_meaning: Ram, though unborn and imperishable, is moving through a human life. Then he sees Jatayu lying fallen, still remembering Ram's marked feet.
ramacharitamanas::3843.simple_insight: Even in grief, remembrance of Ram stays alive.
ramacharitamanas::3843.detailed_meaning: Searching for Sita in the forest, Ram comes upon the fallen Jatayu, the noble vulture who tried to stop Ravana. The verse highlights Ram's divine nature and Jatayu's devotion just before Ram touches him with compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3843.modern_relevance: You find someone collapsed after trying to help and realize they were holding on to the memory of what mattered most. Even at the edge of loss, devotion can remain.
ramacharitamanas::3843.insight: It shifts attention from the tragedy of the body to the endurance of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::3844.verse_sanskrit: कर सरोज सिर परसेउ कृपासिंधु रघुबीर। निरखि राम छबि धाम मुख बिगत भई सब पीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3844.verse_hindi: कृपा सागर श्री रघुवीर ने अपने करकमल से उसके सिर का स्पर्श किया (उसके सिर पर करकमल फेर दिया)। शोभाधाम श्री रामजी का (परम सुंदर) मुख देखकर उसकी सब पीड़ा जाती रही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3844.english_translation: The ocean of compassion, Raghubir, touched his head with his lotus hand. Seeing Ram's beauty, all his pain vanished.
ramacharitamanas::3844.translation_literal: कर (hand) / सरोज (lotus) / सिर (head) / परसेउ (touched) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / रघुबीर (Raghu's hero) / निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty) / धाम (abode) / मुख (face) / बिगत (gone) / भई (became) / सब (all) / पीर (pain)
ramacharitamanas::3844.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3844.essence: Ram's touch and sight heal where strength cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3844.simple_meaning: Ram gently touches Jatayu's head, and the sight of his beautiful face removes all suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3844.simple_insight: A single moment of grace can ease pain more deeply than words ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3844.detailed_meaning: Jatayu lies wounded after fighting Ravana to protect Sita. Ram reaches him, places a lotus hand on his head, and lets his beauty and compassion do what battle and grief cannot: soothe the dying bird.
ramacharitamanas::3844.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone hurting and say almost nothing. Then you place a hand on their shoulder, and the room softens. Presence itself can be medicine.
ramacharitamanas::3844.insight: It shows that compassionate presence can relieve suffering without explanation or argument.

ramacharitamanas::3845.verse_sanskrit: तब कह गीध बचन धरि धीरा। सुनहु राम भंजन भव भीरा॥ नाथ दसानन यह गति कीन्ही। तेहिं खल जनकसुता हरि लीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3845.verse_hindi: तब धीरज धरकर गीध ने यह वचन कहा- हे भव (जन्म-मृत्यु) के भय का नाश करने वाले श्री रामजी! सुनिए। हे नाथ! रावण ने मेरी यह दशा की है। उसी दुष्ट ने जानकीजी को हर लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3845.english_translation: Then Gid, gathering himself, spoke: "Listen, Ram, destroyer of the fear of worldly existence. Lord, Ravana has done this to me. That wicked one has taken Janaki away."
ramacharitamanas::3845.translation_literal: तब (then) / कह (said) / गीध (the vulture-king) / बचन (words) / धरि (holding) / धीरा (steadiness) / सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / भंजन (destroyer) / भव (worldly existence) / भीरा (fear)॥ नाथ (Lord) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / यह (this) / गति (condition) / कीन्ही (did) / तेहिं (that) / खल (wicked one) / जनकसुता (Janaka's daughter, Sita) / हरि (carried away) / लीन्ही (took away) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3845.speaker: Jatayu
ramacharitamanas::3845.essence: Pain becomes useful when it names the wrong clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3845.simple_meaning: Jatayu tells Ram that Ravana has carried Sita away and asks Ram to hear him out.
ramacharitamanas::3845.simple_insight: Even in pain, clear speech can become an offering.
ramacharitamanas::3845.detailed_meaning: Jatayu, wounded after trying to stop Ravana, steadies himself before speaking to Ram. He names the attacker, identifies Sita as the one taken, and turns his suffering into testimony. The verse moves the rescue story forward.
ramacharitamanas::3845.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you finally say the truth plainly: who did what, what was lost, and what must happen next.
ramacharitamanas::3845.insight: It teaches you to speak with steadiness even when hurt, so the truth can still help.

ramacharitamanas::3846.verse_sanskrit: लै दच्छिन दिसि गयउ गोसाईं। बिलपति अति कुररी की नाईं॥ दरस लाग प्रभु राखेउँ प्राना। चलन चहत अब कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3846.verse_hindi: हे गोसाईं! वह उन्हें लेकर दक्षिण दिशा को गया है। सीताजी कुररी (कुर्ज) की तरह अत्यंत विलाप कर रही थीं। हे प्रभो! आपके दर्शनों के लिए ही प्राण रोक रखे थे। हे कृपानिधान! अब ये चलना ही चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3846.english_translation: He has taken her toward the south. Sita was crying bitterly like a kurri bird. 'Lord, I held my breath only to see you. Now, O treasure of grace, I want to leave my body.'
ramacharitamanas::3846.translation_literal: लै (taking) / दच्छिन दिसि (toward the south) / गयउ (went) / गोसाईं (lord) / बिलपति (lamenting) / अति (very) / कुररी (kurri bird) / की नाईं (like) / दरस (sight) / लाग (for) / प्रभु (lord) / राखेउँ (I kept) / प्राना (breath/life) / चलन (to leave) / चहत (wanting) / अब (now) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of grace)
ramacharitamanas::3846.speaker: Jatayu
ramacharitamanas::3846.essence: Grief becomes a final message when love is still alive.
ramacharitamanas::3846.simple_meaning: Jatayu tells Ram that Ravana carried Sita southward. Sita cried in pain, and she had stayed alive only to see Ram again before leaving her body.
ramacharitamanas::3846.simple_insight: Love can keep you alive through unbearable grief, even when your heart is already breaking.
ramacharitamanas::3846.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the wounded Jatayu is telling Ram what he witnessed: Ravana carried Sita away toward the south, and Sita cried out in helpless sorrow. This is the moment the search becomes a rescue, and grief turns into urgency.
ramacharitamanas::3846.modern_relevance: You hear, after the fact, that someone you love was taken from a place you thought was safe. The stomach-drop comes first; action comes next.
ramacharitamanas::3846.insight: It turns private sorrow into clear direction: the loss is real, and Ram must move immediately.

ramacharitamanas::3847.verse_sanskrit: राम कहा तनु राखहु ताता। मुख मुसुकाइ कही तेहिं बाता॥ जाकर नाम मरत मुख आवा। अधमउ मुकुत होइ श्रुति गावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3847.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा- हे तात! शारीर को बनाए रखिए। तब उसने मुस्कुराते हुए मुँह से यह बात कही- मरते समय जिनका नाम मुख में आ जाने से अधम (महान् पापी) भी मुक्त हो जाता है, ऐसा वेद गाते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3847.english_translation: Ram said, “Keep your body alive, my dear.” Then, smiling, he answered, “The Vedas sing that even the lowest person becomes free when Ram’s name comes to the mouth at death.”
ramacharitamanas::3847.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कहा (said) / तनु (body) / राखहु (keep) / ताता (dear) / मुख (mouth) / मुसुकाइ (smiling) / कही (said) / तेहिं (that) / बाता (word)॥ / जाकर (whose) / नाम (name) / मरत (dying) / मुख (mouth) / आवा (comes) / अधमउ (even the lowest) / मुकुत (free) / होइ (becomes) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गावा (sing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3847.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3847.essence: Ram’s name can lift even the fallen at the end.
ramacharitamanas::3847.simple_meaning: Ram says the old bird should keep living, then reminds him that even the most fallen person can be freed by remembering Ram at death.
ramacharitamanas::3847.simple_insight: There is no one beyond grace when the heart turns toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3847.detailed_meaning: Jatayu lies wounded after fighting Ravana to protect Sita. Ram comforts him, but Jatayu knows his end is near. Smiling through pain, he points to the power of Ram’s name and finds dignity in dying with remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::3847.modern_relevance: A hospital room goes quiet after bad news. Someone you love is fading, and all the usual plans feel small. This verse says the last breath is not empty if Ram is remembered.
ramacharitamanas::3847.insight: It shifts attention from fear of death to the saving power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::3848.verse_sanskrit: सो मम लोचन गोचर आगें। राखौं देह नाथ केहि खाँगें॥ जल भरि नयन कहहिं रघुराई। तात कर्म निज तें गति पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3848.verse_hindi: वही (आप) मेरे नेत्रों के विषय होकर सामने खड़े हैं। हे नाथ! अब मैं किस कमी (की पूर्ति) के लिए देह को रखूँ? नेत्रों में जल भरकर श्री रघुनाथजी कहने लगे- हे तात! आपने अपने श्रेष्ठ कर्मों से (दुर्लभ) गति पाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3848.english_translation: You are standing before my eyes. O Lord, why should I keep this body now? With tears in his eyes, Raghunath said, 'Father, by your own noble actions you have reached a rare state.'
ramacharitamanas::3848.translation_literal: सो (that) / मम (my) / लोचन (eyes) / गोचर (within sight) / आगें (before) / राखौं (should I keep) / देह (body) / नाथ (lord) / केहि (for what) / खाँगें (need) ॥ / जल (water) / भरि (filled) / नयन (eyes) / कहहिं (say) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / तात (father) / कर्म (actions) / निज (own) / तें (from) / गति (state, destination) / पाई (obtained) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3848.speaker: Rama
ramacharitamanas::3848.essence: A life of noble action can make even death feel like fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::3848.simple_meaning: Seeing the beloved before him, he feels there is no need to keep living in the same way. He also honors the father’s noble actions as the cause of a rare spiritual state.
ramacharitamanas::3848.simple_insight: Deep love can make clinging to the body feel empty. What matters is the quality of your actions.
ramacharitamanas::3848.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram stands before the dying Jatayu, the vulture who fought Ravana to protect Sita. Overcome with tenderness, Ram speaks through tears: the sight of such devotion makes even the body seem unnecessary, and he blesses Jatayu for his noble deeds.
ramacharitamanas::3848.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital room after they have fought for everyone else. Their presence makes everything else smaller. This verse knows the quiet dignity of a life lived well.
ramacharitamanas::3848.insight: It shifts attention from fear of loss to the worth of a life shaped by noble action.

ramacharitamanas::3849.verse_sanskrit: परहित बस जिन्ह के मन माहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ जग दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तनु तिज तात जाहु मम धामा। देउँ काह तुम्ह पूरनकामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3849.verse_hindi: जिनके मन में दूसरे का हित बसता है (समाया रहता है), उनके लिए जगत् में कुछ भी (कोई भी गति) दुर्लभ नहीं है। हे तात! शरीर छोड़कर आप मेरे परम धाम में जाइए। मैं आपको क्या दूँ? आप तो पूर्णकाम हैं (सब कुछ पा चुके हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3849.english_translation: Those whose minds dwell on the welfare of others lose nothing in this world. Dear father, leave this body and go to my supreme abode. What can I give you? You are already fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::3849.translation_literal: परहित (others' welfare) / बस (dwells) / जिन्ह (whose) / के (of) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / तिन्ह (for them) / कहुँ (for) / जग (world) / दुर्लभ (hard to obtain) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (not) ॥ / तनु (body) / तिज (leaving) / तात (dear father) / जाहु (go) / मम (my) / धामा (abode) ॥ / देउँ (shall give) / काह (what) / तुम्ह (to you) / पूरनकामा (fully fulfilled one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3849.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3849.essence: A heart for others is already full.
ramacharitamanas::3849.simple_meaning: A heart focused on the welfare of others is never deprived. Ram tells the devoted father to leave the body and come to his own abode, because a fully fulfilled person needs nothing more.
ramacharitamanas::3849.simple_insight: True fullness comes from caring beyond yourself, not from collecting more.
ramacharitamanas::3849.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a dying father speaks with Ram after hearing the truth about his son. Ram answers with tenderness: anyone whose mind rests on others' welfare lacks nothing, and such a person is already complete. The moment turns grief into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3849.modern_relevance: You spend years helping everyone else, then realize you no longer feel hungry for praise or payoff. That quiet fullness is what this verse honors: a life shaped by concern for others becomes inwardly complete.
ramacharitamanas::3849.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to generous concern, showing that wholeness grows through care.

ramacharitamanas::3850.verse_sanskrit: सीता हरन तात जनि कहहु पिता सन जाइ। जौं मैं राम त कुल सहित कहिहि दसानन आइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3850.verse_hindi: हे तात! सीता हरण की बात आप जाकर पिताजी से न कहिएगा। यदि मैं राम हूँ तो दशमुख रावण कुटुम्ब सहित वहाँ आकर स्वयं ही कहेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3850.english_translation: Do not go tell Father about Sita's abduction. If I am Ram, then Ravana of ten faces will come there himself, with his whole family, and say it.
ramacharitamanas::3850.translation_literal: सीता हरन (Sita's abduction) / तात (dear father) / जनि (do not) / कहहु (say/tell) / पिता सन (to Father) / जाइ (going) / जौं (if) / मैं (I) / राम (Ram) / त कुल सहित (with the whole family) / कहिहि (will say) / दसानन (Ravana, ten-faced one) / आइ (coming)
ramacharitamanas::3850.speaker: Jatayu
ramacharitamanas::3850.essence: True faith is calm enough to let justice arrive on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3850.simple_meaning: Jatayu tells Rama not to report Sita's abduction to Dasharath. He is so sure of Rama's power that he says Ravana himself will eventually come and answer for it.
ramacharitamanas::3850.simple_insight: Faith can be so steady that even humiliation feels temporary.
ramacharitamanas::3850.detailed_meaning: Jatayu lies wounded after fighting Ravana to protect Sita. In his final moments, he urges Rama not to burden Dasharath with the news. He trusts that Rama's justice is so certain that Ravana will be forced to face it directly.
ramacharitamanas::3850.modern_relevance: You know the people who wronged you will eventually have to face what they did, even if nobody sees it today. That quiet confidence keeps panic from taking over.
ramacharitamanas::3850.insight: It shifts you from frantic reporting of harm to calm trust that wrongdoing answers to dharma.

ramacharitamanas::3851.verse_sanskrit: गीध देह तजि धरि हरि रूपा। भूषन बहु पट पीत अनूपा॥ स्याम गात बिसाल भुज चारी। अस्तुति करत नयन भरि बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3851.verse_hindi: जटायु ने गीध की देह त्यागकर हरि का रूप धारण किया और बहुत से अनुपम (दिव्य) आभूषण और (दिव्य) पीताम्बर पहन लिए। श्याम शरीर है, विशाल चार भुजाएँ हैं और नेत्रों में (प्रेम तथा आनंद के आँसुओं का) जल भरकर वह स्तुति कर रहा है- ॥ छंद :
ramacharitamanas::3851.english_translation: Jatayu, leaving behind the body of a vulture, assumed the form of Hari. He wore many incomparable divine ornaments and a beautiful yellow garment. His body was dark, his four arms were broad, and tears filled his eyes as he praised Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3851.translation_literal: गीध (vulture) / देह (body) / तजि (leaving) / धरि (taking) / हरि (Hari/Ram) / रूपा (form) / भूषन (ornaments) / बहु (many) / पट (cloth/garment) / पीत (yellow) / अनूपा (incomparable) / स्याम (dark) / गात (body) / बिसाल (vast) / भुज (arms) / चारी (four) / अस्तुति (praise) / करत (doing) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (filled) / बारी (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::3851.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3851.essence: Pure devotion can turn even a broken body into worship.
ramacharitamanas::3851.simple_meaning: Jatayu's fallen body is transformed into a radiant form of Ram, and he praises Ram with tears of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3851.simple_insight: Love does not end with death or loss; it can lift even grief into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3851.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has just given his life trying to stop Ravana from taking Sita. In this moment of sacred ending, his vulture body is described as taking on Ram's form, showing that pure devotion turns even death into worship.
ramacharitamanas::3851.modern_relevance: You visit someone in the hospital after a heartbreaking diagnosis, and they still speak with gratitude. Something in that room changes — pain is still there, but it no longer has the final word.
ramacharitamanas::3851.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing loss as defeat to seeing devotion as transformation.

ramacharitamanas::3852.verse_sanskrit: जय राम रूप अनूप निर्गुन सगुन गुन प्रेरक सही। दससीस बाहु प्रचंड खंडन चंड सर मंडन मही॥ पाथोद गात सरोज मुख राजीव आयत लोचनं। नित नौमि रामु कृपाल बाहु बिसाल भव भय मोचनं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3852.verse_hindi: हे रामजी! आपकी जय हो। आपका रूप अनुपम है, आप निर्गुण हैं, सगुण हैं और सत्य ही गुणों के (माया के) प्रेरक हैं। दस सिर वाले रावण की प्रचण्ड भुजाओं को खंड-खंड करने के लिए प्रचण्ड बाण धारण करने वाले, पृथ्वी को सुशोभित करने वाले, जलयुक्त मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर वाले, कमल के समान मुख और (लाल) कमल के समान विशाल नेत्रों वाले, विशाल भुजाओं वाले और भव-भय से छुड़ाने वाले कृपालु श्री रामजी को मैं नित्य नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3852.english_translation: Victory to Ram, whose form is incomparable: beyond qualities and yet the source of qualities. He shattered ten-headed Ravana's mighty arms, adorns the earth, has a dark body like a raincloud, a lotus face, wide lotus eyes, vast arms, and is the compassionate remover of the fear of becoming.
ramacharitamanas::3852.translation_literal: जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / रूप (form) / अनूप (incomparable) / निर्गुन (beyond qualities) / सगुन (with qualities) / गुन (qualities) / प्रेरक (stimulator/source) / सही (truly) / दससीस (ten-headed) / बाहु (arms) / प्रचंड (mighty) / खंडन (shattering) / चंड (fierce) / सर (arrow) / मंडन (adornment) / मही (earth) / पाथोद (raincloud) / गात (body) / सरोज (lotus) / मुख (face) / राजीव (lotus) / आयत (wide) / लोचनं (eyes) / नित (always) / नौमि (I bow) / रामु (Ram) / कृपाल (compassionate) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाल (vast) / भव (becoming/worldly existence) / भय (fear) / मोचनं (remover)
ramacharitamanas::3852.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3852.essence: Ram is both beyond all qualities and lovingly present in form.
ramacharitamanas::3852.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as beyond qualities and yet full of qualities, beautiful in form, mighty in battle, and endlessly compassionate. He is the one who removes fear and is worthy of constant reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3852.simple_insight: You can love the infinite without losing the beauty of a personal form.
ramacharitamanas::3852.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu's sacrifice in the forest, Tulsidas turns from the scene of grief to praise. He bows to Ram as both beyond attributes and vividly present, the compassionate protector whose power destroys Ravana and whose beauty steadies the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3852.modern_relevance: You stand in front of your home altar after a hard day, too tired for theory and too wounded for slogans. What you need is a presence that is both vast enough for your fear and close enough to hold it.
ramacharitamanas::3852.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract distance to intimate reverence for a form that carries the infinite.

ramacharitamanas::3853.verse_sanskrit: बलमप्रमेयमनादिमजमब्यक्तमेकमगोचरं। गोबिंद गोपर द्वंद्वहर बिग्यानघन धरनीधरं॥ जे राम मंत्र जपंत संत अनंत जन मन रंजनं। नित नौमि राम अकाम प्रिय कामादि खल दल गंजनं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3853.verse_hindi: आप अपरिमित बलवाले हैं, अनादि, अजन्मा, अव्यक्त (निराकार), एक अगोचर (अलक्ष्य), गोविंद (वेद वाक्यों द्वारा जानने योग्य), इंद्रियों से अतीत, (जन्म-मरण, सुख-दुःख, हर्ष-शोकादि) द्वंद्वों को हरने वाले, विज्ञान की घनमूर्ति और पृथ्वी के आधार हैं तथा जो संत राम मंत्र को जपते हैं, उन अनन्त सेवकों के मन को आनंद देने वाले हैं। उन निष्कामप्रिय (निष्कामजनों के प्रेमी अथवा उन्हें प्रिय) तथा काम आदि दुष्टों (दुष्ट वृत्तियों) के दल का दलन करने वाले श्री रामजी को मैं नित्य नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3853.english_translation: You are immeasurable in strength, without beginning, unborn, unmanifest, one, beyond the senses, the giver of wisdom, the remover of duality, and the support of the earth. Saints who chant Ram's mantra delight in you forever. I bow daily to Ram, dear to the selfless, destroyer of desire and its dark forces.
ramacharitamanas::3853.translation_literal: बलम (strength) / अप्रमेय (immeasurable) / अनादि (without beginning) / अज (unborn) / अब्यक्त (unmanifest) / एक (one) / अगोचरं (beyond the senses) / गोबिंद (knower of the senses) / गोपर (protector of the senses) / द्वंद्वहर (remover of duality) / बिग्यानघन (dense mass of wisdom) / धरनीधरं (support of the earth) / जे (those who) / राम (Ram) / मंत्र (mantra) / जपंत (chant) / संत (saints) / अनंत (endless) / जन (beings) / मन (mind) / रंजनं (delighting) / नित (daily) / नौमि (I bow) / राम (Ram) / अकाम (without desire) / प्रिय (dear) / कामादि (desire and others) / खल (dark) / दल (forces) / गंजनं (destroyer)
ramacharitamanas::3853.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3853.essence: The highest Ram is nearest to the heart that repeats his name.
ramacharitamanas::3853.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond all limits and beyond the senses, yet his name brings joy to devoted hearts. Tulsidas bows to him as the destroyer of desire and darkness.
ramacharitamanas::3853.simple_insight: You do not have to grasp the infinite to be held by it.
ramacharitamanas::3853.detailed_meaning: In the forest, after Jatayu's praise and before the next description of Ram's form, Tulsidas pauses to name Ram as both beyond form and intimate to devotion. He links cosmic greatness with the peace given to those who repeat Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3853.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard day, scrolling for something to calm the noise in your head. What settles you is not more stimulation, but a name, a presence, a reminder that what is highest can also be nearest.
ramacharitamanas::3853.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to a lived refuge that quiets desire and confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3854.verse_sanskrit: जेहि श्रुति निरंजन ब्रह्म ब्यापक बिरज अज कहि गावहीं। करि ध्यान ग्यान बिराग जोग अनेक मुनि जेहि पावहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::3854.verse_hindi: सो प्रगट करुना कंद सोभा बृंद अग जग मोहई। मम हृदय पंकज भृंग अंग अनंग बहु छबि सोहई ॥ जिनको श्रुतियाँ निरंजन (माया से परे), ब्रह्म, व्यापक, निर्विकार और जन्मरहित कहकर गान करती हैं। मुनि जिन्हें ध्यान, ज्ञान, वैराग्य और योग आदि अनेक साधन करके पाते हैं। वे ही करुणाकन्द, शोभा के समूह (स्वयं श्री भगवान् ) प्रकट होकर जड़-चेतन समस्त जगत् को मोहित कर रहे हैं। मेरे हृदय कमल के भ्रमर रूप उनके अंग-अंग में बहुत से कामदेवों की छवि शोभा पा रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3854.english_translation: The Vedas sing of the one who is stainless Brahman, all-pervading, free from impurity, unborn. Many sages attain that one through meditation, knowledge, detachment, and yoga. That same one has now appeared as the source of compassion, whose beauty enchants the worlds, and whose form fills my heart like a bee in a lotus.
ramacharitamanas::3854.translation_literal: जेहि (whom) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / निरंजन (stainless, beyond illusion) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / बिरज (free from impurity) / अज (unborn) / कहि (saying) / गावहीं (sing) / करि (doing) / ध्यान (meditation) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिराग (detachment) / जोग (yoga) / अनेक (many) / मुनि (sages) / जेहि (whom) / पावहीं (attain) / सो (that same one) / प्रगट (manifest) / करुना (compassion) / कंद (source) / सोभा (beauty) / बृंद (group, abundance) / अग (moving) / जग (world) / मोहई (enchants) / मम (my) / हृदय (heart) / पंकज (lotus) / भृंग (bee) / अंग (limb, body) / अनंग (love, beauty) / बहु (many) / छबि (splendors) / सोहई (adorns)
ramacharitamanas::3854.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3854.essence: What sages seek as absolute appears here as beloved and near.
ramacharitamanas::3854.simple_meaning: The Vedas describe the supreme reality as pure, all-pervading, unborn, and beyond impurity. Sages reach it through meditation, knowledge, detachment, and yoga. Yet that same reality now appears as Ram, whose beauty captivates the world.
ramacharitamanas::3854.simple_insight: What seems remote and absolute can also arrive as intimate and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::3854.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poet turns from abstract praise to direct devotion. He says the reality described by the Vedas and reached by sages through hard practice is now standing before him as Ram, radiant with compassion and beauty, filling his heart completely.
ramacharitamanas::3854.modern_relevance: You spend years trying to understand something noble through books, silence, and discipline. Then one day it feels near, personal, and unmistakably alive — as if the truth you chased has been looking back at you.
ramacharitamanas::3854.insight: It shifts the mind from distant abstraction to living presence, showing that the highest reality can be loved directly.

ramacharitamanas::3855.verse_sanskrit: जो अगम सुगम सुभाव निर्मल असम सम सीतल सदा। पस्यंति जं जोगी जतन करि करत मन गो बस सदा॥ सो राम रमा निवास संतत दास बस त्रिभुवन धनी। मम उर बसउ सो समन संसृति जासु कीरति पावनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3855.verse_hindi: जो अगम और सुगम हैं, निर्मल स्वभाव हैं, विषम और सम हैं और सदा शीतल (शांत) हैं। मन और इंद्रियों को सदा वश में करते हुए योगी बहुत साधन करने पर जिन्हें देख पाते हैं। वे तीनों लोकों के स्वामी, रमानिवास श्री रामजी निरंतर अपने दासों के वश में रहते हैं। वे ही मेरे हृदय में निवास करें, जिनकी पवित्र कीर्ति आवागमन को मिटाने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3855.english_translation: You are hard to reach, yet easy to reach by your own nature: pure, even-minded, always cool. Yogis can see you only after great effort, when they have fully mastered the mind and senses. You, Ram, the home of Lakshmi and lord of the three worlds, live under the control of your devotees. May you dwell in my heart; your holy fame ends the cycle of rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::3855.translation_literal: जो (who) / अगम (hard to reach) / सुगम (easy to reach) / सुभाव (own nature) / निर्मल (pure) / असम (unequal) / सम (equal) / सीतल (cool, शांत) / सदा (always) / पस्यंति (see) / जं (whom) / जोगी (yogis) / जतन करि (with effort) / करत (doing) / मन (mind) / गोबस (under control) / सदा (always) / सो (that) / राम (Ram) / रमा (Lakshmi) / निवास (abode) / संतत (always) / दास (devotees) / बस (under the control) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / धनी (lord) / मम (my) / उर (heart) / बसउ (may dwell) / सो (that one) / समन (destroys) / संसृति (cycle of rebirth) / जासु (whose) / कीरति (fame) / पावनी (purifying)
ramacharitamanas::3855.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3855.essence: Ram is hardest to reach and easiest to love.
ramacharitamanas::3855.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond ordinary reach, yet he becomes near through devotion. Even yogis need deep discipline to glimpse him, but he belongs willingly to his devotees and brings freedom from rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::3855.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that closeness to the divine is not earned by strain alone.
ramacharitamanas::3855.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Tulsidas turns from the danger of exile to Ram's nature itself. He praises Ram as the one yogis struggle to perceive, yet who lovingly stays under the care of his devotees. The prayer ends with a plea for Ram to live in the poet's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3855.modern_relevance: You can meditate for years and still feel far away, then one sincere prayer suddenly makes the room feel full. This verse says nearness is not only about effort; it is also about loving surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3855.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship: the seeker is not only climbing toward Ram, but being welcomed by him.

ramacharitamanas::3856.verse_sanskrit: अबिरल भगति मागि बर गीध गयउ हरिधाम। तेहि की क्रिया जथोचित निज कर कीन्ही राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3856.verse_hindi: अखंड भक्ति का वर माँगकर गृध्रराज जटायु श्री हरि के परमधाम को चला गया। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उसकी (दाहकर्म आदि सारी) क्रियाएँ यथायोग्य अपने हाथों से कीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3856.english_translation: Having asked for the boon of unwavering devotion, the vulture-king Jatayu went to the abode of the divine. Ram himself performed the rites for him properly with his own hands.
ramacharitamanas::3856.translation_literal: अबिरल (unbroken) / भगति (devotion) / मागि (having asked for) / बर (boon) / गीध (vulture) / गयउ (went) / हरिधाम (the abode of Hari) / तेहि (for him) / की (of) / क्रिया (rites) / जथोचित (properly) / निज (own) / कर (hand) / कीन्ही (did) / राम (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::3856.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3856.essence: Unbroken devotion makes Ram personally answer your final hour.
ramacharitamanas::3856.simple_meaning: Jatayu asked only for unbroken devotion and went to Ram's abode. Ram then personally performed his funeral rites with proper care.
ramacharitamanas::3856.simple_insight: Love given to the divine is never ignored; even death is met with tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3856.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu fights Ravana to protect Sita and is mortally wounded, he asks only for unbroken devotion before leaving this world. Ram arrives, grieves him, and performs the rites himself, showing the depth of divine gratitude and care.
ramacharitamanas::3856.modern_relevance: You stand beside someone who gave everything and received nothing back. This verse says that true devotion is seen, remembered, and honored — even when the world is late.
ramacharitamanas::3856.insight: It teaches you that selfless service creates a bond strong enough to outlast loss.

ramacharitamanas::3857.verse_sanskrit: कोमल चित अति दीनदयाला। कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला॥ गीध अधम खग आमिष भोगी। गति दीन्ही जो जाचत जोगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3857.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी अत्यंत कोमल चित्त वाले, दीनदयालु और बिना ही करण कृपालु हैं। गीध (पक्षियों में भी) अधम पक्षी और मांसाहारी था, उसको भी वह दुर्लभ गति दी, जिसे योगीजन माँगते रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3857.english_translation: Raghunath has a very soft heart, is deeply compassionate to the humble, and shows mercy without any cause. He gave Jatayu, a lowly bird and meat-eater, the state that yogis keep asking for.
ramacharitamanas::3857.translation_literal: कोमल (soft) / चित (heart-mind) / अति (very) / दीनदयाला (compassionate to the humble) / कारन (cause) / बिनु (without) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / कृपाला (merciful) / गीध (vulture/Jatayu) / अधम (lowly) / खग (bird) / आमिष (meat) / भोगी (eater) / गति (state/destination) / दीन्ही (gave) / जो (which) / जाचत (asking) / जोगी (yogis) /
ramacharitamanas::3857.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3857.essence: Ram lifts the lowly to the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::3857.simple_meaning: Ram is naturally gentle and compassionate. He gave Jatayu, though a humble bird, the highest state that even yogis seek.
ramacharitamanas::3857.simple_insight: You do not have to be impressive to be held by grace.
ramacharitamanas::3857.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has just died protecting Sita. In the forest, Ram does not see a mere bird or a failed creature; he sees devotion and courage, and he honors it with the highest grace. The verse reveals how Ram responds to selfless love.
ramacharitamanas::3857.modern_relevance: You stayed by a friend in the hospital when everyone else drifted away. No applause came, but your care mattered. This verse says that quiet loyalty is never wasted.
ramacharitamanas::3857.insight: It shifts the mind from judging worth by status to recognizing devotion and sacrifice as what truly matters.

ramacharitamanas::3858.verse_sanskrit: सुनहू उमा ते लोग अभागी। हरि तजि होहिं बिषय अनुरागी। पुनि सीतहि खोजत द्वौ भाई। चले बिलोकत बन बहुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3858.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! सुनो, वे लोग अभागे हैं, जो भगवान् को छोड़कर विषयों से अनुराग करते हैं। फिर दोनों भाई सीताजी को खोजते हुए आगे चले। वे वन की सघनता देखते जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3858.english_translation: Listen, Uma: those people are unfortunate who abandon Hari and become attached to worldly pleasures. Then the two brothers continued searching for Sita, walking onward and looking over the forest.
ramacharitamanas::3858.translation_literal: सुनहू (listen) / उमा (Uma) / ते (those) / लोग (people) / अभागी (unfortunate) / हरि (Hari) / तजि (leaving) / होहिं (become) / बिषय (worldly pleasures) / अनुरागी (attached) / पुनि (then) / सीतहि (Sita) / खोजत (searching) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) / चले (walked) / बिलोकत (looking) / बन (forest) / बहुताई (much, in abundance)
ramacharitamanas::3858.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3858.essence: Leaving the divine for cravings is the real misfortune.
ramacharitamanas::3858.simple_meaning: People lose their way when they turn from Hari and cling to worldly pleasures. After that warning, Ram and Lakshman keep moving through the forest to search for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3858.simple_insight: Attachment narrows the heart; devotion keeps you moving through hard terrain.
ramacharitamanas::3858.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to Parvati in the forest-search section of Aranyakand. He first gives a sharp moral warning about abandoning Hari for sense-pleasures, then the scene returns to Ram and Lakshman pressing on through the wilderness as they search for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3858.modern_relevance: You scroll for comfort after a hard day, and the hour disappears. The verse points to that same drift: turning away from what matters most makes you feel poorer, not fuller.
ramacharitamanas::3858.insight: It contrasts inner loss with steady action: avoid being pulled into craving, and keep walking toward what matters.

ramacharitamanas::3859.verse_sanskrit: संकुल लता बिटप घन कानन। बहु खग मृग तहँ गज पंचानन॥ आवत पंथ कबंध निपाता। तेहिं सब कही साप कै बाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3859.verse_hindi: वह सघन वन लताओं और वृक्षों से भरा है। उसमें बहुत से पक्षी, मृग, हाथी और सिंह रहते हैं। श्री रामजी ने रास्ते में आते हुए कबंध राक्षस को मार डाला। उसने अपने शाप की सारी बात कही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3859.english_translation: The forest is thick with vines and trees, full of birds, deer, elephants, and lions. As Ram walked the path, he struck down Kabandha, and Kabandha told the story of his curse.
ramacharitamanas::3859.translation_literal: संकुल (crowded/thick) / लता (vines) / बिटप (trees) / घन (dense) / कानन (forest) / बहु (many) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer) / तहँ (there) / गज (elephants) / पंचानन (lions) / आवत (coming) / पंथ (path) / कबंध (Kabandha) / निपाता (struck down) / तेहिं (he) / सब (all) / कही (told) / साप (curse) / कै (of) / बाता (story)
ramacharitamanas::3859.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3859.essence: A cursed obstacle can become the next clue forward.
ramacharitamanas::3859.simple_meaning: The forest is crowded with life, and Ram meets Kabandha on the path, strikes him down, and hears the story of his curse.
ramacharitamanas::3859.simple_insight: Even a dangerous encounter can become part of a larger rescue.
ramacharitamanas::3859.detailed_meaning: In the forest search for Sita, Ram and Lakshman move through dense wilderness alive with animals. Kabandha appears on the path, is slain, and then reveals the curse that bound him. The verse shifts the story from danger to revelation.
ramacharitamanas::3859.modern_relevance: You are walking through a situation that feels tangled and unsafe, then one hard encounter suddenly explains what has been hidden all along.
ramacharitamanas::3859.insight: It turns a frightening obstacle into a doorway for understanding.

ramacharitamanas::3860.verse_sanskrit: दुरबासा मोहि दीन्ही सापा। प्रभु पद पेखि मिटा सो पापा॥ सुनु गंधर्ब कहउँ मैं तोही। मोहि न सोहाइ ब्रह्मकुल द्रोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3860.verse_hindi: (वह बोला-) दुर्वासाजी ने मुझे शाप दिया था। अब प्रभु के चरणों को देखने से वह पाप मिट गया। (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे गंधर्व! सुनो, मैं तुम्हें कहता हूँ, ब्राह्मणकुल से द्रोह करने वाला मुझे नहीं सुहाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3860.english_translation: (He said:) Durvasa had cursed me. Seeing the Lord's feet, that wrongdoing was washed away. (Shri Ram said:) O Gandharva, listen, I tell you: I do not approve of anyone who betrays the Brahmin community.
ramacharitamanas::3860.translation_literal: दुरबासा (Durvasa) / मोहि (me) / दीन्ही (gave) / सापा (curse) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / पेखि (seeing) / मिटा (was erased) / सो (that) / पापा (wrongdoing) / सुनु (listen) / गंधर्ब (Gandharva) / कहउँ (I say) / मैं (I) / तोही (to you) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / सोहाइ (is pleasing) / ब्रह्मकुल (Brahmin line/community) / द्रोही (betrayer)
ramacharitamanas::3860.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3860.essence: Grace can wash away guilt, but it never excuses betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::3860.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram removes the burden of wrongdoing. Ram then says that betraying the Brahmin community is unacceptable to him.
ramacharitamanas::3860.simple_insight: Devotion cleanses the heart, but integrity in conduct still matters.
ramacharitamanas::3860.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram and Lakshman are moving through the aftermath of Jatayu and Kabandha when a Gandharva speaks of his curse and release. Ram responds by affirming a moral boundary: betrayal of the Brahmin community is never pleasing to him.
ramacharitamanas::3860.modern_relevance: A person may feel relieved after a private apology or prayer, yet still need to face the harm they caused. Inner relief does not cancel ethical responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::3860.insight: It separates spiritual relief from moral accountability: cleansing the heart does not excuse betrayal.

ramacharitamanas::3861.verse_sanskrit: मन क्रम बचन कपट तजि जो कर भूसुर सेव। मोहि समेत बिरंचि सिव बस ताकें सब देव ॥
ramacharitamanas::3861.verse_hindi: मन, वचन और कर्म से कपट छोड़कर जो भूदेव ब्राह्मणों की सेवा करता है, मुझ समेत ब्रह्मा, शिव आदि सब देवता उसके वश हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3861.english_translation: One who serves the learned with body, mind, and speech, without deceit, wins the favor of me, Brahma, Shiva, and all radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::3861.translation_literal: मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / कपट (deceit) / तजि (leaving) / जो (who) / कर (does) / भूसुर (learned Brahmins) / सेव (service) / मोहि (me) / समेत (together with) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सिव (Shiva) / बस (under control) / ताकें (of that one) / सब (all) / देव (radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::3861.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3861.essence: Sincere service without deceit makes even higher powers responsive.
ramacharitamanas::3861.simple_meaning: Serve holy people sincerely in thought, word, and action, without any trickery, and even the highest powers become favorable to you.
ramacharitamanas::3861.simple_insight: Pure service makes you feel supported by something larger than yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3861.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has just spoken with a cursed being whose pain lifts when he sees Ram's feet. The teaching turns from rescue to conduct: serve the learned with complete sincerity, because true service changes the whole order around you.
ramacharitamanas::3861.modern_relevance: You help an elder carry groceries, but you do it without showing off or expecting praise. That quiet sincerity changes the room more than the favor itself.
ramacharitamanas::3861.insight: It shifts the mind from performance to wholehearted service, where integrity matters more than display.

ramacharitamanas::3862.verse_sanskrit: सापत ताड़त परुष कहंता। बिप्र पूज्य अस गावहिं संता॥ पूजिअ बिप्र सील गुन हीना। सूद्र न गुन गन ग्यान प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3862.verse_hindi: शाप देता हुआ, मारता हुआ और कठोर वचन कहता हुआ भी ब्राह्मण पूजनीय है, ऐसा संत कहते हैं। शील और गुण से हीन भी ब्राह्मण पूजनीय है। और गुण गणों से युक्त और ज्ञान में निपुण भी शूद्र पूजनीय नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3862.english_translation: Even if a Brahmin curses, beats, or speaks harshly, the saints say he remains worthy of honor. Even a Brahmin lacking character and virtue is to be honored. But a Shudra rich in qualities and wisdom is not honored.
ramacharitamanas::3862.translation_literal: सापत (cursing) / ताड़त (beating) / परुष (harsh) / कहंता (speaking) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / पूज्य (worthy of honor) / अस (thus) / गावहिं (sing) / संता (the saints)॥ / पूजिअ (is honored) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / सील (character) / गुन (virtues) / हीना (lacking) / सूद्र (Shudra) / न (not) / गुन (virtues) / गन (groups) / ग्यान (wisdom) / प्रबीना (skilled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3862.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3862.essence: Status can command reverence even when character is lacking.
ramacharitamanas::3862.simple_meaning: The verse says that saints honor a Brahmin even when he behaves badly, while a Shudra is not honored even if he is wise and virtuous.
ramacharitamanas::3862.simple_insight: It challenges easy judgments and asks you to see how social duty can override personal merit.
ramacharitamanas::3862.detailed_meaning: After the Gandharva is forgiven, the poem turns to a hard social teaching. Ram explains the traditional order of honor in this world: even a flawed Brahmin is to be revered, while a capable Shudra is not placed in that same position. The moment reveals the values of the age.
ramacharitamanas::3862.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone with status says something crude and still gets respect, while a quietly capable person is overlooked. The verse exposes how communities often honor rank before character.
ramacharitamanas::3862.insight: It separates social reverence from personal virtue, showing how inherited order can outrank individual excellence.

ramacharitamanas::3863.verse_sanskrit: कहि निज धर्म ताहि समुझावा। निज पद प्रीति देखि मन भावा॥ रघुपति चरन कमल सिरु नाई। गयउ गगन आपनि गति पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3863.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने अपना धर्म (भागवत धर्म) कहकर उसे समझाया। अपने चरणों में प्रेम देखकर वह उनके मन को भाया। तदनन्तर श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाकर वह अपनी गति (गंधर्व का स्वरूप) पाकर आकाश में चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3863.english_translation: Having explained his own dharma, he was pleased to see devotion in his own feet. Bowing his head to the lotus feet of Raghupati, he went to the sky and attained his own form.
ramacharitamanas::3863.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / निज (own) / धर्म (dharma) / ताहि (to him) / समुझावा (explained) / निज (own) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / देखि (seeing) / मन (mind) / भावा (was pleased)॥ / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / चरन (feet) / कमल (lotus) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / गयउ (went) / गगन (sky) / आपनि (own) / गति (form/state) / पाई (having attained)॥
ramacharitamanas::3863.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3863.essence: Devotion to Ram returns you to your true form.
ramacharitamanas::3863.simple_meaning: Ram explains the being's rightful duty, and the being is moved by love for Ram's feet. After bowing, it rises to the sky and regains its original form.
ramacharitamanas::3863.simple_insight: Love for Ram transforms you and restores what was hidden in you all along.
ramacharitamanas::3863.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram meets a celestial being in disguise and teaches him his true dharma. Seeing real devotion in that being's heart, Ram is pleased. The being bows to Ram's lotus feet and is released back to his own heavenly form.
ramacharitamanas::3863.modern_relevance: You meet someone who sees your goodness before you can name it. That trust can steady you, and honest reverence can change the direction of your life.
ramacharitamanas::3863.insight: It shows that devotion is not just emotion; it restores identity and lifts the devotee beyond limitation.

ramacharitamanas::3864.verse_sanskrit: ताहि देइ गति राम उदारा। सबरी कें आश्रम पगु धारा॥ सबरी देखि राम गृहँ आए। मुनि के बचन समुझि जियँ भाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3864.verse_hindi: उदार श्री रामजी उसे गति देकर शबरीजी के आश्रम में पधारे। शबरीजी ने श्री रामचंद्रजी को घर में आए देखा, तब मुनि मतंगजी के वचनों को याद करके उनका मन प्रसन्न हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3864.english_translation: Granting him his onward state, noble Ram went to Shabari's hermitage. Seeing Ram come to her home, Shabari's heart rejoiced, remembering the sage Matanga's words.
ramacharitamanas::3864.translation_literal: ताहि (to him) / देइ (giving) / गति (the onward state) / राम (Ram) / उदारा (noble, generous) / सबरी कें (to Shabari's) / आश्रम (hermitage) / पगु (footsteps) / धारा (brought, placed) ॥ / सबरी (Shabari) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / गृहँ (home) / आए (came) / मुनि (sage) / के (of) / बचन (words) / समुझि (remembering, understanding) / जियँ (in the heart) / भाए (became pleasing, rejoiced) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3864.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3864.essence: Love makes room for Ram, and Ram comes.
ramacharitamanas::3864.simple_meaning: Ram blesses Shabari and comes to her hermitage. When she sees him arrive, she feels joy because the sage's promise has come true.
ramacharitamanas::3864.simple_insight: Waiting with devotion is not empty; it can become the very space where joy arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3864.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram reaches Shabari's humble hermitage after the sage Matanga's blessing has ripened. She sees him enter her home, and the remembered promise fills her heart with joy. This is devotion answered by presence.
ramacharitamanas::3864.modern_relevance: You keep a small lamp burning for someone you love, long after everyone else has stopped believing. Then, one day, they arrive and the whole room changes.
ramacharitamanas::3864.insight: It shifts attention from anxious waiting to faithful welcome. Devotion becomes readiness for grace.

ramacharitamanas::3865.verse_sanskrit: सरसिज लोचन बाहु बिसाला। जटा मुकुट सिर उर बनमाला॥ स्याम गौर सुंदर दोउ भाई। सबरी परी चरन लपटाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3865.verse_hindi: कमल सदृश नेत्र और विशाल भुजाओं वाले, सिर पर जटाओं का मुकुट और हृदय पर वनमाला धारण किए हुए सुंदर, साँवले और गोरे दोनों भाइयों के चरणों में शबरीजी लिपट पड़ीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3865.english_translation: With lotus-like eyes and broad arms, wearing matted hair as a crown and a forest garland on their chests, the beautiful dark and fair brothers, Shabari fell at their feet and clung to them.
ramacharitamanas::3865.translation_literal: सरसिज (lotus-like) / लोचन (eyes) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाला (broad, विशाल) / जटा (matted hair) / मुकुट (crown) / सिर (head) / उर (chest) / बनमाला (forest garland) / स्याम (dark) / गौर (fair) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / सबरी (Shabari) / परी (fell) / चरन (feet) / लपटाई (clung)
ramacharitamanas::3865.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3865.essence: Real devotion rushes toward the beloved without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3865.simple_meaning: Shabari is overwhelmed by Ram and Lakshman’s beauty and devotion, and she throws herself at their feet in joy.
ramacharitamanas::3865.simple_insight: Love can dissolve hesitation instantly. When the heart recognizes what it longs for, reverence becomes natural.
ramacharitamanas::3865.detailed_meaning: In Shabari’s forest hermitage, Ram and Lakshman arrive at last. Their presence is so beautiful and tender that Shabari cannot stay composed; she rushes to their feet and clings to them in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3865.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person whose kindness you trusted from afar, and all your practiced calm disappears. The body knows before the mind does: this is safe, this is cherished.
ramacharitamanas::3865.insight: It shifts devotion from an idea into a bodily response of recognition and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::3866.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम मगन मुख बचन न आवा। पुनि पुनि पद सरोज सिर नावा॥ सादर जल लै चरन पखारे। पुनि सुंदर आसन बैठारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3866.verse_hindi: वे प्रेम में मग्न हो गईं, मुख से वचन नहीं निकलता। बार-बार चरण-कमलों में सिर नवा रही हैं। फिर उन्होंने जल लेकर आदरपूर्वक दोनों भाइयों के चरण धोए और फिर उन्हें सुंदर आसनों पर बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3866.english_translation: She was so filled with love that no words came from her mouth. Again and again, she bowed her head at the lotus feet. With reverence, she brought water and washed the brothers' feet, then seated them on a beautiful seat.
ramacharitamanas::3866.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / मुख (mouth) / बचन (words) / न (not) / आवा (came) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पद (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / सिर (head) / नावा (bowed) / सादर (with reverence) / जल (water) / लै (taking) / चरन (feet) / पखारे (washed) / पुनि (again) / सुंदर (beautiful) / आसन (seat) / बैठारे (seated)
ramacharitamanas::3866.speaker: Shabari
ramacharitamanas::3866.essence: Love that is real turns into service before it turns into speech.
ramacharitamanas::3866.simple_meaning: Shabari is so overwhelmed with love that she cannot speak. Instead, she bows repeatedly, washes Ram and Lakshman’s feet, and seats them with honor.
ramacharitamanas::3866.simple_insight: Real devotion does not stay in the heart alone; it moves into humble, caring action.
ramacharitamanas::3866.detailed_meaning: In Shabari’s forest hermitage, Ram and Lakshman have finally arrived after years of waiting. Overcome by love, she cannot speak clearly. Her devotion shows itself in repeated bows, washing their feet, and offering them the best seat she has.
ramacharitamanas::3866.modern_relevance: You open the door to someone you’ve prayed for, and your throat tightens before you can say hello. The care is already in your hands.
ramacharitamanas::3866.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to embodied welcome, where respect becomes practical care.

ramacharitamanas::3867.verse_sanskrit: कंद मूल फल सुरस अति दिए राम कहुँ आनि। प्रेम सहित प्रभु खाए बारंबार बखानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3867.verse_hindi: उन्होंने अत्यंत रसीले और स्वादिष्ट कन्द, मूल और फल लाकर श्री रामजी को दिए। प्रभु ने बार-बार प्रशंसा करके उन्हें प्रेम सहित खाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3867.english_translation: They brought very juicy and delicious roots, bulbs, and fruits for Ram. The Lord ate them with love, praising them again and again.
ramacharitamanas::3867.translation_literal: कंद (roots/bulbs) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / सुरस (very juicy, tasteful) / अति (very) / दिए (gave) / राम कहुँ (to Ram) / आनि (bringing) / प्रेम सहित (with love) / प्रभु (the Lord) / खाए (ate) / बारंबार (again and again) / बखानि (praising)
ramacharitamanas::3867.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3867.essence: Love turns plain food into a feast.
ramacharitamanas::3867.simple_meaning: Shabari offers Ram simple forest food, and Ram accepts it lovingly, praising her devotion over the food itself.
ramacharitamanas::3867.simple_insight: Love makes even the simplest offering feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::3867.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shabari has just welcomed Ram and Lakshman after years of waiting. She gathers roots, bulbs, and fruits with care and offers them. Ram eats them gladly and praises her again and again, showing that devotion matters more than luxury.
ramacharitamanas::3867.modern_relevance: You bring someone homemade food after a hard day, and they light up because you remembered them. The gift is small; the care inside it is everything.
ramacharitamanas::3867.insight: It shifts attention from the value of the offering to the love that animates it.

ramacharitamanas::3868.verse_sanskrit: पानि जोरि आगें भइ ठाढ़ी। प्रभुहि बिलोकि प्रीति अति बाढ़ी॥ केहि बिधि अस्तुति करौं तुम्हारी। अधम जाति मैं जड़मति भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3868.verse_hindi: फिर वे हाथ जोड़कर आगे खड़ी हो गईं। प्रभु को देखकर उनका प्रेम अत्यंत बढ़ गया। (उन्होंने कहा-) मैं किस प्रकार आपकी स्तुति करूँ? मैं नीच जाति की और अत्यंत मूढ़ बुद्धि हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3868.english_translation: Then she stood before him with folded hands. Seeing the Lord, her love surged even more. “How can I praise you? I am of low birth and very dull-minded.”
ramacharitamanas::3868.translation_literal: पानि (hands) / जोरि (joining) / आगें (in front) / भइ (became) / ठाढ़ी (standing) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / प्रीति (love) / अति (very) / बाढ़ी (grew) / केहि (which) / बिधि (way) / अस्तुति (praise) / करौं (shall I do) / तुम्हारी (your) / अधम (low) / जाति (birth) / मैं (I) / जड़मति (dull-minded) / भारी (very much)
ramacharitamanas::3868.speaker: Shabari
ramacharitamanas::3868.essence: Love can make you feel unworthy and still draw you closer.
ramacharitamanas::3868.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram, Shabari’s love rises so much that she feels unworthy to praise him. Her devotion is mixed with deep humility.
ramacharitamanas::3868.simple_insight: Real devotion doesn’t inflate the self; it softens it into gratitude and awe.
ramacharitamanas::3868.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shabari stands before Ram with folded hands after serving him fruit with love. Now that she is face to face with him, her heart overflows, and she feels too small to find words. The moment turns from service into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3868.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you’ve admired for years, and all your rehearsed words disappear. What remains is a quiet feeling: your respect is bigger than your language.
ramacharitamanas::3868.insight: It shifts you from self-conscious performance to humble, wordless devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3869.verse_sanskrit: अधम ते अधम अधम अति नारी। तिन्ह महँ मैं मतिमंद अघारी॥ कह रघुपति सुनु भामिनि बाता। मानउँ एक भगति कर नाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3869.verse_hindi: जो अधम से भी अधम हैं, स्त्रियाँ उनमें भी अत्यंत अधम हैं, और उनमें भी हे पापनाशन! मैं मंदबुद्धि हूँ। श्री रघुनाथजी ने कहा- हे भामिनि! मेरी बात सुन! मैं तो केवल एक भक्ति ही का संबंध मानता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3869.english_translation: “I am lower than the lowest, lower than the lowest of the low. Among them, I am a foolish sinner. Raghupati said, ‘Listen, O gentle one: I accept only one bond—bond of devotion.’”
ramacharitamanas::3869.translation_literal: अधम (lowest) / ते (than) / अधम (lowest) / अधम (lowest) / अति (very) / नारी (woman) / तिन्ह (among them) / महँ (among) / मैं (I) / मतिमंद (foolish) / अघारी (sin-destroying one) / कह (said) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / सुनु (listen) / भामिनि (gentle one) / बाता (words) / मानउँ (I accept) / एक (one) / भगति (devotion) / कर (of) / नाता (bond)
ramacharitamanas::3869.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3869.essence: Devotion, not status, is the bond Ram recognises.
ramacharitamanas::3869.simple_meaning: Status, birth, and pride do not matter here. Ram says he accepts only one real relationship: devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3869.simple_insight: You can stop trying to be impressive. What matters most is the sincerity of your love.
ramacharitamanas::3869.detailed_meaning: Sita stands before Ram in the forest, humbled by his kindness and overwhelmed by his presence. She calls herself low and unworthy, but Ram answers by redefining worth: he recognises only the bond of devotion. That turns the scene into a teaching about love, not status.
ramacharitamanas::3869.modern_relevance: You walk into a room feeling small because everyone else seems more polished, more educated, more important. Then someone you respect responds to your sincerity, not your resume. That is the relief Ram offers here.
ramacharitamanas::3869.insight: It shifts attention from social worth to the quality of your devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3870.verse_sanskrit: जाति पाँति कुल धर्म बड़ाई। धन बल परिजन गुन चतुराई॥ भगति हीन नर सोहइ कैसा। बिनु जल बारिद देखिअ जैसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3870.verse_hindi: जाति, पाँति, कुल, धर्म, बड़ाई, धन, बल, कुटुम्ब, गुण और चतुरता- इन सबके होने पर भी भक्ति से रहित मनुष्य कैसा लगता है, जैसे जलहीन बादल (शोभाहीन) दिखाई पड़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3870.english_translation: What good are caste, class, family, duty, fame, wealth, strength, relatives, virtues, and cleverness? Without devotion, a person is like a cloud without water.
ramacharitamanas::3870.translation_literal: जाति (caste) / पाँति (social rank) / कुल (family line) / धर्म (duty) / बड़ाई (greatness) / धन (wealth) / बल (strength) / परिजन (relatives) / गुन (virtues) / चतुराई (cleverness) / भगति हीन (devoid of devotion) / नर (person) / सोहइ (looks beautiful) / कैसा (how) / बिनु (without) / जल (water) / बारिद (cloud) / देखिअ (is seen) / जैसा (like)
ramacharitamanas::3870.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3870.essence: Without devotion, even greatness feels empty.
ramacharitamanas::3870.simple_meaning: Caste, family, wealth, strength, and intelligence cannot make a person truly radiant without devotion. Without it, a person is like a cloud that holds no water.
ramacharitamanas::3870.simple_insight: What you have matters less than what fills your heart. Devotion gives life its real substance.
ramacharitamanas::3870.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the humble woman stands before Ram and asks how to praise him. Ram answers with a teaching that cuts through social pride: rank, wealth, family, and talent mean little if devotion is absent. The next verse unfolds the shape of true bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::3870.modern_relevance: You can have the degree, the salary, the polished resume, and still feel strangely thin inside. Ram's answer says the missing thing is not more achievement — it's devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3870.insight: It shifts attention from outer status to the inner quality that makes a life feel full.

ramacharitamanas::3871.verse_sanskrit: नवधा भगति कहउँ तोहि पाहीं। सावधान सुनु धरु मन माहीं॥ प्रथम भगति संतन्ह कर संगा। दूसरि रति मम कथा प्रसंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3871.verse_hindi: मैं तुझसे अब अपनी नवधा भक्ति कहता हूँ। तू सावधान होकर सुन और मन में धारण कर। पहली भक्ति है संतों का सत्संग। दूसरी भक्ति है मेरे कथा प्रसंग में प्रेम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3871.english_translation: I now tell you the nine forms of devotion. Listen carefully and hold it in your heart. The first devotion is keeping company with saints. The second is loving attention to my stories.
ramacharitamanas::3871.translation_literal: नवधा (ninefold) / भगति (devotion) / कहउँ (I tell) / तोहि (to you) / पाहीं (here, near you) / सावधान (carefully) / सुनु (listen) / धरु (hold) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / प्रथम (first) / भगति (devotion) / संतन्ह (of saints) / कर (of) / संगा (company) / दूसरि (second) / रति (love) / मम (my) / कथा (story) / प्रसंगा (in the context)
ramacharitamanas::3871.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3871.essence: Devotion begins with the company you keep and the stories you love.
ramacharitamanas::3871.simple_meaning: True devotion begins with the company you keep and the stories you love. Listen carefully, because these two shape your heart.
ramacharitamanas::3871.simple_insight: What you repeatedly sit with slowly becomes who you are.
ramacharitamanas::3871.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram begins teaching Sita the nine forms of devotion. He starts with the foundation: keep the company of the holy, and let your heart rest in his stories. The teaching is practical, intimate, and meant to shape daily life.
ramacharitamanas::3871.modern_relevance: You open your phone before bed and fall into voices that leave you restless. Ram points you toward a different feed: the people you keep close and the stories you let settle inside you.
ramacharitamanas::3871.insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony alone to daily proximity, attention, and companionship.

ramacharitamanas::3872.verse_sanskrit: गुर पद पंकज सेवा तीसरि भगति अमान। चौथि भगति मम गुन गन करइ कपट तजि गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3872.verse_hindi: तीसरी भक्ति है अभिमानरहित होकर गुरु के चरण कमलों की सेवा और चौथी भक्ति यह है कि कपट छोड़कर मेरे गुण समूहों का गान करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3872.english_translation: The third devotion is selfless service at the guru's lotus feet. The fourth devotion is singing my qualities, leaving all deceit behind.
ramacharitamanas::3872.translation_literal: गुर (guru) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / सेवा (service) / तीसरि (third) / भगति (devotion) / अमान (without pride) / चौथि (fourth) / भगति (devotion) / मम (my) / गुन (qualities) / गन (group) / करइ (does) / कपट (deceit) / तजि (leaving) / गान (singing)
ramacharitamanas::3872.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3872.essence: Humility and honesty are part of real devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3872.simple_meaning: True devotion includes humble service to the teacher and honest praise of Ram, without pride or pretence.
ramacharitamanas::3872.simple_insight: Devotion becomes real when ego drops and gratitude becomes sincere.
ramacharitamanas::3872.detailed_meaning: In the Aranyakand, Ram begins listing the nine forms of devotion to explain what genuine love looks like. After praising saintly company and listening to his stories, he now adds humble service to the guru and honest singing of his qualities.
ramacharitamanas::3872.modern_relevance: You sit in front of your mentor after making a mistake, tempted to defend yourself. Real growth begins when you drop the performance, serve honestly, and speak with gratitude instead of image-management.
ramacharitamanas::3872.insight: It shifts devotion from display to humility, and from praise as performance to praise as truth.

ramacharitamanas::3873.verse_sanskrit: मंत्र जाप मम दृढ़ बिस्वासा। पंचम भजन सो बेद प्रकासा॥ छठ दम सील बिरति बहु करमा। निरत निरंतर सज्जन धरमा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3873.verse_hindi: मेरे (राम) मंत्र का जाप और मुझमें दृढ़ विश्वास- यह पाँचवीं भक्ति है, जो वेदों में प्रसिद्ध है। छठी भक्ति है इंद्रियों का निग्रह, शील (अच्छा स्वभाव या चरित्र), बहुत कार्यों से वैराग्य और निरंतर संत पुरुषों के धर्म (आचरण) में लगे रहना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3873.english_translation: Chanting my mantra and having firm faith in me is the fifth devotion, known in the Vedas. The sixth devotion is restraint of the senses, good character, detachment from many actions, and constant engagement in the conduct of noble people.
ramacharitamanas::3873.translation_literal: मंत्र (mantra) / जाप (chanting) / मम (my) / दृढ़ (firm) / बिस्वासा (faith) / पंचम (fifth) / भजन (devotion) / सो (that) / बेद (Vedas) / प्रकासा (made known) / छठ (sixth) / दम (restraint) / सील (good character) / बिरति (detachment) / बहु (many) / करमा (actions) / निरत (engaged) / निरंतर (constantly) / सज्जन (noble people) / धरमा (conduct)
ramacharitamanas::3873.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3873.essence: Faith becomes real when your habits begin to match your prayer.
ramacharitamanas::3873.simple_meaning: Chant Ram’s mantra with firm trust. Also practice self-control, good conduct, detachment from busy action, and steady noble behavior.
ramacharitamanas::3873.simple_insight: Devotion is not only feeling; it also trains your habits, your speech, and your restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3873.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram is teaching the full shape of devotion to a listener who wants the path in clear steps. After satsang, service, and praise, he adds mantra, faith, self-control, character, detachment, and steady noble conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3873.modern_relevance: You repeat a prayer before opening your phone, hoping it will steady you. This verse says the chant matters because it is joined to firm trust and a disciplined life.
ramacharitamanas::3873.insight: It links devotion with daily restraint, turning belief into a lived discipline.

ramacharitamanas::3874.verse_sanskrit: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3874.verse_hindi: सातवीं भक्ति है जगत् भर को समभाव से मुझमें ओतप्रोत (राममय) देखना और संतों को मुझसे भी अधिक करके मानना। आठवीं भक्ति है जो कुछ मिल जाए, उसी में संतोष करना और स्वप्न में भी पराए दोषों को न देखना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3874.english_translation: The seventh devotion is to see the whole world as permeated by me, and to regard saints as even greater than me. The eighth devotion is to be content with whatever comes, and not to see others' faults even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::3874.translation_literal: सातवँ (seventh) / सम (equal) / मोहि (me) / मय (filled with) / जग (world) / देखा (seen) / मोतें (than me) / संत (saints) / अधिक (greater) / करि (having made) / लेखा (counted)॥ / आठवँ (eighth) / जथालाभ (whatever is obtained) / संतोषा (contentment) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / नहिं (not) / देखइ (sees) / परदोषा (others' faults)॥
ramacharitamanas::3874.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3874.essence: True devotion sees the divine everywhere and drops the habit of fault-finding.
ramacharitamanas::3874.simple_meaning: See everything as filled with Ram, honour the saint above yourself, stay content with what comes, and do not keep looking for other people's faults.
ramacharitamanas::3874.simple_insight: Devotion becomes easier when comparison, complaint, and fault-finding fall away.
ramacharitamanas::3874.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram is listing the forms of devotion that truly please him. He moves from seeing the world as filled with him to honoring saints, then to contentment and refusing to dwell on others' flaws. This is a practical map of a devoted heart.
