ramacharitamanas::3874.modern_relevance: You open your phone and instantly start comparing your life to everyone else's highlight reel. This verse asks for a cleaner gaze: notice the good, stay content, and stop feeding fault-finding.
ramacharitamanas::3874.insight: It shifts attention from criticism and comparison to reverence, contentment, and a wider way of seeing.

ramacharitamanas::3875.verse_sanskrit: नवम सरल सब सन छलहीना। मम भरोस हियँ हरष न दीना॥ नव महुँ एकउ जिन्ह कें होई। नारि पुरुष सचराचर कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3875.verse_hindi: नवीं भक्ति है सरलता और सबके साथ कपटरहित बर्ताव करना, हृदय में मेरा भरोसा रखना और किसी भी अवस्था में हर्ष और दैन्य (विषाद) का न होना। इन नवों में से जिनके एक भी होती है, वह स्त्री-पुरुष, जड़-चेतन कोई भी हो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3875.english_translation: The ninth is simplicity with everyone, free of deceit, full of trust in me, and untouched by elation or despair. Anyone—woman, man, moving or unmoving—who has even one of these nine qualities...
ramacharitamanas::3875.translation_literal: नवम (ninth) / सरल (simple, straightforward) / सब (all) / सन (with) / छलहीना (free of deceit) / मम (my) / भरोस (trust) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / न (not) / दीना (dejection) / नव (nine) / महुँ (among) / एकउ (even one) / जिन्ह (who) / कें (to) / होई (is) / नारि (woman) / पुरुष (man) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / कोई (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::3875.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3875.essence: Real devotion is simple, honest, and steady in every mood.
ramacharitamanas::3875.simple_meaning: The ninth form of devotion is being straightforward with everyone, free from deceit, trusting Ram in your heart, and staying steady through joy or sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3875.simple_insight: You don’t need perfect spiritual performance—just honesty, trust, and steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3875.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram is listing the nine forms of devotion to Parvati. After trust, equality, and contentment, he adds the quiet heart-qualities that make devotion real: simplicity, no deceit, inner trust, and emotional steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3875.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family group chat, trying to stay polite while hiding your real feelings. This verse asks for something cleaner: no masks, no manipulation, and no collapse when emotions rise.
ramacharitamanas::3875.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual display to character: honesty, trust, and emotional steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::3876.verse_sanskrit: सोइ अतिसय प्रिय भामिनि मोरें। सकल प्रकार भगति दृढ़ तोरें॥ जोगि बृंद दुरलभ गति जोई। तो कहुँ आजु सुलभ भइ सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3876.verse_hindi: हे भामिनि! मुझे वही अत्यंत प्रिय है। फिर तुझ में तो सभी प्रकार की भक्ति दृढ़ है। अतएव जो गति योगियों को भी दुर्लभ है, वही आज तेरे लिए सुलभ हो गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3876.english_translation: O lovely one, you are very dear to me. In you, every kind of devotion is firm. So today, the rare state that even yogis struggle to attain has become easy for you.
ramacharitamanas::3876.translation_literal: सोइ (that same) / अतिसय (very much) / प्रिय (dear) / भामिनि (lovely one) / मोरें (to me) / सकल (all) / प्रकार (kinds) / भगति (devotion) / दृढ़ (firm) / तोरें (in you) / जोगि (yogis) / बृंद (group) / दुरलभ (hard to attain) / गति (state) / जोई (which) / तो कहुँ (for you) / आजु (today) / सुलभ (easy to attain) / भइ (has become) / सोई (that same)
ramacharitamanas::3876.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3876.essence: Complete devotion makes the highest attainment effortless.
ramacharitamanas::3876.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita that her devotion is so complete that the rare state sought by yogis has become easy for her to reach.
ramacharitamanas::3876.simple_insight: Love and trust can open what striving alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3876.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram speaks directly to Sita after her unwavering devotion has already been tested by separation, danger, and longing. He says her devotion is complete, and because of that, the highest state is now within easy reach.
ramacharitamanas::3876.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone with no applause, no certainty, and no guarantee of return. That quiet fidelity can open doors striving never could.
ramacharitamanas::3876.insight: It shifts the mind from spiritual achievement to wholehearted devotion as the real opening.

ramacharitamanas::3877.verse_sanskrit: मम दरसन फल परम अनूपा। जीव पाव निज सहज सरूपा॥ जनकसुता कइ सुधि भामिनी। जानहि कहु करिबरगामिनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3877.verse_hindi: मेरे दर्शन का परम अनुपम फल यह है कि जीव अपने सहज स्वरूप को प्राप्त हो जाता है। हे भामिनि! अब यदि तू गजगामिनी जानकी की कुछ खबर जानती हो तो बता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3877.english_translation: The supreme, incomparable fruit of my sight is that a living being attains its natural form. O lovely one, if you know anything of Janaka's daughter, the graceful one who walks like an elephant, tell me.
ramacharitamanas::3877.translation_literal: मम (my) / दरसन (sight, vision) / फल (fruit, result) / परम (supreme) / अनूपा (incomparable) / जीव (living being) / पाव (attains) / निज (own) / सहज (natural, innate) / सरूपा (form, nature) / जनकसुता (daughter of Janaka) / कइ (of) / सुधि (news, account) / भामिनी (lovely one) / जानहि (do you know) / कहु (tell) / करिबरगामिनी (she who walks like an elephant)
ramacharitamanas::3877.speaker: Shabari
ramacharitamanas::3877.essence: Ram's presence restores you to your original nature.
ramacharitamanas::3877.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram gives the deepest possible fruit: you return to your own true nature. Shabari then asks whether anyone has news of Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3877.simple_insight: Being near the divine is not about escape; it is about remembering who you are.
ramacharitamanas::3877.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shabari speaks to Ram after years of waiting and devotion. She says the highest result of seeing Him is not a reward outside herself, but the recovery of the being's own natural form. Then her heart turns to Sita, and she asks for news of the beloved daughter of Janaka.
ramacharitamanas::3877.modern_relevance: After a long meditation retreat, you realize the real shift was not the scenery or silence. Something in you has settled back into place, and now you want to know how someone you love is doing.
ramacharitamanas::3877.insight: It shifts devotion from getting something to being restored by presence.

ramacharitamanas::3878.verse_sanskrit: पंपा सरहि जाहु रघुराई। तहँ होइहि सुग्रीव मिताई॥ सो सब कहिहि देव रघुबीरा। जानतहूँ पूछहु मतिधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3878.verse_hindi: (शबरी ने कहा-) हे रघुनाथजी! आप पंपा नामक सरोवर को जाइए। वहाँ आपकी सुग्रीव से मित्रता होगी। हे देव! हे रघुवीर! वह सब हाल बतावेगा। हे धीरबुद्धि! आप सब जानते हुए भी मुझसे पूछते हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3878.english_translation: O Lord of Raghu, go to Lake Pampa. There you will meet Sugriva and become friends. O divine Raghubira, he will tell you everything. O wise one, you already know everything, yet you still ask me.
ramacharitamanas::3878.translation_literal: पंपा (Pampa) / सरहि (lake) / जाहु (go) / रघुराई (Lord of Raghu) / तहँ (there) / होइहि (will happen) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / मिताई (friendship) / सो (that) / सब (all) / कहिहि (will tell) / देव (divine one) / रघुबीरा (hero of Raghu) / जानतहूँ (even knowing) / पूछहु (you ask) / मतिधीरा (wise one)
ramacharitamanas::3878.speaker: Shabari
ramacharitamanas::3878.essence: The right friendship appears exactly where your path needs it.
ramacharitamanas::3878.simple_meaning: Shabari tells Ram to go to Pampa Lake, where he will meet Sugriva and form a friendship that will help his path forward.
ramacharitamanas::3878.simple_insight: Help often arrives through the right meeting, not through force.
ramacharitamanas::3878.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shabari speaks to Ram after receiving his grace. She directs him toward Pampa Lake and foretells his meeting with Sugriva, while also marveling that the all-knowing Lord still asks her questions.
ramacharitamanas::3878.modern_relevance: You keep circling the problem alone, then one conversation changes everything. The right person appears at the right time, and the path opens without struggle.
ramacharitamanas::3878.insight: It shifts the mind from solitary effort to trusting the meeting that completes the work.

ramacharitamanas::3879.verse_sanskrit: बार बार प्रभु पद सिरु नाई। प्रेम सहित सब कथा सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3879.verse_hindi: बार-बार प्रभु के चरणों में सिर नवाकर, प्रेम सहित उसने सब कथा सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3879.english_translation: Again and again, bowing his head at the Lord’s feet, he told the whole story with love.
ramacharitamanas::3879.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / प्रेम सहित (with love) / सब कथा (the whole story) / सुनाई (told)
ramacharitamanas::3879.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3879.essence: True devotion bows before it speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3879.simple_meaning: He keeps bowing to Ram and speaks with love, not formality. Reverence and affection shape the telling.
ramacharitamanas::3879.simple_insight: Love changes even a simple retelling into an act of worship.
ramacharitamanas::3879.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shabari stands before Ram after a lifetime of waiting. Overcome by devotion, she repeatedly bows at his feet and shares everything she has seen and lived. The moment is less about information than the heart behind it.
ramacharitamanas::3879.modern_relevance: You finally get to tell someone what happened, but gratitude keeps interrupting your words. You lower your head first, then speak from the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3879.insight: It shifts speech from self-expression to reverent offering.

ramacharitamanas::3880.verse_sanskrit: कहि कथा सकल बिलोकि हरि मुख हृदय पद पंकज धरे। तजि जोग पावक देह परि पद लीन भइ जहँ नहिं फिरे॥ नर बिबिध कर्म अधर्म बहु मत सोकप्रद सब त्यागहू। बिस्वास करि कह दास तुलसी राम पद अनुरागहू॥
ramacharitamanas::3880.verse_hindi: सब कथा कहकर भगवान् के मुख के दर्शन कर, उनके चरणकमलों को धारण कर लिया और योगाग्नि से देह को त्याग कर (जलाकर) वह उस दुर्लभ हरिपद में लीन हो गई, जहाँ से लौटना नहीं होता। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि अनेकों प्रकार के कर्म, अधर्म और बहुत से मत- ये सब शोकप्रद हैं, हे मनुष्यों! इनका त्याग कर दो और विश्वास करके श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रेम करो।
ramacharitamanas::3880.english_translation: After telling her whole story, she looked upon Hari's face and held his lotus feet in her heart. Then, through the fire of yoga, she gave up her body and merged into that rare state from which there is no return. Tulsidas says: abandon the many kinds of action, wrongdoing, and the many doctrines that only bring sorrow; trust and love Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3880.translation_literal: कहि (having spoken) / कथा (story) / सकल (entire) / बिलोकि (seeing) / हरि (Hari) / मुख (face) / हृदय (heart) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / धरे (held) / तजि (having left) / जोग पावक (fire of yoga) / देह (body) / परि (having fallen) / पद (state/feet) / लीन (absorbed) / भइ (became) / जहँ (where) / नहिं (not) / फिरे (returns) / नर (people) / बिबिध (various) / कर्म (actions) / अधर्म (wrongdoing) / बहु (many) / मत (doctrines) / सोकप्रद (sorrow-giving) / सब (all) / त्यागहू (abandon) / बिस्वास (trust) / करि (having made) / कह (says) / दास (servant) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / अनुरागहू (love deeply)
ramacharitamanas::3880.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3880.essence: Many sorrow-making paths fall away when you trust Ram completely.
ramacharitamanas::3880.simple_meaning: The verse urges you to drop confusing and painful paths, and instead place your trust and love in Ram. It also describes a devotee who merges into a state beyond return.
ramacharitamanas::3880.simple_insight: You do not need every doctrine to be at peace; a single devoted trust can simplify everything.
ramacharitamanas::3880.detailed_meaning: After speaking with Sabari, the scene turns to a larger teaching in the forest. She has seen Ram, held his feet in her heart, and reached the state from which there is no return. Tulsidas then broadens that moment into advice for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3880.modern_relevance: You have ten tabs open, three opinions in your head, and one quiet ache underneath it all. The verse says the noise can stop: stop chasing every system, and place your heart where it settles.
ramacharitamanas::3880.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered theories and regretful action toward single-pointed trust and loving surrender.

ramacharitamanas::3881.verse_sanskrit: जाति हीन अघ जन्म महि मुक्त कीन्हि असि नारि। महामंद मन सुख चहसि ऐसे प्रभुहि बिसारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3881.verse_hindi: जो नीच जाति की और पापों की जन्मभूमि थी, ऐसी स्त्री को भी जिन्होंने मुक्त कर दिया, अरे महादुर्बुद्धि मन! तू ऐसे प्रभु को भूलकर सुख चाहता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3881.english_translation: O foolish mind, how can you seek happiness while forgetting the Lord who freed even a woman born in a low and sinful condition?
ramacharitamanas::3881.translation_literal: जाति हीन (low-born) / अघ (sinful) / जन्म महि (in the world) / मुक्त कीन्हि (made free) / असि (such) / नारि (woman) / महामंद (greatly foolish) / मन (mind) / सुख (happiness) / चहसि (you desire) / ऐसे (such) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिसारि (forgetting)
ramacharitamanas::3881.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3881.essence: Forgetting the one who frees you is the real foolishness.
ramacharitamanas::3881.simple_meaning: Ram freed even a woman considered low-born and sinful. The speaker rebukes the mind for chasing peace while forgetting such a compassionate Lord.
ramacharitamanas::3881.simple_insight: Real comfort comes from remembering the one who rescues you, not from chasing comfort while ignoring him.
ramacharitamanas::3881.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the story pauses over a startling mercy: Ram has already freed a woman society would have dismissed. The speaker turns that fact into a rebuke, asking why the mind still runs after happiness while forgetting such a Lord.
ramacharitamanas::3881.modern_relevance: You remember who helped you through your worst night, but later you act as if you did it alone. This verse pulls you back to gratitude before pride hardens.
ramacharitamanas::3881.insight: It shifts the mind from self-sufficient chasing to grateful remembrance of the one who has already helped.

ramacharitamanas::3882.verse_sanskrit: चले राम त्यागा बन सोऊ। अतुलित बल नर केहरि दोऊ॥ बिरही इव प्रभु करत बिषादा। कहत कथा अनेक संबादा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3882.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उस वन को भी छोड़ दिया और वे आगे चले। दोनों भाई अतुलनीय बलवान् और मनुष्यों में सिंह के समान हैं। प्रभु विरही की तरह विषाद करते हुए अनेकों कथाएँ और संवाद कहते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3882.english_translation: Ram left that forest and moved on. Both brothers were unmatched in strength, lions among men. The Lord, like one separated from a beloved, felt sorrow and spoke in many stories and conversations.
ramacharitamanas::3882.translation_literal: चले (moved on) / राम (Ram) / त्यागा (left) / बन (forest) / सोऊ (that) / अतुलित (unmatched) / बल (strength) / नर (men) / केहरि (lions) / दोऊ (both) ॥ / बिरही (one separated from a beloved) / इव (like) / प्रभु (the Lord) / करत (doing) / बिषादा (sorrow) / कहत (speaking) / कथा (stories) / अनेक (many) / संबादा (conversations) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3882.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3882.essence: Strength and sorrow can travel together without canceling each other.
ramacharitamanas::3882.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman move on from the forest, strong and steady, while Ram speaks with the sadness of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3882.simple_insight: Even the strongest can feel grief when love is interrupted.
ramacharitamanas::3882.detailed_meaning: After the earlier scene of release, Ram and Lakshman continue through the forest. Tulsidas lingers on their strength, then turns to Ram's tender sorrow: the Lord walks on like someone separated from what he loves, speaking through stories as if to ease the ache.
ramacharitamanas::3882.modern_relevance: You keep walking after the goodbye, even though your chest still feels tight. Strength does not erase grief; sometimes it simply carries it forward.
ramacharitamanas::3882.insight: It shows that true strength can hold sorrow without collapsing into it.

ramacharitamanas::3883.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन देखु बिपिन कइ सोभा। देखत केहि कर मन नहिं छोभा॥ नारि सहित सब खग मृग बृंदा। मानहुँ मोरि करत हहिं निंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3883.verse_hindi: हे लक्ष्मण! जरा वन की शोभा तो देखो। इसे देखकर किसका मन क्षुब्ध नहीं होगा? पक्षी और पशुओं के समूह सभी स्त्री सहित हैं। मानो वे मेरी निंदा कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3883.english_translation: “Look, Lakshman, at the beauty of the forest. Whose mind would not be stirred by seeing it? Every bird and beast is there with its mate, as if they are all reproaching me.”
ramacharitamanas::3883.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / देखु (look) / बिपिन (forest) / कइ (of) / सोभा (beauty) / देखत (seeing) / केहि (whose) / कर (of) / मन (mind) / नहिं (not) / छोभा (stirred) / नारि (female companion/wife) / सहित (together with) / सब (all) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer/beasts) / बृंदा (groups) / मानहुँ (as if) / मोरि (my) / करत (doing) / हहिं (are) / निंदा (reproach)
ramacharitamanas::3883.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3883.essence: Even the forest feels like a reproach when love is absent.
ramacharitamanas::3883.simple_meaning: Ram points out the forest's beauty to Lakshman and says even the animals have mates, which makes him feel the ache of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3883.simple_insight: Longing can make even beauty feel like a wound.
ramacharitamanas::3883.detailed_meaning: In the forest after leaving Ayodhya, Ram walks with Lakshman through a scene of abundant life. Couples of birds and animals surround them, and Ram feels the absence of Sita more sharply. This verse is part of that flowing grief, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3883.modern_relevance: You scroll past a photo of a family picnic, and the ache lands hard because you are the only one eating alone. Beauty can sharpen absence.
ramacharitamanas::3883.insight: It shows how grief changes perception: the same world that looks lovely to others can feel like a reminder of loss.

ramacharitamanas::3884.verse_sanskrit: हमहि देखि मृग निकर पराहीं। मृगीं कहहिं तुम्ह कहँ भय नाहीं॥ तुम्ह आनंद करहु मृग जाए। कंचन मृग खोजन ए आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3884.verse_hindi: हमें देखकर (जब डर के मारे) हिरनों के झुंड भागने लगते हैं, तब हिरनियाँ उनसे कहती हैं- तुमको भय नहीं है। तुम तो साधारण हिरनों से पैदा हुए हो, अतः तुम आनंद करो। ये तो सोने का हिरन खोजने आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3884.english_translation: Seeing us, herds of deer flee in fear. The does say, 'Why should you be afraid? Be happy and go on. These have come searching for a golden deer.'
ramacharitamanas::3884.translation_literal: हमहि (us) / देखि (seeing) / मृग-निकर (herds of deer) / पराहीं (flee) / मृगीं (does) / कहहिं (say) / तुम्ह (you) / कहँ (toward) / भय (fear) / नाहीं (is not)॥ / तुम्ह (you) / आनंद (joy) / करहु (do) / मृग (deer) / जाए (go) / कंचन (golden) / मृग (deer) / खोजन (searching) / ए (these) / आए (have come) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3884.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3884.essence: Even the forest senses that desire is about to disturb it.
ramacharitamanas::3884.simple_meaning: Deer run away in fear, while the does reassure them. The scene points to the strange hunt for the golden deer.
ramacharitamanas::3884.simple_insight: Fear makes even a harmless scene feel charged and unstable.
ramacharitamanas::3884.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram and Lakshman move through a world already alive with tension. The deer flee at their sight, and the does speak as if the forest itself understands the danger of the golden deer. This is part of the lead-up to Sita's abduction.
ramacharitamanas::3884.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone suddenly goes quiet. Even before anything is said, the mood tells you something is wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3884.insight: It sets up the emotional contrast between innocent forest life and the deceptive lure that will soon disrupt it.

ramacharitamanas::3885.verse_sanskrit: संग लाइ करिनीं करि लेहीं। मानहुँ मोहि सिखावनु देहीं॥ सास्त्र सुचिंतित पुनि पुनि देखिअ। भूप सुसेवित बस नहिं लेखिअ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3885.verse_hindi: हाथी हथिनियों को साथ लगा लेते हैं। वे मानो मुझे शिक्षा देते हैं (कि स्त्री को कभी अकेली नहीं छोड़ना चाहिए)। भलीभाँति चिंतन किए हुए शास्त्र को भी बार-बार देखते रहना चाहिए। अच्छी तरह सेवा किए हुए भी राजा को वश में नहीं समझना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3885.english_translation: Elephants keep their cows close, as if teaching me: never leave a woman alone. A well-considered scripture should be examined again and again, and a king, even when well served, should never be assumed to be under control.
ramacharitamanas::3885.translation_literal: संग (together) / लाइ (having brought) / करिनीं (female elephants) / करि (having) / लेहीं (take) / मानहुँ (as if) / मोहि (me) / सिखावनु (instruction) / देहीं (give) / सास्त्र (scripture) / सुचिंतित (well-considered) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / देखिअ (should be seen) / भूप (king) / सुसेवित (well served) / बस (under control) / नहिं (not) / लेखिअ (should be counted)
ramacharitamanas::3885.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3885.essence: What seems settled still needs careful checking.
ramacharitamanas::3885.simple_meaning: The verse warns against careless trust. It says a woman should not be left alone, careful study should be revisited often, and even a well-served king should not be assumed controllable.
ramacharitamanas::3885.simple_insight: It leaves you more alert, less naive, and less willing to mistake familiarity for safety.
ramacharitamanas::3885.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is speaking to Lakshman through everyday examples from nature and court life. He draws a lesson from elephants, then widens it to scripture and kingship: some things need repeated care, and some powers should never be taken lightly.
ramacharitamanas::3885.modern_relevance: You skim a contract once, assume the clause is harmless, and sign. Later, the detail you missed costs you time and money. This verse trains you to look again before trusting what seems settled.
ramacharitamanas::3885.insight: It teaches you to verify before you rely, especially where carelessness can become damage.

ramacharitamanas::3886.verse_sanskrit: राखिअ नारि जदपि उर माहीं। जुबती सास्त्र नृपति बस नाहीं॥ देखहु तात बसंत सुहावा। प्रिया हीन मोहि भय उपजावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3886.verse_hindi: और स्त्री को चाहे हृदय में ही क्यों न रखा जाए, परन्तु युवती स्त्री, शास्त्र और राजा किसी के वश में नहीं रहते। हे तात! इस सुंदर वसंत को तो देखो। प्रिया के बिना मुझको यह भय उत्पन्न कर रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3886.english_translation: Even if you keep a woman in your heart, a young woman, scripture, and a king are not under anyone's control. O father, look at this lovely spring. Without my beloved, it awakens fear in me.
ramacharitamanas::3886.translation_literal: राखिअ (may be kept) / नारि (woman) / जदपि (even if) / उर माहीं (in the heart) / जुबती (young woman) / सास्त्र (scripture) / नृपति (king) / बस (under control) / नाहीं (not) / देखहु (look) / तात (father) / बसंत (spring) / सुहावा (beautiful) / प्रिया (beloved) / हीन (without) / मोहि (to me) / भय (fear) / उपजावा (has arisen)
ramacharitamanas::3886.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3886.essence: Desire makes even beauty feel like danger when you cannot possess it.
ramacharitamanas::3886.simple_meaning: Ravana says that women, scripture, and kings cannot be controlled by force, and that spring makes him afraid because Sita is absent.
ramacharitamanas::3886.simple_insight: What you cannot hold with control often becomes the very thing that unsettles you.
ramacharitamanas::3886.detailed_meaning: In the Ashoka grove, Ravana tries to justify himself while speaking to his companion. He admits that beauty, authority, and desire do not truly submit to control, then reveals his own unease: spring feels dangerous because Sita is not with him.
ramacharitamanas::3886.modern_relevance: You scroll past a perfect couple on your feed and suddenly your own room feels empty. The season, the music, even the weather start to hurt because longing has taken the whole scene hostage.
ramacharitamanas::3886.insight: It exposes how craving turns the world into a mirror of lack, making even beauty feel like threat.

ramacharitamanas::3887.verse_sanskrit: बिरह बिकल बलहीन मोहि जानेसि निपट अकेल। सहित बिपिन मधुकर खग मदन कीन्ह बगमेल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3887.verse_hindi: मुझे विरह से व्याकुल, बलहीन और बिलकुल अकेला जानकर कामदेव ने वन, भौंरों और पक्षियों को साथ लेकर मुझ पर धावा बोल दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3887.english_translation: Seeing me grief-stricken, weak, and utterly alone, desire attacked me with the forest, bees, and birds as its army.
ramacharitamanas::3887.translation_literal: बिरह (separation) / बिकल (distressed) / बलहीन (powerless) / मोहि (me) / जानेसि (you knew) / निपट (utterly) / अकेल (alone) / सहित (together with) / बिपिन (forest) / मधुकर (bees) / खग (birds) / मदन (desire) / कीन्ह (made) / बगमेल (attack)
ramacharitamanas::3887.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::3887.essence: Separation turns the whole world into an enemy.
ramacharitamanas::3887.simple_meaning: Sita says that being separated from Ram has left her weak and alone, and that desire seems to have attacked her through the forest, bees, and birds around her.
ramacharitamanas::3887.simple_insight: Separation makes every small thing feel like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::3887.detailed_meaning: In the Ashoka grove, Sita speaks from the ache of separation. She feels weak, alone, and surrounded by reminders of what she has lost. The forest itself seems to join desire in tormenting her, which is why this line lands as part of a larger cry of loneliness.
ramacharitamanas::3887.modern_relevance: You’re already raw after a breakup, and then every song, street corner, and passing couple feels like it’s aimed at you. Grief can make the whole world seem complicit.
ramacharitamanas::3887.insight: It shows how suffering can magnify the mind’s sense of attack and isolation.

ramacharitamanas::3888.verse_sanskrit: देखि गयउ भ्राता सहित तासु दूत सुनि बात। डेरा कीन्हेउ मनहुँ तब कटकु हटकि मनजात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3888.verse_hindi: परन्तु जब उसका दूत यह देख गया कि मैं भाई के साथ हूँ (अकेला नहीं हूँ), तब उसकी बात सुनकर कामदेव ने मानो सेना को रोककर डेरा डाल दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3888.english_translation: But when his messenger saw that I was with my brother, hearing that news, he seemed to halt his army and pitch camp.
ramacharitamanas::3888.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / गयउ (went) / भ्राता (brother) / सहित (together with) / तासु (his) / दूत (messenger) / सुनि (hearing) / बात (news) / डेरा (camp) / कीन्हेउ (made) / मनहुँ (as if) / तब (then) / कटकु (army) / हटकि (having withdrawn) / मनजात (born of the mind; desire)
ramacharitamanas::3888.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3888.essence: Companionship can stop what loneliness would unleash.
ramacharitamanas::3888.simple_meaning: Desire lost its force when it saw he was not alone. The presence of his brother made the attack pause.
ramacharitamanas::3888.simple_insight: Support makes fear smaller. Even inner pressure weakens when you are not facing it alone.
ramacharitamanas::3888.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is explaining how longing and fear rose against him when Sita was absent. He says that once the messenger saw him with his brother Lakshman, the force of desire seemed to stop and camp outside, unable to overrun him.
ramacharitamanas::3888.modern_relevance: You were about to spiral alone in your room, but then your sibling called. The panic did not vanish, but it lost its grip the moment you felt accompanied.
ramacharitamanas::3888.insight: It shows how companionship can interrupt craving, fear, or emotional overwhelm before they take over.

ramacharitamanas::3889.verse_sanskrit: बिटप बिसाल लता अरुझानी। बिबिध बितान दिए जनु तानी॥ कदलि ताल बर धुजा पताका। देखि न मोह धीर मन जाका ॥
ramacharitamanas::3889.verse_hindi: विशाल वृक्षों में लताएँ उलझी हुई ऐसी मालूम होती हैं मानो नाना प्रकार के तंबू तान दिए गए हैं। केला और ताड़ सुंदर ध्वजा पताका के समान हैं। इन्हें देखकर वही नहीं मोहित होता, जिसका मन धीर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3889.english_translation: Tall trees are tangled with vines, as if many kinds of canopies have been stretched overhead. Banana and palm trees stand like beautiful banners and flags. Only a steady mind is not captivated by this sight.
ramacharitamanas::3889.translation_literal: बिटप (trees) / बिसाल (tall, विशाल) / लता (vines) / अरुझानी (entangled) / बिबिध (various) / बितान (canopies) / दिए (given, placed) / जनु (as if) / तानी (stretched) ॥ कदलि (banana tree) / ताल (palm tree) / बर (excellent, beautiful) / धुजा (banners) / पताका (flags) / देखि (seeing) / न (not) / मोह (deluded, captivated) / धीर (steady) / मन (mind) / जाका (whose)
ramacharitamanas::3889.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3889.essence: Steadiness lets you see beauty without becoming its captive.
ramacharitamanas::3889.simple_meaning: The forest is so beautiful it can enchant the mind, but a steady person is not carried away by appearances.
ramacharitamanas::3889.simple_insight: You can appreciate beauty without losing yourself in it.
ramacharitamanas::3889.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the trees and vines look like hanging canopies, banners, and flags. The scene is so lush that it can stir desire and distraction. Tulsidas points out that only a calm, disciplined mind can look at such beauty without being pulled off balance.
ramacharitamanas::3889.modern_relevance: You scroll through a perfectly lit vacation reel, then another, then another. The pull is real. This verse reminds you that not every beautiful thing deserves your attention or your longing.
ramacharitamanas::3889.insight: It trains the mind to notice attraction without surrendering to it.

ramacharitamanas::3890.verse_sanskrit: बिबिध भाँति फूले तरु नाना। जनु बानैत बने बहु बाना॥ कहुँ कहुँ सुंदर बिटप सुहाए। जनु भट बिलग बिलग होइ छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3890.verse_hindi: अनेकों वृक्ष नाना प्रकार से फूले हुए हैं। मानो अलग-अलग बाना (वर्दी) धारण किए हुए बहुत से तीरंदाज हों। कहीं-कहीं सुंदर वृक्ष शोभा दे रहे हैं। मानो योद्धा लोग अलग-अलग होकर छावनी डाले हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3890.english_translation: The trees bloom in many different ways, as if many archers in different uniforms are standing there. Here and there beautiful trees shine, as if warriors have spread out and set up camp.
ramacharitamanas::3890.translation_literal: बिबिध भाँति (in various ways) / फूले (bloomed) / तरु (trees) / नाना (many, different) / जनु (as if) / बानैत (archers) / बने (in uniforms) / बहु (many) / बाना (uniforms, garb) / कहुँ कहुँ (here and there) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बिटप (trees) / सुहाए (look lovely) / जनु (as if) / भट (warriors) / बिलग बिलग (separately, apart) / होइ (being) / छाए (spread out, encamped)
ramacharitamanas::3890.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3890.essence: Nature is so alive it looks like an army at rest.
ramacharitamanas::3890.simple_meaning: The forest is described as full of blooming trees, each looking like archers and warriors standing in different places.
ramacharitamanas::3890.simple_insight: The scene feels alive and ordered, as if nature itself has gathered into ranks.
ramacharitamanas::3890.detailed_meaning: In the forest where Rama and Lakshmana move through wild beauty, Tulsidas pauses on the trees themselves. Their blossoms and shapes are compared to archers and warriors spread across the landscape, turning the forest into a living battlefield of color.
ramacharitamanas::3890.modern_relevance: You walk into a park after rain and notice every tree standing like it has its own posture. The mind starts seeing pattern, rhythm, and presence instead of random scenery.
ramacharitamanas::3890.insight: It trains attention to see vivid order in the natural world.

ramacharitamanas::3891.verse_sanskrit: कूजत पिक मानहुँ गज माते। ढेक महोख ऊँट बिसराते॥ मोर चकोर कीर बर बाजी। पारावत मराल सब ताजी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3891.verse_hindi: कोयलें कूज रही हैं, वही मानो मतवाले हाथी (चिग्घाड़ रहे) हैं। ढेक और महोख पक्षी मानो ऊँट और खच्चर हैं। मोर, चकोर, तोते, कबूतर और हंस मानो सब सुंदर ताजी (अरबी) घोड़े हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3891.english_translation: Cuckoos call like maddened elephants. The dhenk and mohok birds seem like camels and mules. Peacocks, chakors, parrots, pigeons, and swans appear like fine Arabian horses.
ramacharitamanas::3891.translation_literal: कूजत (calling) / पिक (cuckoos) / मानहुँ (as if) / गज (elephants) / माते (maddened) / ढेक (dhenk birds) / महोख (mohok birds) / ऊँट (camels) / बिसराते (mules) / मोर (peacocks) / चकोर (chakors) / कीर (parrots) / बर (fine) / बाजी (horses) / पारावत (pigeons) / मराल (swans) / सब (all) / ताजी (Arabian horses)
ramacharitamanas::3891.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3891.essence: The forest becomes a living parade of forms and sounds.
ramacharitamanas::3891.simple_meaning: The forest is so alive with birds that Tulsidas compares their calls and forms to elephants, camels, mules, and horses.
ramacharitamanas::3891.simple_insight: Nature can feel like a whole kingdom in motion.
ramacharitamanas::3891.detailed_meaning: The scene is still deep in the forest, and Tulsidas is painting its beauty through playful comparison. Birds are not just birds here; their sounds and shapes become an imagined royal procession, part of the rich landscape before Sita's abduction.
ramacharitamanas::3891.modern_relevance: You walk through a park at dawn and every birdcall feels amplified, almost theatrical. The mind starts turning ordinary sounds into a living parade.
ramacharitamanas::3891.insight: It turns attention from literal description to vivid seeing, letting the reader experience the forest as a moving spectacle.

ramacharitamanas::3892.verse_sanskrit: तीतिर लावक पदचर जूथा। बरनि न जाइ मनोज बरूथा॥ रथ गिरि सिला दुंदुभीं झरना। चातक बंदी गुन गन बरना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3892.verse_hindi: तीतर और बटेर पैदल सिपाहियों के झुंड हैं। कामदेव की सेना का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। पर्वतों की शिलाएँ रथ और जल के झरने नगाड़े हैं। पपीहे भाट हैं, जो गुणसमूह (विरुदावली) का वर्णन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3892.english_translation: The partridges and quails are legions of foot soldiers. The army of Cupid cannot be described. The rocks of the mountains are chariots, and the waterfalls are drums. The chatak birds are bards who sing the praise of countless virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3892.translation_literal: तीतिर (partridges) / लावक (quails) / पदचर (foot soldiers) / जूथा (crowds) / बरनि (described) / न जाइ (cannot be) / मनोज (Cupid) / बरूथा (army) / रथ (chariots) / गिरि (mountains) / सिला (rocks) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / झरना (waterfalls) / चातक (chatak birds) / बंदी (bards) / गुन गन (groups of virtues) / बरना (to praise)
ramacharitamanas::3892.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3892.essence: The forest itself becomes a royal celebration.
ramacharitamanas::3892.simple_meaning: The forest is being described like a grand army and royal procession, with birds, rocks, and waterfalls all imagined as parts of it. It is poetic scene-setting, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3892.simple_insight: Beauty can feel so alive that the mind turns it into music, movement, and celebration.
ramacharitamanas::3892.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the forest is being painted in lavish imagery as the scene opens around Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Birds, rocks, and waterfalls are all compared to soldiers, chariots, drums, and singers. The verse deepens the atmosphere rather than delivering a separate lesson.
ramacharitamanas::3892.modern_relevance: You walk into a hillside at dusk and every sound feels charged — birds, water, wind, stone. The mind starts turning the whole place into a living procession.
ramacharitamanas::3892.insight: It trains attention to see the world as vivid, ordered, and full of motion.

ramacharitamanas::3893.verse_sanskrit: मधुकर मुखर भेरि सहनाई। त्रिबिध बयारि बसीठीं आई॥ चतुरंगिनी सेन सँग लीन्हें। बिचरत सबहि चुनौती दीन्हें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3893.verse_hindi: भौंरों की गुंजार भेरी और शहनाई है। शीतल, मंद और सुगंधित हवा मानो दूत का काम लेकर आई है। इस प्रकार चतुरंगिणी सेना साथ लिए कामदेव मानो सबको चुनौती देता हुआ विचर रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3893.english_translation: Bees hum like drums and shawms. The cool, gentle, fragrant breeze comes like a messenger. With his fourfold army, Kama roams about challenging everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3893.translation_literal: मधुकर (bees) / मुखर (loud) / भेरि (drum) / सहनाई (shawm) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / बयारि (breeze) / बसीठीं (as a messenger) / आई (came) / चतुरंगिनी (fourfold) / सेना (army) / सँग (with) / लीन्हें (taken) / बिचरत (roaming) / सबहि (everyone) / चुनौती (challenge) / दीन्हें (gave)
ramacharitamanas::3893.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3893.essence: Desire advances like an army, disguised as beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3893.simple_meaning: Spring’s sounds and breeze are described like an army advancing under Kama, the force of desire, as he challenges everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3893.simple_insight: Desire can feel beautiful and harmless while still gathering force around you.
ramacharitamanas::3893.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the season itself seems to have changed sides. Bees, breezes, and blossoms become Kama's marching army, and the next verse will spell out the danger this creates for even the steady mind.
ramacharitamanas::3893.modern_relevance: A song starts playing in a quiet room, a message lights up your phone, and suddenly the mood shifts. Desire often arrives dressed as beauty before it starts pulling you.
ramacharitamanas::3893.insight: It turns a pleasant atmosphere into a warning: attraction can organize the mind before you notice it.

ramacharitamanas::3894.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन देखत काम अनीका। रहहिं धीर तिन्ह कै जग लीका॥ ऐहि कें एक परम बल नारी। तेहि तें उबर सुभट सोइ भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3894.verse_hindi: हे लक्ष्मण! कामदेव की इस सेना को देखकर जो धीर बने रहते हैं, जगत् में उन्हीं की (वीरों में) प्रतिष्ठा होती है। इस कामदेव के एक स्त्री का बड़ा भारी बल है। उससे जो बच जाए, वही श्रेष्ठ योद्धा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3894.english_translation: Lakshman, seeing Kama's army, only the steady remain famous in this world. Even one woman is a great power for Kama. The warrior who escapes that is truly the greatest.
ramacharitamanas::3894.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / देखत (seeing) / काम अनीका (Kama's army) / रहहिं (remain) / धीर (steady) / तिन्ह (those) / कै (of) / जग लीका (world's fame) ॥ ऐहि (this) / कें (of) / एक (one) / परम (supreme) / बल (power) / नारी (woman) / तेहि (that) / तें (from) / उबर (escapes) / सुभट (warrior) / सोइ (that very) / भारी (greatest) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3894.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3894.essence: Real strength is staying steady when desire tries to pull you.
ramacharitamanas::3894.simple_meaning: Desire can overwhelm even strong people. The truly great person is the one who stays calm and does not get swept away.
ramacharitamanas::3894.simple_insight: You do not have to be ruled by craving; steadiness itself is a kind of victory.
ramacharitamanas::3894.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman watches a vivid description of Kama's forces. The scene turns from beauty to warning: desire is powerful, and even one alluring form can unsettle the mind. The verse praises the person who stays composed anyway.
ramacharitamanas::3894.modern_relevance: You open your phone “just for a minute,” and one image, one message, one memory starts pulling you off center. The verse points to the quiet strength of not being dragged by that pull.
ramacharitamanas::3894.insight: It shifts you from admiring impulse to watching it without being captured by it.

ramacharitamanas::3895.verse_sanskrit: तात तीनि अति प्रबल खल काम क्रोध अरु लोभ। मुनि बिग्यान धाम मन करहिं निमिष महुँ छोभ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3895.verse_hindi: हे तात! काम, क्रोध और लोभ- ये तीन अत्यंत दुष्ट हैं। ये विज्ञान के धाम मुनियों के भी मनों को पलभर में क्षुब्ध कर देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3895.english_translation: O dear one, desire, anger, and greed are three terrible evils. They can shake even sages, whose minds are homes of discernment, in a moment.
ramacharitamanas::3895.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / तीनि (three) / अति (very) / प्रबल (powerful) / खल (wicked) / काम (desire) / क्रोध (anger) / अरु (and) / लोभ (greed) / मुनि (sage) / बिग्यान (knowledge) / धाम (abode) / मन (mind) / करहिं (make) / निमिष (moment) / महुँ (in) / छोभ (disturbance)
ramacharitamanas::3895.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3895.essence: Even the wisest mind can be overturned by three inner enemies.
ramacharitamanas::3895.simple_meaning: Desire, anger, and greed are three powerful inner enemies. They can disturb even very wise people in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::3895.simple_insight: Knowing the danger is the first protection. Clear seeing begins with humility about how easily the mind can slip.
ramacharitamanas::3895.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman is being taught how dangerous inner weakness can be. After the sight of Kama's army, Tulsidas warns that desire, anger, and greed can disturb even sages who live in wisdom. This verse names the real enemy.
ramacharitamanas::3895.modern_relevance: You open one message, feel insulted, and fire back before thinking. That flash of irritation is exactly what this verse warns about.
ramacharitamanas::3895.insight: It shifts attention from outer threats to the inner forces that hijack judgment: craving, rage, and greed.

ramacharitamanas::3896.verse_sanskrit: लोभ कें इच्छा दंभ बल काम कें केवल नारि। क्रोध कें परुष बचन बल मुनिबर कहहिं बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3896.verse_hindi: लोभ को इच्छा और दम्भ का बल है, काम को केवल स्त्री का बल है और क्रोध को कठोर वचनों का बल है, श्रेष्ठ मुनि विचार कर ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3896.english_translation: Greed is powered by desire and deceit, lust by women, and anger by harsh words, as the wise sages observe.
ramacharitamanas::3896.translation_literal: लोभ (greed) / कें (for) / इच्छा (desire) / दंभ (deceit-pride) / बल (strength) / काम (lust) / कें (for) / केवल (only) / नारि (woman) / क्रोध (anger) / कें (for) / परुष (harsh) / बचन (words) / बल (strength) / मुनिबर (great sages) / कहहिं (say) / बिचारि (having reflected)
ramacharitamanas::3896.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3896.essence: See the fuel, and the fire loses power.
ramacharitamanas::3896.simple_meaning: Greed, lust, and anger each grow from specific triggers: wanting and deceit, attraction, and harsh speech. Wise people notice these causes clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3896.simple_insight: You can weaken a disturbing impulse by seeing what feeds it.
ramacharitamanas::3896.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman is being taught how inner enemies work. After naming desire, anger, and greed as powerful forces, the teaching now breaks them down further: each one has its own fuel. That clarity prepares him for restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3896.modern_relevance: You send a sharp reply in a group chat, and the argument instantly grows teeth. The verse helps you notice that anger often survives on the harshness you add to it.
ramacharitamanas::3896.insight: It shifts attention from fighting the emotion to removing the conditions that strengthen it.

ramacharitamanas::3897.verse_sanskrit: गुनातीत सचराचर स्वामी। राम उमा सब अंतरजामी॥ कामिन्ह कै दीनता देखाई। धीरन्ह कें मन बिरति दृढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3897.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! श्री रामचंद्रजी गुणातीत (तीनों गुणों से परे), चराचर जगत् के स्वामी और सबके अंतर की जानने वाले हैं। (उपर्युक्त बातें कहकर) उन्होंने कामी लोगों की दीनता (बेबसी) दिखलाई है और धीर (विवेकी) पुरुषों के मन में वैराग्य को दृढ़ किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3897.english_translation: Ram is beyond the three qualities, the lord of all moving and unmoving beings, and the knower of every heart. In saying this, Shiva shows the helplessness of desire-driven people and strengthens detachment in the minds of the steady.
ramacharitamanas::3897.translation_literal: गुनातीत (beyond the three qualities) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / स्वामी (lord) / राम (Ram) / उमा (O Uma) / सब (all) / अंतरजामी (inner-knower) ॥ / कामिन्ह (of desire-driven people) / कै (their) / दीनता (helplessness) / देखाई (showed) / धीरन्ह (of the steady ones) / कें (of) / मन (mind) / बिरति (detachment) / दृढ़ाई (made firm) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3897.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3897.essence: Seeing Ram clearly makes desire feel small and detachment feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::3897.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond all qualities, rules over all creation, and knows every heart. This truth exposes how helpless desire makes a person and strengthens detachment in the wise.
ramacharitamanas::3897.simple_insight: You feel desire lose its glamour when you see how small it makes you.
ramacharitamanas::3897.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the forest dialogue. After describing desire, anger, and greed as powerful forces, he turns to Ram himself: the one who stands beyond all qualities and sees every heart. That vision weakens craving and steadies detachment.
ramacharitamanas::3897.modern_relevance: You catch yourself chasing approval in a message thread, refreshing the screen again and again. Then something steadier appears: the need itself is shrinking, and you can see it instead of obeying it.
ramacharitamanas::3897.insight: It shifts attention from craving to clear seeing, so detachment becomes a strength rather than a loss.

ramacharitamanas::3898.verse_sanskrit: क्रोध मनोज लोभ मद माया। छूटहिं सकल राम कीं दाया॥ सो नर इंद्रजाल नहिं भूला। जा पर होइ सो नट अनुकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3898.verse_hindi: क्रोध, काम, लोभ, मद और माया- ये सभी श्री रामजी की दया से छूट जाते हैं। वह नट (नटराज भगवान् ) जिस पर प्रसन्न होता है, वह मनुष्य इंद्रजाल (माया) में नहीं भूलता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3898.english_translation: Anger, desire, greed, pride, and illusion all fall away by Ram's grace. The person whom the divine actor favors is never deceived by illusion.
ramacharitamanas::3898.translation_literal: क्रोध (anger) / मनोज (desire-born) / लोभ (greed) / मद (pride) / माया (illusion) / छूटहिं (are released) / सकल (all) / राम कीं दाया (by Ram's grace)॥ / सो नर (that person) / इंद्रजाल (illusion's net) / नहिं भूला (is not deceived) / जा पर (on whom) / होइ (happens) / सो नट (that divine actor) / अनुकूला (favorable)
ramacharitamanas::3898.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3898.essence: Ram's grace clears the mind where effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3898.simple_meaning: Ram's grace can free you from anger, desire, greed, pride, and confusion. When that grace is present, illusion no longer fools you.
ramacharitamanas::3898.simple_insight: You are not doomed to stay trapped in your worst patterns.
ramacharitamanas::3898.detailed_meaning: Shiva is still teaching Parvati in the forest narrative. He explains that the hardest inner enemies—anger, desire, greed, pride, and illusion—do not disappear by force alone. Ram's grace is what finally loosens their grip.
ramacharitamanas::3898.modern_relevance: You catch yourself rereading the same angry message for the tenth time, or spiraling after a small insult. This verse says the mind's knots do not untie by willpower alone; grace can change what effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3898.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame and struggle to receptive openness to grace.

ramacharitamanas::3899.verse_sanskrit: उमा कहउँ मैं अनुभव अपना। सत हरि भजनु जगत सब सपना॥ पुनि प्रभु गए सरोबर तीरा। पंपा नाम सुभग गंभीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3899.verse_hindi: हे उमा! मैं तुम्हें अपना अनुभव कहता हूँ- हरि का भजन ही सत्य है, यह सारा जगत् तो स्वप्न (की भाँति झूठा) है। फिर प्रभु श्री रामजी पंपा नामक सुंदर और गहरे सरोवर के तीर पर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3899.english_translation: Uma, I tell you my own experience: devotion to Hari alone is real; the whole world is like a dream. Then the Lord went to the bank of a lake named Pampa, beautiful and deep.
ramacharitamanas::3899.translation_literal: उमा (Uma) / कहउँ (I tell) / मैं (I) / अनुभव (experience) / अपना (my own) / सत (real) / हरि (Hari) / भजनु (devotion) / जगत (world) / सब (all) / सपना (dream) / पुनि (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / गए (went) / सरोबर (lake) / तीरा (bank) / पंपा (Pampa) / नाम (named) / सुभग (beautiful) / गंभीरा (deep)
ramacharitamanas::3899.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3899.essence: Devotion is real; the world is only a passing dream.
ramacharitamanas::3899.simple_meaning: Devotion to Ram is the only lasting reality; the rest of the world is fleeting like a dream. After saying this, Ram goes to the beautiful, deep Pampa lake.
ramacharitamanas::3899.simple_insight: You can stop treating appearances as ultimate and rest in what truly lasts.
ramacharitamanas::3899.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the forest journey of Aranyakand. He shares his direct experience that loving Hari is real while worldly appearance is like a dream, then the story moves with Ram toward the serene Pampa lake, deepening the mood of devotion and detachment.
ramacharitamanas::3899.modern_relevance: You scroll through ten opinions, three anxieties, and one message that ruins your mood. Then you remember what actually stays with you after the screen goes dark: the quality of your devotion, not the noise.
ramacharitamanas::3899.insight: It shifts attention away from appearances and toward what is truly worth trusting.

ramacharitamanas::3900.verse_sanskrit: संत हृदय जस निर्मल बारी। बाँधे घाट मनोहर चारी॥ जहँ तहँ पिअहिं बिबिध मृग नीरा। जनु उदार गृह जाचक भीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3900.verse_hindi: उसका जल संतों के हृदय जैसा निर्मल है। मन को हरने वाले सुंदर चार घाट बँधे हुए हैं। भाँति-भाँति के पशु जहाँ-तहाँ जल पी रहे हैं। मानो उदार दानी पुरुषों के घर याचकों की भीड़ लगी हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3900.english_translation: Its water is as pure as a saint’s heart. Four beautiful ghats are built there, pleasing to the mind. Different kinds of animals drink there from all around, like a generous house crowded with beggars.
ramacharitamanas::3900.translation_literal: संत हृदय (saints' hearts) / जस (like) / निर्मल (pure) / बारी (water) / बाँधे (built) / घाट (ghats) / मनोहर (beautiful) / चारी (four) ॥ / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / पिअहिं (drink) / बिबिध (various) / मृग (animals) / नीरा (water) / जनु (as if) / उदार (generous) / गृह (house) / जाचक (beggars) / भीरा (crowd) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3900.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3900.essence: A pure place naturally becomes a place of welcome.
ramacharitamanas::3900.simple_meaning: The lake is described as clear, beautiful, and full of life, with animals drinking from it like visitors at a generous home.
ramacharitamanas::3900.simple_insight: Beauty feels complete when it welcomes everyone without fear or shortage.
ramacharitamanas::3900.detailed_meaning: After leaving the earlier reflections on Ram and the world, the story reaches the peaceful lake at Pampa. Tulsidas paints its water, ghats, and wildlife as a living image of harmony, preparing the scene for what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::3900.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet park lake at dawn and see birds, dogs, and people all sharing the same water. Some places feel generous before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3900.insight: It turns a landscape into a lesson in openness, abundance, and graceful sharing.

ramacharitamanas::3901.verse_sanskrit: पुरइनि सघन ओट जल बेगि न पाइअ मर्म। मायाछन्न न देखिऐ जैसें निर्गुन ब्रह्म ॥
ramacharitamanas::3901.verse_hindi: घनी पुरइनों (कमल के पत्तों) की आड़ में जल का जल्दी पता नहीं मिलता। जैसे माया से ढँके रहने के कारण निर्गुण ब्रह्म नहीं दिखता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3901.english_translation: Just as water is hard to find quickly beneath thick lotus leaves, the formless supreme reality is not seen when covered by the veil of appearance.
ramacharitamanas::3901.translation_literal: पुरइनि (lotus leaves) / सघन (dense, thick) / ओट (covering, screen) / जल (water) / बेगि (quickly) / न पाइअ (is not found) / मर्म (essence, hidden core) / माया-छन्न (covered by appearance) / न देखिऐ (is not seen) / जैसें (just as) / निर्गुन (formless) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality)
ramacharitamanas::3901.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3901.essence: Appearance can hide the formless reality beneath it.
ramacharitamanas::3901.simple_meaning: What matters most is often hidden by what covers it. Just as thick lotus leaves hide water, appearance can hide the supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::3901.simple_insight: Not everything unseen is absent. Patience and clear seeing reveal what first looked hidden.
ramacharitamanas::3901.detailed_meaning: At Pampa lake, after describing the calm water and its beauty, the narration turns inward. The scene becomes a lesson: just as lotus leaves can hide the water below, appearance can hide the formless supreme reality from ordinary sight.
ramacharitamanas::3901.modern_relevance: You scroll past a calm face in a meeting and miss the exhaustion underneath. You judge by the surface and overlook what is actually there.
ramacharitamanas::3901.insight: It trains you to look beyond appearances and notice the reality hidden by the veil of perception.

ramacharitamanas::3902.verse_sanskrit: सुखी मीन सब एकरस अति अगाध जल माहिं। जथा धर्मसीलन्ह के दिन सुख संजुत जाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3902.verse_hindi: उस सरोवर के अत्यंत अथाह जल में सब मछलियाँ सदा एकरस (एक समान) सुखी रहती हैं। जैसे धर्मशील पुरुषों के सब दिन सुखपूर्वक बीतते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3902.english_translation: All the fish in that deep, boundless water remain equally content, just as the days of righteous people pass in ease and harmony.
ramacharitamanas::3902.translation_literal: सुखी (content) / मीन (fish) / सब (all) / एकरस (uniformly) / अति (very) / अगाध (bottomless, unfathomable) / जल (water) / माहिं (in) / जथा (just as) / धर्मसीलन्ह (of the righteous) / के (of) / दिन (days) / सुख संजुत (joined with ease) / जाहिं (go)
ramacharitamanas::3902.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3902.essence: Right living makes life feel naturally spacious.
ramacharitamanas::3902.simple_meaning: In a vast, deep lake, the fish live in the same steady comfort. In the same way, a righteous person's days pass smoothly and peacefully.
ramacharitamanas::3902.simple_insight: A steady inner life makes even ordinary days feel spacious and untroubled.
ramacharitamanas::3902.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing a beautiful lake in the forest: clear, deep, and full of life. The fish move in effortless ease. That image becomes a lesson that a person rooted in dharma can move through life with the same unforced peace.
ramacharitamanas::3902.modern_relevance: You sit in traffic after a long day, but nothing in you is scrambling anymore. The outside is crowded, yet your mind has stopped fighting the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3902.insight: It shifts the mind from agitation to inner steadiness, showing that peace comes from how you inhabit the day.

ramacharitamanas::3903.verse_sanskrit: बिकसे सरसिज नाना रंगा। मधुर मुखर गुंजत बहु भृंगा॥ बोलत जलकुक्कुट कलहंसा। प्रभु बिलोकि जनु करत प्रसंसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3903.verse_hindi: उसमें रंग-बिरंगे कमल खिले हुए हैं। बहुत से भौंरे मधुर स्वर से गुंजार कर रहे हैं। जल के मुर्गे और राजहंस बोल रहे हैं, मानो प्रभु को देखकर उनकी प्रशंसा कर रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3903.english_translation: There, many-colored lotuses bloom. Many bees hum with a sweet sound. Waterfowl and swans speak, as if offering praise upon seeing the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::3903.translation_literal: बिकसे (bloomed) / सरसिज (lotuses) / नाना रंगा (many-colored) / मधुर (sweet) / मुखर (vocal) / गुंजत (humming) / बहु (many) / भृंगा (bees) / बोलत (speaking) / जलकुक्कुट (waterfowl) / कलहंसा (swans) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / जनु (as if) / करत (doing) / प्रसंसा (praise)
ramacharitamanas::3903.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3903.essence: The lake’s beauty makes even birds seem to praise the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::3903.simple_meaning: The lake is full of colorful lotus flowers, humming bees, and birds whose sounds seem like praise for the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::3903.simple_insight: Beauty itself can feel like worship when the mind is open.
ramacharitamanas::3903.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has entered the peaceful lake area in Lanka while searching for Sita. The scene pauses on the beauty around the water: lotuses, bees, and birds. It is a vivid description of the place, not yet a teaching or turning point.
ramacharitamanas::3903.modern_relevance: You walk past a quiet pond at dusk, and even the ripples seem to soften your mind. Some places feel so alive that silence itself feels reverent.
ramacharitamanas::3903.insight: It trains attention to notice sacred atmosphere in ordinary natural beauty.

ramacharitamanas::3904.verse_sanskrit: चक्रबाक बक खग समुदाई। देखत बनइ बरनि नहिं जाई॥ सुंदर खग गन गिरा सुहाई। जात पथिक जनु लेत बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3904.verse_hindi: चक्रवाक, बगुले आदि पक्षियों का समुदाय देखते ही बनता है, उनका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। सुंदर पक्षियों की बोली बड़ी सुहावनी लगती है, मानो (रास्ते में) जाते हुए पथिक को बुलाए लेती हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3904.english_translation: Cranes, herons, and flocks of birds fill the scene; their beauty cannot be fully described. The sweet calls of the lovely birds sound so inviting, as if they are calling to the traveler on the path.
ramacharitamanas::3904.translation_literal: चक्रबाक (cranes) / बक (herons) / खग (birds) / समुदाई (flock, group) / देखत (seeing) / बनइ (becomes) / बरनि (described) / नहिं (not) / जाई (can be done)॥ / सुंदर (beautiful) / खग (birds) / गन (group) / गिरा (voice, call) / सुहाई (pleasant) / जात (going) / पथिक (traveler) / जनु (as if) / लेत (taking) / बोलाई (calling) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3904.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3904.essence: Beauty here is so vivid it seems to call you onward.
ramacharitamanas::3904.simple_meaning: The lake is so full of beautiful birds and sweet sounds that it feels impossible to describe.
ramacharitamanas::3904.simple_insight: Some places feel alive enough to call you forward without a word.
ramacharitamanas::3904.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is moving through the forest around Pampa. Tulsidas lingers on the birds and their calls to deepen the beauty of the landscape before the next scene of the journey unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::3904.modern_relevance: You stop on a quiet road and hear birds in the trees, so clear and welcoming that the whole place feels like an invitation to keep going.
ramacharitamanas::3904.insight: It slows the mind and lets the setting itself carry the mood of the journey.

ramacharitamanas::3905.verse_sanskrit: ताल समीप मुनिन्ह गृह छाए। चहु दिसि कानन बिटप सुहाए॥ चंपक बकुल कदंब तमाला। पाटल पनस परास रसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3905.verse_hindi: उस झील (पंपा सरोवर) के समीप मुनियों ने आश्रम बना रखे हैं। उसके चारों ओर वन के सुंदर वृक्ष हैं। चम्पा, मौलसिरी, कदम्ब, तमाल, पाटल, कटहल, ढाक और आम आदि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3905.english_translation: Near the lake, sages have built their huts. Beautiful trees surround the forest on all sides: champak, bakul, kadamba, tamala, patal, panas, paras, and mango.
ramacharitamanas::3905.translation_literal: ताल (lake) / समीप (near) / मुनिन्ह (sages) / गृह (huts) / छाए (are built) / चहु दिसि (on all four sides) / कानन (forest) / बिटप (trees) / सुहाए (beautiful) / चंपक (champak) / बकुल (bakul) / कदंब (kadamba) / तमाला (tamala) / पाटल (patal) / पनस (jackfruit) / परास (palash) / रसाला (mango)
ramacharitamanas::3905.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3905.essence: Stillness can be felt in the shape of a place.
ramacharitamanas::3905.simple_meaning: Sages live near the lake, and beautiful trees grow all around them.
ramacharitamanas::3905.simple_insight: A quiet life can be surrounded by beauty without needing to possess it.
ramacharitamanas::3905.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the peaceful region near Pampa lake in the forest. Tulsidas pauses the action to paint the scene: sages' huts, trees, and natural abundance all around. It is a serene setting before the next movement of the search.
ramacharitamanas::3905.modern_relevance: You arrive at a hill retreat after a long drive and step out into still air, shaded trees, and silence. The world feels arranged for breathing again.
ramacharitamanas::3905.insight: It slows the mind by placing the search inside a calm, living landscape.

ramacharitamanas::3906.verse_sanskrit: नव पल्लव कुसुमित तरु नाना। चंचरीक पटली कर गाना॥ सीतल मंद सुगंध सुभाऊ। संतत बहइ मनोहर बाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3906.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार के वृक्ष नए-नए पत्तों और (सुगंधित) पुष्पों से युक्त हैं, (जिन पर) भौंरों के समूह गुंजार कर रहे हैं। स्वभाव से ही शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित एवं मन को हरने वाली हवा सदा बहती रहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3906.english_translation: Many kinds of trees are blooming with fresh leaves and flowers; swarms of bees hum around them. A cool, gentle, sweet-smelling breeze keeps flowing, charming the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3906.translation_literal: नव (new) / पल्लव (leaves) / कुसुमित (flowered) / तरु (trees) / नाना (many kinds) / चंचरीक (bees) / पटली (groups) / कर (doing) / गाना (humming) / सीतल (cool) / मंद (gentle) / सुगंध (fragrant) / सुभाऊ (nature) / संतत (continuously) / बहइ (flows) / मनोहर (heart-stealing) / बाऊ (breeze)
ramacharitamanas::3906.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3906.essence: Beauty can be a pause before the next movement.
ramacharitamanas::3906.simple_meaning: The forest is lush, fragrant, and alive with bees and a gentle breeze. It is a beautiful natural scene, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::3906.simple_insight: Sometimes beauty is just there to be received, without needing to be interpreted.
ramacharitamanas::3906.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are in the forest near the serene Pampa region. Tulsidas pauses the story to paint the landscape: blooming trees, humming bees, and a soft breeze. This verse prepares the mood before the next sound of the forest interrupts stillness.
ramacharitamanas::3906.modern_relevance: You step out onto a balcony after rain and notice the wet leaves, the drifting air, the quiet hum of insects. For a moment, nothing needs fixing.
ramacharitamanas::3906.insight: It slows the mind down enough to notice atmosphere before action.

ramacharitamanas::3907.verse_sanskrit: कुहू कुहू कोकिल धुनि करहीं। सुनि रव सरस ध्यान मुनि टरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3907.verse_hindi: कोयलें 'कुहू' 'कुहू' का शब्द कर रही हैं। उनकी रसीली बोली सुनकर मुनियों का भी ध्यान टूट जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3907.english_translation: The cuckoos keep calling 'kuhu, kuhu.' Hearing their sweet song, even the sages' meditation breaks.
ramacharitamanas::3907.translation_literal: कुहू कुहू (kuhu kuhu) / कोकिल (cuckoos) / धुनि (sound) / करहीं (make) / सुनि (hearing) / रव (sound) / सरस (sweet) / ध्यान (meditation) / मुनि (sages) / टरहीं (is broken)
ramacharitamanas::3907.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3907.essence: Beauty can dissolve even a steady meditation.
ramacharitamanas::3907.simple_meaning: The forest is so full of sweet bird calls that even the sages lose concentration.
ramacharitamanas::3907.simple_insight: Even the quietest mind can be touched by beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3907.detailed_meaning: In the forest near the lake, the trees, flowers, and birds are all alive with springlike sweetness. Tulsidas pauses to show that even the sages living there are gently pulled out of meditation by the cuckoos' song.
ramacharitamanas::3907.modern_relevance: You finally sit down to focus, but a song from the next room, a notification, or a passing memory pulls your attention away.
ramacharitamanas::3907.insight: It shows how sensory beauty can interrupt inward concentration, even in a disciplined setting.

ramacharitamanas::3908.verse_sanskrit: फल भारन नमि बिटप सब रहे भूमि निअराइ। पर उपकारी पुरुष जिमि नवहिं सुसंपति पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3908.verse_hindi: फलों के बोझ से झुककर सारे वृक्ष पृथ्वी के पास आ लगे हैं, जैसे परोपकारी पुरुष बड़ी सम्पत्ति पाकर (विनय से) झुक जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3908.english_translation: All the trees bowed low to the earth under the weight of fruit, just as generous people bow in humility after gaining great wealth.
ramacharitamanas::3908.translation_literal: फल (fruit) / भारन (under the weight) / नमि (bowing) / बिटप (trees) / सब (all) / रहे (remained) / भूमि (to the earth) / निअराइ (near) / पर (like) / उपकारी (generous, beneficent) / पुरुष (people) / जिमि (just as) / नवहिं (bow) / सुसंपति (great wealth) / पाइ (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::3908.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3908.essence: True fullness bows lower the more it gives.
ramacharitamanas::3908.simple_meaning: Trees bend down when they are full of fruit. In the same way, truly generous people become more humble when they receive abundance.
ramacharitamanas::3908.simple_insight: Success is meant to soften you, not harden you.
ramacharitamanas::3908.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama and Lakshman move through trees heavy with fruit. Tulsidas turns that sight into a lesson: real fullness does not inflate the heart. It makes a person bow lower, like a tree burdened with giving.
ramacharitamanas::3908.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the bonus, the praise in front of the team — and the real test is whether it makes you gentler. Plenty should deepen your grace, not your ego.
ramacharitamanas::3908.insight: It shifts success from a reason for pride into a reason for humility.

ramacharitamanas::3909.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम अति रुचिर तलावा। मज्जनु कीन्ह परम सुख पावा॥ देखी सुंदर तरुबर छाया। बैठे अनुज सहित रघुराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3909.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने अत्यंत सुंदर तालाब देखकर स्नान किया और परम सुख पाया। एक सुंदर उत्तम वृक्ष की छाया देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित बैठ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3909.english_translation: Seeing a very beautiful pond, Ram bathed and felt great joy. Seeing the shade of a beautiful tree, Raghuraj sat there with his younger brother Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3909.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / अति (very) / रुचिर (beautiful) / तलावा (pond) / मज्जनु (bath) / कीन्ह (did) / परम (supreme) / सुख (joy) / पावा (found) / देखी (seeing) / सुंदर (beautiful) / तरुबर (excellent tree) / छाया (shade) / बैठे (sat) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / रघुराया (lord of the Raghu clan)
ramacharitamanas::3909.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3909.essence: Rest can be holy when the journey itself is demanding.
ramacharitamanas::3909.simple_meaning: Ram sees a lovely pond, bathes, and rests in the shade of a beautiful tree with Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3909.simple_insight: Even sacred journeys include simple pauses that restore the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3909.detailed_meaning: During the forest journey, Ram and Lakshman come upon a beautiful pond and a cool tree. Ram bathes, feels refreshed, and sits down with his brother. The verse slows the story to show peace before the next movement.
ramacharitamanas::3909.modern_relevance: You step out of a crowded train, find a quiet bench under a tree, and finally breathe. Sometimes rest is not a break from the journey; it is part of it.
ramacharitamanas::3909.insight: It teaches you to honour restorative pauses instead of rushing through every moment.

ramacharitamanas::3910.verse_sanskrit: तहँ पुनि सकल देव मुनि आए। अस्तुति करि निज धाम सिधाए॥ बैठे परम प्रसन्न कृपाला। कहत अनुज सन कथा रसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3910.verse_hindi: फिर वहाँ सब देवता और मुनि आए और स्तुति करके अपने-अपने धाम को चले गए। कृपालु श्री रामजी परम प्रसन्न बैठे हुए छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी से रसीली कथाएँ कह रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3910.english_translation: Then all the gods and sages came there, offered praise, and returned to their own abodes. The compassionate Ram sat in great delight, speaking sweet stories with his younger brother.
ramacharitamanas::3910.translation_literal: तहँ (there) / पुनि (again) / सकल (all) / देव (deities) / मुनि (sages) / आए (came) / अस्तुति (praise) / करि (having done) / निज (their own) / धाम (abodes) / सिधाए (departed) / बैठे (sat) / परम (greatly) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / कहत (speaking) / अनुज (younger brother) / सन (with) / कथा (story) / रसाला (sweet, relishable)
ramacharitamanas::3910.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3910.essence: Praise comes and goes; closeness remains.
ramacharitamanas::3910.simple_meaning: The gods and sages arrive, praise Ram, and leave. Ram then sits happily with Lakshman, sharing sweet stories.
ramacharitamanas::3910.simple_insight: Some of the deepest joy is quiet: praise passes, but shared presence remains.
ramacharitamanas::3910.detailed_meaning: After the beautiful stop by the lake, the gods and sages gather around Ram in the forest. They praise him and depart. What remains is a tender scene: Ram, content and unhurried, sits with Lakshman and speaks lovingly.
ramacharitamanas::3910.modern_relevance: A room empties after the guests leave, and the applause fades. What stays is the calm of being with one person who truly knows you.
ramacharitamanas::3910.insight: It shifts attention from public admiration to intimate companionship and ease.

ramacharitamanas::3911.verse_sanskrit: बिरहवंत भगवंतहि देखी। नारद मन भा सोच बिसेषी॥ मोर साप करि अंगीकारा। सहत राम नाना दुख भारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3911.verse_hindi: भगवान् को विरहयुक्त देखकर नारदजी के मन में विशेष रूप से सोच हुआ। (उन्होंने विचार किया कि) मेरे ही शाप को स्वीकार करके श्री रामजी नाना प्रकार के दुःखों का भार सह रहे हैं (दुःख उठा रहे हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3911.english_translation: Seeing the Lord in separation, Narada felt a deep unease. He thought, 'He has accepted my curse and is bearing many kinds of suffering.'
ramacharitamanas::3911.translation_literal: बिरहवंत (enduring separation) / भगवंतहि (the Lord) / देखी (seeing) / नारद (Narada) / मन (mind) / भा (became) / सोच (concern) / बिसेषी (especially) / मोर (my) / साप (curse) / करि (having made) / अंगीकारा (accepted) / सहत (suffering) / राम (Ram) / नाना (many) / दुख (sorrows) / भारा (burden)
ramacharitamanas::3911.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3911.essence: Love becomes compassion when it cannot bear another's suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3911.simple_meaning: Narada sees Ram suffering because of his curse and feels deep concern. The sight of the beloved in pain stirs compassion immediately.
ramacharitamanas::3911.simple_insight: Love becomes real when another's suffering stops feeling distant.
ramacharitamanas::3911.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Narada sees Ram living under the burden of separation and hardship. Realising that Ram has accepted his curse, Narada is shaken by compassion. This moment turns his curiosity into urgent devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3911.modern_relevance: You see someone you admire quietly carrying too much — and the sight hits you harder than their words ever could. Real care begins there.
ramacharitamanas::3911.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to compassionate responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::3912.verse_sanskrit: ऐसे प्रभुहि बिलोकउँ जाई। पुनि न बनिहि अस अवसरु आई॥ यह बिचारि नारद कर बीना। गए जहाँ प्रभु सुख आसीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3912.verse_hindi: ऐसे (भक्त वत्सल) प्रभु को जाकर देखूँ। फिर ऐसा अवसर न बन आवेगा। यह विचार कर नारदजी हाथ में वीणा लिए हुए वहाँ गए, जहाँ प्रभु सुखपूर्वक बैठे हुए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3912.english_translation: I should go and see such a gracious Lord. An opportunity like this may not come again. Thinking this, Narad took up his veena and went to where the Lord was resting in peace.
ramacharitamanas::3912.translation_literal: ऐसे (such) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकउँ (I should see) / जाई (going) / पुनि (again) / न (not) / बनिहि (will happen) / अस (such) / अवसरु (opportunity) / आई (coming) / यह (this) / बिचारि (thinking) / नारद (Narad) / कर (in hand) / बीना (veena) / गए (went) / जहाँ (where) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुख आसीना (resting in ease)
ramacharitamanas::3912.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3912.essence: A rare opening to meet the beloved should not be delayed.
ramacharitamanas::3912.simple_meaning: Narad decides to go see Ram right away, knowing this rare chance may never come again.
ramacharitamanas::3912.simple_insight: When the heart recognizes a rare opening, hesitation falls away.
ramacharitamanas::3912.detailed_meaning: Narad has just seen Ram in a state of loving separation and feels a deep stir in his heart. He decides not to delay, takes his veena, and goes at once to Ram, who is resting peacefully with Lakshman nearby.
ramacharitamanas::3912.modern_relevance: You get a sudden opening to call someone you’ve avoided for months. You know the moment is fragile, and if you wait, the courage may vanish. Narad moves before fear can bargain.
ramacharitamanas::3912.insight: It teaches you to act immediately when devotion or conscience gives you a clear opening.

ramacharitamanas::3913.verse_sanskrit: गावत राम चरित मृदु बानी। प्रेम सहित बहु भाँति बखानी॥ करत दंडवत लिए उठाई। राखे बहुत बार उर लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3913.verse_hindi: वे कोमल वाणी से प्रेम के साथ बहुत प्रकार से बखान-बखान कर रामचरित का गान कर (ते हुए चले आ) रहे थे। दण्डवत् करते देखकर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने नारदजी को उठा लिया और बहुत देर तक हृदय से लगाए रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3913.english_translation: Speaking softly, he sang Ram's story with love in many ways. Seeing him bow down again and again, Ram lifted Narad and held him close to his heart for a long time.
ramacharitamanas::3913.translation_literal: गावत (singing) / राम चरित (Ram's story) / मृदु बानी (soft voice) / प्रेम सहित (with love) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / बखानी (praised) / करत (doing) / दंडवत (full bow) / लिए (having taken) / उठाई (lifted) / राखे (kept) / बहुत बार (for a long time) / उर (heart) / लाई (brought close)
ramacharitamanas::3913.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3913.essence: True devotion is met by immediate embrace.
ramacharitamanas::3913.simple_meaning: Narad sings Ram's story with deep love, bows again and again, and Ram responds by lifting him up and holding him close.
ramacharitamanas::3913.simple_insight: Devotion does not make you small; it brings you into Ram's embrace.
ramacharitamanas::3913.detailed_meaning: Narad has come to see Ram after reflecting on the Lord's suffering. He sings Ram's deeds softly and lovingly, bows down in reverence, and Ram immediately answers with warmth, lifting him up and holding him to His chest.
ramacharitamanas::3913.modern_relevance: You finally speak from the heart to someone you deeply revere, expecting nothing back. Instead of distance, you find welcome — the kind that makes your humility feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::3913.insight: It shows that sincere praise and surrender open the door to intimate closeness.

ramacharitamanas::3914.verse_sanskrit: स्वागत पूँछि निकट बैठारे। लछिमन सादर चरन पखारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3914.verse_hindi: फिर स्वागत (कुशल) पूछकर पास बैठा लिया। लक्ष्मणजी ने आदर के साथ उनके चरण धोए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3914.english_translation: After welcoming him and asking after his welfare, they seated him nearby. Lakshman respectfully washed his feet.
ramacharitamanas::3914.translation_literal: स्वागत (welcome) / पूँछि (asking) / निकट (near) / बैठारे (sat down) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / सादर (with respect) / चरन (feet) / पखारे (washed)
ramacharitamanas::3914.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3914.simple_meaning: Lakshman welcomes Narad warmly, seats him close, and honors him by washing his feet.
ramacharitamanas::3914.simple_insight: Real respect shows up in small, humble acts.
ramacharitamanas::3914.detailed_meaning: Narad has come to meet Ram in the forest, and the welcome is immediate and reverent. Lakshman, always eager in service, responds not with pride but with humility, washing the sage's feet before the deeper conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::3914.modern_relevance: A guest arrives unexpectedly at your door, and you stop everything to make them feel honored. That quiet care says more than any grand speech.
ramacharitamanas::3914.insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that honor is proved by action.

ramacharitamanas::3915.verse_sanskrit: नाना बिधि बिनती करि प्रभु प्रसन्न जियँ जानि। नारद बोले बचन तब जोरि सरोरुह पानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3915.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार से विनती करके और प्रभु को मन में प्रसन्न जानकर तब नारदजी कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3915.english_translation: After offering many kinds of prayer and knowing in his heart that the Lord was pleased, Narad then spoke, joining his lotus-like hands.
ramacharitamanas::3915.translation_literal: नाना बिधि (in many ways) / बिनती (prayer, entreaty) / करि (having done) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / नारद (Narad) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / तब (then) / जोरि (joining) / सरोरुह (lotus-like) / पानि (hands)
ramacharitamanas::3915.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::3915.essence: Prayer prepares the heart before words can truly begin.
ramacharitamanas::3915.simple_meaning: Narad prays until he feels Ram is pleased, then he speaks with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::3915.simple_insight: Devotion listens first. Only after sensing welcome does the heart ask.
ramacharitamanas::3915.detailed_meaning: Narad has approached Ram in the forest and offered repeated respectful prayers. Seeing Ram’s gracious mood, he folds his hands and begins to speak. This verse is the quiet bridge between reverent approach and the request that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3915.modern_relevance: You rehearse a hard conversation, then notice the other person has softened. That opening matters — not because you control them, but because respect has made room for honest words.
ramacharitamanas::3915.insight: It teaches you to begin from reverence, then speak only when the moment is receptive.

ramacharitamanas::3916.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु उदार सहज रघुनायक। सुंदर अगम सुगम बर दायक॥ देहु एक बर मागउँ स्वामी। जद्यपि जानत अंतरजामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3916.verse_hindi: हे स्वभाव से ही उदार श्री रघुनाथजी! सुनिए। आप सुंदर अगम और सुगम वर के देने वाले हैं। हे स्वामी! मैं एक वर माँगता हूँ, वह मुझे दीजिए, यद्यपि आप अंतर्यामी होने के नाते सब जानते ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3916.english_translation: Listen, generous and naturally gracious Lord of the Raghu line. You are the giver of beautiful, hard-to-attain, and easy boons. O master, I ask for one boon; grant it to me, though as the inner knower you already know it.
ramacharitamanas::3916.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / उदार (generous) / सहज (natural) / रघुनायक (Lord of Raghu) / सुंदर (beautiful) / अगम (hard to reach) / सुगम (easy to reach) / बर (boon) / दायक (giver) // देहु (give) / एक (one) / बर (boon) / मागउँ (I ask) / स्वामी (master) // जद्यपि (although) / जानत (knowing) / अंतरजामी (inner knower)
ramacharitamanas::3916.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::3916.essence: Trust lets you ask openly, even before words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3916.simple_meaning: Narada praises Ram as naturally generous and asks Him for a boon, while acknowledging that Ram already knows every heart.
ramacharitamanas::3916.simple_insight: There is peace in asking without pretense when you trust that you are already known.
ramacharitamanas::3916.detailed_meaning: Narada has just been welcomed with honor in the forest. Now he turns to Ram with folded hands and speaks like a devotee who knows both Ram's generosity and His inner knowing. The moment is intimate: an asking that is already an act of trust.
ramacharitamanas::3916.modern_relevance: You finally tell someone what you need, even though they may already sense it. The relief is not in surprising them, but in speaking honestly without hiding.
ramacharitamanas::3916.insight: It shifts prayer from bargaining to trustful openness: ask directly, because nothing in your heart is hidden.

ramacharitamanas::3917.verse_sanskrit: जानहु मुनि तुम्ह मोर सुभाऊ। जन सन कबहुँ कि करऊँ दुराऊ॥ कवन बस्तु असि प्रिय मोहि लागी। जो मुनिबर न सकहुँ तुम्ह मागी ॥
