ramacharitamanas::3917.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मुनि! तुम मेरा स्वभाव जानते ही हो। क्या मैं अपने भक्तों से कभी कुछ छिपाव करता हूँ? मुझे ऐसी कौन सी वस्तु प्रिय लगती है, जिसे हे मुनिश्रेष्ठ! तुम नहीं माँग सकते? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3917.english_translation: O sage, you already know my nature. Do I ever hide anything from my devotees? What thing seems dear to me that you, best of sages, cannot ask for?
ramacharitamanas::3917.translation_literal: जानहु (you know) / मुनि (sage) / तुम्ह (you) / मोर (my) / सुभाऊ (nature) / जन (from people/devotees) / सन (from) / कबहुँ (ever) / कि (whether) / करऊँ (I do) / दुराऊ (hiding) ॥ / कवन (which) / बस्तु (thing) / असि (such) / प्रिय (dear) / मोहि (to me) / लागी (seems) / जो (that) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / न (not) / सकहुँ (can) / तुम्ह (you) / मागी (to ask)
ramacharitamanas::3917.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3917.essence: The devoted heart can ask freely because Ram never hides.
ramacharitamanas::3917.simple_meaning: Ram tells Narad that his nature is open and generous. He never hides from devotees, and there is nothing dear to him that a devoted seeker cannot ask for.
ramacharitamanas::3917.simple_insight: You do not need perfect wording to reach what loves you back.
ramacharitamanas::3917.detailed_meaning: Narad has just praised Ram and asked for a boon. Ram answers with warmth: his heart is never closed to a true devotee. In this forest meeting, the whole exchange turns on trust — Narad may ask freely because Ram never withholds himself.
ramacharitamanas::3917.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone you trust, finally saying the thing you’ve been embarrassed to ask. The fear of being judged fades when you realize the other side is already open.
ramacharitamanas::3917.insight: It shifts asking from hesitation to confidence, showing that devotion can speak plainly.

ramacharitamanas::3918.verse_sanskrit: जन कहुँ कछु अदेय नहिं मोरें। अस बिस्वास तजहु जनि भोरें॥ तब नारद बोले हरषाई। अस बर मागउँ करउँ ढिठाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3918.verse_hindi: मुझे भक्त के लिए कुछ भी अदेय नहीं है। ऐसा विश्वास भूलकर भी मत छोड़ो। तब नारदजी हर्षित होकर बोले- मैं ऐसा वर माँगता हूँ, यह धृष्टता करता हूँ- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3918.english_translation: Nothing is beyond my giving to a devotee. Never let go of that trust. Then Narad, delighted, said, 'I ask for such a boon, though it may seem bold.'
ramacharitamanas::3918.translation_literal: जन (for) / कहुँ (to anyone) / कछु (anything) / अदेय (not to be given) / नहिं (is not) / मोरें (for me) / अस (such) / बिस्वास (trust) / तजहु (abandon) / जनि (do not) / भोरें (in forgetfulness) / तब (then) / नारद (Narad) / बोले (spoke) / हरषाई (joyfully) / अस (such) / बर (boon) / मागउँ (I ask) / करउँ (I do) / ढिठाई (boldness)
ramacharitamanas::3918.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3918.essence: Trust opens the door to what fear calls impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3918.simple_meaning: Ram says nothing is impossible for a devoted heart to receive, and Narad responds with joyful boldness, asking for a boon.
ramacharitamanas::3918.simple_insight: You can ask with confidence when your trust is rooted in love, not in fear.
ramacharitamanas::3918.detailed_meaning: Narad is speaking with Ram in the forest, testing the depth of divine generosity. Ram answers that nothing is off-limits to a true devotee. Hearing that, Narad grows joyful and dares to ask for a boon.
ramacharitamanas::3918.modern_relevance: You hesitate before sending the message, afraid you're asking for too much. But sometimes the fear is yours, not the door's. Real trust speaks plainly.
ramacharitamanas::3918.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded hesitation to confident asking grounded in trust.

ramacharitamanas::3919.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि प्रभु के नाम अनेका। श्रुति कह अधिक एक तें एका॥ राम सकल नामन्ह ते अधिका। होउ नाथ अघ खग गन बधिका ॥
ramacharitamanas::3919.verse_hindi: यद्यपि प्रभु के अनेकों नाम हैं और वेद कहते हैं कि वे सब एक से एक बढ़कर हैं, तो भी हे नाथ! रामनाम सब नामों से बढ़कर हो और पाप रूपी पक्षियों के समूह के लिए यह वधिक के समान हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3919.english_translation: Although the Lord has many names, and the Vedas say that each is greater than the last, may the name Ram be greater than all names, O Lord, and may it be like a hunter to the flock of birds that are sins.
ramacharitamanas::3919.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / प्रभु (Lord) / के (of) / नाम (names) / अनेका (many) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / कह (say) / अधिक (greater) / एक तें एका (one than another) / राम (Ram) / सकल (all) / नामन्ह (names) / ते (than) / अधिका (greater) / होउ (may be) / नाथ (Lord) / अघ (sins) / खग (birds) / गन (group) / बधिका (hunter)
ramacharitamanas::3919.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3919.essence: Ram's name stands above every other name and clears away burden.
ramacharitamanas::3919.simple_meaning: Ram's name is asked to be the highest of all names, powerful enough to destroy the many burdens that bind the mind.
ramacharitamanas::3919.simple_insight: There is relief in having one name strong enough to clear away everything else.
ramacharitamanas::3919.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's name, not just as one sacred name among many, but as the highest refuge. In the middle of the Narad-Ram dialogue, he asks that Ram's name become the force that destroys the mind's burdens.
ramacharitamanas::3919.modern_relevance: You keep repeating a name, a worry, a deadline in your head until it feels larger than you. This verse offers a different repetition: one name that can cut through the noise instead of feeding it.
ramacharitamanas::3919.insight: It shifts attention from many competing supports to one supreme refuge.

ramacharitamanas::3920.verse_sanskrit: राका रजनी भगति तव राम नाम सोइ सोम। अपर नाम उडगन बिमल बसहुँ भगत उर ब्योम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3920.verse_hindi: आपकी भक्ति पूर्णिमा की रात्रि है, उसमें 'राम' नाम यही पूर्ण चंद्रमा होकर और अन्य सब नाम तारागण होकर भक्तों के हृदय रूपी निर्मल आकाश में निवास करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3920.english_translation: Your devotion is a moonlit night, and Ram's name is the full moon. Let all other names dwell like stars in the pure sky of a devotee's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3920.translation_literal: राका (full-moon night) / रजनी (night) / भगति (devotion) / तव (your) / राम (Ram) / नाम (name) / सोइ (that itself) / सोम (moon) / अपर (other) / नाम (names) / उडगन (stars) / बिमल (pure) / बसहुँ (dwell) / भगत (devotee's) / उर (heart) / ब्योम (sky)
ramacharitamanas::3920.speaker: Nārada
ramacharitamanas::3920.essence: One name can become the moon that orders every other prayer.
ramacharitamanas::3920.simple_meaning: Devotion is like a moonlit sky: Ram's name is the brightest presence, and every other sacred name shines around it without losing its place.
ramacharitamanas::3920.simple_insight: You do not have to reject everything else to love deeply; one living center can hold the whole sky.
ramacharitamanas::3920.detailed_meaning: Narada has asked for a blessing about Ram's name. In this verse, he imagines devotion itself as a moonlit night: Ram's name is the full moon, and all other names are stars resting in the clear heart of a devotee.
ramacharitamanas::3920.modern_relevance: You open a prayer app and keep switching between mantras, unsure which one to hold. This verse gives you a center: one name can anchor everything else without making the rest meaningless.
ramacharitamanas::3920.insight: It teaches you to gather devotion around one luminous center instead of scattering attention across many objects.

ramacharitamanas::3921.verse_sanskrit: एवमस्तु मुनि सन कहेउ कृपासिंधु रघुनाथ। तब नारद मन हरष अति प्रभु पद नायउ माथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3921.verse_hindi: कृपा सागर श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुनि से 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहा। तब नारदजी ने मन में अत्यंत हर्षित होकर प्रभु के चरणों में मस्तक नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3921.english_translation: The compassionate Lord of Raghu said, 'So be it' to the sage. Then Narada became deeply joyful and bowed his head at the Lord's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3921.translation_literal: एवमस्तु (so be it) / मुनि (sage) / सन (to) / कहेउ (said) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / रघुनाथ (Lord of Raghu) / तब (then) / नारद (Narada) / मन (in mind) / हरष (joy) / अति (very) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / नायउ (bowed) / माथ (head)
ramacharitamanas::3921.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3921.essence: Grace received becomes joy that bends the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3921.simple_meaning: Ram agrees to the sage's request, and Narada responds with deep joy and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3921.simple_insight: A sincere request answered with grace can turn relief into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3921.detailed_meaning: Narada has just praised Ram's name above all other names. Ram, pleased by the sage's devotion, says 'so be it.' The exchange is brief, but it seals the blessing and leaves Narada overwhelmed with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3921.modern_relevance: You finally get the message you've been hoping for: 'Yes, I'll do it.' Relief floods your chest before you even answer.
ramacharitamanas::3921.insight: It shows how grace answers devotion, and how joy naturally turns into bowing.

ramacharitamanas::3922.verse_sanskrit: अति प्रसन्न रघुनाथहि जानी। पुनि नारद बोले मृदु बानी॥ राम जबहिं प्रेरेउ निज माया मोहेहु मोहि सुनहु रघुराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3922.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी को अत्यंत प्रसन्न जानकर नारदजी फिर कोमल वाणी बोले- हे रामजी! हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए, जब आपने अपनी माया को प्रेरित करके मुझे मोहित किया था, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3922.english_translation: Seeing Raghunath extremely pleased, Narad again spoke softly: "O Ram, when you stirred your own illusion, you deluded me. Listen, Raghu's lord."
ramacharitamanas::3922.translation_literal: अति (very) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / रघुनाथहि (Raghunath) / जानी (knowing) / पुनि (again) / नारद (Narad) / बोले (spoke) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / राम (Ram) / जबहिं (when) / प्रेरेउ (stirred) / निज (your own) / माया (illusion) / मोहेहु (you deluded) / मोहि (me) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुराया (O lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::3922.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::3922.essence: Even being misled can deepen your return to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3922.simple_meaning: Narad gently reminds Ram that even being misled was part of Ram's play, and he speaks with loving familiarity, not complaint.
ramacharitamanas::3922.simple_insight: Even your confusion can become a doorway back to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3922.detailed_meaning: Narad has just seen Ram pleased with his prayer. Instead of speaking boldly, he softens his voice and recalls how Ram once used his own illusion to bewilder him. The moment turns personal devotion into surrendered honesty.
ramacharitamanas::3922.modern_relevance: You look back on the detour that embarrassed you, and somehow it still brought you closer to what matters. Even the wrong turn can become part of the meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3922.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming confusion to seeing how grace can work through it.

ramacharitamanas::3923.verse_sanskrit: तब बिबाह मैं चाहउँ कीन्हा। प्रभु केहि कारन करै न दीन्हा॥ सुनु मुनि तोहि कहउँ सहरोसा। भजहिं जे मोहि तजि सकल भरोसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3923.verse_hindi: तब मैं विवाह करना चाहता था। हे प्रभु! आपने मुझे किस कारण विवाह नहीं करने दिया? (प्रभु बोले-) हे मुनि! सुनो, मैं तुम्हें हर्ष के साथ कहता हूँ कि जो समस्त आशा-भरोसा छोड़कर केवल मुझको ही भजते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3923.english_translation: At that time I wanted to marry, but you did not allow it for some reason. Listen, sage: I tell you with joy that I protect only those who leave all hopes and rely on me alone.
ramacharitamanas::3923.translation_literal: तब (then) / बिबाह (marriage) / मैं (I) / चाहउँ (wanted) / कीन्हा (did) / प्रभु (Lord) / केहि (for what) / कारन (reason) / करै (to do) / न (not) / दीन्हा (allowed) / सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / तोहि (to you) / कहउँ (I say) / सहरोसा (with joy / confidently) / भजहिं (worship) / जे (those who) / मोहि (me) / तजि (leaving) / सकल (all) / भरोसा (reliance)
ramacharitamanas::3923.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3923.essence: Complete trust in Ram becomes complete protection.
ramacharitamanas::3923.simple_meaning: Ram says he did not allow Narad to marry because those who give up every other support and trust him alone receive his protection.
ramacharitamanas::3923.simple_insight: Real security begins when you stop splitting your trust between many supports.
ramacharitamanas::3923.detailed_meaning: Narad has just admitted that Ram's illusion once unsettled him. Smiling, Ram explains why Narad remained unmarried: he wanted to keep Narad free for total devotion. The verse turns that personal story into a promise of protection for anyone who relies on Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::3923.modern_relevance: You keep a backup plan for every relationship, every job, every prayer. Then one day you notice the backup plans are what exhaust you. This verse points to the relief of trusting one steady refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3923.insight: It shifts the mind from divided dependence to single-hearted reliance.

ramacharitamanas::3924.verse_sanskrit: करउँ सदा तिन्ह कै रखवारी। जिमि बालक राखइ महतारी॥ गह सिसु बच्छ अनल अहि धाई। तहँ राखइ जननी अरगाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3924.verse_hindi: मैं सदा उनकी वैसे ही रखवाली करता हूँ, जैसे माता बालक की रक्षा करती है। छोटा बच्चा जब दौड़कर आग और साँप को पकड़ने जाता है, तो वहाँ माता उसे (अपने हाथों) अलग करके बचा लेती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3924.english_translation: I always protect them just as a mother protects her child. When a little child runs toward fire or a snake, the mother pulls the child away and saves it.
ramacharitamanas::3924.translation_literal: करउँ (I do) / सदा (always) / तिन्ह कै (their) / रखवारी (protection) / जिमि (just as) / बालक (child) / राखइ (protects) / महतारी (mother) / गह (when grasping) / सिसु (small child) / बच्छ (calf/child) / अनल (fire) / अहि (snake) / धाई (running) / तहँ (there) / राखइ (saves) / जननी (mother) / अरगाई (pulling away)
ramacharitamanas::3924.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3924.essence: True protection sometimes means pulling you back, not letting you go forward.
ramacharitamanas::3924.simple_meaning: Ram says he protects devotees the way a mother protects a child, even pulling them away from danger they do not yet understand.
ramacharitamanas::3924.simple_insight: Safety can look like being redirected, not indulged.
ramacharitamanas::3924.detailed_meaning: In the forest dialogue, Narad is being reassured about divine care. Ram explains that he watches over those who turn toward him with the same urgency a mother has for a child rushing toward danger.
ramacharitamanas::3924.modern_relevance: You were about to text the person who keeps hurting you, then stopped. Something in you knew the pull back was protection, not punishment.
ramacharitamanas::3924.insight: It shifts trust from self-direction to being gently held away from harm.

ramacharitamanas::3925.verse_sanskrit: प्रौढ़ भएँ तेहि सुत पर माता। प्रीति करइ नहिं पाछिलि बाता॥ मोरें प्रौढ़ तनय सम ग्यानी। बालक सुत सम दास अमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3925.verse_hindi: सयाना हो जाने पर उस पुत्र पर माता प्रेम तो करती है, परन्तु पिछली बात नहीं रहती (अर्थात् मातृ परायण शिशु की तरह फिर उसको बचाने की चिंता नहीं करती, क्योंकि वह माता पर निर्भर न कर अपनी रक्षा आप करने लगता है)। ज्ञानी मेरे प्रौढ़ (सयाने) पुत्र के समान है और (तुम्हारे जैसा) अपने बल का मान न करने वाला सेवक मेरे शिशु पुत्र के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3925.english_translation: A mother loves her grown son, but she no longer worries over his safety like a child’s. My mature devotee is like that wise son, and the humble servant who does not rely on his own strength is like a child to me.
ramacharitamanas::3925.translation_literal: प्रौढ़ भएँ (having grown up) / तेहि सुत पर (for that son) / माता (a mother) / प्रीति करइ (shows affection) / नहिं (not) / पाछिलि बाता (the earlier concern)॥ मोरें (for me) / प्रौढ़ तनय (grown son) / सम (like) / ग्यानी (the wise one) / बालक सुत (child son) / सम (like) / दास (servant) / अमानी (without pride)
ramacharitamanas::3925.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3925.essence: Humility draws care; pride creates distance.
ramacharitamanas::3925.simple_meaning: A wise person may rely on personal understanding, but a humble devotee depends on the divine completely. Humility brings closeness; self-reliance creates distance.
ramacharitamanas::3925.simple_insight: There is relief in not having to prove your strength before the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3925.detailed_meaning: Ram is explaining the difference between two kinds of followers. A mature, wise person is like a grown son who can manage alone. But a humble servant who does not boast of personal power is like a child the divine naturally protects.
ramacharitamanas::3925.modern_relevance: You keep trying to look capable in front of everyone, even when you are exhausted. This verse says the deeper safety comes when you stop performing strength and allow yourself to be held.
ramacharitamanas::3925.insight: It shifts devotion from self-display to dependence, showing that humility creates intimacy.

ramacharitamanas::3926.verse_sanskrit: जनहि मोर बल निज बल ताही। दुहु कहँ काम क्रोध रिपु आही॥ यह बिचारि पंडित मोहि भजहीं। पाएहुँ ग्यान भगति नहिं तजहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3926.verse_hindi: मेरे सेवक को केवल मेरा ही बल रहता है और उसे (ज्ञानी को) अपना बल होता है। पर काम-क्रोध रूपी शत्रु तो दोनों के लिए हैं।(भक्त के शत्रुओं को मारने की जिम्मेवारी मुझ पर रहती है, क्योंकि वह मेरे परायण होकर मेरा ही बल मानता है, परन्तु अपने बल को मानने वाले ज्ञानी के शत्रुओं का नाश करने की जिम्मेवारी मुझ पर नहीं है।) ऐसा विचार कर पंडितजन (बुद्धिमान लोग) मुझको ही भजते हैं। वे ज्ञान प्राप्त होने पर भी भक्ति को नहीं छोड़ते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3926.english_translation: Those who know my strength rely on my strength alone. For both of them, the enemies are lust and anger. Thinking this way, the wise worship me. Even after gaining understanding, they do not abandon devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3926.translation_literal: जनहि (know) / मोर (my) / बल (strength) / निज (own) / बल (strength) / ताही (that one) / दुहु (both) / कहँ (for) / काम (lust) / क्रोध (anger) / रिपु (enemy) / आही (are) / यह (this) / बिचारि (thinking) / पंडित (wise) / मोहि (me) / भजहीं (worship) / पाएहुँ (having attained) / ग्यान (knowledge) / भगति (devotion) / नहिं (not) / तजहीं (abandon)
ramacharitamanas::3926.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3926.essence: Knowing your limits makes devotion wiser, not weaker.
ramacharitamanas::3926.simple_meaning: Those who depend on Ram's strength are protected, while lust and anger threaten everyone. Wise people understand this and keep worshipping him even after gaining knowledge.
ramacharitamanas::3926.simple_insight: Real wisdom does not make you self-sufficient; it makes you more devoted and less afraid.
ramacharitamanas::3926.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram explains why thoughtful people still keep devotion even after gaining understanding. Human strength cannot defeat lust and anger alone. When a person sees that clearly, worship becomes the wiser refuge, not a lesser one.
ramacharitamanas::3926.modern_relevance: You can be the smartest person in the room and still feel hijacked by anger in a family argument or desire in a private moment. The deeper move is not pride in insight, but leaning on a source stronger than your impulses.
ramacharitamanas::3926.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to humble dependence, showing that understanding should lead to deeper devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3927.verse_sanskrit: काम क्रोध लोभादि मद प्रबल मोह कै धारि। तिन्ह महँ अति दारुन दुखद मायारूपी नारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3927.verse_hindi: काम, क्रोध, लोभ और मद आदि मोह (अज्ञान) की प्रबल सेना है। इनमें मायारूपिणी (माया की साक्षात् मूर्ति) स्त्री तो अत्यंत दारुण दुःख देने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3927.english_translation: Desire, anger, greed, pride, and the rest are the strong army of delusion. Among them, the woman shaped by illusion is the most terrible source of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3927.translation_literal: काम (desire) / क्रोध (anger) / लोभादि (greed and the rest) / मद (pride) / प्रबल (strong) / मोह (delusion) / कै (of) / धारि (army) / तिन्ह महँ (among them) / अति (very) / दारुन (terrible) / दुखद (pain-giving) / मायारूपी (shaped like illusion) / नारि (woman)
ramacharitamanas::3927.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3927.essence: Delusion becomes most dangerous when it feels attractive.
ramacharitamanas::3927.simple_meaning: Desire, anger, greed, and pride are powerful forces of confusion. The verse warns that illusion can take a form that causes especially deep suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3927.simple_insight: You can stop mistaking intensity for truth. Not every strong feeling deserves obedience.
ramacharitamanas::3927.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the conversation turns from human weakness to the inner forces that destroy clear seeing. The speaker names desire, anger, greed, and pride as an army of delusion, then warns that illusion itself can become especially dangerous when it takes seductive form.
ramacharitamanas::3927.modern_relevance: A late-night argument starts with one sharp message, then turns into jealousy, defensiveness, and obsession. By morning, you can see the pattern: the mind was never just reacting — it was being pulled by forces you didn't name fast enough.
ramacharitamanas::3927.insight: It teaches you to recognize the hidden pattern behind emotional overwhelm before it hardens into action.

ramacharitamanas::3928.verse_sanskrit: सुनु मुनि कह पुरान श्रुति संता। मोह बिपिन कहुँ नारि बसंता॥ जप तप नेम जलाश्रय झारी। होइ ग्रीषम सोषइ सब नारी॥1
ramacharitamanas::3928.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! सुनो, पुराण, वेद और संत कहते हैं कि मोह रूपी वन (को विकसित करने) के लिए स्त्री वसंत ऋतु के समान है। जप, तप, नियम रूपी संपूर्ण जल के स्थानों को स्त्री ग्रीष्म रूप होकर सर्वथा सोख लेती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3928.english_translation: Listen, O sage: the Puranas, the Vedas, and the saints say that woman is like spring for the forest of delusion. She is like summer, drying up all pools of austerity, vows, and discipline.
ramacharitamanas::3928.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / कह (say) / पुरान (Puranas) / श्रुति (Vedas) / संता (saints) / मोह (delusion) / बिपिन (forest) / कहुँ (for) / नारि (woman) / बसंता (spring) / जप (chanting) / तप (austerity) / नेम (vows) / जलाश्रय (water-sources) / झारी (pools) / होइ (becomes) / ग्रीषम (summer) / सोषइ (dries up) / सब (all) / नारी (woman)
ramacharitamanas::3928.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3928.essence: Desire can look like spring while secretly draining your strength.
ramacharitamanas::3928.simple_meaning: The verse warns that desire can quickly awaken delusion and drain away spiritual practice, vows, and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3928.simple_insight: It leaves you alert to how easily attraction can erode the habits that keep you steady.
ramacharitamanas::3928.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the teaching turns sharp and cautionary. The speaker invokes the authority of the Puranas, the Vedas, and the saints to warn that attraction can nourish delusion and dry up chanting, austerity, and vows. It is part of a larger argument about how the mind loses its footing.
ramacharitamanas::3928.modern_relevance: You open one message “just to check,” and an hour later your focus is gone. The pull did not look dangerous at first, but it quietly ate the day you had set aside for practice.
ramacharitamanas::3928.insight: It shifts attention from the pleasure of temptation to the damage it can do to your discipline.

ramacharitamanas::3929.verse_sanskrit: काम क्रोध मद मत्सर भेका। इन्हहि हरषप्रद बरषा एका॥ दुर्बासना कुमुद समुदाई। तिन्ह कहँ सरद सदा सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3929.verse_hindi: काम, क्रोध, मद और मत्सर (डाह) आदि मेंढक हैं। इनको वर्षा ऋतु होकर हर्ष प्रदान करने वाली एकमात्र यही (स्त्री) है। बुरी वासनाएँ कुमुदों के समूह हैं। उनको सदैव सुख देने वाली यह शरद् ऋतु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3929.english_translation: Lust, anger, pride, and jealousy are like frogs. For them, this is the one rain that brings delight. Evil desires are like clusters of water lilies, and this is the autumn season that always pleases them.
ramacharitamanas::3929.translation_literal: काम (desire) / क्रोध (anger) / मद (pride) / मत्सर (jealousy) / भेका (frogs) / इन्हहि (for these) / हरषप्रद (joy-giving) / बरषा (rainy season) / एका (only one) / दुर्बासना (evil desires) / कुमुद (water lilies) / समुदाई (clusters) / तिन्ह कहँ (for them) / सरद (autumn) / सदा (always) / सुखदाई (pleasing, soothing)
ramacharitamanas::3929.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3929.essence: Desires grow when you unknowingly keep watering them.
ramacharitamanas::3929.simple_meaning: Certain emotions and bad habits flourish under the right conditions. The verse compares desire, anger, pride, and jealousy to creatures or flowers that thrive in their own season.
ramacharitamanas::3929.simple_insight: You are not powerless before your habits; they weaken when you understand what feeds them.
ramacharitamanas::3929.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sages are explaining how delusion grows. After comparing desire to a season that nourishes confusion, this verse adds more images: harmful impulses spread like frogs in rain, and bad tendencies bloom like water lilies in the right weather.
ramacharitamanas::3929.modern_relevance: You open your phone at midnight and the same loop starts again: envy, craving, irritation. The verse points to a hard truth — some habits only grow when the conditions keep favoring them.
ramacharitamanas::3929.insight: It shifts attention from moral blame to pattern recognition: watch the conditions that strengthen reactive habits.

ramacharitamanas::3930.verse_sanskrit: धर्म सकल सरसीरुह बृंदा। होइ हिम तिन्हहि दहइ सुख मंदा॥ पुनि ममता जवास बहुताई। पलुहइ नारि सिसिर रितु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3930.verse_hindi: समस्त धर्म कमलों के झुंड हैं। यह नीच (विषयजन्य) सुख देने वाली स्त्री हिमऋतु होकर उन्हें जला डालती है। फिर ममतारूपी जवास का समूह (वन) स्त्री रूपी शिशिर ऋतु को पाकर हरा-भरा हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3930.english_translation: All virtues are like clusters of lotuses. Woman, as winter, burns them with the cold of low pleasure. Then the thicket of attachment grows green again when woman, like winter, arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3930.translation_literal: धर्म (virtue) / सकल (all) / सरसीरुह (lotuses) / बृंदा (clusters) / होइ (becomes) / हिम (frost, winter) / तिन्हहि (those) / दहइ (burns) / सुख (pleasure) / मंदा (low, slight)॥ / पुनि (again) / ममता (attachment) / जवास (javas grass / dry grass) / बहुताई (many) / पलुहइ (grows green) / नारि (woman) / सिसिर रितु (winter season) / पाई (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::3930.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3930.essence: Outer restraint can fail when attachment quietly returns.
ramacharitamanas::3930.simple_meaning: Virtues are delicate. When attachment and desire return, they can burn away good habits and make old cravings grow again.
ramacharitamanas::3930.simple_insight: It warns you not to mistake a calm phase for freedom; hidden attachment can revive quickly.
ramacharitamanas::3930.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building a vivid warning about desire in the forest teaching. After comparing woman to seasons that awaken lust and anger, he says even virtue can be scorched, while attachment grows back fast when temptation returns.
ramacharitamanas::3930.modern_relevance: You delete the app, feel clean for a week, then one familiar message pulls the old pattern back. What looked conquered was only resting.
ramacharitamanas::3930.insight: It shifts you from trusting temporary restraint to noticing the deeper pull of attachment.

ramacharitamanas::3931.verse_sanskrit: पाप उलूक निकर सुखकारी। नारि निबिड़ रजनी अँधियारी॥ बुधि बल सील सत्य सब मीना। बनसी सम त्रिय कहहिं प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3931.verse_hindi: पाप रूपी उल्लुओं के समूह के लिए यह स्त्री सुख देने वाली घोर अंधकारमयी रात्रि है। बुद्धि, बल, शील और सत्य- ये सब मछलियाँ हैं और उन (को फँसाकर नष्ट करने) के लिए स्त्री बंसी के समान है, चतुर पुरुष ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3931.english_translation: For the flock of sinful owls, a woman is a delighting, pitch-dark night. Wisdom, strength, virtue, and truth are all fish; clever people say a woman is like a fishing rod that catches and destroys them.
ramacharitamanas::3931.translation_literal: पाप (sinful) / उलूक (owls) / निकर (flock) / सुखकारी (delight-giving) / नारि (woman) / निबिड़ (dense) / रजनी (night) / अँधियारी (dark) // बुधि (wisdom) / बल (strength) / सील (virtue) / सत्य (truth) / सब (all) / मीना (fish) / बनसी (fishing rod) / सम (like) / त्रिय (woman) / कहहिं (say) / प्रबीना (the wise)
ramacharitamanas::3931.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3931.essence: Craving can turn your best qualities into easy prey.
ramacharitamanas::3931.simple_meaning: The verse uses harsh images to warn that desire for women can darken judgment and pull down wisdom, strength, character, and truth.
ramacharitamanas::3931.simple_insight: Unchecked desire can quietly swallow the best in you.
ramacharitamanas::3931.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the forest dialogue turns into a moral warning. The speaker compares lust-driven minds to owls and fish drawn into darkness and danger, saying that desire for women can trap wisdom, strength, character, and truth.
ramacharitamanas::3931.modern_relevance: You open one harmless-looking app and keep scrolling until your judgment feels dull. The verse warns that desire can quietly turn sharpness into helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::3931.insight: It shifts attention from attraction itself to the way craving can erode discernment and self-command.

ramacharitamanas::3932.verse_sanskrit: अवगुन मूल सूलप्रद प्रमदा सब दुख खानि। ताते कीन्ह निवारन मुनि मैं यह जियँ जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3932.verse_hindi: युवती स्त्री अवगुणों की मूल, पीड़ा देने वाली और सब दुःखों की खान है, इसलिए हे मुनि! मैंने जी में ऐसा जानकर तुमको विवाह करने से रोका था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3932.english_translation: Woman is the root of faults, a thorn that brings pain, and a mine of sorrow. Therefore, sage, I stopped you from marrying her, knowing this in my heart.
ramacharitamanas::3932.translation_literal: अवगुन (faults) / मूल (root) / सूलप्रद (pain-giving) / प्रमदा (woman) / सब (all) / दुख (sorrow) / खानि (mine) / ताते (therefore) / कीन्ह (did) / निवारन (stopping) / मुनि (sage) / मैं (I) / यह (this) / जियँ (in heart) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::3932.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3932.essence: What looks sweet can hide the seeds of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3932.simple_meaning: Desire can seem attractive, but it often becomes the source of suffering. The speaker says he warned the sage from marriage because he saw that danger clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3932.simple_insight: Not every attraction deserves trust; some desires quietly carry pain inside them.
ramacharitamanas::3932.detailed_meaning: In the forest dialogue, the speaker explains to the sage why he warned against marriage. The verse is part of a larger argument about attachment, desire, and the hidden cost of being pulled by attraction.
ramacharitamanas::3932.modern_relevance: You keep reopening a chat thread because the attention feels sweet, even while you know it leaves you drained. The pull itself can be the warning.
ramacharitamanas::3932.insight: It shifts attention from surface attraction to the hidden consequences of attachment.

ramacharitamanas::3933.verse_sanskrit: सुनि रघुपति के बचन सुहाए। मुनि तन पुलक नयन भरि आए॥ कहहु कवन प्रभु कै असि रीती। सेवक पर ममता अरु प्रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3933.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के सुंदर वचन सुनकर मुनि का शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल से) भर आए। (वे मन ही मन कहने लगे-) कहो तो किस प्रभु की ऐसी रीती है, जिसका सेवक पर इतना ममत्व और प्रेम हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3933.english_translation: Hearing the gracious words of Lord Raghupati, the sage’s body thrilled and his eyes filled with tears. He thought, “Tell me, what Lord has such a nature—so much affection and love for a servant?”
ramacharitamanas::3933.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / रघुपति के (of Raghupati's) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (gracious, lovely) / मुनि (the sage) / तन (body) / पुलक (with thrill) / नयन (eyes) / भरि आए (filled with tears) / कहहु (say) / कवन (which) / प्रभु (Lord) / कै (of) / असि (such) / रीती (nature, manner) / सेवक (servant) / पर (toward) / ममता (affection) / अरु (and) / प्रीती (love)
ramacharitamanas::3933.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3933.essence: Ram’s greatness is that he loves his servant like his own.
ramacharitamanas::3933.simple_meaning: Hearing Ram’s gentle words, the sage is overwhelmed with joy and tears. He realises that Ram loves and cares for a servant in a way no ordinary lord would.
ramacharitamanas::3933.simple_insight: Being loved by the divine can soften even the strongest heart.
ramacharitamanas::3933.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage has just heard Ram speak with unexpected tenderness. His body shivers with joy and his eyes fill with tears as he realises this is no distant ruler. Ram treats a servant with deep affection.
ramacharitamanas::3933.modern_relevance: You finally hear a message from someone you admire, and instead of distance, there is warmth. That shock of being seen changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3933.insight: It shifts devotion from duty alone to intimate trust in Ram’s loving attention.

ramacharitamanas::3934.verse_sanskrit: जे न भजहिं अस प्रभु भ्रम त्यागी। ग्यान रंक नर मंद अभागी॥ पुनि सादर बोले मुनि नारद। सुनहु राम बिग्यान बिसारद ॥
ramacharitamanas::3934.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य भ्रम को त्यागकर ऐसे प्रभु को नहीं भजते, वे ज्ञान के कंगाल, दुर्बुद्धि और अभागे हैं। फिर नारद मुनि आदर सहित बोले- हे विज्ञान-विशारद श्री रामजी! सुनिए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3934.english_translation: Those who, after giving up delusion, do not worship such a Lord are poor in wisdom, foolish, and unfortunate. Then Sage Narada spoke respectfully: "Listen, Ram, knower of all knowledge—"
ramacharitamanas::3934.translation_literal: जे (who) / न (not) / भजहिं (worship) / अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / भ्रम (delusion) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / ग्यान (wisdom) / रंक (poor) / नर (men) / मंद (dull) / अभागी (unfortunate) / पुनि (then) / सादर (respectfully) / बोले (spoke) / मुनि (sage) / नारद (Narada) / सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / बिग्यान (knowledge) / बिसारद (expert)
ramacharitamanas::3934.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::3934.essence: Clarity becomes complete only when it turns into worship.
ramacharitamanas::3934.simple_meaning: Even after seeing through confusion, a person who does not worship Ram remains spiritually poor. Narada then turns to Ram with deep reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3934.simple_insight: Knowing the truth is not enough; the heart still has to turn toward it.
ramacharitamanas::3934.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Narada is speaking to Ram after the earlier discussion about women and worldly attachment. He now says that even clear-minded people are unfortunate if they do not worship Ram. The moment shifts from moral critique into reverent address.
ramacharitamanas::3934.modern_relevance: You can understand your patterns in therapy, name your habits, and still stay unchanged if you never bow to what is higher than your ego. Insight without reverence can become another kind of pride.
ramacharitamanas::3934.insight: It shifts the mind from intellectual clarity alone to devotion as the living completion of understanding.

ramacharitamanas::3935.verse_sanskrit: संतन्ह के लच्छन रघुबीरा। कहहु नाथ भव भंजन भीरा॥ सुनु मुनि संतन्ह के गुन कहऊँ। जिन्ह ते मैं उन्ह कें बस रहऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3935.verse_hindi: हे रघुवीर! हे भव-भय (जन्म-मरण के भय) का नाश करने वाले मेरे नाथ! अब कृपा कर संतों के लक्षण कहिए! (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मुनि! सुनो, मैं संतों के गुणों को कहता हूँ, जिनके कारण मैं उनके वश में रहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3935.english_translation: O Raghuvir, destroyer of the fear of becoming and ceasing, please tell me the marks of holy people. The Lord said, "Listen, sage. I will tell you the qualities of the holy, through which I remain under their sway."
ramacharitamanas::3935.translation_literal: संतन्ह (of the holy ones) / के (of) / लच्छन (marks, qualities) / रघुबीरा (Raghuvir) / कहहु (tell) / नाथ (Lord) / भव (becoming and ceasing, worldly existence) / भंजन (destroyer) / भीरा (of fear) ॥ / सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / संतन्ह (of the holy ones) / के (of) / गुन (qualities) / कहऊँ (I will tell) / जिन्ह (through whom) / ते (because of) / मैं (I) / उन्ह (them) / कें (to) / बस (under control) / रहऊँ (remain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3935.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3935.essence: The pure heart can hold even the divine in loving sway.
ramacharitamanas::3935.simple_meaning: A sage asks Ram to describe the qualities of holy people. Ram answers that such people are so pure and devoted that even he stays under their influence.
ramacharitamanas::3935.simple_insight: Holiness is not weakness; it has a power that can soften even the highest heart.
ramacharitamanas::3935.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Narad asks Ram to explain what makes a saint. Ram does not begin with rules; he begins with reverence. He says the holy have such force that he himself remains under their influence, which turns sainthood into living devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3935.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room. They do not push, perform, or compete — yet you naturally want to be better around them. That quiet gravity is what Ram points to.
ramacharitamanas::3935.insight: It shifts respect from outer status to inner purity, showing that true influence comes from character, not power.

ramacharitamanas::3936.verse_sanskrit: षट बिकार जित अनघ अकामा। अचल अकिंचन सुचि सुखधामा॥ अमित बोध अनीह मितभोगी। सत्यसार कबि कोबिद जोगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3936.verse_hindi: वे संत (काम, क्रोध, लोभ, मोह, मद और मत्सर- इन) छह विकारों (दोषों) को जीते हुए, पापरहित, कामनारहित, निश्चल (स्थिरबुद्धि), अकिंचन (सर्वत्यागी), बाहर-भीतर से पवित्र, सुख के धाम, असीम ज्ञानवान् , इच्छारहित, मिताहारी, सत्यनिष्ठ, कवि, विद्वान, योगी, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3936.english_translation: Saints have conquered the six inner faults, are free from desire, steady, ownerless, and pure. They are homes of peace, boundless understanding, free of wanting, moderate in appetite, rooted in truth, and skilled as poets, scholars, and yogis.
ramacharitamanas::3936.translation_literal: षट (six) / बिकार (faults) / जित (conquered) / अनघ (sinless) / अकामा (without desire) / अचल (steady) / अकिंचन (without possessions) / सुचि (pure) / सुखधामा (abode of peace) / अमित (immeasurable) / बोध (understanding) / अनीह (without wanting) / मितभोगी (moderate eater) / सत्यसार (truth as essence) / कबि (poet) / कोबिद (scholar) / जोगी (yogi)
ramacharitamanas::3936.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3936.essence: True saintliness is freedom from craving, not just good behaviour.
ramacharitamanas::3936.simple_meaning: A saint has conquered the six inner faults and lives without craving, greed, or restlessness. Such a person is pure, steady, content, and rooted in truth.
ramacharitamanas::3936.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that real strength looks quiet, uncluttered, and free from need.
ramacharitamanas::3936.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Narad has asked Ram to describe the marks of true saints. Ram begins the answer by naming their inner victory: they have overcome the six faults, released desire, and become steady, pure, and content from within.
ramacharitamanas::3936.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose house is spotless, but their mind is crowded with wanting. This verse points to a different kind of cleanliness: a life with less grasping, less noise, and more steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3936.insight: It shifts attention from outer respectability to the inner discipline that makes a person trustworthy.

ramacharitamanas::3937.verse_sanskrit: सावधान मानद मदहीना। धीर धर्म गति परम प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3937.verse_hindi: सावधान, दूसरों को मान देने वाले, अभिमानरहित, धैर्यवान, धर्म के ज्ञान और आचरण में अत्यंत निपुण, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3937.english_translation: They are careful, respectful to others, free of pride, patient, and highly skilled in the ways of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3937.translation_literal: सावधान (careful) / मानद (giving honor) / मदहीना (without pride) / धीर (patient) / धर्म (dharma) / गति (way, conduct) / परम (supremely) / प्रबीना (skilled)
ramacharitamanas::3937.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3937.essence: True goodness is humble, patient, and alert in action.
ramacharitamanas::3937.simple_meaning: A true saint is careful, respectful, humble, patient, and deeply skilled in righteous conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3937.simple_insight: Real goodness is steady, humble, and disciplined — not loud or self-important.
ramacharitamanas::3937.detailed_meaning: Ram is answering the sage's question about the marks of holy people. He adds more traits to the picture: alertness, respect for others, humility, patience, and mastery in righteous conduct. This verse supports the larger description rather than standing alone.
ramacharitamanas::3937.modern_relevance: In a tense family conversation, you stay calm, listen fully, and refuse the urge to dominate. That quiet self-command is what this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::3937.insight: It shifts you from performative virtue to steady character shaped by restraint and respect.

ramacharitamanas::3938.verse_sanskrit: गुनागार संसार दुख रहित बिगत संदेह। तजि मम चरन सरोज प्रिय तिन्ह कहुँ देह न गेह ॥
ramacharitamanas::3938.verse_hindi: गुणों के घर, संसार के दुःखों से रहित और संदेहों से सर्वथा छूटे हुए होते हैं। मेरे चरण कमलों को छोड़कर उनको न देह ही प्रिय होती है, न घर ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3938.english_translation: They are treasure-houses of virtues, free from the sorrows of the world and completely beyond doubt. Leaving my lotus feet, neither body nor home is dear to them.
ramacharitamanas::3938.translation_literal: गुनागार (treasure-house of virtues) / संसार (world) / दुख (sorrow) / रहित (free from) / बिगत (gone beyond) / संदेह (doubt) / तजि (leaving) / मम (my) / चरन सरोज (lotus feet) / प्रिय (dear) / तिन्ह कहुँ (to them) / देह (body) / न गेह (nor home)
ramacharitamanas::3938.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3938.essence: Real devotion makes every other attachment feel small.
ramacharitamanas::3938.simple_meaning: Those who truly belong to Ram are full of good qualities, free from worldly sorrow and doubt, and no longer attached to body or home.
ramacharitamanas::3938.simple_insight: There is peace in wanting less, and freedom in letting Ram become your real shelter.
ramacharitamanas::3938.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shiva is describing the highest devotees to Parvati. These people have moved beyond fear, sorrow, and doubt. Their attachment has shifted so completely that body and home no longer matter beside Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3938.modern_relevance: You can be surrounded by comfort, yet still feel unrooted. The verse points to a deeper home: the place in your heart where anxiety loosens and your need to possess things falls away.
ramacharitamanas::3938.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual admiration to total inner belonging.

ramacharitamanas::3939.verse_sanskrit: निज गुन श्रवन सुनत सकुचाहीं। पर गुन सुनत अधिक हरषाहीं॥ सम सीतल नहिं त्यागहिं नीती। सरल सुभाउ सबहि सन प्रीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3939.verse_hindi: कानों से अपने गुण सुनने में सकुचाते हैं, दूसरों के गुण सुनने से विशेष हर्षित होते हैं। सम और शीतल हैं, न्याय का कभी त्याग नहीं करते। सरल स्वभाव होते हैं और सभी से प्रेम रखते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3939.english_translation: They feel shy hearing praise of their own virtues, but rejoice deeply hearing the virtues of others. They remain calm and balanced, never abandoning righteousness. Their nature is simple, and they love everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3939.translation_literal: निज (own) / गुन (virtues) / श्रवन (hearing) / सुनत (while hearing) / सकुचाहीं (feel shy) / पर (others') / गुन (virtues) / सुनत (hearing) / अधिक (more) / हरषाहीं (rejoice) / सम (balanced) / सीतल (cool/calm) / नहिं (do not) / त्यागहिं (abandon) / नीती (righteous conduct) / सरल (simple) / सुभाउ (nature) / सबहि (with everyone) / सन (with) / प्रीति (love)
ramacharitamanas::3939.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3939.essence: Humility makes room for others' goodness and keeps your heart steady.
ramacharitamanas::3939.simple_meaning: A truly noble person is humble about personal praise, happy about others' virtues, steady in conduct, and naturally loving toward everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3939.simple_insight: Real greatness feels warm, not defensive. It makes room for others without losing its own center.
ramacharitamanas::3939.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the sages are describing the qualities of those fit for Ram's grace. The focus is not on status or power, but on a heart that is humble, balanced, righteous, and open to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3939.modern_relevance: You hear someone else get praised in the team meeting, and instead of tightening up, you feel glad. That quiet generosity says more about your character than any self-promotion ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3939.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to open-heartedness, so praise becomes a chance to rejoice rather than compare.

ramacharitamanas::3940.verse_sanskrit: जप तप ब्रत दम संजम नेमा। गुरु गोबिंद बिप्र पद प्रेमा॥ श्रद्धा छमा मयत्री दाया। मुदिता मम पद प्रीति अमाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3940.verse_hindi: वे जप, तप, व्रत, दम, संयम और नियम में रत रहते हैं और गुरु, गोविंद तथा ब्राह्मणों के चरणों में प्रेम रखते हैं। उनमें श्रद्धा, क्षमा, मैत्री, दया, मुदिता (प्रसन्नता) और मेरे चरणों में निष्कपट प्रेम होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3940.english_translation: They live in japa, tapas, vows, self-restraint, discipline, and rules. They hold love for the teacher, the supreme being, and the learned, and they possess trust, forgiveness, friendship, compassion, joy, and pure love for my feet.
ramacharitamanas::3940.translation_literal: जप (recitation) / तप (austerity) / ब्रत (vows) / दम (self-restraint) / संजम (discipline) / नेमा (rules) / गुरु (the teacher) / गोबिंद (the supreme being) / बिप्र (learned ones) / पद (feet) / प्रेमा (love) / श्रद्धा (trust) / छमा (forgiveness) / मयत्री (friendship) / दाया (compassion) / मुदिता (joy) / मम (my) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / अमाया (without deceit)
ramacharitamanas::3940.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3940.essence: Devotion becomes visible as disciplined love and humane conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3940.simple_meaning: A devoted person lives with discipline, respect, trust, forgiveness, friendship, compassion, and joyful love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3940.simple_insight: Love for the divine is real when it changes how you treat everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3940.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram describes the qualities of true devotion. It is not just feeling, but a life shaped by discipline, humility, trust, and tender regard for the teacher, the learned, and the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3940.modern_relevance: You can say you believe deeply, but the truth shows up when you're patient with your partner, respectful with your mentor, and gentle with people who can offer you nothing back.
ramacharitamanas::3940.insight: It turns devotion into character: self-control, reverence, and compassionate conduct toward others.

ramacharitamanas::3941.verse_sanskrit: बिरति बिबेक बिनय बिग्याना। बोध जथारथ बेद पुराना॥ दंभ मान मद करहिं न काऊ। भूलि न देहिं कुमारग पाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3941.verse_hindi: तथा वैराग्य, विवेक, विनय, विज्ञान (परमात्मा के तत्व का ज्ञान) और वेद-पुराण का यथार्थ ज्ञान रहता है। वे दम्भ, अभिमान और मद कभी नहीं करते और भूलकर भी कुमार्ग पर पैर नहीं रखते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3941.english_translation: They possess renunciation, clear seeing, humility, and true understanding of the scriptures. They never act from pride, ego, or intoxication, and they do not step onto the wrong path even by mistake.
ramacharitamanas::3941.translation_literal: बिरति (renunciation) / बिबेक (clear seeing) / बिनय (humility) / बिग्याना (true understanding) / बोध (understanding) / जथारथ (as it is) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas) / दंभ (hypocrisy) / मान (pride) / मद (intoxication) / करहिं (do) / न (not) / काऊ (any) / भूलि (by mistake) / न देहिं (do not give) / कुमारग (wrong path) / पाऊ (step)
ramacharitamanas::3941.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3941.essence: Clear seeing makes pride and wrong action impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3941.simple_meaning: True understanding brings renunciation, humility, and steady conduct. Pride, ego, and intoxication fall away, and the wrong path is avoided.
ramacharitamanas::3941.simple_insight: Real wisdom changes behavior. It makes you simpler, humbler, and harder to mislead.
ramacharitamanas::3941.detailed_meaning: Ram is describing the qualities of a truly noble heart: renunciation, clear seeing, humility, and right understanding of the scriptures. Such a person does not boast, does not swell with ego, and does not drift into wrong action.
ramacharitamanas::3941.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, and the first temptation is to start performing your importance. This verse points to the quieter victory: staying humble, clear, and unhooked from ego.
ramacharitamanas::3941.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to steady discernment and clean conduct.

ramacharitamanas::3942.verse_sanskrit: गावहिं सुनहिं सदा मम लीला। हेतु रहित परहित रत सीला॥ मुनि सुनु साधुन्ह के गुन जेते। कहि न सकहिं सादर श्रुति तेते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3942.verse_hindi: सदा मेरी लीलाओं को गाते-सुनते हैं और बिना ही कारण दूसरों के हित में लगे रहने वाले होते हैं। हे मुनि! सुनो, संतों के जितने गुण हैं, उनको सरस्वती और वेद भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3942.english_translation: They always sing and hear My leelas, and remain ever engaged in selfless service to others. O sage, listen: the virtues of saints are so many that even Saraswati and the Vedas cannot fully describe them.
ramacharitamanas::3942.translation_literal: गावहिं (they sing) / सुनहिं (they hear) / सदा (always) / मम (My) / लीला (divine play) / हेतु (cause) / रहित (without) / परहित (others' good) / रत (engaged) / सीला (whose nature is) ॥ / मुनि (sage) / सुनु (listen) / साधुन्ह (of saints) / के (of) / गुन (virtues) / जेते (as many as) / कहि (say) / न (not) / सकहिं (can) / सादर (respectfully) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / तेते (those many) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3942.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3942.essence: True devotion sings Ram and serves others without asking why.
ramacharitamanas::3942.simple_meaning: Saints keep singing and hearing about Ram, and their nature is to help others without seeking a reason or reward. Their goodness is so vast it cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::3942.simple_insight: Devotion becomes real when it turns outward into service.
ramacharitamanas::3942.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram describes the saints who live by his remembrance. They keep singing his deeds, and their hearts naturally move toward the welfare of others. The verse expands into praise: their virtues are so many that even Saraswati and the Vedas cannot finish listing them.
ramacharitamanas::3942.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same prayer, name, or song while helping a friend move, cook, or sit through grief. That quiet combination of remembrance and service is what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::3942.insight: It links devotion to action: remembrance of Ram should show up as selfless care for other people.

ramacharitamanas::3943.verse_sanskrit: कहि सक न सारद सेष नारद सुनत पद पंकज गहे। अस दीनबंधु कृपाल अपने भगत गुन निज मुख कहे॥ सिरु नाइ बारहिं बार चरनन्हि ब्रह्मपुर नारद गए। ते धन्य तुलसीदास आस बिहाइ जे हरि रँग रँए॥
ramacharitamanas::3943.verse_hindi: 'शेष और शारदा भी नहीं कह सकते' यह सुनते ही नारदजी ने श्री रामजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए। दीनबंधु कृपालु प्रभु ने इस प्रकार अपने श्रीमुख से अपने भक्तों के गुण कहे। भगवान् के चरणों में बार-बार सिर नवाकर नारदजी ब्रह्मलोक को चले गए। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि वे पुरुष धन्य हैं, जो सब आशा छोड़कर केवल श्री हरि के रंग में रँग गए हैं।
ramacharitamanas::3943.english_translation: Shesha and Saraswati cannot fully tell it. Hearing this, Narada held Ram's lotus feet. The compassionate lord of the poor spoke the qualities of his devotees from his own mouth. Bowing again and again at those feet, Narada went to Brahmaloka. Blessed are those, says Tulsidas, who leave all hopes behind and are dyed only in Hari's love.
ramacharitamanas::3943.translation_literal: कहि सक (can say) / न (not) / सारद (Saraswati) / सेष (Shesha) / नारद (Narada) / सुनत (hearing) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / गहे (grasped) / अस (thus) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / कृपाल (compassionate) / अपने (his own) / भगत (devotees) / गुन (qualities) / निज मुख (own mouth) / कहे (spoke) / सिरु नाइ (bowing the head) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / ब्रह्मपुर (Brahmaloka) / नारद (Narada) / गए (went) / ते (those) / धन्य (blessed) / तुलसीदास (Tulsidas) / आस (hope) / बिहाइ (leaving behind) / जे (who) / हरि (Hari) / रँग (color) / रँए (are dyed)
ramacharitamanas::3943.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3943.essence: Total devotion begins when all other hopes fall away.
ramacharitamanas::3943.simple_meaning: Even the great sages cannot fully describe Ram's glory. Narada is overwhelmed, bows at Ram's feet, and Tulsidas blesses those who give up all other hopes and live only in loving remembrance of Hari.
ramacharitamanas::3943.simple_insight: There is peace in wanting nothing except closeness to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3943.detailed_meaning: After hearing that even Shesha, Saraswati, and Narada cannot fully describe Ram's greatness, Narada falls at Ram's lotus feet. Ram then speaks the qualities of his own devotees, and Tulsidas closes by blessing those who abandon every other hope and become wholly absorbed in Hari.
ramacharitamanas::3943.modern_relevance: You keep chasing the next fix, the next reply, the next plan, and still feel hungry. This verse points to a different fullness: the relief of wanting one thing so deeply that everything else loosens.
ramacharitamanas::3943.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered wanting to single-pointed devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3944.verse_sanskrit: रावनारि जसु पावन गावहिं सुनहिं जे लोग। राम भगति दृढ़ पावहिं बिनु बिराग जप जोग ॥
ramacharitamanas::3944.verse_hindi: जो लोग रावण के शत्रु श्री रामजी का पवित्र यश गावेंगे और सुनेंगे, वे वैराग्य, जप और योग के बिना ही श्री रामजी की दृढ़ भक्ति पावेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3944.english_translation: Those who sing and hear the pure fame of Ram, the enemy of Ravana, gain firm devotion to Ram without detachment, chanting, or yoga.
ramacharitamanas::3944.translation_literal: रावनारि (enemy of Ravana) / जसु (fame) / पावन (pure) / गावहिं (sing) / सुनहिं (hear) / जे (those who) / लोग (people) / राम (Ram) / भगति (devotion) / दृढ़ (firm) / पावहिं (obtain) / बिनु (without) / बिराग (detachment) / जप (chanting) / जोग (yoga)
ramacharitamanas::3944.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3944.essence: Ram’s glory can awaken firm devotion before any formal practice.
ramacharitamanas::3944.simple_meaning: Listening to and singing Ram's pure fame awakens strong devotion in you. You do not need special practices first; the story itself changes the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3944.simple_insight: Devotion can begin simply by listening with an open heart.
ramacharitamanas::3944.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas closes this stretch by praising Ram's name and fame. After Narad bows in wonder, the teaching turns outward: anyone who sings and hears Ram's pure glory can gain steady devotion, even before detachment, chanting, or yoga have fully formed.
ramacharitamanas::3944.modern_relevance: You put on a song that reminds you who you want to be, and something in you softens. Repeated, sincere listening can change your loyalties before you even notice it.
ramacharitamanas::3944.insight: It shifts the mind from forced spiritual effort to receptive remembrance that naturally deepens devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3945.verse_sanskrit: दीप सिखा सम जुबति तन मन जनि होसि पतंग। भजहि राम तजि काम मद करहि सदा सतसंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::3945.verse_hindi: युवती स्त्रियों का शरीर दीपक की लौ के समान है, हे मन! तू उसका पतिंगा न बन। काम और मद को छोड़कर श्री रामचंद्रजी का भजन कर और सदा सत्संग कर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3945.english_translation: The body of a young woman is like a lamp flame; mind, do not become a moth. Leave desire and pride, worship Ram, and keep good company always.
ramacharitamanas::3945.translation_literal: दीप (lamp) / सिखा (flame) / सम (like) / जुबति (young woman) / तन (body) / मन (mind) / जनि (do not) / होसि (become) / पतंग (moth) / भजहि (worship) / राम (Ram) / तजि (leaving) / काम (desire) / मद (pride/intoxication) / करहि (do) / सदा (always) / सतसंग (good company)
ramacharitamanas::3945.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3945.essence: What dazzles you can destroy you; Ram and good company protect you.
ramacharitamanas::3945.simple_meaning: Don't let desire pull you toward what will burn you. Turn your mind toward Ram, drop pride and craving, and stay with good company.
ramacharitamanas::3945.simple_insight: You can protect your heart by choosing what nourishes it instead of what dazzles it.
ramacharitamanas::3945.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, the story pauses for a sharp warning. After hearing Ram's praise, Tulsidas turns the reader away from desire and pride, using the image of a moth drawn to flame to urge devotion, restraint, and steady company.
ramacharitamanas::3945.modern_relevance: A message pops up, a photo catches your eye, and you feel the old pull to chase what looks exciting but leaves you emptier. This verse says: step back, choose what strengthens you, and stay in better company.
ramacharitamanas::3945.insight: It shifts attention from seductive impulse to disciplined devotion and supportive surroundings.

ramacharitamanas::3946.verse_sanskrit: कुन्देन्दीवरसुन्दरावतिबलौ विज्ञानधामावुभौ शोभाढ्यौ वरधन्विनौ श्रुतिनुतौ गोविप्रवृन्दप्रियौ। मायामानुषरूपिणौ रघुवरौ सद्धर्मवर्मौ हितौ सीतान्वेषणतत्परौ पथिगतौ भक्तिप्रदौ तौ हि नः ॥
ramacharitamanas::3946.verse_hindi: कुन्दपुष्प और नीलकमल के समान सुंदर गौर एवं श्यामवर्ण, अत्यंत बलवान् , विज्ञान के धाम, शोभा संपन्न, श्रेष्ठ धनुर्धर, वेदों के द्वारा वन्दित, गौ एवं ब्राह्मणों के समूह के प्रिय (अथवा प्रेमी), माया से मनुष्य रूप धारण किए हुए, श्रेष्ठ धर्म के लिए कवचस्वरूप, सबके हितकारी, श्री सीताजी की खोज में लगे हुए, पथिक रूप रघुकुल के श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी और श्री लक्ष्मणजी दोनों भाई निश्चय ही हमें भक्तिप्रद हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3946.english_translation: May the two brothers, Ram and Lakshman, beautiful like a white lotus and a blue lotus, immensely strong, abodes of wisdom, richly radiant, best among archers, praised by the Vedas, dear to cows and learned priests, taking human form through the veil of appearance, protectors of righteous conduct, benefactors of all, eager to search for Sita, and walking the path, surely grant us devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3946.translation_literal: कुन्देन्दीवरसुन्दरौ (beautiful like white lotus and blue lotus) / अतिबलौ (very strong) / विज्ञानधामौ (abodes of wisdom) / उभौ (both) / शोभाढ्यौ (richly radiant) / वरधन्विनौ (best archers) / श्रुतिनुतौ (praised by the Vedas) / गोविप्रवृन्दप्रियौ (dear to cows and groups of learned priests) / मायामानुषरूपिणौ (taking human form through appearance) / रघुवरौ (best of the Raghu clan) / सद्धर्मवर्मौ (shields of righteous conduct) / हितौ (beneficial) / सीतान्वेषणतत्परौ (eager in searching for Sita) / पथिगतौ (gone on the path) / भक्तिप्रदौ (givers of devotion) / तौ (those two) / हि (indeed) / नः (to us)
ramacharitamanas::3946.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3946.essence: Ram and Lakshman awaken devotion simply by who they are.
ramacharitamanas::3946.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are praised as beautiful, strong, righteous, and devoted to finding Sita. The verse asks them to bless the reader with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3946.simple_insight: True devotion feels like being carried by noble presence, not forced by effort alone.
ramacharitamanas::3946.detailed_meaning: At the start of Kishkindhakand, the poet turns from story to praise. Ram and Lakshman are described as radiant, strong, righteous, and already moving toward Sita's search. The verse becomes a prayer that their presence itself will awaken devotion in the listener.
ramacharitamanas::3946.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm strength changes the room before they speak. Their presence makes you want to be better, steadier, more devoted to what matters.
ramacharitamanas::3946.insight: It teaches you to see devotion as contagious: noble action and noble presence can awaken it in others.

ramacharitamanas::3947.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्माम्भोधिसमुद्भवं कलिमलप्रध्वंसनं चाव्ययं श्रीमच्छम्भुमुखेन्दुसुन्दरवरे संशोभितं सर्वदा। संसारामयभेषजं सुखकरं श्रीजानकीजीवनं धन्यास्ते कृतिनः पिबन्ति सततं श्रीरामनामामृतम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::3947.verse_hindi: वे सुकृती (पुण्यात्मा पुरुष) धन्य हैं जो वेद रूपी समुद्र (के मथने) से उत्पन्न हुए कलियुग के मल को सर्वथा नष्ट कर देने वाले, अविनाशी, भगवान श्री शंभु के सुंदर एवं श्रेष्ठ मुख रूपी चंद्रमा में सदा शोभायमान, जन्म-मरण रूपी रोग के औषध, सबको सुख देने वाले और श्री जानकीजी के जीवनस्वरूप श्री राम नाम रूपी अमृत का निरंतर पान करते रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3947.english_translation: Blessed are those wise souls who continually drink the nectar of Ram's name — born from the churning of the Vedas, forever destroying the stains of the age of darkness, ever-shining in Shiva's beautiful moonlike mouth, the medicine for the disease of worldly suffering, and the source of joy for Janaki's beloved.
ramacharitamanas::3947.translation_literal: ब्रह्माम्भोधि (the ocean of Brahman / the Vedas) / समुद्भवम् (born from) / कलिमलप्रध्वंसनम् (destroyer of the stains of the age of darkness) / च (and) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / श्रीमत्-शम्भु-मुख-इन्दु-सुन्दर-वरे (in the beautiful, श्रेष्ठ moon of Shiva's face) / संशोभितम् (shining, adorned) / सर्वदा (always) / संसार-आमय-भेषजम् (medicine for the sickness of worldly existence) / सुखकरम् (giver of joy) / श्री-जानकी-जीवनम् (life of Janaki) / धन्याः ते कृतिनः (blessed are those wise ones) / पिबन्ति (drink) / सततम् (continually) / श्री-राम-नाम-अमृतम् (the nectar of Ram's name)
ramacharitamanas::3947.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3947.essence: Ram's name is the cure you can keep taking forever.
ramacharitamanas::3947.simple_meaning: Ram's name is described as a healing nectar. It removes the darkness of the age, brings joy, and is praised as something wise people keep drinking again and again.
ramacharitamanas::3947.simple_insight: There is comfort in returning to one holy focus again and again.
ramacharitamanas::3947.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the poem pauses from the search and alliance to praise Ram's name itself. Tulsidas says it is not ordinary sound: it is healing, imperishable, joyful, and so precious that wise people keep drinking it without pause.
ramacharitamanas::3947.modern_relevance: You keep opening the same app, the same chat, the same distraction, hoping it will soothe you. This verse points to a different repetition — one that actually restores you instead of draining you.
ramacharitamanas::3947.insight: It shifts repetition from compulsion to nourishment, teaching you to return to what cleanses rather than what numbs.

ramacharitamanas::3948.verse_sanskrit: मुक्ति जन्म महि जानि ग्यान खान अघ हानि कर। जहँ बस संभु भवानि सो कासी सेइअ कस न ॥
ramacharitamanas::3948.verse_hindi: जहाँ श्री शिव-पार्वती बसते हैं, उस काशी को मुक्ति की जन्मभूमि, ज्ञान की खान और पापों का नाश करने वाली जानकर उसका सेवन क्यों न किया जाए?
ramacharitamanas::3948.english_translation: Knowing Kashi as the birthplace of freedom, a mine of wisdom, and the destroyer of sins, why would you not serve it, where Shiva and Bhavani dwell?
ramacharitamanas::3948.translation_literal: मुक्ति (freedom) / जन्म (birthplace) / महि (earth) / जानि (knowing) / ग्यान (wisdom) / खान (mine) / अघ (sins) / हानि (destruction) / कर (doing) / जहँ (where) / बस (dwell) / संभु (Shiva) / भवानि (Bhavani) / सो (that) / कासी (Kashi) / सेइअ (should be served) / कस (why) / न (not)
ramacharitamanas::3948.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3948.essence: A place becomes priceless when it holds freedom, wisdom, and divine presence.
ramacharitamanas::3948.simple_meaning: Kashi is praised as a sacred place where Shiva and Bhavani live, and where freedom, wisdom, and cleansing from wrongdoing are found. Such a place deserves your reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3948.simple_insight: Some places steady the heart just by being near them.
ramacharitamanas::3948.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas turns from describing Ram's glory to praising Kashi, the city where Shiva and Bhavani dwell. He calls it the home of freedom, wisdom, and cleansing, preparing the reader to revere Shiva as the next verse demands.
ramacharitamanas::3948.modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard after a brutal week, and your chest loosens before anyone speaks. Some places do not entertain you; they reset you.
ramacharitamanas::3948.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary geography to sacred presence and the transformation that comes from serving it.

ramacharitamanas::3949.verse_sanskrit: जरत सकल सुर बृंद बिषम गरल जेहिं पान किय। तेहि न भजसि मन मंद को कृपाल संकर सरिस॥
ramacharitamanas::3949.verse_hindi: जिस भीषण हलाहल विष से सब देवतागण जल रहे थे उसको जिन्होंने स्वयं पान कर लिया, रे मन्द मन! तू उन शंकरजी को क्यों नहीं भजता? उनके समान कृपालु (और) कौन है?
ramacharitamanas::3949.english_translation: Why don’t you worship Shankar, who drank the terrible poison that burned all the radiant beings? O dull mind, who is more compassionate than him?
ramacharitamanas::3949.translation_literal: जरत (burning) / सकल (all) / सुर बृंद (group of radiant beings) / बिषम (terrible) / गरल (poison) / जेहिं (by whom) / पान (drinking) / किय (was done) / तेहि (that one) / न (not) / भजसि (you worship) / मन (mind) / मंद (dull) / को (who) / कृपाल (compassionate) / संकर (Shankar) / सरिस (like)
ramacharitamanas::3949.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3949.essence: The one who carried poison for others deserves your worship.
ramacharitamanas::3949.simple_meaning: Shiva took the deadly poison for everyone’s sake, so the speaker asks why a dull mind would not worship him.
ramacharitamanas::3949.simple_insight: Real compassion is proven by what someone is willing to carry for others.
ramacharitamanas::3949.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand’s opening praise, Tulsidas turns from Kashi to Shiva’s mercy. He recalls the cosmic poison-drinking that saved the radiant beings and uses it as a reason to worship Shankar, the one who protected others at his own cost.
ramacharitamanas::3949.modern_relevance: You remember the person who stayed up all night with the sick child, while everyone else slept. That kind of care changes how you trust someone.
ramacharitamanas::3949.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract praise to recognising sacrificial care as the real measure of greatness.

ramacharitamanas::3950.verse_sanskrit: आगें चले बहुरि रघुराया। रिष्यमूक पर्बत निअराया॥ तहँ रह सचिव सहित सुग्रीवा। आवत देखि अतुल बल सींवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3950.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी फिर आगे चले। ऋष्यमूक पर्वत निकट आ गया। वहाँ (ऋष्यमूक पर्वत पर) मंत्रियों सहित सुग्रीव रहते थे। अतुलनीय बल की सीमा श्री रामचंद्रजी और लक्ष्मणजी को आते देखकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3950.english_translation: Raghunath moved ahead again. Rishyamuk Mountain came near. There Sugriva lived with his ministers. Seeing Ram and Lakshman coming, whose strength was unmatched—
ramacharitamanas::3950.translation_literal: आगें (ahead) / चले (moved) / बहुरि (again) / रघुराया (the lord of the Raghu line) / रिष्यमूक (Rishyamuk) / पर्बत (mountain) / निअराया (came near) / तहँ (there) / रह (lived) / सचिव (ministers) / सहित (with) / सुग्रीवा (Sugriva) / आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / अतुल (immeasurable) / बल (strength) / सींवा (Ram and Lakshman)
ramacharitamanas::3950.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3950.essence: Arrival can begin the turning point before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3950.simple_meaning: Ram moves closer to Rishyamuk Mountain, where Sugriva lives with his ministers. Sugriva sees Ram and Lakshman approaching, and their unmatched strength is immediately noticed.
ramacharitamanas::3950.simple_insight: The meeting is approaching, and both sides can already feel its weight.
ramacharitamanas::3950.detailed_meaning: Ram continues toward Rishyamuk Mountain, where Sugriva is hiding with his ministers. The sight of Ram and Lakshman approaching is enough to stir the whole scene, setting up the first contact between the exiled princes and the monkey king.
ramacharitamanas::3950.modern_relevance: You spot the person you’ve been waiting to meet across a crowded station platform. Nothing has been said yet, but the moment already feels decisive.
ramacharitamanas::3950.insight: It sets the stage for alliance by showing that arrival itself can change the mood of a whole place.

ramacharitamanas::3951.verse_sanskrit: अति सभीत कह सुनु हनुमाना। पुरुष जुगल बल रूप निधाना॥ धरि बटु रूप देखु तैं जाई। कहेसु जानि जियँ सयन बुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3951.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव अत्यंत भयभीत होकर बोले- हे हनुमान् ! सुनो, ये दोनों पुरुष बल और रूप के निधान हैं। तुम ब्रह्मचारी का रूप धारण करके जाकर देखो। अपने हृदय में उनकी यथार्थ बात जानकर मुझे इशारे से समझाकर कह देना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3951.english_translation: Sugriva, greatly afraid, said, “Listen, Hanuman. These two men are treasure-houses of strength and beauty. Go in the form of a celibate student, look at them, and understand their true nature in your heart; then tell me by sign.”
ramacharitamanas::3951.translation_literal: अति सभीत (greatly afraid) / कह (said) / सुनु (listen) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / पुरुष (men) / जुगल (two) / बल (strength) / रूप (beauty/form) / निधाना (treasure-houses)॥ धरि (taking) / बटु रूप (celibate-student form) / देखु (look) / तैं (you) / जाई (going) / कहेसु (say) / जानि (having known) / जियँ (in the heart) / सयन (by sign) / बुझाई (making understood) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3951.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3951.essence: Careful seeing comes before safe action.
ramacharitamanas::3951.simple_meaning: Sugriva, frightened, asks Hanuman to approach the two men in disguise, observe them carefully, understand who they really are, and report back silently.
ramacharitamanas::3951.simple_insight: Before you act, see clearly. Fear shrinks when you stop guessing and start observing.
ramacharitamanas::3951.detailed_meaning: At Rishyamukha, Sugriva sees two powerful strangers approaching and panics. He sends Hanuman in disguise to investigate first, trusting careful observation over impulse. The scene is a cautious test before alliance.
ramacharitamanas::3951.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with an unknown caller and your mind starts writing stories. Before you react, you check, listen, and understand what is actually there.
ramacharitamanas::3951.insight: It shifts the mind from fearful assumption to careful observation before response.

ramacharitamanas::3952.verse_sanskrit: पठए बालि होहिं मन मैला। भागौं तुरत तजौं यह सैला॥ बिप्र रूप धरि कपि तहँ गयऊ। माथ नाइ पूछत अस भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3952.verse_hindi: यदि वे मन के मलिन बालि के भेजे हुए हों तो मैं तुरंत ही इस पर्वत को छोड़कर भाग जाऊँ (यह सुनकर) हनुमान् जी ब्राह्मण का रूप धरकर वहाँ गए और मस्तक नवाकर इस प्रकार पूछने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3952.english_translation: If they are Bali's men, I will quickly flee this hill. Hanuman then took the form of a Brahmin, went there, bowed his head, and began to ask in fear.
ramacharitamanas::3952.translation_literal: पठए (sent by) / बालि (Bali) / होहिं (are) / मन (mind) / मैला (tainted) / भागौं (I flee) / तुरत (quickly) / तजौं (leave) / यह (this) / सैला (hill) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / रूप (form) / धरि (taking) / कपि (monkey) / तहँ (there) / गयऊ (went) / माथ (head) / नाइ (bowing) / पूछत (asking) / अस (thus) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::3952.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3952.essence: Careful disguise can open a door that fear would keep shut.
ramacharitamanas::3952.simple_meaning: Sugriva fears strangers and Hanuman goes to meet them in a harmless disguise. The verse shows caution, quick thinking, and careful approach.
ramacharitamanas::3952.simple_insight: Not every approach is direct; sometimes wisdom enters quietly and respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::3952.detailed_meaning: On Rishyamukha hill, Sugriva sees the two warriors approaching and panics, fearing they may be Bali's agents. Hanuman responds by changing into a Brahmin's form, bowing, and going to question them carefully.
ramacharitamanas::3952.modern_relevance: You spot two unfamiliar people at the edge of a tense meeting, and your first instinct is to protect yourself. The verse shows the value of cautious, respectful inquiry before you reveal too much.
ramacharitamanas::3952.insight: It teaches you to assess danger first, then approach with tact instead of raw suspicion.

ramacharitamanas::3953.verse_sanskrit: को तुम्ह स्यामल गौर सरीरा। छत्री रूप फिरहु बन बीरा ॥ कठिन भूमि कोमल पद गामी। कवन हेतु बिचरहु बन स्वामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3953.verse_hindi: हे वीर! साँवले और गोरे शरीर वाले आप कौन हैं, जो क्षत्रिय के रूप में वन में फिर रहे हैं? हे स्वामी! कठोर भूमि पर कोमल चरणों से चलने वाले आप किस कारण वन में विचर रहे हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3953.english_translation: O hero, who are you, with dark and fair bodies, wandering the forest in a warrior's form? O master, why do you move through the forest with soft feet on hard ground?
ramacharitamanas::3953.translation_literal: को (who) / तुम्ह (you) / स्यामल (dark-complexioned) / गौर (fair-complexioned) / सरीरा (bodies) / छत्री (warrior) / रूप (form) / फिरहु (wander) / बन (forest) / बीरा (hero) ॥ कठिन (hard) / भूमि (ground) / कोमल (soft) / पद (feet) / गामी (moving) / कवन (what) / हेतु (reason) / बिचरहु (wander) / बन (forest) / स्वामी (master) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3953.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3953.essence: A stranger's grace can make even fear pause and ask questions.
ramacharitamanas::3953.simple_meaning: Sugriva asks the strangers who they are, why they look so noble, and why they are walking in the forest like princes.
ramacharitamanas::3953.simple_insight: Curiosity can open the door before trust does.
ramacharitamanas::3953.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is terrified and cautious as Hanuman approaches two unknown men in the forest. Seeing their beauty, warrior bearing, and gentle feet, he wonders who they are and why they have come there.
ramacharitamanas::3953.modern_relevance: You notice someone polished and out of place in a rough situation, and your first instinct is to ask: who are they, really?
ramacharitamanas::3953.insight: It frames the meeting as cautious recognition, not instant trust.

ramacharitamanas::3954.verse_sanskrit: मृदुल मनोहर सुंदर गाता। सहत दुसह बन आतप बाता ॥ की तुम्ह तीनि देव महँ कोऊ। नर नारायन की तुम्ह दोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3954.verse_hindi: मन को हरण करने वाले आपके सुंदर, कोमल अंग हैं और आप वन के दुःसह धूप और वायु को सह रहे हैं क्या आप ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महेश- इन तीन देवताओं में से कोई हैं या आप दोनों नर और नारायण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3954.english_translation: Your body is soft and beautiful, yet you endure the unbearable heat and wind of the forest. Are you one among the three radiant beings, or are you both Nara and Narayana?
ramacharitamanas::3954.translation_literal: मृदुल (soft) / मनोहर (delightful) / सुंदर (beautiful) / गाता (body) / सहत (enduring) / दुसह (unbearable) / बन (forest) / आतप (heat) / बाता (wind) / की (whether) / तुम्ह (you) / तीनि (three) / देव (radiant beings) / महँ (among) / कोऊ (someone) / नर (Nara) / नारायन (Narayana) / की (or) / तुम्ह (you) / दोऊ (both)
ramacharitamanas::3954.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3954.essence: True greatness can look soft while enduring what breaks others.
ramacharitamanas::3954.simple_meaning: The speaker sees a stranger whose beautiful body is enduring the forest's harsh conditions and wonders whether he is a radiant being or a divine incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::3954.simple_insight: Some presence is so steady and beautiful that it makes ordinary categories feel too small.
ramacharitamanas::3954.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has approached the disguised Ram and Lakshman in the forest. Seeing their beauty, calm, and endurance in the heat and wind, he begins to suspect they are no ordinary men. His question opens the way to recognition.
ramacharitamanas::3954.modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays gentle under pressure, never showing the strain. Their steadiness makes you wonder what kind of strength they are drawing from.
ramacharitamanas::3954.insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to the quiet power that lets someone remain graceful under hardship.

ramacharitamanas::3955.verse_sanskrit: जग कारन तारन भव भंजन धरनी भार। की तुम्ह अखिल भुवन पति लीन्ह मनुज अवतार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3955.verse_hindi: अथवा आप जगत् के मूल कारण और संपूर्ण लोकों के स्वामी स्वयं भगवान् हैं, जिन्होंने लोगों को भवसागर से पार उतारने तथा पृथ्वी का भार नष्ट करने के लिए मनुष्य रूप में अवतार लिया है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3955.english_translation: Or are you the original cause of the world, the lord of all worlds, who has taken human form to carry beings across the cycle of suffering and relieve the earth's burden?
ramacharitamanas::3955.translation_literal: जग (world) / कारन (cause) / तारन (to carry across) / भव (cycle of suffering) / भंजन (destroyer) / धरनी (earth) / भार (burden) / की (or) / तुम्ह (you) / अखिल (all) / भुवन (worlds) / पति (lord) / लीन्ह (took) / मनुज (human) / अवतार (incarnation)
ramacharitamanas::3955.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3955.essence: The divine may arrive looking entirely human.
ramacharitamanas::3955.simple_meaning: Hanuman wonders if this stranger is actually the supreme being who has taken human form to rescue beings and relieve the world's burden.
ramacharitamanas::3955.simple_insight: Recognition itself becomes devotion when you begin to see greatness hidden in ordinary human form.
ramacharitamanas::3955.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman meets the two brothers in the forest and is struck by their radiance, gentleness, and strength. He moves from curiosity to reverence, wondering whether this is the supreme being who has come as a human to restore the world.
ramacharitamanas::3955.modern_relevance: You meet someone quiet in a crowded room, and something about them feels larger than their role. This verse captures that moment when respect turns into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3955.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to hidden divine identity in human form.

ramacharitamanas::3956.verse_sanskrit: कोसलेस दसरथ के जाए। हम पितु बचन मानि बन आए॥ नाम राम लछिमन दोउ भाई। संग नारि सुकुमारि सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3956.verse_hindi: (श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा-) हम कोसलराज दशरथजी के पुत्र हैं और पिता का वचन मानकर वन आए हैं। हमारे राम-लक्ष्मण नाम हैं, हम दोनों भाई हैं। हमारे साथ सुंदर सुकुमारी स्त्री थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3956.english_translation: We are Dasharath's sons from Kosala, and we came to the forest obeying our father's command. Our names are Ram and Lakshman, the two brothers. A beautiful, gentle woman was with us.
ramacharitamanas::3956.translation_literal: कोसलेस (lord of Kosala) / दसरथ के जाए (born of Dasharath) / हम (we) / पितु (father's) / बचन (word) / मानि (having obeyed) / बन (forest) / आए (came) ॥ / नाम (names) / राम (Ram) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / संग (with) / नारि (woman) / सुकुमारि (delicate) / सुहाई (beautiful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3956.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3956.essence: Keeping your father's word can define your path more than a crown ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3956.simple_meaning: Ram identifies himself and Lakshman as Dasharath's sons who came to the forest because they obeyed their father's command, with Sita accompanying them.
ramacharitamanas::3956.simple_insight: Keeping a hard promise can cost you dearly, but it also reveals who you are.
