ramacharitamanas::3956.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman first meets the disguised brothers and tests who they are. Ram answers simply: he is Dasharath's son, in the forest because he obeyed his father's word, and Sita was with them. The line quietly reveals exile, duty, and loss.
ramacharitamanas::3956.modern_relevance: You leave for the airport with a packed bag and a heavy chest because you promised you would show up. No applause, no reward — just the weight of keeping your word.
ramacharitamanas::3956.insight: It shifts attention from self-presentation to faithful action under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3957.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ हरी निसिचर बैदेही। बिप्र फिरहिं हम खोजत तेही॥ आपन चरित कहा हम गाई। कहहु बिप्र निज कथा बुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3957.verse_hindi: यहाँ (वन में) राक्षस ने (मेरी पत्नी) जानकी को हर लिया। हे ब्राह्मण! हम उसे ही खोजते फिरते हैं। हमने तो अपना चरित्र कह सुनाया। अब हे ब्राह्मण! अपनी कथा समझाकर कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3957.english_translation: Here in the forest, a demon has carried off Sita. We keep searching for her. We have told our own story; now, noble one, please tell us yours and help us understand.
ramacharitamanas::3957.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / हरी (Hari, the divine) / निसिचर (demon) / बैदेही (Sita) / बिप्र (brāhmin) / फिरहिं (wander) / हम (we) / खोजत (searching) / तेही (that one) / आपन (our own) / चरित (story / conduct) / कहा (told) / हम (we) / गाई (sang) / कहहु (tell) / बिप्र (brāhmin) / निज (your own) / कथा (story) / बुझाई (explaining) /
ramacharitamanas::3957.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3957.simple_meaning: Ram explains that Sita has been taken by a demon and that he is searching for her. He asks the stranger to share his own story too.
ramacharitamanas::3957.simple_insight: Even in grief, you can still meet others with openness.
ramacharitamanas::3957.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram has reached the forest while searching for Sita. He speaks to a disguised Hanuman, calmly naming his loss and inviting the stranger to speak. This is the moment before friendship and help begin.
ramacharitamanas::3957.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a train station while carrying private heartbreak. Even then, you can still speak honestly and invite the other person to be real too.
ramacharitamanas::3957.insight: It teaches you to name your situation plainly, without shutting down curiosity about the person in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::3958.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पहिचानि परेउ गहि चरना। सो सुख उमा जाइ नहिं बरना॥ पुलकित तन मुख आव न बचना। देखत रुचिर बेष कै रचना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3958.verse_hindi: प्रभु को पहचानकर हनुमान् जी उनके चरण पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े (उन्होंने साष्टांग दंडवत् प्रणाम किया)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! वह सुख वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। शरीर पुलकित है, मुख से वचन नहीं निकलता। वे प्रभु के सुंदर वेष की रचना देख रहे हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3958.english_translation: Recognizing the Lord, he fell at his feet and held them fast. O Uma, that joy cannot be described. His body thrilled, his voice would not come, and he gazed at the Lord's beautiful form.
ramacharitamanas::3958.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / पहिचानि (having recognized) / परेउ (fell) / गहि (grasping) / चरना (the feet) / सो (that) / सुख (joy) / उमा (Uma) / जाइ (goes) / नहिं (not) / बरना (to describe) / पुलकित (thrilled) / तन (body) / मुख (mouth) / आव (comes) / न (not) / बचना (speech) / देखत (seeing) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बेष (form) / कै (of) / रचना (arrangement)
ramacharitamanas::3958.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3958.essence: Recognizing the Lord leaves you speechless and bowed.
ramacharitamanas::3958.simple_meaning: Hanuman recognizes Ram and falls at his feet in overwhelming joy. The sight leaves him speechless, trembling, and completely absorbed.
ramacharitamanas::3958.simple_insight: Real devotion doesn’t need performance. It moves the whole body before the mind can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::3958.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman finally sees Ram and Lakshman after searching for the Lord’s presence through Sugriva’s world. The recognition is instant and total: he drops at Ram’s feet, overwhelmed beyond speech. Shiva tells Parvati that this joy cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::3958.modern_relevance: You meet someone you have admired from afar, and the room suddenly feels different. The rehearsed words disappear, and all that remains is awe, relief, and the urge to bow inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::3958.insight: It shifts devotion from thought to embodied response — recognition becomes humility, stillness, and praise.

ramacharitamanas::3959.verse_sanskrit: पुनि धीरजु धरि अस्तुति कीन्ही। हरष हृदयँ निज नाथहि चीन्ही॥ मोर न्याउ मैं पूछा साईं। तुम्ह पूछहु कस नर की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3959.verse_hindi: फिर धीरज धर कर स्तुति की। अपने नाथ को पहचान लेने से हृदय में हर्ष हो रहा है। (फिर हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे स्वामी! मैंने जो पूछा वह मेरा पूछना तो न्याय था, (वर्षों के बाद आपको देखा, वह भी तपस्वी के वेष में और मेरी वानरी बुद्धि इससे मैं तो आपको पहचान न सका और अपनी परिस्थिति के अनुसार मैंने आपसे पूछा), परंतु आप मनुष्य की तरह कैसे पूछ रहे हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3959.english_translation: After calming himself, he offered praise. Joy rose in his heart as he recognized his own Lord. "My question was fair, my Lord. But why are you asking like an ordinary man?"
ramacharitamanas::3959.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / धीरजु (patience, composure) / धरि (having held) / अस्तुति (praise) / कीन्ही (did) / हरष (joy) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / निज (own) / नाथहि (lord) / चीन्ही (recognized)॥ / मोर (my) / न्याउ (question, fairness) / मैं (I) / पूछा (asked) / साईं (lord) / तुम्ह (you) / पूछहु (ask) / कस (how) / नर (a man) / की नाईं (like)॥
ramacharitamanas::3959.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3959.essence: Knowing the Lord turns hesitation into praise.
ramacharitamanas::3959.simple_meaning: Hanuman calms himself, praises Ram, and feels joy at recognizing his own Lord. He then says his earlier question was reasonable, but Ram is speaking like an ordinary man.
ramacharitamanas::3959.simple_insight: Recognition can transform confusion into devotion in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::3959.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has just realized that the traveler before him is Ram. After bowing, he steadies himself, praises Ram, and speaks with delighted humility. The moment matters because first contact becomes worship.
ramacharitamanas::3959.modern_relevance: You finally understand the person in front of you is the one you were looking for. The tension drops, your chest opens, and even your awkward question feels forgiven.
ramacharitamanas::3959.insight: It shifts attention from social formality to reverent recognition of what is truly present.

ramacharitamanas::3960.verse_sanskrit: तव माया बस फिरउँ भुलाना। ताते मैं नहिं प्रभु पहिचाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3960.verse_hindi: मैं तो आपकी माया के वश भूला फिरता हूँ इसी से मैंने अपने स्वामी (आप) को नहीं पहचाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3960.english_translation: I wander lost under your veil of appearance, and because of that I did not recognize you, Lord.
ramacharitamanas::3960.translation_literal: तव (your) / माया (veil of appearance) / बस (under the control of) / फिरउँ (I wander) / भुलाना (lost, forgetting) / ताते (because of that) / मैं (I) / नहिं (did not) / प्रभु (Lord) / पहिचाना (recognize)
ramacharitamanas::3960.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3960.essence: Confusion can hide even the one you most need to see.
ramacharitamanas::3960.simple_meaning: Hanuman admits that he failed to recognize Ram because he was caught in the divine veil of appearance and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3960.simple_insight: Even devotion can begin in confusion, and honesty opens the way to recognition.
ramacharitamanas::3960.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just realized that the stranger before him is Ram. In awe and humility, he explains why he did not see it sooner: Ram's veil of appearance had kept him wandering in forgetfulness. The moment turns recognition into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3960.modern_relevance: You stare at a message from someone you care about and still miss what they mean because your own confusion is louder. Sometimes the obstacle is not the person in front of you, but the haze you are carrying.
ramacharitamanas::3960.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to humility, showing that clear seeing can arrive only when confusion is admitted.

ramacharitamanas::3961.verse_sanskrit: एकु मैं मंद मोहबस कुटिल हृदय अग्यान। पुनि प्रभु मोहि बिसारेउ दीनबंधु भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3961.verse_hindi: एक तो मैं यों ही मंद हूँ, दूसरे मोह के वश में हूँ, तीसरे हृदय का कुटिल और अज्ञान हूँ, फिर हे दीनबंधु भगवान् ! प्रभु (आप) ने भी मुझे भुला दिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3961.english_translation: I am dull, deluded, crooked of heart, and ignorant; and yet, O Lord of the lowly, you too have forgotten me.
ramacharitamanas::3961.translation_literal: एकु (one) / मैं (I) / मंद (dull) / मोहबस (under the grip of delusion) / कुटिल (crooked) / हृदय (heart) / अग्यान (ignorant) / पुनि (again) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोहि (me) / बिसारेउ (forgot) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / भगवान (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::3961.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3961.essence: Even your forgetting cannot erase Ram's remembrance of you.
ramacharitamanas::3961.simple_meaning: Hanuman admits his own dullness, delusion, crooked heart, and ignorance, yet still says that Ram did not forget him.
ramacharitamanas::3961.simple_insight: Your weakness does not cancel divine care.
ramacharitamanas::3961.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has just regained recognition and is pouring out humble devotion to Ram. He confesses his own confusion and faults, then marvels that the Lord of the lowly still remembered him despite everything.
ramacharitamanas::3961.modern_relevance: You sent the apology after days of avoiding the message, convinced you had ruined everything. This verse says the deeper bond may still hold even when you feel unworthy.
ramacharitamanas::3961.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to grateful trust in a mercy that outlasts your mistakes.

ramacharitamanas::3962.verse_sanskrit: जदपि नाथ बहु अवगुन मोरें। सेवक प्रभुहि परै जनि भोरें॥ नाथ जीव तव मायाँ मोहा। सो निस्तरइ तुम्हारेहिं छोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3962.verse_hindi: एहे नाथ! यद्यपि मुझ में बहुत से अवगुण हैं, तथापि सेवक स्वामी की विस्मृति में न पड़े (आप उसे न भूल जाएँ)। हे नाथ! जीव आपकी माया से मोहित है। वह आप ही की कृपा से निस्तार पा सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3962.english_translation: Even though I have many faults, Lord, do not let your servant be forgotten. Lord, a living being is deluded by your veil of appearance. That being can cross beyond only through your grace.
ramacharitamanas::3962.translation_literal: जदपि (although) / नाथ (Lord) / बहु (many) / अवगुन (faults) / मोरें (in me) / सेवक (servant) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / परै (falls) / जनि (do not) / भोरें (into forgetting) ॥ नाथ (Lord) / जीव (living being) / तव (your) / मायाँ (veil of appearance) / मोहा (deluded) / सो (that one) / निस्तरइ (crosses beyond) / तुम्हारेहिं (only by your) / छोहा (grace) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3962.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3962.essence: Faults do not block grace; grace is what carries you through.
ramacharitamanas::3962.simple_meaning: Hanuman admits his faults and asks Ram not to forget him. He says every living being is confused by the veil of appearance and can cross beyond it only through Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::3962.simple_insight: You do not need to be flawless to be held. Grace is stronger than confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3962.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman stands before Ram after confessing his confusion and forgetfulness. He now turns that humility into prayer: even with many faults, the servant should not be abandoned, because only Ram's grace can free a being trapped by appearance.
ramacharitamanas::3962.modern_relevance: You miss the deadline, forget the message, and still feel ashamed to ask for help. This verse says your flaws do not cancel your worth; what lifts you out is still grace.
ramacharitamanas::3962.insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to humble reliance on grace.

ramacharitamanas::3963.verse_sanskrit: ता पर मैं रघुबीर दोहाई। जानउँ नहिं कछु भजन उपाई॥ सेवक सुत पति मातु भरोसें। रहइ असोच बनइ प्रभु पोसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3963.verse_hindi: उस पर हे रघुवीर! मैं आपकी दुहाई (शपथ) करके कहता हूँ कि मैं भजन-साधन कुछ नहीं जानता। सेवक स्वामी के और पुत्र माता के भरोसे निश्चिंत रहता है। प्रभु को सेवक का पालन-पोषण करते ही बनता है (करना ही पड़ता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3963.english_translation: Then, O Raghubir, I swear by you: I do not know any way of devotion. A servant rests in the trust of the master, a son in the trust of the mother. So the Lord must sustain the servant.
ramacharitamanas::3963.translation_literal: ता पर (then upon that) / मैं (I) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / दोहाई (appeal; oath) / जानउँ नहिं (I do not know) / कछु (any) / भजन (devotion; worship) / उपाई (means; way) ॥ सेवक (servant) / सुत (son) / पति (master; husband) / मातु (mother) / भरोसें (in trust; relying) / रहइ (remains) / असोच (free from worry) / बनइ (is fitting; is right) / प्रभु (Lord; master) / पोसें (by sustaining; by nurturing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3963.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3963.essence: Real devotion begins when you stop pretending you can carry yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3963.simple_meaning: Hanuman admits he does not know any special method of devotion. He says a servant lives by the master's care, just as a child lives by the mother's care.
ramacharitamanas::3963.simple_insight: Devotion can begin with humility: you do not have to manage everything yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3963.detailed_meaning: Hanuman stands before Ram after crossing into Lanka, speaking with total humility. He says he has no clever method to offer, only dependence. Like a servant, son, or child, he trusts Ram to provide what he cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3963.modern_relevance: You are sitting in the car outside the hospital, too tired to hold yourself together. This verse gives you permission to stop performing control and lean into care.
ramacharitamanas::3963.insight: It shifts devotion from technique to dependence, from self-management to trust in Ram's care.

ramacharitamanas::3964.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि परेउ चरन अकुलाई। निज तनु प्रगटि प्रीति उर छाई॥ तब रघुपति उठाई उर लावा। निज लोचन जल सींचि जुड़ावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3964.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर हनुमान् जी अकुलाकर प्रभु के चरणों पर गिर पड़े, उन्होंने अपना असली शरीर प्रकट कर दिया। उनके हृदय में प्रेम छा गया। तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने उन्हें उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और अपने नेत्रों के जल से सींचकर शीतल किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3964.english_translation: Having said this, Hanuman fell in agitation at the Lord's feet. He revealed his true form, and love filled his heart. Then Raghupati lifted him into his arms, embraced him to his chest, and soothed him with the water of his own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::3964.translation_literal: अस कहि (having said this) / परेउ (fell) / चरन (feet) / अकुलाई (in agitation) / निज तनु (his own body) / प्रगटि (revealing) / प्रीति (love) / उर (heart) / छाई (spread) / तब (then) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / उठाई (lifting) / उर (to chest/heart) / लावा (embraced) / निज लोचन (his own eyes) / जल (water) / सींचि (sprinkling) / जुड़ावा (soothed/coolly comforted)
ramacharitamanas::3964.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3964.essence: The one who falls in love with Ram is gathered, not rejected.
ramacharitamanas::3964.simple_meaning: Hanuman overflows with devotion and falls at Ram's feet. Ram responds with tenderness, lifting him up and comforting him like a beloved child.
ramacharitamanas::3964.simple_insight: Pure devotion does not leave you crushed; it draws you into closeness and care.
ramacharitamanas::3964.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has just spoken with complete humility before Ram. Overcome, he drops at Ram's feet and reveals his true form. Ram does not stay distant; he lifts Hanuman, hugs him to his heart, and comforts him with tears.
ramacharitamanas::3964.modern_relevance: After a hard apology, you expect cold silence. Instead, the person you feared most reaches out, holds your shoulder, and lets the tension break. That is the warmth this verse carries.
ramacharitamanas::3964.insight: It shifts devotion from self-effacement to intimate belonging: surrender is met by embrace, not distance.

ramacharitamanas::3965.verse_sanskrit: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3965.verse_hindi: (फिर कहा-) हे कपि! सुनो, मन में ग्लानि मत मानना (मन छोटा न करना)। तुम मुझे लक्ष्मण से भी दूने प्रिय हो। सब कोई मुझे समदर्शी कहते हैं (मेरे लिए न कोई प्रिय है न अप्रिय) पर मुझको सेवक प्रिय है, क्योंकि वह अनन्यगति होता है (मुझे छोड़कर उसको कोई दूसरा सहारा नहीं होता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3965.english_translation: Listen, monkey, do not feel small in your heart. You are dearer to me than Lakshman. Everyone says I am equal to all, but I especially love the servant who has no other refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3965.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / कपि (monkey) / जियँ (in heart) / मानसि (mentally) / जनि (do not) / ऊना (lessened) / तैं (you) / मम (my) / प्रिय (dear) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / ते (than) / दूना (twice) ॥ समदरसी (equal-seeing) / मोहि (me) / कह (say) / सब (all) / कोऊ (everyone) / सेवक (servant) / प्रिय (dear) / अनन्य (without another refuge) / गति (support/refuge) / सोऊ (that one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3965.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3965.essence: Single-hearted dependence draws the closest love.
ramacharitamanas::3965.simple_meaning: Ram reassures Hanuman that he should not feel lesser. He says Hanuman is even dearer to him than Lakshman, and that he especially values a servant who has nowhere else to turn.
ramacharitamanas::3965.simple_insight: Being small before the divine is not a weakness; it is what opens the deepest closeness.
ramacharitamanas::3965.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just fallen at Ram's feet and confessed that he knows no path except devotion. Ram answers with tenderness, lifting his fear before it can harden into shame. In this moment, Ram reveals what he values most: not pride, but single-hearted refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3965.modern_relevance: You finally admit you don't have it all together, and someone answers with warmth instead of judgment. That is the kind of closeness this verse points to.
ramacharitamanas::3965.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to dependence: the less divided your refuge, the nearer you are held.

ramacharitamanas::3966.verse_sanskrit: सो अनन्य जाकें असि मति न टरइ हनुमंत। मैं सेवक सचराचर रूप स्वामि भगवंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3966.verse_hindi: और हे हनुमान् ! अनन्य वही है जिसकी ऐसी बुद्धि कभी नहीं टलती कि मैं सेवक हूँ और यह चराचर (जड़-चेतन) जगत् मेरे स्वामी भगवान् का रूप है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3966.english_translation: O Hanuman, only that person is truly devoted whose mind never wavers from this understanding: “I am the servant, and the moving and unmoving world is the form of the Lord.”
ramacharitamanas::3966.translation_literal: सो (that) / अनन्य (one-pointed, devoted) / जाकें (for whom) / असि (such) / मति (understanding) / न टरइ (does not waver) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / मैं (I) / सेवक (servant) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / रूप (form) / स्वामि (lord) / भगवंत (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::3966.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3966.essence: One-pointed devotion sees everything as the Lord's form and the self as servant.
ramacharitamanas::3966.simple_meaning: True devotion stays steady in one insight: you are a servant, and everything around you belongs to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3966.simple_insight: Humility becomes freedom when you stop centering yourself and start seeing the divine in all things.
ramacharitamanas::3966.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just bowed before Ram in Kishkindhakand. Ram responds by naming the heart of one-pointed devotion: the mind that never forgets, even for a moment, “I am the servant, and all existence is the Lord’s form.”
ramacharitamanas::3966.modern_relevance: You walk into a room full of people, but the old habit still whispers, “How do I look?” This verse cuts through that noise: you are not the center, and nothing you meet is outside the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3966.insight: It shifts identity from ownership to service, and from separation to sacred belonging.

ramacharitamanas::3967.verse_sanskrit: देखि पवनसुत पति अनुकूला। हृदयँ हरष बीती सब सूला॥ नाथ सैल पर कपिपति रहई। सो सुग्रीव दास तव अहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3967.verse_hindi: स्वामी को अनुकूल (प्रसन्न) देखकर पवन कुमार हनुमान् जी के हृदय में हर्ष छा गया और उनके सब दुःख जाते रहे। (उन्होंने कहा-) हे नाथ! इस पर्वत पर वानरराज सुग्रीव रहते हैं, वह आपका दास है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3967.english_translation: Seeing his master favorable, Hanuman's heart filled with joy and all his sorrow vanished. He said, “Lord, on this mountain lives the king of the monkeys. Sugriva is your servant.”
ramacharitamanas::3967.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / पति (master) / अनुकूला (favorable) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / बीती (passed away) / सब (all) / सूला (sorrows) ॥ / नाथ (Lord) / सैल (mountain) / पर (on) / कपिपति (king of monkeys) / रहई (lives) / सो (that one) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / दास (servant) / तव (your) / अहई (is) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3967.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3967.essence: Grace received turns anxiety into clear, helpful action.
ramacharitamanas::3967.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees that Ram is kindly disposed toward him, and his grief disappears. Then he points out that Sugriva lives on the mountain and is Ram's servant.
ramacharitamanas::3967.simple_insight: When devotion is met with grace, fear drops away at once.
ramacharitamanas::3967.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Ram and Lakshman after leaping across the ocean. Seeing Ram pleased with him, his own pain dissolves. In that relieved, loving state, he immediately introduces Sugriva as Ram's servant, opening the way for alliance.
ramacharitamanas::3967.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting judgment, but the first smile changes everything. The tension leaves your chest, and you can finally speak plainly.
ramacharitamanas::3967.insight: It shifts attention from self-protection to service once acceptance is felt.

ramacharitamanas::3968.verse_sanskrit: तेहि सन नाथ मयत्री कीजे। दीन जानि तेहि अभय करीजे॥ सो सीता कर खोज कराइहि। जहँ तहँ मरकट कोटि पठाइहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3968.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! उससे मित्रता कीजिए और उसे दीन जानकर निर्भय कर दीजिए। वह सीताजी की खोज करवाएगा और जहाँ-तहाँ करोड़ों वानरों को भेजेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3968.english_translation: O Lord, make friendship with him and treat him as humble and fearless. He will arrange the search for Sita and send millions of monkeys everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3968.translation_literal: तेहि सन (with him) / नाथ (O lord) / मयत्री (friendship) / कीजे (do) / दीन (humble, poor) / जानि (knowing) / तेहि (him) / अभय (fearless, without fear) / करीजे (make) / सो (he) / सीता (Sita) / कर (of) / खोज (search) / कराइहि (will cause to be done) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / मरकट (monkeys) / कोटि (crores, millions) / पठाइहि (will send)
ramacharitamanas::3968.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3968.essence: Trust the humble one, and hidden power begins to move.
ramacharitamanas::3968.simple_meaning: Treat Sugriva kindly and without fear. Once he feels safe, he will help search for Sita and send the monkey army everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3968.simple_insight: Compassion and trust can unlock help that force never could.
ramacharitamanas::3968.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just seen that Ram is favorable. Now he urges Ram to befriend Sugriva, the monkey king living in fear and exile. If Sugriva feels protected, he will mobilize the entire monkey force to search for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3968.modern_relevance: You meet someone guarded after a betrayal. Instead of pressing harder, you lower your voice, offer safety, and suddenly they start helping in ways you never expected.
ramacharitamanas::3968.insight: It shifts you from control to relationship: make the other person feel safe, and cooperation becomes possible.

ramacharitamanas::3969.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सकल कथा समुझाई। लिए दुऔ जन पीठि चढ़ाई॥ जब सुग्रीवँ राम कहुँ देखा। अतिसय जन्म धन्य करि लेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3969.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब बातें समझाकर हनुमान् जी ने (श्री राम-लक्ष्मण) दोनों जनों को पीठ पर चढ़ा लिया। जब सुग्रीव ने श्री रामचंद्रजी को देखा तो अपने जन्म को अत्यंत धन्य समझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3969.english_translation: In this way, Hanuman explained everything and carried both of them on his back. When Sugriva saw Ram, he felt that his birth had become truly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3969.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सकल (all) / कथा (story, matters) / समुझाई (having explained) / लिए (took, carried) / दुऔ (both) / जन (persons) / पीठि (back) / चढ़ाई (mounted) / जब (when) / सुग्रीवँ (Sugriva) / राम कहुँ (toward Ram) / देखा (saw) / अतिसय (greatly) / जन्म (birth) / धन्य (blessed) / करि (having made) / लेखा (considered)
ramacharitamanas::3969.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3969.essence: Seeing Ram makes Sugriva’s whole life feel fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::3969.simple_meaning: Hanuman carried Ram and Lakshman on his back to Sugriva. The moment Sugriva saw Ram, he felt his life had become blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3969.simple_insight: Meeting the right presence can make an entire life feel newly meaningful.
ramacharitamanas::3969.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has finished explaining the situation and brings Ram and Lakshman to Kishkindha on his back. The alliance is about to begin, and Sugriva’s first sight of Ram fills him with awe and gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::3969.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person who can change everything, and your chest loosens before a single word is spoken. Recognition itself feels like grace.
ramacharitamanas::3969.insight: It shifts attention from the journey to the transforming power of a single right encounter.

ramacharitamanas::3970.verse_sanskrit: सादर मिलेउ नाइ पद माथा। भेंटेउ अनुज सहित रघुनाथा॥ कपि कर मन बिचार एहि रीती। करिहहिं बिधि मो सन ए प्रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3970.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर आदर सहित मिले। श्री रघुनाथजी भी छोटे भाई सहित उनसे गले लगकर मिले। सुग्रीव मन में इस प्रकार सोच रहे हैं कि हे विधाता! क्या ये मुझसे प्रीति करेंगे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3970.english_translation: Sugriva bowed his head to the feet and met Ram with respect. Raghunath embraced him along with Lakshman. In his mind, the monkey king wondered, “Will they truly care for me?”
ramacharitamanas::3970.translation_literal: सादर (with respect) / मिलेउ (met) / नाइ (bowing) / पद (feet) / माथा (head) / भेंटेउ (embraced/met) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / कपि (monkey) / कर (of the hand / in) / मन (mind) / बिचार (thought) / एहि (this) / रीती (way) / करिहहिं (will they do) / बिधि (fate / the divine order) / मो सन (with me) / ए (these) / प्रीती (love)
ramacharitamanas::3970.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3970.essence: Kindness can arrive before trust is fully ready to believe it.
ramacharitamanas::3970.simple_meaning: Sugriva bows respectfully to Ram, and Ram embraces him with Lakshman. Sugriva still wonders whether this kindness will last.
ramacharitamanas::3970.simple_insight: A first meeting can carry both welcome and fear at once.
ramacharitamanas::3970.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has brought Ram and Lakshman to Sugriva on Mount Rishyamukha. Sugriva greets them with full respect, and Ram responds warmly. But beneath the embrace, Sugriva still doubts whether this friendship will truly hold.
ramacharitamanas::3970.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems kind, but part of you still waits for the catch. The body relaxes before the mind does.
ramacharitamanas::3970.insight: It shows how trust often begins as a gesture before it becomes certainty.

ramacharitamanas::3971.verse_sanskrit: तब हनुमंत उभय दिसि की सब कथा सुनाइ। पावक साखी देइ करि जोरी प्रीति दृढ़ाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3971.verse_hindi: तब हनुमान् जी ने दोनों ओर की सब कथा सुनाकर अग्नि को साक्षी देकर परस्पर दृढ़ करके प्रीति जोड़ दी (अर्थात् अग्नि की साक्षी देकर प्रतिज्ञापूर्वक उनकी मैत्री करवा दी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3971.english_translation: Then Hanuman told both sides the whole story and, taking fire as witness, firmly joined their friendship.
ramacharitamanas::3971.translation_literal: तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / उभय दिसि (on both sides) / की (of) / सब कथा (all the story) / सुनाइ (having told) / पावक (fire) / साखी (witness) / देइ (giving) / करि (having made) / जोरी (joined) / प्रीति (friendship/love) / दृढ़ाइ (made firm)
ramacharitamanas::3971.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::3971.essence: Truth, spoken to both sides, can turn alliance into trust.
ramacharitamanas::3971.simple_meaning: Hanuman explains everything to both sides and uses fire as witness to seal their friendship.
ramacharitamanas::3971.simple_insight: Clear honesty can do what force never can: make trust real.
ramacharitamanas::3971.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman stands between Ram's camp and Sugriva's side. He explains both stories fully, then uses fire as witness so their friendship becomes firm and public.
ramacharitamanas::3971.modern_relevance: You’re mediating between two friends who both feel wronged. Instead of choosing sides, you tell the whole story honestly until something solid can begin again.
ramacharitamanas::3971.insight: It shifts conflict resolution from partial loyalty to transparent, trust-building speech.

ramacharitamanas::3972.verse_sanskrit: कीन्हि प्रीति कछु बीच न राखा। लछिमन राम चरित् सब भाषा॥ कह सुग्रीव नयन भरि बारी। मिलिहि नाथ मिथिलेसकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3972.verse_hindi: दोनों ने (हृदय से) प्रीति की, कुछ भी अंतर नहीं रखा। तब लक्ष्मणजी ने श्री रामचंद्रजी का सारा इतिहास कहा। सुग्रीव ने नेत्रों में जल भरकर कहा- हे नाथ! मिथिलेशकुमारी जानकीजी मिल जाएँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3972.english_translation: They shared friendship with nothing held back. Then Lakshman recounted all of Ram's story. With tears in his eyes, Sugriva said, "My lord, Janaki of Mithila will be found."
ramacharitamanas::3972.translation_literal: कीन्हि (made) / प्रीति (friendship, loving bond) / कछु (anything) / बीच (between, in the middle) / न (not) / राखा (kept) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / चरित् (story, deeds) / सब (all) / भाषा (spoke, told) / कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (filled) / बारी (water, tears) / मिलिहि (will be found, will meet) / नाथ (lord) / मिथिलेसकुमारी (princess of Mithila, Sita)
ramacharitamanas::3972.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3972.essence: Friendship deepens when both sides stop holding anything back.
ramacharitamanas::3972.simple_meaning: The friendship between Ram's group and Sugriva becomes complete and open. Lakshman tells Ram's story, and Sugriva, moved to tears, says Sita will be found.
ramacharitamanas::3972.simple_insight: Real trust shows up when no distance remains between hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3972.detailed_meaning: After the first meeting between Ram and Sugriva, the bond becomes warm and complete. Lakshman speaks about Ram's life, and Sugriva responds with tears and hope that Sita will be found. The verse deepens their alliance, but it is still part of the unfolding scene.
ramacharitamanas::3972.modern_relevance: You finally speak honestly with someone after weeks of careful distance. The conversation changes everything, not because of strategy, but because both hearts are now open.
ramacharitamanas::3972.insight: It shifts relationship from formal alliance to shared feeling and mutual trust.

ramacharitamanas::3973.verse_sanskrit: मंत्रिन्ह सहित इहाँ एक बारा। बैठ रहेउँ मैं करत बिचारा॥ गगन पंथ देखी मैं जाता। परबस परी बहुत बिलपाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3973.verse_hindi: मैं एक बार यहाँ मंत्रियों के साथ बैठा हुआ कुछ विचार कर रहा था। तब मैंने पराए (शत्रु) के वश में पड़ी बहुत विलाप करती हुई सीताजी को आकाश मार्ग से जाते देखा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3973.english_translation: I was once sitting here with my ministers, thinking. Then I saw Sita, weeping helplessly, being carried through the sky.
ramacharitamanas::3973.translation_literal: मंत्रिन्ह (with the ministers) / सहित (together with) / इहाँ (here) / एक बारा (one time) / बैठ रहेउँ (I was sitting) / मैं (I) / करत (doing) / बिचारा (thought) / गगन (sky) / पंथ (path) / देखी (seeing) / मैं (I) / जाता (going) / परबस (powerless / under another's control) / परी (fallen) / बहुत (much) / बिलपाता (lamenting)
ramacharitamanas::3973.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3973.essence: Seeing helpless suffering makes all other concerns shrink.
ramacharitamanas::3973.simple_meaning: Sugriva recalls sitting in counsel when he saw Sita being carried helplessly through the sky, crying in misery.
ramacharitamanas::3973.simple_insight: Some suffering is so stark that it interrupts every plan and leaves only grief.
ramacharitamanas::3973.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is recounting what he saw to Ram and Lakshman. He had been sitting with his ministers, thinking over affairs, when Sita appeared in the sky, trapped and crying. The memory explains why her rescue becomes urgent.
ramacharitamanas::3973.modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting, trying to sort out practical next steps, when a message arrives that someone you care about is in obvious distress. Everything else drops away.
ramacharitamanas::3973.insight: It shifts attention from strategy to urgency when suffering is seen directly.

ramacharitamanas::3974.verse_sanskrit: राम राम हा राम पुकारी। हमहि देखि दीन्हेउ पट डारी॥ मागा राम तुरत तेहिं दीन्हा। पट उर लाइ सोच अति कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3974.verse_hindi: हमें देखकर उन्होंने 'राम! राम! हा राम!' पुकारकर वस्त्र गिरा दिया था। श्री रामजी ने उसे माँगा, तब सुग्रीव ने तुरंत ही दे दिया। वस्त्र को हृदय से लगाकर रामचंद्रजी ने बहुत ही सोच किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3974.english_translation: Seeing us, he cried, 'Ram! Ram! Ha Ram!' and dropped the cloth. When Ram asked for it, Sugriva gave it at once. Ram pressed the cloth to his heart and fell into deep thought.
ramacharitamanas::3974.translation_literal: राम राम हा राम (Ram! Ram! Ha Ram!) / पुकारी (called out) / हमहि (us) / देखि (seeing) / दीन्हेउ (he gave) / पट (cloth) / डारी (dropped)॥ / मागा (asked for) / राम (Ram) / तुरत (immediately) / तेहिं (he) / दीन्हा (gave) / पट (cloth) / उर (to the heart) / लाइ (placing) / सोच (thought) / अति (very much) / कीन्हा (did) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3974.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3974.essence: A humble offering becomes precious when love is present.
ramacharitamanas::3974.simple_meaning: Sugriva is so moved by Ram's presence that he cries out and offers a cloth immediately. Ram receives it and falls into thought.
ramacharitamanas::3974.simple_insight: A small act of offering can carry real devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3974.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has just brought Ram and Lakshman to Sugriva. Overcome by seeing them, Sugriva cries out in joy and drops his cloth. Ram asks for it, and Sugriva gives it at once. Ram holds it to his heart, moved by the moment before speaking to Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::3974.modern_relevance: You hand someone a note, a scarf, or a keepsake, and they hold it like it matters more than the object itself. Some gestures carry the whole weight of trust.
ramacharitamanas::3974.insight: It shows how devotion turns even a simple object into a sign of deep connection.

ramacharitamanas::3975.verse_sanskrit: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। तजहु सोच मन आनहु धीरा॥ सब प्रकार करिहउँ सेवकाई। जेहि बिधि मिलिहि जानकी आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3975.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे रघुवीर! सुनिए। सोच छोड़ दीजिए और मन में धीरज लाइए। मैं सब प्रकार से आपकी सेवा करूँगा, जिस उपाय से जानकीजी आकर आपको मिलें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3975.english_translation: Sugriva said, "Listen, Raghubir. Let go of sorrow and bring steadiness to your mind. I will serve you in every way, by whatever means Sita may come to you."
ramacharitamanas::3975.translation_literal: कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir) / तजहु (let go) / सोच (sorrow) / मन (mind) / आनहु (bring) / धीरा (steadiness) / सब प्रकार (in every way) / करिहउँ (I will do) / सेवकाई (service) / जेहि बिधि (by whatever means) / मिलिहि (may come together) / जानकी (Janaki) / आई (coming)
ramacharitamanas::3975.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3975.essence: True alliance says: calm down, and let me carry the search with you.
ramacharitamanas::3975.simple_meaning: Sugriva asks Ram to stop worrying and stay calm. He promises full service until Sita is found and brought back.
ramacharitamanas::3975.simple_insight: Real support begins when someone else carries part of your burden.
ramacharitamanas::3975.detailed_meaning: After seeing Ram’s grief over Sita, Sugriva responds like a true ally. He asks Ram to steady his mind and promises complete service, committing himself to whatever plan will bring Sita back.
ramacharitamanas::3975.modern_relevance: You’re spiraling after a painful text, and a friend says, “Breathe. I’m with you. We’ll handle this.” That is Sugriva’s role here.
ramacharitamanas::3975.insight: It shifts devotion from sympathy into active help: calming another person and taking responsibility for the next step.

ramacharitamanas::3976.verse_sanskrit: सखा बचन सुनि हरषे कृपासिंधु बलसींव। कारन कवन बसहु बन मोहि कहहु सुग्रीव ॥
ramacharitamanas::3976.verse_hindi: कृपा के समुद्र और बल की सीमा श्री रामजी सखा सुग्रीव के वचन सुनकर हर्षित हुए। (और बोले-) हे सुग्रीव! मुझे बताओ, तुम वन में किस कारण रहते हो? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3976.english_translation: Saying this, the ocean of compassion and strength rejoiced. "Friend Sugriva, tell me: why do you live in the forest?"
ramacharitamanas::3976.translation_literal: सखा (friend) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / हरषे (rejoiced) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / बलसींव (limit of strength) / कारन (cause) / कवन (which) / बसहु (you live) / बन (forest) / मोहि (to me) / कहहु (tell) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva)
ramacharitamanas::3976.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3976.essence: Compassion begins by asking the right question.
ramacharitamanas::3976.simple_meaning: Ram is pleased by Sugriva's words and asks why Sugriva is living in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::3976.simple_insight: A caring question can open the door to real help.
ramacharitamanas::3976.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva has just begun trusting Ram. Ram receives his words with warmth and asks the simple question that matters: why is Sugriva still in the forest? That question draws out the whole story of exile and betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::3976.modern_relevance: Someone finally sits across from you and asks, not what happened in the meeting, but what happened to you. That one honest question can change everything.
ramacharitamanas::3976.insight: It shifts attention from surface talk to the wound that needs attention.

ramacharitamanas::3977.verse_sanskrit: नाथ बालि अरु मैं द्वौ भाइ। प्रीति रही कछु बरनि न जाई॥ मयसुत मायावी तेहि नाऊँ। आवा सो प्रभु हमरें गाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3977.verse_hindi: (सुग्रीव ने कहा-) हे नाथ! बालि और मैं दो भाई हैं, हम दोनों में ऐसी प्रीति थी कि वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। हे प्रभो! मय दानव का एक पुत्र था, उसका नाम मायावी था। एक बार वह हमारे गाँव में आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3977.english_translation: —Sugriva said— "O Lord, Bali and I were two brothers. The love between us cannot be described. O Lord, there was a son of Maya named Mayavi. He came once to our village."
ramacharitamanas::3977.translation_literal: नाथ (O Lord) / बालि (Bali) / अरु (and) / मैं (I) / द्वौ (two) / भाइ (brothers) / प्रीति (love) / रही (remained) / कछु (some) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be) / मयसुत (son of Maya) / मायावी (Mayavi) / तेहि (that) / नाऊँ (by name) / आवा (came) / सो (he) / प्रभु (Lord) / हमरें (our) / गाऊँ (village)
ramacharitamanas::3977.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3977.essence: A broken brotherhood hurts most because it once held real love.
ramacharitamanas::3977.simple_meaning: Sugriva recalls that he and Bali were once very close brothers, and he begins explaining how the trouble started when Mayavi came to their village.
ramacharitamanas::3977.simple_insight: Some betrayals begin in a bond that once felt unbreakable.
ramacharitamanas::3977.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is explaining his painful history to Ram. Before he can ask for help against Bali, he remembers the brotherly love they once shared and introduces the incident with Mayavi that set their conflict in motion.
ramacharitamanas::3977.modern_relevance: You can be speaking to someone who wants the whole truth, yet still find yourself circling the wound that changed everything. Old family pain rarely starts with hatred; it starts with love that got broken.
ramacharitamanas::3977.insight: It shifts attention from the quarrel itself to the earlier bond that made the loss so painful.

ramacharitamanas::3978.verse_sanskrit: अर्ध राति पुर द्वार पुकारा। बाली रिपु बल सहै न पारा॥ धावा बालि देखि सो भागा। मैं पुनि गयउँ बंधु सँग लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3978.verse_hindi: उसने आधी रात को नगर के फाटक पर आकर पुकारा (ललकारा)। बालि शत्रु के बल (ललकार) को सह नहीं सका। वह दौड़ा, उसे देखकर मायावी भागा। मैं भी भाई के संग लगा चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3978.english_translation: He came shouting at the city gate in the middle of the night. Bali could not bear the enemy's challenge. Bali ran after him; seeing him, the illusionist fled. I too went along with my brother.
ramacharitamanas::3978.translation_literal: अर्ध राति (midnight) / पुर द्वार (city gate) / पुकारा (called out) । बाली (Bali) / रिपु (enemy) / बल (strength) / सहै न पारा (could not bear) ॥ धावा (ran) / बालि (Bali) / देखि (seeing) / सो (he) / भागा (fled) । मैं (I) / पुनि (also) / गयउँ (went) / बंधु (brother) / सँग (with) / लागा (attached, followed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3978.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3978.essence: Loyalty can drag you into danger before you understand it.
ramacharitamanas::3978.simple_meaning: Sugriva describes how Bali chased the stranger who challenged him at night, and how Sugriva followed his brother.
ramacharitamanas::3978.simple_insight: Some wounds begin as loyalty and end as exile.
ramacharitamanas::3978.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Sugriva is explaining his broken bond with Bali to Ram and Lakshman. He recalls how a challenger came to the city gate at midnight, Bali rushed out, the challenger fled, and Sugriva followed his brother into danger.
ramacharitamanas::3978.modern_relevance: A friend pulls you into a fight you never wanted, and suddenly you are running on loyalty instead of choice. Later, all you can do is explain how it started.
ramacharitamanas::3978.insight: It sets up the betrayal that made Sugriva afraid and displaced, preparing the case for Ram's help.

ramacharitamanas::3979.verse_sanskrit: गिरिबर गुहाँ पैठ सो जाई। तब बालीं मोहि कहा बुझाई॥ परिखेसु मोहि एक पखवारा। नहिं आवौं तब जानेसु मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3979.verse_hindi: वह मायावी एक पर्वत की गुफा में जा घुसा। तब बालि ने मुझे समझाकर कहा- तुम एक पखवाड़े (पंद्रह दिन) तक मेरी बाट देखना। यदि मैं उतने दिनों में न आऊँ तो जान लेना कि मैं मारा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3979.english_translation: He entered a mountain cave. Then Bali told me, "Wait for me for half a month. If I do not return by then, know that I have been killed."
ramacharitamanas::3979.translation_literal: गिरिबर (mountain) / गुहाँ (cave) / पैठ (entered) / सो (that one) / जाई (going) / तब (then) / बालीं (Bali) / मोहि (to me) / कहा (said) / बुझाई (explaining) / परिखेसु (wait/test) / मोहि (me) / एक पखवारा (one fortnight) / नहिं (not) / आवौं (I return) / तब (then) / जानेसु (know) / मारा (killed)
ramacharitamanas::3979.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3979.essence: A promise to return can become a weapon when fear enters the waiting.
ramacharitamanas::3979.simple_meaning: Sugriva recalls how Bali entered a cave and told him to wait fifteen days. If Bali did not return, Sugriva was to assume Bali had died.
ramacharitamanas::3979.simple_insight: Some promises are really traps, and waiting can become a test of fear.
ramacharitamanas::3979.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is explaining his old wound to Ram. Bali went into a mountain cave after the chase and told Sugriva to wait outside for fifteen days. That instruction becomes part of the betrayal that shaped Sugriva's exile and fear.
ramacharitamanas::3979.modern_relevance: You wait outside a hospital room while someone says, "I'll be back soon," and the silence stretches into dread. A simple promise can become the hinge of your whole trust.
ramacharitamanas::3979.insight: It shows how a delayed return can turn hope into anxiety and suspicion.

ramacharitamanas::3980.verse_sanskrit: मास दिवस तहँ रहेउँ खरारी। निसरी रुधिर धार तहँ भारी॥ बालि हतेसि मोहि मारिहि आई। सिला देइ तहँ चलेउँ पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3980.verse_hindi: हे खरारि! मैं वहाँ महीने भर तक रहा। वहाँ (उस गुफा में से) रक्त की बड़ी भारी धारा निकली। तब (मैंने समझा कि) उसने बालि को मार डाला, अब आकर मुझे मारेगा, इसलिए मैं वहाँ (गुफा के द्वार पर) एक शिला लगाकर भाग आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3980.english_translation: O Kharaari, I stayed there for a month. A great stream of blood flowed out from there. Then I thought, "He has killed Bali and will come to kill me," so I placed a stone there and fled.
ramacharitamanas::3980.translation_literal: मास (month) / दिवस (days) / तहँ (there) / रहेउँ (I stayed) / खरारी (O enemy of Khara) / निसरी (flowed out) / रुधिर (blood) / धार (stream) / तहँ (there) / भारी (great) / बालि (Bali) / हतेसि (you killed) / मोहि (me) / मारिहि (will kill) / आई (coming) / सिला (stone) / देइ (placing) / तहँ (there) / चलेउँ (I went) / पराई (away)
ramacharitamanas::3980.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3980.essence: Fear fills gaps with disaster and pushes you into flight.
ramacharitamanas::3980.simple_meaning: Sugriva says he waited a month in the cave, saw a stream of blood, feared Bali had been killed and would return to kill him, and so he sealed the cave and fled.
ramacharitamanas::3980.simple_insight: Fear can make you run from a moment before you know the full truth.
ramacharitamanas::3980.detailed_meaning: Sugriva is explaining to Ram why he abandoned the cave. He had waited far longer than promised, saw blood pouring out, assumed Bali had died and would come back in rage, and fled by blocking the entrance. This is part of his attempt to justify his fear.
ramacharitamanas::3980.modern_relevance: You get one alarming text, see one unfinished email thread, and your mind writes the worst ending before the facts are clear.
ramacharitamanas::3980.insight: It shows how quickly the mind turns partial signs into certainty and then acts from panic.

ramacharitamanas::3981.verse_sanskrit: मंत्रिन्ह पुर देखा बिनु साईं। दीन्हेउ मोहि राज बरिआईं॥ बाली ताहि मारि गृह आवा। देखि मोहि जियँ भेद बढ़ावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3981.verse_hindi: मंत्रियों ने नगर को बिना स्वामी (राजा) का देखा, तो मुझको जबर्दस्ती राज्य दे दिया। बालि उसे मारकर घर आ गया। मुझे (राजसिंहासन पर) देखकर उसने जी में भेद बढ़ाया (बहुत ही विरोध माना)। (उसने समझा कि यह राज्य के लोभ से ही गुफा के द्वार पर शिला दे आया था, जिससे मैं बाहर न निकल सकूँ और यहाँ आकर राजा बन बैठा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3981.english_translation: The ministers saw the city without a ruler and forcibly gave me the kingdom. Bali killed him and came home. Seeing me on the throne, he grew deeply suspicious and thought I had left the cave door sealed out of greed for power.
ramacharitamanas::3981.translation_literal: मंत्रिन्ह (by the ministers) / पुर (the city) / देखा (saw) / बिनु साईं (without a lord) / दीन्हेउ (gave) / मोहि (to me) / राज (kingdom) / बरिआईं (by force)॥ / बाली (Bali) / ताहि (him) / मारि (having killed) / गृह (home) / आवा (came)॥ / देखि (seeing) / मोहि (me) / जियँ (in his mind) / भेद (distrust) / बढ़ावा (increased)॥
ramacharitamanas::3981.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3981.essence: A rightful placement can look like greed to a wounded mind.
ramacharitamanas::3981.simple_meaning: Sugriva says he was made king when the city was left without a ruler, but Bali misread that as greed and became suspicious.
ramacharitamanas::3981.simple_insight: People often judge your motives by their own fears, not by the truth.
ramacharitamanas::3981.detailed_meaning: Sugriva is explaining his old conflict to Ram and Lakshman. After Bali left, the ministers placed Sugriva on the throne. But when Bali returned and saw him ruling, he assumed betrayal and resentment deepened between them.
ramacharitamanas::3981.modern_relevance: You finally step into a role after someone disappears, and the returning person assumes you schemed for it. Misunderstanding hardens instantly.
ramacharitamanas::3981.insight: It shows how power, fear, and suspicion can turn a practical decision into a moral accusation.

ramacharitamanas::3982.verse_sanskrit: रिपु सम मोहि मारेसि अति भारी। हरि लीन्हसि सर्बसु अरु नारी॥ ताकें भय रघुबीर कृपाला सकल भुवन मैं फिरेउँ बिहाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3982.verse_hindi: उसने मुझे शत्रु के समान बहुत अधिक मारा और मेरा सर्वस्व तथा मेरी स्त्री को भी छीन लिया। हे कृपालु रघुवीर! मैं उसके भय से समस्त लोकों में बेहाल होकर फिरता रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3982.english_translation: He struck me terribly, like an enemy, and took away all my wealth and my wife. O compassionate Raghubir, I wandered through all the worlds in misery, afraid of him.
ramacharitamanas::3982.translation_literal: रिपु सम (like an enemy) / मोहि (me) / मारेसि (struck) / अति भारी (very heavily) / हरि (took away) / लीन्हसि (took) / सर्बसु (all wealth) / अरु (and) / नारी (wife) / ताकें (because of that) / भय (fear) / रघुबीर कृपाला (compassionate Raghubir) / सकल भुवन मैं (in all worlds) / फिरेउँ (I wandered) / बिहाला (distressed)
ramacharitamanas::3982.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3982.essence: Fear turns a single injury into a whole life of exile.
ramacharitamanas::3982.simple_meaning: Sugriva says Vali beat him badly, took his wife and kingdom, and left him wandering in fear everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3982.simple_insight: Fear can shrink your whole world until you can think of nothing else.
ramacharitamanas::3982.detailed_meaning: Sugriva is telling Ram why he has lived in hiding. Vali’s violence cost him his wife, his kingdom, and his peace of mind. This is the wound beneath the alliance: Ram is hearing not strategy, but a life broken by fear.
ramacharitamanas::3982.modern_relevance: After one humiliating betrayal, you start checking doors, rereading messages, and expecting the worst from everyone. Fear can keep you living in exile long after the event is over.
ramacharitamanas::3982.insight: It shows how trauma traps attention in threat, making the whole world feel unsafe.

ramacharitamanas::3983.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ साप बस आवत नाहीं। तदपि सभीत रहउँ मन माहीं॥ सुन सेवक दुःख दीनदयाला फरकि उठीं द्वै भुजा बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3983.verse_hindi: वह शाप के कारण यहाँ नहीं आता, तो भी मैं मन में भयभीत रहता हूँ। सेवक का दुःख सुनकर दीनों पर दया करने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी की दोनों विशाल भुजाएँ फड़क उठीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3983.english_translation: He does not come here because of the curse, yet I still remain afraid in my mind. Hearing the grief of a servant, the arms of the compassionate Raghunath trembled.
ramacharitamanas::3983.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / साप (curse) / बस (only) / आवत (coming) / नाहीं (not) / तदपि (still) / सभीत (afraid) / रहउँ (I remain) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सुन (hearing) / सेवक (servant) / दुःख (sorrow) / दीनदयाला (compassionate to the poor) / फरकि (trembled) / उठीं (rose up) / द्वै (two) / भुजा (arms) / बिसाला (vast)
ramacharitamanas::3983.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3983.essence: Fear can remain in the mind even after danger has passed.
ramacharitamanas::3983.simple_meaning: Sugriva says that even though Bali cannot come here because of a curse, fear still lives in his mind. When Ram hears a servant's pain, his powerful arms stir with compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3983.simple_insight: Fear can linger even when danger seems absent, but true compassion responds instantly to suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3983.detailed_meaning: Sugriva is explaining his lingering fear after Bali's attack. Even with the curse keeping Bali away, he cannot relax. Then Ram, hearing the pain of a servant, reacts at once. The verse shows fear on one side and protective compassion on the other.
ramacharitamanas::3983.modern_relevance: You know the person is blocked from reaching you, yet your body still stays tense. Then someone you trust hears your pain and instantly moves to help. That contrast is this verse.
ramacharitamanas::3983.insight: It shifts attention from abstract safety to the lived reality of fear and the healing force of immediate compassion.

ramacharitamanas::3984.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सुग्रीव मारिहउँ बालिहि एकहिं बान। ब्रह्म रुद्र सरनागत गएँ न उबरिहिं प्रान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3984.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) हे सुग्रीव! सुनो, मैं एक ही बाण से बालि को मार डालूँगा। ब्रह्मा और रुद्र की शरण में जाने पर भी उसके प्राण न बचेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3984.english_translation: Saying, "Listen, Sugriva: I will kill Bali with a single arrow. Even if he seeks refuge in Brahma and Rudra, his life will not be saved."
ramacharitamanas::3984.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / मारिहउँ (I will kill) / बालिहि (Bali) / एकहिं (only one) / बान (arrow) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / रुद्र (Rudra) / सरनागत (having taken refuge) / गएँ (even if going) / न (not) / उबरिहिं (will be saved) / प्रान (life)
ramacharitamanas::3984.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3984.essence: True refuge is not in escape, but in Ram's protection.
ramacharitamanas::3984.simple_meaning: Ram promises Sugriva that he will kill Bali with one arrow, and no refuge will save Bali from that fate.
ramacharitamanas::3984.simple_insight: Some promises are so complete that fear loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::3984.detailed_meaning: Sugriva is explaining his terror and loss to Ram in Kishkindha. In reply, Ram gives a decisive vow: Bali will fall to one arrow, and no higher refuge will protect him. The moment turns fear into guaranteed action.
ramacharitamanas::3984.modern_relevance: You are backing a friend who has been cornered by a bully and every excuse has already failed. A clear promise from someone steady can change panic into courage.
ramacharitamanas::3984.insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to trust in decisive protection.

ramacharitamanas::3985.verse_sanskrit: जे न मित्र दुख होहिं दुखारी। तिन्हहि बिलोकत पातक भारी॥ निज दुख गिरि सम रज करि जाना। मित्रक दुख रज मेरु समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3985.verse_hindi: जो लोग मित्र के दुःख से दुःखी नहीं होते, उन्हें देखने से ही बड़ा पाप लगता है। अपने पर्वत के समान दुःख को धूल के समान और मित्र के धूल के समान दुःख को सुमेरु (बड़े भारी पर्वत) के समान जाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::3985.english_translation: Those who do not feel sorrow at a friend's sorrow are deeply blameworthy to even look upon. Treat your own mountain-sized grief as dust, and your friend's dust-sized grief as Mount Sumeru.
ramacharitamanas::3985.translation_literal: जे (those who) / न (not) / मित्र (friend) / दुख (sorrow) / होहिं (are) / दुखारी (sorrowful) / तिन्हहि (them) / बिलोकत (seeing) / पातक (fault / sin) / भारी (great) / निज (own) / दुख (sorrow) / गिरि (mountain) / सम (like) / रज (dust) / करि (making) / जाना (know) / मित्रक (friend's) / दुख (sorrow) / रज (dust) / मेरु (Mount Sumeru) / समाना (equal to)
ramacharitamanas::3985.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3985.essence: True friendship makes your friend's pain heavier than your own.
ramacharitamanas::3985.simple_meaning: Real friendship means feeling your friend's pain as your own and shrinking your own suffering in comparison.
ramacharitamanas::3985.simple_insight: Love becomes real when another person's pain feels impossible to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::3985.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram is teaching Sugriva what true friendship looks like. A real friend does not stay untouched by another's grief. He feels his friend's pain deeply and does not inflate his own suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3985.modern_relevance: Your best friend texts at 1am from a hospital waiting room, and you answer with advice instead of presence. This verse asks for something harder: let their pain matter to you more than your own discomfort.
ramacharitamanas::3985.insight: It shifts friendship from polite concern to shared burden and shared feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3986.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3986.verse_hindi: जिन्हें स्वभाव से ही ऐसी बुद्धि प्राप्त नहीं है, वे मूर्ख हठ करके क्यों किसी से मित्रता करते हैं? मित्र का धर्म है कि वह मित्र को बुरे मार्ग से रोककर अच्छे मार्ग पर चलावे। उसके गुण प्रकट करे और अवगुणों को छिपावे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3986.english_translation: Those who do not naturally have this kind of wisdom—why do they stubbornly call it friendship? A true friend turns you away from the wrong road and leads you to the right one. They reveal your virtues and hide your faults.
ramacharitamanas::3986.translation_literal: जिन्ह कें (for whom) / असि (such) / मति (wisdom) / सहज (naturally) / न (not) / आई (came) / ते (those) / सठ (fools) / कत (why) / हठि (stubbornly) / करत (do) / मिताई (friendship) ॥ कुपथ (wrong path) / निवारि (turning away) / सुपंथ (good path) / चलावा (leads) / गुन (virtues) / प्रगटै (reveals) / अवगुनन्हि (faults) / दुरावा (hides) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3986.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3986.essence: True friendship protects your best path, not your ego.
ramacharitamanas::3986.simple_meaning: A real friend does not flatter you. They stop you from going wrong, guide you toward what is right, and protect your good qualities.
ramacharitamanas::3986.simple_insight: Good friendship makes you safer, steadier, and more honest with yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3986.detailed_meaning: After Ram promises to kill Bali and the talk turns to friendship, Tulsidas defines what a true friend is. A real friend protects you from bad choices, guides you toward the good, and speaks in a way that strengthens what is best in you.
ramacharitamanas::3986.modern_relevance: You text the friend who tells you the uncomfortable truth before you make the mistake. The one who protects your best self is worth more than the one who only agrees.
ramacharitamanas::3986.insight: It shifts friendship from approval-seeking to moral care: a friend helps you choose better, not just feel better.

ramacharitamanas::3987.verse_sanskrit: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3987.verse_hindi: देने-लेने में मन में शंका न रखे। अपने बल के अनुसार सदा हित ही करता रहे। विपत्ति के समय तो सदा सौगुना स्नेह करे। वेद कहते हैं कि संत (श्रेष्ठ) मित्र के गुण (लक्षण) ये हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3987.english_translation: Keep no doubt in giving or receiving. Always do what is helpful within your power. In hardship, multiply your affection a hundredfold. The Vedas say these are the qualities of a true friend.
ramacharitamanas::3987.translation_literal: देत (giving) / लेत (receiving) / मन (mind) / संक (doubt) / न (not) / धरई (holds) / बल (strength) / अनुमान (according to) / सदा (always) / हित (good) / करई (does) / बिपति (hardship) / काल (time) / कर (of) / सतगुन (hundredfold) / नेहा (affection) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / कह (say) / संत (true) / मित्र (friend) / गुन (qualities) / एहा (these)
ramacharitamanas::3987.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3987.essence: True friendship gives more when life gets harder.
ramacharitamanas::3987.simple_meaning: A true friend gives and receives without suspicion, helps within their ability, and becomes even more loving when trouble comes.
ramacharitamanas::3987.simple_insight: Friendship becomes a refuge when care is steady, generous, and strongest under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3987.detailed_meaning: After defining what a good friend should not be, Tulsidas now gives the positive standard. A true friend does not keep score, helps as much as possible, and in difficult times becomes even more affectionate. This completes the teaching on friendship.
ramacharitamanas::3987.modern_relevance: You answered a late-night call from a friend who was falling apart, even though you were exhausted. You didn't tally effort or ask what you'd get back. That is the kind of loyalty this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::3987.insight: It shifts friendship from exchange to steadfast care, especially when the other person is in pain.

ramacharitamanas::3988.verse_sanskrit: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3988.verse_hindi: जो सामने तो बना-बनाकर कोमल वचन कहता है और पीठ-पीछे बुराई करता है तथा मन में कुटिलता रखता है- हे भाई! (इस तरह) जिसका मन साँप की चाल के समान टेढ़ा है, ऐसे कुमित्र को तो त्यागने में ही भलाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3988.english_translation: If someone speaks sweetly in front but hides harm behind your back, and their mind twists like a snake's path, it is better to leave such a false friend.
ramacharitamanas::3988.translation_literal: आगें (in front) / कह (speaks) / मृदु (soft) / बचन (words) / बनाई (making) / पाछें (behind) / अनहित (harm) / मन (mind) / कुटिलाई (crookedness) / जाकर (whose) / िचत (mind) / अहि (snake) / गति (movement/path) / सम (like) / भाई (brother) / अस (such) / कुमित्र (bad friend) / परिहरेहिं (should abandon) / भलाई (goodness)
ramacharitamanas::3988.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3988.essence: A friend who hides harm is safer left behind.
ramacharitamanas::3988.simple_meaning: A false friend may speak gently in front of you while planning harm behind your back. The wise choice is to let that person go.
ramacharitamanas::3988.simple_insight: You do not owe loyalty to hidden betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::3988.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the teaching on friendship continues after Sugriva's warning. The verse names the friend who smiles openly but carries harm inwardly. Such crookedness is compared to a snake's movement, and the listener is told to drop that friendship.
ramacharitamanas::3988.modern_relevance: You notice a friend praising you in the group chat, then quietly undermining you in private. The sting is not just the betrayal — it is realizing you kept calling it loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3988.insight: It teaches you to judge friendship by consistency, not charm, and to step back from relationships that conceal harm.

ramacharitamanas::3989.verse_sanskrit: सेवक सठ नृप कृपन कुनारी। कपटी मित्र सूल सम चारी॥ सखा सोच त्यागहु बल मोरें। सब बिधि घटब काज मैं तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3989.verse_hindi: मूर्ख सेवक, कंजूस राजा, कुलटा स्त्री और कपटी मित्र- ये चारों शूल के समान पीड़ा देने वाले हैं। हे सखा! मेरे बल पर अब तुम चिंता छोड़ दो। मैं सब प्रकार से तुम्हारे काम आऊँगा (तुम्हारी सहायता करूँगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3989.english_translation: A foolish servant, a miserly king, an unchaste woman, and a deceitful friend — these four are like spears of pain. O friend, now drop your worry; with my strength, I will handle everything for you.
ramacharitamanas::3989.translation_literal: सेवक (servant) / सठ (foolish) / नृप (king) / कृपन (miserly) / कुनारी (unchaste woman) / कपटी (deceitful) / मित्र (friend) / सूल (spear) / सम (like) / चारी (four) / सखा (friend) / सोच (worry) / त्यागहु (give up) / बल (strength) / मोरें (by my) / सब बिधि (in every way) / घटब (I will manage) / काज (task) / मैं (I) / तोरें (for you)
ramacharitamanas::3989.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3989.essence: True friendship replaces fear with help.
ramacharitamanas::3989.simple_meaning: A deceitful friend hurts like a spear, but a true friend removes fear and takes care of your task with full support.
ramacharitamanas::3989.simple_insight: Real friendship feels safe: you can breathe because someone trustworthy stands with you.
ramacharitamanas::3989.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is speaking to Ram after testing the qualities of people and relationships. He warns that false companions wound deeply, then turns to Ram with complete confidence: friendship means removing fear and taking up the task together.
ramacharitamanas::3989.modern_relevance: You finally tell a trusted friend what is overwhelming you, and they don’t flinch. They don’t just listen — they step in. That is the relief Sugriva offers here.
ramacharitamanas::3989.insight: It shifts friendship from social closeness to dependable support under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3990.verse_sanskrit: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। बालि महाबल अति रनधीरा॥ दुंदुभि अस्थि ताल देखराए। बिनु प्रयास रघुनाथ ढहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3990.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे रघुवीर! सुनिए, बालि महान् बलवान् और अत्यंत रणधीर है। फिर सुग्रीव ने श्री रामजी को दुंदुभि राक्षस की हड्डियाँ व ताल के वृक्ष दिखलाए। श्री रघुनाथजी ने उन्हें बिना ही परिश्रम के (आसानी से) ढहा दिया।
ramacharitamanas::3990.english_translation: Sugriva said, "Listen, Raghubira: Bali is immensely powerful and fierce in battle. I showed you the bones of the demon Dundubhi and the palm trees, and Ragunath toppled them without effort."
ramacharitamanas::3990.translation_literal: कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुबीरा (Raghubira) / बालि (Bali) / महाबल (greatly powerful) / अति (very) / रनधीरा (battle-brave) / दुंदुभि (Dundubhi) / अस्थि (bones) / ताल (palm trees) / देखराए (showed) / बिनु (without) / प्रयास (effort) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / ढहाए (knocked down)
ramacharitamanas::3990.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3990.essence: Real power proves itself without strain.
ramacharitamanas::3990.simple_meaning: Sugriva points to Bali's huge strength, then reminds Ram how easily he knocked down Dundubhi's bones and palm trees. The message is clear: Ram's power is enough for the coming fight.
ramacharitamanas::3990.simple_insight: Confidence grows when you remember what has already been proven.
ramacharitamanas::3990.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is trying to win Ram's trust before the duel with Bali. He reminds Ram of Bali's terrifying strength, then points to the bones and palm trees Ram already destroyed without strain. The scene turns proof into courage.
ramacharitamanas::3990.modern_relevance: Before a high-stakes interview, you replay the one presentation where you handled pressure beautifully. That memory steadies you. Sugriva is doing the same for Ram: proving readiness through evidence.
ramacharitamanas::3990.insight: It shifts you from fear of the challenge to confidence in tested capability.

ramacharitamanas::3991.verse_sanskrit: देखि अमित बल बाढ़ी प्रीती। बालि बधब इन्ह भइ परतीती॥ बार-बार नावइ पद सीसा। प्रभुहि जानि मन हरष कपीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3991.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी का अपरिमित बल देखकर सुग्रीव की प्रीति बढ़ गई और उन्हें विश्वास हो गया कि ये बालि का वध अवश्य करेंगे। वे बार-बार चरणों में सिर नवाने लगे। प्रभु को पहचानकर सुग्रीव मन में हर्षित हो रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3991.english_translation: Seeing Ram's immeasurable strength, Sugriva's love grew and he became convinced that Ram would surely kill Bali. Again and again he bowed his head at Ram's feet, and knowing the Lord, the king of monkeys felt joy in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3991.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / अमित (immeasurable) / बल (strength) / बाढ़ी (grew) / प्रीती (love) / बालि (Bali) / बधब (to kill) / इन्ह (these) / भइ (became) / परतीती (conviction) / बार-बार (again and again) / नावइ (bowed) / पद (feet) / सीसा (head) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / जानि (knowing) / मन (mind) / हरष (rejoiced) / कपीसा (king of monkeys)
ramacharitamanas::3991.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3991.essence: Seeing true strength makes trust effortless.
ramacharitamanas::3991.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's power, Sugriva trusted him more and bowed again and again in joy.
ramacharitamanas::3991.simple_insight: Real trust grows when you recognize who is truly strong enough to carry the burden.
ramacharitamanas::3991.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Sugriva has just heard Ram's promise against Bali. Now he sees Ram's unmatched strength for himself, and doubt turns into joyful certainty. The sight of power becomes the birth of trust.
ramacharitamanas::3991.modern_relevance: You watch someone handle the crisis you were dreading, and your chest finally loosens. The proof isn't in promises anymore — it's in what they can actually do.
ramacharitamanas::3991.insight: It shifts trust from hope to recognition, and turns reverence into joyful surrender.

ramacharitamanas::3992.verse_sanskrit: उपजा ग्यान बचन तब बोला। नाथ कृपाँ मन भयउ अलोला॥ सुख संपति परिवार बड़ाई। सब परिहरि करिहउँ सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3992.verse_hindi: जब ज्ञान उत्पन्न हुआ तब वे ये वचन बोले कि हे नाथ! आपकी कृपा से अब मेरा मन स्थिर हो गया। सुख, संपत्ति, परिवार और बड़ाई (बड़प्पन) सबको त्यागकर मैं आपकी सेवा ही करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3992.english_translation: When understanding arose, he spoke these words: “Lord, by your grace my mind has become steady. Leaving behind comfort, wealth, family, and status, I will serve you alone.”
ramacharitamanas::3992.translation_literal: उपजा (arose) / ग्यान (understanding) / बचन (words) / तब (then) / बोला (spoke) / नाथ (Lord) / कृपाँ (by grace) / मन (mind) / भयउ (became) / अलोला (unshaken) / सुख (comfort) / संपति (wealth) / परिवार (family) / बड़ाई (status) / सब (all) / परिहरि (leaving behind) / करिहउँ (I will do) / सेवकाई (service)
ramacharitamanas::3992.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3992.essence: Grace makes every other claim on you feel smaller.
ramacharitamanas::3992.simple_meaning: Sugriva says that by Ram's grace his mind is calm, and he will give up comfort, wealth, family, and status to serve Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3992.simple_insight: Real devotion changes your priorities without force. What once seemed essential quietly loses its hold.
ramacharitamanas::3992.detailed_meaning: After seeing Ram's power, Sugriva's trust deepens into surrender. In front of Ram, he says his mind has become steady by grace and that he will leave behind comfort, wealth, family, and status to serve alone.
ramacharitamanas::3992.modern_relevance: You finally realize the promotion, the praise, and the polished image were never the center of your life. Something deeper has settled, and you want to serve what matters.
ramacharitamanas::3992.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to a complete reordering of life around service.

ramacharitamanas::3993.verse_sanskrit: ए सब राम भगति के बाधक। कहहिं संत तव पद अवराधक॥ सत्रु मित्र सुख, दुख जग माहीं। मायाकृत परमारथ नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3993.verse_hindi: क्योंकि आपके चरणों की आराधना करने वाले संत कहते हैं कि ये सब (सुख-संपत्ति आदि) राम भक्ति के विरोधी हैं। जगत् में जितने भी शत्रु-मित्र और सुख-दुःख (आदि द्वंद्व) हैं, सब के सब मायारचित हैं, परमार्थतः (वास्तव में) नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3993.english_translation: Because saints who worship your feet say that these things are obstacles to Ram's devotion. In this world, enemies and friends, pleasure and pain are all made by illusion; in ultimate reality, they are not real.
ramacharitamanas::3993.translation_literal: ए (these) / सब (all) / राम (Ram) / भगति (devotion) / के (of) / बाधक (obstacles) / कहहिं (say) / संत (saints) / तव (your) / पद (feet) / अवराधक (those who worship)॥ / सत्रु (enemy) / मित्र (friend) / सुख (pleasure) / दुख (pain) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / मायाकृत (made by illusion) / परमारथ (ultimate reality) / नाहीं (not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3993.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3993.essence: The world’s opposites lose power when devotion becomes your center.
ramacharitamanas::3993.simple_meaning: Saints say that comfort, status, friends, enemies, pleasure, and pain all distract from devotion. These opposites belong to appearance, not ultimate reality.
ramacharitamanas::3993.simple_insight: You stop being pulled around by life’s swings and begin to rest in what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3993.detailed_meaning: Sugriva is speaking to Ram after his trust begins to deepen. He sees that wealth, family, status, and even the usual opposites of life cannot compete with devotion. The verse turns his grief into clear renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::3993.modern_relevance: You get praised at work one day and ignored the next. A friend cheers you, then disappoints you. This verse says both swings are temporary patterns, not the center of your life.
ramacharitamanas::3993.insight: It shifts attention away from emotional opposites and toward what remains steady beneath them.

ramacharitamanas::3994.verse_sanskrit: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3994.verse_hindi: हे श्री रामजी! बालि तो मेरा परम हितकारी है, जिसकी कृपा से शोक का नाश करने वाले आप मुझे मिले और जिसके साथ अब स्वप्न में भी लड़ाई हो तो जागने पर उसे समझकर मन में संकोच होगा (कि स्वप्न में भी मैं उससे क्यों लड़ा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3994.english_translation: Bali is my greatest well-wisher, by whose grace I met you, Ram, the remover of sorrow. Even a dream-fight with him would make my heart hesitate in shame when I wake.
ramacharitamanas::3994.translation_literal: बालि (Bali) / परम (highest) / हित (well-being, benefactor) / जासु (whose) / प्रसादा (by grace) / मिलेहु (you met) / राम (Ram) / तुम्ह (you) / समन (remover) / बिषादा (sorrow) / सपनें (in a dream) / जेहि (with whom) / सन (with) / होइ (happens) / लराई (fight) / जागें (upon waking) / समुझत (understanding) / मन (mind) / सकुचाई (hesitates, feels shy)
ramacharitamanas::3994.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3994.essence: Even your worst conflict can become the road to grace.
ramacharitamanas::3994.simple_meaning: Sugriva says Bali is still his greatest benefactor, because the conflict with Bali led him to Ram. Even the memory of fighting Bali now feels shameful to him.
ramacharitamanas::3994.simple_insight: Gratitude can transform resentment into humility.
ramacharitamanas::3994.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva has just found safety beside Ram after years of fear and exile. Looking back on his old conflict with Bali, he sees that even that painful struggle became the path that brought him to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3994.modern_relevance: You look back at a breakup, a firing, or a humiliating argument and realise it pushed you toward the people who truly changed your life.
ramacharitamanas::3994.insight: It shifts you from blaming the wound to noticing the help hidden inside it.

ramacharitamanas::3995.verse_sanskrit: अब प्रभु कृपा करहु एहि भाँति। सब तजि भजनु करौं दिन राती॥ सुनि बिराग संजुत कपि बानी। बोले बिहँसि रामु धनुपानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3995.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो अब तो इस प्रकार कृपा कीजिए कि सब छोड़कर दिन-रात मैं आपका भजन ही करूँ। सुग्रीव की वैराग्ययुक्त वाणी सुनकर (उसके क्षणिक वैराग्य को देखकर) हाथ में धनुष धारण करने वाले श्री रामजी मुस्कुराकर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3995.english_translation: “O Lord, now grant me this grace: let me leave everything and spend day and night in your devotion.” Hearing the monkey’s words of renunciation, bow in hand, Ram smiled and spoke.
ramacharitamanas::3995.translation_literal: अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / कृपा (grace) / करहु (do) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / सब (everything) / तजि (leaving) / भजनु (devotion) / करौं (I may do) / दिन राती (day and night) / सुनि (hearing) / बिराग संजुत (joined with renunciation) / कपि बानी (the monkey's words) / बोले (spoke) / बिहँसि (smiling) / रामु (Ram) / धनुपानी (bow in hand)
ramacharitamanas::3995.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::3995.essence: Renunciation becomes complete when it turns into love.
ramacharitamanas::3995.simple_meaning: Sugriva asks for grace to give up everything else and spend day and night in devotion. Ram hears the sincere longing and smiles at the words.
ramacharitamanas::3995.simple_insight: Real renunciation is not emptiness; it is making room for wholehearted love.
ramacharitamanas::3995.detailed_meaning: After the alliance is formed in Kishkindhakand, Sugriva speaks like a seeker who has tasted loss and wants only Ram. His words show renunciation turning into devotion, and Ram smiles because he sees the heart behind them.
ramacharitamanas::3995.modern_relevance: You finally stop chasing the next promotion, the next distraction, the next excuse — and realize you want a life that actually points somewhere. That quiet turn is what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::3995.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered wanting to single-hearted devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3996.verse_sanskrit: जो कछु कहेहु सत्य सब सोई। सखा बचन मम मृषा न होई॥ नट मरकट इव सबहि नचावत। रामु खगेस बेद अस गावत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3996.verse_hindi: तुमने जो कुछ कहा है, वह सभी सत्य है, परंतु हे सखा! मेरा वचन मिथ्या नहीं होता (अर्थात् बालि मारा जाएगा और तुम्हें राज्य मिलेगा)। (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं कि-) हे पक्षियों के राजा गरुड़! नट (मदारी) के बंदर की तरह श्री रामजी सबको नचाते हैं, वेद ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3996.english_translation: Whatever you have said is entirely true, friend; my word is never false. Like a puppeteer making monkeys dance, Ram moves everyone, as the Vedas declare.
ramacharitamanas::3996.translation_literal: जो (whatever) / कछु (anything) / कहेहु (you said) / सत्य (true) / सब (all) / सोई (that only) / सखा (friend) / बचन (word) / मम (my) / मृषा (false) / न (not) / होई (becomes)॥ / नट (puppeteer) / मरकट (monkeys) / इव (like) / सबहि (everyone) / नचावत (making dance) / रामु (Ram) / खगेस (king of birds) / बेद (the Vedas) / अस (thus) / गावत (sing)॥
ramacharitamanas::3996.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3996.essence: Ram's promise is true, and everything moves in his hands.
ramacharitamanas::3996.simple_meaning: Ram reassures Sugriva that his promise is true, then teaches that Ram moves all beings just as a puppeteer moves monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::3996.simple_insight: You can rest when the one guiding events is trustworthy beyond doubt.
ramacharitamanas::3996.detailed_meaning: Sugriva has just opened his heart to Ram, asking for protection and a life of devotion. Ram answers with reassurance: the promise is real, and the larger order of the world is not random. Even the Vedas describe Ram as the one who moves all beings.
ramacharitamanas::3996.modern_relevance: You finally tell the one person you trust what you need, and they answer without hesitation. The relief is not just in their promise — it's in knowing the whole situation is held by something steadier than your fear.
ramacharitamanas::3996.insight: It shifts you from anxious self-management to trust in a larger, reliable order.

ramacharitamanas::3997.verse_sanskrit: लै सुग्रीव संग रघुनाथा। चले चाप सायक गहि हाथा॥ तब रघुपति सुग्रीव पठावा। गर्जेसि जाइ निकट बल पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3997.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर सुग्रीव को साथ लेकर और हाथों में धनुष-बाण धारण करके श्री रघुनाथजी चले। तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने सुग्रीव को बालि के पास भेजा। वह श्री रामजी का बल पाकर बालि के निकट जाकर गरजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3997.english_translation: Then, taking Sugriva along, Raghunath set out with bow and arrows in hand. Then Raghupati sent Sugriva near Bali, and Sugriva, empowered by Ram's strength, went close and roared.
ramacharitamanas::3997.translation_literal: लै (taking) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / संग (with) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / चले (walked/left) / चाप (bow) / सायक (arrows) / गहि (holding) / हाथा (in hands) ॥ / तब (then) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / पठावा (sent) / गर्जेसि (roared) / जाइ (going) / निकट (near) / बल (strength) / पावा (obtained) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3997.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3997.essence: Ram's backing makes Sugriva bold enough to face Bali.
ramacharitamanas::3997.simple_meaning: Ram and Sugriva move toward Bali together. Ram arms himself, sends Sugriva forward, and Sugriva confronts Bali with Ram's strength behind him.
ramacharitamanas::3997.simple_insight: Support can turn fear into courage.
