ramacharitamanas::3997.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram has agreed to help Sugriva regain his kingdom. Armed with bow and arrows, he walks with Sugriva to the edge of danger, then sends him forward to challenge Bali. The verse shows alliance becoming action.
ramacharitamanas::3997.modern_relevance: You walk into a hard conversation with someone backing you up. Their presence changes your voice before you even speak.
ramacharitamanas::3997.insight: It turns private support into public courage and moves the ally from promise to action.

ramacharitamanas::3998.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बालि क्रोधातुर धावा। गहि कर चरन नारि समुझावा॥ सुनु पति जिन्हहि मिलेउ सुग्रीवा। ते द्वौ बंधु तेज बल सींवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3998.verse_hindi: बालि सुनते ही क्रोध में भरकर वेग से दौड़ा। उसकी स्त्री तारा ने चरण पकड़कर उसे समझाया कि हे नाथ! सुनिए, सुग्रीव जिनसे मिले हैं वे दोनों भाई तेज और बल की सीमा हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3998.english_translation: As soon as Bali heard it, he rushed out in a rage. His wife Tara caught his feet and tried to warn him: "Listen, my lord. The two brothers whom Sugriva has joined are beyond measure in valor and strength."
ramacharitamanas::3998.translation_literal: सुनत (upon hearing) / बालि (Bali) / क्रोधातुर (overtaken by anger) / धावा (rushed) / गहि (grasping) / कर (with hand) / चरन (feet) / नारि (the woman/wife) / समुझावा (counseled) ॥ सुनु (listen) / पति (lord/husband) / जिन्हहि (those whom) / मिलेउ (has met) / सुग्रीवा (Sugriva) / ते (they) / द्वौ (two) / बंधु (brothers) / तेज (splendour) / बल (strength) / सींवा (limit/boundary) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3998.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3998.essence: Anger can outrun wisdom even when danger is plain.
ramacharitamanas::3998.simple_meaning: Bali hears the news and charges forward in anger, while Tara tries to stop him by warning that Sugriva has joined two brothers of immense power.
ramacharitamanas::3998.simple_insight: Anger can make you ignore the one person trying to save you.
ramacharitamanas::3998.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva has allied with Ram and Lakshman against Bali. The news reaches Bali, and fury takes over at once. Tara sees the danger clearly and pleads with him, but his pride is already pulling him into disaster.
ramacharitamanas::3998.modern_relevance: You get one text, feel insulted, and fire back before reading the whole message. The calmer voice beside you sees the danger, but anger has already started driving.
ramacharitamanas::3998.insight: It shows how rage blinds judgment and how warning is wasted on a heated mind.

ramacharitamanas::3999.verse_sanskrit: कोसलेस सुत लछिमन रामा। कालहु जीति सकहिं संग्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3999.verse_hindi: वे कोसलाधीश दशरथजी के पुत्र राम और लक्ष्मण संग्राम में काल को भी जीत सकते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3999.english_translation: Rama and Lakshmana, sons of King Dasharatha of Kosala, can defeat even death in battle.
ramacharitamanas::3999.translation_literal: कोसलेस (of Kosala's lord) / सुत (sons) / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / रामा (Rama) / कालहु (even death) / जीति (conquer) / सकहिं (can) / संग्रामा (in battle)
ramacharitamanas::3999.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3999.essence: Some courage is so complete that even death yields.
ramacharitamanas::3999.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are so powerful in battle that even death cannot stand against them.
ramacharitamanas::3999.simple_insight: Real strength is not just skill — it is courage that does not flinch before the greatest fear.
ramacharitamanas::3999.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the alliance with Sugriva is turning toward confrontation with Bali. This line praises Rama and Lakshmana as warriors of overwhelming power, setting up the confidence and fear that shape the coming clash.
ramacharitamanas::3999.modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you feel your chest tighten because the stakes are real. This verse meets that moment with steadiness: some people enter conflict with such force and clarity that fear itself loses.
ramacharitamanas::3999.insight: It frames courage as a power that can face even death without hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::4000.verse_sanskrit: कह बाली सुनु भीरु प्रिय समदरसी रघुनाथ। जौं कदाचि मोहि मारहिं तौ पुनि होउँ सनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4000.verse_hindi: बालि ने कहा- हे भीरु! (डरपोक) प्रिये! सुनो, श्री रघुनाथजी समदर्शी हैं। जो कदाचित् वे मुझे मारेंगे ही तो मैं सनाथ हो जाऊँगा (परमपद पा जाऊँगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4000.english_translation: Bali said, “Listen, dear and timid one: Raghunath sees all beings equally. If he should kill me, I will at last be truly sheltered.”
ramacharitamanas::4000.translation_literal: कह (said) / बाली (Bali) / सुनु (listen) / भीरु (timid one) / प्रिय (dear) / समदरसी (seeing all equally) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / जौं (if) / कदाचि (perhaps) / मोहि (me) / मारहिं (will kill) / तौ (then) / पुनि (again/at last) / होउँ (I become) / सनाथ (one with a shelter/with refuge)
ramacharitamanas::4000.speaker: Bali
ramacharitamanas::4000.essence: Even death becomes refuge in the hands of one who sees equally.
ramacharitamanas::4000.simple_meaning: Bali recognizes that Ram judges no one by bias. Even if Ram kills him, Bali believes that death will bring him shelter, not ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4000.simple_insight: There is peace in being seen without bias, even in the face of loss.
ramacharitamanas::4000.detailed_meaning: Bali has just been warned that Ram and Lakshman are no ordinary opponents. Instead of rage, he speaks with unexpected clarity: Ram sees all beings equally, and even death at Ram's hands would mean true refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4000.modern_relevance: When someone you respect corrects you sharply, your first reaction is to defend yourself. But sometimes the harder truth is also the safer one: being honestly seen can be a kind of rescue.
ramacharitamanas::4000.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of punishment to trust in fair seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4001.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि चला महा अभिमानी। तृन समान सुग्रीवहि जानी॥ भिरे उभौ बाली अति तर्जा। मुठिका मारि महाधुनि गर्जा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4001.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर वह महान् अभिमानी बालि सुग्रीव को तिनके के समान जानकर चला। दोनों भिड़ गए। बालि ने सुग्रीव को बहुत धमकाया और घूँसा मारकर बड़े जोर से गरजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4001.english_translation: Saying this, the greatly arrogant Bali went on, seeing Sugriva as no more than a blade of grass. The two clashed; Bali threatened Sugriva fiercely, struck him with a fist, and roared loudly.
ramacharitamanas::4001.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / चला (went) / महा (greatly) / अभिमानी (arrogant) / तृन (grass) / समान (like) / सुग्रीवहि (Sugriva) / जानी (having regarded) / भिरे (clashed) / उभौ (both) / बाली (Bali) / अति (very) / तर्जा (threatened) / मुठिका (fist) / मारि (having struck) / महा (greatly) / धुनि (sound) / गर्जा (roared)
ramacharitamanas::4001.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4001.essence: Pride makes an opponent seem smaller than human.
ramacharitamanas::4001.simple_meaning: Bali, full of pride, treats Sugriva as nothing and attacks him. The fight begins with threats, a blow, and a furious roar.
ramacharitamanas::4001.simple_insight: Pride makes another person look smaller than they are.
ramacharitamanas::4001.detailed_meaning: After Bali dismisses Sugriva, the rivalry turns physical. Bali rushes in with contempt, and the brothers clash. This moment shows the force of Bali's arrogance before Sugriva flees to seek Ram's help.
ramacharitamanas::4001.modern_relevance: A heated argument starts when someone decides the other person doesn't matter. The insult comes first; the blow, whether spoken or physical, follows.
ramacharitamanas::4001.insight: It shows how arrogance turns conflict into humiliation before the fight is even over.

ramacharitamanas::4002.verse_sanskrit: तब सुग्रीव बिकल होइ भागा। मुष्टि प्रहार बज्र सम लागा॥ मैं जो कहा रघुबीर कृपाला। बंधु न होइ मोर यह काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4002.verse_hindi: तब सुग्रीव व्याकुल होकर भागा। घूँसे की चोट उसे वज्र के समान लगी (सुग्रीव ने आकर कहा-) हे कृपालु रघुवीर! मैंने आपसे पहले ही कहा था कि बालि मेरा भाई नहीं है, काल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4002.english_translation: Then Sugriva, overwhelmed, fled. The blow of the fist struck like a thunderbolt. “I told you, merciful Raghubir, that Bali is not my brother — he is my death.”
ramacharitamanas::4002.translation_literal: तब (then) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / होइ (having become) / भागा (ran away) । मुष्टि (fist) / प्रहार (strike) / बज्र (thunderbolt) / सम (like) / लागा (felt, struck) । मैं (I) / जो (what) / कहा (said) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / कृपाला (merciful) । बंधु (brother) / न (not) / होइ (is) / मोर (my) / यह (this) / काला (death, dark fate) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4002.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4002.essence: Fear turns a brother into a force of death.
ramacharitamanas::4002.simple_meaning: Sugriva runs in fear after Bali's blow lands hard. He cries out to Ram that Bali is not a brother to him, but death itself.
ramacharitamanas::4002.simple_insight: Fear makes the body flee before the mind can explain itself.
ramacharitamanas::4002.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Bali's power overwhelms Sugriva in the duel. Wounded and terrified, Sugriva runs to Ram and protests that Bali is no brother to him now, only death. The verse deepens the crisis before Ram intervenes.
ramacharitamanas::4002.modern_relevance: You freeze in a confrontation, then blurt out the truth to the one person you trust. In panic, even family can feel like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::4002.insight: It shows how fear strips away polite language and reveals raw dependence on help.

ramacharitamanas::4003.verse_sanskrit: एक रूप तुम्ह भ्राता दोऊ तेहि भ्रम तें नहिं मारेउँ सोऊ॥ कर परसा सुग्रीव सरीरा। तनु भा कुलिस गई सब पीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4003.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) तुम दोनों भाइयों का एक सा ही रूप है। इसी भ्रम से मैंने उसको नहीं मारा। फिर श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव के शरीर को हाथ से स्पर्श किया, जिससे उसका शरीर वज्र के समान हो गया और सारी पीड़ा जाती रही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4003.english_translation: (Lord Ram said:) Your two brothers look exactly alike. Because of that confusion, I did not kill him. Then Ram touched Sugriva's body with his hand, and his body became like thunderbolt; all pain disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::4003.translation_literal: एक रूप (one form / alike) / तुम्ह (your) / भ्राता (brothers) / दोऊ (both) / तेहि (that) / भ्रम तें (because of confusion) / नहिं (not) / मारेउँ (I killed) / सोऊ (him) / कर (hand) / परसा (touched) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सरीरा (body) / तनु (body) / भा (became) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / गई (went away) / सब (all) / पीरा (pain)
ramacharitamanas::4003.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4003.essence: Mercy can heal even the confusion it did not cause.
ramacharitamanas::4003.simple_meaning: Ram explains that he mistook the brothers for each other, so he did not kill the wrong one. Then his touch restores Sugriva's strength and removes his pain.
ramacharitamanas::4003.simple_insight: Even a mistaken blow can be healed by a merciful touch.
ramacharitamanas::4003.detailed_meaning: After Bali has driven Sugriva into fear, Ram explains why he did not strike before: the two brothers looked alike. Then, in the same scene, Ram comforts Sugriva with a touch that restores his body and ends his pain.
ramacharitamanas::4003.modern_relevance: You misread a situation, say the wrong thing, and someone is hurt. A calm explanation and a caring touch can repair what panic made worse.
ramacharitamanas::4003.insight: It shows that clarity and compassion can follow confusion without shame.

ramacharitamanas::4004.verse_sanskrit: मेली कंठ सुमन कै माला। पठवा पुनि बल देइ बिसाला॥ पुनि नाना बिधि भई लराई। बिटप ओट देखहिं रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4004.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव के गले में फूलों की माला डाल दी और फिर उसे बड़ा भारी बल देकर भेजा। दोनों में पुनः अनेक प्रकार से युद्ध हुआ। श्री रघुनाथजी वृक्ष की आड़ से देख रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4004.english_translation: Then Ram placed a garland of flowers around Sugriva's neck and gave him great strength. The two fought again in many ways, while Raghunath watched from behind a tree.
ramacharitamanas::4004.translation_literal: मेली (placed) / कंठ (neck) / सुमन कै माला (garland of flowers) / पठवा (sent) / पुनि (again) / बल देइ (giving strength) / बिसाला (great) / पुनि (again) / नाना बिधि (many ways) / भई (happened) / लराई (fight) / बिटप ओट (behind a tree) / देखहिं (watching) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::4004.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4004.essence: Real help empowers action, then steps back.
ramacharitamanas::4004.simple_meaning: Ram blesses Sugriva, strengthens him, and sends him back into battle. Then the two fight again while Ram watches from hiding.
ramacharitamanas::4004.simple_insight: Sometimes support comes first, and only then does the real test begin.
ramacharitamanas::4004.detailed_meaning: After Ram realizes the brothers were mistaken for each other, he restores Sugriva with a flower garland and renewed strength. The rivalry is not over yet; the decisive duel with Bali is still to come, and Ram waits hidden behind a tree.
ramacharitamanas::4004.modern_relevance: A coach gives you one last pep talk before the match, then steps back and lets the contest unfold. Help can steady you, but it cannot replace the moment of action.
ramacharitamanas::4004.insight: It shows support followed by restraint: strengthen the ally, then wait for the right opening.

ramacharitamanas::4005.verse_sanskrit: बहु छल बल सुग्रीव कर हियँ हारा भय मानि। मारा बालि राम तब हृदय माझ सर तानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4005.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव ने बहुत से छल-बल किए, किंतु (अंत में) भय मानकर हृदय से हार गया। तब श्री रामजी ने तानकर बालि के हृदय में बाण मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4005.english_translation: Sugriva used many tricks and displays of strength, but in the end he was overcome by fear and admitted defeat. Then Ram drew his bow and shot an arrow into Bali's chest.
ramacharitamanas::4005.translation_literal: बहु (many) / छल (tricks) / बल (strength) / सुग्रीव कर (of Sugriva) / हियँ (in heart) / हारा (was defeated) / भय (fear) / मानि (having accepted) / मारा (struck) / बालि (Bali) / राम (Ram) / तब (then) / हृदय माझ (in the middle of the heart) / सर (arrow) / तानि (drawing)
ramacharitamanas::4005.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4005.essence: Fear breaks the contest; Ram's arrow ends it.
ramacharitamanas::4005.simple_meaning: Sugriva finally gave in, and Ram shot Bali with an arrow to end the fight.
ramacharitamanas::4005.simple_insight: Sometimes a conflict ends not with more force, but with the moment someone can no longer hold out.
ramacharitamanas::4005.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva has been tested and Bali has been drawn into a fatal confrontation. This couplet simply marks the turning point: Sugriva yields in fear, and Ram releases the arrow that will decide the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::4005.modern_relevance: A tense argument has gone on too long, and everyone knows the real decision is about to land. This is the moment when the outcome changes, not the talking.
ramacharitamanas::4005.insight: It shifts attention from the struggle itself to the decisive act that ends it.

ramacharitamanas::4006.verse_sanskrit: परा बिकल महि सर के लागें। पुनि उठि बैठ देखि प्रभु आगे॥ स्याम गात सिर जटा बनाएँ। अरुन नयन सर चाप चढ़ाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4006.verse_hindi: बाण के लगते ही बालि व्याकुल होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, किंतु प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी को आगे देखकर वह फिर उठ बैठा। भगवान् का श्याम शरीर है, सिर पर जटा बनाए हैं, लाल नेत्र हैं, बाण लिए हैं और धनुष चढ़ाए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4006.english_translation: Struck by the arrow, Bali fell to the ground in distress, then rose and sat up when he saw Lord Ram before him. The Lord has a dark body, matted hair on his head, red eyes, a drawn bow, and an arrow ready.
ramacharitamanas::4006.translation_literal: परा (fell) / बिकल (distressed) / महि (on the ground) / सर (arrow) / के लागें (having been struck) / पुनि (again) / उठि (rising) / बैठ (sat) / देखि (seeing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आगे (in front) / स्याम (dark) / गात (body) / सिर (head) / जटा (matted hair) / बनाएँ (having made) / अरुन (red) / नयन (eyes) / सर (arrow) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ाएँ (drawn)
ramacharitamanas::4006.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4006.essence: Seeing Ram turns pain into recognition.
ramacharitamanas::4006.simple_meaning: Bali is hit, falls down, then sits up again when he sees Ram standing before him. Ram is shown as a poised warrior with bow and arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4006.simple_insight: Even in pain, seeing the divine presence changes the whole moment.
ramacharitamanas::4006.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram has just shot Bali. This verse pauses on Bali’s stunned body and on Ram’s calm, armed presence before him. The scene is still moving toward Bali’s final recognition and surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4006.modern_relevance: You get the bad news, sit frozen for a second, then look up and see the person you most needed to face. The moment changes because presence changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::4006.insight: It slows the scene to show that recognition comes before surrender. The wounded mind must first see clearly.

ramacharitamanas::4007.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि चितइ चरन चित दीन्हा। सुफल जन्म माना प्रभु चीन्हा॥ हृदयँ प्रीति मुख बचन कठोरा। बोला चितइ राम की ओरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4007.verse_hindi: बालि ने बार-बार भगवान् की ओर देखकर चित्त को उनके चरणों में लगा दिया। प्रभु को पहचानकर उसने अपना जन्म सफल माना। उसके हृदय में प्रीति थी, पर मुख में कठोर वचन थे। वह श्री रामजी की ओर देखकर बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4007.english_translation: Again and again he looked at Ram's feet and fixed his mind there. Recognizing the Lord, he felt his birth had become fruitful. His heart held love, but his mouth spoke harshly. Looking toward Ram, he said:
ramacharitamanas::4007.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / चितइ (looking at) / चरन (feet) / चित (mind) / दीन्हा (gave) / सुफल (fruitful) / जन्म (birth) / माना (considered) / प्रभु (Lord) / चीन्हा (recognized) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / प्रीति (love) / मुख (mouth) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (hard) / बोला (spoke) / चितइ (looking) / राम (Ram) / की ओर (toward)
ramacharitamanas::4007.speaker: Bali
ramacharitamanas::4007.essence: Recognition can soften the heart without fully healing the wound.
ramacharitamanas::4007.simple_meaning: Bali sees Ram clearly and feels blessed by the encounter, even as he speaks with bitterness on the outside. It is the moment before his final words of accusation.
ramacharitamanas::4007.simple_insight: Love can be real even when pain makes the voice sharp.
ramacharitamanas::4007.detailed_meaning: After Ram's arrow strikes Bali, the dying vanara rises and looks again and again at Ram's feet. He knows the Lord before him and feels his life has found meaning, but his wounded pride still shapes his speech. The verse sets up his final complaint.
ramacharitamanas::4007.modern_relevance: You can be deeply moved by someone and still speak from old hurt. Recognition and resentment can live in the same heart for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::4007.insight: It shows how devotion and injury can coexist, and why the next words still carry pain.

ramacharitamanas::4008.verse_sanskrit: धर्म हेतु अवतरेहु गोसाईं। मारेहु मोहि ब्याध की नाईं॥ मैं बैरी सुग्रीव पिआरा। अवगुन कवन नाथ मोहि मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4008.verse_hindi: हे गोसाईं। आपने धर्म की रक्षा के लिए अवतार लिया है और मुझे व्याध की तरह (छिपकर) मारा? मैं बैरी और सुग्रीव प्यारा? हे नाथ! किस दोष से आपने मुझे मारा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4008.english_translation: O Lord, you have incarnated to uphold dharma, yet you struck me like a hunter from hiding? I am your enemy, and Sugriva is dear to you—by what fault did you kill me?
ramacharitamanas::4008.translation_literal: धर्म (righteous order) / हेतु (for the sake of) / अवतरेहु (you incarnated) / गोसाईं (Lord) / मारेहु (you struck) / मोहि (me) / ब्याध (hunter) / की नाईं (like) / मैं (I) / बैरी (enemy) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / पिआरा (dear) / अवगुन (fault) / कवन (which) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (me) / मारा (killed)
ramacharitamanas::4008.speaker: Vali
ramacharitamanas::4008.essence: Wounded pride can make justice feel like betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::4008.simple_meaning: Vali, dying, accuses Ram of killing him from hiding and questions why Ram favored Sugriva over him.
ramacharitamanas::4008.simple_insight: Pain can make even a just defeat feel like betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::4008.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Vali lies wounded before Ram after being struck by an arrow. He knows Ram is divine and that the act was tied to dharma, yet grief and shock spill out as accusation. This verse captures the wounded cry before Ram answers.
ramacharitamanas::4008.modern_relevance: You get blamed in a group chat after someone cuts you off mid-sentence, and your first reaction is, 'Why did you do that to me?' Hurt often speaks before understanding.
ramacharitamanas::4008.insight: It shows how wounded pride turns a moral event into a personal grievance.

ramacharitamanas::4009.verse_sanskrit: अनुज बधू भगिनी सुत नारी। सुनु सठ कन्या सम ए चारी॥ इन्हहि कुदृष्टि बिलोकइ जोई। ताहि बधें कछु पाप न होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4009.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मूर्ख! सुन, छोटे भाई की स्त्री, बहिन, पुत्र की स्त्री और कन्या- ये चारों समान हैं। इनको जो कोई बुरी दृष्टि से देखता है, उसे मारने में कुछ भी पाप नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4009.english_translation: O fool, listen: your younger brother’s wife, your sister, your son’s wife, and your daughter are all the same. Whoever looks at them with lustful intent deserves no blame if punished.
ramacharitamanas::4009.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / बधू (wife) / भगिनी (sister) / सुत (son) / नारी (woman) / सुनु (listen) / सठ (fool) / कन्या (daughter) / सम (equal) / ए (these) / चारी (four) ॥ इन्हहि (these) / कुदृष्टि (evil glance) / बिलोकइ (looks at) / जोई (whoever) / ताहि (that one) / बधें (in killing) / कछु (some) / पाप (sin) / न (not) / होई (is) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4009.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4009.essence: Right seeing protects both the other person and your own character.
ramacharitamanas::4009.simple_meaning: Ram says that a younger brother’s wife, a sister, a son’s wife, and a daughter must all be seen as equal and protected from lustful looking.
ramacharitamanas::4009.simple_insight: Purity begins with how you look at people.
ramacharitamanas::4009.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram is judging Bali after the fatal arrow. Bali still speaks, but Ram answers with a moral line: certain relationships must never be viewed with desire, and violating that boundary is a serious wrong.
ramacharitamanas::4009.modern_relevance: You notice your eyes lingering where they should not, then feel the quiet shame afterward. This verse draws a hard line: train your gaze before desire trains you.
ramacharitamanas::4009.insight: It shifts the mind from consuming others to protecting them through disciplined seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4010.verse_sanskrit: मूढ़ तोहि अतिसय अभिमाना। नारि सिखावन करसि न काना॥ मम भुज बल आश्रित तेहि जानी। मारा चहसि अधम अभिमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4010.verse_hindi: हे मूढ़! तुझे अत्यंत अभिमान है। तूने अपनी स्त्री की सीख पर भी कान (ध्यान) नहीं दिया। सुग्रीव को मेरी भुजाओं के बल का आश्रित जानकर भी अरे अधम अभिमानी! तूने उसको मारना चाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4010.english_translation: You are utterly proud, fool. You would not even listen to your wife’s counsel. Knowing that Sugriva was protected by my arms, you still wanted to kill him, arrogant wretch.
ramacharitamanas::4010.translation_literal: मूढ़ (foolish) / तोहि (you) / अतिसय (extremely) / अभिमाना (proud) / नारि (wife) / सिखावन (advice) / करसि (you do) / काना (ear/listen) / मम (my) / भुज (arms) / बल (strength) / आश्रित (dependent on) / तेहि (him) / जानी (knowing) / मारा (to kill) / चहसि (you wish) / अधम (lowly) / अभिमानी (proud one)
ramacharitamanas::4010.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4010.essence: Pride makes you deaf to the counsel that could save you.
ramacharitamanas::4010.simple_meaning: Ravana is being called out for his arrogance. He ignored wise counsel, forgot Sugriva was under Ram’s protection, and still tried to harm him.
ramacharitamanas::4010.simple_insight: Pride cuts you off from guidance and makes you violate your own better judgment.
ramacharitamanas::4010.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram has just confronted Bali from hiding. Bali’s anger is still burning, but Ram exposes the real wound beneath it: arrogance. Bali ignored advice, misread protection, and let pride turn him against himself.
ramacharitamanas::4010.modern_relevance: You keep arguing in the group chat even after three people warn you to stop. Later, you realize the real problem was not the advice — it was the part of you that refused to hear it.
ramacharitamanas::4010.insight: It shifts attention from outward blame to the inner pride that blocks clear hearing.

ramacharitamanas::4011.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु राम स्वामी सन चल न चातुरी मोरि। प्रभु अजहूँ मैं पापी अंतकाल गति तोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4011.verse_hindi: (बालि ने कहा-) हे श्री रामजी! सुनिए, स्वामी (आप) से मेरी चतुराई नहीं चल सकती। हे प्रभो! अंतकाल में आपकी गति (शरण) पाकर मैं अब भी पापी ही रहा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4011.english_translation: Listen, Ram, my cleverness cannot work against my Lord. O Lord, even now at the end, I remain sinful while taking refuge in you.
ramacharitamanas::4011.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / स्वामी (Lord) / सन (with) / चल (work) / न (not) / चातुरी (cleverness) / मोरि (my) । / प्रभु (Lord) / अजहूँ (even now) / मैं (I) / पापी (sinful) / अंतकाल (at the end) / गति (refuge, destination) / तोरि (your)
ramacharitamanas::4011.speaker: Bali
ramacharitamanas::4011.essence: Cleverness dies at the feet of surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4011.simple_meaning: Bali admits that his tricks cannot work against Ram. He also admits that, at the end, only Ram's refuge remains for him.
ramacharitamanas::4011.simple_insight: Pride drops away when you see that surrender is the only real opening left.
ramacharitamanas::4011.detailed_meaning: Bali has been exposed after attacking Sugriva. Facing Ram, he stops pretending strength or strategy will help him. In this last moment, he speaks with humility: his cleverness is useless, and only Ram's refuge remains.
ramacharitamanas::4011.modern_relevance: You’ve rehearsed the apology, the excuse, the workaround — and then the moment arrives when none of it matters. What remains is honesty and asking for help.
ramacharitamanas::4011.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble surrender when control has already failed.

ramacharitamanas::4012.verse_sanskrit: सुनत राम अति कोमल बानी। बालि सीस परसेउ निज पानी॥ अचल करौं तनु राखहु प्राना। बालि कहा सुनु कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4012.verse_hindi: बालि की अत्यंत कोमल वाणी सुनकर श्री रामजी ने उसके सिर को अपने हाथ से स्पर्श किया (और कहा-) मैं तुम्हारे शरीर को अचल कर दूँ, तुम प्राणों को रखो। बालि ने कहा- हे कृपानिधान! सुनिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4012.english_translation: Hearing Bali's gentle words, Ram touched his head with his own hand. "I can make your body still; keep your life," Bali said. "Listen, treasure of compassion..."
ramacharitamanas::4012.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / राम (Ram) / अति (very) / कोमल (gentle) / बानी (speech) / बालि (Bali) / सीस (head) / परसेउ (touched) / निज (own) / पानी (hand)॥ / अचल (motionless) / करौं (I will make) / तनु (body) / राखहु (keep) / प्राना (life) / बालि (Bali) / कहा (said) / सुनु (listen) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of compassion) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4012.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4012.essence: Mercy does not disappear when justice is done.
ramacharitamanas::4012.simple_meaning: Bali speaks with humility after Ram’s response. Ram shows mercy even in the middle of a fatal confrontation, and Bali recognises that compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4012.simple_insight: Even in judgment, mercy can remain intact.
ramacharitamanas::4012.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Bali has been struck down and now speaks with unusual softness. Ram responds not with cruelty, but with a touch of grace. This moment shifts the scene from punishment to compassion, revealing Ram’s nature.
ramacharitamanas::4012.modern_relevance: A tense conversation after a breakup, firing, or family conflict can still hold dignity. Even when someone has been hurt, the response does not have to become hard or humiliating.
ramacharitamanas::4012.insight: It teaches you to meet conflict without losing gentleness.

ramacharitamanas::4013.verse_sanskrit: जन्म जन्म मुनि जतनु कराहीं। अंत राम कहि आवत नाहीं॥ जासु नाम बल संकर कासी। देत सबहि सम गति अबिनासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4013.verse_hindi: मुनिगण जन्म-जन्म में (प्रत्येक जन्म में) (अनेकों प्रकार का) साधन करते रहते हैं। फिर भी अंतकाल में उन्हें 'राम' नहीं कह आता (उनके मुख से राम नाम नहीं निकलता)। जिनके नाम के बल से शंकरजी काशी में सबको समान रूप से अविनाशिनी गति (मुक्ति) देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4013.english_translation: Sages practice countless disciplines across many births, yet at the end they still cannot utter Ram's name. By the power of whose name, Shankar in Kashi grants everyone the same undying liberation.
ramacharitamanas::4013.translation_literal: जन्म जन्म (birth after birth) / मुनि (sages) / जतनु (effort, practice) / कराहीं (do) / अंत (at the end) / राम (Ram) / कहि (saying) / आवत (comes) / नाहीं (does not)॥ / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / बल (power) / संकर (Shankar) / कासी (in Kashi) / देत (gives) / सबहि (to everyone) / सम (equal) / गति (state, liberation) / अबिनासी (undying) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4013.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4013.essence: Effort may fail; Ram's name does not.
ramacharitamanas::4013.simple_meaning: Even great sages may practice for life after life and still fail to remember Ram at the end. Ram's name is so powerful that even Shankar gives everyone liberation through it.
ramacharitamanas::4013.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing the deepest refuge is not earned by perfection.
ramacharitamanas::4013.detailed_meaning: Bali has just surrendered, and Ram's mercy is being revealed as greater than cleverness or strength. Tulsidas turns the scene into praise: even long ascetic effort can fail, but Ram's name alone has the power to grant freedom.
ramacharitamanas::4013.modern_relevance: You can spend years perfecting your routine, your discipline, your self-control — and still feel strangely empty when life turns serious. This verse points to a refuge deeper than achievement.
ramacharitamanas::4013.insight: It shifts the mind from self-made spiritual effort to trust in Ram's saving name.

ramacharitamanas::4014.verse_sanskrit: मम लोचन गोचर सोई आवा। बहुरि कि प्रभु अस बनिहि बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4014.verse_hindi: वह श्री रामजी स्वयं मेरे नेत्रों के सामने आ गए हैं। हे प्रभो! ऐसा संयोग क्या फिर कभी बन पड़ेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4014.english_translation: He has come before my eyes. O Lord, will such a meeting happen again?
ramacharitamanas::4014.translation_literal: मम (my) / लोचन (eyes) / गोचर (within sight) / सोई (that very one) / आवा (has come) / बहुरि (again) / कि (whether) / प्रभु (Lord) / अस (such) / बनिहि (will happen) / बनावा (a meeting, an occasion)
ramacharitamanas::4014.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4014.essence: True nearness is precious because it may not return.
ramacharitamanas::4014.simple_meaning: The speaker sees Ram directly and feels wonder that such a blessed meeting may never happen again.
ramacharitamanas::4014.simple_insight: Some moments of grace are so rare they change how you hold them.
ramacharitamanas::4014.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the speaker has come face to face with Ram and is overwhelmed by the sight. The heart recognises a rare meeting with the divine and wonders whether such a moment can ever come again.
ramacharitamanas::4014.modern_relevance: You finally sit across from someone you have longed to meet, and the room goes quiet. A part of you already knows this moment will never feel ordinary again.
ramacharitamanas::4014.insight: It shifts attention from possession to reverent noticing of a rare encounter.

ramacharitamanas::4015.verse_sanskrit: सो नयन गोचर जासु गुन नित नेति कहि श्रुति गावहीं। जिति पवन मन गो निरस करि मुनि ध्यान कबहुँक पावहीं॥ मोहि जानि अति अभिमान बस प्रभु कहेउ राखु सरीरही। अस कवन सठ हठि काटि सुरतरु बारि करिहि बबूरही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4015.verse_hindi: श्रुतियाँ 'नेति-नेति' कहकर निरंतर जिनका गुणगान करती रहती हैं तथा प्राण और मन को जीतकर एवं इंद्रियों को (विषयों के रस से सर्वथा) नीरस बनाकर मुनिगण ध्यान में जिनकी कभी क्वचित् ही झलक पाते हैं, वे ही प्रभु (आप) साक्षात् मेरे सामने प्रकट हैं। आपने मुझे अत्यंत अभिमानवश जानकर यह कहा कि तुम शरीर रख लो, परंतु ऐसा मूर्ख कौन होगा जो हठपूर्वक कल्पवृक्ष को काटकर उससे बबूर के बाड़ लगाएगा (अर्थात् पूर्णकाम बना देने वाले आपको छोड़कर आपसे इस नश्वर शरीर की रक्षा चाहेगा?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4015.english_translation: The sages sing of you with endless "not this, not that." By conquering breath and mind and draining the taste from the senses, they glimpse you only sometimes in meditation. Yet you, the Lord, stand before me now. Knowing me proud, you told me to keep this body—but who would foolishly cut down a wish-fulfilling tree to make a thorn fence?
ramacharitamanas::4015.translation_literal: सो (that) / नयन-गोचर (within the range of the eyes) / जासु (whose) / गुन (qualities) / नित (always) / नेति (not this, not this) / कहि (saying) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गावहीं (sing) / जिति (conquering) / पवन (breath) / मन (mind) / गो (senses) / निरस करि (making tasteless) / मुनि (sages) / ध्यान (meditation) / कबहुँक (sometimes) / पावहीं (attain)॥ मोहि (me) / जानि (knowing) / अति (very) / अभिमान बस (because of pride) / प्रभु (Lord) / कहेउ (said) / राखु (keep) / सरीरही (the body) / अस (such) / कवन (which) / सठ (fool) / हठि (stubbornly) / काटि (cutting) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / बारि (water) / करिहि (would make) / बबूरही (a thorn fence)
ramacharitamanas::4015.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4015.essence: What seekers chase in thought stands before the devotee in person.
ramacharitamanas::4015.simple_meaning: The divine reality is beyond description and hard to reach through meditation, yet Hanuman sees Ram directly. He refuses to keep a fragile body instead of the one who fulfills every wish.
ramacharitamanas::4015.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that what is highest can also be near, personal, and present.
ramacharitamanas::4015.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman stands before Ram for the first time. He praises Ram as the one the Vedas can only circle around in negation, then rejects the idea of clinging to a body when Ram himself is present. The moment turns wonder into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4015.modern_relevance: You spend years trying to name what matters, then one meeting makes everything else feel too small. A mentor, a beloved, a calling — once it appears, you stop bargaining with lesser things.
ramacharitamanas::4015.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract searching to direct recognition and wholehearted surrender.

ramacharitamanas::4016.verse_sanskrit: अब नाथ करि करुना बिलोकहु देहु जो बर मागऊँ। जेहि जोनि जन्मौं कर्म बस तहँ राम पद अनुरागऊँ॥ यह तनय मम सम बिनय बल कल्यानप्रद प्रभु लीजिये। गहि बाँह सुर नर नाह आपन दास अंगद कीजिये ॥
ramacharitamanas::4016.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! अब मुझ पर दयादृष्टि कीजिए और मैं जो वर माँगता हूँ उसे दीजिए। मैं कर्मवश जिस योनि में जन्म लूँ, वहीं श्री रामजी (आप) के चरणों में प्रेम करूँ! हे कल्याणप्रद प्रभो! यह मेरा पुत्र अंगद विनय और बल में मेरे ही समान है, इसे स्वीकार कीजिए और हे देवता और मनुष्यों के नाथ! बाँह पकड़कर इसे अपना दास बनाइए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4016.english_translation: O Lord, now show me your compassion and grant the boon I ask. Wherever I am born by the force of my deeds, let me love Ram's feet there. O gracious Lord, please accept this son of mine, Angad, equal to me in humility and strength, and taking him by the arm, make him your servant, O lord of gods and humans.
ramacharitamanas::4016.translation_literal: अब (now) / नाथ (Lord) / करि (doing) / करुना (compassion) / बिलोकहु (look upon) / देहु (give) / जो (which) / बर (boon) / मागऊँ (I ask) / जेहि (wherever) / जोनि (birth-form) / जन्मौं (I am born) / कर्म (deeds) / बस (under the force of) / तहँ (there) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / अनुरागऊँ (I may love) ॥ यह (this) / तनय (son) / मम (my) / सम (equal) / बिनय (humility) / बल (strength) / कल्यानप्रद (giver of welfare) / प्रभु (Lord) / लीजिये (please take) / गहि (grasping) / बाँह (arm) / सुर (devas) / नर (humans) / नाह (lord) / आपन (your own) / दास (servant) / अंगद (Angad) / कीजिये (make)
ramacharitamanas::4016.speaker: Bali
ramacharitamanas::4016.essence: Love for Ram can survive every birth and every change.
ramacharitamanas::4016.simple_meaning: Bali asks for one blessing: no matter where he is born in future lives, he wants love for Ram to remain in his heart. He also asks Ram to accept Angad as a servant.
ramacharitamanas::4016.simple_insight: True devotion is not limited by one life, one body, or one circumstance.
ramacharitamanas::4016.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Bali is facing death after his confrontation with Ram. Instead of bargaining for life, he asks for one thing only: to keep loving Ram in every future birth. He also offers Angad into Ram's service, sealing his surrender through his son.
ramacharitamanas::4016.modern_relevance: You lose a job, move cities, and everything familiar drops away. What stays with you is what you have truly loved. Bali asks for that kind of love to survive every change.
ramacharitamanas::4016.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting a temporary life to protecting devotion itself.

ramacharitamanas::4017.verse_sanskrit: राम चरन दृढ़ प्रीति करि बालि कीन्ह तनु त्याग। सुमन माल जिमि कंठ ते गिरत न जानइ नाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::4017.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के चरणों में दृढ़ प्रीति करके बालि ने शरीर को वैसे ही (आसानी से) त्याग दिया जैसे हाथी अपने गले से फूलों की माला का गिरना न जाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::4017.english_translation: Bali gave up his body with firm love for Ram's feet, just as an elephant does not notice a flower garland slipping from its neck.
ramacharitamanas::4017.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / दृढ़ (firm) / प्रीति (love) / करि (having done) / बालि (Bali) / कीन्ह (did) / तनु (body) / त्याग (abandoning) / सुमन (flower) / माल (garland) / जिमि (like) / कंठ (neck) / ते (from) / गिरत (falling) / न (not) / जानइ (knows) / नाग (elephant)
ramacharitamanas::4017.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4017.essence: Total love makes release feel effortless.
ramacharitamanas::4017.simple_meaning: Bali died with such deep love for Ram that leaving the body felt effortless, like something slipping away unnoticed.
ramacharitamanas::4017.simple_insight: When love is complete, release stops feeling like loss.
ramacharitamanas::4017.detailed_meaning: After Ram strikes Bali, the vanara king does not cling to life. His heart is fixed on Ram's feet, and his body falls away without struggle. Tulsidas turns that death into a sign of total devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4017.modern_relevance: You finally let go of a job, a relationship, or an identity you had outgrown. It hurts less than you feared because something deeper in you has already chosen peace.
ramacharitamanas::4017.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to surrendering without resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4018.verse_sanskrit: राम बालि निज धाम पठावा। नगर लोग सब व्याकुल धावा॥ नाना बिधि बिलाप कर तारा। छूटे केस न देह सँभारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4018.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने बालि को अपने परम धाम भेज दिया। नगर के सब लोग व्याकुल होकर दौड़े। बालि की स्त्री तारा अनेकों प्रकार से विलाप करने लगी। उसके बाल बिखरे हुए हैं और देह की सँभाल नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4018.english_translation: Ram sent Bali to his own divine abode. The people of the city rushed about in distress. Tara wept in many ways, her hair undone and her body no longer composed.
ramacharitamanas::4018.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बालि (Bali) / निज (own) / धाम (abode) / पठावा (sent) / नगर (city) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / व्याकुल (distressed) / धावा (rushed) / नाना (various) / बिधि (ways) / बिलाप (lamentation) / कर (doing) / तारा (Tara) / छूटे (loosened) / केस (hair) / न (not) / देह (body) / सँभारा (composed)
ramacharitamanas::4018.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4018.essence: A righteous act can still leave sorrow in its wake.
ramacharitamanas::4018.simple_meaning: Ram has killed Bali, and the whole city is thrown into grief and confusion. Tara is overwhelmed with lamentation.
ramacharitamanas::4018.simple_insight: Even victory can leave a room full of grief when loss is real.
ramacharitamanas::4018.detailed_meaning: Bali has fallen, and Ram's arrow has ended the conflict. But Kishkindha is not celebrating. The city runs in distress, and Tara collapses into mourning. This verse pauses on the human cost before Ram speaks again.
ramacharitamanas::4018.modern_relevance: The meeting ends, the decision is made, and everyone walks out quietly shaken. One person has won, but another family is still standing in the shock of loss.
ramacharitamanas::4018.insight: It shifts attention from the triumph of action to the grief that follows it.

ramacharitamanas::4019.verse_sanskrit: तारा बिकल देखि रघुराया। दीन्ह ग्यान हरि लीन्ही माया॥ छिति जल पावक गगन समीरा। पंच रचित अति अधम सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4019.verse_hindi: तारा को व्याकुल देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसे ज्ञान दिया और उसकी माया (अज्ञान) हर ली। (उन्होंने कहा-) पृथ्वी, जल, अग्नि, आकाश और वायु- इन पाँच तत्वों से यह अत्यंत अधम शरीर रचा गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4019.english_translation: Seeing Tara distressed, Raghuraya gave her understanding and removed the veil of confusion. He said: this body is made from earth, water, fire, sky, and air — a very lowly composition.
ramacharitamanas::4019.translation_literal: तारा (Tara) / बिकल (distressed) / देखि (seeing) / रघुराया (Lord of the Raghu clan) / दीन्ह (gave) / ग्यान (understanding) / हरि (removed) / लीन्ही (took away) / माया (veil of appearance) ॥ / छिति (earth) / जल (water) / पावक (fire) / गगन (sky) / समीरा (air) / पंच (five) / रचित (made) / अति (very) / अधम (lowly) / सरीरा (body) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4019.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4019.essence: Clear seeing dissolves grief’s grip on what is temporary.
ramacharitamanas::4019.simple_meaning: Ram comforts Tara by showing her that the body is only a temporary mix of five elements, so her grief should ease.
ramacharitamanas::4019.simple_insight: Loss hurts less when you see what is temporary as temporary.
ramacharitamanas::4019.detailed_meaning: After Bali dies, Tara is overwhelmed with grief. Ram sees her distress and gives her clear understanding: the body is only a formed combination of five elements. In that moment, comfort comes through seeing beyond appearances.
ramacharitamanas::4019.modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital bed, unable to accept how quickly a strong body can fail. This verse meets that shock with a hard, tender clarity: what changes was never the whole person.
ramacharitamanas::4019.insight: It shifts attention from the body’s collapse to the deeper reality behind it.

ramacharitamanas::4020.verse_sanskrit: प्रगट सो तनु तव आगे सोवा। जीव नित्य केहि लगि तुम्ह रोवा॥ उपजा ग्यान चरन तब लागी। लीन्हेसि परम भगति बर मागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4020.verse_hindi: वह शरीर तो प्रत्यक्ष तुम्हारे सामने सोया हुआ है, और जीव नित्य है। फिर तुम किसके लिए रो रही हो? जब ज्ञान उत्पन्न हो गया, तब वह भगवान् के चरणों लगी और उसने परम भक्ति का वर माँग लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4020.english_translation: That body lies visibly before you, and the living being is eternal. Then why are you crying for it? When knowledge arose, she bowed at Ram's feet and asked for the boon of supreme devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4020.translation_literal: प्रगट (manifest) / सो (that) / तनु (body) / तव (your) / आगे (before) / सोवा (lying) / जीव (living being) / नित्य (eternal) / केहि लगि (for whom) / तुम्ह (you) / रोवा (wept) / उपजा (arose) / ग्यान (knowledge) / चरन (feet) / तब (then) / लागी (fell) / लीन्हेसि (she took) / परम (supreme) / भगति (devotion) / बर (boon) / मागी (asked)
ramacharitamanas::4020.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4020.essence: What you truly mourn is not what can be seen.
ramacharitamanas::4020.simple_meaning: The visible body is not the whole person. Once true understanding appears, grief softens and turns into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4020.simple_insight: Loss feels different when you stop clinging to the body as the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::4020.detailed_meaning: Tara is overwhelmed after Bali's death. Ram answers her sorrow with a teaching: the body lies there, but the living principle is not destroyed. As understanding dawns, grief turns toward Ram and becomes devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4020.modern_relevance: You’re standing by a hospital bed after hearing the worst news, staring at a still face. This verse speaks to the part of you that knows love is larger than the body it inhabited.
ramacharitamanas::4020.insight: It shifts attention from the body’s ending to the deeper continuity behind it.

ramacharitamanas::4021.verse_sanskrit: उमा दारु जोषित की नाईं। सबहि नचावत रामु गोसाईं॥ तब सुग्रीवहि आयसु दीन्हा। मृतक कर्म बिधिवत सब कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4021.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! स्वामी श्री रामजी सबको कठपुतली की तरह नचाते हैं। तदनन्तर श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव को आज्ञा दी और सुग्रीव ने विधिपूर्वक बालि का सब मृतक कर्म किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4021.english_translation: (Shiva says:) O Uma, Lord Ram moves everyone like a puppet. Then Ram gave Sugriva the order, and Sugriva duly performed all the funeral rites for Bali.
ramacharitamanas::4021.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma) / दारु (wood) / जोषित (woman) / की नाईं (like) / सबहि (everyone) / नचावत (makes dance) / रामु (Ram) / गोसाईं (Lord) // तब (then) / सुग्रीवहि (to Sugriva) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / मृतक (dead body) / कर्म (rites) / बिधिवत (according to rule) / सब (all) / कीन्हा (did)
ramacharitamanas::4021.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4021.essence: Ram guides even the hands that seem to act on their own.
ramacharitamanas::4021.simple_meaning: Ram quietly directs everyone’s actions. After that, Sugriva carries out Bali’s funeral rites exactly as required.
ramacharitamanas::4021.simple_insight: Even grief and duty unfold under a larger order you cannot see.
ramacharitamanas::4021.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Bali has fallen and the aftermath must be handled. Shiva, speaking to Uma, reflects that Ram moves every being like a hidden puppeteer. Then Ram instructs Sugriva, and Sugriva performs Bali’s last rites properly.
ramacharitamanas::4021.modern_relevance: A family is stunned after a sudden death, yet someone still has to call the priest, arrange the rites, and keep everyone steady. This verse reminds you that even chaos has an unseen order.
ramacharitamanas::4021.insight: It shifts attention from visible control to the deeper force guiding events and responsibilities.

ramacharitamanas::4022.verse_sanskrit: राम कहा अनुजहि समुझाई। राज देहु सुग्रीवहि जाई॥ रघुपति चरन नाइ करि माथा। चले सकल प्रेरित रघुनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4022.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण को समझाकर कहा कि तुम जाकर सुग्रीव को राज्य दे दो। श्री रघुनाथजी की प्रेरणा (आज्ञा) से सब लोग श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4022.english_translation: Then Lord Ram explained to his younger brother Lakshman: go and give the kingdom to Sugriva. Everyone bowed their heads at Raghunath's feet and departed, moved by Raghunath's command.
ramacharitamanas::4022.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कहा (said) / अनुजहि (to the younger brother) / समुझाई (explaining) / राज (kingdom) / देहु (give) / सुग्रीवहि (to Sugriva) / जाई (going) // रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / चरन (feet) / नाइ (bowing) / करि (doing) / माथा (head) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / प्रेरित (impelled) / रघुनाथा (by Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::4022.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4022.essence: Power becomes righteous when it gives back what it won.
ramacharitamanas::4022.simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to restore Sugriva's kingdom, and everyone leaves after bowing to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4022.simple_insight: Real strength includes giving back what was promised without clinging to power.
ramacharitamanas::4022.detailed_meaning: After Sugriva's victory, Ram does not let the alliance become possession. He tells Lakshman to return the kingdom, and the whole company moves only after bowing to Ram. The moment shows leadership that keeps its word.
ramacharitamanas::4022.modern_relevance: You finally get the keys, the credit, or the control everyone fought for — and then you return what was never meant to stay with you. That kind of restraint changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::4022.insight: It teaches you to complete an obligation cleanly and release ownership once the promise is fulfilled.

ramacharitamanas::4023.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन तुरत बोलाए पुरजन बिप्र समाज। राजु दीन्ह सुग्रीव कहँ अंगद कहँ जुबराज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4023.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने तुरंत ही सब नगरवासियों को और ब्राह्मणों के समाज को बुला लिया और (उनके सामने) सुग्रीव को राज्य और अंगद को युवराज पद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4023.english_translation: Lakshman quickly summoned the townspeople and the assembly of Brahmins, and in their presence gave Sugriva the kingdom and Angada the crown prince's seat.
ramacharitamanas::4023.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / तुरत (immediately) / बोलाए (called) / पुरजन (townspeople) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / समाज (assembly) / राजु (kingdom) / दीन्ह (gave) / सुग्रीव कहँ (to Sugriva) / अंगद कहँ (to Angada) / जुबराज (crown prince)
ramacharitamanas::4023.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4023.essence: Fairness becomes complete only when it is publicly carried out.
ramacharitamanas::4023.simple_meaning: Lakshman gathers the people and formally installs Sugriva as king and Angada as crown prince.
ramacharitamanas::4023.simple_insight: Right action is public, orderly, and done without delay.
ramacharitamanas::4023.detailed_meaning: After Ram sends Lakshman to restore Sugriva’s rule, Lakshman immediately calls the townspeople and Brahmins together. In front of everyone, he hands Sugriva the kingdom and Angada the heir’s seat. The verse records the formal completion of Ram’s alliance.
ramacharitamanas::4023.modern_relevance: A manager signs the transfer papers in front of the whole team instead of dragging it out in private. Clear, timely action restores trust faster than speeches do.
ramacharitamanas::4023.insight: It teaches you to complete responsibility openly, so fairness becomes visible and real.

ramacharitamanas::4024.verse_sanskrit: उमा राम सम हत जग माहीं। गुरु पितु मातु बंधु प्रभु नाहीं॥ सुर नर मुनि सब कै यह रीती। स्वारथ लागि करहिं सब प्रीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::4024.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! जगत में श्री रामजी के समान हित करने वाला गुरु, पिता, माता, बंधु और स्वामी कोई नहीं है। देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सबकी यह रीति है कि स्वार्थ के लिए ही सब प्रीति करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4024.english_translation: O Parvati, in the world there is no benefactor like Ram, no teacher, father, mother, brother, or lord like him. Gods, humans, and sages all follow this rule: they love only for their own sake.
ramacharitamanas::4024.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma/Parvati) / राम (Ram) / सम (like) / हत (benefactor) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / गुरु (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / बंधु (brother) / प्रभु (lord) / नाहीं (not) / सुर (devas) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / सब (all) / कै (of) / यह (this) / रीती (custom) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / लागि (for) / करहिं (do) / सब (all) / प्रीति (love)
ramacharitamanas::4024.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4024.essence: Ram's love is pure because it asks for nothing in return.
ramacharitamanas::4024.simple_meaning: Ram alone loves without self-interest. Everyone else usually loves with some hidden need or benefit in mind.
ramacharitamanas::4024.simple_insight: It can feel deeply relieving to be held by a love that asks for nothing back.
ramacharitamanas::4024.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to Parvati in the Kishkindhakand, just after Ram has sent Lakshman to restore Sugriva's kingship. He pauses the story to reveal Ram's nature: unlike ordinary relationships built on gain, Ram's care is pure benefit for others.
ramacharitamanas::4024.modern_relevance: You know the difference between the friend who checks in because they care and the one who only calls when they need something. This verse points to the rare kind of love that gives without keeping score.
ramacharitamanas::4024.insight: It shifts your trust away from transactional affection toward selfless care.

ramacharitamanas::4025.verse_sanskrit: बालि त्रास ब्याकुल दिन राती। तन बहु ब्रन चिंताँ जर छाती॥ सोइ सुग्रीव कीन्ह कपि राऊ। अति कृपाल रघुबीर सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4025.verse_hindi: जो सुग्रीव दिन-रात बालि के भय से व्याकुल रहता था, जिसके शरीर में बहुत से घाव हो गए थे और जिसकी छाती चिंता के मारे जला करती थी, उसी सुग्रीव को उन्होंने वानरों का राजा बना दिया। श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्वभाव अत्यंत ही कृपालु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4025.english_translation: The same Sugriva who lived in fear of Bali day and night, whose body bore many wounds and whose chest burned with worry, Ram made king of the monkeys. The nature of Raghubir is deeply compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::4025.translation_literal: बालि (Bali) / त्रास (fear) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / दिन राती (day and night) / तन (body) / बहु (many) / ब्रन (wounds) / चिंताँ (with worry) / जर (burned) / छाती (chest) / सोइ (that same) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / कीन्ह (made) / कपि राऊ (monkey king) / अति (very) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सुभाऊ (nature)
ramacharitamanas::4025.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4025.essence: Compassion restores what fear has taken away.
ramacharitamanas::4025.simple_meaning: Ram lifts Sugriva from fear and suffering into kingship because compassion is his nature.
ramacharitamanas::4025.simple_insight: Real compassion does more than sympathize — it restores dignity and gives someone back their place.
ramacharitamanas::4025.detailed_meaning: After Bali's terror has left Sugriva wounded, anxious, and sleepless, Ram restores him and makes him king of the monkeys. The scene shows that Ram's mercy is not abstract; it changes a broken life and settles the alliance.
ramacharitamanas::4025.modern_relevance: You know the friend who has been shaking through every phone call, carrying old hurt in the body. Then someone finally gives them a real chance, not just sympathy.
ramacharitamanas::4025.insight: It shifts attention from pity to restorative action: help should return agency, not just comfort.

ramacharitamanas::4026.verse_sanskrit: जानतहूँ अस प्रभु परिहरहीं। काहे न बिपति जाल नर परहीं॥ पुनि सुग्रीवहि लीन्ह बोलाई। बहु प्रकार नृपनीति सिखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4026.verse_hindi: जो लोग जानते हुए भी ऐसे प्रभु को त्याग देते हैं, वे क्यों न विपत्ति के जाल में फँसें? फिर श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव को बुला लिया और बहुत प्रकार से उन्हें राजनीति की शिक्षा दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4026.english_translation: Those who knowingly abandon such a Lord fall into the net of trouble. Then Ram called Sugriva back and taught him statecraft in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::4026.translation_literal: जानतहूँ (even knowing) / अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / परिहरहीं (they abandon) / काहे (why) / न (not) / बिपति (trouble) / जाल (net) / नर (people) / परहीं (fall) / पुनि (then) / सुग्रीवहि (Sugriva) / लीन्ह (took) / बोलाई (calling) / बहु प्रकार (many kinds) / नृपनीति (statecraft) / सिखाई (taught)
ramacharitamanas::4026.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4026.essence: Rejecting Ram is itself the path into suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4026.simple_meaning: Turning away from a true helper leads straight into suffering. Ram then calls Sugriva close and teaches him how to rule wisely.
ramacharitamanas::4026.simple_insight: There is relief in staying close to what is wise and protective instead of wandering into avoidable trouble.
ramacharitamanas::4026.detailed_meaning: After Sugriva has been freed from fear, the narration pauses to warn that people who knowingly reject Ram walk into misery. Then Ram turns to Sugriva, not just as a friend but as a future king, and teaches him how to govern well.
ramacharitamanas::4026.modern_relevance: You keep ignoring the friend who always gives the clearest advice, then wonder why the same mess keeps returning. Wisdom is not just hearing good counsel — it is staying close enough to let it shape your choices.
ramacharitamanas::4026.insight: It shifts the mind from casual neglect of guidance to active reliance on what protects and orders life.

ramacharitamanas::4027.verse_sanskrit: कह प्रभु सुनु सुग्रीव हरीसा। पुर न जाउँ दस चारि बरीसा॥ गत ग्रीषम बरषा रितु आई। रहिहउँ निकट सैल पर छाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4027.verse_hindi: फिर प्रभु ने कहा- हे वानरपति सुग्रीव! सुनो, मैं चौदह वर्ष तक गाँव (बस्ती) में नहीं जाऊँगा। ग्रीष्मऋतु बीतकर वर्षाऋतु आ गई। अतः मैं यहाँ पास ही पर्वत पर टिक रहूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4027.english_translation: Then the Lord said, “Listen, Sugriva, king of the monkeys. I will not stay in the town for fourteen years. Summer has passed and the rainy season has arrived, so I will remain nearby on the mountain.”
ramacharitamanas::4027.translation_literal: कह (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुनु (listen) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / हरीसा (lord of the monkeys) / पुर (town) / न (not) / जाउँ (I will go) / दस (ten) / चारि (four) / बरीसा (years) / गत (passed) / ग्रीषम (summer) / बरषा (rainy season) / रितु (season) / आई (has come) / रहिहउँ (I will remain) / निकट (nearby) / सैल (mountain) / पर (on) / छाई (covered, staying)
ramacharitamanas::4027.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4027.essence: True commitment stays near the task, not the comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4027.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sugriva he will stay near the mountain, not in the town, during the rainy season and for the years of exile.
ramacharitamanas::4027.simple_insight: Sometimes loyalty means staying close, not taking the easier place.
ramacharitamanas::4027.detailed_meaning: After Sugriva is restored, Ram speaks like a friend and king. With the rains beginning, he chooses to remain on the mountain rather than return to town, keeping faith with the exile that still binds him.
ramacharitamanas::4027.modern_relevance: You’ve been offered a comfortable seat, but you choose the hard edge of the room because your promise still matters.
ramacharitamanas::4027.insight: It teaches you to stay aligned with your commitment even when comfort is available.

ramacharitamanas::4028.verse_sanskrit: अंगद सहित करहु तुम्ह राजू। संतत हृदयँ धरेहु मम काजू॥ जब सुग्रीव भवन फिरि आए। रामु प्रबरषन गिरि पर छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4028.verse_hindi: तुम अंगद सहित राज्य करो। मेरे काम का हृदय में सदा ध्यान रखना। तदनन्तर जब सुग्रीवजी घर लौट आए, तब श्री रामजी प्रवर्षण पर्वत पर जा टिके ॥
ramacharitamanas::4028.english_translation: You and Angada should rule, keeping my work always in your heart. Then, when Sugriva returned home, Rama stayed on Mount Pravarshana.
ramacharitamanas::4028.translation_literal: अंगद सहित (together with Angada) / करहु (do) / तुम्ह (you) / राजू (kingship, rule) / संतत (always) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धरेहु (keep) / मम (my) / काजू (work, task) / जब (when) / सुग्रीवहि (Sugriva) / भवन (home, house) / फिरि (returning) / आए (came) / रामु (Rama) / प्रबरषन (Pravarshana) / गिरि (mountain) / पर (on) / छाए (stayed, settled)
ramacharitamanas::4028.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4028.essence: Help fully, then step back and let others rule.
ramacharitamanas::4028.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sugriva and Angada to rule, while keeping his work in mind. After Sugriva returns home, Ram stays on Mount Pravarshana.
ramacharitamanas::4028.simple_insight: True leadership can be temporary, and service can continue even after the mission changes.
ramacharitamanas::4028.detailed_meaning: After Sugriva's alliance is secured, Ram entrusts the kingdom to Sugriva and Angada while he withdraws to Mount Pravarshana. The scene shifts from strategy to waiting: Ram has helped restore order, and now he lets the next phase unfold.
ramacharitamanas::4028.modern_relevance: You finish helping a friend rebuild their business, then step back and let them lead. Real support knows when to stay involved and when to leave room.
ramacharitamanas::4028.insight: It shifts the mind from controlling the outcome to supporting the right people at the right time.

ramacharitamanas::4029.verse_sanskrit: प्रथमहिं देवन्ह गिरि गुहा राखेउ रुचिर बनाइ। राम कृपानिधि कछु दिन बास करहिंगे आइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4029.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने पहले से ही उस पर्वत की एक गुफा को सुंदर बना (सजा) रखा था। उन्होंने सोच रखा था कि कृपा की खान श्री रामजी कुछ दिन यहाँ आकर निवास करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4029.english_translation: The gods had already made a lovely cave in the mountain, thinking that Ram, the treasure of grace, would come and stay there for some days.
ramacharitamanas::4029.translation_literal: प्रथमहिं (already, first) / देवन्ह (by the gods) / गिरि (mountain) / गुहा (cave) / राखेउ (kept, made ready) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बनाइ (having made) / राम (Ram) / कृपानिधि (treasure of grace) / कछु दिन (some days) / बास (residence) / करहिंगे (will do) / आइ (coming)
ramacharitamanas::4029.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4029.essence: The right refuge is ready before you arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4029.simple_meaning: The mountain cave was prepared in advance, because the devas expected Ram to stay there for a while.
ramacharitamanas::4029.simple_insight: Even the place of refuge was waiting for him.
ramacharitamanas::4029.detailed_meaning: After Sugriva returns to Kishkindha, Ram prepares to stay on the mountain near the forest. The verse pauses on the cave already made beautiful by the devas, showing that this meeting and resting place were not accidental.
ramacharitamanas::4029.modern_relevance: You arrive at a friend's empty hill cabin and find the firewood stacked, the bed made, the lights on. Someone prepared for your coming before you even asked.
ramacharitamanas::4029.insight: It frames the stay as divinely prepared, not improvised.

ramacharitamanas::4030.verse_sanskrit: सुंदर बन कुसुमित अति सोभा। गुंजत मधुप निकर मधु लोभा॥ कंद मूल फल पत्र सुहाए। भए बहुत जब ते प्रभु आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4030.verse_hindi: सुंदर वन फूला हुआ अत्यंत सुशोभित है। मधु के लोभ से भौंरों के समूह गुंजार कर रहे हैं। जब से प्रभु आए, तब से वन में सुंदर कन्द, मूल, फल और पत्तों की बहुतायत हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4030.english_translation: The beautiful forest is in full bloom, shining with great splendor. Swarms of bees hum, drawn by the sweetness of nectar. Since the Lord arrived, roots, fruits, and leaves have become abundant and lovely.
ramacharitamanas::4030.translation_literal: सुंदर (beautiful) / बन (forest) / कुसुमित (flowering) / अति (very) / सोभा (splendor) / गुंजत (buzzing) / मधुप (bees) / निकर (crowd, swarm) / मधु (nectar, sweetness) / लोभा (greed, attraction) / कंद (roots, tubers) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / पत्र (leaves) / सुहाए (became lovely) / भए (became) / बहुत (many, abundant) / जब (when) / ते (since) / प्रभु (Lord) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::4030.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4030.essence: His arrival makes the forest bloom.
ramacharitamanas::4030.simple_meaning: The forest has become lush and beautiful since Ram arrived there.
ramacharitamanas::4030.simple_insight: Where Ram is welcomed, even the land seems to flourish.
ramacharitamanas::4030.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sugriva are now in Kishkindha’s mountain country. Tulsidas pauses to show the landscape itself responding to Ram’s presence: flowers bloom, bees gather, and the forest’s roots, fruits, and leaves seem richer. It is a scene of blessing, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4030.modern_relevance: You walk into a home after good news has arrived, and the whole place feels lighter. Nothing changed on the walls, yet everything seems to breathe differently.
ramacharitamanas::4030.insight: It shows Ram’s presence as life-giving, turning even wilderness into abundance.

ramacharitamanas::4031.verse_sanskrit: देखि मनोहर सैल अनूपा। रहे तहँ अनुज सहित सुरभूपा॥ मधुकर खग मृग तनु धरि देवा। करहिं सिद्ध मुनि प्रभु कै सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4031.verse_hindi: मनोहर और अनुपम पर्वत को देखकर देवताओं के सम्राट् श्री रामजी छोटे भाई सहित वहाँ रह गए। देवता, सिद्ध और मुनि भौंरों, पक्षियों और पशुओं के शरीर धारण करके प्रभु की सेवा करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4031.english_translation: Seeing the beautiful, unmatched mountain, the lord of the gods stayed there with his younger brother. The devas, siddhas, and sages took the forms of bees, birds, and animals and served the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::4031.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / मनोहर (beautiful) / सैल (mountain) / अनूपा (unmatched) / रहे (remained) / तहँ (there) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / सुरभूपा (lord of the gods) / मधुकर (bees) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / तनु (body) / धरि (taking) / देवा (devas) / करहिं (do) / सिद्ध (siddhas) / मुनि (sages) / प्रभु (Lord) / कै (of) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::4031.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4031.essence: Ram's presence turns even nature into service.
ramacharitamanas::4031.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman stay on a beautiful mountain, and celestial beings take forms of bees, birds, and animals to serve them.
ramacharitamanas::4031.simple_insight: A holy presence changes the whole place into a field of service.
ramacharitamanas::4031.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman reach a beautiful mountain in Kishkindha and stay there. The scene expands beyond nature: devas, siddhas, and sages come in humble forms to serve Ram, showing that his presence draws devotion from all levels of creation.
ramacharitamanas::4031.modern_relevance: You walk into a place that somehow feels different the moment someone deeply grounded arrives. People soften, help appears, and the whole atmosphere starts leaning toward service.
ramacharitamanas::4031.insight: It shifts attention from the setting itself to the way devotion transforms the entire atmosphere around Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4032.verse_sanskrit: मंगलरूप भयउ बन तब ते। कीन्ह निवास रमापति जब ते॥ फटिक सिला अति सुभ्र सुहाई। सुख आसीन तहाँ द्वौ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4032.verse_hindi: जब से रमापति श्री रामजी ने वहाँ निवास किया तब से वन मंगलस्वरूप हो गया। सुंदर स्फटिक मणि की एक अत्यंत उज्ज्वल शिला है, उस पर दोनों भाई सुखपूर्वक विराजमान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4032.english_translation: From the moment Rama took residence there, the forest became auspicious. A beautiful, bright crystal slab was there, and the two brothers sat there in comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4032.translation_literal: मंगलरूप (of auspicious form) / भयउ (became) / बन (forest) / तब ते (from then) / कीन्ह (made) / निवास (residence) / रमापति (Rama, lord of Lakshmi) / जब ते (from when) / फटिक (crystal) / सिला (slab) / अति (very) / सुभ्र (white, bright) / सुहाई (beautiful) / सुख (comfort) / आसीन (seated) / तहाँ (there) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::4032.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4032.essence: Rama's presence turns ordinary ground into a place of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4032.simple_meaning: Rama's presence makes the forest feel blessed, and he and Lakshman sit together on a bright crystal slab.
ramacharitamanas::4032.simple_insight: Even a wild place feels like home when the right presence enters it.
ramacharitamanas::4032.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Rama and Lakshman have reached a beautiful mountain retreat. The forest itself seems transformed by Rama's arrival, and the two brothers rest together on a shining crystal seat before the next conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::4032.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard day, and the tension drops because one steady person is already there. Some places change not by decoration, but by presence.
ramacharitamanas::4032.insight: It shifts attention from scenery to presence: the sacred quality of a place comes from who dwells there.

ramacharitamanas::4033.verse_sanskrit: कहत अनुज सन कथा अनेका। भगति बिरत नृपनीति बिबेका॥ बरषा काल मेघ नभ छाए। गरजत लागत परम सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4033.verse_hindi: श्री राम छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी से भक्ति, वैराग्य, राजनीति और ज्ञान की अनेकों कथाएँ कहते हैं। वर्षाकाल में आकाश में छाए हुए बादल गरजते हुए बहुत ही सुहावने लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4033.english_translation: Ram speaks with his younger brother about many topics—devotion, renunciation, kingship, and discernment. In the rainy season, clouds fill the sky and their thunder sounds especially lovely.
ramacharitamanas::4033.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / अनुज (younger brother) / सन (with) / कथा (stories, talks) / अनेका (many) / भगति (devotion) / बिरत (renunciation) / नृपनीति (kingship, statecraft) / बिबेका (discernment) / बरषा काल (rainy season) / मेघ (clouds) / नभ (sky) / छाए (covered) / गरजत (thundering) / लागत (seem) / परम (very) / सुहाए (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::4033.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4033.essence: Quiet conversation can carry the deepest teachings.
ramacharitamanas::4033.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman spend time in quiet conversation about devotion, renunciation, wise rule, and clear judgment. The rainy clouds overhead make the scene feel beautiful and alive.
ramacharitamanas::4033.simple_insight: Even ordinary moments can become a lesson when the mind is calm and attentive.
ramacharitamanas::4033.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are resting in the forest after the mountain scene has become sacred through Ram's presence. Ram speaks gently with his brother about devotion, detachment, wise conduct, and discernment, while the monsoon clouds gather above them, deepening the mood.
ramacharitamanas::4033.modern_relevance: You sit with someone you trust while rain taps the window, and a simple conversation turns serious. What feels ordinary can hold the deepest guidance when the mind is settled.
ramacharitamanas::4033.insight: It shifts attention from the setting to the quality of awareness and conversation within it.

ramacharitamanas::4034.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन देखु मोर गन नाचत बारिद पेखि। गृही बिरति रत हरष जस बिष्नुभगत कहुँ देखि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4034.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी कहने लगे-) हे लक्ष्मण! देखो, मोरों के झुंड बादलों को देखकर नाच रहे हैं जैसे वैराग्य में अनुरक्त गृहस्थ किसी विष्णुभक्त को देखकर हर्षित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4034.english_translation: O Lakshman, look at my peacocks dancing on seeing the clouds. Householders devoted to renunciation rejoice on seeing a devotee of Vishnu.
ramacharitamanas::4034.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / देखु (look) / मोर (peacocks) / गन (group) / नाचत (dancing) / बारिद (clouds) / पेखि (seeing) / गृही (householders) / बिरति (renunciation) / रत (immersed) / हरष (joy) / जस (like) / बिष्नुभगत (devotee of Vishnu) / कहुँ (to) / देखि (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::4034.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4034.essence: Devotion recognizes devotion and answers with joy.
ramacharitamanas::4034.simple_meaning: Ram notices that even peacocks rejoice at the sight of clouds, just as devoted people feel joy when they see someone devoted to Vishnu.
ramacharitamanas::4034.simple_insight: True devotion is recognizable at once, and it naturally awakens joy in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::4034.detailed_meaning: Ram sits in the forest with Lakshman and points to the peacocks dancing in the rain clouds. He turns that scene into a gentle lesson: hearts already inclined toward renunciation and devotion light up when they meet true devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4034.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel it immediately: one person is calm, sincere, and inwardly gathered. Without thinking, you relax too. Real devotion changes the atmosphere before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4034.insight: It trains you to recognize devotion as something that calls forth joy and alignment, not just belief.

ramacharitamanas::4035.verse_sanskrit: घन घमंड नभ गरजत घोरा। प्रिया हीन डरपत मन मोरा॥ दामिनि दमक रह नघन माहीं। खल कै प्रीति जथा थिर नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4035.verse_hindi: आकाश में बादल घुमड़-घुमड़कर घोर गर्जना कर रहे हैं, प्रिया (सीताजी) के बिना मेरा मन डर रहा है। बिजली की चमक बादलों में ठहरती नहीं, जैसे दुष्ट की प्रीति स्थिर नहीं रहती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4035.english_translation: The dark clouds roar fiercely in the sky. My mind trembles without my beloved. Lightning flashes within the clouds and never stays, just like the love of a wicked person never remains steady.
ramacharitamanas::4035.translation_literal: घन (clouds) / घमंड (pride) / नभ (sky) / गरजत (roaring) / घोरा (fierce) / प्रिया हीन (without beloved) / डरपत (trembles) / मन (mind) / मोरा (mine) / दामिनि (lightning) / दमक (flashes) / रह (stays) / नघन माहीं (within the clouds) / खल (wicked person) / कै (of) / प्रीति (love) / जथा (like) / थिर (steady) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::4035.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4035.essence: True love stays; false love flashes and disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4035.simple_meaning: Ram sees a storm and feels Sita's absence. He compares lightning to unreliable love: bright for a moment, then gone.
ramacharitamanas::4035.simple_insight: Love that only dazzles cannot hold you. Real care stays steady even in hardship.
ramacharitamanas::4035.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram is speaking to Lakshman while watching the monsoon clouds gather. The storm stirs his longing for Sita, and he uses the flashing lightning to point out how unstable false affection is.
ramacharitamanas::4035.modern_relevance: You meet someone who texts with heat for a week, then disappears when life gets difficult. The intensity felt real, but it was only lightning.
ramacharitamanas::4035.insight: It teaches you to test love by steadiness, not by excitement.

ramacharitamanas::4036.verse_sanskrit: बरषहिं जलद भूमि निअराएँ। जथा नवहिं बुध बिद्या पाएँ। बूँद अघात सहहिं गिरि कैसे। खल के बचन संत सह जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4036.verse_hindi: बादल पृथ्वी के समीप आकर (नीचे उतरकर) बरस रहे हैं, जैसे विद्या पाकर विद्वान् नम्र हो जाते हैं। बूँदों की चोट पर्वत कैसे सहते हैं, जैसे दुष्टों के वचन संत सहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4036.english_translation: Clouds, coming close to the earth, pour rain; learned people become humble after gaining wisdom. Mountains endure the blows of raindrops; saints endure the words of the wicked.
ramacharitamanas::4036.translation_literal: बरषहिं (they rain) / जलद (clouds) / भूमि (earth) / निअराएँ (coming near) / जथा (just as) / नवहिं (become new) / बुध (wise people) / बिद्या (knowledge) / पाएँ (having gained) / बूँद (raindrops) / अघात (strikes/blows) / सहहिं (endure) / गिरि (mountain) / कैसे (how) / खल (wicked people) / के (of) / बचन (words) / संत (saints) / सह (endure) / जैसें (just as)
ramacharitamanas::4036.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4036.essence: Real wisdom lowers pride and leaves you unshaken.
ramacharitamanas::4036.simple_meaning: True learning makes a person humble. A steady person can absorb harsh words the way mountains absorb rain.
ramacharitamanas::4036.simple_insight: You do not need to harden yourself to stay strong.
ramacharitamanas::4036.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram watches the monsoon and turns it into a lesson for Lakshman. Clouds lower themselves to give life, the wise grow modest with learning, and saints remain unmoved by cruel speech.
ramacharitamanas::4036.modern_relevance: You finally get praised after years of work, and the first temptation is to puff up. This verse pulls you back down: real growth should make you quieter, not louder.
ramacharitamanas::4036.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to humility and steady endurance.

ramacharitamanas::4037.verse_sanskrit: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4037.verse_hindi: छोटी नदियाँ भरकर (किनारों को) तुड़ाती हुई चलीं, जैसे थोड़े धन से भी दुष्ट इतरा जाते हैं। (मर्यादा का त्याग कर देते हैं)। पृथ्वी पर पड़ते ही पानी गंदला हो गया है, जैसे शुद्ध जीव के माया लिपट गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4037.english_translation: Small rivers swell and break their banks, just as a little wealth makes the wicked boastful. When water falls to the ground, it turns muddy, just as maya clings to a pure living being.
ramacharitamanas::4037.translation_literal: छुद्र (small) / नदीं (rivers) / भरि (filled) / चलीं (moved) / तोराई (breaking banks) / जस (just as) / थोरेहुँ (even little) / धन (wealth) / खल (wicked) / इतराई (become proud) / भूमि (ground) / परत (falling) / भा (became) / ढाबर (muddy) / पानी (water) / जनु (as if) / जीवहि (to the living being) / माया (maya) / लपटानी (clung)
ramacharitamanas::4037.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4037.essence: Small success can swell ego and blur your clarity.
ramacharitamanas::4037.simple_meaning: Small rivers overflow their banks, just as a little wealth can make bad people arrogant. Water becomes muddy when it falls to the ground, just as maya can cling to a pure living being.
ramacharitamanas::4037.simple_insight: What looks small can still distort you. Watch the mind before pride and confusion take hold.
ramacharitamanas::4037.detailed_meaning: While Hanuman's journey through Kishkindha unfolds, the narrator pauses on a natural image: swollen streams, muddy water, and the way a little wealth inflates the wicked. The point is not the river itself, but how quickly clarity and restraint can be lost.
ramacharitamanas::4037.modern_relevance: You get a bonus and suddenly start speaking louder, spending faster, and feeling untouchable. The change is small, but the distortion is real.
ramacharitamanas::4037.insight: It trains you to notice how pride and confusion attach themselves before they feel permanent.

ramacharitamanas::4038.verse_sanskrit: समिटि समिटि जल भरहिं तलावा। जिमि सदगुन सज्जन पहिं आवा॥ सरिता जल जलनिधि महुँ जोई। होइ अचल जिमि जिव हरि पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4038.verse_hindi: जल एकत्र हो-होकर तालाबों में भर रहा है, जैसे सद्गुण (एक-एककर) सज्जन के पास चले आते हैं। नदी का जल समुद्र में जाकर वैसे ही स्थिर हो जाता है, जैसे जीव श्री हरि को पाकर अचल (आवागमन से मुक्त) हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4038.english_translation: Water gathers into ponds, just as good qualities gather in a noble person. River water becomes still in the ocean, just as a living being becomes steady upon reaching Hari.
ramacharitamanas::4038.translation_literal: समिटि-समिटि (gathering together) / जल (water) / भरहिं (fill) / तलावा (ponds) / जिमि (just as) / सदगुन (good qualities) / सज्जन (noble person) / पहिं (to) / आवा (come) ॥ / सरिता (river) / जल (water) / जलनिधि (ocean) / महुँ (in) / जोई (which) / होइ (becomes) / अचल (steady) / जिमि (just as) / जिव (living being) / हरि (Hari) / पाई (having found) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4038.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4038.essence: True steadiness comes when the restless life reaches Hari.
ramacharitamanas::4038.simple_meaning: Good qualities naturally gather in a noble person, and a restless life becomes steady when it reaches Hari.
ramacharitamanas::4038.simple_insight: There is relief in meeting what finally settles you.
ramacharitamanas::4038.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas pauses the story of alliance and search to show a deeper pattern: virtue gathers where the heart is fit, and the restless stream of life becomes still only in Hari. The image turns devotion into inward settling.
ramacharitamanas::4038.modern_relevance: You keep chasing the next fix, the next approval, the next milestone — and still feel scattered. Then one relationship, one practice, one presence makes everything inside you start to settle.
ramacharitamanas::4038.insight: It shifts attention from collecting experiences to finding what truly steadies the mind.

ramacharitamanas::4039.verse_sanskrit: हरित भूमि तृन संकुल समुझि परहिं नहिं पंथ। जिमि पाखंड बाद तें गुप्त होहिं सदग्रंथ ॥
