ramacharitamanas::4039.verse_hindi: पृथ्वी घास से परिपूर्ण होकर हरी हो गई है, जिससे रास्ते समझ नहीं पड़ते। जैसे पाखंड मत के प्रचार से सद्ग्रंथ गुप्त (लुप्त) हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4039.english_translation: The earth has turned green and thick with grass, so the path is no longer visible. In the same way, when false teachings spread, true scriptures become hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4039.translation_literal: हरित (green) / भूमि (earth) / तृन (grass) / संकुल (crowded) / समुझि (understanding) / परहिं (fall) / नहिं (not) / पंथ (path) / जिमि (just as) / पाखंड (false teaching) / बाद (spread) / तें (from) / गुप्त (hidden) / होहिं (become) / सदग्रंथ (true scriptures)
ramacharitamanas::4039.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4039.essence: False noise can hide the path, but it cannot erase it.
ramacharitamanas::4039.simple_meaning: When false ideas spread everywhere, it becomes hard to see the real path, just as thick grass hides a road.
ramacharitamanas::4039.simple_insight: Not every loud voice is guidance. Clarity often means seeing through what covers the way.
ramacharitamanas::4039.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas uses a field image to make a spiritual warning: when the ground is overgrown, the road disappears. In the same way, when false doctrines spread, genuine sacred teaching gets buried from sight.
ramacharitamanas::4039.modern_relevance: You open your phone for a simple answer and get buried under ten confident opinions, half-truths, and recycled advice. The real path is still there — but clutter can hide it.
ramacharitamanas::4039.insight: It trains you to notice how confusion can mask what is reliable, and to look past surface noise for what truly guides.

ramacharitamanas::4040.verse_sanskrit: दादुर धुनि चहु दिसा सुहाई। बेद पढ़हिं जनु बटु समुदाई॥ नव पल्लव भए बिटप अनेका। साधक मन जस मिलें बिबेका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4040.verse_hindi: चारों दिशाओं में मेंढकों की ध्वनि ऐसी सुहावनी लगती है, मानो विद्यार्थियों के समुदाय वेद पढ़ रहे हों। अनेकों वृक्षों में नए पत्ते आ गए हैं, जिससे वे ऐसे हरे-भरे एवं सुशोभित हो गए हैं जैसे साधक का मन विवेक (ज्ञान) प्राप्त होने पर हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4040.english_translation: The sound of frogs sounds pleasant in all four directions, as if groups of students are reciting the Vedas. Many trees have put forth new leaves, becoming lush and beautiful like a seeker’s mind when clear seeing arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4040.translation_literal: दादुर (frogs) / धुनि (sound) / चहु दिसा (four directions) / सुहाई (pleasant) / बेद (Vedas) / पढ़हिं (read/recite) / जनु (as if) / बटु (students) / समुदाई (group) / नव (new) / पल्लव (leaves) / भए (became) / बिटप (trees) / अनेका (many) / साधक (seeker) / मन (mind) / जस (like) / मिलें (having met/received) / बिबेका (clear seeing)
ramacharitamanas::4040.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4040.essence: Clear seeing can make the same world feel newly alive.
ramacharitamanas::4040.simple_meaning: Nature is described as becoming fresh and beautiful, just like a seeker’s mind becomes bright and settled when clear understanding arises.
ramacharitamanas::4040.simple_insight: Confusion can distort everything; clear seeing can make the same world feel alive and meaningful again.
ramacharitamanas::4040.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the poet watches the forest transform after the rains. Frogs, new leaves, and fresh growth become a living image for the seeker’s mind. The verse turns a natural scene into a lesson about how clear seeing changes perception.
ramacharitamanas::4040.modern_relevance: You step outside after a long, heavy week and notice the air, the trees, even the noise differently. Nothing changed out there — but your mind did.
ramacharitamanas::4040.insight: It shifts attention from external conditions to the inner clarity that changes how everything is experienced.

ramacharitamanas::4041.verse_sanskrit: अर्क जवास पात बिनु भयऊ। जस सुराज खल उद्यम गयऊ॥ खोजत कतहुँ मिलइ नहिं धूरी। करइ क्रोध जिमि धरमहि दूरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4041.verse_hindi: मदार और जवासा बिना पत्ते के हो गए (उनके पत्ते झड़ गए)। जैसे श्रेष्ठ राज्य में दुष्टों का उद्यम जाता रहा (उनकी एक भी नहीं चलती)। धूल कहीं खोजने पर भी नहीं मिलती, जैसे क्रोध धर्म को दूर कर देता है। (अर्थात् क्रोध का आवेश होने पर धर्म का ज्ञान नहीं रह जाता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4041.english_translation: The madar and javasa plants became leafless, just as the efforts of the wicked fail in a well-ruled kingdom. Dust cannot be found anywhere, just as anger drives dharma far away.
ramacharitamanas::4041.translation_literal: अर्क (madar) / जवास (javasa) / पात (leaves) / बिनु (without) / भयऊ (became) / जस (just as) / सुराज (well-ruled kingdom) / खल (wicked) / उद्यम (effort) / गयऊ (went away) / खोजत (searching) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / मिलइ (is found) / नहिं (not) / धूरी (dust) / करइ (does) / क्रोध (anger) / जिमि (just as) / धरमहि (dharma) / दूरी (far away)
ramacharitamanas::4041.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4041.simple_meaning: A peaceful, well-run order leaves wrongdoing powerless. In the same way, anger blinds you and pushes right conduct far away.
ramacharitamanas::4041.simple_insight: You do not have to obey the first surge of heat. A pause can keep your judgment intact.
ramacharitamanas::4041.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the forest is being described through signs of a healthy order: plants shed leaves, the wicked lose their force, and the world looks settled. Tulsidas then turns that image inward and warns that anger does the opposite of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::4041.modern_relevance: You get a sharp email, feel your face heat up, and type a reply you will regret. In that tiny gap before sending, your whole course can change.
ramacharitamanas::4041.insight: It teaches you to interrupt anger before it cuts off clear judgment.

ramacharitamanas::4042.verse_sanskrit: ससि संपन्न सोह महि कैसी। उपकारी कै संपति जैसी॥ निसि तम घन खद्योत बिराजा। जनु दंभिन्ह कर मिला समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4042.verse_hindi: अन्न से युक्त (लहराती हुई खेती से हरी-भरी) पृथ्वी कैसी शोभित हो रही है, जैसी उपकारी पुरुष की संपत्ति। रात के घने अंधकार में जुगनू शोभा पा रहे हैं, मानो दम्भियों का समाज आ जुटा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4042.english_translation: The earth looks beautiful when it is full of grain, just as wealth makes a generous person shine. In the dark of night, fireflies glow like a crowd of boastful people gathered together.
ramacharitamanas::4042.translation_literal: ससि (grain-filled) / संपन्न (well-provided) / सोह (looks beautiful) / महि (earth) / कैसी (how) / उपकारी (generous, helpful) / कै (of) / संपति (wealth) / जैसी (like) ॥ / निसि (night) / तम (darkness) / घन (dense) / खद्योत (fireflies) / बिराजा (shine) / जनु (as if) / दंभिन्ह (of the boastful) / कर (of) / मिला (gathered) / समाजा (assembly) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4042.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4042.essence: Real worth shines quietly; pride only glitters in the dark.
ramacharitamanas::4042.simple_meaning: A fertile earth looks lovely, just as generous wealth looks fitting. Fireflies in the dark are like proud people showing off together.
ramacharitamanas::4042.simple_insight: Beauty and brightness can be misleading when they come from pride instead of real worth.
ramacharitamanas::4042.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing a world after rain and growth, using nature to make a moral point. The fertile earth and the glowing fireflies are not just scenery; they become images of true usefulness versus empty display.
ramacharitamanas::4042.modern_relevance: A room full of loud voices and shiny clothes can look impressive for a moment. Then you notice who actually helps, who actually feeds people, and who only wants to be seen.
ramacharitamanas::4042.insight: It trains you to distinguish genuine value from showy appearance.

ramacharitamanas::4043.verse_sanskrit: महाबृष्टि चलि फूटि किआरीं। जिमि सुतंत्र भएँ बिगरहिं नारीं॥ कृषी निरावहिं चतुर किसाना। जिमि बुध तजहिं मोह मद माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4043.verse_hindi: भारी वर्षा से खेतों की क्यारियाँ फूट चली हैं, जैसे स्वतंत्र होने से स्त्रियाँ बिगड़ जाती हैं। चतुर किसान खेतों को निरा रहे हैं (उनमें से घास आदि को निकालकर फेंक रहे हैं।) जैसे विद्वान् लोग मोह, मद और मान का त्याग कर देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4043.english_translation: Heavy rain has broken the field ridges, just as women become unruly when left independent. Wise farmers weed their fields, just as the learned cast off delusion, pride, and conceit.
ramacharitamanas::4043.translation_literal: महाबृष्टि (heavy rain) / चलि (having moved) / फूटि (broken) / किआरीं (field ridges) / जिमि (just as) / सुतंत्र भएँ (when made independent) / बिगरहिं (become unruly) / नारीं (women) ॥ कृषी (fields) / निरावहिं (weed out) / चतुर (wise) / किसाना (farmers) / जिमि (just as) / बुध (the learned) / तजहिं (give up) / मोह (delusion) / मद (pride/intoxication) / माना (conceit) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4043.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4043.essence: Clear seeing begins when pride and delusion are pulled out by the roots.
ramacharitamanas::4043.simple_meaning: A wise person removes inner weeds the way a farmer clears a field. Real understanding means dropping delusion, pride, and self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::4043.simple_insight: Growth becomes possible when you stop protecting the habits that choke it.
ramacharitamanas::4043.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the narration keeps using nature images to explain inner life. Here, Tulsidas compares a farmer clearing a field after heavy rain to a wise person clearing the mind of delusion, pride, and conceit.
ramacharitamanas::4043.modern_relevance: You finally sit down to work, but your mind keeps feeding on comparison, defensiveness, and the need to look smart. Real clarity begins when you start pulling those weeds out.
ramacharitamanas::4043.insight: It shifts attention from managing appearances to removing the habits that block clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4044.verse_sanskrit: देखिअत चक्रबाक खग नाहीं। कलिहि पाइ जिमि धर्म पराहीं॥ ऊषर बरषइ तृन नहिं जामा। जिमि हरिजन हियँ उपज न कामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4044.verse_hindi: चक्रवाक पक्षी दिखाई नहीं दे रहे हैं, जैसे कलियुग को पाकर धर्म भाग जाते हैं। ऊसर में वर्षा होती है, पर वहाँ घास तक नहीं उगती। जैसे हरिभक्त के हृदय में काम नहीं उत्पन्न होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4044.english_translation: The chakravaka birds are nowhere to be seen, as dharma flees when Kali arrives. Rain falls on barren ground, yet no grass grows there. In the heart of a devotee of Hari, desire does not arise.
ramacharitamanas::4044.translation_literal: देखिअत (are seen) / चक्रबाक (chakravaka birds) / खग (birds) / नाहीं (not) / कलिहि (in Kali) / पाइ (having obtained) / जिमि (as) / धर्म (dharma) / पराहीं (flee away) ॥ ऊषर (barren land) / बरषइ (it rains) / तृन (grass) / नहिं (not) / जामा (grows) ॥ जिमि (as) / हरिजन (Hari's devotee) / हियँ (in the heart) / उपज (arises) / न (not) / कामा (desire) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4044.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4044.essence: A heart full of Hari leaves no soil for desire.
ramacharitamanas::4044.simple_meaning: A devotee of Hari becomes inwardly barren to desire, just as grass cannot grow on dry land. The verse also says dharma retreats in the age of Kali.
ramacharitamanas::4044.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that deep devotion can quiet the pull of craving.
ramacharitamanas::4044.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas is building a chain of nature images to show how the world changes with moral climate. After comparing fertile and barren land, he turns to the inner life: in a heart filled with Hari, desire has no place to sprout.
ramacharitamanas::4044.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check and feel the old hunger return. But when your mind is anchored in something sacred, that restless wanting has nowhere to settle.
ramacharitamanas::4044.insight: It shifts attention from suppressing desire to cultivating a heart where desire cannot take root.

ramacharitamanas::4045.verse_sanskrit: बिबिध जंतु संकुल महि भ्राजा। प्रजा बाढ़ जिमि पाइ सुराजा॥ जहँ तहँ रहे पथिक थकि नाना। जिमि इंद्रिय गन उपजें ग्याना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4045.verse_hindi: पृथ्वी अनेक तरह के जीवों से भरी हुई उसी तरह शोभायमान है, जैसे सुराज्य पाकर प्रजा की वृद्धि होती है। जहाँ-तहाँ अनेक पथिक थककर ठहरे हुए हैं, जैसे ज्ञान उत्पन्न होने पर इंद्रियाँ (शिथिल होकर विषयों की ओर जाना छोड़ देती हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4045.english_translation: The earth shines with many kinds of living beings, like a kingdom where the people flourish under good rule. Travelers rest everywhere, like the senses fall quiet when true understanding arises.
ramacharitamanas::4045.translation_literal: बिबिध (various) / जंतु (living beings) / संकुल (filled with) / महि (earth) / भ्राजा (shines) / प्रजा (people) / बाढ़ (increase, flourish) / जिमि (like) / पाइ (having obtained) / सुराजा (good rule) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / रहे (remained) / पथिक (travelers) / थकि (tired) / नाना (many) / जिमि (like) / इंद्रिय गन (the group of senses) / उपजें (when arising) / ग्याना (knowledge)
ramacharitamanas::4045.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4045.essence: Understanding stills the senses the way good rule steadies a kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::4045.simple_meaning: A well-ordered world looks alive and flourishing. In the same way, when understanding arises, the senses stop roaming and become still.
ramacharitamanas::4045.simple_insight: Real understanding brings relief: the mind no longer chases every passing thing.
ramacharitamanas::4045.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas is building a comparison from nature and society to inner life. A land under good rule flourishes, and tired travelers finally rest. In the same way, when understanding arises, the senses stop their restless wandering.
ramacharitamanas::4045.modern_relevance: You finally close ten browser tabs after reading something that actually makes sense. The urge to chase every distraction drops away because your mind has found its footing.
ramacharitamanas::4045.insight: It shifts attention from sensory chasing to inner settling through understanding.

ramacharitamanas::4046.verse_sanskrit: कबहुँ प्रबल बह मारुत जहँ तहँ मेघ बिलाहिं। जिमि कपूत के उपजें कुल सद्धर्म नसाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4046.verse_hindi: कभी-कभी वायु बड़े जोर से चलने लगती है, जिससे बादल जहाँ-तहाँ गायब हो जाते हैं। जैसे कुपुत्र के उत्पन्न होने से कुल के उत्तम धर्म (श्रेष्ठ आचरण) नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4046.english_translation: Sometimes fierce winds blow and the clouds vanish here and there. In the same way, when a bad son is born, a family’s noble conduct is destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::4046.translation_literal: कबहुँ (sometimes) / प्रबल (strong) / बह (blows) / मारुत (wind) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / मेघ (clouds) / बिलाहिं (disappear) / जिमि (just as) / कपूत (bad son) के (of) / उपजें (being born) / कुल (family) / सद्धर्म (noble conduct) / नसाहिं (are destroyed)
ramacharitamanas::4046.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4046.essence: One corrupted life can darken an entire family.
ramacharitamanas::4046.simple_meaning: A family can lose its good name and conduct when one child goes badly astray. The image is of strong wind scattering clouds.
ramacharitamanas::4046.simple_insight: Small moral failures can ripple outward farther than you expect.
ramacharitamanas::4046.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the poet is comparing nature to family life. Just as strong winds scatter clouds, a bad son can erase the noble conduct of an entire lineage. It is a warning about how one person’s corruption affects the whole family.
ramacharitamanas::4046.modern_relevance: You watch one teenager start lying, and soon the whole house is tense, defensive, and ashamed. One person’s choices can change the emotional climate for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::4046.insight: It shifts attention from isolated misbehavior to the wider damage a corrupting influence can cause.

ramacharitamanas::4047.verse_sanskrit: कबहु दिवस महँ निबिड़ तम कबहुँक प्रगट पतंग। बिनसइ उपजइ ग्यान जिमि पाइ कुसंग सुसंग॥15ख॥
ramacharitamanas::4047.verse_hindi: कभी (बादलों के कारण) दिन में घोर अंधकार छा जाता है और कभी सूर्य प्रकट हो जाते हैं। जैसे कुसंग पाकर ज्ञान नष्ट हो जाता है और सुसंग पाकर उत्पन्न हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4047.english_translation: Sometimes thick darkness covers the day; sometimes the sun appears. In the same way, understanding is lost in bad company and born again in good company.
ramacharitamanas::4047.translation_literal: कबहु (sometimes) / दिवस महँ (in the day) / निबिड़ (dense) / तम (darkness) / कबहुँक (sometimes) / प्रगट (manifest) / पतंग (sun) / बिनसइ (is destroyed) / उपजइ (is born) / ग्यान (knowledge) / जिमि (just as) / पाइ (having found) / कुसंग (bad company) / सुसंग (good company)
ramacharitamanas::4047.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4047.essence: Your mind follows the company you keep.
ramacharitamanas::4047.simple_meaning: Bad company can hide good judgment, while good company helps clear understanding return.
ramacharitamanas::4047.simple_insight: Who you spend time with quietly shapes what you can see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4047.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the forest journey turns into a lesson about influence. After describing changing weather and signs in nature, the narrator compares darkness and sunlight to the way bad company erases understanding and good company revives it.
ramacharitamanas::4047.modern_relevance: You leave a group chat feeling smaller, sharper, and strangely convinced of things you didn't believe yesterday. Then one honest friend says a few words, and your mind clears.
ramacharitamanas::4047.insight: It teaches you to protect your judgment by choosing the people and environments that sharpen, not distort, your mind.

ramacharitamanas::4048.verse_sanskrit: बरषा बिगत सरद रितु आई। लछमन देखहु परम सुहाई॥ फूलें कास सकल महि छाई। जनु बरषाँ कृत प्रगट बुढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4048.verse_hindi: हे लक्ष्मण! देखो, वर्षा बीत गई और परम सुंदर शरद् ऋतु आ गई। फूले हुए कास से सारी पृथ्वी छा गई। मानो वर्षा ऋतु ने (कास रूपी सफेद बालों के रूप में) अपना बुढ़ापा प्रकट किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4048.english_translation: The rains have passed, and the lovely autumn has arrived, Lakshman. The blooming kans grass covers the earth, as if the rainy season has shown its old age.
ramacharitamanas::4048.translation_literal: बरषा (rainy season) / बिगत (passed) / सरद रितु (autumn season) / आई (has come) / लछमन (Lakshman) / देखहु (look) / परम (very) / सुहाई (beautiful) / फूलें (blooming) / कास (kans grass) / सकल (entire) / महि (earth) / छाई (covered) / जनु (as if) / बरषाँ (the rainy season) / कृत (done/made) / प्रगट (manifest) / बुढ़ाई (old age)
ramacharitamanas::4048.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4048.essence: Beauty can also be a sign that time has moved on.
ramacharitamanas::4048.simple_meaning: The rainy season has ended, autumn has arrived, and the white kans grass now covers the land like the season's aging hair.
ramacharitamanas::4048.simple_insight: Even seasons change and fade; what looks permanent is already passing.
ramacharitamanas::4048.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the scene shifts from the rains to autumn as Ram and Lakshman move through the forest. The poet pauses on the landscape itself, using the blooming kans grass to show time passing and the world changing before the next movement of the story.
ramacharitamanas::4048.modern_relevance: You notice the first cool morning after weeks of rain, and the street outside looks washed clean. Even the season has turned a page without asking permission.
ramacharitamanas::4048.insight: It trains the mind to notice impermanence through ordinary nature, preparing you for the deeper teaching that follows.

ramacharitamanas::4049.verse_sanskrit: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4049.verse_hindi: अगस्त्य के तारे ने उदय होकर मार्ग के जल को सोख लिया, जैसे संतोष लोभ को सोख लेता है। नदियों और तालाबों का निर्मल जल ऐसी शोभा पा रहा है जैसे मद और मोह से रहित संतों का हृदय! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4049.english_translation: The star Agastya rises and dries up the path’s water, just as contentment dries up greed. The clear water of rivers and ponds shines like the hearts of saints free from pride and delusion.
ramacharitamanas::4049.translation_literal: उदित (having risen) / अगस्ति (Agastya) / पंथ (path) / जल (water) / सोषा (dries up) / जिमि (just as) / लोभहिं (greed) / सोषइ (dries up) / संतोषा (contentment) / सरिता (rivers) / सर (ponds) / निर्मल (clear) / जल (water) / सोहा (shines) / संत (saints) / हृदय (heart) / जस (like) / गत (gone) / मद (pride) / मोहा (delusion)
ramacharitamanas::4049.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4049.essence: Contentment clears greed, and a humble heart becomes radiant.
ramacharitamanas::4049.simple_meaning: Contentment weakens greed, and a mind free from pride and confusion becomes clear and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::4049.simple_insight: You do not need to fight greed with force; a settled heart naturally clears it away.
ramacharitamanas::4049.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the season shifts into autumn and the narrator watches nature change. The drying waters and clear ponds become a lesson for Lakshman: contentment thins greed, and a saint’s heart shines when pride and delusion are gone.
ramacharitamanas::4049.modern_relevance: You finally stop checking your phone after sending the message, and the urge to chase reassurance loosens. Something steadier takes over — and the mind feels clean again.
ramacharitamanas::4049.insight: It shifts attention from craving more to cultivating enough, so the mind becomes transparent and calm.

ramacharitamanas::4050.verse_sanskrit: रस रस सूख सरित सर पानी। ममता त्याग करहिं जिमि ग्यानी॥ जानि सरद रितु खंजन आए। पाइ समय जिमि सुकृत सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4050.verse_hindi: नदी और तालाबों का जल धीरे-धीरे सूख रहा है। जैसे ज्ञानी (विवेकी) पुरुष ममता का त्याग करते हैं। शरद ऋतु जानकर खंजन पक्षी आ गए। जैसे समय पाकर सुंदर सुकृत आ सकते हैं। (पुण्य प्रकट हो जाते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4050.english_translation: The waters of rivers and ponds slowly dry up, just as wise people let go of possessiveness. Knowing that autumn has arrived, the khanjan birds come, just as good deeds appear when the right time comes.
ramacharitamanas::4050.translation_literal: रस रस (gradually) / सूख (drying) / सरित (rivers) / सर (ponds) / पानी (water) / ममता (possessiveness) / त्याग (letting go) / करहिं (do) / जिमि (just as) / ग्यानी (wise people) / जानि (knowing) / सरद रितु (autumn season) / खंजन (khanjan birds) / आए (came) / पाइ (having found) / समय (the right time) / जिमि (just as) / सुकृत (good deeds) / सुहाए (become lovely / appear beautifully)
ramacharitamanas::4050.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4050.essence: Wise people release possessiveness, and good things arrive in their own time.
ramacharitamanas::4050.simple_meaning: As the season changes, water dries up and birds arrive at the right time. In the same way, wise people let go of possessiveness and let good things come naturally.
ramacharitamanas::4050.simple_insight: You do not have to grip life so tightly. When you loosen possessiveness, life can move in its own season.
ramacharitamanas::4050.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the forest is changing with autumn. Tulsidas watches rivers shrink and khanjan birds return, then turns the scene into a lesson: wisdom is not clinginess. Letting go creates the space where right action and good fortune can appear.
ramacharitamanas::4050.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending the message, hoping the reply will hurry up. But some things arrive only when you stop squeezing them. Possessiveness dries the moment; patience lets it ripen.
ramacharitamanas::4050.insight: It shifts you from grasping for outcomes to allowing life to unfold in its proper season.

ramacharitamanas::4051.verse_sanskrit: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4051.verse_hindi: न कीचड़ है न धूल? इससे धरती (निर्मल होकर) ऐसी शोभा दे रही है जैसे नीतिनिपुण राजा की करनी! जल के कम हो जाने से मछलियाँ व्याकुल हो रही हैं, जैसे मूर्ख (विवेक शून्य) कुटुम्बी (गृहस्थ) धन के बिना व्याकुल होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4051.english_translation: The mud and dust are gone, so the earth shines like a wise king's conduct. With the water reduced, the fish are restless, like a foolish householder without wealth.
ramacharitamanas::4051.translation_literal: पंक (mud) / न (not) / रेनु (dust) / सोह (shines) / असि (thus) / धरनी (earth) / नीति (conduct) / निपुन (skilled) / नृप (king) / कै (of) / जसि (like) / करनी (conduct)॥ / जल (water) / संकोच (lessening) / बिकल (restless) / भइँ (became) / मीना (fish) / अबुध (foolish) / कुटुंबी (householder) / जिमि (like) / धनहीना (without wealth)॥
ramacharitamanas::4051.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4051.essence: What is released can brighten life; what is depended on can create panic.
ramacharitamanas::4051.simple_meaning: When excess is gone, beauty appears. But when resources shrink, the unprepared become anxious and restless.
ramacharitamanas::4051.simple_insight: Not every loss is a loss; some removals make life clearer, while attachment turns scarcity into panic.
ramacharitamanas::4051.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas is describing the dry season with nature as his teacher. The mud and excess water are gone, so the land looks clean and bright; the fish, however, are distressed. The verse turns that scene into a lesson about what happens when attachment meets shortage.
ramacharitamanas::4051.modern_relevance: Your room feels calm after you finally clear the piles from the floor. But if your savings suddenly drop and your whole mood collapses, this verse is showing you where attachment still rules.
ramacharitamanas::4051.insight: It shifts attention from outer abundance to inner readiness, showing that removal can refine you while dependence exposes you.

ramacharitamanas::4052.verse_sanskrit: बिनु घन निर्मल सोह अकासा। हरिजन इव परिहरि सब आसा॥ कहुँ कहुँ बृष्टि सारदी थोरी। कोउ एक भाव भगति जिमि मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4052.verse_hindi: बिना बादलों का निर्मल आकाश ऐसा शोभित हो रहा है जैसे भगवद्भक्त सब आशाओं को छोड़कर सुशोभित होते हैं। कहीं-कहीं (विरले ही स्थानों में) शरद् ऋतु की थोड़ी-थोड़ी वर्षा हो रही है। जैसे कोई विरले ही मेरी भक्ति पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4052.english_translation: The clear sky shines without clouds, like devotees who have let go of every hope. Scattered showers of autumn fall here and there, just as only a rare few receive my devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4052.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / घन (clouds) / निर्मल (clear) / सोह (shines beautifully) / अकासा (sky) / हरिजन (devotees of the divine) / इव (like) / परिहरि (giving up) / सब (all) / आसा (hope, desire)॥ कहुँ कहुँ (here and there) / बृष्टि (rain) / सारदी (autumnal) / थोरी (little) / कोउ (someone) / एक (only one) / भाव (devotional feeling) / भगति (devotion) / जिमि (like) / मोरी (mine) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4052.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4052.essence: Freedom from craving makes the heart clear enough for devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4052.simple_meaning: A mind without clinging becomes bright and open. True devotion is rare, and only a few people receive it deeply.
ramacharitamanas::4052.simple_insight: There is relief in wanting less, because openness makes room for devotion to arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4052.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas watches the autumn sky and turns it into a lesson. The cloudless brightness mirrors devotees who have dropped craving, while the rare autumn showers show how uncommon deep devotion is.
ramacharitamanas::4052.modern_relevance: You finally stop refreshing your phone for one message, and the room feels bigger. The quiet that follows is the same clearing Tulsidas points to.
ramacharitamanas::4052.insight: It shifts attention from chasing outcomes to making inner space for devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4053.verse_sanskrit: चले हरषि तजि नगर नृप तापस बनिक भिखारि। जिमि हरिभगति पाइ श्रम तजहिं आश्रमी चारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4053.verse_hindi: (शरद् ऋतु पाकर) राजा, तपस्वी, व्यापारी और भिखारी (क्रमशः विजय, तप, व्यापार और भिक्षा के लिए) हर्षित होकर नगर छोड़कर चले। जैसे श्री हरि की भक्ति पाकर चारों आश्रम वाले (नाना प्रकार के साधन रूपी) श्रमों को त्याग देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4053.english_translation: Kings, ascetics, merchants, and beggars all left the city gladly. In the same way, when you find devotion to Hari, the weariness of all four life-stages falls away.
ramacharitamanas::4053.translation_literal: चले (went) / हरषि (joyfully) / तजि (leaving) / नगर (city) / नृप (king) / तापस (ascetic) / बनिक (merchant) / भिखारि (beggar) / जिमि (as) / हरि-भगति (devotion to Hari) / पाइ (having obtained) / श्रम (weariness, effort) / तजहिं (leave) / आश्रमी (those of the four life-stages) / चारि (four)
ramacharitamanas::4053.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4053.essence: Real devotion makes every lesser burden feel light.
ramacharitamanas::4053.simple_meaning: People leave their ordinary work gladly, because devotion to Hari makes all effort feel lighter and less burdensome.
ramacharitamanas::4053.simple_insight: There’s relief in finding a love so deep that striving no longer feels like a burden.
ramacharitamanas::4053.detailed_meaning: The poem watches the season turn and people naturally move out of the city for their different purposes. Tulsidas uses that easy movement to show a deeper truth: when devotion to Ram truly takes hold, the strain of all other pursuits begins to drop away.
ramacharitamanas::4053.modern_relevance: You finally close the laptop after chasing one more task, and the body feels empty but restless. Then something steadier takes over — the relief of caring for what matters most, not everything at once.
ramacharitamanas::4053.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered striving to a single, steady orientation toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4054.verse_sanskrit: सुखी मीन जे नीर अगाधा। जिमि हरि सरन न एकऊ बाधा॥ फूलें कमल सोह सर कैसा। निर्गुन ब्रह्म सगुन भएँ जैसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4054.verse_hindi: जो मछलियाँ अथाह जल में हैं, वे सुखी हैं, जैसे श्री हरि के शरण में चले जाने पर एक भी बाधा नहीं रहती। कमलों के फूलने से तालाब कैसी शोभा दे रहा है, जैसे निर्गुण ब्रह्म सगुण होने पर शोभित होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4054.english_translation: Fish are happy in deep water, just as no obstacle remains in Hari's refuge. A blooming lotus beautifies a lake, just as the formless supreme reality shines when it takes form.
ramacharitamanas::4054.translation_literal: सुखी (happy) / मीन (fish) / जे (who) / नीर (water) / अगाधा (deep, unfathomable) / जिमि (just as) / हरि (Hari) / सरन (refuge) / न (not) / एकऊ (even one) / बाधा (obstacle)॥ / फूलें (having bloomed) / कमल (lotus) / सोह (beautifies) / सर (lake) / कैसा (how) / निर्गुन (formless) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सगुन (with form) / भएँ (having become) / जैसा (as)
ramacharitamanas::4054.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4054.essence: Complete refuge makes obstacles disappear and hidden greatness visible.
ramacharitamanas::4054.simple_meaning: Taking refuge in the divine removes all obstacles. The verse also says that the formless supreme reality becomes beautifully manifest through form, like a lotus brightening a lake.
ramacharitamanas::4054.simple_insight: You can stop bracing yourself; real shelter changes how everything is held.
ramacharitamanas::4054.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the season's beauty to deepen a devotional point. Fish thrive in deep water because nothing threatens them there; likewise, a devotee in Ram's refuge meets no obstacle. The lotus then becomes a second image: form reveals hidden greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4054.modern_relevance: You finally stop checking your phone after sending the hard message. The fear was in carrying it alone; once you place it where it belongs, the weight changes shape.
ramacharitamanas::4054.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to complete reliance, and from formless abstraction to living presence.

ramacharitamanas::4055.verse_sanskrit: गुंजत मधुकर मुखर अनूपा। सुंदर खग रव नाना रूपा॥ चक्रबाक मन दुख निसि पेखी। जिमि दुर्जन पर संपति देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4055.verse_hindi: भौंरे अनुपम शब्द करते हुए गूँज रहे हैं तथा पक्षियों के नाना प्रकार के सुंदर शब्द हो रहे हैं। रात्रि देखकर चकवे के मन में वैसे ही दुःख हो रहा है, जैसे दूसरे की संपत्ति देखकर दुष्ट को होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4055.english_translation: Bees hum with lovely, unmatched sounds, and birds sing in many beautiful tones. The chakravaka bird feels sorrow at night, just as a wicked person feels pain seeing another's prosperity.
ramacharitamanas::4055.translation_literal: गुंजत (humming) / मधुकर (bees) / मुखर (vocal) / अनूपा (matchless) / सुंदर (beautiful) / खग (birds) / रव (sounds) / नाना (many) / रूपा (forms) / चक्रबाक (chakravaka bird) / मन (mind) / दुख (sorrow) / निसि (night) / पेखी (seeing) / जिमि (just as) / दुर्जन (wicked person) / पर (another's) / संपति (prosperity) / देखी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::4055.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4055.essence: Another person's success only hurts the mind that compares.
ramacharitamanas::4055.simple_meaning: The scene is full of sweet bird calls and bee hums, but the chakravaka bird suffers at night. Tulsidas compares that pain to a bad person's jealousy at another's success.
ramacharitamanas::4055.simple_insight: Envy turns another person's good fortune into your own sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4055.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is moving through the forested landscape of Kishkindha, where nature itself mirrors inner states. Bees and birds fill the air with beauty, yet the chakravaka bird grieves at night. Tulsidas uses that contrast to expose the bitterness of envy.
ramacharitamanas::4055.modern_relevance: You scroll past a friend's promotion announcement and feel a twist in your chest. Their good news has not harmed you, but comparison has made it sting.
ramacharitamanas::4055.insight: It trains the mind to notice envy as a self-created wound, not a response caused by the other person's gain.

ramacharitamanas::4056.verse_sanskrit: चातक रटत तृषा अति ओही। जिमि सुख लहइ न संकर द्रोही॥ सरदातप निसि ससि अपहरई। संत दरस जिमि पातक टरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4056.verse_hindi: पपीहा रट लगाए है, उसको बड़ी प्यास है, जैसे श्री शंकरजी का द्रोही सुख नहीं पाता (सुख के लिए झीखता रहता है) शरद् ऋतु के ताप को रात के समय चंद्रमा हर लेता है, जैसे संतों के दर्शन से पाप दूर हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4056.english_translation: The chatak bird keeps crying out in thirst, just as one who turns against Shiva finds no lasting peace. The moon removes the heat of a autumn night, just as the sight of holy people removes sin.
ramacharitamanas::4056.translation_literal: चातक (chatak bird) / रटत (keeps crying) / तृषा (thirst) / अति (very much) / ओही (for that alone) / जिमि (just as) / सुख (peace) / लहइ (gets) / न (not) / संकर (Shiva) / द्रोही (one hostile to) / सरदातप (autumn heat) / निसि (night) / ससि (moon) / अपहरई (removes) / संत (holy people) / दरस (sight) / जिमि (just as) / पातक (wrongdoing) / टरई (is removed)
ramacharitamanas::4056.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4056.essence: Right company cools the thirst that nothing else can.
ramacharitamanas::4056.simple_meaning: A thirsty bird keeps calling for water. In the same way, the heart finds relief through holy company, and old wrongdoing falls away.
ramacharitamanas::4056.simple_insight: What you stay near begins to shape what you can endure.
ramacharitamanas::4056.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the forest images keep building a lesson for Hanuman and Sugriva’s world: longing is not weakness when it is aimed rightly. The thirsty chatak, the cooling moon, and the cleansing presence of holy people all point to the same truth.
ramacharitamanas::4056.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is calm, and your shoulders drop without effort. The company around you can either inflame your restlessness or quietly wash it away.
ramacharitamanas::4056.insight: It shifts you from chasing relief alone to seeking the company that naturally restores you.

ramacharitamanas::4057.verse_sanskrit: देखि इंदु चकोर समुदाई। चितवहिं जिमि हरिजन हरि पाई॥ मसक दंस बीते हिम त्रासा। जिमि द्विज द्रोह किएँ कुल नासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4057.verse_hindi: चकोरों के समुदाय चंद्रमा को देखकर इस प्रकार टकटकी लगाए हैं जैसे भगवद्भक्त भगवान् को पाकर उनके (निर्निमेष नेत्रों से) दर्शन करते हैं। मच्छर और डाँस जाड़े के डर से इस प्रकार नष्ट हो गए जैसे ब्राह्मण के साथ वैर करने से कुल का नाश हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4057.english_translation: Seeing the moon, the whole flock of chakoras gazes at it just as devotees gaze at the divine after finding the divine. Mosquitoes and gnats are destroyed by the fear of winter just as a family is ruined by hostility toward a brahmin.
ramacharitamanas::4057.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / इंदु (moon) / चकोर (chakora birds) / समुदाई (group, flock) / चितवहिं (they gaze) / जिमि (as) / हरिजन (devotees) / हरि (the divine) / पाई (having found) / मसक (mosquitoes) / दंस (gnats, biting insects) / बीते (perished, passed away) / हिम (cold, winter) / त्रासा (fear) / जिमि (as) / द्विज (brahmin) / द्रोह (enmity) / किएँ (by doing) / कुल (family, lineage) / नासा (ruin, destruction)
ramacharitamanas::4057.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4057.essence: Longing can become a steady, wordless gaze; hostility can erase a whole line.
ramacharitamanas::4057.simple_meaning: The verse gives two similes from nature: chakoras stare at the moon the way devotees gaze at the divine, and small insects vanish in winter just as a family is ruined by hostility toward a brahmin.
ramacharitamanas::4057.simple_insight: It reminds you that longing can be pure, and hostility can quietly destroy a whole line.
ramacharitamanas::4057.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand’s nature-rich opening, Tulsidas keeps painting the world in comparisons. Here he uses the chakora’s fixed gaze and the fate of insects in cold weather to build emotional and moral atmosphere, not to make a direct teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::4057.modern_relevance: You notice how a child can stare at a beloved parent without blinking, or how one bitter feud can poison an entire household. The verse turns both into living images.
ramacharitamanas::4057.insight: It trains the mind to read nature as a mirror for devotion and consequence.

ramacharitamanas::4058.verse_sanskrit: भूमि जीव संकुल रहे गए सरद रितु पाइ। सदगुर मिलें जाहिं जिमि संसय भ्रम समुदाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4058.verse_hindi: (वर्षा ऋतु के कारण) पृथ्वी पर जो जीव भर गए थे, वे शरद् ऋतु को पाकर वैसे ही नष्ट हो गए जैसे सद्गुरु के मिल जाने पर संदेह और भ्रम के समूह नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4058.english_translation: The creatures crowded on the earth during the rainy season disappeared when autumn arrived, just as doubt and confusion disappear when a true teacher is found.
ramacharitamanas::4058.translation_literal: भूमि (earth) / जीव (creatures) / संकुल (crowded, packed together) / रहे (remained) / गए (went away, disappeared) / सरद रितु (autumn season) / पाइ (having obtained, upon arrival) / सदगुर (true teacher) / मिलें (when met) / जाहिं (go away) / जिमि (just as) / संसय (doubt) / भ्रम (confusion, delusion) / समुदाइ (group, mass)
ramacharitamanas::4058.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4058.essence: A true teacher makes confusion fall away on contact.
ramacharitamanas::4058.simple_meaning: When autumn arrives, the earth is no longer crowded with creatures from the rains. In the same way, meeting a true teacher makes doubt and confusion disappear.
ramacharitamanas::4058.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that confusion is not permanent.
ramacharitamanas::4058.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is moving through a season of searching in Kishkindhakand, and Tulsidas pauses to teach through nature. The rains have ended, the world is clearer, and that clearing becomes an image for what happens when guidance finally arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4058.modern_relevance: You’ve been turning the same problem over in your head for weeks, and then one honest conversation cuts through everything. The mess was real, but it was never the whole picture.
ramacharitamanas::4058.insight: It shifts the mind from wrestling with confusion to seeking clear guidance.

ramacharitamanas::4059.verse_sanskrit: बरषा गत निर्मल रितु आई। सुधि न तात सीता कै पाई॥ एक बार कैसेहुँ सुधि जानौं। कालुह जीति निमिष महुँ आनौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4059.verse_hindi: वर्षा बीत गई, निर्मल शरद्ऋतु आ गई, परंतु हे तात! सीता की कोई खबर नहीं मिली। एक बार कैसे भी पता पाऊँ तो काल को भी जीतकर पल भर में जानकी को ले आऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4059.english_translation: The rains have ended and the clear season has come, but, O father, I have found no news of Sita. If I could learn her whereabouts even once, I would conquer time itself and bring Janaki back in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4059.translation_literal: बरषा (rainy season) / गत (ended) / निर्मल (clear, pure) / रितु (season) / आई (has come) / सुधि (news, tidings) / न (not) / तात (father) / सीता (of Sita) / कै (of) / पाई (found) / एक (one) / बार (time) / कैसेहुँ (somehow) / सुधि (news) / जानौं (may I know) / कालुह (time itself) / जीति (conquering) / निमिष (moment) / महुँ (within) / आनौं (may I bring)
ramacharitamanas::4059.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4059.essence: A single clue can turn waiting into unstoppable action.
ramacharitamanas::4059.simple_meaning: Hanuman has reached the clear season, but he still has no news of Sita. He says that if he can find even one clue, he will overcome time and bring her back immediately.
ramacharitamanas::4059.simple_insight: Hope becomes unstoppable when it has a clear direction.
ramacharitamanas::4059.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is in Lanka, still searching for Sita after the rains have passed. The city is no easier to read, and he has no sign of her yet. But his devotion is so focused that one real clue would make him fearless enough to outrun time itself.
ramacharitamanas::4059.modern_relevance: You are waiting for a reply that will decide everything, and the silence is wearing you down. Then one small message arrives, and your whole body changes. Clarity does that.
ramacharitamanas::4059.insight: It turns longing into decisive action by showing how one clue can release total effort.

ramacharitamanas::4060.verse_sanskrit: कतहुँ रहउ जौं जीवति होई। तात जतन करि आनउँ सोई॥ सुग्रीवहुँ सुधि मोरि बिसारी। पावा राज कोस पुर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4060.verse_hindi: कहीं भी रहे, यदि जीती होगी तो हे तात! यत्न करके मैं उसे अवश्य लाऊँगा। राज्य, खजाना, नगर और स्त्री पा गया, इसलिए सुग्रीव ने भी मेरी सुध भुला दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4060.english_translation: Wherever she may be, if she is still alive, I will search and bring her back with effort. Sugriva has forgotten my help now that he has gained kingdom, treasure, city, and woman.
ramacharitamanas::4060.translation_literal: कतहुँ (anywhere) / रहउ (may remain) / जौं (if) / जीवति (alive) / होई (is) / तात (dear one) / जतन (effort) / करि (doing) / आनउँ (I will bring) / सोई (her) ॥ / सुग्रीवहुँ (even Sugriva) / सुधि (memory) / मोरि (my) / बिसारी (forgot) / पावा (having obtained) / राज (kingdom) / कोस (treasure) / पुर (city) / नारी (woman) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4060.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4060.essence: Love keeps searching even after being forgotten.
ramacharitamanas::4060.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he will search for Sita and bring her back if she is alive, even though Sugriva has forgotten his help after gaining power and comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4060.simple_insight: True service keeps going even when recognition disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4060.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman is still searching for Sita in the forest alliance with Sugriva. He vows to keep looking and bring her back if she is alive, while also noticing that Sugriva has already moved on after receiving his reward.
ramacharitamanas::4060.modern_relevance: You helped someone through their worst week, and now they barely reply. The hurt is real. This verse reminds you that sincere service does not depend on being remembered.
ramacharitamanas::4060.insight: It shifts attention from gratitude received to duty fulfilled.

ramacharitamanas::4061.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं सायक मारा मैं बाली। तेहिं सर हतौं मूढ़ कहँ काली॥ जासु कृपाँ छूटहिं मद मोहा। ता कहुँ उमा कि सपनेहुँ कोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4061.verse_hindi: जिस बाण से मैंने बालि को मारा था, उसी बाण से कल उस मूढ़ को मारूँ! (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! जिनकी कृपा से मद और मोह छूट जाते हैं उनको कहीं स्वप्न में भी क्रोध हो सकता है? (यह तो लीला मात्र है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4061.english_translation: The same arrow with which I struck Bali, I would strike that fool tomorrow. O Uma, can those whom divine grace has freed from pride and delusion ever feel anger, even in a dream?
ramacharitamanas::4061.translation_literal: जेहिं (with which) / सायक (arrow) / मारा (struck) / मैं (I) / बाली (Bali) / तेहिं (with that) / सर (arrow) / हतौं (I would strike) / मूढ़ (fool) / कहँ (to) / काली (tomorrow) / जासु (whose) / कृपाँ (by grace) / छूटहिं (are released) / मद (pride) / मोहा (delusion) / ता कहुँ (for that one) / उमा (O Uma) / कि (can) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / कोहा (anger)
ramacharitamanas::4061.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4061.essence: When pride falls away, anger has no place to land.
ramacharitamanas::4061.simple_meaning: Shiva says the arrow that killed Bali would still be the right one, but only as divine play. Anyone freed from pride and confusion cannot truly feel anger.
ramacharitamanas::4061.simple_insight: You can stop taking your reactions so personally; the calmer your seeing, the less anger can grip you.
ramacharitamanas::4061.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram has just helped Sugriva regain his kingdom, and the story turns to Bali's death. Shiva explains to Uma that the act was not driven by anger. For one freed from pride and delusion, even a seeming threat is only divine play.
ramacharitamanas::4061.modern_relevance: You replay a harsh message in your head and feel your chest tighten. Then you notice the real wound is not the text — it's the pride underneath it. Once that loosens, the anger loses its fuel.
ramacharitamanas::4061.insight: It shifts attention from the outer event to the inner distortion that makes anger possible.

ramacharitamanas::4062.verse_sanskrit: जानहिं यह चरित्र मुनि ग्यानी। जिन्ह रघुबीर चरन रति मानी॥ लछिमन क्रोधवंत प्रभु जाना। धनुष चढ़ाई गहे कर बाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4062.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी मुनि जिन्होंने श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में प्रीति मान ली है (जोड़ ली है), वे ही इस चरित्र (लीला रहस्य) को जानते हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने जब प्रभु को क्रोधयुक्त जाना, तब उन्होंने धनुष चढ़ाकर बाण हाथ में ले लिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4062.english_translation: Only wise sages who have placed their love at Raghubir’s feet know this secret play. When Lakshman saw the Lord angry, he raised his bow and took an arrow in hand.
ramacharitamanas::4062.translation_literal: जानहिं (know) / यह (this) / चरित्र (play, sacred episode) / मुनि (sages) / ग्यानी (wise) / जिन्ह (who) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love, devotion) / मानी (held, placed)॥ / लछिमन (Lakshman) / क्रोधवंत (angry) / प्रभु (the Lord) / जाना (saw, understood) / धनुष (bow) / चढ़ाई (raised) / गहे (took hold of) / कर (in hand) / बाना (arrow)॥
ramacharitamanas::4062.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4062.essence: Ram’s deepest play opens only to devotion, and loyal love reacts without delay.
ramacharitamanas::4062.simple_meaning: Only those with deep devotion can understand Ram’s hidden play. Lakshman, seeing Ram angry, immediately picked up his bow and arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4062.simple_insight: Some truths are understood by devotion, not analysis. Loyalty also means being ready at once.
ramacharitamanas::4062.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram is dealing with Sugriva and the tense politics around Vali’s death. Tulsidas says the deeper meaning of Ram’s actions is known only to sages devoted to his feet, while Lakshman instantly moves to protect Ram when he senses anger.
ramacharitamanas::4062.modern_relevance: You can read a situation a hundred times and still miss its meaning. The person who loves deeply often understands fastest, and acts before anyone else has finished explaining.
ramacharitamanas::4062.insight: It shifts you from intellectual distance to devoted understanding and immediate protective action.

ramacharitamanas::4063.verse_sanskrit: तब अनुजहि समुझावा रघुपति करुना सींव। भय देखाइ लै आवहु तात सखा सुग्रीव ॥
ramacharitamanas::4063.verse_hindi: तब दया की सीमा श्री रघुनाथजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को समझाया कि हे तात! सखा सुग्रीव को केवल भय दिखलाकर ले आओ (उसे मारने की बात नहीं है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4063.english_translation: Then Raghupati, full of compassion, explained to his younger brother: 'Dear brother, bring Sugriva here only by showing him fear.'
ramacharitamanas::4063.translation_literal: तब (then) / अनुजहि (to the younger brother) / समुझावा (explained) / रघुपति (Raghupati, Lord of the Raghu clan) / करुना (compassion) / सींव (limit) / भय (fear) / देखाइ (showing) / लै (bringing) / आवहु (bring) / तात (dear brother) / सखा (friend) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva)
ramacharitamanas::4063.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4063.essence: Compassion sets the limit on force.
ramacharitamanas::4063.simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to bring Sugriva by frightening him, not by killing him. Compassion guides even the use of force.
ramacharitamanas::4063.simple_insight: Strength becomes humane when it is held by compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4063.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Ram is preparing to meet Sugriva, the monkey king who may become an ally. Lakshman is ready to strike, but Ram stops him and sets the limit: scare Sugriva into coming, do not destroy him.
ramacharitamanas::4063.modern_relevance: You catch a teammate hiding from a hard conversation. You do not need to crush them to get their attention; a firm warning can open the door to repair.
ramacharitamanas::4063.insight: It teaches you to apply pressure with restraint, so correction serves the relationship instead of damaging it.

ramacharitamanas::4064.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ पवनसुत हृदयँ बिचारा। राम काजु सुग्रीवँ बिसारा॥ निकट जाइ चरनन्हि सिरु नावा। चारिहु बिधि तेहि कहि समुझावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4064.verse_hindi: यहाँ (किष्किन्धा नगरी में) पवनकुमार श्री हनुमान् जी ने विचार किया कि सुग्रीव ने श्री रामजी के कार्य को भुला दिया। उन्होंने सुग्रीव के पास जाकर चरणों में सिर नवाया। (साम, दान, दंड, भेद) चारों प्रकार की नीति कहकर उन्हें समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4064.english_translation: Here, Hanuman thought in his heart that Sugriva had forgotten Ram's work. He went close, bowed his head at Sugriva's feet, and explained the four methods of policy: conciliation, gifts, division, and force.
ramacharitamanas::4064.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारा (considered) / राम (Ram) / काजु (task) / सुग्रीवँ (Sugriva) / बिसारा (forgot) / निकट (near) / जाइ (going) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / चारिहु (four) / बिधि (methods) / तेहि (to him) / कहि (having said) / समुझावा (explained)
ramacharitamanas::4064.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4064.essence: True service corrects without pride and acts without noise.
ramacharitamanas::4064.simple_meaning: Hanuman notices that Sugriva has forgotten Ram's task. He approaches respectfully, bows, and gently reminds him using practical counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4064.simple_insight: Real service can be both respectful and effective.
ramacharitamanas::4064.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Hanuman sees that Sugriva has slipped into forgetfulness after gaining power. Rather than confront him harshly, he approaches with respect, bows, and uses wise policy to bring him back to Ram's cause.
ramacharitamanas::4064.modern_relevance: A teammate has drifted from the plan, and you need to bring them back without ego or embarrassment. Hanuman shows how to correct with dignity, not dominance.
ramacharitamanas::4064.insight: It teaches you to pair firmness with humility when someone forgets their responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::4065.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुग्रीवँ परम भय माना। बिषयँ मोर हरि लीन्हेउ ग्याना॥ अब मारुतसुत दूत समूहा। पठवहु जहँ तहँ बानर जूहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4065.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर सुग्रीव ने बहुत ही भय माना। (और कहा-) विषयों ने मेरे ज्ञान को हर लिया। अब हे पवनसुत! जहाँ-तहाँ वानरों के यूथ रहते हैं, वहाँ दूतों के समूहों को भेजो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4065.english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's words, Sugriva felt great fear and said, 'Desires have stolen away my wisdom. Now, O son of the wind, send messengers to the monkey bands wherever they are.'
ramacharitamanas::4065.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुग्रीवँ (Sugriva) / परम (great) / भय (fear) / माना (felt) / बिषयँ (desires) / मोर (my) / हरि (stolen away) / लीन्हेउ (have taken) / ग्याना (wisdom) ॥ / अब (now) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind) / दूत (messengers) / समूहा (groups) / पठवहु (send) / जहँ तहँ (wherever) / बानर (monkey) / जूहा (bands) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4065.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4065.essence: Seeing your own confusion is the first step back to right action.
ramacharitamanas::4065.simple_meaning: Sugriva admits that desire has clouded his judgment and asks Hanuman to send messengers to all the monkey groups.
ramacharitamanas::4065.simple_insight: It feels honest to name the weakness before trying to fix it.
ramacharitamanas::4065.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Hanuman has just reminded Sugriva of Ram's cause. Sugriva admits his mind has been overtaken by desire and fear, then immediately turns to action: send messengers to gather the monkey bands.
ramacharitamanas::4065.modern_relevance: You finally admit that craving has made you sloppy, and then you call the team, send the texts, and fix the mess before it spreads.
ramacharitamanas::4065.insight: It shifts the mind from self-deception to corrective action once distraction is recognised.

ramacharitamanas::4066.verse_sanskrit: कहहु पाख महुँ आव न जोई। मोरें कर ता कर बध होई॥ तब हनुमंत बोलाए दूता। सब कर करि सनमान बहूता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4066.verse_hindi: और कहला दो कि एक पखवाड़े में (पंद्रह दिनों में) जो न आ जाएगा, उसका मेरे हाथों वध होगा। तब हनुमान् जी ने दूतों को बुलाया और सबका बहुत सम्मान करके- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4066.english_translation: And say: whoever does not come within a fortnight will be killed by my hand. Then Hanuman called the messengers and honoured them all greatly.
ramacharitamanas::4066.translation_literal: कहहु (say) / पाख महुँ (within a fortnight) / आव (come) / न (not) / जोई (whoever) / मोरें (by my) / कर (hand) / ता कर (that one’s) / बध (killing) / होई (will be) ॥ / तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / बोलाए (called) / दूता (messengers) / सब कर (of all) / करि (doing) / सनमान (honour) / बहूता (greatly) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4066.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4066.essence: Firm boundaries can still be delivered with respect.
ramacharitamanas::4066.simple_meaning: Hanuman sends a firm warning: if someone does not return within fifteen days, he will be punished. Then he respectfully sends the messengers away.
ramacharitamanas::4066.simple_insight: Strength can be firm without becoming rude.
ramacharitamanas::4066.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Hanuman is handling Sugriva’s urgent command after reminding him of Ram’s cause. The message is meant to restore discipline among the monkeys, not to create chaos. Hanuman speaks with authority and still treats the messengers with respect.
ramacharitamanas::4066.modern_relevance: You have to send a hard message to a team that has gone slack, but you still choose your words carefully. Firmness does not require humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::4066.insight: It shows how to combine authority with courtesy: enforce the standard, but keep your dignity intact.

ramacharitamanas::4067.verse_sanskrit: भय अरु प्रीति नीति देखराई। चले सकल चरनन्हि सिर नाई॥ एहि अवसर लछिमन पुर आए। क्रोध देखि जहँ तहँ कपि धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4067.verse_hindi: सबको भय, प्रीति और नीति दिखलाई। सब बंदर चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले। इसी समय लक्ष्मणजी नगर में आए। उनका क्रोध देखकर बंदर जहाँ-तहाँ भागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4067.english_translation: They showed fear, affection, and policy. All the monkeys bowed their heads and left. Just then Lakshman entered the city, and seeing his anger, the monkeys fled here and there.
ramacharitamanas::4067.translation_literal: भय (fear) / अरु (and) / प्रीति (affection) / नीति (policy) / देखराई (showed) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / एहि (this) / अवसर (occasion) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / पुर (city) / आए (came) / क्रोध (anger) / देखि (seeing) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / कपि (monkeys) / धाए (ran)
ramacharitamanas::4067.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4067.essence: Lakshman’s anger instantly changes the whole mood of the city.
ramacharitamanas::4067.simple_meaning: The monkeys are brought under control by fear, affection, and good conduct. Then Lakshman arrives in anger, and they scatter.
ramacharitamanas::4067.simple_insight: Sometimes a group only becomes orderly when a stronger presence arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4067.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva has just secured his alliance and sent out his commands. The monkeys bow, obey, and move off in respect. Then Lakshman arrives in the city, his anger shaking everyone, and the scene shifts from order to alarm.
ramacharitamanas::4067.modern_relevance: A calm room can turn tense the moment the manager walks in with a hard face. People who were cooperating a second ago suddenly start looking for the nearest exit.
ramacharitamanas::4067.insight: It shows how quickly a mood can spread through a group when one powerful person enters.

ramacharitamanas::4068.verse_sanskrit: धनुष चढ़ाइ कहा तब जारि करउँ पुर छार। ब्याकुल नगर देखि तब आयउ बालिकुमार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4068.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर लक्ष्मणजी ने धनुष चढ़ाकर कहा कि नगर को जलाकर अभी राख कर दूँगा। तब नगरभर को व्याकुल देखकर बालिपुत्र अंगदजी उनके पास आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4068.english_translation: Then Lakshman raised his bow and said, 'I will burn the city to ashes now.' Seeing the city in turmoil, Bali's son Angad came to him.
ramacharitamanas::4068.translation_literal: धनुष (bow) / चढ़ाइ (raising) / कहा (said) / तब (then) / जारि (burning) / करउँ (I will do) / पुर (city) / छार (ashes) / ब्याकुल (disturbed) / नगर (city) / देखि (seeing) / तब (then) / आयउ (came) / बालिकुमार (son of Bali)
ramacharitamanas::4068.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4068.essence: Anger raises the stakes, and courage must answer it.
ramacharitamanas::4068.simple_meaning: Lakshman threatens to burn the city to ashes, and Angad comes forward when he sees the city in distress.
ramacharitamanas::4068.simple_insight: A threat can break the silence of a tense moment, but it is not the end of the encounter.
ramacharitamanas::4068.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Lakshman’s anger flares after the monkey leaders delay their response. He lifts his bow and threatens destruction. The city panics, and Angad steps in to face him and calm the crisis.
ramacharitamanas::4068.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone says, 'Fine, I’ll handle this myself.' The threat changes the mood, but it also invites the first real response.
ramacharitamanas::4068.insight: It shows how force can shake people into action, but reconciliation still needs someone to step forward.

ramacharitamanas::4069.verse_sanskrit: चर नाइ सिरु बिनती कीन्ही। लछिमन अभय बाँह तेहि दीन्ही॥ क्रोधवंत लछिमन सुनि काना। कह कपीस अति भयँ अकुलाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4069.verse_hindi: अंगद ने उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर विनती की (क्षमा-याचना की) तब लक्ष्मणजी ने उनको अभय बाँह दी (भुजा उठाकर कहा कि डरो मत)। सुग्रीव ने अपने कानों से लक्ष्मणजी को क्रोधयुक्त सुनकर भय से अत्यंत व्याकुल होकर कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4069.english_translation: Angad bowed his head at their feet and pleaded for mercy. Lakshmana then raised his arm and gave him fearlessness. Hearing Lakshmana’s angry words, Sugriva became deeply alarmed and said—
ramacharitamanas::4069.translation_literal: चर (feet) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / बिनती (plea) / कीन्ही (made) / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / अभय (fearlessness) / बाँह (arm) / तेहि (to him) / दीन्ही (gave) / क्रोधवंत (angry) / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (ears) / कह (said) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / अति (very) / भयँ (with fear) / अकुलाना (distressed)
ramacharitamanas::4069.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4069.essence: Mercy can calm a moment, but anger can keep fear alive.
ramacharitamanas::4069.simple_meaning: Angad asks for mercy, Lakshmana reassures him, and Sugriva is shaken by Lakshmana’s anger.
ramacharitamanas::4069.simple_insight: Fear eases when respect is restored, but tension returns fast when anger stays alive.
ramacharitamanas::4069.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, the monkey leaders are trying to calm Lakshmana after the insult to Sugriva. Angad bows and pleads, Lakshmana lifts his arm in reassurance, and Sugriva still trembles because the danger has not fully passed.
ramacharitamanas::4069.modern_relevance: A tense group chat goes silent after one harsh message. Someone apologizes, one person softens, but another is still bracing for the next blow.
ramacharitamanas::4069.insight: It shows how quickly a room can shift from apology to relief to renewed fear.

ramacharitamanas::4070.verse_sanskrit: सुनु हनुमंत संग लै तारा। करि बिनती समुझाउ कुमारा॥ तारा सहित जाइ हनुमाना। चरन बंदि प्रभु सुजस बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4070.verse_hindi: हे हनुमान् सुनो, तुम तारा को साथ ले जाकर विनती करके राजकुमार को समझाओ (समझा-बुझाकर शांत करो)। हनुमान् जी ने तारा सहित जाकर लक्ष्मणजी के चरणों की वंदना की और प्रभु के सुंदर यश का बखान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4070.english_translation: Hanuman, take Tara with you. Go with respectful words and calm the prince. Hanuman went with Tara, bowed at the feet of the Lord, and praised his glorious fame.
ramacharitamanas::4070.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / संग (with) / लै (taking) / तारा (Tara) / करि (doing) / बिनती (request) / समुझाउ (explain/calm) / कुमारा (the prince) ॥ / तारा (Tara) / सहित (together with) / जाइ (going) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / सुजस (glorious fame) / बखाना (praised)
ramacharitamanas::4070.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4070.essence: Humility opens the door that anger has shut.
ramacharitamanas::4070.simple_meaning: Hanuman is sent with Tara to speak gently to Lakshman and calm the situation. He bows first, then praises Ram's glory.
ramacharitamanas::4070.simple_insight: Respect can soften anger faster than force.
ramacharitamanas::4070.detailed_meaning: Laxman has just threatened Lanka, and the city is trembling. Tara steps in as mediator, and Hanuman goes with her to face Lakshman respectfully. Before speaking, he bows and praises Ram, turning confrontation into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4070.modern_relevance: A heated family argument is one message away from exploding. Someone calmer steps in first, speaks with respect, and lowers the temperature before anyone tries to win.
ramacharitamanas::4070.insight: It teaches you to enter conflict with humility, not escalation, and to lead with reverence before persuasion.

ramacharitamanas::4071.verse_sanskrit: करि बिनती मंदिर लै आए। चरन पखारि पलँग बैठाए॥ तब कपीस चरनन्हि सिरु नावा। गहि भुज लछिमन कंठ लगावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4071.verse_hindi: वे विनती करके उन्हें महल में ले आए तथा चरणों को धोकर उन्हें पलँग पर बैठाया। तब वानरराज सुग्रीव ने उनके चरणों में सिर नवाया और लक्ष्मणजी ने हाथ पकड़कर उनको गले से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4071.english_translation: They brought him in with a request, washed his feet, and seated him on a couch. Then Sugriva bowed his head at Lakshmana's feet, and Lakshmana embraced him by the arm and held him to his chest.
ramacharitamanas::4071.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिनती (request) / मंदिर (palace) / लै (taking) / आए (came) / चरन (feet) / पखारि (washing) / पलँग (couch) / बैठाए (seated) / तब (then) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / गहि (holding) / भुज (arm) / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / कंठ (neck) / लगावा (embraced)
ramacharitamanas::4071.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4071.essence: Humility turns an enemy meeting into friendship.
ramacharitamanas::4071.simple_meaning: Sugriva welcomes Lakshmana with honor, bows to him, and receives a loving embrace in return.
ramacharitamanas::4071.simple_insight: Respect softens fear, and dignity returns when pride steps aside.
ramacharitamanas::4071.detailed_meaning: After the tense meeting in Kishkindha, Sugriva brings Lakshmana into the palace with humility. His feet are washed, he is seated with honor, and the earlier hostility melts as Sugriva bows and Lakshmana embraces him.
ramacharitamanas::4071.modern_relevance: You finally sit down with someone after a tense misunderstanding. One honest gesture — a lowered head, a warm hand, a careful welcome — changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::4071.insight: It shifts conflict into trust through visible humility and respect.

ramacharitamanas::4072.verse_sanskrit: नाथ विषय सम मद कछु नाहीं। मुनि मन मोह करइ छन माहीं। सुनत बिनीत बचन सुख पावा। लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4072.verse_hindi: (सुग्रीव ने कहा-) हे नाथ! विषय के समान और कोई मद नहीं है। यह मुनियों के मन में भी क्षणमात्र में मोह उत्पन्न कर देता है (फिर मैं तो विषयी जीव ही ठहरा)। सुग्रीव के विनययुक्त वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने सुख पाया और उनको बहुत प्रकार से समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4072.english_translation: (Sugriva said-) O Lord, there is no pride like desire for pleasure. It can bewilder even the minds of sages in a moment. Hearing his humble words, Lakshman felt pleased and explained many things to him in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::4072.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / विषय (sense-pleasures) / सम (like) / मद (intoxication) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (is not) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / मोह (delusion) / करइ (does) / छन माहीं (in a moment) / सुनत (hearing) / बिनीत (humble) / बचन (words) / सुख (ease / pleasure) / पावा (received) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / तेहि (him) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / समुझावा (explained)
ramacharitamanas::4072.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4072.essence: Desire can confuse even the wise; humility restores clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::4072.simple_meaning: Desire for pleasure is so powerful it can confuse even wise people. Humble words can soften the heart and open the way to understanding.
ramacharitamanas::4072.simple_insight: It reminds you that craving distorts judgment, while humility makes real dialogue possible.
ramacharitamanas::4072.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva is speaking with Lakshman after tensions have eased. He admits how dangerous desire can be, even for sages, and Lakshman responds with calm understanding. The moment turns suspicion into trust.
ramacharitamanas::4072.modern_relevance: You know that moment when a craving starts running the whole day — the third scroll, the extra drink, the need to be chosen. A humble conversation can interrupt that spiral before it hardens into conflict.
ramacharitamanas::4072.insight: It shifts attention from judging others to noticing how desire distorts your own mind.

ramacharitamanas::4073.verse_sanskrit: पवन तनय सब कथा सुनाई। जेहि बिधि गए दूत समुदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4073.verse_hindi: तब पवनसुत हनुमान् जी ने जिस प्रकार सब दिशाओं में दूतों के समूह गए थे वह सब हाल सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4073.english_translation: Then Hanuman, son of the wind, told the whole story of how the envoys had gone out in all directions.
ramacharitamanas::4073.translation_literal: पवन तनय (son of the wind) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / जेहि बिधि (the manner in which) / गए (went) / दूत (envoys) / समुदाई (in groups)
ramacharitamanas::4073.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4073.essence: A report moves the alliance toward its next step.
ramacharitamanas::4073.simple_meaning: Hanuman recounts how the messengers had been sent out in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::4073.simple_insight: Some moments are only bridges: they move the story forward without carrying a full teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4073.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman is reporting back after the search begins. He explains how the envoys went out in groups in every direction. The verse mainly advances the scene, leading into Sugriva's next move.
ramacharitamanas::4073.modern_relevance: You finish a briefing and simply pass along what happened so the next step can begin.
ramacharitamanas::4073.insight: It keeps attention on the unfolding action rather than on a standalone lesson.

ramacharitamanas::4074.verse_sanskrit: हरषि चले सुग्रीव तब अंगदादि कपि साथ। रामानुज आगें करि आए जहँ रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4074.verse_hindi: तब अंगद आदि वानरों को साथ लेकर और श्री रामजी के छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को आगे करके (अर्थात् उनके पीछे-पीछे) सुग्रीव हर्षित होकर चले और जहाँ रघुनाथजी थे वहाँ आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4074.english_translation: Then Sugriva, delighted, set out with Angada and the other monkeys, placing Lakshmana in front, and came to where Raghunath was.
ramacharitamanas::4074.translation_literal: हरषि (delighted) / चले (set out) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / तब (then) / अंगदादि (Angada and the others) / कपि (monkeys) / साथ (with) / रामानुज (Ram's younger brother) / आगें (in front) / करि (having placed) / आए (came) / जहँ (where) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / ॥
ramacharitamanas::4074.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4074.essence: Trust now has legs and is walking toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4074.simple_meaning: Sugriva, along with Angada and the monkeys, went happily to meet Ram, with Lakshmana leading the way.
ramacharitamanas::4074.simple_insight: Joyful movement matters too; when trust returns, even a meeting feels effortless.
ramacharitamanas::4074.detailed_meaning: After hearing Hanuman's report, Sugriva gathers Angada and the monkey chiefs and goes to meet Ram. Lakshmana is placed ahead as a mark of respect. The verse simply shows the alliance moving from talk into action.
ramacharitamanas::4074.modern_relevance: After days of tense messages, you finally walk into the room where the other side is waiting. The stiffness is gone; respect and relief now do the work.
ramacharitamanas::4074.insight: It turns a promise into a meeting, showing trust becoming visible action.

ramacharitamanas::4075.verse_sanskrit: नाइ चरन सिरु कह कर जोरी॥ नाथ मोहि कछु नाहिन खोरी॥ अतिसय प्रबल देव तव माया॥ छूटइ राम करहु जौं दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4075.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर हाथ जोड़कर सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे नाथ! मुझे कुछ भी दोष नहीं है। हे देव! आपकी माया अत्यंत ही प्रबल है। आप जब दया करते हैं, हे राम! तभी यह छूटती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4075.english_translation: Bowing his head to Ram's feet and joining his hands, Sugriva said, 'Lord, I have no fault. Your veil of appearance is very powerful. It falls away only when you show mercy, Ram.'
ramacharitamanas::4075.translation_literal: नाइ (bowing) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / कह (said) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (me) / कछु (some) / नाहिन (not) / खोरी (fault) / अतिसय (extremely) / प्रबल (powerful) / देव (divine one) / तव (your) / माया (veil of appearance) / छूटइ (falls away) / राम (Ram) / करहु (do) / जौं (if) / दाया (mercy)
ramacharitamanas::4075.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4075.essence: Only mercy can lift the veil that keeps you confused.
ramacharitamanas::4075.simple_meaning: Sugriva bows to Ram and admits that the power of appearance is overwhelming. He says only Ram's mercy can free someone from it.
ramacharitamanas::4075.simple_insight: Humility opens the door when self-blame and confusion have closed it.
ramacharitamanas::4075.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva comes before Ram after the alliance is formed. He bows low, admits his helplessness, and names Ram's veil of appearance as the force that traps beings. The moment turns from politics to surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4075.modern_relevance: You keep circling the same mistake, sure the problem is your weakness. Then one honest conversation reveals how much of the confusion was the mind's own veil.
ramacharitamanas::4075.insight: It shifts blame away from personal failure and toward the deeper force of appearance that mercy can dissolve.

ramacharitamanas::4076.verse_sanskrit: बिषय बस्य सुर नर मुनि स्वामी॥ मैं पावँर पसु कपि अति कामी॥ नारि नयन सर जाहि न लागा। घोर क्रोध तम निसि जो जागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4076.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सभी विषयों के वश में हैं। फिर मैं तो पामर पशु और पशुओं में भी अत्यंत कामी बंदर हूँ। स्त्री का नयन बाण जिसको नहीं लगा, जो भयंकर क्रोध रूपी अँधेरी रात में भी जागता रहता है (क्रोधान्ध नहीं होता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4076.english_translation: All radiant beings, humans, sages, and rulers are bound by desire. I am a miserable creature, a lowly monkey, and intensely driven by craving. The arrow from a woman's eyes has not struck me, and I remain awake even in the dark night of fierce anger.
ramacharitamanas::4076.translation_literal: बिषय (sense-objects/desire) / बस्य (under the control of) / सुर (radiant beings) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / स्वामी (rulers)॥ / मैं (I) / पावँर (miserable) / पसु (creature) / कपि (monkey) / अति (very) / कामी (full of wanting)॥ / नारि (woman) / नयन (eyes) / सर (arrow) / जाहि (which) / न (not) / लागा (has struck) / घोर (fierce) / क्रोध (anger) / तम (darkness) / निसि (night) / जो (who) / जागा (awake) / ॥
ramacharitamanas::4076.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4076.essence: Humility sees its own weakness and becomes ready for mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4076.simple_meaning: Sugriva humbly says that even great beings are often ruled by desire, while he feels even more vulnerable and full of craving.
ramacharitamanas::4076.simple_insight: Honesty about your weakness can open the door to grace.
ramacharitamanas::4076.detailed_meaning: Sugriva stands before Ram after being brought forward by Lakshman and the monkey chiefs. He bows and confesses his own impurity, contrasting himself with even gods, humans, sages, and rulers who fall under desire. This humility prepares the way for Ram's mercy in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::4076.modern_relevance: You sit in front of someone whose approval could change everything, and instead of pretending, you admit your weakness. That kind of honesty can be the beginning of trust.
ramacharitamanas::4076.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to clear self-recognition before asking for help.

ramacharitamanas::4077.verse_sanskrit: लोभ पाँस जेहिं गर न बँधाया। सो नर तुम्ह समान रघुराया॥ यह गुन साधन तें नहिं होई। तुम्हरी कृपा पाव कोइ कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4077.verse_hindi: और लोभ की फाँसी से जिसने अपना गला नहीं बँधाया, हे रघुनाथजी! वह मनुष्य आप ही के समान है। ये गुण साधन से नहीं प्राप्त होते। आपकी कृपा से ही कोई-कोई इन्हें पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4077.english_translation: A person who has not bound their neck in the noose of greed is like you, Raghunath. Such qualities are not gained by practice; only a rare few receive them by your grace.
ramacharitamanas::4077.translation_literal: लोभ (greed) / पाँस (noose) / जेहिं (who) / गर (neck) / न (not) / बँधाया (bound) / सो (that) / नर (person) / तुम्ह (you) / समान (equal to) / रघुराया (Raghunath) / यह (these) / गुन (qualities) / साधन (practice) / तें (from) / नहिं (not) / होई (become) / तुम्हरी (your) / कृपा (grace) / पाव (receives) / कोइ कोई (only a rare few)
ramacharitamanas::4077.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4077.essence: Freedom from greed is a gift, not a personal achievement.
ramacharitamanas::4077.simple_meaning: A person who is free from greed is like Ram. Such qualities cannot be forced through practice alone; they come only by grace.
ramacharitamanas::4077.simple_insight: It softens pride in self-improvement and opens the heart to gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::4077.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Sugriva is apologising to Ram after admitting his weakness and fear. He says that freedom from greed is no ordinary achievement, and that such purity appears only when Ram's grace touches a person.
ramacharitamanas::4077.modern_relevance: You open your banking app after a salary hike and still feel hungry for more. This verse reminds you that some freedom cannot be manufactured by ambition alone.
ramacharitamanas::4077.insight: It shifts the mind from self-made virtue to receptive humility before grace.

ramacharitamanas::4078.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुपति बोले मुसुकाई। तुम्ह प्रिय मोहि भरत जिमि भाई॥ अब सोइ जतनु करह मन लाई। जेहि बिधि सीता कै सुधि पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4078.verse_hindi: तब श्री रघुनाथजी मुस्कुराकर बोले- हे भाई! तुम मुझे भरत के समान प्यारे हो। अब मन लगाकर वही उपाय करो जिस उपाय से सीता की खबर मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4078.english_translation: Then Raghupati smiled and said, "You are dear to me, brother, just as Bharat is. Now apply your mind to the same effort by which Sita's news can be found."
ramacharitamanas::4078.translation_literal: तब (then) रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) बोले (spoke) मुसुकाई (smiling) / तुम्ह (you) प्रिय (dear) मोहि (to me) भरत (Bharat) जिमि (like) भाई (brother) / अब (now) सोइ (that same) जतनु (effort) करह (do) मन (mind) लाई (applying) / जेहि (by which) बिधि (way) सीता (Sita) कै (of) सुधि (news) पाई (is found)
ramacharitamanas::4078.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4078.essence: Being dear to Ram means helping with what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::4078.simple_meaning: Ram smiles and tells Hanuman that he is as dear as Bharat, then asks him to use his full attention to find news of Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4078.simple_insight: Love becomes action when care turns into a focused search.
ramacharitamanas::4078.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has just humbled himself before Ram. Ram answers with warmth, comparing Hanuman's closeness to Bharat's, then gives him the task that matters most now: find Sita. Affection and mission meet in one moment.
ramacharitamanas::4078.modern_relevance: A friend trusts you with something precious, not because you bragged, but because you stayed steady. That quiet trust changes everything about how you show up.
ramacharitamanas::4078.insight: It links closeness with responsibility: real affection becomes careful, purposeful action.

ramacharitamanas::4079.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि होत बतकही आए बानर जूथ। नाना बरन सकल दिसि देखिअ कीस बरूथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4079.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार बातचीत हो रही थी कि वानरों के यूथ (झुंड) आ गए। अनेक रंगों के वानरों के दल सब दिशाओं में दिखाई देने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4079.english_translation: While they were talking like this, the monkey troops arrived. Monkey bands of many colors became visible in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::4079.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this manner) / होत (was happening) / बतकही (talking) / आए (came) / बानर (monkeys) / जूथ (troops) । / नाना (many) / बरन (colors/types) / सकल (all) / दिसि (directions) / देखिअ (were seen) / कीस (monkeys) / बरूथ (bands/troops) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4079.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4079.essence: The meeting gives way to a gathering army.
ramacharitamanas::4079.simple_meaning: The conversation is interrupted as monkey troops arrive from all directions in many colors.
ramacharitamanas::4079.simple_insight: Some moments are not for more discussion — they are for the arrival of help.
ramacharitamanas::4079.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just heard Ram's message and is moving to act. While the talk is still unfolding, monkey troops begin arriving from every direction. This verse simply widens the scene before the alliance gathers fully.
ramacharitamanas::4079.modern_relevance: You are still talking through the plan when the team starts arriving, each person bringing a different strength. The moment shifts from discussion to momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4079.insight: It shifts attention from the exchange itself to the gathering force around it.
