ramacharitamanas::4080.verse_sanskrit: बानर कटक उमा मैं देखा। सो मूरुख जो करन चह लेखा॥ आइ राम पद नावहिं माथा। निरखि बदनु सब होहिं सनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4080.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! वानरों की वह सेना मैंने देखी थी। उसकी जो गिनती करना चाहे वह महान् मूर्ख है। सब वानर आ-आकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाते हैं और (सौंदर्य-माधुर्यनिधि) श्रीमुख के दर्शन करके कृतार्थ होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4080.english_translation: O Uma, I saw that army of monkeys. Anyone who tries to count it is a fool. They come and bow their heads at Ram's feet, and by seeing his face they feel fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::4080.translation_literal: बानर कटक (monkey army) / उमा (Uma) / मैं (I) / देखा (saw) / सो (that) / मूरुख (fool) / जो (who) / करन चह (wants to do) / लेखा (counting) / आइ (coming) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / नावहिं (bow) / माथा (heads) / निरखि (seeing) / बदनु (face) / सब (all) / होहिं (become) / सनाथा (fulfilled / having a lord)
ramacharitamanas::4080.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4080.essence: Real greatness makes counting irrelevant and devotion natural.
ramacharitamanas::4080.simple_meaning: The monkey army is too vast to count, and every monkey comes to bow before Ram and feels complete just by seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::4080.simple_insight: Some presence is so full that even being near it feels like receiving everything.
ramacharitamanas::4080.detailed_meaning: In the Kishkindhakand, Shiva tells Uma about the gathering of Ram's monkey army. He says the force is beyond counting, but what matters more is their devotion: each one bows at Ram's feet and feels fulfilled by his sight.
ramacharitamanas::4080.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded hall and still notice one person everyone keeps turning toward. It isn't numbers that matter — it's the kind of presence that makes people bow their heads without being asked.
ramacharitamanas::4080.insight: It shifts attention from quantity and spectacle to the quiet power of reverent presence.

ramacharitamanas::4081.verse_sanskrit: अस कपि एक न सेना माहीं। राम कुसल जेहि पूछी नाहीं॥ यह कछु नहिं प्रभु कइ अधिकाई। बिस्वरूप ब्यापक रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4081.verse_hindi: सेना में एक भी वानर ऐसा नहीं था जिससे श्री रामजी ने कुशल न पूछी हो, प्रभु के लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है, क्योंकि श्री रघुनाथजी विश्वरूप तथा सर्वव्यापक हैं (सारे रूपों और सब स्थानों में हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4081.english_translation: Not a single monkey in the army had been left unasked about by Ram. This is no great feat for the Lord, because Raghunath is all-pervading and of universal form.
ramacharitamanas::4081.translation_literal: अस (such) / कपि (monkey) / एक (one) / न (not) / सेना (army) / माहीं (within) / राम (Ram) / कुसल (well-being) / जेहि (whom) / पूछी (asked) / नाहीं (not)॥ यह (this) / कछु (some) / नहिं (not) / प्रभु (Lord) / कइ (of) / अधिकाई (greatness) / बिस्वरूप (universal form) / व्यापक (all-pervading) / रघुराई (Raghunath)॥
ramacharitamanas::4081.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4081.essence: What seems impossible to others is effortless for the all-pervading Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4081.simple_meaning: Ram asked after every monkey in the army, and that is natural for him because he is present everywhere in every form.
ramacharitamanas::4081.simple_insight: You are already held in a care larger than distance or notice.
ramacharitamanas::4081.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, the monkey army gathers around Ram and Sugriva. Shiva pauses the scene to marvel that Ram greeted and asked about the well-being of every single monkey. For the all-pervading Raghunath, such universal attention is effortless.
ramacharitamanas::4081.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded family gathering and somehow the one person everyone overlooks remembers your name, your work, and the thing you were worried about. That kind of attention feels impossible — until love makes it natural.
ramacharitamanas::4081.insight: It shifts reverence from spectacle to presence: true greatness notices everyone without strain.

ramacharitamanas::4082.verse_sanskrit: ठाढ़े जहँ तहँ आयसु पाई। कह सुग्रीव सबहि समुझाई॥ राम काजु अरु मोर निहोरा। बानर जूथ जाहु चहुँ ओरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4082.verse_hindi: आज्ञा पाकर सब जहाँ-तहाँ खड़े हो गए। तब सुग्रीव ने सबको समझाकर कहा कि हे वानरों के समूहों! यह श्री रामचंद्रजी का कार्य है और मेरा निहोरा (अनुरोध) है, तुम चारों ओर जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4082.english_translation: Receiving the order, everyone stood where they were. Then Sugriva explained to all of them and said, “This is Ram’s task and my request: O troop of monkeys, go in all directions.”
ramacharitamanas::4082.translation_literal: ठाढ़े (stood) / जहँ तहँ (here and there, in every place) / आयसु (order) / पाई (having received) / कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सबहि (to all) / समुझाई (having explained) / राम (Ram) / काजु (task) / अरु (and) / मोर (my) / निहोरा (request) / बानर (monkeys) / जूथ (troops) / जाहु (go) / चहुँ ओरा (in all four directions)
ramacharitamanas::4082.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4082.essence: Clear command turns loyalty into movement.
ramacharitamanas::4082.simple_meaning: Sugriva gives the search party their assignment: this is Ram’s work, and he wants them to spread out in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::4082.simple_insight: Real help begins when everyone knows their part.
ramacharitamanas::4082.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Sugriva has just received Ram’s command to search for Sita. He turns to the monkey troops and organizes them at once, making the mission clear: this is Ram’s work, and every direction must be covered.
ramacharitamanas::4082.modern_relevance: A team gathers after the plan is finally approved. Instead of more debate, someone assigns the next steps clearly, and the whole room shifts from waiting to moving.
ramacharitamanas::4082.insight: It turns intention into coordinated action by giving each person a clear role.

ramacharitamanas::4083.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुता कहुँ खोजहु जाई। मास दिवस महँ आएहु भाई॥ अवधि मेटि जो बिनु सुधि पाएँ। आवइ बनिहि सो मोहि मराएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4083.verse_hindi: और जाकर जानकीजी को खोजो। हे भाई! महीने भर में वापस आ जाना। जो (महीने भर की) अवधि बिताकर बिना पता लगाए ही लौट आएगा उसे मेरे द्वारा मरवाते ही बनेगा (अर्थात् मुझे उसका वध करवाना ही पड़ेगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4083.english_translation: Go search for Janaka's daughter, and return within a month, brother. If you come back without finding her after the deadline, I will have you put to death.
ramacharitamanas::4083.translation_literal: जनकसुता (Janaka's daughter) / कहुँ (for) / खोजहु (search) / जाई (going) / मास (month) / दिवस (days) / महँ (within) / आएहु (come back) / भाई (brother) / अवधि (deadline) / मेटि (ending) / जो (who) / बिनु (without) / सुधि (news) / पाएँ (having found) / आवइ (returns) / बनिहि (will become) / सो (that one) / मोहि (to me) / मराएँ (for killing)
ramacharitamanas::4083.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4083.essence: Urgent duty becomes real only when time is fixed.
ramacharitamanas::4083.simple_meaning: Sugriva sends the monkeys out to search for Sita and gives them a strict time limit. He makes it clear that failure to return with news will bring punishment.
ramacharitamanas::4083.simple_insight: Serious responsibility needs clear timing, not vague intention.
ramacharitamanas::4083.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Sugriva has just allied with Ram and now orders the monkey chiefs to search for Sita in every direction. The mission is urgent, and the deadline shows how seriously he treats Ram's cause.
ramacharitamanas::4083.modern_relevance: You tell your team to find the missing file before the client call, not 'sometime today.' Clear urgency changes scattered effort into real search.
ramacharitamanas::4083.insight: It teaches you to set firm deadlines when a task matters, so effort becomes focused and accountable.

ramacharitamanas::4084.verse_sanskrit: बचन सुनत सब बानर जहँ तहँ चले तुरंत। तब सुग्रीवँ बोलाए अंगद नल हनुमंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4084.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव के वचन सुनते ही सब वानर तुरंत जहाँ-तहाँ (भिन्न-भिन्न दिशाओं में) चल दिए। तब सुग्रीव ने अंगद, नल, हनुमान् आदि प्रधान-प्रधान योद्धाओं को बुलाया (और कहा-) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4084.english_translation: As soon as they heard Sugriva's words, all the monkeys left at once in different directions. Then Sugriva called Angad, Nala, Hanuman, and the others.
ramacharitamanas::4084.translation_literal: बचन (words) / सुनत (hearing) / सब (all) / बानर (monkeys) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / चले (went) / तुरंत (at once) / तब (then) / सुग्रीवँ (Sugriva) / बोलाए (called) / अंगद (Angad) / नल (Nala) / हनुमंत (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4084.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4084.essence: Clear command turns many hands into one search.
ramacharitamanas::4084.simple_meaning: The monkeys split up immediately after Sugriva's order, and he then summoned the chief warriors.
ramacharitamanas::4084.simple_insight: Good leadership turns a crowd into a clear, coordinated response.
ramacharitamanas::4084.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Sugriva has already told the vanara army to search for Sita. This verse shows the command taking effect: the monkeys scatter, and the leaders Angad, Nala, and Hanuman are gathered for the next step.
ramacharitamanas::4084.modern_relevance: A team meeting ends, and everyone moves without confusion because the next action is clear. No drama, no delay — just clean execution.
ramacharitamanas::4084.insight: It shifts attention from intention to organised action under a trusted leader.

ramacharitamanas::4085.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु नील अंगद हनुमाना। जामवंत मतिधीर सुजाना॥ सकल सुभट मिलि दच्छिन जाहू। सीता सुधि पूँछेहु सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4085.verse_hindi: हे धीरबुद्धि और चतुर नील, अंगद, जाम्बवान् और हनुमान! तुम सब श्रेष्ठ योद्धा मिलकर दक्षिण दिशा को जाओ और सब किसी से सीताजी का पता पूछना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4085.english_translation: Listen, Neel, Angad, Hanuman, and wise Jambavan. All of you brave warriors should go south and ask everyone for news of Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4085.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / नील (Neel) / अंगद (Angad) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / मतिधीर (steady-minded) / सुजाना (wise) / सकल (all) / सुभट (brave warriors) / मिलि (together) / दच्छिन (south) / जाहू (go) / सीता (Sita) / सुधि (news) / पूँछेहु (ask) / सब (all) / काहू (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::4085.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4085.essence: Urgent service becomes effective when brave people move as one.
ramacharitamanas::4085.simple_meaning: Sugriva sends Hanuman, Angad, Neel, and Jambavan south to search for Sita and ask everyone they meet.
ramacharitamanas::4085.simple_insight: Real help begins when everyone takes a clear role and moves together.
ramacharitamanas::4085.detailed_meaning: After Sugriva promises help to Ram, the search teams fan out from Kishkindha. In this verse, he gives Hanuman, Angad, Neel, and Jambavan their assignment: go south, work together, and gather news of Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4085.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with panic after someone goes missing. One person calls, another checks the route, another asks neighbors. This verse is about coordinated effort when the situation is urgent.
ramacharitamanas::4085.insight: It teaches you to turn concern into organized action instead of scattered worry.

ramacharitamanas::4086.verse_sanskrit: मन क्रम बचन सो जतन बिचारेहु। रामचंद्र कर काजु सँवारेहु॥ भानु पीठि सेइअ उर आगी। स्वामिहि सर्ब भाव छल त्यागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4086.verse_hindi: मन, वचन तथा कर्म से उसी का (सीताजी का पता लगाने का) उपाय सोचना। श्री रामचंद्रजी का कार्य संपन्न (सफल) करना। सूर्य को पीठ से और अग्नि को हृदय से (सामने से) सेवन करना चाहिए, परंतु स्वामी की सेवा तो छल छोड़कर सर्वभाव से (मन, वचन, कर्म से) करनी चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4086.english_translation: Think of a way with mind, words, and action. Carry out Ramchandra's task. Serve the sun from behind and fire from the front, but serve your master with all your being, without deceit.
ramacharitamanas::4086.translation_literal: मन (mind) / क्रम (order, sequence) / बचन (words) / सो (that) / जतन (effort, method) / बिचारेहु (consider) / रामचंद्र (Ramchandra) / कर (of) / काजु (task) / सँवारेहु (make successful) / भानु (sun) / पीठि (back) / सेइअ (serve) / उर (heart) / आगी (front, in front) / स्वामिहि (master) / सर्ब (all) / भाव (feeling, manner) / छल (deceit) / त्यागी (abandoning)
ramacharitamanas::4086.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4086.essence: True service gives Ram your whole mind, not just your hands.
ramacharitamanas::4086.simple_meaning: Use your whole mind, speech, and action for the work in front of you. Serve your master sincerely, without trickery or divided loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::4086.simple_insight: Real service is complete: no hidden agenda, no split attention, no performance.
ramacharitamanas::4086.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Sugriva is sending Hanuman and the others south to search for Sita. He tells them to plan carefully, carry out Ram's work, and serve with total sincerity. The mission is not just travel — it is loyal action without deceit.
ramacharitamanas::4086.modern_relevance: You agree to help a friend move, but you keep checking your phone and hoping the day ends quickly. This verse calls you back to full presence: do the task cleanly, without hidden resistance.
ramacharitamanas::4086.insight: It shifts service from reluctant compliance to wholehearted commitment.

ramacharitamanas::4087.verse_sanskrit: तजि माया सेइअ परलोका। मिटहिं सकल भवसंभव सोका॥ देह धरे कर यह फलु भाई। भजिअ राम सब काम बिहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4087.verse_hindi: माया (विषयों की ममता-आसक्ति) को छोड़कर परलोक का सेवन (भगवान के दिव्य धाम की प्राप्ति के लिए भगवत्सेवा रूप साधन) करना चाहिए, जिससे भव (जन्म-मरण) से उत्पन्न सारे शोक मिट जाएँ। हे भाई! देह धारण करने का यही फल है कि सब कामों (कामनाओं) को छोड़कर श्री रामजी का भजन ही किया जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4087.english_translation: Give up illusion and serve the higher realm. Then all sorrow born from becoming and becoming again is erased. O brother, the true fruit of having a body is to छोड़ all desires and worship Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4087.translation_literal: तजि (giving up) / माया (illusion) / सेइअ (serve) / परलोका (the higher realm) / मिटहिं (are erased) / सकल (all) / भवसंभव (born from becoming and becoming again) / सोका (sorrows) / देह (body) / धरे (having taken) / कर (of) / यह (this) / फलु (fruit) / भाई (brother) / भजिअ (worship) / राम (Ram) / सब (all) / काम (desires) / बिहाई (leaving behind)
ramacharitamanas::4087.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4087.essence: Letting go of craving reveals the real purpose of being alive.
ramacharitamanas::4087.simple_meaning: Let go of attachment to worldly illusion and devote yourself to Ram. That is how sorrow ends and life becomes meaningful.
ramacharitamanas::4087.simple_insight: You don't have to be ruled by wanting; devotion can make life feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::4087.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the monkey heroes are being sent to search for Sita. Tulsidas pauses the action to state the deeper rule behind their mission: worldly attachment breeds sorrow, and a human birth is fulfilled only by turning toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4087.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping one more message will settle your mind. It doesn't. The ache eases when you stop feeding craving and give your attention to what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::4087.insight: It shifts attention from chasing wants to anchoring life in devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4088.verse_sanskrit: सोइ गुनग्य सोई बड़भागी। जो रघुबीर चरन अनुरागी॥ आयसु मागि चरन सिरु नाई। चले हरषि सुमिरत रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4088.verse_hindi: सद्गुणों को पहचानने वाला (गुणवान) तथा बड़भागी वही है जो श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों का प्रेमी है। आज्ञा माँगकर और चरणों में फिर सिर नवाकर श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करते हुए सब हर्षित होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4088.english_translation: Only the one who loves Raghubir's feet is truly wise and truly fortunate. They asked for permission, bowed their heads to his feet, and departed joyfully, remembering Raghu's lord.
ramacharitamanas::4088.translation_literal: सोइ (that alone) / गुनग्य (knower of virtues) / सोई (that alone) / बड़भागी (most fortunate) / जो (who) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागी (loving-attached) ॥ / आयसु (permission) / मागि (having asked) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / चले (they went) / हरषि (joyfully) / सुमिरत (remembering) / रघुराई (lord of Raghu) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4088.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4088.essence: Loving Ram matters more than being clever or fortunate.
ramacharitamanas::4088.simple_meaning: Real wisdom and real good fortune belong to the person who loves Ram deeply. With his permission, they bowed, remembered him, and went away happily.
ramacharitamanas::4088.simple_insight: Love for Ram changes how you leave, how you act, and how you feel.
ramacharitamanas::4088.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the mission has been set in motion. The companions ask Ram's leave, bow at his feet, and move off with joy. Tulsidas pauses to say that true wisdom and fortune belong to the one whose heart is attached to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4088.modern_relevance: You leave a difficult meeting, not with a victory speech, but with quiet relief because you stayed honest. What makes the moment meaningful is not applause — it's that your heart stayed aligned.
ramacharitamanas::4088.insight: It shifts value from status or cleverness to loving alignment with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4089.verse_sanskrit: पाछें पवन तनय सिरु नावा। जानि काज प्रभु निकट बोलावा॥ परसा सीस सरोरुह पानी। करमुद्रिका दीन्हि जन जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4089.verse_hindi: सबके पीछे पवनसुत श्री हनुमान् जी ने सिर नवाया। कार्य का विचार करके प्रभु ने उन्हें अपने पास बुलाया। उन्होंने अपने करकमल से उनके सिर का स्पर्श किया तथा अपना सेवक जानकर उन्हें अपने हाथ की अँगूठी उतारकर दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4089.english_translation: Hanuman bowed his head from behind. Knowing the purpose, the Lord called him near. He touched Hanuman's head like a lotus with his hand and gave him his ring, recognizing him as a servant.
ramacharitamanas::4089.translation_literal: पाछें (from behind) / पवन-तनय (son of the wind, Hanuman) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / जानि (knowing) / काज (purpose, task) / प्रभु (the Lord) / निकट (near) / बोलावा (called) / परसा (touched) / सीस (head) / सरोरुह (lotus) / पानी (hand) / करमुद्रिका (ring) / दीन्हि (gave) / जन (servant) / जानी (knowing, recognizing)
ramacharitamanas::4089.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4089.essence: Quiet service is what brings you closest.
ramacharitamanas::4089.simple_meaning: Hanuman bows before Ram, and Ram calls him close, touches his head, and gives him a ring as a sign of trust and service.
ramacharitamanas::4089.simple_insight: True devotion is noticed. Quiet service can become the very reason you are called near.
ramacharitamanas::4089.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has arrived before Ram after the alliance with Sugriva begins to take shape. He bows from behind, and Ram immediately sees his usefulness and his devotion. The ring becomes a token for the mission ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4089.modern_relevance: You stay late to help without making noise, and the right person notices. A quiet act of service can open the next door.
ramacharitamanas::4089.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to faithful readiness. Service, not status, becomes the mark of closeness.

ramacharitamanas::4090.verse_sanskrit: बहु प्रकार सीतहि समुझाएहु। कहि बल बिरह बेगि तुम्ह आएहु॥ हनुमत जन्म सुफल करि माना। चलेउ हृदयँ धरि कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4090.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) बहुत प्रकार से सीता को समझाना और मेरा बल तथा विरह (प्रेम) कहकर तुम शीघ्र लौट आना। हनुमान् जी ने अपना जन्म सफल समझा और कृपानिधान प्रभु को हृदय में धारण करके वे चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4090.english_translation: “Tell Sita many things for me. Tell her of my strength and my longing, and come back quickly.” Hanuman considered his birth fulfilled and departed, holding the merciful Lord in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4090.translation_literal: बहु प्रकार (in many ways) / सीतहि (to Sita) / समुझाएहु (explain) / कहि (saying) / बल (strength) / बिरह (separation-longing) / बेगि (quickly) / तुम्ह (you) / आएहु (come) / हनुमत (Hanuman) / जन्म (birth) / सुफल (fruitful) / करि (having made) / माना (considered) / चलेउ (departed) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धरि (holding) / कृपानिधाना (the merciful one)
ramacharitamanas::4090.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4090.essence: A life becomes fruitful when it is spent carrying love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4090.simple_meaning: Ram asks Hanuman to reassure Sita and return quickly. Hanuman feels his life has succeeded because he has served Ram and carries Ram in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4090.simple_insight: Service becomes fulfillment when love, not ego, is at the center.
ramacharitamanas::4090.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally reached Ram's beloved Sita. Ram tells him to comfort her with news of his strength and longing, then return quickly. Hanuman receives the command as the completion of his life and leaves with Ram held close in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4090.modern_relevance: You finally get the message that someone you love has been waiting for. The errand is simple, but it feels sacred because it lets you carry care across distance.
ramacharitamanas::4090.insight: It shifts service from a task to a sacred fulfillment of relationship.

ramacharitamanas::4091.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि प्रभु जानत सब बाता। राजनीति राखत सुरत्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4091.verse_hindi: यद्यपि देवताओं की रक्षा करने वाले प्रभु सब बात जानते हैं, तो भी वे राजनीति की रक्षा कर रहे हैं (नीति की मर्यादा रखने के लिए सीताजी का पता लगाने को जहाँ-तहाँ वानरों को भेज रहे हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4091.english_translation: Although the Lord who protects the radiant beings knows everything, he still upholds righteous conduct.
ramacharitamanas::4091.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / प्रभु (the Lord) / जानत (knows) / सब (all) / बाता (things) / राजनीति (righteous conduct) / राखत (upholding) / सुरत्राता (protector of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::4091.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4091.essence: Even perfect knowledge still respects the right way to act.
ramacharitamanas::4091.simple_meaning: Ram already knows where Sita is, but he still sends the monkeys out to search so the search follows proper conduct and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::4091.simple_insight: Knowing the answer does not cancel the need to walk the proper path.
ramacharitamanas::4091.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just been sent forward in the search for Sita. Even though Ram already knows all things, he does not skip the outward effort. He keeps the search moving through proper conduct, so the mission stays honorable.
ramacharitamanas::4091.modern_relevance: You already know the shortcut would work, but you still choose the honest process: the interview, the apology, the careful check, the extra step that keeps your actions clean.
ramacharitamanas::4091.insight: It shifts you from chasing efficiency alone to respecting the integrity of the process.

ramacharitamanas::4092.verse_sanskrit: चले सकल बन खोजत सरिता सर गिरि खोह। राम काज लयलीन मन बिसरा तन कर छोह ॥
ramacharitamanas::4092.verse_hindi: सब वानर वन, नदी, तालाब, पर्वत और पर्वतों की कन्दराओं में खोजते हुए चले जा रहे हैं। मन श्री रामजी के कार्य में लवलीन है। शरीर तक का प्रेम (ममत्व) भूल गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4092.english_translation: The monkey band moved through forests, rivers, lakes, mountains, and caves in search. Their minds were absorbed in Ram's work, and even attachment to the body was forgotten.
ramacharitamanas::4092.translation_literal: चले (moved/went) / सकल (all) / बन (forest) / खोजत (searching) / सरिता (rivers) / सर (lakes) / गिरि (mountains) / खोह (caves) / राम (Ram) / काज (work) / लयलीन (fully absorbed) / मन (mind) / बिसरा (forgot) / तन (body) / कर (of) / छोह (attachment)
ramacharitamanas::4092.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4092.essence: When Ram's work fills the mind, personal comfort disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4092.simple_meaning: The monkey army keeps searching everywhere, completely absorbed in Ram's mission. They are so focused that they forget even bodily comfort and attachment.
ramacharitamanas::4092.simple_insight: Total service can quiet self-consciousness so deeply that even comfort stops mattering.
ramacharitamanas::4092.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman's allies are now fully committed to Ram's search. They fan out through forests, rivers, lakes, mountains, and caves. The verse shows how Ram's task has taken over their minds, erasing personal comfort and concern.
ramacharitamanas::4092.modern_relevance: A team stays late combing through messages, documents, and files because someone needs an answer tonight. Nobody is thinking about sleep, snacks, or credit anymore.
ramacharitamanas::4092.insight: It shows how wholehearted service can dissolve self-importance and make effort fearless.

ramacharitamanas::4093.verse_sanskrit: कतहुँ होइ निसिचर सैं भेटा। प्रान लेहिं एक एक चपेटा॥ बहु प्रकार गिरि कानन हेरहिं। कोउ मुनि मिलइ ताहि सब घेरहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4093.verse_hindi: कहीं किसी राक्षस से भेंट हो जाती है, तो एक-एक चपत में ही उसके प्राण ले लेते हैं। पर्वतों और वनों को बहुत प्रकार से खोज रहे हैं। कोई मुनि मिल जाता है तो पता पूछने के लिए उसे सब घेर लेते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4093.english_translation: Sometimes they ran into a demon, and killed him with a single slap. They searched mountains and forests in many ways. If they met a sage, they surrounded him all at once to ask for directions.
ramacharitamanas::4093.translation_literal: कतहुँ (somewhere) / होइ (happening) / निसिचर (demon) / सैं (with) / भेटा (encounter) / प्रान (life) / लेहिं (take) / एक एक (one by one) / चपेटा (slap) ॥ / बहु प्रकार (many kinds) / गिरि (mountains) / कानन (forests) / हेरहिं (search) / कोउ (some) / मुनि (sage) / मिलइ (meets) / ताहि (him) / सब (all) / घेरहिं (surround) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4093.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4093.essence: The search continues through danger, question, and motion.
ramacharitamanas::4093.simple_meaning: The search party moves through forests and mountains, defeating hostile beings on the way and surrounding any sage they meet to ask for directions.
ramacharitamanas::4093.simple_insight: Sometimes progress is just relentless searching, one obstacle and one question at a time.
ramacharitamanas::4093.detailed_meaning: Hanuman and the monkey search party are deep in Kishkindhakand, combing mountains and forests for Sita. They destroy any hostile being they meet, and if they find a sage, they crowd around him for guidance. The verse keeps the search moving forward.
ramacharitamanas::4093.modern_relevance: You are lost in a new city, checking lane after lane, asking strangers, and getting nowhere fast. The only option is to keep moving and keep asking.
ramacharitamanas::4093.insight: It shows steady, practical searching under pressure, with no pause for comfort or hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::4094.verse_sanskrit: लागि तृषा अतिसय अकुलाने। मिलइ न जल घन गहन भुलाने॥ मन हनुमान् कीन्ह अनुमाना। मरन चहत सब बिनु जल पाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4094.verse_hindi: इतने में ही सबको अत्यंत प्यास लगी, जिससे सब अत्यंत ही व्याकुल हो गए, किंतु जल कहीं नहीं मिला। घने जंगल में सब भुला गए। हनुमान् जी ने मन में अनुमान किया कि जल पिए बिना सब लोग मरना ही चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4094.english_translation: Everyone became terribly thirsty and restless, but no water could be found. Lost in the deep forest, they forgot the way. Hanuman understood in his mind that they seemed ready to die without water.
ramacharitamanas::4094.translation_literal: लागि (struck by) / तृषा (thirst) / अतिसय (extreme) / अकुलाने (became restless) / मिलइ (is found) / न (not) / जल (water) / घन (dense) / गहन (deep) / भुलाने (forgotten / lost) / मन (in the mind) / हनुमान् (Hanuman) / कीन्ह (made) / अनुमाना (an inference) / मरन (to die) / चहत (seem to want) / सब (all) / बिनु (without) / जल (water) / पाना (getting / obtaining)
ramacharitamanas::4094.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4094.essence: Clear seeing begins when you notice exhaustion before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4094.simple_meaning: The search has gone on so long that everyone is thirsty, lost, and close to collapse. Hanuman notices their condition and quietly understands the danger.
ramacharitamanas::4094.simple_insight: Sometimes the first rescue is simply seeing the crisis clearly before it gets worse.
ramacharitamanas::4094.detailed_meaning: The monkey army has been searching the forest for days in service of Ram. Hunger, thirst, and confusion are now pressing on them. Hanuman watches their condition and realizes they cannot go much farther without water, setting up the next discovery.
ramacharitamanas::4094.modern_relevance: You keep walking through a long, hot afternoon with no bottle, no shade, and no clear direction. Before panic starts, someone has to notice what exhaustion is doing.
ramacharitamanas::4094.insight: It trains attention to read the real condition of a group before the situation turns desperate.

ramacharitamanas::4095.verse_sanskrit: चढ़ि गिरि सिखर चहूँ दिसि देखा। भूमि बिबर एक कौतुक पेखा॥ चक्रबाक बक हंस उड़ाहीं। बहुतक खग प्रबिसहिं तेहि माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4095.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पहाड़ की चोटी पर चढ़कर चारों ओर देखा तो पृथ्वी के अंदर एक गुफा में उन्हें एक कौतुक (आश्चर्य) दिखाई दिया। उसके ऊपर चकवे, बगुले और हंस उड़ रहे हैं और बहुत से पक्षी उसमें प्रवेश कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4095.english_translation: They climbed the mountain peak and looked in all four directions. They saw a curious cave in the earth. Cranes, herons, and swans flew above it, and many birds entered it.
ramacharitamanas::4095.translation_literal: चढ़ि (having climbed) / गिरि (mountain) / सिखर (peak) / चहूँ दिसि (in all four directions) / देखा (saw) / भूमि (earth) / बिबर (cave) / एक (one) / कौतुक (wonder) / पेखा (saw) / चक्रबाक (cranes) / बक (herons) / हंस (swans) / उड़ाहीं (fly) / बहुतक (many) / खग (birds) / प्रबिसहिं (enter) / तेहि (that) / माहीं (into)
ramacharitamanas::4095.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4095.essence: A higher view reveals the hidden opening.
ramacharitamanas::4095.simple_meaning: From the mountain top, they spot a strange cave filled with birds flying in and out.
ramacharitamanas::4095.simple_insight: Sometimes the path forward is hidden inside what first looks ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::4095.detailed_meaning: Hanuman and the search party have reached a mountain and are still looking for water and clues. From the peak, they notice a strange cave where birds gather, hinting that something important lies inside. The verse sets up the discovery that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4095.modern_relevance: You climb to the top of a parking garage to get signal and notice a hidden stairwell you had missed below. A clue appears only after you change your vantage point.
ramacharitamanas::4095.insight: It trains attention to notice unusual openings that a hurried mind would overlook.

ramacharitamanas::4096.verse_sanskrit: गिरि ते उतरि पवनसुत आवा। सब कहुँ लै सोइ बिबर देखावा॥ आगें कै हनुमंतहि लीन्हा। पैठे बिबर बिलंबु न कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4096.verse_hindi: पवन कुमार हनुमान् जी पर्वत से उतर आए और सबको ले जाकर उन्होंने वह गुफा दिखलाई। सबने हनुमान् जी को आगे कर लिया और वे गुफा में घुस गए, देर नहीं की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4096.english_translation: Hanuman came down from the mountain and showed everyone the cave. They placed Hanuman in front and entered the cave without delay.
ramacharitamanas::4096.translation_literal: गिरि (mountain) / ते (from) / उतरि (coming down) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / आवा (came) / सब कहुँ (to everyone) / लै (taking) / सोइ (that same) / बिबर (cave) / देखावा (showed) / आगें (in front) / कै (making) / हनुमंतहि (Hanuman) / लीन्हा (took) / पैठे (entered) / बिबर (cave) / बिलंबु (delay) / न (not) / कीन्हा (did)
ramacharitamanas::4096.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4096.essence: The one who sees clearly also leads the way.
ramacharitamanas::4096.simple_meaning: Hanuman leads the others to the cave, and they enter quickly without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4096.simple_insight: Sometimes trust means letting the most capable person go first.
ramacharitamanas::4096.detailed_meaning: The thirsty group has found a strange opening in the mountain. Hanuman comes down, shows them the cave, and takes the lead. This verse simply moves the scene forward toward the hidden garden inside.
ramacharitamanas::4096.modern_relevance: You spot a narrow stairwell behind a locked door, and the person who noticed it first goes ahead. The group follows because confidence is contagious.
ramacharitamanas::4096.insight: It shifts attention from the discovery itself to the trust that lets the group move together.

ramacharitamanas::4097.verse_sanskrit: दीख जाइ उपबन बर सर बिगसित बहु कंज। मंदिर एक रुचिर तहँ बैठि नारि तप पुंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4097.verse_hindi: अंदर जाकर उन्होंने एक उत्तम उपवन (बगीचा) और तालाब देखा, जिसमें बहुत से कमल खिले हुए हैं। वहीं एक सुंदर मंदिर है, जिसमें एक तपोमूर्ति स्त्री बैठी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4097.english_translation: Entering inside, they saw a beautiful garden and a lake with many blooming lotuses. There stood a lovely hermitage, where a woman of great austerity sat.
ramacharitamanas::4097.translation_literal: दीख (was seen) / जाइ (upon going) / उपबन (garden) / बर (excellent) / सर (lake) / बिगसित (blooming) / बहु (many) / कंज (lotuses) / मंदिर (hermitage/temple) / एक (one) / रुचिर (beautiful) / तहँ (there) / बैठि (sitting) / नारि (woman) / तप पुंज (mass of austerity)
ramacharitamanas::4097.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4097.essence: The search leads them to a hidden presence of purity and patience.
ramacharitamanas::4097.simple_meaning: They go inside and find a beautiful garden, a lotus-filled lake, and a woman absorbed in austerity.
ramacharitamanas::4097.simple_insight: Sometimes the search ends in a quiet, unexpected sight.
ramacharitamanas::4097.detailed_meaning: Hanuman and the others have entered the hidden cave area in Kishkindha. After the strange discovery outside, they now see a lovely garden, a lake full of lotuses, and a woman sitting like embodied austerity. The verse simply sets up Sita's discovery.
ramacharitamanas::4097.modern_relevance: You follow a lead into a place you barely understand and suddenly find the clue you were hoping for. The moment is still, clear, and charged with meaning.
ramacharitamanas::4097.insight: It shifts attention from movement and searching to the quiet revelation waiting inside the unknown.

ramacharitamanas::4098.verse_sanskrit: दूरि ते ताहि सबन्हि सिरु नावा। पूछें निज बृत्तांत सुनावा॥ तेहिं तब कहा करहु जल पाना। खाहु सुरस सुंदर फल नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4098.verse_hindi: दूर से ही सबने उसे सिर नवाया और पूछने पर अपना सब वृत्तांत कह सुनाया। तब उसने कहा- जलपान करो और भाँति-भाँति के रसीले सुंदर फल खाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4098.english_translation: From afar, everyone bowed their heads to him and, when asked, told their whole story. Then he said, "Drink water and eat the many sweet, beautiful fruits."
ramacharitamanas::4098.translation_literal: दूरि ते (from afar) / ताहि (to him) / सबन्हि (all) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bent) / पूछें (having asked) / निज (their own) / बृत्तांत (account/story) / सुनावा (told) / तेहिं (then he) / तब (then) / कहा (said) / करहु (do) / जल पाना (water-drinking) / खाहु (eat) / सुरस (sweet) / सुंदर (beautiful) / फल (fruits) / नाना (many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::4098.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4098.essence: Respect and hospitality open the door before words do.
ramacharitamanas::4098.simple_meaning: They greet him respectfully, tell him their story, and he welcomes them with food and drink.
ramacharitamanas::4098.simple_insight: A kind welcome can turn strangers into companions.
ramacharitamanas::4098.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has led the search party into the hidden place. The group meets the woman there, bows to her from a distance, and explains who they are. She responds not with fear, but with hospitality, giving them water and fruit before the deeper conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::4098.modern_relevance: You walk into a house where nobody knows you yet, and the first thing offered is water and food. Before any explanation, simple kindness changes the whole mood.
ramacharitamanas::4098.insight: It shows how care begins with welcoming the other person before asking anything more.

ramacharitamanas::4099.verse_sanskrit: मज्जनु कीन्ह मधुर फल खाए। तासु निकट पुनि सब चलि आए॥ तेहिं सब आपनि कथा सुनाई। मैं अब जाब जहाँ रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4099.verse_hindi: (आज्ञा पाकर) सबने स्नान किया, मीठे फल खाए और फिर सब उसके पास चले आए। तब उसने अपनी सब कथा कह सुनाई (और कहा-) मैं अब वहाँ जाऊँगी जहाँ श्री रघुनाथजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4099.english_translation: After bathing and eating sweet fruit, they all came back to him. Then he told them his story and said, “I will now go where Raghunath is.”
ramacharitamanas::4099.translation_literal: मज्जनु (bathing) / कीन्ह (did) / मधुर (sweet) / फल (fruit) / खाए (ate) / तासु (his) / निकट (near) / पुनि (again) / सब (all) / चलि आए (came) / तेहिं (he) / सब (all) / आपनि (his own) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / मैं (I) / अब (now) / जाब (will go) / जहाँ (where) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::4099.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4099.essence: Rest is not the end; devotion keeps walking toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4099.simple_meaning: After the meal, the group gathers again, listens to the story, and the speaker chooses to go where Ram is.
ramacharitamanas::4099.simple_insight: Even after relief and rest, the deepest pull remains: moving toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4099.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the monkeys have been welcomed, fed, and refreshed in the grove. Once they return, one of them tells the story of his life and declares that his real destination is with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4099.modern_relevance: You finally sit down after a long day, eat something warm, and the noise in your head softens. But one quiet thought remains: where is the place, or person, your heart is actually moving toward?
ramacharitamanas::4099.insight: It shifts attention from temporary comfort to the deeper direction your life is taking.

ramacharitamanas::4100.verse_sanskrit: मूदहु नयन बिबर तजि जाहू। पैहहु सीतहि जनि पछिताहू॥ नयन मूदि पुनि देखहिं बीरा। ठाढ़े सकल सिंधु कें तीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4100.verse_hindi: तुम लोग आँखें मूँद लो और गुफा को छोड़कर बाहर जाओ। तुम सीताजी को पा जाओगे, पछताओ नहीं (निराश न होओ)। आँखें मूँदकर फिर जब आँखें खोलीं तो सब वीर क्या देखते हैं कि सब समुद्र के तीर पर खड़े हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4100.english_translation: Close your eyes and leave the cave. You will find Sita; do not regret it. When the warriors shut their eyes and open them again, they are standing on the seashore.
ramacharitamanas::4100.translation_literal: मूदहु (close) / नयन (eyes) / बिबर (cave) / तजि (leaving) / जाहू (go) / पैहहु (you will find) / सीतहि (Sita) / जनि (do not) / पछिताहू (regret) / नयन (eyes) / मूदि (closing) / पुनि (again) / देखहिं (they see) / बीरा (warriors) / ठाढ़े (standing) / सकल (all) / सिंधु (sea) / कें (at) / तीरा (shore)
ramacharitamanas::4100.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4100.essence: Trust can carry you where sight alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4100.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells the search party to trust him and leave the cave. When they obey, they find themselves at the seashore, close to Sita's trail.
ramacharitamanas::4100.simple_insight: Faith can move you through confusion faster than doubt can map it.
ramacharitamanas::4100.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has led the search party to a hidden passage. He tells the warriors to close their eyes and follow him without fear. They obey, and when they open their eyes, they are on the shore, one step closer to Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4100.modern_relevance: You are stuck in a problem so long that your own thinking starts to feel like the only map. Then someone who sees more clearly says, 'Follow me,' and the next step appears before you can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::4100.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious overthinking to obedient trust in a clearer guide.

ramacharitamanas::4101.verse_sanskrit: सो पुनि गई जहाँ रघुनाथा। जाइ कमल पद नाएसि माथा॥ नाना भाँति बिनय तेहिं कीन्हीं। अनपायनी भगति प्रभु दीन्हीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4101.verse_hindi: और वह स्वयं वहाँ गई जहाँ श्री रघुनाथजी थे। उसने जाकर प्रभु के चरण कमलों में मस्तक नवाया और बहुत प्रकार से विनती की। प्रभु ने उसे अपनी अनपायिनी (अचल) भक्ति दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4101.english_translation: She went there where Raghunath was. She bowed her head at his lotus feet and prayed in many ways; the Lord granted her unwavering devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4101.translation_literal: सो (she) / पुनि (again) / गई (went) / जहाँ (where) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / जाइ (going) / कमल (lotus) / पद (feet) / नाएसि (bowed) / माथा (head) / नाना (many) / भाँति (ways) / बिनय (prayer) / तेहिं (she) / कीन्हीं (did) / अनपायनी (unwavering) / भगति (devotion) / प्रभु (Lord) / दीन्हीं (gave)
ramacharitamanas::4101.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4101.essence: True humility opens the door to lasting devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4101.simple_meaning: She goes to Ram, bows at his feet, and prays sincerely. In response, Ram gives her steady devotion that does not break.
ramacharitamanas::4101.simple_insight: Reverence is not empty gesture; it can become the doorway to a love that stays.
ramacharitamanas::4101.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the alliance is taking shape and trust is being tested. She comes to Raghunath, bows low, and pleads from the heart. Ram answers not with words alone but by giving her unshakable devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4101.modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room and admit what you need instead of performing strength. That honest bow can change the whole relationship.
ramacharitamanas::4101.insight: It shifts the reader from self-protection to sincere surrender, showing that humility can receive what pride cannot.

ramacharitamanas::4102.verse_sanskrit: बदरीबन कहुँ सो गई प्रभु अग्या धरि सीस। उर धरि राम चरन जुग जे बंदत अज ईस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4102.verse_hindi: प्रभु की आज्ञा सिर पर धारण कर और श्री रामजी के युगल चरणों को, जिनकी ब्रह्मा और महेश भी वंदना करते हैं, हृदय में धारण कर वह (स्वयंप्रभा) बदरिकाश्रम को चली गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4102.english_translation: Taking the Lord's command upon her head, and holding in her heart Ram's twin feet, which even Brahma and Shiva worship, she went to Badarivan.
ramacharitamanas::4102.translation_literal: बदरीबन (to Badarivan) / कहुँ (toward) / सो (she) / गई (went) / प्रभु (Lord's) / अग्या (command) / धरि (placing) / सीस (head) / उर (heart) / धरि (placing) / राम (Ram's) / चरन (feet) / जुग (pair) / जे (which) / बंदत (worship) / अज (Brahma) / ईस (Shiva) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4102.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4102.essence: True devotion obeys outwardly while staying inwardly with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4102.simple_meaning: She leaves by accepting Ram's command completely and keeping his feet in her heart. Obedience and devotion move together.
ramacharitamanas::4102.simple_insight: There is peace in letting guidance lead while love stays alive inside you.
ramacharitamanas::4102.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the search for Sita is still unresolved. Selfprabha receives Ram's command, places it above her own will, and walks to Badarivan with Ram's feet in her heart. The verse shows obedient devotion in motion.
ramacharitamanas::4102.modern_relevance: You get a hard message from someone you trust, and you don't argue with it for three hours. You absorb it, keep your heart steady, and do what needs doing.
ramacharitamanas::4102.insight: It teaches you to let duty and devotion work together, instead of treating obedience as cold and love as vague.

ramacharitamanas::4103.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ बिचारहिं कपि मन माहीं। बीती अवधि काज कछु नाहीं॥ सब मिलि कहहिं परस्पर बाता। बिनु सुधि लएँ करब का भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4103.verse_hindi: यहाँ वानरगण मन में विचार कर रहे हैं कि अवधि तो बीत गई, पर काम कुछ न हुआ। सब मिलकर आपस में बात करने लगे कि हे भाई! अब तो सीताजी की खबर लिए बिना लौटकर भी क्या करेंगे! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4103.english_translation: The monkeys were thinking in their hearts: the time limit had passed, and nothing had been done. They all spoke among themselves: Brother, what use is it to return without news of Sita?
ramacharitamanas::4103.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / बिचारहिं (they are thinking) / कपि (monkeys) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / बीती (passed) / अवधि (time limit) / काज (work) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (not)॥ सब (all) / मिलि (together) / कहहिं (they say) / परस्पर (to one another) / बाता (words, talk) / बिनु (without) / सुधि (news) / लएँ (taking) / करब (to do) / का (what) / भ्राता (brother)॥
ramacharitamanas::4103.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4103.essence: Without the one answer that matters, even returning feels empty.
ramacharitamanas::4103.simple_meaning: The search has run out of time, and the monkeys have still found no news of Sita. They wonder what returning would even mean without that news.
ramacharitamanas::4103.simple_insight: Some efforts feel unfinished until the one thing that matters is found.
ramacharitamanas::4103.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman's search party has spent its allotted time and still has no trace of Sita. The monkeys gather in worry and ask each other whether going back empty-handed would mean anything at all.
ramacharitamanas::4103.modern_relevance: You’ve spent the whole day chasing leads, and the one message that matters still hasn’t come. At some point, the question becomes: what is returning without resolution?
ramacharitamanas::4103.insight: It shifts attention from completing the trip to confronting the real unmet need.

ramacharitamanas::4104.verse_sanskrit: कह अंगद लोचन भरि बारी। दुहुँ प्रकार भइ मृत्यु हमारी॥ इहाँ न सुधि सीता कै पाई। उहाँ गएँ मारिहि कपिराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4104.verse_hindi: अंगद ने नेत्रों में जल भरकर कहा कि दोनों ही प्रकार से हमारी मृत्यु हुई। यहाँ तो सीताजी की सुध नहीं मिली और वहाँ जाने पर वानरराज सुग्रीव मार डालेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4104.english_translation: Angad, eyes full of tears, said, 'We have died in both ways. Here we have found no news of Sita, and if we return there, Sugriva will kill us.'
ramacharitamanas::4104.translation_literal: कह (said) / अंगद (Angad) / लोचन (eyes) / भरि (filling) / बारी (water, tears) / दुहुँ (both) / प्रकार (ways) / भइ (became) / मृत्यु (death) / हमारी (our) / इहाँ (here) / न (not) / सुधि (news, trace) / सीता (Sita) / कै (of) / पाई (found) / उहाँ (there) / गएँ (going) / मारिहि (will kill) / कपिराई (the monkey king)
ramacharitamanas::4104.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4104.essence: When the mission fails, even returning home can feel dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::4104.simple_meaning: Angad says the search has failed in every direction: they found no news of Sita, and returning home feels deadly too.
ramacharitamanas::4104.simple_insight: Sometimes failure feels trapped on both sides, with no safe way forward.
ramacharitamanas::4104.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's search has reached a painful dead end. Angad looks at the others with tears in his eyes and says they have failed to find Sita, yet going back empty-handed may bring death from Sugriva. The whole mission feels cornered.
ramacharitamanas::4104.modern_relevance: You miss the deadline, and the client is angry either way: stay and keep fixing it, or send it in and risk blame. Angad knows that trapped feeling.
ramacharitamanas::4104.insight: It captures the pressure of a mission where every option seems costly and no outcome feels safe.

ramacharitamanas::4105.verse_sanskrit: पिता बधे पर मारत मोही। राखा राम निहोर न ओही॥ पुनि पुनि अंगद कह सब पाहीं। मरन भयउ कछु संसय नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4105.verse_hindi: वे तो पिता के वध होने पर ही मुझे मार डालते। श्री रामजी ने ही मेरी रक्षा की, इसमें सुग्रीव का कोई एहसान नहीं है। अंगद बार-बार सबसे कह रहे हैं कि अब मरण हुआ, इसमें कुछ भी संदेह नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4105.english_translation: They would have killed me when my father was slain. Ram protected me, not Sugriva. Angad keeps telling everyone again and again: death has come, and there is no doubt about it.
ramacharitamanas::4105.translation_literal: पिता (father) / बधे (when killed) / पर (then) / मारत (killing) / मोही (me) / राखा (protected) / राम (Ram) / निहोर (by favor) / न ओही (not that one)॥ पुनि (again) / पुनि (again) / अंगद (Angad) / कह (says) / सब (to all) / पाहीं (near) / मरन (death) / भयउ (has happened) / कछु (any) / संसय (doubt) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::4105.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4105.simple_meaning: Angad says he would have died already if Ram had not protected him. He tells the others that death is certain and there is no doubt left.
ramacharitamanas::4105.simple_insight: When fear strips away pride, you see who truly kept you alive.
ramacharitamanas::4105.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the monkey leaders have failed to find Sita and are sinking into despair. Angad speaks with raw finality: without Ram's protection, he would already be dead. His words deepen the group's grief and certainty that their mission has reached a breaking point.
ramacharitamanas::4105.modern_relevance: You look back on a crisis and realise you did not make it through on your own. Someone's protection, timing, or grace carried you farther than pride wants to admit.
ramacharitamanas::4105.insight: It shifts attention from self-credit to the unseen support that made survival possible.

ramacharitamanas::4106.verse_sanskrit: अंगद बचन सुन कपि बीरा। बोलि न सकहिं नयन बह नीरा॥ छन एक सोच मगन होइ रहे। पुनि अस बचन कहत सब भए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4106.verse_hindi: वानर वीर अंगद के वचन सुनते हैं, किंतु कुछ बोल नहीं सकते। उनके नेत्रों से जल बह रहा है। एक क्षण के लिए सब सोच में मग्न हो रहे। फिर सब ऐसा वचन कहने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4106.english_translation: Hearing Angad's words, the monkey warriors could not speak; tears flowed from their eyes. For a moment they sat lost in thought, and then all began to speak thus.
ramacharitamanas::4106.translation_literal: अंगद (Angad) / बचन (words) / सुन (hearing) / कपि बीरा (monkey warriors) / बोलि (speaking) / न सकहिं (could not) / नयन (eyes) / बह (flowing) / नीरा (water/tears) / छन (moment) / एक (one) / सोच (thought) / मगन (immersed) / होइ (having become) / रहे (remained) / पुनि (then) / अस (such) / बचन (words) / कहत (speaking) / सब (all) / भए (became)
ramacharitamanas::4106.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4106.essence: Pain can silence a crowd before it turns into resolve.
ramacharitamanas::4106.simple_meaning: Angad's words leave the monkey warriors speechless and tearful for a moment before they respond together.
ramacharitamanas::4106.simple_insight: Some words are so heavy they silence everyone before they can answer.
ramacharitamanas::4106.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Angad has just spoken with painful courage after the failed search for Sita. The monkey warriors are struck silent, moved to tears, and then gather themselves to answer him as one.
ramacharitamanas::4106.modern_relevance: You hear a hard truth in a room and nobody can speak for a second. The silence itself shows how deeply it landed.
ramacharitamanas::4106.insight: It shows grief and resolve arriving together, before the group turns pain into a shared response.

ramacharitamanas::4107.verse_sanskrit: हम सीता कै सुधि लीन्हें बिना। नहिं जैहैं जुबराज प्रबीना॥ अस कहि लवन सिंधु तट जाई। बैठे कपि सब दर्भ डसाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4107.verse_hindi: हे सुयोग्य युवराज! हम लोग सीताजी की खोज लिए बिना नहीं लौटेंगे। ऐसा कहकर लवणसागर के तट पर जाकर सब वानर कुश बिछाकर बैठ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4107.english_translation: “We will not return without finding Sita.” Saying this, the monkeys went to the shore of the ocean and sat down on kusa grass.
ramacharitamanas::4107.translation_literal: हम (we) / सीता कै (of Sita) / सुधि (news, trace) / लीन्हें (having found) / बिना (without) / नहिं (not) / जैहैं (will go) / जुबराज (young prince) / प्रबीना (wise, capable) ॥ अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / लवन सिंधु (ocean) / तट (shore) / जाई (going) / बैठे (sat) / कपि (monkeys) / सब (all) / दर्भ (kusa grass) / डसाई (spread, laid down) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4107.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4107.essence: Real loyalty stays put until the search is complete.
ramacharitamanas::4107.simple_meaning: The monkeys refuse to go back until they have found Sita. They go to the seashore and sit down on kusa grass.
ramacharitamanas::4107.simple_insight: Sometimes loyalty means staying with the search, even when you have no answer yet.
ramacharitamanas::4107.detailed_meaning: After Angad's painful stand before Ravana, the monkey leaders gather on the shore of the ocean. They decide together that they will not return to Ram without news of Sita, and they sit in resolve, waiting for the next guidance.
ramacharitamanas::4107.modern_relevance: You leave the hospital parking lot after another unanswered update, but you still don't drive home. Not until you know what happened, not until you can tell the family something real.
ramacharitamanas::4107.insight: It shifts the mind from retreat to steadfast commitment when the task is unfinished.

ramacharitamanas::4108.verse_sanskrit: जामवंत अंगद दुख देखी। कहीं कथा उपदेस बिसेषी॥ तात राम कहुँ नर जनि मानहु। निर्गुन ब्रह्म अजित अज जानहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4108.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् ने अंगद का दुःख देखकर विशेष उपदेश की कथाएँ कहीं। (वे बोले-) हे तात! श्री रामजी को मनुष्य न मानो, उन्हें निर्गुण ब्रह्म, अजेय और अजन्मा समझो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4108.english_translation: Seeing Angad's sorrow, Jambavan spoke a special teaching. "Dear one, do not think of Ram as merely human. Know him as the attributeless supreme reality, unconquerable and unborn."
ramacharitamanas::4108.translation_literal: जामवंत (Jambavan) / अंगद (Angad) / दुख (sorrow) / देखी (seeing) / कहीं (spoke) / कथा (teaching story) / उपदेस (instruction) / बिसेषी (special)॥ / तात (dear one) / राम कहुँ (Ram as) / नर (human) / जनि (do not) / मानहु (think) / निर्गुन (attributeless) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / अजित (unconquerable) / अज (unborn) / जानहु (know)
ramacharitamanas::4108.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4108.essence: Ram is not limited by human form or human weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4108.simple_meaning: Jambavan comforts the grieving monkeys by reminding them that Ram is not limited to a human form. He is beyond ordinary nature, beyond defeat, and beyond birth itself.
ramacharitamanas::4108.simple_insight: Your faith deepens when you stop measuring the divine by human limits.
ramacharitamanas::4108.detailed_meaning: Angad and the monkey army are shaken after hearing they may have failed in their search. Jambavan steps in with a turning-point teaching: Ram is not merely a man to be judged by human standards, but the supreme reality itself.
ramacharitamanas::4108.modern_relevance: You start doubting after a setback and begin treating what you love as small, ordinary, or fragile. This verse pulls you back from that reduction and restores reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4108.insight: It shifts the mind from judging Ram by appearance to recognising his limitless nature.

ramacharitamanas::4109.verse_sanskrit: हम सब सेवक अति बड़भागी। संतत सगुन ब्रह्म अनुरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4109.verse_hindi: हम सब सेवक अत्यंत बड़भागी हैं, जो निरंतर सगुण ब्रह्म (श्री रामजी) में प्रीति रखते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4109.english_translation: We servants are truly fortunate, for we remain ever devoted to the manifest supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::4109.translation_literal: हम (we) / सब (all) / सेवक (servants) / अति (very) / बड़भागी (fortunate) / संतत (continually) / सगुन (with qualities, manifest) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / अनुरागी (loving, devoted)
ramacharitamanas::4109.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4109.essence: Steady love for Ram is itself the greatest good.
ramacharitamanas::4109.simple_meaning: The servants are called fortunate because they keep loving Ram in his visible, personal form.
ramacharitamanas::4109.simple_insight: Love becomes a blessing when it has a living object, not just an idea.
ramacharitamanas::4109.detailed_meaning: Jambavan has just lifted the vanaras out of grief by reminding them who Ram really is. In that moment, the servants recognise that their greatest fortune is not strength or victory, but steady love for Ram as the manifest supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::4109.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone for one message that could change your day. The deeper relief comes when your heart already has a place to rest, not just a goal to chase.
ramacharitamanas::4109.insight: It shifts devotion from vague admiration to a living relationship with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4110.verse_sanskrit: निज इच्छाँ प्रभु अवतरइ सुर मह गोद्वज लागि। सगुन उपासक संग तहँ रहहिं मोच्छ सब त्यागि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4110.verse_hindi: देवता, पृथ्वी, गो और ब्राह्मणों के लिए प्रभु अपनी इच्छा से (किसी कर्मबंधन से नहीं) अवतार लेते हैं। वहाँ सगुणोपासक (भक्तगण सालोक्य, सामीप्य, सारुप्य, सार्ष्टि और सायुज्य) सब प्रकार के मोक्षों को त्यागकर उनकी सेवा में साथ रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4110.english_translation: The Lord descends by His own will for the sake of the gods, the earth, cows, and brahmins. There, devotees of the divine form stay with Him in service, abandoning all kinds of freedom in the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::4110.translation_literal: निज इच्छाँ (by His own will) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अवतरइ (descends) / सुर (gods) / मह (for) / गोद्वज (cows and brahmins) / लागि (for the sake of) / सगुन (with form) / उपासक (worshippers) / संग (with) / तहँ (there) / रहहिं (remain) / मोच्छ (freedom) / सब (all) / त्यागि (abandoning)
ramacharitamanas::4110.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4110.essence: True devotion would rather stay near Ram than claim release.
ramacharitamanas::4110.simple_meaning: Ram comes of His own will to protect the gods, the earth, cows, and brahmins. Devotees stay near Him in loving service, even if that means giving up all forms of liberation.
ramacharitamanas::4110.simple_insight: Love can value closeness more than escape. Being near the beloved feels greater than any reward.
ramacharitamanas::4110.detailed_meaning: Jambavan is teaching the grieving monkeys about Ram’s true nature. Ram is not forced into the world; He comes willingly to protect what is righteous. Those who love Him do not chase release for themselves — they stay beside Him in service.
ramacharitamanas::4110.modern_relevance: You finally get the offer you thought you wanted: the promotion, the exit, the clean break. But your heart says the real prize is staying with what you love and serving it well.
ramacharitamanas::4110.insight: It shifts devotion from using the divine for personal gain to choosing loving nearness over spiritual reward.

ramacharitamanas::4111.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि कथा कहहिं बहु भाँती। गिरि कंदराँ सुनी संपाती॥ बाहेर होइ देखि बहु कीसा। मोहि अहार दीन्ह जगदीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4111.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार जाम्बवान् बहुत प्रकार से कथाएँ कह रहे हैं। इनकी बातें पर्वत की कन्दरा में सम्पाती ने सुनीं। बाहर निकलकर उसने बहुत से वानर देखे। (तब वह बोला-) जगदीश्वर ने मुझको घर बैठे बहुत सा आहार भेज दिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4111.english_translation: In this way, Jambavan was telling many kinds of stories. Sampati heard them from a mountain cave. Coming outside, he saw many monkeys and thought, "The divine ruler has sent me food right here at home."
ramacharitamanas::4111.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / कथा (stories) / कहहिं (they tell) / बहु भाँती (in many ways) / गिरि (mountain) / कंदराँ (cave) / सुनी (heard) / संपाती (Sampati) / बाहेर (outside) / होइ (having become) / देखि (seeing) / बहु (many) / कीसा (monkeys) / मोहि (to me) / अहार (food) / दीन्ह (gave) / जगदीसा (the Lord of the world)
ramacharitamanas::4111.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4111.essence: Need can turn sight into appetite.
ramacharitamanas::4111.simple_meaning: Sampati overhears the monkeys' conversation, comes out of his cave, sees them, and thinks the monkeys are food sent to him by the divine ruler.
ramacharitamanas::4111.simple_insight: A hungry mind can turn even a blessing into a threat.
ramacharitamanas::4111.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Jambavan and the monkeys are speaking near Sampati's mountain cave. Sampati, weak and hungry, hears them from inside. When he comes out and sees the monkeys, his first thought is not friendship but food.
ramacharitamanas::4111.modern_relevance: You overhear a conversation while exhausted and immediately read danger into it. When hunger or fear is driving, even neutral things can look like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::4111.insight: It shows how deprivation distorts perception before any real judgment can happen.

ramacharitamanas::4112.verse_sanskrit: आजु सबहि कहँ भच्छन करऊँ। दिन हबु चले अहार बिनु मरऊँ॥ कबहुँ न मिल भरि उदर अहारा। आजु दीन्ह बिधि एकहिं बारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4112.verse_hindi: आज इन सबको खा जाऊँगा। बहुत दिन बीत गए, भोजन के बिना मर रहा था। पेटभर भोजन कभी नहीं मिलता। आज विधाता ने एक ही बार में बहुत सा भोजन दे दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4112.english_translation: Today I will eat all of you. For many days I have gone without food and am dying. I have never once had enough to fill my belly. Today fate has given me a full meal at one stroke.
ramacharitamanas::4112.translation_literal: आजु (today) / सबहि (all) / कहँ (for) / भच्छन (eating) / करऊँ (I will do) । / दिन (days) / हबु (have) / चले (passed) / अहार (food) / बिनु (without) / मरऊँ (I die) ॥ / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / मिल (get) / भरि (full) / उदर (belly) / अहारा (food) । / आजु (today) / दीन्ह (gave) / बिधि (fate) / एकहिं (in one) / बारा (time) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4112.speaker: Sampati
ramacharitamanas::4112.essence: Desperation can turn a starving mind into a threat.
ramacharitamanas::4112.simple_meaning: Sampati says he will eat the monkeys because he has been starving for a long time and has never had enough food.
ramacharitamanas::4112.simple_insight: Hunger can turn a desperate mind toward violence and greed.
ramacharitamanas::4112.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the monkeys have just encountered Sampati, the aged vulture. Hearing their movement outside the cave, he reveals his own hunger and sees them as a sudden feast. The line is a raw outburst, not a teaching, and it sets up the fear that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4112.modern_relevance: A person who has gone too long without support can start seeing other people as resources instead of lives. Desperation narrows the mind until everything looks like a chance to survive.
ramacharitamanas::4112.insight: It shows how deprivation can warp judgment and make others seem like prey.

ramacharitamanas::4113.verse_sanskrit: डरपे गीध बचन सुनि काना। अब भा मरन सत्य हम जाना॥ कपि सब उठे गीध कहँ देखी। जामवंत मन सोच बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4113.verse_hindi: गीध के वचन कानों से सुनते ही सब डर गए कि अब सचमुच ही मरना हो गया। यह हमने जान लिया। फिर उस गीध (सम्पाती) को देखकर सब वानर उठ खड़े हुए। जाम्बवान् के मन में विशेष सोच हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4113.english_translation: Hearing the vulture's words, everyone was struck with fear: now we know death is certain. Then, seeing that vulture, the monkeys sprang up, and Jambavan felt deep concern.
ramacharitamanas::4113.translation_literal: डरपे (were struck with fear) / गीध (vulture) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (with ears) / अब (now) / भा (became) / मरन (death) / सत्य (certain) / हम (we) / जाना (knew) ॥ कपि (monkeys) / सब (all) / उठे (rose up) / गीध (vulture) / कहँ (toward) / देखी (seeing) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / मन (mind) / सोच (concern) / बिसेषी (special, deep) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4113.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4113.essence: Fear rises first; understanding comes only after seeing clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4113.simple_meaning: The monkeys hear the vulture's words and panic, thinking death is near. Then they see him clearly, and Jambavan begins to think carefully.
ramacharitamanas::4113.simple_insight: Fear softens when you stop reacting and actually look.
ramacharitamanas::4113.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the exhausted monkeys have been speaking in the cave when Sampati, the old vulture, reveals what he knows. His words shock them into fear, then his visible presence changes the moment. Jambavan turns inward and starts weighing what this means.
ramacharitamanas::4113.modern_relevance: Someone sends a terrifying voice note, and your stomach drops before you even read it fully. Then you open the message, see the full context, and your mind finally steadies.
ramacharitamanas::4113.insight: It shows how fear can surge from words alone, but clear seeing brings the mind back to thought.

ramacharitamanas::4114.verse_sanskrit: कह अंगद बिचारि मन माहीं। धन्य जटायू सम कोउ नाहीं॥ राम काज कारन तनु त्यागी। हरि पुर गयउ परम बड़भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4114.verse_hindi: अंगद ने मन में विचार कर कहा- अहा! जटायु के समान धन्य कोई नहीं है। श्री रामजी के कार्य के लिए शरीर छोड़कर वह परम बड़भागी भगवान् के परमधाम को चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4114.english_translation: Angada thought to himself, “No one is as blessed as Jatayu. He gave up his body for Ram’s work and went to the supreme abode, most fortunate indeed.”
ramacharitamanas::4114.translation_literal: कह (said) / अंगद (Angada) / बिचारि (having reflected) / मन माहीं (within the mind) / धन्य (blessed) / जटायू (Jatayu) / सम (like) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (not)॥ / राम काज (Ram’s work) / कारन (for the sake of) / तनु (body) / त्यागी (having given up) / हरि (Ram) / पुर (abode) / गयउ (went) / परम (supreme) / बड़भागी (most fortunate) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4114.speaker: Angada
ramacharitamanas::4114.essence: Selfless service can make a life truly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::4114.simple_meaning: Angada honors Jatayu as the most blessed being because he gave his life for Ram’s cause and reached the supreme abode.
ramacharitamanas::4114.simple_insight: A life becomes radiant when it is spent for something greater than itself.
ramacharitamanas::4114.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the vanaras have just heard of Jatayu’s sacrifice. Angada reflects inwardly and praises the fallen bird who fought for Ram and died in service. The moment turns grief into reverence, showing what true greatness looks like.
ramacharitamanas::4114.modern_relevance: You remember the friend who showed up when it mattered, gave everything, and asked for nothing back. Some lives shine brightest at the moment they are spent.
ramacharitamanas::4114.insight: It shifts admiration toward self-giving service instead of status, survival, or reward.

ramacharitamanas::4115.verse_sanskrit: सुनि खग हरष सोक जुत बानी। आवा निकट कपिन्ह भय मानी॥ तिन्हहि अभय करि पूछेसि जाई। कथा सकल तिन्ह ताहि सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4115.verse_hindi: हर्ष और शोक से युक्त वाणी (समाचार) सुनकर वह पक्षी (सम्पाती) वानरों के पास आया। वानर डर गए। उनको अभय करके (अभय वचन देकर) उसने पास जाकर जटायु का वृत्तांत पूछा, तब उन्होंने सारी कथा उसे कह सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4115.english_translation: Hearing the news filled with joy and sorrow, the bird came close to the monkeys, who were afraid. After giving them reassurance, he went near and asked about Jatayu, and they told him the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::4115.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / खग (the bird) / हरष (joy) / सोक (sorrow) / जुत (joined with) / बानी (speech, news) / आवा (came) / निकट (near) / कपिन्ह (to the monkeys) / भय (fear) / मानी (feeling) / तिन्हहि (them) / अभय (fearlessness, reassurance) / करि (having done) / पूछेसि (he asked) / जाई (going) / कथा (story) / सकल (all) / तिन्ह (they) / ताहि (to him) / सुनाई (told)
ramacharitamanas::4115.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4115.essence: Reassurance opens the door to painful truth.
ramacharitamanas::4115.simple_meaning: The bird came to the monkeys after hearing mixed news. They were afraid, but he reassured them and asked about Jatayu, then heard the full story.
ramacharitamanas::4115.simple_insight: Fear softens when someone offers reassurance before asking for the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4115.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the monkeys have just spoken of Jatayu’s fate. Sampati approaches with mixed joy and sorrow in his heart, while the monkeys fear him at first. He calms them, asks about his brother, and receives the full account that will move the search forward.
ramacharitamanas::4115.modern_relevance: A tense group chat goes quiet after bad news. Someone finally says, “Take a breath — tell me what happened.” That small reassurance opens the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::4115.insight: It shows how trust must be restored before painful truth can be shared.

ramacharitamanas::4116.verse_sanskrit: सुनि संपाति बंधु कै करनी। रघुपति महिमा बहुबिधि बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4116.verse_hindi: भाई जटायु की करनी सुनकर सम्पाती ने बहुत प्रकार से श्री रघुनाथजी की महिमा वर्णन की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4116.english_translation: Hearing about his brother Jatayu's deed, Sampati praised the glory of Raghunath in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::4116.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / संपाति (Sampati) / बंधु (brother) / कै (of) / करनी (deed) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / महिमा (glory) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / बरनी (described)
ramacharitamanas::4116.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4116.essence: Devotion grows when sacrifice is seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4116.simple_meaning: Sampati hears of Jatayu's sacrifice and responds by praising Ram's greatness in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::4116.simple_insight: A noble act can awaken devotion in someone who only hears about it.
ramacharitamanas::4116.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the vanaras have reached Sampati after Jatayu's story. Hearing how his brother died serving Ram, Sampati is moved beyond grief into praise. His response becomes the bridge that leads the search onward.
ramacharitamanas::4116.modern_relevance: You hear what someone did for a cause bigger than themselves, and your cynicism drops. A single story of courage can make you speak differently, trust differently, and act differently.
ramacharitamanas::4116.insight: It shifts the mind from family loss to reverence for a greater purpose.

ramacharitamanas::4117.verse_sanskrit: मोहि लै जाहु सिंधुतट देउँ तिलांजलि ताहि। बचन सहाइ करबि मैं पैहहु खोजहु जाहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4117.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) मुझे समुद्र के किनारे ले चलो, मैं जटायु को तिलांजलि दे दूँ। इस सेवा के बदले मैं तुम्हारी वचन से सहायता करूँगा (अर्थात् सीताजी कहाँ हैं सो बतला दूँगा), जिसे तुम खोज रहे हो उसे पा जाओगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4117.english_translation: Take me to the shore of the ocean. I will offer libations to Jatayu. In return for that service, I will help with my word and tell you where to find the one you seek.
ramacharitamanas::4117.translation_literal: मोहि (me) / लै (taking) / जाहु (go) / सिंधुतट (to the ocean shore) / देउँ (I will give) / तिलांजलि (water-offering) / ताहि (to him) / बचन (word) / सहाइ (helping) / करबि (I will do) / मैं (I) / पैहहु (you will get) / खोजहु (search) / जाहि (whom)
ramacharitamanas::4117.speaker: Sampati
ramacharitamanas::4117.essence: Honor given without calculation returns as guidance.
ramacharitamanas::4117.simple_meaning: Sampati asks the monkeys to take him to the sea so he can honor Jatayu, and promises to help them find Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4117.simple_insight: Small acts of respect can unlock unexpected help.
ramacharitamanas::4117.detailed_meaning: After hearing of his brother Jatayu's fate, Sampati is moved to repay that loss with honor. He asks Hanuman and the monkeys to take him to the seashore for the funeral offering, then offers the clue they have been seeking.
ramacharitamanas::4117.modern_relevance: You stop to help an older man place flowers at a roadside memorial, expecting nothing back. Later, he gives you the exact contact you needed. Respect can become a bridge.
ramacharitamanas::4117.insight: It links care for the dead with practical help for the living, showing how service can create trust and open doors.

ramacharitamanas::4118.verse_sanskrit: अनुज क्रिया करि सागर तीरा। कहि निज कथा सुनहु कपि बीरा॥ हम द्वौ बंधु प्रथम तरुनाई। गगन गए रबि निकट उड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4118.verse_hindi: समुद्र के तीर पर छोटे भाई जटायु की क्रिया (श्राद्ध आदि) करके सम्पाती अपनी कथा कहने लगा- हे वीर वानरों! सुनो, हम दोनों भाई उठती जवानी में एक बार आकाश में उड़कर सूर्य के निकट चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4118.english_translation: After performing the rites for his younger brother at the seashore, Sampati began to tell his own story: "Listen, brave monkeys. We two brothers, in our youth, once flew up into the sky and went near the sun."
ramacharitamanas::4118.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / क्रिया करि (having performed the rites) / सागर तीरा (at the seashore) / कहि (saying) / निज कथा (his own story) / सुनहु (listen) / कपि बीरा (brave monkeys) / हम द्वौ (we both) / बंधु (brothers) / प्रथम (first) / तरुनाई (in youth) / गगन (sky) / गए (went) / रबि (sun) / निकट (near) / उड़ाई (flying)
ramacharitamanas::4118.speaker: Sampati
ramacharitamanas::4118.essence: A painful loss opens the door to crucial memory.
ramacharitamanas::4118.simple_meaning: Sampati finishes his brother's rites and begins telling the monkeys how he and Jatayu once flew close to the sun in their youth.
ramacharitamanas::4118.simple_insight: Even great beings can be carried by a story of loss, pride, and what came before.
ramacharitamanas::4118.detailed_meaning: On the seashore, Sampati performs Jatayu's final rites and turns to Hanuman and the monkeys. He begins recounting the brothers' youth, setting up the reason for his fall and the knowledge he can now give them.
ramacharitamanas::4118.modern_relevance: At a funeral gathering, someone who has lost a sibling starts speaking slowly about the years before everything changed. The memory itself becomes the bridge to what must be heard next.
ramacharitamanas::4118.insight: It shifts attention from the present loss to the backstory that explains it.

ramacharitamanas::4119.verse_sanskrit: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4119.verse_hindi: वह (जटायु) तेज नहीं सह सका, इससे लौट आया (किंतु), मैं अभिमानी था इसलिए सूर्य के पास चला गया। अत्यंत अपार तेज से मेरे पंख जल गए। मैं बड़े जोर से चीख मारकर जमीन पर गिर पड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4119.english_translation: He could not bear the brilliance and returned. But I was proud, so I went near the sun. My wings were burned by that immense radiance, and I fell to the ground with a terrible cry.
ramacharitamanas::4119.translation_literal: तेज (radiance) / न (not) / सहि (bearing) / सक (was able) / सो (he) / फिरि (back) / आवा (came) / मैं (I) / अभिमानी (proud) / रबि (sun) / निअरावा (went near) / जरे (burned) / पंख (wings) / अति (very) / तेज (radiance) / अपारा (immeasurable) / परेउँ (fell) / भूमि (ground) / करि (making) / घोर (terrible) / चिकारा (cry)
ramacharitamanas::4119.speaker: Sampati
ramacharitamanas::4119.essence: Pride can send you toward the fire that breaks you.
ramacharitamanas::4119.simple_meaning: Sampati explains that his brother turned back from the sun's heat, but his own pride drove him too close, burning his wings and sending him crashing down.
ramacharitamanas::4119.simple_insight: Pride makes you reach for what your body and mind cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::4119.detailed_meaning: Sampati, grieving over Jatayu, tells the vanaras how his own arrogance led him to the sun. This is not the teaching itself, only the painful reason he became unable to fly and had to be healed by later wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4119.modern_relevance: You take on the job, the pace, or the relationship that looks dazzling from far away, then realize you were trying to stand too close to what would burn you.
ramacharitamanas::4119.insight: It shows how ego pushes a person past their limits, creating the very collapse that later makes humility possible.

ramacharitamanas::4120.verse_sanskrit: मुनि एक नाम चंद्रमा ओही। लागी दया देखि करि मोही॥ बहु प्रकार तेहिं ग्यान सुनावा। देहजनित अभिमान छुड़ावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4120.verse_hindi: वहाँ चंद्रमा नाम के एक मुनि थे। मुझे देखकर उन्हें बड़ी दया लगी। उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से मुझे ज्ञान सुनाया और मेरे देहजनित (देह संबंधी) अभिमान को छुड़ा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4120.english_translation: There was a sage named Chandrama. He felt deep compassion for me when he saw me. In many ways he taught me wisdom and removed my pride born of the body.
ramacharitamanas::4120.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / एक (one) / नाम (named) / चंद्रमा (Chandrama) / ओही (there) / लागी (felt) / दया (compassion) / देखि (seeing) / करि (doing) / मोही (me) / बहु (many) / प्रकार (ways) / तेहिं (by him) / ग्यान (wisdom) / सुनावा (taught) / देह-जनित (born from the body) / अभिमान (pride) / छुड़ावा (removed)
ramacharitamanas::4120.speaker: Sampati
ramacharitamanas::4120.essence: Kindness can remove the pride that blocks understanding.
ramacharitamanas::4120.simple_meaning: A compassionate sage taught Sampati and freed him from bodily pride. Real wisdom began when someone saw him with kindness and helped him drop his false identification.
ramacharitamanas::4120.simple_insight: Being corrected feels easier when it comes with care.
ramacharitamanas::4120.detailed_meaning: Sampati is recounting his past on the seashore. After his reckless flight and fall, a sage named Chandrama takes pity on him, teaches him in many ways, and strips away the pride tied to his physical form.
ramacharitamanas::4120.modern_relevance: You make a mistake, and instead of being shamed, one calm person explains what you could not see. That gentle correction can do what anger never will.
ramacharitamanas::4120.insight: It shows that clear seeing often arrives through compassionate guidance, not harsh criticism.

ramacharitamanas::4121.verse_sanskrit: त्रेताँ ब्रह्म मनुज तनु धरिही। तासु नारि निसिचर पति हरिही॥ तासु खोज पठइहि प्रभु दूता। तिन्हहि मिलें तैं होब पुनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4121.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) त्रेतायुग में साक्षात् परब्रह्म मनुष्य शरीर धारण करेंगे। उनकी स्त्री को राक्षसों का राजा हर ले जाएगा। उसकी खोज में प्रभु दूत भेजेंगे। उनसे मिलने पर तू पवित्र हो जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4121.english_translation: In Treta Yuga, the supreme reality will take a human body. The king of demons will carry off his wife. The Lord will send messengers to search for her. Meeting them will purify you.
ramacharitamanas::4121.translation_literal: त्रेताँ (in Treta) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / मनुज तनु (human body) / धरिही (will take) / तासु (his) / नारि (wife) / निसिचर पति (king of the night-beings) / हरिही (will carry off) / तासु (his) / खोज (search) / पठइहि (will send) / प्रभु (the Lord) / दूता (messengers) / तिन्हहि (them) / मिलें (meeting) / तैं (you) / होब (will become) / पुनीता (purified)
ramacharitamanas::4121.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::4121.essence: Ram's messengers are enough to change you.
ramacharitamanas::4121.simple_meaning: The sage predicts that Ram will be born as a human, Sita will be taken away, and Ram will send messengers to search for her. Even meeting those messengers will purify you.
ramacharitamanas::4121.simple_insight: Grace can reach you through the people sent to help.
ramacharitamanas::4121.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is hearing a sage's old prediction come true in the middle of his leap toward Lanka. The sage had foretold Ram's human birth, Sita's abduction, and the coming of Ram's messengers. That prophecy now becomes Hanuman's own doorway into sanctity.
ramacharitamanas::4121.modern_relevance: A stranger gives you directions that later save your day, and you realise the help was never random. Sometimes the people sent your way carry more than information — they carry a turning point.
ramacharitamanas::4121.insight: It shifts you from seeing helpers as ordinary contacts to recognising them as carriers of transformation.
