ramacharitamanas::4122.verse_sanskrit: जमिहहिं पंख करसि जनि चिंता। तिन्हहि देखाइ देहेसु तैं सीता॥ मुनि कइ गिरा सत्य भइ आजू। सुनि मम बचन करहु प्रभु काजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4122.verse_hindi: और तेरे पंख उग आएँगे, चिंता न कर। उन्हें तू सीताजी को दिखा देना। मुनि की वह वाणी आज सत्य हुई। अब मेरे वचन सुनकर तुम प्रभु का कार्य करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4122.english_translation: Your wings will grow. Do not worry. Show Sita to them. The sage's words have come true today. Now, hearing my words, do the Lord's work.
ramacharitamanas::4122.translation_literal: जमिहहिं (will grow) / पंख (wings) / करसि (you do) / जनि (do not) / चिंता (worry) / तिन्हहि (to them) / देखाइ (showing) / देहेसु (you will show) / तैं (you) / सीता (Sita) / मुनि (sage) / कइ (of) / गिरा (speech) / सत्य (true) / भइ (became) / आजू (today) / सुनि (hearing) / मम (my) / बचन (words) / करहु (do) / प्रभु (Lord's) / काजू (work)
ramacharitamanas::4122.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4122.essence: Faith turns impossible work into clear service.
ramacharitamanas::4122.simple_meaning: Hanuman is told not to worry; his wings will come, he will show Sita, and he should carry out Ram's task.
ramacharitamanas::4122.simple_insight: Fear fades when you trust that help will arrive exactly when needed.
ramacharitamanas::4122.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is being prepared for the leap into Lanka. A sage's earlier words are now proving true: his wings will grow, and he will find Sita. The moment turns his mission from doubt into confident service.
ramacharitamanas::4122.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the call, or take the leap, and your chest tightens. Then something in you says: keep going, the next step will reveal itself.
ramacharitamanas::4122.insight: It shifts you from anxious hesitation to confident action in service of a larger purpose.

ramacharitamanas::4123.verse_sanskrit: गिरि त्रिकूट ऊपर बस लंका। तहँ रह रावन सहज असंका॥ तहँ असोक उपबन जहँ रहई। सीता बैठि सोच रत अहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4123.verse_hindi: त्रिकूट पर्वत पर लंका बसी हुई है। वहाँ स्वभाव से ही निडर रावण रहता है। वहाँ अशोक नाम का उपवन (बगीचा) है, जहाँ सीताजी रहती हैं। (इस समय भी) वे सोच में मग्न बैठी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4123.english_translation: Lanka stands atop Mount Trikuta. There lives Ravana, naturally fearless. There is the Ashoka grove, where Sita sits, absorbed in sorrowful thought.
ramacharitamanas::4123.translation_literal: गिरि (mountain) / त्रिकूट (Trikuta) / ऊपर (on top) / बस (dwells) / लंका (Lanka) / तहँ (there) / रह (lives) / रावन (Ravana) / सहज (natural) / असंका (fearlessness)॥ / तहँ (there) / असोक (Ashoka) / उपबन (grove) / जहँ (where) / रहई (dwells) / सीता (Sita) / बैठि (sitting) / सोच (sorrow, thought) / रत (absorbed in) / अहई (is)
ramacharitamanas::4123.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4123.essence: A fortress can look fearless while holding deep sorrow within it.
ramacharitamanas::4123.simple_meaning: Lanka sits high on Mount Trikuta, ruled by fearless Ravana. In the Ashoka grove there, Sita sits lost in sorrowful thought.
ramacharitamanas::4123.simple_insight: Power and sorrow can exist side by side in the same place.
ramacharitamanas::4123.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka and is learning the lay of the land. The verse sketches the enemy city, Ravana’s confidence, and Sita’s lonely presence in the Ashoka grove, setting up the moment when Hanuman will finally find her.
ramacharitamanas::4123.modern_relevance: You walk into a glittering place where everyone seems powerful, yet one person is sitting quietly with a broken heart. This verse holds both images at once.
ramacharitamanas::4123.insight: It shifts attention from the city’s strength to the hidden suffering at its center.

ramacharitamanas::4124.verse_sanskrit: मैं देखउँ तुम्ह नाहीं गीधहि दृष्टि अपार। बूढ़ भयउँ न त करतेउँ कछुक सहाय तुम्हार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4124.verse_hindi: मैं उन्हें देख रहा हूँ, तुम नहीं देख सकते, क्योंकि गीध की दृष्टि अपार होती है (बहुत दूर तक जाती है)। क्या करूँ? मैं बूढ़ा हो गया, नहीं तो तुम्हारी कुछ तो सहायता अवश्य करता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4124.english_translation: I can see them, but you cannot. A vulture's sight reaches far. What can I do? I have grown old; otherwise I would surely help you.
ramacharitamanas::4124.translation_literal: मैं (I) / देखउँ (see) / तुम्ह (you) / नाहीं (not) / गीधहि (of the vulture) / दृष्टि (sight) / अपार (vast) / बूढ़ (old) / भयउँ (have become) / त (then) / न (not) / करतेउँ (would do) / कछुक (some) / सहाय (help) / तुम्हार (your)
ramacharitamanas::4124.speaker: Jatayu
ramacharitamanas::4124.essence: Clear sight can remain even after strength is gone.
ramacharitamanas::4124.simple_meaning: Jatayu says he can still see Sita, but his age has taken away the strength to help more than this.
ramacharitamanas::4124.simple_insight: Even when strength is gone, care can still remain fully alive.
ramacharitamanas::4124.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is receiving Jatayu's final guidance near the forest path to Lanka. Jatayu points toward Sita's direction and admits that old age has drained his power. His words are a sorrowful bridge between knowledge and action.
ramacharitamanas::4124.modern_relevance: You know exactly how to fix the problem, but your body or energy won't cooperate. Someone you care about is counting on you, and all you can offer is one clear direction.
ramacharitamanas::4124.insight: It shows that seeing clearly is not the same as being able to act. Age, limits, and love can exist together.

ramacharitamanas::4125.verse_sanskrit: जो नाघइ सत जोजन सागर। करइ सो राम काज मति आगर॥ मोहि बिलोकि धरहु मन धीरा। राम कृपाँ कस भयउ सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4125.verse_hindi: जो सौ योजन (चार सौ कोस) समुद्र लाँघ सकेगा और बुद्धिनिधान होगा, वही श्री रामजी का कार्य कर सकेगा। (निराश होकर घबराओ मत) मुझे देखकर मन में धीरज धरो। देखो, श्री रामजी की कृपा से (देखते ही देखते) मेरा शरीर कैसा हो गया (बिना पाँख का बेहाल था, पाँख उगने से सुंदर हो गया) ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4125.english_translation: Whoever can cross the hundred-yojana ocean and is wise can do Ram's work. Seeing me, keep your mind steady. By Ram's grace, see what has happened to my body.
ramacharitamanas::4125.translation_literal: जो (whoever) / नाघइ (crosses) / सत जोजन (hundred yojanas) / सागर (ocean) / करइ (does) / सो (that one) / राम काज (Ram's work) / मति आगर (wise, foremost in understanding) ॥ / मोहि (me) / बिलोकि (seeing) / धरहु (keep) / मन धीरा (mind steady) ॥ / राम कृपाँ (by Ram's grace) / कस (how) / भयउ (became) / सरीरा (body) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4125.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4125.essence: Ram's work is done by the one who trusts enough to cross fear.
ramacharitamanas::4125.simple_meaning: Hanuman says that only someone wise and bold enough to cross the vast ocean can do Ram's work. He tells the listener to stay calm and trust Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4125.simple_insight: Great tasks become possible when courage rests on grace, not on self-doubt.
ramacharitamanas::4125.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka after leaping across the ocean, and he stands before Sita's search with proof of Ram's power in his own transformed body. He tells the listener that Ram's work needs steadiness, wisdom, and trust.
ramacharitamanas::4125.modern_relevance: You are about to send the risky message, take the hard trip, or make the call nobody else wants to make. The task feels impossible until you remember what steadies you.
ramacharitamanas::4125.insight: It shifts effort from panic to confident action grounded in grace.

ramacharitamanas::4126.verse_sanskrit: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4126.verse_hindi: पापी भी जिनका नाम स्मरण करके अत्यंत पार भवसागर से तर जाते हैं। तुम उनके दूत हो, अतः कायरता छोड़कर श्री रामजी को हृदय में धारण करके उपाय करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4126.english_translation: Even sinners cross the vast ocean of becoming by remembering that name. You are that divine messenger, so drop your fear, hold Ram in your heart, and find a way.
ramacharitamanas::4126.translation_literal: पापिउ (even sinners) / जाकर (whose) / नाम (name) / सुमिरहीं (remember) / अति (very) / अपार (vast) / भवसागर (ocean of becoming) / तरहीं (cross) ॥ / तासु (that) / दूत (messenger) / तुम्ह (you) / तजि (leaving) / कदराई (cowardice) / राम (Ram) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धरि (placing) / करहु (do) / उपाई (a way) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4126.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4126.essence: Ram's name carries even the fallen across the deepest waters.
ramacharitamanas::4126.simple_meaning: Ram's name is so powerful that even people with serious faults can be carried across life's greatest flood. Hanuman is told to stop hesitating and act with courage.
ramacharitamanas::4126.simple_insight: You do not need to be flawless to be effective. Trust can move you where fear cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4126.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the search for Sita has become urgent. Hanuman is being urged toward Lanka, but hesitation still lingers. The reminder is clear: Ram's name itself carries even the fallen across the deepest waters, so Ram's messenger should act without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4126.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could change everything, and your thumb freezes over the screen. This verse says courage is not the absence of fear — it is remembering who you serve.
ramacharitamanas::4126.insight: It shifts you from self-doubt to trust in Ram's power working through you.

ramacharitamanas::4127.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि गरुड़ गीध जब गयऊ। तिन्ह के मन अति बिसमय भयऊ॥ निज निज बल सब काहूँ भाषा। पार जाइ कर संसय राखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4127.verse_hindi: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! इस प्रकार कहकर जब गीध चला गया, तब उन (वानरों) के मन में अत्यंत विस्मय हुआ। सब किसी ने अपना-अपना बल कहा। पर समुद्र के पार जाने में सभी ने संदेह प्रकट किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4127.english_translation: After saying this, the vulture departed, and the hearts of all were filled with wonder. Each one spoke of his own strength, yet everyone still doubted crossing the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4127.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / गरुड़ (Garuda) / गीध (vulture) / जब (when) / गयऊ (went) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / मन (minds) / अति (very) / बिसमय (wonder) / भयऊ (became) ॥ / निज (own) / निज (own) / बल (strength) / सब (all) / काहूँ (each) / भाषा (spoke) / पार (across) / जाइ (going) / कर (of) / संसय (doubt) / राखा (kept) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4127.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4127.essence: Strength without certainty still hesitates before the impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4127.simple_meaning: The monkeys were amazed, but no one was sure they could cross the sea. Each one spoke of his strength, yet doubt remained.
ramacharitamanas::4127.simple_insight: Pride can speak loudly, but uncertainty still lingers when the task is truly hard.
ramacharitamanas::4127.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just challenged the monkey chiefs to face the impossible task of reaching Lanka. After the vulture leaves, the gathering is stunned. The warriors can name their strengths, but none can yet claim certainty about crossing the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4127.modern_relevance: In a team meeting, everyone lists their qualifications, but the room still goes quiet when the hardest problem appears. Confidence is easy until the real threshold shows up.
ramacharitamanas::4127.insight: It shows the gap between boasting about ability and meeting an actual obstacle.

ramacharitamanas::4128.verse_sanskrit: जरठ भयउँ अब कहइ रिछेसा। नहिं तन रहा प्रथम बल लेसा॥ जबहिं त्रिबिक्रम भए खरारी। तब मैं तरुन रहेउँ बल भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4128.verse_hindi: ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् कहने लगे- मैं बूढ़ा हो गया। शरीर में पहले वाले बल का लेश भी नहीं रहा। जब खरारि (खर के शत्रु श्री राम) वामन बने थे, तब मैं जवान था और मुझ में बड़ा बल था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4128.english_translation: I have grown old now, O king of the bears. Not a trace remains of my former strength. When the destroyer of demons became Trivikrama, I was young and full of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4128.translation_literal: जरठ (old) / भयउँ (have become) / अब (now) / कहइ (says) / रिछेसा (O king of the bears) / नहिं (not) / तन (body) / रहा (remained) / प्रथम (former) / बल (strength) / लेसा (trace)॥ / जबहिं (when) / त्रिबिक्रम (Trivikrama) / भए (became) / खरारी (destroyer of demons) / तब (then) / मैं (I) / तरुन (young) / रहेउँ (was) / बल (strength) / भारी (great)॥
ramacharitamanas::4128.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4128.essence: Old age does not cancel the strength that once met Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4128.simple_meaning: Jambavan says he is old now and no longer has his former strength, but he remembers the time when Ram appeared as Trivikrama and he was young and powerful.
ramacharitamanas::4128.simple_insight: Even when your body changes, your memory of courage can still awaken action.
ramacharitamanas::4128.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Jambavan is urging the hesitant monkeys to remember what they are capable of. He first admits his own age and weakness, then recalls an earlier age when he witnessed Ram as Trivikrama. That memory becomes proof that Ram's greatness is real.
ramacharitamanas::4128.modern_relevance: You open a dusty photo album and see the version of yourself that once moved fast, feared little, and believed. The body is older now, but the part that remembers still knows how to rise.
ramacharitamanas::4128.insight: It shifts attention from present weakness to remembered proof, so courage can return.

ramacharitamanas::4129.verse_sanskrit: बलि बाँधत प्रभु बाढ़ेउ सो तनु बरनि न जाइ। उभय घरी महँ दीन्हीं सात प्रदच्छिन धाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4129.verse_hindi: बलि के बाँधते समय प्रभु इतने बढ़े कि उस शरीर का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, किंतु मैंने दो ही घड़ी में दौड़कर (उस शरीर की) सात प्रदक्षिणाएँ कर लीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4129.english_translation: When Bali was being bound, the Lord grew so large that his body cannot be described. Yet in two moments I ran around that form seven times.
ramacharitamanas::4129.translation_literal: बलि (Bali) / बाँधत (while being bound) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बाढ़ेउ (grew large) / सो (that) / तनु (body) / बरनि (described) / न जाइ (cannot be) / उभय (both) / घरी (moments) / महँ (in) / दीन्हीं (I gave/did) / सात (seven) / प्रदच्छिन (circumambulations) / धाइ (running)
ramacharitamanas::4129.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4129.essence: Ram's form overwhelms description, and devotion moves faster than thought.
ramacharitamanas::4129.simple_meaning: The speaker recalls how Ram became vast when Bali was bound, and how quickly he ran around that immense form seven times.
ramacharitamanas::4129.simple_insight: Some moments are so overwhelming that even memory turns them into wonder.
ramacharitamanas::4129.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the story turns toward Hanuman and the alliance with Sugriva, but this line looks back to Bali's binding. The speaker marvels at Ram's extraordinary form and the speed of the circumambulation, using the memory to heighten Ram's divine grandeur.
ramacharitamanas::4129.modern_relevance: You remember the moment someone walked into the room and changed everything. Later, even the details feel larger than language can hold.
ramacharitamanas::4129.insight: It turns a past event into reverent astonishment, making Ram's presence feel immeasurable.

ramacharitamanas::4130.verse_sanskrit: अंगद कहइ जाउँ मैं पारा। जियँ संसय कछु फिरती बारा॥ जामवंत कह तुम्ह सब लायक। पठइअ किमि सबही कर नायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4130.verse_hindi: अंगद ने कहा- मैं पार तो चला जाऊँगा, परंतु लौटते समय के लिए हृदय में कुछ संदेह है। जाम्बवान् ने कहा- तुम सब प्रकार से योग्य हो, परंतु तुम सबके नेता हो, तुम्हे कैसे भेजा जाए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4130.english_translation: Angad said, "I can cross over, but my heart still has some doubt about the return journey." Jambavan said, "You are fully capable, but you are the leader of all of us—how can we send you?"
ramacharitamanas::4130.translation_literal: अंगद (Angad) / कहइ (says) / जाउँ (I may go) / मैं (I) / पारा (across) / जियँ (in the heart) / संसय (doubt) / कछु (some) / फिरती (returning) / बारा (time) ॥ / जामवंत (Jambavan) / कह (said) / तुम्ह (you) / सब (all) / लायक (capable) / पठइअ (should be sent) / किमि (how) / सबही (of all) / कर (of) / नायक (leader) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4130.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4130.essence: Ability alone does not decide who should carry the mission.
ramacharitamanas::4130.simple_meaning: Angad says he can go across, but he is unsure about coming back. Jambavan then praises his ability, while also noting that he is the leader and should not be sent lightly.
ramacharitamanas::4130.simple_insight: Even strength needs the right person for the right task.
ramacharitamanas::4130.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, the search party is choosing who can leap to Lanka. Angad knows he has strength, but he hesitates about the return. Jambavan affirms his worth, yet also recognizes his leadership role in the group.
ramacharitamanas::4130.modern_relevance: You may be able to take on the challenge, but still hesitate because others depend on you. The question is not only can you do it, but should you be the one sent?
ramacharitamanas::4130.insight: It shifts attention from raw ability to wise assignment of responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::4131.verse_sanskrit: कहइ रीछपति सुनु हनुमाना। का चुप साधि रहेहु बलवाना॥ पवन तनय बल पवन समाना। बुधि बिबेक बिग्यान निधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4131.verse_hindi: ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् ने श्री हनुमानजी से कहा- हे हनुमान् ! हे बलवान् ! सुनो, तुमने यह क्या चुप साध रखी है? तुम पवन के पुत्र हो और बल में पवन के समान हो। तुम बुद्धि-विवेक और विज्ञान की खान हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4131.english_translation: Jambavan, lord of the bears, said to Hanuman: "Listen, mighty one—why are you sitting silent? You are the son of the wind, and your strength is like the wind itself. You are a treasure-house of wisdom, clear seeing, and knowledge."
ramacharitamanas::4131.translation_literal: कहइ (said) / रीछपति (lord of the bears) / सुनु (listen) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / का (what) / चुप (silent) / साधि (holding) / रहेहु (you remain) / बलवाना (mighty one) / पवन तनय (son of the wind) / बल (strength) / पवन समाना (like the wind) / बुधि (wisdom) / बिबेक (clear seeing) / बिग्यान (knowledge) / निधाना (treasure-house)
ramacharitamanas::4131.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4131.essence: True strength wakes when someone names it clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4131.simple_meaning: Jambavan reminds Hanuman that he is not ordinary: he has great strength and deep wisdom, so he should speak up and act.
ramacharitamanas::4131.simple_insight: You may need a reminder of what is already true about you.
ramacharitamanas::4131.detailed_meaning: On the far shore of the ocean, the monkey leaders are stalled and doubtful. Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has been silent, and calls out his hidden greatness. This praise is the spark that awakens Hanuman for Ram's work.
ramacharitamanas::4131.modern_relevance: Everyone in the room looks stuck, and you keep quiet because you think someone else is better for the task. Then one trusted person names what you can do, and your whole posture changes.
ramacharitamanas::4131.insight: It shifts you from hesitation to rightful confidence by recognizing your latent capacity.

ramacharitamanas::4132.verse_sanskrit: कवन सो काज कठिन जग माहीं। जो नहिं होइ तात तुम्ह पाहीं॥ राम काज लगि तव अवतारा। सुनतहिं भयउ पर्बताकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4132.verse_hindi: जगत् में कौन सा ऐसा कठिन काम है जो हे तात! तुमसे न हो सके। श्री रामजी के कार्य के लिए ही तो तुम्हारा अवतार हुआ है। यह सुनते ही हनुमान् जी पर्वत के आकार के (अत्यंत विशालकाय) हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4132.english_translation: What task in the world is too hard for you, dear one? You were born for Ram's work. Hearing this, Hanuman became mountain-sized.
ramacharitamanas::4132.translation_literal: कवन (which) / सो (that) / काज (task) / कठिन (difficult) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / जो (which) / नहिं (not) / होइ (is) / तात (dear one) / तुम्ह (you) / पाहीं (by/with you)॥ राम (Ram) / काज (work) / लगि (for) / तव (your) / अवतारा (incarnation/birth) / सुनतहिं (upon hearing) / भयउ (became) / पर्बताकारा (mountain-shaped, विशालकाय) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4132.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4132.essence: Your real strength appears when your work is named correctly.
ramacharitamanas::4132.simple_meaning: Jambavan reminds Hanuman that no task is beyond him, because he was born for Ram's work. The reminder awakens Hanuman's full power.
ramacharitamanas::4132.simple_insight: Being seen clearly can restore strength you forgot you had.
ramacharitamanas::4132.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Jambavan finally names Hanuman's hidden greatness. After long hesitation, Hanuman hears that his life is meant for Ram's work, and his body and confidence surge at once.
ramacharitamanas::4132.modern_relevance: A friend says, "You can do this," right when you've started doubting yourself before a hard call, a move, or a rescue. Sometimes the right reminder unlocks the strength already in you.
ramacharitamanas::4132.insight: It shifts you from self-doubt to decisive action by linking ability with purpose.

ramacharitamanas::4133.verse_sanskrit: कनक बरन तन तेज बिराजा। मानहुँ अपर गिरिन्ह कर राजा॥ सिंहनाद करि बारहिं बारा। लीलहिं नाघउँ जलनिधि खारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4133.verse_hindi: उनका सोने का सा रंग है, शरीर पर तेज सुशोभित है, मानो दूसरा पर्वतों का राजा सुमेरु हो। हनुमान् जी ने बार-बार सिंहनाद करके कहा- मैं इस खारे समुद्र को खेल में ही लाँघ सकता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4133.english_translation: His golden body shone with radiance, like another king of mountains. Roaring like a lion again and again, Hanuman declared, "I can leap across this salty sea as if it were play."
ramacharitamanas::4133.translation_literal: कनक बरन (golden-colored) / तन (body) / तेज (radiance) / बिराजा (shone) / मानहुँ (as if) / अपर (another) / गिरिन्ह (of mountains) / कर (of) / राजा (king) / सिंहनाद (lion's roar) / करि (doing) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / लीलहिं (playfully) / नाघउँ (I leap across) / जलनिधि (ocean) / खारा (salty)
ramacharitamanas::4133.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4133.essence: When your strength is remembered, the impossible becomes a game.
ramacharitamanas::4133.simple_meaning: Hanuman’s body shines like a mountain king, and he boldly declares that crossing the ocean is easy for him.
ramacharitamanas::4133.simple_insight: Real strength sounds calm when fear has already been mastered.
ramacharitamanas::4133.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Jambavan has just reminded Hanuman of his power and his purpose. Hanuman’s body blazes with renewed force, and he roars that the ocean is no obstacle. This verse shows the moment confidence becomes action.
ramacharitamanas::4133.modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a task that once felt impossible, and something in you finally wakes up. The fear is still there, but it no longer gets to speak first.
ramacharitamanas::4133.insight: It shifts you from hesitation to decisive confidence when the right reminder awakens your capacity.

ramacharitamanas::4134.verse_sanskrit: सहित सहाय रावनहि मारी। आनउँ इहाँ त्रिकूट उपारी॥ जामवंत मैं पूँछउँ तोही। उचित सिखावनु दीजहु मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4134.verse_hindi: और सहायकों सहित रावण को मारकर त्रिकूट पर्वत को उखाड़कर यहाँ ला सकता हूँ। हे जाम्बवान् ! मैं तुमसे पूछता हूँ, तुम मुझे उचित सीख देना (कि मुझे क्या करना चाहिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4134.english_translation: I can kill Ravana and his allies and bring Mount Trikuta here. O Jambavan, I ask you to guide me properly.
ramacharitamanas::4134.translation_literal: सहित (together with) / सहाय (helpers, allies) / रावनहि (Ravana) / मारी (killing) / आनउँ (I will bring) / इहाँ (here) / त्रिकूट (Trikuta) / उपारी (uprooted, lifted up) ॥ / जामवंत (Jambavan) / मैं (I) / पूँछउँ (ask) / तोही (you) / उचित (proper) / सिखावनु (instruction) / दीजहु (give) / मोही (to me) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4134.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4134.essence: Great power stays humble enough to ask for direction.
ramacharitamanas::4134.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he can defeat Ravana and even uproot a mountain, but he still asks Jambavan for proper guidance.
ramacharitamanas::4134.simple_insight: True strength still listens. Power becomes clean when it stays teachable.
ramacharitamanas::4134.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has already shown astonishing force. Even then, he does not rush ahead on pride. He tells Jambavan he can destroy Ravana and lift Trikuta, but he asks for the right instruction before moving.
ramacharitamanas::4134.modern_relevance: You finally solve the hard part of the project, then stop and ask the senior colleague to check your next move. Real confidence can still take correction.
ramacharitamanas::4134.insight: It teaches you to pair courage with guidance, so strength does not turn careless.

ramacharitamanas::4135.verse_sanskrit: एतना करहु तात तुम्ह जाई। सीतहि देखि कहहु सुधि आई॥ तब निज भुज बल राजिवनैना। कौतुक लागि संग कपि सेना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4135.verse_hindi: (जाम्बवान् ने कहा-) हे तात! तुम जाकर इतना ही करो कि सीताजी को देखकर लौट आओ और उनकी खबर कह दो। फिर कमलनयन श्री रामजी अपने बाहुबल से (ही राक्षसों का संहार कर सीताजी को ले आएँगे, केवल) खेल के लिए ही वे वानरों की सेना साथ लेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4135.english_translation: Go and do only this, dear one: see Sita and come back with news of her. Then lotus-eyed Ram, by his own strength, will destroy the demons and bring her back, taking the monkey army only for sport.
ramacharitamanas::4135.translation_literal: एतना (only this) / करहु (do) / तात (dear one) / तुम्ह (you) / जाई (going) / सीतहि (Sita) / देखि (seeing) / कहहु (say) / सुधि (news) / आई (coming) / तब (then) / निज (own) / भुज (arm) / बल (strength) / राजिवनैना (lotus-eyed one) / कौतुक (for sport) / लागि (for the sake of) / संग (with) / कपि (monkey) / सेना (army)
ramacharitamanas::4135.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4135.essence: Your task is small; Ram's work is vast.
ramacharitamanas::4135.simple_meaning: Jambavan tells Hanuman to go find Sita, see her, and return with news. Ram himself will then defeat the demons and rescue her.
ramacharitamanas::4135.simple_insight: You do not need to carry the whole victory. Do the next faithful thing, and let the larger power work.
ramacharitamanas::4135.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindhakand, Hanuman has just awakened to his strength and wants to leap into Lanka. Jambavan steadies him: go, find Sita, and come back with word. The rescue belongs to Ram; Hanuman's task is faithful contact.
ramacharitamanas::4135.modern_relevance: You finally get the courage to call the person you need to help. You do not have to solve everything in one breath — first make contact, then let the larger answer unfold.
ramacharitamanas::4135.insight: It shifts you from trying to control the whole outcome to completing the one faithful step in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::4136.verse_sanskrit: कपि सेन संग सँघारि निसिचर रामु सीतहि आनि हैं। त्रैलोक पावन सुजसु सुर मुनि नारदादि बखानि हैं॥ जो सुनत गावत कहत समुक्षत परमपद नर पावई। रघुबीर पद पाथोज मधुकर दास तुलसी गावई॥
ramacharitamanas::4136.verse_hindi: वानरों की सेना साथ लेकर राक्षसों का संहार करके श्री रामजी सीताजी को ले आएँगे। तब देवता और नारदादि मुनि भगवान् के तीनों लोकों को पवित्र करने वाले सुंदर यश का बखान करेंगे, जिसे सुनने, गाने, कहने और समझने से मनुष्य परमपद पाते हैं और जिसे श्री रघुवीर के चरणकमल का मधुकर (भ्रमर) तुलसीदास गाता है।
ramacharitamanas::4136.english_translation: With the monkey army, Ram will destroy the demons and bring Sita back. Then the gods, sages, and Narad will sing his pure fame that purifies the three worlds. Whoever hears, sings, speaks, or reflects on it attains the highest state; Tulsidas sings as a bee at the lotus feet of Raghuvir.
ramacharitamanas::4136.translation_literal: कपि सेन (monkey army) / संग (with) / सँघारि (destroying) / निसिचर (demons) / रामु (Ram) / सीतहि (Sita) / आनि हैं (will bring) / त्रैलोक (three worlds) / पावन (purifying) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / नारदादि (Narad and others) / बखानि हैं (will praise) / जो (who) / सुनत (hearing) / गावत (singing) / कहत (speaking) / समुक्षत (reflecting) / परमपद (highest state) / नर (person) / पावई (attains) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / पद पाथोज (lotus feet) / मधुकर (bee) / दास तुलसी (servant Tulsidas) / गावई (sings)
ramacharitamanas::4136.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4136.essence: Ram's fame purifies you just by being heard.
ramacharitamanas::4136.simple_meaning: Ram will defeat the demons, bring Sita back, and his fame will purify the three worlds. Hearing, singing, speaking, or reflecting on that fame leads a person to the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::4136.simple_insight: Devotion is not passive admiration — it changes what you become by letting sacred remembrance live in you.
ramacharitamanas::4136.detailed_meaning: Hanuman's mission is nearing its purpose: Ram will come with the monkey army, defeat Lanka's forces, and restore Sita. Tulsidas then turns from the rescue itself to Ram's fame, saying it purifies the worlds and lifts anyone who hears it.
ramacharitamanas::4136.modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone who stayed faithful through loss, and it steadies you more than advice ever could. Some names carry enough purity to reorient a whole heart.
ramacharitamanas::4136.insight: It shifts attention from the event to the sacred remembrance behind the event, treating praise itself as transformative practice.

ramacharitamanas::4137.verse_sanskrit: भव भेषज रघुनाथ जसु सुनहिं जे नर अरु नारि। तिन्ह कर सकल मनोरथ सिद्ध करहिं त्रिसिरारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4137.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीर का यश भव (जन्म-मरण) रूपी रोग की (अचूक) दवा है। जो पुरुष और स्त्री इसे सुनेंगे, त्रिशिरा के शत्रु श्री रामजी उनके सब मनोरथों को सिद्ध करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4137.english_translation: The glory of Raghunath is the cure for the cycle of birth and death. Men and women who hear it have all their wishes fulfilled by Ram, the destroyer of the three-headed demon.
ramacharitamanas::4137.translation_literal: भव (cycle of birth and death) / भेषज (medicine) / रघुनाथ (Lord Ram) / जसु (glory) / सुनहिं (hear) / जे (who) / नर (men) / अरु (and) / नारि (women) / तिन्ह (their) / कर (of) / सकल (all) / मनोरथ (wishes) / सिद्ध (fulfilled) / करहिं (will make) / त्रिसिरारि (Ram, enemy of the three-headed demon)
ramacharitamanas::4137.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4137.essence: Ram's glory heals the restless cycle and fulfills sincere longing.
ramacharitamanas::4137.simple_meaning: Hearing Ram's praise is said to heal the pain of repeated birth and death, and to fulfill the wishes of anyone who listens with faith.
ramacharitamanas::4137.simple_insight: You do not have to force everything; deep listening can change what effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4137.detailed_meaning: As Hanuman's mission in Lanka nears its turning point, Tulsidas steps back from the battle and sings the power of Ram's fame itself. In this bhakti-filled couplet, hearing Ram's glory becomes both healing and blessing for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::4137.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after months of trying to fix everything yourself. Then one song, one prayer, one line of truth lands differently — and something in you loosens before you even understand why.
ramacharitamanas::4137.insight: It shifts attention from control to receptive listening, showing that devotion can heal and complete what striving cannot.

ramacharitamanas::4138.verse_sanskrit: नीलोत्पल तन स्याम काम कोटि सोभा अधिक। सुनिअ तासु गुन ग्राम जासु नाम अघ खग बधिक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4138.verse_hindi: जिनका नीले कमल के समान श्याम शरीर है, जिनकी शोभा करोड़ों कामदेवों से भी अधिक है और जिनका नाम पापरूपी पक्षियों को मारने के लिए बधिक (व्याधा) के समान है, उन श्री राम के गुणों के समूह (लीला) को अवश्य सुनना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4138.english_translation: His body is dark like a blue lotus, his beauty surpasses millions of Cupids, and his name is like a hunter that kills the birds of sin. You should listen to the many virtues of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4138.translation_literal: नीलोत्पल (blue lotus) / तन (body) / स्याम (dark) / काम (desire) / कोटि (crore / millions) / सोभा (beauty) / अधिक (greater) / सुनिअ (should be heard) / तासु (his) / गुन (virtues) / ग्राम (group / cluster) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / अघ (sins) / खग (birds) / बधिक (hunter)
ramacharitamanas::4138.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4138.essence: Ram's name does what desire and effort cannot: it clears the stain.
ramacharitamanas::4138.simple_meaning: Ram is unimaginably beautiful, and even his name has the power to destroy inner wrongs. The verse urges you to listen to his qualities with attention.
ramacharitamanas::4138.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that remembrance can cleanse what effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4138.detailed_meaning: At the end of a praise-filled passage in Kishkindhakand, Tulsidas turns from promise to praise. He describes Ram's dark, lotus-like beauty and says that even Ram's name destroys the stains that burden people. The verse crowns the hymn by urging listeners to drink in Ram's qualities.
ramacharitamanas::4138.modern_relevance: You are scrolling past a hundred noisy voices, and one name still stops you. Some words don't just inform you — they purify the mood you were carrying.
ramacharitamanas::4138.insight: It shifts attention from Ram's outward beauty to the cleansing power of remembering his name.

ramacharitamanas::4139.verse_sanskrit: शान्तं शाश्वतमप्रमेयमनघं निर्वाणशान्तिप्रदं ब्रह्माशम्भुफणीन्द्रसेव्यमनिशं वेदान्तवेद्यं विभुम् । रामाख्यं जगदीश्वरं सुरगुरुं मायामनुष्यं हरिं वन्देऽहं करुणाकरं रघुवरं भूपालचूडामणिम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::4139.verse_hindi: शान्त, सनातन, अप्रमेय (प्रमाणों से परे), निष्पाप, मोक्षरूप परमशान्ति देने वाले, ब्रह्मा, शम्भु और शेषजी से निरंतर सेवित, वेदान्त के द्वारा जानने योग्य, सर्वव्यापक, देवताओं में सबसे बड़े, माया से मनुष्य रूप में दिखने वाले, समस्त पापों को हरने वाले, करुणा की खान, रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ तथा राजाओं के शिरोमणि राम कहलाने वाले जगदीश्वर की मैं वंदना करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4139.english_translation: I bow to Ram, the peaceful, eternal, immeasurable, stainless, giver of freedom and deep stillness, ever served by Brahma, Shiva, and Shesha, known through the end of the Vedas, all-pervading, lord of the world, teacher of the gods, appearing as a human through his own power, remover of suffering, full of compassion, best of the Raghu line, and crown jewel of kings.
ramacharitamanas::4139.translation_literal: शान्तं (peaceful) / शाश्वतम् (eternal) / अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable) / अनघम् (stainless) / निर्वाणशान्तिप्रदम् (giver of freedom and peace) / ब्रह्माशम्भुफणीन्द्रसेव्यम् (served by Brahma, Shiva, and Shesha) / अनिशम् (constantly) / वेदान्तवेद्यम् (known through the Vedas' end) / विभुम् (all-pervading) / रामाख्यम् (named Ram) / जगदीश्वरम् (lord of the world) / सुरगुरुम् (teacher of the gods) / मायामनुष्यम् (human by his own power) / हरिम् (Hari) / वन्देऽहम् (I bow) / करुणाकरम् (ocean of compassion) / रघुवरम् (best of the Raghu line) / भूपालचूडामणिम् (crown jewel of kings)
ramacharitamanas::4139.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4139.essence: Ram is beyond measure, yet close enough to receive your bow.
ramacharitamanas::4139.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as peaceful, eternal, beyond measurement, pure, and full of compassion. He is the supreme ruler who appears in human form and is worthy of worship.
ramacharitamanas::4139.simple_insight: Reverence grows when greatness feels both vast and intimate.
ramacharitamanas::4139.detailed_meaning: At the opening of Sundarkand, Tulsidas offers a full hymn to Ram before Hanuman's mission begins. He gathers Ram's cosmic greatness, human form, compassion, and kingship into one praise, setting a devotional mood for the search ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4139.modern_relevance: Before a hard meeting, you may feel small and overmatched. This verse reminds you that what is highest can still feel near, personal, and worthy of trust.
ramacharitamanas::4139.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing power as distant to seeing it as compassionate and approachable.

ramacharitamanas::4140.verse_sanskrit: नान्या स्पृहा रघुपते हृदयेऽस्मदीये सत्यं वदामि च भवानखिलान्तरात्मा। भक्तिं प्रयच्छ रघुपुंगव निर्भरां मे कामादिदोषरहितं कुरु मानसं च ॥
ramacharitamanas::4140.verse_hindi: हे रघुनाथजी! मैं सत्य कहता हूँ और फिर आप सबके अंतरात्मा ही हैं (सब जानते ही हैं) कि मेरे हृदय में दूसरी कोई इच्छा नहीं है। हे रघुकुलश्रेष्ठ! मुझे अपनी निर्भरा (पूर्ण) भक्ति दीजिए और मेरे मन को काम आदि दोषों से रहित कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4140.english_translation: O Lord of the Raghu line, I speak truth: there is no other desire in my heart. You are the inner witness of everything. Grant me unwavering devotion and make my mind free of desire and fault.
ramacharitamanas::4140.translation_literal: नान्या (no other) / स्पृहा (desire) / रघुपते (O Lord of the Raghu line) / हृदये (in the heart) / अस्मदीये (of mine) / सत्यं (truth) / वदामि (I speak) / च (and) / भवान् (You) / अखिल-अन्तरात्मा (inner self of all) / भक्तिं (devotion) / प्रयच्छ (grant) / रघुपुंगव (O best of the Raghu line) / निर्भरां (complete, unwavering) / मे (to me) / काम-आदि-दोष-रहितं (free from desire and other faults) / कुरु (make) / मानसं (mind) / च (and)
ramacharitamanas::4140.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4140.essence: Full devotion leaves no room for private desire.
ramacharitamanas::4140.simple_meaning: The speaker tells Ram that there is no other desire in the heart, asks for complete devotion, and asks for a mind freed from desire and flaw.
ramacharitamanas::4140.simple_insight: Real devotion is not mixed with secret wanting; it feels clean, complete, and inwardly free.
ramacharitamanas::4140.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is preparing to serve Ram in Lanka. Before action begins, he prays for a heart with no divided motive. This verse turns the mission into surrender: only devotion, no craving, no hidden agenda.
ramacharitamanas::4140.modern_relevance: Before sending that text, you check your own motive: are you helping, or hoping to be noticed? This verse asks for cleaner reasons and a quieter mind.
ramacharitamanas::4140.insight: It shifts attention from mixed motives to wholehearted devotion, and from self-interest to inner cleanliness.

ramacharitamanas::4141.verse_sanskrit: अतुलितबलधामं हेमशैलाभदेहं दनुजवनकृशानुं ज्ञानिनामग्रगण्यम् । सकलगुणनिधानं वानराणामधीशं रघुपतिप्रियभक्तं वातजातं नमामि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4141.verse_hindi: अतुल बल के धाम, सोने के पर्वत (सुमेरु) के समान कान्तियुक्त शरीर वाले, दैत्य रूपी वन (को ध्वंस करने) के लिए अग्नि रूप, ज्ञानियों में अग्रगण्य, संपूर्ण गुणों के निधान, वानरों के स्वामी, श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रिय भक्त पवनपुत्र श्री हनुमान् जी को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4141.english_translation: I bow to Hanuman, the son of the Wind, whose strength is unmatched, whose body shines like a golden mountain, who is the fire that burns the forest of demons, foremost among the wise, a treasury of all virtues, lord of the monkeys, and the beloved devotee of Raghupati.
ramacharitamanas::4141.translation_literal: अतुलितबलधामं (abode of unmatched strength) / हेमशैलाभदेहं (body like a golden mountain) / दनुजवनकृशानुं (fire for the forest of demons) / ज्ञानिनामग्रगण्यम् (foremost among the wise) / सकलगुणनिधानं (treasury of all virtues) / वानराणामधीशं (lord of the monkeys) / रघुपतिप्रियभक्तं (beloved devotee of Raghupati) / वातजातं (born of the wind) / नमामि (I bow)
ramacharitamanas::4141.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4141.essence: True greatness shines through devoted service.
ramacharitamanas::4141.simple_meaning: Hanuman is praised as unmatched in strength, wisdom, virtue, and service to Ram. He is not just powerful; his greatness comes from devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4141.simple_insight: There is dignity in serving something greater than your own pride.
ramacharitamanas::4141.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, the search for Sita is about to move forward through Hanuman. Before the action begins, Tulsidas pauses to bow to him: the fearless servant of Ram, brilliant, virtuous, and immense in power, yet defined by devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4141.modern_relevance: You see someone handle impossible pressure without bragging, without panic, and without needing credit. That calm force is what Hanuman embodies.
ramacharitamanas::4141.insight: It teaches you to measure greatness by service, not self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::4142.verse_sanskrit: जामवंत के बचन सुहाए। सुनि हनुमंत हृदय अति भाए॥ तब लगि मोहि परिखेहु तुम्ह भाई। सहि दुख कंद मूल फल खाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4142.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् के सुंदर वचन सुनकर हनुमान् जी के हृदय को बहुत ही भाए। (वे बोले-) हे भाई! तुम लोग दुःख सहकर, कन्द-मूल-फल खाकर तब तक मेरी राह देखना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4142.english_translation: Jambavan’s gentle words pleased Hanuman deeply. Hanuman said, “Until then, my brothers, endure the hardship and wait for me, eating roots, bulbs, and fruits.”
ramacharitamanas::4142.translation_literal: जामवंत (Jambavan) / के (of) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (pleasant) / सुनि (hearing) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / हृदय (heart) / अति (very) / भाए (were pleasing) / तब (then) / लगि (until) / मोहि (me) / परिखेहु (test) / तुम्ह (you all) / भाई (brothers) / सहि (bearing) / दुख (sorrow) / कंद (roots) / मूल (bulbs) / फल (fruits) / खाई (eat)
ramacharitamanas::4142.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4142.essence: Love keeps moving while others wait in faith.
ramacharitamanas::4142.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks his companions to wait and endure hardship while he goes ahead to find Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4142.simple_insight: Real devotion includes letting others wait on your courage, without losing faith in the return.
ramacharitamanas::4142.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just been encouraged by Jambavan. He turns to the other vanaras and asks them to stay behind, live simply, and wait through hardship while he goes on the decisive search for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4142.modern_relevance: You leave your friends behind at the train station before a difficult trip, asking them to trust you and hold the line until you return with news. That’s the steadiness in Hanuman’s words.
ramacharitamanas::4142.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to carrying responsibility for others’ hope.

ramacharitamanas::4143.verse_sanskrit: जब लगि आवौं सीतहि देखी। होइहि काजु मोहि हरष बिसेषी॥ यह कहि नाइ सबन्हि कहुँ माथा । चलेउ हरषि हियँ धरि रघुनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4143.verse_hindi: जब तक मैं सीताजी को देखकर (लौट) न आऊँ। काम अवश्य होगा, क्योंकि मुझे बहुत ही हर्ष हो रहा है। यह कहकर और सबको मस्तक नवाकर तथा हृदय में श्री रघुनाथजी को धारण करके हनुमान् जी हर्षित होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4143.english_translation: Until I return after seeing Sita, the task will surely succeed, and I feel great joy. Saying this, bowing to everyone, and holding Ram in his heart, Hanuman departed in delight.
ramacharitamanas::4143.translation_literal: जब लगि (until) / आवौं (I return) / सीतहि (Sita) / देखी (having seen) / होइहि (will happen) / काजु (task) / मोहि (for me) / हरष (joy) / बिसेषी (special, great) ॥ / यह (this) / कहि (saying) / नाइ (bowing) / सबन्हि (to everyone) / कहुँ (to) / माथा (head) । / चलेउ (went) / हरषि (joyfully) / हियँ (in heart) / धरि (holding) / रघुनाथा (Ram) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4143.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4143.essence: Remembering Ram turns a hard mission into joyful certainty.
ramacharitamanas::4143.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he will not rest until he sees Sita, and he feels certain the mission will succeed. He bows to everyone and leaves with Ram in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4143.simple_insight: When your heart is fixed on the right purpose, courage feels lighter.
ramacharitamanas::4143.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has received encouragement and now turns fully toward the search for Sita. He promises to return only after finding her, bows to the others, and sets off with Ram held in his heart. Faith has become motion.
ramacharitamanas::4143.modern_relevance: You leave a difficult conversation, breathe once in the hallway, and remind yourself why you came. The fear is still there, but something steadier is walking with you.
ramacharitamanas::4143.insight: It shifts action from anxious effort to joyful resolve rooted in remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::4144.verse_sanskrit: सिंधु तीर एक भूधर सुंदर। कौतुक कूदि चढ़ेउ ता ऊपर॥ बार-बार रघुबीर सँभारी। तरकेउ पवनतनय बल भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4144.verse_hindi: समुद्र के तीर पर एक सुंदर पर्वत था। हनुमान् जी खेल से ही (अनायास ही) कूदकर उसके ऊपर जा चढ़े और बार-बार श्री रघुवीर का स्मरण करके अत्यंत बलवान् हनुमान् जी उस पर से बड़े वेग से उछले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4144.english_translation: On the seashore stood a beautiful mountain. Hanuman leapt up playfully and climbed it. Recalling Raghubir again and again, the son of the wind sprang onward with immense force.
ramacharitamanas::4144.translation_literal: सिंधु (sea) / तीर (shore) / एक (one) / भूधर (mountain) / सुंदर (beautiful) / कौतुक (playfully) / कूदि (leaping) / चढ़ेउ (climbed) / ता (that) / ऊपर (on top) / बार-बार (again and again) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सँभारी (remembering) / तरकेउ (sprang across) / पवनतनय (son of the wind) / बल (strength) / भारी (great)
ramacharitamanas::4144.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4144.essence: Remembering Ram turns impossible distance into a single leap.
ramacharitamanas::4144.simple_meaning: Hanuman reaches a mountain by the sea, leaps onto it, and launches forward by remembering Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4144.simple_insight: Real strength rises when your mind stays with what you love.
ramacharitamanas::4144.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just accepted the mission to find Sita in Lanka. At the seashore, he treats a mountain like a stepping-stone, then pushes onward by holding Ram in mind. The scene shows momentum, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::4144.modern_relevance: You grab your bag, take one deep breath, and step into the hard conversation. The body moves first; courage follows the name you keep close.
ramacharitamanas::4144.insight: It shows devotion as fuel for action, not a separate feeling.

ramacharitamanas::4145.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं गिरि चरन देइ हनुमंता। चलेउ सो गा पाताल तुरंता॥ जिमि अमोघ रघुपति कर बाना। एही भाँति चलेउ हनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4145.verse_hindi: जिस पर्वत पर हनुमान् जी पैर रखकर चले (जिस पर से वे उछले), वह तुरंत ही पाताल में धँस गया। जैसे श्री रघुनाथजी का अमोघ बाण चलता है, उसी तरह हनुमान् जी चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4145.english_translation: The mountain sank into the underworld the moment Hanuman stepped on it. Hanuman moved like an unfailing arrow of Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::4145.translation_literal: जेहिं (on which) / गिरि (mountain) / चरन (foot) / देइ (having placed) / हनुमंता (Hanuman) / चलेउ (moved) / सो (that) / गा (went) / पाताल (underworld) / तुरंता (immediately)॥ / जिमि (like) / अमोघ (unfailing) / रघुपति (Raghupati's) / कर (hand) / बाना (arrow) / एही भाँति (in this way) / चलेउ (moved) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4145.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4145.essence: True force moves straight through resistance.
ramacharitamanas::4145.simple_meaning: Hanuman’s weight and force are so great that the mountain sinks when he pushes off from it. His movement is compared to Ram’s unstoppable arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4145.simple_insight: Real power moves cleanly and leaves no hesitation behind.
ramacharitamanas::4145.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has launched himself from the mountain and is now crossing toward Lanka. The hill cannot bear the force of his leap and sinks away. Tulsidas compares that motion to Ram’s unstoppable arrow, making Hanuman’s speed feel sacred and inevitable.
ramacharitamanas::4145.modern_relevance: You leave a meeting, and the decision is already made in your body. No second-guessing, no backtracking — just clean movement toward what you came to do.
ramacharitamanas::4145.insight: It turns raw momentum into a sign of complete alignment with purpose.

ramacharitamanas::4146.verse_sanskrit: जलनिधि रघुपति दूत बिचारी। तैं मैनाक होहि श्रम हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4146.verse_hindi: समुद्र ने उन्हें श्री रघुनाथजी का दूत समझकर मैनाक पर्वत से कहा कि हे मैनाक! तू इनकी थकावट दूर करने वाला हो (अर्थात् अपने ऊपर इन्हें विश्राम दे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4146.english_translation: Seeing him as the messenger of Raghupati, the ocean told Mainaka, “O Mainaka, become the one who relieves his fatigue.”
ramacharitamanas::4146.translation_literal: जलनिधि (the ocean) / रघुपति (Raghupati, Lord Ram) / दूत (messenger) / बिचारी (having considered) / तैं (you) / मैनाक (Mainaka) / होहि (become) / श्रम (fatigue) / हारी (remover)
ramacharitamanas::4146.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4146.essence: True service moves creation itself to help you.
ramacharitamanas::4146.simple_meaning: The ocean recognizes Hanuman as Ram’s messenger and asks Mainaka to give him a place to rest.
ramacharitamanas::4146.simple_insight: Even the world pauses to support sincere service.
ramacharitamanas::4146.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is crossing the ocean on Ram's mission. The sea notices his purpose and offers help through Mainaka, a mountain rising to receive him. It is a small pause in the larger journey, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::4146.modern_relevance: You are racing from one responsibility to the next, and a friend quietly opens the door, brings water, and says, “Sit for a minute.”
ramacharitamanas::4146.insight: It shows how a worthy mission can attract unexpected support, even from the world around you.

ramacharitamanas::4147.verse_sanskrit: हनूमान तेहि परसा कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम। राम काजु कीन्हें बिनु मोहि कहाँ बिश्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4147.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने उसे हाथ से छू दिया, फिर प्रणाम करके कहा- भाई! श्री रामचंद्रजी का काम किए बिना मुझे विश्राम कहाँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4147.english_translation: Hanuman touched him, then bowed again and said, "Brother, how can I rest before completing Ram's work?"
ramacharitamanas::4147.translation_literal: हनूमान (Hanuman) / तेहि (him) / परसा (touched) / कर (hand) / पुनि (again) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनाम (bowed) / राम काजु (Ram's work) / कीन्हें (having done) / बिनु (without) / मोहि (me) / कहाँ (where) / बिश्राम (rest)
ramacharitamanas::4147.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4147.essence: Devotion makes rest impossible until the beloved's work is complete.
ramacharitamanas::4147.simple_meaning: Hanuman shows complete devotion: even after being honored, he says he cannot rest until Ram's task is finished.
ramacharitamanas::4147.simple_insight: True devotion keeps you moving without needing comfort or applause.
ramacharitamanas::4147.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just leapt across the ocean and accepted a brief touch of respect from the mountain he spared. Even then, he bows again. In Lanka's approach, his mind stays fixed on Ram's task alone.
ramacharitamanas::4147.modern_relevance: You finish helping a friend move, and they offer tea, a chair, a break. You smile, but your mind is still on the boxes left in the truck. Hanuman knows that feeling of service before comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4147.insight: It shifts attention from personal ease to wholehearted service.

ramacharitamanas::4148.verse_sanskrit: जात पवनसुत देवन्ह देखा। जानैं कहुँ बल बुद्धि बिसेषा॥ सुरसा नाम अहिन्ह कै माता। पठइन्हि आइ कही तेहिं बाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4148.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी को जाते हुए देखा। उनकी विशेष बल-बुद्धि को जानने के लिए (परीक्षार्थ) उन्होंने सुरसा नामक सर्पों की माता को भेजा, उसने आकर हनुमान् जी से यह बात कही- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4148.english_translation: As Hanuman, son of the wind, was seen passing by, the devas wanted to test his exceptional strength and intelligence. So they sent Surasa, mother of the serpents, who came and spoke to him.
ramacharitamanas::4148.translation_literal: जात (going) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / देवन्ह (by the devas) / देखा (seen) / जानैं (to know) / कहुँ (for) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (intelligence) / बिसेषा (special) / सुरसा (Surasa) / नाम (named) / अहिन्ह (of serpents) / कै (of) / माता (mother) / पठइन्हि (they sent) / आइ (coming) / कही (said) / तेहिं (to him) / बाता (the words)
ramacharitamanas::4148.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4148.essence: Before a great task opens, a test often appears first.
ramacharitamanas::4148.simple_meaning: The devas notice Hanuman's extraordinary strength and intelligence, so they send Surasa to test him.
ramacharitamanas::4148.simple_insight: Great capacity often meets a test before it meets success.
ramacharitamanas::4148.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is on his leap toward Lanka, moving with unstoppable purpose. The devas watch his passing and decide to test the power and intelligence within him, so Surasa is sent to confront him. This verse sets up the trial, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4148.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to prove yourself, and the first thing you meet is a test you did not choose.
ramacharitamanas::4148.insight: It frames success as something that invites examination, not applause.

ramacharitamanas::4149.verse_sanskrit: आजु सुरन्ह मोहि दीन्ह अहारा। सुनत बचन कह पवनकुमारा॥ राम काजु करि फिरि मैं आवौं। सीता कइ सुधि प्रभुहि सुनावौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4149.verse_hindi: आज देवताओं ने मुझे भोजन दिया है। यह वचन सुनकर पवनकुमार हनुमान् जी ने कहा- श्री रामजी का कार्य करके मैं लौट आऊँ और सीताजी की खबर प्रभु को सुना दूँ, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4149.english_translation: The gods have given me food today. Hearing this, Hanuman said, 'I will return only after finishing Ram's work, and I will tell the Lord news of Sita.'
ramacharitamanas::4149.translation_literal: आजु (today) / सुरन्ह (by the gods) / मोहि (to me) / दीन्ह (given) / अहारा (food) । / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (the words) / कह (said) / पवनकुमारा (son of the wind) ॥ / राम काजु (Ram's work) / करि (doing) / फिरि (returning) / मैं (I) / आवौं (will come) । / सीता कइ (of Sita) / सुधि (news) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / सुनावौं (I will tell) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4149.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4149.essence: Devotion keeps moving until the work is complete.
ramacharitamanas::4149.simple_meaning: Hanuman refuses to stop for food or comfort. He will return only after completing Ram's task and bringing Sita's news back.
ramacharitamanas::4149.simple_insight: Single-minded service can be stronger than hunger, fear, or comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4149.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is being tested while racing to find Sita. Even when Surasa blocks him, he stays fixed on one aim: finish Ram's work, then report back. This verse shows bhakti as total focus.
ramacharitamanas::4149.modern_relevance: You are halfway through helping a friend move when someone offers snacks and a break. You can pause, but part of you knows the real relief comes after the job is finished.
ramacharitamanas::4149.insight: It shifts attention from personal comfort to faithful completion of the task in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::4150.verse_sanskrit: तब तव बदन पैठिहउँ आई। सत्य कहउँ मोहि जान दे माई॥ कवनेहुँ जतन देइ नहिं जाना। ग्रससि न मोहि कहेउ हनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4150.verse_hindi: तब मैं आकर तुम्हारे मुँह में घुस जाऊँगा (तुम मुझे खा लेना)। हे माता! मैं सत्य कहता हूँ, अभी मुझे जाने दे। जब किसी भी उपाय से उसने जाने नहीं दिया, तब हनुमान् जी ने कहा- तो फिर मुझे खा न ले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4150.english_translation: Then I will enter your mouth and come through. I speak the truth, Mother, let me go. When no other way worked, Hanuman said, 'Then eat me if you must.'
ramacharitamanas::4150.translation_literal: तब (then) / तव (your) / बदन (mouth) / पैठिहउँ (I will enter) / आई (coming) / सत्य (truth) / कहउँ (I speak) / मोहि (me) / जान दे (let go) / माई (mother) / कवनेहुँ (by any) / जतन (means/effort) / देइ (giving) / नहिं (not) / जाना (she knew/allowed) / ग्रससि (you swallow) / न (not) / मोहि (me) / कहेउ (said) / हनुमाना (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4150.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4150.essence: Real resolve keeps moving when every normal route is closed.
ramacharitamanas::4150.simple_meaning: Hanuman refuses to be stopped. If the guardian will not let him pass, he is ready to go straight through her mouth to continue his mission.
ramacharitamanas::4150.simple_insight: Obstacles do not end commitment; they reveal how determined you are.
ramacharitamanas::4150.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is being tested by Surasa, the mother of serpents. She blocks his path and will not release him. He answers with fearless creativity: if she will not let him go, he will enter her mouth and still continue toward Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4150.modern_relevance: You are at the airport gate, your documents are wrong, and the line is closing. Instead of collapsing, you start looking for the next workable move. That is Hanuman’s energy.
ramacharitamanas::4150.insight: It teaches you to treat resistance as a problem to route around, not a reason to stop.

ramacharitamanas::4151.verse_sanskrit: जोजन भरि तेहिं बदनु पसारा। कपि तनु कीन्ह दुगुन बिस्तारा ॥ सोरह जोजन मुख तेहिं ठयऊ। तुरत पवनसुत बत्तिस भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4151.verse_hindi: उसने योजनभर (चार कोस में) मुँह फैलाया। तब हनुमान् जी ने अपने शरीर को उससे दूना बढ़ा लिया। उसने सोलह योजन का मुख किया। हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही बत्तीस योजन के हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4151.english_translation: She spread her mouth to a span of one yojana. Hanuman doubled his body. She made her mouth sixteen yojanas wide. At once, the Son of Wind became thirty-two yojanas tall.
ramacharitamanas::4151.translation_literal: जोजन भरि (one yojana in extent) / तेहिं (then she) / बदनु (mouth) / पसारा (spread) / कपि (monkey) / तनु (body) / कीन्ह (made) / दुगुन (double) / बिस्तारा (expansion) / सोरह (sixteen) / जोजन (yojanas) / मुख (mouth) / तेहिं (then she) / ठयऊ (made) / तुरत (immediately) / पवनसुत (Son of Wind) / बत्तिस (thirty-two) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::4151.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4151.essence: Real strength grows to meet resistance without panic.
ramacharitamanas::4151.simple_meaning: Surasa keeps enlarging her mouth, and Hanuman keeps doubling his size to match her challenge.
ramacharitamanas::4151.simple_insight: Some obstacles are answered not by fear, but by meeting them with greater force and flexibility.
ramacharitamanas::4151.detailed_meaning: On the ocean crossing to Lanka, Hanuman meets Surasa, who tests him by opening her mouth wider and wider. He responds by expanding his body again and again, showing quick intelligence and fearless adaptability before moving on.
ramacharitamanas::4151.modern_relevance: A problem keeps getting bigger while you stand there in the middle of it — the deadline, the bill, the conversation. You don't freeze; you adjust fast and stay larger than the obstacle.
ramacharitamanas::4151.insight: It trains the mind to respond dynamically to resistance instead of shrinking before it.

ramacharitamanas::4152.verse_sanskrit: जस जस सुरसा बदनु बढ़ावा। तासु दून कपि रूप देखावा॥ सत जोजन तेहिं आनन कीन्हा। अति लघु रूप पवनसुत लीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4152.verse_hindi: जैसे-जैसे सुरसा मुख का विस्तार बढ़ाती थी, हनुमान् जी उसका दूना रूप दिखलाते थे। उसने सौ योजन (चार सौ कोस का) मुख किया। तब हनुमान् जी ने बहुत ही छोटा रूप धारण कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4152.english_translation: As Surasa kept widening her mouth, Hanuman showed a form twice as large. When she made her mouth one hundred yojanas wide, the son of the wind took a very small form.
ramacharitamanas::4152.translation_literal: जस (as) / जस (as) / सुरसा (Surasa) / बदनु (mouth) / बढ़ावा (kept widening) / तासु (her) / दून (double) / कपि (monkey) / रूप (form) / देखावा (showed)॥ / सत (one hundred) / जोजन (yojanas) / तेहिं (she) / आनन (mouth) / कीन्हा (made) / अति (very) / लघु (small) / रूप (form) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / लीन्हा (took)
ramacharitamanas::4152.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4152.essence: Real strength knows when to expand and when to shrink.
ramacharitamanas::4152.simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps adjusting his size to match Surasa's challenge. He first grows larger, then becomes tiny when she opens her mouth huge.
ramacharitamanas::4152.simple_insight: Flexibility can be a form of strength when force alone would fail.
ramacharitamanas::4152.detailed_meaning: On the way to Lanka, Hanuman faces Surasa, a test sent by the divine powers guarding the sea route. She keeps changing the size of her mouth, and Hanuman answers by changing his form again and again, showing quick intelligence under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::4152.modern_relevance: A tense conversation is going nowhere until you stop pushing the same point and change your approach. Sometimes the smartest move is to adapt instantly.
ramacharitamanas::4152.insight: It teaches you to meet resistance with agility instead of stubborn force.

ramacharitamanas::4153.verse_sanskrit: बदन पइठि पुनि बाहेर आवा। मागा बिदा ताहि सिरु नावा॥ मोहि सुरन्ह जेहि लागि पठावा। बुधि बल मरमु तोर मैं पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4153.verse_hindi: और उसके मुख में घुसकर (तुरंत) फिर बाहर निकल आए और उसे सिर नवाकर विदा माँगने लगे। (उसने कहा-) मैंने तुम्हारे बुद्धि-बल का भेद पा लिया, जिसके लिए देवताओं ने मुझे भेजा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4153.english_translation: He entered her mouth and came back out at once, then bowed and asked leave. She said, "I have understood the secret of your intelligence and strength—the reason the devas sent me to test you."
ramacharitamanas::4153.translation_literal: बदन (mouth) / पइठि (entering) / पुनि (again) / बाहेर (outside) / आवा (came) / मागा (asked) / बिदा (leave) / ताहि (to her) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / मोहि (me) / सुरन्ह (by the devas) / जेहि (for which) / लागि (for the sake of) / पठावा (sent) / बुधि (intelligence) / बल (strength) / मरमु (secret) / तोर (your) / मैं (I) / पावा (have found)
ramacharitamanas::4153.speaker: Surasa
ramacharitamanas::4153.simple_meaning: Hanuman passes Surasa's test, then respectfully asks permission to leave. Surasa recognises that his intelligence and strength are extraordinary and that the devas sent her to test him.
ramacharitamanas::4153.simple_insight: Real strength can be quiet, respectful, and still completely unshaken.
ramacharitamanas::4153.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's sky, Surasa blocks Hanuman's path and tests him by opening her mouth wide. He outwits the test without arrogance, bows, and asks leave. She then names the hidden force behind him: a mind guided by strength and purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4153.modern_relevance: You handled a difficult conversation without raising your voice, then left with grace. The other person may still disagree, but they can feel the steadiness in you.
ramacharitamanas::4153.insight: It shows that true power does not need to dominate; it can pass through challenge with composure and courtesy.

ramacharitamanas::4154.verse_sanskrit: राम काजु सबु करिहहु तुम्ह बल बुद्धि निधान। आसिष देइ गई सो हरषि चलेउ हनुमान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4154.verse_hindi: तुम श्री रामचंद्रजी का सब कार्य करोगे, क्योंकि तुम बल-बुद्धि के भंडार हो। यह आशीर्वाद देकर वह चली गई, तब हनुमान् जी हर्षित होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4154.english_translation: You will accomplish all of Ram's work, for you are a treasury of strength and wisdom. Giving this blessing, she left, and Hanuman went on joyfully.
ramacharitamanas::4154.translation_literal: राम (Ram's) / काजु (work) / सबु (all) / करिहहु (you will do) / तुम्ह (you) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (wisdom) / निधान (treasury) / आसिष (blessing) / देइ (giving) / गई (went) / सो (she) / हरषि (joyfully) / चलेउ (went) / हनुमान (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4154.speaker: Surasa
ramacharitamanas::4154.essence: When your strength serves Ram's work, even obstacles become blessings.
ramacharitamanas::4154.simple_meaning: Surasa blesses Hanuman and recognizes that he has the strength and wisdom to complete Ram's mission.
ramacharitamanas::4154.simple_insight: Real confidence comes from knowing your abilities are in service of something greater.
ramacharitamanas::4154.detailed_meaning: After testing Hanuman by enlarging her mouth, Surasa finally bows to his skill. She blesses him, calling him a storehouse of strength and wisdom. Hanuman leaves delighted, ready for the next challenge on the road to Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4154.modern_relevance: A senior colleague sees your work under pressure and says, quietly, that you can handle the whole project. That recognition steadies you more than praise ever could.
ramacharitamanas::4154.insight: It shifts your focus from self-doubt to capable service.

ramacharitamanas::4155.verse_sanskrit: निसिचरि एक सिंधु महुँ रहई। करि माया नभु के खग गहई॥ जीव जंतु जे गगन उड़ाहीं। जल बिलोकि तिन्ह कै परिछाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4155.verse_hindi: समुद्र में एक राक्षसी रहती थी। वह माया करके आकाश में उड़ते हुए पक्षियों को पकड़ लेती थी। आकाश में जो जीव-जंतु उड़ा करते थे, वह जल में उनकी परछाईं देखकर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4155.english_translation: A demoness lived in the ocean. Using illusion, she caught birds flying in the sky. Any creature that flew above, she spotted by its reflection in the water.
ramacharitamanas::4155.translation_literal: निसिचरि (demoness) / एक (one) / सिंधु (ocean) / महुँ (in) / रहई (lived) / करि (doing) / माया (illusion) / नभु (sky) / के (of) / खग (birds) / गहई (caught) / जीव (living beings) / जंतु (creatures) / जे (who) / गगन (sky) / उड़ाहीं (flew) / जल (water) / बिलोकि (seeing) / तिन्ह (their) / कै (of) / परिछाहीं (reflections)
ramacharitamanas::4155.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4155.essence: Hidden traps watch for the slightest sign of movement.
ramacharitamanas::4155.simple_meaning: A sea-dwelling demoness uses illusion to trap flying creatures by spotting their reflections in the water.
ramacharitamanas::4155.simple_insight: Deception often works by watching for the smallest trace of movement.
ramacharitamanas::4155.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's waters, Hanuman is moving through enemy territory. Tulsidas pauses to describe a demoness who catches flying creatures by first noticing their reflection in the sea. The scene sets up the trap Hanuman is about to face.
ramacharitamanas::4155.modern_relevance: A scammer watches the faintest reply time on your phone and knows you're interested. The danger is not the trap itself, but how carefully it studies your movement.
ramacharitamanas::4155.insight: It prepares the reader for hidden danger and shows how illusion exploits even a shadow of presence.

ramacharitamanas::4156.verse_sanskrit: गहइ छाहँ सक सो न उड़ाई। एहि बिधि सदा गगनचर खाई॥ सोइ छल हनूमान् कहँ कीन्हा। तासु कपटु कपि तुरतहिं चीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4156.verse_hindi: उस परछाईं को पकड़ लेती थी, जिससे वे उड़ नहीं सकते थे (और जल में गिर पड़ते थे) इस प्रकार वह सदा आकाश में उड़ने वाले जीवों को खाया करती थी। उसने वही छल हनुमान् जी से भी किया। हनुमान् जी ने तुरंत ही उसका कपट पहचान लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4156.english_translation: She would seize the shadow, so they could not fly and would fall into the water. In this way she kept eating the creatures that flew through the sky. She used the same trick on Hanuman, but Hanuman recognized her deceit at once.
ramacharitamanas::4156.translation_literal: गहइ (seized) / छाहँ (shadow) / सक (able) / सो (she) / न (not) / उड़ाई (let fly) / एहि (this) / बिधि (way) / सदा (always) / गगनचर (sky-traveling beings) / खाई (ate) / सोइ (same) / छल (deceit) / हनूमान् (Hanuman) / कहँ (to) / कीन्हा (did) / तासु (her) / कपटु (trick) / कपि (monkey) / तुरतहिं (immediately) / चीन्हा (recognized)
ramacharitamanas::4156.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4156.essence: Clear seeing breaks a trick before it can work.
ramacharitamanas::4156.simple_meaning: A sea-dwelling ogress traps flying beings by grabbing their shadows. She tries the same trick on Hanuman, but he sees through it immediately.
ramacharitamanas::4156.simple_insight: Not every danger attacks openly; clear seeing protects you faster than force.
ramacharitamanas::4156.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s outer waters, Hanuman has just crossed into enemy territory. A shadow-stealing creature tries her old trick on him, hoping to drag him down like other sky-travelers. But Hanuman’s alert mind catches the fraud instantly.
ramacharitamanas::4156.modern_relevance: A scam email lands in your inbox with urgent language and a fake logo. You pause, notice the mismatch, and delete it before it can hook you. Quick recognition saves you.
ramacharitamanas::4156.insight: It trains you to spot deception before reacting, using alert perception rather than brute strength.

ramacharitamanas::4157.verse_sanskrit: ताहि मारि मारुतसुत बीरा। बारिधि पार गयउ मतिधीरा॥ तहाँ जाइ देखी बन सोभा। गुंजत चंचरीक मधु लोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4157.verse_hindi: पवनपुत्र धीरबुद्धि वीर श्री हनुमान् जी उसको मारकर समुद्र के पार गए। वहाँ जाकर उन्होंने वन की शोभा देखी। मधु (पुष्प रस) के लोभ से भौंरे गुंजार कर रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4157.english_translation: Hanuman, the brave and steady-minded one, killed that obstacle and crossed the ocean. Then he went and saw the beauty of the forest, where bees hummed for the nectar of flowers.
ramacharitamanas::4157.translation_literal: ताहि (that one) / मारि (killing) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind) / बीरा (hero) / बारिधि (ocean) / पार (across) / गयउ (went) / मतिधीरा (steady-minded) / तहाँ (there) / जाइ (going) / देखी (saw) / बन (forest) / सोभा (beauty) / गुंजत (humming) / चंचरीक (bees) / मधु (nectar) / लोभा (greed/desire)
ramacharitamanas::4157.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4157.essence: Once the obstacle falls, the journey can continue.
ramacharitamanas::4157.simple_meaning: Hanuman overcomes the obstacle, crosses the ocean, and reaches a beautiful forest filled with birds, animals, and humming bees.
ramacharitamanas::4157.simple_insight: The hard crossing is over; now the path opens into beauty and life.
ramacharitamanas::4157.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just outwitted the sea-dwelling demoness who trapped flying creatures in illusion. With that danger gone, he crosses the ocean and lands on Lanka's shore, where the forest's beauty briefly contrasts with the mission ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4157.modern_relevance: You finally get through the airport delay, the traffic jam, the obstacle that almost made you turn back—and then the city opens up in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4157.insight: It moves the scene from struggle to arrival, showing that courage clears the way for the next step.

ramacharitamanas::4158.verse_sanskrit: नाना तरु फल फूल सुहाए। खग मृग बृंद देखि मन भाए॥ सैल बिसाल देखि एक आगें। ता पर धाइ चढ़ेउ भय त्यागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4158.verse_hindi: अनेकों प्रकार के वृक्ष फल-फूल से शोभित हैं। पक्षी और पशुओं के समूह को देखकर तो वे मन में (बहुत ही) प्रसन्न हुए। सामने एक विशाल पर्वत देखकर हनुमान् जी भय त्यागकर उस पर दौड़कर जा चढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4158.english_translation: Many kinds of trees stood bright with fruit and flowers. Seeing flocks of birds and herds of animals, he felt delighted. When he saw a huge mountain ahead, Hanuman threw off fear and leapt up it.
ramacharitamanas::4158.translation_literal: नाना (many kinds) / तरु (trees) / फल (fruits) / फूल (flowers) / सुहाए (were lovely) । / खग (birds) / मृग (deer/animals) / बृंद (groups) / देखि (seeing) / मन (mind) / भाए (were pleased) ॥ / सैल (mountain) / बिसाल (huge) / देखि (seeing) / एक (one) / आगें (ahead) / ता पर (onto that) / धाइ (running) / चढ़ेउ (he climbed) / भय (fear) / त्यागें (having cast off) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4158.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4158.essence: Beauty uplifts him, and a mountain only makes him move faster.
ramacharitamanas::4158.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees a beautiful forest, feels happy among the birds and animals, then spots a huge mountain and climbs it without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4158.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when attention turns outward to beauty and purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4158.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has crossed the ocean and entered Lanka's outer world. The forest delights him, but the sight of a great mountain calls him onward. This is a movement verse, showing his fearless momentum before the search for Sita deepens.
ramacharitamanas::4158.modern_relevance: You step out of a tense airport into sunlight, see trees, people, and open space, and your chest loosens. Then the next challenge appears, and you keep moving anyway.
ramacharitamanas::4158.insight: It shifts you from hesitant looking to fearless forward motion.

ramacharitamanas::4159.verse_sanskrit: उमा न कछु कपि कै अधिकाई। प्रभु प्रताप जो कालहि खाई॥ गिरि पर चढ़ि लंका तेहिं देखी। कहि न जाइ अति दुर्ग बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4159.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! इसमें वानर हनुमान् की कुछ बड़ाई नहीं है। यह प्रभु का प्रताप है, जो काल को भी खा जाता है। पर्वत पर चढ़कर उन्होंने लंका देखी। बहुत ही बड़ा किला है, कुछ कहा नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4159.english_translation: Uma, Hanuman's greatness is nothing of his own. It is the power of the Lord, who devours even death. Climbing the mountain, he saw Lanka. Its special fortifications cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::4159.translation_literal: उमा (Uma) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / कपि (monkey) / कै (of) / अधिकाई (greatness) / प्रभु (Lord's) / प्रताप (power, glory) / जो (which) / कालहि (death itself) / खाई (devours) / गिरि (mountain) / पर (on) / चढ़ि (climbing) / लंका (Lanka) / तेहिं (he) / देखी (saw) / कहि (said) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / अति (very) / दुर्ग (fortified) / बिसेषी (especially, uniquely)
ramacharitamanas::4159.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4159.essence: Your finest feats are often the Lord's power moving through you.
ramacharitamanas::4159.simple_meaning: Hanuman's feat is really the Lord's power working through him. After reaching the hilltop, he sees Lanka as an immense, unbeatable fortress.
ramacharitamanas::4159.simple_insight: What looks like personal greatness is often borrowed strength.
ramacharitamanas::4159.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman crosses the ocean and climbs the mountain, Shiva pauses the scene to tell Uma that the feat is not Hanuman's alone. The real force is Ram's power. From that height, Hanuman sees Lanka's massive fortifications and recognises the scale of the task ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4159.modern_relevance: You pulled off something impossible and everyone praised your talent. But deep down, you know support, timing, and grace carried you too.
ramacharitamanas::4159.insight: It shifts credit away from ego and toward the deeper power that makes action possible.

ramacharitamanas::4160.verse_sanskrit: अति उतंग जलनिधि चहुँ पासा। कनक कोट कर परम प्रकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4160.verse_hindi: वह अत्यंत ऊँचा है, उसके चारों ओर समुद्र है। सोने के परकोटे (चहारदीवारी) का परम प्रकाश हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4160.english_translation: It stands extremely high, with the ocean on all four sides. The golden rampart shines with a brilliant light.
ramacharitamanas::4160.translation_literal: अति उतंग (extremely high) / जलनिधि (ocean) / चहुँ पासा (on all four sides) / कनक (golden) / कोट (rampart) / कर (making) / परम (supreme) / प्रकासा (brightness)
ramacharitamanas::4160.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4160.essence: Lanka is shown as a dazzling fortress before the search begins.
ramacharitamanas::4160.simple_meaning: The verse describes Lanka as a towering city surrounded by the sea, with golden walls shining brightly.
ramacharitamanas::4160.simple_insight: The scene feels grand and unreachable, setting up the challenge ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4160.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka and is looking at the city from outside. Before any search begins, Tulsidas pauses to show its height, the sea around it, and the gleam of its golden walls. The verse builds the sense of a powerful, fortified enemy city.
ramacharitamanas::4160.modern_relevance: You arrive at a place that feels impossible to enter — a guarded campus, a locked building, a system built to keep outsiders out. The scale itself is meant to intimidate.
ramacharitamanas::4160.insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the obstacle's size and strength.

ramacharitamanas::4161.verse_sanskrit: कनक कोटि बिचित्र मनि कृत सुंदरायतना घना। चउहट्ट हट्ट सुबट्ट बीथीं चारु पुर बहु बिधि बना॥ गज बाजि खच्चर निकर पदचर रथ बरूथन्हि को गनै। बहुरूप निसिचर जूथ अतिबल सेन बरनत नहिं बनै ॥
ramacharitamanas::4161.verse_hindi: विचित्र मणियों से जड़ा हुआ सोने का परकोटा है, उसके अंदर बहुत से सुंदर-सुंदर घर हैं। चौराहे, बाजार, सुंदर मार्ग और गलियाँ हैं, सुंदर नगर बहुत प्रकार से सजा हुआ है। हाथी, घोड़े, खच्चरों के समूह तथा पैदल और रथों के समूहों को कौन गिन सकता है! अनेक रूपों के राक्षसों के दल हैं, उनकी अत्यंत बलवती सेना वर्णन करते नहीं बनती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4161.english_translation: The city is ringed with a golden wall studded with strange jewels. Inside are many beautiful houses, crossroads, markets, fine roads, and lovely streets, all arranged in splendid ways. Who can count the elephants, horses, mules, foot soldiers, and chariots? Countless demons of many forms fill the mighty army; their strength cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::4161.translation_literal: कनक (golden) / कोटि (wall or fort) / बिचित्र (strange, varied) / मनि (jewels) / कृत (made) / सुंदरायतना (beautiful dwellings) / घना (dense, plentiful) / चउहट्ट (crossroads) / हट्ट (markets) / सुबट्ट (fine roads) / बीथीं (streets) / चारु (beautiful) / पुर (city) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / बना (made) / गज (elephants) / बाजि (horses) / खच्चर (mules) / निकर (groups) / पदचर (foot soldiers) / रथ (chariots) / बरूथन्हि (troops) / को (who) / गनै (count) / बहुरूप (many-formed) / निसिचर (demons) / जूथ (crowds) / अतिबल (very mighty) / सेन (army) / बरनत (describing) / नहिं बनै (is not possible)
ramacharitamanas::4161.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4161.essence: Lanka looks magnificent, but its power makes it feel unapproachable.
ramacharitamanas::4161.simple_meaning: Lanka is described as a dazzling, heavily fortified city packed with wealth, roads, buildings, and a vast army. The point is its overwhelming scale, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4161.simple_insight: Some places feel too large and guarded to enter. This verse lets you feel that weight before the story turns.
ramacharitamanas::4161.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka and is taking in the city from above. Tulsidas pauses the action to paint its riches, fortifications, and military power, building the sense of danger before Hanuman begins his search for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4161.modern_relevance: You step off a train into a city that feels impossible to navigate: glittering towers, crowded roads, security gates, and no clear way in. The verse captures that first stunned look.
ramacharitamanas::4161.insight: It frames the scene as one of scale and intimidation, preparing the mind for the challenge ahead.

ramacharitamanas::4162.verse_sanskrit: बन बाग उपबन बाटिका सर कूप बापीं सोहहीं। नर नाग सुर गंधर्ब कन्या रूप मुनि मन मोहहीं॥ कहुँ माल देह बिसाल सैल समान अतिबल गर्जहीं। नाना अखारेन्ह भिरहिं बहुबिधि एक एकन्ह तर्जहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4162.verse_hindi: वन, बाग, उपवन (बगीचे), फुलवाड़ी, तालाब, कुएँ और बावलियाँ सुशोभित हैं। मनुष्य, नाग, देवताओं और गंधर्वों की कन्याएँ अपने सौंदर्य से मुनियों के भी मन को मोहे लेती हैं। कहीं पर्वत के समान विशाल शरीर वाले बड़े ही बलवान् मल्ल (पहलवान) गरज रहे हैं। वे अनेकों अखाड़ों में बहुत प्रकार से भिड़ते और एक-दूसरे को ललकारते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4162.english_translation: Gardens, groves, orchards, ponds, wells, and tanks shine there. Humans, serpents, radiant beings, and celestial maidens enchant even the minds of sages with their beauty. Somewhere, mighty wrestlers with mountain-like bodies are roaring. In many arenas, they grapple in many ways and challenge one another.
