ramacharitamanas::4162.translation_literal: बन (forest) / बाग (garden) / उपबन (grove) / बाटिका (orchard) / सर (pond) / कूप (well) / बापीं (tank) / सोहहीं (shine) / नर (humans) / नाग (serpents) / सुर (radiant beings) / गंधर्ब (celestial beings) / कन्या (maidens) / रूप (beauty) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / मोहहीं (delight) / कहुँ (somewhere) / माल (wrestlers) / देह (body) / बिसाल (huge) / सैल (mountain) / समान (like) / अतिबल (very strong) / गर्जहीं (roar) / नाना (many) / अखारेन्ह (arenas) / भिरहिं (grapple) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / एक एकन्ह (one another) / तर्जहीं (challenge)
ramacharitamanas::4162.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4162.essence: Lanka gleams with beauty, but its strength is restless and menacing.
ramacharitamanas::4162.simple_meaning: Lanka is shown as a glittering city full of gardens, waterworks, beautiful beings, and powerful wrestlers. The verse is describing its splendor and strength, not teaching a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::4162.simple_insight: The city feels dazzling and dangerous at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::4162.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has crossed into Lanka and is moving through a city unlike anything he has seen. Tulsidas pauses to paint its beauty, wealth, and brute power before the search for Sita tightens.
ramacharitamanas::4162.insight: It sets the stage by showing a world of luxury, beauty, and force before the real search begins.

ramacharitamanas::4163.verse_sanskrit: करि जतन भट कोटिन्ह बिकट तन नगर चहुँ दिसि रच्छहीं। कहुँ महिष मानुष धेनु खर अज खल निसाचर भच्छहीं॥ एहि लागि तुलसीदास इन्ह की कथा कछु एक है कही। रघुबीर सर तीरथ सरीरन्हि त्यागि गति पैहहिं सही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4163.verse_hindi: भयंकर शरीर वाले करोड़ों योद्धा यत्न करके (बड़ी सावधानी से) नगर की चारों दिशाओं में (सब ओर से) रखवाली करते हैं। कहीं दुष्ट राक्षस भैंसों, मनुष्यों, गायों, गदहों और बकरों को खा रहे हैं। तुलसीदास ने इनकी कथा इसीलिए कुछ थोड़ी सी कही है कि ये निश्चय ही श्री रामचंद्रजी के बाण रूपी तीर्थ में शरीरों को त्यागकर परमगति पावेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4163.english_translation: With fierce bodies, countless warriors guard the city on all four sides. Elsewhere, evil beings are devouring buffaloes, humans, cows, donkeys, and goats. Tulsidas mentions only a little of their story because they will surely give up their bodies at Ram's arrow like pilgrims at a sacred crossing and reach the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::4163.translation_literal: करि (having done) / जतन (careful effort) / भट (warriors) / कोटिन्ह (in crores, countless) / बिकट (fierce, terrible) / तन (bodies) / नगर (city) / चहुँ दिसि (in four directions) / रच्छहीं (guard) / कहुँ (somewhere) / महिष (buffaloes) / मानुष (humans) / धेनु (cows) / खर (donkeys) / अज (goats) / खल (wicked) / निसाचर (night-dwelling beings) / भच्छहीं (devour) / एहि लागि (for this reason) / तुलसीदास (Tulsidas) / इन्ह की (of these) / कथा (story) / कछु एक (a little) / है (is) / कही (told) / रघुबीर (Ram) / सर (arrow) / तीरथ (pilgrimage crossing) / सरीरन्हि (bodies) / त्यागि (leaving) / गति (higher state) / पैहहिं (will attain) / सही (certainly)
ramacharitamanas::4163.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4163.essence: Even the strongest cruelty is already headed toward its end.
ramacharitamanas::4163.simple_meaning: Lanka is heavily guarded, and its cruel inhabitants are destroying living beings. Tulsidas says this only briefly because Ram's arrow will end their bodies and send them onward.
ramacharitamanas::4163.simple_insight: Some scenes are only shown long enough to reveal their end.
ramacharitamanas::4163.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just reached Lanka and sees a city packed with armed guards, danger, and cruelty on every side. Tulsidas pauses the scene to remind the reader that this fearsome power is already doomed before Ram's arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4163.modern_relevance: You walk into a place that feels untouchable — security everywhere, power everywhere, cruelty everywhere — and still something in you knows it will not last.
ramacharitamanas::4163.insight: It shifts attention from intimidating appearances to the larger force that ends them.

ramacharitamanas::4164.verse_sanskrit: दोहा- पुर रखवारे देखि बहु कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार। अति लघु रूप धरों निसि नगर करौं पइसार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4164.verse_hindi: नगर के बहुसंख्यक रखवालों को देखकर हनुमान् जी ने मन में विचार किया कि अत्यंत छोटा रूप धरूँ और रात के समय नगर में प्रवेश करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4164.english_translation: Seeing the many guards of the city, Hanuman thought to take a very small form and enter the city at night.
ramacharitamanas::4164.translation_literal: पुर (city) / रखवारे (guards) / देखि (seeing) / बहु (many) / कपि (the monkey) / मन (mind) / कीन्ह (made) / बिचार (thought) / अति (very) / लघु (small) / रूप (form) / धरों (I take) / निसि (at night) / नगर (city) / करौं (I will) / पइसार (entry)
ramacharitamanas::4164.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4164.essence: Care beats force when the path is watched.
ramacharitamanas::4164.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees the heavy city guard and decides to shrink his form so he can slip in at night.
ramacharitamanas::4164.simple_insight: Sometimes the smartest move is quiet, not forceful.
ramacharitamanas::4164.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has reached the city walls and sees how heavily it is guarded. Instead of rushing in, he pauses and chooses a smaller form for a night entry. This is a tactical moment, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4164.modern_relevance: You reach a locked building after midnight and realize the front entrance is watched. Instead of forcing your way in, you slow down, change approach, and move quietly.
ramacharitamanas::4164.insight: It models adaptive action: assess the obstacle first, then choose the least exposed way through.

ramacharitamanas::4165.verse_sanskrit: मसक समान रूप कपि धरी। लंकहि चलेउ सुमिरि नरहरी॥ नाम लंकिनी एक निसिचरी। सो कह चलेसि मोहि निंदरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4165.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी मच्छड़ के समान (छोटा सा) रूप धारण कर नर रूप से लीला करने वाले भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करके लंका को चले (लंका के द्वार पर) लंकिनी नाम की एक राक्षसी रहती थी। वह बोली- मेरा निरादर करके (बिना मुझसे पूछे) कहाँ चला जा रहा है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4165.english_translation: Hanuman took a tiny form like a mosquito and, remembering Lord Ram, set out for Lanka. At the gate stood a demoness named Lankini, who said, "Why are you passing me by without respect?"
ramacharitamanas::4165.translation_literal: मसक समान (like a mosquito) / रूप (form) / कपि (monkey-devotee) / धरी (took) / लंकहि (to Lanka) / चलेउ (went) / सुमिरि (remembering) / नरहरी (the man-lion, Ram) ॥ / नाम (named) / लंकिनी (Lankini) / एक (a) / निसिचरी (night-demoness) / सो (she) / कह (said) / चलेसि (are going) / मोहि (me) / निंदरी (without respect) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4165.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4165.essence: Remembering Ram makes even the smallest form fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4165.simple_meaning: Hanuman shrinks himself, remembers Ram, and heads into Lanka. At the gate, Lankini stops him and complains that he is ignoring her.
ramacharitamanas::4165.simple_insight: Smallness and remembrance let you move through fear without losing focus.
ramacharitamanas::4165.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka and is about to enter the enemy city. To avoid notice, he becomes tiny and keeps Ram in mind. At the gate, Lankini confronts him, setting up the first obstacle inside Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4165.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, keep your composure, and ignore the urge to prove yourself. Quiet focus gets you farther than force.
ramacharitamanas::4165.insight: It teaches you to enter difficulty lightly, with memory and restraint instead of ego.

ramacharitamanas::4166.verse_sanskrit: जानेहि नहीं मरमु सठ मोरा। मोर अहार जहाँ लगि चोरा॥ मुठिका एक महा कपि हनी। रुधिर बमत धरनीं ढनमनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4166.verse_hindi: हे मूर्ख! तूने मेरा भेद नहीं जाना जहाँ तक (जितने) चोर हैं, वे सब मेरे आहार हैं। महाकपि हनुमान् जी ने उसे एक घूँसा मारा, जिससे वह खून की उलटी करती हुई पृथ्वी पर ल़ुढक पड़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4166.english_translation: You fool! You have not understood my secret. All the thieves here are my food. The great monkey struck her with one blow, and she fell to the ground vomiting blood.
ramacharitamanas::4166.translation_literal: जानेहि (do not know) / नहीं (not) / मरमु (secret) / सठ (fool) / मोरा (my) / मोर (my) / अहार (food) / जहाँ लगि (as far as) / चोरा (thieves) / मुठिका (fist/blow) / एक (one) / महा कपि (great monkey) / हनी (struck) / रुधिर (blood) / बमत (vomiting) / धरनीं (to the ground) / ढनमनी (collapsed)
ramacharitamanas::4166.speaker: Lankini
ramacharitamanas::4166.essence: Pride looks fierce until it meets the right blow.
ramacharitamanas::4166.simple_meaning: Lankini boasts that intruders are her prey, but Hanuman knocks her down in one blow.
ramacharitamanas::4166.simple_insight: False strength collapses instantly when it meets true force.
ramacharitamanas::4166.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just entered Lanka in a tiny form. The gatekeeper Lankini blocks him, boasts of her power, and attacks. Hanuman answers with a single blow, revealing that his mission cannot be stopped by force or pride.
ramacharitamanas::4166.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one person tries to intimidate everyone with loud confidence. The moment real competence shows up, the performance ends.
ramacharitamanas::4166.insight: It shows that arrogant resistance falls quickly before disciplined power.

ramacharitamanas::4167.verse_sanskrit: पुनि संभारि उठी सो लंका। जोरि पानि कर बिनय ससंका॥ जब रावनहि ब्रह्म बर दीन्हा। चलत बिरंच कहा मोहि चीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4167.verse_hindi: वह लंकिनी फिर अपने को संभालकर उठी और डर के मारे हाथ जोड़कर विनती करने लगी। (वह बोली-) रावण को जब ब्रह्माजी ने वर दिया था, तब चलते समय उन्होंने मुझे राक्षसों के विनाश की यह पहचान बता दी थी कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4167.english_translation: She then gathered herself and stood up. Terrified, the female guardian of Lanka folded her hands and pleaded. She said, 'When Brahma gave Ravana his boon, as he was leaving he told me this sign: ...'
ramacharitamanas::4167.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / संभारि (gathering herself) / उठी (rose) / सो (that) / लंका (Lanka) / जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / कर (doing) / बिनय (request) / ससंका (fearfully) / जब (when) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / बर (boon) / दीन्हा (gave) / चलत (while leaving) / बिरंच (Brahma) / कहा (said) / मोहि (to me) / चीन्हा (sign)
ramacharitamanas::4167.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4167.essence: A small defeat can reveal a much larger danger.
ramacharitamanas::4167.simple_meaning: The guardian of Lanka regains herself, then speaks fearfully. She explains that Brahma once gave Ravana a boon and left behind a warning sign.
ramacharitamanas::4167.simple_insight: Fear can make even the strong become careful and humble.
ramacharitamanas::4167.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just struck Lanka’s guardian and crossed into the city. Shaken, she rises again and explains why she is afraid: Brahma’s boon to Ravana came with a warning sign. This verse sets up the next revelation about Hanuman’s power.
ramacharitamanas::4167.modern_relevance: You get corrected hard, then suddenly realize the other person was never just being difficult. Their fear has history, and now the conversation changes.
ramacharitamanas::4167.insight: It shifts attention from the blow itself to the meaning the blow reveals.

ramacharitamanas::4168.verse_sanskrit: बिकल होसि तैं कपि कें मारे। तब जानेसु निसिचर संघारे॥ तात मोर अति पुन्य बहूता। देखेउँ नयन राम कर दूता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4168.verse_hindi: जब तू बंदर के मारने से व्याकुल हो जाए, तब तू राक्षसों का संहार हुआ जान लेना। हे तात! मेरे बड़े पुण्य हैं, जो मैं श्री रामचंद्रजी के दूत (आप) को नेत्रों से देख पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4168.english_translation: When you are thrown into confusion by a monkey's blow, then know that the slaughter of the demons has begun. O dear one, I have great merit indeed, for I have seen with my own eyes the messenger of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4168.translation_literal: बिकल (disturbed/confused) / होसि (you will become) / तैं (you) / कपि (monkey) / कें (by) / मारे (struck) / तब (then) / जानेसु (know) / निसिचर (demons) / संघारे (slaughtered) / तात (dear one) / मोर (my) / अति (very) / पुन्य (merit) / बहूता (great/much) / देखेउँ (I saw) / नयन (with eyes) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / दूता (messenger)
ramacharitamanas::4168.speaker: Lankini
ramacharitamanas::4168.essence: Ram's messenger turns even a blow into a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4168.simple_meaning: Lankini realizes that Hanuman's blow means her side is in danger, and she feels blessed to have seen Ram's messenger with her own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4168.simple_insight: A shock can become a blessing when it wakes you up to something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::4168.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the guardian Lankini has just been struck by Hanuman. Instead of holding onto pride, she recognizes the deeper sign: Ram's work has begun, and seeing his messenger is itself a rare blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4168.modern_relevance: You get corrected hard by someone you underestimated, and instead of spiraling, you realize the encounter woke you up. Sometimes the blow is also the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4168.insight: It shifts the mind from resisting disruption to recognizing sacred arrival in it.

ramacharitamanas::4169.verse_sanskrit: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग। तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::4169.verse_hindi: हे तात! स्वर्ग और मोक्ष के सब सुखों को तराजू के एक पलड़े में रखा जाए, तो भी वे सब मिलकर (दूसरे पलड़े पर रखे हुए) उस सुख के बराबर नहीं हो सकते, जो लव (क्षण) मात्र के सत्संग से होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4169.english_translation: O friend, if all the joys of heaven and liberation are placed on one side of a scale, they still cannot equal the joy of even a moment's company with holy fellowship.
ramacharitamanas::4169.translation_literal: तात (O friend) / स्वर्ग (heaven) / अपबर्ग (liberation) / सुख (joys) / धरिअ (place) / तुला (scale) / एक (one) / अंग (side) / तूल (equal) / न (not) / ताहि (that) / सकल (all) / मिलि (together) / जो (which) / सुख (joy) / लव (a moment) / सतसंग (holy fellowship)
ramacharitamanas::4169.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4169.essence: Holy company outweighs every reward, even freedom itself.
ramacharitamanas::4169.simple_meaning: Even the greatest rewards cannot equal the joy that comes from a brief moment in the company of the wise and devoted.
ramacharitamanas::4169.simple_insight: What truly nourishes you is not achievement, but the company that lifts your heart.
ramacharitamanas::4169.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has already earned Lankini's respect, and the poem pauses to state the real treasure: not power, not escape, but even a moment of holy company. Tulsidas turns the search for Sita into a lesson on what is priceless.
ramacharitamanas::4169.modern_relevance: You leave a noisy party and sit for ten quiet minutes with someone who truly understands you. That relief, that settling, is worth more than all the applause you chased that night.
ramacharitamanas::4169.insight: It shifts value from external rewards to the company that shapes your mind and heart.

ramacharitamanas::4170.verse_sanskrit: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4170.verse_hindi: अयोध्यापुरी के राजा श्री रघुनाथजी को हृदय में रखे हुए नगर में प्रवेश करके सब काम कीजिए। उसके लिए विष अमृत हो जाता है, शत्रु मित्रता करने लगते हैं, समुद्र गाय के खुर के बराबर हो जाता है, अग्नि में शीतलता आ जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4170.english_translation: Enter the city and do all your work while keeping the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a person, poison becomes nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean becomes as small as a cow's hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
ramacharitamanas::4170.translation_literal: प्रबिसि (entering) / नगर (city) / कीजे (do) / सब (all) / काजा (works) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / राखि (keeping) / कोसलपुर (of Kosala city) / राजा (king) / गरल (poison) / सुधा (nectar) / रिपु (enemies) / करहिं (do) / मिताई (friendship) / गोपद (cow's hoofprint) / सिंधु (ocean) / अनल (fire) / सितलाई (coolness)
ramacharitamanas::4170.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4170.essence: Ram in the heart makes danger lose its power.
ramacharitamanas::4170.simple_meaning: Go into the world with Ram held in your heart. Then even what looks harmful, impossible, or hostile can turn helpful.
ramacharitamanas::4170.simple_insight: You do not have to master every situation first; steady remembrance can change how life meets you.
ramacharitamanas::4170.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is about to enter Lanka alone, disguised and vulnerable. Tulsidas gives the rule for that mission: carry Ram in the heart, and the city itself loses its power to harm you.
ramacharitamanas::4170.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering with your chest already tight. If you hold on to what is steady inside, the room does not get to define you.
ramacharitamanas::4170.insight: It shifts attention from outer threat to inner remembrance, so action becomes fearless and clear.

ramacharitamanas::4171.verse_sanskrit: गरुड़ सुमेरु रेनु सम ताही। राम कृपा करि चितवा जाही॥ अति लघु रूप धरेउ हनुमाना। पैठा नगर सुमिरि भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4171.verse_hindi: और हे गरुड़जी! सुमेरु पर्वत उसके लिए रज के समान हो जाता है, जिसे श्री रामचंद्रजी ने एक बार कृपा करके देख लिया। तब हनुमान् जी ने बहुत ही छोटा रूप धारण किया और भगवान् का स्मरण करके नगर में प्रवेश किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4171.english_translation: And Garuda, even Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust for the one whom Ram has once looked upon with grace. Then Hanuman took a very small form and entered the city while remembering the divine.
ramacharitamanas::4171.translation_literal: गरुड़ (Garuda) / सुमेरु (Mount Sumeru) / रेनु (dust) / सम (like) / ताही (for that one) / राम (Ram) / कृपा करि (having shown grace) / चितवा (looked upon) / जाही (whom) / अति (very) / लघु (small) / रूप (form) / धरेउ (took) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / पैठा (entered) / नगर (city) / सुमिरि (remembering) / भगवाना (the divine)
ramacharitamanas::4171.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4171.essence: Ram’s grace makes the impossible feel small.
ramacharitamanas::4171.simple_meaning: Ram’s grace makes the impossible feel small. Hanuman then shrinks his form, keeps Ram in mind, and enters the city quietly.
ramacharitamanas::4171.simple_insight: You can move through danger lightly when your heart is steady on the divine.
ramacharitamanas::4171.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is now inside Lanka, and the real power behind his mission is Ram’s grace. Tulsidas says that for one who has been seen by Ram, even Mount Sumeru is like dust. With that confidence, Hanuman makes himself tiny and slips into the city, remembering Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4171.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone seems bigger, louder, and more certain than you. Then you remember who stands with you, and the fear loses its size.
ramacharitamanas::4171.insight: It shifts attention from your own scale to the protection and courage that grace gives.

ramacharitamanas::4172.verse_sanskrit: मंदिर मंदिर प्रति करि सोधा। देखे जहँ तहँ अगनित जोधा॥ गयउ दसानन मंदिर माहीं। अति बिचित्र कहि जात सो नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4172.verse_hindi: उन्होंने एक-एक (प्रत्येक) महल की खोज की। जहाँ-तहाँ असंख्य योद्धा देखे। फिर वे रावण के महल में गए। वह अत्यंत विचित्र था, जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4172.english_translation: He searched each palace in turn and saw countless warriors everywhere. Then he entered Ravana's palace, which was so strange it cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::4172.translation_literal: मंदिर (palace) / मंदिर (palace) / प्रति (in each) / करि (having done) / सोधा (search) / देखे (saw) / जहँ (where) / तहँ (there) / अगनित (countless) / जोधा (warriors) / गयउ (went) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / मंदिर (palace) / माहीं (inside) / अति (very) / बिचित्र (strange) / कहि (said) / जात (can be told) / सो (that) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::4172.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4172.essence: The search continues until the hidden place is reached.
ramacharitamanas::4172.simple_meaning: Hanuman carefully searched every palace, saw many warriors, and finally entered Ravana's extraordinary palace.
ramacharitamanas::4172.simple_insight: Sometimes the path to what matters is just patient searching, one place at a time.
ramacharitamanas::4172.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is moving through Lanka alone, checking palace after palace in his search for Sita. He sees guards and warriors everywhere, then enters Ravana's own palace. The verse slows the suspense before the next reveal.
ramacharitamanas::4172.modern_relevance: You check the last room in the house after midnight, still hoping the missing thing is there. The search itself has become a test of patience.
ramacharitamanas::4172.insight: It keeps attention on careful searching, not on dramatic discovery yet.

ramacharitamanas::4173.verse_sanskrit: सयन किएँ देखा कपि तेही। मंदिर महुँ न दीखि बैदेही॥ भवन एक पुनि दीख सुहावा। हरि मंदिर तहँ भिन्न बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4173.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने उस (रावण) को शयन किए देखा, परंतु महल में जानकीजी नहीं दिखाई दीं। फिर एक सुंदर महल दिखाई दिया। वहाँ (उसमें) भगवान् का एक अलग मंदिर बना हुआ था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4173.english_translation: Hanuman saw him lying down, but did not see Sita in the palace. Then he saw a beautiful separate shrine there, a temple dedicated to Hari.
ramacharitamanas::4173.translation_literal: सयन किएँ (while lying down) / देखा (saw) / कपि (the monkey) / तेही (him) / मंदिर महुँ (in the palace) / न (not) / दीखि (was seen) / बैदेही (Sita)॥ / भवन (mansion/palace) / एक (one) / पुनि (again) / दीख (was seen) / सुहावा (beautiful) / हरि (Hari's) / मंदिर (temple) / तहँ (there) / भिन्न (separate) / बनावा (made)
ramacharitamanas::4173.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4173.essence: Ram's presence survives even inside Ravana's palace.
ramacharitamanas::4173.simple_meaning: Hanuman found Ravana asleep, but Sita was not in the palace. Then he noticed a lovely separate shrine to Hari inside the building.
ramacharitamanas::4173.simple_insight: Even in the enemy's house, devotion leaves a visible trace.
ramacharitamanas::4173.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is searching Ravana's palace in Lanka, moving room by room under the cover of night. He sees Ravana asleep and still cannot find Sita. Then a different beauty appears: a separate shrine to Hari, showing that even inside Ravana's world, Ram's presence has not been erased.
ramacharitamanas::4173.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everything feels hostile, and then you notice one small sign of faith on a shelf or wall. Even there, devotion has survived.
ramacharitamanas::4173.insight: It shifts attention from the search itself to the hidden sign that Ram's presence remains even in enemy territory.

ramacharitamanas::4174.verse_sanskrit: रामायुध अंकित गृह सोभा बरनि न जाइ। नव तुलसिका बृंद तहँ देखि हरष कपिराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4174.verse_hindi: वह महल श्री रामजी के आयुध (धनुष-बाण) के चिह्नों से अंकित था, उसकी शोभा वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। वहाँ नवीन-नवीन तुलसी के वृक्ष-समूहों को देखकर कपिराज श्री हनुमान् जी हर्षित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4174.english_translation: The mansion was marked with the emblems of Ram's weapons; its beauty cannot be described. Seeing fresh groves of tulsi there, Hanuman, king of the monkeys, felt joy.
ramacharitamanas::4174.translation_literal: रामायुध (Ram's weapons) / अंकित (marked) / गृह (house, mansion) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / बरनि (to describe) / न जाइ (cannot be done) / नव (new, fresh) / तुलसिका (tulsi plants) / बृंद (clusters, groups) / तहँ (there) / देखि (seeing) / हरष (joy) / कपिराई (king of monkeys, Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4174.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4174.essence: Ram's signs make even an enemy city feel like home.
ramacharitamanas::4174.simple_meaning: Hanuman finds a house marked by Ram's symbols and filled with tulsi, and his joy rises because he recognizes Ram's presence there.
ramacharitamanas::4174.simple_insight: Devotion becomes joy when you suddenly recognize signs of the beloved everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::4174.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has entered Lanka alone, searching for Sita in a city ruled by fear. After checking palace after palace, he finds one house unlike the rest: marked with Ram's weapons and planted with tulsi. The sight tells him a righteous heart lives there, and he feels immediate joy.
ramacharitamanas::4174.modern_relevance: You walk into a stranger's home and spot a small framed image, a prayer corner, a tulsi plant on the balcony. In that instant, the room stops feeling strange. Recognition creates warmth before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4174.insight: It trains you to notice the quiet signs of shared devotion and feel connection instead of isolation.

ramacharitamanas::4175.verse_sanskrit: लंका निसिचर निकर निवासा। इहाँ कहाँ सज्जन कर बासा॥ मन महुँ तरक करैं कपि लागा। तेहीं समय बिभीषनु जागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4175.verse_hindi: लंका तो राक्षसों के समूह का निवास स्थान है। यहाँ सज्जन (साधु पुरुष) का निवास कहाँ? हनुमान् जी मन में इस प्रकार तर्क करने लगे। उसी समय विभीषणजी जागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4175.english_translation: Lanka is the dwelling place of hosts of demons. Where could a good person possibly live here? Hanuman began thinking this in his mind, and at that very moment Vibhishana woke up.
ramacharitamanas::4175.translation_literal: लंका (Lanka) / निसिचर (night-wanderers, demons) / निकर (crowd, host) / निवासा (dwelling place) / इहाँ (here) / कहाँ (where) / सज्जन (good person) / कर (of) / बासा (dwelling)॥ / मन (mind) / महुँ (in) / तरक (reasoning, doubt) / करैं (to do) / कपि (monkey, Hanuman) / लागा (began) / तेहीं (at that) / समय (time) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / जागा (woke up)॥
ramacharitamanas::4175.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4175.essence: A good heart can be hidden inside a corrupt place.
ramacharitamanas::4175.simple_meaning: Hanuman looks at Lanka and wonders how any good person could live there. Just then, Vibhishana wakes up.
ramacharitamanas::4175.simple_insight: Sometimes the right meeting begins before either person speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4175.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already found a house marked by Ram's signs, but Sita is still missing. He sees the city as a place of darkness and wonders where a virtuous person could belong here. At that exact moment, Vibhishana wakes up.
ramacharitamanas::4175.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everything feels off, and then one quiet person changes the whole atmosphere. Recognition often begins before introductions.
ramacharitamanas::4175.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd around you to the one person who does not belong to its corruption.

ramacharitamanas::4176.verse_sanskrit: राम राम तेहिं सुमिरन कीन्हा। हृदयँ हरष कपि सज्जन चीन्हा॥ एहि सन सठि करिहउँ पहिचानी। साधु ते होइ न कारज हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4176.verse_hindi: उन्होंने (विभीषण ने) राम नाम का स्मरण (उच्चारण) किया। हनमान् जी ने उन्हें सज्जन जाना और हृदय में हर्षित हुए। (हनुमान् जी ने विचार किया कि) इनसे हठ करके (अपनी ओर से ही) परिचय करूँगा, क्योंकि साधु से कार्य की हानि नहीं होती। (प्रत्युत लाभ ही होता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4176.english_translation: He remembered Ram's name. Hanuman rejoiced in his heart and recognized him as a good person. He thought, "I will introduce myself to this one, because a good person never causes harm in a task."
ramacharitamanas::4176.translation_literal: राम राम (Ram's name) / तेहिं (then) / सुमिरन (remembering) / कीन्हा (did) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / कपि (the monkey) / सज्जन (good person) / चीन्हा (recognized) / एहि (this) / सन (with) / सठि (firmly) / करिहउँ (I will do) / पहिचानी (recognition) / साधु (good person) / ते (from) / होइ (becomes) / न (not) / कारज (task) / हानी (loss)
ramacharitamanas::4176.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4176.essence: Shared reverence reveals who can be trusted.
ramacharitamanas::4176.simple_meaning: Hearing Ram's name, Hanuman feels joy and instantly trusts Vibhishana. He sees that a good person will not spoil the task.
ramacharitamanas::4176.simple_insight: Trust grows fast when the heart recognizes sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::4176.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just found Vibhishana, Ravana's righteous brother. When Vibhishana remembers Ram's name, Hanuman's suspicion melts into joy. The meeting becomes possible because devotion can recognize devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4176.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a tense room and they mention the same value you live by. The suspicion eases. Sometimes one honest signal is enough to know who can be trusted.
ramacharitamanas::4176.insight: It shifts you from guarded doubt to discerning trust based on character and shared devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4177.verse_sanskrit: बिप्र रूप धरि बचन सुनाए। सुनत बिभीषन उठि तहँ आए॥ करि प्रनाम पूँछी कुसलाई। बिप्र कहहु निज कथा बुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4177.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मण का रूप धरकर हनुमान् जी ने उन्हें वचन सुनाए (पुकारा)। सुनते ही विभीषणजी उठकर वहाँ आए। प्रणाम करके कुशल पूछी (और कहा कि) हे ब्राह्मणदेव! अपनी कथा समझाकर कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4177.english_translation: Taking the form of a Brahmin, Hanuman spoke to him. Hearing that, Vibhishana came there at once. He bowed and asked after his welfare, then said, "Brahmin, please tell me who you are and explain your story."
ramacharitamanas::4177.translation_literal: बिप्र रूप (Brahmin form) / धरि (taking) / बचन (words) / सुनाए (spoke, made heard) / सुनत (hearing) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / उठि (rising) / तहँ (there) / आए (came) / करि (doing) / प्रनाम (bowing) / पूँछी (asked) / कुसलाई (welfare) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / कहहु (tell) / निज (your own) / कथा (story) / बुझाई (explaining)
ramacharitamanas::4177.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4177.essence: Trust begins with respectful approach, not immediate revelation.
ramacharitamanas::4177.simple_meaning: Hanuman approaches in disguise, and Vibhishana responds with respect and curiosity, asking him to explain who he is and why he has come.
ramacharitamanas::4177.simple_insight: Respect opens the door to real conversation.
ramacharitamanas::4177.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Vibhishana and is testing the ground before revealing himself. Vibhishana rises, bows, and speaks with humility. The scene is still moving toward trust, not yet into full disclosure.
ramacharitamanas::4177.modern_relevance: You meet someone new at a gathering and feel they may understand you. Before you reveal yourself, you ask careful questions and wait for trust to form.
ramacharitamanas::4177.insight: It shows how humility and courtesy create the first bridge between strangers.

ramacharitamanas::4178.verse_sanskrit: की तुम्ह हरि दासन्ह महँ कोई। मोरें हृदय प्रीति अति होई॥ की तुम्ह रामु दीन अनुरागी। आयहु मोहि करन बड़भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4178.verse_hindi: क्या आप हरिभक्तों में से कोई हैं? क्योंकि आपको देखकर मेरे हृदय में अत्यंत प्रेम उमड़ रहा है। अथवा क्या आप दीनों से प्रेम करने वाले स्वयं श्री रामजी ही हैं जो मुझे बड़भागी बनाने (घर-बैठे दर्शन देकर कृतार्थ करने) आए हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4178.english_translation: Are you one of Ram's devotees? My heart is overflowing with love. Or are you Ram himself, who loves the humble and has come to bless me?
ramacharitamanas::4178.translation_literal: की (or) / तुम्ह (you) / हरि (Ram) / दासन्ह (devotees) / महँ (among) / कोई (someone) / मोरें (my) / हृदय (heart) / प्रीति (love) / अति (very much) / होई (is) / की (or) / तुम्ह (you) / रामु (Ram) / दीन (humble) / अनुरागी (loving) / आयहु (have come) / मोहि (to me) / करन (to make) / बड़भागी (fortunate)
ramacharitamanas::4178.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4178.essence: Devotion is so real it can feel like Ram has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::4178.simple_meaning: Vibhishana sees Hanuman and feels such deep affection that he wonders whether this visitor is a devotee of Ram or Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::4178.simple_insight: Pure devotion can make another person feel instantly safe, loved, and recognised.
ramacharitamanas::4178.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana meets Hanuman in disguise. Before any proof is given, his heart responds with trust and tenderness. He asks whether this stranger is a devotee of Ram or Ram himself, because the feeling of grace is already unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::4178.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a hospital corridor and feel calm before they even speak. Some people carry such sincerity that being near them feels like being met by grace.
ramacharitamanas::4178.insight: It teaches you to recognise devotion by its effect: it softens fear and awakens trust before words arrive.

ramacharitamanas::4179.verse_sanskrit: तब हनुमंत कही सब राम कथा निज नाम। सुनत जुगल तन पुलक मन मगन सुमिरि गुन ग्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4179.verse_hindi: तब हनुमान् जी ने श्री रामचंद्रजी की सारी कथा कहकर अपना नाम बताया। सुनते ही दोनों के शरीर पुलकित हो गए और श्री रामजी के गुण समूहों का स्मरण करके दोनों के मन (प्रेम और आनंद में) मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4179.english_translation: Then Hanuman told the whole story of Ram and revealed his own name. Hearing it, both bodies thrilled, and both minds became absorbed in remembering Ram's countless virtues.
ramacharitamanas::4179.translation_literal: तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / कही (told) / सब (all) / राम कथा (Ram's story) / निज नाम (his own name) / सुनत (hearing) / जुगल (both) / तन (bodies) / पुलक (thrilled) / मन (minds) / मगन (absorbed) / सुमिरि (remembering) / गुन ग्राम (groups of virtues)
ramacharitamanas::4179.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4179.essence: Ram’s story turns strangers into companions.
ramacharitamanas::4179.simple_meaning: Hanuman shares Ram’s story and his own identity, and that remembrance fills everyone with joy and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4179.simple_insight: There is relief in how quickly love spreads when Ram is spoken of with sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::4179.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just tested Vibhishana’s heart. He answers not with pride, but with Ram's story and his own humble identity. The moment their meeting becomes real, both are swept into joy by remembering Ram's virtues.
ramacharitamanas::4179.modern_relevance: You meet someone who already loves the same teacher, ideal, or cause you do. One honest sentence about what matters most, and the whole room changes.
ramacharitamanas::4179.insight: It shows that sincere remembrance of Ram creates instant connection and shared joy.

ramacharitamanas::4180.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु पवनसुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महुँ जीभ बिचारी॥ तात कबहुँ मोहि जानि अनाथा। करिहहिं कृपा भानुकुल नाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4180.verse_hindi: (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे पवनपुत्र! मेरी रहनी सुनो। मैं यहाँ वैसे ही रहता हूँ जैसे दाँतों के बीच में बेचारी जीभ। हे तात! मुझे अनाथ जानकर सूर्यकुल के नाथ श्री रामचंद्रजी क्या कभी मुझ पर कृपा करेंगे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4180.english_translation: Listen, son of the wind, to my way of living. I live like a tongue trapped between the teeth. O friend, if the Lord of the solar line knows me as helpless, will he ever show me grace?
ramacharitamanas::4180.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / रहनि (way of living) / हमारी (my) / जिमि (like) / दसनन्हि (teeth) / महुँ (within) / जीभ (tongue) / बिचारी (poor, helpless) / तात (friend) / कबहुँ (ever) / मोहि (me) / जानि (knowing) / अनाथा (helpless, without a protector) / करिहहिं (will do) / कृपा (grace) / भानुकुल (solar line) / नाथा (Lord)
ramacharitamanas::4180.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4180.essence: Helplessness becomes the doorway to Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4180.simple_meaning: Vibhishana says he feels trapped in Lanka and helpless, like a tongue caught between teeth. He wonders whether Ram will ever take pity on him.
ramacharitamanas::4180.simple_insight: There is relief in admitting you cannot rescue yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4180.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana speaks to Hanuman after revealing his inner conflict. He sees himself as powerless inside Ravana's world, with no strength to free himself. His question turns the moment into a plea for Ram's mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4180.modern_relevance: You know that moment when you finally admit, after months of pretending, that you cannot fix the mess alone? Vibhishana stands there first, asking for mercy instead of control.
ramacharitamanas::4180.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to honest surrender.

ramacharitamanas::4181.verse_sanskrit: तामस तनु कछु साधन नाहीं। प्रीत न पद सरोज मन माहीं॥ अब मोहि भा भरोस हनुमंता। बिनु हरिकृपा मिलहिं नहिं संता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4181.verse_hindi: मेरा तामसी (राक्षस) शरीर होने से साधन तो कुछ बनता नहीं और न मन में श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणकमलों में प्रेम ही है, परंतु हे हनुमान् ! अब मुझे विश्वास हो गया कि श्री रामजी की मुझ पर कृपा है, क्योंकि हरि की कृपा के बिना संत नहीं मिलते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4181.english_translation: My body is born of darkness, so I have no real practice, and my mind holds no love for the lotus feet of Ram. Yet now, Hanuman, I trust that Ram has shown me grace, because without the divine's grace, noble seekers are not found.
ramacharitamanas::4181.translation_literal: तामस (dark) / तनु (body) / कछु (some) / साधन (practice) / नाहीं (not) / प्रीत (love) / न (not) / पद (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / अब (now) / मोहि (to me) / भा (became) / भरोस (trust) / हनुमंता (Hanuman) / बिनु (without) / हरि-कृपा (the divine's grace) / मिलहिं (are found) / नहिं (not) / संता (noble seekers)
ramacharitamanas::4181.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4181.essence: Grace can reach you before you feel worthy of it.
ramacharitamanas::4181.simple_meaning: Vibhishana says he feels spiritually unprepared, but he now trusts that Ram's grace has reached him. Noble seekers do not arrive by their own power alone.
ramacharitamanas::4181.simple_insight: You do not have to feel qualified before grace can meet you.
ramacharitamanas::4181.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana stands before Hanuman after revealing his loyalty to Ram. He admits his dark nature and lack of devotion, yet he suddenly trusts that Ram has already turned toward him. This is the moment his surrender begins.
ramacharitamanas::4181.modern_relevance: You sit in the therapist's waiting room, convinced you waited too long to ask for help. Then you realize the door was open before you found the courage to knock.
ramacharitamanas::4181.insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to receptive trust, showing that grace can precede your own readiness.

ramacharitamanas::4182.verse_sanskrit: जौं रघुबीर अनुग्रह कीन्हा। तौ तुम्ह मोहि दरसु हठि दीन्हा॥ सुनहु बिभीषन प्रभु कै रीती। करहिं सदा सेवक पर प्रीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::4182.verse_hindi: जब श्री रघुवीर ने कृपा की है, तभी तो आपने मुझे हठ करके (अपनी ओर से) दर्शन दिए हैं। (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे विभीषणजी! सुनिए, प्रभु की यही रीति है कि वे सेवक पर सदा ही प्रेम किया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4182.english_translation: If Raghubir has shown grace, then you have forced me to reveal myself to you. Listen, Vibhishan: the Lord's way is always to love the servant.
ramacharitamanas::4182.translation_literal: जौं (if) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / अनुग्रह (grace) / कीन्हा (did) / तौ (then) / तुम्ह (you) / मोहि (me) / दरसु (appearance / sight) / हठि (by insistence) / दीन्हा (gave)॥ / सुनहु (listen) / बिभीषन (Vibhishan) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कै (of) / रीती (way) / तीति (way / custom) / करहिं (do) / सदा (always) / सेवक (servant) / पर (toward) / प्रीति (love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4182.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4182.essence: Grace arrives first, and love naturally follows the servant.
ramacharitamanas::4182.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Vibhishan that their meeting happened only because Ram was gracious. He says Ram's nature is to always love and care for those who serve him.
ramacharitamanas::4182.simple_insight: Devotion is not chasing the divine; it is discovering that grace was already reaching toward you.
ramacharitamanas::4182.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally met Vibhishan, the lonely brother who has turned toward Ram. Vibhishan feels unworthy and cut off, but Hanuman answers with reassurance: this meeting itself is Ram's grace, and Ram naturally loves anyone who serves him.
ramacharitamanas::4182.modern_relevance: You finally call the person who helped you through a hard season, and they act like it was nothing. That quiet warmth is what Hanuman is pointing to: true love moves toward service without keeping score.
ramacharitamanas::4182.insight: It shifts the mind from self-doubt to trust in a relationship that welcomes sincere service.

ramacharitamanas::4183.verse_sanskrit: कहहु कवन मैं परम कुलीना। कपि चंचल सबहीं बिधि हीना॥ प्रात लेइ जो नाम हमारा। तेहि दिन ताहि न मिलै अहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4183.verse_hindi: भला कहिए, मैं ही कौन बड़ा कुलीन हूँ? (जाति का) चंचल वानर हूँ और सब प्रकार से नीच हूँ, प्रातःकाल जो हम लोगों (बंदरों) का नाम ले ले तो उस दिन उसे भोजन न मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4183.english_translation: What high birth do I have? I am a restless monkey, lacking every virtue. If someone even names us monkeys at dawn, that person will not get food that day.
ramacharitamanas::4183.translation_literal: कहहु (tell me) / कवन (which) / मैं (I) / परम (highest) / कुलीना (of noble birth) / कपि (monkey) / चंचल (restless) / सबहीं (all) / बिधि (ways) / हीना (lacking) ॥ / प्रात (at dawn) / लेइ (taking) / जो (who) / नाम (name) / हमारा (our) / तेहि (that) / दिन (day) / ताहि (to him) / न (not) / मिलै (gets) / अहारा (food) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4183.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4183.essence: The one who drops pride becomes fit for grace.
ramacharitamanas::4183.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he is not noble or impressive by himself. He is a monkey with no special merit, and even his name brings bad luck to others. His worth comes only through Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4183.simple_insight: Humility can become a doorway to grace instead of a wound to pride.
ramacharitamanas::4183.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is speaking to Vibhishana after being found out as a stranger. Rather than claim status, he lowers himself completely, calling himself unworthy and insignificant. That humility prepares the way for trust and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4183.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone seems polished, connected, and important. Instead of performing, you admit you are not the center. That honesty can open more doors than self-promotion.
ramacharitamanas::4183.insight: It shifts the mind from proving status to receiving grace through humility.

ramacharitamanas::4184.verse_sanskrit: अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु मोहू पर रघुबीर। कीन्हीं कृपा सुमिरि गुन भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4184.verse_hindi: हे सखा! सुनिए, मैं ऐसा अधम हूँ, पर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने तो मुझ पर भी कृपा ही की है। भगवान् के गुणों का स्मरण करके हनुमान् जी के दोनों नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4184.english_translation: O friend, listen: I am so lowly, yet Lord Raghubir has shown mercy even to me. Remembering the Lord's qualities, tears filled Hanuman's eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4184.translation_literal: अस (thus) / मैं (I) / अधम (lowly) / सखा (friend) / सुनु (listen) / मोहू (even me) / पर (upon) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / कीन्हीं (did) / कृपा (grace) / सुमिरि (remembering) / गुन (qualities) / भरे (filled) / बिलोचन (eyes) / नीर (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::4184.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4184.essence: Ram's grace reaches you before your worthiness does.
ramacharitamanas::4184.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he is unworthy, yet Ram has still shown him kindness. Thinking of Ram's qualities moves him to tears.
ramacharitamanas::4184.simple_insight: You do not have to be worthy first; devotion itself opens the heart.
ramacharitamanas::4184.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just been speaking humbly to Vibhishana about Ram's favor. He calls himself lowly, yet says Ram's grace reached him anyway. As he remembers Ram's qualities, his eyes fill with tears, showing how bhakti softens pride.
ramacharitamanas::4184.modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet car after a hard day, feeling like you have failed too many times to be loved well. Then one small memory of kindness breaks you open again.
ramacharitamanas::4184.insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to receptive devotion, where grace matters more than status.

ramacharitamanas::4185.verse_sanskrit: जानतहूँ अस स्वामि बिसारी। फिरहिं ते काहे न होहिं दुखारी॥ एहि बिधि कहत राम गुन ग्रामा। पावा अनिर्बाच्य बिश्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4185.verse_hindi: जो जानते हुए भी ऐसे स्वामी (श्री रघुनाथजी) को भुलाकर (विषयों के पीछे) भटकते फिरते हैं, वे दुःखी क्यों न हों? इस प्रकार श्री रामजी के गुण समूहों को कहते हुए उन्होंने अनिर्वचनीय (परम) शांति प्राप्त की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4185.english_translation: Those who forget such a master even after knowing him still wander after pleasures—why would they not suffer? In this way, speaking the many virtues of Ram, he attained indescribable peace.
ramacharitamanas::4185.translation_literal: जानतहूँ (even knowing) / अस (such) / स्वामि (master) / बिसारी (having forgotten) / फिरहिं (wander) / ते (those) / काहे (why) / न (not) / होहिं (become) / दुखारी (sorrowful) ॥ एहि बिधि (in this manner) / कहत (speaking) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / ग्रामा (group/collection) / पावा (he attained) / अनिर्बाच्य (indescribable) / बिश्रामा (rest, peace) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4185.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4185.essence: Forgetting Ram brings suffering; remembering him brings peace.
ramacharitamanas::4185.simple_meaning: Even after knowing Ram, people who forget him and chase other things end up in suffering. Speaking of Ram's virtues brings Hanuman deep peace.
ramacharitamanas::4185.simple_insight: Forgetting what truly matters creates restlessness; remembering it steadies the heart.
ramacharitamanas::4185.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already found Sita's trail and is speaking from the fullness of devotion. He reflects that anyone who knows Ram yet turns away into distractions will suffer. As he keeps praising Ram, his own mind settles into unspoken peace.
ramacharitamanas::4185.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and somehow lose an hour. The noise feels normal until you remember what actually holds your life together.
ramacharitamanas::4185.insight: It shifts attention from scattered wanting back to the source of real steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::4186.verse_sanskrit: पुनि सब कथा बिभीषन कही। जेहि बिधि जनकसुता तहँ रही॥ तब हनुमंत कहा सुनु भ्राता। देखी चहउँ जानकी माता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4186.verse_hindi: फिर विभीषणजी ने, श्री जानकीजी जिस प्रकार वहाँ (लंका में) रहती थीं, वह सब कथा कही। तब हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे भाई सुनो, मैं जानकी माता को देखता चाहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4186.english_translation: Then Vibhishana told the whole story of how Janaki had been living there. Then Hanuman said, "Brother, listen. I want to see Mother Janaki."
ramacharitamanas::4186.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / कही (told) / जेहि बिधि (in the manner that) / जनकसुता (Janak's daughter, Sita) / तहँ (there) / रही (remained) / तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / कहा (said) / सुनु (listen) / भ्राता (brother) / देखी (to see) / चहउँ (I want) / जानकी (Janaki) / माता (Mother)
ramacharitamanas::4186.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4186.essence: Devotion is not satisfied by success; it wants presence.
ramacharitamanas::4186.simple_meaning: After hearing how Sita has been living in Lanka, Hanuman says he wants to see her. His mission is no longer just to find her; it becomes a direct, heartfelt longing to behold her.
ramacharitamanas::4186.simple_insight: Love turns a task into a living ache.
ramacharitamanas::4186.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just explained how Sita has been surviving there. Hanuman, who crossed the ocean on Ram's mission, now speaks like a devoted son: he wants to see Janaki himself. The search becomes personal and intimate.
ramacharitamanas::4186.modern_relevance: You finally reach the hospital room after days of worry, but standing at the door is not enough. You need to see the person you came for, hear their voice, know they are really there.
ramacharitamanas::4186.insight: It shifts action from mere completion to loving presence.

ramacharitamanas::4187.verse_sanskrit: हनुमान् जी का अशोक वाटिका में सीताजी को देकर दुःखी होना और रावण का सीताजी को भय दिखलाना जुगुति बिभीषन सकल सुनाई। चलेउ पवन सुत बिदा कराई॥ करि सोइ रूप गयउ पुनि तहवाँ। बन असोक सीता रह जहवाँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4187.verse_hindi: विभीषणजी ने (माता के दर्शन की) सब युक्तियाँ (उपाय) कह सुनाईं। तब हनुमान् जी विदा लेकर चले। फिर वही (पहले का मसक सरीखा) रूप धरकर वहाँ गए, जहाँ अशोक वन में (वन के जिस भाग में) सीताजी रहती थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4187.english_translation: Vibhishana explained every way to reach Sita. Then Hanuman took leave and went back in the same form, to the part of Ashoka grove where Sita stayed.
ramacharitamanas::4187.translation_literal: जुगुति (ways / methods) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / सकल (all) / सुनाई (told) / चलेउ (went) / पवन सुत (son of the wind) / बिदा (farewell / leave) / कराई (having taken) / करि (doing) / सोइ (that same) / रूप (form) / गयउ (went) / पुनि (again) / तहवाँ (there) / बन (grove / forest) / असोक (Ashoka) / सीता (Sita) / रह (stayed) / जहवाँ (where)
ramacharitamanas::4187.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4187.essence: The path is revealed; the meeting is still ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4187.simple_meaning: Vibhishana gives Hanuman the route and method. Hanuman leaves, returns in the same disguise, and goes to the part of Ashoka grove where Sita is kept.
ramacharitamanas::4187.simple_insight: Sometimes the right move is quiet, exact, and hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4187.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has finished explaining how Sita can be approached safely. Hanuman, already inside the enemy city, takes leave and slips back in the same tiny form. This verse is a bridge into the meeting with Sita, not the meeting itself.
ramacharitamanas::4187.modern_relevance: You get the address, the timing, and the plan before slipping into the room where someone is waiting for you. The real work is still ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4187.insight: It keeps the focus on preparation and stealth, not on emotional resolution yet.

ramacharitamanas::4188.verse_sanskrit: देखि मनहि महुँ कीन्ह प्रनामा। बैठेहिं बीति जात निसि जामा॥ कृस तनु सीस जटा एक बेनी। जपति हृदयँ रघुपति गुन श्रेनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4188.verse_hindi: सीताजी को देखकर हनुमान् जी ने उन्हें मन ही में प्रणाम किया। उन्हें बैठे ही बैठे रात्रि के चारों पहर बीत जाते हैं। शरीर दुबला हो गया है, सिर पर जटाओं की एक वेणी (लट) है। हृदय में श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूहों का जाप (स्मरण) करती रहती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4188.english_translation: Seeing Sita, Hanuman bowed to her inwardly. He sat there as the night’s four watches passed. Her body had grown thin, her hair was tied in one braid, and her heart kept repeating the qualities of Raghupati.
ramacharitamanas::4188.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / मनहि महुँ (within the mind) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामा (bow) / बैठेहिं (while seated) / बीति जात (passing) / निसि (night) / जामा (watches)॥ / कृस (thin) / तनु (body) / सीस (head) / जटा (matted hair) / एक (one) / बेनी (braid) / जपति (repeating) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / गुन श्रेनी (rows of qualities)॥
ramacharitamanas::4188.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4188.essence: True devotion begins with silent respect and steady remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::4188.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees Sita and bows to her inwardly. She sits in deep sorrow, worn thin by waiting, while her mind stays fixed on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4188.simple_insight: Love can stay steady even in unbearable separation.
ramacharitamanas::4188.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s Ashoka grove, Hanuman has finally found Sita. He bows to her in his heart and watches her through the night. She is exhausted, grieving, and still holding Ram in her mind. The scene prepares the emotional meeting that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4188.modern_relevance: You finally reach the person you came to help, and they look shattered from waiting. Before words come, respect and tenderness do.
ramacharitamanas::4188.insight: It teaches you to meet suffering with quiet reverence before trying to fix it.

ramacharitamanas::4189.verse_sanskrit: निज पद नयन दिएँ मन राम पद कमल लीन। परम दुखी भा पवनसुत देखि जानकी दीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4189.verse_hindi: श्री जानकीजी नेत्रों को अपने चरणों में लगाए हुए हैं (नीचे की ओर देख रही हैं) और मन श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों में लीन है। जानकीजी को दीन (दुःखी) देखकर पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी बहुत ही दुःखी हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4189.english_translation: Sita’s eyes rest on her own feet, while her mind rests on Ram’s lotus feet. Seeing Janaki so helpless, Hanuman became deeply distressed.
ramacharitamanas::4189.translation_literal: निज (own) / पद (feet) / नयन (eyes) / दिएँ (having placed) / मन (mind) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / लीन (absorbed) / परम (greatly) / दुखी (distressed) / भा (became) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / देखि (seeing) / जानकी (Janaki) / दीन (helpless, sorrowful)
ramacharitamanas::4189.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4189.essence: Sorrow can bend the body without moving the heart from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4189.simple_meaning: Sita is physically bowed in sorrow, but inwardly fixed on Ram. Hanuman feels deep pain when he sees her helpless state.
ramacharitamanas::4189.simple_insight: Real devotion does not erase pain; it makes another’s suffering impossible to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::4189.detailed_meaning: Hidden in Lanka’s Ashoka grove, Hanuman finally sees Sita. Her body is worn down by grief, yet her mind still rests on Ram. That sight breaks Hanuman’s heart, because her devotion and suffering are both unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::4189.modern_relevance: You visit someone in the hospital and they smile weakly while still asking about the person they love most. Their devotion is intact, and that makes their suffering hit even harder.
ramacharitamanas::4189.insight: It teaches you to notice both inner faith and outer pain at once, instead of reducing a person to only what you see.

ramacharitamanas::4190.verse_sanskrit: तरु पल्लव महँ रहा लुकाई। करइ बिचार करौं का भाई॥ तेहि अवसर रावनु तहँ आवा। संग नारि बहु किएँ बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4190.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी वृक्ष के पत्तों में छिप रहे और विचार करने लगे कि हे भाई! क्या करूँ (इनका दुःख कैसे दूर करूँ)? उसी समय बहुत सी स्त्रियों को साथ लिए सज-धजकर रावण वहाँ आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4190.english_translation: Hanuman hid among the leaves of a tree and thought, 'Brother, what should I do?' At that moment, Ravana arrived there, adorned and accompanied by many women.
ramacharitamanas::4190.translation_literal: तरु (tree) / पल्लव (leaves) / महँ (in) / रहा (remained) / लुकाई (hiding) / करइ (does) / बिचार (thought) / करौं (shall I do) / का (what) / भाई (brother) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / रावनु (Ravana) / तहँ (there) / आवा (came) / संग (with) / नारि (women) / बहु (many) / किएँ (adorned) / बनावा (made/arrayed)
ramacharitamanas::4190.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4190.essence: Hidden patience can be the smartest form of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4190.simple_meaning: Hanuman hides in the tree and wonders what to do next. Then Ravana arrives, surrounded by women and dressed up.
ramacharitamanas::4190.simple_insight: Sometimes the right move is to wait quietly until the moment reveals itself.
ramacharitamanas::4190.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita and is watching from concealment. He is not acting yet; he is holding himself back, thinking through the next step. Then Ravana enters the scene with royal display, setting up the confrontation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4190.modern_relevance: You spot the person you need to avoid at the same event and stay still behind the crowd, waiting for the right opening instead of rushing in.
ramacharitamanas::4190.insight: It teaches restraint before action, so the next move comes from awareness rather than impulse.

ramacharitamanas::4191.verse_sanskrit: बहु बिधि खल सीतहि समुझावा। साम दान भय भेद देखावा॥ कह रावनु सुनु सुमुखि सयानी। मंदोदरी आदि सब रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4191.verse_hindi: उस दुष्ट ने सीताजी को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। साम, दान, भय और भेद दिखलाया। रावण ने कहा- हे सुमुखि! हे सयानी! सुनो! मंदोदरी आदि सब रानियों को- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4191.english_translation: The wicked one tried many ways to persuade Sita, showing her conciliation, gifts, fear, and division. Ravana said, 'Listen, beautiful and wise one. Mandodari and all the queens...'
ramacharitamanas::4191.translation_literal: बहु बिधि (many ways) / खल (the wicked one) / सीतहि (to Sita) / समुझावा (tried to persuade) / साम (conciliation) / दान (gifts) / भय (fear) / भेद (division) / देखावा (showed) / कह (said) / रावनु (Ravana) / सुनु (listen) / सुमुखि (beautiful-faced one) / सयानी (wise one) / मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / आदि (and others) / सब (all) / रानी (queens)
ramacharitamanas::4191.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4191.essence: Power without reverence turns into coercion.
ramacharitamanas::4191.simple_meaning: Ravana tries every tactic he can think of to win Sita over: kindness, gifts, threats, and manipulation. He speaks as if flattery and power can bend her will.
ramacharitamanas::4191.simple_insight: Pressure can wear many masks, but it is still pressure.
ramacharitamanas::4191.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman watches from hiding as Ravana stands before Sita and tries every method of control. He flatters her, threatens her, and even brings his queens into the scene. The moment shows the full force of Ravana's desperation and ego.
ramacharitamanas::4191.modern_relevance: Someone keeps texting after you said no, first sweetly, then angrily, then through mutual friends. The tactics change, but the attempt is the same.
ramacharitamanas::4191.insight: It exposes how manipulation shifts forms when direct control fails.

ramacharitamanas::4192.verse_sanskrit: तव अनुचरीं करउँ पन मोरा। एक बार बिलोकु मम ओरा॥ तृन धरि ओट कहति बैदेही। सुमिरि अवधपति परम सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4192.verse_hindi: मैं तुम्हारी दासी बना दूँगा, यह मेरा प्रण है। तुम एक बार मेरी ओर देखो तो सही! अपने परम स्नेही कोसलाधीश श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करके जानकीजी तिनके की आड़ (परदा) करके कहने लगीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4192.english_translation: I will become your servant; that is my vow. Look at me just once. Hiding herself behind a blade of grass, Vaidehi remembered the lord of Ayodhya, her beloved protector.
ramacharitamanas::4192.translation_literal: तव (your) / अनुचरीं (female attendant; servant) / करउँ (I will make) / पन (vow) / मोरा (my) / एक बार (one time) / बिलोकु (look) / मम (my) / ओरा (side; toward) / तृन (grass) / धरि (placing) / ओट (screen; cover) / कहति (saying) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / सुमिरि (remembering) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / परम (supreme) / सनेही (beloved)
ramacharitamanas::4192.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4192.essence: True loyalty stays with the beloved even under threat.
ramacharitamanas::4192.simple_meaning: Sita, hidden and pleading, asks Ravana to look at her once while she remembers Ram, her beloved protector.
ramacharitamanas::4192.simple_insight: Even in fear, love keeps a person inwardly anchored to what is sacred and safe.
ramacharitamanas::4192.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressuring Sita to yield. Hidden behind a blade of grass, she answers with quiet dignity: she will serve only if he can truly win her over. But her mind is already with Ram, the beloved lord of Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::4192.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you to compromise your values in a room where you feel cornered. You stay inwardly loyal to the person, principle, or love that still protects your heart.
ramacharitamanas::4192.insight: It shifts the mind from outward pressure to inward allegiance.

ramacharitamanas::4193.verse_sanskrit: सुनु दसमुख खद्योत प्रकासा। कबहुँ कि नलिनी करइ बिकासा॥ अस मन समुझु कहति जानकी। खल सुधि नहिं रघुबीर बान की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4193.verse_hindi: हे दशमुख! सुन, जुगनू के प्रकाश से कभी कमलिनी खिल सकती है? जानकीजी फिर कहती हैं- तू (अपने लिए भी) ऐसा ही मन में समझ ले। रे दुष्ट! तुझे श्री रघुवीर के बाण की खबर नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4193.english_translation: O ten-faced one, listen: can a water lily ever bloom by the light of a firefly? Understand this in your own mind as well. O wicked one, you do not know the force of Raghubir's arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4193.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / दसमुख (ten-faced one) / खद्योत (firefly) / प्रकासा (light, radiance) / कबहुँ (ever) / कि (can) / नलिनी (water lily) / करइ (does, makes) / बिकासा (blooming, opening) / अस (like this) / मन (mind) / समुझु (understand) / कहति (saying) / जानकी (Janaki) / खल (wicked one) / सुधि (news, awareness) / नहिं (not) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बान की (of arrows)
ramacharitamanas::4193.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4193.essence: Tiny force cannot touch what is protected by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4193.simple_meaning: Sita tells Ravana that his tiny power cannot overcome Ram's strength. She warns him to understand his own weakness before it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4193.simple_insight: False power always looks bigger to itself than it really is.
ramacharitamanas::4193.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps trying to break Sita's resolve with threats and persuasion. Sita answers without fear: his power is as small as a firefly's light beside a lotus opening. This is her quiet refusal and warning.
ramacharitamanas::4193.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you in a meeting, acting louder than they are strong. You do not need to match the noise to know the truth of the situation.
ramacharitamanas::4193.insight: It teaches you to see intimidation clearly and refuse to be overawed by it.

ramacharitamanas::4194.verse_sanskrit: सठ सूनें हरि आनेहि मोही। अधम निलज्ज लाज नहिं तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4194.verse_hindi: रे पापी! तू मुझे सूने में हर लाया है। रे अधम! निर्लज्ज! तुझे लज्जा नहीं आती? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4194.english_translation: You shameless fool, you brought me here in secret.
ramacharitamanas::4194.translation_literal: सठ (fool) / सूनें (secretly, in a hidden place) / हरि (carried away) / आनेहि (you brought) / मोही (me) । अधम (base one) / निलज्ज (shameless) / लाज (shame) / नहिं (not) / तोही (to you) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4194.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4194.essence: Hidden cruelty becomes more shameful when it meets clear speech.
ramacharitamanas::4194.simple_meaning: Sita rebukes Ravana for abducting her in secret and for having no shame.
ramacharitamanas::4194.simple_insight: Some actions are so dishonourable that they expose the actor more than the victim.
ramacharitamanas::4194.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is trapped in Ravana's power, but she does not surrender her dignity. After refusing his advances, she turns his own behaviour into a moral accusation, calling out the shame of his secret abduction.
ramacharitamanas::4194.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a private message, a closed room, or a manipulative conversation, hoping silence will make you smaller. Her words remind you that dishonour does not become power just because it hides.
ramacharitamanas::4194.insight: It names wrongdoing directly, refusing to let fear or isolation soften the truth.

ramacharitamanas::4195.verse_sanskrit: आपुहि सुनि खद्योत सम रामहि भानु समान। परुष बचन सुनि काढ़ि असि बोला अति खिसिआन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4195.verse_hindi: अपने को जुगनू के समान और रामचंद्रजी को सूर्य के समान सुनकर और सीताजी के कठोर वचनों को सुनकर रावण तलवार निकालकर बड़े गुस्से में आकर बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4195.english_translation: Hearing himself compared to a firefly and Ramchandra to the sun, and hearing Sita's harsh words, Ravana drew his sword and spoke in great fury.
ramacharitamanas::4195.translation_literal: आपुहि (himself) / सुनि (hearing) / खद्योत (firefly) / सम (like) / रामहि (Ram) / भानु (sun) / समान (equal to) / परुष (harsh) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / काढ़ि (drew out) / असि (sword) / बोला (spoke) / अति (very) / खिसिआन (angry)
ramacharitamanas::4195.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4195.essence: Pride cannot bear comparison, so it reaches for force.
ramacharitamanas::4195.simple_meaning: Ravana is insulted by Sita's words and enraged enough to draw his sword.
ramacharitamanas::4195.simple_insight: Pride turns a spoken truth into instant violence.
ramacharitamanas::4195.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just compared Ravana's weakness to Ram's brilliance. Her words strike his ego, and he reacts like an injured tyrant, drawing his sword in fury. The scene is still building toward his threat.
ramacharitamanas::4195.modern_relevance: Someone points out your blind spot in a meeting, and your first urge is to snap back. That flash of anger reveals how fragile pride can be.
ramacharitamanas::4195.insight: It shows how wounded ego reacts before reason can return.

ramacharitamanas::4196.verse_sanskrit: सीता तैं मम कृत अपमाना। कटिहउँ तव सिर कठिन कृपाना॥ नाहिं त सपदि मानु मम बानी। सुमुखि होति न त जीवन हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4196.verse_hindi: सीता! तूने मेरा अपनाम किया है। मैं तेरा सिर इस कठोर कृपाण से काट डालूँगा। नहीं तो (अब भी) जल्दी मेरी बात मान ले। हे सुमुखि! नहीं तो जीवन से हाथ धोना पड़ेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4196.english_translation: Sita, you have insulted me. I will cut off your head with this sharp sword. Obey my words at once, fair-faced one, or you will lose your life.
ramacharitamanas::4196.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / तैं (you have) / मम (my) / कृत (done) / अपमाना (insult) / कटिहउँ (I will cut off) / तव (your) / सिर (head) / कठिन (hard/sharp) / कृपाना (sword) / नाहिं (if not) / त (then) / सपदि (at once) / मानु (accept) / मम (my) / बानी (words) / सुमुखि (fair-faced one) / होति (becomes) / न (not) / त (then) / जीवन (life) / हानी (loss)
ramacharitamanas::4196.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4196.essence: Ego, when challenged, reaches for violence.
ramacharitamanas::4196.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens Sita with death unless she obeys him immediately.
ramacharitamanas::4196.simple_insight: Pride turns fear into cruelty, and cruelty into self-destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4196.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has dragged Sita into his power and is enraged by her refusal. Her fearless words have wounded his pride, and he answers with a violent threat. This moment exposes how ego turns rejection into rage.
ramacharitamanas::4196.modern_relevance: Someone feels rejected in a relationship and suddenly starts speaking in threats, blame, or ultimatums. The real wound is not the refusal — it is the bruised ego underneath it.
ramacharitamanas::4196.insight: It shows how wounded pride tries to regain control through intimidation.

ramacharitamanas::4197.verse_sanskrit: स्याम सरोज दाम सम सुंदर। प्रभु भुज करि कर सम दसकंधर॥ सो भुज कंठ कि तव असि घोरा। सुनु सठ अस प्रवान पन मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4197.verse_hindi: (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे दशग्रीव! प्रभु की भुजा जो श्याम कमल की माला के समान सुंदर और हाथी की सूँड के समान (पुष्ट तथा विशाल) है, या तो वह भुजा ही मेरे कंठ में पड़ेगी या तेरी भयानक तलवार ही। रे शठ! सुन, यही मेरा सच्चा प्रण है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4197.english_translation: Sita said: "O Dashanan, the beautiful arm of the Lord is like a garland of dark lotuses and strong as an elephant's trunk. Either that arm will rest on my neck, or your dreadful sword will. Listen, fool — this is my true vow."
ramacharitamanas::4197.translation_literal: स्याम (dark) / सरोज (lotus) / दाम (garland) / सम (like) / सुंदर (beautiful) / प्रभु (Lord's) / भुज (arm) / करि (elephant) / कर (trunk) / सम (like) / दसकंधर (Dashanan) / सो (that) / भुज (arm) / कंठ (neck) / कि (or) / तव (your) / असि (sword) / घोरा (terrible) / सुनु (listen) / सठ (fool) / अस (this) / प्रवान (true) / पन (vow) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::4197.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4197.essence: Love becomes unbreakable when fear no longer decides.
ramacharitamanas::4197.simple_meaning: Sita refuses Ravana's threat and declares her vow: only Ram's arm or Ravana's sword will reach her neck.
ramacharitamanas::4197.simple_insight: Steadfast love can stand in front of fear without bending.
ramacharitamanas::4197.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just threatened Sita with death if she will not submit. Instead of pleading, she names Ram's beauty and strength, then answers with a vow: only Ram's arm or Ravana's sword will touch her neck. Her devotion has become unshakable courage.
ramacharitamanas::4197.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with an ultimatum in a message thread, expecting panic or compromise. You pause, remember what you will not betray, and answer from that center instead of from fear.
ramacharitamanas::4197.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to vow-keeping under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4198.verse_sanskrit: चंद्रहास हरु मम परितापं। रघुपति बिरह अनल संजातं॥ सीतल निसित बहसि बर धारा। कह सीता हरु मम दुख भारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4198.verse_hindi: सीताजी कहती हैं- हे चंद्रहास (तलवार)! श्री रघुनाथजी के विरह की अग्नि से उत्पन्न मेरी बड़ी भारी जलन को तू हर ले, हे तलवार! तू शीतल, तीव्र और श्रेष्ठ धारा बहाती है (अर्थात् तेरी धारा ठंडी और तेज है), तू मेरे दुःख के बोझ को हर ले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4198.english_translation: O Chandrahasa, remove my burning pain. The fire of separation from Raghupati has arisen in me. You flow as a cool, sharp, excellent blade. O Sita says, remove the heavy burden of my sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4198.translation_literal: चंद्रहास (Chandrahasa, sword) / हरु (remove) / मम (my) / परितापं (burning pain) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / बिरह (separation) / अनल (fire) / संजातं (arisen) / सीतल (cool) / निसित (sharp) / बहसि (you flow) / बर (excellent) / धारा (blade, stream) / कह (said) / सीता (Sita) / हरु (remove) / मम (my) / दुख (sorrow) / भारा (burden)
ramacharitamanas::4198.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4198.essence: Separation burns so hot that even a sword feels like mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4198.simple_meaning: Sita, overwhelmed by separation from Ram, asks a sword to cut away her pain and heavy sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4198.simple_insight: Longing can become so intense that even pain feels easier than waiting.
ramacharitamanas::4198.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is trapped in Ravana’s palace and consumed by Ram’s absence. Her sorrow has become a fire inside her, and in that desperate moment she speaks to a sword as if it could cool her suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4198.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone at 2 a.m., waiting for one message that would calm everything. When longing gets that sharp, even a small sign can feel like rescue.
ramacharitamanas::4198.insight: It reveals how separation can overwhelm the mind, and how devotion can speak through raw pain instead of composure.

ramacharitamanas::4199.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बचन पुनि मारन धावा। मयतनयाँ कहि नीति बुझावा॥ कहेसि सकल निसिचरिन्ह बोलाई। सीतहि बहु बिधि त्रासहु जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4199.verse_hindi: सीताजी के ये वचन सुनते ही वह मारने दौड़ा। तब मय दानव की पुत्री मन्दोदरी ने नीति कहकर उसे समझाया। तब रावण ने सब दासियों को बुलाकर कहा कि जाकर सीता को बहुत प्रकार से भय दिखलाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4199.english_translation: Hearing Sita's words, he rushed to kill her. Then Mandodari, daughter of Maya, tried to counsel him with reason. Ravana then called all the female attendants and ordered them to go and frighten Sita in every way.
ramacharitamanas::4199.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / पुनि (again) / मारन (to kill) / धावा (rushed) / मयतनयाँ (daughter of Maya, Mandodari) / कहि (saying) / नीति (reason / policy) / बुझावा (explained) / कहेसि (he said) / सकल (all) / निसिचरिन्ह (female attendants of the night-dwellers) / बोलाई (calling) / सीतहि (to Sita) / बहु बिधि (many ways) / त्रासहु (frighten) / जाई (go)
ramacharitamanas::4199.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4199.essence: Pride, when checked, often turns to intimidation.
ramacharitamanas::4199.simple_meaning: Ravana reacts with rage, then shifts to intimidation. Mandodari tries to restrain him, but he orders his attendants to scare Sita instead.
ramacharitamanas::4199.simple_insight: Unchecked anger first lashes out, then looks for smaller ways to harm.
ramacharitamanas::4199.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita's refusal has wounded Ravana's pride. He lunges toward violence, but Mandodari tries to steady him with practical counsel. He does not soften; he turns his fury on Sita's attendants and orders them to terrorize her.
ramacharitamanas::4199.modern_relevance: You get a harsh message and instantly want to strike back. A calmer voice tries to interrupt, but your hurt still looks for someone weaker to intimidate.
ramacharitamanas::4199.insight: It shows how wounded ego turns from direct attack to calculated cruelty.

ramacharitamanas::4200.verse_sanskrit: मास दिवस महुँ कहा न माना। तौ मैं मारबि काढ़ि कृपाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4200.verse_hindi: यदि महीने भर में यह कहा न माने तो मैं इसे तलवार निकालकर मार डालूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4200.english_translation: If she does not agree within a month, I will draw my sword and kill her.
ramacharitamanas::4200.translation_literal: मास (month) / दिवस (days) / महुँ (within) / कहा (said) / न (not) / माना (accepted) / तौ (then) / मैं (I) / मारबि (will kill) / काढ़ि (drawing out) / कृपाना (sword)
ramacharitamanas::4200.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4200.essence: Threats begin where real influence has ended.
ramacharitamanas::4200.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens Sita with death if she does not give in within a month.
ramacharitamanas::4200.simple_insight: Cruel pressure often reveals fear disguised as power.
ramacharitamanas::4200.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already failed to break Sita's resolve. Frustrated, he turns to threats, setting a one-month limit before violence. The line shows his desperation and the hardening of the situation around Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4200.modern_relevance: A person sends one last message: answer by Friday, or else. The deadline is really a mask for helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::4200.insight: It exposes how coercion replaces persuasion when ego cannot accept refusal.

ramacharitamanas::4201.verse_sanskrit: भवन गयउ दसकंधर इहाँ पिसाचिनि बृंद। सीतहि त्रास देखावहिं धरहिं रूप बहु मंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::4201.verse_hindi: (यों कहकर) रावण घर चला गया। यहाँ राक्षसियों के समूह बहुत से बुरे रूप धरकर सीताजी को भय दिखलाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4201.english_translation: Ravana went home, and there the women-demons took many ugly forms to frighten Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4201.translation_literal: भवन (home / palace) / गयउ (went) / दसकंधर (the ten-necked one, Ravana) / इहाँ (here) / पिसाचिनि (female demons) / बृंद (group) / सीतहि (Sita) / त्रास (fear) / देखावहिं (showed) / धरहिं (they assumed) / रूप (forms) / बहु (many) / मंद (ugly / vile)
ramacharitamanas::4201.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4201.essence: Cruelty tries to win by multiplying fear around the vulnerable.
ramacharitamanas::4201.simple_meaning: Ravana leaves, and his demon attendants try to scare Sita by taking on many ugly forms.
ramacharitamanas::4201.simple_insight: Fear often arrives in a crowd, not just in a single threat.
ramacharitamanas::4201.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has gone back to his palace after threatening Sita. Left behind, his demon women swarm around her, twisting their faces and forms to terrorize her. The verse is a scene-setting detail in the buildup to Trijata's compassionate intervention.
ramacharitamanas::4201.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the argument ends, but the pressure still hangs there. Then the people around you start adding their own fear, making the moment feel even smaller.
ramacharitamanas::4201.insight: It shows how intimidation multiplies when fear is used as a group tactic.

ramacharitamanas::4202.verse_sanskrit: त्रिजटा नाम राच्छसी एका। राम चरन रति निपुन बिबेका॥ सबन्हौ बोलि सुनाएसि सपना। सीतहि सेइ करहु हित अपना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4202.verse_hindi: उनमें एक त्रिजटा नाम की राक्षसी थी। उसकी श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में प्रीति थी और वह विवेक (ज्ञान) में निपुण थी। उसने सबों को बुलाकर अपना स्वप्न सुनाया और कहा- सीताजी की सेवा करके अपना कल्याण कर लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4202.english_translation: There was a demoness named Trijata who was skilled in clear seeing and loved Ram's feet. She called everyone and told them her dream: serve Sita and do what is good for you.
ramacharitamanas::4202.translation_literal: त्रिजटा (Trijata) / नाम (named) / राच्छसी (demoness) / एका (one) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love) / निपुन (skilled) / बिबेका (in clear seeing) ॥ / सबन्हौ (everyone) / बोलि (calling) / सुनाएसि (she told) / सपना (dream) / सीतहि (to Sita) / सेइ (serve) / करहु (do) / हित (good) / अपना (your own) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4202.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4202.essence: Clear seeing turns loyalty into service.
ramacharitamanas::4202.simple_meaning: Trijata, a demoness loyal to Ram, sees clearly enough to protect Sita and advise the other women to serve her for their own good.
ramacharitamanas::4202.simple_insight: Real vision softens hostility and turns fear into care.
ramacharitamanas::4202.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the demonesses are frightening Sita, but one among them, Trijata, sees differently. Loyal to Ram, she understands the dream as a warning and tells the others to serve Sita instead of harming her.
ramacharitamanas::4202.modern_relevance: At work, everyone is mocking the person under pressure, but one colleague quietly helps instead of joining in. That small act of loyalty changes the room.
ramacharitamanas::4202.insight: It shifts you from crowd cruelty to protective action guided by clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4203.verse_sanskrit: सपनें बानर लंका जारी। जातुधान सेना सब मारी॥ खर आरूढ़ नगन दससीसा। मुंडित सिर खंडित भुज बीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4203.verse_hindi: स्वप्न (मैंने देखा कि) एक बंदर ने लंका जला दी। राक्षसों की सारी सेना मार डाली गई। रावण नंगा है और गदहे पर सवार है। उसके सिर मुँडे हुए हैं, बीसों भुजाएँ कटी हुई हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4203.english_translation: In the dream, a monkey burned Lanka. The entire army of demons was slain. Ravana rode naked on a donkey, with his head shaved and all twenty arms cut off.
ramacharitamanas::4203.translation_literal: सपनें (in a dream) / बानर (monkey) / लंका (Lanka) / जारी (burned) / जातुधान (demons) / सेना (army) / सब (all) / मारी (were slain) / खर (donkey) / आरूढ़ (mounted) / नगन (naked) / दससीसा (ten-headed one, Ravana) / मुंडित (shaved) / सिर (head) / खंडित (cut) / भुज (arms) / बीसा (twenty)
ramacharitamanas::4203.speaker: Trijata
ramacharitamanas::4203.essence: The nightmare of oppression is already breaking in the mind of a true witness.
ramacharitamanas::4203.simple_meaning: Trijata dreams that a monkey destroys Lanka, Ravana is humiliated, and his army is wiped out. The dream is a sign that Sita's suffering will end.
ramacharitamanas::4203.simple_insight: Hope can arrive before events do, quietly changing the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::4203.detailed_meaning: Inside Lanka, Sita is surrounded by fear while the demon women mock her. Trijata, unlike the others, sees a dream of Ravana's defeat and Hanuman's victory. Her vision gives Sita the first clear sign that Ram's side will prevail.
ramacharitamanas::4203.modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise after a nightmare, still shaken — then one calm message changes everything. Relief can begin before the situation itself has changed.
ramacharitamanas::4203.insight: It shifts attention from present fear to a larger pattern of coming reversal.

ramacharitamanas::4204.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सो दच्छिन दिसि जाई। लंका मनहुँ बिभीषन पाई॥ नगर फिरी रघुबीर दोहाई। तब प्रभु सीता बोलि पठाई ॥
