ramacharitamanas::4204.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार से वह दक्षिण (यमपुरी की) दिशा को जा रहा है और मानो लंका विभीषण ने पाई है। नगर में श्री रामचंद्रजी की दुहाई फिर गई। तब प्रभु ने सीताजी को बुला भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4204.english_translation: In this way he went toward the southern direction, as if Lanka had already been won by Vibhishana. The cry of Lord Ram spread through the city. Then the Lord sent for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4204.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this manner) / सो (he) / दच्छिन दिसि (toward the southern direction) / जाई (going) / लंका (Lanka) / मनहुँ (as if) / बिभीषन (by Vibhishana) / पाई (obtained)॥ / नगर (the city) / फिरी (spread) / रघुबीर (Ram) / दोहाई (the cry / proclamation) / तब (then) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सीता (Sita) / बोलि (calling) / पठाई (sent)
ramacharitamanas::4204.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4204.essence: Ram's presence has already begun remaking Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4204.simple_meaning: He moves through Lanka as if it already belongs to Vibhishana, Ram's call spreads everywhere, and then Sita is summoned.
ramacharitamanas::4204.simple_insight: The search is turning into certainty; hope is no longer hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4204.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's mission is nearing its turning point. The city feels conquered in spirit, Vibhishana's future is implied, Ram's name is already echoing through the streets, and now Sita is being called forward. It is a transition, not the final revelation.
ramacharitamanas::4204.modern_relevance: You hear your name called from the next room after days of waiting. Something has shifted, but you still don't know the whole story yet.
ramacharitamanas::4204.insight: It marks movement from hidden searching to open recognition and the next step in reunion.

ramacharitamanas::4205.verse_sanskrit: यह सपना मैं कहउँ पुकारी। होइहि सत्य गएँ दिन चारी॥ तासु बचन सुनि ते सब डरीं। जनकसुता के चरनन्हि परीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4205.verse_hindi: मैं पुकारकर (निश्चय के साथ) कहती हूँ कि यह स्वप्न चार (कुछ ही) दिनों बाद सत्य होकर रहेगा। उसके वचन सुनकर वे सब राक्षसियाँ डर गईं और जानकीजी के चरणों पर गिर पड़ीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4205.english_translation: I declare with certainty that this dream will come true in four days. Hearing her words, they all grew afraid and fell at Janaki's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4205.translation_literal: यह (this) / सपना (dream) / मैं (I) / कहउँ (say) / पुकारी (calling out) / होइहि (will become) / सत्य (true) / गएँ (gone) / दिन (days) / चारी (four) / तासु (that) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / ते (they) / सब (all) / डरीं (became afraid) / जनकसुता (Janaki, daughter of Janak) / के (of) / चरनन्हि (feet) / परीं (fell)
ramacharitamanas::4205.speaker: Shurpanakha's attendants
ramacharitamanas::4205.essence: Fear collapses when truth speaks with certainty.
ramacharitamanas::4205.simple_meaning: The women hear a confident prediction that Sita's rescue is near, and their fear breaks. They bow to her in alarm and respect.
ramacharitamanas::4205.simple_insight: A steady voice can calm a room full of fear.
ramacharitamanas::4205.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the demon women hear a bold prediction that Hanuman's dream will soon become real. Their panic softens into submission as they fall at Sita's feet, showing her growing spiritual strength even in captivity.
ramacharitamanas::4205.modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet when someone speaks with calm certainty. The people who were mocking you a moment ago suddenly feel how shaky their confidence really was.
ramacharitamanas::4205.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd's panic to the quiet authority of truth.

ramacharitamanas::4206.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ गईं सकल तब सीता कर मन सोच। मास दिवस बीतें मोहि मारिहि निसिचर पोच ॥
ramacharitamanas::4206.verse_hindi: तब (इसके बाद) वे सब जहाँ-तहाँ चली गईं। सीताजी मन में सोच करने लगीं कि एक महीना बीत जाने पर नीच राक्षस रावण मुझे मारेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4206.english_translation: Then all of them went away here and there, and Sita thought in her mind: after a month passes, that wicked demon will kill me.
ramacharitamanas::4206.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (here and there) / गईं (went) / सकल (all) / तब (then) / सीता (Sita) / कर (of) / मन (mind) / सोच (thought) / मास (month) / दिवस (days) / बीतें (having passed) / मोहि (me) / मारिहि (will kill) / निसिचर (demon) / पोच (wicked)
ramacharitamanas::4206.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4206.essence: Fear makes waiting feel like punishment.
ramacharitamanas::4206.simple_meaning: After the demon women leave, Sita feels trapped and fears that once a month passes, Ravana will kill her.
ramacharitamanas::4206.simple_insight: Fear can make time feel heavy and unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::4206.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the demon women have gone away and Sita is left alone in Ashoka Vatika. Her mind turns inward to dread: she believes that once a month passes, Ravana will kill her. This verse shows the weight of her waiting.
ramacharitamanas::4206.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone for a message that never comes, and every hour starts to feel like bad news. Waiting under pressure can stretch time into suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4206.insight: It reveals how fear magnifies time and turns waiting into emotional pain.

ramacharitamanas::4207.verse_sanskrit: त्रिजटा सन बोलीं कर जोरी। मातु बिपति संगिनि तैं मोरी॥ तजौं देह करु बेगि उपाई। दुसह बिरहु अब नहिं सहि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4207.verse_hindi: सीताजी हाथ जोड़कर त्रिजटा से बोलीं- हे माता! तू मेरी विपत्ति की संगिनी है। जल्दी कोई ऐसा उपाय कर जिससे मैं शरीर छोड़ सकूँ। विरह असह्म हो चला है, अब यह सहा नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4207.english_translation: Sita, with folded hands, said to Trijata: “Mother, you are my companion in this suffering. Quickly find some way for me to leave this body. This unbearable separation can no longer be endured.”
ramacharitamanas::4207.translation_literal: त्रिजटा सन (to Trijata) / बोलीं (spoke) / कर जोरी (with folded hands) / मातु (mother) / बिपति (suffering) / संगिनि (companion) / तैं (you are) / मोरी (mine) / तजौं (may I छोड़ूँ) / देह (body) / करु (do) / बेगि (quickly) / उपाई (remedy) / दुसह (unbearable) / बिरहु (separation) / अब (now) / नहिं (not) / सहि जाई (can be endured)
ramacharitamanas::4207.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4207.essence: Shared suffering can become a plea for release.
ramacharitamanas::4207.simple_meaning: Sita tells Trijata that she feels utterly overwhelmed by separation and asks for any way to end her suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4207.simple_insight: Even in anguish, being truly seen can make the burden feel less solitary.
ramacharitamanas::4207.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has found an unlikely ally in Trijata, one of Ravana's attendants who has begun protecting her. Overcome by longing for Ram, Sita folds her hands and begs for release from the body itself, showing how severe her separation has become.
ramacharitamanas::4207.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital corridor, and they finally say the pain is too much to carry alone. What they need first is not advice, but a witness.
ramacharitamanas::4207.insight: It shifts attention from fixing suffering to staying present with someone who is suffering.

ramacharitamanas::4208.verse_sanskrit: आनि काठ रचु चिता बनाई। मातु अनल पुनि देहि लगाई॥ सत्य करहि मम प्रीति सयानी। सुनै को श्रवन सूल सम बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4208.verse_hindi: काठ लाकर चिता बनाकर सजा दे। हे माता! फिर उसमें आग लगा दे। हे सयानी! तू मेरी प्रीति को सत्य कर दे। रावण की शूल के समान दुःख देने वाली वाणी कानों से कौन सुने? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4208.english_translation: Bring wood and make a pyre. O mother, then set it alight. Wise one, make my love come true. Who can bear these words, sharp as a spear, in the ears?
ramacharitamanas::4208.translation_literal: आनि (bringing) / काठ (wood) / रचु (make) / चिता (funeral pyre) / बनाई (having made) / मातु (mother) / अनल (fire) / पुनि (then) / देहि (give) / लगाई (having applied) / सत्य (true) / करहि (make) / मम (my) / प्रीति (love) / सयानी (wise one) / सुनै (to hear) / को (who) / श्रवन (ears) / सूल (thorn/spear) / सम (like) / बानी (speech/words)
ramacharitamanas::4208.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4208.essence: When suffering becomes unbearable, even hearing more can feel like another wound.
ramacharitamanas::4208.simple_meaning: Sita begs Trijata to build a pyre and light it so she can end her suffering. She says hearing Ravana's painful words is unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::4208.simple_insight: Grief can become so sharp that even hearing more feels like another wound.
ramacharitamanas::4208.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is trapped in Ashoka Vatika and overwhelmed by separation from Ram. She turns to Trijata like a trusted companion and asks for release, showing how unbearable captivity and fear have become in this moment.
ramacharitamanas::4208.modern_relevance: You keep the phone face down because one more message from the person who hurt you would break you again. Sometimes pain is so raw that even hearing more feels like injury.
ramacharitamanas::4208.insight: It shows the mind at the edge of endurance, where the wish is not for answers but for escape from suffering.

ramacharitamanas::4209.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बचन पद गहि समुझाएसि। प्रभु प्रताप बल सुजसु सुनाएसि॥ निसि न अनल मिल सुनु सुकुमारी। अस कहि सो निज भवन सिधारी।3॥
ramacharitamanas::4209.verse_hindi: सीताजी के वचन सुनकर त्रिजटा ने चरण पकड़कर उन्हें समझाया और प्रभु का प्रताप, बल और सुयश सुनाया। (उसने कहा-) हे सुकुमारी! सुनो रात्रि के समय आग नहीं मिलेगी। ऐसा कहकर वह अपने घर चली गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4209.english_translation: Hearing her words, Trijata took her by the feet and consoled her. She spoke of the Lord's power, strength, and fame. “Listen, gentle one: at night, fire will not be found.” Saying this, she returned to her own home.
ramacharitamanas::4209.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / पद (feet) / गहि (grasping) / समुझाएसि (she consoled) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रताप (majesty) / बल (strength) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुनाएसि (she recounted) / निसि (night) / न (not) / अनल (fire) / मिल (found) / सुनु (listen) / सुकुमारी (gentle one) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / सो (she) / निज (own) / भवन (home) / सिधारी (departed)
ramacharitamanas::4209.speaker: Trijata
ramacharitamanas::4209.essence: Hope returns when someone names the strength still guarding you.
ramacharitamanas::4209.simple_meaning: Trijata comforts Sita by praising Ram’s power and telling her that fire cannot be found at night.
ramacharitamanas::4209.simple_insight: A frightened heart can be steadied by someone who reminds it of what is still protecting it.
ramacharitamanas::4209.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has begged Trijata for help in ending her suffering. Trijata responds with compassion, kneels at her feet, and reassures her by praising Ram’s power and fame. She leaves after giving Sita one hope: fire will not come at night.
ramacharitamanas::4209.modern_relevance: A friend sits beside you after midnight, when panic feels absolute. They do not argue with your pain; they steady you with a truth bigger than the fear.
ramacharitamanas::4209.insight: It shifts you from despair to trust in protection that may not be visible yet.

ramacharitamanas::4210.verse_sanskrit: कह सीता बिधि भा प्रतिकूला। मिलिहि न पावक मिटिहि न सूला॥ देखिअत प्रगट गगन अंगारा। अवनि न आवत एकउ तारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4210.verse_hindi: सीताजी (मन ही मन) कहने लगीं- (क्या करूँ) विधाता ही विपरीत हो गया। न आग मिलेगी, न पीड़ा मिटेगी। आकाश में अंगारे प्रकट दिखाई दे रहे हैं, पर पृथ्वी पर एक भी तारा नहीं आता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4210.english_translation: Sita said inwardly, 'Fate has turned against me. I will not find fire, and my pain will not end. The sky appears filled with burning embers, yet not a single star comes down to the earth.'
ramacharitamanas::4210.translation_literal: कह (said) / सीता (Sita) / बिधि (fate) / भा (became) / प्रतिकूला (opposed) / मिलिहि (will be found) / न (not) / पावक (fire) / मिटिहि (will be erased) / न (not) / सूला (pain, thorn) / देखिअत (while seeing) / प्रगट (visible) / गगन (sky) / अंगारा (burning embers) / अवनि (earth) / न (not) / आवत (coming) / एकउ (even one) / तारा (star)
ramacharitamanas::4210.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4210.essence: Despair can make even a bright sky feel empty.
ramacharitamanas::4210.simple_meaning: Sita feels that even the world has turned against her. She sees no way for her suffering to end, and no relief seems possible.
ramacharitamanas::4210.simple_insight: Pain can make the whole world look hostile, even when the sky is still bright.
ramacharitamanas::4210.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita sits in Ashoka Grove, isolated and grieving after Hanuman has left. She looks at the sky and feels that every sign of hope has failed her. This is a moment of inward despair, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4210.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone at 2 a.m. and still see nothing that changes the situation. When fear is this heavy, even ordinary things start to look cruel.
ramacharitamanas::4210.insight: It captures how suffering narrows perception until even beauty feels unavailable.

ramacharitamanas::4211.verse_sanskrit: पावकमय ससि स्रवत न आगी। मानहुँ मोहि जानि हतभागी॥ सुनहि बिनय मम बिटप असोका। सत्य नाम करु हरु मम सोका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4211.verse_hindi: चंद्रमा अग्निमय है, किंतु वह भी मानो मुझे हतभागिनी जानकर आग नहीं बरसाता। हे अशोक वृक्ष! मेरी विनती सुन। मेरा शोक हर ले और अपना (अशोक) नाम सत्य कर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4211.english_translation: The moon is made of fire, yet it does not rain fire on me, as if it knows I am unfortunate. Listen to my plea, Ashoka tree: remove my sorrow and make your name truly true.
ramacharitamanas::4211.translation_literal: पावकमय (made of fire) / ससि (moon) / स्रवत (pours) / न (not) / आगी (fire) / मानहुँ (as if) / मोहि (me) / जानि (knowing) / हतभागी (unfortunate) / सुनहि (listen) / बिनय (plea) / मम (my) / बिटप (tree) / असोका (Ashoka) / सत्य (true) / नाम (name) / करु (make) / हरु (remove) / मम (my) / सोका (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::4211.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4211.essence: Even grief can become a prayer for relief.
ramacharitamanas::4211.simple_meaning: Sita feels so abandoned that even the moon seems unwilling to burn her. She pleads with the Ashoka tree to live up to its name and remove her sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4211.simple_insight: When pain is heavy, even nature can feel like a witness to it.
ramacharitamanas::4211.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita sits alone in Ashoka Grove, surrounded by grief and guarded by enemies. Looking at the moon and then the Ashoka tree, she speaks as someone who has almost run out of strength, asking the tree to truly become a remover of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4211.modern_relevance: You sit alone at night after a message that never came, staring at the window like it might answer. Sita knows that feeling: when sorrow is so close, even the world seems to reflect it back.
ramacharitamanas::4211.insight: It turns private suffering into a direct plea, showing how devotion can speak to the world itself.

ramacharitamanas::4212.verse_sanskrit: नूतन किसलय अनल समाना। देहि अगिनि जनि करहि निदाना॥ देखि परम बिरहाकुल सीता। सो छन कपिहि कलप सम बीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4212.verse_hindi: तेरे नए-नए कोमल पत्ते अग्नि के समान हैं। अग्नि दे, विरह रोग का अंत मत कर (अर्थात् विरह रोग को बढ़ाकर सीमा तक न पहुँचा) सीताजी को विरह से परम व्याकुल देखकर वह क्षण हनुमान् जी को कल्प के समान बीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4212.english_translation: Your tender new leaves look like fire. Give me fire, but do not end this burning. Seeing Sita utterly overwhelmed by separation, that one moment felt like a world-age to Hanuman.
ramacharitamanas::4212.translation_literal: नूतन (new) / किसलय (tender leaves) / अनल (fire) / समाना (like) / देहि (give) / अगिनि (fire) / जनि (do not) / करहि (do) / निदाना (ending) / देखि (seeing) / परम (utterly) / बिरहाकुल (overwhelmed by separation) / सीता (Sita) / सो (that) / छन (moment) / कपिहि (to Hanuman) / कलप (world-age) / सम (like) / बीता (passed)
ramacharitamanas::4212.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4212.essence: Compassion makes another's suffering feel like your own clock has stopped.
ramacharitamanas::4212.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees Sita's intense sorrow and feels time slow to a crawl. He is moved by her suffering and the unbearable heat of the Ashoka grove.
ramacharitamanas::4212.simple_insight: Real compassion makes another person's pain feel immediate and heavy, not distant.
ramacharitamanas::4212.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's Ashoka grove, Hanuman finally sees Sita, worn down by separation and surrounded by blazing leaves. Her suffering strikes him so deeply that one brief moment feels like an age, and his heart shifts from searching to responding.
ramacharitamanas::4212.modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend in the emergency room and keep checking the clock, but the minutes barely move. When someone's pain matters to you, time stops behaving normally.
ramacharitamanas::4212.insight: It trains you to feel another person's distress as urgent and real, not as a story happening at a distance.

ramacharitamanas::4213.verse_sanskrit: कपि करि हृदयँ बिचार दीन्हि मुद्रिका डारि तब। जनु असोक अंगार दीन्ह हरषि उठि कर गहेउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4213.verse_hindi: तब हनुमान् जी ने हदय में विचार कर (सीताजी के सामने) अँगूठी डाल दी, मानो अशोक ने अंगारा दे दिया। (यह समझकर) सीताजी ने हर्षित होकर उठकर उसे हाथ में ले लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4213.english_translation: Then Hanuman, thinking deeply in his heart, placed the ring there. It was as if the Ashoka tree had handed over a spark; delighted, Sita rose and took it in her hand.
ramacharitamanas::4213.translation_literal: कपि (monkey; Hanuman) / करि (having done) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचार (thought; reflection) / दीन्हि (gave; placed) / मुद्रिका (ring) / डारि (having thrown; placed) / तब (then) / जनु (as if) / असोक (Ashoka tree) / अंगार (ember) / दीन्ह (gave) / हरषि (rejoicing) / उठि (having risen) / कर (hand) / गहेउ (she took; grasped)
ramacharitamanas::4213.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4213.essence: A small sign can turn grief into hope.
ramacharitamanas::4213.simple_meaning: Hanuman places Ram's ring before Sita, and she receives it with joy. The moment feels like a spark of hope in the middle of deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4213.simple_insight: Hope can arrive as a tiny object that changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::4213.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka grove, Hanuman finally reveals the proof Sita has been waiting for. He places Ram's ring before her, and the sight lifts her from grief into hope. This is the turning point where recognition begins.
ramacharitamanas::4213.modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you thought had forgotten you, and one small sign changes your whole body. That is this moment.
ramacharitamanas::4213.insight: It shows how a single unmistakable sign can break despair and restore trust.

ramacharitamanas::4214.verse_sanskrit: तब देखी मुद्रिका मनोहर। राम नाम अंकित अति सुंदर॥ चकित चितव मुदरी पहिचानी। हरष बिषाद हृदयँ अकुलानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4214.verse_hindi: तब उन्होंने राम-नाम से अंकित अत्यंत सुंदर एवं मनोहर अँगूठी देखी। अँगूठी को पहचानकर सीताजी आश्चर्यचकित होकर उसे देखने लगीं और हर्ष तथा विषाद से हृदय में अकुला उठीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4214.english_translation: Then she saw the beautiful ring, engraved with Ram's name, very lovely indeed. Recognizing the ring, Sita stared in wonder, and her heart trembled with joy and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4214.translation_literal: तब (then) / देखी (saw) / मुद्रिका (ring) / मनोहर (beautiful) / राम नाम (Ram's name) / अंकित (engraved) / अति सुंदर (very beautiful) / चकित (astonished) / चितव (looked at) / मुदरी (ring) / पहिचानी (recognized) / हरष (joy) / बिषाद (sorrow) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अकुलानी (became agitated)
ramacharitamanas::4214.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4214.essence: A beloved sign can bring joy and grief together.
ramacharitamanas::4214.simple_meaning: Sita recognizes Ram's ring and is shaken by both joy and grief at once.
ramacharitamanas::4214.simple_insight: Recognition can break you open with both relief and longing.
ramacharitamanas::4214.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just placed Ram's ring before Sita. She sees the engraving, knows it at once, and her heart surges with hope and ache together. The verse captures the instant when proof of Ram's nearness stirs both comfort and pain.
ramacharitamanas::4214.modern_relevance: You open a message and see a name you had almost stopped hoping for. Relief arrives first, then the ache of everything still missing.
ramacharitamanas::4214.insight: It shows how a single sign can awaken both memory and longing at the same time.

ramacharitamanas::4215.verse_sanskrit: जीति को सकइ अजय रघुराई। माया तें असि रचि नहिं जाई॥ सीता मन बिचार कर नाना। मधुर बचन बोलेउ हनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4215.verse_hindi: (वे सोचने लगीं-) श्री रघुनाथजी तो सर्वथा अजेय हैं, उन्हें कौन जीत सकता है? और माया से ऐसी (माया के उपादान से सर्वथा रहित दिव्य, चिन्मय) अँगूठी बनाई नहीं जा सकती। सीताजी मन में अनेक प्रकार के विचार कर रही थीं। इसी समय हनुमान् जी मधुर वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4215.english_translation: Who can conquer the unconquerable Raghunath? No one can create such a ring except through divine power. Sita reflected on this in many ways, and then Hanuman spoke sweetly.
ramacharitamanas::4215.translation_literal: जीति (to conquer) / को (who) / सकइ (can) / अजय (unconquerable) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / माया (divine power) / तें (from/by) / असि (such) / रचि (create) / नहिं (not) / जाई (can be done) / सीता (Sita) / मन (mind) / बिचार (thought) / कर (doing) / नाना (many) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / बोलेउ (spoke) / हनुमाना (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4215.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4215.essence: Proof arrives before certainty, and the heart knows first.
ramacharitamanas::4215.simple_meaning: Sita recognizes that Ram is unconquerable and that this ring could only come through divine power. While she weighs these thoughts, Hanuman begins speaking gently.
ramacharitamanas::4215.simple_insight: Even in doubt, a true sign can open the heart before words do.
ramacharitamanas::4215.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is staring at the ring Hanuman has brought. She sees Ram's name, feels the impossible tenderness of the proof, and wonders how such a thing could exist. Her mind turns in many directions just before Hanuman speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4215.modern_relevance: You hold a message that feels too precise to be coincidence, and your mind keeps circling it. Before you can name the feeling, someone speaks and confirms what your heart already sensed.
ramacharitamanas::4215.insight: It shows how recognition can arise before certainty, and how gentle speech can meet a mind full of wonder.

ramacharitamanas::4216.verse_sanskrit: रामचंद्र गुन बरनैं लागा। सुनतहिं सीता कर दुख भागा॥ लागीं सुनैं श्रवन मन लाई। आदिहु तें सब कथा सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4216.verse_hindi: वे श्री रामचंद्रजी के गुणों का वर्णन करने लगे, (जिनके) सुनते ही सीताजी का दुःख भाग गया। वे कान और मन लगाकर उन्हें सुनने लगीं। हनुमान् जी ने आदि से लेकर अब तक की सारी कथा कह सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4216.english_translation: Hanuman began to describe Ramchandra's virtues, and as soon as Sita heard them, her sorrow fell away. She listened with her ears and mind fully focused, and Hanuman told the whole story from the beginning.
ramacharitamanas::4216.translation_literal: रामचंद्र (Ramchandra) / गुन (virtues) / बरनैं (to describe) / लागा (began) / सुनतहिं (as soon as hearing) / सीता (Sita) / कर (of) / दुख (sorrow) / भागा (ran away) / लागीं (began) / सुनैं (to listen) / श्रवन (ears) / मन (mind) / लाई (placing, applying) / आदिहु (from the beginning) / तें (from) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told)
ramacharitamanas::4216.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4216.essence: Ram's virtues can lift grief before any problem is solved.
ramacharitamanas::4216.simple_meaning: Hanuman praises Ram, and Sita's sorrow fades as she listens with complete attention. Then he tells her the whole story from the beginning.
ramacharitamanas::4216.simple_insight: The right words can steady a broken heart and make room for hope again.
ramacharitamanas::4216.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally found Sita after Ram's ring has proved his identity. Seeing her grief, he begins praising Ramchandra. The moment she hears Ram's virtues, her sorrow eases, and she listens with full attention as Hanuman recounts everything from the beginning.
ramacharitamanas::4216.modern_relevance: You are shaking after bad news, and one calm voice begins naming what is still true. Your chest loosens before the problem is solved.
ramacharitamanas::4216.insight: It shows how remembrance of what is beloved can dissolve despair and restore attention.

ramacharitamanas::4217.verse_sanskrit: श्रवनामृत जेहिं कथा सुहाई। कही सो प्रगट होति किन भाई॥ तब हनुमंत निकट चलि गयऊ। फिरि बैठीं मन बिसमय भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4217.verse_hindi: (सीताजी बोलीं-) जिसने कानों के लिए अमृत रूप यह सुंदर कथा कही, वह हे भाई! प्रकट क्यों नहीं होता? तब हनुमान् जी पास चले गए। उन्हें देखकर सीताजी फिरकर (मुख फेरकर) बैठ गईं? उनके मन में आश्चर्य हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4217.english_translation: “The one who spoke this sweet story, nectar for the ears — why does he not appear, brother?” Then Hanuman moved close. Seeing him, Sita turned away again, and wonder filled her mind.
ramacharitamanas::4217.translation_literal: श्रवनामृत (nectar for the ears) / जेहिं (by whom) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (sweet, lovely) / कही (spoken) / सो (that one) / प्रगट (visible, manifest) / होति (becomes) / किन (why) / भाई (brother) / तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / निकट (near) / चलि (having moved) / गयऊ (went) / फिरि (turning back) / बैठीं (sat) / मन (mind) / बिसमय (wonder) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::4217.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4217.essence: The comforted heart longs to meet the one who brought the comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4217.simple_meaning: Sita wonders why the one who spoke such a sweet, comforting story is not visible. Then Hanuman comes closer, and she turns away in surprise.
ramacharitamanas::4217.simple_insight: Even comfort can feel incomplete until the person behind it is near.
ramacharitamanas::4217.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Sita has just heard Hanuman describe Ram so beautifully that her sorrow begins to lift. Now she asks why the speaker himself is still hidden. As Hanuman steps closer, her wonder and caution rise together.
ramacharitamanas::4217.modern_relevance: You hear a voice note that calms you after a brutal day, and then you want to see the person behind it. Relief often turns into wonder when comfort becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::4217.insight: It shifts attention from the message alone to the living presence that carries it.

ramacharitamanas::4218.verse_sanskrit: राम दूत मैं मातु जानकी। सत्य सपथ करुनानिधान की॥ यह मुद्रिका मातु मैं आनी। दीन्हि राम तुम्ह कहँ सहिदानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4218.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता जानकी मैं श्री रामजी का दूत हूँ। करुणानिधान की सच्ची शपथ करता हूँ, हे माता! यह अँगूठी मैं ही लाया हूँ। श्री रामजी ने मुझे आपके लिए यह सहिदानी (निशानी या पहिचान) दी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4218.english_translation: I am Rama's messenger, Mother Janaki. I swear this truth by the compassionate one. I brought this ring, and Rama gave it to me as your token.
ramacharitamanas::4218.translation_literal: राम दूत (Rama's messenger) / मैं (I) / मातु जानकी (Mother Janaki) / सत्य (truth) / सपथ (oath) / करुनानिधान (treasure of compassion) / की (of) ॥ यह (this) / मुद्रिका (ring) / मातु (Mother) / मैं (I) / आनी (brought) / दीन्हि (gave) / राम (Rama) / तुम्ह कहँ (for you) / सहिदानी (token of recognition) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4218.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4218.essence: True devotion proves itself by carrying the beloved's token.
ramacharitamanas::4218.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that he is Ram's messenger and proves it by showing the ring Ram gave him.
ramacharitamanas::4218.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it arrives with proof, not just words.
ramacharitamanas::4218.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally reached Sita after crossing the ocean and searching through enemy territory. To calm her doubt, he identifies himself as Ram's messenger and offers the ring as proof that Ram has sent him.
ramacharitamanas::4218.modern_relevance: You hear from someone after weeks of silence, and the first thing you need is proof it really is them. Sometimes a small token carries more comfort than a thousand promises.
ramacharitamanas::4218.insight: It teaches you that devotion is made credible through faithful action and recognizable signs.

ramacharitamanas::4219.verse_sanskrit: नर बानरहि संग कहु कैसें। कही कथा भइ संगति जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4219.verse_hindi: (सीताजी ने पूछा-) नर और वानर का संग कहो कैसे हुआ? तब हनुमानजी ने जैसे संग हुआ था, वह सब कथा कही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4219.english_translation: How did a man and a monkey come together? Hanuman then told the whole story of how that bond happened.
ramacharitamanas::4219.translation_literal: नर (man) / बानरहि (to the monkey) / संग (together, in company) / कहु (tell) / कैसें (how) / कही (told) / कथा (story) / भइ (became) / संगति (association, coming together) / जैसें (as, in the way that)
ramacharitamanas::4219.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4219.essence: Trust grows when the hidden story is finally told.
ramacharitamanas::4219.simple_meaning: Sita asks how a human and a monkey came to be together, and Hanuman begins explaining their bond.
ramacharitamanas::4219.simple_insight: Curiosity can open the door to trust.
ramacharitamanas::4219.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just heard Hanuman's words and seen Ram's ring. Still unsure, she asks how a man and a monkey came to be linked at all. Hanuman responds by telling the story behind their meeting.
ramacharitamanas::4219.modern_relevance: You meet someone who feels impossible to trust, then one honest conversation changes everything. Sometimes the bond makes sense only after you hear the story behind it.
ramacharitamanas::4219.insight: It shifts attention from the strange pairing to the story that created trust.

ramacharitamanas::4220.verse_sanskrit: कपि के बचन सप्रेम सुनि उपजा मन बिस्वास जाना मन क्रम बचन यह कृपासिंधु कर दास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4220.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी के प्रेमयक्त वचन सुनकर सीताजी के मन में विश्वास उत्पन्न हो गया, उन्होंने जान लिया कि यह मन, वचन और कर्म से कृपासागर श्री रघुनाथजी का दास है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4220.english_translation: Hearing the monkey's loving words, trust arose in Sita's mind. She knew him to be a servant of the merciful Raghunath in mind, action, and speech.
ramacharitamanas::4220.translation_literal: कपि (monkey) / के बचन (words) / सप्रेम (with love) / सुनि (hearing) / उपजा (arose) / मन (mind) / बिस्वास (trust) / जाना (knew) / मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / यह (this) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of mercy) / कर (of) / दास (servant)
ramacharitamanas::4220.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4220.essence: Trust awakens when love, speech, and action all point the same way.
ramacharitamanas::4220.simple_meaning: Sita hears Hanuman speak with love and immediately trusts him. She recognises that his mind, words, and actions all belong to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4220.simple_insight: Trust deepens when love and conduct match.
ramacharitamanas::4220.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has heard many claims, but Hanuman's loving speech breaks through her fear. She sees that he is not speaking for himself. His whole being belongs to Ram, and that sincerity creates trust at once.
ramacharitamanas::4220.modern_relevance: Someone texts you with perfect words, but their actions feel off. Then one message arrives with warmth, consistency, and no agenda — and you know you can trust them.
ramacharitamanas::4220.insight: It teaches you to look for alignment between intention, speech, and action before giving your trust.

ramacharitamanas::4221.verse_sanskrit: हरिजन जानि प्रीति अति गाढ़ी। सजल नयन पुलकावलि बाढ़ी॥ बूड़त बिरह जलधि हनुमाना। भयहु तात मो कहुँ जलजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4221.verse_hindi: भगवान का जन (सेवक) जानकर अत्यंत गाढ़ी प्रीति हो गई। नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया और शरीर अत्यंत पुलकित हो गया (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे तात हनुमान् ! विरहसागर में डूबती हुई मुझको तुम जहाज हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4221.english_translation: Knowing him as a servant of the divine, her love became intense. Her eyes filled with tears, her body thrilled with joy. (Sita said,) "Hanuman, I was drowning in the ocean of separation; you became the boat that carried me across."
ramacharitamanas::4221.translation_literal: हरिजन (servant of the divine) / जानि (knowing) / प्रीति (love) / अति (very) / गाढ़ी (intense) / सजल (moist) / नयन (eyes) / पुलकावलि (horripilation / thrill) / बाढ़ी (increased) / बूड़त (drowning) / बिरह (separation) / जलधि (ocean) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / भयहु (you became) / तात (dear one) / मो कहुँ (for me) / जलजाना (boat)
ramacharitamanas::4221.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4221.essence: True devotion becomes a boat for someone drowning in separation.
ramacharitamanas::4221.simple_meaning: Sita recognises Hanuman as a devoted servant and feels deep love and relief. His arrival feels like a boat rescuing her from the ocean of separation.
ramacharitamanas::4221.simple_insight: Real devotion doesn’t just comfort; it carries someone through what felt impossible to survive.
ramacharitamanas::4221.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has been waiting in loneliness and grief. When Hanuman proves his devotion to Ram, her heart opens at once. She feels tears, joy, and relief, and names him the boat that can carry her across separation.
ramacharitamanas::4221.modern_relevance: You finally hear from the one person who understood your pain without explanation. In that moment, their presence doesn’t just soothe you — it makes survival feel possible again.
ramacharitamanas::4221.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract admiration to active rescue: love becomes something that helps another person cross suffering.

ramacharitamanas::4222.verse_sanskrit: अब कहु कुसल जाउँ बलिहारी। अनुज सहित सुख भवन खरारी॥ कोमलचित कृपाल रघुराई। कपि केहि हेतु धरी निठुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4222.verse_hindi: मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, अब छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित खर के शत्रु सुखधाम प्रभु का कुशल-मंगल कहो। श्री रघुनाथजी तो कोमल हृदय और कृपालु हैं। फिर हे हनुमान् ! उन्होंने किस कारण यह निष्ठुरता धारण कर ली है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4222.english_translation: I bow to you. Tell me now of the welfare of the Lord of the auspicious home, along with Lakshman, his younger brother. Raghunath is tender-hearted and full of grace. Then, O Hanuman, why has he taken on such harshness?
ramacharitamanas::4222.translation_literal: अब (now) / कहु (tell) / कुसल (welfare) / जाउँ (I go) / बलिहारी (I am devotedly grateful) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (along with) / सुख भवन (abode of joy) / खरारी (enemy of Khara) / कोमलचित (soft-hearted) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुराई (Lord of Raghu) / कपि (O monkey) / केहि हेतु (for what reason) / धरी (took on) / निठुराई (harshness)
ramacharitamanas::4222.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4222.essence: True tenderness can seem hidden when love is stretched by separation.
ramacharitamanas::4222.simple_meaning: Sita asks Hanuman to tell her whether Ram and Lakshman are well. She remembers Ram as kind and soft-hearted, so his seeming harshness pains her.
ramacharitamanas::4222.simple_insight: Love notices even a small change in tone and cannot ignore it.
ramacharitamanas::4222.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just begun to trust Hanuman after hearing his gentle words. Now she asks about Ram and Lakshman, calling Ram tender and compassionate. Her question carries longing: if Ram is truly so kind, why has he remained so severe toward her?
ramacharitamanas::4222.modern_relevance: You read a short, flat text from someone who once loved you warmly, and your chest tightens. You know their tenderness too well to mistake silence for indifference.
ramacharitamanas::4222.insight: It teaches you to notice how separation can make even love feel like hardness.

ramacharitamanas::4223.verse_sanskrit: सहज बानि सेवक सुखदायक। कबहुँक सुरति करत रघुनायक॥ कबहुँ नयन मम सीतल ताता। होइहहिं निरखि स्याम मृदु गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4223.verse_hindi: सेवक को सुख देना उनकी स्वाभाविक बान है। वे श्री रघुनाथजी क्या कभी मेरी भी याद करते हैं? हे तात! क्या कभी उनके कोमल साँवले अंगों को देखकर मेरे नेत्र शीतल होंगे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4223.english_translation: Service is their natural way of being. Do they ever remember me? O father, will my eyes grow cool when I see his soft dark form?
ramacharitamanas::4223.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / बानि (way, nature) / सेवक (for the servant) / सुखदायक (giving joy) / कबहुँक (ever, at some time) / सुरति (remembrance) / करत (doing) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / कबहुँ (ever) / नयन (eyes) / मम (my) / सीतल (cool, soothed) / ताता (father, dear one) / होइहहिं (will become) / निरखि (seeing) / स्याम (dark, blue-black) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / गाता (body, form)
ramacharitamanas::4223.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4223.essence: Ram's servants find comfort because his nature is to remember and soothe them.
ramacharitamanas::4223.simple_meaning: Ram naturally brings comfort to those who serve him. Sita longs for his remembrance and hopes that seeing his gentle form will soothe her grief.
ramacharitamanas::4223.simple_insight: Love softens suffering when you trust that you are remembered.
ramacharitamanas::4223.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita speaks from the pain of separation. She knows Ram as the one who gives joy to his servants, yet she wonders whether he remembers her. Her longing turns into hope that one glimpse of his gentle form will calm her burning eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4223.modern_relevance: You wait by your phone after sending a message that matters. The silence hurts, but part of you still trusts that the person who loves you has not forgotten.
ramacharitamanas::4223.insight: It shifts longing from panic to trust: remembrance itself becomes a refuge.

ramacharitamanas::4224.verse_sanskrit: बचनु न आव नयन भरे बारी। अहह नाथ हौं निपट बिसारी॥ देखि परम बिरहाकुल सीता। बोला कपि मृदु बचन बिनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4224.verse_hindi: (मुँह से) वचन नहीं निकलता, नेत्रों में (विरह के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। (बड़े दुःख से वे बोलीं-) हा नाथ! आपने मुझे बिलकुल ही भुला दिया! सीताजी को विरह से परम व्याकुल देखकर हनुमान् जी कोमल और विनीत वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4224.english_translation: Her words would not come out; tears filled her eyes. "Ah, Lord, you have completely forgotten me." Seeing Sita overwhelmed by separation, Hanuman spoke gentle, humble words.
ramacharitamanas::4224.translation_literal: बचनु (word/speech) / न (not) / आव (came) / नयन (eyes) / भरे (filled) / बारी (water, tears) / अहह (ah) / नाथ (Lord) / हौं (I) / निपट (completely) / बिसारी (forgotten) / देखि (seeing) / परम (utterly) / बिरहाकुल (distressed by separation) / सीता (Sita) / बोला (spoke) / कपि (monkey, Hanuman) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / बिनीता (humble)
ramacharitamanas::4224.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4224.essence: Deep grief needs gentle speech, not force.
ramacharitamanas::4224.simple_meaning: Sita is so overwhelmed by separation that she cannot speak clearly, and Hanuman responds with gentle, respectful words.
ramacharitamanas::4224.simple_insight: Even in grief, being met with gentleness can keep you from breaking completely.
ramacharitamanas::4224.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman finally sees Sita in Ashoka Vatika, worn down by longing and tears. She cries that Ram has forgotten her. Hanuman, moved by her pain, answers with softness instead of urgency, because this meeting is as much about comfort as it is about news.
ramacharitamanas::4224.modern_relevance: You call someone at 2 a.m. after a breakup and can barely speak. The right response is not advice first, but a voice gentle enough to hold your shaking.
ramacharitamanas::4224.insight: It teaches you to meet raw grief with restraint, tenderness, and respect before trying to fix anything.

ramacharitamanas::4225.verse_sanskrit: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता॥ जनि जननी मानह जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4225.verse_hindi: हे माता! सुंदर कृपा के धाम प्रभु भाई लक्ष्मणजी के सहित (शरीर से) कुशल हैं, परंतु आपके दुःख से दुःखी हैं। हे माता! मन में ग्लानि न मानिए (मन छोटा करके दुःख न कीजिए)। श्री रामचंद्रजी के हृदय में आपसे दूना प्रेम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4225.english_translation: Mother, the Lord and Lakshman are well, but they grieve with your grief. Do not feel hurt in your heart; Ram loves you twice as much.
ramacharitamanas::4225.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / कुसल (well) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेता (together with) / तव (your) / दुख (sorrow) / दुखी (sorrowful) / सुकृपा (of gracious mercy) / निकेता (abode) / जनि (do not) / जननी (mother) / मानह (take) / जियँ (in the heart) / ऊना (less) / तुम्ह ते (than you) / प्रेमु (love) / राम कें (for Ram) / दूना (double)
ramacharitamanas::4225.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4225.essence: Love stays alive even when separation makes it feel far away.
ramacharitamanas::4225.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that Ram and Lakshman are safe, share her sorrow, and love her deeply. He asks her not to feel diminished in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::4225.simple_insight: Love is not absent just because you cannot see it.
ramacharitamanas::4225.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman finally speaks to Sita after finding her in deep anguish. He brings the first real comfort she has heard in months: Ram and Lakshman are safe, they feel her pain, and Ram's love for her is even greater than before.
ramacharitamanas::4225.modern_relevance: You finally get the text you were waiting for after a terrible week: 'We’re okay.' The message doesn’t erase the hurt, but it tells you the bond is still alive.
ramacharitamanas::4225.insight: It shifts the heart from self-blame and doubt toward reassurance in being remembered and loved.

ramacharitamanas::4226.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति कर संदेसु अब सुनु जननी धरि धीर। अस कहि कपि गदगद भयउ भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4226.verse_hindi: हे माता! अब धीरज धरकर श्री रघुनाथजी का संदेश सुनिए। ऐसा कहकर हनुमान् जी प्रेम से गद्गद हो गए। उनके नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4226.english_translation: O Mother, now listen with patience to the message of Raghupati. Saying this, the monkey became choked with emotion, and his eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::4226.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu; Ram) / कर (of) / संदेसु (message) / अब (now) / सुनु (listen) / जननी (Mother) / धरि (holding) / धीर (patience) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / कपि (monkey) / गदगद (choked with emotion) / भयउ (became) / भरे (filled) / बिलोचन (eyes) / नीर (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::4226.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4226.essence: Devotion makes even a message feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::4226.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Sita to steady herself and listen to Ram's message. He is so moved by devotion that he cannot speak without tears.
ramacharitamanas::4226.simple_insight: A loving message can carry more comfort when it comes from a heart that trembles with care.
ramacharitamanas::4226.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally found Sita after crossing the ocean alone. Before he can deliver Ram's words, emotion overwhelms him. The message is not just information; it arrives through devotion, longing, and tears.
ramacharitamanas::4226.modern_relevance: You finally call the person who has been waiting for news, and your voice breaks before you even begin. Some messages matter so much that your emotion speaks first.
ramacharitamanas::4226.insight: It shifts communication from mere words to presence, showing that sincerity can be felt before it is understood.

ramacharitamanas::4227.verse_sanskrit: कहेउ राम बियोग तव सीता। मो कहुँ सकल भए बिपरीता॥ नव तरु किसलय मनहुँ कृसानू। कालनिसा सम निसि ससि भानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4227.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी बोले-) श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा है कि हे सीते! तुम्हारे वियोग में मेरे लिए सभी पदार्थ प्रतिकूल हो गए हैं। वृक्षों के नए-नए कोमल पत्ते मानो अग्नि के समान, रात्रि कालरात्रि के समान, चंद्रमा सूर्य के समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4227.english_translation: Ram said that in separation from you, Sita, everything has become opposite for me. New tender leaves seem like fire, night feels like death-darkness, and the moon seems like the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4227.translation_literal: कहेउ (said) / राम (Ram) / बियोग (separation) / तव (your) / सीता (Sita) / मो कहुँ (for me) / सकल (all) / भए (became) / बिपरीता (opposite) / नव (new) / तरु (tree) / किसलय (tender leaves) / मनहुँ (as if) / कृसानू (fire) / कालनिसा (death-darkness) / सम (like) / निसि (night) / ससि (moon) / भानू (sun)
ramacharitamanas::4227.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4227.essence: Separation makes even beauty feel like fire.
ramacharitamanas::4227.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita that her absence has changed his whole experience of the world. Things that once felt pleasant now feel harsh or wrong.
ramacharitamanas::4227.simple_insight: Love can make the same world feel completely different when someone is missing.
ramacharitamanas::4227.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is carrying Sita's message back from Lanka. To reassure her, he repeats Ram's own words: in her absence, even the world itself has turned painful. The verse shows how deep their bond is.
ramacharitamanas::4227.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a breakup and every small thing feels altered — the music, the light, the air. This verse names that strange reordering of reality.
ramacharitamanas::4227.insight: It shows how longing reshapes perception, turning neutral things into either comfort or pain.

ramacharitamanas::4228.verse_sanskrit: कुबलय बिपिन कुंत बन सरिसा। बारिद तपत तेल जनु बरिसा॥ जे हित रहे करत तेइ पीरा। उरग स्वास सम त्रिबिध समीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4228.verse_hindi: और कमलों के वन भालों के वन के समान हो गए हैं। मेघ मानो खौलता हुआ तेल बरसाते हैं। जो हित करने वाले थे, वे ही अब पीड़ा देने लगे हैं। त्रिविध (शीतल, मंद, सुगंध) वायु साँप के श्वास के समान (जहरीली और गरम) हो गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4228.english_translation: The lotus groves have become forests of spears. Clouds now pour down like boiling oil. What once gave comfort now brings pain. Even the breeze of three kinds feels like a snake’s breath.
ramacharitamanas::4228.translation_literal: कुबलय (lotus) / बिपिन (grove, forest) / कुंत (spear) / बन (forest) / सरिसा (like) / बारिद (clouds) / तपत (boiling) / तेल (oil) / जनु (as if) / बरिसा (rains) / जे (which) / हित (comforting, helpful) / रहे (were) / करत (doing) / तेइ (those very) / पीरा (pain) / उरग (snake) / स्वास (breath) / सम (like) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / समीरा (wind)
ramacharitamanas::4228.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4228.essence: Love in separation can make comfort feel like pain.
ramacharitamanas::4228.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that everything around him now feels hostile and painful, even things that normally give comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4228.simple_insight: Separation can make the whole world feel turned against you.
ramacharitamanas::4228.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is giving Sita Ram’s message after finding her in deep sorrow. He describes how Ram’s absence has made even ordinary comforts feel cruel, showing the intensity of longing and the emotional world of separation.
ramacharitamanas::4228.modern_relevance: You walk into a room that used to feel safe, but after one painful loss everything feels sharp, cold, and wrong. Grief can change the texture of the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::4228.insight: It turns private longing into a shared language of pain, so Sita knows Ram’s love is alive in his absence.

ramacharitamanas::4229.verse_sanskrit: कहेहू तें कछु दुख घटि होई। काहि कहौं यह जान न कोई॥ तत्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा। जानत प्रिया एकु मनु मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4229.verse_hindi: मन का दुःख कह डालने से भी कुछ घट जाता है। पर कहूँ किससे? यह दुःख कोई जानता नहीं। हे प्रिये! मेरे और तेरे प्रेम का तत्त्व (रहस्य) एक मेरा मन ही जानता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4229.english_translation: Speaking of it can lessen sorrow a little, but whom can I tell? No one knows this pain. O beloved, the secret of your love and mine is known only to my own mind.
ramacharitamanas::4229.translation_literal: कहेहू तें (by speaking of it) / कछु (some) / दुख (sorrow) / घटि (lessens) / होई (happens) / काहि (to whom) / कहौं (should I tell) / यह (this) / जान (pain) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) / तत्व (essence) / प्रेम (love) / कर (of) / मम (my) / अरु (and) / तोरा (your) / जानत (knows) / प्रिया (beloved) / एकु (only) / मनु (mind) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::4229.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4229.essence: True love can be shared only by hearts that already know it.
ramacharitamanas::4229.simple_meaning: Speaking about sorrow can lessen it, but this love is too deep for anyone else to fully understand. Only the speaker's own mind knows its secret.
ramacharitamanas::4229.simple_insight: Some feelings are healed by being held in the heart, even when no one else can fully understand them.
ramacharitamanas::4229.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is carrying Ram's message to Sita in Lanka, and the message turns tender and intimate. Ram speaks of separation so deep that words only partly ease it, because the full meaning of their love lives in one heart alone.
ramacharitamanas::4229.modern_relevance: You try to explain a heartbreak over tea, and the other person nods but cannot really enter it. Still, naming it aloud can make the ache more bearable.
ramacharitamanas::4229.insight: It shifts you from demanding perfect understanding to trusting that honest speech can still soften pain.

ramacharitamanas::4230.verse_sanskrit: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4230.verse_hindi: और वह मन सदा तेरे ही पास रहता है। बस, मेरे प्रेम का सार इतने में ही समझ ले। प्रभु का संदेश सुनते ही जानकीजी प्रेम में मग्न हो गईं। उन्हें शरीर की सुध न रही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4230.english_translation: And my mind always remains with you. Understand the essence of love in this much alone. Hearing the Lord's message, Sita was lost in love; she forgot her body.
ramacharitamanas::4230.translation_literal: सो (that) / मनु (mind) / सदा (always) / रहत (remains) / तोहि (with you) / पाहीं (near) / जानु (know) / प्रीति (love) / रसु (essence/juice) / एतनेहि (in this much) / माहीं (within) / प्रभु (Lord's) / संदेसु (message) / सुनत (hearing) / बैदेही (Sita) / मगन (immersed) / प्रेम (love) / तन (body) / सुधि (awareness) / नहिं (not) / तेही (that)
ramacharitamanas::4230.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4230.essence: True love keeps the mind near the beloved, even across separation.
ramacharitamanas::4230.simple_meaning: Sita says her mind is always with Ram, and hearing his message fills her with such love that she forgets her body.
ramacharitamanas::4230.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that it dissolves self-consciousness and leaves only presence.
ramacharitamanas::4230.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally reached Sita and is carrying Ram's message. Sita answers from the depth of separation and devotion: her mind has never left Ram, and his words plunge her into such love that she loses awareness of her body.
ramacharitamanas::4230.modern_relevance: You hear a voice note from someone you have been missing for weeks, and your whole chest softens. For a moment, your body is still there, but your attention belongs completely to them.
ramacharitamanas::4230.insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling to a total mental presence that can overpower bodily awareness.

ramacharitamanas::4231.verse_sanskrit: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता। सुमिरु राम सेवक सुखदाता॥ उर आनहु रघुपति प्रभुताई। सुनि मम बचन तजहु कदराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4231.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे माता! हृदय में धैर्य धारण करो और सेवकों को सुख देने वाले श्री रामजी का स्मरण करो। श्री रघुनाथजी की प्रभुता को हृदय में लाओ और मेरे वचन सुनकर कायरता छोड़ दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4231.english_translation: Hanuman said: "Mother, keep courage in your heart. Remember Ram, the giver of joy to his servants. Hold the greatness of Raghupati in your heart, and hearing my words, let go of your fear."
ramacharitamanas::4231.translation_literal: कह (said) / कपि (the monkey) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धीर (steadiness) / धरु (hold) / माता (mother) / सुमिरु (remember) / राम (Ram) / सेवक (servant) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) / उर (in the heart) / आनहु (bring) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / प्रभुताई (lordship, greatness) / सुनि (hearing) / मम (my) / बचन (words) / तजहु (leave behind) / कदराई (cowardice)
ramacharitamanas::4231.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4231.essence: Remembering Ram gives you courage before the fear can rule.
ramacharitamanas::4231.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita to stay brave, remember Ram, and let go of fear. Trust in Ram's greatness is what steadies the heart.
ramacharitamanas::4231.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when remembrance becomes stronger than panic.
ramacharitamanas::4231.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita and is speaking to her after Ram's message. She is overwhelmed by longing and fear, and he answers with reassurance: remember Ram's greatness, and courage will return.
ramacharitamanas::4231.modern_relevance: You are waiting for a difficult call, and your mind keeps inventing the worst outcome. Then one steady reminder arrives: breathe, remember what is larger than this moment, and the panic loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::4231.insight: It shifts the mind from fear-driven spiraling to trust anchored in remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::4232.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर निकर पतंग सम रघुपति बान कृसानु। जननी हृदयँ धीर धरु जरे निसाचर जानु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4232.verse_hindi: राक्षसों के समूह पतंगों के समान और श्री रघुनाथजी के बाण अग्नि के समान हैं। हे माता! हृदय में धैर्य धारण करो और राक्षसों को जला ही समझो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4232.english_translation: The demons are like moths, and Raghupati's arrows are fire. Mother, keep your heart steady and know the night-demons are already burned.
ramacharitamanas::4232.translation_literal: निसिचर (night-demons) / निकर (group) / पतंग (moths) / सम (like) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / बान (arrows) / कृसानु (fire) / जननी (mother) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धीर (steadiness) / धरु (hold) / जरे (burned) / निसाचर (night-demons) / जानु (know)
ramacharitamanas::4232.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4232.essence: What looks terrifying is already reduced to ash.
ramacharitamanas::4232.simple_meaning: Hanuman reassures Sita that Ravana's forces are helpless before Ram's power, and she should stay calm because their defeat is already certain.
ramacharitamanas::4232.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you trust that the threat is not ultimate.
ramacharitamanas::4232.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita in Ashoka Vatika and is building her courage with Ram's message. He compares the demons to moths and Ram's arrows to fire, telling her that their destruction is already certain, so she can steady her heart.
ramacharitamanas::4232.modern_relevance: You are waiting for a test result, and your mind keeps replaying worst-case stories. This verse says the threat is not as powerful as it feels; steady yourself before the outcome arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4232.insight: It shifts attention from the size of the threat to the certainty of divine protection.

ramacharitamanas::4233.verse_sanskrit: जौं रघुबीर होति सुधि पाई। करते नहिं बिलंबु रघुराई॥ राम बान रबि उएँ जानकी। तम बरुथ कहँ जातुधान की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4233.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने यदि खबर पाई होती तो वे बिलंब न करते। हे जानकीजी! रामबाण रूपी सूर्य के उदय होने पर राक्षसों की सेना रूपी अंधकार कहाँ रह सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4233.english_translation: If Raghuvir had received the news, Raghu Rai would not have delayed. Janaki, when the sun of Ram's arrow rises, how can the darkness of the demon host remain?
ramacharitamanas::4233.translation_literal: जौं (if) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir, Ram) / होति (had been) / सुधि (news, tidings) / पाई (received) / करते (would do) / नहिं (not) / बिलंबु (delay) / रघुराई (Raghu Rai, Ram)॥ / राम (Ram) / बान (arrow) / रबि (sun) / उएँ (having risen) / जानकी (Janaki, Sita) की (of) / तम (darkness) / बरुथ (host, army) / कहँ (where) / जातुधान (demons) की (of the) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4233.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4233.essence: Ram's arrival makes delay and darkness impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4233.simple_meaning: If Ram knew Sita's situation, he would not wait. Just as sunrise ends darkness, Ram's power destroys the demon army.
ramacharitamanas::4233.simple_insight: You are not abandoned for long. The moment help truly arrives, fear loses its place.
ramacharitamanas::4233.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is speaking to Sita in Lanka, trying to steady her heart after her long suffering. He assures her that Ram would come at once if he knew, and that Ram's power is like sunrise: once it appears, the enemy's darkness cannot remain.
ramacharitamanas::4233.modern_relevance: You are waiting for a text that could change everything, and the silence feels endless. This verse speaks to the certainty that real help, once awakened, does not hesitate.
ramacharitamanas::4233.insight: It shifts the mind from helpless waiting to trust in the force of true support.

ramacharitamanas::4234.verse_sanskrit: अबहिं मातु मैं जाउँ लवाई। प्रभु आयुस नहिं राम दोहाई॥ कछुक दिवस जननी धरु धीरा। कपिन्ह सहित अइहहिं रघुबीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4234.verse_hindi: हे माता! मैं आपको अभी यहाँ से लिवा जाऊँ, पर श्री रामचंद्रजी की शपथ है, मुझे प्रभु (उन) की आज्ञा नहीं है। (अतः) हे माता! कुछ दिन और धीरज धरो। श्री रामचंद्रजी वानरों सहित यहाँ आएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4234.english_translation: Mother, I would take you away right now, but I cannot do so without the Lord's command. So, mother, hold on with courage for a few more days. Lord Ram will come here with the monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::4234.translation_literal: अबहिं (right now) / मातु (mother) / मैं (I) / जाउँ (go) / लवाई (to take away) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयुस (command) / नहिं (not) / राम (Ram) / दोहाई (by oath) / कछुक (some) / दिवस (days) / जननी (mother) / धरु (hold) / धीरा (courage) / कपिन्ह (with monkeys) / सहित (together) / अइहहिं (will come) / रघुबीरा (Lord Ram)
ramacharitamanas::4234.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4234.essence: True courage can wait without losing hope.
ramacharitamanas::4234.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita he cannot leave immediately because he must wait for Ram's order. He asks her to stay brave a little longer, promising that Ram will come with the monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::4234.simple_insight: Waiting can be an act of strength when it stays loyal to the right order.
ramacharitamanas::4234.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita in Ashoka Vatika. He longs to rescue her at once, but he will not act outside Ram's command. Instead, he gives her courage and a promise of help.
ramacharitamanas::4234.modern_relevance: You want to send the message, make the move, fix it now — but the wiser step is to wait for the right signal. Courage sometimes means not rushing ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4234.insight: It teaches you to restrain impulse until action aligns with rightful authority or purpose.

ramacharitamanas::4235.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर मारि तोहि लै जैहहिं। तिहुँ पुर नारदादि जसु गैहहिं॥ हैं सुत कपि सब तुम्हहि समाना। जातुधान अति भट बलवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4235.verse_hindi: और राक्षसों को मारकर आपको ले जाएँगे। नारद आदि (ऋषि-मुनि) तीनों लोकों में उनका यश गाएँगे। (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे पुत्र! सब वानर तुम्हारे ही समान (नन्हें-नन्हें से) होंगे, राक्षस तो बड़े बलवान, योद्धा हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4235.english_translation: Killing the demons, they will take you back. Narada and others will sing their praise in the three worlds. "Son, all the monkeys are as small as you, while the demons are mighty warriors and very strong."
ramacharitamanas::4235.translation_literal: निसिचर (demons) / मारि (having killed) / तोहि (you) / लै जैहहिं (will take and go) / तिहुँ पुर (in the three worlds) / नारदादि (Narada and others) / जसु (praise) / गैहहिं (will sing) / हैं (are) / सुत (son) / कपि (monkeys) / सब (all) / तुम्हहि (like you) / समाना (equal) / जातुधान (demons) / अति (very) / भट (warriors) / बलवाना (strong)
ramacharitamanas::4235.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4235.essence: Doubt sees only size and misses hidden strength.
ramacharitamanas::4235.simple_meaning: Sita says Hanuman would have to defeat the demons before taking her back, but she doubts the monkeys are strong enough for that fight.
ramacharitamanas::4235.simple_insight: Fear can make even hope sound impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4235.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Hanuman has found Sita and is trying to reassure her. Sita answers with loving doubt: the demons are powerful, and the monkeys seem small by comparison. This is the moment before Hanuman reveals his true form.
ramacharitamanas::4235.modern_relevance: You finally tell someone you can help, and they still look at your small frame and doubt you. Their fear is real, but it is not the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::4235.insight: It shows how despair can shrink trust, even when rescue is near.

ramacharitamanas::4236.verse_sanskrit: मोरें हृदय परम संदेहा। सुनि कपि प्रगट कीन्हि निज देहा॥ कनक भूधराकार सरीरा। समर भयंकर अतिबल बीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4236.verse_hindi: अतः मेरे हृदय में बड़ा भारी संदेह होता है (कि तुम जैसे बंदर राक्षसों को कैसे जीतेंगे!)। यह सुनकर हनुमान् जी ने अपना शरीर प्रकट किया। सोने के पर्वत (सुमेरु) के आकार का (अत्यंत विशाल) शरीर था, जो युद्ध में शत्रुओं के हृदय में भय उत्पन्न करने वाला, अत्यंत बलवान् और वीर था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4236.english_translation: Then Sita said, "I have deep doubt in my heart." Hearing this, Hanuman revealed his true form. His body was like a golden mountain, terrifying in battle, immensely strong, and heroic.
ramacharitamanas::4236.translation_literal: मोरें (in my) / हृदय (heart) / परम (great) / संदेहा (doubt) / सुनि (hearing) / कपि (the monkey) / प्रगट (manifested) / कीन्हि (made) / निज (own) / देहा (body) / कनक (golden) / भूधराकार (mountain-shaped) / सरीरा (body) / समर (battle) / भयंकर (fearsome) / अतिबल (very strong) / बीरा (hero)
ramacharitamanas::4236.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4236.essence: A hidden truth becomes believable when it is fully revealed.
ramacharitamanas::4236.simple_meaning: Sita doubts Hanuman at first, so he reveals his enormous, powerful form to reassure her.
ramacharitamanas::4236.simple_insight: Sometimes trust arrives only after the truth becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::4236.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally found Sita, but she cannot yet fully trust this unexpected messenger from Ram. Hearing her doubt, he reveals his true vast form — not to boast, but to remove fear and prove his strength.
ramacharitamanas::4236.modern_relevance: You explain yourself carefully, but the other person still hesitates. Then one honest act, one visible proof, changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::4236.insight: It shows that trust can be earned through clear, embodied evidence, not words alone.

ramacharitamanas::4237.verse_sanskrit: सीता मन भरोस तब भयऊ। पुनि लघु रूप पवनसुत लयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4237.verse_hindi: तब (उसे देखकर) सीताजी के मन में विश्वास हुआ। हनुमान् जी ने फिर छोटा रूप धारण कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4237.english_translation: Then Sita's mind was filled with trust. Hanuman again took on a small form.
ramacharitamanas::4237.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / मन (mind) / भरोस (trust) / तब (then) / भयऊ (became) / पुनि (again) / लघु (small) / रूप (form) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / लयऊ (took)
ramacharitamanas::4237.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4237.essence: Trust grows when fear is answered by visible strength.
ramacharitamanas::4237.simple_meaning: Seeing Hanuman's true power, Sita's fear softens into trust, and Hanuman returns to a smaller form.
ramacharitamanas::4237.simple_insight: Real trust quiets fear without needing perfect explanations.
ramacharitamanas::4237.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just doubted whether this tiny messenger can really help her. Hanuman reveals his vast form, and her heart settles. Once trust is born, he resumes his humble size.
ramacharitamanas::4237.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a moment of crisis, and they prove themselves by calmly doing what seemed impossible. Your suspicion drops, and the room feels safe again.
ramacharitamanas::4237.insight: It shifts the mind from doubt to confidence through direct experience, not argument.

ramacharitamanas::4238.verse_sanskrit: सुनु माता साखामृग नहिं बल बुद्धि बिसाल। प्रभु प्रताप तें गरुड़हि खाइ परम लघु ब्याल ॥
ramacharitamanas::4238.verse_hindi: हे माता! सुनो, वानरों में बहुत बल-बुद्धि नहीं होती, परंतु प्रभु के प्रताप से बहुत छोटा सर्प भी गरुड़ को खा सकता है। (अत्यंत निर्बल भी महान् बलवान् को मार सकता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4238.english_translation: Listen, Mother: monkeys do not have great strength or intelligence, yet by the Lord's power even a tiny serpent can swallow Garuda.
ramacharitamanas::4238.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / माता (Mother) / साखामृग (monkeys) / नहिं (not) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (intelligence) / बिसाल (vast) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रताप (power, glory) / तें (by) / गरुड़हि (Garuda) / खाइ (can eat/swallow) / परम (very) / लघु (small) / ब्याल (serpent)
ramacharitamanas::4238.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4238.essence: Smallness is no obstacle when the Lord's power is with you.
ramacharitamanas::4238.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that monkeys may seem weak, but the Lord's power can make even the smallest being overcome the greatest one.
ramacharitamanas::4238.simple_insight: Confidence grows when you stop measuring yourself only by your own limits.
ramacharitamanas::4238.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just seen Hanuman reveal his true form and shrink again. He reassures her that victory does not depend on monkey strength alone. Ram's power works through even the smallest form, so no obstacle is too large.
ramacharitamanas::4238.modern_relevance: You walk into a room feeling underqualified, while everyone else seems sharper, louder, and more prepared. Then one calm reminder changes everything: what matters most is not your size, but what power is working through you.
ramacharitamanas::4238.insight: It shifts attention from personal capability to the source of strength behind action.

ramacharitamanas::4239.verse_sanskrit: मन संतोष सुनत कपि बानी। भगति प्रताप तेज बल सानी॥ आसिष दीन्हि राम प्रिय जाना। होहु तात बल सील निधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4239.verse_hindi: भक्ति, प्रताप, तेज और बल से सनी हुई हनुमान् जी की वाणी सुनकर सीताजी के मन में संतोष हुआ। उन्होंने श्री रामजी के प्रिय जानकर हनुमान् जी को आशीर्वाद दिया कि हे तात! तुम बल और शील के निधान होओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4239.english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's speech filled with devotion, radiance, power, and strength, Sita felt reassured. Recognising him as dear to Ram, she blessed him: “O child, may you become a storehouse of strength and character.”
ramacharitamanas::4239.translation_literal: मन (mind) / संतोष (contentment) / सुनत (hearing) / कपि (monkey) / बानी (speech) / भगति (devotion) / प्रताप (radiance/power) / तेज (splendour) / बल (strength) / सानी (filled with) / आसिष (blessing) / दीन्हि (gave) / राम (Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / जाना (knowing) / होहु (may you be) / तात (child) / बल (strength) / सील (character) / निधाना (treasure-house)
ramacharitamanas::4239.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4239.essence: Devotion that carries strength also brings comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4239.simple_meaning: Sita feels calm when she hears Hanuman's devoted, powerful speech. Seeing that he is dear to Ram, she blesses him to be full of strength and good character.
ramacharitamanas::4239.simple_insight: True devotion doesn’t just impress; it comforts, reassures, and blesses others.
ramacharitamanas::4239.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally revealed himself to Sita. His words carry devotion, power, radiance, and strength, and her fear begins to dissolve. Seeing that he belongs to Ram, she blesses him like a mother blessing a worthy son.
ramacharitamanas::4239.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such sincerity that your shoulders drop. No performance, no agenda — just steady goodness. That kind of presence makes trust possible again.
ramacharitamanas::4239.insight: It shows that spiritual strength becomes visible as calm, and that calm can awaken blessing in others.

ramacharitamanas::4240.verse_sanskrit: अजर अमर गुननिधि सुत होहू। करहुँ बहुत रघुनायक छोहू॥ करहुँ कृपा प्रभु अस सुनि काना। निर्भर प्रेम मगन हनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4240.verse_hindi: हे पुत्र! तुम अजर (बुढ़ापे से रहित), अमर और गुणों के खजाने होओ। श्री रघुनाथजी तुम पर बहुत कृपा करें। 'प्रभु कृपा करें' ऐसा कानों से सुनते ही हनुमान् जी पूर्ण प्रेम में मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4240.english_translation: “May you be unborn by decay, deathless, and a treasure-house of virtues. May Lord Raghunath show you great grace.” Hearing the words “the Lord will show grace,” Hanuman was lost in love.
ramacharitamanas::4240.translation_literal: अजर (free from aging) / अमर (deathless) / गुननिधि (treasure-house of virtues) / सुत (son) / होहू (may you become) / करहुँ (may [he] do) / बहुत (greatly) / रघुनायक (Lord of Raghu) / छोहू (grace) / करहुँ (may [he] do) / कृपा (grace) / प्रभु (Lord) / अस (thus) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (with the ears) / निर्भर (fully) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / हनुमाना (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4240.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4240.essence: Ram's grace alone is enough to dissolve Hanuman into love.
ramacharitamanas::4240.simple_meaning: Sita blesses Hanuman with long life, virtue, and Ram's grace. The moment he hears that Ram's grace is being spoken of, he is filled completely with love.
ramacharitamanas::4240.simple_insight: Even the hint of grace can open the heart fully.
ramacharitamanas::4240.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Sita blesses Hanuman after seeing his devotion and courage. She wishes him imperishable life and noble qualities, then speaks of Ram's grace. The mere hearing of that grace sends Hanuman into complete loving absorption.
ramacharitamanas::4240.modern_relevance: You hear one line from someone you trust — “you’re still in their good graces” — and your chest loosens instantly. That is the kind of devotion this verse captures.
ramacharitamanas::4240.insight: It shows how loving attention can move the mind from effort into pure absorption.

ramacharitamanas::4241.verse_sanskrit: बार बार नाएसि पद सीसा। बोला बचन जोरि कर कीसा॥ अब कृतकृत्य भयउँ मैं माता। आसिष तव अमोघ बिख्याता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4241.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने बार-बार सीताजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया और फिर हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे माता! अब मैं कृतार्थ हो गया। आपका आशीर्वाद अमोघ (अचूक) है, यह बात प्रसिद्ध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4241.english_translation: Hanuman bowed again and again at Sita's feet, then spoke with folded hands: "Mother, I am now fulfilled. Your blessing is known to be unfailing."
ramacharitamanas::4241.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / नाएसि (he bowed) / पद (feet) / सीसा (head) / बोला (spoke) / बचन (words) / जोरि कर (joining hands) / कीसा (the monkey) / अब (now) / कृतकृत्य (fulfilled) / भयउँ (I became) / मैं (I) / माता (mother) / आसिष (blessing) / तव (your) / अमोघ (unfailing) / बिख्याता (well-known)
ramacharitamanas::4241.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4241.essence: Bow without pride, and service itself becomes your fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::4241.simple_meaning: Hanuman bows to Sita with deep respect and says he feels fulfilled by her blessing, which never fails.
ramacharitamanas::4241.simple_insight: True devotion leaves no emptiness behind; even a hard journey can end in quiet completion.
ramacharitamanas::4241.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita after crossing the ocean and risking everything for Ram. Before asking anything more, he bows again and again at her feet and says he feels fulfilled, because her blessing is certain and powerful.
ramacharitamanas::4241.modern_relevance: After helping someone through a crisis, you leave the room without needing praise, because the act itself already settled something inside you.
ramacharitamanas::4241.insight: It shifts the mind from seeking recognition to feeling complete through selfless service.

ramacharitamanas::4242.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु मातु मोहि अतिसय भूखा। लागि देखि सुंदर फल रूखा॥ सुनु सुत करहिं बिपिन रखवारी। परम सुभट रजनीचर भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4242.verse_hindi: हे माता! सुनो, सुंदर फल वाले वृक्षों को देखकर मुझे बड़ी ही भूख लग आई है। (सीताजी ने कहा-) हे बेटा! सुनो, बड़े भारी योद्धा राक्षस इस वन की रखवाली करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4242.english_translation: Listen, Mother: I am very hungry. Seeing these beautiful fruit trees has made me eager for them. Listen, my son: mighty night-watchers guard this grove.
ramacharitamanas::4242.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / मातु (mother) / मोहि (to me) / अतिसय (very much) / भूखा (hungry) / लागि (having felt) / देखि (seeing) / सुंदर (beautiful) / फल (fruits) / रूखा (trees)॥ / सुनु (listen) / सुत (son) / करहिं (are doing) / बिपिन (forest) / रखवारी (guarding) / परम (great) / सुभट (warriors) / रजनीचर (night-roamers) / भारी (mighty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4242.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4242.essence: A simple excuse opens the door to a dangerous meeting.
ramacharitamanas::4242.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita he is hungry after seeing the fruit trees, and Sita warns him that fierce night-guardians protect the grove.
ramacharitamanas::4242.simple_insight: Even a holy mission can begin with a simple, human need.
ramacharitamanas::4242.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Hanuman finally meets Sita after crossing into Lanka. He speaks lightly about hunger to avoid alarming her, and Sita answers with caution, reminding him that fierce guards watch the grove. The exchange sets up the next step of their secret meeting.
ramacharitamanas::4242.modern_relevance: You walk into a place where you do not belong, trying to stay calm while your stomach knots and every sound feels risky. Even then, you keep the conversation gentle.
ramacharitamanas::4242.insight: It shows how courage can wear the face of ordinary conversation, even under danger.

ramacharitamanas::4243.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह कर भय माता मोहि नाहीं। जौं तुम्ह सुख मानहु मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4243.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! यदि आप मन में सुख मानें (प्रसन्न होकर) आज्ञा दें तो मुझे उनका भय तो बिलकुल नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4243.english_translation: Mother, I have no fear of them. If you are pleased in your heart, then give me your blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4243.translation_literal: तिन्ह (of them) / कर (their) / भय (fear) / माता (mother) / मोहि (to me) / नाहीं (not) / जौं (if) / तुम्ह (you) / सुख (pleased) / मानहु (consider) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::4243.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4243.essence: Fear disappears when service is rooted in another's approval.
ramacharitamanas::4243.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that the guards do not frighten him. What matters most is whether she is pleased and gives permission.
ramacharitamanas::4243.simple_insight: Real courage grows when your heart is aligned with the person you serve.
ramacharitamanas::4243.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Hanuman has found Sita and is speaking gently after offering her fruit and news of Ram. She warns him about the fierce guards around the grove. Hanuman answers that their fear means nothing if she is pleased in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::4243.modern_relevance: You ask for permission before stepping in to help a friend in crisis. The room is tense, but what steadies you is not confidence in yourself — it is knowing they trust you.
ramacharitamanas::4243.insight: It shifts courage from self-confidence to faithful service and consent.

ramacharitamanas::4244.verse_sanskrit: देखि बुद्धि बल निपुन कपि कहेउ जानकीं जाहु। रघुपति चरन हृदयँ धरि तात मधुर फल खाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4244.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी को बुद्धि और बल में निपुण देखकर जानकीजी ने कहा- जाओ। हे तात! श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों को हृदय में धारण करके मीठे फल खाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4244.english_translation: Seeing the monkey's skill in intelligence and strength, Sita said, "Go. O dear one, keep Raghupati's feet in your heart and eat the sweet fruits."
ramacharitamanas::4244.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / बुद्धि (intelligence) / बल (strength) / निपुन (skilled) / कपि (monkey) / कहेउ (said) / जानकीं (to Janaki) / जाहु (go) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / चरन (feet) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धरि (placing) / तात (dear one) / मधुर (sweet) / फल (fruits) / खाहु (eat)
ramacharitamanas::4244.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4244.essence: Remembrance of Ram turns even eating into bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::4244.simple_meaning: Sita sees Hanuman's skill and gives him permission to eat the fruit, asking him to keep Ram in his heart while doing so.
ramacharitamanas::4244.simple_insight: Even a simple act becomes safe and joyful when it is rooted in remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::4244.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Vatika, Sita has just tested Hanuman's strength and intelligence. Seeing that he is capable and trustworthy, she gives him permission to eat the fruits, but only after placing Ram in his heart. The moment turns a hungry search into sacred service.
ramacharitamanas::4244.modern_relevance: You open a snack after a brutal day, but your mind is still racing. This verse says even ordinary relief can begin with remembrance, not distraction.
ramacharitamanas::4244.insight: It shifts action from appetite alone to action guided by devotion and inner recollection.

ramacharitamanas::4245.verse_sanskrit: चलेउ नाइ सिरु पैठेउ बागा। फल खाएसि तरु तोरैं लागा॥ रहे तहाँ बहु भट रखवारे। कछु मारेसि कछु जाइ पुकारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4245.verse_hindi: वे सीताजी को सिर नवाकर चले और बाग में घुस गए। फल खाए और वृक्षों को तोड़ने लगे। वहाँ बहुत से योद्धा रखवाले थे। उनमें से कुछ को मार डाला और कुछ ने जाकर रावण से पुकार की- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4245.english_translation: He bowed his head and entered the grove. He ate the fruit and began uprooting the trees. Many guards were stationed there. He killed some, and some ran to report it.
ramacharitamanas::4245.translation_literal: चलेउ (he went) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / पैठेउ (entered) / बागा (grove) / फल (fruit) / खाएसि (he ate) / तरु (trees) / तोरैं (to break/uproot) / लागा (began) / रहे (were stationed) / तहाँ (there) / बहु (many) / भट (warriors) / रखवारे (guards) / कछु (some) / मारेसि (he killed) / कछु (some) / जाइ (going) / पुकारे (called out)
ramacharitamanas::4245.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4245.essence: Fearless service can look disruptive to those guarding power.
ramacharitamanas::4245.simple_meaning: Hanuman enters the grove, eats the fruit, uproots the trees, and fights the guards who try to stop him.
ramacharitamanas::4245.simple_insight: Sometimes a mission asks for complete fearlessness, not politeness.
ramacharitamanas::4245.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka and stepped into Ashoka Vatika after bowing to Sita in his heart. What begins as a search quickly becomes a bold challenge to Ravana's power: he eats, tears down trees, and confronts the guards.
ramacharitamanas::4245.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to stay small, but your purpose is bigger than their discomfort. You do the work anyway.
ramacharitamanas::4245.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to fearless action when the moment demands it.

ramacharitamanas::4246.verse_sanskrit: नाथ एक आवा कपि भारी। तेहिं असोक बाटिका उजारी॥ खाएसि फल अरु बिटप उपारे। रच्छक मर्दि मर्दि महि डारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4246.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) हे नाथ! एक बड़ा भारी बंदर आया है। उसने अशोक वाटिका उजाड़ डाली। फल खाए, वृक्षों को उखाड़ डाला और रखवालों को मसल-मसलकर जमीन पर डाल दिया ॥
