ramacharitamanas::4246.english_translation: “Lord, a huge monkey has come. He has ruined the Ashoka grove, eaten the fruit, uprooted the trees, and crushed the guards to the ground.”
ramacharitamanas::4246.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / एक (one) / आवा (came) / कपि (monkey) / भारी (huge, heavy) / तेहिं (by him) / असोक (Ashoka) / बाटिका (grove) / उजारी (ruined) / खाएसि (he ate) / फल (fruit) / अरु (and) / बिटप (trees) / उपारे (uprooted) / रच्छक (guards) / मर्दि मर्दि (crushing repeatedly) / महि (to the ground) / डारे (threw down)
ramacharitamanas::4246.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4246.essence: The search has turned into force.
ramacharitamanas::4246.simple_meaning: A guard reports that Hanuman has torn through the Ashoka grove, eaten the fruit, uprooted trees, and beaten the guards down.
ramacharitamanas::4246.simple_insight: It is a moment of alarm, not reflection — the search has turned into open conflict.
ramacharitamanas::4246.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a frightened guard rushes to Ravana with news of Hanuman's rampage in the Ashoka grove. The message is not philosophical; it is a report of disruption that raises the stakes before the fighting intensifies.
ramacharitamanas::4246.modern_relevance: A colleague bursts into the room saying the quiet plan has already collapsed, and the person everyone underestimated has changed everything.
ramacharitamanas::4246.insight: It sets up the next clash by showing that Hanuman is no longer hiding or waiting.

ramacharitamanas::4247.verse_sanskrit: सुनि रावन पठए भट नाना। तिन्हहि देखि गर्जेउ हनुमाना॥ सब रजनीचर कपि संघारे। गए पुकारत कछु अधमारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4247.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर रावण ने बहुत से योद्धा भेजे। उन्हें देखकर हनुमान् जी ने गर्जना की। हनुमान् जी ने सब राक्षसों को मार डाला, कुछ जो अधमरे थे, चिल्लाते हुए गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4247.english_translation: Hearing this, Ravana sent many warriors. Seeing them, Hanuman roared. He killed all the night-walkers; some half-dead ran away crying.
ramacharitamanas::4247.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / रावन (Ravana) / पठए (sent) / भट (warriors) / नाना (many) / तिन्हहि (them) / देखि (seeing) / गर्जेउ (roared) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / सब (all) / रजनीचर (night-walkers) / कपि (monkey) / संघारे (killed) / गए (went) / पुकारत (crying out) / कछु (some) / अधमारे (half-dead)
ramacharitamanas::4247.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4247.essence: Force without steadiness only creates more defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4247.simple_meaning: Ravana sends more fighters, but Hanuman meets them with fierce force and defeats them all.
ramacharitamanas::4247.simple_insight: Some threats collapse the moment they meet steady courage.
ramacharitamanas::4247.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers Hanuman's devastation of the Ashoka grove by sending more warriors. Hanuman roars back and crushes them too. The verse keeps the action moving, showing how quickly Ravana's defense turns into another defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4247.modern_relevance: A group chat turns hostile, and you realize the first sharp reply only invites more noise. Sometimes the strongest response is simply not to be shaken.
ramacharitamanas::4247.insight: It shows that fear-fed resistance can be broken by unflinching strength.

ramacharitamanas::4248.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पठयउ तेहिं अच्छकुमारा। चला संग लै सुभट अपारा॥ आवत देखि बिटप गहि तर्जा। ताहि निपाति महाधुनि गर्जा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4248.verse_hindi: फिर रावण ने अक्षयकुमार को भेजा। वह असंख्य श्रेष्ठ योद्धाओं को साथ लेकर चला। उसे आते देखकर हनुमान् जी ने एक वृक्ष (हाथ में) लेकर ललकारा और उसे मारकर महाध्वनि (बड़े जोर) से गर्जना की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4248.english_translation: Ravana sent Akshayakumar again. He came with countless elite warriors. Seeing him approach, Hanuman seized a tree and challenged him, then struck him down and roared with a thunderous cry.
ramacharitamanas::4248.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / पठयउ (sent) / तेहिं (he) / अच्छकुमारा (Akshayakumar) / चला (went) / संग (with) / लै (taking) / सुभट (elite warriors) / अपारा (countless) / आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / बिटप (tree) / गहि (grasping) / तर्जा (challenged) / ताहि (him) / निपाति (struck down) / महाधुनि (great sound) / गर्जा (roared)
ramacharitamanas::4248.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4248.essence: Fear collapses when you meet force with fearless presence.
ramacharitamanas::4248.simple_meaning: Ravana sends another commander with a huge force. Hanuman grabs a tree, confronts him, kills him, and roars in victory.
ramacharitamanas::4248.simple_insight: Some challenges only meet you with full force. When you stand your ground, fear loses its hold.
ramacharitamanas::4248.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps sending stronger fighters to stop Hanuman from destroying the Ashoka grove. Akshayakumar arrives with a large force, but Hanuman answers with fearless strength, killing him in open confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::4248.modern_relevance: A problem keeps escalating in your inbox, and then a manager forwards it to someone even tougher. You stop shrinking, face it directly, and the pressure changes.
ramacharitamanas::4248.insight: It shows that fear is broken by direct, fearless response, not by retreat.

ramacharitamanas::4249.verse_sanskrit: कछु मारेसि कछु मर्देसि कछु मिलएसि धरि धूरि। कछु पुनि जाइ पुकारे प्रभु मर्कट बल भूरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4249.verse_hindi: उन्होंने सेना में से कुछ को मार डाला और कुछ को मसल डाला और कुछ को पकड़-पकड़कर धूल में मिला दिया। कुछ ने फिर जाकर पुकार की कि हे प्रभु! बंदर बहुत ही बलवान् है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4249.english_translation: He killed some, crushed some, and flung some into the dust. Some ran back crying, “My lord, that monkey is immensely strong!”
ramacharitamanas::4249.translation_literal: कछु (some) / मारेसि (he killed) / कछु (some) / मर्देसि (he crushed) / कछु (some) / मिलएसि (he mixed/flung) / धरि (into) / धूरि (dust) / कछु (some) / पुनि (again) / जाइ (going) / पुकारे (called out) / प्रभु (lord) / मर्कट (monkey) / बल (strength) / भूरि (very much)
ramacharitamanas::4249.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4249.essence: Panic spreads when resistance meets unstoppable force.
ramacharitamanas::4249.simple_meaning: Hanuman overwhelms Ravana’s soldiers so completely that the survivors flee and report his immense strength.
ramacharitamanas::4249.simple_insight: The scene shows fear spreading faster than resistance when courage is overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::4249.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already destroyed wave after wave of Ravana’s troops. The survivors run back in panic, reporting his power to their lord. This is not a teaching verse but a battlefield detail that carries the fight forward.
ramacharitamanas::4249.insight: It advances the battle by showing that Hanuman’s force has broken the enemy’s confidence.

ramacharitamanas::4250.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुत बध लंकेस रिसाना। पठएसि मेघनाद बलवाना॥ मारसि जनि सुत बाँधेसु ताही। देखिअ कपिहि कहाँ कर आही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4250.verse_hindi: पुत्र का वध सुनकर रावण क्रोधित हो उठा और उसने (अपने जेठे पुत्र) बलवान् मेघनाद को भेजा। (उससे कहा कि-) हे पुत्र! मारना नहीं उसे बाँध लाना। उस बंदर को देखा जाए कि कहाँ का है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4250.english_translation: Hearing of his son’s death, Ravana burned with rage and sent the mighty Meghnad. “Do not kill him; bind him and bring him. Let us see what kind of monkey this is.”
ramacharitamanas::4250.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुत (son) / बध (killing) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / रिसाना (became enraged) / पठएसि (sent) / मेघनाद (Meghnad) / बलवाना (powerful) ॥ / मारसि (kill) / जनि (do not) / सुत (son) / बाँधेसु (bind and bring) / ताही (him) ॥ / देखिअ (let us see) / कपिहि (the monkey) / कहाँ (from where) / कर (of) / आही (has come) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4250.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4250.essence: Pride does not seek understanding; it seeks to seize and punish.
ramacharitamanas::4250.simple_meaning: Ravana hears that his son has been killed, grows furious, and sends Meghnad with orders to capture Hanuman alive.
ramacharitamanas::4250.simple_insight: Rage narrows the mind fast; it stops asking what is wise and only wants control.
ramacharitamanas::4250.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears that his son has been slain. Furious and humiliated, he sends Meghnad, his strongest son, with a strange order: do not kill the monkey, capture him alive and find out who he is.
ramacharitamanas::4250.modern_relevance: You get the message that someone has crossed a line, and your first impulse is not clarity but retaliation. The mind wants to strike back before it understands.
ramacharitamanas::4250.insight: It shows how wounded pride turns into a demand to dominate rather than to discern.

ramacharitamanas::4251.verse_sanskrit: चला इंद्रजित अतुलित जोधा। बंधु निधन सुनि उपजा क्रोधा॥ कपि देखा दारुन भट आवा। कटकटाइ गर्जा अरु धावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4251.verse_hindi: इंद्र को जीतने वाला अतुलनीय योद्धा मेघनाद चला। भाई का मारा जाना सुन उसे क्रोध हो आया। हनुमान् जी ने देखा कि अबकी भयानक योद्धा आया है। तब वे कटकटाकर गर्जे और दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4251.english_translation: The incomparable warrior Indrajit advanced. Hearing of his brother's death, anger arose in him. Hanuman saw that a terrible fighter had arrived, and he roared and charged.
ramacharitamanas::4251.translation_literal: चला (advanced) / इंद्रजित (Indrajit) / अतुलित (incomparable) / जोधा (warrior)। / बंधु (brother) / निधन (death) / सुनि (hearing) / उपजा (arose) / क्रोधा (anger)॥ / कपि (monkey; Hanuman) / देखा (saw) / दारुन (terrible) / भट (fighter) / आवा (had come)। / कटकटाइ (roaring fiercely) / गर्जा (roared) / अरु (and) / धावा (charged)॥
ramacharitamanas::4251.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4251.essence: Fury meets fearless force on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4251.simple_meaning: Indrajit comes forward in anger after hearing his brother was killed, and Hanuman meets him with a fierce roar and charge.
ramacharitamanas::4251.simple_insight: It shows courage that answers rage without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4251.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sends Indrajit after hearing of his son's death. The mighty warrior advances in fury, and Hanuman sees a dangerous opponent coming. This verse marks the clash before the next fierce exchange.
ramacharitamanas::4251.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room after hearing bad news, jaw set and heart hot. Someone else meets that heat without flinching.
ramacharitamanas::4251.insight: It keeps the focus on action under pressure, not inner debate.

ramacharitamanas::4252.verse_sanskrit: अति बिसाल तरु एक उपारा। बिरथ कीन्ह लंकेस कुमारा॥ रहे महाभट ताके संगा। गहि गहि कपि मर्दई निज अंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4252.verse_hindi: उन्होंने एक बहुत बड़ा वृक्ष उखाड़ लिया और (उसके प्रहार से) लंकेश्वर रावण के पुत्र मेघनाद को बिना रथ का कर दिया। (रथ को तोड़कर उसे नीचे पटक दिया)। उसके साथ जो बड़े-बड़े योद्धा थे, उनको पकड़-पकड़कर हनुमान् जी अपने शरीर से मसलने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4252.english_translation: He uprooted a huge tree and struck Ravana's son, leaving him without a chariot. Then he grabbed the great warriors with him and crushed them against his own body.
ramacharitamanas::4252.translation_literal: अति (very) / बिसाल (huge) / तरु (tree) / एक (one) / उपारा (uprooted) / बिरथ (without a chariot) / कीन्ह (made) / लंकेस (of Lanka's lord) / कुमारा (son) / रहे (remained) / महाभट (great warriors) / ताके (with him) / संगा (together) / गहि गहि (grasping again and again) / कपि (the monkey) / मर्दई (crushed) / निज (his own) / अंगा (body)
ramacharitamanas::4252.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4252.essence: Force meets force in a single, unstoppable burst.
ramacharitamanas::4252.simple_meaning: Hanuman tears up a tree, destroys Meghnad's chariot, and overpowers the warriors around him with sheer force.
ramacharitamanas::4252.simple_insight: Raw strength can clear a path when nothing else will.
ramacharitamanas::4252.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already turned from search to combat. Meghnad arrives with elite warriors, and Hanuman answers with a tree torn from the ground. The scene is a burst of battlefield force, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4252.modern_relevance: A crisis hits fast: the phone rings, the plan collapses, and you stop overthinking and do the one hard thing in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4252.insight: It shifts attention from strategy to decisive action under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4253.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि निपाति ताहि सन बाजा। भिरे जुगल मानहुँ गजराजा॥ मुठिका मारि चढ़ा तरु जाई। ताहि एक छन मुरुछा आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4253.verse_hindi: उन सबको मारकर फिर मेघनाद से लड़ने लगे। (लड़ते हुए वे ऐसे मालूम होते थे) मानो दो गजराज (श्रेष्ठ हाथी) भिड़ गए हों। हनुमान् जी उसे एक घूँसा मारकर वृक्ष पर जा चढ़े। उसको क्षणभर के लिए मूर्च्छा आ गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4253.english_translation: After defeating them all, he fought with Meghnad again. The two clashed like mighty elephants. Hanuman struck him with a fist, leapt back up into a tree, and Meghnad fell unconscious for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::4253.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (them all) / निपाति (having struck down) / ताहि (him) / सन (with) / बाजा (he fought) / भिरे (clashed) / जुगल (the pair) / मानहुँ (as if) / गजराजा (king-elephants) / मुठिका (with a fist) / मारि (striking) / चढ़ा (he climbed) / तरु (tree) / जाई (going) / ताहि (him) / एक (one) / छन (moment) / मुरुछा (fainting) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::4253.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4253.essence: The fight keeps moving, and Hanuman keeps answering.
ramacharitamanas::4253.simple_meaning: Hanuman defeats Meghnad's men, fights Meghnad like two powerful elephants, lands a fist, and briefly knocks him unconscious.
ramacharitamanas::4253.simple_insight: Steady courage can keep rising even after a hard blow.
ramacharitamanas::4253.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is still in battle after smashing Meghnad's allies. He and Meghnad clash head-on like great elephants. Hanuman lands a punch, leaps into a tree, and briefly staggers the enemy prince. The verse keeps the fight moving, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4253.modern_relevance: You’re in the middle of a heated argument and the other person comes back harder than before. You don’t need a grand speech — just enough steadiness to stay standing.
ramacharitamanas::4253.insight: It shows relentless action under pressure, not reflection or doctrine.

ramacharitamanas::4254.verse_sanskrit: उठि बहोरि कीन्हिसि बहु माया। जीति न जाइ प्रभंजन जाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4254.verse_hindi: फिर उठकर उसने बहुत माया रची, परंतु पवन के पुत्र उससे जीते नहीं जाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4254.english_translation: Rising again, he cast many illusions, but the son of the wind could not be defeated.
ramacharitamanas::4254.translation_literal: उठि (rising) / बहोरि (again) / कीन्हिसि (he made) / बहु (many) / माया (illusions) / जीति (to be defeated) / न (not) / जाइ (is possible) / प्रभंजन जाया (the son of the wind)
ramacharitamanas::4254.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4254.essence: Repeated tricks cannot defeat steady courage.
ramacharitamanas::4254.simple_meaning: Ravana's side uses more tricks, but Hanuman still cannot be overcome.
ramacharitamanas::4254.simple_insight: False appearances lose their force when courage stays steady.
ramacharitamanas::4254.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already smashed Meghnad's attack. Meghnad rises again and throws out more illusions, trying to confuse him. But Hanuman, the son of the wind, remains unconquerable in this clash.
ramacharitamanas::4254.modern_relevance: A room full of polished lies can still fail against someone who stays clear and steady. The pressure rises, the tricks multiply, but you do not have to be shaken.
ramacharitamanas::4254.insight: It shows that endurance and clarity can outlast even repeated deception.

ramacharitamanas::4255.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्म अस्त्र तेहि साँधा कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार। जौं न ब्रह्मसर मानउँ महिमा मिटइ अपार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4255.verse_hindi: अंत में उसने ब्रह्मास्त्र का संधान (प्रयोग) किया, तब हनुमान् जी ने मन में विचार किया कि यदि ब्रह्मास्त्र को नहीं मानता हूँ तो उसकी अपार महिमा मिट जाएगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4255.english_translation: Hanuman then thought: if I do not respect the Brahmastra, its great power will be diminished.
ramacharitamanas::4255.translation_literal: ब्रह्म-अस्त्र (Brahma-weapon) / तेहि (that) / साँधा (aimed) / कपि (the monkey) / मन (mind) / कीन्ह (made) / बिचार (thought) / जौं (if) / न (not) / ब्रह्म-सर (Brahma-arrow) / मानउँ (I respect) / महिमा (glory) / मिटइ (will diminish) / अपार (vast)
ramacharitamanas::4255.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4255.essence: True strength can honour force without losing itself.
ramacharitamanas::4255.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees the Brahmastra coming and decides to honor it, because refusing it would diminish its immense power.
ramacharitamanas::4255.simple_insight: Even strength bows to a force greater than itself.
ramacharitamanas::4255.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already fought through Meghnad's tricks and superiority display. When the Brahmastra is aimed at him, he does not react with pride. He pauses and chooses respect, knowing that ignoring it would dishonour its immense force.
ramacharitamanas::4255.modern_relevance: You are in a heated argument and could bulldoze ahead, but you stop and acknowledge the other person's point. That pause keeps your strength from becoming arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4255.insight: It teaches you to recognize legitimate power without letting ego turn resistance into self-defeat.

ramacharitamanas::4256.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मबान कपि कहुँ तेहिं मारा। परतिहुँ बार कटकु संघारा॥ तेहिं देखा कपि मुरुछित भयऊ। नागपास बाँधेसि लै गयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4256.verse_hindi: उसने हनुमान् जी को ब्रह्मबाण मारा, (जिसके लगते ही वे वृक्ष से नीचे गिर पड़े), परंतु गिरते समय भी उन्होंने बहुत सी सेना मार डाली। जब उसने देखा कि हनुमान् जी मूर्छित हो गए हैं, तब वह उनको नागपाश से बाँधकर ले गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4256.english_translation: He struck Hanuman with a Brahma weapon; even as he fell, he destroyed many troops. When he saw Hanuman unconscious, he bound him with the serpent noose and carried him away.
ramacharitamanas::4256.translation_literal: ब्रह्मबान (Brahma weapon) / कपि कहुँ (at the monkey) / तेहिं (he) / मारा (struck) / परतिहुँ (even while falling) / बार (many) / कटकु (troops) / संघारा (destroyed) / तेहिं (he) / देखा (saw) / कपि (the monkey) / मुरुछित (unconscious) / भयऊ (became) / नागपास (serpent noose) / बाँधेसि (bound) / लै गयऊ (carried away)
ramacharitamanas::4256.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4256.essence: Even when struck down, true resolve keeps fighting.
ramacharitamanas::4256.simple_meaning: Hanuman is struck down, yet even in falling he keeps destroying the enemy. Then the enemy binds him with a serpent noose and takes him away.
ramacharitamanas::4256.simple_insight: Even defeat cannot erase courage when your cause is larger than fear.
ramacharitamanas::4256.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been fighting through Ravana's forces alone. A Brahma weapon finally knocks him unconscious, but not before he cuts down more troops in his fall. Seeing him stunned, the enemy captures and binds him with the serpent noose.
ramacharitamanas::4256.modern_relevance: A project collapses after weeks of effort, yet your work still leaves a mark before it ends. Sometimes the final fall does not cancel the force of what you gave.
ramacharitamanas::4256.insight: It shows that steadfast effort can continue even under collapse, before the body or plan finally yields.

ramacharitamanas::4257.verse_sanskrit: जासु नाम जपि सुनहु भवानी। भव बंधन काटहिं नर ग्यानी॥ तासु दूत कि बंध तरु आवा। प्रभु कारज लगि कपिहिं बँधावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4257.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी सुनो, जिनका नाम जपकर ज्ञानी (विवेकी) मनुष्य संसार (जन्म-मरण) के बंधन को काट डालते हैं, उनका दूत कहीं बंधन में आ सकता है? किंतु प्रभु के कार्य के लिए हनुमान् जी ने स्वयं अपने को बँधा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4257.english_translation: O Bhavani, listen: by chanting whose name wise people cut through the bonds of worldly becoming, could that being's messenger ever be bound? Yet for the Lord's work, Hanuman allowed himself to be bound.
ramacharitamanas::4257.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / जपि (chanting) / सुनहु (listen) / भवानी (Bhavani) / भव (worldly becoming) / बंधन (bondage) / काटहिं (cut) / नर (men) / ग्यानी (wise) / तासु (of that one) / दूत (messenger) / कि (can?) / बंध (bond) / तरु (tree) / आवा (came) / प्रभु (Lord's) / कारज (work) / लगि (for) / कपिहिं (the monkey) / बँधावा (was bound / bound himself)
ramacharitamanas::4257.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4257.essence: True devotion can turn even bondage into service.
ramacharitamanas::4257.simple_meaning: Ram's name frees wise people from bondage, so his messenger cannot truly be bound. Hanuman was bound only because he chose to serve Ram's work.
ramacharitamanas::4257.simple_insight: Real devotion can make even restraint feel like service, not defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4257.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just been captured after the brahmastra and brought before Ravana's court. Shiva turns to Parvati and points out the paradox: the one whose name frees people from bondage cannot be bound in any ordinary sense. Hanuman's chains exist only because he accepts them for Ram's mission.
ramacharitamanas::4257.modern_relevance: You take the blame in a meeting to protect someone else. It looks like defeat from the outside, but you know exactly why you stayed quiet.
ramacharitamanas::4257.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing surrender as weakness to seeing it as chosen service.

ramacharitamanas::4258.verse_sanskrit: कपि बंधन सुनि निसिचर धाए। कौतुक लागि सभाँ सब आए॥ दसमुख सभा दीखि कपि जाई। कहि न जाइ कछु अति प्रभुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4258.verse_hindi: बंदर का बाँधा जाना सुनकर राक्षस दौड़े और कौतुक के लिए (तमाशा देखने के लिए) सब सभा में आए। हनुमान् जी ने जाकर रावण की सभा देखी। उसकी अत्यंत प्रभुता (ऐश्वर्य) कुछ कही नहीं जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4258.english_translation: Hearing that the monkey had been bound, the demons rushed out and came to the assembly for a spectacle. Hanuman then went and saw Ravana's court; its immense splendor cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::4258.translation_literal: कपि (monkey) / बंधन (binding) / सुनि (hearing) / निसिचर (demons) / धाए (ran) । / कौतुक (curiosity, spectacle) / लागि (for) / सभाँ (assembly) / सब (all) / आए (came) ॥ / दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / सभा (court) / दीखि (seeing) / कपि (monkey) / जाई (went) । / कहि (said) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / कछु (anything) / अति (great) / प्रभुताई (splendor, majesty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4258.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4258.essence: Power can fill a room and still fail to shake the fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4258.simple_meaning: The demons hurry to see the bound Hanuman, and Hanuman is brought before Ravana's magnificent court.
ramacharitamanas::4258.simple_insight: Even in captivity, you can still walk into the center of power without losing yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4258.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, news spreads that Hanuman has been captured. The demons rush in to watch the spectacle. Hanuman is then taken into Ravana's assembly, where he sees the full force of Ravana's royal display before the deeper confrontation begins.
ramacharitamanas::4258.modern_relevance: You walk into a boardroom where everyone already knows your name, and the room is built to intimidate. The size of the place is real, but so is your steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::4258.insight: It sets up the contrast between Ravana's outward grandeur and Hanuman's unshaken presence.

ramacharitamanas::4259.verse_sanskrit: कर जोरें सुर दिसिप बिनीता। भृकुटि बिलोकत सकल सभीता॥ देखि प्रताप न कपि मन संका। जिमि अहिगन महुँ गरुड़ असंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4259.verse_hindi: देवता और दिक्पाल हाथ जोड़े बड़ी नम्रता के साथ भयभीत हुए सब रावण की भौं ताक रहे हैं। (उसका रुख देख रहे हैं) उसका ऐसा प्रताप देखकर भी हनुमान् जी के मन में जरा भी डर नहीं हुआ। वे ऐसे निःशंख खड़े रहे, जैसे सर्पों के समूह में गरुड़ निःशंख निर्भय) रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4259.english_translation: The radiant beings and guardians of the directions folded their hands in fear, watching his stern brow. Yet Hanuman felt no fear at all; he stood unshaken, like Garuda among a mass of serpents.
ramacharitamanas::4259.translation_literal: कर जोरें (with hands folded) / सुर (radiant beings) / दिसिप (guardians of the directions) / बिनीता (humble) / भृकुटि (brow) / बिलोकत (watching) / सकल (all) / सभीता (fearful) / देखि (seeing) / प्रताप (power, splendour) / न (not) / कपि (the monkey hero) / मन (mind) / संका (doubt, fear) / जिमि (like) / अहिगन (serpent groups) / महुँ (among) / गरुड़ (Garuda) / असंका (fearless)
ramacharitamanas::4259.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4259.essence: Fear loses its grip when your purpose is steady.
ramacharitamanas::4259.simple_meaning: Even the celestial beings fear Ravana, but Hanuman does not. His courage stays steady in the middle of danger.
ramacharitamanas::4259.simple_insight: Real courage is calm when everyone else is shrinking back.
ramacharitamanas::4259.detailed_meaning: Inside Ravana’s court in Lanka, the heavens themselves seem to bow before his power. The guards and radiant beings are afraid, but Hanuman stands before him without a tremor. This verse shows the fearless poise that makes his mission possible.
ramacharitamanas::4259.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is intimidated by the loudest person there. Your chest tightens, but you keep your footing and speak clearly anyway.
ramacharitamanas::4259.insight: It teaches you to stay steady when power tries to make you smaller.

ramacharitamanas::4260.verse_sanskrit: कपिहि बिलोकि दसानन बिहसा कहि दुर्बाद। सुत बध सुरति कीन्हि पुनि उपजा हृदयँ बिसाद ॥
ramacharitamanas::4260.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी को देखकर रावण दुर्वचन कहता हुआ खूब हँसा। फिर पुत्र वध का स्मरण किया तो उसके हृदय में विषाद उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4260.english_translation: Seeing Hanuman, Ravana laughed hard and spoke abusive words. Then he remembered his son's death, and sorrow rose in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4260.translation_literal: कपिहि (the monkey) / बिलोकि (seeing) / दसानन (the ten-faced one) / बिहसा (laughed) / कहि (speaking) / दुर्बाद (abusive words) / सुत (son) / बध (killing) / सुरति (memory) / कीन्हि (did) / पुनि (again) / उपजा (arose) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिसाद (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::4260.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4260.essence: Mockery can hide grief for only a moment.
ramacharitamanas::4260.simple_meaning: Ravana first mocks Hanuman, then remembers his dead son and feels sudden sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4260.simple_insight: Pride can laugh in one moment and collapse into grief the next.
ramacharitamanas::4260.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana’s court after being seized. Ravana tries to cover fear with contempt, but the sight also stirs the memory of his slain son. The verse captures his flicker between arrogance and pain before the questioning begins.
ramacharitamanas::4260.modern_relevance: You snap at someone in public, then one private memory undoes you. The mask of strength drops the moment grief returns.
ramacharitamanas::4260.insight: It shows how quickly ego can turn from mockery to wounded sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::4261.verse_sanskrit: कह लंकेस कवन तैं कीसा। केहि कें बल घालेहि बन खीसा॥ की धौं श्रवन सुनेहि नहिं मोही। देखउँ अति असंक सठ तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4261.verse_hindi: लंकापति रावण ने कहा- रे वानर! तू कौन है? किसके बल पर तूने वन को उजाड़कर नष्ट कर डाला? क्या तूने कभी मुझे (मेरा नाम और यश) कानों से नहीं सुना? रे शठ! मैं तुझे अत्यंत निःशंख देख रहा हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4261.english_translation: Lankesh Ravana said, “O monkey, who are you? By whose power have you ruined the forest? Have you never heard of me? I see you utterly fearless, fool.”
ramacharitamanas::4261.translation_literal: कह (said) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / कवन (who) / तैं (you) / कीसा (monkey) / केहि कें (by whose) / बल (strength) / घालेहि (you have ruined) / बन (forest) / खीसा (destroyed) / की धौं (or what, perhaps) / श्रवन (ears) / सुनेहि (have you heard) / नहिं (not) / मोही (me) / देखउँ (I see) / अति (very) / असंक (fearless) / सठ (fool) / तोही (you)
ramacharitamanas::4261.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4261.essence: Arrogance questions what fearless devotion already knows.
ramacharitamanas::4261.simple_meaning: Ravana confronts Hanuman with arrogance, demanding to know who he is and by what power he has acted so boldly.
ramacharitamanas::4261.simple_insight: Pride always wants to know what it can dominate. Fearless presence unsettles it.
ramacharitamanas::4261.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just seen the monkey who entered his city without fear. Instead of understanding Hanuman, he tries to reduce him with insults and threats. This is Ravana's ego meeting a devotion that cannot be intimidated.
ramacharitamanas::4261.modern_relevance: A powerful manager leans back and asks, "Who do you think you are?" when you calmly challenge a bad decision. That question often reveals more insecurity than strength.
ramacharitamanas::4261.insight: It shows how ego reacts when it meets courage it cannot control.

ramacharitamanas::4262.verse_sanskrit: मारे निसिचर केहिं अपराधा। कहु सठ तोहि न प्रान कइ बाधा॥ सुनु रावन ब्रह्मांड निकाया। पाइ जासु बल बिरचति माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4262.verse_hindi: तूने किस अपराध से राक्षसों को मारा? रे मूर्ख! बता, क्या तुझे प्राण जाने का भय नहीं है? (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे रावण! सुन, जिनका बल पाकर माया संपूर्ण ब्रह्मांडों के समूहों की रचना करती है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4262.english_translation: For what offense did you kill the demons? Tell me, fool—do you not fear for your life? Listen, Ravana: by whose power the countless worlds of the universe are formed through maya.
ramacharitamanas::4262.translation_literal: मारे (killed) / निसिचर (demons) / केहिं (which) / अपराधा (offense) / कहु (tell) / सठ (fool) / तोहि (you) / न (not) / प्रान (life) / कइ (of) / बाधा (fear or harm) ॥ सुनु (listen) / रावन (Ravana) / ब्रह्मांड (universe) / निकाया (multitudes or collections) / पाइ (having obtained) / जासु (whose) / बल (power) / बिरचति (creates) / माया (the veil of appearance) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4262.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4262.essence: Real fear disappears when your strength comes from beyond yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4262.simple_meaning: Hanuman answers Ravana's taunt by saying that true power belongs to the one whose strength creates the universe itself. Ravana's threats are small beside that.
ramacharitamanas::4262.simple_insight: Confidence becomes fearless when it rests on something far greater than ego.
ramacharitamanas::4262.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana mocks Hanuman and asks why he killed the demons and whether he fears death. Hanuman does not shrink back. He turns the exchange into a declaration that all power in the universe comes from the one who upholds creation itself.
ramacharitamanas::4262.modern_relevance: A hostile manager corners you in front of the team and tries to make you flinch. Hanuman's answer reminds you that real strength does not come from intimidation, but from what you stand on.
ramacharitamanas::4262.insight: It shifts courage away from personal bravado to trust in a power greater than threats.

ramacharitamanas::4263.verse_sanskrit: जाकें बल बिरंचि हरि ईसा। पालत सृजत हरत दससीसा॥ जा बल सीस धरत सहसानन। अंडकोस समेत गिरि कानन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4263.verse_hindi: जिनके बल से हे दशशीश! ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महेश (क्रमशः) सृष्टि का सृजन, पालन और संहार करते हैं, जिनके बल से सहस्रमुख (फणों) वाले शेषजी पर्वत और वनसहित समस्त ब्रह्मांड को सिर पर धारण करते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4263.english_translation: By whose power, O ten-headed one, Brahma creates, Vishnu preserves, and Shiva destroys. By whose power, Shesha with a thousand hoods holds the entire universe, including mountains and forests, upon his head.
ramacharitamanas::4263.translation_literal: जाकें (whose) / बल (power) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / ईसा (Shiva) / पालत (preserve) / सृजत (create) / हरत (destroy) / दससीसा (ten-headed one) / जा (whose) / बल (power) / सीस (head) / धरत (holds) / सहसानन (thousand-faced Shesha) / अंडकोस (universe) / समेत (together with) / गिरि (mountains) / कानन (forests)
ramacharitamanas::4263.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4263.essence: All power belongs to Ram, not to the proud who borrow it.
ramacharitamanas::4263.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that the supreme power behind creation, preservation, and destruction is not Ravana's strength, but Ram's.
ramacharitamanas::4263.simple_insight: Pride softens when you remember that even the greatest powers depend on something higher.
ramacharitamanas::4263.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to intimidate Hanuman. Hanuman answers without fear: the force behind Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and even Shesha is Ram's power. The boast of the king of Lanka collapses before a devotee who sees the source of all strength.
ramacharitamanas::4263.modern_relevance: A powerful executive storms into the room, expecting everyone to shrink. One calm person doesn't flinch because they know status is borrowed, not owned.
ramacharitamanas::4263.insight: It shifts attention from visible authority to the source that makes authority possible.

ramacharitamanas::4264.verse_sanskrit: धरइ जो बिबिध देह सुरत्राता। तुम्ह से सठन्ह सिखावनु दाता॥ हर कोदंड कठिन जेहिं भंजा। तेहि समेत नृप दल मद गंजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4264.verse_hindi: जो देवताओं की रक्षा के लिए नाना प्रकार की देह धारण करते हैं और जो तुम्हारे जैसे मूर्खों को शिक्षा देने वाले हैं, जिन्होंने शिवजी के कठोर धनुष को तोड़ डाला और उसी के साथ राजाओं के समूह का गर्व चूर्ण कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4264.english_translation: The one who protects the radiant beings takes many forms, teaches fools like you, broke Shiva’s hard bow, and crushed the pride of kings.
ramacharitamanas::4264.translation_literal: धरइ (takes) / जो (who) / बिबिध (various) / देह (bodies) / सुरत्राता (protector of the radiant beings) / तुम्ह (you) / से (like) / सठन्ह (fools) / सिखावनु (teaching) / दाता (giver) / हर (the one who removes) / कोदंड (bow) / कठिन (hard) / जेहिं (by whom) / भंजा (was broken) / तेहि (that) / समेत (along with) / नृप (kings) / दल (groups) / मद (pride) / गंजा (crushed)
ramacharitamanas::4264.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4264.essence: Ram’s greatness is proven by both compassion and irresistible power.
ramacharitamanas::4264.simple_meaning: Ram is the protector of the devas, the teacher of the foolish, the breaker of Shiva’s bow, and the destroyer of royal pride.
ramacharitamanas::4264.simple_insight: Greatness is not just power; it also has the force to correct arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4264.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana and speaks with fearless certainty. He names Ram as the divine protector, the teacher of the arrogant, the one who broke Shiva’s bow in Janakpur, and the one who shattered the pride of kings.
ramacharitamanas::4264.modern_relevance: A room full of powerful people can still go silent when one person speaks with unshakable clarity. The right presence does not just impress — it exposes arrogance and resets the room.
ramacharitamanas::4264.insight: It shifts reverence from brute strength to the power that protects, teaches, and restores right order.

ramacharitamanas::4265.verse_sanskrit: खर दूषन त्रिसिरा अरु बाली। बधे सकल अतुलित बलसाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4265.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने खर, दूषण, त्रिशिरा और बालि को मार डाला, जो सब के सब अतुलनीय बलवान् थे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4265.english_translation: He killed Khara, Dushana, Trisira, and Bali, all of them immeasurably powerful.
ramacharitamanas::4265.translation_literal: खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / त्रिसिरा (Trisira) / अरु (and) / बाली (Bali) / बधे (were slain) / सकल (all) / अतुलित (immeasurable) / बलसाली (powerful)
ramacharitamanas::4265.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4265.essence: Even the strongest foes fall before Ram's power.
ramacharitamanas::4265.simple_meaning: Ram's power is shown through the defeat of four mighty enemies.
ramacharitamanas::4265.simple_insight: Strength feels steady when it is rooted in a cause larger than ego.
ramacharitamanas::4265.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is praising Ram's unmatched power in Lanka. He reminds Ravana that Ram has already destroyed Khara, Dushana, Trisira, and Bali, each famous for immense strength. The point is not just victory, but proof that Ravana is facing someone far greater.
ramacharitamanas::4265.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses you because you look alone or outnumbered. Then they remember the one time you handled a problem everyone else feared. Reputation changes the room before you speak.
ramacharitamanas::4265.insight: It shifts attention from raw force to the source of force behind it.

ramacharitamanas::4266.verse_sanskrit: जाके बल लवलेस तें जितेहु चराचर झारि। तास दूत मैं जा करि हरि आनेहु प्रिय नारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4266.verse_hindi: जिनके लेशमात्र बल से तुमने समस्त चराचर जगत् को जीत लिया और जिनकी प्रिय पत्नी को तुम (चोरी से) हर लाए हो, मैं उन्हीं का दूत हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4266.english_translation: I am the messenger of the one whose mere slightest power you have conquered the entire moving and unmoving world, and whose beloved wife you have carried away.
ramacharitamanas::4266.translation_literal: जाके (whose) / बल (power) / लवलेस तें (by a mere particle) / जितेहु (you conquered) / चराचर (moving and unmoving world) / झारि (completely) / तास (of that one) / दूत (messenger) / मैं (I) / जा करि (for whom) / हरि (Hari) / आनेहु (you have brought away) / प्रिय नारि (beloved wife)
ramacharitamanas::4266.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4266.essence: Even the smallest trace of Ram's power makes conquest meaningless.
ramacharitamanas::4266.simple_meaning: Hanuman identifies himself as the messenger of Ram, whose tiny fraction of power has already defeated the entire world. Ravana is being warned that this is no ordinary envoy.
ramacharitamanas::4266.simple_insight: Real strength is often hidden behind humility, and pride fails when it ignores who sent the messenger.
ramacharitamanas::4266.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana after revealing his mission. He reminds Ravana that Ram, whom he has insulted by taking Sita, is the one whose slightest power has already conquered everything. The verse sharpens the warning before Ravana answers.
ramacharitamanas::4266.modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room, not noticing they speak for someone far stronger than they look. The mistake is never about the messenger alone.
ramacharitamanas::4266.insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to the source of authority behind an action or message.

ramacharitamanas::4267.verse_sanskrit: जानउँ मैं तुम्हारि प्रभुताई। सहसबाहु सन परी लराई॥ समर बालि सन करि जसु पावा। सुनि कपि बचन बिहसि बिहरावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4267.verse_hindi: मैं तुम्हारी प्रभुता को खूब जानता हूँ सहस्रबाहु से तुम्हारी लड़ाई हुई थी और बालि से युद्ध करके तुमने यश प्राप्त किया था। हनुमान् जी के (मार्मिक) वचन सुनकर रावण ने हँसकर बात टाल दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4267.english_translation: I know your power well. You fought Sahasrabahu and won fame by battling Bali. Hearing the monkey's words, Ravana laughed and brushed them aside.
ramacharitamanas::4267.translation_literal: जानउँ (I know) / मैं (I) / तुम्हारि (your) / प्रभुताई (power, lordship) / सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / सन (with) / परी (occurred) / लराई (battle) / समर (war) / बालि (Bali) / सन (with) / करि (having done) / जसु (fame) / पावा (obtained) / सुनि (hearing) / कपि (monkey) / बचन (words) / बिहसि (laughing) / बिहरावा (dismissed, brushed aside)
ramacharitamanas::4267.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4267.essence: Knowing the truth means nothing if pride refuses to bow.
ramacharitamanas::4267.simple_meaning: Ravana admits Hanuman knows Ram's strength, but he laughs it off and refuses to take the warning seriously.
ramacharitamanas::4267.simple_insight: Pride can hear the truth and still refuse to change.
ramacharitamanas::4267.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just hinted at Ram's might by naming the enemies Ram has already defeated. Ravana understands the warning perfectly, but his ego cannot absorb it. He laughs instead of listening, and that dismissal pushes the scene toward confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::4267.modern_relevance: Someone warns you plainly that your shortcut will backfire, and you smile because you think you're untouchable. Ravana is that moment before the fall.
ramacharitamanas::4267.insight: It shows how ego turns clear warning into entertainment instead of action.

ramacharitamanas::4268.verse_sanskrit: खायउँ फल प्रभु लागी भूँखा। कपि सुभाव तें तोरेउँ रूखा॥ सब कें देह परम प्रिय स्वामी। मारहिं मोहि कुमारग गामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4268.verse_hindi: हे (राक्षसों के) स्वामी मुझे भूख लगी थी, (इसलिए) मैंने फल खाए और वानर स्वभाव के कारण वृक्ष तोड़े। हे (निशाचरों के) मालिक! देह सबको परम प्रिय है। कुमार्ग पर चलने वाले (दुष्ट) राक्षस जब मुझे मारने लगे॥2
ramacharitamanas::4268.english_translation: I ate fruit because I was hungry, Lord, and I broke trees by my monkey nature. Dear master of the night-roamers, everyone loves their own body; when the ones who walk the wrong path began to strike me...
ramacharitamanas::4268.translation_literal: खायउँ (I ate) / फल (fruit) / प्रभु (Lord) / लागी (because of) / भूँखा (hunger) / कपि (monkey) / सुभाव (nature) / तें (from) / तोरेउँ (I broke) / रूखा (trees) / सब (everyone) / कें (of) / देह (body) / परम (very) / प्रिय (dear) / स्वामी (master) / मारहिं (strike) / मोहि (me) / कुमारग (wrong path) / गामी (one who walks) /
ramacharitamanas::4268.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4268.essence: You can speak plainly without losing your calm.
ramacharitamanas::4268.simple_meaning: Hanuman explains that he ate fruit because he was hungry and broke trees because of his monkey nature. He reminds the listener that every being loves its own body, even when acting harshly.
ramacharitamanas::4268.simple_insight: Even in conflict, he speaks without pride and with a calm understanding of why fear makes others strike.
ramacharitamanas::4268.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been caught after searching for Sita. Before Ravana's court, he defends his actions without anger: he was hungry, he acted like a monkey, and the guards attacked him first. He then points to a deeper truth about fear and self-protection.
ramacharitamanas::4268.modern_relevance: You get snapped at in a tense meeting after speaking bluntly. Instead of escalating, you can name what happened plainly, without ego, and see the fear underneath the reaction.
ramacharitamanas::4268.insight: It teaches you to answer accusation with clarity, not defensiveness, and to recognise how self-protection drives harsh behaviour.

ramacharitamanas::4269.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह मोहि मारा ते मैं मारे। तेहि पर बाँधेउँ तनयँ तुम्हारे॥ मोहि न कछु बाँधे कइ लाजा। कीन्ह चहउँ निज प्रभु कर काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4269.verse_hindi: तब जिन्होंने मुझे मारा, उनको मैंने भी मारा। उस पर तुम्हारे पुत्र ने मुझको बाँध लिया (किंतु), मुझे अपने बाँधे जाने की कुछ भी लज्जा नहीं है। मैं तो अपने प्रभु का कार्य करना चाहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4269.english_translation: Those who struck me, I struck back. Then your son bound me, but I feel no shame in being bound. I only wanted to do my Lord's work.
ramacharitamanas::4269.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / मोहि (me) / मारा (struck) / ते (those) / मैं (I) / मारे (struck back) / तेहि पर (then upon that) / बाँधेउँ (bound) / तनयँ (son) / तुम्हारे (your) / मोहि (me) / न (not) / कछु (any) / बाँधे (being bound) / कइ (of) / लाजा (shame) / कीन्ह (did) / चहउँ (I want) / निज (my own) / प्रभु (Lord) / कर (of) / काजा (work)
ramacharitamanas::4269.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4269.essence: Service makes even humiliation feel small.
ramacharitamanas::4269.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he fought back when attacked, was then bound by Ravan's son, and felt no shame because he only wanted to serve Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4269.simple_insight: When your purpose is clear, even humiliation loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::4269.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been captured after deliberately allowing himself to be bound. He speaks calmly to Ravana's side, turning his restraint into a sign of strength. His only concern is doing Ram's work, not protecting his pride.
ramacharitamanas::4269.modern_relevance: You get blamed in a meeting for something you did not start, and your first impulse is to defend your ego. This verse reminds you that dignity can stay intact when your purpose is bigger than embarrassment.
ramacharitamanas::4269.insight: It shifts attention from protecting your image to serving your calling.

ramacharitamanas::4270.verse_sanskrit: बिनती करउँ जोरि कर रावन। सुनहु मान तजि मोर सिखावन॥ देखहु तुम्ह निज कुलहि बिचारी। भ्रम तजि भजहु भगत भय हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4270.verse_hindi: हे रावण! मैं हाथ जोड़कर तुमसे विनती करता हूँ, तुम अभिमान छोड़कर मेरी सीख सुनो। तुम अपने पवित्र कुल का विचार करके देखो और भ्रम को छोड़कर भक्त भयहारी भगवान् को भजो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4270.english_translation: I beg you with folded hands, Ravana. Listen to my teaching and drop your pride. Look at your own noble lineage, cast off confusion, and worship the one who removes fear from devotees.
ramacharitamanas::4270.translation_literal: बिनती (request) / करउँ (I make) / जोरि कर (joining hands) / रावन (Ravana) / सुनहु (listen) / मान (pride) / तजि (leaving) / मोर (my) / सिखावन (teaching) / देखहु (look) / तुम्ह (you) / निज (own) / कुलहि (lineage) / बिचारी (considering) / भ्रम (confusion) / तजि (leaving) / भजहु (worship) / भगत (devotees) / भय हारी (fear-removing one)
ramacharitamanas::4270.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4270.essence: Pride blinds you to the very refuge that can free you.
ramacharitamanas::4270.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Ravana to stop being arrogant, think about his lineage, clear his confusion, and turn toward Ram, who frees devotees from fear.
ramacharitamanas::4270.simple_insight: Pride narrows vision; humility makes room for the right turning.
ramacharitamanas::4270.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already faced Ravana's force and survived being bound. Now he speaks directly to the king who refuses to see clearly. This is not flattery; it is a final warning to drop ego before ruin deepens.
ramacharitamanas::4270.modern_relevance: You're arguing with someone who refuses every warning, even as their choices keep hurting them. Sometimes the kindest thing is to name the pride underneath the mess.
ramacharitamanas::4270.insight: It teaches you to speak truth plainly to ego, and to choose clear seeing over self-protection.

ramacharitamanas::4271.verse_sanskrit: जाकें डर अति काल डेराई। जो सुर असुर चराचर खाई॥ तासों बयरु कबहुँ नहिं कीजै। मोरे कहें जानकी दीजै ॥
ramacharitamanas::4271.verse_hindi: जो देवता, राक्षस और समस्त चराचर को खा जाता है, वह काल भी जिनके डर से अत्यंत डरता है, उनसे कदापि वैर न करो और मेरे कहने से जानकीजी को दे दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4271.english_translation: Do not make enmity with the one whom even Time fears deeply, who devours gods, demons, and all moving and unmoving beings. In my words, give Sita back.
ramacharitamanas::4271.translation_literal: जाकें (to whom) / डर (fear) / अति (greatly) / काल (Time) / डेराई (is afraid) / जो (who) / सुर (radiant beings) / असुर (beings of ego and shadow) / चराचर (moving and unmoving beings) / खाई (devours) / तासों (with that one) / बयरु (enmity) / कबहुँ (ever) / नहिं (not) / कीजै (make) / मोरे (my) / कहें (by saying) / जानकी (Sita) / दीजै (give back)
ramacharitamanas::4271.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4271.essence: Even the strongest pride must yield before the one Time fears.
ramacharitamanas::4271.simple_meaning: Hanuman warns Ravana not to oppose Ram, whose power exceeds even Time itself, and tells him to return Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4271.simple_insight: Real strength is knowing when resistance is hopeless and surrender is wiser.
ramacharitamanas::4271.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already exposed Ravana's weakness and is still urging him to turn back. He describes Ram as the one even Time fears, then makes the central demand of the mission: return Sita before ruin becomes certain.
ramacharitamanas::4271.modern_relevance: You keep arguing with a situation that has already outgrown your control. A wiser voice says: stop the fight, face reality, and return what should never have been taken.
ramacharitamanas::4271.insight: It shifts you from prideful resistance to clear-eyed surrender before damage deepens.

ramacharitamanas::4272.verse_sanskrit: प्रनतपाल रघुनायक करुना सिंधु खरारि। गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4272.verse_hindi: खर के शत्रु श्री रघुनाथजी शरणागतों के रक्षक और दया के समुद्र हैं। शरण जाने पर प्रभु तुम्हारा अपराध भुलाकर तुम्हें अपनी शरण में रख लेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4272.english_translation: Raghu's lord is the protector of those who seek refuge, an ocean of compassion. If you surrender, the Lord will forget your wrongdoing and keep you in his shelter.
ramacharitamanas::4272.translation_literal: प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / रघुनायक (lord of Raghu) / करुना सिंधु (ocean of compassion) / खरारि (enemy of Khara) / गएँ (having gone) / सरन (to refuge) / प्रभु (the Lord) / राखिहैं (will keep) / तव (your) / अपराध (wrongdoing) / बिसारि (forgetting)
ramacharitamanas::4272.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4272.essence: Surrender to Ram, and even your past can be released.
ramacharitamanas::4272.simple_meaning: Ram protects anyone who comes to him in surrender. He does not cling to your past mistakes; he receives you fully.
ramacharitamanas::4272.simple_insight: There is relief in being met by mercy instead of judgment.
ramacharitamanas::4272.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman speaks to Ravana after warning him to abandon pride and return Sita. He says Ram is the protector of those who seek refuge, and that surrender can erase the weight of wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::4272.modern_relevance: You finally admit you were wrong in a message you’ve delayed for days. The fear says you’ve ruined everything; this verse says a sincere return can still be received.
ramacharitamanas::4272.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to surrender, trusting that honest return matters more than past error.

ramacharitamanas::4273.verse_sanskrit: राम चरन पंकज उर धरहू। लंका अचल राजु तुम्ह करहू॥ रिषि पुलस्ति जसु बिमल मयंका। तेहि ससि महुँ जनि होहु कलंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4273.verse_hindi: तुम श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों को हृदय में धारण करो और लंका का अचल राज्य करो। ऋषि पुलस्त्यजी का यश निर्मल चंद्रमा के समान है। उस चंद्रमा में तुम कलंक न बनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4273.english_translation: Keep Ram's lotus feet in your heart, and rule Lanka firmly. Sage Pulastya's fame is like a spotless moon; do not become a stain upon that moon.
ramacharitamanas::4273.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / उर (heart) / धरहू (keep) / लंका (Lanka) / अचल (firm, unshaken) / राजु (rule, kingdom) / तुम्ह (you) / करहू (do) / रिषि (sage) / पुलस्ति (Pulastya) / जसु (fame) / बिमल (pure) / मयंका (moon) / तेहि (that) / ससि (moon) / महुँ (in) / जनि (do not) / होहु (become) / कलंका (stain)
ramacharitamanas::4273.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4273.essence: Power remains noble only when it bows to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4273.simple_meaning: Ravana is told to keep Ram in his heart, rule Lanka steadily, and never stain the pure fame of his lineage.
ramacharitamanas::4273.simple_insight: Real strength stays clean when it bows to something higher than ego.
ramacharitamanas::4273.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman speaks to Ravana with fearless compassion. He offers the path of safety: place Ram at the center, keep your kingdom steady, and do not tarnish the honor of Pulastya's noble line.
ramacharitamanas::4273.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, but everyone is watching how you use it. Power feels bigger when it stays humble, and smaller when ego starts writing the script.
ramacharitamanas::4273.insight: It shifts ambition from self-display to reverence and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::4274.verse_sanskrit: राम नाम बिनु गिरा न सोहा। देखु बिचारि त्यागि मद मोहा॥ बसन हीन नहिं सोह सुरारी। सब भूषन भूषित बर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4274.verse_hindi: राम नाम के बिना वाणी शोभा नहीं पाती, मद-मोह को छोड़, विचारकर देखो। हे देवताओं के शत्रु! सब गहनों से सजी हुई सुंदरी स्त्री भी कपड़ों के बिना (नंगी) शोभा नहीं पाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4274.english_translation: Without Ram's name, speech has no beauty. See clearly, and let go of pride and delusion. A woman without clothes is not graceful, even if she is adorned with every ornament.
ramacharitamanas::4274.translation_literal: राम नाम (Ram's name) / बिनु (without) / गिरा (speech) / न (not) / सोहा (looks beautiful) / देखु (see) / बिचारि (after considering) / त्यागि (leaving behind) / मद (pride) / मोहा (delusion) / बसन (clothes) / हीन (without) / नहिं (not) / सोह (looks graceful) / सुरारी (enemy of the gods) / सब (all) / भूषन (ornaments) / भूषित (adorned) / बर (fine, beautiful) / नारी (woman)
ramacharitamanas::4274.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4274.essence: Speech only becomes graceful when pride gives way to Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::4274.simple_meaning: Speech becomes truly beautiful only when it carries Ram's name. Pride and delusion strip away real grace, no matter how polished things look on the outside.
ramacharitamanas::4274.simple_insight: What you say matters less than the presence behind it.
ramacharitamanas::4274.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is speaking in Lanka, urging a proud heart to turn toward Ram. He says that even the most decorated appearance or the cleverest speech lacks real beauty without devotion and clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::4274.modern_relevance: You can sound polished in a meeting, but if your words are inflated by ego, people feel it immediately. The same sentence lands differently when it comes from humility and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4274.insight: It shifts attention from performance to the quality of heart behind speech.

ramacharitamanas::4275.verse_sanskrit: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4275.verse_hindi: रामविमुख पुरुष की संपत्ति और प्रभुता रही हुई भी चली जाती है और उसका पाना न पाने के समान है। जिन नदियों के मूल में कोई जलस्रोत नहीं है। (अर्थात् जिन्हें केवल बरसात ही आसरा है) वे वर्षा बीत जाने पर फिर तुरंत ही सूख जाती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4275.english_translation: A person turned away from Ram may keep wealth and power for a while, but they slip away. Like rivers with no source, they dry up as soon as the rains end.
ramacharitamanas::4275.translation_literal: राम बिमुख (turned away from Ram) / संपति (wealth) / प्रभुताई (power, authority) / जाइ रही (keeps going away) / पाई बिनु पाई (having it is like not having it at all) ॥ / सजल (with water) / मूल (source) / जिन्ह (whose) / सरितन्ह (rivers) / नाहीं (not) ॥ / बरषि गएँ (when the rains have passed) / पुनि (again) / तबहिं (then) / सुखाहीं (dry up) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4275.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4275.essence: What is cut off from Ram cannot endure, no matter how grand it looks.
ramacharitamanas::4275.simple_meaning: Wealth and authority do not truly stay with someone who turns away from Ram. They may seem present, but they fade quickly like rivers that have no real source.
ramacharitamanas::4275.simple_insight: What looks secure can vanish fast when it is not rooted in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4275.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is speaking in Lanka and warning Ravana. The message is blunt: power, wealth, and status cannot protect someone cut off from Ram. Anything without a true source collapses as soon as conditions change.
ramacharitamanas::4275.modern_relevance: You finally get the title, the money, the praise — and still feel one bad week away from losing it all. Anything built without a deeper center can disappear overnight.
ramacharitamanas::4275.insight: It shifts attention from holding status to finding what actually sustains it.

ramacharitamanas::4276.verse_sanskrit: सुनु दसकंठ कहउँ पन रोपी। बिमुख राम त्राता नहिं कोपी॥ संकर सहस बिष्नु अज तोही। सकहिं न राखि राम कर द्रोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4276.verse_hindi: हे रावण! सुनो, मैं प्रतिज्ञा करके कहता हूँ कि रामविमुख की रक्षा करने वाला कोई भी नहीं है। हजारों शंकर, विष्णु और ब्रह्मा भी श्री रामजी के साथ द्रोह करने वाले तुमको नहीं बचा सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4276.english_translation: O ten-headed one, listen: I swear that no protector can save one who turns away from Ram. Even thousands of Shankar, Vishnu, and Brahma cannot save you if you oppose Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4276.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / दसकंठ (ten-necked one; Ravana) / कहउँ (I say) / पन (vow) / रोपी (having planted; firmly sworn) / बिमुख (turned away) / राम (Ram) / त्राता (protector) / नहिं (not) / कोपी (anyone) / संकर (Shankar/Shiva) / सहस (thousands) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / अज (Brahma) / तोही (you) / सकहिं (are able) / न (not) / राखि (to save) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / द्रोही (enemy; one who opposes)
ramacharitamanas::4276.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4276.essence: Opposing Ram leaves you beyond every other shelter.
ramacharitamanas::4276.simple_meaning: Hanuman warns Ravana that anyone who turns away from Ram loses all protection. Even the greatest forces cannot save someone who opposes Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4276.simple_insight: There is relief in choosing the side that truly holds you.
ramacharitamanas::4276.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman faces Ravana after finding Sita. He stops speaking as a messenger and speaks as a warning: Ram's protection is real, and no amount of power can shield someone who stands against him.
ramacharitamanas::4276.modern_relevance: You keep doubling down on a choice that is clearly breaking trust, then hope status or connections will cover it. This verse says they won't.
ramacharitamanas::4276.insight: It shifts the mind from relying on external protection to aligning with what is right.

ramacharitamanas::4277.verse_sanskrit: मोहमूल बहु सूल प्रद त्यागहु तम अभिमान। भजहु राम रघुनायक कृपा सिंधु भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4277.verse_hindi: मोह ही जिनका मूल है ऐसे (अज्ञानजनित), बहुत पीड़ा देने वाले, तमरूप अभिमान का त्याग कर दो और रघुकुल के स्वामी, कृपा के समुद्र भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी का भजन करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4277.english_translation: Give up the dark pride born of delusion, which brings many pains. Worship Ram, the lord of Raghu, the ocean of grace.
ramacharitamanas::4277.translation_literal: मोह-मूल (rooted in delusion) / बहु (many) / सूल (pains) / प्रद (giving) / त्यागहु (give up) / तम (darkness) / अभिमान (pride) / भजहु (worship) / राम (Ram) / रघुनायक (lord of Raghu) / कृपा-सिंधु (ocean of grace) / भगवान (the divine lord)
ramacharitamanas::4277.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4277.essence: Pride rooted in confusion only hurts; devotion to Ram heals it.
ramacharitamanas::4277.simple_meaning: Pride born from confusion only brings suffering. Let it go and turn toward Ram with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4277.simple_insight: You do not need to defend the ego that is hurting you.
ramacharitamanas::4277.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka and speaks to Ravana with fearless kindness. He cuts straight to the heart of the problem: deluded pride is the source of suffering, and the cure is devotion to Ram, who gives grace freely.
ramacharitamanas::4277.modern_relevance: You replay a harsh text message for hours, building a story around being disrespected. That tightening in the chest is pride doing its work; the release begins when you stop feeding it.
ramacharitamanas::4277.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to humble remembrance of Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4278.verse_sanskrit: जदपि कही कपि अति हित बानी। भगति बिबेक बिरति नय सानी॥ बोला बिहसि महा अभिमानी। मिला हमहि कपि गुर बड़ ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4278.verse_hindi: यद्यपि हनुमान् जी ने भक्ति, ज्ञान, वैराग्य और नीति से सनी हुई बहुत ही हित की वाणी कही, तो भी वह महान् अभिमानी रावण बहुत हँसकर (व्यंग्य से) बोला कि हमें यह बंदर बड़ा ज्ञानी गुरु मिला! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4278.english_translation: Although Hanuman spoke words of great benefit, filled with devotion, discernment, detachment, and wise conduct, the great arrogant Ravana laughed and said, 'We have met a monkey guru, a great scholar!'
ramacharitamanas::4278.translation_literal: जदपि (although) कही (said) कपि (the monkey) अति (very) हित (beneficial) बानी (speech) / भगति (devotion) बिबेक (discernment) बिरति (detachment) नय (conduct) सानी (mixed with) ॥ / बोला (spoke) बिहसि (laughing) महा (great) अभिमानी (arrogant one) / मिला (met) हमहि (to us) कपि (monkey) गुर (teacher) बड़ (great) ग्यानी (knowledgeable) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4278.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4278.essence: Arrogance hears wisdom as an insult and misses its own rescue.
ramacharitamanas::4278.simple_meaning: Hanuman gives Ravana a wise, helpful warning, but Ravana laughs it off because his ego cannot receive advice.
ramacharitamanas::4278.simple_insight: It stings to see how pride can make someone reject the very guidance that could save them.
ramacharitamanas::4278.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already spoken with care, mixing devotion, clear seeing, restraint, and right conduct. But Ravana, swollen with ego, does not hear wisdom. He laughs instead, turning a warning into an insult.
ramacharitamanas::4278.modern_relevance: You finally tell a friend the hard truth they asked for, and they smirk like you’re the problem. That moment is Ravana’s blindness in modern clothes.
ramacharitamanas::4278.insight: It shows how ego filters out correction, turning counsel into comedy before it can do any work.

ramacharitamanas::4279.verse_sanskrit: मृत्यु निकट आई खल तोही। लागेसि अधम सिखावन मोही॥ उलटा होइहि कह हनुमाना। मतिभ्रम तोर प्रगट मैं जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4279.verse_hindi: रे दुष्ट! तेरी मृत्यु निकट आ गई है। अधम! मुझे शिक्षा देने चला है। हनुमान् जी ने कहा- इससे उलटा ही होगा (अर्थात् मृत्यु तेरी निकट आई है, मेरी नहीं)। यह तेरा मतिभ्रम (बुद्धि का फेर) है, मैंने प्रत्यक्ष जान लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4279.english_translation: “Your death is near, wicked one. You try to teach me, lowly one? Hanuman replied, “The opposite will happen. I see clearly that your mind is confused.”
ramacharitamanas::4279.translation_literal: मृत्यु (death) / निकट (near) / आई (has come) / खल (wicked one) / तोही (to you) / लागेसि (you seem) / अधम (lowly one) / सिखावन (to teach) / मोही (me)॥ / उलटा (opposite) / होइहि (will happen) / कहि (said) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / मतिभ्रम (confusion of mind) / तोर (your) / प्रगट (clearly) / मैं (I) / जाना (have known)॥
ramacharitamanas::4279.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4279.essence: Ego mistakes itself for wisdom until clear seeing names the confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4279.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that death is coming for him, not for Hanuman. Ravana’s attempt to lecture him only reveals Ravana’s own confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4279.simple_insight: Clear seeing stays steady even when arrogance gets loud.
ramacharitamanas::4279.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already spoken with courage and wisdom. Ravana answers with pride, but Hanuman cuts through it at once: the one trying to instruct others is the one who is confused. This is the moment Hanuman exposes ego as self-blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4279.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting keeps talking over everyone, certain they understand the situation better than anyone else. You can feel the gap between volume and clarity. Hanuman shows how to name that gap without losing your center.
ramacharitamanas::4279.insight: It teaches you to recognize when confidence is actually confusion, and to answer from clear seeing instead of intimidation.

ramacharitamanas::4280.verse_sanskrit: सुनि कपि बचन बहुत खिसिआना। बेगि न हरहु मूढ़ कर प्राना॥ सुनत निसाचर मारन धाए। सचिवन्ह सहित बिभीषनु आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4280.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर वह बहुत ही कुपित हो गया। (और बोला-) अरे! इस मूर्ख का प्राण शीघ्र ही क्यों नहीं हर लेते? सुनते ही राक्षस उन्हें मारने दौड़े उसी समय मंत्रियों के साथ विभीषणजी वहाँ आ पहुँचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4280.english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's words, Ravana grew very angry and said, "Why not quickly take this fool's life?" As the demons rushed to kill him, Vibhishana arrived with the ministers.
ramacharitamanas::4280.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / कपि (monkey) / बचन (words) / बहुत (very much) / खिसिआना (angered) / बेगि (quickly) / न (not) / हरहु (take away) / मूढ़ (foolish) / कर (of) / प्राना (life)॥ / सुनत (on hearing) / निसाचर (demons) / मारन (to kill) / धाए (rushed) / सचिवन्ह (with ministers) / सहित (along with) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / आए (came)॥
ramacharitamanas::4280.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4280.essence: Pride wants instant punishment; dharma arrives with restraint.
ramacharitamanas::4280.simple_meaning: Ravana loses his temper at Hanuman's words and orders him killed. The demons rush in, and Vibhishana arrives with the ministers.
ramacharitamanas::4280.simple_insight: Pride reacts first; wisdom comes too late to stop the damage.
ramacharitamanas::4280.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just spoken boldly to Ravana. The insult stings Ravana's pride, and he immediately orders Hanuman killed. Before the attack lands, Vibhishana enters with the ministers, setting up the next clash over right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::4280.modern_relevance: A harsh message lands in a group chat, and someone instantly wants to punish the sender. The room fills with heat before anyone asks what is actually right.
ramacharitamanas::4280.insight: It shows how ego rushes toward retaliation, while a steadier voice arrives to check it.

ramacharitamanas::4281.verse_sanskrit: नाइ सीस करि बिनय बहूता। नीति बिरोध न मारिअ दूता॥ आन दंड कछु करिअ गोसाँई। सबहीं कहा मंत्र भल भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4281.verse_hindi: उन्होंने सिर नवाकर और बहुत विनय करके रावण से कहा कि दूत को मारना नहीं चाहिए, यह नीति के विरुद्ध है। हे गोसाईं। कोई दूसरा दंड दिया जाए। सबने कहा- भाई! यह सलाह उत्तम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4281.english_translation: They bowed their heads and spoke with great humility: killing a messenger goes against righteous conduct. My lord, give some other punishment. Everyone said, “Brother, that advice is good.”
ramacharitamanas::4281.translation_literal: नाइ (bowing) / सीस (head) / करि (doing) / बिनय (humility) / बहूता (much) / नीति (righteous conduct) / बिरोध (against) / न मारिअ (should not be killed) / दूता (messenger) / आन (other) / दंड (punishment) / कछु (some) / करिअ (should be done) / गोसाँई (lord) / सबहीं (everyone) / कहा (said) / मंत्र (advice) / भल (good) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::4281.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4281.essence: Even an enemy must be answered within the limits of conduct.
ramacharitamanas::4281.simple_meaning: A messenger should not be killed. Even in anger, there should be some other punishment instead.
ramacharitamanas::4281.simple_insight: Power still has a moral limit. Even when you are offended, how you respond matters.
ramacharitamanas::4281.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been captured and brought before Ravana. Before the king answers, the courtiers advise restraint: a messenger should not be killed, because even enemies have rules. This verse slows the scene and shows the court trying to preserve order before Ravana breaks it.
ramacharitamanas::4281.modern_relevance: A furious email lands in your inbox, and your first impulse is to destroy the person who sent it. This verse reminds you that even anger needs boundaries.
ramacharitamanas::4281.insight: It shifts the mind from revenge to proportion, asking for a response that still respects conduct.

ramacharitamanas::4282.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बिहसि बोला दसकंधर। अंग भंग करि पठइअ बंदर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4282.verse_hindi: यह सुनते ही रावण हँसकर बोला- अच्छा तो, बंदर को अंग-भंग करके भेज (लौटा) दिया जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4282.english_translation: Hearing this, the ten-headed Ravana laughed and said, "Maim the monkey and send him back."
ramacharitamanas::4282.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बिहसि (laughing) / बोला (spoke) / दसकंधर (the ten-headed one) / अंग (limbs) / भंग (breaking, maiming) / करि (doing) / पठइअ (send back) / बंदर (monkey)
ramacharitamanas::4282.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4282.essence: Mockery can be the first step toward self-destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4282.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman and orders that the monkey be mutilated and sent back.
ramacharitamanas::4282.simple_insight: Pride turns warning into ridicule, and ridicule into cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::4282.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just spoken boldly before Ravana's court. The ministers plead for restraint, but Ravana laughs off their advice and orders the monkey punished. The scene turns from tense negotiation to humiliation and violence.
ramacharitamanas::4282.modern_relevance: A boss laughs off a serious warning in a meeting, then doubles down just to save face. That reflex can turn a small problem into a bigger one.
ramacharitamanas::4282.insight: It shows how ego blocks wise counsel and escalates conflict.

ramacharitamanas::4283.verse_sanskrit: कपि कें ममता पूँछ पर सबहि कहउँ समुझाइ। तेल बोरि पट बाँधि पुनि पावक देहु लगाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4283.verse_hindi: मैं सबको समझाकर कहता हूँ कि बंदर की ममता पूँछ पर होती है। अतः तेल में कपड़ा डुबोकर उसे इसकी पूँछ में बाँधकर फिर आग लगा दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4283.english_translation: I tell everyone after making them understand: a monkey's attachment is to its tail. So soak cloth in oil, tie it to the tail, and then set it on fire.
ramacharitamanas::4283.translation_literal: कपि (monkey) / कें (of) / ममता (attachment) / पूँछ (tail) / पर (on) / सबहि (everyone) / कहउँ (I say) / समुझाइ (explaining) / तेल (oil) / बोरि (soak) / पट (cloth) / बाँधि (tying) / पुनि (then) / पावक (fire) / देहु (give) / लगाइ (apply)
ramacharitamanas::4283.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4283.essence: Pride tries to shame what it cannot control.
ramacharitamanas::4283.simple_meaning: Ravana orders Hanuman's tail to be soaked in oil, wrapped in cloth, and set on fire.
ramacharitamanas::4283.simple_insight: Pride turns cruelty into a joke until it becomes its own undoing.
ramacharitamanas::4283.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been caught but still speaks with fearless dignity. Ravana laughs at the advice around him and orders the monkey's tail to be burned, thinking humiliation will restore his power. The scene sets up the punishment that will become his disaster.
ramacharitamanas::4283.modern_relevance: A manager mocks the person who exposed a mistake and tries to make an example of them. The humiliation feels powerful for a moment, but it often plants the seed of a bigger collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4283.insight: It shows how ego reacts to challenge with humiliation instead of wisdom, creating the very consequence it wants to avoid.

ramacharitamanas::4284.verse_sanskrit: पूँछहीन बानर तहँ जाइहि। तब सठ निज नाथहि लइ आइहि॥ जिन्ह कै कीन्हिसि बहुत बड़ाई। देखउ मैं तिन्ह कै प्रभुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4284.verse_hindi: जब बिना पूँछ का यह बंदर वहाँ (अपने स्वामी के पास) जाएगा, तब यह मूर्ख अपने मालिक को साथ ले आएगा। जिनकी इसने बहुत बड़ाई की है, मैं जरा उनकी प्रभुता (सामर्थ्य) तो देखूँ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4284.english_translation: When this tailless monkey goes there, that fool will bring his master along. Let me see the power of those he has praised so much.
ramacharitamanas::4284.translation_literal: पूँछहीन (without a tail) / बानर (monkey) / तहँ (there) / जाइहि (will go) / तब (then) / सठ (fool) / निज (own) / नाथहि (master) / लइ (taking) / आइहि (will come) / जिन्ह (those who) / कै (of) / कीन्हिसि (has done) / बहुत (much) / बड़ाई (praise) / देखउ (let me see) / मैं (I) / तिन्ह (their) / कै (of) / प्रभुताई (power, lordship)
ramacharitamanas::4284.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4284.essence: Pride laughs first, then discovers what it feared.
ramacharitamanas::4284.simple_meaning: Ravana thinks Hanuman will return to Ram and prove Ram's power. He mocks the monkey while secretly challenging the strength of Ram and his devotees.
ramacharitamanas::4284.simple_insight: Pride often turns its own fear into mockery.
ramacharitamanas::4284.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just ordered Hanuman's tail to be burned. He imagines that a tailless monkey will run back to its master and expose the strength of the one Hanuman praised. His insult reveals both arrogance and unease.
ramacharitamanas::4284.modern_relevance: You dismiss someone’s warning at the meeting, then spend the next hour trying to prove they were wrong. Pride can make fear sound like confidence.
ramacharitamanas::4284.insight: It shows how ego misreads devotion as weakness and treats a challenge as a joke.

ramacharitamanas::4285.verse_sanskrit: बचन सुनत कपि मन मुसुकाना। भइ सहाय सारद मैं जाना॥ जातुधान सुनि रावन बचना। लागे रचैं मूढ़ सोइ रचना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4285.verse_hindi: यह वचन सुनते ही हनुमान् जी मन में मुस्कुराए (और मन ही मन बोले कि) मैं जान गया, सरस्वतीजी (इसे ऐसी बुद्धि देने में) सहायक हुई हैं। रावण के वचन सुनकर मूर्ख राक्षस वही (पूँछ में आग लगाने की) तैयारी करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4285.english_translation: Hearing these words, Hanuman smiled inwardly, knowing that Saraswati had helped him. Hearing Ravana's words, the foolish demons set about making that very plan.
ramacharitamanas::4285.translation_literal: बचन (words) / सुनत (hearing) / कपि (the monkey devotee) / मन (mind) / मुसुकाना (smiled) / भइ (was) / सहाय (helper) / सारद (Saraswati) / मैं (I) / जाना (knew) / जातुधान (demons) / सुनि (hearing) / रावन (Ravana) / बचना (words) / लागे (began) / रचैं (to devise) / मूढ़ (foolish) / सोइ (that very) / रचना (plan)
ramacharitamanas::4285.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4285.essence: Clear seeing stays calm while foolishness rushes ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4285.simple_meaning: Hanuman realizes his own cleverness is being guided from beyond, while Ravana's followers blindly turn his words into action.
ramacharitamanas::4285.simple_insight: You can stay clear-headed even inside other people's foolish plans.
ramacharitamanas::4285.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already been cornered and his tail is about to be set on fire. He understands the trick at once and quietly sees a higher help at work, while Ravana's men, trapped in their own foolishness, rush to carry out the very scheme that will expose them.
ramacharitamanas::4285.modern_relevance: Someone tries to embarrass you in a meeting, and the whole room starts following their lead. You see the setup instantly, stay calm, and let their own move reveal their mistake.
ramacharitamanas::4285.insight: It shifts attention from reacting to recognizing the hidden stupidity in the situation.

ramacharitamanas::4286.verse_sanskrit: रहा न नगर बसन घृत तेला। बाढ़ी पूँछ कीन्ह कपि खेला॥ कौतुक कहँ आए पुरबासी। मारहिं चरन करहिं बहु हाँसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4286.verse_hindi: (पूँछ के लपेटने में इतना कपड़ा और घी-तेल लगा कि) नगर में कपड़ा, घी और तेल नहीं रह गया। हनुमान् जी ने ऐसा खेल किया कि पूँछ बढ़ गई (लंबी हो गई)। नगरवासी लोग तमाशा देखने आए। वे हनुमान् जी को पैर से ठोकर मारते हैं और उनकी हँसी करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4286.english_translation: So much cloth, ghee, and oil were used that the city ran short. Hanuman turned the whole thing into play, and his tail grew long. The townspeople came to watch for fun, then kicked him and mocked him.
ramacharitamanas::4286.translation_literal: रहा (remained) / न (not) / नगर (city) / बसन (cloth) / घृत (ghee) / तेला (oil) / बाढ़ी (grew) / पूँछ (tail) / कीन्ह (made) / कपि (monkey) / खेला (play)॥ / कौतुक (for sport) / कहँ (for) / आए (came) / पुरबासी (townspeople) / मारहिं (strike) / चरन (with feet) / करहिं (do) / बहु (much) / हाँसी (laughter) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4286.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4286.simple_meaning: The people of Lanka use up cloth, ghee, and oil to wrap Hanuman's tail, then come mockingly to watch him.
ramacharitamanas::4286.simple_insight: Pride can turn cruelty into its own spectacle.
ramacharitamanas::4286.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman is captured, the city turns his punishment into entertainment. Cloth, ghee, and oil are gathered to wrap his tail, and the townspeople crowd in to laugh and kick him. The scene sets up the fire that will change everything.
ramacharitamanas::4286.modern_relevance: A crowd gathers around someone already embarrassed, turning humiliation into a public event. What feels like a joke in the moment can become the very thing that exposes arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4286.insight: It shows how mob laughter can hide fear, and how humiliation often precedes a reversal of power.

ramacharitamanas::4287.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं ढोल देहिं सब तारी। नगर फेरि पुनि पूँछ प्रजारी॥ पावक जरत देखि हनुमंता। भयउ परम लघुरूप तुरंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4287.verse_hindi: ढोल बजते हैं, सब लोग तालियाँ पीटते हैं। हनुमान् जी को नगर में फिराकर, फिर पूँछ में आग लगा दी। अग्नि को जलते हुए देखकर हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही बहुत छोटे रूप में हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4287.english_translation: Drums beat and everyone claps. Hanuman is paraded through the city, then his tail is set on fire. Seeing the flame burn, Hanuman instantly takes a very small form.
ramacharitamanas::4287.translation_literal: बाजहिं (are beaten) / ढोल (drums) / देहिं (give) / सब (all) / तारी (claps) / नगर (city) / फेरि (having turned around) / पुनि (again) / पूँछ (tail) / प्रजारी (set on fire) / पावक (fire) / जरत (burning) / देखि (seeing) / हनुमंता (Hanuman) / भयउ (became) / परम (extremely) / लघुरूप (small form) / तुरंता (immediately)
ramacharitamanas::4287.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4287.essence: Humiliation does not control you when your response stays free.
ramacharitamanas::4287.simple_meaning: The city celebrates Hanuman's humiliation, then sets his tail on fire. Hanuman responds by shrinking instantly to a tiny form.
ramacharitamanas::4287.simple_insight: You do not need to meet force with force; calm awareness can change the whole situation.
ramacharitamanas::4287.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been captured and mocked. The crowd rejoices as he is marched around and his tail is lit. Instead of panic, he instantly changes size, preparing for what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::4287.modern_relevance: You are being laughed at in a room, and your body wants to flare up. Instead, you breathe, adjust, and respond with precision rather than ego.
ramacharitamanas::4287.insight: It shows how composure can turn humiliation into readiness.

ramacharitamanas::4288.verse_sanskrit: निबुकि चढ़ेउ कप कनक अटारीं। भईं सभीत निसाचर नारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4288.verse_hindi: बंधन से निकलकर वे सोने की अटारियों पर जा चढ़े। उनको देखकर राक्षसों की स्त्रियाँ भयभीत हो गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4288.english_translation: Free of restraint, he climbed the golden rooftops, and the demon women grew frightened at the sight.
ramacharitamanas::4288.translation_literal: निबुकि (free of restraint) / चढ़ेउ (climbed) / कप (monkey) / कनक (golden) / अटारीं (rooftops) / भईं (became) / सभीत (frightened) / निसाचर (demon) / नारीं (women)
ramacharitamanas::4288.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4288.essence: Fearless movement itself becomes a force.
ramacharitamanas::4288.simple_meaning: Hanuman breaks free and moves onto the golden rooftops. The women of Lanka are startled by his presence.
ramacharitamanas::4288.simple_insight: Some presence is so fearless that it unsettles an entire place.
ramacharitamanas::4288.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has already turned Lanka upside down in his fiery form. Now he breaks free, climbs the golden palaces, and his sudden movement frightens the women inside. The scene keeps building toward his leap into the sky.
