ramacharitamanas::4288.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after everyone has written you off, and the whole mood changes. Your calm movement can unsettle fear more than noise ever could.
ramacharitamanas::4288.insight: It shows how fearless action can shake a hostile environment without a single speech.

ramacharitamanas::4289.verse_sanskrit: हरि प्रेरित तेहि अवसर चले मरुत उनचास। अट्टहास करि गर्जा कपि बढ़ि लाग अकास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4289.verse_hindi: उस समय भगवान् की प्रेरणा से उनचासों पवन चलने लगे। हनुमान् जी अट्टहास करके गर्जे और बढ़कर आकाश से जा लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4289.english_translation: At that moment, moved by Ram's will, the forty-nine winds began to blow. Hanuman roared with a loud laugh and leapt up into the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4289.translation_literal: हरि (Ram) / प्रेरित (moved) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / चले (began to move) / मरुत (winds) / उनचास (forty-nine) / अट्टहास (loud laugh) / करि (doing) / गर्जा (roared) / कपि (monkey) / बढ़ि (rising) / लाग (went) / अकास (sky)
ramacharitamanas::4289.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4289.essence: When Ram moves you, even the sky becomes reachable.
ramacharitamanas::4289.simple_meaning: Ram's will sets the winds in motion, and Hanuman rises into the sky with a fearless roar.
ramacharitamanas::4289.simple_insight: When purpose is aligned, even the world seems to open for you.
ramacharitamanas::4289.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the burning of the city and the humiliation of the demons, Hanuman is no longer hiding. At the very moment Ram's power moves the winds, Hanuman laughs, roars, and launches himself upward, ready for the next leap.
ramacharitamanas::4289.modern_relevance: You finish the hard part, take one breath, and suddenly the next step feels possible. Confidence changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::4289.insight: It shifts attention from effort alone to the force that rises when you act in alignment.

ramacharitamanas::4290.verse_sanskrit: देह बिसाल परम हरुआई। मंदिर तें मंदिर चढ़ धाई॥ जरइ नगर भा लोग बिहाला। झपट लपट बहु कोटि कराला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4290.verse_hindi: देह बड़ी विशाल, परंतु बहुत ही हल्की (फुर्तीली) है। वे दौड़कर एक महल से दूसरे महल पर चढ़ जाते हैं। नगर जल रहा है लोग बेहाल हो गए हैं। आग की करोड़ों भयंकर लपटें झपट रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4290.english_translation: His body was huge yet wonderfully light. He leapt from palace to palace in an instant. The city burned, people were distressed, and countless fierce flames sprang up everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::4290.translation_literal: देह (body) / बिसाल (huge) / परम (extremely) / हरुआई (lightness) / मंदिर (palace) / तें (from) / मंदिर (palace) / चढ़ (climb) / धाई (rushing) / जरइ (is burning) / नगर (city) / भा (became) / लोग (people) / बिहाला (distressed) / झपट (snatching) / लपट (flame) / बहु (many) / कोटि (crores) / कराला (terrible)
ramacharitamanas::4290.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4290.essence: Great power can move with effortless speed.
ramacharitamanas::4290.simple_meaning: Hanuman’s huge body moved with astonishing lightness as he rushed across the burning city from roof to roof.
ramacharitamanas::4290.simple_insight: Even immense strength can move with complete ease when it is fully in service.
ramacharitamanas::4290.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already entered the city and begun his search. His enormous form moves with impossible speed from palace to palace while the city burns around him. This is a vivid action scene, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4290.insight: It shows unstoppable action: strength, speed, and purpose all working together without hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::4291.verse_sanskrit: तात मातु हा सुनिअ पुकारा। एहिं अवसर को हमहि उबारा॥ हम जो कहा यह कपि नहिं होई। बानर रूप धरें सुर कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4291.verse_hindi: हाय बप्पा! हाय मैया! इस अवसर पर हमें कौन बचाएगा? (चारों ओर) यही पुकार सुनाई पड़ रही है। हमने तो पहले ही कहा था कि यह वानर नहीं है, वानर का रूप धरे कोई देवता है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4291.english_translation: “Father! Mother! Who will save us now?” That cry is heard everywhere. “We said before that this is no monkey — it must be some radiant being in monkey form!”
ramacharitamanas::4291.translation_literal: तात (father) / मातु (mother) / हा (alas) / सुनिअ (is heard) / पुकारा (cry) / एहिं (this) / अवसर (occasion) / को (who) / हमहि (us) / उबारा (saved) / हम (we) / जो (what) / कहा (said) / यह (this) / कपि (monkey) / नहिं (not) / होई (is) / बानर (monkey) / रूप (form) / धरें (having taken) / सुर (radiant being) / कोई (someone)
ramacharitamanas::4291.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4291.essence: Pride breaks first when the truth arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4291.simple_meaning: The people of Lanka panic and call out for help as they realize Hanuman is no ordinary monkey.
ramacharitamanas::4291.simple_insight: Panic makes the mind confess what pride had denied.
ramacharitamanas::4291.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman’s blazing leap has turned the city into chaos. The frightened people cry for their parents and ask who can save them, while some finally admit this is no ordinary monkey. The verse marks the city’s fear and dawning recognition.
ramacharitamanas::4291.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the mistake becomes impossible to hide. The people who were certain a threat was harmless suddenly feel the full weight of what they ignored.
ramacharitamanas::4291.insight: It shows how arrogance collapses into fear when reality can no longer be denied.

ramacharitamanas::4292.verse_sanskrit: साधु अवग्या कर फलु ऐसा। जरइ नगर अनाथ कर जैसा॥ जारा नगरु निमिष एक माहीं। एक बिभीषन कर गृह नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4292.verse_hindi: साधु के अपमान का यह फल है कि नगर, अनाथ के नगर की तरह जल रहा है। हनुमान् जी ने एक ही क्षण में सारा नगर जला डाला। एक विभीषण का घर नहीं जलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4292.english_translation: The result of insulting a saint is like this: the city burns like a helpless town. In a single moment the whole city was set ablaze, yet not Vibhishana's house.
ramacharitamanas::4292.translation_literal: साधु (saint) / अवग्या (disrespect) / कर (of) / फलु (result) / ऐसा (like this) / जरइ (burns) / नगर (city) / अनाथ (helpless) / कर (as) / जैसा (like) / जारा (burned) / नगरु (the city) / निमिष (moment) / एक (one) / माहीं (within) / एक (one) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / कर (of) / गृह (house) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::4292.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4292.essence: Disrespect the noble, and ruin follows; honor remains protected.
ramacharitamanas::4292.simple_meaning: Disrespecting a holy person brings ruin. Lanka burns in a moment, but Vibhishana's home is spared.
ramacharitamanas::4292.simple_insight: How you treat the pure-hearted shapes whether you are protected or exposed.
ramacharitamanas::4292.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has entered Lanka in search of Sita. After being insulted and attacked, he sets the city on fire in one flash. Yet Vibhishana's house is untouched, showing that devotion and right conduct create safety even in chaos.
ramacharitamanas::4292.modern_relevance: You mock the one person in the room who stayed decent, and suddenly the whole group dynamic turns against you. Respect matters more than you think.
ramacharitamanas::4292.insight: It teaches you that contempt for the worthy invites destruction, while integrity can remain untouched in the middle of chaos.

ramacharitamanas::4293.verse_sanskrit: ताकर दूत अनल जेहिं सिरिजा। जरा न सो तेहि कारन गिरिजा॥ उलटि पलटि लंका सब जारी। कूदि परा पुनि सिंधु मझारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4293.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! जिन्होंने अग्नि को बनाया, हनुमान् जी उन्हीं के दूत हैं। इसी कारण वे अग्नि से नहीं जले। हनुमान् जी ने उलट-पलटकर (एक ओर से दूसरी ओर तक) सारी लंका जला दी। फिर वे समुद्र में कूद पड़े॥
ramacharitamanas::4293.english_translation: O Parvati, the one who created fire also sent Hanuman as his messenger. That is why fire could not burn him. Hanuman turned Lanka upside down and burned it all, then jumped back into the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4293.translation_literal: ताकर (his) / दूत (messenger) / अनल (fire) / जेहिं (who) / सिरिजा (created) / जरा (burned) / न (not) / सो (he) / तेहि (that) / कारन (because) / गिरिजा (O Parvati) / उलटि (turning over) / पलटि (flipping) / लंका (Lanka) / सब (all) / जारी (burned) / कूदि (leaping) / परा (fell/jumped) / पुनि (again) / सिंधु (sea) / मझारी (into the middle)
ramacharitamanas::4293.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4293.essence: The fire that should destroy him cannot touch the one sent by its maker.
ramacharitamanas::4293.simple_meaning: Hanuman is beyond fire because the creator of fire sent him. He burns Lanka completely, then returns by leaping into the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4293.simple_insight: When your mission is protected, even danger cannot stop you.
ramacharitamanas::4293.detailed_meaning: Shiva is explaining to Parvati how Hanuman's mission in Lanka unfolded. The fire that destroys the city cannot touch him, because he moves under a higher protection. This verse marks the moment of total destruction before his return to Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4293.modern_relevance: You walk into a situation everyone says will burn you out, but your purpose keeps you steady. What should have destroyed you becomes the very thing you pass through.
ramacharitamanas::4293.insight: It shows that true protection comes from the mission itself, not from external safety.

ramacharitamanas::4294.verse_sanskrit: पूँछ बुझाइ खोइ श्रम धरि लघु रूप बहोरि। जनकसुता कें आगें ठाढ़ भयउ कर जोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4294.verse_hindi: पूँछ बुझाकर, थकावट दूर करके और फिर छोटा सा रूप धारण कर हनुमान् जी श्री जानकीजी के सामने हाथ जोड़कर जा खड़े हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4294.english_translation: After putting out his tail, shaking off his fatigue, and taking a small form again, Hanuman stood before Janakasuta with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::4294.translation_literal: पूँछ (tail) / बुझाइ (having extinguished) / खोइ (removing) / श्रम (fatigue) / धरि (taking) / लघु (small) / रूप (form) / बहोरि (again) / जनकसुता (Janaka's daughter) / कें (before) / आगें (in front) / ठाढ़ (standing) / भयउ (became) / कर (hands) / जोरि (folded)
ramacharitamanas::4294.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4294.essence: Power becomes beautiful when it returns as humility.
ramacharitamanas::4294.simple_meaning: Hanuman cools his tail, recovers from exhaustion, shrinks again, and stands respectfully before Sita with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::4294.simple_insight: True devotion can move from fierce action to humble reverence in a breath.
ramacharitamanas::4294.detailed_meaning: After burning Lanka, Hanuman returns to Sita’s presence not as a conqueror but as a servant. He cools his tail, sheds fatigue, takes his small form again, and stands before Janaki with folded hands. The scene prepares for his message and Sita’s response.
ramacharitamanas::4294.modern_relevance: You finish the hard part, wipe the sweat from your face, and then walk back in humble enough to listen. Real strength knows when to bow.
ramacharitamanas::4294.insight: It shifts action into service: after achievement, the next move is respect, not display.

ramacharitamanas::4295.verse_sanskrit: मातु मोहि दीजे कछु चीन्हा। जैसें रघुनायक मोहि दीन्हा॥ चूड़ामनि उतारि तब दयऊ। हरष समेत पवनसुत लयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4295.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! मुझे कोई चिह्न (पहचान) दीजिए, जैसे श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुझे दिया था। तब सीताजी ने चूड़ामणि उतारकर दी। हनुमान् जी ने उसको हर्षपूर्वक ले लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4295.english_translation: “Mother, give me some token of recognition, just as Raghunath gave me.” Then Sita removed her jeweled hair ornament and gave it. Hanuman received it joyfully.
ramacharitamanas::4295.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / मोहि (to me) / दीजे (please give) / कछु (some) / चीन्हा (token of recognition) / जैसें (just as) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / मोहि (to me) / दीन्हा (gave)॥ / चूड़ामनि (jewel ornament) / उतारि (removing) / तब (then) / दयऊ (gave) / हरष (joy) / समेत (with) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / लयऊ (took)॥
ramacharitamanas::4295.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4295.essence: A true token carries the whole bond within it.
ramacharitamanas::4295.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Sita for a token from Ram, and she gives him her jeweled ornament. The exchange confirms their bond and sends him back with joy.
ramacharitamanas::4295.simple_insight: A small token can hold the strength of a whole relationship.
ramacharitamanas::4295.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita after crossing the ocean for Ram. Before leaving, he asks for a sign to carry back, just as Ram once gave him one. Sita removes her crown jewel and gives it gladly.
ramacharitamanas::4295.modern_relevance: You save a note, a photo, or a voice message because it carries someone’s presence across distance. A small thing can steady you more than a long speech.
ramacharitamanas::4295.insight: It teaches you to value symbols that keep love and trust alive across separation.

ramacharitamanas::4296.verse_sanskrit: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4296.verse_hindi: (जानकीजी ने कहा-) हे तात! मेरा प्रणाम निवेदन करना और इस प्रकार कहना- हे प्रभु! यद्यपि आप सब प्रकार से पूर्ण काम हैं (आपको किसी प्रकार की कामना नहीं है), तथापि दीनों (दुःखियों) पर दया करना आपका विरद है (और मैं दीन हूँ) अतः उस विरद को याद करके, हे नाथ! मेरे भारी संकट को दूर कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4296.english_translation: Tell him, dear one: offer my प्रणाम. Say that the Lord is complete in every way and has no want. Yet the Lord’s very vow is to protect the lowly; remembering that vow, O Master, remove my great suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4296.translation_literal: कहेहु (say) / तात (dear one) / अस (thus) / मोर (my) / प्रनामा (salutation) / सब प्रकार (in every way) / प्रभु (Lord) / पूरनकामा (fully fulfilled, without desire) / दीन दयाल (compassionate to the humble) / बिरिदु (vow, sacred custom) / संभारी (remembering) / हरहु (remove) / नाथ (Master) / सम संकट (great distress) / भारी (heavy)
ramacharitamanas::4296.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4296.essence: Needless strength becomes mercy when it remembers its own vow.
ramacharitamanas::4296.simple_meaning: Sita asks Hanuman to greet Ram respectfully and remind him that, although he needs nothing, his special nature is to protect the helpless. She begs him to end her suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4296.simple_insight: Even in distress, trust can speak with dignity and hope.
ramacharitamanas::4296.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just reached Sita in Ashoka Vatika and received her token. Now Sita sends him back to Ram with a message: she knows Ram is पूर्णकाम, beyond need, but she appeals to his vow of mercy. This is desperate longing shaped by trust.
ramacharitamanas::4296.modern_relevance: You text the one person who can help, even though they owe you nothing. You do not flatter them; you remind them of who they are and ask them to act from that.
ramacharitamanas::4296.insight: It teaches you to ask for help by appealing to character, not entitlement.

ramacharitamanas::4297.verse_sanskrit: तात सक्रसुत कथा सनाएहु। बान प्रताप प्रभुहि समुझाएहु॥ मास दिवस महुँ नाथु न आवा। तौ पुनि मोहि जिअत नहिं पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4297.verse_hindi: हे तात! इंद्रपुत्र जयंत की कथा (घटना) सुनाना और प्रभु को उनके बाण का प्रताप समझाना (स्मरण कराना)। यदि महीने भर में नाथ न आए तो फिर मुझे जीती न पाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4297.english_translation: Dear Hanuman, tell him the story of Jayanta, Indra's son, and remind him of the power of his arrow. If my Lord does not come within a month, he will never find me alive again.
ramacharitamanas::4297.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / सक्रसुत (Indra's son) / कथा (story) / सनाएहु (tell) / बान (arrow) / प्रताप (power, glory) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / समुझाएहु (make understand, remind) / मास (month) / दिवस (days) / महुँ (within) / नाथु (Lord) / न (not) / आवा (came) / तौ (then) / पुनि (again) / मोहि (me) / जिअत (alive) / नहिं (not) / पावा (will find)
ramacharitamanas::4297.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4297.essence: Faith waits, but it still asks for Ram to come soon.
ramacharitamanas::4297.simple_meaning: Sita asks Hanuman to tell Ram about Jayanta and his own arrow's power, then says that if Ram does not come within a month, she will not remain alive.
ramacharitamanas::4297.simple_insight: Love can endure absence, but it still longs for a return it can trust.
ramacharitamanas::4297.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has finally received Hanuman's message from Ram. Before he leaves, she asks him to carry one more plea: remind Ram of Jayanta and the power of his arrow. Her waiting is almost spent, and that urgency gives the verse its ache.
ramacharitamanas::4297.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a message that changed everything, then nothing follows. That quiet stretch of waiting is what Sita is living through: hope held together by memory and faith.
ramacharitamanas::4297.insight: It shifts longing into a clear request: carry the message, strengthen trust, and name the limit of waiting.

ramacharitamanas::4298.verse_sanskrit: कहु कपि केहि बिधि राखौं प्राना। तुम्हहू तात कहत अब जाना॥ तोहि देखि सीतलि भइ छाती। पुनि मो कहुँ सोइ दिनु सो राती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4298.verse_hindi: हे हनुमान् ! कहो, मैं किस प्रकार प्राण रखूँ! हे तात! तुम भी अब जाने को कह रहे हो। तुमको देखकर छाती ठंडी हुई थी। फिर मुझे वही दिन और वही रात! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4298.english_translation: O Hanuman, tell me how I am to keep my life! You too, dear one, are now saying you must go. Seeing you had cooled my heart; now I will face the same day and the same night again.
ramacharitamanas::4298.translation_literal: कहु (tell) / कपि (Hanuman) / केहि बिधि (by what means) / राखौं (shall I keep) / प्राना (life-breath) / तुम्हहू (you also) / तात (dear one) / कहत (saying) / अब (now) / जाना (to go) / तोहि (you) / देखि (seeing) / सीतलि (cool) / भइ (became) / छाती (heart/chest) / पुनि (again) / मो कहुँ (for me) / सोइ (the same) / दिनु (day) / सो (the same) / राती (night)
ramacharitamanas::4298.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4298.essence: A brief refuge can make separation hurt even more.
ramacharitamanas::4298.simple_meaning: Sita tells Hanuman that his presence brought her comfort, and his departure will leave her facing the same unbearable loneliness again.
ramacharitamanas::4298.simple_insight: Love can be a shelter, and its departure can feel like the return of darkness.
ramacharitamanas::4298.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has finally found Hanuman, the messenger of Ram. His arrival cools her grief for a moment, but now he must leave to carry news back to Ram. She speaks from the ache of separation, knowing that his departure will reopen her lonely vigil.
ramacharitamanas::4298.modern_relevance: You finally hear from the person who has been checking on you through the worst week of your life. Then they say they have to go, and the room feels empty again.
ramacharitamanas::4298.insight: It names how relief can deepen attachment, making separation feel sharper after comfort.

ramacharitamanas::4299.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुतहि समुझाइ करि बहु बिधि धीरजु दीन्ह। चरन कमल सिरु नाइ कपि गवनु राम पहिं कीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::4299.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने जानकीजी को समझाकर बहुत प्रकार से धीरज दिया और उनके चरणकमलों में सिर नवाकर श्री रामजी के पास गमन किया ॥ समुद्र के इस पार आना, सबका लौटना, मधुवन प्रवेश, सुग्रीव मिलन,
ramacharitamanas::4299.english_translation: After comforting Janaki in many ways, Hanuman bowed his head to her lotus feet and went to meet Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4299.translation_literal: जनकसुतहि (to Janaki, daughter of Janak) / समुझाइ (having reassured) / करि (doing) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / धीरजु (steadiness, courage) / दीन्ह (gave) / चरन कमल (lotus feet) / सिरु नाइ (bowing head) / कपि (the monkey devotee) / गवनु (departure) / राम पहिं (toward Ram) / कीन्ह (made, did)
ramacharitamanas::4299.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4299.essence: Devotion first comforts the suffering, then returns to the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::4299.simple_meaning: Hanuman reassures Sita, bows to her feet, and then goes to Ram. His devotion shows itself through comfort, humility, and action.
ramacharitamanas::4299.simple_insight: True devotion makes you gentler, not louder.
ramacharitamanas::4299.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita after a long search. Before leaving, he gives her courage in every possible way, bows to her feet, and only then heads back to Ram. The moment shows devotion expressed as care and humility.
ramacharitamanas::4299.modern_relevance: You finish helping a frightened friend pack their bags, wait until they can breathe again, and only then walk out the door. Real devotion does not rush past the person in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4299.insight: It teaches you to combine reassurance, humility, and faithful action in one response.

ramacharitamanas::4300.verse_sanskrit: चलत महाधुनि गर्जेसि भारी। गर्भ स्रवहिं सुनि निसिचर नारी॥ नाघि सिंधु एहि पारहि आवा। सबद किलिकिला कपिन्ह सुनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4300.verse_hindi: चलते समय उन्होंने महाध्वनि से भारी गर्जन किया, जिसे सुनकर राक्षसों की स्त्रियों के गर्भ गिरने लगे। समुद्र लाँघकर वे इस पार आए और उन्होंने वानरों को किलकिला शब्द (हर्षध्वनि) सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4300.english_translation: As he went, he roared so fiercely that the demon women miscarried at the sound. After crossing the ocean, he came to this shore and gave the monkeys a joyful cry.
ramacharitamanas::4300.translation_literal: चलत (while going) / महाधुनि (great roar) / गर्जेसि (he roared) / भारी (fiercely) / गर्भ (wombs / pregnancies) / स्रवहिं (flow away / miscarry) / सुनि (hearing) / निसिचर (demon) / नारी (women) / नाघि (having crossed) / सिंधु (the ocean) / एहि पारहि (to this shore) / आवा (came) / सबद (sound) / किलिकिला (joyful cry) / कपिन्ह (to the monkeys) / सुनावा (he made heard)
ramacharitamanas::4300.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4300.essence: A true return carries both thunder and joy.
ramacharitamanas::4300.simple_meaning: Hanuman crossed the ocean, roared in triumph, and reached the monkeys with a cry of joy. The verse mainly describes the scene, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4300.simple_insight: Sometimes victory announces itself before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4300.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has crossed Lanka’s ocean and is returning to the monkey army after finding Sita. His roar shakes the enemy world, then becomes a joyful signal to his own side. The verse heightens the arrival before the reunion.
ramacharitamanas::4300.modern_relevance: You come home after the hardest part is over, still buzzing from the win, and your voice gives the good news before your face does.
ramacharitamanas::4300.insight: It frames success as something that changes the atmosphere around you before you explain it.

ramacharitamanas::4301.verse_sanskrit: हरषे सब बिलोकि हनुमाना। नूतन जन्म कपिन्ह तब जाना॥ मुख प्रसन्न तन तेज बिराजा। कीन्हेसि रामचंद्र कर काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4301.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी को देखकर सब हर्षित हो गए और तब वानरों ने अपना नया जन्म समझा। हनुमान् जी का मुख प्रसन्न है और शरीर में तेज विराजमान है, (जिससे उन्होंने समझ लिया कि) ये श्री रामचंद्रजी का कार्य कर आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4301.english_translation: Everyone rejoiced on seeing Hanuman; the monkeys felt they had been born anew. Hanuman’s face was bright with joy, and his body shone with radiance, showing that he had done Ramchandra’s work.
ramacharitamanas::4301.translation_literal: हरषे (rejoiced) / सब (all) / बिलोकि (seeing) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / नूतन (new) / जन्म (birth) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / तब (then) / जाना (knew) / मुख (face) / प्रसन्न (joyful) / तन (body) / तेज (radiance) / बिराजा (dwelt) / कीन्हेसि (he did) / रामचंद्र (Ramchandra) / कर (of) / काजा (task)
ramacharitamanas::4301.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4301.essence: Completed service leaves a glow others can instantly recognize.
ramacharitamanas::4301.simple_meaning: The monkeys are overjoyed to see Hanuman return, and his shining face shows he has completed Ram's task.
ramacharitamanas::4301.simple_insight: True success is visible. When you return with purpose fulfilled, even your presence carries relief.
ramacharitamanas::4301.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has crossed back from Lanka after finding Sita. The monkeys see his radiant face and immediately know Ram’s work is done. Their joy is so complete it feels like being born again.
ramacharitamanas::4301.modern_relevance: You walk into the room after a hard trip, and everyone can read it on your face: the mission is done, and the tension breaks at once.
ramacharitamanas::4301.insight: It shifts attention from the feat itself to the visible peace that comes after faithful service.

ramacharitamanas::4302.verse_sanskrit: मिले सकल अति भए सुखारी। तलफत मीन पाव जिमि बारी॥ चले हरषि रघुनायक पासा। पूँछत कहत नवल इतिहासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4302.verse_hindi: सब हनुमान् जी से मिले और बहुत ही सुखी हुए, जैसे तड़पती हुई मछली को जल मिल गया हो। सब हर्षित होकर नए-नए इतिहास (वृत्तांत) पूछते- कहते हुए श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4302.english_translation: Everyone met Hanuman and became deeply joyful, like a thirsty fish finding water. Rejoicing, they went to Raghunath, asking and telling fresh accounts.
ramacharitamanas::4302.translation_literal: मिले (met) / सकल (all) / अति (very) / भए (became) / सुखारी (happy) / तलफत (thirsting, gasping) / मीन (fish) / पाव (finds) / जिमि (like) / बारी (water)॥ / चले (went) / हरषि (rejoicing) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / पासा (near) / पूँछत (asking) / कहत (telling) / नवल (new) / इतिहासा (stories)॥
ramacharitamanas::4302.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4302.essence: Meeting the one you longed for turns relief into joy.
ramacharitamanas::4302.simple_meaning: The vanaras are overjoyed to see Hanuman, and they hurry to Ram with fresh questions and stories.
ramacharitamanas::4302.simple_insight: Real joy is often simple: finding the one you were waiting for.
ramacharitamanas::4302.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has crossed the ocean and reached the monkey camp in Lanka. The others meet him with relief so deep it feels like a fish finding water. Their happiness spills into motion as they rush to Ram, eager to hear everything.
ramacharitamanas::4302.modern_relevance: You spot the friend who finally made it through the airport crowd, and your whole body relaxes. Relief turns into rapid-fire questions, because the person you were waiting for is finally here.
ramacharitamanas::4302.insight: It shows how reunion naturally becomes conversation, gratitude, and movement toward what matters most.

ramacharitamanas::4303.verse_sanskrit: तब मधुबन भीतर सब आए। अंगद संमत मधु फल खाए॥ रखवारे जब बरजन लागे। मुष्टि प्रहार हनत सब भागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4303.verse_hindi: तब सब लोग मधुवन के भीतर आए और अंगद की सम्मति से सबने मधुर फल (या मधु और फल) खाए। जब रखवाले बरजने लगे, तब घूँसों की मार मारते ही सब रखवाले भाग छूटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4303.english_translation: Then everyone entered the Madhu grove, and with Angad's approval ate the sweet fruits. When the guards tried to stop them, a few punches sent them running.
ramacharitamanas::4303.translation_literal: तब (then) / मधुबन (Madhu grove) / भीतर (inside) / सब (all) / आए (came) / अंगद (Angad) / संमत (with approval) / मधु (sweet) / फल (fruits) / खाए (ate) / रखवारे (guards) / जब (when) / बरजन (to stop/rebuke) / लागे (began) / मुष्टि प्रहार (punch blows) / हनत (striking) / सब (all) / भागे (ran away)
ramacharitamanas::4303.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4303.essence: Bold action can clear the way before resistance gathers.
ramacharitamanas::4303.simple_meaning: Hanuman and the monkeys enter the grove, eat the fruits, and chase away the guards who try to stop them.
ramacharitamanas::4303.simple_insight: Some moments ask for boldness, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4303.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has already found his companions in Lanka. Now the monkeys enter the Madhu grove under Angad's lead, enjoy the fruit, and drive off the guards. The scene shows their fearless confidence after Hanuman's success.
ramacharitamanas::4303.modern_relevance: A team walks into a space where they do not feel welcome, gets the job done, and leaves before fear can take over.
ramacharitamanas::4303.insight: It shifts attention from caution to decisive action when the moment calls for it.

ramacharitamanas::4304.verse_sanskrit: जाइ पुकारे ते सब बन उजार जुबराज। सुनि सुग्रीव हरष कपि करि आए प्रभु काज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4304.verse_hindi: उन सबने जाकर पुकारा कि युवराज अंगद वन उजाड़ रहे हैं। यह सुनकर सुग्रीव हर्षित हुए कि वानर प्रभु का कार्य कर आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4304.english_translation: When they went and cried out that Prince Angad was destroying the grove, Sugriva heard it and rejoiced that the monkeys had completed the Lord's work.
ramacharitamanas::4304.translation_literal: जाइ (going) / पुकारे (called out) / ते (they) / सब (all) / बन (grove) / उजार (destroying) / जुबराज (prince) / सुनि (hearing) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / हरष (rejoiced) / कपि (monkeys) / करि (having done) / आए (came) / प्रभु (Lord's) / काज (work)
ramacharitamanas::4304.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4304.essence: What looks like trouble can still be faithful service.
ramacharitamanas::4304.simple_meaning: The guards complain that Angad is wrecking the grove, and Sugriva is pleased because the monkeys have done Ram's work.
ramacharitamanas::4304.simple_insight: Even a complaint can become good news when your side is acting in service.
ramacharitamanas::4304.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman's reunion, the monkeys enter Madhuvan and eat the fruit. The guards run to report that Prince Angad is ruining the grove. Sugriva hears the report and feels joy, because he sees the episode as service to Ram, not misconduct.
ramacharitamanas::4304.modern_relevance: A manager hears that the team caused a stir at a client site, but the real issue was never the noise. What matters is whether the work got done.
ramacharitamanas::4304.insight: It shifts judgment from appearances to the larger purpose behind an action.

ramacharitamanas::4305.verse_sanskrit: जौं न होति सीता सुधि पाई। मधुबन के फल सकहिं कि काई॥ एहि बिधि मन बिचार कर राजा। आइ गए कपि सहित समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4305.verse_hindi: यदि सीताजी की खबर न पाई होती तो क्या वे मधुवन के फल खा सकते थे? इस प्रकार राजा सुग्रीव मन में विचार कर ही रहे थे कि समाज सहित वानर आ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4305.english_translation: If Sita's news had not been found, could the monkeys have eaten the fruits of the grove? While Sugriva was thinking this in his mind, the monkeys arrived with the whole company.
ramacharitamanas::4305.translation_literal: जौं (if) / न (not) / होति (had been) / सीता (Sita) / सुधि (news) / पाई (found) / मधुबन (Madhuban grove) / के (of) / फल (fruits) / सकहिं (could) / कि (whether) / काई (eat)॥ एहि (in this) / बिधि (manner) / मन (mind) / बिचार (thought) / कर (doing) / राजा (king) / आइ (having come) / गए (went) / कपि (monkeys) / सहित (with) / समाजा (company) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4305.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4305.essence: Enjoyment has meaning only after the real mission is fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::4305.simple_meaning: Sugriva reflects that the monkeys would not have enjoyed the grove if they had not first found news of Sita. As he thinks this, Hanuman and the others arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4305.simple_insight: The joy of success feels different when it is tied to a greater purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4305.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already found Sita, and the monkeys have tasted the reward of that mission in Madhuban. Sugriva is thinking about how impossible their enjoyment would have been without that breakthrough, when Hanuman returns with the full company.
ramacharitamanas::4305.modern_relevance: You finally relax after a long search, but the reward only matters because the real problem was solved first. The relief comes before the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::4305.insight: It frames pleasure as secondary to completing the true task.

ramacharitamanas::4306.verse_sanskrit: आइ सबन्हि नावा पद सीसा। मिलेउ सबन्हि अति प्रेम कपीसा॥ पूँछी कुसल कुसल पद देखी। राम कृपाँ भा काजु बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4306.verse_hindi: (सबने आकर सुग्रीव के चरणों में सिर नवाया। कपिराज सुग्रीव सभी से बड़े प्रेम के साथ मिले। उन्होंने कुशल पूछी, (तब वानरों ने उत्तर दिया-) आपके चरणों के दर्शन से सब कुशल है। श्री रामजी की कृपा से विशेष कार्य हुआ (कार्य में विशेष सफलता हुई है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4306.english_translation: All the monkeys bowed their heads at Sugriva’s feet. The king of the monkeys greeted them with great love. He asked after their well-being, and they replied that seeing his feet had made everything well. By Ram’s grace, their mission had been especially successful.
ramacharitamanas::4306.translation_literal: आइ (having come) / सबन्हि (all) / नावा (bowed) / पद (feet) / सीसा (heads) । मिलेउ (met) / सबन्हि (all) / अति (great) / प्रेम (love) / कपीसा (king of monkeys) ॥ पूँछी (asked) / कुसल (well-being) / कुसल (well-being) / पद (feet) / देखी (seeing) । राम (Ram) / कृपाँ (by grace) / भा (became) / काजु (task) / बिसेषी (special) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4306.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4306.essence: Love received well makes hard work feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::4306.simple_meaning: The monkeys bow to Sugriva, and he welcomes them warmly. They say that seeing his feet has made them well, and that Ram’s grace has made their mission succeed.
ramacharitamanas::4306.simple_insight: A humble welcome can turn danger into relief.
ramacharitamanas::4306.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, Hanuman and the returning monkeys come before Sugriva after finding Sita’s trace. They bow, he receives them with love, and the whole mood shifts from anxious waiting to grateful success.
ramacharitamanas::4306.modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day, and the first warm face at the door changes everything. Relief often begins with being received well.
ramacharitamanas::4306.insight: It shows how respect, affection, and grace can confirm that a difficult task has been completed.

ramacharitamanas::4307.verse_sanskrit: नाथ काजु कीन्हेउ हनुमाना। राखे सकल कपिन्ह के प्राना॥ सुनि सुग्रीव बहुरि तेहि मिलेऊ कपिन्ह सहित रघुपति पहिं चलेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4307.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! हनुमान ने सब कार्य किया और सब वानरों के प्राण बचा लिए। यह सुनकर सुग्रीवजी हनुमान् जी से फिर मिले और सब वानरों समेत श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4307.english_translation: O Lord, Hanuman has done the task and saved the lives of all the monkeys. Hearing this, Sugriva met him again, and he went with all the monkeys to Raghupati.
ramacharitamanas::4307.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / काजु (task) / कीन्हेउ (did) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / राखे (saved) / सकल (all) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / के (of) / प्राना (lives) / सुनि (hearing) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / बहुरि (again) / तेहि (him) / मिलेऊ (met) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / सहित (with) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / पहिं (toward) / चलेऊ (went)
ramacharitamanas::4307.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4307.essence: True success is when everyone survives the task.
ramacharitamanas::4307.simple_meaning: Hanuman completes the mission and saves the monkey army. Sugriva rejoins him, and everyone goes together to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4307.simple_insight: Real service protects others first; recognition comes later.
ramacharitamanas::4307.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's aftermath, Hanuman's success is no longer private. Sugriva hears that the mission is complete and that the monkey army has been spared, so he gathers everyone and heads back to Ram. The verse moves the story from search to reunion.
ramacharitamanas::4307.modern_relevance: You finish the hard part of a group project at 1 a.m. and quietly keep everyone from falling apart. Only after the crisis passes does the team move together again.
ramacharitamanas::4307.insight: It shifts attention from personal triumph to the welfare of the whole group.

ramacharitamanas::4308.verse_sanskrit: राम कपिन्ह जब आवत देखा। किएँ काजु मन हरष बिसेषा॥ फटिक सिला बैठे द्वौ भाई। परे सकल कपि चरनन्हि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4308.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने जब वानरों को कार्य किए हुए आते देखा तब उनके मन में विशेष हर्ष हुआ। दोनों भाई स्फटिक शिला पर बैठे थे। सब वानर जाकर उनके चरणों पर गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4308.english_translation: When Ram saw the monkeys returning after completing the task, his heart filled with special joy. The two brothers sat on a crystal rock, and all the monkeys fell at their feet.
ramacharitamanas::4308.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / जब (when) / आवत (coming) / देखा (saw) / किएँ (having done) / काजु (task) / मन (mind/heart) / हरष (joy) / बिसेषा (special) / फटिक (crystal) / सिला (rock) / बैठे (sat) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) / परे (fell) / सकल (all) / कपि (monkeys) / चरनन्हि (at feet) / जाई (going)
ramacharitamanas::4308.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4308.essence: Completed effort becomes sweeter when it is received with love.
ramacharitamanas::4308.simple_meaning: Ram is pleased when the monkeys return after finishing their task. He and Lakshman sit together, and the monkeys bow at their feet.
ramacharitamanas::4308.simple_insight: There is deep relief in returning to someone who welcomes your effort with joy.
ramacharitamanas::4308.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman’s success in Lanka, the monkeys return to Ram and Lakshman on the crystal rock. Ram sees that the mission has been completed and feels special joy. The whole army bows down in gratitude and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4308.modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day and someone sees the effort behind your tired face. That quiet welcome can feel like the real reward.
ramacharitamanas::4308.insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the bond that gives the task meaning.

ramacharitamanas::4309.verse_sanskrit: प्रीति सहित सब भेंटे रघुपति करुना पुंज॥ पूछी कुसल नाथ अब कुसल देखि पद कंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4309.verse_hindi: दया की राशि श्री रघुनाथजी सबसे प्रेम सहित गले लगकर मिले और कुशल पूछी। (वानरों ने कहा-) हे नाथ! आपके चरण कमलों के दर्शन पाने से अब कुशल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4309.english_translation: Raghupati, a mass of compassion, embraced them all with love and asked after their welfare. Seeing your lotus feet, O Lord, now all is well.
ramacharitamanas::4309.translation_literal: प्रीति सहित (with affection) / सब (all) / भेंटे (met, embraced) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / करुना पुंज (mass of compassion)॥ / पूछी (asked) / कुसल (welfare, well-being) / नाथ (Lord) / अब (now) / कुसल (well) / देखि (having seen) / पद कंज (lotus feet)
ramacharitamanas::4309.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4309.essence: Love makes a simple meeting feel like blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4309.simple_meaning: Ram lovingly greets the monkeys and asks how they are. They reply that simply seeing his feet has made everything feel well.
ramacharitamanas::4309.simple_insight: Being near what you love can restore you more than any answer can.
ramacharitamanas::4309.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman's success, Ram meets the returning monkeys in Sundarkand. He greets them with affection and asks about their welfare. The monkeys answer that the sight of his feet itself has made them feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::4309.modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room after a long, hard day, and the person you trust most just looks relieved to see you. No speech is needed. Presence itself becomes the comfort.
ramacharitamanas::4309.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to presence: being seen by the beloved is itself the reward.

ramacharitamanas::4310.verse_sanskrit: जामवंत कह सुनु रघुराया। जा पर नाथ करहु तुम्ह दाया॥ ताहि सदा सुभ कुसल निरंतर। सुर नर मुनि प्रसन्न ता ऊपर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4310.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् ने कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए। हे नाथ! जिस पर आप दया करते हैं, उसे सदा कल्याण और निरंतर कुशल है। देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सभी उस पर प्रसन्न रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4310.english_translation: Jambavan said: Listen, O Lord of Raghu. Whoever receives your grace lives in lasting well-being. Devas, humans, and sages are pleased with that person.
ramacharitamanas::4310.translation_literal: जामवंत (Jambavan) / कह (said) / सुनु (listen) / रघुराया (O Lord of Raghu) / जा पर (on whom) / नाथ (Lord) / करहु (you do) / तुम्ह (you) / दाया (grace) / ताहि (to that one) / सदा (always) / सुभ (auspicious) / कुसल (well-being) / निरंतर (continuously) / सुर (radiant beings) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / ता ऊपर (upon that one)
ramacharitamanas::4310.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4310.essence: Ram’s grace makes a person permanently fortunate and universally welcomed.
ramacharitamanas::4310.simple_meaning: Jambavan tells Ram that anyone touched by Ram's grace lives in lasting well-being, and even the higher beings, people, and sages feel pleased with that person.
ramacharitamanas::4310.simple_insight: It brings relief to know that being held by Ram changes everything around you.
ramacharitamanas::4310.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman’s success, Jambavan speaks to Ram with reverence. He explains that Ram’s grace is not temporary luck but a lasting blessing: the one who receives it lives in continual well-being, and all noble beings rejoice in that person.
ramacharitamanas::4310.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence steadies a whole room. Their confidence isn’t loud, but everyone relaxes around them. Jambavan says that kind of steadiness comes from being touched by Ram’s grace.
ramacharitamanas::4310.insight: It shifts attention from self-made success to the quiet power of being supported by grace.

ramacharitamanas::4311.verse_sanskrit: सोइ बिजई बिनई गुन सागर। तासु सुजसु त्रैलोक उजागर॥ प्रभु कीं कृपा भयउ सबु काजू। जन्म हमार सुफल भा आजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4311.verse_hindi: वही विजयी है, वही विनयी है और वही गुणों का समुद्र बन जाता है। उसी का सुंदर यश तीनों लोकों में प्रकाशित होता है। प्रभु की कृपा से सब कार्य हुआ। आज हमारा जन्म सफल हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4311.english_translation: He alone is victorious, humble, and an ocean of virtues. His beautiful fame shines through the three worlds. By the Lord's grace, everything was accomplished. Today our birth has become fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::4311.translation_literal: सोइ (that very one) / बिजई (victorious) / बिनई (humble) / गुन सागर (ocean of virtues) / तासु (his) / सुजसु (good fame) / त्रैलोक (three worlds) / उजागर (illuminated) / प्रभु (Lord) / कीं कृपा (by grace) / भयउ (became) / सबु (all) / काजू (work) / जन्म (birth) / हमार (our) / सुफल (fruitful) / भा (became) / आजू (today)
ramacharitamanas::4311.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4311.essence: Victory becomes holy when humility and grace stand behind it.
ramacharitamanas::4311.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as victorious, humble, and endlessly virtuous. Because of his grace, Hanuman's mission succeeds and his life feels fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::4311.simple_insight: True fulfillment feels like grace, not self-congratulation.
ramacharitamanas::4311.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita and returned to Ram's camp. Jambavan speaks with awe, praising Ram's victory, humility, and fame. The rescue has worked, and the whole journey now feels like a blessed turning point.
ramacharitamanas::4311.modern_relevance: You finish the hardest part of a project and realize the relief isn't pride — it's gratitude. The outcome feels larger than your effort because something beyond ego carried it through.
ramacharitamanas::4311.insight: It shifts credit away from personal achievement toward grace and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4312.verse_sanskrit: नाथ पवनसुत कीन्हि जो करनी। सहसहुँ मुख न जाइ सो बरनी॥ पवनतनय के चरित सुहाए। जामवंत रघुपतिहि सुनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4312.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! पवनपुत्र हनुमान् ने जो करनी की, उसका हजार मुखों से भी वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। तब जाम्बवान् ने हनुमान् जी के सुंदर चरित्र (कार्य) श्री रघुनाथजी को सुनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4312.english_translation: O Lord, the deeds Hanuman performed cannot be described even with a thousand mouths. Then Jambavan told Raghunath the lovely story of the son of the wind.
ramacharitamanas::4312.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / कीन्हि (did) / जो (which) / करनी (deed) / सहसहुँ (even a thousand) / मुख (mouths) / न (not) / जाइ (can) / सो (that) / बरनी (described)॥ / पवनतनय (son of the wind) / के (of) / चरित (deeds / character) / सुहाए (lovely) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / रघुपतिहि (to Raghupati) / सुनाए (told)॥
ramacharitamanas::4312.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4312.essence: Real devotion makes a person impossible to fully describe.
ramacharitamanas::4312.simple_meaning: Hanuman’s actions are so great they cannot be fully described. Jambavan then tells Ram about Hanuman’s noble deeds.
ramacharitamanas::4312.simple_insight: True greatness needs no self-praise; it reveals itself through action.
ramacharitamanas::4312.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Jambavan is speaking to Ram after Hanuman’s extraordinary search and service. He says Hanuman’s deeds are beyond description, then begins recounting them so Ram can hear who this devoted servant truly is.
ramacharitamanas::4312.modern_relevance: You see someone quietly fix the mess, stay late, and carry the whole burden without asking for credit. Later, the room finally understands what that person did.
ramacharitamanas::4312.insight: It shifts attention from self-advertisement to deeds that speak for themselves.

ramacharitamanas::4313.verse_sanskrit: सुनत कृपानिधि मन अति भाए। पुनि हनुमान हरषि हियँ लाए॥ कहहु तात केहि भाँति जानकी। रहति करति रच्छा स्वप्रान की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4313.verse_hindi: (वे चरित्र) सुनने पर कृपानिधि श्री रामचंदजी के मन को बहुत ही अच्छे लगे। उन्होंने हर्षित होकर हनुमान् जी को फिर हृदय से लगा लिया और कहा- हे तात! कहो, सीता किस प्रकार रहती और अपने प्राणों की रक्षा करती हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4313.english_translation: Hearing this, the compassionate Lord was greatly pleased. He embraced Hanuman with joy and said, "Tell me, dear one, in what way does Janaki live and protect her life?"
ramacharitamanas::4313.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / भाए (pleased) । पुनि (again) / हनुमान (Hanuman) / हरषि (rejoicing) / हियँ (to the heart) / लाए (brought close, embraced) ॥ कहहु (tell) / तात (dear one) / केहि भाँति (in what way) / जानकी (Janaki) / रहति (lives, remains) / करति (doing) / रच्छा (protection) / स्वप्रान की (of her own life) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4313.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4313.essence: Devotion makes even the Lord long for news of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::4313.simple_meaning: Ram is delighted by Hanuman's report and embraces him warmly, then asks how Sita is surviving and protecting herself.
ramacharitamanas::4313.simple_insight: Love makes room for closeness, even across separation.
ramacharitamanas::4313.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just spoken of Sita's condition. Ram's heart is softened by the news; he pulls Hanuman close again and immediately asks about Sita's safety. The scene shows devotion turning into intimate concern.
ramacharitamanas::4313.modern_relevance: You finally hear from someone you love after days of silence. Relief comes first, but your next question is the real one: are they safe, and how are they holding up?
ramacharitamanas::4313.insight: It shifts attention from heroic achievement to the living bond that gives the mission its meaning.

ramacharitamanas::4314.verse_sanskrit: नाम पाहरू दिवस निसि ध्यान तुम्हार कपाट। लोचन निज पद जंत्रित जाहिं प्रान केहिं बाट ॥
ramacharitamanas::4314.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) आपका नाम रात-दिन पहरा देने वाला है, आपका ध्यान ही किंवाड़ है। नेत्रों को अपने चरणों में लगाए रहती हैं, यही ताला लगा है, फिर प्राण जाएँ तो किस मार्ग से? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4314.english_translation: Your name guards me day and night; your meditation is the lock. My eyes stay fixed on your feet—how could my life leave by any other way?
ramacharitamanas::4314.translation_literal: नाम (name) / पाहरू (guard) / दिवस (day) / निसि (night) / ध्यान (meditation) / तुम्हार (your) / कपाट (door-bar) / लोचन (eyes) / निज (own) / पद (feet) / जंत्रित (fastened) / जाहिं (go) / प्रान (life-breath) / केहिं (which) / बाट (path)
ramacharitamanas::4314.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4314.essence: Remembrance becomes protection when your whole attention rests on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4314.simple_meaning: Ram's name protects Hanuman constantly, and keeping Ram in mind keeps his life secure. With his gaze fixed on Ram's feet, nothing can pull him away.
ramacharitamanas::4314.simple_insight: There is calm in being held by remembrance, not by your own control.
ramacharitamanas::4314.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita and is speaking from complete devotion. He tells Ram that Ram's name itself guards him day and night, while meditation on Ram acts like a locked gate. This is the heart of his fearless bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::4314.modern_relevance: You wake up at 3 a.m. with the same worry looping again. Something steadier than panic can hold you too: a name, a practice, a presence you return to until fear loses the doorway.
ramacharitamanas::4314.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to refuge in constant remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::4315.verse_sanskrit: चलत मोहि चूड़ामनि दीन्हीं। रघुपति हृदयँ लाइ सोइ लीन्ही॥ नाथ जुगल लोचन भरि बारी। बचन कहे कछु जनककुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4315.verse_hindi: चलते समय उन्होंने मुझे चूड़ामणि (उतारकर) दी। श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसे लेकर हृदय से लगा लिया। (हनुमान् जी ने फिर कहा-) हे नाथ! दोनों नेत्रों में जल भरकर जानकीजी ने मुझसे कुछ वचन कहे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4315.english_translation: As she left, she gave me her jewel from the hair. Raghupati took it and held it to his heart. Then, with both eyes full of tears, Janak’s daughter spoke a few words to me.
ramacharitamanas::4315.translation_literal: चलत (while leaving) / मोहि (to me) / चूड़ामनि (hair-jewel) / दीन्हीं (gave) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लाइ (bringing) / सोइ (that) / लीन्ही (took) / नाथ (O Lord) / जुगल (both) / लोचन (eyes) / भरि (filled) / बारी (with water/tears) / बचन (words) / कहे (spoke) / कछु (some) / जनककुमारी (daughter of Janak)
ramacharitamanas::4315.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4315.essence: Love turns a small token into living presence.
ramacharitamanas::4315.simple_meaning: Sita gave Hanuman a token for Ram, and Ram received it with deep emotion. Her tears and words show how much she longs to be reunited.
ramacharitamanas::4315.simple_insight: Love can travel through a small object and still carry the whole heart.
ramacharitamanas::4315.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally found Sita. Before sending him back, she gives him her hair-jewel as proof for Ram. Ram presses it to his heart, and Sita speaks through tears. The scene turns a token into living connection.
ramacharitamanas::4315.modern_relevance: You find a note, a photo, or a voice message from someone you miss, and your whole chest tightens. A small thing can carry a whole relationship when love is real.
ramacharitamanas::4315.insight: It teaches you to see how devotion turns even a token into presence.

ramacharitamanas::4316.verse_sanskrit: अनुज समेत गहेहु प्रभु चरना। दीन बंधु प्रनतारति हरना॥ मन क्रम बचन चरन अनुरागी। केहिं अपराध नाथ हौं त्यागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4316.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई समेत प्रभु के चरण पकड़ना (और कहना कि) आप दीनबंधु हैं, शरणागत के दुःखों को हरने वाले हैं और मैं मन, वचन और कर्म से आपके चरणों की अनुरागिणी हूँ। फिर स्वामी (आप) ने मुझे किस अपराध से त्याग दिया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4316.english_translation: With your younger brother beside you, you held the Lord's feet and said: 'You are the friend of the lowly, the remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge. I am devoted to your feet in mind, speech, and action. O Lord, what fault of mine caused you to cast me aside?'
ramacharitamanas::4316.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / गहेहु (you held) / प्रभु (Lord) / चरना (feet) / दीनबंधु (friend of the lowly) / प्रनतारति हरना (remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge) / मन (mind) / क्रम (speech) / बचन (action/words) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागी (attached with loving devotion) / केहिं (which) / अपराध (fault) / नाथ (Lord) / हौं (I) / त्यागी (cast aside)
ramacharitamanas::4316.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4316.essence: True devotion can ask hard questions without losing love.
ramacharitamanas::4316.simple_meaning: Sita calls Ram the friend of the helpless and says her mind, speech, and actions are devoted to him. She asks why he has abandoned her.
ramacharitamanas::4316.simple_insight: Love can remain whole even in heartbreak, and still ask for the wound to be named.
ramacharitamanas::4316.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita speaks through Hanuman's message back to Ram. She names Ram as the protector of the helpless and says her whole being is fixed on him, then asks what fault could possibly justify her abandonment. The verse carries devotion and pain together.
ramacharitamanas::4316.modern_relevance: You send a message after being hurt, trying to stay loving without hiding the ache. You still care completely, but you need to know why the distance exists.
ramacharitamanas::4316.insight: It shows how devotion can coexist with honest sorrow, without collapsing into bitterness or self-erasure.

ramacharitamanas::4317.verse_sanskrit: अवगुन एक मोर मैं माना। बिछुरत प्रान न कीन्ह पयाना॥ नाथ सो नयनन्हि को अपराधा। निसरत प्रान करहिं हठि बाधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4317.verse_hindi: (हाँ) एक दोष मैं अपना (अवश्य) मानती हूँ कि आपका वियोग होते ही मेरे प्राण नहीं चले गए, किंतु हे नाथ! यह तो नेत्रों का अपराध है जो प्राणों के निकलने में हठपूर्वक बाधा देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4317.english_translation: I count one fault of my own: when you were taken from me, my life did not leave. O Lord, that is the fault of my eyes, which stubbornly block my breath from going out.
ramacharitamanas::4317.translation_literal: अवगुन (fault) / एक (one) / मोर (my) / मैं (I) / माना (counted) / बिछुरत (upon separation) / प्रान (life-breath) / न (not) / कीन्ह (did) / पयाना (departure) ॥ / नाथ (Lord) / सो (that) / नयनन्हि (of the eyes) / को (of) / अपराधा (fault) / निसरत (leaving) / प्रान (life-breath) / करहिं (do) / हठि (stubbornly) / बाधा (obstruction) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4317.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4317.essence: Separation is so sharp that even survival feels like resistance.
ramacharitamanas::4317.simple_meaning: Sita says her only fault is that separation from Ram did not kill her at once. She blames her eyes for stubbornly keeping her life-breath from leaving.
ramacharitamanas::4317.simple_insight: Love can hurt so deeply that even staying alive feels like an accident.
ramacharitamanas::4317.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just given Sita Ram's ring and news of him. Overwhelmed by separation, she speaks as if her own body has failed her devotion. The next verse explains how intense that grief is.
ramacharitamanas::4317.modern_relevance: You get the message you've been waiting for after months of silence, and relief arrives mixed with ache. Part of you wonders why you had to keep going at all.
ramacharitamanas::4317.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to seeing how grief can overwhelm even the body's will to release.

ramacharitamanas::4318.verse_sanskrit: बिरह अगिनि तनु तूल समीरा। स्वास जरइ छन माहिं सरीरा॥ नयन स्रवहिं जलु निज हित लागी। जरैं न पाव देह बिरहागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4318.verse_hindi: विरह अग्नि है, शरीर रूई है और श्वास पवन है, इस प्रकार (अग्नि और पवन का संयोग होने से) यह शरीर क्षणमात्र में जल सकता है, परंतु नेत्र अपने हित के लिए प्रभु का स्वरूप देखकर (सुखी होने के लिए) जल (आँसू) बरसाते हैं, जिससे विरह की आग से भी देह जलने नहीं पाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4318.english_translation: The fire of separation is in the body, the body is like cotton, and breath is like wind; in a moment the body could burn. Yet the eyes pour out tears for their own relief, and so the body does not burn in the fire of separation.
ramacharitamanas::4318.translation_literal: बिरह (separation) / अगिनि (fire) / तनु (body) / तूल (cotton) / समीरा (wind) / स्वास (breath) / जरइ (burns) / छन (moment) / माहिं (within) / सरीरा (body) / नयन (eyes) / स्रवहिं (flow) / जलु (water/tears) / निज (own) / हित (welfare) / लागी (for) / जरैं (burn) / न पाव (do not allow) / देह (body) / बिरहागी (burning in separation)
ramacharitamanas::4318.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4318.essence: Longing burns, but tears keep the heart from being consumed.
ramacharitamanas::4318.simple_meaning: Separation feels like a fire that could consume the body, but tears from the eyes ease that pain and keep the body from burning up.
ramacharitamanas::4318.simple_insight: Longing hurts, but honest feeling can also protect you from being destroyed by it.
ramacharitamanas::4318.detailed_meaning: Sita is trapped in Lanka, speaking from the ache of separation from Ram. She describes her body as cotton, breath as wind, and separation as fire. The verse shows how grief burns, yet tears keep that burning from becoming total ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4318.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after a message that never came, feeling heat rise in your chest. The tears, the shaking, the quiet release — they are not weakness; they are what keep heartbreak from hardening into collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4318.insight: It shifts you from resisting grief to letting expression discharge its heat before it overwhelms you.

ramacharitamanas::4319.verse_sanskrit: सीता कै अति बिपति बिसाला। बिनहिं कहें भलि दीनदयाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4319.verse_hindi: सीताजी की विपत्ति बहुत बड़ी है। हे दीनदयालु! वह बिना कही ही अच्छी है (कहने से आपको बड़ा क्लेश होगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4319.english_translation: Sita's suffering is immense. O Merciful One, it is better left unspoken.
ramacharitamanas::4319.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / कै (of) / अति (very great) / बिपति (trouble) / बिसाला (vast) / बिनहिं (without) / कहें (saying) / भलि (better) / दीनदयाला (O merciful one)
ramacharitamanas::4319.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::4319.essence: True compassion hears pain before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4319.simple_meaning: Sita's distress is so severe that even speaking of it feels unbearable. The line turns toward Ram as the one who understands without needing details.
ramacharitamanas::4319.simple_insight: There are moments when compassion begins before words do.
ramacharitamanas::4319.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita's agony has become overwhelming. The speaker cannot even continue describing it plainly and turns to Ram as the merciful one who already knows the depth of her suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4319.modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend in the hospital and run out of words. What matters most is not explanation, but the quiet recognition that their pain is real.
ramacharitamanas::4319.insight: It trains you to respond to suffering with presence first, not explanation.

ramacharitamanas::4320.verse_sanskrit: निमिष निमिष करुनानिधि जाहिं कलप सम बीति। बेगि चलिअ प्रभु आनिअ भुज बल खल दल जीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::4320.verse_hindi: हे करुणानिधान! उनका एक-एक पल कल्प के समान बीतता है। अतः हे प्रभु! तुरंत चलिए और अपनी भुजाओं के बल से दुष्टों के दल को जीतकर सीताजी को ले आइए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4320.english_translation: O treasure of compassion, for her every moment passes like an age. Please come at once, and by the strength of your arms defeat the enemy host and bring Sita back.
ramacharitamanas::4320.translation_literal: निमिष (moment) / निमिष (moment) / करुनानिधि (treasure of compassion) / जाहिं (goes) / कलप (age) / सम (like) / बीति (passes) / बेगि (quickly) / चलिअ (let us go) / प्रभु (Lord) / आनिअ (bring) / भुज (arms) / बल (strength) / खल (wicked) / दल (army) / जीति (having defeated)
ramacharitamanas::4320.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4320.essence: Real devotion cannot watch suffering slowly.
ramacharitamanas::4320.simple_meaning: Sita's suffering feels unbearably long, so Hanuman pleads with Ram to come quickly, defeat the enemy forces, and rescue her.
ramacharitamanas::4320.simple_insight: Love does not stay abstract when someone is suffering; it moves fast, speaks plainly, and asks for help.
ramacharitamanas::4320.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita and heard the full weight of her separation. He now speaks as her messenger, feeling her pain as urgent time itself, and begs Ram to come at once and rescue her.
ramacharitamanas::4320.modern_relevance: You get a voice note from someone you love, and one sentence tells you they are barely holding on. You stop everything. That urgency is what Hanuman feels here.
ramacharitamanas::4320.insight: It turns devotion into immediate action for someone else's suffering, not private emotion.

ramacharitamanas::4321.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना। भरि आए जल राजिव नयना॥ बचन कायँ मन मम गति जाही। सपनेहुँ बूझिअ बिपति कि ताही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4321.verse_hindi: सीताजी का दुःख सुनकर सुख के धाम प्रभु के कमल नेत्रों में जल भर आया (और वे बोले-) मन, वचन और शरीर से जिसे मेरी ही गति (मेरा ही आश्रय) है, उसे क्या स्वप्न में भी विपत्ति हो सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4321.english_translation: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord whose home is joy had tears fill his lotus eyes. He said, “For the one whose refuge in mind, speech, and body is mine, can there be adversity even in a dream?”
ramacharitamanas::4321.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सीता (Sita's) / दुख (sorrow) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुख (joy) / अयना (home) / भरि आए (filled up) / जल (water / tears) / राजिव (lotus) / नयना (eyes) / बचन (speech) / कायँ (body) / मन (mind) / मम (my) / गति (refuge / destination) / जाही (for whom) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / बूझिअ (is there) / बिपति (adversity) / कि (whether) / ताही (for that one)
ramacharitamanas::4321.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4321.essence: Complete refuge makes even adversity feel unreal.
ramacharitamanas::4321.simple_meaning: Ram is moved to tears by Sita's suffering, and he says that anyone who takes refuge in him completely cannot be touched by real danger.
ramacharitamanas::4321.simple_insight: There is deep comfort in knowing total trust is met with total care.
ramacharitamanas::4321.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has brought news of Sita's misery to Ram. Ram's heart breaks, his lotus eyes fill with tears, and he declares that the one who belongs to him in mind, speech, and body cannot be abandoned to adversity.
ramacharitamanas::4321.modern_relevance: You call someone in panic after a night of bad news, and they answer with steady care instead of distance. That is the feeling this verse carries: being held completely when you are most vulnerable.
ramacharitamanas::4321.insight: It shifts trust from partial reliance to wholehearted refuge, showing that surrender and protection belong together.

ramacharitamanas::4322.verse_sanskrit: कह हनुमंत बिपति प्रभु सोई। जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई॥ केतिक बात प्रभु जातुधान की। रिपुहि जीति आनिबी जानकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4322.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे प्रभु! विपत्ति तो वही (तभी) है जब आपका भजन-स्मरण न हो। हे प्रभो! राक्षसों की बात ही कितनी है? आप शत्रु को जीतकर जानकीजी को ले आवेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4322.english_translation: Hanuman said, "O Lord, the only real trouble is when your remembrance and devotion are absent. What are these demons to you? You will defeat the enemy and bring Sita back."
ramacharitamanas::4322.translation_literal: कह (said) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / बिपति (trouble) / प्रभु (Lord) / सोई (that only) / जब (when) / तव (your) / सुमिरन (remembrance) / भजन (devotion) / न (not) / होई (happens)॥ / केतिक (how much) / बात (matter) / प्रभु (Lord) / जातुधान (demons) / की (of) / रिपुहि (enemy) / जीति (defeating) / आनिबी (will bring back) / जानकी (Sita) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4322.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4322.essence: Separation from Ram is the only real danger.
ramacharitamanas::4322.simple_meaning: Hanuman says the worst suffering is forgetting Ram. With Ram in mind, even demons and danger are not a real problem.
ramacharitamanas::4322.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when devotion becomes your center.
ramacharitamanas::4322.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has found Sita and is speaking with total confidence. He tells Ram that the real crisis is not the enemy's strength but separation from Ram's remembrance. From that devotion, victory and rescue become certain.
ramacharitamanas::4322.modern_relevance: You are stuck in traffic, late, and your chest tightens. Then you remember what truly steadies you. The problem is still there, but it no longer owns you.
ramacharitamanas::4322.insight: It shifts the mind from outer danger to inner anchoring in devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4323.verse_sanskrit: सुनु कपि तोहि समान उपकारी। नहिं कोउ सुर नर मुनि तनुधारी॥ प्रति उपकार करौं का तोरा। सनमुख होइ न सकत मन मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4323.verse_hindi: (भगवान् कहने लगे-) हे हनुमान् ! सुन, तेरे समान मेरा उपकारी देवता, मनुष्य अथवा मुनि कोई भी शरीरधारी नहीं है। मैं तेरा प्रत्युपकार (बदले में उपकार) तो क्या करूँ, मेरा मन भी तेरे सामने नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4323.english_translation: O monkey, listen: no embodied being among gods, humans, or sages has helped me like you. What can I give you in return? My mind cannot even face you.
ramacharitamanas::4323.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / कपि (monkey) / तोहि (to you) / समान (equal) / उपकारी (benefactor) / नहिं (not) / कोउ (any) / सुर (deva) / नर (human) / मुनि (sage) / तनुधारी (embodied) / प्रति (in return) / उपकार (favor) / करौं (I do) / का (what) / तोरा (of yours) / सनमुख (face to face) / होइ (to be) / न सकत (not able) / मन (mind) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::4323.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4323.essence: Real devotion creates a debt love itself cannot repay.
ramacharitamanas::4323.simple_meaning: Ram tells Hanuman that no one else has served him like this, and he cannot repay such devotion in any ordinary way.
ramacharitamanas::4323.simple_insight: Deep devotion creates a bond beyond exchange, praise, or repayment.
ramacharitamanas::4323.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman's fearless service has already brought Sita's hope to life, Ram speaks with rare tenderness. He admits that no being—divine, human, or sage—has helped him like Hanuman has, and that even repayment feels impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4323.modern_relevance: You stay up all night helping a friend through a crisis, and they say, almost helplessly, that they can never make it up to you. Some acts of love simply outgrow accounting.
ramacharitamanas::4323.insight: It shifts the mind from transactional giving to devotion that cannot be measured or settled.

ramacharitamanas::4324.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सुत तोहि उरिन मैं नाहीं। देखेउँ करि बिचार मन माहीं॥ पुनि पुनि कपिहि चितव सुरत्राता। लोचन नीर पुलक अति गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4324.verse_hindi: हे पुत्र! सुन, मैंने मन में (खूब) विचार करके देख लिया कि मैं तुझसे उऋण नहीं हो सकता। देवताओं के रक्षक प्रभु बार-बार हनुमान् जी को देख रहे हैं। नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं का जल भरा है और शरीर अत्यंत पुलकित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4324.english_translation: Son, listen: after careful thought, I see that I can never repay you. The protector of the gods keeps looking at Hanuman again and again, with tears in his eyes and his body bristling with joy.
ramacharitamanas::4324.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सुत (son) / तोहि (to you) / उरिन (free from debt) / मैं (I) / नाहीं (am not) / देखेउँ (I saw) / करि (having done) / बिचार (thought) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कपिहि (the monkey) / चितव (looked at) / सुरत्राता (protector of the gods) / लोचन (eyes) / नीर (water) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / अति (very) / गाता (body)
ramacharitamanas::4324.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4324.essence: Pure devotion leaves even the beloved unable to repay it.
ramacharitamanas::4324.simple_meaning: Ram tells Hanuman that no amount of thought can make him feel repaid. Hanuman's devotion is so complete that Ram keeps gazing at him with tears and delight.
ramacharitamanas::4324.simple_insight: Real devotion creates a bond no debt can measure.
ramacharitamanas::4324.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman returns from Lanka, Ram speaks with overwhelming affection. He says he has thought deeply and still cannot repay Hanuman. Looking at Hanuman again and again, Ram's eyes fill with tears and his body trembles with joy.
ramacharitamanas::4324.modern_relevance: You help someone through a crisis, expecting nothing back. Later, they try to thank you and fall short. Some care changes the relationship so deeply that repayment no longer makes sense.
ramacharitamanas::4324.insight: It shifts the mind from transaction to gratitude, showing that selfless service creates a bond beyond compensation.

ramacharitamanas::4325.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन बिलोकि मुख गात हरषि हनुमंत। चरन परेउ प्रेमाकुल त्राहि त्राहि भगवंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4325.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर और उनके (प्रसन्न) मुख तथा (पुलकित) अंगों को देखकर हनुमान् जी हर्षित हो गए और प्रेम में विकल होकर 'हे भगवन् ! मेरी रक्षा करो, रक्षा करो' कहते हुए श्री रामजी के चरणों में गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4325.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words and seeing His joyful face and thrilled body, Hanuman was filled with delight and, overcome by love, fell at Ram's feet crying, "Protect me, protect me, O Lord."
ramacharitamanas::4325.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / बचन (words) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मुख (face) / गात (body) / हरषि (rejoicing) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / चरन (feet) / परेउ (fell) / प्रेमाकुल (overcome with love) / त्राहि त्राहि (protect, protect) / भगवंत (O Lord)
ramacharitamanas::4325.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4325.essence: When love is real, surrender happens before you plan it.
ramacharitamanas::4325.simple_meaning: Hanuman hears Ram's loving words, sees His joy, and is so moved that he falls at Ram's feet in surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4325.simple_insight: Real devotion doesn't stay in the head; it spills into the body as gratitude and surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4325.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just received Ram's tender response after proving his devotion. Seeing Ram's joyful face and hearing His words, Hanuman loses all self-consciousness and drops at His feet, crying for protection in love.
ramacharitamanas::4325.modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you were not expecting, and your chest loosens before you can explain why. Some moments don't call for analysis — only surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4325.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to embodied surrender, where love becomes action before speech.

ramacharitamanas::4326.verse_sanskrit: बार बार प्रभु चहइ उठावा। प्रेम मगन तेहि उठब न भावा॥ प्रभु कर पंकज कपि कें सीसा। सुमिरि सो दसा मगन गौरीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4326.verse_hindi: प्रभु उनको बार-बार उठाना चाहते हैं, परंतु प्रेम में डूबे हुए हनुमान् जी को चरणों से उठना सुहाता नहीं। प्रभु का करकमल हनुमान् जी के सिर पर है। उस स्थिति का स्मरण करके शिवजी प्रेममग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4326.english_translation: Again and again, the Lord tries to lift him, but Hanuman, lost in love, does not wish to rise. The Lord’s lotus hand rests on Hanuman’s head; remembering that scene, Shiva becomes absorbed in love.
ramacharitamanas::4326.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चहइ (wants) / उठावा (to lift) / प्रेम मगन (drowned in love) / तेहि (he) / उठब (to rise) / न (not) / भावा (is pleasing)॥ / प्रभु (the Lord) / कर (hand) / पंकज (lotus) / कपि (monkey devotee) / कें (of) / सीसा (head) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सो (that) / दसा (state) / मगन (absorbed) / गौरीसा (Shiva)॥
ramacharitamanas::4326.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4326.essence: Love can make even honor feel too small to accept.
ramacharitamanas::4326.simple_meaning: Hanuman is so absorbed in love for Ram that he does not want to get up, even when Ram tries to lift him. Shiva remembers this and is moved by devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4326.simple_insight: Love can make surrender feel more natural than standing apart.
ramacharitamanas::4326.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has reached Ram’s presence after crossing into Lanka and bringing news of Sita. Ram keeps trying to lift him, but Hanuman remains overwhelmed by love. Shiva, remembering that scene, becomes lost in devotion himself.
ramacharitamanas::4326.modern_relevance: You finally hear the praise you worked for, but all you feel is gratitude and awe. Some moments are too sacred for self-importance to stand up in them.
ramacharitamanas::4326.insight: It shifts attention from receiving recognition to resting inside devotion itself.

ramacharitamanas::4327.verse_sanskrit: सावधान मन करि पुनि संकर। लागे कहन कथा अति सुंदर॥ कपि उठाई प्रभु हृदयँ लगावा। कर गहि परम निकट बैठावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4327.verse_hindi: फिर मन को सावधान करके शंकरजी अत्यंत सुंदर कथा कहने लगे- हनुमान् जी को उठाकर प्रभु ने हृदय से लगाया और हाथ पकड़कर अत्यंत निकट बैठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4327.english_translation: Then, with his mind made attentive, Shankar began to tell the most beautiful story. The Lord lifted Hanuman, pressed him to His heart, and seated him very close, holding his hand.
ramacharitamanas::4327.translation_literal: सावधान (attentive) / मन (mind) / करि (having made) / पुनि (then) / संकर (Shankar) / लागे (began) / कहन (to tell) / कथा (story) / अति सुंदर (very beautiful) / कपि (monkey devotee, Hanuman) / उठाई (lifting) / प्रभु (the Lord) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लगावा (pressed) / कर (hand) / गहि (holding) / परम निकट (very near) / बैठावा (seated)
ramacharitamanas::4327.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4327.essence: Devotion is answered by being brought close, not kept apart.
ramacharitamanas::4327.simple_meaning: Shiva grows attentive and continues the story, while Ram lifts Hanuman, holds him to His heart, and seats him beside Him in deep closeness.
ramacharitamanas::4327.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing devotion is answered with nearness, not distance.
ramacharitamanas::4327.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Shiva is guiding Parvati through Hanuman's meeting with Ram. As the story turns inward, Ram responds to Hanuman's devotion by lifting him, embracing him, and seating him close. The moment shows how love rewards surrender with intimacy.
ramacharitamanas::4327.modern_relevance: You finally tell someone the truth you've been carrying, and instead of pulling away, they move closer and listen fully. That is the kind of welcome this verse holds.
ramacharitamanas::4327.insight: It shifts devotion from effort alone to intimate mutual presence.

ramacharitamanas::4328.verse_sanskrit: कहु कपि रावन पालित लंका। केहि बिधि दहेउ दुर्ग अति बंका॥ प्रभु प्रसन्न जाना हनुमाना। बोला बचन बिगत अभिमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4328.verse_hindi: हे हनुमान् ! बताओ तो, रावण के द्वारा सुरक्षित लंका और उसके बड़े बाँके किले को तुमने किस तरह जलाया? हनुमान् जी ने प्रभु को प्रसन्न जाना और वे अभिमानरहित वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4328.english_translation: Tell me, monkey, how did you burn Lanka, guarded by Ravana, and its vast, crooked fortress? Hanuman knew the Lord was pleased and spoke words free of pride.
ramacharitamanas::4328.translation_literal: कहु (tell) / कपि (monkey) / रावन (Ravana's) / पालित (protected) / लंका (Lanka) / केहि बिधि (by what way) / दहेउ (you burned) / दुर्ग (fortress) / अति (very) / बंका (crooked, formidable)॥ / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / जाना (knew) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / बोला (spoke) / बचन (words) / बिगत (free of) / अभिमाना (pride)
ramacharitamanas::4328.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4328.essence: Great action stays pure when pride has no place in it.
ramacharitamanas::4328.simple_meaning: Shiva asks Hanuman how he burned Lanka, and Hanuman answers only after sensing Ram's pleasure, with no trace of pride.
ramacharitamanas::4328.simple_insight: Even great achievement stays clean when pride is absent.
ramacharitamanas::4328.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman has found Sita and set the city ablaze, Shiva presses him to explain how it happened. Hanuman waits until he feels Ram's approval, then speaks without self-importance, showing that true service never turns into self-display.
ramacharitamanas::4328.modern_relevance: You finally finish the project everyone doubted. Before you start telling the story, you check whether you're speaking from gratitude or from ego.
ramacharitamanas::4328.insight: It shifts attention from celebrating your own feat to speaking only from humility and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4329.verse_sanskrit: साखामग कै बड़ि मनुसाई। साखा तें साखा पर जाई॥ नाघि सिंधु हाटकपुर जारा। निसिचर गन बधि बिपिन उजारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4329.verse_hindi: बंदर का बस, यही बड़ा पुरुषार्थ है कि वह एक डाल से दूसरी डाल पर चला जाता है। मैंने जो समुद्र लाँघकर सोने का नगर जलाया और राक्षसगण को मारकर अशोक वन को उजाड़ डाला, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4329.english_translation: The great feat of a monkey is to leap from branch to branch. I crossed the ocean, burned the golden city, killed the demon hosts, and cleared the grove.
ramacharitamanas::4329.translation_literal: साखामग (branch-walker / monkey) / कै (of) / बड़ि (great) / मनुसाई (manliness / valor) / साखा (branch) / तें (from) / साखा (branch) / पर (onto) / जाई (goes) ॥ / नाघि (crossing) / सिंधु (the ocean) / हाटकपुर (golden city / Lanka) / जारा (burned) / निसिचर (demon beings) / गन (hosts) / बधि (killing) / बिपिन (grove / forest) / उजारा (laid waste) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4329.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4329.essence: Great deeds lose their shine when you refuse to call them yours.
ramacharitamanas::4329.simple_meaning: Hanuman says his real monkey strength is leaping from branch to branch, and everything else he did came from Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4329.simple_insight: Even great deeds can be held lightly when ego is absent.
ramacharitamanas::4329.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman has found Sita and ravaged Ravana's stronghold, he answers Ram with playful humility. He shrinks his own glory, calling branch-leaping the true greatness of a monkey, so that every heroic act points back to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4329.modern_relevance: You finish the hardest part of the project, and someone praises your brilliance. You know the truth: the real strength was never yours alone.
ramacharitamanas::4329.insight: It turns achievement into offering, not self-display.

ramacharitamanas::4330.verse_sanskrit: सो सब तव प्रताप रघुराई। नाथ न कछू मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4330.verse_hindi: यह सब तो हे श्री रघुनाथजी! आप ही का प्रताप है। हे नाथ! इसमें मेरी प्रभुता (बड़ाई) कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4330.english_translation: All of that is your power, O Raghuvir. Lord, none of it is my own greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4330.translation_literal: सो (that) / सब (all) / तव (your) / प्रताप (power, glory) / रघुराई (O Raghuvir) / नाथ (Lord) / न (not) / कछू (anything) / मोरि (my) / प्रभुताई (greatness, mastery)
ramacharitamanas::4330.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4330.essence: True power becomes devotion when you stop calling it your own.
ramacharitamanas::4330.simple_meaning: Hanuman gives all credit to Ram. He says the feat was possible only because of Ram's power, not his own greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4330.simple_insight: Real strength feels humble. The more clearly you see help, grace, and support, the less inflated you become.
ramacharitamanas::4330.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just described burning the city and defeating its guardians. Instead of claiming credit, he turns to Ram and says the achievement was entirely Ram's power. The scene turns victory into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4330.modern_relevance: You finish a project everyone praises, but you know the late-night help, the timing, and the support around you made it possible. Hanuman's response is the opposite of self-congratulation.
ramacharitamanas::4330.insight: It shifts credit away from the separate self and back toward the source of strength.
