ramacharitamanas::4331.verse_sanskrit: ता कहुँ प्रभु कछु अगम नहिं जा पर तुम्ह अनुकूल। तव प्रभावँ बड़वानलहि जारि सकइ खलु तूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::4331.verse_hindi: हे प्रभु! जिस पर आप प्रसन्न हों, उसके लिए कुछ भी कठिन नहीं है। आपके प्रभाव से रूई (जो स्वयं बहुत जल्दी जल जाने वाली वस्तु है) बड़वानल को निश्चय ही जला सकती है (अर्थात् असंभव भी संभव हो सकता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4331.english_translation: For one who has your favor, nothing is impossible. By your power, even cotton can burn the ocean-fire.
ramacharitamanas::4331.translation_literal: ता (for that one) / कहुँ (for whom) / प्रभु (Lord) / कछु (anything) / अगम (hard to reach) / नहिं (not) / जा पर (on whom) / तुम्ह (you) / अनुकूल (favorable) / तव (your) / प्रभावँ (by power) / बड़वानलहि (the ocean-fire) / जारि सकइ (can burn) / खलु (indeed) / तूल (cotton)
ramacharitamanas::4331.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4331.essence: Ram's favor makes the impossible feel ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::4331.simple_meaning: When Ram is pleased, no task is too hard. His power can make even the impossible happen.
ramacharitamanas::4331.simple_insight: You can stop measuring your limits only by your own strength.
ramacharitamanas::4331.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has crossed the ocean, burned Lanka, and returned to praise Ram. After denying any personal greatness, he explains the real source of his success: Ram's favor. In this moment, Hanuman turns victory into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4331.modern_relevance: You are staring at a task everyone says cannot be done — a broken relationship, a failed plan, a deadline that feels too big. This verse reminds you that support, grace, and alignment can change what effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4331.insight: It shifts you from self-credit to trust in a power beyond ego.

ramacharitamanas::4332.verse_sanskrit: नाथ भगति अति सुखदायनी। देहु कृपा करि अनपायनी॥ सुनि प्रभु परम सरल कपि बानी। एवमस्तु तब कहेउ भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4332.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मुझे अत्यंत सुख देने वाली अपनी निश्चल भक्ति कृपा करके दीजिए। हनुमान् जी की अत्यंत सरल वाणी सुनकर, हे भवानी! तब प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4332.english_translation: O Lord, grant me your unfailing devotion, the one that gives the highest joy. Hearing Hanuman's utterly simple words, O Uma, the Lord said, "So be it."
ramacharitamanas::4332.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / भगति (devotion) / अति (very) / सुखदायनी (joy-giving) / देहु (give) / कृपा (grace) / करि (doing) / अनपायनी (unfailing) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (Lord) / परम (supremely) / सरल (simple) / कपि (monkey-devotee) / बानी (speech) / एवमस्तु (so be it) / तब (then) / कहेउ (said) / भवानी (O Uma)
ramacharitamanas::4332.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4332.essence: The purest request is for devotion itself.
ramacharitamanas::4332.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Ram for unwavering devotion, saying it is the greatest source of joy. Ram is pleased by Hanuman's simple, sincere words and grants the request.
ramacharitamanas::4332.simple_insight: The heart’s best request is not for power, but for a love that never breaks.
ramacharitamanas::4332.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ram after finding Sita. He does not ask for reward, victory, or praise. He asks only for devotion that cannot fail. Ram hears the purity of that request and immediately blesses it.
ramacharitamanas::4332.modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for what you want, and you stop reaching for status or control. What comes out is simpler: give me a heart that stays loyal.
ramacharitamanas::4332.insight: It shifts desire from outer gain to inner devotion, showing that the highest gift is a steady bond with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4333.verse_sanskrit: उमा राम सुभाउ जेहिं जाना। ताहि भजनु तजि भाव न आना॥ यह संबाद जासु उर आवा। रघुपति चरन भगति सोइ पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4333.verse_hindi: हे उमा! जिसने श्री रामजी का स्वभाव जान लिया, उसे भजन छोड़कर दूसरी बात ही नहीं सुहाती। यह स्वामी-सेवक का संवाद जिसके हृदय में आ गया, वही श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों की भक्ति पा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4333.english_translation: O Uma, whoever has understood Ram's nature finds no taste in anything except devotion. Whoever lets this exchange settle in the heart receives devotion at Raghupati's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4333.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma) / राम (Ram) / सुभाउ (nature) / जेहिं (whoever) / जाना (has known) / ताहि (for that one) / भजनु (devotion) / तजि (leaving) / भाव (liking/taste) / न (not) / आना (other) / यह (this) / संबाद (exchange/dialogue) / जासु (whose) / उर (heart) / आवा (came) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / चरन (feet) / भगति (devotion) / सोइ (that very one) / पावा (received)
ramacharitamanas::4333.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4333.essence: Seeing Ram clearly makes every other desire fade.
ramacharitamanas::4333.simple_meaning: When you truly understand Ram's nature, devotion stops feeling like a duty and becomes the only thing your heart wants. Letting this truth settle inside brings devotion at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::4333.simple_insight: Real understanding changes desire itself, until devotion feels natural and satisfying.
ramacharitamanas::4333.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has just asked for steadfast devotion, and Ram responds through the larger truth behind bhakti. Tulsidas now tells Uma that once Ram's nature is known, the heart loses interest in everything else and naturally turns to his feet.
ramacharitamanas::4333.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, kindness, and integrity quietly rearrange your priorities. After that, shallow thrills lose their pull, and loyalty starts to feel obvious.
ramacharitamanas::4333.insight: It shifts devotion from effortful practice to the natural result of clear recognition.

ramacharitamanas::4334.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन कहहिं कपि बृंदा। जय जय जय कृपाल सुखकंदा॥ तब रघुपति कपिपतिहि बोलावा। कहा चलैं कर करहु बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4334.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर वानरगण कहने लगे- कृपालु आनंदकंद श्री रामजी की जय हो जय हो, जय हो! तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने कपिराज सुग्रीव को बुलाया और कहा- चलने की तैयारी करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4334.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, the monkey hosts cried, “Victory, victory to the compassionate, bliss-filled one!” Then Raghupati called the lord of the monkeys and said, “Get ready to depart.”
ramacharitamanas::4334.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / बचन (words) / कहहिं (they say) / कपि बृंदा (the monkey hosts) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / कृपाल (compassionate) / सुखकंदा (bliss-source) / तब (then) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / कपिपतिहि (to the lord of monkeys) / बोलावा (called) / कहा (said) / चलैं (to go) / कर (make) / करहु (do) / बनावा (preparation)
ramacharitamanas::4334.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4334.essence: Devotion becomes action the moment Ram gives the word.
ramacharitamanas::4334.simple_meaning: The monkeys rejoice when Ram speaks, and Ram tells Sugriva to prepare to move.
ramacharitamanas::4334.simple_insight: Joy and readiness often arrive together when the right call is heard.
ramacharitamanas::4334.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman's message has reached the heart of the monkey army. They burst into praise, and Ram immediately turns that devotion into action by calling Sugriva and ordering preparations for departure.
ramacharitamanas::4334.modern_relevance: You get the message you were waiting for, and suddenly the room changes. Relief turns into motion, and everyone starts getting ready.
ramacharitamanas::4334.insight: It shifts the moment from celebration to decisive preparation.

ramacharitamanas::4335.verse_sanskrit: अब बिलंबु केह कारन कीजे। तुरंत कपिन्ह कहँ आयसु दीजे॥ कौतुक देखि सुमन बहु बरषी। नभ तें भवन चले सुर हरषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4335.verse_hindi: अब विलंब किस कारण किया जाए। वानरों को तुरंत आज्ञा दो। (भगवान् की) यह लीला (रावणवध की तैयारी) देखकर, बहुत से फूल बरसाकर और हर्षित होकर देवता आकाश से अपने-अपने लोक को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4335.english_translation: Why delay any longer? Give the monkeys their orders at once. Seeing this divine play, many devas showered flowers and, delighted, returned to their own realms from the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4335.translation_literal: अब (now) / बिलंबु (delay) / केह कारन (for what reason) / कीजे (should be made) / तुरंत (at once) / कपिन्ह (to the monkeys) / कहँ (to) / आयसु (order) / दीजे (give) / कौतुक (wonder/play) / देखि (seeing) / सुमन (flowers) / बहु (many) / बरषी (showered) / नभ तें (from the sky) / भवन (to their realms) / चले (went) / सुर (devas) / हरषी (delighted)
ramacharitamanas::4335.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4335.essence: The right moment has come; delay only breaks the momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4335.simple_meaning: There is no reason to wait now. The army should be sent immediately, and the devas, delighted by the divine play, shower flowers and leave.
ramacharitamanas::4335.simple_insight: When the moment is ripe, hesitation only dilutes the force of right action.
ramacharitamanas::4335.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, the turning point has arrived after the revelation of Sita’s condition and Ram’s next move. The court of allies is ready, the devas watch in joy, and the story shifts from search to decisive action.
ramacharitamanas::4335.modern_relevance: You’ve already gathered the team, checked the plan, and waited long enough at the door. At some point, delaying again only weakens what is ready to move.
ramacharitamanas::4335.insight: It shifts attention from waiting to immediate execution once the right moment has arrived.

ramacharitamanas::4336.verse_sanskrit: कपिपति बेगि बोलाए आए जूथप जूथ। नाना बरन अतुल बल बानर भालु बरूथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4336.verse_hindi: वानरराज सुग्रीव ने शीघ्र ही वानरों को बुलाया, सेनापतियों के समूह आ गए। वानर-भालुओं के झुंड अनेक रंगों के हैं और उनमें अतुलनीय बल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4336.english_translation: Sugriva quickly summoned the monkey chiefs, and the troop leaders arrived. The monkey and bear bands were of many colors and had unmatched strength.
ramacharitamanas::4336.translation_literal: कपिपति (the lord of monkeys) / बेगि (quickly) / बोलाए (called) / आए (came) / जूथप (troop leaders) / जूथ (troops) / नाना (many) / बरन (colors) / अतुल (unmatched) / बल (strength) / बानर (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / बरूथ (bands)
ramacharitamanas::4336.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4336.essence: A mission begins when many strengths gather at once.
ramacharitamanas::4336.simple_meaning: Sugriva quickly calls the leaders, and the monkey and bear armies gather in many colors and great strength.
ramacharitamanas::4336.simple_insight: Great tasks begin when the right people are gathered quickly.
ramacharitamanas::4336.detailed_meaning: After Ram asks for action, Sugriva immediately summons the monkey chiefs. The commanders and their mixed troops of monkeys and bears arrive in force, setting the stage for the march against Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4336.modern_relevance: A group chat lights up, and within minutes the right people are on the road, carrying tools, snacks, and urgency. Big work moves when everyone answers at once.
ramacharitamanas::4336.insight: It shows how decisive leadership turns scattered allies into a ready force.

ramacharitamanas::4337.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पद पंकज नावहिं सीसा। गर्जहिं भालु महाबल कीसा॥ देखी राम सकल कपि सेना। चितइ कृपा करि राजिव नैना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4337.verse_hindi: वे प्रभु के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाते हैं। महान् बलवान् रीछ और वानर गरज रहे हैं। श्री रामजी ने वानरों की सारी सेना देखी। तब कमल नेत्रों से कृपापूर्वक उनकी ओर दृष्टि डाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4337.english_translation: They bow their heads at the Lord's lotus feet. The mighty bears and monkeys roar. Seeing the whole monkey army, Ram looked upon them with compassionate lotus eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4337.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / नावहिं (bow) / सीसा (heads) / गर्जहिं (roar) / भालु (bears) / महाबल (great strength) / कीसा (monkeys) / देखी (seeing) / राम (Ram) / सकल (entire) / कपि (monkey) / सेना (army) / चितइ (looking) / कृपा (compassion) / करि (doing) / राजिव (lotus) / नैना (eyes)
ramacharitamanas::4337.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4337.essence: Strength becomes complete when it meets compassionate regard.
ramacharitamanas::4337.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army bows to Ram, roars with strength, and Ram looks at them with kindness.
ramacharitamanas::4337.simple_insight: Even great strength feels complete when it bows to compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4337.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has returned, and Ram is preparing the army for the final march. The bears and monkeys bow before him, roaring with confidence, while Ram receives them with mercy. It is a brief scene of devotion before action.
ramacharitamanas::4337.modern_relevance: Before the team walks into the big presentation, everyone is keyed up and ready. The strongest person in the room still needs to be seen with kindness, not just used for their power.
ramacharitamanas::4337.insight: It shifts attention from raw force to the grace that gathers and directs it.

ramacharitamanas::4338.verse_sanskrit: राम कृपा बल पाइ कपिंदा। भए पच्छजुत मनहुँ गिरिंदा॥ हरषि राम तब कीन्ह पयाना। सगुन भए सुंदर सुभ नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4338.verse_hindi: राम कृपा का बल पाकर श्रेष्ठ वानर मानो पंखवाले बड़े पर्वत हो गए। तब श्री रामजी ने हर्षित होकर प्रस्थान (कूच) किया। अनेक सुंदर और शुभ शकुन हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4338.english_translation: Having received the strength of Ram's grace, the chief monkeys became like great mountains with wings. Then Ram set out in joy, and many beautiful, auspicious signs appeared.
ramacharitamanas::4338.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / बल (strength) / पाइ (having received) / कपिंदा (chief monkeys) / भए (became) / पच्छजुत (with wings) / मनहुँ (as if) / गिरिंदा (great mountains) / हरषि (rejoicing) / राम (Ram) / तब (then) / कीन्ह (made/did) / पयाना (departure) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / भए (became) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुभ (auspicious) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::4338.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4338.essence: Grace makes small strength feel mountain-sized.
ramacharitamanas::4338.simple_meaning: Ram's grace gives the monkeys such strength that they seem like winged mountains. Then Ram departs happily, and auspicious signs appear everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::4338.simple_insight: Grace can turn ordinary strength into something vast and fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4338.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, the monkey army has gathered around Ram before the march forward. Tulsidas shows their power as coming not from pride or training alone, but from Ram's grace. The scene then shifts to Ram's joyful departure, marked by auspicious signs.
ramacharitamanas::4338.modern_relevance: A team walks into a hard meeting after weeks of preparation. The room still feels heavy, but something bigger than nerves is carrying them now.
ramacharitamanas::4338.insight: It shifts attention from personal ability to the empowering force behind it.

ramacharitamanas::4339.verse_sanskrit: जासु सकल मंगलमय कीती। तासु पयान सगुन यह नीती॥ प्रभु पयान जाना बैदेहीं। फरकि बाम अँग जनु कहि देहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4339.verse_hindi: जिनकी कीर्ति सब मंगलों से पूर्ण है, उनके प्रस्थान के समय शकुन होना, यह नीति है (लीला की मर्यादा है)। प्रभु का प्रस्थान जानकीजी ने भी जान लिया। उनके बाएँ अंग फड़क-फड़ककर मानो कहे देते थे (कि श्री रामजी आ रहे हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4339.english_translation: For one whose fame is full of every blessing, auspicious signs accompany departure by nature. Janaki knew the Lord was leaving; her left side fluttered as if announcing his arrival.
ramacharitamanas::4339.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / सकल (all) / मंगलमय (filled with auspiciousness) / कीती (fame, glory) / तासु (for that one) / पयान (departure, going) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / यह (this) / नीती (custom, rule)॥ / प्रभु (Lord) / पयान (departure) / जाना (knew) / बैदेहीं (Janaki) / फरकि (fluttered) / बाम अँग (left side) / जनु (as if) / कहि देहीं (were saying) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4339.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4339.essence: Ram's presence is so complete that even departure feels auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::4339.simple_meaning: Ram's departure is naturally accompanied by auspicious signs. Sita senses his leaving immediately, and even her body seems to announce his arrival.
ramacharitamanas::4339.simple_insight: Love can recognize the beloved before the mind catches up.
ramacharitamanas::4339.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Ram is about to move forward after seeing Hanuman's army. Tulsidas pauses on a devotional detail: Ram's very departure draws auspicious signs, and Sita feels it instantly in her body. The verse shows the hidden connection between them.
ramacharitamanas::4339.modern_relevance: You are halfway across the city when your phone buzzes and you already know who it is. Some people carry a presence that announces itself before they arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4339.insight: It teaches you to notice how deep connection can be felt before it is explained.

ramacharitamanas::4340.verse_sanskrit: जोइ जोइ सगुन जानकिहि होई। असगुन भयउ रावनहिं सोई॥ चला कटकु को बरनैं पारा। गर्जहिं बानर भालु अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4340.verse_hindi: जानकीजी को जो-जो शकुन होते थे, वही-वही रावण के लिए अपशकुन हुए। सेना चली, उसका वर्णन कौन कर सकता है? असंख्य वानर और भालू गर्जना कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4340.english_translation: Whatever signs were auspicious for Sita became inauspicious for Ravana. The army marched on—who could describe it? Countless monkeys and bears roared.
ramacharitamanas::4340.translation_literal: जोइ (whatever) / जोइ (whatever) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / जानकिहि (for Janaki/Sita) / होई (happened) / असगुन (inauspicious signs) / भयउ (became) / रावनहिं (for Ravana) / सोई (that same)॥ / चला (moved) / कटकु (army) / को (who) / बरनैं (to describe) / पारा (was able) / गर्जहिं (roared) / बानर (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / अपारा (countless)॥
ramacharitamanas::4340.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4340.essence: One event can become blessing or warning depending on your side.
ramacharitamanas::4340.simple_meaning: What is lucky for Sita becomes a bad sign for Ravana. Then the army moves forward, with countless monkeys and bears roaring loudly.
ramacharitamanas::4340.simple_insight: The same moment can bless one side and undo the other.
ramacharitamanas::4340.detailed_meaning: As Ram's army prepares to advance toward Lanka, the mood splits in two: Sita's signs turn hopeful, while Ravana's turn ominous. The verse then swells into a battlefield roar, with monkey and bear ranks surging forward.
ramacharitamanas::4340.modern_relevance: A room can feel like victory to one person and warning to another. The same meeting, the same news, the same moment lands very differently depending on what you stand for.
ramacharitamanas::4340.insight: It frames the march to battle as a turning point where fate favors dharma and unsettles ego.

ramacharitamanas::4341.verse_sanskrit: नख आयुध गिरि पादपधारी। चले गगन महि इच्छाचारी॥ केहरिनाद भालु कपि करहीं। डगमगाहिं दिग्गज चिक्करहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4341.verse_hindi: नख ही जिनके शस्त्र हैं, वे इच्छानुसार (सर्वत्र बेरोक-टोक) चलने वाले रीछ-वानर पर्वतों और वृक्षों को धारण किए कोई आकाश मार्ग से और कोई पृथ्वी पर चले जा रहे हैं। वे सिंह के समान गर्जना कर रहे हैं। (उनके चलने और गर्जने से) दिशाओं के हाथी विचलित होकर चिंग्घाड़ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4341.english_translation: Their only weapons are their nails; they carry mountains and trees. Some move through the sky, some across the earth, all at will. The bears and monkeys roar like lions, and the elephants of the directions tremble and cry out.
ramacharitamanas::4341.translation_literal: नख (nails) / आयुध (weapons) / गिरि (mountain) / पादप (tree) / धारी (bearing) / चले (moved) / गगन (sky) / महि (earth) / इच्छाचारी (moving at will) / केहरि-नाद (lion-roar) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / करहीं (make) / डगमगाहिं (tremble) / दिग्गज (direction-elephants) / चिक्करहीं (cry out)
ramacharitamanas::4341.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4341.essence: Power is already moving before the fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::4341.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army moves in wild force, carrying mountains and trees, roaring so loudly that even the directions tremble.
ramacharitamanas::4341.simple_insight: Some forces announce themselves so fully that the whole world seems to shake.
ramacharitamanas::4341.detailed_meaning: Hanuman’s army has gathered for the march to Lanka. These lines do not teach a doctrine; they build the scene with thunderous motion, showing the bears and monkeys advancing with raw, unstoppable energy before the battle begins.
ramacharitamanas::4341.modern_relevance: A stadium erupts before the final play, and the noise rolls through your chest. Before anything has even happened, you can feel a turning point arriving.
ramacharitamanas::4341.insight: It heightens the sense of collective momentum, preparing the reader for the battle that follows.

ramacharitamanas::4342.verse_sanskrit: चिक्करहिं दिग्गज डोल महि गिरि लोल सागर खरभरे। मन हरष सभ गंधर्ब सुर मुनि नाग किंनर दुख टरे॥ कटकटहिं मर्कट बिकट भट बहु कोटि कोटिन्ह धावहीं। जय राम प्रबल प्रताप कोसलनाथ गुन गन गावहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4342.verse_hindi: दिशाओं के हाथी चिंग्घाड़ने लगे, पृथ्वी डोलने लगी, पर्वत चंचल हो गए (काँपने लगे) और समुद्र खलबला उठे। गंधर्व, देवता, मुनि, नाग, किन्नर सब के सब मन में हर्षित हुए' कि (अब) हमारे दुःख टल गए। अनेकों करोड़ भयानक वानर योद्धा कटकटा रहे हैं और करोड़ों ही दौड़ रहे हैं। 'प्रबल प्रताप कोसलनाथ श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो' ऐसा पुकारते हुए वे उनके गुणसमूहों को गा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4342.english_translation: The guardian elephants of the directions cried out, the earth shook, the mountains trembled, and the ocean churned. Gandharvas, radiant beings, sages, serpents, and kinnaras rejoiced that their suffering had ended. Countless fierce monkey-warriors roared and rushed forward by the millions, singing the glory of the mighty Lord of Kosala, Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4342.translation_literal: चिक्करहिं (cry out) / दिग्गज (guardian elephants of the directions) / डोल (shook) / महि (earth) / गिरि (mountains) / लोल (trembling) / सागर (ocean) / खरभरे (churned violently) / मन (in the mind) / हरष (rejoiced) / सभ (all) / गंधर्ब (Gandharvas) / सुर (radiant beings) / मुनि (sages) / नाग (serpents) / किंनर (kinnaras) / दुख (suffering) / टरे (ended) / कटकटहिं (roar) / मर्कट (monkey warriors) / बिकट (fierce) / भट (warriors) / बहु (many) / कोटि कोटिन्ह (millions and millions) / धावहीं (rush) / जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / प्रबल (mighty) / प्रताप (glory) / कोसलनाथ (Lord of Kosala) / गुन गन (clusters of qualities) / गावहीं (sing)
ramacharitamanas::4342.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4342.essence: Ram's arrival makes the whole world feel alive with victory.
ramacharitamanas::4342.simple_meaning: Nature and the heavenly beings react as Ram's army advances. The world shakes with the force of the march, while the warriors sing Ram's praise.
ramacharitamanas::4342.simple_insight: When your purpose is clear, even the world around you seems to move with you.
ramacharitamanas::4342.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has already leapt into Lanka and Ram's great army is now advancing. The scale is cosmic: elephants, mountains, and ocean all seem to tremble, while gods and sages rejoice. This verse amplifies the power and joy surrounding Ram's march.
ramacharitamanas::4342.modern_relevance: A stadium erupts, the floor vibrates, and a whole crowd starts chanting one name together. You can feel how shared conviction turns motion into momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4342.insight: It turns a march into a public hymn, showing that true force carries devotion, not just power.

ramacharitamanas::4343.verse_sanskrit: सहि सक न भार उदार अहिपति बार बारहिं मोहई। गह दसन पुनि पुनि कमठ पृष्ठ कठोर सो किमि सोहई॥ रघुबीर रुचिर प्रयान प्रस्थिति जानि परम सुहावनी। जनु कमठ खर्पर सर्पराज सो लिखत अबिचल पावनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4343.verse_hindi: उदार (परम श्रेष्ठ एवं महान् ) सर्पराज शेषजी भी सेना का बोझ नहीं सह सकते, वे बार-बार मोहित हो जाते (घबड़ा जाते) हैं और पुनः-पुनः कच्छप की कठोर पीठ को दाँतों से पकड़ते हैं। ऐसा करते (अर्थात् बार-बार दाँतों को गड़ाकर कच्छप की पीठ पर लकीर सी खींचते हुए) वे कैसे शोभा दे रहे हैं मानो श्री रामचंद्रजी की सुंदर प्रस्थान यात्रा को परम सुहावनी जानकर उसकी अचल पवित्र कथा को सर्पराज शेषजी कच्छप की पीठ पर लिख रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4343.english_translation: The noble king of serpents cannot bear the army's weight; again and again he is bewildered. He bites the tortoise's back, and how does that hard back look beautiful? It is as if, knowing the exquisitely lovely march of Raghubir, the serpent king Shesha is writing that immovable, holy account on the tortoise's shell.
ramacharitamanas::4343.translation_literal: सहि सक (can bear) / न (not) / भार (weight) / उदार (noble) / अहिपति (king of serpents) / बार बारहिं (again and again) / मोहई (is bewildered) / गह (grasping) / दसन (teeth) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कमठ (tortoise) / पृष्ठ (back) / कठोर (hard) / सो (that) / किमि (how) / सोहई (looks beautiful) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / रुचिर (lovely) / प्रयान (march) / प्रस्थिति (departure / progress) / जानि (knowing) / परम (supremely) / सुहावनी (beautiful) / जनु (as if) / कमठ (tortoise) / खर्पर (shell / back) / सर्पराज (king of serpents) / सो (that) / लिखत (writing) / अबिचल (immovable) / पावनी (holy)
ramacharitamanas::4343.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4343.essence: Even the cosmos tries to preserve Ram's departure as holy memory.
ramacharitamanas::4343.simple_meaning: Shesha, the king of serpents, is overwhelmed by Ram's grand departure. The verse imagines him marking that holy event on the tortoise's back, as if preserving its beauty forever.
ramacharitamanas::4343.simple_insight: Some moments are so sacred that even the impossible feels like a way to remember them.
ramacharitamanas::4343.detailed_meaning: As Ram begins his beautiful journey toward the sea, the whole world seems to tremble with wonder. Tulsidas imagines Shesha, the serpent king, so moved that he keeps biting the tortoise's back, as if writing Ram's holy march into the world itself.
ramacharitamanas::4343.modern_relevance: You watch a loved one leave for a life-changing journey, and you know words will never hold it. So you remember it in fragments, photos, and tiny rituals.
ramacharitamanas::4343.insight: It turns a physical image into devotion, showing how cosmic beings witness Ram's movement as sacred history.

ramacharitamanas::4344.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि जाइ कृपानिधि उतरे सागर तीर। जहँ तहँ लागे खान फल भालु बिपुल कपि बीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4344.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार कृपानिधान श्री रामजी समुद्र तट पर जा उतरे। अनेकों रीछ-वानर वीर जहाँ-तहाँ फल खाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4344.english_translation: In this way, the gracious one reached the shore of the ocean. There, the bears and many monkey warriors began eating fruit wherever they could.
ramacharitamanas::4344.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / जाइ (going) / कृपानिधि (treasury of grace) / उतरे (descended, arrived) / सागर (ocean) / तीर (shore) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / लागे (began) / खान (eating) / फल (fruit) / भालु (bears) / बिपुल (many, numerous) / कपि (monkeys) / बीर (warriors)
ramacharitamanas::4344.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4344.essence: Even after a great advance, the army pauses for ordinary relief.
ramacharitamanas::4344.simple_meaning: Ram reaches the ocean shore, and the bear and monkey warriors spread out to eat fruit.
ramacharitamanas::4344.simple_insight: After the strain of the march, even the warriors are allowed a simple breath.
ramacharitamanas::4344.detailed_meaning: Hanuman's great leap has already shaken the world, and Ram's army has finally reached the ocean shore. In this brief resting moment, the bear and monkey warriors scatter to eat fruit before the next decisive step toward Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4344.modern_relevance: You finally arrive after a long drive, drop your bags, and reach for the first snack you can find. The body needs its small relief before the next hard thing begins.
ramacharitamanas::4344.insight: It marks a pause in the journey, not the end of the mission.

ramacharitamanas::4345.verse_sanskrit: उहाँ निसाचर रहहिं ससंका। जब तें जारि गयउ कपि लंका॥ निज निज गृहँ सब करहिं बिचारा। नहिं निसिचर कुल केर उबारा।1॥
ramacharitamanas::4345.verse_hindi: वहाँ (लंका में) जब से हनुमान् जी लंका को जलाकर गए, तब से राक्षस भयभीत रहने लगे। अपने-अपने घरों में सब विचार करते हैं कि अब राक्षस कुल की रक्षा (का कोई उपाय) नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4345.english_translation: After Hanuman burned Lanka, the night-dwellers lived in fear. In their own homes, they kept thinking there was no way to save their clan.
ramacharitamanas::4345.translation_literal: उहाँ (there) / निसाचर (night-dwellers) / रहहिं (remain) / ससंका (fearful) / जब तें (since the time) / जारि (burning) / गयउ (went) / कपि (the monkey) / लंका (Lanka)॥ / निज निज (each one's own) / गृहँ (home) / सब (all) / करहिं (do) / बिचारा (thinking) / नहिं (not) / निसिचर (night-dwellers) / कुल (clan) / केर (of) / उबारा (protection)॥
ramacharitamanas::4345.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4345.essence: A single fearless act can expose an entire kingdom’s weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4345.simple_meaning: Hanuman’s burning of Lanka leaves the night-dwellers terrified and worried that their clan has no protection left.
ramacharitamanas::4345.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast when a single force exposes how fragile power really is.
ramacharitamanas::4345.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman’s fire has already shaken the city. The night-dwellers hide in their homes, stunned and afraid, realizing that even their own side cannot protect them now. This verse sets up the panic before Ravana’s court responds.
ramacharitamanas::4345.modern_relevance: A company’s biggest team player quits, and suddenly everyone in the building feels exposed. The real shock is not the loss itself, but the feeling that the old safety was never solid.
ramacharitamanas::4345.insight: It shifts attention from outward strength to the insecurity underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::4346.verse_sanskrit: जासु दूत बल बरनि न जाई। तेहि आएँ पुर कवन भलाई॥ दूतिन्ह सन सुनि पुरजन बानी। मंदोदरी अधिक अकुलानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4346.verse_hindi: जिसके दूत का बल वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, उसके स्वयं नगर में आने पर कौन भलाई है (हम लोगों की बड़ी बुरी दशा होगी)? दूतियों से नगरवासियों के वचन सुनकर मंदोदरी बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4346.english_translation: The strength of that messenger cannot even be described. If he himself has come to the city, what good can possibly remain? Hearing the city's words from the female messengers, Mandodari became deeply distressed.
ramacharitamanas::4346.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / दूत (messenger) / बल (strength) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be done) / तेहि (that one) / आएँ (having come) / पुर (city) / कवन (what) / भलाई (good) / दूतिन्ह (from the female messengers) / सन (from) / सुनि (hearing) / पुरजन (city-dwellers) / बानी (words) / मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / अधिक (very much) / अकुलानी (became distressed)
ramacharitamanas::4346.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4346.essence: When the messenger is unstoppable, the city’s fear is justified.
ramacharitamanas::4346.simple_meaning: Mandodari hears that Hanuman is a messenger so powerful that his strength cannot be described. His arrival inside Lanka feels like a sign that disaster is already at the door.
ramacharitamanas::4346.simple_insight: Fear grows fast when you realise the danger is not distant anymore.
ramacharitamanas::4346.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman has burned the city, the demons are still shaken. News spreads through the women of the palace that this messenger's power is beyond description. Mandodari hears it and panics, sensing that Ravana's city is no longer safe.
ramacharitamanas::4346.modern_relevance: You hear that the one person who already exposed every weakness is walking into the meeting. Suddenly everyone in the room knows the situation has changed.
ramacharitamanas::4346.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary alarm to the recognition that a decisive force has already entered the scene.

ramacharitamanas::4347.verse_sanskrit: रहसि जोरि कर पति पग लागी। बोली बचन नीति रस पागी॥ कंत करष हरि सन परिहरहू। मोर कहा अति हित हियँ धरहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4347.verse_hindi: वह एकांत में हाथ जोड़कर पति (रावण) के चरणों लगी और नीतिरस में पगी हुई वाणी बोली- हे प्रियतम! श्री हरि से विरोध छोड़ दीजिए। मेरे कहने को अत्यंत ही हितकर जानकर हृदय में धारण कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4347.english_translation: In private, she joined her hands and fell at her husband's feet. Filled with wise feeling, she spoke: “Dear one, give up hostility toward Hari. Take my words as deeply beneficial and keep them in your heart.”
ramacharitamanas::4347.translation_literal: रहसि (in private) / जोरि (joining) / कर (hands) / पति (husband) / पग (feet) / लागी (fell at) / बोली (spoke) / बचन (words) / नीति (wise conduct) / रस (essence) / पागी (filled) / कंत (beloved) / करष (hostility) / हरि (Hari) / सन (with) / परिहरहू (give up) / मोर (my) / कहा (words) / अति (very) / हित (beneficial) / हियँ (in heart) / धरहू (hold)
ramacharitamanas::4347.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4347.essence: True care tells you to drop the fight that is destroying you.
ramacharitamanas::4347.simple_meaning: Mandodari privately begs Ravana to stop opposing Ram and to take her warning seriously as loving, useful counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4347.simple_insight: Love sometimes sounds like warning. Real care tells you the truth before it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4347.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman’s terrifying visit, Mandodari speaks to Ravana in private. She bows at his feet and urges him to stop fighting Ram. Her words are not anger but clear-eyed concern for his ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4347.modern_relevance: You watch a friend double down on a choice that is clearly breaking their life. Speaking gently may be the most loving thing you can do, even if they resist it.
ramacharitamanas::4347.insight: It teaches you to recognise wise counsel as an act of care, not control.

ramacharitamanas::4348.verse_sanskrit: समुझत जासु दूत कइ करनी। स्रवहिं गर्भ रजनीचर घरनी॥ तासु नारि निज सचिव बोलाई। पठवहु कंत जो चहहु भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4348.verse_hindi: जिनके दूत की करनी का विचार करते ही (स्मरण आते ही) राक्षसों की स्त्रियों के गर्भ गिर जाते हैं, हे प्यारे स्वामी! यदि भला चाहते हैं, तो अपने मंत्री को बुलाकर उसके साथ उनकी स्त्री को भेज दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4348.english_translation: Just thinking of what this messenger has done makes the women of the demon households miscarry. Dear lord, if you want what is good, call your minister and send his wife along with him.
ramacharitamanas::4348.translation_literal: समुझत (thinking) / जासु (whose) / दूत (messenger) / कइ (of) / करनी (deed) / स्रवहिं (flow away) / गर्भ (wombs) / रजनीचर (demon-folk) / घरनी (women) / तासु (his) / नारि (wife) / निज (own) / सचिव (minister) / बोलाई (calling) / पठवहु (send) / कंत (lord) / जो (who) / चहहु (you want) / भलाई (good)
ramacharitamanas::4348.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4348.essence: Ignoring a clear warning only makes the fall harder.
ramacharitamanas::4348.simple_meaning: Even the memory of this messenger's power is terrifying. Mandodari urges Ravana to send Sita back with his minister if he wants safety.
ramacharitamanas::4348.simple_insight: Pride narrows judgment until danger becomes obvious too late.
ramacharitamanas::4348.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari sees what Ravana refuses to see: Hanuman is no ordinary envoy. She warns that even his mere deed has shaken demon households, and she pleads for a practical escape before disaster deepens.
ramacharitamanas::4348.modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the warning signs because admitting them would bruise your pride. Someone close to you sees the danger first and begs you to act before the damage spreads.
ramacharitamanas::4348.insight: It shows how ego blocks clear seeing, even when the threat is already undeniable.

ramacharitamanas::4349.verse_sanskrit: तव कुल कमल बिपिन दुखदाई। सीता सीत निसा सम आई॥ सुनहु नाथ सीता बिनु दीन्हें। हित न तुम्हार संभु अज कीन्हें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4349.verse_hindi: सीता आपके कुल रूपी कमलों के वन को दुःख देने वाली जाड़े की रात्रि के समान आई है। हे नाथ। सुनिए, सीता को दिए (लौटाए) बिना शम्भु और ब्रह्मा के किए भी आपका भला नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4349.english_translation: Sita has come like a winter night, bringing sorrow to your lotus-forest of a lineage. Listen, lord: without giving Sita back, even Shiva and Brahma cannot bring you true welfare.
ramacharitamanas::4349.translation_literal: तव (your) / कुल (lineage) / कमल (lotus) / बिपिन (forest) / दुखदाई (sorrow-giving) / सीता (Sita) / सीत (cold) / निसा (night) / सम (like) / आई (came) / सुनहु (listen) / नाथ (lord) / सीता (Sita) / बिनु (without) / दीन्हें (giving back) / हित (welfare) / न (not) / तुम्हार (your) / संभु (Shiva) / अज (Brahma) / कीन्हें (done)
ramacharitamanas::4349.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4349.essence: No blessing can grow from a stolen wrong.
ramacharitamanas::4349.simple_meaning: Mandodari warns Ravana that Sita has brought sorrow to his family line, and no blessing can come until he returns her.
ramacharitamanas::4349.simple_insight: A stolen gain can never become a lasting gain. Relief begins when you undo the harm.
ramacharitamanas::4349.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari is trying to shake Ravana out of his pride. She says Sita has brought misery to his lineage like a cold night in a lotus grove, and even the highest powers cannot help him unless he returns her.
ramacharitamanas::4349.modern_relevance: You know the feeling of winning something and then sleeping badly because you got it the wrong way. The relief does not come from defending the mistake. It comes from undoing it.
ramacharitamanas::4349.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to a wrongful gain toward restoring what was taken.

ramacharitamanas::4350.verse_sanskrit: राम बान अहि गन सरिस निकर निसाचर भेक। जब लगि ग्रसत न तब लगि जतनु करहु तजि टेक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4350.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के बाण सर्पों के समूह के समान हैं और राक्षसों के समूह मेंढक के समान। जब तक वे इन्हें ग्रस नहीं लेते (निगल नहीं जाते) तब तक हठ छोड़कर उपाय कर लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4350.english_translation: Ram's arrows are like a flock of snakes, and the demons are like frogs. Before they are swallowed up, abandon stubbornness and make peace with what must be done.
ramacharitamanas::4350.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बान (arrows) / अहि (snakes) / गन (group) / सरिस (like) / निकर (flock) / निसाचर (demons) / भेक (frogs) / जब (when) / लगि (until) / ग्रसत (swallowing) / न (not) / तब (then) / लगि (until) / जतनु (effort) / करहु (do) / तजि (leaving) / टेक (stubbornness)
ramacharitamanas::4350.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4350.essence: Stubbornness only makes the blow harder to bear.
ramacharitamanas::4350.simple_meaning: Ram's power is overwhelming. The wise response is not stubbornness, but quick, practical action before destruction arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4350.simple_insight: You don't need to win by force of ego. You need to respond clearly before things harden.
ramacharitamanas::4350.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned about Ram's unstoppable power. The image is brutal: Ram's arrows are snakes, and the demons are frogs. The verse urges him to drop pride and act wisely before it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4350.modern_relevance: You keep arguing in a text thread long after the room has already turned against you. The smarter move is to stop defending your ego and deal with the real problem.
ramacharitamanas::4350.insight: It shifts you from prideful resistance to timely, practical response.

ramacharitamanas::4351.verse_sanskrit: श्रवन सुनी सठ ता करि बानी। बिहसा जगत बिदित अभिमानी॥ सभय सुभाउ नारि कर साचा। मंगल महुँ भय मन अति काचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4351.verse_hindi: मूर्ख और जगत प्रसिद्ध अभिमानी रावण कानों से उसकी वाणी सुनकर खूब हँसा (और बोला-) स्त्रियों का स्वभाव सचमुच ही बहुत डरपोक होता है। मंगल में भी भय करती हो। तुम्हारा मन (हृदय) बहुत ही कच्चा (कमजोर) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4351.english_translation: The arrogant Ravana, famous across the world, heard her words and laughed. He said, 'Women are naturally timid. Even in a place of good fortune, you are afraid. Your heart is very weak.'
ramacharitamanas::4351.translation_literal: श्रवन (with ears) / सुनी (having heard) / सठ (foolish one) / ता करि (that) / बानी (speech) / बिहसा (laughed) / जगत बिदित (world-famous) / अभिमानी (proud) / सभय (fearful) / सुभाउ (nature) / नारि (woman) / कर (of) / साचा (true) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / महुँ (in) / भय (fear) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / काचा (unripe/weak)
ramacharitamanas::4351.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4351.essence: Pride laughs at what it cannot understand.
ramacharitamanas::4351.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Sita's fear and dismisses her courage as weakness. His pride blinds him to her strength and to the danger closing in on him.
ramacharitamanas::4351.simple_insight: Pride makes you misread courage as weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4351.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just spoken with quiet resolve, warning Ravana that her rescue is coming. Ravana, the proud king who thinks himself beyond challenge, laughs at her words instead of hearing them. His mockery reveals how deeply ego distorts judgment.
ramacharitamanas::4351.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your concern in a meeting with a smirk, calling you overreactive. The real issue is not your fear — it's their refusal to see what is already obvious.
ramacharitamanas::4351.insight: It shows how ego turns a warning into a joke and blocks clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4352.verse_sanskrit: जौं आवइ मर्कट कटकाई। जिअहिं बिचारे निसिचर खाई॥ कंपहिं लोकप जाकीं त्रासा। तासु नारि सभीत बड़ि हासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4352.verse_hindi: यदि वानरों की सेना आवेगी तो बेचारे राक्षस उसे खाकर अपना जीवन निर्वाह करेंगे। लोकपाल भी जिसके डर से काँपते हैं, उसकी स्त्री डरती हो, यह बड़ी हँसी की बात है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4352.english_translation: If the monkey army comes, the poor demons will have to eat them to stay alive. The wife of one whom even the guardians of the worlds fear—how could she possibly be afraid? What a joke.
ramacharitamanas::4352.translation_literal: जौं (if) / आवइ (comes) / मर्कट (monkeys) / कटकाई (army) / जिअहिं (they live) / बिचारे (poor) / निसिचर (demons) / खाई (eating) / कंपहिं (tremble) / लोकप (guardians of the worlds) / जाकीं (whose) / त्रासा (fear) / तासु (of that one) / नारि (wife) / सभीत (afraid) / बड़ि (great) / हासा (laughter / joke)
ramacharitamanas::4352.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4352.essence: Pride turns warning into a joke and blinds you to danger.
ramacharitamanas::4352.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman's threat. He says the monkey army is so small that the demons could swallow it, and Sita could never be afraid of someone who frightens even the guardians of the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::4352.simple_insight: Arrogance makes danger look ridiculous right before it strikes.
ramacharitamanas::4352.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just heard Hanuman's warning and laughs it off in front of his court. He treats the monkey army as food for his demons and dismisses Sita's fear as impossible, exposing the pride that blinds him before disaster.
ramacharitamanas::4352.modern_relevance: You brush off the warning because the problem looks too small to matter. Then it grows teeth, and your confidence was the first thing it ate.
ramacharitamanas::4352.insight: It shows how pride distorts judgment, making real danger seem laughable until it is too late.

ramacharitamanas::4353.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि बिहसि ताहि उर लाई। चलेउ सभाँ ममता अधिकाई॥ फमंदोदरी हृदयँ कर चिंता। भयउ कंत पर बिधि बिपरीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4353.verse_hindi: रावण ने ऐसा कहकर हँसकर उसे हृदय से लगा लिया और ममता बढ़ाकर (अधिक स्नेह दर्शाकर) वह सभा में चला गया। मंदोदरी हृदय में चिंता करने लगी कि पति पर विधाता प्रतिकूल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4353.english_translation: Ravana said this, laughed, and drew her close to his chest. Then, with even more affection, he went back to the court. Mandodari felt worry in her heart: fate had turned against her husband.
ramacharitamanas::4353.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / बिहसि (laughing) / ताहि (her) / उर (to the chest) / लाई (brought) / चलेउ (went) / सभाँ (to the court) / ममता (affection) / अधिकाई (increased) / फमंदोदरी (Mandodari) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / कर (of) / चिंता (worry) / भयउ (became) / कंत (husband) / पर (upon) / बिधि (fate) / बिपरीता (turned adverse)
ramacharitamanas::4353.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4353.essence: Pride keeps smiling even as ruin begins.
ramacharitamanas::4353.simple_meaning: Ravana laughs off the warning, holds Mandodari close, and returns to the court. She alone feels the unease: something has already turned against him.
ramacharitamanas::4353.simple_insight: Pride can look like confidence right before it becomes blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4353.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana dismisses the warning with a laugh and goes back to his court, still wrapped in misplaced affection and self-confidence. Mandodari sees what he cannot: the turning of fate and the shadow gathering over him.
ramacharitamanas::4353.modern_relevance: You brush off the one warning that matters, smile through it, and walk back into the meeting pretending nothing is wrong. Someone beside you can already feel the collapse coming.
ramacharitamanas::4353.insight: It shows how ego can stay cheerful while reality is already closing in.

ramacharitamanas::4354.verse_sanskrit: बैठेउ सभाँ खबरि असि पाई। सिंधु पार सेना सब आई॥ बूझेसि सचिव उचित मत कहहू। ते सब हँसे मष्ट करि रहहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4354.verse_hindi: ज्यों ही वह सभा में जाकर बैठा, उसने ऐसी खबर पाई कि शत्रु की सारी सेना समुद्र के उस पार आ गई है, उसने मंत्रियों से पूछा कि उचित सलाह कहिए (अब क्या करना चाहिए?)। तब वे सब हँसे और बोले कि चुप किए रहिए (इसमें सलाह की कौन सी बात है?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4354.english_translation: As soon as he sat in the assembly, he received the news that the entire army had crossed the ocean. He asked his ministers for proper advice, and they all laughed and said, 'Stay quiet—what advice is there in this?'
ramacharitamanas::4354.translation_literal: बैठेउ (sat) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / खबरि (news) / असि (such) / पाई (having received) / सिंधु (ocean) / पार (across) / सेना (army) / सब (all) / आई (has come) / बूझेसि (he asked) / सचिव (ministers) / उचित (proper) / मत (advice) / कहहू (tell) / ते (they) / सब (all) / हँसे (laughed) / मष्ट (silenced / hushed) / करि (having made) / रहहू (remain)
ramacharitamanas::4354.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4354.essence: A ruler in denial cannot summon wise counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4354.simple_meaning: Ravana hears that the enemy has crossed the ocean and asks for advice, but his ministers mock the situation instead of helping.
ramacharitamanas::4354.simple_insight: Panic gets worse when the people around you cannot face reality.
ramacharitamanas::4354.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sits in his court after hearing that Ram's army has reached the far shore. He turns to his ministers for counsel, but they respond with laughter and empty bravado. The moment shows a kingdom already failing before the battle begins.
ramacharitamanas::4354.modern_relevance: You finally open the group chat after a crisis hits, hoping someone has a plan. Instead, everyone jokes, deflects, and pretends the problem will vanish.
ramacharitamanas::4354.insight: It shows how denial in leadership turns danger into disaster.

ramacharitamanas::4355.verse_sanskrit: जितेहु सुरासुर तब श्रम नाहीं। नर बानर केहि लेखे माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4355.verse_hindi: आपने देवताओं और राक्षसों को जीत लिया, तब तो कुछ श्रम ही नहीं हुआ। फिर मनुष्य और वानर किस गिनती में हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4355.english_translation: You conquered gods and demons without strain. What are humans and monkeys to you?
ramacharitamanas::4355.translation_literal: जितेहु (you conquered) / सुरासुर (gods and demons) / तब (then) / श्रम (effort, strain) / नाहीं (not) / नर (humans) / बानर (monkeys) / केहि (what) / लेखे (count, account) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::4355.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4355.essence: Victory can become the reason you misjudge the next threat.
ramacharitamanas::4355.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that Hanuman and the vanara army are nothing compared with the beings he has already defeated.
ramacharitamanas::4355.simple_insight: Pride makes real danger look small until it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4355.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears that Ram's forces have reached the shore. Instead of fear, he answers with contempt, measuring the coming threat against his past victories over celestial beings. The line reveals his overconfidence just before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4355.modern_relevance: You brush off a problem because last month’s crisis felt worse. That same dismissal is often how bigger trouble slips in unnoticed.
ramacharitamanas::4355.insight: It exposes the blindness of ego: past success can make you underestimate the next challenge.

ramacharitamanas::4356.verse_sanskrit: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4356.verse_hindi: मंत्री, वैद्य और गुरु- ये तीन यदि (अप्रसन्नता के) भय या (लाभ की) आशा से (हित की बात न कहकर) प्रिय बोलते हैं (ठकुर सुहाती कहने लगते हैं), तो (क्रमशः) राज्य, शरीर और धर्म- इन तीन का शीघ्र ही नाश हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4356.english_translation: If ministers, doctors, and teachers speak only what is pleasing out of fear or hope of gain, then kingdom, body, and dharma quickly fall apart.
ramacharitamanas::4356.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / बैद (doctor) / गुर (teacher) / तीनि (three) / जौं (if) / प्रिय (pleasant) / बोलहिं (speak) / भय (fear) / आस (hope) / राज धर्म (kingdom-duty) / तन (body) / तीनि (three) / कर (of) / होइ (becomes) / बेगिहीं (quickly) / नास (destruction)
ramacharitamanas::4356.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4356.essence: Pleasing words from trusted guides can quietly ruin everything.
ramacharitamanas::4356.simple_meaning: People who should guide you must tell the truth, not just what feels nice. When they speak to please fear or gain, leadership, health, and right conduct suffer.
ramacharitamanas::4356.simple_insight: Real care sometimes sounds uncomfortable. Honest guidance protects what polite approval destroys.
ramacharitamanas::4356.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana's court has already sunk into praise and self-deception, Tulsidas pauses for a blunt warning. Ministers, doctors, and teachers who soften the truth to stay liked or rewarded end up destroying the very things they are meant to protect.
ramacharitamanas::4356.modern_relevance: A manager tells the team everything is fine because she wants the room to stay calm. A doctor avoids the hard warning. A mentor sugarcoats the feedback. The problem grows quietly while everyone feels reassured.
ramacharitamanas::4356.insight: It teaches you to value truthful counsel over comfort, because false kindness can become a form of harm.

ramacharitamanas::4357.verse_sanskrit: सोइ रावन कहुँ बनी सहाई। अस्तुति करहिं सुनाइ सुनाई॥ अवसर जानि बिभीषनु आवा। भ्राता चरन सीसु तेहिं नावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4357.verse_hindi: रावण के लिए भी वही सहायता (संयोग) आ बनी है। मंत्री उसे सुना-सुनाकर (मुँह पर) स्तुति करते हैं। (इसी समय) अवसर जानकर विभीषणजी आए। उन्होंने बड़े भाई के चरणों में सिर नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4357.english_translation: The same support had come to Ravana as well. His ministers kept praising him to his face. Just then, seeing the right moment, Vibhishana arrived and bowed his head at his elder brother's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4357.translation_literal: सोइ (the same) / रावन (Ravana) / कहुँ (for) / बनी (came to be) / सहाई (help, support) / अस्तुति (praise) / करहिं (they do) / सुनाइ सुनाई (again and again, making him hear) / अवसर (opportunity, right moment) / जानि (knowing) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / आवा (came) / भ्राता (brother) / चरन (feet) / सीसु (head) / तेहिं (he) / नावा (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::4357.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4357.essence: Flattery surrounds power; humility arrives with the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4357.simple_meaning: Ravana is surrounded by flattering ministers, and at the right moment Vibhishana arrives and bows to his brother.
ramacharitamanas::4357.simple_insight: Not every arrival is random; some moments open exactly when a sincere heart is ready.
ramacharitamanas::4357.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trapped inside praise that hides the truth. His ministers flatter him, but Vibhishana arrives at the right moment, not to flatter but to bow. This is the quiet opening before his decisive counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4357.modern_relevance: A meeting where everyone is saying what the boss wants to hear, and one person finally walks in with honesty. The room changes the moment sincerity enters.
ramacharitamanas::4357.insight: It sets up the contrast between flattering speech and truthful surrender before Vibhishana speaks.

ramacharitamanas::4358.verse_sanskrit: पुनि सिरु नाइ बैठ निज आसन। बोला बचन पाइ अनुसासन॥ जौ कृपाल पूँछिहु मोहि बाता। मति अनुरूप कहउँ हित ताता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4358.verse_hindi: फिर से सिर नवाकर अपने आसन पर बैठ गए और आज्ञा पाकर ये वचन बोले- हे कृपाल जब आपने मुझसे बात (राय) पूछी ही है, तो हे तात! मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार आपके हित की बात कहता हूँ- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4358.english_translation: He bowed his head again, sat on his own seat, and then spoke after receiving permission: “If you, O gracious one, ask me for advice, then, father, I will speak what I think is for your good.”
ramacharitamanas::4358.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / बैठ (sat) / निज (own) / आसन (seat) / बोला (spoke) / बचन (words) / पाइ (having received) / अनुसासन (permission, instruction) / जौ (if) / कृपाल (gracious one) / पूँछिहु (you ask) / मोहि (me) / बाता (matter, talk) / मति (mind, understanding) / अनुरूप (according to) / कहउँ (I speak) / हित (for good) / ताता (father)
ramacharitamanas::4358.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4358.essence: Respect opens the door for honest counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4358.simple_meaning: Vibhishana bows respectfully, takes his seat, and says he will speak honestly for Ravana's good if asked.
ramacharitamanas::4358.simple_insight: Real help begins with humility and truth, not flattery.
ramacharitamanas::4358.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just come to Ravana’s court. After bowing and waiting for permission, he speaks carefully but plainly, promising to say what is truly beneficial. This verse sets up the honest counsel that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4358.modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to speak in a tense family meeting, and everyone expects a safe answer. This verse is the courage to be respectful without becoming false.
ramacharitamanas::4358.insight: It teaches you to offer counsel only after permission, and to keep it aligned with what is actually helpful.

ramacharitamanas::4359.verse_sanskrit: जो आपन चाहै कल्याना। सुजसु सुमति सुभ गति सुख नाना॥ सो परनारि लिलार गोसाईं। तजउ चउथि के चंद कि नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4359.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य अपना कल्याण, सुंदर यश, सुबुद्धि, शुभ गति और नाना प्रकार के सुख चाहता हो, वह हे स्वामी! परस्त्री के ललाट को चौथ के चंद्रमा की तरह त्याग दे (अर्थात् जैसे लोग चौथ के चंद्रमा को नहीं देखते, उसी प्रकार परस्त्री का मुख ही न देखे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4359.english_translation: One who wants well-being, good fame, right understanding, auspicious progress, and many kinds of happiness should, O lord, avoid another man's wife as one avoids the moon on the fourth night.
ramacharitamanas::4359.translation_literal: जो (who) आपन (own) चाहै (wants) कल्याना (well-being) / सुजसु (good fame) सुमति (right understanding) सुभ (auspicious) गति (progress) सुख (happiness) नाना (many kinds) / सो (that one) परनारि (another man's wife) लिलार (forehead/face) गोसाईं (O lord) / तजउ (should abandon) चउथि (fourth) के (of) चंद (moon) कि (like) नाईं (as)
ramacharitamanas::4359.speaker: Bibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4359.essence: What you refuse in private shapes everything you become.
ramacharitamanas::4359.simple_meaning: Real well-being, good name, clear judgment, and lasting happiness come from avoiding another man's wife.
ramacharitamanas::4359.simple_insight: Self-control protects both your character and your future.
ramacharitamanas::4359.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just bowed before Ravana and begun speaking with painful honesty. He explains that a person who wants real prosperity must reject desire for another man's wife, because that kind of craving destroys judgment and honor.
ramacharitamanas::4359.modern_relevance: You are scrolling late at night, and one tempting image could become a habit you hide from everyone. The verse says your future is shaped by what you refuse to entertain.
ramacharitamanas::4359.insight: It shifts desire from indulgence to restraint, showing that discipline protects both reputation and inner clarity.

ramacharitamanas::4360.verse_sanskrit: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4360.verse_hindi: चौदहों भुवनों का एक ही स्वामी हो, वह भी जीवों से वैर करके ठहर नहीं सकता (नष्ट हो जाता है) जो मनुष्य गुणों का समुद्र और चतुर हो, उसे चाहे थोड़ा भी लोभ क्यों न हो, तो भी कोई भला नहीं कहता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4360.english_translation: Even the ruler of the fourteen worlds cannot endure if he harms living beings. And even a wise, capable person is not praised if even a little greed remains.
ramacharitamanas::4360.translation_literal: चौदह (fourteen) / भुवन (worlds) / एक (one) / पति (lord) / होई (becomes) / भूत (living beings) / द्रोह (harm, hostility) / तिष्टइ (endures, remains) / नहिं (not) / सोई (that one) / गुन (qualities) / सागर (ocean) / नागर (clever, refined) / नर (person) / जोऊ (whoever) / अलप (small) / लोभ (greed) / भल (good) / कहइ (says) / न (not) / कोऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::4360.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4360.essence: Greatness survives only when power stays kind and greed stays absent.
ramacharitamanas::4360.simple_meaning: No ruler can remain secure if he harms living beings. And no matter how capable someone is, even a little greed ruins their goodness.
ramacharitamanas::4360.simple_insight: Real strength feels clean. Power without kindness, or skill without restraint, stops looking admirable.
ramacharitamanas::4360.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman speaks as a wise messenger after warning against lust for another man's wife. He turns from private conduct to public character: even a world-ruler falls if he turns hostile to living beings, and even a gifted person loses honour if greed remains.
ramacharitamanas::4360.modern_relevance: You get promoted, but the way you treat people in meetings starts turning cold. The title grows, yet respect quietly drains away. This verse sees that before anyone says it aloud.
ramacharitamanas::4360.insight: It shifts judgment from status to conduct: power must be humane, and talent must be free of greed.

ramacharitamanas::4361.verse_sanskrit: काम क्रोध मद लोभ सब नाथ नरक के पंथ। सब परिहरि रघुबीरहि भजहु भजहिं जेहि संत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4361.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! काम, क्रोध, मद और लोभ- ये सब नरक के रास्ते हैं, इन सबको छोड़कर श्री रामचंद्रजी को भजिए, जिन्हें संत (सत्पुरुष) भजते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4361.english_translation: O Lord, desire, anger, pride, and greed are all paths to ruin. Leave them all behind and worship Raghubir, whom the saints worship.
ramacharitamanas::4361.translation_literal: काम (desire) / क्रोध (anger) / मद (pride) / लोभ (greed) / सब (all) / नाथ (O Lord) / नरक (ruin's) / के (of) / पंथ (path) / सब (all) / परिहरि (leaving behind) / रघुबीरहि (Raghubir) / भजहु (worship) / भजहिं (worship) / जेहि (whom) / संत (saints)
ramacharitamanas::4361.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4361.essence: The saints escape ruin by turning away from the four poisons and toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4361.simple_meaning: Desire, anger, pride, and greed pull you toward ruin. Let them go and turn toward Ram, the one the saints worship.
ramacharitamanas::4361.simple_insight: You do not have to follow every urge; there is a cleaner place to stand.
ramacharitamanas::4361.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman's search in Lanka has become a moral teaching for anyone who wants true good. Tulsidas warns that desire, anger, pride, and greed destroy you, and then points to Ram as the refuge chosen by the saints.
ramacharitamanas::4361.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and end up spiraling into comparison, irritation, and wanting more. The verse names that drift before it owns you, then points you back to what steadies you.
ramacharitamanas::4361.insight: It shifts attention from feeding the four inner poisons to choosing a steadier refuge.

ramacharitamanas::4362.verse_sanskrit: तात राम नहिं नर भूपाला। भुवनेस्वर कालहु कर काला॥ ब्रह्म अनामय अज भगवंता। ब्यापक अजित अनादि अनंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4362.verse_hindi: हे तात! राम मनुष्यों के ही राजा नहीं हैं। वे समस्त लोकों के स्वामी और काल के भी काल हैं। वे (संपूर्ण ऐश्वर्य, यश, श्री, धर्म, वैराग्य एवं ज्ञान के भंडार) भगवान् हैं, वे निरामय (विकाररहित), अजन्मे, व्यापक, अजेय, अनादि और अनंत ब्रह्म हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4362.english_translation: Ram is not merely a human king. He is the lord of all worlds, even the master of time itself. He is the flawless, unborn, all-pervading, unconquerable, beginningless, endless supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::4362.translation_literal: तात (father/child, respectful address) / राम (Ram) / नहिं (not) / नर (human) / भूपाला (king) / भुवनेस्वर (lord of the worlds) / कालहु (even of time) / कर (of the hand/authority) / काला (time) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / अनामय (flawless) / अज (unborn) / भगवंता (the blessed one, supreme lord) / व्यापक (all-pervading) / अजित (unconquerable) / अनादि (beginningless) / अनंता (endless)
ramacharitamanas::4362.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4362.essence: Ram is not limited by form, time, or defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4362.simple_meaning: Ram is not just a human ruler. He is the supreme reality itself: unborn, all-pervading, beyond change, beyond defeat, without beginning or end.
ramacharitamanas::4362.simple_insight: The heart relaxes when it sees that the one it loves is not limited by time, fear, or loss.
ramacharitamanas::4362.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is building Sita's hope by praising Ram to her. He is not speaking of a local prince but of the highest reality in human form: the one who rules all worlds, transcends time, and cannot be overcome.
ramacharitamanas::4362.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary at first, then realise they carry a steadiness that fear cannot shake. This verse names that deeper reality: the one you trust is larger than the whole mess around you.
ramacharitamanas::4362.insight: It shifts devotion from a personal preference to recognition of Ram's boundless nature.

ramacharitamanas::4363.verse_sanskrit: गो द्विज धेनु देव हितकारी। कृपा सिंधु मानुष तनुधारी॥ जन रंजन भंजन खल ब्राता। बेद धर्म रच्छक सुनु भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4363.verse_hindi: उन कृपा के समुद्र भगवान् ने पृथ्वी, ब्राह्मण, गो और देवताओं का हित करने के लिए ही मनुष्य शरीर धारण किया है। हे भाई! सुनिए, वे सेवकों को आनंद देने वाले, दुष्टों के समूह का नाश करने वाले और वेद तथा धर्म की रक्षा करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4363.english_translation: For the welfare of the earth, the learned, cows, and the radiant beings, the ocean of compassion took human form. Listen, brother: he delights his followers, destroys the company of the wicked, and protects the Vedas and dharma.
ramacharitamanas::4363.translation_literal: गो (cows) / द्विज (the learned) / धेनु (cows) / देव (radiant beings) / हितकारी (beneficial) / कृपा-सिंधु (ocean of compassion) / मानुष-तनु (human body) / धारी (wearing, taking)॥ / जन-रंजन (delighting people) / भंजन (destroying) / खल-ब्राता (company of the wicked) / बेद (Vedas) / धर्म (dharma) / रच्छक (protector) / सुनु (listen) / भ्राता (brother)॥
ramacharitamanas::4363.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4363.essence: Ram takes human form to protect, delight, and restore what is right.
ramacharitamanas::4363.simple_meaning: Ram took a human body to help the earth, the learned, cows, and the radiant beings. He brings joy to devotees, removes evil company, and protects dharma.
ramacharitamanas::4363.simple_insight: You are not being asked to worship a distant figure, but to trust a presence that comes close and protects what matters.
ramacharitamanas::4363.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is describing Ram to Sita and to himself as he steadies his mission in Lanka. This verse expands Ram’s identity: he is not only mighty, but compassionate, protective, and deeply concerned with the world’s order.
ramacharitamanas::4363.modern_relevance: When someone shows up at 2 a.m. to help you move, then quietly fixes the broken lock before leaving, you feel what this verse points to: power that serves, not power that boasts.
ramacharitamanas::4363.insight: It shifts you from seeing divinity as remote to seeing it as protective, practical, and close to human life.

ramacharitamanas::4364.verse_sanskrit: ताहि बयरु तजि नाइअ माथा। प्रनतारति भंजन रघुनाथा॥ देहु नाथ प्रभु कहुँ बैदेही। भजहु राम बिनु हेतु सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4364.verse_hindi: वैर त्यागकर उन्हें मस्तक नवाइए। वे श्री रघुनाथजी शरणागत का दुःख नाश करने वाले हैं। हे नाथ! उन प्रभु (सर्वेश्वर) को जानकीजी दे दीजिए और बिना ही कारण स्नेह करने वाले श्री रामजी को भजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4364.english_translation: Put aside hostility and bow your head to him. Raghunath destroys the suffering of those who take refuge. O Lord, give Janaki to that supreme Lord, and worship Ram, the loving one without cause.
ramacharitamanas::4364.translation_literal: ताहि (to him) / बयरु (enmity) / तजि (leaving aside) / नाइअ (bow) / माथा (head) / प्रनतारति (the suffering of the surrendered) / भंजन (destroyer) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / देहु (give) / नाथ (Lord) / प्रभु (the supreme Lord) / कहुँ (to) / बैदेही (Janaki) / भजहु (worship) / राम (Ram) / बिनु (without) / हेतु (cause) / सनेही (loving one)
ramacharitamanas::4364.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4364.essence: Ram answers surrender by ending suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4364.simple_meaning: Let go of enmity and bow to Ram. He removes the suffering of anyone who takes refuge in him, and he is loved without needing a reason.
ramacharitamanas::4364.simple_insight: You do not have to win your way into love; surrender can be enough.
ramacharitamanas::4364.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is explaining Ram to Sita through the language of refuge and devotion. He says that hostility should be dropped, because Raghunath relieves the pain of anyone who bows to him. Ram is not loved for a bargain; he is loved without cause.
ramacharitamanas::4364.modern_relevance: You finally stop rehearsing the argument before sending the message. Instead of protecting your pride, you choose the softer move that makes repair possible.
ramacharitamanas::4364.insight: It shifts the mind from guarding against hurt to trusting that surrender can meet pain more cleanly than resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4365.verse_sanskrit: सरन गएँ प्रभु ताहु न त्यागा। बिस्व द्रोह कृत अघ जेहि लागा॥ जासु नाम त्रय ताप नसावन। सोइ प्रभु प्रगट समुझु जियँ रावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4365.verse_hindi: जिसे संपूर्ण जगत् से द्रोह करने का पाप लगा है, शरण जाने पर प्रभु उसका भी त्याग नहीं करते। जिनका नाम तीनों तापों का नाश करने वाला है, वे ही प्रभु (भगवान् ) मनुष्य रूप में प्रकट हुए हैं। हे रावण! हृदय में यह समझ लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4365.english_translation: He does not abandon anyone who comes to him for refuge, even one burdened with the sin of betraying the whole world. His name removes the three kinds of suffering. Understand in your heart: that same Lord has appeared in human form, O Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4365.translation_literal: सरन गएँ (having gone for refuge) / प्रभु (the Lord) / ताहु (even that one) / न त्यागा (does not abandon) / बिस्व (the world) / द्रोह (betrayal) / कृत (done) / अघ (sin/burden) / जेहि (to whom) / लागा (attached) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / त्रय (three) / ताप (pains) / नसावन (destroying) / सोइ (that same) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रगट (manifest) / समुझु (understand) / जियँ (in your heart) / रावन (Ravana)
ramacharitamanas::4365.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4365.essence: Surrender is stronger than your worst failure.
ramacharitamanas::4365.simple_meaning: Even someone burdened by terrible wrongdoing is not rejected if they seek refuge. Ram's name also removes the three kinds of suffering, showing that the Lord has come in human form.
ramacharitamanas::4365.simple_insight: You are not too stained to be welcomed back.
ramacharitamanas::4365.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is trying to shake Ravana out of pride. He reminds him that Ram does not reject even the most fallen person who surrenders. This is not just theology; it is a direct appeal to Ravana's last chance.
ramacharitamanas::4365.modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you replay the worst thing you said and assume the relationship is over. This verse says the door can still open if you truly come back humble.
ramacharitamanas::4365.insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to surrender, and from judging others to recognising refuge as available.

ramacharitamanas::4366.verse_sanskrit: बार बार पद लागउँ बिनय करउँ दससीस। परिहरि मान मोह मद भजहु कोसलाधीस॥39क॥ मुनि पुलस्ति निज सिष्य सन कहि पठई यह बात। तुरत सो मैं प्रभु सन कही पाइ सुअवसरु तात॥39ख॥
ramacharitamanas::4366.verse_hindi: हे दशशीश! मैं बार-बार आपके चरणों लगता हूँ और विनती करता हूँ कि मान, मोह और मद को त्यागकर आप कोसलपति श्री रामजी का भजन कीजिए ॥ मुनि पुलस्त्यजी ने अपने शिष्य के हाथ यह बात कहला भेजी है। हे तात! सुंदर अवसर पाकर मैंने तुरंत ही वह बात प्रभु (आप) से कह दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4366.english_translation: "O ten-faced one, I bow to your feet again and again and beg you: give up pride, delusion, and arrogance, and worship the Lord of Kosala. The sage Pulastya sent this message through his disciple. O dear one, I quickly told that to the Lord at the right moment."
ramacharitamanas::4366.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / पद (feet) / लागउँ (I bow) / बिनय (humble request) / करउँ (I make) / दससीस (ten-faced one) / परिहरि (giving up) / मान (pride) / मोह (delusion) / मद (arrogance) / भजहु (worship) / कोसलाधीस (Lord of Kosala) ॥ मुनि (sage) / पुलस्ति (Pulastya) / निज (own) / सिष्य (disciple) / सन (through) / कहि (having said) / पठई (sent) / यह (this) / बात (message) / तुरत (quickly) / सो (that) / मैं (I) / प्रभु (Lord) / सन (to) / कही (said) / पाइ (having found) / सुअवसरु (good opportunity) / तात (dear one)
ramacharitamanas::4366.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4366.essence: Pride keeps you from the very refuge that could save you.
ramacharitamanas::4366.simple_meaning: Vibhishana begs Ravana to abandon pride, delusion, and arrogance and turn to Ram. He says he has passed this message along at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::4366.simple_insight: Real strength begins when you stop defending the ego and let yourself be guided.
ramacharitamanas::4366.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana keeps pleading with Ravana, the ten-headed king who is trapped in pride. He urges him to drop ego and worship Ram, then explains that this warning was sent through Pulastya's line and delivered at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::4366.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could save a friendship, but your own pride keeps editing it. This verse reminds you that timely honesty matters more than winning the argument.
ramacharitamanas::4366.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble surrender before the divine.

ramacharitamanas::4367.verse_sanskrit: माल्यवंत अति सचिव सयाना। तासु बचन सुनि अति सुख माना॥ तात अनुज तव नीति बिभूषन। सो उर धरहु जो कहत बिभीषन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4367.verse_hindi: माल्यवान् नाम का एक बहुत ही बुद्धिमान मंत्री था। उसने उन (विभीषण) के वचन सुनकर बहुत सुख माना (और कहा-) हे तात! आपके छोटे भाई नीति विभूषण (नीति को भूषण रूप में धारण करने वाले अर्थात् नीतिमान् ) हैं। विभीषण जो कुछ कह रहे हैं उसे हृदय में धारण कर लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4367.english_translation: Malyavan, a very wise minister, heard his words and felt great joy. "Dear one, your younger brother is a jewel of good conduct. Hold in your heart what Vibhishana is saying."
ramacharitamanas::4367.translation_literal: माल्यवंत (Malyavan) / अति (very) / सचिव (minister) / सयाना (wise) / तासु (his) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / सुख (joy) / माना (felt)॥ / तात (dear one) / अनुज (younger brother) / तव (your) / नीति (good conduct) / बिभूषन (ornament/jewel) / सो (that) / उर (heart) / धरहु (hold) / जो (what) / कहत (says) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana)॥
ramacharitamanas::4367.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4367.essence: Wise words matter most when pride wants to throw them away.
ramacharitamanas::4367.simple_meaning: Malyavan recognizes Vibhishana's advice as wise and urges Ravana to take it seriously.
ramacharitamanas::4367.simple_insight: Clear advice can feel relieving because it cuts through pride.
ramacharitamanas::4367.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still refusing to listen. Malyavan, one of his shrewd ministers, hears Vibhishana's warning and immediately sees its value. He tells Ravana to keep that counsel in mind before pride closes every door.
ramacharitamanas::4367.modern_relevance: A friend texts you the hard truth after you have already decided to ignore it. The relief comes later, when you realize the honest voice was trying to save you from yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4367.insight: It shifts you from defending your ego to receiving inconvenient truth.

ramacharitamanas::4368.verse_sanskrit: रिपु उतकरष कहत सठ दोऊ। दूरि न करहु इहाँ हइ कोऊ॥ माल्यवंत गह गयउ बहोरी। कहइ बिभीषनु पुनि कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4368.verse_hindi: (रावन ने कहा-) ये दोनों मूर्ख शत्रु की महिमा बखान रहे हैं। यहाँ कोई है? इन्हें दूर करो न! तब माल्यवान् तो घर लौट गया और विभीषणजी हाथ जोड़कर फिर कहने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4368.english_translation: The two fools keep praising the enemy's greatness. Is there no one here? Drive them away! Then Malyavan went back home, and Vibhishana again spoke with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::4368.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / उतकरष (greatness, praise) / कहत (saying) / सठ (fools) / दोऊ (both) / दूरि (away) / न (not) / करहु (do) / इहाँ (here) / हइ (is) / कोऊ (someone) / माल्यवंत (Malyavan) / गह (taking) / गयउ (went) / बहोरी (back again) / कहइ (speaks) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / पुनि (again) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined)
ramacharitamanas::4368.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4368.essence: Pride drives away the counsel that could still save you.
ramacharitamanas::4368.simple_meaning: Ravana angrily rejects advice that praises his enemy. Malyavan leaves, and Vibhishana continues pleading with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::4368.simple_insight: Pride cannot bear honest counsel, even when it could save everything.
ramacharitamanas::4368.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears Malyavan and Vibhishana speaking in Ram's favor. Offended, he calls them fools and orders them away. Malyavan withdraws, but Vibhishana keeps pleading. The scene shows Ravana's growing blindness just before the next warning about good and bad judgment.
ramacharitamanas::4368.modern_relevance: You snap at the one person telling you the hard truth, then wonder why the situation keeps slipping. Pride often throws away the very warning that could have saved you.
ramacharitamanas::4368.insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to listening for correction before damage hardens.

ramacharitamanas::4369.verse_sanskrit: सुमति कुमति सब कें उर रहहीं। नाथ पुरान निगम अस कहहीं॥ जहाँ सुमति तहँ संपति नाना। जहाँ कुमति तहँ बिपति निदाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4369.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! पुराण और वेद ऐसा कहते हैं कि सुबुद्धि (अच्छी बुद्धि) और कुबुद्धि (खोटी बुद्धि) सबके हृदय में रहती है, जहाँ सुबुद्धि है, वहाँ नाना प्रकार की संपदाएँ (सुख की स्थिति) रहती हैं और जहाँ कुबुद्धि है वहाँ परिणाम में विपत्ति (दुःख) रहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4369.english_translation: Good and bad judgment both live in every heart. The Puranas and Vedas say this, O Lord. Where good judgment lives, many blessings gather; where bad judgment lives, disaster follows.
ramacharitamanas::4369.translation_literal: सुमति (good judgment) / कुमति (bad judgment) / सब कें (in everyone) / उर (heart) / रहहीं (remain) / नाथ (Lord) / पुरान (Puranas) / निगम (Vedas) / अस (thus) / कहहीं (say) ॥ जहाँ (where) / सुमति (good judgment) / तहँ (there) / संपति (blessings, prosperity) / नाना (many) / जहाँ (where) / कुमति (bad judgment) / तहँ (there) / बिपति (disaster) / निदाना (at the end, in the end) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4369.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4369.essence: Your life follows the judgment you choose to trust.
ramacharitamanas::4369.simple_meaning: Good and bad judgment both live in every heart. When clear judgment leads, life becomes fruitful; when confused judgment leads, trouble follows.
ramacharitamanas::4369.simple_insight: You are not helpless before your habits; the quality of your judgment changes the quality of your life.
ramacharitamanas::4369.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana is answering Ravana’s court. He reminds the king that the old scriptures already teach this: every heart contains both clear and confused judgment. What you follow inside yourself decides whether life ripens or collapses.
ramacharitamanas::4369.modern_relevance: You know that moment when you ignore the quiet, sensible voice and choose the louder impulse instead. Hours later, the mess is not random — it grew from the judgment you fed.
ramacharitamanas::4369.insight: It shifts attention from events outside you to the quality of discernment inside you.

ramacharitamanas::4370.verse_sanskrit: तव उर कुमति बसी बिपरीता। हित अनहित मानहु रिपु प्रीता॥ कालराति निसिचर कुल केरी। तेहि सीता पर प्रीति घनेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4370.verse_hindi: आपके हृदय में उलटी बुद्धि आ बसी है। इसी से आप हित को अहित और शत्रु को मित्र मान रहे हैं। जो राक्षस कुल के लिए कालरात्रि (के समान) हैं, उन सीता पर आपकी बड़ी प्रीति है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4370.english_translation: Your heart has been taken over by twisted judgment. That is why you call what helps you harmful, and what harms you friendly. For the race of demons, Sita is like the night of destruction, yet you feel deep affection for her.
ramacharitamanas::4370.translation_literal: तव (your) / उर (heart) / कुमति (bad judgment) / बसी (has settled) / बिपरीता (reversed) / हित (benefit) / अनहित (harm) / मानहु (you consider) / रिपु (enemy) / प्रीता (friendship) / कालराति (night of destruction) / निसिचर (demon) / कुल (lineage) / केरी (of) / तेहि (that) / सीता (Sita) / पर (toward) / प्रीति (affection) / घनेरी (very great)
ramacharitamanas::4370.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4370.essence: Desire can make ruin look like love.
ramacharitamanas::4370.simple_meaning: A corrupted mind reverses values: it mistakes harm for benefit and the enemy for a friend. Ravana’s desire for Sita is proof of that confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4370.simple_insight: It hurts to see how desire can make you trust the very thing that will undo you.
ramacharitamanas::4370.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana is still trying to reason with Ravana. After warning that wise and foolish minds live in every heart, he now points directly at Ravana’s reversal of values: he protects what should be rejected and desires what will bring ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4370.modern_relevance: You keep defending a relationship that keeps draining you. Everyone else can see the pattern, but your mind keeps calling it loyalty. This verse names that dangerous reversal.
