ramacharitamanas::4370.insight: It shifts the mind from defending desire to checking whether desire has distorted judgment.

ramacharitamanas::4371.verse_sanskrit: तात चरन गहि मागउँ राखहु मोर दुलार। सीता देहु राम कहुँ अहित न होइ तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4371.verse_hindi: हे तात! मैं चरण पकड़कर आपसे भीख माँगता हूँ (विनती करता हूँ)। कि आप मेरा दुलार रखिए (मुझ बालक के आग्रह को स्नेहपूर्वक स्वीकार कीजिए) श्री रामजी को सीताजी दे दीजिए, जिसमें आपका अहित न हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4371.english_translation: O father, I hold your feet and beg you: keep my love for you. Give Sita to Ram, and no harm will come to you.
ramacharitamanas::4371.translation_literal: तात (father) / चरन (feet) / गहि (grasping) / मागउँ (I beg) / राखहु (keep) / मोर (my) / दुलार (affection, love) / सीता (Sita) / देहु (give) / राम कहुँ (to Ram) / अहित (harm) / न होइ (will not be) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::4371.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4371.essence: Real care sometimes means asking someone to let go before ruin arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4371.simple_meaning: Vibhishana pleads with Ravana as a son and advisor: show affection, return Sita to Ram, and you will not suffer for it.
ramacharitamanas::4371.simple_insight: Love is not weakness when it tells the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4371.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana kneels before Ravana and speaks like a loyal younger brother trying to save his family. He asks Ravana to give Sita back to Ram, promising that no harm will come if he lets go now.
ramacharitamanas::4371.modern_relevance: You know the conversation where a friend is about to lose everything, and you say the hard thing anyway. This is that moment: affection without honesty becomes cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::4371.insight: It teaches you to speak truth with care, even when the other person may resist it.

ramacharitamanas::4372.verse_sanskrit: बुध पुरान श्रुति संमत बानी। कही बिभीषन नीति बखानी॥ सुनत दसानन उठा रिसाई। खल तोहिं निकट मृत्यु अब आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4372.verse_hindi: विभीषण ने पंडितों, पुराणों और वेदों द्वारा सम्मत (अनुमोदित) वाणी से नीति बखानकर कही। पर उसे सुनते ही रावण क्रोधित होकर उठा और बोला कि रे दुष्ट! अब मृत्यु तेरे निकट आ गई है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4372.english_translation: Vibhishana spoke words approved by the wise, the Puranas, and the Vedas, explaining right conduct. Hearing this, Ravana rose in anger and said, “Wretch, death is now near you!”
ramacharitamanas::4372.translation_literal: बुध (wise) / पुरान (Puranas) / श्रुति (Vedas) / संमत (approved) / बानी (speech) / कही (said) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / नीति (right conduct) / बखानी (explained)॥ / सुनत (hearing) / दसानन (Ravana, ten-faced one) / उठा (rose) / रिसाई (in anger) / खल (wretch) / तोहिं (you) / निकट (near) / मृत्यु (death) / अब (now) / आई (has come)॥
ramacharitamanas::4372.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4372.essence: Pride turns even wise counsel into a threat.
ramacharitamanas::4372.simple_meaning: Vibhishana speaks with support from respected wisdom traditions, but Ravana reacts with rage instead of listening.
ramacharitamanas::4372.simple_insight: It feels sobering to see how pride can turn advice into insult.
ramacharitamanas::4372.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana tries to warn Ravana with counsel grounded in respected learning and right conduct. Ravana does not hear the warning; he hears only threat. The scene shows a mind so sealed by pride that wisdom itself becomes unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::4372.modern_relevance: A friend calmly points out the mistake in your plan, and your chest tightens before they finish the sentence. The verse captures that instant when ego hears correction as attack.
ramacharitamanas::4372.insight: It teaches you to notice when defensiveness is blocking clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4373.verse_sanskrit: जिअसि सदा सठ मोर जिआवा। रिपु कर पच्छ मूढ़ तोहि भावा॥ कहसि न खल अस को जग माहीं। भुज बल जाहि जिता मैं नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4373.verse_hindi: अरे मूर्ख! तू जीता तो है सदा मेरा जिलाया हुआ (अर्थात् मेरे ही अन्न से पल रहा है), पर हे मूढ़! पक्ष तुझे शत्रु का ही अच्छा लगता है। अरे दुष्ट! बता न, जगत् में ऐसा कौन है जिसे मैंने अपनी भुजाओं के बल से न जीता हो? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4373.english_translation: You fool, you live only because I keep you alive. You side with my enemy. Tell me, is there anyone in the world I have not conquered by my own strength?
ramacharitamanas::4373.translation_literal: जिअसि (you live) / सदा (always) / सठ (fool) / मोर (my) / जिआवा (made to live, kept alive) / रिपु (enemy) / कर (of) / पच्छ (side) / मूढ़ (deluded one) / तोहि (you) / भावा (pleased, seems good) / कहसि (you say) / न (not) / खल (wicked one) / अस (such) / को (who) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / भुज (arms) / बल (strength) / जाहि (whom) / जिता (conquered) / मैं (I) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::4373.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4373.essence: Ego boasts of control even while depending on others.
ramacharitamanas::4373.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he keeps people alive, insults Vibhishana as foolish, and claims he has conquered everyone by his own strength.
ramacharitamanas::4373.simple_insight: Pride makes a person forget who supports them and overestimate their own power.
ramacharitamanas::4373.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just spoken hard truth to Ravana and urged him toward right conduct. Ravana explodes in anger, mocking his brother as foolish and boasting that no one in the world can stand against his strength. The verse shows ego refusing correction.
ramacharitamanas::4373.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting, then acts as if they alone built the whole project. The louder the boast, the more it hides dependence on others.
ramacharitamanas::4373.insight: It exposes how ego turns every relationship into a contest and every warning into an insult.

ramacharitamanas::4374.verse_sanskrit: मम पुर बसि तपसिन्ह पर प्रीती। सठ मिलु जाइ तिन्हहि कहु नीती॥ अस कहि कीन्हेसि चरन प्रहारा। अनुज गहे पद बारहिं बारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4374.verse_hindi: मेरे नगर में रहकर प्रेम करता है तपस्वियों पर। मूर्ख! उन्हीं से जा मिल और उन्हीं को नीति बता। ऐसा कहकर रावण ने उन्हें लात मारी, परंतु छोटे भाई विभीषण ने (मारने पर भी) बार-बार उसके चरण ही पकड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4374.english_translation: Living in my city, you love ascetics. Fool, go join them and tell them your morals. Saying this, Ravana kicked him, but Vibhishana kept holding his brother's feet again and again.
ramacharitamanas::4374.translation_literal: मम (my) / पुर (city) / बसि (living) / तपसिन्ह (ascetics) / पर (toward) / प्रीती (love) / सठ (fool) / मिलु (go join) / जाइ (going) / तिन्हहि (them) / कहु (tell) / नीती (morals) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / कीन्हेसि (he did) / चरन (feet) / प्रहारा (blow/kick) / अनुज (younger brother) / गहे (held) / पद (feet) / बारहिं बारा (again and again)
ramacharitamanas::4374.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4374.essence: Loyalty can survive even when it is kicked away.
ramacharitamanas::4374.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Vibhishana for loving holy people, kicks him, and Vibhishana still keeps clinging to his feet.
ramacharitamanas::4374.simple_insight: Even rejection cannot break true loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::4374.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just exploded at Vibhishana for speaking righteous counsel. He insults him, kicks him, and the younger brother responds not with anger but by grasping Ravana's feet again and again. The scene shows both Ravana's ego and Vibhishana's unshaken devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4374.modern_relevance: You try to speak calmly to someone who is already furious, and they lash out. The real test is whether your care survives their contempt.
ramacharitamanas::4374.insight: It reveals the contrast between wounded pride and steady loyalty under attack.

ramacharitamanas::4375.verse_sanskrit: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4375.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! संत की यही बड़ाई (महिमा) है कि वे बुराई करने पर भी (बुराई करने वाले की) भलाई ही करते हैं। (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) आप मेरे पिता के समान हैं, मुझे मारा सो तो अच्छा ही किया, परंतु हे नाथ! आपका भला श्री रामजी को भजने में ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4375.english_translation: Uma, this is the greatness of the noble: even when harmed, they do good. You are like my father; striking me was for my good. But, Lord, your true welfare lies in worshipping Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4375.translation_literal: उमा (Uma) / संत (noble ones) / कइ (of) / इहइ (this) / बड़ाई (greatness) / मंद (badly) / करत (doing) / जो (who) / करइ (does) / भलाई (good) / तुम्ह (you) / पितु (father) / सरिस (like) / भलेहिं (for good) / मोहि (me) / मारा (struck) / रामु (Ram) / भजें (by worshipping) / हित (welfare) / नाथ (Lord) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::4375.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4375.essence: True goodness keeps blessing even after being hurt, and points others to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4375.simple_meaning: Noble people keep wishing well even after being hurt. Vibhishana says Ravana's blow was still for his good, and that real welfare comes from turning to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4375.simple_insight: You can respond to harm without becoming hard. The highest good is still calling you toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4375.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana strikes Vibhishana and mocks him, Vibhishana answers without hatred. He explains that saints repay harm with goodwill, then turns the moment into a final invitation: Ravana's real welfare lies in taking refuge in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4375.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a family argument, then acts like nothing happened. Instead of matching their bitterness, you see the deeper opening: you can stay kind, and you can still point them toward what heals them.
ramacharitamanas::4375.insight: It shifts you from reacting to injury toward answering with goodwill and spiritual clarity.

ramacharitamanas::4376.verse_sanskrit: सचिव संग लै नभ पथ गयऊ। सबहि सुनाइ कहत अस भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4376.verse_hindi: (इतना कहकर) विभीषण अपने मंत्रियों को साथ लेकर आकाश मार्ग में गए और सबको सुनाकर वे ऐसा कहने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4376.english_translation: Taking his ministers along, Vibhishana went by the sky path and, making everyone hear it, began to speak thus.
ramacharitamanas::4376.translation_literal: सचिव (ministers) / संग (along with) / लै (taking) / नभ (sky) / पथ (path) / गयऊ (went) / सबहि (to everyone) / सुनाइ (making hear) / कहत (speaking) / अस (thus) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::4376.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4376.essence: A private break becomes a public declaration.
ramacharitamanas::4376.simple_meaning: Vibhishana leaves with his ministers and goes into the sky, preparing to speak publicly.
ramacharitamanas::4376.simple_insight: He is moving from private decision to public declaration.
ramacharitamanas::4376.detailed_meaning: After Ravana has insulted him, Vibhishana does not stay silent. He leaves with his ministers, rises into the sky, and prepares to announce his stand before everyone. The next verse reveals the substance of that declaration.
ramacharitamanas::4376.modern_relevance: You draft the message, then stop and decide to send it to the whole group. The real moment is not the typing — it is when you choose to say it out loud.
ramacharitamanas::4376.insight: It frames the coming declaration as a public turning point, not a philosophical conclusion.

ramacharitamanas::4377.verse_sanskrit: रामु सत्यसंकल्प प्रभु सभा कालबस तोरि। मैं रघुबीर सरन अब जाउँ देहु जनि खोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4377.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी सत्य संकल्प एवं (सर्वसमर्थ) प्रभु हैं और (हे रावण) तुम्हारी सभा काल के वश है। अतः मैं अब श्री रघुवीर की शरण जाता हूँ, मुझे दोष न देना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4377.english_translation: Ram is the Lord whose resolve never fails, and your court is already under Time's control. I now go to the refuge of Raghubir; do not blame me for this.
ramacharitamanas::4377.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / सत्यसंकल्प (whose resolve is true) / प्रभु (Lord) / सभा (court) / कालबस (under the control of Time) / तोरि (your) / मैं (I) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सरन (refuge) / अब (now) / जाउँ (go) / देहु (give) / जनि (do not) / खोरि (blame)
ramacharitamanas::4377.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4377.essence: Surrender becomes clear when you see which side is already falling.
ramacharitamanas::4377.simple_meaning: Vibhishana says Ram always keeps his promise, while Ravana's court is doomed. So he leaves Ravana and seeks Ram's protection, asking not to be blamed.
ramacharitamanas::4377.simple_insight: There is relief in leaving what is already collapsing and choosing the safer refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4377.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just defended Ram and the righteous way to live. Now he openly turns away from Ravana's court, naming it doomed by Time itself. This is the moment he fully surrenders and chooses Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4377.modern_relevance: You are in a group chat where everyone is mocking the one person telling the truth. The atmosphere has gone rotten, and staying silent would mean joining it. Vibhishana shows the courage to leave and stand elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::4377.insight: It shifts loyalty from a failing power structure to a refuge that can actually hold you.

ramacharitamanas::4378.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि चला बिभीषनु जबहीं। आयू हीन भए सब तबहीं॥ साधु अवग्या तुरत भवानी। कर कल्यान अखिल कै हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4378.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर विभीषणजी ज्यों ही चले, त्यों ही सब राक्षस आयुहीन हो गए। (उनकी मृत्यु निश्चित हो गई)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! साधु का अपमान तुरंत ही संपूर्ण कल्याण की हानि (नाश) कर देता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4378.english_translation: As soon as Vibhishana left, all the demons became lifeless. Then Shiva said to Parvati: the insult of a noble person quickly destroys all well-being.
ramacharitamanas::4378.translation_literal: अस कहि (thus saying) / चला (went) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / जबहीं (just then) / आयू (life) / हीन (deprived) / भए (became) / सब (all) / तबहीं (then) / साधु (noble one) / अवग्या (insult/disrespect) / तुरत (immediately) / भवानी (O Bhavani) / कर (does) / कल्यान (well-being) / अखिल (all) / कै (of) / हानी (loss)
ramacharitamanas::4378.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4378.essence: Disrespecting the noble destroys the very good you depend on.
ramacharitamanas::4378.simple_meaning: When Vibhishana departs, the demons lose their life-force. Shiva then warns Parvati that insulting a noble person instantly harms all that is good.
ramacharitamanas::4378.simple_insight: Your treatment of the worthy shapes the fate of your own life.
ramacharitamanas::4378.detailed_meaning: Vibhishana has just walked away from Ravana and chosen Ram. The moment he leaves, the demons are spiritually finished. Shiva turns to Parvati and draws the lesson: when you dishonor a noble person, you cut off your own welfare.
ramacharitamanas::4378.modern_relevance: You mock the colleague who quietly keeps the team afloat, then wonder why the whole room feels colder. This verse says contempt has a cost long before anyone admits it.
ramacharitamanas::4378.insight: It shifts you from casual disrespect to careful recognition of character and value.

ramacharitamanas::4379.verse_sanskrit: रावन जबहिं बिभीषन त्यागा। भयउ बिभव बिनु तबहिं अभागा॥ चलेउ हरषि रघुनायक पाहीं। करत मनोरथ बहु मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4379.verse_hindi: रावण ने जिस क्षण विभीषण को त्यागा, उसी क्षण वह अभागा वैभव (ऐश्वर्य) से हीन हो गया। विभीषणजी हर्षित होकर मन में अनेकों मनोरथ करते हुए श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4379.english_translation: The moment Ravana cast Vibhishana aside, he was left bereft of fortune. Vibhishana then walked joyfully toward Raghunath, holding many hopes in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4379.translation_literal: रावन (Ravana) / जबहिं (the moment) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / त्यागा (abandoned) / भयउ (became) / बिभव (splendour, fortune) / बिनु (without) / तबहिं (then, at that very time) / अभागा (unfortunate, bereft)॥ / चलेउ (went) / हरषि (joyfully) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / पाहीं (toward) / करत (doing, making) / मनोरथ (wishes, hopes) / बहु (many) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within)॥
ramacharitamanas::4379.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4379.essence: Pride loses everything the moment it rejects refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4379.simple_meaning: Ravana loses his greatness the instant he rejects Vibhishana. Vibhishana, by contrast, walks joyfully toward Ram, full of hope.
ramacharitamanas::4379.simple_insight: What you cast away in ego can become the very thing that carries you home.
ramacharitamanas::4379.detailed_meaning: After Vibhishana declares his refusal to stand with Ravana, the bond is broken for good. Ravana loses his inner and outer fortune at once, while Vibhishana heads toward Ram with hope and relief. The verse marks the turn from pride to refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4379.modern_relevance: The friend you dismissed finally stops trying to save the friendship, and only then do you realize what your pride cost you. The other person walks away lighter, not bitter.
ramacharitamanas::4379.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to status toward seeing refuge as real gain.

ramacharitamanas::4380.verse_sanskrit: देखिहउँ जाइ चरन जलजाता। अरुन मृदुल सेवक सुखदाता॥ जे पद परसि तरी रिषनारी। दंडक कानन पावनकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4380.verse_hindi: (वे सोचते जाते थे-) मैं जाकर भगवान् के कोमल और लाल वर्ण के सुंदर चरण कमलों के दर्शन करूँगा, जो सेवकों को सुख देने वाले हैं, जिन चरणों का स्पर्श पाकर ऋषि पत्नी अहल्या तर गईं और जो दंडकवन को पवित्र करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4380.english_translation: I will go and behold the lotus feet—soft, red, and full of comfort for devotees. Those feet touched Ahalya and purified the Dandaka forest.
ramacharitamanas::4380.translation_literal: देखिहउँ (I will see) / जाइ (going) / चरन (feet) / जलजाता (lotus-born / lotus-like) / अरुन (red) / मृदुल (soft) / सेवक (devotee / servant) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) ॥ जे (those) / पद (feet) / परसि (touching) / तरी (was liberated) / रिषनारी (sage-woman Ahalya) / दंडक (Dandaka) / कानन (forest) / पावनकारी (purifier)
ramacharitamanas::4380.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4380.essence: Ram's feet are both tender refuge and transforming power.
ramacharitamanas::4380.simple_meaning: Vibhishana thinks of Ram's beautiful feet with devotion. He sees them as tender, freeing, and purifying—feet that liberated Ahalya and sanctified the Dandaka forest.
ramacharitamanas::4380.simple_insight: Love focuses on the source of blessing, not on itself.
ramacharitamanas::4380.detailed_meaning: Vibhishana has just left Ravana and is walking toward Ram with hope in his heart. As he goes, he remembers Ram's lotus feet: soft to devotees, powerful enough to free Ahalya, and holy enough to purify the Dandaka forest.
ramacharitamanas::4380.modern_relevance: You leave a draining conversation and keep thinking about the one person whose presence steadies you. What you are really reaching for is not approval, but the kind of contact that restores you.
ramacharitamanas::4380.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract praise to a concrete longing for Ram's presence and grace.

ramacharitamanas::4381.verse_sanskrit: जे पद जनकसुताँ उर लाए। कपट कुरंग संग धर धाए॥ हर उर सर सरोज पद जेई। अहोभाग्य मैं देखिहउँ तेई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4381.verse_hindi: जिन चरणों को जानकीजी ने हृदय में धारण कर रखा है, जो कपटमृग के साथ पृथ्वी पर (उसे पकड़ने को) दौड़े थे और जो चरणकमल साक्षात् शिवजी के हृदय रूपी सरोवर में विराजते हैं, मेरा अहोभाग्य है कि उन्हीं को आज मैं देखूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4381.english_translation: The feet that Janaki holds in her heart, that ran across the earth with the deceptive deer, and that rest like lotus feet in Shiva's heart-lake — it is my great fortune to see those feet today.
ramacharitamanas::4381.translation_literal: जे (which) / पद (feet) / जनकसुताँ (by Janaki) / उर (heart) / लाए (held) / कपट (deceptive) / कुरंग (deer) / संग (with) / धर (earth) / धाए (ran) / हर (Shiva) / उर (heart) / सर (lake) / सरोज (lotus) / पद (feet) / जेई (which indeed) / अहोभाग्य (great fortune) / मैं (I) / देखिहउँ (will see) / तेई (those very)
ramacharitamanas::4381.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4381.essence: Ram's feet are precious because love has already claimed them.
ramacharitamanas::4381.simple_meaning: Hanuman feels blessed to see Ram's feet, which Sita holds in her heart and Shiva reveres. The verse turns a sight into a sacred privilege.
ramacharitamanas::4381.simple_insight: Devotion makes ordinary seeing feel like grace arriving in person.
ramacharitamanas::4381.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is closing in on the moment he has crossed oceans for. He thinks of Ram's feet as beloved by Sita and worshipped by Shiva, and that makes his own sight of them feel like a miracle.
ramacharitamanas::4381.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence has steadied two people you trust most. The room feels different, because you know you are standing near what they have cherished for years.
ramacharitamanas::4381.insight: It shifts attention from the object seen to the love already gathered around it.

ramacharitamanas::4382.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह पायन्ह के पादुकन्हि भरतु रहे मन लाइ। ते पद आजु बिलोकिहउँ इन्ह नयनन्हि अब जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4382.verse_hindi: जिन चरणों की पादुकाओं में भरतजी ने अपना मन लगा रखा है, अहा! आज मैं उन्हीं चरणों को अभी जाकर इन नेत्रों से देखूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4382.english_translation: The feet whose sandals Bharat held in his heart — today I will go and see those very feet with these eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4382.translation_literal: जिन्ह (whose) / पायन्ह (feet) / के (of) / पादुकन्हि (sandals) / भरतु (Bharat) / रहे (remained) / मन लाइ (with mind fixed) / ते (those) / पद (feet) / आजु (today) / बिलोकिहउँ (I will behold) / इन्ह (these) / नयनन्हि (with eyes) / अब (now) / जाइ (going)
ramacharitamanas::4382.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4382.essence: What your heart has cherished from afar can still become immediate.
ramacharitamanas::4382.simple_meaning: Hanuman feels joy that the feet Bharat revered through Ram's sandals are finally before him. He is eager to see with his own eyes what Bharat loved from afar.
ramacharitamanas::4382.simple_insight: Love can make even a distant holy presence feel immediate and real.
ramacharitamanas::4382.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman reaches the far shore of Lanka after crossing the ocean in devotion. Before the larger search continues, he pauses in reverence: these are the feet Bharat held dear through Ram's sandals, and now Hanuman longs to behold them directly.
ramacharitamanas::4382.modern_relevance: You finally meet the mentor, place, or person you have admired only from stories. The anticipation is not curiosity alone — it is reverence meeting reality.
ramacharitamanas::4382.insight: It shifts attention from secondhand devotion to direct encounter with what the heart has already trusted.

ramacharitamanas::4383.verse_sanskrit: ऐहि बिधि करत सप्रेम बिचारा। आयउ सपदि सिंदु एहिं पारा॥ कपिन्ह बिभीषनु आवत देखा। जाना कोउ रिपु दूत बिसेषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4383.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार प्रेमसहित विचार करते हुए वे शीघ्र ही समुद्र के इस पार (जिधर श्री रामचंद्रजी की सेना थी) आ गए। वानरों ने विभीषण को आते देखा तो उन्होंने जाना कि शत्रु का कोई खास दूत है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4383.english_translation: Thinking in this loving way, he quickly crossed to the far shore of the ocean. The monkeys saw Vibhishana coming and thought, 'A special envoy from the enemy has arrived.'
ramacharitamanas::4383.translation_literal: ऐहि बिधि (in this way) / करत (doing) / सप्रेम (with love) / बिचारा (thinking) / आयउ (came) / सपदि (quickly) / सिंदु (ocean) / एहिं पारा (to this shore) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / आवत (coming) / देखा (saw) / जाना (understood) / कोउ (some) / रिपु (enemy) / दूत (messenger) / बिसेषा (special)
ramacharitamanas::4383.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4383.essence: A new arrival can change the whole mood in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4383.simple_meaning: Vibhishana crosses the ocean quickly, and the monkeys notice him as a suspicious messenger from the enemy side.
ramacharitamanas::4383.simple_insight: Not every arrival is welcome; wise people notice carefully before they trust.
ramacharitamanas::4383.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the shore near Ram's army after searching Lanka. Vibhishana now appears from the enemy side, and the monkeys immediately become alert. This is a movement scene that sets up the meeting, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::4383.modern_relevance: A stranger walks into a tense room just after a major conflict. Everyone goes quiet, trying to read whether this person brings help, danger, or both.
ramacharitamanas::4383.insight: It trains attention to read context before granting trust.

ramacharitamanas::4384.verse_sanskrit: ताहि राखि कपीस पहिं आए। समाचार सब ताहि सुनाए॥ कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुराई। आवा मिलन दसानन भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4384.verse_hindi: उन्हें (पहरे पर) ठहराकर वे सुग्रीव के पास आए और उनको सब समाचार कह सुनाए। सुग्रीव ने (श्री रामजी के पास जाकर) कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए, रावण का भाई (आप से) मिलने आया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4384.english_translation: They left him guarded and came to Sugriva, telling him everything. Sugriva said, “Listen, Raghunath: Ravana’s brother has come to meet you.”
ramacharitamanas::4384.translation_literal: ताहि (him) / राखि (having kept) / कपीस पहिं (to Sugriva) / आए (came) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / ताहि (to him) / सुनाए (told)॥ / कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / आवा (has come) / मिलन (to meet) / दसानन (ten-faced Ravana) / भाई (brother) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4384.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4384.essence: News reaches the right hands before the next move begins.
ramacharitamanas::4384.simple_meaning: Hanuman and the others report Vibhishana’s arrival to Sugriva, who then informs Ram that Ravana’s brother has come seeking an audience.
ramacharitamanas::4384.simple_insight: Not every important moment is a teaching; some verses simply move the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::4384.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the shore and the search is turning toward action. The watch is left in place, the news is carried to Sugriva, and Vibhishana’s arrival is announced to Ram. This verse sets up the decision that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4384.modern_relevance: You get the message, check the facts, and pass it to the right person before anyone acts. That quiet relay can change everything.
ramacharitamanas::4384.insight: It keeps attention on the chain of communication, not on interpretation or judgment.

ramacharitamanas::4385.verse_sanskrit: कह प्रभु सखा बूझिए काहा। कहइ कपीस सुनहु नरनाहा॥ जानि न जाइ निसाचर माया। कामरूप केहि कारन आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4385.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामजी ने कहा- हे मित्र! तुम क्या समझते हो (तुम्हारी क्या राय है)? वानरराज सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे महाराज! सुनिए, राक्षसों की माया जानी नहीं जाती। यह इच्छानुसार रूप बदलने वाला (छली) न जाने किस कारण आया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4385.english_translation: Lord Ram said, 'Friend, what do you think?' Sugriva replied, 'Listen, king of men. The nature of a demon cannot be known. This shape-shifter has come for some hidden reason.'
ramacharitamanas::4385.translation_literal: कह (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सखा (friend) / बूझिए (should be asked / tell me) / काहा (what) / कहइ (said) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / सुनहु (listen) / नरनाहा (king of men) / जानि (known) / न जाइ (cannot be) / निसाचर (demon) / माया (deception / illusion) / कामरूप (shape-shifting) / केहि (what) / कारन (reason) / आया (came)
ramacharitamanas::4385.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4385.essence: What looks friendly may still hide a dangerous purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4385.simple_meaning: Ram asks Sugriva for his opinion, and Sugriva warns that the shape-shifting enemy cannot be understood easily and may have come with a hidden purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4385.simple_insight: Not every stranger is harmless; careful judgment matters before you trust what you cannot read.
ramacharitamanas::4385.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just returned from Lanka, and the monkey army is trying to understand the strange arrival of Vibhishana, Ravana's brother. Ram asks for counsel, and Sugriva suspects deception. The scene builds the tension before Ram decides how to respond.
ramacharitamanas::4385.modern_relevance: A new person joins the group chat and seems helpful, but something feels off. You pause, ask for judgment, and do not rush into trust just because the surface looks friendly.
ramacharitamanas::4385.insight: It trains you to question appearances and seek the hidden motive before acting.

ramacharitamanas::4386.verse_sanskrit: भेद हमार लेन सठ आवा। राखिअ बाँधि मोहि अस भावा॥ सखा नीति तुम्ह नीकि बिचारी। मम पन सरनागत भयहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4386.verse_hindi: (जान पड़ता है) यह मूर्ख हमारा भेद लेने आया है, इसलिए मुझे तो यही अच्छा लगता है कि इसे बाँध रखा जाए। (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे मित्र! तुमने नीति तो अच्छी विचारी, परंतु मेरा प्रण तो है शरणागत के भय को हर लेना! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4386.english_translation: He has come to spy on us, you fool. It seems right to me to keep him bound. Friend, you have thought well about policy, but my vow is to remove the fear of anyone who has come seeking refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4386.translation_literal: भेद (secret / spy-work) / हमार (our) / लेन (to take) / सठ (fool) / आवा (has come) / राखिअ (keep bound) / बाँधि (binding) / मोहि (to me) / अस (this / thus) / भावा (seems good) ॥ / सखा (friend) / नीति (policy / prudence) / तुम्ह (you) / नीकि (well) / बिचारी (considered) / मम (my) / पन (vow) / सरनागत (one who has sought refuge) / भयहारी (fear-removing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4386.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4386.essence: A surrendered one is protected, not punished.
ramacharitamanas::4386.simple_meaning: Ram says policy is not the highest rule here. Even if someone seems suspicious, a person who has come seeking shelter should be protected, not punished.
ramacharitamanas::4386.simple_insight: Real strength is measured by how safe others feel in your care.
ramacharitamanas::4386.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been caught after searching for Sita. Sugriva sees a possible spy and wants him bound. Ram stops that instinct and states his own vow: anyone who comes in surrender must be freed from fear, not treated as an enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4386.modern_relevance: Someone shows up at your door after a mistake, scared and ashamed, and everyone else wants to shut them out. This verse asks whether you will choose caution or refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4386.insight: It shifts you from suspicion-first thinking to refuge-first action.

ramacharitamanas::4387.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन हरष हनुमाना। सरनागत बच्छल भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4387.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर हनुमान् जी हर्षित हुए (और मन ही मन कहने लगे कि) भगवान् कैसे शरणागतवत्सल (शरण में आए हुए पर पिता की भाँति प्रेम करने वाले) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4387.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, Hanuman was delighted. The Lord is so loving to those who take refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4387.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बचन (words) / हरष (delighted) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) । / सरनागत (those who have taken refuge) / बच्छल (loving/protective) / भगवाना (the Lord) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4387.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4387.essence: Refuge is not weakness; it is where loving protection begins.
ramacharitamanas::4387.simple_meaning: Hanuman feels joyful hearing Ram's words and recognises that Ram lovingly protects anyone who seeks refuge in him.
ramacharitamanas::4387.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing you do not have to defend yourself alone.
ramacharitamanas::4387.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman hears Ram speak about refuge and feels immediate joy. After the fear of being treated as an enemy, he sees Ram's heart clearly: anyone who surrenders is met with protection, not rejection.
ramacharitamanas::4387.modern_relevance: You finally admit you need help, and instead of judgment, someone responds with warmth. That moment of being received is what Hanuman feels here.
ramacharitamanas::4387.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to trust in loving surrender.

ramacharitamanas::4388.verse_sanskrit: सरनागत कहुँ जे तजहिं निज अनहित अनुमानि। ते नर पावँर पापमय तिन्हहि बिलोकत हानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4388.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी फिर बोले-) जो मनुष्य अपने अहित का अनुमान करके शरण में आए हुए का त्याग कर देते हैं, वे पामर (क्षुद्र) हैं, पापमय हैं, उन्हें देखने में भी हानि है (पाप लगता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4388.english_translation: Those who abandon someone who has come seeking refuge, fearing harm to themselves, are wretched and stained by wrongdoing; even looking at them brings harm.
ramacharitamanas::4388.translation_literal: सरनागत (one who has come for refuge) / कहुँ (for) / जे (those who) / तजहिं (abandon) / निज (their own) / अनहित (harm) / अनुमानि (having considered) / ते (those) / नर (people) / पावँर (wretched) / पापमय (full of wrongdoing) / तिन्हहि (them) / बिलोकत (seeing) / हानि (harm)
ramacharitamanas::4388.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4388.essence: Refuge loses meaning the moment fear overrides compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4388.simple_meaning: Anyone who turns away a person seeking refuge, just because they fear trouble, is acting shamefully and wrongly.
ramacharitamanas::4388.simple_insight: Real strength is measured by how safely others can rest with you.
ramacharitamanas::4388.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been caught, and Ram is speaking through the logic of refuge itself. He says that a person who rejects someone who has surrendered out of fear is not noble but stained by wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::4388.modern_relevance: A friend shows up at your door after a breakup, scared and embarrassed, and you think about your own inconvenience. This verse asks whether your comfort matters more than their safety.
ramacharitamanas::4388.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to sheltering the vulnerable.

ramacharitamanas::4389.verse_sanskrit: कोटि बिप्र बध लागहिं जाहू। आएँ सरन तजउँ नहिं ताहू॥ सनमुख होइ जीव मोहि जबहीं। जन्म कोटि अघ नासहिं तबहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4389.verse_hindi: जिसे करोड़ों ब्राह्मणों की हत्या लगी हो, शरण में आने पर मैं उसे भी नहीं त्यागता। जीव ज्यों ही मेरे सम्मुख होता है, त्यों ही उसके करोड़ों जन्मों के पाप नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4389.english_translation: Even one burdened with the killing of millions of priests is not abandoned if that person comes in refuge. The moment a living being turns toward me, the sins of countless births are destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::4389.translation_literal: कोटि (millions) / बिप्र (priests) / बध (killing) / लागहिं (attach, burden) / जाहू (even if) / आएँ (having come) / सरन (refuge) / तजउँ (I abandon) / नहिं (not) / ताहू (that one) / सनमुख (facing toward) / होइ (becomes) / जीव (living being) / मोहि (toward me) / जबहीं (as soon as) / जन्म (births) / कोटि (millions) / अघ (sins) / नासहिं (are destroyed) / तबहीं (then, at that moment)
ramacharitamanas::4389.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4389.essence: Turning toward Ram erases what once seemed unerasable.
ramacharitamanas::4389.simple_meaning: No matter how heavy someone's past may be, coming in refuge changes everything. Turning toward Ram ends the burden of countless wrongs.
ramacharitamanas::4389.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that sincere turning matters more than a stained past.
ramacharitamanas::4389.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Hanuman hears Ram's promise about refuge, the teaching becomes clear: no one is too stained to be received. Ram says that even the worst burden is not a barrier if the heart turns toward him.
ramacharitamanas::4389.modern_relevance: You finally admit what you've done to a friend after months of avoiding their calls. The shame feels huge, but the first honest step toward repair matters more than the whole backstory.
ramacharitamanas::4389.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to the power of sincere turning and trust.

ramacharitamanas::4390.verse_sanskrit: पापवंत कर सहज सुभाऊ। भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥ जौं पै दुष्ट हृदय सोइ होई। मोरें सनमुख आव कि सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4390.verse_hindi: पापी का यह सहज स्वभाव होता है कि मेरा भजन उसे कभी नहीं सुहाता। यदि वह (रावण का भाई) निश्चय ही दुष्ट हृदय का होता तो क्या वह मेरे सम्मुख आ सकता था? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4390.english_translation: A sinful person's natural tendency is that my devotion never pleases him. If he were truly cruel at heart, could he have come before me?
ramacharitamanas::4390.translation_literal: पापवंत (sinful) / कर (of) / सहज (natural) / सुभाऊ (nature) / भजनु (devotion) / मोर (my) / तेहि (to that) / भाव (pleases) / न (not) / काऊ (at all) / जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / दुष्ट (cruel, wicked) / हृदय (heart) / सोइ (that one) / होई (is) / मोरें (before me) / सनमुख (facing) / आव (comes) / कि (whether) / सोई (that one)
ramacharitamanas::4390.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4390.essence: Coming near Ram already shows the heart has not fully closed.
ramacharitamanas::4390.simple_meaning: A dishonest or cruel heart does not naturally enjoy devotion. Coming close to Ram itself shows some openness, not total evil.
ramacharitamanas::4390.simple_insight: You are not rejected for imperfect motives; even approaching with mixed intent can become a turning point.
ramacharitamanas::4390.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is speaking of Ram's mercy while the search for Sita continues. The verse says a truly wicked heart would not even come near Ram. The very act of facing Ram already reveals a hidden openness.
ramacharitamanas::4390.modern_relevance: You open a prayer app after months away, half out of habit and half out of longing. That mixed motive is not a failure — it may be the first crack in the wall.
ramacharitamanas::4390.insight: It shifts the mind from judging entry to noticing the seed of sincerity already present.

ramacharitamanas::4391.verse_sanskrit: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4391.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य निर्मल मन का होता है, वही मुझे पाता है। मुझे कपट और छल-छिद्र नहीं सुहाते। यदि उसे रावण ने भेद लेने को भेजा है, तब भी हे सुग्रीव! अपने को कुछ भी भय या हानि नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4391.english_translation: One with a pure mind finds me. I do not like deceit, trickery, or hidden flaws. Even if Ravana sent him to spy, Sugriva, you need not fear any harm.
ramacharitamanas::4391.translation_literal: निर्मल (pure) / मन (mind) / जन (person) / सो (that one) / मोहि (me) / पावा (finds) / मोहि (me) / कपट (deceit) / छल (trickery) / छिद्र (hidden flaw) / न (not) / भावा (pleasing) / भेद (secret) / लेन (to take) / पठवा (sent) / दससीसा (ten-headed one) / तबहुँ (even then) / न (not) / कछु (any) / भय (fear) / हानि (harm) / कपीसा (lord of monkeys)
ramacharitamanas::4391.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4391.essence: Ram is found by purity, not by clever disguise.
ramacharitamanas::4391.simple_meaning: A pure mind is what brings you close to Ram. He does not welcome deceit or hidden motives. Even a spy cannot shake the safety of sincere devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4391.simple_insight: You can stop performing and start being honest. What is clean in you already knows the way.
ramacharitamanas::4391.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is still moving through danger while speaking with Sugriva by implication through Ram's assurance. Ram says the one with a clean mind reaches him, and even a spy sent by Ravana cannot cause fear or loss.
ramacharitamanas::4391.modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a relationship after weeks of careful half-sentences. The relief is immediate: what matters most is not polish, but whether your heart is clean.
ramacharitamanas::4391.insight: It shifts attention from strategic image-management to inner honesty and trust.

ramacharitamanas::4392.verse_sanskrit: जग महुँ सखा निसाचर जेते। लछिमनु हनइ निमिष महुँ तेते॥ जौं सभीत आवा सरनाईं। रखिहउँ ताहि प्रान की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4392.verse_hindi: क्योंकि हे सखे! जगत में जितने भी राक्षस हैं, लक्ष्मण क्षणभर में उन सबको मार सकते हैं और यदि वह भयभीत होकर मेरी शरण आया है तो मैं तो उसे प्राणों की तरह रखूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4392.english_translation: O friend, all the demons in the world could be slain by Lakshman in a moment. But if he has come here in fear and sought refuge, I will protect him as I would my own life.
ramacharitamanas::4392.translation_literal: जग (world) / महुँ (in) / सखा (friend) / निसाचर (demons) / जेते (as many as) / लछिमनु (Lakshman) / हनइ (can kill) / निमिष महुँ (in a moment) / तेते (all those) / जौं (if) / सभीत (afraid) / आवा (has come) / सरनाईं (for refuge) / रखिहउँ (I will keep/protect) / ताहि (him) / प्रान की नाईं (like life itself)
ramacharitamanas::4392.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4392.essence: Power becomes mercy when someone comes to you in fear.
ramacharitamanas::4392.simple_meaning: Ram says Lakshman could destroy all the demons quickly, but anyone who comes in fear and seeks refuge will be protected like life itself.
ramacharitamanas::4392.simple_insight: Real strength is measured by how you treat the one who is vulnerable, not by how easily you can punish the dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::4392.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been tested and judged. Ram answers the question of what to do with a frightened visitor: Lakshman can defeat enemies, but fear and surrender call forth protection, not violence. This is Ram's mercy in action.
ramacharitamanas::4392.modern_relevance: A stranger shows up at your door after a frightening night, shaking and ashamed. You do not ask what they deserve first. You decide whether you can be safe enough for them to rest.
ramacharitamanas::4392.insight: It shifts you from threat-based judgment to refuge-based care.

ramacharitamanas::4393.verse_sanskrit: उभय भाँति तेहि आनहु हँसि कह कृपानिकेत। जय कृपाल कहि कपि चले अंगद हनू समेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4393.verse_hindi: कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी ने हँसकर कहा- दोनों ही स्थितियों में उसे ले आओ। तब अंगद और हनुमान् सहित सुग्रीवजी 'कपालु श्री रामजी की जय हो' कहते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4393.english_translation: Smiling, the abode of mercy said, "Bring him either way." Then Angad and Hanuman set out, crying, "Victory to the compassionate Lord," and went with Hanuman beside them.
ramacharitamanas::4393.translation_literal: उभय भाँति (in both ways) / तेहि (him) / आनहु (bring) / हँसि (smiling) / कह (said) / कृपानिकेत (abode of mercy) / जय (victory) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / कहि (saying) / कपि (monkey) / चले (went) / अंगद (Angad) / हनू (Hanuman) / समेत (together with)
ramacharitamanas::4393.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4393.essence: Compassion brings the seeker in before fear can turn them away.
ramacharitamanas::4393.simple_meaning: Ram says Vibhishana should be brought to him no matter which way it happens. Angad and Hanuman leave with joy and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4393.simple_insight: Mercy does not hesitate. It makes room for the one who comes in trust.
ramacharitamanas::4393.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Vibhishana has sought refuge, Ram smiles and tells the monkeys to bring him in either way. The mission is no longer suspicion or strategy; it is welcome. Angad and Hanuman go, praising Ram's compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4393.modern_relevance: Someone finally admits they need help, and you do not make them prove themselves first. You open the door, steady and unguarded, because mercy is stronger than doubt.
ramacharitamanas::4393.insight: It shifts the mind from testing a seeker to receiving them with trust.

ramacharitamanas::4394.verse_sanskrit: सादर तेहि आगें करि बानर। चले जहाँ रघुपति करुनाकर॥ दूरिहि ते देखे द्वौ भ्राता। नयनानंद दान के दाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4394.verse_hindi: विभीषणजी को आदर सहित आगे करके वानर फिर वहाँ चले, जहाँ करुणा की खान श्री रघुनाथजी थे। नेत्रों को आनंद का दान देने वाले (अत्यंत सुखद) दोनों भाइयों को विभीषणजी ने दूर ही से देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4394.english_translation: Placing Vibhishana respectfully in front, the monkeys went on to where Raghupati, the compassionate one, was. From a distance, Vibhishana saw the two brothers, the givers of delight to the eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4394.translation_literal: सादर (with respect) / तेहि (him) / आगें (in front) / करि (having made) / बानर (monkeys) / चले (went) / जहाँ (where) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / करुनाकर (ocean of compassion) / दूरिहि (from a distance) / ते (he) / देखे (saw) / द्वौ (two) / भ्राता (brothers) / नयनानंद (delight of the eyes) / दान (giving) / के (of) / दाता (givers)
ramacharitamanas::4394.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4394.essence: Respect opens the way before devotion speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4394.simple_meaning: The monkeys escort Vibhishana toward Ram, and Vibhishana sees Ram and Lakshman from afar.
ramacharitamanas::4394.simple_insight: Some meetings begin with reverence before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4394.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman and the monkeys bring Vibhishana forward with respect toward Ram. Before anyone speaks, Vibhishana catches sight of the two brothers from a distance, and the moment itself carries the weight of surrender and welcome.
ramacharitamanas::4394.modern_relevance: You walk into a room behind someone who has vouched for you, and the whole atmosphere changes before you say a word.
ramacharitamanas::4394.insight: It shows how trust, introduction, and presence can create belonging before explanation.

ramacharitamanas::4395.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि राम छबिधाम बिलोकी। रहेउ ठटुकि एकटक पल रोकी॥ भुज प्रलंब कंजारुन लोचन। स्यामल गात प्रनत भय मोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4395.verse_hindi: फिर शोभा के धाम श्री रामजी को देखकर वे पलक (मारना) रोककर ठिठककर (स्तब्ध होकर) एकटक देखते ही रह गए। भगवान् की विशाल भुजाएँ हैं लाल कमल के समान नेत्र हैं और शरणागत के भय का नाश करने वाला साँवला शरीर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4395.english_translation: Then he looked again at Ram's radiant form and stood still, eyes fixed without blinking. Ram's long arms, red-lotus eyes, and dark body free the sheltered from fear.
ramacharitamanas::4395.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / राम (Ram) / छबिधाम (abode of beauty) / बिलोकी (having seen) / रहेउ (he remained) / ठटुकि (stunned) / एकटक (one-pointed) / पल (moment) / रोकी (stopping) / भुज (arms) / प्रलंब (long) / कंजारुन (lotus-red) / लोचन (eyes) / स्यामल (dark) / गात (body) / प्रनत (for the surrendered) / भय (fear) / मोचन (releaser)
ramacharitamanas::4395.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4395.essence: Ram's beauty does what fear cannot: it makes you still and safe.
ramacharitamanas::4395.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's beauty leaves the devotee stunned and motionless. His form is not just beautiful; it brings fearlessness to anyone who seeks refuge in him.
ramacharitamanas::4395.simple_insight: A single moment of true seeing can quiet fear more deeply than argument.
ramacharitamanas::4395.detailed_meaning: Hanuman and the others have reached Lanka and are finally near Ram. Vibhishana looks at Ram and cannot move. The sight of Ram's beauty overwhelms him, and that beauty itself feels like protection.
ramacharitamanas::4395.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm makes your own panic loosen. Nothing is said, but their presence feels safer than all your planning.
ramacharitamanas::4395.insight: It shifts attention from judging appearance to recognising the peace a presence can carry.

ramacharitamanas::4396.verse_sanskrit: सघ कंध आयत उर सोहा। आनन अमित मदन मन मोहा॥ नयन नीर पुलकित अति गाता। मन धरि धीर कही मृदु बाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4396.verse_hindi: सिंह के से कंधे हैं, विशाल वक्षःस्थल (चौड़ी छाती) अत्यंत शोभा दे रहा है। असंख्य कामदेवों के मन को मोहित करने वाला मुख है। भगवान् के स्वरूप को देखकर विभीषणजी के नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया और शरीर अत्यंत पुलकित हो गया। फिर मन में धीरज धरकर उन्होंने कोमल वचन कहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4396.english_translation: His lion-like shoulders and broad chest were beautiful. His face captivated countless Cupids. Seeing that form, Vibhishana's eyes filled with tears, his body thrilled with love, and then, steadying his mind, he spoke gently.
ramacharitamanas::4396.translation_literal: सघ कंध (lion-like shoulders) / आयत उर (broad chest) / सोहा (shone beautifully) / आनन (face) / अमित (countless) / मदन (Cupids) / मन (mind) / मोहा (delighted/captivated) / नयन (eyes) / नीर (water/tears) / पुलकित (thrilled) / अति (very) / गाता (body) / मन (mind) / धरि (holding) / धीर (steadiness) / कही (spoke) / मृदु (soft) / बाता (words)
ramacharitamanas::4396.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4396.essence: Beauty worthy of reverence can steady a wavering heart.
ramacharitamanas::4396.simple_meaning: Ram's beauty overwhelms Vibhishana so deeply that he trembles with tears before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::4396.simple_insight: Real reverence leaves you wordless for a moment before it gives you speech.
ramacharitamanas::4396.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has finally reached Ram after leaving Ravana behind. Standing before Ram's radiant form, he is flooded with love and awe, shaken into tears. Only after steadying himself does he begin the humble confession that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4396.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence silences you for a second — not because you're intimidated, but because something in you recognizes what is noble.
ramacharitamanas::4396.insight: It shows devotion as a bodily response first: tears, trembling, then gentle speech.

ramacharitamanas::4397.verse_sanskrit: नाथ दसानन कर मैं भ्राता। निसिचर बंस जनम सुरत्राता॥ सहज पापप्रिय तामस देहा। जथा उलूकहि तम पर नेहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4397.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मैं दशमुख रावण का भाई हूँ। हे देवताओं के रक्षक! मेरा जन्म राक्षस कुल में हुआ है। मेरा तामसी शरीर है, स्वभाव से ही मुझे पाप प्रिय हैं, जैसे उल्लू को अंधकार पर सहज स्नेह होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4397.english_translation: O Lord, I am the brother of ten-headed Ravana. I was born in the race of demons, O protector of the radiant beings. My body is born of darkness, and I naturally love what is evil, just as an owl loves the night.
ramacharitamanas::4397.translation_literal: नाथ (O Lord) / दसानन (ten-headed one, Ravana) / कर (of) / मैं (I) / भ्राता (brother) / निसिचर (demon) / बंस (race) / जनम (born) / सुरत्राता (protector of the radiant beings) / सहज (natural) / पापप्रिय (fond of evil) / तामस (dark) / देहा (body) / जथा (just as) / उलूकहि (to an owl) / तम (darkness) / पर (on) / नेहा (love/liking)
ramacharitamanas::4397.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4397.essence: Honest surrender begins with admitting your own darkness.
ramacharitamanas::4397.simple_meaning: Vibhishana admits his dark lineage and flawed nature, comparing himself to an owl drawn to night. He is confessing his unworthiness before seeking Ram's protection.
ramacharitamanas::4397.simple_insight: You do not need to hide your brokenness before asking for help.
ramacharitamanas::4397.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana stands before Ram after leaving Ravana's side. He does not defend himself. He names his own darkness, his demon birth, and his attraction to evil, making his surrender complete and honest.
ramacharitamanas::4397.modern_relevance: After a relapse, you sit in your car outside the house and finally text, “I need help.” The honesty hurts, but it also opens the door.
ramacharitamanas::4397.insight: It teaches you to stop performing goodness and speak plainly from your real condition.

ramacharitamanas::4398.verse_sanskrit: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4398.verse_hindi: मैं कानों से आपका सुयश सुनकर आया हूँ कि प्रभु भव (जन्म-मरण) के भय का नाश करने वाले हैं। हे दुखियों के दुःख दूर करने वाले और शरणागत को सुख देने वाले श्री रघुवीर! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4398.english_translation: I have come after hearing your glorious fame, O Lord who destroys the fear of worldly existence. O Raghubir, remover of suffering and giver of peace to those who seek refuge, protect me, protect me.
ramacharitamanas::4398.translation_literal: श्रवन (through the ears) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुनि (hearing) / आयउँ (I came) / प्रभु (Lord) / भंजन (destroyer) / भव (worldly becoming) / भीर (fear) / त्राहि त्राहि (protect, protect) / आरति (suffering) / हरन (remover) / सरन (refuge) / सुखद (giver of peace) / रघुबीर (Raghubir)
ramacharitamanas::4398.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4398.essence: Hearing Ram's name can bring you all the way home.
ramacharitamanas::4398.simple_meaning: Vibhishana comes to Ram after hearing of his fame and asks for protection. He trusts Ram as the one who ends fear and gives peace to anyone who takes refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4398.simple_insight: You do not need perfect strength to begin. Hearing the right name can move you toward safety.
ramacharitamanas::4398.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana stands before Ram after leaving Ravana's side. He does not argue for himself; he simply says he has heard Ram's fame and come for refuge. This is the turning point where surrender becomes speech.
ramacharitamanas::4398.modern_relevance: After months of carrying everything alone, you finally call the one person who can actually help. You do not need a perfect explanation. You need refuge, and you ask for it plainly.
ramacharitamanas::4398.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to open surrender. Help begins when you stop defending your isolation.

ramacharitamanas::4399.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि करत दंडवत देखा। तुरत उठे प्रभु हरष बिसेषा॥ दीन बचन सुनि प्रभु मन भावा। भुज बिसाल गहि हृदयँ लगावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4399.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने उन्हें ऐसा कहकर दंडवत् करते देखा तो वे अत्यंत हर्षित होकर तुरंत उठे। विभीषणजी के दीन वचन सुनने पर प्रभु के मन को बहुत ही भाए। उन्होंने अपनी विशाल भुजाओं से पकड़कर उनको हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4399.english_translation: Seeing him prostrate like that, the Lord was filled with special joy and rose at once. Hearing Vibhishana's humble words, the Lord was pleased in heart. He took him in his broad arms and held him to his chest.
ramacharitamanas::4399.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / करत (doing) / दंडवत (prostration) / देखा (saw) / तुरत (immediately) / उठे (rose) / प्रभु (the Lord) / हरष (joy) / बिसेषा (special) / दीन (humble) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मन (mind) / भावा (was pleased) / भुज (arms) / बिसाल (broad) / गहि (grasping) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लगावा (embraced)
ramacharitamanas::4399.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4399.essence: Humility is enough to bring Ram into your arms.
ramacharitamanas::4399.simple_meaning: Vibhishana bows in complete surrender, and Ram responds with immediate joy, acceptance, and a loving embrace.
ramacharitamanas::4399.simple_insight: There is safety in being received exactly as you are.
ramacharitamanas::4399.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just approached Ram after leaving Ravana's side. He bows low and speaks with humility. Ram is delighted, lifts him up, and embraces him before the next conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::4399.modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth after weeks of pretending you were fine. Instead of judgment, someone listens and pulls you closer. That relief is the point.
ramacharitamanas::4399.insight: It shifts the mind from earning acceptance to receiving it through sincerity and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::4400.verse_sanskrit: अनुज सहित मिलि ढिग बैठारी। बोले बचन भगत भय हारी॥ कहु लंकेस सहित परिवारा। कुसल कुठाहर बास तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4400.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित गले मिलकर उनको अपने पास बैठाकर श्री रामजी भक्तों के भय को हरने वाले वचन बोले- हे लंकेश! परिवार सहित अपनी कुशल कहो। तुम्हारा निवास बुरी जगह पर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4400.english_translation: Embracing him with Lakshman by his side, Ram seated him near himself and spoke words that remove a devotee's fear: “Tell me, Lord of Lanka, how are you and your family? You live in a bad place.”
ramacharitamanas::4400.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / मिलि (meeting) / ढिग (near) / बैठारी (having seated) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / भगत (devotee) / भय (fear) / हारी (remover) / कहु (tell) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / सहित (along with) / परिवारा (family) / कुसल (well-being) / कुठाहर (bad place) / बास (residence) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::4400.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4400.essence: True welcome makes fear loosen at once.
ramacharitamanas::4400.simple_meaning: Ram welcomes Vibhishana kindly, sits him near himself, and speaks in a way that removes fear. He asks after Vibhishana’s well-being and notices the hardship of living in Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4400.simple_insight: Being received with kindness can dissolve fear before any answer is given.
ramacharitamanas::4400.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has brought Vibhishana to Ram in Lanka. After Vibhishana’s humble surrender, Ram sits with him beside Lakshman and speaks gently. This moment shows Ram’s first response to a seeker: warmth, safety, and recognition.
ramacharitamanas::4400.modern_relevance: You walk into a room already braced for judgment, and someone pulls out a chair beside them. Before any explanation, your shoulders drop. That is the kind of welcome Ram gives here.
ramacharitamanas::4400.insight: It teaches you to meet sincere surrender with immediate warmth, not suspicion.

ramacharitamanas::4401.verse_sanskrit: खल मंडली बसहु दिनु राती। सखा धरम निबहइ केहि भाँती॥ मैं जानउँ तुम्हारि सब रीती। अति नय निपुन न भाव अनीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4401.verse_hindi: दिन-रात दुष्टों की मंडली में बसते हो। (ऐसी दशा में) हे सखे! तुम्हारा धर्म किस प्रकार निभता है? मैं तुम्हारी सब रीति (आचार-व्यवहार) जानता हूँ। तुम अत्यंत नीतिनिपुण हो, तुम्हें अनीति नहीं सुहाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4401.english_translation: You live day and night among the wicked. Friend, how can your duty be upheld there? I know all your ways: you are deeply skilled in fairness, and injustice does not please you.
ramacharitamanas::4401.translation_literal: खल (wicked) / मंडली (company) / बसहु (you live) / दिनु राती (day and night) / सखा (friend) / धरम (duty) / निबहइ (is upheld) / केहि भाँती (in what way) / मैं (I) / जानउँ (know) / तुम्हारि (your) / सब (all) / रीती (ways) / अति (very) / नय (fairness) / निपुन (skilled) / न भाव (does not please) / अनीती (injustice)
ramacharitamanas::4401.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4401.essence: Character weakens when you keep living inside corruption.
ramacharitamanas::4401.simple_meaning: Bad company makes it hard to live rightly. Vibhishana is telling Ram that he knows Ram values fairness and cannot abide injustice.
ramacharitamanas::4401.simple_insight: Who you stay around quietly shapes what you tolerate.
ramacharitamanas::4401.detailed_meaning: Vibhishana has just come near Ram in Lanka and is being received with warmth. He speaks with humility, pointing to the corruption around him and praising Ram’s natural fairness. The verse prepares his surrender by showing why he cannot remain there.
ramacharitamanas::4401.modern_relevance: You keep showing up to a group chat where cruelty passes as humor. After a while, you notice your own voice changing. This verse names that slow drift before it hardens.
ramacharitamanas::4401.insight: It shifts attention from isolated intention to the moral pressure of your environment.

ramacharitamanas::4402.verse_sanskrit: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4402.verse_hindi: हे तात! नरक में रहना वरन् अच्छा है, परंतु विधाता दुष्ट का संग (कभी) न दे। (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे रघुनाथजी! अब आपके चरणों का दर्शन कर कुशल से हूँ, जो आपने अपना सेवक जानकर मुझ पर दया की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4402.english_translation: It is better, dear one, to live in hell than to keep company with the wicked. Now that I have seen the feet of Raghunath, I am well, because you have shown mercy to me, knowing me as your servant.
ramacharitamanas::4402.translation_literal: बरु (rather) / भल (better) / बास (dwelling) / नरक (hell) / कर (than) / ताता (dear one) / दुष्ट (wicked) / संग (company) / जनि (do not) / देइ (give) / बिधाता (the Creator) / अब (now) / पद (feet) / देखि (seeing) / कुसल (well-being) / रघुराया (Raghuraya) / जौं (if/because) / तुम्ह (you) / कीन्हि (did) / जानि (knowing) / जन (servant) / दाया (mercy)
ramacharitamanas::4402.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4402.essence: The right company can feel better than comfort itself.
ramacharitamanas::4402.simple_meaning: Bad company is worse than any hardship. Vibhishana says he feels well now because he has seen Ram and received his mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4402.simple_insight: You can feel relief the moment you step away from corrupt company and into grace.
ramacharitamanas::4402.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just come into Ram's presence after leaving Ravana's side. He tells Ram that even hell would be better than the company of the wicked, and that seeing Ram's feet has already given him safety and peace.
ramacharitamanas::4402.modern_relevance: You leave a group chat full of cruelty and feel your chest unclench at once. Sometimes the real relief is not comfort — it's finally standing near what is clean.
ramacharitamanas::4402.insight: It shifts the mind from tolerating harmful company to valuing the peace that comes from choosing the right presence.

ramacharitamanas::4403.verse_sanskrit: तब लगि कुसल न जीव कहुँ सपनेहुँ मन बिश्राम। जब लगि भजत न राम कहुँ सोक धाम तजि काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4403.verse_hindi: तब तक जीव की कुशल नहीं और न स्वप्न में भी उसके मन को शांति है, जब तक वह शोक के घर काम (विषय-कामना) को छोड़कर श्री रामजी को नहीं भजता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4403.english_translation: Until a person turns from desire and worships Ram, the mind finds no real well-being or even dreamlike rest.
ramacharitamanas::4403.translation_literal: तब लगि (until then) / कुसल (well-being) / न (not) / जीव कहुँ (for the living being) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / मन (mind) / बिश्राम (rest) / जब लगि (until) / भजत (worships) / न (not) / राम कहुँ (Ram) / सोक धाम (the house of sorrow) / तजि (leaving) / काम (desire)
ramacharitamanas::4403.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4403.essence: Desire keeps you homeless; Ram gives the mind a place to rest.
ramacharitamanas::4403.simple_meaning: Real peace doesn't come while desire rules the mind. It comes when you turn away from craving and turn toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4403.simple_insight: The mind stops fighting itself when it stops chasing what cannot satisfy it.
ramacharitamanas::4403.detailed_meaning: Vibhishana has just defended his choice to leave Ravana's court and seek Ram. In Lanka's dark atmosphere, he states the heart of devotion: no being finds true ease while trapped in desire and sorrow; only Ram ends that unrest.
ramacharitamanas::4403.modern_relevance: You close the app, then open another one, then another, hoping the restlessness will finally settle. It doesn't. This verse names the deeper cure: stop feeding craving, and let Ram become the center.
ramacharitamanas::4403.insight: It shifts you from chasing relief to placing your trust where rest can actually begin.

ramacharitamanas::4404.verse_sanskrit: तब लगि हृदयँ बसत खल नाना। लोभ मोह मच्छर मद माना॥ जब लगि उर न बसत रघुनाथा। धरें चाप सायक कटि भाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4404.verse_hindi: लोभ, मोह, मत्सर (डाह), मद और मान आदि अनेकों दुष्ट तभी तक हृदय में बसते हैं, जब तक कि धनुष-बाण और कमर में तरकस धारण किए हुए श्री रघुनाथजी हृदय में नहीं बसते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4404.english_translation: Only then do many vices dwell in the heart: greed, delusion, jealousy, pride, and conceit. Only when Raghunath does not dwell in the heart, bow in hand and quiver at the waist.
ramacharitamanas::4404.translation_literal: तब लगि (until then) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बसत (dwell) / खल (vicious ones) / नाना (many) / लोभ (greed) / मोह (delusion) / मच्छर (jealousy) / मद (pride) / माना (conceit) / जब लगि (until when) / उर (in the heart) / न बसत (does not dwell) / रघुनाथा (Raghunatha) / धरें (holding) / चाप (bow) / सायक (arrows) / कटि (at the waist) / भाथा (quiver)
ramacharitamanas::4404.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4404.essence: Without Ram in the heart, the vices take over.
ramacharitamanas::4404.simple_meaning: Greed, delusion, jealousy, pride, and conceit stay in the heart only until Ram takes that place.
ramacharitamanas::4404.simple_insight: Inner corruption fades when the heart is filled with the right presence.
ramacharitamanas::4404.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has brought Vibhishana’s words into the larger truth of devotion. The verse says the heart is not neutral: if Ram does not dwell there, greed, delusion, jealousy, pride, and conceit move in and rule it.
ramacharitamanas::4404.modern_relevance: You can scroll all day, chase approval, and still feel strangely crowded inside. The mind settles when something worth loving takes the central seat.
ramacharitamanas::4404.insight: It shifts attention from fighting every flaw separately to placing the heart under Ram's presence.

ramacharitamanas::4405.verse_sanskrit: ममता तरुन तमी अँधिआरी। राग द्वेष उलूक सुखकारी॥ तब लगि बसति जीव मन माहीं। जब लगि प्रभु प्रताप रबि नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4405.verse_hindi: ममता पूर्ण अँधेरी रात है, जो राग-द्वेष रूपी उल्लुओं को सुख देने वाली है। वह (ममता रूपी रात्रि) तभी तक जीव के मन में बसती है, जब तक प्रभु (आप) का प्रताप रूपी सूर्य उदय नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4405.english_translation: Attachment is a dark night. Desire and aversion thrive in it like owls. They live in the mind only until the Lord's radiance rises like the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4405.translation_literal: ममता (attachment/possessiveness) / तरुन (young) / तमी (night) / अँधिआरी (dark) / राग (desire/attachment) / द्वेष (aversion) / उलूक (owls) / सुखकारी (giving comfort)॥ / तब लगि (until then) / बसति (reside) / जीव (the living being) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / जब लगि (as long as) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रताप (radiance/power) / रबि (sun) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::4405.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4405.essence: Attachment survives only where inner light has not risen.
ramacharitamanas::4405.simple_meaning: Attachment clouds the mind like night. Desire and aversion thrive there until Ram's power brings inner light.
ramacharitamanas::4405.simple_insight: You can stop feeding what distorts your mind and let clarity do its quiet work.
ramacharitamanas::4405.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has reached Lanka and is describing the inner darkness that keeps beings trapped. Possessiveness, craving, and aversion spread only while Ram's presence has not lit the mind. The verse explains why suffering feels self-sustaining.
ramacharitamanas::4405.modern_relevance: You scroll through old messages at 1am, replaying what someone said and what they meant. The loop keeps going because the mind is still in darkness.
ramacharitamanas::4405.insight: It shifts attention from emotional reactivity to the need for clear seeing that dissolves it.

ramacharitamanas::4406.verse_sanskrit: अब मैं कुसल मिटे भय भारे। देखि राम पद कमल तुम्हारे॥ तुम्ह कृपाल जा पर अनुकूला। ताहि न ब्याप त्रिबिध भव सूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4406.verse_hindi: हे श्री रामजी! आपके चरणारविन्द के दर्शन कर अब मैं कुशल से हूँ, मेरे भारी भय मिट गए। हे कृपालु! आप जिस पर अनुकूल होते हैं, उसे तीनों प्रकार के भवशूल (आध्यात्मिक, आधिदैविक और आधिभौतिक ताप) नहीं व्यापते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4406.english_translation: O Shri Ram, seeing your lotus feet, all my fears are gone, and I am now at peace. O compassionate one, whoever you favor is never troubled by the three kinds of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4406.translation_literal: अब (now) / मैं (I) / कुसल (well, at peace) / मिटे (gone) / भय (fears) / भारे (heavy, great) / देखि (having seen) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / तुम्हारे (your) ॥ / तुम्ह (you) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / जा (whom) / पर (on) / अनुकूला (favorable, gracious) / ताहि (that one) / न (not) / ब्याप (afflict) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / भव (worldly existence) / सूला (pains, spears) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4406.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4406.essence: Fear ends where loving refuge begins.
ramacharitamanas::4406.simple_meaning: Hanuman says that just seeing Ram's lotus feet has removed his fear. He adds that anyone favored by Ram is not struck by the three kinds of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4406.simple_insight: Fear softens when you feel held by something greater than your own control.
ramacharitamanas::4406.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally reached Ram's beloved presence through devotion alone. Standing before the Lord's feet, he feels his terror vanish. The verse turns his relief into a wider truth: Ram's grace protects the one who belongs to him.
ramacharitamanas::4406.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room after hearing bad news, and your chest is tight. Then someone you trust sits beside you, and the panic eases. Presence changes everything before any solution arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4406.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to refuge in grace.

ramacharitamanas::4407.verse_sanskrit: मैं निसिचर अति अधम सुभाऊ। सुभ आचरनु कीन्ह नहिं काऊ॥ जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा। तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4407.verse_hindi: मैं अत्यंत नीच स्वभाव का राक्षस हूँ। मैंने कभी शुभ आचरण नहीं किया। जिनका रूप मुनियों के भी ध्यान में नहीं आता, उन प्रभु ने स्वयं हर्षित होकर मुझे हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4407.english_translation: I am a vile creature of the night, with no good conduct at all. Yet the Lord, whose form even sages cannot hold in meditation, joyfully drew me close to his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4407.translation_literal: मैं (I) / निसिचर (creature of the night) / अति (very) / अधम (lowly) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सुभ (good) / आचरनु (conduct) / कीन्ह (did) / नहिं (not) / काऊ (any) / जासु (whose) / रूप (form) / मुनि (sages) / ध्यान (meditation) / न (not) / आवा (came) / तेहिं (that) / प्रभु (Lord) / हरषि (with joy) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / मोहि (me) / लावा (brought)
ramacharitamanas::4407.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4407.essence: Ram's embrace reaches farther than your failures.
ramacharitamanas::4407.simple_meaning: Vibhishana admits his lowly nature and lack of good conduct, yet says Ram still joyfully accepted him and drew him close.
ramacharitamanas::4407.simple_insight: There is relief in being received before you have become perfect.
ramacharitamanas::4407.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana stands before Ram after leaving Ravana's side. He calls himself low and unfit, then marvels that Ram, whose form even sages struggle to hold in meditation, has welcomed him into his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4407.modern_relevance: You walk into a room convinced you've already been judged, but someone listens without flinching. That quiet welcome can undo years of shame.
ramacharitamanas::4407.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to grateful surrender before grace.

ramacharitamanas::4408.verse_sanskrit: अहोभाग्य मम अमित अति राम कृपा सुख पुंज। देखेउँ नयन बिरंचि सिव सेब्य जुगल पद कंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4408.verse_hindi: हे कृपा और सुख के पुंज श्री रामजी! मेरा अत्यंत असीम सौभाग्य है, जो मैंने ब्रह्मा और शिवजी के द्वारा सेवित युगल चरण कमलों को अपने नेत्रों से देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4408.english_translation: O Ram, treasure of grace and joy, my boundless fortune is this: with these eyes I have seen the twin lotus-feet served by Brahma and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::4408.translation_literal: अहोभाग्य (oh, great fortune) / मम (my) / अमित (boundless) / अति (very) / राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / सुख (joy) / पुंज (heap, treasure) / देखेउँ (I saw) / नयन (with eyes) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सिव (Shiva) / सेब्य (served by) / जुगल (twin) / पद (feet) / कंज (lotus)
ramacharitamanas::4408.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4408.essence: Seeing Ram's feet is fortune beyond all measure.
ramacharitamanas::4408.simple_meaning: Hanuman says his greatest blessing is seeing Ram's lotus feet with his own eyes, feet even Brahma and Shiva serve.
ramacharitamanas::4408.simple_insight: Real joy comes from closeness to what is worthy, not from status or possession.
ramacharitamanas::4408.detailed_meaning: Hanuman stands before Ram in Lanka after surviving fear, loneliness, and the search for Sita. Overwhelmed, he calls this meeting his greatest fortune: he has seen Ram's feet, the same feet served by Brahma and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::4408.modern_relevance: After months of chasing recognition, you finally sit beside someone whose presence steadies your whole mind. In that moment, applause feels small and contact feels priceless.
ramacharitamanas::4408.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing achievement to treasuring direct presence with what is sacred.

ramacharitamanas::4409.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु सखा निज कहउँ सुभाऊ। जान भुसुंडि संभु गिरिजाऊ॥ जौं नर होइ चराचर द्रोही। आवै सभय सरन तकि मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4409.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे सखा! सुनो, मैं तुम्हें अपना स्वभाव कहता हूँ, जिसे काकभुशुण्डि, शिवजी और पार्वतीजी भी जानती हैं। कोई मनुष्य (संपूर्ण) जड़-चेतन जगत् का द्रोही हो, यदि वह भी भयभीत होकर मेरी शरण तक कर आ जाए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4409.english_translation: Listen, friend, I will tell you my own nature. Kak Bhushundi, Shiva, and Parvati know it. If a person has become an enemy of all that moves and all that does not move, and comes to me in fear seeking refuge,
ramacharitamanas::4409.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / सखा (friend) / निज (my own) / कहउँ (I tell) / सुभाऊ (nature) / जान (know) / भुसुंडि (Bhushundi) / संभु (Shiva) / गिरिजाऊ (Parvati) / जौं (if) / नर (person) / होइ (is) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / द्रोही (enemy) / आवै (comes) / सभय (fearful) / सरन (refuge) / तकि (seeking) / मोही (me)
ramacharitamanas::4409.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4409.essence: Fearful surrender is enough to reopen the way home.
ramacharitamanas::4409.simple_meaning: Ram says his nature is to accept even someone who has become hostile to the whole world, as long as that person comes to him in fear and seeks refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4409.simple_insight: You do not have to be clean or worthy before turning back. The door opens at the moment you surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4409.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has found Sita and the mood is turning from search to revelation. Ram describes his own nature to Hanuman: even the one who has become hostile to all beings can still come in fear and be received. The next verse explains how quickly that refuge transforms a person.
ramacharitamanas::4409.modern_relevance: After a bitter argument, you sit in the car outside someone's house, rehearsing your apology and your pride at the same time. This verse says the first honest step matters more than the mess you carry.
ramacharitamanas::4409.insight: It shifts the mind from self-exclusion to return: the act of seeking refuge matters more than past estrangement.

ramacharitamanas::4410.verse_sanskrit: तजि मद मोह कपट छल नाना। करउँ सद्य तेहि साधु समाना॥ जननी जनक बंधु सुत दारा। तनु धनु भवन सुहृद परिवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4410.verse_hindi: और मद, मोह तथा नाना प्रकार के छल-कपट त्याग दे तो मैं उसे बहुत शीघ्र साधु के समान कर देता हूँ। माता, पिता, भाई, पुत्र, स्त्री, शरीर, धन, घर, मित्र और परिवार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4410.english_translation: If you give up pride, delusion, and all kinds of deceit, I quickly make you like a saint. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, home, friends, and family.
ramacharitamanas::4410.translation_literal: तजि (giving up) / मद (pride) / मोह (delusion) / कपट (deceit) / छल (fraud) / नाना (many kinds) / करउँ (I make) / सद्य (quickly) / तेहि (that person) / साधु (saintly) / समाना (like) / जननी (mother) / जनक (father) / बंधु (brother) / सुत (son) / दारा (wife) / तनु (body) / धनु (wealth) / भवन (home) / सुहृद (friend) / परिवारा (family)
ramacharitamanas::4410.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4410.essence: Drop ego and pretense, and transformation comes quickly.
ramacharitamanas::4410.simple_meaning: Ram says that anyone who drops pride, confusion, and trickery can quickly become saint-like. The next line lists the bonds of attachment that usually keep the mind tied down.
ramacharitamanas::4410.simple_insight: Freedom begins when you stop pretending and stop clinging.
ramacharitamanas::4410.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Ram is describing the inner conditions that make a person fit for grace. He says that when pride, confusion, and deceit are dropped, transformation comes quickly. The following list shows the ordinary ties that keep people bound.
ramacharitamanas::4410.modern_relevance: You finally admit you were performing, not living. The relief is immediate: once the mask drops, a cleaner way of being becomes possible.
ramacharitamanas::4410.insight: It shifts the focus from self-protection to inner honesty, showing that surrender begins with dropping the mask.

ramacharitamanas::4411.verse_sanskrit: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4411.verse_hindi: इन सबके ममत्व रूपी तागों को बटोरकर और उन सबकी एक डोरी बनाकर उसके द्वारा जो अपने मन को मेरे चरणों में बाँध देता है। (सारे सांसारिक संबंधों का केंद्र मुझे बना लेता है), जो समदर्शी है, जिसे कुछ इच्छा नहीं है और जिसके मन में हर्ष, शोक और भय नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4411.english_translation: Gathering up all the threads of attachment, you tie your mind to my feet with a single cord. You see all beings equally, want nothing, and keep no joy, sorrow, or fear in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::4411.translation_literal: सब कै (of all) / ममता (attachment) / ताग (threads) / बटोरी (gathering) / मम (my) / पद (feet) / मनहि (the mind) / बाँध (bind) / बरि (choosing) / डोरी (cord) / समदरसी (equal-seeing) / इच्छा (desire) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (not) / हरष (joy) / सोक (sorrow) / भय (fear) / नहिं (not) / मन माहीं (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::4411.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4411.essence: Gather every attachment into one devotion, and the mind becomes steady.
ramacharitamanas::4411.simple_meaning: Real devotion gathers every scattered attachment and places the mind on Ram alone. In that state, you see everyone equally and are no longer ruled by desire, joy, sorrow, or fear.
ramacharitamanas::4411.simple_insight: There is relief in giving your heart one true center instead of many competing pulls.
ramacharitamanas::4411.detailed_meaning: Ram is explaining what makes a true devotee. After saying he becomes close to the one who drops pride and deceit, he names the inner shape of that person: all attachments gathered into one cord, the mind tied to his feet, equal vision, and freedom from emotional turbulence.
ramacharitamanas::4411.modern_relevance: You check your phone, your family group, work chat, and old messages before sunrise, already split into pieces. This verse offers a calmer center: one heart, one anchor, less inner noise.
ramacharitamanas::4411.insight: It shifts devotion from scattered attachment to single-pointed surrender and steady emotional balance.

ramacharitamanas::4412.verse_sanskrit: अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4412.verse_hindi: ऐसा सज्जन मेरे हृदय में कैसे बसता है, जैसे लोभी के हृदय में धन बसा करता है। तुम सरीखे संत ही मुझे प्रिय हैं। मैं और किसी के निहोरे से (कृतज्ञतावश) देह धारण नहीं करता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4412.english_translation: How can a good person live in my heart, the way wealth lives in the heart of a greedy person? Saints like you are dear to me. I do not take a body because of anyone else's request.
