ramacharitamanas::4412.translation_literal: अस (such) / सज्जन (good person) / मम (my) / उर (heart) / बस (dwells) / कैसें (how) / लोभी (greedy person) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बसइ (dwells) / धनु (wealth) / जैसें (as) ॥ / तुम्ह (you) / सारिखे (like) / संत (saints) / प्रिय (dear) / मोरें (to me) / धरउँ (I take/assume) / देह (body) / नहिं (not) / आन (other) / निहोरे (at request) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4412.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4412.essence: True devotion makes you dear to Ram without bargaining.
ramacharitamanas::4412.simple_meaning: Ram says that true saints are dear to him, and he comes into the world for those who are devoted and pure-hearted.
ramacharitamanas::4412.simple_insight: Devotion is not a demand made on the divine; it is what draws divine presence close.
ramacharitamanas::4412.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is speaking Ram's message in Lanka after describing the qualities that make someone dear to Ram. The verse turns from moral description to intimacy: Ram says he lives for saints like this, not for selfish requests.
ramacharitamanas::4412.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness is effortless, whose loyalty costs them something, and you feel instantly at ease. That same quality is what this verse calls dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4412.insight: It shifts attention from asking for favors to becoming the kind of person who naturally draws grace.

ramacharitamanas::4413.verse_sanskrit: सगुन उपासक परहित निरत नीति दृढ़ नेम। ते नर प्रान समान मम जिन्ह कें द्विज पद प्रेम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4413.verse_hindi: जो सगुण (साकार) भगवान् के उपासक हैं, दूसरे के हित में लगे रहते हैं, नीति और नियमों में दृढ़ हैं और जिन्हें ब्राह्मणों के चरणों में प्रेम है, वे मनुष्य मेरे प्राणों के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4413.english_translation: Those who worship the divine in a personal form, work for the good of others, keep to righteous conduct and firm vows, and love the feet of the learned are as dear to me as life itself.
ramacharitamanas::4413.translation_literal: सगुन (with attributes / personal form) / उपासक (worshippers) / परहित (others' welfare) / निरत (engaged) / नीति (righteous conduct) / दृढ़ (firm) / नेम (vows, observances) / ते (those) / नर (people) / प्रान (life-breath) / समान (equal) / मम (my) / जिन्ह कें (for whom) / द्विज (learned ones / brahmins) / पद (feet) / प्रेम (love)
ramacharitamanas::4413.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4413.essence: Love for the divine becomes visible as service, discipline, and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4413.simple_meaning: Ram says that people who worship him, help others, keep righteous discipline, and respect the learned are as dear to him as his own life.
ramacharitamanas::4413.simple_insight: Love for the divine shows up as service, discipline, and humility.
ramacharitamanas::4413.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman has reached Lanka and Ram’s words are being remembered as a measure of true devotion. Ram describes the kind of person who lives close to him: one who serves others, keeps steady conduct, and honours the wise.
ramacharitamanas::4413.modern_relevance: You keep your promises when nobody is watching, help without announcing it, and still stay teachable. That combination quietly makes you unforgettable to the people who matter most.
ramacharitamanas::4413.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to visible character and service.

ramacharitamanas::4414.verse_sanskrit: सुनु लंकेस सकल गुन तोरें। तातें तुम्ह अतिसय प्रिय मोरें॥। राम बचन सुनि बानर जूथा। सकल कहहिं जय कृपा बरूथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4414.verse_hindi: हे लंकापति! सुनो, तुम्हारे अंदर उपर्युक्त सब गुण हैं। इससे तुम मुझे अत्यंत ही प्रिय हो। श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर सब वानरों के समूह कहने लगे- कृपा के समूह श्री रामजी की जय हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4414.english_translation: O king of Lanka, listen: all those qualities are yours, and because of them you are very dear to me. Hearing Ram's words, the whole troop of monkeys cried, "Victory to the one whose grace is a host of kindness!"
ramacharitamanas::4414.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / लंकेस (king of Lanka) / सकल (all) / गुन (qualities) / तोरें (yours) / तातें (therefore) / तुम्ह (you) / अतिसय (very) / प्रिय (dear) / मोरें (to me) / राम बचन (Ram's words) / सुनि (hearing) / बानर जूथा (monkey troop) / सकल (all) / कहहिं (say) / जय (victory) / कृपा (grace) / बरूथा (host)
ramacharitamanas::4414.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4414.essence: Virtue makes you naturally dear to the one who sees clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4414.simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana that his virtues make him dear, and the monkey army responds with joyful praise.
ramacharitamanas::4414.simple_insight: Character opens the door to closeness; grace is recognized, not earned by performance.
ramacharitamanas::4414.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram is speaking to Vibhishana after seeing his noble qualities. The monkey army hears Ram's words and bursts into praise. This moment confirms that surrender and goodness are already being received.
ramacharitamanas::4414.modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly does the right thing when no one is watching. People trust them instantly. That kind of steadiness still makes hearts open.
ramacharitamanas::4414.insight: It shifts attention from status to character as the basis of trust and belonging.

ramacharitamanas::4415.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बिभीषनु प्रभु कै बानी। नहिं अघात श्रवनामृत जानी॥ पद अंबुज गहि बारहिं बारा। हृदयँ समात न प्रेमु अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4415.verse_hindi: प्रभु की वाणी सुनते हैं और उसे कानों के लिए अमृत जानकर विभीषणजी अघाते नहीं हैं। वे बार-बार श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों को पकड़ते हैं अपार प्रेम है, हृदय में समाता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4415.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, Vibhishana never feels satisfied, knowing them as nectar for the ears. Again and again he grasps the lotus feet, and his boundless love cannot fit inside his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4415.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / प्रभु कै (of the Lord's) / बानी (words) / नहिं (not) / अघात (satisfied) / श्रवनामृत (nectar for the ears) / जानी (knowing) / पद (feet) / अंबुज (lotus) / गहि (grasping) / बारहिं (again and again) / बारा (times) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समात (fits) / न (not) / प्रेमु (love) / अपारा (boundless)
ramacharitamanas::4415.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4415.essence: Real devotion keeps returning because love cannot be exhausted.
ramacharitamanas::4415.simple_meaning: Vibhishana hears Ram's words as nectar and cannot get enough. His love is so vast that he keeps bowing again and again.
ramacharitamanas::4415.simple_insight: Devotion deepens desire for closeness instead of tiring it out.
ramacharitamanas::4415.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just heard Ram speak to him with grace. The words feel like nectar, but the real flood is love: he keeps touching Ram's feet again and again because gratitude has overflowed beyond restraint.
ramacharitamanas::4415.modern_relevance: You replay a voice note from someone who truly understood you, then listen again just to feel that warmth return. Some words do not get old; they open the heart wider each time.
ramacharitamanas::4415.insight: It shifts devotion from a momentary feeling to a repeating act of reverence and closeness.

ramacharitamanas::4416.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु देव सचराचर स्वामी। प्रनतपाल उर अंतरजामी॥ उर कछु प्रथम बासना रही। प्रभु पद प्रीति सरित सो बही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4416.verse_hindi: (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे देव! हे चराचर जगत् के स्वामी! हे शरणागत के रक्षक! हे सबके हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले! सुनिए, मेरे हृदय में पहले कुछ वासना थी। वह प्रभु के चरणों की प्रीति रूपी नदी में बह गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4416.english_translation: Listen, O divine one, lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of the surrendered, inner knower of every heart. Some desire still remained in my heart; it was carried away by the river of love for the Lord's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4416.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / देव (divine one) / सचराचर (moving-and-unmoving) / स्वामी (lord) / प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (inner knower) / उर (heart) / कछु (some) / प्रथम (first) / बासना (desire) / रही (remained) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / सरित (river) / सो (that) / बही (flowed away)
ramacharitamanas::4416.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4416.essence: Surrender becomes complete when love carries away the last trace of wanting.
ramacharitamanas::4416.simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ram that a small trace of desire still remained in his heart, but love for Ram's feet has carried it away.
ramacharitamanas::4416.simple_insight: You do not have to be perfectly clean before surrendering. Love itself can finish the cleansing.
ramacharitamanas::4416.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana stands before Ram after choosing the side of dharma. He bows and admits that some old desire still lingered in his heart. But Ram's presence and love have swept it away, making his surrender complete.
ramacharitamanas::4416.modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a therapy session: part of you still wants approval, even while you want to change. Naming it is not failure. Being met with care can loosen what self-criticism could not.
ramacharitamanas::4416.insight: It shifts the mind from hiding imperfection to letting devotion or trust complete the work of release.

ramacharitamanas::4417.verse_sanskrit: अब कृपाल निज भगति पावनी। देहु सदा सिव मन भावनी॥ एवमस्तु कहि प्रभु रनधीरा। मागा तुरत सिंधु कर नीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4417.verse_hindi: अब तो हे कृपालु! शिवजी के मन को सदैव प्रिय लगने वाली अपनी पवित्र भक्ति मुझे दीजिए। 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहकर रणधीर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने तुरंत ही समुद्र का जल माँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4417.english_translation: “Now, O compassionate one, grant me your pure devotion, ever dear to Shiva’s heart.” Saying “So be it,” the brave Ram at once asked for the ocean’s water.
ramacharitamanas::4417.translation_literal: अब (now) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / निज (your own) / भगति (devotion) / पावनी (purifying) / देहु (give) / सदा (always) / सिव (Shiva) / मन (mind) / भावनी (dear) / एवमस्तु (so be it) / कहि (saying) / प्रभु (lord) / रनधीरा (brave in battle) / मागा (asked for) / तुरत (at once) / सिंधु (ocean) / कर (of) / नीरा (water)
ramacharitamanas::4417.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4417.essence: The highest gift is devotion itself, and Ram grants it at once.
ramacharitamanas::4417.simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram for pure devotion that is always dear to Shiva. Ram agrees immediately and then asks for the ocean’s water.
ramacharitamanas::4417.simple_insight: The deepest gift is not relief from trouble, but a heart made fit to love the divine.
ramacharitamanas::4417.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has surrendered to Ram and is speaking like a true devotee. He does not ask for power or safety; he asks for devotion itself. Ram accepts at once, and the next step in the mission begins.
ramacharitamanas::4417.modern_relevance: You finally get a quiet moment after a long crisis, and instead of asking for the problem to vanish, you ask for the strength to stay faithful. That is the turn this verse makes.
ramacharitamanas::4417.insight: It shifts desire from external rescue to inner devotion, showing that readiness itself is a gift.

ramacharitamanas::4418.verse_sanskrit: जदपि सखा तव इच्छा नहीं। मोर दरसु अमोघ जग माहीं॥ अस कहि राम तिलक तेहि सारा। सुमन बृष्टि नभ भई अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4418.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) हे सखा! यद्यपि तुम्हारी इच्छा नहीं है, पर जगत् में मेरा दर्शन अमोघ है (वह निष्फल नहीं जाता)। ऐसा कहकर श्री रामजी ने उनको राजतिलक कर दिया। आकाश से पुष्पों की अपार वृष्टि हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4418.english_translation: And said, "Friend, even if your wish is absent, my sight in the world never goes in vain." Saying this, Ram immediately crowned him, and an endless shower of flowers fell from the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4418.translation_literal: जदपि (although) / सखा (friend) / तव (your) / इच्छा (wish) / नहीं (not) / मोर (my) / दरसु (sight / vision) / अमोघ (never failing) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / राम (Ram) / तिलक (crown / coronation) / तेहि (that one) / सारा (gave) / सुमन (flowers) / बृष्टि (shower) / नभ (sky) / भई (became) / अपारा (boundless)
ramacharitamanas::4418.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4418.essence: Ram's gaze makes even unasked surrender fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::4418.simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana that even without asking, his sight is never fruitless, then crowns him as king while flowers rain from the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4418.simple_insight: Grace can arrive before you feel ready to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::4418.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has surrendered and asked for refuge. Ram answers not with hesitation but with immediate honor: even if Vibhishana did not ask for this, Ram's presence never fails. He crowns him king and heaven responds with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::4418.modern_relevance: You show up for someone who has already given up on being seen, and you give them trust before they can earn it. That is the kind of recognition this verse carries.
ramacharitamanas::4418.insight: It shifts the mind from earning worthiness to receiving grace and responsibility together.

ramacharitamanas::4419.verse_sanskrit: रावन क्रोध अनल निज स्वास समीर प्रचंड। जरत बिभीषनु राखेउ दीन्हेउ राजु अखंड॥49क॥
ramacharitamanas::4419.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने रावण की क्रोध रूपी अग्नि में, जो अपनी (विभीषण की) श्वास (वचन) रूपी पवन से प्रचंड हो रही थी, जलते हुए विभीषण को बचा लिया और उसे अखंड राज्य दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4419.english_translation: Rama rescued Vibhishana, who was burning in Ravana's fire of anger fanned by the fierce wind of his own breath, and gave him an undivided kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::4419.translation_literal: रावन (Ravana) / क्रोध (anger) / अनल (fire) / निज (own) / स्वास (breath) / समीर (wind) / प्रचंड (fierce) / जरत (burning) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / राखेउ (saved) / दीन्हेउ (gave) / राजु (kingdom) / अखंड (undivided)
ramacharitamanas::4419.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4419.essence: Surrender to Ram turns danger into shelter and loss into belonging.
ramacharitamanas::4419.simple_meaning: Rama protects Vibhishana when Ravana's anger is burning around him, and then gives him lasting kingship.
ramacharitamanas::4419.simple_insight: You are not abandoned when you choose the right side; surrender can open the door to protection and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::4419.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's rage is consuming everything, and Vibhishana stands exposed after choosing Ram over his brother's pride. Ram does not just spare him; he lifts him out of danger and grants him a secure kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::4419.modern_relevance: You leave a toxic family meeting, heart pounding, after finally telling the truth. You expect loss, but instead someone steadies you and helps you rebuild with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::4419.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing surrender to seeing it as the doorway to safety and rightful place.

ramacharitamanas::4420.verse_sanskrit: जो संपति सिव रावनहि दीन्हि दिएँ दस माथ। सोइ संपदा बिभीषनहि सकुचि दीन्हि रघुनाथ॥49ख॥
ramacharitamanas::4420.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने जो संपत्ति रावण को दसों सिरों की बलि देने पर दी थी, वही संपत्ति श्री रघुनाथजी ने विभीषण को बहुत सकुचते हुए दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4420.english_translation: The wealth Shiva gave Ravana for offering his ten heads, that same wealth Raghunath gave Vibhishana with humility.
ramacharitamanas::4420.translation_literal: जो (which) / संपति (wealth) / सिव (Shiva) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / दीन्हि (gave) / दिएँ (by offering) / दस माथ (ten heads) / सोइ (that same) / संपदा (wealth) / बिभीषनहि (to Vibhishana) / सकुचि (with humility) / दीन्हि (gave) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::4420.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4420.essence: The same honor becomes sacred when it is given without pride.
ramacharitamanas::4420.simple_meaning: Ram gives Vibhishana the same royal honor that Shiva once gave Ravana, but he does it humbly and with care.
ramacharitamanas::4420.simple_insight: You are not defined by where grace first appeared. It can return in a purer, kinder form.
ramacharitamanas::4420.detailed_meaning: After Vibhishana surrenders, Ram accepts him fully. The poem recalls how Shiva had once granted Ravana power through sacrifice, then shows Ram giving the same kind of honour to Vibhishana, but without pride and with visible softness.
ramacharitamanas::4420.modern_relevance: Someone who once ignored your effort suddenly trusts you with responsibility. The old wound is still there, but this time the respect arrives quietly, without display.
ramacharitamanas::4420.insight: It shifts the mind from earning worth through struggle to receiving honour through surrender and right alignment.

ramacharitamanas::4421.verse_sanskrit: अस प्रभु छाड़ि भजहिं जे आना। ते नर पसु बिनु पूँछ बिषाना॥ निज जन जानि ताहि अपनावा। प्रभु सुभाव कपि कुल मन भावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4421.verse_hindi: ऐसे परम कृपालु प्रभु को छोड़कर जो मनुष्य दूसरे को भजते हैं, वे बिना सींग-पूँछ के पशु हैं। अपना सेवक जानकर विभीषण को श्री रामजी ने अपना लिया। प्रभु का स्वभाव वानरकुल के मन को (बहुत) भाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4421.english_translation: Those who abandon such a gracious Lord and worship someone else are beasts without horns or tails. Recognizing Vibhishana as his own servant, Lord Rama accepted him. The Lord's nature delighted the minds of the monkey race.
ramacharitamanas::4421.translation_literal: अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / छाड़ि (leaving) / भजहिं (worship) / जे (who) / आना (another) / ते (they) / नर (men) / पसु (beasts) / बिनु (without) / पूँछ (tail) / बिषाना (horns) / निज (own) / जन (servant) / जानि (knowing) / ताहि (him) / अपनावा (accepted) / प्रभु (Lord's) / सुभाव (nature) / कपि (monkey) / कुल (race) / मन (mind) / भावा (pleased)
ramacharitamanas::4421.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4421.essence: Ram's own nature makes surrender feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::4421.simple_meaning: Only Ram deserves full devotion. Those who turn away from him lose their true humanity. Ram welcomed Vibhishana because he saw him as one of his own, and that loving nature pleased the monkey army.
ramacharitamanas::4421.simple_insight: You are safest when you place your trust where mercy is certain.
ramacharitamanas::4421.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's brother Vibhishana has come over to Ram, the poem pauses to explain why this matters. Ram accepts him without suspicion, and the monkeys rejoice at a Lord whose nature is to welcome the sincere.
ramacharitamanas::4421.modern_relevance: You finally tell the one person who can help you the whole truth, even though it makes you feel exposed. The relief is immediate when they respond with welcome instead of judgment.
ramacharitamanas::4421.insight: It shifts devotion from fear to confidence: the heart can move toward Ram without holding back.

ramacharitamanas::4422.verse_sanskrit: पुनि सर्बग्य सर्ब उर बासी। सर्बरूप सब रहित उदासी॥ बोले बचन नीति प्रतिपालक। कारन मनुज दनुज कुल घालक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4422.verse_hindi: फिर सब कुछ जानने वाले, सबके हृदय में बसने वाले, सर्वरूप (सब रूपों में प्रकट), सबसे रहित, उदासीन, कारण से (भक्तों पर कृपा करने के लिए) मनुष्य बने हुए तथा राक्षसों के कुल का नाश करने वाले श्री रामजी नीति की रक्षा करने वाले वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4422.english_translation: Then the all-knowing one, dwelling in every heart, present in every form, yet beyond all forms and untouched, spoke words that uphold right conduct: the cause of human birth and the destroyer of the demon clans.
ramacharitamanas::4422.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / सर्ब (all) / उर बासी (dweller in the heart) / सर्बरूप (all-forms) / सब रहित (free from all) / उदासी (untouched, detached) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / नीति (right conduct) / प्रतिपालक (upholder) / कारन (cause) / मनुज (human) / दनुज (demon) / कुल (clan) / घालक (destroyer)
ramacharitamanas::4422.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4422.essence: The one beyond all forms still speaks through form to restore right order.
ramacharitamanas::4422.simple_meaning: Ram is all-knowing, present in every heart, and beyond every form. From that place, he speaks as the upholder of right conduct and the destroyer of demonic forces.
ramacharitamanas::4422.simple_insight: There is comfort in meeting power that is intimate, clear, and never trapped by the world it moves through.
ramacharitamanas::4422.detailed_meaning: After accepting Vibhishana, Ram stands before the next challenge in Lanka. Tulsidas pauses to reveal who is speaking: the one who lives in every heart, yet remains beyond every form. His words are not random; they come from perfect awareness and moral order.
ramacharitamanas::4422.modern_relevance: You hear a voice in a tense room that is calm, precise, and strangely kind. It does not react from ego; it sees clearly, holds its center, and says exactly what needs to be said.
ramacharitamanas::4422.insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to the presence that sees through all appearances without being caught by them.

ramacharitamanas::4423.verse_sanskrit: सुनु कपीस लंकापति बीरा। केहि बिधि तरिअ जलधि गंभीरा॥ संकुल मकर उरग झष जाती। अति अगाध दुस्तर सब भाँति ॥
ramacharitamanas::4423.verse_hindi: हे वीर वानरराज सुग्रीव और लंकापति विभीषण! सुनो, इस गहरे समुद्र को किस प्रकार पार किया जाए? अनेक जाति के मगर, साँप और मछलियों से भरा हुआ यह अत्यंत अथाह समुद्र पार करने में सब प्रकार से कठिन है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4423.english_translation: Listen, lord of the monkeys and warrior of Lanka: how can this deep ocean be crossed? Full of crocodiles, serpents, and fish, it is utterly vast and hard to pass in every way.
ramacharitamanas::4423.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / लंकापति (lord of Lanka) / बीरा (warrior) / केहि बिधि (by what means) / तरिअ (is crossed) / जलधि (ocean) / गंभीरा (deep) / संकुल (crowded, filled) / मकर (crocodiles) / उरग (serpents) / झष (fish) / जाती (kinds, species) / अति (very) / अगाध (bottomless) / दुस्तर (hard to cross) / सब भाँति (in every way)
ramacharitamanas::4423.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4423.essence: The obstacle is so vast that ordinary means are not enough.
ramacharitamanas::4423.simple_meaning: The sea in front of them is huge, dangerous, and seemingly impossible to cross. The speaker is asking how anyone could get across it.
ramacharitamanas::4423.simple_insight: Some problems feel larger than strength alone can solve.
ramacharitamanas::4423.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is in Lanka, and the next task is no longer finding Sita but figuring out how Ram's side can cross the ocean to reach Ravana. Vibhishana names the scale of the obstacle so the answer can rise beyond ordinary effort.
ramacharitamanas::4423.modern_relevance: You open the map and realise the drive is not the problem — the storm, the distance, and the broken bridge are. Before action, you have to face the size of what stands in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4423.insight: It frames the mission as a real obstacle that requires more than force.

ramacharitamanas::4424.verse_sanskrit: कह लंकेस सुनहु रघुनायक। कोटि सिंधु सोषक तव सायक॥ जद्यपि तदपि नीति असि गाई। बिनय करिअ सागर सन जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4424.verse_hindi: विभीषणजी ने कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए, यद्यपि आपका एक बाण ही करोड़ों समुद्रों को सोखने वाला है (सोख सकता है), तथापि नीति ऐसी कही गई है (उचित यह होगा) कि (पहले) जाकर समुद्र से प्रार्थना की जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4424.english_translation: Vibhishana said, "Listen, Lord of the Raghu clan. Your arrow could dry up millions of oceans. Yet the right course is to go and ask the sea first."
ramacharitamanas::4424.translation_literal: कह (said) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka, Vibhishana) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कोटि (crores, millions) / सिंधु (oceans) / सोषक (drying up) / तव (your) / सायक (arrow) // जद्यपि (although) / तदपि (even so) / नीति (right conduct) / असि (is) / गाई (said) / बिनय (humble request) / करिअ (should be done) / सागर (sea) / सन (with) / जाई (going)
ramacharitamanas::4424.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4424.essence: Power becomes righteous when it begins with humility.
ramacharitamanas::4424.simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ram that even though Ram could force the sea to part, the proper way is to approach it respectfully first.
ramacharitamanas::4424.simple_insight: Real strength does not rush past courtesy; it begins by honoring the right order.
ramacharitamanas::4424.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Ram's army faces the impossible sea. Vibhishana, now with Ram, points out that Ram could crush the obstacle instantly, but chooses the path of right conduct: first ask, then act.
ramacharitamanas::4424.modern_relevance: You know you could fire off the angry email and end the matter in ten minutes. But you pause, call first, and try the respectful route. That pause is not weakness; it is discipline.
ramacharitamanas::4424.insight: It shifts you from brute force to principled action, where power is guided by restraint and etiquette.

ramacharitamanas::4425.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु तुम्हार कुलगुर जलधि कहिहि उपाय बिचारि॥ बिनु प्रयास सागर तरिहि सकल भालु कपि धारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4425.verse_hindi: हे प्रभु! समुद्र आपके कुल में बड़े (पूर्वज) हैं, वे विचारकर उपाय बतला देंगे। तब रीछ और वानरों की सारी सेना बिना ही परिश्रम के समुद्र के पार उतर जाएगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4425.english_translation: O Lord, your family teacher will think it over and tell a way. Then the whole army of bears and monkeys will cross the sea without effort.
ramacharitamanas::4425.translation_literal: प्रभु (O Lord) / तुम्हार (your) / कुलगुर (family teacher) / जलधि (sea) / कहिहि (will tell) / उपाय (means, way) / बिचारि (after considering) / बिनु (without) / प्रयास (effort) / सागर (sea) / तरिहि (will cross) / सकल (all) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / धारि (having held together)
ramacharitamanas::4425.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4425.essence: The hardest crossing becomes easy when you trust the right guide.
ramacharitamanas::4425.simple_meaning: Vibhishana says the sea will be crossed easily if the right teacher is consulted and a proper plan is found.
ramacharitamanas::4425.simple_insight: You do not always need force; the right guidance can make the impossible feel light.
ramacharitamanas::4425.detailed_meaning: On Lanka’s shore, Hanuman has already shown the sea is not ordinary. Vibhishana now tells Ram that the family teacher of the ocean will consider the matter and reveal a method, so the monkey army can cross without strain.
ramacharitamanas::4425.modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem too large to brute-force, and someone older, calmer, or wiser knows the route. Relief begins when you stop wrestling and ask the right person.
ramacharitamanas::4425.insight: It shifts the mind from panic and force to trust in wise guidance.

ramacharitamanas::4426.verse_sanskrit: सखा कही तुम्ह नीति उपाई। करिअ दैव जौं होइ सहाई। मंत्र न यह लछिमन मन भावा। राम बचन सुनि अति दुख पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4426.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे सखा! तुमने अच्छा उपाय बताया। यही किया जाए, यदि दैव सहायक हों। यह सलाह लक्ष्मणजी के मन को अच्छी नहीं लगी। श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर तो उन्होंने बहुत ही दुःख पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4426.english_translation: Friend, you have suggested a wise plan. Let it be done if fate helps. That advice did not please Lakshman’s mind. Hearing Ram’s words, he felt deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4426.translation_literal: सखा (friend) / कही (spoken) / तुम्ह (your) / नीति (wise) / उपाई (plan) / करिअ (let be done) / दैव (fate) / जौं (if) / होइ (is) / सहाई (helpful) / मंत्र (counsel) / न (not) / यह (this) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / मन (mind) / भावा (pleased) / राम (Ram) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / दुख (sorrow) / पावा (felt)
ramacharitamanas::4426.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4426.essence: Wise restraint can hurt the part of you that wants instant victory.
ramacharitamanas::4426.simple_meaning: Ram approves Vibhishana’s advice but leaves the outcome to divine help. Lakshman is hurt because he wants bold action, not waiting on fate.
ramacharitamanas::4426.simple_insight: Even wise advice can feel painful when your heart wants immediate action.
ramacharitamanas::4426.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has urged caution before crossing the sea. Ram accepts the suggestion, but Lakshman, fierce and ready for battle, is distressed by any hint of delay. The scene turns from strategy to emotion.
ramacharitamanas::4426.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense group chat, and someone suggests waiting instead of acting now. The calm answer makes sense, but your body still wants to strike immediately.
ramacharitamanas::4426.insight: It shows how devotion can include restraint, even when another part of you demands force.

ramacharitamanas::4427.verse_sanskrit: नाथ दैव कर कवन भरोसा। सोषिअ सिंधु करिअ मन रोसा॥ कादर मन कहुँ एक अधारा। दैव दैव आलसी पुकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4427.verse_hindi: (लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा-) हे नाथ! दैव का कौन भरोसा! मन में क्रोध कीजिए (ले आइए) और समुद्र को सुखा डालिए। यह दैव तो कायर के मन का एक आधार (तसल्ली देने का उपाय) है। आलसी लोग ही दैव-दैव पुकारा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4427.english_translation: “My Lord, what can fate be trusted for? Dry up the ocean with anger. Fate is only a support for a cowardly mind; only the lazy keep crying, ‘fate, fate.’”
ramacharitamanas::4427.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / दैव (fate) / कर (of) / कवन (what) / भरोसा (trust) । / सोषिअ (dry up) / सिंधु (ocean) / करिअ (do) / मन (mind) / रोसा (anger) ॥ / कादर (cowardly) / मन (mind) / कहुँ (for) / एक (one) / अधारा (support) । / दैव (fate) / दैव (fate) / आलसी (lazy) / पुकारा (call out) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4427.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::4427.essence: Courage acts first and leaves excuses behind.
ramacharitamanas::4427.simple_meaning: Lakshman rejects passive waiting. He says courage should act directly, not lean on fate as an excuse. A lazy mind blames destiny instead of taking responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::4427.simple_insight: It gives you permission to stop excusing yourself and meet the problem head-on.
ramacharitamanas::4427.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Ram has just heard a suggestion to seek help from the sea's ruler. Lakshman, frustrated by delay, pushes back hard: trust in fate is no support for a brave heart. He wants action, not waiting.
ramacharitamanas::4427.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your inbox hoping the answer will appear, but the hard conversation still hasn’t happened. Lakshman’s words cut through that delay: stop hiding behind uncertainty and do the thing that actually moves matters forward.
ramacharitamanas::4427.insight: It shifts the mind from passive hoping to decisive effort.

ramacharitamanas::4428.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बिहसि बोले रघुबीरा। ऐसेहिं करब धरहु मन धीरा॥ अस कहि प्रभु अनुजहि समुझाई। सिंधु समीप गए रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4428.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर श्री रघुवीर हँसकर बोले- ऐसे ही करेंगे, मन में धीरज रखो। ऐसा कहकर छोटे भाई को समझाकर प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी समुद्र के समीप गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4428.english_translation: Hearing this, Raghubir laughed and said, "That is exactly how we will do it. Keep your mind steady." Saying this, the Lord explained to his younger brother and went near the ocean.
ramacharitamanas::4428.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बिहसि (smiling, laughing) / बोले (spoke) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir) / ऐसेहिं (just so, exactly so) / करब (we will do) / धरहु (hold, keep) / मन (mind) / धीरा (steady, patient) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / प्रभु (Lord) / अनुजहि (to the younger brother) / समुझाई (explaining, reassuring) / सिंधु (ocean) / समीप (near) / गए (went) / रघुराई (Lord of Raghu's line)
ramacharitamanas::4428.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4428.essence: Steady calm can turn a crisis into clear action.
ramacharitamanas::4428.simple_meaning: Ram responds with calm confidence, reassures Lakshman, and walks to the ocean with a steady mind.
ramacharitamanas::4428.simple_insight: Calm is not passivity; it can be the strongest way to meet a hard moment.
ramacharitamanas::4428.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just challenged the idea of waiting on fate. Ram smiles, answers without fear, and gently steadies his brother. Then he goes to the seashore, ready to act. The scene shifts from argument to composed resolve.
ramacharitamanas::4428.modern_relevance: You are standing at the edge of a difficult conversation, and your chest is tight. Someone beside you wants urgency; you choose calm, explain clearly, and take the next step without losing yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4428.insight: It teaches you to answer pressure with steadiness, then move forward with composed action.

ramacharitamanas::4429.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम प्रनाम कीन्ह सिरु नाई। बैठे पुनि तट दर्भ डसाई॥ जबहिं बिभीषन प्रभु पहिं आए। पाछें रावन दूत पठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4429.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पहले सिर नवाकर प्रणाम किया। फिर किनारे पर कुश बिछाकर बैठ गए। इधर ज्यों ही विभीषणजी प्रभु के पास आए थे, त्यों ही रावण ने उनके पीछे दूत भेजे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4429.english_translation: He first bowed his head in reverence and sat down on the shore on a mat of kusa grass. Just then Vibhishana came to the Lord, and behind him Ravana sent messengers.
ramacharitamanas::4429.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / प्रनाम (reverent bow) / कीन्ह (did) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bending) / बैठे (sat) / पुनि (then) / तट (shore) / दर्भ (kusa grass) / डसाई (spread) / जबहिं (just then) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / प्रभु (Lord) / पहिं (near) / आए (came) / पाछें (behind) / रावन (Ravana) / दूत (messengers) / पठाए (sent)
ramacharitamanas::4429.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4429.essence: A true turn toward refuge begins with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4429.simple_meaning: Vibhishana comes respectfully to Ram and sits near him on the shore, while Ravana sends messengers after him.
ramacharitamanas::4429.simple_insight: Real refuge begins with a bow, not with control.
ramacharitamanas::4429.detailed_meaning: On the seashore, Hanuman and Ram are in the middle of a tense pause before the crossing. Vibhishana arrives and bows to Ram, choosing refuge over his brother's side. At the same moment, Ravana answers with messengers, showing how far apart the two brothers now stand.
ramacharitamanas::4429.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where loyalty is already splitting apart a family. One person lowers their head and seeks the right place; another sends pressure behind them. The verse holds both choices in one frame.
ramacharitamanas::4429.insight: It shifts attention from force and reaction to the quiet power of choosing the right company.

ramacharitamanas::4430.verse_sanskrit: सकल चरित तिन्ह देखे धरें कपट कपि देह। प्रभु गुन हृदयँ सराहहिं सरनागत पर नेह ॥
ramacharitamanas::4430.verse_hindi: कपट से वानर का शरीर धारण कर उन्होंने सब लीलाएँ देखीं। वे अपने हृदय में प्रभु के गुणों की और शरणागत पर उनके स्नेह की सराहना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4430.english_translation: Having seen all the events while wearing a monkey disguise, he praised the Lord's virtues in his heart and the Lord's affection for those who take refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4430.translation_literal: सकल (all) / चरित (deeds, events) / तिन्ह (those) / देखे (saw) / धरें (wearing, taking on) / कपट (disguise, deceit) / कपि (monkey) / देह (body) / प्रभु (Lord) / गुन (virtues) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सराहहिं (praised) / सरनागत (one who has come for refuge) / पर (on) / नेह (affection, love)
ramacharitamanas::4430.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4430.essence: Disguise cannot interrupt a heart fixed on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4430.simple_meaning: Hanuman, disguised as a monkey, saw everything in Lanka and quietly praised Ram's virtues and his care for anyone who seeks refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4430.simple_insight: Real devotion keeps honoring the divine even while you are hidden, uncertain, or in hostile surroundings.
ramacharitamanas::4430.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has taken a monkey form to move unseen. After observing everything, he inwardly praises Ram's qualities and Ram's love for anyone who surrenders. This moment shows devotion staying steady even before the mission is complete.
ramacharitamanas::4430.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where nobody knows what you're carrying inside. Instead of performing, you stay inwardly loyal to what you love and quietly remember who protects you.
ramacharitamanas::4430.insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to inward allegiance, showing that devotion can continue without announcement.

ramacharitamanas::4431.verse_sanskrit: प्रगट बखानहिं राम सुभाऊ। अति सप्रेम गा बिसरि दुराऊ॥ रिपु के दूत कपिन्ह तब जाने। सकल बाँधि कपीस पहिं आने ॥
ramacharitamanas::4431.verse_hindi: फिर वे प्रकट रूप में भी अत्यंत प्रेम के साथ श्री रामजी के स्वभाव की बड़ाई करने लगे उन्हें दुराव (कपट वेश) भूल गया। सब वानरों ने जाना कि ये शत्रु के दूत हैं और वे उन सबको बाँधकर सुग्रीव के पास ले आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4431.english_translation: Then, openly and with great love, they praised Ram's nature and forgot the disguise. The monkeys recognized them as the enemy's messengers and brought them, bound, to Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::4431.translation_literal: प्रगट (openly) / बखानहिं (they praise) / राम (Ram) / सुभाऊ (nature, character) / अति (very) / सप्रेम (with love) / गा (sang) / बिसरि (forgot) / दुराऊ (concealment, disguise) / रिपु (enemy) / के (of) / दूत (messengers) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / तब (then) / जाने (knew) / सकल (all) / बाँधि (binding) / कपीस (Sugriva, lord of monkeys) / पहिं (to) / आने (brought)
ramacharitamanas::4431.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4431.essence: Love for Ram makes disguise impossible to keep.
ramacharitamanas::4431.simple_meaning: In their true form, they praised Ram with love and forgot their disguise. The monkeys then recognized them as enemy messengers and brought them bound to Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::4431.simple_insight: Love for Ram can be so natural that false appearances fall away on their own.
ramacharitamanas::4431.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman's disguised visit in Lanka, the scene shifts to the monkey camp. The spies are exposed, but the verse lingers on the deeper movement: once Ram is truly praised, concealment loses its hold and the enemy's messengers are taken before Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::4431.modern_relevance: You keep acting composed in a room full of strangers, but one sincere conversation makes the mask slip. What you truly love shows before your cover does.
ramacharitamanas::4431.insight: It shifts attention from disguise and strategy to the power of heartfelt speech to reveal allegiance.

ramacharitamanas::4432.verse_sanskrit: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु सब बानर। अंग भंग करि पठवहु निसिचर॥ सुनि सुग्रीव बचन कपि धाए। बाँधि कटक चहु पास फिराए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4432.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव ने कहा- सब वानरों! सुनो, राक्षसों के अंग-भंग करके भेज दो। सुग्रीव के वचन सुनकर वानर दौड़े। दूतों को बाँधकर उन्होंने सेना के चारों ओर घुमाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4432.english_translation: Sugriva said, 'Listen, all you monkeys: maim the demons and send them back.' Hearing Sugriva's command, the monkeys rushed forward. They bound the messengers and marched them around the camp on all sides.
ramacharitamanas::4432.translation_literal: कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सुनहु (listen) / सब (all) / बानर (monkeys) / अंग भंग (mangling the limbs) / करि (having done) / पठवहु (send) / निसिचर (demons) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / बचन (words/command) / कपि (monkeys) / धाए (ran) / बाँधि (binding) / कटक (camp/army) / चहु पास (all four sides) / फिराए (made to go around) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4432.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4432.essence: A clear command makes scattered strength move as one.
ramacharitamanas::4432.simple_meaning: Sugriva orders the monkeys to punish the enemy messengers, and the monkeys obey at once.
ramacharitamanas::4432.simple_insight: Clear command turns hesitation into action.
ramacharitamanas::4432.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already exposed Ravana's spies and the mood has shifted from secrecy to open defiance. Sugriva now gives a sharp order, and the monkeys immediately seize the messengers and parade them around the encampment.
ramacharitamanas::4432.modern_relevance: A team finally gets the green light after weeks of waiting, and everyone moves at once. The energy changes the moment one person speaks with authority.
ramacharitamanas::4432.insight: It shows how decisive leadership can instantly organize scattered force into one response.

ramacharitamanas::4433.verse_sanskrit: बहु प्रकार मारन कपि लागे। दीन पुकारत तदपि न त्यागे॥ जो हमार हर नासा काना। तेहि कोसलाधीस कै आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4433.verse_hindi: वानर उन्हें बहुत तरह से मारने लगे। वे दीन होकर पुकारते थे, फिर भी वानरों ने उन्हें नहीं छोड़ा। (तब दूतों ने पुकारकर कहा-) जो हमारे नाक-कान काटेगा, उसे कोसलाधीश श्री रामजी की सौगंध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4433.english_translation: The monkeys beat them in many ways. Even while pleading pitifully, they were not released. Then the envoys cried out, "If anyone cuts our noses and ears, by the oath of the Lord of Kosala, let that be done to him."
ramacharitamanas::4433.translation_literal: बहु प्रकार (many kinds) / मारन (to beat) / कपि (monkeys) / लागे (began) / दीन (helpless) / पुकारत (crying out) / तदपि (even then) / न (not) / त्यागे (released) / जो (whoever) / हमार (our) / हर (nose) / नासा (nose) / काना (ears) / तेहि (that one) / कोसलाधीस (Lord of Kosala) / कै (of) / आना (oath) /
ramacharitamanas::4433.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4433.essence: Pride collapses fast when fear takes over.
ramacharitamanas::4433.simple_meaning: The monkeys capture and beat the enemy messengers, and the messengers plead for mercy. Then they invoke Ram's oath to protect their faces.
ramacharitamanas::4433.simple_insight: It shows how quickly pride turns into fear when power slips away.
ramacharitamanas::4433.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's mission has turned into humiliation for Ravana's envoys. The monkeys punish them, the messengers beg, and then they try to save themselves by invoking Ram's authority. The scene is still moving toward Lakshman’s response.
ramacharitamanas::4433.modern_relevance: A group chat turns cruel after one person is publicly mocked. The loud confidence vanishes, and everyone starts searching for the safest words.
ramacharitamanas::4433.insight: It keeps the focus on the consequences of aggression, not just the thrill of retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::4434.verse_sanskrit: सुनि लछिमन सब निकट बोलाए। दया लागि हँसि तुरत छोड़ाए॥ रावन कर दीजहु यह पाती। लछिमन बचन बाचु कुलघाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4434.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने सबको निकट बुलाया। उन्हें बड़ी दया लगी, इससे हँसकर उन्होंने राक्षसों को तुरंत ही छुड़ा दिया। (और उनसे कहा-) रावण के हाथ में यह चिट्ठी देना (और कहना-) हे कुलघातक! लक्ष्मण के शब्दों (संदेसे) को बाँचो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4434.english_translation: Hearing this, Lakshman called everyone close. Moved by compassion, he smiled and immediately freed them. He said, "Give this letter to Ravana, and tell that clan-destroyer to read Lakshman's words."
ramacharitamanas::4434.translation_literal: सुनि (having heard) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / सब (all) / निकट (near) / बोलाए (called) / दया लागि (feeling compassion) / हँसि (smiling) / तुरत (immediately) / छोड़ाए (freed)॥ / रावन (Ravana) / कर (to the hand of) / दीजहु (give) / यह (this) / पाती (letter)। / लछिमन (Lakshman's) / बचन (words) / बाचु (read) / कुलघाती (clan-destroyer)
ramacharitamanas::4434.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::4434.essence: Compassion can restrain force without weakening the warning.
ramacharitamanas::4434.simple_meaning: Lakshman feels compassion, frees the captive messengers, and sends Ravana a warning letter. The scene shifts from punishment to a direct message.
ramacharitamanas::4434.simple_insight: Mercy can be stronger than anger when you still speak plainly.
ramacharitamanas::4434.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sugriva's angry orders have just led the monkeys to beat Ravana's messengers. Lakshman steps in, softens the punishment with compassion, and turns the moment into a warning for Ravana. The verse bridges cruelty and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::4434.modern_relevance: You catch your team piling on someone who made a mistake, and you stop it before the room hardens. Kindness does not cancel the boundary; it gives the boundary dignity.
ramacharitamanas::4434.insight: It shifts response from retaliation to measured mercy without losing firmness.

ramacharitamanas::4435.verse_sanskrit: कहेहु मुखागर मूढ़ सन मम संदेसु उदार। सीता देइ मिलहु न त आवा कालु तुम्हार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4435.verse_hindi: फिर उस मूर्ख से जबानी यह मेरा उदार (कृपा से भरा हुआ) संदेश कहना कि सीताजी को देकर उनसे (श्री रामजी से) मिलो, नहीं तो तुम्हारा काल आ गया (समझो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4435.english_translation: Then tell that fool in plain words my gracious message: give back Sita and meet Ram, or your end has come.
ramacharitamanas::4435.translation_literal: कहेहु (say) / मुखागर (face-to-face, plainly) / मूढ़ (foolish one) / सन (to) / मम (my) / संदेसु (message) / उदार (gracious, generous) / सीता (Sita) / देइ (having given) / मिलहु (meet) / न (if not) / त आवा (has come) / कालु (death, end) / तुम्हार (your)
ramacharitamanas::4435.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4435.simple_meaning: Hanuman is told to deliver Ram's final warning to Ravana: return Sita and face Ram, or be destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::4435.simple_insight: Some choices leave no middle ground.
ramacharitamanas::4435.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's mission has reached its turning point. After the rakshasas are restrained and released, Lakshman gives the envoys Ram's message to carry back to Ravana: return Sita immediately or meet destruction. The verse is the warning itself.
ramacharitamanas::4435.modern_relevance: You finally send the message you have been avoiding: enough excuses, enough delay, make it right now or face the consequences.
ramacharitamanas::4435.insight: It turns hesitation into a clear boundary and makes the next step unmistakable.

ramacharitamanas::4436.verse_sanskrit: तुरत नाइ लछिमन पद माथा। चले दूत बरनत गुन गाथा॥ कहत राम जसु लंकाँ आए। रावन चरन सीस तिन्ह नाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4436.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर, श्री रामजी के गुणों की कथा वर्णन करते हुए दूत तुरंत ही चल दिए। श्री रामजी का यश कहते हुए वे लंका में आए और उन्होंने रावण के चरणों में सिर नवाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4436.english_translation: The messengers bowed at Lakshman's feet and left at once, praising Ram's virtues. Speaking of Ram's glory, they entered Lanka and bowed their heads at Ravana's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4436.translation_literal: तुरत (immediately) / नाइ (bowing) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / पद (feet) / माथा (head) / चले (went) / दूत (messengers) / बरनत (describing) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (song/story)॥ / कहत (saying) / राम (Ram) / जसु (glory) / लंकाँ (to Lanka) / आए (came) / रावन (Ravana) / चरन (feet) / सीस (head) / तिन्ह (they) / नाए (bowed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4436.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4436.essence: Honor can travel into enemy territory without losing itself.
ramacharitamanas::4436.simple_meaning: The messengers leave respectfully, speaking only of Ram's greatness. When they reach Lanka, they bow even before Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4436.simple_insight: True devotion stays steady even in hostile places.
ramacharitamanas::4436.detailed_meaning: After Lakshman frees the captured messengers, they depart at once. Still praising Ram, they enter Lanka and bow before Ravana. The verse simply marks their movement into the enemy city before Ravana begins questioning them.
ramacharitamanas::4436.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to shrink, but you still carry your values with you. Respect does not mean surrendering your center.
ramacharitamanas::4436.insight: It shows how dignity and courtesy can remain intact under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4437.verse_sanskrit: बिहसि दसानन पूँछी बाता। कहसि न सुक आपनि कुसलाता॥ पुन कहु खबरि बिभीषन केरी। जाहि मृत्यु आई अति नेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4437.verse_hindi: दशमुख रावण ने हँसकर बात पूछी- अरे शुक! अपनी कुशल क्यों नहीं कहता? फिर उस विभीषण का समाचार सुना, मृत्यु जिसके अत्यंत निकट आ गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4437.english_translation: Ravana laughed and asked, "Why do you not speak of your own well-being, Shuka? Tell me about Vibhishana, whose death is now very near."
ramacharitamanas::4437.translation_literal: बिहसि (laughing) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / पूँछी (asked) / बाता (matter, news) / कहसि (do you speak) / न (not) / सुक (Shuka) / आपनि (your own) / कुसलाता (well-being) / पुन (again) / कहु (tell) / खबरि (news) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / केरी (of) / जाहि (whose) / मृत्यु (death) / आई (has come) / अति (very) / नेरी (near)
ramacharitamanas::4437.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4437.essence: Arrogance laughs at danger until danger is already at the door.
ramacharitamanas::4437.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the messenger and asks about Vibhishana, saying death is already close to him.
ramacharitamanas::4437.simple_insight: Pride makes a person speak with contempt right before disaster.
ramacharitamanas::4437.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's messenger has reached Ravana's court. Ravana laughs instead of listening seriously, taunts Shuka, and then asks about Vibhishana, the brother who chose righteousness. The scene shows Ravana's arrogance hardening just before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4437.modern_relevance: Someone gets a warning email, smirks at it, and keeps scrolling as if consequences are for other people. That is Ravana's mind in one breath.
ramacharitamanas::4437.insight: It shows how ego turns danger into a joke and blinds you to the truth.

ramacharitamanas::4438.verse_sanskrit: करत राज लंका सठ त्यागी। होइहि जव कर कीट अभागी॥ पुनि कहु भालु कीस कटकाई। कठिन काल प्रेरित चलि आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4438.verse_hindi: मूर्ख ने राज्य करते हुए लंका को त्याग दिया। अभागा अब जौ का कीड़ा (घुन) बनेगा (जौ के साथ जैसे घुन भी पिस जाता है, वैसे ही नर वानरों के साथ वह भी मारा जाएगा), फिर भालु और वानरों की सेना का हाल कह, जो कठिन काल की प्रेरणा से यहाँ चली आई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4438.english_translation: The fool has abandoned Lanka while ruling it. Now he will be ground down like a cursed grain. Tell me next about the army of bears and monkeys that has come here, driven by harsh fate.
ramacharitamanas::4438.translation_literal: करत (while doing) / राज (rule, kingship) / लंका (Lanka) / सठ (fool, wicked one) / त्यागी (abandoned) / होइहि (will become) / जव (barley) / कर (of) / कीट (insect, weevil) / अभागी (unlucky, cursed) / पुनि (again) / कहु (tell) / भालु (bears) / कीस (monkeys) / कटकाई (army, host) / कठिन (hard, severe) / काल (time, fate) / प्रेरित (impelled) / चलि (having come) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::4438.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4438.essence: Pride laughs at danger before danger reaches the door.
ramacharitamanas::4438.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the supposed traitor and asks for news of the bears and monkeys that have arrived against Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4438.simple_insight: Pride makes danger look small until it is already at the gate.
ramacharitamanas::4438.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just heard that one of his own has turned away and that an enemy force has arrived. He sneers at the defection, dismisses the threat, and demands more news. The verse is part of his arrogant reaction, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::4438.modern_relevance: You hear bad news in a meeting and immediately brush it off as impossible. That first wave of denial can be the most dangerous part.
ramacharitamanas::4438.insight: It shows how ego dismisses warning signs instead of preparing for them.

ramacharitamanas::4439.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह के जीवन कर रखवारा। भयउ मृदुल चित सिंधु बिचारा॥ कहु तपसिन्ह कै बात बहोरी। जिन्ह के हृदयँ त्रास अति मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4439.verse_hindi: और जिनके जीवन का रक्षक कोमल चित्त वाला बेचारा समुद्र बन गया है (अर्थात् ) उनके और राक्षसों के बीच में यदि समुद्र न होता तो अब तक राक्षस उन्हें मारकर खा गए होते। फिर उन तपस्वियों की बात बता, जिनके हृदय में मेरा बड़ा डर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4439.english_translation: And the gentle ocean has become the protector of their lives. Tell me more about those ascetics whose hearts are filled with fear of me.
ramacharitamanas::4439.translation_literal: जिन्ह के (whose) / जीवन (life) / कर (of) / रखवारा (protector) / भयउ (became) / मृदुल (gentle) / चित (mind/heart) / सिंधु (ocean) / बिचारा (poor, helpless) / कहु (tell) / तपसिन्ह (of the ascetics) / कै (of) / बात (matter) / बहोरी (again) / जिन्ह के (whose) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / त्रास (fear) / अति (very) / मोरी (of me)
ramacharitamanas::4439.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4439.essence: Pride laughs at danger while secretly feeding on fear.
ramacharitamanas::4439.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the sea for protecting the lives of those beyond it, then asks about ascetics who fear him deeply.
ramacharitamanas::4439.simple_insight: Pride makes danger sound like comedy, even when fear is still running underneath.
ramacharitamanas::4439.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is questioning the disguised Hanuman after hearing of enemies across the sea. He boasts about the ocean, then turns to the ascetics who supposedly tremble before him. The verse shows his ego and hunger to measure his own terror by others' fear.
ramacharitamanas::4439.modern_relevance: Someone laughs off a problem in a meeting, then spends the rest of the day checking who is against them. That split between swagger and insecurity is Ravana's mind.
ramacharitamanas::4439.insight: It reveals how ego turns fear into mockery and keeps searching for proof of its own power.

ramacharitamanas::4440.verse_sanskrit: की भइ भेंट कि फिरि गए श्रवन सुजसु सुनि मोर। कहसि न रिपु दल तेज बल बहुत चकित चित तोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4440.verse_hindi: उनसे तेरी भेंट हुई या वे कानों से मेरा सुयश सुनकर ही लौट गए? शत्रु सेना का तेज और बल बताता क्यों नहीं? तेरा चित्त बहुत ही चकित (भौंचक्का सा) हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4440.english_translation: Did they meet you, or did they turn back after hearing my fame? Why do you not speak of the enemy army's power and strength? Your mind seems greatly stunned.
ramacharitamanas::4440.translation_literal: की (whether) / भइ (happened) / भेंट (meeting) / कि (or) / फिरि (turning back) / गए (went) / श्रवन (with the ears) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुनि (hearing) / मोर (my) / कहसि (you say/tell) / न (not) / रिपु (enemy) / दल (army) / तेज (splendor/force) / बल (strength) / बहुत (very) / चकित (astonished) / चित (mind) / तोर (your)
ramacharitamanas::4440.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4440.essence: Pride hears a challenge, not a truth.
ramacharitamanas::4440.simple_meaning: Ravana asks whether Hanuman met the enemy or merely heard his fame and fled, then demands news of the enemy army. He notices Hanuman looks shaken.
ramacharitamanas::4440.simple_insight: Pride makes him read fear into silence and miss the truth right in front of him.
ramacharitamanas::4440.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana questions the stranger who has entered his court after the search for Sita. He wonders if the visitor met Ram's side or fled after hearing his fame, and he presses for details about the enemy force. The verse shows Ravana's suspicion and Hanuman's calm pressure.
ramacharitamanas::4440.modern_relevance: Someone storms into a room after a tense meeting and starts asking sharp questions, trying to control the story before hearing it. Pride often talks first because it is afraid to listen.
ramacharitamanas::4440.insight: It exposes how ego interrogates others to protect itself instead of facing reality directly.

ramacharitamanas::4441.verse_sanskrit: नाथ कृपा करि पूँछेहु जैसें। मानहु कहा क्रोध तजि तैसें॥ मिला जाइ जब अनुज तुम्हारा। जातहिं राम तिलक तेहि सारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4441.verse_hindi: (दूत ने कहा-) हे नाथ! आपने जैसे कृपा करके पूछा है, वैसे ही क्रोध छोड़कर मेरा कहना मानिए (मेरी बात पर विश्वास कीजिए)। जब आपका छोटा भाई श्री रामजी से जाकर मिला, तब उसके पहुँचते ही श्री रामजी ने उसको राजतिलक कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4441.english_translation: O lord, kindly listen and accept my words, setting aside your anger. When your younger brother met Ram, Ram immediately crowned him on arrival.
ramacharitamanas::4441.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / कृपा करि (having shown grace) / पूँछेहु (you asked) / जैसें (as) / मानहु (accept) / कहा (what is said) / क्रोध (anger) / तजि (leaving) / तैसें (thus)॥ / मिला (met) / जाइ (having gone) / जब (when) / अनुज (younger brother) / तुम्हारा (your) / जातहिं (upon going) / राम (Ram) / तिलक (coronation) / तेहि (that) / सारा (entirely, at once) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4441.speaker: Ravana's messenger
ramacharitamanas::4441.essence: Ram honors even the one who leaves his side for righteousness.
ramacharitamanas::4441.simple_meaning: The messenger asks Ravana to calm down and trust his report. He says that when Vibhishana met Ram, Ram honored him immediately.
ramacharitamanas::4441.simple_insight: Pride makes you suspicious; humility lets you hear the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4441.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s messenger returns after seeing the enemy camp. He tries to calm his furious king by giving the clearest proof he has: Vibhishana, Ravana’s own brother, was welcomed and honored by Ram at once.
ramacharitamanas::4441.modern_relevance: You’re ready to dismiss bad news because it bruises your ego. Sometimes the most useful message arrives only after you stop defending yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4441.insight: It shows how a messenger appeals to evidence that even a proud listener cannot ignore.

ramacharitamanas::4442.verse_sanskrit: रावन दूत हमहि सुनि काना। कपिन्ह बाँधि दीन्हें दुख नाना॥ श्रवन नासिका काटैं लागे। राम सपथ दीन्हें हम त्यागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4442.verse_hindi: हम रावण के दूत हैं, यह कानों से सुनकर वानरों ने हमें बाँधकर बहुत कष्ट दिए, यहाँ तक कि वे हमारे नाक-कान काटने लगे। श्री रामजी की शपथ दिलाने पर कहीं उन्होंने हमको छोड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4442.english_translation: We said we were Ravana's messengers, and the monkeys bound us and gave us many kinds of pain. They cut our ears and noses, and only released us after we swore by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4442.translation_literal: रावन (of Ravana) / दूत (messengers) / हमहि (us) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (the ears) / कपिन्ह (by the monkeys) / बाँधि (binding) / दीन्हें (gave) / दुख (pain) / नाना (many kinds) / श्रवन (ears) / नासिका (nose) / काटैं (to cut) / लागे (began) / राम (Ram) / सपथ (oath) / दीन्हें (gave) / हम (us) / त्यागे (released)
ramacharitamanas::4442.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4442.essence: Boasting allegiance to power can end in public humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::4442.simple_meaning: The messengers say the monkeys punished them harshly after hearing they came from Ravana, and let them go only when they swore by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4442.simple_insight: Pride can turn a simple message into humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::4442.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's envoys are reporting back after meeting Hanuman and the monkeys. They describe being captured, mutilated, and freed only after invoking Ram's name. The verse supports their warning about the power and fury of Ram's side.
ramacharitamanas::4442.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting to look in control, and leave rattled because the other side saw through you immediately.
ramacharitamanas::4442.insight: It shifts the mind from boasting about position to respecting the force you are facing.

ramacharitamanas::4443.verse_sanskrit: पूँछिहु नाथ राम कटकाई। बदन कोटि सत बरनि न जाई॥ नाना बरन भालु कपि धारी। बिकटानन बिसाल भयकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4443.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपने श्री रामजी की सेना पूछी, सो वह तो सौ करोड़ मुखों से भी वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। अनेकों रंगों के भालु और वानरों की सेना है, जो भयंकर मुख वाले, विशाल शरीर वाले और भयानक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4443.english_translation: O lord, you asked about Ram's army. It cannot be described even with hundreds of millions of mouths. There are many kinds of bears and monkeys, with terrible faces, huge bodies, and fearsome looks.
ramacharitamanas::4443.translation_literal: पूँछिहु (you asked) / नाथ (lord) / राम (Ram) / कटकाई (army) / बदन (mouths/faces) / कोटि सत (hundreds of millions) / बरनि (describe) / न जाई (cannot be done) / नाना (many) / बरन (colors/kinds) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / धारी (having) / बिकटानन (fearsome faces) / बिसाल (huge) / भयकारी (fear-inducing)
ramacharitamanas::4443.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4443.essence: Ram's army is beyond counting and beyond tidy description.
ramacharitamanas::4443.simple_meaning: Ram's army is so vast and varied that no one can fully describe it. It includes many kinds of bears and monkeys, all fierce-looking and enormous.
ramacharitamanas::4443.simple_insight: Some forces are too large for neat description. Their scale itself is the message.
ramacharitamanas::4443.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's messenger is answering questions about Ram's forces. He begins to describe the vast bear-and-monkey army before turning, in the next verse, to the warrior who burned the city. This line is vivid scene-setting, not a completed teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4443.modern_relevance: You try to summarize a whole movement, team, or crisis in one neat sentence, and it fails. Some realities are bigger, wilder, and more alive than your labels.
ramacharitamanas::4443.insight: It shifts attention from exact counting to the overwhelming presence of Ram's forces.

ramacharitamanas::4444.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं पुर दहेउ हतेउ सुत तोरा। सकल कपिन्ह महँ तेहि बलु थोरा॥ अमित नाम भट कठिन कराला। अमित नाग बल बिपुल बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4444.verse_hindi: जिसने नगर को जलाया और आपके पुत्र अक्षय कुमार को मारा, उसका बल तो सब वानरों में थोड़ा है। असंख्य नामों वाले बड़े ही कठोर और भयंकर योद्धा हैं। उनमें असंख्य हाथियों का बल है और वे बड़े ही विशाल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4444.english_translation: The one who burned the city and killed your son has less strength than all the monkeys here. There are countless fierce warriors with the force of countless elephants, vast and terrible.
ramacharitamanas::4444.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / पुर (city) / दहेउ (burned) / हतेउ (killed) / सुत (son) / तोरा (your) / सकल (all) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / महँ (among) / तेहि (that) / बलु (strength) / थोरा (little)॥ / अमित (countless) / नाम (names) / भट (warriors) / कठिन (hard-fierce) / कराला (terrible)॥ / अमित (countless) / नाग (elephants) / बल (strength) / बिपुल (great) / बिसाला (vast)॥
ramacharitamanas::4444.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4444.essence: Even a terrifying enemy is only one part of the larger field of power.
ramacharitamanas::4444.simple_meaning: The enemy who burned your city and killed your son is still weaker than the monkeys here. Their army is full of countless fierce warriors with enormous strength.
ramacharitamanas::4444.simple_insight: Even overwhelming opposition can be sized up clearly when courage is steady.
ramacharitamanas::4444.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is describing Ram's allies and the enemy's strength in the middle of a war briefing. The verse narrows attention to the enemy's power and the scale of the monkey army, preparing the listener for the coming battle rather than offering a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4444.modern_relevance: Before a big presentation, you list the obstacles and realize the room is full of people ready to help. The fear stays real, but it no longer feels larger than your resources.
ramacharitamanas::4444.insight: It shifts attention from panic to realistic assessment of strength on both sides.

ramacharitamanas::4445.verse_sanskrit: द्विबिद मयंद नील नल अंगद गद बिकटासि। दधिमुख केहरि निसठ सठ जामवंत बलरासि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4445.verse_hindi: द्विविद, मयंद, नील, नल, अंगद, गद, विकटास्य, दधिमुख, केसरी, निशठ, शठ और जाम्बवान् ये सभी बल की राशि हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4445.english_translation: Dvivida, Mainda, Nila, Nala, Angada, Gada, Vikatasya, Dadhimukha, Kesari, Nishatha, Shatha, and Jambavan are all masses of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4445.translation_literal: द्विबिद (Dvivida) / मयंद (Mainda) / नील (Nila) / नल (Nala) / अंगद (Angada) / गद (Gada) / बिकटासि (Vikatasya) / दधिमुख (Dadhimukha) / केहरि (Kesari) / निसठ (Nishatha) / सठ (Shatha) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / बलरासि (mass of strength)
ramacharitamanas::4445.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4445.essence: Strength multiplies when capable allies stand together.
ramacharitamanas::4445.simple_meaning: The verse lists powerful monkey warriors and says each one is a storehouse of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4445.simple_insight: Great things are often carried by many capable people, not just one hero.
ramacharitamanas::4445.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is describing Ram's allied army in Lanka. After naming fierce warriors and saying their strength is beyond counting, this line adds more of the same mighty names. It is part of a larger buildup, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4445.modern_relevance: You open a team chat and see names of people who can each handle a crisis. Relief comes from knowing the work is carried by many strong hands, not one exhausted person.
ramacharitamanas::4445.insight: It shifts attention from a single standout to the collective force already present.

ramacharitamanas::4446.verse_sanskrit: ए कपि सब सुग्रीव समाना। इन्ह सम कोटिन्ह गनइ को नाना॥ राम कृपाँ अतुलित बल तिन्हहीं। तृन समान त्रैलोकहि गनहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4446.verse_hindi: ये सब वानर बल में सुग्रीव के समान हैं और इनके जैसे (एक-दो नहीं) करोड़ों हैं, उन बहुत सो को गिन ही कौन सकता है। श्री रामजी की कृपा से उनमें अतुलनीय बल है। वे तीनों लोकों को तृण के समान (तुच्छ) समझते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4446.english_translation: These monkeys are all like Sugriva. There are countless more just like them. By Ram's grace they possess unmatched strength, and they count the three worlds as no more than grass.
ramacharitamanas::4446.translation_literal: ए (these) / कपि (monkeys) / सब (all) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / समाना (equal) । / इन्ह (these) / सम (like) / कोटिन्ह (in millions) / गनइ (to count) / को (who) / नाना (many) ॥ / राम (Ram) / कृपाँ (by grace) / अतुलित (matchless) / बल (strength) / तिन्हहीं (in them) । / तृन (grass) / समान (like) / त्रैलोकहि (the three worlds) / गनहीं (they count) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4446.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4446.essence: Grace turns an ordinary army into something immeasurable.
ramacharitamanas::4446.simple_meaning: Ram's army is vast and mighty. These monkeys are all powerful like Sugriva, and their strength comes from Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4446.simple_insight: Real strength can feel ordinary when it is rooted in grace.
ramacharitamanas::4446.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is describing Ram's monkey allies to Ravana. After naming their champions, he widens the picture: this army is not small or fragile, and its power does not come from pride. Ram's grace makes them fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4446.modern_relevance: A team walks into a crisis with no flashy image, yet everyone moves with quiet confidence. Their courage comes from trust in something larger than personal ego.
ramacharitamanas::4446.insight: It shifts attention from visible size to the source of courage and capability.

ramacharitamanas::4447.verse_sanskrit: अस मैं सुना श्रवन दसकंधर। पदुम अठारह जूथप बंदर॥ नाथ कटक महँ सो कपि नाहीं। जो न तुम्हहि जीतै रन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4447.verse_hindi: हे दशग्रीव! मैंने कानों से ऐसा सुना है कि अठारह पद्म तो अकेले वानरों के सेनापति हैं। हे नाथ! उस सेना में ऐसा कोई वानर नहीं है, जो आपको रण में न जीत सके ॥
ramacharitamanas::4447.english_translation: O Ravana, I have heard that there are eighteen crore monkey commanders. In that army, there is no monkey who cannot defeat you in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4447.translation_literal: अस (thus) / मैं (I) / सुना (have heard) / श्रवन (through the ears) / दसकंधर (O ten-headed one, Ravana) / पदुम (crore / hundred million) / अठारह (eighteen) / जूथप (herd-leader / commander) / बंदर (monkeys) / नाथ (O lord) / कटक (army) / महँ (in) / सो (that) / कपि (monkey) / नाहीं (not) / जो (who) / न (not) / तुम्हहि (you) / जीतै (defeats) / रन (battle) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::4447.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4447.essence: Pride looks small when it faces a force it cannot count.
ramacharitamanas::4447.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that Ram's army is enormous and full of commanders strong enough to defeat him.
ramacharitamanas::4447.simple_insight: Even the enemy's pride starts to shake when faced with a force bigger than ego can measure.
ramacharitamanas::4447.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana and speaks without fear. After describing Ram's mighty monkey allies, he reminds Ravana that this army has countless commanders and no weak link. The point is to warn Ravana that resistance is already futile.
ramacharitamanas::4447.modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting knowing the other side has underestimated you. Calmly, you name the strength they missed — and the room changes.
ramacharitamanas::4447.insight: It shifts the focus from Ravana's confidence to the overwhelming strength already gathered against him.

ramacharitamanas::4448.verse_sanskrit: परम क्रोध मीजहिं सब हाथा। आयसु पै न देहिं रघुनाथा॥ सोषहिं सिंधु सहित झष ब्याला। पूरहिं न त भरि कुधर बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4448.verse_hindi: सब के सब अत्यंत क्रोध से हाथ मीजते हैं। पर श्री रघुनाथजी उन्हें आज्ञा नहीं देते। हम मछलियों और साँपों सहित समुद्र को सोख लेंगे। नहीं तो बड़े-बड़े पर्वतों से उसे भरकर पूर (पाट) देंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4448.english_translation: All of them grind their hands in fierce anger, but Raghunath does not give them the order. We will dry up the ocean, along with its fish and serpents. If not, we will fill it with great mountains.
ramacharitamanas::4448.translation_literal: परम (extreme) / क्रोध (anger) / मीजहिं (rub their hands) / सब (all) / हाथा (hands) / आयसु (order) / पै (but) / न (not) / देहिं (give) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / सोषहिं (we will dry up) / सिंधु (ocean) / सहित (along with) / झष (fish) / ब्याला (serpents) / पूरहिं (we will fill) / न (not) / त (then) / भरि (filling) / कुधर (mountains) / बिसाला (great)
ramacharitamanas::4448.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4448.essence: Power becomes effective only when it waits for the right command.
ramacharitamanas::4448.simple_meaning: The monkey army is furious and ready to destroy the ocean, but Ram has not yet given the command. Their energy is immense, but it still waits for his word.
ramacharitamanas::4448.simple_insight: Even raw power needs the right command before it becomes action.
ramacharitamanas::4448.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has stirred up the monkey host. The warriors burn with anger and boast that they can dry the ocean or bury it under mountains, but they still wait for Ram's order. The verse shows their force, not the final move.
ramacharitamanas::4448.modern_relevance: A team is fired up in a late-night war room, ready to smash the problem. But everyone still waits for the one clear call before charging ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4448.insight: It shifts attention from strength alone to disciplined action under rightful direction.

ramacharitamanas::4449.verse_sanskrit: मर्दि गर्द मिलवहिं दससीसा। ऐसेइ बचन कहहिं सब कीसा॥ गर्जहिं तर्जहिं सहज असंका। मानहुँ ग्रसन चहत हहिं लंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4449.verse_hindi: और रावण को मसलकर धूल में मिला देंगे। सब वानर ऐसे ही वचन कह रहे हैं। सब सहज ही निडर हैं, इस प्रकार गरजते और डपटते हैं मानो लंका को निगल ही जाना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4449.english_translation: And they will crush Ravana into dust. All the monkeys speak like this. They roar and threaten without fear, as if they mean to swallow Lanka itself.
ramacharitamanas::4449.translation_literal: मर्दि (crush) / गर्द (dust) / मिलवहिं (will mix together) / दससीसा (ten-headed one, Ravana) / ऐसेइ (just like this) / बचन (words) / कहहिं (say) / सब (all) / कीसा (monkeys) / गर्जहिं (roar) / तर्जहिं (threaten) / सहज (naturally) / असंका (fearless) / मानहुँ (as if) / ग्रसन (to swallow) / चहत (want) / हहिं (are) / लंका (Lanka)
ramacharitamanas::4449.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4449.essence: Fearless unity can feel like a force that devours everything in its path.
ramacharitamanas::4449.simple_meaning: The monkey army speaks with fearless confidence. They roar as if they can swallow Lanka and crush Ravana completely.
ramacharitamanas::4449.simple_insight: Courage spreads through a team when everyone feels carried by a bigger purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4449.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears reports about the invading monkey army. The scouts describe not just their numbers but their wild confidence: every monkey speaks like a victor already. This verse heightens the fear on Ravana's side before the battle fully begins.
ramacharitamanas::4449.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is already aligned, loud, and unafraid. Before the meeting even starts, the energy has shifted, and the opposition can feel it.
ramacharitamanas::4449.insight: It shows how collective confidence can become its own force before any blow is struck.

ramacharitamanas::4450.verse_sanskrit: सहज सूर कपि भालु सब पुनि सिर पर प्रभु राम। रावन काल कोटि कहुँ जीति सकहिं संग्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4450.verse_hindi: सब वानर-भालू सहज ही शूरवीर हैं फिर उनके सिर पर प्रभु (सर्वेश्वर) श्री रामजी हैं। हे रावण! वे संग्राम में करोड़ों कालों को जीत सकते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4450.english_translation: All the bears and monkeys are naturally brave, and Lord Ram stands above them. Ravana, they can defeat even countless deaths in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4450.translation_literal: सहज (naturally) / सूर (brave) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / सब (all) / पुनि (again) / सिर पर (above the head) / प्रभु (lord) / राम (Ram) / रावन (Ravana) / काल (death) / कोटि (crores / countless) / कहुँ (for) / जीति सकहिं (can defeat) / संग्राम (battle)
ramacharitamanas::4450.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4450.essence: Devotion turns ordinary strength into victory over death itself.
ramacharitamanas::4450.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears are naturally fearless, and with Ram above them, they can defeat even countless deaths in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4450.simple_insight: Courage becomes limitless when it is held in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4450.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the vanara and bear army is roaring before battle. Their fearlessness is not just their own strength; it comes from Ram standing over them as their lord. This line lifts their courage into a warning for Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4450.modern_relevance: A team walks into the hardest room of the year — a final pitch, a court hearing, a hospital waiting area — and no one is shaking because everyone knows who they are fighting for.
ramacharitamanas::4450.insight: It shifts bravery from personal toughness to courage rooted in surrender to Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4451.verse_sanskrit: राम तेज बल बुधि बिपुलाई। सेष सहस सत सकहिं न गाई॥ सक सर एक सोषि सत सागर। तव भ्रातहि पूँछेउ नय नागर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4451.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के तेज (सामर्थ्य), बल और बुद्धि की अधिकता को लाखों शेष भी नहीं गा सकते। वे एक ही बाण से सैकड़ों समुद्रों को सोख सकते हैं, परंतु नीति निपुण श्री रामजी ने (नीति की रक्षा के लिए) आपके भाई से उपाय पूछा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4451.english_translation: The splendor, strength, and wisdom of Ram are beyond counting. With one arrow he could dry up hundreds of oceans, yet the master of righteous conduct still asked your brother for a way.
ramacharitamanas::4451.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / तेज (radiance, power) / बल (strength) / बुधि (wisdom) / बिपुलाई (vast, abundant) / सेष (Shesha) / सहस सत (thousands and hundreds) / सकहिं (can) / न (not) / गाई (sing, describe) ॥ / सक (one) / सर (arrow) / एक (one) / सोषि (dry up) / सत (hundreds) / सागर (oceans) / तव (your) / भ्रातहि (brother) / पूँछेउ (asked) / नय (righteous conduct) / नागर (skilled, refined) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4451.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4451.essence: True strength can choose restraint without losing any power.
ramacharitamanas::4451.simple_meaning: Ram's power, strength, and wisdom are beyond measure. Even though he could dry up the ocean with one arrow, he still chose the righteous path and asked for help.
ramacharitamanas::4451.simple_insight: Real strength includes restraint. You do not prove power by forcing every possible outcome.
ramacharitamanas::4451.detailed_meaning: In Sundarkand, Hanuman is describing Ram's greatness while Lanka and the sea stand in the way. Ram is not helpless; he is fully capable of overwhelming force. Yet he chooses righteous conduct and asks the sea for a path instead of acting harshly.
ramacharitamanas::4451.modern_relevance: You know the answer in the meeting, but you let someone else speak first because the room needs trust, not domination. That is the kind of strength this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::4451.insight: It shifts you from proving power to using power with restraint and respect.

ramacharitamanas::4452.verse_sanskrit: तासु बचन सुनि सागर पाहीं। मागत पंथ कृपा मन माहीं॥ सुनत बचन बिहसा दससीसा। जौं असि मति सहाय कृत कीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4452.verse_hindi: उनके (आपके भाई के) वचन सुनकर वे (श्री रामजी) समुद्र से राह माँग रहे हैं, उनके मन में कृपा भी है (इसलिए वे उसे सोखते नहीं)। दूत के ये वचन सुनते ही रावण खूब हँसा (और बोला-) जब ऐसी बुद्धि है, तभी तो वानरों को सहायक बनाया है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4452.english_translation: Hearing that message, Ravana laughed hard: “So this is their intelligence — that’s why they’ve taken monkeys as allies!”
ramacharitamanas::4452.translation_literal: तासु (their) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / सागर (the ocean) / पाहीं (near) / मागत (asking for) / पंथ (path) / कृपा (compassion) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) ॥ सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / बिहसा (laughed) / दससीसा (the ten-headed one) / जौं (if) / असि (such) / मति (intelligence) / सहाय (helpers) / कृत (made) / कीसा (monkeys) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4452.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4452.essence: Ego laughs at mercy because it cannot recognize strength without violence.
ramacharitamanas::4452.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the message, laughing at the idea that Ram would ask the ocean for a path instead of forcing one open.
ramacharitamanas::4452.simple_insight: Pride makes you laugh at what you do not yet understand.
ramacharitamanas::4452.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman carries Ram's message to Ravana after reaching the city alone. The report that Ram is asking the ocean for passage, while still showing mercy, only deepens Ravana's contempt. His laughter reveals the blindness of ego.
ramacharitamanas::4452.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses a careful plan in a meeting because it looks too gentle to work. Later, that same restraint proves wiser than brute force.
ramacharitamanas::4452.insight: It shows how arrogance turns mercy into weakness and blinds you to real strength.

ramacharitamanas::4453.verse_sanskrit: सहज भीरु कर बचन दृढ़ाई। सागर सन ठानी मचलाई॥ मूढ़ मृषा का करसि बड़ाई। रिपु बल बुद्धि थाह मैं पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4453.verse_hindi: स्वाभाविक ही डरपोक विभीषण के वचन को प्रमाण करके उन्होंने समुद्र से मचलना (बालहठ) ठाना है। अरे मूर्ख! झूठी बड़ाई क्या करता है? बस, मैंने शत्रु (राम) के बल और बुद्धि की थाह पा ली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4453.english_translation: “The timid brother’s words only make me more stubborn. Fool, why boast falsely? I have now measured the strength and intelligence of my enemy.”
ramacharitamanas::4453.translation_literal: सहज (by nature) / भीरु (timid, fearful) / कर (of) / बचन (words) / दृढ़ाई (strengthening, making firm) / सागर (the ocean) / सन (with) / ठानी (resolved, decided) / मचलाई (to act stubbornly, to throw a tantrum) ॥ / मूढ़ (fool) / मृषा (false) / का (why) / करसि (do you make) / बड़ाई (boasting, praise) / रिपु (enemy) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (intelligence) / थाह (depth, measure) / मैं (I) / पाई (have found, measured) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4453.speaker: Ravana
