ramacharitamanas::4453.essence: Pride mistakes stubbornness for strength and calls it insight.
ramacharitamanas::4453.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the messenger’s warning and doubles down on his pride. He thinks he has already measured Ram’s power and intelligence, so he keeps taunting instead of listening.
ramacharitamanas::4453.simple_insight: Pride can turn warning into fuel for deeper mistakes.
ramacharitamanas::4453.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears the report about Ram and the ocean. Instead of softening, he hardens. He dismisses Vibhishana’s caution, mocks the messenger, and convinces himself that he already understands his enemy. The verse shows ego closing the door to wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4453.modern_relevance: You get one careful warning before a bad decision, but your ego calls it weakness and pushes ahead anyway. That is the trap Ravana is in.
ramacharitamanas::4453.insight: It shows how contempt for advice becomes self-blindness.

ramacharitamanas::4454.verse_sanskrit: सचिव सभीत बिभीषन जाकें। बिजय बिभूति कहाँ जग ताकें॥ सुनि खल बचन दूत रिस बाढ़ी। समय बिचारि पत्रिका काढ़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4454.verse_hindi: जिसके डरपोंक बिभीषण से मंत्री हैं उसके विजय और विभूति कहाँ? || खल रावनके ये वचन सुनकर दूतको बड़ा क्रोध आया| इससे उसने अवसर जानकर लक्ष्मणके हाथकी पत्री निकाली||
ramacharitamanas::4454.english_translation: “How can that world have victory or splendor where the timid Vibhishana serves as minister?” Hearing the villain’s words, the envoy’s anger rose. Seeing the moment, he took out the letter.
ramacharitamanas::4454.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / सभीत (fearful) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / जाकें (for whom) / बिजय (victory) / बिभूति (splendor, prosperity) / कहाँ (where) / जग (world) / ताकें (for that one) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / खल (villain's) / बचन (words) / दूत (envoy) / रिस (anger) / बाढ़ी (increased) ॥ / समय (the right moment) / बिचारि (having considered) / पत्रिका (letter) / काढ़ी (took out) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4454.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4454.essence: Pride speaks loudly; the wiser reply waits for the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::4454.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Vibhishana and claims a kingdom led by him cannot truly prosper. The envoy gets angry, then chooses the right moment to reveal the letter he carries.
ramacharitamanas::4454.simple_insight: Pride tries to shame, but the right response is calm timing, not immediate reaction.
ramacharitamanas::4454.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sneers at Vibhishana and questions his worth as a minister. Hanuman, the envoy, hears the insult, feels anger rise, and waits for the right instant before producing Lakshman's letter. The scene is tense, but still tactical.
ramacharitamanas::4454.modern_relevance: Someone insults the person you came to defend, and your face burns. You want to fire back immediately, but the wiser move is to wait for the exact second that serves the truth best.
ramacharitamanas::4454.insight: It teaches you to hold anger briefly and use timing as part of your response.

ramacharitamanas::4455.verse_sanskrit: रामानुज दीन्हीं यह पाती। नाथ बचाइ जुड़ावहु छाती॥ बिहसि बाम कर लीन्हीं रावन। सचिव बोलि सठ लाग बचावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4455.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) श्री रामजी के छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण ने यह पत्रिका दी है। हे नाथ! इसे बचवाकर छाती ठंडी कीजिए। रावण ने हँसकर उसे बाएँ हाथ से लिया और मंत्री को बुलवाकर वह मूर्ख उसे बँचाने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4455.english_translation: Lakshman sent this letter. O lord, save it and cool your chest. Ravana laughed and took it with his left hand, then called his minister and the fool tried to explain it away.
ramacharitamanas::4455.translation_literal: रामानुज (younger brother of Ram) / दीन्हीं (gave) / यह (this) / पाती (letter) / नाथ (lord) / बचाइ (saving) / जुड़ावहु (cool) / छाती (chest) ॥ बिहसि (laughing) / बाम (left) / कर (hand) / लीन्हीं (took) / रावन (Ravana) / सचिव (minister) / बोलि (calling) / सठ (fool) / लाग (began) / बचावन (to excuse)
ramacharitamanas::4455.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4455.essence: Mocking a warning only deepens the fall.
ramacharitamanas::4455.simple_meaning: Lakshman’s message reaches Ravana, but Ravana mocks it instead of taking it seriously.
ramacharitamanas::4455.simple_insight: Pride makes a warning feel like a joke until consequences arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4455.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman’s letter from Lakshman is delivered to Ravana after the first taunts at the gate. The message is a final warning, but Ravana laughs, takes it lightly, and tries to dismiss its force instead of facing the danger.
ramacharitamanas::4455.modern_relevance: You get a serious text from someone you’ve hurt, and your first instinct is to joke, deflect, or explain it away. That little laugh can be the beginning of a much bigger collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4455.insight: It shows how ego protects itself by mocking what it cannot answer.

ramacharitamanas::4456.verse_sanskrit: बातन्ह मनहि रिझाइ सठ जनि घालसि कुल खीस। राम बिरोध न उबरसि सरन बिष्नु अज ईस॥56क॥
ramacharitamanas::4456.verse_hindi: (पत्रिका में लिखा था-) अरे मूर्ख! केवल बातों से ही मन को रिझाकर अपने कुल को नष्ट-भ्रष्ट न कर। श्री रामजी से विरोध करके तू विष्णु, ब्रह्मा और महेश की शरण जाने पर भी नहीं बचेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4456.english_translation: Fool, do not destroy your own family line by soothing your mind with empty words. If you oppose Ram, you will not be saved even by taking refuge in Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::4456.translation_literal: बातन्ह (with words) / मनहि (the mind) / रिझाइ (pleasing) / सठ (fool) / जनि (do not) / घालसि (destroy) / कुल (family line) / खीस (ruin) / राम (Ram) / बिरोध (opposition) / न (not) / उबरसि (you will be saved) / सरन (refuge) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / अज (Brahma) / ईस (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::4456.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4456.essence: No amount of self-talk can protect you from the cost of opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4456.simple_meaning: False comfort and clever talk cannot protect you. If you stand against Ram, no higher refuge will save you from the consequences.
ramacharitamanas::4456.simple_insight: Pride can sound persuasive, but it still leaves you exposed.
ramacharitamanas::4456.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana mocks the warning sent by Ram through Vibhishana. The message is blunt: stop flattering yourself, stop ruining your own house, and do not imagine that any refuge will protect you if you keep opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4456.modern_relevance: You keep telling yourself the damage is manageable, that one more excuse will fix it, that the fallout will pass. But some choices keep cutting deeper no matter how well you explain them.
ramacharitamanas::4456.insight: It pushes you to see self-justification as a danger, not a defense.

ramacharitamanas::4457.verse_sanskrit: की तजि मान अनुज इव प्रभु पद पंकज भृंग। होहि कि राम सरानल खल कुल सहित पतंग॥56ख॥
ramacharitamanas::4457.verse_hindi: या तो अभिमान छोड़कर अपने छोटे भाई विभीषण की भाँति प्रभु के चरण कमलों का भ्रमर बन जा। अथवा रे दुष्ट! श्री रामजी के बाण रूपी अग्नि में परिवार सहित पतिंगा हो जा (दोनों में से जो अच्छा लगे सो कर) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4457.english_translation: Give up pride and become, like Vibhishana, a bee at the Lord’s lotus feet. Or, wicked one, become a moth, along with your whole family, in Ram’s arrow-fire.
ramacharitamanas::4457.translation_literal: की (or) / तजि (giving up) / मान (pride) / अनुज (younger brother) / इव (like) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / भृंग (bee) / होहि (become) / कि (or) / राम (Ram) / सरानल (arrow-fire) / खल (wicked one) / कुल सहित (along with family) / पतंग (moth)
ramacharitamanas::4457.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4457.essence: Pride leaves only two endings: surrender or destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4457.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned to give up arrogance and surrender like Vibhishana, or else face destruction with his family in Ram’s fiery arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4457.simple_insight: Pride narrows your choices until only surrender or self-destruction remain.
ramacharitamanas::4457.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just been urged to stop provoking Ram. The warning is blunt: follow Vibhishana’s example and bow at Ram’s feet, or keep clinging to ego and be destroyed along with your clan.
ramacharitamanas::4457.modern_relevance: You keep defending a decision in a family group chat, even as the room goes quiet. At some point, the issue is no longer the argument — it is whether pride is worth the damage.
ramacharitamanas::4457.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting ego to choosing humility before consequences harden.

ramacharitamanas::4458.verse_sanskrit: सुनत सभय मन मुख मुसुकाई। कहत दसानन सबहि सुनाई॥ भूमि परा कर गहत अकासा। लघु तापस कर बाग बिलासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4458.verse_hindi: पत्रिका सुनते ही रावण मन में भयभीत हो गया, परंतु मुख से (ऊपर से) मुस्कुराता हुआ वह सबको सुनाकर कहने लगा- जैसे कोई पृथ्वी पर पड़ा हुआ हाथ से आकाश को पकड़ने की चेष्टा करता हो, वैसे ही यह छोटा तपस्वी (लक्ष्मण) वाग्विलास करता है (डींग हाँकता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4458.english_translation: Hearing it, Ravana felt fear in his mind but smiled on his face and spoke so everyone could hear: "It is like someone lying on the ground trying to catch the sky with his hands. This little ascetic is just showing off with words."
ramacharitamanas::4458.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / सभय (fearful) / मन (mind) / मुख (face) / मुसुकाई (smiled) / कहत (speaking) / दसानन (Ravana) / सबहि (to everyone) / सुनाई (made hear) / भूमि (earth) / परा (fallen) / कर (hand) / गहत (grasping) / अकासा (sky) / लघु (small) / तापस (ascetic) / कर (of) / बाग (speech) / बिलासा (display)
ramacharitamanas::4458.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4458.essence: Fear hidden by pride turns into ridicule.
ramacharitamanas::4458.simple_meaning: Ravana is afraid inside, but he hides it with a smile and mocks Lakshman’s words as empty boasting.
ramacharitamanas::4458.simple_insight: Pride can make fear wear a confident face.
ramacharitamanas::4458.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just heard Vibhishana’s warning and Lakshman’s challenge. Though fear has entered his mind, he refuses to show weakness. Instead, he laughs it off before his court, exposing the gap between inner fear and outward pride.
ramacharitamanas::4458.modern_relevance: You get a hard message in a group chat, feel the sting, then reply with a joke so nobody sees it landed. Ravana’s mask is painfully familiar.
ramacharitamanas::4458.insight: It reveals how ego protects itself by turning real fear into public mockery.

ramacharitamanas::4459.verse_sanskrit: कह सुक नाथ सत्य सब बानी। समुझहु छाड़ि प्रकृति अभिमानी॥ सुनहु बचन मम परिहरि क्रोधा। नाथ राम सन तजहु बिरोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4459.verse_hindi: शुक (दूत) ने कहा- हे नाथ! अभिमानी स्वभाव को छोड़कर (इस पत्र में लिखी) सब बातों को सत्य समझिए। क्रोध छोड़कर मेरा वचन सुनिए। हे नाथ! श्री रामजी से वैर त्याग दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4459.english_translation: Shuk said: O lord, set aside pride and understand every word as true. Listen to my words without anger, and give up your enmity with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4459.translation_literal: कह (said) / सुक नाथ (Shuk, O lord) / सत्य (true) / सब (all) / बानी (words) / समुझहु (understand) / छाड़ि (leaving aside) / प्रकृति (nature) / अभिमानी (prideful) / सुनहु (listen) / बचन (words) / मम (my) / परिहरि (leaving) / क्रोधा (anger) / नाथ (lord) / राम (Ram) / सन (with) / तजहु (give up) / बिरोधा (enmity)
ramacharitamanas::4459.speaker: Shuk
ramacharitamanas::4459.essence: Pride blocks the message that could save you.
ramacharitamanas::4459.simple_meaning: Shuk asks Ravana to drop pride, listen calmly, and stop opposing Ram. The way forward is not more force, but surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4459.simple_insight: Softening the heart can open what resistance keeps shut.
ramacharitamanas::4459.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Shuk arrives with Ram's message and speaks directly to Ravana. He warns him to stop clinging to pride, anger, and hostility. This moment matters because Ravana's real battle is not outside him but inside his own refusal to yield.
ramacharitamanas::4459.modern_relevance: You are halfway through drafting a furious reply when you realize the real issue is your wounded pride. If you can put that down, the conversation may finally become possible.
ramacharitamanas::4459.insight: It shifts you from defensive reaction to receptive listening, so truth can land before conflict hardens.

ramacharitamanas::4460.verse_sanskrit: अति कोमल रघुबीर सुभाऊ। जद्यपि अखिल लोक कर राऊ॥ मिलत कृपा तुम्ह पर प्रभु करिही। उर अपराध न एकउ धरिही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4460.verse_hindi: यद्यपि श्री रघुवीर समस्त लोकों के स्वामी हैं, पर उनका स्वभाव अत्यंत ही कोमल है। मिलते ही प्रभु आप पर कृपा करेंगे और आपका एक भी अपराध वे हृदय में नहीं रखेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4460.english_translation: Though Lord Raghubir is the ruler of all worlds, his nature is extremely gentle. When he meets you, he will shower you with grace and will not keep even one offense in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4460.translation_literal: अति कोमल (extremely gentle) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सुभाऊ (nature) / जद्यपि (although) / अखिल (entire) / लोक (worlds) / कर (of) / राऊ (ruler)॥ / मिलत (meeting) / कृपा (grace) / तुम्ह पर (upon you) / प्रभु (the Lord) / करिही (will do)॥ / उर (heart) / अपराध (offense) / न (not) / एकउ (even one) / धरिही (will keep)॥
ramacharitamanas::4460.speaker: Shuk
ramacharitamanas::4460.essence: Power becomes lovable when it carries no resentment.
ramacharitamanas::4460.simple_meaning: Ram is gentle, even as the ruler of all worlds. If you meet him, he will show mercy and not keep your faults in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4460.simple_insight: You can come close without fear of being remembered only for your mistakes.
ramacharitamanas::4460.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s messenger is being warned not to answer with pride. The verse turns from warning to reassurance: Ram, though lord of everything, is soft-hearted and forgiving. This is meant to open the door to surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4460.modern_relevance: You finally send the apology text you have avoided for weeks. The reply comes back kinder than you feared. This verse reminds you that real strength can still be tender.
ramacharitamanas::4460.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of judgment to trust in mercy.

ramacharitamanas::4461.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुता रघुनाथहि दीजे। एतना कहा मोर प्रभु कीजे॥ जब तेहिं कहा देन बैदेही। चरन प्रहार कीन्ह सठ तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4461.verse_hindi: जानकीजी श्री रघुनाथजी को दे दीजिए। हे प्रभु! इतना कहना मेरा कीजिए। जब उस (दूत) ने जानकीजी को देने के लिए कहा, तब दुष्ट रावण ने उसको लात मारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4461.english_translation: Give Janaki to Raghunath. Tell my Lord only this. When the messenger said to give back Vaidehi, that wicked Ravana kicked him.
ramacharitamanas::4461.translation_literal: जनकसुता (Janaka's daughter) / रघुनाथहि (to Raghunath) / दीजे (give) / एतना (this much) / कहा (said) / मोर (my) / प्रभु (Lord) / कीजे (do) / जब (when) / तेहिं (he) / कहा (said) / देन (to give) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / चरन (foot) / प्रहार (a blow) / कीन्ह (did) / सठ (wicked one) / तेही (to him)
ramacharitamanas::4461.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4461.essence: Ego does not negotiate; it lashes out at truth.
ramacharitamanas::4461.simple_meaning: Ravana orders Sita to be handed over to Ram, but when the messenger repeats that demand, Ravana kicks him in rage.
ramacharitamanas::4461.simple_insight: Pride can hear the truth and still strike it down.
ramacharitamanas::4461.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana receives a warning from Ram's messenger. The message is simple: return Sita. Instead of listening, Ravana's anger and ego explode, and he attacks the messenger. The scene shows how far he has fallen.
ramacharitamanas::4461.modern_relevance: Someone gives you a hard truth in a calm voice, and you snap before they finish the sentence. The reaction itself proves the message was needed.
ramacharitamanas::4461.insight: It exposes how ego turns a chance to correct course into fresh harm.

ramacharitamanas::4462.verse_sanskrit: नाइ चरन सिरु चला सो तहाँ। कृपासिंधु रघुनायक जहाँ॥ करि प्रनामु निज कथा सुनाई। राम कृपाँ आपनि गति पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4462.verse_hindi: वह भी (विभीषण की भाँति) चरणों में सिर नवाकर वहीं चला, जहाँ कृपासागर श्री रघुनाथजी थे। प्रणाम करके उसने अपनी कथा सुनाई और श्री रामजी की कृपा से अपनी गति (मुनि का स्वरूप) पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4462.english_translation: He bowed his head at the feet and went there, where the ocean of compassion, Raghunath, was. After bowing, he told his own story, and by Ram's grace he attained his rightful state.
ramacharitamanas::4462.translation_literal: नाइ (bowing) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / चला (went) / सो (that one) / तहाँ (there) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / रघुनायक (Raghunath, lord of the Raghu line) / जहाँ (where)॥ / करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bowing) / निज (own) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / राम कृपाँ (by Ram's grace) / आपनि (own) / गति (state, rightful condition) / पाई (obtained)॥
ramacharitamanas::4462.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4462.essence: Humility opens the way for grace to change your state.
ramacharitamanas::4462.simple_meaning: He approaches Ram with humility, tells his story, and receives his true place through Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4462.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to help you cannot force yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4462.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already located Sita and now the larger rescue is unfolding around Ram's compassion. A humbled seeker comes, bows, speaks his truth, and receives a transformed destiny through Ram's mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4462.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a mistake, lower your pride, and tell the truth plainly. The moment you stop defending yourself, help can actually reach you.
ramacharitamanas::4462.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to humble disclosure, trusting grace instead of control.

ramacharitamanas::4463.verse_sanskrit: रिषि अगस्ति कीं साप भवानी। राछस भयउ रहा मुनि ग्यानी॥ बंदि राम पद बारहिं बारा। मुनि निज आश्रम कहुँ पगु धारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4463.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! वह ज्ञानी मुनि था, अगस्त्य ऋषि के शाप से राक्षस हो गया था। बार-बार श्री रामजी के चरणों की वंदना करके वह मुनि अपने आश्रम को चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4463.english_translation: (Shiva says to Parvati:) O Bhavani, he was a wise sage who became a demon by the curse of Sage Agastya. Bowing again and again at Ram's feet, the sage went back to his own hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::4463.translation_literal: रिषि (sage) / अगस्ति (Agastya) / कीं साप (was cursed) / भवानी (Bhavani) / राछस (demon) / भयउ (became) / रहा (was) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / बंदि (bowing) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / मुनि (sage) / निज (own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / कहुँ (to) / पगु (footsteps) / धारा (placed)
ramacharitamanas::4463.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4463.essence: Repeated bowing to Ram restores what curse had broken.
ramacharitamanas::4463.simple_meaning: A wise sage had once been cursed into a demon. After repeatedly bowing to Ram's feet, he returned to his hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::4463.simple_insight: Even a cursed life can turn back through humble devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4463.detailed_meaning: Shiva is telling Parvati about a sage who had fallen into a demon form because of Agastya's curse. The turning point is not force but repeated reverence to Ram. After that bowing, the sage is able to go home again.
ramacharitamanas::4463.modern_relevance: You can feel trapped by one mistake, one label, or one bad season. But humility can reopen the road home faster than pride ever will.
ramacharitamanas::4463.insight: It shifts the mind from fixed identity to the possibility of return through devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4464.verse_sanskrit: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीनि दिन बीति। बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::4464.verse_hindi: इधर तीन दिन बीत गए, किंतु जड़ समुद्र विनय नहीं मानता। तब श्री रामजी क्रोध सहित बोले- बिना भय के प्रीति नहीं होती! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4464.english_translation: Three days passed, but the stubborn ocean would not respond to humility. Then Ram spoke in anger: "Without fear, there is no love."
ramacharitamanas::4464.translation_literal: बिनय (humility) / न (not) / मानत (accepting) / जलधि (ocean) / जड़ (stubborn) / गए (passed) / तीनि (three) / दिन (days) / बीति (passed) / बोले (spoke) / राम (Ram) / सकोप (with anger) / तब (then) / भय (fear) / बिनु (without) / होइ (becomes) / न (not) / प्रीति (love)
ramacharitamanas::4464.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4464.essence: Without respect, even love becomes powerless.
ramacharitamanas::4464.simple_meaning: The ocean ignores Ram's peaceful request, so he warns that love without awe or restraint cannot last.
ramacharitamanas::4464.simple_insight: Some bonds only become real when you stop treating everything casually.
ramacharitamanas::4464.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the seashore, and Ram has waited three days for the ocean to yield a path. The sea still refuses. Ram’s anger becomes a teaching: closeness and cooperation do not come from softness alone; they also require reverence and response.
ramacharitamanas::4464.modern_relevance: You keep explaining your boundary to someone who keeps crossing it, hoping kindness alone will work. At some point, firmness is not cruelty — it is the condition for respect.
ramacharitamanas::4464.insight: It shifts you from endless politeness to clear limits when gentleness is being ignored.

ramacharitamanas::4465.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन बान सरासन आनू। सोषौं बारिधि बिसिख कृसानु॥ सठ सन बिनय कुटिल सन प्रीति। सहज कृपन सन सुंदर नीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::4465.verse_hindi: हे लक्ष्मण! धनुष-बाण लाओ, मैं अग्निबाण से समुद्र को सोख डालूँ। मूर्ख से विनय, कुटिल के साथ प्रीति, स्वाभाविक ही कंजूस से सुंदर नीति (उदारता का उपदेश), ॥
ramacharitamanas::4465.english_translation: “Lakshman, bring the bow and arrows. I will dry up the ocean with fire-arrows. Advice to the foolish, affection for the crooked, and noble conduct from the miserly come naturally.”
ramacharitamanas::4465.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / बान (bow) / सरासन (bow with arrows) / आनू (bring) / सोषौं (I will dry up) / बारिधि (ocean) / बिसिख (arrows) / कृसानु (fire) ॥ सठ (foolish person) / सन (from/with) / बिनय (humble appeal) / कुटिल (crooked person) / सन (from/with) / प्रीति (affection) / सहज (natural) / कृपन (miserly person) / सन (from/with) / सुंदर (noble) / नीति (conduct) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4465.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4465.essence: Gentleness has limits; some resistance must be met with force.
ramacharitamanas::4465.simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to bring the bow and says he will burn through the ocean. He also says some people do not respond to gentleness, crookedness does not deserve affection, and the miserly do not inspire noble treatment.
ramacharitamanas::4465.simple_insight: Not every situation can be solved with softness; sometimes clear force is the honest response.
ramacharitamanas::4465.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Ram has already waited three days for the sea to yield. Now he turns to Lakshman and prepares to act. The verse sharpens his resolve: some beings and situations do not respond to sweetness, so direct power must come first.
ramacharitamanas::4465.modern_relevance: You’ve explained the same boundary three times and the other person still pushes. At some point, kindness stops meaning passivity, and you need a firmer line.
ramacharitamanas::4465.insight: It shifts you from endless appeasement to decisive action when persuasion has failed.

ramacharitamanas::4466.verse_sanskrit: ममता रत सन ग्यान कहानी। अति लोभी सन बिरति बखानी॥ क्रोधिहि सम कामिहि हरिकथा। ऊसर बीज बएँ फल जथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4466.verse_hindi: ममता में फँसे हुए मनुष्य से ज्ञान की कथा, अत्यंत लोभी से वैराग्य का वर्णन, क्रोधी से शम (शांति) की बात और कामी से भगवान् की कथा, इनका वैसा ही फल होता है जैसा ऊसर में बीज बोने से होता है (अर्थात् ऊसर में बीज बोने की भाँति यह सब व्यर्थ जाता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4466.english_translation: Talking about wisdom to someone bound by possessiveness, non-attachment to someone drowning in greed, calmness to someone ruled by anger, and tales of the divine to someone ruled by desire is like sowing seeds in barren ground.
ramacharitamanas::4466.translation_literal: ममता रत (attached to possessiveness) / सन (to) / ग्यान कहानी (story of wisdom) / अति लोभी (extremely greedy) / सन (to) / बिरति बखानी (praise of non-attachment) / क्रोधिहि (to the angry one) / सम (peace) / कामिहि (to the desirous one) / हरिकथा (tales of Hari) / ऊसर (barren soil) / बीज (seed) / बएँ (sown) / फल (fruit) / जथा (like)
ramacharitamanas::4466.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4466.essence: Truth cannot take root in a heart that rejects it.
ramacharitamanas::4466.simple_meaning: A person trapped in possessiveness, greed, anger, or desire cannot receive teachings that ask for wisdom, detachment, peace, or devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4466.simple_insight: Not every mind can receive every truth; readiness matters as much as the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4466.detailed_meaning: On the seashore, Ram has just pressed the ocean to answer. Before the bow is drawn, this verse explains why some words fail: a clouded mind cannot absorb what would free it. The problem is not the teaching, but the soil.
ramacharitamanas::4466.modern_relevance: You try to calm a friend who is furious, but every sentence lands like an insult. The message may be right, yet the mind hearing it is too heated to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::4466.insight: It shifts you from forcing advice to noticing whether the listener is ready for it.

ramacharitamanas::4467.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि रघुपति चाप चढ़ावा। यह मत लछिमन के मन भावा॥ संधानेउ प्रभु बिसिख कराला। उठी उदधि उर अंतर ज्वाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4467.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने धनुष चढ़ाया। यह मत लक्ष्मणजी के मन को बहुत अच्छा लगा। प्रभु ने भयानक (अग्नि) बाण संधान किया, जिससे समुद्र के हृदय के अंदर अग्नि की ज्वाला उठी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4467.english_translation: After saying this, Raghupati raised his bow. Lakshman was pleased by this resolve. The Lord aimed a terrible arrow, and a fire rose within the ocean's heart.
ramacharitamanas::4467.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ावा (raised) / यह (this) / मत (resolve) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / के (of) / मन (mind) / भावा (was pleasing) / संधानेउ (aimed) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिसिख (arrow) / कराला (terrible) / उठी (rose) / उदधि (ocean) / उर (heart) / अंतर (within) / ज्वाला (flame)
ramacharitamanas::4467.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4467.essence: Resolve can move what patience could not.
ramacharitamanas::4467.simple_meaning: Ram raises his bow and readies a fierce arrow to confront the ocean. Lakshman approves, and the sea is shaken from within by the threat.
ramacharitamanas::4467.simple_insight: Sometimes firm resolve creates movement before force is even used.
ramacharitamanas::4467.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Ram has already tested patience and diplomacy. Now, with Lakshman at his side, he lifts his bow and prepares a blazing arrow. The ocean itself begins to tremble, and this moment sets up the sea's response.
ramacharitamanas::4467.modern_relevance: You’ve tried being reasonable, waiting, and asking nicely. Then you finally set a boundary that cannot be ignored.
ramacharitamanas::4467.insight: It shifts the mind from endless delay to decisive action when a situation refuses to move.

ramacharitamanas::4468.verse_sanskrit: मकर उरग झष गन अकुलाने। जरत जंतु जलनिधि जब जाने॥ कनक थार भरि मनि गन नाना। बिप्र रूप आयउ तजि माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4468.verse_hindi: मगर, साँप तथा मछलियों के समूह व्याकुल हो गए। जब समुद्र ने जीवों को जलते जाना, तब सोने के थाल में अनेक मणियों (रत्नों) को भरकर अभिमान छोड़कर वह ब्राह्मण के रूप में आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4468.english_translation: The crocodiles, snakes, and fish grew restless. When the ocean saw the creatures burning, it came in the form of a Brahmin, giving up pride, with a golden tray full of many gems.
ramacharitamanas::4468.translation_literal: मकर (crocodiles) / उरग (snakes) / झष (fish) / गन (groups) / अकुलाने (became restless) / जरत (burning) / जंतु (creatures) / जलनिधि (the ocean) / जब (when) / जाने (saw/knew) / कनक (golden) / थार (tray) / भरि (filled) / मनि (gems) / गन (groups) / नाना (many) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / रूप (form) / आयउ (came) / तजि (giving up) / माना (pride)
ramacharitamanas::4468.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4468.essence: Pride falls away when suffering can no longer be ignored.
ramacharitamanas::4468.simple_meaning: The sea grows troubled when it sees the creatures inside it suffering, and it comes forward humbly with gifts.
ramacharitamanas::4468.simple_insight: Real power does not cling to pride; it responds when others are in pain.
ramacharitamanas::4468.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just brought the fiery threat to the ocean’s edge. The waters, with their creatures in distress, are forced to react. Instead of stubbornness, the sea appears humbly in Brahmin form, carrying offerings, because the moment has become too grave for pride.
ramacharitamanas::4468.modern_relevance: A tense meeting is about to explode, and the person who has been defensive suddenly softens, apologises, and brings what is needed. Pressure can strip away ego faster than arguments can.
ramacharitamanas::4468.insight: It shows that when suffering becomes visible, pride must give way to humility and swift repair.

ramacharitamanas::4469.verse_sanskrit: काटेहिं पइ कदरी फरइ कोटि जतन कोउ सींच। बिनय न मान खगेस सुनु डाटेहिं पइ नव नीच ॥
ramacharitamanas::4469.verse_hindi: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे गरुड़जी! सुनिए, चाहे कोई करोड़ों उपाय करके सींचे, पर केला तो काटने पर ही फलता है। नीच विनय से नहीं मानता, वह डाँटने पर ही झुकता है (रास्ते पर आता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4469.english_translation: Listen, Garuda: even if you pour effort into a banana plant for a million lifetimes, it fruits only when it is cut; a low-minded person does not respond to gentleness, but to sharp correction.
ramacharitamanas::4469.translation_literal: काटेहिं (by cutting) / पइ (indeed) / कदरी (banana plant) / फरइ (fruits) / कोटि (crores, millions) / जतन (efforts, care) / कोउ (someone) / सींच (waters) / बिनय (humility, gentle request) / न (not) / मान (accepts) / खगेस (lord of birds, Garuda) / सुनु (listen) / डाटेहिं (by scolding) / पइ (indeed) / नव (new, low) / नीच (low-minded person)
ramacharitamanas::4469.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::4469.essence: Some people change only when gentle words become hard truth.
ramacharitamanas::4469.simple_meaning: Some people do not respond to gentle advice. Like a banana plant that fruits only after being cut, they change only through forceful correction.
ramacharitamanas::4469.simple_insight: Not every resistance can be met with softness; sometimes truth has to arrive firmly.
ramacharitamanas::4469.detailed_meaning: Kak Bhushundi is teaching Garuda in Uttarkand, drawing on a blunt image from ordinary life. The point is not gardening but human nature: some beings ignore humility and only wake up when correction becomes unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::4469.modern_relevance: You keep explaining calmly to someone who keeps repeating the same harmful pattern. After the fifth conversation, you realize kindness alone is not always enough to break denial.
ramacharitamanas::4469.insight: It shifts you from assuming every problem can be solved by softness to recognizing when firmer correction is needed.

ramacharitamanas::4470.verse_sanskrit: सभय सिंधु गहि पद प्रभु केरे। छमहु नाथ सब अवगुन मेरे॥। गगन समीर अनल जल धरनी। इन्ह कइ नाथ सहज जड़ करनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4470.verse_hindi: समुद्र ने भयभीत होकर प्रभु के चरण पकड़कर कहा- हे नाथ! मेरे सब अवगुण (दोष) क्षमा कीजिए। हे नाथ! आकाश, वायु, अग्नि, जल और पृथ्वी- इन सबकी करनी स्वभाव से ही जड़ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4470.english_translation: The ocean, afraid, held the Lord's feet and said, 'Forgive all my faults. O Lord, sky, air, fire, water, and earth are by nature inert.'
ramacharitamanas::4470.translation_literal: सभय (afraid) / सिंधु (the ocean) / गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / केरे (of) / छमहु (forgive) / नाथ (Lord) / सब (all) / अवगुन (faults) / मेरे (my) / गगन (sky) / समीर (air) / अनल (fire) / जल (water) / धरनी (earth) / इन्ह (these) / कइ (of) / नाथ (Lord) / सहज (by nature) / जड़ (inert) / करनी (condition)
ramacharitamanas::4470.speaker: Ocean
ramacharitamanas::4470.essence: True power kneels first and becomes fit to serve.
ramacharitamanas::4470.simple_meaning: The ocean humbles itself before Ram and asks forgiveness. It admits that the elements themselves are naturally inert and depend on divine power.
ramacharitamanas::4470.simple_insight: Humility opens the way for grace; even vast power becomes gentle when it bows.
ramacharitamanas::4470.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the sea in Lanka's shadow, and the ocean itself is made to speak. Afraid before Ram's power, it falls at his feet, asks forgiveness, and explains that the elements are naturally inert without the divine will.
ramacharitamanas::4470.modern_relevance: You realize you were wrong in the middle of a tense conversation, and the room changes the moment you stop defending yourself. Humility does what force never can.
ramacharitamanas::4470.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to surrender, showing that real strength begins with bowing.

ramacharitamanas::4471.verse_sanskrit: तव प्रेरित मायाँ उपजाए। सृष्टि हेतु सब ग्रंथनि गाए॥ प्रभु आयसु जेहि कहँ जस अहई। सो तेहि भाँति रहें सुख लहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4471.verse_hindi: आपकी प्रेरणा से माया ने इन्हें सृष्टि के लिए उत्पन्न किया है, सब ग्रंथों ने यही गाया है। जिसके लिए स्वामी की जैसी आज्ञा है, वह उसी प्रकार से रहने में सुख पाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4471.english_translation: By your prompting, Maya brought them forth for creation, as all the scriptures declare. Whoever has whatever command the Lord has given them finds ease by living in that way.
ramacharitamanas::4471.translation_literal: तव (your) / प्रेरित (prompted) / मायाँ (Maya) / उपजाए (brought forth) / सृष्टि (creation) / हेतु (for the purpose of) / सब (all) / ग्रंथनि (scriptures) / गाए (have sung) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयसु (command) / जेहि (for whom) / कहँ (to) / जस (as) / अहई (is) / सो (that one) / तेहि (that) / भाँति (manner) / रहें (to remain) / सुख (ease) / लहई (finds)
ramacharitamanas::4471.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4471.essence: Peace comes from living in alignment with your allotted role.
ramacharitamanas::4471.simple_meaning: Everything in creation has its place because the divine power set it in motion. A person finds ease by living according to the role and instruction meant for them.
ramacharitamanas::4471.simple_insight: There is relief in not fighting the shape of your own life.
ramacharitamanas::4471.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Shiva explains to Parvati that the world runs through divine order, not random force. Maya acts under that power, and every being finds ease when it follows the role and command given to it.
ramacharitamanas::4471.modern_relevance: You keep forcing yourself into someone else’s life plan, then wonder why everything feels tight. The strain softens when you stop arguing with the role that is actually yours.
ramacharitamanas::4471.insight: It shifts you from resistance to alignment: look for the way of living that matches your actual role.

ramacharitamanas::4472.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु भल कीन्ह मोहि सिख दीन्हीं। मरजादा पुनि तुम्हरी कीन्हीं॥ ढोल गवाँर सूद्र पसु नारी। सकल ताड़ना के अधिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4472.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने अच्छा किया जो मुझे शिक्षा (दंड) दी, किंतु मर्यादा (जीवों का स्वभाव) भी आपकी ही बनाई हुई है। ढोल, गँवार, शूद्र, पशु और स्त्री- ये सब शिक्षा के अधिकारी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4472.english_translation: The Lord did well to teach me, but the code of conduct was also made by you. Drum, fool, low-born, animal, and woman — all are fit for correction.
ramacharitamanas::4472.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / भल (well) / कीन्ह (did) / मोहि (me) / सिख (teaching/correction) / दीन्हीं (gave) / मरजादा (code of conduct / proper limits) / पुनि (also) / तुम्हरी (your) / कीन्हीं (made) / ढोल (drum) / गवाँर (fool) / सूद्र (low-born) / पसु (animal) / नारी (woman) / सकल (all) / ताड़ना (correction) / के (of) / अधिकारी (worthy)
ramacharitamanas::4472.speaker: Sea
ramacharitamanas::4472.essence: True correction belongs to the order that also gives it.
ramacharitamanas::4472.simple_meaning: The sea accepts Ram's rebuke as rightful, and says that the boundaries of conduct also come from Ram. The verse then gives a harsh list of those considered fit for correction.
ramacharitamanas::4472.simple_insight: Even correction can be received as care when it comes from the one you trust.
ramacharitamanas::4472.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the ocean and demanded passage in Ram's name. The sea, frightened and humbled, bows before Ram's authority. It praises Ram's correction as just, then speaks in the harsh social language of its time while yielding to that higher order.
ramacharitamanas::4472.modern_relevance: You get called out by someone you respect, and your first reaction is to bristle. Then you realize the correction was never meant to shame you — it was meant to restore order.
ramacharitamanas::4472.insight: It shifts the mind from taking correction personally to seeing it as part of a larger moral order.

ramacharitamanas::4473.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु प्रताप मैं जाब सुखाई। उतरिहि कटकु न मोरि बड़ाई॥ प्रभु अग्या अपेल श्रुति गाई। करौं सो बेगि जो तुम्हहि सोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4473.verse_hindi: प्रभु के प्रताप से मैं सूख जाऊँगा और सेना पार उतर जाएगी, इसमें मेरी बड़ाई नहीं है (मेरी मर्यादा नहीं रहेगी)। तथापि प्रभु की आज्ञा अपेल है (अर्थात् आपकी आज्ञा का उल्लंघन नहीं हो सकता) ऐसा वेद गाते हैं। अब आपको जो अच्छा लगे, मैं तुरंत वही करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4473.english_translation: By the Lord's power I would dry up, and the army would cross over; that would not be my greatness. The Vedas sing that the Lord's command cannot be disobeyed. I will quickly do whatever pleases you.
ramacharitamanas::4473.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord's) / प्रताप (power, glory) / मैं (I) / जाब (would go, would become) / सुखाई (drying up, dry) / उतरिहि (will cross over) / कटकु (army) / न (not) / मोरि (my) / बड़ाई (greatness) / प्रभु (Lord's) / अग्या (command) / अपेल (not to be disobeyed) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाई (sing) / करौं (I will do) / सो (that) / बेगि (quickly) / जो (what) / तुम्हहि (to you) / सोहाई (pleases, is fitting)
ramacharitamanas::4473.speaker: Samudra
ramacharitamanas::4473.essence: Pride vanishes when you place your power under a higher command.
ramacharitamanas::4473.simple_meaning: The sea says it will obey Ram at once. Even if its own power could make the army cross, it does not claim credit. Ram's command must be followed.
ramacharitamanas::4473.simple_insight: Real strength is willing obedience, not self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::4473.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the shore of Lanka, and the sea is finally answering Ram's approach. The ocean bows before Ram's authority, saying that even its own vast power is not its glory. It will do whatever Ram wants, at once.
ramacharitamanas::4473.modern_relevance: A senior colleague quietly hands you the final call on a project after days of tension. You stop trying to protect your image and just do what is right.
ramacharitamanas::4473.insight: It shifts the mind from claiming credit to honouring the right command.

ramacharitamanas::4474.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बिनीत बचन अति कह कृपाल मुसुकाइ। जेहि बिधि उतरै कपि कटकु तात सो कहहु उपाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4474.verse_hindi: समुद्र के अत्यंत विनीत वचन सुनकर कृपालु श्री रामजी ने मुस्कुराकर कहा- हे तात! जिस प्रकार वानरों की सेना पार उतर जाए, वह उपाय बताओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4474.english_translation: Hearing the ocean's humble words, the compassionate Lord smiled and said, 'Father, tell me a way by which the monkey army can cross.'
ramacharitamanas::4474.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बिनीत (humble) / बचन (words) / अति (very) / कह (said) / कृपाल (the compassionate one) / मुसुकाइ (smiling) / जेहि बिधि (by which way) / उतरै (may cross) / कपि कटकु (monkey army) / तात (father) / सो (that) / कहहु (tell) / उपाइ (means)
ramacharitamanas::4474.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4474.essence: Humility opens the door to help.
ramacharitamanas::4474.simple_meaning: Ram smiles at the ocean's humble request and asks for a practical way to help the monkey army cross.
ramacharitamanas::4474.simple_insight: Gentle humility can turn a problem into a shared search for a way through.
ramacharitamanas::4474.detailed_meaning: At the edge of the sea, the proud obstacle has softened into speech. Ram hears the ocean's respectful plea, smiles, and asks for a method to carry the monkey army across. The moment turns force into cooperation.
ramacharitamanas::4474.modern_relevance: You finally admit you need help, and the person across from you doesn't shame you. They lean in, smile, and start thinking with you instead of against you.
ramacharitamanas::4474.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding control to inviting wise help.

ramacharitamanas::4475.verse_sanskrit: नाथ नील नल कपि द्वौ भाई। लरिकाईं रिषि आसिष पाई॥ तिन्ह कें परस किएँ गिरि भारे। तरिहहिं जलधि प्रताप तुम्हारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4475.verse_hindi: (समुद्र ने कहा)) हे नाथ! नील और नल दो वानर भाई हैं। उन्होंने लड़कपन में ऋषि से आशीर्वाद पाया था। उनके स्पर्श कर लेने से ही भारी-भारी पहाड़ भी आपके प्रताप से समुद्र पर तैर जाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4475.english_translation: O Lord, Nila and Nala are two monkey brothers. In childhood they received a sage's blessing. By their touch, even heavy mountains will float across the ocean through your power.
ramacharitamanas::4475.translation_literal: नाथ (O Lord) / नील (Nila) / नल (Nala) / कपि (monkey) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) / लरिकाईं (in childhood) / रिषि (sage) / आसिष (blessing) / पाई (having received) / तिन्ह (their) / कें (by) / परस (touch) / किएँ (by doing) / गिरि (mountains) / भारे (heavy) / तरिहहिं (will float across) / जलधि (ocean) / प्रताप (power, glory) / तुम्हारे (your)
ramacharitamanas::4475.speaker: Ocean
ramacharitamanas::4475.essence: Your power makes even mountains float.
ramacharitamanas::4475.simple_meaning: The ocean explains that Nila and Nala, blessed in childhood, can make even heavy mountains float because of Ram's power.
ramacharitamanas::4475.simple_insight: What seems impossible becomes possible when the right power stands behind you.
ramacharitamanas::4475.detailed_meaning: The ocean is still trying to help Ram's army cross. It names Nila and Nala, two monkey brothers blessed long ago by a sage, and points to their touch as the reason mountains can float. Their gift is real, but Ram's power makes it work.
ramacharitamanas::4475.modern_relevance: A team is stuck on a task everyone calls impossible. Then one person with the right training, the right blessing, or the right backing changes everything. Hidden support can carry what raw effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4475.insight: It shifts attention from brute force to the unseen support that makes action succeed.

ramacharitamanas::4476.verse_sanskrit: मैं पुनि उर धरि प्रभु प्रभुताई। करिहउँ बल अनुमान सहाई॥ एहि बिधि नाथ पयोधि बँधाइअ। जेहिं यह सुजसु लोक तिहुँ गाइअ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4476.verse_hindi: मैं भी प्रभु की प्रभुता को हृदय में धारण कर अपने बल के अनुसार (जहाँ तक मुझसे बन पड़ेगा) सहायता करूँगा। हे नाथ! इस प्रकार समुद्र को बँधाइए, जिससे तीनों लोकों में आपका सुंदर यश गाया जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4476.english_translation: I will keep your greatness in my heart and help as far as my strength allows. O Lord, in this way bind the ocean so your splendid fame is sung in all three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::4476.translation_literal: मैं (I) / पुनि (again) / उर (heart) / धरि (placing) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रभुताई (lordship, greatness) / करिहउँ (I will do) / बल (strength) / अनुमान (according to, as much as) / सहाई (help) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / नाथ (Lord) / पयोधि (ocean) / बँधाइअ (bind) / जेहिं (so that) / यह (this) / सुजसु (good fame) / लोक (worlds) / तिहुँ (three) / गाइअ (is sung)
ramacharitamanas::4476.speaker: Ocean
ramacharitamanas::4476.essence: True help starts when pride bows to a greater purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4476.simple_meaning: The ocean offers to remember Ram's greatness and help in whatever way it can, so that Ram's fame spreads through all the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::4476.simple_insight: Real help begins with humility: you do your part, while honoring a power larger than yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4476.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached the ocean and asked how Ram's army can cross. The ocean, humbled, speaks of Ram's greatness and offers cooperation within its limits. This becomes the turning point where surrender and practical help meet.
ramacharitamanas::4476.modern_relevance: You are in a tense meeting, and the problem is bigger than your team. Instead of posturing, you say, 'I'll do what I can, and keep the bigger purpose in view.'
ramacharitamanas::4476.insight: It shifts the mind from ego-driven control to humble, coordinated action.

ramacharitamanas::4477.verse_sanskrit: एहि सर मम उत्तर तट बासी। हतहु नाथ खल नर अघ रासी॥ सुनि कृपाल सागर मन पीरा। तुरतहिं हरी राम रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4477.verse_hindi: इस बाण से मेरे उत्तर तट पर रहने वाले पाप के राशि दुष्ट मनुष्यों का वध कीजिए। कृपालु और रणधीर श्री रामजी ने समुद्र के मन की पीड़ा सुनकर उसे तुरंत ही हर लिया (अर्थात् बाण से उन दुष्टों का वध कर दिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4477.english_translation: With this arrow, kill the heap of wicked men living on my northern shore. Hearing the ocean's pain, compassionate and battle-hardened Ram quickly removed it.
ramacharitamanas::4477.translation_literal: एहि (with this) / सर (arrow) / मम (my) / उत्तर (northern) / तट (shore) / बासी (dwelling) / हतहु (kill) / नाथ (lord) / खल (wicked) / नर (men) / अघ (sin) / रासी (heap) / सुनि (hearing) / कृपाल (compassionate) / सागर (ocean) / मन (mind) / पीरा (pain) / तुरतहिं (immediately) / हरी (took away) / राम (Ram) / रनधीरा (battle-hardened)
ramacharitamanas::4477.speaker: Ocean
ramacharitamanas::4477.essence: Compassion can demand decisive force against harm.
ramacharitamanas::4477.simple_meaning: The ocean asks Ram to use his arrow against the wicked people living on its northern shore. Ram hears the ocean's distress and quickly acts.
ramacharitamanas::4477.simple_insight: Sometimes mercy means removing what keeps harming everyone.
ramacharitamanas::4477.detailed_meaning: At the edge of Lanka, the ocean has finally yielded to Ram. No longer resisting, it asks Ram to strike the wicked men on its northern shore. Ram hears that plea and acts at once, showing both compassion and strength.
ramacharitamanas::4477.modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth about the person who keeps hurting everyone in the group. The relief is not in revenge, but in ending the damage.
ramacharitamanas::4477.insight: It shifts the focus from raw force to protective action guided by compassion.

ramacharitamanas::4478.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम बल पौरुष भारी। हरषि पयोनिधि भयउ सुखारी॥ सकल चरित कहि प्रभुहि सुनावा। चरन बंदि पाथोधि सिधावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4478.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी का भारी बल और पौरुष देखकर समुद्र हर्षित होकर सुखी हो गया। उसने उन दुष्टों का सारा चरित्र प्रभु को कह सुनाया। फिर चरणों की वंदना करके समुद्र चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4478.english_translation: Seeing Ram's great strength and valour, the ocean became joyful and relieved. It told the Lord the whole story of the wicked ones, then bowed at his feet and departed.
ramacharitamanas::4478.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / बल (strength) / पौरुष (valour) / भारी (great) / हरषि (rejoicing) / पयोनिधि (ocean) / भयउ (became) / सुखारी (happy)॥ / सकल (all) / चरित (deeds/story) / कहि (telling) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / सुनावा (made heard)॥ / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / पाथोधि (ocean) / सिधावा (departed)॥
ramacharitamanas::4478.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4478.essence: Power that is aligned with dharma ends struggle without further force.
ramacharitamanas::4478.simple_meaning: The ocean sees Ram's power, feels relieved, explains the situation, bows, and leaves.
ramacharitamanas::4478.simple_insight: Even resistance softens when it meets real strength.
ramacharitamanas::4478.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's tense opening, the ocean has already been pressed by Ram's arrows and mercy. Seeing Ram's force, it stops resisting, tells the truth about the wicked beings on its shores, bows, and withdraws. The scene moves the story forward, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4478.modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally hear the other person speak with calm authority. The tension drops, the facts come out, and everyone can breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::4478.insight: It shows that truth can emerge once fear and pride are broken.

ramacharitamanas::4479.verse_sanskrit: निज भवन गवनेउ सिंधु श्रीरघुपतिहि यह मत भायऊ। यह चरित कलि मल हर जथामति दास तुलसी गायऊ॥ सुख भवन संसय समन दवन बिषाद रघुपति गुन गना। तजि सकल आस भरोस गावहि सुनहि संतत सठ मना॥
ramacharitamanas::4479.verse_hindi: समुद्र अपने घर चला गया, श्री रघुनाथजी को यह मत (उसकी सलाह) अच्छा लगा। यह चरित्र कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाला है, इसे तुलसीदास ने अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार गाया है। श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूह सुख के धाम, संदेह का नाश करने वाले और विषाद का दमन करने वाले हैं। अरे मूर्ख मन! तू संसार का सब आशा-भरोसा त्यागकर निरंतर इन्हें गा और सुन।
ramacharitamanas::4479.english_translation: The ocean returned to its home, and this pleased Shri Raghunath. Tulsidas sings this story according to his understanding, for it removes the stains of Kali Yuga. The qualities of Raghupati are a house of joy, the destroyer of doubt, and the end of sorrow. O foolish mind, give up all other hopes and keep singing and listening with steady devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4479.translation_literal: निज (own) / भवन (home) / गवनेउ (went) / सिंधु (the ocean) / श्रीरघुपतिहि (to Shri Raghupati) / यह (this) / मत (opinion/advice) / भायऊ (was pleasing) / यह (this) / चरित (story/deed) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / मल (stain) / हर (removing) / जथामति (according to understanding) / दास (servant) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / गायऊ (sang) / सुख (joy) / भवन (house) / संसय (doubt) / समन (destroyer) / दवन (burning) / बिषाद (sorrow) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / गुन (qualities) / गना (counted/sung) / तजि (leaving) / सकल (all) / आस (hopes) / भरोस (trusts) / गावहि (sing) / सुनहि (listen) / संतत (continuously) / सठ (foolish) / मना (mind)
ramacharitamanas::4479.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4479.essence: Ram’s praise turns confusion and sorrow into steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::4479.simple_meaning: Ram’s story and qualities are presented as medicine for confusion and sorrow. Tulsidas says that keeping Ram in your heart and hearing his praise brings joy and clears the mind.
ramacharitamanas::4479.simple_insight: You do not need to carry every fear alone; devotion can steady what your mind keeps shaking.
ramacharitamanas::4479.detailed_meaning: After the ocean yields to Ram, Tulsidas steps back from the scene and turns it into teaching. He says this whole story removes the stains of the age, and that Ram’s qualities are a shelter from doubt and grief. The verse ends by urging the listener to let go of every other support and keep singing.
ramacharitamanas::4479.modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a hard conversation, replaying every line and building worst-case stories. This verse says the mind does not heal by more spinning; it steadies by returning to what is trustworthy.
ramacharitamanas::4479.insight: It shifts attention from anxious speculation to repeated remembrance of Ram’s qualities.

ramacharitamanas::4480.verse_sanskrit: सकल सुमंगल दायक रघुनायक गुन गान। सादर सुनहिं ते तरहिं भव सिंधु बिना जलजान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4480.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी का गुणगान संपूर्ण सुंदर मंगलों का देने वाला है। जो इसे आदर सहित सुनेंगे, वे बिना किसी जहाज (अन्य साधन) के ही भवसागर को तर जाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4480.english_translation: The praise of Raghunath brings every blessing. Those who listen with reverence cross the sea of becoming without any boat.
ramacharitamanas::4480.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / दायक (giver) / रघुनायक (Raghunath, lord of Raghu) / गुन गान (praise of qualities) / सादर (with reverence) / सुनहिं (they hear) / ते (those) / तरहिं (cross) / भव सिंधु (sea of becoming) / बिना (without) / जलजान (boat)
ramacharitamanas::4480.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4480.essence: Reverent praise becomes the boat across struggle.
ramacharitamanas::4480.simple_meaning: Listening to Ram's praise with respect brings blessings and helps you cross the cycle of struggle without needing any other support.
ramacharitamanas::4480.simple_insight: What you give your attention to can become a crossing, not just a sound.
ramacharitamanas::4480.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has finished his mission in Lanka, and the sea has already yielded to Ram's power. Tulsidas closes the Sundarkand by saying that reverent listening to Ram's praise itself becomes the boat across the ocean of repeated struggle.
ramacharitamanas::4480.modern_relevance: You’re exhausted after a long day, and one honest song, prayer, or story steadies you more than another plan ever could. Reverent attention can carry you farther than control.
ramacharitamanas::4480.insight: It shifts attention from external rescue to inward receptivity, showing that devotion itself becomes the means of crossing.

ramacharitamanas::4481.verse_sanskrit: श्लोक: रामं कामारिसेव्यं भवभयहरणं कालमत्तेभसिंहं योगीन्द्रं ज्ञानगम्यं गुणनिधिमजितं निर्गुणं निर्विकारम् । मायातीतं सुरेशं खलवधनिरतं ब्रह्मवृन्दैकदेवं वन्दे कन्दावदातं सरसिजनयनं देवमुर्वीशरूपम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::4481.verse_hindi: कामदेव के शत्रु शिवजी के सेव्य, भव (जन्म-मृत्यु) के भय को हरने वाले, काल रूपी मतवाले हाथी के लिए सिंह के समान, योगियों के स्वामी (योगीश्वर), ज्ञान के द्वारा जानने योग्य, गुणों की निधि, अजेय, निर्गुण, निर्विकार, माया से परे, देवताओं के स्वामी, दुष्टों के वध में तत्पर, ब्राह्मणवृन्द के एकमात्र देवता (रक्षक), जल वाले मेघ के समान सुंदर श्याम, कमल के से नेत्र वाले, पृथ्वीपति (राजा) के रूप में परमदेव श्री रामजी की मैं वंदना करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4481.english_translation: I bow to Ram, served by Shiva, who removes the fear of becoming and death, who is like a lion to the wild elephant of Time, lord of yogis, known through insight, treasure of virtues, unconquered, beyond qualities, beyond change, beyond illusion, lord of the divine beings, ready to destroy the wicked, the one and only divine protector of the learned, beautiful as a dark cloud, with lotus eyes, and appearing as the ruler of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::4481.translation_literal: रामम् (Ram) / कामारि-सेव्यं (served by the enemy of desire) / भव-भय-हरणं (remover of fear of becoming and death) / काल-मत्त-एभ-सिंहं (lion to the intoxicated elephant of Time) / योगीन्द्रं (lord of yogis) / ज्ञान-गम्यं (reachable through knowledge) / गुण-निधिम् (treasure of virtues) / अजितं (unconquered) / निर्गुणं (without qualities) / निर्विकारम् (unchanging) / माया-अतीतम् (beyond illusion) / सुर-ईशम् (lord of the divine beings) / खल-वध-निरतम् (intent on destroying the wicked) / ब्रह्म-वृन्द-एक-देवम् (one deity for the learned) / वन्दे (I bow) / कन्द-आवदातम् (beautiful as a dark cloud) / सरसिज-नयनम् (lotus-eyed) / देवम् (divine one) / उर्वीश-रूपम् (appearing as ruler of the earth)
ramacharitamanas::4481.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4481.essence: Ram is the refuge that stands beyond fear, time, and change.
ramacharitamanas::4481.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the supreme, unchanging reality who removes fear, defeats time, and stands beyond illusion. He is both the ruler of the world and the refuge of seekers.
ramacharitamanas::4481.simple_insight: There is relief in meeting something larger than fear, change, and control.
ramacharitamanas::4481.detailed_meaning: At the opening of Lankakand, Tulsidas pauses the war story for a grand praise of Ram. Before the battle fully unfolds, he presents Ram as the force beyond death, illusion, and time — the only refuge worth bowing to.
ramacharitamanas::4481.modern_relevance: When your phone is full of bad news, deadlines, and family pressure, this verse pulls you out of the panic spiral. It reminds you that what is stable is larger than the storm around you.
ramacharitamanas::4481.insight: It shifts attention from temporary threats to the one reality that cannot be shaken.

ramacharitamanas::4482.verse_sanskrit: शंखेन्द्वाभमतीवसुन्दरतनुं शार्दूलचर्माम्बरं कालव्यालकरालभूषणधरं गंगाशशांकप्रियम् । काशीशं कलिकल्मषौघशमनं कल्याणकल्पद्रुमं नौमीड्यं गिरिजापतिं गुणनिधिं कन्दर्पहं शंकरम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::4482.verse_hindi: शंख और चंद्रमा की सी कांति के अत्यंत सुंदर शरीर वाले, व्याघ्रचर्म के वस्त्र वाले, काल के समान (अथवा काले रंग के) भयानक सर्पों का भूषण धारण करने वाले, गंगा और चंद्रमा के प्रेमी, काशीपति, कलियुग के पाप समूह का नाश करने वाले, कल्याण के कल्पवृक्ष, गुणों के निधान और कामदेव को भस्म करने वाले,
ramacharitamanas::4482.english_translation: I bow to Shankara, whose body is beautiful like a conch and moon, who wears tiger skin, who bears dark serpents as ornaments, who loves the Ganga and the moon, who is lord of Kashi, who removes the burdens of this age, who is a wish-fulfilling tree of well-being, who is full of virtues, and who burns desire to ashes.
ramacharitamanas::4482.translation_literal: शंखेन्द्वाभ (like conch and moon) / अतीवसुन्दरतनुं (extremely beautiful-bodied) / शार्दूलचर्माम्बरं (tiger-skin-clad) / कालव्यालकरालभूषणधरं (wearing terrible dark serpents as ornaments) / गंगाशशांकप्रियम् (dear to the Ganga and the moon) / काशीशं (lord of Kashi) / कलिकल्मषौघशमनं (remover of the mass of Kali's impurities) / कल्याणकल्पद्रुमं (wish-fulfilling tree of well-being) / नौमि (I bow) / इड्यं (worthy of praise) / गिरिजापतिं (consort of Girija) / गुणनिधिं (treasure of virtues) / कन्दर्पहं (destroyer of Kama) / शंकरम् (Shankara)
ramacharitamanas::4482.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4482.essence: True greatness can be beautiful, fierce, and merciful at once.
ramacharitamanas::4482.simple_meaning: Tulsidas offers a reverent praise of Shiva, describing his beauty, power, purity, and his ability to remove the heaviness of this age.
ramacharitamanas::4482.simple_insight: Reverence can hold opposites at once: calm beauty, fierce power, and deep compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4482.detailed_meaning: In the opening praise of Lankakand, Tulsidas turns from the war story to worship Shiva. He describes Shankara as beautiful, fearsome, virtuous, and compassionate, setting a devotional frame before the battle unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::4482.modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded temple at dusk, tired and restless, and then the chant begins. Something in you remembers that strength does not have to be harsh, and beauty does not have to be weak.
ramacharitamanas::4482.insight: It trains the mind to see sacred power as both tender and immense.

ramacharitamanas::4483.verse_sanskrit: पार्वती पति वन्दनीय श्री शंकरजी को मैं नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥ यो ददाति सतां शम्भुः कैवल्यमपि दुर्लभम् । खलानां दण्डकृद्योऽसौ शंकरः शं तनोतु मे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4483.verse_hindi: जो सत् पुरुषों को अत्यंत दुर्लभ कैवल्यमुक्ति तक दे डालते हैं और जो दुष्टों को दण्ड देने वाले हैं, वे कल्याणकारी श्री शम्भु मेरे कल्याण का विस्तार करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4483.english_translation: I bow to Shankar, the husband of Parvati. May auspicious Shambhu, who grants even the hard-to-attain freedom to the good and punishes the wicked, spread blessing over me.
ramacharitamanas::4483.translation_literal: पार्वती पति (Parvati's husband) / वन्दनीय (worthy of worship) / श्री (auspicious) / शंकरजी (Shankar) / को (to) / मैं (I) / नमस्कार करता हूँ (bow) ॥ / यो (who) / ददाति (gives) / सतां (to the good) / शम्भुः (Shambhu) / कैवल्यम् (freedom) / अपि (even) / दुर्लभम् (hard to attain) । / खलानां (of the wicked) / दण्डकृत् (one who gives punishment) / यः (who) / असौ (that) / शंकरः (Shankar) / शम् (blessing) / तनोतु (may spread) / मे (for me) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4483.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4483.essence: The same presence that blesses the good also restrains what harms.
ramacharitamanas::4483.simple_meaning: Shiva is praised as the one who gives deep freedom to the noble and gives punishment to the wicked. The speaker asks for Shiva's blessing and protection.
ramacharitamanas::4483.simple_insight: Reverence can hold both tenderness and strength at once.
ramacharitamanas::4483.detailed_meaning: In the opening praise of Lankakand, Tulsidas turns to Shiva before the war begins. He honors Parvati's husband as the one who grants rare freedom to the good and disciplines the wicked, asking that this auspicious power protect him.
ramacharitamanas::4483.modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you may want only comfort. This verse reminds you that real support can also include correction, boundaries, and the courage to face what is wrong.
ramacharitamanas::4483.insight: It shifts devotion from soft admiration to trust in a power that also judges and corrects.

ramacharitamanas::4484.verse_sanskrit: लव निमेष परमानु जुग बरष कलप सर चंड। भजसि न मन तेहि राम को कालु जासु कोदंड॥
ramacharitamanas::4484.verse_hindi: लव, निमेष, परमाणु, वर्ष, युग और कल्प जिनके प्रचण्ड बाण हैं और काल जिनका धनुष है, हे मन! तू उन श्री रामजी को क्यों नहीं भजता?
ramacharitamanas::4484.english_translation: O mind, why do you not worship Shri Ram, whose fierce bow is time itself and whose arrows are moments, atoms, years, ages, and cycles?
ramacharitamanas::4484.translation_literal: लव (moment) / निमेष (blink) / परमानु (atom) / जुग (age) / बरष (year) / कलप (cycle) / सर (arrows) / चंड (fierce) / भजसि (you worship) / न (not) / मन (mind) / तेहि (that) / राम को (of Ram) / कालु (time) / जासु (whose) / कोदंड (bow)
ramacharitamanas::4484.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4484.essence: Even time is only an instrument in Ram's hands.
ramacharitamanas::4484.simple_meaning: Ram is greater than time itself. The mind should turn toward him instead of chasing temporary things.
ramacharitamanas::4484.simple_insight: What feels unstoppable in life is still smaller than the one you can trust completely.
ramacharitamanas::4484.detailed_meaning: In the war in Lanka, Tulsidas pauses the battle to praise Ram's vast power. He says even time is like Ram's bow, with moments and ages as its arrows. The verse turns awe into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4484.modern_relevance: You are staring at the clock before a medical result, an interview, or a hard conversation. The verse reminds you that time is not the final power in the room.
ramacharitamanas::4484.insight: It shifts attention from fearing time to placing trust in Ram's greater order.

ramacharitamanas::4485.verse_sanskrit: सिंधु बचन सुनि राम सचिव बोलि प्रभु अस कहेउ। अब बिलंबु केहि काम करहु सेतु उतरै कटकु॥
ramacharitamanas::4485.verse_hindi: समुद्र के वचन सुनकर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने मंत्रियों को बुलाकर ऐसा कहा- अब विलंब किसलिए हो रहा है? सेतु (पुल) तैयार करो, जिसमें सेना उतरे।
ramacharitamanas::4485.english_translation: Hearing the ocean's words, Lord Ram called his ministers and said, “Why delay now? Build the bridge so the army can cross.”
ramacharitamanas::4485.translation_literal: सिंधु (ocean) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / राम (Ram) / सचिव (ministers) / बोलि (calling) / प्रभु (Lord) / अस (thus) / कहेउ (said) / अब (now) / बिलंबु (delay) / केहि (why) / काम (for what purpose) / करहु (do) / सेतु (bridge) / उतरै (may cross/down) / कटकु (army)
ramacharitamanas::4485.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4485.essence: Once the way is known, delay becomes waste.
ramacharitamanas::4485.simple_meaning: Ram hears the ocean and immediately tells his ministers to stop delaying and build the bridge for the army to cross.
ramacharitamanas::4485.detailed_meaning: At the shore before Lanka, the ocean has answered Ram's call, and the army is waiting. Ram does not linger in frustration. He turns to his ministers at once and orders the bridge built so the forces can cross.
ramacharitamanas::4485.modern_relevance: You have the plan, the team, and the deadline — but everyone is still talking. This verse cuts through the stall and asks for movement, not more discussion.
ramacharitamanas::4485.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive execution when the path is already clear.

ramacharitamanas::4486.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु भानुकुल केतु जामवंत कर जोरि कह। नाथ नाम तव सेतु नर चढ़ि भव सागर तरहिं॥
ramacharitamanas::4486.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् ने हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे सूर्यकुल के ध्वजास्वरूप (कीर्ति को बढ़ाने वाले) श्री रामजी! सुनिए। हे नाथ! (सबसे बड़ा) सेतु तो आपका नाम ही है, जिस पर चढ़कर (जिसका आश्रय लेकर) मनुष्य संसार रूपी समुद्र से पार हो जाते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::4486.english_translation: Jambavan, with folded hands, said: "Listen, Lord of the solar line. Your name itself is the bridge; by taking refuge in it, people cross the ocean of worldly existence."
ramacharitamanas::4486.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / भानुकुल (solar line) / केतु (banner) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / कर जोरि (with joined hands) / कह (said) / नाथ (Lord) / नाम (name) / तव (your) / सेतु (bridge) / नर (people) / चढ़ि (climbing upon) / भव सागर (ocean of becoming) / तरहिं (cross)
ramacharitamanas::4486.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4486.essence: Ram's name becomes the bridge that carries you across.
ramacharitamanas::4486.simple_meaning: Ram's name is described as the bridge that carries people across the restless cycle of worldly life.
ramacharitamanas::4486.simple_insight: You do not have to cross by your own strength alone; faithful remembrance can carry you through.
ramacharitamanas::4486.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Jambavan folds his hands before Ram and speaks with reverence. The army has reached the edge of the ocean, and the question is how anyone can cross. He answers that Ram's name itself becomes the bridge.
ramacharitamanas::4486.modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels too wide to cross — a broken relationship, a debt, a decision you've delayed for months. Something steadier than your panic can still carry you through.
ramacharitamanas::4486.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant strain to trusting refuge in what is greater than effort alone.

ramacharitamanas::4487.verse_sanskrit: यह लघु जलधि तरत कति बारा। अस सुनि पुनि कह पवनकुमारा॥ प्रभु प्रताप बड़वानल भारी। सोषेउ प्रथम पयोनिधि बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4487.verse_hindi: फिर यह छोटा सा समुद्र पार करने में कितनी देर लगेगी? ऐसा सुनकर फिर पवनकुमार श्री हनुमान् जी ने कहा- प्रभु का प्रताप भारी बड़वानल (समुद्र की आग) के समान है। इसने पहले समुद्र के जल को सोख लिया था, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4487.english_translation: How long will it take to cross this small sea? Hearing this, Hanuman spoke again: The power of the Lord is like a great fire that had first dried up the ocean's waters.
ramacharitamanas::4487.translation_literal: यह (this) / लघु (small) / जलधि (ocean) / तरत (crossing) / कति (how much) / बारा (time) / अस (thus) / सुनि (hearing) / पुनि (again) / कहेउ (said) / पवनकुमारा (Hanuman) / प्रभु (Lord's) / प्रताप (power/glory) / बड़वानल (great fire of the ocean) / भारी (great) / सोषेउ (drained) / प्रथम (first) / पयोनिधि (ocean) / बारी (waters)
ramacharitamanas::4487.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4487.essence: Ram's power makes even an ocean feel small.
ramacharitamanas::4487.simple_meaning: Hanuman says Ram's power is so great that it once dried up the ocean itself. He speaks to show that crossing this sea is no real obstacle for Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4487.simple_insight: What looks impossible becomes small when Ram's power is in view.
ramacharitamanas::4487.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Hanuman answers the doubt about crossing the sea. He points to Ram's glory as the force that can dry up oceans. The verse is part of a growing argument that the mission will succeed through Ram's power, not Hanuman's alone.
ramacharitamanas::4487.modern_relevance: You're staring at a task that feels absurdly large, but someone you trust reminds you of what has already been carried through. The size of the obstacle changes when you remember the source of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4487.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring difficulty to remembering the power behind the mission.

ramacharitamanas::4488.verse_sanskrit: तव रिपु नारि रुदन जल धारा। भरेउ बहोरि भयउ तेहिं खारा॥ सुनि अति उकुति पवनसुत केरी। हरषे कपि रघुपति तन हेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4488.verse_hindi: परन्तु आपके शत्रुओं की स्त्रियों के आँसुओं की धारा से यह फिर भर गया और उसी से खारा भी हो गया। हनुमान् जी की यह अत्युक्ति (अलंकारपूर्ण युक्ति) सुनकर वानर श्री रघुनाथजी की ओर देखकर हर्षित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4488.english_translation: But the tears of your enemies' women filled it again, and that made it salty. Hearing Hanuman's bold claim, the monkeys rejoiced, looking at Raghu's lord.
ramacharitamanas::4488.translation_literal: तव (your) / रिपु (enemy) / नारि (women) / रुदन (crying) / जल धारा (stream of water) / भरेउ (filled) / बहोरि (again) / भयउ (became) / तेहिं (by that) / खारा (salty) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / उकुति (bold claim) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / केरी (of) / हरषे (rejoiced) / कपि (monkeys) / रघुपति (lord of Raghu) / तन (toward) / हेरी (looking) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4488.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4488.essence: Confidence can turn fear into momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4488.simple_meaning: Hanuman says the sea was filled again by the tears of the enemy women and became salty. The monkeys are delighted by his clever confidence and look toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4488.simple_insight: Bold faith can lift everyone around you, even before the task is done.
ramacharitamanas::4488.detailed_meaning: On Lanka's shore, Hanuman keeps answering the impossible with confidence. He says the sea is already being refilled by the enemy women’s tears. The monkeys hear his daring and brighten, because Ram's cause suddenly feels winnable.
ramacharitamanas::4488.modern_relevance: You're in a tense group chat before a huge deadline, and one person makes a fearless joke that breaks the fear. The mood changes before the work does.
ramacharitamanas::4488.insight: It shows how courage can spread through a team by turning fear into shared momentum.

ramacharitamanas::4489.verse_sanskrit: जामवंत बोले दोउ भाई। नल नीलहि सब कथा सुनाई॥ राम प्रताप सुमिरि मन माहीं। करहु सेतु प्रयास कछु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4489.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् ने नल-नील दोनों भाइयों को बुलाकर उन्हें सारी कथा कह सुनाई (और कहा-) मन में श्री रामजी के प्रताप को स्मरण करके सेतु तैयार करो, (रामप्रताप से) कुछ भी परिश्रम नहीं होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4489.english_translation: Jambavan spoke to the two brothers, Nala and Nila, and told them the whole story. "Remember Ram's power in your heart and build the bridge; then the effort will feel light."
ramacharitamanas::4489.translation_literal: जामवंत (Jambavan) / बोले (spoke) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / नल (Nala) / नीलहि (to Nila) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / राम (Ram) / प्रताप (power, glory) / सुमिरि (remembering) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / करहु (do) / सेतु (bridge) / प्रयास (effort) / कछु (some) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::4489.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4489.essence: Remember Ram, and the hardest work loses its weight.
ramacharitamanas::4489.simple_meaning: Keep Ram in mind while doing the task, and the work will not feel heavy.
ramacharitamanas::4489.simple_insight: Faith can change how effort feels, even when the task is still real.
ramacharitamanas::4489.detailed_meaning: On the shore of Lanka, Jambavan turns to Nala and Nila after Hanuman's leap has opened the way. He reminds them that Ram's power is the real force behind the bridge, so the impossible work can be done without strain.
ramacharitamanas::4489.modern_relevance: You're staring at a task that feels too big to start — a move, a deadline, a family crisis. Remembering what you stand for can make the burden feel workable.
ramacharitamanas::4489.insight: It shifts effort from self-reliance to remembrance of Ram's support.

ramacharitamanas::4490.verse_sanskrit: बोलि लिए कपि निकर बहोरी। सकल सुनहु बिनती कछु मोरी॥ राम चरन पंकज उर धरहू। कौतुक एक भालु कपि करहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4490.verse_hindi: फिर वानरों के समूह को बुला लिया (और कहा-) आप सब लोग मेरी कुछ विनती सुनिए। अपने हृदय में श्री रामजी के चरण-कमलों को धारण कर लीजिए और सब भालू और वानर एक खेल कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4490.english_translation: Hanuman called the monkeys together again and said, "Listen to my request. Hold Ram's lotus feet in your heart, and let all the bears and monkeys join in one play."
ramacharitamanas::4490.translation_literal: बोलि लिए (called together) / कपि निकर (the troop of monkeys) / बहोरी (again) / सकल (all) / सुनहु (listen) / बिनती (request) / कछु (some) / मोरी (my) / राम चरन पंकज (Ram's lotus-feet) / उर (heart) / धरहू (hold) / कौतुक (play) / एक (one) / भालु (bear) / कपि (monkey) / करहू (do)
ramacharitamanas::4490.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4490.essence: Ram in the heart turns hard work into joyful play.
ramacharitamanas::4490.simple_meaning: Hanuman gathers the monkeys and bears, asks them to keep Ram in their hearts, and urges them to begin the work with a playful spirit.
ramacharitamanas::4490.simple_insight: Devotion can turn hard work into joyful teamwork.
ramacharitamanas::4490.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already found Sita and now rallies the monkey and bear army for the bridge-building effort. He does not lead with force or fear, but with Ram in the heart. That devotion makes the task feel like play.
ramacharitamanas::4490.modern_relevance: You walk into a volunteer shift, a family repair job, or a late-night team push already tired. Then someone reminds everyone why it matters, and the whole room changes. The burden softens when the heart is set right.
ramacharitamanas::4490.insight: It shifts action from strain to shared devotion, so effort becomes lighter and more unified.

ramacharitamanas::4491.verse_sanskrit: धावहु मर्कट बिकट बरूथा। आनहु बिटप गिरिन्ह के जूथा॥ सुनि कपि भालु चले करि हूहा। जय रघुबीर प्रताप समूहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4491.verse_hindi: विकट वानरों के समूह (आप) दौड़ जाइए और वृक्षों तथा पर्वतों के समूहों को उखाड़ लाइए। यह सुनकर वानर और भालू हूह (हुँकार) करके और श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रताप समूह की (अथवा प्रताप के पुंज श्री रामजी की) जय पुकारते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4491.english_translation: Run, fierce monkeys, and bring whole trees and mountains. Hearing this, the monkeys and bears moved off with a roar, crying victory to Raghubir's power.
ramacharitamanas::4491.translation_literal: धावहु (run) / मर्कट (monkeys) / बिकट (fierce) / बरूथा (troops) / आनहु (bring) / बिटप (trees) / गिरिन्ह (mountains) / के (of) / जूथा (groups) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / चले (went) / करि (making) / हूहा (roar) / जय (victory) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / प्रताप (power) / समूहा (in multitude) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4491.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4491.essence: When purpose is shared, even heavy work feels light.
ramacharitamanas::4491.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army is ordered to fetch trees and mountains for the bridge, and they rush off cheering Ram's power.
ramacharitamanas::4491.simple_insight: Shared purpose turns effort into joy.
ramacharitamanas::4491.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the bridge is being built for Ram's army. Jamvant has already rallied the troops, and now the monkeys and bears are sent scrambling for trees and mountains. Their response is immediate, loud, and united.
ramacharitamanas::4491.modern_relevance: A team hears the deadline has moved up, and nobody complains. Everyone stands up, grabs what they can, and gets moving because the mission is bigger than discomfort.
ramacharitamanas::4491.insight: It shows how devotion to a shared cause can make hard labor feel like spirited play.

ramacharitamanas::4492.verse_sanskrit: अति उतंग गिरि पादप लीलहिं लेहिं उठाइ। आनि देहिं नल नीलहि रचहिं ते सेतु बनाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4492.verse_hindi: बहुत ऊँचे-ऊँचे पर्वतों और वृक्षों को खेल की तरह ही (उखाड़कर) उठा लेते हैं और ला-लाकर नल-नील को देते हैं। वे अच्छी तरह गढ़कर (सुंदर) सेतु बनाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4492.english_translation: They lift huge mountains and trees as if playing, bring them to Nala and Neela, and build the bridge with skill.
ramacharitamanas::4492.translation_literal: अति उतंग (very lofty) / गिरि (mountains) / पादप (trees) / लीलहिं (playfully) / लेहिं (lift) / उठाइ (raising) / आनि (bringing) / देहिं (give) / नल नीलहि (to Nala and Neela) / रचहिं (construct) / ते (they) / सेतु (bridge) / बनाइ (having made)
ramacharitamanas::4492.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4492.essence: Shared zeal turns impossible obstacles into building material.
ramacharitamanas::4492.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears move huge mountains and trees as if they were toys, handing them to Nala and Neela to build the bridge.
ramacharitamanas::4492.simple_insight: Great effort can feel light when everyone is united in one purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4492.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram's army is building the bridge to cross the sea. The vanaras and bears uproot mountains and trees with ease, and Nala and Neela shape them into a bridge. This verse is a supporting action scene, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::4492.insight: It shows coordinated effort: many hands supply the raw material, and skilled builders turn it into structure.

ramacharitamanas::4493.verse_sanskrit: सैल बिसाल आनि कपि देहीं। कंदुक इव नल नील ते लेहीं॥ देखि सेतु अति सुंदर रचना। बिहसि कृपानिधि बोले बचना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4493.verse_hindi: वानर बड़े-बड़े पहाड़ ला-लाकर देते हैं और नल-नील उन्हें गेंद की तरह ले लेते हैं। सेतु की अत्यंत सुंदर रचना देखकर कृपासिन्धु श्री रामजी हँसकर वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4493.english_translation: The monkeys bring huge mountains, and Nala and Neela take them as if they were balls. Seeing the bridge's beautiful construction, the compassionate Lord smiled and spoke.
ramacharitamanas::4493.translation_literal: सैल (mountain) / बिसाल (huge) / आनि (bringing) / कपि (monkeys) / देहीं (give) / कंदुक इव (like a ball) / नल नील (Nala and Neela) / ते (them) / लेहीं (take) / देखि (seeing) / सेतु (bridge) / अति सुंदर (very beautiful) / रचना (construction) / बिहसि (smiling) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / बोले (spoke) / बचना (words)
ramacharitamanas::4493.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4493.essence: Work becomes light when everyone gives their strength to one purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4493.simple_meaning: The monkeys keep bringing mountains, Nala and Neela use them like balls, and Ram smiles at the beautiful bridge being built.
ramacharitamanas::4493.simple_insight: Even impossible work can become joyful when it is done in service.
ramacharitamanas::4493.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, the monkey army is building Ram's bridge across the ocean. Monkeys haul mountains; Nala and Neela fit them into place. Ram watches the teamwork with a smile, and this verse simply captures that living, moving scene.
ramacharitamanas::4493.modern_relevance: You watch a team move heavy boxes up three flights of stairs, laughing through the strain, and the whole job feels lighter. Shared purpose changes exhaustion into play.
ramacharitamanas::4493.insight: It shifts attention from the burden of the task to the joy created by coordinated service.

ramacharitamanas::4494.verse_sanskrit: परम रम्य उत्तम यह धरनी। महिमा अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ करिहउँ इहाँ संभु थापना। मोरे हृदयँ परम कलपना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4494.verse_hindi: यह (यहाँ की) भूमि परम रमणीय और उत्तम है। इसकी असीम महिमा वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। मैं यहाँ शिवजी की स्थापना करूँगा। मेरे हृदय में यह महान् संकल्प है ॥
