ramacharitamanas::4494.english_translation: This land is supremely beautiful and excellent. Its boundless glory cannot be described. I will establish Shiva here. That great resolve is in my heart.
ramacharitamanas::4494.translation_literal: परम रम्य (supremely beautiful) / उत्तम (excellent) / यह (this) / धरनी (land) / महिमा (glory) / अमित (limitless) / जाइ (goes) / नहिं (not) / बरनी (described) / करिहउँ (I will do) / इहाँ (here) / संभु (Shiva) / थापना (establishment) / मोरे (my) / हृदयँ (in heart) / परम (great) / कलपना (resolve)
ramacharitamanas::4494.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4494.essence: Victory becomes complete when humility makes room for reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4494.simple_meaning: This place is so beautiful and sacred that its greatness cannot be fully described. Ram resolves to establish Shiva there.
ramacharitamanas::4494.simple_insight: Some places feel worthy of reverence before any explanation arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4494.detailed_meaning: After the bridge to Lanka is built, Ram looks at the land and feels its sacredness. He decides to establish Shiva there, showing that victory is complete only when reverence comes before pride.
ramacharitamanas::4494.modern_relevance: You reach the finish line and feel the urge to celebrate yourself. Instead, you pause, honor what made the work possible, and place respect before triumph.
ramacharitamanas::4494.insight: It shifts success from self-congratulation to reverent gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::4495.verse_sanskrit: सुनि कपीस बहु दूत पठाए। मुनिबर सकल बोलि लै आए॥ लिंग थापि बिधिवत करि पूजा। सिव समान प्रिय मोहि न दूजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4495.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर वानरराज सुग्रीव ने बहुत से दूत भेजे, जो सब श्रेष्ठ मुनियों को बुलाकर ले आए। शिवलिंग की स्थापना करके विधिपूर्वक उसका पूजन किया (फिर भगवान बोले-) शिवजी के समान मुझको दूसरा कोई प्रिय नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4495.english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, Sugriva sent many messengers and brought all the great sages. After establishing the ling and worshipping it properly, the Lord said, 'No one is dearer to me than Shiva.'
ramacharitamanas::4495.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / कपीस (lord of the monkeys) / बहु (many) / दूत (messengers) / पठाए (sent) / मुनिबर (best sages) / सकल (all) / बोलि (calling) / लै (taking) / आए (came) / लिंग (ling) / थापि (establishing) / बिधिवत (according to proper rule) / करि (doing) / पूजा (worship) / सिव (Shiva) / समान (equal to) / प्रिय (dear) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / दूजा (another)
ramacharitamanas::4495.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4495.essence: True devotion honors what it loves without rivalry.
ramacharitamanas::4495.simple_meaning: Ram has the sages brought in, then honors Shiva by स्थापितing and worshipping the ling properly. He declares that no one is dearer to him than Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::4495.simple_insight: Devotion becomes fuller when reverence is not selective.
ramacharitamanas::4495.detailed_meaning: At the bridge to Lanka, Ram pauses before battle and asks for Shiva to be properly स्थापितed and worshipped. Sugriva sends messengers to gather sages, and Ram openly declares Shiva his dearest, showing harmony between devotion and righteous action.
ramacharitamanas::4495.modern_relevance: Before a big confrontation, you stop, gather the right people, and make space for respect instead of ego. Real strength does not need to dismiss what it honors.
ramacharitamanas::4495.insight: It teaches you to let reverence guide action, even in the middle of urgency.

ramacharitamanas::4496.verse_sanskrit: सिव द्रोही मम भगत कहावा। सो नर सपनेहुँ मोहि न पावा॥ संकर बिमुख भगति चह मोरी। सो नारकी मूढ़ मति थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4496.verse_hindi: जो शिव से द्रोह रखता है और मेरा भक्त कहलाता है, वह मनुष्य स्वप्न में भी मुझे नहीं पाता। शंकरजी से विमुख होकर (विरोध करके) जो मेरी भक्ति चाहता है, वह नरकगामी, मूर्ख और अल्पबुद्धि है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4496.english_translation: One who opposes Shiva and still calls himself my devotee never finds me, even in dreams. One who wants my devotion while turning away from Shankar is foolish and headed for a lower realm.
ramacharitamanas::4496.translation_literal: सिव (Shiva) / द्रोही (hostile) / मम (my) / भगत (devotee) / कहावा (is called) / सो (that) / नर (person) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / मोहि (me) / न (not) / पावा (finds) ॥ / संकर (Shankar) / बिमुख (turned away) / भगति (devotion) / चह (wants) / मोरी (my) / सो (that) / नारकी (one headed to a lower realm) / मूढ़ (foolish) / मति (understanding) / थोरी (poor) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4496.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4496.essence: You cannot reach Ram by rejecting Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::4496.simple_meaning: Ram says that anyone who hates Shiva cannot truly reach him. Real devotion to Ram includes reverence for Shiva, not opposition to him.
ramacharitamanas::4496.simple_insight: Devotion becomes whole when it stops making enemies of what the divine honors.
ramacharitamanas::4496.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram has asked for Shiva's worship, he states a hard truth: devotion to him cannot be built on hostility toward Shankar. The scene turns worship into a test of humility, showing that Ram and Shiva are not rivals.
ramacharitamanas::4496.modern_relevance: You praise one teacher while sneering at the teacher they honor. That split reveals something in you, not in them. Real reverence doesn't need rivalry.
ramacharitamanas::4496.insight: It shifts devotion from selective preference to respectful wholeness, where love for Ram includes honor for Shiva.

ramacharitamanas::4497.verse_sanskrit: संकरप्रिय मम द्रोही सिव द्रोही मम दास। ते नर करहिं कलप भरि घोर नरक महुँ बास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4497.verse_hindi: जिनको शंकरजी प्रिय हैं, परन्तु जो मेरे द्रोही हैं एवं जो शिवजी के द्रोही हैं और मेरे दास (बनना चाहते) हैं, वे मनुष्य कल्पभर घोर नरक में निवास करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4497.english_translation: Those who love Shankara but are hostile to me, and those who are hostile to Shankara while calling themselves my servants, dwell in terrible lower realms for a full cycle.
ramacharitamanas::4497.translation_literal: संकरप्रिय (dear to Shankara) / मम (my) / द्रोही (hostile) / सिव (Shiva) / द्रोही (hostile) / मम (my) / दास (servant) / ते (those) / नर (people) / करहिं (do) / कलप भरि (for a full cycle) / घोर (terrible) / नरक (lower realm) / महुँ (in) / बास (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::4497.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4497.essence: Devotion to Ram cannot survive hostility toward Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::4497.simple_meaning: You cannot claim devotion to Ram while opposing Shiva. Real devotion does not split the divine into sides.
ramacharitamanas::4497.simple_insight: Devotion becomes whole when reverence is complete, not selective.
ramacharitamanas::4497.detailed_meaning: Ram is speaking after the call to honor Shiva. He draws a hard line: anyone who claims to be his servant while hating Shiva, or who loves Shiva but turns against him, misses the point of devotion entirely.
ramacharitamanas::4497.modern_relevance: You praise one mentor in public, then mock the other who taught you the same discipline. The split feels clever for a moment, but it reveals divided loyalty, not devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4497.insight: It shifts devotion from preference to integrity: reverence must be consistent across what you honor.

ramacharitamanas::4498.verse_sanskrit: जे रामेस्वर दरसनु करिहहिं। ते तनु तजि मम लोक सिधरिहहिं॥ जो गंगाजलु आनि चढ़ाइहि। सो साजुज्य मुक्ति नर पाइहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4498.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य (मेरे स्थापित किए हुए इन) रामेश्वरजी का दर्शन करेंगे, वे शरीर छोड़कर मेरे लोक को जाएँगे और जो गंगाजल लाकर इन पर चढ़ावेगा, वह मनुष्य सायुज्य मुक्ति पावेगा (अर्थात् मेरे साथ एक हो जाएगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4498.english_translation: Whoever comes to see Rameshwar will leave the body and reach my realm. Whoever brings Ganga water and offers it there will attain union with me.
ramacharitamanas::4498.translation_literal: जे (who) / रामेस्वर (Rameshwar) / दरसनु (darshan, sacred viewing) / करिहहिं (will do) / ते (they) / तनु (body) / तजि (leaving) / मम (my) / लोक (realm) / सिधरिहिं (will go) ॥ / जो (who) / गंगाजलु (Ganga water) / आनि (bringing) / चढ़ाइहि (will offer) / सो (that) / साजुज्य (union) / मुक्ति (freedom) / नर (person) / पाइहि (will attain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4498.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4498.essence: A sincere offering at Rameshwar can carry you beyond the body.
ramacharitamanas::4498.simple_meaning: Seeing Rameshwar and offering Ganga water there brings the deepest freedom. The body is left behind, and the devotee reaches Ram's own realm.
ramacharitamanas::4498.simple_insight: Sacred offering is not small; it can carry you into closeness with the divine.
ramacharitamanas::4498.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war section, the text turns from battle to worship. Ram speaks about the Rameshwar lingam he established and says that even seeing it, or offering Ganga water there, brings the devotee beyond bodily life into his own realm.
ramacharitamanas::4498.modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded temple queue with a small bottle of water in your hand, tired but sincere. The value is not in the size of the offering; it is in the heart that brings it.
ramacharitamanas::4498.insight: It shifts devotion from a ritual act to a direct path of belonging and release.

ramacharitamanas::4499.verse_sanskrit: होइ अकाम जो छल तजि सेइहि। भगति मोरि तेहि संकर देइहि॥ मम कृत सेतु जो दरसनु करिही। सो बिनु श्रम भवसागर तरिही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4499.verse_hindi: जो छल छोड़कर और निष्काम होकर श्री रामेश्वरजी की सेवा करेंगे, उन्हें शंकरजी मेरी भक्ति देंगे और जो मेरे बनाए सेतु का दर्शन करेगा, वह बिना ही परिश्रम संसार रूपी समुद्र से तर जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4499.english_translation: Whoever serves me without desire and without deceit, Shiva will give them devotion to me. Whoever beholds the bridge I built will cross the ocean of becoming without effort.
ramacharitamanas::4499.translation_literal: होइ (becomes) / अकाम (without desire) / जो (who) / छल (deceit) / तजि (leaving) / सेइहि (will serve) / भगति (devotion) / मोरि (to me) / तेहि (to that one) / संकर (Shankar) / देइहि (will give) / मम (my) / कृत (made) / सेतु (bridge) / जो (who) / दरसनु (vision) / करिही (will do) / सो (that one) / बिनु (without) / श्रम (effort) / भवसागर (ocean of becoming) / तरिही (will cross)
ramacharitamanas::4499.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4499.essence: Clean service opens the door to devotion and release.
ramacharitamanas::4499.simple_meaning: A heart free from desire and deceit receives devotion, and even seeing Ram's bridge becomes a way across life's vast suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4499.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that sincerity matters more than strain.
ramacharitamanas::4499.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Shiva explains the power of Ram's bridge at Rameshwaram. Those who serve without deceit and without craving receive devotion itself, and even the sight of Ram's bridge can carry a seeker beyond the ocean of becoming.
ramacharitamanas::4499.modern_relevance: You help someone late at night with no hidden agenda, no need to be praised, no plan to use it later. That clean-heartedness changes what the act becomes.
ramacharitamanas::4499.insight: It shifts action from self-interest to pure offering, where sincerity itself becomes the path.

ramacharitamanas::4500.verse_sanskrit: राम बचन सब के जिय भाए। मुनिबर निज निज आश्रम आए॥ गिरिजा रघुपति कै यह रीती। संतत करहिं प्रनत पर प्रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4500.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वचन सबके मन को अच्छे लगे। तदनन्तर वे श्रेष्ठ मुनि अपने-अपने आश्रमों को लौट आए। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! श्री रघुनाथजी की यह रीति है कि वे शरणागत पर सदा प्रीति करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4500.english_translation: Ram's words pleased everyone's heart. Then the great sages returned to their own hermitages. Parvati, this is Raghu's way: he always loves those who take refuge in him.
ramacharitamanas::4500.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बचन (words) / सब (all) / के (of) / जिय (heart) / भाए (were pleasing) / मुनिबर (great sages) / निज निज (each his own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / आए (came/returned) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / कै (of) / यह (this) / रीती (way/custom) / संतत (always) / करहिं (do) / प्रनत (one who bows/takes refuge) / पर (upon) / प्रीती (love)
ramacharitamanas::4500.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4500.essence: Surrender is answered by steady love.
ramacharitamanas::4500.simple_meaning: Ram's words satisfy everyone, and the sages return home. Shiva tells Parvati that Ram always loves and protects those who come to him in surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4500.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing you are not rejected when you reach out in humility.
ramacharitamanas::4500.detailed_meaning: After the bridge is discussed, Ram speaks and the gathered sages are pleased. As they return to their hermitages, Shiva turns to Parvati and reveals Ram's nature: he never withholds love from those who bow to him.
ramacharitamanas::4500.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, the room goes quiet and you finally hear the one sentence you needed. The fear of being turned away loosens when you realize humility can still be met with warmth.
ramacharitamanas::4500.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded self-protection to confident trust in surrender.

ramacharitamanas::4501.verse_sanskrit: बाँधा सेतु नील नल नागर। राम कृपाँ जसु भयउ उजागर॥ बूड़हिं आनहि बोरहिं जेई। भए उपल बोहित सम तेई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4501.verse_hindi: चतुर नल और नील ने सेतु बाँधा। श्री रामजी की कृपा से उनका यह (उज्ज्वल) यश सर्वत्र फैल गया। जो पत्थर आप डूबते हैं और दूसरों को डुबा देते हैं, वे ही जहाज के समान (स्वयं तैरने वाले और दूसरों को पार ले जाने वाले) हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4501.english_translation: Nala and Nila built the bridge. By Ram's grace, their fame shone everywhere. The stones that sink and sink others became like ships.
ramacharitamanas::4501.translation_literal: बाँधा (built) / सेतु (bridge) / नील (Nila) / नल (Nala) / नागर (skilled) / राम कृपाँ (by Ram's grace) / जसु (fame) / भयउ (became) / उजागर (brightly known) / बूड़हिं (they sink) / आनहि (bring others down) / बोरहिं (sink) / जेई (those who) / भए (became) / उपल (stones) / बोहित (ships) / सम (like) / तेई (they)
ramacharitamanas::4501.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4501.essence: Ram's grace turns even sinking stones into a way across.
ramacharitamanas::4501.simple_meaning: Nala and Nila built the bridge, and Ram's grace made their work famous. Even heavy stones became like boats, carrying others across.
ramacharitamanas::4501.simple_insight: What seems impossible can become a passage when grace works through skill.
ramacharitamanas::4501.detailed_meaning: On the shore before Lanka, Nala and Nila lead the building of Ram's bridge. The verse marvels that Ram's grace turns sinking stones into floating support, making the crossing possible and their fame unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::4501.modern_relevance: You fix something no one else can. What should have failed becomes the thing that carries everyone forward.
ramacharitamanas::4501.insight: It shifts attention from material limits to the transforming power of grace working through action.

ramacharitamanas::4502.verse_sanskrit: महिमा यह न जलधि कइ बरनी। पाहन गुन न कपिन्ह कइ करनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4502.verse_hindi: यह न तो समुद्र की महिमा वर्णन की गई है, न पत्थरों का गुण है और न वानरों की ही कोई करामात है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4502.english_translation: The glory is neither the sea's nor the stones' nor the monkeys' alone.
ramacharitamanas::4502.translation_literal: महिमा (glory) / यह (this) / न (not) / जलधि (sea) / कइ (of) / बरनी (described) / पाहन (stones) / गुन (virtue) / न (not) / कपिन्ह (of monkeys) / कइ (of) / करनी (deed)
ramacharitamanas::4502.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4502.essence: What looks like human achievement is really grace at work.
ramacharitamanas::4502.simple_meaning: The crossing was not only the sea's wonder, the stones' property, or the monkeys' skill. Ram's grace made it happen.
ramacharitamanas::4502.simple_insight: You can give your full effort and still know the deeper power was never just yours.
ramacharitamanas::4502.detailed_meaning: After the bridge is built in Lanka, the poem pauses to name what really made it possible. The sea, the stones, and the monkeys all played their part, but Tulsidas says the true force was Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4502.modern_relevance: You finish a project that should have failed, and everyone praises the team, the tools, or the timing. Quietly, you know something larger carried the work through.
ramacharitamanas::4502.insight: It shifts credit from visible skill to the divine grace behind successful action.

ramacharitamanas::4503.verse_sanskrit: श्री रघुबीर प्रताप ते सिंधु तरे पाषान। ते मतिमंद जे राम तजि भजहिं जाइ प्रभु आन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4503.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीर के प्रताप से पत्थर भी समुद्र पर तैर गए। ऐसे श्री रामजी को छोड़कर जो किसी दूसरे स्वामी को जाकर भजते हैं वे (निश्चय ही) मंदबुद्धि हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4503.english_translation: By the power of Lord Raghubir, stones crossed the sea. Those who, abandoning Ram, go to worship another lord are surely dull-minded.
ramacharitamanas::4503.translation_literal: श्री रघुबीर (Lord Raghubir) / प्रताप (power, glory) / ते (by) / सिंधु (sea) / तरे (crossed) / पाषान (stones) / ते (those) / मतिमंद (dull-minded) / जे (who) / राम (Ram) / तजि (abandoning) / भजहिं (worship) / जाइ (going) / प्रभु (lord) / आन (another)
ramacharitamanas::4503.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4503.essence: Ram's power carries the impossible; turning elsewhere is self-defeating.
ramacharitamanas::4503.simple_meaning: Ram's power made stones float across the sea. So leaving Ram for another master is called foolish.
ramacharitamanas::4503.simple_insight: Trust grows when you remember who actually carries you through what feels impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4503.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the bridge is taking shape and the impossible is becoming visible. Tulsidas pauses to name the real force behind it: Ram's power. The stones float because of him, and that makes abandoning him for another refuge look foolish.
ramacharitamanas::4503.modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels heavier than your own strength — a sick parent, a broken plan, a future you cannot engineer. This verse says: remember who has carried you before you start shopping for another anchor.
ramacharitamanas::4503.insight: It shifts you from divided loyalty to single-hearted refuge in Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4504.verse_sanskrit: बाँधि सेतु अति सुदृढ़ बनावा। देखि कृपानिधि के मन भावा॥ चली सेन कछु बरनि न जाई। गर्जहिं मर्कट भट समुदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4504.verse_hindi: नल-नील ने सेतु बाँधकर उसे बहुत मजबूत बनाया। देखने पर वह कृपानिधान श्री रामजी के मन को (बहुत ही) अच्छा लगा। सेना चली, जिसका कुछ वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। योद्धा वानरों के समुदाय गरज रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4504.english_translation: Nala and Nila built the bridge so strong that it pleased the compassionate Lord's heart. The army moved forward beyond description, and the monkey warriors roared as one.
ramacharitamanas::4504.translation_literal: बाँधि (having built) / सेतु (bridge) / अति (very) / सुदृढ़ (strong) / बनावा (made) / देखि (seeing) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / के (of) / मन (mind/heart) / भावा (was pleasing)॥ चली (moved) / सेना (army) / कछु (some) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be) / गर्जहिं (roar) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भट (warriors) / समुदाई (group, multitude) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4504.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4504.essence: The bridge is ready, and the army can move.
ramacharitamanas::4504.simple_meaning: Nala and Nila finish the bridge, and Ram is pleased. Then the army advances with a roar that cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::4504.simple_insight: Some moments matter because the work is done and the journey can begin.
ramacharitamanas::4504.detailed_meaning: Nala and Nila have completed the bridge to Lanka, and Ram sees that it is strong enough to trust. The monkey army now moves forward in force. This verse is a transition, not a teaching: the crossing is ready, and the war is about to enter its next stage.
ramacharitamanas::4504.modern_relevance: You finally finish the structure everyone depended on, and the room shifts from planning to movement. The real test begins only after the bridge holds.
ramacharitamanas::4504.insight: It marks the turning point from preparation to action, with no need for reflection or instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4505.verse_sanskrit: सेतुबंध ढिग चढ़ि रघुराई। चितव कृपाल सिंधु बहुताई॥ देखन कहुँ प्रभु करुना कंदा। प्रगट भए सब जलचर बृंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4505.verse_hindi: कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी सेतुबन्ध के तट पर चढ़कर समुद्र का विस्तार देखने लगे। करुणाकन्द (करुणा के मूल) प्रभु के दर्शन के लिए सब जलचरों के समूह प्रकट हो गए (जल के ऊपर निकल आए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4505.english_translation: Raghunath climbed onto the bridge's edge and looked over the vast sea. At the sight of the compassionate one, all the creatures of the water emerged.
ramacharitamanas::4505.translation_literal: सेतुबंध (the bridge) / ढिग (near) / चढ़ि (climbing) / रघुराई (Raghurai, Ram) / चितव (looked) / कृपाल (the compassionate one) / सिंधु (sea) / बहुताई (vastness)॥ / देखन (to see) / कहुँ (for) / प्रभु (Lord) / करुना (compassion) / कंदा (source)॥ / प्रगट (manifested) / भए (became) / सब (all) / जलचर (water-creatures) / बृंदा (groups)॥
ramacharitamanas::4505.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4505.essence: Compassion makes even the hidden world come forward.
ramacharitamanas::4505.simple_meaning: Ram stands by the bridge and looks out over the sea. His compassionate presence draws all the sea-creatures into view.
ramacharitamanas::4505.simple_insight: Even the world seems to open when compassion is near.
ramacharitamanas::4505.detailed_meaning: On the shore at the bridge, Ram pauses to look over the sea before the war. His presence is so full of mercy that the hidden creatures of the water emerge, making the scene vivid and alive.
ramacharitamanas::4505.modern_relevance: You stop at the edge of something enormous — a decision, a loss, a future you can't see clearly — and the moment you soften, hidden things begin to surface.
ramacharitamanas::4505.insight: It frames stillness and compassion as forces that reveal what is otherwise unseen.

ramacharitamanas::4506.verse_sanskrit: मकर नक्र नाना झष ब्याला। सत जोजन तन परम बिसाला॥ अइसेउ एक तिन्हहि जे खाहीं। एकन्ह कें डर तेपि डेराहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4506.verse_hindi: बहुत तरह के मगर, नाक (घड़ियाल), मच्छ और सर्प थे, जिनके सौ-सौ योजन के बहुत बड़े विशाल शरीर थे। कुछ ऐसे भी जन्तु थे, जो उनको भी खा जाएँ। किसी-किसी के डर से तो वे भी डर रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4506.english_translation: There were many kinds of crocodiles, alligators, fish, and serpents, with bodies a hundred yojanas vast. Some creatures could even swallow them, and they too feared others.
ramacharitamanas::4506.translation_literal: मकर (crocodiles) / नक्र (alligators) / नाना (many kinds) / झष (fish) / ब्याला (serpents) / सत जोजन (hundred yojanas) / तन (body) / परम बिसाला (extremely vast) / अइसेउ (even such) / एक (some) / तिन्हहि (them) / जे खाहीं (who eat) / एकन्ह कें (of some) / डर (fear) / तेपि (also) / डेराहीं (are afraid)
ramacharitamanas::4506.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4506.essence: Even the fiercest beings live under fear.
ramacharitamanas::4506.simple_meaning: The sea is full of enormous, frightening creatures, and even the biggest ones are afraid of something bigger.
ramacharitamanas::4506.simple_insight: Fear is relative; even the powerful are not beyond trembling.
ramacharitamanas::4506.detailed_meaning: At the edge of the ocean, Ram's army is facing the impossible. The narrator describes the sea's monstrous life to show the scale of the crossing ahead. This is not the lesson yet, only the fearful setting before the deeper turning toward Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::4506.modern_relevance: Standing at the mouth of a dark tunnel, you notice how every shadow feels larger than the last. What looked dominant a moment ago is already afraid of something else.
ramacharitamanas::4506.insight: It shifts attention from imagined monsters to the fact that every force has limits.

ramacharitamanas::4507.verse_sanskrit: प्रभुहि बिलोकहिं टरहिं न टारे। मन हरषित सब भए सुखारे॥ तिन्ह कीं ओट न देखिअ बारी। मगन भए हरि रूप निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4507.verse_hindi: वे सब (वैर-विरोध भूलकर) प्रभु के दर्शन कर रहे हैं, हटाने से भी नहीं हटते। सबके मन हर्षित हैं, सब सुखी हो गए। उनकी आड़ के कारण जल नहीं दिखाई पड़ता। वे सब भगवान् का रूप देखकर (आनंद और प्रेम में) मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4507.english_translation: They all gaze at the Lord and cannot be driven away. Every heart is joyful and at ease. The water is hidden by their bodies. Seeing the form of Hari, they are lost in delight.
ramacharitamanas::4507.translation_literal: प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकहिं (look at) / टरहिं (move away) / न (not) / टारे (driven away) / मन (minds) / हरषित (filled with joy) / सब (all) / भए (became) / सुखारे (at ease) / तिन्ह (their) / कीं (of) / ओट (covering) / न (not) / देखिअ (is seen) / बारी (water) / मगन (absorbed) / भए (became) / हरि (Hari) / रूप (form) / निहारी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::4507.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4507.essence: Awe makes even the sea forget itself.
ramacharitamanas::4507.simple_meaning: The sea-creatures gather to see Ram and become so delighted that they do not move away, blocking the water from view.
ramacharitamanas::4507.simple_insight: Wonder can make you forget everything else.
ramacharitamanas::4507.detailed_meaning: At the edge of the sea, Ram stands on the shore and the ocean’s creatures rise to behold him. They press in so closely that the water disappears from sight. This is a scene of joyful marvel, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4507.modern_relevance: You stop mid-step at a street performance, and the crowd around the stage becomes part of the experience. The moment itself is the point, not what it teaches.
ramacharitamanas::4507.insight: It simply records a shared burst of wonder, with no moral instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4508.verse_sanskrit: चला कटकु प्रभु आयसु पाई। को कहि सक कपि दल बिपुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4508.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर सेना चली। वानर सेना की विपुलता (अत्यधिक संख्या) को कौन कह सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4508.english_translation: The army moved forward after receiving the Lord's command. Who can describe the vast monkey host?
ramacharitamanas::4508.translation_literal: चला (moved) / कटकु (army) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / को (who) / कहि (say) / सक (can) / कपि (monkey) / दल (host) / बिपुलाई (vast)
ramacharitamanas::4508.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4508.essence: Once the command is given, the vast force moves as one.
ramacharitamanas::4508.simple_meaning: After Ram gave the order, the monkey army moved out. Its size was so immense that no one could fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::4508.simple_insight: Great movements begin with clear command, then flow beyond what words can count.
ramacharitamanas::4508.detailed_meaning: On the bridge to Lanka, Ram's command sets the host in motion. The monkeys surge forward as one immense force, and the poet pauses to marvel at their number before the crossing continues.
ramacharitamanas::4508.modern_relevance: A team finally gets the green light, and the room shifts from planning to motion. The scale of what follows is bigger than anyone can neatly count.
ramacharitamanas::4508.insight: It shifts attention from the order itself to the unstoppable momentum that follows clear leadership.

ramacharitamanas::4509.verse_sanskrit: सेतुबंध भइ भीर अति कपि नभ पंथ उड़ाहिं। अपर जलचरन्हि ऊपर चढ़ि चढ़ि पारहि जाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4509.verse_hindi: सेतुबन्ध पर बड़ी भीड़ हो गई, इससे कुछ वानर आकाश मार्ग से उड़ने लगे और दूसरे (कितने ही) जलचर जीवों पर चढ़-चढ़कर पार जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4509.english_translation: The bridge grew so crowded that some monkeys flew through the sky, while others climbed over water creatures and crossed the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4509.translation_literal: सेतुबंध (the bridge across the sea) / भइ (became) / भीर (crowded) / अति (very) / कपि (monkeys) / नभ (sky) / पंथ (path) / उड़ाहिं (fly) / अपर (others) / जलचरन्हि (water creatures) / ऊपर (on top) / चढ़ि चढ़ि (climbing again and again) / पारहि (across) / जाहिं (go)
ramacharitamanas::4509.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4509.essence: The crossing is so crowded it turns into a spectacle.
ramacharitamanas::4509.simple_meaning: The crossing became so crowded that some monkeys flew overhead and others crossed by stepping over sea creatures.
ramacharitamanas::4509.simple_insight: It is a vivid scene of movement, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4509.detailed_meaning: As Ram's army crosses the sea after the bridge is built, the scene becomes packed with monkeys surging forward in every possible way. The verse simply paints the bustle and wonder of the crossing before Ram and Lakshman follow.
ramacharitamanas::4509.modern_relevance: A festival crowd pours over a narrow bridge, people squeezing forward from every side. The verse captures motion, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::4509.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to spectacle, showing the crossing as a living scene.

ramacharitamanas::4510.verse_sanskrit: अस कौतुक बिलोकि द्वौ भाई। बिहँसि चले कृपाल रघुराई॥ सेन सहित उतरे रघुबीरा। कहि न जाइ कपि जूथप भीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4510.verse_hindi: कृपालु रघुनाथजी (तथा लक्ष्मणजी) दोनों भाई ऐसा कौतुक देखकर हँसते हुए चले। श्री रघुवीर सेना सहित समुद्र के पार हो गए। वानरों और उनके सेनापतियों की भीड़ कही नहीं जा सकती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4510.english_translation: Seeing this strange spectacle, the two brothers laughed and moved on. The compassionate Raghunath crossed over with the army; the crowd of monkeys and their leaders cannot be counted.
ramacharitamanas::4510.translation_literal: अस (such) / कौतुक (wonderful spectacle) / बिलोकि (seeing) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) / बिहँसि (laughing) / चले (went) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुराई (Raghunath)॥ / सेन (with army) / सहित (together) / उतरे (crossed over) / रघुबीरा (Raghu-hero)॥ / कहि (said) / न (not) / जाइ (can be told) / कपि (monkey) / जूथप (leaders) / भीरा (crowd) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4510.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4510.essence: The crossing is so immense it becomes a sight to behold.
ramacharitamanas::4510.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman laugh at the sight, then cross the sea with the army. The monkey hosts are so vast that no one can count them.
ramacharitamanas::4510.simple_insight: Some moments are too vast for numbers; you simply move with them.
ramacharitamanas::4510.detailed_meaning: The bridge is complete and the march continues into Lanka. Ram and Lakshman smile at the scene before them, then lead the entire vanara force across the sea. The verse lingers on the sheer scale of the crossing, not on a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4510.modern_relevance: You watch a crowd pour out of a stadium after midnight, friends and strangers moving in one tide. The moment is bigger than any one person, and all you can do is keep walking.
ramacharitamanas::4510.insight: It keeps attention on the unfolding scene rather than on interpretation or instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4511.verse_sanskrit: सिंधु पार प्रभु डेरा कीन्हा। सकल कपिन्ह कहुँ आयसु दीन्हा॥ खाहु जाइ फल मूल सुहाए। सुनत भालू कपि जहँ तहँ धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4511.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने समुद्र के पार डेरा डाला और सब वानरों को आज्ञा दी कि तुम जाकर सुंदर फल-मूल खाओ। यह सुनते ही रीछ-वानर जहाँ-तहाँ दौड़ पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4511.english_translation: The Lord camped beyond the sea and told all the monkeys, "Go eat the lovely fruits and roots." Hearing this, the bears and monkeys rushed off in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::4511.translation_literal: सिंधु (sea) / पार (across) / प्रभु (the Lord) / डेरा (camp) / कीन्हा (made) / सकल (all) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / कहुँ (to) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / खाहु (eat) / जाइ (go) / फल (fruits) / मूल (roots) / सुहाए (pleasant) / सुनत (hearing) / भालू (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / धाए (ran)
ramacharitamanas::4511.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4511.essence: Even in war, Ram gives his followers rest.
ramacharitamanas::4511.simple_meaning: Ram sets up camp beyond the sea and tells the monkeys to go enjoy the fruit and roots nearby. The whole army then scatters happily to forage.
ramacharitamanas::4511.simple_insight: After the crossing, even rest becomes part of service.
ramacharitamanas::4511.detailed_meaning: After the army crosses the sea, Ram settles the camp and gives the monkeys permission to go eat. The verse pauses the war story for a moment of relief, showing the army’s ease after a hard crossing.
ramacharitamanas::4511.modern_relevance: You finally finish the exhausting trip, drop your bags, and hear, "Go eat, rest, breathe." The job is not victory alone; it is also knowing when to release the strain.
ramacharitamanas::4511.insight: It shifts attention from struggle to restoration without losing the larger mission.

ramacharitamanas::4512.verse_sanskrit: सब तरु फरे राम हित लागी। रितु अरु कुरितु काल गति त्यागी॥ खाहिं मधुर फल बिटप हलावहिं। लंका सन्मुख सिखर चलावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4512.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के हित (सेवा) के लिए सब वृक्ष ऋतु-कुऋतु- समय की गति को छोड़कर फल उठे। वानर-भालू मीठे फल खा रहे हैं, वृक्षों को हिला रहे हैं और पर्वतों के शिखरों को लंका की ओर फेंक रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4512.english_translation: For Rama's sake, all the trees bore fruit, ignoring season, unseason, and the movement of time. The monkeys and bears ate sweet fruit, shook the trees, and hurled mountain peaks toward Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4512.translation_literal: सब (all) / तरु (trees) / फरे (fruited) / राम हित लागी (for Rama's sake) / रितु (season) / अरु (and) / कुरितु (out-of-season) / काल गति (movement of time) / त्यागी (having छोड़ा) / खाहिं (eat) / मधुर (sweet) / फल (fruit) / बिटप (trees) / हलावहिं (shake) / लंका सन्मुख (toward Lanka) / सिखर (peaks) / चलावहिं (send/throw)
ramacharitamanas::4512.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4512.essence: When Ram is the aim, even nature seems to serve.
ramacharitamanas::4512.simple_meaning: The forest itself seems to cooperate with Ram's army. Trees bear fruit out of season, and the monkeys and bears use the land's gifts as they prepare for Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4512.simple_insight: When your purpose is clear, even obstacles start feeling like support.
ramacharitamanas::4512.detailed_meaning: Ram's army has camped near the sea. In this charged moment, the forest responds as if it knows the mission: trees fruit at the wrong time, the monkeys feast, and the mountain peaks become weapons aimed at Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4512.modern_relevance: You're working late on a cause you believe in, and help appears from unexpected places — a friend texts, a tool works, a door opens. Momentum can feel like the world is joining in.
ramacharitamanas::4512.insight: It frames the march to Lanka as a world aligned with dharma, not just an army on the move.

ramacharitamanas::4513.verse_sanskrit: जहँ कहुँ फिरत निसाचर पावहिं। घेरि सकल बहु नाच नचावहिं॥ दसनन्हि काटि नासिका काना। कहि प्रभु सुजसु देहिं तब जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4513.verse_hindi: घूमते-घूमते जहाँ कहीं किसी राक्षस को पा जाते हैं तो सब उसे घेरकर खूब नाच नचाते हैं और दाँतों से उसके नाक-कान काटकर, प्रभु का सुयश कहकर (अथवा कहलाकर) तब उसे जाने देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4513.english_translation: Wherever they find a demon wandering, they surround him and make him dance a lot. Then they bite off his nose and ears with their teeth, speak the Lord's fame, and only then let him go.
ramacharitamanas::4513.translation_literal: जहँ कहुँ (wherever) / फिरत (wandering) / निसाचर (demon) / पावहिं (they find) / घेरि (surrounding) / सकल (all) / बहु (much) / नाच (dance) / नचावहिं (make dance) / दसनन्हि (with teeth) / काटि (cut) / नासिका (nose) / काना (ears) / कहि (speaking) / प्रभु (Lord's) / सुजसु (fame) / देहिं (they give) / तब (then) / जाना (let go)
ramacharitamanas::4513.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4513.essence: Ram's fame travels even through the enemy's humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::4513.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears torment any demon they find, cut off his nose and ears, and only then let him leave after praising Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4513.simple_insight: Even in war, Ram's side turns violence into a display of his fame.
ramacharitamanas::4513.detailed_meaning: The monkey army has crossed into Lanka and is roaming freely. Any demon they catch is humiliated, marked, and released with Ram's name on their lips. The verse is a vivid battle-detail, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4513.insight: It shows the enemy's fear spreading through humiliation and word of Ram's power.

ramacharitamanas::4514.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह कर नासा कान निपाता। तिन्ह रावनहि कही सब बाता॥ सुनत श्रवन बारिधि बंधाना। दस मुख बोलि उठा अकुलाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4514.verse_hindi: जिन राक्षसों के नाक और कान काट डाले गए, उन्होंने रावण से सब समाचार कहा। समुद्र (पर सेतु) का बाँधा जाना कानों से सुनते ही रावण घबड़ाकर दसों मुखों से बोल उठा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4514.english_translation: The demons whose noses and ears had been cut off told Ravana everything. Hearing that the ocean had been bridged, Ravana grew uneasy and spoke with all ten mouths.
ramacharitamanas::4514.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / कर (whose) / नासा (nose) / कान (ears) / निपाता (cut off) / तिन्ह (they) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / कही (said) / सब (all) / बाता (news)॥ / सुनत (hearing) / श्रवन (through ears) / बारिधि (ocean) / बंधाना (being bound) / दस मुख (ten mouths) / बोलि (speaking) / उठा (rose up) / अकुलाना (agitated) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4514.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4514.essence: Denial collapses the moment the facts become impossible to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::4514.simple_meaning: Wounded demons report the news to Ravana, and the report of the bridge across the ocean shakes him badly.
ramacharitamanas::4514.simple_insight: Pride starts to crack the moment reality reaches it.
ramacharitamanas::4514.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the maimed demons return with news of Hanuman's campaign. They tell Ravana that the ocean has been bridged. The report lands like a blow, and the ten-headed king is thrown into agitation.
ramacharitamanas::4514.modern_relevance: You keep hearing updates that everything is slipping beyond your control. One message, one headline, one call — and the confidence you built starts to wobble.
ramacharitamanas::4514.insight: It shows how fear spreads when a person can no longer deny the scale of what is coming.

ramacharitamanas::4515.verse_sanskrit: बाँध्यो बननिधि नीरनिधि जलधि सिंधु बारीस। सत्य तोयनिधि कंपति उदधि पयोधि नदीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4515.verse_hindi: वननिधि, नीरनिधि, जलधि, सिंधु, वारीश, तोयनिधि, कंपति, उदधि, पयोधि, नदीश को क्या सचमुच ही बाँध लिया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4515.english_translation: Has the ocean of waters really been bound? The sea, the great river-lord, trembles at the news.
ramacharitamanas::4515.translation_literal: बाँध्यो (was bound) / बननिधि (ocean of forests) / नीरनिधि (ocean of waters) / जलधि (sea) / सिंधु (ocean) / बारीस (lord of waters) / सत्य (truly) / तोयनिधि (ocean of water) / कंपति (trembles) / उदधि (ocean) / पयोधि (sea) / नदीस (lord of rivers)
ramacharitamanas::4515.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4515.essence: What seemed unbridgeable now trembles before Ram's resolve.
ramacharitamanas::4515.simple_meaning: The verse marvels that the sea itself seems shaken by the news that Ram's army has bound it. It is a poetic question, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4515.simple_insight: Great obstacles can look smaller when courage moves first.
ramacharitamanas::4515.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's men report that the ocean has been bridged. The news reaches the court like a shockwave. This doha pauses on the impossible scale of what Ram's side has done, before the story moves on to Ravana's disturbed reaction.
ramacharitamanas::4515.modern_relevance: You hear that the thing everyone called impossible is already underway, and your own certainty wobbles for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::4515.insight: It frames a near-impossible achievement as a fact that unsettles pride.

ramacharitamanas::4516.verse_sanskrit: निज बिकलता बिचारि बहोरी॥ बिहँसि गयउ गृह करि भय भोरी॥ मंदोदरीं सुन्यो प्रभु आयो। कौतुकहीं पाथोधि बँधायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4516.verse_hindi: फिर अपनी व्याकुलता को समझकर (ऊपर से) हँसता हुआ, भय को भुलाकर, रावण महल को गया। (जब) मंदोदरी ने सुना कि प्रभु श्री रामजी आ गए हैं और उन्होंने खेल में ही समुद्र को बँधवा लिया है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4516.english_translation: After thinking over his own agitation, Ravana laughed it off and went back to the palace, putting fear aside. When Mandodari heard that Lord Ram had arrived and had bound the ocean almost playfully,
ramacharitamanas::4516.translation_literal: निज (own) / बिकलता (agitation) / बिचारि (thinking over) / बहोरी (again) / बिहँसि (laughing) / गयउ (went) / गृह (home/palace) / करि (doing) / भय (fear) / भोरी (throwing aside) / मंदोदरीं (Mandodari) / सुन्यो (heard) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयो (has come) / कौतुकहीं (as play) / पाथोधि (ocean) / बँधायो (bound)
ramacharitamanas::4516.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4516.essence: Fear can be disguised, but it still follows you home.
ramacharitamanas::4516.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to shake off his fear and return to the palace, while Mandodari hears that Ram has arrived and has bound the ocean easily.
ramacharitamanas::4516.simple_insight: Panic can be hidden for a moment, but it does not disappear.
ramacharitamanas::4516.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just heard that the ocean has been bridged. He forces himself to laugh and goes back inside, trying to cover his fear. At the same time, Mandodari hears the impossible news: Ram has come, and the sea has been bound as if it were a game.
ramacharitamanas::4516.modern_relevance: You get alarming news, force a calm face, and walk back into the meeting as if nothing happened. Inside, the fear is still there, waiting.
ramacharitamanas::4516.insight: It shows how ego tries to mask fear with laughter, even when reality has already shifted.

ramacharitamanas::4517.verse_sanskrit: कर गहि पतिहि भवन निज आनी। बोली परम मनोहर बानी॥ चरन नाइ सिरु अंचलु रोपा। सुनहु बचन पिय परिहरि कोपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4517.verse_hindi: (तब) वह हाथ पकड़कर, पति को अपने महल में लाकर परम मनोहर वाणी बोली। चरणों में सिर नवाकर उसने अपना आँचल पसारा और कहा- हे प्रियतम! क्रोध त्याग कर मेरा वचन सुनिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4517.english_translation: Then she took her husband by the hand and brought him into her palace. She spoke in a most lovely voice. Bowing her head at his feet, she spread out her garment and said, “My beloved, please set aside your anger and hear me.”
ramacharitamanas::4517.translation_literal: कर (hand) / गहि (grasping) / पतिहि (the husband) / भवन (palace) / निज (own) / आनी (bringing) / बोली (spoke) / परम (supremely) / मनोहर (beautiful) / बानी (speech)॥ / चरन (feet) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / अंचलु (garment's edge) / रोपा (spread)॥ / सुनहु (listen) / बचन (words) / पिय (beloved) / परिहरि (setting aside) / कोपा (anger)॥
ramacharitamanas::4517.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4517.essence: Gentle speech can reach even an angry heart.
ramacharitamanas::4517.simple_meaning: Mandodari gently brings Ravana inside, bows to him, and asks him to drop his anger and listen to her.
ramacharitamanas::4517.simple_insight: Even in a broken moment, calm speech can still reach the person you love.
ramacharitamanas::4517.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just returned shaken after hearing that Ram has bridged the ocean. Mandodari meets him with tenderness, not force. She leads him inside, bows low, and tries to pull him back from pride before disaster becomes final.
ramacharitamanas::4517.modern_relevance: Your partner comes home furious after a humiliating day, and every sharp reply would only deepen the wound. This verse shows the power of soft words when anger is already burning.
ramacharitamanas::4517.insight: It teaches you to lower the temperature before you try to be heard.

ramacharitamanas::4518.verse_sanskrit: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4518.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! वैर उसी के साथ करना चाहिए, जिससे बुद्धि और बल के द्वारा जीत सकें। आप में और श्री रघुनाथजी में निश्चय ही कैसा अंतर है, जैसा जुगनू और सूर्य में! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4518.english_translation: O Lord, you should fight only with someone you can defeat by intelligence and strength. What difference is there between you and Raghupati? The wicked are like fireflies before the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4518.translation_literal: नाथ (O lord) / बयरु (enmity) / कीजे (should be done) / ताही सों (with that one) / बुधि (intelligence) / बल (strength) / सकिअ (can be) / जीति (to defeat) / जाही सों (with whom) ॥ / तुम्हहि (you) / रघुपतिहि (with Raghupati) / अंतर (difference) / कैसा (what kind) / खलु (wicked one) / खद्योत (firefly) / दिनकरहि (to the sun) / जैसा (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4518.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4518.essence: Pride fails when it mistakes a firefly for the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4518.simple_meaning: Mandodari warns Ravana that enmity should be chosen only against someone he can actually defeat. She says his power is nothing beside Ram's, like a firefly beside the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4518.simple_insight: Pride shrinks when you finally see the scale of what stands before you.
ramacharitamanas::4518.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari pleads with Ravana after hearing that Ram has come. She tries to stop his reckless pride by comparing his strength to Ram's vast power. Her warning is not just marital concern; it is a last attempt to save him from a doomed choice.
ramacharitamanas::4518.modern_relevance: You send the angry reply, then stare at the screen and realise the other person can ruin your day, not your life. Mandodari's warning says: don't confuse noise with power.
ramacharitamanas::4518.insight: It shifts you from ego-driven conflict to clear-eyed judgment about who and what you can truly oppose.

ramacharitamanas::4519.verse_sanskrit: अति बल मधु कैटभ जेहिं मारे। महाबीर दितिसुत संघारे॥ जेहिं बलि बाँधि सहस भुज मारा। सोइ अवतरेउ हरन महि भारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4519.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने (विष्णु रूप से) अत्यन्त बलवान् मधु और कैटभ (दैत्य) मारे और (वराह और नृसिंह रूप से) महान् शूरवीर दिति के पुत्रों (हिरण्याक्ष और हिरण्यकशिपु) का संहार किया, जिन्होंने (वामन रूप से) बलि को बाँधा और (परशुराम रूप से) सहस्रबाहु को मारा, वे ही (भगवान् ) पृथ्वी का भार हरण करने के लिए (रामरूप में) अवतीर्ण (प्रकट) हुए हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4519.english_translation: The one who destroyed mighty Madhu and Kaitabha, who slew the great warrior sons of Diti, who bound Bali and killed Sahasrabahu, has now appeared as Ram to lift the burden of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::4519.translation_literal: अति बल (very powerful) / मधु (Madhu) / कैटभ (Kaitabha) / जेहिं (who) / मारे (killed)॥ / महाबीर (great hero) / दितिसुत (sons of Diti) / संघारे (destroyed)॥ / जेहिं (who) / बलि (Bali) / बाँधि (binding) / सहस भुज (thousand-armed) / मारा (killed)॥ / सोइ (that same one) / अवतरेउ (has descended) / हरन (to remove) / महि (earth) / भारा (burden)॥
ramacharitamanas::4519.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4519.essence: The same power that conquered chaos has arrived in gentle form.
ramacharitamanas::4519.simple_meaning: The speaker praises Ram as the same supreme being who once defeated many mighty enemies and has now appeared on earth to remove its burden.
ramacharitamanas::4519.simple_insight: You are not facing a smaller power. The one who helps you has already overcome every force that seemed impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4519.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari is pleading with Ravana not to fight Ram. She reminds him that the being now standing before him is not ordinary: the same divine power that destroyed ancient demons and humbled kings has come as Ram to relieve the world's burden.
ramacharitamanas::4519.modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels ancient and unbeatable, as if it has defeated everyone before you. This verse says the force that can lift it is not new, weak, or uncertain.
ramacharitamanas::4519.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing appearances to trusting the power behind them.

ramacharitamanas::4520.verse_sanskrit: तासु बिरोध न कीजिअ नाथा। काल करम जिव जाकें हाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4520.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! उनका विरोध न कीजिए, जिनके हाथ में काल, कर्म और जीव सभी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4520.english_translation: O Lord, do not oppose the one in whose hands are time, action, and every living being.
ramacharitamanas::4520.translation_literal: तासु (to that one) / बिरोध (opposition) / न (not) / कीजिअ (should be done) / नाथा (O Lord) / काल (time) / करम (action) / जिव (living being) / जाकें (whose) / हाथा (hands)
ramacharitamanas::4520.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4520.essence: Resistance is foolish before the one who governs time and life.
ramacharitamanas::4520.simple_meaning: Do not oppose Ram, because time, action, and every living being are under his control.
ramacharitamanas::4520.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop fighting what already exceeds your control.
ramacharitamanas::4520.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a speaker is urging Ravana to stop his hostility. The warning is simple and absolute: Ram is not an ordinary enemy, because time, action, and every living being move in his hand.
ramacharitamanas::4520.modern_relevance: You are arguing with a situation that has already moved beyond your control: a diagnosis, a breakup, a deadline, a loss. This verse asks you to stop resisting reality and bow to what is greater than your will.
ramacharitamanas::4520.insight: It shifts the mind from defiance to surrender before the power that governs all outcomes.

ramacharitamanas::4521.verse_sanskrit: रामहि सौंपि जानकी नाइ कमल पद माथ। सुत कहुँ राज समर्पि बन जाइ भजिअ रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4521.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी) के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर (उनकी शरण में जाकर) उनको जानकीजी सौंप दीजिए और आप पुत्र को राज्य देकर वन में जाकर श्री रघुनाथजी का भजन कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4521.english_translation: Bow your head at Ram's lotus feet, entrust Janaki to him, give the kingdom to your son, and go to the forest to worship Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::4521.translation_literal: रामहि (to Ram) / सौंपि (entrusting) / जानकी (Janaki) / नाइ (bowing) / कमल पद (lotus feet) / माथ (head) / सुत कहुँ (to the son) / राज (kingdom) / समर्पि (giving up) / बन जाइ (going to the forest) / भजिअ (worship) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::4521.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4521.essence: True devotion begins when you stop trying to keep what was never yours.
ramacharitamanas::4521.simple_meaning: Bow to Ram, hand over what you love, and stop clinging to power. Real devotion is choosing him over possession.
ramacharitamanas::4521.simple_insight: Letting go can feel like loss, but it can also become the most faithful act of your life.
ramacharitamanas::4521.detailed_meaning: In the war's opening counsel, a speaker urges total surrender: place Janaki in Ram's care, hand the kingdom to the son, and withdraw into the forest to live in devotion. The verse turns renunciation into the highest form of loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::4521.modern_relevance: You finally admit you cannot keep everything: the relationship, the role, the control. Instead of forcing it, you hand over what you cannot hold and choose what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::4521.insight: It shifts the mind from possession to surrender, showing that devotion begins where control ends.

ramacharitamanas::4522.verse_sanskrit: नाथ दीनदयाल रघुराई। बाघउ सनमुख गएँ न खाई॥ चाहिअ करन सो सब करि बीते। तुम्ह सुर असुर चराचर जीते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4522.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! श्री रघुनाथजी तो दीनों पर दया करने वाले हैं। सम्मुख (शरण) जाने पर तो बाघ भी नहीं खाता। आपको जो कुछ करना चाहिए था, वह सब आप कर चुके। आपने देवता, राक्षस तथा चर-अचर सभी को जीत लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4522.english_translation: O Lord, Raghunath is kind to the poor. Even a tiger does not eat when one approaches him in surrender. You have already done all that needed doing. You have conquered the gods, demons, and all moving and unmoving beings.
ramacharitamanas::4522.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / दीनदयाल (compassionate to the poor) / रघुराई (Lord of Raghu) / बाघउ (even tiger) / सनमुख (facing, in surrender) / गएँ (going) / न (not) / खाई (eats) ॥ चाहिअ (needed) / करन (to do) / सो (that) / सब (all) / करि (having done) / बीते (passed) ॥ तुम्ह (you) / सुर (gods) / असुर (demons) / चराचर (moving and unmoving beings) / जीते (conquered) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4522.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4522.essence: Surrender to Ram, and even fear loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::4522.simple_meaning: Ram is compassionate to anyone who comes to him openly. The speaker says the listener has already done everything required and has already conquered every being.
ramacharitamanas::4522.simple_insight: There is relief in laying down the burden of proving yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4522.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a voice urges Ravana to stop resisting. Ram is not a force that devours the surrendered; he is kind to the helpless. The speaker says the time for action has passed, because Ram's victory already spans all beings.
ramacharitamanas::4522.modern_relevance: You’ve spent the whole night trying to fix what cannot be forced. The moment you stop bracing and ask for help honestly, the room feels less hostile.
ramacharitamanas::4522.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to surrender, and from self-effort to refuge in Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4523.verse_sanskrit: संत कहहिं असि नीति दसानन। चौथेंपन जाइहि नृप कानन॥ तासु भजनु कीजिअ तहँ भर्ता। जो कर्ता पालक संहर्ता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4523.verse_hindi: हे दशमुख! संतजन ऐसी नीति कहते हैं कि चौथेपन (बुढ़ापे) में राजा को वन में चला जाना चाहिए। हे स्वामी! वहाँ (वन में) आप उनका भजन कीजिए जो सृष्टि के रचने वाले, पालने वाले और संहार करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4523.english_translation: The saints say this policy, O Ravana: in old age, a king should go to the forest. There, O master, worship the one who creates, sustains, and destroys all.
ramacharitamanas::4523.translation_literal: संत (saints) / कहहिं (say) / असि (this) / नीति (policy) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / चौथेंपन (in old age) / जाइहि (should go) / नृप (king) / कानन (to the forest) / तासु (that one’s) / भजनु (worship) / कीजिअ (should be done) / तहँ (there) / भर्ता (master) / जो (who) / कर्ता (creator) / पालक (sustainer) / संहर्ता (destroyer)
ramacharitamanas::4523.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4523.essence: Power should end in reverence, not in more grasping.
ramacharitamanas::4523.simple_meaning: A ruler should eventually leave worldly power behind and turn toward worship of the one behind creation, preservation, and dissolution.
ramacharitamanas::4523.simple_insight: Power is temporary; what matters is where you place your attention when life quiets down.
ramacharitamanas::4523.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, wise counsel is being offered to Ravana. The speaker says that a king should withdraw in old age and turn to worship the power behind all existence. The point is not just retirement, but a final reorientation of life.
ramacharitamanas::4523.modern_relevance: You’ve spent decades building a name, a company, a family role, a reputation. Then one day the noise drops, and the deeper question arrives: what have you been serving all along?
ramacharitamanas::4523.insight: It shifts the mind from preserving status to preparing for a deeper reckoning.

ramacharitamanas::4524.verse_sanskrit: सोइ रघुबीर प्रनत अनुरागी। भजहु नाथ ममता सब त्यागी॥ मुनिबर जतनु करहिं जेहि लागी। भूप राजु तजि होहिं बिरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4524.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आप विषयों की सारी ममता छोड़कर उन्हीं शरणागत पर प्रेम करने वाले भगवान् का भजन कीजिए। जिनके लिए श्रेष्ठ मुनि साधन करते हैं और राजा राज्य छोड़कर वैरागी हो जाते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4524.english_translation: O Lord, worship that Raghubir who loves the surrendered and is loved by those who have given up all attachment. Great sages practice austerity to reach Him, and kings renounce their kingdoms to become detached.
ramacharitamanas::4524.translation_literal: सोइ (that very) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Lord Ram) / प्रनत (the surrendered) / अनुरागी (loving) / भजहु (worship) / नाथ (O Lord) / ममता (attachment, possessiveness) / सब (all) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / मुनिबर (great sages) / जतनु (effort, practice) / करहिं (do) / जेहि (for whom) / लागी (for the sake of) / भूप (kings) / राजु (kingdom, rule) / तजि (giving up) / होहिं (become) / बिरागी (detached, renunciant)
ramacharitamanas::4524.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4524.essence: The one you seek comes closest when you stop clinging.
ramacharitamanas::4524.simple_meaning: Ram is reached by letting go of possessiveness. Sages strive for Him, and even kings renounce power to become detached.
ramacharitamanas::4524.simple_insight: Real closeness begins when you stop gripping what was never truly yours.
ramacharitamanas::4524.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned that the Lord he is facing is not won by pride or possession. The verse turns the scene into a teaching: sages labor for Him, kings give up power for Him, and He loves those who have already let go.
ramacharitamanas::4524.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping one message will settle your heart. But the ache only loosens when you stop clinging to control and make room for something deeper.
ramacharitamanas::4524.insight: It shifts devotion from bargaining to release, showing that attachment itself blocks nearness.

ramacharitamanas::4525.verse_sanskrit: सोइ कोसलाधीस रघुराया। आयउ करन तोहि पर दाया॥ जौं पिय मानहु मोर सिखावन। सुजसु होइ तिहुँ पुर अति पावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4525.verse_hindi: वही कोसलाधीश श्री रघुनाथजी आप पर दया करने आए हैं। हे प्रियतम! यदि आप मेरी सीख मान लेंगे, तो आपका अत्यंत पवित्र और सुंदर यश तीनों लोकों में फैल जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4525.english_translation: That Lord of Kosala, Raghu's king, has come to show you mercy. Dear one, if you accept my counsel, your pure fame will spread through all three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::4525.translation_literal: सोइ (that very) / कोसलाधीस (lord of Kosala) / रघुराया (king of Raghu) / आयउ (has come) / करन (to do) / तोहि (to you) / पर (upon) / दाया (mercy) ॥ / जौं (if) / पिय (dear one) / मानहु (you accept) / मोर (my) / सिखावन (counsel) / सुजसु (pure fame) / होइ (will become) / तिहुँ (three) / पुर (worlds) / अति (very) / पावन (pure, sacred) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4525.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4525.essence: Mercy is already here; your pride decides whether it becomes fame or ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4525.simple_meaning: Ram has come to show mercy, and Mandodari urges Ravana to accept her advice so his name can become pure and honored everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::4525.simple_insight: Even now, a wise warning can still turn ruin into grace.
ramacharitamanas::4525.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari speaks to Ravana after the war has turned against him. She points to Ram's mercy and pleads with her husband to listen before everything is lost. The verse is one urgent appeal inside a larger final warning.
ramacharitamanas::4525.modern_relevance: A friend calls you after a reckless decision and tells you there is still time to stop. The advice is uncomfortable, but accepting it could save your name and your future.
ramacharitamanas::4525.insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn pride to the possibility of repair through humility.

ramacharitamanas::4526.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि नयन नीर भरि गहि पद कंपित गात। नाथ भजहु रघुनाथहि अचल होइ अहिवात ॥
ramacharitamanas::4526.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर, नेत्रों में (करुणा का) जल भरकर और पति के चरण पकड़कर, काँपते हुए शरीर से मंदोदरी ने कहा- हे नाथ! श्री रघुनाथजी का भजन कीजिए, जिससे मेरा सुहाग अचल हो जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4526.english_translation: After saying this, with tears filling her eyes and clasping her husband's feet, her body trembling, Mandodari said: "O lord, worship Raghunath so that my married life may remain unbroken."
ramacharitamanas::4526.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying thus) / नयन (eyes) / नीर (water, tears) / भरि (filling) / गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / कंपित (trembling) / गात (body) / नाथ (lord) / भजहु (worship) / रघुनाथहि (Raghunath) / अचल (unbroken, steady) / होइ (may become) / अहिवात (married life, wifely bond)
ramacharitamanas::4526.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4526.essence: Devotion can become the last shelter when everything else is collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::4526.simple_meaning: Mandodari begs Ravana to worship Ram so her married life can remain secure. Her plea comes from fear, love, and a last hope for protection.
ramacharitamanas::4526.simple_insight: Even in danger, turning toward Ram is seen as the deepest protection.
ramacharitamanas::4526.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final hours, Mandodari stands before Ravana with tears and trembling hands. She is not arguing politics; she is pleading for the one refuge that can still save her marriage and her life. Her words expose Ravana’s refusal to listen.
ramacharitamanas::4526.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love double down on a choice that is clearly разрушing everything. In that moment, you stop negotiating and plead for the one change that could still hold the relationship together.
ramacharitamanas::4526.insight: It shifts the mind from control and pride toward humble refuge in Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4527.verse_sanskrit: तब रावन मयसुता उठाई। कहै लाग खल निज प्रभुताई॥ सुनु तैं प्रिया बृथा भय माना। जग जोधा को मोहि समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4527.verse_hindi: तब रावण ने मंदोदरी को उठाया और वह दुष्ट उससे अपनी प्रभुता कहने लगा- हे प्रिये! सुन, तूने व्यर्थ ही भय मान रखा है। बता तो जगत् में मेरे समान योद्धा है कौन? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4527.english_translation: Then Ravana lifted Mandodari and began boasting of his own power. "Listen, my dear, your fear is pointless. Tell me, who in the world is my equal as a warrior?"
ramacharitamanas::4527.translation_literal: तब (then) / रावन (Ravana) / मयसुता (Mandodari) / उठाई (lifted) / कहै लाग (began to say) / खल (wicked one) / निज (own) / प्रभुताई (power, lordship)॥ सुनु (listen) / तैं (you) / प्रिया (dear one) / बृथा (pointless, vain) / भय (fear) / माना (taken, held) / जग (world) / जोधा (warrior) / को (who) / मोहि (to me) / समाना (equal) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4527.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4527.essence: Pride makes a person dismiss the very warning meant to save them.
ramacharitamanas::4527.simple_meaning: Ravana comforts Mandodari by bragging about his own strength and saying no warrior in the world matches him.
ramacharitamanas::4527.simple_insight: Pride speaks loudest when fear is near.
ramacharitamanas::4527.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari has just warned Ravana that Ram is coming and that his pride is leading him toward ruin. Ravana answers by lifting her up and boasting of his unmatched power, turning her concern into proof of his arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4527.modern_relevance: You hear the warning in a partner's voice, but instead of listening, you start listing your achievements. That reflex to defend your ego can blind you to danger.
ramacharitamanas::4527.insight: It exposes how self-importance blocks clear seeing and turns warning into a threat to the ego.

ramacharitamanas::4528.verse_sanskrit: बरुन कुबेर पवन जम काला। भुज बल जितेउँ सकल दिगपाला॥ देव दनुज नर सब बस मोरें। कवन हेतु उपजा भय तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4528.verse_hindi: वरुण, कुबेर, पवन, यमराज आदि सभी दिक्पालों को तथा काल को भी मैंने अपनी भुजाओं के बल से जीत रखा है। देवता, दानव और मनुष्य सभी मेरे वश में हैं। फिर तुझको यह भय किस कारण उत्पन्न हो गया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4528.english_translation: Varuna, Kubera, the wind, Yama, and even Time have all been conquered by the strength of my arms. Gods, demons, and humans are all under my control. Then why has fear arisen in you?
ramacharitamanas::4528.translation_literal: बरुन (Varuna) / कुबेर (Kubera) / पवन (wind) / जम (Yama) / काला (Time) / भुज बल (strength of arms) / जितेउँ (I conquered) / सकल (all) / दिगपाला (guardians of the directions)॥ / देव (devas) / दनुज (demons) / नर (humans) / सब (all) / बस (under control) / मोरें (of mine) / कवन (which) / हेतु (reason) / उपजा (arisen) / भय (fear) / तोरें (in you) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4528.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4528.essence: Domination is hollow when fear still owns you.
ramacharitamanas::4528.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he has conquered all powers and beings, so Mandodari should not fear. His words reveal arrogance, not true strength.
ramacharitamanas::4528.simple_insight: Confidence built on domination still trembles from within.
ramacharitamanas::4528.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to silence Mandodari's fear with a boast. He claims victory over the guardians of the directions, gods, demons, humans, and even Time itself. The scene exposes how ego talks when it feels threatened.
ramacharitamanas::4528.modern_relevance: You have the title, the money, the team, and the reputation — yet one worried thought can still wreck your night. Ravana's speech sounds like control, but it is fear wearing armor.
ramacharitamanas::4528.insight: It shifts attention from outward dominance to the hidden insecurity that drives it.

ramacharitamanas::4529.verse_sanskrit: नाना बिधि तेहि कहेसि बुझाई। सभाँ बहोरि बैठ सो जाई॥ मंदोदरीं हृदयँ अस जाना। काल बस्य उपजा अभिमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4529.verse_hindi: मंदोदरी ने उसे बहुत तरह से समझाकर कहा (किन्तु रावण ने उसकी एक भी बात न सुनी) और वह फिर सभा में जाकर बैठ गया। मंदोदरी ने हृदय में ऐसा जान लिया कि काल के वश होने से पति को अभिमान हो गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4529.english_translation: Mandodari tried to explain to him in many ways, but he did not listen. He went back and sat in the assembly. Mandodari understood in her heart that, under time's grip, his pride had arisen.
ramacharitamanas::4529.translation_literal: नाना बिधि (in many ways) / तेहि (to him) / कहेसि (she said) / बुझाई (explaining) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / बहोरि (again) / बैठ (sat) / सो (he) / जाई (going) / मंदोदरीं (Mandodari) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अस (thus) / जाना (knew) / काल बस्य (under time's control) / उपजा (arose) / अभिमाना (pride)
ramacharitamanas::4529.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4529.essence: Pride grows fastest when time is already against you.
ramacharitamanas::4529.simple_meaning: Mandodari tries to warn Ravana, but he returns to the assembly unmoved. She sees that time has already fed his pride.
ramacharitamanas::4529.simple_insight: Pride can make you stop hearing the truth, even when it comes from someone who loves you.
ramacharitamanas::4529.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari pleads with Ravana to turn back from disaster. He ignores her and returns to the court. Watching him, she realises his arrogance has swollen under the pressure of time, and that he no longer sees clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4529.modern_relevance: Someone you love keeps brushing off every warning, laughing it off as if nothing can touch them. You can see the drift toward disaster long before they can.
ramacharitamanas::4529.insight: It shows how unchecked pride shuts down counsel and blinds a person to danger.

ramacharitamanas::4530.verse_sanskrit: सभाँ आइ मंत्रिन्ह तेहिं बूझा। करब कवन बिधि रिपु सैं जूझा॥ कहहिं सचिव सुनु निसिचर नाहा। बार बार प्रभु पूछहु काहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4530.verse_hindi: सभा में आकर उसने मंत्रियों से पूछा कि शत्रु के साथ किस प्रकार से युद्ध करना होगा? मंत्री कहने लगे- हे राक्षसों के नाथ! हे प्रभु! सुनिए, आप बार-बार क्या पूछते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4530.english_translation: Coming to the assembly, he asked his ministers how the enemy should be fought. The ministers said, 'Listen, lord of the demons, why do you keep asking again and again?'
ramacharitamanas::4530.translation_literal: सभाँ (in the assembly) / आइ (coming) / मंत्रिन्ह (from the ministers) / तेहिं (he) / बूझा (asked) / करब (to do) / कवन बिधि (which way) / रिपु (enemy) / सैं (with) / जूझा (to fight)॥ / कहहिं (they say) / सचिव (ministers) / सुनु (listen) / निसिचर नाहा (lord of demons) / बार बार (again and again) / प्रभु (lord) / पूछहु (you ask) / काहा (why)॥
ramacharitamanas::4530.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4530.essence: Pride asks for strategy after it has already refused wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4530.simple_meaning: Ravana asks his ministers how to fight the enemy, but they answer with impatience, as if he is asking the obvious.
ramacharitamanas::4530.simple_insight: Pride keeps asking for guidance even after it has already decided not to listen.
ramacharitamanas::4530.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana returns to his council after ignoring Mandodari's warning. He asks his ministers how to fight Ram, but their response shows the mood of the court: they are still trapped in Ravana's arrogance and cannot give him a path that will save him.
ramacharitamanas::4530.modern_relevance: You call a meeting after ignoring every warning, then ask for advice as if the answer were still missing. The room already knows the real problem: you won't listen.
ramacharitamanas::4530.insight: It exposes how ego keeps seeking confirmation instead of correction.

ramacharitamanas::4531.verse_sanskrit: कहहु कवन भय करिअ बिचारा। नर कपि भालु अहार हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4531.verse_hindi: कहिए तो (ऐसा) कौन-सा बड़ा भय है, जिसका विचार किया जाए? (भय की बात ही क्या है?) मनुष्य और वानर-भालू तो हमारे भोजन (की सामग्री) हैं॥
ramacharitamanas::4531.english_translation: Tell me, what fear should be considered? Human beings, monkeys, and bears are our food.
ramacharitamanas::4531.translation_literal: कहहु (tell me) / कवन (which) / भय (fear) / करिअ (should be considered) / बिचारा (thought over) / नर (humans) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / अहार (food) / हमारा (our)
ramacharitamanas::4531.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4531.essence: Arrogance makes real danger look laughably small.
ramacharitamanas::4531.simple_meaning: Ravana dismisses the danger, saying there is no reason to fear because humans, monkeys, and bears are his prey.
ramacharitamanas::4531.simple_insight: Overconfidence can make real danger look ridiculous right before it strikes.
ramacharitamanas::4531.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already ignored Mandodari and now questions his ministers about war. Instead of taking Rama's army seriously, he boasts that monkeys and bears are only food to him. The line exposes his arrogance before the coming collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4531.modern_relevance: A manager laughs off a small competitor, calling them irrelevant, then loses the market because he never took them seriously.
ramacharitamanas::4531.insight: It shows how pride blinds judgment and turns caution into mockery.

ramacharitamanas::4532.verse_sanskrit: सब के बचन श्रवन सुनि कह प्रहस्त कर जोरि। नीति बिरोध न करिअ प्रभु मंत्रिन्ह मति अति थोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4532.verse_hindi: कानों से सबके वचन सुनकर (रावण का पुत्र) प्रहस्त हाथ जोड़कर कहने लगा- हे प्रभु! नीति के विरुद्ध कुछ भी नहीं करना चाहिए, मन्त्रियों में बहुत ही थोड़ी बुद्धि है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4532.english_translation: Hearing everyone's words, Prahasta joined his hands and said, "Lord, do not act against policy; your ministers have very little wisdom."
ramacharitamanas::4532.translation_literal: सब (all) / के (of the) / बचन (words) / श्रवन (ears, hearing) / सुनि (having heard) / कह (said) / प्रहस्त (Prahasta) / कर (hands) / जोरि (joining) / नीति (policy, right conduct) / बिरोध (against) / न (not) / करिअ (should be done) / प्रभु (Lord) / मंत्रिन्ह (ministers) / मति (wisdom, judgment) / अति (very) / थोरि (little)
ramacharitamanas::4532.speaker: Prahasta
ramacharitamanas::4532.essence: Rash power still needs wise restraint.
ramacharitamanas::4532.simple_meaning: Prahasta warns Ravana not to ignore good judgment. He says the ministers are foolish, but the larger point is that rash action against right conduct is dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::4532.simple_insight: Not every confident voice is wise. You still need to check whether a decision is against good sense.
ramacharitamanas::4532.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, after boastful talk about the coming war, Prahasta steps forward with folded hands. He tries to restrain his king from reckless action, saying that policy should not be violated and the ministers' judgment is shallow. The verse shows warning inside a court already leaning toward pride.
ramacharitamanas::4532.modern_relevance: A group chat is cheering a risky plan, and one person finally says, "Hold on — this is not smart." That pause can save everyone from a mistake.
ramacharitamanas::4532.insight: It shifts the mind from crowd confidence to sober judgment before action.

ramacharitamanas::4533.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं सचिव सठ ठकुर सोहाती। नाथ न पूर आव एहि भाँती॥ बारिधि नाघि एक कपि आवा। तासु चरित मन महुँ सबु गावा॥ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4533.verse_hindi: ये सभी मूर्ख (खुशामदी) मन्त्र ठकुरसुहाती (मुँहदेखी) कह रहे हैं। हे नाथ! इस प्रकार की बातों से पूरा नहीं पड़ेगा। एक ही बंदर समुद्र लाँघकर आया था। उसका चरित्र सब लोग अब भी मन-ही-मन गाया करते हैं (स्मरण किया करते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4533.english_translation: These flattering ministers are speaking like fools. Lord, this kind of talk will not fill the need. One monkey crossed the ocean, and everyone still remembers his story in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::4533.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / सचिव (ministers) / सठ (fools) / ठकुर सोहाती (courtly flattery) / नाथ (lord) / न पूर (will not suffice) / आव (come) / एहि भाँती (in this manner)॥ / बारिधि (ocean) / नाघि (crossing) / एक (one) / कपि (monkey) / आवा (came) / तासु (his) / चरित (story/character) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / सबु (everyone) / गावा (sings/remembers)॥
ramacharitamanas::4533.speaker: Ravana's ministers
ramacharitamanas::4533.simple_meaning: Empty praise is useless here. What matters is the example of Hanuman, whose crossing of the ocean is still remembered.
ramacharitamanas::4533.simple_insight: You feel the difference between words that flatter power and actions that actually change what is possible.
ramacharitamanas::4533.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's ministers try to soothe him with polished talk, but their words cannot solve the crisis. They point to Hanuman, the lone monkey who crossed the ocean, as the real measure of strength and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4533.modern_relevance: A room full of advisors nods politely while the problem keeps growing. Then one person points to the only thing that actually worked, and the whole mood changes.
ramacharitamanas::4533.insight: It shifts attention from flattering speech to proven action and memorable service.

ramacharitamanas::4534.verse_sanskrit: छुधा न रही तुम्हहि तब काहू। जारत नगरु कस न धरि खाहू॥ सुनत नीक आगें दुख पावा। सचिवन अस मत प्रभुहि सुनावा॥ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4534.verse_hindi: उस समय तुम लोगों में से किसी को भूख न थी? (बंदर तो तुम्हारा भोजन ही हैं, फिर) नगर जलाते समय उसे पकड़कर क्यों नहीं खा लिया? इन मन्त्रियों ने स्वामी (आप) को ऐसी सम्मति सुनायी है जो सुनने में अच्छी है पर जिससे आगे चलकर दुःख पाना होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4534.english_translation: Weren't you all hungry then? Why didn't you catch and eat him when he was burning the city? The ministers gave their lord advice that sounded pleasant but would bring sorrow later.
ramacharitamanas::4534.translation_literal: छुधा (hunger) / न रही (did not remain) / तुम्हहि (for you all) / तब (then) / काहू (for anyone) / जारत (burning) / नगरु (the city) / कस (why) / न (not) / धरि (having caught) / खाहू (would eat) / सुनत (hearing) / नीक (pleasant) / आगें (later / ahead) / दुख (sorrow) / पावा (was obtained) / सचिवन (by the ministers) / अस (such) / मत (advice) / प्रभुहि (to the lord) / सुनावा (was spoken)
ramacharitamanas::4534.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4534.essence: Pleasant advice can be the first step toward suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4534.simple_meaning: The speaker mocks the ministers: if the monkeys were so hungry, why didn't they catch and eat Hanuman while he burned the city? Pleasant advice can still lead to later suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4534.simple_insight: Flattering advice can feel safe now and still ruin you later.
ramacharitamanas::4534.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war council, Ravana's side is scrambling to justify itself after Hanuman's fiery raid. A sharp voice ridicules the ministers' soft counsel, exposing how pleasing words can hide disaster. The verse is a bite in the middle of a larger argument.
ramacharitamanas::4534.modern_relevance: A friend says, 'Just say yes, keep the peace.' It sounds kind in the moment, but you know it will cost you later.
ramacharitamanas::4534.insight: It warns you to test advice by consequence, not by how soothing it sounds.

ramacharitamanas::4535.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं बारीस बँधायउ हेला। उतरेउ सेन समेत सुबेला॥ सो भनु मनुज खाब हम भाई। बचन कहहिं सब गाल फुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4535.verse_hindi: जिसने खेल-ही-खेल में समुद्र बँधा लिया और जो सेना सहित सुबेल पर्वत पर आ उतरा है। हे भाई! कहो वह मनुष्य है, जिसे कहते हो कि हम खा लेंगे? सब गाल फुला-फुलाकर (पागलों की तरह) वचन कह रहे हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4535.english_translation: He who, in play, bound the ocean and then descended with an army at Suvela—brother, is that the man you say we can eat? They speak with puffed cheeks like fools.
ramacharitamanas::4535.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / बारीस (the ocean) / बँधायउ (was bound) / हेला (in play) / उतरेउ (descended) / सेन (with an army) / समेत (together) / सुबेला (Suvela mountain) / सो (that) / भनु (say) / मनुज (man) / खाब (to eat) / हम (we) / भाई (brother) / बचन (words) / कहहिं (they speak) / सब (all) / गाल (cheeks) / फुलाई (puffed up)
ramacharitamanas::4535.speaker: Ravana's warriors
ramacharitamanas::4535.essence: You cannot reduce great power to a joke.
ramacharitamanas::4535.simple_meaning: Ravana's side is mocking the idea that Hanuman can be eaten. They point out that someone who bound the ocean and arrived with an army is no ordinary man.
ramacharitamanas::4535.simple_insight: Arrogance collapses when it meets a force it cannot name.
ramacharitamanas::4535.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's followers are arguing after Hanuman's arrival. They try to dismiss him as food, but another voice cuts through their bluster: the one who crossed the ocean and came down at Suvela cannot be treated like an ordinary captive.
ramacharitamanas::4535.modern_relevance: You laugh at the quiet newcomer in the room, then realize they already handled the thing everyone else feared. Mockery fades fast when reality walks in.
ramacharitamanas::4535.insight: It shifts the mind from contempt to recognition of true strength.

ramacharitamanas::4536.verse_sanskrit: तात बचन मम सुनु अति आदर। जनि मन गुनहु मोहि करि कादर। प्रिय बानी जे सुनहिं जे कहहीं। ऐसे नर निकाय जग अहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4536.verse_hindi: हे तात! मेरे वचनों को बहुत आदर से (बड़े गौर से) सुनिए। मुझे मन में कायर न समझ लीजिएगा। जगत् में ऐसे मनुष्य झुंड-के-झुंड (बहुत अधिक) हैं, जो प्यारी (मुँह पर मीठी लगने वाली) बात ही सुनते और कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4536.english_translation: My dear father, listen to my words with great respect. Do not think of me as a coward in your mind. In this world, people are many who only hear and speak pleasant words.
ramacharitamanas::4536.translation_literal: तात (father) / बचन (words) / मम (my) / सुनु (listen) / अति आदर (great respect) / जनि (do not) / मन (in mind) / गुनहु (consider) / मोहि (me) / करि (as) / कादर (coward) / प्रिय बानी (pleasant speech) / जे (those who) / सुनहिं (hear) / जे (those who) / कहहीं (speak) / ऐसे (such) / नर (people) / निकाय (many) / जग (world) / अहहीं (are)
ramacharitamanas::4536.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4536.essence: Pleasant words are common; truthful ones are rare.
