ramacharitamanas::4536.simple_meaning: Ravana asks his father to hear him respectfully and not judge him as weak. He says most people only like sweet words and repeat them.
ramacharitamanas::4536.simple_insight: Not every gentle voice is honest, and not every hard truth is cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::4536.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is defending himself before his father after boasting about his power. He asks for respect, rejects the label of cowardice, and points out that most people prefer flattering speech. The next verse sharpens the lesson: hard truth is rare.
ramacharitamanas::4536.modern_relevance: You finally say what needs saying in a family argument, and everyone wants the softer version. Ravana is naming that reflex: people often prefer pleasant words over useful ones.
ramacharitamanas::4536.insight: It trains you to value honest speech over approval-seeking language.

ramacharitamanas::4537.verse_sanskrit: बचन परम हित सुनत कठोरे। सुनहिं जे कहहिं ते नर प्रभु थोरे॥ प्रथम बसीठ पठउ सुनु नीती। सीता देइ करहु पुनि प्रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4537.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! सुनने में कठोर परन्तु (परिणाम में) परम हितकारी वचन जो सुनते और कहतेहैं,वे मनुष्य बहुत ही थोड़े हैं। नीति सुनिये, (उसके अनुसार) पहले दूत भेजिये, और (फिर) सीता को देकर श्रीरामजी से प्रीति (मेल) कर लीजिये ॥
ramacharitamanas::4537.english_translation: Words that are harsh to hear but deeply beneficial are heard and spoken by very few. Follow policy: first send an envoy, then give Sita and make peace with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4537.translation_literal: बचन (words) / परम (supreme) / हित (beneficial) / सुनत (while hearing) / कठोरे (harsh) / सुनहिं (they hear) / जे (those who) / कहहिं (speak) / ते (those) / नर (people) / प्रभु (lord) / थोरे (few)॥ / प्रथम (first) / बसीठ (envoy) / पठउ (send) / सुनु (listen) / नीती (policy) / सीता (Sita) / देइ (giving) / करहु (do) / पुनि (again) / प्रीती (peace/friendship)॥
ramacharitamanas::4537.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4537.essence: The hardest advice is often the one that saves you.
ramacharitamanas::4537.simple_meaning: Few people can hear and speak words that sting at first but help in the end. The advice here is practical: send a messenger first, then make peace by returning Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4537.simple_insight: Real wisdom is often uncomfortable before it becomes helpful.
ramacharitamanas::4537.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's council is weighing how to respond to Ram. The speaker urges a cautious, diplomatic path: hear hard advice, send an envoy first, and avoid a war that can still be prevented by returning Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4537.modern_relevance: A tense family group chat is spiraling, and the one message that could calm everything feels hardest to send. The verse values the advice that stings before it saves you from a bigger mess.
ramacharitamanas::4537.insight: It shifts you from pride-driven reaction to strategic restraint and reconciliation.

ramacharitamanas::4538.verse_sanskrit: नारि पाइ फिरि जाहिं जौं तौ न बढ़ाइअ रारि। नाहिं त सन्मुख समर महि तात करिअ हठि मारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4538.verse_hindi: यदि वे स्त्री पाकर लौट जाएँ, तब तो (व्यर्थ) झगड़ा न बढ़ाइये। नहीं तो (यदि न फिरें तो) हे तात! सम्मुख युद्धभूमि में उनसे हठपूर्वक (डटकर) मार-काट कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4538.english_translation: If they return after finding the woman, do not prolong the quarrel. Otherwise, father, face them in open battle and strike them down with resolve.
ramacharitamanas::4538.translation_literal: नारि (the woman) / पाइ (having found) / फिरि (back) / जाहिं (they go) / जौं (if) / तौ (then) / न (not) / बढ़ाइअ (prolong) / रारि (quarrel) / नाहिं (otherwise) / त सन्मुख (in front) / समर (battle) / महि (on the field) / तात (father) / करिअ (do) / हठि (with resolve) / मारि (striking)
ramacharitamanas::4538.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4538.essence: Stop the quarrel if the goal is met; fight only when conflict is unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::4538.simple_meaning: If the enemy leaves after finding Sita, do not drag out the fight. If they refuse, meet them head-on and fight firmly.
ramacharitamanas::4538.simple_insight: Not every conflict needs escalation; some moments call for restraint, others for decisive force.
ramacharitamanas::4538.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a strategic voice is advising Ravana on how to handle the search for Sita and the coming war. The counsel is practical: avoid needless escalation if the goal is already achieved, but fight without hesitation if battle becomes unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::4538.modern_relevance: A tense family argument is heading toward a blowup. One part of you wants to keep proving a point; another knows when to stop. This verse is about knowing the difference.
ramacharitamanas::4538.insight: It teaches you to separate unnecessary conflict from necessary action, and to respond accordingly.

ramacharitamanas::4539.verse_sanskrit: यह मत जौं मानहु प्रभु मोरा। उभय प्रकार सुजसु जग तोरा॥ सुत सन कह दसकंठ रिसाई। असि मति सठ केहिं तोहि सिखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4539.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! यदि आप मेरी यह सम्मति मानेंगे, तो जगत् में दोनों ही प्रकार से आपका सुयश होगा। रावण ने गुस्से में भरकर पुत्र से कहा- अरे मूर्ख! तुझे ऐसी बुद्धि किसने सिखायी? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4539.english_translation: “If you accept my advice, your fame will spread in both ways. Ravana, furious, said to his son, ‘Fool, who taught you such thinking?’”
ramacharitamanas::4539.translation_literal: यह (this) / मत (advice) / जौं (if) / मानहु (you accept) / प्रभु (lord) / मोरा (my) / उभय (both) / प्रकार (kinds) / सुजसु (good fame) / जग (world) / तोरा (your)॥ सुत (son) / सन (to) / कह (said) / दसकंठ (ten-necked one, Ravana) / रिसाई (in anger) / असि (such) / मति (wisdom) / सठ (fool) / केहिं (by whom) / तोहि (you) / सिखाई (taught)
ramacharitamanas::4539.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4539.essence: Pride hears counsel as an insult.
ramacharitamanas::4539.simple_meaning: Ravana urges his son to accept his advice, claiming it will protect his reputation either way. Then he angrily insults his son for disagreeing.
ramacharitamanas::4539.simple_insight: Pride cannot hear counsel; it turns advice into insult.
ramacharitamanas::4539.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still trying to force a path that preserves his pride. He tells his son that his plan will bring him fame either way, but the son’s resistance only makes Ravana furious. This is the moment his ego hardens into abuse.
ramacharitamanas::4539.modern_relevance: You offer careful feedback in a tense family argument, and the other person hears only disrespect. The real issue is no longer the advice — it is wounded pride.
ramacharitamanas::4539.insight: It shows how ego converts guidance into threat and shuts down listening.

ramacharitamanas::4540.verse_sanskrit: अबहीं ते उर संसय होई। बेनुमूल सुत भयहु घमोई॥ सुनि पितु गिरा परुष अति घोरा। चला भवन कहि बचन कठोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4540.verse_hindi: अभी से हृदय में सन्देह (भय) हो रहा है? हे पुत्र! तू तो बाँस की जड़ में घमोई हुआ (तू मेरे वंश के अनुकूल या अनुरूप नहीं हुआ)। पिता की अत्यन्त घोर और कठोर वाणी सुनकर प्रहस्त ये कड़े वचन कहता हुआ घर को चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4540.english_translation: Is doubt already rising in your heart? O son, you are not fitting the line of bamboo. Hearing his father's harsh, terrible words, Prahasta left for his house, speaking hard words.
ramacharitamanas::4540.translation_literal: अबहीं (already now) / ते (from) / उर (heart) / संसय (doubt) / होई (is happening) । बेनुमूल (bamboo-root) / सुत (son) / भयहु (you became) / घमोई (crooked / not fitting) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / पितु (father's) / गिरा (speech) / परुष (harsh) / अति (very) / घोरा (terrible) । चला (went) / भवन (home) / कहि (saying) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (hard) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4540.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4540.essence: Pride makes even guidance feel like rejection.
ramacharitamanas::4540.simple_meaning: A father rebukes his son so harshly that the son leaves in anger and hurt. The verse shows a family split by pride and cutting words.
ramacharitamanas::4540.simple_insight: Harsh words can wound more deeply than the argument itself.
ramacharitamanas::4540.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Prahasta is being judged by his own father in the middle of Ravana's courtly war council. The insult lands as rejection, not guidance, and he walks away seething. This is a character beat, not the passage's main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4540.modern_relevance: A parent says one sharp sentence at the dinner table, and the room goes cold. No one throws a plate, but the damage is already done.
ramacharitamanas::4540.insight: It highlights how criticism without care turns advice into resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4541.verse_sanskrit: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4541.verse_hindi: हित की सलाह आपको कैसे नहीं लगती (आप पर कैसे असर नहीं करती), जैसे मृत्यु के वश हुए (रोगी) को दवा नहीं लगती। संध्या का समय जानकर रावण अपनी बीसों भुजाओं को देखता हुआ महल को चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4541.english_translation: Why does good advice not affect you, like medicine does not help a person already seized by death? Knowing it was evening, Ravana went home, looking at his twenty arms.
ramacharitamanas::4541.translation_literal: हित (benefit / good counsel) / मत (advice) / तोहि (to you) / न (not) / लागत (applies, affects) / कैसें (how) / काल (death) / बिबस (under the control of) / कहुँ (to one) / भेषज (medicine) / जैसें (like)॥ / संध्या (evening / dusk) / समय (time) / जानि (knowing) / दससीसा (Ravana, ten-headed one) / भवन (to the house / palace) / चलेउ (went) / निरखत (looking at) / भुज (arms) / बीसा (twenty)॥
ramacharitamanas::4541.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4541.essence: Pride makes even life-saving counsel useless.
ramacharitamanas::4541.simple_meaning: Ravana is beyond advice, like a dying patient beyond medicine. He heads home at dusk, still admiring his twenty arms.
ramacharitamanas::4541.simple_insight: Pride can make even good counsel bounce off untouched.
ramacharitamanas::4541.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana ignores wise counsel from his own side. The narrator compares him to someone beyond medicine, then shows him walking home at dusk, still absorbed in his own strength. The scene exposes how ego blocks correction.
ramacharitamanas::4541.modern_relevance: Someone keeps brushing off every warning, even after the third friend, the doctor, and the email all say the same thing. Pride makes the message feel optional.
ramacharitamanas::4541.insight: It shifts attention from the advice itself to the ego that refuses to receive it.

ramacharitamanas::4542.verse_sanskrit: लंका सिखर उपर आगारा। अति बिचित्र तहँ होइ अखारा॥ बैठ जाइ तेहिं मंदिर रावन। लागे किंनर गुन गन गावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4542.verse_hindi: लंका की चोटी पर एक अत्यन्त विचित्र महल था। वहाँ नाच-गान का अखाड़ा जमता था। रावण उस महल में जाकर बैठ गया। किन्नर उसके गुण समूहों को गाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4542.english_translation: Atop Lanka's peak stood a wondrous hall. There the arena of music and dance was held. Ravana sat in that palace, and the celestial singers praised his qualities.
ramacharitamanas::4542.translation_literal: लंका (Lanka) / सिखर (peak) / उपर (on top) / आगारा (mansion, hall) / अति (very) / बिचित्र (wondrous, strange) / तहँ (there) / होइ (was held) / अखारा (arena, stage) / बैठ जाइ (having sat down) / तेहिं (in that) / मंदिर (palace) / रावन (Ravana) / लागे (began) / किंनर (celestial singers) / गुन (qualities) / गन (groups, heaps) / गावन (to sing)
ramacharitamanas::4542.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4542.essence: Ravana's grandeur is already hollow with self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::4542.simple_meaning: Ravana sits in a magnificent palace on Lanka's peak, where celestial singers praise him and music fills the hall.
ramacharitamanas::4542.simple_insight: Pride can turn even praise into a stage for the ego.
ramacharitamanas::4542.detailed_meaning: As the battle in Lanka unfolds, the scene pauses inside Ravana's own palace. He sits surrounded by luxury, music, and praise from celestial singers. The verse shows the atmosphere of his court before the collapse of his power.
ramacharitamanas::4542.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is flattering the most powerful person there. The applause sounds grand, but you can already feel how fragile it is.
ramacharitamanas::4542.insight: It shifts attention from outer splendor to the ego that feeds on it.

ramacharitamanas::4543.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं ताल पखाउज बीना। नृत्य करहिं अपछरा प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4543.verse_hindi: ताल (करताल), पखावज (मृदंग) और बीणा बज रहे हैं। नृत्य में प्रवीण अप्सराएँ नाच रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4543.english_translation: Cymbals, drums, and veenas are sounding, and skilled celestial dancers are performing.
ramacharitamanas::4543.translation_literal: बाजहिं (are sounding) / ताल (cymbals) / पखाउज (drum) / बीना (veena) / नृत्य (dance) / करहिं (do) / अपछरा (celestial dancers) / प्रबीना (skilled)
ramacharitamanas::4543.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4543.essence: Luxury can keep dancing while ruin waits overhead.
ramacharitamanas::4543.simple_meaning: The verse describes the music and dancing happening in Ravana's palace. It is a scene-setting detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4543.simple_insight: Sometimes a glittering atmosphere is just decoration around a deeper collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4543.detailed_meaning: Ravana has returned to his palace on Lanka's peak, still surrounded by luxury and performance while Rama's pressure closes in. The music and dancing continue, showing how completely he is lost in pleasure even as danger stands above him.
ramacharitamanas::4543.modern_relevance: You walk into a party where the lights are perfect and everyone is laughing, but the room feels strangely hollow. The celebration is real; so is the warning underneath it.
ramacharitamanas::4543.insight: It shows how pleasure can keep going even when danger is already at the door.

ramacharitamanas::4544.verse_sanskrit: सुनासीर सत सरिस सो संतत करइ बिलास। परम प्रबल रिपु सीस पर तद्यपि सोच न त्रास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4544.verse_hindi: वह निरन्तर सैकड़ों इन्द्रों के समान भोग-विलास करता रहता है। यद्यपि (श्रीरामजी-सरीखा) अत्यन्त प्रबल शत्रु सिर पर है, फिर भी उसको न तो चिन्ता है और न डर ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4544.english_translation: He keeps enjoying pleasures like a hundred Indras, yet a far stronger enemy stands over his head, and still he feels neither worry nor fear.
ramacharitamanas::4544.translation_literal: सुनासीर (Indra) / सत (hundreds) / सरिस (like) / सो (that one) / संतत (continuously) / करइ (does) / बिलास (pleasure, enjoyment) / परम (extremely) / प्रबल (powerful) / रिपु (enemy) / सीस (head) / पर (upon) / तद्यपि (even so) / सोच (worry) / न (not) / त्रास (fear)
ramacharitamanas::4544.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4544.essence: Luxury can blind you to the danger already at your door.
ramacharitamanas::4544.simple_meaning: Ravana is still lost in luxury even though Ram, his greatest enemy, is closing in. He feels no fear or concern at all.
ramacharitamanas::4544.simple_insight: Unchecked pleasure can make danger invisible until it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4544.detailed_meaning: Inside Lanka, Ravana sits amid music, dance, and luxury while the war is already at his door. Tulsidas shows the blindness of pride: even with Ram rising against him, Ravana remains unshaken, unaware that destruction is near.
ramacharitamanas::4544.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling, shopping, or partying while the deadline, the diagnosis, or the hard conversation waits outside the door. Distraction can feel like power right up to the moment it collapses.
ramacharitamanas::4544.insight: It warns you to notice when comfort is covering denial.

ramacharitamanas::4545.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ सुबेल सैल रघुबीरा। उतरे सेन सहित अति भीरा॥ सिखर एक उतंग अति देखी। परम रम्य सम सुभ्र बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4545.verse_hindi: यहाँ श्री रघुवीर सुबेल पर्वत पर सेना की बड़ी भीड़ (बड़े समूह) के साथ उतरे। पर्वत का एक बहुत ऊँचा, परम रमणीय, समतल और विशेष रूप से उज्ज्वल शिखर देखकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4545.english_translation: Here, on Mount Suvel, Raghubir descended with a great crowd of his army. Seeing one very high summit, wonderfully beautiful, level, and especially bright—
ramacharitamanas::4545.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / सुबेल सैल (Suvel mountain) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir, Ram) / उतरे (descended) / सेन सहित (with the army) / अति भीरा (very crowded) ॥ / सिखर (summit) / एक (one) / उतंग (high) / अति (very) / देखी (seeing) / परम (supremely) / रम्य (beautiful) / सम (level) / सुभ्र (bright/white) / बिसेषी (especially) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4545.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4545.essence: A single fitting place can shape everything that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4545.simple_meaning: Ram arrives at Mount Suvel with his army and notices a high, beautiful, level, bright summit.
ramacharitamanas::4545.simple_insight: Sometimes the next step begins with simply noticing the right place to stand.
ramacharitamanas::4545.detailed_meaning: Ram has reached Mount Suvel with a large army during the war in Lanka. Before any action begins, the scene pauses on the mountain itself: a bright, level summit catches attention, setting up the place where the army will rest and prepare.
ramacharitamanas::4545.modern_relevance: You arrive at a crowded hillside before a long day’s work, scanning for the one flat spot where everyone can gather and breathe.
ramacharitamanas::4545.insight: It shifts attention from movement to location, showing that even a war depends on choosing the right ground.

ramacharitamanas::4546.verse_sanskrit: तहँ तरु किसलय सुमन सुहाए। लछिमन रचि निज हाथ डसाए॥ ता पर रुचिर मृदुल मृगछाला। तेहिं आसन आसीन कृपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4546.verse_hindi: वहाँ लक्ष्मणजी ने वृक्षों के कोमल पत्ते और सुंदर फूल अपने हाथों से सजाकर बिछा दिए। उस पर सुंदर और कोमल मृग छाला बिछा दी। उसी आसन पर कृपालु श्री रामजी विराजमान थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4546.english_translation: There Lakshman arranged tender leaves and lovely flowers with his own hands. On top of that he spread a soft, beautiful deerskin. The compassionate Ram sat on that seat.
ramacharitamanas::4546.translation_literal: तहँ (there) / तरु (tree) / किसलय (tender leaves) / सुमन (flowers) / सुहाए (beautiful) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / रचि (arranging) / निज (own) / हाथ (hands) / डसाए (spread out) ॥ / ता पर (on that) / रुचिर (lovely) / मृदुल (soft) / मृगछाला (deerskin) / तेहिं (that) / आसन (seat) / आसीन (seated) / कृपाला (the compassionate one)
ramacharitamanas::4546.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4546.essence: A humble seat becomes royal when love prepares it.
ramacharitamanas::4546.simple_meaning: Lakshman prepares a simple, beautiful seat for Ram using leaves, flowers, and deerskin. Ram sits there quietly, showing ease with a humble life in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::4546.simple_insight: Care is shown in small acts, and dignity does not depend on luxury.
ramacharitamanas::4546.detailed_meaning: On Suvel mountain during the war, Ram has not entered a palace but a forest camp. Lakshman lovingly arranges a seat from leaves, flowers, and deerskin. The scene shows their shared simplicity before the battle continues.
ramacharitamanas::4546.modern_relevance: You clean a spare room with care before a guest arrives, though nothing about the visit is grand. The welcome itself becomes the gift.
ramacharitamanas::4546.insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that devotion is expressed through thoughtful preparation.

ramacharitamanas::4547.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु कृत सीस कपीस उछंगा। बाम दहिन दिसि चाप निषंगा दुहुँ कर कमल सुधारत बाना। कह लंकेस मंत्र लगि काना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4547.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामजी वानरराज सुग्रीव की गोद में अपना सिर रखे हैं। उनकी बायीं ओर धनुष तथा दाहिनी ओर तरकस (रखा) है। वे अपने दोनों करकमलों से बाण सुधार रहे हैं। विभीषणजी कानों से लगकर सलाह कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4547.english_translation: Lord Ram rests his head in Sugriva's lap. His bow is on the left and his quiver on the right. With both lotus hands he readies his arrows, while Vibhishana speaks counsel into his ear.
ramacharitamanas::4547.translation_literal: प्रभु (lord) / कृत (placed) / सीस (head) / कपीस (of the monkey-king) / उछंगा (lap) / बाम (left) / दहिन (right) / दिसि (side) / चाप (bow) / निषंगा (quiver) / दुहुँ (both) / कर (hands) / कमल (lotus) / सुधारत (adjusting/readying) / बाना (arrows) / कह (speaks) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / मंत्र (counsel) / लगि (near) / काना (ear)
ramacharitamanas::4547.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4547.essence: Readiness can be calm when trust holds the circle around you.
ramacharitamanas::4547.simple_meaning: Ram sits calmly among his allies, ready for battle, while Vibhishana offers advice. The scene shows trust, preparation, and shared purpose before the final fight.
ramacharitamanas::4547.simple_insight: You do not have to face hard moments alone; steady allies can hold you while you prepare.
ramacharitamanas::4547.detailed_meaning: On Suvela mountain, the war camp is settled into a moment of quiet readiness. Ram rests in Sugriva's lap, Lakshman has arranged his seat, and Vibhishana leans in with counsel. The verse shows the battle's still center before action resumes.
ramacharitamanas::4547.modern_relevance: After a brutal day, you sit on the edge of a couch while a friend quietly helps you think straight. The next step is still hard, but you are no longer carrying it alone.
ramacharitamanas::4547.insight: It shifts the mind from solitary strain to supported readiness.

ramacharitamanas::4548.verse_sanskrit: बड़भागी अंगद हनुमाना। चरन कमल चापत बिधि नाना॥ प्रभु पाछें लछिमन बीरासन। कटि निषंग कर बान सरासन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4548.verse_hindi: परम भाग्यशाली अंगद और हनुमान अनेकों प्रकार से प्रभु के चरण कमलों को दबा रहे हैं। लक्ष्मणजी कमर में तरकस कसे और हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए वीरासन से प्रभु के पीछे सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4548.english_translation: Angada and Hanuman, greatly blessed, massage the lotus feet of the Lord in many ways. Behind the Lord stands Lakshmana in a warrior’s stance, with quiver at his waist and bow and arrows in hand.
ramacharitamanas::4548.translation_literal: बड़भागी (greatly blessed) / अंगद (Angada) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / चरन कमल (lotus feet) / चापत (pressing/massaging) / बिधि नाना (in many ways) ॥ प्रभु (the Lord) / पाछें (behind) / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / बीरासन (warrior’s stance) / कटि (at the waist) / निषंग (quiver) / कर (in hand) / बान (arrows) / सरासन (bow and arrows) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4548.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4548.essence: Love near the beloved becomes service and protection.
ramacharitamanas::4548.simple_meaning: Angada and Hanuman serve Ram by massaging his feet, while Lakshmana stands behind him armed and ready.
ramacharitamanas::4548.simple_insight: True closeness shows itself as service, vigilance, and readiness, all at once.
ramacharitamanas::4548.detailed_meaning: In the war camp at Lanka, Ram rests after the strain of battle. Angada and Hanuman attend him with devoted service, while Lakshmana stands guard behind him, fully armed. The scene shows Ram surrounded by loving protection, not isolated power.
ramacharitamanas::4548.modern_relevance: You’re exhausted after a hard day, and the people who love you quietly handle the small things, stay alert, and keep watch without asking for credit.
ramacharitamanas::4548.insight: It shifts attention from status to service: devotion is shown by what you do around someone, not what you say about them.

ramacharitamanas::4549.verse_sanskrit: ऐहि बिधि कृपा रूप गुन धाम रामु आसीन। धन्य ते नर एहिं ध्यान जे रहत सदा लयलीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4549.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार कृपा, रूप (सौंदर्य) और गुणों के धाम श्री रामजी विराजमान हैं। वे मनुष्य धन्य हैं, जो सदा इस ध्यान में लौ लगाए रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4549.english_translation: In this way, Ram, the abode of grace, beauty, and virtue, sits there. Blessed are those people who remain forever absorbed in this meditation.
ramacharitamanas::4549.translation_literal: ऐहि बिधि (in this way) / कृपा रूप गुन धाम (abode of grace, beauty, and virtues) / रामु (Ram) / आसीन (seated) / धन्य (blessed) / ते (those) / नर (people) / एहिं (this) / ध्यान (meditation) / जे (who) / रहत (remain) / सदा (always) / लयलीन (absorbed)
ramacharitamanas::4549.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4549.essence: Ram's presence makes steady remembrance feel like a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::4549.simple_meaning: Ram sits there as the source of grace, beauty, and good qualities. People are blessed when they keep their mind steadily fixed on him.
ramacharitamanas::4549.simple_insight: There is quiet dignity in resting the mind on what is noble and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::4549.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the long search and the gathering for war, Ram sits surrounded by Sugriva, Hanuman, Lakshman, and the others. Tulsidas pauses the action to show why Ram is worthy of constant remembrance: his presence itself draws the mind into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4549.modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a hard day, and your mind keeps replaying noise, fear, and unfinished tasks. This verse offers a gentler anchor: place attention on what is worthy, and the mind begins to settle.
ramacharitamanas::4549.insight: It shifts attention from restless looping to steady remembrance of what ennobles you.

ramacharitamanas::4550.verse_sanskrit: पूरब दिसा बिलोकि प्रभु देखा उदित मयंक। कहत सबहि देखहु ससिहि मृगपति सरिस असंक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4550.verse_hindi: पूर्व दिशा की ओर देखकर प्रभु श्री रामजी ने चंद्रमा को उदय हुआ देखा। तब वे सबसे कहने लगे- चंद्रमा को तो देखो। कैसा सिंह के समान निडर है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4550.english_translation: Looking toward the east, the Lord saw the moon rise and said to everyone, 'Look at the moon. How fearless it is, like a lion!'
ramacharitamanas::4550.translation_literal: पूरब दिसा (toward the east) / बिलोकि (looking) / प्रभु (the Lord) / देखा (saw) / उदित (risen) / मयंक (moon) / कहत (saying) / सबहि (to everyone) / देखहु (look) / ससिहि (the moon) / मृगपति (lion) / सरिस (like) / असंक (fearless)
ramacharitamanas::4550.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4550.essence: Even the moon becomes a lesson when Ram is the one who sees it.
ramacharitamanas::4550.simple_meaning: Ram notices the rising moon and points it out as a sign of fearless beauty.
ramacharitamanas::4550.simple_insight: A simple sight becomes a reminder to see courage and grace together.
ramacharitamanas::4550.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the war has turned in Ram's favor, Ram looks east and sees the moon rising. He points it out to those around him, turning an ordinary night scene into a quiet moment of wonder and praise.
ramacharitamanas::4550.modern_relevance: You step outside after a long, brutal day and notice the moon above the rooftops. For a second, your mind stops fighting and simply sees beauty.
ramacharitamanas::4550.insight: It trains attention to pause on what is steady, calm, and fearless.

ramacharitamanas::4551.verse_sanskrit: पूरब दिसि गिरिगुहा निवासी। परम प्रताप तेज बल रासी॥ मत्त नाग तम कुंभ बिदारी। ससि केसरी गगन बन चारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4551.verse_hindi: पूर्व दिशा रूपी पर्वत की गुफा में रहने वाला, अत्यंत प्रताप, तेज और बल की राशि यह चंद्रमा रूपी सिंह अंधकार रूपी मतवाले हाथी के मस्तक को विदीर्ण करके आकाश रूपी वन में निर्भय विचर रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4551.english_translation: Facing east, the mountain-cave dweller, a storehouse of supreme splendor, radiance, and strength, tears apart the forehead of the drunken elephant of darkness and roams fearlessly through the sky-forest like the moon-lion.
ramacharitamanas::4551.translation_literal: पूरब (east) / दिसि (direction) / गिरिगुहा (mountain cave) / निवासी (dweller) / परम (supreme) / प्रताप (majesty) / तेज (radiance) / बल (strength) / रासी (heap, storehouse) / मत्त (intoxicated) / नाग (elephant) / तम (darkness) / कुंभ (forehead, temple) / बिदारी (splitting, tearing) / ससि (moon) / केसरी (lion) / गगन (sky) / बन (forest) / चारी (wandering)
ramacharitamanas::4551.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4551.essence: Radiance does not fight darkness — it breaks it apart.
ramacharitamanas::4551.simple_meaning: Ram is described through a vivid moon image: radiant, powerful, fearless, and able to break through darkness.
ramacharitamanas::4551.simple_insight: A clear image can carry reverence better than explanation.
ramacharitamanas::4551.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram points out the moon to his companions, Tulsidas turns that sight into praise. Ram is pictured as the moon-lion moving freely through the sky, while darkness collapses before his radiance.
ramacharitamanas::4551.modern_relevance: You look up after a long, draining day and see one clean light cutting through the dark street. Sometimes strength is not loud — it simply makes fear look smaller.
ramacharitamanas::4551.insight: It shifts attention from darkness itself to the power that makes darkness retreat.

ramacharitamanas::4552.verse_sanskrit: बिथुरे नभ मुकुताहल तारा। निसि सुंदरी केर सिंगारा॥ कह प्रभु ससि महुँ मेचकताई। कहहु काह निज निज मति भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4552.verse_hindi: आकाश में बिखरे हुए तारे मोतियों के समान हैं, जो रात्रि रूपी सुंदर स्त्री के श्रृंगार हैं। प्रभु ने कहा- भाइयो! चंद्रमा में जो कालापन है, वह क्या है? अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार कहो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4552.english_translation: The stars scattered across the sky are pearls, the ornaments of the night as a beautiful woman. The Lord said, "Brothers, what is the dark mark in the moon? Tell me according to your own understanding."
ramacharitamanas::4552.translation_literal: बिथुरे (scattered) / नभ (sky) / मुकुताहल (pearls) / तारा (stars) / निसि (night) / सुंदरी (beautiful woman) / केर (of) / सिंगारा (ornament) / कह (said) / प्रभु (Lord) / ससि (moon) / महुँ (in) / मेचकताई (darkness / black mark) / कहहु (tell) / काह (what) / निज (your own) / निज (own) / मति (understanding) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::4552.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4552.essence: Clear seeing begins by asking what others miss.
ramacharitamanas::4552.simple_meaning: Ram points out the moon's dark mark and invites everyone to explain it using their own understanding. The verse values careful seeing and thoughtful questioning.
ramacharitamanas::4552.simple_insight: You do not have to accept first impressions. Clear seeing begins when you ask better questions.
ramacharitamanas::4552.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield night, Ram looks up at the moon and turns the moment into a shared inquiry. He describes the stars as ornaments of the sky, then asks his companions to explain the moon's dark mark. The scene becomes a lesson in seeing with discernment.
ramacharitamanas::4552.modern_relevance: You notice a flaw in someone's message, a strange line in a report, or a tense look in a friend's face. Before reacting, Ram's question asks you to look again and think for yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4552.insight: It trains the mind to pause at appearances and investigate before forming a conclusion.

ramacharitamanas::4553.verse_sanskrit: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुराई। ससि महुँ प्रगट भूमि कै झाँई॥ मारेउ राहु ससिहि कह कोई। उर महँ परी स्यामता सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4553.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव ने कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिए! चंद्रमा में पृथ्वी की छाया दिखाई दे रही है। किसी ने कहा- चंद्रमा को राहु ने मारा था। वही (चोट का) काला दाग हृदय पर पड़ा हुआ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4553.english_translation: Sugriva said, “Listen, Raghuraj! The moon seems to show the Earth’s shadow. Someone says Rahu struck the moon. That same dark mark lies in the heart.”
ramacharitamanas::4553.translation_literal: कह (said) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुराई (Raghuraj) / ससि (moon) / महुँ (in) / प्रगट (visible) / भूमि (earth) / कै (of) / झाँई (shadow) / मारेउ (struck) / राहु (Rahu) / ससिहि (the moon) / कह (says) / कोई (someone) / उर (heart) / महँ (in) / परी (fell) / स्यामता (darkness) / सोई (that same)
ramacharitamanas::4553.speaker: Sugriva
ramacharitamanas::4553.essence: A dark mark on the moon becomes a poetic clue, not a complete idea.
ramacharitamanas::4553.simple_meaning: Sugriva points to a dark mark on the moon and repeats an old explanation for it. The verse is part of a poetic comparison, not a teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4553.simple_insight: Some images only make sense as part of a larger flow.
ramacharitamanas::4553.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sugriva is speaking to Ram while the scene turns poetic. He notices the moon’s dark mark and offers a folk explanation about Rahu. The verse serves as a moving image in a longer description, not a complete teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4553.modern_relevance: You hear a fragment of a story in the middle of a conversation and try to make it mean more than it does. Some lines are only stepping-stones to the next image.
ramacharitamanas::4553.insight: It stays with the surrounding verses, using one image to support the next.

ramacharitamanas::4554.verse_sanskrit: कोउ कह जब बिधि रति मुख कीन्हा। सार भाग ससि कर हरि लीन्हा॥ छिद्र सो प्रगट इंदु उर माहीं। तेहि मग देखिअ नभ परिछाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4554.verse_hindi: कोई कहता है- जब ब्रह्मा ने (कामदेव की स्त्री) रति का मुख बनाया, तब उसने चंद्रमा का सार भाग निकाल लिया (जिससे रति का मुख तो परम सुंदर बन गया, परन्तु चंद्रमा के हृदय में छेद हो गया)। वही छेद चंद्रमा के हृदय में वर्तमान है, जिसकी राह से आकाश की काली छाया उसमें दिखाई पड़ती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4554.english_translation: Someone says: when Brahma made Rati's face, he took the best part of the moon. That is why a hollow remains in the moon's heart, and the dark shadow of the sky is seen there.
ramacharitamanas::4554.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / जब (when) / बिधि (Brahma) / रति (Rati) / मुख (face) / कीन्हा (made) / सार (essence) / भाग (part) / ससि (moon) / कर (of) / हरि (took away) / लीन्हा (took) / छिद्र (hollow) / सो (that) / प्रगट (manifest) / इंदु (moon) / उर (heart) / माहीं (in) / तेहि (that) / मग (path) / देखिअ (is seen) / नभ (sky) / परिछाहीं (shadow)
ramacharitamanas::4554.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4554.essence: Beauty can still carry the mark of loss.
ramacharitamanas::4554.simple_meaning: People are explaining the moon's dark mark as a hollow left after its best essence was taken away.
ramacharitamanas::4554.simple_insight: Even beauty can carry a visible wound.
ramacharitamanas::4554.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the night sky becomes a field for playful explanation. Ram and the others are speaking of the moon's dark mark, and this verse offers one more image: the moon looks beautiful, but it also bears an inward hollow.
ramacharitamanas::4554.modern_relevance: You smile for the photo, but the tiredness still shows around your eyes. People may see the glow first, yet the crack in you can still be there.
ramacharitamanas::4554.insight: It turns a celestial image into a reminder that visible beauty can coexist with hidden absence.

ramacharitamanas::4555.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु कह गरल बंधु ससि केरा। अति प्रिय निज उर दीन्ह बसेरा॥ बिष संजुत कर निकर पसारी। जारत बिरहवंत नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4555.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामजी ने कहा- विष चंद्रमा का बहुत प्यारा भाई है, इसी से उसने विष को अपने हृदय में स्थान दे रखा है। विषयुक्त अपने किरण समूह को फैलाकर वह वियोगी नर-नारियों को जलाता रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4555.english_translation: The Lord said: poison is the moon's dear brother, and so the moon has given it a place in its heart. Spreading its poisoned rays, it burns men and women who are separated from their beloved.
ramacharitamanas::4555.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / कह (said) / गरल (poison) / बंधु (brother) / ससि (moon) / केरा (of) / अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / निज (own) / उर (heart) / दीन्ह (gave) / बसेरा (dwelling) / बिष (poison) / संजुत (filled with) / कर (hand) / निकर (group) / पसारी (spreading) / जारत (burning) / बिरहवंत (those in separation) / नर (men) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::4555.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4555.essence: Longing makes even beauty feel like fire.
ramacharitamanas::4555.simple_meaning: Ram explains the moon's dark mark as something it keeps close, and says its rays burn people suffering separation.
ramacharitamanas::4555.simple_insight: Even beauty can carry pain when love is absent.
ramacharitamanas::4555.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the conversation turns playful and poetic as Ram and Hanuman look at the moon. Ram gives a tender, imaginative explanation for the moon's dark mark, linking it to the ache of separation that burns lovers everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::4555.modern_relevance: You stare at the moon on a night after a breakup, and it feels almost cruelly beautiful. What shines can still remind you of what hurts.
ramacharitamanas::4555.insight: It turns a natural image into a mirror for longing, making separation feel universal rather than private.

ramacharitamanas::4556.verse_sanskrit: कह हनुमंत सुनहु प्रभु ससि तुम्हार प्रिय दास। तव मूरति बिधु उर बसति सोइ स्यामता अभास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4556.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे प्रभो! सुनिए, चंद्रमा आपका प्रिय दास है। आपकी सुंदर श्याम मूर्ति चंद्रमा के हृदय में बसती है, वही श्यामता की झलक चंद्रमा में है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4556.english_translation: Hanuman said, “Listen, Lord: the moon is your beloved servant. Your beautiful dark form dwells in the moon’s heart; that is why the moon shows a trace of that dark hue.”
ramacharitamanas::4556.translation_literal: कह (said) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / सुनहु (listen) / प्रभु (Lord) / ससि (moon) / तुम्हार (your) / प्रिय (beloved) / दास (servant) / तव (your) / मूरति (form) / बिधु (moon) / उर (heart) / बसति (dwells) / सोइ (that) / स्यामता (dark hue) / अभास (trace)
ramacharitamanas::4556.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4556.essence: Devotion sees the beloved’s mark in all beauty.
ramacharitamanas::4556.simple_meaning: Hanuman praises Ram by saying the moon reflects Ram’s dark beauty because Ram’s form dwells in it.
ramacharitamanas::4556.simple_insight: Love makes the whole world look like a reminder of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::4556.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is speaking to Ram after finding Sita. Instead of ordinary praise, he turns the moon into a sign of Ram’s presence. The moment is intimate bhakti: everything beautiful points back to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4556.modern_relevance: You look up at the moon after a long night and feel your chest loosen. In that quiet moment, even beauty feels like it is pointing beyond itself.
ramacharitamanas::4556.insight: It trains the mind to see every beauty as an echo of the divine presence.

ramacharitamanas::4557.verse_sanskrit: पवन तनय के बचन सुनि बिहँसे रामु सुजान। दच्छिन दिसि अवलोकि प्रभु बोले कृपा निधान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4557.verse_hindi: पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर सुजान श्री रामजी हँसे। फिर दक्षिण की ओर देखकर कृपानिधान प्रभु बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4557.english_translation: Hearing Hanuman's words, wise Ram smiled. Looking toward the south, the Lord of grace then spoke.
ramacharitamanas::4557.translation_literal: पवन तनय (son of the wind) / के बचन (words) / सुनि (having heard) / बिहँसे (smiled) / रामु (Ram) / सुजान (wise) / दच्छिन दिसि (south direction) / अवलोकि (looking) / प्रभु (Lord) / बोले (spoke) / कृपा निधान (treasure of grace)
ramacharitamanas::4557.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4557.essence: Ram receives devotion with calm and answers by moving the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::4557.simple_meaning: Ram smiles at Hanuman's words and then turns south to speak. The verse mainly moves the scene forward into the next instruction.
ramacharitamanas::4557.simple_insight: A calm smile can come before a decisive response.
ramacharitamanas::4557.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just spoken to Ram through the unfolding scene. Ram smiles at the faithful messenger and looks south, where the next action is about to begin. This line serves as a bridge into the coming instruction.
ramacharitamanas::4557.modern_relevance: You hear something hopeful, smile for a second, and then turn toward the harder part of the conversation. Not every meaningful response needs many words.
ramacharitamanas::4557.insight: It shifts attention from the messenger's report to the next practical step.

ramacharitamanas::4558.verse_sanskrit: देखु विभीषन दच्छिन आसा। घन घमंड दामिनी बिलासा॥ मधुर मधुर गरजइ घन घोरा। होइ बृष्टि जनि उपल कठोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4558.verse_hindi: हे विभीषण! दक्षिण दिशा की ओर देखो, बादल कैसा घुमड़ रहा है और बिजली चमक रही है। भयानक बादल मीठे-मीठे (हल्के-हल्के) स्वर से गरज रहा है। कहीं कठोर ओलों की वर्षा न हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4558.english_translation: Look, Vibhishana, toward the south. Clouds are swelling, and lightning is flashing. The dark clouds rumble softly, softly. May hard hailstones not fall as rain.
ramacharitamanas::4558.translation_literal: देखु (look) / विभीषन (Vibhishana) / दच्छिन (south) / आसा (toward) / घन (clouds) / घमंड (swelling pride) / दामिनी (lightning) / बिलासा (play/display) / मधुर (sweet) / मधुर (sweet) / गरजइ (rumbles) / घन (cloud) / घोरा (fierce) / होइ (may be) / बृष्टि (rain) / जनि (not) / उपल (hailstones) / कठोरा (hard)
ramacharitamanas::4558.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4558.essence: The sky darkens before the next turn in the story.
ramacharitamanas::4558.simple_meaning: Ram points out the dark clouds and lightning to Vibhishana, warning that hail may fall. It is a scene-setting verse, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4558.simple_insight: Not every vivid moment carries a lesson; some verses simply move the scene forward.
ramacharitamanas::4558.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram is speaking to Vibhishana and noticing the southern sky. Clouds gather, lightning flashes, and the air feels charged before the next turn in the story. The verse mainly paints the atmosphere and prepares for what follows.
ramacharitamanas::4558.insight: It shifts attention to the immediate scene, not to inner instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4559.verse_sanskrit: कहत विभीषन सुनहू कृपाला। होइ न तड़ित न बारिद माला॥ लंका सिखर उपर आगारा। तहँ दसकंधर देख अखारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4559.verse_hindi: विभीषण बोले- हे कृपालु! सुनिए, यह न तो बिजली है, न बादलों की घटा। लंका की चोटी पर एक महल है। दशग्रीव रावण वहाँ (नाच-गान का) अखाड़ा देख रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4559.english_translation: Vibhishana said, "Listen, O compassionate one. This is neither lightning nor a garland of clouds. On Lanka's summit there is a palace; there, Ravana is watching a dance arena."
ramacharitamanas::4559.translation_literal: कहत (saying) / विभीषन (Vibhishana) / सुनहू (listen) / कृपाला (compassionate one)। होइ (is) / न (not) / तड़ित (lightning) / न (nor) / बारिद (clouds) / माला (garland, line)॥ लंका (Lanka) / सिखर (peak) / उपर (on) / आगारा (palace)। तहँ (there) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / देख (seeing) / अखारा (arena, dance hall) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4559.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4559.essence: What looks like a storm is really Ravana's pride on display.
ramacharitamanas::4559.simple_meaning: Vibhishana points out that the strange sight in Lanka is not a storm. It is Ravana on the palace peak, watching a dance arena.
ramacharitamanas::4559.simple_insight: Some threats are not natural forces at all — they are ego putting on a show.
ramacharitamanas::4559.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ram and Vibhishana look toward the city and see a dramatic shape in the sky. Vibhishana corrects the first impression: it is not weather, but Ravana above his palace, absorbed in display while danger closes in.
ramacharitamanas::4559.modern_relevance: You glimpse chaos from across the street and assume disaster. Then you get closer and see it is one person making a spectacle, while everyone else pays the price.
ramacharitamanas::4559.insight: It shifts attention from appearances to the real source of disorder.

ramacharitamanas::4560.verse_sanskrit: छत्र मेघडंबर सिर धारी। सोइ जनु जलद घटा अति कारी॥ मंदोदरी श्रवन ताटंका। सोइ प्रभु जनु दामिनी दमंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4560.verse_hindi: रावण ने सिर पर मेघडंबर (बादलों के डंबर जैसा विशाल और काला) छत्र धारण कर रखा है। वही मानो बादलों की काली घटा है। मंदोदरी के कानों में जो कर्णफूल हिल रहे हैं, हे प्रभो! वही मानो बिजली चमक रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4560.english_translation: Ravana wears a huge black umbrella on his head, like a mass of dark clouds. The earrings in Mandodari's ears flash like lightning.
ramacharitamanas::4560.translation_literal: छत्र (umbrella/canopy) / मेघडंबर (cloud-like huge black mass) / सिर (head) / धारी (wearing) / सोइ (that very) / जनु (as if) / जलद (clouds) / घटा (mass/cluster) / अति (very) / कारी (black) / मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / श्रवन (ears) / ताटंका (earrings) / सोइ (that very) / प्रभु (O lord) / जनु (as if) / दामिनी (lightning) / दमंका (flashing/glittering)
ramacharitamanas::4560.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4560.essence: Ravana is framed as a storm before the battle even begins.
ramacharitamanas::4560.simple_meaning: Ravana is described through vivid comparisons: his umbrella looks like dark clouds, and Mandodari’s earrings look like lightning.
ramacharitamanas::4560.simple_insight: The scene builds Ravana’s grandeur and menace through images of storm and flash.
ramacharitamanas::4560.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the narration keeps painting Ravana’s court like a storm gathering over the city. His black canopy becomes a cloud mass, and Mandodari’s earrings become lightning, heightening the atmosphere before the war turns fully violent.
ramacharitamanas::4560.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the boss walks in, and every small detail suddenly feels charged. The mind starts reading power into shadows, shine, and movement.
ramacharitamanas::4560.insight: It trains attention to see how imagery can turn a scene into a warning.

ramacharitamanas::4561.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं ताल मृदंग अनूपा। सोइ रव मधुर सुनहू सुरभूपा। प्रभु मुसुकान समुझि अभिमाना। चाप चढ़ाव बान संधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4561.verse_hindi: हे देवताओं के सम्राट! सुनिए, अनुपम ताल मृदंग बज रहे हैं। वही मधुर (गर्जन) ध्वनि है। रावण का अभिमान समझकर प्रभु मुस्कुराए। उन्होंने धनुष चढ़ाकर उस पर बाण का सन्धान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4561.english_translation: O lord of the gods, listen: the drums beat with unmatched rhythm. That very sweet sound is the thunder. Seeing Ravana's pride, the Lord smiled and drew his bow, stringing the arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4561.translation_literal: बाजहिं (are sounding) / ताल (rhythm) / मृदंग (drums) / अनूपा (matchless) / सोइ (that very) / रव (sound) / मधुर (sweet) / सुनहू (listen) / सुरभूपा (lord of the gods) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मुसुकान (smile) / समुझि (understanding) / अभिमाना (pride) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ाव (raised) / बान (arrow) / संधाना (set in place)
ramacharitamanas::4561.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4561.essence: Pride is met with calm, then decisive action.
ramacharitamanas::4561.simple_meaning: The drums sound like thunder as the battle begins. Ram smiles at Ravana's pride, then lifts his bow and readies an arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4561.simple_insight: A calm smile can meet arrogance without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4561.detailed_meaning: Vibhishana is pointing out Ravana's display from Lanka's heights while the war closes in. The sound of drums becomes a sign of battle. Ram sees through the pride, smiles, and prepares to strike.
ramacharitamanas::4561.modern_relevance: You hear the room get loud before a difficult conversation starts. Someone is posturing, but you stay steady, notice the ego, and prepare your response without losing yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4561.insight: It shifts you from reacting to bravado toward seeing clearly and acting cleanly.

ramacharitamanas::4562.verse_sanskrit: छत्र मुकुट तांटक तब हते एकहीं बान। सब कें देखत महि परे मरमु न कोऊ जान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4562.verse_hindi: और एक ही बाण से (रावण के) छत्र-मुकुट और (मंदोदरी के) कर्णफूल काट गिराए। सबके देखते-देखते वे जमीन पर आ पड़े, पर इसका भेद (कारण) किसी ने नहीं जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4562.english_translation: With a single arrow, the crown, umbrella, and earrings were cut down. Everyone saw them fall to the ground, but no one understood how it happened.
ramacharitamanas::4562.translation_literal: छत्र (umbrella/canopy) / मुकुट (crown) / तांटक (earrings) / तब (then) / हते (were struck down) / एकहीं (by a single) / बान (arrow) / सब (all) / कें (for) / देखत (watching) / महि (to the ground) / परे (fell) / मरमु (the secret) / न (not) / कोऊ (anyone) / जान (knew)
ramacharitamanas::4562.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4562.essence: Pride falls first; understanding comes later.
ramacharitamanas::4562.simple_meaning: One arrow sent Ravana’s crown, umbrella, and earrings falling to the ground before everyone’s eyes, and no one could tell how it was done.
ramacharitamanas::4562.simple_insight: Power can collapse in an instant, even before anyone understands what changed.
ramacharitamanas::4562.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram’s arrow has already shattered Ravana’s display of royal pride. The crown, canopy, and ornaments fall in front of the whole court, but the deeper blow is invisible: Ravana’s grandeur is being stripped away.
ramacharitamanas::4562.modern_relevance: A person walks into the meeting trying to look untouchable, and one calm sentence exposes everything. The room sees the shift before anyone can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::4562.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the hidden force that breaks arrogance.

ramacharitamanas::4563.verse_sanskrit: अस कौतुक करि राम सर प्रबिसेउ आई निषंग। रावन सभा ससंक सब देखि महा रसभंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::4563.verse_hindi: ऐसा चमत्कार करके श्री रामजी का बाण (वापस) आकर (फिर) तरकस में जा घुसा। यह महान् रस भंग (रंग में भंग) देखकर रावण की सारी सभा भयभीत हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4563.english_translation: After such a marvel, Ram's arrow returned and entered the quiver again. Seeing this great disruption of their revelry, Ravana's whole assembly was struck with fear.
ramacharitamanas::4563.translation_literal: अस (such) / कौतुक (wonder / marvel) / करि (having done) / राम (Ram) / सर (arrow) / प्रबिसेउ (entered) / आई (coming back) / निषंग (quiver) / रावन (Ravana's) / सभा (assembly) / ससंक (fearful) / सब (all) / देखि (seeing) / महा (great) / रसभंग (disruption of delight)
ramacharitamanas::4563.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4563.essence: Ram's power is so complete that even his arrow returns at once.
ramacharitamanas::4563.simple_meaning: Ram's arrow returned to his quiver after the strike, and Ravana's court was thrown into fear by the sudden disruption.
ramacharitamanas::4563.simple_insight: Even victory can unsettle arrogance in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4563.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has turned into a display of Ram's effortless power. After the arrow cuts down Ravana's pride, it returns to the quiver. Ravana's court, still watching, loses all composure as fear spreads through the assembly.
ramacharitamanas::4563.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one calm sentence lands harder than a shouting match. Everyone who was smirking a second ago suddenly feels the weight of what just happened.
ramacharitamanas::4563.insight: It shows that true force does not need to linger; one precise act can collapse pride completely.

ramacharitamanas::4564.verse_sanskrit: कंप न भूमि न मरुत बिसेषा। अस्त्र सस्त्र कछु नयन न देखा। सोचहिं सब निज हृदय मझारी। असगुन भयउ भयंकर भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4564.verse_hindi: न भूकम्प हुआ, न बहुत जोर की हवा (आँधी) चली। न कोई अस्त्र-शस्त्र ही नेत्रों से देखे। (फिर ये छत्र, मुकुट और कर्णफूल जैसे कटकर गिर पड़े?) सभी अपने-अपने हृदय में सोच रहे हैं कि यह बड़ा भयंकर अपशकुन हुआ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4564.english_translation: No earthquake shook the earth, and no strong wind blew. No weapons were seen by anyone's eyes. Yet everyone kept thinking in their own hearts, 'This is a terrible omen.'
ramacharitamanas::4564.translation_literal: कंप (shaking) / न (not) / भूमि (earth) / न (not) / मरुत (wind) / बिसेषा (especially, strongly) / अस्त्र (weapons) / सस्त्र (arms, weapons) / कछु (any) / नयन (eyes) / न (not) / देखा (saw) / सोचहिं (they think) / सब (all) / निज (their own) / हृदय (heart) / मझारी (within) / असगुन (bad omen) / भयउ (became) / भयंकर (terrible) / भारी (very great)
ramacharitamanas::4564.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4564.essence: Fear turns a mystery into a disaster before facts arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4564.simple_meaning: Nothing outward explains the shock, yet everyone feels a deep fear and reads the moment as a bad omen.
ramacharitamanas::4564.simple_insight: Fear can make a mind invent disaster even when nothing visible has changed.
ramacharitamanas::4564.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Ram's arrow has just cut down the royal insignia without any obvious disturbance in the air or earth. The assembly cannot explain what they saw, so their minds turn inward and fill the gap with dread.
ramacharitamanas::4564.modern_relevance: A message arrives with no context, and your mind races ahead before anyone has explained a thing. The facts are still small, but fear has already written the story.
ramacharitamanas::4564.insight: It shows how quickly uncertainty becomes omen when the mind is already shaken.

ramacharitamanas::4565.verse_sanskrit: दसमुख देखि सभा भय पाई। बिहसि बचन कह जुगुति बनाई। सिरउ गिरे संतत सुभ जाही। मुकुट परे कस असगुन ताही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4565.verse_hindi: सभा को भयतीत देखकर रावण ने हँसकर युक्ति रचकर ये वचन कहे- सिरों का गिरना भी जिसके लिए निरंतर शुभ होता रहा है, उसके लिए मुकुट का गिरना अपशकुन कैसा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4565.english_translation: Seeing the assembly afraid, Ravana laughed and spoke, making a clever excuse. "For one whose heads have always fallen as a blessing, how can the falling of a crown be an omen?"
ramacharitamanas::4565.translation_literal: दसमुख (ten-faced Ravana) / देखि (seeing) / सभा (the assembly) / भय (fear) / पाई (having obtained) / बिहसि (laughing) / बचन (words) / कह (spoke) / जुगुति (a clever device) / बनाई (having made) / सिरउ (heads) / गिरे (fell) / संतत (continuously) / सुभ (auspicious) / जाही (for whom) / मुकुट (crown) / परे (fell) / कस (how) / असगुन (bad omen) / ताही (for that one)
ramacharitamanas::4565.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4565.essence: Pride turns warning signs into excuses.
ramacharitamanas::4565.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to calm the frightened assembly by twisting the situation into confidence. He says that if heads falling has always meant victory for him, then a crown falling cannot be a bad sign.
ramacharitamanas::4565.simple_insight: Pride can turn danger into a joke, even when the threat is real.
ramacharitamanas::4565.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sees his court shaken by fear after the strange signs around the battlefield. Rather than face the fear honestly, he laughs and speaks cleverly, trying to steady everyone with bravado. The verse shows his ego defending itself.
ramacharitamanas::4565.modern_relevance: You notice a project is slipping, but the boss cracks a joke and calls it fine. Sometimes confidence is just panic wearing a smile.
ramacharitamanas::4565.insight: It reveals how ego protects itself by dressing fear up as certainty.

ramacharitamanas::4566.verse_sanskrit: मन्दोदरी का फिर रावण को समझाना और श्री राम की महिमा कहना सयन करहु निज निज गृह जाईं। गवने भवन सकल सिर नाई॥ मंदोदरी सोच उर बसेऊ। जब ते श्रवनपूर महि खसेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4566.verse_hindi: अपने-अपने घर जाकर सो रहो (डरने की कोई बात नहीं है) तब सब लोग सिर नवाकर घर गए। जब से कर्णफूल पृथ्वी पर गिरा, तब से मंदोदरी के हृदय में सोच बस गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4566.english_translation: Mandodari again advises Ravana and speaks of Ram's greatness: "Go and sleep in your own homes." Everyone then bowed and went home. But when the earrings fell to the ground, Mandodari's heart filled with worry.
ramacharitamanas::4566.translation_literal: मन्दोदरी (Mandodari) / का (of) / फिर (again) / रावण को (to Ravana) / समझाना (advising) / और (and) / श्री राम की महिमा (the greatness of Shri Ram) / कहना (speaking) / सयन करहु (go to sleep) / निज निज (your own) / गृह (homes) / जाईं (go) / गवने (went) / भवन (to their homes) / सकल (all) / सिर नाई (bowing their heads) / मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / सोच (worry) / उर (in the heart) / बसेऊ (entered) / जब (when) / ते (that) / श्रवनपूर (ear-ornament) / महि (to the ground) / खसेऊ (fell)
ramacharitamanas::4566.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4566.essence: A court can pretend calm, but one falling sign awakens fear.
ramacharitamanas::4566.simple_meaning: Mandodari tries again to calm Ravana and point him toward Ram's greatness. The court disperses, but the fallen earring leaves her heart uneasy.
ramacharitamanas::4566.simple_insight: Sometimes one small sign of collapse tells you what denial is hiding.
ramacharitamanas::4566.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the court has been shaken by ominous signs. Mandodari speaks again, trying to steady Ravana and turn his mind toward Ram. The immediate panic passes, but the fall of the earring settles fear into her heart.
ramacharitamanas::4566.modern_relevance: You tell everyone the crisis is under control, and the room quiets for a moment. Then one tiny detail—a dropped phone, a missed call, a silence—makes your stomach tighten.
ramacharitamanas::4566.insight: It shows how a single unsettling sign can break through public confidence and expose private fear.

ramacharitamanas::4567.verse_sanskrit: सजल नयन कह जुग कर जोरी। सुनहु प्रानपति बिनती मोरी॥ कंत राम बिरोध परिहरहू। जानि मनुज जनि हठ लग धरहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4567.verse_hindi: नेत्रों में जल भरकर, दोनों हाथ जोड़कर वह (रावण से) कहने लगी- हे प्राणनाथ! मेरी विनती सुनिए। हे प्रियतम! श्री राम से विरोध छोड़ दीजिए। उन्हें मनुष्य जानकर मन में हठ न पकड़े रहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4567.english_translation: With tears in her eyes, she folded both hands and said, "Listen to my plea, my beloved lord. O dear one, give up hostility toward Ram. Do not stubbornly cling to the thought that He is only a human."
ramacharitamanas::4567.translation_literal: सजल (filled with water / tearful) / नयन (eyes) / कह (said) / जुग कर (both hands) / जोरी (joined) / सुनहु (listen) / प्रानपति (lord of my life) / बिनती (request / plea) / मोरी (my) ॥ कंत (beloved) / राम (Ram) / बिरोध (hostility / opposition) / परिहरहू (give up / leave aside) ॥ जानि (knowing) / मनुज (human) / जनि (do not) / हठ (stubbornness) / लग (to) / धरहू (hold) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4567.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4567.essence: Stubborn pride fails when it refuses to see Ram clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4567.simple_meaning: Mandodari begs Ravana to stop opposing Ram and to drop the stubborn belief that Ram is merely human.
ramacharitamanas::4567.simple_insight: Pride can make you blind to what is standing right in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4567.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari sees Ravana still refusing to yield even as ruin closes in. With tears and folded hands, she pleads for him to stop treating Ram as an ordinary man and to let go of his hard pride.
ramacharitamanas::4567.modern_relevance: You keep arguing with a truth your partner, friend, or conscience has already made clear. The longer you defend the wrong story, the more damage you do to yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4567.insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn denial to humble recognition of reality.

ramacharitamanas::4568.verse_sanskrit: बिस्वरूप रघुबंस मनि करहु बचन बिस्वासु। लोक कल्पना बेद कर अंग अंग प्रति जासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4568.verse_hindi: मेरे इन वचनों पर विश्वास कीजिए कि ये रघुकुल के शिरोमणि श्री रामचंद्रजी विश्व रूप हैं- (यह सारा विश्व उन्हीं का रूप है)। वेद जिनके अंग-अंग में लोकों की कल्पना करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4568.english_translation: Believe my words: the jewel of the Raghu clan is the cosmic form, and the Vedas imagine all worlds as parts of him.
ramacharitamanas::4568.translation_literal: बिस्वरूप (cosmic form) / रघुबंस मनि (jewel of the Raghu clan) / करहु (do) / बचन (word) / बिस्वासु (trust) / लोक (worlds) / कल्पना (imagination) / बेद (Vedas) / कर (of) / अंग अंग (each and every limb) / प्रति (in regard to) / जासु (whose)
ramacharitamanas::4568.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4568.essence: Ram is not inside the world; the world rests inside Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4568.simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana to trust her: Ram is not just a prince, but the cosmic form behind all existence, with every world as part of him.
ramacharitamanas::4568.simple_insight: What looks like one man is far larger than your fear can measure.
ramacharitamanas::4568.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari tries one last time to save Ravana from ruin. She does not argue politics; she points to Ram's cosmic nature. This verse begins her vision of Ram as the form in which all worlds are contained.
ramacharitamanas::4568.modern_relevance: You are staring at one person, one problem, one loss, and it feels absolute. This verse widens the frame: what seems small to you may be held inside something much larger.
ramacharitamanas::4568.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as limited form to seeing him as the ground of all forms.

ramacharitamanas::4569.verse_sanskrit: पद पाताल सीस अज धामा। अपर लोक अँग अँग बिश्रामा॥ भृकुटि बिलास भयंकर काला। नयन दिवाकर कच घन माला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4569.verse_hindi: पाताल (जिन विश्व रूप भगवान् का) चरण है, ब्रह्म लोक सिर है, अन्य (बीच के सब) लोकों का विश्राम (स्थिति) जिनके अन्य भिन्न-भिन्न अंगों पर है। भयंकर काल जिनका भृकुटि संचालन (भौंहों का चलना) है। सूर्य नेत्र हैं, बादलों का समूह बाल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4569.english_translation: The underworld is his feet, the realm of Brahma is his head, and all the worlds rest in his many limbs. Fearsome Time is the movement of his brow; the sun is his eyes, and clouds are his hair.
ramacharitamanas::4569.translation_literal: पद (feet) / पाताल (the underworld) / सीस (head) / अज धामा (the abode of Brahma) / अपर लोक (other worlds) / अँग अँग (each limb) / बिश्रामा (resting place) / भृकुटि (brow) / बिलास (movement/play) / भयंकर (fearsome) / काला (Time/black) / नयन (eyes) / दिवाकर (sun) / कच (hair) / घन माला (garland of clouds)
ramacharitamanas::4569.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4569.essence: Everything rests inside Ram's vast form, even Time.
ramacharitamanas::4569.simple_meaning: Ram's cosmic form contains every realm within itself. The whole universe rests in him, and even Time seems like a small movement within his body.
ramacharitamanas::4569.simple_insight: The world feels less overwhelming when you see it held inside something greater.
ramacharitamanas::4569.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana is urging Ravana to stop opposing Ram by describing Ram's universal form. This verse expands that vision: every realm, from the underworld to Brahma's abode, is only a limb of Ram. The point is to make Ravana see who he is really confronting.
ramacharitamanas::4569.modern_relevance: You are staring at a crisis that feels bigger than your control. Then a wider view returns: the pressure, the fear, even time itself are not the whole of reality.
ramacharitamanas::4569.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the world as fragmented to seeing it as held within one vast order.

ramacharitamanas::4570.verse_sanskrit: जासु घ्रान अस्विनीकुमारा। निसि अरु दिवस निमेष अपारा॥ श्रवन दिसा दस बेद बखानी। मारुत स्वास निगम निज बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4570.verse_hindi: अश्विनी कुमार जिनकी नासिका हैं, रात और दिन जिनके अपार निमेष (पलक मारना और खोलना) हैं। दसों दिशाएँ कान हैं, वेद ऐसा कहते हैं। वायु श्वास है और वेद जिनकी अपनी वाणी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4570.english_translation: The Ashwini Kumaras are his nostrils; night and day are his endless blinking. The ten directions are his ears, the Vedas declare. Wind is his breath, and the Vedas are his own speech.
ramacharitamanas::4570.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / घ्रान (nose, nostrils) / अस्विनीकुमारा (the Ashwini Kumaras) / निसि (night) / अरु (and) / दिवस (day) / निमेष (blink) / अपारा (boundless) / श्रवन (ears) / दिसा (directions) / दस (ten) / बेद (the Vedas) / बखानी (declare) / मारुत (wind) / स्वास (breath) / निगम (the Vedas) / निज (own) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::4570.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4570.essence: Everything sacred and living is already contained in Ram's vast form.
ramacharitamanas::4570.simple_meaning: Ram's cosmic form is being described as vast enough to contain the powers of nature, the Vedas, and the directions themselves.
ramacharitamanas::4570.simple_insight: The divine is not distant here — everything you know is already held within him.
ramacharitamanas::4570.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still unfolding Ram's universal form after the earlier declaration that every part of the world belongs to him. This verse adds more sacred correspondences: healing powers, time, space, breath, and scripture itself all become features of Ram's body.
ramacharitamanas::4570.modern_relevance: You look up at the night sky after a hard day and feel small, but also strangely held. This verse turns that feeling into devotion: the world is not outside the divine presence; it is inside it.
ramacharitamanas::4570.insight: It shifts your view from seeing Ram as one figure among many to seeing all reality as his form.

ramacharitamanas::4571.verse_sanskrit: अधर लोभ जम दसन कराला। माया हास बाहु दिगपाला॥ आनन अनल अंबुपति जीहा। उतपति पालन प्रलय समीहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4571.verse_hindi: लोभ जिनका अधर (होठ) है, यमराज भयानक दाँत हैं। माया हँसी है, दिक्पाल भुजाएँ हैं। अग्नि मुख है, वरुण जीभ है। उत्पत्ति, पालन और प्रलय जिनकी चेष्टा (क्रिया) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4571.english_translation: Greed is the lips, and Yama's fearsome teeth. Illusion is the smile, and the guardians of the directions are the arms. Fire is the face, Varuna is the tongue. Creation, preservation, and destruction are the movements of that all-encompassing form.
ramacharitamanas::4571.translation_literal: अधर (lips) / लोभ (greed) / जम (Yama) / दसन (teeth) / कराला (fierce) / माया (illusion) / हास (smile) / बाहु (arms) / दिगपाला (guardians of the directions) / आनन (face) / अनल (fire) / अंबुपति (Varuna, lord of waters) / जीहा (tongue) / उतपति (creation) / पालन (preservation) / प्रलय (destruction) / समीहा (movements)
ramacharitamanas::4571.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4571.essence: Everything that seems separate is part of one immense form.
ramacharitamanas::4571.simple_meaning: The verse maps the universe onto one vast cosmic form: greed, illusion, death, fire, water, and the powers that govern the world all appear as parts of it.
ramacharitamanas::4571.simple_insight: What feels separate is actually held inside one larger reality.
ramacharitamanas::4571.detailed_meaning: The war has paused for a cosmic vision. After showing the world-body's limbs in the previous lines, the poet now names more features: greed, death, illusion, the guardians of space, fire, and water. The point is to reveal one immense form containing every force.
ramacharitamanas::4571.modern_relevance: You look at a system and see only separate parts: money, fear, power, appetite, control. Then you notice they all feed one larger machine, and your view changes completely.
ramacharitamanas::4571.insight: It shifts attention from isolated forces to the single reality that contains them all.

ramacharitamanas::4572.verse_sanskrit: रोम राजि अष्टादस भारा। अस्थि सैल सरिता नस जारा॥ उदर उदधि अधगो जातना। जगमय प्रभु का बहु कलपना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4572.verse_hindi: अठारह प्रकार की असंख्य वनस्पतियाँ जिनकी रोमावली हैं, पर्वत अस्थियाँ हैं, नदियाँ नसों का जाल है, समुद्र पेट है और नरक जिनकी नीचे की इंद्रियाँ हैं। इस प्रकार प्रभु विश्वमय हैं, अधिक कल्पना (ऊहापोह) क्या की जाए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4572.english_translation: Eighteen kinds of countless plants are his body hair; mountains are his bones, rivers his network of veins, the ocean his belly, and the lower realms his lower organs. The Lord is all-pervading—what more is there to imagine?
ramacharitamanas::4572.translation_literal: रोम राजि (body hair) / अष्टादस भारा (eighteen kinds, countless) / अस्थि (bones) / सैल (mountains) / सरिता (rivers) / नस (veins) / जारा (network) / उदर (belly) / उदधि (ocean) / अधगो (below) / जातना (lower organs, suffering places) / जगमय (world-filled, all-pervading) / प्रभु (Lord) / का (what) / बहु (much) / कलपना (imagination, speculation)
ramacharitamanas::4572.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4572.essence: The universe is not separate from the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::4572.simple_meaning: The whole universe is described as Ram's body: plants, mountains, rivers, oceans, and even lower regions all belong to him. He fills everything, so there is no need for more speculation.
ramacharitamanas::4572.simple_insight: You can stop feeling separate from the world and rest in a larger wholeness.
ramacharitamanas::4572.detailed_meaning: In Lankakand, Tulsidas pauses the war to reveal Ram's cosmic form. The world is not outside him; it is his body. After describing that vastness, the verse closes the mind's argument: there is nothing more to figure out.
ramacharitamanas::4572.modern_relevance: You are staring at a night sky after a hard day, feeling small and cut off. Then it hits you that nothing is truly outside the larger order holding it all together.
ramacharitamanas::4572.insight: It shifts attention from fragmented details to a single all-pervading reality.

ramacharitamanas::4573.verse_sanskrit: अहंकार सिव बुद्धि अज मन ससि चित्त महान। मनुज बास सचराचर रूप राम भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4573.verse_hindi: शिव जिनका अहंकार हैं, ब्रह्मा बुद्धि हैं, चंद्रमा मन हैं और महान (विष्णु) ही चित्त हैं। उन्हीं चराचर रूप भगवान श्री रामजी ने मनुष्य रूप में निवास किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4573.english_translation: Shiva is their ego, Brahma their intellect, the moon their mind, and the great one their inner state. The Lord Ram, whose form is all moving and unmoving beings, dwells in human form.
ramacharitamanas::4573.translation_literal: अहंकार (ego) / सिव (Shiva) / बुद्धि (intellect) / अज (unborn Brahma) / मन (mind) / ससि (moon) / चित्त (inner state) / महान (great one) / मनुज (human) / बास (dwelling) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / रूप (form) / राम भगवान (Lord Ram)
ramacharitamanas::4573.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4573.essence: The highest reality can choose to live as an ordinary person.
ramacharitamanas::4573.simple_meaning: Ram is described as the supreme being present in all moving and unmoving forms, yet also dwelling in human form. The verse points to his cosmic nature and his chosen nearness to people.
ramacharitamanas::4573.simple_insight: What feels ordinary may hold the highest presence.
ramacharitamanas::4573.detailed_meaning: After describing the vast, body-like form of the cosmic Lord, Tulsidas turns the vision inward: Ram is not only beyond the world, he has entered it as a human being. The verse crowns the passage by revealing divinity hidden in human form.
ramacharitamanas::4573.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, almost easy to overlook, and later realise their quiet presence changed everything. This verse asks you to look again at the human face in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4573.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as distant power to recognising sacred presence in human form.

ramacharitamanas::4574.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि सुनु प्रानपति प्रभु सन बयरु बिहाइ। प्रीति करहु रघुबीर पद मम अहिवात न जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4574.verse_hindi: हे प्राणपति सुनिए, ऐसा विचार कर प्रभु से वैर छोड़कर श्री रघुवीर के चरणों में प्रेम कीजिए, जिससे मेरा सुहाग न जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4574.english_translation: O lord of my life, think this through: give up enmity toward the Lord and love the feet of Raghubir, so my marriage bond may not be broken.
ramacharitamanas::4574.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / सुनु (listen) / प्रानपति (lord of my life) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सन (with) / बयरु (enmity) / बिहाइ (leaving) / प्रीति (love) / करहु (do) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / पद (feet) / मम (my) / अहिवात (marital bond) / न (not) / जाइ (go away)
ramacharitamanas::4574.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4574.essence: Love for Ram protects what hatred destroys.
ramacharitamanas::4574.simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana to stop opposing Ram and turn to devotion, warning that his wifehood and household will be ruined otherwise.
ramacharitamanas::4574.simple_insight: Pride can destroy even the bonds you are trying to protect.
ramacharitamanas::4574.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari pleads with Ravana one last time. She asks him to think clearly, give up hostility toward Ram, and bow in love instead. Her warning is personal: if he does not change, her marriage and his house will collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4574.modern_relevance: You are mid-argument, and the thing you are trying hardest to defend is the thing your anger is breaking. One honest turn could save the relationship.
ramacharitamanas::4574.insight: It shifts you from defending ego to seeing the cost of stubborn opposition.

ramacharitamanas::4575.verse_sanskrit: बिहँसा नारि बचन सुनि काना। अहो मोह महिमा बलवाना॥ नारि सुभाउ सत्य सब कहहीं। अवगुन आठ सदा उर रहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4575.verse_hindi: पत्नी के वचन कानों से सुनकर रावण खूब हँसा (और बोला-) अहो! मोह (अज्ञान) की महिमा बड़ी बलवान् है। स्त्री का स्वभाव सब सत्य ही कहते हैं कि उसके हृदय में आठ अवगुण सदा रहते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4575.english_translation: Hearing his wife's words, Ravana laughed and said, "Ah, how powerful delusion is! Women’s nature is said to hold eight faults always in the heart."
ramacharitamanas::4575.translation_literal: बिहँसा (laughed) / नारि (woman) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (with ears) / अहो (ah) / मोह (delusion) / महिमा (greatness) / बलवाना (very powerful) / नारि (woman) / सुभाउ (nature) / सत्य (true) / सब (all) / कहहीं (say) / अवगुन (faults) / आठ (eight) / सदा (always) / उर (heart) / रहहीं (remain)
ramacharitamanas::4575.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4575.essence: Delusion makes warning sound like insult.
ramacharitamanas::4575.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks his wife's warning and blames delusion, showing that he cannot hear wisdom without turning it into pride and contempt.
ramacharitamanas::4575.simple_insight: Pride makes even a warning sound like proof that you were right.
ramacharitamanas::4575.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just heard Mandodari's warning about the danger ahead. Instead of listening, he laughs it off and turns her words into contempt. The verse shows his mind already trapped by delusion before the fall begins.
ramacharitamanas::4575.modern_relevance: Someone texts you a careful warning, and you read it as criticism. By the time you start defending yourself, the real message is already lost.
ramacharitamanas::4575.insight: It reveals how ego converts feedback into self-justification and blocks clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4576.verse_sanskrit: साहस अनृत चपलता माया। भय अबिबेक असौच अदाया॥ रिपु कर रूप सकल तैं गावा। अति बिसाल भय मोहि सुनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4576.verse_hindi: साहस, झूठ, चंचलता, माया (छल), भय (डरपोकपन) अविवेक (मूर्खता), अपवित्रता और निर्दयता। तूने शत्रु का समग्र (विराट) रूप गाया और मुझे उसका बड़ा भारी भय सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4576.english_translation: Courage, falsehood, fickleness, illusion, fear, lack of discernment, impurity, and cruelty — you have described the enemy's whole vast form and filled me with terrible fear.
ramacharitamanas::4576.translation_literal: साहस (courage) / अनृत (falsehood) / चपलता (fickleness) / माया (illusion) / भय (fear) / अबिबेक (lack of discernment) / असौच (impurity) / अदाया (cruelty) / रिपु (enemy) / कर (of) / रूप (form) / सकल (entire) / तैं (you) / गावा (sang/described) / अति (very) / बिसाल (vast) / भय (fear) / मोहि (to me) / सुनावा (you told)
ramacharitamanas::4576.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4576.essence: Fear turns a real threat into a monstrous one.
ramacharitamanas::4576.simple_meaning: Ravana says the woman has described the enemy as a bundle of fear, falsehood, illusion, and cruelty, making him seem terrifyingly vast.
ramacharitamanas::4576.simple_insight: What you fear can grow larger than what is real.
ramacharitamanas::4576.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari tries to wake Ravana by naming the enemy's true nature. He answers by listing the very distortions that rule him and complain that she has made the enemy seem enormous. The verse exposes how fear and ignorance magnify danger.
ramacharitamanas::4576.modern_relevance: You read a message late at night and suddenly the whole situation feels catastrophic. Half the terror comes from your own mind filling in blanks.
ramacharitamanas::4576.insight: It shifts you from emotional exaggeration to clear seeing, so you can name what is actually there.

ramacharitamanas::4577.verse_sanskrit: सो सब प्रिया सहज बस मोरें। समुझि परा अब प्रसाद तोरें॥ जानिउँ प्रिया तोरि चतुराई। एहि बिधि कहहु मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4577.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! वह सब (यह चराचर विश्व तो) स्वभाव से ही मेरे वश में है। तेरी कृपा से मुझे यह अब समझ पड़ा। हे प्रिये! तेरी चतुराई मैं जान गया। तू इस प्रकार (इसी बहाने) मेरी प्रभुता का बखान कर रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4577.english_translation: Everything that exists is naturally under my control. By your grace, I now understand this. O beloved, I see your cleverness: in this way, you are praising my greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4577.translation_literal: सो (that) / सब (all) / प्रिया (beloved) / सहज (naturally) / बस (under control) / मोरें (of mine) । / समुझि (understanding) / परा (has fallen) / अब (now) / प्रसाद (grace) / तोरें (of yours) ॥ / जानिउँ (I know) / प्रिया (beloved) / तोरि (your) / चतुराई (cleverness) । / एहि (this) / बिधि (way) / कहहु (you speak) / मोरि (my) / प्रभुताई (greatness, lordship) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4577.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4577.simple_meaning: Ravana says he now understands that everything is already under his control, and he thinks Mandodari is cleverly praising his power through her words.
ramacharitamanas::4577.simple_insight: Pride can turn even a warning into praise.
ramacharitamanas::4577.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari is trying to warn Ravana by speaking carefully about his downfall. Instead of hearing concern, Ravana twists her words into flattery. This verse shows how ego blocks honest counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4577.modern_relevance: Someone points out the risk in your plan, but you hear only criticism of your brilliance. The mind that needs to feel superior can turn every warning into applause.
ramacharitamanas::4577.insight: It exposes how self-importance distorts listening and turns correction into confirmation.

ramacharitamanas::4578.verse_sanskrit: तव बतकही गूढ़ मृगलोचनि। समुझत सुखद सुनत भय मोचनि॥ मंदोदरि मन महुँ अस ठयऊ। पियहि काल बस मति भ्रम भयउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4578.verse_hindi: हे मृगनयनी! तेरी बातें बड़ी गूढ़ (रहस्यभरी) हैं, समझने पर सुख देने वाली और सुनने से भय छुड़ाने वाली हैं। मंदोदरी ने मन में ऐसा निश्चय कर लिया कि पति को कालवश मतिभ्रम हो गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4578.english_translation: O doe-eyed one, your words are profound: they bring delight when understood and remove fear when heard. Mandodari resolved in her mind that her husband had become deluded by time's power.
ramacharitamanas::4578.translation_literal: तव (your) / बतकही (speech) / गूढ़ (deep, hidden) / मृगलोचनि (doe-eyed one) / समुझत (understanding) / सुखद (joy-giving) / सुनत (hearing) / भय (fear) / मोचनि (removing) ॥ / मंदोदरि (Mandodari) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / अस (thus) / ठयऊ (resolved) / पियहि (the husband) / काल बस (under time's power) / मति (mind, understanding) / भ्रम (delusion) / भयउ (became) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4578.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4578.essence: Delusion can make even clear truth sound like comfort and warning.
ramacharitamanas::4578.simple_meaning: Mandodari sees that Ravana has become confused by time and pride. She recognizes that wise words can calm fear, but his mind is no longer clear enough to receive them.
ramacharitamanas::4578.simple_insight: It is painful to watch someone you love stay blind to the truth.
