ramacharitamanas::4578.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari speaks to Ravana with the tenderness of someone trying to reach a man already slipping beyond reason. She sees that his mind has been clouded by time and delusion, and that her words can soothe fear even if they cannot save him.
ramacharitamanas::4578.modern_relevance: You explain the situation carefully, but the other person is already defending a decision they made in anger. You can feel the conversation landing nowhere, even as your words are perfectly clear.
ramacharitamanas::4578.insight: It shifts attention from the content of advice to the receiver's state of mind.

ramacharitamanas::4579.verse_sanskrit: ऐहि बिधि करत बिनोद बहु प्रात प्रगट दसकंध। सहज असंक लंकपति सभाँ गयउ मद अंध ॥
ramacharitamanas::4579.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार (अज्ञानवश) बहुत से विनोद करते हुए रावण को सबेरा हो गया। तब स्वभाव से ही निडर और घमंड में अंधा लंकापति सभा में गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4579.english_translation: In this way, while making many idle jokes, dawn arrived for Ravana. Then the lord of Lanka, naturally fearless and blinded by pride, went to the assembly.
ramacharitamanas::4579.translation_literal: ऐहि बिधि (in this way) / करत (doing) / बिनोद (playful talk, idle amusement) / बहु (many) / प्रात (morning) / प्रगट (appeared, arrived) / दसकंध (ten-necked one, Ravana) / सहज (naturally) / असंक (fearless) / लंकपति (lord of Lanka) / सभाँ (to the assembly) / गयउ (went) / मद (pride, intoxication) / अंध (blind)
ramacharitamanas::4579.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4579.essence: Pride keeps you fearless until it blinds you.
ramacharitamanas::4579.simple_meaning: Ravana spends the night in careless amusement, then goes to his council in a state of fearless pride and blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4579.simple_insight: Pride can make a person feel untouchable right before they walk into their own downfall.
ramacharitamanas::4579.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the tense exchange with Mandodari, Ravana does not repent or reflect. He passes the night in idle amusement, and at dawn he walks into his assembly still blind with arrogance. The verse sets up how deeply his pride has taken hold.
ramacharitamanas::4579.modern_relevance: You keep joking in the group chat after the warning signs are obvious. By morning, you walk into the meeting still convinced nothing can touch you.
ramacharitamanas::4579.insight: It shows how ego can turn danger into entertainment and block any real self-correction.

ramacharitamanas::4580.verse_sanskrit: फूलइ फरइ न बेत जदपि सुधा बरषहिं जलद। मूरुख हृदयँ न चेत जौं गुर मिलहिं बिरंचि सम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4580.verse_hindi: यद्यपि बादल अमृत सा जल बरसाते हैं तो भी बेत फूलता-फलता नहीं। इसी प्रकार चाहे ब्रह्मा के समान भी ज्ञानी गुरु मिलें, तो भी मूर्ख के हृदय में चेत (ज्ञान) नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4580.english_translation: Even if nectar-like rain falls from the clouds, bamboo never flowers or bears fruit. In the same way, even if a teacher like Brahma is found, a fool's heart does not awaken.
ramacharitamanas::4580.translation_literal: फूलइ (flowers) / फरइ (bears fruit) / न (not) / बेत (bamboo) / जदपि (even though) / सुधा (nectar-like) / बरषहिं (they rain) / जलद (clouds) / मूरुख (foolish) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / न (not) / चेत (awakening) / जौं (even if) / गुर (teacher) / मिलहिं (are found) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सम (like)
ramacharitamanas::4580.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4580.essence: Wisdom cannot bloom in a heart that refuses to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::4580.simple_meaning: A person who refuses to awaken will not change, even with the best guidance. Real understanding needs an open and receptive heart.
ramacharitamanas::4580.simple_insight: Growth begins with receptivity, not just access to wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4580.detailed_meaning: Ravana's court has been shown as blind with pride, and this verse sharpens that warning. Tulsidas compares a fool's heart to bamboo: even if the heavens pour nectar and the greatest teacher appears, nothing will grow there.
ramacharitamanas::4580.modern_relevance: You keep explaining the same thing to someone who only wants to win the argument. No amount of perfect advice helps until the person is willing to hear it.
ramacharitamanas::4580.insight: It shifts attention from finding better instruction to becoming teachable.

ramacharitamanas::4581.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ प्रात जागे रघुराई। पूछा मत सब सचिव बोलाई॥ कहहु बेगि का करिअ उपाई। जामवंत कह पद सिरु नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4581.verse_hindi: यहाँ (सुबेल पर्वत पर) प्रातःकाल श्री रघुनाथजी जागे और उन्होंने सब मंत्रियों को बुलाकर सलाह पूछी कि शीघ्र बताइए, अब क्या उपाय करना चाहिए? जाम्बवान् ने श्री रामजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4581.english_translation: At dawn, Raghunath woke up, called all the ministers together, and asked what should be done quickly. Jambavan bowed his head at Ram's feet and said:
ramacharitamanas::4581.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / प्रात (at dawn) / जागे (woke up) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / पूछा (asked) / मत (counsel) / सब (all) / सचिव (ministers) / बोलाई (having called) / कहहु (tell) / बेगि (quickly) / का (what) / करिअ (should be done) / उपाई (measure) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / कह (said) / पद (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::4581.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4581.essence: Real strength asks for guidance before it moves.
ramacharitamanas::4581.simple_meaning: Ram wakes at dawn, gathers his council, and asks for a quick solution. Jambavan responds with reverence and practical advice.
ramacharitamanas::4581.simple_insight: Even the highest leader listens first. Clear action begins with humble counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4581.detailed_meaning: On Suvela mountain, before the war's next move, Ram rises at dawn and calls his ministers for advice. The moment is urgent: the army needs direction, and Jambavan answers by bowing first, then speaking.
ramacharitamanas::4581.modern_relevance: You wake up to a crisis message and resist the urge to guess. You gather the right people, ask plainly what should be done, and let wisdom come before speed.
ramacharitamanas::4581.insight: It shifts leadership from reacting alone to seeking grounded counsel before acting.

ramacharitamanas::4582.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सर्बग्य सकल उर बासी। बुधि बल तेज धर्म गुन रासी॥ मंत्र कहउँ निज मति अनुसारा। दूत पठाइअ बालि कुमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4582.verse_hindi: हे सर्वज्ञ (सब कुछ जानने वाले)! हे सबके हृदय में बसने वाले (अंतर्यामी)! हे बुद्धि, बल, तेज, धर्म और गुणों की राशि! सुनिए! मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार सलाह देता हूँ कि बालिकुमार अंगद को दूत बनाकर भेजा जाए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4582.english_translation: O all-knowing one, who dwells in every heart and is the storehouse of wisdom, strength, radiance, virtue, and goodness, hear me. I offer my counsel according to my understanding: send Angad, the son of Bali, as the messenger.
ramacharitamanas::4582.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / सकल (all) / उर (heart) / बासी (dweller) / बुधि (wisdom) / बल (strength) / तेज (radiance) / धर्म (righteousness) / गुन (qualities) / रासी (heap, store) ॥ मंत्र (counsel) / कहउँ (I say) / निज (my own) / मति (understanding) / अनुसारा (according to) / दूत (messenger) / पठाइअ (send) / बालि कुमारा (son of Bali, Angad) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4582.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4582.essence: Reverence and practical counsel can move together.
ramacharitamanas::4582.simple_meaning: Jambavan praises Ram and suggests sending Angad as the messenger. The verse is part of a larger plan, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4582.simple_insight: Good counsel starts with seeing Ram clearly, then choosing the right person for the task.
ramacharitamanas::4582.detailed_meaning: On Suvela mountain, after the monkeys gather for strategy, Jambavan speaks to Ram with reverence. He praises Ram as the all-knowing one who lives in every heart, then offers a practical plan: send Angad, Bali’s son, as the messenger to Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4582.modern_relevance: In a tense team meeting, someone who truly respects the leader still brings a concrete solution, not just praise. Reverence and practical judgment can live together.
ramacharitamanas::4582.insight: It links devotion with strategy: honor the highest truth, then choose the right messenger for the mission.

ramacharitamanas::4583.verse_sanskrit: नीक मंत्र सब के मन माना। अंगद सन कह कृपानिधाना॥ बालितनय बुधि बल गुन धामा। लंका जाहु तात मम कामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4583.verse_hindi: यह अच्छी सलाह सबके मन में जँच गई। कृपा के निधान श्री रामजी ने अंगद से कहा- हे बल, बुद्धि और गुणों के धाम बालिपुत्र! हे तात! तुम मेरे काम के लिए लंका जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4583.english_translation: The wise counsel pleased everyone. The Lord of compassion then said to Angad, "Son of Bali, treasure of strength, wisdom, and virtue, go to Lanka for my task."
ramacharitamanas::4583.translation_literal: नीक (good) / मंत्र (counsel) / सब (all) / के (of) / मन (minds) / माना (was accepted) / अंगद (Angad) / सन (to) / कह (said) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of compassion)॥ / बालितनय (son of Bali) / बुधि (wisdom) / बल (strength) / गुन (virtue) / धामा (abode) / लंका (Lanka) / जाहु (go) / तात (son/dear one) / मम (my) / कामा (task) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4583.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4583.essence: True capability is proven when trust becomes responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::4583.simple_meaning: Ram accepts the plan and sends Angad to Lanka on his mission. He praises Angad’s strength, wisdom, and virtue before giving the task.
ramacharitamanas::4583.simple_insight: Being chosen matters less than being ready to serve when the moment comes.
ramacharitamanas::4583.detailed_meaning: On Suvela, after the council has agreed on a plan, Ram turns to Angad. He sees in Bali’s son the strength and judgment needed for a dangerous mission and sends him to Lanka as his messenger.
ramacharitamanas::4583.modern_relevance: Your team finally agrees on the approach, and then someone turns to you: "Can you handle the hard part?" The moment feels heavy, but it is also trust.
ramacharitamanas::4583.insight: It shifts attention from debate to execution: the right person is sent for the right task.

ramacharitamanas::4584.verse_sanskrit: बहुत बुझाइ तुम्हहि का कहऊँ। परम चतुर मैं जानत अहऊँ॥ काजु हमार तासु हित होई। रिपु सन करेहु बतकही सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4584.verse_hindi: तुमको बहुत समझाकर क्या कहूँ! मैं जानता हूँ, तुम परम चतुर हो। शत्रु से वही बातचीत करना, जिससे हमारा काम हो और उसका कल्याण हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4584.english_translation: Why explain much to you? I know you are extremely clever. Speak with the enemy in a way that serves our purpose and his good.
ramacharitamanas::4584.translation_literal: बहुत (much) / बुझाइ (explaining) / तुम्हहि (to you) / का (what) / कहऊँ (shall I say) / परम (supremely) / चतुर (clever) / मैं (I) / जानत (know) / अहऊँ (am)॥ / काजु (task) / हमार (our) / तासु (his) / हित (good) / होई (will be) / रिपु (enemy) / सन (with) / करेहु (do) / बतकही (conversation) / सोई (that very) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4584.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4584.essence: Clever speech should serve both the mission and the other person's good.
ramacharitamanas::4584.simple_meaning: Ram trusts Angad's intelligence and tells him to speak to the enemy in a way that helps their mission and still leaves room for the enemy's welfare.
ramacharitamanas::4584.simple_insight: Real strength can stay strategic without becoming cruel.
ramacharitamanas::4584.detailed_meaning: Before Lanka's final fall, Ram sends Angad to Ravana's court. Knowing Angad's sharp mind, Ram does not micromanage him. He gives a clear mission: speak in a way that advances the cause and still leaves room for the enemy's good.
ramacharitamanas::4584.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting knowing one wrong sentence could shut everyone down. The wisest move is not blunt force, but words that keep the goal alive without needless harm.
ramacharitamanas::4584.insight: It teaches you to use intelligence with restraint, aiming for effectiveness without losing goodwill.

ramacharitamanas::4585.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु अग्या धरि सीस चरन बंदि अंगद उठेउ। सोइ गुन सागर ईस राम कृपा जा कर करहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4585.verse_hindi: प्रभु की आज्ञा सिर चढ़कर और उनके चरणों की वंदना करके अंगदजी उठे (और बोले-) हे भगवान् श्री रामजी! आप जिस पर कृपा करें, वही गुणों का समुद्र हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4585.english_translation: Aṅgada rose, bowing his head to the Lord's command and worshipping his feet: "O Ram, the ocean of virtues becomes great only by your grace."
ramacharitamanas::4585.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / अग्या (command) / धरि (taking) / सीस (head) / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / अंगद (Aṅgada) / उठेउ (rose) / सोइ (that same) / गुन (virtues) / सागर (ocean) / ईस (Lord) / राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / जा कर (whose) / करहु (do/make)
ramacharitamanas::4585.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4585.essence: True greatness rises only after you bow first.
ramacharitamanas::4585.simple_meaning: Aṅgada rises only after bowing to Ram's command, and he says that real greatness comes from Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::4585.simple_insight: Humility is not weakness; it is the doorway through which real strength arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4585.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram sends Aṅgada to speak before the enemy. Aṅgada first bows to Ram's feet, then rises with confidence. The verse shows that his courage and worth come from surrender, not ego.
ramacharitamanas::4585.modern_relevance: You walk into a hard conversation after quietly reminding yourself who you answer to. The steadiness you feel is not self-importance — it's the relief of being aligned with something higher.
ramacharitamanas::4585.insight: It shifts confidence from self-display to grace-filled service.

ramacharitamanas::4586.verse_sanskrit: स्वयंसिद्ध सब काज नाथ मोहि आदरु दियउ। अस बिचारि जुबराज तन पुलकित हरषित हियउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4586.verse_hindi: स्वामी सब कार्य अपने-आप सिद्ध हैं, यह तो प्रभु ने मुझ को आदर दिया है (जो मुझे अपने कार्य पर भेज रहे हैं)। ऐसा विचार कर युवराज अंगद का हृदय हर्षित और शरीर पुलकित हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4586.english_translation: All tasks are already self-succeeded, Lord. Thinking this, the prince's heart thrilled and his body shivered with joy.
ramacharitamanas::4586.translation_literal: स्वयंसिद्ध (self-succeeded) / सब (all) / काज (tasks) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (me) / आदरु (honor) / दियउ (gave) / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / जुबराज (prince) / तन (body) / पुलकित (goosebumped) / हरषित (joyful) / हियउ (heart)
ramacharitamanas::4586.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4586.essence: True service feels like being trusted, not being burdened.
ramacharitamanas::4586.simple_meaning: Angad feels honored, not burdened. He sees the mission as already blessed and takes it as a sign of trust.
ramacharitamanas::4586.simple_insight: When service feels like honor, the heart becomes light and fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4586.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has been sent to face Ravana's court. After hearing Ram's message, he does not feel pressure or pride. He feels chosen. That shift turns duty into joy before he even moves.
ramacharitamanas::4586.modern_relevance: You get assigned the difficult presentation and stop seeing it as a test of your worth. The moment you treat it as trust, your body relaxes and your mind sharpens.
ramacharitamanas::4586.insight: It shifts you from self-conscious performance to joyful service.

ramacharitamanas::4587.verse_sanskrit: बंदि चरन उर धरि प्रभुताई। अंगद चलेउ सबहि सिरु नाई॥ प्रभु प्रताप उर सहज असंका। रन बाँकुरा बालिसुत बंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4587.verse_hindi: चरणों की वंदना करके और भगवान् की प्रभुता हृदय में धरकर अंगद सबको सिर नवाकर चले। प्रभु के प्रताप को हृदय में धारण किए हुए रणबाँकुरे वीर बालिपुत्र स्वाभाविक ही निर्भय हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4587.english_translation: Bowing to the feet and holding the Lord's majesty in his heart, Angad departed, bowing to everyone. With the Lord's glory in his heart, the brave son of Bali is naturally fearless in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4587.translation_literal: बंदि (bowing) / चरन (feet) / उर (in the heart) / धरि (holding) / प्रभुताई (lordship, majesty) / अंगद (Angad) / चलेउ (departed) / सबहि (to everyone) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रताप (glory, power) / उर (in the heart) / सहज (natural) / असंका (fearlessness, doubtlessness) / रन (battle) / बाँकुरा (brave) / बालिसुत (son of Bali) / बंका (valiant, bold)
ramacharitamanas::4587.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4587.essence: True fearlessness comes from carrying the Lord's glory within.
ramacharitamanas::4587.simple_meaning: Angad leaves with respect for everyone, but his heart stays steady because he trusts the Lord's power. That trust makes him naturally fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4587.simple_insight: Respect does not weaken courage; devotion can make you steady in the middle of danger.
ramacharitamanas::4587.detailed_meaning: Angad has just received Ram's command and rises with joy. He bows, accepts Ram's authority in his heart, and walks out to face Lanka. The verse highlights the calm fearlessness that comes from carrying Ram's glory inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::4587.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, knowing a hard conversation is coming. Your voice stays steady because you are anchored in something deeper than the reaction you might get.
ramacharitamanas::4587.insight: It shifts courage from personal toughness to inward trust in Ram's power.

ramacharitamanas::4588.verse_sanskrit: पुर पैठत रावन कर बेटा। खेलत रहा सो होइ गै भेंटा॥ बातहिं बात करष बढ़ि आई। जुगल अतुल बल पुनि तरुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4588.verse_hindi: लंका में प्रवेश करते ही रावण के पुत्र से भेंट हो गई, जो वहाँ खेल रहा था। बातों ही बातों में दोनों में झगड़ा बढ़ गया (क्योंकि) दोनों ही अतुलनीय बलवान् थे और फिर दोनों की युवावस्था थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4588.english_translation: As Angad entered Lanka, he met Ravana's son, who was playing there. In talk after talk, the quarrel grew, because both were unmatched in strength and both were young.
ramacharitamanas::4588.translation_literal: पुर (city) / पैठत (entering) / रावन (Ravana) / कर (of) / बेटा (son) / खेलत (playing) / रहा (was) / सो (that one) / होइ (became) / गै (went) / भेंटा (meeting) / बातहिं बात (talk after talk) / करष (quarrel) / बढ़ि (grew) / आई (came) / जुगल (both) / अतुल (matchless) / बल (strength) / पुनि (again) / तरुनाई (youth)
ramacharitamanas::4588.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4588.essence: A small meeting turns fierce when pride and strength meet.
ramacharitamanas::4588.simple_meaning: Angad runs into Ravana's son in Lanka, and a small exchange quickly turns into a fight because both are young and powerful.
ramacharitamanas::4588.simple_insight: Pride and youth can turn a passing encounter into conflict in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4588.detailed_meaning: Angad has just entered Lanka on Ram's mission. Before the larger clash begins, he meets Ravana's son at play, and casual words quickly harden into rivalry. The verse sets up the coming physical confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::4588.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering already tense, and one careless remark from a young cousin turns the whole room sharp. Sometimes strength and ego need only a spark.
ramacharitamanas::4588.insight: It shows how quickly unguarded pride can escalate a simple encounter into conflict.

ramacharitamanas::4589.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं अंगद कहुँ लात उठाई। गहि पद पटकेउ भूमि भवाँई॥ निसिचर निकर देखि भट भारी। जहँ तहँ चले न सकहिं पुकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4589.verse_hindi: उसने अंगद पर लात उठाई। अंगद ने (वही) पैर पकड़कर उसे घुमाकर जमीन पर दे पटका (मार गिराया)। राक्षस के समूह भारी योद्धा देखकर जहाँ-तहाँ (भाग) चले, वे डर के मारे पुकार भी न मचा सके ॥
ramacharitamanas::4589.english_translation: He kicked Angad, and Angad seized his foot, whirled him around, and slammed him to the ground. Seeing the great warrior among the demon host, they scattered everywhere and could not even cry out.
ramacharitamanas::4589.translation_literal: तेहिं (then/he) / अंगद (Angad) / कहुँ (at) / लात (kick) / उठाई (raised) / गहि (seizing) / पद (foot) / पटकेउ (threw down) / भूमि (on the ground) / भवाँई (whirled around) / निसिचर (demon) / निकर (group) / देखि (seeing) / भट (warrior) / भारी (great) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / चले (ran) / न सकहिं (could not) / पुकारी (cry out)
ramacharitamanas::4589.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4589.essence: True strength turns aggression back on itself.
ramacharitamanas::4589.simple_meaning: He attacks Angad, but Angad turns the move back and throws him down. The enemy troops panic and flee in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::4589.simple_insight: Real strength can make an aggressor lose control in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4589.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just entered as Ram's envoy and challenger. A demon prince tries to strike him with a kick, but Angad catches the foot and hurls him down. The sight of Angad's force sends the enemy troops into panic.
ramacharitamanas::4589.modern_relevance: A bully lunges in front of a crowd, expecting fear. Instead, the calm response knocks the whole room off balance and the noise dies instantly.
ramacharitamanas::4589.insight: It shows how steady force can reverse intimidation and break collective panic.

ramacharitamanas::4590.verse_sanskrit: एक एक सन मरमु न कहहीं। समुझि तासु बध चुप करि रहहीं॥ भयउ कोलाहल नगर मझारी। आवा कपि लंका जेहिं जारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4590.verse_hindi: एक-दूसरे को मर्म (असली बात) नहीं बतलाते, उस (रावण के पुत्र) का वध समझकर सब चुप मारकर रह जाते हैं। (रावण पुत्र की मृत्यु जानकर और राक्षसों को भय के मारे भागते देखकर) नगरभर में कोलाहल मच गया कि जिसने लंका जलाई थी, वही वानर फिर आ गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4590.english_translation: No one tells the others the real matter. Thinking him already slain, they fall silent. Then the city erupts in uproar: the monkey who burned Lanka has come again.
ramacharitamanas::4590.translation_literal: एक एक (one another) / सन (to) / मरमु (the real matter) / न (not) / कहहीं (tell) / समुझि (thinking/understanding) / तासु (his) / बध (killing) / चुप (silent) / करि (having made) / रहहीं (remain)॥ / भयउ (became) / कोलाहल (uproar) / नगर (city) / मझारी (in the middle) / आवा (came) / कपि (monkey) / लंका (Lanka) / जेहिं (who) / जारी (burned) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4590.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4590.essence: Fear fills silence with its own story.
ramacharitamanas::4590.simple_meaning: The enemies stay quiet, thinking the young warrior has been killed. Then panic spreads through Lanka when they realize the same monkey has returned.
ramacharitamanas::4590.simple_insight: Fear makes people misread events and spread panic before they understand what happened.
ramacharitamanas::4590.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just overwhelmed Ravana's son. The frightened warriors do not even speak plainly to one another. Before the truth settles, the whole city is in uproar, convinced the same monkey who burned Lanka has returned.
ramacharitamanas::4590.modern_relevance: A group chat goes silent after one bad screenshot, then rumors explode before anyone checks the facts. Panic fills the gap where clear seeing should have been.
ramacharitamanas::4590.insight: It shows how fear turns partial information into collective confusion.

ramacharitamanas::4591.verse_sanskrit: अब धौं कहा करिहि करतारा। अति सभीत सब करहिं बिचारा॥ बिनु पूछें मगु देहिं दिखाई। जेहि बिलोक सोइ जाइ सुखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4591.verse_hindi: सब अत्यंत भयभीत होकर विचार करने लगे कि विधाता अब न जाने क्या करेगा। वे बिना पूछे ही अंगद को (रावण के दरबार की) राह बता देते हैं। जिसे ही वे देखते हैं, वही डर के मारे सूख जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4591.english_translation: All were utterly frightened, wondering what fate would do next. Without even asking, they showed Angad the way. Whoever saw him withers in fear.
ramacharitamanas::4591.translation_literal: अब धौं (now) / कहा (what) / करिहि (will do) / करतारा (the maker) / अति (very) / सभीत (frightened) / सब (all) / करहिं (do) / बिचारा (reflection)॥ / बिनु (without) / पूछें (asking) / मगु (path/way) / देहिं (give) / दिखाई (showing) / जेहि (whom) / बिलोक (seeing) / सोइ (that very one) / जाइ (goes) / सुखाई (withers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4591.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4591.essence: Fear makes even enemies hand over the path.
ramacharitamanas::4591.simple_meaning: Everyone is so frightened that they stop thinking clearly and even point out the way without being asked. Angad's presence alone makes people lose courage.
ramacharitamanas::4591.simple_insight: Fear can make people reveal what they would normally hide.
ramacharitamanas::4591.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Angad has shaken Ravana's court, the demons are stunned. They whisper among themselves, terrified of what will happen next, and even give him directions without resistance. The verse shows how completely Angad's courage has unsettled the enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4591.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, and the people who planned to corner you suddenly soften. Sometimes calm courage changes the whole atmosphere before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4591.insight: It shifts attention from force to presence: steady courage can disarm fear without a fight.

ramacharitamanas::4592.verse_sanskrit: गयउ सभा दरबार तब सुमिरि राम पद कंज। सिंह ठवनि इत उत चितव धीर बीर बल पुंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4592.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों का स्मरण करके अंगद रावण की सभा के द्वार पर गए और वे धीर, वीर और बल की राशि अंगद सिंह की सी ऐंड़ (शान) से इधर-उधर देखने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4592.english_translation: Then Angad went to the court, remembering Ram's lotus feet. Like a lion, steady and brave, he looked all around, a mass of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4592.translation_literal: गयउ (went) / सभा दरबार (court assembly) / तब (then) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम पद कंज (Ram's lotus feet) / सिंह ठवनि (with lion-like stance) / इत उत (here and there) / चितव (looked) / धीर (steady) / बीर (brave) / बल पुंज (a mass of strength)
ramacharitamanas::4592.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4592.essence: Remembering Ram makes Angad fearless in enemy territory.
ramacharitamanas::4592.simple_meaning: Angad enters Ravana's court with Ram in mind, calm and fearless. His presence itself shows courage and strength.
ramacharitamanas::4592.simple_insight: Real courage can look like calmness when the pressure is highest.
ramacharitamanas::4592.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad reaches Ravana's court after the monkeys fear what will happen next. He does not enter shaken or pleading. Remembering Ram, he stands like a lion, scanning the hall with steady strength.
ramacharitamanas::4592.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting where everyone expects you to fold. Instead, you breathe, hold your ground, and let calm confidence speak first.
ramacharitamanas::4592.insight: It shows that remembrance can steady the body and sharpen presence under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4593.verse_sanskrit: तुरत निसाचर एक पठावा। समाचार रावनहि जनावा॥ सुनत बिहँसि बोला दससीसा। आनहु बोलि कहाँ कर कीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4593.verse_hindi: तुरंत ही उन्होंने एक राक्षस को भेजा और रावण को अपने आने का समाचार सूचित किया। सुनते ही रावण हँसकर बोला- बुला लाओ, (देखें) कहाँ का बंदर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4593.english_translation: At once a demon was sent to inform Ravana. Hearing it, Ravana laughed and said, "Bring him here. Let us see what kind of monkey he is."
ramacharitamanas::4593.translation_literal: तुरत (at once) / निसाचर (demon) / एक (one) / पठावा (was sent) / समाचार (news) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / जनावा (was made known) // सुनत (hearing) / बिहँसि (laughing) / बोला (spoke) / दससीसा (ten-headed one, Ravana) / आनहु (bring [him]) / बोलि (calling) / कहाँ (where) / कर (of) / कीसा (monkey)
ramacharitamanas::4593.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4593.essence: Pride laughs first, even when danger is already at the door.
ramacharitamanas::4593.simple_meaning: A messenger rushes to Ravana with the news. Ravana laughs and dismisses Angad, mocking him as just a monkey.
ramacharitamanas::4593.simple_insight: Pride makes a person laugh at what could humble him.
ramacharitamanas::4593.detailed_meaning: Angad has come to Ravana's court as Ram's envoy, and the atmosphere is tense. A demon rushes to report the arrival. Ravana responds with laughter and contempt, exposing the arrogance that still blinds him before the real confrontation begins.
ramacharitamanas::4593.modern_relevance: You get the text that a difficult conversation is waiting in the next room, and you laugh it off to feel bigger. That joke can be the first sign you're already losing.
ramacharitamanas::4593.insight: It shows how ego reacts to danger with mockery instead of clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4594.verse_sanskrit: आयसु पाइ दूत बहु धाए। कपिकुंजरहि बोलि लै आए॥ अंगद दीख दसानन बैसें। सहित प्रान कज्जलगिरि जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4594.verse_hindi: आज्ञा पाकर बहुत से दूत दौड़े और वानरों में हाथी के समान अंगद को बुला लाए। अंगद ने रावण को ऐसे बैठे हुए देखा, जैसे कोई प्राणयुक्त (सजीव) काजल का पहाड़ हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4594.english_translation: At his command, many messengers ran and brought Angad, the monkey-chief. Angad saw Ravana seated there, like a living mountain of black collyrium.
ramacharitamanas::4594.translation_literal: आयसु (command) / पाइ (having received) / दूत (messengers) / बहु (many) / धाए (ran) / कपिकुंजरहि (the monkey-elephant, Angad) / बोलि (calling) / लै (taking) / आए (brought) / अंगद (Angad) / दीख (saw) / दसानन (the ten-faced one, Ravana) / बैसें (seated) / सहित (with) / प्रान (life) / कज्जलगिरि (mountain of collyrium) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::4594.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4594.essence: The confrontation begins with a charged first look.
ramacharitamanas::4594.simple_meaning: Ravana's messengers hurry to bring Angad before him, and Angad sees the king of Lanka sitting there like a dark, living mountain.
ramacharitamanas::4594.simple_insight: The scene is set for confrontation: one side rushes, the other sits in pride.
ramacharitamanas::4594.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, the messengers bring Angad forward after receiving orders. Angad looks at Ravana seated before him, and the verse pauses on the tense visual contrast before the challenge begins.
ramacharitamanas::4594.insight: It frames the meeting as a face-off, not a conversation, and builds tension before the exchange.

ramacharitamanas::4595.verse_sanskrit: भुजा बिटप सिर सृंग समाना। रोमावली लता जनु नाना॥ मुख नासिका नयन अरु काना। गिरि कंदरा खोह अनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4595.verse_hindi: भुजाएँ वृक्षों के और सिर पर्वतों के शिखरों के समान हैं। रोमावली मानो बहुत सी लताएँ हैं। मुँह, नाक, नेत्र और कान पर्वत की कन्दराओं और खोहों के बराबर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4595.english_translation: His arms were like tree trunks and his head like mountain peaks. His body hair was like many creeping vines. His mouth, nose, eyes, and ears were like mountain caves and hollows.
ramacharitamanas::4595.translation_literal: भुजा (arms) / बिटप (tree) / सिर (head) / सृंग (peak) / समाना (like) / रोमावली (body hair) / लता (creeper) / जनु (as if) / नाना (many) / मुख (mouth) / नासिका (nose) / नयन (eyes) / अरु (and) / काना (ears) / गिरि (mountain) / कंदरा (cave) / खोह (hollow) / अनुमान (comparison)
ramacharitamanas::4595.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4595.essence: Angad's body is described as a living mountain to magnify his presence.
ramacharitamanas::4595.simple_meaning: Angad's huge body is described through mountain-and-forest imagery to show his enormous, awe-inspiring form.
ramacharitamanas::4595.simple_insight: Some presences are so large they change the whole room before they speak.
ramacharitamanas::4595.detailed_meaning: Angad has entered Ravana's सभा in Lanka. Before he even speaks, the poet pauses to paint his body as a landscape of trees, peaks, vines, caves, and hollows. The image builds his intimidating presence for the confrontation ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4595.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and everyone notices before you open your mouth. The room reads your presence first, your words second.
ramacharitamanas::4595.insight: It shifts attention from speech to embodied presence: how you enter a space can carry force before you say anything.

ramacharitamanas::4596.verse_sanskrit: गयउ सभाँ मन नेकु न मुरा। बालितनय अतिबल बाँकुरा॥ उठे सभासद कपि कहुँ देखी। रावन उर भा क्रोध बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4596.verse_hindi: अत्यंत बलवान् बाँके वीर बालिपुत्र अंगद सभा में गए, वे मन में जरा भी नहीं झिझके। अंगद को देखते ही सब सभासद् उठ खड़े हुए। यह देखकर रावण के हृदय में बड़ा क्रोध हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4596.english_translation: Angad entered the assembly without the slightest hesitation. When the courtiers saw the mighty son of Bali, they rose to their feet. Ravana's heart filled with intense anger.
ramacharitamanas::4596.translation_literal: गयउ (went) / सभाँ (into the assembly) / मन (mind) / नेकु (not even a little) / न (not) / मुरा (wavered) / बालितनय (son of Bali) / अतिबल (very powerful) / बाँकुरा (brave and upright) ॥ / उठे (rose) / सभासद (members of the assembly) / कपि (monkey) / कहुँ (for) / देखी (seeing) / रावन (Ravana) / उर (in heart) / भा (became) / क्रोध (anger) / बिसेषी (great) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4596.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4596.essence: Steady courage can shake a room before any speech begins.
ramacharitamanas::4596.simple_meaning: Angad walks into Ravana's court without fear. The courtiers stand up when they see him, and Ravana burns with anger.
ramacharitamanas::4596.simple_insight: Courage changes the room before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4596.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad enters Ravana's assembly as an envoy from Ram. The courtiers rise at his presence, but this is still only the opening shock of the meeting. The verse shows the tension before the real challenge begins.
ramacharitamanas::4596.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and say nothing yet. Still, everyone notices your steadiness before you open your mouth.
ramacharitamanas::4596.insight: It shows how fearless presence can unsettle pride and command attention without force.

ramacharitamanas::4597.verse_sanskrit: जथा मत्त गज जूथ महुँ पंचानन चलि जाइ। राम प्रताप सुमिरि मन बैठ सभाँ सिरु नाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4597.verse_hindi: जैसे मतवाले हाथियों के झुंड में सिंह (निःशंक होकर) चला जाता है, वैसे ही श्री रामजी के प्रताप का हृदय में स्मरण करके वे (निर्भय) सभा में सिर नवाकर बैठ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4597.english_translation: Like a lion walking into a herd of drunk elephants, he entered the assembly without fear, remembering Ram's power in his heart and bowing before sitting down.
ramacharitamanas::4597.translation_literal: जथा (as) / मत्त (intoxicated) / गज (elephants) / जूथ (herd) / महुँ (in) / पंचानन (lion) / चलि (walking) / जाइ (goes) / राम (Ram) / प्रताप (power, glory) / सुमिरि (remembering) / मन (mind) / बैठ (sat) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::4597.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4597.essence: Remember Ram, and fear cannot rule you.
ramacharitamanas::4597.simple_meaning: Remembering Ram's power, Angad entered a hostile assembly with complete fearlessness and sat down respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::4597.simple_insight: Real courage comes from remembering something greater than the room in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4597.detailed_meaning: Angad has just walked into Ravana's court, where every eye is hostile. Instead of shrinking, he remembers Ram's power, bows, and sits down with fearless dignity. The verse shows how devotion turns danger into composure.
ramacharitamanas::4597.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is judging you, and your chest tightens. Then you remember who stands behind your work, your word, your values — and your body settles.
ramacharitamanas::4597.insight: It shifts courage from self-confidence to remembrance of a higher support.

ramacharitamanas::4598.verse_sanskrit: कह दसकंठ कवन तैं बंदर। मैं रघुबीर दूत दसकंधर॥ मम जनकहि तोहि रही मिताई। तव हित कारन आयउँ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4598.verse_hindi: रावण ने कहा- अरे बंदर! तू कौन है? (अंगद ने कहा-) हे दशग्रीव! मैं श्री रघुवीर का दूत हूँ। मेरे पिता से और तुमसे मित्रता थी, इसलिए हे भाई! मैं तुम्हारी भलाई के लिए ही आया हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4598.english_translation: Ravana said, “Hey monkey, who are you? I am the messenger of the mighty Raghu lord, O ten-headed one. My father and you were once friends, so I have come for your good, brother.”
ramacharitamanas::4598.translation_literal: कह (said) / दसकंठ (ten-necked one, Ravana) / कवन (who) / तैं (you) / बंदर (monkey) / मैं (I) / रघुबीर (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / दूत (messenger) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / मम (my) / जनकहि (father) / तोहि (you) / रही (was) / मिताई (friendship) / तव (your) / हित (good) / कारन (for the reason) / आयउँ (I came) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::4598.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4598.essence: True courage can challenge someone without losing goodwill.
ramacharitamanas::4598.simple_meaning: Angad answers Ravana boldly: he is Ram’s messenger, and he has come for Ravana’s own good, not to insult him.
ramacharitamanas::4598.detailed_meaning: In Ravana’s court, Angad stands alone before the enemy king and refuses to shrink. Ravana mocks him as a monkey, but Angad answers as Ram’s envoy, reminding Ravana of old friendship and saying he has come only for Ravana’s welfare.
ramacharitamanas::4598.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room where everyone expects you to back down. Instead, you speak firmly, without venom, because honesty can still be kind.
ramacharitamanas::4598.insight: It teaches you to hold your ground while keeping your intention clean.

ramacharitamanas::4599.verse_sanskrit: उत्तम कुल पुलस्ति कर नाती। सिव बिंरचि पूजेहु बहु भाँती॥ बर पायहु कीन्हेहु सब काजा। जीतेहु लोकपाल सब राजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4599.verse_hindi: तुम्हारा उत्तम कुल है, पुलस्त्य ऋषि के तुम पौत्र हो। शिवजी की और ब्रह्माजी की तुमने बहुत प्रकार से पूजा की है। उनसे वर पाए हैं और सब काम सिद्ध किए हैं। लोकपालों और सब राजाओं को तुमने जीत लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4599.english_translation: You are from an excellent lineage, grandson of Pulastya. You have worshipped Shiva and Brahma in many ways. You have received boons and accomplished all tasks. You have conquered the guardians of the worlds and all kings.
ramacharitamanas::4599.translation_literal: उत्तम (excellent) / कुल (lineage) / पुलस्ति (Pulastya) / कर (of) / नाती (grandson) / सिव (Shiva) / बिंरचि (Brahma) / पूजेहु (you worshipped) / बहु भाँती (in many ways) / बर (boons) / पायहु (you obtained) / कीन्हेहु (you did) / सब (all) / काजा (tasks) / जीतेहु (you conquered) / लोकपाल (guardians of the worlds) / सब (all) / राजा (kings)
ramacharitamanas::4599.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4599.essence: Great power means nothing when it only strengthens ego.
ramacharitamanas::4599.simple_meaning: Ravana is being reminded of his great lineage, devotion, boons, and conquests. The praise is real, but it also sets up the warning that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4599.simple_insight: Achievement feels hollow when it becomes proof of superiority.
ramacharitamanas::4599.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana stands before Angad, still proud after years of conquest. Angad first acknowledges everything Ravana has built: birth, worship, boons, victories. That praise is the opening move before he turns the knife toward Ravana’s arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4599.modern_relevance: You’ve built the company, won the promotion, and collected every sign of status — then one honest conversation shows how brittle the ego still is.
ramacharitamanas::4599.insight: It separates real accomplishment from the mind that clings to it as identity.

ramacharitamanas::4600.verse_sanskrit: नृप अभिमान मोह बस किंबा। हरि आनिहु सीता जगदंबा॥ अब सुभ कहा सुनहु तुम्ह मोरा। सब अपराध छमिहि प्रभु तोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4600.verse_hindi: राजमद से या मोहवश तुम जगज्जननी सीताजी को हर लाए हो। अब तुम मेरे शुभ वचन (मेरी हितभरी सलाह) सुनो! (उसके अनुसार चलने से) प्रभु श्री रामजी तुम्हारे सब अपराध क्षमा कर देंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4600.english_translation: You may have brought Sita, the mother of the world, here out of pride or confusion. Now hear my good counsel: if you follow it, Lord Ram will forgive all your offenses.
ramacharitamanas::4600.translation_literal: नृप (kingly) / अभिमान (pride) / मोह (delusion) / बस (under the sway of) / किंबा (perhaps) / हरि (Ram) / आनिहु (you brought) / सीता (Sita) / जगदंबा (mother of the world) / अब (now) / सुभ (good) / कहा (speech/counsel) / सुनहु (listen) / तुम्ह (you) / मोरा (my) / सब (all) / अपराध (offenses) / छमिहि (will forgive) / प्रभु (Lord) / तोरा (your)
ramacharitamanas::4600.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4600.essence: Pride can be undone if you are willing to hear the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4600.simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ravana that Sita may have been brought through pride or confusion, but there is still a way back: listen to good counsel, and Ram will forgive everything.
ramacharitamanas::4600.simple_insight: Even after grave wrongdoing, the door to mercy is not closed if you are willing to listen.
ramacharitamanas::4600.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana speaks to Ravana after the theft of Sita. He does not flatter him; he names the pride and confusion behind the act, then offers a path back. This moment turns from accusation to mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4600.modern_relevance: You know that moment after a terrible argument when your chest is tight and your phone is in your hand. One honest conversation, one willingness to listen, can still change what happens next.
ramacharitamanas::4600.insight: It shifts the mind from defensiveness to receptivity, showing that correction and forgiveness begin with listening.

ramacharitamanas::4601.verse_sanskrit: दसन गहहु तृन कंठ कुठारी। परिजन सहित संग निज नारी॥ सादर जनकसुता करि आगें। एहि बिधि चलहु सकल भय त्यागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4601.verse_hindi: दाँतों में तिनका दबाओ, गले में कुल्हाड़ी डालो और कुटुम्बियों सहित अपनी स्त्रियों को साथ लेकर, आदरपूर्वक जानकीजी को आगे करके, इस प्रकार सब भय छोड़कर चलो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4601.english_translation: Hold a blade of grass in your teeth, a noose at your neck, and come with your family and your women. Place Janak's daughter respectfully in front, and come this way, leaving all fear behind.
ramacharitamanas::4601.translation_literal: दसन (teeth) / गहहु (hold) / तृन (grass) / कंठ (neck) / कुठारी (axe) / परिजन (relatives) / सहित (together with) / संग (along with) / निज (your own) / नारी (women, wives) / सादर (respectfully) / जनकसुता (Janak's daughter) / करि (making) / आगें (in front) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / चलहु (come/walk) / सकल (all) / भय (fear) / त्यागें (having छोड़ा, leaving)
ramacharitamanas::4601.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4601.essence: Fear falls away only when pride is laid down.
ramacharitamanas::4601.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told to abandon pride and fear, bring his family, and approach Sita respectfully as a sign of surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4601.simple_insight: Real strength begins when you stop clinging to pride and meet the moment humbly.
ramacharitamanas::4601.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already been warned that his power and cleverness cannot save him. In this tense exchange, he is told to come with complete humility, bring his household, place Sita respectfully ahead, and drop all fear. The scene pushes him toward surrender before ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4601.modern_relevance: After a bitter argument, you finally send the message you should have sent hours ago: no excuses, no posturing, just honesty. The first real step is dropping the armor.
ramacharitamanas::4601.insight: It teaches you to replace defensiveness with humility before conflict hardens into damage.

ramacharitamanas::4602.verse_sanskrit: प्रनतपाल रघुबंसमनि त्राहि त्राहि अब मोहि। आरत गिरा सुनत प्रभु अभय करेंगे तोहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4602.verse_hindi: और 'हे शरणागत के पालन करने वाले रघुवंश शिरोमणि श्री रामजी! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए।' (इस प्रकार आर्त प्रार्थना करो।) आर्त पुकार सुनते ही प्रभु तुमको निर्भय कर देंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4602.english_translation: Call out, 'O Ram, jewel of the Raghu line, protector of those who seek refuge, save me, save me.' Hearing a cry of distress, the Lord will make you fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4602.translation_literal: प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / त्राहि त्राहि (save, save) / अब (now) / मोहि (me) / आरत (distressed) / गिरा (cry/voice) / सुनत (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अभय (fearless) / करेंगे (will make) / तोहि (you)
ramacharitamanas::4602.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4602.essence: Fear loosens when you call on Ram without pretence.
ramacharitamanas::4602.simple_meaning: Call on Ram from a place of need, and he answers by removing fear.
ramacharitamanas::4602.simple_insight: You do not need polished words to be held; honest distress is enough.
ramacharitamanas::4602.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is speaking in Lanka, facing Ravana's pride and threat. He teaches that the right answer to danger is not cleverness, but a direct cry to Ram, the protector of those who seek refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4602.modern_relevance: Your hands shake before the difficult phone call, and you cannot find the perfect words. Say the honest sentence anyway. This verse says that raw need can become courage.
ramacharitamanas::4602.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to direct refuge, trusting that sincere calling changes your inner state.

ramacharitamanas::4603.verse_sanskrit: रे कपिपोत बोलु संभारी। मूढ़ न जानेहि मोहि सुरारी॥ कहु निज नाम जनक कर भाई। केहि नातें मानिऐ मिताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4603.verse_hindi: (रावण ने कहा-) अरे बंदर के बच्चे! सँभालकर बोल! मूर्ख! मुझ देवताओं के शत्रु को तूने जाना नहीं? अरे भाई! अपना और अपने बाप का नाम तो बता। किस नाते से मित्रता मानता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4603.english_translation: Ravana said, “Hey, monkey cub, speak carefully. Fool, you do not know me, enemy of the radiant beings. Tell me your own name and your father’s name. On what basis do you claim friendship?”
ramacharitamanas::4603.translation_literal: रे (hey) / कपिपोत (monkey cub) / बोलु (speak) / संभारी (carefully) / मूढ़ (fool) / न (not) / जानेहि (you know) / मोहि (me) / सुरारी (enemy of the radiant beings) / कहु (tell) / निज (your own) / नाम (name) / जनक (father) / कर (of) / भाई (brother) / केहि (by what) / नातें (relation) / मानिऐ (is claimed) / मिताई (friendship)
ramacharitamanas::4603.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4603.essence: Pride cannot hear truth without first demanding rank.
ramacharitamanas::4603.simple_meaning: Ravana insults Angad, demands to know who he is, and challenges the basis for calling him a friend.
ramacharitamanas::4603.simple_insight: Pride always wants identity, rank, and proof before it will listen.
ramacharitamanas::4603.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has entered Ravana’s court as a messenger from Ram. Ravana responds with contempt, mocking his youth and demanding his name and lineage. The scene shows Ravana’s ego refusing to meet an envoy with humility.
ramacharitamanas::4603.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting and asks, with a smirk, “And who exactly are you to speak?” The need to dominate the room is louder than the words.
ramacharitamanas::4603.insight: It reveals how ego reduces every encounter to status and bloodline instead of listening to the message.

ramacharitamanas::4604.verse_sanskrit: अंगद नाम बालि कर बेटा। तासों कबहुँ भई ही भेंटा॥ अंगद बचन सुनत सकुचाना। रहा बालि बानर मैं जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4604.verse_hindi: (अंगद ने कहा-) मेरा नाम अंगद है, मैं बालि का पुत्र हूँ। उनसे कभी तुम्हारी भेंट हुई थी? अंगद का वचन सुनते ही रावण कुछ सकुचा गया (और बोला-) हाँ, मैं जान गया (मुझे याद आ गया), बालि नाम का एक बंदर था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4604.english_translation: Angad said, “My name is Angad. I am Bali’s son. Have you ever met him?” Hearing Angad’s words, Ravana became uneasy and said, “Yes, I remember now—there was a monkey named Bali.”
ramacharitamanas::4604.translation_literal: अंगद (Angad) / नाम (name) / बालि कर बेटा (Bali's son) / तासों (with him) / कबहुँ (ever) / भई (was) / ही भेंटा (meeting)॥ / अंगद बचन (Angad's words) / सुनत (hearing) / सकुचाना (became uneasy/hesitant) / रहा (remained) / बालि बानर (Bali, the monkey) / मैं जाना (I remembered / I came to know)॥
ramacharitamanas::4604.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4604.essence: A true name can shake pride before a single blow is struck.
ramacharitamanas::4604.simple_meaning: Angad identifies himself as Bali’s son, and Ravana is startled into remembering Bali. The verse is a step in the larger exchange, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4604.simple_insight: Even a calm introduction can unsettle pride when it carries real lineage and memory.
ramacharitamanas::4604.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana as a messenger from Ram’s side. He names himself as Bali’s son and asks whether Ravana ever met Bali. The mention jolts Ravana into uneasy recognition, setting up the sharper challenge that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4604.modern_relevance: You introduce yourself in a room where someone expected weakness, and suddenly their confidence shifts. A single name can carry the weight of history.
ramacharitamanas::4604.insight: It shows how identity and memory can puncture arrogance before any argument begins.

ramacharitamanas::4605.verse_sanskrit: अंगद तहीं बालि कर बालक। उपजेहु बंस अनल कुल घालक॥ गर्भ न गयहु ब्यर्थ तुम्ह जायहु। निज मुख तापस दूत कहायहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4605.verse_hindi: अरे अंगद! तू ही बालि का लड़का है? अरे कुलनाशक! तू तो अपने कुलरूपी बाँस के लिए अग्नि रूप ही पैदा हुआ! गर्भ में ही क्यों न नष्ट हो गया तू? व्यर्थ ही पैदा हुआ जो अपने ही मुँह से तपस्वियों का दूत कहलाया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4605.english_translation: Are you Angad, Bali's son? O destroyer of your own line, you were born like fire for the bamboo of your clan. Why were you not lost in the womb? You were born in vain if you call yourself a messenger with your own mouth.
ramacharitamanas::4605.translation_literal: अंगद (Angad) / तहीं (you indeed) / बालि (Bali) / कर (of) / बालक (son) / उपजेहु (you were born) / बंस (lineage) / अनल (fire) / कुल (clan) / घालक (destroyer) / गर्भ (womb) / न (not) / गयहु (you went) / ब्यर्थ (wasted) / तुम्ह (you) / जायहु (were born) / निज (your own) / मुख (mouth) / तापस (ascetic) / दूत (messenger) / कहायहु (you called yourself)
ramacharitamanas::4605.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4605.essence: Ravana's insult exposes his own fear, not Angad's weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4605.simple_meaning: Ravana insults Angad, calling him a useless destroyer of his own family and mocking his role as a messenger.
ramacharitamanas::4605.simple_insight: Pride often turns into abuse when it feels challenged.
ramacharitamanas::4605.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana as a messenger from Ram. Ravana, stung by Angad's fearless speech, lashes out with family insults and contempt. The verse is part of that escalating confrontation, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4605.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a heated meeting and starts attacking your family, background, and motives instead of answering the point. The insult reveals their panic more than your worth.
ramacharitamanas::4605.insight: It shows how wounded ego tries to regain control by humiliating the other person.

ramacharitamanas::4606.verse_sanskrit: अब कहु कुसल बालि कहँ अहई। बिहँसि बचन तब अंगद कहई॥ दिन दस गएँ बालि पहिं जाई। बूझेहु कुसल सखा उर लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4606.verse_hindi: अब बालि की कुशल तो बता, वह (आजकल) कहाँ है? तब अंगद ने हँसकर कहा- दस (कुछ) दिन बीतने पर (स्वयं ही) बालि के पास जाकर, अपने मित्र को हृदय से लगाकर, उसी से कुशल पूछ लेना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4606.english_translation: Now tell me, how is Bali doing? Where is he? Angad then said with a smile, "Go to Bali yourself after ten days, hold your friend close to your heart, and ask him about his welfare."
ramacharitamanas::4606.translation_literal: अब (now) / कहु (tell) / कुसल (well-being) / बालि (Bali) / कहँ (where) / अहई (is) / बिहँसि (smiling) / बचन (words) / तब (then) / अंगद (Angad) / कहई (said) / दिन (days) / दस (ten) / गएँ (after passing) / बालि (Bali) / पहिं (to) / जाई (go) / बूझेहु (ask) / कुसल (well-being) / सखा (friend) / उर (heart) / लाई (placing)
ramacharitamanas::4606.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4606.essence: A calm reply can turn pride back on itself.
ramacharitamanas::4606.simple_meaning: Angad answers Ravana with sharp irony: if you want to know how Bali is, go ask him yourself in the next world.
ramacharitamanas::4606.simple_insight: Mockery can expose fear more sharply than argument.
ramacharitamanas::4606.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana after exposing his lineage and strength. Ravana tries to probe Bali's condition, but Angad turns the question back on him with a smile, implying Bali is no longer among the living and that Ravana will soon know the same fate.
ramacharitamanas::4606.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with a smug question, expecting you to shrink. You smile, answer indirectly, and make them feel the weight of their own words.
ramacharitamanas::4606.insight: It shows how fearless speech can dismantle arrogance without losing composure.

ramacharitamanas::4607.verse_sanskrit: राम बिरोध कुसल जसि होई। सो सब तोहि सुनाइहि सोई॥ सुनु सठ भेद होइ मन ताकें। श्री रघुबीर हृदय नहिं जाकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4607.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी से विरोध करने पर जैसी कुशल होती है, वह सब तुमको वे सुनावेंगे। हे मूर्ख! सुन, भेद उसी के मन में पड़ सकता है, (भेद नीति उसी पर अपना प्रभाव डाल सकती है) जिसके हृदय में श्री रघुवीर न हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4607.english_translation: The good that comes from opposing Ram — Angad will tell you that. Listen, fool: only a heart without Shri Raghubir can be split by deceit.
ramacharitamanas::4607.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिरोध (opposition) / कुसल (good fortune) / जसि (as) / होई (happens) / सो (that) / सब (all) / तोहि (to you) / सुनाइहि (will tell) / सोई (that only) ॥ / सुनु (listen) / सठ (fool) / भेद (division / deceit) / होइ (happens) / मन (mind) / ताकें (in that) / श्री रघुबीर (Shri Raghubir) / हृदय (heart) / नहिं (not) / जाकें (in which) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4607.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4607.essence: A heart anchored in Ram cannot be broken by deceit.
ramacharitamanas::4607.simple_meaning: Turning against Ram leaves you vulnerable to confusion and ruin. A heart that holds Ram cannot be split by trickery.
ramacharitamanas::4607.simple_insight: What protects you is not cleverness, but where your heart is anchored.
ramacharitamanas::4607.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad answers Ravana's taunts without fear. He says the result of opposing Ram will reveal itself, and deceit works only in a heart that lacks Shri Raghubir. This is a sharp warning before the war turns final.
ramacharitamanas::4607.modern_relevance: A group chat starts turning poisonous, and one person keeps feeding the worst interpretation of everything. The verse points to a simple test: when your heart is steady, manipulation loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::4607.insight: It shifts attention from external tricks to the inner condition that lets those tricks work.

ramacharitamanas::4608.verse_sanskrit: हम कुल घालक सत्य तुम्ह कुल पालक दससीस। अंधउ बधिर न अस कहहिं नयन कान तव बीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4608.verse_hindi: सच है, मैं तो कुल का नाश करने वाला हूँ और हे रावण! तुम कुल के रक्षक हो। अंधे-बहरे भी ऐसी बात नहीं कहते, तुम्हारे तो बीस नेत्र और बीस कान हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4608.english_translation: I am the destroyer of my line, and you, Ravana, are the protector of your line. Even the blind and deaf would not say such a thing; you have twenty eyes and twenty ears.
ramacharitamanas::4608.translation_literal: हम (I) / कुल (lineage) / घालक (destroyer) / सत्य (true) / तुम्ह (you) / कुल (lineage) / पालक (protector) / दससीस (ten-headed one, Ravana) / अंधउ (blind) / बधिर (deaf) / न (not) / अस (such) / कहहिं (say) / नयन (eyes) / कान (ears) / तव (your) / बीस (twenty)
ramacharitamanas::4608.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4608.essence: Power without clear seeing becomes self-destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4608.simple_meaning: Hanuman mocks Ravana’s pride: Ravana claims to protect his own family, while Hanuman calls himself the one who will destroy his own line. The point is that Ravana is blind to his own condition.
ramacharitamanas::4608.simple_insight: Pride can leave you fully equipped and still unable to see reality.
ramacharitamanas::4608.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana after being captured. Ravana boasts of power and status, but Hanuman answers with fearless irony, exposing Ravana’s self-deception. The verse cuts through ego by showing that possession of power is not the same as clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::4608.modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting, defending a bad decision because backing down feels humiliating. Everyone can see the flaw except you. This verse captures that dangerous blindness of ego.
ramacharitamanas::4608.insight: It shifts attention from outward capability to inward perception, warning that ego can distort judgment even when the facts are obvious.

ramacharitamanas::4609.verse_sanskrit: सिव बिरंचि सुर मुनि समुदाई। चाहत जासु चरन सेवकाई॥ तासु दूत होइ हम कुल बोरा। अइसिहुँ मति उर बिहर न तोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4609.verse_hindi: शिव, ब्रह्मा (आदि) देवता और मुनियों के समुदाय जिनके चरणों की सेवा (करना) चाहते हैं, उनका दूत होकर मैंने कुल को डुबा दिया? अरे ऐसी बुद्धि होने पर भी तुम्हारा हृदय फट नहीं जाता? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4609.english_translation: Shiva, Brahma, the gods, and the gathered sages long to serve at his feet. Yet I, his messenger, have ruined my own clan? Even with such understanding, does your heart not break?
ramacharitamanas::4609.translation_literal: सिव (Shiva) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / समुदाई (gathered company) / चाहत (desire) / जासु (whose) / चरन (feet) / सेवकाई (service) / तासु (his) / दूत (messenger) / होइ (having become) / हम (I) / कुल (clan) / बोरा (sunk) / अइसिहुँ (even such) / मति (understanding) / उर (heart) / बिहर (split) / न (not) / तोरा (your)
ramacharitamanas::4609.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4609.essence: Pride collapses when it has to answer to reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4609.simple_meaning: Ravana shames himself for becoming the messenger of one who is worshipped by Shiva, Brahma, gods, and sages. He says this should have shattered Ravana's heart.
ramacharitamanas::4609.simple_insight: Pride becomes unbearable when it has to face its own foolishness.
ramacharitamanas::4609.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers the insult with a deeper insult to himself. He names Ram as the one revered by Shiva, Brahma, gods, and sages, then recoils at his own role as that being's messenger. The verse exposes Ravana's wounded pride before the next exchange.
ramacharitamanas::4609.modern_relevance: You bragged all week about being untouchable, then had to admit you were wrong in front of everyone. The shame hurts most when your own words corner you.
ramacharitamanas::4609.insight: It turns humiliation into self-exposure: the real wound is not the insult, but seeing your own arrogance clearly.

ramacharitamanas::4610.verse_sanskrit: सुनि कठोर बानी कपि केरी। कहत दसानन नयन तरेरी॥ खल तव कठिन बचन सब सहऊँ। नीति धर्म मैं जानत अहऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4610.verse_hindi: वानर (अंगद) की कठोर वाणी सुनकर रावण आँखें तरेरकर (तिरछी करके) बोला- अरे दुष्ट! मैं तेरे सब कठोर वचन इसीलिए सह रहा हूँ कि मैं नीति और धर्म को जानता हूँ (उन्हीं की रक्षा कर रहा हूँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4610.english_translation: Hearing the monkey's harsh words, Ravana glared and said, 'Villain, I bear your harsh speech because I know policy and dharma.'
ramacharitamanas::4610.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / कठोर (harsh) / बानी (speech) / कपि (monkey) / केरी (of) / कहत (speaking) / दसानन (Ravana) / नयन (eyes) / तरेरी (glared) / खल (villain) / तव (your) / कठिन (harsh) / बचन (words) / सब (all) / सहऊँ (I bear) / नीति (policy) / धर्म (dharma) / मैं (I) / जानत (know) / अहऊँ (am)
ramacharitamanas::4610.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4610.essence: You can speak of dharma while your pride still leads.
ramacharitamanas::4610.simple_meaning: Ravana claims he can tolerate harsh words because he understands policy and dharma, but his reaction shows his pride is still in control.
ramacharitamanas::4610.simple_insight: Knowing the right words means little if your ego still reacts first.
ramacharitamanas::4610.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just insulted Ravana in front of his court. Ravana answers with anger, yet tries to sound restrained and principled, claiming he understands policy and dharma. The scene exposes the gap between self-image and self-mastery.
ramacharitamanas::4610.modern_relevance: You stay calm in the meeting and say, 'I understand the bigger picture,' while your jaw is tight and your mind is burning. The words may be polished; the reaction tells the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4610.insight: It separates intellectual knowledge from actual self-control, showing that insight must be embodied to matter.

ramacharitamanas::4611.verse_sanskrit: कह कपि धर्मसीलता तोरी। हमहुँ सुनी कृत पर त्रिय चोरी॥ देखी नयन दूत रखवारी। बूड़ि न मरहु धर्म ब्रतधारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4611.verse_hindi: अंगद ने कहा- तुम्हारी धर्मशीलता मैंने भी सुनी है। (वह यह कि) तुमने पराई स्त्री की चोरी की है! और दूत की रक्षा की बात तो अपनी आँखों से देख ली। ऐसे धर्म के व्रत को धारण (पालन) करने वाले तुम डूबकर मर नहीं जाते! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4611.english_translation: Angad said, "I have also heard of your righteousness. You stole another man's wife, and I have seen with my own eyes how you guarded your own messenger. Do not die drowning while claiming to uphold righteousness!"
ramacharitamanas::4611.translation_literal: कह (said) / कपि (monkey) / धर्मसीलता (righteousness) / तोरी (your) / हमहुँ (I also) / सुनी (heard) / कृत (done) / पर (another's) / त्रिय (woman/wife) / चोरी (stealing) / देखी (seen) / नयन (eyes) / दूत (messenger) / रखवारी (guarding) / बूड़ि (drowning) / न (not) / मरहु (die) / धर्म (righteousness) / ब्रतधारी (vow-bearer)
ramacharitamanas::4611.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4611.essence: Your actions expose the truth your pride tries to hide.
ramacharitamanas::4611.simple_meaning: Angad mocks Ravana's claim of righteousness by pointing to his own actions: abducting another man's wife and protecting his messenger. The point is that conduct, not labels, reveals character.
ramacharitamanas::4611.simple_insight: It stings, but it clears the fog: your real character is shown by what you do, not what you call yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4611.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana and turns his own boast back on him. Ravana has spoken of dharma, but Angad points to Sita's abduction and to the way Ravana spared the messenger. The verse strips away false self-image.
ramacharitamanas::4611.modern_relevance: You post about integrity, then cut a corner when no one is watching. Angad's words land because they expose the gap between your self-image and your actual behavior.
ramacharitamanas::4611.insight: It shifts attention from self-description to self-observation, forcing you to measure yourself by action instead of image.

ramacharitamanas::4612.verse_sanskrit: कान नाक बिनु भगिनि निहारी। छमा कीन्हि तुम्ह धर्म बिचारी॥ धर्मसीलता तव जग जागी। पावा दरसु हमहुँ बड़भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4612.verse_hindi: नाक-कान से रहित बहिन को देखकर तुमने धर्म विचारकर ही तो क्षमा कर दिया था! तुम्हारी धर्मशीलता जगजाहिर है। मैं भी बड़ा भाग्यवान् हूँ, जो मैंने तुम्हारा दर्शन पाया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4612.english_translation: Seeing your sister without her nose and ears, you still forgave her after considering dharma. Your devotion to righteousness is famous in the world. I too am fortunate to have seen you.
ramacharitamanas::4612.translation_literal: कान (ears) / नाक (nose) / बिनु (without) / भगिनि (sister) / निहारी (having seen) / छमा (forgiveness) / कीन्हि (you did) / तुम्ह (you) / धर्म (dharma) / बिचारी (considering) / धर्मसीलता (righteousness) / तव (your) / जग (world) / जागी (awoke / became known) / पावा (obtained) / दरसु (darshan / sight) / हमहुँ (I too) / बड़भागी (very fortunate)
ramacharitamanas::4612.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4612.essence: Pride can disguise itself as respect when it feels cornered.
ramacharitamanas::4612.simple_meaning: Ravana flatters Angad by saying he once forgave a mutilated sister after thinking about dharma, and that his righteousness is well known.
ramacharitamanas::4612.simple_insight: Charm and praise can hide pride; not every compliment is sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::4612.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has confronted Ravana with fearless words. Ravana answers with polished flattery, trying to soften the exchange by praising Angad's supposed righteousness and claiming he is fortunate to have seen him. The verse is part of Ravana's evasive, prideful response.
ramacharitamanas::4612.modern_relevance: Someone argues with you, then suddenly starts complimenting your character to regain control of the room. The praise sounds respectful, but it is really a tactic.
ramacharitamanas::4612.insight: It shows how ego can use praise as a shield, turning moral language into manipulation.

ramacharitamanas::4613.verse_sanskrit: जनि जल्पसि जड़ जंतु कपि सठ बिलोकु मम बाहु। लोकपाल बल बिपुल ससि ग्रसन हेतु सब राहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4613.verse_hindi: (रावण ने कहा-) अरे जड़ जन्तु वानर! व्यर्थ बक-बक न कर, अरे मूर्ख! मेरी भुजाएँ तो देख। ये सब लोकपालों के विशाल बल रूपी चंद्रमा को ग्रसने के लिए राहु हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4613.english_translation: Ravana said, "You foolish monkey, stop babbling and look at my arms. These are all Rahus meant to swallow the great moon of the guardians of the worlds."
ramacharitamanas::4613.translation_literal: जनि (do not) / जल्पसि (speak idly) / जड़ (foolish) / जंतु (creature) / कपि (monkey) / सठ (fool) / बिलोकु (look) / मम (my) / बाहु (arms) / लोकपाल (guardians of the worlds) / बल (strength) / बिपुल (vast) / ससि (moon) / ग्रसन (to swallow) / हेतु (for the purpose of) / सब (all) / राहु (Rahu)
ramacharitamanas::4613.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4613.essence: Ego mistakes its own force for invincibility.
ramacharitamanas::4613.simple_meaning: Ravana insults Hanuman and boasts that his arms are so powerful they can swallow the might of all the world’s guardians.
ramacharitamanas::4613.simple_insight: Boasting can make strength look impressive while hiding the blindness underneath.
ramacharitamanas::4613.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman keeps testing Ravana’s pride. Ravana answers not with reflection but with swagger, pointing to his own arms as proof of unmatched power. The scene shows ego inflating itself just before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4613.modern_relevance: You dominate the meeting with sharp words and a louder voice, but everyone can feel the insecurity underneath. The room hears strength; the wiser eye sees fear.
ramacharitamanas::4613.insight: It shifts the mind to recognize bravado as a sign of inner blindness, not real power.

ramacharitamanas::4614.verse_sanskrit: पुनि नभ सर मम कर निकर कमलन्हि पर करि बास। सोभत भयउ मराल इव संभु सहित कैलास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4614.verse_hindi: फिर (तूने सुना ही होगा कि) आकाश रूपी तालाब में मेरी भुजाओं रूपी कमलों पर बसकर शिवजी सहित कैलास हंस के समान शोभा को प्राप्त हुआ था! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4614.english_translation: Then, as you must have heard, the sky-lake found a swan-like beauty when Shiva and Kailash rested on my arms like lotuses.
ramacharitamanas::4614.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / नभ (sky) / सर (lake) / मम (my) / कर (arms) / निकर (group) / कमलन्हि (lotuses) / पर (on) / करि (having done) / बास (dwelling) / सोभत (shining) / भयउ (became) / मराल (swan) / इव (like) / संभु (Shiva) / सहित (together with) / कैलास (Kailash)
ramacharitamanas::4614.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4614.essence: Pride turns strength into a story about yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4614.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that even Shiva and Kailash once seemed to rest beautifully on his arms, showing off his own strength and grandeur.
ramacharitamanas::4614.simple_insight: Pride makes a person turn even old stories into proof of superiority.
ramacharitamanas::4614.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers Hanuman’s challenge with another boast. He recalls his own cosmic power, claiming that even Shiva and Kailash looked graceful on his arms. The verse is not teaching humility; it shows the arrogance that fuels the coming confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::4614.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting starts listing old achievements to shut down a challenge. The room goes quiet, but everyone can feel the same thing: insecurity dressed up as power.
ramacharitamanas::4614.insight: It exposes how ego inflates memory into self-worship and blocks real listening.

ramacharitamanas::4615.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हरे कटक माझ सुनु अंगद। मो सन भिरिहि कवन जोधा बद॥ तब प्रभु नारि बिरहँ बलहीना। अनुज तासु दुख दुखी मलीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4615.verse_hindi: अरे अंगद! सुन, तेरी सेना में बता, ऐसा कौन योद्धा है, जो मुझसे भिड़ सकेगा। तेरा मालिक तो स्त्री के वियोग में बलहीन हो रहा है और उसका छोटा भाई उसी के दुःख से दुःखी और उदास है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4615.english_translation: Listen, Angad: in your army, tell me, which warrior can fight me? Your lord is weakening from separation from his wife, and his younger brother is sorrowful and dulled by that grief.
ramacharitamanas::4615.translation_literal: तुम्हरे (your) / कटक (army) / माझ (among) / सुनु (listen) / अंगद (Angad) / मो (me) / सन (with) / भिरिहि (will fight) / कवन (which) / जोधा (warrior) / बद (strong) / तब (then) / प्रभु (lord) / नारि (wife) / बिरहँ (in separation) / बलहीना (powerless) / अनुज (younger brother) / तासु (his) / दुख (sorrow) / दुखी (sorrowful) / मलीना (dull, dimmed)
ramacharitamanas::4615.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4615.essence: Boasting grows loudest when it fears defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4615.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that no warrior in Angad's army can match him, then mocks Ram as weakened by separation from Sita and Lakshman as weakened by Ram's sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4615.simple_insight: Pride always looks strongest when it is trying hardest to sound fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4615.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana taunts Angad during the war. He boasts of his own strength, then tries to belittle Ram and Lakshman by pointing to Ram's grief for Sita and Lakshman's shared sorrow. The verse is part of Ravana's swaggering challenge, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::4615.modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing their own achievements and then reaches for your weakest wound. The words sound powerful, but they are really panic dressed as confidence.
ramacharitamanas::4615.insight: It shows how ego attacks by exaggerating itself and reducing others through their pain.

ramacharitamanas::4616.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह सुग्रीव कूलद्रुम दोऊ। अनुज हमार भीरु अति सोऊ॥ जामवंत मंत्री अति बूढ़ा। सो कि होइ अब समरारूढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4616.verse_hindi: तुम और सुग्रीव, दोनों (नदी) तट के वृक्ष हो (रहा) मेरा छोटा भाई विभीषण, (सो) वह भी बड़ा डरपोक है। मंत्री जाम्बवान् बहुत बूढ़ा है। वह अब लड़ाई में क्या चढ़ (उद्यत हो) सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4616.english_translation: You and Sugriva are both riverside trees. My younger brother Vibhishana is very timid. Jambavan is very old—how can he now be ready for battle?
ramacharitamanas::4616.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / कूलद्रुम (riverside trees) / दोऊ (both) । / अनुज (younger brother) / हमार (my) / भीरु (timid) / अति (very) / सोऊ (he) ॥ / जामवंत (Jambavan) / मंत्री (minister) / अति (very) / बूढ़ा (old) । / सो (he) / कि (how) / होइ (can be) / अब (now) / समरारूढ़ा (ready for battle) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4616.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4616.essence: Arrogance shrinks others so it can feel larger.
ramacharitamanas::4616.simple_meaning: Ravana dismisses the strength of the opposing side by calling Sugriva and Vibhishana timid and Jambavan too old for war.
ramacharitamanas::4616.simple_insight: Pride makes other people look small, even when they are not.
ramacharitamanas::4616.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is mocking Hanuman's allies before the war. He belittles Sugriva, Vibhishana, and the aged Jambavan to reassure himself that Ram's side cannot truly challenge him. The verse shows Ravana's arrogance, not reality.
ramacharitamanas::4616.modern_relevance: You brush off a team because one person is quiet, another is new, and another is older. The mistake is not theirs — it's your blind spot.
ramacharitamanas::4616.insight: It exposes how ego misreads weakness and mistakes contempt for insight.

ramacharitamanas::4617.verse_sanskrit: सिल्पि कर्म जानहिं नल नीला। है कपि एक महा बलसीला॥ आवा प्रथम नगरु जेहिं जारा। सुनत बचन कह बालिकुमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4617.verse_hindi: नल-नील तो शिल्प-कर्म जानते हैं (वे लड़ना क्या जानें?)। हाँ, एक वानर जरूर महान् बलवान् है, जो पहले आया था और जिसने लंका जलाई थी। यह वचन सुनते ही बालि पुत्र अंगद ने कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4617.english_translation: Nala and Nila know only craftsmanship. There is one monkey of great strength who came first and burned the city. Hearing this, Angada, the son of Bali, said—
ramacharitamanas::4617.translation_literal: सिल्पि (craftsman) / कर्म (work) / जानहिं (know) / नल (Nala) / नीला (Nila) / है (is) / कपि (monkey) / एक (one) / महा (great) / बलसीला (strong) / आवा (came) / प्रथम (first) / नगरु (city) / जेहिं (which) / जारा (burned) / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / कह (said) / बालिकुमारा (son of Bali)
ramacharitamanas::4617.speaker: Angada
ramacharitamanas::4617.essence: One remembered act of courage can outweigh a roomful of boasts.
ramacharitamanas::4617.simple_meaning: Angada points out that Nala and Nila are builders, not warriors, and recalls the one powerful monkey who burned Lanka first.
ramacharitamanas::4617.simple_insight: Sometimes a single remembered feat shifts the whole conversation.
ramacharitamanas::4617.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is testing Hanuman's allies by mocking their strength. Angada answers sharply, separating skilled builders Nala and Nila from the one monkey whose fire reached the city first. The exchange turns the focus toward Hanuman's unmatched power.
ramacharitamanas::4617.modern_relevance: In a tense meeting, someone dismisses the quiet people in the room. Then one person names the moment everyone remembers — and the whole balance changes.
ramacharitamanas::4617.insight: It shows how reputation can silence arrogance before the fight even begins.

ramacharitamanas::4618.verse_sanskrit: सत्य बचन कहु निसिचर नाहा। साँचेहुँ कीस कीन्ह पुर दाहा॥ रावण नगर अल्प कपि दहई। सुनि अस बचन सत्य को कहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4618.verse_hindi: हे राक्षसराज! सच्ची बात कहो! क्या उस वानर ने सचमुच तुम्हारा नगर जला दिया? रावण (जैसे जगद्विजयी योद्धा) का नगर एक छोटे से वानर ने जला दिया। ऐसे वचन सुनकर उन्हें सत्य कौन कहेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4618.english_translation: O lord of the demons, speak truly. Did that monkey really burn your city? Ravana's city was burned by a tiny monkey. Hearing such words, who would believe they are true?
ramacharitamanas::4618.translation_literal: सत्य (true) / बचन (words) / कहु (tell) / निसिचर नाहा (lord of the demons) / साँचेहुँ (indeed, truly) / कीस (monkey) / कीन्ह (did) / पुर (city) / दाहा (burn) / रावण (Ravana) / नगर (city) / अल्प (small) / कपि (monkey) / दहई (burns) / सुनि (hearing) / अस (such) / बचन (words) / सत्य (true) / को (who) / कहई (would say)
ramacharitamanas::4618.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4618.essence: Great deeds can sound unbelievable before they are understood.
ramacharitamanas::4618.simple_meaning: The speaker asks Ravana to confirm the unbelievable report that a tiny monkey burned Lanka. The verse highlights how strange Hanuman's feat sounds.
ramacharitamanas::4618.simple_insight: Sometimes truth is so startling that pride cannot even recognize it.
ramacharitamanas::4618.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's own people are trying to make sense of the destruction. The speaker presses him to admit what happened: a lone monkey set the city ablaze. The verse sits inside a chain of taunting questions, not as the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4618.modern_relevance: You hear a story so absurd it sounds impossible, yet the damage is already in front of you. Sometimes reality arrives wearing the face of disbelief.
ramacharitamanas::4618.insight: It frames Hanuman's feat as so extraordinary that even enemies struggle to name it honestly.

ramacharitamanas::4619.verse_sanskrit: जो अति सुभट सराहेहु रावन। सो सुग्रीव केर लघु धावन॥ चलइ बहुत सो बीर न होई। पठवा खबरि लेन हम सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4619.verse_hindi: हे रावण! जिसको तुमने बहुत बड़ा योद्धा कहकर सराहा है, वह तो सुग्रीव का एक छोटा सा दौड़कर चलने वाला हरकारा है। वह बहुत चलता है, वीर नहीं है। उसको तो हमने (केवल) खबर लेने के लिए भेजा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4619.english_translation: O Ravana, the one you praised as a great warrior is only Sugriva’s small messenger. He runs a lot, but he is not a true hero. We sent him only to gather news.
ramacharitamanas::4619.translation_literal: जो (who) / अति (very) / सुभट (great warrior) / सराहेहु (you praised) / रावन (Ravana) / सो (that one) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva’s) / केर (of) / लघु (small) / धावन (runner, messenger) ॥ चलइ (runs) / बहुत (much) / सो (he) / बीर (hero) / न (not) / होई (is) / पठवा (sent) / खबरि (news) / लेन (to take) / हम (we) / सोई (that only) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4619.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4619.essence: Fear makes a messenger look like a monster.
ramacharitamanas::4619.simple_meaning: The monkey Ravana praised was not a warrior at all, just a messenger sent to gather information.
ramacharitamanas::4619.simple_insight: Pride can turn a scout into a legend, but the facts stay plain.
ramacharitamanas::4619.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to identify the monkey who burned the city. The reply cuts down Ravana’s fear: the one he praised as a mighty fighter was only Sugriva’s messenger, sent to scout and report back.
ramacharitamanas::4619.modern_relevance: A rumor spreads through a group chat, and by noon the quiet person who asked one question has become a threat in everyone’s mind. Fear often inflates what is actually ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::4619.insight: It shifts the mind from exaggerated fear to clear-eyed proportion.

ramacharitamanas::4620.verse_sanskrit: सत्य नगरु कपि जारेउ बिनु प्रभु आयसु पाइ। फिरि न गयउ सुग्रीव पहिं तेहिं भय रहा लुकाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4620.verse_hindi: क्या सचमुच ही उस वानर ने प्रभु की आज्ञा पाए बिना ही तुम्हारा नगर जला डाला? मालूम होता है, इसी डर से वह लौटकर सुग्रीव के पास नहीं गया और कहीं छिप रहा! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4620.english_translation: Did that monkey burn your city without receiving his Lord's command? It seems he did not return to Sugriva because of fear, but hid somewhere instead.
ramacharitamanas::4620.translation_literal: सत्य (true) / नगरु (city) / कपि (monkey) / जारेउ (burned) / बिनु (without) / प्रभु (lord) / आयसु (command) / पाइ (having received) / फिरि (again) / न (not) / गयउ (went) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / पहिं (to) / तेहिं (he) / भय (fear) / रहा (remained) / लुकाइ (hidden)
ramacharitamanas::4620.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4620.essence: Pride can make courage look like fear.
ramacharitamanas::4620.simple_meaning: Ravana is still trying to make sense of Hanuman's burning of Lanka, assuming it happened without Ram's command and out of fear.
ramacharitamanas::4620.simple_insight: Pride keeps turning a real event into a story that protects itself.
ramacharitamanas::4620.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being questioned about the burning of his city. Instead of seeing Hanuman's courage and mission clearly, he tries to explain it away as fear and hiding. The verse keeps the scene moving toward his own self-deception.
