ramacharitamanas::4620.modern_relevance: You get a message that clearly shows someone acted with purpose, but you rewrite it as panic or accident because the truth stings your pride.
ramacharitamanas::4620.insight: It exposes how ego distorts evidence to avoid feeling diminished.

ramacharitamanas::4621.verse_sanskrit: सत्य कहहि दसकंठ सब मोहि न सुनि कछु कोह। कोउ न हमारें कटक अस तो सन लरत जो सोह ॥
ramacharitamanas::4621.verse_hindi: हे रावण! तुम सब सत्य ही कहते हो, मुझे सुनकर कुछ भी क्रोध नहीं है। सचमुच हमारी सेना में कोई भी ऐसा नहीं है, जो तुमसे लड़ने में शोभा पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4621.english_translation: Ravana, you speak the truth. I feel no anger at hearing it. There is no one in our army who would be worthy to fight you.
ramacharitamanas::4621.translation_literal: सत्य (truth) / कहहि (you speak) / दसकंठ (ten-necked one, Ravana) / सब (all) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / सुनि (hearing) / कछु (any) / कोह (anger) / कोउ (someone) / न (not) / हमारें (in our) / कटक (army) / अस (such) / तो (then) / सन (with) / लरत (fighting) / जो (who) / सोह (would be worthy)
ramacharitamanas::4621.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4621.essence: Strength is met best by calm honesty, not wounded pride.
ramacharitamanas::4621.simple_meaning: Ravana is told that his boast is true, and there is no anger in reply. The speaker admits that no one in his army is fit to match Ravana in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4621.simple_insight: Pride can be answered without rage. Sometimes the clearest reply is simply seeing strength as it is.
ramacharitamanas::4621.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the taunts and boasts are escalating before the war. Ravana is being addressed in a way that strips away flattery and fear alike. The speaker calmly admits Ravana's strength, setting up the sharper moral point that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4621.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you down in front of a room, expecting a fight. You don't scramble to prove yourself; you answer cleanly, without heat, and the tension changes.
ramacharitamanas::4621.insight: It teaches you to meet arrogance with clear seeing, not reactive anger.

ramacharitamanas::4622.verse_sanskrit: प्रीति बिरोध समान सन करिअ नीति असि आहि। जौं मृगपति बध मेडुकन्हि भल कि कहइ कोउ ताहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4622.verse_hindi: प्रीति और वैर बराबरी वाले से ही करना चाहिए, नीति ऐसी ही है। सिंह यदि मेंढकों को मारे, तो क्या उसे कोई भला कहेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4622.english_translation: Friendship and hostility belong with equals; that is the proper rule. If a lion kills frogs, who would call that noble?
ramacharitamanas::4622.translation_literal: प्रीति (friendship) / बिरोध (enmity) / समान (equal) / सन (with) / करिअ (should be done) / नीति (right conduct) / असि (such) / आहि (is) / जौं (if) / मृगपति (lion, lord of beasts) / बध (killing) / मेडुकन्हि (frogs) / भल (good) / कि (whether) / कहइ (says) / कोउ (anyone) / ताहि (to him)
ramacharitamanas::4622.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4622.essence: True conduct does not prove itself by hurting the powerless.
ramacharitamanas::4622.simple_meaning: Ravana says true conduct is to deal with equals, not to attack the weak. A great person does not win praise by harming those beneath them.
ramacharitamanas::4622.simple_insight: Real strength shows restraint. Power feels empty when it is only used against those who cannot answer back.
ramacharitamanas::4622.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned that Hanuman has acted boldly. Instead of reflecting, he turns the moment into a boast about proper conduct: the strong should meet the strong. The line exposes his pride while sounding like moral reasoning.
ramacharitamanas::4622.modern_relevance: You win an argument with someone who has no voice in the room, then call it firmness. The discomfort you feel afterward is this verse: strength is only worthy when it meets strength.
ramacharitamanas::4622.insight: It shifts the mind from domination to fairness in conflict.

ramacharitamanas::4623.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि लघुता राम कहुँ तोहि बधें बड़ दोष। तदपि कठिन दसकंठ सुनु छत्र जाति कर रोष ॥
ramacharitamanas::4623.verse_hindi: यद्यपि तुम्हें मारने में श्री रामजी की लघुता है और बड़ा दोष भी है तथापि हे रावण! सुनो, क्षत्रिय जाति का क्रोध बड़ा कठिन होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4623.english_translation: Although it would be a slight for Ram to kill you and a great fault, still listen, Ravana: the anger of a kshatriya is hard to restrain.
ramacharitamanas::4623.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / लघुता (smallness, slight) / राम कहुँ (for Ram) / तोहि बधें (to kill you) / बड़ दोष (great fault) / तदपि (still, even so) / कठिन (hard, severe) / दसकंठ (ten-necked one, Ravana) / सुनु (listen) / छत्र जाति (kshatriya caste) / कर रोष (the anger of)
ramacharitamanas::4623.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4623.essence: True strength can choose restraint even when anger is justified.
ramacharitamanas::4623.simple_meaning: Angad says that killing Ravana would be beneath Ram and morally wrong, but a warrior's anger is still fierce and difficult to stop.
ramacharitamanas::4623.simple_insight: Strength is not the same as restraint. Real dignity can hold power without losing force.
ramacharitamanas::4623.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana during the tense exchange after his taunts. He answers with sharp, measured words: Ram is too great to need such a killing, yet a kshatriya's wrath is not easy to dismiss. The verse keeps the confrontation alive.
ramacharitamanas::4623.modern_relevance: In a heated family argument, you know you could land the final blow with one cruel sentence. But you also know restraint matters more than winning.
ramacharitamanas::4623.insight: It shifts the mind from raw retaliation to disciplined force, showing that power is strongest when it can hold itself back.

ramacharitamanas::4624.verse_sanskrit: बक्र उक्ति धनु बचन सर हृदय दहेउ रिपु कीस। प्रतिउत्तर सड़सिन्ह मनहुँ काढ़त भट दससीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4624.verse_hindi: वक्रोक्ति रूपी धनुष से वचन रूपी बाण मारकर अंगद ने शत्रु का हृदय जला दिया। वीर रावण उन बाणों को मानो प्रत्युत्तर रूपी सँड़सियों से निकाल रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4624.english_translation: Angad's crooked words, like arrows from a bow, burned the enemy's heart. Ravana, the ten-headed one, was like a warrior pulling those arrows out with iron tongs.
ramacharitamanas::4624.translation_literal: बक्र उक्ति (crooked speech) / धनु (bow) / बचन (words) / सर (arrows) / हृदय (heart) / दहेउ (burned) / रिपु (enemy) / कीस (monkey) / प्रतिउत्तर (reply) / सड़सिन्ह (with tongs) / मनहुँ (as if) / काढ़त (pulling out) / भट (warrior) / दससीस (ten-headed one)
ramacharitamanas::4624.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4624.essence: Words can strike harder than arrows when pride is the target.
ramacharitamanas::4624.simple_meaning: Angad's sharp words strike Ravana so hard that they feel like arrows burning his heart. Ravana tries to pull the insult out, but it only exposes his pride.
ramacharitamanas::4624.simple_insight: Pride can be wounded by words more deeply than by weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4624.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana and speaks with cutting force. His words are not random insult; they are a deliberate challenge that lands like a weapon. Ravana's reaction shows that his real wound is not physical fear but wounded ego.
ramacharitamanas::4624.modern_relevance: A calm sentence in a tense meeting can hit harder than a raised voice. The other person smiles, but you can see they are still pulling the words out of their chest.
ramacharitamanas::4624.insight: It shows how verbal truth can expose ego more sharply than force.

ramacharitamanas::4625.verse_sanskrit: हँसि बोलेउ दसमौलि तब कपि कर बड़ गुन एक। जो प्रतिपालइ तासु हित करइ उपाय अनेक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4625.verse_hindi: तब रावण हँसकर बोला- बंदर में यह एक बड़ा गुण है कि जो उसे पालता है, उसका वह अनेकों उपायों से भला करने की चेष्टा करता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4625.english_translation: Ravana then laughed and said, "Monkeys have one great quality: whoever feeds them, they try to help in many ways."
ramacharitamanas::4625.translation_literal: हँसि (laughing) / बोलेउ (spoke) / दसमौलि (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / तब (then) / कपि (monkey) / कर (of) / बड़ (great) / गुन (quality) / एक (one) / जो (whoever) / प्रतिपालइ (nurtures) / तासु (that one’s) / हित (good) / करइ (does) / उपाय (means) / अनेक (many)
ramacharitamanas::4625.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4625.essence: Pride turns devotion into a joke.
ramacharitamanas::4625.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman by saying a monkey repays care by trying to help its benefactor in every possible way.
ramacharitamanas::4625.simple_insight: Even praise can hide contempt when pride is speaking.
ramacharitamanas::4625.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just been stung by Angad's bold words. Still smiling, he turns Hanuman's nature into a taunt, calling selfless helpfulness a monkey's habit. The line is part of his larger attempt to dismiss the devotion standing before him.
ramacharitamanas::4625.modern_relevance: A person smiles in a meeting and says, "You mean well," but the tone cuts deeper than anger. Pride can disguise dismissal as compliment.
ramacharitamanas::4625.insight: It shows how ego can reduce genuine loyalty into something trivial or useful.

ramacharitamanas::4626.verse_sanskrit: धन्य कीस जो निज प्रभु काजा। जहँ तहँ नाचइ परिहरि लाजा॥ नाचि कूदि करि लोग रिझाई। पति हित करइ धर्म निपुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4626.verse_hindi: बंदर को धन्य है, जो अपने मालिक के लिए लाज छोड़कर जहाँ-तहाँ नाचता है। नाच-कूदकर, लोगों को रिझाकर, मालिक का हित करता है। यह उसके धर्म की निपुणता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4626.english_translation: Blessed is the monkey who, for his own lord's work, forgets shame and dances wherever needed. By dancing and leaping, he delights people and serves his lord well; that is skill in righteous duty.
ramacharitamanas::4626.translation_literal: धन्य (blessed) / कीस (monkey) / जो (who) / निज (own) / प्रभु (lord) / काजा (work) / जहँ तहँ (here and there / wherever) / नाचइ (dances) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / लाजा (shame) ॥ / नाचि (dancing) / कूदि (leaping) / करि (doing) / लोग (people) / रिझाई (pleases) / पति (lord) / हित (welfare) / करइ (does) / धर्म (duty) / निपुनाई (skillfulness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4626.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4626.essence: True service forgets embarrassment and becomes fearless usefulness.
ramacharitamanas::4626.simple_meaning: A devoted servant is praised for setting aside embarrassment, doing whatever helps the master, and using skillful, even playful action to serve well.
ramacharitamanas::4626.simple_insight: Real devotion stops worrying about appearances and becomes useful, joyful, and fearless.
ramacharitamanas::4626.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just spoken with Ravana and the court is watching. Tulsidas praises the servant who can drop pride, move freely, and do whatever helps his lord. Service becomes skill, not stiffness.
ramacharitamanas::4626.modern_relevance: You volunteer to lead the messy part of the event, even if it means looking awkward in front of everyone. What matters is that the work gets done and the people you serve are helped.
ramacharitamanas::4626.insight: It shifts service from image-management to wholehearted usefulness.

ramacharitamanas::4627.verse_sanskrit: अंगद स्वामिभक्त तव जाती। प्रभु गुन कस न कहसि एहि भाँती॥ मैं गुन गाहक परम सुजाना। तव कटु रटनि करउँ नहिं काना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4627.verse_hindi: हे अंगद! तेरी जाति स्वामिभक्त है (फिर भला) तू अपने मालिक के गुण इस प्रकार कैसे न बखानेगा? मैं गुण ग्राहक (गुणों का आदर करने वाला) और परम सुजान (समझदार) हूँ, इसी से तेरी जली-कटी बक-बक पर कान (ध्यान) नहीं देता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4627.english_translation: Angad, your nature is to serve your master. How could you not praise your lord's virtues in this way? I am a true appreciator of virtues and deeply wise, so I do not even listen to your bitter taunts.
ramacharitamanas::4627.translation_literal: अंगद (Angad) / स्वामिभक्त (devoted to his master) / तव (your) / जाती (nature, lineage) / प्रभु (lord, master) / गुन (virtues) / कस (how) / न (not) / कहसि (you speak) / एहि भाँती (in this way) ॥ / मैं (I) / गुन (virtues) / गाहक (one who values, appreciates) / परम (supremely) / सुजाना (wise) / तव (your) / कटु (bitter) / रटनि (repetition, taunts) / करउँ (I do) / नहिं (not) / काना (ear) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4627.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4627.essence: Pride can wear the mask of wisdom and still remain untouched.
ramacharitamanas::4627.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Angad that a loyal servant naturally praises his master, and he claims he is wise enough not to be bothered by Angad's harsh words.
ramacharitamanas::4627.simple_insight: Pride can disguise itself as calm, even while it is being challenged.
ramacharitamanas::4627.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad is confronting Ravana on Ram's behalf. Ravana answers with polished sarcasm, pretending to be above Angad's insults while actually trying to defend his own pride. The exchange is part of a larger verbal battle, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4627.modern_relevance: Someone makes a cutting remark in a meeting, and you answer with a smile that hides your irritation. Ravana's tone feels like that kind of controlled defensiveness.
ramacharitamanas::4627.insight: It shows how wounded ego can sound composed while still resisting the truth.

ramacharitamanas::4628.verse_sanskrit: कह कपि तव गुन गाहकताई। सत्य पवनसुत मोहि सुनाई॥ बन बिधंसि सुत बधि पुर जारा। तदपि न तेहिं कछु कृत अपकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4628.verse_hindi: अंगद ने कहा- तुम्हारी सच्ची गुण ग्राहकता तो मुझे हनुमान् ने सुनाई थी। उसने अशोक वन में विध्वंस (तहस-नहस) करके, तुम्हारे पुत्र को मारकर नगर को जला दिया था। तो भी (तुमने अपनी गुण ग्राहकता के कारण यही समझा कि) उसने तुम्हारा कुछ भी अपकार नहीं किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4628.english_translation: Angad said, "Hanuman himself told me of your true love for virtue. He had destroyed the Ashoka grove, killed your son, and burned the city, yet you still felt he had done you no harm."
ramacharitamanas::4628.translation_literal: कह (said) / कपि (monkey-devotee) / तव (your) / गुन (virtues) / गाहकताई (the quality of appreciating) / सत्य (truly) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / मोहि (to me) / सुनाई (told)॥ / बन (grove/forest) / बिधंसि (destroying) / सुत (son) / बधि (killing) / पुर (city) / जारा (burned)॥ / तदपि (even then) / न (not) / तेहिं (by that) / कछु (any) / कृत (done) / अपकारा (harm) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4628.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4628.essence: You reveal your own greatness when you can praise the one who hurt you.
ramacharitamanas::4628.simple_meaning: A noble heart can recognize goodness even after being hurt. Angad says Ravana's ability to appreciate Hanuman's qualities proved his own hidden virtue.
ramacharitamanas::4628.simple_insight: Real greatness can notice merit even in an enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4628.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana and speaks boldly about Hanuman. He reminds Ravana that even after Hanuman wrecked the grove, killed a son, and burned the city, Ravana still admitted Hanuman's worth. That strange generosity is the point.
ramacharitamanas::4628.modern_relevance: Someone criticizes you harshly, yet still admits, quietly, that you handled the hardest part better than anyone else. That split-second honesty is what Angad notices in Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4628.insight: It shifts attention from offense to character: a strong mind can recognize excellence even under attack.

ramacharitamanas::4629.verse_sanskrit: सोइ बिचारि तव प्रकृति सुहाई। दसकंधर मैं कीन्हि ढिठाई॥ देखेउँ आइ जो कछु कपि भाषा। तुम्हरें लाज न रोष न माखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4629.verse_hindi: तुम्हारा वही सुंदर स्वभाव विचार कर, हे दशग्रीव! मैंने कुछ धृष्टता की है। हनुमान् ने जो कुछ कहा था, उसे आकर मैंने प्रत्यक्ष देख लिया कि तुम्हें न लज्जा है, न क्रोध है और न चिढ़ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4629.english_translation: Thinking of your fine nature, O Ravana, I have acted boldly. I came and saw for myself what Hanuman had said: you feel no shame, no anger, and no embarrassment.
ramacharitamanas::4629.translation_literal: सोइ (that very) / बिचारि (having considered) / तव (your) / प्रकृति (nature) / सुहाई (beautiful) / दसकंधर (O ten-necked one, Ravana) / मैं (I) / कीन्हि (did) / ढिठाई (boldness, audacity) ॥ / देखेउँ (I saw) / आइ (coming) / जो (what) / कछु (whatever) / कपि (monkey, Hanuman) / भाषा (said) / तुम्हरें (in your) / लाज (shame) / न (not) / रोष (anger) / न (not) / माखा (resentment, irritation) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4629.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4629.essence: Seeing clearly leaves no room for flattering denial.
ramacharitamanas::4629.simple_meaning: Angad says he spoke boldly only after seeing Ravana's character firsthand. He confirms Hanuman's warning: Ravana has no shame, anger, or restraint.
ramacharitamanas::4629.simple_insight: Clear seeing is stronger than flattery. It stops you from excusing what is plainly in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4629.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana as a messenger of Ram. He says his boldness came only after judging Ravana's nature for himself. Hanuman's earlier warning proved true: Ravana is untouched by shame or remorse.
ramacharitamanas::4629.modern_relevance: You finally meet the manager everyone warned you about, and the room feels colder than the stories did. The mask is gone; you can see the pattern yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4629.insight: It teaches you to trust direct observation over reputation or excuses.

ramacharitamanas::4630.verse_sanskrit: जौं असि मति पितु खाए कीसा। कहि अस बचन हँसा दससीसा॥ पितहि खाइ खातेउँ पुनि तोही। अबहीं समुझि परा कछु मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4630.verse_hindi: (रावण बोला-) अरे वानर! जब तेरी ऐसी बुद्धि है, तभी तो तू बाप को खा गया। ऐसा वचन कहकर रावण हँसा। अंगद ने कहा- पिता को खाकर फिर तुमको भी खा डालता, परन्तु अभी तुरंत कुछ और ही बात मेरी समझ में आ गई! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4630.english_translation: Ravana said, "If your mind is like this, you must have eaten your father too." Laughing at those words, Angada replied, "I would have eaten my father and then eaten you too, but just now I understood something else."
ramacharitamanas::4630.translation_literal: जौं (if) / असि (such) / मति (mind) / पितु (father) / खाए (eaten) / कीसा (monkey) / कहि (saying) / अस (such) / बचन (words) / हँसा (laughed) / दससीसा (ten-headed one) / पितहि (father) / खाइ (eating) / खातेउँ (I would eat) / पुनि (again) / तोही (you) / अबहीं (now) / समुझि (understanding) / परा (fell) / कछु (something) / मोही (to me)
ramacharitamanas::4630.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4630.essence: Mockery answers mockery until someone remembers the real stakes.
ramacharitamanas::4630.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Angada with a cruel insult, and Angada answers with sharp wit, saying he would have destroyed Ravana too if not for a new realization.
ramacharitamanas::4630.simple_insight: It shows how pride turns even conversation into a contest of contempt.
ramacharitamanas::4630.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angada stands before Ravana and his court without fear. Ravana sneers at him with a filthy insult about his father, and Angada fires back with even greater force. The exchange is less teaching than provocation, setting up the moral clash that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4630.modern_relevance: Someone throws a nasty joke in a group chat, and the room goes quiet. You can feel the old reflex to strike back harder, even when the real issue is someone's wounded pride.
ramacharitamanas::4630.insight: It reveals how insult escalates into performance when ego is in charge.

ramacharitamanas::4631.verse_sanskrit: बालि बिमल जस भाजन जानी। हतउँ न तोहि अधम अभिमानी॥ कहु रावन रावन जग केते। मैं निज श्रवन सुने सुनु जेते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4631.verse_hindi: अरे नीच अभिमानी! बालि के निर्मल यश का पात्र (कारण) जानकर तुम्हें मैं नहीं मारता। रावण! यह तो बता कि जगत् में कितने रावण हैं? मैंने जितने रावण अपने कानों से सुन रखे हैं, उन्हें सुन- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4631.english_translation: Knowing you were the kind of man who brought fame to Bali, I did not kill you, arrogant one. Tell me, Ravana: how many Ravanas are there in the world? I have heard many with my own ears.
ramacharitamanas::4631.translation_literal: बालि (Bali) / बिमल (pure) / जस (fame) / भाजन (vessel) / जानी (knowing) / हतउँ (I killed) / न (not) / तोहि (you) / अधम (base) / अभिमानी (arrogant one) / कहु (tell) / रावन (Ravana) / रावन (Ravana) / जग (world) / केते (how many) / मैं (I) / निज (my own) / श्रवन (ears) / सुने (heard) / सुनु (listen) / जेते (as many as)
ramacharitamanas::4631.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4631.essence: Ego is not unique; it is the same mask wearing many names.
ramacharitamanas::4631.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the enemy's pride and says his arrogance is nothing special. He treats Ravana-like ego as a common pattern, not a unique identity.
ramacharitamanas::4631.simple_insight: Pride becomes smaller when you see it as a familiar pattern instead of a personal crown.
ramacharitamanas::4631.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers Angad's taunts with contempt. He says he spared Angad only because Angad's arrogance reminded him of Bali's fame, then turns the insult back: there are many Ravanas in the world. The verse exposes ego as repetitive, not grand.
ramacharitamanas::4631.modern_relevance: You meet someone who keeps repeating the same boast in a group chat, as if no one has heard that tone before. The room goes quiet when you realize the swagger is just a costume worn by many insecure minds.
ramacharitamanas::4631.insight: It shifts attention from the person to the pattern of ego driving the speech.

ramacharitamanas::4632.verse_sanskrit: बलिहि जितन एक गयउ पताला। राखेउ बाँधि सिसुन्ह हयसाला॥ खेलहिं बालक मारहिं जाई। दया लागि बलि दीन्ह छोड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4632.verse_hindi: एक रावण तो बलि को जीतने पाताल में गया था, तब बच्चों ने उसे घुड़साल में बाँध रखा। बालक खेलते थे और जा-जाकर उसे मारते थे। बलि को दया लगी, तब उन्होंने उसे छुड़ा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4632.english_translation: One Ravana had gone down to the netherworld to conquer Bali, and the children had tied him up in the stable. The children played by going and striking him, and Bali, moved by compassion, released him.
ramacharitamanas::4632.translation_literal: बलिहि (Bali) / जितन (to conquer) / एक (one) / गयउ (went) / पताला (to the netherworld) / राखेउ (they kept) / बाँधि (bound) / सिसुन्ह (by children) / हयसाला (in the stable) / खेलहिं (they play) / बालक (children) / मारहिं (strike) / जाई (going) / दया लागि (out of compassion) / बलि (Bali) / दीन्ह (gave) / छोड़ाई (release)
ramacharitamanas::4632.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4632.essence: Power becomes human when it can still release the defeated.
ramacharitamanas::4632.simple_meaning: Bali once caught Ravana and had him tied up in a stable, where children mocked and hit him. Feeling pity, Bali set him free.
ramacharitamanas::4632.simple_insight: Compassion can appear even toward someone defeated and hated.
ramacharitamanas::4632.detailed_meaning: In the war narrative, Tulsidas pauses to recall an older episode from Ravana's life: Bali once subdued him and had him tied up like a captive animal. When children tormented him, Bali felt pity and released him. The verse deepens Ravana's humiliation before his final fall.
ramacharitamanas::4632.modern_relevance: A bully at school gets cornered, mocked, and suddenly looks smaller than the anger around him. The real test is whether you can still choose mercy when you have the upper hand.
ramacharitamanas::4632.insight: It shifts the mind from revenge to mercy, even when the other person has done wrong.

ramacharitamanas::4633.verse_sanskrit: एक बहोरि सहसभुज देखा। धाइ धरा जिमि जंतु बिसेषा॥ कौतुक लागि भवन लै आवा। सो पुलस्ति मुनि जाइ छोड़ावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4633.verse_hindi: फिर एक रावण को सहस्रबाहु ने देखा, और उसने दौड़कर उसको एक विशेष प्रकार के (विचित्र) जन्तु की तरह (समझकर) पकड़ लिया। तमाशे के लिए वह उसे घर ले आया। तब पुलस्त्य मुनि ने जाकर उसे छुड़ाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4633.english_translation: Again, Ravana was seen by Sahasrabahu, who ran and seized him as if he were a strange creature. For amusement, he carried him home. Then the sage Pulastya went and freed him.
ramacharitamanas::4633.translation_literal: एक (one) / बहोरि (again) / सहसभुज (Sahasrabahu, thousand-armed one) / देखा (saw) । धाइ (running) / धरा (seized) / जिमि (as if) / जंतु (creature) / बिसेषा (strange, special) ॥ कौतुक (for amusement) / लागि (for the sake of) / भवन (home) / लै (taking) / आवा (came) । सो (that one) / पुलस्ति मुनि (sage Pulastya) / जाइ (going) / छोड़ावा (freed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4633.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4633.essence: Pride shrinks fast when reality grabs hold.
ramacharitamanas::4633.simple_meaning: Sahasrabahu catches Ravana like an odd creature and takes him home as a joke. Pulastya later goes and frees Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4633.simple_insight: Pride can make a person look ridiculous before the very people he tries to impress.
ramacharitamanas::4633.detailed_meaning: The poem is recalling an old humiliation of Ravana to mock his boastful claims. Sahasrabahu once seized him like a curiosity and carried him home for amusement. Pulastya had to intervene and release him, so the verse supports the larger argument against Ravana's pride.
ramacharitamanas::4633.modern_relevance: Someone posts a grand self-image online, then gets exposed by a simple fact everyone else already knows. The humiliation lands hardest because the arrogance was so loud.
ramacharitamanas::4633.insight: It shifts the mind from inflated self-image to sober self-awareness.

ramacharitamanas::4634.verse_sanskrit: एक कहत मोहि सकुच अति रहा बालि कीं काँख। इन्ह महुँ रावन तैं कवन सत्य बदहि तजि माख ॥
ramacharitamanas::4634.verse_hindi: एक रावण की बात कहने में तो मुझे बड़ा संकोच हो रहा है- वह (बहुत दिनों तक) बालि की काँख में रहा था। इनमें से तुम कौन से रावण हो? खीझना छोड़कर सच-सच बताओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4634.english_translation: I feel too shy to even mention one Ravana. One stayed in Bali's armpit. Which Ravana are you? Drop the irritation and tell the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4634.translation_literal: एक (one) / कहत (speaking) / मोहि (to me) / सकुच (shyness) / अति (very) / रहा (was) / बालि (Bali) / कीं (of) / काँख (armpit) / इन्ह (these) / महुँ (among) / रावन (Ravana) / तैं (you) / कवन (which) / सत्य (truth) / बदहि (say) / तजि (leaving) / माख (irritation)
ramacharitamanas::4634.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4634.essence: Pride softens when truth is demanded without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4634.simple_meaning: The speaker jokes that there have been different Ravanas in strange situations, so the listener should stop getting offended and speak plainly.
ramacharitamanas::4634.simple_insight: Humor can cut through ego and force a direct answer.
ramacharitamanas::4634.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the conversation turns sharp and playful. A speaker taunts Ravana by recalling absurd stories of other Ravanas, then challenges him to stop bristling and tell the truth about who he is. The verse sets up Ravana's proud reply.
ramacharitamanas::4634.modern_relevance: Someone keeps dodging a straight question with wounded pride and defensive jokes. A calm, teasing line can sometimes do what pressure cannot: make the truth come out.
ramacharitamanas::4634.insight: It shifts the exchange from ego-protection to honest self-disclosure.

ramacharitamanas::4635.verse_sanskrit: चौपाई : : सुनु सठ सोइ रावन बलसीला। हरगिरि जान जासु भुज लीला॥ जान उमापति जासु सुराई। पूजेउँ जेहि सिर सुमन चढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4635.verse_hindi: (रावण ने कहा-) अरे मूर्ख! सुन, मैं वही बलवान् रावण हूँ, जिसकी भुजाओं की लीला (करामात) कैलास पर्वत जानता है। जिसकी शूरता उमापति महादेवजी जानते हैं, जिन्हें अपने सिर रूपी पुष्प चढ़ा-चढ़ाकर मैंने पूजा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4635.english_translation: Listen, fool: I am that mighty Ravana, whose arms even Mount Kailash has known. Lord Shiva, husband of Uma, knows my valor, and I have worshiped him by offering my own heads as flowers.
ramacharitamanas::4635.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सठ (fool) / सोइ (that same) / रावन (Ravana) / बलसीला (mighty, powerful) / हरगिरि (Mount Kailash) / जान (knows) / जासु (whose) / भुज (arms) / लीला (play, display) ॥ / जान (knows) / उमापति (Shiva, husband of Uma) / जासु (whose) / सुराई (valor, heroism) / पूजेउँ (I worshiped) / जेहि (whom) / सिर (heads) / सुमन (flowers) / चढ़ाई (offered) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4635.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4635.essence: Pride can dress itself up as devotion and still remain pride.
ramacharitamanas::4635.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that even Shiva and Mount Kailash know his power, and he claims to have worshiped Shiva by offering his own heads.
ramacharitamanas::4635.simple_insight: Pride can turn devotion into self-display, making worship another way to praise yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4635.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to intimidate his opponent with grand claims about his strength and past devotion. He boasts that even Shiva knows his might, and that he once offered his own heads in worship. The verse reveals his ego more than his greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4635.modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing every sacrifice they ever made, not to be understood but to win. The story feels familiar because wounded pride loves a résumé.
ramacharitamanas::4635.insight: It exposes how ego can hijack even sincere devotion and turn it into a performance.

ramacharitamanas::4636.verse_sanskrit: सिर सरोज निज करन्हि उतारी। पूजेउँ अमित बार त्रिपुरारी॥ भुज बिक्रम जानहिं दिगपाला। सठ अजहूँ जिन्ह कें उर साला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4636.verse_hindi: सिर रूपी कमलों को अपने हाथों से उतार-उतारकर मैंने अगणित बार त्रिपुरारि शिवजी की पूजा की है। अरे मूर्ख! मेरी भुजाओं का पराक्रम दिक्पाल जानते हैं, जिनके हृदय में वह आज भी चुभ रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4636.english_translation: I have lifted the lotus-like heads with my own hands and worshipped Tripurari countless times. Fools, the mighty force of my arms is known to the guardians of the directions, and that ache still stings their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::4636.translation_literal: सिर (heads) / सरोज (lotus-like) / निज (own) / करन्हि (with hands) / उतारी (lifted off) / पूजेउँ (I worshipped) / अमित (countless) / बार (times) / त्रिपुरारी (Tripurari) / भुज (arms) / बिक्रम (valor) / जानहिं (know) / दिगपाला (guardians of the directions) / सठ (fool) / अजहूँ (even now) / जिन्ह कें (whose) / उर (heart) / साला (ache, sting)
ramacharitamanas::4636.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4636.essence: Devotion loses its purity when it becomes proof of superiority.
ramacharitamanas::4636.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he has worshipped Shiva many times and that even the guardians of the directions know how powerful his arms are.
ramacharitamanas::4636.simple_insight: Pride can turn even devotion into a weapon for self-display.
ramacharitamanas::4636.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to intimidate his opponent with a flood of self-praise. He invokes his worship of Shiva and his battlefield strength, not to seek truth, but to inflate his own image before the war.
ramacharitamanas::4636.modern_relevance: You start listing your achievements in a tense conversation, hoping the other person will back down. The words may be true, but the need to prove yourself is already the problem.
ramacharitamanas::4636.insight: It exposes how ego borrows even sacred acts to defend itself.

ramacharitamanas::4637.verse_sanskrit: जानहिं दिग्गज उर कठिनाई। जब जब भिरउँ जाइ बरिआई॥ जिन्ह के दसन कराल न फूटे। उर लागत मूलक इव टूटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4637.verse_hindi: दिग्गज (दिशाओं के हाथी) मेरी छाती की कठोरता को जानते हैं। जिनके भयानक दाँत, जब-जब जाकर मैं उनसे जबरदस्ती भिड़ा, मेरी छाती में कभी नहीं फूटे (अपना चिह्न भी नहीं बना सके), बल्कि मेरी छाती से लगते ही वे मूली की तरह टूट गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4637.english_translation: The great elephants of the directions know my chest's hardness. When I fought them by force again and again, their terrible tusks never broke my chest; instead, they shattered like radishes against it.
ramacharitamanas::4637.translation_literal: जानहिं (know) / दिग्गज (direction-elephants) / उर (chest) / कठिनाई (hardness) / जब जब (again and again) / भिरउँ (I fought) / जाइ (going) / बरिआई (by force) / जिन्ह (whose) / के दसन (teeth) / कराल (terrible) / न (not) / फूटे (broke) / उर (on the chest) / लागत (touching) / मूलक (radish) / इव (like) / टूटे (broke)
ramacharitamanas::4637.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4637.essence: Hardness can become a boast that blinds you.
ramacharitamanas::4637.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that even the strongest beings could not break his chest in battle; their teeth shattered against him instead.
ramacharitamanas::4637.simple_insight: Pride makes a person measure worth by impact, not by wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4637.detailed_meaning: Ravana is still boasting in Lanka, trying to terrify his listeners with stories of his own invulnerability. He claims even the mighty direction-elephants could not wound him, turning strength into a display of ego before the war's final collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4637.modern_relevance: You keep listing the times you survived the worst blow, as if toughness proves you are right. Sometimes that very hardness is what keeps you from seeing clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4637.insight: It exposes how raw force and self-glorification can masquerade as strength while hiding inner blindness.

ramacharitamanas::4638.verse_sanskrit: जासु चलत डोलति इमि धरनी। चढ़त मत्त गज जिमि लघु तरनी॥ सोइ रावन जग बिदित प्रतापी। सुनेहि न श्रवन अलीक प्रलापी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4638.verse_hindi: जिसके चलते समय पृथ्वी इस प्रकार हिलती है जैसे मतवाले हाथी के चढ़ते समय छोटी नाव! मैं वही जगत प्रसिद्ध प्रतापी रावण हूँ। अरे झूठी बकवास करने वाले! क्या तूने मुझको कानों से कभी सुना? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4638.english_translation: As he walked, the earth trembled, just as a small boat rocks when a drunken elephant climbs aboard. I am that famous, mighty Ravana known throughout the world. Have you ever heard me with your own ears, you false babbler?
ramacharitamanas::4638.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / चलत (while walking) / डोलति (trembles) / इमि (thus) / धरनी (earth) / चढ़त (while climbing) / मत्त (drunken) / गज (elephant) / जिमि (like) / लघु (small) / तरनी (boat)॥ / सोइ (that very) / रावन (Ravana) / जग (world) / बिदित (known) / प्रतापी (mighty) / सुनेहि (have you heard) / न (not) / श्रवन (ears) / अलीक (false) / प्रलापी (babbler)॥
ramacharitamanas::4638.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4638.essence: Ego shouts its greatness and cannot hear the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4638.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his power shakes the earth and that his fame is known everywhere. He dismisses the speaker as a liar and pretends his own greatness proves everything.
ramacharitamanas::4638.simple_insight: Pride makes a person deaf to correction, even when the truth is standing right there.
ramacharitamanas::4638.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers Hanuman with bluster instead of listening. He inflates his own greatness, compares his power to an elephant shaking a boat, and mocks the messenger. The scene shows ego hardening just before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4638.modern_relevance: Someone interrupts you in a meeting and starts listing their achievements instead of hearing the warning in front of them. That reflex to defend status can block the very help that could save them.
ramacharitamanas::4638.insight: It exposes how self-importance turns listening into self-defense.

ramacharitamanas::4639.verse_sanskrit: तेहि रावन कहँ लघु कहसि नर कर करसि बखान। रे कपि बर्बर खर्ब खल अब जाना तव ग्यान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4639.verse_hindi: उस (महान प्रतापी और जगत प्रसिद्ध) रावण को (मुझे) तू छोटा कहता है और मनुष्य की बड़ाई करता है? अरे दुष्ट, असभ्य, तुच्छ बंदर! अब मैंने तेरा ज्ञान जान लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4639.english_translation: Why do you call Ravana small and praise a mere human? O vile, crude, worthless monkey, now I have understood your wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4639.translation_literal: तेहि (that) / रावन (Ravana) / कहँ (to) / लघु (small) / कहसि (you call) / नर (human) / कर (as) / करसि (you do) / बखान (praise) / रे (hey) / कपि (monkey) / बर्बर (crude) / खर्ब (worthless) / खल (vile one) / अब (now) / जाना (known) / तव (your) / ग्यान (wisdom)
ramacharitamanas::4639.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4639.essence: Pride cannot hear truth without feeling attacked.
ramacharitamanas::4639.simple_meaning: Ravana insults Angad for praising Ram and calling Ravana small. He takes the praise as an attack on his pride and dismisses Angad as foolish.
ramacharitamanas::4639.simple_insight: Pride hears correction as insult and misses its own blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4639.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has come as Ram's envoy and spoken with fearless dignity before Ravana's court. Ravana, stung by the comparison, lashes out and mocks Angad's understanding. The verse shows ego reacting before reason can enter.
ramacharitamanas::4639.modern_relevance: Someone points out a blind spot in a meeting, and you snap back at them instead of hearing the truth. Ravana's response is what wounded pride sounds like.
ramacharitamanas::4639.insight: It shows how ego turns honest challenge into contempt and blocks self-correction.

ramacharitamanas::4640.verse_sanskrit: सुनि अंगद सकोप कह बानी। बोलु संभारि अधम अभिमानी॥ सहसबाहु भुज गहन अपारा। दहन अनल सम जासु कुठारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4640.verse_hindi: रावण के ये वचन सुनकर अंगद क्रोध सहित वचन बोले- अरे नीच अभिमानी! सँभलकर (सोच-समझकर) बोल। जिनका फरसा सहस्रबाहु की भुजाओं रूपी अपार वन को जलाने के लिए अग्नि के समान था, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4640.english_translation: Hearing Ravana's words, Angada spoke in anger: "Speak carefully, you shameless fool. Parashurama's axe was like fire, burning through the boundless forest of Sahasrabahu's arms."
ramacharitamanas::4640.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / अंगद (Angada) / सकोप (with anger) / कह (said) / बानी (words, speech) / बोलु (speak) / संभारि (carefully, with restraint) / अधम (base, lowly) / अभिमानी (proud, ego-filled) / सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / भुज (arms) / गहन (dense, deep) / अपारा (boundless, immeasurable) / दहन (burning) / अनल (fire) / सम (like) / जासु (whose) / कुठारा (axe)
ramacharitamanas::4640.speaker: Angada
ramacharitamanas::4640.essence: Boastful pride meets a voice that refuses to bow.
ramacharitamanas::4640.simple_meaning: Angada angrily tells Ravana to speak carefully and calls him arrogant and lowly. He then praises Parashurama's axe as a fire that burned through Sahasrabahu's vast armory of power.
ramacharitamanas::4640.simple_insight: Pride gets answered with sharp correction, not polite silence.
ramacharitamanas::4640.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana boasts of his greatness. Angada, sent by Ram, answers in fury and warns him to choose his words carefully. He then invokes Parashurama's terrible axe as proof that arrogance can be cut down.
ramacharitamanas::4640.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting starts bragging so loudly that the room tightens. You don't have to flatter that energy. Sometimes the clean response is a firm correction.
ramacharitamanas::4640.insight: It shows how righteous anger can interrupt ego before it spreads.

ramacharitamanas::4641.verse_sanskrit: जासु परसु सागर खर धारा। बूड़े नृप अगनित बहु बारा॥ तासु गर्ब जेहि देखत भागा। सो नर क्यों दससीस अभागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4641.verse_hindi: जिनके फरसा रूपी समुद्र की तीव्र धारा में अनगिनत राजा अनेकों बार डूब गए, उन परशुरामजी का गर्व जिन्हें देखते ही भाग गया, अरे अभागे दशशीश! वे मनुष्य क्यों कर हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4641.english_translation: The fierce stream of Parashurama's axe has sunk countless kings many times. Even his pride fled at the sight of him. Why, then, can that unlucky ten-headed one call him a mere man?
ramacharitamanas::4641.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / परसु (axe) / सागर (ocean) / खर (fierce) / धारा (current) / बूड़े (were drowned) / नृप (kings) / अगनित (countless) / बहु (many) / बारा (times)॥ / तासु (his) / गर्ब (pride) / जेहि (whose) / देखत (seeing) / भागा (fled) / सो (that) / नर (man) / क्यों (how) / दससीस (ten-headed one) / अभागा (unlucky one)॥
ramacharitamanas::4641.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4641.essence: Pride cannot recognize the power that will undo it.
ramacharitamanas::4641.simple_meaning: Angad reminds Ravana that Parashurama is no ordinary man: his axe has destroyed many kings, and even pride itself would flee before him. Ravana is foolish to dismiss such power.
ramacharitamanas::4641.simple_insight: Arrogance makes you blind to danger right in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4641.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war council, Angad answers Ravana's insult with biting force. He invokes Parashurama's terrifying reputation to expose Ravana's stupidity: a ruler who once humbled countless kings is not someone to mock.
ramacharitamanas::4641.modern_relevance: You brush off a warning because you think you already know better. Then the room goes quiet, and you realise the person you dismissed had every reason to be feared.
ramacharitamanas::4641.insight: It exposes how pride distorts judgment and invites self-destruction.

ramacharitamanas::4642.verse_sanskrit: राम मनुज कस रे सठ बंगा। धन्वी कामु नदी पुनि गंगा॥ पसु सुरधेनु कल्पतरु रूखा। अन्न दान अरु रस पीयूषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4642.verse_hindi: क्यों रे मूर्ख उद्दण्ड! श्री रामचंद्रजी मनुष्य हैं? कामदेव भी क्या धनुर्धारी है? और गंगाजी क्या नदी हैं? कामधेनु क्या पशु है? और कल्पवृक्ष क्या पेड़ है? अन्न भी क्या दान है? और अमृत क्या रस है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4642.english_translation: How can you say Ram is merely a man, you fool? Is desire merely an archer, is the Ganges merely a river? Is Kamadhenu merely an animal, is the wish-fulfilling tree merely a tree? Is giving merely food, is nectar merely a drink?
ramacharitamanas::4642.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / मनुज (human) / कस (how) / रे (hey) / सठ (fool) / बंगा (crooked) / धन्वी (archer) / कामु (desire) / नदी (river) / पुनि (again) / गंगा (Ganga) / पसु (animal) / सुरधेनु (Kamadhenu) / कल्पतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / रूखा (tree) / अन्न (food) / दान (gift) / अरु (and) / रस (juice/drink) / पीयूषा (nectar)
ramacharitamanas::4642.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4642.essence: Ram cannot be reduced to an ordinary human life.
ramacharitamanas::4642.simple_meaning: Angad rebukes Ravana for reducing Ram to an ordinary man. He says sacred things cannot be judged by surface appearances, because their true power is far greater.
ramacharitamanas::4642.simple_insight: Respect deepens when you stop measuring the divine by ordinary categories.
ramacharitamanas::4642.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Angad answers Ravana's insult with sharp devotion. He stacks up sacred comparisons to show that Ram cannot be reduced to a human label. The verse is a protest against spiritual blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4642.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses a mentor, parent, or quiet devotee because they look unimpressive. Later, their strength, grace, or wisdom changes the room. This verse warns you not to mistake appearance for worth.
ramacharitamanas::4642.insight: It shifts the mind from literal appearance to hidden greatness.

ramacharitamanas::4643.verse_sanskrit: बैनतेय खग अहि सहसानन। चिंतामनि पुनि उपल दसानन॥ सुनु मतिमंद लोक बैकुंठा। लाभ कि रघुपति भगति अकुंठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4643.verse_hindi: गरुड़जी क्या पक्षी हैं? शेषजी क्या सर्प हैं? अरे रावण! चिंतामणि भी क्या पत्थर है? अरे ओ मूर्ख! सुन, वैकुण्ठ भी क्या लोक है? और श्री रघुनाथजी की अखण्ड भक्ति क्या (और लाभों जैसा ही) लाभ है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4643.english_translation: Is Garuda merely a bird? Is Shesha merely a serpent? O Ravana, is even the wish-fulfilling gem just a stone? O dull-minded one, listen: is Vaikuntha merely a realm, and is devoted love for Raghunath not the greatest gain?
ramacharitamanas::4643.translation_literal: बैनतेय (Garuda) / खग (bird) / अहि (serpent) / सहसानन (Shesha, thousand-faced one) / चिंतामनि (wish-fulfilling gem) / पुनि (again) / उपल (stone) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / सुनु (listen) / मतिमंद (dull-minded one) / लोक (realm) / बैकुंठा (Vaikuntha) / लाभ (gain) / कि (whether) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / भगति (devoted love) / अकुंठा (unwavering, unbounded)
ramacharitamanas::4643.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4643.essence: Devotion to Ram makes every lesser prize look small.
ramacharitamanas::4643.simple_meaning: Garuda is not just a bird, Shesha is not just a serpent, and Vaikuntha is not the only prize. Devoted love for Ram is the greatest gain of all.
ramacharitamanas::4643.simple_insight: What looks ordinary becomes priceless when it is joined to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4643.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the poem turns from mocking Ravana to praising devotion. Tulsidas says Garuda is more than a bird, Shesha more than a serpent, and even the wish-fulfilling gem is more than a stone. Then he lands the real point: loving Ram is the greatest gain.
ramacharitamanas::4643.modern_relevance: You can chase a promotion, a perfect address, or a bigger bank balance and still feel empty. Then one quiet practice of love and remembrance changes what counts as wealth.
ramacharitamanas::4643.insight: It shifts the mind from status and objects to the value of unwavering devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4644.verse_sanskrit: सेन सहित तव मान मथि बन उजारि पुर जारि। कस रे सठ हनुमान कपि गयउ जो तव सुत मारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4644.verse_hindi: सेना समेत तेरा मान मथकर, अशोक वन को उजाड़कर, नगर को जलाकर और तेरे पुत्र को मारकर जो लौट गए (तू उनका कुछ भी न बिगाड़ सका), क्यों रे दुष्ट! वे हनुमान् जी क्या वानर हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4644.english_translation: You fool! After Hanuman, with his army, churned up your pride, ruined the Ashoka grove, burned the city, and killed your son, do you still ask what kind of monkey he is?
ramacharitamanas::4644.translation_literal: सेन सहित (with army) / तव (your) / मान (pride) / मथि (churning up) / बन (grove/forest) / उजारि (destroying) / पुर (city) / जारि (burning) / कस रे सठ (why, fool) / हनुमान कपि (Hanuman, monkey) / गयउ (went) / जो (who) / तव सुत (your son) / मारि (killed)
ramacharitamanas::4644.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4644.essence: Pride keeps asking questions reality has already answered.
ramacharitamanas::4644.simple_meaning: Ravana is mocked for still doubting Hanuman's power after Hanuman has already devastated Lanka and killed his son.
ramacharitamanas::4644.simple_insight: Pride can stay blind even after reality has already struck it hard.
ramacharitamanas::4644.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has already exposed Ravana's weakness. Hanuman has torn through the Ashoka grove, burned the city, and killed Ravana's son. Yet Ravana still speaks with arrogance, and the poet sharpens the insult to show how delusion survives defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4644.modern_relevance: You ignore the warning signs, then act shocked when the damage is already done. Pride can make even obvious consequences feel unreal.
ramacharitamanas::4644.insight: It exposes how ego keeps arguing even after it has been proven wrong.

ramacharitamanas::4645.verse_sanskrit: सुनु रावन परिहरि चतुराई। भजसि न कृपासिंधु रघुराई॥ जौं खल भएसि राम कर द्रोही। ब्रह्म रुद्र सक राखि न तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4645.verse_hindi: अरे रावण! चतुराई (कपट) छोड़कर सुन। कृपा के समुद्र श्री रघुनाथजी का तू भजन क्यों नहीं करता? अरे दुष्ट! यदि तू श्री रामजी का वैरी हुआ तो तुझे ब्रह्मा और रुद्र भी नहीं बचा सकेंगे।
ramacharitamanas::4645.english_translation: Ravana, give up your cleverness and worship compassionate Raghunath. If you become an enemy of Ram, even Brahma and Rudra cannot save you.
ramacharitamanas::4645.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / रावन (Ravana) / परिहरि (giving up) / चतुराई (cleverness, cunning) / भजसि (you worship) / न (not) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / रघुराई (Raghunath) ॥ जौं (if) / खल (wicked one) / भएसि (you become) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / द्रोही (enemy) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / रुद्र (Rudra) / सक (even) / राखि (save) / न (not) / तोही (you) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4645.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4645.essence: Cleverness cannot save you from opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4645.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned to stop being clever and turn to Ram in devotion. If he chooses enmity instead, no higher power can protect him.
ramacharitamanas::4645.simple_insight: Pride can make you feel powerful right up until it leaves you exposed.
ramacharitamanas::4645.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already been warned many times, but he still clings to his own brilliance. Tulsidas cuts through that arrogance here: Ram is compassionate, yet opposition to him is self-destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4645.modern_relevance: You keep drafting the perfect reply, trying to win the argument by being sharper than everyone else. This verse says that kind of cleverness can still leave you helpless.
ramacharitamanas::4645.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection through control to safety through devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4646.verse_sanskrit: मूढ़ बृथा जनि मारसि गाला। राम बयर अस होइहि हाला॥ तव सिर निकर कपिन्ह के आगें। परिहहिं धरनि राम सर लागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4646.verse_hindi: हे मूढ़! व्यर्थ गाल न मार (डींग न हाँक)। श्री रामजी से वैर करने पर तेरा ऐसा हाल होगा कि तेरे सिर समूह श्री रामजी के बाण लगते ही वानरों के आगे पृथ्वी पर पड़ेंगे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4646.english_translation: O fool, stop your empty boasting. If you oppose Ram, this will be your end: your heads will fall before the monkeys when Ram's arrows strike you.
ramacharitamanas::4646.translation_literal: मूढ़ (fool) / बृथा (useless, empty) / जनि (do not) / मारसि (strike, boast) / गाला (boasts, empty talk) / राम (Ram) / बयर (enmity) / अस (such) / होइहि (will become) / हाला (state, condition) / तव (your) / सिर (heads) / निकर (group, multitude) / कपिन्ह (of monkeys) / के आगें (in front) / परिहहिं (will fall) / धरनि (on the ground) / राम (Ram) / सर (arrows) / लागें (when struck)
ramacharitamanas::4646.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4646.essence: Boasting cannot save you from the result of your own defiance.
ramacharitamanas::4646.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that his empty boasting will end in disaster if he keeps opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4646.simple_insight: Pride sounds powerful until reality answers it.
ramacharitamanas::4646.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps boasting after Hanuman's destruction and before the final war. The warning is blunt: Ram's arrows will bring his heads crashing down before the monkey army. The verse strips away Ravana's arrogance and shows the cost of defying dharma.
ramacharitamanas::4646.modern_relevance: You keep arguing in the group chat like words can protect you. But some battles are already lost the moment pride takes over.
ramacharitamanas::4646.insight: It exposes ego as self-destructive and shifts the mind from bravado to consequence.

ramacharitamanas::4647.verse_sanskrit: ते तव सिर कंदुक सम नाना। खेलिहहिं भालु कीस चौगाना॥ जबहिं समर कोपिहि रघुनायक। छुटिहहिं अति कराल बहु सायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4647.verse_hindi: और रीछ-वानर तेरे उन गेंद के समान अनेकों सिरों से चौगान खेलेंगे। जब श्री रघुनाथजी युद्ध में कोप करेंगे और उनके अत्यंत तीक्ष्ण बहुत से बाण छूटेंगे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4647.english_translation: The bears and monkeys will play with your many heads like balls. When Raghunath grows angry in battle, many terrible arrows will fly.
ramacharitamanas::4647.translation_literal: ते (those) / तव (your) / सिर (heads) / कंदुक (ball) / सम (like) / नाना (many) / खेलिहहिं (will play) / भालु (bears) / कीस (monkeys) / चौगाना (at the game of polo) ॥ जबहिं (when) / समर (battle) / कोपिहि (will become angry) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / छुटिहहिं (will be released) / अति (very) / कराल (terrible) / बहु (many) / सायक (arrows) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4647.speaker: Angada
ramacharitamanas::4647.essence: Arrogance is already losing before the arrows fly.
ramacharitamanas::4647.simple_meaning: Angada warns Ravana that his many heads will be treated like balls by the monkeys and bears, and that Ram's arrows will be deadly in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4647.simple_insight: Pride looks powerful until reality answers it.
ramacharitamanas::4647.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Angada stands before Ravana and keeps pressing him to surrender. He describes the coming defeat in brutal, vivid images: the monkey and bear armies will mock his many heads, and Ram's arrows will tear through the war.
ramacharitamanas::4647.modern_relevance: You keep bluffing in a tense meeting, but everyone can see the numbers on the screen. Confidence without reality collapses the moment the hard facts arrive.
ramacharitamanas::4647.insight: It turns Ravana's swagger into a warning: arrogance invites humiliation and destruction.

ramacharitamanas::4648.verse_sanskrit: तब कि चलिहि अस गाल तुम्हारा। अस बिचारि भजु राम उदारा॥ सुनत बचन रावन परजरा। जरत महानल जनु घृत परा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4648.verse_hindi: तब क्या तेरा गाल चलेगा? ऐसा विचार कर उदार (कृपालु) श्री रामजी को भज। अंगद के ये वचन सुनकर रावण बहुत अधिक जल उठा। मानो जलती हुई प्रचण्ड अग्नि में घी पड़ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4648.english_translation: Then what will your boasting achieve? Think this through and worship noble Ram. Hearing Angad's words, Ravana burned even hotter, like ghee poured into a blazing fire.
ramacharitamanas::4648.translation_literal: तब (then) / कि (what) / चलिहि (will work) / अस (such) / गाल (boasting) / तुम्हारा (your) / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / भजु (worship) / राम (Ram) / उदारा (noble, generous) ॥ / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / रावन (Ravana) / परजरा (burned fiercely) / जरत (burning) / महानल (great fire) / जनु (as if) / घृत (ghee) / परा (was poured) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4648.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4648.essence: Boasting collapses before truth; pride answers with fire.
ramacharitamanas::4648.simple_meaning: Angad tells Ravana to stop boasting and turn to Ram instead. Ravana only grows angrier when he hears it.
ramacharitamanas::4648.simple_insight: Pride cannot hear correction; it only burns brighter when challenged.
ramacharitamanas::4648.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court in Lanka, Angad refuses to be intimidated and speaks bluntly: empty boasting will not save anyone, so turn to generous Ram. Ravana hears the rebuke and flares with rage instead of reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4648.modern_relevance: You get called out in a meeting and feel your face go hot before you even answer. The sharper the truth, the more your ego may resist it.
ramacharitamanas::4648.insight: It shows how ego reacts to truth with heat, not humility.

ramacharitamanas::4649.verse_sanskrit: कुंभकरन अस बंधु मम सुत प्रसिद्ध सक्रारि। मोर पराक्रम नहिं सुनेहि जितेऊँ चराचर झारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4649.verse_hindi: (वह बोला- अरे मूर्ख!) कुंभकर्ण- ऐसा मेरा भाई है, इन्द्र का शत्रु सुप्रसिद्ध मेघनाद मेरा पुत्र है! और मेरा पराक्रम तो तूने सुना ही नहीं कि मैंने संपूर्ण जड़-चेतन जगत् को जीत लिया है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4649.english_translation: My brother is Kumbhakarna, and my son is the famed enemy of Indra. You have not even heard of my power, by which I have conquered all moving and unmoving beings.
ramacharitamanas::4649.translation_literal: कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / अस (such) / बंधु (brother) / मम (my) / सुत (son) / प्रसिद्ध (famed) / सक्रारि (enemy of Indra) / मोर (my) / पराक्रम (power, valor) / नहिं (not) / सुनेहि (you have heard) / जितेऊँ (I conquered) / चराचर (moving and unmoving beings) / झारि (all, utterly)
ramacharitamanas::4649.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4649.essence: Conquest means nothing when the mind still needs to boast.
ramacharitamanas::4649.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts about his family and his supposed conquest of the whole world. He is trying to overwhelm Angad with pride instead of answering his challenge honestly.
ramacharitamanas::4649.simple_insight: Boasting often hides fear. When you need to prove everything, you are already losing inner steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::4649.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just wounded Ravana's pride and urged him to surrender to Ram. Ravana answers with arrogance, naming Kumbhakarna and Meghnad and claiming he has conquered all creation. The verse shows ego trying to cover its own weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4649.modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting and someone challenges your plan. Instead of listening, you start listing your wins, your title, your past victories. The louder the defense, the more fragile it feels.
ramacharitamanas::4649.insight: It shifts attention from outward bragging to the insecurity underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::4650.verse_sanskrit: सठ साखामृग जोरि सहाई। बाँधा सिंधु इहइ प्रभुताई॥ नाघहिं खग अनेक बारीसा। सूर न होहिं ते सुनु सब कीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4650.verse_hindi: रे दुष्ट! वानरों की सहायता जोड़कर राम ने समुद्र बाँध लिया, बस, यही उसकी प्रभुता है। समुद्र को तो अनेकों पक्षी भी लाँघ जाते हैं। पर इसी से वे सभी शूरवीर नहीं हो जाते। अरे मूर्ख बंदर! सुन- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4650.english_translation: You fool! Ram built a bridge across the ocean with the help of the monkey army — that is his true power. Many birds can cross the sea, but that does not make them heroes.
ramacharitamanas::4650.translation_literal: सठ (fool) / साखामृग (monkey-animals) / जोरि (joining) / सहाई (help) / बाँधा (built) / सिंधु (the ocean) / इहइ (this only) / प्रभुताई (lordship, power)॥ / नाघहिं (cross) / खग (birds) / अनेक (many) / बारीसा (the sea) / सूर (heroes) / न होहिं (are not) / ते (they) / सुनु (listen) / सब (all) / कीसा (monkeys)॥
ramacharitamanas::4650.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4650.essence: Pride belittles what it cannot equal.
ramacharitamanas::4650.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman by saying Ram's greatness is not real strength, since birds can cross the ocean too.
ramacharitamanas::4650.simple_insight: Pride always tries to shrink what it cannot match.
ramacharitamanas::4650.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trapped in wounded arrogance after Hanuman's message. He scoffs at the monkey army and belittles Ram's bridge over the sea, trying to turn a miraculous act into a cheap trick before the argument continues.
ramacharitamanas::4650.modern_relevance: Someone online dismisses your months of work with one snide comment: 'Anyone could have done that.' Ravana's voice is the voice that cannot bear another's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4650.insight: It exposes the mind of ego: it explains away achievement instead of facing it.

ramacharitamanas::4651.verse_sanskrit: मम भुज सागर बल जल पूरा। जहँ बूड़े बहु सुर नर सूरा॥ बीस पयोधि अगाध अपारा। को अस बीर जो पाइहि पारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4651.verse_hindi: मेरा एक-एक भुजा रूपी समुद्र बल रूपी जल से पूर्ण है, जिसमें बहुत से शूरवीर देवता और मनुष्य डूब चूके हैं। (बता,) कौन ऐसा शूरवीर है, जो मेरे इन अथाह और अपार बीस समुद्रों का पार पा जाएगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4651.english_translation: My arms are like oceans, full of the water of strength. Many gods, humans, and heroes have drowned in them. Who is the warrior who can cross my twenty boundless, unfathomable oceans?
ramacharitamanas::4651.translation_literal: मम (my) / भुज (arms) / सागर (oceans) / बल (strength) / जल (water) / पूरा (full) / जहँ (where) / बूड़े (drowned) / बहु (many) / सुर (radiant beings) / नर (humans) / सूरा (heroes) / बीस (twenty) / पयोधि (oceans) / अगाध (unfathomable) / अपारा (without shore) / को (who) / अस (such) / बीर (warrior) / जो (who) / पाइहि (will find) / पारा (the far shore)
ramacharitamanas::4651.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4651.essence: Pride turns strength into a boast that cannot save you.
ramacharitamanas::4651.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his strength is immense and that many powerful beings have already fallen before him. He asks who could possibly survive or cross his twenty boundless oceans of power.
ramacharitamanas::4651.simple_insight: Pride makes a person feel untouchable, even as that pride is already closing in on defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4651.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers Hanuman's challenge with raw arrogance. He turns his own body into a threat, boasting that even gods and heroes have been swallowed by his power. The verse deepens the confrontation before the real fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::4651.modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing every win, every influence, every person who has backed down before them. The volume is high because the fear underneath is even higher.
ramacharitamanas::4651.insight: It exposes how ego inflates strength into a shield and mistakes intimidation for real power.

ramacharitamanas::4652.verse_sanskrit: दिगपालन्ह मैं नीर भरावा। भूप सुजस खल मोहि सुनावा॥ जौं पै समर सुभट तव नाथा। पुनि पुनि कहसि जासु गुन गाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4652.verse_hindi: अरे दुष्ट! मैंने दिक्पालों तक से जल भरवाया और तू एक राजा का मुझे सुयश सुनाता है! यदि तेरा मालिक, जिसकी गुणगाथा तू बार-बार कह रहा है, संग्राम में लड़ने वाला योद्धा है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4652.english_translation: I made the guardians of the directions pour water for me, and you boast of a king's fame to me! If your master, whose praises you keep repeating, is a warrior in battle—
ramacharitamanas::4652.translation_literal: दिगपालन्ह (by the guardians of the directions) / मैं (for me) / नीर (water) / भरावा (was made to fill) / भूप (king's) / सुजस (good fame) / खल (wicked one) / मोहि (to me) / सुनावा (you told) / जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / समर (in battle) / सुभट (warrior) / तव (your) / नाथा (master) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कहसि (you speak) / जासु (whose) / गुन गाथा (praise-song of virtues)
ramacharitamanas::4652.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4652.essence: Ego hears praise of another as an insult to itself.
ramacharitamanas::4652.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he has power over cosmic forces and mocks the messenger for praising a king's fame. He challenges the claim by asking whether that king is really a fighter in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4652.simple_insight: Pride makes you dismiss what you cannot yet understand.
ramacharitamanas::4652.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is ridiculing Hanuman's praise of Ram. He boasts of his own grandeur, claiming even the guardians of the directions serve him, and tries to belittle Ram by asking whether this praised king can fight at all.
ramacharitamanas::4652.modern_relevance: Someone on a group chat keeps mocking the person you admire, waving around their own status like proof. The verse captures that reflex to belittle what threatens your ego.
ramacharitamanas::4652.insight: It shows how arrogance turns conversation into a contest of status instead of a search for truth.

ramacharitamanas::4653.verse_sanskrit: तौ बसीठ पठवत केहि काजा। रिपु सन प्रीति करत नहिं लाजा॥ हरगिरि मथन निरखु मम बाहू। पुनि सठ कपि निज प्रभुहि सराहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4653.verse_hindi: तो (फिर) वह दूत किसलिए भेजता है? शत्रु से प्रीति (सन्धि) करते उसे लाज नहीं आती? (पहले) कैलास का मथन करने वाली मेरी भुजाओं को देख। फिर अरे मूर्ख वानर! अपने मालिक की सराहना करना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4653.english_translation: Then why send an envoy? Does he feel no shame making peace with an enemy? Look at my arms that churned Mount Kailash. Then, fool of a monkey, praise your own lord.
ramacharitamanas::4653.translation_literal: तौ (then) / बसीठ (envoy) / पठवत (sending) / केहि (for what) / काजा (purpose) / रिपु (enemy) / सन (with) / प्रीति (friendship) / करत (making) / नहिं (not) / लाजा (shame)॥ / हरगिरि (mountain of Shiva) / मथन (churning) / निरखु (look at) / मम (my) / बाहू (arms)॥ / पुनि (then) / सठ (fool) / कपि (monkey) / निज (your own) / प्रभुहि (lord) / सराहू (praise)॥
ramacharitamanas::4653.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4653.essence: Ego cannot meet a challenge without boasting.
ramacharitamanas::4653.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Hanuman, asking why anyone would send an envoy to an enemy and boasting of his own strength before telling Hanuman to praise his own lord.
ramacharitamanas::4653.simple_insight: Pride turns even a warning into self-display.
ramacharitamanas::4653.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been captured and brought before Ravana. Ravana is furious and boasts of his own power, mocking the idea of sending a messenger to an enemy. This is not a teaching verse but a sharp piece of confrontation in the middle of the war scene.
ramacharitamanas::4653.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting and turns every answer into a chance to brag about themselves. The real issue disappears under ego.
ramacharitamanas::4653.insight: It shows how wounded pride attacks the messenger instead of facing the message.

ramacharitamanas::4654.verse_sanskrit: सूर कवन रावन सरिस स्वकर काटि जेहिं सीस। हुने अनल अति हरष बहु बार साखि गौरीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4654.verse_hindi: रावण के समान शूरवीर कौन है? जिसने अपने हाथों से सिर काट-काटकर अत्यंत हर्ष के साथ बहुत बार उन्हें अग्नि में होम दिया! स्वयं गौरीपति शिवजी इस बात के साक्षी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4654.english_translation: Who is as brave as Ravana, who cut off his own heads with his own hands and offered them into the fire again and again in great joy? Lord Shiva himself is witness to this.
ramacharitamanas::4654.translation_literal: सूर (brave one) / कवन (who) / रावन (Ravana) / सरिस (like) / स्वकर (with his own hands) / काटि (cutting off) / जेहिं (who) / सीस (heads) / हुने (offered) / अनल (in fire) / अति (greatly) / हरष (joy) / बहु बार (many times) / साखि (witness) / गौरीस (Lord of Gauri)
ramacharitamanas::4654.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4654.essence: Ego can glorify even its own destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4654.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that no one is as brave as he is, because he once cut off his own heads and offered them into fire with delight. He uses Shiva as a witness to his arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4654.simple_insight: Pride can turn suffering into a trophy and call it courage.
ramacharitamanas::4654.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers the envoy with inflated self-praise, trying to overwhelm the challenge before him. He boasts of terrifying feats and invokes Shiva as witness. The verse exposes ego that mistakes self-harm for greatness.
ramacharitamanas::4654.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the hardest thing you survived like it proves you’re untouchable. Sometimes the mind turns pain into a badge and calls it power.
ramacharitamanas::4654.insight: It teaches you to notice when bravado is just ego defending itself.

ramacharitamanas::4655.verse_sanskrit: जरत बिलोकेउँ जबहि कपाला। बिधि के लिखे अंक निज भाला॥ नर कें कर आपन बध बाँची। हसेउँ जानि बिधि गिरा असाँची ॥
ramacharitamanas::4655.verse_hindi: मस्तकों के जलते समय जब मैंने अपने ललाटों पर लिखे हुए विधाता के अक्षर देखे, तब मनुष्य के हाथ से अपनी मृत्यु होना बाँचकर, विधाता की वाणी (लेख को) असत्य जानकर मैं हँसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4655.english_translation: When I saw the skulls burning, and the marks of fate written on my forehead, I laughed, knowing that death by a human hand had been escaped and that the words of fate were false.
ramacharitamanas::4655.translation_literal: जरत (burning) / बिलोकेउँ (I saw) / जबहि (when) / कपाला (skulls) / बिधि (fate) / के (of) / लिखे (written) / अंक (marks) / निज (my own) / भाला (forehead) / नर (human) / कें (by) / कर (hand) / आपन (my own) / बध (death) / बाँची (escaped) / हसेउँ (I laughed) / जानि (knowing) / बिधि (fate) / गिरा (speech/words) / असाँची (false)
ramacharitamanas::4655.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4655.essence: Ego laughs at warning signs until reality answers.
ramacharitamanas::4655.simple_meaning: Ravana laughs at the idea that fate controls him. He believes he has escaped death at human hands and treats destiny itself as false.
ramacharitamanas::4655.simple_insight: Pride can make you laugh at danger right before it closes in.
ramacharitamanas::4655.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is boasting after seeing burning skulls and reading the marks on his own forehead. He thinks he has already outsmarted death and mocks the written decree of fate, revealing the arrogance that will soon destroy him.
ramacharitamanas::4655.modern_relevance: You ignore the warning signs because you think you are still untouchable. That confident laugh can be the last thing standing before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4655.insight: It exposes the blindness of ego: when you trust your own invincibility, you stop seeing the truth in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::4656.verse_sanskrit: सोउ मन समुझि त्रास नहिं मोरें। लिखा बिरंचि जरठ मति भोरें॥ आन बीर बल सठ मम आगें। पुनि पुनि कहसि लाज पति त्यागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4656.verse_hindi: उस बात को समझकर (स्मरण करके) भी मेरे मन में डर नहीं है। (क्योंकि मैं समझता हूँ कि) बूढ़े ब्रह्मा ने बुद्धि भ्रम से ऐसा लिख दिया है। अरे मूर्ख! तू लज्जा और मर्यादा छोड़कर मेरे आगे बार-बार दूसरे वीर का बल कहता है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4656.english_translation: Knowing that, I still feel no fear. Old Brahma must have written this in a clouded mind. Fool, you keep speaking before me of another warrior's strength, abandoning shame and restraint again and again!
ramacharitamanas::4656.translation_literal: सोउ (that) / मन (mind) / समुझि (understanding) / त्रास (fear) / नहिं (not) / मोरें (for me) । लिखा (written) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / जरठ (old) / मति (mind/intellect) / भोरें (in confusion) ॥ आन (other) / बीर (warrior) / बल (strength) / सठ (fool) / मम (my) / आगें (before) । पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कहसि (you say) / लाज (shame) / पति (restraint/modesty) / त्यागें (abandoning) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4656.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4656.essence: Pride hears warning as an insult and learns nothing.
ramacharitamanas::4656.simple_meaning: Ravana says he feels no fear, dismisses fate as a confused mistake, and insults the speaker for repeatedly praising another warrior instead of showing proper restraint.
ramacharitamanas::4656.simple_insight: Pride can make you mock what you most need to hear.
ramacharitamanas::4656.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana answers Angada’s warning with contempt. Instead of reflecting, he brags that no fear touches him and blames Brahma for his fate. The verse deepens his arrogance before Angada exposes it.
ramacharitamanas::4656.modern_relevance: Someone keeps warning you that your plan is collapsing, but you brush it off and double down. Ravana is that moment when ego turns every correction into an insult.
ramacharitamanas::4656.insight: It shows how wounded pride blocks self-correction and turns wise counsel into provocation.

ramacharitamanas::4657.verse_sanskrit: कह अंगद सलज्ज जग माहीं। रावन तोहि समान कोउ नाहीं॥ लाजवंत तव सहज सुभाऊ। निज मुख निज गुन कहसि न काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4657.verse_hindi: अंगद ने कहा- अरे रावण! तेरे समान लज्जावान् जगत् में कोई नहीं है। लज्जाशीलता तो तेरा सहज स्वभाव ही है। तू अपने मुँह से अपने गुण कभी नहीं कहता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4657.english_translation: Angada said, 'Ravana, there is no one in the world like you in modesty. Shyness is your natural nature. You never speak of your own virtues yourself.'
ramacharitamanas::4657.translation_literal: कह (said) / अंगद (Angada) / सलज्ज (modest) / जग माहीं (in the world) / रावन (Ravana) / तोहि (to you) / समान (like) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (is not) ॥ / लाजवंत (shy/modest) / तव (your) / सहज (natural) / सुभाऊ (nature) / निज (own) / मुख (mouth) / निज (own) / गुन (virtues) / कहसि (you speak) / न काऊ (never) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4657.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4657.essence: Mock praise can reveal pride more sharply than accusation.
ramacharitamanas::4657.simple_meaning: Angad sarcastically praises Ravana, mocking his arrogance by calling him modest and saying he never boasts about himself.
ramacharitamanas::4657.simple_insight: Sometimes praise can be the sharpest way to expose pride.
ramacharitamanas::4657.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana as an envoy and taunts him with bitter irony. The exchange is part of a larger confrontation where Ravana’s pride is being cornered from every side, and Angad uses mock praise to strip away his self-image.
ramacharitamanas::4657.modern_relevance: In a tense meeting, someone says, “Of course you never need credit,” and the room goes quiet. Everyone hears the sarcasm. Angad is doing that on a battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4657.insight: It shows how irony can puncture ego without a direct lecture.

ramacharitamanas::4658.verse_sanskrit: सिर अरु सैल कथा चित रही। ताते बार बीस तैं कहीं॥ सो भुजबल राखेहु उर घाली। जीतेहु सहसबाहु बलि बाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4658.verse_hindi: सिर काटने और कैलास उठाने की कथा चित्त में चढ़ी हुई थी, इससे तूने उसे बीसों बार कहा। भुजाओं के उस बल को तूने हृदय में ही टाल (छिपा) रखा है, जिससे तूने सहस्रबाहु, बलि और बालि को जीता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4658.english_translation: The story of cutting off heads and lifting Mount Kailash has stayed in your mind, so you have said it twenty times. You kept that arm-strength hidden in your heart, the strength that defeated Sahasrabahu, Bali, and Vali.
ramacharitamanas::4658.translation_literal: सिर (head) / अरु (and) / सैल (mountain) / कथा (story) / चित (in the mind) / रही (remained) / ताते (therefore) / बार (times) / बीस (twenty) / तैं (by you) / कहीं (said)॥ / सो (that) / भुजबल (arm-strength) / राखेहु (you kept) / उर (in the heart) / घाली (placing) / जीतेहु (you defeated) / सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / बलि (Bali) / बाली (Vali)॥
ramacharitamanas::4658.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4658.essence: Boasts about old feats mean little without present courage.
ramacharitamanas::4658.simple_meaning: Angad mocks Ravana for repeating old boasts about cutting off heads and lifting mountains. He says Ravana has hidden the real strength of his arms, the strength that once defeated powerful kings and warriors.
ramacharitamanas::4658.simple_insight: Empty boasting cannot replace real courage.
ramacharitamanas::4658.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad is challenging Ravana before the final war. Ravana keeps repeating tales of his past feats, but Angad turns them against him, saying the true test is not stories but present courage. This is sharp taunting, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4658.modern_relevance: Someone keeps bringing up what they did years ago, but the room can feel the gap between memory and current strength. Angad’s words cut through that performance.
ramacharitamanas::4658.insight: It exposes how bravado can hide fear and how past victories do not prove present power.

ramacharitamanas::4659.verse_sanskrit: सुनु मतिमंद देहि अब पूरा। काटें सीस कि होइअ सूरा॥ इंद्रजालि कहुँ कहिअ न बीरा। काटइ निज कर सकल सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4659.verse_hindi: अरे मंद बुद्धि! सुन, अब बस कर। सिर काटने से भी क्या कोई शूरवीर हो जाता है? इंद्रजाल रचने वाले को वीर नहीं कहा जाता, यद्यपि वह अपने ही हाथों अपना सारा शरीर काट डालता है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4659.english_translation: Listen, fool, enough now. Does cutting off a head make someone brave? A magician is not called a hero, even if he cuts up his own body with his own hands.
ramacharitamanas::4659.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / मतिमंद (foolish one) / देहि (give) / अब (now) / पूरा (enough, full) / काटें (by cutting) / सीस (head) / कि (does) / होइअ (become) / सूरा (heroic) / इंद्रजालि (magician, illusion-maker) / कहुँ (for) / कहिअ (is called) / न (not) / बीरा (hero) / काटइ (cuts) / निज (own) / कर (hand) / सकल (all) / सरीरा (body)
ramacharitamanas::4659.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4659.essence: Courage is not proved by spectacle or self-harm.
ramacharitamanas::4659.simple_meaning: Bravery is not proved by dramatic self-harm or showy tricks. Real courage is something deeper than a violent display.
ramacharitamanas::4659.simple_insight: You do not become strong by hurting yourself for appearances.
ramacharitamanas::4659.detailed_meaning: Angad is mocking Ravana in Lanka after exposing his empty boasting. He says that cutting off heads or performing illusion-like feats does not make anyone brave. The verse pushes Ravana’s pride toward humiliation before the war turns fully against him.
ramacharitamanas::4659.modern_relevance: You post a dramatic apology, a fierce rant, or a self-destructive stunt and hope it proves something. It does not. Performance is not courage.
ramacharitamanas::4659.insight: It separates real courage from theatrical display and self-inflicted damage.

ramacharitamanas::4660.verse_sanskrit: जरहिं पतंग मोह बस भार बहहिं खर बृंद। ते नहिं सूर कहावहिं समुझि देखु मतिमंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::4660.verse_hindi: अरे मंद बुद्धि! समझकर देख। पतंगे मोहवश आग में जल मरते हैं, गदहों के झुंड बोझ लादकर चलते हैं, पर इस कारण वे शूरवीर नहीं कहलाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4660.english_translation: Fool, look and understand: moths burn in fire under the spell of delusion, and donkeys carry heavy loads in herds, but they are not called heroes for that.
ramacharitamanas::4660.translation_literal: जरहिं (burn) / पतंग (moths) / मोह बस (under the sway of delusion) / भार बहहिं (carry loads) / खर बृंद (herds of donkeys) / ते (they) / नहिं (not) / सूर (heroes) / कहावहिं (are called) / समुझि देखु (understand and see) / मतिमंद (fool)
ramacharitamanas::4660.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4660.essence: Extreme behavior is not the same as true courage.
ramacharitamanas::4660.simple_meaning: Doing something extreme does not make you brave. A moth burns itself and a donkey carries weight, but neither becomes heroic because of that.
ramacharitamanas::4660.simple_insight: Not every sacrifice is strength. Sometimes you are only acting out of confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4660.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the argument is turning sharp. Ravana has been boasting, and the speaker cuts through his pride with blunt examples: a moth rushing into fire, or a donkey hauling loads. Mere intensity or endurance does not equal true heroism.
ramacharitamanas::4660.modern_relevance: You stayed up all night proving a point, then called it commitment. Or you kept carrying everyone else's load and called it strength. The verse asks you to look harder.
ramacharitamanas::4660.insight: It separates real courage from compulsive or deluded action, so you stop glorifying self-destructive effort.

ramacharitamanas::4661.verse_sanskrit: अब जनि बतबढ़ाव खल करही। सुनु मम बचन मान परिहरही॥ दसमुख मैं न बसीठीं आयउँ। अस बिचारि रघुबीर पठायउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4661.verse_hindi: अरे दुष्ट! अब बतबढ़ाव मत कर, मेरा वचन सुन और अभिमान त्याग दे! हे दशमुख! मैं दूत की तरह (सन्धि करने) नहीं आया हूँ। श्री रघुवीर ने ऐसा विचार कर मुझे भेजा है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4661.english_translation: “Do not boast now, wicked one. Hear my words and let go of pride. O ten-faced one, I did not come here as a messenger for a truce. Considering this, Raghuvir sent me.”
ramacharitamanas::4661.translation_literal: अब (now) / जनि (do not) / बतबढ़ाव (boast) / खल (wicked one) / करही (do) / सुनु (listen) / मम (my) / बचन (words) / मान (obey) / परिहरही (give up) / दसमुख (ten-faced one) / मैं (I) / न (not) / बसीठीं (messenger for truce) / आयउँ (came) / अस (thus) / बिचारि (considering) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / पठायउँ (sent)
ramacharitamanas::4661.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4661.essence: Purpose speaks plainly and does not bow to arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4661.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana to stop boasting, listen carefully, and drop his pride. He says he did not come as a peace messenger; Ram sent him for a different purpose.
ramacharitamanas::4661.simple_insight: Clear speech has power when it is free of fear and ego.
ramacharitamanas::4661.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana after crossing the ocean and finding Sita. Ravana tries to dominate the moment with pride, but Hanuman answers without flinching: he is not here to negotiate, only to deliver Ram's command.
ramacharitamanas::4661.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting where someone is trying to overpower the room with bluster. You do not need to shrink, flatter, or perform. You can say exactly why you are there.
ramacharitamanas::4661.insight: It teaches you to hold your role firmly and speak without apologising for your purpose.

ramacharitamanas::4662.verse_sanskrit: बार बार अस कहइ कृपाला। नहिं गजारि जसु बंधे सृकाला॥ मन महुँ समुझि बचन प्रभु केरे। सहेउँ कठोर बचन सठ तेरे ॥
