ramacharitamanas::4662.verse_hindi: कृपालु श्री रामजी बार-बार ऐसा कहते हैं कि स्यार के मारने से सिंह को यश नहीं मिलता। अरे मूर्ख! प्रभु के (उन) वचनों को मन में समझकर (याद करके) ही मैंने तेरे कठोर वचन सहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4662.english_translation: Again and again the compassionate Lord says this: a jackal does not gain fame by killing a lion. Remembering the Lord's words in my heart, I have endured your harsh speech, fool.
ramacharitamanas::4662.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / अस (thus) / कहइ (says) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / नहिं (not) / गजारि (lion) / जसु (fame) / बंधे (is gained) / सृकाला (by a jackal) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / समुझि (remembering/understanding) / बचन (words) / प्रभु केरे (of the Lord) / सहेउँ (I endured) / कठोर (harsh) / बचन (words) / सठ (fool) / तेरे (your)
ramacharitamanas::4662.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4662.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he endured Ravana's insults because he remembered Ram's words, and he reminds Ravana that a weak creature does not win glory by attacking the strong.
ramacharitamanas::4662.simple_insight: Real strength is staying steady when provoked, not proving yourself in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4662.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana after speaking firmly for Ram. Ravana answers with insults, but Hanuman does not lose himself. He says he has already remembered Ram's instruction and can therefore endure abuse without reacting.
ramacharitamanas::4662.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting and expects a sharp reply. You remember who you are, let the insult pass, and answer from steadiness instead of ego.
ramacharitamanas::4662.insight: It teaches you to hold your center under provocation by recalling a higher instruction before reacting.

ramacharitamanas::4663.verse_sanskrit: नाहिं त करि मुख भंजन तोरा। लैं जातेउँ सीतहि बरजोरा॥ जानेउँ तव बल अधम सुरारी। सूनें हरि आनिहि परनारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4663.verse_hindi: नहीं तो तेरे मुँह तोड़कर मैं सीताजी को जबरदस्ती ले जाता। अरे अधम! देवताओं के शत्रु! तेरा बल तो मैंने तभी जान लिया, जब तू सूने में पराई स्त्री को हर (चुरा) लाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4663.english_translation: Otherwise, I would have smashed your face and carried Sita away by force. I knew your strength, vile enemy of the devas, when you stole another man's wife in secret.
ramacharitamanas::4663.translation_literal: नाहिं (otherwise/not) / त (then) / करि (doing) / मुख भंजन (face-breaking) / तोरा (your) / लैं जातेउँ (would have taken away) / सीतहि (Sita) / बरजोरा (by force) / जानेउँ (I knew) / तव (your) / बल (strength) / अधम (base one) / सुरारी (enemy of the devas) / सूनें (in secret) / हरि (stole) / आनिहि (brought) / परनारी (another man's wife)
ramacharitamanas::4663.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4663.essence: Real strength can choose not to strike.
ramacharitamanas::4663.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he could have used force against Ravana, but chose not to. He also says Ravana's strength was already clear from the way he secretly abducted Sita.
ramacharitamanas::4663.simple_insight: Power is not proven by cruelty; restraint can be stronger than rage.
ramacharitamanas::4663.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana after delivering Ram's warning. Ravana keeps boasting, but Hanuman answers with calm contempt: he could have struck him and taken Sita by force, yet he stayed within Ram's purpose. The exchange strips away Ravana's pride.
ramacharitamanas::4663.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you in a tense conversation, trying to make you lose your temper. You do not need to prove strength by exploding; sometimes the stronger move is refusing the bait.
ramacharitamanas::4663.insight: It shifts the mind from reactive aggression to disciplined restraint under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4664.verse_sanskrit: तै निसिचर पति गर्ब बहूता। मैं रघुपति सेवक कर दूता॥ जौं न राम अपमानहिं डरऊँ। तोहि देखत अस कौतुक करउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4664.verse_hindi: तू राक्षसों का राजा और बड़ा अभिमानी है, परन्तु मैं तो श्री रघुनाथजी के सेवक (सुग्रीव) का दूत (सेवक का भी सेवक) हूँ। यदि मैं श्री रामजी के अपमान से न डरूँ तो तेरे देखते-देखते ऐसा तमाशा करूँ कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4664.english_translation: You are the king of the demons and full of pride, but I am only the servant-messenger of Raghunath's servant. If I do not fear disrespect to Ram, I will do such a feat before you that...
ramacharitamanas::4664.translation_literal: तै (you) / निसिचर पति (king of the night-walkers) / गर्ब (pride) / बहूता (much) / मैं (I) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / सेवक (servant) / कर (of) / दूता (messenger)॥ / जौं (if) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / अपमानहिं (disrespect) / डरऊँ (I fear) / तोहि (you) / देखत (seeing) / अस (such) / कौतुक (feat) / करउँ (I do) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4664.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4664.essence: Loyalty to Ram makes fear irrelevant.
ramacharitamanas::4664.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Ravana that he is only Ram's servant-messenger, and that his real concern is protecting Ram's honour, not his own safety.
ramacharitamanas::4664.simple_insight: True strength comes from loyalty that is bigger than fear.
ramacharitamanas::4664.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands before Ravana after revealing his mission. Ravana's pride fills the room, but Hanuman answers without shrinking. He defines himself only as Ram's servant, and turns the confrontation into a test of Ravana's arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4664.modern_relevance: You are cornered in a tense meeting and someone tries to intimidate you. The calmest reply comes when you know exactly who you serve and what you will not let be disrespected.
ramacharitamanas::4664.insight: It shifts courage from self-protection to protecting what you stand for.

ramacharitamanas::4665.verse_sanskrit: तोहि पटकि महि सेन हति चौपट करि तव गाउँ। तव जुबतिन्ह समेत सठ जनकसुतहि लै जाउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4665.verse_hindi: तुझे जमीन पर पटककर, तेरी सेना का संहार कर और तेरे गाँव को चौपट (नष्ट-भ्रष्ट) करके, अरे मूर्ख! तेरी युवती स्त्रियों सहित जानकीजी को ले जाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4665.english_translation: I would throw you down, wipe out your army, ruin your city, and carry off Janaki along with your women, fool.
ramacharitamanas::4665.translation_literal: तोहि (you) / पटकि (throwing down) / महि (to the ground) / सेन (army) / हति (destroying) / चौपट करि (making ruin) / तव (your) / गाउँ (town) / तव (your) / जुबतिन्ह (with women) / समेत (along with) / सठ (fool) / जनकसुतहि (Janaka's daughter) / लै जाउँ (I would take away)
ramacharitamanas::4665.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4665.essence: Boastful force can threaten ruin, but it is still only boasting.
ramacharitamanas::4665.simple_meaning: He boasts that he could throw Ravana down, destroy his army and city, and carry Sita away with Ravana's women.
ramacharitamanas::4665.simple_insight: Pride talks big, but it still cannot prove strength.
ramacharitamanas::4665.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman keeps provoking Ravana after exposing his own power. This line is part of a taunt, not a teaching: he describes total destruction to shame Ravana before the larger confrontation continues.
ramacharitamanas::4665.modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing everything they could do if they really lost control. The words sound powerful, but they only reveal how far the clash has gone.
ramacharitamanas::4665.insight: It shows how boastful anger tries to dominate with threats instead of restraint.

ramacharitamanas::4666.verse_sanskrit: जौं अस करौं तदपि न बड़ाई। मुएहि बधें नहिं कछु मनुसाई॥ कौल कामबस कृपिन बिमूढ़ा। अति दरिद्र अजसी अति बूढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4666.verse_hindi: यदि ऐसा करूँ, तो भी इसमें कोई बड़ाई नहीं है। मरे हुए को मारने में कुछ भी पुरुषत्व (बहादुरी) नहीं है। वाममार्गी, कामी, कंजूस, अत्यंत मूढ़, अति दरिद्र, बदनाम, बहुत बूढ़ा, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4666.english_translation: If I do this, there is still no greatness in it. There is no manliness in killing one who is already dead. A heretic, ruled by desire, miserly, deluded, extremely poor, disgraced, and very old...
ramacharitamanas::4666.translation_literal: जौं (if) / अस (such) / करौं (I do) / तदपि (even then) / न (not) / बड़ाई (greatness)। / मुएहि (the dead one) / बधें (by killing) / नहिं (not) / कछु (any) / मनुसाई (manliness)॥ / कौल (heretic / wrong-sect follower) / कामबस (under desire's control) / कृपिन (miserly) / बिमूढ़ा (deluded) / अति (very) / दरिद्र (poor) / अजसी (disgraced) / अति (very) / बूढ़ा (old)॥
ramacharitamanas::4666.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4666.essence: Cruelty toward the helpless is not strength at all.
ramacharitamanas::4666.simple_meaning: Ravana says that attacking someone who is already helpless or defeated is not a brave act. He also piles on insults to belittle the enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4666.simple_insight: Real strength does not need to humiliate what is already down.
ramacharitamanas::4666.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps speaking from pride while the war closes in around him. He tries to dismiss his enemy as weak and unworthy of a fair fight, revealing more about his own arrogance than about anyone else's power.
ramacharitamanas::4666.modern_relevance: You win the argument in the group chat, then keep mocking the person after they stop replying. The extra blow doesn't make you stronger; it only shows how little restraint you have.
ramacharitamanas::4666.insight: It shifts attention from domination to the character revealed by how you treat the vulnerable.

ramacharitamanas::4667.verse_sanskrit: सदा रोगबस संतत क्रोधी। बिष्नु बिमुख श्रुति संत बिरोधी॥ तनु पोषक निंदक अघ खानी जीवत सव सम चौदह प्रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4667.verse_hindi: नित्य का रोगी, निरंतर क्रोधयुक्त रहने वाला, भगवान् विष्णु से विमुख, वेद और संतों का विरोधी, अपना ही शरीर पोषण करने वाला, पराई निंदा करने वाला और पाप की खान (महान् पापी)- ये चौदह प्राणी जीते ही मुरदे के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4667.english_translation: Those who are always sick, always angry, turned away from Vishnu, hostile to the Vedas and saints, feeding only their own bodies, slandering others, and full of sin — these fourteen kinds of beings are dead while still alive.
ramacharitamanas::4667.translation_literal: सदा (always) / रोगबस (under the control of illness) / संतत (continually) / क्रोधी (angry) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / बिमुख (turned away) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / संत (saints) / बिरोधी (opposed to) / तनु (body) / पोषक (nourisher) / निंदक (slanderer) / अघ (sin) / खानी (mine) / जीवत (living) / सव (corpse) / सम (like) / चौदह (fourteen) / प्रानी (beings)
ramacharitamanas::4667.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4667.essence: A body can keep moving long after the inner life has collapsed.
ramacharitamanas::4667.simple_meaning: A person trapped in illness, anger, arrogance, and criticism is counted as spiritually dead even while breathing.
ramacharitamanas::4667.simple_insight: It stings, but it also warns you: a life can continue outwardly while its inner health is gone.
ramacharitamanas::4667.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Angad is confronting Ravana’s court and exposing the kind of life that has already collapsed from within. The verse lists the traits of a ruined person, not to insult, but to show how far ego can fall before the body dies.
ramacharitamanas::4667.modern_relevance: You know that coworker who is always irritated, always mocking, always feeding only their own comfort? Being busy and breathing is not the same as being alive in any meaningful way.
ramacharitamanas::4667.insight: It shifts attention from outward survival to inner condition, asking whether your habits are making you more awake or more deadened.

ramacharitamanas::4668.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि खल बधउँ न तोही। अब जनि रिस उपजावसि मोही॥ सुनि सकोप कह निसिचर नाथा। अधर दसन दसि मीजत हाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4668.verse_hindi: अरे दुष्ट! ऐसा विचार कर मैं तुझे नहीं मारता। अब तू मुझमें क्रोध न पैदा कर (मुझे गुस्सा न दिला)। अंगद के वचन सुनकर राक्षस राज रावण दाँतों से होठ काटकर, क्रोधित होकर हाथ मलता हुआ बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4668.english_translation: Thinking this, I do not kill you. Do not stir anger in me now. Hearing this, the lord of demons spoke in rage, biting his lip with his teeth and rubbing his hands.
ramacharitamanas::4668.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / खल (wicked one) / बधउँ (I kill) / न (not) / तोही (you) / अब (now) / जनि (do not) / रिस (anger) / उपजावसि (cause to arise) / मोही (in me) / सुनि (hearing) / सकोप (with anger) / कह (said) / निसिचर नाथा (lord of demons) / अधर (lip) / दसन (teeth) / दसि (biting) / मीजत (rubbing) / हाथा (hands)
ramacharitamanas::4668.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4668.essence: Pride pretends restraint, but anger still shows through.
ramacharitamanas::4668.simple_meaning: Ravana says he is sparing Angad for now and warns him not to provoke his anger. Angad's words have made Ravana furious.
ramacharitamanas::4668.simple_insight: Pride can look like restraint, but it is still anger waiting to burst.
ramacharitamanas::4668.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just spoken boldly before Ravana. Ravana tries to appear controlled, saying he is not killing Angad only because of his own calculation. But the next line shows the truth: he is already boiling with rage.
ramacharitamanas::4668.modern_relevance: You say, "I'm fine," but your jaw is clenched and your hands won't stay still. The anger is already speaking before you do.
ramacharitamanas::4668.insight: It exposes how ego disguises fury as self-control while the body reveals the real state.

ramacharitamanas::4669.verse_sanskrit: रे कपि अधम मरन अब चहसी। छोटे बदन बात बड़ि कहसी॥ कटु जल्पसि जड़ कपि बल जाकें। बल प्रताप बुधि तेज न ताकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4669.verse_hindi: अरे नीच बंदर! अब तू मरना ही चाहता है! इसी से छोटे मुँह बड़ी बात कहता है। अरे मूर्ख बंदर! तू जिसके बल पर कड़ुए वचन बक रहा है, उसमें बल, प्रताप, बुद्धि अथवा तेज कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4669.english_translation: You lowly monkey! Do you now want to die? Small mouth, yet such big talk. Foolish monkey, the power you rely on has no strength, glory, wisdom, or brilliance.
ramacharitamanas::4669.translation_literal: रे (hey) / कपि (monkey) / अधम (lowly) / मरन (death) / अब (now) / चहसी (you want) / छोटे (small) / बदन (mouth) / बात (speech) / बड़ि (big) / कहसी (you say) / कटु (bitter) / जल्पसि (you speak) / जड़ (foolish) / कपि (monkey) / बल (strength) / जाकें (whose) / बल (strength) / प्रताप (glory) / बुधि (wisdom) / तेज (radiance) / न (not) / ताकें (in that one)
ramacharitamanas::4669.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4669.essence: Arrogance mocks what it cannot defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4669.simple_meaning: Ravana insults Hanuman, mocking his size and claiming that the power Hanuman depends on has no real strength or wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4669.simple_insight: Pride always tries to shrink what it cannot understand.
ramacharitamanas::4669.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is cornered by Hanuman's fearless words. Instead of seeing the warning, he lashes out with contempt, mocking Hanuman's small form and denying Ram's power. The verse shows ego defending itself when truth is near.
ramacharitamanas::4669.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your warning in a meeting by sneering at your experience instead of answering the point. The insult is loud, but it only reveals their fear of being exposed.
ramacharitamanas::4669.insight: It reveals how arrogance attacks the messenger when it cannot face the message.

ramacharitamanas::4670.verse_sanskrit: अगुन अमान जानि तेहि दीन्ह पिता बनबास। सो दुख अरु जुबती बिरह पुनि निसि दिन मम त्रास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4670.verse_hindi: उसे गुणहीन और मानहीन समझकर ही तो पिता ने वनवास दे दिया। उसे एक तो वह (उसका) दुःख, उस पर युवती स्त्री का विरह और फिर रात-दिन मेरा डर बना रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4670.english_translation: He was sent to the forest because his father saw him as without qualities and without honor. On top of that came his sorrow, his separation from his young wife, and my fear day and night.
ramacharitamanas::4670.translation_literal: अगुन (without qualities) / अमान (without honor) / जानि (knowing) / तेहि (him) / दीन्ह (gave) / पिता (father) / बनबास (forest exile) / सो (that) / दुख (sorrow) / अरु (and) / जुबती (young woman / wife) / बिरह (separation) / पुनि (again) / निसि दिन (night and day) / मम (my) / त्रास (fear)
ramacharitamanas::4670.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4670.essence: Ravana defends himself by turning Ram's suffering into a weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4670.simple_meaning: Ravana reminds Angad that Ram was sent into exile, suffered separation from Sita, and still remains a threat that keeps Ravana afraid.
ramacharitamanas::4670.simple_insight: Pride starts to shake when you remember who still stands against you.
ramacharitamanas::4670.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just spoken fearlessly before Ravana. Ravana answers by pointing to Ram's exile, Sita's separation, and the pressure of war. This is not a teaching verse; it is part of Ravana's defensive argument.
ramacharitamanas::4670.modern_relevance: A person cornered in an argument reaches for old facts to protect their pride. The tone is less truth-seeking than self-defense.
ramacharitamanas::4670.insight: It shows how ego clings to comparison and fear when it cannot answer directly.

ramacharitamanas::4671.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह के बल कर गर्ब तोहि अइसे मनुज अनेक। खाहिं निसाचर दिवस निसि मूढ़ समुझु तजि टेक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4671.verse_hindi: जिनके बल का तुझे गर्व है, ऐसे अनेकों मनुष्यों को तो राक्षस रात-दिन खाया करते हैं। अरे मूढ़! जिद्द छोड़कर समझ (विचार कर) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4671.english_translation: The beings whose strength you boast of are eaten day and night by many others. Fool, let go of stubbornness and understand.
ramacharitamanas::4671.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / के (whose) / बल (strength) / कर (from) / गर्ब (pride) / तोहि (you) / अइसे (such) / मनुज (humans) / अनेक (many) / खाहिं (eat) / निसाचर (night-walkers, demons) / दिवस (day) / निसि (night) / मूढ़ (fool) / समुझु (understand) / तजि (leaving) / टेक (stubbornness)
ramacharitamanas::4671.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4671.essence: Pride collapses when it meets facts.
ramacharitamanas::4671.simple_meaning: Boasting about power is foolish when that same power is weak against real danger. Clinging to pride only blocks clear thinking.
ramacharitamanas::4671.simple_insight: Pride shrinks when you see how fragile your support really is.
ramacharitamanas::4671.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana mocks Hanuman after the monkey envoy speaks boldly in his court. Ravana tries to belittle him by pointing out that many powerful humans are already easy prey for demons. The verse exposes Ravana's arrogance and Hanuman's fearless clarity.
ramacharitamanas::4671.modern_relevance: You defend a shaky plan in a meeting because you hate admitting it's weak. The louder you sound, the less you want to see what is actually true.
ramacharitamanas::4671.insight: It shifts you from defending ego to checking reality before you speak.

ramacharitamanas::4672.verse_sanskrit: जब तेहिं कीन्हि राम कै निंदा। क्रोधवंत अति भयउ कपिंदा॥ हरि हर निंदा सुनइ जो काना। होइ पाप गोघात समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4672.verse_hindi: जब उसने श्री रामजी की निंदा की, तब तो कपिश्रेष्ठ अंगद अत्यंत क्रोधित हुए, क्योंकि (शास्त्र ऐसा कहते हैं कि) जो अपने कानों से भगवान् विष्णु और शिव की निंदा सुनता है, उसे गो वध के समान पाप होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4672.english_translation: When he spoke ill of Ram, Angada became fiercely angry. Listening to slander of Hari and Hara is said to be a sin equal to killing a cow.
ramacharitamanas::4672.translation_literal: जब (when) / तेहिं (he) / कीन्हि (did) / राम कै (of Ram) / निंदा (slander) / क्रोधवंत (full of anger) / अति (very) / भयउ (became) / कपिंदा (chief of monkeys)॥ / हरि (Hari) / हर (Hara) / निंदा (slander) / सुनइ (hears) / जो (who) / काना (ears) / होइ (becomes) / पाप (sin) / गोघात (killing a cow) / समाना (equal)॥
ramacharitamanas::4672.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4672.essence: Disrespect toward the divine is never just talk.
ramacharitamanas::4672.simple_meaning: Angada is enraged when Ravana insults Ram. The verse adds that hearing slander of Hari and Shiva is considered a grave offense.
ramacharitamanas::4672.simple_insight: Some words are not harmless; they reveal whether your ears are open to reverence or cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::4672.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the peace talks turn sharp. Ravana insults Ram, and Angada's patience breaks into anger. The verse then broadens the moment into a warning: hearing contempt for Hari and Hara is itself spiritually damaging.
ramacharitamanas::4672.modern_relevance: You hear someone mock what you deeply respect, and your body tightens before you can answer. The verse catches that instant when reverence turns into fierce protection.
ramacharitamanas::4672.insight: It shifts attention from clever speech to the moral weight of what you allow into your hearing.

ramacharitamanas::4673.verse_sanskrit: कटकटान कपिकुंजर भारी। दुहु भुजदंड तमकि महि मारी॥ डोलत धरनि सभासद खसे। चले भाजि भय मारुत ग्रसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4673.verse_hindi: वानर श्रेष्ठ अंगद बहुत जोर से कटकटाए (शब्द किया) और उन्होंने तमककर (जोर से) अपने दोनों भुजदण्डों को पृथ्वी पर दे मारा। पृथ्वी हिलने लगी, (जिससे बैठे हुए) सभासद् गिर पड़े और भय रूपी पवन (भूत) से ग्रस्त होकर भाग चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4673.english_translation: The mighty monkey-hero Angada clattered loudly, and with a fierce strike he slammed both arms to the ground. The earth shook, the assembled courtiers fell, and, seized by fear, they fled like beings possessed by panic.
ramacharitamanas::4673.translation_literal: कटकटान (clattered/loudly rattled) / कपिकुंजर (elephant among monkeys, great monkey-hero) / भारी (mighty, weighty) / दुहु (both) / भुजदंड (arm-pillars, arms) / तमकि (with a fierce start/jerk) / महि (earth) / मारी (struck, slammed) ॥ / डोलत (shaking) / धरनि (earth) / सभासद (court members, assembled listeners) / खसे (fell) ॥ / चले (they ran) / भाजि (fleeing) / भय (fear) / मारुत (wind) / ग्रसे (gripped, seized) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4673.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4673.essence: Fear collapses when courage enters the room.
ramacharitamanas::4673.simple_meaning: Angada strikes the ground so hard that the earth shakes, the court collapses, and everyone runs away in fear.
ramacharitamanas::4673.simple_insight: Raw force can silence a room before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4673.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Angada answers insult with thunderous presence. He slams both arms down, shaking the hall so badly that the assembled courtiers lose their composure and flee. The scene builds the pressure before Ravana rises again.
ramacharitamanas::4673.modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet when someone stops apologizing for taking up space. Before the meeting even begins, everyone feels the shift in power.
ramacharitamanas::4673.insight: It shows how fearless presence can overturn intimidation without a long speech.

ramacharitamanas::4674.verse_sanskrit: गिरत सँभारि उठा दसकंधर। भूतल परे मुकुट अति सुंदर॥ कछु तेहिं लै निज सिरन्हि सँवारे। कछु अंगद प्रभु पास पबारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4674.verse_hindi: रावण गिरते-गिरते सँभलकर उठा। उसके अत्यंत सुंदर मुकुट पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। कुछ तो उसने उठाकर अपने सिरों पर सुधाकर रख लिए और कुछ अंगद ने उठाकर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के पास फेंक दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4674.english_translation: Ravana staggered, caught himself, and stood up. His very beautiful crown fell to the ground. He picked up some pieces and fixed them back on his own head, and Angad tossed some of them to Lord Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4674.translation_literal: गिरत (while falling) / सँभारि (regaining balance) / उठा (rose) / दसकंधर (Ravana, the ten-necked one) / भूतल (on the ground) / परे (fell) / मुकुट (crown) / अति सुंदर (very beautiful) / कछु (some) / तेहिं (he) / लै (taking) / निज (own) / सिरन्हि (on the head) / सँवारे (adjusted, set right) / कछु (some) / अंगद (Angad) / प्रभु (Lord) / पास (near) / पबारे (threw, sent)
ramacharitamanas::4674.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4674.essence: Pride falls hard, then rushes to cover its own wound.
ramacharitamanas::4674.simple_meaning: Ravana regains his footing after falling, and his crown scatters on the ground. Some pieces go back on his head, and some are flung toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4674.simple_insight: Pride can be shaken, but it still tries to gather itself back together.
ramacharitamanas::4674.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ravana is knocked down before Ram and the monkey warriors. Even in defeat, he scrambles to restore his royal appearance, while Angad turns the fallen crown into a sign of his humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::4674.modern_relevance: You take a public hit, then immediately try to look composed again. Everyone saw the stumble; the real question is what your pride does next.
ramacharitamanas::4674.insight: It shows how ego tries to repair its image even after being exposed.

ramacharitamanas::4675.verse_sanskrit: आवत मुकुट देखि कपि भागे। दिनहीं लूक परन बिधि लागे॥ की रावन करि कोप चलाए। कुलिस चारि आवत अति धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4675.verse_hindi: मुकुटों को आते देखकर वानर भागे। (सोचने लगे) विधाता! क्या दिन में ही उल्कापात होने लगा (तारे टूटकर गिरने लगे)? अथवा क्या रावण ने क्रोध करके चार वज्र चलाए हैं, जो बड़े धाए के साथ (वेग से) आ रहे हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4675.english_translation: Seeing the crowns coming toward them, the monkeys ran. They thought, 'Has a meteor shower begun in daylight? Or has Ravana, in anger, hurled four thunderbolts rushing toward us?'
ramacharitamanas::4675.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / मुकुट (crowns) / देखि (seeing) / कपि (monkeys) / भागे (ran away) / दिनहीं (in daytime) / लूक (meteor) / परन (falling) / बिधि (fate / the creator) / लागे (seemed) / की (or) / रावन (Ravana) / करि (having done) / कोप (anger) / चलाए (sent) / कुलिस (thunderbolts / vajras) / चारि (four) / आवत (coming) / अति (very) / धाए (rushing)
ramacharitamanas::4675.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4675.essence: Fear makes even harmless things look like disaster.
ramacharitamanas::4675.simple_meaning: The monkeys see the crowns flying toward them and panic, mistaking them for falling meteors or thunderbolts.
ramacharitamanas::4675.simple_insight: Fear can turn an ordinary sight into a disaster in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::4675.detailed_meaning: In the battle for Lanka, Angad has just struck fear into Ravana's side. Now the monkeys see crowns flying through the air and instinctively flee, imagining cosmic danger. The verse is a brief scene of confusion before Ram clarifies what is happening.
ramacharitamanas::4675.modern_relevance: You see a few urgent messages pop up on your phone and your stomach drops. For a moment, your mind turns them into catastrophe before you even know what they are.
ramacharitamanas::4675.insight: It shows how quickly perception can be distorted by fear, before facts are even checked.

ramacharitamanas::4676.verse_sanskrit: कह प्रभु हँसि जनि हृदयँ डेराहू। लूक न असनि केतु नहिं राहू॥ ए किरीट दसकंधर केरे। आवत बालितनय के प्रेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4676.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने (उनसे) हँसकर कहा- मन में डरो नहीं। ये न उल्का हैं, न वज्र हैं और न केतु या राहु ही हैं। अरे भाई! ये तो रावण के मुकुट हैं, जो बालिपुत्र अंगद के फेंके हुए आ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4676.english_translation: The Lord smiled and said, “Do not be afraid in your heart. These are not meteors, not thunderbolts, not Ketu or Rahu. They are Ravana’s crowns, being hurled by Angada, the son of Vali.”
ramacharitamanas::4676.translation_literal: कह (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / हँसि (smiling) / जनि (do not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / डेराहू (be afraid) / लूक (meteor) / न (not) / असनि (thunderbolt) / केतु (Ketu) / नहिं (not) / राहू (Rahu) / ए (these) / किरीट (crowns) / दसकंधर (of Ravana) / केरे (belonging to) / आवत (coming) / बालितनय (son of Vali, Angada) / के (of) / प्रेरे (thrown)
ramacharitamanas::4676.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4676.essence: Clear seeing dissolves fear faster than force.
ramacharitamanas::4676.simple_meaning: Ram reassures the frightened monkeys that the flying objects are only Ravana’s crowns, thrown by Angada, not some terrible omen.
ramacharitamanas::4676.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when you name what is actually happening.
ramacharitamanas::4676.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s battlefield, Ravana has just stumbled and his crowns are flying through the air. The monkeys panic, mistaking them for deadly celestial signs. Ram smiles and calmly identifies the scene, restoring courage in the middle of chaos.
ramacharitamanas::4676.modern_relevance: A sudden crash in the next room makes everyone freeze. Before panic invents a disaster, someone calm looks, names the facts, and the whole room breathes again.
ramacharitamanas::4676.insight: It teaches you to replace panic with clear naming of reality.

ramacharitamanas::4677.verse_sanskrit: तरकि पवनसुत कर गहे आनि धरे प्रभु पास। कौतुक देखहिं भालु कपि दिनकर सरिस प्रकास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4677.verse_hindi: पवन पुत्र श्री हनुमान् जी ने उछलकर उनको हाथ से पकड़ लिया और लाकर प्रभु के पास रख दिया। रीछ और वानर तमाशा देखने लगे। उनका प्रकाश सूर्य के समान था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4677.english_translation: Hanuman quickly seized them and brought them to the Lord. The bears and monkeys watched in amazement; they shone like the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4677.translation_literal: तरकि (quickly) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / कर (by hand) / गहे (seized) / आनि (bringing) / धरे (placed) / प्रभु (Lord) / पास (near) / कौतुक (wonder) / देखहिं (watch) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / दिनकर (sun) / सरिस (like) / प्रकास (radiance)
ramacharitamanas::4677.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4677.essence: What looked threatening is revealed as dazzling and harmless.
ramacharitamanas::4677.simple_meaning: Hanuman quickly brings the crowns to Ram, and the bears and monkeys stare in wonder at their sun-like brilliance.
ramacharitamanas::4677.simple_insight: A moment of triumph turns into awe, not pride.
ramacharitamanas::4677.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army has mistaken Ravana's crowns for dangerous signs. Hanuman rushes in, grabs them, and places them before Ram. The bears and monkeys stare at the radiant sight, while the scene quietly sets up Ravana's anger next.
ramacharitamanas::4677.modern_relevance: You finally finish the thing everyone was doubting, and for a second the room goes quiet. The result speaks before you do.
ramacharitamanas::4677.insight: It shifts attention from suspense to revelation: the object of fear becomes an object of wonder.

ramacharitamanas::4678.verse_sanskrit: उहाँ सकोपि दसानन सब सन कहत रिसाइ। धरहु कपिहि धरि मारहु सुनि अंगद मुसुकाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4678.verse_hindi: वहाँ (सभा में) क्रोधयुक्त रावण सबसे क्रोधित होकर कहने लगा कि- बंदर को पकड़ लो और पकड़कर मार डालो। अंगद यह सुनकर मुस्कुराने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4678.english_translation: There, Ravana grew furious and told everyone in anger, "Seize the monkey, hold him down, and kill him." Angada only smiled when he heard it.
ramacharitamanas::4678.translation_literal: उहाँ (there) / सकोपि (angrily) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / सब सन (to everyone) / कहत (saying) / रिसाइ (in rage) / धरहु (seize) / कपिहि (the monkey) / धरि (holding) / मारहु (kill) / सुनि (hearing) / अंगद (Angada) / मुसुकाइ (smiled)
ramacharitamanas::4678.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4678.essence: Rage exposes weakness; calm exposes strength.
ramacharitamanas::4678.simple_meaning: Ravana orders his men to seize and kill Hanuman, but Angada remains calm and smiles.
ramacharitamanas::4678.simple_insight: Panic often makes power speak loudest, while steadiness stays untouched.
ramacharitamanas::4678.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, the insult of Hanuman's arrival has ignited his rage. He orders the monkey seized and killed, but Angada's quiet smile shows that fear has not entered the room.
ramacharitamanas::4678.modern_relevance: A manager snaps in front of the whole team and demands someone be removed. The loudest voice in the room is often the one most threatened.
ramacharitamanas::4678.insight: It shows how ego lashes out when challenged, while inner steadiness does not need to shout back.

ramacharitamanas::4679.verse_sanskrit: एहि बधि बेगि सुभट सब धावहु। खाहु भालु कपि जहँ जहँ पावहु॥ मर्कटहीन करहु महि जाई। जिअत धरहु तापस द्वौ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4679.verse_hindi: (रावण फिर बोला-) इसे मारकर सब योद्धा तुरंत दौड़ो और जहाँ कहीं रीछ-वानरों को पाओ, वहीं खा डालो। पृथ्वी को बंदरों से रहित कर दो और जाकर दोनों तपस्वी भाइयों (राम-लक्ष्मण) को जीते जी पकड़ लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4679.english_translation: Then Ravana said, "Go at once, all warriors. Eat up every bear and monkey wherever you find them. Make the earth free of monkeys, and go seize the two ascetics alive."
ramacharitamanas::4679.translation_literal: एहि (this) / बधि (after killing) / बेगि (quickly) / सुभट (warriors) / सब (all) / धावहु (run) / खाहु (eat up) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / जहँ जहँ (wherever) / पावहु (you find) / मर्कटहीन (without monkeys) / करहु (make) / महि (earth) / जाई (going) / जिअत (alive) / धरहु (seize) / तापस (ascetics) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::4679.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4679.simple_meaning: Ravana orders his warriors to kill the monkeys and bears, clear them from the earth, and capture Ram and Lakshman alive.
ramacharitamanas::4679.simple_insight: Rage narrows a ruler until he can only command destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4679.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just seen Angad stand fearless in his court. Enraged, he lashes out at everyone around him and orders a brutal attack on the monkey army, while also demanding that Ram and Lakshman be taken alive.
ramacharitamanas::4679.modern_relevance: A person cornered in a meeting starts issuing harsh orders and turning every disagreement into a purge. Anger makes the mind think in enemies, not solutions.
ramacharitamanas::4679.insight: It shows how unchecked fury turns strategy into blind violence.

ramacharitamanas::4680.verse_sanskrit: पुनि सकोप बोलेउ जुबराजा। गाल बजावत तोहि न लाजा॥ मरु गर काटि निलज कुलघाती। बल बिलोकि बिहरति नहिं छाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4680.verse_hindi: (रावण के ये कोपभरे वचन सुनकर) तब युवराज अंगद क्रोधित होकर बोले- तुझे गाल बजाते लाज नहीं आती! अरे निर्लज्ज! अरे कुलनाशक! गला काटकर (आत्महत्या करके) मर जा! मेरा बल देखकर भी क्या तेरी छाती नहीं फटती! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4680.english_translation: Then Angada, the young prince, spoke in anger: “Do you have no shame, still boasting like this? Die, you shameless destroyer of your line! Even after seeing my strength, does your chest not split open?”
ramacharitamanas::4680.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / सकोप (angrily) / बोलेउ (spoke) / जुबराजा (the young prince) / गाल बजावत (boasting) / तोहि (you) / न लाजा (no shame do you have) / मरु (die) / गर काटि (cutting the throat) / निलज (shameless) / कुलघाती (destroyer of the line) / बल (strength) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिहरति (bursting) / नहिं (not) / छाती (chest)
ramacharitamanas::4680.speaker: Angada
ramacharitamanas::4680.essence: Angada answers arrogance with fearless contempt.
ramacharitamanas::4680.simple_meaning: Angada angrily rebukes Ravana for his shameless boasting and tells him he should die for disgracing his own line.
ramacharitamanas::4680.simple_insight: Pride looks loud from the outside, but it collapses when met with clear courage.
ramacharitamanas::4680.detailed_meaning: In Ravana’s court in Lanka, the war has turned into insult and fury. After Ravana’s threats against the monkeys, Angada answers without fear, exposing Ravana’s shame and moral collapse. The scene is still escalating, not yet reaching its teaching point.
ramacharitamanas::4680.modern_relevance: Someone keeps talking big in a meeting, hoping volume will hide weakness. A calm, fearless reply can puncture the performance without needing to shout louder.
ramacharitamanas::4680.insight: It shows how fearless speech can break the spell of bluster and force false pride into the open.

ramacharitamanas::4681.verse_sanskrit: रे त्रिय चोर कुमारग गामी। खल मल रासि मंदमति कामी॥ सन्यपात जल्पसि दुर्बादा। भएसि कालबस खल मनुजादा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4681.verse_hindi: अरे स्त्री के चोर! अरे कुमार्ग पर चलने वाले! अरे दुष्ट, पाप की राशि, मन्द बुद्धि और कामी! तू सन्निपात में क्या दुर्वचन बक रहा है? अरे दुष्ट राक्षस! तू काल के वश हो गया है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4681.english_translation: O thief of another man's wife, walker of the wrong path, heap of evil, dull-minded and lustful one! Why do you babble these foul words in a fit of madness? O wicked one, you are under time's power.
ramacharitamanas::4681.translation_literal: रे (O) / त्रिय (another man's wife) / चोर (thief) / कुमारग (wrong path) / गामी (walker) / खल (wicked) / मल (filth) / रासि (heap) / मंदमति (dull-minded) / कामी (lustful) / सन्यपात (madness/fit) / जल्पसि (you babble) / दुर्बादा (foul words) / भएसि (you have become) / कालबस (under time's power) / खल (wicked) / मनुजादा (man-eater / demon)
ramacharitamanas::4681.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4681.essence: Raging abuse can be the sign of fear already losing.
ramacharitamanas::4681.simple_meaning: Ravana is being insulted as wicked, lustful, and deluded. The speaker says his filthy speech shows he is already under death's power.
ramacharitamanas::4681.simple_insight: Pride can make you speak from collapse, not strength.
ramacharitamanas::4681.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Angad answers Ravana's insults with sharp rebuke. Ravana has crossed from boasting into frenzy, and Angad names the moral rot behind the rage. This verse is part of that heated exchange.
ramacharitamanas::4681.modern_relevance: Someone sends a furious voice note full of insults, but the anger only exposes how cornered they feel. The louder they get, the less control they have.
ramacharitamanas::4681.insight: It turns aggression into evidence of inner defeat, not power.

ramacharitamanas::4682.verse_sanskrit: याको फलु पावहिगो आगें। बानर भालु चपेटन्हि लागें॥ रामु मनुज बोलत असि बानी। गिरहिं न तव रसना अभिमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4682.verse_hindi: इसका फल तू आगे वानर और भालुओं के चपेटे लगने पर पावेगा। राम मनुष्य हैं, ऐसा वचन बोलते ही, अरे अभिमानी! तेरी जीभें नहीं गिर पड़तीं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4682.english_translation: You will pay for this later, when monkeys and bears strike you down. You call Ram a mere human—how do your arrogant tongues not fall to the ground?
ramacharitamanas::4682.translation_literal: याको (of this) / फलु (fruit, result) / पावहिगो (you will get) / आगें (later, ahead) / बानर (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / चपेटन्हि (with blows, strikes) / लागें (when struck) / रामु (Ram) / मनुज (human) / बोलत (saying) / असि (such) / बानी (words) / गिरहिं (fall) / न (not) / तव (your) / रसना (tongue) / अभिमानी (arrogant one)
ramacharitamanas::4682.speaker: Angada
ramacharitamanas::4682.essence: Arrogant speech plants the seed of its own defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4682.simple_meaning: Angada warns Ravana that his insult will bring a painful result. He says that calling Ram merely human is such arrogance that Ravana's own tongue should fall away.
ramacharitamanas::4682.simple_insight: Mocking what is sacred carries its own cost.
ramacharitamanas::4682.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angada answers Ravana's insult with fierce certainty. Ravana has mocked Ram as only human, and Angada tells him that this arrogance will be repaid in the battle ahead, when the monkey army and bears strike back.
ramacharitamanas::4682.modern_relevance: You make a cruel joke in a room full of people, and the silence after it lands heavier than the laugh. Some words return to you as consequence, not applause.
ramacharitamanas::4682.insight: It shifts the mind from careless speech to awareness that contempt has consequences.

ramacharitamanas::4683.verse_sanskrit: गिरिहहिं रसना संसय नाहीं। सिरन्हि समेत समर महि माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4683.verse_hindi: इसमें संदेह नहीं है कि तेरी जीभें (अकेले नहीं वरन) सिरों के साथ रणभूमि में गिरेंगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4683.english_translation: There is no doubt: your tongues will fall on the battlefield together with your heads.
ramacharitamanas::4683.translation_literal: गिरिहहिं (will fall) / रसना (tongues) / संसय (doubt) / नाहीं (no) / सिरन्हि (with heads) / समेत (together) / समर (battlefield) / महि (on the ground) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::4683.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4683.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens that the offending tongues will be cut down along with the heads in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4683.simple_insight: Rage can turn speech into a weapon and make violence feel like certainty.
ramacharitamanas::4683.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is hurling insults at the messenger who has spoken Ram's name without fear. The exchange is escalating fast: Ravana answers blasphemy with a threat of battlefield slaughter, showing his pride and fury before the war fully breaks open.
ramacharitamanas::4683.modern_relevance: A heated argument on a group chat can suddenly turn cruel, with threats and insults replacing any real listening. Pride makes the mouth promise violence before the mind has cooled.
ramacharitamanas::4683.insight: It shows how ego answers challenge with domination instead of reflection.

ramacharitamanas::4684.verse_sanskrit: सो नर क्यों दसकंध बालि बध्यो जेहिं एक सर। बीसहुँ लोचन अंध धिग तव जन्म कुजाति जड़ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4684.verse_hindi: रे दशकन्ध! जिसने एक ही बाण से बालि को मार डाला, वह मनुष्य कैसे है? अरे कुजाति, अरे जड़! बीस आँखें होने पर भी तू अंधा है। तेरे जन्म को धिक्कार है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4684.english_translation: O ten-headed one, how can he be called a man who killed Bali with a single arrow? You have twenty eyes and still you are blind. Shame on your birth, you fool.
ramacharitamanas::4684.translation_literal: सो (that) / नर (man) / क्यों (how) / दसकंध (ten-headed one) / बालि (Bali) / बध्यो (was killed) / जेहिं (by whom) / एक (one) / सर (arrow) / बीसहुँ (even twenty) / लोचन (eyes) / अंध (blind) / धिग (shame) / तव (your) / जन्म (birth) / कुजाति (base-born) / जड़ (fool)
ramacharitamanas::4684.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4684.essence: Pride can make even obvious truth invisible.
ramacharitamanas::4684.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Ram, refusing to see his divinity. He points to Bali's death and uses it as proof that Ram is no ordinary man, while his own pride makes him blind.
ramacharitamanas::4684.simple_insight: Pride can leave you surrounded by evidence and still unable to see the obvious.
ramacharitamanas::4684.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is raging at Ram's messenger and twisting the story of Bali's death into an insult. Instead of seeing Ram's power, he clings to arrogance. The verse shows a mind so bent by ego that clear evidence becomes blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4684.modern_relevance: You read the same message three times, but your anger decides what it means. The facts are there; your pride is what refuses them.
ramacharitamanas::4684.insight: It shifts attention from external proof to the way ego distorts perception.

ramacharitamanas::4685.verse_sanskrit: तव सोनित कीं प्यास तृषित राम सायक निकर। तजउँ तोहि तेहि त्रास कटु जल्पक निसिचर अधम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4685.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के बाण समूह तेरे रक्त की प्यास से प्यासे हैं। (वे प्यासे ही रह जाएँगे) इस डर से, अरे कड़वी बकवाद करने वाले नीच राक्षस! मैं तुझे छोड़ता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4685.english_translation: Ram's arrows are thirsty for your blood. I would spare you only because I fear that, you foul-tongued low creature.
ramacharitamanas::4685.translation_literal: तव (your) / सोनित (blood) / कीं (of) / प्यास (thirst) / तृषित (thirsty) / राम (Ram's) / सायक (arrows) / निकर (group) / तजउँ (I would leave/spare) / तोहि (you) / तेहि (that) / त्रास (fear) / कटु (harsh) / जल्पक (speaker) / निसिचर (night-dweller, demon) / अधम (low, vile)
ramacharitamanas::4685.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4685.essence: Power becomes clean when it waits for the right command.
ramacharitamanas::4685.simple_meaning: The speaker says Ram's arrows are eager to drink the enemy's blood, but he will spare the enemy only because of Ram's command.
ramacharitamanas::4685.simple_insight: Even anger stays disciplined when it serves a higher command.
ramacharitamanas::4685.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the confrontation is still raging. Hanuman mocks Ravana's pride, but he is not acting on personal rage. He says he could destroy the enemy now, yet holds back because Ram has not ordered it.
ramacharitamanas::4685.modern_relevance: You are furious in a meeting and have the perfect comeback ready. Then you remember you do not need to win the room to prove your strength.
ramacharitamanas::4685.insight: It shifts force from personal vengeance to obedience to dharma.

ramacharitamanas::4686.verse_sanskrit: मैं तव दसन तोरिबे लायक। आयसु मोहि न दीन्ह रघुनायक॥ असि रिस होति दसउ मुख तोरौं। लंका गहि समुद्र महँ बोरौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4686.verse_hindi: मैं तेरे दाँत तोड़ने में समर्थ हूँ। पर क्या करूँ? श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुझे आज्ञा नहीं दी। ऐसा क्रोध आता है कि तेरे दसों मुँह तोड़ डालूँ और (तेरी) लंका को पकड़कर समुद्र में डुबो दूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4686.english_translation: I am capable of breaking your teeth. But what can I do? Raghunath has not given me orders. Such anger rises that I would smash all ten of your mouths and sink Lanka into the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4686.translation_literal: मैं (I) / तव (your) / दसन (teeth) / तोरिबे (to break) / लायक (capable) / आयसु (order) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / दीन्ह (given) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / असि (such) / रिस (anger) / होति (arises) / दसउ (all ten) / मुख (mouths) / तोरौं (I would break) / लंका (Lanka) / गहि (seizing) / समुद्र (sea) / महँ (into) / बोरौं (I would sink)
ramacharitamanas::4686.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4686.essence: Power becomes pure when it waits for the right command.
ramacharitamanas::4686.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he has the power to destroy Lanka, but he will not act until Ram gives the order.
ramacharitamanas::4686.simple_insight: Real strength is not uncontrolled force; it is force held in service of the right command.
ramacharitamanas::4686.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is face-to-face with Ravana's pride. He knows he could crush the demon king and wreck the city, but he restrains himself because Ram has not commanded it. The moment reveals seva shaped by discipline.
ramacharitamanas::4686.modern_relevance: You know the email could end the argument in one sharp sentence. You have the power to win — but you pause because winning is not the same as serving what matters.
ramacharitamanas::4686.insight: It teaches you to hold capability inside obedience, so action stays clean and purposeful.

ramacharitamanas::4687.verse_sanskrit: गूलरि फल समान तव लंका। बसहु मध्य तुम्ह जंतु असंका॥ मैं बानर फल खात न बारा। आयसु दीन्ह न राम उदारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4687.verse_hindi: तेरी लंका गूलर के फल के समान है। तुम सब कीड़े उसके भीतर (अज्ञानवश) निडर होकर बस रहे हो। मैं बंदर हूँ, मुझे इस फल को खाते क्या देर थी? पर उदार (कृपालु) श्री रामचंद्रजी ने वैसी आज्ञा नहीं दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4687.english_translation: Your Lanka is like a fig fruit. All you creatures live inside it, fearless and unaware. I am a monkey; I could have eaten this fruit long ago, but noble Ram did not give me that order.
ramacharitamanas::4687.translation_literal: गूलरि (fig) / फल (fruit) / समान (like) / तव (your) / लंका (Lanka) / बसहु (you live) / मध्य (inside) / तुम्ह (you all) / जंतु (creatures) / असंका (without fear) / मैं (I) / बानर (monkey) / फल (fruit) / खात (eating) / न (not) / बारा (delay) / आयसु (order) / दीन्ह (given) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / उदारा (noble/generous)
ramacharitamanas::4687.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4687.essence: True power can strike, but chooses restraint until duty speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4687.simple_meaning: Angad mocks Lanka as an easy fruit to crack open, but says he is restrained only because Ram has not ordered him to act.
ramacharitamanas::4687.simple_insight: Power is not proved by impulse. Real strength waits for the right command.
ramacharitamanas::4687.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana and his court, taunting them with fearless confidence. He says the city is as fragile as a fig fruit, yet he holds back because Ram has not commanded him to strike. The boast is part warning, part loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::4687.modern_relevance: You know the moment you could fire off the message, make the sharp remark, or take the win by force. Real control is holding back until your action is truly right.
ramacharitamanas::4687.insight: It shifts strength from raw impulse to disciplined obedience.

ramacharitamanas::4688.verse_sanskrit: जुगुति सुनत रावन मुसुकाई। मूढ़ सिखिहि कहँ बहुत झुठाई॥ बालि न कबहुँ गाल अस मारा। मिलि तपसिन्ह तैं भएसि लबारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4688.verse_hindi: अंगद की युक्ति सुनकर रावण मुस्कुराया (और बोला-) अरे मूर्ख! बहुत झूठ बोलना तूने कहाँ से सीखा? बालि ने तो कभी ऐसा गाल नहीं मारा। जान पड़ता है तू तपस्वियों से मिलकर लबार हो गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4688.english_translation: Ravana smiled at Angad's strategy and said, "Fool, where did you learn so much lying? Bali never spoke like this. You seem to have become a liar by mixing with ascetics."
ramacharitamanas::4688.translation_literal: जुगुति (strategy/plan) / सुनत (hearing) / रावन (Ravana) / मुसुकाई (smiled) / मूढ़ (fool) / सिखिहि (learned) / कहँ (from where) / बहुत (much) / झुठाई (lying)॥ / बालि (Bali) / न (not) / कबहुँ (ever) / गाल (boast/taunt) / अस (like this) / मारा (uttered/spoke) / मिलि (having met) / तपसिन्ह (ascetics) / तैं (you) / भएसि (became) / लबारा (liar) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4688.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4688.essence: Pride laughs at warning because it cannot bear correction.
ramacharitamanas::4688.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Angad's words and calls him a liar, saying Bali never spoke like that and ascetics must have taught him falsehood.
ramacharitamanas::4688.simple_insight: Pride refuses to hear truth and turns warning into insult.
ramacharitamanas::4688.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court at Lanka, Angad has come as Ram's envoy and is testing Ravana's pride with bold words. Ravana laughs off the challenge, dismissing Angad as a liar instead of facing the threat. The exchange sharpens the clash before open conflict.
ramacharitamanas::4688.modern_relevance: You point out a hard truth in a meeting, and someone smiles it away as nonsense. The problem is not your words — it's their refusal to face them.
ramacharitamanas::4688.insight: It shows how ego protects itself by mocking the messenger instead of answering the message.

ramacharitamanas::4689.verse_sanskrit: साँचेहुँ मैं लबार भुज बीहा। जौं न उपारिउँ तव दस जीहा॥ समुझि राम प्रताप कपि कोपा। सभा माझ पन करि पद रोपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4689.verse_hindi: (अंगद ने कहा-) अरे बीस भुजा वाले! यदि तेरी दसों जीभें मैंने नहीं उखाड़ लीं तो सचमुच मैं लबार ही हूँ। श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रताप को समझकर (स्मरण करके) अंगद क्रोधित हो उठे और उन्होंने रावण की सभा में प्रण करके (दृढ़ता के साथ) पैर रोप दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4689.english_translation: Angad said, “If I do not tear out your ten tongues, O twenty-armed one, then I am truly a liar.” Remembering Ram’s power, Angad grew angry and planted his foot firmly in Ravana’s assembly.
ramacharitamanas::4689.translation_literal: साँचेहुँ (truly) / मैं (I) / लबार (liar) / भुज बीहा (twenty-armed one) / जौं (if) / न (not) / उपारिउँ (I tear out) / तव (your) / दस जीहा (ten tongues) / समुझि (remembering) / राम प्रताप (Ram’s power) / कपि (the monkey) / कोपा (became angry) / सभा माझ (in the middle of the assembly) / पन करि (taking a vow) / पद (foot) / रोपा (planted firmly)
ramacharitamanas::4689.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4689.essence: Firmness comes from remembering Ram, not from personal pride.
ramacharitamanas::4689.simple_meaning: Angad vows to rip out Ravana’s ten tongues if he keeps insulting him, and he stands firm in Ravana’s court after remembering Ram’s power.
ramacharitamanas::4689.simple_insight: Real courage comes from remembering what you stand for before you speak or act.
ramacharitamanas::4689.detailed_meaning: In Ravana’s court, Angad has come as Ram’s envoy, but the exchange has turned sharp. Ravana mocks him, and Angad answers with fearless defiance, planting his foot in the assembly as proof of Ram’s strength and his own resolve.
ramacharitamanas::4689.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your work in a meeting, and your chest tightens. You don’t need noise or panic — you need the steadiness that comes from remembering who you represent.
ramacharitamanas::4689.insight: It shifts confidence from personal ego to remembrance of a higher cause.

ramacharitamanas::4690.verse_sanskrit: जौं मम चरन सकसि सठ टारी। फिरहिं रामु सीता मैं हारी॥ सुनहु सुभट सब कह दससीसा। पद गहि धरनि पछारहु कीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4690.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) अरे मूर्ख! यदि तू मेरा चरण हटा सके तो श्री रामजी लौट जाएँगे, मैं सीताजी को हार गया। रावण ने कहा- हे सब वीरो! सुनो, पैर पकड़कर बंदर को पृथ्वी पर पछाड़ दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4690.english_translation: “If you can move my foot, fool, then Ram will return and I will have lost Sita.” Ravana said, “Hear me, all warriors: seize the monkey’s feet and throw him to the ground.”
ramacharitamanas::4690.translation_literal: जौं (if) / मम (my) / चरन (foot) / सकसि (you can) / सठ (fool) / टारी (move away) / फिरहिं (will return) / रामु (Ram) / सीता (Sita) / मैं (I) / हारी (have lost)॥ / सुनहु (listen) / सुभट (great warriors) / सब (all) / कह (said) / दससीसा (ten-headed one) / पद (feet) / गहि (seizing) / धरनि (to the ground) / पछारहु (throw down) / कीसा (monkey) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4690.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4690.essence: Pride mocks danger until it is forced to command violence.
ramacharitamanas::4690.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that if Hanuman can move his foot, then Ram will return and he will have lost Sita. He then orders his warriors to grab Hanuman and throw him down.
ramacharitamanas::4690.simple_insight: Pride turns even a threat into a challenge, and that challenge becomes its own trap.
ramacharitamanas::4690.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war council, Hanuman has planted his foot on Ravana’s throne-like pride and refuses to budge. Ravana laughs off the insult, then tries to turn the moment into a show of force by ordering his warriors to crush the monkey.
ramacharitamanas::4690.modern_relevance: Someone mocks your boundary in a meeting, then suddenly calls in three colleagues to pressure you into backing down. The real issue was never the gesture — it was the ego behind it.
ramacharitamanas::4690.insight: It shows how ego answers humiliation with bluster instead of seeing reality.

ramacharitamanas::4691.verse_sanskrit: इंद्रजीत आदिक बलवाना। हरषि उठे जहँ तहँ भट नाना॥ झपटहिं करि बल बिपुल उपाई। पद न टरइ बैठहिं सिरु नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4691.verse_hindi: इंद्रजीत (मेघनाद) आदि अनेकों बलवान् योद्धा जहाँ-तहाँ से हर्षित होकर उठे। वे पूरे बल से बहुत से उपाय करके झपटते हैं। पर पैर टलता नहीं, तब सिर नीचा करके फिर अपने-अपने स्थान पर जा बैठ जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4691.english_translation: Indrajit and other mighty warriors rose up, delighted, from here and there. They rushed forward with great force and many different tactics, but their feet could not move Angad's stance; then they sat back down, bowing their heads.
ramacharitamanas::4691.translation_literal: इंद्रजीत (Indrajit) / आदिक (and others) / बलवाना (mighty) / हरषि (rejoicing) / उठे (rose) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / भट (warriors) / नाना (many)॥ / झपटहिं (they rush) / करि (with) / बल (strength) / बिपुल (great) / उपाई (strategies) / पद (feet) / न टरइ (do not move) / बैठहिं (they sit) / सिरु नाई (bowing heads)॥
ramacharitamanas::4691.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4691.essence: Powerful resistance collapses when it meets unshakable steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::4691.simple_meaning: Many powerful warriors rush in with confidence and clever tactics, but they cannot dislodge Angad. Defeated, they lower their heads and sit back down.
ramacharitamanas::4691.simple_insight: Pride can charge forward hard and still fail against steady resolve.
ramacharitamanas::4691.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Angad has planted his foot and challenged the warriors to move it. Indrajit and other mighty fighters leap up with force and strategy, but none can budge him. Their failure exposes the limit of raw power.
ramacharitamanas::4691.modern_relevance: A room full of senior people keeps arguing, sending in smarter plans, sharper objections, better numbers — yet the one calm person in the corner doesn't budge. Force keeps changing shape; resolve stays put.
ramacharitamanas::4691.insight: It shifts attention from aggressive effort to the unshakeable center that effort cannot move.

ramacharitamanas::4692.verse_sanskrit: पुनि उठि झपटहिं सुर आराती। टरइ न कीस चरन एहि भाँती॥ पुरुष कुजोगी जिमि उरगारी। मोह बिटप नहिं सकहिं उपारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4692.verse_hindi: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) वे देवताओं के शत्रु (राक्षस) फिर उठकर झपटते हैं, परन्तु हे सर्पों के शत्रु गरुड़जी! अंगद का चरण उनसे वैसे ही नहीं टलता जैसे कुयोगी (विषयी) पुरुष मोह रूपी वृक्ष को नहीं उखाड़ सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4692.english_translation: They rise and lunge again, but the monkey's foot does not move. In the same way, misguided people cannot uproot the tree of delusion.
ramacharitamanas::4692.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / उठि (rising) / झपटहिं (they lunge) / सुर आराती (enemies of the radiant beings) / टरइ (moves away) / न (not) / कीस (monkey) / चरन (foot) / एहि भाँती (in this manner) / पुरुष (man) / कुजोगी (misguided) / जिमि (like) / उरगारी (enemy of serpents) / मोह (delusion) / बिटप (tree) / नहिं (not) / सकहिं (can) / उपारी (uproot)
ramacharitamanas::4692.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::4692.essence: What is firmly rooted cannot be shaken by repeated force.
ramacharitamanas::4692.simple_meaning: A firm devotee does not get shaken by repeated attacks, just as confused people cannot uproot delusion’s hold by force alone.
ramacharitamanas::4692.simple_insight: Steadiness is stronger than repeated pressure. What is rooted in devotion does not easily budge.
ramacharitamanas::4692.detailed_meaning: Kak Bhushundi is describing the battle in Lanka through a larger truth. The warriors keep rushing in, but Angad’s foot stays fixed. Their force fails, just as a confused mind cannot simply tear out delusion by effort alone.
ramacharitamanas::4692.modern_relevance: You keep getting pulled into the same argument, the same craving, the same panic — and yet a part of you can stay unmoved. That steadiness is the real victory.
ramacharitamanas::4692.insight: It shifts attention from reactive struggle to inner firmness. The verse teaches that some forces break against unwavering presence.

ramacharitamanas::4693.verse_sanskrit: कोटिन्ह मेघनाद सम सुभट उठे हरषाइ। झपटहिं टरै न कपि चरन पुनि बैठहिं सिर नाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4693.verse_hindi: करोड़ों वीर योद्धा जो बल में मेघनाद के समान थे, हर्षित होकर उठे, वे बार-बार झपटते हैं, पर वानर का चरण नहीं उठता, तब लज्जा के मारे सिर नवाकर बैठ जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4693.english_translation: Millions of warriors as mighty as Meghnad rose up in joy. They kept lunging, but the monkey's foot never moved; then, ashamed, they sat down bowing their heads.
ramacharitamanas::4693.translation_literal: कोटिन्ह (millions) / मेघनाद सम (like Meghnad) / सुभट (warriors) / उठे (rose up) / हरषाइ (in joy) / झपटहिं (they lunge) / टरै न (does not move) / कपि चरन (the monkey's foot) / पुनि (again) / बैठहिं (they sit) / सिर नाइ (bowing the head)
ramacharitamanas::4693.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4693.essence: Unmoved steadiness makes force collapse on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4693.simple_meaning: Countless powerful warriors rise and attack, but the monkey warrior does not budge. Their force fails, and they sit down in shame.
ramacharitamanas::4693.simple_insight: Steady courage can outlast even overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::4693.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's warriors surge forward again and again against Angad. They are fierce enough to be compared to Meghnad, yet Angad's planted foot does not move. Their repeated failure becomes humiliation, not victory.
ramacharitamanas::4693.modern_relevance: A room full of people pushes back against your boundary, expecting you to fold. You stay calm, unmoved, and the pressure loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::4693.insight: It teaches you that rooted steadiness can defeat frantic aggression without a larger fight.

ramacharitamanas::4694.verse_sanskrit: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
ramacharitamanas::4694.verse_hindi: जैसे करोड़ों विघ्न आने पर भी संत का मन नीति को नहीं छोड़ता, वैसे ही वानर (अंगद) का चरण पृथ्वी को नहीं छोड़ता। यह देखकर शत्रु (रावण) का मद दूर हो गया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4694.english_translation: Like a saint who never abandons righteous conduct even through countless obstacles, Angada's foot did not leave the ground. Seeing this, Ravana's pride fell away.
ramacharitamanas::4694.translation_literal: भूमि (earth) / न छाँड़त (does not leave) / कपि चरन (the monkey's foot) / देखत (seeing) / रिपु मद (enemy's pride) / भाग (fled) / कोटि बिघ्न (crores of obstacles) / ते (even through) / संत कर मन (the saint's mind) / जिमि (like) / नीति (righteous conduct) / न त्याग (does not abandon)
ramacharitamanas::4694.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4694.essence: Firm conduct can break pride more than force can.
ramacharitamanas::4694.simple_meaning: Angada stands so firmly that even Ravana's pride breaks. The image compares that steadiness to a saint who never drops righteous conduct, no matter how many obstacles appear.
ramacharitamanas::4694.simple_insight: Steadiness can humble arrogance without a single blow.
ramacharitamanas::4694.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angada plants his foot in Ravana's court and refuses to move. The demon king's pride begins to crack as everyone watches this impossible stillness. The couplet supports the larger challenge scene, not a full teaching by itself.
ramacharitamanas::4694.modern_relevance: You stay calm in a room where everyone expects you to fold. Your silence, more than your argument, exposes the other person's bluster.
ramacharitamanas::4694.insight: It shifts attention from force to unshakable conduct under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4695.verse_sanskrit: कपि बल देखि सकल हियँ हारे। उठा आपु कपि कें परचारे॥ गहत चरन कह बालिकुमारा। मम पद गहें न तोर उबारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4695.verse_hindi: अंगद का बल देखकर सब हृदय में हार गए। तब अंगद के ललकारने पर रावण स्वयं उठा। जब वह अंगद का चरण पकड़ने लगा, तब बालि कुमार अंगद ने कहा- मेरा चरण पकड़ने से तेरा बचाव नहीं होगा! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4695.english_translation: Seeing Angad's strength, everyone lost heart. Then, at Angad's challenge, Ravana himself rose. When he tried to seize Angad's foot, the son of Bali said, 'Holding my foot will not save you!'
ramacharitamanas::4695.translation_literal: कपि (monkey/vanara) / बल (strength) / देखि (seeing) / सकल (all) / हियँ (in heart) / हारे (were defeated) / उठा (rose) / आपु (himself) / कपि (monkey/vanara) / कें (of) / परचारे (challenge/provocation) / गहत (seizing/holding) / चरन (foot) / कह (said) / बालिकुमारा (son of Bali) / मम (my) / पद (foot) / गहें (by holding) / न (not) / तोर (your) / उबारा (rescue/saving)
ramacharitamanas::4695.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4695.essence: Bravado collapses when courage refuses to bow.
ramacharitamanas::4695.simple_meaning: Angad's strength shakes the enemy force, and Ravana rises to face him. But Angad makes it clear that grabbing his foot cannot save Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4695.simple_insight: Pride can be rattled by courage, but real surrender still has to happen.
ramacharitamanas::4695.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana as an envoy with fearless strength. The demon king is shaken, rises, and reaches for Angad's foot in a last attempt to preserve face. Angad answers with a sharp reminder that only Ram can save him.
ramacharitamanas::4695.modern_relevance: Someone finally calls out the person dominating the room, and the whole mood changes. But the real turning point still comes only when ego stops bargaining and faces the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4695.insight: It shows that intimidation may bend pride, but it cannot replace true surrender.

ramacharitamanas::4696.verse_sanskrit: गहसि न राम चरन सठ जाई॥ सुनत फिरा मन अति सकुचाई॥ भयउ तेजहत श्री सब गई। मध्य दिवस जिमि ससि सोहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4696.verse_hindi: अरे मूर्ख- तू जाकर श्री रामजी के चरण क्यों नहीं पकड़ता? यह सुनकर वह मन में बहुत ही सकुचाकर लौट गया। उसकी सारी श्री जाती रही। वह ऐसा तेजहीन हो गया जैसे मध्याह्न में चंद्रमा दिखाई देता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4696.english_translation: “Why don’t you go and grasp Ram’s feet, fool?” Hearing this, he turned back in deep shame. All his radiance vanished, and he looked like the moon at midday.
ramacharitamanas::4696.translation_literal: गहसि (grasp) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / सठ (fool) / जाई (go) ॥ / सुनत (hearing) / फिरा (turned back) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / सकुचाई (ashamed) ॥ / भयउ (became) / तेजहत (without radiance) / श्री (splendor) / सब (all) / गई (went away) ॥ / मध्य (middle) / दिवस (day) / जिमि (like) / ससि (moon) / सोहई (shines) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4696.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4696.essence: Ego loses its shine the moment surrender is demanded.
ramacharitamanas::4696.simple_meaning: He is told to surrender to Ram, but shame makes him retreat. His pride collapses, and his former brilliance disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4696.simple_insight: Pride can vanish in a single moment when the heart is finally asked to bow.
ramacharitamanas::4696.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Angad’s challenge, Ravana is pushed toward a humiliating truth: only Ram can save him. This verse shows his inward collapse as he hears the command to seek Ram’s feet and loses the shine of ego.
ramacharitamanas::4696.modern_relevance: You rehearse your defense in the car, then hear one sentence that exposes everything. Your face goes hot, your certainty drops, and the part of you that wanted to stay untouchable suddenly feels small.
ramacharitamanas::4696.insight: It shifts the mind from defending pride to seeing surrender as the only real opening.

ramacharitamanas::4697.verse_sanskrit: सिंघासन बैठेउ सिर नाई। मानहुँ संपति सकल गँवाई॥ जगदातमा प्रानपति रामा। तासु बिमुख किमि लह बिश्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4697.verse_hindi: वह सिर नीचा करके सिंहासन पर जा बैठा। मानो सारी सम्पत्ति गँवाकर बैठा हो। श्री रामचंद्रजी जगत् भर के आत्मा और प्राणों के स्वामी हैं। उनसे विमुख रहने वाला शांति कैसे पा सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4697.english_translation: He sat on the throne with his head bowed, as if he had lost all his wealth. Lord Ram is the soul of the world and the master of life itself; how can anyone turned away from him find peace?
ramacharitamanas::4697.translation_literal: सिंघासन (throne) / बैठेउ (sat) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / मानहुँ (as if) / संपति (wealth, possession) / सकल (all) / गँवाई (lost) / जगदातमा (soul of the world) / प्रानपति (lord of life) / रामा (Ram) / तासु (his) / बिमुख (turned away) / किमि (how) / लह (find) / बिश्रामा (rest, peace)
ramacharitamanas::4697.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4697.essence: Separation from Ram leaves even power unable to rest.
ramacharitamanas::4697.simple_meaning: Ram is the life of everything, so turning away from him leaves a person unable to find peace.
ramacharitamanas::4697.simple_insight: Real peace comes from alignment, not position or possession.
ramacharitamanas::4697.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has lost his confidence and sits on his throne with his head bowed. Tulsidas shows the deeper loss beneath the political defeat: a ruler cut off from Ram has already lost the only peace that matters.
ramacharitamanas::4697.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the title, the bigger apartment — and still feel strangely unsettled at night. Something deeper than success is missing, and this verse names it.
ramacharitamanas::4697.insight: It shifts the mind from outer status to inner alignment with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4698.verse_sanskrit: उमा राम की भृकुटि बिलासा। होइ बिस्व पुनि पावइ नासा॥ तृन ते कुलिस कुलिस तृन करई। तासु दूत पन कहु किमि टरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4698.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! जिन श्री रामचंद्रजी के भ्रूविलास (भौंह के इशारे) से विश्व उत्पन्न होता है और फिर नाश को प्राप्त होता है, जो तृण को वज्र और वज्र को तृण बना देते हैं (अत्यंत निर्बल को महान् प्रबल और महान् प्रबल को अत्यंत निर्बल कर देते हैं), उनके दूत का प्रण कहो, कैसे टल सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4698.english_translation: O Uma, by Ram's glance alone the world arises and then returns to ruin. He can turn straw into thunderbolt and thunderbolt into straw; how can his messenger's pledge ever be turned aside?
ramacharitamanas::4698.translation_literal: उमा (Uma) / राम की (of Ram's) / भृकुटि (eyebrow) / बिलासा (play) / होइ (becomes) / बिस्व (world) / पुनि (again) / पावइ (gets) / नासा (destruction) / तृन (straw) / ते (from) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / तृन (straw) / करई (makes) / तासु (his) / दूत (messenger) / पन (pledge) / कहु (tell) / किमि (how) / टरई (can be turned away)
ramacharitamanas::4698.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4698.essence: Ram's backing makes a messenger unstoppable.
ramacharitamanas::4698.simple_meaning: Ram's smallest glance shapes creation and destruction. If his messenger is sent on a mission, no force can block that vow.
ramacharitamanas::4698.simple_insight: When the divine backs you, your task is already protected.
ramacharitamanas::4698.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana after showing his strength and refusing to bow. Shiva tells Uma that Ram's power is so vast that even a messenger sent by him carries an unbreakable pledge. Ravana is facing more than a warrior; he is facing Ram's will.
ramacharitamanas::4698.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where every person has already decided against you. Still, something in you stays unshaken because you know who sent you and why.
ramacharitamanas::4698.insight: It shifts confidence from personal ability to the authority behind your action.

ramacharitamanas::4699.verse_sanskrit: पुनि कपि कही नीति बिधि नाना। मान न ताहि कालु निअराना॥ रिपु मद मथि प्रभु सुजसु सुनायो। यह कहि चल्यो बालि नृप जायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4699.verse_hindi: फिर अंगद ने अनेकों प्रकार से नीति कही। पर रावण नहीं माना, क्योंकि उसका काल निकट आ गया था। शत्रु के गर्व को चूर करके अंगद ने उसको प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी का सुयश सुनाया और फिर वह राजा बालि का पुत्र यह कहकर चल दिया- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4699.english_translation: Then Angada spoke many kinds of wise counsel. But Ravana did not agree, because his time of death was near. Crushing the enemy's pride, Angada spoke the glory of Lord Ram, and then, saying this, he left, the son of Bali.
ramacharitamanas::4699.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / कपि (monkey) / कही (spoke) / नीति (wise counsel) / बिधि (many kinds) / नाना (various) / मान (accepted) / न ताहि (not that) / कालु (time/death) / निअराना (had come near) / रिपु (enemy) / मद (pride) / मथि (crushing/churning) / प्रभु (Lord) / सुजसु (glory) / सुनायो (made heard) / यह कहि (saying this) / चल्यो (left) / बालि (Bali) / नृप (king) / जायो (born/son)
ramacharitamanas::4699.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4699.essence: Pride can make even clear counsel useless.
ramacharitamanas::4699.simple_meaning: Angada tried many kinds of counsel, but Ravana would not listen. His pride was already too strong, and his end was close. Angada then praised Ram and left.
ramacharitamanas::4699.simple_insight: Some people cannot hear wisdom once pride has taken over.
ramacharitamanas::4699.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's court, Angada stands before Ravana and speaks with courage. He offers wise counsel, but Ravana's arrogance blocks every word. Angada crushes that pride by praising Ram's glory, then walks away.
ramacharitamanas::4699.modern_relevance: You explain the consequences clearly, but the other person keeps defending a bad choice. At some point, the healthiest move is to speak truth once and step back.
ramacharitamanas::4699.insight: It shows that counsel has limits when ego has already hardened into refusal.

ramacharitamanas::4700.verse_sanskrit: हतौं न खेत खेलाइ खेलाई। तोहि अबहिं का करौं बड़ाई॥ प्रथमहिं तासु तनय कपि मारा। सो सुनि रावन भयउ दुखारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4700.verse_hindi: रणभूमि में तुझे खेला-खेलाकर न मारूँ तब तक अभी (पहले से) क्या बड़ाई करूँ। अंगद ने पहले ही (सभा में आने से पूर्व ही) उसके पुत्र को मार डाला था। वह संवाद सुनकर रावण दुःखी हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4700.english_translation: How can I boast now unless I first make you fight and kill you in battle? Hearing that Angad had already killed his son before coming to the assembly, Ravana was stricken with grief.
ramacharitamanas::4700.translation_literal: हतौं (I would kill) / न (not) / खेत (in battle) / खेलाइ (making play) / खेलाई (having played) / तोहि (you) / अबहिं (now) / का (what) / करौं (do I) / बड़ाई (boast)॥ / प्रथमहिं (first) / तासु (his) / तनय (son) / कपि (monkey-hero) / मारा (killed) / सो (that) / सुनि (hearing) / रावन (Ravana) / भयउ (became) / दुखारा (grieved)॥
ramacharitamanas::4700.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4700.essence: Boasting means nothing until victory is real.
ramacharitamanas::4700.simple_meaning: Angad taunts Ravana, saying he cannot claim victory unless he defeats him in battle. The mention of Ravana's son being killed earlier only deepens Ravana's grief.
ramacharitamanas::4700.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when grief is already inside it.
ramacharitamanas::4700.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Angad has already challenged the demon king's arrogance. He reminds Ravana that real boasting comes only after victory in battle, then twists the knife by mentioning the death of Ravana's son. The line lands as humiliation, not philosophy.
ramacharitamanas::4700.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone makes a smug claim, and you answer with one sentence that exposes how little they can actually prove. The air changes because the boast has nowhere left to stand.
ramacharitamanas::4700.insight: It shows how taunts can expose false pride by forcing it to face loss.

ramacharitamanas::4701.verse_sanskrit: जातुधान अंगद पन देखी। भय ब्याकुल सब भए बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4701.verse_hindi: अंगद का प्रण (सफल) देखकर सब राक्षस भय से अत्यन्त ही व्याकुल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4701.english_translation: Seeing Angad's vow succeed, all the demons became especially terrified and agitated with fear.
ramacharitamanas::4701.translation_literal: जातुधान (demons) / अंगद (Angad) / पन (vow) / देखी (seeing) / भय (fear) / ब्याकुल (agitated) / सब (all) / भए (became) / बिसेषी (especially)
ramacharitamanas::4701.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4701.essence: Fear spreads fast when pride is publicly defeated.
ramacharitamanas::4701.simple_meaning: The demons saw Angad's challenge succeed, and fear spread through all of them.
ramacharitamanas::4701.simple_insight: Courage can shake a whole room when fear has been hiding behind pride.
ramacharitamanas::4701.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Angad has already humiliated the enemy's pride and proved his challenge true. Now the demons watch that vow stand firm, and their confidence collapses into panic.
ramacharitamanas::4701.modern_relevance: A quiet person speaks one clear truth in a tense meeting, and the whole room shifts. What looked like confidence was only bluster.
ramacharitamanas::4701.insight: It shows how a single fearless act can break collective arrogance.

ramacharitamanas::4702.verse_sanskrit: रिपु बल धरषि हरषि कपि बालितनय बल पुंज। पुलक सरीर नयन जल गहे राम पद कंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::4702.verse_hindi: शत्रु के बल का मर्दन कर, बल की राशि बालि पुत्र अंगदजी ने हर्षित होकर आकर श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए। उनका शरीर पुलकित है और नेत्रों में (आनंदाश्रुओं का) जल भरा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4702.english_translation: Having crushed the enemy's power, Angad, son of Bali and a mass of strength, came rejoicing and grasped Ram's lotus feet. His body thrilled, and tears filled his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::4702.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / बल (strength) / धरषि (crushing) / हरषि (rejoicing) / कपि (monkey) / बालि-तनय (Bali's son) / बल-पुंज (mass of strength) / पुलक (horripilation) / सरीर (body) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / गहे (grasped) / राम (Ram) / पद-कंज (lotus feet)
ramacharitamanas::4702.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4702.essence: Strength becomes complete when it returns to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4702.simple_meaning: Angad defeats the enemy's pride and then comes joyfully to Ram, overwhelmed with devotion. Victory leads him not to self-display, but to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4702.simple_insight: True strength ends in humility, not self-congratulation.
ramacharitamanas::4702.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has just shaken Ravana's court with his fearless challenge. After breaking the enemy's confidence, Bali's son returns not as a victor seeking praise, but as a devotee who rushes to Ram's feet, trembling with joy and tears.
ramacharitamanas::4702.modern_relevance: You finally win the argument, close the deal, or prove your point — and the real relief is not being right. It is coming back to what you serve.
ramacharitamanas::4702.insight: It shifts success from self-importance to surrender, showing that real power bows down.

ramacharitamanas::4703.verse_sanskrit: साँझ जानि दसकंधर भवन गयउ बिलखाइ। मंदोदरीं रावनहिं बहुरि कहा समुझाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4703.verse_hindi: सन्ध्या हो गई जानकर दशग्रीव बिलखता हुआ (उदास होकर) महल में गया। मन्दोदरी ने रावण को समझाकर फिर कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4703.english_translation: Knowing that evening had fallen, Ravana went sorrowfully back to the palace. Mandodari then tried again to counsel him.
ramacharitamanas::4703.translation_literal: साँझ (evening) / जानि (knowing) / दसकंधर (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / भवन (palace) / गयउ (went) / बिलखाइ (sorrowfully) / मंदोदरीं (Mandodari) / रावनहिं (to Ravana) / बहुरि (again) / कहा (said) / समुझाइ (explaining/counselling)
ramacharitamanas::4703.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4703.essence: Defeat becomes dangerous when pride refuses counsel.
ramacharitamanas::4703.simple_meaning: Ravana returns to his palace in distress after dusk, and Mandodari tries once more to reason with him.
ramacharitamanas::4703.simple_insight: Pride can survive a battle, but it cannot escape the voice of conscience.
ramacharitamanas::4703.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Angad's challenge shakes the demon court, Ravana goes home at dusk in grief. Mandodari meets him again and tries to pull him back from ruin. The verse sets up her warning, not the warning itself.
ramacharitamanas::4703.modern_relevance: You come home after a meeting where your plan fell apart, and the silence feels heavier than the failure. Someone who loves you still tries to reach you before you harden.
ramacharitamanas::4703.insight: It shifts attention from the outer defeat to the inner collapse that follows stubbornness.

ramacharitamanas::4704.verse_sanskrit: कंत समुझि मन तजहु कुमतिही। सोह न समर तुम्हहि रघुपतिही॥ रामानुज लघु रेख खचाई। सोउ नहिं नाघेहु असि मनुसाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4704.verse_hindi: हे कान्त! मन में समझकर (विचारकर) कुबुद्धि को छोड़ दो। आप से और श्री रघुनाथजी से युद्ध शोभा नहीं देता। उनके छोटे भाई ने एक जरा सी रेखा खींच दी थी, उसे भी आप नहीं लाँघ सके, ऐसा तो आपका पुरुषत्व है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4704.english_translation: O dear one, think carefully in your mind and abandon foolish thinking. A war with Raghupati does not suit you. You could not even cross the small line drawn by Lakshmana, so is that your manliness?
