ramacharitamanas::4704.translation_literal: कंत (dear one) / समुझि (having understood) / मन (mind) / तजहु (abandon) / कुमतिही (foolish thinking) / सोह (is fitting) / न (not) / समर (war) / तुम्हहि (for you) / रघुपतिही (with Raghupati) / रामानुज (Lakshmana, younger brother of Ram) / लघु (small) / रेख (line) / खचाई (drawn) / सोउ (that also) / नहिं (not) / नाघेहु (you crossed) / असि (such) / मनुसाई (manliness)
ramacharitamanas::4704.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4704.essence: Ego cannot see its own limits until it is already trapped.
ramacharitamanas::4704.simple_meaning: Mandodari urges Ravana to drop his bad judgment and avoid fighting Ram. She reminds him that he could not even cross Lakshmana's small line, so his pride is misplaced.
ramacharitamanas::4704.simple_insight: Pride weakens judgment. Sometimes the bravest move is to admit a limit before it becomes ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4704.detailed_meaning: As evening falls in Lanka, Ravana returns home shaken after another setback. Mandodari tries one last time to reach him with reason and shame, pointing to Lakshmana's line as proof that his arrogance has already failed. This verse is part of her warning, not the final conclusion.
ramacharitamanas::4704.modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry text that will end the relationship. A quieter voice in you already knows the argument is bigger than your ego.
ramacharitamanas::4704.insight: It shifts the mind from bravado to honest self-assessment before acting.

ramacharitamanas::4705.verse_sanskrit: पिय तुम्ह ताहि जितब संग्रामा। जाके दूत केर यह कामा॥ कौतुक सिंधु नाघि तव लंका। आयउ कपि केहरी असंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4705.verse_hindi: हे प्रियतम! आप उन्हें संग्राम में जीत पाएँगे, जिनके दूत का ऐसा काम है? खेल से ही समुद्र लाँघकर वह वानरों में सिंह (हनुमान् ) आपकी लंका में निर्भय चला आया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4705.english_translation: Dear one, how can you win a battle against the one whose messenger did this? Crossing the ocean was play for him; that fearless monkey-lion entered your Lanka without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4705.translation_literal: पिय (dear one) / तुम्ह (you) / ताहि (that one) / जितब (to win) / संग्रामा (battle) / जाके (whose) / दूत (messenger) / केर (of) / यह (this) / कामा (deed) ॥ / कौतुक (sport/play) / सिंधु (ocean) / नाघि (crossing) / तव (your) / लंका (Lanka) ॥ / आयउ (came) / कपि (monkey) / केहरी (lion) / असंका (without fear) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4705.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4705.essence: Fearless action exposes the futility of arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4705.simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana that he cannot defeat Ram in battle when Ram's messenger has already crossed the ocean and entered Lanka fearlessly.
ramacharitamanas::4705.simple_insight: A single fearless act can reveal the scale of a power you underestimated.
ramacharitamanas::4705.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari keeps trying to wake Ravana before the war destroys everything. She points to Hanuman's impossible leap and fearless entry into the city as proof that Ram's side cannot be treated lightly. Her warning is part of a larger plea, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramacharitamanas::4705.modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room, then discover they already handled the hardest part without asking permission. The warning came too late to save your pride.
ramacharitamanas::4705.insight: It shifts the mind from swagger to sober recognition of strength already demonstrated.

ramacharitamanas::4706.verse_sanskrit: रखवारे हति बिपिन उजारा। देखत तोहि अच्छ तेहिं मारा॥ जारि सकल पुर कीन्हेसि छारा। कहाँ रहा बल गर्ब तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4706.verse_hindi: रखवालों को मारकर उसने अशोक वन उजाड़ डाला। आपके देखते-देखते उसने अक्षयकुमार को मार डाला और संपूर्ण नगर को जलाकर राख कर दिया। उस समय आपके बल का गर्व कहाँ चला गया था? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4706.english_translation: He killed the guards and laid waste to the grove. In front of your own eyes, he killed Akshayakumar. He burned the whole city to ashes. Where did your boast of strength go then?
ramacharitamanas::4706.translation_literal: रखवारे (guards) / हति (killing) / बिपिन (grove) / उजारा (laid waste) / देखत (while seeing) / तोहि (you) / अच्छ (in front) / तेहिं (that one) / मारा (killed) / जारि (burning) / सकल (whole) / पुर (city) / कीन्हेसि (made) / छारा (ashes) / कहाँ (where) / रहा (went) / बल (strength) / गर्ब (pride) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::4706.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4706.essence: Pride sounds powerful until events prove otherwise.
ramacharitamanas::4706.simple_meaning: Hanuman has already destroyed the grove, killed the guards, slain Akshayakumar, and burned Lanka. Ravana's boast about his strength is exposed as empty.
ramacharitamanas::4706.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when reality has already happened in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4706.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being confronted with the damage already done by Hanuman. The guards are dead, the grove is ruined, Akshayakumar has fallen, and the city is burning. The verse strips away Ravana's boast and shows his power failing in real time.
ramacharitamanas::4706.modern_relevance: You bragged you had it under control, then the mess was already on fire. A single hard fact can expose how fragile your confidence really was.
ramacharitamanas::4706.insight: It forces the mind to face consequences instead of hiding behind pride.

ramacharitamanas::4707.verse_sanskrit: अब पति मृषा गाल जनि मारहु। मोर कहा कछु हृदयँ बिचारहु॥ पति रघुपतिहि नृपति जनि मानहु। अग जग नाथ अतुलबल जानहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4707.verse_hindi: अब हे स्वामी! झूठ (व्यर्थ) गाल न मारिए (डींग न हाँकिए) मेरे कहने पर हृदय में कुछ विचार कीजिए। हे पति! आप श्री रघुपति को (निरा) राजा मत समझिए, बल्कि अग-जगनाथ (चराचर के स्वामी) और अतुलनीय बलवान् जानिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4707.english_translation: Now, husband, do not hurl empty insults. Think carefully about what I am saying in your heart. Do not take Raghupati for a mere king; know Him as the lord of all worlds and of immeasurable strength.
ramacharitamanas::4707.translation_literal: अब (now) / पति (husband, master) / मृषा (false, empty) / गाल (abuse, insults) / जनि (do not) / मारहु (throw, hurl) / मोर (my) / कहा (what) / कछु (some) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारहु (consider) / पति (husband, master) / रघुपतिहि (Raghupati) / नृपति (king) / जनि (do not) / मानहु (consider) / अग (all) / जग (worlds) / नाथ (lord) / अतुलबल (immeasurable strength) / जानहु (know)
ramacharitamanas::4707.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4707.essence: Pride is dangerous because it refuses to see power clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4707.simple_meaning: Mandodari warns Ravana not to insult Ram. She tells him to think seriously and stop treating Ram like an ordinary king, because Ram is the lord of all worlds and immeasurably powerful.
ramacharitamanas::4707.simple_insight: Pride makes you misread the very power that can end you.
ramacharitamanas::4707.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari pleads with Ravana after Hanuman's devastation. She is trying to break through his arrogance before it destroys him. This verse is one more urgent attempt to make him see Ram clearly, but his mind is already hardened.
ramacharitamanas::4707.modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the warning because admitting it would bruise your ego. A friend, a partner, or a colleague is trying to save you from a choice you still call harmless.
ramacharitamanas::4707.insight: It shifts the mind from contempt to clear seeing before arrogance becomes ruin.

ramacharitamanas::4708.verse_sanskrit: बान प्रताप जान मारीचा। तासु कहा नहिं मानेहि नीचा॥ जनक सभाँ अगनित भूपाला। रहे तुम्हउ बल अतुल बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4708.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के बाण का प्रताप तो नीच मारीच भी जानता था, परन्तु आपने उसका कहना भी नहीं माना। जनक की सभा में अगणित राजागण थे। वहाँ विशाल और अतुलनीय बल वाले आप भी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4708.english_translation: Even lowly Maricha knew the power of Rama's arrow, yet you did not heed his warning. In Janaka's assembly there were countless kings; you too were there, mighty and immeasurable in strength.
ramacharitamanas::4708.translation_literal: बान (arrow) / प्रताप (power, glory) / जान (knowing) / मारीचा (Maricha) / तासु (his) / कहा (saying) / नहिं (not) / मानेहि (you accepted) / नीचा (lowly one) / जनक (Janaka) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / अगनित (countless) / भूपाला (kings) / रहे (were) / तुम्हउ (you too) / बल (strength) / अतुल (matchless) / बिसाला (vast)
ramacharitamanas::4708.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4708.essence: Pride can hear the truth and still refuse it.
ramacharitamanas::4708.simple_meaning: Ravana is being reminded that even Maricha knew Rama's power, and that Ravana was also present in Janaka's court among many kings.
ramacharitamanas::4708.simple_insight: Pride makes you ignore warnings even when the evidence is right in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4708.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the argument turns back on Ravana. The speaker recalls Maricha's warning and Janaka's court, where Ravana had already seen Rama's unmatched strength. The verse exposes how ego can hear the truth and still refuse it.
ramacharitamanas::4708.modern_relevance: You ignore the one colleague who quietly sees the risk clearly, then act surprised when the plan collapses. The warning was never hidden; your pride was louder.
ramacharitamanas::4708.insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to remembering earlier evidence and hard lessons.

ramacharitamanas::4709.verse_sanskrit: भंजि धनुष जानकी बिआही। तब संग्राम जितेहु किन ताही॥ सुरपति सुत जानइ बल थोरा। राखा जिअत आँखि गहि फोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4709.verse_hindi: वहाँ शिवजी का धनुष तोड़कर श्री रामजी ने जानकी को ब्याहा, तब आपने उनको संग्राम में क्यों नहीं जीता? इंद्रपुत्र जयन्त उनके बल को कुछ-कुछ जानता है। श्री रामजी ने पकड़कर, केवल उसकी एक आँख ही फोड़ दी और उसे जीवित ही छोड़ दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4709.english_translation: When Ram broke Shiva's bow and married Janaki, why did you not defeat him in battle then? Jayant, the son of Indra, knows something of Ram's strength; Ram seized him, broke only one of his eyes, and left him alive.
ramacharitamanas::4709.translation_literal: भंजि (breaking) / धनुष (bow) / जानकी (Janaki) / बिआही (married) / तब (then) / संग्राम (battle) / जितेहु (you conquered) / किन (why) / ताही (him) / सुरपति (of Indra) / सुत (son) / जानइ (knows) / बल (strength) / थोरा (a little) / राखा (kept) / जिअत (alive) / आँखि (eye) / गहि (seizing) / फोरा (broke)
ramacharitamanas::4709.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4709.essence: Even Ravana admits Ram's power, yet his pride still will not bend.
ramacharitamanas::4709.simple_meaning: Ravana reminds Sita's captor that Ram already proved his power by breaking Shiva's bow and sparing Jayant after wounding him.
ramacharitamanas::4709.simple_insight: Pride sounds strongest when it is already cornered by the truth.
ramacharitamanas::4709.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to justify his arrogance before Sita. He points to Ram's past feats — breaking Shiva's bow, winning Janaki, and sparing Jayant — to argue that Ram's strength is real, even though Ravana still refuses to yield.
ramacharitamanas::4709.modern_relevance: You keep arguing with someone whose record already speaks for itself. The facts are plain, but your ego still wants the last word.
ramacharitamanas::4709.insight: It exposes how ego can acknowledge reality and still refuse to submit to it.

ramacharitamanas::4710.verse_sanskrit: सूपनखा कै गति तुम्ह देखी। तदपि हृदयँ नहिं लाज बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4710.verse_hindi: शूर्पणखा की दशा तो आपने देख ही ली। तो भी आपके हृदय में (उनसे लड़ने की बात सोचते) विशेष (कुछ भी) लज्जा नहीं आती! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4710.english_translation: You saw what happened to Shurpanakha, and still your heart feels no special shame.
ramacharitamanas::4710.translation_literal: सूपनखा (Shurpanakha) / कै (of) / गति (fate, condition) / तुम्ह (you) / देखी (saw) / तदपि (even then) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / नहिं (not) / लाज (shame) / बिसेषी (special, great)
ramacharitamanas::4710.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4710.essence: Seeing the warning means nothing if pride stays untouched.
ramacharitamanas::4710.simple_meaning: You saw Shurpanakha’s condition, yet you still feel no shame about what happened next.
ramacharitamanas::4710.simple_insight: Pride can keep you from learning even after the warning is obvious.
ramacharitamanas::4710.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the speaker is pressing Ravana with examples of his own blindness. Shurpanakha’s humiliation should have warned him, yet he stayed unashamed and unchanged. The verse is one more blow in a larger argument, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4710.modern_relevance: You watch a friend ignore every warning sign, then repeat the same mistake anyway. The hard part is not lack of information — it is refusing to feel the lesson.
ramacharitamanas::4710.insight: It shifts attention from facts to self-correction: seeing clearly means letting the lesson change you.

ramacharitamanas::4711.verse_sanskrit: बधि बिराध खर दूषनहि लीलाँ हत्यो कबंध। बालि एक सर मार् यो तेहि जानहु दसकंध ॥
ramacharitamanas::4711.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने विराध और खर-दूषण को मारकर लीला से ही कबन्ध को भी मार डाला और जिन्होंने बालि को एक ही बाण से मार दिया, हे दशकन्ध! आप उन्हें (उनके महत्व को) समझिए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4711.english_translation: O ten-headed one, understand their power: they killed Viradh, Khara, and Dushana, slew Kabandha effortlessly, and struck Bali down with a single arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4711.translation_literal: बधि (having killed) / बिराध (Viradh) / खर (Khara) / दूषनहि (Dushana) / लीलाँ (playfully, effortlessly) / हत्यो (killed) / कबंध (Kabandha) / बालि (Bali) / एक सर (with one arrow) / मार् यो (struck down) / तेहि (him) / जानहु (know/understand) / दसकंध (O ten-headed one)
ramacharitamanas::4711.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4711.essence: Past victories should end your false confidence.
ramacharitamanas::4711.simple_meaning: Ravana is reminded that Ram has already destroyed powerful foes with ease, so he should not underestimate him.
ramacharitamanas::4711.simple_insight: Arrogance fades when you remember how often strength has already been proven.
ramacharitamanas::4711.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the argument is tightening around Ravana. The speaker lists Ram's victories over Viradh, Khara, Dushana, Kabandha, and Bali to warn him that this is not a weak enemy. The verse supports the larger warning rather than standing alone.
ramacharitamanas::4711.modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the person you hurt with one careless remark, forgetting how steadily they have handled harder blows before.
ramacharitamanas::4711.insight: It shifts attention from Ravana's pride to Ram's proven power and the danger of underestimating it.

ramacharitamanas::4712.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं जलनाथ बँधायउ हेला। उतरे प्रभु दल सहित सुबेला॥ कारुनीक दिनकर कुल केतू। दूत पठायउ तव हित हेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4712.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने खेल से ही समुद्र को बँधा लिया और जो प्रभु सेना सहित सुबेल पर्वत पर उतर पड़े, उन सूर्यकुल के ध्वजास्वरूप (कीर्ति को बढ़ाने वाले) करुणामय भगवान् ने आप ही के हित के लिए दूत भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4712.english_translation: He who, by a mere play, bound the ocean and descended with his army to Mount Suvela— that compassionate banner of the solar line sent a messenger for your own good.
ramacharitamanas::4712.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / जलनाथ (ocean-lord) / बँधायउ (bound) / हेला (playfully) / उतरे (descended) / प्रभु (the Lord) / दल सहित (with the army) / सुबेला (Suvela) / कारुनीक (compassionate) / दिनकर कुल (solar line) / केतू (banner) / दूत (messenger) / पठायउ (sent) / तव (your) / हित (welfare) / हेतू (for the sake of)
ramacharitamanas::4712.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4712.essence: True power still leaves room for one last warning.
ramacharitamanas::4712.simple_meaning: Ram, who effortlessly bridged the ocean and came with his army to Suvela, even sent a messenger for Ravana's welfare.
ramacharitamanas::4712.simple_insight: Power does not always rush to punish; sometimes it first offers a final chance to turn back.
ramacharitamanas::4712.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the scene shifts from battlefield force to one last act of mercy. Ram has already crossed the ocean and positioned his army, yet before the final destruction he sends a messenger to Ravana. The verse highlights strength restrained by compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4712.modern_relevance: You finally have the leverage to crush someone who has been blocking you for months. Instead, you send one last message that says, 'Step back now and this can still end well.'
ramacharitamanas::4712.insight: It teaches you to let strength be guided by mercy before it becomes force.

ramacharitamanas::4713.verse_sanskrit: सभा माझ जेहिं तव बल मथा। करि बरूथ महुँ मृगपति जथा॥ अंगद हनुमत अनुचर जाके। रन बाँकुरे बीर अति बाँके ॥
ramacharitamanas::4713.verse_hindi: जिसने बीच सभा में आकर आपके बल को उसी प्रकार मथ डाला जैसे हाथियों के झुंड में आकर सिंह (उसे छिन्न-भिन्न कर डालता है) रण में बाँके अत्यंत विकट वीर अंगद और हनुमान् जिनके सेवक हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4713.english_translation: He who, in the middle of the assembly, churned up your strength like a lion in an elephant herd; Angad and Hanuman are his attendants, and his warriors are fierce and unbending.
ramacharitamanas::4713.translation_literal: सभा (assembly) / माझ (in the middle) / जेहिं (who) / तव (your) / बल (strength) / मथा (churned up, shook) / करि (having done) / बरूथ महुँ (in the herd) / मृगपति (lion, lord of beasts) / जथा (like) / अंगद (Angad) / हनुमत (Hanuman) / अनुचर (attendants, followers) / जाके (whose) / रन (battle) / बाँकुरे (fierce, bent on valor) / बीर (heroes) / अति (very) / बाँके (unyielding, bold)
ramacharitamanas::4713.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4713.essence: Real strength makes pride collapse in public.
ramacharitamanas::4713.simple_meaning: Ravana is boasting that Ram openly crushed his pride in the court, and that powerful warriors like Angad and Hanuman serve Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4713.simple_insight: Pride sounds grand until it meets someone stronger and steadier.
ramacharitamanas::4713.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking before his court, trying to steady his shaken pride after seeing Ram's power. He admits Ram has already humbled him in public and names Angad and Hanuman as proof that Ram is surrounded by unmatched warriors.
ramacharitamanas::4713.modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready to dominate, and one calm person changes the whole atmosphere. Their quiet strength exposes how thin your confidence really was.
ramacharitamanas::4713.insight: It shifts the mind from boasting about power to recognizing power that cannot be faked.

ramacharitamanas::4714.verse_sanskrit: तेहि कहँ पिय पुनि पुनि नर कहहू। मुधा मान ममता मद बहहू॥ अहह कंत कृत राम बिरोधा। काल बिबस मन उपज न बोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4714.verse_hindi: हे पति! उन्हें आप बार-बार मनुष्य कहते हैं। आप व्यर्थ ही मान, ममता और मद का बोझ ढो रहे हैं! हा प्रियतम! आपने श्री रामजी से विरोध कर लिया और काल के विशेष वश होने से आपके मन में अब भी ज्ञान नहीं उत्पन्न होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4714.english_translation: O husband, you keep calling him only a human being. You carry the burden of pride, possessiveness, and intoxication in vain. Ah, beloved, you have opposed Ram, and under the grip of time, understanding no longer arises in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::4714.translation_literal: तेहि (that one) / कहँ (to) / पिय (beloved) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / नर (human being) / कहहू (you say) / मुधा (in vain) / मान (pride) / ममता (possessiveness) / मद (intoxication) / बहहू (you carry) / अहह (alas) / कंत (husband) / कृत (done) / राम (Ram) / बिरोधा (opposition) / काल (time) / बिबस (under the control of) / मन (mind) / उपज (arises) / न (not) / बोधा (understanding)
ramacharitamanas::4714.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4714.essence: Pride makes you blind before defeat arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4714.simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana that he keeps dismissing Ram as merely human while carrying pride and attachment. By opposing Ram, he has lost clear understanding.
ramacharitamanas::4714.simple_insight: Pride can feel powerful while quietly making you unable to see what is right in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4714.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Mandodari pleads with Ravana after his war with Ram has already begun to collapse his world. She warns him that his contempt, ego, and attachment are blinding him, and that time itself has already begun to strip away his judgment.
ramacharitamanas::4714.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a heated argument and keep repeating your point just to win. Later, you realise the need to be right was the very thing that made you unable to listen.
ramacharitamanas::4714.insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to noticing how ego destroys discernment.

ramacharitamanas::4715.verse_sanskrit: काल दंड गहि काहु न मारा। हरइ धर्म बल बुद्धि बिचारा॥ निकट काल जेहि आवत साईं। तेहि भ्रम होइ तुम्हारिहि नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4715.verse_hindi: काल दण्ड (लाठी) लेकर किसी को नहीं मारता। वह धर्म, बल, बुद्धि और विचार को हर लेता है। हे स्वामी! जिसका काल (मरण समय) निकट आ जाता है, उसे आप ही की तरह भ्रम हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4715.english_translation: Death does not strike with a staff. It takes away righteousness, strength, discernment, and judgment. O master, when death draws near, confusion arises in you as well.
ramacharitamanas::4715.translation_literal: काल (death/time) / दंड (staff) / गहि (taking) / काहु (someone) / न (not) / मारा (struck) / हरइ (takes away) / धर्म (righteous conduct) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (discernment) / बिचारा (judgment) / निकट (near) / काल (death/time) / जेहि (whom) / आवत (approaches) / साईं (master) / तेहि (that one) / भ्रम (confusion) / होइ (happens) / तुम्हारिहि (to you) / नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::4715.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4715.essence: Death begins by stealing your clarity, not your body.
ramacharitamanas::4715.simple_meaning: Death is not a physical blow. It first weakens your judgment, strength, and sense of right, leaving you confused when the end approaches.
ramacharitamanas::4715.simple_insight: Fear can cloud your best judgment long before any crisis arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4715.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's allies are already unraveling. One voice warns that death does not merely kill bodies; it strips away discernment, strength, and moral clarity first. The line explains why pride can collapse from within before the final blow.
ramacharitamanas::4715.modern_relevance: You know that moment when panic hits and your sharpest thinking disappears? This verse names that collapse: pressure can take away judgment before it takes anything else.
ramacharitamanas::4715.insight: It shifts attention from external danger to the inner erosion that makes bad choices inevitable.

ramacharitamanas::4716.verse_sanskrit: दुइ सुत मरे दहेउ पुर अजहुँ पूर पिय देहु। कृपासिंधु रघुनाथ भजि नाथ बिमल जसु लेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4716.verse_hindi: आपके दो पुत्र मारे गए और नगर जल गया। (जो हुआ सो हुआ) हे प्रियतम! अब भी (इस भूल की) पूर्ति (समाप्ति) कर दीजिए (श्री रामजी से वैर त्याग दीजिए) और हे नाथ! कृपा के समुद्र श्री रघुनाथजी को भजकर निर्मल यश लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4716.english_translation: Your two sons are dead and the city has burned. Even now, end this feud, and worship Raghunath, the ocean of grace, to earn spotless fame.
ramacharitamanas::4716.translation_literal: दुइ (two) / सुत (sons) / मरे (died) / दहेउ (was burned) / पुर (city) / अजहुँ (even now) / पूर (end, complete) / पिय (beloved) / देहु (give) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / भजि (worshipping) / नाथ (lord) / बिमल (pure) / जसु (fame) / लेहु (take, obtain)
ramacharitamanas::4716.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4716.essence: Even after ruin, you can still choose Ram and begin again.
ramacharitamanas::4716.simple_meaning: Even after terrible loss, the speaker urges reconciliation and devotion to Ram instead of continuing revenge.
ramacharitamanas::4716.simple_insight: Loss does not have to harden you; it can become the moment you soften.
ramacharitamanas::4716.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana has lost two sons and his city has been burned, a final appeal is made to him. The speaker urges him to end hostility, turn to Ram, and gain pure fame instead of deeper ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4716.modern_relevance: You just got the message that the deal collapsed, the money is gone, and the relationship is shattered. Even then, you can stop feeding the feud and choose the path that restores you.
ramacharitamanas::4716.insight: It shifts you from retaliation to reconciliation, showing that humility can begin after damage is done.

ramacharitamanas::4717.verse_sanskrit: नारि बचन सुनि बिसिख समाना। सभाँ गयउ उठि होत बिहाना॥ बैठ जाइ सिंघासन फूली। अति अभिमान त्रास सब भूली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4717.verse_hindi: स्त्री के बाण के समान वचन सुनकर वह सबेरा होते ही उठकर सभा में चला गया और सारा भय भुलाकर अत्यंत अभिमान में फूलकर सिंहासन पर जा बैठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4717.english_translation: Hearing the woman's words, he rose at dawn and went to the assembly. Sitting on the throne, he forgot all fear and swelled with great pride.
ramacharitamanas::4717.translation_literal: नारि (woman's) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / बिसिख (arrow) / समाना (like) / सभाँ (to the assembly) / गयउ (went) / उठि (rising) / होत बिहाना (at dawn) / बैठ जाइ (having sat) / सिंघासन (throne) / फूली (blossomed) / अति अभिमान (great pride) / त्रास (fear) / सब (all) / भूली (forgot)
ramacharitamanas::4717.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4717.essence: Pride can make danger feel distant until it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4717.simple_meaning: He heard sharp, stinging words, went to the court at daybreak, sat on the throne, and let pride erase all fear.
ramacharitamanas::4717.simple_insight: Pride can make you forget danger for a moment, but it also blinds you completely.
ramacharitamanas::4717.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears a woman's cutting words and reacts by rushing to his assembly at dawn. He sits on his throne, swollen with pride, and forgets fear. The scene shows how ego hardens him just before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4717.modern_relevance: You get one harsh message before sunrise, then spend the morning rehearsing your own importance instead of hearing the warning. Pride can feel like strength right before it becomes blindness.
ramacharitamanas::4717.insight: It exposes how wounded ego turns warning into self-inflation instead of self-correction.

ramacharitamanas::4718.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ राम अंगदहि बोलावा। आइ चरन पंकज सिरु नावा॥ अति आदर समीप बैठारी। बोले बिहँसि कृपाल खरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4718.verse_hindi: यहाँ (सुबेल पर्वत पर) श्री रामजी ने अंगद को बुलाया। उन्होंने आकर चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया। बड़े आदर से उन्हें पास बैठाकर खर के शत्रु कृपालु श्री रामजी हँसकर बोले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4718.english_translation: Here, on Suvela Mountain, Ram called Angad. Angad came and bowed his head at Ram's lotus feet. Ram seated him nearby with great respect and, smiling, the compassionate destroyer of evil spoke.
ramacharitamanas::4718.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / राम (Ram) / अंगदहि (Angad) / बोलावा (called) / आइ (coming) / चरन पंकज (lotus feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / अति आदर (great respect) / समीप (near) / बैठारी (seated) / बोले (spoke) / बिहँसि (smiling) / कृपाल (compassionate) / खरारी (destroyer of evil)
ramacharitamanas::4718.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4718.essence: Respect turns an enemy meeting into a human one.
ramacharitamanas::4718.simple_meaning: Ram calls Angad close, honors him, and speaks to him kindly.
ramacharitamanas::4718.simple_insight: Respect can open the way for honest words.
ramacharitamanas::4718.detailed_meaning: On Suvela Mountain during the war, Ram summons Angad, Bali's son, and welcomes him with honor instead of hostility. Angad bows low, and Ram's gentle smile sets up the serious exchange that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4718.modern_relevance: A tense meeting gets easier the moment someone offers respect first — the shoulders drop, the guard softens, and real conversation becomes possible.
ramacharitamanas::4718.insight: It shows that dignity can disarm conflict before a single argument begins.

ramacharitamanas::4719.verse_sanskrit: बालितनय कौतुक अति मोही। तात सत्य कहुँ पूछउँ तोही॥ रावनु जातुधान कुल टीका। भुज बल अतुल जासु जग लीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4719.verse_hindi: हे बालि के पुत्र! मुझे बड़ा कौतूहल है। हे तात! इसी से मैं तुमसे पूछता हूँ, सत्य कहना। जो रावण राक्षसों के कुल का तिलक है और जिसके अतुलनीय बाहुबल की जगत् भर में धाक है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4719.english_translation: O son of Bali, I am deeply curious. Tell me the truth, father, I ask you this: Ravana is the ornament of the race of the demons, and his unmatched arm-strength is feared throughout the world.
ramacharitamanas::4719.translation_literal: बालितनय (son of Bali) / कौतुक (curious) / अति (very) / मोही (am amazed) / तात (father) / सत्य (truth) / कहुँ (say) / पूछउँ (I ask) / तोही (you) / रावनु (Ravana) / जातुधान-कुल (demon race) / टीका (ornament/mark) / भुज-बल (arm-strength) / अतुल (matchless) / जासु (whose) / जग (world) / लीका (fame/fear)
ramacharitamanas::4719.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4719.essence: Great reputation still has to face a truthful question.
ramacharitamanas::4719.simple_meaning: Ram asks Angad to tell the truth about Ravana’s great strength and fame. The verse sets up a challenge: how was such a mighty ruler humbled?
ramacharitamanas::4719.simple_insight: Even the strongest pride has to answer to truth.
ramacharitamanas::4719.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Lanka, Ram speaks kindly to Angad, the son of Bali. After Ravana’s arrogance and Angad’s bold entrance, Ram asks a pointed question about Ravana’s famed power, preparing the ground for Angad’s answer.
ramacharitamanas::4719.modern_relevance: In a tense meeting, someone names the most intimidating person in the room and asks for the real story. The question is calm, but it cuts through fear and reputation.
ramacharitamanas::4719.insight: It shifts attention from public image to the facts underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::4720.verse_sanskrit: तासु मुकुट तुम्ह चारि चलाए। कहहु तात कवनी बिधि पाए॥ सुनु सर्बग्य प्रनत सुखकारी। मुकुट न होहिं भूप न गुन चारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4720.verse_hindi: उसके चार मुकुट तुमने फेंके। हे तात! बताओ, तुमने उनको किस प्रकार से पाया! (अंगद ने कहा-) हे सर्वज्ञ! हे शरणागत को सुख देने वाले! सुनिए। वे मुकुट नहीं हैं। वे तो राजा के चार गुण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4720.english_translation: You threw down his four crowns. Tell me, dear one, how did you get them? Listen, all-knowing one who brings comfort to the surrendered: those are not crowns at all. They are the four qualities of a king.
ramacharitamanas::4720.translation_literal: तासु (his) / मुकुट (crowns) / तुम्ह (you) / चारि (four) / चलाए (threw down) / कहहु (tell) / तात (dear one) / कवनी बिधि (by what method) / पाए (obtained) / सुनु (listen) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing one) / प्रनत (to the surrendered) / सुखकारी (giver of comfort) / मुकुट (crowns) / न होहिं (are not) / भूप (king) / न (not) / गुन (qualities) / चारी (four)
ramacharitamanas::4720.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4720.essence: Power is real only when it rests on four inner qualities.
ramacharitamanas::4720.simple_meaning: Angad explains that the four items Ram threw down are not real crowns. They represent the four qualities a king should have.
ramacharitamanas::4720.simple_insight: True status is not in ornaments, but in the qualities that hold a life together.
ramacharitamanas::4720.detailed_meaning: On Suvela mountain, Ram has invited Angad and asked about the four crowns he knocked down. Angad answers respectfully that they were never literal crowns. He turns the moment into a lesson about the four royal qualities a ruler must embody.
ramacharitamanas::4720.modern_relevance: A team celebrates the flashy title on a business card, but the room falls silent when the person cannot lead, protect, or decide. Angad would say the real crown is character.
ramacharitamanas::4720.insight: It shifts attention from outward symbols of authority to the inner qualities that make authority real.

ramacharitamanas::4721.verse_sanskrit: साम दान अरु दंड बिभेदा। नृप उर बसहिं नाथ कह बेदा॥ नीति धर्म के चरन सुहाए। अस जियँ जानि पहिं आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4721.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! वेद कहते हैं कि साम, दान, दण्ड और भेद- ये चारों राजा के हृदय में बसते हैं। ये नीति-धर्म के चार सुंदर चरण हैं, (किन्तु रावण में धर्म का अभाव है) ऐसा जी में जानकर ये नाथ के पास आ गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4721.english_translation: O Lord, the Vedas say that conciliation, gifts, punishment, and division dwell in a king's heart. These are the four beautiful limbs of righteous policy. Knowing this in their hearts, they have come to you.
ramacharitamanas::4721.translation_literal: साम (conciliation) / दान (gift) / अरु (and) / दंड (punishment) / बिभेदा (division) / नृप (king) / उर (heart) / बसहिं (dwell) / नाथ (Lord) / कह (said) / बेदा (the Vedas) / नीति (policy) / धर्म (righteous conduct) / के (of) / चरन (feet/limbs) / सुहाए (beautiful) / अस (thus) / जियँ (in heart) / जानि (knowing) / पहिं (to) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::4721.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4721.essence: Power becomes wise only when it knows how to respond.
ramacharitamanas::4721.simple_meaning: A king should know how to use persuasion, generosity, firmness, and strategy. Angad says these royal qualities are what brought him here.
ramacharitamanas::4721.simple_insight: Real strength includes restraint, timing, and the right response—not just force.
ramacharitamanas::4721.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad stands before Ravana after showing his strength. He now explains why he came to Ram instead of staying with a ruler who has lost his moral compass. The verse frames kingship as disciplined action, not raw power.
ramacharitamanas::4721.modern_relevance: You are leading a tense family meeting, and everyone wants a different answer. Before you speak, you need to know whether this moment calls for softness, generosity, firmness, or a strategic pause.
ramacharitamanas::4721.insight: It teaches you to choose the right form of response instead of defaulting to force.

ramacharitamanas::4722.verse_sanskrit: धर्महीन प्रभु पद बिमुख काल बिबस दससीस। तेहि परिहरि गुन आए सुनहु कोसलाधीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4722.verse_hindi: दशशीश रावण धर्महीन, प्रभु के पद से विमुख और काल के वश में है, इसलिए हे कोसलराज! सुनिए, वे गुण रावण को छोड़कर आपके पास आ गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4722.english_translation: Ravana is without dharma, turned away from the feet of the Lord, and helpless in the grip of time. Leaving him aside, those virtues have come to you, O Lord of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::4722.translation_literal: धर्महीन (without dharma) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / बिमुख (turned away) / काल (time) / बिबस (helpless, under control) / दससीस (ten-headed one, Ravana) / तेहि (that one) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / गुन (virtues) / आए (came) / सुनहु (listen) / कोसलाधीस (Lord of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::4722.speaker: Angad
ramacharitamanas::4722.essence: Power without dharma empties itself; virtue moves toward what is aligned.
ramacharitamanas::4722.simple_meaning: Ravana has abandoned dharma and turned away from Ram, so his good qualities no longer belong to him. They now rest with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4722.simple_insight: Real strength stays with the one who stays aligned with what is right.
ramacharitamanas::4722.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad is speaking boldly before Ravana's court. He tells Ravana that his power has become empty because he has turned away from Ram and from dharma. The qualities Ravana once claimed now belong to Ram instead.
ramacharitamanas::4722.modern_relevance: A talented manager keeps winning praise while breaking trust with everyone around them. Slowly, the team stops seeing strength and starts seeing emptiness. Character, not image, decides where respect lives.
ramacharitamanas::4722.insight: It shifts attention from outer power to the alignment that makes power meaningful.

ramacharitamanas::4723.verse_sanskrit: परम चतुरता श्रवन सुनि बिहँसे रामु उदार। समाचार पुनि सब कहे गढ़ के बालिकुमार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4723.verse_hindi: अंगद की परम चतुरता (पूर्ण उक्ति) कानों से सुनकर उदार श्री रामचंद्रजी हँसने लगे। फिर बालि पुत्र ने किले के (लंका के) सब समाचार कहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4723.english_translation: Hearing Angad's wonderfully clever words, generous Ram laughed. Then Bali's son told him all the news of the fortress.
ramacharitamanas::4723.translation_literal: परम (supreme) / चतुरता (cleverness) / श्रवन (with the ears) / सुनि (having heard) / बिहँसे (laughed) / रामु (Ram) / उदार (generous) / समाचार (news) / पुनि (then again) / सब (all) / कहे (told) / गढ़ (fortress) / के (of) / बालिकुमार (Bali's son)
ramacharitamanas::4723.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4723.essence: Grace lets you hear hard news without losing composure.
ramacharitamanas::4723.simple_meaning: Ram smiles at Angad's clever words, and Angad then reports everything happening inside Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::4723.simple_insight: A calm mind can receive even tense news without losing itself.
ramacharitamanas::4723.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad has entered as a bold messenger. His sharp words have reached Ram, who responds with a smile rather than tension. Then Angad continues, describing everything he has seen inside the fortress.
ramacharitamanas::4723.modern_relevance: You get a message that could spark panic, but you read it twice and stay steady. That pause lets you see clearly instead of reacting on impulse.
ramacharitamanas::4723.insight: It shows how steadiness and wit can hold pressure without collapse.

ramacharitamanas::4724.verse_sanskrit: रिपु के समाचार जब पाए। राम सचिव सब निकट बोलाए॥ लंका बाँके चारि दुआरा। केहि बिधि लागिअ करहु बिचारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4724.verse_hindi: जब शत्रु के समाचार प्राप्त हो गए, तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने सब मंत्रियों को पास बुलाया (और कहा-) लंका के चार बड़े विकट दरवाजे हैं। उन पर किस तरह आक्रमण किया जाए, इस पर विचार करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4724.english_translation: When news of the enemy arrived, Ram called all his ministers close and said, “Lanka has four strong gates. Think carefully about how to attack them.”
ramacharitamanas::4724.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / के (of) / समाचार (news) / जब (when) / पाए (were received) / राम (Ram) / सचिव (ministers) / सब (all) / निकट (near) / बोलाए (called) / लंका (Lanka) / बाँके (strong, tricky) / चारि (four) / दुआरा (gates) / केहि बिधि (by what method) / लागिअ (should be applied/attacked) / करहु (do) / बिचारा (consideration)
ramacharitamanas::4724.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4724.essence: Before the assault, wisdom asks how to enter well.
ramacharitamanas::4724.simple_meaning: Ram hears the enemy’s situation, gathers his ministers, and asks them to think through the best way to attack Lanka’s four fortified gates.
ramacharitamanas::4724.simple_insight: Good action starts with clear-eyed planning, not rushed force.
ramacharitamanas::4724.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after hearing fresh reports about the enemy, Ram immediately calls his ministers together. The next move is not impulsive attack but careful strategy: four fortified gates stand before the army, and the plan must be chosen wisely.
ramacharitamanas::4724.modern_relevance: You get the update, gather the team, and stare at the problem before charging in. Real leadership asks for thought first, then force.
ramacharitamanas::4724.insight: It shifts the mind from reaction to strategic deliberation before action.

ramacharitamanas::4725.verse_sanskrit: तब कपीस रिच्छेस बिभीषन। सुमरि हृदयँ दिनकर कुल भूषन॥ करि बिचार तिन्ह मंत्र दृढ़ावा। चारि अनी कपि कटकु बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4725.verse_hindi: तब वानरराज सुग्रीव, ऋक्षपति जाम्बवान् और विभीषण ने हृदय में सूर्य कुल के भूषण श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण किया और विचार करके उन्होंने कर्तव्य निश्चित किया। वानरों की सेना के चार दल बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4725.english_translation: Then Sugriva, Jambavan, and Vibhishana remembered in their hearts the ornament of the solar line, Lord Raghunath. After considering, they fixed their plan and formed the monkey army into four divisions.
ramacharitamanas::4725.translation_literal: तब (then) / कपीस (lord of monkeys, Sugriva) / रिच्छेस (lord of bears, Jambavan) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / सुमरि (remembering) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / दिनकर कुल भूषन (ornament of the solar line) / करि (having done) / बिचार (consideration) / तिन्ह (they) / मंत्र (plan/counsel) / दृढ़ावा (made firm) / चारि (four) / अनी (divisions) / कपि (monkey) / कटकु (army) / बनावा (made)
ramacharitamanas::4725.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4725.essence: Remembering Ram turns confusion into disciplined strategy.
ramacharitamanas::4725.simple_meaning: Sugriva, Jambavan, and Vibhishana remember Ram, decide on a plan, and divide the monkey army into four parts.
ramacharitamanas::4725.simple_insight: Good action starts with remembering what you serve, not just what you fear.
ramacharitamanas::4725.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram consults his allies about the fort’s four gates, Sugriva, Jambavan, and Vibhishana turn inward to remember Ram and then organize the army. Their devotion becomes strategy, and their strategy becomes action.
ramacharitamanas::4725.modern_relevance: You’re in a crisis call, everyone talking at once, and someone quietly asks, “What are we actually trying to serve here?” That pause can turn panic into a plan.
ramacharitamanas::4725.insight: It shifts leadership from scattered reaction to remembered purpose and organized action.

ramacharitamanas::4726.verse_sanskrit: जथाजोग सेनापति कीन्हे। जूथप सकल बोलि तब लीन्हे॥ प्रभु प्रताप कहि सब समुझाए। सुनि कपि सिंघनाद करि धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4726.verse_hindi: और उनके लिए यथायोग्य (जैसे चाहिए वैसे) सेनापति नियुक्त किए। फिर सब यूथपतियों को बुला लिया और प्रभु का प्रताप कहकर सबको समझाया, जिसे सुनकर वानर, सिंह के समान गर्जना करके दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4726.english_translation: And he appointed the commanders as suited to each. Then he called all the troop leaders and explained the Lord's power; hearing this, the monkeys roared like lions and rushed forward.
ramacharitamanas::4726.translation_literal: जथाजोग (as appropriate) / सेनापति (commanders) / कीन्हे (made) / जूथप (troop leaders) / सकल (all) / बोलि (calling) / तब (then) / लीन्हे (took) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रताप (power, glory) / कहि (saying) / सब (all) / समुझाए (explained) / सुनि (hearing) / कपि (monkeys) / सिंघनाद (lion-roar) / करि (making) / धाए (rushed)
ramacharitamanas::4726.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4726.essence: Right leadership turns raw strength into fearless momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4726.simple_meaning: Ram organizes the monkey army by assigning leaders and reminding everyone of his power. The troops respond with fearless energy and rush into action.
ramacharitamanas::4726.simple_insight: Clear leadership can turn fear into courage in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4726.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the war council, Ram assigns commanders to the monkey forces and strengthens everyone with a reminder of his power. The army answers with lion-like roars and surges forward, ready for battle.
ramacharitamanas::4726.modern_relevance: Right before a tense team presentation, someone finally names who is handling what and why it matters. The room changes instantly — confusion drops, energy rises, and everyone moves together.
ramacharitamanas::4726.insight: It shows how direction and shared purpose convert scattered strength into coordinated action.

ramacharitamanas::4727.verse_sanskrit: हरषित राम चरन सिर नावहिं। गहि गिरि सिखर बीर सब धावहिं॥ गर्जहिं तर्जहिं भालु कपीसा। जय रघुबीर कोसलाधीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4727.verse_hindi: वे हर्षित होकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में सिर नवाते हैं और पर्वतों के शिखर ले-लेकर सब वीर दौड़ते हैं। 'कोसलराज श्री रघुवीरजी की जय हो' पुकारते हुए भालू और वानर गरजते और ललकारते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4727.english_translation: Joyfully, they bow their heads to Ram's feet. Then every warrior rushes forward, lifting mountain peaks. Bears and monkeys roar and shout, 'Victory to Raghubir, lord of Kosala!'
ramacharitamanas::4727.translation_literal: हरषित (joyful) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / सिर (head) / नावहिं (bow) / गहि (grasping) / गिरि (mountain) / सिखर (peak) / बीर (warriors) / सब (all) / धावहिं (run) / गर्जहिं (roar) / तर्जहिं (shout in challenge) / भालु (bears) / कपीसा (monkey chiefs) / जय (victory) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / कोसलाधीसा (lord of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::4727.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4727.essence: Devotion turns fear into fearless motion.
ramacharitamanas::4727.simple_meaning: The allied warriors bow to Ram, then rush into battle with mountain peaks in hand, roaring his victory.
ramacharitamanas::4727.simple_insight: When devotion is steady, courage becomes effortless.
ramacharitamanas::4727.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Sugriva, Jambavan, Vibhishana, bears, and monkeys are no longer hesitant. They bow to Ram, lift mountain peaks, and surge forward together. This is the moment their fear turns into fearless charge.
ramacharitamanas::4727.modern_relevance: A team takes one deep breath before the launch, then moves as one. The nervousness is still there, but shared purpose turns it into momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4727.insight: It turns hesitation into collective action by rooting courage in reverence.

ramacharitamanas::4728.verse_sanskrit: जानत परम दुर्ग अति लंका। प्रभु प्रताप कपि चले असंका॥ घटाटोप करि चहुँ दिसि घेरी॥ मुखहिं निसार बजावहिं भेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4728.verse_hindi: लंका को अत्यंत श्रेष्ठ (अजेय) किला जानते हुए भी वानर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रताप से निडर होकर चले। चारों ओर से घिरी हुई बादलों की घटा की तरह लंका को चारों दिशाओं से घेरकर वे मुँह से डंके और भेरी बजाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4728.english_translation: Knowing Lanka to be an exceedingly strong fortress, the monkeys marched on fearlessly by Ram's power. They surrounded it on all sides like a mass of storm clouds, blowing trumpets and drums with their mouths.
ramacharitamanas::4728.translation_literal: जानत (knowing) / परम (supreme) / दुर्ग (fortress) / अति (very) / लंका (Lanka) / प्रभु (Lord's) / प्रताप (power, glory) / कपि (monkeys) / चले (went, marched) / असंका (without fear) / घटाटोप (dense cloud-cover) / करि (making) / चहुँ दिसि (in four directions) / घेरी (surrounded) / मुखहिं (with mouths) / निसार (drums) / बजावहिं (they blew) / भेरी (war-drums)
ramacharitamanas::4728.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4728.essence: Ram's power turns a fortress into something you can face.
ramacharitamanas::4728.simple_meaning: Even though Lanka is a nearly impregnable fortress, the monkeys advance without fear because of Ram's power. They surround the city and sound their war-drums.
ramacharitamanas::4728.simple_insight: Courage grows when fear is carried by something larger than yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4728.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's army has crossed from strategy into open challenge. They know the city is a fortress, yet Ram's power has steadied them. With confidence, they spread around it and begin the battle cry.
ramacharitamanas::4728.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to back down. Your hands may shake, but something deeper keeps you steady enough to speak.
ramacharitamanas::4728.insight: It shifts fear from a command into background noise.

ramacharitamanas::4729.verse_sanskrit: जयति राम जय लछिमन जय कपीस सुग्रीव। गर्जहिं सिंहनाद कपि भालु महा बल सींव ॥
ramacharitamanas::4729.verse_hindi: महान् बल की सीमा वे वानर-भालू सिंह के समान ऊँचे स्वर से 'श्री रामजी की जय', 'लक्ष्मणजी की जय', 'वानरराज सुग्रीव की जय'- ऐसी गर्जना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4729.english_translation: Victory to Ram, victory to Lakshman, victory to the lord of monkeys, Sugriva. The monkeys and bears roared like lions, their great strength at its limit.
ramacharitamanas::4729.translation_literal: जयति (victory) / राम (Ram) / जय (victory) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / जय (victory) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / गर्जहिं (they roar) / सिंहनाद (lion-roar) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / महा (great) / बल (strength) / सींव (limit)
ramacharitamanas::4729.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4729.essence: Shared courage turns into a roar.
ramacharitamanas::4729.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear warriors shout victory for Ram, Lakshman, and Sugriva as they roar with lion-like force.
ramacharitamanas::4729.simple_insight: Courage spreads fast when a whole team fights as one.
ramacharitamanas::4729.detailed_meaning: The army has reached Lanka. Ram's allies are no longer just approaching; they are announcing themselves. The monkeys and bears roar the names of their leaders, and the noise itself becomes a weapon before the battle fully begins.
ramacharitamanas::4729.modern_relevance: A team steps onto the field before the final match, shouting each other's names to steady their nerves. The sound is not noise alone — it is shared courage made audible.
ramacharitamanas::4729.insight: It shows how collective confidence can become action before the first strike lands.

ramacharitamanas::4730.verse_sanskrit: लंकाँ भयउ कोलाहल भारी। सुना दसानन अति अहँकारी॥ देखहु बनरन्ह केरि ढिठाई। बिहँसि निसाचर सेन बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4730.verse_hindi: लंका में बड़ा भारी कोलाहल (कोहराम) मच गया। अत्यंत अहंकारी रावण ने उसे सुनकर कहा- वानरों की ढिठाई तो देखो! यह कहते हुए हँसकर उसने राक्षसों की सेना बुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4730.english_translation: A great uproar rose in Lanka. Hearing it, the deeply arrogant Ravana said, “Look at the audacity of the monkeys!” Laughing, he summoned the demon army.
ramacharitamanas::4730.translation_literal: लंकाँ (in Lanka) / भयउ (became) / कोलाहल (uproar) / भारी (great) / सुना (hearing) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / अति (very) / अहँकारी (arrogant) / देखहु (look) / बनरन्ह (of the monkeys) / केरि (of) / ढिठाई (audacity) / बिहँसि (laughing) / निसाचर (demon) / सेना (army) / बोलाई (summoned)
ramacharitamanas::4730.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4730.essence: Arrogance laughs first and understands last.
ramacharitamanas::4730.simple_meaning: Lanka erupts in noise, and Ravana mocks the monkeys before calling his army to fight.
ramacharitamanas::4730.simple_insight: Pride makes real danger look like a joke until it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4730.detailed_meaning: The monkeys have reached Lanka, and their advance shakes the city. Ravana hears the uproar, but instead of caution he answers with contempt. He laughs at their boldness and calls his forces together.
ramacharitamanas::4730.modern_relevance: You hear the team has already found the flaw in your plan. Instead of pausing, you laugh it off and double down — exactly the kind of mistake arrogance makes.
ramacharitamanas::4730.insight: It shows how ego turns warning into ridicule and prepares its own defeat.

ramacharitamanas::4731.verse_sanskrit: आए कीस काल के प्रेरे। छुधावंत सब निसिचर मेरे॥ बअस कहि अट्टहास सठ कीन्हा। गृह बैठें अहार बिधि दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4731.verse_hindi: बंदर काल की प्रेरणा से चले आए हैं। मेरे राक्षस सभी भूखे हैं। विधाता ने इन्हें घर बैठे भोजन भेज दिया। ऐसा कहकर उस मूर्ख ने अट्टहास किया (वह बड़े जोर से ठहाका मारकर हँसा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4731.english_translation: The monkeys have come, driven by Time. All my demons are starving. Fate has sent them food right to my house." Saying this, the fool laughed loudly.
ramacharitamanas::4731.translation_literal: आए (have come) / कीस (monkeys) / काल (Time) / के (by) / प्रेरे (driven) / छुधावंत (hungry) / सब (all) / निसिचर (demons) / मेरे (my) / बअस (fate) / कहि (saying) / अट्टहास (loud laughter) / सठ (fool) / कीन्हा (did) / गृह (home) / बैठें (sitting) / अहार (food) / बिधि (by fate) / दीन्हा (given)
ramacharitamanas::4731.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4731.essence: Arrogance mistakes its own downfall for a feast.
ramacharitamanas::4731.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks the arriving monkeys and thinks they have come as easy food for his hungry warriors.
ramacharitamanas::4731.simple_insight: Pride makes danger look like a gift.
ramacharitamanas::4731.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears the uproar and dismisses the monkey army with contempt. He assumes the invaders are helpless prey and laughs at what is actually the beginning of his ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4731.modern_relevance: You laugh off the warning signs because you feel untouchable. That same smugness can turn a real threat into your blind spot.
ramacharitamanas::4731.insight: It shows how arrogance turns clear danger into comic relief.

ramacharitamanas::4732.verse_sanskrit: सुभट सकल चारिहुँ दिसि जाहू। धरि धरि भालु कीस सब खाहू॥ उमा रावनहि अस अभिमाना। जिमि टिट्टिभ खग सूत उताना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4732.verse_hindi: (और बोला-) हे वीरों! सब लोग चारों दिशाओं में जाओ और रीछ-वानर सबको पकड़-पकड़कर खाओ। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! रावण को ऐसा अभिमान था जैसा टिटिहिरी पक्षी पैर ऊपर की ओर करके सोता है (मानो आकाश को थाम लेगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4732.english_translation: “O warriors, go in all four directions. Catch and eat all the bears and monkeys. O Uma, Ravana’s pride was like a bird that sleeps with its feet raised upward, as if it could hold up the sky.”
ramacharitamanas::4732.translation_literal: सुभट (warriors) / सकल (all) / चारिहुँ दिसि (in all four directions) / जाहू (go) / धरि धरि (seizing again and again) / भालु (bears) / कीस (monkeys) / सब (all) / खाहू (eat) / उमा (O Uma) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / अस (such) / अभिमाना (pride) / जिमि (like) / टिट्टिभ (the titihiri bird) / खग (bird) / सूत (sleeps) / उताना (with feet raised upward)
ramacharitamanas::4732.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4732.essence: Pride can make you feel strongest just as collapse begins.
ramacharitamanas::4732.simple_meaning: Ravana orders his warriors to attack the monkeys and bears from every side. Shiva then remarks to Uma that Ravana’s pride was absurdly inflated, like a bird sleeping with its feet raised as if it could support the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4732.simple_insight: Pride makes people feel invincible right before they fall.
ramacharitamanas::4732.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still sneering even as danger closes in. He orders his warriors to spread out and devour the monkey and bear army. Shiva interrupts the scene to show Uma the real problem: Ravana’s pride has made him laughably blind.
ramacharitamanas::4732.modern_relevance: A manager mocks the team’s warning, then tells everyone to charge ahead anyway. The danger is not just bad strategy — it is the arrogance that cannot imagine being wrong.
ramacharitamanas::4732.insight: It turns victory-talk into a warning about ego’s blindness.

ramacharitamanas::4733.verse_sanskrit: चले निसाचर आयसु मागी। गहि कर भिंडिपाल बर साँगी॥ तोमर मुद्गर परसु प्रचंडा। सूल कृपान परिघ गिरिखंडा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4733.verse_hindi: आज्ञा माँगकर और हाथों में उत्तम भिंदिपाल, साँगी (बरछी), तोमर, मुद्गर, प्रचण्ड फरसे, शूल, दोधारी तलवार, परिघ और पहाड़ों के टुकड़े लेकर राक्षस चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4733.english_translation: The night-rangers asked for orders and marched out, carrying fine bhindipal, spears, lances, maces, axes, tridents, swords, iron clubs, and chunks of mountain.
ramacharitamanas::4733.translation_literal: चले (went) / निसाचर (night-rangers) / आयसु (order) / मागी (having asked) / गहि (grasping) / कर (hand) / भिंडिपाल (bhindipal) / बर (fine) / साँगी (spear) / तोमर (lance) / मुद्गर (mace) / परसु (axe) / प्रचंडा (fierce) / सूल (trident) / कृपान (sword) / परिघ (iron club) / गिरिखंडा (mountain chunks)
ramacharitamanas::4733.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4733.essence: Armed rage moves forward once authority gives the signal.
ramacharitamanas::4733.simple_meaning: The demon warriors asked for orders and went out armed with many weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4733.simple_insight: Some scenes only build tension; they are not asking you to reflect yet.
ramacharitamanas::4733.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s forces are being unleashed after his boastful command. The warriors ask permission, arm themselves with brutal weapons, and surge into battle. This verse is a movement detail, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::4733.modern_relevance: A tense group chat suddenly turns into a mob, and everyone starts escalating instead of thinking. The verse captures the moment when force gets set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::4733.insight: It shows the war machine starting to move, with violence gathering momentum.

ramacharitamanas::4734.verse_sanskrit: जिमि अरुनोपल निकर निहारी। धावहिं सठ खग मांस अहारी॥ चोंच भंग दुख तिन्हहि न सूझा। तिमि धाए मनुजाद अबूझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4734.verse_hindi: जैसे मूर्ख मांसाहारी पक्षी लाल पत्थरों का समूह देखकर उस पर टूट पड़ते हैं, (पत्थरों पर लगने से) चोंच टूटने का दुःख उन्हें नहीं सूझता, वैसे ही ये बेसमझ राक्षस दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4734.english_translation: Like foolish flesh-eating birds that see a cluster of red stones and rush at it, not noticing the pain of their broken beaks, the mindless demons charged forward.
ramacharitamanas::4734.translation_literal: जिमि (like) / अरुनोपल (red stones) / निकर (cluster) / निहारी (seeing) / धावहिं (they rush) / सठ (foolish) / खग (birds) / मांस अहारी (flesh-eating) / चोंच (beak) / भंग (breakage) / दुख (pain) / तिन्हहि (to them) / न सूझा (did not occur) / तिमि (likewise) / धाए (rushed) / मनुजाद (man-eaters) / अबूझा (unthinking)
ramacharitamanas::4734.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4734.essence: Blind desire charges ahead without seeing the damage it invites.
ramacharitamanas::4734.simple_meaning: The demons rush into battle blindly, like birds flying toward red stones and ignoring the pain that will follow.
ramacharitamanas::4734.simple_insight: Blind impulse can make danger look like opportunity.
ramacharitamanas::4734.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just ordered his warriors forward. Tulsidas compares their charge to foolish birds attacking red stones, showing that pride and hunger have made them ignore the harm waiting for them.
ramacharitamanas::4734.modern_relevance: You hit send on a furious message before reading it twice. For a moment it feels powerful; a minute later, you can already see the broken beak.
ramacharitamanas::4734.insight: It warns you to see consequences before rushing into action.

ramacharitamanas::4735.verse_sanskrit: नानायुध सर चाप धर जातुधान बल बीर। कोट कँगूरन्हि चढ़ि गए कोटि कोटि रनधीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4735.verse_hindi: अनेकों प्रकार के अस्त्र-शस्त्र और धनुष-बाण धारण किए करोड़ों बलवान् और रणधीर राक्षस वीर परकोटे के कँगूरों पर चढ़ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4735.english_translation: Armed with many kinds of weapons, arrows, bows, and great strength, countless valiant demon warriors climbed onto the ramparts.
ramacharitamanas::4735.translation_literal: नानायुध (many kinds of weapons) / सर (arrows) / चाप (bows) / धर (holding) / जातुधान (demon warriors) / बल (strength) / बीर (heroes) / कोट कँगूरन्हि (on the ramparts) / चढ़ि गए (climbed up) / कोटि कोटि (countless, millions and millions) / रनधीर (battle-brave)
ramacharitamanas::4735.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4735.essence: The fortress is packed with armed warriors ready for war.
ramacharitamanas::4735.simple_meaning: Countless demon warriors, heavily armed and fearless, climbed onto the fort walls.
ramacharitamanas::4735.simple_insight: The scene builds tension before the battle erupts.
ramacharitamanas::4735.detailed_meaning: Lanka is bristling for war. Demon warriors, armed with every kind of weapon, climb the fort walls in huge numbers. The verse is part of a battle sequence, building the scene rather than offering a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4735.modern_relevance: A stadium hums before kickoff, the crowd rising to its feet. The moment is all pressure and momentum, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4735.insight: It sets the battlefield in motion without shifting into instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4736.verse_sanskrit: कोट कँगूरन्हि सोहहिं कैसे। मेरु के सृंगनि जनु घन बैसे॥ बाजहिं ढोल निसान जुझाऊ। सुनि धुनि होइ भटन्हि मन चाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4736.verse_hindi: वे परकोटे के कँगूरों पर कैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, मानो सुमेरु के शिखरों पर बादल बैठे हों। जुझाऊ ढोल और डंके आदि बज रहे हैं, (जिनकी) ध्वनि सुनकर योद्धाओं के मन में (लड़ने का) चाव होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4736.english_translation: How beautifully they shine on the battlements, like clouds resting on Mount Meru's peaks. War drums and battle horns sound, and the warriors' hearts fill with eagerness.
ramacharitamanas::4736.translation_literal: कोट कँगूरन्हि (on the battlements) / सोहहिं (they shine) / कैसे (how) / मेरु (Meru) / के (of) / सृंगनि (peaks) / जनु (as if) / घन (clouds) / बैसे (sat) / बाजहिं (sound) / ढोल (drums) / निसान (battle horns) / जुझाऊ (war-like) / सुनि (hearing) / धुनि (sound) / होइ (becomes) / भटन्हि (of warriors) / मन (mind) / चाऊ (eagerness)
ramacharitamanas::4736.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4736.essence: Battle energy rises before the first blow lands.
ramacharitamanas::4736.simple_meaning: The forts are lined with warriors and the war drums are sounding. The sight and sound stir the fighters into battle excitement.
ramacharitamanas::4736.simple_insight: Sound and spectacle can awaken courage, even before the fighting begins.
ramacharitamanas::4736.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's army crowds the fortress walls and battlements, shining like storm clouds on a mountain peak. Drums and horns echo through the city, and the warriors grow eager for battle. The verse paints the charged atmosphere before combat.
ramacharitamanas::4736.modern_relevance: A stadium roars before the match begins. The crowd, the lights, the noise — all of it can pull people into a mood before a single move is made.
ramacharitamanas::4736.insight: It shows how atmosphere shapes emotion and can push people toward action.

ramacharitamanas::4737.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं भेरि नफीरि अपारा। सुनि कादर उर जाहिं दरारा॥ देखिन्ह जाइ कपिन्ह के ठट्टा। अति बिसाल तनु भालु सुभट्टा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4737.verse_hindi: अगणित नफीरी और भेरी बज रही है, (जिन्हें) सुनकर कायरों के हृदय में दरारें पड़ जाती हैं। उन्होंने जाकर अत्यन्त विशाल शरीर वाले महान् योद्धा वानर और भालुओं के ठट्ट (समूह) देखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4737.english_translation: Countless bugles and drums were sounding. Hearing them, the hearts of the timid cracked with fear. Then they saw the troop of monkeys, huge-bodied bears, and great warriors.
ramacharitamanas::4737.translation_literal: बाजहिं (are sounding) / भेरि (drums) / नफीरि (bugles) / अपारा (countless) / सुनि (hearing) / कादर (timid) / उर (hearts) / जाहिं (go) / दरारा (cracks) / देखिन्ह (they saw) / जाइ (going) / कपिन्ह (of monkeys) / के (of) / ठट्टा (troop) / अति (very) / बिसाल (huge) / तनु (bodies) / भालु (bears) / सुभट्टा (great warriors)
ramacharitamanas::4737.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4737.essence: Noise can terrify the weak, but real strength is already there.
ramacharitamanas::4737.simple_meaning: War horns blare, timid hearts split with fear, and the enemy then sees the massive monkey and bear forces.
ramacharitamanas::4737.simple_insight: Fear changes the body before the battle even begins.
ramacharitamanas::4737.detailed_meaning: On Lanka's walls, Ravana's army is fully armed and roaring. Their drums shake the city, but the sound only exposes fear in the weak. Then the defenders finally see Hanuman's vast monkey force and the bear warriors advancing.
ramacharitamanas::4737.modern_relevance: You hear the room go silent before your presentation starts. The noise in your head is louder than the threat itself, until you see who is actually standing with you.
ramacharitamanas::4737.insight: It shifts attention from intimidation to the actual strength already present.

ramacharitamanas::4738.verse_sanskrit: धावहिं गनहिं न अवघट घाटा। पर्बत फोरि करहिं गहि बाटा॥ कटकटाहिं कोटिन्ह भट गर्जहिं। दसन ओठ काटहिं अति तर्जहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4738.verse_hindi: (देखा कि) वे रीछ-वानर दौड़ते हैं, औघट (ऊँची-नीची, विकट) घाटियों को कुछ नहीं गिनते। पकड़कर पहाड़ों को फोड़कर रास्ता बना लेते हैं। करोड़ों योद्धा कटकटाते और गर्जते हैं। दाँतों से होठ काटते और खूब डपटते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4738.english_translation: The bears and monkeys run, ignoring steep, difficult terrain. They tear open mountains and make paths by force. Millions of warriors grind their teeth, roar, bite their lips, and shout threats.
ramacharitamanas::4738.translation_literal: धावहिं (they run) / गनहिं न (do not count) / अवघट घाटा (steep difficult slopes) / पर्बत (mountains) / फोरि (breaking) / करहिं (they make) / गहि (seizing) / बाटा (paths) / कटकटाहिं (they grind) / कोटिन्ह (millions) / भट (warriors) / गर्जहिं (roar) / दसन (teeth) / ओठ (lips) / काटहिं (bite) / अति (very) / तर्जहिं (threaten)
ramacharitamanas::4738.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4738.essence: Battle here is raw force, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4738.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army rushes through impossible terrain and forces its way forward. The enemy side roars and threatens in response.
ramacharitamanas::4738.simple_insight: When purpose is shared, obstacles stop feeling impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4738.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has fully erupted. The bear and monkey forces surge across cliffs and ravines, breaking mountains to make a way. The verse lingers on the chaos and force of battle rather than any teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4738.insight: It shows the sheer momentum of battle, where terrain and fear are both overrun.

ramacharitamanas::4739.verse_sanskrit: उत रावन इत राम दोहाई। जयति जयति जय परी लराई॥ निसिचर सिखर समूह ढहावहिं। कूदि धरहिं कपि फेरि चलावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4739.verse_hindi: उधर रावण की और इधर श्री रामजी की दुहाई बोली जा रही है। 'जय' 'जय' 'जय' की ध्वनि होते ही लड़ाई छिड़ गई। राक्षस पहाड़ों के ढेर के ढेर शिखरों को फेंकते हैं। वानर कूदकर उन्हें पकड़ लेते हैं और वापस उन्हीं की ओर चलाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4739.english_translation: On one side, Ravana's cry and on the other, Ram's cry rose up. As the shout of victory and victory rang out, the battle broke open. The demons hurl mountain peaks in heaps, and the monkeys leap to catch them and throw them back.
ramacharitamanas::4739.translation_literal: उत (on one side) / रावन (Ravana) / इत (on this side) / राम (Ram) / दोहाई (cry for help; invocation) / जयति (victory) / जयति (victory) / जय (victory) / परी (fell; broke out) / लराई (battle)॥ / निसिचर (night-walkers; demons) / सिखर (peaks) / समूह (heap; multitude) / ढहावहिं (hurl down) / कूदि (leaping) / धरहिं (catch; seize) / कपि (monkeys) / फेरि (again; back) / चलावहिं (send; throw)
ramacharitamanas::4739.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4739.essence: War has become instant reaction, strike answered by strike.
ramacharitamanas::4739.simple_meaning: The battle erupts with both sides shouting their war cries. Demons throw mountain peaks, and the monkeys leap up to catch and hurl them back.
ramacharitamanas::4739.simple_insight: It is pure action under pressure: every attack is met immediately, without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4739.detailed_meaning: The war at Lanka has fully broken open. Ravana's side and Ram's side are both shouting their battle cries as demons and monkey warriors hurl mountain peaks at one another. This verse keeps the scene moving, showing the clash rather than teaching a separate lesson.
ramacharitamanas::4739.modern_relevance: A crisis hits fast: messages fly, tempers rise, and everyone starts reacting before thinking. This verse is the speed of conflict itself.
ramacharitamanas::4739.insight: It shows a battle where force is answered instantly with force, without pause or reflection.

ramacharitamanas::4740.verse_sanskrit: धरि कुधर खंड प्रचंड मर्कट भालु गढ़ पर डारहीं। झपटहिं चरन गहि पटकि महि भजि चलत बहुरि पचारहीं॥ अति तरल तरुन प्रताप तरपहिं तमकि गढ़ चढ़ि चढ़ि गए। कपि भालु चढ़ि मंदिरन्ह जहँ तहँ राम जसु गावत भए॥
ramacharitamanas::4740.verse_hindi: प्रचण्ड वानर और भालू पर्वतों के टुकड़े ले-लेकर किले पर डालते हैं। वे झपटते हैं और राक्षसों के पैर पकड़कर उन्हें पृथ्वी पर पटककर भाग चलते हैं और फिर ललकारते हैं। बहुत ही चंचल और बड़े तेजस्वी वानर-भालू बड़ी फुर्ती से उछलकर किले पर चढ़-चढ़कर गए और जहाँ-तहाँ महलों में घुसकर श्री रामजी का यश गाने लगे।
ramacharitamanas::4740.english_translation: The fierce monkeys and bears hurl mountain fragments onto the fort. They leap, seize the demons by the feet, slam them to the ground, and dash away again. Swift and radiant, they climb the ramparts in a flash, and wherever they go, they fill the palaces with Ram's praise.
ramacharitamanas::4740.translation_literal: धरि (taking) / कुधर (mountain fragments) / खंड (pieces) / प्रचंड (fierce) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / गढ़ (fort) / पर (on) / डारहीं (throw) / झपटहिं (they leap) / चरन (feet) / गहि (grasping) / पटकि (slamming) / महि (on the ground) / भजि (running away) / चलत (while moving) / बहुरि (again) / पचारहीं (they drive on) / अति (very) / तरल (swift) / तरुन (young) / प्रताप (radiance) / तरपहिं (they surge) / तमकि (with a spring) / गढ़ (fort) / चढ़ि (climbing) / चढ़ि (climbing) / गए (went) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / चढ़ि (climbing) / मंदिरन्ह (into the palaces) / जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / राम (Ram's) / जसु (praise) / गावत (singing) / भए (became)
ramacharitamanas::4740.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4740.essence: The fort falls into chaos as Ram's warriors surge through it.
ramacharitamanas::4740.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears storm the fort, throw rocks, wrestle demons down, and race through the palaces singing Ram's praise.
ramacharitamanas::4740.simple_insight: When courage is alive, even a fortress becomes a place of praise.
ramacharitamanas::4740.detailed_meaning: The battle at Lanka is in full roar. Monkeys and bears hurl mountain fragments, leap onto the fort, and overpower the defenders. The verse is not teaching a principle; it is showing the chaos and momentum of war as Ram's army breaks through.
ramacharitamanas::4740.insight: It intensifies the battle scene rather than offering a separable lesson.

ramacharitamanas::4741.verse_sanskrit: एकु एकु निसिचर गहि पुनि कपि चले पराइ। ऊपर आपु हेठ भट गिरहिं धरनि पर आइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4741.verse_hindi: फिर एक-एक राक्षस को पकड़कर वे वानर भाग चले। ऊपर आप और नीचे (राक्षस) योद्धा- इस प्रकार वे (किले से) धरती पर आ गिरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4741.english_translation: One by one the monkeys seized the demons and ran off. Above were the monkeys, below the warriors, and they all fell to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::4741.translation_literal: एकु एकु (one by one) / निसिचर (demons) / गहि (seizing) / पुनि (again) / कपि (monkeys) / चले (went) / पराइ (running away) / ऊपर (above) / आपु (themselves) / हेठ (below) / भट (warriors) / गिरहिं (fall) / धरनि पर (onto the ground) / आइ (coming)
ramacharitamanas::4741.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4741.essence: The fort fight has turned into sheer chaos.
ramacharitamanas::4741.simple_meaning: The monkeys grab enemy fighters one by one, carry them off, and both sides tumble down from the fort in the chaos of battle.
ramacharitamanas::4741.simple_insight: It shows the wild momentum of war, where control slips away in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4741.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s battle, Ram’s monkey army surges over the fort walls. They seize enemy fighters one by one, then rush away, dragging the combat into a chaotic fall from the ramparts. The verse is a vivid combat detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4741.insight: It records the melee as a moving battlefield scene, with no separate moral claim.

ramacharitamanas::4742.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रताप प्रबल कपिजूथा। मर्दहिं निसिचर सुभट बरूथा॥ चढ़े दुर्ग पुनि जहँ तहँ बानर। जय रघुबीर प्रताप दिवाकर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4742.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के प्रताप से प्रबल वानरों के झुंड राक्षस योद्धाओं के समूह के समूह मसल रहे हैं। वानर फिर जहाँ-तहाँ किले पर चढ़ गए और प्रताप में सूर्य के समान श्री रघुवीर की जय बोलने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4742.english_translation: By Ram's power, the mighty monkey hosts crush the demon warriors. Then the monkeys climb the forts everywhere, crying victory to Raghubir, whose glory shines like the sun.
ramacharitamanas::4742.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रताप (power, glory) / प्रबल (mighty) / कपिजूथा (monkey host) / मर्दहिं (crush) / निसिचर (demons) / सुभट (warriors) / बरूथा (bands) / चढ़े (climbed) / दुर्ग (forts) / पुनि (again) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / बानर (monkeys) / जय (victory) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / प्रताप (glory) / दिवाकर (sun)
ramacharitamanas::4742.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4742.essence: Ram's power turns a scattered army into an unstoppable force.
ramacharitamanas::4742.simple_meaning: Ram's power makes the monkey army overpower the enemy, then they spread through the forts shouting victory.
ramacharitamanas::4742.simple_insight: Victory belongs to the force larger than fear, not to the side that looks stronger.
ramacharitamanas::4742.detailed_meaning: The battle at Lanka is in full swing. Ram's monkey army surges over the forts, crushing the demon warriors and spreading through the strongholds. Their cry of victory shows the tide has turned, but this is still part of the larger war scene.
ramacharitamanas::4742.modern_relevance: A team finally gets traction after weeks of pressure, and suddenly the whole room changes. The momentum feels bigger than any one person, because it is.
ramacharitamanas::4742.insight: It shows how collective courage can break a hardened resistance once fear starts to collapse.

ramacharitamanas::4743.verse_sanskrit: चले निसाचर निकर पराई। प्रबल पवन जिमि घन समुदाई॥ हाहाकार भयउ पुर भारी। रोवहिं बालक आतुर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4743.verse_hindi: राक्षसों के झुंड वैसे ही भाग चले जैसे जोर की हवा चलने पर बादलों के समूह तितर-बितर हो जाते हैं। लंका नगरी में बड़ा भारी हाहाकार मच गया। बालक, स्त्रियाँ और रोगी (असमर्थता के कारण) रोने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4743.english_translation: The ranks of the demons fled like a mass of clouds blown apart by a strong wind. Great panic swept through Lanka; children, women, and the helpless cried out.
ramacharitamanas::4743.translation_literal: चले (went/fled) / निसाचर (demons) / निकर (crowds) / पराई (ran away) / प्रबल (strong) / पवन (wind) / जिमि (like) / घन (clouds) / समुदाई (mass) ॥ / हाहाकार (uproar of grief and panic) / भयउ (became) / पुर (city) / भारी (great) / रोवहिं (they cry) / बालक (children) / आतुर (helpless/distressed) / नारी (women) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4743.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4743.essence: Panic multiplies when strength begins to fail.
ramacharitamanas::4743.simple_meaning: The demon army breaks and runs. Panic spreads through Lanka, and the vulnerable begin to weep.
ramacharitamanas::4743.simple_insight: When fear takes hold, even a proud city can unravel in moments.
ramacharitamanas::4743.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final battle, Ravana’s forces are collapsing under Ram’s power. The demons flee in confusion, and the city itself is shaken by cries of panic. This verse shows the breakdown before Ravana hears the full extent of the defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4743.modern_relevance: A workplace rumor hits the group chat before the meeting even starts. People panic, blame each other, and the whole room changes before anyone knows the full story.
ramacharitamanas::4743.insight: It shows how quickly fear spreads once confidence in control is lost.

ramacharitamanas::4744.verse_sanskrit: सब मिलि देहिं रावनहि गारी। राज करत एहिं मृत्यु हँकारी॥ निज दल बिचल सुनी तेहिं काना। फेरि सुभट लंकेस रिसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4744.verse_hindi: सब मिलकर रावण को गालियाँ देने लगे कि राज्य करते हुए इसने मृत्यु को बुला लिया। रावण ने जब अपनी सेना का विचलित होना कानों से सुना, तब (भागते हुए) योद्धाओं को लौटाकर वह क्रोधित होकर बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4744.english_translation: Everyone together began abusing Ravana, saying, "While ruling, you have invited death." When Ravana heard his own army wavering, he turned back the fleeing warriors and, enraged, spoke.
ramacharitamanas::4744.translation_literal: सब (all) / मिलि (together) / देहिं (give) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / गारी (abuses) / राज (rule) / करत (doing) / एहिं (this) / मृत्यु (death) / हँकारी (called out, invited) / निज (own) / दल (army) / बिचल (wavering) / सुनी (heard) / तेहिं (he) / काना (with ears) / फेरि (turned back) / सुभट (warriors) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / रिसाना (angered)
ramacharitamanas::4744.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4744.essence: Ego turns panic into anger when its control begins to slip.
ramacharitamanas::4744.simple_meaning: Ravana is mocked by his own side as his army starts to break. Hearing the panic, he turns back the fleeing warriors in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4744.simple_insight: Pride can survive praise, but it cracks when your own side starts to falter.
ramacharitamanas::4744.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has already begun to collapse around Ravana. His own warriors are wavering, and the city is in panic. Hearing the unrest, Ravana whips the fleeing fighters back into line and answers fear with rage.
ramacharitamanas::4744.modern_relevance: You hear the tone change in a group chat after the plan starts failing. People begin blaming the leader, and the leader snaps back instead of steadying anyone.
ramacharitamanas::4744.insight: It shows how ego reacts when control starts slipping: by blaming, shouting, and forcing others back into place.

ramacharitamanas::4745.verse_sanskrit: जो रन बिमुख सुना मैं काना। सो मैं हतब कराल कृपाना॥ सर्बसु खाइ भोग करि नाना। समर भूमि भए बल्लभ प्राना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4745.verse_hindi: मैं जिसे रण से पीठ देकर भागा हुआ अपने कानों सुनूँगा, उसे स्वयं भयानक दोधारी तलवार से मारूँगा। मेरा सब कुछ खाया, भाँति-भाँति के भोग किए और अब रणभूमि में प्राण प्यारे हो गए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4745.english_translation: I will kill anyone I hear has turned back from battle with this terrible sword. After enjoying every luxury and consuming all wealth, life itself has become dear only on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4745.translation_literal: जो (who) / रन (battle) / बिमुख (turned away from) / सुना (heard) / मैं (I) / काना (with my ears) / सो (that one) / मैं (I) / हतब (will kill) / कराल (terrible) / कृपाना (sword) ॥ / सर्बसु (all wealth) / खाइ (having eaten/consumed) / भोग (enjoyments) / करि (having done) / नाना (many) / समर (war) / भूमि (ground) / भए (have become) / बल्लभ (beloved) / प्राना (lives) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4745.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4745.essence: Ego turns fear into threats and calls it courage.
ramacharitamanas::4745.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he will kill any warrior who flees battle, and says that after enjoying every pleasure, he now values life only in war.
ramacharitamanas::4745.simple_insight: Pride can make violence sound like courage, even when it is really fear of losing status.
ramacharitamanas::4745.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hears his army faltering after defeat and erupts in rage. He tries to restore their courage with threats and boasts, turning his own fear into a show of strength. This verse is part of that breakdown.
ramacharitamanas::4745.modern_relevance: A leader hears the team is losing confidence before a major launch and starts barking threats instead of calming anyone. The panic is still there, just wearing a louder voice.
ramacharitamanas::4745.insight: It exposes how ego tries to rule through intimidation when real steadiness is gone.

ramacharitamanas::4746.verse_sanskrit: उग्र बचन सुनि सकल डेराने। चले क्रोध करि सुभट लजाने॥ सन्मुख मरन बीर कै सोभा। तब तिन्ह तजा प्रान कर लोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4746.verse_hindi: रावण के उग्र (कठोर) वचन सुनकर सब वीर डर गए और लज्जित होकर क्रोध करके युद्ध के लिए लौट चले। रण में (शत्रु के) सम्मुख (युद्ध करते हुए) मरने में ही वीर की शोभा है। (यह सोचकर) तब उन्होंने प्राणों का लोभ छोड़ दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4746.english_translation: Hearing Ravana's fierce words, all the warriors were frightened. Ashamed, they turned back to fight in anger. In battle, dying face to face is the warrior's true honor. Thinking this, they let go of their fear of death.
