ramacharitamanas::4746.translation_literal: उग्र (fierce) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / सकल (all) / डेराने (became afraid) / चले (went) / क्रोध (anger) / करि (doing) / सुभट (warriors) / लजाने (ashamed) / सन्मुख (face to face) / मरन (dying) / बीर (hero) / कै (of) / सोभा (honor) / तब (then) / तिन्ह (they) / तजा (gave up) / प्रान (life) / कर (of) / लोभा (desire)
ramacharitamanas::4746.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4746.essence: True courage is choosing the fight over the fear of dying.
ramacharitamanas::4746.simple_meaning: Ravana's harsh words shake the warriors at first, but they recover their courage. They decide that a warrior's honor is to face death directly in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4746.simple_insight: Fear can be shaken off when honor matters more than survival.
ramacharitamanas::4746.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Ravana's harsh command has just rattled his own side. The warriors feel fear and shame, then force themselves back into battle, choosing face-to-face combat over clinging to life.
ramacharitamanas::4746.modern_relevance: You hear a brutal message in a tense meeting and want to shrink back. Then pride, duty, or self-respect pulls you upright and back into the room.
ramacharitamanas::4746.insight: It shifts the mind from self-preservation to courageous engagement under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4747.verse_sanskrit: बहु आयुध धर सुभट सब भिरहिं पचारि पचारि। ब्याकुल किए भालु कपि परिघ त्रिसूलन्हि मारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4747.verse_hindi: बहुत से अस्त्र-शस्त्र धारण किए, सब वीर ललकार-ललकारकर भिड़ने लगे। उन्होंने परिघों और त्रिशूलों से मार-मारकर सब रीछ-वानरों को व्याकुल कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4747.english_translation: All the great warriors, armed with many weapons, rushed in again and again. They struck the bears and monkeys with clubs and tridents, leaving them shaken.
ramacharitamanas::4747.translation_literal: बहु (many) / आयुध (weapons) / धर (holding) / सुभट (great warriors) / सब (all) / भिरहिं (clash) / पचारि पचारि (again and again, driving forward) / ब्याकुल (distressed, shaken) / किए (made) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / परिघ (clubs/maces) / त्रिसूलन्हि (with tridents) / मारि (striking)
ramacharitamanas::4747.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4747.essence: The war spills into brutal close combat.
ramacharitamanas::4747.simple_meaning: The battle turns fierce. Armed warriors charge repeatedly and hammer the bears and monkeys with heavy weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4747.simple_insight: Some moments are only force and movement; they need to be faced before meaning can return.
ramacharitamanas::4747.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, the fighting surges into raw violence. Ravana’s warriors rush forward with clubs and tridents, battering the monkey and bear army into confusion. This line simply deepens the battle scene before the next turn.
ramacharitamanas::4747.insight: It keeps the focus on the physical clash, not on reflection or strategy.

ramacharitamanas::4748.verse_sanskrit: भय आतुर कपि भागत लागे। जद्यपि उमा जीतिहहिं आगे॥ कोउ कह कहँ अंगद हनुमंता। कहँ नल नील दुबिद बलवंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4748.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) वानर भयातुर होकर (डर के मारे घबड़ाकर) भागने लगे, यद्यपि हे उमा! आगे चलकर (वे ही) जीतेंगे। कोई कहता है- अंगद-हनुमान् कहाँ हैं? बलवान् नल, नील और द्विविद कहाँ हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4748.english_translation: The monkeys, frightened, began to flee, though, O Uma, they would win in the end. Some cried, “Where are Angad and Hanuman? Where are the strong Nala, Neela, and Dvivid?”
ramacharitamanas::4748.translation_literal: भय (fear) / आतुर (anxious) / कपि (monkeys) / भागत (running away) / लागे (began) / जद्यपि (although) / उमा (Uma) / जीतिहहिं (they will win) / आगे (later) / कोउ (someone) / कह (said) / कहँ (where) / अंगद (Angad) / हनुमंता (Hanuman) / कहँ (where) / नल (Nala) / नील (Neela) / दुबिद (Dvivid) / बलवंता (the strong ones)
ramacharitamanas::4748.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4748.essence: Fear can scatter you even when victory is still coming.
ramacharitamanas::4748.simple_meaning: The monkey army panics and runs, even though victory will still come later. In the confusion, warriors call out for their strongest allies.
ramacharitamanas::4748.simple_insight: Fear can shake you in the moment without deciding the final outcome.
ramacharitamanas::4748.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the monkey forces are under crushing pressure. Shiva, speaking to Uma, notes their panic even while foreseeing their eventual victory. The verse captures a moment of confusion, when warriors look around for their strongest defenders.
ramacharitamanas::4748.modern_relevance: You watch a team panic during a crisis call, voices overlapping, everyone asking where the strongest people are. The situation feels lost for a moment, even though recovery is still possible.
ramacharitamanas::4748.insight: It separates temporary panic from the larger arc of success.

ramacharitamanas::4749.verse_sanskrit: निज दल बिकल सुना हनुमाना। पच्छिम द्वार रहा बलवाना॥ मेघनाद तहँ करइ लराई। टूट न द्वार परम कठिनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4749.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने जब अपने दल को विकल (भयभीत) हुआ सुना, उस समय वे बलवान् पश्चिम द्वार पर थे। वहाँ उनसे मेघनाद युद्ध कर रहा था। वह द्वार टूटता न था, बड़ी भारी कठिनाई हो रही थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4749.english_translation: When Hanuman heard that his own army was shaken, the mighty one was at the western gate. There Megnada fought him, and the gate would not break despite the great struggle.
ramacharitamanas::4749.translation_literal: निज दल (his own army) / बिकल (distressed, shaken) / सुना (heard) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / पच्छिम द्वार (western gate) / रहा (was staying) / बलवाना (the mighty one) / मेघनाद (Megnada) / तहँ (there) / करइ (is doing) / लराई (battle) / टूट (breaks) / न (not) / द्वार (gate) / परम (extreme) / कठिनाई (difficulty)
ramacharitamanas::4749.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4749.essence: Holding the gate is still a kind of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4749.simple_meaning: Hanuman is holding the western gate while Megnada attacks. The gate is still holding, even as the fighting grows intense.
ramacharitamanas::4749.simple_insight: Some duties hold you in place even when everything around you is shaking.
ramacharitamanas::4749.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Hanuman stands at the western gate while the monkey army elsewhere is thrown into panic. Megnada keeps pressing the attack, but the gate still holds. The verse simply freezes that tense moment before Hanuman's next burst of force.
ramacharitamanas::4749.modern_relevance: You're in the middle of a crisis call, one team is panicking, and you're still holding the line at your end. This is the moment before you move again.
ramacharitamanas::4749.insight: It keeps the focus on steady presence under pressure, not on victory yet.

ramacharitamanas::4750.verse_sanskrit: पवनतनय मन भा अति क्रोधा। गर्जेउ प्रबल काल सम जोधा॥ कूदि लंक गढ़ ऊपर आवा। गहि गिरि मेघनाद कहुँ धावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4750.verse_hindi: तब पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी के मन में बड़ा भारी क्रोध हुआ। वे काल के समान योद्धा बड़े जोर से गरजे और कूदकर लंका के किले पर आ गए और पहाड़ लेकर मेघनाद की ओर दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4750.english_translation: Then Hanuman's mind burned with fierce anger. That warrior roared like Time itself, leapt onto Lanka's fort, and charged at Meghnad with a mountain in hand.
ramacharitamanas::4750.translation_literal: पवनतनय (son of the wind) / मन (mind) / भा (became) / अति (very) / क्रोधा (anger) / गर्जेउ (roared) / प्रबल (powerful) / काल (Time/death) / सम (like) / जोधा (warrior) / कूदि (leaping) / लंक (Lanka) / गढ़ (fort) / ऊपर (on top) / आवा (came) / गहि (grasping) / गिरि (mountain) / मेघनाद (Meghnad) / कहुँ (toward) / धावा (charged)
ramacharitamanas::4750.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4750.essence: Devotion can become thunder when someone you serve is under attack.
ramacharitamanas::4750.simple_meaning: Hanuman becomes furious, leaps onto Lanka's fort, and charges at Meghnad with a mountain in his hand.
ramacharitamanas::4750.simple_insight: Sometimes devotion turns into fearless force when something precious is threatened.
ramacharitamanas::4750.detailed_meaning: Hanuman hears that his own side is shaken in battle. Standing at Lanka's western gate, he loses patience with delay, leaps onto the fort, and rushes at Meghnad with raw force. This is the instant before the clash.
ramacharitamanas::4750.modern_relevance: You hear your friend is being cornered, and something in you snaps awake. You stop hesitating, move fast, and step straight into the danger.
ramacharitamanas::4750.insight: It shifts courage from thought to action when protection is needed.

ramacharitamanas::4751.verse_sanskrit: भंजेउ रथ सारथी निपाता। ताहि हृदय महुँ मारेसि लाता॥ दुसरें सूत बिकल तेहि जाना। स्यंदन घालि तुरत गृह आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4751.verse_hindi: रथ तोड़ डाला, सारथी को मार गिराया और मेघनाद की छाती में लात मारी। दूसरा सारथी मेघनाद को व्याकुल जानकर, उसे रथ में डालकर, तुरंत घर ले आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4751.english_translation: He smashed the chariot, struck down the charioteer, and kicked Meghnada in the chest. Seeing Meghnada shaken, the second charioteer quickly loaded him into the chariot and took him home.
ramacharitamanas::4751.translation_literal: भंजेउ (broke) / रथ (chariot) / सारथी (charioteer) / निपाता (struck down) / ताहि (him) / हृदय (heart/chest) / महुँ (in) / मारेसि (struck) / लाता (with a kick) / दुसरें (the other) / सूत (charioteer) / बिकल (distressed) / तेहि (him) / जाना (knew) / स्यंदन (chariot) / घालि (placing) / तुरत (quickly) / गृह (home) / आना (brought)
ramacharitamanas::4751.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4751.essence: Force can collapse pride in a single blow.
ramacharitamanas::4751.simple_meaning: Hanuman destroys Meghnada's chariot, kills the charioteer, and kicks Meghnada in the chest. Another charioteer sees Meghnada is shaken and takes him home quickly.
ramacharitamanas::4751.simple_insight: Some moments in battle are pure force: the fight turns, and the wounded must be carried away.
ramacharitamanas::4751.detailed_meaning: On Lanka's battlefield, Hanuman has burst into the fighting alone. He smashes Meghnada's chariot, drops the charioteer, and drives Meghnada back. The scene is still moving, but this verse is only a tactical snapshot in the larger clash.
ramacharitamanas::4751.modern_relevance: A meeting goes sideways in seconds, and the person who seemed in control suddenly has to be escorted out. Momentum can change that fast.
ramacharitamanas::4751.insight: It shows how quickly pressure can break confidence and force retreat.

ramacharitamanas::4752.verse_sanskrit: अंगद सुना पवनसुत गढ़ पर गयउ अकेल। रन बाँकुरा बालिसुत तरकि चढ़ेउ कपि खेल ॥
ramacharitamanas::4752.verse_hindi: इधर अंगद ने सुना कि पवनपुत्र हनुमान् किले पर अकेले ही गए हैं, तो रण में बाँके बालि पुत्र वानर के खेल की तरह उछलकर किले पर चढ़ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4752.english_translation: When Angad heard that Hanuman had gone alone onto the fort, the brave son of Bali leapt up there as if in play.
ramacharitamanas::4752.translation_literal: अंगद (Angad) / सुना (heard) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / गढ़ (fort) / पर (on) / गयउ (went) / अकेल (alone) / रन (battle) / बाँकुरा (brave) / बालिसुत (son of Bali) / तरकि (leaping) / चढ़ेउ (climbed) / कपि (monkey) / खेल (play)
ramacharitamanas::4752.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4752.essence: True courage can feel like play when loyalty leads it.
ramacharitamanas::4752.simple_meaning: Angad hears that Hanuman has gone alone into the fort, and he instantly leaps up after him with fearless energy.
ramacharitamanas::4752.simple_insight: Loyalty can turn into courage the moment someone you love goes ahead alone.
ramacharitamanas::4752.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already stormed the fort and stirred the enemy. Angad hears of it and cannot stay back. He jumps up to follow, treating danger like a game and joining the attack without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4752.modern_relevance: You hear your friend has walked into a hard conversation alone, and you stand up immediately. Fear shrinks when loyalty moves first.
ramacharitamanas::4752.insight: It shows how devotion can become instant action, with courage rising from shared purpose rather than self-interest.

ramacharitamanas::4753.verse_sanskrit: जुद्ध बिरुद्ध क्रुद्ध द्वौ बंदर। राम प्रताप सुमिरि उर अंतर॥ रावन भवन चढ़े द्वौ धाई। करहिं कोसलाधीस दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4753.verse_hindi: युद्ध में शत्रुओं के विरुद्ध दोनों वानर क्रुद्ध हो गए। हृदय में श्री रामजी के प्रताप का स्मरण करके दोनों दौड़कर रावण के महल पर जा चढ़े और कोसलराज श्री रामजी की दुहाई बोलने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4753.english_translation: Both monkeys grew furious against their enemies in battle. Remembering Ram's power in their hearts, they rushed to Ravana's palace and cried out the name of the lord of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::4753.translation_literal: जुद्ध (battle) / बिरुद्ध (against the enemy) / क्रुद्ध (furious) / द्वौ (both) / बंदर (monkeys)। / राम (Ram) / प्रताप (power, glory) / सुमिरि (remembering) / उर (heart) / अंतर (within)॥ / रावन (Ravana) / भवन (palace) / चढ़े (climbed) / द्वौ (both) / धाई (rushing)। / करहिं (they cry) / कोसलाधीस (lord of Kosala) / दोहाई (call for help, invoke)॥
ramacharitamanas::4753.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4753.essence: Remembered strength turns battle into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4753.simple_meaning: The two monkeys, fired up in battle, remembered Ram and rushed straight to Ravana's palace, shouting Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::4753.simple_insight: Real courage comes from remembering what stands behind you.
ramacharitamanas::4753.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Angad and another monkey warrior are no longer just fighting; they are charged with Ram's presence in their hearts. They charge Ravana's palace, turning battle into a loud declaration of allegiance.
ramacharitamanas::4753.modern_relevance: You step into a tense room with your chest tight and your phone buzzing, but you remember who you are fighting for. That memory steadies your feet.
ramacharitamanas::4753.insight: It shifts action from personal aggression to fearless service backed by remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::4754.verse_sanskrit: कलस सहित गहि भवनु ढहावा। देखि निसाचरपति भय पावा॥ नारि बृंद कर पीटहिं छाती। अब दुइ कपि आए उतपाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4754.verse_hindi: उन्होंने कलश सहित महल को पकड़कर ढहा दिया। यह देखकर राक्षस राज रावण डर गया। सब स्त्रियाँ हाथों से छाती पीटने लगीं (और कहने लगीं-) अब की बार दो उत्पाती वानर (एक साथ) आ गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4754.english_translation: They pulled down the palace, kalasha and all. Seeing this, the lord of the demons was struck with fear. The women beat their chests and cried, "Now two troublemaking monkeys have come!"
ramacharitamanas::4754.translation_literal: कलस सहित (with the finial) / गहि (grasping) / भवनु (the palace) / ढहावा (pulled down) / देखि (seeing) / निसाचरपति (the lord of the night-dwellers) / भय पावा (felt fear) / नारि बृंद (the group of women) / कर (with hands) / पीटहिं (beat) / छाती (chests) / अब (now) / दुइ (two) / कपि (monkeys) / आए (have come) / उतपाती (mischievous, troublemaking)
ramacharitamanas::4754.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4754.essence: False power crumbles when courage enters the room.
ramacharitamanas::4754.simple_meaning: Hanuman and Angad tear down a palace in Lanka, frightening Ravana and sending the women into panic.
ramacharitamanas::4754.simple_insight: Power built on fear collapses fast when courage walks in.
ramacharitamanas::4754.detailed_meaning: Inside Lanka, Angad and Hanuman surge through Ravana’s stronghold. They rip down the palace itself, and Ravana’s confidence breaks into fear. The women of the palace panic, seeing that two fierce monkeys have brought the war right home.
ramacharitamanas::4754.modern_relevance: A room full of polished confidence can go silent in one moment when the truth is finally acted on. What looked untouchable suddenly feels fragile.
ramacharitamanas::4754.insight: It shows how fearless action can expose the weakness behind intimidation.

ramacharitamanas::4755.verse_sanskrit: कपिलीला करि तिन्हहि डेरावहिं। रामचंद्र कर सुजसु सुनावहिं॥ पुनि कर गहि कंचन के खंभा। कहेन्हि करिअ उतपात अरंभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4755.verse_hindi: वानरलीला करके (घुड़की देकर) दोनों उनको डराते हैं और श्री रामचंद्रजी का सुंदर यश सुनाते हैं। फिर सोने के खंभों को हाथों से पकड़कर उन्होंने (परस्पर) कहा कि अब उत्पात आरंभ किया जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4755.english_translation: They frightened them with monkey-play and sang the glorious praise of Ramchandra. Then they grabbed the golden pillars and said, "Let the mischief begin."
ramacharitamanas::4755.translation_literal: कपिलीला (monkey-play) / करि (having done) / तिन्हहि (those two / them) / डेरावहिं (frighten) / रामचंद्र (Ramchandra) / कर (of) / सुजसु (good fame / glorious praise) / सुनावहिं (make hear) / पुनि (then) / कर (hand) / गहि (grasping) / कंचन (golden) / के (of) / खंभा (pillars) / कहेन्हि (they said) / करिअ (let be done) / उतपात (mischief / upheaval) / अरंभा (beginning)
ramacharitamanas::4755.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4755.essence: Fearless devotion can make destruction feel like play.
ramacharitamanas::4755.simple_meaning: The monkeys terrorize the enemy while praising Ram, then seize the palace pillars and prepare to keep causing chaos.
ramacharitamanas::4755.simple_insight: Sometimes courage looks playful before it turns fierce.
ramacharitamanas::4755.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the two monkey warriors are already inside Ravana's world, turning fear into sport. They mock the enemies, sing Ram's glory, and then grab the golden pillars as they prepare to wreak more havoc. The verse is a moving detail in the raid, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::4755.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and lighten it with a joke, then calmly handle the real problem. The mood shifts because you are unafraid.
ramacharitamanas::4755.insight: It shows how fearless devotion can turn even attack into play.

ramacharitamanas::4756.verse_sanskrit: गर्जि परे रिपु कटक मझारी। लागे मर्दै भुज बल भारी॥ काहुहि लात चपेटन्हि केहू। भजहु न रामहि सो फल लेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4756.verse_hindi: वे गर्जकर शत्रु की सेना के बीच में कूद पड़े और अपने भारी भुजबल से उसका मर्दन करने लगे। किसी की लात से और किसी की थप्पड़ से खबर लेते हैं (और कहते हैं कि) तुम श्री रामजी को नहीं भजते, उसका यह फल लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4756.english_translation: They leaped roaring into the enemy ranks and crushed them with heavy arms. Some got kicks, some slaps: "If you do not remember Ram, take this result."
ramacharitamanas::4756.translation_literal: गर्जि (roaring) / परे (fell/leaped) / रिपु (enemy) / कटक (army) / मझारी (amidst) / लागे (began) / मर्दै (crushing) / भुज (arms) / बल (strength) / भारी (heavy)॥ / काहुहि (to some) / लात (kick) / चपेटन्हि (with slaps) / केहू (someone) / भजहु (worship/remember) / न (not) / रामहि (Ram) / सो (that) / फल (result) / लेहू (take)॥
ramacharitamanas::4756.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4756.essence: The war surges forward in raw, unstoppable force.
ramacharitamanas::4756.simple_meaning: The monkeys charge into the enemy army and beat them hard. It is a battle scene, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4756.simple_insight: Sometimes the story moves by force, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4756.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war at Lanka, the monkey warriors roar into Ravana's army and strike from every side. Their blows are followed by a taunting warning about Ram. The verse is part of the action, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4756.modern_relevance: A crowd surges forward at a packed event, and everything becomes noise, motion, and impact. This is the kind of moment where the story is carried by sheer force.
ramacharitamanas::4756.insight: It keeps the reader inside the battle flow rather than pausing for interpretation.

ramacharitamanas::4757.verse_sanskrit: एक एक सों मर्दहिं तोरि चलावहिं मुंड। रावन आगें परहिं ते जनु फूटहिं दधि कुंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::4757.verse_hindi: एक को दूसरे से (रगड़कर) मसल डालते हैं और सिरों को तोड़कर फेंकते हैं। वे सिर जाकर रावण के सामने गिरते हैं और ऐसे फूटते हैं, मानो दही के कूंडे फूट रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4757.english_translation: One by one they crush and hurl the heads away; the heads fall before Ravana and burst like curds in a pot.
ramacharitamanas::4757.translation_literal: एक एक सों (one by one) / मर्दहिं (they crush) / तोरि (breaking) / चलावहिं (they send away) / मुंड (heads) / रावन आगें (before Ravana) / परहिं (they fall) / ते (those) / जनु (as if) / फूटहिं (burst) / दधि कुंड (curd pots)
ramacharitamanas::4757.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4757.essence: Violence in battle is shown in one brutal, unforgettable image.
ramacharitamanas::4757.simple_meaning: The fighters keep crushing heads and throwing them away. The heads fall before Ravana and burst like pots of curd.
ramacharitamanas::4757.simple_insight: Some scenes only show the force of chaos, not a lesson to hold onto.
ramacharitamanas::4757.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, the monkey warriors are tearing through Ravana’s forces with raw violence. This line does not teach a principle; it intensifies the battlefield image, showing how heads fly back and burst before Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::4757.insight: It heightens the battle scene by showing the enemy army being broken apart.

ramacharitamanas::4758.verse_sanskrit: महा महा मुखिआ जे पावहिं। ते पद गहि प्रभु पास चलावहिं॥ कहइ बिभीषनु तिन्ह के नामा। देहिं राम तिन्हहू निज धामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4758.verse_hindi: जिन बड़े-बड़े मुखियों (प्रधान सेनापतियों) को पकड़ पाते हैं, उनके पैर पकड़कर उन्हें प्रभु के पास फेंक देते हैं। विभीषणजी उनके नाम बतलाते हैं और श्री रामजी उन्हें भी अपना धाम (परम पद) दे देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4758.english_translation: They seize the great commanders, drag them by the feet to the Lord, and Vibhishana names them. Ram gives even them his own abode.
ramacharitamanas::4758.translation_literal: महा महा (great-great) / मुखिआ (leaders, commanders) / जे (who) / पावहिं (are able to catch) / ते (they) / पद (feet) / गहि (grasping) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पास (near) / चलावहिं (they send, bring) ॥ कहइ (speaks) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / नामा (names) / देहिं (give) / राम (Ram) / तिन्हहू (to them also) / निज (his own) / धामा (abode, dwelling) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4758.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4758.essence: Ram's welcome reaches even those brought in as captives.
ramacharitamanas::4758.simple_meaning: Even the enemy leaders are brought before Ram, and Ram gives them his own dwelling. His welcome reaches farther than punishment.
ramacharitamanas::4758.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that mercy can reach the people you would least expect.
ramacharitamanas::4758.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final battle, the monkey warriors seize even the enemy's top commanders and bring them before Ram. Vibhishana identifies them, and Ram responds not with rejection but with welcome, showing the scale of his grace.
ramacharitamanas::4758.modern_relevance: Someone who has hurt everyone in the room is finally brought into the meeting, and the atmosphere changes. You expect judgment, but a deeper kindness makes space instead.
ramacharitamanas::4758.insight: It shifts the mind from scoring enemies to recognising that grace can include even the worst case.

ramacharitamanas::4759.verse_sanskrit: खल मनुजाद द्विजामिष भोगी। पावहिं गति जो जाचत जोगी॥ उमा राम मृदुचित करुनाकर। बयर भाव सुमिरत मोहि निसिचर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4759.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मणों का मांस खाने वाले वे नरभोजी दुष्ट राक्षस भी वह परम गति पाते हैं, जिसकी योगी भी याचना किया करते हैं, (परन्तु सहज में नहीं पाते)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! श्री रामजी बड़े ही कोमल हृदय और करुणा की खान हैं। (वे सोचते हैं कि) राक्षस मुझे वैरभाव से ही सही, स्मरण तो करते ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4759.english_translation: Even cruel man-eaters and flesh-eating sinners can attain the highest state that yogis beg for. Uma, Ram is soft-hearted and a fountain of compassion; even if demons remember me in hatred, he still counts that as remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::4759.translation_literal: खल (wicked) / मनुजाद (man-eaters) / द्विजामिष-भोगी (those who eat the flesh of brahmins) / पावहिं (attain) / गति (state / destination) / जो (which) / जाचत (asking for) / जोगी (yogis) ॥ उमा (Uma) / राम (Ram) / मृदुचित (soft-hearted) / करुनाकर (fountain of compassion) / बयर-भाव (hostile feeling) / सुमिरत (remembering) / मोहि (me) / निसिचर (demons) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4759.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4759.essence: Even hostile remembrance can become a doorway to freedom.
ramacharitamanas::4759.simple_meaning: Ram's compassion is so great that even the worst beings can reach the highest state. He values even hostile remembrance as a form of connection.
ramacharitamanas::4759.simple_insight: You do not need to be pure to be held by compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4759.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Shiva turns to Uma and explains Ram's nature. Even demons who live by violence can still reach the highest state, because Ram is not looking for perfection first — he is looking for any living remembrance at all.
ramacharitamanas::4759.modern_relevance: You snapped in anger and then felt ashamed for hours. Even that messy, half-broken turn back toward the divine still matters more than you think.
ramacharitamanas::4759.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to trust in compassion that notices every turning toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4760.verse_sanskrit: देहिं परम गति सो जियँ जानी। अस कृपाल को कहहु भवानी॥ अस प्रभु सुनि न भजहिं भ्रम त्यागी। नर मतिमंद ते परम अभागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4760.verse_hindi: ऐसा हृदय में जानकर वे उन्हें परमगति (मोक्ष) देते हैं। हे भवानी! कहो तो ऐसे कृपालु (और) कौन हैं? प्रभु का ऐसा स्वभाव सुनकर भी जो मनुष्य भ्रम त्याग कर उनका भजन नहीं करते, वे अत्यंत मंदबुद्धि और परम भाग्यहीन हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4760.english_translation: Knowing this in their hearts, they grant the highest freedom. Tell me, Bhavani, who else is so compassionate? Even after hearing such a Lord, those who still do not turn from confusion to devotion are utterly dull and most unfortunate.
ramacharitamanas::4760.translation_literal: देहिं (they give) / परम गति (the highest freedom) / सो (that) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानी (knowing) / अस (such) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / को (who) / कहहु (tell) / भवानी (Bhavani) / अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / सुनि (hearing) / न (not) / भजहिं (they worship) / भ्रम (confusion) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / नर (people) / मतिमंद (dull-minded) / ते (they) / परम अभागी (most unfortunate)
ramacharitamanas::4760.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4760.essence: Ram's kindness is so complete that refusing him becomes the real loss.
ramacharitamanas::4760.simple_meaning: Ram gives the highest freedom to anyone who truly knows him in the heart. Hearing this, the verse says, how can anyone still refuse to worship him and leave confusion behind?
ramacharitamanas::4760.simple_insight: Devotion feels less like duty and more like the obvious response to overwhelming kindness.
ramacharitamanas::4760.detailed_meaning: Shiva is still speaking to Parvati in the Lanka war frame, explaining Ram's nature. After saying that even the worst beings can reach the highest state, he turns to Ram's compassion itself and asks who could be kinder. The verse then shames stubborn minds that still refuse devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4760.modern_relevance: You meet someone who keeps forgiving you, even after repeated mistakes, and still you keep acting guarded. At some point, the problem is no longer their distance — it's your refusal to trust what is already being offered.
ramacharitamanas::4760.insight: It shifts the mind from skepticism about grace to recognition of Ram's compassion as the natural reason to turn toward him.

ramacharitamanas::4761.verse_sanskrit: अंगद अरु हनुमंत प्रबेसा। कीन्ह दुर्ग अस कह अवधेसा॥ लंकाँ द्वौ कपि सोहहिं कैसें। मथहिं सिंधु दुइ मंदर जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4761.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने कहा कि अंगद और हनुमान किले में घुस गए हैं। दोनों वानर लंका में (विध्वंस करते) कैसे शोभा देते हैं, जैसे दो मन्दराचल समुद्र को मथ रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4761.english_translation: Angada and Hanuman entered the fortress. The king of Ayodhya said, “How splendid those two monkeys look in Lanka, like two Mount Mandara churning the ocean.”
ramacharitamanas::4761.translation_literal: अंगद (Angada) / अरु (and) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / प्रबेसा (entered) / कीन्ह (made) / दुर्ग (fortress) / अस (thus) / कह (said) / अवधेसा (the Lord of Ayodhya) / लंकाँ (in Lanka) / द्वौ (two) / कपि (monkeys) / सोहहिं (look splendid) / कैसें (how) / मथहिं (churn) / सिंधु (the ocean) / दुइ (two) / मंदर (Mandara mountains) / जैसें (as)
ramacharitamanas::4761.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4761.essence: Fearless service can make even danger look magnificent.
ramacharitamanas::4761.simple_meaning: Angada and Hanuman enter Lanka’s fortress. Ram marvels at how splendid the two look there, like two great mountains churning the sea.
ramacharitamanas::4761.simple_insight: Great courage can look beautiful when it serves a righteous cause.
ramacharitamanas::4761.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angada and Hanuman push deep into Ravana’s stronghold as the war intensifies. Ram watches their fearless advance and praises their presence with a vivid image of cosmic force. The verse heightens the battle, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4761.modern_relevance: Two people walk into a hostile room knowing they may be outnumbered, but they do it anyway. Their courage changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::4761.insight: It turns battlefield action into a picture of fearless, purposeful force.

ramacharitamanas::4762.verse_sanskrit: भुज बल रिपु दल दलमलि देखि दिवस कर अंत। कूदे जुगल बिगत श्रम आए जहँ भगवंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4762.verse_hindi: भुजाओं के बल से शत्रु की सेना को कुचलकर और मसलकर, फिर दिन का अंत होता देखकर हनुमान् और अंगद दोनों कूद पड़े और श्रम थकावट रहित होकर वहाँ आ गए, जहाँ भगवान् श्री रामजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4762.english_translation: After crushing and grinding the enemy army with their arm strength, and seeing the end of day, Hanuman and Angad leapt and reached where Lord Ram was, free from fatigue.
ramacharitamanas::4762.translation_literal: भुज बल (with arm strength) / रिपु दल (enemy army) / दलमलि (crushing and grinding) / देखि (seeing) / दिवस कर अंत (the end of day) / कूदे (they leapt) / जुगल (the two) / बिगत श्रम (free from fatigue) / आए (came) / जहँ (where) / भगवंत (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::4762.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4762.essence: Service can carry you beyond fatigue.
ramacharitamanas::4762.simple_meaning: Hanuman and Angad finish their battle work and return to Ram without weariness.
ramacharitamanas::4762.simple_insight: Total effort can leave you strong when it is offered in service.
ramacharitamanas::4762.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman and Angad have smashed through the enemy forces. As evening arrives, they leap back to Ram without exhaustion. The verse simply marks their return after fierce service, setting up Ram’s delighted welcome in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::4762.modern_relevance: You finish a hard day, hands sore, clothes dusty, but you still make it to the person who matters. Service can outlast fatigue when the heart is steady.
ramacharitamanas::4762.insight: It shifts attention from personal exhaustion to wholehearted service and return.

ramacharitamanas::4763.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पद कमल सीस तिन्ह नाए। देखि सुभट रघुपति मन भाए॥ राम कृपा करि जुगल निहारे। भए बिगतश्रम परम सुखारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4763.verse_hindi: उन्होंने प्रभु के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाए। उत्तम योद्धाओं को देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए। श्री रामजी ने कृपा करके दोनों को देखा, जिससे वे श्रमरहित और परम सुखी हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4763.english_translation: They bowed their heads at the Lord's lotus feet. Seeing the brave warriors, Raghupati was pleased in his heart. Ram, by his grace, looked upon the two, and they became free of fatigue and filled with supreme joy.
ramacharitamanas::4763.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / पद कमल (lotus feet) / सीस (head) / तिन्ह (they) / नाए (bowed) || देखि (seeing) / सुभट (brave warriors) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / मन (mind) / भाए (became pleased) || राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / करि (doing) / जुगल (both) / निहारे (looked upon) || भए (became) / बिगतश्रम (free of fatigue) / परम (supreme) / सुखारे (filled with joy)
ramacharitamanas::4763.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4763.essence: Devotion is answered by a glance that restores everything.
ramacharitamanas::4763.simple_meaning: Angad and Hanuman bow to Ram. Ram is pleased to see their courage, and his gracious glance leaves them refreshed and deeply joyful.
ramacharitamanas::4763.simple_insight: True devotion is mutual: you offer yourself, and grace answers with strength and delight.
ramacharitamanas::4763.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Angad and Hanuman have just returned from fierce action inside Ravana's fortress. They bow at Ram's feet, and Ram, pleased by their courage, blesses them with a look that removes their fatigue. The verse serves the flow of battle, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4763.modern_relevance: You come home after carrying everyone else's burden, too tired to speak. One look from someone who truly sees you can restore what effort drained away.
ramacharitamanas::4763.insight: It shows that sincere service is met by grace, and that being seen can renew exhausted strength.

ramacharitamanas::4764.verse_sanskrit: गए जानि अंगद हनुमाना। फिरे भालु मर्कट भट नाना॥ जातुधान प्रदोष बल पाई। धाए करि दससीस दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4764.verse_hindi: अंगद और हनुमान् को गए जानकर सभी भालू और वानर वीर लौट पड़े। राक्षसों ने प्रदोष (सायं) काल का बल पाकर रावण की दुहाई देते हुए वानरों पर धावा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4764.english_translation: Knowing that Angada and Hanuman had gone, the bears and many monkey warriors turned back. The demons, empowered by the dusk hour, rushed forward shouting Ravana's name.
ramacharitamanas::4764.translation_literal: गए (gone) / जानि (knowing) / अंगद (Angada) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / फिरे (turned back) / भालु (bears) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भट (warriors) / नाना (many) ॥ जातुधान (demons) / प्रदोष (dusk) / बल (strength) / पाई (having gained) / धाए (rushed) / करि (making) / दससीस (ten-headed Ravana) / दोहाई (crying out)
ramacharitamanas::4764.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4764.essence: Momentum can turn in a single moment on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4764.simple_meaning: When Angada and Hanuman moved away, the bear and monkey fighters pulled back. The demons, strengthened by dusk, charged while crying Ravana's name.
ramacharitamanas::4764.simple_insight: The scene shifts from advance to counterattack, and the battle tightens again.
ramacharitamanas::4764.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Angada and Hanuman have moved on, and the bear and monkey warriors fall back. Sensing dusk’s advantage, Ravana’s demon army surges forward, turning the fight into another fierce clash.
ramacharitamanas::4764.insight: It marks a tactical reversal: retreat on one side, renewed pressure on the other.

ramacharitamanas::4765.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर अनी देखि कपि फिरे। जहँ तहँ कटकटाइ भट भिरे॥ द्वौ दल प्रबल पचारि पचारी। लरत सुभट नहिं मानहिं हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4765.verse_hindi: राक्षसों की सेना आती देखकर वानर लौट पड़े और वे योद्धा जहाँ-तहाँ कटकटाकर भिड़ गए। दोनों ही दल बड़े बलवान् हैं। योद्धा ललकार-ललकारकर ल़ड़ते हैं, कोई हार नहीं मानते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4765.english_translation: Seeing the demon army advance, the monkeys fell back, and the warriors clashed here and there. Both armies are powerful; the brave fighters challenge each other again and again, and none accepts defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4765.translation_literal: निसिचर (demon) / अनी (army) / देखि (seeing) / कपि (monkeys) / फिरे (turned back) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / कटकटाइ (clashing noisily) / भट (warriors) / भिरे (fought) ॥ / द्वौ (two) / दल (armies) / प्रबल (powerful) / पचारि पचारी (challenging each other again and again) / लरत (fighting) / सुभट (brave warriors) / नहिं (not) / मानहिं (accept) / हारी (defeat) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4765.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4765.essence: Two equal forces meet, and neither will yield.
ramacharitamanas::4765.simple_meaning: The two armies keep colliding in fierce combat, and neither side is willing to back down.
ramacharitamanas::4765.simple_insight: Sometimes conflict becomes pure force, with no one ready to yield.
ramacharitamanas::4765.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has fully broken open. The monkey army sees the demon ranks advancing and surges into scattered clashes across the field. Tulsidas pauses the story here to show the raw equality of strength and fury before the next wave of fighting.
ramacharitamanas::4765.modern_relevance: Two teams keep interrupting each other in a tense meeting, each refusing to give ground. No one is listening anymore; only force is answering force.
ramacharitamanas::4765.insight: It shifts attention from strategy to the exhaustion of mutual resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4766.verse_sanskrit: महाबीर निसिचर सब कारे। नाना बरन बलीमुख भारे॥ सबल जुगल दल समबल जोधा। कौतुक करत लरत करि क्रोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4766.verse_hindi: सभी राक्षस महान् वीर और अत्यंत काले हैं और वानर विशालकाय तथा अनेकों रंगों के हैं। दोनों ही दल बलवान् हैं और समान बल वाले योद्धा हैं। वे क्रोध करके लड़ते हैं और खेल करते (वीरता दिखलाते) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4766.english_translation: The great heroes, the demons are all dark; the monkeys are of many colors and large-bodied. Both armies are evenly matched warriors, fighting in anger and almost as if in play.
ramacharitamanas::4766.translation_literal: महाबीर (great heroes) / निसिचर (night-walkers, demons) / सब (all) / कारे (dark) / नाना (many) / बरन (colors) / बलीमुख (strong-faced, powerful-bodied) / भारे (large) / सबल (strong) / जुगल (both) / दल (armies) / समबल (equal strength) / जोधा (warriors) / कौतुक (play, sport) / करत (doing) / लरत (fighting) / करि (with) / क्रोधा (anger)
ramacharitamanas::4766.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4766.essence: The battle is evenly matched, fierce, and almost playful in its intensity.
ramacharitamanas::4766.simple_meaning: The two armies are matched in strength. The demons are dark and the monkeys are many-colored and huge. They fight fiercely, almost like a contest of skill.
ramacharitamanas::4766.simple_insight: Even in chaos, the scene has order: both sides are fully committed, and neither yields easily.
ramacharitamanas::4766.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the war has fully opened. Tulsidas pauses to paint the combatants: Ravana's dark demon warriors and the many-colored monkey heroes, each side equally strong. The verse is a vivid scene-setting detail in the middle of the battle.
ramacharitamanas::4766.modern_relevance: You walk into a packed stadium and feel the tension before the whistle blows. Two sides are evenly matched, each fully ready, and the air itself feels charged.
ramacharitamanas::4766.insight: It shifts attention from individual fighters to the balanced force of the whole conflict.

ramacharitamanas::4767.verse_sanskrit: प्राबिट सरद पयोद घनेरे। लरत मनहुँ मारुत के प्रेरे॥ अनिप अकंपन अरु अतिकाया। बिचलत सेन कीन्हि इन्ह माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4767.verse_hindi: (राक्षस और वानर युद्ध करते हुए ऐसे जान पड़ते हैं) मानो क्रमशः वर्षा और शरद् ऋतु में बहुत से बादल पवन से प्रेरित होकर लड़ रहे हों। अकंपन और अतिकाय इन सेनापतियों ने अपनी सेना को विचलित होते देखकर माया की ॥
ramacharitamanas::4767.english_translation: The Rakshasa and monkey armies clash like clouds driven by the wind in rainy and autumn skies. Seeing their forces begin to waver, Akampana and Atikaya use illusion to shake them.
ramacharitamanas::4767.translation_literal: प्राबिट (rainy season) / सरद (autumn) / पयोद (clouds) / घनेरे (dense, many) / लरत (fighting) / मनहुँ (as if) / मारुत (wind) / के (of) / प्रेरे (driven) / अनिप (Akampana) / अकंपन (Akampana) / अरु (and) / अतिकाया (Atikaya) / बिचलत (wavering) / सेन (army) / कीन्हि (made) / इन्ह (these) / माया (illusion)
ramacharitamanas::4767.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4767.essence: Battlefields can turn from force to confusion in a single moment.
ramacharitamanas::4767.simple_meaning: The two armies fight fiercely, like storm clouds blown by the wind. When their side starts to lose steadiness, Akampana and Atikaya use illusion to unsettle the troops.
ramacharitamanas::4767.simple_insight: Pressure can make even strong people lose their footing fast.
ramacharitamanas::4767.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, monkey and demon forces collide in a chaotic surge. Akampana and Atikaya see their army wavering and answer with illusion, trying to restore control. The verse is a vivid war image, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4767.modern_relevance: A room full of people starts to panic when one confident voice cracks. In a crisis, fear spreads fast, and someone always tries to steady the crowd with a false show of control.
ramacharitamanas::4767.insight: It shows how quickly morale can collapse when fear and confusion enter the field.

ramacharitamanas::4768.verse_sanskrit: भयउ निमिष महँ अति अँधिआरा। बृष्टि होइ रुधिरोपल छारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4768.verse_hindi: पलभर में अत्यंत अंधकार हो गया। खून, पत्थर और राख की वर्षा होने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4768.english_translation: In an instant, darkness became overwhelming, and a rain of blood, stones, and ash fell.
ramacharitamanas::4768.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / निमिष महँ (in a moment) / अति अँधिआरा (extreme darkness) / बृष्टि (rain) / होइ (happened) / रुधिरोपल (blood-and-stone) / छारा (ash)
ramacharitamanas::4768.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4768.essence: The battlefield itself seems to collapse into chaos.
ramacharitamanas::4768.simple_meaning: The battlefield suddenly went dark, and blood, stones, and ash began falling like rain.
ramacharitamanas::4768.simple_insight: The scene turns chaotic so fast that even courage has trouble finding footing.
ramacharitamanas::4768.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is raging between Ram's army and Ravana's forces. After the armies clash, the sky itself seems to break: darkness covers everything and a violent shower of blood, stones, and ash falls. It is a battle image, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4768.insight: It heightens the battle scene rather than giving a separate lesson.

ramacharitamanas::4769.verse_sanskrit: देखि निबिड़ तम दसहुँ दिसि कपिदल भयउ खभार। एकहि एक न देखई जहँ तहँ करहिं पुकार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4769.verse_hindi: दसों दिशाओं में अत्यंत घना अंधकार देखकर वानरों की सेना में खलबली पड़ गई। एक को एक (दूसरा) नहीं देख सकता और सब जहाँ-तहाँ पुकार रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4769.english_translation: Seeing dense darkness in all ten directions, the monkey army was thrown into confusion. They could not see one another anywhere and were calling out everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::4769.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / निबिड़ (dense) / तम (darkness) / दसहुँ दिसि (all ten directions) / कपिदल (monkey army) / भयउ (became) / खभार (confused) / एकहि एक (one another) / न देखई (do not see) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / करहिं (they do) / पुकार (calling out)
ramacharitamanas::4769.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4769.essence: When sight disappears, courage turns into confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4769.simple_meaning: The battlefield goes dark, and the monkey army loses its bearings. They cannot see each other and cry out in confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4769.simple_insight: When confusion closes in, even brave people can feel suddenly alone.
ramacharitamanas::4769.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war turns chaotic. Darkness covers the battlefield so completely that the monkey army cannot see one another. Fear spreads through the ranks, and their voices rise in confusion before Ram restores order.
ramacharitamanas::4769.modern_relevance: You open your phone in the middle of a crisis and the messages blur together. Everyone is talking, nobody is clear, and you feel the same panic the army feels here.
ramacharitamanas::4769.insight: It shows how quickly fear spreads when perception fails and coordination breaks down.

ramacharitamanas::4770.verse_sanskrit: सकल मरमु रघुनायक जाना। लिए बोलि अंगद हनुमाना॥ समाचार सब कहि समुझाए। सुनत कोपि कपिकुंजर धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4770.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी सब रहस्य जान गए। उन्होंने अंगद और हनुमान् को बुला लिया और सब समाचार कहकर समझाया। सुनते ही वे दोनों कपिश्रेष्ठ क्रोध करके दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4770.english_translation: Lord Raghunath understood the whole situation. He called Angad and Hanuman, told them everything, and explained the plan. Hearing this, the two best of monkeys rushed forward in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4770.translation_literal: सकल (all) / मरमु (secret / inner matter) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / जाना (knew) / लिए (took) / बोलि (calling) / अंगद (Angad) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / कहि (telling) / समुझाए (explained) / सुनत (on hearing) / कोपि (angrily) / कपिकुंजर (best of monkeys) / धाए (ran)
ramacharitamanas::4770.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4770.essence: Seeing clearly lets the right response rise at once.
ramacharitamanas::4770.simple_meaning: Ram understood the situation, called Angad and Hanuman, explained the news, and sent them rushing out in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4770.simple_insight: Clear leadership means seeing the whole situation and giving others the right task at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::4770.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s darkness, Ram sees through the crisis at once. He calls Angad and Hanuman, gives them the news, and steadies them for action. Their anger turns into movement because his understanding restores direction.
ramacharitamanas::4770.modern_relevance: A group chat is spiralling after bad news, and everyone is guessing wildly. One person reads the full situation, names the facts, and the whole team can move again.
ramacharitamanas::4770.insight: It shows how calm understanding can gather scattered energy into purposeful action.

ramacharitamanas::4771.verse_sanskrit: पुनि कृपाल हँसि चाप चढ़ावा। पावक सायक सपदि चलावा॥ भयउ प्रकास कतहुँ तम नाहीं। ग्यान उदयँ जिमि संसय जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4771.verse_hindi: फिर कृपालु श्री रामजी ने हँसकर धनुष चलाया और तुरंत ही अग्निबाण चलाया, जिससे प्रकाश हो गया, कहीं अँधेरा नहीं रह गया। जैसे ज्ञान के उदय होने पर (सब प्रकार के) संदेह दूर हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4771.english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord Ram smiled, raised his bow, and at once launched a fire-arrow. Light spread everywhere; no darkness remained. Just as doubt disappears when knowledge rises, all gloom vanished.
ramacharitamanas::4771.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / कृपाल (the compassionate one) / हँसि (smiling) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ावा (raised) / पावक (fire) / सायक (arrow) / सपदि (at once) / चलावा (launched) / भयउ (became) / प्रकास (light) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / तम (darkness) / नाहीं (not) / ग्यान (knowledge) / उदयँ (on rising) / जिमि (just as) / संसय (doubt) / जाहीं (go away)
ramacharitamanas::4771.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4771.essence: Clear seeing can end confusion as suddenly as light ends darkness.
ramacharitamanas::4771.simple_meaning: Ram fires a blazing arrow, and the darkness disappears. The verse compares that sudden light to how rising understanding clears away doubt.
ramacharitamanas::4771.simple_insight: A clear mind can change everything in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::4771.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army has been thrown into panic by a thick darkness. Ram calmly raises his bow and releases a fire-arrow. The darkness lifts at once, and the verse explains the moment as the arrival of knowledge dispelling confusion.
ramacharitamanas::4771.modern_relevance: You stare at a problem until it feels sealed shut, then one clear insight arrives and the whole situation opens. The fear was real; the darkness was not permanent.
ramacharitamanas::4771.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to clear seeing: one true insight can dissolve confusion faster than struggle.

ramacharitamanas::4772.verse_sanskrit: भालु बलीमुख पाई प्रकासा। धाए हरष बिगत श्रम त्रासा॥ हनूमान अंगद रन गाजे। हाँक सुनत रजनीचर भाजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4772.verse_hindi: भालू और वानर प्रकाश पाकर श्रम और भय से रहित तथा प्रसन्न होकर दौड़े। हनुमान् और अंगद रण में गरज उठे। उनकी हाँक सुनते ही राक्षस भाग छूटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4772.english_translation: The bears and monkeys, seeing the light, ran forward free of fatigue and fear. Hanuman and Angad roared in battle; hearing their cry, the night-wanderers fled.
ramacharitamanas::4772.translation_literal: भालु (bears) / बलीमुख (monkey-faced ones) / पाई (having received) / प्रकासा (light) / धाए (ran) / हरष (in joy) / बिगत (without) / श्रम (fatigue) / त्रासा (fear)॥ / हनूमान (Hanuman) / अंगद (Angad) / रन (in battle) / गाजे (roared)॥ / हाँक (battle cry) / सुनत (hearing) / रजनीचर (night-wanderers) / भाजे (fled)॥
ramacharitamanas::4772.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4772.essence: When darkness lifts, courage returns and fear scatters.
ramacharitamanas::4772.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear armies surge forward once they can see clearly. Hanuman and Angad roar so fiercely that the enemy runs away.
ramacharitamanas::4772.simple_insight: Clear vision and courage can turn hesitation into momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4772.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final battle, Ram’s fiery arrow has just lit the darkness. The monkey and bear warriors, no longer blinded, rush ahead with fresh energy. Hanuman and Angad thunder in the front line, and the demon army breaks and runs.
ramacharitamanas::4772.modern_relevance: The room goes bright after a power cut, and everyone suddenly moves with purpose. What felt impossible a moment ago becomes simple once fear and confusion lift.
ramacharitamanas::4772.insight: It shows how clarity restores courage and makes decisive action possible.

ramacharitamanas::4773.verse_sanskrit: भागत भट पटकहिं धरि धरनी। करहिं भालु कपि अद्भुत करनी॥ गहि पद डारहिं सागर माहीं। मकर उरग झष धरि धरि खाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4773.verse_hindi: भागते हुए राक्षस योद्धाओं को वानर और भालू पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर दे मारते हैं और अद्भुत (आश्चर्यजनक) करनी करते हैं (युद्धकौशल दिखलाते हैं)। पैर पकड़कर उन्हें समुद्र में डाल देते हैं। वहाँ मगर, साँप और मच्छ उन्हें पकड़-पकड़कर खा डालते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4773.english_translation: The fleeing demon warriors are seized and slammed to the ground by the monkeys and bears, who perform astonishing feats. They are grabbed by the feet and thrown into the sea, where crocodiles, serpents, and fish seize and devour them.
ramacharitamanas::4773.translation_literal: भागत (fleeing) / भट (warriors) / पटकहिं (they hurl) / धरि (seizing) / धरनी (the ground) / करहिं (they do) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / अद्भुत (astonishing) / करनी (deeds) / गहि (grabbing) / पद (feet) / डारहिं (they throw) / सागर (sea) / माहीं (into) / मकर (crocodiles) / उरग (serpents) / झष (fish) / धरि धरि (seizing again and again) / खाहीं (eat)
ramacharitamanas::4773.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4773.essence: Defeat becomes total when retreat itself turns into danger.
ramacharitamanas::4773.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears overpower the fleeing warriors, throw them down, and even cast some into the sea, where sea creatures attack them.
ramacharitamanas::4773.simple_insight: Sometimes fear collapses when courage keeps pressing forward.
ramacharitamanas::4773.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has turned sharply against Ravana's forces. As the monkeys and bears surge ahead, the enemy breaks and runs. This verse records the rout in vivid detail, showing the chaos of defeat rather than a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4773.modern_relevance: A crowd panic at a concert exit turns into bodies pushing, stumbling, and scattering. This verse captures the raw moment when control is gone and momentum decides everything.
ramacharitamanas::4773.insight: It shifts attention from heroic combat to the collapse of a losing side under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4774.verse_sanskrit: कछु मारे कछु घायल कछु गढ़ चढ़े पराइ। गर्जहिं भालु बलीमुख रिपु दल बल बिचलाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4774.verse_hindi: कुछ मारे गए, कुछ घायल हुए, कुछ भागकर गढ़ पर चढ़ गए। अपने बल से शत्रुदल को विचलित करके रीछ और वानर (वीर) गरज रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4774.english_translation: Some were killed, some wounded, and some fled to the fort. The bears and monkeys roar, shaking the enemy host with their strength.
ramacharitamanas::4774.translation_literal: कछु (some) / मारे (killed) / कछु (some) / घायल (wounded) / कछु (some) / गढ़ (fort) / चढ़े (climbed) / पराइ (fled) / गर्जहिं (roar) / भालु (bears) / बलीमुख (monkeys of strength) / रिपु (enemy) / दल (host) / बल (strength) / बिचलाइ (shaking)
ramacharitamanas::4774.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4774.essence: The enemy line breaks under relentless force.
ramacharitamanas::4774.simple_meaning: The battle is going badly for Ravana's forces. Some warriors fall, some are hurt, and others flee to the fort while the bears and monkeys keep roaring and driving them back.
ramacharitamanas::4774.simple_insight: Victory often looks like steady pressure, not one dramatic moment.
ramacharitamanas::4774.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is still raging. Ravana's soldiers are being cut down, wounded, or forced back into the fort, while the bears and monkeys roar through the battlefield. This verse simply records the changing tide of combat.
ramacharitamanas::4774.insight: It shows a battle scene in motion, with no separate teaching beyond the fighting.

ramacharitamanas::4775.verse_sanskrit: निसा जानि कपि चारिउ अनी। आए जहाँ कोसला धनी॥ राम कृपा करि चितवा सबही। भए बिगतश्रम बानर तबही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4775.verse_hindi: रात हुई जानकर वानरों की चारों सेनाएँ (टुकड़ियाँ) वहाँ आईं, जहाँ कोसलपति श्री रामजी थे। श्री रामजी ने ज्यों ही सबको कृपा करके देखा त्यों ही ये वानर श्रमरहित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4775.english_translation: When night fell, the four divisions of the monkeys came to where the Lord of Kosala was. As soon as Ram looked on them with grace, all the monkeys became free of fatigue.
ramacharitamanas::4775.translation_literal: निसा (night) / जानि (knowing) / कपि (monkeys) / चारिउ (four) / अनी (divisions) / आए (came) / जहाँ (where) / कोसला धनी (the Lord of Kosala) / राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / करि (having done) / चितवा (looked upon) / सबही (all) / भए (became) / बिगतश्रम (free from fatigue) / बानर (monkeys) / तबही (then)
ramacharitamanas::4775.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4775.essence: Ram's glance ends exhaustion before rest does.
ramacharitamanas::4775.simple_meaning: At night, the four monkey divisions returned to Ram. His gracious glance removed their exhaustion at once.
ramacharitamanas::4775.simple_insight: Rest can arrive the moment you feel truly seen.
ramacharitamanas::4775.detailed_meaning: After the fighting in Lanka, the four monkey divisions return to Ram at night. They are worn out from battle, but Ram's compassionate glance restores them instantly. The verse shows how his presence renews those who serve him.
ramacharitamanas::4775.modern_relevance: You come home drained after carrying everyone else's crisis, and one gentle look from someone you trust makes your shoulders drop. Being seen can restore what effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4775.insight: It shifts attention from heroic strain to the renewing power of grace and belonging.

ramacharitamanas::4776.verse_sanskrit: उहाँ दसानन सचिव हँकारे। सब सन कहेसि सुभट जे मारे॥ आधा कटकु कपिन्ह संघारा। कहहु बेगि का करिअ बिचारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4776.verse_hindi: वहाँ (लंका में) रावण ने मंत्रियों को बुलाया और जो योद्धा मारे गए थे, उन सबको सबसे बताया। (उसने कहा-) वानरों ने आधी सेना का संहार कर दिया! अब शीघ्र बताओ, क्या विचार (उपाय) करना चाहिए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4776.english_translation: There Ravana summoned his ministers and told them about the warriors who had been killed. He said, “The monkeys have destroyed half the army! Speak quickly—what should be done now?”
ramacharitamanas::4776.translation_literal: उहाँ (there) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / सचिव (ministers) / हँकारे (summoned) / सब (all) / सन (to) / कहेसि (he said) / सुभट (great warriors) / जे (who) / मारे (killed) / आधा (half) / कटकु (army) / कपिन्ह (by the monkeys) / संघारा (destroyed) / कहहु (tell) / बेगि (quickly) / का (what) / करिअ (should be done) / बिचारा (deliberation, remedy)
ramacharitamanas::4776.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4776.essence: When pride is wounded, even power starts asking for help.
ramacharitamanas::4776.simple_meaning: Ravana calls his ministers after heavy losses and asks them for a quick plan. The battle has turned badly for him.
ramacharitamanas::4776.simple_insight: Panic grows when pride meets reality and has no answer ready.
ramacharitamanas::4776.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sees his forces breaking under the monkey army's attack. He summons his ministers and admits the damage: half his army is gone. This verse is a tense battlefield setback, setting up the counsel that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4776.modern_relevance: Your team’s biggest client just walked away, and the room goes quiet. Someone finally asks, “What now?” That is Ravana’s moment.
ramacharitamanas::4776.insight: It shifts attention from boasting to damage control, showing how quickly ego must face consequences.

ramacharitamanas::4777.verse_sanskrit: माल्यवंत अति जरठ निसाचर। रावन मातु पिता मंत्री बर॥ बोला बचन नीति अति पावन। सुनहु तात कछु मोर सिखावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4777.verse_hindi: माल्यवंत (नाम का एक) अत्यंत बूढ़ा राक्षस था। वह रावण की माता का पिता (अर्थात् उसका नाना) और श्रेष्ठ मंत्री था। वह अत्यंत पवित्र नीति के वचन बोला- हे तात! कुछ मेरी सीख भी सुनो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4777.english_translation: Malyavant was an extremely old rakshasa. He was Ravana's maternal grandfather and a great minister. He spoke words of very pure policy: "Listen, dear one, and hear some advice from me."
ramacharitamanas::4777.translation_literal: माल्यवंत (Malyavant) / अति (very) / जरठ (old, feeble) / निसाचर (night-walker, rakshasa) / रावन (Ravana's) / मातु (mother's) / पिता (father) / मंत्री (minister) / बर (excellent) ॥ / बोला (spoke) / बचन (words) / नीति (wise conduct, policy) / अति (very) / पावन (pure) / सुनहु (listen) / तात (dear one) / कछु (some) / मोर (my) / सिखावन (instruction) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4777.speaker: Malyavant
ramacharitamanas::4777.essence: Wise advice matters most when pride is about to close the door.
ramacharitamanas::4777.simple_meaning: Malyavant, Ravana's old and respected minister, steps forward to give him wise advice.
ramacharitamanas::4777.simple_insight: Sometimes the clearest warning comes from someone who cares enough to speak plainly.
ramacharitamanas::4777.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana learns how badly the war is going, his elders gather around him. Malyavant, the aged and respected minister, speaks with moral seriousness and tries to guide Ravana away from ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4777.modern_relevance: A senior colleague pulls you aside after a disastrous meeting and says, quietly, "Listen carefully." The advice is hard, but it comes from someone who sees the damage before everyone else does.
ramacharitamanas::4777.insight: It highlights the role of wise counsel before pride hardens into disaster.

ramacharitamanas::4778.verse_sanskrit: जब ते तुम्ह सीता हरि आनी। असगुन होहिं न जाहिं बखानी॥ बेद पुरान जासु जसु गायो। राम बिमुख काहुँ न सुख पायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4778.verse_hindi: जब से तुम सीता को हर लाए हो, तब से इतने अपशकुन हो रहे हैं कि जो वर्णन नहीं किए जा सकते। वेद-पुराणों ने जिनका यश गाया है, उन श्री राम से विमुख होकर किसी ने सुख नहीं पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4778.english_translation: Ever since you carried Sita away, omens have multiplied beyond telling. The Vedas and Puranas sing of Ram’s glory, and no one who turns away from Ram finds peace.
ramacharitamanas::4778.translation_literal: जब ते (since) / तुम्ह (you) / सीता (Sita) / हरि (carried off) / आनी (brought) / असगुन (inauspicious omens) / होहिं (become) / न (not) / जाहिं (go) / बखानी (described) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / जासु (whose) / जसु (glory) / गायो (sang) / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (turned away from) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / सुख (peace) / पायो (found)
ramacharitamanas::4778.speaker: Malyavan
ramacharitamanas::4778.essence: Turning from Ram leaves even victory without peace.
ramacharitamanas::4778.simple_meaning: Ravana is told that taking Sita has brought terrible signs, and that no one who turns away from Ram ever finds lasting peace.
ramacharitamanas::4778.simple_insight: Some choices do not just break rules; they break your own peace.
ramacharitamanas::4778.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has summoned his ministers after heavy losses. The old minister Malyavan warns him that abducting Sita has filled the world with bad omens, and that turning away from Ram never leads to peace. The warning is both political and spiritual.
ramacharitamanas::4778.modern_relevance: You keep ignoring the knot in your stomach after one more dishonest shortcut. The warning signs are not random; they are what it feels like to move against what is right.
ramacharitamanas::4778.insight: It shifts attention from winning at any cost to noticing the inner disorder created by wrong action.

ramacharitamanas::4779.verse_sanskrit: हिरन्याच्छ भ्राता सहित मधु कैटभ बलवान। जेहिं मारे सोइ अवतरेउ कृपासिंधु भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4779.verse_hindi: भाई हिरण्यकशिपु सहित हिरण्याक्ष को बलवान् मधु-कैटभ को जिन्होंने मारा था, वे ही कृपा के समुद्र भगवान् (रामरूप से) अवतरित हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4779.english_translation: The compassionate Lord who killed Madhu and Kaitabha, along with the powerful brothers Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu, has now appeared in Ram's form.
ramacharitamanas::4779.translation_literal: हिरन्याच्छ (Hiranyaksha) / भ्राता सहित (along with the brother) / मधु (Madhu) / कैटभ (Kaitabha) / बलवान (powerful) / जेहिं (whom) / मारे (killed) / सोइ (the same) / अवतरेउ (has descended) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / भगवान (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::4779.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4779.essence: The same compassionate power that ended old dangers has returned in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4779.simple_meaning: Ram is the same compassionate Lord who once destroyed powerful enemies. His descent is not random; it is the return of divine mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4779.simple_insight: You are not meeting an unfamiliar force. The one who protects has always been protecting.
ramacharitamanas::4779.detailed_meaning: In Lankakand, as Ravana's downfall draws near, Tulsidas pauses to remind you who Ram really is. The warrior before Lanka is the same compassionate Lord who had already destroyed mighty enemies in earlier ages.
ramacharitamanas::4779.modern_relevance: When life feels like a fresh crisis, you may forget the strength that has carried you before. This verse reminds you that help can return in a form you recognize only after the fear passes.
ramacharitamanas::4779.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as a new arrival to seeing him as timeless protection in action.

ramacharitamanas::4780.verse_sanskrit: कालरूप खल बन दहन गुनागार घनबोध। सिव बिरंचि जेहि सेवहिं तासों कवन बिरोध ॥
ramacharitamanas::4780.verse_hindi: जो कालस्वरूप हैं, दुष्टों के समूह रूपी वन के भस्म करने वाले (अग्नि) हैं, गुणों के धाम और ज्ञानघन हैं एवं शिवजी और ब्रह्माजी भी जिनकी सेवा करते हैं, उनसे वैर कैसा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4780.english_translation: They are Time itself, the fire that burns the forest of evil, the storehouse of virtues and dense wisdom. Shiva and Brahma serve them—so what enmity can exist with them?
ramacharitamanas::4780.translation_literal: कालरूप (time-form) / खल (evil) / बन (forest) / दहन (burning) / गुनागार (storehouse of virtues) / घनबोध (dense wisdom) / सिव (Shiva) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / जेहि (whom) / सेवहिं (serve) / तासों (with them) / कवन (what) / बिरोध (enmity)
ramacharitamanas::4780.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4780.essence: Even the highest beings serve Ram, so resistance to him is pointless.
ramacharitamanas::4780.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond opposition: he is time, destroyer of evil, full of virtue and wisdom, and even Shiva and Brahma serve him.
ramacharitamanas::4780.simple_insight: It softens pride. When you see who stands before you, resistance loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::4780.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has been warned again and again, but he still clings to hostility. This couplet cuts through that stubbornness by naming Ram's vastness: time itself, destroyer of evil, overflowing with virtue and wisdom, served even by Shiva and Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::4780.modern_relevance: You are arguing with someone who has already shown more patience, restraint, and depth than your anger can match. The better move is not to fight harder, but to recognise what is higher than your ego.
ramacharitamanas::4780.insight: It shifts the mind from defiance to reverence, making opposition feel foolish in the face of greatness.

ramacharitamanas::4781.verse_sanskrit: परिहरि बयरु देहु बैदेही। भजहु कृपानिधि परम सनेही॥ ताके बचन बान सम लागे। करिआ मुँह करि जाहि अभागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4781.verse_hindi: (अतः) वैर छोड़कर उन्हें जानकीजी को दे दो और कृपानिधान परम स्नेही श्री रामजी का भजन करो। रावण को उसके वचन बाण के समान लगे। (वह बोला-) अरे अभागे! मुँह काला करके (यहाँ से) निकल जा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4781.english_translation: Leave hostility, give Sita back, and worship Ram, the compassionate lord and most loving friend. Those words struck Ravana like arrows, and he snapped, “You wretch, get out of my sight!”
ramacharitamanas::4781.translation_literal: परिहरि (giving up) / बयरु (enmity) / देहु (give) / बैदेही (Sita) / भजहु (worship) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / परम (supreme) / सनेही (beloved friend) / ताके (of that) / बचन (words) / बान (arrows) / सम (like) / लागे (seemed) / करिआ (blacken) / मुँह (face) / करि (having done) / जाहि (go) / अभागे (unlucky one)
ramacharitamanas::4781.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4781.essence: Pride makes even saving advice feel like an insult.
ramacharitamanas::4781.simple_meaning: A messenger tells Ravana to end the conflict, return Sita, and turn toward Ram. Ravana takes the advice as an insult and lashes out in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4781.simple_insight: Pride turns even mercy into an attack.
ramacharitamanas::4781.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a messenger confronts Ravana with a final plea: abandon hostility, return Sita, and seek Ram instead. The advice lands like arrows in Ravana's heart, and his furious reply shows how ego cannot hear rescue as rescue.
ramacharitamanas::4781.modern_relevance: Someone finally tells you the honest truth in a tense conversation, and you hear only criticism. The wound is not the words alone — it is the pride that cannot receive them.
ramacharitamanas::4781.insight: It shows how wounded ego converts guidance into offense and blocks repentance.

ramacharitamanas::4782.verse_sanskrit: बूढ़ भएसि न त मरतेउँ तोही। अब जनि नयन देखावसि मोही॥ तेहिं अपने मन अस अनुमाना। बध्यो चहत एहि कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4782.verse_hindi: तू बूढ़ा हो गया, नहीं तो तुझे मार ही डालता। अब मेरी आँखों को अपना मुँह न दिखला। रावण के ये वचन सुनकर उसने (माल्यवान् ने) अपने मन में ऐसा अनुमान किया कि इसे कृपानिधान श्री रामजी अब मारना ही चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4782.english_translation: You are old now; otherwise, I would have killed you. Now do not show me your face again. Hearing these words, Malyavan thought to himself that the Lord of grace must now want Ravana killed.
ramacharitamanas::4782.translation_literal: बूढ़ (old) / भएसि (you have become) / न त (otherwise not) / मरतेउँ (I would have killed) / तोही (you) / अब (now) / जनि (do not) / नयन (eyes/face) / देखावसि (show) / मोही (to me) / तेहिं (then) / अपने (his own) / मन (mind) / अस (thus) / अनुमाना (thought/understood) / बध्यो (to be killed) / चहत (wants) / एहि (this) / कृपानिधाना (Lord of grace)
ramacharitamanas::4782.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4782.essence: Ravana's insult only confirms that his defeat is already near.
ramacharitamanas::4782.simple_meaning: Malyavan hears Ravana's insult and realizes that Ram's hand is now turning toward Ravana's destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4782.simple_insight: Even a boastful threat can reveal the deeper turn of events.
ramacharitamanas::4782.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana hurls contempt at the elder Malyavan after hearing his warning. Malyavan does not answer with pride; he reads the moment clearly and sees that Ravana's end is approaching, because Ram's will is now moving against him.
ramacharitamanas::4782.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone makes one cruel, careless remark. The people who understand the situation know the real story is no longer the insult — it is the collapse that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4782.insight: It shifts attention from Ravana's words to the larger force closing in on him.

ramacharitamanas::4783.verse_sanskrit: सो उठि गयउ कहत दुर्बादा। तब सकोप बोलेउ घननादा॥ कौतुक प्रात देखिअहु मोरा। करिहउँ बहुत कहौं का थोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4783.verse_hindi: वह रावण को दुर्वचन कहता हुआ उठकर चला गया। तब मेघनाद क्रोधपूर्वक बोला- सबेरे मेरी करामात देखना। मैं बहुत कुछ करूँगा, थोड़ा क्या कहूँ? (जो कुछ वर्णन करूँगा थोड़ा ही होगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4783.english_translation: He rose and left, speaking insults. Then Meghnada spoke in anger: "See my feat in the morning. I will do far more than I can even describe."
ramacharitamanas::4783.translation_literal: सो (then) / उठि (rising) / गयउ (went) / कहत (speaking) / दुर्बादा (evil words) / तब (then) / सकोप (with anger) / बोलेउ (spoke) / घननादा (Meghnada)॥ / कौतुक (feat / spectacle) / प्रात (morning) / देखिअहु (see) / मोरा (my) / करिहउँ (I will do) / बहुत (much) / कहौं (I say) / का (what) / थोरा (little) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4783.speaker: Meghnada
ramacharitamanas::4783.essence: Boasting is easiest before the test arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4783.simple_meaning: Meghnada leaves in anger and boasts that the next morning will reveal his power.
ramacharitamanas::4783.simple_insight: Pride speaks before action, but it cannot prove itself by words alone.
ramacharitamanas::4783.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the exchange with Ravana and the elder's rebuke, Meghnada storms out burning with anger. He answers not with reflection but with a boast, promising a display by morning. The verse sets up his overconfidence before the next confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::4783.modern_relevance: You leave the argument fuming and text, "Just wait till tomorrow." The need to prove yourself has already taken over.
ramacharitamanas::4783.insight: It shows how anger turns into boasting, and how ego announces strength before it has done anything.

ramacharitamanas::4784.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुत बचन भरोसा आवा। प्रीति समेत अंक बैठावा॥ करत बिचार भयउ भिनुसारा। लागे कपि पुनि चहूँ दुआरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4784.verse_hindi: पुत्र के वचन सुनकर रावण को भरोसा आ गया। उसने प्रेम के साथ उसे गोद में बैठा लिया। विचार करते-करते ही सबेरा हो गया। वानर फिर चारों दरवाजों पर जा लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4784.english_translation: Hearing his son's words, Ravana felt reassured. He seated him in his lap with affection. While he was thinking, dawn arrived, and the monkeys again moved to the four gates.
ramacharitamanas::4784.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुत (son) / बचन (words) / भरोसा (confidence) / आवा (came) / प्रीति (affection) / समेत (together with) / अंक (lap) / बैठावा (made sit) / करत (doing) / बिचार (thought) / भयउ (became) / भिनुसारा (dawn) / लागे (began) / कपि (monkeys) / पुनि (again) / चहूँ (four) / दुआरा (gates)
ramacharitamanas::4784.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4784.essence: Confidence returns fast, but dawn brings the same pressure back.
ramacharitamanas::4784.simple_meaning: Ravana relaxes after hearing his son's words and holds him affectionately. While he thinks, morning comes, and the monkeys return to the gates.
ramacharitamanas::4784.simple_insight: Even fear can briefly soften when you feel protected by your own side.
ramacharitamanas::4784.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's tense night, Ravana hears his son's assurances and feels his confidence return. He holds him close, but the calm does not last. Dawn breaks, and the monkey army resumes pressure on the fortress gates.
ramacharitamanas::4784.modern_relevance: You finally hear the reassuring text from someone you trust, and your shoulders drop for a moment. Then morning comes, and the problem is still waiting.
ramacharitamanas::4784.insight: It shows how reassurance can steady the mind briefly, even when the larger crisis remains unchanged.

ramacharitamanas::4785.verse_sanskrit: कोपि कपिन्ह दुर्घट गढ़ु घेरा। नगर कोलाहलु भयउ घनेरा॥ बिबिधायुध धर निसिचर धाए। गढ़ ते पर्बत सिखर ढहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4785.verse_hindi: वानरों ने क्रोध करके दुर्गम किले को घेर लिया। नगर में बहुत ही कोलाहल (शोर) मच गया। राक्षस बहुत तरह के अस्त्र-शस्त्र धारण करके दौड़े और उन्होंने किले पर पहाड़ों के शिखर ढहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4785.english_translation: The monkeys, in anger, surrounded the hard-to-approach fortress. The city filled with a great uproar. The demons rushed out carrying many kinds of weapons, and they brought down the fortress peaks from the walls.
ramacharitamanas::4785.translation_literal: कोपि (in anger) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / दुर्घट (hard to assail) / गढ़ु (fortress) / घेरा (surrounded) / नगर (city) / कोलाहलु (uproar) / भयउ (became) / घनेरा (great) / बिबिधायुध (various weapons) / धर (bearing) / निसिचर (demons) / धाए (rushed) / गढ़ (fortress) / ते (from) / पर्बत (mountain) / सिखर (peaks) / ढहाए (brought down)
ramacharitamanas::4785.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4785.essence: Outer defenses break first when the real assault begins.
ramacharitamanas::4785.simple_meaning: The monkeys surrounded Lanka’s fortress, the city erupted in noise, and the defenders rushed out with weapons as the walls were battered.
ramacharitamanas::4785.simple_insight: Pressure exposes what a strong wall can and cannot protect.
ramacharitamanas::4785.detailed_meaning: In the war for Lanka, the monkey army closes in on Ravana’s fortress. The city erupts in panic as demon fighters rush out with weapons and the outer defenses begin to crumble. The verse is a battle transition, not a teaching by itself.
ramacharitamanas::4785.modern_relevance: A crisis hits the building, and everyone starts moving at once — phones ringing, doors opening, people shouting instructions. The calm edge of control is gone, and the real strength of the system shows.
ramacharitamanas::4785.insight: It shifts attention from the fortress’s appearance of strength to how quickly pressure reveals weakness.

ramacharitamanas::4786.verse_sanskrit: ढाहे महीधर सिखर कोटिन्ह बिबिध बिधि गोला चले। घहरात जिमि पबिपात गर्जत जनु प्रलय के बादले॥ मर्कट बिकट भट जुटत कटत न लटत तन जर्जर भए। गहि सैल तेहि गढ़ पर चलावहि जहँ सो तहँ निसिचर हए॥
ramacharitamanas::4786.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पर्वतों के करोड़ों शिखर ढहाए, अनेक प्रकार से गोले चलने लगे। वे गोले ऐसा घहराते हैं जैसे वज्रपात हुआ हो (बिजली गिरी हो) और योद्धा ऐसे गरजते हैं, मानो प्रलयकाल के बादल हों। विकट वानर योद्धा भिड़ते हैं, कट जाते हैं (घायल हो जाते हैं), उनके शरीर जर्जर (चलनी) हो जाते हैं, तब भी वे लटते नहीं (हिम्मत नहीं हारते)। वे पहाड़ उठाकर उसे किले पर फेंकते हैं। राक्षस जहाँ के तहाँ (जो जहाँ होते हैं, वहीं) मारे जाते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::4786.english_translation: They toppled mountain peaks and launched countless kinds of missiles. The missiles roared like thunderbolts and rumbled like clouds of destruction. Fierce monkey warriors clashed, their bodies torn and battered, yet they did not fall back. They lifted mountains and hurled them at the fort, and the demons were struck down wherever they stood.
ramacharitamanas::4786.translation_literal: ढाहे (toppled) / महीधर (mountains) / सिखर (peaks) / कोटिन्ह (by the millions) / बिबिध बिधि (in many ways) / गोला (missiles) / चले (were launched) / घहरात (roaring) / जिमि (like) / पबिपात (thunderbolts) / गर्जत (rumbling) / जनु (as if) / प्रलय के बादले (clouds of destruction) / मर्कट (monkey warriors) / बिकट (fierce) / भट (warriors) / जुटत (clashing) / कटत (cut and wounded) / न लटत (did not fall back) / तन जर्जर भए (their bodies became battered) / गहि (lifting) / सैल (mountains) / तेहि गढ़ (at that fort) / पर चलावहि (they hurled) / जहँ सो तहँ (wherever) / निसिचर (demons) / हए (were slain)
ramacharitamanas::4786.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4786.essence: Pressure does not end the fight when resolve is still standing.
ramacharitamanas::4786.simple_meaning: The battle turns fierce. Mountains become weapons, missiles fill the sky, and the monkey warriors keep fighting even while badly wounded.
ramacharitamanas::4786.simple_insight: Courage is not the absence of damage; it is refusing to back away while hurt.
ramacharitamanas::4786.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the siege has begun. Monkey warriors press the fortress with mountains and missiles while the demon defenders answer in chaos. This verse is battlefield motion, showing the scale and fury of the war before the next commander steps forward.
ramacharitamanas::4786.modern_relevance: A project is collapsing around you, deadlines are exploding, and you keep working through the damage because quitting would cost everyone more. This is sheer pressure without pause.
ramacharitamanas::4786.insight: It shows how relentless effort can continue even when the body is already taking hits.

ramacharitamanas::4787.verse_sanskrit: मेघनाद सुनि श्रवन अस गढ़ पुनि छेंका आइ। उतर् यो बीर दुर्ग तें सन्मुख चल्यो बजाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4787.verse_hindi: मेघनाद ने कानों से ऐसा सुना कि वानरों ने आकर फिर किले को घेर लिया है। तब वह वीर किले से उतरा और डंका बजाकर उनके सामने चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4787.english_translation: When Meghnad heard that the monkeys had again surrounded the fort, the brave warrior came down from the fort and advanced before them, beating his drum.
ramacharitamanas::4787.translation_literal: मेघनाद (Meghnad) / सुनि (having heard) / श्रवन (with ears) / अस (such) / गढ़ (fort) / पुनि (again) / छेंका (surrounded) / आइ (coming) / उतर् यो (came down) / बीर (warrior) / दुर्ग तें (from the fort) / सन्मुख (facing) / चल्यो (went) / बजाइ (beating)
ramacharitamanas::4787.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4787.essence: The warrior leaves the fort and meets danger head-on.
ramacharitamanas::4787.simple_meaning: Meghnad hears the fort is under siege again, comes down from the fort, and marches out boldly to face the attackers.
ramacharitamanas::4787.simple_insight: Some moments are not for hiding. He steps forward when the fight reaches his gate.
ramacharitamanas::4787.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkeys have returned and surrounded the fortress again. Meghnad, Ravana’s son and a fierce warrior, hears the alarm, descends from the fort, and goes out beating his drum to confront them. The verse is a battle movement, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4787.insight: It marks a combat entrance, showing open challenge rather than retreat.

ramacharitamanas::4788.verse_sanskrit: कहँ कोसलाधीस द्वौ भ्राता। धन्वी सकल लोत बिख्याता॥ कहँ नल नील दुबिद सुग्रीवा। अंगद हनूमंत बल सींवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4788.verse_hindi: (मेघनाद ने पुकारकर कहा-) समस्त लोकों में प्रसिद्ध धनुर्धर कोसलाधीश दोनों भाई कहाँ हैं? नल, नील, द्विविद, सुग्रीव और बल की सीमा अंगद और हनुमान् कहाँ हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4788.english_translation: (Meghnad called out:) Where are the two brothers, the lords of Kosala, the famed archers? Where are Nala, Nila, Dwivid, Sugriva, Angad, and Hanuman, whose strength is beyond measure?
ramacharitamanas::4788.translation_literal: कहँ (where are) / कोसलाधीस (the lord of Kosala) / द्वौ भ्राता (the two brothers) / धन्वी (archers) / सकल (all) / लोत (worlds) / बिख्याता (famous) ॥ / कहँ (where are) / नल (Nala) / नील (Nila) / दुबिद (Dwivid) / सुग्रीवा (Sugriva) / अंगद (Angad) / हनूमंत (Hanuman) / बल (strength) / सींवा (limit) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4788.speaker: Meghnad
