ramacharitamanas::4788.essence: Pride calls out strength because it cannot rest in silence.
ramacharitamanas::4788.simple_meaning: Meghnad taunts the enemy army by asking where Rama, Lakshman, and their strongest allies are. He is trying to provoke them before the fight intensifies.
ramacharitamanas::4788.simple_insight: Boasting often hides fear. The louder the challenge, the more desperate the speaker may be.
ramacharitamanas::4788.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Meghnad stands before the advancing forces and shouts for the heroes by name. He is not teaching anything here; he is mocking the enemy and setting up the next clash as the war tightens around Ravana’s city.
ramacharitamanas::4788.modern_relevance: A person in a tense argument starts listing names, credentials, and strengths just to dominate the room. The words sound bold, but they are really a challenge thrown into the air.
ramacharitamanas::4788.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to confrontation, showing how pride turns speech into a weapon.

ramacharitamanas::4789.verse_sanskrit: कहाँ बिभीषनु भ्राताद्रोही। आजु सबहि हठि मारउँ ओही॥ अस कहि कठिन बान संधाने। अतिसय क्रोध श्रवन लगि ताने ॥
ramacharitamanas::4789.verse_hindi: भाई से द्रोह करने वाला विभीषण कहाँ है? आज मैं सबको और उस दुष्ट को तो हठपूर्वक (अवश्य ही) मारूँगा। ऐसा कहकर उसने धनुष पर कठिन बाणों का सन्धान किया और अत्यंत क्रोध करके उसे कान तक खींचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4789.english_translation: Where is Vibhishana, the brother-betrayer? Today I will surely kill that wicked one. Saying this, he fitted a hard arrow to his bow and, in great rage, drew it back to his ear.
ramacharitamanas::4789.translation_literal: कहाँ (where) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / भ्राताद्रोही (brother-betrayer) / आजु (today) / सबहि (all) / हठि (with stubborn force) / मारउँ (I will kill) / ओही (that one) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / कठिन (hard, firm) / बान (arrow) / संधाने (fitted, strung) / अतिसय (extreme) / क्रोध (anger) / श्रवन (ear) / लगि (up to) / ताने (drew)
ramacharitamanas::4789.speaker: Meghnad
ramacharitamanas::4789.essence: Rage makes a person aim before thinking.
ramacharitamanas::4789.simple_meaning: Meghnad, furious at the battlefield, singles out Vibhishana as a traitor and vows to kill him. He draws his bow back in rage, preparing to fire.
ramacharitamanas::4789.simple_insight: Blind anger narrows the mind until it sees only an enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4789.detailed_meaning: On the walls of Lanka, Meghnad has just mocked the monkey warriors and now turns his fury toward Vibhishana, Ravana's righteous brother. This is not a teaching verse but a surge of battle rage, setting up the deadly arrows that follow.
ramacharitamanas::4789.modern_relevance: You’re in a group chat, and one message makes your chest burn. Before you can think, you’re already typing the reply that will wound back.
ramacharitamanas::4789.insight: It shows how rage turns a person from seeing the whole scene to targeting one name.

ramacharitamanas::4790.verse_sanskrit: सर समूह सो छाड़ै लागा। जनु सपच्छ धावहिं बहु नागा॥ जहँ तहँ परत देखिअहिं बानर। सन्मुख होइ न सके तेहि अवसर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4790.verse_hindi: वह बाणों के समूह छोड़ने लगा। मानो बहुत से पंखवाले साँप दौड़े जा रहे हों। जहाँ-तहाँ वानर गिरते दिखाई पड़ने लगे। उस समय कोई भी उसके सामने न हो सके ॥
ramacharitamanas::4790.english_translation: He loosed a shower of arrows, like many winged snakes racing forth. Monkeys fell everywhere, and no one could face him in that moment.
ramacharitamanas::4790.translation_literal: सर समूह (a shower of arrows) / सो (that) / छाड़ै (he released) / लागा (began) / जनु (as if) / सपच्छ (with wings) / धावहिं (they run) / बहु (many) / नागा (snakes) ॥ / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / परत (falling) / देखिअहिं (were seen) / बानर (monkeys) / सन्मुख (in front) / होइ (becoming) / न सके (could not) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4790.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4790.essence: A storm of force can break a whole line at once.
ramacharitamanas::4790.simple_meaning: He released a deadly rain of arrows. The monkeys fell in every direction, and no one could stand before him.
ramacharitamanas::4790.simple_insight: Some moments are so overwhelming that courage itself scatters.
ramacharitamanas::4790.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, a warrior unleashes a fierce volley of arrows against Ram's army. The monkeys and bears are struck down everywhere, and the scene becomes one of panic and helplessness rather than teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4790.modern_relevance: A meeting turns hostile before you can even answer. The room fills with sharp words, and everyone who came prepared suddenly feels exposed.
ramacharitamanas::4790.insight: It shows the force of a sustained attack and the collapse of resistance under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4791.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ भागि चले कपि रीछा। बिसरी सबहि जुद्ध कै ईछा॥ सो कपि भालु न रन महँ देखा। कीन्हेसि जेहि न प्रान अवसेषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4791.verse_hindi: रीछ-वानर जहाँ-तहाँ भाग चले। सबको युद्ध की इच्छा भूल गई। रणभूमि में ऐसा एक भी वानर या भालू नहीं दिखाई पड़ा, जिसको उसने प्राणमात्र अवशेष न कर दिया हो (अर्थात् जिसके केवल प्राणमात्र ही न बचे हों, बल, पुरुषार्थ सारा जाता न रहा हो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4791.english_translation: The monkeys and bears ran here and there. Everyone forgot the wish to fight. Not a single monkey or bear remained in the battlefield whom he had not reduced to mere breath.
ramacharitamanas::4791.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (here and there) / भागि (having fled) / चले (went) / कपि (monkeys) / रीछा (bears) / बिसरी (was forgotten) / सबहि (to all) / जुद्ध (battle) / कै (of) / ईछा (desire) // सो (that) / कपि (monkey) / भालु (bear) / न (not) / रन (battlefield) / महँ (in) / देखा (seen) / जेहि (whom) / न (not) / प्रान (life-breath) / अवसेषा (left over)
ramacharitamanas::4791.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4791.essence: Overwhelming force can drain courage before the fight is over.
ramacharitamanas::4791.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear warriors flee in fear, and the battle spirit leaves them. The enemy has struck so hard that no one on the field is left with real strength.
ramacharitamanas::4791.simple_insight: Fear can empty even brave hearts when pressure becomes overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::4791.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ravana's side is pressing hard. After a storm of arrows, the monkey and bear warriors scatter in panic. This verse simply records the collapse of their fighting spirit before the next blow lands.
ramacharitamanas::4791.modern_relevance: You were holding it together in a tense room, then one harsh email arrived and everyone went quiet. The energy to keep pushing just vanished.
ramacharitamanas::4791.insight: It shows how momentum can break an entire team when one side dominates relentlessly.

ramacharitamanas::4792.verse_sanskrit: दस दस सर सब मारेसि परे भूमि कपि बीर। सिंहनाद करि गर्जा मेघनाद बल धीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4792.verse_hindi: फिर उसने सबको दस-दस बाण मारे, वानर वीर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। बलवान् और धीर मेघनाद सिंह के समान नाद करके गरजने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4792.english_translation: Then he struck them all with ten arrows each; the monkey warriors fell to the ground. The strong and steady Meghnad roared with a lion's cry.
ramacharitamanas::4792.translation_literal: दस-दस (ten each) / सर (arrows) / सब (all) / मारेसि (struck) / परे (fell) / भूमि (ground) / कपि (monkey) / बीर (warriors) / सिंहनाद (lion-roar) / करि (having done) / गर्जा (roared) / मेघनाद (Meghnad) / बल (strength) / धीर (steady)
ramacharitamanas::4792.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4792.essence: The battle tilts as Meghnad drives the monkey army back.
ramacharitamanas::4792.simple_meaning: Meghnad keeps pressing the monkey army hard, striking them down with many arrows and roaring in triumph.
ramacharitamanas::4792.simple_insight: Sometimes one fierce moment can scatter a whole force.
ramacharitamanas::4792.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Meghnad is overwhelming the monkey warriors with repeated volleys. They are falling back in disorder, and his roar shows his confidence. This is a combat beat, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4792.modern_relevance: When a project collapses under one brutal setback, the scene feels like this: everyone scrambling, one confident voice still pressing forward.
ramacharitamanas::4792.insight: It advances the battle scene by showing Meghnad's dominance and the monkeys' collapse.

ramacharitamanas::4793.verse_sanskrit: देखि पवनसुत कटक बिहाला। क्रोधवंत जनु धायउ काला॥ महासैल एक तुरत उपारा। अति रिस मेघनाद पर डारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4793.verse_hindi: सारी सेना को बेहाल (व्याकुल) देखकर पवनसुत हनुमान् क्रोध करके ऐसे दौड़े मानो स्वयं काल दौड़ आता हो। उन्होंने तुरंत एक बड़ा भारी पहाड़ उखाड़ लिया और बड़े ही क्रोध के साथ उसे मेघनाद पर छोड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4793.english_translation: Seeing his army in distress, Hanuman rushed in fury like death itself. He instantly uprooted a great mountain and hurled it at Meghanada in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4793.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / पवनसुत (Hanuman, son of the wind) / कटक (army) / बिहाला (distressed) / क्रोधवंत (filled with anger) / जनु (as if) / धायउ (rushed) / काला (death)॥ / महासैल (great mountain) / एक (one) / तुरत (immediately) / उपारा (uplifted) / अति (very) / रिस (anger) / मेघनाद (Meghanada) / पर (upon) / डारा (threw)॥
ramacharitamanas::4793.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4793.essence: Hanuman's rage turns instantly into a mountain strike.
ramacharitamanas::4793.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees his side suffering, rushes forward in anger, lifts a mountain, and throws it at Meghanada.
ramacharitamanas::4793.simple_insight: Protective courage can turn grief into immediate action.
ramacharitamanas::4793.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Hanuman sees his army battered and shaken by Meghanada's attack. His anger becomes force: he tears up a mountain and hurls it straight back. This is a combat moment, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4793.insight: It shows Hanuman's battle fury as a response to the army's suffering, not a reflective principle.

ramacharitamanas::4794.verse_sanskrit: आवत देखि गयउ नभ सोई। रथ सारथी तुरग सब खोई॥ बार बार पचार हनुमाना। निकट न आव मरमु सो जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4794.verse_hindi: पहाड़ों को आते देखकर वह आकाश में उड़ गया। (उसके) रथ, सारथी और घोड़े सब नष्ट हो गए (चूर-चूर हो गए) हनुमान् जी उसे बार-बार ललकारते हैं। पर वह निकट नहीं आता, क्योंकि वह उनके बल का मर्म जानता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4794.english_translation: Seeing the mountains coming at him, he flew into the sky. His chariot, charioteer, and horses were all destroyed. Hanuman kept challenging him again and again, but he would not come close, because he knew Hanuman's strength.
ramacharitamanas::4794.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / गयउ (went) / नभ (sky) / सोई (he) / रथ (chariot) / सारथी (charioteer) / तुरग (horses) / सब (all) / खोई (lost) / बार (again) / बार (again) / पचार (challenged) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / निकट (near) / न (not) / आव (come) / मरमु (secret/strength) / सो (that) / जाना (knew)
ramacharitamanas::4794.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4794.essence: Power can end a fight before the next blow falls.
ramacharitamanas::4794.simple_meaning: Meghanad escapes into the sky after his vehicle is destroyed. Hanuman keeps challenging him, but Meghanad stays away because he knows Hanuman's power.
ramacharitamanas::4794.simple_insight: Real strength can make an opponent back away without a second blow.
ramacharitamanas::4794.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is tearing through Ravana's forces. Meghanad's chariot is smashed, and he rises into the sky to avoid Hanuman's reach. This verse keeps the battle moving, showing fear, skill, and tactical retreat.
ramacharitamanas::4794.modern_relevance: You corner someone in an argument, and they suddenly stop posting, stop replying, and vanish. Sometimes retreat is not defeat — it is recognition of force.
ramacharitamanas::4794.insight: It shows how visible strength changes the opponent's choices before the next strike lands.

ramacharitamanas::4795.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति निकट गयउ घननादा। नाना भाँति करेसि दुर्बादा॥ अस्त्र सस्त्र आयुध सब डारे। कौतुकहीं प्रभु काटि निवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4795.verse_hindi: (तब) मेघनाद श्री रघुनाथजी के पास गया और उसने (उनके प्रति) अनेकों प्रकार के दुर्वचनों का प्रयोग किया। (फिर) उसने उन पर अस्त्र-शस्त्र तथा और सब हथियार चलाए। प्रभु ने खेल में ही सबको काटकर अलग कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4795.english_translation: Then Meghnad went close to Raghupati and used many kinds of abusive words. He hurled all sorts of weapons, and the Lord cut them all aside as if in play.
ramacharitamanas::4795.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / निकट (near) / गयउ (went) / घननादा (Meghnad) / नाना भाँति (many kinds) / करेसि (did) / दुर्बादा (abusive speech) / अस्त्र (weapons) / सस्त्र (arms) / आयुध (weapons) / सब (all) / डारे (threw) / कौतुकहीं (as play) / प्रभु (the Lord) / काटि (cut) / निवारे (warded off)
ramacharitamanas::4795.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4795.simple_meaning: Meghnad insults Ram and attacks him with every weapon he has, but Ram dismisses them effortlessly.
ramacharitamanas::4795.simple_insight: Real power does not need to prove itself. It stays calm while aggression spends itself out.
ramacharitamanas::4795.detailed_meaning: In the Lanka war, Meghnad comes close to Ram, hurling insults and every weapon he can muster. Ram does not struggle or panic; he cuts each attack aside with ease. The verse shows Ram's unshaken mastery before the next twist in the battle.
ramacharitamanas::4795.modern_relevance: Someone sends a furious message, piles on criticism, and tries every tactic to provoke you. You answer cleanly, without losing your center.
ramacharitamanas::4795.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to force to meeting force with steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::4796.verse_sanskrit: देखि प्रताप मूढ़ खिसिआना। करै लाग माया बिधि नाना॥ जिमि कोउ करै गरुड़ सैं खेला। डरपावै गहि स्वल्प सपेला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4796.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी का प्रताप (सामर्थ्य) देखकर वह मूर्ख लज्जित हो गया और अनेकों प्रकार की माया करने लगा। जैसे कोई व्यक्ति छोटा सा साँप का बच्चा हाथ में लेकर गरुड़ को डरावे और उससे खेल करे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4796.english_translation: Seeing Ram's power, the fool grew ashamed and began using all kinds of tricks. It was like someone trying to frighten Garuda by holding a tiny snake and playing games.
ramacharitamanas::4796.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / प्रताप (power, glory) / मूढ़ (foolish one) / खिसिआना (becoming ashamed) / करै लाग (began to do) / माया (tricks, illusions) / बिधि (many kinds) / नाना (various) / जिमि (like) / कोउ (someone) / करै (does) / गरुड़ सैं (with Garuda) / खेला (play, game) / डरपावै (tries to frighten) / गहि (holding) / स्वल्प (small) / सपेला (snakelet)
ramacharitamanas::4796.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4796.essence: Small tricks cannot hide a shaken ego.
ramacharitamanas::4796.simple_meaning: Ravana feels humiliated by Ram's power, so he turns to more tricks and illusions. But his efforts are laughably small beside what he is facing.
ramacharitamanas::4796.simple_insight: Ego gets more deceptive when it feels exposed.
ramacharitamanas::4796.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Meghnad has already been pushed back, and the battle is tightening around Ravana's side. Seeing Ram's unmatched power, the foolish enemy grows embarrassed and falls back on cheap tricks. The comparison shows how small his cleverness really is.
ramacharitamanas::4796.modern_relevance: Someone loses an argument, then suddenly starts twisting facts, changing the subject, and making jokes to cover the sting. That scramble is the same old pattern of wounded pride.
ramacharitamanas::4796.insight: It shifts the mind to see deception as a sign of weakness, not strength.

ramacharitamanas::4797.verse_sanskrit: जासु प्रबल माया बस सिव बिरंचि बड़ छोट। ताहि दिखावइ निसिचर निज माया मति खोट ॥
ramacharitamanas::4797.verse_hindi: शिवजी और ब्रह्माजी तक बड़े-छोटे (सभी) जिनकी अत्यंत बलवान् माया के वश में हैं, नीच बुद्धि निशाचर उनको अपनी माया दिखलाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4797.english_translation: Even Shiva and Brahma are under the sway of the mighty veil of appearance; that low-minded demon tries to display his own illusion.
ramacharitamanas::4797.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / प्रबल (mighty) / माया (veil of appearance) / बस (under control) / सिव (Shiva) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / बड़ (great) / छोट (small) / ताहि (that one) / दिखावइ (shows) / निसिचर (demon) / निज (his own) / माया (illusion) / मति (mind/intellect) / खोट (crooked)
ramacharitamanas::4797.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4797.essence: Even powerful beings are touched by illusion; ego only deepens the trap.
ramacharitamanas::4797.simple_meaning: Even the greatest beings are subject to the power of illusion, but Ravana's son still tries to use his own tricks against Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4797.simple_insight: Pride makes a person think their tricks can outmatch reality.
ramacharitamanas::4797.detailed_meaning: In the battle with Ram, Meghnada is attacking with arrogance and magical deception. The poet steps back to show the deeper irony: even Shiva and Brahma are under the power of the great veil of appearance, yet this demon still tries to display his own crooked illusion.
ramacharitamanas::4797.modern_relevance: Someone walks into a meeting thinking clever spin will save them, even though the bigger reality is already against them. The verse exposes how overconfidence turns into self-deception.
ramacharitamanas::4797.insight: It shifts attention from flashy tactics to the limits of ego-driven control.

ramacharitamanas::4798.verse_sanskrit: चौपाई : : नभ चढ़ि बरष बिपुल अंगारा। महि ते प्रगट होहिं जलधारा॥ नाना भाँति पिसाच पिसाची। मारु काटु धुनि बोलहिं नाची ॥
ramacharitamanas::4798.verse_hindi: आकाश में (ऊँचे) चढ़कर वह बहुत से अंगारे बरसाने लगा। पृथ्वी से जल की धाराएँ प्रकट होने लगीं। अनेक प्रकार के पिशाच तथा पिशाचिनियाँ नाच-नाचकर 'मारो, काटो' की आवाज करने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4798.english_translation: He rose into the sky and rained down showers of burning embers. From the earth, streams of water appeared. In many forms, ghosts and female spirits danced, crying, 'Strike! Cut!'
ramacharitamanas::4798.translation_literal: नभ (sky) / चढ़ि (having climbed) / बरष (rained) / बिपुल (many) / अंगारा (burning embers)। / महि (earth) / ते (from) / प्रगट (manifested) / होहिं (became) / जलधारा (streams of water)। / नाना (various) / भाँति (kinds) / पिसाच (ghosts) / पिसाची (female spirits) / मारु (strike) / काटु (cut) / धुनि (cry) / बोलहिं (spoke) / नाची (dancing)
ramacharitamanas::4798.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4798.essence: Fear can dress itself as reality, but it remains illusion.
ramacharitamanas::4798.simple_meaning: The enemy uses illusion to create terrifying sights and sounds in the sky and on the ground, trying to panic the other side.
ramacharitamanas::4798.simple_insight: Fear can be manufactured, but it still loses its power when seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4798.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's side answers defeat with illusion. The sky fills with burning embers, the ground seems to pour water, and frightening spirits dance and shout. It is not wisdom, only panic dressed up as power.
ramacharitamanas::4798.modern_relevance: A rumor starts in a group chat and suddenly everyone is acting like the worst outcome is already here. The pressure feels real, but it may be only noise built from fear.
ramacharitamanas::4798.insight: It shows how panic can create convincing illusions that try to overpower clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::4799.verse_sanskrit: बिष्टा पूय रुधिर कच हाड़ा। बरषइ कबहुँ उपल बहु छाड़ा॥ बरषि धूरि कीन्हेसि अँधिआरा। सूझ न आपन हाथ पसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4799.verse_hindi: वह कभी तो विष्टा, पीब, खून, बाल और हड्डियाँ बरसाता था और कभी बहुत से पत्थर फेंक देता था। फिर उसने धूल बरसाकर ऐसा अँधेरा कर दिया कि अपना ही पसारा हुआ हाथ नहीं सूझता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4799.english_translation: He sometimes rained filth, blood, hair, and bones, and sometimes hurled many stones. Then he scattered dust so thickly that darkness fell and he could not see his own outstretched hand.
ramacharitamanas::4799.translation_literal: बिष्टा (filth) / पूय (pus) / रुधिर (blood) / कच (hair) / हाड़ा (bones) / बरषइ (rains) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / उपल (stones) / बहु (many) / छाड़ा (threw) / बरषि (having rained) / धूरि (dust) / कीन्हेसि (he made) / अँधिआरा (darkness) / सूझ (is seen) / न (not) / आपन (own) / हाथ (hand) / पसारा (outstretched)
ramacharitamanas::4799.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4799.essence: Chaos can blind you before the real fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::4799.simple_meaning: The enemy fills the sky with filthy, frightening illusions until everything becomes hard to see.
ramacharitamanas::4799.simple_insight: Fear grows when confusion is thrown at you faster than you can think.
ramacharitamanas::4799.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s power is shown as a terrifying display of illusion and violence. He hurls filth, stones, and dust to blind the vanara army. This verse is a scene of escalating chaos, not a teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4799.modern_relevance: A group chat explodes with half-truths, screenshots, and panic, and suddenly no one can tell what is real anymore. Confusion itself becomes the weapon.
ramacharitamanas::4799.insight: It shows how disorder can overwhelm judgment before courage even gets a chance to act.

ramacharitamanas::4800.verse_sanskrit: कपि अकुलाने माया देखें। सब कर मरन बना ऐहि लेखें॥ कौतुक देखि राम मुसुकाने। भए सभीत सकल कपि जाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::4800.verse_hindi: माया देखकर वानर अकुला उठे। वे सोचने लगे कि इस हिसाब से (इसी तरह रहा) तो सबका मरण आ बना। यह कौतुक देखकर श्री रामजी मुस्कुराए। उन्होंने जान लिया कि सब वानर भयभीत हो गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4800.english_translation: Seeing the illusion, the monkey warriors grew anxious. They thought, "At this rate, everyone is doomed." Seeing their confusion, Ram smiled. He understood that all the monkeys had become afraid.
ramacharitamanas::4800.translation_literal: कपि (monkey warriors) / अकुलाने (grew agitated) / माया (illusion) / देखें (seeing) / सब (all) / कर (of) / मरन (death) / बना (became) / ऐहि (this) / लेखें (account)॥ / कौतुक (wonder/play) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / भए (became) / सभीत (afraid) / सकल (all) / कपि (monkeys) / जाने (knew)॥
ramacharitamanas::4800.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4800.essence: Fear multiplies in the crowd, but clear seeing remains untouched.
ramacharitamanas::4800.simple_meaning: The monkey warriors panic when they see the illusion, but Ram stays calm and sees their fear at once.
ramacharitamanas::4800.simple_insight: When fear spreads, steady awareness can still see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4800.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana’s sorcery throws the monkey army into confusion. They think the illusion means certain death. Ram watches their fear, smiles, and sees exactly what has happened before the next strike breaks the spell.
ramacharitamanas::4800.modern_relevance: You’re in a crowded room when one person’s panic infects everyone else. The noise rises fast, but the calm person who sees clearly can stop the spiral before it takes over.
ramacharitamanas::4800.insight: It shows the value of clear witnessing under pressure instead of being swallowed by collective fear.

ramacharitamanas::4801.verse_sanskrit: एक बान काटी सब माया। जिमि दिनकर हर तिमिर निकाया॥ कृपादृष्टि कपि भालु बिलोके। भए प्रबल रन रहहिं न रोके ॥
ramacharitamanas::4801.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामजी ने एक ही बाण से सारी माया काट डाली, जैसे सूर्य अंधकार के समूह को हर लेता है। तदनन्तर उन्होंने कृपाभरी दृष्टि से वानर-भालुओं की ओर देखा, (जिससे) वे ऐसे प्रबल हो गए कि रण में रोकने पर भी नहीं रुकते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4801.english_translation: Then Ram cut down all the illusion with a single arrow, just as the sun drives away a mass of darkness. After that, he looked at the monkeys and bears with a merciful glance, and they became so strong that even in battle they could not be held back.
ramacharitamanas::4801.translation_literal: एक (one) / बान (arrow) / काटी (cut) / सब (all) / माया (illusion) / जिमि (as) / दिनकर (the sun) / हर (drives away) / तिमिर (darkness) / निकाया (mass)॥ कृपादृष्टि (merciful glance) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / बिलोके (looked upon) / भए (became) / प्रबल (strong) / रन (battle) / रहहिं (remain) / न (not) / रोके (stopped)
ramacharitamanas::4801.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4801.essence: One clear act can break confusion and restore courage.
ramacharitamanas::4801.simple_meaning: Ram ends the confusion in one stroke, then strengthens his allies with one compassionate glance.
ramacharitamanas::4801.simple_insight: Clear seeing and kindness can change everything faster than force alone.
ramacharitamanas::4801.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana's magic had thrown the monkey army into confusion. Ram answers with one arrow that cuts through the illusion, then steadies Hanuman's side with a merciful look. The verse shows divine power restoring courage before the next fight.
ramacharitamanas::4801.modern_relevance: A panic-filled room can shift in seconds when one calm person sees clearly and speaks with care. The confusion does not always need more noise; sometimes it needs a steady presence.
ramacharitamanas::4801.insight: It teaches you to meet confusion first with clarity, then with encouragement.

ramacharitamanas::4802.verse_sanskrit: आयसु मागि राम पहिं अंगदादि कपि साथ। लछिमन चले क्रुद्ध होइ बान सरासन हाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4802.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी से आज्ञा माँगकर, अंगद आदि वानरों के साथ हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए हुए श्री लक्ष्मणजी क्रुद्ध होकर चले॥।52॥
ramacharitamanas::4802.english_translation: After asking Ram's permission, Lakshman went with Angad and the other monkeys, angry and armed with bow and arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4802.translation_literal: आयसु (permission) / मागि (having asked) / राम पहिं (to Ram) / अंगदादि (Angad and others) / कपि (monkeys) / साथ (with) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / चले (went) / क्रुद्ध होइ (becoming angry) / बान (arrows) / सरासन (bow) / हाथ (in hand)
ramacharitamanas::4802.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4802.essence: True strength waits for the right command before it strikes.
ramacharitamanas::4802.simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Ram for permission, then goes out with Angad and the monkeys, carrying his bow and arrows in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4802.simple_insight: Even anger becomes disciplined when it moves under rightful permission.
ramacharitamanas::4802.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram cuts through the enemy's illusion, Lakshman does not rush ahead on impulse. He first seeks Ram's leave, then goes with Angad and the monkeys, ready for battle. The verse shows obedience, urgency, and controlled force together.
ramacharitamanas::4802.modern_relevance: You are furious after a disrespectful message, but you still pause before replying. Real strength is not raw reaction; it is anger placed under right order.
ramacharitamanas::4802.insight: It teaches you to channel force through permission and purpose, not through impulsive reaction.

ramacharitamanas::4803.verse_sanskrit: छतज नयन उर बाहु बिसाला। हिमगिरि निभ तनु कछु एक लाला॥ इहाँ दसानन सुभट पठाए। नाना अस्त्र सस्त्र गहि धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4803.verse_hindi: उनके लाल नेत्र हैं, चौड़ी छाती और विशाल भुजाएँ हैं। हिमाचल पर्वत के समान उज्ज्वल (गौरवर्ण) शरीर कुछ ललाई लिए हुए है। इधर रावण ने भी बड़े-बड़े योद्धा भेजे, जो अनेकों अस्त्र-शस्त्र लेकर दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4803.english_translation: Their eyes were red, their chests broad, and their arms massive. Their bodies shone like the Himalayas, with a faint flush of red. Meanwhile, Ravana sent out mighty warriors, who rushed forward with many kinds of weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4803.translation_literal: छतज (red) / नयन (eyes) / उर (chest) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाला (vast, broad) / हिमगिरि (Himalaya) / निभ (like) / तनु (body) / कछु (some) / एक (a) / लाला (redness) / इहाँ (here) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / सुभट (warriors) / पठाए (sent) / नाना (many) / अस्त्र (weapons) / सस्त्र (arms/weapons) / गहि (grasping) / धाए (rushed)
ramacharitamanas::4803.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4803.essence: Battle energy rises as both sides rush toward impact.
ramacharitamanas::4803.simple_meaning: The verse describes the two sides of the battle: the fierce appearance of the warriors and Ravana’s troops rushing in with weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4803.simple_insight: It prepares you for conflict by showing how quickly pride turns into force.
ramacharitamanas::4803.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, the warriors are described in vivid detail as they surge forward. Ravana has already sent his strongest fighters, and the scene is building toward open combat, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4803.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the argument starts, and you can feel the tension in everyone’s shoulders. This is the moment before words become impact.
ramacharitamanas::4803.insight: It shifts attention from personalities to the raw momentum of confrontation.

ramacharitamanas::4804.verse_sanskrit: भूधर नख बिटपायुध धारी। धाए कपि जय राम पुकारी॥ भिरे सकल जोरिहि सन जोरी। इत उत जय इच्छा नहिं थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4804.verse_hindi: पर्वत, नख और वृक्ष रूपी हथियार धारण किए हुए वानर 'श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय' पुकारकर दौड़े। वानर और राक्षस सब जोड़ी से जोड़ी भिड़ गए। इधर और उधर दोनों ओर जय की इच्छा कम न थी (अर्थात् प्रबल थी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4804.english_translation: Armed with mountains, nails, and trees, the monkeys charged, crying, 'Victory to Ram.' Monkeys and demons clashed one-to-one, and both sides burned with equal hunger to win.
ramacharitamanas::4804.translation_literal: भूधर (mountain) / नख (nails) / बिटपायुध (tree-weapons) / धारी (bearing) / धाए (rushed) / कपि (monkeys) / जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / पुकारी (calling out) / भिरे (clashed) / सकल (all) / जोरिहि (pair by pair) / सन (with) / जोरी (joined) / इत (here) / उत (there) / जय (victory) / इच्छा (desire) / नहिं (not) / थोरी (small)
ramacharitamanas::4804.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4804.essence: The battle becomes total when both sides fight with everything they have.
ramacharitamanas::4804.simple_meaning: The monkeys rush into battle with whatever weapons they have, shouting Ram's name. On both sides, every fighter is fully committed to winning.
ramacharitamanas::4804.simple_insight: Sometimes courage looks like moving forward with what you have, not waiting for perfect tools.
ramacharitamanas::4804.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has fully broken open. Hanuman's side charges with mountains, nails, and trees as weapons, while the demons meet them face to face. This verse shows the battle at its fiercest, with no pause for reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4804.insight: It shows pure combat momentum: once the clash begins, neither side hesitates or yields.

ramacharitamanas::4805.verse_sanskrit: मुठिकन्ह लातन्ह दातन्ह काटहिं। कपि जयसील मारि पुनि डाटहिं॥ मारु मारु धरु धरु धरु मारू। सीस तोरि गहि भुजा उपारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4805.verse_hindi: वानर उनको घूँसों और लातों से मारते हैं, दाँतों से काटते हैं। विजयशील वानर उन्हें मारकर फिर डाँटते भी हैं। 'मारो, मारो, पकड़ो, पकड़ो, पकड़कर मार दो, सिर तोड़ दो और भुजाऐँ पकड़कर उखाड़ लो' ॥
ramacharitamanas::4805.english_translation: They strike with fists, kicks, and teeth. The victorious monkeys beat them and even shout at them. "Strike, strike; seize, seize; seize and kill; break the head and tear out the arms!"
ramacharitamanas::4805.translation_literal: मुठिकन्ह (with fists) / लातन्ह (with kicks) / दातन्ह (with teeth) / काटहिं (they bite) / कपि (monkeys) / जयसील (victorious, victory-loving) / मारि (having struck) / पुनि (again) / डाटहिं (they scold) / मारु (strike) / मारु (strike) / धरु (seize) / धरु (seize) / धरु (seize) / मारू (kill) / सीस (head) / तोरि (breaking) / गहि (seizing) / भुजा (arms) / उपारू (pull out, uproot)
ramacharitamanas::4805.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4805.essence: The war has become raw, physical, and relentless.
ramacharitamanas::4805.simple_meaning: The monkey warriors attack the enemy with fists, kicks, and bites, then keep pressing the fight with fierce cries.
ramacharitamanas::4805.simple_insight: The scene is pure force and momentum, with no pause for hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4805.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army has fully entered battle. The fighting is chaotic and savage, with bodies striking bodies in every direction. This verse is one beat in the larger war scene, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4805.insight: It shows the battle at its most violent and immediate, before the next wave of destruction.

ramacharitamanas::4806.verse_sanskrit: असि रव पूरि रही नव खंडा। धावहिं जहँ तहँ रुंड प्रचंडा॥ देखहिं कौतुक नभ सुर बृंदा। कबहुँक बिसमय कबहुँ अनंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4806.verse_hindi: नवों खंडों में ऐसी आवाज भर रही है। प्रचण्ड रुण्ड (धड़) जहाँ-तहाँ दौड़ रहे हैं। आकाश में देवतागण यह कौतुक देख रहे हैं। उन्हें कभी खेद होता है और कभी आनंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::4806.english_translation: Such a roar filled the nine divisions of the world. Fierce trunks ran here and there. The hosts of the heavens watched the spectacle from the sky, sometimes stunned, sometimes delighted.
ramacharitamanas::4806.translation_literal: असि (such) / रव (roar, sound) / पूरि रही (was filling) / नव खंडा (the nine divisions) / धावहिं (run) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / रुंड (trunks, headless bodies) / प्रचंडा (fierce) / देखहिं (they see) / कौतुक (wonder, spectacle) / नभ (in the sky) / सुर बृंदा (hosts of radiant beings) / कबहुँक (sometimes) / बिसमय (astonishment) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / अनंदा (joy)
ramacharitamanas::4806.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4806.essence: Violence has become so extreme that even witnesses cannot settle into one feeling.
ramacharitamanas::4806.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so fierce that headless bodies keep moving, and even the beings in the sky watch in shock and wonder.
ramacharitamanas::4806.simple_insight: Some moments are so overwhelming they leave even distant witnesses torn between horror and awe.
ramacharitamanas::4806.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has become utterly wild. Bodies keep moving after death, and the sky-dwellers look down on the chaos with mixed shock and fascination. This verse is a vivid battle-scene detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4806.modern_relevance: A news clip keeps replaying a disaster so extreme that you can’t look away, yet you feel uneasy for watching. The verse captures that split between fascination and dread.
ramacharitamanas::4806.insight: It shifts attention from the fighters themselves to the terrifying spectacle of unchecked violence.

ramacharitamanas::4807.verse_sanskrit: रुधिर गाड़ भरि भरि जम्यो ऊपर धूरि उड़ाइ। जनु अँगार रासिन्ह पर मृतक धूम रह्यो छाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4807.verse_hindi: खून गड्ढों में भर-भरकर जम गया है और उस पर धूल उड़कर पड़ रही है (वह दृश्य ऐसा है) मानो अंगारों के ढेरों पर राख छा रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4807.english_translation: Blood has pooled in the pits and hardened there; dust whirls over it, like ash settling on heaps of embers.
ramacharitamanas::4807.translation_literal: रुधिर (blood) / गाड़ (in pits) / भरि भरि (filling up again and again) / जम्यो (has frozen / hardened) / ऊपर (on top) / धूरि (dust) / उड़ाइ (having blown) / जनु (as if) / अँगार (embers) / रासिन्ह (heaps) / पर (on) / मृतक (dead) / धूम (ash/smoke) / रह्यो (remained) / छाइ (spread over)
ramacharitamanas::4807.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4807.essence: War leaves the ground looking like dying fire.
ramacharitamanas::4807.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so soaked with blood and dust that it looks like ash covering burning coals.
ramacharitamanas::4807.simple_insight: Some scenes are too violent for words; they leave only a stunned silence.
ramacharitamanas::4807.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, the fighting has become so brutal that blood has collected in pits and dust settles over it. Tulsidas lingers on the battlefield’s texture, not to teach a principle, but to show the aftermath of relentless combat.
ramacharitamanas::4807.modern_relevance: You walk past the aftermath of a major accident and see the road marked by shattered glass, dust, and stillness. The mind goes quiet before it can explain anything.
ramacharitamanas::4807.insight: It keeps the moment in view as raw aftermath, not heroic victory.

ramacharitamanas::4808.verse_sanskrit: घायल बीर बिराजहिं कैसे। कुसुमति किंसुक के तरु जैसे॥ लछिमन मेघनाद द्वौ जोधा। भिरहिं परसपर करि अति क्रोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4808.verse_hindi: घायल वीर कैसे शोभित हैं, जैसे फूले हुए पलास के पेड़। लक्ष्मण और मेघनाद दोनों योद्धा अत्यंत क्रोध करके एक-दूसरे से भिड़ते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4808.english_translation: Wounded warriors still look splendid, like blossoming palash trees. Lakshman and Meghnad, both furious, clash with each other.
ramacharitamanas::4808.translation_literal: घायल (wounded) / बीर (warriors) / बिराजहिं (look splendid) / कैसे (how) / कुसुमति (in bloom) / किंसुक (palash) / के (of) / तरु (trees) / जैसे (like) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / मेघनाद (Meghnad) / द्वौ (both) / जोधा (warriors) / भिरहिं (clash) / परसपर (with each other) / करि (doing) / अति (very) / क्रोधा (anger)
ramacharitamanas::4808.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4808.essence: Battle can still look beautiful even while it is savage.
ramacharitamanas::4808.simple_meaning: Even wounded warriors can look striking, like blooming palash trees. Here, Lakshman and Meghnad rush at each other in fierce anger.
ramacharitamanas::4808.simple_insight: The scene is about battle intensity, not inner teaching. It shows how war can be both brutal and strangely vivid.
ramacharitamanas::4808.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, the narration pauses on a fierce duel: Lakshman and Meghnad, both wounded and enraged, charge at one another. The verse paints the battlefield as a living picture rather than offering a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::4808.modern_relevance: You see two exhausted rivals still forcing themselves into one more round, faces set, pride intact. The moment is all collision, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4808.insight: It keeps attention on the clash itself, building the tension before the next blow.

ramacharitamanas::4809.verse_sanskrit: एकहि एक सकइ नहिं जीती। निसिचर छल बल करइ अनीती॥ क्रोधवंत तब भयउ अनंता। भंजेउ रथ सारथी तुरंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4809.verse_hindi: एक-दूसरे को (कोई किसी को) जीत नहीं सकता। राक्षस छल-बल (माया) और अनीति (अधर्म) करता है, तब भगवान् अनन्तजी (लक्ष्मणजी) क्रोधित हुए और उन्होंने तुरंत उसके रथ को तोड़ डाला और सारथी को टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर दिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4809.english_translation: He could not defeat the other. The demon fought with deceit, force, and unrighteousness. Then, in anger, the endless one quickly smashed the chariot and destroyed the charioteer.
ramacharitamanas::4809.translation_literal: एकहि एक (one another) / सकइ नहिं (could not) / जीती (defeat) / निसिचर (demon) / छल (deceit) / बल (force) / करइ (does) / अनीती (unrighteousness) / क्रोधवंत (full of anger) / तब (then) / भयउ (became) / अनंता (the endless one) / भंजेउ (broke) / रथ (chariot) / सारथी (charioteer) / तुरंता (immediately)
ramacharitamanas::4809.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4809.essence: The duel turns savage when deceit meets fury.
ramacharitamanas::4809.simple_meaning: Neither warrior can defeat the other. Meghnada fights with deceit and force, so Lakshman grows fierce and destroys the chariot and charioteer at once.
ramacharitamanas::4809.simple_insight: Some fights stop being fair contests and become pure force against force.
ramacharitamanas::4809.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshman and Meghnada are locked in a brutal duel. The demon keeps using trickery and unrighteous tactics, and the fight escalates until Lakshman strikes hard enough to smash the chariot and kill the charioteer. It is a combat detail, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4809.modern_relevance: A shouting match in a family argument can become the same thing: no one is trying to understand, only to overpower. This verse just drives the clash forward.
ramacharitamanas::4809.insight: It shows the battle escalating from matched strength into destructive retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::4810.verse_sanskrit: नाना बिधि प्रहार कर सेषा। राच्छस भयउ प्रान अवसेषा॥ रावन सुत निज मन अनुमाना। संकठ भयउ हरिहि मम प्राना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4810.verse_hindi: शेषजी (लक्ष्मणजी) उस पर अनेक प्रकार से प्रहार करने लगे। राक्षस के प्राणमात्र शेष रह गए। रावणपुत्र मेघनाद ने मन में अनुमान किया कि अब तो प्राण संकट आ बना, ये मेरे प्राण हर लेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4810.english_translation: Sesha attacked him in many ways. The demon was left with barely any life. Ravana's son thought to himself, "Now my life is in danger; he will take it away."
ramacharitamanas::4810.translation_literal: नाना बिधि (in many ways) / प्रहार (blows, attacks) / कर (doing) / सेषा (Sesha) / राच्छस (demon) / भयउ (became) / प्रान (life-breath) / अवसेषा (left over)॥ / रावन सुत (Ravana's son) / निज (his own) / मन (mind) / अनुमाना (having inferred) / संकठ (danger, crisis) / भयउ (became) / हरिहि (will take away) / मम (my) / प्राना (life-breath) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4810.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4810.essence: The fight turns when the enemy realizes his own life is at stake.
ramacharitamanas::4810.simple_meaning: Laxman keeps pressing the enemy until he is nearly finished. Meghnad realizes his life is now in danger.
ramacharitamanas::4810.simple_insight: Pressure changes everything when the other side finally sees the cost.
ramacharitamanas::4810.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Lakshman is driving Meghnad back with relentless force. Meghnad, Ravana's son, suddenly understands that his own life is slipping away. The verse records that moment of fear, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4810.modern_relevance: A tense meeting turns when the other person realizes you are not bluffing. The room changes the moment the pressure becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::4810.insight: It marks the point where battle pressure becomes personal fear.

ramacharitamanas::4811.verse_sanskrit: बीरघातिनी छाड़िसि साँगी। तेजपुंज लछिमन उर लागी॥ मुरुछा भई सक्ति के लागें। तब चलि गयउ निकट भय त्यागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4811.verse_hindi: तब उसने वीरघातिनी शक्ति चलाई। वह तेजपूर्ण शक्ति लक्ष्मणजी की छाती में लगी। शक्ति लगने से उन्हें मूर्छा आ गई। तब मेघनाद भय छोड़कर उनके पास चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4811.english_translation: Then Meghnad hurled the weapon called Veerghatini. The blazing weapon struck Lakshman in the chest. When the weapon hit him, Lakshman fell unconscious. Then Meghnad, throwing off his fear, came near him.
ramacharitamanas::4811.translation_literal: बीरघातिनी (the warrior-killing weapon) / छाड़िसि (he hurled) / साँगी (the spear-like weapon) / तेजपुंज (a mass of radiance) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / उर (chest) / लागी (struck) / मुरुछा (fainting) / भई (occurred) / सक्ति (the weapon) / के लागें (on striking) / तब (then) / चलि गयउ (he went) / निकट (near) / भय (fear) / त्यागें (having abandoned)
ramacharitamanas::4811.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4811.essence: One blow changes the whole battle’s rhythm.
ramacharitamanas::4811.simple_meaning: Meghnad fires a deadly weapon at Lakshman, knocking him unconscious, and then moves in closer without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4811.simple_insight: Sometimes the turning point comes when fear drops away and action becomes direct.
ramacharitamanas::4811.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Meghnad strikes Lakshman with a blazing weapon called Veerghatini. Lakshman collapses unconscious. Seeing that his blow has landed, Meghnad loses his fear and moves in close, setting up the next crisis in the war.
ramacharitamanas::4811.modern_relevance: A sudden email lands like a blow, and for a moment you go blank. Then the person on the other side keeps pressing forward, and the situation becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::4811.insight: It shows how battle can shift from distance to immediate danger in a single strike.

ramacharitamanas::4812.verse_sanskrit: मेघनाद सम कोटि सत जोधा रहे उठाइ। जगदाधार सेष किमि उठै चले खिसिआइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4812.verse_hindi: मेघनाद के समान सौ करोड़ (अगणित) योद्धा उन्हें उठा रहे हैं, परन्तु जगत् के आधार श्री शेषजी (लक्ष्मणजी) उनसे कैसे उठते? तब वे लजाकर चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4812.english_translation: Even after hundreds of millions of warriors tried to lift him like Meghnad, how could the bearer of the world, Shesh, rise? Ashamed, they turned away.
ramacharitamanas::4812.translation_literal: मेघनाद सम (like Meghnad) / कोटि सत (hundreds of millions) / जोधा (warriors) / रहे उठाइ (kept lifting) / जगदाधार (bearer of the world) / सेष (Shesh) / किमि (how) / उठै (would rise) / चले (went) / खिसिआइ (ashamed)
ramacharitamanas::4812.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4812.essence: True weight cannot be lifted by force.
ramacharitamanas::4812.simple_meaning: Even an endless crowd of warriors cannot lift Lakshman now. The scene ends in shame for the enemy, not victory.
ramacharitamanas::4812.simple_insight: Some strength is beyond force; pride collapses when it meets what it cannot move.
ramacharitamanas::4812.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Lakshman lies after Meghnad’s weapon strikes him. Meghnad sends countless warriors to lift him, but even they cannot move the one who bears the world. Their effort ends in humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::4812.modern_relevance: You keep pushing a locked door with all your strength, then finally step back and realize the problem was never effort alone.
ramacharitamanas::4812.insight: It shifts the mind from brute force to reverence for what cannot be overpowered.

ramacharitamanas::4813.verse_sanskrit: सुनु गिरिजा क्रोधानल जासू। जारइ भुवन चारिदस आसू॥ सक संग्राम जीति को ताही। सेवहिं सुर नर अग जग जाही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4813.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे गिरिजे! सुनो, (प्रलयकाल में) जिन (शेषनाग) के क्रोध की अग्नि चौदहों भुवनों को तुरंत ही जला डालती है और देवता, मनुष्य तथा समस्त चराचर (जीव) जिनकी सेवा करते हैं, उनको संग्राम में कौन जीत सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4813.english_translation: Listen, Girija: whose fire of anger burns the fourteen worlds to ashes, and whom gods, humans, and all beings serve—who can defeat that one in battle?
ramacharitamanas::4813.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / गिरिजा (O Girija) / क्रोधानल (fire of anger) / जासू (whose) / जारइ (burns) / भुवन (worlds) / चारिदस (fourteen) / आसू (in an instant) / सक (all) / संग्राम (battle) / जीति (to defeat) / को (who) / ताही (that one) / सेवहिं (serve) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / अग (and) / जग (world) / जाही (all beings)
ramacharitamanas::4813.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4813.essence: No ordinary force can overcome what all beings already serve.
ramacharitamanas::4813.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati that the one whose anger can burn the worlds and who is served by all beings cannot be defeated in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4813.simple_insight: Power rooted in cosmic force cannot be measured by ordinary standards.
ramacharitamanas::4813.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshman lies struck down. Shiva, speaking to Parvati in the outer frame, points to the deeper truth behind the crisis: the one being praised here is beyond ordinary defeat. The verse lifts the moment from injury to cosmic scale.
ramacharitamanas::4813.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone lashes out, and everyone feels the heat in the air. Some people carry a force so large that casual opposition only reveals how little you can grasp them.
ramacharitamanas::4813.insight: It shifts attention from the visible fight to the deeper power behind the scene.

ramacharitamanas::4814.verse_sanskrit: यह कौतूहल जानइ सोई। जा पर कृपा राम कै होई॥ संध्या भय फिरि द्वौ बाहनी। लगे सँभारन निज निज अनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4814.verse_hindi: इस लीला को वही जान सकता है, जिस पर श्री रामजी की कृपा हो। संध्या होने पर दोनों ओर की सेनाएँ लौट पड़ीं, सेनापति अपनी-अपनी सेनाएँ संभालने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4814.english_translation: Only one who has received Ram's grace can understand this wonder. As evening fell, both armies withdrew, and the commanders began gathering their forces.
ramacharitamanas::4814.translation_literal: यह (this) / कौतूहल (wonder) / जानइ (knows) / सोई (that one) / जा पर (on whom) / कृपा (grace) / राम कै (of Ram) / होई (is)॥ / संध्या (evening) / भय (having come) / फिरि (turning back) / द्वौ (both) / बाहनी (armies) / लगे (began) / सँभारन (to gather) / निज निज (each one's own) / अनी (troops) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4814.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4814.essence: Only grace lets you see the meaning hidden inside the scene.
ramacharitamanas::4814.simple_meaning: Ram's grace lets you understand the wonder of this scene. By evening, both armies pull back and regroup.
ramacharitamanas::4814.simple_insight: Some moments are too large to grasp without grace.
ramacharitamanas::4814.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the day ends and both sides pull back to regroup. Tulsidas pauses the action to say that the full wonder of this war is understood only by Ram's grace, not by ordinary sight.
ramacharitamanas::4814.modern_relevance: You watch a tense meeting end with everyone pretending calm, then feel the room still buzzing afterward. Some situations only make sense when your mind is quiet enough to receive them.
ramacharitamanas::4814.insight: It shifts attention from surface events to the deeper force that makes them intelligible.

ramacharitamanas::4815.verse_sanskrit: व्यापक ब्रह्म अजित भुवनेस्वर। लछिमन कहाँ बूझ करुनाकर॥ तब लगि लै आयउ हनुमाना। अनुज देखि प्रभु अति दुख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4815.verse_hindi: व्यापक, ब्रह्म, अजेय, संपूर्ण ब्रह्मांड के ईश्वर और करुणा की खान श्री रामचंद्रजी ने पूछा- लक्ष्मण कहाँ है? तब तक हनुमान् उन्हें ले आए। छोटे भाई को (इस दशा में) देखकर प्रभु ने बहुत ही दुःख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4815.english_translation: The all-pervading, unborn, unconquerable lord of the universe, compassionate Ram, asked, “Where is Lakshman?” Then Hanuman brought him. Seeing his younger brother in that condition, the Lord felt deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4815.translation_literal: व्यापक (all-pervading) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / अजित (unconquerable) / भुवनेस्वर (lord of the universe) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / कहाँ (where) / बूझ (asked) / करुनाकर (compassionate one) ॥ तब (then) / लगि (until) / लै आयउ (brought) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) । अनुज (younger brother) / देखि (seeing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अति (very) / दुख (sorrow) / माना (felt) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4815.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4815.essence: True greatness still aches for the one it loves.
ramacharitamanas::4815.simple_meaning: Ram is described as the all-pervading lord, yet he still asks where Lakshman is. When Hanuman brings him, Ram is overwhelmed by grief at his brother's condition.
ramacharitamanas::4815.simple_insight: Even the greatest power can feel love as pain when someone precious is hurt.
ramacharitamanas::4815.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the fighting has paused and Lakshman lies badly wounded. Ram, though described as the unconquerable lord of the universe, anxiously asks where his brother is. Hanuman brings Lakshman, and Ram's sorrow shows how deeply he loves him.
ramacharitamanas::4815.modern_relevance: You can hold a whole room together and still feel undone when your brother, child, or closest friend is hurt. Strength does not cancel tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::4815.insight: It shifts the reader from seeing greatness as emotional distance to seeing greatness as deep capacity to care.

ramacharitamanas::4816.verse_sanskrit: जामवंत कह बैद सुषेना। लंकाँ रहइ को पठई लेना॥ धरि लघु रूप गयउ हनुमंता। आनेउ भवन समेत तुरंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4816.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् ने कहा- लंका में सुषेण वैद्य रहता है, उसे लाने के लिए किसको भेजा जाए? हनुमान् जी छोटा रूप धरकर गए और सुषेण को उसके घर समेत तुरंत ही उठा लाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4816.english_translation: Jambavan said, "Sushena the physician lives in Lanka. Who should be sent to bring him?" Hanuman took a small form, went, and quickly brought Sushena along with his house.
ramacharitamanas::4816.translation_literal: जामवंत (Jambavan) / कह (said) / बैद (physician) / सुषेना (Sushena) / लंकाँ (in Lanka) / रहइ (lives) / को (whom) / पठई (send) / लेना (to bring)॥ / धरि (taking) / लघु (small) / रूप (form) / गयउ (went) / हनुमंता (Hanuman) / आनेउ (brought) / भवन (house) / समेत (together with) / तुरंता (immediately) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4816.speaker: Jambavan
ramacharitamanas::4816.essence: Real service is quick, humble, and exactly what the moment needs.
ramacharitamanas::4816.simple_meaning: Jambavan asks who can bring Sushena from Lanka, and Hanuman instantly goes in a small form and returns with him.
ramacharitamanas::4816.simple_insight: Steady courage looks ordinary until the moment it is needed.
ramacharitamanas::4816.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram learns Lakshman has fallen, the allies need a physician fast. Jambavan identifies Sushena as the one who can help. Hanuman shrinks himself, enters the enemy city, and returns at once with the doctor and his household.
ramacharitamanas::4816.modern_relevance: Someone in the group chat says, "We need a specialist now." You don't argue, hesitate, or make it about you. You just go, get what is needed, and come back.
ramacharitamanas::4816.insight: It shifts attention from heroics to useful action done without delay or self-display.

ramacharitamanas::4817.verse_sanskrit: राम पदारबिंद सिर नायउ आइ सुषेन। कहा नाम गिरि औषधी जाहु पवनसुत लेन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4817.verse_hindi: सुषेण ने आकर श्री रामजी के चरणारविन्दों में सिर नवाया। उसने पर्वत और औषध का नाम बताया, (और कहा कि) हे पवनपुत्र! औषधि लेने जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4817.english_translation: Sushena came and bowed his head at Ram's lotus feet. He named the mountain and the herbs, and said, 'Pawanputra, go bring them.'
ramacharitamanas::4817.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / पदारबिंद (lotus feet) / सिर (head) / नायउ (bowed) / आइ (coming) / सुषेन (Sushena) / कहा (said) / नाम (name) / गिरि (mountain) / औषधी (herbs) / जाहु (go) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / लेन (to bring)
ramacharitamanas::4817.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4817.essence: Clear guidance turns grief into the next step.
ramacharitamanas::4817.simple_meaning: Sushena bows to Ram and identifies the mountain and herbs needed to heal Lakshman. Hanuman is then sent to bring them.
ramacharitamanas::4817.simple_insight: Healing begins when the right help is named clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4817.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Lakshman lies wounded and Ram is distressed. Hanuman has already brought the physician Sushena. Now Sushena bows to Ram, identifies the needed mountain and herbs, and sends Hanuman to fetch them. The verse moves the rescue forward.
ramacharitamanas::4817.modern_relevance: When someone is injured or overwhelmed, the turning point is often simple: the right expert, the right diagnosis, the right next step. Relief begins when confusion ends.
ramacharitamanas::4817.insight: It shifts attention from panic to precise action.

ramacharitamanas::4818.verse_sanskrit: राम चरन सरसिज उर राखी। चला प्रभंजनसुत बल भाषी॥ उहाँ दूत एक मरमु जनावा। रावनु कालनेमि गृह आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4818.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों को हृदय में रखकर पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी अपना बल बखानकर (अर्थात् मैं अभी लिए आता हूँ, ऐसा कहकर) चले। उधर एक गुप्तचर ने रावण को इस रहस्य की खबर दी। तब रावण कालनेमि के घर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4818.english_translation: Keeping Ram's lotus feet in his heart, Hanuman, the son of the wind, set off, praising his own strength. Meanwhile, a spy revealed the secret to Ravana, and Ravana came to the house of Kalanemi.
ramacharitamanas::4818.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / सरसिज (lotus) / उर (heart) / राखी (keeping) / चला (went) / प्रभंजनसुत (son of the wind) / बल (strength) / भाषी (speaking)॥ / उहाँ (there) / दूत (spy/messenger) / एक (one) / मरमु (secret) / जनावा (revealed) / रावनु (Ravana) / कालनेमि (Kalanemi) / गृह (house) / आवा (came) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4818.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4818.essence: Hanuman moves forward; Ravana scrambles to respond.
ramacharitamanas::4818.simple_meaning: Hanuman leaves with Ram in his heart, and a spy informs Ravana about the search for the healing herb. Ravana then goes to Kalanemi's house.
ramacharitamanas::4818.simple_insight: Not every movement is wisdom; sometimes events simply set the next turn in motion.
ramacharitamanas::4818.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just been sent to fetch the healing herb for Lakshman. He departs with Ram fixed in his heart, while a spy alerts Ravana to the danger. Ravana rushes to Kalanemi, and the plot tightens.
ramacharitamanas::4818.modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room with one urgent task in mind, while someone else is already calling to block your path. The next obstacle is already moving.
ramacharitamanas::4818.insight: It shifts the scene from Hanuman's confident departure to Ravana's reactive counter-move.

ramacharitamanas::4819.verse_sanskrit: दसमुख कहा मरमु तेहिं सुना। पुनि पुनि कालनेमि सिरु धुना॥ देखत तुम्हहि नगरु जेहिं जारा। तासु पंथ को रोकन पारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4819.verse_hindi: रावण ने उसको सारा मर्म (हाल) बतलाया। कालनेमि ने सुना और बार-बार सिर पीटा (खेद प्रकट किया)। (उसने कहा-) तुम्हारे देखते-देखते जिसने नगर जला डाला, उसका मार्ग कौन रोक सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4819.english_translation: Ravana told him the whole matter. Kalnemi heard it and kept shaking his head in regret. "The one who burned the city before your eyes — who can block his path?"
ramacharitamanas::4819.translation_literal: दसमुख (ten-faced Ravana) / कहा (said) / मरमु (the secret, whole matter) / तेहिं (to him) / सुना (heard) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कालनेमि (Kalnemi) / सिरु (head) / धुना (shook) / देखत (while seeing) / तुम्हहि (you) / नगरु (the city) / जेहिं (who) / जारा (burned) / तासु (his) / पंथ (path) / को (which) / रोकन (to stop) / पारा (able)
ramacharitamanas::4819.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4819.essence: A threat already proven cannot be dismissed.
ramacharitamanas::4819.simple_meaning: Ravana explains the situation to Kalnemi, and Kalnemi admits that the one who burned the city cannot be stopped.
ramacharitamanas::4819.simple_insight: Some dangers are so clear that denial becomes impossible.
ramacharitamanas::4819.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tells Kalnemi what has happened. Kalnemi reacts with alarm and regret, admitting that Hanuman is no ordinary intruder — he has already burned the city. The verse sets up the next response, not a teaching of its own.
ramacharitamanas::4819.modern_relevance: You watch a problem grow past the point of polite denial: the evidence is already smoking in front of you, and everyone knows the easy fix is gone.
ramacharitamanas::4819.insight: It keeps the focus on consequence and recognition, not strategy or moral reflection.

ramacharitamanas::4820.verse_sanskrit: भजि रघुपति करु हित आपना। छाँड़हु नाथ मृषा जल्पना॥ नील कंज तनु सुंदर स्यामा। हृदयँ राखु लोचनाभिरामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4820.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी का भजन करके तुम अपना कल्याण करो! हे नाथ! झूठी बकवाद छोड़ दो। नेत्रों को आनंद देने वाले नीलकमल के समान सुंदर श्याम शरीर को अपने हृदय में रखो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4820.english_translation: Take refuge in Raghupati and do what is good for you. Leave behind false talk, and keep the beautiful dark form of the beloved of the eyes in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::4820.translation_literal: भजि (worship) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / करु (do) / हित (good) / आपना (your own) / छाँड़हु (leave) / नाथ (lord) / मृषा (false) / जल्पना (talking) / नील (blue) / कंज (lotus) / तनु (body) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्यामा (dark-complexioned) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / राखु (keep) / लोचनाभिरामा (delight of the eyes)
ramacharitamanas::4820.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4820.essence: Your real good begins when you turn toward Ram and drop false speech.
ramacharitamanas::4820.simple_meaning: Choose Ram for your own good. Stop empty, false speech. Keep his beautiful form in your heart with love.
ramacharitamanas::4820.simple_insight: There is peace in dropping noise and holding onto what truly matters.
ramacharitamanas::4820.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the search for Sita is moving through danger and deception. This verse cuts through the confusion with a direct appeal: turn to Ram, stop false speech, and keep his beautiful form in your heart as your real refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4820.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a tense argument and know the conversation has turned into posturing. The verse asks you to stop the performance, return to what is good, and hold onto what steadies you.
ramacharitamanas::4820.insight: It shifts attention from verbal display to inward refuge and right action.

ramacharitamanas::4821.verse_sanskrit: मैं तैं मोर मूढ़ता त्यागू। महा मोह निसि सूतत जागू॥ काल ब्याल कर भच्छक जोई। सपनेहुँ समर कि जीतिअ सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4821.verse_hindi: मैं-तू (भेद-भाव) और ममता रूपी मूढ़ता को त्याग दो। महामोह (अज्ञान) रूपी रात्रि में सो रहे हो, सो जाग उठो, जो काल रूपी सर्प का भी भक्षक है, कहीं स्वप्न में भी वह रण में जीता जा सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4821.english_translation: Give up the delusion of “I” and “mine.” Wake up from the night of deep confusion. Can the one who is devoured by Time, the serpent, ever win a battle, even in a dream?
ramacharitamanas::4821.translation_literal: मैं तैं (I and you / self-other division) / मोर (mine) / मूढ़ता (delusion) / त्यागू (give up) / महा (great) / मोह (delusion) / निसि (night) / सूतत (sleeping) / जागू (wake up) / काल (Time) / ब्याल (serpent) / कर (of) / भच्छक (devourer) / जोई (who) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / समर (battle) / कि (whether) / जीतिअ (is won) / सोई (that one)
ramacharitamanas::4821.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4821.essence: Ego sleeps through danger; clear seeing wakes before it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4821.simple_meaning: Let go of ego and possessiveness. Stay awake in awareness, because someone lost in confusion cannot win against Time.
ramacharitamanas::4821.simple_insight: There’s strength in seeing clearly before the fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::4821.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has exposed the truth and warned Ravana’s side to turn back. Now this verse cuts through delusion itself: the mind clinging to “I” and “mine” is already asleep, and such a person cannot defeat Time.
ramacharitamanas::4821.modern_relevance: You keep replaying a fight in your head after the meeting is over, still defending your pride. The real loss happened earlier, when you stopped seeing clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4821.insight: It shifts you from ego-driven reaction to clear seeing before action.

ramacharitamanas::4822.verse_sanskrit: सुनि दसकंठ रिसान अति तेहिं मन कीन्ह बिचार। राम दूत कर मरौं बरु यह खल रत मल भार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4822.verse_hindi: उसकी ये बातें सुनकर रावण बहुत ही क्रोधित हुआ। तब कालनेमि ने मन में विचार किया कि (इसके हाथ से मरने की अपेक्षा) श्री रामजी के दूत के हाथ से ही मरूँ तो अच्छा है। यह दुष्ट तो पाप समूह में रत है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4822.english_translation: Hearing this, Ravana became very angry. Then he thought: better to die at the hands of Rama's messenger than by this wretch, who is steeped in filth and evil.
ramacharitamanas::4822.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / दसकंठ (Ravana) / रिसान (became angry) / अति (greatly) / तेहिं (then) / मन (in mind) / कीन्ह (made) / बिचार (thought) / राम दूत (Rama's messenger) / कर (by hand of) / मरौं (let me die) / बरु (better) / यह (this) / खल (wicked one) / रत (engaged) / मल (filth) / भार (mass)
ramacharitamanas::4822.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4822.essence: Pride would rather face death than accept insult.
ramacharitamanas::4822.simple_meaning: Ravana hears the insult and burns with anger. He thinks it would be better to die at the hands of Rama's messenger than by this wicked man's.
ramacharitamanas::4822.simple_insight: Pride can twist even danger into a challenge you would rather face than shame.
ramacharitamanas::4822.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the exchange around Hanuman's message, Ravana's anger flares. The scene is still moving toward confrontation, but this line mainly shows his pride and contempt before the next action begins.
ramacharitamanas::4822.modern_relevance: Someone mocks you in a group chat, and your first impulse is not safety but pride. You'd rather face the harder blow than look weak.
ramacharitamanas::4822.insight: It shows how ego can make a person choose danger over humiliation.

ramacharitamanas::4823.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि चला रचिसि मग माया। सर मंदिर बर बाग बनाया॥ मारुतसुत देखा सुभ आश्रम। मुनिहि बूझि जल पियौं जाइ श्रम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4823.verse_hindi: वह मन ही मन ऐसा कहकर चला और उसने मार्ग में माया रची। तालाब, मंदिर और सुंदर बाग बनाया। हनुमान् जी ने सुंदर आश्रम देखकर सोचा कि मुनि से पूछकर जल पी लूँ, जिससे थकावट दूर हो जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4823.english_translation: Saying this to himself, he went on and created an illusion along the road. He made a lake, a temple, and a beautiful garden. Seeing the lovely hermitage, Hanuman thought, "Let me ask the sage and drink water, so I can rest from my fatigue."
ramacharitamanas::4823.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / चला (went) / रचिसि (created) / मग (on the road) / माया (illusion) / सर (lake) / मंदिर (temple) / बर (fine) / बाग (garden) / बनाया (made) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind) / देखा (saw) / सुभ (beautiful) / आश्रम (hermitage) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / बूझि (asking) / जल (water) / पियौं (I may drink) / जाइ (going) / श्रम (fatigue)
ramacharitamanas::4823.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4823.essence: A pleasant appearance can hide a trap.
ramacharitamanas::4823.simple_meaning: A demon disguises his trickery as a peaceful hermitage to trap Hanuman. Hanuman, tired from travel, sees the place as a chance to rest and ask for water.
ramacharitamanas::4823.simple_insight: Not every peaceful-looking place is safe; tiredness can make deception easier to miss.
ramacharitamanas::4823.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a demon uses illusion to build a fake lake, temple, and garden beside the road. Hanuman, weary from his search, sees a pleasant hermitage and wants to ask for water before resting. The scene is setting up the trap.
ramacharitamanas::4823.modern_relevance: You stop at a roadside café after a long drive, relieved by the quiet and the trees. Sometimes the most welcoming place is designed to lower your guard.
ramacharitamanas::4823.insight: It teaches you to stay alert even when something looks harmless and inviting.

ramacharitamanas::4824.verse_sanskrit: राच्छस कपट बेष तहँ सोहा। मायापति दूतहि चह मोहा॥ जाइ पवनसुत नायउ माथा। लाग सो कहै राम गुन गाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4824.verse_hindi: राक्षस वहाँ कपट (से मुनि) का वेष बनाए विराजमान था। वह मूर्ख अपनी माया से मायापति के दूत को मोहित करना चाहता था। मारुति ने उसके पास जाकर मस्तक नवाया। वह श्री रामजी के गुणों की कथा कहने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4824.english_translation: A demon sat there disguised as a holy man, hoping to delude the divine messenger through his tricks. Hanuman went to him, bowed his head, and began speaking of Ram's virtues.
ramacharitamanas::4824.translation_literal: राच्छस (demon) / कपट (deceit) / बेष (disguise) / तहँ (there) / सोहा (looked splendid) / मायापति (master of illusion) / दूतहि (the messenger) / चह (wanted) / मोहा (to delude) / जाइ (going) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head) / लाग (began) / सो (he) / कहै (to speak) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (song/story)
ramacharitamanas::4824.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4824.essence: False appearances lose power when your mind stays with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4824.simple_meaning: A demon in disguise tries to trick Hanuman, but Hanuman bows first and answers with Ram's praise.
ramacharitamanas::4824.simple_insight: Your devotion can stay steady even in a room built on deception.
ramacharitamanas::4824.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a demon has dressed up like a holy man to trap Hanuman. But Hanuman does not react with fear or suspicion. He bows respectfully, then fills the moment with Ram's name instead of the demon's trap.
ramacharitamanas::4824.modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting where someone is clearly performing sincerity. Instead of getting pulled into the act, you stay respectful, steady, and anchored in what you know is real.
ramacharitamanas::4824.insight: It teaches you to meet deception without losing your center or your devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4825.verse_sanskrit: होत महा रन रावन रामहिं। जितिहहिं राम न संसय या महिं॥ इहाँ भएँ मैं देखउँ भाई। ग्यान दृष्टि बल मोहि अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4825.verse_hindi: (वह बोला-) रावण और राम में महान् युद्ध हो रहा है। रामजी जीतेंगे, इसमें संदेह नहीं है। हे भाई! मैं यहाँ रहता हुआ ही सब देख रहा हूँ। मुझे ज्ञानदृष्टि का बहुत बड़ा बल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4825.english_translation: A great war is raging between Ravana and Ram. Ram will surely win; there is no doubt in this. Here, I can see everything myself, brother. I have great power of wisdom-vision.
ramacharitamanas::4825.translation_literal: होत (is happening) / महा (great) / रन (war) / रावन (Ravana) / रामहिं (for Ram) / जितिहहिं (will win) / राम (Ram) / न (no) / संसय (doubt) / या (in this) / महिं (world) / इहाँ (here) / भएँ (having been) / मैं (I) / देखउँ (see) / भाई (brother) / ग्यान (knowledge) / दृष्टि (vision) / बल (power) / मोहि (to me) / अधिकाई (greatly)
ramacharitamanas::4825.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4825.essence: Clear seeing knows Ram's victory before the battle ends.
ramacharitamanas::4825.simple_meaning: The speaker says Ram is certain to win and claims he can see this clearly through wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::4825.simple_insight: Confidence becomes calm when you see clearly instead of guessing.
ramacharitamanas::4825.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a disguised watcher is trying to mislead Hanuman, but the watcher suddenly reveals a deeper sight. He declares that the war belongs to Ram and that Ram's victory is certain, because wisdom lets him see beyond appearances.
ramacharitamanas::4825.modern_relevance: You are in a room full of confident opinions, but one person quietly sees the larger pattern. Their calm certainty is not arrogance — it comes from seeing past the noise.
ramacharitamanas::4825.insight: It shifts you from reacting to appearances to trusting clear discernment.

ramacharitamanas::4826.verse_sanskrit: मागा जल तेहिं दीन्ह कमंडल। कह कपि नहिं अघाउँ थोरें जल॥ सर मज्जन करि आतुर आवहु। दिच्छा देउँ ग्यान जेहिं पावहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::4826.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने उससे जल माँगा, तो उसने कमण्डलु दे दिया। हनुमान् जी ने कहा- थोड़े जल से मैं तृप्त नहीं होने का। तब वह बोला- तालाब में स्नान करके तुरंत लौट आओ तो मैं तुम्हे दीक्षा दूँ, जिससे तुम ज्ञान प्राप्त करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4826.english_translation: He asked for water, and the being gave him a water pot. Hanuman said he would not be satisfied with so little water. Then the being said, "Bathe in the lake and return quickly; I will give you initiation so you may gain knowledge."
ramacharitamanas::4826.translation_literal: मागा (asked for) / जल (water) / तेहिं (he) / दीन्ह (gave) / कमंडल (water pot) / कह (said) / कपि (the monkey) / नहिं (not) / अघाउँ (satisfied) / थोरें (little) / जल (water) / सर (lake) / मज्जन (bathing) / करि (having done) / आतुर (quickly) / आवहु (come back) / दिच्छा (initiation) / देउँ (I will give) / ग्यान (knowledge) / जेहिं (by which) / पावहु (you may obtain)
ramacharitamanas::4826.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4826.essence: A false teacher offers knowledge as bait.
ramacharitamanas::4826.simple_meaning: The being offers Hanuman a chance to bathe and return for initiation into knowledge, but this is part of a trap, not a teaching for the reader.
ramacharitamanas::4826.simple_insight: Not every promise of guidance is safe; discernment matters before you follow.
ramacharitamanas::4826.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has entered the lake area while searching for Sita. A deceptive figure offers him water and then proposes initiation after a bath. The exchange is bait, leading directly into the next attack by the crocodile-like creature.
ramacharitamanas::4826.modern_relevance: Someone on a crowded train platform offers you a too-helpful shortcut, a free scan, a quick sign-up. The surface kindness hides a trap, and Hanuman’s caution is the skill you need.
ramacharitamanas::4826.insight: It trains you to pause before trusting guidance that arrives from a suspicious place.

ramacharitamanas::4827.verse_sanskrit: सर पैठत कपि पद गहा मकरीं तब अकुलान। मारी सो धरि दिब्य तनु चली गगन चढ़ि जान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4827.verse_hindi: तालाब में प्रवेश करते ही एक मगरी ने अकुलाकर उसी समय हनुमान् जी का पैर पकड़ लिया। हनुमान् जी ने उसे मार डाला। तब वह दिव्य देह धारण करके विमान पर चढ़कर आकाश को चली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4827.english_translation: As Hanuman entered the lake, a crocodile seized his foot in panic. He killed her, and then she took a divine form and rose into the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4827.translation_literal: सर (lake) / पैठत (entering) / कपि (the monkey) / पद (foot) / गहा (seized) / मकरीं (the crocodile) / तब (then) / अकुलान (in panic) / मारी (killed) / सो (that one) / धरि (taking) / दिब्य तनु (divine body) / चली (went) / गगन (sky) / चढ़ि (ascending) / जान (to know)
ramacharitamanas::4827.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4827.essence: The encounter matters, but its meaning is still unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::4827.simple_meaning: Hanuman enters the lake, is seized by a crocodile, kills it, and the crocodile reveals a divine form and ascends into the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4827.simple_insight: The scene moves the story forward; the real meaning comes in the crocodile's later words.
ramacharitamanas::4827.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is testing the strange lake after asking for water. A crocodile grabs his foot, he kills it, and the creature transforms. This is a turning point in the encounter, but the teaching arrives in the next verse.
ramacharitamanas::4827.modern_relevance: A situation turns strange before you understand it: a small danger, a quick response, and only later the reason becomes clear.
ramacharitamanas::4827.insight: It keeps attention on the event itself, not on a lesson that has not yet been spoken.

ramacharitamanas::4828.verse_sanskrit: कपि तव दरस भइउँ निष्पापा। मिटा तात मुनिबर कर सापा॥ मुनि न होइ यह निसिचर घोरा। मानहु सत्य बचन कपि मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4828.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) हे वानर! मैं तुम्हारे दर्शन से पापरहित हो गई। हे तात! श्रेष्ठ मुनि का शाप मिट गया। हे कपि! यह मुनि नहीं है, घोर निशाचर है। मेरा वचन सत्य मानो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4828.english_translation: “By seeing you, O monkey, I have become free of stain. O noble one, the curse of the great sage has been removed. O monkey, this is not a sage; he is a terrible night-wanderer. Believe my words as true.”
ramacharitamanas::4828.translation_literal: कपि (monkey) / तव (your) / दरस (sight) / भइउँ (became) / निष्पापा (free of stain) / मिटा (was removed) / तात (noble one) / मुनिबर (great sage) / कर (of) / सापा (curse) / मुनि (sage) / न (not) / होइ (is) / यह (this) / निसिचर (night-wanderer) / घोरा (terrible) / मानहु (believe) / सत्य (true) / बचन (words) / कपि (monkey) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::4828.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4828.essence: False holiness can be exposed by clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::4828.simple_meaning: The woman says Hanuman's presence has freed her from a curse and revealed the truth: the person before him is not a sage but a dangerous demon.
ramacharitamanas::4828.simple_insight: Clear seeing can break a curse faster than force.
ramacharitamanas::4828.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is testing a strange figure who appears to be a sage. An apsara, freed by his presence, warns him that this is actually a fierce demon in disguise. The verse pushes the scene toward recognition, not combat.
ramacharitamanas::4828.modern_relevance: You meet someone who sounds wise, but something feels off. A single clear warning from a person who has seen more than you can save you from trusting the wrong face.
ramacharitamanas::4828.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to discernment, showing that spiritual danger often hides behind respectable form.

ramacharitamanas::4829.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि गई अपछरा जबहीं। निसिचर निकट गयउ कपि तबहीं॥ कह कपि मुनि गुरदछिना लेहू। पाछें हमहिं मंत्र तुम्ह देहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4829.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर ज्यों ही वह अप्सरा गई, त्यों ही हनुमान् जी निशाचर के पास गए। हनुमान् जी ने कहा- हे मुनि! पहले गुरुदक्षिणा ले लीजिए। पीछे आप मुझे मंत्र दीजिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4829.english_translation: As soon as she left, Hanuman went to the demon. Hanuman said, "O sage, take your guru's fee first; after that, give me the mantra."
ramacharitamanas::4829.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / गई (went) / अपछरा (celestial maiden) / जबहीं (just then) / निसिचर (demon) / निकट (near) / गयउ (went) / कपि (monkey, Hanuman) / तबहीं (then) / कह (said) / कपि (Hanuman) / मुनि (sage) / गुरदछिना (guru's fee) / लेहू (take) / पाछें (afterward) / हमहिं (to me) / मंत्र (mantra) / तुम्ह (you) / देहू (give)
ramacharitamanas::4829.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4829.essence: Power stays clean when humility comes first.
ramacharitamanas::4829.simple_meaning: Hanuman shows humility and respect. Before asking for the mantra, he tells the sage to accept the teacher's fee first.
ramacharitamanas::4829.simple_insight: Real spiritual strength begins with humility, not entitlement.
ramacharitamanas::4829.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has reached a hidden teacher after the strange encounter with the celestial maiden. Instead of demanding help, he bows to proper conduct first: pay the guru's fee, then receive the mantra. His power is wrapped in respect.
ramacharitamanas::4829.modern_relevance: You want a mentor's help, a recommendation, or a new skill, but you show up acting entitled. This verse reminds you that respect opens doors faster than pressure ever will.
ramacharitamanas::4829.insight: It shifts you from grabbing for results to honoring the relationship that makes learning possible.

ramacharitamanas::4830.verse_sanskrit: सिर लंगूर लपेटि पछारा। निज तनु प्रगटेसि मरती बारा॥ राम राम कहि छाड़ेसि प्राना। सुनि मन हरषि चलेउ हनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4830.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने उसके सिर को पूँछ में लपेटकर उसे पछाड़ दिया। मरते समय उसने अपना (राक्षसी) शरीर प्रकट किया। उसने राम-राम कहकर प्राण छोड़े। यह (उसके मुँह से राम-राम का उच्चारण) सुनकर हनुमान् जी मन में हर्षित होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4830.english_translation: Hanuman wrapped his tail around her head and threw her down. As she was dying, she revealed her true demonic form. She gave up her life saying "Ram, Ram." Hearing this, Hanuman's heart filled with joy, and he moved on.
ramacharitamanas::4830.translation_literal: सिर (head) / लंगूर (tail) / लपेटि (wrapping) / पछारा (threw down) / निज (own) / तनु (body) / प्रगटेसि (revealed) / मरती (dying) / बारा (time) / राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / कहि (saying) / छाड़ेसि (gave up) / प्राना (life-breath) / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / हरषि (filled with joy) / चलेउ (moved on) / हनुमाना (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4830.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4830.essence: Ram's name can surface even at the edge of death.
ramacharitamanas::4830.simple_meaning: Hanuman defeats a demon in disguise, and the demon dies calling on Ram. Hanuman feels pleased and continues his search.
ramacharitamanas::4830.simple_insight: Even an enemy's last breath can become a reminder of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4830.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is moving through danger while searching for Sita. He confronts a deceptive being who had hidden her true form. After he defeats her, she dies repeating Ram's name, and Hanuman goes on, heartened by that sound.
