ramacharitamanas::4830.modern_relevance: You finally see through someone's act, and the whole scene changes. Even in conflict, a single sincere word can cut through fear and leave you lighter.
ramacharitamanas::4830.insight: It shifts attention from the fight itself to the unexpected power of Ram's name.

ramacharitamanas::4831.verse_sanskrit: देखा सैल न औषध चीन्हा। सहसा कपि उपारि गिरि लीन्हा॥ गहि गिरि निसि नभ धावक भयऊ। अवधपुरी ऊपर कपि गयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4831.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पर्वत को देखा, पर औषध न पहचान सके। तब हनुमान् जी ने एकदम से पर्वत को ही उखाड़ लिया। पर्वत लेकर हनुमान् जी रात ही में आकाश मार्ग से दौड़ चले और अयोध्यापुरी के ऊपर पहुँच गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4831.english_translation: He could not identify the mountain or the herbs. So Hanuman suddenly lifted the whole mountain. Carrying it, the monkey raced through the night across the sky and reached above Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::4831.translation_literal: देखा (saw) / सैल (mountain) / न (not) / औषध (herbs) / चीन्हा (recognized) / सहसा (suddenly) / कपि (the monkey) / उपारि (upward) / गिरि (mountain) / लीन्हा (took) / गहि (grasping) / गिरि (the mountain) / निसि (night) / नभ (sky) / धावक (racing) / भयऊ (became) / अवधपुरी (Ayodhya city) / ऊपर (above) / कपि (the monkey) / गयऊ (went)
ramacharitamanas::4831.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4831.essence: Service does not wait for perfect certainty.
ramacharitamanas::4831.simple_meaning: Hanuman could not tell which mountain held the healing herbs, so he lifted the entire mountain and flew back across the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4831.simple_insight: When the exact answer is unclear, wholehearted action can still save the day.
ramacharitamanas::4831.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already found Sita and now races back with the healing herb for Lakshman. Unable to identify the right plant on the mountain, he refuses delay and lifts the whole peak, hurrying through the night toward Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::4831.modern_relevance: You are staring at a messy problem and cannot tell which detail matters most. Instead of freezing, you grab the whole thing, move fast, and keep the rescue going.
ramacharitamanas::4831.insight: It shifts you from precision paralysis to decisive service when time matters more than perfect sorting.

ramacharitamanas::4832.verse_sanskrit: देखा भरत बिसाल अति निसिचर मन अनुमानि। बिनु फर सायक मारेउ चाप श्रवन लगि तानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4832.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने आकाश में अत्यंत विशाल स्वरूप देखा, तब मन में अनुमान किया कि यह कोई राक्षस है। उन्होंने कान तक धनुष को खींचकर बिना फल का एक बाण मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4832.english_translation: Bharat saw the huge form and thought it was a demon. He drew his bow to his ear and shot a harmless arrow.
ramacharitamanas::4832.translation_literal: देखा (saw) / भरत (Bharat) / बिसाल (huge) / अति (very) / निसिचर (demon) / मन (mind) / अनुमानि (having judged) / बिनु (without) / फर (fruit) / सायक (arrow) / मारेउ (he shot) / चाप (bow) / श्रवन (ear) / लगि (to) / तानि (drawing)
ramacharitamanas::4832.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4832.essence: First impressions can trigger action before recognition arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4832.simple_meaning: Bharat sees a huge figure in the sky and mistakes it for a demon, so he quickly shoots an arrow without trying to kill.
ramacharitamanas::4832.simple_insight: Even a noble heart can misread a moment when fear and urgency take over.
ramacharitamanas::4832.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been leaping back toward Ram after finding Sita. Bharat sees his enormous shape from afar and assumes danger. He acts at once, but his arrow is harmless, setting up the next moment of recognition.
ramacharitamanas::4832.modern_relevance: You spot a stranger moving fast toward your house at dusk and tense up before you know who it is. The first reaction is often fear, not truth.
ramacharitamanas::4832.insight: It shows how quickly the mind labels the unknown and how action can follow before understanding.

ramacharitamanas::4833.verse_sanskrit: परेउ मुरुछि महि लागत सायक। सुमिरत राम राम रघुनायक॥ सुनि प्रिय बचन भरत तब धाए। कपि समीप अति आतुर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4833.verse_hindi: बाण लगते ही हनुमान् जी 'राम, राम, रघुपति' का उच्चारण करते हुए मूर्च्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। प्रिय वचन (रामनाम) सुनकर भरतजी उठकर दौड़े और बड़ी उतावली से हनुमान् जी के पास आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4833.english_translation: At the strike of the arrow, Hanuman fell unconscious to the ground, chanting, “Ram, Ram, Raghunath.” Hearing those beloved words, Bharat rushed forward and came anxiously to Hanuman’s side.
ramacharitamanas::4833.translation_literal: परेउ (fell) / मुरुछि (unconscious) / महि (to the ground) / लागत (striking) / सायक (arrow) / सुमिरत (remembering, chanting) / राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रिय (dear, beloved) / बचन (words) / भरत (Bharat) / तब (then) / धाए (ran) / कपि (monkey devotee) / समीप (near) / अति (very) / आतुर (anxious) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::4833.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4833.essence: Ram’s name wakes love faster than pain can speak.
ramacharitamanas::4833.simple_meaning: Hanuman collapses while repeating Ram’s name, and Bharat runs to him as soon as he hears those beloved words.
ramacharitamanas::4833.simple_insight: Ram’s name draws care, even in the middle of battle.
ramacharitamanas::4833.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has been struck down in the fighting and falls unconscious while repeating Ram’s name. Bharat hears those cherished words and instantly runs to Hanuman’s side, showing how deeply Ram’s name moves him.
ramacharitamanas::4833.modern_relevance: You hear your child whisper a name you love from the next room, and you drop everything. Some words pull the heart forward before the mind catches up.
ramacharitamanas::4833.insight: It shows how devotion can turn a battlefield into a moment of tenderness and instant response.

ramacharitamanas::4834.verse_sanskrit: बिकल बिलोकि कीस उर लावा। जागत नहिं बहु भाँति जगावा॥ मुख मलीन मन भए दुखारी। कहत बचन भरि लोचन बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4834.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी को व्याकुल देखकर उन्होंने हृदय से लगा लिया। बहुत तरह से जगाया, पर वे जागते न थे! तब भरतजी का मुख उदास हो गया। वे मन में बड़े दुःखी हुए और नेत्रों में (विषाद के आँसुओं का) जल भरकर ये वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4834.english_translation: Seeing Hanuman distressed, Bharata embraced him to his heart. He tried many ways to wake him, but he did not awaken. Bharata's face grew sorrowful. His mind filled with grief, and tears welled in his eyes as he spoke.
ramacharitamanas::4834.translation_literal: बिकल (distressed) / बिलोकि (seeing) / कीस (the monkey) / उर (heart) / लावा (placed) / जागत (waking) / नहिं (not) / बहु भाँति (many ways) / जगावा (woke) / मुख (face) / मलीन (sad) / मन (mind) / भए (became) / दुखारी (grieved) / कहत (speaking) / बचन (words) / भरि (filled) / लोचन (eyes) / बारी (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::4834.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4834.essence: Compassion holds first and speaks later.
ramacharitamanas::4834.simple_meaning: Bharata sees Hanuman in distress, holds him close, and becomes deeply saddened when Hanuman will not wake.
ramacharitamanas::4834.simple_insight: Real care is felt first in the body, then in tears.
ramacharitamanas::4834.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has fallen unconscious after being struck. Bharata rushes to him, lifts him into his arms, and tries everything to wake him. When nothing works, compassion turns into grief, and the next words rise from a heart already breaking.
ramacharitamanas::4834.modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend after bad news, trying every gentle word you know. Nothing changes their face, and your own throat tightens because their pain has become yours.
ramacharitamanas::4834.insight: It shifts attention from fixing someone quickly to staying present with their suffering.

ramacharitamanas::4835.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं बिधि राम बिमुख मोहि कीन्हा। तेहिं पुनि यह दारुन दुख दीन्हा॥ जौं मोरें मन बच अरु काया॥ प्रीति राम पद कमल अमाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4835.verse_hindi: जिस विधाता ने मुझे श्री राम से विमुख किया, उसी ने फिर यह भयानक दुःख भी दिया। यदि मन, वचन और शरीर से श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों में मेरा निष्कपट प्रेम हो, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4835.english_translation: The same fate that turned me away from Ram has now given me this terrible sorrow. If my mind, speech, and body hold pure love for Ram's lotus feet,
ramacharitamanas::4835.translation_literal: जेहिं (by which) / बिधि (fate, arrangement) / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (turned away) / मोहि (me) / कीन्हा (made) / तेहिं (that same) / पुनि (again) / यह (this) / दारुन (terrible) / दुख (sorrow) / दीन्हा (gave) ॥ जौं (if) / मोरें (my) / मन (mind) / बच (speech) / अरु (and) / काया (body) ॥ प्रीति (love) / राम (for Ram) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / अमाया (without deceit, pure)
ramacharitamanas::4835.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::4835.essence: Pain can deepen the love that first seemed to fail.
ramacharitamanas::4835.simple_meaning: Bharat says the same power that kept him away from Ram has now brought this pain. He asks for pure love toward Ram with mind, speech, and body.
ramacharitamanas::4835.simple_insight: Even grief can become a doorway back to wholehearted devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4835.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has fallen unconscious in the battlefield, and Bharat rushes to him with deep concern. In that moment, Bharat speaks from the ache of separation: the force that kept him away from Ram has also brought him suffering. Yet he still asks for pure love at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::4835.modern_relevance: You realize, halfway through a painful mistake, that the same choices that pulled you away from what matters are now teaching you what devotion costs. The wound becomes a reminder of what you still love.
ramacharitamanas::4835.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming events to offering the whole self in devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4836.verse_sanskrit: तौ कपि होउ बिगत श्रम सूला। जौं मो पर रघुपति अनुकूला॥ सुनत बचन उठि बैठ कपीसा। कहि जय जयति कोसलाधीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4836.verse_hindi: और यदि श्री रघुनाथजी मुझ पर प्रसन्न हों तो यह वानर थकावट और पीड़ा से रहित हो जाए। यह वचन सुनते ही कपिराज हनुमान् जी 'कोसलपति श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो, जय हो' कहते हुए उठ बैठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4836.english_translation: If Lord Raghupati is pleased with me, may this monkey be freed from fatigue and pain. Hearing these words, Hanuman rose at once and cried, "Victory to the Lord of Kosala, victory!"
ramacharitamanas::4836.translation_literal: तौ (then) / कपि (monkey) / होउ (may become) / बिगत (without) / श्रम (fatigue) / सूला (pain) / जौं (if) / मो पर (on me) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / अनुकूला (favourable) ॥ / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / उठि (rising) / बैठ (sat up) / कपीसा (lord of monkeys) / कहि (saying) / जय (victory) / जयति (victory) / कोसलाधीसा (Lord of Kosala) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4836.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::4836.essence: Ram's favor restores what effort has spent.
ramacharitamanas::4836.simple_meaning: Hanuman says that if Ram is pleased with him, his fatigue and pain will disappear. Hearing this, he immediately sits up and praises Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4836.simple_insight: Trust can restore strength faster than rest can.
ramacharitamanas::4836.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Bharat has found Hanuman collapsed from strain after carrying news of Sita. Rather than treating him as merely exhausted, he frames relief as Ram's grace. The moment Hanuman hears that, devotion itself lifts him back to life.
ramacharitamanas::4836.modern_relevance: You are drained after helping someone all day, and one kind message makes you sit up straighter. Being seen with love can restore energy that effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::4836.insight: It shifts attention from physical exhaustion to the renewing power of devotion and goodwill.

ramacharitamanas::4837.verse_sanskrit: लीन्ह कपिहि उर लाइ पुलकित तनु लोचन सजल। प्रीति न हृदय समाइ सुमिरि राम रघुकुल तिलक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4837.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने वानर (हनुमान् जी) को हृदय से लगा लिया, उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में (आनंद तथा प्रेम के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। रघुकुलतिलक श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करके भरतजी के हृदय में प्रीति समाती न थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4837.english_translation: Bharat embraced Hanuman to his heart. His body thrilled with joy, his eyes filled with tears. Remembering Ram, the jewel of Raghu's line, love could not fit inside Bharat's heart.
ramacharitamanas::4837.translation_literal: लीन्ह (took) / कपिहि (the monkey, Hanuman) / उर लाइ (placing to the chest, embraced) / पुलकित (thrilled) / तनु (body) / लोचन (eyes) / सजल (wet with tears) / प्रीति (love) / न (not) / हृदय (heart) / समाइ (fit inside) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम (Ram) / रघुकुल तिलक (ornament of the Raghu line)
ramacharitamanas::4837.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4837.essence: True devotion makes the heart too full to contain itself.
ramacharitamanas::4837.simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram is so full that it spills over into tears, joy, and an embrace of Hanuman.
ramacharitamanas::4837.simple_insight: Deep love makes the heart overflow instead of close in on itself.
ramacharitamanas::4837.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's aftermath, Hanuman reaches Bharat with news of Ram. Bharat hugs him like a brother and cannot contain his longing. The sight of Hanuman brings Ram so vividly to mind that Bharat's love breaks into tears.
ramacharitamanas::4837.modern_relevance: You finally hear from someone you have been missing for months, and your whole body reacts before you can speak. The message is not just information; it is presence returning.
ramacharitamanas::4837.insight: It shifts attention from possession to remembrance: love becomes fuller the more vividly you hold Ram in mind.

ramacharitamanas::4838.verse_sanskrit: तात कुसल कहु सुखनिधान की। सहित अनुज अरु मातु जानकी॥ लकपि सब चरित समास बखाने। भए दुखी मन महुँ पछिताने ॥
ramacharitamanas::4838.verse_hindi: (भरतजी बोले-) हे तात! छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण तथा माता जानकी सहित सुखनिधान श्री रामजी की कुशल कहो। वानर (हनुमान् जी) ने संक्षेप में सब कथा कही। सुनकर भरतजी दुःखी हुए और मन में पछताने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4838.english_translation: “Tell me, father, about the well-being of Ram, the treasure of joy, along with Lakshman, Sita, and his younger brother.” Hanuman briefly told the whole story. Hearing it, Bharat became sorrowful and repented in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::4838.translation_literal: तात (father) / कुसल (well-being) / कहु (tell) / सुखनिधान (treasure of joy) / की (of) / सहित (together with) / अनुज (younger brother) / अरु (and) / मातु (mother) / जानकी (Janaki) / लकपि (Hanuman, by context) / सब (all) / चरित (events) / समास (briefly) / बखाने (told) / भए (became) / दुखी (sad) / मन (mind) / महुँ (in) / पछिताने (repented)
ramacharitamanas::4838.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::4838.essence: Love makes distance unbearable, even before reunion arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4838.simple_meaning: Bharat asks after Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Hanuman gives a brief account, and Bharat is overcome with sorrow and regret.
ramacharitamanas::4838.simple_insight: Love can hurt when you realize how much you care too late.
ramacharitamanas::4838.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just reached Bharat with news from Ram. Bharat asks eagerly about Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Hanuman answers in brief, and the little he hears is enough to break Bharat's heart with grief and remorse.
ramacharitamanas::4838.modern_relevance: You finally get the update you were waiting for, and it lands heavier than you expected. Relief and regret arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::4838.insight: It shows how deep attachment makes even good news feel painful when separation has lasted too long.

ramacharitamanas::4839.verse_sanskrit: अहह दैव मैं कत जग जायउँ। प्रभु के एकहु काज न आयउँ॥ जानि कुअवसरु मन धरि धीरा। पुनि कपि सन बोले बलबीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4839.verse_hindi: हा दैव! मैं जगत् में क्यों जन्मा? प्रभु के एक भी काम न आया। फिर कुअवसर (विपरीत समय) जानकर मन में धीरज धरकर बलवीर भरतजी हनुमान् जी से बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4839.english_translation: Alas! Why was I born in this world? I have not been useful in even one task of the Lord. Knowing the wrong moment, Bharata gathered his courage and spoke again to Hanuman.
ramacharitamanas::4839.translation_literal: अहह (alas) / दैव (fate) / मैं (I) / कत (why) / जग (world) / जायउँ (was born) / प्रभु (Lord) / के (of) / एकहु (even one) / काज (task) / न (not) / आयउँ (came) / जानि (knowing) / कुअवसरु (wrong time) / मन (mind) / धरि (holding) / धीरा (steadiness) / पुनि (again) / कपि (to Hanuman) / सन (to) / बोले (spoke) / बलबीरा (mighty hero)
ramacharitamanas::4839.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::4839.essence: Your life feels empty when it serves no one you love.
ramacharitamanas::4839.simple_meaning: Bharat feels he has failed because he has not served Ram in any way. He steadies himself and speaks to Hanuman at the wrong moment, trying to make the next task happen quickly.
ramacharitamanas::4839.simple_insight: Real dignity comes from being useful to what you love, not from status or self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::4839.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Bharat is speaking to Hanuman with urgency after hearing news of Ram and Sita. He is shaken by regret, feeling he has done nothing worthy for Ram. Still, he gathers himself and turns back to the task at hand.
ramacharitamanas::4839.modern_relevance: You finish a long day and realize you were busy, but not truly helpful to anyone who mattered. That quiet sting is Bharat's: the ache of wanting your effort to count for someone you love.
ramacharitamanas::4839.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to useful action for what matters most.

ramacharitamanas::4840.verse_sanskrit: तात गहरु होइहि तोहि जाता। काजु नसाइहि होत प्रभाता॥ चढ़ु मम सायक सैल समेता। पठवौं तोहि जहँ कृपानिकेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4840.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुमको जाने में देर होगी और सबेरा होते ही काम बिगड़ जाएगा। (अतः) तुम पर्वत सहित मेरे बाण पर चढ़ जाओ, मैं तुमको वहाँ भेज दूँ जहाँ कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4840.english_translation: O dear one, if you delay, it will be too late and the task will fail by dawn. Mount the mountain on my arrow, and I will send you to the abode of grace, where Ram dwells.
ramacharitamanas::4840.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / गहरु (delay) / होइहि (will happen) / तोहि (to you) / जाता (going) / काजु (task) / नसाइहि (will fail) / होत (becoming) / प्रभाता (dawn) / चढ़ु (mount) / मम (my) / सायक (arrow) / सैल (mountain) / समेता (together with) / पठवौं (I will send) / तोहि (you) / जहँ (where) / कृपानिकेता (abode of grace)
ramacharitamanas::4840.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::4840.essence: True help moves before the moment is lost.
ramacharitamanas::4840.simple_meaning: Bharat tells Hanuman that there is no time to waste. He must go at once, and Bharat offers to send him quickly to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4840.simple_insight: The right help is urgent help. Love sometimes means moving fast before the moment disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4840.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Bharat speaks to Hanuman with urgency. The task is time-sensitive, and delay would ruin it. Rather than merely advise, Bharat offers immediate help so Hanuman can reach Ram without losing the chance.
ramacharitamanas::4840.modern_relevance: You see the last train pulling away while your friend is still tying their bag. Sometimes care means cutting the hesitation short and getting them moving before the moment is lost.
ramacharitamanas::4840.insight: It teaches you to act decisively when timing matters, and to help others without making them wait.

ramacharitamanas::4841.verse_sanskrit: सुनि कपि मन उपजा अभिमाना। मोरें भार चलिहि किमि बाना॥ राम प्रभाव बिचारि बहोरी। बंदि चरन कह कपि कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4841.verse_hindi: भरतजी की यह बात सुनकर (एक बार तो) हनुमान् जी के मन में अभिमान उत्पन्न हुआ कि मेरे बोझ से बाण कैसे चलेगा? (किन्तु) फिर श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रभाव का विचार करके वे भरतजी के चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4841.english_translation: Hearing this, Hanuman felt pride arise in his mind: how could the arrow move with my weight on it? Then, remembering Ram's power, he bowed at Bharat's feet with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::4841.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / कपि (Hanuman) / मन (mind) / उपजा (arose) / अभिमाना (pride) / मोरें (with me) / भार (weight) / चलिहि (will move) / किमि (how) / बाना (arrow) ॥ / राम (Ram) / प्रभाव (power) / बिचारि (remembering) / बहोरी (again) / बंदि (bowing) / चरन (feet) / कह (said) / कपि (Hanuman) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined)
ramacharitamanas::4841.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4841.essence: Pride fades when you remember the power behind your own strength.
ramacharitamanas::4841.simple_meaning: Hanuman briefly feels proud of his own strength, then remembers Ram's power and humbly bows to Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::4841.simple_insight: Real strength becomes humble the moment you remember its source.
ramacharitamanas::4841.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Bharat has asked Hanuman to carry a mountain on his arrow. For a moment, Hanuman wonders if his own weight will stop the bow. Then remembrance of Ram's power dissolves the pride, and he bows in respect.
ramacharitamanas::4841.modern_relevance: You almost brag about handling the whole project alone, then remember who trained you, supported you, and made the work possible. The chest loosens the moment gratitude returns.
ramacharitamanas::4841.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverence, so ability becomes service instead of ego.

ramacharitamanas::4842.verse_sanskrit: तव प्रताप उर राखि प्रभु जैहउँ नाथ तुरंत। अस कहि आयसु पाइ पद बंदि चलेउ हनुमंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4842.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! हे प्रभो! मैं आपका प्रताप हृदय में रखकर तुरंत चला जाऊँगा। ऐसा कहकर आज्ञा पाकर और भरतजी के चरणों की वंदना करके हनुमान् जी चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4842.english_translation: O Lord, I will keep your glory in my heart and go at once. Saying this, and receiving permission, Hanuman bowed at Bharata's feet and departed.
ramacharitamanas::4842.translation_literal: तव (your) / प्रताप (glory, power) / उर (in the heart) / राखि (keeping) / प्रभु (Lord) / जैहउँ (I will go) / नाथ (O master) / तुरंत (at once) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / आयसु (permission, command) / पाइ (having received) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / चलेउ (went) / हनुमंत (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4842.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::4842.essence: Humility lets devotion move without delay.
ramacharitamanas::4842.simple_meaning: Hanuman says he will carry Bharata's greatness in his heart and leave immediately, after bowing and receiving permission.
ramacharitamanas::4842.simple_insight: True devotion moves quickly, with humility first and delay nowhere.
ramacharitamanas::4842.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just received Bharata's message and his great burden. He overcomes a flicker of pride, remembers Ram's power, bows in respect, and leaves at once. The moment shows how even victory stays humble in service.
ramacharitamanas::4842.modern_relevance: You get praised in the meeting, but you don't linger on it. You thank everyone, do the respectful thing, and get back to the task before the moment turns into ego.
ramacharitamanas::4842.insight: It teaches you to let reverence dissolve pride and turn praise into action.

ramacharitamanas::4843.verse_sanskrit: भरत बाहु बल सील गुन प्रभु पद प्रीति अपार। मन महुँ जात सराहत पुनि पुनि पवनकुमार ॥
ramacharitamanas::4843.verse_hindi: भरतजी के बाहुबल, शील (सुंदर स्वभाव), गुण और प्रभु के चरणों में अपार प्रेम की मन ही मन बारंबार सराहना करते हुए मारुति श्री हनुमान् जी चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4843.english_translation: Hanuman walked on, silently praising Bharat’s strength, character, virtues, and his immense love for the Lord’s feet again and again.
ramacharitamanas::4843.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बाहु-बल (arm-strength) / सील (character) / गुन (virtues) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / अपार (immeasurable) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / जात (going) / सराहत (praising) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पवनकुमार (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4843.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4843.essence: Devotion keeps moving while the mind keeps bowing.
ramacharitamanas::4843.simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps going while admiring Bharat’s strength, good character, virtues, and deep love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4843.simple_insight: True devotion notices greatness in others without stopping its own task.
ramacharitamanas::4843.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just received Bharat’s message and is moving onward in the war-torn world of Lanka. As he travels, he keeps inwardly honoring Bharat’s strength, character, virtues, and devotion to Ram’s feet. The verse is a passing reflection, not a new teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4843.modern_relevance: You leave a difficult conversation and keep replaying the one line that revealed someone’s character. Even while moving forward, your mind keeps bowing to what is noble.
ramacharitamanas::4843.insight: It shows how a devoted mind can stay active while quietly recognising virtue in another person.

ramacharitamanas::4844.verse_sanskrit: उहाँ राम लछिमनहि निहारी। बोले बचन मनुज अनुसारी॥ अर्ध राति गइ कपि नहिं आयउ। राम उठाइ अनुज उर लायउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4844.verse_hindi: वहाँ लक्ष्मणजी को देखकर श्री रामजी साधारण मनुष्यों के अनुसार (समान) वचन बोले- आधी रात बीत चुकी है, हनुमान् नहीं आए। यह कहकर श्री रामजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4844.english_translation: Seeing Lakshman there, Ram spoke as an ordinary human would. "Midnight has passed and Hanuman has not come yet." Saying this, Ram lifted his younger brother and held him to his chest.
ramacharitamanas::4844.translation_literal: उहाँ (there) / राम (Ram) / लछिमनहि (Lakshman) / निहारी (seeing) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / मनुज (human) / अनुसारी (according to) ॥ / अर्ध (half) / राति (night) / गइ (passed) / कपि (monkey) / नहिं (not) / आयउ (came) / राम (Ram) / उठाइ (lifting) / अनुज (younger brother) / उर (chest) / लायउ (brought)
ramacharitamanas::4844.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4844.essence: Love stays tender even in the middle of worry.
ramacharitamanas::4844.simple_meaning: Ram speaks like an ordinary person and hugs Lakshman while waiting for Hanuman to return.
ramacharitamanas::4844.simple_insight: Even the strongest heart can show tenderness while waiting.
ramacharitamanas::4844.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the night has stretched on and Hanuman still has not returned from his mission. Ram looks at Lakshman, speaks in a human way, and draws his brother close. The scene shows worry, love, and the quiet bond between them.
ramacharitamanas::4844.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone at 1:30 a.m., waiting for a message that should have come hours ago. In that restless silence, you want to hold someone close and pretend you are not afraid.
ramacharitamanas::4844.insight: It shifts attention from heroic distance to intimate care under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4845.verse_sanskrit: सकहु न दुखित देखि मोहि काउ। बंधु सदा तव मृदुल सुभाऊ॥ मम हित लागि तजेहु पितु माता। सहेहु बिपिन हिम आतप बाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4845.verse_hindi: (और बोले-) हे भाई! तुम मुझे कभी दुःखी नहीं देख सकते थे। तुम्हारा स्वभाव सदा से ही कोमल था। मेरे हित के लिए तुमने माता-पिता को भी छोड़ दिया और वन में जाड़ा, गरमी और हवा सब सहन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4845.english_translation: Brother, you could never bear to see me in pain. Your nature has always been gentle. For my sake, you left your mother and father and endured the forest's cold, heat, and wind.
ramacharitamanas::4845.translation_literal: सकहु (could bear) / न (not) / दुखित (suffering) / देखि (seeing) / मोहि (me) / काउ (ever) / बंधु (brother) / सदा (always) / तव (your) / मृदुल (gentle) / सुभाऊ (nature) / मम (my) / हित (for the good) / लागि (for) / तजेहु (you left) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) / सहेहु (you endured) / बिपिन (forest) / हिम (cold) / आतप (heat) / बाता (wind)
ramacharitamanas::4845.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4845.essence: Love becomes visible when someone endures hardship for your sake.
ramacharitamanas::4845.simple_meaning: Ram praises Lakshman’s tender nature and remembers how Lakshman left his parents and endured the forest’s hardships for Ram’s sake.
ramacharitamanas::4845.simple_insight: Real love is willing to carry discomfort for someone else without complaint.
ramacharitamanas::4845.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram finds Lakshman wounded and overwhelmed by grief. Before the battle can move forward, Ram remembers Lakshman’s lifelong tenderness and the sacrifices he made to follow him into exile. The verse turns brotherly pain into a measure of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4845.modern_relevance: You stayed up all night with a sibling after a breakup, then went to work exhausted. No one saw the cost, but the love was real. Ram sees that kind of sacrifice completely.
ramacharitamanas::4845.insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to the quiet endurance that proves devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4846.verse_sanskrit: सो अनुराग कहाँ अब भाई। उठहु न सुनि मम बच बिकलाई॥ जौं जनतेउँ बन बंधु बिछोहू। पिता बचन मनतेउँ नहिं ओहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4846.verse_hindi: हे भाई! वह प्रेम अब कहाँ है? मेरे व्याकुलतापूर्वक वचन सुनकर उठते क्यों नहीं? यदि मैं जानता कि वन में भाई का विछोह होगा तो मैं पिता का वचन (जिसका मानना मेरे लिए परम कर्तव्य था) उसे भी न मानता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4846.english_translation: O brother, where is that love now? Why do you not rise at my distressed words? If I had known that exile would mean separation from my brother, I would not have kept my father's word.
ramacharitamanas::4846.translation_literal: सो (that) अनुराग (love/affection) कहाँ (where) अब (now) भाई (brother) / उठहु (rise) न (not) सुनि (hearing) मम (my) बच (words) बिकलाई (distressed, agitated) ॥ / जौं (if) जनतेउँ (had known) बन (forest/exile) बंधु (brother) बिछोहू (separation) / पिता (father) बचन (word) मनतेउँ (I would have kept/obeyed) नहिं (not) ओहू (that too) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4846.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4846.essence: Duty can be obeyed and still break your heart.
ramacharitamanas::4846.simple_meaning: Ram grieves Lakshman’s silence and says he would not have obeyed his father if he had known exile would separate him from his brother.
ramacharitamanas::4846.simple_insight: Love can make duty feel unbearable when it costs you someone you cannot live without.
ramacharitamanas::4846.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Lakshman lies wounded, Ram speaks to him in anguish. He remembers Lakshman’s lifelong devotion and says that if he had known exile would bring this separation, he would not have accepted his father’s command.
ramacharitamanas::4846.modern_relevance: You take a call from the hospital and suddenly every plan feels small. In that moment, duty, family, and love collide exactly the way Ram feels it here.
ramacharitamanas::4846.insight: It shows that even the noblest duty can be pierced by human attachment and grief.

ramacharitamanas::4847.verse_sanskrit: सुत बित नारि भवन परिवारा। होहिं जाहिं जग बारहिं बारा॥ अस बिचारि जियँ जागहु ताता। मिलइ न जगत सहोदर भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4847.verse_hindi: पुत्र, धन, स्त्री, घर और परिवार- ये जगत् में बार-बार होते और जाते हैं, परन्तु जगत् में सहोदर भाई बार-बार नहीं मिलता। हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर हे तात! जागो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4847.english_translation: Children, wealth, wife, house, and family come and go again and again in the world, but a real brother is not found again. Thinking this in your heart, wake up, dear one!
ramacharitamanas::4847.translation_literal: सुत (children) / बित (wealth) / नारि (wife) / भवन (house) / परिवारा (family) / होहिं (come to be) / जाहिं (go away) / जग (world) / बारहिं बारा (again and again)॥ / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / जियँ (in the heart) / जागहु (wake up) / ताता (dear one)॥ / मिलइ (is found) / न (not) / जगत (in the world) / सहोदर (real brother) / भ्राता (brother)॥
ramacharitamanas::4847.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::4847.essence: What is replaceable should not outrank what is rare.
ramacharitamanas::4847.simple_meaning: Worldly things like children, wealth, wife, house, and family keep coming and going. A true brother is hard to find, so remember what really matters.
ramacharitamanas::4847.simple_insight: It softens attachment to what is temporary and sharpens gratitude for rare, loyal bonds.
ramacharitamanas::4847.detailed_meaning: Lakshman is speaking to Ram after the pain of separation has opened everything up. He reminds Ram that worldly possessions and relationships keep changing, but a brother like him is not something the world easily gives twice.
ramacharitamanas::4847.modern_relevance: You move apartments, change jobs, and replace possessions without much thought. Then one loyal friend shows up when everything falls apart, and you realize how rare real kinship is.
ramacharitamanas::4847.insight: It shifts attention from replaceable comforts to the few bonds that deserve your deepest care.

ramacharitamanas::4848.verse_sanskrit: जथा पंख बिनु खग अति दीना। मनि बिनु फनि करिबर कर हीना॥ अस मम जिवन बंधु बिनु तोही। जौं जड़ दैव जिआवै मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4848.verse_hindi: जैसे पंख बिना पक्षी, मणि बिना सर्प और सूँड बिना श्रेष्ठ हाथी अत्यंत दीन हो जाते हैं, हे भाई! यदि कहीं जड़ दैव मुझे जीवित रखे तो तुम्हारे बिना मेरा जीवन भी ऐसा ही होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4848.english_translation: Like a bird without wings, a serpent without a jewel, and a great elephant without its trunk, my life without you, brother, would be the same—if fate somehow kept me alive.
ramacharitamanas::4848.translation_literal: जथा (like) / पंख (wings) / बिनु (without) / खग (bird) / अति (very) / दीना (miserable) / मनि (jewel) / बिनु (without) / फनि (serpent) / करिबर (great elephant) / कर (trunk) / हीना (without) / अस (thus) / मम (my) / जिवन (life) / बंधु (brother) / बिनु (without) / तोही (you) / जौं (if) / जड़ (lifeless) / दैव (fate) / जिआवै (keeps alive) / मोही (me)
ramacharitamanas::4848.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4848.essence: Love can make absence feel like losing your own limbs.
ramacharitamanas::4848.simple_meaning: Ram says that life without Lakshman would be as helpless as a bird without wings or an elephant without its trunk.
ramacharitamanas::4848.simple_insight: Real love is not decorative; it feels like losing a part of yourself when the other is absent.
ramacharitamanas::4848.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram speaks to Lakshman after seeing how much his brother means to him. The war is not only about victory now; it is about whether Ram can bear the thought of returning to Ayodhya without the brother who has stood beside him in exile and battle.
ramacharitamanas::4848.modern_relevance: You look at the empty seat beside you after the hospital visit, the road trip, or the long night of crisis. Some people are not just company; they are part of how you stay upright.
ramacharitamanas::4848.insight: It shifts attention from possession to interdependence: some relationships are not additions, but supports your life leans on.

ramacharitamanas::4849.verse_sanskrit: जैहउँ अवध कौन मुहु लाई। नारि हेतु प्रिय भाई गँवाई॥ बरु अपजस सहतेउँ जग माहीं। नारि हानि बिसेष छति नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4849.verse_hindi: स्त्री के लिए प्यारे भाई को खोकर, मैं कौन सा मुँह लेकर अवध जाऊँगा? मैं जगत् में बदनामी भले ही सह लेता (कि राम में कुछ भी वीरता नहीं है जो स्त्री को खो बैठे)। स्त्री की हानि से (इस हानि को देखते) कोई विशेष क्षति नहीं थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4849.english_translation: How can I return to Ayodhya and face anyone? I have lost my dear brother for a woman. I would rather bear disgrace in the world; the loss of a woman is not a special loss compared to this.
ramacharitamanas::4849.translation_literal: जैहउँ (shall go) / अवध (to Ayodhya) / कौन (which) / मुहु (face) / लाई (bringing, with) / नारि (woman) / हेतु (for the sake of) / प्रिय (dear) / भाई (brother) / गँवाई (lost) / बरु (better) / अपजस (disgrace) / सहतेउँ (I would bear) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / नारि (woman) / हानि (loss) / बिसेष (special) / छति (damage, loss) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::4849.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4849.essence: Some losses wound deeper than shame ever could.
ramacharitamanas::4849.simple_meaning: Ram says he could bear public shame more easily than the pain of losing his brother for a woman.
ramacharitamanas::4849.simple_insight: Love and duty can be weighed by what you are willing to endure for them.
ramacharitamanas::4849.detailed_meaning: After Lakshman is struck down in Lanka, Ram speaks from raw grief. He says he could face disgrace in Ayodhya, but not the loss of his brother for Sita’s sake. The verse shows how deeply he values Lakshman’s service.
ramacharitamanas::4849.modern_relevance: You let someone down who trusted you completely, and the embarrassment sits in your chest all day. What hurts more is not being judged — it is knowing you failed the bond that mattered most.
ramacharitamanas::4849.insight: It shifts attention from public image to the cost of breaking a sacred relationship.

ramacharitamanas::4850.verse_sanskrit: अब अपलोकु सोकु सुत तोरा। सहिहि निठुर कठोर उर मोरा॥ निज जननी के एक कुमारा। तात तासु तुम्ह प्रान अधारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4850.verse_hindi: अब तो हे पुत्र! मेरे निष्ठुर और कठोर हृदय यह अपयश और तुम्हारा शोक दोनों ही सहन करेगा। हे तात! तुम अपनी माता के एक ही पुत्र और उसके प्राणाधार हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4850.english_translation: Now this disgrace and your grief, my hard and cruel heart, will endure. Son, you are your mother’s only child, and the support of her life.
ramacharitamanas::4850.translation_literal: अब (now) / अपलोकु (disgrace) / सोकु (grief) / सुत (son) / तोरा (your) / सहिहि (will bear) / निठुर (cruel) / कठोर (hard) / उर (heart) / मोरा (my) / निज (own) / जननी (mother) / के (of) / एक (one) / कुमारा (son) / तात (son) / तासु (her) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रान (life) / अधारा (support)
ramacharitamanas::4850.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::4850.essence: Love can be spoken as duty while hiding deep harm.
ramacharitamanas::4850.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi tells her son that her heart will bear the shame and his sorrow, and reminds him that he is his mother’s only child and life-support.
ramacharitamanas::4850.simple_insight: A parent’s words can wound even while sounding like love.
ramacharitamanas::4850.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is pushing Bharat toward accepting the throne after Ram’s exile. She speaks as a mother trying to justify the unbearable by appealing to her son’s duty to her, even while the family is already breaking apart.
ramacharitamanas::4850.modern_relevance: A mother says, “I only want what’s best for you,” but the room already feels poisoned. The pressure to protect family can become a way of controlling it.
ramacharitamanas::4850.insight: It exposes how affection can be used to pressure someone into carrying another person’s burden.

ramacharitamanas::4851.verse_sanskrit: सौंपेसि मोहि तुम्हहि गहि पानी। सब बिधि सुखद परम हित जानी॥ उतरु काह दैहउँ तेहि जाई। उठि किन मोहि सिखावहु भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4851.verse_hindi: सब प्रकार से सुख देने वाला और परम हितकारी जानकर उन्होंने तुम्हें हाथ पकड़कर मुझे सौंपा था। मैं अब जाकर उन्हें क्या उत्तर दूँगा? हे भाई! तुम उठकर मुझे सिखाते (समझाते) क्यों नहीं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4851.english_translation: He entrusted you to me, holding your hand, knowing you were the source of every kind of happiness and supreme good. What answer will I give him now? Brother, why don't you rise and teach me?
ramacharitamanas::4851.translation_literal: सौंपेसि (entrusted) / मोहि (to me) / तुम्हहि (you) / गहि (holding) / पानी (hand) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सुखद (giving happiness) / परम हित (highest good) / जानी (knowing) / उतरु (answer) / काह (what) / दैहउँ (shall I give) / तेहि (to him) / जाई (going) / उठि (rising) / किन (why) / मोहि (me) / सिखावहु (teach) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::4851.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4851.essence: Trust becomes unbearable when you cannot honor it.
ramacharitamanas::4851.simple_meaning: The speaker says someone was handed over as a source of happiness and good, and now he cannot face the one who trusted him.
ramacharitamanas::4851.simple_insight: Regret feels heaviest when you know you were trusted and still failed to protect what mattered.
ramacharitamanas::4851.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking after the loss of Kumbhakarna and the collapse of his cause. He remembers that his brother was given to him as a source of happiness and welfare, and now he cannot imagine what answer to give back to the one who entrusted him.
ramacharitamanas::4851.modern_relevance: You promised to look after a younger brother, a teammate, or a friend, and then let them down. The shame is not just failure — it is having to face the person who trusted you.
ramacharitamanas::4851.insight: It shifts the mind from pride to accountability, showing how trust creates moral weight.

ramacharitamanas::4852.verse_sanskrit: बहु बिधि सोचत सोच बिमोचन। स्रवत सलिल राजिव दल लोचन॥ उमा एक अखंड रघुराई। नर गति भगत कृपाल देखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4852.verse_hindi: सोच से छुड़ाने वाले श्री रामजी बहुत प्रकार से सोच कर रहे हैं। उनके कमल की पंखुड़ी के समान नेत्रों से (विषाद के आँसुओं का) जल बह रहा है। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! श्री रघुनाथजी एक (अद्वितीय) और अखंड (वियोगरहित) हैं। भक्तों पर कृपा करने वाले भगवान् ने (लीला करके) मनुष्य की दशा दिखलाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4852.english_translation: Ram, who frees beings from sorrow, is now sorrowing in many ways. Tears flow from his lotus-petal eyes. Uma, the one and undivided Raghu lord has shown the human condition to his devotees out of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4852.translation_literal: बहु बिधि (in many ways) / सोचत (thinking sorrowfully) / सोच बिमोचन (the remover of sorrow) / स्रवत (flowing) / सलिल (water) / राजिव दल लोचन (lotus-petal eyes) / उमा (Uma) / एक (one) / अखंड (undivided) / रघुराई (Raghu lord) / नर गति (human condition) / भगत (for devotees) / कृपाल (compassionate) / देखाई (showed)
ramacharitamanas::4852.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4852.essence: Compassion can wear the face of grief.
ramacharitamanas::4852.simple_meaning: Ram, who removes sorrow, is shown here weeping like a human being. Shiva explains that this is Ram's compassion at work: he reveals the human condition to help devotees.
ramacharitamanas::4852.simple_insight: You are not abandoned in grief; the divine can meet you inside it.
ramacharitamanas::4852.detailed_meaning: After the devastating news in Lanka, Ram stands overwhelmed, tears flowing from eyes like lotus petals. Shiva tells Uma that this is not weakness but divine compassion: the one undivided Raghu lord has chosen to show human sorrow so devotees can feel his nearness.
ramacharitamanas::4852.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in the hospital and cannot fix anything. You only stay, listen, and let your eyes fill too. That shared grief is not failure; it is love entering human form.
ramacharitamanas::4852.insight: It shifts devotion from distant reverence to intimate nearness: the sacred is willing to enter human pain.

ramacharitamanas::4853.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु प्रलाप सुनि कान बिकल भए बानर निकर। आइ गयउ हनुमान जिमि करुना महँ बीर रस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4853.verse_hindi: प्रभु के (लीला के लिए किए गए) प्रलाप को कानों से सुनकर वानरों के समूह व्याकुल हो गए। (इतने में ही) हनुमान् जी आ गए, जैसे करुणरस (के प्रसंग) में वीर रस (का प्रसंग) आ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4853.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's lament, the monkeys grew restless. Then Hanuman arrived, like courage entering a scene of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4853.translation_literal: प्रभु (lord) / प्रलाप (lament) / सुनि (hearing) / कान (ears) / बिकल (disturbed) / भए (became) / बानर (monkeys) / निकर (group) / आइ (coming) / गयउ (arrived) / हनुमान (Hanuman) / जिमि (like) / करुना (compassion) / महँ (in) / बीर रस (heroic mood)
ramacharitamanas::4853.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4853.essence: Strength can enter sorrow without breaking its tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::4853.simple_meaning: The monkeys are shaken by Ram's grief, and Hanuman arrives at exactly the right moment, bringing strength into a scene of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4853.simple_insight: Even in grief, help can arrive carrying courage.
ramacharitamanas::4853.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram's sorrow is being felt by the monkey army. Before the next healing step begins, Hanuman appears. The verse pauses on that arrival, comparing him to heroic energy entering a moment of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4853.modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a friend who has just broken down, and then the one person who knows what to do walks in. Relief can feel like that.
ramacharitamanas::4853.insight: It shifts attention from the grief itself to the force that can answer it.

ramacharitamanas::4854.verse_sanskrit: हरषि राम भेंटेउ हनुमाना। अति कृतग्य प्रभु परम सुजाना॥ तुरत बैद तब कीन्ह उपाई। उठि बैठे लछिमन हरषाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4854.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी हर्षित होकर हनुमान् जी से गले मिले। प्रभु परम सुजान (चतुर) और अत्यंत ही कृतज्ञ हैं। तब वैद्य (सुषेण) ने तुरंत उपाय किया, (जिससे) लक्ष्मणजी हर्षित होकर उठ बैठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4854.english_translation: Ram joyfully embraced Hanuman. The Lord is deeply grateful and profoundly wise. Then the physician quickly applied his remedy, and Lakshman rose up, delighted.
ramacharitamanas::4854.translation_literal: हरषि (rejoicing) / राम (Ram) / भेंटेउ (embraced/met) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / अति (very) / कृतग्य (grateful) / प्रभु (Lord) / परम (supremely) / सुजाना (wise) / तुरत (immediately) / बैद (physician) / तब (then) / कीन्ह (did) / उपाई (remedy) / उठि (rising) / बैठे (sat up) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / हरषाई (delighted)
ramacharitamanas::4854.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4854.essence: Devotion is met with embrace, gratitude, and healing.
ramacharitamanas::4854.simple_meaning: Ram welcomes Hanuman with joy, shows deep gratitude, and Lakshman is healed and sits up again.
ramacharitamanas::4854.simple_insight: True devotion is met with warmth, not distance.
ramacharitamanas::4854.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman returns after finding Sita and bringing hope back to the grieving camp. Ram embraces him with joy and gratitude. Then Sushena quickly treats Lakshman, and the fallen brother rises again.
ramacharitamanas::4854.modern_relevance: You finally hear back from the friend who showed up when everything was falling apart. The relief is not just in the help — it is in being seen and treasured.
ramacharitamanas::4854.insight: It shows that sincere service is answered by recognition, and that healing begins in grateful connection.

ramacharitamanas::4855.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ लाइ प्रभु भेंटेउ भ्राता। हरषे सकल भालु कपि ब्राता॥ कपि पुनि बैद तहाँ पहुँचावा। जेहि बिधि तबहिं ताहि लइ आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4855.verse_hindi: प्रभु भाई को हृदय से लगाकर मिले। भालू और वानरों के समूह सब हर्षित हो गए। फिर हनुमान् जी ने वैद्य को उसी प्रकार वहाँ पहुँचा दिया, जिस प्रकार वे उस बार (पहले) उसे ले आए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4855.english_translation: Ram embraced his brother to his heart. The bears and monkeys were all delighted. Then Hanuman carried the physician back there again, just as he had brought him before.
ramacharitamanas::4855.translation_literal: हृदयँ (to the heart) / लाइ (bringing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / भेंटेउ (met / embraced) / भ्राता (brother) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सकल (all) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / ब्राता (brothers / companions) / कपि (the monkey) / पुनि (again) / बैद (physician) / तहाँ (there) / पहुँचावा (caused to पहुंचना / delivered) / जेहि बिधि (in the same way) / तबहिं (then / at that time) / ताहि (him) / लइ (taking) / आवा (brought)
ramacharitamanas::4855.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4855.essence: Love rejoices, and service leaves quietly once its work is done.
ramacharitamanas::4855.simple_meaning: Ram warmly embraces Lakshman, and the whole monkey and bear army rejoices. Hanuman then brings the physician back exactly as before.
ramacharitamanas::4855.simple_insight: Joy returns when care is restored and everyone is safe again.
ramacharitamanas::4855.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Lakshman has just been revived. Ram embraces his brother with relief, the bears and monkeys celebrate, and Hanuman immediately carries Sushen back once his help is done. The verse simply completes the healing moment.
ramacharitamanas::4855.modern_relevance: After a long night in the emergency room, your sibling finally opens their eyes. The relief is so complete that even the smallest next task feels light.
ramacharitamanas::4855.insight: It closes the healing scene by showing gratitude, relief, and swift selfless service.

ramacharitamanas::4856.verse_sanskrit: यह बृत्तांत दसानन सुनेऊ। अति बिषाद पुनि पुनि सिर धुनेऊ॥ ब्याकुल कुंभकरन पहिं आवा। बिबिध जतन करि ताहि जगावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4856.verse_hindi: यह समाचार जब रावण ने सुना, तब उसने अत्यंत विषाद से बार-बार सिर पीटा। वह व्याकुल होकर कुंभकर्ण के पास गया और बहुत से उपाय करके उसने उसको जगाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4856.english_translation: When Ravana heard this news, he was filled with grief and kept striking his head again and again. Agitated, he went to Kumbhakarna and woke him with many efforts.
ramacharitamanas::4856.translation_literal: यह (this) / बृत्तांत (account, news) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / सुनेऊ (heard) / अति (very) / बिषाद (grief) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / सिर (head) / धुनेऊ (shook, struck) / ब्याकुल (agitated) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / पहिं (to, near) / आवा (came) / बिबिध (various) / जतन (efforts, attempts) / करि (having done) / ताहि (him) / जगावा (woke up)
ramacharitamanas::4856.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4856.essence: Fear makes even the powerful reach for help in disorder.
ramacharitamanas::4856.simple_meaning: Ravana hears the bad news, panics, and rushes to wake Kumbhakarna with repeated efforts.
ramacharitamanas::4856.simple_insight: Panic makes you reach for help fast, even when the situation is already slipping away.
ramacharitamanas::4856.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has turned against Ravana. Hearing the report, he loses composure, strikes his own head in despair, and runs to Kumbhakarna for rescue. This is a turning-point of fear, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4856.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were dreading. You pace the room, then call the one person you think can still fix it. That is Ravana's mind here.
ramacharitamanas::4856.insight: It shows how fear scatters judgment and pushes you into desperate action.

ramacharitamanas::4857.verse_sanskrit: जागा निसिचर देखिअ कैसा। मानहुँ कालु देह धरि बैसा॥ कुंभकरन बूझा कहु भाई। काहे तव मुख रहे सुखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4857.verse_hindi: कुंभकर्ण जगा (उठ बैठा) वह कैसा दिखाई देता है मानो स्वयं काल ही शरीर धारण करके बैठा हो। कुंभकर्ण ने पूछा- हे भाई! कहो तो, तुम्हारे मुख सूख क्यों रहे हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4857.english_translation: What a sight the demon was when he woke up, as if Time itself had taken a body and sat there. Kumbhakarna asked, "Brother, tell me—why does your face look so dry and weary?"
ramacharitamanas::4857.translation_literal: जागा (woke up) / निसिचर (demon) / देखिअ (to be seen) / कैसा (how) / मानहुँ (as if) / कालु (Time/Death) / देह (body) / धरि (having taken) / बैसा (sat) ॥ / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / बूझा (asked) / कहु (tell) / भाई (brother) / काहे (why) / तव (your) / मुख (face) / रहे (remains) / सुखाई (dry, withered) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4857.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4857.essence: Delayed help arrives after the damage has already deepened.
ramacharitamanas::4857.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna wakes up looking terrifying, like death itself in a body, and asks Ravana why he looks so drained.
ramacharitamanas::4857.simple_insight: A giant can wake up late and still miss the disaster already unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::4857.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just roused Kumbhakarna in desperation after hearing of his losses. The sleeping giant wakes like embodied death and immediately notices Ravana's fear and exhaustion. The scene builds toward Ravana explaining the whole crisis.
ramacharitamanas::4857.modern_relevance: You finally reach the friend who ignored every warning, and now they look shocked that everything has collapsed. The damage was already done before they asked for help.
ramacharitamanas::4857.insight: It frames the crisis as already advanced, so the next verse can reveal the full disaster.

ramacharitamanas::4858.verse_sanskrit: कथा कही सब तेहिं अभिमानी। जेहि प्रकार सीता हरि आनी॥ तात कपिन्ह सब निसिचर मारे। महा महा जोधा संघारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4858.verse_hindi: उस अभिमानी (रावण) ने उससे जिस प्रकार से वह सीता को हर लाया था (तब से अब तक की) सारी कथा कही। (फिर कहा-) हे तात! वानरों ने सब राक्षस मार डाले। बड़े-बड़े योद्धाओं का भी संहार कर डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4858.english_translation: That arrogant one told him the whole story, including how he had carried off Sita. Then he said, "Brother, the monkeys have killed all the demons. They have slain even the greatest warriors."
ramacharitamanas::4858.translation_literal: कथा (story) / कही (told) / सब (all) / तेहिं (that one) / अभिमानी (arrogant one) / जेहि प्रकार (in which manner) / सीता (Sita) / हरि (carried off) / आनी (brought) ॥ / तात (brother) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / सब (all) / निसिचर (demons) / मारे (killed) / महा महा (great, great) / जोधा (warriors) / संघारे (slain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4858.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4858.essence: Pride speaks loudly, even as its world collapses.
ramacharitamanas::4858.simple_meaning: Ravana recounts how he abducted Sita and admits that the monkey army has destroyed his warriors.
ramacharitamanas::4858.simple_insight: Pride can keep talking even while defeat is already standing in the room.
ramacharitamanas::4858.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just woken Kumbhakarna and is trying to explain the disaster. He retells the abduction of Sita and admits that the monkeys have killed many of his strongest fighters. The scene shows panic breaking through his arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::4858.modern_relevance: You keep explaining how things went wrong after the loss is already obvious. The longer you defend your pride, the more exposed you feel.
ramacharitamanas::4858.insight: It shows how ego keeps narrating its own story even when reality has already overturned it.

ramacharitamanas::4859.verse_sanskrit: दुर्मुख सुररिपु मनुज अहारी। भट अतिकाय अकंपन भारी॥ अपर महोदर आदिक बीरा। परे समर महि सब रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4859.verse_hindi: दुर्मुख, देवशत्रु (देवान्तक), मनुष्य भक्षक (नरान्तक), भारी योद्धा अतिकाय और अकम्पन तथा महोदर आदि दूसरे सभी रणधीर वीर रणभूमि में मारे गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4859.english_translation: Dumukha, the enemy of the radiant beings, Narantaka the man-eater, the mighty warrior Atikaya and Akampana, along with Mahodara and other brave fighters, all fell on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4859.translation_literal: दुर्मुख (Dumukha) / सुररिपु (enemy of the radiant beings) / मनुज (human) / अहारी (devourer) / भट (warrior) / अतिकाय (Atikaya) / अकंपन (Akampana) / भारी (mighty) / अपर (other) / महोदर (Mahodara) / आदिक (and others) / बीरा (heroes) / परे (fell) / समर (battle) / महि (on the ground) / सब (all) / रनधीरा (battle-brave)
ramacharitamanas::4859.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4859.essence: Great strength means little when it is already falling.
ramacharitamanas::4859.simple_meaning: Several of Ravana's great warriors have been killed in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4859.simple_insight: Power can fall quickly when it stands against what is right.
ramacharitamanas::4859.detailed_meaning: Inside Lanka, Ravana is listing the losses to Kumbhakarna. The names are not teachings but a grim report: his strongest fighters have already fallen, and the war is turning against him.
ramacharitamanas::4859.modern_relevance: A team that once looked unbeatable starts losing key people one by one. The confidence was loud, but the damage is real.
ramacharitamanas::4859.insight: It frames the war as a collapse of force, not a heroic advance.

ramacharitamanas::4860.verse_sanskrit: सुनि दसकंधर बचन तब कुंभकरन बिलखान। जगदंबा हरि आनि अब सठ चाहत कल्यान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4860.verse_hindi: तब रावण के वचन सुनकर कुंभकर्ण बिलखकर (दुःखी होकर) बोला- अरे मूर्ख! जगज्जननी जानकी को हर लाकर अब कल्याण चाहता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4860.english_translation: Hearing Ravana's words, Kumbhakarna lamented, "Fool! You brought away the Mother of the world, and now you still want well-being?"
ramacharitamanas::4860.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / दसकंधर (Ravana) / बचन (words) / तब (then) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / बिलखान (lamented) / जगदंबा (Mother of the world) / हरि (having taken away) / आनि (bringing) / अब (now) / सठ (fool) / चाहत (you want) / कल्यान (well-being)
ramacharitamanas::4860.speaker: Kumbhakarna
ramacharitamanas::4860.essence: Pride that harms others cannot also secure your good.
ramacharitamanas::4860.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna rebukes Ravana for abducting Sita and still hoping for good outcomes. He sees that harmful action and real well-being cannot coexist.
ramacharitamanas::4860.simple_insight: Some actions poison the future so deeply that no wish for comfort can undo them.
ramacharitamanas::4860.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana boasts about the war and his old crime of abducting Sita. Kumbhakarna, half-awake and shaken, hears the pride behind the words and calls him a fool. The moment exposes Ravana's blindness before the coming collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4860.modern_relevance: You send a harsh message at midnight, then keep checking your phone for a warm reply. Part of you already knows the damage is done, and pretending otherwise only deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::4860.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justifying pride to honest recognition of consequence.

ramacharitamanas::4861.verse_sanskrit: भल न कीन्ह तैं निसिचर नाहा। अब मोहि आइ जगाएहि काहा॥ अजहूँ तात त्यागि अभिमाना। भजहु राम होइहि कल्याना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4861.verse_hindi: हे राक्षसराज! तूने अच्छा नहीं किया। अब आकर मुझे क्यों जगाया? हे तात! अब भी अभिमान छोड़कर श्री रामजी को भजो तो कल्याण होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4861.english_translation: O king of the demons, you did not do well. Why have you come to wake me now? Even now, brother, give up pride and worship Ram; you will find welfare.
ramacharitamanas::4861.translation_literal: भल (well) / न (not) / कीन्ह (did) / तैं (you) / निसिचर नाहा (O lord of demons) / अब (now) / मोहि (me) / आइ (coming) / जगाएहि (you wake) / काहा (why) / अजहूँ (even now) / तात (brother) / त्यागि (giving up) / अभिमाना (pride) / भजहु (worship) / राम (Ram) / होइहि (will be) / कल्याना (welfare)
ramacharitamanas::4861.speaker: Kumbhakarna
ramacharitamanas::4861.essence: Pride is not the last word; turning to Ram still is.
ramacharitamanas::4861.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna rebukes Ravana for waking him and tells him that even now, if he gives up pride and turns to Ram, things can still improve.
ramacharitamanas::4861.simple_insight: There is still a door open, even after terrible choices.
ramacharitamanas::4861.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has woken Kumbhakarna to strengthen his side in the war. Instead of approving, Kumbhakarna scolds him. He says Ravana's pride has ruined everything, and even now the only wise move is to abandon ego and take Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::4861.modern_relevance: You get the late-night call after a disastrous decision, and the person on the line still won't admit they were wrong. This verse cuts through that stubbornness: the first healing step is dropping pride.
ramacharitamanas::4861.insight: It shifts the mind from defending ego to choosing repair before it's too late.

ramacharitamanas::4862.verse_sanskrit: हैं दससीस मनुज रघुनायक। जाके हनूमान से पायक॥ अहह बंधु तैं कीन्हि खोटाई। प्रथमहिं मोहि न सुनाएहि आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4862.verse_hindi: हे रावण! जिनके हनुमान् सरीखे सेवक हैं, वे श्री रघुनाथजी क्या मनुष्य हैं? हाय भाई! तूने बुरा किया, जो पहले ही आकर मुझे यह हाल नहीं सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4862.english_translation: O Ravana, are those whose servant is Hanuman truly human? Alas, brother, you did wrong by not telling me this first.
ramacharitamanas::4862.translation_literal: हैं (are) / दससीस (ten-headed one, Ravana) / मनुज (human) / रघुनायक (Raghunath, Lord Ram) / जाके (whose) / हनूमान (Hanuman) / से (like) / पायक (servant)॥ / अहह (alas) / बंधु (brother) / तैं (you) / कीन्हि (did) / खोटाई (wrong) / प्रथमहिं (at first) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / सुनाएहि (told) / आई (coming)॥
ramacharitamanas::4862.speaker: Kumbhakarna
ramacharitamanas::4862.essence: The servant reveals the greatness of the one served.
ramacharitamanas::4862.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna realises Ram cannot be ordinary if Hanuman serves him. He blames Ravana for not telling him earlier, because this changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::4862.simple_insight: Real greatness is measured by the kind of devotion it inspires.
ramacharitamanas::4862.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Kumbhakarna has just woken and heard Ravana's story. The moment he learns that Hanuman serves Ram, his attitude shifts at once. Even Ravana's brother can sense that a being with such a devotee cannot be ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::4862.modern_relevance: You meet someone’s longtime assistant and immediately understand the person better. The way people serve them, speak of them, and stay loyal reveals more than their title ever could.
ramacharitamanas::4862.insight: It shifts attention from status to the quality of devotion a person draws out in others.

ramacharitamanas::4863.verse_sanskrit: कीन्हेहु प्रभु बिरोध तेहि देवक। सिव बिरंचि सुर जाके सेवक॥ नारद मुनि मोहि ग्यान जो कहा। कहतेउँ तोहि समय निरबाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4863.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! तुमने उस परम देवता का विरोध किया, जिसके शिव, ब्रह्मा आदि देवता सेवक हैं। नारद मुनि ने मुझे जो ज्ञान कहा था, वह मैं तुझसे कहता, पर अब तो समय जाता रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4863.english_translation: O Lord, you opposed that supreme being whom Shiva, Brahma, and the radiant beings serve. Narada the sage told me this wisdom, and I would have told it to you, but now the proper time has passed.
ramacharitamanas::4863.translation_literal: कीन्हेहु (you did) / प्रभु (Lord) / बिरोध (opposition) / तेहि (that) / देवक (supreme being) / सिव (Shiva) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सुर (radiant beings) / जाके (whose) / सेवक (servants) / नारद (Narada) / मुनि (sage) / मोहि (to me) / ग्यान (wisdom) / जो (which) / कहा (said) / कहतेउँ (I would have said) / तोहि (to you) / समय (time) / निरबाहा (has passed)
ramacharitamanas::4863.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::4863.essence: Pride can make wisdom arrive too late.
ramacharitamanas::4863.simple_meaning: Mandodari tells Ravana that he has opposed the supreme being served by Shiva, Brahma, and the radiant beings. She says Narada had already warned her of this, but now it is too late.
ramacharitamanas::4863.simple_insight: Ignoring wise warning can leave you face to face with consequences you can no longer change.
ramacharitamanas::4863.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final collapse, Mandodari speaks to Ravana with grief and clarity. She names Ram as the supreme being even the greatest powers serve, and reminds Ravana that Narada's warning came earlier. This is regret after wisdom was refused.
ramacharitamanas::4863.modern_relevance: You finally read the warning after the contract is signed. The pattern was obvious, but pride kept you from listening until the cost was already real.
ramacharitamanas::4863.insight: It shifts the mind from defensive pride to belated recognition of a truth already seen by others.

ramacharitamanas::4864.verse_sanskrit: अब भरि अंक भेंटु मोहि भाई। लोचन सुफल करौं मैं जाई॥ स्याम गात सरसीरुह लोचन। देखौं जाइ ताप त्रय मोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4864.verse_hindi: हे भाई! अब तो (अन्तिम बार) अँकवार भरकर मुझसे मिल ले। मैं जाकर अपने नेत्र सफल करूँ। तीनों तापों को छुड़ाने वाले श्याम शरीर, कमल नेत्र श्री रामजी के जाकर दर्शन करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4864.english_translation: “Brother, now embrace me fully one last time. I will go and make my eyes fruitful by seeing the dark-bodied Ram with lotus eyes, the remover of the three kinds of suffering.”
ramacharitamanas::4864.translation_literal: अब (now) / भरि (full) / अंक (embrace) / भेंटु (meet) / मोहि (me) / भाई (brother) / लोचन (eyes) / सुफल (fruitful) / करौं (I will make) / मैं (I) / जाई (going) / स्याम (dark/blue) / गात (body) / सरसीरुह (lotus) / लोचन (eyes) / देखौं (I will see) / जाइ (going) / ताप (suffering) / त्रय (three) / मोचन (remover)
ramacharitamanas::4864.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4864.essence: Even the fallen can find fulfillment in one last sight of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4864.simple_meaning: Ravana asks his brother for one last embrace and says he will go behold Ram, whose sight brings the eyes true fulfillment and frees one from suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4864.simple_insight: Even at the edge of death, the heart can turn toward what is most sacred.
ramacharitamanas::4864.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield’s final turn, Ravana has already been warned that he has opposed the supreme being. Now, facing death, he asks his brother for a final embrace and says he wants to see Ram once before leaving the world.
ramacharitamanas::4864.modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, someone who spent years chasing power suddenly asks to see the person they ignored. The last thing the heart wants is not victory, but a final clear sight.
ramacharitamanas::4864.insight: It shifts the mind from pride and possession to longing for direct vision of the divine.

ramacharitamanas::4865.verse_sanskrit: राम रूप गुन सुमिरत मगन भयउ छन एक। रावन मागेउ कोटि घट मद अरु महिष अनेक ॥
ramacharitamanas::4865.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के रूप और गुणों को स्मरण करके वह एक क्षण के लिए प्रेम में मग्न हो गया। फिर रावण से करोड़ों घड़े मदिरा और अनेकों भैंसे मँगवाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4865.english_translation: Remembering Ram's form and virtues, he became absorbed for a moment. Then he asked Ravana for millions of jars of liquor and many buffaloes.
ramacharitamanas::4865.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / रूप (form) / गुन (virtues) / सुमिरत (remembering) / मगन (absorbed) / भयउ (became) / छन (moment) / एक (one) / रावन (Ravana) / मागेउ (asked for) / कोटि (millions) / घट (jars) / मद (liquor) / अरु (and) / महिष (buffaloes) / अनेक (many)
ramacharitamanas::4865.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4865.essence: A glimpse of Ram vanishes when appetite takes over.
ramacharitamanas::4865.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna briefly remembers Ram with devotion, then asks Ravana for huge amounts of liquor and many buffaloes.
ramacharitamanas::4865.simple_insight: Even a flash of devotion can appear inside a mind ruled by appetite.
ramacharitamanas::4865.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to awaken Kumbhakarna for battle. For a moment, Kumbhakarna remembers Ram's beauty and virtues, but the glimpse passes quickly. He immediately turns back to craving drink and meat, showing how deep his sleep of ignorance remains.
ramacharitamanas::4865.modern_relevance: You have one clear moment of conscience at midnight, then you open the fridge, the feed, or the bottle again. A brief insight is not the same as a changed life.
ramacharitamanas::4865.insight: It shows how quickly higher feeling can be swallowed by old craving when discipline is absent.

ramacharitamanas::4866.verse_sanskrit: महिषखाइ करि मदिरा पाना। गर्जा बज्राघात समाना॥ कुंभकरन दुर्मद रन रंगा। चला दुर्ग तजि सेन न संगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4866.verse_hindi: भैंसे खाकर और मदिरा पीकर वह वज्रघात (बिजली गिरने) के समान गरजा। मद से चूर रण के उत्साह से पूर्ण कुंभकर्ण किला छोड़कर चला। सेना भी साथ नहीं ली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4866.english_translation: Feasting on buffalo meat and drinking liquor, he roared like a thunderbolt. Drunk with pride, Kumbhakarna left the fortress and marched out in battle fury without even taking an army.
ramacharitamanas::4866.translation_literal: महिषखाइ (having eaten buffalo meat) / करि (having made) / मदिरा पाना (drinking liquor) / गर्जा (roared) / बज्राघात समाना (like a thunderbolt)॥ / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / दुर्मद (intoxicated with pride) / रन रंगा (coloured by battle) / चला (went) / दुर्ग तजि (leaving the fortress) / सेन न संगा (without company of an army) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4866.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4866.essence: Pride turns strength into reckless noise.
ramacharitamanas::4866.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna, drunk and furious, storms out of the fortress alone, ready for battle.
ramacharitamanas::4866.simple_insight: Raw force without restraint only makes destruction louder.
ramacharitamanas::4866.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final war, Ravana's brother Kumbhakarna wakes for battle after feasting and drinking. He leaves the fortress without even an army, roaring into the fight. The verse builds the scene before Vibhishana steps forward in the next moment.
ramacharitamanas::4866.modern_relevance: A person slams the car door after an argument and storms back inside, too angry to think. The body is moving fast, but judgment has already gone missing.
ramacharitamanas::4866.insight: It shows how pride and intoxication push action into blind force.

ramacharitamanas::4867.verse_sanskrit: देखि बिभीषनु आगें आयउ। परेउ चरन निज नाम सुनायउ॥ अनुज उठाइ हृदयँ तेहि लायो। रघुपति भक्त जानि मन भायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4867.verse_hindi: उसे देखकर विभीषण आगे आए और उसके चरणों पर गिरकर अपना नाम सुनाया। छोटे भाई को उठाकर उसने हृदय से लगा लिया और श्री रघुनाथजी का भक्त जानकर वे उसके मन को प्रिय लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4867.english_translation: Seeing Vibhishana come forward, he fell at his feet and told his name. He lifted his younger brother and held him to his heart; knowing him to be a devotee of Raghupati, he was pleased in his mind.
ramacharitamanas::4867.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / आगें (forward) / आयउ (came) / परेउ (fell) / चरन (feet) / निज (own) / नाम (name) / सुनायउ (told) / अनुज (younger brother) / उठाइ (lifting) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / तेहि (him) / लायो (held) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / भक्त (devotee) / जानि (knowing) / मन (mind) / भायो (was pleased)
ramacharitamanas::4867.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4867.essence: Ram receives the one who comes bowed, not the one who comes proud.
ramacharitamanas::4867.simple_meaning: Vibhishana approaches with humility, and Ram welcomes him warmly because he recognizes true devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4867.simple_insight: You do not need status to be received; sincerity speaks before words do.
ramacharitamanas::4867.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the battle’s fury, Vibhishana steps forward alone and bows before Ram’s side. He names himself, and Ram responds by lifting him up and holding him close, pleased to see a heart aligned with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4867.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after making a hard choice that cost you approval. Someone who sees your sincerity doesn’t interrogate your past — they simply make space for you.
ramacharitamanas::4867.insight: It shifts attention from outer allegiance to the inward quality of devotion and humility.

ramacharitamanas::4868.verse_sanskrit: तात लात रावन मोहि मारा। कहत परम हित मंत्र बिचारा॥ तेहिं गलानि रघुपति पहिं आयउँ। देखि दीन प्रभु के मन भायउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4868.verse_hindi: (विभीषण ने कहा-) हे तात! परम हितकर सलाह एवं विचार करने पर रावण ने मुझे लात मारी। उसी ग्लानि के मारे मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के पास चला आया। दीन देखकर प्रभु के मन को मैं (बहुत) प्रिय लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4868.english_translation: “Dear brother, Ravana kicked me after hearing my well-meaning counsel. Shamed by that, I came to Lord Raghunath. Seeing the humble, I became dear to the Lord’s mind.”
ramacharitamanas::4868.translation_literal: तात (dear brother) / लात (kick) / रावन (Ravana) / मोहि (me) / मारा (struck) / कहत (saying) / परम हित (highest good) / मंत्र (counsel) / बिचारा (considered) / तेहिं (by that) / गलानि (shame) / रघुपति (Lord Raghunath) / पहिं (to) / आयउँ (I came) / देखि (seeing) / दीन (the humble) / प्रभु (the Lord) / के (of) / मन (mind) / भायउँ (became pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::4868.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4868.essence: Humility, not status, is what draws Ram close.
ramacharitamanas::4868.simple_meaning: Vibhishana says Ravana insulted him after ignoring good advice, so he came to Ram in shame. Ram welcomes the humble and values their surrender.
ramacharitamanas::4868.simple_insight: You do not need to defend your pride to be received. Honest humility can open the door.
ramacharitamanas::4868.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just crossed over from Ravana’s side and bowed before Ram. He explains that he came because Ravana rejected wise counsel and struck him in anger. That shame becomes the turning point: Ram’s heart is drawn to the humble seeker.
ramacharitamanas::4868.modern_relevance: You finally admit you were wrong in a family argument, and the room goes quiet. The apology does not weaken you; it makes real connection possible.
ramacharitamanas::4868.insight: It shifts you from protecting ego to approaching with honesty and humility.

ramacharitamanas::4869.verse_sanskrit: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4869.verse_hindi: (कुंभकर्ण ने कहा-) हे पुत्र! सुन, रावण तो काल के वश हो गया है (उसके सिर पर मृत्यु नाच रही है)। वह क्या अब उत्तम शिक्षा मान सकता है? हे विभीषण! तू धन्य है, धन्य है। हे तात! तू राक्षस कुल का भूषण हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4869.english_translation: Listen, Ravana has fallen under the power of death. Can he still accept the highest teaching now? Blessed, blessed are you, Vibhishana. You have become the ornament of the demon line, dear son.
ramacharitamanas::4869.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / भयउ (has become) / कालबस (under the power of time and death) / रावन (Ravana) / सो (that) / कि (can) / मान (accept) / अब (now) / परम (highest) / सिखावन (teaching) / धन्य (blessed) / धन्य (blessed) / तैं (you) / धन्य (blessed) / विभीषन (Vibhishana) / भयहु (you have become) / तात (dear son) / निसिचर (demon) / कुल (lineage) / भूषन (ornament)
ramacharitamanas::4869.speaker: Kumbhakarna
ramacharitamanas::4869.essence: Truth honors you even when others are past saving.
ramacharitamanas::4869.simple_meaning: Ravana is already beyond instruction because death has taken hold of him. Vibhishana, by choosing what is right, brings honor to his entire lineage.
ramacharitamanas::4869.simple_insight: It feels good to know that integrity can redeem your name even when others refuse correction.
ramacharitamanas::4869.detailed_meaning: Kumbhakarna speaks after Vibhishana has come to Ram. Seeing the truth too late, he admits that Ravana is no longer reachable by advice. Then he praises Vibhishana for leaving false loyalty and honoring his clan through right action.
ramacharitamanas::4869.modern_relevance: You finally tell a friend the hard truth, but they are already too deep in denial to hear it. Still, your honesty matters — sometimes it is the only thing that keeps your own name clean.
ramacharitamanas::4869.insight: It shifts you from trying to fix the unresponsive to honoring the clear choice you can still make.

ramacharitamanas::4870.verse_sanskrit: बंधु बंस तैं कीन्ह उजागर। भजेहु राम सोभा सुख सागर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4870.verse_hindi: हे भाई! तूने अपने कुल को दैदीप्यमान कर दिया, जो शोभा और सुख के समुद्र श्री रामजी को भजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4870.english_translation: You have made your family shine brightly by worshipping Ram, the ocean of beauty and joy.
ramacharitamanas::4870.translation_literal: बंधु (brother) / बंस (family line) / तैं (you) / कीन्ह (made) / उजागर (bright, shining) / भजेहु (you worshipped) / राम (Ram) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / सुख (joy) / सागर (ocean)
ramacharitamanas::4870.speaker: Kumbhakarna
ramacharitamanas::4870.essence: Turning to Ram makes your whole lineage radiant.
ramacharitamanas::4870.simple_meaning: Worshipping Ram brings honor not just to you, but to your whole family line.
ramacharitamanas::4870.simple_insight: Devotion does not shrink you; it lifts everyone connected to you.
ramacharitamanas::4870.detailed_meaning: Kumbhakarna is speaking to Vibhishana after Ravana has rejected him. Instead of scolding, he recognizes the deeper truth: Vibhishana has brought glory to his family by choosing Ram over pride and cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::4870.modern_relevance: You choose honesty over protecting a family secret, and the room goes quiet. Later, people may not praise the choice, but your name carries a different weight because of it.
ramacharitamanas::4870.insight: It shifts pride from bloodline status to moral alignment with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4871.verse_sanskrit: बचन कर्म मन कपट तजि भजेहु राम रनधीर। जाहु न निज पर सूझ मोहि भयउँ कालबस बीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4871.verse_hindi: मन, वचन और कर्म से कपट छोड़कर रणधीर श्री रामजी का भजन करना। हे भाई! मैं काल (मृत्यु) के वश हो गया हूँ, मुझे अपना-पराया नहीं सूझता, इसलिए अब तुम जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4871.english_translation: Leave deceit in mind, speech, and action, and worship courageous Ram. Brother, I have fallen under death’s power; I can no longer tell friend from foe, so now you must go.
ramacharitamanas::4871.translation_literal: बचन (speech) / कर्म (action) / मन (mind) / कपट (deceit) / तजि (having छोड़कर) / भजेहु (worship) / राम (Ram) / रनधीर (battle-courageous) / जाहु (go) / न (not) / निज (own) / पर (other) / सूझ (is understood) / मोहि (to me) / भयउँ (I became) / कालबस (under death’s control) / बीर (brother/warrior)
ramacharitamanas::4871.speaker: Kumbhakarna
ramacharitamanas::4871.essence: Deceit falls away when death is near; only fearless devotion remains.
ramacharitamanas::4871.simple_meaning: Speak and act without deceit, and turn to Ram with courage. Kumbhakarna says he is now under death’s control and can no longer distinguish friend from foe.
ramacharitamanas::4871.simple_insight: When clarity is gone, only honest devotion and right action remain.
ramacharitamanas::4871.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Kumbhakarna speaks to Vibhishana as the war closes in. He sees that death has already claimed him, so he urges his brother to abandon deceit and turn to Ram, the fearless warrior.
ramacharitamanas::4871.modern_relevance: A family argument has gone too far, and everyone is speaking from hurt instead of honesty. In that moment, the only useful move is to drop the mask and face what is real.
ramacharitamanas::4871.insight: It shifts the mind from divided loyalty to clean, truthful alignment with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::4872.verse_sanskrit: बंधु बचन सुनि चला बिभीषन। आयउ जहँ त्रैलोक बिभूषन॥ नाथ भूधराकार सरीरा। कुंभकरन आवत रनधीरा ॥॥
ramacharitamanas::4872.verse_hindi: भाई के वचन सुनकर विभीषण लौट गए और वहाँ आए, जहाँ त्रिलोकी के भूषण श्री रामजी थे। (विभीषण ने कहा-) हे नाथ! पर्वत के समान (विशाल) देह वाला रणधीर कुंभकर्ण आ रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4872.english_translation: Hearing his brother's words, Vibhishana went back and came to where Ram, the ornament of the three worlds, was. He said, "Lord, the mountain-like body of the brave Kumbhakarna is coming into battle."
ramacharitamanas::4872.translation_literal: बंधु (brother) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / चला (went) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / आयउ (came) / जहँ (where) / त्रैलोक (three worlds) / बिभूषन (ornament) / नाथ (lord) / भूधराकार (mountain-shaped) / सरीरा (body) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / आवत (coming) / रनधीरा (battle-brave one)
ramacharitamanas::4872.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4872.essence: The battle is about to widen, and Vibhishana sees it first.
ramacharitamanas::4872.simple_meaning: Vibhishana returns to Ram and warns that Kumbhakarna is coming to fight, describing his huge mountain-like body.
ramacharitamanas::4872.simple_insight: Some moments are only a warning before the real clash begins.
