ramacharitamanas::4872.detailed_meaning: After hearing his brother's words, Vibhishana goes back to Ram, the ornament of the three worlds. He warns that Kumbhakarna, with a mountain-like body, is advancing toward battle. The verse sets up the next surge of war.
ramacharitamanas::4872.modern_relevance: You spot the storm before it hits: a message arrives, the room tightens, and everyone braces for what is coming next.
ramacharitamanas::4872.insight: It shifts attention from the warning itself to the approaching action that follows.

ramacharitamanas::4873.verse_sanskrit: एतना कपिन्ह सुना जब काना। किलकिलाइ धाए बलवाना॥ लिए उठाइ बिटप अरु भूधर। कटकटाइ डारहिं ता ऊपर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4873.verse_hindi: वानरों ने जब कानों से इतना सुना, तब वे बलवान् किलकिलाकर (हर्षध्वनि करके) दौड़े। वृक्ष और पर्वत (उखाड़कर) उठा लिए और (क्रोध से) दाँत कटकटाकर उन्हें उसके ऊपर डालने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4873.english_translation: When the monkeys heard this, the mighty ones shouted in delight and rushed forward. They lifted trees and mountains and, grinding their teeth in anger, hurled them down upon him.
ramacharitamanas::4873.translation_literal: एतना (so much) / कपिन्ह (by the monkeys) / सुना (heard) / जब (when) / काना (with ears) / किलकिलाइ (shouting gleefully) / धाए (ran) / बलवाना (the strong ones) / लिए (took) / उठाइ (lifting up) / बिटप (trees) / अरु (and) / भूधर (mountains) / कटकटाइ (grinding teeth) / डारहिं (they throw) / ता ऊपर (on top of him)
ramacharitamanas::4873.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4873.essence: Battle energy becomes unstoppable once the army hears the signal.
ramacharitamanas::4873.simple_meaning: The monkeys hear the news, roar with excitement, and rush into battle, tearing up trees and mountains to throw at the enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4873.simple_insight: When courage catches fire, hesitation disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4873.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army hears that the fight has begun in earnest. Their response is immediate and fierce: they shout, uproot trees and mountains, and charge forward as the battle turns fully violent.
ramacharitamanas::4873.modern_relevance: A crowd hears the final call and suddenly moves as one — phones down, chairs pushed back, everyone rushing into the same urgent task.
ramacharitamanas::4873.insight: It shifts the scene from tension to full-force action, showing collective momentum before impact.

ramacharitamanas::4874.verse_sanskrit: कोटि कोटि गिरि सिखर प्रहारा। करहिं भालु कपि एक एक बारा॥ मुर् यो न मनु तनु टर् यो न टार् यो। जिमि गज अर्क फलनि को मार् यो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4874.verse_hindi: रीछ-वानर एक-एक बार में ही करोड़ों पहाड़ों के शिखरों से उस पर प्रहार करते हैं, परन्तु इससे न तो उसका मन ही मुड़ा (विचलित हुआ) और न शरीर ही टाले टला, जैसे मदार के फलों की मार से हाथी पर कुछ भी असर नहीं होता! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4874.english_translation: The bears and monkeys strike him again and again with peaks of mountains, but his mind does not turn and his body does not yield, just as an elephant is unaffected by strikes from madar fruits.
ramacharitamanas::4874.translation_literal: कोटि-कोटि (millions upon millions) / गिरि-सिखर (mountain peaks) / प्रहारा (blows) / करहिं (they do) / भालु-कपि (bears and monkeys) / एक-एक बारा (one by one, in turn) / मुर् यो न (did not turn) / मनु (mind) / तनु (body) / टर् यो न (did not move away) / टार् यो (was turned) / जिमि (like) / गज (elephant) / अर्क-फलनि (madar fruits) / को मार् यो (struck by)
ramacharitamanas::4874.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4874.essence: Force can fail completely against a fixed mind.
ramacharitamanas::4874.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears keep attacking, but the enemy does not flinch. He stays unmoved, like an elephant ignoring weak blows.
ramacharitamanas::4874.simple_insight: Some resistance is so hardened that force alone cannot shake it.
ramacharitamanas::4874.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s battle, the bears and monkeys hurl mountain peaks at their foe again and again. The verse lingers on his stubborn unmoved state, building tension before Hanuman steps in and breaks that resistance.
ramacharitamanas::4874.modern_relevance: You keep explaining, pushing, and proving your point in a meeting, but the other person sits there unchanged. Sometimes brute force only reveals how fixed someone already is.
ramacharitamanas::4874.insight: It shows that not every obstacle yields to pressure; some must be met differently.

ramacharitamanas::4875.verse_sanskrit: तब मारुतसुत मुठिका हन्यो। परयो धरनि ब्याकुल सिर धुन्यो॥ पुनि उठि तेहिं मारेउ हनुमंता। घुर्मित भूतल परेउ तुरंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4875.verse_hindi: तब हनुमान् जी ने उसे एक घूँसा मारा, जिससे वह व्याकुल होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा और सिर पीटने लगा। फिर उसने उठकर हनुमान् जी को मारा। वे चक्कर खाकर तुरंत ही पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4875.english_translation: Then Hanuman struck him with his fist, and he fell to the ground, shaken and clutching his head. Rising again, he struck Hanuman, and Hanuman reeled and fell at once.
ramacharitamanas::4875.translation_literal: तब (then) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / मुठिका (with a fist) / हन्यो (struck) / परयो (fell) / धरनि (on the ground) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / सिर (head) / धुन्यो (shook) / पुनि (again) / उठि (rising) / तेहिं (by him) / मारेउ (struck) / हनुमंता (Hanuman) / घुर्मित (reeling) / भूतल (on the earth) / परेउ (fell) / तुरंता (immediately)
ramacharitamanas::4875.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4875.essence: The fight keeps surging back and forth.
ramacharitamanas::4875.simple_meaning: Hanuman and the enemy warrior trade blows in fierce combat, each knocking the other down in turn.
ramacharitamanas::4875.simple_insight: The scene is pure force and momentum, with no teaching beyond the clash itself.
ramacharitamanas::4875.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Hanuman is in the middle of a brutal exchange of blows. He drops one warrior, then is struck back and falls himself. The verse keeps the action moving, building the larger war scene rather than offering a separate lesson.
ramacharitamanas::4875.insight: It shows a combat beat, not a transferable principle.

ramacharitamanas::4876.verse_sanskrit: पुनि नल नीलहि अवनि पछारेसि। जहँ तहँ पटकि पटकि भट डारेसि॥ चली बलीमुख सेन पराई। अति भय त्रसित न कोउ समुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4876.verse_hindi: फिर उसने नल-नील को पृथ्वी पर पछाड़ दिया और दूसरे योद्धाओं को भी जहाँ-तहाँ पटककर डाल दिया। वानर सेना भाग चली। सब अत्यंत भयभीत हो गए, कोई सामने नहीं आता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4876.english_translation: Then he threw Nala and Neela to the ground and hurled warriors here and there. The monkey army fled. Everyone was terrified; no one dared face him.
ramacharitamanas::4876.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / नल नीलहि (Nala and Neela) / अवनि (earth) / पछारेसि (threw down) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / पटकि पटकि (repeatedly hurling) / भट (warriors) / डारेसि (threw) / चली (fled) / बलीमुख (powerful-faced) / सेन (army) / पराई (ran away) / अति (very) / भय (fear) / त्रसित (terrified) / न (not) / कोउ (anyone) / समुहाई (faced forward)
ramacharitamanas::4876.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4876.essence: Overwhelming force can scatter even a brave army.
ramacharitamanas::4876.simple_meaning: The enemy warrior overpowers Nala, Neela, and the monkey army, driving them into fear and retreat.
ramacharitamanas::4876.simple_insight: Sometimes courage needs a pause; even the brave can be shaken by overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::4876.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, one terrifying warrior crashes through the monkey ranks. Nala and Neela are thrown down, other fighters are tossed aside, and the army breaks in fear. The scene is still building toward the larger clash.
ramacharitamanas::4876.insight: It shows the battle turning through sheer force, before the next counterattack changes the tide.

ramacharitamanas::4877.verse_sanskrit: अंगदादि कपि मुरुछित करि समेत सुग्रीव। काँख दाबि कपिराज कहुँ चला अमित बल सींव ॥
ramacharitamanas::4877.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव समेत अंगदादि वानरों को मूर्छित करके फिर वह अपरिमित बल की सीमा कुंभकर्ण वानरराज सुग्रीव को काँख में दाबकर चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4877.english_translation: After knocking Angad and the other monkeys unconscious along with Sugriva, Kumbhakarna, with immense strength, carried the monkey king away under his arm.
ramacharitamanas::4877.translation_literal: अंगदादि (Angad and others) / कपि (monkeys) / मुरुछित (unconscious) / करि (having made) / समेत (along with) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / काँख (under the arm) / दाबि (pressing) / कपिराज (monkey king) / कहुँ (to) / चला (went) / अमित (immeasurable) / बल (strength) / सींव (boundary/limit)
ramacharitamanas::4877.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4877.essence: Raw strength can scatter a whole army in moments.
ramacharitamanas::4877.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna knocks out Angad and the other monkeys, then picks up Sugriva under his arm and carries him off.
ramacharitamanas::4877.simple_insight: The scene is about overwhelming force, not a lesson to apply directly.
ramacharitamanas::4877.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Kumbhakarna tears through the monkey ranks. Angad and the others collapse unconscious, and even Sugriva is seized and carried away. The verse keeps the action moving, showing the terror of his strength before Shiva’s reflection on Ram’s playfulness.
ramacharitamanas::4877.modern_relevance: A crowd freezes when one person’s anger takes over the room. Nothing is being argued anymore; sheer force has taken the stage.
ramacharitamanas::4877.insight: It shifts attention to the scale of the battle rather than a moral instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4878.verse_sanskrit: उमा करत रघुपति नरलीला। खेलत गरुड़ जिमि अहिगन मीला॥ भृकुटि भंग जो कालहि खाई। ताहि कि सोहइ ऐसि लराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4878.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! श्री रघुनाथजी वैसे ही नरलीला कर रहे हैं, जैसे गरुड़ सर्पों के समूह में मिलकर खेलता हो। जो भौंह के इशारे मात्र से (बिना परिश्रम के) काल को भी खा जाता है, उसे कहीं ऐसी लड़ाई शोभा देती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4878.english_translation: O Uma, Raghupati is performing a human drama, just as Garuda plays among a group of snakes. Does such a fight suit one who swallows even Time with a mere movement of his brow?
ramacharitamanas::4878.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma) / करत (is doing) / रघुपति (Lord Raghus, Ram) / नरलीला (human play) / खेलत (playing) / गरुड़ (Garuda) / जिमि (like) / अहिगन (among snakes) / मीला (mixed) / भृकुटि (eyebrow) / भंग (movement) / जो (who) / कालहि (Time) / खाई (devours) / ताहि (to him) / कि (does) / सोहइ (suit) / ऐसि (such) / लराई (fight)
ramacharitamanas::4878.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4878.essence: Ram enters battle as play, not as struggle.
ramacharitamanas::4878.simple_meaning: Ram is only appearing to fight like a human, while remaining far beyond danger. Such a battle cannot touch his true power.
ramacharitamanas::4878.simple_insight: What looks like struggle is only a divine play. You can stop confusing appearance with reality.
ramacharitamanas::4878.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Shiva speaks to Uma about Ram. Even while armies clash and Kumbhakarna rages, Shiva sees Ram as untouched, playing the role of a warrior the way Garuda moves among snakes. The verse reframes the war as divine play, not threat.
ramacharitamanas::4878.modern_relevance: You watch someone handle a crisis with complete ease while everyone else panics. What looks like pressure to others may be only the role they are playing, not their real condition.
ramacharitamanas::4878.insight: It shifts the mind from taking appearances literally to seeing the larger power beneath them.

ramacharitamanas::4879.verse_sanskrit: जग पावनि कीरति बिस्तरिहहिं। गाइ गाइ भवनिधि नर तरिहहिं॥ मुरुछा गइ मारुतसुत जागा। सुग्रीवहि तब खोजन लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4879.verse_hindi: भगवान् (इसके द्वारा) जगत् को पवित्र करने वाली वह कीर्ति फैलाएँगे, जिसे गा-गाकर मनुष्य भवसागर से तर जाएँगे। मूर्च्छा जाती रही, तब मारुति हनुमान् जी जागे और फिर वे सुग्रीव को खोजने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4879.english_translation: He will spread the fame that purifies the world; by singing it again and again, people will cross the ocean of becoming. When the swoon passed, Hanuman woke up and began searching for Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::4879.translation_literal: जग (world) / पावनि (purifying) / कीरति (fame, glory) / बिस्तरिहहिं (will spread) / गाइ (singing) / गाइ (singing) / भवनिधि (ocean of existence) / नर (people) / तरिहहिं (will cross) / मुरुछा (fainting) / गइ (went away) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / जागा (woke up) / सुग्रीवहि (Sugriva) / तब (then) / खोजन (to search) / लागा (began)
ramacharitamanas::4879.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4879.essence: Ram's fame saves; Hanuman wakes and serves again.
ramacharitamanas::4879.simple_meaning: Ram's glory will spread through the world and help people cross life's ocean. Meanwhile, Hanuman wakes from the blow and resumes searching for Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::4879.simple_insight: Even after collapse, devotion wakes up and continues the work.
ramacharitamanas::4879.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just been struck down in the chaos of battle. The verse turns from the promise of Ram's world-purifying fame to a sudden practical moment: Hanuman regains consciousness and immediately returns to his mission of finding Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::4879.modern_relevance: You get knocked sideways in the middle of a hard day, then remember what matters and get back to it. The work was never about your pride; it was about the mission.
ramacharitamanas::4879.insight: It shifts attention from personal setback to the next faithful step.

ramacharitamanas::4880.verse_sanskrit: सुग्रीवहु कै मुरुछा बीती। निबुकि गयउ तेहि मृतक प्रतीती॥ काटेसि दसन नासिका काना। गरजि अकास चलेउ तेहिं जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4880.verse_hindi: सुग्रीव की भी मूर्च्छा दूर हुई, तब वे (मुर्दे से होकर) खिसक गए (काँख से नीचे गिर पड़े)। कुम्भकर्ण ने उनको मृतक जाना। उन्होंने कुम्भकर्ण के नाक-कान दाँतों से काट लिए और फिर गरज कर आकाश की ओर चले, तब कुम्भकर्ण ने जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4880.english_translation: Sugriva's fainting spell passed too. Kumbhakarna thought he was dead, so he slipped under him. He bit off ears, nose, and teeth, then roared into the sky; only then did Kumbhakarna realize it.
ramacharitamanas::4880.translation_literal: सुग्रीवहु (of Sugriva too) / कै (was) / मुरुछा (fainting) / बीती (passed) / निबुकि (slipped under) / गयउ (went) / तेहि (him) / मृतक (dead) / प्रतीती (the belief) / काटेसि (he bit/cut) / दसन (teeth) / नासिका (nose) / काना (ears) / गरजि (roaring) / अकास (sky) / चलेउ (went) / तेहिं (then) / जाना (knew)
ramacharitamanas::4880.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4880.essence: A single misjudgment can turn defeat into sudden escape.
ramacharitamanas::4880.simple_meaning: Sugriva wakes from his fainting spell, and Kumbhakarna mistakes him for dead. Sugriva then attacks fiercely and leaps back into the sky.
ramacharitamanas::4880.simple_insight: Even in chaos, a hidden opening can appear the moment someone is underestimated.
ramacharitamanas::4880.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Kumbhakarna thinks Sugriva has died and lowers his guard. Sugriva suddenly revives, mauls him, and escapes upward. The verse is a fast-moving combat detail, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::4880.modern_relevance: In a match where everyone assumes you're finished, you catch one breath, rise, and change the whole rhythm. The moment they relax is the moment you move.
ramacharitamanas::4880.insight: It shows how quickly battlefield fortunes can reverse when one fighter misjudges the other.

ramacharitamanas::4881.verse_sanskrit: गहेउ चरन गहि भूमि पछारा। अति लाघवँ उठि पुनि तेहि मारा॥ पुनि आयउ प्रभु पहिं बलवाना। जयति जयति जय कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4881.verse_hindi: उसने सुग्रीव का पैर पकड़कर उनको पृथ्वी पर पछाड़ दिया। फिर सुग्रीव ने बड़ी फुर्ती से उठकर उसको मारा और तब बलवान् सुग्रीव प्रभु के पास आए और बोले- कृपानिधान प्रभु की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4881.english_translation: He seized Sugriva by the foot and threw him to the ground. Sugriva sprang up swiftly and struck him again. Then the mighty Sugriva came to the Lord and cried, “Victory, victory, victory to the ocean of mercy!”
ramacharitamanas::4881.translation_literal: गहेउ (seized) / चरन (foot) / गहि (grasping) / भूमि (ground) / पछारा (threw down) / अति (very) / लाघवँ (swiftly) / उठि (rising) / पुनि (again) / तेहि (him) / मारा (struck) / पुनि (again) / आयउ (came) / प्रभु (Lord) / पहिं (near) / बलवाना (the mighty one) / जयति (victory) / जयति (victory) / जय (victory) / कृपानिधाना (ocean of mercy)
ramacharitamanas::4881.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4881.essence: A setback does not end your strength; you can rise and return in praise.
ramacharitamanas::4881.simple_meaning: Sugriva is knocked down, gets up quickly, strikes back, and then returns to Ram praising His mercy.
ramacharitamanas::4881.simple_insight: No matter how hard you fall, you can rise again and return with gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::4881.detailed_meaning: In the battle with Kumbhakarna, Sugriva is hurled to the ground but springs back with speed and fights again. After the clash, he goes back to Ram and hails Him as the ocean of mercy. The verse mainly keeps the action moving.
ramacharitamanas::4881.modern_relevance: You get knocked flat in a tough meeting, recover fast, and keep going. The real win is not pretending you never fell — it is rising and returning steady.
ramacharitamanas::4881.insight: It shows resilience in action: fall, recover, respond, then come back to gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::4882.verse_sanskrit: नाक कान काटे जियँ जानी। फिरा क्रोध करि भइ मन ग्लानी॥ सहज भीम पुनि बिनु श्रुति नासा। देखत कपि दल उपजी त्रासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4882.verse_hindi: नाक-कान काटे गए, ऐसा मन में जानकर बड़ी ग्लानि हुई और वह क्रोध करके लौटा। एक तो वह स्वभाव (आकृति) से ही भयंकर था और फिर बिना नाक-कान का होने से और भी भयानक हो गया। उसे देखते ही वानरों की सेना में भय उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4882.english_translation: Seeing his nose and ears cut off, he returned in rage, filled with shame. Naturally terrible already, now disfigured without nose and ears, he terrified the monkey army at a glance.
ramacharitamanas::4882.translation_literal: नाक (nose) / कान (ears) / काटे (cut off) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानी (having known) / फिरा (returned) / क्रोध (anger) / करि (doing) / भइ (became) / मन (mind) / ग्लानी (shame, humiliation)॥ / सहज (naturally) / भीम (terrible, huge) / पुनि (again) / बिनु (without) / श्रुति (ears) / नासा (nose) / देखत (seeing) / कपि दल (monkey army) / उपजी (arose) / त्रासा (fear)॥
ramacharitamanas::4882.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4882.essence: Humiliation can harden into a more frightening force.
ramacharitamanas::4882.simple_meaning: He came back furious and humiliated after being disfigured. His terrifying appearance made the monkey army afraid.
ramacharitamanas::4882.simple_insight: Pride can turn pain into rage, and rage can spread fear fast.
ramacharitamanas::4882.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the wounded enemy returns after his nose and ears are cut off. Humiliated, he burns with anger. His already fearsome form becomes even more horrifying, and the monkey troops recoil before the sight of him.
ramacharitamanas::4882.modern_relevance: Someone gets publicly embarrassed in a meeting, leaves the room fuming, and comes back sharper and more dangerous. Humiliation often returns as intimidation.
ramacharitamanas::4882.insight: It shows how wounded pride can intensify aggression and unsettle everyone nearby.

ramacharitamanas::4883.verse_sanskrit: जय जय जय रघुबंस मनि धाए कपि दै हूह। एकहि बार तासु पर छाड़ेन्हि गिरि तरु जूह ॥
ramacharitamanas::4883.verse_hindi: 'रघुवंशमणि की जय हो, जय हो' ऐसा पुकारकर वानर हूह करके दौड़े और सबने एक ही साथ उस पर पहाड़ और वृक्षों के समूह छोड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4883.english_translation: “Victory, victory to the jewel of the Raghu line!” the monkeys cried, and with a roar they rushed forward. In one instant they hurled mountains and trees down upon him.
ramacharitamanas::4883.translation_literal: जय (victory) / जय (victory) / जय (victory) / रघुबंस मनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / धाए (rushed) / कपि (monkeys) / दै (giving) / हूह (roar) / एकहि बार (in one instant) / तासु पर (upon him) / छाड़ेन्हि (they hurled) / गिरि (mountains) / तरु (trees) / जूह (groups)
ramacharitamanas::4883.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4883.essence: Praise becomes force when everyone moves together.
ramacharitamanas::4883.simple_meaning: The monkeys shout Ram's praise and attack at once, hurling mountains and trees in a single surge.
ramacharitamanas::4883.simple_insight: Devotion turns into force without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4883.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the monkey army has already driven the enemy back. Now, praising Ram as the jewel of Raghu's line, they surge forward together and hurl mountains and trees at the foe. It is a battle movement, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4883.modern_relevance: A team hears the final call before a deadline and moves as one—no debate, no delay, just full commitment to the task.
ramacharitamanas::4883.insight: It shifts attention to collective action powered by shared devotion, not individual heroics.

ramacharitamanas::4884.verse_sanskrit: कुंभकरन रन रंग बिरुद्धा। सन्मुख चला काल जनु क्रुद्धा॥ कोटि कोटि कपि धरि धरि खाई। जनु टीड़ी गिरि गुहाँ समाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4884.verse_hindi: रण के उत्साह में कुंभकर्ण विरुद्ध होकर (उनके) सामने ऐसा चला मानो क्रोधित होकर काल ही आ रहा हो। वह करोड़-करोड़ वानरों को एक साथ पकड़कर खाने लगा! (वे उसके मुँह में इस तरह घुसने लगे) मानो पर्वत की गुफा में टिड्डियाँ समा रही हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4884.english_translation: Kumbhakarna, fierce in battle, strode forward against them like Death itself in anger. He seized and devoured countless monkeys, as if grasshoppers were disappearing into a mountain cave.
ramacharitamanas::4884.translation_literal: कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / रन (battle) / रंग (in the field) / बिरुद्धा (opposed) / सन्मुख (facing forward) / चला (walked) / काल (Death) / जनु (as if) / क्रुद्धा (angry)॥ / कोटि कोटि (countless) / कपि (monkeys) / धरि धरि (grabbing again and again) / खाई (ate) / जनु (as if) / टीड़ी (grasshoppers) / गिरि (mountain) / गुहाँ (cave) / समाई (entered) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4884.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4884.essence: Raw force turns battle into terror.
ramacharitamanas::4884.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna charges into battle like raging death and devours the monkey warriors by the countless.
ramacharitamanas::4884.simple_insight: Some force is so overwhelming that courage alone cannot stop it.
ramacharitamanas::4884.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Kumbhakarna enters the battlefield in a frenzy, turning the tide by sheer size and fury. The monkeys are no longer facing a warrior but a living catastrophe, and the verse lingers on their helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::4884.modern_relevance: A problem walks into the room already bigger than your plan — a deadline, a crisis, a person in full rage. Before you can think, it is already swallowing your options.
ramacharitamanas::4884.insight: It frames danger as overwhelming force, not a fair contest, heightening the urgency of the battle.

ramacharitamanas::4885.verse_sanskrit: कोटिन्ह गहि सरीर सन मर्दा। कोटिन्ह मीजि मिलव महि गर्दा॥ मुख नासा श्रवनन्हि कीं बाटा। निसरि पराहिं भालु कपि ठाटा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4885.verse_hindi: करोड़ों (वानरों) को पकड़कर उसने शरीर से मसल डाला। करोड़ों को हाथों से मलकर पृथ्वी की धूल में मिला दिया। (पेट में गए हुए) भालू और वानरों के ठट्ट के ठट्ट उसके मुख, नाक और कानों की राह से निकल-निकलकर भाग रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4885.english_translation: He seized millions and crushed them in his grip, ground millions into dust with his hands. Crowds of bears and monkeys kept pouring out through his mouth, nose, and ears.
ramacharitamanas::4885.translation_literal: कोटिन्ह (millions) / गहि (seizing) / सरीर (body) / सन (with) / मर्दा (crushed) / कोटिन्ह (millions) / मीजि (rubbing) / मिलव (mixed) / महि (earth) / गर्दा (dust) / मुख (mouth) / नासा (nose) / श्रवनन्हि (ears) / कीं (of) / बाटा (paths) / निसरि (coming out) / पराहिं (ran away) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / ठाटा (crowds)
ramacharitamanas::4885.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4885.essence: Kumbhakarna’s strength is so wild it turns the battlefield into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4885.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna is so huge and violent that he crushes countless bears and monkeys. Even after swallowing them, they spill back out through his face.
ramacharitamanas::4885.simple_insight: Raw force can be terrifying, but it is still only brute force.
ramacharitamanas::4885.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Kumbhakarna tears through the monkey army in a frenzy. The verse lingers on his monstrous strength and the chaos around him, not to teach a principle, but to intensify the war scene before the next blow.
ramacharitamanas::4885.insight: It heightens the battle’s scale by showing unstoppable physical violence, not reflective action.

ramacharitamanas::4886.verse_sanskrit: रन मद मत्त निसाचर दर्पा। बिस्व ग्रसिहि जनु ऐहि बिधि अर्पा॥ मुरे सुभट सब फिरहिं न फेरे। सूझ न नयन सुनहिं नहिं टेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4886.verse_hindi: रण के मद में मत्त राक्षस कुंभकर्ण इस प्रकार गर्वित हुआ, मानो विधाता ने उसको सारा विश्व अर्पण कर दिया हो और उसे वह ग्रास कर जाएगा। सब योद्धा भाग खड़े हुए, वे लौटाए भी नहीं लौटते। आँखों से उन्हें सूझ नहीं पड़ता और पुकारने से सुनते नहीं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::4886.english_translation: Intoxicated by the pride of battle, the demon became arrogant, as if fate had handed him the whole world to devour. The brave warriors ran away and would not turn back. They could not see with their eyes, and they could not hear when called.
ramacharitamanas::4886.translation_literal: रन (battle) / मद (intoxication) / मत्त (drunk, intoxicated) / निसाचर (demon) / दर्पा (became arrogant) / बिस्व (world) / ग्रसिहि (to devour) / जनु (as if) / ऐहि (to this) / बिधि (way) / अर्पा (handed over)॥ / मुरे (fled) / सुभट (brave warriors) / सब (all) / फिरहिं (turn back) / न (not) / फेरे (turned) / सूझ (see) / न (not) / नयन (eyes) / सुनहिं (hear) / नहिं (not) / टेरे (called)
ramacharitamanas::4886.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4886.essence: Overwhelming rage can make an army lose its senses.
ramacharitamanas::4886.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna’s battle fury makes everyone panic. The warriors flee, and in the chaos they cannot see or hear clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4886.simple_insight: Unchecked force spreads confusion so fast that even brave people lose their footing.
ramacharitamanas::4886.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Kumbhakarna surges forward in a terrifying rage. His overwhelming power breaks the courage of the opposing warriors, who scatter in panic and cannot even respond to calls to regroup.
ramacharitamanas::4886.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one furious person starts shouting. Even capable people stop thinking clearly when fear and force take over.
ramacharitamanas::4886.insight: It shows how raw aggression can paralyze an entire group before any real strategy begins.

ramacharitamanas::4887.verse_sanskrit: कुंभकरन कपि फौज बिडारी। सुनि धाई रजनीचर धारी॥ देखी राम बिकल कटकाई। रिपु अनीक नाना बिधि आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4887.verse_hindi: कुंभकर्ण ने वानर सेना को तितर-बितर कर दिया। यह सुनकर राक्षस सेना भी दौड़ी। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने देखा कि अपनी सेना व्याकुल है और शत्रु की नाना प्रकार की सेना आ गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4887.english_translation: Kumbhakarna scattered the monkey army. Hearing this, the demon army rushed forward. Ram saw his forces in distress and the enemy hosts arrive in many formations.
ramacharitamanas::4887.translation_literal: कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / कपि फौज (monkey army) / बिडारी (scattered) / सुनि (hearing) / धाई (rushed) / रजनीचर (night-walkers, demons) / धारी (arrayed, held formation) / देखी (seeing) / राम (Ram) / बिकल (distressed) / कटकाई (army) / रिपु (enemy) / अनीक (battle formations) / नाना बिधि (in many ways) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::4887.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4887.essence: The battle tightens when one side starts to break.
ramacharitamanas::4887.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna breaks the monkey ranks, and the demon army surges in response. Ram sees his own army shaken as the enemy advances in many formations.
ramacharitamanas::4887.simple_insight: Pressure reveals itself fast when the battle line starts to break.
ramacharitamanas::4887.detailed_meaning: On the Lankakand battlefield, Kumbhakarna tears through the monkey army and the demon forces rush in behind him. Ram watches his side falter as fresh enemy formations arrive, setting up the next command.
ramacharitamanas::4887.modern_relevance: A team meeting goes silent after one hard question, and suddenly everyone can feel the room tilt. The setback is visible before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::4887.insight: It shows the turning point where a leader must respond to a weakening front.

ramacharitamanas::4888.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सुग्रीव बिभीषन अनुज सँभारेहु सैन। मैं देखउँ खल बल दलहि बोले राजिवनैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4888.verse_hindi: तब कमलनयन श्री रामजी बोले- हे सुग्रीव! हे विभीषण! और हे लक्ष्मण! सुनो, तुम सेना को संभालना। मैं इस दुष्ट के बल और सेना को देखता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4888.english_translation: Then lotus-eyed Ram said: "Sugriva, Vibhishana, and Lakshman, hold the army together. I will look at this rogue's strength and forces."
ramacharitamanas::4888.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / अनुज (younger brother) / सँभारेहु (support/hold together) / सैन (army) / मैं (I) / देखउँ (will see) / खल (wicked one) / बल (strength) / दलहि (army) / बोले (said) / राजिवनैन (lotus-eyed)
ramacharitamanas::4888.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4888.essence: Clear seeing comes before decisive force.
ramacharitamanas::4888.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sugriva, Vibhishana, and Lakshman to hold the army steady while he assesses the enemy's strength.
ramacharitamanas::4888.simple_insight: Stay steady in the middle of pressure; clear seeing begins before action.
ramacharitamanas::4888.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Kumbhakarna has shattered the monkey ranks and the battle line is shaking. Ram turns to Sugriva, Vibhishana, and Lakshman, assigns them the army, and prepares to judge the enemy's real strength before striking.
ramacharitamanas::4888.modern_relevance: Your team is rattled, people are talking over each other, and the room feels close to panic. Instead of rushing blindly, someone has to steady the group and read the situation clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4888.insight: It shifts you from reactive chaos to calm assessment and organized response.

ramacharitamanas::4889.verse_sanskrit: कर सारंग साजि कटि भाथा। अरि दल दलन चले रघुनाथा॥ प्रथम कीन्हि प्रभु धनुष टंकोरा। रिपु दल बधिर भयउ सुनि सोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4889.verse_hindi: हाथ में शार्गंधनुष और कमर में तरकस सजाकर श्री रघुनाथजी शत्रु सेना को दलन करने चले। प्रभु ने पहले तो धनुष का टंकार किया, जिसकी भयानक आवाज सुनते ही शत्रु दल बहरा हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4889.english_translation: Armed with his bow and quiver, Raghunath went to crush the enemy army. First, the Lord sounded his bow, and the enemy ranks were stunned and deafened by the terrible roar.
ramacharitamanas::4889.translation_literal: कर (with) / सारंग (the bow) / साजि (adorned, equipped) / कटि (at the waist) / भाथा (quiver) / अरि (enemy) / दल (army) / दलन (to crush) / चले (went) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) ॥ / प्रथम (first) / कीन्हि (did) / प्रभु (the Lord) / धनुष (bow) / टंकोरा (a resounding twang) / रिपु (enemy) / दल (army) / बधिर (deaf) / भयउ (became) / सुनि (hearing) / सोरा (the roar)
ramacharitamanas::4889.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4889.essence: A single fearless presence can shake an entire army.
ramacharitamanas::4889.simple_meaning: Ram arms himself, goes to battle, and strikes his bow so powerfully that the enemy army is shaken and stunned.
ramacharitamanas::4889.simple_insight: Sometimes presence itself is the first victory.
ramacharitamanas::4889.detailed_meaning: The battlefield has already turned violent: Kumbhakarna has broken the monkey ranks, and Ram now steps forward to answer that chaos. He arms himself, advances toward the enemy, and sounds his bow so fiercely that the opposing army loses its composure before the real attack begins.
ramacharitamanas::4889.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and say nothing at first. Your calm, clear presence changes the temperature before a single argument starts.
ramacharitamanas::4889.insight: It shows how decisive presence can unsettle confusion before force is even used.

ramacharitamanas::4890.verse_sanskrit: सत्यसंध छाँड़े सर लच्छा। कालसर्प जनु चले सपच्छा॥ जहँ तहँ चले बिपुल नाराचा। लगे कटन भट बिकट पिसाचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4890.verse_hindi: फिर सत्यप्रतिज्ञ श्री रामजी ने एक लाख बाण छोड़े। वे ऐसे चले मानो पंखवाले काल सर्प चले हों। जहाँ-तहाँ बहुत से बाण चले, जिनसे भयंकर राक्षस योद्धा कटने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4890.english_translation: Then the truthful Ram released a hundred thousand arrows. They moved like winged serpents of death. Arrows flew everywhere, and the fierce demon warriors began to be cut down.
ramacharitamanas::4890.translation_literal: सत्यसंध (true to his vow) / छाँड़े (released) / सर (arrows) / लच्छा (a hundred thousand) / कालसर्प (serpent of death) / जनु (as if) / चले (moved) / सपच्छा (with wings) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / चले (moved) / बिपुल (many) / नाराचा (arrows) / लगे (began) / कटन (to cut down) / भट (warriors) / बिकट (fierce) / पिसाचा (fiends)
ramacharitamanas::4890.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4890.essence: Decisive force now matters more than hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4890.simple_meaning: Ram unleashes a huge rain of arrows, and the enemy warriors start falling under the attack.
ramacharitamanas::4890.simple_insight: Some moments in life call for decisive force, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4890.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram has already signaled that he will face the enemy directly. Now the fighting turns intense: his arrows fly in every direction, and Ravana's warriors begin to break under the assault.
ramacharitamanas::4890.modern_relevance: When a crisis finally reaches the point where talk is over, you stop circling the issue and act with full force.
ramacharitamanas::4890.insight: It shifts attention from strategy to execution in the decisive moment.

ramacharitamanas::4891.verse_sanskrit: कटहिं चरन उर सिर भुजदंडा। बहुतक बीर होहिं सत खंडा॥ घुर्मि घुर्मि घायल महि परहीं। उठि संभारि सुभट पुनि लरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4891.verse_hindi: उनके चरण, छाती, सिर और भुजदण्ड कट रहे हैं। बहुत से वीरों के सौ-सौ टुकड़े हो जाते हैं। घायल चक्कर खा-खाकर पृथ्वी पर पड़ रहे हैं। उत्तम योद्धा फिर संभलकर उठते और लड़ते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4891.english_translation: Their feet, chests, heads, and arms are being cut apart. Many warriors are split into a hundred pieces. Wounded, they reel and fall to the ground, then rise again and keep fighting.
ramacharitamanas::4891.translation_literal: कटहिं (are cut) / चरन (feet) / उर (chest) / सिर (head) / भुजदंडा (arms) / बहुतक (many) / बीर (warriors) / होहिं (become) / सत खंडा (hundred pieces) / घुर्मि घुर्मि (reeling again and again) / घायल (wounded) / महि (on the earth) / परहीं (fall) / उठि (rising) / संभारि (gathering themselves) / सुभट (brave warriors) / पुनि (again) / लरहीं (fight)
ramacharitamanas::4891.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4891.essence: Even shattered warriors rise and fight again.
ramacharitamanas::4891.simple_meaning: The battle is so fierce that warriors are being chopped apart, falling wounded, then getting up and fighting again.
ramacharitamanas::4891.simple_insight: Raw courage can keep a body moving even after it has been broken.
ramacharitamanas::4891.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the war has become savage and relentless. Warriors are being struck down in pieces, collapsing from wounds, then forcing themselves back up to fight again. This is a combat-detail verse, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4891.modern_relevance: A sports final goes into extra time and both teams are running on fumes, still chasing every loose ball. The verse captures sheer battle-hardened refusal to stop.
ramacharitamanas::4891.insight: It shows exhausted fighters still pushing forward, turning pain into renewed resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4892.verse_sanskrit: लागत बान जलद जिमि गाजहिं। बहुतक देखि कठिन सर भाजहिं॥ रुंड प्रचंड मुंड बिनु धावहिं। धरु धरु मारु मारु धुनि गावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4892.verse_hindi: बाण लगते ही वे मेघ की तरह गरजते हैं। बहुत से तो कठिन बाणों को देखकर ही भाग जाते हैं। बिना मुण्ड (सिर) के प्रचण्ड रुण्ड (धड़) दौड़ रहे हैं और 'पकड़ो, पकड़ो, मारो, मारो' का शब्द करते हुए गा (चिल्ला) रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4892.english_translation: As the arrows strike, they roar like clouds. Many flee just at the sight of the fierce shafts. Trunks without heads rush about, crying, 'Catch them, catch them, kill them, kill them.'
ramacharitamanas::4892.translation_literal: लागत (on striking) / बान (arrows) / जलद (clouds) / जिमि (like) / गाजहिं (they thunder) / बहुतक (many) / देखि (seeing) / कठिन (fierce, hard) / सर (arrows) / भाजहिं (flee) / रुंड (trunks) / प्रचंड (terrible) / मुंड (head) / बिनु (without) / धावहिं (run) / धरु धरु (catch, catch) / मारु मारु (kill, kill) / धुनि (sound) / गावहिं (sing, cry out)
ramacharitamanas::4892.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4892.essence: Violence has become so wild that even the fallen seem to keep fighting.
ramacharitamanas::4892.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so fierce that arrows thunder, enemies flee, and headless bodies keep rushing and shouting.
ramacharitamanas::4892.simple_insight: War can become so chaotic that fear and violence seem to move on their own.
ramacharitamanas::4892.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has become a storm of arrows and collapsing warriors. Ravana's forces are being cut down so fast that even headless bodies seem to keep moving. This verse is a vivid combat detail, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4892.modern_relevance: A crisis can get so intense that people stop thinking clearly and start reacting on instinct alone.
ramacharitamanas::4892.insight: It shows battle as chaos without reflection, where motion continues even after judgment is gone.

ramacharitamanas::4893.verse_sanskrit: छन महुँ प्रभु के सायकन्हि काटे बिकट पिसाच। पुनि रघुबीर निषंग महुँ प्रबिसे सब नाराच ॥
ramacharitamanas::4893.verse_hindi: प्रभु के बाणों ने क्षण मात्र में भयानक राक्षसों को काटकर रख दिया। फिर वे सब बाण लौटकर श्री रघुनाथजी के तरकस में घुस गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4893.english_translation: In an instant, the Lord's arrows cut down the terrible demons. Then all the arrows returned and entered Raghubir's quiver.
ramacharitamanas::4893.translation_literal: छन महुँ (in an instant) / प्रभु (the Lord) / के (of) / सायकन्हि (arrows) / काटे (cut) / बिकट (terrible) / पिसाच (demons) / पुनि (again) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / निषंग महुँ (into the quiver) / प्रबिसे (entered) / सब (all) / नाराच (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::4893.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4893.essence: Ram's arrows strike and return in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::4893.simple_meaning: Ram's arrows destroy the demons instantly, and then return to his quiver.
ramacharitamanas::4893.simple_insight: The scene is about unstoppable force, not a teaching to hold onto.
ramacharitamanas::4893.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ram's arrows slice through the demon ranks so quickly that the battlefield barely has time to react. The verse simply records the speed and power of the fighting before Kumbhakarna enters the scene.
ramacharitamanas::4893.modern_relevance: A news alert flashes, then the next one replaces it before you can process the first. This verse is not asking you to reflect; it is showing the pace of war.
ramacharitamanas::4893.insight: It keeps attention on the battle's motion, not on a moral principle.

ramacharitamanas::4894.verse_sanskrit: कुंभकरन मन दीख बिचारी। हति छन माझ निसाचर धारी॥ भा अति क्रुद्ध महाबल बीरा। कियो मृगनायक नाद गँभीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4894.verse_hindi: कुंभकर्ण ने मन में विचार कर देखा कि श्री रामजी ने क्षण मात्र में राक्षसी सेना का संहार कर डाला। तब वह महाबली वीर अत्यंत क्रोधित हुआ और उसने गंभीर सिंहनाद किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4894.english_translation: Kumbhakarna thought to himself that Ram had destroyed the demon army in an instant. Then that mighty warrior grew furious and let out a deep lion's roar.
ramacharitamanas::4894.translation_literal: कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / मन (mind) / दीख (saw) / बिचारी (considering) / हति (having killed) / छन माझ (in an instant) / निसाचर धारी (the demon host) / भा (became) / अति (very) / क्रुद्ध (angry) / महाबल बीरा (mighty warrior) / कियो (made) / मृगनायक नाद (lion-like roar) / गँभीरा (deep)
ramacharitamanas::4894.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4894.essence: Kumbhakarna's pride answers Ram's victory with rage.
ramacharitamanas::4894.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna sees how quickly Ram has wiped out the demon forces, and his anger bursts out in a thunderous roar.
ramacharitamanas::4894.simple_insight: Pride turns instantly into fury when it cannot control the moment.
ramacharitamanas::4894.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Kumbhakarna watches Ram cut down the demon army in moments. The sight inflames him, and his first response is a deep, terrifying roar. The verse is a battle beat, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4894.insight: It shows the next escalation in the war: a defeated side hardening into fiercer resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4895.verse_sanskrit: कोपि महीधर लेइ उपारी। डारइ जहँ मर्कट भट भारी॥ आवत देखि सैल प्रभु भारे। सरन्हि काटि रज सम करि डारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4895.verse_hindi: वह क्रोध करके पर्वत उखाड़ लेता है और जहाँ भारी-भारी वानर योद्धा होते हैं, वहाँ डाल देता है। बड़े-बड़े पर्वतों को आते देखकर प्रभु ने उनको बाणों से काटकर धूल के समान (चूर-चूर) कर डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4895.english_translation: He angrily uproots a mountain and hurls it where the mighty monkey warriors stand. Seeing the mountains come flying, the Lord cuts them apart with arrows and scatters them like dust.
ramacharitamanas::4895.translation_literal: कोपि (angrily) / महीधर (mountain) / लेइ (taking) / उपारी (uprooted) / डारइ (throws) / जहँ (where) / मर्कट (monkey) / भट (warriors) / भारी (mighty) / आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / सैल (mountains) / प्रभु (the Lord) / भारे (heavy/mighty) / सरन्हि (with arrows) / काटि (cutting) / रज (dust) / सम (like) / करि (making) / डारे (scattered)
ramacharitamanas::4895.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4895.essence: Raw force collapses when it meets precise response.
ramacharitamanas::4895.simple_meaning: Kumbhakaran tears up mountains and throws them at the monkey warriors, but Ram cuts the mountains to dust with his arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4895.simple_insight: No force is too large when steady skill meets it.
ramacharitamanas::4895.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Kumbhakaran hurls mountains at the monkey army in rage. Ram answers instantly, slicing the flying rocks apart before they can land. The verse is part of a fast-moving combat sequence, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4895.modern_relevance: A crisis can feel like one huge thing thrown at you at once. This verse stays in the moment of impact: meet the threat quickly, cleanly, and without panic.
ramacharitamanas::4895.insight: It shows how disciplined response can break even overwhelming force into harmless pieces.

ramacharitamanas::4896.verse_sanskrit: पुनि धनु तानि कोपि रघुनायक। छाँड़े अति कराल बहु सायक॥ तनु महुँ प्रबिसि निसरि सर जाहीं। जिमि दामिनि घन माझ समाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4896.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी ने क्रोध करके धनुष को तानकर बहुत से अत्यंत भयानक बाण छोड़े। वे बाण कुंभकर्ण के शरीर में घुसकर (पीछे से इस प्रकार) निकल जाते हैं (कि उनका पता नहीं चलता), जैसे बिजलियाँ बादल में समा जाती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4896.english_translation: Then Raghunath drew his bow in anger and released many terrible arrows. The arrows entered Kumbhakarna's body and came out unseen, like lightning disappearing into a cloud.
ramacharitamanas::4896.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / धनु (bow) / तानि (drawing tight) / कोपि (angrily) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / छाँड़े (released) / अति (very) / कराल (fierce, terrible) / बहु (many) / सायक (arrows)॥ / तनु (body) / महुँ (into) / प्रबिसि (entering) / निसरि (coming out) / सर (arrows) / जाहीं (go) / जिमि (like) / दामिनि (lightning) / घन (cloud) / माझ (within) / समाहीं (disappear)॥
ramacharitamanas::4896.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4896.essence: Ram's arrows pass through resistance as if it were empty air.
ramacharitamanas::4896.simple_meaning: Ram draws his bow and sends fierce arrows into Kumbhakarna's body. The arrows pass through him so completely that they vanish, like lightning swallowed by a cloud.
ramacharitamanas::4896.simple_insight: Some force is so complete that resistance cannot hold it.
ramacharitamanas::4896.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Kumbhakarna has just smashed through armies and mountains. Ram answers by drawing his bow and releasing arrows so fierce they pierce the giant clean through. This is part of the escalating combat, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4896.modern_relevance: The moment a crisis turns physical, there is no speech left — only decisive action. This verse sits inside that surge, where force meets force and the field keeps moving.
ramacharitamanas::4896.insight: It shows unstoppable response: when the moment demands it, Ram's action goes straight through obstruction.

ramacharitamanas::4897.verse_sanskrit: सोनित स्रवत सोह तन कारे। जनु कज्जल गिरि गेरु पनारे॥ बिकल बिलोकि भालु कपि धाए। बिहँसा जबहिं निकट कपि आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4897.verse_hindi: उसके काले शरीर से रुधिर बहता हुआ ऐसे शोभा देता है, मानो काजल के पर्वत से गेरु के पनाले बह रहे हों। उसे व्याकुल देखकर रीछ वानर दौड़े। वे ज्यों ही निकट आए, त्यों ही वह हँसा, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4897.english_translation: Blood flowed from his dark body, looking like red streams running from a mountain of lampblack. Seeing him stagger, the bears and monkeys rushed in. As soon as they came close, he laughed.
ramacharitamanas::4897.translation_literal: सोनित (blood) / स्रवत (flowing) / सोह (looked beautiful) / तन (body) / कारे (dark) // जनु (as if) / कज्जल (lampblack) / गिरि (mountain) / गेरु (red earth) / पनारे (streams) // बिकल (unsteady) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / धाए (rushed) // बिहँसा (he laughed) / जबहिं (as soon as) / निकट (near) / कपि (monkeys) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::4897.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4897.simple_meaning: Ravana is bleeding badly, the monkey and bear warriors rush toward him, and he suddenly laughs when they get close.
ramacharitamanas::4897.simple_insight: Even in the middle of chaos, the enemy can turn fear into mockery.
ramacharitamanas::4897.detailed_meaning: In the battle of Lanka, Ravana has just been struck hard. His dark body is streaming with blood, and the monkey and bear warriors surge toward him, thinking he is weakened. But when they close in, he laughs, showing the fight is far from over.
ramacharitamanas::4897.modern_relevance: You see someone stumble in a heated argument and think they’re done. Then they look up, smile, and the whole room realizes the conflict is not finished.
ramacharitamanas::4897.insight: It keeps the scene in motion: apparent weakness can hide a fresh burst of resistance.

ramacharitamanas::4898.verse_sanskrit: महानाद करि गर्जा कोटि कोटि गहि कीस। महि पटकइ गजराज इव सपथ करइ दससीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4898.verse_hindi: और बड़ा घोर शब्द करके गरजा तथा करोड़-करोड़ वानरों को पकड़कर वह गजराज की तरह उन्हें पृथ्वी पर पटकने लगा और रावण की दुहाई देने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4898.english_translation: Then, roaring fiercely, he seized countless monkeys and hurled them to the ground like an elephant, calling on Ravana's name as he fought.
ramacharitamanas::4898.translation_literal: महानाद (with a great roar) / करि (doing) / गर्जा (roared) / कोटि कोटि (countless, countless) / गहि (seizing) / कीस (monkeys) / महि (on the earth) / पटकइ (hurls, throws down) / गजराज इव (like an elephant king) / सपथ करइ (takes an oath, calls on as witness) / दससीस (Ravana, the ten-headed one)
ramacharitamanas::4898.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4898.essence: Violence surges here as a war detail, not a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::4898.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna roars, grabs hordes of monkeys, and slams them to the ground while shouting Ravana's name.
ramacharitamanas::4898.simple_insight: Raw force can overwhelm bodies, but it cannot create victory.
ramacharitamanas::4898.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Kumbhakarna rages through the battlefield after being struck by Ram's arrows. He roars, seizes monkey warriors in bulk, and throws them down like an elephant. The verse shows the terrifying scale of his violence, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4898.insight: It frames the scene as battlefield fury, not reflection.

ramacharitamanas::4899.verse_sanskrit: भागे भालु बलीमुख जूथा। बृकु बिलोकि जिमि मेष बरूथा॥ चले भागि कपि भालु भवानी। बिकल पुकारत आरत बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4899.verse_hindi: यह देखकर रीछ-वानरों के झुंड ऐसे भागे जैसे भेड़िये को देखकर भेड़ों के झुंड! (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! वानर-भालू व्याकुल होकर आर्तवाणी से पुकारते हुए भाग चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4899.english_translation: Seeing this, the bear and monkey groups fled like sheep before a wolf. O Bhavani, the monkeys and bears fled in distress, crying out in helpless fear.
ramacharitamanas::4899.translation_literal: भागे (fled) / भालु (bears) / बलीमुख (monkey-faced) / जूथा (groups) / बृकु (wolf) / बिलोकि (seeing) / जिमि (like) / मेष (sheep) / बरूथा (flocks) / चले (went) / भागि (fleeing) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / भवानी (O Bhavani) / बिकल (distressed) / पुकारत (crying out) / आरत (helpless) / बानी (voice)
ramacharitamanas::4899.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4899.essence: Panic spreads faster than strength in a battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4899.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear armies panic and run when they see the enemy. This is a battle scene showing fear spreading through the ranks.
ramacharitamanas::4899.simple_insight: Fear can break a group in seconds when danger feels overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::4899.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Ravana's assault has thrown the monkey and bear forces into panic. Shiva, speaking to Parvati, describes them scattering like sheep before a wolf. The verse prepares for the next turn in the battle, where fear gives way to a plea for divine help.
ramacharitamanas::4899.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one harsh voice cuts through the meeting. People who were ready a moment ago suddenly lose their nerve and look for the exit.
ramacharitamanas::4899.insight: It shows how quickly courage collapses when fear becomes contagious.

ramacharitamanas::4900.verse_sanskrit: यह निसिचर दुकाल सम अहई। कपिकुल देस परन अब चहई॥ कृपा बारिधर राम खरारी। पाहि पाहि प्रनतारति हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4900.verse_hindi: (वे कहने लगे-) यह राक्षस दुर्भिक्ष के समान है, जो अब वानर कुल रूपी देश में पड़ना चाहता है। हे कृपा रूपी जल के धारण करने वाले मेघ रूप श्री राम! हे खर के शत्रु! हे शरणागत के दुःख हरने वाले! रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए! ॥।
ramacharitamanas::4900.english_translation: “This demon is like a famine, and now it wants to fall upon the monkey race’s land. O Ram, cloud of compassion, slayer of the demon Khara, protector of those who take refuge, save us, save us!”
ramacharitamanas::4900.translation_literal: यह (this) / निसिचर (demon) / दुकाल (famine) / सम (like) / अहई (is) । / कपिकुल (monkey race) / देस (land) / परन (to fall upon) / अब (now) / चहई (wants) । / कृपा (compassion) / बारिधर (cloud-bearer) / राम (Ram) / खरारी (enemy of Khara) । / पाहि (protect) / पाहि (protect) / प्रनतारति-हारी (remover of the distress of those who take refuge) ।
ramacharitamanas::4900.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4900.essence: When danger swallows everything, refuge becomes the only real answer.
ramacharitamanas::4900.simple_meaning: The monkey army sees Ravana’s attack as a disaster and cries out to Ram for rescue.
ramacharitamanas::4900.simple_insight: In fear, the mind still knows where safety lives.
ramacharitamanas::4900.detailed_meaning: The battlefield has turned desperate. Ravana’s terror is scattering the monkey and bear forces, and they cry to Ram as their only shelter. This verse is part of that urgent call for protection, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4900.modern_relevance: When everything feels like it is collapsing at once, you stop arguing with the moment and reach for the one thing that can steady you.
ramacharitamanas::4900.insight: It shifts panic into refuge, turning helplessness into a direct call for help.

ramacharitamanas::4901.verse_sanskrit: सकरुन बचन सुनत भगवाना। चले सुधारि सरासन बाना॥ राम सेन निज पाछें घाली। चले सकोप महा बलसाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4901.verse_hindi: करुणा भरे वचन सुनते ही भगवान् धनुष-बाण सुधारकर चले। महाबलशाली श्री रामजी ने सेना को अपने पीछे कर लिया और वे (अकेले) क्रोधपूर्वक चले (आगे बढ़े) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4901.english_translation: Hearing those sorrowful words, the Lord set his bow and arrow in order. Ram placed his army behind him and moved forward in fierce anger, mighty and alone.
ramacharitamanas::4901.translation_literal: सकरुन (full of compassion) / बचन (words) / सुनत (hearing) / भगवाना (the Lord) / चले (moved) / सुधारि (setting right) / सरासन (bow) / बाना (arrow) / राम (Ram) / सेन (army) / निज (his own) / पाछें (behind) / घाली (placed) / चले (moved) / सकोप (with anger) / महा (great) / बलसाली (mighty)
ramacharitamanas::4901.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4901.essence: True strength steps forward first and leaves fear behind.
ramacharitamanas::4901.simple_meaning: Hearing the plea, Ram readies his bow, puts his army behind him, and advances alone in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4901.simple_insight: Sometimes real protection means stepping forward first, not waiting for others to move.
ramacharitamanas::4901.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, frightened allies speak in distress after seeing the enemy’s force. Ram hears their sorrow, readies his weapons, and moves ahead with his army kept behind him. The verse sets up the attack that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4901.modern_relevance: A family crisis hits, everyone starts talking at once, and you quietly step forward to handle the hardest part yourself.
ramacharitamanas::4901.insight: It shows decisive leadership: absorb the fear, gather your strength, and move before panic spreads.

ramacharitamanas::4902.verse_sanskrit: खैंचि धनुष सर सत संधाने। छूटे तीर सरीर समाने॥ लागत सर धावा रिस भरा। कुधर डगमगत डोलति धरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4902.verse_hindi: उन्होंने धनुष को खींचकर सौ बाण संधान किए। बाण छूटे और उसके शरीर में समा गए। बाणों के लगते ही वह क्रोध में भरकर दौड़ा। उसके दौड़ने से पर्वत डगमगाने लगे और पृथ्वी हिलने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4902.english_translation: He drew his bow and loosed a hundred arrows. The arrows entered his body. Hit by the arrows, he ran in rage. His charging made the mountains shake and the earth tremble.
ramacharitamanas::4902.translation_literal: खैंचि (drawing) / धनुष (bow) / सर (arrows) / सत (hundred) / संधाने (set in place) / छूटे (were released) / तीर (arrows) / सरीर (body) / समाने (entered) / लागत (on striking) / सर (arrows) / धावा (rushed) / रिस (rage) / भरा (filled) / कुधर (mountains) / डगमगत (shaking) / डोलति (trembling) / धरा (earth)
ramacharitamanas::4902.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4902.essence: Rage hit by force only grows more violent.
ramacharitamanas::4902.simple_meaning: Ram draws his bow, sends a hundred arrows, and wounds the enemy. Enraged, the enemy charges so violently that the mountains and earth shake.
ramacharitamanas::4902.simple_insight: Power can turn rage into motion, but that fury still shakes the world around it.
ramacharitamanas::4902.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ram faces a furious enemy in single combat. He answers with precise force: a hundred arrows in an instant. The enemy's rage only makes the battle more violent, and the whole battlefield seems to tremble.
ramacharitamanas::4902.modern_relevance: A shouting argument can feel like this: one sharp reply, then the other person storms back harder, and the whole room goes tense. Escalation spreads fast.
ramacharitamanas::4902.insight: It shows how violence and anger amplify each other until the whole field of action is disturbed.

ramacharitamanas::4903.verse_sanskrit: लीन्ह एक तेंहि सैल उपाटी। रघुकुलतिलक भुजा सोइ काटी॥ धावा बाम बाहु गिरि धारी। प्रभु सोउ भुजा काटि महि पारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4903.verse_hindi: उसने एक पर्वत उखाड़ लिया। रघुकुल तिलक श्री रामजी ने उसकी वह भुजा ही काट दी। तब वह बाएँ हाथ में पर्वत को लेकर दौड़ा। प्रभु ने उसकी वह भुजा भी काटकर पृथ्वी पर गिरा दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4903.english_translation: He uprooted a mountain. Raghukul's jewel Ram cut off that arm too. Then he ran with the mountain in his left arm. The Lord cut off that arm as well and dropped it to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::4903.translation_literal: लीन्ह (took) / एक (one) / तेंहि (then he) / सैल (mountain) / उपाटी (uprooted) / रघुकुलतिलक (ornament of the Raghu clan) / भुजा (arm) / सोइ (that same) / काटी (cut off) / धावा (ran) / बाम (left) / बाहु (arm) / गिरि (mountain) / धारी (holding) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सोउ (that too) / भुजा (arm) / काटि (cutting) / महि (on the earth) / पारी (threw down)
ramacharitamanas::4903.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4903.essence: Pride keeps charging even after it has already been cut down.
ramacharitamanas::4903.simple_meaning: The enemy keeps fighting even after losing an arm, and Ram cuts down that second attack too.
ramacharitamanas::4903.simple_insight: Violence fed by pride only shrinks the attacker further.
ramacharitamanas::4903.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final battle, a furious warrior tears up a mountain and rushes back into attack. Ram answers each surge instantly, cutting off both arms. The scene is pure combat motion, showing the enemy's rage and Ram's unstoppable control.
ramacharitamanas::4903.modern_relevance: A person lashes out in a meeting, then doubles down when corrected. The more they push from anger, the more exposed their weakness becomes.
ramacharitamanas::4903.insight: It shows how unchecked aggression collapses under clear, decisive response.

ramacharitamanas::4904.verse_sanskrit: काटें भुजा सोह खल कैसा। पच्छहीन मंदर गिरि जैसा॥ उग्र बिलोकनि प्रभुहि बिलोका। ग्रसन चहत मानहुँ त्रैलोका ॥
ramacharitamanas::4904.verse_hindi: भुजाओं के कट जाने पर वह दुष्ट कैसी शोभा पाने लगा, जैसे बिना पंख का मंदराचल पहाड़ हो। उसने उग्र दृष्टि से प्रभु को देखा। मानो तीनों लोकों को निगल जाना चाहता हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4904.english_translation: How strange that the villain looked after losing his arms, like Mount Mandara without wings. He stared at the Lord with a fierce glare, as if he meant to swallow the three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::4904.translation_literal: काटें (after being cut) / भुजा (arms) / सोह (looked beautiful/strange) / खल (villain) / कैसा (how) / पच्छहीन (without wings) / मंदर (Mandara) / गिरि (mountain) / जैसा (like) / उग्र (fierce) / बिलोकनि (gaze) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोका (looked) / ग्रसन (to swallow) / चहत (wanting) / मानहुँ (as if) / त्रैलोका (the three worlds) (to swallow)
ramacharitamanas::4904.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4904.essence: Pride can keep roaring long after its strength is gone.
ramacharitamanas::4904.simple_meaning: With both arms cut off, the enemy still glares at Ram like a wingless mountain, as if he can devour everything.
ramacharitamanas::4904.simple_insight: Pride can remain fierce even after it has been wounded.
ramacharitamanas::4904.detailed_meaning: In the Lanka war, Ram has already cut off the warrior's arms. Instead of yielding, the enemy only grows more terrifying, glaring at Ram with blind rage. The image shows ego refusing to surrender even when physically broken.
ramacharitamanas::4904.modern_relevance: Someone gets called out in a meeting, loses the argument, and still keeps pushing with the same hardened face. Wounded pride can look stronger than it is.
ramacharitamanas::4904.insight: It shows how ego can stay aggressive even when its power has been shattered.

ramacharitamanas::4905.verse_sanskrit: करि चिक्कार घोर अति धावा बदनु पसारि। गगन सिद्ध सुर त्रासित हा हा हेति पुकारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4905.verse_hindi: वह बड़े जोर से चिग्घाड़ करके मुँह फैलाकर दौड़ा। आकाश में सिद्ध और देवता डरकर हा! हा! हा! इस प्रकार पुकारने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4905.english_translation: He roared fiercely and rushed forward, mouth wide open. The siddhas and radiant beings in the sky cried out in fear, "Alas! Alas!"
ramacharitamanas::4905.translation_literal: करि (doing) / चिक्कार (a loud roar) / घोर (terrible) / अति (very) / धावा (rushed) / बदनु (mouth) / पसारि (spreading open) / गगन (sky) / सिद्ध (siddhas) / सुर (radiant beings) / त्रासित (frightened) / हा हा हेति (with cries of "ha ha") / पुकारि (calling out)
ramacharitamanas::4905.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4905.essence: Raw fury can shake even the unseen witnesses above.
ramacharitamanas::4905.simple_meaning: The enemy charges with a terrifying roar, and even the beings in the sky are shaken with fear.
ramacharitamanas::4905.simple_insight: Some moments are so fierce that fear spreads beyond the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4905.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the wounded warrior keeps charging even after losing his arms. His rage is so terrible that the siddhas and radiant beings above cry out in alarm. The verse only heightens the combat before Ram's next response.
ramacharitamanas::4905.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when one furious person storms in, and everyone feels the tension before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4905.insight: It sharpens the scene of danger, showing how overwhelming force can unsettle everyone around it.

ramacharitamanas::4906.verse_sanskrit: सभय देव करुनानिधि जान्यो। श्रवन प्रजंत सरासुन तान्यो॥ बिसिख निकर निसिचर मुख भरेऊ। तदपि महाबल भूमि न परेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4906.verse_hindi: करुणानिधान भगवान् ने देवताओं को भयभीत जाना। तब उन्होंने धनुष को कान तक तानकर राक्षस के मुख को बाणों के समूह से भर दिया। तो भी वह महाबली पृथ्वी पर न गिरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4906.english_translation: The compassionate Lord saw the gods afraid. He drew the bow to his ear and filled the demon's mouth with arrows. Even so, that mighty one did not fall to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::4906.translation_literal: सभय (afraid) / देव (the gods) / करुनानिधि (ocean of compassion) / जान्यो (saw, knew) / श्रवन (ear) / प्रजंत (up to) / सरासुन (bow and arrow) / तान्यो (drew) / बिसिख (arrows) / निकर (group, cluster) / निसिचर (demon) / मुख (mouth) / भरेऊ (filled) / तदपि (even then) / महाबल (greatly strong) / भूमि (ground) / न (not) / परेऊ (fell)
ramacharitamanas::4906.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4906.essence: Compassion does not prevent force when force is needed.
ramacharitamanas::4906.simple_meaning: Ram sees the frightened gods, draws his bow fully, and rains arrows into the demon's mouth. Even after that, the demon still does not fall.
ramacharitamanas::4906.simple_insight: Some battles do not end with the first blow. Courage sometimes means striking again without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4906.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the demon has already lost his arms yet keeps rushing forward in rage. Ram sees the gods trembling, draws the bow to his ear, and fills the demon's mouth with arrows. Still, the enemy remains standing.
ramacharitamanas::4906.modern_relevance: You finally speak up in a room where everyone else is frozen. Even after your first clear boundary, the pressure keeps coming, and you have to stay steady.
ramacharitamanas::4906.insight: It shows that decisive action may need to be repeated until resistance truly breaks.

ramacharitamanas::4907.verse_sanskrit: सरन्हि भरा मुख सन्मुख धावा। काल त्रोन सजीव जनु आवा॥ तब प्रभु कोपि तीब्र सर लीन्हा। धर ते भिन्न तासु सिर कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4907.verse_hindi: मुख में बाण भरे हुए वह (प्रभु के) सामने दौड़ा। मानो काल रूपी सजीव तरकस ही आ रहा हो। तब प्रभु ने क्रोध करके तीक्ष्ण बाण लिया और उसके सिर को धड़ से अलग कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4907.english_translation: He rushed straight toward the Lord, his mouth full of arrows, like living Death itself. Then the Lord, in anger, took a sharp arrow and severed his head from his body.
ramacharitamanas::4907.translation_literal: सरन्हि (arrows) / भरा (filled) / मुख (mouth) / सन्मुख (straight toward) / धावा (rushed) / काल (Death) / त्रोन (quiver) / सजीव (living) / जनु (as if) / आवा (came) / तब (then) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कोपि (angrily) / तीब्र (sharp) / सर (arrow) / लीन्हा (took) / धर (from the body) / ते (from) / भिन्न (separated) / तासु (his) / सिर (head) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::4907.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4907.essence: Danger is met with immediate, forceful action.
ramacharitamanas::4907.simple_meaning: A fierce enemy charged at Ram with arrows in his mouth. Ram answered at once by cutting off his head.
ramacharitamanas::4907.simple_insight: Some moments leave no room for hesitation; action must meet danger directly.
ramacharitamanas::4907.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, a terrible demon charges Ram with arrows in his mouth, looking like Death itself come alive. Ram responds instantly in battle and cuts off his head. The verse is part of a fast-moving combat sequence, not a teaching moment on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4907.modern_relevance: A crisis hits before you have time to think: a phone call, a crash, a sudden accusation. In that instant, there is only response, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4907.insight: It shows direct, decisive response under threat, without delay or confusion.

ramacharitamanas::4908.verse_sanskrit: सो सिर परेउ दसानन आगें। बिकल भयउ जिमि फनि मनि त्यागें॥ धरनि धसइ धर धाव प्रचंडा। तब प्रभु काटि कीन्ह दुइ खंडा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4908.verse_hindi: वह सिर रावण के आगे जा गिरा उसे देखकर रावण ऐसा व्याकुल हुआ जैसे मणि के छूट जाने पर सर्प। कुंभकर्ण का प्रचण्ड धड़ दौड़ा, जिससे पृथ्वी धँसी जाती थी। तब प्रभु ने काटकर उसके दो टुकड़े कर दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4908.english_translation: The head fell before Ravana, and he was shaken like a serpent losing its jewel. The mighty body rushed on, making the earth sink, and the Lord cut it into two pieces.
ramacharitamanas::4908.translation_literal: सो (that) / सिर (head) / परेउ (fell) / दसानन (Ravana) / आगें (before) / बिकल (disturbed) / भयउ (became) / जिमि (like) / फनि (serpent) / मनि (jewel) / त्यागें (having lost) ॥ धरनि (earth) / धसइ (sinks) / धर (the ground) / धाव (rushed) / प्रचंडा (mighty) ॥ तब (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / काटि (cutting) / कीन्ह (made) / दुइ (two) / खंडा (pieces) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4908.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4908.essence: Momentum without awareness keeps charging until it is cut down.
ramacharitamanas::4908.simple_meaning: Ravana is shaken when he sees the fallen head, and the huge body keeps charging until Ram cuts it into two.
ramacharitamanas::4908.simple_insight: Some force keeps moving even after its heart is gone — until it is finally stopped.
ramacharitamanas::4908.detailed_meaning: In the heat of the Lanka battle, Kumbhakarna has just been struck down. His severed head falls before Ravana, rattling him, while the enormous body still surges forward and presses the earth down. Ram ends the charge by cutting it apart.
ramacharitamanas::4908.modern_relevance: A project can keep running on momentum long after the real failure is already visible. At some point, someone has to name it and stop it.
ramacharitamanas::4908.insight: It shows how blind force continues after collapse, and how decisive action ends what cannot be reasoned with.

ramacharitamanas::4909.verse_sanskrit: परे भूमि जिमि नभ तें भूधर। हेठ दाबि कपि भालु निसाचर॥ तासु तेज प्रभु बदन समाना। सुर मुनि सबहिं अचंभव माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4909.verse_hindi: वानर-भालू और निशाचरों को अपने नीचे दबाते हुए वे दोनों टुकड़े पृथ्वी पर ऐसे पड़े जैसे आकाश से दो पहाड़ गिरे हों। उसका तेज प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के मुख में समा गया। (यह देखकर) देवता और मुनि सभी ने आश्चर्य माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4909.english_translation: The monkey, bear, and demon bodies lay on the ground as if two mountains had fallen from the sky. Their radiance merged into Lord Ram's face, and all the gods and sages were amazed.
ramacharitamanas::4909.translation_literal: परे (fell) / भूमि (on the ground) / जिमि (as if) / नभ तें (from the sky) / भूधर (mountains) / हेठ (beneath) / दाबि (pressing down) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / निसाचर (demons) / तासु (their) / तेज (radiance) / प्रभु (Lord) / बदन (face) / समाना (merged) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / सबहिं (all) / अचंभव (wonder) / माना (considered)
ramacharitamanas::4909.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4909.essence: Defeat here becomes a sign of Ram's radiance, not mere destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4909.simple_meaning: The fallen bodies lie like mountains, and their radiance merges into Ram's face while all the celestial beings and sages marvel.
ramacharitamanas::4909.simple_insight: Even in victory, the scene is bigger than violence — it becomes awe, not triumph.
ramacharitamanas::4909.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ram's arrows have just cut down the great foes. Their massive bodies crash to the earth, and their last radiance seems to return to Ram's face. Gods and sages watch in amazement as the war turns into revelation.
ramacharitamanas::4909.modern_relevance: After the tense meeting ends and the room goes quiet, everyone feels the shift: what looked like conflict has become clarity, and no one can quite explain why.
ramacharitamanas::4909.insight: It shifts attention from the defeat itself to the sacred order revealed through it.

ramacharitamanas::4910.verse_sanskrit: सुर दुंदुभीं बजावहिं हरषहिं। अस्तुति करहिं सुमन बहु बरषहिं॥ करि बिनती सुर सकल सिधाए। तेही समय देवरिषि आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4910.verse_hindi: देवता नगाड़े बजाते, हर्षित होते और स्तुति करते हुए बहुत से फूल बरसा रहे हैं। विनती करके सब देवता चले गए। उसी समय देवर्षि नारद आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4910.english_translation: The devas beat drums, rejoice, sing praises, and shower flowers. After offering their prayers, all the devas departed. At that very moment, the sage Narada arrived.
ramacharitamanas::4910.translation_literal: सुर (devas) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजावहिं (beat) / हरषहिं (rejoice) / अस्तुति (praise) / करहिं (do) / सुमन (flowers) / बहु (many) / बरषहिं (shower) / करि (having done) / बिनती (prayer) / सुर (devas) / सकल (all) / सिधाए (departed) / तेही समय (at that very time) / देवरिषि (sage among devas) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::4910.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4910.essence: Celebration gives way to the next turning of the story.
ramacharitamanas::4910.simple_meaning: The devas celebrate Ram's victory with drums, praise, and flowers, then leave. Narada arrives just after they depart.
ramacharitamanas::4910.simple_insight: Joy can fill a moment completely, then make room for a new arrival.
ramacharitamanas::4910.detailed_meaning: After the killing of Ravana's great warriors, the devas celebrate from above with drums, praise, and flower showers. Their prayer ends, they depart, and Narada arrives at the exact moment the scene is ready for the next divine message.
ramacharitamanas::4910.modern_relevance: The applause ends after the presentation, the room empties, and one thoughtful person walks in with the next question. Some moments are only a bridge to what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::4910.insight: It marks a transition in the battle narrative, moving from celestial celebration to Narada's arrival.

ramacharitamanas::4911.verse_sanskrit: गगनोपरि हरि गुन गन गाए। रुचिर बीररस प्रभु मन भाए॥ बेगि हतहु खल कहि मुनि गए। राम समर महि सोभत भए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4911.verse_hindi: आकाश के ऊपर से उन्होंने श्री हरि के सुंदर वीर रसयुक्त गुण समूह का गान किया, जो प्रभु के मन को बहुत ही भाया। मुनि यह कहकर चले गए कि अब दुष्ट रावण को शीघ्र मारिए। (उस समय) श्री रामचंद्रजी रणभूमि में आकर (अत्यंत) सुशोभित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4911.english_translation: From above the sky, the sages sang the beautiful praises of Hari’s heroic qualities, which delighted the Lord’s heart. The sage then said, “Quickly strike down the wicked one.” At that moment, Ram shone brilliantly on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4911.translation_literal: गगनोपरि (above the sky) / हरि (Hari) / गुन गन (clusters of qualities) / गाए (sang) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बीररस (heroic sentiment) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मन (mind/heart) / भाए (were pleasing) / बेगि (quickly) / हतहु (strike down) / खल (the wicked one) / कहि (saying) / मुनि (the sage) / गए (went) / राम (Ram) / समर (battle) / महि (on the earth) / सोभत (shining, being splendid) / भए (became)
ramacharitamanas::4911.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4911.essence: Praise becomes courage, and courage becomes action.
ramacharitamanas::4911.simple_meaning: The sages praise Ram’s heroic nature and urge him to defeat evil quickly, while Ram appears radiant on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4911.simple_insight: True praise does not flatter; it strengthens courage and calls for right action.
ramacharitamanas::4911.detailed_meaning: As the battle in Lanka intensifies, sages in the sky sing Ram’s heroic virtues and bless the fight. Their words delight Ram, and they urge him to end Ravana’s wickedness quickly. The verse then turns to Ram standing gloriously on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::4911.modern_relevance: A mentor’s message before a hard confrontation can steady you: remember what is noble, act decisively, and do not let delay protect what is harmful.
ramacharitamanas::4911.insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to righteous decisiveness in the face of wrongdoing.

ramacharitamanas::4912.verse_sanskrit: संग्राम भूमि बिराज रघुपति अतुल बल कोसल धनी। श्रम बिंदु मुख राजीव लोचन अरुन तन सोनित कनी॥ भुज जुगल फेरत सर सरासन भालु कपि चहु दिसि बने। कह दास तुलसी कहि न सक छबि सेष जेहि आनन घने॥
ramacharitamanas::4912.verse_hindi: अतुलनीय बल वाले कोसलपति श्री रघुनाथजी रणभूमि में सुशोभित हैं। मुख पर पसीने की बूँदें हैं, कमल समान नेत्र कुछ लाल हो रहे हैं। शरीर पर रक्त के कण हैं, दोनों हाथों से धनुष-बाण फिरा रहे हैं। चारों ओर रीछ-वानर सुशोभित हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि प्रभु की इस छबि का वर्णन शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते, जिनके बहुत से (हजार) मुख हैं।
ramacharitamanas::4912.english_translation: Raghupati, the lord of Kosala, stands radiant on the battlefield with unmatched strength. Sweat beads on his face; his lotus eyes are slightly red; drops of blood mark his body. He keeps turning his bow and arrows in both hands while bears and monkeys gather all around. Tulsidas says even Shesha with a thousand mouths cannot describe that beauty.
ramacharitamanas::4912.translation_literal: संग्राम-भूमि (battlefield) / बिराज (shine, stand radiant) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / अतुल-बल (matchless strength) / कोसल-धनी (lord of Kosala) / श्रम-बिंदु (drops of sweat) / मुख (face) / राजीव-लोचन (lotus-eyed) / अरुन-तन (reddened body) / सोनित-कनी (drops of blood) / भुज-जुगल (pair of arms) / फेरत (turning, moving) / सर-सरासन (arrows and bow) / भालु-कपि (bears and monkeys) / चहु दिसि (on all four sides) / बने (arrayed, adorned) / कह दास तुलसी (says servant Tulsidas) / कहि न सक (cannot say) / छबि (beauty, radiance) / सेष (Shesha) / जेहि (whose) / आनन (mouths, faces) / घने (many, dense)
ramacharitamanas::4912.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4912.essence: Even in battle, Ram's worn body shines with unmatched beauty.
ramacharitamanas::4912.simple_meaning: Ram stands on the battlefield looking radiant, powerful, and beautifully alive. Even the thousand-mouthed Shesha cannot fully describe his form.
ramacharitamanas::4912.simple_insight: There is wonder in seeing courage and beauty together, not apart.
ramacharitamanas::4912.detailed_meaning: On the war field in Lanka, Ram stands among bears and monkeys after the fighting. His body shows the effort of battle, yet Tulsidas sees only splendour. The verse pauses the war to praise Ram's radiant presence beyond speech.
ramacharitamanas::4912.modern_relevance: After a brutal day, you catch your reflection in the elevator: tired, sweat on your face, work still unfinished, yet you know you showed up fully. Some victories are visible before the result arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4912.insight: It shifts attention from battlefield success to the living dignity of wholehearted effort.

ramacharitamanas::4913.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर अधम मलाकर ताहि दीन्ह निज धाम। गिरिजा ते नर मंदमति जे न भजहिं श्रीराम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4913.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे गिरिजे! कुंभकर्ण, जो नीच राक्षस और पाप की खान था, उसे भी श्री रामजी ने अपना परमधाम दे दिया। अतः वे मनुष्य (निश्चय ही) मंदबुद्धि हैं, जो उन श्री रामजी को नहीं भजते ॥
ramacharitamanas::4913.english_translation: O Girija, even Kumbhakarna, that vile demon and heap of impurity, was given Ram's own abode. Therefore, people who do not worship Shri Ram are surely dull-minded.
ramacharitamanas::4913.translation_literal: निसिचर (night-dweller / demon) / अधम (lowest) / मलाकर (heap of impurity) / ताहि (to him) / दीन्ह (gave) / निज (own) / धाम (abode) / गिरिजा (O Girija) / ते (therefore) / नर (people) / मंदमति (dull-minded) / जे (who) / न (not) / भजहिं (worship) / श्रीराम (Shri Ram)
ramacharitamanas::4913.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4913.essence: Ram's welcome is so wide that even an enemy can enter it.
ramacharitamanas::4913.simple_meaning: Ram's grace is so vast that even a great enemy received his refuge. If that is true, then refusing to worship Ram is sheer foolishness.
ramacharitamanas::4913.simple_insight: You are not being measured by your past. What matters is whether you turn toward the one who welcomes even the fallen.
ramacharitamanas::4913.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Shiva turns to Parvati and points to Kumbhakarna as proof of Ram's limitless grace. Even a terrible enemy received Ram's refuge, so the real blindness is not weakness but refusing to worship Ram at all.
ramacharitamanas::4913.modern_relevance: You watched someone who hurt everyone still get a second chance, and it stung. This verse says grace can reach farther than your anger, and your refusal to trust it may be the smaller mind.
ramacharitamanas::4913.insight: It shifts the mind from judging who deserves grace to recognising Ram's mercy as wider than your categories.

ramacharitamanas::4914.verse_sanskrit: दिन के अंत फिरीं द्वौ अनी। समर भई सुभटन्ह श्रम घनी॥ राम कृपाँ कपि दल बल बाढ़ा। जिमि तृन पाइ लाग अति डाढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4914.verse_hindi: दिन का अन्त होने पर दोनों सेनाएँ लौट पड़ीं। (आज के युद्ध में) योद्धाओं को बड़ी थकावट हुई, परन्तु श्री रामजी की कृपा से वानर सेना का बल उसी प्रकार बढ़ गया, जैसे घास पाकर अग्नि बहुत बढ़ जाती है ॥(घ)॥
ramacharitamanas::4914.english_translation: When day ended, both armies withdrew. The warriors were worn out by battle, but by Ram's grace the monkey army's strength grew, like fire flaring up when given grass.
ramacharitamanas::4914.translation_literal: दिन (day) / के अंत (at the end) / फिरीं (turned back) / द्वौ (both) / अनी (armies) / समर (battle) / भई (became) / सुभटन्ह (for the warriors) / श्रम (weariness) / घनी (great) / राम (Ram) / कृपाँ (by grace) / कपि दल (monkey army) / बल (strength) / बाढ़ा (increased) / जिमि (just as) / तृन (grass) / पाइ (having obtained) / लाग (started) / अति (greatly) / डाढ़ा (to blaze)
ramacharitamanas::4914.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4914.essence: Grace can refill you after battle has emptied you.
ramacharitamanas::4914.simple_meaning: The battle pauses at sunset. Both sides are exhausted, but Ram's grace renews the monkey army's strength.
ramacharitamanas::4914.simple_insight: Even after total exhaustion, support beyond you can restore what effort spent.
