ramacharitamanas::4914.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war reaches the end of another day. Both armies pull back, and the fighters are drained. Yet the monkey army does not merely survive the strain — Ram's grace makes their strength rise again, like a fire fed with grass.
ramacharitamanas::4914.modern_relevance: You come home after a brutal day, shoulders aching, mind empty, and somehow a single kind message or quiet blessing gives you a second wind.
ramacharitamanas::4914.insight: It shifts attention from personal stamina to the restoring power of grace.

ramacharitamanas::4915.verse_sanskrit: छीजहिं निसिचर दिनु अरु राती। निज मुख कहें सुकृत जेहि भाँती॥ बहु बिलाप दसकंधर करई। बंधु सीस पुनि पुनि उर धरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4915.verse_hindi: उधर राक्षस दिन-रात इस प्रकार घटते जा रहे हैं, जिस प्रकार अपने ही मुख से कहने पर पुण्य घट जाते हैं। रावण बहुत विलाप कर रहा है। बार-बार भाई (कुंभकर्ण) का सिर कलेजे से लगाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4915.english_translation: The demons are wasting away day and night, like merit that shrinks when spoken of too much. Ravana grieves greatly, again and again pressing his brother's head to his chest.
ramacharitamanas::4915.translation_literal: छीजहिं (are wasting away) / निसिचर (demons) / दिनु (day) / अरु (and) / राती (night) / निज (own) / मुख (mouth) / कहें (by speaking) / सुकृत (merit) / जेहि भाँती (in whatever way) / बहु (much) / बिलाप (lamentation) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / करई (does) / बंधु (brother) / सीस (head) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / उर (chest) / धरई (presses)
ramacharitamanas::4915.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4915.essence: Pride collapses when the one you relied on is gone.
ramacharitamanas::4915.simple_meaning: The demon forces are falling apart, and Ravana is openly grieving for his brother, holding Kumbhakarna's head to his chest again and again.
ramacharitamanas::4915.simple_insight: Grief can make even the proudest person look helpless.
ramacharitamanas::4915.detailed_meaning: After Kumbhakarna's death in Lanka, the demon army is weakening and the palace is filled with mourning. Ravana, usually unbending, cannot contain his sorrow and keeps clutching his brother's head in despair.
ramacharitamanas::4915.modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed after a loss, unable to fix anything, only holding on. Pride disappears fast when grief finally arrives.
ramacharitamanas::4915.insight: It shows how defeat and loss strip away ego and expose raw attachment.

ramacharitamanas::4916.verse_sanskrit: रोवहिं नारि हृदय हति पानी। तासु तेज बल बिपुल बखानी॥ मेघनाद तेहि अवसर आयउ। कहि बहु कथा पिता समुझायउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4916.verse_hindi: स्त्रियाँ उसके बड़े भारी तेज और बल को बखान करके हाथों से छाती पीट-पीटकर रो रही हैं। उसी समय मेघनाद आया और उसने बहुत सी कथाएँ कहकर पिता को समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4916.english_translation: The women wept, beating their chests, praising his great power and strength. At that moment Meghanad arrived and comforted his father with many words.
ramacharitamanas::4916.translation_literal: रोवहिं (weep) / नारि (women) / हृदय (heart) / हति (striking) / पानी (hands) / तासु (his) / तेज (splendor/valor) / बल (strength) / बिपुल (great) / बखानी (described) / मेघनाद (Meghanad) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / आयउ (came) / कहि (having said) / बहु (many) / कथा (stories/words) / पिता (father) / समुझायउ (consoled/explained)
ramacharitamanas::4916.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4916.essence: Grief and pride arrive together, and words rush in to hold them up.
ramacharitamanas::4916.simple_meaning: Ravana's women mourn his greatness, and Meghanad arrives to comfort him with words.
ramacharitamanas::4916.simple_insight: Even in collapse, pride tries to dress itself as strength.
ramacharitamanas::4916.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's household is grieving as the war closes in. The women cry over his power and glory, while Meghanad steps in to steady his father with talk. The verse is a scene of emotional support, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4916.modern_relevance: A family sits in a hospital waiting room, still trying to speak proudly about the person who is slipping away. Someone arrives and starts saying whatever will keep everyone from breaking.
ramacharitamanas::4916.insight: It shows how people try to protect collapsing pride with comforting words.

ramacharitamanas::4917.verse_sanskrit: देखेहु कालि मोरि मनुसाई। अबहिं बहुत का करौं बड़ाई॥ इष्टदेव सैं बल रथ पायउँ। सो बल तात न तोहि देखायउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4917.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) कल मेरा पुरुषार्थ देखिएगा। अभी बहुत बड़ाई क्या करूँ? हे तात! मैंने अपने इष्टदेव से जो बल और रथ पाया था, वह बल (और रथ) अब तक आपको नहीं दिखलाया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4917.english_translation: “See my manly power tomorrow. Why should I boast more now? Father, I had received strength and a chariot from my chosen deity, and I had not yet shown you that strength and chariot.”
ramacharitamanas::4917.translation_literal: देखेहु (see) / कालि (tomorrow) / मोरि (my) / मनुसाई (manliness) / अबहिं (still now) / बहुत (much) / का (why) / करौं (should I do) / बड़ाई (boasting)॥ / इष्टदेव (chosen deity) / सैं (from) / बल (strength) / रथ (chariot) / पायउँ (I received) / सो (that) / बल (strength) / तात (father) / न (not) / तोहि (to you) / देखायउँ (showed)॥
ramacharitamanas::4917.speaker: Meghanad
ramacharitamanas::4917.essence: Boasting often appears when real power has not yet been proved.
ramacharitamanas::4917.simple_meaning: Meghanad boasts that his real strength will be shown tomorrow, and says he has not yet revealed the power and chariot given by his chosen deity.
ramacharitamanas::4917.simple_insight: Pride can sound like confidence, but it often hides desperation.
ramacharitamanas::4917.detailed_meaning: Inside Lanka, the demon warriors are collapsing and Ravana is grieving. Meghnad arrives to steady his father, promising that tomorrow he will show his full power. His words are bravado before the battle, not a teaching in themselves.
ramacharitamanas::4917.modern_relevance: A person sends one last overconfident message before a huge presentation, trying to sound untouchable. The bluff is louder than the courage.
ramacharitamanas::4917.insight: It shows how ego speaks before action, trying to borrow strength from words.

ramacharitamanas::4918.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि जल्पत भयउ बिहाना। चहुँ दुआर लागे कपि नाना॥ इति कपि भालु काल सम बीरा। उत रजनीचर अति रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4918.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार डींग मारते हुए सबेरा हो गया। लंका के चारों दरवाजों पर बहुत से वानर आ डटे। इधर काल के समान वीर वानर-भालू हैं और उधर अत्यंत रणधीर राक्षस ॥
ramacharitamanas::4918.english_translation: Thus, while they kept boasting, morning broke. Many monkeys gathered at Lanka's four gates. On one side stood monkey and bear warriors like death itself; on the other, fierce night-raiders ready for battle.
ramacharitamanas::4918.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / जल्पत (talking boastfully) / भयउ (became) / बिहाना (morning) / चहुँ (four) / दुआर (gates) / लागे (stood/assembled) / कपि (monkeys) / नाना (many) / इति (thus) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / काल (death/time) / सम (like) / बीरा (warriors) / उत (there) / रजनीचर (night-roamers) / अति (very) / रनधीरा (battle-brave)
ramacharitamanas::4918.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4918.essence: Boasting ends when dawn brings the real clash.
ramacharitamanas::4918.simple_meaning: Morning arrives while both armies keep talking and gathering. Monkeys and bears face the night-raiders at Lanka's four gates, ready for war.
ramacharitamanas::4918.simple_insight: The battle has moved from words to full confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::4918.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the night of taunts and boasts ends as dawn breaks. Monkey and bear forces take positions at the city's four gates, while Ravana's fierce warriors stand ready. The verse is scene-setting, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4918.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet after the last argument, and everyone finally takes their seat. The tension is still there, but now the real confrontation begins.
ramacharitamanas::4918.insight: It shifts attention from boasting to the moment action becomes unavoidable.

ramacharitamanas::4919.verse_sanskrit: लरहिं सुभट निज निज जय हेतू। बरनि न जाइ समर खगकेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::4919.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर के योद्धा अपनी-अपनी जय के लिए लड़ रहे हैं। हे गरुड़ उनके युद्ध का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4919.english_translation: Both sides' warriors fight for their own victory. O Garuda, their battle cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::4919.translation_literal: लरहिं (fight) / सुभट (brave warriors) / निज निज (each their own) / जय (victory) / हेतू (for the sake of) । / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / समर (battle) / खगकेतू (O Garuda) ।
ramacharitamanas::4919.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4919.essence: The battle is so fierce that language fails.
ramacharitamanas::4919.simple_meaning: The warriors on both sides are fighting hard for victory, and the battle is beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::4919.simple_insight: Some struggles are too vast for words; only the force of them can be felt.
ramacharitamanas::4919.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has fully broken open. Monkey warriors and demon warriors are locked in fierce combat, each driven by the wish to win. The scene is so intense that the narrator says even Garuda cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::4919.modern_relevance: You watch two teams collide on a field, each desperate to win, and the noise swallows every other thought. Some moments are felt in the body before they can be explained.
ramacharitamanas::4919.insight: It shifts attention from the meaning of victory to the sheer scale of conflict.

ramacharitamanas::4920.verse_sanskrit: मेघनाद मायामय रथ चढ़ि गयउ अकास। गर्जेउ अट्टहास करि भइ कपि कटकहि त्रास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4920.verse_hindi: मेघनाद उसी (पूर्वोक्त) मायामय रथ पर चढ़कर आकाश में चला गया और अट्टहास करके गरजा, जिससे वानरों की सेना में भय छा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4920.english_translation: Meghanada climbed onto that illusion-made chariot and rose into the sky, then roared with a loud laugh, striking fear into the monkey army.
ramacharitamanas::4920.translation_literal: मेघनाद (Meghanada) / मायामय (illusion-made) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ि (having mounted) / गयउ (went) / अकास (sky) / गर्जेउ (roared) / अट्टहास (loud laugh) / करि (doing) / भइ (became) / कपि (monkey) / कटकहि (army) / त्रास (fear)
ramacharitamanas::4920.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4920.essence: Fear can be manufactured with noise, height, and show.
ramacharitamanas::4920.simple_meaning: Meghanada rises into the sky on a deceptive chariot and frightens the monkey army with his loud roar.
ramacharitamanas::4920.simple_insight: Pride can look powerful from above, but it still works by fear.
ramacharitamanas::4920.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Meghanada mounts a magical chariot and attacks from the sky, laughing loudly to shake the monkey ranks. This is one move in the larger war scene, not a teaching verse on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4920.modern_relevance: A loud person takes over the meeting with swagger, sudden confidence, and a show of force. The room goes quiet, not because they are right, but because they know how to intimidate.
ramacharitamanas::4920.insight: It shows how spectacle and fear can become weapons in conflict.

ramacharitamanas::4921.verse_sanskrit: सक्ति सूल तरवारि कृपाना। अस्त्र सस्त्र कुलिसायुध नाना॥ डारइ परसु परिघ पाषाना। लागेउ बृष्टि करै बहु बाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4921.verse_hindi: वह शक्ति, शूल, तलवार, कृपाण आदि अस्त्र, शास्त्र एवं वज्र आदि बहुत से आयुध चलाने तथा फरसे, परिघ, पत्थर आदि डालने और बहुत से बाणों की वृष्टि करने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4921.english_translation: He hurled many weapons—spear, trident, sword, dagger, axe, mace, stones, and a rain of arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4921.translation_literal: सक्ति (spear) / सूल (trident) / तरवारि (sword) / कृपाना (dagger) / अस्त्र (missile-weapon) / सस्त्र (weapon) / कुलिसायुध (thunderbolt-weapon) / नाना (many)॥ / डारइ (throws) / परसु (axe) / परिघ (mace) / पाषाना (stones) / लागेउ (began) / बृष्टि (rain) / करै (to do) / बहु (many) / बाना (arrows) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4921.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4921.essence: Battle becomes a rain of weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4921.simple_meaning: A warrior unleashes every kind of weapon at once, including arrows, stones, and heavy arms.
ramacharitamanas::4921.simple_insight: The scene is all force and motion, with no room for hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4921.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the fighting has become a storm. A warrior hurls every weapon he has—spear, trident, sword, axe, stones, and arrows—turning combat into chaos. The verse is a vivid battle detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4921.insight: It paints the violence of war as overwhelming and indiscriminate.

ramacharitamanas::4922.verse_sanskrit: दस दिसि रहे बान नभ छाई। मानहुँ मघा मेघ झरि लाई॥ धरु धरु मारु सुनिअ धुनि काना। जो मारइ तेहि कोउ न जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4922.verse_hindi: आकाश में दसों दिशाओं में बाण छा गए, मानो मघा नक्षत्र के बादलों ने झड़ी लगा दी हो। 'पकड़ो, पकड़ो, मारो' ये शब्द सुनाई पड़ते हैं। पर जो मार रहा है, उसे कोई नहीं जान पाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::4922.english_translation: Bows filled the sky in all ten directions, like a shower of clouds after the Magha star. Cries of 'Catch him, catch him, kill him' were heard. But no one could tell who was striking.
ramacharitamanas::4922.translation_literal: दस दिसि (in ten directions) / रहे (were spread) / बान (arrows) / नभ (sky) / छाई (covered) । / मानहुँ (as if) / मघा (Magha star) / मेघ (clouds) / झरि (pouring) / लाई (brought) । / धरु धरु (catch, catch) / मारु (kill) / सुनिअ (are heard) / धुनि (sounds) / काना (in the ears) । / जो (who) / मारइ (strikes) / तेहि (that one) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / जाना (knows) ।
ramacharitamanas::4922.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4922.essence: Noise can surround you while the cause stays hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4922.simple_meaning: Arrows fill the sky from every direction, and voices shout to catch and kill. Yet the attacker remains hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4922.simple_insight: Chaos can be loud and still leave you unable to see what is really happening.
ramacharitamanas::4922.detailed_meaning: In the battle of Lanka, Meghnad is attacking from a hidden, magical position. Arrows cover the sky, the monkey army hears the cries of war, but the true source of the attack stays concealed. The verse deepens the confusion before the next move.
ramacharitamanas::4922.modern_relevance: You hear alarms, messages, and shouted instructions in a crisis room, but no one can identify the real source of the problem. The noise is everywhere; the cause stays hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4922.insight: It shifts attention from the noise of events to the need to locate their real source.

ramacharitamanas::4923.verse_sanskrit: गहि गिरि तरु अकास कपि धावहिं। देखहिं तेहि न दुखित फिरि आवहिं॥ अवघट घाट बाट गिरि कंदर। माया बल कीन्हेसि सर पंजर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4923.verse_hindi: पर्वत और वृक्षों को लेकर वानर आकाश में दौड़कर जाते हैं। पर उसे देख नहीं पाते, इससे दुःखी होकर लौट आते हैं। मेघनाद ने माया के बल से अटपटी घाटियों, रास्तों और पर्वतों-कन्दराओं को बाणों के पिंजरे बना दिए (बाणों से छा दिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4923.english_translation: The monkeys ran through the sky carrying mountains and trees, but could not see him; they returned in sorrow. By the power of illusion, Meghnad turned the rough passes, paths, hills, and caves into a cage of arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4923.translation_literal: गहि (grasping) / गिरि (mountain) / तरु (tree) / अकास (sky) / कपि (monkeys) / धावहिं (run) / देखहिं (see) / तेहि (him) / न (not) / दुखित (grieved) / फिरि (again) / आवहिं (come back) / अवघट (rough) / घाट (passes) / बाट (paths) / गिरि (hills) / कंदर (caves) / माया (illusion) / बल (power) / कीन्हेसि (he made) / सर (arrows) / पंजर (cage)
ramacharitamanas::4923.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4923.essence: Illusion can turn every path into a trap.
ramacharitamanas::4923.simple_meaning: The monkeys rush through the air with mountains and trees, but their search fails. Meghnad's illusion traps the whole landscape in arrows, leaving them confused and helpless.
ramacharitamanas::4923.simple_insight: Sometimes effort alone is not enough when confusion has turned the whole path against you.
ramacharitamanas::4923.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's army is trying to move through a battlefield warped by Meghnad's illusion. The monkeys leap with mountains and trees, but cannot locate him. His arrow-magic turns roads, hills, and caves into a trap, and their confidence breaks.
ramacharitamanas::4923.modern_relevance: You are trying to find your way through a problem, but every route seems to fold back on itself. The harder you search, the more trapped you feel.
ramacharitamanas::4923.insight: It shows how confusion can make even strong effort feel useless until the illusion is broken.

ramacharitamanas::4924.verse_sanskrit: जाहिं कहाँ ब्याकुल भए बंदर। सुरपति बंदि परे जनु मंदर॥ मारुतसुत अंगद नल नीला। कीन्हेसि बिकल सकल बलसीला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4924.verse_hindi: अब कहाँ जाएँ, यह सोचकर (रास्ता न पाकर) वानर व्याकुल हो गए। मानो पर्वत इंद्र की कैद में पड़े हों। मेघनाद ने मारुति हनुमान् , अंगद, नल और नील आदि सभी बलवानों को व्याकुल कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4924.english_translation: The monkeys became distressed, wondering, “Where can we go now?” It was as if mountains had fallen captive before Indra. Maruti's son, Angad, Nala, and Neela, the mighty warriors, were all thrown into confusion by Meghnad.
ramacharitamanas::4924.translation_literal: जाहिं (where) / कहाँ (where) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / भए (became) / बंदर (monkeys) । सुरपति (lord of the gods, Indra) / बंदि (captive) / परे (fell) / जनु (as if) / मंदर (mountains) ॥ मारुतसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / अंगद (Angad) / नल (Nala) / नीला (Neela) । कीन्हेसि (he made) / बिकल (confused, distressed) / सकल (all) / बलसीला (mighty warriors) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4924.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4924.essence: Power without clarity leaves even the strong unable to move.
ramacharitamanas::4924.simple_meaning: The warriors are overwhelmed and confused by Meghnad’s attack. Even the strongest among the monkeys lose their footing and cannot see what to do next.
ramacharitamanas::4924.simple_insight: Even strength can be shaken when the situation turns completely unclear.
ramacharitamanas::4924.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, Meghnad’s tactics have thrown the monkey army into confusion. Hanuman, Angad, Nala, and Neela are all unsettled, unable to find a way forward. This verse shows the pressure before the next turn in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4924.modern_relevance: You’re in a group project when the plan collapses, the deadline is near, and even the most capable people are staring at each other. This is what confusion feels like when the route disappears.
ramacharitamanas::4924.insight: It shows how pressure can scatter even skilled people when they lose a clear direction.

ramacharitamanas::4925.verse_sanskrit: पुनि लछिमन सुग्रीव बिभीषन। सरन्हि मारि कीन्हेसि जर्जर तन॥ पुनि रघुपति सैं जूझै लागा। सर छाँड़इ होइ लागहिं नागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4925.verse_hindi: फिर उसने लक्ष्मणजी, सुग्रीव और विभीषण को बाणों से मारकर उनके शरीर को छलनी कर दिया। फिर वह श्री रघुनाथजी से लड़ने लगा। वह जो बाण छोड़ता है, वे साँप होकर लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4925.english_translation: Then he wounded Lakshman, Sugriva, and Vibhishana so badly that their bodies were riddled with arrows. Then he turned to fight Raghupati. The arrows he released came like serpents.
ramacharitamanas::4925.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / सरन्हि (with arrows) / मारि (striking) / कीन्हेसि (he made) / जर्जर (riddled, shattered) / तन (body) ॥ पुनि (again) / रघुपति (Raghupati, Ram) / सैं (toward) / जूझै (to fight) / लागा (began) / सर (arrows) / छाँड़इ (he released) / होइ (becoming) / लागहिं (they strike) / नागा (serpents) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4925.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4925.essence: The fight intensifies as Meghanad turns his power on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4925.simple_meaning: Meghanad keeps fighting fiercely, wounding Lakshman, Sugriva, and Vibhishana, then attacks Ram with arrows that seem like serpents.
ramacharitamanas::4925.simple_insight: Some moments are pure force, with no lesson except the danger in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::4925.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Meghanad presses his attack after the earlier confusion. Lakshman, Sugriva, and Vibhishana are struck hard, and then Ram himself is engaged. The verse keeps the action moving, setting up the next image of serpent-like arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4925.modern_relevance: A situation spirals fast: one harsh email becomes three people hurt, then the conflict turns toward you. The moment is still moving, and all you can do is stay standing.
ramacharitamanas::4925.insight: It keeps the scene in motion without pausing for reflection; the verse functions as battle escalation.

ramacharitamanas::4926.verse_sanskrit: ब्याल पास बस भए खरारी। स्वबस अनंत एक अबिकारी॥ नट इव कपट चरित कर नाना। सदा स्वतंत्र एक भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4926.verse_hindi: जो स्वतंत्र, अनन्त, एक (अखंड) और निर्विकार हैं, वे खर के शत्रु श्री रामजी (लीला से) नागपाश के वश में हो गए (उससे बँध गए) श्री रामचंद्रजी सदा स्वतंत्र, एक, (अद्वितीय) भगवान् हैं। वे नट की तरह अनेकों प्रकार के दिखावटी चरित्र करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4926.english_translation: The enemy of Khara is one, unchanging, and beyond all change, yet by his own will he came under the serpent-noose. Like an actor, the Lord performs many kinds of seeming roles while remaining forever free.
ramacharitamanas::4926.translation_literal: ब्याल (serpent) / पास (noose) / बस (under control) / भए (became) / खरारी (enemy of Khara) / स्वबस (under his own will) / अनंत (endless) / एक (one) / अबिकारी (unchanging) / नट (actor) / इव (like) / कपट (seeming) / चरित (deeds/roles) / कर (doing) / नाना (many) / सदा (always) / स्वतंत्र (free) / एक (one) / भगवाना (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::4926.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4926.essence: Freedom remains intact even when the Lord appears bound.
ramacharitamanas::4926.simple_meaning: Ram is untouched and free, yet he can appear to be bound by his own choice. He takes on many forms and roles without losing his changeless nature.
ramacharitamanas::4926.simple_insight: Even what looks like limitation can be part of a greater freedom.
ramacharitamanas::4926.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ram allows himself to be caught in the serpent-noose, not because he is helpless, but because he is beyond compulsion. The poet pauses to reveal his true nature: changeless, sovereign, and free, even while acting out many roles.
ramacharitamanas::4926.modern_relevance: You can be stuck in a role, a deadline, or a family duty and still not be trapped by it. The outer pressure is real, but it does not define who you are.
ramacharitamanas::4926.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing life as confinement to seeing it as chosen participation.

ramacharitamanas::4927.verse_sanskrit: रन सोभा लगि प्रभुहिं बँधायो। नागपास देवन्ह भय पायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4927.verse_hindi: रण की शोभा के लिए प्रभु ने अपने को नागपाश में बाँध लिया, किन्तु उससे देवताओं को बड़ा भय हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4927.english_translation: For the sake of the battle's splendour, the Lord let himself be bound by the serpent-noose, yet that filled the gods with great fear.
ramacharitamanas::4927.translation_literal: रन (battle) / सोभा (splendour) / लगि (for the sake of) / प्रभुहिं (the Lord) / बँधायो (was bound) / नागपास (serpent-noose) / देवन्ह (the gods) / भय (fear) / पायो (felt)
ramacharitamanas::4927.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4927.essence: What looks like defeat can still be pure divine play.
ramacharitamanas::4927.simple_meaning: Ram allows himself to be bound by the serpent-noose as part of the battle's play, but the celestial beings become fearful because even this apparent defeat reveals his immense power.
ramacharitamanas::4927.simple_insight: Apparent weakness can hide overwhelming strength.
ramacharitamanas::4927.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's weapon seems to trap Ram for a moment. But this is not real helplessness; it is part of the divine play. The scene shocks the celestial beings, who realise that even Ram's apparent bondage is full of power.
ramacharitamanas::4927.modern_relevance: You take a public hit in a meeting and everyone assumes you are finished. But the quiet person in the room knows the deeper game: not every setback means loss.
ramacharitamanas::4927.insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearances to recognising that true power is not reduced by outward constraint.

ramacharitamanas::4928.verse_sanskrit: गिरिजा जासु नाम जपि मुनि काटहिं भव पास। सो कि बंध तर आवइ ब्यापक बिस्व निवास ॥
ramacharitamanas::4928.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे गिरिजे! जिनका नाम जपकर मुनि भव (जन्म-मृत्यु) की फाँसी को काट डालते हैं, वे सर्वव्यापक और विश्व निवास (विश्व के आधार) प्रभु कहीं बंधन में आ सकते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4928.english_translation: O Girija, by chanting whose name sages cut the noose of worldly becoming, can the all-pervading Lord of the universe ever come under bondage?
ramacharitamanas::4928.translation_literal: गिरिजा (O Girija) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / जपि (chanting) / मुनि (sages) / काटहिं (cut) / भव (worldly becoming) / पास (noose) / सो (that) / कि (can) / बंध (bondage) / तर (under) / आवइ (come) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / बिस्व (universe) / निवास (dweller)
ramacharitamanas::4928.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4928.essence: The one whose name frees others cannot be confined by any bond.
ramacharitamanas::4928.simple_meaning: Chanting Ram's name frees sages from the cycle of rebirth. The all-pervading Lord of the universe cannot truly be tied up.
ramacharitamanas::4928.simple_insight: What looks like capture is still under divine freedom.
ramacharitamanas::4928.detailed_meaning: After Ram lets himself be bound by the serpent noose for the sake of the cosmic play, Shiva turns to Parvati and corrects the appearance. He reminds her that the one whose name cuts the bonds of worldly becoming cannot himself be trapped.
ramacharitamanas::4928.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love get blamed, cornered, or misread, and the story feels bigger than the moment. This verse reminds you that what is truly free cannot be reduced by appearances.
ramacharitamanas::4928.insight: It shifts the mind from surface events to the deeper reality that names, forms, and bonds do not limit the divine.

ramacharitamanas::4929.verse_sanskrit: चरित राम के सगुन भवानी। तर्कि न जाहिं बुद्धि बल बानी॥ अस बिचारि जे तग्य बिरागी। रामहि भजहिं तर्क सब त्यागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4929.verse_hindi: हे भवानी! श्री रामजी की इस सगुण लीलाओं के विषय में बुद्धि और वाणी के बल से तर्क (निर्णय) नहीं किया जा सकता। ऐसा विचार कर जो तत्त्वज्ञानी और विरक्त पुरुष हैं, वे सब तर्क (शंका) छोड़कर श्री रामजी का भजन ही करते हैं॥।1॥
ramacharitamanas::4929.english_translation: O Bhavani, the nature of Ram's manifested play cannot be settled by intellect, strength, or speech. Knowing this, the wise and detached abandon argument and worship Ram instead.
ramacharitamanas::4929.translation_literal: चरित (deeds / conduct) / राम के (of Ram) / सगुन (with form, manifested) / भवानी (Bhavani) / तर्कि (by reasoning) / न जाहिं (cannot be reached) / बुद्धि (intellect) / बल (strength) / बानी (speech)॥ अस (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / जे (those who) / तग्य (knowers) / बिरागी (detached) / रामहि (Ram) / भजहिं (worship) / तर्क (argument) / सब (all) / त्यागी (having abandoned)॥
ramacharitamanas::4929.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4929.essence: When reason reaches its limit, devotion becomes the wiser response.
ramacharitamanas::4929.simple_meaning: Ram's divine play cannot be fully understood through intellect, force, or speech. Real wisdom is to stop arguing and turn to loving devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4929.simple_insight: There is peace in releasing the need to explain everything before you can trust it.
ramacharitamanas::4929.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the Lankakand frame, reflecting on Ram's manifested deeds. He says Ram's divine play cannot be captured by logic alone. The truly wise, seeing this limit, drop argument and take refuge in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::4929.modern_relevance: You keep reopening the same question at 1:30 a.m., hoping one more argument will make the pain or mystery make sense. Some things are not meant to be solved first; they are meant to be trusted.
ramacharitamanas::4929.insight: It shifts you from compulsive analysis to humble surrender when reason reaches its limit.

ramacharitamanas::4930.verse_sanskrit: ब्याकुल कटकु कीन्ह घननादा। पुनि भा प्रगट कहइ दुर्बादा॥ जामवंत कह खल रहु ठाढ़ा। सुनि करि ताहि क्रोध अति बाढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4930.verse_hindi: मेघनाद ने सेना को व्याकुल कर दिया। फिर वह प्रकट हो गया और दुर्वचन कहने लगा। इस पर जाम्बवान् ने कहा- अरे दुष्ट! खड़ा रह। यह सुनकर उसे बड़ा क्रोध बढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4930.english_translation: Megnada threw the army into confusion and then appeared openly, speaking insults. Jambavan said, "You villain, stand still!" Hearing this, his anger rose even more.
ramacharitamanas::4930.translation_literal: ब्याकुल (confused) / कटकु (army) / कीन्ह (made) / घननादा (Megnada) / पुनि (then) / भा (became) / प्रगट (manifest) / कहइ (speaks) / दुर्बादा (abusive words) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / कह (said) / खल (villain) / रहु (remain) / ठाढ़ा (standing) / सुनि (hearing) / करि (having done) / ताहि (to him) / क्रोध (anger) / अति (very) / बाढ़ा (increased)
ramacharitamanas::4930.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4930.essence: Insults turn confusion into open combat.
ramacharitamanas::4930.simple_meaning: Megnada shakes the army, steps forward, and hurls insults. Jambavan challenges him, and Megnada's anger flares.
ramacharitamanas::4930.simple_insight: Pride escalates fast when no one steps back.
ramacharitamanas::4930.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's battlefield, Megnada breaks the army's composure and then emerges openly to taunt the warriors. Jambavan answers with fearless contempt, and the exchange pushes the conflict into a fiercer clash.
ramacharitamanas::4930.modern_relevance: A tense group chat turns ugly after one sharp insult, and suddenly everyone is defending ego instead of solving the problem.
ramacharitamanas::4930.insight: It shows how a single taunt can turn confusion into open confrontation.

ramacharitamanas::4931.verse_sanskrit: बूढ़ जानि सठ छाँड़ेउँ तोही। लागेसि अधम पचारै मोही॥ अस कहि तरल त्रिसूल चलायो। जामवंत कर गहि सोइ धायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4931.verse_hindi: अरे मूर्ख! मैंने बूढ़ा जानकर तुझको छोड़ दिया था। अरे अधम! अब तू मुझे ही ललकारने लगा है? ऐसा कहकर उसने चमकता हुआ त्रिशूल चलाया। जाम्बवान् उसी त्रिशूल को हाथ से पकड़कर दौड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4931.english_translation: “You fool! I spared you because I thought you were old. You lowly one, now you dare challenge me?” Saying this, he hurled his shining trident. Jambavan seized that trident and rushed forward.
ramacharitamanas::4931.translation_literal: बूढ़ (old) / जानि (knowing) / सठ (fool) / छाँड़ेउँ (I spared) / तोही (you) / लागेसि (you began) / अधम (vile one) / पचारै (to challenge) / मोही (me)॥ अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / तरल (shining) / त्रिसूल (trident) / चलायो (hurled) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / कर (hand) / गहि (seizing) / सोइ (that same) / धायो (rushed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4931.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4931.essence: Insult and force collide in a split second of battle.
ramacharitamanas::4931.simple_meaning: This is a battle taunt and a burst of action: the enemy insults Jambavan, throws a trident, and Jambavan catches it and charges.
ramacharitamanas::4931.simple_insight: It shows how pride turns instantly into violence when ego is challenged.
ramacharitamanas::4931.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, Jambavan has just provoked Meghnad. Meghnad snaps back with insults, hurls his trident, and Jambavan catches it mid-attack. The verse is part of a fast-moving combat sequence, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4931.insight: It captures the raw escalation that happens when wounded pride meets open challenge.

ramacharitamanas::4932.verse_sanskrit: मारिसि मेघनाद कै छाती। परा भूमि घुर्मित सुरघाती॥ पुनि रिसान गहि चरन फिरायो। महि पछारि निज बल देखरायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4932.verse_hindi: और उसे मेघनाद की छाती पर दे मारा। वह देवताओं का शत्रु चक्कर खाकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। जाम्बवान् ने फिर क्रोध में भरकर पैर पकड़कर उसको घुमाया और पृथ्वी पर पटककर उसे अपना बल दिखलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4932.english_translation: He struck Meghnad in the chest. The enemy of the radiant beings fell to the ground, dazed. Then, in anger, he grabbed Meghnad's feet, whirled him around, and slammed him to the earth to show his strength.
ramacharitamanas::4932.translation_literal: मारिसि (struck) / मेघनाद (Meghnad) / कै (of) / छाती (chest) / परा (fell) / भूमि (ground) / घुर्मित (dazed, whirling) / सुरघाती (enemy of the radiant beings) / पुनि (again) / रिसान (in anger) / गहि (grasping) / चरन (feet) / फिरायो (whirled) / महि (earth) / पछारि (slammed) / निज (own) / बल (strength) / देखरायो (showed)
ramacharitamanas::4932.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4932.essence: The clash turns into a display of sheer force.
ramacharitamanas::4932.simple_meaning: Jambavan strikes Meghnad hard, knocks him down, then grabs his feet and throws him to the ground again.
ramacharitamanas::4932.simple_insight: Some moments in conflict are not about victory speeches — just raw force and complete dominance.
ramacharitamanas::4932.detailed_meaning: In the battle for Lanka, Meghnad has already been taunting the warriors. Jambavan answers without hesitation, hurling him down and then flinging him again to prove his strength. The verse is a combat beat, not a teaching turn.
ramacharitamanas::4932.modern_relevance: A fight breaks out in a crowded street, and the older man who seemed quiet suddenly moves with startling force. This is pure battlefield momentum, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::4932.insight: It keeps the scene moving with physical action rather than moral instruction.

ramacharitamanas::4933.verse_sanskrit: बर प्रसाद सो मरइ न मारा। तब गहि पद लंका पर डारा॥ इहाँ देवरिषि गरुड़ पठायो। राम समीप सपदि सो आयो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4933.verse_hindi: (किन्तु) वरदान के प्रताप से वह मारे नहीं मरता। तब जाम्बवान् ने उसका पैर पकड़कर उसे लंका पर फेंक दिया। इधर देवर्षि नारदजी ने गरुड़ को भेजा। वे तुरंत ही श्री रामजी के पास आ पहुँचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4933.english_translation: Because of a boon, he could not die even when struck. Then Jambavan seized his foot and hurled him onto Lanka. Meanwhile, the sage Narada sent Garuda, and he quickly came near Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4933.translation_literal: बर (boon) / प्रसाद (grace) / सो (that one) / मरइ (dies) / न (not) / मारा (killed) / तब (then) / गहि (seizing) / पद (foot) / लंका (to Lanka) / पर (onto) / डारा (threw)॥ / इहाँ (here) / देवरिषि (sage among the gods) / गरुड़ (Garuda) / पठायो (sent) / राम (Ram) / समीप (near) / सपदि (quickly) / सो (he) / आयो (came)॥
ramacharitamanas::4933.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4933.essence: What cannot be ended by force is shifted by timing and help.
ramacharitamanas::4933.simple_meaning: A warrior protected by a boon cannot be killed, so Jambavan throws him aside. At the same time, Garuda is sent to Ram and arrives quickly.
ramacharitamanas::4933.simple_insight: Sometimes force is not enough; a deeper help arrives at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::4933.detailed_meaning: In the heat of Lanka's battle, Jambavan cannot kill the enemy because a boon protects him from death. So he throws him onto Lanka instead. At the same time, Garuda is sent to Ram and comes at once, setting up the next turn in the fight.
ramacharitamanas::4933.modern_relevance: You keep pushing a problem and it refuses to break. Then one call, one person, one opening appears and changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::4933.insight: It shows that the battle is moving by larger forces than brute strength alone.

ramacharitamanas::4934.verse_sanskrit: खगपति सब धरि खाए माया नाग बरुथ। माया बिगत भए सब हरषे बानर जूथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4934.verse_hindi: पक्षीराज गरुड़जी सब माया-सर्पों के समूहों को पकड़कर खा गए। तब सब वानरों के झुंड माया से रहित होकर हर्षित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4934.english_translation: Garuda swallowed all the groups of illusory serpents. Freed from the illusion, all the monkey hosts rejoiced.
ramacharitamanas::4934.translation_literal: खगपति (lord of birds) / सब (all) / धरि (seizing) / खाए (ate) / माया (illusion) / नाग (serpents) / बरुथ (groups, hosts) / माया (illusion) / बिगत (gone) / भए (became) / सब (all) / हरषे (rejoiced) / बानर (monkey) / जूथ (hosts)
ramacharitamanas::4934.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4934.essence: Illusion feeds fear; clear seeing gives courage back.
ramacharitamanas::4934.simple_meaning: Garuda destroys the illusion of serpent-like threats, and the monkey army feels relieved and joyful again.
ramacharitamanas::4934.simple_insight: When confusion is cleared away, courage returns on its own.
ramacharitamanas::4934.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has reached a strange, deceptive stage. Garuda arrives and wipes out the magical serpent forms that were troubling the monkey army. Once the illusion is broken, the monkeys recover their confidence.
ramacharitamanas::4934.modern_relevance: You finally read the message that had you spiraling all morning. It was not as dangerous as it seemed, and your body relaxes at once.
ramacharitamanas::4934.insight: It shifts attention from imagined threat to clear seeing, so fear loses its grip.

ramacharitamanas::4935.verse_sanskrit: गहि गिरि पादप उपल नख धाए कीस रिसाइ। चले तमीचर बिकलतर गढ़ पर चढ़े पराइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4935.verse_hindi: पर्वत, वृक्ष, पत्थर और नख धारण किए वानर क्रोधित होकर दौड़े। निशाचर विशेष व्याकुल होकर भाग चले और भागकर किले पर चढ़ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4935.english_translation: The monkeys, furious, rushed with mountains, trees, stones, and nails in hand. The night-dwellers, utterly alarmed, fled and climbed the fort.
ramacharitamanas::4935.translation_literal: गहि (taking) / गिरि (mountain) / पादप (tree) / उपल (stone) / नख (nails) / धाए (rushed) / कीस (monkeys) / रिसाइ (in anger) / चले (went) / तमीचर (night-dwellers) / बिकलतर (more distressed) / गढ़ (fort) / पर चढ़े (climbed) / पराइ (fleeing)
ramacharitamanas::4935.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4935.essence: Anger and courage together can drive fear into retreat.
ramacharitamanas::4935.simple_meaning: The monkey army charges in anger with whatever it can grab, and the enemy panics, runs, and hides inside the fort.
ramacharitamanas::4935.simple_insight: Fear scatters fast when courage surges forward.
ramacharitamanas::4935.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s battle, the monkey forces have broken into fierce momentum. Grabbing mountains, trees, stones, and even their nails, they rush the enemy so hard that the night-dwellers lose composure and scramble up into the fort.
ramacharitamanas::4935.modern_relevance: When a room full of people is suddenly in crisis, one calm, determined move can change everything. Panic spreads one way; courage spreads faster.
ramacharitamanas::4935.insight: It shifts attention from enemy strength to the force of collective resolve.

ramacharitamanas::4936.verse_sanskrit: मेघनाद कै मुरछा जागी। पितहि बिलोकि लाज अति लागी॥ तुरत गयउ गिरिबर कंदरा। करौं अजय मख अस मन धरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4936.verse_hindi: मेघनाद की मूर्च्छा छूटी, (तब) पिता को देखकर उसे बड़ी शर्म लगी। मैं अजय (अजेय होने को) यज्ञ करूँ, ऐसा मन में निश्चय करके वह तुरंत श्रेष्ठ पर्वत की गुफा में चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4936.english_translation: Meghanad's fainting passed, and seeing his father he felt deep shame. Resolving in his mind, "I will perform the invincible sacrifice," he quickly went into the mountain cave.
ramacharitamanas::4936.translation_literal: मेघनाद (Meghanad) / कै (of) / मुरछा (fainting) / जागी (awoke) / पितहि (father) / बिलोकि (seeing) / लाज (shame) / अति (greatly) / लागी (felt) / तुरत (immediately) / गयउ (went) / गिरिबर (great mountain) / कंदरा (cave) / करौं (I shall do) / अजय (invincible) / मख (sacrifice) / अस (such) / मन (mind) / धरा (held/formed)
ramacharitamanas::4936.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4936.essence: Shame drives him toward greater force, not wiser seeing.
ramacharitamanas::4936.simple_meaning: Meghanad regains consciousness, feels ashamed in front of his father, and rushes to a cave to prepare a sacrifice meant to make him invincible.
ramacharitamanas::4936.simple_insight: Pride can turn pain into a desperate plan for more power.
ramacharitamanas::4936.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Meghanad wakes after fainting and sees his father Ravana. The sight stings his pride. Instead of reflection, he hurries to a mountain cave to begin a sacrifice meant to make him invincible.
ramacharitamanas::4936.modern_relevance: You get embarrassed after failing in front of someone you wanted to impress, and your first instinct is to double down, not rethink. That rush can lead you deeper into the same trap.
ramacharitamanas::4936.insight: It shows how wounded pride can push a person toward more extreme, self-protective action.

ramacharitamanas::4937.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ बिभीषन मंत्र बिचारा। सुनहु नाथ बल अतुल उदारा॥ मेघनाद मख करइ अपावन। खल मायावी देव सतावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4937.verse_hindi: यहाँ विभीषण ने सलाह विचारी (और श्री रामचंद्रजी से कहा-) हे अतुलनीय बलवान् उदार प्रभो! देवताओं को सताने वाला दुष्ट, मायावी मेघनाद अपवित्र यज्ञ कर रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4937.english_translation: Here Vibhishana considered a plan and said, “Listen, Lord of immeasurable strength and generosity: the wicked, deceitful Meghnad is performing a polluted sacrifice that torments the radiant beings.”
ramacharitamanas::4937.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / मंत्र (plan; counsel) / बिचारा (considered) / सुनहु (listen) / नाथ (Lord) / बल (strength) / अतुल (immeasurable) / उदारा (generous) / मेघनाद (Meghnad) / मख (sacrifice) / करइ (is doing) / अपावन (impure) / खल (wicked one) / मायावी (deceitful; illusion-making) / देव (radiant beings) / सतावन (tormenting)
ramacharitamanas::4937.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4937.essence: Courageous counsel can interrupt a danger before it becomes unstoppable.
ramacharitamanas::4937.simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ram that Meghnad is carrying out an impure sacrifice that harms the radiant beings and must be stopped.
ramacharitamanas::4937.simple_insight: Clear seeing begins when someone names the danger without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4937.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Meghnad has gone into a cave to perform a forbidden sacrifice that could make him unbeatable. Vibhishana sees the threat plainly and warns Ram at once. The verse is a crucial alert, not the climax itself.
ramacharitamanas::4937.modern_relevance: You notice the meeting is turning into a trap, and one calm voice names it before everyone else gets carried away.
ramacharitamanas::4937.insight: It teaches you to speak up early when you see harmful intent taking shape.

ramacharitamanas::4938.verse_sanskrit: जौं प्रभु सिद्ध होइ सो पाइहि। नाथ बेगि पुनि जीति न जाइहि॥ सुनि रघुपति अतिसय सुख माना। बोले अंगदादि कपि नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4938.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! यदि वह यज्ञ सिद्ध हो पाएगा तो हे नाथ! फिर मेघनाद जल्दी जीता न जा सकेगा। यह सुनकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने बहुत सुख माना और अंगदादि बहुत से वानरों को बुलाया (और कहा-) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4938.english_translation: If that sacrifice succeeds, O Lord, then he will not be defeated quickly again. Hearing this, Raghupati felt great joy and called Angad and the other monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::4938.translation_literal: जौं (if) / प्रभु (Lord) / सिद्ध (successful) / होइ (becomes) / सो (that) / पाइहि (will obtain) / नाथ (O Lord) / बेगि (quickly) / पुनि (again) / जीति (defeated) / न (not) / जाइहि (will be able to be) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / अतिसय (great) / सुख (joy) / माना (felt) / बोले (spoke) / अंगदादि (Angad and others) / कपि (monkeys) / नाना (many) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4938.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4938.essence: Stop the source now, or the battle grows harder.
ramacharitamanas::4938.simple_meaning: Meghanad's success in the sacrifice would make him hard to defeat again. Ram is pleased by this news and gathers his monkey allies.
ramacharitamanas::4938.simple_insight: A small opening can change the whole battle.
ramacharitamanas::4938.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Meghanad is trying to gain invincibility through a sacrifice. Vibhishana warns Ram that if the rite succeeds, the war will become much harder. Ram listens, feels relief at the chance to stop it, and calls Angad and the other monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::4938.modern_relevance: You hear the warning just in time: if this plan goes through, fixing the mess later will be far harder. Good teams move fast when the opening is still open.
ramacharitamanas::4938.insight: It shifts attention from fighting the enemy directly to stopping the source of the enemy's power.

ramacharitamanas::4939.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन संग जाहु सब भाई। करहु बिधंस जग्य कर जाई॥ तुम्ह लछिमन मारेहु रन ओही। देखि सभय सुर दुख अति मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4939.verse_hindi: हे भाइयों! सब लोग लक्ष्मण के साथ जाओ और जाकर यज्ञ को विध्वंस करो। हे लक्ष्मण! संग्राम में तुम उसे मारना। देवताओं को भयभीत देखकर मुझे बड़ा दुःख है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4939.english_translation: All of you, go with Lakshman and destroy the sacrifice. Lakshman, kill him in battle. Seeing the gods frightened fills me with great sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::4939.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / संग (with) / जाहु (go) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers) / करहु (do) / बिधंस (destruction) / जग्य (sacrifice) / कर (having done) / जाई (go) ॥ तुम्ह (you) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / मारेहु (kill) / रन (battle) / ओही (that one) / देखि (seeing) / सभय (frightened) / सुर (deities) / दुख (sorrow) / अति (very) / मोही (me) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4939.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4939.essence: Stop the source of harm before it grows stronger.
ramacharitamanas::4939.simple_meaning: Ram sends Lakshman and the others to destroy the sacrificial rite and kill the enemy in battle. He feels deep sorrow seeing the radiant beings frightened.
ramacharitamanas::4939.simple_insight: Sometimes protecting what is right means stopping a harmful act before it spreads fear.
ramacharitamanas::4939.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has reached a critical turn. Ram sees Megnath's sacrificial rite empowering the enemy and orders Lakshman and the brothers to break it. His grief comes from watching the radiant beings suffer under that dark power.
ramacharitamanas::4939.modern_relevance: You watch a harmful plan gather momentum in a group chat, a workplace, or a family meeting. At some point, silence only helps the damage spread.
ramacharitamanas::4939.insight: It shifts you from passive concern to decisive intervention when harm is being strengthened.

ramacharitamanas::4940.verse_sanskrit: मारेहु तेहि बल बुद्धि उपाई। जेहिं छीजै निसिचर सुनु भाई॥ जामवंत सुग्रीव बिभीषन। सेन समेत रहेहु तीनिउ जन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4940.verse_hindi: हे भाई! सुनो, उसको ऐसे बल और बुद्धि के उपाय से मारना, जिससे निशाचर का नाश हो। हे जाम्बवान, सुग्रीव और विभीषण! तुम तीनों जन सेना समेत (इनके) साथ रहना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4940.english_translation: O brother, strike him down by strength, wisdom, and strategy so that the demon is finished. O Jambavan, Sugriva, and Vibhishana, you three should stay with the army.
ramacharitamanas::4940.translation_literal: मारेहु (strike) / तेहि (him) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (wisdom) / उपाई (strategy) / जेहिं (by which) / छीजै (is worn down, is destroyed) / निसिचर (demon) / सुनु (listen) / भाई (brother) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / सेन (army) / समेत (together with) / रहेहु (remain) / तीनिउ (all three) / जन (persons)
ramacharitamanas::4940.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4940.essence: Victory needs strength, intelligence, and the right people in place.
ramacharitamanas::4940.simple_meaning: Ram gives a tactical command: defeat the enemy through strength, intelligence, and strategy, while three trusted allies stay with the army.
ramacharitamanas::4940.simple_insight: Clear action matters more than panic. Use strength with thought, and keep the right support in place.
ramacharitamanas::4940.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram is directing the battle against the demon forces. He gives Lakshman a practical plan for destroying the enemy and tells Jambavan, Sugriva, and Vibhishana to hold the army together. The verse is part of the command, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4940.modern_relevance: A team is in crisis, and everyone is shouting over each other. One calm voice assigns the right people to the right roles, and the whole mess becomes workable.
ramacharitamanas::4940.insight: It shifts you from emotional reaction to coordinated execution under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4941.verse_sanskrit: जब रघुबीर दीन्हि अनुसासन। कटि निषंग कसि साजि सरासन॥ प्रभु प्रताप उर धरि रनधीरा। बोले घन इव गिरा गँभीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4941.verse_hindi: (इस प्रकार) जब श्री रघुवीर ने आज्ञा दी, तब कमर में तरकस कसकर और धनुष सजाकर (चढ़ाकर) रणधीर श्री लक्ष्मणजी प्रभु के प्रताप को हृदय में धारण करके मेघ के समान गंभीर वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::4941.english_translation: When Raghubir gave the command, Lakshman tightened his quiver at his waist, fitted his bow, held Ram's power in his heart, and spoke in a voice deep as thunder.
ramacharitamanas::4941.translation_literal: जब (when) रघुबीर (Raghubir) दीन्हि (gave) अनुसासन (command) / कटि (waist) निषंग (quiver) कसि (tightened) साजि (fitted) सरासन (bow) / प्रभु (lord/master) प्रताप (power/glory) उर (heart) धरि (holding) रनधीरा (battle-brave one) / बोले (spoke) घन (cloud) इव (like) गिरा (voice) गँभीरा (deep)
ramacharitamanas::4941.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4941.essence: Courage becomes clean when Ram's command is already in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::4941.simple_meaning: Lakshman receives Ram's command, arms himself, remembers Ram's power, and answers with calm courage.
ramacharitamanas::4941.simple_insight: True readiness is not noise; it is steady strength held in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::4941.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ram has just ordered Lakshman and the others into action against the enemy's sacrifice. Lakshman responds at once: he prepares his weapons, keeps Ram's power in mind, and speaks with grave courage before moving forward.
ramacharitamanas::4941.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with a hard message, and you breathe once before replying. The body gets ready, but the mind stays anchored. That is Lakshman's kind of strength.
ramacharitamanas::4941.insight: It shifts readiness from panic to composed action under guidance.

ramacharitamanas::4942.verse_sanskrit: जौं तेहि आजु बंधे बिनु आवौं। तौ रघुपति सेवक न कहावौं॥ जौं सत संकर करहिं सहाई। तदपि हतउँ रघुबीर दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4942.verse_hindi: यदि मैं आज उसे बिना मारे आऊँ, तो श्री रघुनाथजी का सेवक न कहलाऊँ। यदि सैकड़ों शंकर भी उसकी सहायता करें तो भी श्री रघुवीर की दुहाई है, आज मैं उसे मार ही डालूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4942.english_translation: If I return today without binding him, I will not be called Raghupati's servant. Even if a hundred Shankaras help him, by Raghubir's command I will kill him.
ramacharitamanas::4942.translation_literal: जौं (if) / तेहि (him) / आजु (today) / बंधे (having bound) / बिनु (without) / आवौं (I come) / तौ (then) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / सेवक (servant) / न (not) / कहावौं (I am called)॥ / जौं (if) / सत (hundreds) / संकर (Shankara) / करहिं (do) / सहाई (help) / तदपि (even then) / हतउँ (I will strike/kill) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / दोहाई (by the appeal/command)॥
ramacharitamanas::4942.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::4942.essence: Service means finishing the hard thing, even against impossible odds.
ramacharitamanas::4942.simple_meaning: Lakshman says he must finish the mission today. If he fails to bind the enemy, he feels unworthy of being called Ram's servant.
ramacharitamanas::4942.simple_insight: Real loyalty shows up in action, not intention.
ramacharitamanas::4942.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshman has been sent forward to crush the enemy. He declares that if he returns without binding Ravana, he does not deserve the name of Ram's servant. Even divine help would not make him turn back.
ramacharitamanas::4942.modern_relevance: You promised to handle the crisis, and the room is waiting on you. This is the moment when excuses disappear and character becomes visible in what you actually finish.
ramacharitamanas::4942.insight: It shifts you from self-image to responsibility: service is measured by completed action, not claimed devotion.

ramacharitamanas::4943.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति चरन नाइ सिरु चलेउ तुरंत अनंत। अंगद नील मयंद नल संग सुभट हनुमंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::4943.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर शेषावतार श्री लक्ष्मणजी तुरंत चले। उनके साथ अंगद, नील, मयंद, नल और हनुमान आदि उत्तम योद्धा थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4943.english_translation: Bowing his head at Raghupati's feet, he left at once. Angada, Nila, Mainda, Nala, and the brave Hanuman went with him.
ramacharitamanas::4943.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / चरन (feet) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / चलेउ (went) / तुरंत (at once) / अनंत (endless) / अंगद (Angada) / नील (Nila) / मयंद (Mainda) / नल (Nala) / संग (with) / सुभट (brave warriors) / हनुमंत (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4943.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4943.essence: Bowing first, they move as one.
ramacharitamanas::4943.simple_meaning: Laxman bows to Ram and immediately sets out, accompanied by Angada, Nila, Mainda, Nala, and Hanuman.
ramacharitamanas::4943.simple_insight: True service moves quickly, without hesitation or self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::4943.detailed_meaning: After Ram gives the order, Laxman bows at his feet and leaves at once with Angada, Nila, Mainda, Nala, and Hanuman. The verse simply marks the departure of the warrior band before the next act of battle.
ramacharitamanas::4943.modern_relevance: A team gets the final go-ahead, and the most reliable person is already moving before anyone else finishes talking.
ramacharitamanas::4943.insight: It shifts attention from planning to immediate, loyal action.

ramacharitamanas::4944.verse_sanskrit: जाइ कपिन्ह सो देखा बैसा। आहुति देत रुधिर अरु भैंसा॥ कीन्ह कपिन्ह सब जग्य बिधंसा। जब न उठइ तब करहिं प्रसंसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4944.verse_hindi: वानरों ने जाकर देखा कि वह बैठा हुआ खून और भैंसे की आहुति दे रहा है। वानरों ने सब यज्ञ विध्वंस कर दिया। फिर भी वह नहीं उठा, तब वे उसकी प्रशंसा करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4944.english_translation: The monkeys went and saw him seated, offering blood and buffaloes into the fire. The monkeys destroyed the whole sacrifice. Even then he did not get up, so they began to praise him.
ramacharitamanas::4944.translation_literal: जाइ (going) / कपिन्ह (by the monkeys) / सो (that one) / देखा (saw) / बैसा (seated) / आहुति (offering) / देत (giving) / रुधिर (blood) / अरु (and) / भैंसा (buffaloes) / कीन्ह (did) / कपिन्ह (by the monkeys) / सब (all) / जग्य (sacrifice) / बिधंसा (destruction) / जब (when) / न (not) / उठइ (gets up) / तब (then) / करहिं (they do) / प्रसंसा (praise)
ramacharitamanas::4944.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4944.essence: A ruined ritual only deepens the tension before the fight.
ramacharitamanas::4944.simple_meaning: The monkeys find an enemy priest or sorcerer performing a bloody sacrifice. They smash the ritual, but he still refuses to rise, so they mockingly praise him.
ramacharitamanas::4944.simple_insight: Some resistance is so strange that even praise becomes a tactic.
ramacharitamanas::4944.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkeys discover a man seated at a dark sacrificial fire, offering blood and buffaloes. They destroy the ritual, but he still does not move. This is a tense battle episode, not a teaching verse, and it leads directly into the fight that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4944.insight: It advances the battle scene by showing the enemy's strange calm before the next attack.

ramacharitamanas::4945.verse_sanskrit: तदपि न उठइ धरेन्हि कच जाई। लातन्हि हति हति चले पराई॥ लै त्रिसूल धावा कपि भागे। आए जहँ रामानुज आगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4945.verse_hindi: इतने पर भी वह न उठा, (तब) उन्होंने जाकर उसके बाल पकड़े और लातों से मार-मारकर वे भाग चले। वह त्रिशूल लेकर दौड़ा, तब वानर भागे और वहाँ आ गए, जहाँ आगे लक्ष्मणजी खड़े थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4945.english_translation: Even then he would not rise. So they seized his hair and beat him with kicks until he fled. Then he grabbed a trident and chased them, and the monkeys ran to where Lakshman stood ahead.
ramacharitamanas::4945.translation_literal: तदपि (even then) / न (not) / उठइ (rises) / धरेन्हि (they seized) / कच (hair) / जाई (going) / लातन्हि (with kicks) / हति हति (striking and striking) / चले (they went) / पराई (fled away) / लै (taking) / त्रिसूल (trident) / धावा (rushed) / कपि (monkeys) / भागे (ran) / आए (came) / जहँ (where) / रामानुज (Lakshman) / आगे (in front)
ramacharitamanas::4945.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4945.essence: Force only deepens the clash and pushes it toward the next defender.
ramacharitamanas::4945.simple_meaning: The fight keeps escalating: the enemy refuses to rise, the monkeys attack, and then he chases them with a trident until they run to Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::4945.simple_insight: Some conflicts only move forward by force, not persuasion.
ramacharitamanas::4945.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkeys have found a sacrificial scene and shattered it. The enemy still refuses to stand, so they grab his hair and kick him. He answers with a trident, driving them toward Lakshman as the battle widens.
ramacharitamanas::4945.modern_relevance: A tense group chat turns into insults, then threats, then everyone drags in one more person. The conflict has stopped being about the issue and become pure escalation.
ramacharitamanas::4945.insight: It shows a battle scene turning from restraint into open chase and counterattack.

ramacharitamanas::4946.verse_sanskrit: आवा परम क्रोध कर मारा। गर्ज घोर रव बारहिं बारा॥ कोपि मरुतसुत अंगद धाए। हति त्रिसूल उर धरनि गिराए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4946.verse_hindi: वह अत्यंत क्रोध का मारा हुआ आया और बार-बार भयंकर शब्द करके गरजने लगा। मारुति (हनुमान् ) और अंगद क्रोध करके दौड़े। उसने छाती में त्रिशूल मारकर दोनों को धरती पर गिरा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4946.english_translation: Overcome by fierce rage, he came roaring again and again. Maruti and Angada charged in anger, but he struck them in the chest with his trident and hurled them to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::4946.translation_literal: आवा (came) / परम (fierce) / क्रोध (rage) / कर (having) / मारा (struck) / गर्ज (roared) / घोर (terrible) / रव (sound) / बारहिं बार (again and again)॥ / कोपि (in anger) / मरुतसुत (Maruti) / अंगद (Angada) / धाए (rushed) / हति (striking) / त्रिसूल (trident) / उर (chest) / धरनि (to the ground) / गिराए (threw down) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4946.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4946.essence: Rage turns the battlefield into pure impact.
ramacharitamanas::4946.simple_meaning: In the battle, the enemy rushes forward in rage and knocks Hanuman and Angada down with his trident.
ramacharitamanas::4946.simple_insight: Some scenes are only force and impact — no lesson, just the cost of battle.
ramacharitamanas::4946.detailed_meaning: The fight in Lanka is still raging. After the earlier clash with the vanara warriors, the trident-wielding enemy returns in fury, roaring and striking down Maruti and Angada. The verse simply carries the action forward into the next blow.
ramacharitamanas::4946.modern_relevance: A conflict escalates before anyone has time to think. Voices rise, bodies tense, and the room becomes pure reaction.
ramacharitamanas::4946.insight: It keeps the battle moving by showing the immediate consequences of rage and counterattack.

ramacharitamanas::4947.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु कहँ छाँड़ेसि सूल प्रचंडा। सर हति कृत अनंत जुग खंडा॥ उठि बहोरि मारुति जुबराजा। हतहिं कोपि तेहि घाउ न बाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4947.verse_hindi: फिर उसने प्रभु श्री लक्ष्मणजी पर त्रिशूल छोड़ा। अनन्त (श्री लक्ष्मणजी) ने बाण मारकर उसके दो टुकड़े कर दिए। हनुमान् जी और युवराज अंगद फिर उठकर क्रोध करके उसे मारने लगे, उसे चोट न लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4947.english_translation: Then he hurled the fierce trident at Lord Lakshman. Lakshman struck it and split it into two. Hanuman and Prince Angad rose again in anger to strike him, but he felt no wound.
ramacharitamanas::4947.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / कहँ (toward) / छाँड़ेसि (he hurled) / सूल (trident) / प्रचंडा (fierce) / सर (arrow) / हति (striking) / कृत (made) / अनंत (endless) / जुग (ages) / खंडा (split) / उठि (rising) / बहोरि (again) / मारुति (Hanuman) / जुबराजा (prince) / हतहिं (striking) / कोपि (in anger) / तेहि (him) / घाउ (wound) / न (not) / बाजा (appeared)
ramacharitamanas::4947.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4947.essence: The fight continues even after a blow seems to land.
ramacharitamanas::4947.simple_meaning: The enemy throws a fierce trident at Lakshman, but Lakshman breaks it. Hanuman and Angad attack again, yet the enemy seems untouched.
ramacharitamanas::4947.simple_insight: Some battles keep going even after a blow lands. Courage means rising again without losing heart.
ramacharitamanas::4947.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshman faces Meghnad's relentless attack. Hanuman and Angad keep pressing forward, but the enemy neither falls nor shows pain. The verse is one more movement in the larger combat, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramacharitamanas::4947.modern_relevance: You fix one problem at midnight, then three more appear by morning. The work is not finished just because the first strike landed.
ramacharitamanas::4947.insight: It keeps the focus on endurance in conflict, not on a single decisive moment.

ramacharitamanas::4948.verse_sanskrit: फिरे बीर रिपु मरइ न मारा। तब धावा करि घोर चिकारा॥ आवत देखि कुरद्ध जनु काला। लछिमन छाड़े बिसिख कराला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4948.verse_hindi: शत्रु (मेघनाद) मारे नहीं मरता, यह देखकर जब वीर लौटे, तब वह घोर चिग्घाड़ करके दौड़ा। उसे क्रुद्ध काल की तरह आता देखकर लक्ष्मणजी ने भयानक बाण छोड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4948.english_translation: Seeing that the warrior would not die even after being struck, he roared and rushed forward. Seeing him come on like angry death itself, Lakshman released terrible arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4948.translation_literal: फिरे (turned back) / बीर (the warrior) / रिपु (enemy) / मरइ न मारा (does not die even when struck) / तब (then) / धावा (charged) / करि (making) / घोर (fierce) / चिकारा (roar) / आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / कुरद्ध (angry) / जनु (as if) / काला (death) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / छाड़े (released) / बिसिख (arrows) / कराला (terrible)
ramacharitamanas::4948.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4948.essence: Some battles demand instant force, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4948.simple_meaning: The enemy kept fighting even after being struck, so the battle surged again. Lakshman answered with fierce arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4948.simple_insight: When pressure rises, courage shows up as a clean, immediate response.
ramacharitamanas::4948.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final battle, the enemy warrior keeps escaping death and returns to attack again. Lakshman sees him rushing in like death itself and fires terrible arrows. The verse keeps the combat moving; it does not pause for a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4948.modern_relevance: You are in a heated argument, and the other person keeps pushing even after the point is made. You stop explaining and answer firmly, without losing your nerve.
ramacharitamanas::4948.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive action under threat.

ramacharitamanas::4949.verse_sanskrit: देखेसि आवत पबि सम बाना। तुरत भयउ खल अंतरधाना॥ बिबिध बेष धरि करइ लराई। कबहुँक प्रगट कबहुँ दुरि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4949.verse_hindi: वज्र के समान बाणों को आते देखकर वह दुष्ट तुरंत अंतर्धान हो गया और फिर भाँति-भाँति के रूप धारण करके युद्ध करने लगा। वह कभी प्रकट होता था और कभी छिप जाता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4949.english_translation: Seeing the arrows coming like thunderbolts, the wicked one at once vanished. Taking many disguises, he fought, appearing and disappearing again and again.
ramacharitamanas::4949.translation_literal: देखेसि (he saw) / आवत (coming) / पबि सम (like a thunderbolt) / बाना (arrows) / तुरत (at once) / भयउ (became) / खल (the wicked one) / अंतरधाना (vanished) / बिबिध (many) / बेष (forms/disguises) / धरि (taking) / करइ (does) / लराई (battle) / कबहुँक (sometimes) / प्रगट (visible) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / दुरि जाई (goes away / hides)
ramacharitamanas::4949.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4949.essence: Clever hiding cannot stop what is closing in.
ramacharitamanas::4949.simple_meaning: The enemy keeps changing form to avoid being hit, appearing and disappearing as the battle continues.
ramacharitamanas::4949.simple_insight: Evasion can look clever, but it only delays what must be faced.
ramacharitamanas::4949.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Lakshman has forced Meghnad into desperate tactics. Seeing the arrows rush in like thunderbolts, the enemy vanishes and keeps changing form to confuse the fighters. The verse adds movement to the battle, not its teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4949.modern_relevance: A person keeps changing the story in a tense conversation, dodging every direct question. You can feel the truth slipping away, even as the performance gets more elaborate.
ramacharitamanas::4949.insight: It shows how fear and cunning create motion without resolution.

ramacharitamanas::4950.verse_sanskrit: देखि अजय रिपु डरपे कीसा। परम क्रुद्ध तब भयउ अहीसा॥ लछिमन मन अस मंत्र दृढ़ावा। ऐहि पापिहि मैं बहुत खेलावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4950.verse_hindi: शत्रु को पराजित न होता देखकर वानर डरे। तब सर्पराज शेषजी (लक्ष्मणजी) बहुत क्रोधित हुए। लक्ष्मणजी ने मन में यह विचार दृढ़ किया कि इस पापी को मैं बहुत खेला चुका (अब और अधिक खेलाना अच्छा नहीं, अब तो इसे समाप्त ही कर देना चाहिए।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4950.english_translation: Seeing the enemy could not be defeated, the monkeys grew afraid. Then Lakshman became fiercely angry. In his mind he resolved, "I have toyed with this sinner enough."
ramacharitamanas::4950.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / अजय (not conquerable) / रिपु (enemy) / डरपे (the monkeys became afraid) / कीसा (monkeys) / परम (extremely) / क्रुद्ध (angry) / तब (then) / भयउ (became) / अहीसा (Lakshman, the serpent-king) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / मन (mind) / अस (thus) / मंत्र (resolve) / दृढ़ावा (made firm) / ऐहि (this) / पापिहि (sinner) / मैं (I) / बहुत (much) / खेलावा (toyed with)
ramacharitamanas::4950.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4950.essence: Delay has a limit; righteous force eventually becomes necessary.
ramacharitamanas::4950.simple_meaning: The monkeys lose confidence when the enemy keeps escaping, and Lakshman decides it is time to end the fight.
ramacharitamanas::4950.simple_insight: There comes a point when patience turns into decisive action.
ramacharitamanas::4950.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the enemy keeps slipping away through tricks and disguises. The monkey army starts to fear he cannot be beaten. Lakshman, already burning with anger, hardens his resolve and decides the fight must end now.
ramacharitamanas::4950.modern_relevance: You keep giving someone another chance, and they keep slipping out of every consequence. Then the moment comes when hesitation feels like permission, and you finally decide enough is enough.
ramacharitamanas::4950.insight: It shifts the mind from tolerating endless evasion to making a clear, final decision.

ramacharitamanas::4951.verse_sanskrit: सुमिरि कोसलाधीस प्रतापा। सर संधान कीन्ह करि दापा॥ छाड़ा बान माझ उर लागा। मरती बार कपटु सब त्यागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4951.verse_hindi: कोसलपति श्री रामजी के प्रताप का स्मरण करके लक्ष्मणजी ने वीरोचित दर्प करके बाण का संधान किया। बाण छोड़ते ही उसकी छाती के बीच में लगा। मरते समय उसने सब कपट त्याग दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4951.english_translation: Remembering the glory of the Lord of Kosala, Lakshmana drew his bow with fierce courage. The arrow struck him in the middle of the chest, and at the moment of death he gave up all deceit.
ramacharitamanas::4951.translation_literal: सुमिरि (remembering) / कोसलाधीस (the Lord of Kosala) / प्रतापा (glory, power) / सर (arrow) / संधान (setting, nocking) / कीन्ह (did) / करि (with) / दापा (pride, fierce courage)॥ / छाड़ा (released) / बान (arrow) / माझ (middle) / उर (chest) / लागा (struck)॥ / मरती (dying) / बार (time) / कपटु (deceit, trickery) / सब (all) / त्यागा (abandoned)॥
ramacharitamanas::4951.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4951.essence: Ram-centered resolve makes the arrow true and the mask fall away.
ramacharitamanas::4951.simple_meaning: Lakshmana, remembering Ram's power, shot his arrow with fierce resolve. It struck the enemy in the chest, and death made the enemy drop all deceit.
ramacharitamanas::4951.simple_insight: Even a cunning heart can become honest when death strips away its masks.
ramacharitamanas::4951.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the enemy keeps changing form and slipping away. Lakshmana, burning with anger for Ram's sake, fixes his mind on Ram's glory and shoots true. The blow lands, and the dying foe finally drops all disguise.
ramacharitamanas::4951.modern_relevance: You can spend months hiding behind image, strategy, and half-truths. One hard moment can strip all that away and show what was real.
ramacharitamanas::4951.insight: It shows that decisive action, rooted in remembrance of Ram, cuts through deception.

ramacharitamanas::4952.verse_sanskrit: रामानुज कहँ रामु कहँ अस कहि छाँड़ेसि प्रान। धन्य धन्य तव जननी कह अंगद हनुमान ॥
ramacharitamanas::4952.verse_hindi: राम के छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? राम कहाँ हैं? ऐसा कहकर उसने प्राण छोड़ दिए। अंगद और हनुमान कहने लगे- तेरी माता धन्य है, धन्य है (जो तू लक्ष्मणजी के हाथों मरा और मरते समय श्री राम-लक्ष्मण को स्मरण करके तूने उनके नामों का उच्चारण किया।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4952.english_translation: Where is Ram's younger brother Lakshman? Where is Ram? Saying this, he gave up his life. Angad and Hanuman said, "Blessed, blessed is your mother."
ramacharitamanas::4952.translation_literal: रामानुज (Ram's younger brother) / कहँ (where is) / रामु (Ram) / कहँ (where is) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / छाँड़ेसि (gave up) / प्रान (life/breath) / धन्य (blessed) / धन्य (blessed) / तव (your) / जननी (mother) / कह (said) / अंगद (Angad) / हनुमान (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4952.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4952.essence: Your final thought reveals where your heart has been.
ramacharitamanas::4952.simple_meaning: He dies with Ram and Lakshman on his lips, and Angad and Hanuman praise the rare blessing of that final remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::4952.simple_insight: The last words matter. Even in death, the mind can turn toward what it loves most.
ramacharitamanas::4952.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshman has struck down a foe so completely that the enemy dies asking for Ram and Lakshman. Angad and Hanuman immediately honour that final remembrance, seeing it as a sacred ending rather than a defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4952.modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, someone who spent years resisting faith suddenly whispers the name they trusted most. The people around them feel the weight of that last turning.
ramacharitamanas::4952.insight: It shifts attention from the violence of the moment to the direction of the final thought.

ramacharitamanas::4953.verse_sanskrit: बिनु प्रयास हनुमान उठायो। लंका द्वार राखि पुनि आयो॥ तासु मरन सुनि सुर गंधर्बा। चढ़ि बिमान आए नभ सर्बा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4953.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने उसको बिना ही परिश्रम के उठा लिया और लंका के दरवाजे पर रखकर वे लौट आए। उसका मरना सुनकर देवता और गंधर्व आदि सब विमानों पर चढ़कर आकाश में आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4953.english_translation: Hanuman lifted him effortlessly, placed him at Lanka's gate, and returned. Hearing of his death, the gods and gandharvas all came in their flying chariots.
ramacharitamanas::4953.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / प्रयास (effort) / हनुमान (Hanuman) / उठायो (lifted) / लंका (Lanka) / द्वार (gate) / राखि (having placed) / पुनि (again) / आयो (came) ॥ / तासु (his) / मरन (death) / सुनि (hearing) / सुर (deities) / गंधर्बा (gandharvas) / चढ़ि (having mounted) / बिमान (flying chariots) / आए (came) / नभ (sky) / सर्बा (all)
ramacharitamanas::4953.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4953.essence: True force acts cleanly and leaves no pride behind.
ramacharitamanas::4953.simple_meaning: Hanuman easily carried the body, set it at Lanka's gate, and returned. When the enemy died, celestial beings came to witness the moment.
ramacharitamanas::4953.simple_insight: Some acts are so complete that even the higher worlds take notice.
ramacharitamanas::4953.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final battle, Hanuman lifts a fallen foe without strain and leaves him at the city gate before returning. The death is so significant that celestial beings descend to witness it, marking the end of a fierce encounter.
ramacharitamanas::4953.modern_relevance: You finish the hardest part of a conflict, then step back and let the moment speak for itself. Even private victories can feel larger than the room you're in.
ramacharitamanas::4953.insight: It frames decisive action as something that can be completed cleanly, without drama or attachment.

ramacharitamanas::4954.verse_sanskrit: बरषि सुमन दुंदुभीं बजावहिं। श्रीरघुनाथ बिमल जसु गावहिं॥ जय अनंत जय जगदाधारा। तुम्ह प्रभु सब देवन्हि निस्तारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4954.verse_hindi: वे फूल बरसाकर नगाड़े बजाते हैं और श्री रघुनाथजी का निर्मल यश गाते हैं। हे अनन्त! आपकी जय हो, हे जगदाधार! आपकी जय हो। हे प्रभो! आपने सब देवताओं का (महान् विपत्ति से) उद्धार किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4954.english_translation: They shower flowers, beat the drums, and sing the pure glory of Shri Raghunath. Victory to the endless one, victory to the support of the worlds. O Lord, you have delivered all the radiant beings from great danger.
ramacharitamanas::4954.translation_literal: बरषि (shower) / सुमन (flowers) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजावहिं (they beat) / श्रीरघुनाथ (Shri Raghunath) / बिमल (pure) / जसु (glory) / गावहिं (they sing) / जय (victory) / अनंत (endless one) / जय (victory) / जगदाधारा (support of the worlds) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रभु (Lord) / सब (all) / देवन्हि (radiant beings) / निस्तारा (delivered)
ramacharitamanas::4954.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4954.essence: Ram's victory turns fear into praise.
ramacharitamanas::4954.simple_meaning: The gods celebrate Ram with flowers, drums, and praise, calling him the endless support of the worlds and the one who saved them.
ramacharitamanas::4954.simple_insight: Praise rises naturally when suffering has ended and rescue has come.
ramacharitamanas::4954.detailed_meaning: After Hanuman carries the dying messenger back from Lanka, the celestial beings gather above the battlefield. They celebrate Ram's victory, sing his spotless glory, and praise him as the endless support who rescued the radiant beings from danger.
ramacharitamanas::4954.modern_relevance: You finally hear the message you feared might never come: the crisis has passed. Relief can feel almost ceremonial, like your whole body wants to sing before your mind catches up.
ramacharitamanas::4954.insight: It frames rescue as something that deserves gratitude, not just relief.

ramacharitamanas::4955.verse_sanskrit: अस्तुति करि सुर सिद्ध सिधाए। लछिमन कृपासिंधु पहिं आए॥ सुत बध सुना दसानन जबहीं। मुरुछित भयउ परेउ महि तबहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4955.verse_hindi: देवता और सिद्ध स्तुति करके चले गए, तब लक्ष्मणजी कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी के पास आए। रावण ने ज्यों ही पुत्रवध का समाचार सुना, त्यों ही वह मूर्च्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4955.english_translation: After the gods and siddhas offered praise and departed, Lakshman came to the compassionate Lord. As soon as Ravana heard of his son's death, he fainted and fell to the earth.
ramacharitamanas::4955.translation_literal: अस्तुति (praise) / करि (having done) / सुर (gods) / सिद्ध (siddhas) / सिधाए (departed) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / पहिं (to, near) / आए (came) / सुत (son) / बध (death, killing) / सुना (heard) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / जबहीं (as soon as) / मुरुछित (fainted) / भयउ (became) / परेउ (fell) / महि (on the earth) / तबहीं (then)
ramacharitamanas::4955.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4955.essence: Ravana's pride falls the moment loss becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::4955.simple_meaning: The celestial beings leave after praising Ram. Lakshman returns to Ram. Ravana hears that his son has been killed and collapses in grief.
ramacharitamanas::4955.simple_insight: Pride can hold until loss becomes personal; then it breaks.
ramacharitamanas::4955.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the gods and perfected beings have just praised Ram and gone away. Lakshman returns to Ram, while Ravana receives the crushing news of his son's death. The verse marks the instant his strength gives way.
ramacharitamanas::4955.modern_relevance: You keep your face steady through the meeting, the texts, the noise — then one phone call about your child, and everything inside drops at once.
ramacharitamanas::4955.insight: It shows how quickly ego can collapse when grief reaches the heart.

ramacharitamanas::4956.verse_sanskrit: मंदोदरी रुदन कर भारी। उर ताड़न बहु भाँति पुकारी॥ रनगर लोग सब ब्याकुल सोचा। सकल कहहिं दसकंधर पोचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4956.verse_hindi: मंदोदरी छाती पीट-पीटकर और बहुत प्रकार से पुकार-पुकारकर बड़ा भारी विलाप करने लगी। नगर के सब लोग शोक से व्याकुल हो गए। सभी रावण को नीच कहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4956.english_translation: Mandodari broke into a great lament, beating her chest and crying out in many ways. All the people of the city became agitated with grief and sorrow. Everyone began calling Ravana base and fallen.
ramacharitamanas::4956.translation_literal: मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / रुदन (lamenting) / कर (doing) / भारी (great) / उर (chest) / ताड़न (beating) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / पुकारी (cried out) / रनगर (city of war) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / ब्याकुल (disturbed) / सोचा (in sorrow) / सकल (everyone) / कहहिं (say) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / पोचा (base, fallen)
ramacharitamanas::4956.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4956.essence: Pride collapses when its losses finally reach the home.
ramacharitamanas::4956.simple_meaning: Mandodari grieves loudly, the city is thrown into sorrow, and Ravana is openly condemned.
ramacharitamanas::4956.simple_insight: Pride leaves behind only grief, and even power cannot stop that reckoning.
ramacharitamanas::4956.detailed_meaning: After Ravana learns of his son's death, Lanka is no longer triumphant. Mandodari cries out in anguish, the whole city is shaken, and people begin speaking of Ravana with contempt. The war's cost is now visible inside his own home.
ramacharitamanas::4956.modern_relevance: A family receives the call no one wanted, and the house goes silent except for one person crying in the kitchen. The damage is no longer abstract; everyone can feel what pride has cost.
ramacharitamanas::4956.insight: It shifts attention from victory to consequence, showing how private grief exposes public failure.

ramacharitamanas::4957.verse_sanskrit: तब दसकंठ बिबिधि बिधि समुझाईं सब नारि। नस्वर रूप जगत सब देखहु हृदयँ बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4957.verse_hindi: तब रावण ने सब स्त्रियों को अनेकों प्रकार से समझाया कि समस्त जगत् का यह (दृश्य)रूप नाशवान् है, हृदय में विचारकर देखो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4957.english_translation: Then Ravana, in many ways, tried to console all the women: "See with your heart that the whole world is only a passing form."
