ramacharitamanas::4957.translation_literal: तब (then) / दसकंठ (Ravana) / बिबिधि बिधि (in many ways) / समुझाईं (explained, consoled) / सब नारि (all the women) / नस्वर (impermanent, perishable) / रूप (form) / जगत (world) / सब (all) / देखहु (see) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारि (having reflected)
ramacharitamanas::4957.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4957.essence: Seeing impermanence is the first release from grief.
ramacharitamanas::4957.simple_meaning: Ravana tells the women to remember that the visible world does not last. He urges them to reflect inwardly instead of clinging to appearances.
ramacharitamanas::4957.simple_insight: Letting go becomes possible when you stop treating passing things as permanent.
ramacharitamanas::4957.detailed_meaning: After the death of his son, Ravana tries to steady the women around him. In the middle of grief and collapse, he speaks like a teacher of impermanence, asking them to look inward and see that the visible world cannot be held.
ramacharitamanas::4957.modern_relevance: At a hospital corridor after bad news, someone keeps repeating, "It was fine yesterday." This verse asks you to face change honestly instead of bargaining with what cannot remain.
ramacharitamanas::4957.insight: It shifts attention from emotional clinging to clear seeing of impermanence.

ramacharitamanas::4958.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि ग्यान उपदेसा रावन। आपुन मंद कथा सुभ पावन॥ पर उपदेस कुसल बहुतेरे। जे आचरहिं ते नर न घनेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4958.verse_hindi: रावण ने उनको ज्ञान का उपदेश किया। वह स्वयं तो नीच है, पर उसकी कथा (बातें) शुभ और पवित्र हैं। दूसरों को उपदेश देने में तो बहुत लोग निपुण होते हैं। पर ऐसे लोग अधिक नहीं हैं, जो उपदेश के अनुसार आचरण भी करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4958.english_translation: Ravana preached wisdom to them. He himself was base, yet his story is pure and auspicious. Many people are skilled at advising others, but few live by their own advice.
ramacharitamanas::4958.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (to them) / ग्यान (wisdom) / उपदेसा (gave instruction) / रावन (Ravana) / आपुन (himself) / मंद (base) / कथा (story, account) / सुभ (auspicious) / पावन (pure) / पर (but) / उपदेस (instruction) / कुसल (skilled) / बहुतेरे (many) / जे (those who) / आचरहिं (practice) / ते (they) / नर (people) / न घनेरे (not many)
ramacharitamanas::4958.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4958.essence: Words can sound pure while the speaker remains unchanged.
ramacharitamanas::4958.simple_meaning: Ravana can speak about wisdom, but he does not live it. Many people can advise others; very few practice what they preach.
ramacharitamanas::4958.simple_insight: It stings the ego and invites honesty: knowledge means little without lived conduct.
ramacharitamanas::4958.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to steady the women with lofty words even as his own collapse is near. The narrator cuts through the performance: a person may speak beautifully, yet still fail to embody the very counsel he gives.
ramacharitamanas::4958.modern_relevance: A manager gives the team a speech about integrity, then quietly breaks the same rule in private. The gap between polished advice and lived conduct is exactly what this verse exposes.
ramacharitamanas::4958.insight: It shifts attention from sounding wise to becoming trustworthy through action.

ramacharitamanas::4959.verse_sanskrit: निसा सिरानि भयउ भिनुसारा। लगे भालु कपि चारिहुँ द्वारा॥ सुभट बोलाइ दसानन बोला। रन सन्मुख जाकर मन डोला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4959.verse_hindi: रात बीत गई, सबेरा हुआ। रीछ-वानर (फिर) चारों दरवाजों पर जा डटे। योद्धाओं को बुलाकर दशमुख रावण ने कहा- लड़ाई में शत्रु के सम्मुख मन डाँवाडोल हो, ॥
ramacharitamanas::4959.english_translation: Night passed and dawn broke. The monkeys and bears took positions at the four gates. Ravana called his warriors and said, 'In battle, your mind should not waver before the enemy.'
ramacharitamanas::4959.translation_literal: निसा (night) / सिरानि (having passed) / भयउ (became) / भिनुसारा (dawn) / लगे (were stationed) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / चारिहुँ (four) / द्वारा (gates) / सुभट (warriors) / बोलाइ (having called) / दसानन (ten-faced one) / बोला (spoke) / रन (battle) / सन्मुख (facing) / जाकर (having gone) / मन (mind) / डोला (wavered)
ramacharitamanas::4959.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4959.essence: Bravado can rise just as fear begins to show.
ramacharitamanas::4959.simple_meaning: Dawn comes, the armies take their positions, and Ravana rallies his warriors by warning them not to lose their nerve in battle.
ramacharitamanas::4959.simple_insight: Pressure reveals whether courage is real or only spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4959.detailed_meaning: At dawn in Lanka, the monkeys and bears hold the four gates while Ravana gathers his warriors. He tries to steady them before the final clash, but his own words already hint at the fear beneath his pride.
ramacharitamanas::4959.modern_relevance: The meeting starts in five minutes, and everyone can feel the tension. You straighten your notes and try to sound confident, even though your own mind is shaking.
ramacharitamanas::4959.insight: It shows how people facing defeat often speak bravely to hide inner instability.

ramacharitamanas::4960.verse_sanskrit: सो अबहीं बरु जाउ पराई। संजुग बिमुख भएँ न भलाई॥ निज भुज बल मैं बयरु बढ़ावा। देहउँ उतरु जो रिपु चढ़ि आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4960.verse_hindi: अच्छा है वह अभी भाग जाए। युद्ध में जाकर विमुख होने (भागने) में भलाई नहीं है। मैंने अपनी भुजाओं के बल पर बैर बढ़ाया है। जो शत्रु चढ़ आया है, उसको मैं (अपने ही) उत्तर दे लूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4960.english_translation: It is better that he flee now. There is no honor in turning away once battle has begun. I have increased my enmity by my own strength, and I will answer any enemy who comes up against me.
ramacharitamanas::4960.translation_literal: सो (so/therefore) / अबहीं (right now) / बरु (better) / जाउ (let him go) / पराई (away, flee) / संजुग (in battle) / बिमुख (facing away, retreating) / भएँ (having become) / न (not) / भलाई (goodness, honor)॥ / निज (own) / भुज (arms) / बल (strength) / मैं (by) / बयरु (enmity) / बढ़ावा (I increased) / देहउँ (I will give) / उतरु (answer) / जो (who) / रिपु (enemy) / चढ़ि आवा (has come up, advanced) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4960.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4960.essence: Pride would rather fight than admit fear.
ramacharitamanas::4960.simple_meaning: Ravana says it is better to face the enemy than run away. He insists that since he built this conflict by his own strength, he will answer the challenger himself.
ramacharitamanas::4960.simple_insight: Pride can make retreat feel worse than defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4960.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is rallying his warriors as the war closes in. Rather than admit fear, he frames the coming clash as a matter of honor and personal strength. The verse shows his pride hardening into defiance.
ramacharitamanas::4960.modern_relevance: You know that moment when backing out would save you trouble, but your ego says you have to prove yourself? Ravana lives there.
ramacharitamanas::4960.insight: It reveals how ego turns conflict into a personal challenge instead of a wise choice.

ramacharitamanas::4961.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि मरुत बेग रथ साजा। बाजे सकल जुझाऊ बाजा॥ चले बीर सब अतुलित बली। जनु कज्जल कै आँधी चली ॥
ramacharitamanas::4961.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर उसने पवन के समान तेज चलने वाला रथ सजाया। सारे जुझाऊ (लड़ाई के) बाजे बजने लगे। सब अतुलनीय बलवान् वीर ऐसे चले मानो काजल की आँधी चली हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::4961.english_translation: Having said this, he had his wind-swift chariot prepared. All the war drums began to sound. All the mighty warriors moved out, like a storm of kohl rolling in.
ramacharitamanas::4961.translation_literal: अस कहि (having said this) / मरुत (wind) / बेग (swiftly) / रथ (chariot) / साजा (was prepared) / बाजे (sounded) / सकल (all) / जुझाऊ (war-like) / बाजा (drums/instruments) / चले (moved) / बीर (warriors) / सब (all) / अतुलित बली (immeasurably strong) / जनु (as if) / कज्जल (kohl) / कै (of) / आँधी (storm) / चली (moved)
ramacharitamanas::4961.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4961.essence: Pride can sound like strength right before it turns into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4961.simple_meaning: Ravana prepares for battle, and his warriors march out with great force. The verse mainly shows the army moving into action.
ramacharitamanas::4961.simple_insight: Big displays of force can still be just motion toward collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4961.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already rejected warning and chosen pride. Now he orders his wind-fast chariot prepared, war drums to sound, and his strongest warriors to march out. The scene builds the pressure before the next line reveals the omens he ignores.
ramacharitamanas::4961.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with aggressive messages, the meeting starts, and everyone rushes in acting invincible. The energy looks powerful, but it is only momentum.
ramacharitamanas::4961.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to what it is hiding: pride rushing ahead of judgment.

ramacharitamanas::4962.verse_sanskrit: असगुन अमित होहिं तेहि काला। गनइ न भुज बल गर्ब बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4962.verse_hindi: उस समय असंख्य अपशकुन होने लगे। पर अपनी भुजाओं के बल का बड़ा गर्व होने से रावण उन्हें गिनता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4962.english_translation: At that moment, countless bad omens appeared, but Ravana’s vast pride in his own strength made him ignore them.
ramacharitamanas::4962.translation_literal: असगुन (bad omens) / अमित (countless) / होहिं (happen) / तेहि (that) / काला (time) / गनइ (counts/considers) / न (not) / भुज बल (arm strength) / गर्ब (pride) / बिसाला (vast)
ramacharitamanas::4962.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4962.essence: Pride makes even clear warnings unreadable.
ramacharitamanas::4962.simple_meaning: Ravana is surrounded by warning signs, but his pride in his own strength makes him dismiss them.
ramacharitamanas::4962.simple_insight: Ego can make obvious danger feel invisible.
ramacharitamanas::4962.detailed_meaning: Ravana is already marching into war, and the signs around him are turning dark. Instead of stopping to reflect, he trusts his own power so completely that he cannot read the warnings.
ramacharitamanas::4962.modern_relevance: You keep seeing the same red flags in a relationship, but your confidence says you can handle it. Pride can make the obvious look optional.
ramacharitamanas::4962.insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence without reflection to honest attention to warning signs.

ramacharitamanas::4963.verse_sanskrit: अति गर्ब गनइ न सगुन असगुन स्रवहिं आयुध हाथ ते। भट गिरत रथ ते बाजि गज चिक्करत भाजहिं साथ ते॥ गोमाय गीध कराल खर रव स्वान बोलहिं अति घने। जनु कालदूत उलूक बोलहिं बचन परम भयावने॥
ramacharitamanas::4963.verse_hindi: अत्यंत गर्व के कारण वह शकुन-अपशकुन का विचार नहीं करता। हथियार हाथों से गिर रहे हैं। योद्धा रथ से गिर पड़ते हैं। घोड़े, हाथी साथ छोड़कर चिग्घाड़ते हुए भाग जाते हैं। स्यार, गीध, कौए और गदहे शब्द कर रहे हैं। बहुत अधिक कुत्ते बोल रहे हैं। उल्लू ऐसे अत्यंत भयानक शब्द कर रहे हैं, मानो काल के दूत हों। (मृत्यु का संदेसा सुना रहे हों)।
ramacharitamanas::4963.english_translation: Out of overwhelming pride, he ignores omens and ill omens. Weapons slip from his hands; warriors fall from their chariots; horses and elephants flee, neighing and trumpeting. Jackals, vultures, crows, and donkeys cry out. Dogs bark loudly, and owls sound like messengers of death, speaking terrifying words.
ramacharitamanas::4963.translation_literal: अति (excessive) / गर्ब (pride) / गनइ न (does not count) / सगुन (omens) / असगुन (ill omens) / स्रवहिं (slip/fall) / आयुध (weapons) / हाथ ते (from the hands) / भट (warriors) / गिरत (falling) / रथ ते (from chariots) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / चिक्करत (crying out) / भाजहिं (run away) / साथ ते (from with them) / गोमाय (jackals) / गीध (vultures) / कराल (fierce) / खर (donkeys) / रव (sounds) / स्वान (dogs) / बोलहिं (bark) / अति घने (very many) / जनु (as if) / कालदूत (messengers of death) / उलूक (owls) / बोलहिं (cry out) / बचन (words) / परम (extremely) / भयावने (terrifying)
ramacharitamanas::4963.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4963.essence: Pride makes even death's warnings sound like noise.
ramacharitamanas::4963.simple_meaning: Ravana is so proud that he ignores every warning sign. Around him, weapons slip, animals flee, and ominous cries fill the air like death itself is announcing his defeat.
ramacharitamanas::4963.simple_insight: Pride can make danger obvious to everyone except the person trapped inside it.
ramacharitamanas::4963.detailed_meaning: As Ravana rides out to war in Lankakand, the world itself seems to warn him. Weapons slip, soldiers stumble, and wild cries rise around him, but his pride is too swollen to notice. This verse shows the blindness that comes before collapse.
ramacharitamanas::4963.modern_relevance: You ignore the red flags in a project because you are sure your plan cannot fail. By the time the warnings feel loud enough, the damage has already begun.
ramacharitamanas::4963.insight: It shifts attention from external warnings to the inner blindness that refuses them.

ramacharitamanas::4964.verse_sanskrit: ताहि कि संपति सगुन सुभ सपनेहुँ मन बिश्राम। भूत द्रोह रत मोहबस राम बिमुख रति काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::4964.verse_hindi: जो जीवों के द्रोह में रत है, मोह के बस हो रहा है, रामविमुख है और कामासक्त है, उसको क्या कभी स्वप्न में भी सम्पत्ति, शुभ शकुन और चित्त की शांति हो सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::4964.english_translation: Can there ever be wealth, good omens, or peace of mind for one who delights in harming beings, is deluded, turns away from Ram, and is ruled by desire?
ramacharitamanas::4964.translation_literal: ताहि (for that one) / कि (can there be?) / संपति (wealth, prosperity) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सुभ (good) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / मन (mind) / बिश्राम (rest, peace) / भूत (beings) / द्रोह (harm, hostility) / रत (engaged) / मोहबस (under the grip of delusion) / राम बिमुख (turned away from Ram) / रति (attachment, delight) / काम (desire)
ramacharitamanas::4964.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4964.essence: A mind ruled by harm and craving cannot settle into peace.
ramacharitamanas::4964.simple_meaning: A mind filled with harm, delusion, and craving cannot find prosperity, good signs, or even peace in dreams.
ramacharitamanas::4964.simple_insight: What you feed in the mind becomes the atmosphere you live in.
ramacharitamanas::4964.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana's pride is collapsing under bad omens. This couplet explains why: a being ruled by harm, delusion, and desire cannot receive steadiness, even in sleep. The disorder inside has already broken the world around him.
ramacharitamanas::4964.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone after sending a cruel message, hoping for calm. But the mind that feeds on harm never settles, even when the room goes quiet.
ramacharitamanas::4964.insight: It shifts attention from external signs to the moral condition of the mind.

ramacharitamanas::4965.verse_sanskrit: चलेउ निसाचर कटकु अपारा। चतुरंगिनी अनी बहु धारा॥ बिबिधि भाँति बाहन रथ जाना। बिपुल बरन पताक ध्वज नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4965.verse_hindi: राक्षसों की अपार सेना चली। चतुरंगिणी सेना की बहुत सी Uटुकडि़याँ हैं। अनेकों प्रकार के वाहन, रथ और सवारियाँ हैं तथा बहुत से रंगों की अनेकों पताकाएँ और ध्वजाएँ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4965.english_translation: The vast army of demons marched out. It was a fourfold force with many divisions. There were many kinds of vehicles, chariots, and riders, and countless banners and flags of many colors.
ramacharitamanas::4965.translation_literal: चलेउ (marched out) / निसाचर (night-dwellers, demons) / कटकु (army) / अपारा (boundless) । चतुरंगिनी (fourfold) / अनी (army division) / बहु (many) / धारा (streams, divisions) । बिबिधि (various) / भाँति (kinds) / बाहन (vehicles) / रथ (chariots) / जाना (riders) । बिपुल (many) / बरन (colors) / पताक (banners) / ध्वज (flags) / नाना (many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::4965.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4965.essence: Power announces itself before the first blow lands.
ramacharitamanas::4965.simple_meaning: Ravana's huge army moves out in full force, with divisions, vehicles, chariots, riders, banners, and flags.
ramacharitamanas::4965.simple_insight: Sometimes the scale of conflict is the point: everything is mobilized, and nothing is hidden.
ramacharitamanas::4965.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war machine finally rolls forward. Ravana's side sends out its immense, organized force in layers and formations, with every kind of transport and display. The verse builds the visual weight before the fighting begins.
ramacharitamanas::4965.modern_relevance: A convoy of black SUVs, motorcycles, and loud banners blocks the street before a political rally. You can feel the power on display before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::4965.insight: It shifts attention from individual fighters to the full machinery of confrontation.

ramacharitamanas::4966.verse_sanskrit: चले मत्त गज जूथ घनेरे। प्राबिट जलद मरुत जनु प्रेरे॥ बरन बरन बिरदैत निकाया। समर सूर जानहिं बहु माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4966.verse_hindi: मतवाले हाथियों के बहुत से झुंड चले। मानो पवन से प्रेरित हुए वर्षा ऋतु के बादल हों। रंग-बिरंगे बाना धारण करने वाले वीरों के समूह हैं, जो युद्ध में बड़े शूरवीर हैं और बहुत प्रकार की माया जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4966.english_translation: Many groups of maddened elephants marched on, like monsoon clouds driven by the wind. Groups of warriors in many colors advanced, great heroes in battle who knew many kinds of illusion.
ramacharitamanas::4966.translation_literal: चले (marched) / मत्त (maddened) / गज (elephants) / जूथ (herds, groups) / घनेरे (many, dense) / प्राबिट (of the rainy season) / जलद (clouds) / मरुत (wind) / जनु (as if) / प्रेरे (driven, urged) / बरन बरन (many-colored) / बिरदैत (warriors) / निकाया (groups, companies) / समर (battle) / सूर (heroes) / जानहिं (know) / बहु (many) / माया (illusions, tricks)
ramacharitamanas::4966.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4966.essence: The enemy host advances like a storm front.
ramacharitamanas::4966.simple_meaning: The demon army advances in massive, colorful ranks, with elephants and warriors moving like storm clouds. It is a battlefield description, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::4966.simple_insight: Sometimes the scale of conflict itself is the message: overwhelming force, moving in waves.
ramacharitamanas::4966.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is gathering momentum. Ravana's forces surge forward in dense formations, elephants first, then warrior bands in bright armor. Tulsidas lingers on the sheer spectacle of their advance before the fighting begins.
ramacharitamanas::4966.insight: It sets the scene for battle by emphasizing mass, motion, and menace.

ramacharitamanas::4967.verse_sanskrit: अति बिचित्र बाहिनी बिराजी। बीर बसंत सेन जनु साजी॥ चलत कटक दिगसिंधुर डगहीं। छुभित पयोधि कुधर डगमगहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4967.verse_hindi: अत्यंत विचित्र फौज शोभित है। मानो वीर वसंत ने सेना सजाई हो। सेना के चलने से दिशाओं के हाथी डिगने लगे, समुद्र क्षुभित हो गए और पर्वत डगमगाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4967.english_translation: The army looked astonishingly splendid, as if the warrior of spring had assembled it. As the troops moved, even the elephants of the directions shook, the ocean was stirred, and the mountains trembled.
ramacharitamanas::4967.translation_literal: अति (very) / बिचित्र (astonishingly varied) / बाहिनी (army) / बिराजी (shone) / बीर (warrior) / बसंत (spring) / सेन (army) / जनु (as if) / साजी (assembled)॥ / चलत (moving) / कटक (troops) / दिगसिंधुर (elephants of the directions) / डगहीं (shook)॥ / छुभित (stirred) / पयोधि (ocean) / कुधर (mountains) / डगमगहीं (trembled)॥
ramacharitamanas::4967.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4967.essence: A great army can make the whole world feel unstable.
ramacharitamanas::4967.simple_meaning: The army is described as dazzling and immense, with such force that the world itself seems to shake.
ramacharitamanas::4967.simple_insight: Some movements feel so overwhelming they seem to disturb everything around them.
ramacharitamanas::4967.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the massive army of the rākshasas is on the move. Tulsidas lingers on its impossible grandeur: bright, varied, and terrifying. The verse is part of a flowing battlefield description, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::4967.modern_relevance: A crowd pours out of a stadium after the final whistle, loud enough to rattle the streetlights. The scene feels bigger than any one person inside it.
ramacharitamanas::4967.insight: It turns a battle march into a cosmic-scale image of force and momentum.

ramacharitamanas::4968.verse_sanskrit: उठी रेनु रबि गयउ छपाई। मरुत थकित बसुधा अकुलाई॥ पनव निसान घोर रव बाजहिं। प्रलय समय के घन जनु गाजहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4968.verse_hindi: इतनी धूल उड़ी कि सूर्य छिप गए। (फिर सहसा) पवन रुक गया और पृथ्वी अकुला उठी। ढोल और नगाड़े भीषण ध्वनि से बज रहे हैं, जैसे प्रलयकाल के बादल गरज रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4968.english_translation: So much dust rose that the sun was hidden. The wind grew still and the earth seemed to tremble. Drums and kettledrums thundered with a fierce roar, like clouds rumbling at the time of dissolution.
ramacharitamanas::4968.translation_literal: उठी (rose) / रेनु (dust) / रबि (sun) / गयउ (went) / छपाई (hidden) / मरुत (wind) / थकित (weary, still) / बसुधा (earth) / अकुलाई (became restless) / पनव (drums) / निसान (kettledrums) / घोर (fierce) / रव (sound) / बाजहिं (sound) / प्रलय (dissolution) / समय (time) / के (of) / घन (clouds) / जनु (as if) / गाजहिं (thunder)
ramacharitamanas::4968.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4968.essence: The battlefield itself seems to shake under the coming war.
ramacharitamanas::4968.simple_meaning: Dust, silence, and thunderous war-noise fill the battlefield as the armies move like a force of nature.
ramacharitamanas::4968.simple_insight: Some moments are so intense they feel bigger than human effort.
ramacharitamanas::4968.detailed_meaning: As the war in Lanka gathers force, the battlefield becomes overwhelming: dust hides the sun, the wind stills, and the earth seems to writhe. This verse is part of the mounting scene, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::4968.insight: It heightens the battle scene through sound and motion, preparing the reader for the clash ahead.

ramacharitamanas::4969.verse_sanskrit: भेरि नफीरि बाज सहनाई। मारू राग सुभट सुखदाई॥ केहरि नाद बीर सब करहीं। निज निज बल पौरुष उच्चरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4969.verse_hindi: भेरी, नफीरी (तुरही) और शहनाई में योद्धाओं को सुख देने वाला मारू राग बज रहा है। सब वीर सिंहनाद करते हैं और अपने-अपने बल पौरुष का बखान कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4969.english_translation: Drums, trumpets, and shawms sound; the martial Maru melody delights the warriors. All the heroes roar like lions and proclaim their own strength and valor.
ramacharitamanas::4969.translation_literal: भेरि (drum) / नफीरि (trumpet) / बाज (are played) / सहनाई (shawms) / मारू राग (the Maru melody) / सुभट (for brave warriors) / सुखदाई (giving delight)॥ / केहरि (lion) / नाद (roar) / बीर (heroes) / सब (all) / करहीं (do)॥ / निज निज (each one’s own) / बल (strength) / पौरुष (valor) / उच्चरहीं (proclaim)॥
ramacharitamanas::4969.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4969.essence: Battle noise turns courage into a performance.
ramacharitamanas::4969.simple_meaning: The war music swells, and the warriors answer it with lion-like roars and boasts of their strength.
ramacharitamanas::4969.simple_insight: Raw battle energy fills the air before the clash begins.
ramacharitamanas::4969.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, both armies are pressing forward. Drums and trumpets thunder, the warriors roar, and each side stirs itself by declaring its own courage. The scene builds the tension before Ravana speaks.
ramacharitamanas::4969.modern_relevance: The room gets loud before a high-stakes presentation begins: chairs scrape, voices rise, and everyone tries to look fearless. This is that charged moment before impact.
ramacharitamanas::4969.insight: It shifts the mind from inner reflection to the public display of force.

ramacharitamanas::4970.verse_sanskrit: कहइ दसानन सुनहू सुभट्टा। मर्दहु भालु कपिन्ह के ठट्टा॥ हौं मारिहउँ भूप द्वौ भाई। अस कहि सन्मुख फौज रेंगाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4970.verse_hindi: रावण ने कहा- हे उत्तम योद्धाओं! सुनो तुम रीछ-वानरों के ठट्ट को मसल डालो और मैं दोनों राजकुमार भाइयों को मारूँगा। ऐसा कहकर उसने अपनी सेना सामने चलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4970.english_translation: Ravana said, “Hear me, great warriors! Crush the bears and monkeys. I will kill the two royal brothers.” Saying this, he drove his army forward.
ramacharitamanas::4970.translation_literal: कहइ (said) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / सुनहू (listen) / सुभट्टा (great warriors) / मर्दहु (crush) / भालु (bears) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / के ठट्टा (their crowd) / हौं (I) / मारिहउँ (will kill) / भूप (kings) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / सन्मुख (forward-facing) / फौज (army) / रेंगाई (moved forward)
ramacharitamanas::4970.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4970.essence: Pride charges forward, even when ruin is close.
ramacharitamanas::4970.simple_meaning: Ravana orders his warriors to attack the monkey army and says he will kill Ram and Lakshman himself.
ramacharitamanas::4970.simple_insight: Pride speaks like certainty, even when defeat is already near.
ramacharitamanas::4970.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana tries to rally his troops by mocking the monkey army and promising to kill Ram and Lakshman himself. It is a boastful war command, not a teaching verse, and it simply drives the battle forward.
ramacharitamanas::4970.insight: It shows how ego turns fear into bluster and pushes violence ahead of wisdom.

ramacharitamanas::4971.verse_sanskrit: यह सुधि सकल कपिन्ह जब पाई। धाए करि रघुबीर दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::4971.verse_hindi: जब सब वानरों ने यह खबर पाई, तब वे श्री राम की दुहाई देते हुए दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::4971.english_translation: When all the monkeys heard this news, they rushed forward crying out for Raghuvir's help.
ramacharitamanas::4971.translation_literal: यह (this) / सुधि (news, report) / सकल (all) / कपिन्ह (of the monkeys) / जब (when) / पाई (received) / धाए (rushed) / करि (making) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir, Ram) / दोहाई (cry for help, invocation)
ramacharitamanas::4971.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4971.essence: Ram's name turns fear into instant courage.
ramacharitamanas::4971.simple_meaning: When the monkeys heard the news, they rushed into action, calling on Ram's name as they ran.
ramacharitamanas::4971.simple_insight: Fear turns to courage fast when your heart is anchored in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::4971.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana has ordered his forces forward. When the monkey army hears what is happening, they do not hesitate. They surge ahead at once, crying out to Ram as their strength and refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4971.modern_relevance: The group chat lights up with bad news, and you stop overthinking. You call the one person who steadies you and move.
ramacharitamanas::4971.insight: It shows how devotion can turn alarm into immediate, fearless response.

ramacharitamanas::4972.verse_sanskrit: धाए बिसाल कराल मर्कट भालु काल समान ते। मानहुँ सपच्छ उड़ाहिं भूधर बृंद नाना बान ते॥ नख दसन सैल महाद्रुमायुध सबल संक न मानहीं। जय राम रावन मत्त गज मृगराज सुजसु बखानहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::4972.verse_hindi: वे विशाल और काल के समान कराल वानर-भालू दौड़े। मानो पंख वाले पर्वतों के समूह उड़ रहे हों। वे अनेक वर्णों के हैं। नख, दाँत, पर्वत और बड़े-बड़े वृक्ष ही उनके हथियार हैं। वे बड़े बलवान् हैं और किसी का भी डर नहीं मानते। रावण रूपी मतवाले हाथी के लिए सिंह रूप श्री रामजी का जय-जयकार करके वे उनके सुंदर यश का बखान करते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::4972.english_translation: The huge, fierce monkeys and bears rushed forward like death itself. It was as if winged mountains of many kinds were flying through the sky. Their claws, teeth, hills, and great trees were their weapons. Strong and fearless, they roared praise of Ram, the lion against Ravana the drunken elephant, and sang his glorious fame.
ramacharitamanas::4972.translation_literal: धाए (rushed) / बिसाल (huge) / कराल (fierce) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / काल समान (like death) / ते (as) / मानहुँ (as if) / सपच्छ (winged) / उड़ाहिं (fly) / भूधर बृंद (groups of mountains) / नाना बान ते (of many kinds) / नख (claws) / दसन (teeth) / सैल (hills) / महाद्रुमायुध (great trees as weapons) / सबल (strong) / संक (fear) / न मानहीं (do not accept) / जय राम (victory to Ram) / रावन मत्त गज (Ravana, drunken elephant) / मृगराज (lion-king) / सुजसु (glorious fame) / बखानहीं (they proclaim)
ramacharitamanas::4972.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4972.essence: Fearless service moves like a mountain in flight.
ramacharitamanas::4972.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army charges forward fearlessly, using whatever they can as weapons, while praising Ram as they fight.
ramacharitamanas::4972.simple_insight: Courage can be so complete that even fear turns into praise.
ramacharitamanas::4972.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana has ordered his forces forward, and the monkey allies answer at once. Tulsidas paints their charge in vivid motion, but this is still scene-setting: the verse shows the army's ferocity and devotion before the clash begins.
ramacharitamanas::4972.insight: It frames battle as devotion in action, not mere violence or rage.

ramacharitamanas::4973.verse_sanskrit: दुहु दिसि जय जयकार करि निज जोरी जानि। भिरे बीर इत रामहि उत रावनहि बखानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::4973.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर के योद्धा जय-जयकार करके अपनी-अपनी जोड़ी जान (चुन) कर इधर श्री रघुनाथजी का और उधर रावण का बखान करके परस्पर भिड़ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4973.english_translation: On both sides, the warriors shouted victory and chose their own champions. Then they fought, praising Ram on one side and Ravana on the other.
ramacharitamanas::4973.translation_literal: दुहु दिसि (on both sides) / जय जयकार (victory-cries) / करि (doing) / निज जोरी (their own pair/champion) / जानि (knowing, choosing) / भिरे (fought) / बीर (warriors) / इत (here) / रामहि (Ram) / उत (there) / रावनहि (Ravana) / बखानि (praising, describing)
ramacharitamanas::4973.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4973.essence: War begins when praise turns into allegiance.
ramacharitamanas::4973.simple_meaning: The two armies rush into combat, each side cheering for its own champion and praising its own leader.
ramacharitamanas::4973.simple_insight: In battle, loyalty becomes instant and total.
ramacharitamanas::4973.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is in full motion. Warriors on both sides shout and rush forward, each taking up the name of their chosen leader. This is not a teaching verse, just the clash beginning to swell.
ramacharitamanas::4973.modern_relevance: A crowd picks sides before the facts are even clear, and the room fills with noise, certainty, and tribal loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::4973.insight: It shows how quickly conflict turns people into teams, each defending its own banner.

ramacharitamanas::4974.verse_sanskrit: रावनु रथी बिरथ रघुबीरा। देखि बिभीषन भयउ अधीरा॥ अधिक प्रीति मन भा संदेहा। बंदि चरन कह सहित सनेहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4974.verse_hindi: रावण को रथ पर और श्री रघुवीर को बिना रथ के देखकर विभीषण अधीर हो गए। प्रेम अधिक होने से उनके मन में सन्देह हो गया (कि वे बिना रथ के रावण को कैसे जीत सकेंगे)। श्री रामजी के चरणों की वंदना करके वे स्नेह पूर्वक कहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4974.english_translation: Seeing Ravana on a chariot and Raghubir without one, Vibhishana became restless. His love deepened into doubt, so he bowed at Ram's feet and spoke with affection.
ramacharitamanas::4974.translation_literal: रावनु (Ravana) / रथी (chariot-mounted warrior) / बिरथ (without a chariot) / रघुबीरा (Raghu's hero, Ram) / देखि (seeing) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / भयउ (became) / अधीरा (restless)॥ / अधिक (more) / प्रीति (love) / मन (mind) / भा (became) / संदेहा (doubt)॥ / बंदि (bowing) / चरन (feet) / कह (said) / सहित (with) / सनेहा (affection)॥
ramacharitamanas::4974.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4974.essence: Love sees danger first and cannot stay silent.
ramacharitamanas::4974.simple_meaning: Vibhishana sees Ravana armed and Ram unarmed, and his love turns into anxious doubt. He bows to Ram and speaks lovingly.
ramacharitamanas::4974.simple_insight: Love can make you worry for someone you trust, even when faith is still there.
ramacharitamanas::4974.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Vibhishana watches Ravana on a chariot and Ram standing without one. His devotion to Ram is so strong that it becomes anxiety. He bows and speaks up, opening the next exchange about divine protection.
ramacharitamanas::4974.modern_relevance: You watch someone you care about walk into a hard meeting with nothing prepared, while the other side looks fully armed. Your concern rises before your confidence does.
ramacharitamanas::4974.insight: It shows how devotion can sharpen perception and move you to speak honestly when danger feels immediate.

ramacharitamanas::4975.verse_sanskrit: नाथ न रथ नहि तन पद त्राना। केहि बिधि जितब बीर बलवाना॥ सुनहु सखा कह कृपानिधाना। जेहिं जय होइ सो स्यंदन आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4975.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपके न रथ है, न तन की रक्षा करने वाला कवच है और न जूते ही हैं। वह बलवान् वीर रावण किस प्रकार जीता जाएगा? कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने कहा- हे सखे! सुनो, जिससे जय होती है, वह रथ दूसरा ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4975.english_translation: O Lord, you have no chariot, no armor for your body, and no shoes. How can the mighty warrior be conquered? The ocean of compassion Ram said, "Listen, friend: the chariot that brings victory is something else."
ramacharitamanas::4975.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / न रथ (no chariot) / नहि (not) / तन (body) / पद त्राना (foot-protection, shoes) / केहि बिधि (by what means) / जितब (to be won) / बीर बलवाना (mighty warrior) / सुनहु (listen) / सखा (friend) / कह (said) / कृपानिधाना (the ocean of compassion) / जेहिं (by which) / जय (victory) / होइ (happens) / सो (that) / स्यंदन (chariot) / आना (other)
ramacharitamanas::4975.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4975.essence: What wins is not the visible setup, but the inner vehicle.
ramacharitamanas::4975.simple_meaning: Bibhishana worries that Ram has no visible protection or vehicle, but Ram says real victory depends on a different kind of support.
ramacharitamanas::4975.simple_insight: You stop measuring strength by appearances and start looking for the deeper causes of success.
ramacharitamanas::4975.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Bibhishana sees Ram standing without a chariot, armor, or shoes and fears the battle is unwinnable. Ram answers with calm confidence, beginning to teach that victory comes from inner qualities, not outer equipment.
ramacharitamanas::4975.modern_relevance: You walk into a difficult meeting with no title, no backup, and no polished script. The room looks stacked against you, but the thing that changes outcomes is not always what people can see.
ramacharitamanas::4975.insight: It shifts attention from outward support to the inner qualities that actually carry action through.

ramacharitamanas::4976.verse_sanskrit: सौरज धीरज तेहि रथ चाका। सत्य सील दृढ़ ध्वजा पताका॥ बल बिबेक दम परहित घोरे। छमा कृपा समता रजु जोरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4976.verse_hindi: शौर्य और धैर्य उस रथ के पहिए हैं। सत्य और शील (सदाचार) उसकी मजबूत ध्वजा और पताका हैं। बल, विवेक, दम (इंद्रियों का वश में होना) और परोपकार- ये चार उसके घोड़े हैं, जो क्षमा, दया और समता रूपी डोरी से रथ में जोड़े हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4976.english_translation: Sauraj and dhiraj are the wheels of that chariot. Truth and good conduct are its strong banner and pennant. Strength, discernment, self-restraint, and service to others are the horses, yoked by forgiveness, compassion, and evenness.
ramacharitamanas::4976.translation_literal: सौरज (courage) / धीरज (patience) / तेहि (that) / रथ (chariot) / चाका (wheels) / सत्य (truth) / सील (good conduct) / दृढ़ (firm) / ध्वजा (banner) / पताका (pennant) / बल (strength) / बिबेक (discernment) / दम (self-restraint) / परहित (service to others) / घोरे (horses) / छमा (forgiveness) / कृपा (compassion) / समता (evenness) / रजु (reins) / जोरे (yoked)
ramacharitamanas::4976.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::4976.essence: Your real chariot is built from character, not equipment.
ramacharitamanas::4976.simple_meaning: A well-lived life needs courage, patience, truth, good conduct, self-restraint, discernment, and service, all held together by forgiveness, compassion, and balance.
ramacharitamanas::4976.simple_insight: Real strength is not raw force. It becomes useful only when guided by character and steadied by compassion.
ramacharitamanas::4976.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Vibhishana worries that Ram has no visible war chariot. The reply turns the image inward: the real chariot is made of character, not wood. This verse names the qualities that let a person face life without fear.
ramacharitamanas::4976.modern_relevance: You are about to walk into a hard conversation with your boss, your partner, or your child. What carries you through is not just confidence, but the steadiness, truth, and self-control you bring with you.
ramacharitamanas::4976.insight: It shifts the mind from outer support to inner formation.

ramacharitamanas::4977.verse_sanskrit: ईस भजनु सारथी सुजाना। बिरति चर्म संतोष कृपाना॥ दान परसु बुधि सक्ति प्रचंडा। बर बिग्यान कठिन कोदंडा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4977.verse_hindi: ईश्वर का भजन ही (उस रथ को चलाने वाला) चतुर सारथी है। वैराग्य ढाल है और संतोष तलवार है। दान फरसा है, बुद्धि प्रचण्ड शक्ति है, श्रेष्ठ विज्ञान कठिन धनुष है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4977.english_translation: Devotion to the divine is the skilled charioteer. Non-attachment is the shield, and contentment the sword. Generosity is the axe, discerning wisdom the fierce power, and true understanding the hard bow.
ramacharitamanas::4977.translation_literal: ईस (of the divine) / भजनु (devotion) / सारथी (charioteer) / सुजाना (skillful) । / बिरति (non-attachment) / चर्म (shield) / संतोष (contentment) / कृपाना (sword) । / दान (giving) / परसु (axe) / बुधि (discerning wisdom) / सक्ति (power) / प्रचंडा (fierce) । / बर (excellent) / बिग्यान (true understanding) / कठिन (hard) / कोदंडा (bow) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4977.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4977.essence: The real chariot of victory is built from inner qualities, not outer force.
ramacharitamanas::4977.simple_meaning: Inner victory comes from devotion, non-attachment, contentment, generosity, wisdom, and true understanding. These qualities are the real equipment for facing hard struggles.
ramacharitamanas::4977.simple_insight: You do not win by force alone. Your deepest strength comes from how you live inside.
ramacharitamanas::4977.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war, Ram explains that victory is not won by weapons alone. He turns the body into a chariot and names the inner qualities that must carry it: devotion, non-attachment, contentment, generosity, discernment, and understanding.
ramacharitamanas::4977.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting with your jaw tight, your phone buzzing, and your chest already braced for attack. What steadies you is not more noise — it is devotion, restraint, and a mind that can see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::4977.insight: It shifts the idea of strength from outer power to inner equipment.

ramacharitamanas::4978.verse_sanskrit: अमल अचल मन त्रोन समाना। सम जम नियम सिलीमुख नाना॥ कवच अभेद बिप्र गुर पूजा। एहि सम बिजय उपाय न दूजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4978.verse_hindi: निर्मल (पापरहित) और अचल (स्थिर) मन तरकस के समान है। शम (मन का वश में होना), (अहिंसादि) यम और (शौचादि) नियम- ये बहुत से बाण हैं। ब्राह्मणों और गुरु का पूजन अभेद्य कवच है। इसके समान विजय का दूसरा उपाय नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4978.english_translation: A pure, steady mind is the quiver. Restraint, discipline, and rules are many arrows. Worship of Brahmins and the teacher is an impenetrable armor. There is no other way to victory.
ramacharitamanas::4978.translation_literal: अमल (pure) / अचल (steady) / मन (mind) / त्रोन (quiver) / समाना (is like) / सत्य (restraint) / जम (self-control) / नियम (disciplines) / सिलीमुख (arrows) / नाना (many) / कवच (armor) / अभेद (unbreakable) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / गुर (teacher) / पूजा (worship) / एहि (this) / सम (like) / बिजय (victory) / उपाय (means) / न (not) / दूजा (other)
ramacharitamanas::4978.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4978.essence: Victory comes from a trained mind and disciplined character.
ramacharitamanas::4978.simple_meaning: A calm, steady mind becomes your base. Self-control, discipline, and respect for teachers protect you and help you succeed.
ramacharitamanas::4978.simple_insight: Real strength comes from inner order, not force alone.
ramacharitamanas::4978.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Krishna's battlefield teaching to Arjuna, Tulsidas turns the chariot into a symbol of inner victory. A pure mind, disciplined senses, and reverence for the wise are not extras here — they are the equipment that makes success possible.
ramacharitamanas::4978.modern_relevance: Before a hard exam, a difficult conversation, or a messy family decision, you can feel your mind scatter. This verse says victory begins when your attention is steady and your character is trained.
ramacharitamanas::4978.insight: It shifts the focus from raw effort to inner preparation, where discipline makes action effective.

ramacharitamanas::4979.verse_sanskrit: सखा धर्ममय अस रथ जाकें। जीतन कहँ न कतहुँ रिपु ताकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::4979.verse_hindi: हे सखे! ऐसा धर्ममय रथ जिसके हो उसके लिए जीतने को कहीं शत्रु ही नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::4979.english_translation: O friend, for the one who has such a righteous chariot, there is no enemy left to conquer.
ramacharitamanas::4979.translation_literal: सखा (friend) / धर्ममय (made of righteousness) / अस (such) / रथ (chariot) / जाकें (for whom) / जीतन (to conquer) / कहँ (for) / न (not) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / रिपु (enemy) / ताकें (for that one)
ramacharitamanas::4979.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::4979.essence: A life ordered by dharma cannot be truly defeated.
ramacharitamanas::4979.simple_meaning: A life built on righteousness leaves nothing truly able to defeat you. The real victory comes from having the right inner structure, not from fighting harder.
ramacharitamanas::4979.simple_insight: You can stop chasing outer wins when your inner life is aligned.
ramacharitamanas::4979.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Ram explains to Sugriva that the true chariot of victory is not made of wood and weapons. It is built from devotion, restraint, generosity, wisdom, and discipline. With that foundation, even the fiercest enemy cannot truly win.
ramacharitamanas::4979.modern_relevance: You walk into a difficult meeting already shaken, but your preparation, values, and calm are in place. The room still matters, but it no longer controls you.
ramacharitamanas::4979.insight: It shifts victory from external struggle to inner alignment with dharma.

ramacharitamanas::4980.verse_sanskrit: महा अजय संसार रिपु जीति सकइ सो बीर। जाकें अस रथ होइ दृढ़ सुनहु सखा मतिधीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::4980.verse_hindi: हे धीरबुद्धि वाले सखा! सुनो, जिसके पास ऐसा दृढ़ रथ हो, वह वीर संसार (जन्म-मृत्यु) रूपी महान् दुर्जय शत्रु को भी जीत सकता है (रावण की तो बात ही क्या है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4980.english_translation: O steadfast-minded friend, listen: the hero who has such a firm chariot can conquer the great, hard-to-defeat enemy called the cycle of birth and death.
ramacharitamanas::4980.translation_literal: महा (great) / अजय (unconquerable) / संसार (world-cycle) / रिपु (enemy) / जीति (having conquered) / सकइ (can) / सो (that) / बीर (hero) / जाकें (whose) / अस (such) / रथ (chariot) / होइ (is) / दृढ़ (firm) / सुनहु (listen) / सखा (friend) / मतिधीर (steadfast-minded)
ramacharitamanas::4980.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::4980.essence: A firm inner foundation can defeat the hardest enemy.
ramacharitamanas::4980.simple_meaning: A person with a strong, disciplined inner foundation can defeat even the greatest enemy of repeated birth and death.
ramacharitamanas::4980.simple_insight: Strength is not just force; it is having an unshaken inner structure that can face anything.
ramacharitamanas::4980.detailed_meaning: Before the final victory, Ram teaches the war's secret to Vibhishana: the true chariot is made of discipline, restraint, and steady conduct. With that foundation, even the vast enemy of the cycle of reactivity can be overcome.
ramacharitamanas::4980.modern_relevance: You are about to send a message that could start a fight, but you pause, breathe, and choose your words carefully. That inner steadiness is the real weapon.
ramacharitamanas::4980.insight: It shifts the focus from outer power to the disciplined inner structure that makes victory possible.

ramacharitamanas::4981.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन बिभीषन हरषि गहे पद कंज। एहि मिस मोहि उपदेसेहु राम कृपा सुख पुंज॥80 ख
ramacharitamanas::4981.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर विभीषणजी ने हर्षित होकर उनके चरण कमल पकड़ लिए (और कहा-) हे कृपा और सुख के समूह श्री रामजी! आपने इसी बहाने मुझे (महान् ) उपदेश दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4981.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, Vibhishana rejoiced and clasped the lotus feet, saying, 'O Ram, treasure of mercy and joy, you have taught me through this very moment.'
ramacharitamanas::4981.translation_literal: सुनि (having heard) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / बचन (words) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / हरषि (rejoicing) / गहे (grasped) / पद कंज (lotus feet) / एहि मिस (through this means) / मोहि (to me) / उपदेसेहु (you taught) / राम (Ram) / कृपा सुख पुंज (a mass of mercy and joy)
ramacharitamanas::4981.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::4981.essence: Ram's mercy teaches the surrendered heart without formal instruction.
ramacharitamanas::4981.simple_meaning: Vibhishana feels joy on hearing Ram and bows at his feet, saying Ram's mercy itself has taught him something important.
ramacharitamanas::4981.simple_insight: Real teaching can arrive as kindness, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::4981.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Vibhishana has surrendered to Ram, he hears Ram speak and immediately bows in joy. He recognises that Ram's mercy itself has become his teaching, confirming that surrender has already transformed him.
ramacharitamanas::4981.modern_relevance: You finally hear the calm reply after a painful conversation, and something in you softens. Sometimes the lesson is not the answer — it's the kindness behind it.
ramacharitamanas::4981.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding explanation to recognising grace as guidance.

ramacharitamanas::4982.verse_sanskrit: उत पचार दसकंधर इत अंगद हनुमान। लरत निसाचर भालु कपि करि निज निज प्रभु आन ॥
ramacharitamanas::4982.verse_hindi: उधर से रावण ललकार रहा है और इधर से अंगद और हनुमान् । राक्षस और रीछ-वानर अपने-अपने स्वामी की दुहाई देकर लड़ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4982.english_translation: Ravana roars from one side, Angada and Hanuman from the other. Demons, bears, and monkeys fight, each calling on their own lord.
ramacharitamanas::4982.translation_literal: उत (on that side) / पचार (shouting challenge) / दसकंधर (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / इत (on this side) / अंगद (Angada) / हनुमान (Hanuman) / लरत (fighting) / निसाचर (night-dwellers, demons) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / करि (doing) / निज निज (each one's own) / प्रभु (lord) / आन (calling out)
ramacharitamanas::4982.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4982.essence: War becomes a contest of loyalties, not just weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4982.simple_meaning: The battle is split between two sides, with each army fighting under its own leader.
ramacharitamanas::4982.simple_insight: Some conflicts are not about logic anymore; they become pure loyalty and force.
ramacharitamanas::4982.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka has fully erupted. Ravana shouts from one side while Angada and Hanuman answer from the other. Demons, bears, and monkeys clash across the field, each fighting in the name of its own master.
ramacharitamanas::4982.modern_relevance: A crowd argument breaks out at a family gathering, and suddenly everyone is speaking for their side, not for the truth. This verse shows how conflict can turn into tribal allegiance.
ramacharitamanas::4982.insight: It shifts attention from individual fighters to the larger loyalties driving the battle.

ramacharitamanas::4983.verse_sanskrit: सुर ब्रह्मादि सिद्ध मुनि नाना। देखत रन नभ चढ़े बिमाना॥ हमहू उमा रहे तेहिं संगा। देखत राम चरित रन रंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4983.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा आदि देवता और अनेकों सिद्ध तथा मुनि विमानों पर चढ़े हुए आकाश से युद्ध देख रहे हैं। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! मैं भी उस समाज में था और श्री रामजी के रण-रंग (रणोत्साह) की लीला देख रहा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::4983.english_translation: The gods, Brahma, the perfected beings, and many sages rose into the sky in flying chariots to watch the battle. Shiva says to Uma, "I was there too, watching Ram's war-play."
ramacharitamanas::4983.translation_literal: सुर (gods) / ब्रह्मादि (Brahma and others) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनि (sages) / नाना (many) / देखत (watching) / रन (battle) / नभ (sky) / चढ़े (rose up) / बिमाना (flying chariots)॥ / हमहू (I too) / उमा (Uma) / रहे (was) / तेहिं (there) / संगा (with) / देखत (watching) / राम (Ram) / चरित (deeds) / रन (battle) / रंगा (play)
ramacharitamanas::4983.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::4983.essence: Heaven itself pauses to watch Ram's battle.
ramacharitamanas::4983.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings and sages are watching the battle from above, and Shiva tells Uma that he was there too, witnessing Ram's battle-play.
ramacharitamanas::4983.simple_insight: Great events can become a sacred spectacle when seen with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::4983.detailed_meaning: As the war in Lanka intensifies, even the celestial beings and sages rise into the sky to watch. Shiva, speaking to Uma in the outer frame, says he was among them, witnessing Ram's battle as a divine play. It is a scene-setting verse, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4983.modern_relevance: A crowd gathers on a rooftop to watch a final match under floodlights. The moment feels larger than the people in it, but the verse is only setting the scene.
ramacharitamanas::4983.insight: It places the reader inside the war's sacred atmosphere before the next clash begins.

ramacharitamanas::4984.verse_sanskrit: सुभट समर रस दुहु दिसि माते। कपि जयसील राम बल ताते॥ एक एक सन भिरहिं पचारहिं। एकन्ह एक मर्दि महि पारहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4984.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर के योद्धा रण रस में मतवाले हो रहे हैं। वानरों को श्री रामजी का बल है, इससे वे जयशील हैं (जीत रहे हैं)। एक-दूसरे से भिड़ते और ललकारते हैं और एक-दूसरे को मसल-मसलकर पृथ्वी पर डाल देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4984.english_translation: The brave warriors on both sides are drunk with the thrill of battle. The monkeys have Ram's strength, so they keep winning. They clash, challenge each other, and crush one another to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::4984.translation_literal: सुभट (brave warriors) / समर (battle) / रस (taste, thrill) / दुहु दिसि (on both sides) / माते (intoxicated) / कपि (monkeys) / जयसील (victorious by nature) / राम (Ram) / बल (strength) / ताते (because of that) / एक एक सन (with each one) / भिरहिं (they clash) / पचारहिं (they challenge) / एकन्ह (some) / एक (others) / मर्दि (crushing) / महि (earth) / पारहिं (they throw down)
ramacharitamanas::4984.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4984.essence: Battle becomes a force that sweeps everyone into motion.
ramacharitamanas::4984.simple_meaning: Both armies are fully caught up in fierce combat, and Ram's side keeps gaining the upper hand.
ramacharitamanas::4984.simple_insight: Some moments are pure force and momentum, with no room for hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4984.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, the battle has become a frenzy. Warriors on both sides are locked in close combat, but the monkey army fights with Ram's power behind it and keeps pressing forward. This is a vivid slice of the larger battle scene.
ramacharitamanas::4984.modern_relevance: In a crowded sports arena, bodies surge, shouts rise, and every move becomes instinct. This verse captures that raw momentum before anyone has time to think.
ramacharitamanas::4984.insight: It shows battle as total immersion, where strength, challenge, and resistance all hit at once.

ramacharitamanas::4985.verse_sanskrit: मारहिं काटहिं धरहिं पछारहिं। सीस तोरि सीसन्ह सन मारहिं॥ उदर बिदारहिं भुजा उपारहिं। गहि पद अवनि पटकि भट डारहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4985.verse_hindi: वे मारते, काटते, पकड़ते और पछाड़ देते हैं और सिर तोड़कर उन्हीं सिरों से दूसरों को मारते हैं। पेट फाड़ते हैं, भुजाएँ उखाड़ते हैं और योद्धाओं को पैर पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर पटक देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4985.english_translation: They strike, cut, seize, and throw down. They break heads and use those very heads to strike again. They tear open bellies, rip up arms, and grab warriors by the feet to slam them to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::4985.translation_literal: मारहिं (they strike) / काटहिं (they cut) / धरहिं (they seize) / पछारहिं (they throw down) / सीस (head) / तोरि (breaking) / सीसन्ह (with heads) / सन (with) / मारहिं (they strike) / उदर (belly) / बिदारहिं (they tear open) / भुजा (arms) / उपारहिं (they rip up) / गहि (grabbing) / पद (feet) / अवनि (ground) / पटकि (slamming) / भट (warriors) / डारहिं (they throw)
ramacharitamanas::4985.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4985.essence: The battle has turned into savage, unbroken violence.
ramacharitamanas::4985.simple_meaning: The battle is brutal and chaotic, with fighters killing and maiming each other in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::4985.simple_insight: Violence, once unleashed, becomes raw and unrestrained.
ramacharitamanas::4985.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is raging at full force. Monkeys and demon warriors are locked in savage hand-to-hand combat, with no pause or mercy. This verse is not teaching a principle; it intensifies the battlefield scene.
ramacharitamanas::4985.insight: It shows the war reaching a ferocious, uncontrolled level of close combat.

ramacharitamanas::4986.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर भट महि गाड़हिं भालू। ऊपर ढारि देहिं बहु बालू॥ बीर बलीमुख जुद्ध बिरुद्धे। देखिअत बिपुल काल जनु क्रुद्धे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4986.verse_hindi: राक्षस योद्धाओं को भालू पृथ्वी में गाड़ देते हैं और ऊपर से बहुत सी बालू डाल देते हैं। युद्ध में शत्रुओं से विरुद्ध हुए वीर वानर ऐसे दिखाई पड़ते हैं मानो बहुत से क्रोधित काल हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4986.english_translation: The bear-warriors bury the demon fighters in the ground and cover them with heaps of sand. The brave monkey warriors, fierce in battle, look like many enraged forms of death.
ramacharitamanas::4986.translation_literal: निसिचर (demon fighters) / भट (warriors) / महि (in the earth) / गाड़हिं (bury) / भालू (bear-warriors) / ऊपर (on top) / ढारि (pouring) / देहिं (give, place) / बहु (much, many) / बालू (sand) / बीर (brave) / बलीमुख (strong-faced, mighty-faced) / जुद्ध (battle) / बिरुद्धे (opposed) / देखिअत (are seen) / बिपुल (many, abundant) / काल (death) / जनु (as if) / क्रुद्धे (enraged)
ramacharitamanas::4986.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4986.essence: Battle has become a storm of relentless destruction.
ramacharitamanas::4986.simple_meaning: The battle is so fierce that bears bury enemies in the earth while monkey warriors look like many raging figures of death.
ramacharitamanas::4986.simple_insight: Some conflicts are so intense that everyone in them seems transformed by force and fury.
ramacharitamanas::4986.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is already raging. Bears and monkey warriors are tearing through the demon army with brutal force, burying enemies and flinging sand over them. The scene is not teaching doctrine; it is intensifying the battlefield chaos.
ramacharitamanas::4986.insight: It keeps the focus on the sheer violence of the clash, not on strategy or reflection.

ramacharitamanas::4987.verse_sanskrit: क्रुद्धे कृतांत समान कपि तन स्रवत सोनित राजहीं। मर्दहिं निसाचर कटक भट बलवंत घन जिमि गाजहीं॥ मारहिं चपेटन्हि डाटि दातन्ह काटि लातन्ह मीजहीं। चिक्करहिं मर्कट भालु छल बल करहिं जेहिं खल छीजहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::4987.verse_hindi: क्रोधित हुए काल के समान वे वानर खून बहते हुए शरीरों से शोभित हो रहे हैं। वे बलवान् वीर राक्षसों की सेना के योद्धाओं को मसलते और मेघ की तरह गरजते हैं। डाँटकर चपेटों से मारते, दाँतों से काटकर लातों से पीस डालते हैं। वानर-भालू चिग्घाड़ते और ऐसा छल-बल करते हैं, जिससे दुष्ट राक्षस नष्ट हो जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4987.english_translation: Angry like death itself, the monkeys’ bodies shine with blood. They crush the strong demon troops and roar like thunderclouds. They strike with slaps, bites, and kicks, and the monkeys and bears shout so that the wicked are destroyed by force and trickery.
ramacharitamanas::4987.translation_literal: क्रुद्धे (angry) / कृतांत (death) / समान (like) / कपि (monkeys) / तन (bodies) / स्रवत (flowing) / सोनित (blood) / राजहीं (shine) / मर्दहिं (they crush) / निसाचर (demon) / कटक (troops) / भट (warriors) / बलवंत (strong) / घन (clouds) / जिमि (like) / गाजहीं (they roar) / मारहिं (they strike) / चपेटन्हि (with slaps) / डाटि (with bites) / दातन्ह (with teeth) / काटि (cutting) / लातन्ह (with kicks) / मीजहीं (they grind) / चिक्करहिं (they shout) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / छल (trickery) / बल (force) / करहिं (they do) / जेहिं (by which) / खल (wicked) / छीजहीं (are destroyed)
ramacharitamanas::4987.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4987.essence: The battle surges with savage, unstoppable force.
ramacharitamanas::4987.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear warriors fight with fierce, overwhelming force, crushing the demon army in brutal close combat.
ramacharitamanas::4987.simple_insight: Sometimes survival means meeting violence with total courage and no hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4987.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the monkey and bear forces are in the thick of the war. Their bodies are bloodied, their cries thunderous, and they tear into Ravana’s troops with raw ferocity. This verse is part of a rapid battle sequence, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4987.insight: It intensifies the war scene rather than offering a separate lesson.

ramacharitamanas::4988.verse_sanskrit: धरि गाल फारहिं उर बिदारहिं गल अँतावरि मेलहीं। प्रह्लादपति जनु बिबिध तनु धरि समर अंगन खेलहीं॥ धरु मारु काटु पछारु घोर गिरा गगन महि भरि रही। जय राम जो तृन ते कुलिस कर कुलिस ते कर तृन सही ॥
ramacharitamanas::4988.verse_hindi: वे राक्षसों के गाल पकड़कर फाड़ डालते हैं, छाती चीर डालते हैं और उनकी अँतड़ियाँ निकालकर गले में डाल लेते हैं। वे वानर ऐसे दिख पड़ते हैं मानो प्रह्लाद के स्वामी श्री नृसिंह भगवान् अनेकों शरीर धारण करके युद्ध के मैदान में क्रीड़ा कर रहे हों। पकड़ो, मारो, काटो, पछाड़ो आदि घोर शब्द आकाश और पृथ्वी में भर (छा) गए हैं। श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो, जो सचमुच तृण से वज्र और वज्र से तृण कर देते हैं (निर्बल को सबल और सबल को निर्बल कर देते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4988.english_translation: They seize the demons by the cheeks, tear open their chests, and stuff their entrails into their throats. The monkeys seem like Lord Narasimha, the protector of Prahlad, playing on the battlefield in many forms. "Seize! Kill! Cut! Throw down!" — fierce cries fill the sky and earth. Victory to Ram, who turns straw into thunderbolt and thunderbolt into straw.
ramacharitamanas::4988.translation_literal: धरि (seizing) / गाल (cheeks) / फारहिं (tear) / उर (chest) / बिदारहिं (split open) / गल (throat) / अँतावरि (entrails) / मेलहीं (place) / प्रह्लादपति (Lord of Prahlad) / जनु (as if) / बिबिध (many) / तनु (forms) / धरि (taking) / समर (battle) / अंगन (field) / खेलहीं (play) / धरु (seize) / मारु (kill) / काटु (cut) / पछारु (throw down) / घोर (fierce) / गिरा (cries) / गगन (sky) / महि (earth) / भरि (filled) / रही (remained) / जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / जो (who) / तृन (straw) / ते (from) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कर (make) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / ते (from) / कर (make) / तृन (straw) / सही (indeed)
ramacharitamanas::4988.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4988.essence: Ram can turn weakness into force and force into weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4988.simple_meaning: The battlefield has become so intense that the monkeys seem like fierce divine forms at play. Ram's power makes the weak strong and the strong weak.
ramacharitamanas::4988.simple_insight: Even overwhelming force is still held inside a greater power.
ramacharitamanas::4988.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army is driving the demons back with terrifying force. Tulsidas heightens the scene by comparing them to Narasimha himself and ends by praising Ram, whose power reverses all strength and weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4988.modern_relevance: A situation turns brutal fast: voices rise, tempers snap, and everyone feels the room tilt. In that moment, the verse reminds you that power is never finally yours to control.
ramacharitamanas::4988.insight: It shifts attention from battlefield fury to Ram's hidden sovereignty over strength itself.

ramacharitamanas::4989.verse_sanskrit: निज दल बिचलत देखेसि बीस भुजाँ दस चाप। रथ चढ़ि चलेउ दसानन फिरहु फिरहु करि दाप ॥
ramacharitamanas::4989.verse_hindi: अपनी सेना को विचलित होते हुए देखा, तब बीस भुजाओं में दस धनुष लेकर रावण रथ पर चढ़कर गर्व करके 'लौटो, लौटो' कहता हुआ चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4989.english_translation: Seeing his army wavering, Ravana mounted his chariot with ten bows in his twenty arms and cried, "Turn back, turn back!" in pride.
ramacharitamanas::4989.translation_literal: निज (own) / दल (army) / बिचलत (wavering) / देखेसि (he saw) / बीस (twenty) / भुजाँ (arms) / दस (ten) / चाप (bows) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ि (having mounted) / चलेउ (he went) / दसानन (ten-faced one, Ravana) / फिरहु (turn back) / फिरहु (turn back) / करि (doing) / दाप (pride)
ramacharitamanas::4989.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4989.essence: Ego shouts hardest when it senses weakness.
ramacharitamanas::4989.simple_meaning: Ravana sees his army faltering, climbs onto his chariot, and shouts in pride for the enemy to turn back.
ramacharitamanas::4989.simple_insight: Pride often gets louder right when control is slipping.
ramacharitamanas::4989.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana notices his forces wavering. Loaded with bows and mounted on his chariot, he tries to steady them through sheer arrogance. The verse is a scene-setting move before the fighting surges again.
ramacharitamanas::4989.modern_relevance: You spot the room going quiet after your mistake, and you try to cover it with volume. The louder you get, the more everyone sees the fear underneath.
ramacharitamanas::4989.insight: It shows how ego reacts when power begins to slip.

ramacharitamanas::4990.verse_sanskrit: धायउ परम क्रुद्ध दसकंधर। सन्मुख चले हूह दै बंदर॥ गहि कर पादप उपल पहारा। डारेन्हि ता पर एकहिं बारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4990.verse_hindi: रावण अत्यंत क्रोधित होकर दौड़ा। वानर हुँकार करते हुए (लड़ने के लिए) उसके सामने चले। उन्होंने हाथों में वृक्ष, पत्थर और पहाड़ लेकर रावण पर एक ही साथ डाले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4990.english_translation: Ravana, furious beyond measure, charged forward. The monkeys advanced toward him with loud cries. They seized trees, stones, and mountains and hurled them all at once.
ramacharitamanas::4990.translation_literal: धायउ (charged) / परम (extremely) / क्रुद्ध (angry) / दसकंधर (Ravana) । / सन्मुख (facing forward) / चले (moved) / हूह दै (shouting) / बंदर (monkeys) ॥ / गहि (seizing) / कर (hands) / पादप (trees) / उपल (stones) / पहारा (struck/ hurled) । / डारेन्हि (they threw) / ता पर (upon him) / एकहिं बारा (all at once) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4990.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4990.essence: Battle surges forward in a storm of fury and flying mountains.
ramacharitamanas::4990.simple_meaning: Ravana rushes into battle, and the monkeys meet him by hurling trees, stones, and mountains together.
ramacharitamanas::4990.simple_insight: When rage meets force, the scene becomes pure collision.
ramacharitamanas::4990.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's battlefield, Ravana charges in fury while the monkey army answers with a roar. They tear up trees, stones, and even mountains, throwing them together in a wild surge of war. The verse is a combat snapshot, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4990.insight: It keeps the focus on the raw momentum of battle rather than any inner lesson.

ramacharitamanas::4991.verse_sanskrit: लागहिं सैल बज्र तन तासू। खंड खंड होइ फूटहिं आसू॥ चला न अचल रहा रथ रोपी। रन दुर्मद रावन अति कोपी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4991.verse_hindi: पर्वत उसके वज्रतुल्य शरीर में लगते ही तुरंत टुकड़े-टुकड़े होकर फूट जाते हैं। अत्यंत क्रोधी रणोन्मत्त रावण रथ रोककर अचल खड़ा रहा, (अपने स्थान से) जरा भी नहीं हिला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4991.english_translation: Mountains strike his body like thunderbolts and shatter at once. Furious in battle, Ravana stopped his chariot and stood unmoving, not shifting even a little.
ramacharitamanas::4991.translation_literal: लागहिं (strike) / सैल (mountains) / बज्र (thunderbolt) / तन (body) / तासू (his) / खंड खंड (into pieces) / होइ (become) / फूटहिं (burst) / आसू (at once)॥ / चला (moved) / न (not) / अचल (immovable) / रहा (remained) / रथ (chariot) / रोपी (stopped) / रन (battle) / दुर्मद (intoxicated with pride) / रावन (Ravana) / अति (very) / कोपी (furious) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4991.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4991.essence: Pride can stand unmoved even under overwhelming attack.
ramacharitamanas::4991.simple_meaning: Mountains hit Ravana's body and break apart. He stands unmoved in his chariot, burning with rage.
ramacharitamanas::4991.simple_insight: Raw force alone does not stop pride; it can only harden it.
ramacharitamanas::4991.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, the monkey warriors are hurling mountains and rocks at Ravana. His body seems unbreakable, and his rage only deepens. This verse simply shows his terrifying resistance before the fighting surges on.
ramacharitamanas::4991.modern_relevance: A room full of criticism lands on someone who refuses to bend. They don't soften; they only get more rigid, more defensive, more dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::4991.insight: It shows how ego can turn pain into hardness instead of learning.

ramacharitamanas::4992.verse_sanskrit: इत उत झपटि दपटि कपि जोधा। मर्दै लाग भयउ अति क्रोधा॥ चले पराइ भालु कपि नाना। त्राहि त्राहि अंगद हनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::4992.verse_hindi: उसे बहुत ही क्रोध हुआ। वह इधर-उधर झपटकर और डपटकर वानर योद्धाओं को मसलने लगा। अनेकों वानर-भालू 'हे अंगद! हे हनुमान् ! रक्षा करो, रक्षा करो' (पुकारते हुए) भाग चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4992.english_translation: He grew furious. Leaping here and there, he struck and crushed the monkey warriors. Many monkeys and bears ran away crying, 'Protect us, Angad! Protect us, Hanuman!'
ramacharitamanas::4992.translation_literal: इत उत (here and there) / झपटि (leaping) / दपटि (thrusting, striking) / कपि जोधा (monkey warriors) / मर्दै (crushing) / लाग (began) / भयउ (became) / अति क्रोधा (extremely angry) / चले (ran) / पराइ (fleeing) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / नाना (many kinds) / त्राहि त्राहि (save us, save us) / अंगद (Angad) / हनुमाना (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::4992.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4992.essence: Blind fury can drive even brave hearts into flight.
ramacharitamanas::4992.simple_meaning: Ravana attacks wildly, and the monkey and bear fighters panic and flee, calling for Angad and Hanuman to protect them.
ramacharitamanas::4992.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast when strength turns brutal and uncontrolled.
ramacharitamanas::4992.detailed_meaning: On the Lanka battlefield, Ravana’s rage surges through the monkey ranks. He lunges everywhere, crushing fighters with brute force. The monkeys and bears lose their footing and cry out for Angad and Hanuman as they scatter.
ramacharitamanas::4992.modern_relevance: A room full of people goes silent when one person explodes in anger. The force may look powerful, but it also makes everyone else retreat.
ramacharitamanas::4992.insight: It shows how raw aggression can scatter courage and expose the need for steadier protectors.

ramacharitamanas::4993.verse_sanskrit: पाहि पाहि रघुबीर गोसाईं। यह खल खाइ काल की नाईं॥ तेहिं देखे कपि सकल पराने। दसहुँ चाप सायक संधाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::4993.verse_hindi: हे रघुवीर! हे गोसाईं! रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए। यह दुष्ट काल की भाँति हमें खा रहा है। उसने देखा कि सब वानर भाग छूटे, तब (रावण ने) दसों धनुषों पर बाण संधान किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::4993.english_translation: “Protect us, protect us, O Raghubir, O Lord. This villain is devouring us like death itself.” Seeing the monkeys flee, Ravana then strung all ten bows and drew his arrows.
ramacharitamanas::4993.translation_literal: पाहि (protect) / पाहि (protect) / रघुबीर (Lord of the Raghu clan) / गोसाईं (Lord) / यह (this) / खल (villain) / खाइ (eats/devours) / काल (death) / की नाईं (like)॥ तेहिं (then/he) / देखे (seeing) / कपि (monkeys) / सकल (all) / पराने (ran away) / दसहुँ (all ten) / चाप (bows) / सायक (arrows) / संधाने (strung/drew) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4993.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4993.essence: Fear calls for refuge when force becomes overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::4993.simple_meaning: The monkeys cry out to Ram for protection as Ravana overwhelms them and prepares another fierce arrow attack.
ramacharitamanas::4993.simple_insight: When pressure becomes too much, the heart reaches for help before it reaches for strategy.
ramacharitamanas::4993.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana has driven the monkey warriors back. They cry out to Ram for rescue, calling Ravana a death-like force. Seeing their retreat, Ravana tightens every bow and readies more arrows, deepening the crisis.
ramacharitamanas::4993.modern_relevance: You’re in the middle of a group project, messages are failing, and one person is bulldozing everyone else. Panic rises first; clear help comes next.
ramacharitamanas::4993.insight: It shows the moment fear turns into a cry for protection, just before the next assault begins.

ramacharitamanas::4994.verse_sanskrit: संधानि धनु सर निकर छाड़ेसि उरग जिमि उड़ि लागहीं। रहे पूरि सर धरनी गगन दिसि बिदिसि कहँ कपि भागहीं॥ भयो अति कोलाहल बिकल कपि दल भालु बोलहिं आतुरे। रघुबीर करुना सिंधु आरत बंधु जन रच्छक हरे॥
ramacharitamanas::4994.verse_hindi: उसने धनुष पर सन्धान करके बाणों के समूह छोड़े। वे बाण सर्प की तरह उड़कर जा लगते थे। पृथ्वी-आकाश और दिशा-विदिशा सर्वत्र बाण भर रहे हैं। वानर भागें तो कहाँ? अत्यंत कोलाहल मच गया। वानर-भालुओं की सेना व्याकुल होकर आर्त्त पुकार करने लगी- हे रघुवीर! हे करुणासागर! हे पीड़ितों के बन्धु! हे सेवकों की रक्षा करके उनके दुःख हरने वाले हरि!
ramacharitamanas::4994.english_translation: Having fitted his bow, he loosed a shower of arrows. They flew like serpents and struck everywhere. Earth, sky, and all directions were filled with arrows. Where could the monkeys run? A terrible uproar rose as the monkey and bear army, shaken and desperate, cried out, "O Raghubir, ocean of compassion, friend of the distressed, protector who removes the suffering of your servants!"
ramacharitamanas::4994.translation_literal: संधानि (having fitted) / धनु (bow) / सर (arrows) / निकर (shower, cluster) / छाड़ेसि (he loosed) / उरग (serpents) / जिमि (like) / उड़ि (flying) / लागहीं (strike, hit) / रहे (remained) / पूरि (filled) / सर (arrows) / धरनी (earth) / गगन (sky) / दिसि (directions) / बिदिसि (intermediate directions) / कहँ (where) / कपि (monkeys) / भागहीं (run) / भयो (became) / अति (very) / कोलाहल (uproar) / बिकल (shaken, distressed) / कपि दल (monkey army) / भालु (bears) / बोलहिं (cry out) / आतुरे (anxious) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / करुना (compassion) / सिंधु (ocean) / आरत (distressed) / बंधु (friend, kinsman) / जन (servants, people) / रच्छक (protector) / हरे (Hari, the remover of suffering)
ramacharitamanas::4994.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4994.essence: When everything closes in, devotion becomes the only refuge.
ramacharitamanas::4994.simple_meaning: Arrows fill every direction, leaving the monkey and bear army with nowhere to escape. In their panic, they cry out to Ram as the compassionate protector of the suffering.
ramacharitamanas::4994.simple_insight: When pressure closes in, the deepest instinct is to call for help that can truly hold you.
ramacharitamanas::4994.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle turns brutal. A demon warrior unleashes arrows so densely that the monkey and bear forces can barely move. Surrounded and shaken, they stop fighting and cry out to Ram, revealing that their real refuge is not strength but his protection.
ramacharitamanas::4994.modern_relevance: You open your inbox and everything feels like it is hitting at once — messages, deadlines, demands, fear. In that moment, the mind reaches for the one steady refuge it trusts.
ramacharitamanas::4994.insight: It shifts the mind from panic and scattering to seeking shelter in what can actually protect you.

ramacharitamanas::4995.verse_sanskrit: निज दल बिकल देखि कटि कसि निषंग धनु हाथ। लछिमन चले क्रुद्ध होइ नाइ राम पद माथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::4995.verse_hindi: अपनी सेना को व्याकुल देखकर कमर में तरकस कसकर और हाथ में धनुष लेकर श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों पर मस्तक नवाकर लक्ष्मणजी क्रोधित होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::4995.english_translation: Seeing his own army distressed, Lakshman tightened his quiver, took his bow in hand, bowed his head at Ram's feet, and went out in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4995.translation_literal: निज (own) / दल (army) / बिकल (distressed) / देखि (seeing) / कटि (at the waist) / कसि (tightening) / निषंग (quiver) / धनु (bow) / हाथ (in hand) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / चले (went) / क्रुद्ध होइ (becoming angry) / नाइ (bowing) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / माथ (head)
ramacharitamanas::4995.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4995.essence: True service bows first, then fights without delay.
ramacharitamanas::4995.simple_meaning: Lakshman sees his side in trouble, arms himself, bows to Ram, and rushes into battle in anger.
ramacharitamanas::4995.simple_insight: He does not freeze when others are shaken. He turns loyalty into action.
ramacharitamanas::4995.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Ravana's side has driven the monkeys into panic. Lakshman sees his own army wavering, fastens his quiver, bows to Ram, and charges forward. The verse sets up the fierce exchange that follows.
ramacharitamanas::4995.modern_relevance: Your team is rattled, the room is tense, and everyone is waiting for someone to move. You steady yourself, remember who you serve, and step in without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::4995.insight: It shifts loyalty from feeling into immediate, protective action.

ramacharitamanas::4996.verse_sanskrit: रे खल का मारसि कपि भालू। मोहि बिलोकु तोर मैं कालू॥ खोजत रहेउँ तोहि सुतघाती। आजु निपाति जुड़ावउँ छाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::4996.verse_hindi: (लक्ष्मणजी ने पास जाकर कहा-) अरे दुष्ट! वानर भालुओं को क्या मार रहा है? मुझे देख, मैं तेरा काल हूँ। (रावण ने कहा-) अरे मेरे पुत्र के घातक! मैं तुझी को ढूँढ रहा था। आज तुझे मारकर (अपनी) छाती ठंडी करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::4996.english_translation: “You villain, why are you killing monkeys and bears? Look at me — I am your death.” “I have been searching for you, killer of my son. Today I will kill you and cool my burning chest.”
ramacharitamanas::4996.translation_literal: रे (hey) / खल (wicked one) / का (why) / मारसि (are you killing) / कपि (monkeys) / भालू (bears) / मोहि (me) / बिलोकु (look at) / तोर (your) / मैं (I) / कालू (death) / खोजत (searching) / रहेउँ (was) / तोहि (you) / सुतघाती (son-killer) / आजु (today) / निपाति (having killed) / जुड़ावउँ (will cool) / छाती (chest)
ramacharitamanas::4996.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::4996.essence: Rage makes the wounded man seek his own ruin.
ramacharitamanas::4996.simple_meaning: Ravana challenges Lakshman in anger, saying he has been looking for him and will kill him to ease his burning rage.
ramacharitamanas::4996.simple_insight: Pride turns pain into violence and makes a person hunt the very thing that can destroy him.
ramacharitamanas::4996.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshman has cut down Ravana's forces and advanced to face him directly. Ravana, furious over his son's death and the chaos around him, confronts Lakshman in rage. This is the moment before their fierce duel begins.
ramacharitamanas::4996.modern_relevance: Two people trade words after a family fight, and old grief comes out as threat. What should have been sorrow becomes a need to strike back.
ramacharitamanas::4996.insight: It shows how wounded ego turns loss into aggression instead of reflection.

ramacharitamanas::4997.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि छाड़ेसि बान प्रचंडा। लछिमन किए सकल सत खंडा॥ कोटिन्ह आयुध रावन डारे। तिल प्रवान करि काटि निवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::4997.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर उसने प्रचण्ड बाण छोड़े। लक्ष्मणजी ने सबके सैकड़ों टुकड़े कर डाले। रावण ने करोड़ों अस्त्र-शस्त्र चलाए। लक्ष्मणजी ने उनको तिल के बराबर करके काटकर हटा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::4997.english_translation: After saying this, he released fierce arrows. Lakshman shattered them into hundreds of pieces. Ravana hurled millions of weapons, and Lakshman cut them down as if they were sesame seeds.
ramacharitamanas::4997.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying this) / छाड़ेसि (he released) / बान (arrows) / प्रचंडा (fierce) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / किए (made) / सकल (all) / सत (hundreds) / खंडा (pieces) / कोटिन्ह (millions) / आयुध (weapons) / रावन (Ravana) / डारे (threw) / तिल (sesame seed) / प्रवान (like) / करि (making) / काटि (cutting) / निवारे (removed)
ramacharitamanas::4997.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4997.essence: No barrage can shake the one who stays ready.
ramacharitamanas::4997.simple_meaning: Ravana unleashes weapon after weapon, but Lakshman cuts every attack apart and keeps advancing.
ramacharitamanas::4997.simple_insight: Some battles are won by staying unshaken while everything is thrown at you.
ramacharitamanas::4997.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the duel between Lakshman and Ravana has turned fierce. Ravana fires a storm of weapons, but Lakshman slices through every one. The verse keeps the focus on combat momentum, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::4997.modern_relevance: A crisis meeting keeps throwing new objections at you, one after another. You stay calm, answer each one, and refuse to be thrown off center.
ramacharitamanas::4997.insight: It shifts attention from the volume of opposition to steadiness under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::4998.verse_sanskrit: पुनि निज बानन्ह कीन्ह प्रहारा। स्यंदनु भंजि सारथी मारा॥ सत सत सर मारे दस भाला। गिरि सृंगन्ह जनु प्रबिसहिं ब्याला ॥
ramacharitamanas::4998.verse_hindi: फिर अपने बाणों से (उस पर) प्रहार किया और (उसके) रथ को तोड़कर सारथी को मार डाला। (रावण के) दसों मस्तकों में सौ-सौ बाण मारे। वे सिरों में ऐसे पैठ गए मानो पहाड़ के शिखरों में सर्प प्रवेश कर रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::4998.english_translation: Then he struck again with his arrows, shattered the chariot, and killed the charioteer. He shot a hundred arrows into each of Ravana's ten heads, and they pierced them like snakes entering mountain peaks.
ramacharitamanas::4998.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / निज (his own) / बानन्ह (arrows) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रहारा (strike) । स्यंदनु (chariot) / भंजि (breaking) / सारथी (charioteer) / मारा (killed) ॥ सत (hundred) / सत (hundred) / सर (arrows) / मारे (struck) / दस (ten) / भाला (heads) । गिरि (mountain) / सृंगन्ह (peaks) / जनु (as if) / प्रबिसहिं (enter) / ब्याला (snakes) ॥
ramacharitamanas::4998.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4998.essence: Ravana's defenses are shattered in a single, overwhelming strike.
ramacharitamanas::4998.simple_meaning: Ravana is hit hard in battle: his chariot is broken, his charioteer is killed, and arrows pierce all ten heads.
ramacharitamanas::4998.simple_insight: Some struggles are not subtle. They hit every defense at once.
ramacharitamanas::4998.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, the combat between Ravana and his opponent intensifies. This verse is a battlefield blow-by-blow: the chariot is smashed, the charioteer falls, and Ravana's many heads are riddled with arrows. It is part of a running fight, not a complete teaching on its own.
