ramacharitamanas::4998.modern_relevance: A crisis can hit all at once: the plan breaks, the support person disappears, and the pressure lands from every side.
ramacharitamanas::4998.insight: It shows total battlefield collapse, not a moral principle. The focus stays on action, force, and damage.

ramacharitamanas::4999.verse_sanskrit: पुनि सुत सर मारा उर माहीं। परेउ धरनि तल सुधि कछु नाहीं॥ उठा प्रबल पुनि मुरुछा जागी। छाड़िसि ब्रह्म दीन्हि जो साँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::4999.verse_hindi: फिर सौ बाण उसकी छाती में मारे। वह पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, उसे कुछ भी होश न रहा। फिर मूर्च्छा छूटने पर वह प्रबल रावण उठा और उसने वह शक्ति चलाई जो ब्रह्माजी ने उसे दी थी ॥ छंद :
ramacharitamanas::4999.english_translation: Then he shot a hundred arrows into his chest. He fell to the ground, unconscious. When the fainting passed, mighty Ravana rose again and launched the weapon given by Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::4999.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / सुत सर (a hundred arrows) / मारा (struck) / उर माहीं (into the chest) / परेउ (fell) / धरनि तल (to the ground) / सुधि (consciousness) / कछु नाहीं (none at all) / उठा (rose) / प्रबल (mighty) / पुनि (again) / मुरुछा (fainting) / जागी (ended / woke) / छाड़िसि (released) / ब्रह्म दीन्हि (given by Brahma) / जो साँगी (that weapon)
ramacharitamanas::4999.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::4999.essence: Defeat does not end ego; it often makes it reach for stronger force.
ramacharitamanas::4999.simple_meaning: Ravana is struck down, loses consciousness, then rises again and uses a powerful weapon given by Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::4999.simple_insight: Even after being knocked down, a hardened mind can rise with its old weapons.
ramacharitamanas::4999.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Lakshman has already shattered Ravana's chariot and armor. Here Ravana takes another pounding, falls unconscious, then regains himself and unleashes the divine weapon Brahma once gave him. The battle is still raging, and Lakshman is about to face it.
ramacharitamanas::4999.modern_relevance: You get hit with bad news, sit stunned for a minute, then stand up and reach for the same old defense. The pattern is older than the problem.
ramacharitamanas::4999.insight: It shows how ego can recover quickly and respond with inherited power instead of surrendering.

ramacharitamanas::5000.verse_sanskrit: सो ब्रह्म दत्त प्रचंड सक्ति अनंत उर लागी सही। पर् यो बीर बिकल उठाव दसमुख अतुल बल महिमा रही॥ ब्रह्मांड भवन बिराज जाकें एक सिर जिमि रज कनी। तेहि चह उठावन मूढ़ रावन जान नहिं त्रिभुअन धनी॥
ramacharitamanas::5000.verse_hindi: वह ब्रह्मा की दी हुई प्रचण्ड शक्ति लक्ष्मणजी की ठीक छाती में लगी। वीर लक्ष्मणजी व्याकुल होकर गिर पड़े। तब रावण उन्हें उठाने लगा, पर उसके अतुलित बल की महिमा यों ही रह गई, (व्यर्थ हो गई, वह उन्हें उठा न सका)। जिनके एक ही सिर पर ब्रह्मांड रूपी भवन धूल के एक कण के समान विराजता है, उन्हें मूर्ख रावण उठाना चाहता है! वह तीनों भुवनों के स्वामी लक्ष्मणजी को नहीं जानता।
ramacharitamanas::5000.english_translation: The fierce power given by Brahma struck Lakshmana squarely in the chest. Brave Lakshmana fell in distress. Then Ravana tried to lift him, but his unmatched strength proved useless. The fool does not know the Lord of the three worlds, whose one head bears the universe like a speck of dust.
ramacharitamanas::5000.translation_literal: सो (that) / ब्रह्मदत्त (given by Brahma) / प्रचंड (fierce) / सक्ति (power) / अनंत (endless) / उर (chest) / लागी (struck) / सही (endured) / पर् यो (fell) / बीर (warrior) / बिकल (distressed) / उठाव (lifted) / दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / अतुल बल (matchless strength) / महिमा (glory) / रही (remained) / ब्रह्मांड (universe) / भवन (dwelling) / बिराज (rests) / जाकें (in whose) / एक सिर (one head) / जिमि (like) / रज कनी (a speck of dust) / तेहि (him) / चह (wished) / उठावन (to lift) / मूढ़ (foolish) / रावन (Ravana) / जान नहिं (does not know) / त्रिभुअन धनी (lord of the three worlds)
ramacharitamanas::5000.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5000.essence: Pride is weakest when it mistakes greatness for weakness.
ramacharitamanas::5000.simple_meaning: Ravana's blow fells Lakshmana, but even then Ravana cannot lift him. The verse exposes Ravana's blindness: he does not understand Lakshmana's true greatness.
ramacharitamanas::5000.simple_insight: Real strength is not just force; it is seeing clearly what you are facing.
ramacharitamanas::5000.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Lakshmana has been struck down by a terrible divine weapon and lies in distress. Ravana, still proud of his power, tries to lift him. The verse turns that moment into humiliation: Ravana cannot even move the one he has wounded.
ramacharitamanas::5000.modern_relevance: You keep trying to control a person who has already slipped beyond your reach. The harder you push, the more your own helplessness shows.
ramacharitamanas::5000.insight: It shifts the mind from raw force to humility before what cannot be mastered.

ramacharitamanas::5001.verse_sanskrit: देखि पवनसुत धायउ बोलत बचन कठोर। आवत कपिहि हन्यो तेहिं मुष्टि प्रहार प्रघोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5001.verse_hindi: यह देखकर पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी कठोर वचन बोलते हुए दौड़े। हनुमान् जी के आते ही रावण ने उन पर अत्यंत भयंकर घूँसे का प्रहार किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5001.english_translation: Seeing this, Hanuman rushed forward, speaking harsh words. As he came near, Ravana struck him with a fierce blow of his fist.
ramacharitamanas::5001.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / धायउ (rushed) / बोलत (speaking) / बचन (words) / कठोर (hard, harsh) / आवत (coming) / कपिहि (to the monkey) / हन्यो (struck) / तेहिं (he) / मुष्टि (fist) / प्रहार (blow) / प्रघोर (fierce)
ramacharitamanas::5001.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5001.essence: The next clash begins the moment courage steps forward.
ramacharitamanas::5001.simple_meaning: Hanuman rushes in with sharp words, and Ravana answers with a brutal punch.
ramacharitamanas::5001.simple_insight: The scene turns from challenge to combat in a single instant.
ramacharitamanas::5001.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final battle, Hanuman rushes toward Ravana after seeing Lakshman wounded. Ravana meets him with a savage fist strike. The verse is a brief combat beat that drives the fight forward.
ramacharitamanas::5001.insight: It moves the story into direct confrontation, with no pause or reflection.

ramacharitamanas::5002.verse_sanskrit: जानु टेकि कपि भूमि न गिरा। उठा सँभारि बहुत रिस भरा॥ मुठिका एक ताहि कपि मारा। परेउ सैल जनु बज्र प्रहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5002.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी घुटने टेककर रह गए, पृथ्वी पर गिरे नहीं और फिर क्रोध से भरे हुए संभलकर उठे। हनुमान् जी ने रावण को एक घूँसा मारा। वह ऐसा गिर पड़ा जैसे वज्र की मार से पर्वत गिरा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5002.english_translation: Hanuman knelt, did not fall to the ground, then rose up, full of rage. He struck Ravana with one fist, and Ravana fell like a mountain struck by thunderbolt.
ramacharitamanas::5002.translation_literal: जानु (knee) / टेकि (bent, touched down) / कपि (the monkey, Hanuman) / भूमि (earth) / न (not) / गिरा (fell) / उठा (rose) / सँभारि (steadying himself) / बहुत (very) / रिस (rage) / भरा (filled) / मुठिका (fist) / एक (one) / ताहि (him) / कपि (the monkey) / मारा (struck) / परेउ (fell) / सैल (mountain) / जनु (like) / बज्र (thunderbolt) / प्रहारा (blow, strike)
ramacharitamanas::5002.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5002.essence: A single retaliatory blow drops Ravana hard.
ramacharitamanas::5002.simple_meaning: Hanuman steadies himself, rises in anger, and lands a crushing blow on Ravana that sends him down hard.
ramacharitamanas::5002.simple_insight: Sometimes one clear strike matters more than endless struggle.
ramacharitamanas::5002.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana has just struck Hanuman. Hanuman dips to one knee, regains himself, and answers with a single devastating punch. The verse is a vivid combat beat, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::5002.insight: It keeps the focus on immediate combat action, not reflection or principle.

ramacharitamanas::5003.verse_sanskrit: मुरुछा गै बहोरि सो जागा। कपि बल बिपुल सराहन लागा॥ धिग धिग मम पौरुष धिग मोही। जौं तैं जिअत रहेसि सुरद्रोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5003.verse_hindi: मूर्च्छा भंग होने पर फिर वह जागा और हनुमान् जी के बड़े भारी बल को सराहने लगा। (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) मेरे पौरुष को धिक्कार है, धिक्कार है और मुझे भी धिक्कार है, जो हे देवद्रोही! तू अब भी जीता रह गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5003.english_translation: After fainting, he woke again and began praising Hanuman's immense strength. "Shame on my strength, shame on me, if you, enemy of the radiant beings, still live!"
ramacharitamanas::5003.translation_literal: मुरुछा (fainting) / गै (went) / बहोरि (again) / सो (he) / जागा (woke up) / कपि (monkey; Hanuman) / बल (strength) / बिपुल (great, abundant) / सराहन (to praise) / लागा (began) ॥ धिग (shame) / धिग (shame) / मम (my) / पौरुष (manliness, valor) / धिग (shame) / मोही (me) / जौं (if) / तैं (you) / जिअत (living) / रहेसि (have remained) / सुरद्रोही (enemy of the radiant beings) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5003.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5003.essence: Ego collapses fastest when it meets real strength.
ramacharitamanas::5003.simple_meaning: Ravana regains consciousness, admires Hanuman's power, and then curses his own courage for failing to kill him.
ramacharitamanas::5003.simple_insight: Pride can turn instantly into self-disgust when it meets someone stronger.
ramacharitamanas::5003.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has just struck Ravana down in single combat. Ravana wakes from the blow, sees the force that hit him, and reacts with shocked admiration and bitter shame. The scene is still combat, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5003.modern_relevance: After a humiliating loss, you replay the moment and hear your own ego cracking. The sting is real, but so is the recognition of someone stronger.
ramacharitamanas::5003.insight: It shows defeat exposing ego, not just weakening the body.

ramacharitamanas::5004.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि लछिमन कहुँ कपि ल्यायो। देखि दसानन बिसमय पायो॥ कह रघुबीर समुझु जियँ भ्राता। तुम्ह कृतांत भच्छक सुर त्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5004.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर और लक्ष्मणजी को उठाकर हनुमान् जी श्री रघुनाथजी के पास ले आए। यह देखकर रावण को आश्चर्य हुआ। श्री रघुवीर ने (लक्ष्मणजी से) कहा- हे भाई! हृदय में समझो, तुम काल के भी भक्षक और देवताओं के रक्षक हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5004.english_translation: Having said this, Hanuman brought Lakshman to Ram. Ravana was astonished to see it. Then Ram said to his brother, "Understand in your heart: you are the eater of even Time, and the protector of the radiant beings."
ramacharitamanas::5004.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / लछिमन कहुँ (to Lakshman) / कपि (the monkey, Hanuman) / ल्यायो (brought) / देखि (seeing) / दसानन (the ten-faced one, Ravana) / बिसमय (wonder) / पायो (felt) ॥ कह (said) / रघुबीर (Ram, hero of the Raghu clan) / समुझु (understand) / जियँ (in the heart) / भ्राता (brother) / तुम्ह (you) / कृतांत (Time, death) / भच्छक (eater) / सुर (radiant beings) / त्राता (protector) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5004.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5004.essence: Your deepest strength can remain untouched even after defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5004.simple_meaning: Hanuman brings the wounded Lakshman back to Ram, and Ram reassures him with words of strength and honor.
ramacharitamanas::5004.simple_insight: Even in injury, you can be reminded of your deeper strength.
ramacharitamanas::5004.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Hanuman carries the fallen Lakshman back to Ram. Ravana watches in shock. Ram then speaks to Lakshman not as a broken warrior, but as one whose true strength still stands beneath the wound.
ramacharitamanas::5004.modern_relevance: A teammate comes back from a brutal setback, and everyone is watching to see whether they collapse. The right words can restore courage faster than any bandage.
ramacharitamanas::5004.insight: It shifts attention from temporary weakness to the larger courage still intact.

ramacharitamanas::5005.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बचन उठि बैठ कृपाला। गई गगन सो सकति कराला॥ पुनि कोदंड बान गहि धाए। रिपु सन्मुख अति आतुर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5005.verse_hindi: ये वचन सुनते ही कृपालु लक्ष्मणजी उठ बैठे। वह कराल शक्ति आकाश को चली गई। लक्ष्मणजी फिर धनुष-बाण लेकर दौड़े और बड़ी शीघ्रता से शत्रु के सामने आ पहुँचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5005.english_translation: Hearing those words, the compassionate one rose up. The terrible Shakti went into the sky. Then, taking bow and arrows, he rushed forward and came eagerly before the enemy.
ramacharitamanas::5005.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / उठि (rising) / बैठ (sat up) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / गई (went) / गगन (sky) / सो (that) / सकति (Shakti) / कराला (terrible) / पुनि (again) / कोदंड (bow) / बान (arrows) / गहि (taking) / धाए (ran) / रिपु (enemy) / सन्मुख (before) / अति (very) / आतुर (eagerly) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::5005.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5005.essence: A single word of hope can bring strength back at once.
ramacharitamanas::5005.simple_meaning: Hearing the words, Lakshman rises at once, and the fierce Shakti disappears. He grabs his bow and arrows and rushes toward the enemy.
ramacharitamanas::5005.simple_insight: True courage returns the moment resolve returns.
ramacharitamanas::5005.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Lakshman has been struck down, and Hanuman has just brought him back to Ram. The enemy's weapon loses its hold, and Lakshman rises again, armed and eager. The verse shows the turning point before the next attack.
ramacharitamanas::5005.modern_relevance: You hear one encouraging message after a crushing setback, and your body changes first. The slump lifts, your hands move, and you are back in the fight.
ramacharitamanas::5005.insight: It shows how restored confidence can dissolve fear and restart decisive action.

ramacharitamanas::5006.verse_sanskrit: आतुर बहोरि बिभंजि स्यंदन सूत हति ब्याकुल कियो। गिर् यो धरनि दसकंधर बिकलतर बान सत बेध्यो हियो॥ सारथी दूसर घालि रथ तेहि तुरत लंका लै गयो। रघुबीर बंधु प्रताप पुंज बहोरि प्रभु चरनन्हि नयो॥
ramacharitamanas::5006.verse_hindi: फिर उन्होंने बड़ी ही शीघ्रता से रावण के रथ को चूर-चूर कर और सारथी को मारकर उसे (रावण को) व्याकुल कर दिया। सौ बाणों से उसका हृदय बेध दिया, जिससे रावण अत्यंत व्याकुल होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। तब दूसरा सारथी उसे रथ में डालकर तुरंत ही लंका को ले गया। प्रताप के समूह श्री रघुवीर के भाई लक्ष्मणजी ने फिर आकर प्रभु के चरणों में प्रणाम किया।
ramacharitamanas::5006.english_translation: Then, in great haste, he shattered Ravana's chariot and killed the charioteer, throwing him into confusion. He pierced Ravana's heart with a hundred arrows, and Ravana fell to the ground, shaken and helpless. Another charioteer quickly carried him back to Lanka. Lakshman, the shining brother of Raghubir, came again and bowed at the Lord's feet.
ramacharitamanas::5006.translation_literal: आतुर (in haste) / बहोरि (again) / बिभंजि (shattering) / स्यंदन (chariot) / सूत (charioteer) / हति (killing) / ब्याकुल (confused) / कियो (made) / गिर् यो (fell) / धरनि (to the ground) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / बिकलतर (utterly helpless) / बान (arrows) / सत (hundred) / बेध्यो (pierced) / हियो (heart) / सारथी (charioteer) / दूसर (another) / घालि (placing) / रथ (chariot) / तेहि (him) / तुरत (quickly) / लंका (to Lanka) / लै गयो (took away) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / बंधु (brother) / प्रताप पुंज (mass of splendour) / बहोरि (again) / प्रभु (Lord) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / नयो (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::5006.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5006.essence: Power is complete only when it ends in surrender at the Lord's feet.
ramacharitamanas::5006.simple_meaning: Laxman defeats Ravana in battle, leaving him stunned and carried back to Lanka, then returns to bow before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5006.simple_insight: Victory is not shown as pride here, but as service returning to humility.
ramacharitamanas::5006.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Lakshman smashes Ravana's chariot, kills the charioteer, and drives the wounded king down. Ravana is carried away in shock, while Lakshman immediately returns to Ram and bows. The verse keeps the action moving, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5006.modern_relevance: A hard-won win at work or in sport can still end with you stepping back quietly, not strutting. The real measure is what you do after the impact.
ramacharitamanas::5006.insight: It shifts attention from battlefield triumph to the discipline of returning to service.

ramacharitamanas::5007.verse_sanskrit: उहाँ दसानन जागि करि करै लाग कछु जग्य। राम बिरोध बिजय चह सठ हठ बस अति अग्य ॥
ramacharitamanas::5007.verse_hindi: वहाँ (लंका में) रावण मूर्छा से जागकर कुछ यज्ञ करने लगा। वह मूर्ख और अत्यंत अज्ञानी हठवश श्री रघुनाथजी से विरोध करके विजय चाहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5007.english_translation: There, Ravana woke from his fainting spell and began some ritual. That fool, driven by stubbornness and deep ignorance, still wanted victory while opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5007.translation_literal: उहाँ (there) / दसानन (the ten-faced one, Ravana) / जागि (waking) / करि (having done) / करै लाग (began to do) / कछु (some) / जग्य (ritual sacrifice) / राम (Ram) / बिरोध (opposition) / बिजय (victory) / चह (wants) / सठ (fool) / हठ (stubbornness) / बस (under the control of) / अति (very) / अग्य (ignorant)
ramacharitamanas::5007.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5007.essence: Stubborn pride keeps reaching for victory after defeat has already begun.
ramacharitamanas::5007.simple_meaning: Ravana wakes up and starts a ritual, still stubbornly hoping to win by opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5007.simple_insight: Pride can keep chasing victory long after reality has already answered.
ramacharitamanas::5007.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana has just been badly shaken and left nearly broken. Instead of yielding, he wakes and turns to ritual, hoping stubborn effort will still save him. The verse shows his blindness, not his strength.
ramacharitamanas::5007.modern_relevance: You get a harsh warning from the numbers, but you still double down and call it strategy. That is Ravana's mind at work.
ramacharitamanas::5007.insight: It exposes how ego keeps repeating failed methods instead of facing the truth.

ramacharitamanas::5008.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ बिभीषन सब सुधि पाई। सपदि जाइ रघुपतिहि सुनाई॥ नाथ करइ रावन एक जागा। सिद्ध भएँ नहिं मरिहि अभागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5008.verse_hindi: यहाँ विभीषणजी ने सब खबर पाई और तुरंत जाकर श्री रघुनाथजी को कह सुनाई कि हे नाथ! रावण एक यज्ञ कर रहा है। उसके सिद्ध होने पर वह अभागा सहज ही नहीं मरेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5008.english_translation: Here, Vibhishana learned all the news and quickly went to tell Raghupati: "Lord, Ravana is performing a sacrifice. If it succeeds, that unlucky one will not die."
ramacharitamanas::5008.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / सब (all) / सुधि (news, information) / पाई (having obtained) / सपदि (quickly) / जाइ (going) / रघुपतिहि (to Raghupati) / सुनाई (told) ॥ / नाथ (Lord) / करइ (is doing) / रावन (Ravana) / एक (a) / जागा (sacrifice) / सिद्ध भएँ (if it is completed) / नहिं (not) / मरिहि (will die) / अभागा (unlucky one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5008.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5008.essence: Early warning can change the whole battle.
ramacharitamanas::5008.simple_meaning: Vibhishana learns that Ravana is trying to complete a sacrifice, and he urgently warns Ram that this would make Ravana harder to defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5008.simple_insight: Good timing can matter more than force.
ramacharitamanas::5008.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just risen from defeat and begun a ritual to regain strength. Vibhishana, loyal to Ram, hears the news at once and rushes to report it. The verse sets up Ram's next move.
ramacharitamanas::5008.modern_relevance: You hear the group chat blow up just as a bad decision is about to become irreversible. Speaking up early can stop damage that brute force later can't undo.
ramacharitamanas::5008.insight: It teaches you to act on urgent information before a problem hardens.

ramacharitamanas::5009.verse_sanskrit: पठवहु नाथ बेगि भट बंदर। करहिं बिधंस आव दसकंधर॥ प्रात होत प्रभु सुभट पठाए। हनुमदादि अंगद सब धाए॥2।
ramacharitamanas::5009.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! तुरंत वानर योद्धाओं को भेजिए, जो यज्ञ का विध्वंस करें, जिससे रावण युद्ध में आवे। प्रातःकाल होते ही प्रभु ने वीर योद्धाओं को भेजा। हनुमान् और अंगद आदि सब (प्रधान वीर) दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5009.english_translation: O Lord, quickly send the monkey warriors. Let them destroy the sacrifice so Ravana comes to battle. At dawn the Lord sent out the brave fighters; Hanuman, Angada, and the others rushed forth.
ramacharitamanas::5009.translation_literal: पठवहु (send) / नाथ (lord) / बेगि (quickly) / भट (warriors) / बंदर (monkeys) / करहिं (may they do) / बिधंस (destruction) / आव (let come) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / प्रात होत (at dawn) / प्रभु (the lord) / सुभट (brave warriors) / पठाए (sent) / हनुमदादि (Hanuman and others) / अंगद (Angada) / सब (all) / धाए (rushed)
ramacharitamanas::5009.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5009.essence: Swift action can stop a danger before it matures.
ramacharitamanas::5009.simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram to send the monkey warriors to stop Ravana’s sacrifice and draw him into battle. Ram then sends Hanuman, Angada, and the others at dawn.
ramacharitamanas::5009.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response is immediate action, not waiting for the enemy to finish.
ramacharitamanas::5009.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has just warned Ram that Ravana is performing a sacrifice meant to gain power. He urges Ram to send the monkey warriors at once. At dawn, Ram sends Hanuman, Angada, and the others to break it.
ramacharitamanas::5009.modern_relevance: You spot a problem before it becomes a disaster, and you act fast instead of hoping it will fix itself.
ramacharitamanas::5009.insight: It shifts the mind from passive concern to decisive, timely response.

ramacharitamanas::5010.verse_sanskrit: कौतुक कूदि चढ़े कपि लंका। पैठे रावन भवन असंका॥ जग्य करत जबहीं सो देखा। सकल कपिन्ह भा क्रोध बिसेषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5010.verse_hindi: वानर खेल से ही कूदकर लंका पर जा चढ़े और निर्भय होकर रावण के महल में जा घुसे। ज्यों ही उसको यज्ञ करते देखा, त्यों ही सब वानरों को बहुत क्रोध हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5010.english_translation: The monkeys leaped onto Lanka as if for sport and entered Ravana's palace without fear. The moment they saw him performing the sacrifice, all the monkeys felt a fierce anger.
ramacharitamanas::5010.translation_literal: कौतुक (as sport) / कूदि (leaping) / चढ़े (climbed) / कपि (monkeys) / लंका (Lanka) / पैठे (entered) / रावन (Ravana's) / भवन (palace) / असंका (without fear) / जग्य (sacrifice) / करत (doing) / जबहीं (the very moment) / सो (that) / देखा (saw) / सकल (all) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / भा (became) / क्रोध (anger) / बिसेषा (intense)
ramacharitamanas::5010.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5010.essence: Fearless entry becomes fury the moment injustice is seen.
ramacharitamanas::5010.simple_meaning: The monkeys entered Lanka fearlessly, and seeing Ravana's sacrifice made them angry.
ramacharitamanas::5010.simple_insight: Sometimes courage turns instantly into resolve when you see what must be stopped.
ramacharitamanas::5010.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman and the monkey warriors slip into Ravana's palace after hearing that he is performing a sacrifice. The scene is still moving toward confrontation, and this verse simply shows their fearless entry and immediate anger at what they find.
ramacharitamanas::5010.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting a routine meeting, then see someone being cornered unfairly. Your calm turns sharp in an instant, and you know exactly where you stand.
ramacharitamanas::5010.insight: It shows how clear sight can convert boldness into righteous action without hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::5011.verse_sanskrit: रन ते निलज भाजि गृह आवा। इहाँ आइ बक ध्यान लगावा। अस कहि अंगद मारा लाता। चितव न सठ स्वारथ मन राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5011.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) अरे ओ निर्लज्ज! रणभूमि से घर भाग आया और यहाँ आकर बगुले का सा ध्यान लगाकर बैठा है? ऐसा कहकर अंगद ने लात मारी। पर उसने इनकी ओर देखा भी नहीं, उस दुष्ट का मन स्वार्थ में अनुरक्त था ॥
ramacharitamanas::5011.english_translation: “You shameless one, you fled the battlefield and came home, then sat here in monk-like stillness?” Angada said this and kicked him, but the fool did not even look; his mind was fixed on selfish gain.
ramacharitamanas::5011.translation_literal: रन ते (from the battlefield) / निलज (shameless one) / भाजि (fleeing) / गृह (home) / आवा (came) / इहाँ (here) / आइ (coming) / बक (heron-like) / ध्यान (meditation) / लगावा (applied) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / अंगद (Angada) / मारा (struck) / लाता (kick) / चितव (looked) / न (not) / सठ (fool) / स्वारथ (selfish gain) / मन (mind) / राता (coloured, absorbed)
ramacharitamanas::5011.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5011.essence: A selfish mind can stay untouched even by disgrace.
ramacharitamanas::5011.simple_meaning: Angada mocks a coward who fled battle, then kicked him. The man stays unmoved because his mind is absorbed in selfishness.
ramacharitamanas::5011.simple_insight: Self-interest can make a person unmoved even by shame or force.
ramacharitamanas::5011.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the monkeys disrupt Ravana's ritual, Angada confronts one of the cowards who ran from battle. The man sits pretending to be absorbed, but he is really lost in selfish attachment. The scene shows contempt, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5011.modern_relevance: A person who has already chosen self-protection over courage can sit through the harshest criticism without blinking. The problem is not lack of hearing; it is a mind already sold.
ramacharitamanas::5011.insight: It shows how selfish fixation can block even shame, warning you that inner attachment can make correction useless.

ramacharitamanas::5012.verse_sanskrit: नहिं चितव जब करि कोप कपि गहि दसन लातन्ह मारहीं। धरि केस नारि निकारि बाहेर तेऽतिदीन पुकारहीं॥ तब उठेउ क्रुद्ध कृतांत सम गहि चरन बानर डारई। एहि बीच कपिन्ह बिधंस कृत मख देखि मन महुँ हारई॥
ramacharitamanas::5012.verse_hindi: जब उसने नहीं देखा, तब वानर क्रोध करके उसे दाँतों से पकड़कर (काटने और) लातों से मारने लगे। स्त्रियों को बाल पकड़कर घर से बाहर घसीट लाए, वे अत्यंत ही दीन होकर पुकारने लगीं। तब रावण काल के समान क्रोधित होकर उठा और वानरों को पैर पकड़कर पटकने लगा। इसी बीच में वानरों ने यज्ञ विध्वंस कर डाला, यह देखकर वह मन में हारने लगा। (निराश होने लगा)।
ramacharitamanas::5012.english_translation: When Ravana looked away, the monkeys grew angry, seized him with their teeth, and struck him with kicks. They grabbed the women by the hair and dragged them outside, where the helpless women cried out. Then Ravana rose in rage like Death itself and seized the monkeys by the feet to hurl them down. In the meantime, the monkeys destroyed the sacrifice, and seeing that, he began to lose heart.
ramacharitamanas::5012.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / चितव (looked) / जब (when) / करि (doing) / कोप (anger) / कपि (monkeys) / गहि (seizing) / दसन (teeth) / लातन्ह (with kicks) / मारहीं (struck) / धरि (grabbing) / केस (hair) / नारि (women) / निकारि (dragged out) / बाहेर (outside) / तेऽतिदीन (very helpless) / पुकारहीं (cried out) / तब (then) / उठेउ (rose) / क्रुद्ध (angry) / कृतांत (Death) / सम (like) / गहि (seizing) / चरन (feet) / बानर (monkeys) / डारई (threw) / एहि बीच (in this meantime) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / बिधंस (destroyed) / कृत (done) / मख (sacrifice) / देखि (seeing) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / हारई (lost heart)
ramacharitamanas::5012.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5012.essence: Power begins to crack the moment confidence breaks.
ramacharitamanas::5012.simple_meaning: The monkeys attack Ravana's people, Ravana fights back in fury, and the sacrifice is ruined. Seeing the destruction, Ravana starts to lose confidence.
ramacharitamanas::5012.simple_insight: Pride can look fierce, but one broken plan can still shake it.
ramacharitamanas::5012.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman's allies have turned Ravana's sacred ritual into chaos. The monkeys rough up the palace, the women cry out, Ravana attacks like death itself, and the sacrifice is ruined. This verse shows the battle spilling into Ravana's inner collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5012.modern_relevance: A room full of confidence can change in seconds when a plan falls apart and everyone starts reacting at once. The real loss is often not the event itself, but the confidence it shatters.
ramacharitamanas::5012.insight: It shows how quickly anger, humiliation, and fear can unravel control.

ramacharitamanas::5013.verse_sanskrit: जग्य बिधंसि कुसल कपि आए रघुपति पास। चलेउ निसाचर कु्रद्ध होइ त्यागि जिवन कै आस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5013.verse_hindi: यज्ञ विध्वंस करके सब चतुर वानर रघुनाथजी के पास आ गए। तब रावण जीने की आश छोड़कर क्रोधित होकर चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::5013.english_translation: The clever monkeys returned to Raghupati after ruining the sacrifice. Then Ravana, abandoning all hope of living, went off in anger.
ramacharitamanas::5013.translation_literal: जग्य (sacrifice) / बिधंसि (having destroyed) / कुसल (clever) / कपि (monkeys) / आए (came) / रघुपति (to Raghupati) / पास (near) / चलेउ (went) / निसाचर (Ravana, night-walker) / क्रुद्ध होइ (becoming angry) / त्यागि (abandoning) / जिवन (life) / कै आस (hope)
ramacharitamanas::5013.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5013.essence: Pride leaves in anger when hope is gone.
ramacharitamanas::5013.simple_meaning: The monkeys returned to Ram after disrupting the sacrifice, and Ravana left in fury, no longer hoping to survive.
ramacharitamanas::5013.simple_insight: Some defeats end in rage before they end in surrender.
ramacharitamanas::5013.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman and the other monkeys have already broken Ravana's ritual and humiliated his side. This couplet simply marks the turning point: the monkeys return to Ram, while Ravana storms off in anger, his confidence collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::5013.modern_relevance: A project has gone wrong, the room is tense, and someone storms out after losing control. The verse captures that moment when pride turns into anger because hope has already cracked.
ramacharitamanas::5013.insight: It shifts attention from action to aftermath: victory gathers the righteous, while ego leaves in fury.

ramacharitamanas::5014.verse_sanskrit: चलत होहिं अति असुभ भयंकर। बैठहिं गीध उड़ाइ सिरन्ह पर॥ भयउ कालबस काहु न माना। कहेसि बजावहु जुद्ध निसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5014.verse_hindi: चलते समय अत्यंत भयंकर अमंगल (अपशकुन) होने लगे। गीध उड़-उड़कर उसके सिरों पर बैठने लगे, किन्तु वह काल के वश था, इससे किसी भी अपशकुन को नहीं मानता था। उसने कहा- युद्ध का डंका बजाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5014.english_translation: As he walked, terrible omens appeared. Vultures circled and sat on his heads, but he was under the sway of time and ignored every sign. He ordered the war drums to sound.
ramacharitamanas::5014.translation_literal: चलत (while walking) / होहिं (happen) / अति (very) / असुभ (inauspicious) / भयंकर (terrible) / बैठहिं (sit) / गीध (vultures) / उड़ाइ (flying) / सिरन्ह (on the heads) / पर (upon)॥ भयउ (became) / कालबस (under time's control) / काहु (any) / न (not) / माना (considered) / कहेसि (he said) / बजावहु (sound) / जुद्ध (war) / निसाना (drum)
ramacharitamanas::5014.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5014.essence: Pride can make even clear warning signs useless.
ramacharitamanas::5014.simple_meaning: Terrible signs appeared, but Ravana ignored them and ordered the war drums sounded.
ramacharitamanas::5014.simple_insight: When pride is in charge, even warning signs cannot reach you.
ramacharitamanas::5014.detailed_meaning: Ravana marches out after the failed attack on the sacrifice. As he moves, vultures gather overhead and other omens turn dark, but his mind is already seized by death and rage. Instead of stopping, he orders the drums of war.
ramacharitamanas::5014.modern_relevance: You keep pushing ahead after the warning lights come on, telling yourself it will be fine. By the time you admit the risk, the decision has already hardened.
ramacharitamanas::5014.insight: It shows how a mind captured by ego stops reading reality and rushes toward ruin.

ramacharitamanas::5015.verse_sanskrit: चली तमीचर अनी अपारा। बहु गज रथ पदाति असवारा॥ प्रभु सन्मुख धाए खल कैसें। सलभ समूह अनल कहँ जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::5015.verse_hindi: निशाचरों की अपार सेना चली। उसमें बहुत से हाथी, रथ, घुड़सवार और पैदल हैं। वे दुष्ट प्रभु के सामने कैसे दौड़े, जैसे पतंगों के समूह अग्नि की ओर (जलने के लिए) दौड़ते हैं॥।2॥
ramacharitamanas::5015.english_translation: The immense army of night-dwellers marched on, with many elephants, chariots, horsemen, and foot soldiers. How could those wicked ones rush before the Lord, like a swarm of moths racing into fire?
ramacharitamanas::5015.translation_literal: चली (marched) / तमीचर (night-dwellers) / अनी (army) / अपारा (boundless) / बहु (many) / गज (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / पदाति (foot soldiers) / असवारा (horsemen) / प्रभु (Lord) / सन्मुख (toward, before) / धाए (rushed) / खल (wicked ones) / कैसें (how) / सलभ (moths) / समूह (swarm) / अनल (fire) / कहँ (toward) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::5015.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5015.essence: Might can rush forward and still be helpless.
ramacharitamanas::5015.simple_meaning: Ravana's vast army advances with every kind of war machine and soldier, but its rush toward Ram is as futile as moths flying into fire.
ramacharitamanas::5015.simple_insight: Power can charge forward and still be completely helpless before what is greater.
ramacharitamanas::5015.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Ravana sends out his immense night-dwelling army with elephants, chariots, cavalry, and foot soldiers. The verse only paints the charge: the force, the scale, the arrogance. It sets up the next moment, where even that power looks tiny before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5015.modern_relevance: A room full of people may back the wrong choice, and the momentum can feel unstoppable. But sheer force does not make a thing wise, safe, or lasting.
ramacharitamanas::5015.insight: It shifts the mind from admiring raw force to seeing its fragility before a higher order.

ramacharitamanas::5016.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ देवतन्ह अस्तुति कीन्ही। दारुन बिपति हमहि एहिं दीन्ही॥ अब जनि राम खेलावहु एही। अतिसय दुखित होति बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5016.verse_hindi: इधर देवताओं ने स्तुति की कि हे श्री रामजी! इसने हमको दारुण दुःख दिए हैं। अब आप इसे (अधिक) न खेलाइए। जानकीजी बहुत ही दुःखी हो रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5016.english_translation: Here the gods offered praise: "This has brought us terrible suffering. Now do not keep playing with him; Sita is deeply distressed."
ramacharitamanas::5016.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / देवतन्ह (by the gods) / अस्तुति (praise) / कीन्ही (was done) / दारुन (terrible) / बिपति (trouble) / हमहि (to us) / एहिं (by this one) / दीन्ही (given)॥ / अब (now) / जनि (do not) / राम (Ram) / खेलावहु (keep playing) / एही (with this one) / अतिसय (very much) / दुखित (grieved) / होति (is becoming) / बैदेही (Sita)॥
ramacharitamanas::5016.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5016.simple_meaning: The gods praise Ram and ask him to stop prolonging Sita's suffering.
ramacharitamanas::5016.simple_insight: Even divine help can arrive with tenderness, not just power.
ramacharitamanas::5016.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, the gods watch Ram's intervention unfold and speak up in praise. They ask him not to delay any longer, because Sita is suffering deeply and the crisis has gone on too long.
ramacharitamanas::5016.modern_relevance: You finally have the chance to end a painful situation, and everyone is waiting for relief. The kindest move is not to stretch the moment any longer.
ramacharitamanas::5016.insight: It frames rescue as an act of compassion, not spectacle.

ramacharitamanas::5017.verse_sanskrit: देव बचन सुनि प्रभु मुसुकाना। उठि रघुबीर सुधारे बाना॥ जटा जूट दृढ़ बाँधें माथे। सोहहिं सुमन बीच बिच गाथे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5017.verse_hindi: देवताओं के वचन सुनकर प्रभु मुस्कुराए। फिर श्री रघुवीर ने उठकर बाण सुधारे। मस्तक पर जटाओं के जूड़े को कसकर बाँधे हुए हैं, उसके बीच-बीच में पुष्प गूँथे हुए शोभित हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5017.english_translation: Hearing the gods' words, the Lord smiled. Rising up, Raghubir adjusted his arrow. His matted hair was tightly bound on his head, with flowers woven through it, shining beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::5017.translation_literal: देव (the gods) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मुसुकाना (smiled) / उठि (rising) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सुधारे (adjusted, set right) / बाना (arrow) / जटा-जूट (matted hair knot) / दृढ़ (firmly) / बाँधें (bound) / माथे (on the head) / सोहहिं (are shining, look beautiful) / सुमन (flowers) / बीच-बिच (in between) / गाथे (woven)
ramacharitamanas::5017.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5017.essence: Calm strength prepares for action without losing gentleness.
ramacharitamanas::5017.simple_meaning: Ram smiles at the gods' plea, then prepares his bow and stands ready for battle, crowned with matted hair and flowers.
ramacharitamanas::5017.simple_insight: Real readiness can be calm. You can face conflict without losing your grace.
ramacharitamanas::5017.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, the gods beg Ram not to prolong the suffering. Ram answers with a smile, not anger. He rises, readies his bow, and stands in the warrior's form that will soon end Ravana's rule.
ramacharitamanas::5017.modern_relevance: When a tense message lands on your phone and your chest tightens, you can still pause, breathe, and respond without losing your center.
ramacharitamanas::5017.insight: It shows that strength and composure can belong to the same moment.

ramacharitamanas::5018.verse_sanskrit: अरुन नयन बारिद तनु स्यामा। अखिल लोक लोचनाभिरामा॥ कटितट परिकर कस्यो निषंगा। कर कोदंड कठिन सारंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5018.verse_hindi: लाल नेत्र और मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर वाले और संपूर्ण लोकों के नेत्रों को आनंद देने वाले हैं। प्रभु ने कमर में फेंटा तथा तरकस कस लिया और हाथ में कठोर शार्गं धनुष ले लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5018.english_translation: His eyes were red, his body dark like rainclouds, and he delighted the eyes of all the worlds. He tightened the belt at his waist, fastened his quiver, and took up the hard Saranga bow in his hand.
ramacharitamanas::5018.translation_literal: अरुन (red) / नयन (eyes) / बारिद (cloud) / तनु (body) / स्यामा (dark) / अखिल (all) / लोक (worlds) / लोचनाभिरामा (delighting the eyes) / कटितट (waist) / परिकर (belt) / कस्यो (tightened) / निषंगा (quiver) / कर (hand) / कोदंड (bow) / कठिन (hard) / सारंगा (Saranga)
ramacharitamanas::5018.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5018.essence: True readiness is calm, beautiful, and already armed.
ramacharitamanas::5018.simple_meaning: Ram is described as beautiful and ready for battle. He tightens his belt and quiver, then lifts his bow.
ramacharitamanas::5018.simple_insight: Even in war, his presence is calm, beautiful, and fully prepared.
ramacharitamanas::5018.detailed_meaning: After the gods praise Ram and ask him to stop Ravana’s cruelty, Ram rises in response. Tulsidas lingers on his form: dark as rainclouds, red-eyed, radiant, and fully armed. This is the moment before action begins.
ramacharitamanas::5018.modern_relevance: You pause before a hard conversation, straighten your clothes, and take one steady breath. Readiness can be quiet, beautiful, and complete.
ramacharitamanas::5018.insight: It shifts attention from drama to composed readiness before decisive action.

ramacharitamanas::5019.verse_sanskrit: सारंग कर सुंदर निषंग सिलीमुखाकर कटि कस्यो। भुजदंड पीन मनोहरायत उर धरासुर पद लस्यो॥ कह दास तुलसी जबहिं प्रभु सर चाप कर फेरन लगे। ब्रह्मांड दिग्गज कमठ अहि महि सिंधु भूधर डगमगे॥
ramacharitamanas::5019.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने हाथ में शार्गं धनुष लेकर कमर में बाणों की खान (अक्षय) सुंदर तरकस कस लिया। उनके भुजदण्ड पुष्ट हैं और मनोहर चौड़ी छाती पर ब्राह्मण (भृगुजी) के चरण का चिह्न शोभित है। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं, ज्यों ही प्रभु धनुष-बाण हाथ में लेकर फिराने लगे, त्यों ही ब्रह्माण्ड, दिशाओं के हाथी, कच्छप, शेषजी, पृथ्वी, समुद्र और पर्वत सभी डगमगा उठे।
ramacharitamanas::5019.english_translation: He took the beautiful Saranga bow and the quiver of arrows at his waist. His powerful arms were lovely, and the mark of the brahmin's feet shone on his broad chest. Tulsidas says that as soon as the Lord began to turn the bow and arrow in his hands, the universe, the guardians of the directions, the cosmic turtle, Shesha, the earth, the ocean, and the mountains all trembled.
ramacharitamanas::5019.translation_literal: सारंग (Saranga bow) / कर (in hand) / सुंदर (beautiful) / निषंग (quiver) / सिलीमुखाकर (arrow-store) / कटि (waist) / कस्यो (fastened) / भुजदंड (arms) / पीन (strong) / मनोहरायत (beautifully broad) / उर (chest) / धरासुर (brahmin's feet) / पद (feet) / लस्यो (shone) / कह (says) / दास तुलसी (servant Tulsidas) / जबहिं (as soon as) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सर (arrow) / चाप (bow) / कर (hand) / फेरन (to turn) / लगे (began) / ब्रह्मांड (universe) / दिग्गज (direction-elephants) / कमठ (cosmic turtle) / अहि (Shesha serpent) / महि (earth) / सिंधु (ocean) / भूधर (mountains) / डगमगे (trembled)
ramacharitamanas::5019.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5019.essence: Ram's smallest movement reveals a power that shakes the cosmos.
ramacharitamanas::5019.simple_meaning: Ram takes up his bow and arrows, and the whole cosmos trembles at the sight of his power.
ramacharitamanas::5019.simple_insight: True strength does not need to announce itself; it changes everything around it the moment it moves.
ramacharitamanas::5019.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, just before the war turns decisive, Ram stands fully armed. Tulsidas lingers on his beauty, strength, and sacred marks, then shows the universe itself trembling when Ram handles his weapons. The verse magnifies his divine force.
ramacharitamanas::5019.modern_relevance: You watch someone calm and unhurried walk into the room, and the mood shifts before they speak. Some presence carries weight without noise.
ramacharitamanas::5019.insight: It shifts attention from visible action to the power beneath it: Ram's mere movement reveals cosmic authority.

ramacharitamanas::5020.verse_sanskrit: सोभा देखि हरषि सुर बरषहिं सुमन अपार। जय जय जय करुनानिधि छबि बल गुन आगार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5020.verse_hindi: (भगवान् की) शोभा देखकर देवता हर्षित होकर फूलों की अपार वर्षा करने लगे और शोभा, शक्ति और गुणों के धाम करुणानिधान प्रभु की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो (ऐसा पुकारने लगे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5020.english_translation: Seeing his splendor, the devas rejoiced and showered endless flowers. "Victory, victory, victory to the compassionate one, the source of beauty, strength, and virtues!"
ramacharitamanas::5020.translation_literal: सोभा (splendor) / देखि (seeing) / हरषि (rejoiced) / सुर (devas) / बरषहिं (shower) / सुमन (flowers) / अपार (endless) / जय (victory) / जय (victory) / जय (victory) / करुनानिधि (compassionate one) / छबि (beauty) / बल (strength) / गुन (virtues) / आगार (source)
ramacharitamanas::5020.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5020.essence: His presence makes praise the only possible response.
ramacharitamanas::5020.simple_meaning: The devas are so moved by Ram's beauty that they shower flowers and praise him as the compassionate source of beauty, strength, and virtue.
ramacharitamanas::5020.simple_insight: Some presence is so whole that praise feels like the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::5020.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram stands ready for battle, radiant and unshaken. The devas look on from above, overwhelmed by his splendor, and answer with flowers and cries of victory. It is a brief moment of divine recognition before the war surges forward.
ramacharitamanas::5020.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension changes before you speak. Sometimes the calm, strength, and kindness you carry announce themselves more clearly than words.
ramacharitamanas::5020.insight: It frames true greatness as something that naturally draws reverence, not self-display.

ramacharitamanas::5021.verse_sanskrit: एहीं बीच निसाचर अनी। कसमसात आई अति घनी॥ देखि चले सन्मुख कपि भट्टा। प्रलयकाल के जनु घन घट्टा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5021.verse_hindi: इसी बीच में निशाचरों की अत्यंत घनी सेना कसमसाती हुई (आपस में टकराती हुई) आई। उसे देखकर वानर योद्धा इस प्रकार (उसके) सामने चले जैसे प्रलयकाल के बादलों के समूह हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5021.english_translation: In that moment, the demon army surged forward in a dense, crashing mass. Seeing it, the monkey warriors advanced like clouds at the end of cosmic dissolution.
ramacharitamanas::5021.translation_literal: एहीं बीच (in that moment) / निसाचर (demons) / अनी (army) / कसमसात (jostling, crashing) / आई (came) / अति घनी (very dense)॥ / देखि (seeing) / चले (moved) / सन्मुख (toward, face-to-face) / कपि भट्टा (monkey warriors)॥ / प्रलयकाल (time of dissolution) / के (of) / जनु (as if) / घन (clouds) / घट्टा (mass, cluster) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5021.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5021.essence: The two armies meet like storm clouds before the end.
ramacharitamanas::5021.simple_meaning: The demon army rushes in, and the monkey warriors move to meet it head-on like storm clouds before destruction.
ramacharitamanas::5021.simple_insight: Some moments demand presence, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::5021.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana's forces surge forward in thick ranks. The monkey warriors answer without flinching, advancing to meet the charge. The verse is a scene of momentum and clash, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5021.insight: It sets the battle in motion and shows both armies closing in without delay.

ramacharitamanas::5022.verse_sanskrit: बहु कृपान तरवारि चमंकहिं। जनु दहँ दिसि दामिनीं दमंकहिं॥ गज रथ तुरग चिकार कठोरा। गर्जहिं मनहुँ बलाहक घोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5022.verse_hindi: बहुत से कृपाल और तलवारें चमक रही हैं। मानो दसों दिशाओं में बिजलियाँ चमक रही हों। हाथी, रथ और घोड़ों का कठोर चिंग्घाड़ ऐसा लगता है मानो बादल भयंकर गर्जन कर रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5022.english_translation: Many spears and swords flash like lightning in all ten directions. Elephants, chariots, and horses cry out harshly, as if dark clouds were thundering.
ramacharitamanas::5022.translation_literal: बहु (many) / कृपान (spears) / तरवारि (swords) / चमंकहिं (flash) / जनु (as if) / दहँ दिसि (ten directions) / दामिनीं (lightning) / दमंकहिं (flash) / गज (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / तुरग (horses) / चिकार (cries) / कठोरा (harsh) / गर्जहिं (roar) / मनहुँ (as if) / बलाहक (clouds) / घोरा (dark, fierce)
ramacharitamanas::5022.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5022.essence: War arrives like a storm of flashing steel and thunder.
ramacharitamanas::5022.simple_meaning: Weapons flash everywhere while elephants, chariots, and horses thunder and cry out. The battlefield feels like a storm made of metal and noise.
ramacharitamanas::5022.simple_insight: The scene feels overwhelming because war turns movement, sound, and fear into one force.
ramacharitamanas::5022.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana's forces surge forward in a mass of weapons, elephants, chariots, and horses. The poet pauses on the sensory chaos before the clash, making the army feel like a storm rolling toward Hanuman's side.
ramacharitamanas::5022.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded station at rush hour: horns, shouting, flashing screens, bodies moving everywhere. Before anything even happens, the whole place already feels like pressure.
ramacharitamanas::5022.insight: It turns battle into a sensory image so the reader feels its scale before the fighting begins.

ramacharitamanas::5023.verse_sanskrit: कपि लंगूर बिपुल नभ छाए। मनहुँ इंद्रधनु उए सुहाए॥ उठइ धूरि मानहुँ जलधारा। बान बुंद भै बृष्टि अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5023.verse_hindi: वानरों की बहुत सी पूँछें आकाश में छाई हुई हैं। (वे ऐसी शोभा दे रही हैं) मानो सुंदर इंद्रधनुष उदय हुए हों। धूल ऐसी उठ रही है मानो जल की धारा हो। बाण रूपी बूँदों की अपार वृष्टि हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5023.english_translation: The monkeys' tails filled the sky like beautiful rainbows. Dust rose like a stream of water, and arrows fell in an endless shower.
ramacharitamanas::5023.translation_literal: कपि (monkeys) / लंगूर (tails) / बिपुल (many, vast) / नभ (sky) / छाए (covered) / मनहुँ (as if) / इंद्रधनु (rainbows) / उए (rose) / सुहाए (beautiful) / उठइ (rises) / धूरि (dust) / मानहुँ (as if) / जलधारा (stream of water) / बान (arrows) / बुंद (drops) / भै (became) / बृष्टि (rainfall) / अपारा (endless)
ramacharitamanas::5023.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5023.essence: The battlefield becomes a storm of motion and color.
ramacharitamanas::5023.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so crowded and intense that monkey tails seem to fill the sky, dust looks like flowing water, and arrows fall like heavy rain.
ramacharitamanas::5023.simple_insight: The scene overwhelms the senses, showing how vast and fierce the battle has become.
ramacharitamanas::5023.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army surges forward and the war turns almost surreal. Tails, dust, and arrows blur the battlefield into a storm of motion. This verse is vivid scene-setting, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5023.modern_relevance: A stadium erupts, dust rises from the ground, flags whip overhead, and the noise turns everything into motion. You feel the whole place become one living surge.
ramacharitamanas::5023.insight: It shifts attention from individual fighters to the scale and chaos of the battle.

ramacharitamanas::5024.verse_sanskrit: दुहुँ दिसि पर्बत करहिं प्रहारा। बज्रपात जनु बारहिं बारा॥ रघुपति कोपि बान झरि लाई। घायल भै निसिचर समुदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5024.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर से योद्धा पर्वतों का प्रहार करते हैं। मानो बारंबार वज्रपात हो रहा हो। श्री रघुनाथजी ने क्रोध करके बाणों की झड़ी लगा दी, (जिससे) राक्षसों की सेना घायल हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5024.english_translation: On both sides, warriors hurl mountain-like blows, as if thunderbolts are striking again and again. Lord Raghunath grew fierce and sent a rain of arrows, and the demon army was wounded.
ramacharitamanas::5024.translation_literal: दुहुँ दिसि (on both sides) / पर्बत (mountain) / करहिं (they do) / प्रहारा (strikes) / बज्रपात (thunderbolt-strike) / जनु (as if) / बारहिं बारा (again and again) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कोपि (having become fierce) / बान (arrows) / झरि (a shower) / लाई (sent) / घायल (wounded) / भै (became) / निसिचर (demon) / समुदाई (host)
ramacharitamanas::5024.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5024.essence: Decisive force can break a chaos that force alone created.
ramacharitamanas::5024.simple_meaning: The battle grows more intense on both sides, and Ram answers the enemy attack with a fierce rain of arrows that wounds their army.
ramacharitamanas::5024.simple_insight: Sometimes the moment calls for direct force, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::5024.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is in full swing. Mountain blows crash from both sides like repeated thunderbolts, and then Ram turns fierce and releases a shower of arrows. This is the battlefield turning point where the demon army begins to suffer.
ramacharitamanas::5024.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a crisis call, messages flying, everyone talking over each other. Then you stop hesitating, choose a response, and the whole situation changes.
ramacharitamanas::5024.insight: It shifts the mind from passive watching to decisive response under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::5025.verse_sanskrit: लागत बान बीर चिक्करहीं। घुर्मि घुर्मि जहँ तहँ महि परहीं॥ स्रवहिं सैल जनु निर्झर भारी। सोनित सरि कादर भयकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5025.verse_hindi: बाण लगते ही वीर चीत्कार कर उठते हैं और चक्कर खा-खाकर जहाँ-तहाँ पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ते हैं। उनके शरीर से ऐसे खून बह रहा है मानो पर्वत के भारी झरनों से जल बह रहा हो। इस प्रकार डरपोकों को भय उत्पन्न करने वाली रुधिर की नदी बह चली ॥
ramacharitamanas::5025.english_translation: As the arrows strike, the warriors cry out and reel to the ground. Their blood flows like a mountain stream, and a fearsome river of blood runs forth.
ramacharitamanas::5025.translation_literal: लागत (striking) / बान (arrows) / बीर (warriors) / चिक्करहीं (cry out) / घुर्मि घुर्मि (reeling and spinning) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / महि (earth) / परहीं (fall) / स्रवहिं (flow) / सैल (mountain) / जनु (as if) / निर्झर (stream) / भारी (great) / सोनित (blood) / सरि (river) / कादर (timid) / भयकारी (fearsome)
ramacharitamanas::5025.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5025.essence: War turns bodies into a rushing river of blood.
ramacharitamanas::5025.simple_meaning: Arrows strike the warriors, they cry out and fall, and blood pours across the battlefield like a mountain stream.
ramacharitamanas::5025.simple_insight: The scene is meant to overwhelm you with the cost and force of war.
ramacharitamanas::5025.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, arrows are tearing through the enemy ranks. Warriors scream, stagger, and collapse as blood runs everywhere. The verse is not teaching a principle; it is intensifying the war scene before the next image of the battlefield river.
ramacharitamanas::5025.insight: It sharpens the battlefield into a vivid image of collapse and terror.

ramacharitamanas::5026.verse_sanskrit: कादर भयंकर रुधिर सरिता चली परम अपावनी। दोउ कूल दल रथ रेत चक्र अबर्त बहति भयावनी॥ जलजंतु गज पदचर तुरग खर बिबिध बाहन को गने। सर सक्ति तोमर सर्प चाप तरंग चर्म कमठ घने॥
ramacharitamanas::5026.verse_hindi: डरपोकों को भय उपजाने वाली अत्यंत अपवित्र रक्त की नदी बह चली। दोनों दल उसके दोनों किनारे हैं। रथ रेत है और पहिए भँवर हैं। वह नदी बहुत भयावनी बह रही है। हाथी, पैदल, घोड़े, गदहे तथा अनेकों सवारियाँ ही, जिनकी गिनती कौन करे, नदी के जल जन्तु हैं। बाण, शक्ति और तोमर सर्प हैं, धनुष तरंगें हैं और ढाल बहुत से कछुवे हैं।
ramacharitamanas::5026.english_translation: A terrifying, impure river of blood began to flow. The two armies became its two banks; chariots were sand and wheels were whirlpools. It flowed fearfully. Elephants, foot soldiers, horses, donkeys, and countless mounts became its water-creatures. Arrows, spears, tridents, snakes, bows, waves, shields, and many turtles filled it.
ramacharitamanas::5026.translation_literal: कादर (fearful/for the timid) / भयंकर (terrifying) / रुधिर (blood) / सरिता (river) / चली (flowed) / परम (extremely) / अपावनी (impure) / दोउ (both) / कूल (banks) / दल (armies) / रथ (chariots) / रेत (sand) / चक्र (wheels) / अबर्त (whirlpools) / बहति (flowing) / भयावनी (fearsome) / जलजंतु (water-creatures) / गज (elephants) / पदचर (foot soldiers) / तुरग (horses) / खर (donkeys) / बिबिध (various) / बाहन (mounts) / को (of) / गने (counted) / सर (arrows) / सक्ति (spears) / तोमर (tridents) / सर्प (snakes) / चाप (bows) / तरंग (waves) / चर्म (shields) / तर (turtles) / कमठ (turtles) / घने (many)
ramacharitamanas::5026.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5026.essence: War has become a river of blood that swallows everything.
ramacharitamanas::5026.simple_meaning: The battlefield is compared to a terrifying river made of blood, weapons, bodies, and wreckage.
ramacharitamanas::5026.simple_insight: War is shown as total chaos, where everything living and made becomes part of the same destruction.
ramacharitamanas::5026.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is raging so fiercely that the poet stops describing strategy and turns the battlefield into an image of a blood river. Armies, chariots, weapons, animals, and fallen warriors are all folded into one horrifying scene.
ramacharitamanas::5026.modern_relevance: After a fight explodes in a crowded street, broken glass, shouting, and sirens blur together. Nothing looks orderly anymore; everything feels swept into the same violence.
ramacharitamanas::5026.insight: It turns battle into a single overwhelming image of collapse, not a series of separate actions.

ramacharitamanas::5027.verse_sanskrit: बीर परहिं जनु तीर तरु मज्जा बहु बह फेन। कादर देखि डरहिं तहँ सुभटन्ह के मन चेन ॥
ramacharitamanas::5027.verse_hindi: वीर पृथ्वी पर इस तरह गिर रहे हैं, मानो नदी-किनारे के वृक्ष ढह रहे हों। बहुत सी मज्जा बह रही है, वही फेन है। डरपोक जहाँ इसे देखकर डरते हैं, वहाँ उत्तम योद्धाओं के मन में सुख होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5027.english_translation: Heroes fall like trees on a riverbank; their marrow flows like foam. Cowards are afraid, but brave hearts find comfort there.
ramacharitamanas::5027.translation_literal: बीर (heroes) / परहिं (fall) / जनु (as if) / तीर (riverbank) / तरु (trees) / मज्जा (marrow) / बहु (much) / बह (flows) / फेन (foam) / कादर (cowards) / देखि (seeing) / डरहिं (are afraid) / तहँ (there) / सुभटन्ह (for brave warriors) / के (of) / मन (minds) / चेन (comfort)
ramacharitamanas::5027.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5027.essence: The same battlefield frightens the timid and steadies the brave.
ramacharitamanas::5027.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so fierce that fallen warriors look like trees collapsing by a river. Cowards are terrified by it, but true warriors feel calm and steady there.
ramacharitamanas::5027.simple_insight: Courage changes what the same scene means: terror for one person, steadiness for another.
ramacharitamanas::5027.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has turned brutal. Bodies fall, blood and marrow flood the ground, and the scene is compared to a riverbank stripped of trees. Tulsidas lingers on the contrast between fear and heroic composure.
ramacharitamanas::5027.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a brutal argument and feel your stomach tighten. Someone else stays calm, seeing the same chaos without flinching.
ramacharitamanas::5027.insight: It shows how courage reshapes perception, letting you remain steady in the middle of violence or crisis.

ramacharitamanas::5028.verse_sanskrit: मज्जहिं भूत पिसाच बेताला। प्रमथ महा झोटिंग कराला॥ काक कंक लै भुजा उड़ाहीं। एक ते छीनि एक लै खाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5028.verse_hindi: भूत, पिशाच और बेताल, बड़े-बड़े झोंटों वाले महान् भयंकर झोटिंग और प्रमथ (शिवगण) उस नदी में स्नान करते हैं। कौए और चील भुजाएँ लेकर उड़ते हैं और एक-दूसरे से छीनकर खा जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5028.english_translation: Ghosts, fiends, and wandering spirits bathe there. Fierce, wild Shiva-attendants too. Crows and vultures fly off with arms, snatching them from one another and eating them.
ramacharitamanas::5028.translation_literal: मज्जहिं (bathe) / भूत (ghosts) / पिसाच (fiends) / बेताला (wandering spirits) / प्रमथ (Shiva-attendants) / महा (great) / झोटिंग (wild ones) / कराला (fierce) / काक (crows) / कंक (vultures) / लै (taking) / भुजा (arms) / उड़ाहीं (fly away) / एक ते (from one) / छीनि (snatching) / एक लै (one taking) / खाहीं (eat)
ramacharitamanas::5028.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5028.essence: Violence has made the battlefield feel inhabited by death itself.
ramacharitamanas::5028.simple_meaning: The battlefield has become so horrific that even ghosts, spirits, and fierce beings seem to swarm there. Birds snatch body parts from the dead as the carnage continues.
ramacharitamanas::5028.simple_insight: This is not a place for glory anymore; it is a scene of total ruin.
ramacharitamanas::5028.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka has turned the ground into a river of blood and remains. Tulsidas piles up terrifying images—spirits, fierce attendants, crows, vultures—to show how completely violence has swallowed the field. This verse deepens the battlefield horror, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5028.modern_relevance: A news clip shows smoke, sirens, and bodies carried past broken walls. You stop looking for winners because the damage has already outgrown victory.
ramacharitamanas::5028.insight: It shifts attention from combat as heroics to combat as devastation.

ramacharitamanas::5029.verse_sanskrit: एक कहहिं ऐसिउ सौंघाई। सठहु तुम्हार दरिद्र न जाई॥ कहँरत भट घायल तट गिरे। जहँ तहँ मनहुँ अर्धजल परे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5029.verse_hindi: एक (कोई) कहते हैं, अरे मूर्खों! ऐसी सस्ती (बहुतायत) है, फिर भी तुम्हारी दरिद्रता नहीं जाती? घायल योद्धा तट पर पड़े कराह रहे हैं, मानो जहाँ-तहाँ अर्धजल (वे व्यक्ति जो मरने के समय आधे जल में रखे जाते हैं) पड़े हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5029.english_translation: Someone says, “Fools, is the abundance still not enough to end your poverty?” Wounded warriors lie groaning on the shore, as if half-submerged bodies were scattered everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::5029.translation_literal: एक (someone) / कहहिं (say) / ऐसिउ (even so, this much) / सौंघाई (cheap abundance) / सठहु (fools) / तुम्हार (your) / दरिद्र (poverty) / न जाई (does not go away) / कहँरत (groaning) / भट (warriors) / घायल (wounded) / तट (shore) / गिरे (fallen) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / मनहुँ (as if) / अर्धजल (half-submerged bodies) / परे (lying)
ramacharitamanas::5029.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5029.essence: War leaves so much ruin that even speech turns bitter.
ramacharitamanas::5029.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so full of wounded men that someone mockingly asks why poverty still remains. The shore looks scattered with half-submerged bodies.
ramacharitamanas::5029.simple_insight: It shows how war turns human bodies into debris, and how cruelly people can speak even amid ruin.
ramacharitamanas::5029.detailed_meaning: On the banks of Lanka, the battle has become grotesque. Wounded warriors lie groaning on the shore, while others mock the scene as if the abundance of bodies should somehow end poverty. The verse is part of a grim battlefield description.
ramacharitamanas::5029.modern_relevance: You scroll past headlines of another disaster, and the language starts to sound numb. This verse catches that coldness: suffering becomes so common that even pity can turn sarcastic.
ramacharitamanas::5029.insight: It pulls attention back to the cost of violence, not the spectacle of victory.

ramacharitamanas::5030.verse_sanskrit: खैचहिं गीध आँत तट भए। जनु बंसी खेलत चित दए॥ बहु भट बहहिं चढ़े खग जाहीं। जनु नावरि खेलहिं सरि माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5030.verse_hindi: गीध आँतें खींच रहे हैं, मानो मछली मार नदी तट पर से चित्त लगाए हुए (ध्यानस्थ होकर) बंसी खेल रहे हों (बंसी से मछली पकड़ रहे हों)। बहुत से योद्धा बहे जा रहे हैं और पक्षी उन पर चढ़े चले जा रहे हैं। मानो वे नदी में नावरि (नौका क्रीड़ा) खेल रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5030.english_translation: Vultures pull out intestines at the riverbank, as if calmly fishing with a rod. Many warriors float by while birds climb over them, as if they are playing on boats in the river.
ramacharitamanas::5030.translation_literal: खैचहिं (pull out) / गीध (vultures) / आँत (intestines) / तट (riverbank) / भए (having become) / जनु (as if) / बंसी (fishing rod) / खेलत (playing) / चित दए (with attention given) / बहु (many) / भट (warriors) / बहहिं (float, are carried away) / चढ़े (climbing, mounted) / खग (birds) / जाहीं (go) / जनु (as if) / नावरि (boat play) / खेलहिं (play) / सरि (river) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::5030.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5030.essence: War leaves only feeding birds and broken bodies behind.
ramacharitamanas::5030.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so full of death that vultures and birds feed on bodies as if they are casually playing by the river.
ramacharitamanas::5030.simple_insight: It strips war of glory and shows only its brutal aftermath.
ramacharitamanas::5030.detailed_meaning: On the banks of Lanka's battlefield, the dead and dying lie everywhere. Vultures tear into bodies while birds settle on floating warriors. The scene is meant to overwhelm the reader with the sheer horror and collapse of the war.
ramacharitamanas::5030.modern_relevance: A news feed full of casualty numbers can feel abstract until you picture one body, one family, one loss. This verse refuses abstraction and makes destruction impossible to romanticize.
ramacharitamanas::5030.insight: It turns the mind away from heroic fantasy and toward the real cost of violence.

ramacharitamanas::5031.verse_sanskrit: जोगिनि भरि भरि खप्पर संचहिं। भूति पिसाच बधू नभ नंचहिं॥ भट कपाल करताल बजावहिं। चामुंडा नाना बिधि गावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5031.verse_hindi: योगिनियाँ खप्परों में भर-भरकर खून जमा कर रही हैं। भूत-पिशाचों की स्त्रियाँ आकाश में नाच रही हैं। चामुण्डाएँ योद्धाओं की खोपड़ियों का करताल बजा रही हैं और नाना प्रकार से गा रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5031.english_translation: The yoginis gather blood in their skull-bowls. The wives of ghosts and spirits dance in the sky. The warriors beat skulls like cymbals, and the Chamundas sing in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::5031.translation_literal: जोगिनि (yoginis) / भरि भरि (again and again, full) / खप्पर (skull-bowl) / संचहिं (collect) / भूति (ghosts) / पिसाच (spirits) / बधू (wives) / नभ (sky) / नंचहिं (dance) / भट (warriors) / कपाल (skull) / करताल (cymbals) / बजावहिं (play) / चामुंडा (Chamunda beings) / नाना बिधि (in many ways) / गावहिं (sing)
ramacharitamanas::5031.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5031.essence: Violence fills the world with grotesque celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5031.simple_meaning: The scene turns grotesque and chaotic: blood, skulls, spirits, and wild dancing fill the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::5031.simple_insight: Sometimes violence makes the world look possessed, not victorious.
ramacharitamanas::5031.detailed_meaning: On the Lankakand battlefield, the slaughter has become so extreme that Tulsidas describes it as a nightmarish spectacle. Spirits, skulls, and dancing figures crowd the sky, showing how war has dissolved order into horror.
ramacharitamanas::5031.modern_relevance: A news feed full of wreckage, sirens, and footage of chaos can feel unreal, almost theatrical. This verse captures that sickening moment when destruction stops looking human.
ramacharitamanas::5031.insight: It turns battle into a vision of disorder, making the cost of violence impossible to ignore.

ramacharitamanas::5032.verse_sanskrit: जंबुक निकर कटक्कट कट्टहिं। खाहिं हुआहिं अघाहिं दपट्टहिं॥ कोटिन्ह रुंड मुंड बिनु डोल्लहिं। सीस परे महि जय जय बोल्लहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5032.verse_hindi: गीदड़ों के समूह कट-कट शब्द करते हुए मुरदों को काटते, खाते, हुआँ-हुआँ करते और पेट भर जाने पर एक-दूसरे को डाँटते हैं। करोड़ों धड़ बिना सिर के घूम रहे हैं और सिर पृथ्वी पर पड़े जय-जय बोल रहे है ॥ छंद :
ramacharitamanas::5032.english_translation: The jackals make a crackling sound as they tear and eat the dead, growling and snapping after they have had enough. Countless headless bodies roam about, while heads fallen on the ground shout, “Victory! Victory!”
ramacharitamanas::5032.translation_literal: जंबुक (jackals) / निकर (crowd) / कटक्कट (crackling sound) / कट्टहिं (tear, cut) / खाहिं (eat) / हुआहिं (growl) / अघाहिं (having had enough) / दपट्टहिं (snap, snarl) ॥ कोटिन्ह (millions) / रुंड (headless bodies) / मुंड (heads) / बिनु (without) / डोल्लहिं (roam, move) / सीस (heads) / परे (fallen) / महि (on the ground) / जय जय (victory, victory) / बोल्लहिं (shout)
ramacharitamanas::5032.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5032.essence: Violence keeps moving after victory has already been lost.
ramacharitamanas::5032.simple_meaning: The battlefield is so ruined that jackals feed on the dead, and even severed heads seem to cry victory. It is a scene of total collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5032.simple_insight: Some victories leave behind only noise, ruin, and bodies.
ramacharitamanas::5032.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, the battlefield has become grotesque beyond measure. Jackals feed among the fallen, headless bodies wander, and severed heads still cry out in chaos. The verse heightens the horror before the fighting continues.
ramacharitamanas::5032.insight: It strips away the glamour of war and shows only its emptiness and destruction.

ramacharitamanas::5033.verse_sanskrit: बोल्लहिं जो जय जय मुंड रुंड प्रचंड सिर बिनु धावहीं। खप्परिन्ह खग्ग अलुज्झि जुज्झहिं सुभट भटन्ह ढहावहीं॥ बानर निसाचर निकर मर्दहिं राम बल दर्पित भए। संग्राम अंगन सुभट सोवहिं राम सर निकरन्हि हए॥
ramacharitamanas::5033.verse_hindi: मुण्ड (कटे सिर) जय-जय बोल बोलते हैं और प्रचण्ड रुण्ड (धड़) बिना सिर के दौड़ते हैं। पक्षी खोपड़ियों में उलझ-उलझकर परस्पर लड़े मरते हैं, उत्तम योद्धा दूसरे योद्धाओं को ढहा रहे हैं। श्री रामचंद्रजी बल से दर्पित हुए वानर राक्षसों के झुंडों को मसले डालते हैं। श्री रामजी के बाण समूहों से मरे हुए योद्धा लड़ाई के मैदान में सो रहे हैं।
ramacharitamanas::5033.english_translation: Heads shout victory, and fierce headless trunks run on. Birds clash in skulls and warriors strike one another down. Monkeys and demons crush each other, swollen with Ram's power. On the battlefield, brave fighters lie as if asleep, struck by Ram's arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5033.translation_literal: बोल्लहिं (shout) / जो (who) / जय जय (victory victory) / मुंड (heads) / रुंड (trunks) / प्रचंड (fierce) / सिर (head) / बिनु (without) / धावहीं (run) / खप्परिन्ह (with skulls) / खग्ग (birds) / अलुज्झि (entangled) / जुज्झहिं (fight) / सुभट (brave warriors) / भटन्ह (warriors) / ढहावहीं (bring down)॥ / बानर (monkeys) / निसाचर (demons) / निकर (groups) / मर्दहिं (crush) / राम (Ram) / बल (power) / दर्पित (filled with pride/power) / भए (became) / संग्राम (battle) / अंगन (arena) / सुभट (brave warriors) / सोवहिं (sleep) / राम (Ram) / सर (arrows) / निकरन्हि (by groups) / हए (struck down)
ramacharitamanas::5033.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5033.essence: Ram's force leaves the battlefield stunned and still.
ramacharitamanas::5033.simple_meaning: The battlefield is full of violent, surreal destruction. Ram's arrows and power are overwhelming the enemy, and warriors lie fallen everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::5033.simple_insight: Some fights are so complete that resistance itself looks like sleep.
ramacharitamanas::5033.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final war, the battlefield has become a nightmare of shattered bodies and chaos. The poet shows demons, monkeys, and warriors collapsing under Ram's force. This is not teaching but vivid aftermath, heightening the terror and scale of the battle.
ramacharitamanas::5033.insight: It presents war as total collapse, not heroic spectacle.

ramacharitamanas::5034.verse_sanskrit: रावन हृदयँ बिचारा भा निसिचर संघार। मैं अकेल कपि भालु बहु माया करौं अपार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5034.verse_hindi: रावण ने हृदय में विचारा कि राक्षसों का नाश हो गया है। मैं अकेला हूँ और वानर-भालू बहुत हैं, इसलिए मैं अब अपार माया रचूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5034.english_translation: Ravana thought in his heart: the demons have been destroyed. I am alone, while the monkeys and bears are many, so now I will create immense illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5034.translation_literal: रावन (Ravana) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारा (thought) / भा (became) / निसिचर (demons) / संघार (destruction) / मैं (I) / अकेल (alone) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / बहु (many) / माया (illusion) / करौं (I will do) / अपार (vast)
ramacharitamanas::5034.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5034.essence: When fear takes over, deception feels like strength.
ramacharitamanas::5034.simple_meaning: Ravana sees that his army is gone and he is outnumbered, so he turns to deception to keep fighting.
ramacharitamanas::5034.simple_insight: Panic can make the mind reach for tricks instead of courage.
ramacharitamanas::5034.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana watches his forces collapse as the monkeys and bears keep advancing. Cornered and alone, he does not surrender or reflect. He immediately plans a huge deception, showing how ego under pressure turns to illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5034.modern_relevance: You realize your plan is failing, your team is shrinking, and instead of facing it cleanly, you start patching with half-truths and spin.
ramacharitamanas::5034.insight: It shows how a threatened ego chooses manipulation when honest response would demand humility.

ramacharitamanas::5035.verse_sanskrit: देवन्ह प्रभुहि पयादें देखा। उपजा उर अति छोभ बिसेषा॥ सुरपति निज रथ तुरत पठावा। हरष सहित मातलि लै आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5035.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने प्रभु को पैदल (बिना सवारी के युद्ध करते) देखा, तो उनके हृदय में बड़ा भारी क्षोभ (दुःख) उत्पन्न हुआ। (फिर क्या था) इंद्र ने तुरंत अपना रथ भेज दिया। (उसका सारथी) मातलि हर्ष के साथ उसे ले आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5035.english_translation: The devas saw the Lord fighting on foot and felt deep distress. Then Indra quickly sent his chariot, and Matali brought it joyfully.
ramacharitamanas::5035.translation_literal: देवन्ह (the devas) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / पयादें (on foot) / देखा (saw) / उपजा (arose) / उर (in the heart) / अति (very) / छोभ (distress) / बिसेषा (great) / सुरपति (lord of the devas) / निज (own) / रथ (chariot) / तुरत (quickly) / पठावा (sent) / हरष (joy) / सहित (with) / मातलि (Matali) / लै (bringing) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::5035.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5035.essence: Even the victorious need help before the battle is over.
ramacharitamanas::5035.simple_meaning: The devas saw Ram fighting without a chariot and felt concern. Indra immediately sent his chariot, and Matali brought it with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5035.simple_insight: Even the higher beings respond when courage is carrying too much alone.
ramacharitamanas::5035.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ram is still fighting on foot while the devas watch from above. Seeing him take on the burden alone, they are moved to distress. Indra then sends his chariot, and Matali brings it to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5035.modern_relevance: You keep doing everything yourself while everyone else watches. Then someone finally notices the load and steps in before you collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5035.insight: It shows that true strength can still need support, and support can arrive as soon as it is seen.

ramacharitamanas::5036.verse_sanskrit: तेज पुंज रथ दिब्य अनूपा। हरषि चढ़े कोसलपुर भूपा॥ चंचल तुरग मनोहर चारी। अजर अमर मन सम गतिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5036.verse_hindi: उस दिव्य अनुपम और तेज के पुंज (तेजोमय) रथ पर कोसलपुरी के राजा श्री रामचंद्रजी हर्षित होकर चढ़े। उसमें चार चंचल, मनोहर, अजर, अमर और मन की गति के समान शीघ्र चलने वाले (देवलोक के) घोड़े जुते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5036.english_translation: Ram, the lord of Kosala, joyfully climbed onto that radiant, incomparable, divine chariot. Four lovely, swift horses were yoked to it, moving as fast as the mind itself.
ramacharitamanas::5036.translation_literal: तेज पुंज (a mass of radiance) / रथ (chariot) / दिब्य (divine) / अनूपा (matchless) / हरषि (joyfully) / चढ़े (mounted) / कोसलपुर भूपा (king of Kosala) / चंचल (swift) / तुरग (horses) / मनोहर (beautiful) / चारी (four) / अजर (unaging) / अमर (deathless) / मन सम (like the mind) / गतिकारी (moving)
ramacharitamanas::5036.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5036.essence: Grace arrives as strength when the struggle is already underway.
ramacharitamanas::5036.simple_meaning: Ram mounts a radiant divine chariot with four beautiful, swift horses.
ramacharitamanas::5036.simple_insight: Even in battle, the scene around Ram carries splendor and ease.
ramacharitamanas::5036.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war, the gods send Ram a divine chariot because he is fighting on foot. The king of Kosala gladly mounts it, and the horses are described as swift, beautiful, and beyond decay. This verse sets up the next surge in the battle.
ramacharitamanas::5036.modern_relevance: You finally get the right support after carrying too much alone. The burden does not vanish, but the path opens and movement becomes possible again.
ramacharitamanas::5036.insight: It shifts attention from strain to divine assistance arriving at the right moment.

ramacharitamanas::5037.verse_sanskrit: रथारूढ़ रघुनाथहि देखी। धाए कपि बलु पाइ बिसेषी॥ सही न जाइ कपिन्ह कै मारी। तब रावन माया बिस्तारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5037.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी को रथ पर चढ़े देखकर वानर विशेष बल पाकर दौड़े। वानरों की मार सही नहीं जाती। तब रावण ने माया फैलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5037.english_translation: Seeing Raghunath seated on the chariot, the monkeys surged forward with renewed strength. The monkeys' blows could not be endured, so Ravana spread his illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5037.translation_literal: रथारूढ़ (mounted on a chariot) / रघुनाथहि (Raghunath) / देखी (seeing) / धाए (rushed) / कपि (monkeys) / बलु (strength) / पाइ (having gained) / बिसेषी (special)॥ / सही (endured) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / कपिन्ह (of the monkeys) / कै (of) / मारी (beating) / तब (then) / रावन (Ravana) / माया (illusion) / बिस्तारी (spread) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5037.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5037.essence: Steady presence gives others strength; desperation turns to illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5037.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram on the chariot, the monkeys rushed in with fresh courage. Ravana then used illusion because the monkeys' attack was too strong to bear.
ramacharitamanas::5037.simple_insight: Courage spreads fast when you see someone you trust standing firm.
ramacharitamanas::5037.detailed_meaning: In the Lanka war, Ram has taken the divine chariot and the monkey warriors see him there. Their strength rises at once and they press the attack so fiercely that Ravana cannot withstand it, so he resorts to illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5037.modern_relevance: You spot your team lead step into the chaos and suddenly everyone straightens up. Momentum changes before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::5037.insight: It shows how visible steadiness can energize a whole group, while panic reaches for tricks when direct resistance fails.

ramacharitamanas::5038.verse_sanskrit: सो माया रघुबीरहि बाँची। लछिमन कपिन्ह सो मानी साँची॥ देखी कपिन्ह निसाचर अनी। अनुज सहित बहु कोसलधनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5038.verse_hindi: एक श्री रघुवीर के ही वह माया नहीं लगी। सब वानरों ने और लक्ष्मणजी ने भी उस माया को सच मान लिया। वानरों ने राक्षसी सेना में भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित बहुत से रामों को देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5038.english_translation: Only Raghubir was untouched by that illusion. The monkeys and Lakshman took it as real, and they saw many Rakshasa warriors and many Ramas, with Lakshman and the prince of Kosala among them.
ramacharitamanas::5038.translation_literal: सो (that) / माया (illusion) / रघुबीरहि (to Raghubir) / बाँची (did not cling) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / कपिन्ह (to the monkeys) / सो (that) / मानी (considered) / साँची (real) / देखी (seeing) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / निसाचर (Rakshasa) / अनी (army) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / बहु (many) / कोसलधनी (lord of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::5038.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5038.essence: Illusion distorts everyone except the one who is steady.
ramacharitamanas::5038.simple_meaning: Ravana's illusion affected the monkeys and Lakshman, but not Ram. They saw a confusing battlefield image of many enemy warriors and many Ramas.
ramacharitamanas::5038.simple_insight: Fear can make the mind accept a false scene as real.
ramacharitamanas::5038.detailed_meaning: In the heat of Lanka's battle, Ravana spreads a deceptive illusion. Ram remains untouched, but Lakshman and the monkey army mistake the false vision for reality and see countless enemies and duplicate Ramas.
ramacharitamanas::5038.modern_relevance: In the middle of a tense group chat, one misleading message can make everyone see a crisis that isn't there. Panic multiplies the illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5038.insight: It shows how confusion spreads through a frightened crowd, while steady awareness stays clear.

ramacharitamanas::5039.verse_sanskrit: बहु राम लछिमन देखि मर्कट भालु मन अति अपडरे। जनु चित्र लिखित समेत लछिमन जहँ सो तहँ चितवहिं खरे॥ निज सेन चकित बिलोकि हँसि सर चाप सजि कोसलधनी। माया हरी हरि निमिष महुँ हरषी सकल मर्कट अनी॥
ramacharitamanas::5039.verse_hindi: बहुत से राम-लक्ष्मण देखकर वानर-भालू मन में मिथ्या डर से बहुत ही डर गए। लक्ष्मणजी सहित वे मानो चित्र लिखे से जहाँ के तहाँ खड़े देखने लगे। अपनी सेना को आश्चर्यचकित देखकर कोसलपति भगवान् हरि (दुःखों के हरने वाले श्री रामजी) ने हँसकर धनुष पर बाण चढ़ाकर, पल भर में सारी माया हर ली। वानरों की सारी सेना हर्षित हो गई।
ramacharitamanas::5039.english_translation: Seeing Ram and Lakshman, the monkeys and bears became deeply afraid. They stood frozen, as though painted in a picture, wherever Lakshman was seen. Seeing his own army stunned, the Lord of Kosala smiled, drew his bow, and in an instant removed the illusion. The entire monkey army rejoiced.
