ramacharitamanas::5039.translation_literal: बहु (many) / राम (Ram) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / देखि (seeing) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / अपडरे (afraid)। / जनु (as if) / चित्र (picture) / लिखित (drawn) / समेत (together with) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / जहँ (where) / सो (there) / तहँ (there) / चितवहिं (they looked) / खरे (fixed)॥ / निज (own) / सेन (army) / चकित (stunned) / बिलोकि (seeing) / हँसि (smiling) / सर (arrow) / चाप (bow) / सजि (readying) / कोसलधनी (Lord of Kosala)। / माया (illusion) / हरी (removed) / हरि (Hari) / निमिष (moment) / महुँ (within) / हरषी (rejoiced) / सकल (all) / मर्कट (monkeys) / अनी (army)॥
ramacharitamanas::5039.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5039.essence: Steady presence breaks the spell of fear.
ramacharitamanas::5039.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears are briefly overwhelmed by Ravana's illusion, but Ram smiles, raises his bow, and breaks the spell at once.
ramacharitamanas::5039.simple_insight: Even confusion can vanish the moment steady presence returns.
ramacharitamanas::5039.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana's magic has briefly shaken the monkey and bear army. They freeze in fear until Ram sees their condition, smiles, and lifts his bow. His calm action cuts through the illusion and restores their courage.
ramacharitamanas::5039.modern_relevance: A group chat spirals into panic after one alarming message, and everyone starts imagining the worst. Then one steady voice answers clearly, and the whole mood changes in a second.
ramacharitamanas::5039.insight: It shows how calm strength can dissolve fear faster than argument or panic.

ramacharitamanas::5040.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि राम सब तन चितइ बोले बचन गँभीर। द्वंदजुद्ध देखहु सकल श्रमित भए अति बीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5040.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामजी सबकी ओर देखकर गंभीर वचन बोले- हे वीरों! तुम सब बहुत ही थक गए हो, इसलिए अब (मेरा और रावण का) द्वंद्व युद्ध देखो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5040.english_translation: Then Ram looked at everyone and spoke in a grave voice: "O heroes, you are all greatly tired, so now watch the duel."
ramacharitamanas::5040.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / राम (Ram) / सब (all) / तन (bodies) / चितइ (looking at) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / गँभीर (grave, deep) / द्वंदजुद्ध (duel-battle) / देखहु (watch) / सकल (all) / श्रमित (tired) / भए (became) / अति (very) / बीर (heroes)
ramacharitamanas::5040.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5040.essence: When everyone is spent, the real battle must be faced directly.
ramacharitamanas::5040.simple_meaning: Ram sees that the warriors are exhausted and tells them to watch the duel instead of fighting on.
ramacharitamanas::5040.simple_insight: Sometimes the wisest move is to step back and let the decisive moment unfold.
ramacharitamanas::5040.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the monkey and bear warriors are worn out after the chaos of war. Ram looks across at them with calm authority and tells them to watch the duel between himself and Ravana, shifting the battle into its final, focused confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::5040.modern_relevance: After a long day of arguments, deadlines, and half-finished battles, you finally stop trying to do everything yourself and let the main issue stand in the open.
ramacharitamanas::5040.insight: It shifts attention from scattered effort to the one निर्णायक confrontation that actually matters.

ramacharitamanas::5041.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि रथ रघुनाथ चलावा। बिप्र चरन पंकज सिरु नावा॥ तब लंकेस क्रोध उर छावा। गर्जत तर्जत सम्मुख धावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5041.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने ब्राह्मणों के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया और फिर रथ चलाया। तब रावण के हृदय में क्रोध छा गया और वह गरजता तथा ललकारता हुआ सामने दौड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5041.english_translation: After saying this, Lord Raghunath bowed his head to the feet of the brahmins and drove the chariot forward. Then anger filled Ravana's heart, and he rushed forward roaring and challenging.
ramacharitamanas::5041.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / रथ (chariot) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath, Ram) / चलावा (drove forward) / बिप्र (brahmins) / चरन (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / तब (then) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka, Ravana) / क्रोध (anger) / उर (heart) / छावा (spread) / गर्जत (roaring) / तर्जत (challenging) / सम्मुख (forward) / धावा (rushed)
ramacharitamanas::5041.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5041.essence: Respect steadies Ram; anger drives Ravana into battle.
ramacharitamanas::5041.simple_meaning: Ram bows to the brahmins before moving ahead, while Ravana is filled with anger and rushes to attack.
ramacharitamanas::5041.simple_insight: Humility and fury meet in the same moment, but only one of them is steady.
ramacharitamanas::5041.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ram first honors the brahmins and then advances in his chariot. Ravana, seeing this, burns with rage and charges forward. The verse sets up the duel, showing the contrast between Ram's composure and Ravana's pride.
ramacharitamanas::5041.modern_relevance: You stay calm, do the respectful thing, and move forward anyway. Someone else may explode in reaction, but their noise does not change your footing.
ramacharitamanas::5041.insight: It contrasts grounded action with ego-driven reaction, preparing the mind for the duel that follows.

ramacharitamanas::5042.verse_sanskrit: जीतेहु जे भट संजुग माहीं। सुनु तापस मैं तिन्ह सम नाहीं॥ रावन नाम जगत जस जाना। लोकप जाकें बंदीखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5042.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) अरे तपस्वी! सुनो, तुमने युद्ध में जिन योद्धाओं को जीता है, मैं उनके समान नहीं हूँ। मेरा नाम रावण है, मेरा यश सारा जगत् जानता है, लोकपाल तक जिसके कैद खाने में पड़े हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5042.english_translation: “Listen, ascetic: I am not like the warriors you have defeated in battle. My name is Ravana, known throughout the world. Even the guardians of the world are prisoners in my fortress.”
ramacharitamanas::5042.translation_literal: जीतेहु (you defeated) / जे (those who) / भट (warriors) / संजुग माहीं (in battle) / सुनु (listen) / तापस (ascetic) / मैं (I) / तिन्ह (those) / सम (like) / नाहीं (am not) / रावन (Ravana) / नाम (name) / जगत (world) / जस (fame) / जाना (known) / लोकप (guardians of the world) / जाकें (whose) / बंदीखाना (prison) /
ramacharitamanas::5042.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5042.essence: Pride speaks loudest when it fears being measured.
ramacharitamanas::5042.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he is unlike the enemies already defeated, claiming world-famous power and control over even the guardians of the world.
ramacharitamanas::5042.simple_insight: Pride makes a person measure himself by domination instead of reality.
ramacharitamanas::5042.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana answers Hanuman’s challenge with raw arrogance. He dismisses the warriors Hanuman has already defeated and inflates his own fame, trying to restore fear through boasting before the duel begins.
ramacharitamanas::5042.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting, then starts listing titles, followers, and past wins to shut everyone down. The noise is trying to cover the insecurity underneath.
ramacharitamanas::5042.insight: It exposes how ego uses reputation and power as armor against being seen clearly.

ramacharitamanas::5043.verse_sanskrit: खर दूषन बिराध तुम्ह मारा। बधेहु ब्याध इव बालि बिचारा॥ निसिचर निकर सुभट संघारेहु। कुंभकरन घननादहि मारेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5043.verse_hindi: तुमने खर, दूषण और विराध को मारा! बेचारे बालि का व्याध की तरह वध किया। बड़े-बड़े राक्षस योद्धाओं के समूह का संहार किया और कुंभकर्ण तथा मेघनाद को भी मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5043.english_translation: You killed Khara, Dushana, and Viradha; you struck down Bali like a hunter. You destroyed ranks of demons and killed Kumbhakarna and Meghnad.
ramacharitamanas::5043.translation_literal: खर (Khara) / दूषन (Dushana) / बिराध (Viradha) / तुम्ह (you) / मारा (killed) / बधेहु (you struck down) / ब्याध इव (like a hunter) / बालि (Bali) / बिचारा (poor/helpless) / निसिचर (demons/night-walkers) / निकर (groups) / सुभट (warriors) / संघारेहु (you destroyed) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / घननादहि (Meghnad) / मारेहु (you killed)
ramacharitamanas::5043.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5043.essence: Even Ravana admits Ram's power before rushing toward defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5043.simple_meaning: Ravana lists Ram's past victories over powerful enemies to boast that he is no easy opponent.
ramacharitamanas::5043.simple_insight: Pride often sounds like praise of the other side before it hardens into defiance.
ramacharitamanas::5043.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana answers Ram's advance by reciting Ram's earlier victories over Khara, Dushana, Viradha, Bali, and even Kumbhakarna and Meghnad. He is not teaching; he is measuring the danger before charging in.
ramacharitamanas::5043.modern_relevance: You’re arguing with someone who has already outperformed everyone else in the room. You list their wins, but your voice is really shaking with the size of the challenge.
ramacharitamanas::5043.insight: It shows a mind trying to steady itself by naming the opponent's strength before attacking.

ramacharitamanas::5044.verse_sanskrit: आजु बयरु सबु लेउँ निबाही। जौं रन भूप भाजि नहिं जाही॥ आजु करउँ खलु काल हवाले। परेहु कठिन रावन के पाले ॥
ramacharitamanas::5044.verse_hindi: अरे राजा! यदि तुम रण से भाग न गए तो आज मैं (वह) सारा वैर निकाल लूँगा। आज मैं तुम्हें निश्चय ही काल के हवाले कर दूँगा। तुम कठिन रावण के पाले पड़े हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5044.english_translation: Today I will settle this old enmity. If you do not flee the battlefield, I will send you to death today. You have fallen into Ravana's grasp.
ramacharitamanas::5044.translation_literal: आजु (today) / बयरु (enmity) / सबु (all) / लेउँ (I take) / निबाही (settle, carry through) / जौं (if) / रन (battlefield) / भूप (king) / भाजि (fleeing) / नहिं (not) / जाही (go) ॥ आजु (today) / करउँ (I do) / खलु (indeed) / काल (death) / हवाले (handing over) / परेहु (you have fallen) / कठिन (hard, severe) / रावन (Ravana's) / के पाले (in the grip, in the protection) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5044.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5044.essence: Arrogance speaks most loudly when it feels cornered.
ramacharitamanas::5044.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens to finish the fight today and says he will hand the king over to death if he does not run away.
ramacharitamanas::5044.simple_insight: Pride turns even fear into a challenge.
ramacharitamanas::5044.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana answers Ram with raw arrogance. After listing the warriors Ram has already defeated, he boasts that he will settle the old feud today and kill him if he does not retreat.
ramacharitamanas::5044.modern_relevance: Someone cornered in an argument suddenly starts sounding fierce, not because they are strong, but because they feel exposed. The louder they speak, the more fear leaks through.
ramacharitamanas::5044.insight: It exposes how ego masks vulnerability with threats.

ramacharitamanas::5045.verse_sanskrit: सुनि दुर्बचन कालबस जाना। बिहँसि बचन कह कृपानिधाना॥ सत्य सत्य सब तव प्रभुताई। जल्पसि जनि देखाउ मनुसाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5045.verse_hindi: रावण के दुर्वचन सुनकर और उसे कालवश जान कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने हँसकर यह वचन कहा- तुम्हारी सारी प्रभुता, जैसा तुम कहते हो, बिल्कुल सच है। पर अब व्यर्थ बकवाद न करो, अपना पुरुषार्थ दिखलाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5045.english_translation: Hearing Ravana's harsh words and knowing he was under the power of time, the Lord of compassion smiled and said: "Yes, yes, all your greatness is true. But stop the empty boasting and show your real strength."
ramacharitamanas::5045.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / दुर्बचन (harsh words) / कालबस (under the power of time) / जाना (knew) / बिहँसि (smiling) / बचन (words) / कह (said) / कृपानिधाना (storehouse of compassion)॥ / सत्य सत्य (true true) / सब (all) / तव (your) / प्रभुताई (greatness, power) / जल्पसि (you boast) / जनि (do not) / देखाउ (show) / मनुसाई (manliness, real strength)॥
ramacharitamanas::5045.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5045.essence: Real strength does not need bragging; it proves itself in action.
ramacharitamanas::5045.simple_meaning: Ram hears Ravana's insults, laughs, and tells him not to waste time bragging. If Ravana has strength, he should prove it in action.
ramacharitamanas::5045.simple_insight: Empty talk loses power fast. What matters is whether your actions can carry the weight of your words.
ramacharitamanas::5045.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana hurls insults at Ram after boasting of his power. Ram, seeing Ravana already under time's grip, smiles instead of reacting in anger. He answers with calm authority: stop the talk and show what you can do.
ramacharitamanas::5045.modern_relevance: Someone sends a long angry text, full of threats and self-importance. You read it once, breathe, and realize the noise is bigger than the power behind it.
ramacharitamanas::5045.insight: It shifts attention from verbal aggression to tested capacity. The verse teaches you to meet bluster with calm and let reality speak.

ramacharitamanas::5046.verse_sanskrit: जनि जल्पना करि सुजसु नासहि नीति सुनहि करहि छमा। संसार महँ पूरुष त्रिबिध पाटल रसाल पनस समा॥ एक सुमनप्रद एक सुमन फल एक फलइ केवल लागहीं। एक कहहिं कहहिं करहिं अपर एक करहिं कहत न बागहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::5046.verse_hindi: व्यर्थ बकवाद करके अपने सुंदर यश का नाश न करो। क्षमा करना, तुम्हें नीति सुनाता हूँ, सुनो! संसार में तीन प्रकार के पुरुष होते हैं- पाटल (गुलाब), आम और कटहल के समान। एक (पाटल) फूल देते हैं, एक (आम) फूल और फल दोनों देते हैं एक (कटहल) में केवल फल ही लगते हैं। इसी प्रकार (पुरुषों में) एक कहते हैं (करते नहीं), दूसरे कहते और करते भी हैं और एक (तीसरे) केवल करते हैं, पर वाणी से कहते नहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::5046.english_translation: Do not waste your good name with empty talk. Listen to this policy: in the world there are three kinds of people, like pātal, mango, and jackfruit. One gives only flowers, one gives both flowers and fruit, and one bears fruit without showing flowers. In the same way, one speaks but does not act, one speaks and acts, and one acts without speaking.
ramacharitamanas::5046.translation_literal: जनि (do not) / जल्पना (empty talk) / करि (doing) / सुजसु (good name) / नासहि (destroy) / नीति (policy / practical wisdom) / सुनहि (listen) / करहि (do) / छमा (forgiveness) / संसार (world) / महँ (in) / पूरुष (people) / त्रिबिध (three kinds) / पाटल (pātal flower) / रसाल (mango) / पनस (jackfruit) / समा (like) / एक (one) / सुमनप्रद (flower-giving) / एक (one) / सुमन (flower) / फल (fruit) / एक (one) / फलइ (bears fruit) / केवल (only) / लागहीं (appear) / एक (one) / कहहिं (speak) / कहहिं (speak) / करहिं (do) / अपर (another) / एक (one) / करहिं (do) / कहत (while speaking) / न (not) / बागहीं (show)
ramacharitamanas::5046.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5046.essence: Your deeds should outlast your words.
ramacharitamanas::5046.simple_meaning: Empty talk can ruin your reputation. The wise person is not the one who only speaks, but the one whose words and actions match.
ramacharitamanas::5046.simple_insight: You feel the dignity of being real: less performance, more integrity.
ramacharitamanas::5046.detailed_meaning: Ram answers Ravana in the middle of war. After mocking threats and pride, he turns the exchange into a lesson on conduct: some people only talk, some speak and act, and some let their actions speak for them.
ramacharitamanas::5046.modern_relevance: You make a big promise in a family group chat, then disappear when the day comes. The verse cuts through that gap between image and follow-through.
ramacharitamanas::5046.insight: It shifts attention from sounding wise to becoming reliable.

ramacharitamanas::5047.verse_sanskrit: राम बचन सुनि बिहँसा मोहि सिखावत ग्यान। बयरु करत नहिं तब डरे अब लागे प्रिय प्रान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5047.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर वह खूब हँसा (और बोला-) मुझे ज्ञान सिखाते हो? उस समय वैर करते तो नहीं डरे, अब प्राण प्यारे लग रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5047.english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, he laughed: 'You are teaching me wisdom? You did not fear then, when you fought me; now you call my life dear.'
ramacharitamanas::5047.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / बिहँसा (laughed) / मोहि (to me) / सिखावत (teaching) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बयरु (enmity) / करत (doing) / नहिं (not) / तब (then) / डरे (feared) / अब (now) / लागे (seem) / प्रिय (dear) / प्रान (life)
ramacharitamanas::5047.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5047.essence: Pride mocks wisdom until danger makes it flinch.
ramacharitamanas::5047.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Ram's advice and says Ram was not afraid to fight before, so he should not act concerned now.
ramacharitamanas::5047.simple_insight: Pride can hear correction as insult, even when the warning is true.
ramacharitamanas::5047.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram has just spoken firmly to Ravana, warning him to stop empty boasting and choose restraint. Ravana answers with laughter, twisting Ram's counsel into mockery. The verse shows his wounded ego before the arrows begin to fly.
ramacharitamanas::5047.modern_relevance: You finally call out a friend's destructive pattern, and they smirk, saying you only care now that things are serious. The defensive laugh comes before the regret.
ramacharitamanas::5047.insight: It reveals how ego turns guidance into provocation and makes peace harder the moment it is offered.

ramacharitamanas::5048.verse_sanskrit: कहि दुर्बचन क्रुद्ध दसकंधर। कुलिस समान लाग छाँड़ै सर॥॥ नानाकार सिलीमुख धाए। दिसि अरु बिदिसि गगन महि छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5048.verse_hindi: दुर्वचन कहकर रावण क्रुद्ध होकर वज्र के समान बाण छोड़ने लगा। अनेकों आकार के बाण दौड़े और दिशा, विदिशा तथा आकाश और पृथ्वी में, सब जगह छा गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5048.english_translation: Ravana, enraged, hurled arrows like thunderbolts after speaking harsh words. Arrows of many kinds rushed forth and filled the sky and earth in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::5048.translation_literal: कहि (having spoken) / दुर्बचन (harsh words) / क्रुद्ध (enraged) / दसकंधर (the ten-necked one, Ravana) / कुलिस समान (like thunderbolts) / लाग (began to) / छाँड़ै (release) / सर (arrows) / नानाकार (of many kinds) / सिलीमुख (arrows) / धाए (rushed) / दिसि (direction) / अरु (and) / बिदिसि (intermediate direction) / गगन (sky) / महि (earth) / छाए (covered)
ramacharitamanas::5048.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5048.essence: Rage throws force everywhere and still cannot find a center.
ramacharitamanas::5048.simple_meaning: Ravana, angry after speaking harshly, unleashes a storm of arrows in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::5048.simple_insight: Anger multiplies force, but not wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::5048.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final battle, Ravana answers Ram’s words with insult and a barrage of arrows. The scene is pure combat movement, showing his rage spreading across sky and earth before Ram responds in the next verse.
ramacharitamanas::5048.modern_relevance: Someone fires off three furious texts, then keeps adding more, making the mess bigger with every reply. Rage often feels powerful right before it becomes reckless.
ramacharitamanas::5048.insight: It shows anger as scattered, self-defeating action rather than clear strength.

ramacharitamanas::5049.verse_sanskrit: पावक सर छाँड़ेउ रघुबीरा। छन महुँ जरे निसाचर तीरा॥ छाड़िसि तीब्र सक्ति खिसिआई। बान संग प्रभु फेरि चलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5049.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीर ने अग्निबाण छोड़ा, (जिससे) रावण के सब बाण क्षणभर में भस्म हो गए। तब उसने खिसियाकर तीक्ष्ण शक्ति छोड़ी, (किन्तु) श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उसको बाण के साथ वापस भेज दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5049.english_translation: Raghubir released a fire-arrow, and in an instant it burned up the demon-king's arrows. Then, in anger, Ravana hurled a fierce weapon, but Lord Ram sent it back along with his own arrow.
ramacharitamanas::5049.translation_literal: पावक (fire) / सर (arrow) / छाँड़ेउ (released) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir) / छन महुँ (in an instant) / जरे (burned) / निसाचर (demon-born) / तीरा (arrows) / छाड़िसि (he released) / तीब्र (fierce) / सक्ति (weapon) / खिसिआई (in anger) / बान (arrow) / संग (with) / प्रभु (the Lord) / फेरि (returned) / चलाई (sent)
ramacharitamanas::5049.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5049.essence: Ram's calm power turns Ravana's fury back on itself.
ramacharitamanas::5049.simple_meaning: Ram burns Ravana's arrows at once, then returns Ravana's weapon back at him.
ramacharitamanas::5049.simple_insight: Force meets a steadier force and loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::5049.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana keeps attacking in rage. Ram answers each move with effortless control: one fire-arrow destroys the assault, and another turns Ravana's own weapon back on him. The verse is a combat detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5049.insight: It shows overwhelming skill in battle, where every attack is neutralized and reversed.

ramacharitamanas::5050.verse_sanskrit: कोटिन्ह चक्र त्रिसूल पबारै। बिनु प्रयास प्रभु काटि निवारै॥ निफल होहिं रावन सर कैसें। खल के सकल मनोरथ जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::5050.verse_hindi: वह करोड़ों चक्र और त्रिशूल चलाता है, परन्तु प्रभु उन्हें बिना ही परिश्रम काटकर हटा देते हैं। रावण के बाण किस प्रकार निष्फल होते हैं, जैसे दुष्ट मनुष्य के सब मनोरथ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5050.english_translation: He hurls millions of discus and tridents, yet the Lord cuts them away without effort. Ravana's arrows fail just like the desires of a wicked heart.
ramacharitamanas::5050.translation_literal: कोटिन्ह (millions) / चक्र (discus) / त्रिसूल (trident) / पबारै (he hurls) / बिनु (without) / प्रयास (effort) / प्रभु (the Lord) / काटि (cutting) / निवारै (drives away) / निफल (fruitless) / होहिं (become) / रावन (Ravana's) / सर (arrows) / कैसें (how) / खल (wicked) / के (of) / सकल (all) / मनोरथ (desires) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::5050.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5050.essence: Desire can throw everything and still reach nothing.
ramacharitamanas::5050.simple_meaning: Ravana throws every weapon he has, but Ram effortlessly cuts them down. His attacks fail completely, like selfish desires that never truly satisfy.
ramacharitamanas::5050.simple_insight: Force can look huge and still accomplish nothing against steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::5050.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana keeps unleashing terrible weapons at Ram. But Ram removes them as if it takes no effort at all. The verse turns that scene into a larger truth: destructive desire may surge wildly, yet it still ends empty.
ramacharitamanas::5050.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the email thread, sending one more message, one more push. But some battles are already over in your mind long before the other side moves.
ramacharitamanas::5050.insight: It shifts attention from aggressive force to the emptiness of unchecked wanting.

ramacharitamanas::5051.verse_sanskrit: तब सत बान सारथी मारेसि। परेउ भूमि जय राम पुकारेसि॥ राम कृपा करि सूत उठावा। तब प्रभु परम क्रोध कहुँ पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5051.verse_hindi: तब उसने श्री रामजी के सारथी को सौ बाण मारे। वह श्री रामजी की जय पुकारकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। श्री रामजी ने कृपा करके सारथी को उठाया। तब प्रभु अत्यंत क्रोध को प्राप्त हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5051.english_translation: Then he struck Ram's charioteer with a hundred arrows. He fell to the ground, crying, "Victory to Ram!" Ram, in compassion, lifted the charioteer up. Then the Lord became intensely wrathful.
ramacharitamanas::5051.translation_literal: तब (then) / सत (hundred) / बान (arrows) / सारथी (charioteer) / मारेसि (struck) / परेउ (fell) / भूमि (on the ground) / जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / पुकारेसि (called out) / राम (Ram) / कृपा (compassion) / करि (having done) / सूत (charioteer) / उठावा (lifted up) / तब (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / परम (intense) / क्रोध (wrath) / कहुँ (toward) / पावा (became)
ramacharitamanas::5051.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5051.essence: Mercy can become the fire that ends cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::5051.simple_meaning: Ravana strikes Ram's charioteer down, but the fallen man still cries Ram's victory. Ram lifts him up with compassion, and that mercy turns into fierce anger against Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::5051.simple_insight: Compassion does not cancel strength; sometimes mercy is exactly what awakens righteous force.
ramacharitamanas::5051.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana wounds Ram's charioteer with a hundred arrows. Even as he falls, he calls out Ram's name. Ram lifts him up with kindness, and that sight ignites the Lord's fierce resolve for the next strike.
ramacharitamanas::5051.modern_relevance: You watch someone get humiliated in front of everyone, and the room goes silent. The urge to protect them rises instantly — not from ego, but from care.
ramacharitamanas::5051.insight: It shows that tenderness and fierce action can arise from the same heart.

ramacharitamanas::5052.verse_sanskrit: भए क्रुद्ध जुद्ध बिरुद्ध रघुपति त्रोन सायक कसमसे। कोदंड धुनि अति चंड सुनि मनुजाद सब मारुत ग्रसे॥ मंदोदरी उर कंप कंपति कमठ भू भूधर त्रसे। चिक्करहिं दिग्गज दसन गहि महि देखि कौतुक सुर हँसे॥
ramacharitamanas::5052.verse_hindi: युद्ध में शत्रु के विरुद्ध श्री रघुनाथजी क्रोधित हुए, तब तरकस में बाण कसमसाने लगे (बाहर निकलने को आतुर होने लगे)। उनके धनुष का अत्यंत प्रचण्ड शब्द (टंकार) सुनकर मनुष्यभक्षी सब राक्षस वातग्रस्त हो गए (अत्यंत भयभीत हो गए)। मंदोदरी का हृदय काँप उठा, समुद्र, कच्छप, पृथ्वी और पर्वत डर गए। दिशाओं के हाथी पृथ्वी को दाँतों से पकड़कर चिग्घाड़ने लगे। यह कौतुक देखकर देवता हँसे।
ramacharitamanas::5052.english_translation: In battle, Raghupati grew fierce against his enemies, and the arrows in his quiver seemed eager to spring forth. Hearing the terrible roar of his bow, the man-eating demons were struck with fear. Mandodari's heart trembled, the sea, tortoise, earth, and mountains shook, and the elephants of the directions cried out. Seeing this wonder, the radiant beings laughed.
ramacharitamanas::5052.translation_literal: भए (became) / क्रुद्ध (angry) / जुद्ध (in battle) / बिरुद्ध (against the enemy) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / त्रोन (quiver) / सायक (arrows) / कसमसे (strained/eagerly stirred) / कोदंड (bow) / धुनि (sound/roar) / अति चंड (very fierce) / सुनि (hearing) / मनुजाद (man-eating beings) / सब (all) / मारुत (wind-struck / blown by wind) / ग्रसे (were seized/devoured) / मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / उर (heart) / कंप कंपति (trembles) / कमठ (tortoise) / भू (earth) / भूधर (mountains) / त्रसे (tremble) / चिक्करहिं (cry out) / दिग्गज (elephants of the directions) / दसन (teeth) / गहि (grasping) / महि (earth) / देखि (seeing) / कौतुक (wonder/sight) / सुर (radiant beings) / हँसे (laughed)
ramacharitamanas::5052.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5052.essence: Ram's battle fury makes the whole world tremble.
ramacharitamanas::5052.simple_meaning: Ram's anger in battle shakes everything around him. His bow roars, his enemies panic, and even the sea, mountains, and celestial beings react.
ramacharitamanas::5052.simple_insight: Power can be so overwhelming that the whole world seems to flinch with it.
ramacharitamanas::5052.detailed_meaning: As the war in Lanka intensifies, Ram's fury rises against the enemy. The sound of his bow terrifies the demons so deeply that the whole scene seems to shake—Mandodari trembles, nature recoils, and the radiant beings watch in amazement.
ramacharitamanas::5052.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the leader finally speaks with force. Everyone feels the shift, not because of volume alone, but because the moment has become undeniable.
ramacharitamanas::5052.insight: It shows how righteous force can expose fear instantly and change the atmosphere around a conflict.

ramacharitamanas::5053.verse_sanskrit: तानेउ चाप श्रवन लगि छाँड़े बिसिख कराल। राम मारगन गन चले लहलहात जनु ब्याल ॥
ramacharitamanas::5053.verse_hindi: धनुष को कान तक तानकर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने भयानक बाण छोड़े। श्री रामजी के बाण समूह ऐसे चले मानो सर्प लहलहाते (लहराते) हुए जा रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5053.english_translation: Drawing his bow to his ear, Ram released terrible arrows. His arrows moved like writhing serpents.
ramacharitamanas::5053.translation_literal: तानेउ (drew tight) / चाप (bow) / श्रवन लगि (to the ear) / छाँड़े (released) / बिसिख (arrows) / कराल (terrible) / राम (Ram) / मारगन गन (groups of arrows) / चले (moved) / लहलहात (waving, writhing) / जनु (as if) / ब्याल (serpents)
ramacharitamanas::5053.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5053.essence: Ram's arrows turn the battlefield into a place of sudden terror.
ramacharitamanas::5053.simple_meaning: Ram draws his bow to his ear and releases fierce arrows that move like snakes.
ramacharitamanas::5053.simple_insight: The battle turns fierce in a single instant.
ramacharitamanas::5053.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ravana's side has already been shaken by the loss of his charioteer. Ram now answers with a deadly volley, and the verse lingers on the force and speed of the arrows as the fight intensifies.
ramacharitamanas::5053.modern_relevance: A tense room goes silent after one sharp decision. The next move lands hard, and everyone feels the change immediately.
ramacharitamanas::5053.insight: It shifts attention from the person to the force of the strike.

ramacharitamanas::5054.verse_sanskrit: चले बान सपच्छ जनु उरगा। प्रथमहिं हतेउ सारथी तुरगा॥ रथ बिभंजि हति केतु पताका। गर्जा अति अंतर बल थाका ॥
ramacharitamanas::5054.verse_hindi: बाण ऐसे चले मानो पंख वाले सर्प उड़ रहे हों। उन्होंने पहले सारथी और घोड़ों को मार डाला। फिर रथ को चूर-चूर करके ध्वजा और पताकाओं को गिरा दिया। तब रावण बड़े जोर से गरजा, पर भीतर से उसका बल थक गया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::5054.english_translation: Rama's arrows flew like winged serpents. They first struck down the charioteer and horses. Then they shattered the chariot and brought down the flag and pennants. Ravana roared loudly, but his inner strength was already exhausted.
ramacharitamanas::5054.translation_literal: चले (flew) / बान (arrows) / सपच्छ (with wings) / जनु (as if) / उरगा (serpents) / प्रथमहिं (first) / हतेउ (struck down) / सारथी (charioteer) / तुरगा (horses) / रथ (chariot) / बिभंजि (breaking) / हति (striking down) / केतु (banner) / पताका (pennants) / गर्जा (roared) / अति (greatly) / अंतर (inside) / बल (strength) / थाका (was exhausted)
ramacharitamanas::5054.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5054.essence: Ravana's roar remains, but his strength is already spent.
ramacharitamanas::5054.simple_meaning: Rama's arrows cut down Ravana's chariot, horses, and banner. Ravana still roared, but his inner power was already fading.
ramacharitamanas::5054.simple_insight: Outward force can remain after inner strength has already gone.
ramacharitamanas::5054.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Rama's arrows tear through Ravana's chariot in layers: driver, horses, wheels, banner, pride. Ravana still roars, but the verse shows his collapse from the inside before the final defeat arrives.
ramacharitamanas::5054.modern_relevance: You keep talking tough in a meeting after your plan has already fallen apart. The volume is still there, but everyone can feel the weakness underneath.
ramacharitamanas::5054.insight: It shifts attention from loud resistance to the quiet collapse beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::5055.verse_sanskrit: तुरत आन रथ चढ़ि खिसिआना। अस्त्र सस्त्र छाँड़ेसि बिधि नाना॥ बिफल होहिं सब उद्यम ताके। जिमि परद्रोह निरत मनसा के ॥
ramacharitamanas::5055.verse_hindi: तुरंत दूसरे रथ पर चढ़कर खिसियाकर उसने नाना प्रकार के अस्त्र-शस्त्र छोड़े। उसके सब उद्योग वैसे ही निष्फल हो गए, जैसे परद्रोह में लगे हुए चित्त वाले मनुष्य के होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5055.english_translation: He quickly climbed another chariot, irritated, and hurled many kinds of weapons. All his efforts failed, just like the efforts of a mind bent on harming others.
ramacharitamanas::5055.translation_literal: तुरत (quickly) / आन (another) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ि (having climbed) / खिसिआना (irritated) / अस्त्र (weapons) / सस्त्र (arms) / छाँड़ेसि (he hurled) / बिधि (many kinds) / नाना (various) / बिफल (fruitless) / होहिं (become) / सब (all) / उद्यम (efforts) / ताके (his) / जिमि (just as) / परद्रोह (harm to others) / निरत (engaged in) / मनसा (mind) / के (of)
ramacharitamanas::5055.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5055.essence: Anger makes even strong effort collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5055.simple_meaning: Ravana jumps to another chariot and attacks again, but his rage only makes his efforts fail. The verse compares that failure to the wasted energy of a harmful mind.
ramacharitamanas::5055.simple_insight: Anger can keep you moving while quietly ruining everything you try to do.
ramacharitamanas::5055.detailed_meaning: In the Lankakand battle, Ravana has just lost his chariot and keeps fighting in fury. He mounts another one and throws every weapon he has, but the verse shows his effort collapsing because his mind is hostile and blinded by spite.
ramacharitamanas::5055.modern_relevance: You fire off another angry email after the first one backfires, then another. The more you push from irritation, the more your own effort starts working against you.
ramacharitamanas::5055.insight: It turns rage into a self-defeating force and shows how hostile intent poisons action.

ramacharitamanas::5056.verse_sanskrit: तब रावन दस सूल चलावा। बाजि चारि महि मारि गिरावा॥ तुरग उठाइ कोपि रघुनायक। खैंचि सरासन छाँड़े सायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::5056.verse_hindi: तब रावण ने दस त्रिशूल चलाए और श्री रामजी के चारों घोड़ों को मारकर पृथ्वी पर गिरा दिया। घोड़ों को उठाकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने क्रोध करके धनुष खींचकर बाण छोड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5056.english_translation: Then Ravana hurled ten tridents, killing Ram's four horses and casting them to the ground. Ram lifted the horses, grew angry, drew his bow, and released arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5056.translation_literal: तब (then) / रावन (Ravana) / दस (ten) / सूल (tridents) / चलावा (hurled) / बाजि (horses) / चारि (four) / महि (to the ground) / मारि (having struck) / गिरावा (cast down) / तुरग (horses) / उठाइ (lifting) / कोपि (in anger) / रघुनायक (Ram, lord of the Raghu line) / खैंचि (drawing) / सरासन (bow) / छाँड़े (released) / सायक (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::5056.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5056.essence: Attack can shake your setup, not your center.
ramacharitamanas::5056.simple_meaning: Ravana attacks Ram's chariot and horses, and Ram responds by lifting the horses, drawing his bow, and firing arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5056.simple_insight: Pressure reveals the next move. When attacked, steady force answers without losing form.
ramacharitamanas::5056.detailed_meaning: In the Lanka war, Ravana keeps striking at Ram's chariot with tridents, killing the horses and trying to break the divine warrior's momentum. Ram immediately lifts the horses, draws his bow, and answers the assault.
ramacharitamanas::5056.modern_relevance: Your plans get wrecked five minutes before the presentation starts. You don't freeze; you reset, steady yourself, and respond with force.
ramacharitamanas::5056.insight: It shows how a true fighter recovers instantly and answers attack without collapse.

ramacharitamanas::5057.verse_sanskrit: रावन सिर सरोज बनचारी। चलि रघुबीर सिलीमुख धारी॥ दस दस बान भाल दस मारे। निसरि गए चले रुधिर पनारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5057.verse_hindi: रावण के सिर रूपी कमल वन में विचरण करने वाले श्री रघुवीर के बाण रूपी भ्रमरों की पंक्ति चली। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उसके दसों सिरों में दस-दस बाण मारे, जो आर-पार हो गए और सिरों से रक्त के पनाले बह चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::5057.english_translation: Like bees moving through a lotus forest of Ravana’s heads, the arrows of Raghubir flew on. Ram struck all ten of Ravana’s heads with ten arrows each, and streams of blood poured out.
ramacharitamanas::5057.translation_literal: रावन (Ravana’s) / सिर (heads) / सरोज (lotus) / बनचारी (moving through a forest) / चलि (moving) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / सिलीमुख (arrows, bee-like darts) / धारी (bearing)॥ / दस (ten) / दस (ten each) / बान (arrows) / भाल (heads) / दस (ten) / मारे (struck) / निसरि (flowing out) / गए (went) / चले (flowed) / रुधिर (blood) / पनारे (streams)॥
ramacharitamanas::5057.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5057.essence: Relentless force meets relentless resistance in battle.
ramacharitamanas::5057.simple_meaning: Ram’s arrows keep striking Ravana’s ten heads again and again, and blood pours out from the wounds.
ramacharitamanas::5057.simple_insight: Even overwhelming force can still be met with steady resolve.
ramacharitamanas::5057.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana keeps fighting even after losing his chariot and horses. Ram answers with relentless precision, sending arrows through all ten heads. The verse is a vivid combat detail in the larger duel.
ramacharitamanas::5057.insight: It keeps the focus on decisive action under pressure, not on drama or hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::5058.verse_sanskrit: स्रवत रुधिर धायउ बलवाना। प्रभु पुनि कृत धनु सर संधाना॥ तीस तीर रघुबीर पबारे। भुजन्हि समेत सीस महि पारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5058.verse_hindi: रुधिर बहते हुए ही बलवान् रावण दौड़ा। प्रभु ने फिर धनुष पर बाण संधान किया। श्री रघुवीर ने तीस बाण मारे और बीसों भुजाओं समेत दसों सिर काटकर पृथ्वी पर गिरा दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5058.english_translation: Ravana, still strong though bleeding, ran on. The Lord drew his bow again. Raghubir loosed thirty arrows and cut down all ten heads along with the twenty arms.
ramacharitamanas::5058.translation_literal: स्रवत (flowing) / रुधिर (blood) / धायउ (ran) / बलवाना (strong one) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पुनि (again) / कृत (having done) / धनु (bow) / सर (arrow) / संधाना (set) / तीस (thirty) / तीर (arrows) / रघुबीर (Raghu's hero) / पबारे (loosed) / भुजन्हि (with arms) / समेत (together with) / सीस (heads) / महि (on the ground) / पारे (cast down)
ramacharitamanas::5058.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5058.essence: What keeps returning must be cut at the root.
ramacharitamanas::5058.simple_meaning: Ravana keeps charging even while bleeding, and Ram answers again with more arrows, cutting down his many heads and arms.
ramacharitamanas::5058.simple_insight: Some struggles keep returning until their root is finished.
ramacharitamanas::5058.detailed_meaning: In the battle at Lanka, Ravana, wounded but still fierce, rushes forward again. Ram calmly draws and shoots once more, sending thirty arrows that sever Ravana’s heads and arms. The scene is still moving toward Ravana’s final defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5058.modern_relevance: You fix one problem, and the same pattern stands back up wearing a new face. The real work is not just damage control — it is ending what keeps regenerating.
ramacharitamanas::5058.insight: It shifts attention from the visible symptom to the stubborn source that keeps returning.

ramacharitamanas::5059.verse_sanskrit: काटतहीं पुनि भए नबीने। राम बहोरि भुजा सिर छीने॥ प्रभु बहु बार बाहु सिर हए। कटत झटिति पुनि नूतन भए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5059.verse_hindi: (सिर और हाथ) काटते ही फिर नए हो गए। श्री रामजी ने फिर भुजाओं और सिरों को काट गिराया। इस तरह प्रभु ने बहुत बार भुजाएँ और सिर काटे, परन्तु काटते ही वे तुरंत फिर नए हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5059.english_translation: Again, as soon as they were cut, new heads and arms appeared. Lord Ram kept cutting off his arms and heads, yet the moment they fell, they became new again. He cut them many times, but they instantly grew back.
ramacharitamanas::5059.translation_literal: काटतहीं (while cutting) / पुनि (again) / भए (became) / नबीने (new) / राम (Ram) / बहोरि (again) / भुजा (arms) / सिर (heads) / छीने (cut off) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बहु बार (many times) / बाहु (arms) / सिर (heads) / हए (were) / कटत (while being cut) / झटिति (immediately) / पुनि (again) / नूतन (new) / भए (became)
ramacharitamanas::5059.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5059.essence: What is cut away returns again until its root is ended.
ramacharitamanas::5059.simple_meaning: Ram keeps cutting off Ravana's heads and arms, but they instantly grow back. The fighting continues without end.
ramacharitamanas::5059.simple_insight: Some struggles don't end with a single blow; they expose how stubborn resistance can be.
ramacharitamanas::5059.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram's arrows keep severing Ravana's many heads and arms. But Ravana's body renews itself again and again, turning victory into an ongoing struggle rather than a final blow.
ramacharitamanas::5059.modern_relevance: You finally fix one problem, and three more appear before lunch. The issue is not solved by force alone; it keeps regenerating.
ramacharitamanas::5059.insight: It shows a battle that cannot be won by ordinary damage, only by ending the force that keeps returning.

ramacharitamanas::5060.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि प्रभु काटत भुज सीसा। अति कौतुकी कोसलाधीसा॥ रहे छाइ नभ सिर अरु बाहू। मानहुँ अमित केतु अरु राहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::5060.verse_hindi: प्रभु बार-बार उसकी भुजा और सिरों को काट रहे हैं, क्योंकि कोसलपति श्री रामजी बड़े कौतुकी हैं। आकाश में सिर और बाहु ऐसे छा गए हैं, मानो असंख्य केतु और राहु हों ॥ छंद :
ramacharitamanas::5060.english_translation: Again and again the Lord cut off his arms and heads. Koshal's lord is full of fierce play. Heads and arms filled the sky, like countless Ketu and Rahu.
ramacharitamanas::5060.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / प्रभु (the Lord) / काटत (cutting) / भुज (arms) / सीसा (heads) / अति (very) / कौतुकी (playful) / कोसलाधीसा (lord of Kosala) / रहे (remained) / छाइ (spread out) / नभ (sky) / सिर (heads) / अरु (and) / बाहू (arms) / मानहुँ (as if) / अमित (countless) / केतु (Ketu) / अरु (and) / राहू (Rahu)
ramacharitamanas::5060.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5060.essence: Relentless action is needed when resistance keeps returning.
ramacharitamanas::5060.simple_meaning: Ram keeps cutting down Ravana's heads and arms again and again. The battlefield fills with flying limbs, like countless celestial shadows in the sky.
ramacharitamanas::5060.simple_insight: Some struggles do not end quickly; they demand steady force and patience.
ramacharitamanas::5060.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana's many heads and arms keep returning after each blow. Ram keeps striking without hesitation, and the sky seems filled with the scattered forms of the enemy. The verse intensifies the combat before the final collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5060.modern_relevance: You fix one problem, and two more seem to grow back by morning. The work can feel endless, but steady action still matters.
ramacharitamanas::5060.insight: It shifts attention from a single victory to persistent, repeated effort against a stubborn obstacle.

ramacharitamanas::5061.verse_sanskrit: जनु राहु केतु अनेक नभ पथ स्रवत सोनित धावहीं। रघुबीर तीर प्रचंड लागहिं भूमि गिरत न पावहीं॥ एक एक सर सिर निकर छेदे नभ उड़त इमि सोहहीं। जनु कोपि दिनकर कर निकर जहँ तहँ बिधुंतुद पोहहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::5061.verse_hindi: मानो अनेकों राहु और केतु रुधिर बहाते हुए आकाश मार्ग से दौड़ रहे हों। श्री रघुवीर के प्रचण्ड बाणों के (बार-बार) लगने से वे पृथ्वी पर गिरने नहीं पाते। एक-एक बाण से समूह के समूह सिर छिदे हुए आकाश में उड़ते ऐसे शोभा दे रहे हैं मानो सूर्य की किरणें क्रोध करके जहाँ-तहाँ राहुओं को पिरो रही हों।
ramacharitamanas::5061.english_translation: As if many Rahus and Ketus were rushing through the sky, shedding blood. The mighty arrows of Raghubir strike them so hard that they cannot fall to the ground. Split by one arrow after another, whole clusters of heads fly in the sky, shining as if the sun's rays, in anger, were piercing Rahus everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::5061.translation_literal: जनु (as if) / राहु (Rahu) / केतु (Ketu) / अनेक (many) / नभ पथ (sky-path) / स्रवत (flowing) / सोनित (blood) / धावहीं (run) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / तीर (arrows) / प्रचंड (fierce) / लागहिं (strike) / भूमि (ground) / गिरत (falling) / न पावहीं (do not get to) / एक एक (one by one) / सर (arrow) / सिर (head) / निकर (clusters) / छेदे (pierced) / नभ (sky) / उड़त (flying) / इमि (thus) / सोहहीं (look beautiful) / जनु (as if) / कोपि (angrily) / दिनकर (sun) / कर निकर (ray-clusters) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / बिधुंतुद (Rahu) / पोहहीं (pierce)
ramacharitamanas::5061.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5061.essence: Ravana's heads fill the sky like burning celestial bodies.
ramacharitamanas::5061.simple_meaning: The scene compares Ravana's many severed heads to Rahu and Ketu racing through the sky, while Ram's arrows keep striking them before they can fall.
ramacharitamanas::5061.simple_insight: The battle is overwhelming and relentless, but this verse is still about motion, not meaning.
ramacharitamanas::5061.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Ram keeps cutting down Ravana's heads, and the poet turns the carnage into a vivid sky image. The verse is part of a longer battle description showing the heads multiplying and flying, not a separate teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::5061.insight: It adds visual force to the battle, but does not introduce a new principle.

ramacharitamanas::5062.verse_sanskrit: जिमि जिमि प्रभु हर तासु सिर तिमि होहिं अपार। सेवत बिषय बिबर्ध जिमि नित नित नूतन मार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5062.verse_hindi: जैसे-जैसे प्रभु उसके सिरों को काटते हैं, वैसे ही वैसे वे अपार होते जाते हैं। जैसे विषयों का सेवन करने से काम (उन्हें भोगने की इच्छा) दिन-प्रतिदिन नया-नया बढ़ता जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5062.english_translation: As the Lord cuts off his heads again and again, they become countless. Just as serving the senses makes desire grow anew each day.
ramacharitamanas::5062.translation_literal: जिमि (just as) / जिमि (just as) / प्रभु (the Lord) / हर (cuts off) / तासु (his) / सिर (heads) / तिमि (so) / होहिं (become) / अपार (countless) / सेवत (by serving) / बिषय (sense-objects) / बिबर्ध (grows) / जिमि (just as) / नित नित (day by day) / नूतन (new) / मार (desire)
ramacharitamanas::5062.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5062.essence: What you indulge grows; what you fight without insight returns stronger.
ramacharitamanas::5062.simple_meaning: Ravana's heads keep multiplying as Ram cuts them off, showing that craving only grows stronger when it is fed.
ramacharitamanas::5062.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that not every urge deserves more attention.
ramacharitamanas::5062.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana's heads keep rising even as Ram strikes them down. Tulsidas turns the scene into a warning: the more you feed desire through indulgence, the more it renews itself.
ramacharitamanas::5062.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one minute and end up scrolling for forty. The appetite didn't disappear after the first hit — it got louder. This verse names that trap exactly.
ramacharitamanas::5062.insight: It shifts you from feeding craving to noticing how repetition strengthens it.

ramacharitamanas::5063.verse_sanskrit: दसमुख देखि सिरन्ह कै बाढ़ी। बिसरा मरन भई रिस गाढ़ी॥ गर्जेउ मूढ़ महा अभिमानी। धायउ दसहु सरासन तानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5063.verse_hindi: सिरों की बाढ़ देखकर रावण को अपना मरण भूल गया और बड़ा गहरा क्रोध हुआ। वह महान् अभिमानी मूर्ख गरजा और दसों धनुषों को तानकर दौड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5063.english_translation: Seeing the growth of his many heads, Ravana forgot death and was flooded with fierce rage. The great fool, swollen with ego, roared and rushed forward, drawing all ten bows.
ramacharitamanas::5063.translation_literal: दसमुख (the ten-faced one) / देखि (seeing) / सिरन्ह कै (of the heads) / बाढ़ी (increase, growth) / बिसरा (forgot) / मरन (death) / भई (became) / रिस (anger) / गाढ़ी (intense) / गर्जेउ (roared) / मूढ़ (foolish one) / महा (great) / अभिमानी (ego-filled) / धायउ (rushed) / दसहु (all ten) / सरासन (bows) / तानी (drawing, pulling)
ramacharitamanas::5063.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5063.essence: Ego turns even near-defeat into blind attack.
ramacharitamanas::5063.simple_meaning: Ravana becomes so swollen with rage and ego that he forgets death itself and charges into battle with all ten bows drawn.
ramacharitamanas::5063.simple_insight: Pride can make danger invisible, right until it destroys you.
ramacharitamanas::5063.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana watches his many heads keep multiplying under Ram's arrows. Instead of waking up, he sinks deeper into rage and ego, grabs all ten bows, and rushes forward. The verse shows how delusion hardens at the very moment it should break.
ramacharitamanas::5063.modern_relevance: You get one harsh email and suddenly everything becomes a fight. The real issue disappears, and your ego takes the wheel.
ramacharitamanas::5063.insight: It shows how wounded pride turns a person reckless and blind to consequences.

ramacharitamanas::5064.verse_sanskrit: समर भूमि दसकंधर कोप्यो। बरषि बान रघुपति रथ तोप्यो॥ दंड एक रथ देखि न परेउ। जनु निहार महुँ दिनकर दुरेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5064.verse_hindi: रणभूमि में रावण ने क्रोध किया और बाण बरसाकर श्री रघुनाथजी के रथ को ढँक दिया। एक दण्ड (घड़ी) तक रथ दिखलाई न पड़ा, मानो कुहरे में सूर्य छिप गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5064.english_translation: On the battlefield, Ravana grew furious and showered arrows so thick that he hid Raghupati's chariot. For a moment, the chariot could not be seen, as if the sun had disappeared into fog.
ramacharitamanas::5064.translation_literal: समर भूमि (battlefield) / दसकंधर (Ravana, the ten-necked one) / कोप्यो (became angry) / बरषि (showering) / बान (arrows) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / रथ (chariot) / तोप्यो (covered, concealed)॥ / दंड (moment) / एक (one) / रथ (chariot) / देखि (seeing) / न (not) / परेउ (appeared) / जनु (as if) / निहार (fog) / महुँ (in) / दिनकर (sun) / दुरेऊ (disappeared) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5064.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5064.essence: Fury can briefly hide even what cannot be destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::5064.simple_meaning: Ravana's arrows were so dense that Ram's chariot disappeared from view for a moment, like the sun hidden by fog.
ramacharitamanas::5064.simple_insight: Sometimes pressure can make even the strongest presence seem to vanish for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::5064.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war at Lanka, Ravana lashes out in fury and rains arrows over Ram's chariot. The attack is so thick that, for a brief moment, even the divine chariot disappears from sight. This is a combat detail, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::5064.modern_relevance: A meeting turns chaotic, voices overlap, and the main point disappears under noise. For a moment, you cannot even see what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::5064.insight: It shows how overwhelming force can briefly obscure what is steady and true.

ramacharitamanas::5065.verse_sanskrit: हाहाकार सुरन्ह जब कीन्हा। तब प्रभु कोपि कारमुक लीन्हा॥ सर निवारि रिपु के सिर काटे। ते दिसि बिदिसि गगन महि पाटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5065.verse_hindi: जब देवताओं ने हाहाकार किया, तब प्रभु ने क्रोध करके धनुष उठाया और शत्रु के बाणों को हटाकर उन्होंने शत्रु के सिर काटे और उनसे दिशा, विदिशा, आकाश और पृथ्वी सबको पाट दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5065.english_translation: When the gods cried out in alarm, the Lord angrily took up his bow. He cleared away the enemy's arrows, cut off his heads, and filled the directions, sky, and earth with them.
ramacharitamanas::5065.translation_literal: हाहाकार (alarm and uproar) / सुरन्ह (of the radiant beings) / जब (when) / कीन्हा (was made) / तब (then) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कोपि (becoming angry) / कारमुक (bow) / लीन्हा (took up) ॥ / सर (arrows) / निवारि (removing) / रिपु के (of the enemy) / सिर (heads) / काटे (cut off) / ते (those) / दिसि (directions) / बिदिसि (intermediate directions) / गगन (sky) / महि (earth) / पाटे (filled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5065.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5065.essence: Protective power can be sudden, total, and unstoppable.
ramacharitamanas::5065.simple_meaning: The divine beings cry out, and Ram responds at once. He takes up his bow, clears the enemy's arrows, and cuts off the heads, filling the sky and earth with them.
ramacharitamanas::5065.simple_insight: Sometimes protection is fierce, not gentle.
ramacharitamanas::5065.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the gods watch the war and cry out as Ravana's side rages on. Ram answers by lifting his bow, sweeping aside the attack, and striking down the enemy in a scene of overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::5065.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when a crisis finally breaks. You stop explaining, stand up, and do what the moment demands without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::5065.insight: It shows decisive action that clears chaos instead of negotiating with it.

ramacharitamanas::5066.verse_sanskrit: काटे सिर नभ मारग धावहिं। जय जय धुनि करि भय उपजावहिं॥ कहँ लछिमन सुग्रीव कपीसा। कहँ रघुबीर कोसलाधीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5066.verse_hindi: काटे हुए सिर आकाश मार्ग से दौड़ते हैं और जय-जय की ध्वनि करके भय उत्पन्न करते हैं। 'लक्ष्मण और वानरराज सुग्रीव कहाँ हैं? कोसलपति रघुवीर कहाँ हैं?' ॥
ramacharitamanas::5066.english_translation: The severed heads rush through the sky, shouting victory and spreading fear. "Where are Lakshman and Sugriva, lord of the monkeys? Where is Raghubir, king of Kosala?"
ramacharitamanas::5066.translation_literal: काटे (cut) / सिर (heads) / नभ (sky) / मारग (path) / धावहिं (run) / जय (victory) / जय (victory) / धुनि (sound) / करि (making) / भय (fear) / उपजावहिं (cause to arise) / कहँ (where) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / सुग्रीव (Sugriva) / कपीसा (lord of monkeys) / कहँ (where) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / कोसलाधीसा (lord of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::5066.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5066.essence: Defeat still throws out one last wave of fear.
ramacharitamanas::5066.simple_meaning: The severed heads fly through the sky and terrify the battlefield, while the warriors cry out for Lakshman, Sugriva, and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5066.simple_insight: Fear can keep moving even after defeat, but it cannot change what has already been decided.
ramacharitamanas::5066.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ravana's severed heads still surge through the sky, shouting and frightening the vanaras. The verse is a vivid battle detail, not a fresh teaching, and it leads directly into Ram answering with his arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5066.modern_relevance: A fight keeps replaying in your head long after the argument ends. The body may still be tense, but the decision has already moved on.
ramacharitamanas::5066.insight: It keeps the scene in motion and heightens the terror before Ram's next decisive strike.

ramacharitamanas::5067.verse_sanskrit: कहँ रामु कहि सिर निकर धाए देखि मर्कट भजि चले। संधानि धनु रघुबंसमनि हँसि सरन्हि सिर बेधे भले॥ सिर मालिका कर कालिका गहि बृंद बृंदन्हि बहु मिलीं। करि रुधिर सरि मज्जनु मनहुँ संग्राम बट पूजन चलीं॥
ramacharitamanas::5067.verse_hindi: 'राम कहाँ हैं?' यह कहकर सिरों के समूह दौड़े, उन्हें देखकर वानर भाग चले। तब धनुष सन्धान करके रघुकुलमणि श्री रामजी ने हँसकर बाणों से उन सिरों को भलीभाँति बेध डाला। हाथों में मुण्डों की मालाएँ लेकर बहुत सी कालिकाएँ झुंड की झुंड मिलकर इकट्ठी हुईं और वे रुधिर की नदी में स्नान करके चलीं। मानो संग्राम रूपी वटवृक्ष की पूजा करने जा रही हों।
ramacharitamanas::5067.english_translation: “Where is Ram?” Crying this, the heads rushed forth; seeing them, the monkeys fled. Then, the jewel of Raghu’s line strung his bow and, smiling, pierced the heads with his arrows. Many groups of dark goddesses gathered, each holding garlands of skulls; bathing in the river of blood, they seemed to go to worship the battle-tree.
ramacharitamanas::5067.translation_literal: कहँ (where is) / रामु (Ram) / कहि (saying) / सिर (heads) / निकर (groups) / धाए (ran) / देखि (seeing) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भजि (fleeing) / चले (went) / संधानि (having strung) / धनु (the bow) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / हँसि (smiling) / सरन्हि (with arrows) / सिर (heads) / बेधे (pierced) / भले (well) / सिर (heads) / मालिका (garlands) / कर (in hand) / कालिका (dark goddesses) / गहि (holding) / बृंद बृंदन्हि (in many groups) / बहु (many) / मिलीं (gathered) / करि (doing) / रुधिर (blood) / सरि (river) / मज्जनु (bathing) / मनहुँ (as if) / संग्राम (battle) / बट (tree) / पूजन (worship) / चलीं (went)
ramacharitamanas::5067.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5067.essence: War’s horror is met by Ram’s unshaken response.
ramacharitamanas::5067.simple_meaning: The battlefield turns terrifying: severed heads surge forward, the monkeys scatter, and Ram answers by calmly shooting them down again. The scene ends with dark goddesses gathering as if to honor the battle itself.
ramacharitamanas::5067.simple_insight: Even in chaos, steady courage can cut fear down at the root.
ramacharitamanas::5067.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the war has become grotesque and overwhelming. Flying heads terrify the monkey army, but Ram remains unshaken, strings his bow, and destroys them again. The verse is vivid battle imagery, not a teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::5067.insight: It shows a battle scene where terror is met with composed force, but no standalone lesson is stated.

ramacharitamanas::5068.verse_sanskrit: पुनि दसकंठ क्रुद्ध होइ छाँड़ी सक्ति प्रचंड। चली बिभीषन सन्मुख मनहुँ काल कर दंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::5068.verse_hindi: फिर रावण ने क्रोधित होकर प्रचण्ड शक्ति छोड़ी। वह विभीषण के सामने ऐसी चली जैसे काल (यमराज) का दण्ड हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5068.english_translation: Then Ravana, furious, hurled a blazing weapon. It rushed toward Vibhishana like the staff of death.
ramacharitamanas::5068.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / दसकंठ (ten-necked one, Ravana) / क्रुद्ध होइ (becoming angry) / छाँड़ी (released, hurled) / सक्ति (a weapon) / प्रचंड (terrible, fierce) / चली (went, rushed) / बिभीषन सन्मुख (toward Vibhishana) / मनहुँ (as if) / काल कर दंड (the staff of death)
ramacharitamanas::5068.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5068.essence: Anger makes even your own brother look like a target.
ramacharitamanas::5068.simple_meaning: Ravana, enraged, launches a terrible weapon straight at Vibhishana, as if death itself were attacking him.
ramacharitamanas::5068.simple_insight: Anger narrows vision until even family becomes a target.
ramacharitamanas::5068.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ravana has already lost control of the battlefield and his own mind. Seeing Vibhishana stand against him, he hurls a fearsome weapon at his own brother. The moment shows rage turning inward on kin.
ramacharitamanas::5068.modern_relevance: A furious text reply is already typed, and the person on the other end is your own family. In that instant, anger stops being strength and becomes self-damage.
ramacharitamanas::5068.insight: It shows how unchecked rage turns relationship into enemy territory.

ramacharitamanas::5069.verse_sanskrit: आवत देखि सक्ति अति घोरा। प्रनतारति भंजन पन मोरा॥ तुरत बिभीषन पाछें मेला। सन्मुख राम सहेउ सोइ सेला ॥
ramacharitamanas::5069.verse_hindi: अत्यंत भयानक शक्ति को आती देख और यह विचार कर कि मेरा प्रण शरणागत के दुःख का नाश करना है, श्री रामजी ने तुरंत ही विभीषण को पीछे कर लिया और सामने होकर वह शक्ति स्वयं सह ली ॥
ramacharitamanas::5069.english_translation: Seeing the terrible weapon coming, Ram remembered his vow: to protect the one who has surrendered. He quickly moved Vibhishana behind him and took the blow himself.
ramacharitamanas::5069.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / सक्ति (weapon) / अति (very) / घोरा (terrible) / प्रनतारति (the suffering of the surrendered) / भंजन (destroying) / पन (vow) / मोरा (my) ॥ तुरत (immediately) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / पाछें (behind) / मेला (placed) / सन्मुख (in front) / राम (Ram) / सहेउ (endured) / सोइ (that) / सेला (spear/weapon) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5069.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5069.essence: Refuge is real only when you take the wound yourself.
ramacharitamanas::5069.simple_meaning: Ram keeps his promise to protect anyone who comes to him for refuge. He shields Vibhishana and takes the weapon himself.
ramacharitamanas::5069.simple_insight: Real protection means standing where the danger is, not asking someone else to face it.
ramacharitamanas::5069.detailed_meaning: In the battle at Lanka, Ravana hurls a terrible weapon toward Vibhishana. Ram sees it and acts instantly. He moves Vibhishana out of harm's way and receives the strike himself, showing what refuge really means.
ramacharitamanas::5069.modern_relevance: A friend is about to get blamed in a meeting for a mistake you both saw coming. You step in, take the heat, and make sure they are not left exposed.
ramacharitamanas::5069.insight: It shifts devotion from words to protection: the one who shelters others must be willing to absorb the cost.

ramacharitamanas::5070.verse_sanskrit: लागि सक्ति मुरुछा कछु भई। प्रभु कृत खेल सुरन्ह बिकलई॥ देखि बिभीषन प्रभु श्रम पायो। गहि कर गदा क्रुद्ध होइ धायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5070.verse_hindi: शक्ति लगने से उन्हें कुछ मूर्छा हो गई। प्रभु ने तो यह लीला की, पर देवताओं को व्याकुलता हुई। प्रभु को श्रम (शारीरिक कष्ट) प्राप्त हुआ देखकर विभीषण क्रोधित हो हाथ में गदा लेकर दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5070.english_translation: The blow caused him to faint a little. For the Lord, it was all a play, but the gods were unsettled. Seeing the Lord in pain, Vibhishana grew angry, took up his mace, and rushed forward.
ramacharitamanas::5070.translation_literal: लागि (having struck) / सक्ति (the शक्ति weapon) / मुरुछा (fainting) / कछु (some) / भई (happened) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कृत (done) / खेल (play) / सुरन्ह (for the gods) / बिकलई (agitation) / देखि (seeing) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / प्रभु (the Lord) / श्रम (fatigue) / पायो (got) / गहि (grasping) / कर (in hand) / गदा (mace) / क्रुद्ध होइ (becoming angry) / धायो (ran)
ramacharitamanas::5070.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5070.essence: Love rushes forward the moment the beloved seems hurt.
ramacharitamanas::5070.simple_meaning: Ravana's weapon briefly stuns Ram, but the moment is only a divine play. The celestial beings are shaken, and Vibhishana rushes to defend Ram when he sees Ram weary.
ramacharitamanas::5070.simple_insight: Even a small sign of pain in someone you love can awaken fierce loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::5070.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's battlefield, Ravana's weapon lands and Ram seems briefly dazed. The poet reminds us that this is divine play, though the heavens tremble. Vibhishana sees Ram showing strain and immediately charges forward with his mace.
ramacharitamanas::5070.modern_relevance: You see someone you care about flinch after a harsh comment, and something in you tightens at once. Love does that: it turns concern into action before you even think.
ramacharitamanas::5070.insight: It shifts attention from the wound itself to the loyalty it awakens in others.

ramacharitamanas::5071.verse_sanskrit: रे कुभाग्य सठ मंद कुबुद्धे। तैं सुर नर मुनि नाग बिरुद्धे॥ सादर सिव कहुँ सीस चढ़ाए। एक एक के कोटिन्ह पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5071.verse_hindi: (और बोले-) अरे अभागे! मूर्ख, नीच दुर्बुद्धि! तूने देवता, मनुष्य, मुनि, नाग सभी से विरोध किया। तूने आदर सहित शिवजी को सिर चढ़ाए। इसी से एक-एक के बदले में करोड़ों पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5071.english_translation: “O unlucky fool, dull and misguided one, you have made yourself hostile to gods, humans, sages, and serpents. Yet with reverence you placed Shiva on your head, and from each one you received millions in return.”
ramacharitamanas::5071.translation_literal: रे (O) / कुभाग्य (unlucky) / सठ (fool) / मंद (dull) / कुबुद्धे (misguided one) / तैं (you) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / नाग (serpents) / बिरुद्धे (hostile) / सादर (with reverence) / सिव (Shiva) / कहुँ (toward) / सीस (head) / चढ़ाए (placed) / एक एक (each one) / के (of) / कोटिन्ह (millions) / पाए (received)
ramacharitamanas::5071.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5071.essence: Reverence cannot protect a life ruled by arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::5071.simple_meaning: Ravana is mocked for turning against everyone while still honoring Shiva. The verse says that even good acts cannot save a mind ruled by arrogance and bad judgment.
ramacharitamanas::5071.simple_insight: Respect alone is not enough if the heart stays crooked.
ramacharitamanas::5071.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana lies wounded after battling Ram. He is being reminded that he once showed reverence to Shiva, yet still used his power against everyone else. The verse exposes the contradiction at the heart of his downfall.
ramacharitamanas::5071.modern_relevance: You can donate generously, pray sincerely, and still sabotage your life with arrogance in every conversation. A few noble acts cannot cover a pattern of contempt.
ramacharitamanas::5071.insight: It shifts attention from isolated piety to the overall direction of the heart.

ramacharitamanas::5072.verse_sanskrit: तेहि कारन खल अब लगि बाँच्यो। अब तव कालु सीस पर नाच्यो॥ राम बिमुख सठ चहसि संपदा। अस कहि हनेसि माझ उर गदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5072.verse_hindi: उसी कारण से अरे दुष्ट! तू अब तक बचा है, (किन्तु) अब काल तेरे सिर पर नाच रहा है। अरे मूर्ख! तू राम विमुख होकर सम्पत्ति (सुख) चाहता है? ऐसा कहकर विभीषण ने रावण की छाती के बीचों-बीच गदा मारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5072.english_translation: That is why, you villain, you have survived until now. But now time is dancing on your head. Fool, you want prosperity while turning away from Ram? Saying this, Vibhishana struck Ravana's chest with his mace.
ramacharitamanas::5072.translation_literal: तेहि कारन (for that reason) / खल (villain) / अब लगि (until now) / बाँच्यो (have survived) / अब (now) / तव (your) / कालु (time/death) / सीस पर (on the head) / नाच्यो (is dancing) / राम बिमुख (turned away from Ram) / सठ (fool) / चहसि (you want) / संपदा (prosperity) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / हनेसि (struck) / माझ उर (middle of the chest) / गदा (mace)
ramacharitamanas::5072.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5072.essence: Refusing Ram leaves Ravana with nothing but his own downfall.
ramacharitamanas::5072.simple_meaning: Vibhishana tells Ravana he has survived only by past grace, but now his end is near because he still wants comfort while rejecting Ram. Then he strikes Ravana with his mace.
ramacharitamanas::5072.simple_insight: Pride can keep asking for more even when collapse has already begun.
ramacharitamanas::5072.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Vibhishana confronts Ravana after seeing him defy Ram and all right conduct. He warns that Ravana's time is over, then drives a mace into his chest. The verse is part of the blow-by-blow combat, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5072.modern_relevance: You keep doubling down on a choice that is already costing you. The warning has come, the damage is visible, and still the old craving reaches for more.
ramacharitamanas::5072.insight: It shows how refusal to turn back can make a person fight their own ruin.

ramacharitamanas::5073.verse_sanskrit: उर माझ गदा प्रहार घोर कठोर लागत महि पर् यो। दस बदन सोनित स्रवत पुनि संभारि धायो रिस भर् यो॥ द्वौ भिरे अतिबल मल्लजुद्ध बिरुद्ध एकु एकहि हनै। रघुबीर बल दर्पित बिभीषनु घालि नहिं ता कहुँ गनै॥
ramacharitamanas::5073.verse_hindi: बीच छाती में कठोर गदा की घोर और कठिन चोट लगते ही वह पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। उसके दसों मुखों से रुधिर बहने लगा, वह अपने को फिर संभालकर क्रोध में भरा हुआ दौड़ा। दोनों अत्यंत बलवान् योद्धा भिड़ गए और मल्लयुद्ध में एक-दूसरे के विरुद्ध होकर मारने लगे। श्री रघुवीर के बल से गर्वित विभीषण उसको (रावण जैसे जगद्विजयी योद्धा को) पासंग के बराबर भी नहीं समझते।
ramacharitamanas::5073.english_translation: A fierce, crushing blow of the mace struck his chest, and he fell to the ground. Blood flowed from his ten faces, yet he gathered himself and rushed back in rage. The two mighty warriors clashed, locked in wrestling combat, striking each other. Filled with the power of Raghuvir, Vibhishana did not count him as even a trifle.
ramacharitamanas::5073.translation_literal: उर माझ (in the middle of the chest) / गदा (mace) / प्रहार (strike) / घोर (terrible) / कठोर (hard) / लागत (striking) / महि (earth) / पर् (on) / यो (thus) / दस बदन (ten-faced one) / सोनित (blood) / स्रवत (flowing) / पुनि (again) / संभारि (gathering himself) / धायो (rushed) / रिस (anger) / भर् यो (filled) / द्वौ (both) / भिरे (clashed) / अतिबल (very strong) / मल्लजुद्ध (wrestling combat) / बिरुद्ध (opposed) / एकु एकहि (one another) / हनै (strike) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / बल (power) / दर्पित (filled with pride) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / घालि (placing) / नहिं (not) / ता कहुँ (him) / गनै (counted)
ramacharitamanas::5073.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5073.essence: Powerful people can still fall; true steadiness comes from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5073.simple_meaning: This is a battle scene: Ravana is struck, falls, rises again, and keeps fighting. Vibhishana, empowered by Ram, sees Ravana as no great threat.
ramacharitamanas::5073.simple_insight: Sometimes the body falls before the will does. Courage is the choice to rise again.
ramacharitamanas::5073.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final war, Ravana takes a brutal hit to the chest and crashes down, blood on his ten faces. He rises in fury and resumes hand-to-hand combat. The verse also shows Vibhishana, steady in Ram's power, no longer fearing Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::5073.modern_relevance: A boxer gets knocked to the mat in front of a roaring crowd, wipes the blood away, and stands back up. The point is not the fall — it's the refusal to stay down.
ramacharitamanas::5073.insight: It shifts attention from damage to endurance, and from intimidation to steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::5074.verse_sanskrit: उमा बिभीषनु रावनहि सन्मुख चितव कि काउ। सो अब भिरत काल ज्यों श्री रघुबीर प्रभाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5074.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! विभीषण क्या कभी रावण के सामने आँख उठाकर भी देख सकता था? परन्तु अब वही काल के समान उससे भिड़ रहा है। यह श्री रघुवीर का ही प्रभाव है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5074.english_translation: O Uma, could Vibhishana ever even dare to face Ravana? Yet now he fights him like Death itself. Such is the power of Shri Raghubir.
ramacharitamanas::5074.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / सन्मुख (facing) / चितव (looked) / कि (even) / काउ (ever) / सो (he) / अब (now) / भिरत (fighting) / काल ज्यों (like Death) / श्री रघुबीर प्रभाउ (the power of Shri Raghubir)
ramacharitamanas::5074.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5074.essence: Ram's power can turn fear into fearless action.
ramacharitamanas::5074.simple_meaning: Vibhishana once could not even look at Ravana directly, but now he is fighting him fearlessly. That change comes from Ram's power.
ramacharitamanas::5074.simple_insight: Grace can turn fear into courage faster than you expect.
ramacharitamanas::5074.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Shiva points out to Uma the impossible reversal before them: Vibhishana, once too afraid to face Ravana, now attacks him like Death. The verse is a supporting remark in the larger war scene, showing Ram's power working through his devotee.
ramacharitamanas::5074.modern_relevance: Someone who used to shrink in a room finally speaks up and holds their ground. The courage does not come from personality alone; something stronger has steadied them.
ramacharitamanas::5074.insight: It shifts attention from personal bravery to the transforming power behind brave action.

ramacharitamanas::5075.verse_sanskrit: देखा श्रमित बिभीषनु भारी। धायउ हनूमान गिरि धारी॥ रथ तुरंग सारथी निपाता। हृदय माझ तेहि मारेसि लाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5075.verse_hindi: विभीषण को बहुत ही थका हुआ देखकर हनुमान् जी पर्वत धारण किए हुए दौड़े। उन्होंने उस पर्वत से रावण के रथ, घोड़े और सारथी का संहार कर डाला और उसके सीने पर लात मारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5075.english_translation: Seeing Vibhishana exhausted, Hanuman rushed forward carrying a mountain. With that mountain he destroyed Ravana's chariot, horses, and charioteer, then struck him in the chest with his foot.
ramacharitamanas::5075.translation_literal: देखा (saw) / श्रमित (weary) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / भारी (greatly) / धायउ (rushed) / हनूमान (Hanuman) / गिरि धारी (carrying a mountain) / रथ (chariot) / तुरंग (horses) / सारथी (charioteer) / निपाता (destroyed) / हृदय (chest) / माझ (in) / तेहि (him) / मारेसि (struck) / लाता (with the foot)
ramacharitamanas::5075.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5075.essence: True loyalty rushes in before exhaustion becomes defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5075.simple_meaning: Hanuman sees Vibhishana exhausted and rushes in with a mountain, smashing Ravana's chariot and striking him down.
ramacharitamanas::5075.simple_insight: Real loyalty moves fast when someone you care about is struggling.
ramacharitamanas::5075.detailed_meaning: In the heat of Lanka's war, Vibhishana is worn out after fighting Ravana. Hanuman sees his ally in trouble, charges in carrying a mountain, and tears apart Ravana's war machine. The verse is a quick battle turn, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5075.modern_relevance: A friend is getting overwhelmed in the middle of a hard conversation, and you step in without waiting to be asked. That instinct to protect is this moment's energy.
ramacharitamanas::5075.insight: It shows support as immediate action: notice strain, move in, remove pressure.

ramacharitamanas::5076.verse_sanskrit: ठाढ़ रहा अति कंपित गाता। गयउ बिभीषनु जहँ जनत्राता॥ पुनि रावन कपि हतेउ पचारी। चलेउ गगन कपि पूँछ पसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5076.verse_hindi: रावण खड़ा रहा, पर उसका शरीर अत्यंत काँपने लगा। विभीषण वहाँ गए, जहाँ सेवकों के रक्षक श्री रामजी थे। फिर रावण ने ललकारकर हनुमान् जी को मारा। वे पूँछ फैलाकर आकाश में चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5076.english_translation: Ravana stood there, but his body trembled violently. Vibhishana went to where Ram, the protector of servants, was. Then Ravana challenged Hanuman and struck him. Hanuman flew into the sky with his tail spread wide.
ramacharitamanas::5076.translation_literal: ठाढ़ (stood) / रहा (remained) / अति (greatly) / कंपित (shaking) / गाता (body) / गयउ (went) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / जहँ (where) / जनत्राता (protector of servants) / पुनि (then) / रावन (Ravana) / कपि (monkey; Hanuman) / हतेउ (struck) / पचारी (challenged) / चलेउ (went) / गगन (sky) / कपि (Hanuman) / पूँछ (tail) / पसारी (spread out)
ramacharitamanas::5076.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5076.essence: Battle pressure exposes fear, refuge, and defiance at once.
ramacharitamanas::5076.simple_meaning: Ravana trembles in battle, Vibhishana goes to Ram for refuge, and Hanuman leaps back into the sky after being struck.
ramacharitamanas::5076.simple_insight: The scene keeps moving fast, but the real force is courage under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::5076.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana is shaken even while standing his ground. Vibhishana turns toward Ram, the protector of those who seek refuge. In the same clash, Hanuman is struck and rises again, showing the momentum of the war.
ramacharitamanas::5076.modern_relevance: In the middle of a heated argument, one person shakes, another reaches for support, and someone else answers with a sharp comeback. Pressure reveals who stands where.
ramacharitamanas::5076.insight: It shifts attention from the blow itself to the larger battle of resolve, refuge, and retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::5077.verse_sanskrit: गहिसि पूँछ कपि सहित उड़ाना। पुनि फिरि भिरेउ प्रबल हनुमाना॥ लरत अकास जुगल सम जोधा। एकहि एकु हनत करि क्रोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5077.verse_hindi: रावण ने पूँछ पकड़ ली, हनुमान् जी उसको साथ लिए ऊपर उड़े। फिर लौटकर महाबलवान् हनुमान् जी उससे भिड़ गए। दोनों समान योद्धा आकाश में लड़ते हुए एक-दूसरे को क्रोध करके मारने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5077.english_translation: Ravana seized Hanuman's tail and carried him upward. Then the mighty Hanuman turned back and clashed with him again. The two equal warriors fought in the sky, each striking the other in anger.
ramacharitamanas::5077.translation_literal: गहिसि (seized) / पूँछ (tail) / कपि (monkey) / सहित (together with) / उड़ाना (carried upward) / पुनि (then) / फिरि (again) / भिरेउ (clashed) / प्रबल (mighty) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / लरत (fighting) / अकास (sky) / जुगल (both) / सम (equal) / जोधा (warriors) / एकहि (one) / एकु (the other) / हनत (striking) / करि (doing) / क्रोधा (anger)
ramacharitamanas::5077.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5077.essence: A trapped moment becomes a fierce counterattack.
ramacharitamanas::5077.simple_meaning: Ravana grabs Hanuman's tail, but Hanuman turns and fights back in the sky. Their battle is fierce and evenly matched.
ramacharitamanas::5077.simple_insight: Even in chaos, courage can turn capture into resistance.
ramacharitamanas::5077.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's burning skies, Ravana tries to overpower Hanuman by grabbing his tail and lifting him away. But Hanuman refuses to stay trapped. The fight becomes a fierce aerial struggle between two equally matched warriors.
ramacharitamanas::5077.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, tries to twist the story, and expects you to freeze. You recover, answer cleanly, and the whole room feels the shift.
ramacharitamanas::5077.insight: It shows how pressure can be met with instant counterforce instead of panic.

ramacharitamanas::5078.verse_sanskrit: सोहहिं नभ छल बल बहु करहीं। कज्जलगिरि सुमेरु जनु लरहीं॥ बुधि बल निसिचर परइ न पारयो। तब मारुतसुत प्रभु संभार् यो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5078.verse_hindi: दोनों बहुत से छल-बल करते हुए आकाश में ऐसे शोभित हो रहे हैं मानो कज्जलगिरि और सुमेरु पर्वत लड़ रहे हों। जब बुद्धि और बल से राक्षस गिराए न गिरा तब मारुति श्री हनुमान् जी ने प्रभु को स्मरण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5078.english_translation: They shone in the sky, fighting with many tricks and great force, like black mountain and Mount Sumeru battling. When the demon could not be brought down by intelligence or strength, Hanuman remembered the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::5078.translation_literal: सोहहिं (shone) / नभ (sky) / छल (tricks) / बल (force) / बहु (many) / करहीं (do) / कज्जलगिरि (black mountain) / सुमेरु (Sumeru) / जनु (as if) / लरहीं (are fighting)॥ / बुधि (intelligence) / बल (strength) / निसिचर (demon) / परइ (fell) / न पारयो (could not) / तब (then) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / प्रभु (Lord) / संभार्यो (remembered)॥
ramacharitamanas::5078.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5078.essence: When your own power fails, remembrance gives you the next move.
ramacharitamanas::5078.simple_meaning: The two fighters clash in the sky like huge mountains. When brute force and cleverness fail, Hanuman remembers Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5078.simple_insight: Some battles are won only after you stop relying on yourself and remember what truly supports you.
ramacharitamanas::5078.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman and Ravana are locked in aerial combat, matching strength with strength and trick with trick. The fight stalls until Hanuman realises that his own skill is not enough, and he turns inward to remember Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5078.modern_relevance: You keep trying three different fixes on the same broken problem, and nothing moves. Then, in the middle of the mess, you remember who you are fighting for.
ramacharitamanas::5078.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance alone to remembrance as the source of real force.

ramacharitamanas::5079.verse_sanskrit: संभारि श्रीरघुबीर धीर पचारि कपि रावनु हन्यो। महि परत पुनि उठि लरत देवन्ह जुगल कहुँ जय जय भन्यो॥ हनुमंत संकट देखि मर्कट भालु क्रोधातुर चले। रन मत्त रावन सकल सुभट प्रचण्ड भुज बल दलमले॥
ramacharitamanas::5079.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीर का स्मरण करके धीर हनुमान् जी ने ललकारकर रावण को मारा। वे दोनों पृथ्वी पर गिरते और फिर उठकर लड़ते हैं, देवताओं ने दोनों की 'जय-जय' पुकारी। हनुमान् जी पर संकट देखकर वानर-भालू क्रोधातुर होकर दौड़े, किन्तु रण-मद-माते रावण ने सब योद्धाओं को अपनी प्रचण्ड भुजाओं के बल से कुचल और मसल डाला।
ramacharitamanas::5079.english_translation: Remembering the steadfast Lord of the Raghu line, Hanuman challenged and struck Ravana. They fell to the ground, rose again, and fought on; the gods cried victory for both. Seeing Hanuman in danger, the monkeys and bears rushed in anger, but the battle-drunk Ravana crushed all the warriors with the force of his mighty arms.
