ramacharitamanas::5079.translation_literal: संभारि (remembering) / श्रीरघुबीर (the noble Lord of Raghu) / धीर (steady) / पचारि (challenging, shouting at) / कपि (monkey) / रावनु (Ravana) / हन्यो (struck, killed) / महि (on the ground) / परत (falling) / पुनि (again) / उठि (rising) / लरत (fighting) / देवन्ह (by the gods) / जुगल (both) / कहुँ (for) / जय जय (victory, victory) / भन्यो (was said) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / संकट (danger) / देखि (seeing) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / क्रोधातुर (filled with anger) / चले (ran) / रन (battle) / मत्त (intoxicated) / रावन (Ravana) / सकल (all) / सुभट (warriors) / प्रचण्ड (fierce) / भुज (arms) / बल (strength) / दलमले (crushed, ground down)
ramacharitamanas::5079.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5079.essence: Bravery ignites the fight, but brute force still rules the field.
ramacharitamanas::5079.simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps fighting Ravana with fearless courage, while the monkey and bear army rushes to defend him. Ravana still overwhelms the warriors with his great strength.
ramacharitamanas::5079.simple_insight: Courage can spread, but so can chaos. Some moments are won by sheer force before wisdom returns.
ramacharitamanas::5079.detailed_meaning: On Lanka's battlefield, Hanuman calls on Ram and presses Ravana hard enough that even the gods cheer both fighters. But the clash is not over: as the monkey and bear forces surge to protect Hanuman, Ravana, drunk on battle, smashes through them with brutal strength.
ramacharitamanas::5079.modern_relevance: You jump into a heated group chat to defend a friend, and suddenly everyone is shouting at once. Loyalty is noble, but raw force can still flatten the room.
ramacharitamanas::5079.insight: It shifts attention from heroic impulse alone to the cost of uncontrolled force in conflict.

ramacharitamanas::5080.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुबीर पचारे धाए कीस प्रचंड। कपि बल प्रबल देखि तेहिं कीन्ह प्रगट पाषंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::5080.verse_hindi: तब श्री रघुवीर के ललकारने पर प्रचण्ड वीर वानर दौड़े। वानरों के प्रबल दल को देखकर रावण ने माया प्रकट की ॥
ramacharitamanas::5080.english_translation: Then, at Raghubir's challenge, the fierce monkeys rushed forward. Seeing the monkeys' powerful force, Ravana revealed his illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5080.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / पचारे (challenged, called out) / धाए (rushed) / कीस (monkeys) / प्रचंड (fierce, powerful) / कपि (monkey) / बल (strength) / प्रबल (strong, intense) / देखि (seeing) / तेहिं (he) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रगट (manifest) / पाषंड (illusion, deceit)
ramacharitamanas::5080.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5080.simple_meaning: At Ram's challenge, the monkey warriors rushed ahead. Ravana saw their strength and answered with illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5080.simple_insight: Pressure can make hidden tactics surface.
ramacharitamanas::5080.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final battle, Ram's call sends the monkey army surging forward. Ravana, cornered by their strength, does not yield; he answers with deception. The verse is a brief battle move, not a teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::5080.modern_relevance: A meeting turns tense, and someone who feels outmatched suddenly starts deflecting, bluffing, or changing the subject. When real strength appears, weak tactics often show themselves.
ramacharitamanas::5080.insight: It shows how ego under pressure reaches for concealment instead of clarity.

ramacharitamanas::5081.verse_sanskrit: अंतरधान भयउ छन एका। पुनि प्रगटे खल रूप अनेका॥ रघुपति कटक भालु कपि जेते। जहँ तहँ प्रगट दसानन तेते ॥
ramacharitamanas::5081.verse_hindi: क्षणभर के लिए वह अदृश्य हो गया। फिर उस दुष्ट ने अनेकों रूप प्रकट किए। श्री रघुनाथजी की सेना में जितने रीछ-वानर थे, उतने ही रावण जहाँ-तहाँ (चारों ओर) प्रकट हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5081.english_translation: For a moment he disappeared. Then the villain appeared in many forms. In Raghunath's army, wherever there were bears and monkeys, there Ravana appeared as many.
ramacharitamanas::5081.translation_literal: अंतरधान (disappeared) / भयउ (became) / छन (moment) / एका (one) / पुनि (again) / प्रगटे (appeared) / खल (villain) / रूप (forms) / अनेका (many) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / कटक (army) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / जेते (as many as) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / प्रगट (appeared) / दसानन (Ravana) / तेते (so many)
ramacharitamanas::5081.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5081.essence: False appearances multiply fear before anyone can see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::5081.simple_meaning: Ravana vanishes, then multiplies himself into many forms to confuse Ram's army.
ramacharitamanas::5081.simple_insight: Chaos can look overwhelming, but it is still just a trick of appearances.
ramacharitamanas::5081.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ravana uses illusion to shake Hanuman and the monkey army. He disappears, then seems to appear everywhere at once, forcing Ram's side into confusion before the next outcry.
ramacharitamanas::5081.modern_relevance: A crowded group chat suddenly fills with five versions of the same rumor, and panic spreads before anyone checks the source. This verse captures how confusion multiplies when appearance outruns discernment.
ramacharitamanas::5081.insight: It shows how illusion can scatter attention and make fear feel larger than it is.

ramacharitamanas::5082.verse_sanskrit: देखे कपिन्ह अमित दससीसा। जहँ तहँ भजे भालु अरु कीसा॥ भागे बानर धरहिं न धीरा। त्राहि त्राहि लछिमन रघुबीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5082.verse_hindi: वानरों ने अपरिमित रावण देखे। भालू और वानर सब जहाँ-तहाँ (इधर-उधर) भाग चले। वानर धीरज नहीं धरते। हे लक्ष्मणजी! हे रघुवीर! बचाइए, बचाइए, यों पुकारते हुए वे भागे जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5082.english_translation: The monkeys saw countless Ravanas. The bears and monkeys ran everywhere. The monkeys could not keep their courage. Crying, 'Save us, Lakshman! Save us, Raghubir!' they fled.
ramacharitamanas::5082.translation_literal: देखे (saw) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / अमित (countless) / दससीसा (ten-headed ones, Ravanas) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / भजे (ran) / भालु (bears) / अरु (and) / कीसा (monkeys) / भागे (ran away) / बानर (monkeys) / धरहिं (hold) / न (not) / धीरा (steadiness) / त्राहि त्राहि (save, save) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir)
ramacharitamanas::5082.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5082.essence: Illusion makes one enemy feel like many.
ramacharitamanas::5082.simple_meaning: Ravana multiplies into countless forms, and the monkey army panics and runs in every direction, crying out for Lakshman and Ram to save them.
ramacharitamanas::5082.simple_insight: Fear can spread fast when the threat seems everywhere at once.
ramacharitamanas::5082.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just unleashed illusion against Ram's army. The monkeys and bears suddenly see him everywhere, lose their steadiness, and cry out in panic. This verse shows the immediate effect of his trick before the battle turns again.
ramacharitamanas::5082.modern_relevance: You open your phone and see ten urgent messages, three deadlines, and a crisis in the family chat. For a moment, everything feels like it's coming from everywhere at once.
ramacharitamanas::5082.insight: It shows how confusion multiplies fear before reason can regain control.

ramacharitamanas::5083.verse_sanskrit: दहँ दिसि धावहिं कोटिन्ह रावन। गर्जहिं घोर कठोर भयावन॥ डरे सकल सुर चले पराई। जय कै आस तजहु अब भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5083.verse_hindi: दसों दिशाओं में करोड़ों रावण दौड़ते हैं और घोर, कठोर भयानक गर्जन कर रहे हैं। सब देवता डर गए और ऐसा कहते हुए भाग चले कि हे भाई! अब जय की आशा छोड़ दो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5083.english_translation: Ravana multiplies into millions, rushing in all ten directions with terrible, harsh roars. All the radiant beings are frightened and flee, saying, “Brother, give up hope of victory now.”
ramacharitamanas::5083.translation_literal: दहँ दिसि (in ten directions) / धावहिं (run) / कोटिन्ह (millions of) / रावन (Ravanas) / गर्जहिं (roar) / घोर (terrible) / कठोर (harsh) / भयावन (frightening) / डरे (were afraid) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / चले (went) / पराई (away) / जय (victory) / कै (of) / आस (hope) / तजहु (give up) / अब (now) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::5083.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5083.essence: Fear can make one enemy feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::5083.simple_meaning: Ravana seems to be everywhere at once, terrifying everyone so badly that even the radiant beings lose hope and run away.
ramacharitamanas::5083.simple_insight: Fear can make the strongest side feel defeated before the fight is over.
ramacharitamanas::5083.detailed_meaning: In the battle for Lanka, Ravana multiplies himself into countless forms and charges from every direction. The radiant beings panic and retreat, convinced victory is no longer possible. This verse heightens the crisis before the next turn in the war.
ramacharitamanas::5083.modern_relevance: A project collapses into chaos, every problem seems to arrive at once, and even your confidence starts to shake. This is what panic feels like when it multiplies the threat.
ramacharitamanas::5083.insight: It shows how fear distorts reality until one obstacle looks like a thousand.

ramacharitamanas::5084.verse_sanskrit: सब सुर जिते एक दसकंधर। अब बहु भए तकहु गिरि कंदर॥ रहे बिरंचि संभु मुनि ग्यानी। जिन्ह जिन्ह प्रभु महिमा कछु जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5084.verse_hindi: एक ही रावण ने सब देवताओं को जीत लिया था, अब तो बहुत से रावण हो गए हैं। इससे अब पहाड़ की गुफाओं का आश्रय लो (अर्थात् उनमें छिप रहो)। वहाँ ब्रह्मा, शम्भु और ज्ञानी मुनि ही डटे रहे, जिन्होंने प्रभु की कुछ महिमा जानी थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5084.english_translation: One Ravana had already conquered all the radiant beings; now many Ravanas have appeared. So take shelter in mountain caves. Brahma, Shiva, and the wise sages remained fearless because they knew something of the Lord's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::5084.translation_literal: सब (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / जिते (conquered) / एक (one) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / अब (now) / बहु (many) / भए (became) / तकहु (take shelter) / गिरि (mountain) / कंदर (caves) / रहे (remained) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / संभु (Shiva) / मुनि (sages) / ग्यानी (knowing ones) / जिन्ह (those who) / जिन्ह (those who) / प्रभु (Lord) / महिमा (greatness) / कछु (some) / जानी (knew)
ramacharitamanas::5084.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5084.essence: Fear multiplies when Ram's greatness is forgotten.
ramacharitamanas::5084.simple_meaning: Ravana's terror has multiplied so much that only those who know the Lord's greatness stay unafraid.
ramacharitamanas::5084.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when you remember what is larger than the threat.
ramacharitamanas::5084.detailed_meaning: In the chaos of Lanka, the monkey army sees Ravana everywhere and panics. This verse contrasts that fear with the calm of Brahma, Shiva, and the sages, who remain steady because they understand Ram's greatness better than the scene before them.
ramacharitamanas::5084.modern_relevance: You open your phone and see one alarming headline after another until everything feels like the same threat. The panic eases only when you remember there is something larger than the noise.
ramacharitamanas::5084.insight: It shifts attention from multiplying threats to remembering the scale of divine protection.

ramacharitamanas::5085.verse_sanskrit: जाना प्रताप ते रहे निर्भय कपिन्ह रिपु माने फुरे। चले बिचलि मर्कट भालु सकल कृपाल पाहि भयातुरे॥ हनुमंत अंगद नील नल अतिबल लरत रन बाँकुरे। मर्दहिं दसानन कोटि कोटिन्ह कपट भू भट अंकुरे॥
ramacharitamanas::5085.verse_hindi: जो प्रभु का प्रताप जानते थे, वे निर्भय डटे रहे। वानरों ने शत्रुओं (बहुत से रावणों) को सच्चा ही मान लिया। (इससे) सब वानर-भालू विचलित होकर 'हे कृपालु! रक्षा कीजिए' (यों पुकारते हुए) भय से व्याकुल होकर भाग चले। अत्यंत बलवान् रणबाँकुरे हनुमान् जी, अंगद, नील और नल लड़ते हैं और कपट रूपी भूमि से अंकुर की भाँति उपजे हुए कोटि-कोटि योद्धा रावणों को मसलते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::5085.english_translation: Those who knew his power stood fearless, but the monkeys mistook the enemies as real. All the monkeys and bears, shaken and crying, rushed away in fear. Yet Hanuman, Angada, Nila, and Nala, mighty and bold in battle, crushed the countless Ravanas, those warriors born from the soil of illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5085.translation_literal: जाना (having known) / प्रताप (power, glory) / ते (by that) / रहे (remained) / निर्भय (fearless) / कपिन्ह (the monkeys) / रिपु (enemy) / माने (considered) / फुरे (real, true) / चले (went) / बिचलि (shaken) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / सकल (all) / कृपाल (O merciful one) / पाहि (protect) / भयातुरे (fear-stricken) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / अंगद (Angada) / नील (Nila) / नल (Nala) / अतिबल (very strong) / लरत (fighting) / रन (battle) / बाँकुरे (bold, fearless) / मर्दहिं (crush) / दसानन (Ravana) / कोटि कोटिन्ह (millions and millions) / कपट (illusion, deceit) / भू (earth, soil) / भट (warriors) / अंकुरे (sprouts, shoots)
ramacharitamanas::5085.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5085.essence: Illusion terrifies the unsteady, but clear courage cuts through it.
ramacharitamanas::5085.simple_meaning: Those who understood Ram's power stayed fearless. The rest were shaken by illusion and ran in fear, while Hanuman, Angada, Nila, and Nala kept fighting and crushed the fake Ravanas.
ramacharitamanas::5085.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when you see clearly; illusion grows when you take appearances as real.
ramacharitamanas::5085.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's battlefield, Ravana's illusion multiplies into countless terrifying forms. Some monkeys panic and call for protection, but Hanuman, Angada, Nila, and Nala keep their footing and strike through the deception. The verse shows confusion breaking some and courage revealing others.
ramacharitamanas::5085.modern_relevance: A group chat explodes with worst-case assumptions, and suddenly everyone is reacting to a problem that isn't fully real. One steady person sees through the panic and acts anyway.
ramacharitamanas::5085.insight: It trains you to separate appearance from reality before fear starts steering your actions.

ramacharitamanas::5086.verse_sanskrit: सुर बानर देखे बिकल हँस्यो कोसलाधीस। सजि सारंग एक सर हते सकल दससीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5086.verse_hindi: देवताओं और वानरों को विकल देखकर कोसलपति श्री रामजी हँसे और शार्गं धनुष पर एक बाण चढ़ाकर (माया के बने हुए) सब रावणों को मार डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::5086.english_translation: Seeing the gods and monkeys bewildered, the Lord of Kosala smiled. He fitted one arrow to his bow and struck down all the many Ravanas.
ramacharitamanas::5086.translation_literal: सुर (gods) / बानर (monkeys) / देखे (saw) / बिकल (bewildered) / हँस्यो (smiled) / कोसलाधीस (Lord of Kosala) / सजि (having fitted) / सारंग (the bow) / एक (one) / सर (arrow) / हते (struck down) / सकल (all) / दससीस (ten-headed ones / Ravanas)
ramacharitamanas::5086.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5086.essence: One clear strike can end a whole field of confusion.
ramacharitamanas::5086.simple_meaning: Ram sees everyone shaken, smiles, and destroys the many false Ravanas with one arrow.
ramacharitamanas::5086.simple_insight: Even overwhelming confusion can end in a single clear act.
ramacharitamanas::5086.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has turned strange: the gods and monkeys are bewildered by Ravana's multiplying forms. Ram, calm as ever, smiles, draws his bow, and ends the illusion in one decisive strike.
ramacharitamanas::5086.modern_relevance: A room full of people is panicking, the problem looks endless, and everyone is waiting for someone to fix it. Then one clear decision cuts through the chaos.
ramacharitamanas::5086.insight: It shifts attention from the appearance of many problems to the one clear action that resolves them.

ramacharitamanas::5087.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु छन महुँ माया सब काटी। जिमि रबि उएँ जाहिं तम फाटी॥ रावनु एकु देखि सुर हरषे। फिरे सुमन बहु प्रभु पर बरषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5087.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने क्षणभर में सब माया काट डाली। जैसे सूर्य के उदय होते ही अंधकार की राशि फट जाती है (नष्ट हो जाती है)। अब एक ही रावण को देखकर देवता हर्षित हुए और उन्होंने लौटकर प्रभु पर बहुत से पुष्प बरसाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5087.english_translation: The Lord cut through all the illusion in a moment, just as darkness breaks when the sun rises. Seeing only one Ravana now, the radiant beings rejoiced and showered many flowers on the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::5087.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / छन महुँ (in a moment) / माया (illusion) / सब (all) / काटी (cut away) / जिमि (just as) / रबि (the sun) / उएँ (having risen) / जाहिं (goes) / तम (darkness) / फाटी (split, break apart) / रावनु (Ravana) / एकु (one) / देखि (seeing) / सुर (the radiant beings) / हरषे (rejoiced) / फिरे (returned) / सुमन (flowers) / बहु (many) / प्रभु पर (upon the Lord) / बरषे (rained)
ramacharitamanas::5087.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5087.essence: Clarity can end a whole storm of confusion at once.
ramacharitamanas::5087.simple_meaning: Ram instantly ends the magical illusion, and the gods rejoice when they see the real Ravana again.
ramacharitamanas::5087.simple_insight: What looked overwhelming vanishes fast when clarity arrives.
ramacharitamanas::5087.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana has multiplied himself through illusion to confuse the allies of Ram. In the next breath, Ram cuts through the deception, revealing the single real Ravana. The gods rejoice and shower flowers as the false fear disappears.
ramacharitamanas::5087.modern_relevance: You panic when a problem looks like ten problems at once, then one clear look shows it was never that large.
ramacharitamanas::5087.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to appearances to seeing what is actually there.

ramacharitamanas::5088.verse_sanskrit: भुज उठाइ रघुपति कपि फेरे। फिरे एक एकन्ह तब टेरे॥ प्रभु बलु पाइ भालु कपि धाए। तरल तमकि संजुग महि आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5088.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने भुजा उठाकर सब वानरों को लौटाया। तब वे एक-दूसरे को पुकार-पुकार कर लौट आए। प्रभु का बल पाकर रीछ-वानर दौड़ पड़े। जल्दी से कूदकर वे रणभूमि में आ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5088.english_translation: Raghupati raised his arm and sent the monkeys back. Then they returned, calling to one another. Filled with the Lord's strength, the bears and monkeys rushed forward and leapt back into the battle.
ramacharitamanas::5088.translation_literal: भुज (arm) / उठाइ (raising) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कपि (monkeys) / फेरे (sent back) / फिरे (returned) / एक एकन्ह (one by one, to one another) / तब (then) / टेरे (called) / प्रभु (Lord) / बलु (strength) / पाइ (having obtained) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / धाए (rushed) / तरल (swiftly) / तमकि (leaping) / संजुग (battle) / महि (to the ground / into the field) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::5088.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5088.essence: A single signal from Ram turns retreat into renewed charge.
ramacharitamanas::5088.simple_meaning: Ram signals the monkeys to pull back, then they regroup and surge into battle again with renewed strength.
ramacharitamanas::5088.simple_insight: Real courage is not panic or frenzy; it is returning together when the moment calls.
ramacharitamanas::5088.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ram has just cut through Ravana's illusion. With one raised arm, he gathers the monkey and bear army back into formation. They answer each other, regain heart, and rush forward again as the fight continues.
ramacharitamanas::5088.modern_relevance: A team freezes after a failed pitch, then someone raises a hand and resets everyone. The energy comes back not from ego, but from shared trust and a clear signal.
ramacharitamanas::5088.insight: It shows how calm leadership restores a scattered group and turns confusion back into coordinated action.

ramacharitamanas::5089.verse_sanskrit: अस्तुति करत देवतन्हि देखें। भयउँ एक मैं इन्ह के लेखें॥ सठहु सदा तुम्ह मोर मरायल। अस कहि कोपि गगन पर धायल ॥
ramacharitamanas::5089.verse_hindi: देवताओं को श्री रामजी की स्तुति करते देख कर रावण ने सोचा, मैं इनकी समझ में एक हो गया, (परन्तु इन्हें यह पता नहीं कि इनके लिए मैं एक ही बहुत हूँ) और कहा- अरे मूर्खों! तुम तो सदा के ही मेरे मरैल (मेरी मार खाने वाले) हो। ऐसा कहकर वह क्रोध करके आकाश पर (देवताओं की ओर) दौड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5089.english_translation: Seeing the deities praising Ram, Ravana thought, "I am one in their eyes, but to them I am far too many." He shouted, "You fools, you are always the ones I strike down!" Then, enraged, he rushed through the sky.
ramacharitamanas::5089.translation_literal: अस्तुति (praise) / करत (doing) / देवतन्हि (the deities) / देखें (saw) । भयउँ (I became) / एक (one) / मैं (I) / इन्ह के लेखें (in their view) ॥ सठहु (fools) / सदा (always) / तुम्ह (you) / मोर (my) / मरायल (the ones struck down) । अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / कोपि (in anger) / गगन पर (into the sky) / धायल (rushed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5089.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5089.essence: Ego turns admiration into insult and then into attack.
ramacharitamanas::5089.simple_meaning: Ravana sees the deities praising Ram and reacts with anger and contempt. He boasts that they are always the ones he defeats, then rushes toward them in fury.
ramacharitamanas::5089.simple_insight: Pride cannot tolerate being outshone, so it turns praise into rage.
ramacharitamanas::5089.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war, the deities are praising Ram after seeing his power. Ravana hears it and bristles, mocking them and charging upward. The verse shows his ego flaring before the next clash.
ramacharitamanas::5089.modern_relevance: You hear someone else being praised for the exact thing you wanted credit for. Your face tightens, and the need to prove yourself starts the next mistake.
ramacharitamanas::5089.insight: It exposes how wounded pride rushes straight into reckless action.

ramacharitamanas::5090.verse_sanskrit: हाहाकार करत सुर भागे। खलहु जाहु कहँ मोरें आगे॥ देखि बिकल सुर अंगद धायो। कूदि चरन गहि भूमि गिरायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5090.verse_hindi: देवता हाहाकार करते हुए भागे। (रावण ने कहा-) दुष्टों! मेरे आगे से कहाँ जा सकोगे? देवताओं को व्याकुल देखकर अंगद दौड़े और उछलकर रावण का पैर पकड़कर (उन्होंने) उसको पृथ्वी पर गिरा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5090.english_translation: The devas fled in panic. Ravana shouted, "O vile ones, where can you go before me?" Seeing the devas distressed, Angada rushed forward, leapt, seized Ravana's foot, and threw him to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::5090.translation_literal: हाहाकार (with cries of alarm) / करत (doing) / सुर (the devas) / भागे (fled) / खलहु (O wicked one) / जाहु (go) / कहँ (where) / मोरें (before me) / आगे (in front) / देखि (seeing) / बिकल (distressed) / सुर (the devas) / अंगद (Angada) / धायो (rushed) / कूदि (leaping) / चरन (foot) / गहि (seizing) / भूमि (to the ground) / गिरायो (threw down)
ramacharitamanas::5090.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5090.essence: Angada answers fear with immediate force.
ramacharitamanas::5090.simple_meaning: The gods run in fear, Ravana boasts, and Angada jumps in to strike him down.
ramacharitamanas::5090.simple_insight: Courage can appear in a single leap when fear is at its loudest.
ramacharitamanas::5090.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's war, Ravana is still raging while the devas flee in alarm. Angada sees their distress, rushes at him, grabs his foot, and throws him down. The moment is a flash of battlefield courage, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5090.insight: It shows a sudden act of bravery that interrupts panic and humiliation.

ramacharitamanas::5091.verse_sanskrit: गहि भूमि पार् यो लात मार् यो बालिसुत प्रभु पहिं गयो। संभारि उठि दसकंठ घोर कठोर रव गर्जत भयो॥ करि दाप चाप चढ़ाइ दस संधानि सर बहु बरषई। किए सकल भट घायल भयाकुल देखि निज बल हरषई॥
ramacharitamanas::5091.verse_hindi: उसे पकड़कर पृथ्वी पर गिराकर लात मारकर बालिपुत्र अंगद प्रभु के पास चले गए। रावण संभलकर उठा और बड़े भंयकर कठोर शब्द से गरजने लगा। वह दर्प करके दसों धनुष चढ़ाकर उन पर बहुत से बाण संधान करके बरसाने लगा। उसने सब योद्धाओं को घायल और भय से व्याकुल कर दिया और अपना बल देखकर वह हर्षित होने लगा।
ramacharitamanas::5091.english_translation: Seizing him, Angad threw him to the ground and kicked him before going to the Lord. Ravana recovered, roared with a fierce and harsh voice, drew his ten bows, and showered many arrows. He wounded all the warriors, filled them with fear, and rejoiced in his own strength.
ramacharitamanas::5091.translation_literal: गहि (seizing) / भूमि (the ground) / पार् यो (threw down) / लात मार् यो (kicked) / बालिसुत (the son of Bali, Angad) / प्रभु पहिं (to the Lord) / गयो (went) / संभारि (recovering) / उठि (rose) / दसकंठ (ten-throated, Ravana) / घोर (fierce) / कठोर (harsh) / रव (voice) / गर्जत (roaring) / भयो (became) / करि (doing) / दाप (pride) / चाप (bows) / चढ़ाइ (drawing) / दस (ten) / संधानि (aiming) / सर (arrows) / बहु (many) / बरषई (rained) / किए (made) / सकल (all) / भट (warriors) / घायल (wounded) / भयाकुल (fear-stricken) / देखि (seeing) / निज (his own) / बल (strength) / हरषई (rejoiced)
ramacharitamanas::5091.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5091.essence: Wounded pride answers humiliation with more violence.
ramacharitamanas::5091.simple_meaning: Angad humbles Ravana, but Ravana quickly rises and attacks with fierce pride, injuring the warriors and delighting in his own power.
ramacharitamanas::5091.simple_insight: Pride can turn pain into fuel, but it still cannot stay humble.
ramacharitamanas::5091.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Angad has just insulted Ravana by throwing him down and kicking him. Ravana rises in fury, floods the field with arrows, and grows pleased with his own force. The scene shows ego answering humiliation with violence.
ramacharitamanas::5091.modern_relevance: Someone mocks you in a group chat, and your first urge is to fire back harder. The verse shows how wounded pride reaches for force instead of clarity.
ramacharitamanas::5091.insight: It shows how ego reacts to humiliation by escalating conflict and feeding on its own display of strength.

ramacharitamanas::5092.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुपति रावन के सीस भुजा सर चाप। काटे बहुत बढ़े पुनि जिमि तीरथ कर पाप ॥
ramacharitamanas::5092.verse_hindi: तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने रावण के सिर, भुजाएँ, बाण और धनुष काट डाले। पर वे फिर बहुत बढ़ गए, जैसे तीर्थ में किए हुए पाप बढ़ जाते हैं (कई गुना अधिक भयानक फल उत्पन्न करते हैं)! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5092.english_translation: Then Raghu's lord cut off Ravana's heads, arms, arrows, and bow. But they grew back again, just as sins done at sacred places grow into even worse consequences.
ramacharitamanas::5092.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / रावन (Ravana) / के (of) / सीस (heads) / भुजा (arms) / सर (arrows) / चाप (bow) / काटे (cut off) / बहुत (many) / बढ़े (grew) / पुनि (again) / जिमि (just as) / तीरथ (sacred place) / कर (done at) / पाप (sins)
ramacharitamanas::5092.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5092.essence: What is rooted in ego returns until the root is cut.
ramacharitamanas::5092.simple_meaning: Ravana's heads, arms, arrows, and bow are cut off, but they keep growing back. The image compares this to wrongdoing that only multiplies its own consequences.
ramacharitamanas::5092.simple_insight: Some forces do not yield to force alone; they keep returning until the root is changed.
ramacharitamanas::5092.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram keeps striking Ravana down, yet Ravana's many heads and arms return again and again. The image shows a stubborn ego that cannot be ended by ordinary blows, and the comparison to sins at sacred places makes the danger feel even sharper.
ramacharitamanas::5092.modern_relevance: You keep deleting the same problem from your phone, and it returns through another app, another tab, another habit. Until the source changes, the pattern keeps coming back.
ramacharitamanas::5092.insight: It shifts attention from defeating symptoms to removing the underlying cause.

ramacharitamanas::5093.verse_sanskrit: सिर भुज बाढ़ि देखि रिपु केरी। भालु कपिन्ह रिस भई घनेरी॥ मरत न मूढ़ कटेहुँ भुज सीसा। धाए कोपि भालु भट कीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5093.verse_hindi: शत्रु के सिर और भुजाओं की बढ़ती देखकर रीछ-वानरों को बहुत ही क्रोध हुआ। यह मूर्ख भुजाओं के और सिरों के कटने पर भी नहीं मरता, (ऐसा कहते हुए) भालू और वानर योद्धा क्रोध करके दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5093.english_translation: Seeing the enemy's heads and arms grow back, the bears and monkeys became furious. "That fool does not die even when his heads and arms are cut!" Crying out in anger, the bears and monkey warriors rushed forward.
ramacharitamanas::5093.translation_literal: सिर (heads) / भुज (arms) / बाढ़ि (growing) / देखि (seeing) / रिपु (enemy) / केरी (of) / भालु (bears) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / रिस (anger) / भई (became) / घनेरी (very great)॥ / मरत (dies) / न (not) / मूढ़ (fool) / कटेहुँ (even when cut) / भुज (arms) / सीसा (heads) / धाए (rushed) / कोपि (in fury) / भालु (bears) / भट (warriors) / कीसा (monkeys) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5093.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5093.essence: The battle intensifies when defeat refuses to stay defeated.
ramacharitamanas::5093.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear warriors are enraged because Ravana's cut-off heads and arms keep growing back, so they charge again.
ramacharitamanas::5093.simple_insight: Some fights only harden resolve; anger can become fuel when evil seems impossible to stop.
ramacharitamanas::5093.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana keeps regenerating after every blow. Angad, Hanuman, and the other monkey and bear warriors watch his heads and arms grow back and lose patience. This verse shows the battle turning fiercer, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::5093.modern_relevance: You keep fixing the same problem, and it keeps coming back worse. At some point, frustration turns into a harder push.
ramacharitamanas::5093.insight: It shifts attention from strategy to escalation: when resistance multiplies, the response becomes collective force.

ramacharitamanas::5094.verse_sanskrit: बालितनय मारुति नल नीला। बानरराज दुबिद बलसीला॥ बिटप महीधर करहिं प्रहारा। सोइ गिरि तरु गहि कपिन्ह सो मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5094.verse_hindi: बालिपुत्र अंगद, मारुति हनुमान् जी, नल, नील, वानरराज सुग्रीव और द्विविद आदि बलवान् उस पर वृक्ष और पर्वतों का प्रहार करते हैं। वह उन्हीं पर्वतों और वृक्षों को पकड़कर वानरों को मारता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5094.english_translation: Angada, Hanuman, Nala, Neela, Sugriva, and the mighty monkey warriors, including Dvivida, hurl trees and mountains at him. He seizes those same mountains and trees and kills the monkeys with them.
ramacharitamanas::5094.translation_literal: बालितनय (son of Bali) / मारुति (Hanuman) / नल (Nala) / नीला (Neela) / बानरराज (king of the monkeys) / दुबिद (Dvivida) / बलसीला (strong and valiant)॥ / बिटप (tree) / महीधर (mountain) / करहिं (do) / प्रहारा (strikes) / सोइ (those same) / गिरि (mountains) / तरु (trees) / गहि (seizing) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / सो (he) / मारा (killed)॥
ramacharitamanas::5094.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5094.essence: The battle escalates as each side turns the other's weapons back on them.
ramacharitamanas::5094.simple_meaning: The monkey warriors attack with trees and mountains, but the enemy grabs those weapons and turns them back on them.
ramacharitamanas::5094.simple_insight: In a crisis, force can be met with force, and the same weapon can be turned against you.
ramacharitamanas::5094.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, the monkey army presses its attack on Ravana's side with trees and mountains. But the enemy is so fierce that he catches those very weapons and uses them to kill the attackers. The scene is still pure combat, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5094.insight: It records a violent exchange in the war, with no separate moral claim.

ramacharitamanas::5095.verse_sanskrit: एक नखन्हि रिपु बपुष बिदारी। भागि चलहिं एक लातन्ह मारी। तब नल नील सिरन्हि चढ़ि गयऊ। नखन्हि लिलार बिदारत भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5095.verse_hindi: कोई एक वानर नखों से शत्रु के शरीर को फाड़कर भाग जाते हैं, तो कोई उसे लातों से मारकर। तब नल और नील रावण के सिरों पर चढ़ गए और नखों से उसके ललाट को फाड़ने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5095.english_translation: One monkey tears the enemy’s body with claws and runs off; another strikes with kicks. Then Nala and Nila climbed onto Ravana’s heads and began tearing his forehead with their claws.
ramacharitamanas::5095.translation_literal: एक (one) / नखन्हि (with claws) / रिपु (enemy) / बपुष (body) / बिदारी (tearing apart) / भागि (running away) / चलहिं (they move) / एक (one) / लातन्ह (with kicks) / मारी (striking) / तब (then) / नल (Nala) / नील (Nila) / सिरन्हि (on heads) / चढ़ि (climbing) / गयऊ (went) / नखन्हि (with claws) / लिलार (forehead) / बिदारत (tearing) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::5095.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5095.essence: The war turns savage as the monkey warriors swarm Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::5095.simple_meaning: The monkey warriors attack Ravana in many ways, clawing, kicking, and tearing at his forehead. This is a vivid battle detail, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::5095.simple_insight: Sometimes the scene is only the scene: relentless force, no reflection, no lesson yet.
ramacharitamanas::5095.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, the monkey army swarms Ravana from every side. Nala and Nila leap onto his heads and claw at his forehead while others strike and dart away. The verse heightens the chaos before the next response.
ramacharitamanas::5095.insight: It stays in the action, showing the battle’s ferocity without shifting into reflection.

ramacharitamanas::5096.verse_sanskrit: रुधिर देखि बिषाद उर भारी। तिन्हहि धरन कहुँ भुजा पसारी॥ गहे न जाहिं करन्हि पर फिरहीं। जनु जुग मधुप कमल बन चरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5096.verse_hindi: खून देखकर उसे हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ। उसने उनको पकड़ने के लिए हाथ फैलाए, पर वे पकड़ में नहीं आते, हाथों के ऊपर-ऊपर ही फिरते हैं मानो दो भौंरे कमलों के वन में विचरण कर रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5096.english_translation: Seeing the blood, grief weighed heavily on his heart. He stretched out his arms to seize them, but they could not be caught; they kept circling just beyond his hands, like two bees moving through a grove of lotuses.
ramacharitamanas::5096.translation_literal: रुधिर (blood) / देखि (seeing) / बिषाद (grief) / उर (heart) / भारी (heavy) / तिन्हहि (them) / धरन (to hold) / कहुँ (for) / भुजा (arms) / पसारी (stretched out)॥ गहे (caught) / न (not) / जाहिं (are able to be) / करन्हि (by the hands) / पर (upon) / फिरहीं (they keep circling)॥ जनु (as if) / जुग (pair) / मधुप (bees) / कमल (lotus) / बन (grove) / चरहीं (wander/feed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5096.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5096.essence: Grief and rage make even power slip through empty hands.
ramacharitamanas::5096.simple_meaning: Ravana is shaken by the sight of blood and keeps reaching for the monkeys, but they slip past his grasp like bees around flowers.
ramacharitamanas::5096.simple_insight: Pride can turn frantic when it finally meets resistance.
ramacharitamanas::5096.detailed_meaning: In the battle at Lanka, Ravana is being battered by the monkey warriors. The sight of blood fills him with grief and agitation, and he keeps lunging to seize them. But they stay just beyond his hands, darting around him.
ramacharitamanas::5096.modern_relevance: You keep trying to regain control in a meeting that has already slipped away. The harder you reach, the more everything stays just out of grasp.
ramacharitamanas::5096.insight: It shows a mind losing command under pressure, turning desperate instead of clear.

ramacharitamanas::5097.verse_sanskrit: कोपि कूदि द्वौ धरेसि बहोरी। महि पटकत भजे भुजा मरोरी॥ पुनि सकोप दस धनु कर लीन्हे। सरन्हि मारि घायल कपि कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5097.verse_hindi: तब उसने क्रोध करके उछलकर दोनों को पकड़ लिया। पृथ्वी पर पटकते समय वे उसकी भुजाओं को मरोड़कर भाग छूटे। फिर उसने क्रोध करके हाथों में दसों धनुष लिए और वानरों को बाणों से मारकर घायल कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5097.english_translation: Then, in anger, he sprang up and seized the two again. As they struck the ground, they twisted free by wrenching his arms. Then, angry again, he took up all ten bows and wounded the monkeys with arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5097.translation_literal: कोपि (in anger) / कूदि (leaping up) / द्वौ (the two) / धरेसि (he seized) / बहोरी (again) / महि (on the ground) / पटकत (while throwing down) / भजे (they broke free) / भुजा (arms) / मरोरी (twisting) / पुनि (again) / सकोप (with anger) / दस (ten) / धनु (bows) / कर (in hand) / लीन्हे (he took) / सरन्हि (with arrows) / मारि (striking) / घायल (wounded) / कपि (monkeys) / कीन्हे (he made)
ramacharitamanas::5097.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5097.essence: Anger only multiplies force; it never restores control.
ramacharitamanas::5097.simple_meaning: Ravana keeps fighting back in fury. He grabs the monkeys, they escape, and then he attacks them with arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5097.simple_insight: Raw anger can keep escalating, but it still cannot create calm strength.
ramacharitamanas::5097.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ravana is still locked in fierce combat with the monkey warriors. Even after they slip from his grasp, he surges back in rage, arms full of bows, striking and wounding them. The scene is a moving burst of battlefield resistance.
ramacharitamanas::5097.modern_relevance: A heated argument keeps restarting because nobody wants to back down. Each sharp reply only tightens the knot, and the original problem gets buried under reaction.
ramacharitamanas::5097.insight: It shows how anger feeds on itself and turns every response into escalation.

ramacharitamanas::5098.verse_sanskrit: हनुमदादि मुरुछित करि बंदर। पाइ प्रदोष हरष दसकंधर॥ मुरुछित देखि सकल कपि बीरा। जामवंत धायउ रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5098.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी आदि सब वानरों को मूर्च्छित करके और संध्या का समय पाकर रावण हर्षित हुआ। समस्त वानर-वीरों को मूर्च्छित देखकर रणधीर जाम्बवत् दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5098.english_translation: Having stunned Hanuman and the other monkeys, Ravana grew delighted as evening fell. Seeing all the monkey-heroes stunned, brave Jambavan rushed forward to the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::5098.translation_literal: हनुमदादि (Hanuman and others) / मुरुछित (stunned, fainted) / करि (having done) / बंदर (monkeys) / पाइ (having found) / प्रदोष (evening) / हरष (delighted) / दसकंधर (ten-headed Ravana) / मुरुछित (stunned) / देखि (seeing) / सकल (all) / कपि (monkey) / बीरा (heroes) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / धायउ (rushed) / रनधीरा (battle-brave)
ramacharitamanas::5098.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5098.essence: A fallen army still has one last fighter.
ramacharitamanas::5098.simple_meaning: Ravana knocks Hanuman and the other monkey warriors unconscious, then rejoices at dusk. Seeing his allies fallen, Jambavan charges back into the fight.
ramacharitamanas::5098.simple_insight: Even in defeat, courage can rise again when someone refuses to stay down.
ramacharitamanas::5098.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s war, Ravana has just stunned Hanuman and the monkey heroes, and the evening hour seems to favor him. But the sight of his fallen allies ignites Jambavan, who immediately rushes to defend the cause.
ramacharitamanas::5098.modern_relevance: You watch a team collapse halfway through a brutal meeting, and the room goes quiet. Then the oldest, steadiest person stands up and keeps the work alive.
ramacharitamanas::5098.insight: It shifts attention from the setback to the one who answers it with action.

ramacharitamanas::5099.verse_sanskrit: संग भालु भूधर तरु धारी। मारन लगे पचारि पचारी॥ भयउ क्रुद्ध रावन बलवाना। गहि पद महि पटकइ भट नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5099.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् के साथ जो भालू थे, वे पर्वत और वृक्ष धारण किए रावण को ललकार-ललकार कर मारने लगे। बलवान् रावण क्रोधित हुआ और पैर पकड़-पकड़कर वह अनेकों योद्धाओं को पृथ्वी पर पटकने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5099.english_translation: With Jambavan and the bears carrying mountains and trees, they challenged Ravana again and again and struck at him. The mighty Ravana grew furious and, seizing warriors by the feet, hurled many of them to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::5099.translation_literal: संग (with) / भालु (bears) / भूधर (mountains) / तरु (trees) / धारी (carrying) / मारन (to strike) / लगे (began) / पचारि पचारी (again and again, challenging)॥ / भयउ (became) / क्रुद्ध (furious) / रावन (Ravana) / बलवाना (powerful) / गहि (seizing) / पद (feet) / महि (to the ground) / पटकइ (hurls) / भट (warriors) / नाना (many)॥
ramacharitamanas::5099.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5099.essence: Battle surges on with raw force and fury.
ramacharitamanas::5099.simple_meaning: The battle keeps surging back and forth. The bears attack with mountains and trees, and Ravana answers by seizing warriors and slamming them down.
ramacharitamanas::5099.simple_insight: Some moments are pure force and reaction — no reflection, only impact.
ramacharitamanas::5099.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's battlefield, Jambavan's bear army presses Ravana with mountains and trees. Ravana, enraged and powerful, grabs fighters by the feet and hurls them down. The scene is still the clash before any turning point.
ramacharitamanas::5099.modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a pile-on, and everyone starts hitting back harder than before. Nobody is thinking clearly anymore; only impact is spreading.
ramacharitamanas::5099.insight: It shows a combat scene in motion, not a teaching, so it stays as battlefield narration.

ramacharitamanas::5100.verse_sanskrit: देखि भालुपति निज दल घाता। कोपि माझ उर मारेसि लाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5100.verse_hindi: जाम्बवान् ने अपने दल का विध्वंस देखकर क्रोध करके रावण की छाती में लात मारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5100.english_translation: Seeing his own army struck down, the lord of the bears, in anger, kicked Ravana in the chest.
ramacharitamanas::5100.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / भालुपति (lord of the bears) / निज दल (his own force) / घाता (struck down) / कोपि (angrily) / माझ उर (in the middle of the chest) / मारेसि (struck) / लाता (with a kick)
ramacharitamanas::5100.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5100.essence: Battle fury becomes a single decisive blow.
ramacharitamanas::5100.simple_meaning: Jambavan sees his side being battered and answers with a furious kick to Ravana's chest.
ramacharitamanas::5100.simple_insight: The battle turns on raw courage: pain does not end the fight; it can ignite it.
ramacharitamanas::5100.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana has been smashing the monkey and bear forces. Seeing his own side being crushed, Jambavan, the bear leader, surges forward in anger and kicks Ravana in the chest. It is a brief combat beat inside the larger war scene.
ramacharitamanas::5100.modern_relevance: A teammate gets publicly humiliated in front of everyone, and you feel your body tense before you even think. Loyalty can make you stand up faster than fear can sit you down.
ramacharitamanas::5100.insight: It shows how protective anger can become immediate action when someone you stand with is attacked.

ramacharitamanas::5101.verse_sanskrit: उर लात घात प्रचंड लागत बिकल रथ ते महि परा। गहि भालु बीसहुँ कर मनहुँ कमलन्हि बसे निसि मधुकरा॥ मुरुछित बिलोकि बहोरि पद हति भालुपति प्रभु पहिं गयो॥ निसि जानि स्यंदन घालि तेहि तब सूत जतनु करय भयो॥
ramacharitamanas::5101.verse_hindi: छाती में लात का प्रचण्ड आघात लगते ही रावण व्याकुल होकर रथ से पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा। उसने बीसों हाथों में भालुओं को पकड़ रखा था। (ऐसा जान पड़ता था) मानो रात्रि के समय भौंरे कमलों में बसे हुए हों। उसे मूर्च्छित देखकर, फिर लात मारकर ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् प्रभु के पास चले। रात्रि जानकर सारथी रावण को रथ में डालकर उसे होश में लाने का उपाय करने लगा॥
ramacharitamanas::5101.english_translation: The force of the blow to his chest knocked Ravana off the chariot and onto the ground. He clutched the bears with all twenty hands, like bees in lotus flowers at night. Seeing him stunned, Jambavan kicked him again and went to the Lord. Knowing it was night, the charioteer then placed Ravana back in the chariot and tried to revive him.
ramacharitamanas::5101.translation_literal: उर (chest) / लात (kick) / घात (strike) / प्रचंड (fierce) / लागत (upon hitting) / बिकल (distressed) / रथ ते (from the chariot) / महि (to the ground) / परा (fell) / गहि (grasping) / भालु (bears) / बीसहुँ (all twenty) / कर (hands) / मनहुँ (as if) / कमलन्हि (in lotuses) / बसे (dwelt) / निसि (night) / मधुकरा (bees) / मुरुछित (fainted) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बहोरि (again) / पद (with the foot) / हति (striking) / भालुपति (lord of bears) / प्रभु पहिं (to the Lord) / गयो (went) / निसि (night) / जानि (knowing) / स्यंदन (chariot) / घालि (placing) / तेहि (him) / तब (then) / सूत (charioteer) / जतनु (effort) / करय (did) / भयो (became)
ramacharitamanas::5101.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5101.essence: Pride falls fast when it meets a stronger blow.
ramacharitamanas::5101.simple_meaning: Ravana is battered in battle and falls from his chariot. Jambavan leaves him stunned and returns to Ram, while Ravana's charioteer tries to recover him.
ramacharitamanas::5101.simple_insight: Pride can be knocked down in an instant, even when it looks invincible.
ramacharitamanas::5101.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Jambavan's blow sends Ravana crashing from his chariot. The scene turns on raw combat, not instruction: Ravana is stunned, Jambavan moves back toward Ram, and the charioteer scrambles to restore order.
ramacharitamanas::5101.modern_relevance: A person who has been performing confidently in a meeting suddenly loses composure after one sharp question. The room changes in a second, and everyone can feel the shift.
ramacharitamanas::5101.insight: It shows how quickly force and status can collapse when challenged.

ramacharitamanas::5102.verse_sanskrit: मुरुछा बिगत भालु कपि सब आए प्रभु पास। निसिचर सकल रावनहि घेरि रहे अति त्रास ॥
ramacharitamanas::5102.verse_hindi: मूर्च्छा दूर होने पर सब रीछ-वानर प्रभु के पास आए। उधर सब राक्षसों ने बहुत ही भयभीत होकर रावण को घेर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5102.english_translation: When their faintness passed, all the bears and monkeys came to the Lord. Meanwhile, all the demons, terrified, gathered around Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::5102.translation_literal: मुरुछा (faintness) / बिगत (gone) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / सब (all) / आए (came) / प्रभु (Lord) / पास (near) / निसिचर (demons) / सकल (all) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / घेरि रहे (kept surrounding) / अति (very) / त्रास (fear)
ramacharitamanas::5102.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5102.essence: The armies regroup around the two centers of fear and trust.
ramacharitamanas::5102.simple_meaning: After the shock passed, the monkey army gathered back around Ram, while Ravana's frightened forces closed in around him.
ramacharitamanas::5102.simple_insight: In fear, people cluster around the power they trust or the power they cannot escape.
ramacharitamanas::5102.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ravana has just been struck down and the fighting is in chaos. The bear and monkey warriors regroup around Ram, while Ravana's own side huddles around their shaken king in fear. It is a scene-setting verse, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5102.insight: It keeps the focus on battlefield movement, not on a moral or inner lesson.

ramacharitamanas::5103.verse_sanskrit: तेही निसि सीता पहिं जाई। त्रिजटा कहि सब कथा सुनाई॥ सिर भुज बाढ़ि सुनत रिपु केरी। सीता उर भइ त्रास घनेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5103.verse_hindi: उसी रात त्रिजटा ने सीताजी के पास जाकर उन्हें सब कथा कह सुनाई। शत्रु के सिर और भुजाओं की बढ़ती का संवाद सुनकर सीताजी के हृदय में बड़ा भय हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5103.english_translation: That night Trijata went to Sita and told her the whole story. Hearing that the enemy's head and arms were growing larger, Sita felt deep fear in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::5103.translation_literal: तेही (that) / निसि (night) / सीता पहिं (to Sita) / जाई (going) / त्रिजटा (Trijata) / कहि (telling) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (made hear) ॥ / सिर (head) / भुज (arms) / बाढ़ि (increasing) / सुनत (hearing) / रिपु केरी (of the enemy) / सीता (Sita) / उर (in heart) / भइ (became) / त्रास (fear) / घनेरी (very great) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5103.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5103.essence: News of the beloved's danger brings fear before any answer arrives.
ramacharitamanas::5103.simple_meaning: Trijata tells Sita about the battle, and Sita becomes very afraid when she hears the enemy is growing stronger.
ramacharitamanas::5103.simple_insight: Fear returns quickly when the person you love seems to be losing.
ramacharitamanas::5103.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Trijata brings Sita news from the battlefield in the same night. She reports the strange rise of Ravana's power, and Sita's heart tightens with fear. The scene is a quiet pause between war and hope.
ramacharitamanas::5103.modern_relevance: You refresh the news after midnight and see the situation getting worse for someone you love. Your chest tightens before you can even think.
ramacharitamanas::5103.insight: It shows how deeply Sita is emotionally tied to Ram's struggle, and how quickly hope can turn into anxiety.

ramacharitamanas::5104.verse_sanskrit: मुख मलीन उपजी मन चिंता। त्रिजटा सन बोली तब सीता॥ होइहि कहा कहसि किन माता। केहि बिधि मरिहि बिस्व दुखदाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5104.verse_hindi: (उनका) मुख उदास हो गया, मन में चिंता उत्पन्न हो गई। तब सीताजी त्रिजटा से बोलीं- हे माता! बताती क्यों नहीं? क्या होगा? संपूर्ण विश्व को दुःख देने वाला यह किस प्रकार मरेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5104.english_translation: Her face grew pale and her mind filled with worry. Then Sita spoke to Trijata: "Mother, why do you not tell me? How will the one who brings sorrow to the whole world die?"
ramacharitamanas::5104.translation_literal: मुख (face) / मलीन (faded, pale) / उपजी (arose) / मन (mind) / चिंता (worry) / त्रिजटा (Trijata) / सन (to) / बोली (spoke) / तब (then) / सीता (Sita)॥ / होइहि (will happen) / कहा (what) / कहसि (you say) / किन (why not) / माता (mother) / केहि बिधि (in what way) / मरिहि (will die) / बिस्व दुखदाता (world's giver of sorrow) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5104.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5104.essence: Worry rises when justice seems far away.
ramacharitamanas::5104.simple_meaning: Sita grows worried after hearing that Ravana has been wounded and asks Trijata how the world’s tormentor will die.
ramacharitamanas::5104.simple_insight: Love can make you anxious for justice, even before the outcome is clear.
ramacharitamanas::5104.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Trijata has just told Sita that Ravana’s head and arms keep growing back. Sita’s face falls and worry rises in her heart. She turns to Trijata, desperate to know how the tyrant who has caused so much suffering will finally die.
ramacharitamanas::5104.modern_relevance: You hear that someone who has hurt many people may still escape consequences. Your chest tightens because you want the world made right, not delayed again.
ramacharitamanas::5104.insight: It shifts attention from the wound itself to the longing for moral resolution.

ramacharitamanas::5105.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति सर सिर कटेहुँ न मरई। बिधि बिपरीत चरित सब करई॥ मोर अभाग्य जिआवत ओही। जेहिं हौं हरि पद कमल बिछोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5105.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के बाणों से सिर कटने पर भी नहीं मरता। विधाता सारे चरित्र विपरीत (उलटे) ही कर रहा है। (सच बात तो यह है कि) मेरा दुर्भाग्य ही उसे जिला रहा है, जिसने मुझे भगवान् के चरणकमलों से अलग कर दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5105.english_translation: Even if Raghunath's arrow cuts off his head, he does not die. Fate is making everything run in reverse. My own bad fortune is keeping him alive, the one who separated me from the lotus feet of Hari.
ramacharitamanas::5105.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / सर (arrow) / सिर (head) / कटेहुँ (even if cut) / न (not) / मरई (dies) / बिधि (fate / the cosmic order) / बिपरीत (reverse) / चरित (conduct / happenings) / सब (all) / करई (does) / मोर (my) / अभाग्य (misfortune) / जिआवत (keeps alive) / ओही (him) / जेहिं (who) / हौं (I) / हरि (Hari / Ram) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / बिछोही (separated from)
ramacharitamanas::5105.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5105.essence: Separation from Ram makes even survival feel like a curse.
ramacharitamanas::5105.simple_meaning: Sita feels that Ravana can survive only because her own misfortune still holds her in separation from Ram. She sees the world as turned upside down by fate.
ramacharitamanas::5105.simple_insight: Grief can make everything look reversed, as if pain itself is keeping the wrong things alive.
ramacharitamanas::5105.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just heard that Ravana keeps rising even after terrible wounds. Still trapped in Ashoka Vatika, she speaks from fear and sorrow, blaming the twisted order of fate and her own bad fortune for the enemy's survival.
ramacharitamanas::5105.modern_relevance: You watch someone keep escaping consequences while you sit with the mess they caused. In that moment, it can feel as if the whole world is working backward.
ramacharitamanas::5105.insight: It shows how separation and fear distort perception, making suffering feel like the force that sustains the problem.

ramacharitamanas::5106.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं कृत कपट कनक मृग झूठा। अजहुँ सो दैव मोहि पर रूठा॥ जेहिं बिधि मोहि दुख दुसह सहाए। लछिमन कहुँ कटु बचन कहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5106.verse_hindi: जिसने कपट का झूठा स्वर्ण मृग बनाया था, वही दैव अब भी मुझ पर रूठा हुआ है, जिस विधाता ने मुझसे दुःसह दुःख सहन कराए और लक्ष्मण को कड़ुवे वचन कहलाए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::5106.english_translation: The one who made the false golden deer still seems angry with me. The same fate has made me endure unbearable pain and made Lakshman speak harsh words.
ramacharitamanas::5106.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / कृत (made) / कपट (deceit) / कनक (golden) / मृग (deer) / झूठा (false) / अजहुँ (still) / सो (that) / दैव (fate) / मोहि (to me) / पर (upon) / रूठा (angry) / जेहिं (who) / बिधि (ordainer) / मोहि (to me) / दुख (pain) / दुसह (unbearable) / सहाए (made endure) / लछिमन कहुँ (for Lakshman) / कटु (harsh) / बचन (words) / कहाए (caused to be spoken)
ramacharitamanas::5106.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5106.essence: Pain turns separate wounds into one enemy.
ramacharitamanas::5106.simple_meaning: Sita blames the same cruel force for both the false golden deer and her present suffering. She feels that this force has kept hurting her and even caused Lakshman to speak harshly.
ramacharitamanas::5106.simple_insight: Grief often links every wound into one long story of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::5106.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is drowning in fear and separation from Ram. Remembering the golden deer, Lakshman’s departure, and her own unbearable ordeal, she sees one cruel chain behind it all. This verse is part of her lament, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::5106.modern_relevance: After one betrayal, every small delay feels like proof that life is against you. In that state, the mind ties separate hurts into one unbearable pattern.
ramacharitamanas::5106.insight: It shows how pain can make the mind see a single hostile force behind many events.

ramacharitamanas::5107.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति बिरह सबिष सर भारी। तकि तकि मार बार बहु मारी॥ ऐसेहुँ दुख जो राख मम प्राना। सोइ बिधि ताहि जिआव न आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5107.verse_hindi: जो श्री रघुनाथजी के विरह रूपी बड़े विषैले बाणों से तक-तककर मुझे बहुत बार मारकर, अब भी मार रहा है और ऐसे दुःख में भी जो मेरे प्राणों को रख रहा है, वही विधाता उस (रावण) को जिला रहा है, दूसरा कोई नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5107.english_translation: The sharp arrows of separation from Raghupati strike me again and again, yet my life still remains. The same fate that keeps me alive in this pain keeps Ravana alive too; no one else does.
ramacharitamanas::5107.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / बिरह (separation) / सबिष (poisoned) / सर (arrows) / भारी (heavy, great) / तकि तकि (again and again, looking) / मार (striking) / बार बार (repeatedly) / बहु (many) / मारी (killed)॥ / ऐसेहुँ (even so) / दुख (pain) / जो (which) / राख (keeps) / मम (my) / प्राना (life-breath) / सोइ (that same) / बिधि (fate, ordaining power) / ताहि (him) / जिआव (keeps alive) / न (not) / आना (another)॥
ramacharitamanas::5107.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5107.essence: Separation can keep you alive while feeling like repeated death.
ramacharitamanas::5107.simple_meaning: Ravana says Ram’s absence feels like poisoned arrows hitting him again and again. Even while this pain keeps him alive, the same power is keeping Ram’s enemy alive too.
ramacharitamanas::5107.simple_insight: Separation can wound so deeply that staying alive feels like its own punishment.
ramacharitamanas::5107.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking in anguish after the war has turned against him. He blames the same power that keeps him alive in unbearable pain for also keeping him alive at all. The verse deepens his collapse before the final defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5107.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a breakup, and every glance stings. The hurt doesn’t just visit once — it keeps returning, and somehow you are still standing through it.
ramacharitamanas::5107.insight: It shifts the mind from triumphal pride to the unbearable cost of clinging to what is already lost.

ramacharitamanas::5108.verse_sanskrit: बहु बिधि कर बिलाप जानकी। करि करि सुरति कृपानिधान की॥ कह त्रिजटा सुनु राजकुमारी। उर सर लागत मरइ सुरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5108.verse_hindi: कृपानिधान श्री रामजी की याद कर-करके जानकीजी बहुत प्रकार से विलाप कर रही हैं। त्रिजटा ने कहा- हे राजकुमारी! सुनो, देवताओं का शत्रु रावण हृदय में बाण लगते ही मर जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5108.english_translation: Sita wept in many ways, remembering the compassionate Lord again and again. Trijata said, “Listen, princess. The enemy of the radiant beings will die the moment an arrow strikes his heart.”
ramacharitamanas::5108.translation_literal: बहु बिधि (many ways) / कर (doing) / बिलाप (lamentation) / जानकी (Sita) / करि करि (again and again doing) / सुरति (remembrance) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion) की (of) / कह (said) / त्रिजटा (Trijata) / सुनु (listen) / राजकुमारी (princess) / उर (heart) / सर (arrow) लागत (striking) / मरइ (dies) / सुरारी (enemy of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::5108.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5108.essence: Grief is met here with a promise that the end is near.
ramacharitamanas::5108.simple_meaning: Sita grieves for Ram, and Trijata comforts her by saying Ravana will die when an arrow reaches his heart.
ramacharitamanas::5108.simple_insight: Even in captivity, hope can arrive through a single steady voice.
ramacharitamanas::5108.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita remembers Ram and weeps in many ways. Trijata, the compassionate watcher in the Ashoka grove, answers her grief with reassurance: Ravana’s end is near, and a heart-striking arrow will finish him.
ramacharitamanas::5108.modern_relevance: You sit alone with a message thread unanswered, replaying the same pain. Then one calm friend says, “This won’t last forever,” and your breathing changes.
ramacharitamanas::5108.insight: It shifts the mind from helpless grief to patient expectation of relief.

ramacharitamanas::5109.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु ताते उर हतइ न तेही। एहि के हृदयँ बसति बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5109.verse_hindi: परन्तु प्रभु उसके हृदय में बाण इसलिए नहीं मारते कि इसके हृदय में जानकीजी (आप) बसती हैं ॥ छंद :
ramacharitamanas::5109.english_translation: But the Lord does not strike his heart with arrows, because Janaki lives in that heart.
ramacharitamanas::5109.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / ताते (therefore) / उर (heart) / हतइ (strikes) / न (not) / तेही (that one) / एहि (this) / के (of) / हृदयँ (heart) / बसति (dwells) / बैदेही (Vaidehi / Sita)
ramacharitamanas::5109.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5109.essence: A heart already filled with devotion cannot be easily wounded.
ramacharitamanas::5109.simple_meaning: The Lord does not harm the one whose heart already holds Sita. Love for her becomes a shield.
ramacharitamanas::5109.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that devotion itself can protect you.
ramacharitamanas::5109.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Trijata explains to Sita why Ravana's burning arrows do not fully strike one man. The reason is simple and sacred: Sita already lives in his heart. That inner devotion shields him.
ramacharitamanas::5109.modern_relevance: You open your messages and see a cruel reply waiting to ruin your mood. But one steady love, one deep commitment, can keep bitterness from taking over your heart.
ramacharitamanas::5109.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of attack to the protecting power of inward devotion.

ramacharitamanas::5110.verse_sanskrit: एहि के हृदयँ बस जानकी जानकी उर मम बास है। मम उदर भुअन अनेक लागत बान सब कर नास है॥ सुनि बचन हरष बिषाद मन अति देखि पुनि त्रिजटाँ कहा। अब मरिहि रिपु एहि बिधि सुनहि सुंदरि तजहि संसय महा॥
ramacharitamanas::5110.verse_hindi: वे यही सोचकर रह जाते हैं कि) इसके हृदय में जानकी का निवास है, जानकी के हृदय में मेरा निवास है और मेरे उदर में अनेकों भुवन हैं। अतः रावण के हृदय में बाण लगते ही सब भुवनों का नाश हो जाएगा। यह वचन सुनकर सीताजी के मन में अत्यंत हर्ष और विषाद हुआ देखकर त्रिजटा ने फिर कहा- हे सुंदरी! महान् संदेह का त्याग कर दो, अब सुनो, शत्रु इस प्रकार मरेगा-
ramacharitamanas::5110.english_translation: Because Sita lives in his heart, and Ravana lives in Sita's heart, and countless worlds dwell in Ravana's belly, no arrow can yet destroy him. Hearing this, Sita felt both joy and sorrow. Seeing that, Trijata said again: "O beautiful one, cast away this great doubt. Listen now: the enemy will die in this way."
ramacharitamanas::5110.translation_literal: एहि (in this) / के (of) / हृदयँ (heart) / बस (dwells) / जानकी (Janaki) / जानकी (Janaki) / उर (in heart) / मम (my) / बास (dwelling) है (is) / मम (my) / उदर (belly) / भुअन (worlds) / अनेक (many) / लागत (appearing) / बान (arrow) / सब (all) / कर (of) / नास (destruction) है (is)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / हरष (joy) / बिषाद (sorrow) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / देखि (seeing) / पुनि (again) / त्रिजटाँ (Trijata) / कहा (said)॥ / अब (now) / मरिहि (will die) / रिपु (enemy) / एहि (in this) / बिधि (way) / सुनहि (listen) / सुंदरि (beautiful one) / तजहि (abandon) / संसय (doubt) / महा (great)॥
ramacharitamanas::5110.speaker: Trijata
ramacharitamanas::5110.essence: What holds the enemy alive is the mind's own attachment.
ramacharitamanas::5110.simple_meaning: Trijata explains that Ravana cannot be killed yet because Sita remains in his heart. She comforts Sita by saying the enemy will die only after his attachment to her breaks.
ramacharitamanas::5110.simple_insight: What protects ego is not strength, but obsession. When fixation falls away, its hold ends.
ramacharitamanas::5110.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita hears Trijata describe Ravana's strange dependence on her presence in his heart. Sita feels both hope and grief. Trijata notices her reaction and reassures her that Ravana will die only after his mind loses its grip on Sita.
ramacharitamanas::5110.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone because one person still has too much power over your mood. As long as your mind is stuck there, the pattern stays alive.
ramacharitamanas::5110.insight: It shifts attention from outer conflict to inner fixation as the real source of bondage.

ramacharitamanas::5111.verse_sanskrit: काटत सिर होइहि बिकल छुटि जाइहि तव ध्यान। तब रावनहि हृदय महुँ मरिहहिं रामु सुजान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5111.verse_hindi: सिरों के बार-बार काटे जाने से जब वह व्याकुल हो जाएगा और उसके हृदय से तुम्हारा ध्यान छूट जाएगा, तब सुजान (अंतर्यामी) श्री रामजी रावण के हृदय में बाण मारेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5111.english_translation: When his head is cut again and again and he becomes distracted, and your remembrance leaves his heart, then wise Ram will strike Ravana in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::5111.translation_literal: काटत (cutting) / सिर (head) / होइहि (will become) / बिकल (disturbed) / छुटि जाइहि (will slip away) / तव (your) / ध्यान (remembrance) / तब (then) / रावनहि (Ravana) / हृदय महुँ (in the heart) / मरिहहिं (will strike) / रामु (Ram) / सुजान (wise, all-knowing)
ramacharitamanas::5111.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5111.essence: Ego falls only when its grip on attention breaks.
ramacharitamanas::5111.simple_meaning: Ravana can be defeated only after repeated blows make him lose focus. Once his remembrance of Sita slips, Ram will strike at his heart.
ramacharitamanas::5111.simple_insight: What protects ego is not strength, but attention. When attention breaks, the heart becomes vulnerable.
ramacharitamanas::5111.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final battle, Ravana keeps rising after each blow. The verse explains the turning point: only when his mind is shaken and his remembrance of Sita weakens can Ram's arrow reach him. It is a tactical and spiritual ending to Ravana's pride.
ramacharitamanas::5111.modern_relevance: You keep defending a bad habit until exhaustion cracks your concentration. The moment your grip loosens, the thing that seemed invincible starts to fall.
ramacharitamanas::5111.insight: It shifts you from seeing victory as force alone to seeing attention and fixation as the real battlefield.

ramacharitamanas::5112.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि बहुत भाँति समुझाई। पुनि त्रिजटा निज भवन सिधाई॥ राम सुभाउ सुमिरि बैदेही। उपजी बिरह बिथा अति तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5112.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर और सीताजी को बहुत प्रकार से समझाकर फिर त्रिजटा अपने घर चली गई। श्री रामचंद्रजी के स्वभाव का स्मरण करके जानकीजी को अत्यंत विरह व्यथा उत्पन्न हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5112.english_translation: Thus speaking, and after comforting Sita in many ways, Trijata returned to her own home. Remembering Rama's nature, Vaidehi was filled with intense pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::5112.translation_literal: अस कहि (thus speaking) / बहुत भाँति (in many ways) / समुझाई (having comforted) / पुनि (then) / त्रिजटा (Trijata) / निज भवन (to her own home) / सिधाई (returned) / राम सुभाउ (Rama's nature) / सुमिरि (remembering) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / उपजी (arose) / बिरह बिथा (pain of separation) / अति (greatly) / तेही (in her)
ramacharitamanas::5112.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5112.essence: Remembering what you love can make absence feel sharper.
ramacharitamanas::5112.simple_meaning: Trijata reassures Sita and goes home, but Sita's memory of Rama makes her separation hurt even more.
ramacharitamanas::5112.simple_insight: Love can deepen pain before it becomes relief.
ramacharitamanas::5112.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Trijata has just tried to steady Sita with kind words and explanations. Once she leaves, Sita is left alone with her longing. The thought of Rama's nature only intensifies the ache of separation.
ramacharitamanas::5112.insight: It shows how remembrance can intensify longing rather than soothe it.

ramacharitamanas::5113.verse_sanskrit: निसिहि ससिहि निंदति बहु भाँति। जुग सम भई सिराति न राती॥ करति बिलाप मनहिं मन भारी। राम बिरहँ जानकी दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5113.verse_hindi: वे रात्रि की और चंद्रमा की बहुत प्रकार से निंदा कर रही हैं (और कह रही हैं-) रात युग के समान बड़ी हो गई, वह बीतती ही नहीं। जानकीजी श्री रामजी के विरह में दुःखी होकर मन ही मन भारी विलाप कर रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5113.english_translation: She keeps blaming the night and the moon in many ways. The night feels like an age and still does not end. Janaki grieves inwardly, heavy with sorrow over Ram's separation.
ramacharitamanas::5113.translation_literal: निसिहि (the night) / ससिहि (the moon) / निंदति (blames) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / जुग (an age) / सम (like) / भई (became) / सिराति (ends) / न (not) / राती (the night) / करति (doing) / बिलाप (lamentation) / मनहिं मन (within the mind) / भारी (heavy) / राम (Ram) / बिरहँ (in separation) / जानकी (Janaki) / दुखारी (grieving)
ramacharitamanas::5113.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5113.essence: Longing makes time itself feel cruel.
ramacharitamanas::5113.simple_meaning: Sita is so heartbroken that the night feels endless, and she quietly laments Ram's absence.
ramacharitamanas::5113.simple_insight: Separation can stretch a single night into something unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::5113.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is alone in Ashoka Vatika, waiting for Ram while surrounded by fear and longing. The night feels endless, and even the moon seems to mock her as she grieves inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::5113.modern_relevance: You keep checking the clock at 2:13 a.m., and the room feels too quiet. When your heart is waiting for someone, even a short night can feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::5113.insight: It shifts attention to the lived weight of longing, not just the fact of waiting.

ramacharitamanas::5114.verse_sanskrit: जब अति भयउ बिरह उर दाहू। फरकेउ बाम नयन अरु बाहू॥ सगुन बिचारि धरी मन धीरा। अब मिलिहहिं कृपाल रघुबीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5114.verse_hindi: जब विरह के मारे हृदय में दारुण दाह हो गया, तब उनका बायाँ नेत्र और बाहु फड़क उठे। शकुन समझकर उन्होंने मन में धैर्य धारण किया कि अब कृपालु श्री रघुवीर अवश्य मिलेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5114.english_translation: When the pain of separation burned fiercely in her heart, her left eye and arm twitched. Reading it as an omen, she steadied her mind: now the merciful Raghubir will surely come to me.
ramacharitamanas::5114.translation_literal: जब (when) / अति (greatly) / भयउ (became) / बिरह (separation) / उर (heart) / दाहू (burning) / फरकेउ (twitching) / बाम (left) / नयन (eye) / अरु (and) / बाहू (arm)॥ / सगुन (omen) / बिचारि (considering) / धरी (held) / मन (mind) / धीरा (steady) / अब (now) / मिलिहहिं (will meet) / कृपाल (merciful) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir)॥
ramacharitamanas::5114.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5114.essence: Hope can arrive first as a sign before it arrives as proof.
ramacharitamanas::5114.simple_meaning: Sita’s separation becomes so intense that her body reacts, but she reads the sign as hope and steadies herself, believing Ram will soon come.
ramacharitamanas::5114.simple_insight: Even in deep longing, you can let a sign restore your courage.
ramacharitamanas::5114.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has spent night after night grieving Ram’s absence. The pain becomes so sharp that her body trembles. Then she notices an omen, calms her mind, and lets hope return: Ram, the merciful one, is coming.
ramacharitamanas::5114.modern_relevance: You’re staring at your phone after a hard message, trying not to spiral. Then something small—a call back, a missed sign, a sudden calm—lets you breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::5114.insight: It teaches you to read hope without forcing certainty and to steady yourself before fear takes over.

ramacharitamanas::5115.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ अर्धनिसि रावनु जागा। निज सारथि सन खीझन लागा। सठ रनभूमि छड़ाइसि मोही। धिग धिग अधम मंदमति तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5115.verse_hindi: यहाँ आधी रात को रावण (मूर्च्छा से) जागा और अपने सारथी पर रुष्ट होकर कहने लगा- अरे मूर्ख! तूने मुझे रणभूमि से अलग कर दिया। अरे अधम! अरे मंदबुद्धि! तुझे धिक्कार है, धिक्कार है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5115.english_translation: Here, in the middle of the night, Ravana woke up and began scolding his charioteer. “Fool! You dragged me away from the battlefield. Shame on you, shame on you, lowly, dull-witted one!”
ramacharitamanas::5115.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / अर्धनिसि (midnight) / रावनु (Ravana) / जागा (woke up) / निज (his own) / सारथि (charioteer) / सन (to/with) / खीझन (to scold) / लागा (began) / सठ (fool) / रनभूमि (battlefield) / छड़ाइसि (you made me leave) / मोही (me) / धिग धिग (shame shame) / अधम (lowly) / मंदमति (dull-witted) / तोही (you)
ramacharitamanas::5115.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5115.essence: Pride cannot bear defeat, so it attacks the helper.
ramacharitamanas::5115.simple_meaning: Ravana wakes in the night and angrily abuses his charioteer for pulling him away from battle.
ramacharitamanas::5115.simple_insight: Pride lashes out first at whoever is nearest.
ramacharitamanas::5115.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lankakand war, Ravana regains consciousness and immediately turns his anger on his own charioteer. The scene shows wounded pride, not wisdom: even after defeat, he still blames others instead of himself.
ramacharitamanas::5115.modern_relevance: You snap at the driver, the assistant, or the teammate who only carried your mistake forward. The anger is loud, but the wound underneath is bruised pride.
ramacharitamanas::5115.insight: It reveals how ego protects itself by blaming the nearest person.

ramacharitamanas::5116.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं पद गहि बहु बिधि समुझावा। भोरु भएँ रथ चढ़ि पुनि धावा॥ सुनि आगवनु दसानन केरा। कपि दल खरभर भयउ घनेरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5116.verse_hindi: सारथि ने चरण पकड़कर रावण को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। सबेरा होते ही वह रथ पर चढ़कर फिर दौड़ा। रावण का आना सुनकर वानरों की सेना में बड़ी खलबली मच गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5116.english_translation: The charioteer clasped his feet and tried to persuade him in many ways. At dawn he mounted the chariot and charged again. Hearing Ravana return, the monkey army fell into great confusion.
ramacharitamanas::5116.translation_literal: तेहिं (to him) / पद (feet) / गहि (grasping) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / समुझावा (persuaded) / भोरु भएँ (at dawn) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ि (mounting) / पुनि (again) / धावा (charged)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / आगवनु (arrival) / दसानन केरा (of Ravana) / कपि दल (monkey army) / खरभर (commotion) / भयउ (became) / घनेरा (great)॥
ramacharitamanas::5116.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5116.essence: Reckless return can disturb everyone around you.
ramacharitamanas::5116.simple_meaning: The charioteer tries to calm Ravana, but Ravana rides out again at dawn, and the monkey army is thrown into confusion.
ramacharitamanas::5116.simple_insight: Even after warning, reckless force can return and unsettle everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::5116.detailed_meaning: In the heat of Lankakand’s war, Ravana has just been shaken by defeat and confusion. His charioteer pleads with him and tries to steady him, but morning comes and Ravana charges back into battle. The monkey army hears of it and panics.
ramacharitamanas::5116.modern_relevance: A tense group chat blows up again after everyone thought the issue was over. One person charges back in, and the whole room tightens at once.
ramacharitamanas::5116.insight: It shows how one impulsive return can spread fear through an entire crowd.

ramacharitamanas::5117.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ भूधर बिटप उपारी। धाए कटकटाइ भट भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5117.verse_hindi: वे भारी योद्धा जहाँ-तहाँ से पर्वत और वृक्ष उखाड़कर (क्रोध से) दाँत कटकटाकर दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5117.english_translation: The mighty warriors rushed from every side, uprooting mountains and trees, grinding their teeth in fury.
ramacharitamanas::5117.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (from here and there) / भूधर (mountains) / बिटप (trees) / उपारी (uprooted) / धाए (rushed) / कटकटाइ (grinding teeth) / भट (warriors) / भारी (mighty)
ramacharitamanas::5117.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5117.essence: The battle surges forward in sheer fury.
ramacharitamanas::5117.simple_meaning: Warriors from all sides tore up mountains and trees and rushed forward in rage.
ramacharitamanas::5117.simple_insight: The verse shows raw battle force, not a teaching to carry forward.
ramacharitamanas::5117.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, the battlefield erupts again. Fighters on both sides grab mountains and trees as weapons and charge with clenched rage. The verse simply intensifies the clash before the next blows land.
ramacharitamanas::5117.insight: It shifts attention from inner meaning to the physical violence of the battle scene.

ramacharitamanas::5118.verse_sanskrit: धाए जो मर्कट बिकट भालु कराल कर भूधर धरा। अति कोप करहिं प्रहार मारत भजि चले रजनीचरा॥ बिचलाइ दल बलवंत कीसन्ह घेरि पुनि रावनु लियो। चहुँ दिसि चपेटन्हि मारि नखन्हि बिदारि तन ब्याकुल कियो॥
ramacharitamanas::5118.verse_hindi: विकट और विकराल वानर-भालू हाथों में पर्वत लिए दौड़े। वे अत्यंत क्रोध करके प्रहार करते हैं। उनके मारने से राक्षस भाग चले। बलवान् वानरों ने शत्रु की सेना को विचलित करके फिर रावण को घेर लिया। चारों ओर से चपेटे मारकर और नखों से शरीर विदीर्ण कर वानरों ने उसको व्याकुल कर दिया॥
ramacharitamanas::5118.english_translation: The fierce monkeys and bears rushed forward with mountains in their hands. In great rage they struck, and the demons fled. The powerful monkeys scattered the enemy army and then surrounded Ravana again. They lashed him from all sides, clawed him apart, and left him reeling in pain.
ramacharitamanas::5118.translation_literal: धाए (rushed) / जो (who) / मर्कट (monkeys) / बिकट (fierce) / भालु (bears) / कराल (terrible) / कर (hands) / भूधर (mountains) / धरा (held) / अति (greatly) / कोप (rage) / करहिं (they do) / प्रहार (strikes) / मारत (striking) / भजि (fleeing) / चले (ran) / रजनीचरा (demons) ॥ / बिचलाइ (disrupting) / दल (army) / बलवंत (powerful) / कीसन्ह (monkeys) / घेरि (surrounding) / पुनि (again) / रावनु (Ravana) / लियो (took) / चहुँ दिसि (from all four sides) / चपेटन्हि (with slaps/blows) / मारि (striking) / नखन्हि (with claws) / बिदारि (rending) / तन (body) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / कियो (made)
ramacharitamanas::5118.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5118.essence: The battlefield swings back as Ravana is driven into retreat.
ramacharitamanas::5118.simple_meaning: The monkey and bear army attacks fiercely, scatters the demons, and surrounds Ravana again, leaving him battered and overwhelmed.
ramacharitamanas::5118.simple_insight: Sometimes pressure breaks the attacker’s confidence before it breaks your body.
ramacharitamanas::5118.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ravana’s forces surge forward again, but Hanuman’s side answers with raw force. Monkeys and bears hurl mountains, break the enemy line, and close in on Ravana himself. The verse is battlefield action, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5118.insight: It shows the tide of battle turning through coordinated force and relentless counterattack.

ramacharitamanas::5119.verse_sanskrit: देखि महा मर्कट प्रबल रावन कीन्ह बिचार। अंतरहित होइ निमिष महुँ कृत माया बिस्तार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5119.verse_hindi: वानरों को बड़ा ही प्रबल देखकर रावण ने विचार किया और अंतर्धान होकर क्षणभर में उसने माया फैलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5119.english_translation: Seeing the mighty monkeys, Ravana thought it over and vanished in a moment, spreading his illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5119.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / महा (great) / मर्कट (monkeys) / प्रबल (powerful) / रावन (Ravana) / कीन्ह (did) / बिचार (thought) / अंतरहित (unseen, vanished) / होइ (becoming) / निमिष महुँ (in a moment) / कृत (made) / माया (illusion) / बिस्तार (spread, expansion)
ramacharitamanas::5119.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5119.essence: Fear hides, then reaches for illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5119.simple_meaning: Ravana sees the monkey army, hides himself, and creates an illusion to confuse them.
ramacharitamanas::5119.simple_insight: Panic can make the mind choose deception over courage.
ramacharitamanas::5119.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the monkey army is pressing hard against Ravana's side. Seeing their force, Ravana does not stand openly; he disappears at once and begins using illusion to shift the battle.
ramacharitamanas::5119.modern_relevance: A person gets cornered in a meeting, goes quiet, and starts spinning half-truths instead of facing the question directly.
ramacharitamanas::5119.insight: It shows how fear and ego can turn a fight into manipulation.

ramacharitamanas::5120.verse_sanskrit: जब कीन्ह तेहिं पाषंड। भए प्रगट जंतु प्रचंड॥ बेताल भूत पिसाच। कर धरें धनु नाराच ॥
ramacharitamanas::5120.verse_hindi: जब उसने पाखंड (माया) रचा, तब भयंकर जीव प्रकट हो गए। बेताल, भूत और पिशाच हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए प्रकट हुए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5120.english_translation: When he created that deception, fierce beings appeared. Vampires, ghosts, and spirits appeared with bows and arrows in their hands.
ramacharitamanas::5120.translation_literal: जब (when) / कीन्ह (made) / तेहिं (that) / पाषंड (deception, false appearance) / भए (became) / प्रगट (manifest) / जंतु (beings) / प्रचंड (fierce) / बेताल (vampires) / भूत (ghosts) / पिसाच (spirits) / कर (hand) / धरें (held) / धनु (bow) / नाराच (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::5120.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5120.essence: False appearances can turn fear into a crowd.
