ramacharitamanas::5120.simple_meaning: Ravana’s illusion makes terrifying figures appear, each armed and ready to attack. The scene is meant to overwhelm the eye and frighten the enemy.
ramacharitamanas::5120.simple_insight: Fear grows fast when appearance is used as a weapon.
ramacharitamanas::5120.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana answers the monkey army’s strength with illusion. He turns deception into a spectacle of horror, making monstrous figures appear with weapons. The verse is one step in that larger display.
ramacharitamanas::5120.modern_relevance: A rumor hits your phone and suddenly everyone seems dangerous, guilty, or against you. Fear can multiply faster than facts when imagination takes over.
ramacharitamanas::5120.insight: It shows how deception can manufacture panic by dressing fear in visible forms.

ramacharitamanas::5121.verse_sanskrit: जोगिनि गहें करबाल। एक हाथ मनुज कपाल॥ करि सद्य सोनित पान। नाचहिं करहिं बहु गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5121.verse_hindi: योगिनियाँ एक हाथ में तलवार और दूसरे हाथ में मनुष्य की खोपड़ी लिए ताजा खून पीकर नाचने और बहुत तरह के गीत गाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5121.english_translation: Yoginis, with a sword in one hand and a human skull in the other, drank fresh blood, then danced and sang in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::5121.translation_literal: जोगिनि (yoginis) / गहें (holding) / करबाल (sword) / एक हाथ (one hand) / मनुज कपाल (human skull) / करि (having done) / सद्य (fresh) / सोनित पान (drinking blood) / नाचहिं (they dance) / करहिं (they do) / बहु गान (many songs)
ramacharitamanas::5121.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5121.essence: Illusion can turn fear into a weapon.
ramacharitamanas::5121.simple_meaning: The verse describes terrifying magical figures appearing in battle, armed and drinking blood as they dance and sing.
ramacharitamanas::5121.simple_insight: Fear can be manufactured to shake courage before a blow is even struck.
ramacharitamanas::5121.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has used illusion to terrify the monkey army. After ghosts and fierce beings appear, this verse adds yoginis with weapons and skulls, drinking blood and dancing. It is part of a rapid sequence of battlefield terror, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::5121.modern_relevance: A rumor starts in a crowded group chat, and suddenly everyone imagines the worst. Fear spreads faster than facts, just like Ravana's illusion here.
ramacharitamanas::5121.insight: It shows how spectacle and terror can be used to unsettle the mind before real harm arrives.

ramacharitamanas::5122.verse_sanskrit: धरु मारु बोलहिं घोर। रहि पूरि धुनि चहुँ ओर॥ मुख बाइ धावहिं खान। तब लगे कीस परान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5122.verse_hindi: वे 'पक़ड़ो, मारो' आदि घोर शब्द बोल रही हैं। चारों ओर (सब दिशाओं में) यह ध्वनि भर गई। वे मुख फैलाकर खाने दौड़ती हैं। तब वानर भागने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5122.english_translation: They cry out in fierce voices, “Seize! Kill!” The sound fills all directions. With mouths gaping, they rush to devour, and then the monkeys begin to flee.
ramacharitamanas::5122.translation_literal: धरु (seize) / मारु (kill) / बोलहिं (they cry out) / घोर (fierce) / रहि (remaining) / पूरि (filled) / धुनि (sound) / चहुँ ओर (in all four directions) / मुख (mouths) / बाइ (opening wide) / धावहिं (they rush) / खान (to eat) / तब (then) / लगे (began) / कीस (monkeys) / परान (to flee)
ramacharitamanas::5122.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5122.essence: Chaos can make even the brave run.
ramacharitamanas::5122.simple_meaning: Fierce cries fill the air, and terrifying beings rush forward to devour the monkeys, who panic and run.
ramacharitamanas::5122.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast when chaos feels everywhere at once.
ramacharitamanas::5122.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s dark magic has already summoned terrifying beings. Their cries now ring in every direction, and the monkey army loses its footing as the creatures rush to feed. This verse shows the immediate panic before the next wave of attack.
ramacharitamanas::5122.modern_relevance: A room erupts in shouting, and before you can think, everyone is reacting at once. Panic becomes contagious the moment danger feels all around you.
ramacharitamanas::5122.insight: It shows how disorder breaks courage by overwhelming the senses before the mind can respond.

ramacharitamanas::5123.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जाहिं मर्कट भागि। तहँ बरत देखहिं आगि॥ भए बिकल बानर भालु। पुनि लाग बरषै बालु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5123.verse_hindi: वानर भागकर जहाँ भी जाते हैं, वहीं आग जलती देखते हैं। वानर-भालू व्याकुल हो गए। फिर रावण बालू बरसाने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5123.english_translation: Wherever the monkeys ran, they found fire blazing there. The monkeys and bears grew frantic. Then Ravana began raining sand.
ramacharitamanas::5123.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / जाहिं (go) / मर्कट (monkeys) / भागि (running away) / तहँ (there) / बरत (burning) / देखहिं (see) / आगि (fire)॥ / भए (became) / बिकल (distressed) / बानर (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / पुनि (again) / लाग (began) / बरषै (to rain) / बालु (sand)॥
ramacharitamanas::5123.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5123.essence: Ravana turns escape itself into another wound.
ramacharitamanas::5123.simple_meaning: The fleeing monkey and bear forces keep meeting fire and sand, which leaves them confused and helpless.
ramacharitamanas::5123.simple_insight: Panic spreads fast when every direction feels blocked.
ramacharitamanas::5123.detailed_meaning: In the Lanka war, Ravana's side keeps turning the battlefield into a trap. As the monkey and bear army runs, fire appears everywhere and sand is hurled down on them, leaving them shaken before the next attack.
ramacharitamanas::5123.modern_relevance: You open one app to fix a problem, and three more alerts hit before you finish. Everything you try seems to trigger another obstacle.
ramacharitamanas::5123.insight: It shows how pressure can multiply until even retreat feels impossible.

ramacharitamanas::5124.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ थकित करि कीस। गर्जेउ बहुरि दससीस॥ लछिमन कपीस समेत। भए सकल बीर अचेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::5124.verse_hindi: वानरों को जहाँ-तहाँ थकित (शिथिल) कर रावण फिर गरजा। लक्ष्मणजी और सुग्रीव सहित सभी वीर अचेत हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5124.english_translation: Ravana wearied the monkeys everywhere, then roared again. Lakshmana, Sugriva, and all the heroes fell unconscious.
ramacharitamanas::5124.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (here and there / everywhere) / थकित करि (making weary) / कीस (the monkeys) / गर्जेउ (roared) / बहुरि (again) / दससीस (ten-headed Ravana)॥ / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / कपीस (lord of monkeys, Sugriva) / समेत (together with) / भए (became) / सकल (all) / बीर (warriors) / अचेत (unconscious)॥
ramacharitamanas::5124.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5124.essence: Pressure can wear down even the bravest.
ramacharitamanas::5124.simple_meaning: Ravana keeps pressuring the monkey army until even Lakshmana and Sugriva lose consciousness.
ramacharitamanas::5124.simple_insight: Some fights drain everyone at once; even the strongest can be overwhelmed.
ramacharitamanas::5124.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ravana keeps hammering the monkey forces until their strength breaks. Lakshmana and Sugriva, along with all the heroes, are left unconscious. The verse is a battlefield report, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5124.modern_relevance: A long day of crisis leaves everyone frayed: the team is exhausted, the leader is numb, and even the most capable people cannot keep pushing forever.
ramacharitamanas::5124.insight: It shows the cost of sustained pressure: force can exhaust courage itself.

ramacharitamanas::5125.verse_sanskrit: हा राम हा रघुनाथ। कहि सुभट मीजहिं हाथ॥ ऐहि बिधि सकल बल तोरि। तेहिं कीन्ह कपट बहोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5125.verse_hindi: हा राम! हा रघुनाथ पुकारते हुए श्रेष्ठ योद्धा अपने हाथ मलते (पछताते) हैं। इस प्रकार सब का बल तोड़कर रावण ने फिर दूसरी माया रची ॥
ramacharitamanas::5125.english_translation: Crying, “Ha Ram! Ha Raghunath!” the great warriors wrung their hands in despair. After breaking everyone’s strength this way, Ravana then used another trick.
ramacharitamanas::5125.translation_literal: हा (alas) / राम (Ram) / हा (alas) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / कहि (saying) / सुभट (great warriors) / मीजहिं (rub) / हाथ (hands) / ऐहि बिधि (in this way) / सकल (all) / बल (strength) / तोरि (breaking) / तेहिं (he) / कीन्ह (did) / कपट (deceit) / बहोरि (again)
ramacharitamanas::5125.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5125.essence: Pressure can break strength before the next blow lands.
ramacharitamanas::5125.simple_meaning: The warriors were so exhausted and shaken that they cried out in despair. Ravana then used another deceptive tactic to keep them off balance.
ramacharitamanas::5125.simple_insight: Exhaustion makes even brave people lose their center.
ramacharitamanas::5125.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ravana has already battered the monkey army and stunned even Lakshman and Sugriva. This verse shows the pressure deepening: the warriors cry out in helplessness, and Ravana immediately turns that weakness into another trap.
ramacharitamanas::5125.modern_relevance: After three brutal meetings, your team is drained, confused, and ready to quit. The hardest part is not the fight itself — it is what pressure does to judgment.
ramacharitamanas::5125.insight: It shows how relentless pressure can weaken resolve before the next move even begins.

ramacharitamanas::5126.verse_sanskrit: प्रगटेसि बिपुल हनुमान। धाए गहे पाषान॥ तिन्ह रामु घेरे जाइ। चहुँ दिसि बरूथ बनाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5126.verse_hindi: उसने बहुत से हनुमान् प्रकट किए, जो पत्थर लिए दौड़े। उन्होंने चारों ओर दल बनाकर श्री रामचंद्रजी को जा घेरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5126.english_translation: He manifested countless Hanumans, who ran forward with stones in hand. They surrounded Ram on all four sides, forming ranks.
ramacharitamanas::5126.translation_literal: प्रगटेसि (manifested) / बिपुल (many, vast) / हनुमान (Hanumans) / धाए (ran) / गहे (holding) / पाषान (stones) / तिन्ह (they) / रामु (Ram) / घेरे (surrounded) / जाइ (going) / चहुँ दिसि (four directions) / बरूथ (ranks, battalions) / बनाइ (making)
ramacharitamanas::5126.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5126.essence: The fight tightens as Hanuman's ranks close around Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5126.simple_meaning: Many Hanumans rush in with stones and surround Ram from all sides, forming battle lines.
ramacharitamanas::5126.simple_insight: The army closes in as the battle tightens around Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5126.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the fighting swells into confusion. Ravana's side keeps pressuring the battlefield, and then the monkey forces surge forward with stones in hand, encircling Ram in tight ranks. It is a movement detail, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::5126.insight: It shows the battle turning into a full encirclement, with forces gathering around Ram.

ramacharitamanas::5127.verse_sanskrit: मारहु धरहु जनि जाइ। कटकटहिं पूँछ उठाइ॥ दहँ दिसि लँगूर बिराज। तेहिं मध्य कोसलराज ॥
ramacharitamanas::5127.verse_hindi: वे पूँछ उठाकर कटकटाते हुए पुकारने लगे, 'मारो, पकड़ो, जाने न पावे'। उनके लंगूर (पूँछ) दसों दिशाओं में शोभा दे रहे हैं और उनके बीच में कोसलराज श्री रामजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5127.english_translation: Shout, seize him, do not let him go! With tails raised and rattling, they stand in all ten directions, and in their midst is the king of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::5127.translation_literal: मारहु (strike) / धरहु (seize) / जनि (do not) / जाइ (let go) / कटकटहिं (rattling) / पूँछ (tails) / उठाइ (raised) / दहँ (ten) / दिसि (directions) / लँगूर (tails/monkey-tails) / बिराज (stand splendidly) / तेहिं (in that) / मध्य (middle) / कोसलराज (king of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::5127.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5127.essence: Ram stands secure in the middle of gathered strength.
ramacharitamanas::5127.simple_meaning: The monkey warriors raise their tails and surround Ram from every side, ready for battle.
ramacharitamanas::5127.simple_insight: No one stands alone when courage gathers around the right cause.
ramacharitamanas::5127.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle has become a ring of pressure around Ram. Hanuman and the monkey warriors close in from every direction, tails raised, shouting to stop the enemy. The verse paints the living battle scene before the next description of Ram's beauty in their midst.
ramacharitamanas::5127.modern_relevance: A team crowds around a friend in crisis, all speaking at once, all ready to help. The moment is not quiet, but no one is left unsupported.
ramacharitamanas::5127.insight: It frames courage as collective force, with Ram held safe at the center.

ramacharitamanas::5128.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं मध्य कोसलराज सुंदर स्याम तन सोभा लही। जनु इंद्रधनुष अनेक की बर बारि तुंग तमालही॥ प्रभु देखि हरष बिषाद उर सुर बदत जय जय जय करी। रघुबीर एकहिं तीर कोपि निमेष महुँ माया हरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5128.verse_hindi: उनके बीच में कोसलराज का सुंदर श्याम शरीर ऐसी शोभा पा रहा है, मानो ऊँचे तमाल वृक्ष के लिए अनेक इंद्रधनुषों की श्रेष्ठ बाढ़ (घेरा) बनाई गई हो। प्रभु को देखकर देवता हर्ष और विषादयुक्त हृदय से 'जय, जय, जय' ऐसा बोलने लगे। तब श्री रघुवीर ने क्रोध करके एक ही बाण में निमेषमात्र में रावण की सारी माया हर ली ॥
ramacharitamanas::5128.english_translation: In their midst, the handsome dark form of the Lord of Kosala shone like many rainbows encircling a tall tamala tree. Seeing the Lord, the beings of heaven felt joy and sorrow together and cried, "Victory, victory, victory." Then Raghuvir, in anger, in a single arrow and in a moment, stripped away Ravana's illusion.
ramacharitamanas::5128.translation_literal: तेहिं मध्य (in that midst) / कोसलराज (the Lord of Kosala) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्याम तन (dark body) / सोभा (splendor) / लही (received) / जनु (as if) / इंद्रधनुष (rainbows) / अनेक (many) / की (of) / बर (excellent) / बारि (enclosure) / तुंग (tall) / तमालही (tamala tree) / प्रभु (the Lord) / देखि (seeing) / हरष (joy) / बिषाद (sorrow) / उर (in the heart) / सुर (heavenly beings) / बदत (saying) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / करी (did) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / एकहिं तीर (with one arrow) / कोपि (angrily) / निमेष महुँ (in a moment) / माया (illusion) / हरी (removed)
ramacharitamanas::5128.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5128.essence: One clear strike can end the illusion that multiplies fear.
ramacharitamanas::5128.simple_meaning: Ram stands shining in the battle, and even the heavenly beings are overwhelmed when they see him. With one arrow, he destroys Ravana's illusion at once.
ramacharitamanas::5128.simple_insight: Real strength is quiet and clear: one decisive act can end what looked overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::5128.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, Ram stands at the center while the monkey forces surge around him. The heavenly beings watch in awe as he answers Ravana's magic with a single arrow, cutting through the illusion that had been confusing the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::5128.modern_relevance: You finally see the real problem behind the chaos in a tense meeting, and one clear decision dissolves the whole mess. What looked huge was mostly smoke.
ramacharitamanas::5128.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of confusion to the one action that breaks it.

ramacharitamanas::5129.verse_sanskrit: माया बिगत कपि भालु हरषे बिटप गिरि गहि सब फिरे। सर निकर छाड़े राम रावन बाहु सिर पुनि महि गिरे॥ श्रीराम रावन समर चरित अनेक कल्प जो गावहीं। सत सेष सारद निगम कबि तेउ तदपि पार न पावहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5129.verse_hindi: माया दूर हो जाने पर वानर-भालू हर्षित हुए और वृक्ष तथा पर्वत ले-लेकर सब लौट पड़े। श्री रामजी ने बाणों के समूह छोड़े, जिनसे रावण के हाथ और सिर फिर कट-कटकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। श्री रामजी और रावण के युद्ध का चरित्र यदि सैकड़ों शेष, सरस्वती, वेद और कवि अनेक कल्पों तक गाते रहें, तो भी उसका पार नहीं पा सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::5129.english_translation: When the veil of illusion lifted, the monkeys and bears rejoiced and returned, lifting trees and mountains. Lord Ram then loosed volleys of arrows, and Ravana's arms and heads fell again and again to the ground. The deeds of the war between Lord Ram and Ravana are beyond measure: even if hundreds of Shesh, Saraswati, the Vedas, and poets sang for countless ages, they could not reach the far shore.
ramacharitamanas::5129.translation_literal: माया (veil of illusion) / बिगत (gone) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / हरषे (rejoiced) / बिटप (trees) / गिरि (mountains) / गहि (grasping) / सब (all) / फिरे (returned) / सर (arrows) / निकर (rows, heaps) / छाड़े (released) / राम (Ram) / रावन (Ravana) / बाहु (arms) / सिर (heads) / पुनि (again) / महि (to the earth) / गिरे (fell) ॥ श्रीराम (Lord Ram) / रावन (Ravana) / समर (war) / चरित (deeds, story) / अनेक (many) / कल्प (ages) / जो (who) / गावहीं (sing) / सत (hundred) / सेष (Shesh) / सारद (Saraswati) / निगम (Vedas) / कबि (poets) / तेउ (even they) / तदपि (still) / पार (far shore, end) / न (not) / पावहीं (reach) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5129.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5129.essence: Some events are so vast that even endless telling cannot finish them.
ramacharitamanas::5129.simple_meaning: The battle surges again: the monkeys and bears return to fighting, Ram keeps cutting down Ravana's arms and heads, and the poem says this war is too vast for anyone to fully describe.
ramacharitamanas::5129.simple_insight: Some events are too large to contain in words, even when the heart tries.
ramacharitamanas::5129.detailed_meaning: The war in Lanka is at its fiercest. With the illusion of fear gone, the monkey and bear army surges back into battle while Ram keeps striking Ravana down again and again. The verse then pauses to say that even endless praise could never fully capture this struggle.
ramacharitamanas::5129.insight: It shifts attention from the battle's details to its overwhelming scale and epic weight.

ramacharitamanas::5130.verse_sanskrit: ताके गुन गन कछु कहे जड़मति तुलसीदास। जिमि निज बल अनुरूप ते माछी उड़इ अकास ॥
ramacharitamanas::5130.verse_hindi: उसी चरित्र के कुछ गुणगण मंदबुद्धि तुलसीदास ने कहे हैं, जैसे मक्खी भी अपने पुरुषार्थ के अनुसार आकाश में उड़ती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5130.english_translation: Tulsidas, with dull wit, has spoken some qualities of that character, just as a fly flies in the sky according to its own small strength.
ramacharitamanas::5130.translation_literal: ताके (of that) / गुन गन (qualities, many) / कछु (some) / कहे (said) / जड़मति (dull-minded) / तुलसीदास (Tulsidas) / जिमि (just as) / निज (own) / बल (strength) / अनुरूप (according to) / ते (that) / माछी (fly) / उड़इ (flies) / अकास (sky)
ramacharitamanas::5130.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5130.essence: Even praise is tiny beside what it tries to name.
ramacharitamanas::5130.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he has only described a few qualities of Ram's character, and only to the limit of his own small ability.
ramacharitamanas::5130.simple_insight: Real reverence is humble: you speak only as far as your own strength allows.
ramacharitamanas::5130.detailed_meaning: In Lankakand, after the fierce battle scenes, Tulsidas steps back and bows his head. He says he has described only a few of Ram's qualities, and even that was possible only within his limited capacity, like a fly crossing the sky on tiny wings.
ramacharitamanas::5130.modern_relevance: You finish a big project and still feel it barely captured what mattered. That quiet honesty — knowing your reach without pretending otherwise — is what this line models.
ramacharitamanas::5130.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to humility before greatness.

ramacharitamanas::5131.verse_sanskrit: काटे सिर भुज बार बहु मरत न भट लंकेस। प्रभु क्रीड़त सुर सिद्ध मुनि ब्याकुल देखि कलेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5131.verse_hindi: सिर और भुजाएँ बहुत बार काटी गईं। फिर भी वीर रावण मरता नहीं। प्रभु तो खेल कर रहे हैं, परन्तु मुनि, सिद्ध और देवता उस क्लेश को देखकर (प्रभु को क्लेश पाते समझकर) व्याकुल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5131.english_translation: His heads and arms were cut off many times, yet the lord of Lanka did not die. The divine one was merely playing, but sages, perfected beings, and radiant beings were distressed to see the suffering.
ramacharitamanas::5131.translation_literal: काटे (cut) / सिर (heads) / भुज (arms) / बार बहु (many times) / मरत न (did not die) / भट (warrior) / लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / प्रभु (the divine one) / क्रीड़त (playing) / सुर (radiant beings) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनि (sages) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / देखि (seeing) / कलेस (suffering)
ramacharitamanas::5131.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5131.essence: What looks like suffering may be only divine play.
ramacharitamanas::5131.simple_meaning: Ravana keeps surviving even after repeated attacks, and the onlookers are upset because they think the divine one is suffering.
ramacharitamanas::5131.simple_insight: What looks like defeat can still be part of a larger play you cannot yet understand.
ramacharitamanas::5131.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Ram keeps striking Ravana down, yet Ravana rises again. The battlefield looks endless. Sages and radiant beings watching from above grow anxious, mistaking the divine play for real distress.
ramacharitamanas::5131.modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix the same problem, and it only seems to multiply. From the outside, it looks like failure; from a wider view, the pattern is still unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::5131.insight: It shifts attention from visible struggle to the larger meaning hidden inside it.

ramacharitamanas::5132.verse_sanskrit: काटत बढ़हिं सीस समुदाई। जिमि प्रति लाभ लोभ अधिकाई॥ मरइ न रिपु श्रम भयउ बिसेषा। राम बिभीषन तन तब देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5132.verse_hindi: काटते ही सिरों का समूह बढ़ जाता है, जैसे प्रत्येक लाभ पर लोभ बढ़ता है। शत्रु मरता नहीं और परिश्रम बहुत हुआ। तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने विभीषण की ओर देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5132.english_translation: As soon as they are cut, the heads multiply, just as greed grows with every gain. The enemy does not die, and the effort has been great. Then Lord Ramchandra looked toward Vibhishana.
ramacharitamanas::5132.translation_literal: काटत (while cutting) / बढ़हिं (grow) / सीस (heads) / समुदाई (in a group, in multitude) / जिमि (just as) / प्रति (each) / लाभ (gain) / लोभ (greed) / अधिकाई (increases) / मरइ (dies) / न (not) / रिपु (enemy) / श्रम (effort, exertion) / भयउ (became, was) / बिसेषा (great, especially) / राम (Ram) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / तन (toward) / तब (then) / देखा (looked)
ramacharitamanas::5132.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5132.essence: Brute force fails when the problem keeps regenerating.
ramacharitamanas::5132.simple_meaning: Cutting down this enemy only makes more heads appear, like greed that grows with every gain. The struggle has been exhausting, and Ram turns toward Vibhishana for help.
ramacharitamanas::5132.simple_insight: Some problems multiply when attacked the wrong way.
ramacharitamanas::5132.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the battle against Ravana is dragging on. Every time a head is cut off, more seem to appear, and the warriors are worn out. Seeing the limits of brute force, Ram turns toward Vibhishana, the one who can guide the next move.
ramacharitamanas::5132.modern_relevance: You keep deleting spam accounts, and two more appear. You keep patching the leak, and the pipe still bursts. Sometimes force alone only proves that the real answer lies elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::5132.insight: It shifts attention from repeated attack to wiser strategy and the right ally.

ramacharitamanas::5133.verse_sanskrit: उमा काल मर जाकीं ईछा। सो प्रभु जन कर प्रीति परीछा॥ सुनु सरबग्य चराचर नायक। प्रनतपाल सुर मुनि सुखदायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::5133.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! जिसकी इच्छा मात्र से काल भी मर जाता है, वही प्रभु सेवक की प्रीति की परीक्षा ले रहे हैं। (विभीषणजी ने कहा-) हे सर्वज्ञ! हे चराचर के स्वामी! हे शरणागत के पालन करने वाले! हे देवता और मुनियों को सुख देने वाले! सुनिए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5133.english_translation: O Uma, the Lord by whose wish even Time can die is testing the devotion of his servant. Listen, all-knowing one, ruler of all moving and unmoving beings, protector of those who surrender, giver of joy to gods and sages.
ramacharitamanas::5133.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma) / काल (Time) / मर (dies) / जाकीं (whose) / ईछा (wish) / सो (that) / प्रभु (Lord) / जन कर (of the servant) / प्रीति (love/devotion) / परीछा (test) ॥ सुनु (listen) / सरबग्य (all-knowing) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / नायक (ruler/leader) / प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / सुर (devas) / मुनि (sages) / सुखदायक (giver of joy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5133.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5133.essence: Even the all-powerful may test the heart that loves him.
ramacharitamanas::5133.simple_meaning: Ram is so powerful that even Time obeys him, yet he still tests the devotion of his servant. He is also praised as the all-knowing protector of everyone who seeks refuge.
ramacharitamanas::5133.simple_insight: Love deepens when it is tested and still remains steady.
ramacharitamanas::5133.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's repeated wounds fail to end the battle, Shiva explains to Uma that Ram is not struggling because he lacks power. He is testing Vibhishana's devotion. Vibhishana then praises Ram as the all-knowing protector of all beings.
ramacharitamanas::5133.modern_relevance: You finally reach out for help after a long crisis, and the person you trust seems silent. That silence may not be rejection; it may be the moment your sincerity is being refined.
ramacharitamanas::5133.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding immediate proof to staying faithful through the test.

ramacharitamanas::5134.verse_sanskrit: नाभिकुंड पियूष बस याकें। नाथ जिअत रावनु बल ताकें॥ सुनत बिभीषन बचन कृपाला। हरषि गहे कर बान कराला ॥
ramacharitamanas::5134.verse_hindi: इसके नाभिकुंड में अमृत का निवास है। हे नाथ! रावण उसी के बल पर जीता है। विभीषण के वचन सुनते ही कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी ने हर्षित होकर हाथ में विकराल बाण लिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5134.english_translation: There is nectar in his navel-cavity, and by that strength Ravana still lives. Hearing Vibhishana's words, the compassionate Lord Raghunath rejoiced and took up a fierce arrow.
ramacharitamanas::5134.translation_literal: नाभिकुंड (navel-cavity) / पियूष (nectar) / बस (dwells) / याकें (in this) / नाथ (lord) / जिअत (living) / रावनु (Ravana) / बल (strength) / ताकें (by that)॥ / सुनत (hearing) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana's) / बचन (words) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / हरषि (rejoicing) / गहे (took) / कर (in hand) / बान (arrow) / कराला (fierce) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5134.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5134.essence: Hidden knowledge can turn a long struggle into a single decisive move.
ramacharitamanas::5134.simple_meaning: Vibhishana points out that Ravana survives because of a hidden nectar in his navel. Hearing this, Ram takes up a fierce arrow at once.
ramacharitamanas::5134.simple_insight: Seeing the real weakness changes everything. Clear information can end hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::5134.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final war, Vibhishana reveals Ravana’s secret weakness to Ram. The battle is no longer just force against force; it now has a hidden target. Ram responds immediately, ready to end the conflict.
ramacharitamanas::5134.modern_relevance: You finally learn the real reason a project keeps failing: not the obvious problem, but the hidden one underneath. The whole mood shifts once the truth is named.
ramacharitamanas::5134.insight: It shows that accurate insight turns effort into decisive action.

ramacharitamanas::5135.verse_sanskrit: असुभ होन लागे तब नाना। रोवहिं खर सृकाल बहु स्वाना॥ बोलहिं खग जग आरति हेतू। प्रगट भए नभ जहँ तहँ केतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::5135.verse_hindi: उस समय नाना प्रकार के अपशकुन होने लगे। बहुत से गदहे, स्यार और कुत्ते रोने लगे। जगत् के दुःख (अशुभ) को सूचित करने के लिए पक्षी बोलने लगे। आकाश में जहाँ-तहाँ केतु (पुच्छल तारे) प्रकट हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5135.english_translation: At that time, many bad omens began to appear. Donkeys, jackals, and many dogs howled. Birds cried out, and comets appeared everywhere in the sky, signaling a world of distress.
ramacharitamanas::5135.translation_literal: असुभ (inauspicious) / होन (to happen) / लागे (began) / तब (then) / नाना (various) / रोवहिं (howl/cry) / खर (donkeys) / सृकाल (jackals) / बहु (many) / स्वाना (dogs) / बोलहिं (cry out) / खग (birds) / जग (world) / आरति (distress) / हेतू (for the sake of) / प्रगट (manifest) / भए (became) / नभ (sky) / जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / केतू (comets)
ramacharitamanas::5135.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5135.essence: The world itself seems to announce approaching ruin.
ramacharitamanas::5135.simple_meaning: Bad omens appear everywhere: animals howl, birds cry out, and comets flash in the sky.
ramacharitamanas::5135.simple_insight: When everything feels off, the world itself seems to warn you before the fall.
ramacharitamanas::5135.detailed_meaning: As the war in Lanka turns toward disaster, the scene darkens with signs of coming ruin. Donkeys, jackals, and dogs howl, birds cry out, and comets fill the sky. It is a warning before the next blow.
ramacharitamanas::5135.modern_relevance: You wake before dawn and something feels wrong before the email arrives, before the call comes, before anyone says it aloud. The air itself seems to know.
ramacharitamanas::5135.insight: It heightens the sense of approaching collapse by using nature as a warning signal.

ramacharitamanas::5136.verse_sanskrit: दस दिसि दाह होन अति लागा। भयउ परब बिनु रबि उपरागा॥ मंदोदरि उर कंपति भारी। प्रतिमा स्रवहिं नयन मग बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5136.verse_hindi: दसों दिशाओं में अत्यंत दाह होने लगा (आग लगने लगी) बिना ही पर्व (योग) के सूर्यग्रहण होने लगा। मंदोदरी का हृदय बहुत काँपने लगा। मूर्तियाँ नेत्र मार्ग से जल बहाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5136.english_translation: A fierce burning spread in all ten directions. An eclipse appeared without the moon's proper alignment. Mandodari's heart shook hard. Even the statues began to weep through their eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5136.translation_literal: दस दिसि (ten directions) / दाह (burning) / होन (to happen) / अति (very much) / लागा (began) / भयउ (became) / परब (eclipse/festival day) / बिनु (without) / रबि (sun) / उपरागा (eclipse) / मंदोदरि (Mandodari) / उर (heart) / कंपति (trembles) / भारी (greatly) / प्रतिमा (statues) / स्रवहिं (flow) / नयन (eyes) / मग (path) / बारी (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::5136.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5136.essence: When adharma ripens, even the world seems to grieve.
ramacharitamanas::5136.simple_meaning: The world around Lanka turns ominous: heat, tremors, tears, and unnatural signs all signal disaster.
ramacharitamanas::5136.simple_insight: When reality itself feels disturbed, you know something deeply wrong is unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::5136.detailed_meaning: As the battle tightens around Lanka, the sky and earth begin to revolt. Heat rises in every direction, Mandodari trembles, and even statues seem to cry. Tulsidas uses these signs to show Ravana's world collapsing before the final blow.
ramacharitamanas::5136.modern_relevance: The room goes strangely quiet before bad news lands. A phone keeps buzzing, your stomach tightens, and even small things feel off. You can sense that a structure is breaking before it falls.
ramacharitamanas::5136.insight: It shifts attention to warning signs that a situation has crossed into collapse.

ramacharitamanas::5137.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिमा रुदहिं पबिपात नभ अति बात बह डोलति मही। बरषहिं बलाहक रुधिर कच रज असुभ अति सक को कही॥ उतपात अमित बिलोकि नभ सुर बिकल बोलहिं जय जए। सुर सभय जानि कृपाल रघुपति चाप सर जोरत भए॥
ramacharitamanas::5137.verse_hindi: मूर्तियाँ रोने लगीं, आकाश से वज्रपात होने लगे, अत्यंत प्रचण्ड वायु बहने लगी, पृथ्वी हिलने लगी, बादल रक्त, बाल और धूल की वर्षा करने लगे। इस प्रकार इतने अधिक अमंगल होने लगे कि उनको कौन कह सकता है? अपरिमित उत्पात देखकर आकाश में देवता व्याकुल होकर जय-जय पुकार उठे। देवताओं को भयभीत जानकर कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी धनुष पर बाण सन्धान करने लगे।
ramacharitamanas::5137.english_translation: Idols began to weep, lightning struck the sky, fierce winds blew, the earth trembled, and clouds rained blood, hair, and dust. Who could count such countless omens? Seeing the sky filled with calamities, the gods grew restless and cried out, “Victory! Victory!” Knowing them afraid, compassionate Raghu’s lord drew his bow and prepared his arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5137.translation_literal: प्रतिमा (idols) / रुदहिं (weep) / पबिपात (lightning-strike) / नभ (sky) / अति (very) / बात (wind) / बह (blows) / डोलति (trembles) / मही (earth) / बरषहिं (rain) / बलाहक (clouds) / रुधिर (blood) / कच (hair) / रज (dust) / असुभ (inauspicious) / अति (very) / सक (who) / कही (say) / उतपात (omens/calamities) / अमित (countless) / बिलोकि (seeing) / नभ (sky) / सुर (gods) / बिकल (agitated) / बोलहिं (cry out) / जय जए (victory, victory) / सुर (the gods) / सभय (afraid) / जानि (knowing) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुपति (lord of Raghu) / चाप (bow) / सर (arrows) / जोरत (joining/preparing) / भए (became)
ramacharitamanas::5137.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5137.essence: True composure shows itself when everything else is shaking.
ramacharitamanas::5137.simple_meaning: The world fills with terrible signs as the battle turns. Even the gods panic, and Ram calmly prepares his bow to protect them.
ramacharitamanas::5137.simple_insight: When chaos peaks, steadiness becomes the real power.
ramacharitamanas::5137.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s final war, the sky and earth themselves seem to revolt: idols weep, storms rage, and the gods lose their composure. Seeing their fear, Ram responds not with panic but with action, lifting his bow to restore order.
ramacharitamanas::5137.modern_relevance: The group chat is exploding, the deadline has broken, and everyone is spiraling. In the middle of that noise, someone still needs a steady hand.
ramacharitamanas::5137.insight: It shifts attention from reacting to crisis toward becoming the one who can meet it cleanly.

ramacharitamanas::5138.verse_sanskrit: खैंचि सरासन श्रवन लगि छाड़े सर एकतीस। रघुनायक सायक चले मानहुँ काल फनीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5138.verse_hindi: कानों तक धनुष को खींचकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने इकतीस बाण छोड़े। वे श्री रामचंद्रजी के बाण ऐसे चले मानो कालसर्प हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5138.english_translation: Drawing the bow to his ear, Raghunath released thirty-one arrows. Rama's arrows flew like the serpent of time.
ramacharitamanas::5138.translation_literal: खैंचि (drawing) / सरासन (the bow) / श्रवन लगि (up to the ear) / छाड़े (released) / सर (arrows) / एकतीस (thirty-one) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / सायक (arrows) / चले (flew) / मानहुँ (as if) / काल (time/death) / फनीस (serpent)
ramacharitamanas::5138.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5138.essence: Ram's arrows strike with the force of time itself.
ramacharitamanas::5138.simple_meaning: Ram draws his bow to his ear and releases thirty-one arrows with force, as if time itself has become a serpent.
ramacharitamanas::5138.simple_insight: The moment calls for complete force, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::5138.detailed_meaning: In the battle of Lanka, the fighting has turned ominous and the sky itself seems disturbed. Ram answers Ravana's side with a deadly volley of thirty-one arrows. The verse is a vivid combat detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5138.insight: It shows the speed and decisiveness of action in battle.

ramacharitamanas::5139.verse_sanskrit: सायक एक नाभि सर सोषा। अपर लगे भुज सिर करि रोषा॥ लै सिर बाहु चले नाराचा। सिर भुज हीन रुंड महि नाचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5139.verse_hindi: एक बाण ने नाभि के अमृत कुंड को सोख लिया। दूसरे तीस बाण कोप करके उसके सिरों और भुजाओं में लगे। बाण सिरों और भुजाओं को लेकर चले। सिरों और भुजाओं से रहित रुण्ड (धड़) पृथ्वी पर नाचने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5139.english_translation: One arrow dried up the nectar pool in his navel. The other arrows, in anger, struck his heads and arms. The arrows carried away the heads and arms. The headless trunk danced on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::5139.translation_literal: सायक (arrow) / एक (one) / नाभि (navel) / सर (pool) / सोषा (dried up) / अपर (other) / लगे (struck) / भुज (arms) / सिर (heads) / करि (with) / रोषा (anger) / लै (taking) / सिर (heads) / बाहु (arms) / चले (went) / नाराचा (arrows) / सिर (head) / भुज (arms) / हीन (without) / रुंड (trunk) / महि (on the earth) / नाचा (danced)
ramacharitamanas::5139.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5139.essence: Ravana’s strength is cut down to frantic ruin.
ramacharitamanas::5139.simple_meaning: Rama’s arrows strike Ravana so fiercely that his life source is drained, his heads and arms are severed, and his body thrashes on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::5139.simple_insight: Pride can look powerful right up to the moment it falls apart.
ramacharitamanas::5139.detailed_meaning: In the Lankakand battle, Ravana is already being overwhelmed. Rama’s arrows hit the hidden life-centre in his body, then tear through his heads and arms. The verse is a vivid combat detail, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5139.modern_relevance: A public argument has already gone too far, and the other person keeps lashing out. You can see the collapse beneath the noise, even before it fully lands.
ramacharitamanas::5139.insight: It shows how quickly force and arrogance can turn into helplessness.

ramacharitamanas::5140.verse_sanskrit: धरनि धसइ धर धाव प्रचंडा। तब सर हति प्रभु कृत दुइ खंडा॥ गर्जेउ मरत घोर रव भारी। कहाँ रामु रन हतौं पचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5140.verse_hindi: धड़ प्रचण्ड वेग से दौड़ता है, जिससे धरती धँसने लगी। तब प्रभु ने बाण मारकर उसके दो टुकड़े कर दिए। मरते समय रावण बड़े घोर शब्द से गरजकर बोला- राम कहाँ हैं? मैं ललकारकर उनको युद्ध में मारूँ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5140.english_translation: The body rushed forward with fierce speed, and the earth seemed to sink. Then the Lord struck with an arrow and cut it into two pieces. As he was dying, Ravana roared in a terrible voice, "Where is Ram? I will challenge him and kill him in battle!"
ramacharitamanas::5140.translation_literal: धरनि (earth) / धसइ (sinks) / धर (body) / धाव (runs) / प्रचंडा (fiercely) / तब (then) / सर (arrow) / हति (struck) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कृत (made) / दुइ (two) / खंडा (pieces) / गर्जेउ (roared) / मरत (dying) / घोर (terrible) / रव (voice) / भारी (great) / कहाँ (where) / रामु (Ram) / रन (battle) / हतौं (I will strike/kill) / पचारी (challenging, calling out)
ramacharitamanas::5140.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5140.essence: Ego can keep shouting after defeat has already arrived.
ramacharitamanas::5140.simple_meaning: Ravana’s body lunges forward, but Ram’s arrow cuts him down. Even while dying, Ravana keeps shouting challenges instead of surrendering.
ramacharitamanas::5140.simple_insight: Pride can survive even at the edge of collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5140.detailed_meaning: In the Lankakand battle, Ravana’s massive body surges with one last burst of force. Ram answers instantly, splitting him apart. But even in death, Ravana’s ego keeps shouting for a fight, showing how deeply arrogance can outlast the body.
ramacharitamanas::5140.modern_relevance: Someone loses the argument, the job, the relationship — and still keeps texting, defending, and posturing as if nothing has changed. The body may fall before the ego does.
ramacharitamanas::5140.insight: It shows how unchecked ego refuses reality, even when defeat is already complete.

ramacharitamanas::5141.verse_sanskrit: डोली भूमि गिरत दसकंधर। छुभित सिंधु सरि दिग्गज भूधर॥ धरनि परेउ द्वौ खंड बढ़ाई। चापि भालु मर्कट समुदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5141.verse_hindi: रावण के गिरते ही पृथ्वी हिल गई। समुद्र, नदियाँ, दिशाओं के हाथी और पर्वत क्षुब्ध हो उठे। रावण धड़ के दोनों टुकड़ों को फैलाकर भालू और वानरों के समुदाय को दबाता हुआ पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5141.english_translation: As Ravana fell, the earth trembled. The ocean, rivers, guardian elephants, and mountains were shaken. His two severed halves fell to the ground, crushing the bears and monkeys as they struck the earth.
ramacharitamanas::5141.translation_literal: डोली (trembled) / भूमि (earth) / गिरत (falling) / दसकंधर (ten-necked one, Ravana) / छुभित (shaken) / सिंधु (ocean) / सरि (rivers) / दिग्गज (guardian elephants of the directions) / भूधर (mountains) / धरनि (on the earth) / परेउ (fell) / द्वौ (two) / खंड (halves) / बढ़ाई (spread out) / चापि (crushing) / भालु (bears) / मर्कट (monkeys) / समुदाई (community, host)
ramacharitamanas::5141.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5141.essence: His fall is so vast it shakes the world around him.
ramacharitamanas::5141.simple_meaning: Ravana's fall shakes the whole world, and his broken body crushes the monkey and bear armies as it hits the ground.
ramacharitamanas::5141.simple_insight: Even a fallen ego can still cause damage on its way down.
ramacharitamanas::5141.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just been cut down in battle. As his huge body collapses, the earth itself seems to shudder, and the sea, rivers, elephants, and mountains are disturbed. This is a vivid battlefield detail showing the scale of his fall, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5141.modern_relevance: A powerful person loses everything in public, and the whole room still feels the impact. Even collapse can leave a mess behind.
ramacharitamanas::5141.insight: It keeps the focus on the physical aftermath of defeat rather than on victory or moral reflection.

ramacharitamanas::5142.verse_sanskrit: मंदोदरि आगें भुज सीसा। धरि सर चले जहाँ जगदीसा॥ प्रबिसे सब निषंग महुँ जाई। देखि सुरन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5142.verse_hindi: रावण की भुजाओं और सिरों को मंदोदरी के सामने रखकर रामबाण वहाँ चले, जहाँ जगदीश्वर श्री रामजी थे। सब बाण जाकर तरकस में प्रवेश कर गए। यह देखकर देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5142.english_translation: Holding Ravana's arms and heads before Mandodari, the arrows went back to where the Lord of the world was. All the arrows entered the quiver again. Seeing this, the radiant beings beat their drums.
ramacharitamanas::5142.translation_literal: मंदोदरि (before Mandodari) / आगें (in front) / भुज (arms) / सीसा (heads) / धरि (holding) / सर (arrows) / चले (went) / जहाँ (where) / जगदीसा (Lord of the world) / प्रबिसे (entered) / सब (all) / निषंग (quiver) / महुँ (into) / जाई (going) / देखि (seeing) / सुरन्ह (the radiant beings) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजाई (beat)
ramacharitamanas::5142.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5142.essence: Even victory returns to Ram's hands.
ramacharitamanas::5142.simple_meaning: The arrows finish their work and return to Ram's quiver. The radiant beings celebrate what they see.
ramacharitamanas::5142.simple_insight: Some victories are so complete they seem to undo themselves.
ramacharitamanas::5142.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just fallen. In the stunned silence after his defeat, the arrows that destroyed him are shown returning to Ram's quiver, as if the battle itself bows back to dharma. The radiant beings rejoice because the war's turning point is complete.
ramacharitamanas::5142.modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you realize the sharp words are already gone, and all that's left is the relief of what did not have to continue.
ramacharitamanas::5142.insight: It turns a killing blow into a sign of perfect control, not rage.

ramacharitamanas::5143.verse_sanskrit: तासु तेज समान प्रभु आनन। हरषे देखि संभु चतुरानन॥ जय जय धुनि पूरी ब्रह्मंडा। जय रघुबीर प्रबल भुजदंडा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5143.verse_hindi: रावण का तेज प्रभु के मुख में समा गया। यह देखकर शिवजी और ब्रह्माजी हर्षित हुए। ब्रह्माण्डभर में जय-जय की ध्वनि भर गई। प्रबल भुजदण्डों वाले श्री रघुवीर की जय हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5143.english_translation: Ravana's power was absorbed into the Lord's face. Seeing this, Shiva and Brahma rejoiced. The cry of victory filled the whole universe: victory to the mighty-armed Raghubir!
ramacharitamanas::5143.translation_literal: तासु (his) / तेज (splendor, power) / समान (equal to) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आनन (face) / हरषे (rejoiced) / देखि (seeing) / संभु (Shiva) / चतुरानन (four-faced Brahma) / जय (victory) / जय (victory) / धुनि (sound, cry) / पूरी (filled) / ब्रह्मंडा (the universe) / जय (victory) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / प्रबल (mighty) / भुजदंडा (arms like clubs)
ramacharitamanas::5143.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5143.essence: Ram's victory is the universe's relief.
ramacharitamanas::5143.simple_meaning: Ravana is defeated, and even the gods rejoice as victory for Ram spreads through the universe.
ramacharitamanas::5143.simple_insight: When arrogance falls, the whole world can breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::5143.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just been struck down in battle. His power is swallowed into Ram's radiance, and Shiva and Brahma rejoice at the sight. The victory cry now rolls through creation itself as the war turns decisively in Ram's favor.
ramacharitamanas::5143.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after the person who dominated everyone finally loses their grip. The relief is instant — not because someone won, but because the pressure of ego has lifted.
ramacharitamanas::5143.insight: It shifts attention from the enemy's force to the calm authority that ends it.

ramacharitamanas::5144.verse_sanskrit: बरषहिं सुमन देव मुनि बृंदा। जय कृपाल जय जयति मुकुंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5144.verse_hindi: देवता और मुनियों के समूह फूल बरसाते हैं और कहते हैं- कृपालु की जय हो, मुकुन्द की जय हो, जय हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5144.english_translation: The gods and sages shower flowers, crying, “Victory to the compassionate one! Victory to Mukunda!”
ramacharitamanas::5144.translation_literal: बरषहिं (are showering) / सुमन (flowers) / देव (gods) / मुनि (sages) / बृंदा (groups) / जय (victory) / कृपाल (to the compassionate one) / जय (victory) / जयति (victorious) / मुकुंदा (Mukunda)
ramacharitamanas::5144.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5144.essence: Ram's victory draws praise because compassion has triumphed.
ramacharitamanas::5144.simple_meaning: The gods and sages celebrate Ram with flowers and praise, calling him compassionate and victorious.
ramacharitamanas::5144.simple_insight: Some victories are met with gratitude, not fear.
ramacharitamanas::5144.detailed_meaning: After Ravana falls, the heavens answer with praise. Gods and sages shower flowers on Ram, celebrating the compassionate one whose victory restores order. This verse is part of the victory scene, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5144.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after the hard meeting ends, and the people who saw the struggle finally exhale. Some moments are not for argument anymore — only for recognition.
ramacharitamanas::5144.insight: It shifts attention from battle to blessing, showing that true victory invites reverence.

ramacharitamanas::5145.verse_sanskrit: जय कृपा कंद मुकुंद द्वंद हरन सरन सुखप्रद प्रभो। खल दल बिदारन परम कारन कारुनीक सदा बिभो॥ सुर सुमन बरषहिं हरष संकुल बाज दुंदुभि गहगही। संग्राम अंगन राम अंग अनंग बहु सोभा लही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5145.verse_hindi: हे कृपा के कंद! हे मोक्षदाता मुकुन्द! हे (राग-द्वेष, हर्ष-शोक, जन्म-मृत्यु आदि) द्वंद्वों के हरने वाले! हे शरणागत को सुख देने वाले प्रभो! हे दुष्ट दल को विदीर्ण करने वाले! हे कारणों के भी परम कारण! हे सदा करुणा करने वाले! हे सर्वव्यापक विभो! आपकी जय हो। देवता हर्ष में भरे हुए पुष्प बरसाते हैं, घमाघम नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। रणभूमि में श्री रामचंद्रजी के अंगों ने बहुत से कामदेवों की शोभा प्राप्त की ॥
ramacharitamanas::5145.english_translation: Victory to the source of grace, to Mukunda who ends all dualities, to the Lord who gives refuge and happiness! Victory to the destroyer of the wicked host, the supreme cause, the ever-compassionate, the all-pervading one. The devas shower flowers in joy and the drums thunder. On the battlefield, Ram's limbs gained the beauty of many love-gods.
ramacharitamanas::5145.translation_literal: जय (victory) / कृपा (grace) / कंद (source) / मुकुंद (Mukunda) / द्वंद (duality) / हरन (remover) / सरन (refuge) / सुखप्रद (giver of happiness) / प्रभो (Lord) / खल (wicked) / दल (host) / बिदारन (destroyer) / परम (supreme) / कारन (cause) / कारुनीक (compassionate) / सदा (always) / बिभो (all-pervading) / सुर (devas) / सुमन (flowers) / बरषहिं (shower) / हरष (joy) / संकुल (filled) / बाज (sound) / दुंदुभि (drums) / गहगही (resounding) / संग्राम (battle) / अंगन (field) / राम (Ram) / अंग (limbs) / अनंग (love-god) / बहु (many) / सोभा (beauty) / लही (gained)
ramacharitamanas::5145.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5145.essence: Ram turns the battlefield into a place of grace.
ramacharitamanas::5145.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the giver of refuge, the remover of conflict, and the destroyer of evil. The gods rejoice, flowers rain down, and the battlefield itself becomes beautiful around him.
ramacharitamanas::5145.simple_insight: Even in war, Ram is being seen as mercy, refuge, and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::5145.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, the victory cry rises around Ram as the gods shower flowers and drums thunder. This verse is part of that celebration, piling up praise for Ram before the scene shifts to his radiant appearance in battle.
ramacharitamanas::5145.modern_relevance: You step into a room where everything feels tense, and somehow your steady presence lowers the temperature. That is the kind of force this verse celebrates.
ramacharitamanas::5145.insight: It shifts attention from violence itself to the radiance, mercy, and order that surround right action.

ramacharitamanas::5146.verse_sanskrit: सिर जटा मुकुट प्रसून बिच बिच अति मनोहर राजहीं। जनु नीलगिरि पर तड़ित पटल समेत उडुगन भ्राजहीं॥ भुजदंड सर कोदंड फेरत रुधिर कन तन अति बने। जनु रायमुनीं तमाल पर बैठीं बिपुल सुख आपने ॥
ramacharitamanas::5146.verse_hindi: सिर पर जटाओं का मुकुट है, जिसके बीच में अत्यंत मनोहर पुष्प शोभा दे रहे हैं। मानो नीले पर्वत पर बिजली के समूह सहित नक्षत्र सुशो भित हो रहे हैं। श्री रामजी अपने भुजदण्डों से बाण और धनुष फिरा रहे हैं। शरीर पर रुधिर के कण अत्यंत सुंदर लगते हैं। मानो तमाल के वृक्ष पर बहुत सी ललमुनियाँ चिड़ियाँ अपने महान् सुख में मग्न हुई निश्चल बैठी हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5146.english_translation: His hair is matted like a crown, with flowers shining beautifully among the locks, like stars gleaming on a blue mountain with flashes of lightning. Ram moves his bow and arrow with his mighty arms; the drops of blood on his body look beautiful, like flocks of birds resting in delight on a tamala tree.
ramacharitamanas::5146.translation_literal: सिर (head) / जटा (matted hair) / मुकुट (crown) / प्रसून (flowers) / बिच बिच (here and there) / अति (very) / मनोहर (beautiful) / राजहीं (shine) / जनु (as if) / नीलगिरि (blue mountain) / पर (on) / तड़ित पटल (sheet of lightning) / समेत (together with) / उडुगन (stars) / भ्राजहीं (shine)॥ / भुजदंड (arm-like staff, mighty arms) / सर (arrow) / कोदंड (bow) / फेरत (turning, moving) / रुधिर (blood) / कन (drops) / तन (body) / अति (very) / बने (beautiful) / जनु (as if) / रायमुनीं (royal sages) / तमाल (tamala tree) / पर (on) / बैठीं (sitting) / बिपुल (great) / सुख (joy) / आपने (their own)॥
ramacharitamanas::5146.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5146.essence: Beauty can shine even through the marks of battle.
ramacharitamanas::5146.simple_meaning: Ram is shown in the aftermath of battle, radiant and beautiful despite the blood on his body. The verse turns his warlike form into a vision of splendor and calm.
ramacharitamanas::5146.simple_insight: Even in struggle, true dignity can remain untouched.
ramacharitamanas::5146.detailed_meaning: After the war’s turning point, Ram stands with matted hair, flowers, bow, and blood-spotted body. The poet lingers on his appearance, not to glorify violence, but to reveal divine beauty shining through battle and victory.
ramacharitamanas::5146.modern_relevance: You come home exhausted after a hard day, clothes stained, body aching, yet something in you feels steady. The outer mess does not cancel the inner nobility.
ramacharitamanas::5146.insight: It shifts attention from the wound itself to the radiance that can remain present through conflict.

ramacharitamanas::5147.verse_sanskrit: कृपादृष्टि करि बृष्टि प्रभु अभय किए सुर बृंद। भालु कीस सब हरषे जय सुख धाम मुकुंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::5147.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कृपा दृष्टि की वर्षा करके देव समूह को निर्भय कर दिया। वानर-भालू सब हर्षित हुए और सुखधाम मुकुन्द की जय हो, ऐसा पुकारने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5147.english_translation: By showering his gracious glance, the Lord made the celestial hosts fearless. All the monkeys and bears rejoiced and cried, “Victory to Mukunda, the home of bliss!”
ramacharitamanas::5147.translation_literal: कृपादृष्टि (gracious glance) / करि (having done) / बृष्टि (rain) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अभय (fearless) / किए (made) / सुर बृंद (hosts of radiant beings) / भालु (bears) / कीस (monkeys) / सब (all) / हरषे (rejoiced) / जय (victory) / सुख धाम (home of bliss) / मुकुंद (Mukunda)
ramacharitamanas::5147.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5147.essence: A gracious glance can turn fear into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5147.simple_meaning: Ram’s gracious glance removes fear and fills everyone with joy. Even the monkeys and bears celebrate his victory.
ramacharitamanas::5147.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you feel truly seen and protected.
ramacharitamanas::5147.detailed_meaning: After the battle’s turning point, Ram’s gracious glance falls on the gathered beings. The celestial hosts lose their fear, and the monkeys and bears erupt in joy, praising the Lord of bliss before the next sorrowful scene unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::5147.modern_relevance: After a tense family argument, one calm look from the person at the center changes the room. The fear drops first; relief and gratitude follow.
ramacharitamanas::5147.insight: It shifts attention from battle tension to the soothing power of divine presence.

ramacharitamanas::5148.verse_sanskrit: पति सिर देखत मंदोदरी। मुरुछित बिकल धरनि खसि परी॥ जुबति बृंद रोवत उठि धाईं। तेहि उठाइ रावन पहिं आईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5148.verse_hindi: पति के सिर देखते ही मंदोदरी व्याकुल और मूर्च्छित होकर धरती पर गिर पड़ी। स्त्रियाँ रोती हुई दौड़ीं और उस (मंदोदरी) को उठाकर रावण के पास आईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5148.english_translation: When she saw her husband’s head, Mandodari fainted and fell to the ground. The women ran weeping, lifted her up, and brought her to Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::5148.translation_literal: पति (husband) / सिर (head) / देखत (seeing) / मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / मुरुछित (fainted) / बिकल (distressed) / धरनि (ground) / खसि (falling) / परी (fell)॥ / जुबति (women) / बृंद (group) / रोवत (weeping) / उठि (rising) / धाईं (ran) / तेहि (her) / उठाइ (lifting) / रावन (Ravana) / पहिं (to) / आईं (came)॥
ramacharitamanas::5148.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5148.essence: Grief can strike so hard it drops the body first.
ramacharitamanas::5148.simple_meaning: Mandodari collapses in grief when she sees Ravana’s severed head, and the women rush to help her and bring her to him.
ramacharitamanas::5148.simple_insight: Some losses hit so hard that the body falls before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::5148.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has been defeated and killed. Mandodari sees his severed head and loses consciousness from shock. The women around her cry, lift her up, and carry her back to Ravana’s body, deepening the scene of ruin.
ramacharitamanas::5148.modern_relevance: You open a message and realize the relationship is over before you can even sit down. Your body reacts first; grief arrives faster than thought.
ramacharitamanas::5148.insight: It shows grief as immediate, physical, and overwhelming before any reflection can begin.

ramacharitamanas::5149.verse_sanskrit: पति गति देखि ते करहिं पुकारा। छूटे कच नहिं बपुष सँभारा॥ उर ताड़ना करहिं बिधि नाना। रोवत करहिं प्रताप बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5149.verse_hindi: पति की दशा देखकर वे पुकार-पुकारकर रोने लगीं। उनके बाल खुल गए, देह की संभाल नहीं रही। वे अनेकों प्रकार से छाती पीटती हैं और रोती हुई रावण के प्रताप का बखान करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5149.english_translation: Seeing their husband's condition, they cried out in grief. Their hair came loose and they could not hold themselves together. Beating their chests in many ways, they wept and praised Ravana's power.
ramacharitamanas::5149.translation_literal: पति (husband) / गति (condition) / देखि (seeing) / ते (they) / करहिं (do) / पुकारा (crying out) / छूटे (loosened) / कच (hair) / नहिं (not) / बपुष (body) / सँभारा (held together) / उर (chest) / ताड़ना (beating) / करहिं (do) / बिधि (many) / नाना (kinds) / रोवत (weeping) / करहिं (do) / प्रताप (power) / बखाना (praise)
ramacharitamanas::5149.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5149.essence: Grief can still praise what it has lost.
ramacharitamanas::5149.simple_meaning: The women are overwhelmed by grief at Ravana's fall. They lose control of themselves, weep loudly, and even praise the power he once had.
ramacharitamanas::5149.simple_insight: Shock can make admiration and grief spill out together.
ramacharitamanas::5149.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ravana's household women see his ruined state. Mandodari has already collapsed, and now the others cry, beat their chests, and speak of the strength he once possessed. The scene deepens the sorrow around his defeat.
ramacharitamanas::5149.modern_relevance: You stand at a hospital door after hearing news that changes everything. Your mind cannot sort grief from memory, and even praise slips out for what is already gone.
ramacharitamanas::5149.insight: It shows how collapse can leave people clinging to old images of power even while mourning the loss.

ramacharitamanas::5150.verse_sanskrit: तव बल नाथ डोल नित धरनी। तेज हीन पावक ससि तरनी॥ सेष कमठ सहि सकहिं न भारा। सो तनु भूमि परेउ भरि छारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5150.verse_hindi: (वे कहती हैं-) हे नाथ! तुम्हारे बल से पृथ्वी सदा काँपती रहती थी। अग्नि, चंद्रमा और सूर्य तुम्हारे सामने तेजहीन थे। शेष और कच्छप भी जिसका भार नहीं सह सकते थे, वही तुम्हारा शरीर आज धूल में भरा हुआ पृथ्वी पर पड़ा है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5150.english_translation: O lord, by your strength the earth always trembled. Fire, the moon, and the sun lost their brilliance before you. Even Shesha and the Tortoise could not bear your burden, and now that same body lies on the ground, covered with dust.
ramacharitamanas::5150.translation_literal: तव (your) / बल (strength) / नाथ (lord) / डोल (trembles) / नित (always) / धरनी (earth) / तेज (radiance) / हीन (without) / पावक (fire) / ससि (moon) / तरनी (sun) / सेष (Shesha) / कमठ (tortoise) / सहि (bearing) / सकहिं (can bear) / न (not) / भारा (burden) / सो (that) / तनु (body) / भूमि (on the ground) / परेउ (fell) / भरि (filled with) / छारा (dust)
ramacharitamanas::5150.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5150.essence: Great power can end in dust in a single moment.
ramacharitamanas::5150.simple_meaning: The women mourn Ravana by recalling how immense his strength once was, then contrast it with his body lying powerless in dust.
ramacharitamanas::5150.simple_insight: Power looks hollow when it cannot keep even its own body from falling.
ramacharitamanas::5150.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has been slain and the women around him are grieving over his body. They remember the terror of his strength, the way even cosmic forces seemed dim beside him, and now face the shock of that same might reduced to dust.
ramacharitamanas::5150.modern_relevance: You once filled the room with force, certainty, and noise. Now the silence after the fall makes everyone remember how temporary that power was.
ramacharitamanas::5150.insight: It shifts attention from dominance to impermanence, showing how quickly force becomes helplessness.

ramacharitamanas::5151.verse_sanskrit: बरुन कुबेर सुरेस समीरा। रन सन्मुख धरि काहुँ न धीरा॥ भुजबल जितेहु काल जम साईं। आजु परेहु अनाथ की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5151.verse_hindi: वरुण, कुबेर, इंद्र और वायु, इनमें से किसी ने भी रण में तुम्हारे सामने धैर्य धारण नहीं किया। हे स्वामी! तुमने अपने भुजबल से काल और यमराज को भी जीत लिया था। वही तुम आज अनाथ की तरह पड़े हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5151.english_translation: Varuna, Kubera, Indra, and Vayu could not hold their courage before you in battle. Lord, by your own arm strength you conquered even Time and Yama. Today you lie fallen like one without support.
ramacharitamanas::5151.translation_literal: बरुन (Varuna) / कुबेर (Kubera) / सुरेस (lord of the devas, Indra) / समीरा (Vayu) / रन (battle) / सन्मुख (face to face) / धरि (holding) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / धीरा (steadfast)॥ / भुजबल (arm-strength) / जितेहु (you conquered) / काल (Time) / जम (Yama) / साईं (lord) / आजु (today) / परेहु (you have fallen) / अनाथ (without support) / की नाईं (like)॥
ramacharitamanas::5151.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5151.essence: What once looked invincible can collapse into helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::5151.simple_meaning: The queens remember Ravana’s old power: even the great forces of the world once could not face him. Now he lies helpless, and all that strength has vanished.
ramacharitamanas::5151.simple_insight: Power can fill a life and still leave it empty in the end.
ramacharitamanas::5151.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the queens look at Ravana’s fallen body and grieve in shock. They recall how even Varuna, Kubera, Indra, and Vayu once could not stand before him, and how he had seemed to conquer even death itself. That memory makes his collapse unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::5151.modern_relevance: You watch someone who once dominated every room now unable to answer a phone call. The same force that looked unshakable can end in helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::5151.insight: It shifts the mind from admiring raw power to seeing how fragile ego-driven greatness really is.

ramacharitamanas::5152.verse_sanskrit: जगत बिदित तुम्हारि प्रभुताई। सुत परिजन बल बरनि न जाई॥ राम बिमुख अस हाल तुम्हारा। रहा न कोउ कुल रोवनिहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5152.verse_hindi: तुम्हारी प्रभुता जगत् भर में प्रसिद्ध है। तुम्हारे पुत्रों और कुटुम्बियों के बल का हाय! वर्णन ही नहीं हो सकता। श्री रामचंद्रजी के विमुख होने से तुम्हारी ऐसी दुर्दशा हुई कि आज कुल में कोई रोने वाला भी न रह गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5152.english_translation: Your rule was known throughout the world. No one could even describe the strength of your sons and kin. But being opposed to Ram has brought you to this state, where no one in your clan remains to weep for you.
ramacharitamanas::5152.translation_literal: जगत (world) / बिदित (known) / तुम्हारि (your) / प्रभुताई (sovereignty, rule) / सुत (sons) / परिजन (kin) / बल (strength) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be done)॥ / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (turned away from) / अस (such) / हाल (condition) / तुम्हारा (your) / रहा (remained) / न (not) / कोउ (any) / कुल (clan) / रोवनिहारा (one who weeps)॥
ramacharitamanas::5152.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::5152.essence: Power without alignment ends in loneliness.
ramacharitamanas::5152.simple_meaning: Ravana's former power was famous everywhere, but turning away from Ram has left him utterly broken, with no family member left to mourn him.
ramacharitamanas::5152.simple_insight: Pride can look untouchable until it meets the cost of separation.
ramacharitamanas::5152.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final collapse, Mandodari grieves over Ravana. She recalls how his power and family once seemed beyond measure, then points to the ruin brought by his rejection of Ram. The verse is part of her lament, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5152.modern_relevance: You can build a life that looks unbeatable from the outside, then lose its center in one stubborn refusal to listen. By the time the damage is visible, the room is already empty.
ramacharitamanas::5152.insight: It shifts attention from outward power to the inner cost of resisting what is right.

ramacharitamanas::5153.verse_sanskrit: तव बस बिधि प्रचंड सब नाथा। सभय दिसिप नित नावहिं माथा॥ अब तव सिर भुज जंबुक खाहीं। राम बिमुख यह अनुचित नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5153.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! विधाता की सारी सृष्टि तुम्हारे वश में थी। लोकपाल सदा भयभीत होकर तुमको मस्तक नवाते थे, किन्तु हाय! अब तुम्हारे सिर और भुजाओं को गीदड़ खा रहे हैं। राम विमुख के लिए ऐसा होना अनुचित भी नहीं है (अर्थात् उचित ही है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5153.english_translation: O lord, all creation once stood under your control. The guardians of the directions bowed their heads to you in fear. Now jackals eat your head and arms. For one turned away from Ram, this is not improper.
ramacharitamanas::5153.translation_literal: तव (your) / बस (under control) / बिधि (the creator) / प्रचंड (powerful) / सब (all) / नाथा (lords) / सभय (fearful) / दिसिप (direction-guardians) / नित (always) / नावहिं (bow) / माथा (head) / अब (now) / तव (your) / सिर (head) / भुज (arms) / जंबुक (jackals) / खाहीं (eat) / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (turned away) / यह (this) / अनुचित (improper) / नाहीं (is not)
ramacharitamanas::5153.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5153.essence: Greatness collapses fast when it turns away from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5153.simple_meaning: Even the mightiest ruler can be reduced to ruin. The verse says that turning away from Ram leaves no real protection, and the fall that follows is not surprising.
ramacharitamanas::5153.simple_insight: It can wake you up to how fragile power is when it is cut off from what is higher.
ramacharitamanas::5153.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final collapse, the fallen king is no longer being praised but judged. The verse looks at Ravana's broken body and broken pride, then turns that ruin into a moral verdict: power without devotion has already begun to die.
ramacharitamanas::5153.modern_relevance: A leader who once filled every room now sits alone after the company collapses. Titles, fear, and status cannot protect what pride has already hollowed out.
ramacharitamanas::5153.insight: It shifts the mind from admiring force to seeing the emptiness underneath force without surrender.

ramacharitamanas::5154.verse_sanskrit: काल बिबस पति कहा न माना। अग जग नाथु मनुज करि जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5154.verse_hindi: हे पति! काल के पूर्ण वश में होने से तुमने (किसी का) कहना नहीं माना और चराचर के नाथ परमात्मा को मनुष्य करके जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5154.english_translation: O husband, under the power of Time, you would not listen to anyone, and you saw the lord of all moving and unmoving beings as merely human.
ramacharitamanas::5154.translation_literal: काल (Time) / बिबस (helpless, under control) / पति (husband) / कहा न माना (did not accept what was said) / अग जग नाथु (lord of the moving and unmoving world) / मनुज करि जाना (knew as human)
ramacharitamanas::5154.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::5154.essence: Pride under Time turns even the highest into something ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::5154.simple_meaning: Mandodari says Ravana was trapped by Time and pride, so he refused wise counsel and failed to recognize Ram's true nature.
ramacharitamanas::5154.simple_insight: It hurts to see how self-will can make you blind to what could save you.
ramacharitamanas::5154.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana's ruin has begun, Mandodari faces the cost of his refusal to listen. She names the real failure: Time had already overpowered his judgment, and he could no longer see Ram as the lord of all beings.
ramacharitamanas::5154.modern_relevance: You ignore three people who warn you not to make the same mistake, because you are sure you know better. Later, the truth is obvious — but your certainty had already closed your eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5154.insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn self-certainty to clear seeing before damage is done.

ramacharitamanas::5155.verse_sanskrit: जान्यो मनुज करि दनुज कानन दहन पावक हरि स्वयं। जेहि नमत सिव ब्रह्मादि सुर पिय भजेहु नहिं करुनामयं॥ आजन्म ते परद्रोह रत पापौघमय तव तनु अयं। तुम्हहू दियो निज धाम राम नमामि ब्रह्म निरामयं॥
ramacharitamanas::5155.verse_hindi: दैत्य रूपी वन को जलाने के लिए अग्निस्वरूप साक्षात् श्री हरि को तुमने मनुष्य करके जाना। शिव और ब्रह्मा आदि देवता जिनको नमस्कार करते हैं, उन करुणामय भगवान् को हे प्रियतम! तुमने नहीं भजा। तुम्हारा यह शरीर जन्म से ही दूसरों से द्रोह करने में तत्पर तथा पाप समूहमय रहा! इतने पर भी जिन निर्विकार ब्रह्म श्री रामजी ने तुमको अपना धाम दिया, उनको मैं नमस्कार करती हूँ।
ramacharitamanas::5155.english_translation: You mistook the supreme being for a man, and the one all Shiva, Brahma, and the radiant beings bow to you did not worship. Your life was steeped in betrayal and sin from birth, yet Ram still gave you his own abode. I bow to that flawless Brahman, Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5155.translation_literal: जान्यो (knew) / मनुज करि (as a human) / दनुज कानन (forest of demons) / दहन (burning) / पावक (fire) / हरि (Hari) / स्वयं (himself) । / जेहि (whom) / नमत (bow) / सिव (Shiva) / ब्रह्मादि (Brahma and others) / सुर (radiant beings) / पिय (beloved) / भजेहु (you worshipped) / नहिं (not) / करुनामयं (full of compassion) ॥ / आजन्म (from birth) / ते (indeed) / परद्रोह (harm to others) / रत (inclined) / पापौघमय (filled with heaps of sin) / तव (your) / तनु (body) / अयं (this) । / तुम्हहू (even you) / दियो (gave) / निज (own) / धाम (abode) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / निरामयं (flawless, free from affliction) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5155.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5155.essence: Ram's mercy can still hold the one who rejected him.
ramacharitamanas::5155.simple_meaning: Ravana wrongly saw Ram as only human, ignored the compassionate Lord, lived in harmful pride, yet still received Ram's own abode. The speaker bows to Ram as the flawless supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::5155.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that even the worst life can still meet mercy.
ramacharitamanas::5155.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being judged after his fall in Lanka. Tulsidas contrasts Ravana's blindness and lifelong hostility with Ram's boundless compassion: even the enemy who rejected him is given refuge. The verse becomes a final praise of Ram's mercy.
ramacharitamanas::5155.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the one mistake that should have shut every door. This verse says mercy can still arrive after rejection, pride, and a lifetime of wrong turns.
ramacharitamanas::5155.insight: It shifts the mind from deserved punishment to the astonishing reach of grace.

ramacharitamanas::5156.verse_sanskrit: अहह नाथ रघुनाथ सम कृपासिंधु नहिं आन। जोगि बृंद दुर्लभ गति तोहि दीन्हि भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5156.verse_hindi: अहह! नाथ! श्री रघुनाथजी के समान कृपा का समुद्र दूसरा कोई नहीं है, जिन भगवान् ने तुमको वह गति दी, जो योगि समाज को भी दुर्लभ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5156.english_translation: Ah, Lord! There is no other ocean of grace like Raghunath. The Lord has given you a state that is hard even for yogis to attain.
ramacharitamanas::5156.translation_literal: अहह (ah) / नाथ (Lord) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / सम (like) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / नहिं (not) / आन (other) / जोगि बृंद (groups of yogis) / दुर्लभ (hard to attain) / गति (state / attainment) / तोहि (to you) / दीन्हि (gave) / भगवान (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::5156.speaker: Mandodari
ramacharitamanas::5156.essence: Grace can give what even disciplined striving cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::5156.simple_meaning: Raghunath alone gives a mercy and spiritual state that even great yogis find hard to reach.
ramacharitamanas::5156.simple_insight: You are not held back by effort alone; grace can carry you where striving stops.
ramacharitamanas::5156.detailed_meaning: Mandodari, shaken by Ravana's fall, sees clearly what pride hid from him. In the war's aftermath, she praises Ram as the only boundless source of grace, saying he has given Ravana a rare state beyond the reach of ordinary spiritual striving.
ramacharitamanas::5156.modern_relevance: You can meditate, read, and discipline yourself for years, yet still feel stuck at the edge of change. This verse reminds you that some openings arrive through grace, not force.
ramacharitamanas::5156.insight: It shifts the mind from self-powered attainment to humble receptivity to grace.

ramacharitamanas::5157.verse_sanskrit: मंदोदरी बचन सुनि काना। सुर मुनि सिद्ध सबन्हि सुख माना॥ अज महेस नारद सनकादी। जे मुनिबर परमारथबादी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5157.verse_hindi: मंदोदरी के वचन कानों में सुनकर देवता, मुनि और सिद्ध सभी ने सुख माना। ब्रह्मा, महादेव, नारद और सनकादि तथा और भी जो परमार्थवादी (परमात्मा के तत्त्व को जानने और कहने वाले) श्रेष्ठ मुनि थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5157.english_translation: Hearing Mandodari's words, all the gods, sages, and perfected beings felt joy. Brahma, Mahesh, Narad, and Sanak and other great sages who speak of the highest reality...
ramacharitamanas::5157.translation_literal: मंदोदरी (Mandodari) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (in the ears) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / सबन्हि (all) / सुख (joy) / माना (felt) / अज (Brahma) / महेस (Shiva) / नारद (Narad) / सनकादी (Sanak and others) / जे (those who) / मुनिबर (great sages) / परमारथबादी (who speak of the highest reality)
ramacharitamanas::5157.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5157.essence: Truth spoken at the right moment can calm even the highest minds.
ramacharitamanas::5157.simple_meaning: Mandodari's words moved everyone present, from gods to great sages, into joy and approval.
ramacharitamanas::5157.simple_insight: Even in a ruined court, truthful words can steady every heart in the room.
ramacharitamanas::5157.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's fall, Mandodari speaks, and the scene widens to include gods, sages, and perfected beings. Their joy is not from victory alone, but from seeing truth finally acknowledged in Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::5157.modern_relevance: A tense family meeting finally softens when someone says the honest thing no one wanted to hear. Relief spreads fast when truth enters the room.
ramacharitamanas::5157.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the healing power of clear, truthful speech.

ramacharitamanas::5158.verse_sanskrit: भरि लोचन रघुपतिहि निहारी। प्रेम मगन सब भए सुखारी॥ रुदन करत देखीं सब नारी। गयउ बिभीषनु मनु दुख भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5158.verse_hindi: वे सभी श्री रघुनाथजी को नेत्र भरकर निरखकर प्रेममग्न हो गए और अत्यंत सुखी हुए। अपने घर की सब स्त्रियों को रोती हुई देखकर विभीषणजी के मन में बड़ा भारी दुःख हुआ और वे उनके पास गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5158.english_translation: They all gazed at Raghupati with eyes full of tears and became lost in love, filled with bliss. Seeing all the women weeping, Vibhishana felt a great sorrow in his heart and went to them.
ramacharitamanas::5158.translation_literal: भरि (filled) / लोचन (eyes) / रघुपतिहि (Raghupati) / निहारी (having seen) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (absorbed) / सब (all) / भए (became) / सुखारी (blissful) ॥ / रुदन (weeping) / करत (doing) / देखीं (seeing) / सब (all) / नारी (women) / गयउ (went) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / मनु (mind) / दुख (sorrow) / भारी (heavy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5158.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5158.essence: Ram's presence awakens love, while another's sorrow still matters.
ramacharitamanas::5158.simple_meaning: Everyone looks at Ram with tears in their eyes and is filled with love. Vibhishana sees the women crying and feels deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::5158.simple_insight: Love and grief can both open the heart at once.
ramacharitamanas::5158.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana's fall, the city is still trembling with emotion. The people behold Ram with tear-filled eyes, overwhelmed by love and relief. Vibhishana, seeing the women weeping, is pierced by their pain and moves toward them.
ramacharitamanas::5158.modern_relevance: You reach the end of a long, painful conflict and finally see the person who ended it. Relief floods the room, but so does grief for everyone who was hurt along the way.
ramacharitamanas::5158.insight: It shows how victory in a broken situation can still carry compassion for those who are left mourning.

ramacharitamanas::5159.verse_sanskrit: बंधु दसा बिलोकि दुख कीन्हा। तब प्रभु अनुजहि आयसु दीन्हा॥ लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझायो। बहुरि बिभीषन प्रभु पहिं आयो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5159.verse_hindi: उन्होंने भाई की दशा देखकर दुःख किया। तब प्रभु श्री रामजी ने छोटे भाई को आज्ञा दी (कि जाकर विभीषण को धैर्य बँधाओ)। लक्ष्मणजी ने उन्हें बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। तब विभीषण प्रभु के पास लौट आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5159.english_translation: Seeing his brother's condition, he felt sorrow. Then Lord Ram gave an order to his younger brother. Lakshman explained many things to him in many ways. Then Vibhishana returned to the Lord's side.
ramacharitamanas::5159.translation_literal: बंधु (brother) / दसा (condition) / बिलोकि (seeing) / दुख (sorrow) / कीन्हा (felt) / तब (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / अनुजहि (to the younger brother) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / तेहि (to him) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / समुझायो (explained) / बहुरि (again) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / प्रभु (Lord) / पहिं (to the side of) / आयो (came)
ramacharitamanas::5159.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5159.essence: Compassion can guide someone back when grief has pulled them away.
ramacharitamanas::5159.simple_meaning: Ram sees Vibhishana's distress, sends Lakshman to comfort him, and Vibhishana returns to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5159.simple_insight: Even in crisis, care can bring someone back from grief to trust.
ramacharitamanas::5159.detailed_meaning: After Lanka falls, Vibhishana is overwhelmed by grief. Ram notices his state, sends Lakshman to speak with him, and the younger brother gently brings him back. This verse is a small bridge from sorrow to reunion.
ramacharitamanas::5159.modern_relevance: You watch a friend go quiet after bad news, then sit beside them instead of fixing them. That steady presence can do more than advice.
ramacharitamanas::5159.insight: It shifts you from reacting to another person's pain toward offering calm, patient support.

ramacharitamanas::5160.verse_sanskrit: कृपादृष्टि प्रभु ताहि बिलोका। करहु क्रिया परिहरि सब सोका॥ कीन्हि क्रिया प्रभु आयसु मानी। बिधिवत देस काल जियँ जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5160.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने उनको कृपापूर्ण दृष्टि से देखा (और कहा-) सब शोक त्यागकर रावण की अंत्येष्टि क्रिया करो। प्रभु की आज्ञा मानकर और हृदय में देश और काल का विचार करके विभीषणजी ने विधिपूर्वक सब क्रिया की ॥
ramacharitamanas::5160.english_translation: The Lord looked upon him with a merciful gaze and said, "Do the rites, and leave aside all sorrow." Obeying the Lord's command and keeping time and place in mind, Vibhishana performed the funeral rites properly.
ramacharitamanas::5160.translation_literal: कृपादृष्टि (merciful gaze) / प्रभु (the Lord) / ताहि (him) / बिलोका (looked upon) / करहु (do) / क्रिया (rites) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / सब (all) / सोका (sorrow) / कीन्हि (did) / क्रिया (rites) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आयसु (command) / मानी (having obeyed) / बिधिवत (according to rule) / देस (place) / काल (time) / जियँ (in heart) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::5160.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5160.essence: Mercy does not remove duty; it makes duty humane.
ramacharitamanas::5160.simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana to set aside grief and complete Ravana's funeral rites properly. Vibhishana obeys and performs the last rites with care and respect.
ramacharitamanas::5160.simple_insight: Even in victory, dignity matters. Grief does not cancel duty.
ramacharitamanas::5160.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's fall, Vibhishana stands before his dead brother in a battlefield soaked with loss. Ram's merciful glance softens the moment, and He tells Vibhishana to do the funeral rites without sorrow. Vibhishana obeys, honoring both duty and the hour.
ramacharitamanas::5160.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after a family fight, but the paperwork, the funeral call, or the final goodbye still needs doing. This verse shows how duty can remain gentle even when the heart is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::5160.insight: It teaches you to act with dignity in the middle of grief, instead of letting emotion erase responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::5161.verse_sanskrit: मंदोदरी आदि सब देह तिलांजलि ताहि। भवन गईं रघुपति गुन गन बरनत मन माहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5161.verse_hindi: मंदोदरी आदि सब स्त्रियाँ उसे (रावण को) तिलांजलि देकर मन में श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूहों का वर्णन करती हुई महल को गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5161.english_translation: Mandodari and the other women offered the final water ritual to him, then returned to the palace, their minds filled with praise of Raghupati's countless virtues.
