ramacharitamanas::5161.translation_literal: मंदोदरी आदि (Mandodari and others) / सब (all) / देह (offered) / तिलांजलि (the final water-offering) / ताहि (to him) / भवन (to the palace) / गईं (went) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / गुन गन (groups of virtues) / बरनत (describing) / मन माहि (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::5161.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5161.essence: Even grief bows before Ram's goodness.
ramacharitamanas::5161.simple_meaning: Ravana's women perform the last rites and leave, inwardly praising Ram's virtues instead of clinging to the fallen king.
ramacharitamanas::5161.simple_insight: Even in grief, the heart can turn toward what is higher and truer.
ramacharitamanas::5161.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's death, Mandodari and the other women complete the final rites. They return to the palace, but their minds are no longer fixed on the fallen king. The scene quietly shifts from loss to reverence for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5161.modern_relevance: At a funeral, someone who once defended a powerful person finally sees the cost of that person's pride. In the quiet walk home, their mind keeps returning to the one who ended the harm.
ramacharitamanas::5161.insight: It moves attention from mourning power to recognising virtue.

ramacharitamanas::5162.verse_sanskrit: आइ बिभीषन पुनि सिरु नायो। कृपासिंधु तब अनुज बोलायो॥ तुम्ह कपीस अंगद नल नीला। जामवंत मारुति नयसीला ॥ सब मिलि जाहु बिभीषन साथा। सारेहु तिलक कहेउ रघुनाथा॥ पिता बचन मैं नगर न आवउँ। आपु सरिस कपि अनुज पठावउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5162.verse_hindi: सब क्रिया-कर्म करने के बाद विभीषण ने आकर पुनः सिर नवाया। तब कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को बुलाया। श्री रघुनाथजी ने कहा कि तुम, वानरराज सुग्रीव, अंगद, नल, नील जाम्बवान् और मारुति सब नीतिनिपुण लोग मिलकर विभीषण के साथ जाओ और उन्हें राजतिलक कर दो। पिताजी के वचनों के कारण मैं नगर में नहीं आ सकता। पर अपने ही समान वानर और छोटे भाई को भेजता हूँ॥1-2॥
ramacharitamanas::5162.english_translation: After the funeral rites were complete, Vibhishana came and bowed again. Then the ocean of compassion, Ram, called his younger brother. Ram said, 'You, Sugriva, Angada, Nala, Neela, Jambavan, and the wise Hanuman should all go with Vibhishana and perform his coronation. Because of my father's word, I cannot enter the city. I send a monkey and a younger brother like myself.'
ramacharitamanas::5162.translation_literal: आइ (coming) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / पुनि (again) / सिरु (head) / नायो (bowed) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / तब (then) / अनुज (younger brother) / बोलायो (called) / तुम्ह (you) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / अंगद (Angada) / नल (Nala) / नीला (Neela) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / मारुति (Hanuman) / नयसीला (wise and well-conducted) / सब (all) / मिलि (together) / जाहु (go) / बिभीषन (with Vibhishana) / साथा (along) / सारेहु (arrange) / तिलक (coronation) / कहेउ (said) / रघुनाथा (Raghunatha) / पिता (father) / बचन (word) / मैं (I) / नगर (city) / न (not) / आवउँ (enter) / आपु (myself) / सरिस (like) / कपि (monkey) / अनुज (younger brother) / पठावउँ (send)
ramacharitamanas::5162.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5162.essence: Keeping a sacred promise matters more than claiming the victory.
ramacharitamanas::5162.simple_meaning: Ram honors his father's word and sends trusted companions to crown Vibhishana. He stays outside the city, but makes sure the right work is done.
ramacharitamanas::5162.simple_insight: Real integrity means keeping your promise without letting pride block useful action.
ramacharitamanas::5162.detailed_meaning: Ravana has fallen, and Vibhishana arrives in humility. Ram does not rush into the city for victory's sake. Instead, he calls Lakshman and the monkey chiefs, sends them to complete the coronation, and stays outside because his father's word still governs his conduct.
ramacharitamanas::5162.modern_relevance: You could walk into the room and take credit, but you don't. You text the team, hand over the spotlight, and still make sure the job gets finished right.
ramacharitamanas::5162.insight: It teaches you to protect your commitments while letting others carry out the practical work.

ramacharitamanas::5163.verse_sanskrit: तुरत चले कपि सुनि प्रभु बचना। कीन्ही जाइ तिलक की रचना॥ सादर सिंहासन बैठारी। तिलक सारि अस्तुति अनुसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5163.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर वानर तुरंत चले और उन्होंने जाकर राजतिलक की सारी व्यवस्था की। आदर के साथ विभीषण को सिंहासन पर बैठाकर राजतिलक किया और स्तुति की ॥
ramacharitamanas::5163.english_translation: At the Lord's word, the monkeys went at once and arranged the coronation. With respect, they seated Vibhishana on the throne and performed the coronation with praise.
ramacharitamanas::5163.translation_literal: तुरत (at once) / चले (went) / कपि (monkeys) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / बचना (words) / कीन्ही (made/did) / जाइ (going) / तिलक (coronation) / की (of) / रचना (arrangement) / सादर (respectfully) / सिंहासन (throne) / बैठारी (seated) / तिलक (coronation) / सारि (placing/performing) / अस्तुति (praise) / अनुसारी (according to)
ramacharitamanas::5163.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5163.essence: Victory becomes complete only when rightful order is restored.
ramacharitamanas::5163.simple_meaning: The monkey allies immediately prepare Vibhishana's coronation, seat him on the throne with respect, and complete the ceremony with praise.
ramacharitamanas::5163.simple_insight: Right action can be immediate, orderly, and respectful when it serves dharma.
ramacharitamanas::5163.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's fall, Ram gives the command and the monkey leaders move at once. They arrange Vibhishana's coronation, seat him on the throne with honour, and complete the ritual. The scene shows the victory turning into rightful rule.
ramacharitamanas::5163.modern_relevance: The meeting ends, and everyone quietly shifts from debate to action: chairs are moved, names are called, the room is reset, and the next leader is welcomed without drama.
ramacharitamanas::5163.insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the dignified work of restoring order.

ramacharitamanas::5164.verse_sanskrit: जोरि पानि सबहीं सिर नाए। सहित बिभीषन प्रभु पहिं आए॥ तब रघुबीर बोलि कपि लीन्हे। कहि प्रिय बचन सुखी सब कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5164.verse_hindi: सभी ने हाथ जोड़कर उनको सिर नवाए। तदनन्तर विभीषणजी सहित सब प्रभु के पास आए। तब श्री रघुवीर ने वानरों को बुला लिया और प्रिय वचन कहकर सबको सुखी किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5164.english_translation: Everyone bowed with folded hands. Then they all came before the Lord along with Vibhishana. Raghubir called the monkeys to him and made everyone happy with kind words.
ramacharitamanas::5164.translation_literal: जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / सबहीं (everyone) / सिर (heads) / नाए (bowed) / सहित (together with) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पहिं (near) / आए (came) / तब (then) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बोलि (calling) / कपि (monkeys) / लीन्हे (took/called) / कहि (saying) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / सुखी (happy) / सब (everyone) / कीन्हे (made)
ramacharitamanas::5164.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5164.essence: True victory makes room for tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::5164.simple_meaning: Everyone bows to Ram, and Ram responds by calling the monkeys close and speaking kindly so they feel at ease.
ramacharitamanas::5164.simple_insight: Respect deepens when power answers with warmth instead of distance.
ramacharitamanas::5164.detailed_meaning: After Vibhishana’s surrender and the victory in Lanka, the monkeys come before Ram with folded hands. Ram does not stand apart as a conqueror; he calls them near and softens the moment with loving words.
ramacharitamanas::5164.modern_relevance: You finish a hard project and walk into the room expecting praise. Instead, the best leader notices the team, pulls everyone close, and speaks in a way that lets the whole room breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::5164.insight: It shifts victory away from display and toward gratitude, making leadership feel humane.

ramacharitamanas::5165.verse_sanskrit: किए सुखी कहि बानी सुधा सम बल तुम्हारें रिपु हयो। पायो बिभीषन राज तिहुँ पुर जसु तुम्हारो नित नयो॥ मोहि सहित सुभ कीरति तुम्हारी परम प्रीति जो गाइहैं। संसार सिंधु अपार पार प्रयास बिनु नर पाइहैं॥
ramacharitamanas::5165.verse_hindi: भगवान् ने अमृत के समान यह वाणी कहकर सबको सुखी किया कि तुम्हारे ही बल से यह प्रबल शत्रु मारा गया और विभीषण ने राज्य पाया। इसके कारण तुम्हारा यश तीनों लोकों में नित्य नया बना रहेगा। जो लोग मेरे सहित तुम्हारी शुभ कीर्ति को परम प्रेम के साथ गाएँगे, वे बिना ही परिश्रम इस अपार संसार का पार पा जाएँगे।
ramacharitamanas::5165.english_translation: After speaking words sweet as nectar, the Lord made everyone happy: "By your strength, this mighty enemy has been slain, and Vibhishana has gained the throne. Your fame will remain ever fresh in the three worlds. Those who sing your noble glory with deep love, along with me, will cross the boundless ocean of worldly struggle without effort."
ramacharitamanas::5165.translation_literal: किए (having made) / सुखी (happy) / कहि (saying) / बानी (speech) / सुधा सम (like nectar) / बल (strength) / तुम्हारें (by your) / रिपु (enemy) / हयो (was slain) / पायो (obtained) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / राज (kingdom) / तिहुँ पुर (in the three worlds) / जसु (fame) / तुम्हारो (your) / नित (ever) / नयो (new) / मोहि (with me) / सहित (together) / सुभ (auspicious) / कीरति (glory) / तुम्हारी (your) / परम (supreme) / प्रीति (love) / जो (who) / गाइहैं (will sing) / संसार (worldly) / सिंधु (ocean) / अपार (boundless) / पार (across) / प्रयास (effort) / बिनु (without) / नर (people) / पाइहैं (will attain)
ramacharitamanas::5165.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5165.essence: Love for Ram turns the impossible crossing into an easy passage.
ramacharitamanas::5165.simple_meaning: Ram praises Hanuman and the others, saying their strength won the battle, Vibhishana received the throne, and anyone who sings their glory with love can cross life's vast troubles without struggle.
ramacharitamanas::5165.simple_insight: Real devotion turns struggle into passage, and praise becomes a way through what feels impossible.
ramacharitamanas::5165.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's defeat and Vibhishana's coronation, Ram speaks to the gathered vanaras and lifts their hearts. He credits their strength, blesses their fame, and says loving praise of his glory can carry a person across the ocean of worldly struggle.
ramacharitamanas::5165.modern_relevance: After the long night of helping a family through a crisis, someone finally says, 'You carried us.' That recognition changes everything. This verse captures how love, gratitude, and praise can become the bridge through exhaustion.
ramacharitamanas::5165.insight: It shifts the mind from self-made effort to devotion-powered crossing through hardship.

ramacharitamanas::5166.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु के बचन श्रवन सुनि नहिं अघाहिं कपि पुंज। बार बार सिर नावहिं गहहिं सकल पद कंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::5166.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन कानों से सुनकर वानर समूह तृप्त नहीं होते। वे सब बार-बार सिर नवाते हैं और चरणकमलों को पकड़ते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5166.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, the monkey hosts are never satisfied. Again and again they bow their heads and hold his lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::5166.translation_literal: प्रभु के (of the Lord's) / बचन (words) / श्रवन (through the ears) / सुनि (hearing) / नहिं (not) / अघाहिं (are sated) / कपि पुंज (hosts of monkeys) / बार बार (again and again) / सिर (heads) / नावहिं (bow) / गहहिं (grasp) / सकल (all) / पद कंज (lotus feet)
ramacharitamanas::5166.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5166.essence: Ram's words create endless gratitude, not satisfaction.
ramacharitamanas::5166.simple_meaning: The monkey army is so moved by Ram's words that they cannot get enough. They keep bowing again and again, holding his feet in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5166.simple_insight: Real devotion does not feel complete after one moment; it keeps returning with gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::5166.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's defeat, Ram speaks kindly to the monkey hosts and to Vibhishana. The warriors are overwhelmed by his grace. They cannot stop bowing, because this victory feels less like conquest and more like being held by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5166.modern_relevance: You leave a meeting where someone finally spoke with rare kindness, and you keep replaying their words all evening. Something in you wants to bow back to that kind of presence.
ramacharitamanas::5166.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to reverent response, showing that love naturally becomes repeated gratitude and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::5167.verse_sanskrit: पुनि प्रभु बोलि लियउ हनुमाना। लंका जाहु कहेउ भगवाना॥ समाचार जानकिहि सुनावहु। तासु कुसल लै तुम्ह चलि आवहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5167.verse_hindi: फिर प्रभु ने हनुमान् जी को बुला लिया। भगवान् ने कहा- तुम लंका जाओ। जानकी को सब समाचार सुनाओ और उसका कुशल समाचार लेकर तुम चले आओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5167.english_translation: Then the Lord called Hanuman again and said, "Go to Lanka. Give Janaki my news, and bring back word of her well-being."
ramacharitamanas::5167.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बोलि (calling) / लियउ (took) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / लंका (to Lanka) / जाहु (go) / कहेउ (said) / भगवाना (the Lord) / समाचार (news) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / सुनावहु (tell) / तासु (her) / कुसल (well-being) / लै (taking) / तुम्ह (you) / चलि (go) / आवहु (come back)
ramacharitamanas::5167.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5167.essence: True triumph still remembers the one who waited in pain.
ramacharitamanas::5167.simple_meaning: Ram sends Hanuman to Lanka with news for Sita and asks him to return with word of her well-being.
ramacharitamanas::5167.simple_insight: Love speaks through messengers when direct meeting is still out of reach.
ramacharitamanas::5167.detailed_meaning: After the war turns in Ram's favour, he calls Hanuman again. The task is now tender, not martial: carry news to Sita in Lanka, reassure her, and return with word of her safety.
ramacharitamanas::5167.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to text the person who has been waiting for good news. The message is simple, but it carries relief, hope, and the weight of being remembered.
ramacharitamanas::5167.insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the care that victory should bring to the one who suffered.

ramacharitamanas::5168.verse_sanskrit: तब हनुमंत नगर महुँ आए। सुनि निसिचरीं निसाचर धाए॥ बहु प्रकार तिन्ह पूजा कीन्ही। जनकसुता देखाइ पुनि दीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5168.verse_hindi: तब हनुमान् जी नगर में आए। यह सुनकर राक्षस-राक्षसी (उनके सत्कार के लिए) दौड़े। उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से हनुमान् जी की पूजा की और फिर श्री जानकीजी को दिखला दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5168.english_translation: Then Hanuman entered the city. Hearing this, the female and male demons rushed out. They honored him in many ways and then showed him Janaki.
ramacharitamanas::5168.translation_literal: तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / नगर (city) / महुँ (into) / आए (came) / सुनि (hearing) / निसिचरीं (female demons) / निसाचर (male demons) / धाए (ran) / बहु प्रकार (many kinds) / तिन्ह (they) / पूजा (honor) / कीन्ही (did) / जनकसुता (Janak's daughter, Sita) / देखाइ (showing) / पुनि (again) / दीन्ही (gave)
ramacharitamanas::5168.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5168.essence: A clear mission can turn even an enemy city into a path forward.
ramacharitamanas::5168.simple_meaning: Hanuman enters the city, and the demons rush to receive him. They honor him and then show him Sita.
ramacharitamanas::5168.simple_insight: Sometimes even in hostile places, a pure purpose opens doors you never expected.
ramacharitamanas::5168.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Lanka on Ram's mission. The city’s demons rush out, not knowing who he is, and treat him with respect before showing him Sita. The scene moves the search forward and prepares the first meeting.
ramacharitamanas::5168.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where nobody knows your name, yet your calm changes the atmosphere. Respect arrives before explanation when your purpose is clean.
ramacharitamanas::5168.insight: It keeps the focus on movement in the search: Hanuman enters, is received, and is brought to Sita.

ramacharitamanas::5169.verse_sanskrit: दूरिहि ते प्रनाम कपि कीन्हा। रघुपति दूत जानकीं चीन्हा॥ कहहु तात प्रभु कृपानिकेता। कुसल अनुज कपि सेन समेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5169.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने (सीताजी को) दूर से ही प्रणाम किया। जानकीजी ने पहचान लिया कि यह वही श्री रघुनाथजी का दूत है (और पूछा-) हे तात! कहो, कृपा के धाम मेरे प्रभु छोटे भाई और वानरों की सेना सहित कुशल से तो हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5169.english_translation: Hanuman bowed from afar. Sita recognized him as Ram's messenger and asked, “Tell me, dear one: is my compassionate Lord well, along with his younger brother and the monkey army?”
ramacharitamanas::5169.translation_literal: दूरिहि (from afar) / ते (from) / प्रनाम (salutation) / कपि (monkey) / कीन्हा (did) / रघुपति (of Ram) / दूत (messenger) / जानकीं (Sita) / चीन्हा (recognized) / कहहु (tell) / तात (dear one) / प्रभु (Lord) / कृपानिकेता (abode of compassion) / कुसल (well-being) / अनुज (younger brother) / कपि (monkey) / सेन (army) / समेता (together with)
ramacharitamanas::5169.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5169.essence: Devotion recognizes the messenger before the message is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::5169.simple_meaning: Sita immediately recognizes Hanuman as Ram's messenger and asks about Ram, Lakshman, and the monkey army.
ramacharitamanas::5169.simple_insight: Love notices the one who brings news of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::5169.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman approaches Sita after crossing enemy territory and finding her in deep separation. She sees him at once as Ram's messenger, not a stranger, and her first concern is Ram's safety, Lakshman's safety, and the army's condition.
ramacharitamanas::5169.modern_relevance: You spot a familiar name in a message from someone you miss, and your first question is not about yourself. You want to know whether the person you love is safe.
ramacharitamanas::5169.insight: It trains attention toward relationship before self-protection, and toward the beloved's welfare before your own relief.

ramacharitamanas::5170.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि कुसल कोसलाधीसा। मातु समर जीत्यो दससीसा॥ अबिचल राजु बिभीषन पायो। सुनि कपि बचन हरष उर छायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5170.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! कोसलपति श्री रामजी सब प्रकार से सकुशल हैं। उन्होंने संग्राम में दस सिर वाले रावण को जीत लिया है और विभीषण ने अचल राज्य प्राप्त किया है। हनुमान् जी के वचन सुनकर सीताजी के हृदय में हर्ष छा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5170.english_translation: The Lord of Kosala is safe in every way. He has defeated the ten-headed Ravana in battle, and Vibhishana has received firm kingship. Hearing Hanuman's words, joy filled Sita's heart.
ramacharitamanas::5170.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / कुसल (safe, well) / कोसलाधीसा (lord of Kosala) / मातु (mother) / समर (battle) / जीत्यो (won, conquered) / दससीसा (ten-headed one, Ravana) / अबिचल (unshakable) / राजु (kingdom, rule) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / पायो (received) / सुनि (hearing) / कपि (monkey, Hanuman) / बचन (words) / हरष (joy) / उर (heart) / छायो (spread)
ramacharitamanas::5170.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5170.essence: True news can restore a heart faster than time can.
ramacharitamanas::5170.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Sita that Ram is safe, Ravana has been defeated, and Vibhishana now rules. Sita hears this and feels deep joy.
ramacharitamanas::5170.simple_insight: A single true report can lift months of grief in one breath.
ramacharitamanas::5170.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has reached Sita in Lanka and is giving her the news she has longed to hear. He tells her that Ram is safe, Ravana is defeated, and Vibhishana has gained the kingdom. The verse ends with Sita's heart filling with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5170.modern_relevance: You wait for one message that could change everything, and then it finally arrives: they are safe, the struggle is over, and relief floods your chest.
ramacharitamanas::5170.insight: It shifts the mind from fear and uncertainty to confirmed relief and renewed hope.

ramacharitamanas::5171.verse_sanskrit: अति हरष मन तन पुलक लोचन सजल कह पुनि पुनि रमा। का देउँ तोहि त्रैलोक महुँ कपि किमपि नहिं बानी समा॥ सुनु मातु मैं पायो अखिल जग राजु आजु न संसयं। रन जीति रिपुदल बंधु जुत पस्यामि राममनामयं॥
ramacharitamanas::5171.verse_hindi: श्री जानकीजी के हृदय में अत्यंत हर्ष हुआ। उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में (आनंदाश्रुओं का) जल छा गया। वे बार-बार कहती हैं- हे हनुमान् ! मैं तुझे क्या दूँ? इस वाणी (समाचार) के समान तीनों लोकों में और कुछ भी नहीं है! (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे माता! सुनिए, मैंने आज निःसंदेह सारे जगत् का राज्य पा लिया, जो मैं रण में शत्रु को जीतकर भाई सहित निर्विकार श्री रामजी को देख रहा हूँ।
ramacharitamanas::5171.english_translation: Sita was filled with great joy. Her body thrilled and tears filled her eyes. She said again and again, “What can I give you, Hanuman? In all the three worlds, nothing equals this news.” Hanuman replied, “Mother, hear me: today I have truly won the kingdom of the whole world, for I have seen Ram, free from sorrow, after defeating the enemy host and with his brother beside him.”
ramacharitamanas::5171.translation_literal: अति (very) / हरष (joy) / मन (mind) / तन (body) / पुलक (horripilation) / लोचन (eyes) / सजल (moist) / कह (said) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / रमा (Sita) / का (what) / देउँ (give) / तोहि (to you) / त्रैलोक (three worlds) / महुँ (in) / कपि (monkey-devotee) / किमपि (anything) / नहिं (not) / बानी (speech/news) / समा (equal)॥ / सुनु (listen) / मातु (mother) / मैं (I) / पायो (have obtained) / अखिल (whole) / जग (world) / राजु (kingdom) / आजु (today) / न (not) / संसयं (doubt) / रन (battle) / जीति (having won) / रिपुदल (enemy host) / बंधु (brother) / जुत (with) / पस्यामि (I see) / राम (Ram) / मनामयं (free from sorrow, serene)
ramacharitamanas::5171.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5171.essence: Seeing Ram safe is greater than owning the world.
ramacharitamanas::5171.simple_meaning: Sita overflows with joy at Hanuman's news, and Hanuman says he has won everything because he has seen Ram safe and victorious.
ramacharitamanas::5171.simple_insight: Real joy comes when the one you love is safe and near.
ramacharitamanas::5171.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally reached Sita with the news she has been aching to hear. Her joy spills over into tears and gratitude, and Hanuman answers with a devotee's reversal: the whole world feels won because Ram lives, wins, and can be seen again.
ramacharitamanas::5171.modern_relevance: You get the message that someone you love made it home safely after a terrifying night. Suddenly, every other worry shrinks. That is the scale of this moment.
ramacharitamanas::5171.insight: It shifts value from personal gain to the well-being of the beloved.

ramacharitamanas::5172.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सुत सदगुन सकल तव हृदयँ बसहुँ हनुमंत। सानुकूल कोसलपति रहहुँ समेत अनंत ॥
ramacharitamanas::5172.verse_hindi: (जानकीजी ने कहा-) हे पुत्र! सुन, समस्त सद्गुण तेरे हृदय में बसें और हे हनुमान् ! शेष (लक्ष्मणजी) सहित कोसलपति प्रभु सदा तुझ पर प्रसन्न रहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::5172.english_translation: “Listen, son. May all virtues dwell in your heart, Hanuman, and may the Lord of Kosala, along with Lakshman, always remain pleased with you.”
ramacharitamanas::5172.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सुत (son) / सदगुन (all virtues) / सकल (all) / तव (your) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बसहुँ (may dwell) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / सानुकूल (favourable, pleased) / कोसलपति (Lord of Kosala) / रहहुँ (may remain) / समेत (together with) / अनंत (the endless one, Lakshman)
ramacharitamanas::5172.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5172.essence: Virtue in the heart invites Ram's favor.
ramacharitamanas::5172.simple_meaning: Sita blesses Hanuman that all good qualities may live in his heart, and that Ram and Lakshman may always remain kindly disposed toward him.
ramacharitamanas::5172.simple_insight: True devotion is blessed from both sides: you cultivate virtue, and grace meets you there.
ramacharitamanas::5172.detailed_meaning: After hearing that Ram has won and that Hanuman has brought the news, Sita pours out her gratitude. She blesses Hanuman like a mother blessing a beloved son: may goodness live in him, and may Ram and Lakshman always be pleased with him.
ramacharitamanas::5172.modern_relevance: You help someone through a crisis, then they quietly tell you, 'May goodness stay with you.' That kind of blessing lands deeper than praise because it names character, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::5172.insight: It links inner virtue with outer grace, showing that devotion ripens into blessing.

ramacharitamanas::5173.verse_sanskrit: अब सोइ जतन करहु तुम्ह ताता। देखौं नयन स्याम मृदु गाता॥ तब हनुमान राम पहिं जाई। जनकसुता कै कुसल सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5173.verse_hindi: हे तात! अब तुम वही उपाय करो, जिससे मैं इन नेत्रों से प्रभु के कोमल श्याम शरीर के दर्शन करूँ। तब श्री रामचंद्रजी के पास जाकर हनुमान् जी ने जानकीजी का कुशल समाचार सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5173.english_translation: O dear one, now do whatever will let me see the dark, gentle form of the Lord with these eyes. Then Hanuman went to Ram and gave news of Janaka's daughter’s well-being.
ramacharitamanas::5173.translation_literal: अब (now) सोइ (that very) जतन (effort / means) करहु (do) तुम्ह (you) ताता (dear one) / देखौं (I may see) नयन (with eyes) स्याम (dark-complexioned) मृदु (gentle) गाता (body) ॥ / तब (then) हनुमान (Hanuman) राम पहिं (to Ram) जाई (going) / जनकसुता (Janaka's daughter) कै (of) कुसल (well-being) सुनाई (told) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5173.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5173.essence: Devotion becomes simple when all you want is Ram’s presence.
ramacharitamanas::5173.simple_meaning: Sita asks for the means to see Ram again, and Hanuman immediately goes to Ram with her message.
ramacharitamanas::5173.simple_insight: Love narrows everything down to one need: to be reunited with the one you long for.
ramacharitamanas::5173.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has finally heard of Hanuman’s arrival and feels a surge of hope. She asks for the one remedy that matters to her: a way to see Ram again. Hanuman then returns to Ram and reports her welfare.
ramacharitamanas::5173.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after months apart, hoping for one message that says the distance is ending. Sita’s heart knows that feeling exactly.
ramacharitamanas::5173.insight: It shifts longing from vague sadness into a clear, devoted request for reunion.

ramacharitamanas::5174.verse_sanskrit: सुनि संदेसु भानुकुलभूषन। बोलि लिए जुबराज बिभीषन॥ मारुतसुत के संग सिधावहु। सादर जनकसुतहि लै आवहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5174.verse_hindi: सूर्य कुलभूषण श्री रामजी ने संदेश सुनकर युवराज अंगद और विभीषण को बुला लिया (और कहा-) पवनपुत्र हनुमान् के साथ जाओ और जानकी को आदर के साथ ले आओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5174.english_translation: Hearing the message, Ram, the jewel of the solar dynasty, called Angad and Vibhishan. He said, "Go with Hanuman and bring Janaki back with respect."
ramacharitamanas::5174.translation_literal: सुनि (having heard) / संदेसु (message) / भानुकुलभूषन (jewel of the solar dynasty) / बोलि लिए (called) / जुबराज (prince) / बिभीषन (Vibhishan) / मारुतसुत (son of the wind) / के संग (with) / सिधावहु (go) / सादर (with respect) / जनकसुतहि (Janaki) / लै आवहु (bring back)
ramacharitamanas::5174.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5174.essence: Love does not rush recovery; it returns the beloved with honor.
ramacharitamanas::5174.simple_meaning: After hearing Hanuman’s report, Ram immediately sends trusted allies to bring Sita back respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::5174.simple_insight: When someone you love is found, care still matters: bring them back with honor, not haste.
ramacharitamanas::5174.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has finally given Ram news of Sita. Ram responds at once by sending Angad and Vibhishan with Hanuman, not as conquerors but as respectful rescuers. The moment turns search into reunion.
ramacharitamanas::5174.modern_relevance: You finally hear that the missing person is safe, and the first thing you think is not speed but dignity. Relief is not enough; how you bring them home matters too.
ramacharitamanas::5174.insight: It shifts rescue from mere success to honorable care.

ramacharitamanas::5175.verse_sanskrit: तुरतहिं सकल गए जहँ सीता। सेवहिं सब निसिचरीं बिनीता॥ बेगि बिभीषन तिन्हहि सिखायो। तिन्ह बहु बिधि मज्जन करवायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5175.verse_hindi: वे सब तुरंत ही वहाँ गए, जहाँ सीताजी थीं। सब की सब राक्षसियाँ नम्रतापूर्वक उनकी सेवा कर रही थीं। विभीषणजी ने शीघ्र ही उन लोगों को समझा दिया। उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से सीताजी को स्नान कराया, ॥
ramacharitamanas::5175.english_translation: They all quickly went to where Sita was. All the female demons served her with humility. Vibhishana promptly instructed them, and they bathed Sita in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::5175.translation_literal: तुरतहिं (immediately) / सकल (all) / गए (went) / जहँ (where) / सीता (Sita) / सेवहिं (serve) / सब (all) / निसिचरीं (female demons) / बिनीता (humble) / बेगि (quickly) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / तिन्हहि (them) / सिखायो (instructed) / तिन्ह (they) / बहु बिधि (many kinds) / मज्जन (bathing) / करवायो (got done)
ramacharitamanas::5175.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5175.essence: True respect shows itself in immediate, humble care.
ramacharitamanas::5175.simple_meaning: Everyone rushes to Sita, and the women there serve her respectfully. Vibhishana quickly arranges for her bath.
ramacharitamanas::5175.simple_insight: Care can be practical, immediate, and deeply respectful.
ramacharitamanas::5175.detailed_meaning: After Ram’s message reaches Lanka, Angad and Vibhishana move at once to Sita. The women serving her are no longer hostile; under Vibhishana’s guidance, they show humility and arrange her bath, preparing the reunion scene.
ramacharitamanas::5175.modern_relevance: A hospital room after bad news can change in an instant: someone finally brings water, a clean towel, a calmer voice. Respect is sometimes shown through small, urgent acts of care.
ramacharitamanas::5175.insight: It shifts attention from grand emotion to the dignity of careful service.

ramacharitamanas::5176.verse_sanskrit: बहु प्रकार भूषन पहिराए। सिबिका रुचिर साजि पुनि ल्याए॥ ता पर हरषि चढ़ी बैदेही। सुमिरि राम सुखधाम सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5176.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार के गहने पहनाए और फिर वे एक सुंदर पालकी सजाकर ले आए। सीताजी प्रसन्न होकर सुख के धाम प्रियतम श्री रामजी का स्मरण करके उस पर हर्ष के साथ चढ़ीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5176.english_translation: They dressed Sita in many kinds of ornaments, then brought a beautiful palanquin. Delighted, she remembered Ram, the abode of joy and her beloved, and climbed into it with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5176.translation_literal: बहु प्रकार (many kinds) / भूषन (ornaments) / पहिराए (were made to wear) / सिबिका (palanquin) / रुचिर (beautiful) / साजि (having prepared) / पुनि (again) / ल्याए (brought) / ता पर (on that) / हरषि (joyfully) / चढ़ी (climbed) / बैदेही (Sita) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम (Ram) / सुखधाम (abode of joy) / सनेही (beloved)
ramacharitamanas::5176.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5176.essence: Remembrance of Ram turns departure into joy.
ramacharitamanas::5176.simple_meaning: Sita is honored, placed in a beautiful palanquin, and leaves joyfully while remembering Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5176.simple_insight: Love can make even a difficult crossing feel light.
ramacharitamanas::5176.detailed_meaning: After Lanka falls, the victors prepare Sita for her return. She is adorned, seated in a splendid palanquin, and lifts her heart toward Ram before setting out. The verse is part of the movement home, not the main teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::5176.modern_relevance: You finally leave the place that held you too long, and someone has already arranged the ride home. You step in quietly, carrying one name in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::5176.insight: It shifts attention from the outward journey to the inward remembrance that makes the journey bearable.

ramacharitamanas::5177.verse_sanskrit: बेतपानि रच्छक चहु पासा। चले सकल मन परम हुलासा॥ देखन भालु कीस सब आए। रच्छक कोपि निवारन धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5177.verse_hindi: चारों ओर हाथों में छड़ी लिए रक्षक चले। सबके मनों में परम उल्लास (उमंग) है। रीछ-वानर सब दर्शन करने के लिए आए, तब रक्षक क्रोध करके उनको रोकने दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5177.english_translation: Four guards with staves walked on all sides, their hearts full of joy. All the bears and monkeys came to look, and the guards angrily rushed to stop them.
ramacharitamanas::5177.translation_literal: बेतपानि (staff in hand) / रच्छक (guards) / चहु पासा (on all four sides) / चले (walked) / सकल (all) / मन (mind) / परम हुलासा (great joy) / देखन (to see) / भालु (bears) / कीस (monkeys) / सब (all) / आए (came) / रच्छक (guards) / कोपि (angrily) / निवारन (to stop) / धाए (ran)
ramacharitamanas::5177.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5177.essence: Joyful arrival still needs watchful protection.
ramacharitamanas::5177.simple_meaning: Guards surrounded the procession with sticks in hand, while bears and monkeys gathered to look. The guards ran forward to stop them.
ramacharitamanas::5177.simple_insight: Even in celebration, the scene still carries tension between protection and curiosity.
ramacharitamanas::5177.detailed_meaning: Sita is being brought out after captivity, and the whole camp is in motion. Guards walk around her with staffs, delighted yet alert, while bears and monkeys rush in to glimpse her. Their protectors move to keep order as the reunion approaches.
ramacharitamanas::5177.modern_relevance: You step into a crowded venue with security at every entrance, while curious people crane their necks to catch a glimpse. Joy and control are moving side by side.
ramacharitamanas::5177.insight: It shows a transition moment where protection, ceremony, and public curiosity all meet.

ramacharitamanas::5178.verse_sanskrit: कह रघुबीर कहा मम मानहु। सीतहि सखा पयादें आनहु॥ देखहुँ कपि जननी की नाईं। बिहसि कहा रघुनाथ गोसाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5178.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीर ने कहा- हे मित्र! मेरा कहना मानो और सीता को पैदल ले आओ, जिससे वानर उसको माता की तरह देखें। गोसाईं श्री रामजी ने हँसकर ऐसा कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5178.english_translation: Raghubir said, “Do as I say: bring Sita on foot, so the monkeys may see her like a mother.” Laughing, Lord Raghunath said this.
ramacharitamanas::5178.translation_literal: कह (said) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / कहा (what) / मम (my) / मानहु (accept) / सीतहि (Sita) / सखा (friend) / पयादें (on foot) / आनहु (bring) / देखहुँ (let [them] see) / कपि (monkeys) / जननी (mother) / की नाईं (like) / बिहसि (laughing) / कहा (said) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / गोसाईं (lord)
ramacharitamanas::5178.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5178.essence: Respect turns a reunion into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::5178.simple_meaning: Ram asks that Sita be brought on foot so the monkeys can see her as a mother. He says it with a smile.
ramacharitamanas::5178.simple_insight: Even in victory, Ram chooses warmth and respect over display.
ramacharitamanas::5178.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the war, Ram is arranging Sita’s return before the gathered monkeys and bears. Instead of a grand entrance, he asks that she come on foot so they may see her with reverence, like a mother. The moment shows his tenderness and maryada.
ramacharitamanas::5178.modern_relevance: You could arrive with all the fanfare, but you choose the kinder entrance. The room feels safer when dignity matters more than spectacle.
ramacharitamanas::5178.insight: It shifts success from performance to care, showing that how you present someone can be an act of honour.

ramacharitamanas::5179.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन भालु कपि हरषे। नभ ते सुरन्ह सुमन बहु बरषे॥ सीता प्रथम अनल महुँ राखी। प्रगट कीन्हि चह अंतर साखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5179.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर रीछ-वानर हर्षित हो गए। आकाश से देवताओं ने बहुत से फूल बरसाए। सीताजी (के असली स्वरूप) को पहिले अग्नि में रखा था। अब भीतर के साक्षी भगवान् उनको प्रकट करना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5179.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, the bears and monkeys rejoiced, and the beings of heaven showered many flowers. Sita had first been placed in fire; now the inner witness wished to reveal her.
ramacharitamanas::5179.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बचन (words) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / हरषे (rejoiced) / नभ ते (from the sky) / सुरन्ह (by the radiant beings) / सुमन (flowers) / बहु (many) / बरषे (were showered) / सीता (Sita) / प्रथम (first) / अनल (fire) / महुँ (in) / राखी (placed) / प्रगट (manifest) / कीन्हि (made) / चह (wished) / अंतर (inner) / साखी (witness)
ramacharitamanas::5179.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5179.essence: What is pure does not need to stay hidden.
ramacharitamanas::5179.simple_meaning: Ram's words fill everyone with joy, flowers fall from the sky, and Sita's hidden purity is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::5179.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that what is true does not stay hidden forever.
ramacharitamanas::5179.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram tells the bears and monkeys to bring Sita forward, everyone rejoices. Even the heavens respond with flowers. The verse then recalls that Sita's purity had already been tested by fire, and now Ram brings that truth openly into view.
ramacharitamanas::5179.modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a room that has been tense for days. The air changes at once — relief arrives, and what was quietly known can now be seen.
ramacharitamanas::5179.insight: It shifts attention from private proof to public recognition of what is already true.

ramacharitamanas::5180.verse_sanskrit: तेहि कारन करुनानिधि कहे कछुक दुर्बाद। सुनत जातुधानीं सब लागीं करै बिषाद ॥
ramacharitamanas::5180.verse_hindi: इसी कारण करुणा के भंडार श्री रामजी ने लीला से कुछ कड़े वचन कहे, जिन्हे सुनकर सब राक्षसियाँ विषाद करने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5180.english_translation: For that reason, the ocean of compassion spoke a few harsh words in play. Hearing them, all the demon women fell into grief.
ramacharitamanas::5180.translation_literal: तेहि कारन (for that reason) / करुनानिधि (ocean of compassion) / कहे (spoke) / कछुक (a little) / दुर्बाद (harsh words) / सुनत (hearing) / जातुधानीं (demon women) / सब (all) / लागीं (began) / करै (to do) / बिषाद (grief)
ramacharitamanas::5180.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5180.essence: Compassion can speak sharply when mercy needs force.
ramacharitamanas::5180.simple_meaning: Ram speaks sternly only to move the scene forward. His words are meant as a dramatic turn, and the women around him fall into sorrow when they hear them.
ramacharitamanas::5180.simple_insight: Even kindness can wear a stern face when a deeper purpose needs to be served.
ramacharitamanas::5180.detailed_meaning: After Sita has been revealed and the moment of rescue is unfolding in Lanka, Ram speaks a few deliberately hard words. The demon women hear them and sink into grief. This verse is a bridge in the scene, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5180.modern_relevance: A parent uses a firm tone to stop a child from running into traffic. The voice sounds harsh, but the care underneath is what matters.
ramacharitamanas::5180.insight: It shows that sharp speech can be a compassionate tool when the situation calls for it.

ramacharitamanas::5181.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु के बचन सीस धरि सीता। बोली मन क्रम बचन पुनीता॥ लछिमन होहु धरम के नेगी। पावक प्रगट करहु तुम्ह बेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5181.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचनों को सिर चढ़ाकर मन, वचन और कर्म से पवित्र श्री सीताजी बोलीं- हे लक्ष्मण! तुम मेरे धर्म के नेगी (धर्माचरण में सहायक) बनो और तुरंत आग तैयार करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5181.english_translation: Holding the Lord's words to her head, Sita spoke, pure in mind, action, and speech: "Lakshman, help me with my dharma and quickly prepare the fire."
ramacharitamanas::5181.translation_literal: प्रभु के बचन (the Lord's words) / सीस धरि (placing on the head) / सीता (Sita) / बोली (spoke) / मन क्रम बचन (mind, action, speech) / पुनीता (pure) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / होहु (be) / धरम के नेगी (helper in dharma) / पावक (fire) / प्रगट करहु (make ready) / तुम्ह (you) / बेगी (quickly)
ramacharitamanas::5181.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5181.essence: True purity can ask for the hardest proof without losing composure.
ramacharitamanas::5181.simple_meaning: Sita accepts Ram's words completely and asks Lakshman to help her prepare the fire right away.
ramacharitamanas::5181.simple_insight: Even in pain, she stays clear, dignified, and devoted to what dharma asks next.
ramacharitamanas::5181.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ram's words, Sita responds with complete inner purity. She turns to Lakshman and asks him to assist her dharma by arranging the fire. This is the moment before the trial of purity is made visible.
ramacharitamanas::5181.modern_relevance: You are in a room where everyone is waiting for your answer, and your voice still comes out steady. Even under pressure, you can choose dignity over panic.
ramacharitamanas::5181.insight: It shows how devotion can stay calm, precise, and obedient even in an unbearable moment.

ramacharitamanas::5182.verse_sanskrit: सुनि लछिमन सीता कै बानी। बिरह बिबेक धरम निति सानी॥ लोचन सजल जोरि कर दोऊ। प्रभु सन कछु कहि सकत न ओऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5182.verse_hindi: श्री सीताजी की विरह, विवेक, धर्म और नीति से सनी हुई वाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी के नेत्रों में (विषाद के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। वे हाथ जोड़े खड़े रहे। वे भी प्रभु से कुछ कह नहीं सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::5182.english_translation: Hearing Sita's words, full of separation, discernment, duty, and right conduct, Lakshman’s eyes filled with tears. He stood with both hands folded and could not say anything to the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::5182.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / सीता कै (of Sita's) / बानी (words) / बिरह (separation) / बिबेक (discernment) / धरम (duty) / निति (right conduct) / सानी (mixed with)॥ / लोचन (eyes) / सजल (moist) / जोरि (joining) / कर (hands) / दोऊ (both) / प्रभु सन (before the Lord) / कछु (something) / कहि (saying) / सकत (able) / न (not) / ओऊ (he)
ramacharitamanas::5182.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5182.essence: True devotion can leave you wordless before duty.
ramacharitamanas::5182.simple_meaning: Lakshman is overwhelmed by Sita’s sorrowful, wise words. Tears fill his eyes, and he stands silently before Ram, unable to speak.
ramacharitamanas::5182.simple_insight: Some moments are too tender for words; devotion can leave even the strongest person silent.
ramacharitamanas::5182.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just spoken with painful clarity about separation, duty, and right conduct. Lakshman hears her and is moved to tears. The scene pauses in shared grief before he goes to serve Ram again.
ramacharitamanas::5182.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such honesty that your throat tightens. You want to answer, but all you can do is stand there, humbled and quiet.
ramacharitamanas::5182.insight: It shows how deep feeling can silence speech and turn attention back to service.

ramacharitamanas::5183.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम रुख लछिमन धाए। पावक प्रगटि काठ बहु लाए॥ पावक प्रबल देखि बैदेही। हृदयँ हरष नहिं भय कछु तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5183.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामजी का रुख देखकर लक्ष्मणजी दौड़े और आग तैयार करके बहुत सी लकड़ी ले आए। अग्नि को खूब बढ़ी हुई देखकर जानकीजी के हृदय में हर्ष हुआ। उन्हें भय कुछ भी नहीं हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5183.english_translation: Seeing Ram's look, Lakshman hurried off and brought plenty of wood to kindle the fire. Seeing the fire blaze strongly, Sita's heart filled with joy, and she felt no fear at all.
ramacharitamanas::5183.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / रुख (look) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / धाए (ran) / पावक (fire) / प्रगटि (having arisen) / काठ (wood) / बहु (much) / लाए (brought) / पावक (fire) / प्रबल (strong) / देखि (seeing) / बैदेही (Sita) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / नहिं (not) / भय (fear) / कछु (any) / तेही (in that)
ramacharitamanas::5183.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5183.essence: Fear falls away when trust is fully present.
ramacharitamanas::5183.simple_meaning: Lakshman quickly brings wood for the fire, and Sita feels joy and no fear when she sees it burning strongly.
ramacharitamanas::5183.simple_insight: Love can steady the heart even in a moment that looks frightening.
ramacharitamanas::5183.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just asked Lakshman to prepare the fire for her vow. Lakshman obeys at once, and when the flames rise, Sita feels only joy. The scene is a quiet test of her inner steadiness before the next vow is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::5183.modern_relevance: You watch the ambulance lights flash outside the hospital entrance, and your hands stop shaking. In a moment of crisis, someone’s calm action can give your heart back its courage.
ramacharitamanas::5183.insight: It shows how decisive support and inner trust can remove fear from a terrifying moment.

ramacharitamanas::5184.verse_sanskrit: जौं मन बच क्रम मम उर माहीं। तजि रघुबीर आन गति नाहीं॥ तौ कृसानु सब कै गति जाना। मो कहुँ होउ श्रीखंड समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5184.verse_hindi: (सीताजी ने लीला से कहा-) यदि मन, वचन और कर्म से मेरे हृदय में श्री रघुवीर को छोड़कर दूसरी गति (अन्य किसी का आश्रय) नहीं है, तो अग्निदेव जो सबके मन की गति जानते हैं, (मेरे भी मन की गति जानकर) मेरे लिए चंदन के समान शीतल हो जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5184.english_translation: If, in mind, speech, and action, I have no refuge other than Raghubir in my heart, then may fire, which knows the movements of all minds, become cool to me like sandalwood.
ramacharitamanas::5184.translation_literal: जौं (if) / मन (mind) / बच (speech) / क्रम (action) / मम (my) / उर (heart) / माहीं (within) / तजि (leaving) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / आन (other) / गति (refuge, destination) / नाहीं (not) / तौ (then) / कृसानु (fire) / सब कै (of all) / गति (movement, state) / जाना (knowing) / मो कहुँ (for me) / होउ (become) / श्रीखंड (sandalwood) / समाना (like)
ramacharitamanas::5184.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::5184.essence: Complete devotion can make even fire feel cool.
ramacharitamanas::5184.simple_meaning: Sita says that if her heart belongs only to Ram in thought, speech, and action, then even fire should become cool and harmless to her.
ramacharitamanas::5184.simple_insight: Total trust can hold you steady even in the hottest trial.
ramacharitamanas::5184.detailed_meaning: Sita stands in Lanka, facing fire as her ordeal closes in. She does not ask for escape through force; she points to her complete devotion to Ram and asks that this truth be recognised by the fire itself.
ramacharitamanas::5184.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a waiting room before hard news, and your chest feels tight. This verse reminds you that when your trust is whole, even fear loses some of its heat.
ramacharitamanas::5184.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to complete reliance on Ram.

ramacharitamanas::5185.verse_sanskrit: श्रीखंड सम पावक प्रबेस कियो सुमिरि प्रभु मैथिली। जय कोसलेस महेस बंदित चरन रति अति निर्मली॥ प्रतिबिंब अरु लौकिक कलंक प्रचंड पावक महुँ जरे। प्रभु चरित काहुँ न लखे नभ सुर सिद्ध मुनि देखहिं खरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5185.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामजी का स्मरण करके और जिनके चरण महादेवजी के द्वारा वंदित हैं तथा जिनमें सीताजी की अत्यंत विशुद्ध प्रीति है, उन कोसलपति की जय बोलकर जानकीजी ने चंदन के समान शीतल हुई अग्नि में प्रवेश किया। प्रतिबिम्ब (सीताजी की छायामूर्ति) और उनका लौकिक कलंक प्रचण्ड अग्नि में जल गए। प्रभु के इन चरित्रों को किसी ने नहीं जाना। देवता, सिद्ध और मुनि सब आकाश में खड़े देखते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5185.english_translation: Remembering Lord Ram, Sita entered the fire that had become cool like sandalwood. She praised the Lord of Kosala, whose feet are worshipped by Shiva and whose pure love is utterly spotless. Her reflection and worldly stain were burned away in the blazing fire. No one understood the Lord's play; gods, perfected beings, and sages stood watching from the sky.
ramacharitamanas::5185.translation_literal: श्रीखंड सम (like sandalwood) / पावक (fire) / प्रबेस कियो (entered) / सुमिरि (remembering) / प्रभु (Lord) / मैथिली (Sita of Mithila) / जय (victory) / कोसलेस (Lord of Kosala) / महेस (Shiva) / बंदित (worshipped) / चरन (feet) / रति (love) / अति (very) / निर्मली (spotless) / प्रतिबिंब (reflection) / अरु (and) / लौकिक (worldly) / कलंक (stain) / प्रचंड (blazing) / पावक (fire) / महुँ (in) / जरे (burned) / प्रभु (Lord's) / चरित (play) / काहुँ (by anyone) / न (not) / लखे (understood) / नभ (sky) / सुर (gods) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनि (sages) / देखहिं (see) / खरे (standing)
ramacharitamanas::5185.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5185.essence: True purity survives fire, while public stain is what burns away.
ramacharitamanas::5185.simple_meaning: Sita enters the fire while remembering Ram. Her shadow and any public stain are burned away, and the divine play remains beyond ordinary understanding.
ramacharitamanas::5185.simple_insight: Some acts of purity cannot be judged from outside; they are answered by a deeper truth than public opinion.
ramacharitamanas::5185.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the war, Sita steps into the fire to prove what only Ram already knows. Shiva is named as one who worships Ram's feet, and the heavens watch as fire burns away the shadow-image and worldly stain, revealing the mystery of Ram's play.
ramacharitamanas::5185.modern_relevance: You know the feeling of being misunderstood in front of everyone, while your real truth is invisible. Sometimes the only answer is to stand in what is true and let time burn away the false story.
ramacharitamanas::5185.insight: It shifts attention from outer judgment to the deeper reality that reveals itself through integrity.

ramacharitamanas::5186.verse_sanskrit: धरि रूप पावक पानि गहि श्री सत्य श्रुति जग बिदित जो। जिमि छीरसागर इंदिरा रामहि समर्पी आनि सो॥ सो राम बाम बिभाग राजति रुचिर अति सोभा भली। नव नील नीरज निकट मानहुँ कनक पंकज की कली ॥
ramacharitamanas::5186.verse_hindi: तब अग्नि ने शरीर धारण करके वेदों में और जगत् में प्रसिद्ध वास्तविक श्री (सीताजी) का हाथ पकड़ उन्हें श्री रामजी को वैसे ही समर्पित किया जैसे क्षीरसागर ने विष्णु भगवान् को लक्ष्मी समर्पित की थीं। वे सीताजी श्री रामचंद्रजी के वाम भाग में विराजित हुईं। उनकी उत्तम शोभा अत्यंत ही सुंदर है। मानो नए खिले हुए नीले कमल के पास सोने के कमल की कली सुशोभित हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5186.english_translation: Then Fire took a form, held the hand of the true Sita celebrated in the Vedas and the world, and offered her to Ram just as the ocean offered Lakshmi to Vishnu. Sita then shone on Ram's left side with exquisite beauty, like a golden lotus bud beside a fresh blue lotus.
ramacharitamanas::5186.translation_literal: धरि (taking) / रूप (form) / पावक (fire) / पानि (hand) / गहि (seizing, holding) / श्री (radiance, prosperity) / सत्य (true) / श्रुति (Vedas, revealed lore) / जग (world) / बिदित (known) / जो (who) / जिमि (just as) / छीरसागर (ocean of milk) / इंदिरा (Lakshmi) / रामहि (to Ram) / समर्पी (offered) / आनि (bringing) / सो (that) / सो (that) / राम (Ram) / बाम (left) / बिभाग (side) / राजति (shines) / रुचिर (beautiful) / अति (very) / सोभा (splendor) / भली (excellent) / नव (new) / नील (blue) / नीरज (lotus) / निकट (near) / मानहुँ (as if) / कनक (golden) / पंकज (lotus) / की (of) / कली (bud)
ramacharitamanas::5186.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5186.essence: Purity is not only proved; it is welcomed back beside love.
ramacharitamanas::5186.simple_meaning: Fire takes a form and formally returns Sita to Ram. The scene ends with Sita seated beside Ram, glowing like a golden lotus beside a blue one.
ramacharitamanas::5186.simple_insight: What was tested in fire is now restored with honor.
ramacharitamanas::5186.detailed_meaning: The trial is over in Lanka. Fire itself appears, takes Sita by the hand, and presents her back to Ram as the Vedas and the world know her. The verse lingers on their reunion, showing her radiant place at Ram's left side.
ramacharitamanas::5186.modern_relevance: After a long public ordeal, you finally hear the words that clear your name. The relief is not just being believed — it is being restored to your place with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::5186.insight: It turns vindication into reunion, not just proof.

ramacharitamanas::5187.verse_sanskrit: बरषहिं सुमन हरषि सुर बाजहिं गगन निसान। गावहिं किंनर सुरबधू नाचहिं चढ़ीं बिमान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5187.verse_hindi: देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसाने लगे। आकाश में डंके बजने लगे। किन्नर गाने लगे। विमानों पर चढ़ी अप्सराएँ नाचने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5187.english_translation: The radiant beings showered flowers in joy. Drums sounded in the sky. Kinnaras sang, and celestial women danced from their flying chariots.
ramacharitamanas::5187.translation_literal: बरषहिं (are showering) / सुमन (flowers) / हरषि (in joy) / सुर (radiant beings) / बाजहिं (are sounding) / गगन (sky) / निसान (drums) / गावहिं (are singing) / किंनर (kinnaras) / सुरबधू (celestial women) / नाचहिं (are dancing) / चढ़ीं (mounted) / बिमान (flying chariots)
ramacharitamanas::5187.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5187.essence: Joy at Ram’s reunion overflows into the whole universe.
ramacharitamanas::5187.simple_meaning: The heavens celebrate with flowers, music, and dancing as the scene turns joyful.
ramacharitamanas::5187.simple_insight: Some moments feel so complete that even the sky seems to rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::5187.detailed_meaning: After Ram and Sita are reunited and their glory is being described, the scene widens into cosmic celebration. Radiant beings shower flowers, drums sound above, and heavenly singers and dancers mark the joy of this sacred reunion.
ramacharitamanas::5187.modern_relevance: You step out of a wedding hall and hear music still ringing behind you, while strangers smile for no reason they can name. Some joy is so full it spills outward.
ramacharitamanas::5187.insight: It turns the reunion into a public, cosmic event rather than a private moment.

ramacharitamanas::5188.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुता समेत प्रभु सोभा अमित अपार। देखि भालु कपि हरषे जय रघुपति सुख सार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5188.verse_hindi: श्री जानकीजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी की अपरिमित और अपार शोभा देखकर रीछ-वानर हर्षित हो गए और सुख के सार श्री रघुनाथजी की जय बोलने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5188.english_translation: Seeing the immeasurable, boundless splendor of the Lord together with Janak's daughter, the bears and monkeys rejoiced and cried, “Victory to Raghupati, the essence of joy!”
ramacharitamanas::5188.translation_literal: जनकसुता (Janak's daughter) / समेत (together with) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सोभा (splendor) / अमित (immeasurable) / अपार (boundless) / देखि (seeing) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / हरषे (rejoiced) / जय (victory) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / सुख (joy) / सार (essence)
ramacharitamanas::5188.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5188.essence: Recognition of the beloved turns relief into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5188.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita appear in radiant glory, and the bears and monkeys burst into joy and praise him.
ramacharitamanas::5188.simple_insight: Joy deepens when you recognize what is sacred right in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::5188.detailed_meaning: Ram has just been reunited with Sita, and the scene is overflowing with relief and wonder. The bears and monkeys see their Lord's boundless splendor and respond with celebration, not analysis. This is a moment of shared joy, not a teaching verse on its own.
ramacharitamanas::5188.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a long, painful separation, and the people who love you simply light up. Some moments do not need explanation — only recognition and gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::5188.insight: It shifts attention from private relief to shared celebration of what has been restored.

ramacharitamanas::5189.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुपति अनुसासन पाई। मातलि चलेउ चरन सिरु नाई॥ आए देव सदा स्वारथी। बचन कहहिं जनु परमारथी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5189.verse_hindi: तब श्री रघुनाथजी की आज्ञा पाकर इंद्र का सारथी मातलि चरणों में सिर नवाकर (रथ लेकर) चला गया। तदनन्तर सदा के स्वार्थी देवता आए। वे ऐसे वचन कह रहे हैं मानो बड़े परमार्थी हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5189.english_translation: Then, receiving Raghupati's command, Matali bowed his head to the ground and departed. After that, the ever-selfish gods came, speaking as if they were great lovers of duty.
ramacharitamanas::5189.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / अनुसासन (command, instruction) / पाई (having received) / मातलि (Matali) / चलेउ (departed) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) ॥ आए (came) / देव (the radiant beings, gods) / सदा (always) / स्वारथी (self-interested) / बचन (words) / कहहिं (they speak) / जनु (as if) / परमारथी (selflessly devoted to duty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5189.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5189.essence: Words can sound selfless while motives stay selfish.
ramacharitamanas::5189.simple_meaning: Matali leaves after bowing to Ram. Then the gods arrive, speaking like selfless seekers even though they are usually self-interested.
ramacharitamanas::5189.simple_insight: Pride can wear the mask of virtue, but action reveals the real motive.
ramacharitamanas::5189.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield in Lanka, Ram has just been glorified and Matali, Indra's charioteer, departs after receiving Ram's command. Then the gods appear, praising in polished words. The verse exposes their flattering, self-serving nature before the next divine response.
ramacharitamanas::5189.modern_relevance: A committee meeting ends, and the same people who stayed silent all month suddenly sound noble and principled. You can hear the performance when motives are louder than words.
ramacharitamanas::5189.insight: It teaches you to look past polished speech and notice whether someone's actions match their claimed virtue.

ramacharitamanas::5190.verse_sanskrit: दीन बंधु दयाल रघुराया। देव कीन्हि देवन्ह पर दाया॥ बिस्व द्रोह रत यह खल कामी। निज अघ गयउ कुमारगगामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5190.verse_hindi: हे दीनबन्धु! हे दयालु रघुराज! हे परमदेव! आपने देवताओं पर बड़ी दया की। विश्व के द्रोह में तत्पर यह दुष्ट, कामी और कुमार्ग पर चलने वाला रावण अपने ही पाप से नष्ट हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5190.english_translation: O friend of the lowly, compassionate Raghu king, you showed mercy to the radiant beings. That wicked one, devoted to hostility against the world, lustful, and walking the wrong path, was destroyed by his own sins.
ramacharitamanas::5190.translation_literal: दीन बंधु (friend of the lowly) / दयाल रघुराया (compassionate Raghu king) / देव (radiant being) / कीन्हि (did) / देवन्ह पर (upon the radiant beings) / दाया (mercy) / बिस्व (world) / द्रोह (hostility) / रत (engaged) / यह (this) / खल (wicked one) / कामी (lustful) / निज (own) / अघ (sins) / गयउ (went/destroyed) / कुमारगगामी (one walking the wrong path)
ramacharitamanas::5190.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5190.essence: Cruelty collapses from within; compassion protects what is worthy.
ramacharitamanas::5190.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as compassionate toward the devas, while Ravana is described as a wicked being destroyed by his own wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::5190.simple_insight: Pride and cruelty carry their own collapse.
ramacharitamanas::5190.detailed_meaning: After Ram’s victory, the poet turns from the battlefield to meaning. The devas are safe because Ram has shown them mercy, while Ravana is not defeated by chance but by the weight of his own corruption. The verse explains why the war ends as it does.
ramacharitamanas::5190.modern_relevance: Someone keeps doubling down on arrogance, blaming everyone else, and acting shocked when everything falls apart. This verse names the pattern: self-made ruin.
ramacharitamanas::5190.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming fate to seeing how harmful choices destroy themselves.

ramacharitamanas::5191.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह समरूप ब्रह्म अबिनासी। सदा एकरस सहज उदासी॥ अकल अगुन अज अनघ अनामय। अजित अमोघसक्ति करुनामय ॥
ramacharitamanas::5191.verse_hindi: आप समरूप, ब्रह्म, अविनाशी, नित्य, एकरस, स्वभाव से ही उदासीन (शत्रु-मित्र-भावरहित), अखंड, निर्गुण (मायिक गुणों से रहित), अजन्मे, निष्पाप, निर्विकार, अजेय, अमोघशक्ति (जिनकी शक्ति कभी व्यर्थ नहीं जाती) और दयामय हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5191.english_translation: You are the same in every form: the imperishable supreme reality, ever one in taste, naturally detached; whole, without qualities, unborn, flawless, unaging, unconquerable, never-failing in power, and full of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::5191.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / समरूप (of the same form) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / सदा (always) / एकरस (one essence) / सहज (natural) / उदासी (detached) / अकल (whole) / अगुन (without qualities) / अज (unborn) / अनघ (flawless) / अनामय (free from defect) / अजित (unconquerable) / अमोघसक्ति (never-failing power) / करुनामय (full of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::5191.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5191.essence: The highest power is also the most untouched and compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::5191.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as changeless, unborn, beyond ordinary qualities, naturally detached, invincible, and full of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::5191.simple_insight: There is comfort in meeting a presence that cannot be shaken, diminished, or exhausted.
ramacharitamanas::5191.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the war has turned against Ravana, the speaker turns to Ram in praise. This is not about battle tactics now, but about who Ram truly is: changeless, unborn, beyond ordinary qualities, and yet deeply compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::5191.modern_relevance: After a long day of being pulled in every direction, you need something in yourself that cannot be shaken by praise, blame, or pressure.
ramacharitamanas::5191.insight: It shifts attention from temporary moods and roles to what remains steady beneath them.

ramacharitamanas::5192.verse_sanskrit: मीन कमठ सूकर नरहरी। बामन परसुराम बपु धरी॥ जब जब नाथ सुरन्ह दुखु पायो। नाना तनु धरि तुम्हइँ नसायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5192.verse_hindi: आपने ही मत्स्य, कच्छप, वराह, नृसिंह, वामन और परशुराम के शरीर धारण किए। हे नाथ! जब-जब देवताओं ने दुःख पाया, तब-तब अनेकों शरीर धारण करके आपने ही उनका दुःख नाश किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5192.english_translation: You took the forms of fish, turtle, boar, man-lion, dwarf, and Parashurama. Whenever the radiant beings suffered, you appeared in many forms and ended their pain.
ramacharitamanas::5192.translation_literal: मीन (fish) / कमठ (turtle) / सूकर (boar) / नरहरी (man-lion) / बामन (dwarf) / परसुराम (Parashurama) / बपु (body/form) / धरी (having taken) / जब-जब (whenever) / नाथ (Lord) / सुरन्ह (of the radiant beings) / दुखु (pain) / पायो (was found/suffered) / नाना (many) / तनु (forms/bodies) / धरि (having taken) / तुम्हइँ (you) / नसायो (destroyed/removed)
ramacharitamanas::5192.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5192.essence: The divine meets suffering by taking whatever form is needed.
ramacharitamanas::5192.simple_meaning: Ram has appeared again and again in different forms to protect the radiant beings whenever they suffered.
ramacharitamanas::5192.simple_insight: You are not abandoned when help looks unexpected.
ramacharitamanas::5192.detailed_meaning: Shiva is praising Ram in Lanka after describing his supreme nature. He recalls the divine descents as fish, turtle, boar, man-lion, dwarf, and Parashurama, saying that whenever the radiant beings were troubled, Ram took whatever form was needed to end their suffering.
ramacharitamanas::5192.modern_relevance: You are breaking under pressure, and the help you need arrives in an unexpected form: a blunt friend, a changed plan, a sudden opening. Care does not always look familiar.
ramacharitamanas::5192.insight: It shifts attention from fixed expectations to the many ways help can arrive.

ramacharitamanas::5193.verse_sanskrit: यह खल मलिन सदा सुरद्रोही। काम लोभ मद रत अति कोही। अधम सिरोमनि तव पद पावा। यह हमरें मन बिसमय आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5193.verse_hindi: यह दुष्ट मलिन हृदय, देवताओं का नित्य शत्रु, काम, लोभ और मद के परायण तथा अत्यंत क्रोधी था। ऐसे अधमों के शिरोमणि ने भी आपका परम पद पा लिया। इस बात का हमारे मन में आश्चर्य हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5193.english_translation: He was vile, filthy, always hostile to the radiant beings, devoted to desire, greed, pride, and fierce anger. Yet even this worst of the low reached your supreme state. That fills our minds with wonder.
ramacharitamanas::5193.translation_literal: यह (this) / खल (wicked one) / मलिन (impure) / सदा (always) / सुरद्रोही (hostile to the radiant beings) / काम (desire) / लोभ (greed) / मद (pride) / रत (attached) / अति (very) / कोही (angry) / अधम (lowest) / सिरोमनि (crest-jewel) / तव (your) / पद (feet/state) / पावा (attained) / यह (this) / हमरे (our) / मन (mind) / बिसमय (wonder) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::5193.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5193.essence: Ram's mercy can reach even the most fallen heart.
ramacharitamanas::5193.simple_meaning: A terrible being, full of anger and greed, still reached Ram's feet. That unexpected mercy leaves everyone amazed.
ramacharitamanas::5193.simple_insight: No one is too fallen to turn back. That possibility softens fear and pride at once.
ramacharitamanas::5193.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana is praising Ram after Ravana's fall. He describes Ravana as deeply corrupt and yet still somehow touched by Ram's grace. The wonder is not Ravana's merit, but Ram's reach.
ramacharitamanas::5193.modern_relevance: You look at someone who has made a mess of everything and assume the door is shut. Then you remember that mercy can reach farther than judgment ever does.
ramacharitamanas::5193.insight: It shifts the mind from moral hopelessness to trust in grace that can still transform the worst case.

ramacharitamanas::5194.verse_sanskrit: हम देवता परम अधिकारी। स्वारथ रत प्रभु भगति बिसारी॥ भव प्रबाहँ संतत हम परे। अब प्रभु पाहि सरन अनुसरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5194.verse_hindi: हम देवता श्रेष्ठ अधिकारी होकर भी स्वार्थपरायण हो आपकी भक्ति को भुलाकर निरंतर भवसागर के प्रवाह (जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्र) में पड़े हैं। अब हे प्रभो! हम आपकी शरण में आ गए हैं, हमारी रक्षा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5194.english_translation: We, the radiant beings, though highly privileged, became self-centered and forgot devotion to the Lord. We have long been swept along by the current of repeated birth and death. Now, Lord, we have come seeking your refuge—please protect us.
ramacharitamanas::5194.translation_literal: हम (we) / देवता (radiant beings) / परम (highest) / अधिकारी (entitled, worthy) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / रत (absorbed) / प्रभु (Lord) / भगति (devotion) / बिसारी (forgot) ॥ भव (worldly becoming) / प्रबाहँ (in the current) / संतत (continually) / हम (we) / परे (fell) / अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / पाहि (protect) / सरन (refuge) / अनुसरे (having come to) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5194.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::5194.essence: Pride can trap even the exalted; surrender opens the way home.
ramacharitamanas::5194.simple_meaning: Even the highest beings lost their way through self-interest and were trapped in repeated suffering. Now they turn back and ask the Lord for protection.
ramacharitamanas::5194.simple_insight: No one is too high to fall, and no one is too far to return.
ramacharitamanas::5194.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's defeat, the gods gather and confess their own failure. Brahma speaks for them: even the radiant beings became self-absorbed, forgot devotion, and got caught in the cycle of repeated birth and death. Now they surrender and ask Ram for protection.
ramacharitamanas::5194.modern_relevance: You finally admit you cannot keep carrying everything alone. After months of pride, burnout, and pretending you're fine, you ask for help without dressing it up.
ramacharitamanas::5194.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance born of ego to humble refuge in what is greater.

ramacharitamanas::5195.verse_sanskrit: दोहा- करि बिनती सुर सिद्ध सब रहे जहँ तहँ कर जोरि। अति सप्रेम तन पु लकि बिधि अस्तुति करत बहोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5195.verse_hindi: विनती करके देवता और सिद्ध सब जहाँ के तहाँ हाथ जोड़े खड़े रहे। तब अत्यंत प्रेम से पुलकित शरीर होकर ब्रह्माजी स्तुति करने लगे-- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5195.english_translation: After offering their prayers, all the gods and perfected beings stood wherever they were with folded hands. Then, with bodies thrilled by deep love, Brahma began to praise him again.
ramacharitamanas::5195.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिनती (prayer, request) / सुर (the radiant beings) / सिद्ध (the perfected beings) / सब (all) / रहे (remained) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / कर (hands) / जोरि (joined) / अति (very) / सप्रेम (with deep love) / तन (body) / पु (then) / लकि (thrilled, shivering with joy) / बिधि (Brahma) / अस्तुति (praise) / करत (doing) / बहोरि (again)
ramacharitamanas::5195.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5195.essence: True greatness makes even the highest bow in love.
ramacharitamanas::5195.simple_meaning: The gods and perfected beings stand with folded hands in prayer, and Brahma begins praising with deep love and awe.
ramacharitamanas::5195.simple_insight: Reverence can leave even the highest beings wordless before what they love.
ramacharitamanas::5195.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after Ravana’s defeat begins to unfold, the gods and perfected beings gather in relief and devotion. They stand with folded hands, overwhelmed by what they are witnessing, and Brahma himself starts offering praise again.
ramacharitamanas::5195.modern_relevance: You finally see someone handle power without arrogance, and your first response is quiet respect. Some moments make admiration feel like the only honest language.
ramacharitamanas::5195.insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the humility and wonder it awakens in others.

ramacharitamanas::5196.verse_sanskrit: छंद- जय राम सदा सुख धाम हरे। रघुनायक सायक चाप धरे॥ भव बारन दारन सिंह प्रभो। गुन सागर नागर नाथ बिभो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5196.verse_hindi: हे नित्य सुखधाम और (दु:खों को हरने वाले) हरि! हे धनुष-बाण धारण किए हुए रघुनाथजी! आपकी जय हो। हे प्रभो! आप भव (जन्म-मरण) रूपी हाथी को विदीर्ण करने के लिए सिंह के समान हैं। हे नाथ! हे सर्वव्यापक! आप गुणों के समुद्र और परम चतुर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5196.english_translation: Victory to Ram, the ever-abiding home of joy, Hari who holds bow and arrows. Lord of the Raghu line, you are like a lion to the elephant of becoming. O Lord, ocean of virtues, master, all-pervading, supremely wise.
ramacharitamanas::5196.translation_literal: जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / सदा (always) / सुख धाम (abode of joy) / हरे (Hari) / रघुनायक (leader of the Raghu line) / सायक (arrows) / चाप (bow) / धरे (holding) / भव (becoming / the cycle of rebirth) / बारन (elephant) / दारन (tearing apart) / सिंह (lion) / प्रभो (O Lord) / गुन (virtues) / सागर (ocean) / नागर (skilled / refined) / नाथ (master) / बिभो (all-pervading one)
ramacharitamanas::5196.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5196.essence: Ram is joy itself and the force that breaks bondage.
ramacharitamanas::5196.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the eternal source of joy, the one who destroys the cycle of rebirth, and the master filled with virtues and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::5196.simple_insight: Praise can steady the heart when fear and restlessness feel overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::5196.detailed_meaning: After the gods and sages bow, Tulsidas turns to direct praise of Ram in the middle of Lanka's war. Ram is not just a warrior here; he is joy itself, the destroyer of bondage, and the all-pervading master whom even victory serves.
ramacharitamanas::5196.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after fighting the same fear for the tenth time, and something in you wants a strength bigger than willpower. This praise names that strength and lets your mind rest in it.
ramacharitamanas::5196.insight: It shifts attention from Ram as a heroic figure to Ram as the power that ends bondage and steadies devotion.

ramacharitamanas::5197.verse_sanskrit: तन काम अनेक अनूप छबी। गुन गावत सिद्ध मुनींद्र कबी॥ जसु पावन रावन नाग महा। खगनाथ जथा करि कोप गहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5197.verse_hindi: आपके शरीर की अनेकों कामदेवों के समान, परंतु अनुपम छवि है। सिद्ध, मुनीश्वर और कवि आपके गुण गाते रहते हैं। आपका यश पवित्र है। आपने रावणरूपी महासर्प को गरुड़ की तरह क्रोध करके पकड़ लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5197.english_translation: Your form is unmatched, as lovely as countless gods of desire. Siddhas, sages, and poets keep singing your qualities. Your fame is pure. With a fierce rush, you seized Ravana, the great serpent, just as Garuda seizes a snake.
ramacharitamanas::5197.translation_literal: तन (body/form) / काम (desire-god) / अनेक (many) / अनूप (matchless) / छबी (beauty, form) / गुन (qualities) / गावत (singing) / सिद्ध (perfect beings) / मुनींद्र (great sages) / कबी (poets) / जसु (fame) / पावन (pure) / रावन (Ravana) / नाग (snake) / महा (great) / खगनाथ (Garuda, lord of birds) / जथा (like) / करि (having done) / कोप (anger) / गहा (seized, grasped)
ramacharitamanas::5197.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::5197.essence: Ram's beauty and power leave even the wise singing.
ramacharitamanas::5197.simple_meaning: Ram's beauty and fame are beyond compare, and even the greatest sages keep praising him. His power is so great that Ravana is caught like a snake in Garuda's grip.
ramacharitamanas::5197.simple_insight: Some greatness does not need explanation — it simply leaves everyone else in awe.
ramacharitamanas::5197.detailed_meaning: After the gods and perfected beings bow, Brahma continues praising Ram in the war's aftermath. He moves from Ram's incomparable beauty to the way Ravana has been overpowered, showing that Ram's grace and force are both beyond ordinary measure.
ramacharitamanas::5197.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone handles a crisis with total calm and absolute force. People do not just notice the result — they feel the presence behind it.
ramacharitamanas::5197.insight: It joins beauty, praise, and power in one image, showing that true greatness can be both gentle and overwhelming.

ramacharitamanas::5198.verse_sanskrit: जन रंजन भंजन सोक भयं। गत क्रोध सदा प्रभु बोधमयं॥ अवतार उदार अपार गुनं। महि भार बिभंजन ग्यानघनं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5198.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! आप सेवकों को आनंद देने वाले, शोक और भय का नाश करने वाले, सदा क्रोधरहित और नित्य ज्ञान स्वरूप हैं। आपका अवतार श्रेष्ठ, अपार दिव्य गुणों वाला, पृथ्वी का भार उतारने वाला और ज्ञान का समूह है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5198.english_translation: You delight your devotees, destroy sorrow and fear, remain free from anger, and are always full of wisdom. Your incarnation is noble and limitless in virtue, the one who lifts the burden of the world and is pure knowledge itself.
ramacharitamanas::5198.translation_literal: जन (people/devotees) / रंजन (delighting) / भंजन (destroying) / सोक (sorrow) / भयं (fear) / गत (gone) / क्रोध (anger) / सदा (always) / प्रभु (Lord) / बोधमयं (full of awareness) / अवतार (incarnation) / उदार (noble/generous) / अपार (limitless) / गुनं (virtues) / महि (earth/world) / भार (burden) / बिभंजन (shattering/removing) / ग्यानघनं (dense mass of knowledge)
ramacharitamanas::5198.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5198.essence: True greatness removes fear and carries burden without anger.
ramacharitamanas::5198.simple_meaning: Ram brings joy to devotees, removes sorrow and fear, never acts in anger, and is full of wisdom. His descent into the world is noble, vast, and meant to lift its burden.
ramacharitamanas::5198.simple_insight: You can trust a presence that steadies fear without losing warmth.
ramacharitamanas::5198.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war in Lanka, the poet pauses to praise Ram directly. After describing his beauty and glory, this verse turns to his inner nature: he comforts, protects, teaches, and carries the world's burden without anger.
ramacharitamanas::5198.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in the hospital waiting room, and their panic starts to soften because you are calm. That quiet steadiness — not force — is what this verse honours.
ramacharitamanas::5198.insight: It shifts admiration from outer power to the inner qualities that make power safe.

ramacharitamanas::5199.verse_sanskrit: अज ब्यापकमेकमनादि सदा। करुनाकर राम नमामि मुदा॥ रघुबंस बिभूषन दूषन हा। कृत भूप बिभीषन दीन रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5199.verse_hindi: (किंतु अवतार लेने पर भी) आप नित्य, अजन्मा, व्यापक, एक (अद्वितीय) और अनादि हैं। हे करुणा की खान श्रीरामजी! मैं आपको बड़े ही हर्ष के साथ नमस्कार करता हूँ। हे रघुकुल के आभूषण! हे दूषण राक्षस को मारने वाले तथा समस्त दोषों को हरने वाले! विभिषण दीन था, उसे आपने (लंका का) राजा बना दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5199.english_translation: (Even after taking an incarnation,) you are eternal, unborn, all-pervading, one, and without beginning. O Ram, treasure of compassion, I bow to you with joy. O ornament of the Raghu line, destroyer of the demon Dushan and remover of all faults, Vibhishana was humble, and you made him king of Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::5199.translation_literal: अज (unborn) / ब्यापकम् (all-pervading) / एकम् (one, without a second) / अनादि (without beginning) / सदा (always) / करुनाकर (ocean of compassion) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow) / मुदा (with joy) / रघुबंस (line of Raghu) / बिभूषन (ornament) / दूषन (Dushan) / हा (destroyer) / कृत (made) / भूप (king) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / दीन (humble, lowly) / रहा (was)
ramacharitamanas::5199.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5199.essence: Ram is greatest because his power always serves compassion.
ramacharitamanas::5199.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond birth and beginning, yet full of compassion. He destroys evil, removes faults, and lifts the humble into honor.
ramacharitamanas::5199.simple_insight: Reverence becomes easier when greatness feels tender, not distant.
ramacharitamanas::5199.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Tulsidas pauses the war to praise Ram’s true nature. Ram is not just a warrior who kills Dushan; he is unborn, all-pervading, and compassionate. The same Ram who defeats evil also crowns the humble Vibhishana.
ramacharitamanas::5199.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems powerful only because they dominate the room. Then they quietly defend the weak and give credit away. That combination of strength and compassion changes how you trust them.
ramacharitamanas::5199.insight: It shifts devotion from fear to love by showing power joined with mercy.

ramacharitamanas::5200.verse_sanskrit: गुन ध्यान निधान अमान अजं। नित राम नमामि बिभुं बिरजं॥ भुजदंड प्रचंड प्रताप बलं। खल बृंद निकंद महा कुसलं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5200.verse_hindi: हे गुण और ज्ञान के भंडार! हे मानरहित! हे अजन्मा, व्यापक और मायिक विकारों से रहित श्रीराम! मैं आपको नित्य नमस्कार करता हूँ। आपके भुजदंडों का प्रताप और बल प्रचंड है। दुष्ट समूह के नाश करने में आप परम निपुण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5200.english_translation: I bow daily to Ram, the treasure of virtues and contemplation, without pride, unborn, all-pervading, and free from blemish. His mighty arms blaze with power, and he is expert at destroying evil forces.
ramacharitamanas::5200.translation_literal: गुन (virtues) / ध्यान (contemplation) / निधान (treasure) / अमान (without pride) / अजं (unborn) / नित (daily) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow) / बिभुं (all-pervading) / बिरजं (without blemish) / भुजदंड (arms) / प्रचंड (mighty) / प्रताप (radiance/power) / बलं (strength) / खल बृंद (groups of evil ones) / निकंद (destroyer) / महा कुसलं (highly skilled)
ramacharitamanas::5200.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5200.essence: True power stays pure, humble, and undefeated by ego.
ramacharitamanas::5200.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as humble, unborn, all-pervading, pure, powerful, and supremely skilled at destroying evil.
ramacharitamanas::5200.simple_insight: Strength feels safest when it is joined with humility and purity.
ramacharitamanas::5200.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is offering another hymn of praise to Ram after the war’s great turning point. He sees Ram not just as victorious, but as limitless, spotless, and humble — the kind of power that removes evil without becoming cruel.
