ramacharitamanas::5200.modern_relevance: You meet someone who can command a room without needing to dominate it. Their strength feels clean, not threatening. That is the kind of power this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::5200.insight: It shifts admiration away from raw force and toward force joined with humility and moral clarity.

ramacharitamanas::5201.verse_sanskrit: बिनु कारन दीन दयाल हितं। छबि धाम नमामि रमा सहितं॥ भव तारन कारन काज परं। मन संभव दारुन दोष हरं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5201.verse_hindi: हे बिना ही कारण दीनों पर दया तथा उनका हित करने वाले और शोभा के धाम! मैं श्रीजानकीजी सहित आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। आप भवसागर से तारने वाले हैं, कारणरूपा प्रकृति और कार्यरूप जगत दोनों से परे हैं और मन से उत्पन्न होने वाले कठिन दोषों को हरने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5201.english_translation: I bow to Ram, joined with Sita, who is kind to the humble without cause, the abode of beauty, the savior from becoming, beyond cause and effect, and the remover of the terrible faults born in the mind.
ramacharitamanas::5201.translation_literal: बिनु कारन (without cause) / दीन दयाल (kind to the humble) / हितं (benefactor) / छबि धाम (abode of beauty) / नमामि (I bow) / रमा सहितं (joined with Sita) / भव तारन (savior from becoming) / कारन काज (cause and effect) / परं (beyond) / मन संभव (born from the mind) / दारुन दोष (terrible faults) / हरं (remover)
ramacharitamanas::5201.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5201.essence: Ram's help arrives without cause and cuts through the mind's worst wounds.
ramacharitamanas::5201.simple_meaning: Ram, with Sita, is praised as the one who helps the humble without any reason, carries beings across the cycle of becoming, and removes deep inner faults.
ramacharitamanas::5201.simple_insight: You are not being judged from a distance; help can meet you before you can even explain yourself.
ramacharitamanas::5201.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, Tulsidas pauses the action to bow to Ram and Sita. He praises Ram as beauty itself, beyond cause and effect, and as the one who frees people from the mind's darkest distortions.
ramacharitamanas::5201.modern_relevance: After a day when your thoughts have turned cruel and self-defeating, you remember that mercy is not earned by perfect performance. Some help reaches you before you can clean yourself up.
ramacharitamanas::5201.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to refuge, and from mental distortion to the possibility of being lifted.

ramacharitamanas::5202.verse_sanskrit: सर चाप मनोहर त्रोन धरं। जलजारुन लोचन भूपबरं॥ सुख मंदिर सुंदर श्रीरमनं। मद मार मुधा ममता समनं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5202.verse_hindi: आप मनोहर बाण, धनुष और तरकस धारण करने वाले हैं। (लाल) कमल के समान रक्तवर्ण आपके नेत्र हैं। आप राजाओं में श्रेष्ठ, सुख के मंदिर, सुंदर, श्री (लक्ष्मीजी) के वल्लभ तथा मद (अहंकार), काम और झूठी ममता के नाश करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5202.english_translation: You hold beautiful arrows, bow, and quiver. Your eyes are red like lotus petals. You are the best among kings, a home of joy, beautiful, beloved of Lakshmi, and the destroyer of pride, desire, and false possessiveness.
ramacharitamanas::5202.translation_literal: सर (arrows) / चाप (bow) / मनोहर (beautiful) / त्रोन (quiver) / धरं (holding) / जलजारुन (lotus-red) / लोचन (eyes) / भूपबरं (best of kings) / सुख (joy) / मंदिर (home) / सुंदर (beautiful) / श्रीरमनं (beloved of Lakshmi) / मद (pride) / मार (desire) / मुधा (false) / ममता (possessiveness) / समनं (destroying)
ramacharitamanas::5202.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5202.essence: Ram's beauty defeats the ego before any weapon is used.
ramacharitamanas::5202.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as a beautiful, noble, joy-giving king whose very presence destroys pride, desire, and possessiveness.
ramacharitamanas::5202.simple_insight: Real greatness does not inflate the ego; it quietly dissolves it.
ramacharitamanas::5202.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final stretch, Tulsidas pauses the battle to praise Ram's form. He sees not just a warrior with bow and arrows, but the king whose beauty, majesty, and presence cut down pride, craving, and false attachment.
ramacharitamanas::5202.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm confidence changes the whole room. No one feels smaller — your own posturing simply stops mattering.
ramacharitamanas::5202.insight: It shifts admiration away from surface power and toward the kind of presence that purifies the mind.

ramacharitamanas::5203.verse_sanskrit: अनवद्य अखंड न गोचर गो। सब रूप सदा सब होइ न गो॥ इति बेद बदंति न दंतकथा। रबि आतप भिन्नमभिन्न जथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5203.verse_hindi: आप अनिन्द्य या दोषरहित हैं, अखंड हैं, इंद्रियों के विषय नहीं हैं। सदा सर्वरूप होते हुए भी आप वह सब कभी हुए ही नहीं, ऐसा वेद कहते हैं। यह (कोई) दंतकथा (कोरी कल्पना) नहीं है। जैसे सूर्य और सूर्य का प्रकाश अलग-अलग हैं और अलग नहीं भी है, वैसे ही आप भी संसार से भिन्न तथा अभिन्न दोनों ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5203.english_translation: You are flawless, indivisible, and beyond the reach of the senses. Though you are always all forms, you never truly become any of them. The Vedas say this, not mere legend. Like sunlight and the sun, you are both different from the world and not different from it.
ramacharitamanas::5203.translation_literal: अनवद्य (flawless) / अखंड (indivisible) / न गोचर (not within reach) / गो (of the senses) / सब रूप (all forms) / सदा (always) / सब (all) / होइ (become) / न गो (not) / इति (thus) / बेद (the Vedas) / बदंति (declare) / न (not) / दंतकथा (legend) / रबि (sun) / आतप (sunlight/heat) / भिन्न (different) / अभिन्न (not different) / जथा (as)
ramacharitamanas::5203.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5203.essence: Ram is beyond form and still present in every form.
ramacharitamanas::5203.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond the senses, perfect, and whole. He appears as many forms without being trapped by any one form, like sunlight and the sun: distinct, yet inseparable.
ramacharitamanas::5203.simple_insight: The divine can be intimate without being small.
ramacharitamanas::5203.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the battle's heat, the poet turns from action to vision. Ram is praised not as a local hero but as the supreme reality: beyond sense-grasp, yet appearing in every form. The Vedas confirm it, and the image of sun and sunlight explains the mystery.
ramacharitamanas::5203.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary in the morning, then later realize one choice from them changed the whole room. Some realities are present everywhere without ever being reducible to what you can point at.
ramacharitamanas::5203.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as one figure among many to recognizing him as present beyond all appearances.

ramacharitamanas::5204.verse_sanskrit: कृतकृत्य बिभो सब बानर ए। निरखंति तनानन सादर ए॥ धिग जीवन देव सरीर हरे। तव भक्ति बिना भव भूलि परे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5204.verse_hindi: हे व्यापक प्रभो! ये सब वानर कृतार्थ रूप हैं, जो आदरपूर्वक ये आपका मुख देख रहे हैं। (और) हे हरे! हमारे (अमर) जीवन और देव (दिव्य) शरीर को धिक्कार है, जो हम आपकी भक्ति से रहित हुए संसार में (सांसारिक विषयों में) भूले पड़े हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5204.english_translation: O all-pervading Lord, these monkeys are fulfilled indeed, for they look upon your face with reverence. And shame on our lives and divine bodies, O Hari, if we remain lost in the world without your devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5204.translation_literal: कृतकृत्य (fully accomplished) / बिभो (O all-pervading Lord) / सब (all) / बानर (monkeys) / ए (these) / निरखंति (are looking) / तनानन (your face) / सादर (with reverence) / ए (indeed) / धिग (shame on) / जीवन (life) / देव (divine) / सरीर (body) / हरे (O Hari) / तव (your) / भक्ति (devotion) / बिना (without) / भव (worldly existence) / भूलि (lost) / परे (fallen)
ramacharitamanas::5204.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5204.essence: Without devotion, even a blessed life feels wasted.
ramacharitamanas::5204.simple_meaning: Hanuman says the monkeys are truly fulfilled because they can look at Ram with reverence. Without devotion to Ram, even a divine life and body feel wasted.
ramacharitamanas::5204.simple_insight: Real fulfillment comes from loving attention, not status or power.
ramacharitamanas::5204.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman stands among the vanaras after the search for Sita and the first great proof of Ram's presence. Looking at Ram, he sees that true accomplishment is not victory or strength, but devotion itself. Without that, even a glorious life feels empty.
ramacharitamanas::5204.modern_relevance: You finish a huge project, but the room feels hollow because you never cared about what it meant. Then one quiet moment of real love or reverence makes everything feel alive again.
ramacharitamanas::5204.insight: It shifts the mind from achievement as success to devotion as fulfillment.

ramacharitamanas::5205.verse_sanskrit: अब दीनदयाल दया करिऐ। मति मोरि बिभेदकरी हरिऐ॥ जेहि ते बिपरीत क्रिया करिऐ। दुख सो सुख मानि सुखी चरिऐ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5205.verse_hindi: हे दीनदयालु! अब दया कीजिए और मेरी उस विभेद उत्पन्न करने वाली बुद्धि को हर लीजिए, जिससे मैं विपरीत कर्म करता हूँ और जो दु:ख है, उसे सुख मानकर आनंद से विचरता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5205.english_translation: O Lord of the poor, show mercy now and take away this dividing intellect of mine, which makes me do the opposite and call suffering happiness, wandering on in false delight.
ramacharitamanas::5205.translation_literal: अब (now) / दीनदयाल (compassionate toward the poor) / दया (mercy) / करिऐ (do) / मति (mind/intellect) / मोरि (my) / बिभेदकरी (causing division) / हरिऐ (remove) / जेहि (by which) / ते (thereby) / बिपरीत (opposite) / क्रिया (action) / करिऐ (do) / दुख (pain) / सो (as) / सुख (happiness) / मानि (considering) / सुखी (happy) / चरिऐ (wander/live)
ramacharitamanas::5205.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5205.essence: Confusion makes suffering look sweet until mercy clears the mind.
ramacharitamanas::5205.simple_meaning: The speaker asks Ram to remove the confused mind that makes him act against his own good and mistake suffering for happiness.
ramacharitamanas::5205.simple_insight: Real relief begins when confusion is removed, not when desire is satisfied.
ramacharitamanas::5205.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the victory is turning toward Ram, Tulsidas suddenly turns inward. Surrounded by the proof of divine grace, he begs Ram to heal the mind itself, because confusion makes a person choose what hurts and still call it joy.
ramacharitamanas::5205.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same message thread, the same habit, the same person, even after it hurts. What feels comforting may be the very thing that keeps you confused.
ramacharitamanas::5205.insight: It shifts you from trusting your impulses to asking for clearer seeing before you act.

ramacharitamanas::5206.verse_sanskrit: खल खंडन मंडन रम्य छमा। पद पंकज सेवित संभु उमा॥ नृप नायक दे बरदानमिदं। चरनांबुज प्रेमु सदा सुभदं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5206.verse_hindi: आप दुष्टों का खंडन करने वाले और पृथ्वी के रमणीय आभूषण हैं। आपके चरणकमल श्री शिव-पार्वती द्वारा स ेवित हैं। हे राजाओं के महाराज! मुझे यह वरदान दीजिए कि आपके चरणकमलों में सदा मेरा कल्याणदायक (अनन्य) प्रेम हो ॥ दोहा-
ramacharitamanas::5206.english_translation: You destroy evil and remain the beautiful ornament of the world. Shiva and Uma serve your lotus feet. O king of kings, grant me this boon: may I always have blessed love for your lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::5206.translation_literal: खल (wicked) / खंडन (destroyer) / मंडन (ornament) / रम्य (beautiful) / छमा (forgiveness, patience) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / सेवित (served) / संभु (Shiva) / उमा (Uma) / नृप (king) / नायक (leader) / दे (give) / बरदानम् (boon) / इदम् (this) / चरनांबुज (lotus feet) / प्रेमु (love) / सदा (always) / सुभदं (auspicious)
ramacharitamanas::5206.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::5206.essence: The highest boon is unbroken love for Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::5206.simple_meaning: Brahma praises Ram as the beautiful destroyer of evil and asks for one blessing: lasting love for Ram's lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::5206.simple_insight: Real fulfillment is not getting more, but loving what is worthy without end.
ramacharitamanas::5206.detailed_meaning: After the war, the victory has become spiritual praise. Brahma bows before Ram, calling him the destroyer of evil and the ornament of the world, while pointing to Shiva and Uma as devotees at his feet. He asks for one thing only: steady love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5206.modern_relevance: You finally reach the moment you worked for, and the applause fades fast. What stays is whether your heart has learned where to rest without bargaining for anything else.
ramacharitamanas::5206.insight: It shifts desire from achievement to devotion, from asking for gain to asking for lasting love.

ramacharitamanas::5207.verse_sanskrit: बिनय कीन्ह चतुरानन प्रेम पुलक अति गात। सोभासिंधु बिलोकत लोचन नहीं अघात ॥
ramacharitamanas::5207.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार ब्रह्माजी ने अत्यंत प्रेम-पुलकित शरीर से विनती की। शोभा के समुद्र श्रीरामजी के दर्शन करते-करते उनके नेत्र तृप्त ही नहीं होते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5207.english_translation: Brahma bowed with great love, his body thrilled with devotion. Gazing at Ram, the ocean of beauty, his eyes could not drink enough.
ramacharitamanas::5207.translation_literal: बिनय (humble request / bowing) / कीन्ह (did) / चतुरानन (four-faced one, Brahma) / प्रेम (love) / पुलक (goosebumps / thrill) / अति (very) / गात (body) / सोभासिंधु (ocean of beauty) / बिलोकत (while seeing) / लोचन (eyes) / नहीं (not) / अघात (became satisfied)
ramacharitamanas::5207.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5207.essence: Ram's beauty awakens devotion that never reaches enough.
ramacharitamanas::5207.simple_meaning: Brahma offers reverence to Ram and is so moved by Ram's beauty that he cannot stop looking.
ramacharitamanas::5207.simple_insight: True beauty does not just please you; it deepens devotion and keeps drawing you closer.
ramacharitamanas::5207.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final turning, Brahma appears before Ram and bows with overwhelming love. Even the creator is stunned by Ram's radiance, and his gaze keeps returning because Ram's beauty is inexhaustible.
ramacharitamanas::5207.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, kindness, or presence feels deeper every time you look. You don't get tired of them; you feel more devoted, more awake, more grateful.
ramacharitamanas::5207.insight: It shifts admiration from possession to reverent seeing. The more clearly you look, the less ordinary the beloved becomes.

ramacharitamanas::5208.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर दसरथ तहँ आए। तनय बिलोकि नयन जल छाए॥ अनुज सहित प्रभु बंदन कीन्हा। आसिरबाद पिताँ तब दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5208.verse_hindi: उसी समय दशरथजी वहाँ आए। पुत्र (श्रीरामजी) को देखकर उनके नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल छा गया। छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु ने उनकी वंदना की और तब पिता ने उनको आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5208.english_translation: At that moment Dasharath arrived there. Seeing his son, tears filled his eyes. The Lord, along with Lakshman, bowed to him, and then the father gave his blessing.
ramacharitamanas::5208.translation_literal: तेहि (that) अवसर (occasion/time) दसरथ (Dasharath) तहँ (there) आए (came) / तनय (son) बिलोकि (seeing) नयन (eyes) जल (water/tears) छाए (filled) / अनुज (younger brother) सहित (along with) प्रभु (the Lord) बंदन (bowing) कीन्हा (did) / आसिरबाद (blessing) पिताँ (by the father) तब (then) दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::5208.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5208.essence: Victory becomes whole only when it is bowed into with love.
ramacharitamanas::5208.simple_meaning: Dasharath arrives, sees Ram and feels overwhelming love, and Ram bows to him with Lakshman before receiving his blessing.
ramacharitamanas::5208.simple_insight: Love can make even a father and son meet with humility, not pride.
ramacharitamanas::5208.detailed_meaning: After Ram returns victorious, Dasharath comes to see him. The sight of his son fills him with tears, and Ram, with Lakshman beside him, bows first. The moment shows family love, reverence, and blessing after long separation and struggle.
ramacharitamanas::5208.modern_relevance: You finally see your child after a long, hard journey, and the first thing you feel is not triumph but tears. Respect still matters, even in joy.
ramacharitamanas::5208.insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the tenderness and humility that complete it.

ramacharitamanas::5209.verse_sanskrit: तात सकल तव पुन्य प्रभाऊ। जीत्यों अजय निसाचर राऊ॥ सुनि सुत बचन प्रीति अति बाढ़ी। नयन सलिल रोमावलि ठाढ़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5209.verse_hindi: (श्रीरामजी ने कहा-) हे तात! यह सब आपके पुण्यों का प्रभाव है, जो मैंने अजेय राक्षसराज को जीत लिया। पुत्र के वचन सुनकर उनकी प्रीति अत्यंत बढ़ गई। नेत्रों में जल छा गया और रोमावली खड़ी हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5209.english_translation: “Father, it is all the power of your merit that I have defeated the unconquerable king of demons.” Hearing his son’s words, his love swelled even more; tears filled his eyes and the hair on his body stood up.
ramacharitamanas::5209.translation_literal: तात (father) / सकल (all) / तव (your) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence) / जीत्यों (I conquered) / अजय (unconquerable) / निसाचर (night-walker, demon) / राऊ (king) / सुनि (hearing) / सुत (son) / बचन (words) / प्रीति (love) / अति (very) / बाढ़ी (increased) / नयन (eyes) / सलिल (water) / रोमावलि (hair on the body) / ठाढ़ी (stood up)
ramacharitamanas::5209.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5209.essence: True victory deepens love when it is offered without pride.
ramacharitamanas::5209.simple_meaning: Ram tells Dasharath that the victory over Ravana came through his merit, not his own pride. Dasharath is overwhelmed with love and emotion at hearing this.
ramacharitamanas::5209.simple_insight: Even a triumph becomes sweeter when it is offered back with humility.
ramacharitamanas::5209.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram meets Dasharath in the victorious gathering. Instead of claiming credit for defeating Ravana, he bows the achievement to his father’s merit. That humble reversal melts Dasharath into tears and love.
ramacharitamanas::5209.modern_relevance: You finally solve the problem everyone thought was impossible, and your first thought is to thank the person who raised you right. That kind of humility changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::5209.insight: It shifts victory away from ego and turns it into gratitude toward those who made it possible.

ramacharitamanas::5210.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति प्रथम प्रेम अनुमाना। चितइ पितहि दीन्हेउ दृढ़ ग्याना॥ ताते उमा मोच्छ नहिं पायो। दसरथ भेद भगति मन लायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5210.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने पहले के (जीवितकाल के) प्रेम को विचारकर, पिता की ओर देखकर ही उन्हें अपने स्वरूप का दृढ़ ज्ञान करा दिया। हे उमा! दशरथजी ने भेद-भक्ति में अपना मन लगाया था, इसी से उन्होंने (कैवल्य) मोक्ष नहीं पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5210.english_translation: Lord of the Raghu clan first remembered the love of earlier times and, looking at his father, gave him firm understanding of his own divine nature. O Uma, Dasharath did not attain liberation, because his mind was absorbed in loving devotion with distinction between lover and beloved.
ramacharitamanas::5210.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / प्रथम (first) / प्रेम (love) / अनुमाना (remembered, inferred) / चितइ (looking at) / पितहि (the father) / दीन्हेउ (gave) / दृढ़ (firm) / ग्याना (understanding, knowledge) / ताते (therefore) / उमा (O Uma) / मोच्छ (liberation) / नहिं (not) / पायो (attained) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / भेद (distinction, duality) / भगति (devotion) / मन (mind) / लायो (placed, fixed)
ramacharitamanas::5210.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5210.essence: Even loving devotion can fall short if separateness remains.
ramacharitamanas::5210.simple_meaning: Ram gave his father clear understanding, but Dasharath remained in loving devotion with a sense of separation. Because of that dual feeling, he did not reach liberation.
ramacharitamanas::5210.simple_insight: Even love can keep you at a distance if you still see yourself as separate.
ramacharitamanas::5210.detailed_meaning: After the war, Dasharath comes to see Ram again. Ram looks at him and awakens firm understanding of his true nature. But Tulsidas adds a subtle point to Parvati: Dasharath's love still held a sense of duality, so he did not merge into freedom.
ramacharitamanas::5210.modern_relevance: You can care deeply for someone and still keep them at arm's length in your mind. A relationship changes when love stops being divided into 'me' and 'you'.
ramacharitamanas::5210.insight: It shifts devotion from emotional attachment toward a more complete surrender of separateness.

ramacharitamanas::5211.verse_sanskrit: सगुनोपासक मोच्छ न लेहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ राम भगति निज देहीं॥ बार बार करि प्रभुहि प्रनामा। दसरथ हरषि गए सुरधामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5211.verse_hindi: (मायारहित सच्चिदानंदमय स्वरूपभूत दिव्यगुणयुक्त) सगुण स्वरूप की उपासना करने वाले भक्त इस प्रकार मोक्ष लेते भी नहीं। उनको श्रीरामजी अपनी भक्ति देते हैं। प्रभु को (इष्टबुद्धि से) बार-बार प्रणाम करके दशरथजी हर्षित होकर देवलोक को चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5211.english_translation: Devotees who worship the divine with form do not seek liberation. Ram gives them his own devotion. Bowing again and again to the Lord, Dasharath went joyfully to the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::5211.translation_literal: सगुनोपासक (worshippers of the divine with form) / मोच्छ (liberation) / न (not) / लेहीं (take) / तिन्ह कहुँ (for them) / राम (Ram) / भगति (devotion) / निज (his own) / देहीं (gives) / बार बार (again and again) / करि (doing) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / प्रनामा (bowing) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / हरषि (joyfully) / गए (went) / सुरधामा (to the higher realm)
ramacharitamanas::5211.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5211.essence: Devotion is richer than liberation, and Ram gives that freely.
ramacharitamanas::5211.simple_meaning: Devotees who love Ram's form are not after liberation as a prize. Ram gives them something even deeper: devotion itself. Dasharath bows again and again, then leaves in joy.
ramacharitamanas::5211.simple_insight: Love becomes its own reward when the heart is fixed on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5211.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just seen Ram after death and heard the consoling truth that even liberation is not the highest gift for a devotee. In this closing movement, Tulsidas shows the king bowing again and again, then departing in joy.
ramacharitamanas::5211.modern_relevance: You finally get the thing you thought would end your restlessness, but it doesn't. What settles you is not getting out of life — it's being given something to love without bargaining.
ramacharitamanas::5211.insight: It shifts the goal from escaping experience to deepening devotion.

ramacharitamanas::5212.verse_sanskrit: दोहा- अनुज जानकी सहित प्रभु कुसल कोसलाधीस। सोभा देखि हरषि मन अस्तुति कर सुर ईस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5212.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और जानकीजी सहित परम कुशल प्रभु श्रीकोसलाधीश की शोभा देखकर देवराज इंद्र मन में हर्षित होकर स्तुति करने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5212.english_translation: Seeing Lord of Kosala in good health, with Lakshman and Janaki beside him, Indra rejoiced in his mind and began to praise the lord of the gods.
ramacharitamanas::5212.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / जानकी सहित (together with Janaki) / प्रभु (lord) / कुसल (well, in good health) / कोसलाधीस (lord of Kosala) / सोभा (splendour) / देखि (seeing) / हरषि (rejoiced) / मन (mind) / अस्तुति (praise) / कर (doing) / सुर ईस (lord of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::5212.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5212.essence: True majesty makes even pride turn into praise.
ramacharitamanas::5212.simple_meaning: Indra sees Ram with Lakshman and Sita, feels joy, and starts praising him.
ramacharitamanas::5212.simple_insight: Even the highest powers bow when they see true majesty.
ramacharitamanas::5212.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram stands radiant in Kosala with Lakshman and Janaki beside him. Indra looks on, feels delight, and begins a hymn. The verse is a transition into praise, not the praise itself.
ramacharitamanas::5212.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard win, and the people who once doubted you fall quiet. Real greatness doesn’t need announcement; it changes the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::5212.insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the reverence victory inspires.

ramacharitamanas::5213.verse_sanskrit: जय राम सोभा धाम। दायक प्रनत बिश्राम॥ धृत त्रोन बर सर चाप। भुजदंड प्रबल प्रताप ॥
ramacharitamanas::5213.verse_hindi: शोभा के धाम, शरणागत को विश्राम देने वाले, श्रेष्ठ तरकस, धनुष और बाण धारण किए हुए, प्रबल प्रतापी भुज दंडों वाले श्रीरामचंद्रजी की जय हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5213.english_translation: Victory to Ram, the home of beauty, the giver of rest to those who seek refuge, bearing the finest quiver, bow, and arrows, with mighty and glorious arms.
ramacharitamanas::5213.translation_literal: जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / सोभा (beauty) / धाम (abode) / दायक (giver) / प्रनत (for the surrendered) / बिश्राम (rest) / धृत (holding) / त्रोन (quiver) / बर (excellent) / सर (arrows) / चाप (bow) / भुजदंड (arms) / प्रबल (mighty) / प्रताप (glory)
ramacharitamanas::5213.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5213.essence: True greatness protects the one who surrenders.
ramacharitamanas::5213.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the source of beauty and the one who gives peace to anyone who takes refuge in him, while also appearing as a mighty warrior ready for battle.
ramacharitamanas::5213.simple_insight: You can feel safe without becoming weak; refuge and strength can live together.
ramacharitamanas::5213.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the gods see Ram after the war has turned in his favor. Even in battle, he is praised not only for power but for the peace he gives to those who come to him. The verse joins majesty and shelter in one image.
ramacharitamanas::5213.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying a hard decision, and someone steady finally says, “I’ve got you.” The relief is real, but so is the respect. That is the feeling this verse carries.
ramacharitamanas::5213.insight: It teaches you to see strength as shelter, not domination.

ramacharitamanas::5214.verse_sanskrit: जय दूषनारि खरारि। मर्दन निसाचर धारि॥ यह दुष्ट मारेउ नाथ। भए देव सकल नाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5214.verse_hindi: हे खरदूषण के शत्रु और राक्षसों की सेना के मर्दन करने वाले! आपकी जय हो! हे नाथ! आपने इस दुष्ट को मारा, जिससे सब देवता सनाथ (सुरक्षित) हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5214.english_translation: Victory to the enemy of Khara and Dushana, the destroyer of the demon hosts. Victory to the Lord! You killed this wicked one, and all the radiant beings became protected.
ramacharitamanas::5214.translation_literal: जय (victory) / दूषनारि (enemy of Dushana) / खरारि (enemy of Khara) / मर्दन (crusher) / निसाचर (night-wanderers, demons) / धारि (bearing) / यह (this) / दुष्ट (wicked one) / मारेउ (killed) / नाथ (Lord) / भए (became) / देव (radiant beings) / सकल (all) / नाथ (protected, having a lord)
ramacharitamanas::5214.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5214.essence: True victory is the safety that follows the end of harm.
ramacharitamanas::5214.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who destroys evil forces and protects everyone who is vulnerable.
ramacharitamanas::5214.simple_insight: Real strength is not domination; it is making others feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::5214.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the demon forces are crushed, the praise rises like a victory hymn. Ram is hailed as the destroyer of Khara and Dushana, the one whose killing of the wicked restores safety to all the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::5214.modern_relevance: You step in when a toxic person is humiliating everyone in the room. The room relaxes the moment the harm stops. That is the kind of protection this verse celebrates.
ramacharitamanas::5214.insight: It shifts power from aggression to guardianship: strength is measured by the safety it creates.

ramacharitamanas::5215.verse_sanskrit: जय हरन धरनी भार। महिमा उदार अपार॥ जय रावनारि कृपाल। किए जातुधान बिहाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::5215.verse_hindi: हे भूमि का भार हरने वाले! हे अपार श्रेष्ठ महिमावाले! आपकी जय हो। हे रावण के शत्रु! हे कृपालु! आपकी जय हो। आपने राक्षसों को बेहाल (तहस-नहस) कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5215.english_translation: Victory to the remover of the earth's burden, whose glory is vast and limitless. Victory to the enemy of Ravana, the compassionate one, who has left the demon hosts reeling.
ramacharitamanas::5215.translation_literal: जय (victory) / हरन (remover) / धरनी (earth) / भार (burden) / महिमा (glory) / उदार (vast, noble) / अपार (limitless) / जय (victory) / रावनारि (enemy of Ravana) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / किए (made) / जातुधान (demons) / बिहाल (distressed, reeling)
ramacharitamanas::5215.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5215.essence: True power relieves burden, it does not merely defeat enemies.
ramacharitamanas::5215.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who lifts the world's burden, destroys evil, and shows compassion while overpowering the forces of chaos.
ramacharitamanas::5215.simple_insight: Strength and kindness are not opposites when they come from the right center.
ramacharitamanas::5215.detailed_meaning: In the war at Lanka, the victory hymns keep rising around Ram after Ravana's forces are crushed. This verse joins that chorus, praising Ram as the compassionate remover of the world's burden and the one who has driven the demon hosts into helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::5215.modern_relevance: After a long fight, you finally shut the laptop and realise the whole team can breathe because you held the line. Relief and gratitude meet in the same moment.
ramacharitamanas::5215.insight: It shifts attention from raw victory to the deeper relief that comes when destructive pressure is lifted.

ramacharitamanas::5216.verse_sanskrit: लंकेस अति बल गर्ब। किए बस्य सुर गंधर्ब॥ मुनि सिद्ध नर खग नाग। हठि पं सब कें लाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::5216.verse_hindi: लंकापति रावण को अपने बल का बहुत घमंड था। उसने देवता और गंधर्व सभी को अपने वश में कर लिया था और वह मुनि, सिद्ध, मनुष्य, पक्षी और नाग आदि सभी के हठपूर्वक (हाथ धोकर) पीछे पड़ गया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::5216.english_translation: Lanka's lord was swollen with pride and had brought gods and celestial beings under his control. He relentlessly harassed sages, perfected beings, humans, birds, and serpents.
ramacharitamanas::5216.translation_literal: लंकेस (lord of Lanka) / अति (very) / बल (strength) / गर्ब (pride) / किए (made) / बस्य (subdued) / सुर (gods) / गंधर्ब (celestial singers)॥ / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / नर (humans) / खग (birds) / नाग (serpents) / हठि (with force) / पं (all) / सब (all) / कें (to) / लाग (attached, harassed)॥
ramacharitamanas::5216.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5216.essence: Pride makes power violent long before it falls.
ramacharitamanas::5216.simple_meaning: Ravana was arrogant, powerful, and oppressive. He dominated even celestial beings and terrorized every kind of living being.
ramacharitamanas::5216.simple_insight: Unchecked pride turns strength into cruelty, and power into a burden for everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::5216.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana stands at the height of power, but his greatness has curdled into arrogance. He has subdued heavenly beings and bullied sages, humans, birds, and serpents. The next verse answers this with the justice that finally reaches him.
ramacharitamanas::5216.modern_relevance: A leader who silences criticism, crushes smaller voices, and treats fear as respect may look untouchable for a while. But that kind of power always exposes itself.
ramacharitamanas::5216.insight: It frames domination as a warning sign, not a triumph, and prepares the mind to expect consequences.

ramacharitamanas::5217.verse_sanskrit: परद्रोह रत अति दुष्ट। पायो सो फलु पापिष्ट॥ अब सुनहु दीन दयाल। राजीव नयन बिसाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::5217.verse_hindi: वह दूसरों से द्रोह करने में तत्पर और अत्यंत दुष्ट था। उस पापी ने वैसा ही फल पाया। अब हे दीनों पर दया करने वाले! हे कमल के समान विशाल नेत्रों वाले! सुनिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5217.english_translation: He was eager to harm others and utterly wicked. That sinner has received the fruit of his own deeds. Now listen, O compassionate one to the humble, O wide-eyed one with lotus-like eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5217.translation_literal: परद्रोह (harm to others) / रत (attached) / अति (very) / दुष्ट (wicked) / पायो (received) / सो (that) / फलु (fruit) / पापिष्ट (most sinful) / अब (now) / सुनहु (listen) / दीनदयाल (compassionate to the humble) / राजीव नयन (lotus-eyed) / बिसाल (wide)
ramacharitamanas::5217.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5217.essence: Harm ripens into its own consequence, yet mercy is still the final appeal.
ramacharitamanas::5217.simple_meaning: Ravana is condemned as deeply harmful and wicked, and his suffering is presented as the result of his own actions. The verse then turns in prayer to Ram, asking the compassionate, wide-eyed Lord to listen.
ramacharitamanas::5217.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that evil is not random, and comfort in turning to mercy after judgment.
ramacharitamanas::5217.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's pride and violence have reached their end in Lanka, the narrator names the moral cause plainly: he harmed others and reaped the result. The verse then shifts from judgment to prayer, addressing Ram as the compassionate witness who can hear the fallen.
ramacharitamanas::5217.modern_relevance: You watch someone sabotage every relationship, then act shocked when everything collapses. This verse says the damage was never mysterious — and even then, mercy is still worth calling on.
ramacharitamanas::5217.insight: It shifts the mind from outrage alone to moral seeing: actions carry their own return, and compassion is still available.

ramacharitamanas::5218.verse_sanskrit: मोहि रहा अति अभिमान। नहिं कोउ मोहि समान॥ अब देखि प्रभु पद कंज। गत मान प्रद दुख पुंज ॥
ramacharitamanas::5218.verse_hindi: मुझे अत्यंत अभिमान था कि मेरे समान कोई नहीं है, पर अब प्रभु (आप) के चरण कमलों के दर्शन करने से दु:ख समूह का देने वाला मेरा वह अभिमान जाता रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5218.english_translation: I was filled with pride, thinking no one was equal to me. But now, seeing the lotus feet of the Lord, that heap of sorrow called pride has gone.
ramacharitamanas::5218.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / रहा (remained) / अति (very) / अभिमान (pride) / नहिं (not) / कोउ (anyone) / मोहि (to me) / समान (equal) / अब (now) / देखि (seeing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पद कंज (lotus feet) / गत (gone) / मान (pride) / प्रद (giver) / दुख पुंज (heap of sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::5218.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5218.essence: Seeing what is greater than you ends the ego's spell.
ramacharitamanas::5218.simple_meaning: Ravana admits that his arrogance made him think no one was equal to him, but seeing Ram's feet has destroyed that pride.
ramacharitamanas::5218.simple_insight: Real seeing softens the ego. What looked like power can vanish the moment you meet something greater.
ramacharitamanas::5218.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands defeated in Lanka and speaks with a broken certainty. The king who once believed himself unmatched now sees Ram's lotus feet and recognises that his pride was only a burden. This confession marks the collapse of ego before divine presence.
ramacharitamanas::5218.modern_relevance: You walk into the room certain you already know the answer, then one honest conversation makes your certainty look small. The humbling is painful, but it frees you.
ramacharitamanas::5218.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to clear seeing, where pride can no longer hide the truth.

ramacharitamanas::5219.verse_sanskrit: कोउ ब्रह्म निर्गुन ध्याव। अब्यक्त जेहि श्रुति गाव॥ मोहि भाव कोसल भूप। श्रीराम सगुन सरूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::5219.verse_hindi: कोई उन निर्गुन ब्रह्म का ध्यान करते हैं जिन्हें वेद अव्यक्त (निराकार) कहते हैं। परंतु हे रामजी! मुझे तो आपका यह सगुण कोसलराज-स्वरूप ही प्रिय लगता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5219.english_translation: Some meditate on the formless Brahman, which the Vedas call unmanifest. But to me, O Ram, your embodied form as the king of Kosala is dear.
ramacharitamanas::5219.translation_literal: कोउ (some) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / निर्गुन (without qualities, formless) / ध्याव (meditate) / अब्यक्त (unmanifest) / जेहि (which) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाव (sing) / मोहि (to me) / भाव (is pleasing/dear) / कोसल भूप (king of Kosala) / श्रीराम (Sri Ram) / सगुन (with qualities, embodied form) / सरूप (having the form)
ramacharitamanas::5219.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5219.essence: The heart chooses the divine it can actually love.
ramacharitamanas::5219.simple_meaning: Ravana admits that some people seek the formless absolute, but he prefers Ram's personal, visible form.
ramacharitamanas::5219.simple_insight: The heart often reaches more easily for what it can love directly.
ramacharitamanas::5219.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's pride is collapsing. After boasting that no one equals him, he suddenly speaks with a strange honesty: some meditate on the unmanifest, but he prefers Ram's radiant form. The verse turns his defeat into an unexpected confession of bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::5219.modern_relevance: You can read a thousand ideas about the ultimate reality, but your heart may still bow to one face, one name, one presence that feels real enough to love.
ramacharitamanas::5219.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract idea to living presence.

ramacharitamanas::5220.verse_sanskrit: बै देहि अनुज समेत। मम हृदयँ करहु निकेत॥ मोहि जानिऐ िनज दास। दे भक्ति रमानिवास ॥
ramacharitamanas::5220.verse_hindi: श्रीजानकीजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित मेरे हृदय में अपना घर बनाइए। हे रमानिवास! मुझे अपना दास समझिए और अपनी भक्ति दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5220.english_translation: O Ram, live in my heart together with Janaki and your younger brother. O Raminivasa, know me as your servant and grant me devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5220.translation_literal: बै देहि (place) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / मम (my) / हृदयँ (heart) / करहु (make) / निकेत (dwelling) / मोहि (me) / जानिऐ (know) / निज (own) / दास (servant) / दे (give) / भक्ति (devotion) / रमानिवास (abode of Lakshmi/Ram)
ramacharitamanas::5220.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::5220.essence: Pride ends when the heart asks to become Ram's home.
ramacharitamanas::5220.simple_meaning: Ravana asks Ram to live in his heart with Sita and Lakshman, to accept him as a servant, and to give him devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5220.simple_insight: Real closeness begins when pride drops and the heart asks to belong.
ramacharitamanas::5220.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's pride breaks, he stands before Ram in surrender. He no longer asks for victory or status. Instead, he begs Ram to dwell in his heart with Sita and Lakshman, to accept him as a servant, and to grant devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5220.modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally stop defending yourself and say, 'I just want this relationship to be whole again.' That is the turn this verse makes.
ramacharitamanas::5220.insight: It shifts the mind from self-assertion to loving surrender and inner belonging.

ramacharitamanas::5221.verse_sanskrit: दे भक्ति रमानिवास त्रास हरन सरन सुखदायकं। सुख धाम राम नमामि काम अनेक छबि रघुनायकं॥ सुर बृंद रंजन द्वंद भंजन मनुजतनु अतुलितबलं। ब्रह्मादि संकर सेब्य राम नमामि करुना कोमलं॥
ramacharitamanas::5221.verse_hindi: हे रमानिवास! हे शरणागत के भय को हरने वाले और उसे सब प्रकार का सुख देने वाले! मुझे अपनी भक्ति दीजिए। हे सुख के धाम! हे अनेकों कामदेवों की छबिवाले रघुकुल के स्वामी श्रीरामचंद्रजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। हे देवसमूह को आनंद देने वाले, (जन्म-मृत्यु, हर्ष-विषाद, सुख-दु:ख आदि) द्वंद्वों के नाश करने वाले, मनुष्य शरीरधारी, अतुलनीय बलवाले, ब्रह्मा और शिव आदि से सेवनीय, करुणा से कोमल श्रीरामजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ।
ramacharitamanas::5221.english_translation: O Ram, dwelling in hearts, remover of fear, giver of refuge and joy, grant me devotion. O abode of bliss, Lord of Raghu, beautiful beyond countless forms, I bow to you. You delight the hosts of radiant beings, break all dualities, wear a human body, possess immeasurable strength, are served by Brahma and Shiva, and are tender with compassion. I bow to you.
ramacharitamanas::5221.translation_literal: दे (grant) / भक्ति (devotion) / रमानिवास (dwelling of Lakshmi; Ram) / त्रास (fear) / हरन (removing) / सरन (refuge) / सुखदायकं (giving joy) / सुख (bliss) / धाम (abode) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow) / काम (desire) / अनेक (many) / छबि (forms / beauty) / रघुनायकं (Lord of Raghu)॥ / सुर (radiant beings) / बृंद (host) / रंजन (delighting) / द्वंद (dualities) / भंजन (breaking) / मनुजतनु (human body) / अतुलितबलं (immeasurable strength) / ब्रह्मादि (Brahma and others) / संकर (Shiva) / सेब्य (served) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow) / करुना (compassion) / कोमलं (tender)
ramacharitamanas::5221.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5221.essence: Devotion becomes refuge when fear has nowhere left to stand.
ramacharitamanas::5221.simple_meaning: Ram is the one who removes fear, gives refuge, and brings joy. He is praised as beautiful, powerful, compassionate, and worthy of worship by even the highest beings.
ramacharitamanas::5221.simple_insight: You do not have to carry fear alone; devotion can become shelter.
ramacharitamanas::5221.detailed_meaning: Hanuman’s prayer in Lanka reaches its peak here. After asking Ram to dwell in his heart, he pours out praise: Ram is the refuge of the frightened, the giver of joy, the destroyer of inner conflict, and the compassionate one served by Brahma and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::5221.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital corridor, trying not to panic while waiting for news. This verse speaks to the part of you that wants more than reassurance — it wants refuge, steadiness, and a presence strong enough to hold fear.
ramacharitamanas::5221.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual praise to total inner refuge in Ram.

ramacharitamanas::5222.verse_sanskrit: दोहा - अब करि कृपा बिलोकि मोहि आयसु देहु कृपाल। काह करौं सुनि प्रिय बचन बोले दीनदयाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::5222.verse_hindi: हे कृपालु! अब मेरी ओर कृपा करके (कृपा दृष्टि से) देखकर आज्ञा दीजिए कि मैं क्या (सेवा) करूँ! इंद्र के ये प्रिय वचन सुनकर दीनदयालु श्रीरामजी बोले ॥ चौपाई
ramacharitamanas::5222.english_translation: “O merciful one, now look upon me with grace and tell me what service I should do.” Hearing these dear words, the compassionate Lord replied.
ramacharitamanas::5222.translation_literal: अब (now) / करि (doing) / कृपा (grace) / बिलोकि (looking upon) / मोहि (me) / आयसु (command) / देहु (give) / कृपाल (merciful one) / काह (what) / करौं (should I do) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / बोले (spoke) / दीनदयाल (compassionate Lord)
ramacharitamanas::5222.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5222.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks Ram for permission to serve and to be told what to do next. Ram, moved by those loving words, answers with compassion.
ramacharitamanas::5222.simple_insight: True devotion waits for direction, not applause.
ramacharitamanas::5222.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman has already found Sita and delivered Ram’s message. Now he stands before Ram with complete humility, asking for one more command. The moment shows pure service: even after victory, Hanuman wants only to know what Ram desires next.
ramacharitamanas::5222.modern_relevance: You finish a hard task and resist the urge to announce yourself. Instead, you ask, “What would help most now?” That is Hanuman’s kind of strength.
ramacharitamanas::5222.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to responsive service.

ramacharitamanas::5223.verse_sanskrit: सुन सुरपति कपि भालु हमारे। परे भूमि निसिचरन्हि जे मारे॥ मम हित लागि तजे इन्ह प्राना। सकल जिआउ सुरेस सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5223.verse_hindi: हे देवराज! सुनो, हमारे वानर-भालू, जिन्हें निशाचरों ने मार डाला है, पृथ्वी पर पड़े हैं। इन्होंने मेरे हित के लिए अपने प्राण त्याग दिए। हे सुजान देवराज! इन सबको जिला दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5223.english_translation: O lord of the gods, listen: our monkeys and bears lie on the ground, slain by the demons. They gave up their lives for my sake. O wise lord of the gods, bring all of them back to life.
ramacharitamanas::5223.translation_literal: सुन (listen) / सुरपति (lord of the gods) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / हमारे (our) / परे (fallen) / भूमि (on the ground) / निसिचरन्हि (by the demons) / जे (who) / मारे (were killed)॥ / मम (my) / हित (for the sake) / लागि (for) / तजे (gave up) / इन्ह (these) / प्राना (lives) / सकल (all) / जिआउ (bring back to life) / सुरेस (lord of the gods) / सुजाना (wise one)॥
ramacharitamanas::5223.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5223.essence: Ram’s victory includes the lives of those who fought for him.
ramacharitamanas::5223.simple_meaning: Ram asks Indra to revive the monkeys and bears who died fighting for him.
ramacharitamanas::5223.simple_insight: True leadership remembers every sacrifice and asks for life to return where loyalty was given.
ramacharitamanas::5223.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Lanka, Ram sees his monkey and bear allies lying dead after fighting the demons for his cause. He turns to Indra, not in triumph, but in care, asking that every fallen helper be restored to life.
ramacharitamanas::5223.modern_relevance: You watch teammates collapse after carrying your project across the finish line. Before celebrating, you notice who paid the hidden cost and want them whole again.
ramacharitamanas::5223.insight: It shifts victory from conquest to responsibility for those who made it possible.

ramacharitamanas::5224.verse_sanskrit: सुनु खगेस प्रभु कै यह बानी। अति अगाध जानहिं मुनि ग्यानी॥ प्रभु सक त्रिभुअन मारि जिआई। केवल सक्रहि दीन्हि बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5224.verse_hindi: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं -) हे गरुड़! सुनिए प्रभु के ये वचन अत्यंत गहन (गूढ़) हैं। ज्ञानी मुनि ही इन्हें जान सकते हैं। प्रभु श्रीरामजी त्रिलोकी को मारकर जिला सकते हैं। यहाँ तो उन्होंने केवल इंद्र को बड़ाई दी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5224.english_translation: Listen, king of birds: this statement of the Lord is very profound. Only sages who truly know can understand it. Lord Ram can destroy and restore the three worlds, yet here he has only granted Indra honor.
ramacharitamanas::5224.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / खगेस (king of birds) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कै (of) / यह (this) / बानी (speech) / अति (very) / अगाध (deep) / जानहिं (know) / मुनि (sages) / ग्यानी (wise) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सक (able) / त्रिभुअन (three worlds) / मारि (destroying) / जिआई (restoring to life) / केवल (only) / सक्रहि (to Indra) / दीन्हि (gave) / बड़ाई (honor)
ramacharitamanas::5224.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::5224.essence: True power often appears as restraint, not display.
ramacharitamanas::5224.simple_meaning: Ram's words are very deep, and only wise sages can understand them. He can destroy and restore the three worlds, yet here he simply gave Indra honor.
ramacharitamanas::5224.simple_insight: Some truths cannot be grasped by surface reading; humility and clear seeing are needed.
ramacharitamanas::5224.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's aftermath, Kak Bhushundi speaks to Garuda about Ram's hidden greatness. Ram has the power over all three worlds, yet he chooses a small, gracious act instead of displaying force. That contrast is what only the wise can understand.
ramacharitamanas::5224.modern_relevance: You read a calm reply in a tense group chat and think it means nothing. Later you realise it was the most powerful response in the room.
ramacharitamanas::5224.insight: It trains you to look past obvious force and recognise quiet greatness.

ramacharitamanas::5225.verse_sanskrit: सुधा बरषि कपि भालु जियाए। हरषि उठे सब प्रभु पहिं आए॥ सुधाबृष्टि भै दुहु दल ऊपर। जिए भालु कपि नहिं रजनीचर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5225.verse_hindi: इंद्र ने अमृत बरसाकर वानर-भालुओं को जिला दिया। सब हर्षित होकर उठे और प्रभु के पास आए। अमृत की वर्षा दोनों ही दलों पर हुई। पर रीछ-वानर ही जीवित हुए, राक्षस नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5225.english_translation: Indra showered nectar and brought the monkeys and bears back to life. Everyone rose in joy and came before the Lord. The nectar fell on both armies, but only the bears and monkeys lived; the demons did not.
ramacharitamanas::5225.translation_literal: सुधा (nectar) / बरषि (showering) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / जियाए (brought to life) / हरषि (joyfully) / उठे (rose) / सब (all) / प्रभु (Lord) / पहिं (to) / आए (came)॥ / सुधाबृष्टि (nectar-rain) / भै (became) / दुहु (both) / दल (armies) / ऊपर (upon) / जिए (lived) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / नहिं (not) / रजनीचर (demons)
ramacharitamanas::5225.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5225.essence: The same grace revives the receptive and passes over the closed.
ramacharitamanas::5225.simple_meaning: Indra rains nectar to revive the monkey and bear warriors. The same nectar falls on both sides, but only the righteous fighters return to life.
ramacharitamanas::5225.simple_insight: What restores life for one side cannot save the side that stood against dharma.
ramacharitamanas::5225.detailed_meaning: After the war's devastation, Indra sends nectar over the battlefield. The fallen monkey and bear warriors rise and hurry to Ram. The demons remain dead, and the next verse explains why: their minds had already turned toward Ram at the end.
ramacharitamanas::5225.modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, two people hear the same apology. One softens and returns; the other stays closed. The same words do not land the same way in every heart.
ramacharitamanas::5225.insight: It shifts attention from the outer event to the inner state that receives it.

ramacharitamanas::5226.verse_sanskrit: रामाकार भए तिन्ह के मन। मुक्त भए छूट भव बंधन॥ सुर अंसिक सब कपि अरु रीछा। जिए सकल रघुपति कीं ईछा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5226.verse_hindi: क्योंकि राक्षस के मन तो मरते समय रामाकार हो गए थे। अत: वे मुक्त हो गए, उनके भवबंधन छूट गए। किंतु वानर और भालू तो सब देवांश (भगवान् की लीला के परिकर) थे। इसलिए वे सब श्रीरघुनाथजी की इच्छा से जीवित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5226.english_translation: Their minds took on Ram's form, and they were freed from the bonds of becoming. The monkeys and bears were all sparks of the divine, and all lived by Raghupati's will.
ramacharitamanas::5226.translation_literal: रामाकार (having Ram's form) / भए (became) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / मन (minds) / मुक्त (freed) / भए (became) / छूट (released) / भव (worldly becoming) / बंधन (bondage) ॥ / सुर (divine beings) / अंसिक (spark-like portions) / सब (all) / कपि (monkeys) / अरु (and) / रीछा (bears) / जिए (lived) / सकल (all) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu line) / कीं (of) / ईछा (will) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5226.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::5226.essence: Ram-filled awareness ends bondage, even at the edge of death.
ramacharitamanas::5226.simple_meaning: A mind filled with Ram is freed from worldly bondage. The monkeys and bears survived because they were divine sparks living by Ram's will.
ramacharitamanas::5226.simple_insight: What you hold in mind shapes whether you feel bound or free.
ramacharitamanas::5226.detailed_meaning: Kak Bhushundi is explaining to Garuda what happened after the war. The slain demons were freed because their minds turned toward Ram at death. Even the monkey and bear warriors lived on, because they were divine sparks moved entirely by Ram's will.
ramacharitamanas::5226.modern_relevance: At the end of a brutal argument, something in you finally softens and the whole fight loses its grip. The mind that turns toward Ram stops living like a prisoner.
ramacharitamanas::5226.insight: It shifts attention from survival in the struggle to freedom through remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::5227.verse_sanskrit: राम सरिस को दीन हितकारी। कीन्हे मुकुत निसाचर झारी॥ खल मल धाम काम रत रावन। गति पाई जो मुनिबर पाव न ॥
ramacharitamanas::5227.verse_hindi: श्रीरामचंद्रजी के समान दीनों का हित करने वाला कौन है? जिन्होंने सारे राक्षसों को मुक्त कर दिया! दुष्ट, पापों के घर और कामी रावण ने भी वह गति पाई जिसे श्रेष्ठ मुनि भी नहीं पाते ॥ दोहा -
ramacharitamanas::5227.english_translation: Who is as kind to the lowly as Ram? He freed even the demons. Ravana, a house of vice and desire, attained a state that great sages do not reach.
ramacharitamanas::5227.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सरिस (like) / को (who) / दीन (the lowly) / हितकारी (benefactor) / कीन्हे (made) / मुकुत (free) / निसाचर (demons) / झारी (all together) / खल (wicked) / मल (filth) / धाम (abode) / काम (desire) / रत (attached) / रावन (Ravana) / गति (state) / पाई (attained) / जो (which) / मुनिबर (great sages) / पाव (do not get) / न (not)
ramacharitamanas::5227.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5227.essence: Ram's grace reaches even those who seem beyond redemption.
ramacharitamanas::5227.simple_meaning: Ram alone brings real benefit to the fallen. Even Ravana, despite his corruption and desire, reached a state beyond what great sages attain.
ramacharitamanas::5227.simple_insight: No one is beyond grace; even the most ruined life can be transformed.
ramacharitamanas::5227.detailed_meaning: After the war, the battlefield is quiet and the dead are being released from their old forms. Tulsidas pauses to praise Ram: he does not just defeat enemies, he grants them a higher fate. Even Ravana, in spite of his darkness, receives a result rare even for sages.
ramacharitamanas::5227.modern_relevance: You look at someone who has wrecked every chance given to them, and still a part of you wonders whether change is possible. This verse says the deepest kindness can reach even there.
ramacharitamanas::5227.insight: It shifts you from judging people as finished to seeing transformation as still possible.

ramacharitamanas::5228.verse_sanskrit: सुमन बरषि सब सुर चले चढ़ि चढ़ि रुचिर बिमान। देखि सुअवसर प्रभु पहिं आयउ संभु सुजान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5228.verse_hindi: फूलों की वर्षा करके सब देवता सुंदर विमानों पर चढ़-चढ़कर चले। तब सुअवसर जानकार सुजान शिवजी प्रभु श्रीरामचंद्रजी के पास आए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5228.english_translation: The gods showered flowers and departed in beautiful flying chariots. Seeing the right moment, wise Shiva came to Lord Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5228.translation_literal: सुमन (flowers) / बरषि (showering) / सब (all) / सुर (gods) / चले (went) / चढ़ि चढ़ि (rising up) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बिमान (flying chariots) / देखि (seeing) / सुअवसर (the right moment) / प्रभु (Lord) / पहिं (to) / आयउ (came) / संभु (Shiva) / सुजान (wise)
ramacharitamanas::5228.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5228.essence: The celebration ends, and the real meeting begins.
ramacharitamanas::5228.simple_meaning: The gods leave after showering flowers, and Shiva approaches Ram at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::5228.simple_insight: Even in celebration, the right meeting happens by perfect timing.
ramacharitamanas::5228.detailed_meaning: After the battle’s turning point, the gods descend in joy, shower flowers, and return to their celestial homes. Then Shiva, seeing the fitting moment, approaches Ram. The verse is a scene transition, not the main teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::5228.modern_relevance: The crowd has moved on, the applause is fading, and one person still waits for the right moment to speak. That quiet timing changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::5228.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the precise moment a deeper conversation can begin.

ramacharitamanas::5229.verse_sanskrit: परम प्रीति कर जोरि जुग नलिन नयन भरि बारि। पुलकित तन गदगद गिराँ बिनय करत त्रिपुरारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5229.verse_hindi: और परम प्रेम से दोनों हाथ जोड़कर, कमल के समान नेत्रों में जल भरकर, पुलकित शरीर और गद् गद् वाणी से त्रिपुरारी शिवजी विनती करने लगे - ॥ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5229.english_translation: With deepest love, Shiva joined his hands. Tears filled his lotus eyes, his body thrilled, and his voice choked as Tripurari began to pray.
ramacharitamanas::5229.translation_literal: परम (supreme) / प्रीति (love) / कर (doing) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / नलिन (lotus) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (filling) / बारि (water/tears) / पुलकित (thrilled) / तन (body) / गदगद (choked) / गिराँ (with words/voice) / बिनय (prayer) / करत (doing) / त्रिपुरारि (destroyer of the three cities)
ramacharitamanas::5229.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5229.essence: True devotion makes pride dissolve into tears.
ramacharitamanas::5229.simple_meaning: Shiva stands before Ram overwhelmed with love, tears in his eyes, body trembling, and voice breaking as he begins to pray.
ramacharitamanas::5229.simple_insight: Love can leave even the greatest heart trembling and wordless.
ramacharitamanas::5229.detailed_meaning: After the gods celebrate Ram's victory, Shiva comes forward in Lanka and bows with tears and trembling. This verse shows not a warrior speaking, but the greatest devotee approaching Ram in complete humility before his prayer begins.
ramacharitamanas::5229.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone who changed your life, and all your rehearsed words disappear. What comes out instead is raw gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::5229.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to surrender, where feeling becomes more honest than eloquence.

ramacharitamanas::5230.verse_sanskrit: मामभिरक्षय रघुकुल नायक। धृत बर चाप रुचिर कर सायक॥ मोह महा घन पटल प्रभंजन। संसय बिपिन अनल सुर रंजन ॥
ramacharitamanas::5230.verse_hindi: हे रघुकुल के स्वामी! सुंदर हाथों में श्रेष्ठ धनुष और सुंदर बाण धारण किए हुए आप मेरी रक्षा कीजिए। आप महामोहरूपी मेघसमूह के (उड़ाने के) लिए प्रचंड पवन हैं, संशयरूपी वन के (भस्म करने के) लिए अग्नि हैं और देवताओं को आनंद देने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5230.english_translation: O Lord of the Raghu line, protect me. You hold the splendid bow and arrows in your beautiful hands. You are the fierce wind that scatters the great cloud of delusion, the fire that burns the forest of doubt, and the delight of the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::5230.translation_literal: मामभिरक्षय (protect me) / रघुकुल नायक (leader of the Raghu line) / धृत (held) / बर (excellent) / चाप (bow) / रुचिर (beautiful) / कर (hands) / सायक (arrows) / मोह (delusion) / महा घन पटल (great cloud mass) / प्रभंजन (scattering wind) / संसय (doubt) / बिपिन (forest) / अनल (fire) / सुर रंजन (delight of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::5230.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5230.essence: Ram is the refuge that destroys confusion at its root.
ramacharitamanas::5230.simple_meaning: Shiva asks Ram to protect him, praising Ram as the one who destroys delusion and doubt.
ramacharitamanas::5230.simple_insight: It feels safe to lean on a presence that can cut through confusion instantly.
ramacharitamanas::5230.detailed_meaning: Shiva has come to Ram after the war, bowing with deep love. He asks Ram to protect him, describing Ram as the one who carries the bow and arrows, clears away delusion, burns doubt, and gives joy even to the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::5230.modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor, rereading the same message, unable to stop your mind from spinning. What you need is not more noise, but something steady enough to cut through fear.
ramacharitamanas::5230.insight: It shifts you from self-protection through control to refuge through surrender.

ramacharitamanas::5231.verse_sanskrit: अगुन सगुन गुन मंदिर सुंदर। भ्रम तम प्रबल प्रताप दिवाकर॥ काम क्रोध मद गज पंचानन। बसहु निरंतर जन मन कानन ॥
ramacharitamanas::5231.verse_hindi: आप निर्गुण, सगुण, दिव्य गुणों के धाम और परम सुंदर हैं। भ्रमरूपी अंधकार के (नाश के) लिए प्रबल प्रतापी सूर्य हैं। काम, क्रोध और मदरूपी हाथियों के (वध के) लिए सिंह के समान आप इस सेवक के मनरूपी वन में निरंतर वास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5231.english_translation: You are beyond attributes and with attributes: a beautiful abode of virtues. You are a mighty sun that destroys the deep darkness of confusion. Remain forever in this servant’s forest of mind, like a lion against the elephants of desire, anger, and pride.
ramacharitamanas::5231.translation_literal: अगुन (without attributes) / सगुन (with attributes) / गुन (virtues) / मंदिर (abode) / सुंदर (beautiful) / भ्रम (confusion) / तम (darkness) / प्रबल (mighty) / प्रताप (radiance/power) / दिवाकर (sun) / काम (desire) / क्रोध (anger) / मद (pride) / गज (elephants) / पंचानन (lion-faced one) / बसहु (dwell) / निरंतर (continually) / जन (servant) / मन (mind) / कानन (forest)
ramacharitamanas::5231.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5231.essence: Ram is both beyond form and the power that clears the mind.
ramacharitamanas::5231.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as beyond form and with form, full of virtues, and powerful enough to destroy confusion, desire, anger, and pride. The speaker asks Ram to stay in the mind forever.
ramacharitamanas::5231.simple_insight: There is relief in inviting a higher presence into the mind instead of fighting every inner storm alone.
ramacharitamanas::5231.detailed_meaning: Shiva is praising Ram while praying for his constant presence. Ram is described as both beyond qualities and full of qualities, like sunlight against confusion and a lion against the elephants of desire, anger, and pride. The prayer is for inner protection, not just praise.
ramacharitamanas::5231.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a harsh argument, replaying every line and feeling your temper rise again. This verse sounds like the prayer to make before the spiral takes over: let something steadier live in the mind.
ramacharitamanas::5231.insight: It shifts the mind from self-managed struggle to devotional inner refuge.

ramacharitamanas::5232.verse_sanskrit: बिषय मनोरथ पुंज कुंज बन। प्रबल तुषार उदार पार मन॥ भव बारिधि मंदर परमं दर। बारय तारय संसृति दुस्तर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5232.verse_hindi: विषयकामनाओं के समूह रूपी कमलवन के (नाश के) लिए आप प्रबल पाला हैं, आप उदार और मन से परे हैं। भवसागर (को मथने) के लिए आप मंदराचल पर्वत हैं। आप हमारे परम भय को दूर कीजिए और हमें दुस्तर संसार सागर से पार कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5232.english_translation: For the cluster of desire-plants, you are the fierce hail. You are generous and beyond the mind. For churning the ocean of becoming, you are the Mount Mandara. Remove our greatest fear and carry us across the hard-to-cross world-sea.
ramacharitamanas::5232.translation_literal: बिषय (sense-objects / desires) / मनोरथ (wishes) / पुंज (cluster) / कुंज (bower / grove) / बन (forest) / प्रबल (strong) / तुषार (hail / frost) / उदार (generous) / पार (beyond / across) / मन (mind) / भव (becoming / worldly existence) / बारिधि (ocean) / मंदर (Mount Mandara) / परमं (supreme / greatest) / दर (fear) / बारय (remove) / तारय (carry across) / संसृति (cycle of worldly wandering) / दुस्तर (hard to cross)
ramacharitamanas::5232.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5232.essence: Ram is the force that cools craving and carries you across fear.
ramacharitamanas::5232.simple_meaning: Ram is asked to destroy the heat of desire, calm the mind, remove fear, and carry the devotee across the hard-to-cross ocean of worldly life.
ramacharitamanas::5232.simple_insight: It brings relief: you do not have to cross every struggle by yourself.
ramacharitamanas::5232.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Lanka war, the devotee turns from battle to prayer and sees Ram as the only real help. Ram is imagined as the force that destroys craving, steadies the mind, and lifts a person over the ocean of repeated struggle.
ramacharitamanas::5232.modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a messy breakup, your mind looping through cravings and fears you cannot outthink. This verse gives you a different move: ask to be carried, not just to be tougher.
ramacharitamanas::5232.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant strain to surrendering trust in Ram's power to steady and carry you.

ramacharitamanas::5233.verse_sanskrit: स्याम गात राजीव बिलोचन। दीन बंधु प्रनतारति मोचन॥ अनुज जानकी सहित निरंतर। बसहु राम नृप मम उर अंतर॥ मुनि रंजन महि मंडल मंडन। तुलसिदास प्रभु त्रास बिखंडन॥ 4-5॥
ramacharitamanas::5233.verse_hindi: हे श्यामसुंदर-शरीर! हे कमलनयन! हे दीनबंधु! हे शरणागत को दु:ख से छुड़ाने वाले! हे राजा रामचंद्रजी! आप छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण और जानकीजी सहित निरंतर मेरे हृदय के अंदर निवास कीजिए। आप मुनियों को आनंद देने वाले, पृथ्वीमंडल के भूषण, तुलसीदास के प्रभु और भय का नाश करने वाले हैं॥ 4-5॥
ramacharitamanas::5233.english_translation: O dark-hued, lotus-eyed Ram, friend of the humble, remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge. O King Ram, stay forever in my heart, along with Lakshman and Sita. You delight sages, adorn the earth, and destroy fear, O Lord of Tulsidas.
ramacharitamanas::5233.translation_literal: स्याम गात (dark-bodied) / राजीव बिलोचन (lotus-eyed) / दीन बंधु (friend of the humble) / प्रनतारति मोचन (remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge) / अनुज (younger brother) / जानकी सहित (with Janaki) / निरंतर (always) / बसहु (reside) / राम (Ram) / नृप (king) / मम (my) / उर अंतर (within the heart) / मुनि रंजन (delighter of sages) / महि मंडल मंडन (ornament of the earth) / तुलसिदास प्रभु (Lord of Tulsidas) / त्रास बिखंडन (destroyer of fear)
ramacharitamanas::5233.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5233.essence: Ram becomes home when you ask him to stay within you.
ramacharitamanas::5233.simple_meaning: The speaker prays to Ram to live in the heart forever, together with Sita and Lakshman, and praises him as the friend of the humble and remover of fear.
ramacharitamanas::5233.simple_insight: Peace comes from making room for what protects you, not just what impresses you.
ramacharitamanas::5233.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's final stretch, Tulsidas turns from battle to prayer. He calls Ram dark-hued, lotus-eyed, and kind to the humble, then asks him to stay forever in the heart with Sita and Lakshman. The verse is a lover's invitation, not a report.
ramacharitamanas::5233.modern_relevance: After a day of noise, you finally sit alone and realize what you want most is not more control. You want one steady presence in the middle of everything that frightens you.
ramacharitamanas::5233.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration at a distance to living companionship within the heart.

ramacharitamanas::5234.verse_sanskrit: दोहा नाथ जबहिं कोसलपुरीं हो इहि तिलक तुम्हार। कृपासिंधु मैं आउब देखन चरित उदार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5234.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! जब अयोध्यापुरी में आपका राजतिलक होगा, तब हे कृपासागर! मैं आपकी उदार लीला देखने आऊँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5234.english_translation: O Lord, when your coronation takes place in Ayodhya, then, ocean of grace, I will come to witness your noble deeds.
ramacharitamanas::5234.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / जबहिं (when) / कोसलपुरीं (in Ayodhya city) / हो (will happen) / इहि (this) / तिलक (coronation) / तुम्हार (your) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / मैं (I) / आउब (will come) / देखन (to see) / चरित (deeds / conduct) / उदार (noble)
ramacharitamanas::5234.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5234.essence: Love waits for the moment goodness is publicly crowned.
ramacharitamanas::5234.simple_meaning: The speaker promises to come back and witness Ram’s coronation in Ayodhya, drawn by love and reverence for Ram’s noble life.
ramacharitamanas::5234.simple_insight: Devotion keeps returning to what it loves most.
ramacharitamanas::5234.detailed_meaning: After the war’s darkness, the speaker looks ahead to Ayodhya’s coronation and longs to see Ram’s noble conduct fulfilled in peace. This is not just a wish to attend a ceremony; it is love waiting for the rightful order to return.
ramacharitamanas::5234.modern_relevance: You keep a date in your heart for the moment someone you trust finally gets what they deserve. You want to be there, not for the event, but for them.
ramacharitamanas::5234.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of success to the joy of witnessing a loved one’s rightful fulfillment.

ramacharitamanas::5235.verse_sanskrit: करि बिनती जब संभु सिधाए। तब प्रभु निकट बिभीषनु आए॥ नाइ चरन सिरु कह मृदु बानी। बिनय सुनहु प्रभु सारँगपानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5235.verse_hindi: जब शिवजी विनती करके चले गए, तब विभीषणजी प्रभु के पास आए और चरणों में सिर नवाकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- हे शार्गं धनुष के धारण करने वाले प्रभो! मेरी विनती सुनिए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5235.english_translation: After Shiva had made his prayer and departed, Vibhishana came near the Lord. Bowing his head at the Lord's feet, he spoke softly: "Listen to my request, Lord who holds the Saranga bow."
ramacharitamanas::5235.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिनती (prayer, request) / जब (when) / संभु (Shiva) / सिधाए (departed) / तब (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / निकट (near) / बिभीषनु (Vibhishana) / आए (came) ॥ / नाइ (bowing) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / कह (said) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / बिनय (humble request) / सुनहु (listen) / प्रभु (Lord) / सारँगपानी (bow-holder, Saranga-handed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5235.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5235.essence: Humility is the door through which surrender enters.
ramacharitamanas::5235.simple_meaning: After Shiva leaves, Vibhishana approaches Ram with bowed head and gentle words, asking Him to listen to his plea.
ramacharitamanas::5235.simple_insight: There is peace in coming honestly, without posture or force.
ramacharitamanas::5235.detailed_meaning: Shiva has already offered his prayer and gone. Now Vibhishana steps forward alone before Ram, bows to His feet, and speaks with complete humility. This is the moment of surrender that opens the way for his refuge.
ramacharitamanas::5235.modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room and admit you need help, without rehearsing a polished version of the story. The truth reaches people faster when you stop protecting your image.
ramacharitamanas::5235.insight: It teaches you to approach what matters with humility first, not self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::5236.verse_sanskrit: सकुल सदल प्रभु रावन मार् यो। पावन जस त्रिभुवन विस्तार् यो॥ दीन मलीन हीन मति जाती। मो पर कृपा कीन्हि बहु भाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::5236.verse_hindi: आपने कुल और सेना सहित रावण का वध किया, त्रिभुवन में अपना पवित्र यश फैलाया और मुझ दीन, पापी, बुद्धिहीन और जातिहीन पर बहुत प्रकार से कृपा की ॥
ramacharitamanas::5236.english_translation: You destroyed Ravana and his army, spread your pure glory through the three worlds, and showed abundant grace to me, lowly, impure, foolish, and outcast.
ramacharitamanas::5236.translation_literal: सकुल (with his whole clan) / सदल (with his whole army) / प्रभु (Lord) / रावन (Ravana) / मार् यो (killed) / पावन (pure) / जस (fame) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / विस्तार् यो (spread) / दीन (humble) / मलीन (stained) / हीन (inferior) / मति (mind) / जाती (birth/status) / मो पर (on me) / कृपा (mercy) / कीन्हि (did) / बहु भाँती (in many ways)
ramacharitamanas::5236.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5236.essence: Victory becomes holy when it is joined with mercy.
ramacharitamanas::5236.simple_meaning: Ram has destroyed Ravana and his forces, and his glory now fills the three worlds. Vibhishana also says Ram has shown him many kinds of mercy despite his lowly state.
ramacharitamanas::5236.simple_insight: Real greatness is not just victory. It is the mercy that follows victory.
ramacharitamanas::5236.detailed_meaning: After Shiva leaves, Vibhishana comes forward in Lanka's ruined aftermath. He praises Ram for destroying Ravana and the army, then turns personal: the same victorious Lord has shown repeated mercy to him, a fallen outsider who has taken refuge.
ramacharitamanas::5236.modern_relevance: You finally win the argument, close the deal, or finish the hard fight — and then someone weaker is still waiting for your kindness. This verse reminds you that victory is incomplete without mercy.
ramacharitamanas::5236.insight: It shifts attention from conquest to grace, showing that true power reveals itself in how it treats the vulnerable.

ramacharitamanas::5237.verse_sanskrit: अब जन गृह पुनीत प्रभु कीजे। मज्जन करिअ समर श्रम छीजे॥ देखि कोस मंदिर संपदा। देहु कृपाल कपिन्ह कहुँ मुदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5237.verse_hindi: अब हे प्रभु! इस दास के घर को पवित्र कीजिए और वहाँ चलकर स्नान कीजिए, जिससे युद्ध की थकावट दूर हो जाए। हे कृपालु! खजाना, महल और सम्पत्ति का निरीक्षण कर प्रसन्नतापूर्वक वानरों को दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5237.english_translation: Now, Lord, make this home pure. Come bathe there and wash away the weariness of battle. O compassionate one, look at the treasury, palace, and wealth, and gladly give them to the monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::5237.translation_literal: अब (now) / जन (servant's) / गृह (home) / पुनीत (pure) / प्रभु (Lord) / कीजे (make) / मज्जन (bathing) / करिअ (do) / समर (battle) / श्रम (fatigue) / छीजे (wear away) / देखि (seeing) / कोस (treasury) / मंदिर (palace) / संपदा (wealth) / देहु (give) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / कपिन्ह (to the monkeys) / कहुँ (to) / मुदा (with joy)
ramacharitamanas::5237.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5237.essence: Surrender turns your home and wealth into offerings.
ramacharitamanas::5237.simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram to enter his home, bathe, rest after battle, and then gladly share Lanka's wealth with the monkey army.
ramacharitamanas::5237.simple_insight: True welcome is not just words; it becomes hospitality, rest, and generous giving.
ramacharitamanas::5237.detailed_meaning: After Ravana falls, Vibhishana stands before Ram with complete surrender. He offers his home for bathing and rest, then asks Ram to distribute Lanka's riches to the monkey warriors. Gratitude turns into service.
ramacharitamanas::5237.modern_relevance: After a long day helping someone move, you open your apartment, hand them water, and insist they eat before leaving. Care is not a speech; it becomes welcome, rest, and generosity.
ramacharitamanas::5237.insight: It shifts devotion from praise into practical hospitality and shared abundance.

ramacharitamanas::5238.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि नाथ मोहि अपनाइअ। पुनि मोहि सहित अवधपुर जाइअ॥ सुनत बचन मृदु दीनदयाला। सजल भए द्वौ नयन बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::5238.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मुझे सब प्रकार से अपना लीजिए और फिर हे प्रभो! मुझे साथ लेकर अयोध्यापुरी को पधारिए। विभीषणजी के कोमल वचन सुनते ही दीनदयालु प्रभु के दोनों विशाल नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5238.english_translation: “O Lord, take me in every way as your own, and then, O compassionate one, take me with you to the city of Ayodhya.” Hearing these gentle words from Vibhishana, the great-eyed Lord’s eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::5238.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (me) / अपनाइअ (take as your own) / पुनि (then) / मोहि (me) / सहित (together with) / अवधपुर (Ayodhya city) / जाइअ (go) / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / दीनदयाला (compassionate one) / सजल (filled with water) / भए (became) / द्वौ (both) / नयन (eyes) / बिसाला (great)
ramacharitamanas::5238.speaker: Vibhishana
ramacharitamanas::5238.essence: Surrender makes you fully accepted, and that acceptance moves the divine.
ramacharitamanas::5238.simple_meaning: Vibhishana asks Ram to accept him completely and take him to Ayodhya. Ram is so moved by his gentle surrender that tears fill his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5238.simple_insight: Real surrender doesn’t shrink you; it opens the heart on both sides.
ramacharitamanas::5238.detailed_meaning: After Ravana’s defeat in Lanka, Vibhishana comes forward not as a victor but as a supplicant. He asks Ram to claim him fully and take him to Ayodhya. Ram’s tears show how deeply surrender moves him.
ramacharitamanas::5238.modern_relevance: After a long fight with your family, you finally say, “Please just let me come home.” The relief in that sentence is bigger than pride. That is Vibhishana’s courage.
ramacharitamanas::5238.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to wholehearted belonging.

ramacharitamanas::5239.verse_sanskrit: तोर कोस गृह मोर सब सत्य बचन सुनु भ्रात। भरत दसा सुमिरत मोहि निमिष कल्प सम जात ॥
ramacharitamanas::5239.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे भाई! सुनो, तुम्हारा खजाना और घर सब मेरा ही है, यह सच बात है। पर भरत की दशा याद करके मुझे एक-एक पल कल्प के समान बीत रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5239.english_translation: “Brother, listen: your treasury and house are all truly mine. But remembering Bharat’s condition, each moment feels like an age to me.”
ramacharitamanas::5239.translation_literal: तोर (your) / कोस-गृह (treasury and house) / मोर (mine) / सब (all) / सत्य (true) / बचन (words) / सुनु (listen) / भ्रात (brother) / भरत (Bharat) / दसा (condition) / सुमिरत (remembering) / मोहि (to me) / निमिष (moment) / कल्प (aeon) / सम (like) / जात (becomes)
ramacharitamanas::5239.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5239.essence: Love owns nothing, yet another’s pain can make time unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::5239.simple_meaning: Ram says the treasury and house belong to him, but what truly weighs on him is Bharat’s suffering. Thinking of Bharat makes even a moment feel unbearably long.
ramacharitamanas::5239.simple_insight: Real love is measured less by ownership and more by how deeply another person’s pain reaches you.
ramacharitamanas::5239.detailed_meaning: After the war, Vibhishana offers hospitality and wealth. Ram answers as a brother, not a conqueror: the house and treasury are already his. Yet his mind is fixed on Bharat in Ayodhya, whose grief makes every passing moment feel like an age.
ramacharitamanas::5239.modern_relevance: You’re in a hotel lobby after a hard family call, smiling at people who think you’re fine. Your body is present, but your mind is still with the person you love who is hurting.
ramacharitamanas::5239.insight: It shifts attention from possession to relationship, showing that devotion feels another’s suffering as your own.

ramacharitamanas::5240.verse_sanskrit: तापस बेष गात कृस जपत निरंतर मोहि। देखौं बेगि सो जतनु करु सखा निहोरउँ तोहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5240.verse_hindi: तपस्वी के वेष में कृश (दुबले) शरीर से निरंतर मेरा नाम जप कर रहे हैं। हे सखा! वही उपाय करो जिससे मैं जल्दी से जल्दी उन्हें देख सकूँ। मैं तुमसे निहोरा (अनुरोध) करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5240.english_translation: In a hermit's dress, with a lean body, he keeps chanting my name without pause. O friend, find a way so I may see him soon; I beg you.
ramacharitamanas::5240.translation_literal: तापस (ascetic) / बेष (dress) / गात (body) / कृस (lean) / जपत (chanting) / निरंतर (without pause) / मोहि (me) / देखौं (may see) / बेगि (soon) / सो (that) / जतनु (means) / करु (do) / सखा (friend) / निहोरउँ (I beg) / तोहि (you)
ramacharitamanas::5240.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5240.essence: Pure devotion makes Ram long to see the devotee first.
ramacharitamanas::5240.simple_meaning: Ram speaks of someone who lives like an ascetic, thin from devotion, constantly chanting Ram's name. He asks for a way to see that devotee soon.
ramacharitamanas::5240.simple_insight: Deep love leaves a mark on the body, the breath, and the whole way a person lives.
ramacharitamanas::5240.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ram hears about the devoted figure who has taken on an ascetic form and keeps chanting his name without rest. The news moves Ram so deeply that he asks Hanuman to arrange a quick meeting.
ramacharitamanas::5240.modern_relevance: You hear that someone has kept your name in their prayers through a hard season, and suddenly everything else feels smaller. Being remembered with that kind of devotion changes how closeness feels.
ramacharitamanas::5240.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to devotion: the one who remembers with love becomes precious.

ramacharitamanas::5241.verse_sanskrit: बीतें अवधि जाउँ जौं जिअत न पावउँ बीर। सुमिरत अनुज प्रीति प्रभु पुनि पुनि पुलक सरीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5241.verse_hindi: यदि अवधि बीत जाने पर जाता हूँ तो भाई को जीता न पाऊँगा। छोटे भाई भरतजी की प्रीति का स्मरण करके प्रभु का शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5241.english_translation: If I leave after the deadline passes, I will not be able to save my brother. Remembering the love of my younger brother Bharata, the Lord's body again and again thrills with emotion.
