ramacharitamanas::5241.translation_literal: बीतें (having passed) / अवधि (the deadline, time limit) / जाउँ (I go) / जौं (if) / जिअत (alive) / न (not) / पावउँ (I may find) / बीर (brother, brave one) / सुमिरत (remembering) / अनुज (younger brother) / प्रीति (love) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पुलक (hairs standing on end, thrill) / सरीर (body)
ramacharitamanas::5241.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5241.essence: True devotion makes even Ram tremble with love.
ramacharitamanas::5241.simple_meaning: Ram says he must reach Bharata before the deadline passes, or he will not find him alive. Remembering Bharata's love makes Ram tremble with emotion.
ramacharitamanas::5241.simple_insight: Real love creates urgency, tenderness, and a living bond that even distance cannot weaken.
ramacharitamanas::5241.detailed_meaning: In Lankakand, Ram is speaking after the war, still carrying Bharata in his heart. He cannot bear the thought of delay, because Bharata's devotion is so deep that even remembering it makes Ram's body thrill.
ramacharitamanas::5241.modern_relevance: You see a message from someone who has waited patiently for your reply, and your chest tightens. Their care matters so much that delay suddenly feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::5241.insight: It shifts attention from duty alone to the emotional force of devotion that gives duty its urgency.

ramacharitamanas::5242.verse_sanskrit: करेहु कल्प भरि राजु तुम्ह मोहि सुमिरेहु मन माहिं। पुनि मम धाम पाइहहु जहाँ संत सब जाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5242.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने फिर कहा-) हे विभीषण! तुम कल्पभर राज्य करना, मन में मेरा निरंतर स्मरण करते रहना। फिर तुम मेरे उस धाम को पा जाओगे, जहाँ सब संत जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5242.english_translation: Rama said, "Rule for ages while remembering me in your heart. Then you will reach my abode, where all the holy ones go."
ramacharitamanas::5242.translation_literal: करेहु (do) / कल्प भरि (for an age) / राजु (rule) / तुम्ह (you) / मोहि (me) / सुमिरेहु (remember) / मन माहिं (in the mind) / पुनि (then) / मम (my) / धाम (abode) / पाइहहु (you will attain) / जहाँ (where) / संत (holy ones) / सब (all) / जाहिं (go)
ramacharitamanas::5242.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5242.essence: You can live fully and still be on the way home.
ramacharitamanas::5242.simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishan to keep ruling for a long time while remembering him inwardly. That remembrance leads to Ram's abode, the place reached by the holy.
ramacharitamanas::5242.simple_insight: You do not have to abandon life to stay close to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::5242.detailed_meaning: After Vibhishan surrenders in Lanka, Ram accepts him completely. Instead of asking him to renounce his new responsibility, Ram blesses him to rule well and keep remembering Ram inwardly. The reward is not status, but arrival at Ram's own abode.
ramacharitamanas::5242.modern_relevance: You are still answering emails, paying bills, and caring for family, yet part of you longs for something higher. This verse says ordinary life does not block remembrance; it can become the place where remembrance matures.
ramacharitamanas::5242.insight: It shifts devotion from withdrawal to inward continuity while living your duties.

ramacharitamanas::5243.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बिभीषन बचन राम के। हरषि गहे पद कृपाधाम के॥ बानर भालु सकल हरषाने। गहि प्रभु पद गुन बिमल बखाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::5243.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनते ही विभीषणजी ने हर्षित होकर कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए। सभी वानर-भालू हर्षित हो गए और प्रभु के चरण पकड़कर उनके निर्मल गुणों का बखान करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5243.english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, Vibhishana joyfully grasped the feet of the abode of grace. All the monkeys and bears rejoiced, took hold of the Lord's feet, and praised his pure virtues.
ramacharitamanas::5243.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / बचन (words) / राम के (of Ram) / हरषि (joyfully) / गहे (grasped) / पद (feet) / कृपाधाम के (of the abode of grace)॥ / बानर (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / सकल (all) / हरषाने (rejoiced) / गहि (taking hold) / प्रभु (Lord's) / पद (feet) / गुन (virtues) / बिमल (pure) / बखाने (praised)॥
ramacharitamanas::5243.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5243.essence: Ram's welcome turns surrender into joy.
ramacharitamanas::5243.simple_meaning: Vibhishana feels immediate joy and surrenders to Ram. The monkey and bear allies also rejoice and praise Ram's pure qualities.
ramacharitamanas::5243.simple_insight: Real relief arrives when you stop standing apart and move toward what is pure.
ramacharitamanas::5243.detailed_meaning: After Ram speaks to Vibhishana, the moment breaks open. Vibhishana falls at Ram's feet in gratitude, and the monkey and bear army celebrates too. The scene shows what Ram's welcome does: it turns fear into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5243.modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you needed, and your chest loosens before you can even explain why. Some moments heal you by making surrender feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::5243.insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling into an outward act of trust and praise.

ramacharitamanas::5244.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि विभीषन भवन सिधायो। मनि गन बसन बिमान भरायो॥ लै पुष्पक प्रभु आगें राखा। हँसि करि कृपासिंधु तब भाषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5244.verse_hindi: फिर विभीषणजी महल को गए और उन्होंने मणियों के समूहों (रत्नों) से और वस्त्रों से विमान को भर लिया। फिर उस पुष्पक विमान को लाकर प्रभु के सामने रखा। तब कृपासागर श्री रामजी ने हँसकर कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5244.english_translation: Then Vibhishana went to the palace and filled the Pushpak with jewels and garments. He brought the Pushpak aircraft before the Lord, and then the ocean of mercy smiled and spoke.
ramacharitamanas::5244.translation_literal: बहुरि (then) / विभीषन (Vibhishana) / भवन (palace) / सिधायो (went) / मनि गन (groups of jewels) / बसन (garments) / बिमान (aircraft) / भरायो (filled)॥ / लै (taking) / पुष्पक (Pushpak) / प्रभु (Lord) / आगें (in front) / राखा (placed) / हँसि (smiling) / करि (having done) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of mercy) / तब (then) / भाषा (spoke) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5244.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5244.essence: Surrender opens the door to grace.
ramacharitamanas::5244.simple_meaning: Vibhishana gathers treasures and clothing, brings the Pushpak aircraft before Ram, and Ram smiles before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::5244.simple_insight: It shows honor flowing naturally after surrender.
ramacharitamanas::5244.detailed_meaning: After Vibhishana has surrendered and Ram has accepted him, he returns to his palace, loads the Pushpak aircraft with jewels and clothes, and brings it before Ram. The verse simply sets up Ram's next gracious instruction.
ramacharitamanas::5244.modern_relevance: You finally bring what you have to offer after a hard apology, and the room softens before anyone says much. The gesture itself already changed the mood.
ramacharitamanas::5244.insight: It prepares the next act of generosity, showing that surrender is met with welcome, not suspicion.

ramacharitamanas::5245.verse_sanskrit: चढ़ि बिमान सुनु सखा बिभीषन। गगन जाइ बरषहु पट भूषन॥ नभ पर जाइ बिभीषन तबही। बरषि दिए मनि अंबर सबही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5245.verse_hindi: हे सखा विभीषण! सुनो, विमान पर चढ़कर, आकाश में जाकर वस्त्रों और गहनों को बरसा दो। तब (आज्ञा सुनते) ही विभीषणजी ने आकाश में जाकर सब मणियों और वस्त्रों को बरसा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5245.english_translation: “Friend Vibhishana, climb the flying chariot and go into the sky to shower down the clothes and ornaments.” At once, Vibhishana went up into the sky and scattered all the jewels and garments.
ramacharitamanas::5245.translation_literal: चढ़ि (having climbed) / बिमान (the flying chariot) / सुनु (listen) / सखा (friend) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / गगन (sky) / जाइ (going) / बरषहु (shower down) / पट (cloths) / भूषन (ornaments) / नभ (sky) / पर (upon) / जाइ (going) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / तबही (then) / बरषि (showering) / दिए (gave) / मनि (jewels) / अंबर (garments) / सबही (all)
ramacharitamanas::5245.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5245.essence: Trust makes obedience effortless and immediate.
ramacharitamanas::5245.simple_meaning: Ram tells Vibhishana to go up in the flying chariot and scatter the clothes and jewels in the sky. Vibhishana obeys at once.
ramacharitamanas::5245.simple_insight: Immediate obedience turns a command into action before doubt can enter.
ramacharitamanas::5245.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's defeat, Ram stands with Vibhishana and the victorious vanaras. The spoils of Lanka are being distributed, and Ram gives a simple order: rise in the chariot and scatter the garments and jewels. Vibhishana obeys instantly.
ramacharitamanas::5245.modern_relevance: A leader gives one clear instruction in the middle of chaos, and the trusted helper moves without hesitation. The moment works because there is no delay between instruction and service.
ramacharitamanas::5245.insight: It shows how trust and service can be so complete that action follows before thought.

ramacharitamanas::5246.verse_sanskrit: जोइ जोइ मन भावइ सोइ लेहीं। मनि मुख मेलि डारि कपि देहीं॥ हँसे रामु श्री अनुज समेता। परम कौतुकी कृपा निकेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5246.verse_hindi: जिसके मन को जो अच्छा लगता है, वह वही ले लेता है। मणियों को मुँह में लेकर वानर फिर उन्हें खाने की चीज न समझकर उगल देते हैं। यह तमाशा देखकर परम विनोदी और कृपा के धाम श्री रामजी, सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित हँसने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5246.english_translation: Whatever each one likes, he takes. The monkeys put the gems in their mouths and then spit them out, not seeing them as food. Seeing this spectacle, Sri Ram, along with his younger brother, laughed with delight; he is the very home of grace.
ramacharitamanas::5246.translation_literal: जोइ जोइ (whatever whatever) / मन (mind) / भावइ (likes) / सोइ (that only) / लेहीं (take) / मनि (gems) / मुख (mouth) / मेलि (placing) / डारि (throwing away) / कपि (monkeys) / देहीं (give) / हँसे (laughed) / रामु (Ram) / श्री (radiant) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेता (together with) / परम (supreme) / कौतुकी (playful) / कृपा (grace) / निकेता (abode)
ramacharitamanas::5246.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5246.essence: Possession means little when joy has already arrived.
ramacharitamanas::5246.simple_meaning: The monkeys grab whatever pleases them, then spit out the gems as if they were useless. Ram, Lakshman, and the others laugh at the scene.
ramacharitamanas::5246.simple_insight: Joy can come from shared play, not from possession.
ramacharitamanas::5246.detailed_meaning: After Lanka falls, the monkeys swarm Ravana’s riches. They mouth the gems and toss them away like pebbles. Ram, Lakshman, and the others laugh at the absurdity. The verse shows the victory’s carefree aftermath, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::5246.modern_relevance: You open a box of expensive gifts after a hard-won celebration, and the children care more about the wrapping paper. The moment reminds you that delight often lives in play, not value.
ramacharitamanas::5246.insight: It shifts attention from what is valuable on paper to what actually delights the heart.

ramacharitamanas::5247.verse_sanskrit: मुनि जेहि ध्यान न पावहिं नेति नेति कह बेद। कृपासिंधु सोइ कपिन्ह सन करत अनेक बिनोद ॥
ramacharitamanas::5247.verse_hindi: जिनको मुनि ध्यान में भी नहीं पाते, जिन्हें वेद नेति-नेति कहते हैं, वे ही कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी वानरों के साथ अनेकों प्रकार के विनोद कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5247.english_translation: The sages cannot reach Him in meditation, and the Vedas describe Him as neither this nor that. Yet that ocean of grace is joking with the monkeys in many playful ways.
ramacharitamanas::5247.translation_literal: मुनि (sages) / जेहि (whom) / ध्यान (meditation) / न पावहिं (do not attain) / नेति नेति (not this, not that) / कह (say) / बेद (the Vedas) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / सोइ (that same) / कपिन्ह सन (with the monkeys) / करत (doing) / अनेक (many) / बिनोद (playful acts)
ramacharitamanas::5247.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5247.essence: The highest reality is closest when it is most loving.
ramacharitamanas::5247.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond the reach of even great sages and beyond ordinary description, yet that same limitless grace is joyfully playing with the monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::5247.simple_insight: You do not have to grasp the infinite before you can be held by it.
ramacharitamanas::5247.detailed_meaning: After the victory in Lanka, the monkeys are receiving gifts and joyfully celebrating. In that atmosphere, Tulsidas reveals the paradox: Ram is beyond meditation and beyond the Vedas' final descriptions, yet He is right there, playing with His devoted companions.
ramacharitamanas::5247.modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to pin down what is ultimate, then find it in a moment of laughter with people who love you. The deepest reality is not distant from warmth and play.
ramacharitamanas::5247.insight: It shifts the mind from remote abstraction to intimate devotion: the highest reality can be personally near.

ramacharitamanas::5248.verse_sanskrit: उमा जोग जप दान तप नाना मख ब्रत नेम। राम कृपा नहिं करहिं तसि जसि निष्केवल प्रेम ॥
ramacharitamanas::5248.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! अनेकों प्रकार के योग, जप, दान, तप, यज्ञ, व्रत और नियम करने पर भी श्री रामचंद्रजी वैसी कृपा नहीं करते जैसी अनन्य प्रेम होने पर करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5248.english_translation: O Uma, even many kinds of yoga, chanting, charity, austerity, sacrifices, vows, and disciplines do not draw Ram's grace the way single-minded love does.
ramacharitamanas::5248.translation_literal: उमा (O Uma) / जोग (yoga) / जप (chanting) / दान (charity) / तप (austerity) / नाना (many kinds of) / मख (sacrifices) / ब्रत (vows) / नेम (disciplines) / राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / नहिं (not) / करहिं (do) / तसि (that way) / जसि (as) / निष्केवल (single-minded, without any other aim) / प्रेम (love)
ramacharitamanas::5248.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5248.essence: Undivided love draws Ram more than any amount of practice.
ramacharitamanas::5248.simple_meaning: Ram's grace comes more readily through undivided love than through many religious practices, rituals, or disciplines.
ramacharitamanas::5248.simple_insight: You don't have to impress the divine; wholehearted love is already enough.
ramacharitamanas::5248.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Uma in the Lankakand's closing devotional mood, after Ram has shown playful grace to the monkeys. He explains that even the most impressive practices cannot compare with one-pointed love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5248.modern_relevance: You have checked every box, followed every rule, and still feel far away. Then a simple, honest cry from the heart lands more deeply than all the polished effort.
ramacharitamanas::5248.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to sincerity, showing that love matters more than spiritual display.

ramacharitamanas::5249.verse_sanskrit: भालु कपिन्ह पट भूषन पाए। पहिरि पहिरि रघुपति पहिं आए॥ नाना जिनस देखि सब कीसा। पुनि पुनि हँसत कोसलाधीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5249.verse_hindi: भालुओं और वानरों ने कपड़े-गहने पाए और उन्हें पहन-पहनकर वे श्री रघुनाथजी के पास आए। अनेकों जातियों के वानरों को देखकर कोसलपति श्री रामजी बार-बार हँस रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5249.english_translation: The bears and monkeys received clothes and ornaments, and, wearing them again and again, came before Raghupati. Seeing the many kinds of monkeys, the Lord of Kosala kept laughing again and again.
ramacharitamanas::5249.translation_literal: भालु (bears) / कपिन्ह (monkeys) / पट (clothes) / भूषन (ornaments) / पाए (received) / पहिरि पहिरि (wearing again and again) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / पहिं (to) / आए (came) ॥ / नाना (many) / जिनस (kinds) / देखि (seeing) / सब (all) / कीसा (monkeys) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / हँसत (laughing) / कोसलाधीसा (Lord of Kosala) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5249.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5249.essence: Victory becomes celebration when Ram looks at everyone with delight.
ramacharitamanas::5249.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears put on the gifts and came to Ram, who laughed at their many different forms.
ramacharitamanas::5249.simple_insight: There is tenderness in being seen with delight, not judgment.
ramacharitamanas::5249.detailed_meaning: After the war, the victorious monkeys and bears receive clothes and ornaments and proudly dress up before Ram. He looks at their many shapes and laughs with affection. The verse is a joyful scene of celebration, not a teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::5249.modern_relevance: At a family wedding, everyone is dressed badly, beautifully, and hilariously all at once — and the person you love most is laughing with affection, not mockery.
ramacharitamanas::5249.insight: It shifts attention from formal victory to shared joy and belonging.

ramacharitamanas::5250.verse_sanskrit: चितइ सबन्हि पर कीन्ही दाया। बोले मृदुल बचन रघुराया॥ तुम्हरें बल मैं रावनु मार् यो। तिलक बिभीषन कहँ पुनि सार् यो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5250.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने कृपा दृष्टि से देखकर सब पर दया की। फिर वे कोमल वचन बोले- हे भाइयो! तुम्हारे ही बल से मैंने रावण को मारा और फिर विभीषण का राजतिलक किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5250.english_translation: Looking at them all with compassion, the Lord of Raghu spoke gently: "By your strength I killed Ravana, and then I crowned Vibhishana."
ramacharitamanas::5250.translation_literal: चितइ (looking at) / सबन्हि (all) / पर (upon) / कीन्ही (did) / दाया (compassion) / बोले (spoke) / मृदुल (gentle) / बचन (words) / रघुराया (Lord of Raghu) / तुम्हरें (by your) / बल (strength) / मैं (I) / रावनु (Ravana) / मार् यो (killed) / तिलक (coronation) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / कहँ (for) / पुनि (again) / सार् यो (performed)
ramacharitamanas::5250.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5250.essence: Victory becomes beautiful when you give the credit away.
ramacharitamanas::5250.simple_meaning: Ram speaks kindly to the monkeys and gives them credit for his victory. He also honors Vibhishana by crowning him king.
ramacharitamanas::5250.simple_insight: True greatness does not boast. It shares credit and lifts others up.
ramacharitamanas::5250.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's defeat, Ram stands before the monkey army and the bears. Instead of claiming the victory, he speaks with tenderness, credits their strength, and honors Vibhishana with kingship. The moment shows how divine victory still looks like humility.
ramacharitamanas::5250.modern_relevance: Your team stayed late to finish the project, but the public praise went to someone else. The deeper leader is the one who names everyone who made the win possible.
ramacharitamanas::5250.insight: It shifts you from self-congratulation to generous acknowledgment, making leadership feel humble and shared.

ramacharitamanas::5251.verse_sanskrit: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5251.verse_hindi: अब तुम सब अपने-अपने घर जाओ। मेरा स्मरण करते रहना और किसी से डरना नहीं। ये वचन सुनते ही सब वानर प्रेम में विह्वल होकर हाथ जोड़कर आदरपूर्वक बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5251.english_translation: Now all of you go back to your own homes. Keep remembering me, and do not fear anyone. Hearing these words, all the monkeys were overwhelmed with love and, joining their hands, spoke respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::5251.translation_literal: निज निज (each one’s own) / गृह (home) / अब (now) / तुम्ह (you all) / सब (all) / जाहू (go) / सुमिरेहु (remember) / मोहि (me) / डरपहु (fear) / जनि (do not) / काहू (anyone) / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / प्रेमाकुल (filled with love) / बानर (monkeys) / जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / बोले (spoke) / सब (all) / सादर (respectfully)
ramacharitamanas::5251.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5251.essence: Remembrance of Ram sends fear packing.
ramacharitamanas::5251.simple_meaning: Ram sends the monkeys home with one instruction: keep remembering him and do not be afraid.
ramacharitamanas::5251.simple_insight: Love becomes courage when you carry a beloved presence in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::5251.detailed_meaning: After the war ends, Ram speaks gently to the monkey army that served him in Lanka. He tells them to return home, keep his remembrance alive, and let fear drop away. Their response shows how devotion turns command into joy.
ramacharitamanas::5251.modern_relevance: You leave a hard season behind, but the nervous system still expects danger. One steady presence in your mind can make the road home feel safe again.
ramacharitamanas::5251.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion to protection: remembrance becomes the source of fearlessness.

ramacharitamanas::5252.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु जोइ कहहु तुम्हहि सब सोहा। हमरें होत बचन सुनि मोहा॥ दीन जानि कपि किए सनाथा। तुम्ह त्रैलोक ईस रघुनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5252.verse_hindi: प्रभो! आप जो कुछ भी कहें, आपको सब सोहता है। पर आपके वचन सुनकर हमको मोह होता है। हे रघुनाथजी! आप तीनों लोकों के ईश्वर हैं। हम वानरों को दीन जानकर ही आपने सनाथ (कृतार्थ) किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5252.english_translation: Whatever you say suits you perfectly, Lord. But hearing your words, we are overcome with wonder. O Raghunath, you are the lord of the three worlds. Seeing us as lowly, you have made us your own.
ramacharitamanas::5252.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / जोइ (whatever) / कहहु (you say) / तुम्हहि (to you) / सब (everything) / सोहा (suits) / हमरें (for us) / होत (happening) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / मोहा (delight / wonder)॥ / दीन (lowly) / जानि (knowing) / कपि (monkeys) / किए (made) / सनाथा (well-supported / your own) / तुम्ह (you) / त्रैलोक (three worlds) / ईस (lord) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5252.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5252.essence: True greatness makes room for the lowly and calls them its own.
ramacharitamanas::5252.simple_meaning: The monkeys praise Ram’s greatness and feel overwhelmed that he has accepted them despite their lowly state.
ramacharitamanas::5252.simple_insight: Being seen with kindness can humble you more deeply than criticism.
ramacharitamanas::5252.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram speaks gently to the monkeys and credits them for Ravana’s defeat. Hanuman answers with awe: Ram is the lord of the three worlds, yet he has made lowly beings his own. The moment becomes pure devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5252.modern_relevance: You get praised for work you barely feel worthy of, and instead of swelling with pride, you feel seen through. That strange mix of humility and love is what this verse holds.
ramacharitamanas::5252.insight: It shifts attention from status to grace: what matters is being received, not ranked.

ramacharitamanas::5253.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन लाज हम मरहीं। मसक कहूँ खगपति हित करहीं॥ देखि राम रुख बानर रीछा। प्रेम मगन नहिं गृह कै ईछा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5253.verse_hindi: प्रभु के (ऐसे) वचन सुनकर हम लाज के मारे मरे जा रहे हैं। कहीं मच्छर भी गरुड़ का हित कर सकते हैं? श्री रामजी का रुख देखकर रीछ-वानर प्रेम में मग्न हो गए। उनकी घर जाने की इच्छा नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5253.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, we feel ashamed to the point of death. Can even a mosquito help Garuda? Seeing Ram's face, the bears and monkeys were lost in love and no longer wanted to go home.
ramacharitamanas::5253.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (Lord) / बचन (words) / लाज (shame) / हम (we) / मरहीं (die) / मसक (mosquito) / कहूँ (even) / खगपति (lord of birds) / हित (good/help) / करहीं (can do) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / रुख (face/turn) / बानर (monkeys) / रीछा (bears) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / नहिं (not) / गृह (home) / कै (of) / ईछा (desire)
ramacharitamanas::5253.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5253.essence: Love for Ram can make leaving feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::5253.simple_meaning: The vanaras and bears feel humbled before Ram's greatness, and Ram's presence fills them with such love that they no longer want to leave.
ramacharitamanas::5253.simple_insight: True devotion makes pride vanish and turns even departure into longing to stay near what you love.
ramacharitamanas::5253.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram tells the vanaras and bears to return home. Their hearts break with humility and love at his words and his face. This verse captures the moment service turns into pure attachment to Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::5253.modern_relevance: You finish helping someone you love, and they tell you to go home. Instead of relief, you feel a quiet ache to stay a little longer. That is what it means to be moved by real devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5253.insight: It shifts the mind from self-consciousness to loving absorption, where Ram's presence matters more than comfort or status.

ramacharitamanas::5254.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु प्रेरित कपि भालु सब राम रूप उर राखि। हरष बिषाद सहित चले बिनय बिबिध बिधि भाषि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5254.verse_hindi: परन्तु प्रभु की प्रेरणा (आज्ञा) से सब वानर-भालू श्री रामजी के रूप को हृदय में रखकर और अनेकों प्रकार से विनती करके हर्ष और विषाद सहित घर को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::5254.english_translation: Moved by the Lord's command, all the monkeys and bears kept Ram's form in their hearts and set out for home, speaking many kinds of prayers with joy and sorrow together.
ramacharitamanas::5254.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रेरित (prompted) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears) / सब (all) / राम रूप (Ram's form) / उर (in the heart) / राखि (keeping) / हरष (joy) / बिषाद (sorrow) / सहित (together with) / चले (went) / बिनय (prayers) / बिबिध (various) / बिधि (ways) / भाषि (speaking)
ramacharitamanas::5254.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5254.essence: True devotion lets you leave without ever letting go.
ramacharitamanas::5254.simple_meaning: The monkeys and bears leave, holding Ram in their hearts and offering many prayers, feeling both joy and sadness as they go home.
ramacharitamanas::5254.simple_insight: Even parting can be full of devotion when your heart stays with what you love.
ramacharitamanas::5254.detailed_meaning: After the victory in Lanka, the monkey and bear leaders are preparing to leave. They are moved by Ram's command, but their hearts remain fixed on him. Their departure is joyful because they have served him, and sorrowful because they must now go away.
ramacharitamanas::5254.modern_relevance: You finish a life-changing retreat, pack your bag, and feel both grateful and empty. The place is behind you, but the presence you found there still travels with you.
ramacharitamanas::5254.insight: It shifts attention from the trip itself to the heart you carry back home.

ramacharitamanas::5255.verse_sanskrit: कपिपति नील रीछपति अंगद नल हनुमान। सहित बिभीषन अपर जे जूथप कपि बलवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5255.verse_hindi: वानरराज सुग्रीव, नील, ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान् , अंगद, नल और हनुमान् तथा विभीषण सहित और जो बलवान् वानर सेनापति हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::5255.english_translation: The monkey kings Sugriva, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, Nala, Hanuman, Vibhishana, and the other powerful leaders of the monkey army.
ramacharitamanas::5255.translation_literal: कपिपति (monkey lords) / नील (Nila) / रीछपति (bear lord) / अंगद (Angada) / नल (Nala) / हनुमान (Hanuman) / सहित (together with) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / अपर (other) / जे (who) / जूथप (herd-leaders) / कपि (monkeys) / बलवान (powerful)
ramacharitamanas::5255.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5255.essence: Many strong allies now stand on Ram's side.
ramacharitamanas::5255.simple_meaning: Sugriva, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, Nala, Hanuman, Vibhishana, and other strong leaders stand together.
ramacharitamanas::5255.simple_insight: Strength becomes larger when it gathers around a shared cause.
ramacharitamanas::5255.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, after the war has turned, Tulsidas lists the leaders standing with Ram: monkey kings, bear chiefs, and Vibhishana. The verse is not teaching yet; it is gathering the names before the emotional sight of them all turning toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5255.modern_relevance: A team meeting ends and the people who once worked separately now stand behind one decision. This is the feeling of many strengths gathering into one purpose.
ramacharitamanas::5255.insight: It shifts attention from individual power to collective alignment.

ramacharitamanas::5256.verse_sanskrit: कहि न सकहिं कछु प्रेम बस भरि भरि लोचन बारि॥ सन्मुख चितवहिं राम तन नयन निमेष निवारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5256.verse_hindi: वे कुछ कह नहीं सकते, प्रेमवश नेत्रों में जल भर-भरकर, नेत्रों का पलक मारना छोड़कर (टकटकी लगाए) सम्मुख होकर श्री रामजी की ओर देख रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5256.english_translation: They cannot say anything. Overcome by love, their eyes fill again and again with tears. They keep looking straight at Ram, refusing even to blink.
ramacharitamanas::5256.translation_literal: कहि (say) / न (not) / सकहिं (are able) / कछु (anything) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the power of) / भरि भरि (again and again filling) / लोचन (eyes) / बारि (water, tears) ॥ / सन्मुख (facing) / चितवहिं (they gaze) / राम (Ram) / तन (toward) / नयन (eyes) / निमेष (blink) / निवारि (stopping) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5256.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5256.essence: True devotion can make speech disappear and attention become complete.
ramacharitamanas::5256.simple_meaning: Love has filled them so completely that they cannot speak. Tears keep coming, and they cannot look away from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5256.simple_insight: Deep love can silence you and still feel more complete than speech.
ramacharitamanas::5256.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram stands before the gathered beings who have fought and suffered for him. Seeing him at last, they are overwhelmed. Words fail, tears rise, and they can only stare without blinking.
ramacharitamanas::5256.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and your throat closes. Nothing clever comes out — only tears and a steady look that says everything.
ramacharitamanas::5256.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to presence: love is proven by attention, not explanation.

ramacharitamanas::5257.verse_sanskrit: अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुराई। लीन्हे सकल बिमान चढ़ाई॥ मन महुँ बिप्र चरन सिरु नायो। उत्तर दिसिहि बिमान चलायो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5257.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने उनका अतिशय प्रेम देखकर सबको विमान पर चढ़ा लिया। तदनन्तर मन ही मन विप्रचरणों में सिर नवाकर उत्तर दिशा की ओर विमान चलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5257.english_translation: Seeing their deep affection, Raghurai took them all aboard the aerial chariot. Then, bowing his head inwardly to the feet of the Brahmin, he set the chariot toward the north.
ramacharitamanas::5257.translation_literal: अतिसय (great) / प्रीति (affection) / देखि (seeing) / रघुराई (Raghurai) / लीन्हे (took) / सकल (all) / बिमान (aerial chariot) / चढ़ाई (having boarded)॥ / मन महुँ (in the mind) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नायो (bowed) / उत्तर (north) / दिसिहि (direction) / बिमान (aerial chariot) / चलायो (sent forth) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5257.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5257.essence: Victory stays pure when humility leads the way.
ramacharitamanas::5257.simple_meaning: Ram notices their devotion, seats everyone in the divine chariot, bows inwardly to the Brahmin’s feet, and sends the chariot north.
ramacharitamanas::5257.simple_insight: Devotion is received with grace; humility keeps victory from turning proud.
ramacharitamanas::5257.detailed_meaning: After Ravana’s defeat, Ram prepares to leave Lanka with the rescued company and his devoted allies. Seeing their overflowing love, he seats them all in the aerial chariot, then bows inwardly to the Brahmin’s feet before setting off north.
ramacharitamanas::5257.modern_relevance: After a hard win, you finally get the group photo, the applause, the relief. The real test is whether you stay humble when everyone else is celebrating.
ramacharitamanas::5257.insight: It shows that true success includes gratitude, humility, and care for everyone who helped.

ramacharitamanas::5258.verse_sanskrit: चलत बिमान कोलाहल होई। जय रघुबीर कहइ सबु कोई॥ सिंहासन अति उच्च मनोहर। श्री समेत प्रभु बैठे ता पर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5258.verse_hindi: विमान के चलते समय बड़ा शोर हो रहा है। सब कोई श्री रघुवीर की जय कह रहे हैं। विमान में एक अत्यंत ऊँचा मनोहर सिंहासन है। उस पर सीताजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी विराजमान हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5258.english_translation: As the विमान moved, there was a great uproar. Everyone cried, "Victory to Raghubir!" In the lofty, beautiful throne, the Lord sat there with Sita.
ramacharitamanas::5258.translation_literal: चलत (while moving) / बिमान (the aerial chariot) / कोलाहल (uproar) / होई (was) / जय (victory) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / कहइ (says) / सबु कोई (everyone) / सिंहासन (throne) / अति उच्च (very high) / मनोहर (beautiful) / श्री समेत (with Sita) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बैठे (sat) / ता पर (on that)
ramacharitamanas::5258.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5258.essence: Victory is now visible, and the whole world is cheering.
ramacharitamanas::5258.simple_meaning: The people celebrate as Ram and Sita ride in a splendid flying chariot and take their seats on a beautiful high throne.
ramacharitamanas::5258.simple_insight: Joy becomes shared when the long struggle finally ends.
ramacharitamanas::5258.detailed_meaning: The war is over, and the returning company is airborne with Ram and Sita seated together in royal splendour. The crowd erupts in praise as the chariot moves, but this verse is mainly a scene of triumph, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5258.modern_relevance: A stadium erupts when the final whistle blows and your team lifts the trophy. The noise, the relief, the shared shout — all of it is the feeling of a hard victory finally becoming real.
ramacharitamanas::5258.insight: It marks the public arrival of peace after conflict, not a new instruction.

ramacharitamanas::5259.verse_sanskrit: राजत रामु सहित भामिनी। मेरु सृंग जनु घन दामिनी॥ रुचिर बिमानु चलेउ अति आतुर। कीन्ही सुमन बृष्टि हरषे सुर ॥
ramacharitamanas::5259.verse_hindi: पत्नी सहित श्री रामजी ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं मानो सुमेरु के शिखर पर बिजली सहित श्याम मेघ हो। सुंदर विमान बड़ी शीघ्रता से चला। देवता हर्षित हुए और उन्होंने फूलों की वर्षा की ॥
ramacharitamanas::5259.english_translation: Rama, together with his wife, shone like dark clouds with lightning on Mount Meru. The lovely celestial chariot moved swiftly, and the radiant beings rejoiced, showering flowers.
ramacharitamanas::5259.translation_literal: राजत (shone) / रामु (Rama) / सहित (together with) / भामिनी (the radiant wife) / मेरु सृंग (Meru's peak) / जनु (like) / घन (cloud) / दामिनी (lightning) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बिमानु (celestial chariot) / चलेउ (moved) / अति आतुर (very swiftly) / कीन्ही (made) / सुमन बृष्टि (flower shower) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सुर (radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::5259.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5259.essence: Restored love shines brighter than victory.
ramacharitamanas::5259.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita shine together like lightning on a mountain peak. Their chariot moves swiftly as the radiant beings celebrate and shower flowers.
ramacharitamanas::5259.simple_insight: Joy follows when what is rightful and beautiful is finally restored.
ramacharitamanas::5259.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram and Sita are leaving Lanka in a celestial chariot. Tulsidas pauses on their radiance, the speed of the chariot, and the joy of the radiant beings. This is the triumph before the return.
ramacharitamanas::5259.modern_relevance: After a long, brutal project finally ends, you step outside with the person who stood by you. The relief is bigger than success — it feels like the world itself is blessing the moment.
ramacharitamanas::5259.insight: It shifts attention from battle to restoration, showing victory as harmony returning.

ramacharitamanas::5260.verse_sanskrit: परम सुखद चलि त्रिबिध बयारी। सागर सर सरि निर्मल बारी॥ सगुन होहिं सुंदर चहुँ पासा। मन प्रसन्न निर्मल नभ आसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5260.verse_hindi: अत्यंत सुख देने वाली तीन प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित) वायु चलने लगी। समुद्र, तालाब और नदियों का जल निर्मल हो गया। चारों ओर सुंदर शकुन होने लगे। सबके मन प्रसन्न हैं, आकाश और दिशाएँ निर्मल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5260.english_translation: A supremely soothing breeze began to blow in three ways. The sea, ponds, and rivers became clear and pure. Beautiful omens appeared on all sides. Everyone's mind was cheerful; the sky and the directions were bright and clear.
ramacharitamanas::5260.translation_literal: परम (supremely) / सुखद (pleasant, soothing) / चलि (began to move) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / बयारी (breeze, wind) / सागर (sea) / सर (pond) / सरि (river) / निर्मल (pure, clear) / बारी (water) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / होहिं (became) / सुंदर (beautiful) / चहुँ पासा (on all four sides) / मन (mind) / प्रसन्न (joyful) / निर्मल (pure, clear) / नभ (sky) / आसा (directions, spaces)
ramacharitamanas::5260.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5260.essence: Victory makes the whole world feel purified.
ramacharitamanas::5260.simple_meaning: Nature itself turns calm and auspicious as Ram returns in victory. The world around him seems to share the joy.
ramacharitamanas::5260.simple_insight: When your heart is aligned, even the world feels less harsh.
ramacharitamanas::5260.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Sita ride back after Ravana's defeat, the return itself feels sacred. The air, waters, omens, and sky all seem purified, as if Lanka and the world are welcoming dharma back into place.
ramacharitamanas::5260.modern_relevance: After a long, tense family gathering finally ends well, the room feels different — lighter, quieter, almost washed clean. Relief can change how everything around you seems to breathe.
ramacharitamanas::5260.insight: It shifts attention from outer noise to the felt harmony that follows right action.

ramacharitamanas::5261.verse_sanskrit: कह रघुबीर देखु रन सीता। लछिमन इहाँ हत्यो इँद्रजीता॥ हनूमान अंगद के मारे। रन महि परे निसाचर भारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5261.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीरजी ने कहा- हे सीते! रणभूमि देखो। लक्ष्मण ने यहाँ इंद्र को जीतने वाले मेघनाद को मारा था। हनुमान् और अंगद के मारे हुए ये भारी-भारी निशाचर रणभूमि में पड़े हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5261.english_translation: Raghubir said, "Look at the battlefield, Sita. Lakshman killed Indrajit here. These mighty night-walkers, struck down by Hanuman and Angad, lie on the field."
ramacharitamanas::5261.translation_literal: कह (said) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / देखु (look) / रन (battlefield) / सीता (Sita) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / इहाँ (here) / हत्यो (killed) / इँद्रजीता (Indrajit) / हनूमान (Hanuman) / अंगद (Angad) / के (by) / मारे (struck down) / रन (battlefield) / महि (on the ground) / परे (fallen) / निसाचर (night-walkers) / भारे (mighty)
ramacharitamanas::5261.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5261.essence: The battlefield remembers who brought the victory.
ramacharitamanas::5261.simple_meaning: Ram points out the battlefield to Sita and names the fallen enemies and the heroes who struck them down.
ramacharitamanas::5261.simple_insight: Victory is made of real sacrifices, not just triumph.
ramacharitamanas::5261.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram shows Sita the battlefield in Lanka. He points to where Lakshman killed Indrajit and where Hanuman and Angad brought down powerful enemies. The verse is a scene of aftermath, not a teaching by itself.
ramacharitamanas::5261.modern_relevance: You walk past the place where a hard season ended — the office emptied, the argument over, the damage visible. The story is still in the marks left behind.
ramacharitamanas::5261.insight: It keeps attention on the cost of victory and the people who made it possible.

ramacharitamanas::5262.verse_sanskrit: कुंभकरन रावन द्वौ भाई। इहाँ हते सुर मुनि दुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5262.verse_hindi: देवताओं और मुनियों को दुःख देने वाले कुंभकर्ण और रावण दोनों भाई यहाँ मारे गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5262.english_translation: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the two brothers who tormented the gods and sages, were killed here.
ramacharitamanas::5262.translation_literal: कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / रावन (Ravana) / द्वौ भाई (the two brothers) / इहाँ (here) / हते (were killed) / सुर (the gods) / मुनि (sages) / दुखदाई (pain-giving, tormenting)
ramacharitamanas::5262.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5262.essence: Two feared brothers fell where they once ruled by terror.
ramacharitamanas::5262.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the two brothers who caused suffering to the gods and sages, were slain here.
ramacharitamanas::5262.simple_insight: It marks the fall of two forces that had long caused fear and pain.
ramacharitamanas::5262.detailed_meaning: In Lanka after the war, Ram is showing Sita the battlefield. The scene is still part of a larger tour of victory and ruin: the brothers Kumbhakarna and Ravana lie defeated here, remembered as the ones who tormented the gods and sages.
ramacharitamanas::5262.modern_relevance: You walk past the place where a long conflict finally ended. The damage is still visible, but so is the fact that what once dominated everything has already fallen.
ramacharitamanas::5262.insight: It shifts attention from the drama of battle to the quiet fact of collapse.

ramacharitamanas::5263.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ सेतु बाँध्यों अरु थापेउँ सिव सुख धाम। सीता सहित कृपानिधि संभुहि कीन्ह प्रनाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::5263.verse_hindi: मैंने यहाँ पुल बाँधा (बँधवाया) और सुखधाम श्री शिवजी की स्थापना की। तदनन्तर कृपानिधान श्री रामजी ने सीताजी सहित श्री रामेश्वर महादेव को प्रणाम किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5263.english_translation: I built the bridge here and established the abode of Shiva. Then the treasure of compassion, Ram, bowed with Sita to Lord Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::5263.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / सेतु (bridge) / बाँध्यों (built) / अरु (and) / थापेउँ (established) / सिव (Shiva) / सुख धाम (abode of bliss) / सीता सहित (together with Sita) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / संभुहि (to Shiva) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनाम (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::5263.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5263.essence: Even victory bows before the sacred.
ramacharitamanas::5263.simple_meaning: Ram says he built the bridge here, established Shiva's sacred place, and then bowed with Sita to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::5263.simple_insight: Great power still bows before reverence.
ramacharitamanas::5263.detailed_meaning: After the war's turning point in Lanka, Ram shows Sita the battlefield and the sacred places tied to the victory. He reminds her that the bridge was built here and that Shiva's holy shrine was established here, then he bows with her to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::5263.modern_relevance: You finish a hard project, then still thank the mentor who shaped it. The victory is real, but so is the humility that keeps it clean.
ramacharitamanas::5263.insight: It teaches you to let accomplishment end in gratitude, not self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::5264.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जहँ कृपासिंधु बन कीन्ह बास बिश्राम। सकल देखाए जानकिहि कहे सबन्हि के नाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::5264.verse_hindi: वन में जहाँ-तहाँ करुणा सागर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने निवास और विश्राम किया था, वे सब स्थान प्रभु ने जानकीजी को दिखलाए और सबके नाम बतलाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5264.english_translation: Wherever the ocean of compassion had lived and rested in the forest, he showed Janaki all those places and told her the name of each one.
ramacharitamanas::5264.translation_literal: जहँ जहँ (wherever) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / बन (forest) / कीन्ह (made) / बास (dwelling) / बिश्राम (rest) / सकल (all) / देखाए (showed) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / कहे (told) / सबन्हि (of all) / के नाम (the names)
ramacharitamanas::5264.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5264.essence: Love turns ordinary places into living remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::5264.simple_meaning: Ram shows Sita the forest places where he had lived and rested, naming each one for her.
ramacharitamanas::5264.simple_insight: Love remembers the places that pain once marked.
ramacharitamanas::5264.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram and Sita move through the forest again. Ram points out each place where he had stayed and rested, naming them for Sita. The moment is tender, but it mainly serves the journey scene, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5264.modern_relevance: You pass an old street and remember exactly where everything happened. A shared place can hold a whole chapter of love, grief, and return.
ramacharitamanas::5264.insight: It shifts attention from action to memory and shared experience.

ramacharitamanas::5265.verse_sanskrit: तुरत बिमान तहाँ चलि आवा। दंडक बन जहँ परम सुहावा॥ कुंभजादि मुनिनायक नाना। गए रामु सब कें अस्थाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5265.verse_hindi: विमान शीघ्र ही वहाँ चला आया, जहाँ परम सुंदर दण्डकवन था और अगस्त्य आदि बहुत से मुनिराज रहते थे। श्री रामजी इन सबके स्थानों में गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5265.english_translation: The celestial vehicle quickly arrived there, where the beautiful Dandaka forest lay and many great sages such as Kumbhaja lived. Ram went to the homes of all of them.
ramacharitamanas::5265.translation_literal: तुरत (quickly) / बिमान (celestial vehicle) / तहाँ (there) / चलि (having gone) / आवा (came) / दंडक बन (Dandaka forest) / जहँ (where) / परम सुहावा (very beautiful) / कुंभजादि (Kumbhaja and others) / मुनिनायक (leaders among sages) / नाना (many) / गए (went) / रामु (Ram) / सब कें (to all) / अस्थाना (homes)
ramacharitamanas::5265.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5265.essence: Ram's presence turns every sage's home into a sacred stop.
ramacharitamanas::5265.simple_meaning: Ram's aerial vehicle reaches the beautiful Dandaka forest, and Ram visits the homes of many great sages there.
ramacharitamanas::5265.simple_insight: The journey matters because every holy place and every sage receives Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::5265.detailed_meaning: After crossing the bridge and honoring Shiva, Ram and Sita continue by celestial vehicle into Dandaka. The vehicle arrives where sages like Agastya live, and Ram visits each hermitage. The verse simply marks the sacred route before the next stop.
ramacharitamanas::5265.modern_relevance: You finally arrive at a place everyone called meaningful, and you don't rush past the people who live there. You make time to meet the ones who have kept that place alive.
ramacharitamanas::5265.insight: It shifts attention from travel itself to honoring the people and places along the way.

ramacharitamanas::5266.verse_sanskrit: सकल रिषिन्ह सन पाइ असीसा। चित्रकूट आए जगदीसा॥ तहँ करि मुनिन्ह केर संतोषा। चला बिमानु तहाँ ते चोखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5266.verse_hindi: संपूर्ण ऋषियों से आशीर्वाद पाकर जगदीश्वर श्री रामजी चित्रकूट आए। वहाँ मुनियों को संतुष्ट किया। (फिर) विमान वहाँ से आगे तेजी के साथ चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::5266.english_translation: After receiving blessings from all the sages, the Lord of the world, Ram, came to Chitrakoot. There he satisfied the sages, and then the aerial chariot moved on quickly from there.
ramacharitamanas::5266.translation_literal: सकल (all) / रिषिन्ह (from the sages) / सन (from) / पाइ (having received) / असीसा (blessings) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / आए (came) / जगदीसा (Lord of the world)॥ / तहँ (there) / करि (having done) / मुनिन्ह (the sages) / केर (of) / संतोषा (satisfaction/contentment) / चला (moved) / बिमानु (the aerial chariot) / तहाँ ते (from there) / चोखा (swiftly/cleanly)॥
ramacharitamanas::5266.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5266.essence: True greatness pauses to bless others before going forward.
ramacharitamanas::5266.simple_meaning: Ram arrives at Chitrakoot, receives the sages’ blessings, gives them joy, and then continues onward.
ramacharitamanas::5266.simple_insight: Blessing and service can happen quietly, without pausing the journey.
ramacharitamanas::5266.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita are moving through the forest on their long exile. At Chitrakoot, Ram receives blessings from the sages, brings them satisfaction, and then the divine journey continues. The verse keeps the story moving while showing how naturally Ram honors holy people.
ramacharitamanas::5266.modern_relevance: You stop by an elder’s home, listen fully, leave them lighter, and still catch your train. Real respect can be brief and complete.
ramacharitamanas::5266.insight: It teaches you to honor those who support you before moving on.

ramacharitamanas::5267.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि राम जानकिहि देखाई। जमुना कलि मल हरनि सुहाई॥ पुनि देखी सुरसरी पुनीता। राम कहा प्रनाम करु सीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5267.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामजी ने जानकीजी को कलियुग के पापों का हरण करने वाली सुहावनी यमुनाजी के दर्शन कराए। फिर पवित्र गंगाजी के दर्शन किए। श्री रामजी ने कहा- हे सीते! इन्हें प्रणाम करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5267.english_translation: Then Ram showed Janaki the lovely Yamuna, remover of the impurities of Kali Yuga. Then he showed the pure Ganga. Ram said, "Bow to them, Sita."
ramacharitamanas::5267.translation_literal: बहुरि (then again) / राम (Ram) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / देखाई (showed) / जमुना (Yamuna) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / मल (impurities) / हरनि (remover) / सुहाई (lovely)॥ / पुनि (again) / देखी (saw) / सुरसरी (Ganga, river of the devas) / पुनीता (pure) / राम (Ram) / कहा (said) / प्रनाम (bow) / करु (do) / सीता (Sita) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5267.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5267.essence: Even Ram teaches reverence by bowing to what purifies.
ramacharitamanas::5267.simple_meaning: Ram shows Sita the sacred Yamuna and Ganga, then asks her to bow to them.
ramacharitamanas::5267.simple_insight: Even the divine bow to what purifies and uplifts.
ramacharitamanas::5267.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Sita travel through holy lands, Ram points out the Yamuna and Ganga to her and asks her to pay respects. The moment turns pilgrimage into devotion, showing that even the ideal king honors sacred waters.
ramacharitamanas::5267.modern_relevance: You pass a river on a road trip and barely look up. This verse reminds you to pause, notice what cleanses you, and meet it with respect.
ramacharitamanas::5267.insight: It turns sacred places into living teachers and models reverence through action.

ramacharitamanas::5268.verse_sanskrit: तीरथपति पुनि देखु प्रयागा। निरखत जन्म कोटि अघ भागा॥ देखु परम पावनि पुनि बेनी। हरनि सोक हरि लोक निसेनी ॥ पुनि देखु अवधपुरि अति पावनि। त्रिबिध ताप भव रोग नसावनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5268.verse_hindi: फिर तीर्थराज प्रयाग को देखो, जिसके दर्शन से ही करोड़ों जन्मों के पाप भाग जाते हैं। फिर परम पवित्र त्रिवेणीजी के दर्शन करो, जो शोकों को हरने वाली और श्री हरि के परम धाम (पहुँचने) के लिए सीढ़ी के समान है। फिर अत्यंत पवित्र अयोध्यापुरी के दर्शन करो, जो तीनों प्रकार के तापों और भव (आवागमन रूपी) रोग का नाश करने वाली है॥4-5॥
ramacharitamanas::5268.english_translation: Then look upon Prayag, lord of pilgrimages, whose sight scatters the sins of countless births. Then behold the supremely pure Triveni, remover of sorrow and the stairway to the realm of Hari. Then look upon the holy city of Ayodhya, destroyer of the threefold heat and the disease of worldly becoming.
ramacharitamanas::5268.translation_literal: तीरथपति (lord of pilgrimages) / पुनि (again) / देखु (look) / प्रयागा (Prayag) / निरखत (by seeing) / जन्म (births) / कोटि (crores/countless) / अघ (sins) / भागा (departed) / देखु (look) / परम (supremely) / पावनि (pure) / पुनि (again) / बेनी (Triveni) / हरनि (remover) / सोक (sorrow) / हरि (Hari's) / लोक (realm) / निसेनी (stairway) / पुनि (again) / देखु (look) / अवधपुरि (Ayodhya city) / अति (very) / पावनि (holy) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / ताप (heat) / भव (worldly becoming) / रोग (disease) / नसावनि (destroyer)
ramacharitamanas::5268.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5268.essence: Holy places can lighten burdens you have carried for years.
ramacharitamanas::5268.simple_meaning: Ram points out Prayag, the Triveni, and Ayodhya as places so pure that simply seeing them removes burdens, sorrow, and the pain of worldly life.
ramacharitamanas::5268.simple_insight: Sacred places matter because they can steady the heart and lift what has been weighing on you.
ramacharitamanas::5268.detailed_meaning: Ram is traveling with Sita and showing her the holy geography of the land. He points to Prayag, the Triveni, and Ayodhya as places of immense purity and relief. The verse builds a devotional map before the final bow to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::5268.modern_relevance: You arrive in a city after a long train ride and step into a temple lane before dawn. The noise drops away, and for a moment your mind feels lighter than it has in months.
ramacharitamanas::5268.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary location to places that can reset the mind and soften suffering.

ramacharitamanas::5269.verse_sanskrit: सीता सहित अवध कहुँ कीन्ह कृपाल प्रनाम। सजल नयन तन पुलकित पुनि पुनि हरषित राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::5269.verse_hindi: यों कहकर कृपालु श्री रामजी ने सीताजी सहित अवधपुरी को प्रणाम किया। सजल नेत्र और पुलकित शरीर होकर श्री रामजी बार-बार हर्षित हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5269.english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord bowed to Ayodhya along with Sita. With tear-filled eyes and a thrilled body, Ram grew joyful again and again.
ramacharitamanas::5269.translation_literal: सीता सहित (along with Sita) / अवध कहुँ (to Ayodhya) / कीन्ह (did) / कृपाल (the compassionate one) / प्रनाम (salutation) / सजल नयन (tear-filled eyes) / तन (body) / पुलकित (horripilated) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / हरषित (joyful) / राम (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::5269.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5269.essence: Even victory bows before the place that held your life.
ramacharitamanas::5269.simple_meaning: Ram, with Sita beside him, bows to Ayodhya with tears in his eyes and joy in his body.
ramacharitamanas::5269.simple_insight: Home is not just a place here — it is something Ram greets with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::5269.detailed_meaning: After the war is over, Ram returns toward Ayodhya with Sita. Before entering, he bows to the city itself, tears in his eyes and joy flooding his body. The moment is tender, not triumphant: home has become sacred.
ramacharitamanas::5269.modern_relevance: You come back to the house where your parents still keep your old room untouched. Before you speak to anyone, your chest tightens. Some places deserve reverence, not just arrival.
ramacharitamanas::5269.insight: It shifts the reader from seeing home as possession to seeing it as something worthy of gratitude and honor.

ramacharitamanas::5270.verse_sanskrit: पुनि प्रभु आइ त्रिबेनीं हरषित मज्जनु कीन्ह। कपिन्ह सहित बिप्रन्ह कहुँ दान बिबिध बिधि दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::5270.verse_hindi: फिर त्रिवेणी में आकर प्रभु ने हर्षित होकर स्नान किया और वानरों सहित ब्राह्मणों को अनेकों प्रकार के दान दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5270.english_translation: Then the Lord came to Triveni, bathed with joy, and gave many kinds of gifts to the monkeys and the brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::5270.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आइ (came) / त्रिबेनीं (to Triveni) / हरषित (joyful) / मज्जनु (bath) / कीन्ह (did) / कपिन्ह (with monkeys) / सहित (together) / बिप्रन्ह (to brahmins) / कहुँ (to) / दान (gifts) / बिबिध (various) / बिधि (ways) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::5270.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5270.essence: Blessing is sealed by joy that becomes giving.
ramacharitamanas::5270.simple_meaning: Ram joyfully bathed at Triveni and gave generous gifts to the monkeys and the brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::5270.simple_insight: Joy becomes complete when it turns into generosity.
ramacharitamanas::5270.detailed_meaning: After honoring Prayag and the sacred confluence, Ram arrives at Triveni with Sita and the company of monkeys. He bathes happily and gives gifts freely to the brahmins and his companions, marking a blessed pause before the journey to Ayodhya continues.
ramacharitamanas::5270.modern_relevance: After a long family trip, you finally reach the river everyone had talked about. Before moving on, you pause, wash off the dust, and quietly share what you have.
ramacharitamanas::5270.insight: It shifts the mind from private enjoyment to grateful giving.

ramacharitamanas::5271.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु हनुमंतहि कहा बुझाई। धरि बटु रूप अवधपुर जाई॥ भरतहि कुसल हमारि सुनाएहु। समाचार लै तुम्ह चलि आएहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5271.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर प्रभु ने हनुमान् जी को समझाकर कहा- तुम ब्रह्मचारी का रूप धरकर अवधपुरी को जाओ। भरत को हमारी कुशल सुनाना और उनका समाचार लेकर चले आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5271.english_translation: Then the Lord instructed Hanuman: "Go to Ayodhya in the form of a celibate ascetic. Give Bharata our news of well-being, and return bringing word of him."
ramacharitamanas::5271.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / हनुमंतहि (to Hanuman) / कहा (said) / बुझाई (explaining) / धरि (taking) / बटु रूप (the form of a celibate ascetic) / अवधपुर (to Ayodhya city) / जाई (go) / भरतहि (to Bharata) / कुसल (well-being) / हमारि (our) / सुनाएहु (tell) / समाचार (news) / लै (bringing) / तुम्ह (you) / चलि (going) / आएहु (come back)
ramacharitamanas::5271.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5271.essence: Even reunion begins with a messenger who knows how to carry love gently.
ramacharitamanas::5271.simple_meaning: Ram sends Hanuman to Ayodhya in disguise. He must tell Bharata that Ram is well and bring back Bharata's news.
ramacharitamanas::5271.simple_insight: Sometimes love moves through a messenger, not a grand reunion.
ramacharitamanas::5271.detailed_meaning: After the victory and the return to Ayodhya, Ram turns to Hanuman with a private task. Hanuman must travel in the guise of a celibate ascetic, reassure Bharata of Ram's well-being, and bring back Bharata's news. The reunion is still being gently prepared.
ramacharitamanas::5271.modern_relevance: You finally have good news for someone who has been waiting far too long, but you still choose the careful, respectful way to deliver it.
ramacharitamanas::5271.insight: It teaches you that even joy can be carried with tact, humility, and care for another person's heart.

ramacharitamanas::5272.verse_sanskrit: तुरत पवनसुत गवनत भयऊ। तब प्रभु भरद्वाज पहिं गयऊ॥ नाना बिधि मुनि पूजा कीन्ही। अस्तुति करि पुनि आसिष दीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5272.verse_hindi: पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही चल दिए। तब प्रभु भरद्वाजजी के पास गए। मुनि ने (इष्ट बुद्धि से) उनकी अनेकों प्रकार से पूजा की और स्तुति की और फिर (लीला की दृष्टि से) आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5272.english_translation: Hanuman left at once. Then the Lord went to Bharadwaja. The sage honored Him in many ways, praised Him, and then gave blessings.
ramacharitamanas::5272.translation_literal: तुरत (at once) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / गवनत (departing) / भयऊ (became) । तब (then) / प्रभु (the Lord) / भरद्वाज पहिं (to Bharadwaja) / गयऊ (went) ॥ नाना बिधि (in many ways) / मुनि (sage) / पूजा (honoring) / कीन्ही (did) । अस्तुति (praise) / करि (doing) / पुनि (again) / आसिष (blessing) / दीन्ही (gave) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5272.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5272.essence: Devotion deepens when action pauses to honor wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::5272.simple_meaning: Hanuman leaves immediately, and Ram visits Bharadwaja. The sage welcomes Him with worship, praise, and blessings.
ramacharitamanas::5272.simple_insight: True devotion meets reverence with ease, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::5272.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just been sent on his mission to Ayodhya. Before the journey continues, Ram goes to meet Bharadwaja, and the sage receives Him with full honor. The verse pauses the action to show sacred hospitality and mutual blessing.
ramacharitamanas::5272.modern_relevance: You finish one urgent task and still pause to greet the elder who helped you begin. That respectful pause changes the whole mood of the day.
ramacharitamanas::5272.insight: It teaches you to honor the people who hold the larger meaning of your work.

ramacharitamanas::5273.verse_sanskrit: मुनि पद बंदि जुगल कर जोरी। चढ़ि बिमान प्रभु चले बहोरी॥ इहाँ निषाद सुना प्रभु आए। नाव नाव कहँ लोग बोलाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5273.verse_hindi: दोनों हाथ जोड़कर तथा मुनि के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रभु विमान पर चढ़कर फिर (आगे) चले। यहाँ जब निषादराज ने सुना कि प्रभु आ गए, तब उसने 'नाव कहाँ है? नाव कहाँ है?' पुकारते हुए लोगों को बुलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5273.english_translation: After bowing to the sage and joining both hands, the Lord boarded the aerial car and moved on. When Nishadraj heard that the Lord had arrived here, he called out, "Where is the boat? Bring the boat!"
ramacharitamanas::5273.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / जुगल (both) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / चढ़ि (having mounted) / बिमान (aerial car) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चले (went) / बहोरी (again) / इहाँ (here) / निषाद (Nishadraj) / सुना (heard) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आए (have come) / नाव (boat) / नाव (boat) / कहँ (where) / लोग (people) / बोलाए (called out)
ramacharitamanas::5273.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5273.essence: Humility and prompt service travel together.
ramacharitamanas::5273.simple_meaning: Ram honors the sage, then continues on. News of his arrival reaches Nishadraj, who urgently calls for a boat.
ramacharitamanas::5273.simple_insight: Even the Lord moves with humility, and true devotion responds at once.
ramacharitamanas::5273.detailed_meaning: Ram leaves the sage after respectful worship and boards the celestial vehicle again. At the same time, Nishadraj hears that Ram has arrived nearby and immediately calls for a boat, preparing to serve without delay.
ramacharitamanas::5273.modern_relevance: You finish thanking someone who helped you, then step back into the car. Nearby, a friend hears you’re coming and starts arranging everything before you even ask.
ramacharitamanas::5273.insight: It shows reverence and readiness together: honor what is sacred, then move quickly to serve the moment.

ramacharitamanas::5274.verse_sanskrit: सुरसरि नाघि जान तब आयो। उतरेउ तट प्रभु आयसु पायो॥ तब सीताँ पूजी सुरसरी। बहु प्रकार पुनि चरनन्हि परी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5274.verse_hindi: इतने में ही विमान गंगाजी को लाँघकर (इस पार) आ गया और प्रभु की आज्ञा पाकर वह किनारे पर उतरा। तब सीताजी बहुत प्रकार से गंगाजी की पूजा करके फिर उनके चरणों पर गिरीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5274.english_translation: Meanwhile the aerial car crossed the Ganga and, on the Lord's command, landed on the bank. Then Sita worshipped the Ganga in many ways and bowed again at her feet.
ramacharitamanas::5274.translation_literal: सुरसरि (the divine river) / नाघि (crossing) / जान (the aerial car) / तब (then) / आयो (came) / उतरेउ (descended) / तट (bank) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आयसु (command) / पायो (received) / तब (then) / सीताँ (Sita) / पूजी (worshipped) / सुरसरी (the divine river) / बहु प्रकार (in many ways) / पुनि (again) / चरनन्हि (feet) / परी (fell)
ramacharitamanas::5274.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5274.essence: Safe arrival deepens humility, not pride.
ramacharitamanas::5274.simple_meaning: The flying car crosses the Ganga, lands on the bank, and Sita honors the river before bowing again.
ramacharitamanas::5274.simple_insight: Even after crossing safely, gratitude still comes first.
ramacharitamanas::5274.detailed_meaning: Ram’s party has crossed the Ganga and reached the bank. Sita responds not with haste, but with reverence: she honors the river that carried her onward. The scene pauses the journey to show humility and gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::5274.modern_relevance: You finally reach the other side after a hard trip, but you still stop to thank the people and forces that carried you there.
ramacharitamanas::5274.insight: It teaches you to meet arrival with gratitude, not entitlement.

ramacharitamanas::5275.verse_sanskrit: दीन्हि असीस हरषि मन गंगा। सुंदरि तव अहिवात अभंगा॥ सुनत गुहा धायउ प्रेमाकुल। आयउ निकट परम सुख संकुल ॥
ramacharitamanas::5275.verse_hindi: गंगाजी ने मन में हर्षित होकर आशीर्वाद दिया- हे सुंदरी! तुम्हारा सुहाग अखंड हो। भगवान् के तट पर उतरने की बात सुनते ही निषादराज गुह प्रेम में विह्वल होकर दौड़ा। परम सुख से परिपूर्ण होकर वह प्रभु के समीप आया, ॥
ramacharitamanas::5275.english_translation: Ganga blessed Sita in joy: “May your marriage be forever unbroken.” Hearing that the Lord had landed, Guha ran toward him, overwhelmed with love, and came near in bliss.
ramacharitamanas::5275.translation_literal: दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / हरषि (rejoicing) / मन (in heart) / गंगा (Ganga) । सुंदरि (beautiful one) / तव (your) / अहिवात (marriage bond / married life) / अभंगा (unbroken) ॥ सुनत (hearing) / गुहा (Guha) / धायउ (ran) / प्रेमाकुल (overwhelmed with love) । आयउ (came) / निकट (near) / परम (supreme) / सुख (joy) / संकुल (filled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5275.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5275.essence: Love recognises the beloved and rushes toward him.
ramacharitamanas::5275.simple_meaning: Ganga blesses Sita’s married life, and Guha rushes toward Ram with overflowing love when he hears that Ram has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::5275.simple_insight: Love moves faster than thought when the heart recognises what it has longed for.
ramacharitamanas::5275.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have just crossed the Ganga and landed on the bank. Ganga blesses Sita with an unbroken married bond, and Guha, the loyal boatman and king of the Nishads, runs to meet Ram in a rush of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5275.modern_relevance: You hear the message that someone you deeply respect has arrived nearby, and your whole body moves before your mind catches up. Some meetings are felt as joy before they are understood.
ramacharitamanas::5275.insight: It shows devotion as an instinctive response: the heart runs toward what it reveres.

ramacharitamanas::5276.verse_sanskrit: प्रभुहि सहित बिलोकि बैदेही। परेउ अवनि तन सुधि नहिं तेही॥ प्रीति परम बिलोकि रघुराई। हरषि उठाइ लियो उर लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5276.verse_hindi: और श्री जानकीजी सहित प्रभु को देखकर वह (आनंद-समाधि में मग्न होकर) पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, उसे शरीर की सुधि न रही। श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसका परम प्रेम देखकर उसे उठाकर हर्ष के साथ हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5276.english_translation: And seeing the Lord together with Sita, he fell to the ground and lost all awareness of his body. Seeing that supreme love, Raghunath joyfully lifted him up and drew him to his heart.
ramacharitamanas::5276.translation_literal: प्रभुहि (the Lord) / सहित (together with) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बैदेही (Sita) / परेउ (fell) / अवनि (on the ground) / तन (body) / सुधि (awareness) / नहिं (not) / तेही (to him) / प्रीति (love) / परम (supreme) / बिलोकि (seeing) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / हरषि (joyfully) / उठाइ (lifting up) / लियो (took) / उर (to the heart) / लाई (having placed)
ramacharitamanas::5276.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5276.essence: Pure devotion collapses the self, and Ram answers by drawing it close.
ramacharitamanas::5276.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram and Sita, Hanuman falls in devotion and loses awareness of his body. Ram responds by lifting him up and holding him close.
ramacharitamanas::5276.simple_insight: Deep love does not make you smaller; it makes you known and welcomed.
ramacharitamanas::5276.detailed_meaning: Hanuman reaches the moment he has crossed oceans for: he sees Ram and Sita together in safety. Overwhelmed, he falls down without body-awareness. Ram notices that pure devotion immediately and embraces him with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5276.modern_relevance: You finally arrive after a long, exhausting journey and see the person you came for safe. The relief is so complete that your knees give way before your mind can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::5276.insight: It shows that sincere devotion is not ignored; it is received, recognized, and answered with intimacy.

ramacharitamanas::5277.verse_sanskrit: लियो हृदयँ लाइ कृपा निधान सुजान रायँ रमापति। बैठारि परम समीप बूझी कुसल सो कर बीनती॥ अब कुसल पद पंकज बिलोकि बिरंचि संकर सेब्य जे। सुख धाम पूरनकाम राम नमामि राम नमामि ते ॥
ramacharitamanas::5277.verse_hindi: सुजानों के राजा (शिरोमणि), लक्ष्मीकांत, कृपानिधान भगवान् ने उसको हृदय से लगा लिया और अत्यंत निकट बैठकर कुशल पूछी। वह विनती करने लगा- आपके जो चरणकमल ब्रह्माजी और शंकरजी से सेवित हैं, उनके दर्शन करके मैं अब सकुशल हूँ। हे सुखधाम! हे पूर्णकाम श्री रामजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ, नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5277.english_translation: The Lord of Lakshmi, the treasure of compassion, drew him to his heart, seated him close, and asked after his well-being. He replied, "Seeing your lotus feet, served by Brahma and Shiva, I am now well. O abode of joy, O one whose every wish is already fulfilled, Lord Ram, I bow to you again and again."
ramacharitamanas::5277.translation_literal: लियो (took) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लाइ (bringing) / कृपा निधान (treasure of compassion) / सुजान रायँ (wise king) / रमापति (Lord of Lakshmi) / बैठारि (having seated) / परम समीप (very near) / बूझी (asked) / कुसल (well-being) / सो (he) / कर (did) / बीनती (request, prayer) / अब (now) / कुसल (well) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / संकर (Shiva) / सेब्य (served by) / जे (which) / सुख धाम (abode of joy) / पूरनकाम (fully fulfilled in desire) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow) / राम (Ram) / नमामि (I bow)
ramacharitamanas::5277.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5277.essence: Ram's nearness turns reverence into relief.
ramacharitamanas::5277.simple_meaning: Ram lovingly brings the devotee close, asks after his welfare, and receives a prayer of reverent surrender. Seeing Ram's feet, served even by Brahma and Shiva, the devotee feels fully blessed.
ramacharitamanas::5277.simple_insight: When devotion becomes real, even greeting Ram feels like receiving everything you needed.
ramacharitamanas::5277.detailed_meaning: After the battle, the devotee is overwhelmed by Ram's presence. Ram pulls him close, seats him near, and asks about his welfare. In response, the devotee bows before the feet that even Brahma and Shiva serve.
ramacharitamanas::5277.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you admire deeply, and they pull out a chair for you and ask how you're doing. The moment you realize their warmth is real, gratitude turns into tears.
ramacharitamanas::5277.insight: It shifts devotion from distance to intimacy: Ram is not only praised, but personally near and caring.

ramacharitamanas::5278.verse_sanskrit: सब भाँति अधम निषाद सो हरि भरत ज्यों उर लाइयो। मतिमंद तुलसीदास सो प्रभु मोह बस बिसराइयो॥ यह रावनारि चरित्र पावन राम पद रतिप्रद सदा। कामादिहर बिग्यानकर सुर सिद्ध मुनि गावहिं मुदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5278.verse_hindi: सब प्रकार से नीच उस निषाद को भगवान् ने भरतजी की भाँति हृदय से लगा लिया। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- इस मंदबुद्धि ने (मैंने) मोहवश उस प्रभु को भुला दिया। रावण के शत्रु का यह पवित्र करने वाला चरित्र सदा ही श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रीति उत्पन्न करने वाला है। यह कामादि विकारों को हरने वाला और (भगवान् के स्वरूप का) विशेष ज्ञान उत्पन्न करने वाला है। देवता, सिद्ध और मुनि आनंदित होकर इसे गाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5278.english_translation: The Lord embraced that utterly low Nishad like Bharat. Tulsidas says: I, dull and deluded, forgot that Lord through confusion. This pure account of the enemy of Ravana always awakens love for Ram's feet. It destroys desire and other faults, and gives special knowledge of the divine form. Devas, perfected beings, and sages sing it with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5278.translation_literal: सब भाँति (in every way) / अधम (lowly) / निषाद (Nishad) / सो (that one) / हरि (Ram) / भरत ज्यों (like Bharat) / उर लाइयो (embraced to the heart) / मतिमंद (dull-minded) / तुलसीदास सो (Tulsidas, that one) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोह बस (under the power of delusion) / बिसराइयो (forgot) / यह (this) / रावनारि (enemy of Ravana) / चरित्र (deeds, story) / पावन (purifying) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / रति प्रद (giver of love) / सदा (always) / कामादिहर (desire and the rest) / बिग्यानकर (making known, giving special knowledge) / सुर (devas) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनि (sages) / गावहिं (sing) / मुदा (with joy)
ramacharitamanas::5278.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5278.essence: Ram's embrace reaches the lowest heart and turns it toward love.
ramacharitamanas::5278.simple_meaning: Ram welcomes the humblest person with the same love he shows Bharat. Tulsidas also admits his own forgetfulness, then says Ram's story purifies the heart, deepens love, and quiets desire.
ramacharitamanas::5278.simple_insight: You do not need to be worthy first; being held by Ram is what makes the heart чист.
ramacharitamanas::5278.detailed_meaning: After the war, the victorious Ram greets even a lowly Nishad with the same affection he showed Bharat. Tulsidas turns inward, confessing his own delusion. He then praises this entire account of Ravana's defeat as a sacred story that softens the heart and awakens devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5278.modern_relevance: You meet someone who feels invisible at a funeral, and everyone else walks past. One kind look changes them more than any speech. This verse says that kind of welcome is Ram's nature.
ramacharitamanas::5278.insight: It shifts the reader from judging worthiness to recognising that devotion grows through being received.

ramacharitamanas::5279.verse_sanskrit: समर बिजय रघुबीर के चरित जे सुनहिं सुजान। बिजय बिबेक बिभूति नित तिन्हहि देहिं भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5279.verse_hindi: जो सुजान लोग श्री रघुवीर की समर विजय संबंधी लीला को सुनते हैं, उनको भगवान् नित्य विजय, विवेक और विभूति (ऐश्वर्य) देते हैं॥।121 (क)॥
ramacharitamanas::5279.english_translation: Those wise ones who hear the victorious battle deeds of Raghubir are always given victory, discernment, and prosperity by the divine.
ramacharitamanas::5279.translation_literal: समर (battle) / बिजय (victory) / रघुबीर के (of Raghubir) / चरित (deeds, story) / जे (who) / सुनहिं (hear) / सुजान (wise) / नित (always) / तिन्हहि (to them) / देहिं (give) / भगवान (the divine) / विजय (victory) / बिबेक (discernment) / बिभूति (prosperity, splendor)
ramacharitamanas::5279.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5279.essence: Ram's victory becomes your own when you truly hear it.
ramacharitamanas::5279.simple_meaning: People who listen deeply to Ram's victorious story receive victory, clear judgment, and prosperity from the divine.
ramacharitamanas::5279.simple_insight: What you take in shapes what returns to you.
ramacharitamanas::5279.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's defeat, Tulsidas closes the war section with a blessing: anyone wise enough to hear Ram's victorious story is inwardly transformed. The story itself becomes a source of strength, clarity, and abundance.
ramacharitamanas::5279.modern_relevance: You finish reading a story of courage on the train ride home, and something in your chest steadies. Certain stories do more than entertain — they quietly train your mind to win cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::5279.insight: It shifts attention from passive listening to receiving a living force that sharpens judgment and strengthens action.

ramacharitamanas::5280.verse_sanskrit: यह कलिकाल मलायतन मन करि देखु बिचार। श्री रघुनाथ नाम तजि नाहिन आन अधार ॥
ramacharitamanas::5280.verse_hindi: अरे मन! विचार करके देख! यह कलिकाल पापों का घर है। इसमें श्री रघुनाथजी के नाम को छोड़कर (पापों से बचने के लिए) दूसरा कोई आधार नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5280.english_translation: O mind, reflect carefully: this age is a dwelling of impurity. Apart from the name of Shri Raghunath, there is no other support.
ramacharitamanas::5280.translation_literal: यह (this) / कलिकाल (the age of Kali) / मलायतन (dwelling of impurity) / मन (mind) / करि (having done) / देखु (see) / बिचार (reflection) / श्री रघुनाथ (Shri Raghunath) / नाम (name) / तजि (leaving) / नाहिन (not) / आन (other) / अधार (support)
ramacharitamanas::5280.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5280.essence: Ram's name is the only support that holds in a corrupt age.
ramacharitamanas::5280.simple_meaning: This age is full of corruption and confusion. In such a time, only Ram's name can truly support you.
ramacharitamanas::5280.simple_insight: You can stop searching for firmer ground and rest in what never fails.
ramacharitamanas::5280.detailed_meaning: After the war and victory, Tulsidas turns from battle to warning the mind itself. He says this age is full of impurity, and when everything else feels unstable, only Shri Raghunath's name remains a true refuge.
ramacharitamanas::5280.modern_relevance: When your phone is full of bad news, your plans have collapsed, and even your own thoughts feel unreliable, you need something steadier than panic. This verse points you back to the one support that does not shake.
ramacharitamanas::5280.insight: It shifts you from scattered reliance to inward refuge in Ram's name.

ramacharitamanas::5281.verse_sanskrit: केकीकण्ठाभनीलं सुरवरविलसद्विप्रपादाब्जचिह्नं शोभाढ्यं पीतवस्त्रं सरसिजनयनं सर्वदा सुप्रसन्नम् । पाणौ नाराचचापं कपिनिकरयुतं बन्धुना सेव्यमानं। नौमीड्यं जानकीशं रघुवरमनिशं पुष्पकारूढरामम् ॥1।
ramacharitamanas::5281.verse_hindi: मोर के कण्ठ की आभा के समान (हरिताभ) नीलवर्ण, देवताओं में श्रेष्ठ, ब्राह्मण (भृगुजी) के चरणकमल के चिह्न से सुशोभित, शोभा से पूर्ण, पीताम्बरधारी, कजानकीकरसरोजलालितौ चिन्तकस्य मनभृंगसंगिनौ ॥ कोसलपुरी के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी के सुंदर और कोमल दोनों चरणकमल ब्रह्माजी और शिवजी द्वारा वन्दित हैं, श्री जानकीजी के करकमलों से दुलराए हुए हैं और चिन्तन करने वाले के मन रूपी भौंरे के नित्य संगी हैं अर्थात् चिन्तन करने वालों का मन रूपी भ्रमर सदा उन चरणकमलों में बसा रहता है ॥ कमल नेत्र, सदा परम प्रसन्न, हाथों में बाण और धनुष धारण किए हुए, वानर समूह से युक्त भाई लक्ष्मणजी से सेवित, स्तुति किए जाने योग्य, श्री जानकीजी के पति, रघुकुल श्रेष्ठ, पुष्पक विमान पर सवार श्री रामचंद्रजी को मैं निरंतर नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5281.english_translation: I bow again and again to Rama, the lord of Janaki, the best of the Raghu line, seated in the Pushpaka विमान, blue like a peacock's neck, marked by the footprints of the best of sages, radiant, clothed in yellow, lotus-eyed, always serene, bearing bow and arrows, served by Lakshmana and a host of monkeys.
ramacharitamanas::5281.translation_literal: केकीकण्ठाभनीलं (blue like a peacock's neck) / सुरवरविलसद्विप्रपादाब्जचिह्नं (marked by the lotus-feet of the best of sages) / शोभाढ्यं (full of splendour) / पीतवस्त्रं (wearing yellow garments) / सरसिजनयनं (lotus-eyed) / सर्वदा सुप्रसन्नम् (always very serene) / पाणौ (in the hand) / नाराचचापं (arrows and bow) / कपिनिकरयुतं (accompanied by a host of monkeys) / बन्धुना (by the brother) / सेव्यमानं (being served) / नौमि (I bow) / ईड्यं (praiseworthy) / जानकीशं (lord of Janaki) / रघुवरम् (best of the Raghu line) / अनिशं (constantly) / पुष्पकारूढरामम् (Rama seated in Pushpaka)
ramacharitamanas::5281.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5281.essence: Rama's greatness is shown through calm beauty, service, and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::5281.simple_meaning: Rama is beautiful, serene, and worthy of constant reverence. He is the lord of Janaki, served by Lakshmana and the monkey host, and seated in the Pushpaka विमान.
ramacharitamanas::5281.simple_insight: Reverence can be steady, tender, and full of detail.
ramacharitamanas::5281.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas opens this section of Uttarkand with praise, not argument. He paints Rama after victory: radiant, calm, honored by sages, served by Lakshmana, and carried in the Pushpaka विमान. The verse sets the devotional mood for what follows.
ramacharitamanas::5281.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a long, hard season and finally notice how peace looks on a face. This verse lingers on that kind of earned radiance.
ramacharitamanas::5281.insight: It shifts attention from abstract divinity to the felt beauty of presence, service, and serenity.

ramacharitamanas::5282.verse_sanskrit: कोसलेन्द्रपदकन्जमंजुलौ कोमलावजमहेशवन्दितौ। कुन्दइन्दुदरगौरसुन्दरं अम्बिकापतिमभीष्टसिद्धिदम् । कारुणीककलकन्जलोचनं नौमि शंकरमनंगमोचनम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::5282.verse_hindi: कुन्द के फूल, चंद्रमा और शंख के समान सुंदर गौरवर्ण, जगज्जननी श्री पार्वतीजी के पति, वान्छित फल के देने वाले, (दुखियों पर सदा), दया करने वाले, सुंदर कमल के समान नेत्र वाले, कामदेव से छुड़ाने वाले (कल्याणकारी) श्री शंकरजी को मैं नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5282.english_translation: I bow to Shankar, the husband of Ambika, whose lotus-like feet are worshipped by Mahesh, whose body is fair and beautiful like jasmine, moonlight, and a conch, whose eyes are like lotus petals, who grants desired fruits, is full of compassion, and frees from desire.
