ramacharitamanas::5282.translation_literal: कोसलेन्द्रपदकन्जमंजुलौ (with lovely lotus-feet of the lord of Kosala) / कोमलावजमहेशवन्दितौ (softly worshipped by Mahesh) / कुन्दइन्दुदरगौरसुन्दरं (fair and beautiful like jasmine, moon, and conch) / अम्बिकापतिमभीष्टसिद्धिदम् (the husband of Ambika, giver of desired fruits) / कारुणीककलकन्जलोचनं (compassionate, with lotus-like eyes) / नौमि (I bow) / शंकरमनंगमोचनम् (to Shankar, the remover of desire)
ramacharitamanas::5282.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5282.simple_meaning: The verse praises Shiva as beautiful, compassionate, and able to free people from desire while granting what they seek.
ramacharitamanas::5282.simple_insight: Reverence can steady the heart before anything else does.
ramacharitamanas::5282.detailed_meaning: At the opening of Uttarkand, the narrator turns from the story of Ram to a devotional praise of Shiva. He is described as beautiful, compassionate, and worshipped even by the great ones, setting a sacred tone before the dialogue begins.
ramacharitamanas::5282.modern_relevance: Before a difficult conversation, you pause for one quiet breath and remember what steadies you. The mind stops chasing approval, and something calmer takes over.
ramacharitamanas::5282.insight: It shifts attention from craving to reverence, so the heart becomes less restless.

ramacharitamanas::5283.verse_sanskrit: रहा एक दिन अवधि कर अति आरत पुर लोग। जहँ तहँ सोचहिं नारि नर कृस तन राम बियोग॥
ramacharitamanas::5283.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के लौटने की अवधि का एक ही दिन बाकी रह गया, अतएव नगर के लोग बहुत आतुर (अधीर) हो रहे हैं। राम के वियोग में दुबले हुए स्त्री-पुरुष जहाँ-तहाँ सोच (विचार) कर रहे हैं (कि क्या बात है श्री रामजी क्यों नहीं आए)।
ramacharitamanas::5283.english_translation: One day remained until the promised return, and the people of the city were deeply restless. Men and women, worn thin by separation from Ram, kept wondering what had kept him away.
ramacharitamanas::5283.translation_literal: रहा (remained) / एक दिन (one day) / अवधि कर (of the promised time) / अति आरत (very restless) / पुर लोग (people of the city) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / सोचहिं (they think) / नारि नर (women and men) / कृस तन (thin-bodied) / राम बियोग (separation from Ram)
ramacharitamanas::5283.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5283.essence: Longing for Ram makes the whole city ache.
ramacharitamanas::5283.simple_meaning: The city is counting the final day before Ram returns, and everyone is anxious with longing.
ramacharitamanas::5283.simple_insight: Waiting can make even a whole city feel thin with longing.
ramacharitamanas::5283.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram's promised return is down to the last day. The people are restless, weakened by separation, and keep asking themselves why he has not yet come. The verse sets up the coming signs of his arrival.
ramacharitamanas::5283.modern_relevance: You keep checking the clock before someone you love is due home, and every minute feels stretched. That restless waiting is exactly the city's mood here.
ramacharitamanas::5283.insight: It captures how longing distorts time and makes absence physically felt.

ramacharitamanas::5284.verse_sanskrit: सगुन होहिं सुंदर सकल मन प्रसन्न सब केर। प्रभु आगवन जनाव जनु नगर रम्य चहुँ फेर॥
ramacharitamanas::5284.verse_hindi: इतने में सब सुंदर शकुन होने लगे और सबके मन प्रसन्न हो गए। नगर भी चारों ओर से रमणीक हो गया। मानो ये सब के सब चिह्न प्रभु के (शुभ) आगमन को जना रहे हैं।
ramacharitamanas::5284.english_translation: In that moment, all the omens turned beautiful and everyone’s heart became joyful. The whole city looked lovely from every side, as if all these signs were announcing the Lord’s arrival.
ramacharitamanas::5284.translation_literal: सगुन (omens) / होहिं (become) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सकल (all) / मन (minds/hearts) / प्रसन्न (joyful) / सब (all) / केर (of everyone) / प्रभु (Lord) / आगवन (arrival) / जनाव (announce) / जनु (as if) / नगर (city) / रम्य (beautiful) / चहुँ फेर (on all four sides)
ramacharitamanas::5284.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5284.essence: Hope makes the whole world look newly alive.
ramacharitamanas::5284.simple_meaning: Good signs appear, everyone feels happy, and the whole city seems to bloom as Ram’s return draws near.
ramacharitamanas::5284.simple_insight: Joy spreads outward when the thing you long for is finally close.
ramacharitamanas::5284.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is counting the last day before Ram’s return. The city’s mood shifts at once: omens brighten, hearts lift, and even the streets seem transformed. This verse paints the atmosphere, not the arrival itself.
ramacharitamanas::5284.modern_relevance: You hear the front door open after a long wait, and the whole house changes before anyone speaks. Relief arrives first as atmosphere, then as words.
ramacharitamanas::5284.insight: It shows how anticipation can turn an ordinary place into a living sign of hope.

ramacharitamanas::5285.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्यादि मातु सब मन अनंद अस होइ। आयउ प्रभु श्री अनुज जुत कहन चहत अब कोइ॥
ramacharitamanas::5285.verse_hindi: कौसल्या आदि सब माताओं के मन में ऐसा आनंद हो रहा है जैसे अभी कोई कहना ही चाहता है कि सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी आ गए।
ramacharitamanas::5285.english_translation: The minds of Kaushalya and the other mothers overflowed with joy, as if someone was about to say that Lord Shri Ram had arrived with his younger brother.
ramacharitamanas::5285.translation_literal: कौसल्यादि (Kaushalya and others) / मातु (mothers) / सब (all) / मन (mind) / अनंद (joy) / अस (like this) / होइ (happened) / आयउ (has come) / प्रभु (the Lord) / श्री (auspicious) / अनुज (younger brother) / जुत (together with) / कहन (to say) / चहत (wants) / अब (now) / कोइ (someone)
ramacharitamanas::5285.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5285.essence: Deep longing can make arrival feel real before it happens.
ramacharitamanas::5285.simple_meaning: The mothers are so happy that it feels as if Ram has already returned with Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::5285.simple_insight: Joy can arrive before the moment itself, when hope becomes almost real.
ramacharitamanas::5285.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is trembling with expectation as Ram's return draws near. The mothers, led by Kaushalya, feel such overwhelming joy that it seems the news is already on their lips: Ram has come back with his younger brother.
ramacharitamanas::5285.modern_relevance: You hear the front door unlock after a long absence, and your whole body lifts before you even see who it is. Hope can make the heart celebrate early.
ramacharitamanas::5285.insight: It captures how longing turns anticipation into felt presence.

ramacharitamanas::5286.verse_sanskrit: भरत नयन भुज दच्छिन फरकत बारहिं बार। जानि सगुन मन हरष अति लागे करन बिचार॥
ramacharitamanas::5286.verse_hindi: भरतजी की दाहिनी आँख और दाहिनी भुजा बार-बार फड़क रही है। इसे शुभ शकुन जानकर उनके मन में अत्यंत हर्ष हुआ और वे विचार करने लगे-
ramacharitamanas::5286.english_translation: Bharat's right eye and right arm kept twitching again and again. Taking it as an auspicious sign, his heart filled with joy, and he began to reflect.
ramacharitamanas::5286.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / नयन (eye) / भुज (arm) / दच्छिन (right) / फरकत (twitching) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / जानि (knowing) / सगुन (auspicious sign) / मन (mind) / हरष (joy) / अति (greatly) / लागे (began) / करन (to do) / बिचार (reflection)
ramacharitamanas::5286.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5286.essence: A longing heart turns even a twitch into news.
ramacharitamanas::5286.simple_meaning: Bharat notices a repeated auspicious twitch in his body and feels hopeful enough to start thinking about what it means.
ramacharitamanas::5286.simple_insight: Hope can arrive through the smallest signs, even before the mind understands them.
ramacharitamanas::5286.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat waits through the final day of Ram's exile, holding the kingdom only as a burden. A repeated twitch in his right eye and arm makes him hopeful for Ram's return, and that hope immediately turns into anxious reflection.
ramacharitamanas::5286.modern_relevance: You catch a small sign in a message, a glance, or a delay, and your whole mood changes. Hope and worry can both begin with the tiniest cue.
ramacharitamanas::5286.insight: It shows how longing makes the mind read meaning into every small sign.

ramacharitamanas::5287.verse_sanskrit: रहेउ एक दिन अवधि अधारा। समुझत मन दुख भयउ अपारा॥ कारन कवन नाथ नहिं आयउ। जानि कुटिल किधौं मोहि बिसरायउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5287.verse_hindi: प्राणों की आधार रूप अवधि का एक ही दिन शेष रह गया। यह सोचते ही भरतजी के मन में अपार दुःख हुआ। क्या कारण हुआ कि नाथ नहीं आए? प्रभु ने कुटिल जानकर मुझे कहीं भुला तो नहीं दिया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5287.english_translation: One day remained in the span that was the support of his life. Thinking this, Bharat felt immense sorrow. "Why has the Lord not come? Has he seen me as crooked and forgotten me?"
ramacharitamanas::5287.translation_literal: रहेउ (remained) / एक दिन (one day) / अवधि (the appointed span) / अधारा (support) । समुझत (thinking) / मन (mind) / दुख (sorrow) / भयउ (became) / अपारा (boundless) ॥ कारन (reason) / कवन (what) / नाथ (Lord) / नहिं (not) / आयउ (came) । जानि (knowing) / कुटिल (crooked) / किधौं (perhaps) / मोहि (me) / बिसरायउ (forgot) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5287.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5287.essence: Longing turns into self-doubt when love does not return on time.
ramacharitamanas::5287.simple_meaning: Bharat has only one day left before his vow ends, and the delay in Ram's return fills him with grief and self-doubt.
ramacharitamanas::5287.simple_insight: Love can become painful when absence stretches too long.
ramacharitamanas::5287.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has been holding the kingdom in trust for Ram, counting the days until his return. Now only one day remains, and the thought that Ram still has not come breaks his heart. He wonders if Ram has judged him crooked and turned away.
ramacharitamanas::5287.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after promising yourself you won't. The silence starts to feel personal, and your mind turns the delay into a verdict.
ramacharitamanas::5287.insight: It shifts the mind from neutral delay to the fear of being rejected.

ramacharitamanas::5288.verse_sanskrit: अहह धन्य लछिमन बड़भागी। राम पदारबिंदु अनुरागी॥ कपटी कुटिल मोहि प्रभु चीन्हा। ताते नाथ संग नहिं लीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5288.verse_hindi: अहा हा! लक्ष्मण बड़े धन्य एवं बड़भागी हैं, जो श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणारविन्द के प्रेमी हैं (अर्थात् उनसे अलग नहीं हुए)। मुझे तो प्रभु ने कपटी और कुटिल पहचान लिया, इसी से नाथ ने मुझे साथ नहीं लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5288.english_translation: Ah, Lakshman is truly blessed and fortunate, for he is devoted to Ram's lotus feet. The Lord recognized me as deceitful and crooked, and so he did not take me along.
ramacharitamanas::5288.translation_literal: अहह (ah) / धन्य (blessed) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / बड़भागी (very fortunate) / राम (Ram) / पदारबिंदु (lotus feet) / अनुरागी (loving devotee) / कपटी (deceitful) / कुटिल (crooked) / मोहि (me) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चीन्हा (recognized) / ताते (therefore) / नाथ (Lord) / संग (with) / नहिं (not) / लीन्हा (took)
ramacharitamanas::5288.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::5288.essence: Ram's nearness reveals love, and exposes what cannot stay close.
ramacharitamanas::5288.simple_meaning: Bharat sees Lakshman as fortunate because he stayed devoted to Ram. He also admits that his own flaws kept him from being taken along.
ramacharitamanas::5288.simple_insight: Devotion draws you close; hidden crookedness quietly creates distance.
ramacharitamanas::5288.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand's grief-filled longing, Bharat waits one day from Ram's promised return and suddenly turns inward. He blesses Lakshman for his steady love, then confesses that Ram saw the deceit in him and left him behind.
ramacharitamanas::5288.modern_relevance: You watch someone else get the trust, the invitation, the closer seat at the table. Instead of blaming the world, you notice the part of you that made distance inevitable.
ramacharitamanas::5288.insight: It shifts attention from resentment to self-honesty, showing that closeness depends on character, not claim.

ramacharitamanas::5289.verse_sanskrit: जौं करनी समुझै प्रभु मोरी। नहिं निस्तार कलप सत कोरी॥ जन अवगुन प्रभु मान न काऊ। दीन बंधु अति मृदुल सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5289.verse_hindi: (बात भी ठीक ही है, क्योंकि) यदि प्रभु मेरी करनी पर ध्यान दें तो सौ करोड़ (असंख्य) कल्पों तक भी मेरा निस्तार (छुटकारा) नहीं हो सकता (परंतु आशा इतनी ही है कि), प्रभु सेवक का अवगुण कभी नहीं मानते। वे दीनबंधु हैं और अत्यंत ही कोमल स्वभाव के हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5289.english_translation: If my deeds are truly weighed, even countless ages cannot save me. But the Lord never counts a servant’s faults; the friend of the humble is tender by nature.
ramacharitamanas::5289.translation_literal: जौं (if) / करनी (deeds, conduct) / समुझै (is understood, is judged) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मोरी (my) / नहिं (not) / निस्तार (release, deliverance) / कलप (ages) / सत (hundred) / कोरी (crores) / जन (servant) / अवगुन (faults) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मान (counts, accepts) / न (not) / काऊ (any) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / अति (very) / मृदुल (gentle, tender) / सुभाऊ (nature)
ramacharitamanas::5289.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::5289.essence: Mercy matters more than your self-judgment.
ramacharitamanas::5289.simple_meaning: Bharat feels unworthy if his conduct is judged honestly, but he trusts that Ram does not keep score of a servant’s faults.
ramacharitamanas::5289.simple_insight: There is relief in being met by mercy instead of judgment.
ramacharitamanas::5289.detailed_meaning: Bharat, grieving in Ayodhya and longing for Ram’s return, turns inward and sees his own flaws. Yet he trusts Ram’s nature: the humble are not rejected, because Ram is gentle with those who serve him.
ramacharitamanas::5289.modern_relevance: You replay one mistake after another while waiting for a reply you dread. This verse steadies you: the person who truly loves you may not be keeping the same harsh record you are.
ramacharitamanas::5289.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to trust in compassionate recognition.

ramacharitamanas::5290.verse_sanskrit: मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ सोई। मिलिहहिं राम सगुन सुभ होई॥ बीतें अवधि रहहिं जौं प्राना। अधम कवन जग मोहि समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5290.verse_hindi: अतएव मेरे हृदय में ऐसा पक्का भरोसा है कि श्री रामजी अवश्य मिलेंगे, (क्योंकि) मुझे शकुन बड़े शुभ हो रहे हैं, किंतु अवधि बीत जाने पर यदि मेरे प्राण रह गए तो जगत् में मेरे समान नीच कौन होगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5290.english_translation: My heart holds firm trust that Ram will meet me, for the signs are all auspicious. But if the time passes and I still live, who in the world would be more lowly than I?
ramacharitamanas::5290.translation_literal: मोरे (my) / जियँ (in the heart) / भरोस (trust) / दृढ़ (firm) / सोई (that only) / मिलिहहिं (will meet) / राम (Ram) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सुभ (good) / होई (are) / बीतें (having passed) / अवधि (the set time) / रहहिं (remain) / जौं (if) / प्राना (life-breath) / अधम (lowest) / कवन (who) / जग (in the world) / मोहि (me) / समाना (equal)
ramacharitamanas::5290.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5290.essence: Firm trust can survive the long silence of waiting.
ramacharitamanas::5290.simple_meaning: The speaker is certain Ram will come because the signs are favorable. If the promised time passes and life still remains, that would feel unbearable and shameful.
ramacharitamanas::5290.simple_insight: Trust can steady you even while you are still waiting and longing.
ramacharitamanas::5290.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand, the speaker is still living inside separation from Ram, yet refuses despair. The heart reads auspicious signs as reassurance, but the real ache is time itself: if the waiting ends and Ram still has not come, life would feel empty.
ramacharitamanas::5290.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending the message that matters most. Nothing has arrived yet, but your heart keeps reading small signs as hope.
ramacharitamanas::5290.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious waiting to trust that can endure delay.

ramacharitamanas::5291.verse_sanskrit: राम बिरह सागर महँ भरत मगन मन होत। बिप्र रूप धरि पवनसुत आइ गयउ जनु पोत॥1क॥
ramacharitamanas::5291.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के विरह समुद्र में भरतजी का मन डूब रहा था, उसी समय पवनपुत्र हनुमान् जी ब्राह्मण का रूप धरकर इस प्रकार आ गए, मानो (उन्हें डूबने से बचाने के लिए) नाव आ गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5291.english_translation: While Bharat was sinking in the ocean of separation from Ram, Hanuman arrived in the form of a Brahmin, like a boat coming to rescue him.
ramacharitamanas::5291.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिरह (separation) / सागर (ocean) / महँ (in) / भरत (Bharat) / मगन (immersed) / मन (mind) / होत (was becoming) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / रूप (form) / धरि (having taken) / पवनसुत (son of the wind, Hanuman) / आइ (coming) / गयउ (came) / जनु (as if) / पोत (boat)
ramacharitamanas::5291.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5291.essence: Help arrives when longing feels most unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::5291.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by longing for Ram, and Hanuman arrives in disguise like a boat that saves someone from drowning.
ramacharitamanas::5291.simple_insight: When grief feels endless, help can arrive quietly and just in time.
ramacharitamanas::5291.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is drowning in separation from Ram after the exile. At that very moment, Hanuman reaches him in the form of a Brahmin, opening the way for their meeting. The verse sets up the rescue; the next line shows Bharat’s tears and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5291.modern_relevance: You are sitting alone after a painful message, staring at your phone, unable to steady yourself. Then a calm friend calls at exactly the right minute.
ramacharitamanas::5291.insight: It frames rescue as timely grace, not self-effort, and prepares the mind for Hanuman’s arrival.

ramacharitamanas::5292.verse_sanskrit: बैठे देखि कुसासन जटा मुकुट कृस गात॥ राम राम रघुपति जपत स्रवत नयन जलजात॥1ख॥
ramacharitamanas::5292.verse_hindi: हनुमान् जी ने दुर्बल शरीर भरतजी को जटाओं का मुकुट बनाए, राम! राम! रघुपति! जपते और कमल के समान नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं) का जल बहाते कुश के आसन पर बैठे देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5292.english_translation: Seeing him seated on a grass seat, with matted hair as his crown and a lean body, he kept chanting, "Ram, Ram, Raghupati," while tears streamed from his lotus eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5292.translation_literal: बैठे (seated) / देखि (seeing) / कुसासन (grass seat) / जटा मुकुट (matted-hair crown) / कृस गात (lean body) / राम राम (Ram Ram) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / जपत (chanting) / स्रवत (flowing) / नयन (eyes) / जलजात (lotus-born)
ramacharitamanas::5292.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5292.essence: What remains when everything else is stripped away is devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5292.simple_meaning: Bharat sits on a simple grass seat, thin and devoted, repeating Ram's name with tears in his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5292.simple_insight: Love can make even grief feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::5292.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand's emotional meeting, Hanuman finds Bharat living like an ascetic, far from royal comfort, chanting Ram's name through tears. The sight reveals how completely Bharat has surrendered power and kept only devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5292.modern_relevance: You open a video call and see someone you love holding themselves together by sheer loyalty. They have almost nothing left, except the name they keep repeating.
ramacharitamanas::5292.insight: It shifts attention from outward status to inward devotion as the true measure of a life.

ramacharitamanas::5293.verse_sanskrit: देखत हनूमान अति हरषेउ। पुलक गात लोचन जल बरषेउ॥ मन महँ बहुत भाँति सुख मानी। बोलेउ श्रवन सुधा सम बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5293.verse_hindi: उन्हें देखते ही हनुमान् जी अत्यंत हर्षित हुए। उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया, नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बरसने लगा। मन में बहुत प्रकार से सुख मानकर वे कानों के लिए अमृत के समान वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5293.english_translation: Seeing him, Hanuman was overjoyed. His body thrilled with delight, and tears of love fell from his eyes. His mind filled with many kinds of happiness, and he spoke words like nectar to the ears.
ramacharitamanas::5293.translation_literal: देखत (seeing) / हनूमान (Hanuman) / अति (greatly) / हरषेउ (rejoiced) । / पुलक (horripilated) / गात (body) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / बरषेउ (rained) । / मन (mind) / महँ (in) / बहुत (many) / भाँति (kinds) / सुख (joy) / मानी (felt) । / बोलेउ (spoke) / श्रवन (ears) / सुधा (nectar) / सम (like) / बानी (speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5293.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5293.essence: Love for Ram overflows before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::5293.simple_meaning: Hanuman feels overwhelming joy on seeing Bharat, and his love shows in tears, goosebumps, and sweet speech.
ramacharitamanas::5293.simple_insight: Deep love shows itself in the body before it finds words.
ramacharitamanas::5293.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has just reached Bharat in Ayodhya, disguised as a brahmin. Seeing Bharat lost in grief over Ram, he is flooded with emotion. This verse shows Hanuman's devotion spilling out before he begins to speak.
ramacharitamanas::5293.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have been worrying about for days, and your chest loosens before you can even say hello. Real care speaks through your body first.
ramacharitamanas::5293.insight: It shows how devotion becomes visible as tears, trembling, and gentle speech.

ramacharitamanas::5294.verse_sanskrit: जासु बिरहँ सोचहु दिन राती। रटहु निरंतर गुन गन पाँती॥ रघुकुल तिलक सुजन सुखदाता। आयउ कुसल देव मुनि त्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5294.verse_hindi: जिनके विरह में आप दिन-रात सोच करते (घुलते) रहते हैं और जिनके गुण समूहों की पंक्तियों को आप निरंतर रटते रहते हैं, वे ही रघुकुल के तिलक, सज्जनों को दुःख देने वाले और देवताओं तथा मुनियों के रक्षक श्री रामजी सकुशल आ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5294.english_translation: The one for whom you grieve day and night, whose virtues you keep repeating, that Raghu-line jewel, friend of the good, protector of the gods and sages, has returned safely.
ramacharitamanas::5294.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / बिरहँ (in separation) / सोचहु (you grieve/think) / दिन राती (day and night) / रटहु (you repeat) / निरंतर (continuously) / गुन गन (groups of virtues) / पाँती (rows) / रघुकुल तिलक (ornament of the Raghu line) / सुजन (for the good) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) / आयउ (has come) / कुसल (safe, well) / देव (gods) / मुनि (sages) / त्राता (protector)
ramacharitamanas::5294.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5294.essence: Devotion turns grief into joy the moment the beloved returns.
ramacharitamanas::5294.simple_meaning: Ram is the one Bharat has missed day and night, and the one whose qualities he keeps repeating. Now that beloved protector has returned safely.
ramacharitamanas::5294.simple_insight: Love does not stay abstract here — it becomes relief when the one you long for finally comes home.
ramacharitamanas::5294.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has been living in Ram's absence, speaking Ram's name constantly and aching for his return. This verse answers that longing: the beloved prince, protector of the good, has come back safely.
ramacharitamanas::5294.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a hard conversation, waiting for the message that says they made it home. The relief is not in solving everything — only in hearing that the one you love is safe.
ramacharitamanas::5294.insight: It shifts longing from endless waiting to grateful recognition that the cherished one has returned.

ramacharitamanas::5295.verse_sanskrit: रिपु रन जीति सुजस सुर गावत। सीता सहित अनुज प्रभु आवत॥ सुनत बचन बिसरे सब दूखा। तृषावंत जिमि पाइ पियूषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5295.verse_hindi: शत्रु को रण में जीतकर सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु आ रहे हैं, देवता उनका सुंदर यश गा रहे हैं। ये वचन सुनते ही (भरतजी को) सारे दुःख भूल गए। जैसे प्यासा आदमी अमृत पाकर प्यास के दुःख को भूल जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5295.english_translation: The Lord is returning with Sita and Lakshman after defeating the enemy in battle; the radiant beings sing his glory. Hearing this, all Bharata's sorrow vanished, like a thirsty man forgetting thirst after drinking nectar.
ramacharitamanas::5295.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / रन (battle) / जीति (having conquered) / सुजस (good fame) / सुर (radiant beings) / गावत (singing) / सीता सहित (together with Sita) / अनुज (younger brother) / प्रभु (Lord) / आवत (is coming) / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / बिसरे (were forgotten) / सब (all) / दूखा (sorrows) / तृषावंत (thirsty one) / जिमि (like) / पाइ (having obtained) / पियूषा (nectar)
ramacharitamanas::5295.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5295.essence: Joy can erase sorrow the moment hope becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::5295.simple_meaning: News of Ram's return with Sita and Lakshman wipes away Bharata's grief at once. Joy enters like nectar reaching a thirsty person.
ramacharitamanas::5295.simple_insight: Some news heals so deeply that sorrow disappears before you can even name it.
ramacharitamanas::5295.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, Bharata has been living on longing and guilt, waiting for Ram's return. When he hears that Ram is coming back victorious with Sita and Lakshman, the pain breaks instantly. The verse lingers on that relief.
ramacharitamanas::5295.modern_relevance: You hear the text you were waiting for after a sleepless night, and your chest loosens before you can even think. Relief can arrive that suddenly.
ramacharitamanas::5295.insight: It shows how a single true message can dissolve years of heaviness in one moment.

ramacharitamanas::5296.verse_sanskrit: को तुम्ह तात कहाँ ते आए। मोहि परम प्रिय बचन सुनाए॥ मारुत सुत मैं कपि हनुमाना। नामु मोर सुनु कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5296.verse_hindi: (भरतजी ने पूछा-) हे तात! तुम कौन हो? और कहाँ से आए हो? (जो) तुमने मुझको (ये) परम प्रिय (अत्यंत आनंद देने वाले) वचन सुनाए। (हनुमान् जी ने कहा) हे कृपानिधान! सुनिए, मैं पवन का पुत्र और जाति का वानर हूँ, मेरा नाम हनुमान् है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5296.english_translation: “Who are you, dear one? Where have you come from? You have spoken words that gave me great joy. I am Hanuman, son of the wind and a monkey by birth; listen, O treasure of grace, my name is Hanuman.”
ramacharitamanas::5296.translation_literal: को (who) / तुम्ह (you) / तात (dear one) / कहाँ ते (from where) / आए (came) / मोहि (to me) / परम प्रिय (most dear) / बचन (words) / सुनाए (made hear, spoke) / मारुत सुत (son of the wind) / मैं (I) / कपि (monkey) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / नामु (name) / मोर (my) / सुनु (listen) / कृपानिधाना (o treasure of grace)
ramacharitamanas::5296.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5296.essence: Humility and warmth make a stranger instantly trustworthy.
ramacharitamanas::5296.simple_meaning: Hanuman introduces himself to Bharat after speaking words that delight him. The verse shows instant warmth, humility, and devotional connection between them.
ramacharitamanas::5296.simple_insight: A gentle voice can create trust before any introduction is complete.
ramacharitamanas::5296.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat meets Hanuman and asks who he is and where he has come from. Hanuman answers with humility, naming himself as the son of the wind and a monkey, while speaking to Bharat with deep respect. The moment opens their bond.
ramacharitamanas::5296.modern_relevance: You meet someone after a message that already feels kind and safe. Before titles or resumes matter, their tone tells you whether trust is possible.
ramacharitamanas::5296.insight: It shifts attention from status to the quality of speech and presence.

ramacharitamanas::5297.verse_sanskrit: दीनबंधु रघुपति कर किंकर। सुनत भरत भेंटेउ उठि सादर॥ मिलत प्रेम नहिं हृदयँ समाता। नयन स्रवतजल पुलकित गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5297.verse_hindi: मैं दीनों के बंधु श्री रघुनाथजी का दास हूँ। यह सुनते ही भरतजी उठकर आदरपूर्वक हनुमान् जी से गले लगकर मिले। मिलते समय प्रेम हृदय में नहीं समाता। नेत्रों से (आनंद और प्रेम के आँसुओं का) जल बहने लगा और शरीर पुलकित हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5297.english_translation: I am the servant of the Lord of the Raghu clan, friend of the humble. Hearing this, Bharata rose and embraced Hanuman with honor. Their love could not fit in the heart; tears flowed from the eyes and the body thrilled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5297.translation_literal: दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कर (of the hand; here, servant) / किंकर (servant) / सुनत (hearing) / भरत (Bharata) / भेंटेउ (met/embraced) / उठि (rising) / सादर (with honor) / मिलत (meeting) / प्रेम (love) / नहिं (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाता (fits) / नयन (eyes) / स्रवतजल (flowing water/tears) / पुलकित (horripilated/thrilled) / गाता (body)
ramacharitamanas::5297.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5297.essence: Devotion turns strangers into family at once.
ramacharitamanas::5297.simple_meaning: Hanuman identifies himself as a servant of Ram, and Bharata responds with deep honor and affection. Their meeting overflows with tears, love, and joy.
ramacharitamanas::5297.simple_insight: Real devotion creates instant recognition and warmth, without hesitation or status.
ramacharitamanas::5297.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata has just learned that the visitor before him is Hanuman, Ram's devoted servant. The moment he hears that identity, he rises, embraces him, and is overwhelmed by love. This verse shows bhakti becoming human closeness.
ramacharitamanas::5297.modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly served the person you love most, and the room changes. No status game survives that moment — only gratitude, respect, and tears.
ramacharitamanas::5297.insight: It teaches you to recognize service as sacred and respond with immediate honor.

ramacharitamanas::5298.verse_sanskrit: कपि तव दरस सकल दुख बीते। मिले आजुमोहि राम पिरीते॥ बार बार बूझी कुसलाता। तो कहुँ देउँ काह सुन भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5298.verse_hindi: (भरतजी ने कहा-) हे हनुमान् - तुम्हारे दर्शन से मेरे समस्त दुःख समाप्त हो गए (दुःखों का अंत हो गया)। (तुम्हारे रूप में) आज मुझे प्यारे रामजी ही मिल गए। भरतजी ने बार-बार कुशल पूछी (और कहा-) हे भाई! सुनो, (इस शुभ संवाद के बदले में) तुम्हें क्या दूँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5298.english_translation: O monkey, seeing you, all my sorrow is gone. Today I have met beloved Ram through you. Again and again I ask after your well-being; tell me, brother, what can I give you?
ramacharitamanas::5298.translation_literal: कपि (monkey) / तव (your) / दरस (seeing) / सकल (all) / दुख (sorrow) / बीते (passed away) / मिले (met) / आजु (today) / मोहि (to me) / राम (Ram) / पिरीते (beloved) / बार बार (again and again) / बूझी (asked) / कुसलाता (well-being) / तो (then) / कहुँ (to you) / देउँ (give) / काह (what) / सुन (listen) / भ्राता (brother)
ramacharitamanas::5298.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::5298.essence: True devotion makes the messenger feel like the beloved's own arrival.
ramacharitamanas::5298.simple_meaning: Bharat feels that Hanuman’s presence has ended his sorrow, because Hanuman has brought Ram’s presence to him. He is so moved that he asks what gift he can offer.
ramacharitamanas::5298.simple_insight: Real devotion makes another person feel the beloved’s presence, not just your own care.
ramacharitamanas::5298.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand, Bharat receives Hanuman with overflowing love. Hanuman has come from Ram, and Bharat feels that meeting him is the same as meeting Ram. His grief dissolves into gratitude, and he asks what he can possibly give in return.
ramacharitamanas::5298.modern_relevance: You open the door to find a message from someone you deeply miss. Before you even read it fully, your chest loosens — because the messenger feels like their presence.
ramacharitamanas::5298.insight: It shifts attention from the messenger as a person to the beloved they carry with them.

ramacharitamanas::5299.verse_sanskrit: एहि संदेस सरिस जग माहीं। करि बिचार देखेउँ कछु नाहीं॥ नाहिन तात उरिन मैं तोही। अब प्रभु चरित सुनावहु मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5299.verse_hindi: इस संदेश के समान (इसके बदले में देने लायक पदार्थ) जगत् में कुछ भी नहीं है, मैंने यह विचार कर देख लिया है। (इसलिए) हे तात! मैं तुमसे किसी प्रकार भी उऋण नहीं हो सकता। अब मुझे प्रभु का चरित्र (हाल) सुनाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5299.english_translation: There is nothing in the world equal to this message. After thinking it over, I see nothing else. I can never repay you, dear one. Now tell me about the Lord's deeds.
ramacharitamanas::5299.translation_literal: एहि (this) / संदेस (message) / सरिस (equal to) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / करि (having done) / बिचार (reflection) / देखेउँ (I saw) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (not) / नाहिन (there is not) / तात (dear one) / उरिन (in debt / repaid) / मैं (I) / तोही (to you) / अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / चरित (deeds / life-story) / सुनावहु (please tell) / मोही (to me)
ramacharitamanas::5299.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::5299.essence: True devotion sees a message as priceless and answers with gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::5299.simple_meaning: Bharat says Hanuman's message is priceless and cannot be repaid. Overwhelmed with gratitude, he asks to hear Ram's story.
ramacharitamanas::5299.simple_insight: Some acts of love create a debt that can only be answered with more love.
ramacharitamanas::5299.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat receives Hanuman as Ram's messenger. The meeting has already softened his grief, and now Bharat says no gift in the world equals this message. He feels forever indebted and asks to hear Ram's story.
ramacharitamanas::5299.modern_relevance: Someone shows up at your door after months of silence, not with explanations, but with a message that changes everything. You realize gratitude has become too large for payment.
ramacharitamanas::5299.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring kindness to receiving it with humility and longing.

ramacharitamanas::5300.verse_sanskrit: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5300.verse_hindi: तब हनुमान् जी ने भरतजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाकर श्री रघुनाथजी की सारी गुणगाथा कही। (भरतजी ने पूछा-) हे हनुमान् ! कहो, कृपालु स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी कभी मुझे अपने दास की तरह याद भी करते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5300.english_translation: Then Hanuman bowed his head at Bharat's feet and spoke the whole story of Ram's virtues. Bharat asked, "Tell me, O gracious Lord, does Ram ever remember me as his servant?"
ramacharitamanas::5300.translation_literal: तब (then) / हनुमंत (Hanuman) / नाइ (bowing) / पद (feet) / माथा (head) / कहे (spoke) / सकल (all) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (song/story)॥ / कहु (tell) / कपि (O monkey) / कबहुँ (ever) / कृपाल (gracious) / गोसाईं (Lord) / सुमिरहिं (remember) / मोहि (me) / दास (servant) / की नाईं (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5300.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::5300.essence: Real devotion wants only to live in Ram's memory.
ramacharitamanas::5300.simple_meaning: Bharat asks Hanuman whether Ram ever remembers him as a devoted servant. The verse shows Bharat's humility and longing for Ram's remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::5300.simple_insight: Love becomes complete when being remembered matters more than being praised.
ramacharitamanas::5300.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat speaks to Hanuman with deep humility. After hearing Ram's virtues, he does not ask for power or comfort — only whether Ram remembers him as a servant. The moment reveals the tenderness of Bharat's devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5300.modern_relevance: You send a message to someone you admire and wait for a simple reply. Not attention, not approval — just the quiet hope that your care is known. Bharat's heart lives there.
ramacharitamanas::5300.insight: It shifts devotion from asking for reward to asking for remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::5301.verse_sanskrit: निज दास ज्यों रघुबंसभूषन कबहुँ मम सुमिरन कर् यो। सुनि भरत बचन बिनीत अति कपि पुलकि तन चरनन्हि पर् यो॥ रघुबीर निज मुख जासु गुन गन कहत अग जग नाथ जो। काहे न होइ बिनीत परम पुनीत सदगुन सिंधु सो॥
ramacharitamanas::5301.verse_hindi: रघुवंश के भूषण श्री रामजी क्या कभी अपने दास की भाँति मेरा स्मरण करते रहे हैं? भरतजी के अत्यंत नम्र वचन सुनकर हनुमान् जी पुलकित शरीर होकर उनके चरणों पर गिर पड़े (और मन में विचारने लगे कि) जो चराचर के स्वामी हैं, वे श्री रघुवीर अपने श्रीमुख से जिनके गुणसमूहों का वर्णन करते हैं, वे भरतजी ऐसे विनम्र, परम पवित्र और सद्गुणों के समुद्र क्यों न हों?
ramacharitamanas::5301.english_translation: "Has Lord Ram, the ornament of Raghu's line, ever remembered me as his servant?" Hearing Bharat's humble words, Hanuman's body thrilled, and he fell at Bharat's feet. "The Lord of all worlds speaks Bharat's virtues with his own mouth; how could such a bearer of pure virtues and deep goodness not be utterly humble and supremely pure?"
ramacharitamanas::5301.translation_literal: निज (own) / दास (servant) / ज्यों (like) / रघुबंसभूषन (ornament of the Raghu line) / कबहुँ (ever) / मम (my) / सुमिरन (remembrance) / कर् यो (did)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / अति (very) / कपि (Hanuman) / पुलकि (thrilled) / तन (body) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / पर् यो (fell)॥ / रघुबीर (Lord of the Raghu line) / निज (his own) / मुख (mouth) / जासु (whose) / गुन (virtues) / गन (groups) / कहत (speaking) / अग (beginningless) / जग (world) / नाथ (lord) / जो (who) / काहे (how) / न (not) / होइ (be) / बिनीत (humble) / परम (supremely) / पुनीत (pure) / सदगुन (good virtues) / सिंधु (ocean) / सो (that one)॥
ramacharitamanas::5301.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5301.essence: Real greatness bows before humility and recognizes itself in it.
ramacharitamanas::5301.simple_meaning: Hanuman is moved by Bharat's humility and realizes that Ram's praise itself proves Bharat's purity and greatness.
ramacharitamanas::5301.simple_insight: True greatness can be recognized by the way the pure-hearted speak of it.
ramacharitamanas::5301.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand, Hanuman is speaking with Bharat about Ram. Bharat's humility overwhelms him. When he hears Ram's own praise of Bharat, Hanuman is filled with reverence and falls at Bharat's feet, seeing that such goodness must be naturally humble and pure.
ramacharitamanas::5301.modern_relevance: Someone quietly deflects praise at a family dinner, and you realize their modesty is not insecurity. It is the mark of a person whose goodness does not need an audience.
ramacharitamanas::5301.insight: It shifts admiration from status to humility, teaching you to trust the character that doesn't advertise itself.

ramacharitamanas::5302.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रान प्रिय नाथ तुम्ह सत्य बचन मम तात। पुनि पुनि मिलत भरत सुनि हरष न हृदयँ समात ॥
ramacharitamanas::5302.verse_hindi: (हनुमान् जी ने कहा-) हे नाथ! आप श्री रामजी को प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं, हे तात! मेरा वचन सत्य है। यह सुनकर भरतजी बार-बार मिलते हैं, हृदय में हर्ष समाता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5302.english_translation: O lord, you are as dear to Ram as life itself. My words are true, dear one. Hearing this, Bharat meets again and again, and his heart cannot contain its joy.
ramacharitamanas::5302.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रान (life) / प्रिय (dear) / नाथ (lord) / तुम्ह (you) / सत्य (true) / बचन (words) / मम (my) / तात (dear one) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / मिलत (meeting) / भरत (Bharat) / सुनि (hearing) / हरष (joy) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समात (contained)
ramacharitamanas::5302.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::5302.essence: Love remembered is joy that cannot stay contained.
ramacharitamanas::5302.simple_meaning: Hanuman tells Bharat that he is as dear to Ram as life itself, and Bharat is so happy hearing this that his heart cannot hold it.
ramacharitamanas::5302.simple_insight: Being loved by the divine can make the heart overflow without needing anything else.
ramacharitamanas::5302.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand, Hanuman has just answered Bharat's tender question about whether Ram remembers him. He reassures Bharat that Ram loves him deeply, and Bharat's joy becomes so great that it cannot stay inside him.
ramacharitamanas::5302.modern_relevance: You finally hear that the person you love most still holds you close. The relief is so strong it feels almost too large for your chest.
ramacharitamanas::5302.insight: It shifts the heart from anxious doubt to the quiet certainty of being cherished.

ramacharitamanas::5303.verse_sanskrit: भरत चरन सिरु नाइ तुरित गयउ कपि राम पहिं। कही कुसल सब जाइ हरषि चलेउ प्रभु जान चढ़ि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5303.verse_hindi: फिर भरतजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर हनुमान् जी तुरंत ही श्री रामजी के पास (लौट) गए और जाकर उन्होंने सब कुशल कही। तब प्रभु हर्षित होकर विमान पर चढ़कर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::5303.english_translation: After bowing his head at Bharata's feet, Hanuman quickly went back to Rama. He told him everything was well, and then the Lord, pleased, set out in the flying chariot.
ramacharitamanas::5303.translation_literal: भरत (Bharata) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / तुरित (quickly) / गयउ (went) / कपि (Hanuman) / राम (Rama) / पहिं (to) / कही (said) / कुसल (well-being) / सब (all) / जाइ (going) / हरषि (rejoicing) / चलेउ (went) / प्रभु (Lord) / जान (chariot) / चढ़ि (mounting)
ramacharitamanas::5303.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5303.essence: Devotion moves swiftly and leaves everyone lighter.
ramacharitamanas::5303.simple_meaning: Hanuman bows to Bharata, returns to Rama, reports that all is well, and Rama leaves happily in the chariot.
ramacharitamanas::5303.simple_insight: When loyalty is pure, even a small report can move the heart.
ramacharitamanas::5303.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's happy reunion, Hanuman first honors Bharata, then rushes back to Rama with the good news. The moment is a bridge between brothers, carrying reassurance from one devoted heart to another.
ramacharitamanas::5303.modern_relevance: You finally get the text that says, 'I'm okay.' The relief is so immediate it changes your whole body.
ramacharitamanas::5303.insight: It shows how devotion becomes action: respect, quick return, clear reporting, and joyful movement.

ramacharitamanas::5304.verse_sanskrit: हरषि भरत कोसलपुर आए। समाचार सब गुरहि सुनाए॥ पुनि मंदिर महँ बात जनाई। आवत नगर कुसल रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5304.verse_hindi: इधर भरतजी भी हर्षित होकर अयोध्यापुरी में आए और उन्होंने गुरुजी को सब समाचार सुनाया! फिर राजमहल में खबर जनाई कि श्री रघुनाथजी कुशलपूर्वक नगर को आ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5304.english_translation: Bharat joyfully arrived in Kosalpur and told the guru everything. Then he announced in the palace that Raghurai was coming to the city safely.
ramacharitamanas::5304.translation_literal: हरषि (rejoicing) / भरत (Bharat) / कोसलपुर (Kosalpur/Ayodhya) / आए (came) । / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / गुरहि (to the guru) / सुनाए (told) ॥ / पुनि (then) / मंदिर (palace/house) / महँ (in) / बात (news) / जनाई (made known) । / आवत (coming) / नगर (to the city) / कुसल (safe/well) / रघुराई (Raghurai/Ram) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5304.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5304.essence: Bharat's happiness becomes the whole city's hope.
ramacharitamanas::5304.simple_meaning: Bharat returns to Ayodhya, shares the news with his teacher, and spreads word that Ram is safely on the way.
ramacharitamanas::5304.simple_insight: Joy can move through a whole city when someone beloved is finally coming home.
ramacharitamanas::5304.detailed_meaning: Bharat comes back to Kosalpur full of relief and happiness. He first tells the guru, then sends the news through the palace that Ram is returning safely. The verse is a bridge from private joy to public celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5304.modern_relevance: You get the message that the person you miss is on the way back, and suddenly you are telling everyone — family, friends, the whole house.
ramacharitamanas::5304.insight: It shifts the moment from waiting alone to shared relief and gathering.

ramacharitamanas::5305.verse_sanskrit: सुनत सकल जननीं उठि धाईं। कहि प्रभु कुसल भरत समुझाईं॥ समाचार पुरबासिन्ह पाए। नर अरु नारि हरषि सब धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5305.verse_hindi: खबर सुनते ही सब माताएँ उठ दौड़ीं। भरतजी ने प्रभु की कुशल कहकर सबको समझाया। नगर निवासियों ने यह समाचार पाया, तो स्त्री-पुरुष सभी हर्षित होकर दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5305.english_translation: When they heard the news, all the mothers rushed up. Bharata reassured everyone by saying that the Lord was well. The people of the city received the news, and men and women all ran out in joy.
ramacharitamanas::5305.translation_literal: सुनत (on hearing) / सकल (all) / जननीं (the mothers) / उठि (rising) / धाईं (ran) / कहि (saying) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कुसल (well-being) / भरत (Bharata) / समुझाईं (explained/reassured) / समाचार (news) / पुरबासिन्ह (to the city-dwellers) / पाए (received) / नर (men) / अरु (and) / नारि (women) / हरषि (joyful) / सब (all) / धाए (ran)
ramacharitamanas::5305.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5305.essence: Relief for Ram becomes joy for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::5305.simple_meaning: The news of Ram's well-being spreads through Ayodhya, and everyone rushes out in joy and relief.
ramacharitamanas::5305.simple_insight: Joy moves faster when a loved one is safe.
ramacharitamanas::5305.detailed_meaning: Bharata has returned to Ayodhya and told the elders that Ram is well. The report ripples through the city at once: the mothers rise, the townspeople surge forward, and relief turns the whole city into motion.
ramacharitamanas::5305.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were waiting for: they made it home safely. In that instant, the whole body moves before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::5305.insight: It shows how shared relief can turn a city from waiting into action.

ramacharitamanas::5306.verse_sanskrit: दधि दुर्बा रोचन फल फूला। नव तुलसी दल मंगल मूला॥ भरि भरि हेम थार भामिनी। गावत चलिं सिंधुरगामिनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5306.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी के स्वागत के लिए) दही, दूब, गोरोचन, फल, फूल और मंगल के मूल नवीन तुलसीदल आदि वस्तुएँ सोने की थाली में भर-भरकर हथिनी की सी चाल वाली सौभाग्यवती स्त्रियाँ (उन्हें लेकर) गाती हुई चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5306.english_translation: For Ram's welcome, curd, durva grass, rochana, fruits, flowers, and fresh tulsi leaves were filled again and again into golden trays, while fortunate women walked singing with the grace of an elephant.
ramacharitamanas::5306.translation_literal: दधि (curd) / दुर्बा (durva grass) / रोचन (rochana) / फल (fruits) / फूला (flowers) / नव (fresh) / तुलसी (tulsi) / दल (leaves) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूला (root) / भरि भरि (again and again filled) / हेम (golden) / थार (trays) / भामिनी (fortunate women) / गावत (singing) / चलिं (walked) / सिंधुरगामिनी (with elephant-like grace)
ramacharitamanas::5306.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5306.essence: Welcome becomes worship when love fills the hands.
ramacharitamanas::5306.simple_meaning: Women carried auspicious offerings in golden trays and sang as they went to welcome Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5306.simple_insight: Joy can become a procession: when love arrives, even simple offerings feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::5306.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has returned with good news, and the city erupts into welcome. Fortunate women prepare trays of auspicious items and sing as they hurry toward Ram's arrival. The verse lingers on the beauty of the reception, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5306.modern_relevance: You see neighbors carrying sweets, flowers, and lamps to a home after a long-awaited return. The joy is in the gathering itself, not in the objects.
ramacharitamanas::5306.insight: It shifts attention from the gift to the devotion behind the gift.

ramacharitamanas::5307.verse_sanskrit: जे जैसेहिं तैसेहिं उठि धावहिं। बाल बृद्ध कहँ संग न लावहिं॥ एक एकन्ह कहँ बूझहिं भाई। तुम्ह देखे दयाल रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5307.verse_hindi: जो जैसे हैं (जहाँ जिस दशा में हैं) वे वैसे ही (वहीं से उसी दशा में) उठ दौड़ते हैं। (देर हो जाने के डर से) बालकों और बूढ़ों को कोई साथ नहीं लाते। एक-दूसरे से पूछते हैं- भाई! तुमने दयालु श्री रघुनाथजी को देखा है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::5307.english_translation: Everyone rushes out just as they are, leaving children and the old behind. Each person asks the other, “Brother, have you seen the compassionate Raghunath?”
ramacharitamanas::5307.translation_literal: जे (who) / जैसेहिं (just as) / तैसेहिं (just so) / उठि (rising) / धावहिं (they run) / बाल (children) / बृद्ध (the old) / कहँ (for) / संग (with) / न (not) / लावहिं (they bring) / एक एकन्ह (one another) / कहँ (to) / बूझहिं (they ask) / भाई (brother) / तुम्ह (you) / देखे (seen) / दयाल (compassionate) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::5307.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5307.essence: Love makes people leave everything and run toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5307.simple_meaning: The whole city is so eager to see Ram that people rush out immediately, without waiting to gather anyone else. Everyone is asking who has seen him.
ramacharitamanas::5307.simple_insight: Longing can make even a crowd move like one heart.
ramacharitamanas::5307.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just heard that Ram is returning. The city’s excitement breaks all ordinary order: people rush out in whatever state they are in, not even stopping for children or elders. In that shared urgency, everyone keeps asking who has seen Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5307.modern_relevance: You get the message that someone you love is finally on the way home, and suddenly nothing else matters. Shoes half-on, phone in hand, you’re already at the door.
ramacharitamanas::5307.insight: It shows how devotion turns a whole city into one searching, eager movement.

ramacharitamanas::5308.verse_sanskrit: अवधपुरी प्रभु आवत जानी। भई सकल सोभा कै खानी॥ बहइ सुहावन त्रिबिध समीरा। भइ सरजू अति निर्मल नीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5308.verse_hindi: प्रभु को आते जानकर अवधपुरी संपूर्ण शोभाओं की खान हो गई। तीनों प्रकार की सुंदर वायु बहने लगी। सरयूजी अति निर्मल जल वाली हो गईं। (अर्थात् सरयूजी का जल अत्यंत निर्मल हो गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5308.english_translation: Knowing that the Lord was coming to Ayodhya, the city became a treasury of beauty. A pleasant breeze from all three directions began to blow, and the Sarayu became extremely clear.
ramacharitamanas::5308.translation_literal: अवधपुरी (Ayodhya city) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आवत (coming) / जानी (knowing) / भई (became) / सकल (all) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / कै खानी (a mine, treasury)॥ / बहइ (blew) / सुहावन (pleasant) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / समीरा (wind, breeze) / भइ (became) / सरजू (Sarayu) / अति (very) / निर्मल (clear, pure) / नीरा (water)॥
ramacharitamanas::5308.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5308.essence: Ram's nearness turns ordinary life radiant.
ramacharitamanas::5308.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is transformed by Ram's arrival. The city, the wind, and the river all seem purified and radiant.
ramacharitamanas::5308.simple_insight: When something sacred draws near, even the world around it feels changed.
ramacharitamanas::5308.detailed_meaning: Ram is about to enter Ayodhya after exile. The city is no longer ordinary; everything responds to his return. The people rush to welcome him, and the landscape itself seems to bloom with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5308.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everyone has been waiting for you, and the whole room changes. The air feels lighter, the water looks clearer, and people stand straighter without meaning to.
ramacharitamanas::5308.insight: It shifts attention from Ram's arrival as an event to Ram's presence as a transforming force.

ramacharitamanas::5309.verse_sanskrit: हरषित गुर परिजन अनुज भूसुर बृंद समेत। चले भरत मन प्रेम अति सन्मुख कृपानिकेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::5309.verse_hindi: गुरु वशिष्ठजी, कुटुम्बी, छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न तथा ब्राह्मणों के समूह के साथ हर्षित होकर भरतजी अत्यंत प्रेमपूर्ण मन से कृपाधाम श्री रामजी के सामने अर्थात् उनकी अगवानी के लिए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::5309.english_translation: With the guru, family, younger brother, and a group of learned priests, Bharat joyfully set out with a love-filled heart to welcome the gracious Lord Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5309.translation_literal: हरषित (joyful) / गुर (guru) / परिजन (family) / अनुज (younger brother) / भूसुर बृंद (group of learned priests) / समेत (together with) / चले (went) / भरत (Bharat) / मन (mind) / प्रेम (love) / अति (very) / सन्मुख (toward / to welcome) / कृपानिकेत (abode of grace)
ramacharitamanas::5309.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5309.essence: Love makes the whole city move toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5309.simple_meaning: Bharat goes out happily with his teacher, family, brother, and priests to welcome Ram with deep love.
ramacharitamanas::5309.simple_insight: True welcome is not formal duty alone; it is love moving the whole household together.
ramacharitamanas::5309.detailed_meaning: Ram is returning to Ayodhya, and the city is alive with anticipation. Bharat leaves with Vashishtha, his family, Shatrughna, and the priests to receive Ram, showing the tenderness and honour of this reunion.
ramacharitamanas::5309.modern_relevance: You hear someone you love is finally coming home, and you step out with everyone who matters to meet them. The joy is shared before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::5309.insight: It shows how love turns a public reception into a shared act of reverence.

ramacharitamanas::5310.verse_sanskrit: बहुतक चढ़ीं अटारिन्ह निरखहिं गगन बिमान। देखि मधुर सुर हरषित करहिं सुमंगल गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5310.verse_hindi: बहुत सी स्त्रियाँ अटारियों पर चढ़ीं आकाश में विमान देख रही हैं और उसे देखकर हर्षित होकर मीठे स्वर से सुंदर मंगल गीत गा रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5310.english_translation: Many women climbed onto the terraces to look at the aerial chariot in the sky. Seeing it, they rejoiced and sang sweet, auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::5310.translation_literal: बहुतक (many) / चढ़ीं (climbed up) / अटारिन्ह (onto terraces) / निरखहिं (they look) / गगन (sky) / बिमान (airborne chariot) / देखि (seeing) / मधुर (sweet) / सुर (melodious) / हरषित (delighted) / करहिं (they do) / सुमंगल (very auspicious) / गान (songs)
ramacharitamanas::5310.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5310.essence: Joy rises naturally when the beloved comes into view.
ramacharitamanas::5310.simple_meaning: People gather on their terraces to watch the flying chariot and sing joyful songs.
ramacharitamanas::5310.simple_insight: Shared joy can turn an ordinary sight into a celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5310.detailed_meaning: As Ram returns to Ayodhya, women climb onto terraces to catch sight of the heavenly chariot in the sky. Their delight spills into sweet auspicious songs, adding to the city’s overflowing welcome.
ramacharitamanas::5310.modern_relevance: You hear the first siren of a parade, and neighbors spill onto balconies with phones raised and smiles breaking through. Joy becomes public before anyone plans it.
ramacharitamanas::5310.insight: It turns a passing sight into a communal act of celebration.

ramacharitamanas::5311.verse_sanskrit: राका ससि रघुपति पुर सिंधु देखि हरषान। बढ़् यो कोलाहल करत जनु नारि तरंग समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5311.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी पूर्णिमा के चंद्रमा हैं तथा अवधपुर समुद्र है, जो उस पूर्णचंद्र को देखकर हर्षित हो रहा है और शोर करता हुआ बढ़ रहा है (इधर-उधर दौड़ती हुई) स्त्रियाँ उसकी तरंगों के समान लगती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5311.english_translation: Raghupati is the full moon, and Ayodhya is the sea; seeing that moon, it swells with joy and noise, while the women moving about are like its waves.
ramacharitamanas::5311.translation_literal: राका (full moon) / ससि (moon) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / पुर (city) / सिंधु (sea) / देखि (seeing) / हरषान (rejoiced) / बढ़् यो (grew) / कोलाहल (noise) / करत (doing) / जनु (as if) / नारि (women) / तरंग (waves) / समान (like)
ramacharitamanas::5311.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5311.essence: Ram's return makes the whole city overflow with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5311.simple_meaning: Ayodhya erupts in joy at Ram's return. The city feels alive, and the women rushing about are compared to waves in a sea.
ramacharitamanas::5311.simple_insight: Joy can spread through a whole community, turning a city into one shared celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5311.detailed_meaning: Ram has returned to Ayodhya after exile and victory. From the palace and streets, the whole city seems to surge like the sea under a full moon. The verse paints public joy, not teaching, as everyone rushes to witness Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5311.modern_relevance: A neighborhood comes alive when the team wins after years of waiting. Doors open, people spill into the street, and even the noise feels like relief.
ramacharitamanas::5311.insight: It turns a return into a shared public celebration, showing how presence can transform an entire place.

ramacharitamanas::5312.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ भानुकुल कमल दिवाकर। कपिन्ह देखावत नगर मनोहर॥ सुनु कपीस अंगद लंकेसा। पावन पुरी रुचिर यह देसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5312.verse_hindi: यहाँ (विमान पर से) सूर्य कुल रूपी कमल को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले सूर्य श्री रामजी वानरों को मनोहर नगर दिखला रहे हैं। (वे कहते हैं-) हे सुग्रीव! हे अंगद! हे लंकापति विभीषण! सुनो। यह पुरी पवित्र है और यह देश सुंदर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5312.english_translation: Here, Rama, the sun of the Solar dynasty, shows the lovely city to the monkeys. "Listen, Sugriva, Angada, and Lord of Lanka Vibhishana: this city is pure, and this land is beautiful."
ramacharitamanas::5312.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / भानुकुल (solar dynasty) / कमल (lotus) / दिवाकर (sun) / कपिन्ह (to the monkeys) / देखावत (showing) / नगर (city) / मनोहर (lovely) / सुनु (listen) / कपीस (lord of monkeys, Sugriva) / अंगद (Angada) / लंकेसा (lord of Lanka, Vibhishana) / पावन (pure) / पुरी (city) / रुचिर (beautiful) / यह (this) / देसा (land)
ramacharitamanas::5312.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5312.essence: Love makes the familiar appear newly pure.
ramacharitamanas::5312.simple_meaning: Rama points out the beauty and purity of Ayodhya to Sugriva, Angada, and Vibhishana as they look down from above.
ramacharitamanas::5312.simple_insight: Even a home can become sacred when seen through love and belonging.
ramacharitamanas::5312.detailed_meaning: From above, Rama is showing the monkeys the city of Ayodhya after his return. Sugriva, Angada, and Vibhishana are with him, and the scene is filled with wonder. This verse is a supporting detail in the larger celebration of Ayodhya's beauty.
ramacharitamanas::5312.modern_relevance: You return to your old neighborhood after years away and suddenly notice the tree-lined street, the temple bell, the familiar rooftops. What once felt ordinary now feels precious.
ramacharitamanas::5312.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverent seeing, where even a city becomes luminous through devotion.

ramacharitamanas::5313.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि सब बैकुंठ बखाना। बेद पुरान बिदित जगु जाना॥ अवधपुरी सम प्रिय नहिं सोऊ। यह प्रसंग जानइ कोउ कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5313.verse_hindi: यद्यपि सबने वैकुण्ठ की बड़ाई की है- यह वेद-पुराणों में प्रसिद्ध है और जगत् जानता है, परंतु अवधपुरी के समान मुझे वह भी प्रिय नहीं है। यह बात (भेद) कई-कोई (बिरले ही) जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5313.english_translation: Although everyone praises Vaikuntha, and the Vedas and Puranas make it famous, Ayodhya is still dearer. Only a rare few understand this distinction.
ramacharitamanas::5313.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / सब (all) / बैकुंठ (Vaikuntha) / बखाना (praise) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / बिदित (known) / जगु (world) / जाना (known) / अवधपुरी (Ayodhya) / सम (equal) / प्रिय (dear) / नहिं (not) / सोऊ (that also) / यह (this) / प्रसंग (distinction) / जानइ (knows) / कोउ (someone) / कोऊ (someone)
ramacharitamanas::5313.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5313.essence: Sacredness deepens when love chooses a place as home.
ramacharitamanas::5313.simple_meaning: Ram says that although Vaikuntha is praised everywhere, Ayodhya is even dearer to him. Only a few people understand this subtle truth.
ramacharitamanas::5313.simple_insight: Love can make a simple home more precious than any perfect realm.
ramacharitamanas::5313.detailed_meaning: In Ram's reign, the sight of Ayodhya fills the sky with joy. Ram pauses to reveal a tender truth: even though sacred texts praise Vaikuntha, his own birthplace is dearer to him. This verse begins that intimate praise of Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::5313.modern_relevance: You can fly across the world and still feel most alive in the street where your mother called you home. Some places matter not because they are perfect, but because they are yours.
ramacharitamanas::5313.insight: It shifts reverence from abstract perfection to lived belonging and love.

ramacharitamanas::5314.verse_sanskrit: जन्मभूमि मम पुरी सुहावनि। उत्तर दिसि बह सरजू पावनि॥ जा मज्जन ते बिनहिं प्रयासा। मम समीप नर पावहिं बासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5314.verse_hindi: यह सुहावनी पुरी मेरी जन्मभूमि है। इसके उत्तर दिशा में जीवों को पवित्र करने वाली सरयू नदी बहती है, जिसमें स्नान करने से मनुष्य बिना ही परिश्रम मेरे समीप निवास (सामीप्य मुक्ति) पा जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5314.english_translation: This lovely city is my birthplace. To its north flows the purifying Sarayu; by bathing in it, people reach closeness to me without effort.
ramacharitamanas::5314.translation_literal: जन्मभूमि (birthplace) / मम (my) / पुरी (city) / सुहावनि (lovely) / उत्तर दिसि (north direction) / बह (flows) / सरजू (Sarayu) / पावनि (purifying) / जा मज्जन (by whose bathing) / ते (from that) / बिनहिं प्रयासा (without effort) / मम समीप (near me) / नर (people) / पावहिं (obtain) / बासा (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::5314.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5314.essence: Grace can make nearness simple, not strenuous.
ramacharitamanas::5314.simple_meaning: Ram says Ayodhya is his beloved birthplace, and the Sarayu there is so pure that bathing in it brings people close to him without effort.
ramacharitamanas::5314.simple_insight: There is comfort in a place where grace feels effortless and closeness is already built into the landscape.
ramacharitamanas::5314.detailed_meaning: Ram is showing the flying vanaras Ayodhya from above and praising his own birthplace. He points to the Sarayu and says that even a simple bath there can bring people into his nearness. The verse turns the city into a living doorway to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5314.modern_relevance: You step into a river at dawn after months of carrying everything alone. For a moment, the noise drops away, and you feel that nearness is not earned by strain alone.
ramacharitamanas::5314.insight: It shifts devotion from effortful striving to receptive purification and place-based remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::5315.verse_sanskrit: अति प्रिय मोहि इहाँ के बासी। मम धामदा पुरी सुख रासी॥ हरषे सब कपि सुनि प्रभु बानी। धन्य अवध जो राम बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5315.verse_hindi: यहाँ के निवासी मुझे बहुत ही प्रिय हैं। यह पुरी सुख की राशि और मेरे परमधाम को देने वाली है। प्रभु की वाणी सुनकर सब वानर हर्षित हुए (और कहने लगे कि) जिस अवध की स्वयं श्री रामजी ने बड़ाई की, वह (अवश्य ही) धन्य है॥
ramacharitamanas::5315.english_translation: The people here are very dear to me. This city is a treasury of joy and the place of my own highest abode. Hearing the Lord's words, all the monkeys rejoiced and said, "Blessed is Ayodhya, praised by Ram."
ramacharitamanas::5315.translation_literal: अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / मोहि (to me) / इहाँ (here) / के (of the) / बासी (residents) / मम (my) / धामदा (bestower of abode) / पुरी (city) / सुख (joy) / रासी (treasury) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सब (all) / कपि (monkeys) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (Lord's) / बानी (words) / धन्य (blessed) / अवध (Ayodhya) / जो (which) / राम (Ram) / बखानी (praised)
ramacharitamanas::5315.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5315.essence: Love makes a city feel like the highest home.
ramacharitamanas::5315.simple_meaning: Ram says the people of Ayodhya are very dear to him, and the city is full of joy because it is his own beloved home. The monkeys rejoice at hearing this praise.
ramacharitamanas::5315.simple_insight: Being cherished by the divine makes an ordinary place feel sacred and alive.
ramacharitamanas::5315.detailed_meaning: Ram has just described Ayodhya as his beloved birthplace beside the Sarayu. Now he deepens that affection: the city's people are dear to him, and the monkeys burst into joy at hearing him praise their home. This is bhakti as belonging.
ramacharitamanas::5315.modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood where everyone knows your name and your burden feels lighter. Ram's words show what it means to be held by a place and a people who truly receive you.
ramacharitamanas::5315.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract worship to lived belonging and mutual affection.

ramacharitamanas::5316.verse_sanskrit: आवत देखि लोग सब कृपासिंधु भगवान। नगर निकट प्रभु प्रेरेउ उतरेउ भूमि बिमान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5316.verse_hindi: कृपा सागर भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी ने सब लोगों को आते देखा, तो प्रभु ने विमान को नगर के समीप उतरने की प्रेरणा की। तब वह पृथ्वी पर उतरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5316.english_translation: Seeing everyone gathered, the compassionate Lord prompted the divine vehicle to descend near the city, and it came down to the earth.
ramacharitamanas::5316.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of mercy) / भगवान (Lord) / नगर (city) / निकट (near) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रेरेउ (prompted) / उतरेउ (descended) / भूमि (earth) / बिमान (divine vehicle)
ramacharitamanas::5316.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5316.essence: Arrival itself becomes blessing when it comes near the people.
ramacharitamanas::5316.simple_meaning: Ram sees the people and brings the divine vehicle down near the city. The moment is about arrival, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5316.simple_insight: Sometimes grace arrives quietly, just by coming close enough to be received.
ramacharitamanas::5316.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is returning after exile and the city is waiting to welcome him. Seeing the gathered people, he has the divine vehicle descend near the city. This verse simply marks the arrival before the celebration begins.
ramacharitamanas::5316.modern_relevance: You pull into the neighborhood after a long trip, and everyone is already outside waiting. The real moment is not the vehicle itself, but the nearness.
ramacharitamanas::5316.insight: It frames the scene as arrival and welcome, not as a doctrinal statement.

ramacharitamanas::5317.verse_sanskrit: उतरि कहेउ प्रभु पुष्पकहि तुम्ह कुबेर पहिं जाहु। प्रेरित राम चलेउ सो हरषु बिरहु अति ताहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5317.verse_hindi: विमान से उतरकर प्रभु ने पुष्पक विमान से कहा कि तुम अब कुबेर के पास जाओ। श्री रामचंद्रजी की प्रेरणा से वह चला, उसे (अपने स्वामी के पास जाने का) हर्ष है और प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी से अलग होने का अत्यंत दुःख भी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5317.english_translation: After stepping down, the Lord told Pushpak, “Go now to Kubera.” Moved by Ram’s will, it departed—glad to return, yet aching to leave Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5317.translation_literal: उतरि (having descended) / कहेउ (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पुष्पकहि (to Pushpak) / तुम्ह (you) / कुबेर पहिं (to Kubera's place) / जाहु (go) / प्रेरित (impelled) / राम (by Ram) / चलेउ (it went) / सो (that) / हरषु (joy) / बिरहु (separation) / अति (very) / ताहु (for it)
ramacharitamanas::5317.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5317.essence: True devotion can make departure feel like both joy and grief.
ramacharitamanas::5317.simple_meaning: Pushpak leaves Ram’s presence because Ram sends it away. It goes gladly, yet it also feels the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::5317.simple_insight: Even joy can carry a quiet ache when something precious must part.
ramacharitamanas::5317.detailed_meaning: Ram has descended from the sky and is nearing Ayodhya. He sends Pushpak back to Kubera. The chariot obeys because it is moved by Ram’s will, and the verse lingers on its strange mix of joy and sorrow at leaving him.
ramacharitamanas::5317.modern_relevance: You finally end a call with someone who steadies you, and the room feels emptier at once. Relief and longing can arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::5317.insight: It shows how even obedience to what is right can include tenderness and loss.

ramacharitamanas::5318.verse_sanskrit: आए भरत संग सब लोगा। कृस तन श्रीरघुबीर बियोगा॥ बामदेव बसिष्ट मुनिनायक। देखे प्रभु महि धरि धनु सायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::5318.verse_hindi: भरतजी के साथ सब लोग आए। श्री रघुवीर के वियोग से सबके शरीर दुबले हो रहे हैं। प्रभु ने वामदेव, वशिष्ठ आदि मुनिश्रेष्ठों को देखा, तो उन्होंने धनुष-बाण पृथ्वी पर रखकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5318.english_translation: Bharat came with all the people. Separated from noble Ram, everyone’s body had grown thin. When the Lord saw Vamadeva, Vashishtha, and the other great sages, he set down his bow and arrows on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::5318.translation_literal: आए (came) / भरत (Bharat) / संग (with) / सब (all) / लोगा (people) / कृस (thin) / तन (body) / श्रीरघुबीर (noble Ram) / बियोगा (from separation) / बामदेव (Vamadeva) / बसिष्ट (Vashishtha) / मुनिनायक (chief sages) / देखे (saw) / प्रभु (the Lord) / महि (on the ground) / धरि (placing) / धनु (bow) / सायक (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::5318.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5318.essence: Separation from what you love leaves its mark; true greatness bows first.
ramacharitamanas::5318.simple_meaning: Bharat arrives with the people, and everyone looks worn down by separation from Ram. Ram sees the sages and respectfully lays down his bow and arrows.
ramacharitamanas::5318.simple_insight: Love and grief show on the body. Respect can be shown in a single, humble gesture.
ramacharitamanas::5318.detailed_meaning: Bharat returns with the gathered people to meet Ram in the forest. Separation from Ram has made everyone lean and strained. When Ram sees Vamadeva, Vashishtha, and the other sages, he lowers his weapons before greeting them.
ramacharitamanas::5318.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital waiting room and see how weeks of worry have hollowed everyone out. Then someone important to the family arrives, and the first thing they do is put their phone down and bow their head.
ramacharitamanas::5318.insight: It teaches you to notice how separation changes people, and to answer reverence with humility.

ramacharitamanas::5319.verse_sanskrit: धाइ धरे गुर चरन सरोरुह। अनुज सहित अति पुलक तनोरुह॥ भेंटि कुसल बूझी मुनिराया। हमरें कुसल तुम्हारिहिं दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5319.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित दौड़कर गुरुजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए, उनके रोम-रोम अत्यंत पुलकित हो रहे हैं। मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी ने (उठाकर) उन्हें गले लगाकर कुशल पूछी। (प्रभु ने कहा-) आप ही की दया में हमारी कुशल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5319.english_translation: Rama and Lakshmana rushed to the guru's lotus feet, their bodies thrilled with joy. Sage Vashishtha embraced them and asked about their welfare. Rama replied, "Our well-being rests in your grace."
ramacharitamanas::5319.translation_literal: धाइ (running) / धरे (held) / गुर (teacher) / चरन (feet) / सरोरुह (lotus) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / अति (very) / पुलक (thrilled) / तनोरुह (body-hair) ॥ भेंटि (meeting/embracing) / कुसल (well-being) / बूझी (asked) / मुनिराया (king of sages) । हमरें (our) / कुसल (well-being) / तुम्हारिहिं (in your) / दाया (grace/mercy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5319.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5319.essence: True well-being begins when pride bows to grace.
ramacharitamanas::5319.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana rush to honor their teacher, and Rama says their welfare depends on his grace.
ramacharitamanas::5319.simple_insight: Respect softens pride, and gratitude turns even power into humility.
ramacharitamanas::5319.detailed_meaning: Back in Ayodhya's restored order, Rama and Lakshmana hurry to Vashishtha like devoted students, not kings. The joy in their bodies shows their humility. When the sage asks after them, Rama answers that their welfare depends on the teacher's mercy.
ramacharitamanas::5319.modern_relevance: You finally meet the mentor who helped you through the hardest season, and you don't perform success — you bow, thank them, and admit how much you still need grace.
ramacharitamanas::5319.insight: It shifts status into reverence, reminding you that strength stays clean when it remains teachable.

ramacharitamanas::5320.verse_sanskrit: सकल द्विजन्ह मिलि नायउ माथा। धर्म धुरंधर रघुकुलनाथा॥ गहे भरत पुनि प्रभु पद पंकज। नमत जिन्हहि सुर मुनि संकर अज ॥
ramacharitamanas::5320.verse_hindi: धर्म की धुरी धारण करने वाले रघुकुल के स्वामी श्री रामजी ने सब ब्राह्मणों से मिलकर उन्हें मस्तक नवाया। फिर भरतजी ने प्रभु के वे चरणकमल पकड़े जिन्हें देवता, मुनि, शंकरजी और ब्रह्माजी (भी) नमस्कार करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5320.english_translation: The Lord of Raghu, who upholds the pillar of dharma, bowed to all the learned priests. Then Bharat held the lotus feet of the Lord, feet that devas, sages, Shiva, and Brahma bow to.
ramacharitamanas::5320.translation_literal: सकल (all) / द्विजन्ह (the twice-born, priests) / मिलि (having met together) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head) / धर्म (dharma) / धुरंधर (bearer of the burden) / रघुकुलनाथा (lord of the Raghu clan)॥ / गहे (grasped) / भरत (Bharat) / पुनि (again) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / नमत (bow) / जिन्हहि (to whom) / सुर (devas) / मुनि (sages) / संकर (Shiva) / अज (Brahma) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5320.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5320.essence: True dignity bows first, and reverence deepens when pride disappears.
ramacharitamanas::5320.simple_meaning: Ram bows to the priests, and Bharat bows to Ram's feet. The verse shows mutual humility and reverence in the royal family.
ramacharitamanas::5320.simple_insight: Real greatness can kneel without losing anything.
ramacharitamanas::5320.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's reunion scene, Ram returns as the upholder of dharma and meets the assembled priests. He bows first, then Bharat rushes to touch the feet that even devas, sages, Shiva, and Brahma honour. The moment deepens the family’s devotion, but it is still part of the larger embrace.
ramacharitamanas::5320.modern_relevance: At a wedding, the youngest cousin bows first to the elders, and the room softens. Status drops away for a moment, and love becomes easier to feel.
ramacharitamanas::5320.insight: It shifts respect from hierarchy to humility, showing that honour grows when ego steps aside.

ramacharitamanas::5321.verse_sanskrit: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5321.verse_hindi: भरतजी पृथ्वी पर पड़े हैं, उठाए उठते नहीं। तब कृपासिंधु श्री रामजी ने उन्हें जबर्दस्ती उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया। (उनके) साँवले शरीर पर रोएँ खड़े हो गए। नवीन कमल के समान नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं के) जल की बाढ़ आ गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5321.english_translation: Bharat lies on the ground and cannot be lifted. Then the ocean of grace lifts him and holds him to his heart. Ram's dark body bristles with goosebumps, and tears flood his newly lotus-like eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5321.translation_literal: परे भूमि (fallen on the ground) / नहिं (not) / उठत (rising) / उठाए (having been lifted) / बर करि (doing a boon / graciously) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / उर (to the heart/chest) / लाए (brought) // स्यामल (dark/blue-black) / गात (body) / रोम (hairs) / भए (became) / ठाढ़े (standing up) / नव (new) / राजीव (lotus) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / बाढ़े (swelled/flooded)
ramacharitamanas::5321.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5321.essence: True devotion is met not with distance, but with an embrace that overflows.
ramacharitamanas::5321.simple_meaning: Bharat is too overwhelmed to get up on his own, so Ram lifts him and embraces him. Their love is so intense that Ram trembles with emotion and tears fill his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::5321.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that dignity disappears and only tenderness remains.
ramacharitamanas::5321.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand's reunion scene, Bharat lies at Ram's feet in surrender and grief. Ram does not wait for him to rise properly; he lifts him, draws him close, and breaks into tears. The moment shows devotion answered by love.
ramacharitamanas::5321.modern_relevance: You finally show up after months of silence, too ashamed to meet someone's eyes. Before you can explain, they pull you in. Some bonds do not need a speech; they need an embrace.
ramacharitamanas::5321.insight: It shifts devotion from formal respect to living intimacy, where surrender is met by immediate embrace.

ramacharitamanas::5322.verse_sanskrit: राजीव लोचन स्रवत जल तन ललित पुलकावलि बनी। अति प्रेम हृदयँ लगाइ अनुजहि मिले प्रभु त्रिभुअन धनी॥ प्रभु मिलत अनुजहि सोह मो पहिं जाति नहिं उपमा कही। जनु प्रेम अरु सिंगार तनु धरि मिले बर सुषमा लही ॥
ramacharitamanas::5322.verse_hindi: कमल के समान नेत्रों से जल बह रहा है। सुंदर शरीर में पुलकावली (अत्यंत) शोभा दे रही है। त्रिलोकी के स्वामी प्रभु श्री रामजी छोटे भाई भरतजी को अत्यंत प्रेम से हृदय से लगाकर मिले। भाई से मिलते समय प्रभु जैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, उसकी उपमा मुझसे कही नहीं जाती। मानो प्रेम और श्रृंगार शरीर धारण करके मिले और श्रेष्ठ शोभा को प्राप्त हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5322.english_translation: Tears flow from the lotus-like eyes. His beautiful body bristles with joy. The Lord of the three worlds embraced his younger brother with great love. No comparison can capture how splendid the Lord looked when meeting his brother. It was as if love and beauty had taken human form and met in perfect grace.
ramacharitamanas::5322.translation_literal: राजीव लोचन (lotus-eyed) / स्रवत (flowing) / जल (tears) / तन (body) / ललित (beautiful) / पुलकावलि (horripilation, a thrill of joy) / बनी (became) / अति (great) / प्रेम (love) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / लगाइ (embracing) / अनुजहि (the younger brother) / मिले (met) / प्रभु (the Lord) / त्रिभुअन धनी (lord of the three worlds)॥ / प्रभु (the Lord) / मिलत (while meeting) / अनुजहि (the younger brother) / सोह (looked splendid) / मो पहिं (to me) / जाति नहिं (does not go) / उपमा (comparison) / कही (spoken) / जनु (as if) / प्रेम (love) / अरु (and) / सिंगार (beauty, adornment) / तनु (body) / धरि (having taken) / मिले (met) / बर (excellent) / सुषमा (splendour) / लही (obtained)
ramacharitamanas::5322.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5322.essence: Love and beauty become visible when reunion finally happens.
ramacharitamanas::5322.simple_meaning: Ram meets Bharat with tears, joy, and an embrace so beautiful that no comparison can fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::5322.simple_insight: Deep love can make even reunion feel sacred and beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::5322.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya after exile, Bharat finally reaches Ram and collapses into him. Ram, ruler of the three worlds, meets his younger brother with tears, thrill, and overwhelming tenderness. The scene pauses on their embrace because this reunion is the emotional center of the chapter.
ramacharitamanas::5322.modern_relevance: You see your brother after years apart at the airport, and both of you go silent before the hug. Some reunions carry a beauty words cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::5322.insight: It shifts attention from status to intimacy, showing that true greatness is revealed in loving reunion.

ramacharitamanas::5323.verse_sanskrit: बूझत कृपानिधि कुसल भरतहि बचन बेगि न आवई॥ सुनु सिवा सो सुख बचन मन ते भिन्न जान जो पावई॥ अब कुसल कौसलनाथ आरत जानि जन दरसन दियो। बूड़त बिरह बारीस कृपानिधान मोहि कर गहि लियो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5323.verse_hindi: कृपानिधान श्री रामजी भरतजी से कुशल पूछते हैं, परंतु आनंदवश भरतजी के मुख से वचन शीघ्र नहीं निकलते। (शिवजी ने कहा-) हे पार्वती! सुनो, वह सुख (जो उस समय भरतजी को मिल रहा था) वचन और मन से परे है, उसे वही जानता है जो उसे पाता है। (भरतजी ने कहा-) हे कोसलनाथ! आपने आर्त्त (दुःखी) जानकर दास को दर्शन दिए, इससे अब कुशल है। विरह समुद्र में डूबते हुए मुझको कृपानिधान ने हाथ पकड़कर बचा लिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::5323.english_translation: The Lord of compassion asks Bharat how he is, but Bharat cannot speak at once in his joy. Shiva says to Parvati: that happiness is beyond words and mind, known only by the one who experiences it.
