Bharat says: O Lord of Kosala, seeing me in distress, you gave me your sight, and now I am well. The ocean of separation was drowning me, but the Lord of compassion held my hand and saved me.
ramacharitamanas::5323.translation_literal: बूझत (asking) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / कुसल (well-being) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / बचन (words) / बेगि (quickly) / न आवई (do not come) ॥ सुनु (listen) / सिवा (Parvati) / सो (that) / सुख (bliss) / बचन (words) / मन (mind) / ते (from) / भिन्न (separate) / जान (know) / जो (who) / पावई (obtains) ॥ अब (now) / कुसल (well-being) / कौसलनाथ (Lord of Kosala) / आरत (distressed) / जानि (knowing) / जन (servant) / दरसन (sight) / दियो (gave) । बूड़त (drowning) / बिरह (separation) / बारीस (ocean) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion) / मोहि (me) / कर (hand) / गहि (holding) / लियो (took) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5323.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::5323.essence: Love can rescue you before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::5323.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed when Ram embraces him and asks after his welfare. The joy is so deep it cannot be spoken. Bharat says Ram’s sight itself has rescued him from the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::5323.simple_insight: Some relief is too deep for language. Being seen with love can feel like being saved.
ramacharitamanas::5323.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s reunion, Ram lifts Bharat into his arms after exile and grief. Bharat is so flooded with love that he cannot answer at first. Then he says the only thing that matters: Ram’s sight has already ended his suffering.
ramacharitamanas::5323.modern_relevance: You finally reach the hospital room after a night of fear, and the person you love opens their eyes. Before any explanation, the relief itself says everything.
ramacharitamanas::5323.insight: It shifts attention from verbal reassurance to the healing power of loving presence.

ramacharitamanas::5324.verse_sanskrit: पुनि प्रभु हरषि सत्रुहन भेंटे हृदयँ लगाइ। लछिमन भरत मिले तब परम प्रेम दोउ भाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5324.verse_hindi: फिर प्रभु हर्षित होकर शत्रुघ्नजी को हृदय से लगाकर उनसे मिले। तब लक्ष्मणजी और भरतजी दोनों भाई परम प्रेम से मिले॥।5॥
ramacharitamanas::5324.english_translation: Then the Lord, delighted, embraced Shatrughna to his heart. Then Lakshman and Bharat met in deep love, both brothers.
ramacharitamanas::5324.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / प्रभु (the Lord) / हरषि (rejoicing) / सत्रुहन (Shatrughna) / भेंटे (met) / हृदयँ लगाइ (embracing to the heart) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / भरत (Bharat) / मिले (met) / तब (then) / परम प्रेम (supreme love) / दोउ भाइ (both brothers)
ramacharitamanas::5324.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5324.essence: Love restores family faster than sorrow can divide it.
ramacharitamanas::5324.simple_meaning: Ram warmly embraces Shatrughna, then Lakshman and Bharat meet in deep affection. The verse simply shows the joy of reunion among the brothers.
ramacharitamanas::5324.simple_insight: Love heals separation faster than words can.
ramacharitamanas::5324.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the long exile and sorrow, Ram finally meets his brothers again. This verse is part of the family reunion: Shatrughna is embraced first, then Lakshman and Bharat come together in overwhelming love.
ramacharitamanas::5324.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months apart, and the first hug says everything. Some reunions do more than comfort — they repair what grief had split.
ramacharitamanas::5324.insight: It highlights reunion as emotional restoration, not just a social greeting.

ramacharitamanas::5325.verse_sanskrit: भरतानुज लछिमन पुनि भेंटे। दुसह बिरह संभव दुख मेटे॥ सीता चरन भरत सिरु नावा। अनुज समेत परम सुख पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5325.verse_hindi: फिर लक्ष्मणजी शत्रुघ्नजी से गले लगकर मिले और इस प्रकार विरह से उत्पन्न दुःसह दुःख का नाश किया। फिर भाई शत्रुघ्नजी सहित भरतजी ने सीताजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया और परम सुख प्राप्त किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5325.english_translation: Lakshman and Shatrughna embraced again. The unbearable pain born of separation disappeared. Bharata bowed his head at Sita's feet with his younger brother, and they found complete joy.
ramacharitamanas::5325.translation_literal: भरतानुज (Bharata's younger brother) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / पुनि (again) / भेंटे (met, embraced) / दुसह (unbearable) / बिरह (separation) / संभव (born of) / दुख (pain) / मेटे (was erased) / सीता (Sita) / चरन (feet) / भरत (Bharata) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / परम (supreme) / सुख (joy) / पावा (found)
ramacharitamanas::5325.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5325.essence: Love ends separation faster than words can.
ramacharitamanas::5325.simple_meaning: Lakshman and Shatrughna embrace, and the pain of separation ends. Bharata bows to Sita with his brother, and joy returns.
ramacharitamanas::5325.simple_insight: Some reunions do more than comfort you — they erase a grief you were carrying in your body.
ramacharitamanas::5325.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the family finally comes together after long separation. Lakshman and Shatrughna embrace, and Bharata bows before Sita with his younger brother. The verse captures the healing that happens when love, duty, and reunion all meet at once.
ramacharitamanas::5325.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after months away and no one needs to explain the tears. A single embrace can end a season of loneliness.
ramacharitamanas::5325.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the healing power of reunion and reverence.

ramacharitamanas::5326.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु बिलोकि हरषे पुरबासी। जनित बियोग बिपति सब नासी॥ प्रेमातुर सब लोग निहारी। कौतुक कीन्ह कृपाल खरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5326.verse_hindi: प्रभु को देखकर अयोध्यावासी सब हर्षित हुए। वियोग से उत्पन्न सब दुःख नष्ट हो गए। सब लोगों को प्रेम विह्नल (और मिलने के लिए अत्यंत आतुर) देखकर खर के शत्रु कृपालु श्री रामजी ने एक चमत्कार किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5326.english_translation: Seeing the Lord, the people of Ayodhya rejoiced. All sorrow born of separation vanished. Seeing everyone overwhelmed with love and longing, the compassionate enemy of Khara performed a wondrous act.
ramacharitamanas::5326.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / हरषे (rejoiced) / पुरबासी (the city-dwellers) / जनित (born) / बियोग (separation) / बिपति (sorrow, trouble) / सब (all) / नासी (destroyed) / प्रेमातुर (overwhelmed with love and longing) / सब (all) / लोग (people) / निहारी (seeing) / कौतुक (wonder, wondrous act) / कीन्ह (did) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / खरारी (enemy of Khara)
ramacharitamanas::5326.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5326.essence: Presence from the beloved ends separation at once.
ramacharitamanas::5326.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya are overjoyed at Ram's return, and their pain of separation disappears. Seeing their longing, Ram responds with a wondrous act.
ramacharitamanas::5326.simple_insight: Being seen by what you love can dissolve grief faster than words.
ramacharitamanas::5326.detailed_meaning: Back in Ayodhya, the city has been living with the ache of separation. Now Ram is finally before them, and the whole town breaks into joy. Their longing is so intense that Ram responds with a miracle of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::5326.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months away, and the people who love you light up before you even speak. That relief, that release, is what this verse holds.
ramacharitamanas::5326.insight: It shifts attention from private grief to the healing power of loving presence.

ramacharitamanas::5327.verse_sanskrit: अमित रूप प्रगटे तेहि काला। जथाजोग मिले सबहि कृपाला॥ कृपादृष्टि रघुबीर बिलोकी। किए सकल नर नारि बिसोकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5327.verse_hindi: उसी समय कृपालु श्री रामजी असंख्य रूपों में प्रकट हो गए और सबसे (एक ही साथ) यथायोग्य मिले। श्री रघुवीर ने कृपा की दृष्टि से देखकर सब नर-नारियों को शोक से रहित कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5327.english_translation: At that moment, the compassionate Lord appeared in countless forms and met everyone in the way each needed. Looking with a merciful glance, Raghubir freed every man and woman from sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::5327.translation_literal: अमित (countless) / रूप (forms) / प्रगटे (appeared) / तेहि काला (at that moment) / जथाजोग (as was fitting) / मिले (met) / सबहि (everyone) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / कृपादृष्टि (merciful glance) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिलोकी (looking) / किए (made) / सकल (all) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / बिसोकी (free from sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::5327.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5327.essence: Compassion takes the shape each heart can receive.
ramacharitamanas::5327.simple_meaning: Ram appears in many forms so he can meet each person appropriately, and his compassionate glance removes everyone's sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::5327.simple_insight: Feeling seen can dissolve grief faster than words.
ramacharitamanas::5327.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram returns and the whole city is overwhelmed by reunion. He appears in many forms, meeting each person in the way they need, and his glance alone quiets the sorrow that had filled every heart.
ramacharitamanas::5327.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is carrying different hurt. One kind look, one careful response, and the whole atmosphere changes.
ramacharitamanas::5327.insight: It teaches you to meet people according to their need, not your script.

ramacharitamanas::5328.verse_sanskrit: छन महिं सबहि मिले भगवाना। उमा मरम यह काहुँ न जाना॥ एहि बिधि सबहि सुखी करि रामा। आगें चले सील गुन धामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5328.verse_hindi: भगवान् क्षण मात्र में सबसे मिल लिए। हे उमा! यह रहस्य किसी ने नहीं जाना। इस प्रकार शील और गुणों के धाम श्री रामजी सबको सुखी करके आगे बढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::5328.english_translation: In an instant, Bhagavan met everyone. O Uma, no one understood this mystery. In this way, Ram, the abode of gentleness and virtues, made everyone happy and moved on.
ramacharitamanas::5328.translation_literal: छन महिं (in a moment) / सबहि (everyone) / मिले (met) / भगवाना (the Lord) / उमा (O Uma) / मरम (mystery) / यह (this) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / जाना (understood) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / सबहि (everyone) / सुखी (happy) / करि (having made) / रामा (Ram) / आगें (ahead) / चले (moved on) / सील (gentleness) / गुन (virtues) / धामा (abode)
ramacharitamanas::5328.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5328.essence: Ram’s presence itself makes people whole.
ramacharitamanas::5328.simple_meaning: Ram met everyone so quickly that no one could even grasp how it happened. He comforted the whole crowd, made them happy, and then moved on.
ramacharitamanas::5328.simple_insight: Some presence heals without needing explanation.
ramacharitamanas::5328.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with joy as Ram returns. In this moment, he greets everyone so swiftly and so completely that even Uma cannot fully grasp the mystery. His gentleness itself becomes the blessing that settles the whole city.
ramacharitamanas::5328.modern_relevance: You walk into a room full of people who have been waiting for you, and somehow the tension drops before you say a word. Some people calm others just by arriving.
ramacharitamanas::5328.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the quiet power of presence and graciousness.

ramacharitamanas::5329.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्यादि मातु सब धाई। निरखि बच्छ जनु धेनु लवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5329.verse_hindi: कौसल्या आदि माताएँ ऐसे दौड़ीं मानों नई ब्यायी हुई गायें अपने बछड़ों को देखकर दौड़ी हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::5329.english_translation: Kausalya and the other mothers ran toward them, like cows rushing to their calves.
ramacharitamanas::5329.translation_literal: कौसल्यादि (Kausalya and others) / मातु (mothers) / सब (all) / धाई (ran) / निरखि (seeing) / बच्छ (calves) / जनु (like) / धेनु (cows) / लवाई (driven or rushing)
ramacharitamanas::5329.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5329.essence: Love runs before the mind can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::5329.simple_meaning: The mothers ran to meet the children, moved by the same instinct as a mother cow rushing to her calf.
ramacharitamanas::5329.simple_insight: Love can pull you forward faster than thought.
ramacharitamanas::5329.detailed_meaning: After Ram appears in many forms and meets everyone with grace, the palace mothers rush toward him and the brothers. The verse lingers on their instinctive joy, comparing them to cows running to their calves.
ramacharitamanas::5329.modern_relevance: You spot your child at the school gate after a long day and move before you even think. Some love is older than language.
ramacharitamanas::5329.insight: It turns a reunion into a living image of natural, bodily affection.

ramacharitamanas::5330.verse_sanskrit: जनु धेनु बालक बच्छ तजि गृहँ चरन बन परबस गईं। दिन अंत पुर रुख स्रवत थन हुंकार करि धावत भईं॥ अति प्रेम प्रभु सब मातु भेटीं बचन मृदु बहुबिधि कहे। गइ बिषम बिपति बियोगभव तिन्ह हरष सुख अगनित लहे॥
ramacharitamanas::5330.verse_hindi: मानो नई ब्यायी हुई गायें अपने छोटे बछड़ों को घर पर छोड़ परवश होकर वन में चरने गई हों और दिन का अंत होने पर (बछड़ों से मिलने के लिए) हुँकार करके थन से दूध गिराती हुईं नगर की ओर दौड़ी हों। प्रभु ने अत्यंत प्रेम से सब माताओं से मिलकर उनसे बहुत प्रकार के कोमल वचन कहे। वियोग से उत्पन्न भयानक विपत्ति दूर हो गई और सबने (भगवान् से मिलकर और उनके वचन सुनकर) अगणित सुख और हर्ष प्राप्त किए।
ramacharitamanas::5330.english_translation: Like freshly calved cows, leaving their calves at home, they went to graze in helplessness and then at day’s end rushed back lowing, milk flowing from their udders. With great love, the Lord met all the mothers and spoke to them in many gentle ways. The terrible suffering born of separation was removed, and they all received immeasurable joy and delight.
ramacharitamanas::5330.translation_literal: जनु (as if) / धेनु (cows) / बालक (young) / बच्छ (calves) / तजि (leaving) / गृहँ (at home) / चरन (to graze) / बन (to the forest) / परबस (helplessly) / गईं (went) / दिन अंत (at day’s end) / पुर (to the town) / रुख (lowing) / स्रवत (flowing) / थन (from the udders) / हुंकार करि (making a call) / धावत (running) / भईं (became) / अति (great) / प्रेम (love) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सब (all) / मातु (mothers) / भेटीं (met) / बचन (words) / मृदु (soft) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / कहे (spoke) / गइ (gone) / बिषम (terrible) / बिपति (distress) / बियोगभव (born of separation) / तिन्ह (their) / हरष (joy) / सुख (happiness) / अगनित (countless) / लहे (received)
ramacharitamanas::5330.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5330.essence: Love meets grief, and grief loses its hold.
ramacharitamanas::5330.simple_meaning: The mothers rush to meet Ram with overwhelming love, and his gentle meeting ends their pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::5330.simple_insight: Being seen by love can dissolve grief faster than explanation ever could.
ramacharitamanas::5330.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s reunion scene, the mothers who had long suffered separation from Ram hurry to him like cows running back to their calves. Ram greets each one tenderly, and their sorrow dissolves in the warmth of his words.
ramacharitamanas::5330.modern_relevance: You finally reach home after a long, draining trip, and the first familiar face makes your chest loosen. Some exhaustion ends the moment love meets it.
ramacharitamanas::5330.insight: It shows how loving presence and gentle words can end separation’s pain.

ramacharitamanas::5331.verse_sanskrit: भेंटेउ तनय सुमित्राँ राम चरन रति जानि। रामहि मिलत कैकई हृदयँ बहुत सकुचानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5331.verse_hindi: सुमित्राजी अपने पुत्र लक्ष्मणजी की श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रीति जानकर उनसे मिलीं। श्री रामजी से मिलते समय कैकेयीजी हृदय में बहुत सकुचाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5331.english_translation: Sumitra met her son, knowing his love for Ram's feet. Kaikeyi felt deeply shy when she met Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5331.translation_literal: भेंटेउ (met) / तनय (son) / सुमित्राँ (Sumitra) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love/attachment) / जानि (knowing) / रामहि (to Ram) / मिलत (meeting) / कैकई (Kaikeyi) / हृदयँ (in heart) / बहुत (very) / सकुचानि (felt shy/hesitated)
ramacharitamanas::5331.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5331.essence: Devotion makes meeting natural; guilt makes it painful.
ramacharitamanas::5331.simple_meaning: Sumitra came to meet Lakshman because she knew his heart belonged to Ram. Kaikeyi, by contrast, felt awkward and ashamed when facing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5331.simple_insight: Love makes reunion easy; guilt makes even a simple meeting feel heavy.
ramacharitamanas::5331.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the mothers gather around their sons after the long separation. Sumitra comes forward warmly, knowing Lakshman’s devotion to Ram. Kaikeyi, burdened by what she has done, cannot meet Ram with ease.
ramacharitamanas::5331.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one parent beams with pride and another can barely look up. The difference is not the room — it is the heart each person brings into it.
ramacharitamanas::5331.insight: It shows how inner devotion creates openness, while inner conflict creates hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::5332.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन सब मातन्ह मिलि हरषे आसिष पाइ। कैकइ कहँ पुनि पुनि मिले मन कर छोभु न जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5332.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी भी सब माताओं से मिलकर और आशीर्वाद पाकर हर्षित हुए। वे कैकेयीजी से बार-बार मिले, परंतु उनके मन का क्षोभ (रोष) नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5332.english_translation: Lakshman was delighted after meeting all the mothers and receiving their blessings. He met Kaikeyi again and again, but the hurt in his heart would not go away.
ramacharitamanas::5332.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / सब (all) / मातन्ह (mothers) / मिलि (meeting) / हरषे (were delighted) / आसिष (blessings) / पाइ (having received) / कैकइ (Kaikeyi) / कहँ (to) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / मिले (met) / मन (mind/heart) / कर (of) / छोभु (hurt/agitation) / जाइ (goes)
ramacharitamanas::5332.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5332.essence: Blessings can soften the moment, but they do not erase old hurt.
ramacharitamanas::5332.simple_meaning: Lakshman is happy to meet the mothers and receive their blessings, but his hurt stays alive when he sees Kaikeyi again.
ramacharitamanas::5332.simple_insight: Some wounds do not vanish just because you are polite.
ramacharitamanas::5332.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s reunion, Lakshman receives the mothers’ blessings with joy. But Kaikeyi’s role in Ram’s exile still stings him, so even repeated meetings cannot erase the hurt. The verse shows a heart torn between respect and pain.
ramacharitamanas::5332.modern_relevance: You smile at the family gathering, but one person’s name still tightens your chest. You can be courteous and still not be healed.
ramacharitamanas::5332.insight: It shows how unresolved hurt can coexist with outward respect and social grace.

ramacharitamanas::5333.verse_sanskrit: सासुन्ह सबनि मिली बैदेही । चरनन्हि लाग हरषु अति तेही॥ देहिं असीस बूझि कुसलाता। होइ अचल तुम्हार अहिवाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::5333.verse_hindi: जानकीजी सब सासुओं से मिलीं और उनके चरणों में लगकर उन्हें अत्यंत हर्ष हुआ। सासुएँ कुशल पूछकर आशीष दे रही हैं कि तुम्हारा सुहाग अचल हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5333.english_translation: Janaki met all her mothers-in-law and bowed at their feet, filling them with great joy. The mothers-in-law asked after her well-being and blessed her: may your married life remain unbroken.
ramacharitamanas::5333.translation_literal: सासुन्ह (mothers-in-law) / सबनि (all) / मिली (met) / बैदेही (Janaki) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / लाग (bowed) / हरषु (joy) / अति (greatly) / तेही (there)॥ देहिं (they give) / असीस (blessings) / बूझि (asking) / कुसलाता (well-being) / होइ (may be) / अचल (unbroken) / तुम्हार (your) / अहिवाता (married life) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5333.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5333.essence: Humility opens the door to blessing.
ramacharitamanas::5333.simple_meaning: Janaki greets all the elder women respectfully, and they bless her with wishes for a lasting marriage.
ramacharitamanas::5333.simple_insight: Respect softens a room, and blessing becomes easy when pride is set aside.
ramacharitamanas::5333.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya after Ram's return, Sita meets the elder women of the family. She bows at their feet, they bless her warmly, and the household's tenderness becomes visible in one simple exchange.
ramacharitamanas::5333.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a long absence, touch the elders' feet, and the whole room relaxes. Respect turns distance into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::5333.insight: It shows how humility invites care and restores harmony in a home.

ramacharitamanas::5334.verse_sanskrit: सब रघुपति मुख कमल बिलोकहिं। मंगल जानि नयन जल रोकहिं॥ कनक थार आरती उतारहिं। बार बार प्रभु गात निहारहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5334.verse_hindi: सब माताएँ श्री रघुनाथजी का कमल सा मुखड़ा देख रही हैं। (नेत्रों से प्रेम के आँसू उमड़े आते हैं, परंतु) मंगल का समय जानकर वे आँसुओं के जल को नेत्रों में ही रोक रखती हैं। सोने के थाल से आरती उतारती हैं और बार-बार प्रभु के श्री अंगों की ओर देखती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5334.english_translation: All the mothers gaze at Raghupati's lotus face. Knowing this is an auspicious moment, they hold back their tears. They wave lamps in worship from golden trays and keep looking again and again at the Lord's beautiful form.
ramacharitamanas::5334.translation_literal: सब (all) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / मुख (face) / कमल (lotus) / बिलोकहिं (they behold) / मंगल (auspicious) / जानि (knowing) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water, tears) / रोकहिं (they hold back) / कनक (golden) / थार (tray) / आरती (worship with lamps) / उतारहिं (they wave off) / बार बार (again and again) / प्रभु (Lord) / गात (body, form) / निहारहिं (they gaze at)
ramacharitamanas::5334.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5334.essence: Joy so full it becomes worship.
ramacharitamanas::5334.simple_meaning: The queens look at Ram with tears of joy, but they hold those tears back because the moment is sacred. They worship him with lamps and cannot stop gazing at him.
ramacharitamanas::5334.simple_insight: Love can be so full it becomes quiet reverence instead of speech.
ramacharitamanas::5334.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram has returned and the palace women are overwhelmed. The mothers stand before him, seeing his lotus-like face, holding back tears because the moment is too blessed for grief. Their worship and repeated gazing show devotion overflowing into ritual.
ramacharitamanas::5334.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have waited months to welcome home. You want to cry, laugh, and speak at once — but first you just look, because presence itself feels sacred.
ramacharitamanas::5334.insight: It shifts attention from words to reverent seeing, where love is expressed through gaze and offering.

ramacharitamanas::5335.verse_sanskrit: नाना भाँति निछावरि करहीं। परमानंद हरष उर भरहीं॥ कौसल्या पुनि पुनि रघुबीरहि। चितवति कृपासिंधु रनधीरहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5335.verse_hindi: अनेकों प्रकार से निछावरें करती हैं और हृदय में परमानंद तथा हर्ष भर रही हैं। कौसल्याजी बार-बार कृपा के समुद्र और रणधीर श्री रघुवीर को देख रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5335.english_translation: They offer many kinds of gifts and their hearts fill with supreme bliss and joy. Kaushalya keeps looking again and again at Raghubir, the ocean of grace and the fearless warrior.
ramacharitamanas::5335.translation_literal: नाना भाँति (many kinds) / निछावरि (offerings) / करहीं (they do) / परमानंद (supreme bliss) / हरष (joy) / उर (heart) / भरहीं (fill) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / रघुबीरहि (Raghubir) / चितवति (looking at) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / रनधीरहि (fearless in battle) /
ramacharitamanas::5335.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5335.essence: Victory becomes sweetest when a mother can only keep looking.
ramacharitamanas::5335.simple_meaning: The women keep offering gifts and feeling joy, while Kaushalya keeps gazing at Ram with overflowing love.
ramacharitamanas::5335.simple_insight: Love makes even a homecoming feel too large for words.
ramacharitamanas::5335.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the family has finally reunited after exile and war. The mothers and women shower gifts on Ram, and Kaushalya cannot stop looking at her son, amazed that the gentle boy is also the fearless victor of Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::5335.modern_relevance: You watch your child come home after years away, and the sight keeps undoing you. Relief, pride, and gratitude all arrive at once.
ramacharitamanas::5335.insight: It turns victory into tenderness, showing that the deepest response to greatness is grateful love.

ramacharitamanas::5336.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ बिचारति बारहिं बारा। कवन भाँति लंकापति मारा॥ अति सुकुमार जुगल मेरे बारे। निसिचर सुभट महाबल भारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5336.verse_hindi: वे बार-बार हृदय में विचारती हैं कि इन्होंने लंकापति रावण को कैसे मारा? मेरे ये दोनों बच्चे बड़े ही सुकुमार हैं और राक्षस तो ब़ड़े भारी योद्धा और महान् बली थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5336.english_translation: She keeps wondering in her heart, again and again: how did they kill the lord of Lanka? My two boys are so tender, while the demons were mighty warriors of great strength.
ramacharitamanas::5336.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारति (keeps thinking) / बारहिं बारा (again and again) / कवन भाँति (by what means) / लंकापति (lord of Lanka) / मारा (was killed) / अति (very) / सुकुमार (tender) / जुगल (the two) / मेरे (my) / बारे (boys/children) / निसिचर (demons) / सुभट (warriors) / महाबल (great strength) / भारे (heavy/mighty)
ramacharitamanas::5336.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::5336.essence: Tenderness can carry a power that looks impossible until it wins.
ramacharitamanas::5336.simple_meaning: Kausalya cannot stop wondering how Rama and Lakshman defeated Ravana. She sees her sons as tender boys and Ravana's side as powerful warriors.
ramacharitamanas::5336.simple_insight: Love often cannot measure courage by appearances.
ramacharitamanas::5336.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the mothers are overwhelmed as Rama returns in victory. Kausalya looks at her gentle sons and cannot reconcile their softness with the defeat of Ravana, the mighty lord of Lanka. Her wonder becomes praise.
ramacharitamanas::5336.modern_relevance: You watch your quiet child stand up to a bully and feel stunned afterward. The strength was always there, even if you could not see it.
ramacharitamanas::5336.insight: It shifts attention from visible fragility to the hidden force that made victory possible.

ramacharitamanas::5337.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन अरु सीता सहित प्रभुहि बिलोकति मातु। परमानंद मगन मन पुनि पुनि पुलकित गातु ॥
ramacharitamanas::5337.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी को माता देख रही हैं। उनका मन परमानंद में मग्न है और शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::5337.english_translation: The mother beholds the Lord with Lakshman and Sita. Her mind is soaked in supreme joy, and her body keeps trembling with delight.
ramacharitamanas::5337.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / अरु (and) / सीता (Sita) / सहित (together with) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकति (beholds) / मातु (the mother) / परमानंद (supreme joy) / मगन (immersed) / मन (mind) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पुलकित (thrilled) / गातु (body)
ramacharitamanas::5337.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5337.essence: Seeing Ram fills the heart so completely that the body cannot stay still.
ramacharitamanas::5337.simple_meaning: Mother Kaushalya sees Ram with Lakshman and Sita, and her heart overflows with joy. Her whole body shivers with happiness.
ramacharitamanas::5337.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that joy shows up in the body itself.
ramacharitamanas::5337.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaushalya finally sees Ram returned with Lakshman and Sita after the war. The sight overwhelms her. Her joy is not quiet relief but a full-body ecstasy, marking the homecoming that closes the grief of exile.
ramacharitamanas::5337.modern_relevance: You spot your child at the airport after months apart, and your chest tightens before you can speak. Some reunions are felt before they are understood.
ramacharitamanas::5337.insight: It shows how devotion and relief can become a physical experience, not just an emotion.

ramacharitamanas::5338.verse_sanskrit: लंकापति कपीस नल नीला। जामवंत अंगद सुभसीला॥ हनुमदादि सब बानर बीरा। धरे मनोहर मनुज सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5338.verse_hindi: लंकापति विभीषण, वानरराज सुग्रीव, नल, नील, जाम्बवान् और अंगद तथा हनुमान् जी आदि सभी उत्तम स्वभाव वाले वीर वानरों ने मनुष्यों के मनोहर शरीर धारण कर लिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5338.english_translation: Vibhishana, king of Lanka; Sugriva, Nala, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, and Hanuman and all the noble monkey warriors took on charming human forms.
ramacharitamanas::5338.translation_literal: लंकापति (lord of Lanka) / कपीस (lord of monkeys) / नल (Nala) / नीला (Nila) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / अंगद (Angada) / सुभसीला (of noble conduct) / हनुमदादि (Hanuman and others) / सब (all) / बानर बीरा (monkey warriors) / धरे (assumed) / मनोहर (charming) / मनुज सरीरा (human bodies)
ramacharitamanas::5338.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5338.essence: The allies appear together in forms fit for celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5338.simple_meaning: Vibhishana, Sugriva, Nala, Nila, Jambavan, Angada, Hanuman, and the other monkey warriors all took beautiful human forms.
ramacharitamanas::5338.simple_insight: A great gathering is being prepared, with each ally now appearing in a form fit for the city.
ramacharitamanas::5338.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the reunion is unfolding. Rama’s allies from Lanka and the monkey host are all shown in human forms as the celebration continues around the returning king. This line simply names the transformed companions before the city’s praise begins.
ramacharitamanas::5338.modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with people you once knew only by role or reputation, and suddenly everyone looks ready for the same joy. The scene matters more than any one face.
ramacharitamanas::5338.insight: It shifts attention from individual identity to the shared dignity of a united company.

ramacharitamanas::5339.verse_sanskrit: भरत सनेह सील ब्रत नेमा। सादर सब बरनहिं अति प्रेमा॥ देखि नगरबासिन्ह कै रीती। सकल सराहहिं प्रभु पद प्रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::5339.verse_hindi: वे सब भरतजी के प्रेम, सुंदर, स्वभाव (त्याग के) व्रत और नियमों की अत्यंत प्रेम से आदरपूर्वक बड़ाई कर रहे हैं और नगर वासियों की (प्रेम, शील और विनय से पूर्ण) रीति देखकर वे सब प्रभु के चरणों में उनके प्रेम की सराहना कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5339.english_translation: They all praise Bharat's love, character, vows, and rules with deep respect. Seeing the way the city people live, they all praise their devotion to the Lord's feet.
ramacharitamanas::5339.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सनेह (love) / सील (character) / ब्रत (vows) / नेमा (rules, observances) / सादर (with respect) / सब (all) / बरनहिं (praise) / अति प्रेमा (with great love)॥ / देखि (seeing) / नगरबासिन्ह (of the city dwellers) / कै (of) / रीती (way, conduct) / सकल (all) / सराहहिं (praise) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / प्रीती (love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5339.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5339.essence: True greatness is praised through love, restraint, and humble devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5339.simple_meaning: Everyone respectfully praises Bharat's loving nature, good conduct, vows, and discipline, along with the city's devotion and humble way of living.
ramacharitamanas::5339.simple_insight: Quiet goodness leaves a deeper mark than loud achievement.
ramacharitamanas::5339.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya after Ram's return, the people are overwhelmed by the nobility around them. They admire Bharat's loving restraint and the city's humble devotion, because this homecoming reveals what true greatness looks like in daily conduct.
ramacharitamanas::5339.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, the person everyone quietly admires is not the loudest one, but the one whose restraint, loyalty, and steadiness make everyone feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::5339.insight: It shifts attention from status to the character that earns genuine respect.

ramacharitamanas::5340.verse_sanskrit: पुनि रघुपति सब सखा बोलाए। मुनि पद लागहु सकल सिखाए॥ गुर बसिष्ट कुलपूज्य हमारे। इन्ह की कृपाँ दनुज रन मारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5340.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी ने सब सखाओं को बुलाया और सबको सिखाया कि मुनि के चरणों में लगो। ये गुरु वशिष्ठजी हमारे कुलभर के पूज्य हैं। इन्हीं की कृपा से रण में राक्षस मारे गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5340.english_translation: Then Raghupati called all his companions and taught them to bow at the feet of the sage. "Vashistha, our family teacher, is worthy of worship. It is by his grace that the demons were slain in battle."
ramacharitamanas::5340.translation_literal: पुनि (then/again) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / सब (all) / सखा (companions) / बोलाए (called) / मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / लागहु (bow/attach yourselves) / सकल (all) / सिखाए (taught) ॥ / गुर (teacher) / बसिष्ट (Vashistha) / कुलपूज्य (family-worthy-of-worship) / हमारे (our) / इन्ह (by these) / की (of) / कृपाँ (grace) / दनुज (demons) / रन (battle) / मारे (were slain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5340.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5340.essence: Victory stays clean when you credit the grace behind it.
ramacharitamanas::5340.simple_meaning: Ram gathers his companions and reminds them to honor their teacher, Vashistha, because the victory in battle came through his grace, not their own strength alone.
ramacharitamanas::5340.simple_insight: Success feels lighter when you remember who helped carry you there.
ramacharitamanas::5340.detailed_meaning: After the war, Ram stands with his companions and points them back to Vashistha, the family teacher. Even after victory, he teaches humility: bow to the one whose grace made the triumph possible.
ramacharitamanas::5340.modern_relevance: You finish a hard project and everyone wants credit to land on the loudest person in the room. Ram’s words pull the spotlight back to the mentor, the support, and the unseen help that made success possible.
ramacharitamanas::5340.insight: It shifts praise away from ego and toward gratitude, so achievement does not harden into pride.

ramacharitamanas::5341.verse_sanskrit: ए सब सखा सुनहु मुनि मेरे। भए समर सागर कहँ बेरे॥ मम हित लागि जन्म इन्ह हारे। भरतहु ते मोहि अधिक पिआरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5341.verse_hindi: (फिर गुरुजी से कहा-) हे मुनि! सुनिए। ये सब मेरे सखा हैं। ये संग्राम रूपी समुद्र में मेरे लिए बेड़े (जहाज) के समान हुए। मेरे हित के लिए इन्होंने अपने जन्म तक हार दिए (अपने प्राणों तक को होम दिया) ये मुझे भरत से भी अधिक प्रिय हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5341.english_translation: O sage, listen: all these friends are mine. They have been like boats for me across the ocean of battle. For my sake they have given up even their lives. They are dearer to me than Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::5341.translation_literal: ए (these) / सब (all) / सखा (friends) / सुनहु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / मेरे (my) / भए (became) / समर (battle) / सागर (ocean) / कहँ (for) / बेरे (boats) / मम (my) / हित (welfare) / लागि (for) / जन्म (life/birth) / इन्ह (these) / हारे (gave up) / भरतहु (even Bharat) / ते (than) / मोहि (to me) / अधिक (more) / पिआरे (dear)
ramacharitamanas::5341.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::5341.essence: Sacrifice turns friends into the boats that carry you across danger.
ramacharitamanas::5341.simple_meaning: Ram praises his friends as the ones who carried him through danger and gave everything for his welfare. He values their loyalty even above Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::5341.simple_insight: Real love shows itself in sacrifice, not words.
ramacharitamanas::5341.detailed_meaning: In Ram's reign, he speaks to the sage and publicly honors the friends who stood with him in battle. He calls them the boats that carried him across danger, saying they gave their lives for his welfare and are dearer to him than Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::5341.modern_relevance: After a crisis, you finally see who stayed when things were hard, who answered the call, who gave time and strength without keeping score. That loyalty changes how you hold them forever.
ramacharitamanas::5341.insight: It shifts attention from status and bloodline to the quiet people whose sacrifice actually carried you.

ramacharitamanas::5342.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन मगन सब भए। निमिष निमिष उपजत सुख नए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5342.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर सब प्रेम और आनंद में मग्न हो गए। इस प्रकार पल-पल में उन्हें नए-नए सुख उत्पन्न हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5342.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, everyone became absorbed in bliss. Moment by moment, new joy kept arising.
ramacharitamanas::5342.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (Lord) / बचन (words) / मगन (absorbed) / सब (all) / भए (became) / निमिष (moment) / निमिष (moment) / उपजत (arising) / सुख (joy) / नए (new)
ramacharitamanas::5342.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5342.essence: Ram's words don't just please you; they keep creating joy.
ramacharitamanas::5342.simple_meaning: Ram's words fill everyone with fresh delight, and that joy keeps renewing itself every moment.
ramacharitamanas::5342.simple_insight: Real devotion doesn't wear out; it keeps opening into fresh joy.
ramacharitamanas::5342.detailed_meaning: After Ram asks everyone to honor the sage and his teacher, the gathered companions hear his words and are swept into delight. In that sacred family atmosphere, joy is not a one-time feeling but a living current that keeps renewing itself.
ramacharitamanas::5342.modern_relevance: You hear a voice note from someone you love after a hard day, and your chest loosens before the message even ends. Some words don't just inform you — they restore you.
ramacharitamanas::5342.insight: It shifts attention from the speaker's command to the transforming effect of sacred speech.

ramacharitamanas::5343.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या के चरनन्हि पुनि तिन्ह नायउ माथ। आसिष दीन्हे हरषि तुम्ह प्रिय मम जिमि रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5343.verse_hindi: फिर उन लोगों ने कौसल्याजी के चरणों में मस्तक नवाए। कौसल्याजी ने हर्षित होकर आशीषें दीं (और कहा-) तुम मुझे रघुनाथ के समान प्यारे हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::5343.english_translation: Then they bowed their heads again at Kaushalya's feet. Kaushalya, delighted, gave her blessings and said, “You are as dear to me as Raghunath himself.”
ramacharitamanas::5343.translation_literal: कौसल्या के (of Kaushalya) / चरनन्हि (feet) / पुनि (again) / तिन्ह (they) / नायउ (bowed) / माथ (head) / आसिष (blessings) / दीन्हे (gave) / हरषि (delighted) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रिय (dear) / मम (to me) / जिमि (like) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::5343.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5343.essence: Love for Ram turns his people into your own.
ramacharitamanas::5343.simple_meaning: Kaushalya blesses the visitors and says they are as dear to her as Ram himself. Their love for Ram has made them part of her own heart.
ramacharitamanas::5343.simple_insight: Devotion does not stay private; it creates family wherever it lands.
ramacharitamanas::5343.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the returned heroes bow to Kaushalya, Ram's mother. She responds not like a queen receiving guests, but like a mother receiving her son's beloved companions. Their bond with Ram has made them precious to her too.
ramacharitamanas::5343.modern_relevance: You bring home a friend who helped you through your hardest year, and your mother greets them like family. Love for one person quietly expands the whole house.
ramacharitamanas::5343.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to shared belonging. Loving Ram changes how you see everyone connected to Him.

ramacharitamanas::5344.verse_sanskrit: सुमन बृष्टि नभ संकुल भवन चले सुखकंद। चढ़ी अटारिन्ह देखहिं नगर नारि नर बृंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::5344.verse_hindi: आनन्दकन्द श्री रामजी अपने महल को चले, आकाश फूलों की वृष्टि से छा गया। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुषों के समूह अटारियों पर चढ़कर उनके दर्शन कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5344.english_translation: Ram, the source of joy, walked toward his palace. The sky filled with showers of flowers, and men and women in the city climbed onto terraces to see him.
ramacharitamanas::5344.translation_literal: सुमन (flowers) / बृष्टि (shower) / नभ (sky) / संकुल (filled) / भवन (palace) / चले (went) / सुखकंद (source of joy) / चढ़ी (having climbed) / अटारिन्ह (terraces) / देखहिं (see) / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / बृंद (groups)
ramacharitamanas::5344.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5344.essence: Joy becomes visible when the whole city turns to look.
ramacharitamanas::5344.simple_meaning: Ram returns to his palace while the sky showers flowers and the city watches him from the rooftops.
ramacharitamanas::5344.simple_insight: The moment is pure celebration, with everyone drawn upward just to behold him.
ramacharitamanas::5344.detailed_meaning: After the blessings and joy of the previous lines, Ram walks back to his palace in Ayodhya. The city responds like a festival: flowers rain from above, and people climb terraces to catch a glimpse of him. The verse is scene-setting, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5344.modern_relevance: A whole neighborhood leans out of balconies for a glimpse of someone they love and trust. The street itself feels blessed because one beloved person has passed through it.
ramacharitamanas::5344.insight: It shifts attention from private arrival to shared reverence.

ramacharitamanas::5345.verse_sanskrit: कंचन कलस बिचित्र सँवारे। सबहिं धरे सजि निज निज द्वारे॥ बंदनवार पताका केतू। सबन्हि बनाए मंगल हेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::5345.verse_hindi: सोने के कलशों को विचित्र रीति से (मणि-रत्नादि से) अलंकृत कर और सजाकर सब लोगों ने अपने-अपने दरवाजों पर रख लिया। सब लोगों ने मंगल के लिए बंदनवार, ध्वजा और पताकाएँ लगाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5345.english_translation: Golden pots, beautifully decorated with jewels, were placed at each home’s doorway. Every house was adorned with festoons, flags, and banners for the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5345.translation_literal: कंचन (golden) / कलस (pots) / बिचित्र (variously) / सँवारे (decorated) / सबहिं (all) / धरे (placed) / सजि (having arranged) / निज निज (each one’s own) / द्वारे (at the doorway) / बंदनवार (festoons) / पताका (flags) / केतू (banners) / सबन्हि (all) / बनाए (made) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / हेतू (for the sake of)
ramacharitamanas::5345.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5345.essence: A beloved arrival turns every doorway into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5345.simple_meaning: Everyone decorated their doorways with golden pots, festoons, flags, and banners to welcome the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5345.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when a whole city prepares together.
ramacharitamanas::5345.detailed_meaning: Ram has returned to Ayodhya, and the city is overflowing with welcome. After the people bow to Kaushalya and watch Ram go to his palace, they begin adorning every doorway with ceremonial beauty. This verse shows the city itself joining the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5345.modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood where every balcony has lights, flowers, and flags because someone beloved is coming home. The streets themselves seem to be smiling.
ramacharitamanas::5345.insight: It shifts attention from one person’s joy to a whole community expressing welcome together.

ramacharitamanas::5346.verse_sanskrit: बीथीं सकल सुगंध सिंचाई। गजमनि रचि बहु चौक पुराईं। नाना भाँति सुमंगल साजे। हरषि नगर निसान बहु बाजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5346.verse_hindi: सारी गलियाँ सुगंधित द्रवों से सिंचाई गईं। गजमुक्ताओं से रचकर बहुत सी चौकें पुराई गईं। अनेकों प्रकार के सुंदर मंगल साज सजाए गए और हर्षपूर्वक नगर में बहुत से डंके बजने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5346.english_translation: All the lanes were sprinkled with fragrant liquids. Courtyards were filled and decorated with elephant pearls. Many kinds of auspicious decorations were arranged, and drums sounded joyfully throughout the city.
ramacharitamanas::5346.translation_literal: बीथीं (lanes/streets) / सकल (all) / सुगंध (fragrant) / सिंचाई (sprinkled/watered) / गजमनि (elephant pearls) / रचि (arranged) / बहु (many) / चौक (courtyards/open squares) / पुराईं (filled) / नाना भाँति (many kinds) / सुमंगल (highly auspicious) / साजे (decorations) / हरषि (joyfully) / नगर (city) / निसान (drums) / बहु (many) / बाजे (sounded)
ramacharitamanas::5346.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5346.essence: Joy announces itself before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::5346.simple_meaning: The city is being decorated for a joyful celebration. Streets are scented, courtyards are prepared, and drums sound everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::5346.simple_insight: Joy changes a whole city into one shared heartbeat.
ramacharitamanas::5346.detailed_meaning: Ram has returned to a city that has waited in longing. The streets are being prepared with fragrance, ornaments, and drums before the people even fully gather. This verse is part of the unfolding welcome, not the central teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::5346.modern_relevance: You catch the smell of fresh flowers in the hallway before guests arrive. The whole house starts feeling different because something precious is coming.
ramacharitamanas::5346.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere devotion creates around it.

ramacharitamanas::5347.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ नारि निछावरि करहीं। देहिं असीस हरष उर भरहीं॥ कंचन थार आरतीं नाना। जुबतीं सजें करहिं सुभ गाना ॥ `
ramacharitamanas::5347.verse_hindi: स्त्रियाँ जहाँ-तहाँ निछावर कर रही हैं और हृदय में हर्षित होकर आशीर्वाद देती हैं। बहुत सी युवती (सौभाग्यवती) स्त्रियाँ सोने के थालों में अनेकों प्रकार की आरती सजाकर मंगलगान कर रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5347.english_translation: Women everywhere offer gifts, give blessings, and sing auspicious songs with joyful hearts. Many young women arrange different kinds of aarti on golden plates.
ramacharitamanas::5347.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / नारि (women) / निछावरि (offerings) / करहीं (do) / देहिं (give) / असीस (blessings) / हरष (joy) / उर (heart) / भरहीं (fill)॥ / कंचन (golden) / थार (plates) / आरतीं (aarti lamps) / नाना (various) / जुबतीं (young women) / सजें (adorned) / करहिं (do) / सुभ (auspicious) / गाना (songs)॥
ramacharitamanas::5347.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5347.essence: Public joy turns into blessing, offering, and song.
ramacharitamanas::5347.simple_meaning: Women across the city are making offerings, blessing others, and singing auspicious songs with full hearts.
ramacharitamanas::5347.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when gratitude turns into offering.
ramacharitamanas::5347.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is being decorated for Ram's return. The streets are ready, and now the women of the city join the welcome with gifts, blessings, aarti, and song. The verse adds to the rising public celebration.
ramacharitamanas::5347.modern_relevance: A neighborhood that has been waiting all week finally sees the guest arrive, and people step out with flowers, lights, and song. Some moments are too full for words alone.
ramacharitamanas::5347.insight: It shows how collective joy naturally becomes ritual, song, and offering.

ramacharitamanas::5348.verse_sanskrit: करहिं आरती आरतिहर कें। रघुकुल कमल बिपिन दिनकर कें॥ पुर सोभा संपति कल्याना। निगम सेष सारदा बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::5348.verse_hindi: वे आर्तिहर (दुःखों को हरने वाले) और सूर्यकुल रूपी कमलवन को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले सूर्य श्री रामजी की आरती कर रही हैं। नगर की शोभा, संपत्ति और कल्याण का वेद, शेषजी और सरस्वतीजी वर्णन करते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::5348.english_translation: They perform the aarti of Ram, the remover of suffering and the sun that makes the Raghu line bloom. The city's beauty, wealth, and auspiciousness are described by the Vedas, Shesha, and Saraswati.
ramacharitamanas::5348.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / आरती (aarti) / आरतिहर (remover of suffering) / कें (of) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / कमल (lotus) / बिपिन (forest) / दिनकर (sun) / कें (of) / पुर (city) / सोभा (beauty) / संपति (wealth) / कल्याना (auspiciousness) / निगम (Vedas) / सेष (Shesha) / सारदा (Saraswati) / बखाना (describe)
ramacharitamanas::5348.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5348.essence: Ram's presence turns a city into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::5348.simple_meaning: People are worshipping Ram as the one who removes suffering and brings the Raghu line to full bloom. His city is so beautiful and blessed that even the Vedas, Shesha, and Saraswati cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::5348.simple_insight: Some presence makes a whole world feel blessed, ordered, and alive.
ramacharitamanas::5348.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is being decorated for Ram's return. Women sing, wave lamps, and praise him as the one who ends suffering. The scene builds the glory of his reign, but this verse is still part of the unfolding celebration, not the central teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5348.modern_relevance: A house fills with light when someone loved returns after a long absence. The decorations matter less than the feeling: relief, joy, and a sense that everything is finally in its place.
ramacharitamanas::5348.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the healing presence that makes celebration possible.

ramacharitamanas::5349.verse_sanskrit: तेउ यह चरित देखि ठगि रहहीं। उमा तासु गुन नर किमि कहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5349.verse_hindi: परंतु वे भी यह चरित्र देखकर ठगे से रह जाते हैं (स्तम्भित हो रहते हैं)। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे उमा! तब भला मनुष्य उनके गुणों को कैसे कह सकते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5349.english_translation: Even they remain stunned after seeing this wondrous play. O Uma, how can any human fully speak of his qualities?
ramacharitamanas::5349.translation_literal: तेउ (even they) / यह (this) / चरित (play, conduct) / देखि (seeing) / ठगि (dazed, stunned) / रहहीं (remain) / उमा (O Uma) / तासु (his) / गुन (qualities) / नर (human) / किमि (how) / कहहीं (can speak)
ramacharitamanas::5349.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5349.essence: Ram's greatness leaves every mind speechless.
ramacharitamanas::5349.simple_meaning: Even the most perceptive beings are left speechless by Ram's deeds. Human language cannot fully capture his qualities.
ramacharitamanas::5349.simple_insight: It leaves you humble, because some greatness can be witnessed but never fully explained.
ramacharitamanas::5349.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's joy, Shiva describes Ram's return and the people's devotion. The scene is so full of wonder that even celestial beings are stunned. Shiva turns to Uma and says Ram's qualities exceed human speech itself.
ramacharitamanas::5349.modern_relevance: You watch someone quietly hold a family together through grief, and everyone around them goes still. The heart knows their greatness long before language catches up.
ramacharitamanas::5349.insight: It shifts attention from explaining sacred greatness to bowing before it.

ramacharitamanas::5350.verse_sanskrit: नारि कुमुदिनीं अवध सर रघुपति बिरह दिनेस। अस्त भएँ बिगसत भईं निरखि राम राकेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5350.verse_hindi: स्त्रियाँ कुमुदनी हैं, अयोध्या सरोवर है और श्री रघुनाथजी का विरह सूर्य है (इस विरह सूर्य के ताप से वे मुरझा गई थीं)। अब उस विरह रूपी सूर्य के अस्त होने पर श्री राम रूपी पूर्णचन्द्र को निरखकर वे खिल उठीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5350.english_translation: Women are like lilies, Ayodhya is the lake, and Raghupati's separation is the sun. When that sun set, they bloomed again at the sight of Ram, the moon.
ramacharitamanas::5350.translation_literal: नारि (women) / कुमुदिनीं (lilies) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सर (lake) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / बिरह (separation) / दिनेस (sun) / अस्त भएँ (having set) / बिगसत (blooming) / भईं (became) / निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / राकेस (moon)
ramacharitamanas::5350.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5350.essence: Ram's return makes what love had wilted bloom again.
ramacharitamanas::5350.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya, especially the women, had wilted in Ram's absence. Now that Ram has returned, they bloom again with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5350.simple_insight: Deep longing can drain the heart; the beloved's return brings it back to life.
ramacharitamanas::5350.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram's exile has weighed on the whole city. Tulsidas compares the women to lilies in a lake: they close under the heat of separation, then open again when Ram, like the moon, is seen. It is a scene of collective relief before Ram's return home.
ramacharitamanas::5350.modern_relevance: You walk into a home that has felt heavy for months, and the mood changes the moment the person everyone missed steps through the door.
ramacharitamanas::5350.insight: It turns absence and return into a living image, showing how love can wilt and revive an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::5351.verse_sanskrit: होहिं सगुन सुभ बिबिधि बिधि बाजहिं गगन निसान। पुर नर नारि सनाथ करि भवन चले भगवान। 9 ख॥
ramacharitamanas::5351.verse_hindi: अनेक प्रकार के शुभ शकुन हो रहे हैं, आकाश में नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। नगर के पुरुषों और स्त्रियों को सनाथ (दर्शन द्वारा कृतार्थ) करके भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी महल को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::5351.english_translation: Many auspicious signs appeared, and drums sounded in the sky. Blessing the men and women of the city with their sight, Bhagavan Shri Ramchandra returned to the palace.
ramacharitamanas::5351.translation_literal: होहिं (are happening) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सुभ (good) / बिबिधि बिधि (in many ways) / बाजहिं (are sounding) / गगन (sky) / निसान (drums) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सनाथ (blessed with a protector) / करि (having made) / भवन (palace) / चले (went) / भगवान (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::5351.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5351.essence: Ram’s presence blesses a city even before he speaks.
ramacharitamanas::5351.simple_meaning: Good omens appear, heavenly drums sound, and Ram returns to the palace after giving the city’s people the blessing of his presence.
ramacharitamanas::5351.simple_insight: Some moments feel holy before anyone speaks. Presence itself can leave people comforted and complete.
ramacharitamanas::5351.detailed_meaning: Ram has already been seen by the people of Ayodhya, and the city is still glowing with that sight. With auspicious signs and celestial drums around him, he turns back toward the palace, leaving men and women feeling blessed and protected.
ramacharitamanas::5351.modern_relevance: You leave a gathering and everyone is still quieter than before, but somehow steadier. A single gracious presence can change the mood of an entire room.
ramacharitamanas::5351.insight: It shifts attention from action alone to the blessing carried by presence itself.

ramacharitamanas::5352.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु जानी कैकई लजानी। प्रथम तासु गृह गए भवानी॥ ताहि प्रबोधि बहुत सुख दीन्हा। पुनि निज भवन गवन हरि कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::5352.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! प्रभु ने जान लिया कि माता कैकेयी लज्जित हो गई हैं (इसलिए), वे पहले उन्हीं के महल को गए और उन्हें समझा-बुझाकर बहुत सुख दिया। फिर श्री हरि ने अपने महल को गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5352.english_translation: Shiva says to Parvati: Knowing that Kaikeyi felt ashamed, the Lord first went to her house and comforted her greatly. Then Hari returned to his own home.
ramacharitamanas::5352.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / जानी (knowing) / कैकई (Kaikeyi) / लजानी (felt ashamed) / प्रथम (first) / तासु (her) / गृह (house) / गए (went) / भवानी (O Bhavani)॥ / ताहि (her) / प्रबोधि (having comforted/consoled) / बहुत (much) / सुख (happiness) / दीन्हा (gave) / पुनि (then) / निज (own) / भवन (home) / गवन (going) / हरि (Hari) / कीन्हा (did)॥
ramacharitamanas::5352.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::5352.essence: Compassion reaches the ashamed before it returns home.
ramacharitamanas::5352.simple_meaning: Ram noticed Kaikeyi’s shame, went to her first, comforted her, and only then returned home.
ramacharitamanas::5352.simple_insight: True grace notices hurt and responds before anyone asks.
ramacharitamanas::5352.detailed_meaning: After the long exile has begun to turn toward healing, Shiva tells Parvati that Ram did not rush only to his own home. He first went to Kaikeyi, who was now ashamed, and soothed her heart before returning.
ramacharitamanas::5352.modern_relevance: You can win an argument and still leave someone wounded. This verse remembers the deeper victory: noticing the other person’s shame and softening it first.
ramacharitamanas::5352.insight: It shifts you from self-focus to restorative action after conflict.

ramacharitamanas::5353.verse_sanskrit: कृपासिंधु जब मंदिर गए। पुर नर नारि सुखी सब भए॥ गुर बसिष्ट द्विज लिए बुलाई। आजु सुघरी सुदिन समुदाई।2॥
ramacharitamanas::5353.verse_hindi: कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी जब अपने महल को गए, तब नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष सब सुखी हुए। गुरु वशिष्ठजी ने ब्राह्मणों को बुला लिया और कहा आज शुभ घड़ी, सुंदर दिन आदि सभी शुभ योग हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5353.english_translation: When the ocean of compassion returned to the palace, all the men and women of the city became happy. Guru Vashistha called the Brahmins and said, "Today is an auspicious hour, a beautiful day, and all signs are favorable."
ramacharitamanas::5353.translation_literal: कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / जब (when) / मंदिर (palace) / गए (went) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सुखी (happy) / सब (all) / भए (became) / गुर (teacher) / बसिष्ट (Vashistha) / द्विज (Brahmins) / लिए (having) / बुलाई (called) / आजु (today) / सुघरी (auspicious) / सुदिन (good day) / समुदाई (all together)
ramacharitamanas::5353.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5353.essence: Ram's return restores ease before the coronation begins.
ramacharitamanas::5353.simple_meaning: Ram returns to the palace, and the whole city feels relieved. Vashistha then gathers the Brahmins and announces that the time is auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::5353.simple_insight: When the right presence returns, the whole atmosphere changes.
ramacharitamanas::5353.detailed_meaning: Ram has come back to the palace after the earlier welcome. The city feels settled again, and Vashistha prepares the Brahmins for the next sacred step of the coronation. This verse mainly sets the scene.
ramacharitamanas::5353.modern_relevance: The house goes quiet the moment the person everyone trusts walks back in. Even before they speak, the tension drops and everyone breathes easier.
ramacharitamanas::5353.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the peace that right order brings.

ramacharitamanas::5354.verse_sanskrit: सब द्विज देहु हरषि अनुसासन। रामचंद्र बैठहिं सिंघासन॥ मुनि बसिष्ट के बचन सुहाए। सुनत सकल बिप्रन्ह अति भाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5354.verse_hindi: आप सब ब्राह्मण हर्षित होकर आज्ञा दीजिए, जिसमें श्री रामचंद्रजी सिंहासन पर विराजमान हों। वशिष्ठ मुनि के सुहावने वचन सुनते ही सब ब्राह्मणों को बहुत ही अच्छे लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5354.english_translation: Let all the Brahmins joyfully give their approval, so that Ramchandra may sit on the throne. Hearing the pleasing words of sage Vashistha, all the Brahmins were greatly pleased.
ramacharitamanas::5354.translation_literal: सब (all) / द्विज (Brahmins) / देहु (give) / हरषि (joyfully) / अनुसासन (approval, instruction) / रामचंद्र (Ramchandra) / बैठहिं (may sit) / सिंघासन (throne)॥ / मुनि (sage) / बसिष्ट (Vashistha) / के (of) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (pleasing) / सुनत (hearing) / सकल (all) / बिप्रन्ह (Brahmins) / अति (very) / भाए (were pleased)॥
ramacharitamanas::5354.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::5354.essence: Ram's kingship is welcomed through joyful consent, not force.
ramacharitamanas::5354.simple_meaning: The Brahmins are asked to gladly approve Ram's enthronement, and Vashistha's words please them all.
ramacharitamanas::5354.simple_insight: Right action is easier when the right people openly bless it.
ramacharitamanas::5354.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the coronation is finally moving forward after the exile crisis. Vashistha gathers the Brahmins and asks them to consent joyfully so Ram can take the throne. Their approval turns grief into public support.
ramacharitamanas::5354.modern_relevance: A family finally agrees on a wedding after weeks of tension, and one calm elder's words settle everyone. Some moments need shared consent before joy can begin.
ramacharitamanas::5354.insight: It shifts the focus from private desire to rightful communal approval.

ramacharitamanas::5355.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं बचन मृदु बिप्र अनेका। जग अभिराम राम अभिषेका॥ अब मुनिबर बिलंब नहिं कीजै। महाराज कहँ तिलक करीजै ॥
ramacharitamanas::5355.verse_hindi: वे सब अनेकों ब्राह्मण कोमल वचन कहने लगे कि श्री रामजी का राज्याभिषेक संपूर्ण जगत को आनंद देने वाला है। हे मुनिश्रेष्ठ! अब विलंब न कीजिए और महाराज का तिलक शीघ्र कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5355.english_translation: Many brahmins spoke gently: "Ram's coronation will delight the whole world. O great sage, do not delay now. Quickly perform the tilak for the king."
ramacharitamanas::5355.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / बिप्र (brahmins) / अनेका (many) / जग (world) / अभिराम (delighting) / राम (Ram's) / अभिषेका (coronation) / अब (now) / मुनिबर (great sage) / बिलंब (delay) / नहिं (not) / कीजै (do) / महाराज (great king) / कहँ (for) / तिलक (tilak) / करीजै (be done)
ramacharitamanas::5355.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5355.essence: Joy should not be held back once the moment is ripe.
ramacharitamanas::5355.simple_meaning: The priests ask Vashishtha to stop delaying and begin Ram's coronation right away, saying it will bring joy to the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::5355.simple_insight: When the right moment arrives, hesitation only delays joy.
ramacharitamanas::5355.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the people and sages have gathered, the brahmins speak politely but urgently to Vashishtha. Ram is ready for coronation, and the whole city is waiting for the blessing of that moment.
ramacharitamanas::5355.modern_relevance: You have everyone assembled, the room is ready, and the only thing left is to begin. Sometimes the kindest move is simply not to stall the moment.
ramacharitamanas::5355.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as delay to ceremony as timely fulfilment.

ramacharitamanas::5356.verse_sanskrit: तब मुनि कहेउ सुमंत्र सन सुनत चलेउ हरषाइ। रथ अनेक बहु बाजि गज तुरत सँवारे जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5356.verse_hindi: तब मुनि ने सुमन्त्रजी से कहा, वे सुनते ही हर्षित होकर चले। उन्होंने तुरंत ही जाकर अनेकों रथ, घोड़े और हाथी सजाए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::5356.english_translation: Then the sage spoke to Sumantra. Hearing it, he went off rejoicing and quickly arranged many chariots, horses, and elephants.
ramacharitamanas::5356.translation_literal: तब (then) / मुनि (sage) / कहेउ (said) / सुमंत्र सन (to Sumantra) / सुनत (hearing) / चलेउ (went) / हरषाइ (rejoicing) / रथ (chariots) / अनेक (many) / बहु (many) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / तुरत (quickly) / सँवारे (arranged) / जाइ (going)
ramacharitamanas::5356.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5356.essence: Joyful obedience turns preparation into worship.
ramacharitamanas::5356.simple_meaning: Sumantra is told to act, and he immediately goes to prepare the royal vehicles and animals with joy.
ramacharitamanas::5356.simple_insight: Readiness becomes beautiful when service is done gladly.
ramacharitamanas::5356.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the coronation preparations are moving forward. Vashishtha gives an instruction to Sumantra, and Sumantra responds at once, arranging chariots, horses, and elephants. The verse is a quick scene of eager service, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::5356.modern_relevance: A message comes through while you're still tying your shoes, and you move without delay. Some tasks become sacred simply because you answer them fully.
ramacharitamanas::5356.insight: It shows prompt, joyful service in action rather than reflection.

ramacharitamanas::5357.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ धावन पठइ पुनि मंगल द्रब्य मगाइ। हरष समेत बसिष्ट पद पुनि सिरु नायउ आइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5357.verse_hindi: और जहाँ-तहाँ (सूचना देने वाले) दूतों को भेजकर मांगलिक वस्तुएँ मँगाकर फिर हर्ष के साथ आकर वशिष्ठजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5357.english_translation: He sent messengers in every direction, brought auspicious items, and then returned joyfully to bow his head at Vashishtha's feet.
ramacharitamanas::5357.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (here and there) / धावन (sending to run, messengers) / पठइ (having sent) / पुनि (again) / मंगल (auspicious) / द्रब्य (items, materials) / मगाइ (having fetched) / हरष (joy) / समेत (with) / बसिष्ट (Vashishtha) / पद (feet) / पुनि (again) / सिरु (head) / नायउ (bowed) / आइ (coming)
ramacharitamanas::5357.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5357.essence: Joy becomes rightful only after you bow to what is higher than ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::5357.simple_meaning: The preparations moved quickly and joyfully. Messengers were sent out, auspicious items were gathered, and respect was shown to Vashishtha before the ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::5357.simple_insight: Big moments begin with humility, not self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::5357.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the coronation preparations are now in motion. Messengers rush out, sacred items are gathered, and the court stays joyful. Before any celebration can begin, respect is first paid to Vashishtha, whose blessing anchors the whole event.
ramacharitamanas::5357.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, launch, or housewarming, someone is still running around for flowers, gifts, and the right arrangements. The real tone of the day is set by whether respect comes before excitement.
ramacharitamanas::5357.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the humility that makes celebration worthy.

ramacharitamanas::5358.verse_sanskrit: अवधपुरी अति रुचिर बनाई। देवन्ह सुमन बृष्टि झरि लाई॥ राम कहा सेवकन्ह बुलाई। प्रथम सखन्ह अन्हवावहु जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5358.verse_hindi: अवधपुरी बहुत ही सुंदर सजाई गई। देवताओं ने पुष्पों की वर्षा की झड़ी लगा दी। श्री रामचंद्रजी ने सेवकों को बुलाकर कहा कि तुम लोग जाकर पहले मेरे सखाओं को स्नान कराओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5358.english_translation: Ayodhya was made beautifully splendid. The deities showered a stream of flowers. Ram called the servants and said, "Go first and bathe my friends."
ramacharitamanas::5358.translation_literal: अवधपुरी (Ayodhya city) / अति (very) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बनाई (made) / देवन्ह (by the radiant beings) / सुमन (flowers) / बृष्टि (shower) / झरि (pouring) / लाई (brought) / राम (Ram) / कहा (said) / सेवकन्ह (to the servants) / बुलाई (having called) / प्रथम (first) / सखन्ह (the friends) / अन्हवावहु (bathe) / जाई (go)
ramacharitamanas::5358.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5358.essence: Honor others first, even when everyone is honoring you.
ramacharitamanas::5358.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is beautifully decorated, flowers fall from the sky, and Ram tells his servants to bathe his friends first.
ramacharitamanas::5358.simple_insight: Love shows itself in small acts of priority, not just grand words.
ramacharitamanas::5358.detailed_meaning: After the return to Ayodhya, the city is glowing with celebration. Ram, now home and honored, does not think of himself first. He asks that his friends be bathed before him, showing the humility and care that define his reign.
ramacharitamanas::5358.modern_relevance: At a wedding, everyone waits for the guest of honor, but you quietly make sure your friend who traveled far gets water first. That small choice reveals the kind of heart Ram has.
ramacharitamanas::5358.insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that true leadership begins by honoring others.

ramacharitamanas::5359.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बचन जहँ तहँ जन धाए। सुग्रीवादि तुरत अन्हवाए॥ पुनि करुनानिधि भरतु हँकारे। निज कर राम जटा निरुआरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5359.verse_hindi: भगवान् के वचन सुनते ही सेवक जहाँ-तहाँ दौड़े और तुरंत ही उन्होंने सुग्रीवादि को स्नान कराया। फिर करुणानिधान श्री रामजी ने भरतजी को बुलाया और उनकी जटाओं को अपने हाथों से सुलझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::5359.english_translation: Hearing the command, the servants ran everywhere and quickly bathed Sugriva and the others. Then the ocean of compassion, Ram, called Bharat and untangled his matted hair with his own hands.
ramacharitamanas::5359.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words, command) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / जन (servants, people) / धाए (ran) / सुग्रीव-आदि (Sugriva and others) / तुरत (immediately) / अन्हवाए (were bathed)॥ / पुनि (then) / करुनानिधि (ocean of compassion) / भरतु (Bharat) / हँकारे (called) / निज (his own) / कर (hand) / राम (Ram) / जटा (matted hair) / निरुआरे (untangled, smoothed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5359.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5359.essence: True love notices hardship and responds with care.
ramacharitamanas::5359.simple_meaning: Ram’s command is carried out at once. Sugriva and the others are bathed, and Ram lovingly untangles Bharat’s matted hair with his own hands.
ramacharitamanas::5359.simple_insight: Love is shown in the smallest acts of care, not just grand words.
ramacharitamanas::5359.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s restored joy, Ram’s word sends everyone into motion. The companions are bathed at once, and Bharat — who has lived in austerity for Ram’s sake — is met with Ram’s own hands, gently undoing the marks of his hardship.
ramacharitamanas::5359.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you love after a long, hard season, and the first thing you do is help them clean up, sit down, and breathe.
ramacharitamanas::5359.insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony to direct, tender service.

ramacharitamanas::5360.verse_sanskrit: अन्हवाए प्रभु तीनिउ भाई। भगत बछल कृपाल रघुराई॥ भरत भाग्य प्रभु कोमलताई। सेष कोटि सत सकहिं न गाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5360.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर भक्त वत्सल कृपालु प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी ने तीनों भाइयों को स्नान कराया। भरतजी का भाग्य और प्रभु की कोमलता का वर्णन अरबों शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::5360.english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord, devoted to his devotees, bathed all three brothers. No one, not even countless Sheshas, can fully describe Bharat's fortune or the Lord's tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::5360.translation_literal: अन्हवाए (bathed) / प्रभु (the Lord) / तीनिउ (all three) / भाई (brothers) / भगत (devotees) / बछल (fond of) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुराई (Lord of Raghu) ॥ भरत (Bharat) / भाग्य (fortune) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कोमलताई (tenderness) / सेष (Shesha) / कोटि (crores) / सत (hundreds) / सकहिं (can) / न (not) / गाई (sing, describe) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5360.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5360.essence: True greatness shows itself as tender care for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::5360.simple_meaning: Ram lovingly bathes all three brothers, and the verse says Bharat's good fortune and Ram's tenderness are beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::5360.simple_insight: You are held by a love so complete that words run out before it does.
ramacharitamanas::5360.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's restored joy, Ram personally bathes Bharat, Lakshman, and Shatrughna. The scene pauses to honour Bharat's rare fortune and Ram's gentle affection, making this a moment of intimate devotion, not just royal ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::5360.modern_relevance: You wash off a long, exhausting day and someone you love quietly brings you water, towel, and care without being asked. That small tenderness can feel larger than praise.
ramacharitamanas::5360.insight: It shifts attention from status to being cherished, and from grandeur to intimate care.

ramacharitamanas::5361.verse_sanskrit: पुनि निज जटा राम बिबराए। गुर अनुसासन मागि नहाए॥ करि मज्जन प्रभु भूषन साजे। अंग अनंग देखि सत लाजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5361.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामजी ने अपनी जटाएँ खोलीं और गुरुजी की आज्ञा माँगकर स्नान किया। स्नान करके प्रभु ने आभूषण धारण किए। उनके (सुशोभित) अंगों को देखकर सैकड़ों (असंख्य) कामदेव लजा गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5361.english_translation: Then Ram opened his own matted locks and, seeking the guru's permission, bathed. After bathing, the Lord adorned himself with ornaments. Seeing his radiant limbs, even countless gods of desire felt ashamed.
ramacharitamanas::5361.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / निज (own) / जटा (matted locks) / राम (Ram) / बिबराए (opened) / गुर (guru) / अनुसासन (permission/instruction) / मागि (having asked) / नहाए (bathed) / करि (having done) / मज्जन (bath) / प्रभु (Lord) / भूषन (ornaments) / साजे (adorned) / अंग (limbs) / अनंग (god of desire) / देखि (seeing) / सत (hundreds) / लाजे (felt ashamed)
ramacharitamanas::5361.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5361.essence: Grace becomes complete when power bows to guidance.
ramacharitamanas::5361.simple_meaning: Ram first asks his teacher's permission, then bathes and dresses himself beautifully. His radiance is so great that even countless gods of desire are humbled.
ramacharitamanas::5361.simple_insight: True dignity can be so complete that beauty itself feels small beside it.
ramacharitamanas::5361.detailed_meaning: After the coronation preparations begin in Ayodhya, Ram sets aside his matted locks, asks his guru for permission, bathes, and adorns himself. The scene is about royal grace and sacred order, not instruction, so it serves the flow rather than standing alone.
ramacharitamanas::5361.modern_relevance: You finally get dressed for a long-awaited ceremony, but you still pause to check with the elder who taught you how to carry yourself. Real polish begins with humility.
ramacharitamanas::5361.insight: It shifts attention from outward beauty to the discipline and reverence that make beauty worthy.

ramacharitamanas::5362.verse_sanskrit: सासुन्ह सादर जानकिहि मज्जन तुरत कराइ। दिब्य बसन बर भूषन अँग अँग सजे बनाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5362.verse_hindi: (इधर) सासुओं ने जानकीजी को आदर के साथ तुरंत ही स्नान कराके उनके अंग-अंग में दिव्य वस्त्र और श्रेष्ठ आभूषण भली-भाँति सजा दिए (पहना दिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5362.english_translation: The mothers respectfully bathed Janaki at once and adorned her body with divine clothes and fine ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::5362.translation_literal: सासुन्ह (the mothers-in-law) / सादर (with respect) / जानकिहि (Janaki) / मज्जन (bath) / तुरत (at once) / कराइ (caused to be done) / दिब्य (divine) / बसन (clothes) / बर (excellent) / भूषन (ornaments) / अँग अँग (every limb) / सजे (adorned) / बनाइ (well, properly)
ramacharitamanas::5362.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5362.essence: Love can be shown through the way you prepare someone to be honoured.
ramacharitamanas::5362.simple_meaning: The household women quickly bathe Sita and dress her beautifully in fine clothes and ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::5362.simple_insight: Care becomes sacred when it is given with respect and tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::5362.detailed_meaning: In Ram's restored household, the mothers-in-law lovingly prepare Janaki for her new place beside him. This is not a teaching verse but a tender domestic detail, showing honour, delight, and the fullness of her welcome.
ramacharitamanas::5362.modern_relevance: A family gets ready for a wedding, and everyone moves around one person with quiet care. That kind of respectful attention can make someone feel truly received.
ramacharitamanas::5362.insight: It shifts attention to the dignity hidden inside ordinary acts of care.

ramacharitamanas::5363.verse_sanskrit: राम बाम दिसि सोभति रमा रूप गुन खानि। देखि मातु सब हरषीं जन्म सुफल निज जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::5363.verse_hindi: श्री राम के बायीं ओर रूप और गुणों की खान रमा (श्री जानकीजी) शोभित हो रही हैं। उन्हें देखकर सब माताएँ अपना जन्म (जीवन) सफल समझकर हर्षित हुईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5363.english_translation: Ram shines on the left, and Rama, the mine of beauty and virtues, shines on his left. Seeing them, all the mothers felt their lives had become fruitful and rejoiced.
ramacharitamanas::5363.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बाम दिसि (left side) / सोभति (shines) / रमा रूप गुन खानि (Rama, mine of beauty and virtues) / देखि (seeing) / मातु सब (all the mothers) / हरषीं (rejoiced) / जन्म (birth/life) / सुफल (fruitful) / निज (their own) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::5363.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5363.essence: True beauty makes even the watcher feel fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::5363.simple_meaning: Ram stands beside Sita in shining beauty, and the mothers watching them feel their lives have been fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::5363.simple_insight: Some sights make the heart feel that life has already been rewarded.
ramacharitamanas::5363.detailed_meaning: After the wedding, Ram and Sita are beautifully adorned and brought together. The mothers look at the couple and feel overwhelming joy, as if merely witnessing this union has made their lives complete.
ramacharitamanas::5363.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of two people deeply right for each other, and something in you relaxes. Beauty, love, and rightness can make the heart feel its work is done.
ramacharitamanas::5363.insight: It shifts attention from possession to blessed witnessing: seeing wholeness can itself be enough.

ramacharitamanas::5364.verse_sanskrit: सुनु खगेस तेहि अवसर ब्रह्मा सिव मुनि बृंद। चढ़ि बिमान आए सब सुर देखन सुखकंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::5364.verse_hindi: (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) हे पक्षीराज गरुड़जी! सुनिए, उस समय ब्रह्माजी, शिवजी और मुनियों के समूह तथा विमानों पर चढ़कर सब देवता आनंदकंद भगवान् के दर्शन करने के लिए आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5364.english_translation: Listen, lord of birds: at that time Brahma, Shiva, and groups of sages, along with all the radiant beings riding in celestial vehicles, came to see the source of joy.
ramacharitamanas::5364.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / खगेस (lord of birds) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (time) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / सिव (Shiva) / मुनि (sages) / बृंद (groups) / चढ़ि (mounted) / बिमान (celestial vehicles) / आए (came) / सब (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / देखन (to see) / सुखकंद (source of joy)
ramacharitamanas::5364.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::5364.essence: Even the highest beings come simply to behold Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5364.simple_meaning: At that moment, Brahma, Shiva, sages, and other radiant beings came in celestial vehicles to see Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5364.simple_insight: Greatness draws even the highest beings toward humble presence.
ramacharitamanas::5364.detailed_meaning: Kak Bhushundi is telling Garuda about Ram's reign in Ayodhya. When Ram is seated in glory, even Brahma, Shiva, sages, and the radiant beings arrive to behold him. The verse sets up the awe of the next scene.
ramacharitamanas::5364.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone truly admirable walks in. No announcement is needed; people simply turn, because presence itself has weight.
ramacharitamanas::5364.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverence: true greatness is recognized, not performed.

ramacharitamanas::5365.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु बिलोकि मुनि मन अनुरागा। तुरत दिब्य सिंघासन मागा॥ रबि सम तेज सो बरनि न जाई। बैठे राम द्विजन्ह सिरु नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::5365.verse_hindi: प्रभु को देखकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी के मन में प्रेम भर आया। उन्होंने तुरंत ही दिव्य सिंहासन मँगवाया, जिसका तेज सूर्य के समान था। उसका सौंदर्य वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। ब्राह्मणों को सिर नवाकर श्री रामचंद्रजी उस पर विराज गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5365.english_translation: Seeing the Lord, Vashishtha’s heart filled with love. He quickly asked for a divine throne, bright as the sun. Its brilliance could not be described. Bowing to the priests, Ram sat upon it.
ramacharitamanas::5365.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / अनुरागा (filled with love) / तुरत (at once) / दिब्य (divine) / सिंघासन (throne) / मागा (asked for) / रबि (sun) / सम (like) / तेज (radiance) / सो (that) / बरनि (described) / जाई (can be) / बैठे (sat) / राम (Ram) / द्विजन्ह (to the priests) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::5365.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5365.essence: Real love for Ram naturally becomes reverent action.
ramacharitamanas::5365.simple_meaning: Vashishtha sees Ram, feels deep love, and arranges a radiant divine throne for him. Ram bows to the priests and sits down.
ramacharitamanas::5365.simple_insight: Honor becomes natural when the heart truly recognises greatness.
