ramacharitamanas::5365.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s homecoming celebration, Vashishtha sees Ram and is moved with love. He immediately has a radiant throne prepared, and Ram, before sitting, bows to the priests. The scene shows reverence turning into action.
ramacharitamanas::5365.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall, everyone is waiting for the guest of honour. The host sees the person arrive, forgets the protocol, and moves with genuine reverence. Respect is no longer performance; it becomes instinct.
ramacharitamanas::5365.insight: It turns admiration into respectful action, showing that true honour is expressed, not just felt.

ramacharitamanas::5366.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुता समेत रघुराई। पेखि प्रहरषे मुनि समुदाई॥ बेद मंत्र तब द्विजन्ह उचारे। नभ सुर मुनि जय जयति पुकारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5366.verse_hindi: श्री जानकीजी के सहित रघुनाथजी को देखकर मुनियों का समुदाय अत्यंत ही हर्षित हुआ। तब ब्राह्मणों ने वेदमंत्रों का उच्चारण किया। आकाश में देवता और मुनि 'जय, हो, जय हो' ऐसी पुकार करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5366.english_translation: Seeing Ram together with Sita, the gathered sages felt great joy. Then the learned priests chanted Vedic mantras, and in the sky the devas and sages cried, “Victory, victory!”
ramacharitamanas::5366.translation_literal: जनकसुता (Janak's daughter, Sita) / समेत (together with) / रघुराई (Ram) / पेखि (seeing) / प्रहरषे (rejoiced greatly) / मुनि (sages) / समुदाई (gathered group) ॥ / बेद (Vedic) / मंत्र (mantras) / तब (then) / द्विजन्ह (the priests) / उचारे (uttered, chanted) / नभ (sky) / सुर (devas) / मुनि (sages) / जय (victory) / जयति (victory) / पुकारे (called out) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5366.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5366.essence: Joy becomes public when Ram and Sita appear together.
ramacharitamanas::5366.simple_meaning: The sages rejoice at seeing Ram and Sita together. The priests chant sacred mantras, and the heavenly beings join in cries of victory.
ramacharitamanas::5366.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of blessing that even the sky seems to celebrate them.
ramacharitamanas::5366.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita have arrived before the assembled sages in the royal setting of Uttarkand. The sight fills everyone with joy, and the priests begin ritual chanting while celestial beings and sages echo the celebration. It is a scene of welcome, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::5366.modern_relevance: A bride and groom walk into a room and everyone goes quiet for a second, then smiles. The moment itself carries the happiness; no explanation is needed.
ramacharitamanas::5366.insight: It shifts attention from analysis to shared celebration and reverence for a blessed arrival.

ramacharitamanas::5367.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम तिलक बसिष्ट मुनि कीन्हा। पुनि सब बिप्रन्ह आयसु दीन्हा॥ सुत बिलोकि हरषीं महतारी। बार बार आरती उतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5367.verse_hindi: (सबसे) पहले मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने तिलक किया। फिर उन्होंने सब ब्राह्मणों को (तिलक करने की) आज्ञा दी। पुत्र को राजसिंहासन पर देखकर माताएँ हर्षित हुईं और उन्होंने बार-बार आरती उतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::5367.english_translation: First, Vashishtha the sage performed the tilak. Then he gave all the priests the order. Seeing their son on the royal seat, the mothers were overjoyed and kept waving the aarti again and again.
ramacharitamanas::5367.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / तिलक (ceremonial mark) / बसिष्ट मुनि (sage Vashishtha) / कीन्हा (did) / पुनि (then) / सब (all) / बिप्रन्ह (to the priests) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / सुत (son) / बिलोकि (seeing) / हरषीं (became joyful) / महतारी (mothers) / बार बार (again and again) / आरती (waving of lamps) / उतारी (performed)
ramacharitamanas::5367.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5367.essence: Love celebrates most when blessing becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::5367.simple_meaning: Vashishtha marks Ram for kingship, then the priests follow. The mothers see their son on the throne and celebrate with repeated aarti.
ramacharitamanas::5367.simple_insight: Joy deepens when a long-awaited honor finally becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::5367.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s coronation scene, Vashishtha begins Ram’s royal consecration and the priests follow his lead. As the mothers watch their son seated as king, their relief and pride overflow into repeated aarti.
ramacharitamanas::5367.modern_relevance: You watch your child walk across the stage in a borrowed gown, and suddenly years of care feel visible at once. Pride, relief, and blessing spill out together.
ramacharitamanas::5367.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the tenderness of being recognized after long waiting.

ramacharitamanas::5368.verse_sanskrit: बिप्रन्ह दान बिबिधि बिधि दीन्हे। जाचक सकल अजाचक कीन्हे॥ सिंघासन पर त्रिभुअन साईं। देखि सुरन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5368.verse_hindi: उन्होंने ब्राह्मणों को अनेकों प्रकार के दान दिए और संपूर्ण याचकों को अयाचक बना दिया (मालामाल कर दिया)। त्रिभुवन के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी को (अयोध्या के) सिंहासन पर (विराजित) देखकर देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::5368.english_translation: He gave many kinds of gifts to the Brahmins and made all beggars into non-beggars. Seeing the Lord of the three worlds seated on the throne, the devas beat their drums.
ramacharitamanas::5368.translation_literal: बिप्रन्ह (to the Brahmins) / दान (gifts) / बिबिधि बिधि (in various ways) / दीन्हे (gave) / जाचक (beggars) / सकल (all) / अजाचक (non-beggars) / कीन्हे (made) / सिंघासन (throne) / पर (on) / त्रिभुअन साईं (Lord of the three worlds) / देखि (seeing) / सुरन्ह (the devas) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजाईं (beat)
ramacharitamanas::5368.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5368.essence: Power becomes rightful when it leaves no one in need.
ramacharitamanas::5368.simple_meaning: Ram gives generously to the priests, leaving no one in need. When the gods see him seated on the throne, they celebrate with drums.
ramacharitamanas::5368.simple_insight: True honor includes generosity; joy deepens when power is joined with giving.
ramacharitamanas::5368.detailed_meaning: Ram has just been crowned in Ayodhya. The court is full of blessing, gifts, and ritual honor. Tulsidas shows the new reign as both generous and cosmic: Ram gives freely, and even the devas rejoice at his enthronement.
ramacharitamanas::5368.modern_relevance: After a promotion, you sign the bonus letters, thank the team, and quietly make sure no one is left behind. Real leadership lifts others as it rises.
ramacharitamanas::5368.insight: It links rightful rule with generosity, showing that authority becomes complete only when it serves others.

ramacharitamanas::5369.verse_sanskrit: नभ दुंदुभीं बाजहिं बिपुल गंधर्ब किंनर गावहीं। नाचहिं अपछरा बृंद परमानंद सुर मुनि पावहीं॥ भरतादि अनुज बिभीषनांगद हनुमदादि समेत ते। गहें छत्र चामर ब्यजन धनु असिचर्म सक्ति बिराजते ॥
ramacharitamanas::5369.verse_hindi: आकाश में बहुत से नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। गन्धर्व और किन्नर गा रहे हैं। अप्सराओं के झुंड के झुंड नाच रहे हैं। देवता और मुनि परमानंद प्राप्त कर रहे हैं। भरत, लक्ष्मण और शत्रुघ्नजी, विभीषण, अंगद, हनुमान् और सुग्रीव आदि सहित क्रमशः छत्र, चँवर, पंखा, धनुष, तलवार, ढाल और शक्ति लिए हुए सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5369.english_translation: In the sky, many drums sound. Gandharvas and Kinnaras sing. Crowds of Apsaras dance. Devas and sages are filled with supreme joy. Bharata, Lakshmana, Shatrughna, Vibhishana, Angada, Hanuman, and Sugriva stand adorned with umbrella, fly-whisk, fan, bow, sword, shield, and spear.
ramacharitamanas::5369.translation_literal: नभ (sky) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बाजहिं (sound) / बिपुल (many) / गंधर्ब (Gandharvas) / किंनर (Kinnaras) / गावहीं (sing) / नाचहिं (dance) / अपछरा बृंद (crowds of Apsaras) / परमानंद (supreme joy) / सुर (devas) / मुनि (sages) / पावहीं (obtain) / भरतादि (Bharata and others) / अनुज (younger brothers) / बिभीषनांगद (Vibhishana and Angada) / हनुमदादि (Hanuman and others) / समेत (together with) / ते (they) / गहें (holding) / छत्र (umbrella) / चामर (fly-whisk) / ब्यजन (fan) / धनु (bow) / असिचर्म (sword and shield) / सक्ति (spear) / बिराजते (shine)
ramacharitamanas::5369.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5369.essence: Ram's coronation becomes a celebration shared by heaven, family, and loyal service.
ramacharitamanas::5369.simple_meaning: The coronation fills the heavens with music and joy. Celestial beings celebrate while Ram's brothers, allies, and warriors stand in royal service around him.
ramacharitamanas::5369.simple_insight: True victory feels shared, not solitary.
ramacharitamanas::5369.detailed_meaning: Ram has been crowned in Ayodhya. As Vashishtha completes the ritual and the city rejoices, the celebration spills beyond earth itself. Celestial beings sing, dance, and bless the scene while Ram's brothers and allies stand around him in honor and service.
ramacharitamanas::5369.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet after the promotion is announced, and the people who helped you get there are smiling harder than you are. Real success never arrives alone.
ramacharitamanas::5369.insight: It shifts attention from personal triumph to the web of support, loyalty, and service that made the triumph possible.

ramacharitamanas::5370.verse_sanskrit: श्री सहित दिनकर बंस भूषन काम बहु छबि सोहई। नव अंबुधर बर गात अंबर पीत सुर मन मोहई॥ मुकुटांगदादि बिचित्र भूषन अंग अंगन्हि प्रति सजे। अंभोज नयन बिसाल उर भुज धन्य नर निरखंति जे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5370.verse_hindi: श्री सीताजी सहित सूर्यवंश के विभूषण श्री रामजी के शरीर में अनेकों कामदेवों की छबि शोभा दे रही है। नवीन जलयुक्त मेघों के समान सुंदर श्याम शरीर पर पीताम्बर देवताओं के मन को भी मोहित कर रहा है। मुकुट, बाजूबंद आदि विचित्र आभूषण अंग-अंग में सजे हुए हैं। कमल के समान नेत्र हैं, चौड़ी छाती है और लंबी भुजाएँ हैं जो उनके दर्शन करते हैं, वे मनुष्य धन्य हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5370.english_translation: With Sita beside him, the jewel of the solar dynasty shines with countless forms of beauty. His dark body, like a fresh raincloud, and his yellow garment delight even the minds of the radiant beings. Crown, armlets, and other ornaments adorn every limb. Blessed are the people who behold his wide lotus eyes, broad chest, and long arms.
ramacharitamanas::5370.translation_literal: श्री सहित (with Sita and prosperity) / दिनकर बंस भूषन (ornament of the solar dynasty) / काम (many cupids/beauties) / बहु (many) / छबि (beauty) / सोहई (shines) / नव (new) / अंबुधर (rainclouds) / बर (excellent) / गात (body) / अंबर (garment) / पीत (yellow) / सुर (radiant beings) / मन (mind) / मोहई (delights) / मुकुटांगदादि (crown, armlets, and others) / बिचित्र (varied) / भूषन (ornaments) / अंग (limbs) / अंगन्हि प्रति (on each limb) / सजे (adorned) / अंभोज (lotus) / नयन (eyes) / बिसाल (wide) / उर (chest) / भुज (arms) / धन्य (blessed) / नर (people) / निरखंति (behold) / जे (who)
ramacharitamanas::5370.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5370.essence: Ram's beauty blesses anyone who truly sees him.
ramacharitamanas::5370.simple_meaning: Ram appears supremely beautiful beside Sita, with dark cloud-like skin, yellow garments, ornaments, lotus eyes, broad chest, and long arms. Anyone who sees him is blessed.
ramacharitamanas::5370.simple_insight: Beauty becomes a blessing when it draws the mind toward reverence.
ramacharitamanas::5370.detailed_meaning: In Ram's reign, the heavens celebrate his coronation. This verse lingers on his form beside Sita: his dark body, yellow cloth, jeweled ornaments, and lotus eyes. The point is not decoration alone, but the joy his presence gives to all who behold him.
ramacharitamanas::5370.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking into a room, and the whole atmosphere changes. Some presences don't just attract attention — they steady the mind and make everyone feel fortunate to be there.
ramacharitamanas::5370.insight: It shifts attention from external beauty as vanity to beauty as a sign of grace and blessing.

ramacharitamanas::5371.verse_sanskrit: वह सोभा समाज सुख कहत न बनइ खगेस। बरनहिं सारद सेष श्रुति सो रस जान महेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::5371.verse_hindi: हे पक्षीराज गरुड़जी ! वह शोभा, वह समाज और वह सुख मुझसे कहते नहीं बनता। सरस्वतीजी, शेषजी और वेद निरंतर उसका वर्णन करते हैं, और उसका रस (आनंद) महादेवजी ही जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5371.english_translation: O king of birds, Garuda, that splendour, that assembly, and that joy cannot be spoken of. Saraswati, Shesha, and the Vedas keep describing it, and only Mahadeva knows its taste.
ramacharitamanas::5371.translation_literal: वह (that) / सोभा (splendour) / समाज (assembly) / सुख (joy) / कहत (speaking) / न (not) / बनइ (is possible) / खगेस (O king of birds) / बरनहिं (describe) / सारद (Saraswati) / सेष (Shesha) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / सो (that) / रस (taste, essence) / जान (know) / महेस (Mahadeva)
ramacharitamanas::5371.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::5371.essence: Ram's glory is spoken of endlessly, but only devotion truly tastes it.
ramacharitamanas::5371.simple_meaning: Ram's glory, gathering, and joy are beyond words. Even great powers can only describe them; only Shiva truly knows their sweetness.
ramacharitamanas::5371.simple_insight: Some realities are not grasped by explanation. They are entered through devotion.
ramacharitamanas::5371.detailed_meaning: In Ram's reign, the heavens overflow with celebration. Kak Bhushundi turns to Garuda and says the beauty of Ram's court cannot be fully spoken. Even Saraswati, Shesha, and the Vedas can only circle around it; only Mahadeva knows its inner taste.
ramacharitamanas::5371.modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed you — a wedding, a sunrise, a prayer answered in silence — and words keep failing. The experience was never meant to be reduced to explanation.
ramacharitamanas::5371.insight: It shifts the mind from describing sacred experience to recognizing that direct love is the real access.

ramacharitamanas::5372.verse_sanskrit: भिन्न भिन्न अस्तुति करि गए सुर निज निज धाम। बंदी बेष बेद तब आए जहँ श्रीराम ॥
ramacharitamanas::5372.verse_hindi: सब देवता अलग-अलग स्तुति करके अपने-अपने लोक को चले गए। तब भाटों का रूप धारण करके चारों वेद वहाँ आए जहाँ श्री रामजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5372.english_translation: The radiant beings offered their separate praises and returned to their own realms. Then the Vedas came there in the guise of bards, where Shri Ram was.
ramacharitamanas::5372.translation_literal: भिन्न-भिन्न (separate) / अस्तुति (praise) / करि (having done) / गए (went) / सुर (radiant beings) / निज-निज (their own) / धाम (abode) / बंदी-बेष (in bard-form) / बेद (Vedas) / तब (then) / आए (came) / जहँ (where) / श्रीराम (Shri Ram)
ramacharitamanas::5372.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5372.essence: Even the Vedas come as humble praise before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::5372.simple_meaning: The radiant beings praised Ram in their own ways and returned to their realms. Then the Vedas arrived in the form of bards to praise him too.
ramacharitamanas::5372.simple_insight: Even the highest praise feels incomplete before Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::5372.detailed_meaning: In Ram's shining court, the radiant beings finish their separate praises and depart. The scene does not end there: the Vedas themselves arrive in bard-like form, showing that even sacred speech comes to honor Ram directly.
ramacharitamanas::5372.modern_relevance: A room full of experts has finished speaking, and the silence that follows makes room for the one truth everyone was circling. Praise gives way to presence.
ramacharitamanas::5372.insight: It shifts attention from many voices of praise to the one reality they all point toward.

ramacharitamanas::5373.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु सर्बग्य कीन्ह अति आदर कृपानिधान। लखेउ न काहूँ मरम कछु लगे करन गुन गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::5373.verse_hindi: कृपानिधान सर्वज्ञ प्रभु ने (उन्हें पहचानकर) उनका बहुत ही आदर किया। इसका भेद किसी ने कुछ भी नहीं जाना। वेद गुणगान करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5373.english_translation: The all-knowing Lord showed them great honor, but no one understood the hidden meaning. Then the Vedas began singing his praise.
ramacharitamanas::5373.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / कीन्ह (did) / अति (greatly) / आदर (honor) / कृपानिधान (storehouse of grace) / लखेउ (was understood) / न (not) / काहूँ (by anyone) / मरम (hidden meaning) / कछु (any) / लगे (began) / करन (to do) / गुन (praise) / गान (singing)
ramacharitamanas::5373.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::5373.essence: The deepest honor is given where ordinary eyes cannot grasp the meaning.
ramacharitamanas::5373.simple_meaning: Ram honored the Vedas, though no one understood the full hidden meaning of what was happening. Then the Vedas began praising him.
ramacharitamanas::5373.simple_insight: There is comfort in not needing everyone to understand what is sacred.
ramacharitamanas::5373.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand, the Vedas arrive before Ram in disguise and are received with deep honor. Ram knows their true identity, yet the full inner meaning of the moment remains hidden from others. That mystery itself becomes praise.
ramacharitamanas::5373.modern_relevance: You do something quietly meaningful, and people around you only notice the surface. The deepest part of what happened never needs a crowd to validate it.
ramacharitamanas::5373.insight: It shifts attention from public recognition to the sacred depth already present in the act.

ramacharitamanas::5374.verse_sanskrit: जय सगुन निर्गुन रूप रूप अनूप भूप सिरोमने। दसकंधरादि प्रचंड निसिचर प्रबल खल भुज बल हने॥ अवतार नर संसार भार बिभंजि दारुन दुख दहे। जय प्रनतपाल दयाल प्रभु संजुक्त सक्ति नमामहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5374.verse_hindi: सगुण और निर्गुण रूप! हे अनुपम रूप-लावण्ययुक्त! हे राजाओं के शिरोमणि! आपकी जय हो। आपने रावण आदि प्रचण्ड, प्रबल और दुष्ट निशाचरों को अपनी भुजाओं के बल से मार डाला। आपने मनुष्य अवतार लेकर संसार के भार को नष्ट करके अत्यंत कठोर दुःखों को भस्म कर दिया। हे दयालु! हे शरणागत की रक्षा करने वाले प्रभो! आपकी जय हो। मैं शक्ति (सीताजी) सहित शक्तिमान् आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::5374.english_translation: Victory to you, the beautiful Lord of both the manifest and unmanifest forms, king among kings. You struck down Ravana and other fierce, powerful evil beings with your own arms. Taking human form, you removed the burden of the world and burned away terrible suffering. Victory to the compassionate Lord who protects the surrendered; I bow to you, the powerful one united with Shakti.
ramacharitamanas::5374.translation_literal: जय (victory) / सगुन (with form) / निर्गुन (without form) / रूप (form) / रूप (form) / अनूप (matchless) / भूप (king) / सिरोमने (crest-jewel) / दसकंधरादि (Ravana and others) / प्रचंड (fierce) / निसिचर (night-dwellers) / प्रबल (powerful) / खल (wicked) / भुज बल (arm-strength) / हने (struck down) / अवतार (incarnation) / नर (human) / संसार भार (burden of the world) / बिभंजि (breaking) / दारुन दुख (terrible suffering) / दहे (burned) / जय (victory) / प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / दयाल (compassionate) / प्रभु (Lord) / संजुक्त (joined with) / सक्ति (Shakti) / नमामहे (I bow)
ramacharitamanas::5374.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::5374.essence: The supreme Lord is both transcendent and personally protective.
ramacharitamanas::5374.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the supreme Lord who is both with form and beyond form. He defeats evil, removes the world's burden, and protects those who take refuge in him.
ramacharitamanas::5374.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing the highest power is also tender toward those who turn inward and ask for help.
ramacharitamanas::5374.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand, the sages and Vedas are praising Ram after his glory is revealed. This verse gathers his divine greatness into one hymn: he is beyond form yet appears in form, destroys Ravana, and protects those who surrender.
ramacharitamanas::5374.modern_relevance: When life feels like too much—family pressure, grief, deadlines, and one more crisis—this verse reminds you that strength is not only force. Real power also knows how to protect, reduce burden, and make room for peace.
ramacharitamanas::5374.insight: It shifts devotion from awe alone to refuge: the highest power is also the one who carries your burden.

ramacharitamanas::5375.verse_sanskrit: तव बिषम माया बस सुरासुर नाग नर अग जग हरे। भव पंथ भ्रमत अमित दिवस निसि काल कर्म गुननि भरे॥ जे नाथ करि करुना बिलोकि त्रिबिधि दुख ते निर्बहे। भव खेद छेदन दच्छ हम कहुँ रच्छ राम नमामहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::5375.verse_hindi: हे हरे! आपकी दुस्तर माया के वशीभूत होने के कारण देवता, राक्षस, नाग, मनुष्य और चर, अचर सभी काल कर्म और गुणों से भरे हुए (उनके वशीभूत हुए) दिन-रात अनन्त भव (आवागमन) के मार्ग में भटक रहे हैं। हे नाथ! इनमें से जिनको आपने कृपा करके (कृपादृष्टि) से देख लिया, वे (माया जनित) तीनों प्रकार के दुःखों से छूट गए। हे जन्म-मरण के श्रम को काटने में कुशल श्री रामजी! हमारी रक्षा कीजिए। हम आपको नमस्कार करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::5375.english_translation: O Hari, under the grip of your hard-to-cross illusion, devas, asuras, serpents, humans, and all moving and unmoving beings wander day and night through the endless path of becoming, weighed down by time, action, and the qualities of nature. O Lord, those whom you look upon with compassion are freed from the three kinds of suffering. O Ram, skilled at cutting the weariness of becoming, we bow to you and seek your protection.
ramacharitamanas::5375.translation_literal: तव (your) / बिषम (hard, difficult) / माया (illusion) / बस (under the control of) / सुरासुर (devas and asuras) / नाग (serpents) / नर (humans) / अग (moving) / जग (unmoving, all creation) / हरे (O Hari) / भव (becoming, worldly existence) / पंथ (path) / भ्रमत (wandering) / अमित (countless) / दिवस (days) / निसि (nights) / काल (time) / कर्म (action) / गुननि (qualities) / भरे (filled) ॥ / जे (those who) / नाथ (Lord) / करि (having done) / करुना (compassion) / बिलोकि (looked upon) / त्रिबिधि (threefold) / दुख (suffering) / ते (from that) / निर्बहे (were freed) ॥ / भव (of becoming) / खेद (weariness) / छेदन (cutting) / दच्छ (skilled) / हम (we) / कहुँ (for) / रच्छ (protect) / राम (Ram) / नमामहे (we bow) ॥
ramacharitamanas::5375.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::5375.essence: Compassion, not struggle, ends the endless wandering.
ramacharitamanas::5375.simple_meaning: The world is trapped in confusion and repeated struggle, but Ram's compassionate glance frees beings from suffering and the weariness of endless becoming.
ramacharitamanas::5375.simple_insight: You are not trapped by the struggle itself; grace can interrupt what feels endless.
ramacharitamanas::5375.detailed_meaning: In Uttarkand's devotional dialogue, Tulsidas turns from praise of Ram's form to Ram's saving power. He says every kind of being is caught in illusion and suffering, but Ram's compassionate glance can free them and protect them from the exhaustion of repeated becoming.
ramacharitamanas::5375.modern_relevance: You keep circling the same argument, the same habit, the same anxious thought at 1:13 a.m. This verse says the loop can break when something kinder than your own effort meets you.
ramacharitamanas::5375.insight: It shifts the mind from self-rescue to receiving help beyond ego and effort.

ramayan::1.verse_sanskrit: तपस्स्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् । नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् । । 111 । ।
ramayan::1.verse_hindi: Ascetic Valmiki enquired of Narada, preeminent among the sages ever engaged in the practice of religious austerities or study of the Vedas and best among the eloquent.
ramayan::1.english_translation: The ascetic Valmiki, ever devoted to austerity and sacred study, respectfully asked Narada, the foremost among eloquent sages.
ramayan::1.translation_literal: तपस्स्वाध्यायनिरतम् (ever engaged in austerity and study) / तपस्वी (ascetic) / वाग्विदां (among those who know speech) / वरम् (best) / नारदम् (Narada) / परिपप्रच्छ (asked respectfully) / वाल्मीकिः (Valmiki) / मुनिपुङ्गवम् (foremost among sages)
ramayan::1.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1.essence: A great story begins with a humble question.
ramayan::1.simple_meaning: Valmiki respectfully asks Narada a question. The verse simply sets up the conversation that follows.
ramayan::1.simple_insight: Sometimes the real beginning is a humble question.
ramayan::1.detailed_meaning: In a quiet opening scene, Valmiki, a sage devoted to austerity and study, approaches Narada with respect. This is the doorway into the Ramayana: the poet does not begin with certainty, but with inquiry.
ramayan::1.modern_relevance: You open a notebook because something important is missing from your understanding. The first honest step is not answering — it is asking the right person.
ramayan::1.insight: It shifts attention from proclaiming truth to seeking it carefully.

ramayan::2.verse_sanskrit: कोन्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान् । धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रत: । । 112 । ।
ramayan::2.verse_hindi: Who in this world lives today endowed with excellent qualities, prowess, righteousness, gratitude, truthfulness and firmness in his vows?
ramayan::2.english_translation: Who in this world lives today endowed with excellent qualities, prowess, righteousness, gratitude, truthfulness, and firmness in his vows?
ramayan::2.translation_literal: कः (who) / नु (indeed) / अस्मिन् (in this) / साम्प्रतम् (now, at present) / लोके (in the world) / गुणवान् (endowed with virtues) / कः (who) / वीर्यवान् (full of prowess) / धर्मज्ञः (knower of righteousness) / च (and) / कृतज्ञः (grateful) / च (and) / सत्यवाक्यः (truthful in speech) / दृढव्रतः (firm in vows)
ramayan::2.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::2.essence: A great story begins by asking who is still worthy of admiration.
ramayan::2.simple_meaning: Valmiki asks Narada to name someone alive today who combines virtue, courage, righteousness, gratitude, truthfulness, and steady commitment.
ramayan::2.simple_insight: The search begins with a hard question: can one person still embody all that is worthy?
ramayan::2.detailed_meaning: Valmiki has just met Narada and is ready to ask the question that will become the Ramayana. He is not asking about power or fame, but about a living person whose character is complete enough to deserve remembrance.
ramayan::2.modern_relevance: After another day of headlines, broken promises, and half-hearted apologies, you may wonder whether anyone still lives by a full standard. The question itself is the beginning of clarity.
ramayan::2.insight: It turns admiration into inquiry: before telling a story, Valmiki asks what a truly complete human being looks like.

ramayan::3.verse_sanskrit: चारित्रेण च को युक्तस्सर्वभूतेषु को हित: । विद्वान्क: कस्समर्थश्च कश्चैकप्रियदर्शन: । । 113 । ।
ramayan::3.verse_hindi: Who is that one gifted with good conduct, given to the wellbeing of all living creatures, learned in the lore (knowledge of all things that is known), capable of doing things which others can not do and singularly handsome?
ramayan::3.english_translation: Who is gifted with good conduct, who cares for all living beings, who is learned, capable of what others cannot do, and uniquely beautiful to behold?
ramayan::3.translation_literal: चारित्रेण (by conduct) / च (and) / कः (who) / युक्तः (endowed) / सर्वभूतेषु (among all beings) / कः (who) / हितः (beneficial) / विद्वान् (learned) / कः (who) / कः (who) / समर्थः (capable) / च (and) / कः (who) / एकप्रियदर्शनः (singularly pleasant to behold)
ramayan::3.speaker: Narada
ramayan::3.essence: True greatness includes character, usefulness, and a presence people trust.
ramayan::3.simple_meaning: The question asks who combines good conduct, care for all beings, learning, capability, and an especially admirable presence.
ramayan::3.simple_insight: Real greatness is not just talent; it includes character, usefulness, and the way you affect everyone around you.
ramayan::3.detailed_meaning: Valmiki has asked Narada to name the best person alive. After asking about virtue, courage, truth, and steadiness, he now adds conduct, compassion, learning, ability, and striking presence. The search is becoming more exact, verse by verse.
ramayan::3.modern_relevance: You meet someone who is brilliant, but they leave people colder. Then you meet the rare person who is capable, kind, and steady under pressure. This verse asks you to notice that fuller kind of excellence.
ramayan::3.insight: It widens the idea of excellence beyond skill into conduct, care, and presence.

ramayan::4.verse_sanskrit: आत्मवान्को जितक्रोधो द्युतिमान्कोऽनसूयक: । कस्य बिभ्यति देवाश्च जातरोषस्य संयुगे । । 114 । ।
ramayan::4.verse_hindi: Who (among men) is selfrestrained? Who has conquered anger? Who is endowed with brilliance and free from envy? Who is that when excited to wrath even the devatas, are afraid of (let alone foes)?
ramayan::4.english_translation: Who is self-restrained? Who has conquered anger? Who is radiant and free from envy? Whose wrath in battle makes even the radiant beings afraid?
ramayan::4.translation_literal: आत्मवान् (self-controlled) / कः (who) / जितक्रोधः (conquered anger) / द्युतिमान् (radiant) / कः (who) / अनसूयकः (free from envy) / कस्य (of whom) / बिभ्यति (are afraid) / देवाः (the radiant beings) / च (and) / जातरोषस्य (whose anger has arisen) / संयुगे (in battle)
ramayan::4.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::4.essence: True strength is anger mastered, not anger unleashed.
ramayan::4.simple_meaning: A truly worthy person is self-controlled, has overcome anger, shines with inner strength, and is free from envy. Even the radiant beings fear the force of such a person in battle.
ramayan::4.simple_insight: Real power is not loudness. It is restraint that stays intact under pressure.
ramayan::4.detailed_meaning: Valmiki begins a defining question to Narada: what kind of man today carries all the highest qualities? He asks for someone self-controlled, anger-free, bright, and unenvying — a person whose force is so complete that even the radiant beings would fear him in battle.
ramayan::4.modern_relevance: You are about to reply to a message that could ignite everything. The strongest version of you is not the fastest reaction — it is the one that can hold its fire.
ramayan::4.insight: It shifts admiration from raw intensity to disciplined self-command.

ramayan::5.verse_sanskrit: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे । महर्षे त्वं समर्थोऽसि ज्ञातुमेवंविधं नरम् । । 115 । ।
ramayan::5.verse_hindi: O Maharshi, I intend to hear about such a man whom you are able to place? Indeed great is my curiosity.
ramayan::5.english_translation: O great sage, I want to hear about such a man. You alone are able to know one like that, and my curiosity is great.
ramayan::5.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / इच्छामि (I wish) / अहम् (I) / श्रोतुम् (to hear) / परम् (great) / कौतूहलम् (curiosity) / हि (indeed) / मे (my) / महर्षे (O great sage) / त्वम् (you) / समर्थः (able) / असि (are) / ज्ञातुम् (to know) / एवंविधम् (of this kind) / नरम् (man)
ramayan::5.speaker: Narada
ramayan::5.essence: The search for an ideal man begins with asking the right sage.
ramayan::5.simple_meaning: Narada says he wants to hear about the rare kind of man Valmiki is describing, because Valmiki is capable of recognizing such a person.
ramayan::5.simple_insight: Real questions deserve a real listener. Curiosity deepens when it meets discernment.
ramayan::5.detailed_meaning: Valmiki has just asked what kind of person truly has virtue, self-control, learning, and courage. Narada responds with interest, saying he wants to hear about such a man from the sage who can recognize him. This opens the Ramayana’s central inquiry.
ramayan::5.modern_relevance: You meet someone who has done the work, and you finally ask the question you have been carrying for years. Not every listener can answer it — but the right one can name what you are really seeking.
ramayan::5.insight: It turns curiosity into inquiry and points the mind toward a trustworthy source of wisdom.

ramayan::6.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा चैतत्ित्रलोकज्ञो वाल्मीकेर्नारदो वच: । श्रूयतामिति चामन्त्त्र्य प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । । 116 । ।
ramayan::6.verse_hindi: Invited by Valmiki to take his seat Narada, knower of the three worlds heard him and said with delight, Listen to me!. And thus spoke.
ramayan::6.english_translation: Hearing this, Narada, knower of the three worlds, greeted Valmiki and said with delight, “Listen to me.” Then he began to speak.
ramayan::6.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / च (and) / एतत् (this) / त्रिलोक-ज्ञः (knower of the three worlds) / वाल्मीकेः (of Valmiki) / नारदः (Narada) / वचः (words) / श्रूयताम् (let it be heard) / इति (thus) / च (and) / आमन्त्र्य (having addressed) / प्रहृष्टः (delighted) / वाक्यम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::6.speaker: Narada
ramayan::6.essence: The answer opens because the question is sincere.
ramayan::6.simple_meaning: Narada hears Valmiki’s question, welcomes it, and prepares to answer with joy.
ramayan::6.simple_insight: A real answer begins when someone is ready to hear the question fully.
ramayan::6.detailed_meaning: Valmiki has asked for the rarest kind of human being. Narada, who knows the three worlds, receives the question with delight and turns to answer it. The verse mainly sets up the teaching that follows.
ramayan::6.modern_relevance: You finally ask the question you’ve been carrying for months, and the right person leans in instead of looking away.
ramayan::6.insight: It shifts attention from the question itself to the readiness of the listener and the teacher.

ramayan::7.verse_sanskrit: बहवो दुर्लभाश्चैव ये त्वया कीर्तिता गुणा: । मुने वक्ष्याम्यहं बुद्ध्वा तैर्युक्तश्श्रूयतान्नर: । । 117 । ।
ramayan::7.verse_hindi: O sage rare indeed are men endowed with the many qualities you have described. I  ascertained one. Listen carefully.
ramayan::7.english_translation: O sage, the many qualities you described are rare indeed. I have found one such man; listen carefully.
ramayan::7.translation_literal: बहवः (many) / दुर्लभाः (rare) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / ये (which) / त्वया (by you) / कीर्तिताः (described) / गुणाः (qualities) / मुने (O sage) / वक्ष्यामि (I will speak) / अहम् (I) / बुद्ध्वा (having understood) / तैः (with those) / युक्तः (endowed) / श्रूयताम् (let it be heard) / नरः (the man)
ramayan::7.speaker: Narada
ramayan::7.essence: Rare virtues become real when Narada names the man who bears them.
ramayan::7.simple_meaning: The speaker says the qualities just described are very rare, but he has found one man who has them and will name him next.
ramayan::7.simple_insight: Some people do embody the ideal you thought was impossible.
ramayan::7.detailed_meaning: Narada responds to Valmiki’s question after hearing the qualities of the ideal man. He agrees such traits are rare, then prepares to identify Rama as the one who truly has them.
ramayan::7.modern_relevance: You hear a list of qualities that feel almost unreal in a person. Then someone quietly says, “I know one.”
ramayan::7.insight: It shifts attention from abstract ideals to a real person who lives them.

ramayan::8.verse_sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवो रामो नाम जनैश्श्रुत: । नियतात्मा महावीर्यो द्युतिमान्धृतिमान् वशी । । 118 । ।
ramayan::8.verse_hindi: People have heard his name as Rama, who was born in the race of king Ikshvaku,
ramayan::8.english_translation: Rama, born in the line of Ikshvaku, is known among people as steadfast, mighty, radiant, patient, and self-controlled.
ramayan::8.translation_literal: इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवः (born in the line of Ikshvaku) / रामः (Rama) / नाम (by name) / जनैः (by people) / श्रुतः (heard of) / नियतात्मा (steadfast in mind) / महावीर्यः (of great might) / द्युतिमान् (radiant) / धृतिमान् (patient) / वशी (self-controlled)
ramayan::8.speaker: Narada
ramayan::8.essence: Rama's fame rests on disciplined strength, not just birth.
ramayan::8.simple_meaning: Rama is introduced as a famous prince from Ikshvaku's line, known for strength, radiance, patience, and self-mastery.
ramayan::8.simple_insight: Greatness begins with steady character, not just fame.
ramayan::8.detailed_meaning: Narada is answering Valmiki's question by naming the one man who truly gathers all noble qualities. He begins Rama's introduction here, listing his lineage and virtues before continuing the fuller description in the next verse.
ramayan::8.modern_relevance: Someone introduces a leader in a meeting by listing what makes him reliable: calm under pressure, strong, clear, and disciplined. The real résumé is character.
ramayan::8.insight: It shifts attention from reputation alone to the steadiness underneath it.

ramayan::9.verse_sanskrit: बुद्धिमान्नीतिमान्वाग्मी श्रीमान् शत्रुनिबर्हण: । विपुलांसो महाबाहु: कम्बुग्रीवो महाहनु: । । 119 । ।
ramayan::9.verse_hindi: He (Sri Rama) is a great intellectual, adherent to rules, eloquent, handsome, destroyer of foes (sins), broadshouldered, strongarmed, having conchshaped neck and   prominent cheeks.
ramayan::9.english_translation: He is wise, righteous, eloquent, splendid, a destroyer of foes, broad-shouldered, strong-armed, with a conch-shaped neck and prominent cheeks.
ramayan::9.translation_literal: बुद्धिमान् (wise) / नीतिमान् (righteous) / वाग्मी (eloquent) / श्रीमान् (splendid) / शत्रुनिबर्हणः (destroyer of foes) / विपुलांसः (broad-shouldered) / महाबाहुः (strong-armed) / कम्बुग्रीवः (with conch-shaped neck) / महाहनुः (with prominent cheeks)
ramayan::9.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::9.essence: True greatness shows itself as harmony between mind, speech, conduct, and power.
ramayan::9.simple_meaning: Rama is being praised as wise, righteous, eloquent, handsome, powerful, and physically magnificent.
ramayan::9.simple_insight: Greatness can be whole: mind, conduct, speech, and strength all aligned.
ramayan::9.detailed_meaning: Brahma is praising Rama to the sage gods before Rama enters the central human drama of the epic. This verse continues a formal description of his qualities, adding intellect, conduct, speech, beauty, and bodily strength.
ramayan::9.modern_relevance: Someone walks into a room and is judged by presence alone — words, posture, calm, and competence all speaking at once. This verse gathers those qualities into one figure.
ramayan::9.insight: It teaches you to see excellence as integrated character, not isolated talent.

ramayan::10.verse_hindi: Possessing a broad chest, armed with a great bow, with fleshy collar bones, knee-long arms, a noble head, a graceful forehead and great prowess, he is the destroyer of foes (sins).
ramayan::10.english_translation: Possessing a broad chest, armed with a great bow, with fleshy collar bones, knee-long arms, a noble head, a graceful forehead and great prowess, he is the destroyer of foes.
ramayan::10.translation_literal: महा-उरस्कः (broad-chested) / महा-इष्वासः (great-bowed, armed with a great bow) / गूढ-जत्रुः (with fleshy collar bones) / अरि-दमः (destroyer of foes) / आजानु-बाहुः (arms reaching the knees) / सु-शिराः (with a noble head) / सु-ललाटः (with a graceful forehead) / सु-विक्रमः (of great prowess)
ramayan::10.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::10.essence: Rama's greatness is shown first in his form, then in his force.
ramayan::10.simple_meaning: Rama is described through his physical strength, beauty, and commanding presence.
ramayan::10.simple_insight: Greatness can be seen in the steadiness of a body that is ready for responsibility.
ramayan::10.detailed_meaning: Valmiki continues Rama's portrait by listing his noble bodily marks: broad chest, long arms, strong build, and fearless presence. This is part of a flowing description of Rama's ideal form, not a separate teaching on its own.
ramayan::10.modern_relevance: A room falls quiet when someone walks in with calm strength and no need to prove anything. You feel it before a word is spoken.
ramayan::10.insight: It shifts attention from abstract praise to embodied presence and readiness.

ramayan::11.verse_sanskrit: समस्समविभक्ताङ्गस्स्निग्धवर्ण: प्रतापवान् । पीनवक्षा विशालाक्षो लक्ष्मीवान् शुभलक्षणः । । 1111 । ।
ramayan::11.verse_hindi: Mighty and powerful, he has a wellproportioned body, neither tall nor short, shining complexion, welldeveloped chest, large eyes, lustrous body and good qualities.
ramayan::11.english_translation: Mighty and powerful, he has a well-proportioned body, neither tall nor short, shining complexion, well-developed chest, large eyes, lustrous body and good qualities.
ramayan::11.translation_literal: समः (equal) / समविभक्ताङ्गः (evenly proportioned limbs) / स्निग्धवर्णः (smooth-complexioned) / प्रतापवान् (full of radiance and power) / पीनवक्षा (broad-chested) / विशालाक्षः (large-eyed) / लक्ष्मीवान् (endowed with splendor) / शुभलक्षणः (marked by auspicious signs)
ramayan::11.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::11.essence: Rama's outward form reflects the steadiness within.
ramayan::11.simple_meaning: Rama is described as physically handsome, balanced, and radiant, with auspicious marks and a powerful presence.
ramayan::11.simple_insight: Greatness can be seen in the way someone carries themselves.
ramayan::11.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing Rama's physical marks as part of a larger portrait of the ideal prince. The description continues from the previous and next verses, building a complete image of his presence, beauty, and noble bearing rather than making a separate teaching here.
ramayan::11.modern_relevance: You notice someone enter a room and everything about them feels composed, steady, and unmistakably dignified. That quiet presence often says more than words.
ramayan::11.insight: It helps you recognize that character can be visible in bearing, not just in speech.

ramayan::12.verse_sanskrit: धर्मज्ञस्सत्यसन्धश्च प्रजानां च हिते रतः । यशस्वी ज्ञानसम्पन्नश्शुचिर्वश्यस्समाधिमान् । । 1112 । ।
ramayan::12.verse_hindi: Pious, firm in his vows, he is ever intent on doing good to his subjects. He is,  illustrious, wise, and pure at heart. He is obedient to elders (or accessible to those who are dependent on him) and ever meditating (on the means of protecting those who take refuge in him).
ramayan::12.english_translation: Pious, firm in his vows, he is ever intent on doing good to his subjects. He is illustrious, wise, and pure at heart. He is obedient to elders and ever mindful of how to protect those who seek refuge in him.
ramayan::12.translation_literal: धर्मज्ञः (knower of dharma) / सत्यसन्धः (firm in vows) / च (and) / प्रजानाम् (of the subjects) / च (and) / हिते (in the welfare) / रतः (delighting) / यशस्वी (illustrious) / ज्ञानसम्पन्नः (endowed with wisdom) / शुचिः (pure) / वश्यः (obedient) / समाधिमान् (meditative, focused)
ramayan::12.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::12.essence: A worthy leader keeps vows and protects those beneath his care.
ramayan::12.simple_meaning: Rama is described as someone who knows what is right, keeps his promises, and works for the good of his people with wisdom and purity.
ramayan::12.simple_insight: Real authority is not self-serving; it becomes trustworthy when it protects others.
ramayan::12.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing Rama's qualities as the ideal king: truthful, wise, pure, disciplined, and devoted to the welfare of his people. This is not praise for its own sake; it defines why Rama is fit to bear the burden of rule.
ramayan::12.modern_relevance: A manager signs off on a hard decision that affects everyone below them. The difference between power and leadership shows up in whether the choice protects the people who depend on it.
ramayan::12.insight: It shifts leadership from status to responsibility: your worth is shown by how carefully you hold others' trust.

ramayan::13.verse_sanskrit: प्रजापतिसमश्श्रीमान् धाता रिपुनिषूदनः । रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य परिरक्षिता । । 1113 । ।
ramayan::13.verse_hindi: Auspicious like Brahma, Sri Rama is the sustainer of this world, destroyer of enemies and protector of all living beings and of the moral code.
ramayan::13.english_translation: Auspicious like Brahma, Rama is the sustainer of this world, the destroyer of enemies, and the protector of all living beings and of dharma.
ramayan::13.translation_literal: प्रजापति-समः (like Brahma) / श्रीमान् (splendid) / धाता (sustainer) / रिपु-निषूदनः (destroyer of enemies) / रक्षिता (protector) / जीवलोकस्य (of the world of living beings) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / परिरक्षिता (chief protector)
ramayan::13.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::13.essence: True greatness protects life and holds the line for dharma.
ramayan::13.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as a majestic protector: one who sustains life, defeats enemies, and guards moral order.
ramayan::13.simple_insight: Power becomes noble when it protects life and right conduct.
ramayan::13.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing Rama's royal qualities in Ayodhya. After describing his body, truthfulness, wisdom, and purity, he now crowns that portrait: Rama is not just admirable, he is a protector of the world, of living beings, and of dharma itself.
ramayan::13.modern_relevance: When you have authority in a family, team, or community, the real test is not how much control you have. It is whether people and principles become safer because you are there.
ramayan::13.insight: It shifts leadership from self-display to protection of others and of right order.

ramayan::14.verse_sanskrit: रक्षिता स्वस्य धर्मस्य स्वजनस्य च रक्षिता । वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठितः । । 1114 । ।
ramayan::14.verse_hindi: He has performed the duties of a king and protected his subjects. knowledgeable in the true nature of the Vedas he is accomplished in military science (he is a great archer).
ramayan::14.english_translation: He has protected his own dharma and protected his people. He knows the true nature of the Vedas and is firmly established in archery.
ramayan::14.translation_literal: रक्षिता (protector) / स्वस्य (of his own) / धर्मस्य (dharma) / च (and) / स्वजनस्य (of his people) / रक्षिता (protector) / वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञः (knower of the true nature of the Vedas and Vedangas) / धनुर्वेदे (in the science of archery) / च (and) / निष्ठितः (firmly established)
ramayan::14.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::14.essence: Mastery matters most when it protects the people who depend on you.
ramayan::14.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as someone who protects his own duty and his people, while also mastering the Vedas and archery.
ramayan::14.simple_insight: Real strength is not just skill; it is using skill to protect what depends on you.
ramayan::14.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing Rama's qualities as the ideal ruler. After praising him as wise and pure, the poem adds that he guards his own duty and the people under his care, while also mastering sacred learning and warfare. It is a portrait of complete kingship.
ramayan::14.modern_relevance: You may know your craft well, but the real test comes when other people rely on you. Skill without responsibility is incomplete; mastery becomes noble only when it protects.
ramayan::14.insight: It shifts the idea of competence from private excellence to public responsibility.

ramayan::15.verse_hindi: Sri Rama knows the true meaning of all scriptures and has a retentive memory. He is talented (possessing brightness of conception). He is beloved and welldisposed towards all people (and courteous even towards those who have done him harm). He has an unperturbed mind (even in times of extreme grief) and is circumspect (in doing right things at the right time).
ramayan::15.english_translation: Sri Rama knows the true meaning of all scriptures and has a retentive memory. He is gifted with quick understanding. He is beloved by all, gentle even toward those who have harmed him, steady in grief, and wise in choosing the right time to act.
ramayan::15.translation_literal: सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञः (knower of the true meaning of all scriptures) / स्मृतिमान् (one who has memory) / प्रतिभानवान् (one who has brilliance of conception) / सर्वलोकप्रियः (beloved by all people) / साधुः (virtuous, gentle) / अदीनात्मा (one whose mind is not depressed) / विचक्षणः (discerning, prudent)
ramayan::15.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::15.essence: True wisdom stays kind, steady, and exact under pressure.
ramayan::15.simple_meaning: Rama is described as wise, quick to understand, memorable, kind to everyone, steady in sorrow, and careful about timing.
ramayan::15.simple_insight: Strength does not have to harden you. A clear mind can stay kind under pressure.
ramayan::15.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing Rama's inner excellence after naming his public duties and learning. This verse shifts from what Rama does to how he thinks and feels: he understands deeply, remembers well, stays unshaken in grief, and chooses action with discernment.
ramayan::15.modern_relevance: You are in a tense meeting, and everyone is watching for a sharp reply. The stronger move is not to win the room, but to stay kind, clear, and timed right.
ramayan::15.insight: It trains the mind to pair intelligence with steadiness, so judgment stays humane under stress.

ramayan::16.verse_hindi: Sri Rama, like sea to rivers, is accessible to men of virtue and has equal disposition towards all. He always has a pleasing appearance.
ramayan::16.english_translation: Sri Rama, like the sea to rivers, is accessible to people of virtue and has equal regard for all. He always has a pleasing appearance.
ramayan::16.translation_literal: सर्वदाभिगतः (always approachable) / सद्भिः (by the virtuous) / समुद्रः इव (like the ocean) / सिन्धुभिः (by rivers) / आर्यः (noble) / सर्वसमः (equal to all) / च एव (and indeed) / सदा (always) / इति प्रियदर्शनः (pleasing to behold)
ramayan::16.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::16.essence: Real greatness stays approachable and treats everyone alike.
ramayan::16.simple_meaning: Rama is easy for good people to approach, treats everyone equally, and carries a naturally pleasing presence.
ramayan::16.simple_insight: True dignity does not create distance. It makes you steady, fair, and approachable.
ramayan::16.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is praising Rama’s character after listing his learning and kingly virtues. The picture is of a ruler whose greatness does not make him cold or partial: he welcomes the virtuous, remains even-minded, and is pleasant to behold.
ramayan::16.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard day, and people can feel whether you bring tension or ease. Rama’s presence shows the rare kind of strength that does not intimidate, exclude, or play favorites.
ramayan::16.insight: It shifts the mind from status-based distance to even-handed presence.

ramayan::17.verse_sanskrit: स च सर्वगुणोपेत: कौसल्यानन्दवर्धन: । समुद्र इव गाम्भीर्ये धैर्येण हिमवानिव । । 1117 । ।
ramayan::17.verse_hindi: Sri Rama, bestowed with all virtues, enhanced the joys of Kausalya,  He is like the sea in deportment and like Himavant in fortitude.
ramayan::17.english_translation: Sri Rama, endowed with every virtue, brought joy to Kausalya. In steadiness he is like the sea, and in fortitude like Himavat.
ramayan::17.translation_literal: स (he) / च (and) / सर्वगुणोपेतः (endowed with all virtues) / कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः (increaser of Kausalya's joy) / समुद्रः इव (like the sea) / गाम्भीर्ये (in depth/steadiness) / धैर्येण (by fortitude) / हिमवान् इव (like Himavat)
ramayan::17.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::17.essence: True greatness is calm, vast, and unbreakable.
ramayan::17.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as fully virtuous, deeply steady, and unbreakably brave. His goodness is not fragile; it has the weight of the sea and the mountain.
ramayan::17.simple_insight: Real strength does not need to be harsh. It can be calm, broad, and dependable.
ramayan::17.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing Rama's qualities in a praise passage. After calling him accessible, wise, and equal to all, he now shows the inner shape of that greatness: he is the joy of Kausalya, vast in depth like the sea, and firm in courage like Himavat.
ramayan::17.modern_relevance: You are in a tense room, and everyone is waiting to see whether you will snap or stay centered. This verse praises the kind of presence that steadies others without needing to dominate them.
ramayan::17.insight: It shifts admiration from flashy strength to quiet steadiness and moral weight.

ramayan::18.verse_sanskrit: विष्णुना सदृशो वीर्ये सोमवत्प्रियदर्शन: । कालाग्निसदृश: क्रोधे क्षमया पृथिवीसम: । । 1118 । । धनदेन समस्त्यागे सत्ये धर्म इवापर: ।
ramayan::18.verse_hindi: Sri Rama is like Visnu in prowess, the Moon in pleasing appearance, the allconsuming fire in anger, the earth in patience, Kubera in chartiy and the Sun in steadfastness.
ramayan::18.english_translation: Sri Rama is like Vishnu in prowess, the Moon in pleasing appearance, the all-consuming fire in anger, the earth in patience, Kubera in charity, and the Sun in steadfastness.
ramayan::18.translation_literal: विष्णुना (like Vishnu) / सदृशः (similar) / वीर्ये (in prowess) / सोमवत् (like the Moon) / प्रियदर्शनः (pleasing in appearance) / कालाग्निसदृशः (like the fire of time) / क्रोधे (in anger) / क्षमया (by patience) / पृथिवीसमः (equal to the earth) / धनदेन (with Kubera) / समः (equal) / त्यागे (in charity) / सत्ये (in truth) / धर्मः इव अपरः (another like dharma)
ramayan::18.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::18.essence: Rama’s greatness is balance: force without cruelty, patience without weakness.
ramayan::18.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as a rare blend of force, beauty, patience, generosity, and truth. He holds opposite qualities without losing balance.
ramayan::18.simple_insight: You do not need to choose between strength and gentleness. Mature character can hold both.
ramayan::18.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing Rama before the coronation crisis fully unfolds. In one compact praise, he gathers the qualities that make Rama fit to rule: fierce when needed, patient under strain, generous in giving, and unwavering in truth.
ramayan::18.modern_relevance: You can be calm in a tense meeting, generous with a colleague, and still unshakable when pressure rises. Real steadiness is not softness — it is balance under force.
ramayan::18.insight: It shifts you from thinking virtue is one trait to seeing it as a disciplined whole.

ramayan::19.verse_sanskrit: तमेवं गुणसम्पन्नं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् । । 1119 । । ज्येष्ठं श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तं प्रियं दशरथस्सुतम् । प्रकृतीनां हितैर्युक्तं प्रकृतिप्रियकाम्यया । । 1120 । । यौवराज्येन संयोक्तुमैच्छत्प्रीत्या महीपति: ।
ramayan::19.verse_hindi: With a desire to promote the welfare of the people king Dasaratha decided to install   Sri Rama, his eldest and affectionate son as heir (apparent) who was bestowed with  all excellent qualities and true prowess, beloved of the people he was ever intent in the welfare of the people.
ramayan::19.english_translation: King Dasharatha, wishing to promote the welfare of the people, wanted to install Rama, his eldest son, beloved for his virtues and true prowess, as heir apparent.
ramayan::19.translation_literal: तम् (him) / एवम् (thus) / गुणसम्पन्नम् (endowed with virtues) / रामम् (Rama) / सत्यपराक्रमम् (true in prowess) / ज्येष्ठम् (eldest) / श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तम् (endowed with excellent qualities) / प्रियम् (beloved) / दशरथस्सुतम् (Dasharatha's son) / प्रकृतीनाम् (of the people) / हितैः (with welfare) / युक्तम् (connected) / प्रकृतिप्रियकाम्यया (with desire for the people's affection) / यौवराज्येन (with the crown-prince office) / संयोक्तुम् (to join / install) / ऐच्छत् (wished) / प्रीत्या (with delight) / महीपतिः (the king)
ramayan::19.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::19.essence: True rule begins with the people's welfare, not personal desire.
ramayan::19.simple_meaning: Dasharatha wants Rama to be crowned because Rama has every virtue and is best for the welfare of the people.
ramayan::19.simple_insight: Good leadership is measured by service, not personal ambition.
ramayan::19.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharatha looks at Rama and sees the obvious heir: eldest, beloved, virtuous, and fit to rule. He wants the kingdom to be guided by someone whose rise will benefit the people, and that decision sets the whole tragedy in motion.
ramayan::19.modern_relevance: A manager finally has a successor to choose and stops asking who is loudest. The real question is who will protect the team, serve the mission, and carry the burden well.
ramayan::19.insight: It shifts leadership from entitlement to responsibility for the common good.

ramayan::20.verse_sanskrit: तस्याभिषेकसम्भारान्दृष्ट्वा भार्याऽथ कैकयी । । 1121 । । पूर्वं दत्तवरा देवी वरमेनमयाचत । विवासनं च रामस्य भरतस्याभिषेचनम् । । 1122 । ।
ramayan::20.verse_hindi: Thereafter, having seen the preparations for installation of Rama, queen Kaikeyi who had been promised earlier with boons by Dasaratha demanded of him the exile of Rama and enthronement of Bharata.
ramayan::20.english_translation: Thereafter, seeing the preparations for Rama's installation, Queen Kaikeyi, who had earlier been granted boons by Dasaratha, asked for Rama's exile and Bharata's coronation.
ramayan::20.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / अभिषेक (coronation) / सम्भारान् (arrangements) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / भार्या (wife) / अथ (then) / कैकयी (Kaikeyi) / पूर्वम् (earlier) / दत्तवरा (given boons) / देवी (queen) / वरम् (boon) / एनम् (this one) / अयाचत (asked for) / विवासनम् (exile) / च (and) / रामस्य (of Rama) / भरतस्य (of Bharata) / अभिषेचनम् (installation)
ramayan::20.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::20.essence: A promised boon becomes the lever that breaks a kingdom's plans.
ramayan::20.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi sees Rama's coronation preparations and uses the boons she already received to demand Rama's exile and Bharata's coronation.
ramayan::20.simple_insight: A single demand can overturn an entire future.
ramayan::20.detailed_meaning: As Ayodhya prepares to crown Rama, Kaikeyi remembers the boons Dasaratha once promised her. In one decisive demand, she asks for Rama to be sent away and Bharata to be installed instead, setting the exile in motion.
ramayan::20.modern_relevance: A meeting is about to celebrate a long-awaited promotion, and one person quietly uses an old promise to change everything. A life can turn on a demand made at the worst possible moment.
ramayan::20.insight: It shows how hidden obligations can suddenly redirect an entire household's fate.

ramayan::21.verse_sanskrit: स सत्यवचनाद्राजा धर्मपाशेन संयत: । विवासयामास सुतं रामं दशरथ: प्रियम् । । 1123 । ।
ramayan::21.verse_hindi: Dasaratha, true to his word and restrained by the bond of duty, sent his beloved  son Rama to the forest.
ramayan::21.english_translation: Dasaratha, true to his word and restrained by the bond of duty, sent his beloved son Rama to the forest.
ramayan::21.translation_literal: स (that) / सत्यवचनात् (because of his true word) / राजा (the king) / धर्मपाशेन (by the bond of duty) / संयत: (bound, restrained) / विवासयामास (sent into exile) / सुतम् (the son) / रामम् (Rama) / दशरथ: (Dasharatha) / प्रियम् (beloved)
ramayan::21.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::21.essence: A kept promise can demand the deepest personal loss.
ramayan::21.simple_meaning: Dasharatha sends Rama into exile because he must keep his promise and follow duty, even though Rama is dearly loved.
ramayan::21.simple_insight: Integrity can demand a painful sacrifice, and the pain does not cancel the rightness of the act.
ramayan::21.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi has demanded her boons, and Dasharatha is trapped by his own promise. The king who planned to crown Rama now sends his beloved son away. The verse captures the cost of keeping a vow when it tears your heart open.
ramayan::21.modern_relevance: You promised something before you knew the full price. Now the cost is real, and backing out would be easier — but your word is still standing there, waiting for you.
ramayan::21.insight: It shifts you from protecting comfort to honoring commitment, even when the commitment hurts.

ramayan::22.verse_sanskrit: स जगाम वनं वीर: प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन् । पितुर्वचननिर्देशात्कैकेय्या: प्रियकारणात् । । 1124 । ।
ramayan::22.verse_hindi: Mighty Sri Rama inorder to please Kaikeyi and obey the word of command of his father, went to the forest and help the king to keep his promise to Kaikeyi.
ramayan::22.english_translation: Mighty Rama went to the forest, keeping his vow, obeying his father's command, and doing what pleased Kaikeyi so that the king's promise would stand.
ramayan::22.translation_literal: स (he) / जगाम (went) / वनं (to the forest) / वीरः (the heroic one) / प्रतिज्ञाम् (the vow) / अनुपालयन् (keeping) / पितुः (of the father) / वचन-निर्देशात् (by the command-word) / कैकेय्याः (of Kaikeyi) / प्रिय-कारणात् (for the sake of pleasing) /
ramayan::22.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::22.essence: He chose exile over convenience because his word had to remain intact.
ramayan::22.simple_meaning: Rama goes to the forest because he is keeping his promise and obeying his father's command, even though it is painful.
ramayan::22.simple_insight: Integrity can demand a loss you never wanted, and still leave you standing tall.
ramayan::22.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just lost its future to Kaikeyi's boon. Rama does not resist. He leaves for the forest to honor his father's word and preserve the king's promise, turning private pain into public duty.
ramayan::22.modern_relevance: You said yes before you knew the full cost. Now the cost has arrived, and backing out would be easier — but your word is on the line.
ramayan::22.insight: It teaches you to place obligation above comfort when the two collide.

ramayan::23.verse_sanskrit: तं व्रजन्तं प्रियो भ्राता लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह । स्नेहाद्विनयसम्पन्नस्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धन: । । 1125 । । भ्रातरं दयितो भ्रातुस्सौभ्रात्रमनुदर्शयन् ।
ramayan::23.verse_hindi: Lakshmana  beloved brother to Rama is drawn towards him. Endowed with modesty he is an enhancer of the joy of his mother Sumitra. Displaying his fraternal love, he followed  Rama who was departing to the forest.
ramayan::23.english_translation: Lakshmana, Rama's beloved younger brother, followed him to the forest. Filled with affection and humility, he brought joy to Sumitra and showed the depth of brotherly love.
ramayan::23.translation_literal: तं (him) / व्रजन्तं (going) / प्रियः (beloved) / भ्राता (brother) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / अनुजगाम (followed) / ह (indeed) / स्नेहात् (from affection) / विनय-सम्पन्नः (endowed with humility) / सुमित्रा-आनन्द-वर्धनः (increaser of Sumitra's joy) / भ्रातरम् (brother) / दयितः (dear one) / भ्रातुः (of the brother) / सौभ्रात्रम् (brotherliness) / अनुदर्शयन् (showing)
ramayan::23.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::23.essence: Brotherhood becomes real when it walks beside pain.
ramayan::23.simple_meaning: Lakshmana did not let Rama go alone. Out of love and humility, he went after him to the forest and showed what true brotherhood looks like.
ramayan::23.simple_insight: Real closeness shows up as loyal presence, not just feeling.
ramayan::23.detailed_meaning: Rama has just left Ayodhya for exile. Lakshmana, younger and devoted, refuses to stay behind. He follows not from duty alone, but from love, humility, and the fierce bond that makes separation unbearable.
ramayan::23.modern_relevance: Your sibling is packing a bag after a family crisis, and you know they should not be alone. You do not solve everything. You just go with them.
ramayan::23.insight: It shifts love from sentiment to accompaniment: you show care by staying close when life turns hard.

ramayan::24.verse_sanskrit: रामस्य दयिता भार्या नित्यं प्राणसमा हिता । । 1126 । । जनकस्य कुले जाता देवमायेव निर्मिता । सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्ना नारीणामुत्तमा वधू: । । 1127 । । सीताप्यनुगता रामं शशिनं रोहिणी यथा ।
ramayan::24.verse_hindi: Born in the race of Janaka and daughterinlaw of Dasaratha, Sita, beloved spouse of Rama is like  his vital breath always desired the wellbeing of Rama she followed him like Rohini, the Moon. Endowed with all virtues she is the foremost woman.
ramayan::24.english_translation: Sita, Rama's beloved wife, was always devoted to his welfare, like a vital breath. Born in Janaka's line, she seemed divinely fashioned, endowed with every virtue, the finest of women. She followed Rama like Rohini follows the moon.
ramayan::24.translation_literal: रामस्य (of Rama) / दयिता (beloved) / भार्या (wife) / नित्यं (always) / प्राणसमा (like life-breath) / हिता (wishing well) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / कुले (in the line) / जाता (born) / देवमाया इव (like divine illusion) / निर्मिता (fashioned) / सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्ना (endowed with all marks/virtues) / नारीणाम् (of women) / उत्तमा (best) / वधूः (bride/daughter-in-law) / सीता अपि (Sita also) / अनुगता (followed) / रामम् (Rama) / शशिनम् (the moon) / रोहिणी यथा (like Rohini)
ramayan::24.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::24.essence: True devotion walks beside hardship, not away from it.
ramayan::24.simple_meaning: Sita is described as Rama's devoted wife, always wishing him well, born in Janaka's family, full of virtues, and following him like Rohini follows the moon.
ramayan::24.simple_insight: Love here is shown as loyal presence, not just feeling.
ramayan::24.detailed_meaning: Rama has left for exile, and the poem pauses to describe Sita as she follows him. Valmiki presents her not as a passive companion but as the ideal wife: devoted, virtuous, and inseparable from Rama's journey.
ramayan::24.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love walk into a hard season, and you choose to stand beside them without making it about yourself.
ramayan::24.insight: It shifts attention from romance as emotion to loyalty as steady companionship.

ramayan::25.verse_sanskrit: पौरैरनुगतो दूरं पित्रा दशरथेन च । । 1128 । । शृङ्गिबेरपुरे सूतं गङ्गाकूले व्यसर्जयत् । गुहमासाद्य धर्मात्मा निषादाधिपतिं प्रियम् । । 1129 । । गुहेन सहितो रामो लक्ष्मणेन च सीतया ।
ramayan::25.verse_hindi: The citizens and Dasaratha followed Rama for a long distance. Rama of righteous nature having approached Guha, king of nishadas, at Shrungiberapura sent back charioteer Sumantra and Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana crossed river Ganga.
ramayan::25.english_translation: The citizens and Dasharatha followed Rama for a long distance. At Shrungiberapura, the righteous Rama met Guha, the king of the Nishadas, and sent back Sumantra on the riverbank. Then Rama, with Sita and Lakshmana, crossed the Ganga.
ramayan::25.translation_literal: पौरैः (by the citizens) / अनुगतः (followed) / दूरम् (for a long distance) / पित्रा (by the father) / दशरथेन (by Dasharatha) / च (and) / शृङ्गिबेरपुरे (at Shrungiberapura) / सूतम् (the charioteer) / गङ्गाकूले (on the bank of the Ganga) / व्यसर्जयत् (sent back) / गुहम् (Guha) / आसाद्य (having approached) / धर्मात्मा (the righteous one) / निषादाधिपतिम् (the king of the Nishadas) / प्रियम् (dear) / गुहेन (with Guha) / सहितः (accompanied by) / रामः (Rama) / लक्ष्मणेन (with Lakshmana) / च (and) / सीतया (with Sita)
ramayan::25.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::25.essence: Leaving home is made real by the people who cannot follow.
ramayan::25.simple_meaning: Rama leaves Ayodhya behind as the people and his father follow him partway. He meets Guha, sends Sumantra back, and continues into exile with Sita and Lakshmana.
ramayan::25.simple_insight: A farewell becomes real when the road keeps going without the people who love you most.
ramayan::25.detailed_meaning: The exile has begun. Citizens and Dasharatha follow Rama only so far, then stop at the riverbank. Rama meets Guha, a trusted forest ally, and sends Sumantra away. The three who remain — Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana — cross into the life ahead.
ramayan::25.modern_relevance: You walk someone to the station, hold the last bag, and watch the train pull away. The real separation starts after the goodbye ends.
ramayan::25.insight: It shows how exile is not a speech but a crossing: support falls away, and the next life begins.

ramayan::26.verse_sanskrit: ते वनेन वनं गत्वा नदीस्तीर्त्वा बहूदका: । । 1130 । । चित्रकूटमनुप्राप्य भरद्वाजस्य शासनात् । रम्यमावसथं कृत्वा रममाणा वने त्रय: । । 1131 । । देवगन्धर्वसङ्काशास्तत्र ते न्यवसन् सुखम् ।
ramayan::26.verse_hindi: Moving from one forest to another and crossing deep and wide rivers with plenty of waters, reached the Chitrakuta mountain by the command of sage Bharadwaja. They raised a hut made of leaves in the forest located in Chitrakuta mountain. and dwelt there happily resembling devas and gandharvas.
ramayan::26.english_translation: Moving from one forest to another and crossing deep, wide rivers, they reached Chitrakuta by the command of Bharadwaja. There they built a pleasant hut of leaves and lived happily in the forest.
ramayan::26.translation_literal: ते (they) / वनेन (through the forest) / वनं (forest) / गत्वा (having gone) / नदीः (rivers) / तीर्त्वा (having crossed) / बहूदकाः (with abundant water) / चित्रकूटम् (to Chitrakuta) / अनुप्राप्य (having reached) / भरद्वाजस्य (of Bharadwaja) / शासनात् (by command) / रम्यम् (pleasant) / आवसथम् (dwelling) / कृत्वा (having made) / रममाणाः (rejoicing) / वने (in the forest) / त्रयः (the three) / देवगन्धर्वसङ्काशाः (resembling devas and gandharvas) / तत्र (there) / ते (they) / न्यवसन् (dwelt)
ramayan::26.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::26.essence: A life in exile can still be lived with grace.
ramayan::26.simple_meaning: Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita travel through forests and rivers, reach Chitrakuta, build a simple hut, and settle there peacefully.
ramayan::26.simple_insight: Even exile can become a home when you carry dignity, order, and calm together.
ramayan::26.detailed_meaning: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana have left Ayodhya behind and are moving deeper into the forest. Guided by Bharadwaja, they reach Chitrakuta, build a leaf hut, and live there in quiet ease. The scene prepares for the sorrow that follows.
ramayan::26.modern_relevance: You arrive in a new city with only a suitcase, a borrowed room, and no certainty. What makes it livable is not comfort — it is how you meet it.
ramayan::26.insight: It shifts attention from loss to the way character can make any place bearable.

ramayan::27.verse_sanskrit: चित्रकूटं गते रामे पुत्रशोकातुरस्तथा । । 1132 । । राजा दशरथस्स्वर्गं जगाम विलपन्सुतम् ।
ramayan::27.verse_hindi: When Rama had set out to Chitrakuta, king Dasaratha, stricken by the grief over the separation from his son and mourning over him departed to heavens.
ramayan::27.english_translation: When Rama had gone to Chitrakuta, king Dasaratha, overcome by grief for his son, departed for heaven while lamenting him.
ramayan::27.translation_literal: चित्रकूटं (to Chitrakuta) / गते (having gone) / रामे (when Rama) / पुत्रशोकातुरः (afflicted by grief for his son) / तथा (thus) / राजा (the king) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / स्वर्गं (to heaven) / जगाम (went) / विलपन् (lamenting) / सुतम् (his son)
ramayan::27.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::27.essence: The exile of a son becomes the death of a father.
ramayan::27.simple_meaning: Rama leaves for Chitrakuta, and Dasharatha dies from the pain of separation from his son.
ramayan::27.simple_insight: Love can be so fierce that separation becomes unbearable.
ramayan::27.detailed_meaning: Rama has already left Ayodhya and reached Chitrakuta. Back in the palace, Dasharatha cannot bear the loss of the son he sent away to exile. His grief becomes so heavy that he dies, and the exile now costs the father his life.
ramayan::27.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love walk out the door after a choice you cannot undo. The room stays the same, but your life does not. Some separations do not end with goodbye.
ramayan::27.insight: It shows how a single forced separation can break a family and change the whole story.

ramayan::28.verse_sanskrit: मृते तु तस्मिन्भरतो वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्द्विजै: । । 1133 । । नियुज्यमानो राज्याय नैच्छद्राज्यं महाबल: ।
ramayan::28.verse_hindi: After Dasaratha had passed away, mighty Bharata did not desire to rule the kingdom  against the orders by Vasishta and other brahmins.
ramayan::28.english_translation: After Dasaratha had passed away, mighty Bharata did not desire to rule the kingdom, even when Vasishta and the other brahmins urged him.
ramayan::28.translation_literal: मृते (when dead) / तु (indeed) / तस्मिन् (that one) / भरतः (Bharata) / वसिष्ठ-प्रमुखैः (by Vasishta-led) / द्विजैः (by brahmins) / नियुज्यमानः (being urged) / राज्याय (for the kingdom) / नैच्छत् (did not इच्छा / desire) / राज्यम् (the kingdom) / महाबलः (mighty)
ramayan::28.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::28.essence: True strength can mean refusing power that should belong to someone else.
ramayan::28.simple_meaning: After Dasaratha died, Bharata did not want the kingdom, even though Vasishta and the priests urged him to take it.
ramayan::28.simple_insight: Refusing what looks like power can be the clearest sign of integrity.
ramayan::28.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has died, and Ayodhya is without its king. Vasishta and the brahmins press Bharata to take the throne, but he will not seize what belongs to Rama. His refusal reveals loyalty stronger than ambition.
ramayan::28.modern_relevance: Everyone is looking at you in the meeting, waiting for you to step into the role that suddenly opened up. You know it would look like success — but it would also betray what you promised.
ramayan::28.insight: It teaches you to separate opportunity from rightful claim, and to refuse power when taking it would violate loyalty.

ramayan::29.verse_hindi: The brave Bharata, who had conquered envy and hatred went to the forest in order to worship Ramas feet.
ramayan::29.english_translation: The brave Bharata, who had conquered envy and hatred, went to the forest to worship Rama's feet.
ramayan::29.translation_literal: स (that) / जगाम (went) / वनं (to the forest) / वीरो (the brave one) / रामपादप्रसादक: (one devoted to worshipping Rama's feet)
ramayan::29.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::29.essence: He rejected power and chose to honor the one who deserved it.
ramayan::29.simple_meaning: Bharata refuses the throne and goes to the forest to honor Rama instead of claiming power for himself.
ramayan::29.simple_insight: Real strength can look like humility when ego has already been defeated.
ramayan::29.detailed_meaning: After Dasharatha's death, Bharata is urged to take the kingdom. Instead, he turns away from power and walks to the forest to meet Rama, carrying reverence rather than ambition. This moment shows what kind of brother he is.
ramayan::29.modern_relevance: You were offered the promotion, the credit, the seat at the center. Instead, you chose to support the person who should rightly stand there. That kind of restraint still has a name: greatness.
ramayan::29.insight: It shifts ambition into reverence, showing that honor can be stronger than possession.

ramayan::30.verse_sanskrit: गत्वा तु सुमहात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् । अयाचद्भ्रातरं राममार्यभावपुरस्कृत: । । 1135 । । त्वमेव राजा धर्मज्ञ इति रामं वचोऽब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::30.verse_hindi: Bharata reached Rama, so pleasing venerable, truthful and chivalrous, worshipped him with reverence and implored.
ramayan::30.english_translation: Bharata reached Rama, so pleasing, venerable, truthful, and chivalrous, worshipped him with reverence, and implored: "You alone are the king, for you know dharma."
ramayan::30.translation_literal: गत्वा (having gone) / तु (then) / सुमहात्मानं (the greatly noble one) / रामं (Rama) / सत्यपराक्रमम् (truthful in valor) / अयाचत् (requested) / भ्रातरं (the brother) / रामम् (Rama) / आर्यभावपुरस्कृतः (with noble reverence) / त्वमेव (you alone) / राजा (king) / धर्मज्ञः (knower of dharma) / इति (thus) / रामं (to Rama) / वचः (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::30.speaker: Bharata
ramayan::30.essence: True reverence can mean giving authority back to the one who deserves it.
ramayan::30.simple_meaning: Bharata approaches Rama with reverence and asks him to take the throne, because Rama alone knows what is right.
ramayan::30.simple_insight: Real humility can mean placing responsibility where it truly belongs.
ramayan::30.detailed_meaning: Bharata has come to the forest after refusing Ayodhya's throne. Standing before Rama, he bows not as a rival but as a devoted brother. In this moment, he asks Rama to accept kingship, because Bharata sees Rama as the one fit to rule.
ramayan::30.modern_relevance: You sit across from the person everyone keeps turning to, even though you were offered the role first. You know the honest move is not to grasp, but to hand back what was never truly yours.
ramayan::30.insight: It shifts ambition into reverence and makes leadership a question of fitness, not possession.

ramayan::31.verse_sanskrit: रामोऽपि परमोदारस्सुमुखस्सुमहायशा: । न चैच्छत्पितुरादेशाद्राज्यं रामो महाबल: । । 1136 । ।
ramayan::31.verse_hindi: Although a source of universal delight, although exceedingly generous and of cheerful countenance, highly renowned and capable Rama refused to accept the kingdom in accordance with the command of his father.
ramayan::31.english_translation: Although a source of universal delight, although exceedingly generous and of cheerful countenance, highly renowned and capable Rama refused to accept the kingdom in accordance with the command of his father.
ramayan::31.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / अपि (also) / परम-उदारः (supremely generous) / सु-मुखः (pleasant-faced) / सु-महायशाः (highly renowned) / न (not) / च (and) / ऐच्छत् (desired) / पितुः (father's) / आदेशात् (by command) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / रामः (Rama) / महा-बलः (very powerful)
ramayan::31.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::31.essence: Power means little when duty has already spoken.
ramayan::31.simple_meaning: Rama, though noble and powerful, would not take the kingdom because his father had commanded otherwise.
ramayan::31.simple_insight: There is dignity in choosing a promise over advantage.
ramayan::31.detailed_meaning: Bharata has come to the forest and pleaded with Rama to return. Rama stands before him as the rightful heir, yet he will not seize the throne against Dasharatha’s command. This moment shows why Bharata reveres him.
ramayan::31.modern_relevance: You are offered a promotion that would require breaking a promise you already made. The temptation is real, but so is the cost. Rama’s choice reminds you that not every gain is worth the breach.
ramayan::31.insight: It trains the mind to treat a binding promise as higher than personal benefit.

ramayan::32.verse_sanskrit: पादुके चास्य राज्याय न्यासं दत्वा पुन:पुन: । निवर्तयामास ततो भरतं भरताग्रज: । । 1137 । ।
ramayan::32.verse_hindi: Having handed over his sandals to Bharata as symbol of authority for ruling the kingdom, Rama persuaded him again and again to return to the capital.
ramayan::32.english_translation: Having handed over his sandals to Bharata as a sign of authority for ruling the kingdom, Rama persuaded him again and again to return to the capital.
ramayan::32.translation_literal: पादुके (the sandals) / च (and) / अस्य (his) / राज्याय (for the kingdom) / न्यासं (a deposit, a trust) / दत्वा (having given) / पुनःपुनः (again and again) / निवर्तयामास (he sent back, he turned away) / ततः (then) / भरतम् (Bharata) / भरताग्रजः (Rama, Bharata's elder brother)
ramayan::32.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::32.essence: True authority can be entrusted without being possessed.
ramayan::32.simple_meaning: Rama gives Bharata his sandals to govern in his place, then keeps urging him to return home.
ramayan::32.simple_insight: Even a rightful burden can be handed on without clinging to power.
ramayan::32.detailed_meaning: Bharata has come to bring Rama back, but Rama will not break his father's command. Instead, he entrusts the kingdom to his sandals, a visible sign of authority, and repeatedly sends Bharata back. The real victory here is restraint.
ramayan::32.modern_relevance: You may be asked to step into a role you never wanted, only to find the person above you refusing to take it back. The hardest part is not carrying power — it's releasing it cleanly.
ramayan::32.insight: It shifts attention from holding authority to honoring obligation without attachment.

ramayan::33.verse_hindi: Disaaponted in his mission to take Rama back, Bharata worshipped the sandals of Rama and ruled the kingdom from Nandigrama, awaiting his return.
ramayan::33.english_translation: Disappointed in his mission to bring Rama back, Bharata worshipped Rama's sandals and ruled the kingdom from Nandigrama, waiting for Rama's return.
