ramayan::267.translation_literal: सरय्वाः (of the Sarayu) / च (and) / उत्तरे (northern) / तीरे (bank) / यज्ञभूमिः (sacrificial ground) / विधीयताम् (let be arranged) / शान्तयः (auspicious rites) / च (and) / अभिवर्धन्ताम् (let increase) / यथाकल्पम् (according to the ritual manual) / यथाविधि (according to the ordinance)
ramayan::267.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::267.essence: Great rites begin with exact preparation.
ramayan::267.simple_meaning: The king orders the sacrifice site to be prepared on the north bank of the Sarayu, with every rite done correctly and in order.
ramayan::267.simple_insight: Sacred work begins with exactness, not hurry.
ramayan::267.detailed_meaning: After hearing the brahmins, the king gives precise instructions for the great sacrifice. The site must be set on the Sarayu’s northern bank, and every rite must follow the prescribed order. This is the practical beginning of a huge ritual undertaking.
ramayan::267.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, a public ceremony, or a major project launch, someone has to check the venue, the sequence, and the details no one else notices. This verse honors that careful preparation.
ramayan::267.insight: It shifts attention from intention alone to disciplined execution of every required step.

ramayan::268.verse_sanskrit: शक्य: प्राप्तुमयं यज्ञस्सर्वेणापि महीक्षिता । नापराधो भवेत्कष्टो यद्यस्मिन्क्रतुसत्तमे । । 1816 । ।
ramayan::268.verse_hindi: If obstructions and omissions do not occur in the conduct of this best of sacrifices, it will be possible for every king to get the results.
ramayan::268.english_translation: If this best of sacrifices is completed without any obstruction or mistake, every king can attain its fruits.
ramayan::268.translation_literal: शक्यः (possible) / प्राप्तुम् (to attain) / अयम् (this) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / सर्वेण अपि (by every indeed) / महीक्षित् (king) / न अपराधः (no fault) / भवेत् (may be) / कष्टः (serious) / यदि (if) / यस्मिन् (in which) / क्रतुसत्तमे (in the best sacrifice)
ramayan::268.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::268.essence: One mistake can ruin even the most carefully prepared rite.
ramayan::268.simple_meaning: A royal sacrifice can succeed for any king if no serious mistake or obstruction occurs.
ramayan::268.simple_insight: Even sacred work can fail through a small flaw.
ramayan::268.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha is arranging a major sacrifice on the Sarayu’s northern bank. The preparations are being ordered with precision, because the ritual’s success depends on avoiding even a single defect. This verse stresses that the outcome hangs on flawless execution.
ramayan::268.modern_relevance: You can spend weeks preparing a launch, a wedding, or a legal filing — and one missed detail can change everything.
ramayan::268.insight: It shifts attention from the goal itself to the need for exact preparation and vigilance.

ramayan::269.verse_sanskrit: छिद्रं हि मृगयन्तेऽत्र विद्वांसो ब्रह्मराक्षसा: । निहतस्य च यज्ञस्य सद्य: कर्ता विनश्यति । । 1817 । ।
ramayan::269.verse_hindi: The learned brahmarakshasas always look out for flaws in the sacrifice so that they can spoil it. If a flaw finds place, the doer of the sacrifice is immediately destroyed.
ramayan::269.english_translation: The learned brahmarakshasas always look out for flaws in the sacrifice so that they can spoil it. If a flaw finds place, the doer of the sacrifice is immediately destroyed.
ramayan::269.translation_literal: छिद्रम् (flaw) / हि (indeed) / मृगयन्ते (seek) / अत्र (here) / विद्वांसः (learned ones) / ब्रह्मराक्षसाः (brahmarakshasas) / निहतस्य (of the ruined) / च (and) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / सद्यः (immediately) / कर्ता (performer) / विनश्यति (perishes)
ramayan::269.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::269.essence: Even a noble act can collapse through one hidden flaw.
ramayan::269.simple_meaning: A sacrifice can be ruined if even a small mistake gives hostile beings a chance to interfere.
ramayan::269.simple_insight: Carelessness can undo even a noble act.
ramayan::269.detailed_meaning: Rama's sacrificial rite is being prepared on the Sarayu's bank. The priests warn that learned brahmarakshasas search for any flaw so they can sabotage the ritual. This verse explains why the arrangements must be exact.
ramayan::269.modern_relevance: You spend weeks preparing something important, then one overlooked detail can unravel the whole thing. The warning is simple: precision protects what care has built.
ramayan::269.insight: It shifts attention from intention alone to exact execution.

ramayan::270.verse_sanskrit: तद्यथा विधिपूर्वं मे क्रतुरेष समाप्यते । तथा विधानं क्रियतां समर्था: करणेष्विह । । 1818 । ।
ramayan::270.verse_hindi: Therefore let the arrangements be made in a manner this sacifice is completed in accordance with the scriptures. And in this, you are experts.
ramayan::270.english_translation: Therefore let the arrangements be made so this sacrifice is completed according to the scriptures. You are all skilled in these preparations.
ramayan::270.translation_literal: तद्यथा (therefore, so that) / विधिपूर्वं (according to proper rule) / मे (my) / क्रतुः (sacrifice) / एषः (this) / समाप्यते (is completed) / तथा (thus) / विधानं (arrangement, procedure) / क्रियताम् (let it be done) / समर्थाः (skilled, capable) / करणेषु (in the preparations, in the practical details) / इह (here)
ramayan::270.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::270.essence: Sacred work succeeds only when every detail is done right.
ramayan::270.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks his ministers to make the sacrifice arrangements carefully and exactly according to scripture, because they are skilled in the required details.
ramayan::270.simple_insight: Care and precision are not extra — they are what protect sacred work from failure.
ramayan::270.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha is preparing the sacrifice that should secure his long-awaited sons. He has already warned that hidden flaws can ruin the rite, so now he tells his ministers to handle every detail exactly as required.
ramayan::270.modern_relevance: You are planning something that cannot afford a sloppy mistake — a wedding, a legal filing, a medical procedure. The big outcome depends on the small details being right.
ramayan::270.insight: It teaches you to respect process, because important results depend on disciplined execution.

ramayan::271.verse_sanskrit: तथेति चाब्रुवन्सर्वे मन्त्रिण:प्रत्यपूजयन् । पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य तद्वाक्यं यथाज्ञप्तं निशम्य ते । । 1819 । ।
ramayan::271.verse_hindi: Having heard these words of this Indra on earth (king Dasaratha) all the ministers with due respect replied: May it be as ordered.
ramayan::271.english_translation: Having heard the king's command, all the ministers respectfully replied, 'Let it be as ordered.'
ramayan::271.translation_literal: तथेति (so be it) / च (and) / अब्रुवन् (they said) / सर्वे (all) / मन्त्रिणः (ministers) / प्रत्यपूजयन् (showed respect) / पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य (of the king) / तत्-वाक्यम् (that speech) / यथा-आज्ञप्तम् (as ordered) / निशम्य (having heard) / ते (they)
ramayan::271.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::271.essence: A command becomes real only when others receive it fully.
ramayan::271.simple_meaning: The ministers hear Dasaratha's instructions and agree to carry them out with respect.
ramayan::271.simple_insight: Respectful agreement can move a plan forward without delay.
ramayan::271.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just given precise instructions for the sacrifice. The ministers listen carefully, honour his authority, and answer in unison. This is the moment the royal command becomes action.
ramayan::271.modern_relevance: A team hears the final decision in a meeting and immediately starts assigning tasks. The work begins the moment everyone stops debating and aligns.
ramayan::271.insight: It shows how clear authority and respectful response turn intention into execution.

ramayan::272.verse_sanskrit: तथा द्विजास्ते धर्मज्ञा वर्धयन्तो नृपोत्तमम् । अनुज्ञातास्ततस्सर्वे पुनर्जग्मुर्यथागतम् । । 1820 । ।
ramayan::272.verse_hindi: Bowing to this best of kings (Dasaratha), all the brahmins who were experts in austerities left all the knowledgeable brahmins as they camewith his permission.
ramayan::272.english_translation: Bowing to this best of kings, all the brahmins learned in sacred duty left with his permission, returning the way they had come.
ramayan::272.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / द्विजाः (the brahmins) / ते (they) / धर्मज्ञाः (knowers of sacred duty) / वर्धयन्तः (praising) / नृपोत्तमम् (the best of kings) / अनुज्ञाताः (having been permitted) / ततः (then) / सर्वे (all) / पुनः (again) / जग्मुः (went) / यथागतम् (as they had come)
ramayan::272.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::272.essence: Respect and permission close the meeting before action begins.
ramayan::272.simple_meaning: The brahmins respectfully praised Dasaratha and left after receiving his permission. It is a formal closing movement after the sacrifice has been arranged.
ramayan::272.simple_insight: Some moments are about proper closure: respect given, permission granted, everyone released.
ramayan::272.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just asked the priests to proceed with the sacrifice. The brahmins, skilled in sacred duty, honor him, receive his permission, and depart. The verse marks the orderly transition from consultation to action.
ramayan::272.modern_relevance: After a long meeting, everyone stands, nods, and leaves with the plan settled. Nothing dramatic changes — but the room has shifted from discussion to execution.
ramayan::272.insight: It marks the handoff from planning to ritual action, showing order, respect, and readiness.

ramayan::273.verse_hindi: After sending away the brahmins, the king said to his ministers: Let this sacrifice be performed as enjoined by scriptures and as directed by the officiating priests.
ramayan::273.english_translation: After sending away the brahmins, the king said to his ministers: Let this sacrifice be performed as enjoined by scripture and as directed by the officiating priests.
ramayan::273.translation_literal: विसर्जयित्वा (having sent away) / तान् (those) / विप्रान् (brahmins) / सचिवान् (ministers) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said) / ऋत्विग्भिः (by the officiating priests) / उपदिष्टः (instructed) / अयम् (this) / यथावत् (properly) / क्रतुः (sacrifice) / आप्यताम् (let it be performed)
ramayan::273.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::273.essence: Proper action begins with following the right instructions.
ramayan::273.simple_meaning: Dasharatha tells his ministers to carry out the sacrifice exactly as the priests have instructed.
ramayan::273.simple_insight: Right action becomes easier when you stop improvising and follow what is sound.
ramayan::273.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has just received the brahmins and ministers for a royal sacrifice. After the priests leave, he turns to his ministers and orders the rite to be performed exactly as prescribed. The verse is a procedural step in the larger setup.
ramayan::273.modern_relevance: You finally get the instructions for something important — a legal filing, a medical procedure, a ceremony — and the relief is in not winging it. Precision matters more than flair.
ramayan::273.insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to faithful execution of an established process.

ramayan::274.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा नृपशार्दूलस्सचिवान्समुपस्थितान् । विसर्जयित्वा स्वं वेश्म प्रविवेश महाद्युति: । । 1822 । ।
ramayan::274.verse_hindi: Having thus ordered his ministers sitting nearby, sent this highly brilliant, this
ramayan::274.english_translation: Having thus ordered his ministers who were seated nearby, the brilliant king dismissed them and entered his own palace.
ramayan::274.translation_literal: इति (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / नृपशार्दूलः (tiger among kings) / सचिवान् (ministers) / समुपस्थितान् (seated nearby) / विसर्जयित्वा (having dismissed) / स्वम् (his own) / वेश्म (palace) / प्रविवेश (entered) / महाद्युतिḥ (greatly radiant)
ramayan::274.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::274.essence: The king steps away from the court and toward the decision that will cost him everything.
ramayan::274.simple_meaning: The king finished speaking, dismissed his ministers, and went into his palace.
ramayan::274.simple_insight: Some moments are only the turning of a door, not the turning of a heart.
ramayan::274.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has just instructed the court about continuing the sacrifice properly. After sending the brahmins away, he dismisses the ministers too and goes back into his palace. The real decision will come next, when he turns from public order to private desire.
ramayan::274.modern_relevance: You leave a meeting with your team, still carrying the weight of what you have not said yet. The important conversation begins after the room empties.
ramayan::274.insight: It marks the shift from public instruction to the private choice that will shape the story.

ramayan::275.verse_sanskrit: ततस्स गत्वा ता:पत्नीर्नरेन्द्रो हृदयप्रिया: । उवाच दीक्षां विशत यक्ष्येऽहं सुतकारणात् । । 1823 । ।
ramayan::275.verse_hindi: Thereafter the king said to his dearest wives: I intend to perform a sacrifice in order to obtain sons. Therefore, you, too, commence religious discipline.
ramayan::275.english_translation: Thereafter the king said to his dearest wives: I intend to perform a sacrifice in order to obtain sons. Therefore, you, too, commence religious discipline.
ramayan::275.translation_literal: ततस् (thereafter) / गत्वा (having gone) / ता:पत्नी: (those wives) / नरेन्द्रः (the king) / हृदयप्रिया: (dear to his heart) / उवाच (said) / दीक्षाम् (ritual discipline) / विशत (enter) / यक्ष्ये (I will perform a sacrifice) / अहम् (I) / सुतकारणात् (for the sake of sons)
ramayan::275.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::275.essence: Even a king must ask for what he wants through discipline and sacrifice.
ramayan::275.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha tells his beloved wives that he will perform a sacrifice to seek sons, and asks them to observe the required discipline with him.
ramayan::275.simple_insight: Big desires often require shared restraint, not just private hope.
ramayan::275.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has just dismissed his ministers and gone to the women of the palace. He tells his beloved queens that the sacrifice for sons is about to begin, and they must also take up ritual discipline. This is the opening of a costly turning point.
ramayan::275.modern_relevance: You decide to try for something life-changing, and it immediately affects everyone close to you. The dream is private only in your mind; the discipline is shared.
ramayan::275.insight: It links desire to preparation, showing that serious aims require ordered action and participation from those around you.

ramayan::276.verse_sanskrit: तासां तेनातिकान्तेन वचनेन सुवर्चसाम् । मुखपद्मान्यशोभन्त पद्मानीव हिमात्यये । । 1824 । ।
ramayan::276.verse_hindi: On listening to these exceedingly charming words, their bright countenances shone resplendent like lotuses after the departure of winter.
ramayan::276.english_translation: On hearing those exceedingly charming words, their bright faces shone like lotuses after winter.
ramayan::276.translation_literal: तासाम् (of them) / तेन (by that) / अतिकान्तेन (exceedingly charming) / वचनेन (with words) / सुवर्चसाम् (of the radiant ones) / मुखपद्मानि (lotus-faces) / अशोभन्त (shone) / पद्मानीव (like lotuses) / हिमात्यये (at the end of winter)
ramayan::276.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::276.essence: Hope returns visibly when a longed-for promise is spoken.
ramayan::276.simple_meaning: The king's wives lit up with joy when they heard his beautiful words.
ramayan::276.simple_insight: Kind words can change the whole mood of a room.
ramayan::276.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has just told his beloved wives that he will perform a sacrifice to seek sons. This verse pauses on their reaction: their faces bloom with delight, like lotuses opening after winter, showing how deeply those words moved them.
ramayan::276.modern_relevance: You finally hear the words you were hoping for after a long, tense wait. Your face changes before you can even speak.
ramayan::276.insight: It draws attention to how reassurance and hope instantly soften fear and strain.

ramayan::277.verse_sanskrit: एतच्छ्रुत्वा रहस्सूतो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् । ऋत्विग्भिरुपदिष्टोऽयं पुरावृत्तो मया श्रुत: । । 191 । ।
ramayan::277.verse_hindi: The charioteer tells the king in privacy that he has heard the advice given by the offciating priests.
ramayan::277.english_translation: Hearing this, the charioteer spoke to the king in private: I have heard this ancient account from the priests who performed the rite.
ramayan::277.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / रहस्सूतो (the charioteer in private) / राजानम् (to the king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / ऋत्विग्भिः (by the officiating priests) / उपदिष्टः (instructed) / अयम् (this) / पुरावृत्तः (ancient account) / मया (by me) / श्रुतः (heard)
ramayan::277.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::277.essence: Private testimony begins the next turn in the story.
ramayan::277.simple_meaning: The charioteer privately tells the king that he has heard an old account from the priests.
ramayan::277.simple_insight: Some truths arrive first as private reports before they become public reality.
ramayan::277.detailed_meaning: In the royal court, a charioteer speaks quietly to the king after the priests have spoken. He is not teaching a principle or making a promise; he is passing on an old account that will lead into the next revelation about the king's future children.
ramayan::277.modern_relevance: You hear a rumor in confidence before anyone else does. It may seem small, but it can change how you understand everything that follows.
ramayan::277.insight: It shifts attention from the speaker's certainty to the chain of testimony behind the message.

ramayan::278.verse_sanskrit: सनत्कुमारो भगवान्पूर्वं कथितवान्कथाम् । ऋषीणां सन्निधौ राजन् तव पुत्रागमं प्रति । । 192 । ।
ramayan::278.verse_hindi: O king, the divine Sanatkumara had narrated a story about your posterity in the presence of sages.
ramayan::278.english_translation: O king, the divine Sanatkumara had narrated a story about your posterity in the presence of sages.
ramayan::278.translation_literal: सनत्कुमारः (Sanatkumara) / भगवान् (the divine one) / पूर्वम् (formerly) / कथितवान् (had narrated) / कथााम् (a story) / ऋषीणाम् (of sages) / सन्निधौ (in the presence) / राजन् (O king) / तव (your) / पुत्रागमम् (the coming of your son) / प्रति (regarding)
ramayan::278.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::278.essence: An old prophecy is being recalled, not fulfilled yet.
ramayan::278.simple_meaning: Sanatkumara once spoke before the sages about a future event in the king's family.
ramayan::278.simple_insight: Some futures are known first as stories, not events.
ramayan::278.detailed_meaning: A court conversation is unfolding around an old prophecy. The charioteer is explaining to the king that Sanatkumara had already spoken of the coming child in a gathering of sages. This verse only introduces the source of the prophecy.
ramayan::278.modern_relevance: A family elder repeats a story that everyone treats as meaningful, even before the promised event has arrived.
ramayan::278.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the tradition that foretells it.

ramayan::279.verse_sanskrit: काश्यपस्यतु पुत्रोऽस्ति विभण्डक इति श्रुत: । ऋष्यशृङ्ग इति ख्यातस्तस्य पुत्रो भविष्यति । । 193 । ।
ramayan::279.verse_hindi: Kasyapa has a famous son named Vibhandaka. It was prophesied that he would have a son named Rsyasringa.
ramayan::279.english_translation: Kasyapa has a famous son named Vibhandaka. It was prophesied that he would have a son named Rsyasringa.
ramayan::279.translation_literal: काश्यपस्य (of Kasyapa) / तु (but) / पुत्रः (son) / अस्ति (is) / विभण्डकः (Vibhandaka) / इति (thus) / श्रुतः (heard of) / ऋष्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / इति (thus) / ख्यातः (known as) / तस्य (his) / पुत्रः (son) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::279.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::279.essence: A future figure is introduced through ancestry, not action.
ramayan::279.simple_meaning: A sage named Vibhandaka is mentioned as the son of Kasyapa, and a son named Rsyasringa is foretold for him.
ramayan::279.simple_insight: Some stories begin with ancestry and prophecy before the person ever appears.
ramayan::279.detailed_meaning: The charioteer is recounting an old prophetic story to the king. After Sanatkumara's words, he names Vibhandaka and the son destined to be born to him, Rsyasringa. The verse is a bridge, not the main point.
ramayan::279.modern_relevance: A family conversation starts with, “Your child’s teacher mentioned something important,” and suddenly the whole room leans in. This verse is that kind of setup — a name, a lineage, a future already taking shape.
ramayan::279.insight: It prepares the listener for a larger story by placing the next character inside a prophetic lineage.

ramayan::280.verse_sanskrit: स वने नित्यसंवृद्धो मुनिर्वनचरस्सदा । नान्यं जानाति विप्रेन्द्रो नित्यं पित्रनुवर्तनात् । । 194 । ।
ramayan::280.verse_hindi: Grown up in the forest and always moving with his father, that sage knows none other than his father.
ramayan::280.english_translation: Grown up in the forest and always moving with his father, that sage knows none other than his father.
ramayan::280.translation_literal: सः (he) / वने (in the forest) / नित्यसंवृद्धः (always raised) / मुनिः (sage) / वनचरः (forest-dwelling) / सदा (always) / न (not) / अन्यम् (another) / जानाति (knows) / विप्रेन्द्रः (best among sages) / नित्यम् (always) / पित्रनुवर्तनात् (because of following his father)
ramayan::280.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::280.essence: His world is so narrow that his father is all he knows.
ramayan::280.simple_meaning: He has been raised in the forest, always with his father, so he knows no other way of life.
ramayan::280.simple_insight: A life shaped too narrowly can leave you unable to see beyond the first bond you know.
ramayan::280.detailed_meaning: Rama’s story is being set up through the birth and upbringing of Rishyasringa. After the prophecy about his future, this verse explains his unusual isolation: he has grown up in the forest, always following his father, and has never known the wider world. That detail matters for the next step in the plan.
ramayan::280.modern_relevance: A child who has only known one household, one routine, one voice can reach adulthood with no map for anything else. The verse quietly shows how environment shapes awareness.
ramayan::280.insight: It shifts attention from character alone to the conditions that formed that character.

ramayan::281.verse_sanskrit: द्वैविध्यं ब्रह्मचर्यस्य भविष्यति महात्मन: । लोकेषु प्रथितं राजन्विप्रैश्च कथितं सदा । । 195 । ।
ramayan::281.verse_hindi: O eminent king, sage Rsyasringa celebrated in the three worlds who practises a twofold brahmacharya life (life of celebacy) described by brahmins (as vratitva and prajapatya).
ramayan::281.english_translation: O eminent king, sage Rsyasringa will be known for a twofold life of brahmacharya, praised by the learned in the world.
ramayan::281.translation_literal: द्वैविध्यम् (twofold nature) / ब्रह्मचर्यस्य (of brahmacharya) / भविष्यति (will be) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / लोकेषु (in the worlds) / प्रथितम् (well-known) / राजन् (O king) / विप्रैः (by the learned) / च (and) / कथितम् (spoken) / सदा (always)
ramayan::281.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::281.essence: His discipline is so complete it becomes his identity.
ramayan::281.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa is described as living a rare, disciplined life of celibacy that is widely respected.
ramayan::281.simple_insight: Some lives are defined by restraint, not by display.
ramayan::281.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing Rsyasringa before his story unfolds. Raised in isolation with his father, he becomes known for an unusual, highly disciplined form of brahmacharya. This verse sets up his character, not a teaching by itself.
ramayan::281.modern_relevance: A child raised inside one narrow routine may grow into an adult whose whole life is shaped by that single pattern. Before anything dramatic happens, the habit is already deciding the person.
ramayan::281.insight: It frames character as something formed by long restraint, not sudden choice.

ramayan::282.verse_sanskrit: तस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य कालस्समभिवर्तत । अग्निं शुश्रूषमाणस्य पितरं च यशस्विनम् । । 196 । ।
ramayan::282.verse_hindi: Worshipping the firegod and attending on his renowned father, he will spend a long time living in this manner (practising vratitva mode of brahmacharya).
ramayan::282.english_translation: While he lived like this, time passed for him, serving the fire and his renowned father.
ramayan::282.translation_literal: तस्य (for him) / एवम् (thus) / वर्तमानस्य (while living) / कालः (time) / समभिवर्तत (passed by) / अग्निम् (the fire) / शुश्रूषमाणस्य (serving) / पितरम् (father) / च (and) / यशस्विनम् (renowned) /
ramayan::282.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::282.essence: A life can be formed quietly by repeated duty and ritual care.
ramayan::282.simple_meaning: Time passed while the young sage kept serving the sacred fire and his respected father.
ramayan::282.simple_insight: A life of steady service can quietly become a whole character.
ramayan::282.detailed_meaning: Rishyashringa is being described in the forest, still bound to his father and to ritual discipline. This verse simply marks the passing of time while he continues that sheltered, devoted way of life, before the larger story turns toward Romapada.
ramayan::282.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for the same small duties every day, and only later do you realize they shaped you.
ramayan::282.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the slow formation of a person through repeated service.

ramayan::283.verse_sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रोमपाद: प्रतापवान् । अङ्गेषु प्रथितो राजा भविष्यति महाबल: । । 197 । ।
ramayan::283.verse_hindi: At this time a powerful king Romapada, mighty and celebrated would be living in the country of Anga.
ramayan::283.english_translation: At this time, the powerful king Romapada, mighty and renowned, would be ruling in Anga.
ramayan::283.translation_literal: एतस्मिन् (at this) / एव (indeed) / काले (time) / तु (but) / रोमपादः (Romapada) / प्रतापवान् (powerful) / अङ्गेषु (in Anga) / प्रथितः (renowned) / राजा (king) / भविष्यति (will be) / महाबलः (mighty)
ramayan::283.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::283.essence: A king is introduced because his future mistake will drive the plot.
ramayan::283.simple_meaning: Romapada, the powerful and famous king of Anga, will be ruling at that time.
ramayan::283.simple_insight: A ruler is introduced because the next events depend on his place in the story.
ramayan::283.detailed_meaning: The scene shifts from Rsyasringa’s disciplined life to the wider world around him. Valmiki names Romapada, the king of Anga, because his rule and later mistake will shape the coming crisis.
ramayan::283.modern_relevance: A story pauses to name the person whose decision will change everything. Sometimes the real turning point is not the event itself, but who has the power to set it in motion.
ramayan::283.insight: It frames the next episode around a ruler whose actions will have consequences beyond his own court.

ramayan::284.verse_sanskrit: तस्य व्यतिक्रमाद्राज्ञो भविष्यति सुदारुणा । अनावृष्टिस्सुघोरा वै सर्वभूतभयावहा । । 198 । ।
ramayan::284.verse_hindi: Because of violation of code of conduct by the king, a terrible, dreadful drought frightening all living beings will set in the kingdom.
ramayan::284.english_translation: Because of the king's breach of conduct, a terrible, dreadful drought will arise, frightening all living beings.
ramayan::284.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / व्यतिक्रमात् (because of transgression) / राज्ञः (of the king) / भविष्यति (will become) / सुदारुणा (very terrible) / अनावृष्टिः (drought) / सुघोरा (dreadful) / वै (indeed) / सर्वभूतभयावहा (bringing fear to all beings)
ramayan::284.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::284.essence: A ruler's breach can turn into suffering for everyone.
ramayan::284.simple_meaning: When a king breaks righteous conduct, the whole kingdom suffers. His failure does not stay private; it turns into fear and hardship for everyone.
ramayan::284.simple_insight: Your choices are never as private as they seem.
ramayan::284.detailed_meaning: In the early Ayodhya story, Valmiki explains why a drought will strike Anga. King Romapada's lapse in conduct disturbs the moral order, and the land itself begins to suffer. The verse shows how a ruler's actions can affect every life under him.
ramayan::284.modern_relevance: A manager cuts corners on safety, and the whole team starts living with the fallout. One person's breach of responsibility can quietly poison an entire system.
ramayan::284.insight: It shifts attention from personal convenience to the wider consequences of broken responsibility.

ramayan::285.verse_sanskrit: अनावृष्ट्यां तु वृत्तायां राजा दु:खसमन्वित: । ब्राह्मणान्श्रुतवृद्धांश्च समानीय प्रवक्ष्यति । । 199 । ।
ramayan::285.verse_hindi: With drought prevailing, the griefstricken king, would summon all those grown old with learning and tell them.
ramayan::285.english_translation: With drought prevailing, the grief-stricken king would summon the Brahmins who were old in learning and speak to them.
ramayan::285.translation_literal: अनावृष्ट्यां (in drought) / तु (indeed) / वृत्तायां (having arisen, having prevailed) / राजा (the king) / दुःखसमन्वितः (accompanied by grief) / ब्राह्मणान् (the Brahmins) / श्रुतवृद्धान् (grown old in learning) / च (and) / समानीय (having brought together) / प्रवक्ष्यति (will speak)
ramayan::285.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::285.essence: Grief makes the king turn to wisdom before acting.
ramayan::285.simple_meaning: The king, distressed by the drought, gathers learned elders and asks them for guidance.
ramayan::285.simple_insight: When a crisis goes beyond your control, wisdom begins with seeking counsel.
ramayan::285.detailed_meaning: Romapada has already been told that a terrible drought has fallen because of a breach of conduct. Now, overwhelmed by grief, he gathers the elders most respected for learning so they can advise him on what to do next.
ramayan::285.insight: It shifts the response from panic to consultation: when the problem is larger than you, seek wise guidance.

ramayan::286.verse_sanskrit: भवन्तश्श्रुतधर्माणो लोकचारित्रवेदिन: । समादिशन्तु नियमं प्रायश्चित्तं यथा भवेत् । । 1910 । ।
ramayan::286.verse_hindi: भवन्तश्श्रुतधर्माणो लोकचारित्रवेदिन: । समादिशन्तु नियमं प्रायश्चित्तं यथा भवेत् । । 1910 । ।
ramayan::286.english_translation: You who know dharma and understand the ways of the world, please instruct us in the rule and the penance that will restore order.
ramayan::286.translation_literal: भवन्तः (you, esteemed ones) / श्रुतधर्माणः (those who have heard dharma) / लोकचारित्रवेदिनः (knowers of worldly conduct) / समादिशन्तु (may instruct) / नियमम् (the rule) / प्रायश्चित्तम् (the expiation) / यथा (how) / भवेत् (it may be)
ramayan::286.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::286.essence: Wrongdoing is repaired by asking how to make amends.
ramayan::286.simple_meaning: The king asks learned elders to explain the proper rule and the corrective act needed to restore balance after wrongdoing.
ramayan::286.simple_insight: Repair begins by asking wise people how to make things right.
ramayan::286.detailed_meaning: A drought has struck because the king has broken moral order. He gathers elder brahmins who know dharma and social conduct, and asks them to prescribe the right rule and penance. This moment shows humility before correction.
ramayan::286.modern_relevance: You realize you’ve messed up, and your first instinct is to defend yourself. Instead, you call the one person who will tell you the truth about how to repair the damage.
ramayan::286.insight: It shifts you from self-justification to seeking precise correction from the wise.

ramayan::287.verse_sanskrit: वक्ष्यन्ति ते महीपालं ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगा: । विभण्डकसुतं राजन्सर्वोपायैरिहानय । । 1911 । ।
ramayan::287.verse_hindi: Those brahmins versed in the Vedas, said, to O king bring here Rsyasringa, son of the sage Vibhandaka by all means.
ramayan::287.english_translation: Those brahmins, well-versed in the Vedas, said to the king: O king, bring here by every means Rsyasringa, the son of Vibhandaka.
ramayan::287.translation_literal: वक्ष्यन्ति (they will say) / ते (to you) / महीपालं (to the king) / ब्राह्मणा (the brahmins) / वेदपारगा: (those who have crossed to the far side of the Vedas) / विभण्डकसुतं (the son of Vibhandaka) / राजन् (O king) / सर्वोपायैः (by all means) / इह (here) / आनय (bring)
ramayan::287.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::287.essence: The crisis now demands the one person who can unlock the next step.
ramayan::287.simple_meaning: The learned brahmins advise the king to bring Rsyasringa to him by any means necessary.
ramayan::287.simple_insight: Sometimes a hard problem needs a practical solution, not hesitation.
ramayan::287.detailed_meaning: A drought has struck the kingdom, and the king has already gathered wise brahmins to find a remedy. They now point to one crucial step: bring Rsyasringa, the son of Vibhandaka, to the palace so the larger plan can begin.
ramayan::287.modern_relevance: The team has exhausted theory, the deadline is close, and one missing person can still change everything. You stop debating and go get the right help.
ramayan::287.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract concern to decisive action.

ramayan::288.verse_sanskrit: आनाय्य च महीपाल ऋश्यशृङ्गं सुसत्कृतम् । प्रयच्छ कन्यां शान्तां वै विधिना सुसमाहित: । । 1912 । ।
ramayan::288.verse_hindi: O monarch, on having brought Rsyasringa here, honour him, and offer him your daughter Santa with due reverence.
ramayan::288.english_translation: O monarch, on having brought Rsyasringa here, honour him, and offer him your daughter Santa with due reverence.
ramayan::288.translation_literal: आनाय्य (having brought) / च (and) / महीपाल (O king) / ऋश्यशृङ्गं (Rsyasringa) / सुसत्कृतम् (well-honoured) / प्रयच्छ (offer) / कन्याम् (daughter) / शान्ताम् (Santa) / वै (indeed) / विधिना (with proper ritual) / सुसमाहितः (with careful attention)
ramayan::288.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::288.essence: Respect and ritual matter when a kingdom depends on the outcome.
ramayan::288.simple_meaning: Bring Rsyasringa here, honour him properly, and then give him Santa with full ritual care.
ramayan::288.simple_insight: A sacred union is being arranged through respect, not haste.
ramayan::288.detailed_meaning: The brahmins advise the king on how to bring Rsyasringa to the court and complete the marriage properly. This is part of a larger plan to secure a blessing for the kingdom, so the verse functions as a practical instruction within the sequence.
ramayan::288.modern_relevance: A family sits around a table planning a difficult alliance, and every detail matters. The right approach is not force, but care, timing, and respect.
ramayan::288.insight: It shifts attention from desire to the proper method of carrying out a serious commitment.

ramayan::289.verse_sanskrit: तेषां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा चिन्तां प्रपत्स्यते । केनोपायेन वै शक्य इहानेतुं स वीर्यवान् । । 1913 । ।
ramayan::289.verse_hindi: On hearing their words, the king in a thoughtful mood said, How can the mighty sage be brought here?
ramayan::289.english_translation: On hearing their words, the king fell into thought: How can that mighty sage be brought here?
ramayan::289.translation_literal: तेषाम् (their) / तु (indeed) / वचनम् (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राजा (the king) / चिन्ताम् (thought/anxiety) / प्रपत्स्यते (falls into) / केन (by what) / उपायेन (means) / वै (indeed) / शक्यः (possible) / इह (here) / आनेतुम् (to bring) / सः (that) / वीर्यवान् (mighty one) ।
ramayan::289.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::289.essence: A command becomes real only when you face the cost of carrying it out.
ramayan::289.simple_meaning: The king hears the request and immediately wonders how such a powerful sage could be brought there.
ramayan::289.simple_insight: Big outcomes often begin with one hard question: how will this actually happen?
ramayan::289.detailed_meaning: The brahmins have just told the king to bring Rishyashringa and honour him properly. Hearing this, the king turns inward and starts weighing the problem. The verse shows the first stir of planning before the mission begins.
ramayan::289.modern_relevance: You get a message that sounds simple: make it happen. Then reality hits — the person, the timing, the constraints. The real work starts when you ask how.
ramayan::289.insight: It shifts the mind from receiving a demand to planning a workable response.

ramayan::290.verse_sanskrit: ततो राजा विनिश्चित्य सह मन्त्रिभिरात्मवान् । पुरोहितममात्यांश्च तत: प्रेष्यति सत्कृतान् । । 1914 । ।
ramayan::290.verse_hindi: Thereafter the confident king, having decided, in consultation with his ministers to bring him (Rsyasringa), sent the priest with the counsellors on this mission.
ramayan::290.english_translation: Thereafter the confident king, having decided with his ministers, sent the honoured priest and counsellors on this mission.
ramayan::290.translation_literal: ततः (thereafter) / राजा (the king) / विनिश्चित्य (having firmly decided) / सह (with) / मन्त्रिभिः (ministers) / आत्मवान् (self-possessed) / पुरोहितम् (the priest) / अमात्यान् (counsellors) / च (and) / ततः (then) / प्रेष्यति (sends) / सत्कृतान् (honoured)
ramayan::290.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::290.essence: Decision becomes real only when you send someone to act.
ramayan::290.simple_meaning: The king makes a clear decision with his ministers and sends trusted officials to carry it out.
ramayan::290.simple_insight: A hard plan becomes real only when someone finally acts on it.
ramayan::290.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has already heard how Rsyasringa might be brought to Ayodhya. After weighing the matter with his ministers, he stops hesitating and sends the priest and counsellors on the mission with respect.
ramayan::290.modern_relevance: You have talked the idea through enough. The real shift comes when you assign people, name the task, and let the plan leave the room.
ramayan::290.insight: It moves the mind from anxious discussion to decisive delegation.

ramayan::291.verse_sanskrit: ते तु राज्ञो वचश्श्रुशृत्वा व्यथिता विनतानना: । न गच्छेम ऋषेर्भीता अनुनेष्यन्ति तं नृपम् । । 1915 । ।
ramayan::291.verse_hindi: On hearing the kings words, distressed and frightened by rishis power, they   appealed to the king, faces bent down, We will not go.
ramayan::291.english_translation: On hearing the king's words, distressed and frightened by the sage's power, they bowed their faces and said, "We will not go."
ramayan::291.translation_literal: ते (they) / तु (indeed) / राज्ञः (of the king) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / व्यथिता (distressed) / विनताननाः (with bowed faces) / न (not) / गच्छेम (we will go) / ऋषेः (of the sage) / भीताः (afraid) / अनुनेष्यन्ति (they will appease / persuade) / तं (him) / नृपम् (the king)
ramayan::291.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::291.essence: Fear makes the messengers refuse the task before they begin.
ramayan::291.simple_meaning: The king's messengers are shaken by the sage's power and refuse to go.
ramayan::291.simple_insight: Fear can stop action before it even begins.
ramayan::291.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha wants the sage Rishyasringa brought to Ayodhya. His messengers hear the order, bow their heads, and admit they are too afraid of the sage's power to go.
ramayan::291.modern_relevance: You get the assignment, then feel your stomach drop because the person involved has a reputation that makes everyone cautious.
ramayan::291.insight: It shows how awe and fear can block even a royal command.

ramayan::292.verse_sanskrit: वक्ष्यन्ति चिन्तयित्वा ते तस्योपायांश्च तत्क्षमान् । आनेष्यामो वयं विप्रं न च दोषो भविष्यति । । 1916 । ।
ramayan::292.verse_hindi: After thinking  about the means to be employed to bring the rishi to the court, they told him they would bring the sage if they are not to blame (in case anything untoward
ramayan::292.english_translation: After thinking over the proper means to bring the sage, they said, "We will bring the Brahmin, and no blame will fall on us."
ramayan::292.translation_literal: वक्ष्यन्ति (they will say) / चिन्तयित्वा (having thought) / ते (they) / तस्य (for that) / उपायान् (means) / च (and) / तत्क्षमान् (proper, suitable) / आनेष्यामः (we will bring) / वयम् (we) / विप्रम् (the Brahmin/sage) / न (not) / च (and) / दोषः (blame) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::292.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::292.essence: They want the result, but not the blame.
ramayan::292.simple_meaning: They quietly worked out a plan to bring the sage to court while avoiding blame themselves.
ramayan::292.simple_insight: A risky plan feels safer when responsibility is pushed away from yourself.
ramayan::292.detailed_meaning: King of Anga has decided to bring Rishyashringa to his court so rain can return. His messengers, frightened by the sage's power, first hesitate, then weigh the safest method. This verse shows their cautious plotting before the actual abduction.
ramayan::292.modern_relevance: You and your team keep circling a hard decision, looking for a way to make it happen without anyone being held responsible.
ramayan::292.insight: It shows how fear makes people seek action with zero accountability.

ramayan::293.verse_sanskrit: एवमङ्गाधिपेनैव गणिकाभि: ऋषेस्सुत: । आनीतोऽवर्षयद्देवश्शान्ता चास्मै प्रदीयते । । 1917 । ।
ramayan::293.verse_hindi: Thus with the help of courtesans of the king of Anga, when the son of the sage (Rsyasringa) was brought rains followed. The king offered his daughter Santa (in marriage to the sage).
ramayan::293.english_translation: Thus, by the king of Anga's courtesans, the sage's son was brought there, the rains came, and Shanta was given to him in marriage.
ramayan::293.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / अङ्गाधिपेन (by the king of Anga) / एव (indeed) / गणिकाभिः (by courtesans) / ऋषेः (of the sage) / सुतः (son) / आनीतः (brought) / अवर्षयत् (caused rain to fall) / देवः (the deity) / शान्ता (Shanta) / च (and) / अस्मै (to him) / प्रदीयते (was given)
ramayan::293.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::293.essence: A kingdom changes when the right person finally arrives.
ramayan::293.simple_meaning: The king of Anga used courtesans to bring Rishyasringa to his court. His arrival brought rain, and Shanta was given to him as a wife.
ramayan::293.simple_insight: A single hidden plan can change a kingdom's future.
ramayan::293.detailed_meaning: Rama's story pauses to explain how King Dasharatha secured Rishyasringa. The king of Anga sent courtesans to bring the sage's son away from his forest life. Once he arrived, rain returned, and Shanta was offered to him.
ramayan::293.modern_relevance: A family problem, a stalled project, and then one careful introduction changes everything. Some outcomes arrive only after the right person is brought into the right place.
ramayan::293.insight: It shows how a strategic move can restore order and set a larger plan in motion.

ramayan::294.verse_sanskrit: ऋश्यशृङ्गस्तु जामाता पुत्रांस्तव विधास्यति । सनत्कुमारकथितमेतावद्व्याहृतं मया । । 1918 । ।
ramayan::294.verse_hindi: Risyasringa, your soninlaw, would help you to obtain sons. Thus said Sanathkumara which I have related to you.
ramayan::294.english_translation: Rsyasringa, your son-in-law, will help you obtain sons. Thus I have repeated what Sanatkumara said.
ramayan::294.translation_literal: ऋश्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / तु (indeed) / जामाता (son-in-law) / पुत्रान् (sons) / तव (your) / विधास्यति (will cause to be obtained) / सनत्कुमारकथितम् (spoken by Sanatkumara) / एतावत् (thus much) / व्याहृतम् (said) / मया (by me)
ramayan::294.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::294.essence: The key help has been named, but the explanation is still unfolding.
ramayan::294.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa is said to be the one who will help Dasaratha get sons. The speaker is only reporting what Sanatkumara had already said.
ramayan::294.simple_insight: Some verses simply move the story forward without carrying the teaching themselves.
ramayan::294.detailed_meaning: The sage is explaining to Dasaratha how the childless king can gain sons. Rsyasringa has just been introduced as the crucial means, but this line is only a report of earlier words, not the heart of the exchange.
ramayan::294.modern_relevance: A friend repeats a message from someone else: the useful part is still ahead, and this line only points toward it.
ramayan::294.insight: It marks a narrative handoff, not a self-contained lesson.

ramayan::295.verse_sanskrit: अथ हृष्टो दशरथस्सुमन्त्रं प्रत्यभाषत । यथर्श्यशृङ्गस्त्वानीतो विस्तरेण त्वयोच्यताम् । । 1919 । ।
ramayan::295.verse_hindi: Thereupon Dasaratha, pleased, (with him), said to Sumantra, Describe in detail the  means by which Rsyasringa was brought (to the court of Romapada).
ramayan::295.english_translation: Thereupon Dasaratha, pleased, said to Sumantra, "Describe in detail the means by which Rsyasringa was brought to the court of Romapada."
ramayan::295.translation_literal: अथ (thereupon) / हृष्टः (pleased) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / सुमन्त्रम् (to Sumantra) / प्रत्यभाषत (spoke in reply) / यथा (how) / ऋश्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / तु (indeed) / आनीतः (was brought) / विस्तरेण (in detail) / त्वया (by you) / उच्यताम् (let it be told)
ramayan::295.speaker: Dasaratha
ramayan::295.essence: Curiosity follows success and asks how it was made possible.
ramayan::295.simple_meaning: Dasaratha asks Sumantra to explain exactly how Rsyasringa was brought to Romapada's court.
ramayan::295.simple_insight: Sometimes the next step is simply to ask for the full story.
ramayan::295.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just heard that Rsyasringa's arrival brought rain and helped fulfill a larger royal purpose. Pleased, he turns to Sumantra and asks for the full account of how the sage was brought to Romapada's court. The verse is a bridge, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::295.modern_relevance: You hear a partial solution and immediately want the full sequence behind it. Before acting, you ask: how did this actually happen?
ramayan::295.insight: It shifts attention from the result to the method that produced it.

ramayan::296.verse_sanskrit: सुमन्त्रश्चोदितो राज्ञा प्रोवाचेदं वचस्तदा । यथर्श्यशृङ्गस्त्वानीत श्श्रुणु मे मन्त्रिभिस्सह । । 1101 । ।
ramayan::296.verse_hindi: Thus prompted by king Dasaratha, Sumantra said,  I shall relate to you the manner in which Rsyasringa was brought to the court. Listen to me along with your ministers.
ramayan::296.english_translation: Thus prompted by king Dasaratha, Sumantra said, "I shall relate to you the manner in which Rsyasringa was brought to the court. Listen to me along with your ministers."
ramayan::296.translation_literal: सुमन्त्रः (Sumantra) / चोदितः (prompted) / राज्ञा (by the king) / प्रोवाच (spoke) / इदम् (this) / वचः (speech) / तदा (then) / यथा (how) / ऋश्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / त्वा (to you) / आनीतः (was brought) / शृणु (listen) / मे (to me) / मन्त्रिभिः (with the ministers) / सह (together)
ramayan::296.speaker: Sumantra
ramayan::296.essence: The story is about to explain itself.
ramayan::296.simple_meaning: Sumantra begins to explain how Rsyasringa was brought to the court, asking Dasaratha and the ministers to listen.
ramayan::296.simple_insight: Some moments are only the doorway to the real story.
ramayan::296.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just asked how Rsyasringa was brought to help secure sons. Sumantra answers by preparing to recount the whole plan to the king and his ministers. The verse only opens the explanation; it does not yet give the teaching or outcome.
ramayan::296.modern_relevance: A meeting starts with, “Let me explain how we got here,” and everyone leans in. This verse is that opening move — the setup before the actual story begins.
ramayan::296.insight: It frames the next verses as explanation, not conclusion, so the reader waits for the full account.

ramayan::297.verse_hindi: The priest accompanied by ministers said to Romapada, We have thought over a plan which will never fail.
ramayan::297.english_translation: The priest, along with the ministers, said to Romapada, "We have thought of a plan that cannot fail."
ramayan::297.translation_literal: रोमपादम् (to Romapada) / उवाच (said) / इदम् (this) / सहामात्यः (together with ministers) / पुरोहितः (the priest) / उपायः (plan / means) / निरपायः (without failure) / अयम् (this) / अस्माभिः (by us) / अभिचिन्तितः (well-considered)
ramayan::297.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::297.essence: A workable plan has been found, but it is only the opening move.
ramayan::297.simple_meaning: The priest and ministers tell Romapada they have devised a plan they believe will work.
ramayan::297.simple_insight: Big outcomes often begin with one careful plan shared at the right moment.
ramayan::297.detailed_meaning: Romapada is being told that his advisers have found a way forward. This is not the solution itself, only the announcement of one. The real plan will be explained in the next verses, so this line serves as setup.
ramayan::297.modern_relevance: A team gathers after hours around a table, and someone finally says, "We found a way." The relief is real, but the work is still ahead.
ramayan::297.insight: It shifts attention from uncertainty to the first credible path forward.

ramayan::298.verse_sanskrit: ऋश्यशृङ्गो वनचरस्तपस्स्वाध्ययने रत: । अनभिज्ञस्स नारीणां विषयाणां सुखस्य च । 1103 । ।
ramayan::298.verse_hindi: Rsyasringa, residing in the forest, is engrossed in the study of the Vedas. He is not acquainted with women and sensual pleasures.
ramayan::298.english_translation: Rsyasringa, dwelling in the forest, is devoted to austerity and Vedic study. He knows nothing of women or sensual pleasures.
ramayan::298.translation_literal: ऋश्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / वनचरः (forest-dwelling) / तपः-स्वाध्याय-रतः (devoted to austerity and study) / अनभिज्ञः (unaware) / सः (he) / नारीणाम् (of women) / विषयाणाम् (of sensual objects) / सुखस्य (of pleasure) / च (and)
ramayan::298.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::298.essence: His innocence is exactly what makes him easy to lure.
ramayan::298.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa lives in the forest, focused on austerity and study, and has no experience of women or sensual pleasure.
ramayan::298.simple_insight: A sheltered mind can be guided easily by whatever it has never learned to resist.
ramayan::298.detailed_meaning: Romapada's ministers are building a plan to bring Rsyasringa to the kingdom. Before they explain the trap, they describe him: a forest-dweller devoted to discipline, untouched by ordinary temptations. That innocence is what makes him vulnerable.
ramayan::298.modern_relevance: Someone raised far from your world can be influenced by what feels ordinary to you. The verse shows how innocence becomes a weakness when others know exactly how to use it.
ramayan::298.insight: It sets up a strategy based on exploiting ignorance rather than strength.

ramayan::299.verse_hindi: By means of  such things that can cause sensual pleasures and overpower the minds of men, we shall be able to bring him to the town. Let it be decided quickly (said the ministers)
ramayan::299.english_translation: By means of such things that can cause sensual pleasures and overpower the minds of men, we shall be able to bring him to the town. Let it be decided quickly.
ramayan::299.translation_literal: इन्द्रियार्थैः (by objects of the senses) / अभिमतैः (pleasing, desired) / नरचित्तप्रमाथिभिः (that disturb men's minds) / पुरम् (to the town) / आनाययिष्यामः (we shall bring) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / च (and) / अध्यवसीयताम् (let it be decided)
ramayan::299.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::299.essence: Pleasure can move the mind faster than reason.
ramayan::299.simple_meaning: The ministers plan to lure Rsyasringa into the town using tempting pleasures that can disturb a man's mind.
ramayan::299.simple_insight: Temptation can be used like a tool, but it also reveals how easily the mind can be led.
ramayan::299.detailed_meaning: Romapada's ministers have found a way to bring Rsyasringa out of the forest. Knowing he has never known women or sensual pleasure, they plan to use attractive delights to draw him into the town. This verse is one step in that scheme, not the whole teaching.
ramayan::299.modern_relevance: A team decides to use every flattering feature, free trial, and polished distraction to pull someone in. The method works because desire moves the mind before judgment catches up.
ramayan::299.insight: It shifts attention to how desire can bypass discernment and steer behavior before reflection begins.

ramayan::300.verse_sanskrit: गणिकास्तत्र गच्छन्तु रूपवत्यस्स्वलङ्कृता: । प्रलोभ्य विविधोपायैरानेष्यन्तीह सत्कृता: । । 1105 । ।
ramayan::300.verse_hindi: Beautiful and welladorned courtesans, may be sent there. They will allure him by various means and honourably bring him here.
ramayan::300.english_translation: Beautiful and well-adorned courtesans should go there. By various means they will tempt him and respectfully bring him here.
ramayan::300.translation_literal: गणिकाः (courtesans) / तत्र (there) / गच्छन्तु (may go) / रूपवत्यः (beautiful) / स्स्वलङ्कृताः (well-adorned) / प्रलोभ्य (having tempted) / विविधोपायैः (by various means) / आनेष्यन्ति (they will bring) / इह (here) / सत्कृताः (honourably treated)
ramayan::300.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::300.essence: A pure mind is being targeted through temptation.
ramayan::300.simple_meaning: The plan is to send attractive, well-dressed courtesans to tempt Rishyashringa and bring him to the city.
ramayan::300.simple_insight: Desire is being used as a tool, not as a feeling.
ramayan::300.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha's advisers are trying to bring Rishyashringa from the forest. After noting his innocence and inexperience, they propose using beautiful courtesans to lure him into Ayodhya so the sacrifice can proceed.
ramayan::300.modern_relevance: A team in a conference room starts talking about influence tactics instead of honesty. The goal is clear, but the method is calculated and manipulative.
ramayan::300.insight: It shows how a plan can succeed by exploiting weakness rather than meeting someone directly.

ramayan::301.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तथेति राजा च प्रत्युवाच पुरोहितम् । पुरोहितो मन्त्रिणश्च तथा चक्रुश्च ते तदा । । 1106 । ।
ramayan::301.verse_hindi: The king, having listened to these words, conveyed his approval saying, Let it be done that way. The priests and ministers acted accordingly.
ramayan::301.english_translation: The king, having listened to these words, conveyed his approval saying, "Let it be done that way." The priests and ministers acted accordingly.
ramayan::301.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तथा इति (so, thus) / राजा (the king) / च (and) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / पुरोहितम् (to the priest) / पुरोहितः (the priest) / मन्त्रिणः (the ministers) / च (and) / तथा (likewise) / चक्रुः (did) / च (and) / ते (they) / तदा (then)
ramayan::301.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::301.essence: Approval turns a scheme into action.
ramayan::301.simple_meaning: The king agrees to the plan, and his priests and ministers carry it out at once.
ramayan::301.simple_insight: Some harmful plans move forward simply because authority approves them.
ramayan::301.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just heard a scheme to lure the sage with tempting women. He gives the order, and his priests and ministers immediately obey. The verse is a brief hinge between planning and action, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::301.modern_relevance: A manager nods at a bad idea in a meeting, and the whole room starts executing it before anyone questions the cost.
ramayan::301.insight: It shows how quickly a destructive decision becomes real once power says yes.

ramayan::302.verse_sanskrit: वारमुख्याश्च तच्छ्रुत्वा वनं प्रविविशुर्महत् । आश्रमस्याविदूरेऽस्मिन् यत्नं कुर्वन्ति दर्शने । । 1107 । । ऋषिपुत्रस्य धीरस्य नित्यमाश्रमवासिन: ।
ramayan::302.verse_hindi: Having heard this, beautiful courtesans entered the great forest and remaining at a  place not far from the hermitage made efforts to steal a sight of this son of a sage (Rsyasringa), this forest dweller, this controller of the senses.
ramayan::302.english_translation: Having heard this, beautiful courtesans entered the great forest and, staying not far from the hermitage, tried to catch a sight of the sage's son, the steadfast forest-dweller who controlled his senses.
ramayan::302.translation_literal: वारमुख्याः (beautiful courtesans) / च (and) / तत् (this) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / वनम् (forest) / प्रविविशुः (entered) / महत् (great) / आश्रमस्य (of the hermitage) / अविदूरे (not far away) / अस्मिन् (in this) / यत्नम् (effort) / कुर्वन्ति (making) / दर्शने (for seeing) / ऋषिपुत्रस्य (of the sage's son) / धीरस्य (steadfast) / नित्यम् (always) / आश्रमवासिनः (dweller in the hermitage)
ramayan::302.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::302.essence: The trap is being set, but the real turning point has not arrived.
ramayan::302.simple_meaning: The courtesans went into the forest and stayed near the hermitage, trying to see Rsyasringa, who lived there in self-control.
ramayan::302.simple_insight: Some scenes only move the plot forward; they do not yet carry the lesson.
ramayan::302.detailed_meaning: The king's plan is now in motion. Beautiful courtesans enter the forest and take positions near the hermitage, hoping to glimpse Rsyasringa, the sage's son who has never left his sheltered life. The verse sets up the trap, not the teaching.
ramayan::302.modern_relevance: A plan is already underway, and people are being placed like pieces on a board. The tension is in the setup, not the reflection.
ramayan::302.insight: It functions as scene preparation, showing the strategy beginning to unfold.

ramayan::303.verse_sanskrit: पितुस्सनित्यसन्तुष्टो नातिचक्राम चाश्रमात् । । 1108 । । न तेन जन्मप्रभृति दृष्टपूर्वं तपस्विना । स्त्री वा पुमान्वा यच्चान्यत्सर्वं नगरराष्ट्रजम् । । 1109 । ।
ramayan::303.verse_hindi: He (Rsyasringa) was always content and never stirred out of his fathers hermitage. Absorbed in penance he had never seen  a woman or a man nor any of the creatures born in towns or cities right from his birth.
ramayan::303.english_translation: He was always content and never went beyond his father's hermitage. Since birth, the ascetic had never seen a woman, a man, or any creature from towns and cities.
ramayan::303.translation_literal: पितुः (of his father) / स-नित्य-सन्तुष्टः (always content) / न (not) / अति-चक्राम (went beyond) / च (and) / आश्रमात् (from the hermitage) । न (not) / तेन (by him) / जन्म-प्रभृति (from birth) / दृष्ट-पूर्वम् (seen before) / तपस्विना (by the ascetic) । स्त्री (woman) / वा (or) / पुमान् (man) / वा (or) / यत् (whatever) / अन्यत् (other) / सर्वम् (all) / नगर-राष्ट्र-जम् (born in towns and cities)
ramayan::303.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::303.essence: His purity is also his vulnerability.
ramayan::303.simple_meaning: Rishyasringa lived in complete seclusion, content with his father's hermitage, and had never seen ordinary social life at all.
ramayan::303.simple_insight: Some lives are shaped by such deep isolation that even the ordinary world feels unimaginable.
ramayan::303.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage of Vibhandaka, his son Rishyasringa has grown up cut off from society. He has never seen men, women, or city life, and that untouched innocence is exactly what the king's agents are about to exploit.
ramayan::303.modern_relevance: A child raised inside one narrow world can become easy to influence the moment the wider world appears. Innocence without exposure can be both purity and vulnerability.
ramayan::303.insight: It shows how complete isolation can leave a person unprepared for social manipulation.

ramayan::304.verse_sanskrit: तत: कदाचित्तं देशमाजगाम यदृच्छया । विभण्डकसुतस्तत्र ताश्चापश्यद्वराङ्गना: । । 11010 । ।
ramayan::304.verse_hindi: One day this son of Vibhandaka (Rsyasringa) accidentally came to the place where he saw the beautiful women.
ramayan::304.english_translation: One day, by chance, Vibhandaka's son came to that place and saw the beautiful women there.
ramayan::304.translation_literal: तत: (then) / कदाचित् (one day) / तम् (that) / देशम् (place) / आजगाम (came) / यदृच्छया (by chance) / विभण्डकसुतः (son of Vibhandaka) / तत्र (there) / ताः (those) / च (and) / अपश्यत् (saw) / वराङ्गनाः (beautiful women)
ramayan::304.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::304.essence: One accidental meeting opens a sealed life to desire.
ramayan::304.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa, who had never left his father's hermitage, wandered to that place by chance and saw the women there.
ramayan::304.simple_insight: A sheltered life can end in a single, unplanned moment.
ramayan::304.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has grown up inside his father's hermitage, untouched by the world. By chance, he reaches the place where the courtesans are waiting. This is the turning point that begins his quiet entanglement with desire and change.
ramayan::304.modern_relevance: You can spend years in one safe routine, then one accidental encounter changes everything you thought you knew.
ramayan::304.insight: It marks the exact moment innocence meets temptation and the story starts moving.

ramayan::305.verse_sanskrit: ताश्चित्रवेषा: प्रमदा गायन्त्यो मधुरस्वरा: । ऋषिपुत्रमुपागम्य सर्वा वचनमब्रुवन् । । 11011 । ।
ramayan::305.verse_hindi: Those wonderfully attired women singing with sweet voices approached the son of the sage (Rsyasringa) and said:
ramayan::305.english_translation: Those beautifully dressed women, singing in sweet voices, approached the son of the sage and spoke to him all together.
ramayan::305.translation_literal: ताः (those women) / चित्रवेषाः (wonderfully dressed) / प्रमदाः (women) / गायन्त्यः (singing) / मधुरस्वराः (with sweet voices) / ऋषिपुत्रम् (to the sage's son) / उपागम्य (having approached) / सर्वाः (all) / वचनम् (words) / अब्रुवन् (they spoke)
ramayan::305.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::305.essence: The first move is often not force, but a carefully staged welcome.
ramayan::305.simple_meaning: Beautiful women, dressed in striking clothes and singing sweetly, came up to the sage's son and began speaking to him.
ramayan::305.simple_insight: A single encounter can open a sealed life.
ramayan::305.detailed_meaning: Rishyashringa, raised in isolation, has never seen women before. After he notices them, these finely dressed women approach him together and begin their carefully chosen speech. The verse sets up the seduction that will pull him out of innocence.
ramayan::305.modern_relevance: You can go years inside one pattern, then meet one person who speaks to the part of you that has never been tested.
ramayan::305.insight: It shows how attraction begins with attention, tone, and invitation before any argument is made.

ramayan::306.verse_sanskrit: कस्त्वं किं वर्तसे ब्रह्मन् ज्ञातुमिच्छामहे वयम् । एकस्त्वं विजने घोरे वने चरसि शंस न: । । 11012 । ।
ramayan::306.verse_hindi: O brahman Who are you? How are you subsisting? We wish to know why you are roaming alone in this dreadful forest? Could you tell us.
ramayan::306.english_translation: O brahman, who are you? How do you live? We want to know why you roam alone in this dreadful forest. Please tell us.
ramayan::306.translation_literal: कस्त्वं (who are you) / किम् (how) / वर्तसे (do you live / subsist) / ब्रह्मन् (O brahman) / ज्ञातुम् (to know) / इच्छामहे (we wish) / वयम् (we) / एकस्त्वम् (you alone) / विजने (in a lonely place) / घोरे (terrible) / वने (in the forest) / चरसि (you roam) / शंस (tell) / नः (to us)
ramayan::306.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::306.essence: A question begins the pull from isolation into contact.
ramayan::306.simple_meaning: The women ask the sage's son who he is, how he survives, and why he is alone in the frightening forest.
ramayan::306.simple_insight: Curiosity opens the next turn of the story.
ramayan::306.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has just seen the women for the first time. They approach him with sweet voices and begin questioning him gently, drawing him out of his isolation. This verse is part of that seduction, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::306.modern_relevance: A stranger starts asking careful questions at the edge of your world. The conversation is not about information alone; it is the first step in changing your direction.
ramayan::306.insight: It sets up the meeting by showing how attention and question can pull someone out of seclusion.

ramayan::307.verse_sanskrit: अदृष्टरूपास्तास्तेन काम्यरूपा वने स्त्रिय: । हार्दात्तस्य मतिर्जाता व्याख्यातुं पितरं स्वकम् । । 11013 । ।
ramayan::307.verse_hindi: He had never seen such charming women in the forest. He developed affection towards them and a desire arose in him to speak about his father.
ramayan::307.english_translation: He had never seen such charming women in the forest. He felt drawn to them, and the wish arose in him to speak about his father.
ramayan::307.translation_literal: अदृष्ट-रूपाः (whose forms had not been seen) / ताः (those) / तेन (by him) / काम्य-रूपाः (desirable forms) / वने (in the forest) / स्त्रियः (women) / हार्दात् (from the heart) / तस्य (his) / मतिः (thought) / जाता (arose) / व्याख्यातुम् (to speak/explain) / पितरम् (father) / स्वकम् (his own)
ramayan::307.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::307.essence: New attraction makes the sheltered mind speak.
ramayan::307.simple_meaning: Seeing beautiful women for the first time stirred his heart, and he wanted to tell them about his father.
ramayan::307.simple_insight: A first attraction can open the door to speech, even in someone who has lived apart from the world.
ramayan::307.detailed_meaning: The women have approached Rishyasringa in the forest and begun questioning him. Their beauty and presence unsettle him for the first time, and that inner stirring leads him toward revealing his identity and family.
ramayan::307.modern_relevance: You meet someone who unsettles your usual certainty, and suddenly you want to explain yourself, your family, your whole life.
ramayan::307.insight: It shows how desire can move a sheltered mind from silence into self-disclosure.

ramayan::308.verse_sanskrit: पिता विभण्डकोऽस्माकं तस्याहं सुत औरस: । ऋश्यशृङ्ग इति ख्यातं नाम कर्म च मे भुवि । । 11014 । ।
ramayan::308.verse_hindi: My father is Vibhandaka. I am his own son. My name is Rsyasringa. I am known the world over by this name associated with my karma.
ramayan::308.english_translation: My father is Vibhandaka. I am his own son. My name is Rsyasringa, and that is the name by which my action is known in the world.
ramayan::308.translation_literal: पिता (father) / विभण्डकः (Vibhandaka) / अस्माकम् (our) / तस्य (his) / अहम् (I) / सुतः (son) / औरसः (born of the body) / ऋश्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / इति (thus) / ख्यातम् (known) / नाम (name) / कर्म (action) / च (and) / मे (my) / भुवि (on earth)
ramayan::308.speaker: Rsyasringa
ramayan::308.essence: Identity here is inherited, named, and still untouched by the wider world.
ramayan::308.simple_meaning: The forest hermit introduces himself plainly: he is Vibhandaka’s son, and his name is Rsyasringa, known by his deed and reputation.
ramayan::308.simple_insight: A simple identity can carry a whole life of training and reputation.
ramayan::308.detailed_meaning: The women have approached the secluded hermitage and asked the lone ascetic who he is. Rsyasringa answers with complete innocence, naming his father and himself. The moment matters because his sheltered life is about to be drawn into a larger human world.
ramayan::308.modern_relevance: Someone asks your name in a room where you feel out of place, and you answer from the only world you know. A sheltered life can still carry a clear identity.
ramayan::308.insight: It shows how a person formed in isolation can still speak with certainty about who he is.

ramayan::309.verse_sanskrit: इहाश्रमपदोऽस्माकं समीपे शुभदर्शना: । करिष्ये वोऽत्र पूजां वै सर्वेषां विधिपूर्वकम् । । 11015 । ।
ramayan::309.verse_hindi: O auspiciouslooking women, our hermitage is nearby. I will extend to you due hospitality.
ramayan::309.english_translation: O auspicious-looking women, our hermitage is nearby. I will offer you proper hospitality there, according to ritual.
ramayan::309.translation_literal: इह (here) / आश्रमपदः (hermitage) / अस्माकम् (our) / समीपे (near) / शुभदर्शनाः (auspicious-looking women) / करिष्ये (I will do) / वः (for you) / अत्र (here) / पूजाम् (hospitality / respectful reception) / वै (indeed) / सर्वेषाम् (for all) / विधिपूर्वकम् (according to proper rite)
ramayan::309.speaker: Rsyasringa
ramayan::309.essence: Courtesy becomes the doorway to entanglement.
ramayan::309.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa tells the women that his hermitage is nearby and that he will receive them properly and respectfully there.
ramayan::309.simple_insight: A gentle invitation can hide a powerful shift in direction.
ramayan::309.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa, newly stirred by the sight of the women, speaks with innocent courtesy. He points them toward the nearby hermitage and promises formal hospitality. In the story, this is the moment that draws him away from his seclusion and into the larger plot.
ramayan::309.modern_relevance: Someone smiles, offers help, and says, “Come this way.” The words sound harmless, but they can quietly change the whole direction of a day.
ramayan::309.insight: It shows how polite words can carry hidden intention and move events forward.

ramayan::310.verse_sanskrit: ऋषिपुत्रवचश्श्रुत्वा सर्वासां मतिरास वै । तदाश्रमपदं द्रष्टुं जग्मुस्सर्वाश्च तेन ता: । । 11016 । ।
ramayan::310.verse_hindi: After listening to the words of the sages son (Rsyasringa), all the beautiful women with a desire to see the hermitage  accompanied him.
ramayan::310.english_translation: After hearing the sage's son, all the women became eager to see the hermitage and went with him.
ramayan::310.translation_literal: ऋषिपुत्रवचः (the words of the sage's son) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सर्वासाम् (of all) / मतिः (the mind, intention) / आसीत् (became) / तत् (that) / आश्रमपदम् (hermitage) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / जग्मुः (they went) / सर्वाः (all) / च (and) / तेन (with him) / ताः (those women)
ramayan::310.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::310.essence: Their curiosity moves them straight into the next step.
ramayan::310.simple_meaning: After hearing Rishyasringa, the women all wanted to see the hermitage and went with him.
ramayan::310.simple_insight: Curiosity can carry people forward before they even notice it.
ramayan::310.detailed_meaning: Rishyasringa has just spoken to the women near his hermitage. His words work exactly as intended: their interest is awakened, and they follow him toward the ashram. The verse simply moves the scene forward.
ramayan::310.modern_relevance: Someone says, “Come see this,” and the whole group starts walking before anyone has fully decided. That small pull of curiosity can change the direction of a moment.
ramayan::310.insight: It shows how attention can be led by a compelling invitation.

ramayan::311.verse_sanskrit: आगतानां तत: पूजामृषिपुत्रश्चकार ह । इदमर्घ्यमिदं पाद्यमिदं मूलमिदं फलं च न: । । 11017 । ।
ramayan::311.verse_hindi: Thereafter the son of ascetic respectfully received the the strangers saying, (Accept) our offerings, here is water for washing feet and  here are roots and fruits.
ramayan::311.english_translation: Thereafter the son of ascetic respectfully received the strangers, saying, "Accept our offerings: here is water for washing feet, and here are roots and fruits."
ramayan::311.translation_literal: आगतानाम् (of those who had come) / ततः (then) / पूजाम् (hospitality, respectful reception) / ऋषिपुत्रः (the son of the sage) / चकार (did, offered) / ह (indeed) / इदम् (this) / अर्घ्यम् (offering for respectful reception) / इदम् (this) / पाद्यम् (water for the feet) / इदम् (this) / मूलम् (roots) / इदम् (this) / फलम् (fruits) / च (and) / नः (our)
ramayan::311.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::311.essence: Respectful welcome matters more than wealth.
ramayan::311.simple_meaning: The sage's son welcomed the arriving visitors with respectful hospitality and offered them water, roots, and fruits.
ramayan::311.simple_insight: Kindness begins with how you receive someone who has just arrived.
ramayan::311.detailed_meaning: Rishyasringa has brought the visitors to the hermitage, and the sage's son responds with formal hospitality. He offers water for the feet, roots, and fruits — the simple, proper welcome of an ascetic home.
ramayan::311.modern_relevance: Someone knocks on your door after a long trip, tired and unsure. Before any big conversation, you offer water, a seat, and something simple to eat.
ramayan::311.insight: It teaches you to meet arrival with dignity before asking anything in return.

ramayan::312.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां सर्वा एव समुत्सुका: । ऋषेर्भीताश्च शीघ्रं ता गमनाय मतिं दधु: । । 11018 । ।
ramayan::312.verse_hindi: The anxious courtesans received the offerings and afraid of the ascetics return, made up their minds to withdraw immediately.
ramayan::312.english_translation: Receiving the offerings, the anxious courtesans became eager to leave at once, fearing the sages.
ramayan::312.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / च (and) / तां (that) / पूजां (offering) / सर्वा एव (all indeed) / समुत्सुका: (eager, anxious) / ऋषेर्भीताश्च (and afraid of the sages) / शीघ्रं (quickly) / ता: (they) / गमनाय (for leaving) / मतिं (resolve) / दधु: (placed, made)
ramayan::312.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::312.essence: Fear ends the encounter before it can become trust.
ramayan::312.simple_meaning: The women accepted the hospitality, but fear of the sages made them decide to leave quickly.
ramayan::312.simple_insight: Politeness can survive fear, but only for a moment.
ramayan::312.detailed_meaning: The courtesans have come to the hermitage of Rishyasringa and been respectfully received. But once they accept the offerings, their anxiety returns at once. The scene turns on their sudden decision to withdraw before the ascetic world can hold them longer.
ramayan::312.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is kind, but your body still wants the door. Courtesy is there, yet your nerves are already planning the exit.
ramayan::312.insight: It shows how fear can override attraction, turning a brief welcome into an immediate retreat.

ramayan::313.verse_sanskrit: अस्माकमपि मुख्यानि फलानीमानि वै द्विज । गृहाण प्रति भद्रं ते भक्षयस्व च मा चिरम् । । 11019 । ।
ramayan::313.verse_hindi: O brahmin, these are excellent fruits. May prosperity be to you. Accept them and eat them without delay.
ramayan::313.english_translation: O brahmin, these are excellent fruits. May prosperity be to you. Accept them and eat them without delay.
ramayan::313.translation_literal: अस्माकम् (our) / अपि (also) / मुख्यानि (excellent, chief) / फलानि (fruits) / इमानि (these) / वै (indeed) / द्विज (O brahmin) / गृहाण (take) / प्रति (receive) / भद्रम् (prosperity, may it be well) / ते (to you) / भक्षयस्व (eat) / च (and) / मा चिरम् (without delay)
ramayan::313.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::313.essence: A hurried gift still carries warmth.
ramayan::313.simple_meaning: The women offer the ascetic the best fruit they have and urge him to take it and eat quickly.
ramayan::313.simple_insight: Kindness can appear even in a hurried, fearful moment.
ramayan::313.detailed_meaning: The ascetic's son has welcomed the strangers, and the courtesans, relieved and anxious to leave, respond with gifts. This line is part of a brief, social exchange of hospitality, not a teaching or turning point.
ramayan::313.modern_relevance: You hand someone the last good fruit from your bag before rushing for the train. The gesture is small, but it still carries care.
ramayan::313.insight: It shows a simple act of courtesy under pressure, not a lasting principle.

ramayan::314.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तास्तं समालिङ्ग्य सर्वा हर्षसमन्विता: । मोदकान्प्रददुस्तस्मै भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान् बहून् । । 11020 । ।
ramayan::314.verse_hindi: Then, all the courtesans embracing him with joy, offered plentiful sweetmeats and various items of food.
ramayan::314.english_translation: Then, all the courtesans embracing him with joy, offered plentiful sweetmeats and various items of food.
ramayan::314.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / ता: (those women) / तम् (him) / समालिङ्ग्य (embracing) / सर्वा: (all) / हर्षसमन्विता: (filled with joy) / मोदकान् (sweetmeats) / प्रददुः (gave) / तस्मै (to him) / भक्ष्यान् (eatables) / च (and) / विविधान् (various) / बहून् (many)
ramayan::314.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::314.essence: Affection and delight are being used to lead him onward.
ramayan::314.simple_meaning: The women welcomed him warmly, embraced him, and gave him many kinds of sweets and food.
ramayan::314.simple_insight: A careful welcome can lower a guard faster than force.
ramayan::314.detailed_meaning: Rishyashringa has been drawn into a world outside the forest. The courtesans, relieved and delighted, greet him with affection and offer food and sweets. This is a scene of seduction and transition, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::314.modern_relevance: A room full of strangers suddenly turns kind, and you relax before you even notice. Warmth can open a door that argument never could.
ramayan::314.insight: It shows how pleasure and welcome can gently redirect someone’s path.

ramayan::315.verse_sanskrit: तानि चास्वाद्य तेजस्वी फलानीति स्म मन्यते । अनास्वादितपूर्वाणि वने नित्यनिवासिनाम् । । 11021 । ।
ramayan::315.verse_hindi: The lustrous (Rsyasringa) who had never tasted any food other than what was offered by the permanent forestdwellers mistook them for fruits.
ramayan::315.english_translation: The radiant Rsyasringa, who had never tasted anything except what the forest-dwellers gave him, mistook those foods for fruits.
ramayan::315.translation_literal: तानि (those) / च (and) / आस्वाद्य (having tasted) / तेजस्वी (the radiant one) / फलानि (fruits) / इति (thus) / स्म (indeed) / मन्यते (he thought) / अनास्वादितपूर्वाणि (never tasted before) / वने (in the forest) / नित्यनिवासिनाम् (of those living there always)
ramayan::315.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::315.essence: What you have never known, you may misname at first.
ramayan::315.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa, unfamiliar with ordinary food, took the offered dishes to be fruits.
ramayan::315.simple_insight: A sheltered mind can mistake the unfamiliar for the familiar.
ramayan::315.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa is being gently lured by the women who have welcomed him with food and affection. Because he has lived only among forest dwellers and never known ordinary meals, he cannot recognize what he is eating. The verse pauses on his innocence before the next step in the seduction unfolds.
ramayan::315.modern_relevance: You can be surrounded by attention and still not understand what is being offered. Innocence often names things by the only world it knows.
ramayan::315.insight: It shows how limited experience can distort perception, making you read new situations through old categories.

ramayan::316.verse_sanskrit: आपृच्छ्य च तदा विप्रं व्रतचर्यां निवेद्य च । गच्छन्ति स्मापदेशात्ता भीतास्तस्य पितुस्स्त्रिय: । । 11022 । ।
ramayan::316.verse_hindi: The ladies apprehensive of (the arrival of) his father took leave of him on the pretext of  observance of (evening) rites.
ramayan::316.english_translation: The women, afraid of his father’s arrival, took leave of him under the pretext of evening rites.
ramayan::316.translation_literal: आपृच्छ्य (having taken leave) / च (and) / तदा (then) / विप्रं (the brahmin) / व्रतचर्यां (the observance of vows) / निवेद्य (having stated) / च (and) / गच्छन्ति स्म (they went) / अपदेशात् (under the pretext) / ता: (those) / भीता: (afraid) / तस्य (of his) / पितुः (father's) / स्त्रियः (women)
ramayan::316.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::316.essence: Polite words can conceal urgent fear.
