ramayan::316.simple_meaning: The women leave him by pretending they need to observe evening rites, because they fear his father may arrive.
ramayan::316.simple_insight: A hidden fear can shape even a polite goodbye.
ramayan::316.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has been welcomed and fed, but the women now worry that his father might appear and disrupt the plan. So they excuse themselves with a religious pretext and leave him alone, keeping the larger scheme in motion.
ramayan::316.modern_relevance: You smile, make an excuse, and leave before the situation gets complicated. The real reason stays unspoken, but it still guides the exit.
ramayan::316.insight: It shows how social grace can hide strategic fear and keep a larger plan moving.

ramayan::317.verse_sanskrit: गतासु तासु सर्वासु काश्यपस्यात्मजो द्विज: । अस्वस्थहृदयश्चासीद्दु:खं स्म परिवर्तते । । 11023 । ।
ramayan::317.verse_hindi: When they all departed, Kasyapas son, the brahmin roamed (Rsyasringa) with a restless mind  charged with sorrow.
ramayan::317.english_translation: When they all departed, Kasyapa's son, the brahmin, wandered with a restless heart, troubled by sorrow.
ramayan::317.translation_literal: गतासु (having departed) / तासु (when those) / सर्वासु (all) / काश्यपस्य (of Kasyapa) / आत्मजः (son) / द्विजः (the brahmin) / अस्वस्थहृदयः (with restless heart) / च (and) / आसीत् (was) / दुःखम् (sorrow) / स्म (indeed) / परिवर्तते (turned about / wandered)
ramayan::317.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::317.essence: Loss of company leaves the mind restless.
ramayan::317.simple_meaning: After the women left, Rsyasringa was left uneasy and sorrowful, unable to settle his mind.
ramayan::317.simple_insight: Separation can leave even a disciplined person unmoored for a moment.
ramayan::317.detailed_meaning: The women have slipped away after their brief visit, and Rsyasringa is left behind in silence. Kasyapa's son, usually steady in his forest life, now wanders with an unsettled heart. The verse simply records his unease before the next encounter.
ramayan::317.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet after everyone leaves, and you suddenly feel the ache you were ignoring. The mind starts pacing only when the noise is gone.
ramayan::317.insight: It shows the first stir of longing before action follows.

ramayan::318.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽपरेद्युस्तं देशमाजगाम स वीर्यवान् । मनोज्ञा यत्र ता दृष्टा वारमुख्यास्स्वलङ्कृताः । । 11024 । ।
ramayan::318.verse_hindi: On the following day, the sage armed with the power of penance, came to the place where he had seen those enticing, welladorned courtesans.
ramayan::318.english_translation: On the following day, the sage armed with the power of penance came to the place where he had seen those enticing, well-adorned courtesans.
ramayan::318.translation_literal: ततः (then) / अपरेद्यु: (on the next day) / तम् (that) / देशम् (to the place) / आजगाम (came) / सः (he) / वीर्यवान् (powerful) / मनोज्ञा: (pleasing) / यत्र (where) / ता: (those) / दृष्टा: (seen) / वारमुख्या: (courtesans) / स्वलङ्कृताः (well-adorned)
ramayan::318.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::318.essence: The mind goes back to what has already caught it.
ramayan::318.simple_meaning: The next day, the ascetic returned to the place where he had seen the beautifully dressed women.
ramayan::318.simple_insight: A single desire can pull attention back to the same place.
ramayan::318.detailed_meaning: Rishyashringa, the son of Kashyapa, has been left disturbed after the women depart. The next day, still carrying that pull, he returns to the place where he saw them. This verse is a bridge in the seduction that will change his life.
ramayan::318.modern_relevance: You tell yourself you'll stop checking the same profile, thread, or place. Then the next day, your feet go back there anyway.
ramayan::318.insight: It shows how curiosity and attraction can quietly turn into repeated return.

ramayan::319.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वैव च तास्तदा विप्रमायान्तं हृष्टमानसा: । उपसृत्य ततस्सर्वास्तास्तमूचुरिदं वच: । । 11025 । ।
ramayan::319.verse_hindi: All of them were rejoiced on seeing the brahmin approaching them, came nearer to him and said:
ramayan::319.english_translation: All of them were delighted on seeing the brahmin approaching, went up to him, and said these words:
ramayan::319.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / ताः (those women) / तदा (then) / विप्रम् (the brahmin) / आयान्तम् (coming) / हृष्टमानसाः (joyful in mind) / उपसृत्य (having approached) / ततः (then) / सर्वाः (all) / ताः (they) / तम् (to him) / ऊचुः (said) / इदम् (these) / वचः (words)
ramayan::319.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::319.essence: Joy meets the one who is finally arriving.
ramayan::319.simple_meaning: The women see the approaching brahmin, feel happy, walk up to him, and begin speaking.
ramayan::319.simple_insight: A welcoming heart makes the first step easy.
ramayan::319.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has reached the place where the women he once saw are waiting. They notice him coming, feel glad, and move toward him together. This verse only sets up the conversation that follows.
ramayan::319.modern_relevance: You spot someone you were hoping to meet across a crowded room. Before a word is spoken, the welcome is already happening.
ramayan::319.insight: It shifts attention from the meeting itself to the warm approach before it.

ramayan::320.verse_sanskrit: एह्याश्रमपदं सौम्य ह्यस्माकमिति चाब्रुवन् । तत्राप्येष विधिश्श्रीमान् विशेषेण भविष्यति । । 11026 । ।
ramayan::320.verse_hindi: O handsome one, come to our hermitage. A special, sumptuous hospitality will be extended to you, they said.
ramayan::320.english_translation: O handsome one, come to our hermitage. A special, sumptuous hospitality will be extended to you, they said.
ramayan::320.translation_literal: एहि (come) / आश्रमपदम् (hermitage-place) / सौम्य (gentle one) / हि (indeed) / अस्माकम् (our) / इति (thus) / च (and) / अब्रुवन् (they said) / तत्र (there) / अपि (also) / एषः (this) / विधिः (hospitality/ritual) / श्रीमान् (splendid) / विशेषेण (especially) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::320.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::320.essence: Hospitality becomes the doorway to what follows.
ramayan::320.simple_meaning: The women invite the sage to their hermitage and promise him special hospitality there.
ramayan::320.simple_insight: A warm invitation can hide a turning point you do not yet see.
ramayan::320.detailed_meaning: The sage has returned to the women he saw earlier. They greet him with courtesy and invite him into their hermitage, promising special hospitality. This is the moment that draws him inward and sets up the next step of the encounter.
ramayan::320.modern_relevance: You accept a friendly invitation because it feels harmless. Only later do you realize the room, the tone, and the timing were all part of the pull.
ramayan::320.insight: It shows how charm and welcome can guide someone into a situation before caution has time to speak.

ramayan::321.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तासां सर्वासां हृदयङ्गमम् । गमनाय मतिं चक्रे तं च निन्युस्तदा स्त्रिय: । । 11027 । ।
ramayan::321.verse_hindi: Having heard their words pleasing to the mind, he agreed to go with them. And the women took him away.
ramayan::321.english_translation: Having heard their words pleasing to the mind, he agreed to go with them. And the women took him away.
ramayan::321.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तु (but) / वचनं (the words) / तासां (of them) / सर्वासां (of all) / हृदयङ्गमम् (pleasing to the heart) / गमनाय (for going) / मतिं (the intention) / चक्रे (made) / तं (him) / च (and) / निन्यु: (they led) / तदा (then) / स्त्रिय: (the women)
ramayan::321.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::321.essence: Kind words can open the door before you even notice it.
ramayan::321.simple_meaning: The sage accepted the women’s invitation and went with them.
ramayan::321.simple_insight: A gentle invitation can move someone more than force ever could.
ramayan::321.detailed_meaning: The women have welcomed the visiting brahmin into their hermitage and invited him to come with them. He is pleased by their words and agrees. This verse simply carries him from invitation into motion, setting up the next event.
ramayan::321.modern_relevance: You hear a kind invitation after a long day and finally say yes, letting yourself be led somewhere unexpected.
ramayan::321.insight: It shifts the moment from hearing to yielding, showing how consent begins with being moved by trust.

ramayan::322.verse_sanskrit: तत्र चानीयमाने तु विप्रे तस्मिन्महात्मनि । ववर्ष सहसा देवो जगत्प्रह्लादयंस्तदा । । 11028 । ।
ramayan::322.verse_hindi: As the illustrious sage was being brought (to Anga) the god of rain (Parjanya) suddenly inundated the earth which looked cherful (with rain).
ramayan::322.english_translation: As the illustrious sage was being brought there, the rain-god suddenly poured down rain, delighting the whole world.
ramayan::322.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / च (and) / आनीयमाने (being brought) / तु (indeed) / विप्रे (the brahmin) / तस्मिन् (that) / महात्मनि (great-souled) / ववर्ष (rained) / सहसा (suddenly) / देवः (the divine being) / जगत् (the world) / प्रह्लादयन् (delighting) / तदा (then)
ramayan::322.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::322.essence: His arrival is so auspicious that the sky answers first.
ramayan::322.simple_meaning: As the revered sage was brought along, rain suddenly fell and refreshed the land.
ramayan::322.simple_insight: A right arrival can change the whole atmosphere around it.
ramayan::322.detailed_meaning: The women have just led the sage toward Anga. At that very moment, rain breaks over the land, as if nature itself responds to his presence. The next verse will show the king recognising the sign.
ramayan::322.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension shifts before anyone speaks. Sometimes the change is not from force, but from the presence you bring.
ramayan::322.insight: It frames auspicious arrival as something the world itself can answer.

ramayan::323.verse_sanskrit: वर्षेणैवागतं विप्रं विषयं स्वं नराधिप: । प्रत्युद्गम्य मुनिं प्रह्वश्शिरसा च महीं गत: । । 11029 । ।
ramayan::323.verse_hindi: The king (Romapada) went out to welcome the ascetic, the brahmin who brought along with him rains to his country. He humbly bowed down his head and prostrated before him.
ramayan::323.english_translation: The king went out to welcome the ascetic, the brahmin who had brought rains to his country. He humbly bowed his head and prostrated before him.
ramayan::323.translation_literal: वर्षेणैव (with rain itself) / आगतं (having arrived) / विप्रं (the brahmin/ascetic) / विषयं (the kingdom/country) / स्वं (his own) / नराधिपः (the king) / प्रत्युद्गम्य (going forth to meet) / मुनिं (the sage) / प्रह्वः (bowed down) / शिरसा (with the head) / च (and) / महीं (to the ground) / गतः (gone/prostrated)
ramayan::323.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::323.essence: Relief deepens into reverence when the rain finally comes.
ramayan::323.simple_meaning: The king greets the sage with deep respect after rain has returned to his land.
ramayan::323.simple_insight: Gratitude becomes real when relief turns into respect.
ramayan::323.detailed_meaning: Romapada has just seen rain return after the sage's arrival. Now he goes out to meet the brahmin who brought that blessing, bowing low before him. The moment is about gratitude, reverence, and the king's recognition of the sage's power.
ramayan::323.modern_relevance: Your project finally works after days of silence, and the person who helped you most walks in. You stop performing and simply bow to the help that changed everything.
ramayan::323.insight: It teaches you to meet help with humility, not entitlement.

ramayan::324.verse_sanskrit: अर्घ्यं च प्रददौ तस्मै न्यायतस्सुसमाहित: । वव्रे प्रसादं विप्रेन्द्रान्मा विप्रं मन्युराविशेत् । । 11030 । ।
ramayan::324.verse_hindi: He gave that Indra among the brahmins offerings righteously with unstinted devotion and asked for his favour that he should not incur the wrath of the sage (his father Vibhandaka for having brought him to Anga).
ramayan::324.english_translation: He gave that foremost brahmin a respectful offering with careful propriety and asked for his blessing, so that the sage's anger would not fall upon him.
ramayan::324.translation_literal: अर्घ्यम् (respectful offering) / च (and) / प्रददौ (gave) / तस्मै (to him) / न्यायतः (righteously, properly) / सुसमाहितः (fully composed, attentive) / वव्रे (he asked, requested) / प्रसादम् (favour, blessing) / विप्रेन्द्रात् (from the foremost brahmin) / मा (not) / विप्रम् (the sage) / मन्युः (anger) / आविशेत् (may enter, may fall upon) / इति (thus)
ramayan::324.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::324.essence: Respect comes first when a relationship can still be repaired.
ramayan::324.simple_meaning: The king welcomes the sage with respect and asks for a blessing so the sage's anger will not touch him.
ramayan::324.simple_insight: Respect can soften fear and keep a difficult relationship from turning harsher.
ramayan::324.detailed_meaning: Romapada receives the brahmin who has brought rain to his drought-struck kingdom. He offers honor first, then asks for protection from the sage's possible anger. The moment is about careful courtesy before a powerful, fragile relationship.
ramayan::324.modern_relevance: You finally get the message back from someone you disappointed. Before explaining yourself, you choose humility and respect, because one careless word could reopen everything.
ramayan::324.insight: It teaches you to approach strained relationships with composure, respect, and a request for goodwill before asking for anything else.

ramayan::325.verse_sanskrit: अन्त:पुरं प्रविश्यास्मै कन्यां दत्त्वा यथाविधि । शान्तां शान्तेन मनसा राजा हर्षमवाप स: । । 11031 । । एवं स न्यवसत्तत्र सर्वकामैस्सुपूजित: ।
ramayan::325.verse_hindi: The king entered the inner apartment, duly offered him his daughter Shanta in marriage and experienced peace and satisfaction.
ramayan::325.english_translation: The king entered the inner apartment, duly offered him his daughter Shanta in marriage, and found peace and satisfaction. He then remained there, honored with every comfort.
ramayan::325.translation_literal: अन्त:पुरं (inner apartment) / प्रविश्य (having entered) / अस्मै (to him) / कन्याम् (the daughter) / दत्त्वा (having given) / यथाविधि (according to proper rite) / शान्ताम् (Shanta) / शान्तेन (with peaceful) / मनसा (mind) / राजा (the king) / हर्षम् (joy) / अवाप (attained) / सः (he) / एवम् (thus) / सः (he) / न्यवसत् (dwelt) / तत्र (there) / सर्वकामैः (with all desired things) / सुपूजितः (well honored)
ramayan::325.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::325.essence: Right action can bring the peace you were chasing.
ramayan::325.simple_meaning: The king gives Shanta in marriage to the sage in the proper way, and that settled his heart with joy.
ramayan::325.simple_insight: Doing what is right can quiet a restless heart more deeply than winning anything else.
ramayan::325.detailed_meaning: Romapada welcomes the sage who brought rain back to his kingdom. To honor him fully, the king enters the inner chambers and gives him Shanta in marriage according to custom. The verse marks the completion of hospitality, gratitude, and reconciliation.
ramayan::325.modern_relevance: You finally make the call you kept postponing, and the tension in your chest eases. Some relief comes only after you do the respectful thing cleanly.
ramayan::325.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as formality to ceremony as the act that restores inner order.

ramayan::326.verse_sanskrit: भूय एव हि राजेन्द्र शृणु मे वचनं हितम् । यथा स देवप्रवर: कथायामेवमब्रवीत् । । 1111 । ।
ramayan::326.verse_hindi: Great king, I shall tell you the way Sanatkumara, great among the celestials further narrated the story. Listen to my words which may prove useful to you (said Sumantra).
ramayan::326.english_translation: Great king, listen again to my useful words. This is how Sanatkumara, the best among the radiant beings, continued the story.
ramayan::326.translation_literal: भूयः (again) / एव (indeed) / हि (for) / राजेन्द्र (O king among kings) / शृणु (listen) / मे (my) / वचनं (words) / हितम् (beneficial) / यथा (how) / सः (he) / देवप्रवरः (best among the radiant beings) / कथायाम् (in the story) / एवम् (thus) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::326.speaker: Sumantra
ramayan::326.essence: The real message comes next; this line only opens the door.
ramayan::326.simple_meaning: Sumantra asks the king to listen carefully as he continues recounting Sanatkumara's story in a useful way.
ramayan::326.simple_insight: Some guidance begins by asking you to listen well before the real teaching starts.
ramayan::326.detailed_meaning: Sumantra is still speaking to the king, framing the next part of a larger tale. He is not teaching a doctrine here; he is preparing the listener for Sanatkumara's words, which will matter in the verses that follow.
ramayan::326.modern_relevance: A friend says, “Wait, there’s one more thing you need to hear,” and you pause before leaving the room. This verse is that pause before the point lands.
ramayan::326.insight: It sets up the next teaching rather than delivering the teaching itself.

ramayan::327.verse_sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातो भविष्यति सुधार्मिक: । राजा दशरथो नाम्ना श्रीमान्सत्यप्रतिश्रव: । । 1112 । ।
ramayan::327.verse_hindi: इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातो भविष्यति सुधार्मिक: । राजा दशरथो नाम्ना श्रीमान्सत्यप्रतिश्रव: । । 1112 । ।
ramayan::327.english_translation: A highly righteous king named Dasharatha will be born in the line of Ikshvaku, noble and true to his word.
ramayan::327.translation_literal: इक्ष्वाकूणां (of the Ikshvaku line) / कुले (in the family) / जातः (born) / भविष्यति (will be) / सुधार्मिकः (highly righteous) / राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / नाम्ना (by name) / श्रीमान् (splendid) / सत्यप्रतिश्रवः (true to his promise)
ramayan::327.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::327.essence: True greatness is being known for keeping your word.
ramayan::327.simple_meaning: Dasharatha will be born in the Ikshvaku line as a noble king who keeps his word.
ramayan::327.simple_insight: Some people are remembered not for power, but for the weight of their promises.
ramayan::327.detailed_meaning: Sanatkumara is continuing a prophetic account of the royal line. He names Dasharatha before his birth, describing him as righteous, splendid, and faithful to his promises. The verse is a character introduction, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::327.modern_relevance: Before a child is born, a family can already be known for the kind of character it carries forward. Some names become heavy because they are expected to stand for integrity.
ramayan::327.insight: It frames kingship as moral credibility, not just political power.

ramayan::328.verse_sanskrit: अङ्गराजेन सख्यं च तस्य राज्ञो भविष्यति । कन्या चास्य महाभागा शान्ता नाम भविष्यति । । 1113 । ।
ramayan::328.verse_hindi: That king (Dasaratha) will develop friendship with the king of Anga. A highly virtuous daughter named Santa will be born to  king of Anga.
ramayan::328.english_translation: That king will form friendship with the king of Anga. A highly virtuous daughter named Shanta will be born to the king of Anga.
ramayan::328.translation_literal: अङ्गराजेन (with the king of Anga) / सख्यं (friendship) / च (and) / तस्य (of that) / राज्ञो (king) / भविष्यति (will be) / कन्या (daughter) / च (and) / अस्य (of him) / महाभागा (highly virtuous, fortunate) / शान्ता (Shanta) / नाम (by name) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::328.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::328.essence: A small alliance here will shape the larger story later.
ramayan::328.simple_meaning: Dasaratha will become friends with the king of Anga, and the king of Anga will have a noble daughter named Shanta.
ramayan::328.simple_insight: Some important turns in life begin as simple connections between families and rulers.
ramayan::328.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is still laying out the chain of events that will lead to Rama's birth. He introduces Dasaratha's friendship with the king of Anga and the birth of Shanta, a detail that matters because it connects royal alliances to the larger story.
ramayan::328.modern_relevance: A casual introduction at a wedding, a school reunion, or a work dinner can quietly change the course of a family for years.
ramayan::328.insight: It frames a future event as part of a larger network of relationships and consequences.

ramayan::329.verse_sanskrit: पुत्रस्तु सोऽङ्गराजस्य रोमपाद इति श्रुत: । तं स राजा दशरथो गमिष्यति महायशा: । । 1114 । ।
ramayan::329.verse_hindi: The famous king Dasaratha will approach the son of the king of Anga known as Romapada.
ramayan::329.english_translation: The famous king Dasaratha will approach the son of the king of Anga, known as Romapada.
ramayan::329.translation_literal: पुत्रः (son) / तु (indeed) / सः (he) / अङ्गराजस्य (of the king of Anga) / रोमपादः (Romapada) / इति (thus) / श्रुतः (known) / तम् (him) / सः (he) / राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / गमिष्यति (will go/approach) / महायशाः (highly famous)
ramayan::329.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::329.essence: One approach here is only a link in a much larger chain.
ramayan::329.simple_meaning: Dasaratha goes to Romapada, the son of the king of Anga, as the next step in the unfolding plan.
ramayan::329.simple_insight: Some important moves are only steps in a larger design, not the whole story.
ramayan::329.detailed_meaning: The sages are tracing the line of events that will lead to Rama's birth. After naming Dasaratha and his friendship with Anga, they identify Romapada as the next person he will approach. The verse is a bridge, not the main teaching.
ramayan::329.modern_relevance: You make one careful call after another, not knowing yet how it will shape the larger outcome. Some meetings matter because they open the next door, not because they finish the journey.
ramayan::329.insight: It shifts attention from isolated action to the sequence of causes that follows it.

ramayan::330.verse_sanskrit: अनपत्योऽस्मि धर्मात्मन् शान्ताभर्ता मम क्रतुम् । आहरेत त्वयाज्ञप्तस्सन्तानार्थं कुलस्य च । । 1115 । ।
ramayan::330.verse_hindi: O righteous king I am issueless. Let Rsyasringa, husband of Santa be ordered to perform the a sacrificial ceremony so that I shall be blessed with I son for the perpetuaion of my race.
ramayan::330.english_translation: O righteous king, I am childless. Let Rsyasringa, Santa's husband, be asked to perform a sacrifice so that I may be blessed with a son for the continuation of my line.
ramayan::330.translation_literal: अनपत्यः (childless) / अस्मि (I am) / धर्मात्मन् (O righteous one) / शान्ताभर्ता (Santa's husband) / मम (for me) / क्रतुम् (sacrifice) / आहरेत (should bring/perform) / त्वया (by you) / आज्ञप्तः (being ordered) / सन्तानार्थम् (for offspring) / कुलस्य (of the family line) / च (and)
ramayan::330.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::330.essence: One request carries the fate of an entire lineage.
ramayan::330.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks for a sacrifice to be arranged so he can have a son and continue his family line.
ramayan::330.simple_insight: Longing for legacy can make a single request carry the weight of an entire life.
ramayan::330.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has gone to Romapada because his kingdom has no heir. He asks that Rsyasringa, Santa's husband, be brought in to perform a sacrifice that may give him a son. The future of Ayodhya now hangs on this plea.
ramayan::330.modern_relevance: You sit across from a doctor, a lender, or a mentor, and one answer could change the shape of your whole family. Some requests are really pleas against extinction.
ramayan::330.insight: It shifts attention from immediate desire to the larger responsibility of sustaining a family or legacy.

ramayan::331.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा राज्ञोऽथ तद्वाक्यं मनसा स विचिन्त्य च । प्रदास्यते पुत्रवन्तं शान्ताभर्तारमात्मवान् । । 1116 । ।
ramayan::331.verse_hindi: On hearing his words and deeply thinking over the matter, the prudent Romapada  agreed to send, Santas husband (Rsyasringa), capable of blessing him with a son.
ramayan::331.english_translation: On hearing the king's words and thinking it over carefully, the prudent Romapada agreed to send Rsyasringa, Santa's husband, who could grant him a son.
ramayan::331.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राज्ञः (the king's) / अथ (then) / तत्-वाक्यम् (that speech) / मनसा (with the mind) / सः (he) / विचिन्त्य (having reflected) / च (and) / प्रदास्यते (will be given) / पुत्रवन्तम् (the one who can give sons) / शान्ताभर्तारम् (Santa's husband) / आत्मवान् (self-possessed)
ramayan::331.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::331.essence: He decides after reflection, not reflex.
ramayan::331.simple_meaning: Romapada listens, reflects, and agrees to send Rsyasringa so the sacrifice can be performed and a son may be born.
ramayan::331.simple_insight: Careful reflection can turn a request into a decisive, generous response.
ramayan::331.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has asked Romapada for help, because he is childless and needs Rsyasringa to perform the rite. Romapada pauses, thinks it through, and chooses to send him. The verse moves the plan forward, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::331.modern_relevance: A friend asks for help that will inconvenience you. You pause, think it through, and decide with a clear head instead of a quick reaction.
ramayan::331.insight: It shows a ruler making a considered decision, not an impulsive one.

ramayan::332.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च तं विप्रं स राजा विगतज्वर: । आहरिष्यति तं यज्ञं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना । । 1117 । ।
ramayan::332.verse_hindi: The king relieved of his suffering, was highly delighted. He would take the brahmin with him and  perform the sacrificial ritual.
ramayan::332.english_translation: The king, relieved of his burden, became deeply glad and took the brahmin to perform the sacrifice.
ramayan::332.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / च (and) / तं (that) / विप्रं (brahmin) / सः (he) / राजा (king) / विगतज्वरः (free from distress) / आहरिष्यति (will bring) / तम् (that) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / प्रहृष्टेन (with delighted) / अन्तरात्मना (with inner self)
ramayan::332.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::332.essence: Relief turns into motion once the right person is received.
ramayan::332.simple_meaning: The king accepted the brahmin, felt relieved, and prepared to carry out the sacrifice.
ramayan::332.simple_insight: Relief can arrive the moment a burden becomes a plan.
ramayan::332.detailed_meaning: Romapada has just heard how to solve his childless suffering. He receives Rishyasringa, the brahmin whose presence will make the sacrifice possible, and his anxiety lifts. But this is still only the setup for Dasaratha's later request.
ramayan::332.modern_relevance: You finally get the expert on board after weeks of worry. The tension drops, but the real work still begins next.
ramayan::332.insight: It marks the shift from anxious waiting to purposeful action.

ramayan::333.verse_sanskrit: तं च राजा दशरथो यष्टुकाम: कृताञ्जलि: । ऋश्यशृङ्गं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वरयिष्यति धर्मवित् । । 1118 । । यज्ञार्थं प्रसवार्थं च स्वर्गार्थं च नरेश्वर: । लभते च स तं कामं द्विजमुख्याद्विशांपति: । । 1119 । ।
ramayan::333.verse_hindi: King Dasaratha, lord of the people, and knower of dharma and truth, desirous of performing the sacrifice would ask Rsyasringa, with folded palms for granting a boon to perform a sacrifice in order to obtain children and to attain heaven. The king will get those desires fulfilled through that chief brahmin.
ramayan::333.english_translation: King Dasaratha, lord of the people, and knower of dharma and truth, desirous of performing the sacrifice would ask Rsyasringa, with folded palms, for a boon to perform a sacrifice in order to obtain children and to attain heaven. Through that chief brahmin, the king would have those desires fulfilled.
ramayan::333.translation_literal: तं (that him) / च (and) / राजा (the king) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / यष्टुकामः (desiring sacrifice) / कृताञ्जलिः (with folded palms) / ऋश्यशृङ्गम् (Rshyasringa) / द्विजश्रेष्ठम् (best among brahmins) / वरयिष्यति (will ask for a boon) / धर्मवित् (knower of dharma) / यज्ञार्थम् (for the sake of sacrifice) / प्रसवार्थम् (for the sake of children) / च (and) / स्वर्गार्थम् (for the sake of heaven) / च (and) / नरेश्वरः (lord of men) / लभते (will obtain) / च (and) / सः (he) / तं (that) / कामम् (desire) / द्विजमुख्यात् (from the chief of brahmins) / विशांपतिः (lord of the people)
ramayan::333.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::333.essence: A king's wish becomes righteous when it serves duty and the future.
ramayan::333.simple_meaning: Dasharatha humbly asks Rshyasringa for help with a sacrifice meant to bring him sons and secure heavenly merit.
ramayan::333.simple_insight: A private longing can become noble when it is placed in the service of a larger purpose.
ramayan::333.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharatha approaches Rshyasringa with folded hands. He wants a sacrifice not just for personal joy, but to secure heirs and fulfil his royal duty. This moment begins the chain that will lead to Rama's birth.
ramayan::333.modern_relevance: You are not just chasing a personal goal; you are trying to build something that outlives your own need. The question is whether your desire can be disciplined into service.
ramayan::333.insight: It shifts desire from self-fulfilment toward a goal tied to responsibility and continuity.

ramayan::334.verse_hindi: Four sons of immense prowess would be born to him bringing glory and fame to their dynasty. They would be renowned in all the worlds.
ramayan::334.english_translation: Four sons of immense prowess would be born to him, bringing glory and fame to their dynasty. They would be renowned in all the worlds.
ramayan::334.translation_literal: पुत्राः (sons) / च (and) / अस्य (of him) / भविष्यन्ति (will be) / चत्वारः (four) / अमितविक्रमााः (of boundless prowess) / वंशप्रतिष्ठानकराः (makers of the dynasty's standing) / सर्वलोकेषु (in all worlds) / विश्रुताः (well-known)
ramayan::334.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::334.essence: His longing will become a dynasty’s lasting glory.
ramayan::334.simple_meaning: Four mighty sons will be born to King Dasharatha, and they will make his lineage famous everywhere.
ramayan::334.simple_insight: Some promises are bigger than one life. They shape the future of an entire family line.
ramayan::334.detailed_meaning: After Dasaratha seeks the sacrifice that will end his childlessness, the blessing turns toward the future of his house. The promise is not just for a son, but for four sons whose strength and fame will restore the standing of the dynasty.
ramayan::334.modern_relevance: A family waiting on years of hope hears news that changes everything. What looked like a private wish becomes a turning point for everyone who comes after you.
ramayan::334.insight: It shifts attention from personal longing to the larger legacy your choices create.

ramayan::335.verse_sanskrit: एवं स देवप्रवर: पूर्वं कथितवान्कथाम् । सनत्कुमारो भगवान्पुरा देवयुगे प्रभु: । । 11111 । ।
ramayan::335.verse_hindi: In early times of Kritayuga, this story was narrated by the holy and competent  Sanatkumara, the great one among the devatas.
ramayan::335.english_translation: In the age of truth long ago, this story was first told by the blessed Sanatkumara, the lordly one among the radiant beings.
ramayan::335.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / सः (that) / देवप्रवरः (best among the radiant beings) / पूर्वम् (formerly) / कथितवान् (had told) / कथाम् (the story) / सनत्कुमारः (Sanatkumara) / भगवान् (the blessed one) / पुरा (long ago) / देवयुगे (in the age of the radiant beings) / प्रभुः (the lord)
ramayan::335.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::335.essence: The story is being passed down from an older source.
ramayan::335.simple_meaning: Sanatkumara told this story long ago, in an earlier age.
ramayan::335.simple_insight: Some stories are older than memory, yet still carry their power.
ramayan::335.detailed_meaning: The narration pauses to give the story its lineage. Valmiki says this account was first told long ago by Sanatkumara in an earlier age. It is a framing detail, not a teaching of its own.
ramayan::335.modern_relevance: You hear a story and assume it began with the person telling it. Sometimes it has already passed through older voices, carrying memory farther than any one speaker can.
ramayan::335.insight: It places the tale inside an older chain of transmission, not as a fresh lesson.

ramayan::336.verse_sanskrit: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमानय सुसत्कृतम् । स्वयमेव महाराज गत्वा सबलवाहन: । । 11112 । ।
ramayan::336.verse_hindi: Greatest among men, O king, along with vehicles and retinue, you may go and bring him (Rsyasringa) personally with due respect.
ramayan::336.english_translation: Greatest among men, O king, go yourself with your forces and vehicles, and bring him back with full honour.
ramayan::336.translation_literal: स (that) / त्वं (you) / पुरुषशार्दूल (tiger among men) / तमानय (bring him) / सुसत्कृतम् (with full honour) / स्वयमेव (yourself) / महाराज (great king) / गत्वा (having gone) / सबलवाहन: (with forces and vehicles)
ramayan::336.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::336.essence: What matters most should be carried by your own hands.
ramayan::336.simple_meaning: The king is told to go personally, with an honoured escort, and bring Rishyasringa back.
ramayan::336.simple_insight: Some duties are too important to delegate. Respect is shown by your own presence.
ramayan::336.detailed_meaning: The court has heard that Rishyasringa is the one who can help end the king's crisis. Now the instruction is direct: Dasharatha should not send a messenger, but go himself with royal honour and bring the sage back.
ramayan::336.modern_relevance: A parent drives across town instead of sending a text. A leader shows up in person for the hard conversation. Some moments need your own presence, not convenience.
ramayan::336.insight: It shifts responsibility from delegation to direct, respectful action.

ramayan::337.verse_sanskrit: अनुमान्य वसिष्ठं च सूतवाक्यं निशम्य च । सान्त:पुरस्सहामात्य: प्रययौ यत्र स द्विज: । । 11113 । ।
ramayan::337.verse_hindi: Having heard the charioteers words and having obtained the consent of Vasishta, he    along with his queens and courtiers departed to the place where the brahmin (Rsyasringa) resided.
ramayan::337.english_translation: Having heard the charioteers' words and having obtained Vasishta's consent, the king, with his queens and courtiers, departed to the place where the brahmin Rsyasringa lived.
ramayan::337.translation_literal: अनुमान्य (having obtained consent) / वसिष्ठं (Vasishta) / च (and) / सूतवाक्यं (the charioteers' words) / निशम्य (having heard) / च (and) / सान्त:पुरस्सहामात्य: (with the inner palace and ministers) / प्रययौ (departed) / यत्र (where) / स (he) / द्विज: (the brahmin)
ramayan::337.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::337.essence: A serious move begins only after the right counsel is heard.
ramayan::337.simple_meaning: The king first checked with Vasishta, then set out with his queens and ministers to meet the brahmin Rsyasringa.
ramayan::337.simple_insight: Even an urgent mission moves better when counsel and consent are in place.
ramayan::337.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has decided to bring Rsyasringa to Ayodhya. Before leaving, he listens to his charioteers and secures Vasishta's approval. Then he travels with his queens and ministers toward the hermitage, setting the next turn of the story in motion.
ramayan::337.modern_relevance: You finally decide to make the call, but you still check with the people who matter before you move. Some decisions need speed; others need alignment first.
ramayan::337.insight: It shifts action from impulse to coordinated movement, showing that important steps can begin with consent and consultation.

ramayan::338.verse_sanskrit: वनानि सरितश्चैव व्यतिक्रम्य शनैश्शनै: । अभिचक्राम तं देशं यत्र वै मुनिपुङ्गव: । । 11114 । ।
ramayan::338.verse_hindi: Crossing forests and rivers slowly, the king reached the place where that foremost of
ramayan::338.english_translation: Crossing forests and rivers slowly, the king reached the place where that foremost of sages was.
ramayan::338.translation_literal: वनानि (forests) / सरितः (rivers) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / व्यतिक्रम्य (having crossed) / शनैः शनैः (slowly, slowly) / अभिचक्राम (approached, reached) / तं (that) / देशं (place) / यत्र (where) / वै (indeed) / मुनिपुङ्गवः (foremost of sages)
ramayan::338.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::338.essence: The journey matters because it leads to a meeting that cannot be rushed.
ramayan::338.simple_meaning: The king traveled slowly through forests and rivers until he reached the sage’s dwelling place.
ramayan::338.simple_insight: Some journeys are measured by reverence, not speed.
ramayan::338.detailed_meaning: After receiving permission, the king leaves with his retinue and travels through wild country toward the sage’s home. This line simply marks the approach, setting up the meeting with Rishyashringa that follows.
ramayan::338.modern_relevance: You drive for hours through rain and traffic to meet someone whose presence matters. The distance feels different when the meeting itself is the point.
ramayan::338.insight: It shifts attention from action to arrival, preparing the reader for the real encounter.

ramayan::339.verse_sanskrit: आसाद्य तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं रोमपादसमीपगम् । ऋषिपुत्रं ददर्शादौ दीप्यमानमिवानलम् । । 11115 । ।
ramayan::339.verse_hindi: He reached the spot and saw the son of the ascetic, the best of brahmins glowing like fire seated next to Romapada.
ramayan::339.english_translation: He reached the spot and saw the son of the ascetic, the best of brahmins, glowing like fire seated next to Romapada.
ramayan::339.translation_literal: आसाद्य (having reached) / तम् (that) / द्विजश्रेष्ठम् (best of brahmins) / रोमपादसमीपगम् (seated near Romapada) / ऋषिपुत्रम् (son of the ascetic) / ददर्श (saw) / आदौ (at first) / दीप्यमानम् इव (as if glowing) / अनलम् (fire)
ramayan::339.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::339.essence: Presence can announce importance before a single word is spoken.
ramayan::339.simple_meaning: Dasaratha arrives and sees the sage's son near Romapada, shining with a fiery presence.
ramayan::339.simple_insight: Some people enter a room with such presence that everyone feels it at once.
ramayan::339.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has travelled through forests and rivers to meet the sage's son near Romapada. The meeting is still just beginning, but the scene already marks the man's presence as powerful and radiant rather than ordinary.
ramayan::339.modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting and instantly notice the one person everyone else seems to orient around. Before anyone speaks, their presence has already set the tone.
ramayan::339.insight: It frames a figure through visible radiance, preparing the scene for an important encounter.

ramayan::340.verse_sanskrit: ततो राजा यथान्यायं पूजां चक्रे विशेषत: । सखित्वात्तस्य वै राज्ञ: प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना । । 11116 । ।
ramayan::340.verse_hindi: Then the king (Romapada), delighted at heart out of friendship with the king (Dasaratha), offered special hospitality with respectful salutations in accordance with propriety.
ramayan::340.english_translation: Then the king, delighted at heart out of friendship with the king, offered special hospitality with respectful salutations in accordance with propriety.
ramayan::340.translation_literal: तत: (then) / राजा (the king) / यथान्यायम् (according to propriety) / पूजाम् (hospitality, honor) / चक्रे (did) / विशेषत: (especially) / सखित्वात् (because of friendship) / तस्य (of that) / वै (indeed) / राज्ञ: (of the king) / प्रहृष्टेन (with delighted) / अन्तरात्मना (with inner heart)
ramayan::340.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::340.essence: Courtesy becomes richer when friendship gives it warmth.
ramayan::340.simple_meaning: Romapada welcomed Dasharatha with special honor, not just as a guest but as a friend, and did so with genuine joy.
ramayan::340.simple_insight: True hospitality feels different when friendship is behind it.
ramayan::340.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has reached the hermitage area after a long journey. Romapada receives him warmly and properly, honoring both royal etiquette and their personal bond. The verse is a small bridge in the larger meeting before the Rishyasringa episode unfolds.
ramayan::340.modern_relevance: You open the door for someone who mattered to you years ago. The meal, the welcome, the extra care — all of it says the relationship still lives.
ramayan::340.insight: It shows how respect becomes deeper when it is joined with real affection.

ramayan::341.verse_sanskrit: रोमपादेन चाख्यातमृषिपुत्राय धीमते । सख्यं सम्बन्धकं चैव तदा तं प्रत्यपूजयत् । । 11117 । ।
ramayan::341.verse_hindi: Romapada explained his friendship and relationship with him (Dasaratha). Rsyasringa of great intellect in return felicitated Dasaratha.
ramayan::341.english_translation: Romapada explained his friendship and family connection with him. The wise Rsyasringa then honoured Dasaratha in return.
ramayan::341.translation_literal: रोमपादेन (by Romapada) / च (and) / आख्यातम् (was explained) / ऋषिपुत्राय (to the son of the ascetic) / धीमते (to the wise one) / सख्यम् (friendship) / सम्बन्धकम् (relationship) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तदा (then) / तम् (him) / प्रत्यपूजयत् (honoured in return)
ramayan::341.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::341.essence: Courtesy follows when friendship is openly recognised.
ramayan::341.simple_meaning: Romapada told Rsyasringa about his friendship and family tie with Dasaratha, and Rsyasringa responded with respect.
ramayan::341.simple_insight: Respect deepens when goodwill is openly named and returned.
ramayan::341.detailed_meaning: Romapada has welcomed Dasaratha's purpose with honor and hospitality. Now he explains the bond between them to Rsyasringa, who is wise enough to answer with courtesy. The verse simply marks this exchange before the king stays on and speaks.
ramayan::341.modern_relevance: At a dinner where two families are meeting for the first time, someone finally names the shared history that made the meeting possible. The room relaxes the moment respect is returned.
ramayan::341.insight: It shows how social bonds are strengthened by acknowledging connection and responding with proper honor.

ramayan::342.verse_sanskrit: एवं सुसत्कृतस्तेन सहोषित्वा नरर्षभ: । सप्ताष्टदिवसान्राजा राजानमिदमब्रवीत् । । 11118 । ।
ramayan::342.verse_hindi: In this manner, the great among men, the king wellhonoured by Romapada, spent seven or eight days there.And then spoke this to Romapada:
ramayan::342.english_translation: In this manner, the great among men, the king, well honoured by Romapada, spent seven or eight days there. Then he spoke this to Romapada:
ramayan::342.translation_literal: एवम् (in this manner) / सुसत्कृतः (well honoured) / तेन (by him) / सहोषित्वा (having stayed together) / नरर्षभः (bull among men) / सप्ताष्टदिवसान् (seven or eight days) / राजा (the king) / राजानम् (to the king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::342.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::342.essence: The meeting pauses before the real request begins.
ramayan::342.simple_meaning: Rama stayed as an honoured guest for several days, then spoke to Romapada.
ramayan::342.simple_insight: Some moments matter only because they prepare the next decisive act.
ramayan::342.detailed_meaning: Romapada has welcomed the visiting king with great respect. After several days of hospitality, the king finally speaks, setting up the real purpose of the meeting that follows in the next verse.
ramayan::342.modern_relevance: You sit through the polite conversation, the tea, the small talk, knowing the real request will come next.
ramayan::342.insight: It marks the transition from hospitality to the actual purpose of the visit.

ramayan::343.verse_sanskrit: शान्ता तव सुता राजन् सह भर्त्रा विशांपते । मदीयनगरं यातु कार्यं हि महदुद्यतम् । । 11119 । ।
ramayan::343.verse_hindi: O lord of people, O king, It has been decided to commence an important sacrificial rite. You may send your daughter Santa along with her husband to my city.
ramayan::343.english_translation: O lord of people, O king, Shanta, your daughter, should go to my city with her husband. A great sacrificial rite is about to begin.
ramayan::343.translation_literal: शान्ता (Shanta) / तव (your) / सुता (daughter) / राजन् (O king) / सह (with) / भर्त्रा (with husband) / विशांपते (O lord of people) / मदीय-नगरं (my city) / यातु (should go) / कार्यं (task) / हि (indeed) / महत् (great) / उद्यतम् (about to begin)
ramayan::343.speaker: Romapada
ramayan::343.essence: A sacred task can require family to be rearranged.
ramayan::343.simple_meaning: Romapada asks King Dasharatha to send Shanta with her husband to his city, because a major sacrificial rite is being prepared there.
ramayan::343.simple_insight: Some duties are shared across households, and a sacred task can reshape family arrangements.
ramayan::343.detailed_meaning: Romapada, speaking after honouring the visiting sage Rishyashringa, asks Dasharatha to send Shanta and her husband to his city. The request is practical, not philosophical: a major rite is about to begin, and their presence is needed for it.
ramayan::343.modern_relevance: A family calendar, a wedding plan, and a ceremony all collide at once, and someone has to be moved with care. The verse is about making room for a larger duty without losing respect.
ramayan::343.insight: It teaches you to let immediate convenience yield to a larger obligation.

ramayan::344.verse_sanskrit: तथेति राजा संश्रुत्य गमनं तस्य धीमत: । उवाच वचनं विप्रं गच्छ त्वं सह भार्यया । । 11120 । ।
ramayan::344.verse_hindi: Having agreed to the departure of the sage Romapada said, Be pleased to go (to Ayodhya) together with your wife.
ramayan::344.english_translation: Having agreed to the departure of the sage, Romapada said, 'Go with your wife.'
ramayan::344.translation_literal: तथेति (so saying) / राजा (the king) / संश्रुत्य (having agreed) / गमनं (departure) / तस्य (of him) / धीमतः (of the wise one) / उवाच (said) / वचनं (words) / विप्रं (to the sage) / गच्छ (go) / त्वं (you) / सह (together with) / भार्यया (with wife)
ramayan::344.speaker: Romapada
ramayan::344.essence: Permission is granted, and the journey can finally move forward.
ramayan::344.simple_meaning: King Romapada agrees to the sage's departure and tells him to go with his wife.
ramayan::344.simple_insight: A formal permission is given. The journey can now begin.
ramayan::344.detailed_meaning: Romapada has hosted the sage for several days and has just heard the request about sending Shanta. He now grants permission for the sage to depart with his wife, clearing the way for the next step in the arrangement.
ramayan::344.modern_relevance: A parent finally says yes to a plan after days of discussion. The tension lifts, not because everything is solved, but because the path forward is now open.
ramayan::344.insight: It marks the moment consent replaces delay and the transition becomes possible.

ramayan::345.verse_sanskrit: ऋषिपुत्र: प्रतिश्रुत्य तथेत्याह नृपं तदा । स नृपेणाभ्यनुज्ञात: प्रययौ सह भार्यया । । 11121 । ।
ramayan::345.verse_hindi: The son of the sage assented to the kings command saying So be it. And permitted by him, departed along with wife (for Ayodhya).
ramayan::345.english_translation: The sage’s son agreed, saying, “So be it.” Permitted by the king, he departed with his wife for Ayodhya.
ramayan::345.translation_literal: ऋषिपुत्र: (the sage's son) / प्रतिश्रुत्य (having agreed) / तथेत्याह (said “so be it”) / नृपं (to the king) / तदा (then) / स (he) / नृपेण (by the king) / अभ्यनुज्ञात: (permitted) / प्रययौ (departed) / सह (together with) / भार्यया (wife)
ramayan::345.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::345.essence: Agreement and permission let the journey begin without strain.
ramayan::345.simple_meaning: The sage’s son accepted the king’s request and left with his wife for Ayodhya.
ramayan::345.simple_insight: A respectful agreement can move events forward without conflict.
ramayan::345.detailed_meaning: Romapada has agreed to send his daughter Shanta to the sage’s home. Now the sage’s son gives his consent, receives the king’s leave, and departs with his wife for Ayodhya. The verse simply completes the exchange.
ramayan::345.modern_relevance: You finally say yes to a family request, and the whole plan begins to move. Sometimes one calm agreement is all that is needed.
ramayan::345.insight: It shows how mutual consent and courtesy can resolve a delicate arrangement cleanly.

ramayan::346.verse_sanskrit: तावन्योन्याञ्जलिं कृत्वा स्नेहात्संश्लिष्य चोरसा । ननन्दतुर्दशरथो रोमपादश्च वीर्यवान् । । 11122 । ।
ramayan::346.verse_hindi: Dasaratha and Romapada, pleased with this, wished each other with folded palms and hugged each other with love.
ramayan::346.english_translation: Dasaratha and Romapada, pleased with this, wished each other with folded palms and hugged each other with love.
ramayan::346.translation_literal: ताव् (those two) / अन्योन्याञ्जलिं (mutual folded-palms greeting) / कृत्वा (having made) / स्नेहात् (from affection) / संश्लिष्य (embracing) / चोरसा (with the chest) / ननन्दतुḥ (rejoiced) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / रोमपादः (Romapada) / च (and) / वीर्यवान् (the valiant)
ramayan::346.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::346.essence: Agreement can end in warmth, not distance.
ramayan::346.simple_meaning: Two allied kings greet each other with respect and affection, then embrace warmly. The verse simply marks the joy of their reunion.
ramayan::346.simple_insight: Some bonds are sealed not by words, but by mutual respect and warmth.
ramayan::346.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha and Romapada have just agreed on the sage's departure. With the matter settled, the two kings exchange folded-palms greetings and embrace. The verse is a brief bridge between negotiation and departure, showing friendship and relief rather than teaching.
ramayan::346.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, the room goes quiet and both people finally exhale. The agreement is done; what remains is the human warmth of being on good terms again.
ramayan::346.insight: It marks closure after negotiation and shows how respect can soften a formal exchange.

ramayan::347.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सुहृदमापृच्छ्य प्रस्थितो रघुनन्दन: । पौरेभ्य: प्रेषयामास दूतान्वै शीघ्रगामिन: । । 11123 । ।
ramayan::347.verse_hindi: Then king Dasaratha, took leave of  his friend and set out. He despatched swiftfooted messengers to the citizens with the command.
ramayan::347.english_translation: Then king Dasaratha took leave of his friend and set out. He sent swift messengers to the citizens with his command.
ramayan::347.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / सुहृदम् (the friend) / आपृच्छ्य (taking leave) / प्रस्थितो (set out) / रघुनन्दनः (Dasaratha, delight of the Raghu line) / पौरेभ्यः (to the citizens) / प्रेषयामास (sent) / दूतान् (messengers) / वै (indeed) / शीघ्रगामिनः (swift-footed)
ramayan::347.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::347.essence: The story shifts forward; the king’s next duty begins.
ramayan::347.simple_meaning: Dasaratha leaves his friend and sends quick messengers to the people with instructions.
ramayan::347.simple_insight: Some moments are only about movement and preparation, not meaning.
ramayan::347.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just parted from his friend Romapada. Now he turns back toward Ayodhya and sends fast messengers ahead to the citizens. The verse simply moves the story into the next scene of royal preparation.
ramayan::347.modern_relevance: A train pulls out and your phone starts lighting up with messages to handle before you arrive. This verse is the motion before the real work begins.
ramayan::347.insight: It marks a transition from private meeting to public action.

ramayan::348.verse_sanskrit: क्रियतां नगरं सर्वं क्षिप्रमेव स्वलङ्कृतम् । धूपितं सिक्तसम्मृष्टं पताकाभिरलङ्कृतम् । । 11124 । ।
ramayan::348.verse_hindi: Let the entire city be welldecorated, perfumed, sprinkled with water and cleaned with flags hoisted.
ramayan::348.english_translation: Let the entire city be quickly decorated, perfumed, sprinkled with water, cleaned, and adorned with flags.
ramayan::348.translation_literal: क्रियताम् (let it be done) / नगरम् (the city) / सर्वम् (entire) / क्षिप्रम् एव (very quickly) / स्वलङ्कृतम् (well-decorated) / धूपितम् (perfumed) / सिक्त (sprinkled with water) / सम्मृष्टम् (swept clean) / पताकाभिः (with flags) / अलङ्कृतम् (adorned)
ramayan::348.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::348.essence: A welcome begins long before the guest arrives.
ramayan::348.simple_meaning: The city is being prepared in a hurry for an important arrival. Everything is cleaned, scented, decorated, and made festive.
ramayan::348.simple_insight: Small acts of care can turn an ordinary place into a welcome.
ramayan::348.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just set out after meeting Romapada, and messengers rush ahead to prepare the city for his return. This verse lists the practical work of welcome: cleaning, perfuming, sprinkling water, and decorating with flags.
ramayan::348.modern_relevance: You get a last-minute text that someone important is coming over, and suddenly the whole house changes. Floors are swept, cushions fixed, incense lit, and every corner made ready.
ramayan::348.insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the visible care that makes them feel sacred.

ramayan::349.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रहृष्टा: पौरास्ते श्रुत्वा राजानमागतम् । तथा प्रचक्रुस्तत्सर्वं राज्ञा यत्प्रेषितं तदा । । 11125 । ।
ramayan::349.verse_hindi: The people of the city having heard the kings arrival were overjoyed. They did
ramayan::349.english_translation: Then, hearing that the king had arrived, the city people were delighted and carried out everything the king had ordered.
ramayan::349.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रहृष्टा: (delighted) / पौराः (the city people) / ते (they) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राजानम् (the king) / आगतम् (arrived) / तथा (thus) / प्रचक्रुः (they carried out) / तत् सर्वम् (all that) / राज्ञा (by the king) / यत् (which) / प्रेषितम् (sent/ordered) / तदा (then)
ramayan::349.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::349.essence: Joy and loyalty turn the king's order into instant action.
ramayan::349.simple_meaning: The citizens were happy to hear the king had arrived, so they quickly did everything he had asked.
ramayan::349.simple_insight: A community moves with ease when it trusts its leader.
ramayan::349.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has sent word ahead, asking the city to be prepared for his return. The citizens hear the news and respond at once, turning his instructions into action. This is a brief scene of public joy and orderly obedience before the king enters Ayodhya.
ramayan::349.modern_relevance: A group chat lights up with news that the team lead is coming in person, and everyone instantly fixes the room, the files, and their own posture. Respect turns into action before anyone has to ask twice.
ramayan::349.insight: It shows how trust and goodwill make instruction easy to fulfill.

ramayan::350.verse_sanskrit: ततस्स्वलङ्कृतं राजा नगरं प्रविवेश ह । शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषै: पुरस्कृत्य द्विजर्षभम् । । 11126 । ।
ramayan::350.verse_hindi: Then the king entered that welldecorated city amidst blares of conches and the beating of drums, with the best of the brahmins (Rsyasringa) in the forefront.
ramayan::350.english_translation: Then the king entered that well-decorated city amidst blares of conches and the beating of drums, with the best of the brahmins, Rsyasringa, in the forefront.
ramayan::350.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / स्वलङ्कृतम् (well-decorated) / राजा (the king) / नगरम् (the city) / प्रविवेश (entered) / ह (indeed) / शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः (with the sounds of conches and drums) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front) / द्विजर्षभम् (the best of the brahmins)
ramayan::350.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::350.essence: The return is made public through ceremony, not words.
ramayan::350.simple_meaning: The king entered the decorated city in a grand procession, with conches and drums sounding and Rsyasringa leading the way.
ramayan::350.simple_insight: A public honor can turn a return into a celebration.
ramayan::350.detailed_meaning: After the city is prepared and the people rejoice, the king enters Ayodhya in splendor with Rsyasringa at the front. The verse is part of a ceremonial arrival, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::350.modern_relevance: A wedding procession moves slowly through streets lined with people, music rising above the traffic. The moment is about arrival, honor, and shared joy, not reflection.
ramayan::350.insight: It marks a formal entrance and shows the city honoring both king and brahmin.

ramayan::351.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रमुदितास्सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तं नागरा द्विजम् । प्रवेश्यमानं सत्कृत्य नरेन्द्रेणेन्द्रकर्मणा । । 11127 । ।
ramayan::351.verse_hindi: The citizens were delighted to behold that brahmin entering the city duly honoured by the king who was equivalent to Indra in valiance৷৷
ramayan::351.english_translation: Then all the citizens were delighted to see that brahmin entering the city, respectfully honoured by the king whose deeds were like Indra's.
ramayan::351.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रमुदिताः (delighted) / सर्वे (all) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तम् (that) / नागराः (citizens) / द्विजम् (brahmin) / प्रवेश्यमानम् (being brought in) / सत्कृत्य (having honoured respectfully) / नरेन्द्रेण (by the king) / इन्द्रकर्मणा (whose deeds are like Indra's)
ramayan::351.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::351.essence: Public honour can make an entire city rejoice.
ramayan::351.simple_meaning: The citizens were happy to see the respected brahmin enter the city with royal honour.
ramayan::351.simple_insight: Respect can turn a public arrival into a shared moment of joy.
ramayan::351.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has returned to Ayodhya with the brahmin guest he has honoured. The city sees the procession, the king's splendour, and the honoured visitor entering safely. The verse lingers on the citizens' delight, not on any teaching.
ramayan::351.modern_relevance: A crowd parts to let someone important through, and everyone can feel the dignity of the moment. Sometimes public respect itself creates the atmosphere of joy.
ramayan::351.insight: It shows how visible honour from a leader can lift the mood of an entire city.

ramayan::352.verse_sanskrit: अन्त:पुरं प्रवेश्यैनं पूजां कृत्वा च शास्त्रत: । कृतकृत्यं तदात्मानं मेने तस्योपवाहनात् । । 11128 । ।
ramayan::352.verse_hindi: He (king Dasaratha) took him in to the inner apartment and extended welcome. He thought that he has as enjoined by the sastras accomplished his objective by bringing him (Rsyasringa).
ramayan::352.english_translation: He brought him into the inner apartment, offered the proper welcome according to scripture, and felt that he had fulfilled his purpose by bringing him there.
ramayan::352.translation_literal: अन्त:पुरं (inner apartment) / प्रवेश्य (having brought in) / एनं (him) / पूजां (worship / honour) / कृत्वा (having done) / च (and) / शास्त्रत: (according to scripture) / कृतकृत्यम् (having accomplished what was to be done) / तत्-आत्मानम् (himself) / मेने (he thought) / तस्य (of that) / उपवाहनात् (by bringing / escorting)
ramayan::352.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::352.essence: Completion can feel sacred when a needed task is finally done.
ramayan::352.simple_meaning: Dasharatha brought Rishyashringa into the palace, honoured him properly, and felt relieved that the ritual purpose had been completed.
ramayan::352.simple_insight: A long-awaited task can end in a quiet sense of completion.
ramayan::352.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has finally brought Rishyashringa into the inner palace after the public welcome. He follows the required forms exactly, and in that moment he feels the ritual objective has been achieved. The scene is part of the effort to secure a child for the royal line.
ramayan::352.modern_relevance: You finally get the person, document, or approval you needed after weeks of effort. The relief is not dramatic — just the calm of knowing the hard part is done.
ramayan::352.insight: It shows how formal action can carry deep emotional release when a long obligation is fulfilled.

ramayan::353.verse_sanskrit: अन्त:पुरस्त्रियस्सर्वाश्शान्तां दृष्ट्वा तथागताम् । सह भर्त्रा विशालाक्षीं प्रीत्यानन्दमुपागमन् । । 11129 । ।
ramayan::353.verse_hindi: All the royal ladies, experienced immense delight when they saw the largeeyed Shanta arriving  along with her husband in that manner.
ramayan::353.english_translation: All the royal women felt deep joy when they saw Shanta, the large-eyed one, arriving in that way with her husband.
ramayan::353.translation_literal: अन्त:पुरस्त्रियः (the women of the inner apartments) / सर्वाः (all) / शान्ताम् (Shanta) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तथा-आगतम् (arrived in that manner) / सह भर्त्रा (with her husband) / विशालाक्षीम् (the large-eyed one) / प्रीत्या (with delight) / आनन्दम् (joy) / उपागमन् (they approached / experienced)
ramayan::353.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::353.essence: Her return filled the palace with joy.
ramayan::353.simple_meaning: The women in the palace were overjoyed to see Shanta return with her husband.
ramayan::353.simple_insight: A long-awaited arrival can soften an entire household at once.
ramayan::353.detailed_meaning: Shanta has entered the inner palace with the brahmin husband who brought her back into royal life. The women of Dasharatha’s household see her arrival and respond with delight, marking a moment of reunion and welcome rather than teaching.
ramayan::353.modern_relevance: You open the door and see someone return with the person they chose. The room changes before anyone speaks.
ramayan::353.insight: It shows how reunion itself can be the event, with no further lesson needed.

ramayan::354.verse_sanskrit: पूज्यमाना च ताभिस्सा राज्ञा चैव विशेषत: । उवास तत्र सुखिता कञ्चित्कालं सहर्त्विजा । । 11130 । ।
ramayan::354.verse_hindi: Honoured and worshipped by royal ladies, especially by king Dasaratha, Santa dwelt there for some time comfortably with the sage.
ramayan::354.english_translation: Honoured and worshipped by the royal ladies, and especially by King Dasaratha, Shanta dwelt there happily for some time with the sage.
ramayan::354.translation_literal: पूज्यमाना (being honoured) / च (and) / ताभिः (by them) / सा (she) / राज्ञा (by the king) / च एव (and indeed) / विशेषत: (especially) / उवास (dwelt) / तत्र (there) / सुखिता (happy) / कञ्चित्-कालं (for some time) / सह-ऋत्विजा (with the sage-priest)
ramayan::354.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::354.essence: Brief welcome can feel like home before the story moves again.
ramayan::354.simple_meaning: Shanta stayed there for a while in comfort, respected by the royal women and especially by Dasaratha.
ramayan::354.simple_insight: A welcomed return can soften old wounds, even if only for a little while.
ramayan::354.detailed_meaning: Shanta has been brought into Ayodhya and received with honor. Dasaratha and the women of the palace treat her with special warmth, and she lives there peacefully with her husband. The verse simply marks a brief season of ease before the larger story moves on.
ramayan::354.modern_relevance: You finally arrive at a family gathering where the tension has eased. People who once kept distance now greet you warmly, and for a moment the room feels repaired.
ramayan::354.insight: It pauses the story to show a fragile peace before the next turn of fate.

ramayan::355.verse_sanskrit: तत: काले बहुतिथे कस्मिंश्चित्सुमनोहरे । वसन्ते समनुप्राप्ते राज्ञो यष्टुं मनोऽभवत् । । 1121 । ।
ramayan::355.verse_hindi: After a long time, at the advent of charming spring a desire arose in the mind of the king (Dasaratha) to perform the sacrifice.
ramayan::355.english_translation: After a long time, when the lovely spring had arrived, King Dasharatha felt the desire to perform a sacrifice.
ramayan::355.translation_literal: तत: (then) / काले (at the time) / बहुतिथे (after a long time) / कस्मिंश्चित् (some) / सुमनोहरे (beautiful) / वसन्ते (in spring) / समनुप्राप्ते (having arrived) / राज्ञः (of the king) / यष्टुम् (to sacrifice) / मनः (mind) / अभवत् (became)
ramayan::355.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::355.essence: The season returns, and so does the king's resolve.
ramayan::355.simple_meaning: After waiting a long time, Dasharatha’s mind turns toward performing a sacrifice when spring arrives.
ramayan::355.simple_insight: A long-delayed wish can return with fresh urgency when the season is right.
ramayan::355.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Shanta has settled in with her husband and been honored by the royal household, Dasharatha feels the pull of spring and turns again toward a sacrifice. This verse only sets up the ritual that will lead to the birth of his sons.
ramayan::355.modern_relevance: You keep postponing something important, and then one morning the timing finally feels right. The urge returns with force, and you know the next step has begun.
ramayan::355.insight: It shifts attention from delay to readiness: the right moment can awaken a dormant resolve.

ramayan::356.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रसाद्य शिरसा तं विप्रं देववर्णिनम् । यज्ञाय वरयामास सन्तानार्थं कुलस्य वै । । 1122 । ।
ramayan::356.verse_hindi: Then bowing his head in respect to that brahmin who was effulgent like a celestial  and having won his grace he chose him to conduct a sacrifice for a son for (the continuity of) his dynasty.
ramayan::356.english_translation: Then bowing his head in respect to that brahmin who was effulgent like a celestial being, and having won his grace, he chose him to conduct a sacrifice for a son for the continuity of his dynasty.
ramayan::356.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रसाद्य (having appeased) / शिरसा (with the head) / तं (that) / विप्रं (brahmin) / देववर्णिनम् (celestial-like, effulgent) / यज्ञाय (for the sacrifice) / वरयामास (chose) / सन्तानार्थं (for offspring) / कुलस्य (of the dynasty) / वै (indeed)
ramayan::356.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::356.essence: Humility becomes the first step toward fulfilling a longing that cannot be forced.
ramayan::356.simple_meaning: Dasharatha respectfully approaches a radiant priest and asks him to lead a sacrifice meant to secure an heir for his royal line.
ramayan::356.simple_insight: Some needs are so deep that even a king must bow before asking for help.
ramayan::356.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has long lacked a son. Now, after the return of spring, he bows before the priest and asks him to conduct the sacrifice that may give his dynasty an heir. The verse marks the turning point from longing to action.
ramayan::356.modern_relevance: You have done everything you can, and the next step is to ask for help with humility. Sometimes the door opens only after pride does.
ramayan::356.insight: It shifts the mind from private longing to disciplined action through respectful seeking.

ramayan::357.verse_sanskrit: तथेति च स राजानमुवाच च सुसत्कृत: । सम्भारा सम्भ्रियन्तां ते तुरगश्च विमुच्यताम् । । 1123 । ।
ramayan::357.verse_hindi: The wellhonoured brahmin agreed, saying, Be it so, let the requisite materials be procured and the sacificial horse, released.
ramayan::357.english_translation: The well-honoured brahmin agreed, saying, "So be it. Let the required materials be gathered, and let the sacrificial horse be released."
ramayan::357.translation_literal: तथेति (so be it) / च (and) / सः (he) / राजानम् (to the king) / उवाच (said) / च (and) / सुसत्कृतः (well-honoured) / सम्भाराः (materials / provisions) / सम्भ्रियन्ताम् (let be gathered) / ते (your) / तुरगः (horse) / च (and) / विमुच्यताम् (let be released)
ramayan::357.speaker: Brahmin
ramayan::357.essence: Agreement becomes action through clear instructions.
ramayan::357.simple_meaning: The priest accepts the king's request and tells him to gather the ritual supplies and release the horse.
ramayan::357.simple_insight: A major ritual begins with a simple agreement and the first practical steps.
ramayan::357.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has asked the priest to begin the horse sacrifice for a son. The priest agrees at once and gives the first instructions: gather the materials and free the horse. The verse is a procedural step in the larger ritual sequence.
ramayan::357.modern_relevance: You finally get the green light on something important, and the next step is practical, not dramatic: gather what you need and begin.
ramayan::357.insight: It shifts attention from desire to execution, from wanting a result to preparing the work.

ramayan::358.verse_sanskrit: ततो राजाऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रिसत्तमम् । सुमन्त्रावाहय क्षिप्रं ऋत्विजो ब्रह्मवादिन: । । 1124 । । सुयज्ञं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ काश्यपम् । पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च ये चान्ये द्विजसत्तमा: । । 1125 । ।
ramayan::358.verse_hindi: Thereafter the king said to Sumantra, Summon immediately, Suyajna, Vamadeva, Jabali and Kasyapa, family priest Vasishta and other foremost and learned brahmins who are the official priests wellversed in the Vedas.
ramayan::358.english_translation: Thereafter the king said to Sumantra, "Summon immediately the priests and Vedic scholars: Suyajna, Vamadeva, Jabali, Kashyapa, the family priest Vasishta, and all other foremost brahmins."
ramayan::358.translation_literal: तत: (thereafter) / राजाऽब्रवीद् (the king said) / वाक्यम् (speech) / सुमन्त्रम् (to Sumantra) / मन्त्रिसत्तमम् (the foremost minister) / सुमन्त्र (Sumantra) / आवाहय (summon) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / ऋत्विजः (priests) / ब्रह्मवादिनः (Vedic scholars) / सुयज्ञम् (Suyajna) / वामदेवम् (Vamadeva) / च (and) / जाबालिम् (Jabali) / अथ (then) / काश्यपम् (Kashyapa) / पुरोहितम् (family priest) / वसिष्ठम् (Vasishta) / च (and) / ये (who) / च (and) / अन्ये (others) / द्विजसत्तमाः (foremost brahmins)
ramayan::358.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::358.essence: The king turns intention into action by summoning the right people.
ramayan::358.simple_meaning: The king orders Sumantra to gather the priests and learned brahmins at once.
ramayan::358.simple_insight: Sometimes a great ritual begins with one clear command.
ramayan::358.detailed_meaning: After securing the brahmin's agreement, the king turns to Sumantra and orders him to bring the ritual experts, Vasishta, and the other learned priests. The sacrifice is now moving from intention into action.
ramayan::358.modern_relevance: A major event is finally underway, and someone has to make the calls, gather the people, and set everything in motion.
ramayan::358.insight: It shows the shift from decision to execution, with authority moving through an organized chain.

ramayan::359.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितं गत्वा त्वरितविक्रम: । समानयत्स तान्विप्रान् समस्तान्वेदपारगान् । । 1126 । ।
ramayan::359.verse_hindi: Then Sumantra, a man of smart movement went immediately and brought all those brahmins who were wellversed in the Vedas.
ramayan::359.english_translation: Then Sumantra, swift in movement, quickly brought together all those brahmins who were well-versed in the Vedas.
ramayan::359.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / सुमन्त्रः (Sumantra) / त्वरितम् (quickly) / गत्वा (having gone) / त्वरितविक्रमः (swift in movement) / समानयत् (brought together) / स (he) / तान् (those) / विप्रान् (brahmins) / समस्तान् (all) / वेदपारगान् (well-versed in the Vedas)
ramayan::359.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::359.essence: Preparation matters before any solemn act can begin.
ramayan::359.simple_meaning: Sumantra quickly gathered the learned brahmins that the king had summoned.
ramayan::359.simple_insight: Some moments are only about moving the right people into place.
ramayan::359.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharatha has begun arranging a sacred rite and has asked for the priests. Sumantra immediately goes and brings the brahmins who know the Vedas, clearing the way for the king's next step.
ramayan::359.modern_relevance: A senior leader sends a last-minute message, and everyone scrambles to gather the right experts before the meeting starts. The real work begins only after the room is ready.
ramayan::359.insight: It shows the importance of swift, precise support before any major undertaking begins.

ramayan::360.verse_sanskrit: तान्पूजयित्वा धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्तदा । धर्मार्थसहितं युक्तं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 1127 । ।
ramayan::360.verse_hindi: After paying respect to them (learned brahmins), virtuous king Dasaratha graciously uttered these words charged with dharma and artha.
ramayan::360.english_translation: After honoring those learned brahmins, the righteous king Dasharatha then spoke gentle words filled with dharma and artha.
ramayan::360.translation_literal: तान् (those) / पूजयित्वा (having honored) / धर्मात्मा (righteous in nature) / राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / तदा (then) / धर्मार्थसहितम् (joined with dharma and artha) / युक्तम् (fit / proper) / श्लक्ष्णम् (gentle / soft) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::360.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::360.essence: Honor and restraint prepare the ground for a painful truth.
ramayan::360.simple_meaning: Dasharatha respectfully greets the brahmins and begins a serious, gentle conversation about what is right and worthwhile.
ramayan::360.simple_insight: Respect comes before hard decisions. He prepares the room before he reveals the ache.
ramayan::360.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has summoned the learned priests and honored them properly before speaking. He is about to reveal a private grief that will shape the whole kingdom: his lack of a son and his wish to perform a sacrifice. This verse sets the emotional and ceremonial stage.
ramayan::360.modern_relevance: You sit down with the one person who can help, after days of hiding the problem. Before you ask for anything, you choose respect, clarity, and a careful first sentence.
ramayan::360.insight: It teaches you to begin difficult conversations with dignity and preparation, not panic.

ramayan::361.verse_sanskrit: मम लालप्यमानस्य पुत्रार्थं नास्ति वै सुखम् । तदर्थं हयमेधेन यक्ष्यामीति मतिर्मम । । 1128 । ।
ramayan::361.verse_hindi: There is no happiness for me. I am overwhelmed with grief as I have no son. Therefore, I intend to perform a horsesacrifice.
ramayan::361.english_translation: There is no happiness for me. I am overwhelmed with grief because I have no son. Therefore, I intend to perform a horse sacrifice.
ramayan::361.translation_literal: मम (for me) / लालप्यमानस्य (for the grieving one) / पुत्रार्थं (for a son) / नास्ति (there is not) / वै (indeed) / सुखम् (happiness) / ततर्थं (for that reason) / हयमेधेन (by the horse sacrifice) / यक्ष्यामि (I will sacrifice) / इति (thus) / मतिः (intention) / मम (my)
ramayan::361.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::361.essence: A missing child makes even a king feel powerless.
ramayan::361.simple_meaning: Dasharatha says he has no happiness because he has no son, and he resolves to perform a horse sacrifice to seek one.
ramayan::361.simple_insight: Even great power cannot fill the ache of unmet longing.
ramayan::361.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has gathered learned priests and speaks from private grief, not royal ceremony. Though he rules Ayodhya, he feels incomplete without a son. This verse reveals the wound that drives him toward the horse sacrifice.
ramayan::361.modern_relevance: You can have status, money, and respect, yet still feel one missing thing more sharply than everything else. A private ache can make a whole life feel unfinished.
ramayan::361.insight: It shows how longing can redirect action toward ritual, remedy, and hope.

ramayan::362.verse_sanskrit: तदहं यष्टुमिच्छामि शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा । ऋषिपुत्रप्रभावेन कामान्प्राप्स्यामि चाप्यहम् । । 1129 । ।
ramayan::362.verse_hindi: I wish to perform the yaga acording to scriptural procedures. And I will have my desire fulfilled by the grace of the sage (Rsyasringa).
ramayan::362.english_translation: I wish to perform the sacrifice according to scriptural procedure. Through the power of the sage's blessing, I will also obtain my desire.
ramayan::362.translation_literal: तद् (therefore) / अहम् (I) / यष्टुम् इच्छामि (wish to sacrifice) / शास्त्र-दृष्टेन (seen in scripture) / कर्मणा (by ritual action) / ऋषि-पुत्र-प्रभावेन (through the power of the sage's son) / कामान् (desires) / प्राप्स्यामि (I will obtain) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अहम् (I)
ramayan::362.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::362.essence: Right action comes first; the desired result follows, if it comes at all.
ramayan::362.simple_meaning: Dasharatha says he wants to perform the sacrifice exactly as the scriptures prescribe, trusting that the sage's power will help fulfill his wish for a son.
ramayan::362.simple_insight: There is relief in doing the right act properly, instead of forcing the outcome.
ramayan::362.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has confessed his pain over childlessness and announced the horse sacrifice. Now he adds that he will do it exactly as scripture requires, relying on Rishyasringa's power to bring the result he longs for.
ramayan::362.modern_relevance: You are about to make a big decision and want a quick fix. This verse reminds you that the process matters as much as the goal, especially when the stakes are personal.
ramayan::362.insight: It shifts attention from grabbing results to honoring the right procedure.

ramayan::363.verse_sanskrit: ततस्साध्विति तद्वाक्यं ब्राह्मणा: प्रत्यपूजयन् । वसिष्ठप्रमुखास्सर्वे पार्थिवस्य मुखाच्च्युतम् । । 11210 । ।
ramayan::363.verse_hindi: When they heard these words from the kings month, those brahmins heades by Vasishta extolled the kings decision exclaiming, wellsaid:
ramayan::363.english_translation: When they heard these words from the king's mouth, the brahmins led by Vasishta praised the king's decision, saying, 'Well said.'
ramayan::363.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / साधु इति (well said) / तत्-वाक्यम् (that speech) / ब्राह्मणाः (the brahmins) / प्रत्यपूजयन् (praised in return) / वसिष्ठ-प्रमुखाः (led by Vasishta) / सर्वे (all) / पार्थिवस्य (of the king) / मुखात् (from the mouth) / च्युतम् (uttered)
ramayan::363.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::363.essence: Wise approval turns a private resolve into an accepted course.
ramayan::363.simple_meaning: The priests approve the king's plan and encourage him to proceed.
ramayan::363.simple_insight: A sincere decision gains strength when wise people recognise it.
ramayan::363.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has just declared his wish to perform the horse sacrifice to gain a son. Vasishta and the other brahmins hear the resolve and immediately approve it, clearing the way for the ritual that will change Ayodhya's fate.
ramayan::363.modern_relevance: You finally say out loud the plan you've been carrying for weeks. The right people hear it, nod, and the path ahead starts to open.
ramayan::363.insight: It shows how a serious intention becomes real when it is endorsed by trusted counsel.

ramayan::364.verse_sanskrit: ऋष्यशृङ्गपुरोगाश्च प्रत्यूचुर्नृपतिं तदा । सम्भारास्सम्भ्रियन्तां ते तुरगश्च विमुच्यताम् । । 11211 । ।
ramayan::364.verse_hindi: The priests led by Rsyasringa replied to the king, saying, Let the sacrificial articles be procured and your sacrificial horse released.
ramayan::364.english_translation: Rsyasrnga and the priests replied to the king, saying, "Let the sacrificial materials be gathered, and let the horse be released."
ramayan::364.translation_literal: ऋष्यशृङ्गपुरोगाः (led by Rsyasrnga) / च (and) / प्रत्यूचुः (replied) / नृपतिम् (to the king) / तदा (then) / सम्भाराः (sacrificial materials) / सम्भ्रियन्ताम् (let be gathered) / ते (those) / तुरगः (horse) / च (and) / विमुच्यताम् (let be released)
ramayan::364.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::364.essence: A sacred wish becomes real only through the right preparations.
ramayan::364.simple_meaning: The priests tell the king to gather the ritual supplies and release the sacrificial horse.
ramayan::364.simple_insight: Big intentions become real only when the necessary steps are finally set in motion.
