ramayan::364.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has asked to begin the horse sacrifice for a son. Rsyasrnga and the priests answer by naming the immediate preparations: gather the ritual items and release the horse. The verse is a procedural step in a larger rite, not the main teaching.
ramayan::364.modern_relevance: You finally decide to start the thing you kept postponing. Now comes the unglamorous part: gathering what you need and setting the process in motion.
ramayan::364.insight: It shifts attention from desire to execution: once the aim is clear, the next step is preparation.

ramayan::365.verse_sanskrit: सर्वथा प्राप्स्यसे पुत्रांश्चत्वारोऽमितविक्रमान् । यस्य ते धार्मिकी बुद्धिरियं पुत्रार्थमागता । । 11212 । ।
ramayan::365.verse_hindi: Since this righteous thought for begetting children has entered your mind, you shall surely get four sons of immense prowess.
ramayan::365.english_translation: Since this righteous thought for begetting children has entered your mind, you shall surely get four sons of immense prowess.
ramayan::365.translation_literal: सर्वथा (surely) / प्राप्स्यसे (you will obtain) / पुत्रान् (sons) / चत्वारः (four) / अमितविक्रमान् (of immeasurable prowess) / यस्य (because) / ते (your) / धार्मिकी (righteous) / बुद्धिः (thought) / इयम् (this) / पुत्रार्थम् (for the sake of sons) / आगता (has arisen)
ramayan::365.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::365.essence: Righteous intention can open the door to the result you need.
ramayan::365.simple_meaning: A pure desire, joined with the right action, is about to be fulfilled. The king will receive four mighty sons.
ramayan::365.simple_insight: Good intentions matter when they are matched by right action.
ramayan::365.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the priests have approved Dasaratha’s vow and the sacrificial preparations are underway. They tell him that because his wish for children has come from a righteous mind, the sacrifice will succeed and he will be blessed with four powerful sons.
ramayan::365.modern_relevance: You finally decide to do something honest after months of avoidance — make the call, start the treatment, ask for help. The shift is small, but it changes what becomes possible next.
ramayan::365.insight: It links inner intention with outward result, showing that right-minded action can open the way for change.

ramayan::366.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रीतोऽभवद्राजा श्रुत्वा तद्विजभाषितम् । अमात्यांश्चाब्रवीद्राजा हर्षेणेदं शुभाक्षरम् । । 11213 । ।
ramayan::366.verse_hindi: Pleased to hear the brahmins words, the king happily addressed his ministers with auspicious words:
ramayan::366.english_translation: Pleased to hear the brahmins' words, the king happily addressed his ministers with auspicious words.
ramayan::366.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रीतः (pleased) / अभवत् (became) / राजा (the king) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तत् (that) / विजभाषितम् (spoken by the brahmins) / अमात्यान् (to the ministers) / च (and) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / राजा (the king) / हर्षेण (with joy) / इदम् (this) / शुभाक्षरम् (auspicious words)
ramayan::366.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::366.essence: Relief turns waiting into immediate instruction.
ramayan::366.simple_meaning: The king is happy after hearing the priests and immediately speaks to his ministers with joy.
ramayan::366.simple_insight: A long-awaited hope can turn command into relief.
ramayan::366.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has just heard the brahmins confirm that his sacrifice can proceed and that his wish for sons will be fulfilled. Relieved and delighted, he turns at once to his ministers and gives the next instructions.
ramayan::366.modern_relevance: You finally hear the expert say the plan can work, and your whole body loosens. Then you turn to the team and move at once.
ramayan::366.insight: It shows how relief quickly becomes action when a long-held hope is validated.

ramayan::367.verse_sanskrit: गुरूणां वचनाच्छीघ्रं सम्भारास्सम्भ्रियन्तु मे । समर्थाधिष्ठितश्चाश्वस्सोपाध्यायो विमुच्यताम् । । 11214 । ।
ramayan::367.verse_hindi: In accordance with the instructions by my spiritual preceptors let the articles (required for performing the sacrifice) be procured and the horse  released under the protection of warriors accompanied by the chief priest.
ramayan::367.english_translation: In accordance with the instructions of my teachers, let the sacrificial materials be gathered at once, and let the horse, under the protection of armed guards and the chief priest, be released.
ramayan::367.translation_literal: गुरूणाम् (of the teachers) / वचनात् (by the word/instruction) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / सम्भाराः (sacrificial materials) / सम्भ्रियन्ताम् (let be gathered) / मे (for me) / समर्थाधिष्ठितः (protected by capable/armed guards) / च (and) / अश्वः (horse) / उपाध्यायः (the chief priest) / विमुच्यताम् (let be released)
ramayan::367.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::367.essence: A solemn promise becomes real through immediate, careful action.
ramayan::367.simple_meaning: The king orders the sacrifice preparations to begin immediately and tells them to release the horse under proper protection.
ramayan::367.simple_insight: Real commitment shows up in logistics, not just intention.
ramayan::367.detailed_meaning: After hearing the sages' blessing, King Dasaratha turns at once to action. He orders the ritual supplies gathered and the sacrificial horse released under guard, because the promised sacrifice must now be carried out correctly.
ramayan::367.modern_relevance: You finally decide to do the hard thing, and the next step is not inspiration — it's arranging the details, calling the right people, and starting now.
ramayan::367.insight: It shifts the mind from wishing to execution: once the vow is made, the practical work begins.

ramayan::368.verse_sanskrit: सरय्वाश्चोत्तरे तीरे यज्ञभूमिर्विधीयताम् । शान्तयश्चाभिवर्धन्तां यथाकल्पं यथाविधि । । 11215 । ।
ramayan::368.verse_hindi: Let a sacrificial pavillion be constructed on the northern bank of Sarayu according to prescribed methods ordained in the kalpa and other scriptures for the uninterrupted completion of the sacrifice.
ramayan::368.english_translation: Let a sacrificial pavilion be constructed on the northern bank of the Sarayu, according to prescribed methods, so the sacrifice may proceed without interruption.
ramayan::368.translation_literal: सरय्वाः (of Sarayu) / च (and) / उत्तरे (northern) / तीरे (bank) / यज्ञभूमिः (sacrificial ground) / विधीयताम् (let be arranged) / शान्तयः (auspicious rites) / च (and) / अभिवर्धन्ताम् (let increase) / यथाकल्पम् (according to ritual rule) / यथाविधि (according to ordinance)
ramayan::368.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::368.essence: Even sacred goals need exact preparation.
ramayan::368.simple_meaning: The king orders the sacrifice site to be set up on the north bank of the Sarayu, with every ritual detail done properly.
ramayan::368.simple_insight: Big undertakings succeed when the groundwork is exact.
ramayan::368.detailed_meaning: After hearing the priests, the king gives practical orders for the horse sacrifice. The pavilion must be built on the Sarayu's north bank, and every rite must follow the rulebooks so nothing is left to chance.
ramayan::368.modern_relevance: Before a major ceremony, launch, or family event, someone has to handle the unglamorous setup: the venue, the timing, the sequence, the details. This verse lives in that invisible work.
ramayan::368.insight: It shifts attention from grand intention to precise preparation.

ramayan::369.verse_sanskrit: शक्य: प्राप्तुमयं यज्ञस्सर्वेणापि महीक्षिता । नापराधो भवेत्कष्टो यद्यस्मिन्क्रतुसत्तमे । । 11216 । ।
ramayan::369.verse_hindi: If in this best of sacrifices aswamedha, obstructions and omissions do not occur it will be possible for the king to get the results.
ramayan::369.english_translation: If in this best of sacrifices, the ashvamedha, no serious flaw or obstruction occurs, the king can obtain its full result.
ramayan::369.translation_literal: शक्यः (possible) / प्राप्तुम् (to obtain) / अयम् (this) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / सर्वेण (by all) / अपि (even) / महीक्षितः (by the king) / न (not) / अपराधः (fault) / भवेत् (may be) / कष्टः (serious) / यत् (that) / यस्मिन् (in which) / क्रतुसत्तमे (in the best sacrifice)
ramayan::369.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::369.essence: The result depends on flawless execution, not noble intention alone.
ramayan::369.simple_meaning: The ashvamedha can succeed only if nothing goes wrong in the ritual. A small mistake can spoil the king’s intended result.
ramayan::369.simple_insight: Some outcomes depend on careful, exact conduct — not just intention.
ramayan::369.detailed_meaning: Rama’s royal sacrifice is being prepared on the Sarayu’s northern bank. The priests are arranging every detail, because this rite is delicate: even a serious lapse can ruin the king’s chance of receiving its fruit.
ramayan::369.modern_relevance: You’ve planned the ceremony, booked the venue, and checked every list twice. One overlooked detail can still unravel the whole thing.
ramayan::369.insight: It shifts attention from grand intention to exact execution, where one mistake can break the result.

ramayan::370.verse_sanskrit: छिद्रं हि मृगयन्तेऽत्र विद्वांसो ब्रह्मराक्षसा: । निहतस्य च यज्ञस्य सद्य: कर्ता विनश्यति । । 11217 । ।
ramayan::370.verse_hindi: The learned brahmarakshasas always look out for flaws in the sacrifice so that they can strike into it. If the sacrifice is damaged, the doer of the sacrifice will be immediately destroyed.
ramayan::370.english_translation: The learned brahmarakshasas always look for flaws in a sacrifice so they can attack it. If the sacrifice is spoiled, the one who performed it is destroyed at once.
ramayan::370.translation_literal: छिद्रम् (flaw) / हि (indeed) / मृगयन्ते (seek out) / अत्र (here) / विद्वांसः (the learned) / ब्रह्मराक्षसाः (brahmarakshasas) / निहतस्य (of the ruined) / च (and) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / सद्यः (immediately) / कर्ता (the performer) / विनश्यति (is destroyed)
ramayan::370.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::370.essence: A single flaw can destroy an entire sacred undertaking.
ramayan::370.simple_meaning: A sacrifice must be flawless, because hostile beings look for any weakness. If the ritual is ruined, the one who began it suffers immediately.
ramayan::370.simple_insight: Carelessness creates openings. What you start must be protected until it is complete.
ramayan::370.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, preparations are underway for Rama's great horse sacrifice. The priests warn that brahmarakshasas search for any mistake, because even a small flaw can ruin the rite and bring disaster on the king who sponsors it.
ramayan::370.modern_relevance: You spend months planning an event, then one overlooked detail — a missing permit, a broken backup, a late delivery — threatens everything. Some efforts only survive if you guard the weak points.
ramayan::370.insight: It teaches you to protect important work from small, preventable errors before they grow into failure.

ramayan::371.verse_sanskrit: तद्यथा विधिपूर्वं मे क्रतुरेष समाप्यते । तथा विधानं क्रियतां समर्था: करणेष्विह । । 11218 । ।
ramayan::371.verse_hindi: Therefore let the arrangements be made in a manner by which this sacifice is completed in accordance with the prescriptions in scriptures and you are experts in doing so.
ramayan::371.english_translation: Therefore let the arrangements be made so that this sacrifice is completed exactly according to the prescribed rites. You are skilled in these matters.
ramayan::371.translation_literal: तद्यथा (therefore) / विधिपूर्वं (according to the prescribed order) / मे (my) / क्रतुः (sacrifice) / एषः (this) / समाप्यते (is completed) / तथा (in that way) / विधानं (arrangement) / क्रियताम् (let it be done) / समर्थाः (capable, skilled) / करणेषु (in the tasks, in the procedures) / इह (here)
ramayan::371.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::371.essence: Success depends on doing the rite exactly as prescribed.
ramayan::371.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks his ministers to make the arrangements exactly as the ritual requires so the sacrifice can be completed properly.
ramayan::371.simple_insight: Careful procedure matters when a sacred task can fail through small mistakes.
ramayan::371.detailed_meaning: The king is preparing the Ashvamedha sacrifice, and the ministers are being warned that even tiny errors can ruin it. Dasharatha instructs them to follow the ritual rules precisely, because the success of the whole rite depends on disciplined execution.
ramayan::371.modern_relevance: You are setting up something that cannot be improvised: a wedding, a legal filing, a medical procedure. One missed step can undo everything, so precision becomes care.
ramayan::371.insight: It shifts attention from intention alone to exact execution of the required method.

ramayan::372.verse_sanskrit: तथेति च ततस्सर्वे मन्त्रिण: प्रत्यपूजयन् । पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य तद्वाक्यं यथाज्ञप्तमकुर्वत । । 11219 । ।
ramayan::372.verse_hindi: Honouring the words of the king, all the ministers did as ordered.
ramayan::372.english_translation: Honouring the words of the king, all the ministers did as ordered.
ramayan::372.translation_literal: तथेति (so be it) / च (and) / ततः (then) / सर्वे (all) / मन्त्रिणः (ministers) / प्रत्यपूजयन् (honoured) / पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य (of the king) / तत् (that) / वाक्यम् (word) / यथाज्ञप्तम् (as ordered) / अकुर्वत (they did)
ramayan::372.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::372.essence: Authority matters only when it turns into immediate action.
ramayan::372.simple_meaning: The ministers accepted the king's instruction and carried it out exactly as he asked.
ramayan::372.simple_insight: Clear leadership becomes real only when people act on it without delay.
ramayan::372.detailed_meaning: Kingly instructions have just been given for completing the sacrifice without flaw. The ministers respond at once, showing obedience, coordination, and respect for the ruler's authority. This is a brief bridge verse: action follows command.
ramayan::372.modern_relevance: A team hears the final decision in the meeting room, and nobody keeps debating. The plan only matters now because people move together.
ramayan::372.insight: It shows how a decision becomes effective only when execution follows without hesitation.

ramayan::373.verse_hindi: Admiring the great king, the knower of righteousness, the brahmins permitted by him  returned to their places as they had some.
ramayan::373.english_translation: Then those brahmins praised the king, the knower of righteousness. Granted permission, all of them returned to their homes as they had come.
ramayan::373.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / द्विजाः (the brahmins) / ते (those) / धर्मज्ञम् (the knower of righteousness) / अस्तुवन् (praised) / पार्थिवर्षभम् (the bull among kings) / अनुज्ञाताः (having been permitted) / ततस् (then) / सर्वे (all) / पुनः (again) / जग्मुः (went) / यथागतम् (as they had come)
ramayan::373.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::373.essence: The priests depart after honoring the king.
ramayan::373.simple_meaning: The brahmins praised Dasaratha, then left with his permission and returned home.
ramayan::373.simple_insight: Respect is shown, the task is complete, and everyone moves on with dignity.
ramayan::373.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just given instructions for the sacrifice. The brahmins praise him as a righteous king, accept his permission, and leave. It is a brief closing movement, not a new teaching.
ramayan::373.modern_relevance: The meeting ends, the formal thanks are exchanged, and people file out of the room. The real work has already been set in motion.
ramayan::373.insight: It marks the orderly close of a ritual exchange, not a standalone lesson.

ramayan::374.verse_sanskrit: गतेष्वथ द्विजाग्य्रेषु मन्त्रिणस्तान्नराधिप: । विसर्जयित्वा स्वं वेश्म प्रविवेश महाद्युति: । । 11221 । ।
ramayan::374.verse_hindi: When the great brahmins  departed, the glorious king (Dasaratha) sent away his ministers and entered his palace.
ramayan::374.english_translation: When the great brahmins had departed, the glorious king Dasaratha sent away his ministers and entered his palace.
ramayan::374.translation_literal: गतेषु (having departed) / अथ (then) / द्विजाग्रेषु (when the foremost brahmins) / मन्त्रिणः (the ministers) / तान् (them) / नराधिपः (the king) / विसर्जयित्वा (having dismissed) / स्वं (his own) / वेश्म (palace) / प्रविवेश (entered) / महाद्युतिḥ (the greatly radiant one)
ramayan::374.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::374.essence: The court clears, and the king returns to wait for what follows.
ramayan::374.simple_meaning: After the brahmins leave, Dasaratha dismisses his ministers and goes back into the palace.
ramayan::374.simple_insight: Some moments are only movement between larger events.
ramayan::374.detailed_meaning: The brahmins have finished their part, and the ministers are dismissed. Dasaratha, still radiant in appearance, turns back into his palace. The verse simply closes the scene and carries the story toward the next royal action.
ramayan::374.modern_relevance: You leave the meeting room after everyone else has gone, still carrying the weight of what comes next.
ramayan::374.insight: It shifts attention from the public gathering to the next private step in the king's path.

ramayan::375.verse_sanskrit: पुन: प्राप्ते वसन्ते तु पूर्णस्संवत्सरोऽभवत् । प्रसवार्थं गतो यष्टुं हयमेधेन वीर्यवान् । । 1131 । ।
ramayan::375.verse_hindi: After completion of one year when spring returned, the valiant king (Dasaratha) entered the sacrificial pavilion to worship celestial beings for begetting sons.
ramayan::375.english_translation: After one full year had passed and spring returned, the valiant Dasaratha entered the sacrificial pavilion to perform the horse sacrifice for the birth of sons.
ramayan::375.translation_literal: पुनः (again) / प्राप्ते (having arrived) / वसन्ते (in spring) / तु (then) / पूर्णः (complete) / संवत्सरः (year) / अभवत् (became) / प्रसवार्थम् (for the purpose of getting sons) / गतः (gone) / यष्टुम् (to sacrifice) / हयमेधेन (with the horse sacrifice) / वीर्यवान् (the valiant one)
ramayan::375.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::375.essence: A year of waiting ends in a ceremony meant to change fate.
ramayan::375.simple_meaning: A year passed, spring came again, and Dasaratha went to begin the horse sacrifice to seek sons.
ramayan::375.simple_insight: Some long-awaited efforts begin only after patience and preparation have fully matured.
ramayan::375.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has already consulted the brahmins and dismissed his ministers. Now, after a full year has turned and spring has returned, he enters the sacrificial pavilion to begin the horse sacrifice that will shape the future of Ayodhya.
ramayan::375.modern_relevance: You wait through an entire year of uncertainty, then finally step into the room where the next chapter begins. Some decisions only become real after time has done its work.
ramayan::375.insight: It marks the transition from waiting to action, when a private hope becomes a formal undertaking.

ramayan::376.verse_sanskrit: अभिवाद्य वसिष्ठं च न्यायत: परिपूज्य च । अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं प्रसवार्थं द्विजोत्तमम् । । 1132 । ।
ramayan::376.verse_hindi: After offering humble salutations and worshipping sage Vasishta in accordance with prescribed ordinance for begetting children, he obediently said:
ramayan::376.english_translation: After offering humble salutations and worshipping sage Vasishta according to proper order for the sake of having children, he said in a respectful voice:
ramayan::376.translation_literal: अभिवाद्य (having saluted) / वसिष्ठं (Vasishta) / च (and) / न्यायतः (according to proper order) / परिपूज्य (having worshipped) / च (and) / अब्रवीत् (said) / प्रश्रितं (humble) / वाक्यं (speech) / प्रसवार्थं (for the sake of progeny) / द्विजोत्तमम् (to the foremost brahmin)
ramayan::376.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::376.essence: Humility comes before any sacred request can bear fruit.
ramayan::376.simple_meaning: Dasharatha bows to Vasishta with humility before speaking, because he is asking for a sacrifice meant to grant him children.
ramayan::376.simple_insight: Even a king begins with respect when he wants something sacred to succeed.
ramayan::376.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has entered the sacrificial pavilion after a year of waiting. Before asking Vasishta to begin the rite for children, he bows, worships him properly, and speaks with restraint. The moment shows that sacred action begins with humility, not demand.
ramayan::376.modern_relevance: You walk into a room needing help with something deeply personal, and you remember that respect changes the whole tone. The way you ask can either open the door or harden it.
ramayan::376.insight: It teaches you to approach important help with humility and proper conduct.

ramayan::377.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञो मे क्रियतां ब्रह्मन्यथोक्तं मुनिपुङ्गव । यथा न विघ्न: क्रियते यज्ञाङ्गेषु विधीयताम् । । 1133 । ।
ramayan::377.verse_hindi: O foremost among ascetics O brahman, may the sacrifice be performed according to  tradition in such a manner that the sacrifice is performed unhindered.
ramayan::377.english_translation: O foremost among ascetics, O brahman, let the sacrifice be performed as instructed, so that no obstacle arises in the sacrificial rites.
ramayan::377.translation_literal: यज्ञः (sacrifice) / मे (for me) / क्रियताम् (may be done) / ब्रह्मन् (O brahman) / यथा उक्तम् (as instructed) / मुनिपुङ्गव (O foremost among ascetics) / यथा (so that) / न (not) / विघ्नः (obstacle) / क्रियते (is made) / यज्ञ-अङ्गेषु (in the parts of the sacrifice) / विधीयताम् (let it be arranged)
ramayan::377.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::377.essence: A sacred act succeeds only when every detail is carefully arranged.
ramayan::377.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks Vasishta to carry out the sacrifice exactly as prescribed, with nothing allowed to interrupt it.
ramayan::377.simple_insight: Careful preparation protects sacred work from avoidable failure.
ramayan::377.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has entered the sacrificial pavilion to seek the rite that may grant him a son. He bows to Vasishta and asks him to arrange every detail correctly, because even a small mistake could ruin the whole undertaking.
ramayan::377.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to do something that matters, and you double-check every step before starting. When the stakes are high, care is not fussiness.
ramayan::377.insight: It shifts attention from desire alone to exact preparation, showing that serious aims need disciplined execution.

ramayan::378.verse_sanskrit: भवान् स्निग्धस्सुहृन्मह्यं गुरुश्च परमो महान् । ओढव्यो भवता चैव भारो यज्ञस्य चोद्यत: । । 1134 । ।
ramayan::378.verse_hindi: You are an affectionate friend and most reverential spiritual guide to me. The burden of performing the sacrifice which has since commenced shall be borne by you.
ramayan::378.english_translation: You are an affectionate friend and most revered guide to me. The burden of the begun sacrifice shall be borne by you.
ramayan::378.translation_literal: भवान् (you) / स्निग्धः (affectionate) / सुहृत् (well-wisher, friend) / मह्यम् (to me) / गुरुः (teacher, revered guide) / च (and) / परमः (supreme, most excellent) / महान् (great) / ओढव्यः (to be borne) / भवता (by you) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / भारः (burden) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / चोद्यताḥ (begun, set in motion)
ramayan::378.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::378.essence: A heavy undertaking becomes possible through trusted guidance.
ramayan::378.simple_meaning: Dasharatha tells Vasishta that he is both a dear friend and a revered teacher, and asks him to take on the responsibility of the sacrifice.
ramayan::378.simple_insight: Great tasks become bearable when trusted to someone wise and close.
ramayan::378.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha has already asked for the sacrifice to be performed. Now he turns to Vasishta with reverence, asking him to carry the ritual burden. The verse is part of a practical exchange, not the main teaching itself.
ramayan::378.modern_relevance: You hand a fragile project to the one person who understands both the rules and your limits. Relief comes when respect and trust meet responsibility.
ramayan::378.insight: It shows how leadership depends on entrusting the right person with the right burden.

ramayan::379.verse_sanskrit: तथेति च स राजानमब्रवीद्द्विजसत्तमः । करिष्ये सर्वमेवैतद्भवता यत्समर्थितम् । । 1135 । ।
ramayan::379.verse_hindi: The great among brahmins answered him saying I shall do everything as proposed by you.
ramayan::379.english_translation: The foremost of brahmins replied to the king, "I will do everything exactly as you have approved."
ramayan::379.translation_literal: तथा इति (so be it) / च (and) / सः (he) / राजा नम् (to the king) / अब्रवीत् (said) / द्विजसत्तमः (the best among brahmins) / करिष्ये (I will do) / सर्वम् एव (everything indeed) / एतत् (this) / भवता (by you) / यत् (what) / समर्थितम् (approved, arranged)
ramayan::379.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::379.essence: Clear consent turns a plan into action.
ramayan::379.simple_meaning: Vasishta agrees to carry out the sacrifice exactly as Rama's father has requested.
ramayan::379.simple_insight: A sacred task begins with clear agreement and complete trust.
ramayan::379.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has asked Vasishta to oversee the sacrifice and remove every obstacle. Vasishta accepts without hesitation, showing the quiet coordination that makes the rite possible. This verse is a brief confirmation, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::379.modern_relevance: You finally get the green light on a project you've been planning for weeks. The real work starts when everyone stops talking and commits to the same plan.
ramayan::379.insight: It shifts attention from intention to execution: once the plan is set, the task is to carry it through fully.

ramayan::380.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽब्रवीद्विजान्वृद्धान्यज्ञकर्मसु निष्ठितान् । स्थापत्ये निष्ठितांश्चैव वृद्धान्परमधार्मिकान् । । 1136 । । कर्मान्तिकान् शिल्पकरान्वर्धकीन् खनकानपि । गणकान्शिल्पिनश्चैव तथैव नटनर्तकान् । । 1137 । । तथा शुचीन्शास्त्रविद: पुरुषान् सुबहुश्रुतान् । यज्ञकर्म समीहन्तां भवन्तो राजशासनात् । । 1138 । । इष्टका बहु साहस्राश्शीघ्रमानीयतामिति । 0उपकार्या: क्रियन्तां च राज्ञां बहुगुणान्विता: । । 1139 । ।
ramayan::380.verse_hindi: Thereafter Vasishta summoned those brahmins who are experienced in the sacrificerelated activities venerable and righteous architects skilled workers brick makers, carpenters, diggers, artisans, account keepers, dancers and actors, men versed in scriptures and honest, wellinformed people and addressed them saying, In accordance with the kings command let the work of the sacrificial ceremony be inauguarated. Let thousands of bricks be brought. Let temporary residential buildings be erected with all the comforts to accommodate royal guests.
ramayan::380.english_translation: Thereafter Vasishta summoned the brahmins skilled in sacrificial rites, the experienced architects, the craftsmen, carpenters, diggers, accountants, artisans, dancers, and learned men, and said: by the king's command, let the sacrifice begin. Let thousands of bricks be brought quickly, and let comfortable lodging for the royal guests be prepared.
ramayan::380.translation_literal: तत: (thereafter) / अब्रवीत् (said) / द्विजान् (brahmins) / वृद्धान् (elderly) / यज्ञकर्मसु (in sacrificial rites) / निष्ठितान् (skilled) / स्थापत्ये (in architecture) / निष्ठितान् (skilled) / च (and) / एव (also) / वृद्धान् (experienced) / परमधार्मिकान् (most righteous) / कर्मान्तिकान् (workers in practical tasks) / शिल्पकरान् (craftsmen) / वर्धकीन् (carpenters) / खनकान् (diggers) / अपि (also) / गणकान् (accountants) / शिल्पिनः (artisans) / च (and) / एव (also) / तथा (likewise) / शुचीन् (pure) / शास्त्रविदः (knowers of scripture) / पुरुषान् (men) / सुबहुश्रुतान् (very learned) / यज्ञकर्म (sacrificial work) / समीहन्ताम् (let them undertake) / भवन्तः (you all) / राजशासनात् (by the king's command) / इष्टका: (bricks) / बहुसाहस्राः (many thousands) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / आनीयताम् (let be brought) / इति (thus) / उपकार्याः (temporary buildings) / क्रियन्ताम् (let be made) / च (and) / राज्ञाम् (for kings) / बहुगुणान्विताः (endowed with many comforts)
ramayan::380.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::380.essence: A sacred act begins only after the right people and preparations are in place.
ramayan::380.simple_meaning: Vasishta organizes the people needed for the sacrifice and orders the work to begin at once, with bricks brought quickly and guest lodging prepared.
ramayan::380.simple_insight: Great rituals also need practical coordination, not just intention.
ramayan::380.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has agreed to oversee the sacrifice for the king. Now he turns from blessing to logistics, summoning priests, builders, craftsmen, and learned men. The ritual can only begin when the entire human structure around it is set in place.
ramayan::380.modern_relevance: A wedding, conference, or community event looks effortless only after someone has lined up dozens of invisible tasks. Sacred work still depends on clear coordination and timely action.
ramayan::380.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony alone to the disciplined labor that makes ceremony possible.

ramayan::381.english_translation: Hundreds of beautiful residences for brahmins should also be built, well supplied with many kinds of food and drink.
ramayan::381.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणावसथाः (residences for brahmins) / च (and) / एव (also) / कर्तव्याः (should be made) / शतशश् (in hundreds) / शुभाः (auspicious, beautiful) / भक्ष्य (food) / अन्न (grain, cooked food) / पानैः (with drinks) / बहुभिः (many) / समुपेताः (well supplied) / सुनिष्ठिताः (well arranged)
ramayan::381.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::381.essence: Respect becomes real only when people are properly cared for.
ramayan::381.simple_meaning: Many beautiful houses should be prepared for brahmins, with plenty of food and drink.
ramayan::381.simple_insight: Care is shown in the details: dignity includes shelter, nourishment, and thoughtful hospitality.
ramayan::381.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is organizing the royal preparations, and this line adds one practical requirement after another. The focus is not on teaching a principle but on making sure the brahmins are properly housed and fed as the larger ritual arrangement takes shape.
ramayan::381.modern_relevance: You are planning a large family gathering and realize respect is not a speech — it is enough chairs, good food, and places to rest.
ramayan::381.insight: It shifts attention from ceremonial intent to the concrete work that makes honour real.

ramayan::382.verse_sanskrit: तथा पौरजनस्यापि कर्तव्या बहुविस्तरा: । आवासा बहुभक्ष्या वै सर्वकामैरुपस्थिता: । । 11311 । ।
ramayan::382.verse_hindi: In the same manner let widely spread residential accommodation be furnished with many items of food and all kinds of entertainment be provided for people from other lands.
ramayan::382.english_translation: In the same manner let widely spread residential accommodation be furnished with many items of food and all kinds of entertainment be provided for people from other lands.
ramayan::382.translation_literal: तथा (in the same manner) / पौरजनस्य (for the townspeople) / अपि (also) / कर्तव्या (should be made) / बहुविस्तराः (widely spread, spacious) / आवासाः (lodgings) / बहुभक्ष्याः (with many foods) / वै (indeed) / सर्वकामैः (with all delights) / उपस्थितााः (provided with)
ramayan::382.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::382.essence: A proper welcome makes room for everyone, not just the important few.
ramayan::382.simple_meaning: Town residents should also be given spacious lodging, plenty of food, and every kind of comfort.
ramayan::382.simple_insight: Care for a gathering means preparing for everyone, not just the main guests.
ramayan::382.detailed_meaning: The priests and officials are arranging a grand sacrificial event. After setting up lodging for learned brahmins, the plan now extends to the townspeople too. The verse is a practical instruction about hospitality, not a separate teaching on its own.
ramayan::382.modern_relevance: A wedding venue runs out of water by noon, and the side guests are left standing in a hallway. Real preparation includes the people who are easy to forget.
ramayan::382.insight: It shifts attention from ceremonial success to inclusive preparation.

ramayan::383.verse_sanskrit: तथा जानपदस्यापि जनस्य बहुशोभनम् । दातव्यमन्नं विधिवत्सत्कृत्य न तु लीलया । । 11312 । ।
ramayan::383.verse_hindi: In the same way people coming from rural areas also should be duly, not casualy treated with respect.
ramayan::383.english_translation: In the same way, people from rural areas should also be given excellent food properly, with respect — not casually.
ramayan::383.translation_literal: तथा (in the same way) / जानपदस्य (of rural people) / अपि (also) / जनस्य (of people) / बहुशोभनम् (very excellent) / दातव्यम् (should be given) / अन्नम् (food) / विधिवत् (according to proper rule) / सत्कृत्य (having treated with respect) / न तु (not indeed) / लीलया (casually)
ramayan::383.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::383.essence: Proper care means honoring people, not just feeding them.
ramayan::383.simple_meaning: People from rural areas should be served proper food with respect, not treated carelessly.
ramayan::383.simple_insight: Dignity is shown in small acts of hospitality, not just grand words.
ramayan::383.detailed_meaning: A royal instruction is laying out how guests and subjects must be hosted. After brahmins and townspeople, the verse extends the same care to rural visitors, insisting that food be offered properly and respectfully.
ramayan::383.modern_relevance: A delivery worker arrives after a long day, and you hand over the package without looking up. This verse asks for the extra second that turns a transaction into respect.
ramayan::383.insight: It shifts service from mere provision to dignified conduct.

ramayan::384.verse_sanskrit: सर्वे वर्णा यथा पूजां प्राप्नुवन्ति सुसत्कृता: । न चावज्ञा प्रयोक्तव्या कामक्रोधवशादपि । । 11313 । ।
ramayan::384.verse_hindi: People from all castes should be welltreated with respect. There should be no insult
ramayan::384.english_translation: All social classes should be treated with respect and honored well. No insult should be used, even under the sway of desire or anger.
ramayan::384.translation_literal: सर्वे (all) / वर्णा (social classes) / यथा (so that) / पूजां (honor) / प्राप्नुवन्ति (they receive) / सुसत्कृता: (well-respected) / न (not) / च (and) / अवज्ञा (insult) / प्रयोक्तव्या (should be used) / कामक्रोधवशादपि (even under the sway of desire and anger)
ramayan::384.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::384.essence: Status never justifies contempt, even in anger.
ramayan::384.simple_meaning: Everyone should be treated with respect, and no one should be insulted just because anger or desire is rising.
ramayan::384.simple_insight: The real test of character is how you speak when you feel provoked.
ramayan::384.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the king is laying down rules for public conduct and hospitality. After ordering generous treatment for visitors and villagers, he broadens the standard: every social group deserves honor, and no one should be demeaned by impulse.
ramayan::384.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in traffic, and the insult rises before you even think. This verse asks you to notice that impulse and refuse to hand it the steering wheel.
ramayan::384.insight: It trains you to replace reactive contempt with deliberate respect.

ramayan::385.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञकर्मसु ये व्यग्रा: पुरुषाश्शिल्पिनस्तथा । तेषामपि विशेषेण पूजा कार्या यथाक्रमम् । । 11314 । । ते च स्युस्सम्भृतास्सर्वे वसुभिर्भोजनेन च ।
ramayan::385.verse_hindi: The people deeply immersed in performing sacrificerelated activities and sculptors be specially honoured according to their nature of work. All of them should be satisfied with money and food.
ramayan::385.english_translation: People deeply engaged in sacrificial work and artisans should also be specially honoured according to their role. They should all be satisfied with gifts and food.
ramayan::385.translation_literal: यज्ञकर्मसु (in sacrificial works) / ये (those who) / व्यग्रा: (busy, absorbed) / पुरुषा: (men) / शिल्पिनः (artisans) / तथा (and so) / तेषाम् (of them) / अपि (also) / विशेषेण (especially) / पूजा (honour) / कार्या (should be done) / यथाक्रमम् (according to proper order) / ते (they) / च (and) / स्युः (should be) / सम्भृताः (satisfied, well-provided) / सर्वे (all) / वसुभिः (with wealth) / भोजनेन (with food) / च (and)
ramayan::385.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::385.essence: Respect is incomplete until it becomes food, gifts, and care.
ramayan::385.simple_meaning: People doing sacred work and skilled craft should be treated with special respect, and given food and support according to their role.
ramayan::385.simple_insight: Dignity grows when recognition is matched by real care.
ramayan::385.detailed_meaning: In this section, Rama’s people are being taught how to host and serve properly. After stressing respect for all groups, the instruction turns specific: those absorbed in ritual work and skilled craft deserve special honour, plus practical support through gifts and food.
ramayan::385.modern_relevance: At a wedding, a repair crew, and the caterers are all working hard while everyone else enjoys the event. This verse says their effort should be noticed, respected, and materially cared for.
ramayan::385.insight: It teaches you to pair appreciation with concrete support, especially for people whose work sustains the whole event.

ramayan::386.verse_sanskrit: यथा सर्वं सुविहितं न किञ्चित्परिहीयते । । 11315 । । तथा भवन्त: कुर्वन्तु प्रीतिस्निग्धेन चेतसा ।
ramayan::386.verse_hindi: Every thing should be wellmanaged. In whatever manner you do, not even the smallest things be left out. Carry out the work with love and affection in your hearts.
ramayan::386.english_translation: Everything should be well managed. Leave out not even the smallest detail. Do the work with a loving, affectionate mind.
ramayan::386.translation_literal: यथा (as) / सर्वं (everything) / सुविहितं (well arranged) / न (not) / किञ्चित् (anything) / परिहीयते (is left out) / तथा (so) / भवन्तः (you all) / कुर्वन्तु (should do) / प्रीतिस्निग्धेन (with loving, affectionate) / चेतसा (mind)
ramayan::386.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::386.essence: Wholehearted work leaves no detail behind.
ramayan::386.simple_meaning: Do the work completely, with care and affection. Nothing important should be neglected, not even the smallest detail.
ramayan::386.simple_insight: Care is not extra; it is what makes the work whole.
ramayan::386.detailed_meaning: In the midst of arranging a formal task, the speakers insist that everything be prepared properly and nothing be omitted. The point is not just efficiency, but a careful, affectionate way of doing work.
ramayan::386.modern_relevance: You are packing for a family trip, checking passports, snacks, chargers, and medicines. The real difference is not speed — it is the loving attention that keeps small mistakes from becoming big ones.
ramayan::386.insight: It shifts your focus from rushing through tasks to completing them with full attention and care.

ramayan::387.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सर्वे समागम्य वसिष्ठमिदमब्रुवन् । । 11316 । । यथोक्तं तत्सुविहितं न किञ्चित्परिहीयते । यथोक्तं तत्करिष्यामो न किञ्चित्परिहास्यते । । 11317 । ।
ramayan::387.verse_hindi: Then all of them approached Vasishta and said, everything has been wellarranged in accordance with your instruction. There is no deficiency. Everything will be done as instructed by you without leaving out anything.
ramayan::387.english_translation: Then all of them approached Vasishta and said, everything has been well arranged in accordance with your instruction. There is no deficiency. Everything will be done as instructed by you without leaving out anything.
ramayan::387.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / सर्वे (all) / समागम्य (having come together) / वसिष्ठम् (to Vasishta) / इदम् (this) / अब्रुवन् (they said) / यथा-उक्तम् (as said) / तत् (that) / सु-विहितम् (well arranged) / न (not) / किञ्चित् (anything) / परिहीयते (is left out) / यथा-उक्तम् (as instructed) / तत् (that) / करिष्यामः (we will do) / न (not) / किञ्चित् (anything) / परिहास्यते (will be omitted)
ramayan::387.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::387.essence: Good work means nothing is left unfinished.
ramayan::387.simple_meaning: Everyone reports back to Vasishta that the arrangements are complete and nothing has been missed. They promise to carry out his instructions exactly.
ramayan::387.simple_insight: Careful preparation creates confidence before the next step.
ramayan::387.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just given instructions for a formal royal gathering. The people responsible for the arrangements return together and confirm that nothing has been overlooked. Their reply marks a smooth handoff before the next command is given.
ramayan::387.modern_relevance: After three rounds of planning a wedding, a product launch, or a funeral, someone finally says, “Nothing’s missing.” That quiet check-in is what lets the next step begin cleanly.
ramayan::387.insight: It shows the value of exact follow-through before moving on to the next task.

ramayan::388.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सुमन्त्रमानीय वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । निमन्त्रयस्व नृपतीन्पृथिव्यां ये च धार्मिका: । । 11318 । ।
ramayan::388.verse_hindi: Then Vasishta, having summoned Sumantra said to him Invite all the righteous kings on earth.
ramayan::388.english_translation: Then Vasishta, having summoned Sumantra, said to him: Invite all the righteous kings on earth.
ramayan::388.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / सुमन्त्रम् (Sumantra) / आनीय (having brought) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / वाक्यम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (said) / निमन्त्रयस्व (invite) / नृपतीन् (kings) / पृथिव्याम् (on the earth) / ये (who) / च (and) / धार्मिकाः (righteous)
ramayan::388.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::388.essence: The right gathering begins with a clear summons.
ramayan::388.simple_meaning: Vasishta tells Sumantra to invite every righteous king across the land.
ramayan::388.simple_insight: Great events begin with careful gathering, not sudden force.
ramayan::388.detailed_meaning: Vasishta calls Sumantra aside and gives him a practical order: invite the righteous kings of the earth. The scene is still in the preparation phase, with the court organizing a major event and ensuring the right people are summoned.
ramayan::388.modern_relevance: You are planning something important and the real work is still invisible: the calls, the lists, the careful invitations that make the whole thing possible.
ramayan::388.insight: It shifts attention to coordination, showing that large undertakings depend on precise, respectful outreach.

ramayan::389.verse_hindi: Extend an honourable invitation to brahmins, kshatriyas, merchants and sudras in their thousands residing in all countries.
ramayan::389.english_translation: Extend an honourable invitation to brahmins, kshatriyas, merchants and sudras in their thousands residing in all countries.
ramayan::389.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणान् (brahmins) / क्षत्रियान् (kshatriyas) / वैश्यान् (merchants) / शूद्रान् (sudras) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सहस्रशः (in thousands) / समानयस्व (bring together / invite) / सत्कृत्य (with honour) / सर्वदेशेषु (in all countries) / मानवान् (people)
ramayan::389.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::389.essence: A proper invitation makes room for everyone.
ramayan::389.simple_meaning: Vasishta asks that people from every social group and every region be invited with respect.
ramayan::389.simple_insight: Honour is not limited by rank or region.
ramayan::389.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is organising a great gathering and instructs Sumantra to invite people from all classes and all lands with proper respect. The verse is part of the practical preparation, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::389.modern_relevance: You are planning a gathering and want it to feel open, not exclusive. The invitation itself becomes a sign of respect.
ramayan::389.insight: It shifts attention from status to inclusive welcome.

ramayan::390.verse_sanskrit: मिथिलाधिपतिं शूरं जनकं सत्यविक्रमम् । निष्ठितं सर्वशास्त्रेषु तथा वेदेषु निष्ठितम् । । 11320 । । तमानय महाभागं स्वयमेव सुसत्कृतम् । पूर्वसम्बन्धिनं ज्ञात्वा तत: पूर्वं ब्रवीमि ते । । 11321 । ।
ramayan::390.verse_hindi: You may personally go and bring with due honour king Janaka who is the distinguished king of Mithila, a warrior whose truth is his strength proficient in all scriptures and the Vedas. Since he is an old ally, I am telling you in advance.
ramayan::390.english_translation: You may personally go and bring with due honour king Janaka, the distinguished king of Mithila, a warrior whose truth is his strength, proficient in all scriptures and the Vedas. Since he is an old ally, I am telling you in advance.
ramayan::390.translation_literal: मिथिलाधिपतिम् (the king of Mithila) / शूरम् (the brave) / जनकम् (Janaka) / सत्यविक्रमम् (whose strength is truth) / निष्ठितम् (well-versed) / सर्वशास्त्रेषु (in all scriptures) / तथा (and) / वेदेषु (in the Vedas) / निष्ठितम् (well-versed) / तम् (him) / आनय (bring) / महाभागम् (the highly fortunate / noble one) / स्वयम् एव (personally) / सुसत्कृतम् (with great honour) / पूर्वसम्बन्धिनम् (an old ally) / ज्ञात्वा (knowing) / ततः (therefore) / पूर्वम् (first) / ब्रवीमि (I tell) / ते (to you)
ramayan::390.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::390.essence: Honour the people whose character and history make them worthy of first welcome.
ramayan::390.simple_meaning: Janaka should be invited with full honour because he is noble, learned, brave, and an old ally of the family.
ramayan::390.simple_insight: Respect is not just for rank; it belongs to character and long-standing bonds.
ramayan::390.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is organizing a royal invitation for a great gathering. After asking Sumantra to summon the righteous kings and the people of all classes, he singles out Janaka of Mithila: honoured, learned, brave, and tied by old friendship. The verse is part of a formal call, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::390.modern_relevance: You’re making a guest list for a wedding or memorial and know exactly who must be received first. Some people are invited for status; others because honour and history demand it.
ramayan::390.insight: It teaches careful social conduct: honour worthy people first, especially those bound by old trust.

ramayan::391.verse_sanskrit: तथा काशीपतिं स्निग्धं सततं प्रियवादिनम् । वयस्यं राजसिंहस्य स्वयमेवानयस्व ह । । 11322 । ।
ramayan::391.verse_hindi: Similarly, you may personally escort king of Kasi who is always affectionate and sweettongued. He is a friend to our king who is a lion among rulers.
ramayan::391.english_translation: Similarly, you may personally escort the king of Kasi, who is affectionate and always speaks kindly. He is a friend of our king, the lion among rulers.
ramayan::391.translation_literal: तथा (similarly) / काशीपतिम् (the lord of Kasi) / स्निग्धम् (affectionate) / सततम् (always) / प्रियवादिनम् (speaking pleasing words) / वयस्यम् (a friend) / राजसिंहस्य (of the lion among kings) / स्वयमेव (personally) / आनयस्व (bring) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::391.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::391.essence: A royal invitation can reveal the bonds that hold a court together.
ramayan::391.simple_meaning: Janaka's invitation is being extended to another respected ally: the king of Kasi, who is close to Rama's royal family and should be brought with honour.
ramayan::391.simple_insight: Some invitations are also acts of respect. Who you include shows what kind of gathering this is.
ramayan::391.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the court is preparing a great royal assembly for Rama's wedding. After Janaka is named, the king of Kasi is added too — not as a random guest, but as a cherished friend of Dasharatha's house. The verse is part of a formal list, not a teaching.
ramayan::391.modern_relevance: You're making a guest list for a milestone event and realizing it is really a map of your loyalties. The people you call first are the relationships you most want to honour.
ramayan::391.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the network of respect surrounding it.

ramayan::392.verse_sanskrit: तथा केकयराजानं वृद्धं परमधार्मिकम् । श्वशुरं राजसिंहस्य सपुत्रं त्वमिहानय । । 11323 । ।
ramayan::392.verse_hindi: Likewise bring here the aged and very righteous king of Kekaya along with his sons. He is fatherinlaw to this lion among kings (Dasaratha).
ramayan::392.english_translation: Likewise bring here the aged and very righteous king of Kekaya along with his sons. He is father-in-law to this lion among kings (Dasaratha).
ramayan::392.translation_literal: तथा (likewise) / केकयराजानम् (the king of Kekaya) / वृद्धम् (aged) / परमधार्मिकम् (very righteous) / श्वशुरम् (father-in-law) / राजसिंहस्य (of the lion among kings) / सपुत्रम् (along with his sons) / त्वम् (you) / इह (here) / आनय (bring)
ramayan::392.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::392.essence: Honor is shown by how carefully you receive the people tied to your house.
ramayan::392.simple_meaning: Bring the aged, righteous king of Kekaya here with his sons. He is Dasaratha's father-in-law.
ramayan::392.simple_insight: No teaching is being given here; the verse simply continues a list of honored guests.
ramayan::392.detailed_meaning: A messenger is being instructed to escort respected allies to the gathering. After Janaka and the king of Kashi, the list continues with the king of Kekaya, Dasaratha's father-in-law, showing the ceremonial care given to royal relations.
ramayan::392.modern_relevance: A host is running through names before a major family event, making sure every elder and ally is received properly. It is the quiet labor behind public honor.
ramayan::392.insight: It shifts attention from drama to protocol: who must be welcomed, and with what respect.

ramayan::393.verse_sanskrit: अङ्गेश्वरम् महाभागं रोमपादं सुसत्कृतम् । वयस्यं राजसिंहस्य समानय यशस्विनम् । । 11324 । ।
ramayan::393.verse_hindi: Bring with honour king of Anga, Romapada, famous and prosperous. He is an intimate friend of the king (Dasaratha).
ramayan::393.english_translation: Bring with honour king of Anga, Romapada, famous and prosperous. He is an intimate friend of the king.
ramayan::393.translation_literal: अङ्गेश्वरम् (the king of Anga) / महाभागम् (greatly fortunate) / रोमपादम् (Romapada) / सुसत्कृतम् (well honoured) / वयस्यम् (friend) / राजसिंहस्य (of the lion among kings) / समानय (bring together) / यशस्विनम् (famous, glorious)
ramayan::393.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::393.essence: A king’s circle is measured by the loyalty he keeps close.
ramayan::393.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks that Romapada, the honoured king of Anga and his close friend, be brought with respect.
ramayan::393.simple_insight: Some bonds are so important they are treated like family.
ramayan::393.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, messengers are being sent to gather allies and honored guests for a royal purpose. Among them is Romapada of Anga, a trusted friend of Dasharatha. The verse simply adds his name to the list.
ramayan::393.modern_relevance: A wedding invitation list is being checked one more time, and one name matters because of years of loyalty. You do not just invite a person; you honour the bond behind them.
ramayan::393.insight: It shows how royal obligation includes remembering and honouring old friendships.

ramayan::394.verse_sanskrit: प्राचीनान्सिन्धु सौवीरान्सौराष्ट्रेयांश्च पार्थिवान् । दाक्षिणात्यान्नरेन्द्रांश्च समस्तानानयस्व ह । । 11325 । ।
ramayan::394.verse_hindi: Bring kings from the countries of the eastern and southern regions, from Sindhu, Sauvera and Saurashtra৷৷
ramayan::394.english_translation: Bring the kings from the eastern and southern regions, from Sindhu, Sauvera, and Saurashtra.
ramayan::394.translation_literal: प्राचीनान् (from the eastern regions) / सिन्धु (Sindhu) / सौवीरान् (the Sauviras) / सौराष्ट्रेयान् (the Saurashtra kings) / च (and) / पार्थिवान् (kings) / दाक्षिणात्यान् (from the southern regions) / नरेन्द्रान् (lords of men, kings) / च (and) / समस्तान् (all) / आनयस्व (bring) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::394.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::394.essence: More kings are being summoned to complete the assembly.
ramayan::394.simple_meaning: He is asking that rulers from many regions be brought here, along with the other allied kings.
ramayan::394.simple_insight: Some moments are about gathering support, not making a moral point.
ramayan::394.detailed_meaning: The speaker is listing more rulers to summon for a larger royal gathering. After naming close allies, he expands the request to kings from eastern, southern, and western regions. The verse simply continues the command; it does not carry a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::394.modern_relevance: A large event is being planned, and every important contact is being called in. The verse is about coordination, not reflection.
ramayan::394.insight: It shifts attention to logistics and alliance-building rather than inner instruction.

ramayan::395.verse_sanskrit: सन्ति स्निग्धाश्च ये चान्ये राजान: पृथिवीतले । तानानय यथाक्षिप्रं सानुगान्सह बान्धवान् । । 11326 । ।
ramayan::395.verse_hindi: Bring all other kings of this earth, who are friendly with us. Along with their retinues, families and relatives.
ramayan::395.english_translation: Bring all other kings of this earth who are friendly with us, along with their retinues, families, and relatives.
ramayan::395.translation_literal: सन्ति (there are) / स्निग्धाः (friendly) / च (and) / ये (who) / अन्ये (other) / राजानः (kings) / पृथिवीतले (on the earth) / तान् (them) / आनय (bring) / यथाक्षिप्रम् (as quickly as possible) / सानुगान् (with retinues) / सह (along with) / बान्धवान् (relatives)
ramayan::395.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::395.essence: A summons to one ruler reaches an entire network of lives.
ramayan::395.simple_meaning: Bring the friendly kings of the land quickly, along with their followers, families, and relatives.
ramayan::395.simple_insight: A royal invitation can gather not just rulers, but whole circles of loyalty.
ramayan::395.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is organizing a grand royal gathering through Sumantra. After naming allied kings from many regions, he adds that all other friendly rulers should come too, with their households and companions. The verse is a logistical command, not a teaching.
ramayan::395.modern_relevance: You’re planning a major event and realizing it is never just about the main guests. Every invitation pulls in teams, families, schedules, and commitments that move together.
ramayan::395.insight: It shifts attention to the ripple effect of leadership decisions and public invitations.

ramayan::396.verse_sanskrit: वसिष्ठवाक्यं तच्छ्रुत्वा सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितस्तदा । व्यादिशत्पुरुषांस्तत्र राज्ञामानयने शुभान् । । 11327 । ।
ramayan::396.verse_hindi: Having heard the words of Vasishta, Sumantra speedily despatched virtuous and auspicious emissaries to bring the kings.
ramayan::396.english_translation: Having heard Vasishta's words, Sumantra quickly sent out virtuous messengers there to bring the kings.
ramayan::396.translation_literal: वसिष्ठवाक्यं (Vasishta's words) / तत् (that) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सुमन्त्रः (Sumantra) / त्वरितः (quickly) / तदा (then) / व्यादिशत् (sent out, dispatched) / पुरुषान् (messengers, men) / तत्र (there) / राज्ञाम् (of kings) / आनयने (for bringing) / शुभान् (virtuous, auspicious)
ramayan::396.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::396.essence: Clear orders matter only when someone moves at once.
ramayan::396.simple_meaning: Sumantra immediately sent messengers to gather the kings after hearing Vasishta's instruction.
ramayan::396.simple_insight: Some moments are just execution: hear clearly, act quickly, and keep the larger plan moving.
ramayan::396.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's gathering, Vasishta gives the order and Sumantra does not hesitate. He sends out trusted men to summon the kings. The verse is a small but necessary link in the larger movement of alliances.
ramayan::396.modern_relevance: Your manager gives a clear instruction in the middle of a crowded day, and you move without delay. The real test is not grand speech — it's clean follow-through.
ramayan::396.insight: It trains the mind to convert instruction into action without hesitation.

ramayan::397.verse_sanskrit: स्वयमेव हि धर्मात्मा प्रययौ मुनिशासनात् । सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितो भूत्वा समानेतुं महीक्षित: । । 11328 । ।
ramayan::397.verse_hindi: In accordance with the ascetics order, righteous Sumantra himself quickly set out to escort Janaka and other kings.
ramayan::397.english_translation: In accordance with the ascetics order, righteous Sumantra himself quickly set out to escort Janaka and other kings.
ramayan::397.translation_literal: स्वयमेव (himself) / हि (indeed) / धर्मात्मा (righteous) / प्रययौ (set out) / मुनिशासनात् (by the sage's command) / सुमन्त्रः (Sumantra) / त्वरितः (quickly) / भूत्वा (having become) / समानेतुम् (to bring together / escort) / महीक्षितः (kings)
ramayan::397.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::397.essence: Right action begins the moment you stop delaying.
ramayan::397.simple_meaning: Sumantra immediately obeys the sage's command and goes to bring the kings.
ramayan::397.simple_insight: Prompt obedience matters when a task must be done without delay.
ramayan::397.detailed_meaning: At Vasishta's command, Sumantra does not hesitate. He quickly goes to bring Janaka and the other kings to the sacrifice, showing how smoothly the royal household responds when the priestly order is given.
ramayan::397.modern_relevance: A message lands in your inbox while everyone else is still discussing who should handle it. You stop, act, and get moving before hesitation spreads.
ramayan::397.insight: It shifts attention from debate to immediate execution of the right instruction.

ramayan::398.verse_sanskrit: ते च कर्मान्तिकास्सर्वे वसिष्ठाय च धीमते । सर्वं निवेदयन्ति स्म यज्ञे यदुपकल्पितम् । । 11329 । ।
ramayan::398.verse_hindi: All the workers reported to the wise sage, Vasishta about the tasks completed for the sacrifice.
ramayan::398.english_translation: All the workers reported to the wise sage, Vasishta, about everything that had been prepared for the sacrifice.
ramayan::398.translation_literal: ते (those) / च (and) / कर्मान्तिकाः (workers) / सर्वे (all) / वसिष्ठाय (to Vasishta) / च (and) / धीमते (to the wise one) / सर्वम् (everything) / निवेदयन्ति स्म (reported) / यज्ञे (for the sacrifice) / यत् (what) / उपकल्पितम् (had been prepared)
ramayan::398.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::398.essence: The sacrifice advances through careful, invisible work.
ramayan::398.simple_meaning: The workers finished their assigned tasks and informed Vasishta that everything for the sacrifice was ready.
ramayan::398.simple_insight: Careful preparation matters, even before the main event begins.
ramayan::398.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s sacrifice, the preparations are nearing completion. The workers report back to Vasishta, the guiding priest, with the details of what has been arranged. It is a quiet logistical moment, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::398.modern_relevance: You finish the setup, check the list, and send the update before the guests arrive. The real work is often invisible until everything is ready.
ramayan::398.insight: It highlights the discipline of preparation and reporting before a major ritual or event.

ramayan::399.verse_sanskrit: तत:प्रीतो द्विजश्रेष्ठस्तान् सर्वानिदमब्रवीत् । अवज्ञया न दातव्यं कस्यचिल्लीलयाऽपि वा । । 11330 । । अवज्ञया कृतं हन्याद्दातारं नात्र संशय: । 28
ramayan::399.verse_hindi: Then, well pleased, the best among brahmins (Vasishta) said to them all Nobody should be offered any thing with disregard. Anything given with contempt undoubtedly  results in the destruction of the donor.
ramayan::399.english_translation: Then, pleased, the best of brahmins said to them all: no gift should ever be given with disrespect, not even in play. A gift made contemptuously destroys the giver; there is no doubt of that.
ramayan::399.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रीतः (pleased) / द्विजश्रेष्ठः (best among brahmins) / तान् (to them) / सर्वान् (all) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said) / अवज्ञया (with disrespect) / न (not) / दातव्यम् (to be given) / कस्यचिद् (to anyone) / लीलया (even in play) / अपि (also) / वा (or) / अवज्ञया (with contempt) / कृतम् (done) / हन्यात् (destroys) / दातारम् (the giver) / न (not) / अत्र (here) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::399.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::399.essence: Disrespect poisons even a gift and turns giving against you.
ramayan::399.simple_meaning: A gift should never be given carelessly or with contempt. The way you give matters as much as what you give.
ramayan::399.simple_insight: Generosity loses its value when it carries disrespect.
ramayan::399.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just overseen the completion of sacrificial arrangements. Pleased with the work, he warns the assembled men that offerings must never be made with contempt or casual mockery, because disrespect in giving turns the act against the giver.
ramayan::399.modern_relevance: You hand someone a late apology, a rushed favor, or money with visible annoyance. The gesture lands as insult, not kindness. The manner of giving can damage what the gift was meant to heal.
ramayan::399.insight: It teaches you to match generosity with reverence, so your action supports rather than corrupts its own meaning.

ramayan::400.verse_sanskrit: तत: कैश्चिदहोरात्रैरुपयाता महीक्षित: । । 11331 । । बहूनि रत्नान्यादाय राज्ञो दशरथस्य वै ।
ramayan::400.verse_hindi: Meanwhile kings from several countries to travelling nights and days arrived bringing with them various kinds of (precious) gifts.
ramayan::400.english_translation: Meanwhile, after some days and nights, kings arrived from many lands, bringing many precious gifts to King Dasharatha.
ramayan::400.translation_literal: तत: (then/meanwhile) / कैश्चित् (by some) / अहोरात्रैः (days and nights) / उपयाताḥ (having arrived) / महीक्षितः (kings) / बहूनि (many) / रत्नानि (gems/precious things) / आदाय (bringing) / राज्ञः (to the king) / दशरथस्य (of Dasharatha) / वै (indeed)
ramayan::400.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::400.essence: The sacrifice draws kings and gifts before a single rite begins.
ramayan::400.simple_meaning: Kings from different lands came to Dasharatha bringing valuable gifts, showing the scale of the gathering around the sacrifice.
ramayan::400.simple_insight: Great occasions draw people, offerings, and attention from far away.
ramayan::400.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just overseen preparations for Dasharatha's sacrifice. Now rulers from many regions arrive over several days and nights with gifts in hand. The verse is scene-setting: it shows the royal gathering growing before the ritual begins.
ramayan::400.modern_relevance: A major event starts to fill with arrivals, deliveries, and formal greetings before the first word is spoken. The real work is already visible in who has shown up.
ramayan::400.insight: It shifts attention from the ritual itself to the network of support gathering around it.

ramayan::401.verse_sanskrit: ततो वसिष्ठस्सुप्रीतो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् । । 11332 । । उपयाता नरव्याघ्र राजानस्तव शासनात् । मयापि सत्कृता: सर्वे यथार्हं राजसत्तमा: । । 11333 । ।
ramayan::401.verse_hindi: Thereupon, wellpleased, Vasishta addressing Dasaratha said O best among men, beacuse of your command, kings from various countries have arrived. I have extended due hospitality to those noble kings according to their station.
ramayan::401.english_translation: Thereupon, well pleased, Vasishta addressed Dasaratha: "O best among men, because of your command, kings from various countries have arrived. I have extended due hospitality to all of them according to their rank."
ramayan::401.translation_literal: तत: (thereupon) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / सुप्रीतः (well pleased) / राजानम् (to the king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / उपयाताḥ (having arrived) / नरव्याघ्र (best among men) / राजानः (kings) / तव (your) / शासनात् (by command) / मया (by me) / अपि (also) / सत्कृताः (honoured) / सर्वे (all) / यथार्हम् (as appropriate) / राजसत्तमाः (excellent kings)
ramayan::401.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::401.essence: Proper welcome prepares the ground for what comes next.
ramayan::401.simple_meaning: Vasishta tells Dasaratha that the visiting kings have arrived because of his order, and that he has welcomed them properly according to their status.
ramayan::401.simple_insight: Respectful treatment matters, especially when many powerful people are gathered together.
ramayan::401.detailed_meaning: At Dasaratha's sacrificial gathering, kings have come from many lands with gifts and attendants. Vasishta reports that the arrangements are complete and that each guest has been received with proper honour, clearing the way for the sacrifice to proceed.
ramayan::401.modern_relevance: The guests are already outside the hall, and the whole event depends on whether the host has prepared well. Before the big moment starts, someone has to make sure everyone feels properly received.
ramayan::401.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the care that makes ceremony meaningful.

ramayan::402.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञीयं च कृतं राजन् पुरुषैस्सुसमाहितै: । निर्यातु च भवान्यष्टुं यज्ञायतनमन्तिकात् । । 11334 । ।
ramayan::402.verse_hindi: O king, persons with composed minds have made preparations for the yaga. Now be pleased to leave for sacrificial altar nearby to perform yaga.
ramayan::402.english_translation: O king, persons with composed minds have made the preparations for the sacrifice. Now please go from here to the nearby sacrificial altar and perform the sacrifice.
ramayan::402.translation_literal: यज्ञीयं (for the sacrifice) / च (and) / कृतं (has been made) / राजन् (O king) / पुरुषैः (by men) / सुसमाहितैः (with composed minds) / निर्यातु (may you go forth) / च (and) / भवान् (you) / अष्टुम् (to perform sacrifice) / यज्ञायतनम् (to the sacrificial altar) / अन्तिकात् (from nearby)
ramayan::402.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::402.essence: The setup is complete; now the king must enter the rite.
ramayan::402.simple_meaning: The preparations are complete, and the king is being asked to go to the sacrificial altar and begin the ritual.
ramayan::402.simple_insight: Some moments are about readiness, not reflection. Once the ground is prepared, you step forward and begin.
ramayan::402.detailed_meaning: Vasishta speaks to Dasharatha after kings have arrived with gifts and the sacrificial setup is finished. This is not a teaching verse; it is a ceremonial instruction moving the king from preparation into action.
ramayan::402.modern_relevance: The room is set, the documents are printed, and everyone is waiting for you to walk in. At some point, preparation stops being preparation and becomes the moment itself.
ramayan::402.insight: It marks the shift from arranging conditions to entering the ritual act.

ramayan::403.verse_sanskrit: सर्वकामैरुपहृतैरुपेतं च समन्तत: । द्रष्टुमर्हसि राजेन्द्र मनसेव विनिर्मितम् । । 11335 । ।
ramayan::403.verse_hindi: O foremost of kings, you ought to see the sacrificial ground full of sources of entertainment arranged everywhere, as though improvised by imagination.
ramayan::403.english_translation: O foremost of kings, you ought to see the sacrificial ground full of every desired offering, arranged all around, as though made by the mind itself.
ramayan::403.translation_literal: सर्वकामैः (with all desired things) / उपहृतैः (offered, brought) / उपेतम् (filled, furnished) / च (and) / समन्ततः (all around) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अर्हसि (you are fit, you should) / राजेन्द्र (O foremost of kings) / मनसा (by the mind) / इव (as if) / विनिर्मितम् (constructed, fashioned)
ramayan::403.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::403.essence: The place is ready; the king only needs to enter.
ramayan::403.simple_meaning: The sacrificial ground has been prepared with everything needed, arranged beautifully all around. Vasishta invites Dasharatha to come and see it.
ramayan::403.simple_insight: Some moments are about readiness: the work is done, and now you are invited to step in.
ramayan::403.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has finished preparing the sacrifice with the help of skilled attendants. He now tells Dasharatha that the sacred ground is ready and worth seeing. This is a ceremonial invitation, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::403.modern_relevance: You walk into a hall after the final cleanup, lights set, chairs aligned, everything waiting for the first guest. The work is invisible now, but the welcome is complete.
ramayan::403.insight: It marks the transition from preparation to participation.

ramayan::404.verse_sanskrit: तथा वसिष्ठवचनादृश्यशृङ्गस्य चोभयो: । शुभे दिवसनक्षत्रे निर्यातो जगतीपति: । । 11336 । ।
ramayan::404.verse_hindi: In response to the words of Vasishta and Rsyasringa, the Lord of the earth (Dasaratha) entered the sacrificial pavilion on a favourable day presided over by an auspicious star.
ramayan::404.english_translation: In response to the words of Vasishta and Rsyasringa, the Lord of the earth, Dasaratha, entered the sacrificial pavilion on a favourable day under an auspicious star.
ramayan::404.translation_literal: तथा (thus/in that way) / वसिष्ठ-वचनात् (from Vasishta's words) / ऋश्यशृङ्गस्य (of Rsyasringa) / च (and) / उभयोः (of both) / शुभे (auspicious) / दिवस-नक्षत्रे (day and star) / निर्यातः (having gone forth) / जगतीपतिḥ (lord of the earth)
ramayan::404.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::404.essence: A king moves when counsel and timing finally align.
ramayan::404.simple_meaning: Dasaratha set out for the sacrificial pavilion when his teachers advised him and the day was auspicious.
ramayan::404.simple_insight: Right timing and wise counsel prepare the way for important action.
ramayan::404.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha is no longer hesitating. After Vasishta and Rsyasringa speak, the king leaves for the sacrificial pavilion on a blessed day. The verse simply marks the transition from preparation to ritual action.
ramayan::404.modern_relevance: You wait for the right moment, the right advice, the right opening — then you finally walk in and begin.
ramayan::404.insight: It marks the shift from planning to entering the work already prepared.

ramayan::405.verse_sanskrit: ततो वसिष्ठप्रमुखास्सर्व एव द्विजोत्तमा: । ऋश्यशृङ्गं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञकर्मारभन् तदा । । 11337 । । यज्ञवाटगतास्सर्वे यथाशास्त्रं यथाविधि । 3
ramayan::405.verse_hindi: At that moment the best of brahmins led by Vasishta and headed by Rsyasringa, entered the sacrificial enclosure and began the sacrifice in accordance with traditions and scriptural stipulations.
ramayan::405.english_translation: At that moment the best of brahmins led by Vasishta, with Rsyasringa at the front, began the sacrificial rites. All of them entered the sacrificial enclosure and performed the sacrifice according to the scriptures and the proper procedure.
ramayan::405.translation_literal: तत: (then) / वसिष्ठ-प्रमुखाः (led by Vasishta) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / द्विजोत्तमाः (best of the twice-born) / ऋश्यशृङ्गम् (Rsyasringa) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing at the front) / यज्ञ-कर्म (sacrificial rites) / आरभन् (began) / तदा (then) / यज्ञ-वाट-गताः (having entered the sacrificial enclosure) / सर्वे (all) / यथा-शास्त्रम् (according to scripture) / यथा-विधि (according to proper procedure)
ramayan::405.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::405.essence: Sacred action begins only when order is obeyed.
ramayan::405.simple_meaning: Vasishta and the other leading priests, with Rsyasringa in front, entered the sacrificial area and began the ritual exactly as prescribed.
ramayan::405.simple_insight: Some moments matter because everyone does the right thing in the right order.
ramayan::405.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has prepared the great sacrifice to win a son. Now Vasishta, Rsyasringa, and the leading priests step into the enclosed ritual space and begin the rites exactly as the tradition demands. The verse marks the formal start of the ceremony.
ramayan::405.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the ceremony begins, and everyone knows the smallest mistake could ruin months of preparation. The real work starts when the right people move in the right order.
ramayan::405.insight: It shifts attention from the desire for results to the precision of proper process.

ramayan::406.verse_sanskrit: अथ संवत्सरे पूर्णे तस्मिन्प्राप्ते तुरङ्गमे । सरय्वाश्चोत्तरे तीरे राज्ञो यज्ञोऽभ्यवर्तत । । 1141 । ।
ramayan::406.verse_hindi: After completion of one year when the sacrificial horse had returned, the sacrifice by the king (Dasaratha) commenced on the northern bank of river Sarayu.
ramayan::406.english_translation: After one full year, when the sacrificial horse had returned, King Dasharatha's sacrifice began on the northern bank of the Sarayu.
ramayan::406.translation_literal: अथ (then) / संवत्सरे (after a year) / पूर्णे (completed) / तस्मिन् (in that) / प्राप्ते (having returned) / तुरङ्गमे (horse) / सरय्वाः (of Sarayu) / चोत्तरे (and on the northern) / तीरे (bank) / राज्ञः (of the king) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / अभ्यवर्तत (began)
ramayan::406.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::406.essence: The long preparation ends, and the real ritual finally starts.
ramayan::406.simple_meaning: A year later, the sacrificial horse returned, and Dasharatha's great ritual began on the Sarayu's northern bank.
ramayan::406.simple_insight: Some moments only mark the turning of a larger wheel.
ramayan::406.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha's horse sacrifice has reached its next stage. After a year, the horse returns and the royal ritual begins on the northern bank of the Sarayu, with priests already gathered around Rsyasringa.
ramayan::406.modern_relevance: You wait months for a plan to mature, and then the real work finally starts. The preparation was necessary, but it was never the whole story.
ramayan::406.insight: It shifts attention from anticipation to the moment action actually begins.

ramayan::407.verse_sanskrit: ऋश्यशृङ्गं पुरस्कृत्य कर्म चक्रुर्द्विजर्षभा: । अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे राज्ञोऽस्य सुमहात्मन: । । 1142 । ।
ramayan::407.verse_hindi: The best of brahmins led by Rsyasringa performed the rituals of aswamedha organised by the exceedingly magnanimous king.
ramayan::407.english_translation: The best of brahmins, led by Rsyasringa, performed the rituals of the great horse sacrifice for that greatly magnanimous king.
ramayan::407.translation_literal: ऋश्यशृङ्गं (Rsyasringa) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front, led by) / कर्म (rituals, work) / चक्रुः (they performed) / द्विजर्षभाः (best of brahmins) / अश्वमेधे (in the horse sacrifice) / महायज्ञे (in the great sacrifice) / राज्ञः (of the king) / अस्य (of this) / सुमहात्मनः (of the greatly magnanimous one)
ramayan::407.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::407.essence: Great undertakings succeed through exact ritual, not just intention.
ramayan::407.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa and the leading brahmins carried out the horse-sacrifice rituals for King Dasharatha exactly as required.
ramayan::407.simple_insight: Big results still depend on careful, disciplined ritual done the right way.
ramayan::407.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha's horse sacrifice has begun on the north bank of the Sarayu. Rsyasringa stands at the front while expert priests perform each rite in order. The verse simply records the sacred machinery of the ceremony, not its teaching.
ramayan::407.modern_relevance: A major project finally starts, and the real work is still hidden in the details no one applauds. The outcome depends on people who know the procedure and keep it exact.
ramayan::407.insight: It shifts attention from the headline event to the disciplined execution that makes it possible.

ramayan::408.verse_sanskrit: कर्म कुर्वन्ति विधिवद्याजका वेदपारगा: । यथाविधि यथान्यायं परिक्रामन्ति शास्त्रत: । । 1143 । ।
ramayan::408.verse_hindi: The chief priests, masters of the Vedas, conducted the rituals in consonance with traditions and scriptures. They officiated in conformity with duties laid down in the Vedas and according to law.
ramayan::408.english_translation: The chief priests, masters of the Vedas, conducted the rituals in consonance with tradition and scripture. They performed every rite according to rule and proper order.
ramayan::408.translation_literal: कर्म (ritual action) / कुर्वन्ति (they do) / विधिवत् (according to rule) / याजका: (the priests) / वेदपारगा: (those who have crossed to the far shore of the Vedas) / यथाविधि (according to ordinance) / यथान्यायम् (according to proper order) / परिक्रामन्ति (they move around / proceed) / शास्त्रत: (according to scripture)
ramayan::408.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::408.essence: Sacred action depends on exact order, not improvisation.
ramayan::408.simple_meaning: The priests carried out the sacrifice exactly as the sacred rules required, following both scripture and proper ritual order.
ramayan::408.simple_insight: Precision matters when a sacred act is being done; care and order are part of the offering.
ramayan::408.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha's horse sacrifice has begun on the northern bank of the Sarayu. Rishyasringa and the priestly experts are not improvising; they are moving through each rite exactly as tradition demands. The verse simply records that disciplined ritual order.
ramayan::408.modern_relevance: A wedding, memorial, or opening ceremony can feel chaotic unless someone holds the sequence steady. This verse values the quiet discipline that lets a public ritual carry meaning.
ramayan::408.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to exactness: the rite matters because it is done properly.

ramayan::409.verse_sanskrit: प्रवर्ग्यं शास्त्रत: कृत्वा तथैवोपसदं द्विजा:चक्रुश्च विधिवत्सर्वमधिकं कर्म शास्त्रत: । । 1144 । ।
ramayan::409.verse_hindi: Brahmins performed pravargya and upasada and other ceremonies as per the scriptures and traditions.
ramayan::409.english_translation: The brahmins performed pravargya, upasad, and all the remaining rites exactly as the scriptures prescribed.
ramayan::409.translation_literal: प्रवर्ग्यम् (pravargya rite) / शास्त्रत: (according to scripture) / कृत्वा (having done) / तथा (likewise) / एव (indeed) / उपसदम् (upasad rite) / द्विजाः (the brahmins) / चक्रुः (performed) / च (and) / विधिवत् (in proper order) / सर्वम् (all) / अधिकम् (additional) / कर्म (rites) / शास्त्रत: (according to scripture)
ramayan::409.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::409.essence: Proper ritual is carried by exactness, not enthusiasm.
ramayan::409.simple_meaning: The priests carried out every required ritual exactly according to the sacred rules.
ramayan::409.simple_insight: Some duties are fulfilled by precision, not improvisation.
ramayan::409.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa and the brahmins are in the middle of Dasharatha's horse sacrifice. This verse is not a teaching in itself; it simply records that the priests completed the prescribed rites in exact order, as part of the larger ceremonial sequence.
ramayan::409.modern_relevance: A wedding team checks each item off the ritual list while the family waits in silence. The moment works only because everyone respects the exact order.
ramayan::409.insight: It shows that sacred action depends on faithful procedure, not personal invention.

ramayan::410.verse_sanskrit: अभिपूज्य ततो हृष्टास्सर्वे चक्रुर्यथाविधि । प्रातस्सवनपूर्वाणि कर्माणि मुनिपुङ्गवा: । । 1145 । ।
ramayan::410.verse_hindi: Thereafter the eminent ascetics, rejoicing in their hearts performed the worship (of celestial beings) and conducted the prescribed rituals starting with morning ablutions etc.
ramayan::410.english_translation: Thereafter the eminent ascetics, rejoicing in their hearts, performed the worship and the prescribed rituals beginning with the morning rites.
ramayan::410.translation_literal: अभिपूज्य (having worshipped) / ततः (then) / हृष्टाः (rejoicing) / सर्वे (all) / चक्रुः (they performed) / यथाविधि (according to proper rule) / प्रातःसवनपूर्वाणि (beginning with the morning libations) / कर्माणि (ritual acts) / मुनिपुङ्गवाः (bulls among sages)
ramayan::410.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::410.essence: The rites matter because they are done in the right order.
