ramayan::410.simple_meaning: The sages joyfully carried out the required worship and rituals in the proper order, starting with the morning rites.
ramayan::410.simple_insight: There is calm in doing sacred work carefully, without haste or confusion.
ramayan::410.detailed_meaning: In a ritual setting, the leading sages complete the worship and then begin the prescribed morning ceremonies in exact order. The verse is part of a sequence describing the rite, not a separate teaching moment.
ramayan::410.modern_relevance: You arrive early to a ceremony, a meeting, or a family function and everyone quietly falls into the proper sequence. Nothing dramatic happens, but the care itself holds the moment together.
ramayan::410.insight: It highlights disciplined ritual order rather than a new principle.

ramayan::411.verse_sanskrit: ऐन्द्रश्च विधिवद्दत्तो राजा चाभिषुतोऽनघ: । माध्यन्दिनं च सवनं प्रावर्तत यथाक्रमम् । । 1146 । ।
ramayan::411.verse_hindi: Havis was duly offered to Indra daily. The juice was extracted in the morning by pressing the soma plant. Midday ablutions were performed. All in proper sequence.
ramayan::411.english_translation: Havis was duly offered to Indra. The soma juice was pressed for the king at the proper time, and the midday rites proceeded in order.
ramayan::411.translation_literal: ऐन्द्रः (for Indra) / च (and) / विधिवत् (according to rule) / दत्तः (offered) / राजा (king) / च (and) / अभिषुतः (pressed) / अनघः (sinless) / माध्यन्दिनम् (midday) / च (and) / सवनम् (pressing/rite) / प्रावर्तत (began) / यथाक्रमम् (in due order)
ramayan::411.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::411.essence: The rite moves forward only when every step is exact.
ramayan::411.simple_meaning: The ritual continues in exact order: offerings are made, soma is pressed, and the midday ceremony begins.
ramayan::411.simple_insight: Some moments are about exactness, not drama.
ramayan::411.detailed_meaning: The sages are conducting a Vedic sacrifice step by step. After the earlier rites, the offering to Indra, the soma pressing, and the midday ceremony all proceed in the prescribed sequence. The verse simply records the ritual order.
ramayan::411.insight: It shows how sacred work depends on sequence, not improvisation.

ramayan::412.verse_sanskrit: तृतीयसवनं चैव राज्ञोऽस्य सुमहात्मन: । चक्रुस्तेशास्त्रतो दृष्ट्वा तथा ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवा: । । 1147 । ।
ramayan::412.verse_hindi: Those exceedingly noble and eminent brahmins performed third pressing of the soma, in conformity with the sastras.
ramayan::412.english_translation: Those exceedingly noble and eminent brahmins performed the third pressing of soma for this great king, in accordance with the scriptures.
ramayan::412.translation_literal: तृतीयसवनं (third pressing) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / राज्ञः (of the king) / अस्य (of this) / सुमहात्मनः (great-souled) / चक्रुः (performed) / ते (they) / शास्त्रतः (according to scripture) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तथा (thus) / ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवाः (best of brahmins)
ramayan::412.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::412.essence: Sacred work is complete only when done exactly right.
ramayan::412.simple_meaning: The priests completed the king's third soma pressing exactly as the sacred rules required.
ramayan::412.simple_insight: Care done properly matters, even when no drama is visible.
ramayan::412.detailed_meaning: At the sacrificial rite for the great king, the leading brahmins carry out the third soma pressing precisely as prescribed. The verse is part of a careful ritual sequence, showing flawless completion rather than teaching a separate principle.
ramayan::412.modern_relevance: You double-check the ceremony setup before guests arrive, and every detail is in place. Quiet competence can carry the whole moment.
ramayan::412.insight: It highlights exact ritual execution, not interpretation or debate.

ramayan::413.verse_sanskrit: न चाहुतमभूत्तत्र स्खलितं वापि किञ्चन । दृश्यते ब्रह्मवत्सर्वं क्षेमयुक्तं हि चक्रिरे । । 1148 । ।
ramayan::413.verse_hindi: There were no omissions in the offerings nor any lappes in the performance. Everything was done through recitation of mantras and in a wholesome way.
ramayan::413.english_translation: There were no omissions in the offerings nor any lapses in the performance. Everything was done through recitation of mantras and in a wholesome way.
ramayan::413.translation_literal: न (not) / च (and not) / अहुतम् (unoffered offering) / अभूत् (was there) / तत्र (there) / स्खलितम् (slip, lapse) / वा (or) / अपि (even) / किञ्चन (anything) / दृश्यते (is seen) / ब्रह्मवत् (like Brahman, in sacred order) / सर्वम् (everything) / क्षेमयुक्तम् (joined with well-being) / हि (indeed) / चक्रिरे (they did, performed)
ramayan::413.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::413.essence: Perfect ritual means nothing is left incomplete.
ramayan::413.simple_meaning: The sacrifice was carried out flawlessly. No offering was missed, and every ritual step was completed properly.
ramayan::413.simple_insight: Care given fully leaves no room for regret.
ramayan::413.detailed_meaning: The brahmins are still describing the great sacrifice. After the soma pressings, they say nothing was left undone: no offering was missed, no ritual slipped out of order, and every act was performed with exact sacred care.
ramayan::413.modern_relevance: You finish the presentation, then check the last slide one more time. Nothing is flashy, but nothing is missing either. That quiet completeness is its own kind of strength.
ramayan::413.insight: It shifts attention from speed to exactness, showing that true care is visible in what you do not overlook.

ramayan::414.verse_sanskrit: न तेष्वहस्सु श्रान्तो वा क्षुधितो वापि दृश्यते । नाविद्वान्ब्राह्मणस्तत्र नाशतानुचरस्तथा । । 1149 । ।
ramayan::414.verse_hindi: During the days (of sacrifice) none felt tired or hungry. There was no brahmin who was not learned or had less than a hundred followers (or disciples).
ramayan::414.english_translation: During the days of the sacrifice, no one was tired or hungry. There was no brahmin there who was not learned or who had fewer than a hundred followers.
ramayan::414.translation_literal: न (not) / तेषु अहस्सु (in those days) / श्रान्तः (tired) / वा (or) / क्षुधितः (hungry) / वा (or) / अपि (even) / दृश्यते (is seen) / न (not) / अविद्वान् (unlearned) / ब्राह्मणः (brahmin) / तत्र (there) / न (not) / अशत-अनुचरः (one with fewer than a hundred followers) / तथा (also)
ramayan::414.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::414.essence: Flawless order shows up even in the smallest human needs.
ramayan::414.simple_meaning: The sacrifice was conducted with such care that no one was tired or hungry, and every brahmin present was learned and well attended.
ramayan::414.simple_insight: When something is done properly, even the smallest details reflect order and care.
ramayan::414.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a royal sacrifice, the scene is one of complete ritual order. The priests are learned, the service is exact, and even basic needs are fully met. The verse adds a supporting detail to show how flawlessly the ceremony was maintained.
ramayan::414.modern_relevance: A long event runs past midnight, yet no one is left scrambling for food, no task is left half-done, and the whole room feels quietly held together.
ramayan::414.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony alone to the discipline that makes ceremony complete.

ramayan::415.verse_sanskrit: ब्राह्मणा भुञ्जते नित्यं नाथवन्तश्च भुञ्जते । तापसा भुञ्जते चापि श्रमणा भुञ्जतेतथा । । 11410 । ।
ramayan::415.verse_hindi: During that period brahmanas as well as those who have masters, (the sudras), ascetics and monks had enough to eat.
ramayan::415.english_translation: Brahmins ate there every day, and so did those with masters, ascetics, and monks.
ramayan::415.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणाः (Brahmins) / भुञ्जते (eat) / नित्यम् (always) / नाथवन्तः (those with masters) / च (and) / भुञ्जते (eat) / तापसाः (ascetics) / भुञ्जते (eat) / च (and) / अपि (also) / श्रमणाः (monks) / भुञ्जते (eat) / तथा (likewise)
ramayan::415.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::415.essence: True abundance is visible in who gets fed.
ramayan::415.simple_meaning: Everyone was fed there: learned Brahmins, ascetics, monks, and even those dependent on others.
ramayan::415.simple_insight: A good household or kingdom leaves no one hungry, no matter their station.
ramayan::415.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a grand sacrificial setting, Valmiki lists who is being fed. Brahmins, ascetics, monks, and dependents all receive food without shortage. The verse is a supporting detail in a larger description of abundance and order.
ramayan::415.modern_relevance: A wedding hall after the meal service, where volunteers keep checking the back tables so no guest leaves hungry. The care is not flashy, but it shows whether the gathering was truly generous.
ramayan::415.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to care: the real measure is whether everyone is sustained.

ramayan::416.verse_sanskrit: वृद्धाश्च व्याधिताश्चैव स्त्रियो बालास्तथैव च । अनिशं भुञ्जमानानां न तृप्तिरुपलभ्यते । । 11411 । ।
ramayan::416.verse_hindi: The aged, the sick, women and also children ate there and knew no limit to their enjoyment.
ramayan::416.english_translation: The aged, the sick, women, and children ate there without ever feeling satisfied.
ramayan::416.translation_literal: वृद्धाः (the aged) / च (and) / व्याधिताः (the sick) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / स्त्रियः (women) / बालाः (children) / तथा (also) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अनिशम् (continuously) / भुञ्जमानानाम् (of those eating) / न (not) / तृप्तिः (satisfaction) / उपलभ्यते (is found)
ramayan::416.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::416.essence: A good feast leaves no one wanting.
ramayan::416.simple_meaning: Even the aged, the sick, women, and children were fed continuously, and no one went away unsatisfied.
ramayan::416.simple_insight: True abundance is when the vulnerable are fed first and no one leaves wanting.
ramayan::416.detailed_meaning: In a great sacrificial gathering, food is being served so generously that even the aged, the sick, women, and children keep eating without reaching the end of their enjoyment. The verse adds to the picture of a feast overflowing with care and abundance.
ramayan::416.modern_relevance: At a wedding buffet where elders, children, and exhausted guests keep returning for more, you can feel the difference between mere catering and real hospitality.
ramayan::416.insight: It highlights abundance measured by care, not by display.

ramayan::417.verse_sanskrit: दीयतां दीयतामन्नं वासांसि विविधानि च । इति सञ्चोदितास्तत्र तथा चक्रुरनेकश: । । 11412 । ।
ramayan::417.verse_hindi: Give food, give, various kinds of clothes echoed the organisers. And they (in charge of distribution) did.
ramayan::417.english_translation: Give food, give various kinds of clothes,' the organisers called out there, and they distributed them in many ways.
ramayan::417.translation_literal: दीयताम् (let it be given) / दीयताम् (let it be given) / अन्नम् (food) / वासांसि (garments) / विविधानि (various kinds) / च (and) / इति (thus) / सञ्चोदिताः (urged) / तत्र (there) / तथा (so) / चक्रुः (they did) / अनेकशः (in many ways)
ramayan::417.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::417.essence: Giving is happening everywhere, on purpose, and in abundance.
ramayan::417.simple_meaning: Food and clothing were handed out freely in many forms, with repeated calls to keep giving.
ramayan::417.simple_insight: Abundance becomes real only when it is shared openly.
ramayan::417.detailed_meaning: In this scene of public distribution, people are being fed and clothed without restraint. The verse is not teaching a principle; it is showing the scale and order of the generosity already underway, just before the next image of mountain-like heaps of food.
ramayan::417.modern_relevance: At a community kitchen, someone keeps calling for more plates, more rice, more clothes. The scene matters less as advice than as proof that care can become organized enough to reach everyone.
ramayan::417.insight: It shows generosity as an active system, not a private feeling.

ramayan::418.verse_sanskrit: अन्नकूटाश्च बहवो दृश्यन्ते पर्वतोपमा: । दिवसे दिवसे तत्र सिद्धस्य विधिवत्तदा । । 11413 । ।
ramayan::418.verse_hindi: There, could be seen day after day heaps of nicely cooked food, looking like mountains.
ramayan::418.english_translation: There, day after day, heaps of well-prepared food could be seen, like mountains.
ramayan::418.translation_literal: अन्नकूटाः (heaps of food) / च (and) / बहवः (many) / दृश्यन्ते (were seen) / पर्वतोपमाः (mountain-like) / दिवसे दिवसे (day after day) / तत्र (there) / सिद्धस्य (of the prepared food) / विधिवत् (properly) / तदा (then)
ramayan::418.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::418.essence: Steady generosity can turn care into something almost mountainous.
ramayan::418.simple_meaning: The gathering was so well supplied that piles of cooked food stood everywhere, as large as mountains.
ramayan::418.simple_insight: Abundance can become visible when care is sustained without interruption.
ramayan::418.detailed_meaning: At a great sacrifice, the organizers are feeding everyone who comes. After the earlier verses about endless eating and constant distribution, this line adds the visual scale: food is prepared in mountain-sized heaps every single day.
ramayan::418.modern_relevance: At a wedding kitchen where trays keep coming out faster than they disappear, you can feel what sustained generosity looks like. Care becomes visible in volume.
ramayan::418.insight: It shifts attention from a single act of giving to the scale of continuous provision.

ramayan::419.verse_hindi: Men and women who had come from various countries to that sacrifice were entertained with food and drink by the magnanimous (king).
ramayan::419.english_translation: Men and women who had come from various countries to that sacrifice were entertained with food and drink by the magnanimous king.
ramayan::419.translation_literal: नानादेशात् (from various countries) / अनुप्राप्ताः (having arrived) / पुरुषाः (men) / स्त्रीगणाः (groups of women) / तथा (and also) / अन्नपानैः (with food and drink) / सुविहिताः (well-provided for) / तस्मिन् (in that) / यज्ञे (sacrifice) / महात्मनः (of the magnanimous one)
ramayan::419.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::419.essence: True greatness shows up in how completely you feed the people around you.
ramayan::419.simple_meaning: People from many lands came to the sacrifice, and the king made sure they were well fed and given drink.
ramayan::419.simple_insight: Generosity is not grand speeches; it is making strangers feel cared for.
ramayan::419.detailed_meaning: At Rama’s great sacrifice, crowds arrive from many regions. The king’s household does not merely host the ritual — it feeds everyone properly. This verse is a supporting detail in the larger scene of abundance, order, and royal hospitality.
ramayan::419.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is overflowing, relatives are tired, and someone quietly keeps the tea, water, and food flowing for every guest. The care is invisible, but everyone feels it.
ramayan::419.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the practical kindness that makes ceremony real.

ramayan::420.verse_sanskrit: अन्नं हि विधिवत्साधु प्रशंसन्ति द्विजर्षभा: । अहो तृप्ता: स्म भद्रं ते इति शुश्राव राघव: । । 11415 । ।
ramayan::420.verse_hindi: Brahmins having tasted the delicious food cooked in prescribed manner, praised saying Ah We are fully satisfied. Prosperity to you. Such were the words heard by king Dasaratha.
ramayan::420.english_translation: The Brahmins praised the food as properly prepared and delicious, saying, 'Ah, we are fully satisfied. Prosperity to you.' King Dasharatha heard those words.
ramayan::420.translation_literal: अन्नं (food) / हि (indeed) / विधिवत् (according to proper ritual) / साधु (excellent) / प्रशंसन्ति (they praise) / द्विजर्षभा: (best of the twice-born) / अहो (ah) / तृप्ता: (satisfied) / स्म (indeed) / भद्रं (prosperity) / ते (to you) / इति (thus) / शुश्राव (heard) / राघव: (Raghava/Dasharatha)
ramayan::420.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::420.essence: Proper care is seen first in the gratitude it awakens.
ramayan::420.simple_meaning: The priests praise the meal as properly made and say they are satisfied. Dasharatha hears their approval.
ramayan::420.simple_insight: Approval can be as nourishing as food when you’ve given your best.
ramayan::420.detailed_meaning: At Dasharatha’s great sacrifice, guests from many lands are being fed in abundance. The Brahmins taste the food, praise its proper preparation, and bless the host. Dasharatha hears their satisfaction as the ritual continues around him.
ramayan::420.modern_relevance: You spent hours preparing the meal, the event, the report, the homecoming. When someone finally says, 'That was wonderful,' the effort lands.
ramayan::420.insight: It shows how careful service is completed by sincere recognition from those served.

ramayan::421.verse_sanskrit: स्वलङ्कृताश्च पुरुषा ब्राह्मणान्पर्यवेषयन् । उपासते च तानन्ये सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डला: । । 11416 । ।
ramayan::421.verse_hindi: While brahmins were being served with food by welldressed men, some others wearing pendents studded with shining jewels assisted them.
ramayan::421.english_translation: While brahmins were being served with food by well-dressed men, some others wearing pendants studded with shining jewels assisted them.
ramayan::421.translation_literal: स्वलङ्कृताः (well-adorned) / च (and) / पुरुषाः (men) / ब्राह्मणान् (the brahmins) / पर्यवेषयन् (served around, attended upon) / उपासते (assisted, waited upon) / च (and) / तान् (them) / अन्ये (others) / सुमृष्ट-मणि-कुण्डलाः (with brightly polished jewel earrings)
ramayan::421.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::421.essence: The ceremony’s greatness appears in the care given to every guest.
ramayan::421.simple_meaning: Well-dressed men served the brahmins, while others with shining jewel earrings helped them.
ramayan::421.simple_insight: A great gathering is shown through its care for guests, not through grandeur alone.
ramayan::421.detailed_meaning: At Rama’s sacrifice, the feast is in full flow. Brahmins are being served by richly dressed attendants, while others with jeweled ornaments help them. The verse adds atmosphere and order, setting the scene before the learned discussion begins.
ramayan::421.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall, servers move quietly between tables while helpers refill water and guide guests. The real dignity of the event is in that invisible care.
ramayan::421.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the disciplined hospitality that makes a sacred gathering complete.

ramayan::422.verse_sanskrit: कर्मान्तरे तदा विप्रा हेतुवादान्बहूनपि । प्राहुश्च वाग्मिनो धीरा: परस्परजिगीषया । । 11417 । ।
ramayan::422.verse_hindi: In the interval between ceremonies, eloquent and sagacious brahmins were engaged in various disputations, desirous of victory.
ramayan::422.english_translation: In the interval between ceremonies, eloquent and sagacious brahmins were engaged in many debates, each seeking victory.
ramayan::422.translation_literal: कर्मान्तरे (in the interval between rites) / तदा (then) / विप्रा (brahmins) / हेतुवादान् (arguments) / बहून् (many) / अपि (also) / प्राहुः (spoke) / च (and) / वाग्मिनः (eloquent) / धीराः (wise, steady) / परस्परजिगीषया (with desire to defeat one another)
ramayan::422.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::422.essence: Learning becomes rivalry when victory matters more than understanding.
ramayan::422.simple_meaning: Between ritual acts, learned priests argued with one another, each trying to outdo the others.
ramayan::422.simple_insight: Even sacred gatherings can turn into contests of ego.
ramayan::422.detailed_meaning: At Dasharatha's sacrifice, the rituals are underway and the priests are well-fed and adorned. In the pauses between offerings, learned brahmins fall into debate, each wanting to win. The verse simply shows the atmosphere around the rite, not a teaching of its own.
ramayan::422.modern_relevance: At a conference lunch break, the smartest people in the room start trying to one-up each other. The setting is formal, but the ego is still looking for an audience.
ramayan::422.insight: It shows how easily even serious knowledge can become competition.

ramayan::423.verse_sanskrit: दिवसे दिवसे तत्र संस्तरे कुशला द्विजा: । सर्वकर्माणि चक्रुस्ते यथाशास्त्रं प्रचोदिता: । । 11418 । ।
ramayan::423.verse_hindi: Every day in that sacrifice brahmins, skilful in rituals, persuaded (by sage Vasishta), performed all their duties as per tradition.
ramayan::423.english_translation: Every day in that sacrifice, brahmins skilled in ritual performed all their duties according to scripture, urged on by Vasishta.
ramayan::423.translation_literal: दिवसे दिवसे (day after day) / तत्र (there) / संस्तरे (in the sacrificial spread or arrangement) / कुशला (skilled) / द्विजा: (the twice-born / brahmins) / सर्वकर्माणि (all rites) / चक्रु: (they performed) / ते (they) / यथाशास्त्रं (according to scripture) / प्रचोदिता: (urged on)
ramayan::423.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::423.essence: Sacred work holds only when every detail is done in order.
ramayan::423.simple_meaning: The priests kept performing every ritual correctly each day, following the sacred rules under Vasishta's guidance.
ramayan::423.simple_insight: Order matters when a sacred task depends on exactness.
ramayan::423.detailed_meaning: At King Janaka's great sacrifice, the ritual pavilion is full of learned priests and polished ceremony. Day after day, Vasishta directs the brahmins, and they carry out each rite exactly as prescribed. The verse adds texture to the scene, not a new teaching.
ramayan::423.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where a wedding, memorial, or major ceremony is being handled with quiet precision. Everyone knows their role, and the whole event depends on that invisible discipline.
ramayan::423.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to exact conduct and steady coordination.

ramayan::424.verse_sanskrit: नाषडङ्गविदत्रासीन्नाव्रतो नाबहुश्रुत: । सदस्यास्तस्य वै राज्ञो नावादकुशला द्विजा: । । 11419 । ।
ramayan::424.verse_hindi: Here (in this sacrificial pavillion), there was none who was not versed in six Vedangas,
ramayan::424.english_translation: In that king's sacrificial hall, there was no one who was not versed in the six Vedangas, who was without vows, who was not widely learned, or who was not skilled in debate.
ramayan::424.translation_literal: न (not) / अषडङ्गविद् (not versed in the six Vedangas) / अत्रासीत् (there was here) / न (not) / अव्रतः (without vows) / न (not) / बहुश्रुतः (widely learned) / सदस्याः (assembly members) / तस्य (of that) / वै (indeed) / राज्ञः (king's) / न (not) / वादकुशलाः (skilled in debate) / द्विजाः (twice-born)
ramayan::424.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::424.essence: The ritual's strength comes from the discipline of those who perform it.
ramayan::424.simple_meaning: Everyone in the king's sacrificial assembly was highly educated, disciplined, and skilled in debate.
ramayan::424.simple_insight: True ceremonies need more than ritual—they need people who are trained, disciplined, and thoughtful.
ramayan::424.detailed_meaning: The sacrifice is underway, and the hall is full of learned priests and scholars. Valmiki pauses to show the caliber of the assembly: these are not ordinary men, but disciplined experts whose presence gives the ritual its authority.
ramayan::424.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where every person seems sharper, calmer, and better prepared than you. That uneasy respect comes from seeing what real training looks like.
ramayan::424.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the quality of character and learning supporting it.

ramayan::425.verse_sanskrit: प्राप्ते यूपोच्छ्रये तस्मिन्षड्बैल्वा: खादिरास्तथा । तावन्तो बिल्वसहिता: पर्णिनश्च तथापरे । । 11420 । । श्लेष्मातकमयस्त्वेको देवदारुमयस्तथा । द्वावेव विहितौ तत्र बाहुव्यस्तपरिग्रहौ । । 11421 । ।
ramayan::425.verse_hindi: When the time came to erect sacrificial posts, six posts, each made of bilva, khadira, parni, sleshmataka and two of devadaru wood, with a distance of two outstretched hands between them were erected.
ramayan::425.english_translation: When the time came to erect the sacrificial posts, six posts of bilva, khadira, parni, sleshmataka, and devadaru wood were set up, with a space of two outstretched hands between them.
ramayan::425.translation_literal: प्राप्ते (when arrived) / यूपोच्छ्रये (for the raising of sacrificial posts) / तस्मिन् (in that) / षड्बैल्वाः (six made of bilva) / खादिराः (khadira) / तथा (and also) / तावन्तः (equal in number) / बिल्वसहिताḥ (with bilva included) / पर्णिनः (made of parni) / च (and) / तथापरे (others likewise) / श्लेष्मातकमयः (made of sleshmataka) / तु (indeed) / एकः (one) / देवदारुमयः (made of devadaru) / तथा (likewise) / द्वौ (two) / एव (only) / विहितौ (were prescribed) / तत्र (there) / बाहुव्यस्तपरिग्रहौ (with a measure of two outstretched arms)
ramayan::425.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::425.essence: Sacred work begins with exact placement, not grand emotion.
ramayan::425.simple_meaning: The sacrifice was being prepared in exact ritual detail, with specific wooden posts measured and placed according to rule.
ramayan::425.simple_insight: Some moments are built by precision, not inspiration.
ramayan::425.detailed_meaning: The scene is a royal sacrifice under careful supervision. Skilled priests are arranging every detail by rule, and this verse lists the exact posts and measurements. It is part of the larger ritual setup, not a teaching by itself.
ramayan::425.modern_relevance: You are setting up chairs before a wedding, checking every row against the plan. No one praises the spacing, but the whole ceremony depends on that unseen precision.
ramayan::425.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to exact preparation.

ramayan::426.verse_sanskrit: कारितास्सर्व एवैते शास्त्रज्ञैर्यज्ञकोविदै: । शोभार्थं तस्य यज्ञस्य काञ्चनालङ्कृताऽभवन् । । 11422 । ।
ramayan::426.verse_hindi: All these posts were prepared by knowers of sastras and by those wellversed in the performance of sacrifices. They were decorated with gold to add elegance to the sacrifice.
ramayan::426.english_translation: All these posts were prepared by knowers of the scriptures and those well-versed in sacrifice. They were decorated with gold to add beauty to the sacrifice.
ramayan::426.translation_literal: कारिताः (were made) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / एते (these) / शास्त्र-ज्ञैः (by knowers of scripture) / यज्ञ-कोविदैः (by those skilled in sacrifice) / शोभा-अर्थम् (for the sake of beauty) / तस्य (of that) / यज्ञस्य (sacrifice) / काञ्चन-अलङ्कृता (adorned with gold) / अभवन् (became)
ramayan::426.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::426.essence: Ritual gains force when skill and beauty meet.
ramayan::426.simple_meaning: The sacrificial posts were expertly made and then covered with gold so the ritual would look splendid.
ramayan::426.simple_insight: Care and beauty can be part of reverence, not just function.
ramayan::426.detailed_meaning: In King Janaka's sacrifice, the ritual space is being prepared with exacting care. Skilled experts shape the sacrificial posts and then gild them, showing that this ceremony is meant to be both precise and magnificent.
ramayan::426.modern_relevance: You set the table before guests arrive and notice the small cloth, the clean edges, the candle. You are not being fussy — you are making space worthy of what matters.
ramayan::426.insight: It shifts attention from bare utility to the dignity of careful preparation.

ramayan::427.verse_hindi: These twentyone sacrificial posts, each measuring twentyone aratni height, were welldecorated wrapped in a piece of cloth.
ramayan::427.english_translation: These twenty-one sacrificial posts, each measuring twenty-one aratni in height, were well-decorated and wrapped in cloth.
ramayan::427.translation_literal: एकविंशतियूपाः (twenty-one sacrificial posts) / ते (they) / एकविंशत्यरत्नयः (twenty-one aratni high) / वासोभिः (with cloths) / एकैकम् (each one) / समलङ्कृताः (well-decorated)
ramayan::427.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::427.essence: Ritual grandeur begins with measured, disciplined detail.
ramayan::427.simple_meaning: The sacrificial posts were built in a precise number, set to a fixed height, and decorated with cloth.
ramayan::427.simple_insight: Even ritual has order, proportion, and care in every detail.
ramayan::427.detailed_meaning: The sacrifice is being prepared with exact ritual precision. After the materials and craftsmen are named, this verse adds the final measurements and decoration of the posts. It is a supporting detail in the larger scene of a grand yajna.
ramayan::427.modern_relevance: You notice the difference between a rushed setup and one done with care: every pole measured, every cloth tied neatly, every detail aligned before the event begins.
ramayan::427.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to exact preparation.

ramayan::428.verse_sanskrit: विन्यस्ता विधिवत्सर्वे शिल्पिभिस्सुकृता दृढा: । अष्टाश्रयस्सर्व एव श्लक्ष्णरूपसमन्विता: । । 11424 । ।
ramayan::428.verse_hindi: All those posts, strong with eight sides and finely finished surfaces, wellcarved  by sculptors were duly erected.
ramayan::428.english_translation: All those posts, strong with eight sides and finely finished surfaces, were duly erected by skilled craftsmen.
ramayan::428.translation_literal: विन्यस्ता (erected) / विधिवत् (according to rule) / सर्वे (all) / शिल्पिभिः (by craftsmen) / सुकृता (well-made) / दृढाः (strong) / अष्टाश्रयः (eight-sided) / ते (those) / सर्वे (all) / श्लक्ष्णरूपसमन्विताः (endowed with smooth form)
ramayan::428.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::428.essence: Sacred grandeur depends on exact, unseen craftsmanship.
ramayan::428.simple_meaning: The sacrificial posts were carefully built, shaped with skill, and set up in the proper way.
ramayan::428.simple_insight: Even sacred work begins with careful preparation and exact craft.
ramayan::428.detailed_meaning: The great sacrifice is being prepared piece by piece. Skilled craftsmen have already made the posts strong, smooth, and properly shaped, and now they are being erected in exact order. The verse is part of a larger scene of ceremonial setup, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::428.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, a stage show, or a public event, someone quietly checks every stand, rope, and light. The beauty people notice later depends on this unseen precision.
ramayan::428.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the disciplined work that makes ritual possible.

ramayan::429.verse_sanskrit: आच्छादितास्ते वासोभि: पुष्पैर्गन्धैश्च भूषिता: । सप्तर्षयो दीप्तिमन्तो विराजन्ते यथा दिवि । । 11425 । ।
ramayan::429.verse_hindi: Decorated with flowers and sandal paste and covered with cloths, stood the  bright sacrificial posts shining like seven sages in the sky.
ramayan::429.english_translation: Decorated with flowers and sandal paste and covered with cloths, stood the bright sacrificial posts shining like seven sages in the sky.
ramayan::429.translation_literal: आच्छादिताः (covered) / ते (those) / वासोभिः (with cloths) / पुष्पैः (with flowers) / गन्धैः (with fragrances) / च (and) / भूषिताः (decorated) / सप्तर्षयः (the seven sages) / दीप्तिमन्तः (shining) / विराजन्ते (shine) / यथा (as) / दिवि (in the sky)
ramayan::429.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::429.essence: Beauty and precision prepare the ground for ritual.
ramayan::429.simple_meaning: The sacrificial posts were beautifully decorated and looked radiant, like the seven sages in the sky.
ramayan::429.simple_insight: Even ritual objects are treated with care, beauty, and reverence here.
ramayan::429.detailed_meaning: This is part of a detailed description of a grand sacrifice. The builders have already set up the posts, and now the poet lingers on their beauty before moving on to the fire altar. It is scene-setting, not a teaching.
ramayan::429.modern_relevance: A hall is being prepared for a major ceremony, and every detail matters — the cloth, the flowers, the finish. The verse simply lets you see the care before the ritual begins.
ramayan::429.insight: It trains attention on preparation and sacred order, not just the event itself.

ramayan::430.verse_sanskrit: इष्टकाश्च यथान्यायं कारिताश्च प्रमाणत: । चितोऽग्निर्ब्राह्मणैस्तत्र कुशलैश्शुल्बकर्मणि । । 11426 । ।
ramayan::430.verse_hindi: The sacrificial fireplace was constructed with bricks with standard measurement by brahmins who were experts in the art of measuring land with a string or single strand.
ramayan::430.english_translation: The sacrificial fireplace was built with bricks of proper measure by brahmins skilled in altar geometry.
ramayan::430.translation_literal: इष्टकाश्च (bricks) / यथान्यायं (according to proper rule) / कारिताश्च (were made) / प्रमाणत: (by measure) / चितोऽग्निः (the fire-altar) / ब्राह्मणैः (by brahmins) / तत्र (there) / कुशलैः (skilled) / शुल्बकर्मणि (in altar-geometry)
ramayan::430.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::430.essence: Sacred acts begin with exact, disciplined construction.
ramayan::430.simple_meaning: The altar for the fire ritual was carefully built to exact measurements by skilled brahmins.
ramayan::430.simple_insight: Great rites depend on precision, not improvisation.
ramayan::430.detailed_meaning: At Dasharatha’s great sacrifice, the altar is being assembled piece by piece. Skilled brahmins lay the bricks to exact measure, following the rules of altar construction. The verse is a technical detail in the larger ritual scene.
ramayan::430.modern_relevance: Before a major ceremony, someone is on the floor checking measurements, rechecking alignment, and correcting a single misplaced brick. The sacred work begins with exactness.
ramayan::430.insight: It shifts attention from grandeur to careful preparation.

ramayan::431.verse_sanskrit: सचित्यो राजसिंहस्य सञ्चित: कुशलैर्द्विजै: । गरुडो रुक्मपक्षो वै त्रिगुणोऽष्टादशात्मक: । । 11427 । ।
ramayan::431.verse_hindi: That sacrificial altar of the lion among kings, (Dasaratha), erected by welltrained brahmins was in the shape of the golden winged Garuda it had three ranges and thrice as many fireplaces i.e eighteen in number.
ramayan::431.english_translation: That sacrificial altar of the lion among kings, Dasaratha, was built by skilled brahmins in the shape of Garuda, with golden wings, three tiers, and eighteen fireplaces.
ramayan::431.translation_literal: सचित्यः (having an altar built) / राजसिंहस्य (of the lion among kings) / सञ्चितः (constructed) / कुशलैः (by skilled) / द्विजैः (brahmins) / गरुडः (Garuda) / रुक्मपक्षः (golden-winged) / वै (indeed) / त्रिगुणः (threefold) / अष्टादशात्मकः (consisting of eighteen parts)
ramayan::431.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::431.essence: Sacred action here depends on exact form, not improvisation.
ramayan::431.simple_meaning: The altar for Dasaratha's sacrifice was carefully built by expert priests in the form of Garuda, with three levels and eighteen fire pits.
ramayan::431.simple_insight: Great rituals were built with exactness, not improvisation.
ramayan::431.detailed_meaning: The scene is still in the preparations for Dasaratha's great sacrifice. Expert brahmins have already shaped the altar with precise ritual design, making it resemble Garuda with three tiers and eighteen fires. It is a technical detail in a larger ceremonial sequence.
ramayan::431.modern_relevance: Before a major ceremony, people spend hours measuring, arranging, and checking every detail no one else will notice. This verse lingers on that unseen precision.
ramayan::431.insight: It highlights the exact ritual order required before the sacrifice can proceed.

ramayan::432.verse_sanskrit: नियुक्तास्तत्र पशवस्तत्तदुद्दिश्य दैवतम् । उरगा: पक्षिणश्चैव यथाशास्त्रं प्रचोदिता: । । 11428 । ।
ramayan::432.verse_hindi: Animals, serpents and birds were kept ready after the sastras intended (for sacrifice) for those respective deities.
ramayan::432.english_translation: Animals, serpents, and birds were kept ready, each assigned according to the prescribed rite for its deity.
ramayan::432.translation_literal: नियुक्ताः (assigned) / तत्र (there) / पशवः (animals) / तत्-तत् (each respective) / उद्दिश्य (for the purpose of) / दैवतम् (deity) / उरगाः (serpents) / पक्षिणः (birds) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / यथाशास्त्रम् (according to scripture) / प्रचोदिताः (directed, arranged)
ramayan::432.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::432.essence: Ritual begins with exact preparation, not improvisation.
ramayan::432.simple_meaning: The sacrificial animals were arranged in advance, each set aside according to ritual rules for the proper offering.
ramayan::432.simple_insight: It shows how carefully the rite was prepared, with nothing left to chance.
ramayan::432.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha’s great sacrifice is being prepared in exact ritual order. After the altar is built, priests arrange the animals, serpents, and birds according to scripture. The verse is a supporting detail in the larger description of the ceremony.
ramayan::432.modern_relevance: Before a major ceremony, every item is laid out in its place: the lamps, the offerings, the vessels, the timing. The verse captures that exactness — a rite only works when preparation is meticulous.
ramayan::432.insight: It shifts attention from drama to precision, showing that sacred action depends on disciplined arrangement.

ramayan::433.verse_sanskrit: शामित्रे तु हयस्तत्र तथा जलचराश्च ये । ऋत्विग्भिस्सर्वमेवैतन्नियुक्तं शास्त्रतस्तदा । । 11429 । ।
ramayan::433.verse_hindi: When the time came to sacrifice the animals, the chief priests, in accordance with tradition, tied up the horse and all the aquatic animals to the sacrificial posts.
ramayan::433.english_translation: When the time came to sacrifice the animals, the chief priests, in accordance with tradition, tied up the horse and all the aquatic animals to the sacrificial posts.
ramayan::433.translation_literal: शामित्रे (at the time of sacrifice) / तु (indeed) / हयः (the horse) / तत्र (there) / तथा (also) / जलचराः (aquatic creatures) / च (and) / ये (those which) / ऋत्विग्भिः (by the priests) / सर्वम् एव (all indeed) / एतत् (this) / नियुक्तम् (was arranged) / शास्त्रतः (according to the scriptures) / तदा (then)
ramayan::433.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::433.essence: The sacrifice begins with strict ritual order, not emotion.
ramayan::433.simple_meaning: The priests prepared the sacrificial animals exactly as tradition required.
ramayan::433.simple_insight: Some moments are not about choice, only about precise preparation.
ramayan::433.detailed_meaning: At Dasharatha’s great sacrifice, the priests move through each prescribed step with exactness. The horse and other animals are bound according to ritual rule, showing a ceremony being carried out before the decisive offering begins.
ramayan::433.modern_relevance: Before a major ceremony, people are still checking ropes, placements, and timing while the room holds its breath. The significance is coming, but first everything must be arranged exactly.
ramayan::433.insight: It shifts attention from drama to ritual precision, showing how sacred acts depend on exact preparation.

ramayan::434.verse_sanskrit: पशूनां त्रिशतं तत्र यूपेषु नियतं तदा । अश्वरत्नोत्तमं तस्य राज्ञो दशरथस्य च । । 11430 । ।
ramayan::434.verse_hindi: Three hundred animals and the jewel of the horses (from the stables) belonging to king Dasaratha were bound to the sacrificial posts.
ramayan::434.english_translation: Three hundred animals and the finest horse from King Dasharatha's stable were bound to the sacrificial posts.
ramayan::434.translation_literal: पशूनाम् (of animals) / त्रिशतम् (three hundred) / तत्र (there) / यूपेषु (to the sacrificial posts) / नियतम् (bound) / तदा (then) / अश्वरत्नोत्तमम् (the finest horse) / तस्य (of that) / राज्ञः (of the king) / दशरथस्य (of Dasharatha) / च (and)
ramayan::434.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::434.essence: The ceremony has crossed from preparation into commitment.
ramayan::434.simple_meaning: Three hundred animals, along with Dasharatha's best horse, were tied to the sacrificial posts for the ritual.
ramayan::434.simple_insight: The ritual is becoming real, step by step, with no turning back.
ramayan::434.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is underway in Dasharatha's court. Priests have already prepared the animals and now bind the king's finest horse to the posts. The verse is a ritual detail, showing the ceremony advancing toward its decisive act.
ramayan::434.modern_relevance: A plan has moved from discussion to execution. The materials are laid out, the room is set, and the moment of commitment is no longer abstract.
ramayan::434.insight: It shifts attention from intention to irreversible action.

ramayan::435.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या तं हयं तत्र परिचर्य समन्तत: । कृपाणैर्विशशासैनं त्रिभि: परमया मुदा । । 11431 । ।
ramayan::435.verse_hindi: Kausalya, with immense glee having gone round and worshipped that horse, severed it with three strokes of scimitar.
ramayan::435.english_translation: Kausalya, with immense glee having gone round and worshipped that horse, severed it with three strokes of scimitar.
ramayan::435.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kausalya) / तं (that) / हयं (horse) / तत्र (there) / परिचर्य (having worshipped) / समन्तत: (all around) / कृपाणैः (with scimitars) / विशशास (severed) / एनं (him/it) / त्रिभिः (with three) / परमया (with utmost) / मुदा (joy)
ramayan::435.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::435.essence: Ritual duty can demand joyful participation in something severe.
ramayan::435.simple_meaning: Kausalya performed the ritual step of circling, honoring, and cutting the sacrificial horse as part of the ceremony.
ramayan::435.simple_insight: Some acts carry sacred weight because they belong to a larger vow, not because they feel easy.
ramayan::435.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is underway for Dasharatha. Priests have already prepared the animals and the king’s finest horse. Kausalya, acting within the ritual order, performs the solemn killing of the horse, showing how the ceremony demands even the queen’s direct participation.
ramayan::435.modern_relevance: You may have to do something formal, exacting, and emotionally hard because a larger commitment depends on it.
ramayan::435.insight: It shows that duty in ritual can require personal participation in an act that would otherwise feel unbearable.

ramayan::436.verse_sanskrit: पतत्रिणा तदा सार्धं सुस्थितेन च चेतसा । अवसद्रजनीमेकां कौशल्या धर्मकाम्यया । । 11432 । ।
ramayan::436.verse_hindi: Kausalya, in her devotion to duty and with a happy state of mind, passed one night near that horse.
ramayan::436.english_translation: Kausalya, in her devotion to duty and with a happy state of mind, passed one night near that horse.
ramayan::436.translation_literal: पतत्रिणा (with the horse) / तदा (then) / सार्धं (together with) / सुस्थितेन (well-placed, settled) / च (and) / चेतसा (with mind) / अवसत् (spent the night) / रजनीम् (night) / एकाम् (one) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / धर्मकाम्यया (with desire for duty)
ramayan::436.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::436.essence: She stayed through the ritual night with a steady mind.
ramayan::436.simple_meaning: Kausalya spent one night beside the sacrificial horse, doing so willingly and with a settled mind.
ramayan::436.simple_insight: Some acts of devotion are quiet, exact, and costly.
ramayan::436.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is underway in Ayodhya. After the horse is ritually prepared, Kausalya spends the night beside it as part of the ceremony. This is a supporting ritual detail, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::436.modern_relevance: You sit through a long, uncomfortable ritual because it matters to someone you love. No one applauds the patience, but the commitment is real.
ramayan::436.insight: It shows how discipline can be expressed through calm, willing participation in a demanding rite.

ramayan::437.verse_sanskrit: होताऽध्वर्युस्तथोद्गाता हस्तेन समयोजयन् । महिष्या परिवृत्त्या च वावातां च तथापराम् । । 11433 । ।
ramayan::437.verse_hindi: Hota, Adhvaryu and Udgata arranged Mahishi, Parivritti, Vavaata and another woman known as Palakali to touch (keep the company of) the sacrificial horse.
ramayan::437.english_translation: The Hota, Adhvaryu, and Udgata arranged for Mahishi, Parivritti, Vavaata, and another woman to attend the sacrificial horse.
ramayan::437.translation_literal: होताऽध्वर्युस्तथोद्गाता (the Hota, Adhvaryu, and Udgata) / हस्तेन (by hand) / समयोजयन् (arranged, joined) / महिष्या (with Mahishi) / परिवृत्त्या (with Parivritti) / च (and) / वावातां (Vavaata) / च (and) / तथापराम् (and another one)
ramayan::437.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::437.essence: The ritual advances through exact placement, not improvisation.
ramayan::437.simple_meaning: The priests assigned specific women to attend the sacrificial horse as part of the ritual.
ramayan::437.simple_insight: Large rituals run on exact roles, not vague intention.
ramayan::437.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is underway, and every action is being carried out by rule. The priests assign particular women to remain with the horse, showing the ceremony's strict order before the next ritual act begins.
ramayan::437.modern_relevance: At a wedding, a courtroom, or a hospital handoff, people move according to exact roles. No one improvises much when the stakes are formal and the sequence matters.
ramayan::437.insight: It shows how sacred or formal work depends on precise coordination and assigned responsibility.

ramayan::438.verse_sanskrit: पतत्रिणस्तस्य वपा मुद्धृत्य नियतेन्द्रिय: । ऋत्विक्परमसम्पन्न: श्रपयामास शास्त्रत: । । 11434 । ।
ramayan::438.verse_hindi: The official priest, highly knowledgeable in scriptures and having restrained senses, removed the marrow from the horse and cooked it according to tradition.
ramayan::438.english_translation: The official priest, highly knowledgeable in scriptures and having restrained senses, removed the marrow from the horse and cooked it according to tradition.
ramayan::438.translation_literal: पतत्रिणः (of the horse) / तस्य (of that) / वपा (marrow/fat) / मुद्धृत्य (having removed) / नियतेन्द्रियः (one with restrained senses) / ऋत्विक् (the priest) / परमसम्पन्नः (highly accomplished) / श्रपयामास (cooked) / शास्त्रतः (according to scripture)
ramayan::438.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::438.essence: Exact ritual work depends on disciplined control.
ramayan::438.simple_meaning: A priest carefully prepared the horse sacrifice exactly as the ritual texts required.
ramayan::438.simple_insight: Precision matters when a rite is meant to be done without error.
ramayan::438.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is underway. After Kausalya’s vigil and the ritual preparations, the priest handles the horse’s marrow with complete restraint and scriptural precision. This is a procedural step, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::438.modern_relevance: A chef follows a complex recipe under pressure, measuring every step because one mistake ruins the whole dish.
ramayan::438.insight: It shows disciplined ritual execution, where correctness comes from restraint and knowledge, not improvisation.

ramayan::439.verse_sanskrit: धूमगन्धं वपायास्तु जिघ्रति स्म नराधिप: । यथाकालं यथान्यायं निर्णुदन्पापमात्मन: । । 11435 । ।
ramayan::439.verse_hindi: The king at appropriate time and in agreement with the scriptures inhaled the odour of the smoke (from the burnt marrow) and absolved himself of his sins.
ramayan::439.english_translation: The king, at the proper time and according to the scriptures, inhaled the smoke of the burnt marrow and freed himself from sin.
ramayan::439.translation_literal: धूमगन्धम् (the smell of smoke) / वपायाः (of the marrow) / तु (indeed) / जिघ्रति स्म (inhaled) / नराधिपः (the king) / यथाकालम् (at the proper time) / यथान्यायम् (according to rule) / निर्णुदन् (removing) / पापम् (sin) / आत्मनः (of himself)
ramayan::439.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::439.essence: Ritual works only when every step is done exactly right.
ramayan::439.simple_meaning: The king followed the ritual exactly, inhaling the prescribed smoke at the proper time to cleanse himself.
ramayan::439.simple_insight: Order and timing matter when a rite is meant to complete its effect.
ramayan::439.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is underway, with priests handling each step by the book. In this verse, the king performs the final prescribed act at the right moment, showing that the ritual’s power lies in exact observance, not improvisation.
ramayan::439.modern_relevance: You can’t rush a ceremony, a contract, or a hard conversation and expect it to work. Some acts only land when done in the right order, at the right moment.
ramayan::439.insight: It shifts attention from intention alone to exact procedure and timing.

ramayan::440.verse_sanskrit: हयस्य यानि चाङ्गानि तानि सर्वाणि ब्राह्मणा: । अग्नौ प्रास्यन्ति विधिवत्समन्त्राष्षोडशर्त्विज: । । 11436 । ।
ramayan::440.verse_hindi: The sixteen officiating priests (brahmins) offered all the horses limbs with prayers as per the customs.
ramayan::440.english_translation: The sixteen officiating priests offered all the horse's limbs into the fire with prayers, according to the prescribed rite.
ramayan::440.translation_literal: हयस्य (of the horse) / यानि (which) / च (and) / अङ्गानि (limbs) / तानि (those) / सर्वाणि (all) / ब्राह्मणा: (the brahmins) / अग्नौ (into the fire) / प्रास्यन्ति (throw/offer) / विधिवत् (according to rule) / समन्त्राः (with mantras) / षोडश-ऋत्विजः (the sixteen officiating priests)
ramayan::440.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::440.essence: The sacrifice depends on exact procedure, not intention alone.
ramayan::440.simple_meaning: The priests placed every part of the horse into the fire exactly as the ritual required.
ramayan::440.simple_insight: Sacred work is done by precision, not improvisation.
ramayan::440.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice is being performed step by step. Priests handle each part of the horse according to strict ritual order, with mantras and exact roles. The verse simply records the procedure, not a teaching or turning point.
ramayan::440.modern_relevance: A ceremony, audit, or legal filing can fail because one small step is skipped. This verse lives in that exact seriousness: doing each required part in the right order matters.
ramayan::440.insight: It shifts attention from drama to exact ritual procedure.

ramayan::441.verse_sanskrit: प्लक्षशाखासु यज्ञानामन्येषां क्रियते हवि: । अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य वैतसो भाग इष्यते । । 11437 । ।
ramayan::441.verse_hindi: In other sacrifices oblations are offered with branches of a plaksha tree but in Aswamedha a branch of cane creeper is chosen instead.
ramayan::441.english_translation: In other sacrifices, offerings are made with plaksha branches, but in the Ashvamedha sacrifice, a cane creeper branch is chosen instead.
ramayan::441.translation_literal: प्लक्षशाखासु (in plaksha branches) / यज्ञानाम् (of sacrifices) / अन्येषाम् (of others) / क्रियते (is made) / हविः (offering) / अश्वमेधस्य (of the Ashvamedha) / यज्ञस्य (sacrifice) / वैतसः (cane-creeper) / भागः (portion) / इष्यते (is desired)
ramayan::441.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::441.essence: The same sacred act can demand a different form.
ramayan::441.simple_meaning: Different sacrifices use different ritual materials. Here, the Ashvamedha has its own prescribed branch, unlike other rites.
ramayan::441.simple_insight: Even sacred work has exact forms. Care is part of the offering.
ramayan::441.detailed_meaning: The priests are deep into the horse sacrifice, following exact ritual rules for every detail. After the horse's parts are handled, the text shifts to another fixed instruction: this sacrifice does not use the same branch as other rites. It is a technical ritual note, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::441.modern_relevance: A chef following a family recipe measures the spice differently for one dish than for another. Precision matters because the whole act changes when the method changes.
ramayan::441.insight: It highlights that ritual is not generic; each act has its own exact procedure.

ramayan::442.verse_hindi: According to Kalpa sutra, aswamedha in conducted for three days. In the first day, chatushtoma is arranged.
ramayan::442.english_translation: According to the Kalpa Sutras, the Ashvamedha is conducted over three days. On the first day, the Chatushtoma rite is arranged.
ramayan::442.translation_literal: त्र्यहोऽश्वमेधः (the three-day Ashvamedha) / सङ्ख्यातः (is counted) / कल्पसूत्रेण (according to the Kalpa Sutra) / ब्राह्मणैः (by the brahmins) / चतुष्टोममहः (the Chatushtoma day) / तस्य (of that) / प्रथमम् (first) / परिकल्पितम् (arranged)
ramayan::442.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::442.essence: The rite begins with strict ordering, not improvisation.
ramayan::442.simple_meaning: The horse sacrifice is described as a three-day ritual, and the first day is set aside for the Chatushtoma ceremony.
ramayan::442.simple_insight: Some moments are about procedure, not meaning. Precision itself can be part of reverence.
ramayan::442.detailed_meaning: The Ashvamedha ceremony is being laid out step by step, with priests following the ritual manual. This verse does not teach a principle; it simply fixes the first day's rite before the account moves on to the next day.
ramayan::442.modern_relevance: You are reading the event plan before the ceremony begins: timings, sequence, and roles. Some moments in life are like that too — the work is to prepare correctly, not to interpret everything.
ramayan::442.insight: It keeps attention on ritual sequence and exact order rather than symbolic interpretation.

ramayan::443.verse_sanskrit: उक्थ्यं द्वितीयं संख्यातमतिरात्रं तथोत्तरम् । कारितास्तत्र बहवो विहिताश्शास्त्रदर्शनात् । । 11439 । ।
ramayan::443.verse_hindi: On the second day Ukthya and on the third day Atiraatra were performed. Many sacrifices fixed according to the scriptures were also performed.
ramayan::443.english_translation: On the second day Ukthya and on the third day Atiraatra were performed. Many sacrifices fixed according to the scriptures were also performed.
ramayan::443.translation_literal: उक्थ्यम् (Ukthya) / द्वितीयम् (second) / संख्यातम् (counted) / अतिरात्रम् (Atiraatra) / तथ (and) / उत्तरम् (later, third) / कारिताः (were performed) / तत्र (there) / बहवः (many) / विहिताः (prescribed) / शास्त्र-दर्शनात् (according to scriptural injunctions)
ramayan::443.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::443.essence: Ritual power here comes from exact order, not enthusiasm.
ramayan::443.simple_meaning: The second and third days of the Ashvamedha are being listed, along with the rites required by scripture.
ramayan::443.simple_insight: Great ceremonies are built from exact steps, not vague intention.
ramayan::443.detailed_meaning: The discussion is still on the Ashvamedha’s structure. After naming the first day, the text now lists the second and third-day rites and the many prescribed ceremonies, showing the sacrifice as a tightly regulated sequence rather than a single act.
ramayan::443.modern_relevance: A wedding, audit, or legal filing can fail because one required step was skipped. This verse points to the discipline of doing a complex task in the right order, not just with good intentions.
ramayan::443.insight: It shifts attention from grand plans to precise execution.

ramayan::444.verse_hindi: Jyotishtoma and Ayuryaga in Atiratra, Abhijit, Viswajit and Aptoryama ceremonies constituting the great sacrifice were performed in the prescribed manner.
ramayan::444.english_translation: Jyotishtoma and Ayuryaga in Atiratra, Abhijit, Viswajit, and Aptoryama ceremonies constituting the great sacrifice were performed in the prescribed manner.
ramayan::444.translation_literal: ज्योतिष्टोमायुषी (Jyotishtoma and Ayuryaga) / च (and) / एवम् (thus) / अतिरात्रौ (in Atiratra) / विनिर्मितौ (were arranged) / अभिजित् (Abhijit) / विश्वजित् (Viswajit) / च (and) / एवम् (thus) / अप्तोर्यामः (Aptoryama) / महाक्रतुḥ (great sacrifice)
ramayan::444.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::444.essence: Great acts are built from exact, unseen preparation.
ramayan::444.simple_meaning: The great sacrifice included several specific ritual days and forms, all arranged according to tradition.
ramayan::444.simple_insight: Some moments matter because they are carefully prepared, not because they are dramatic.
ramayan::444.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the formal structure of Dasharatha's sacrifice. The verse adds more ritual detail after the earlier days are named, showing the scale and exactness of the ceremony before the story turns to the gifts given to the priests.
ramayan::444.modern_relevance: A long event looks effortless only because someone has already planned every part of it. The visible moment rests on a hidden structure of careful preparation.
ramayan::444.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the discipline that makes the spectacle possible.

ramayan::445.verse_sanskrit: प्राचीं होत्रे ददौ राजा दिशं स्वकुलवर्धन: । अध्वर्यवे प्रतीचीं तु ब्रह्मणे दक्षिणां दिशम् । । 11441 । । उद्गात्रे च तथोदीचीं दक्षिणैषा विनिर्मिता । हयमेधे महायज्ञे स्वयंभूविहिते पुरा । । 11442 । ।
ramayan::445.verse_hindi: In order to promote his dynasty, king Dasaratha gave away eastern region to Hotar, western region to Adhvaryu, southern region to Brahma and northern region to Udgata. These offerings were made in accordance with theprescriptions by Brahma long all.
ramayan::445.english_translation: For the growth of his line, King Dasharatha gave the eastern quarter to the Hotar, the western to the Adhvaryu, the southern to Brahma, and the northern to the Udgata. These gifts were made according to the ancient ordinance for the horse sacrifice.
ramayan::445.translation_literal: प्राचीं (eastern) / होत्रे (to the Hotar priest) / ददौ (gave) / राजा (the king) / दिशं (direction, quarter) / स्वकुलवर्धनः (one who increases his own line) / अध्वर्यवे (to the Adhvaryu priest) / प्रतीचीं (western) / तु (and) / ब्रह्मणे (to Brahma) / दक्षिणां (southern) / दिशम् (direction, quarter) / उद्गात्रे (to the Udgata priest) / च (and) / तथा (thus) / उदीचीं (northern) / दक्षिणा (gift) / एषा (this) / विनिर्मिता (arranged, made) / हयमेधे (in the horse sacrifice) / महायज्ञे (in the great sacrifice) / स्वयंभूविहिते (ordained by the self-existent one) / पुरा (formerly, long ago)
ramayan::445.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::445.essence: Sacred acts here depend on precise, prescribed giving.
ramayan::445.simple_meaning: Dasharatha assigns the four directions to the priests as ritual gifts during the horse sacrifice, following ancient rules.
ramayan::445.simple_insight: Some gifts are not generosity alone; they are part of keeping a sacred order intact.
ramayan::445.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha is in the middle of the horse sacrifice, and every part of the rite must be done exactly right. He assigns the quarters of space to the priests as prescribed, showing royal discipline and ritual precision rather than a separate teaching.
ramayan::445.modern_relevance: A ceremony is underway, and every detail has to be correct before anyone can relax. This verse is one more measured step in that larger ritual sequence, not the main lesson itself.
ramayan::445.insight: It shows ritual action as exact, ordered, and publicly accountable.

ramayan::446.verse_sanskrit: क्रतुं समाप्य तु तदा न्यायत: पुरुषर्षभ: । ऋत्विग्भ्यो हि ददौ राजा तां धरां कुलवर्धन: । । 11443 । ।
ramayan::446.verse_hindi: The king best among men and upholder of his dynasty, having concluded the sacrifice according to law, offered this entire earth as gift to priests.
ramayan::446.english_translation: The king, best among men and upholder of his dynasty, having concluded the sacrifice according to law, gave the whole earth as a gift to the priests.
ramayan::446.translation_literal: क्रतुम् (sacrifice) / समाप्य (having completed) / तु (indeed) / तदा (then) / न्यायतः (according to law) / पुरुषर्षभः (best among men) / ऋत्विग्भ्यः (to the priests) / हि (indeed) / ददौ (gave) / राजा (the king) / ताम् (that) / धराम् (earth) / कुलवर्धनः (upholder of the dynasty)
ramayan::446.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::446.essence: Completion becomes real when you can let go of what you hold.
ramayan::446.simple_meaning: After completing the sacrifice properly, the king gave the entire earth to the priests as a gift.
ramayan::446.simple_insight: Great acts are sealed by generosity, not possession.
ramayan::446.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has completed a vast sacrifice with every rite in place. When it ends, he gives the earth itself to the priests who served it. The verse shows royal abundance and ritual completion, not a standalone teaching.
ramayan::446.modern_relevance: You finish a demanding project, then quietly credit the people who made it possible. The real measure of success is not what you keep, but what you can give back.
ramayan::446.insight: It shifts attention from accomplishment to the duty of honoring those who enabled it.

ramayan::447.verse_sanskrit: ऋत्विजस्त्वब्रुवन्सर्वे राजानं गतकल्मषम् । भवानेव महीं कृत्स्नामेको रक्षितुमर्हति । । 11444 । ।
ramayan::447.verse_hindi: But all the priests said to the king purged of his sins, O Lord of men you alone are capable of protecting this earth.
ramayan::447.english_translation: But all the priests said to the king, now free from stain: "You alone are fit to protect this entire earth."
ramayan::447.translation_literal: ऋत्विजः (the priests) / तु (but) / अब्रुवन् (said) / सर्वे (all) / राजानम् (to the king) / गतकल्मषम् (purged of stain) / भवानेव (you alone) / महीं (the earth) / कृत्स्नाम् (entire) / एकः (alone) / रक्षितुम् (to protect) / अर्हति (are fit)
ramayan::447.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::447.essence: Real authority is proven by the ability to protect, not by the title.
ramayan::447.simple_meaning: The priests tell Dasaratha that he is the one person capable of protecting the whole earth.
ramayan::447.simple_insight: Responsibility can reveal itself as recognition, not pressure.
ramayan::447.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just completed a great sacrifice and given away vast gifts to the priests. In return, the priests praise his purity and declare that only he can bear the burden of protecting the entire earth. The verse lifts him from ritual king to rightful guardian.
ramayan::447.modern_relevance: After everyone leaves the meeting, the team still looks to you to steady the project. You did not ask for that weight, but your competence made it arrive.
ramayan::447.insight: It shifts leadership from status to proven capacity: the one who can hold the burden must hold it.

ramayan::448.verse_sanskrit: न भूम्या कार्यमस्माकं न हि शक्तास्स्म पालने । रतास्स्वाध्यायकरणे वयं नित्यं हि भूमिप । । 11445 । । निष्क्रयं किञ्चिदेवेह प्रयच्छतु भवानिति । 4
ramayan::448.verse_hindi: O ruler of the earth We are constantly engaged in the study of the Vedas. We are not capable of ruling the earth and we cannot do anything with its possession. Give some other charity in lieu of that.
ramayan::448.english_translation: O ruler of the earth, we are constantly engaged in the study of the Vedas. We are not capable of ruling the earth, and we cannot do anything with its possession. Give some other charity in lieu of that.
ramayan::448.translation_literal: न (not) / भूम्या (with the earth) / कार्यम् (need, business) / अस्माकम् (for us) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / शक्ताः (able) / स्म (are) / पालने (in protection, ruling) / रताः (engaged) / स्वाध्याय-करणे (in doing self-study, Vedic study) / वयम् (we) / नित्यम् (always) / हि (indeed) / भूमिप (O ruler of the earth) / निष्क्रयम् (as payment, compensation) / किञ्चित् (something) / एव (only) / इह (here) / प्रयच्छतु (may you give) / भवान् (you) / इति (thus)
ramayan::448.speaker: The priests
ramayan::448.essence: Real generosity also respects what people are fit to hold.
ramayan::448.simple_meaning: The priests refuse the earth because they are scholars, not rulers. They ask the king to give them some other gift instead.
ramayan::448.simple_insight: Not every valuable thing belongs in your hands. Some responsibilities are a poor fit, and honesty about that is wisdom.
ramayan::448.detailed_meaning: After the sacrifice, the priests are asked to accept the earth as payment. They decline respectfully. Their life is study, not governance, and they ask Dasharatha for another gift that matches their work.
ramayan::448.modern_relevance: A manager offers you a role that looks prestigious but would pull you away from what you do best. Saying no can be an act of clarity, not weakness.
ramayan::448.insight: It teaches you to match gifts and duties to actual capacity, not to prestige.

ramayan::449.verse_sanskrit: मणिरत्नं सुवर्णं वा गावो यद्वा समुद्यतम् । तत्प्रयच्छ नरश्रेष्ठ धरण्या न प्रयोजनम् । । 11446 । ।
ramayan::449.verse_hindi: O best of men give us gems or gold or cows or whichever is readily available. We have no use with this earth.
ramayan::449.english_translation: O best of men, give us gems, gold, cows, or anything readily available. We have no use for this earth.
ramayan::449.translation_literal: मणिरत्नम् (gems) / सुवर्णम् (gold) / वा (or) / गावः (cows) / यत् वा (or whatever) / समुद्यतम् (readily available) / तत् (that) / प्रयच्छ (give) / नरश्रेष्ठ (best of men) / धरण्या (for the earth) / न (not) / प्रयोजनम् (use/purpose)
ramayan::449.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::449.essence: Respect for limits turns refusal into a clean exchange.
ramayan::449.simple_meaning: The priests say they do not need the earth itself. They ask the king to give them practical gifts instead: gems, gold, cows, or anything available.
ramayan::449.simple_insight: Not every request is for power or possession; sometimes dignity is simply asking for what is fitting.
ramayan::449.detailed_meaning: The priests have already told the king they cannot rule or protect the earth. Now they soften that refusal by asking for a modest gift instead. The moment shows their renunciation and the king’s duty to honour them.
ramayan::449.modern_relevance: A team turns down a project you hoped they would take on, then asks only for the tools or support they actually need. The clean response is not disappointment — it is to give what helps and respect the limit.
ramayan::449.insight: It shifts attention from grand claims to what can actually be offered and received without strain.

ramayan::450.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो नरपतिर्ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगै: । । 11447 । । गवां शतसहस्राणि दश तेभ्यो ददौ नृप: । 4 शतकोटीस्सुवर्णस्य रजतस्य चतुर्गुणम् । । 11448 । ।
ramayan::450.verse_hindi: Lord of men, the king having been thus addressed by brahmins who were wellversed in the Vedas, bestowed on them ten hundred thousand cows, a hundred crore of gold coins and four times as much in silver coins.
ramayan::450.english_translation: The king, addressed by brahmins who were well-versed in the Vedas, gave them ten million cows, a hundred crore gold coins, and four times as much silver.
ramayan::450.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus addressed) / नरपतिः (the king) / ब्राह्मणैः (by the brahmins) / वेदपारगैः (well-versed in the Vedas) / गवाम् (of cows) / शतसहस्राणि (hundreds of thousands) / दश (ten) / तेभ्यः (to them) / ददौ (gave) / नृपः (the king) / शतकोटीः (hundred crore) / सुवर्णस्य (of gold) / रजतस्य (of silver) / चतुर्गुणम् (four times as much)
ramayan::450.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::450.essence: A worthy gift is given fully, without hesitation or smallness.
ramayan::450.simple_meaning: After hearing the brahmins’ request, the king gave them vast gifts of cows, gold, and silver.
ramayan::450.simple_insight: Generosity here is measured by readiness, not by hesitation.
ramayan::450.detailed_meaning: The brahmins have asked for gifts instead of land, and the king responds immediately and lavishly. This is a scene of royal giving, not teaching: wealth is being transferred to the priests before the ritual proceeds.
ramayan::450.modern_relevance: A host settles the bill before anyone starts arguing over it. The point is not the amount — it is the ease with which he gives when the moment calls for it.
ramayan::450.insight: It shows prompt, abundant giving without bargaining or delay.

ramayan::451.verse_sanskrit: ऋत्विजश्च ततस्सर्वे प्रददुस्सहिता वसु । ऋश्यशृङ्गाय मुनये वसिष्ठाय च धीमते । । 11449 । ।
ramayan::451.verse_hindi: All the priests collectively offered that wealth to sage Rsyasringa and Vasishta endowed with prudence.
ramayan::451.english_translation: All the priests together offered that wealth to Sage Rshyasringa and to wise Vasishta.
ramayan::451.translation_literal: ऋत्विजः (priests) / च (and) / ततः (then) / सर्वे (all) / प्रददुः (offered) / सहिताः (together) / वसु (wealth) / ऋश्यशृङ्गाय (to Rshyasringa) / मुनये (to the sage) / वसिष्ठाय (to Vasishta) / च (and) / धीमते (to the wise one)
ramayan::451.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::451.essence: Wealth is being distributed, not interpreted.
ramayan::451.simple_meaning: The priests shared the king's wealth with Rshyasringa and Vasishta. It is a distribution of gifts, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::451.simple_insight: Some verses simply move the story forward; not every line carries a lesson.
ramayan::451.detailed_meaning: After receiving enormous gifts from the king, the priests divide the wealth and offer it to Rshyasringa and the wise Vasishta. The scene is part of a larger exchange of honor and generosity, not a philosophical statement.
ramayan::451.modern_relevance: A ceremony ends and people start dividing the gifts, checking names, and making sure each honored person receives their share. The moment matters to the story, but it is still just the handoff.
ramayan::451.insight: It keeps the narrative moving without adding a new moral principle.

ramayan::452.verse_sanskrit: ततस्ते न्यायत: कृत्वा प्रविभागं द्विजोत्तमा: । सुप्रीतमनसस्सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्मुदिता भृशम् । । 11450 । ।
ramayan::452.verse_hindi: Then those highly pleased brahmins, having distributed that wealth with equity, again said to the king.
ramayan::452.english_translation: Then those highly pleased brahmins, having distributed that wealth with equity, again said to the king.
ramayan::452.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / ते (they) / न्यायतः (with fairness) / कृत्वा (having done) / प्रविभागम् (distribution) / द्विजोत्तमाḥ (best of brahmins) / सुप्रीत-मनसः (with very pleased minds) / सर्वे (all) / प्रत्यूचुः (spoke back) / मुदिताḥ (delighted) / भृशम् (greatly)
ramayan::452.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::452.essence: Even received wealth must be divided justly.
ramayan::452.simple_meaning: The priests divided the gift fairly, felt satisfied, and then spoke again to the king.
ramayan::452.simple_insight: Fairness in sharing keeps gratitude clean and prevents even abundance from becoming conflict.
ramayan::452.detailed_meaning: At Dasaratha’s sacrifice, the brahmins and priests have received a vast gift. Instead of keeping it loosely or selfishly, they divide it justly among themselves. Their joy is complete, and only then do they address the king again.
ramayan::452.modern_relevance: A group gets a bonus after a long project, and the first tension is who gets what. When the split is fair, everyone can actually enjoy the win.
ramayan::452.insight: It shows that generosity becomes fully complete only when it is shared without greed.

ramayan::453.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रसर्पकैभ्यस्तु हिरण्यं सुसमाहित: । जाम्बूनदं कोटिसंख्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ तदा । । 11451 । ।
ramayan::453.verse_hindi: Thereafter, with earnestness king Dasaratha bestowed a crore of gold coins to brahmins who had come to see the sacrifice.
ramayan::453.english_translation: Thereafter, with earnestness, King Dasharatha gave a crore of gold coins to the brahmins gathered for the sacrifice.
ramayan::453.translation_literal: तत: (thereafter) / प्रसर्पकैभ्यस्तु (to those who had come near) / हिरण्यं (gold) / सुसमाहित: (with earnestness, composed) / जाम्बूनदं (of refined gold) / कोटिसंख्यं (counted in crores) / ब्राह्मणेभ्यो (to the brahmins) / ददौ (gave) / तदा (then)
ramayan::453.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::453.essence: A king's generosity here is ceremony, not philosophy.
ramayan::453.simple_meaning: Dasharatha generously gave vast wealth to the brahmins attending the sacrifice.
ramayan::453.simple_insight: True generosity can be immense, orderly, and still deeply personal.
ramayan::453.detailed_meaning: At Dasharatha's sacrifice, the priests have already distributed offerings fairly. Now the king himself gives a crore of refined gold to the brahmins who have come for the rite. It is a ceremonial act of wealth, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::453.modern_relevance: A wedding, temple fundraiser, or family ceremony ends with envelopes, gifts, and careful distribution. The moment is about honoring the occasion properly, not making a speech about it.
ramayan::453.insight: It shows royal giving as part of ritual duty, not self-display.

ramayan::454.verse_sanskrit: दरिद्राय द्विजायाथ हस्ताभरणमुत्तमम् । कस्मैचिद्याचमानाय ददौ राघवनन्दन: । । 11452 । ।
ramayan::454.verse_hindi: Dasaratha then gave his excellent bracelet to a poor brahmin who solicited alms.
ramayan::454.english_translation: Dasaratha then gave his excellent bracelet to a poor brahmin who solicited alms.
ramayan::454.translation_literal: दरिद्राय (to a poor) / द्विजाय (to a brahmin) / अथ (then) / हस्ताभरणम् (hand-ornament, bracelet) / उत्तमम् (excellent) / कस्मैचित् (to someone) / याचमानाय (to one asking) / ददौ (gave) / राघवनन्दनः (Dasaratha, descendant of Raghu)
ramayan::454.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::454.essence: True generosity gives what you would rather keep.
ramayan::454.simple_meaning: Dasaratha gave away his bracelet to a poor brahmin who asked for help.
ramayan::454.simple_insight: Generosity is real when you give something valuable, not just what is easy to spare.
ramayan::454.detailed_meaning: During the sacrifice, Dasaratha is already giving gold to brahmins in abundance. Then he goes further and offers his own bracelet to a poor brahmin who comes asking. The verse shows royal generosity in a concrete, personal act.
ramayan::454.modern_relevance: Someone asks for help when you were already planning your budget carefully. You feel the pinch, then still choose to give something you actually value.
ramayan::454.insight: It shifts generosity from surplus giving to sacrificial giving.

ramayan::455.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रीतेषु नृपतिर्द्विजेषु द्विजवत्सल: । प्रणाममकरोत्तेषां हर्षपर्याकुलेक्षण: । । 11453 । ।
ramayan::455.verse_hindi: When the brahmins were pleased, king Dasaratha who was fond of brahmins bowed to them with his eyes filled with delight.
ramayan::455.english_translation: When the brahmins were pleased, king Dasaratha who was fond of brahmins bowed to them with his eyes filled with delight.
ramayan::455.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रीतेषु (when pleased) / नृपतिः (the king) / द्विजेषु (toward the brahmins) / द्विजवत्सलः (fond of brahmins) / प्रणामम् (salutation) / अकरोत् (made) / तेषाम् (to them) / हर्षपर्याकुलेक्षणः (with eyes agitated by joy)
ramayan::455.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::455.essence: His generosity ended in humility, not self-importance.
ramayan::455.simple_meaning: Dasaratha, happy that the brahmins were satisfied, bowed to them with joy in his eyes.
ramayan::455.simple_insight: Respect deepens when generosity is received with gratitude.
ramayan::455.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just given gifts to brahmins during the sacrifice. Seeing their satisfaction, he bows to them himself, his face bright with joy. The moment is a small but telling sign of royal humility, not a teaching statement.
ramayan::455.modern_relevance: You finally get a thank-you after helping someone, and the relief shows on your face. Being appreciated can soften pride and deepen respect.
ramayan::455.insight: It shows gratitude as a two-way exchange: giving is complete only when humility remains.

ramayan::456.verse_sanskrit: तस्याशिषोऽथ विधिवद्ब्राह्मणैस्समुदीरिता: । उदारस्य नृवीरस्य धरण्यां प्रणतस्य च । । 11454 । ।
ramayan::456.verse_hindi: Brahmins uttered blessings upon the generous king when he prostrated before them
ramayan::456.english_translation: The brahmins then duly uttered blessings for the generous, heroic king who had bowed to the ground.
ramayan::456.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / आशिषो (blessings) / अथ (then) / विधिवत् (according to proper ritual) / ब्राह्मणैः (by the brahmins) / समुदीरिता: (were uttered) / उदारस्य (of the generous) / नृवीरस्य (of the heroic king) / धरण्यां (on the ground) / प्रणतस्य (of the one bowed down) / च (and)
ramayan::456.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::456.essence: Humility completes generosity and opens the way for blessing.
ramayan::456.simple_meaning: The brahmins formally bless Dasaratha after he bows down to them with humility and generosity.
ramayan::456.simple_insight: Respect given freely often returns as blessing.
ramayan::456.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just given gifts to a poor brahmin and won the priests' goodwill. Now he bows before them on the ground, and they respond with formal blessings. The verse is a ritual moment, not a teaching.
ramayan::456.modern_relevance: You thank the people who helped you, even when you were the one in charge. That small bow can change the whole atmosphere of a room.
ramayan::456.insight: It shows how generosity and humility together invite goodwill and blessing.

ramayan::457.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रीतमना राजा प्राप्य यज्ञमनुत्तमम् । पापापहं स्वर्नयनं दुष्करं पार्थिवर्षभै: । । 11455 । ।
ramayan::457.verse_hindi: Sacrifice destroys sins. It leads to heaven. It is incapable of being done by other monarchs. King Dasaratha was very much pleased after performing this great sacrifice.
ramayan::457.english_translation: King Dasaratha was greatly pleased after completing that unsurpassed sacrifice, which removes wrongdoing, leads to a higher realm, and is difficult even for other kings.
ramayan::457.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रीतमनाः (with a delighted mind) / राजा (the king) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / यज्ञम् (the sacrifice) / अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed) / पापापहम् (destroying wrongdoing) / स्वर्नयनम् (leading to a higher realm) / दुष्करम् (difficult) / पार्थिवर्षभैः (by the best of kings)
ramayan::457.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::457.essence: Rare accomplishment brings relief, but it also exposes how costly it was.
ramayan::457.simple_meaning: Dasaratha completes a rare, powerful sacrifice and feels deep joy. The verse praises its spiritual merit and its difficulty for ordinary kings.
ramayan::457.simple_insight: Some achievements matter because they are rare, costly, and complete.
ramayan::457.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just received the priests' blessings and completed a great royal sacrifice. The verse pauses on his relief and pride, highlighting that this rite is both spiritually powerful and beyond the reach of most rulers.
ramayan::457.modern_relevance: You finish something that took months of effort, and the room finally goes quiet. The relief is real — not because it was easy, but because you carried it through to the end.
ramayan::457.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary success to the weight of completing something demanding and meaningful.

ramayan::458.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽब्रवीदृश्यशृङ्गं राजा दशरथस्तदा । कुलस्य वर्धनं त्वं तु कर्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत । । 11456 । ।
ramayan::458.verse_hindi: King Dasaratha then addressing Rsyasringa said O Adherent of vows you can help the continuity of my race.
ramayan::458.english_translation: King Dasaratha then said to Rsyasringa, 'O steadfast one, you can help the continuity of my line.'
ramayan::458.translation_literal: तत: (then) / अब्रवीत् (said) / ऋश्यशृङ्गम् (to Rsyasringa) / राजा दशरथः (King Dasharatha) / तदा (then) / कुलस्य (of the family line) / वर्धनम् (growth, continuation) / त्वम् (you) / तु (indeed) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (are able) / सुव्रत (O steadfast one of vows)
ramayan::458.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::458.essence: A king asks for help that will outlive him.
ramayan::458.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks Rsyasringa to help ensure his family line continues, because he needs sons and a future for his dynasty.
