ramayan::458.simple_insight: Some requests are really about legacy, not convenience.
ramayan::458.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has completed a great sacrifice and now turns to Rsyasringa, the vow-bound sage whose presence made it possible. The king is not asking for comfort; he is asking for sons, continuity, and the survival of his line.
ramayan::458.modern_relevance: You sit with someone who can change the future of your family, your work, or your community. The ask is bigger than a favor — it is about whether something meaningful will outlast you.
ramayan::458.insight: It shifts attention from immediate need to the responsibility of carrying something forward.

ramayan::459.verse_sanskrit: तथेति च स राजानमुवाच द्विजसत्तम: । भविष्यन्ति सुता राजंश्चत्वारस्ते कुलोद्वहा: । । 11457 । ।
ramayan::459.verse_hindi: Rsyasringa, the best of brahmins, addressing the king said, O King Let it be. Four sons perpetuating your race will be born to you.
ramayan::459.english_translation: Rsyasringa, the best of brahmins, addressing the king said, “So be it. Four sons will be born to you who will continue your line.”
ramayan::459.translation_literal: तथेति (so be it) / च (and) / सः (he) / राजानम् (to the king) / उवाच (said) / द्विजसत्तमः (the best of brahmins) / भविष्यन्ति (will be) / सुताḥ (sons) / राजन् (O king) / चत्वारः (four) / ते (your) / कुलोद्वहाḥ (line-bearers, continuers of the family line)
ramayan::459.speaker: Rsyasringa
ramayan::459.essence: What is sought in faith may return as more than one blessing.
ramayan::459.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa tells King Dasharatha that his wish will be fulfilled: four sons will be born to continue his family line.
ramayan::459.simple_insight: Deep longing can be answered, but often through patience and ritual effort.
ramayan::459.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has sought a sacrifice to end his childlessness and secure his dynasty. After being asked to help preserve the royal line, Rsyasringa assures him the sacrifice will bear fruit: four sons will be born.
ramayan::459.modern_relevance: You’ve waited through appointments, prayers, and failed attempts to build a family. Then one clear answer arrives: not everything is immediate, but some hopes do take shape in time.
ramayan::459.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious waiting to trusting that effort can ripen into the right result.

ramayan::460.verse_sanskrit: मेथावी तु ततो ध्यात्वा स किञ्चिदिदमुत्तरम् । लब्धसंज्ञस्ततस्तं तु वेदज्ञो नृपमब्रवीत् । । 1151 । ।
ramayan::460.verse_hindi: Rsyasringa, a highly  intellectual and knowledgeable one in the Vedas, pondered for a while, revived his memory  and said to the king.
ramayan::460.english_translation: Rsyasringa, a highly intelligent and Veda-versed sage, reflected for a moment, regained his composure, and then spoke to the king.
ramayan::460.translation_literal: मेथावी (intelligent) / तु (indeed) / ततः (then) / ध्यात्वा (having reflected) / सः (he) / किञ्चित् (for a little while) / इदम् (this) / उत्तरम् (afterward) / लब्धसंज्ञः (having regained composure) / ततः (then) / तम् (to him) / तु (indeed) / वेदज्ञः (knower of the Vedas) / नृपम् (to the king) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::460.speaker: Rsyasringa
ramayan::460.essence: A wise reply begins after the mind settles.
ramayan::460.simple_meaning: The sage pauses, gathers himself, and then answers the king.
ramayan::460.simple_insight: Even a wise response can begin with a moment of silence.
ramayan::460.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has asked Rsyasringa for help to ensure heirs for his line. The sage does not answer immediately; he reflects, regains his composure, and only then speaks. This verse is the pause before the decisive ritual promise.
ramayan::460.modern_relevance: Someone asks for an answer before you're ready, and you pause instead of blurting out the first thing that comes to mind. That pause can be part of wisdom.
ramayan::460.insight: It teaches you to respond after reflection, not impulse.

ramayan::461.verse_sanskrit: इष्टिं तेऽहं करिष्यामि पुत्रीयां पुत्रकारणात् । अथर्वशिरसि प्रोक्तैर्मन्त्रैस्सिद्धां विधानत: । । 1152 । ।
ramayan::461.verse_hindi: I shall perform putriyeshti to help you beget sons. This is to be done in accordance with tradition for fulfilment of desires through mantras as declared in a portion of the Vedas, atharva siras .
ramayan::461.english_translation: I shall perform the rite for you to beget sons, according to the prescribed method, with mantras taught in the Atharva Shirsha.
ramayan::461.translation_literal: इष्टिं (rite) / ते (for you) / अहं (I) / करिष्यामि (shall perform) / पुत्रीयाम् (for sons) / पुत्रकारणात् (for the cause of sons) / अथर्वशिरसि (in Atharva Shirsha) / प्रोक्तैः (spoken) / मन्त्रैः (with mantras) / सिद्धाम् (made successful) / विधानतः (according to prescription)
ramayan::461.speaker: Rsyasringa
ramayan::461.essence: The right ritual can open what effort alone cannot.
ramayan::461.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa tells Dasharatha he will perform the ritual meant to help him have sons, using the proper mantras and method.
ramayan::461.simple_insight: Some needs are met through disciplined ritual, not force.
ramayan::461.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has been brought to Dasharatha's court because the king longs for sons. After a pause, he agrees to perform the prescribed rite exactly as tradition requires, setting in motion the sacrifice that will change the royal line.
ramayan::461.modern_relevance: You finally find the right specialist after months of trying everything else. The answer is not improvisation now — it is careful, exact follow-through.
ramayan::461.insight: It shifts attention from wishing for a result to performing the right process with precision.

ramayan::462.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्राक्रमदिष्टिं तां पुत्रीयां पुत्रकारणात् । जुहाव चाग्नौ तेजस्वी मन्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा । । 1153 । ।
ramayan::462.verse_hindi: To help Dasaratha beget sons, brilliant Rsyasringa  commenced putriyeshti, a sacrifice for begetting children, by pouring oblations into sacrificial fire and chanting mantras in accordance with traditions.
ramayan::462.english_translation: To help Dasaratha beget sons, brilliant Rsyasringa commenced the putriyeshti sacrifice, pouring oblations into the sacrificial fire and chanting mantras as prescribed.
ramayan::462.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्राक्रमत् (began) / इष्टिम् (the sacrifice) / ताम् (that) / पुत्रीयाम् (for sons) / पुत्रकारणात् (for the cause of sons) / जुहाव (offered) / च (and) / अग्नौ (in the fire) / तेजस्वी (brilliant one) / मन्त्रदृष्टेन (seen in mantra) / कर्मणा (by the ritual act)
ramayan::462.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::462.essence: The result begins with precise action, not impatience.
ramayan::462.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa begins the ritual to help Dasaratha have sons, offering the sacred fire exactly as the tradition prescribes.
ramayan::462.simple_insight: Some outcomes begin with disciplined ritual, not force.
ramayan::462.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has already agreed to help Dasaratha. Now he begins the son-giving sacrifice, carefully placing offerings into the fire with the right mantras. The next verse shows the celestial beings arriving, so this line is a ritual step in a larger unfolding scene.
ramayan::462.modern_relevance: You prepare the room, follow the steps, and trust the process before the result appears.
ramayan::462.insight: It shifts attention from wanting an outcome to performing the exact act required to invite it.

ramayan::463.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवास्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्च परमर्षय: । भागप्रतिग्रहार्थं वै समवेता यथाविधि । । 1154 । ।
ramayan::463.verse_hindi: All the celestial deities etc., along with gandharvas according to tradition, gathered at the sacrifice to receive their share of offerings.
ramayan::463.english_translation: All the celestial beings, along with the gandharvas and great sages, gathered there in proper order to receive their allotted share of the sacrifice.
ramayan::463.translation_literal: तत: (then) / देवाः (the celestial beings) / सगन्धर्वाः (together with gandharvas) / सिद्धाः (the perfected beings) / च (and) / परमर्षयः (great sages) / भागप्रतिग्रहार्थम् (for receiving their share) / वै (indeed) / समवेताः (assembled) / यथाविधि (according to proper order)
ramayan::463.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::463.essence: The sacrifice draws in the unseen world, but only as part of ritual order.
ramayan::463.simple_meaning: The gods, celestial musicians, perfected beings, and great sages came together at the sacrifice to receive their portion of the offerings.
ramayan::463.simple_insight: Some moments are so sacred that even the unseen world shows up in order.
ramayan::463.detailed_meaning: Rsyasringa has begun the sacrifice for Dasharatha’s sons. As the rites proceed, the celestial beings and sages gather in their proper place to accept their share, showing that this is a formal ritual scene, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::463.modern_relevance: A ceremony is underway, and everyone knows their role: the hosts, the guests, the offerings, the timing. The verse simply shows the ritual order settling into place.
ramayan::463.insight: It sets the scene for the sacrifice by showing the cosmic guests arriving in the right order.

ramayan::464.verse_sanskrit: तास्समेत्य यथान्यायं तस्मिन्सदसि देवता: । अब्रुवन् लोककर्तारं ब्रह्माणं वचनं महत् । । 1155 । ।
ramayan::464.verse_hindi: All devatas assembled there as per tradition and thus addressed Lord Brahma the creator of the worlds:
ramayan::464.english_translation: All the radiant beings assembled there in proper order and addressed Brahma, the creator of the worlds, with a great request.
ramayan::464.translation_literal: ताः (those) / समेत्य (having assembled) / यथान्यायम् (according to proper order) / तस्मिन् (in that) / सदसि (assembly) / देवताः (the radiant beings) / अब्रुवन् (spoke) / लोककर्तारम् (to the creator of the worlds) / ब्रह्माणम् (Brahma) / वचनम् (speech) / महत् (great)
ramayan::464.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::464.essence: The appeal begins when everyone turns to the highest authority together.
ramayan::464.simple_meaning: The celestial beings gathered in the sacrificial assembly and spoke to Brahma, the creator of the worlds.
ramayan::464.simple_insight: Some moments begin with a collective plea before any answer can come.
ramayan::464.detailed_meaning: At Rsyasringa’s sacrifice, the celestial beings gather in formal order and turn to Brahma. This verse is not the plea itself, but the opening movement of a larger petition about Ravana’s threat.
ramayan::464.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the hardest conversation begins. Everyone knows the problem is bigger than any one person, so they turn together to the one who can hear the full weight of it.
ramayan::464.insight: It sets up a communal appeal, showing that even the powerful first seek a higher hearing.

ramayan::465.verse_sanskrit: भगवन्त्वत्प्रसादेन रावणो नाम राक्षस: । सर्वान्नो बाधते वीर्याच्छासितुं तं न शक्नुम: । । 1156 । ।
ramayan::465.verse_hindi: O lord a rakshasa by name Ravana who had obtained prowess through your grace is oppressing us. We are unable to punish him.
ramayan::465.english_translation: O lord, a rakshasa named Ravana, empowered by your boon, is oppressing us all. We are unable to punish him.
ramayan::465.translation_literal: भगवन् (O lord) / त्वत्प्रसादेन (by your grace) / रावणः (Ravana) / नाम (named) / राक्षसः (a rakshasa) / सर्वान् (all of us) / नः (us) / बाधते (is oppressing) / वीर्यात् (through power) / शासितुम् (to punish) / तम् (him) / न शक्नुमः (we are unable)
ramayan::465.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::465.essence: A boon can become a burden when it protects the wrong person.
ramayan::465.simple_meaning: The devas tell Brahma that Ravana, strengthened by a boon, has become unbearable and cannot be restrained.
ramayan::465.simple_insight: Power given without wisdom can turn into suffering for everyone.
ramayan::465.detailed_meaning: At Brahma's sacrifice, the devas gather and speak as one. They describe Ravana's growing cruelty and admit they cannot stop him. This plea sets up the larger crisis that will require a higher intervention.
ramayan::465.modern_relevance: A person gets promoted because they impressed the right people, then starts making everyone else miserable. Everyone sees the damage, but no one can easily stop it.
ramayan::465.insight: It shifts attention from outrage at the damage to the source of the power behind it.

ramayan::466.verse_sanskrit: त्वया तस्मै वरो दत्त: प्रीतेन भगवन्पुरा । मानयन्तश्च तं नित्यं सर्वं तस्य क्षमामहे । । 1157 । ।
ramayan::466.verse_hindi: Pleased with his penance, Lord, you had granted him a boon. By honour that boon and daily endure all his cruelty.
ramayan::466.english_translation: Pleased with his penance, Lord, you had granted him a boon. By honouring that boon, we daily endure all his cruelty.
ramayan::466.translation_literal: त्वया (by you) / तस्मै (to him) / वरः (boon) / दत्तः (given) / प्रीतेन (being pleased) / भगवन् (Lord) / पुरा (formerly) / मानयन्तः (honouring) / च (and) / तम् (him) / नित्यम् (daily) / सर्वम् (all) / तस्य (his) / क्षमामहे (we endure / forgive)
ramayan::466.speaker: Devas
ramayan::466.essence: A boon honored too long can become a chain.
ramayan::466.simple_meaning: The devas remind Brahma that he once granted Ravana a boon, so they must now tolerate his oppression without breaking that grant.
ramayan::466.simple_insight: What you approve in a calm moment may become hard to carry later.
ramayan::466.detailed_meaning: The devas have gathered before Brahma because Ravana is tormenting the worlds. They do not deny the old boon; they say it was granted after satisfaction with his penance, and they have been forced to endure his cruelty out of respect for that gift.
ramayan::466.modern_relevance: You sign off on a choice when everything feels safe, and months later you are living inside its consequences. The hard part is not only the mistake — it is honouring what you already set in motion.
ramayan::466.insight: It shifts attention from immediate relief to the long reach of consent and consequence.

ramayan::467.verse_sanskrit: उद्वेजयति लोकान्स्तीनुच्छ्रितान्द्वेष्टि दुर्मति: । शक्रं त्रिदशराजानं प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छति । । 1158 । ।
ramayan::467.verse_hindi: The evilminded Ravana is inflicting pains on the three worlds. He hates the guardians of the earth and intends to assault Indra, lord of the celestials.
ramayan::467.english_translation: The evil-minded Ravana torments the three worlds, hates the guardians of the earth, and wants to attack Indra, lord of the celestials.
ramayan::467.translation_literal: उद्वेजयति (torments) / लोकान् (the worlds) / स्तीन् (the beings) / उच्छ्रितान् (the elevated) / द्वेष्टि (hates) / दुर्मति: (the evil-minded one) / शक्रं (Indra) / त्रिदशराजानं (king of the thirty gods) / प्रधर्षयितुम् (to assault) / इच्छति (wants)
ramayan::467.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::467.essence: Pride does not stay contained; it keeps reaching for more.
ramayan::467.simple_meaning: Ravana is disturbing the worlds, hating the noble protectors, and even planning to attack Indra.
ramayan::467.simple_insight: Unchecked pride spreads outward until it tries to break everything above it.
ramayan::467.detailed_meaning: The sages are describing Ravana's growing arrogance to the divine powers that empowered him. His violence is no longer local; it now threatens the three worlds and even Indra. This verse is one step in a larger plea to stop him.
ramayan::467.modern_relevance: A person who gets away with cruelty once starts reaching for bigger targets next. What began as arrogance in one room can soon poison an entire family, team, or city.
ramayan::467.insight: It shows how power without restraint turns into widening harm.

ramayan::468.verse_hindi: Because of your boon he has become unassailable and puffed with pride deties sages, yakshas, gandharvas, demons and brahmins.
ramayan::468.english_translation: Because of your boon, he has become unassailable and puffed with pride; he oversteps sages, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, and brahmins.
ramayan::468.translation_literal: ऋषीन् (sages) / यक्षान् (yakshas) / सगन्धर्वान् (along with gandharvas) / असुरान् (asuras) / ब्राह्मणान् (brahmins) / तथा (and likewise) / अतिक्रामति (oversteps) / दुर्धर्षः (unassailable) / वरदानेन (by the boon) / मोहितः (deluded / puffed up)
ramayan::468.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::468.essence: A boon meant for strength has become fuel for arrogance.
ramayan::468.simple_meaning: Ravana has become impossible to restrain because of the boon he received. Inflated by that power, he now mistreats sages, celestial beings, demons, and even brahmins.
ramayan::468.simple_insight: Power without restraint turns into arrogance fast.
ramayan::468.detailed_meaning: The gods are pleading about Ravana’s growing menace. They remind the divine giver that a boon has made him untouchable, and that this protection has only fed his pride. He now tramples every sacred boundary.
ramayan::468.modern_relevance: Someone gets promoted, then starts speaking to everyone like they are beneath him. The title was meant to support responsibility, but unchecked power has turned it into contempt.
ramayan::468.insight: It warns that protection or privilege can become a shield for abuse when humility is lost.

ramayan::469.verse_sanskrit: नैनं सूर्य: प्रतपति पार्श्वे वाति न मारुत: । चलोर्मिमाली तं दृष्ट्वा समुद्रोऽपि न कम्पते । । 11510 । ।
ramayan::469.verse_hindi: The Sun does not scorch him  and the wind does not blow by him. Even the ocean with its incessantly moving waves becomes still in his presence.
ramayan::469.english_translation: The Sun does not scorch him, and the wind does not blow by him. Even the ocean with its incessantly moving waves becomes still in his presence.
ramayan::469.translation_literal: नैनं (not him) / सूर्यः (the Sun) / प्रतपति (scorches) / पार्श्वे (at the side) / वाति (blows) / न (not) / मारुतः (the wind) / चल-ऊर्मि-माली (garlanded with moving waves) / तम् (him) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / समुद्रः (the ocean) / अपि (even) / न (not) / कम्पते (trembles)
ramayan::469.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::469.essence: His presence is so forceful that even nature seems to stand still.
ramayan::469.simple_meaning: Nature itself seems to yield before him: the sun, wind, and sea all lose their force near him.
ramayan::469.simple_insight: Some presences are so overwhelming that even the world seems to pause around them.
ramayan::469.detailed_meaning: The sages are describing Ravana’s terrifying power to persuade the divine to act against him. They pile up images of his force: even the sun, wind, and sea seem unable to disturb him. The verse deepens the fear before they beg for a way to stop him.
ramayan::469.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose confidence fills the room before they even speak. The atmosphere changes, and everyone else feels smaller. That kind of force can inspire awe or fear.
ramayan::469.insight: It frames Ravana’s power as so extreme that ordinary forces seem powerless before him.

ramayan::470.verse_sanskrit: तन्महन्नो भयं तस्माद्राक्षसाद्घोरदर्शनात् । वधार्थं तस्य भगवन्नुपायं कर्तुमर्हसि । । 11511 । ।
ramayan::470.verse_hindi: His dreamful appearance of that rakshasa strikes terror into us. O Lord do find some means to kill him.
ramayan::470.english_translation: His terrible form frightens us greatly. O Lord, please devise a way to kill him.
ramayan::470.translation_literal: तत् (that) / महत् (great) / नः (our) / भयम् (fear) / तस्मात् (from that) / राक्षसात् (from the rakshasa) / घोर-दर्शनात् (of terrifying appearance) / वध-अर्थम् (for the purpose of killing) / तस्य (of him) / भगवन् (O Lord) / उपायम् (means) / कर्तुम् अर्हसि (you should make / devise)
ramayan::470.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::470.essence: Fear turns proud beings into petitioners.
ramayan::470.simple_meaning: The devas are terrified by the rakshasa’s terrifying form and ask for a way to destroy him.
ramayan::470.simple_insight: Even the powerful can feel helpless when fear meets overwhelming force.
ramayan::470.detailed_meaning: The devas are facing a rakshasa so formidable that his very appearance unnerves them. After describing his invincibility, they turn to Brahma and plead for a way to end the threat. This line is part of that request, not the final answer.
ramayan::470.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when one person’s presence changes everything. People who usually sound certain start asking, almost desperately, for a way out.
ramayan::470.insight: It shows how fear can push even the mighty to seek help and strategy.

ramayan::471.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्सुरैस्सर्वैश्चिन्तयित्वा ततोऽब्रवीत् । हन्तायं विदितस्तस्य वधोपायो दुरात्मन: । । 11512 । ।
ramayan::471.verse_hindi: After listening to the words of the devatas and reflecting over the matter, Brahma said,    Oh, the means of destruction of that wicked (rakshasa) has struck my mind.
ramayan::471.english_translation: After listening to the words of the devas and reflecting on the matter, Brahma said, "Ah, the means to destroy that wicked being has come to me."
ramayan::471.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (having been spoken to thus) / सुरैः (by the devas) / सर्वैः (all) / चिन्तयित्वा (having reflected) / ततः (then) / अब्रवीत् (he said) / हन्त (ah!) / अयम् (this) / विदितः (known) / तस्य (of him) / वध-उपायः (means of destruction) / दुरात्मनः (of the wicked one)
ramayan::471.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::471.essence: Careful reflection finds the opening fear misses.
ramayan::471.simple_meaning: Brahma thinks carefully after hearing the devas and realises how the powerful rakshasa can be destroyed.
ramayan::471.simple_insight: Clear seeing can turn fear into a workable answer.
ramayan::471.detailed_meaning: The devas have already described Ravana’s terrifying invulnerability. Brahma listens, reflects, and recognises a loophole in the boon that protects him. This is the moment the cosmic problem becomes solvable.
ramayan::471.modern_relevance: A problem feels impossible until someone slows down and sees the hidden condition inside it. The answer is often there, waiting for careful thought instead of panic.
ramayan::471.insight: It shifts the mind from helpless fear to precise understanding.

ramayan::472.verse_sanskrit: तेन गन्धर्वयक्षाणां देवदानवरक्षसाम् । अवध्योऽस्मीति वागुक्ता तथेत्युक्तं च तन्मया । । 11513 । ।
ramayan::472.verse_hindi: When he asked gandharvas, yakshas, gods, demons or rakshasas should never be able to kill him, I said, So be it.
ramayan::472.english_translation: When he asked that gandharvas, yakshas, gods, demons, and rakshasas should not be able to kill him, I said, 'So be it.'
ramayan::472.translation_literal: तेन (by him) / गन्धर्व-यक्षाणाम् (of gandharvas and yakshas) / देव-दानव-रक्षसाम् (of gods, demons, and rakshasas) / अवध्यः (unkillable) / अस्मि (I am) / इति (thus) / वाक् (the word) / उक्ता (spoken) / तथा (so) / इति (thus) / उक्तम् (said) / च (and) / तत् (that) / मया (by me)
ramayan::472.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::472.essence: The protection he demanded left the one opening that mattered.
ramayan::472.simple_meaning: A boon was given with a hidden gap: the enemy could not be killed by many beings, but not by a man.
ramayan::472.simple_insight: Blind pride often builds the very opening that brings ruin.
ramayan::472.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked Brahma how Ravana can be stopped. Brahma recalls granting Ravana a protection against gandharvas, yakshas, gods, demons, and rakshasas. The verse matters because the missing category is the one that will finally destroy him.
ramayan::472.modern_relevance: You write the policy, the contract, the rule — then one ignored exception comes back to expose everything. The smallest blind spot is often the one that breaks the whole design.
ramayan::472.insight: It shifts attention from power to blind spots: what you exclude can become your undoing.

ramayan::473.verse_sanskrit: नाकीर्तयदवज्ञानात्तद्रक्षो मानुषान् प्रति । तस्मात्स मानुषाद्वध्यो मृत्युर्नान्योऽस्य विद्यते । । 11514 । ।
ramayan::473.verse_hindi: The rakshasa did not include man monkey and bear because of his disdain for men. As such he is fit to be destroyed by a man and not by any other means.
ramayan::473.english_translation: The rakshasa did not include humans, monkeys, or bears because of his disdain for humans. Therefore, death will come to him only through a human, and by no other means.
ramayan::473.translation_literal: ना (not) / अकीर्तयत् (mentioned) / अवज्ञानात् (out of contempt) / तद् (that) / रक्षः (rakshasa) / मानुषान् (humans) / प्रति (toward) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सः (he) / मानुषात् (by a human) / वध्यः (killable) / मृत्युः (death) / न (not) / अन्यः (other) / अस्य (of him) / विद्यते (exists)
ramayan::473.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::473.essence: His contempt for humans creates the one way he can be killed.
ramayan::473.simple_meaning: Because Ravana dismissed humans, he left them out of his boon. That blind spot makes him vulnerable only to a human hand.
ramayan::473.simple_insight: Arrogance can build the very opening that ends you.
ramayan::473.detailed_meaning: Brahma is explaining Ravana's boon to the gathered devas and sages. Ravana thought humans beneath notice, so he asked protection from every powerful being except them. That contempt becomes the crack in his invulnerability.
ramayan::473.modern_relevance: You ignore the person you think can never matter, and that one overlooked weakness becomes the way everything collapses.
ramayan::473.insight: It shifts attention from brute strength to the hidden cost of contempt.

ramayan::474.verse_sanskrit: एतच्छ्रुत्वा प्रियं वाक्यं ब्रह्मणा समुदाहृतम् । सर्वे महर्षयो देवाः प्रहृष्टास्तेऽभवंस्तदा । । 11515 । ।
ramayan::474.verse_hindi: Having heard these pleasing words uttered by Brahma, all the devatas and maharshis were overwhelmed with joy.
ramayan::474.english_translation: Having heard these pleasing words uttered by Brahma, all the devas and great sages were filled with joy.
ramayan::474.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / प्रियम् (pleasing) / वाक्यम् (words) / ब्रह्मणा (by Brahma) / समुदाहृतम् (uttered) / सर्वे (all) / महर्षयः (great sages) / देवाः (devas) / प्रहृष्टाः (filled with joy) / ते (they) / अभवन् (became) / तदा (then)
ramayan::474.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::474.essence: Clear truth can lift a room before anything changes.
ramayan::474.simple_meaning: Brahma's words pleased the gathered sages and devas so much that they rejoiced at once.
ramayan::474.simple_insight: Some truths bring instant relief because everyone knows they are right.
ramayan::474.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just explained how Ravana can be defeated. The assembled sages and devas hear the answer and rejoice, because the long threat now has a clear opening. This verse records their immediate relief before Vishnu appears.
ramayan::474.modern_relevance: You finally hear the answer after days of worry, and your whole body loosens. The problem has not vanished, but the path forward has appeared.
ramayan::474.insight: It shows how clarity can turn fear into relief in a single moment.

ramayan::475.verse_sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विष्णुरुपयातो महाद्युति: । शङ्खचक्रगदापाणि: पीतवासा जगत्पति: । । 11516 । ।
ramayan::475.verse_hindi: At this juncture Visnu the lord of the world, highly effulgent and bearing conch, discus and mace in his hands and in yellow apparel arrived.
ramayan::475.english_translation: At this juncture Vishnu, the lord of the world, highly effulgent and bearing conch, discus, and mace in his hands, and wearing yellow garments, arrived.
ramayan::475.translation_literal: एतस्मिन् (at this) / अन्तरे (interval, juncture) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / उपयातः (arrived) / महाद्युति: (highly effulgent) / शङ्खचक्रगदापाणि: (bearing conch-discus-mace in hand) / पीतवासा: (yellow-clad) / जगत्पति: (lord of the world)
ramayan::475.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::475.essence: The answer appears before the next question is spoken.
ramayan::475.simple_meaning: Vishnu arrives in radiant form, carrying his emblems and wearing yellow garments.
ramayan::475.simple_insight: A decisive presence enters the scene, and everything shifts around it.
ramayan::475.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just spoken, and the devas and sages are still rejoicing. In that charged silence, Vishnu himself appears, radiant and armed with his symbols of cosmic power. The verse is a scene transition, not yet the teaching itself.
ramayan::475.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the person who can settle everything walks in. The tension does not vanish by argument; it changes because authority has arrived.
ramayan::475.insight: It marks the arrival of the force that will resolve the gods' petition.

ramayan::476.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मणा च समागम्य तत्र तस्थौ समाहित: । 1तमब्रुवन्सुरास्सर्वे समभिष्टूय सन्नता: । । 11517 । ।
ramayan::476.verse_hindi: Lord Visnu stayed there with a composed mind after meeting Brahma Then thus spoke the devatas prostrated before Visnu and paying him homage with hymns.
ramayan::476.english_translation: Lord Vishnu stayed there with a composed mind after meeting Brahma. Then the devatas, prostrating before Vishnu and offering hymns, spoke.
ramayan::476.translation_literal: ब्रह्मणा (with Brahma) / च (and) / समागम्य (having met) / तत्र (there) / तस्थौ (stood/stayed) / समाहितः (composed, focused) / तम् (him) / अब्रुवन् (spoke) / सुराः (the devas) / सर्वे (all) / समभिष्टूय (having praised) / सन्नताः (bowed down)
ramayan::476.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::476.essence: Real authority can stand still while everyone else bows.
ramayan::476.simple_meaning: Vishnu stands calmly after meeting Brahma, while all the devas bow and praise him before speaking.
ramayan::476.simple_insight: Great power can still be utterly still.
ramayan::476.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just finished speaking, and Vishnu arrives in radiant form with the devas and sages watching. After meeting Brahma, he stands composed while the devas bow low and begin their plea. This verse is only the ceremonial pause before their request.
ramayan::476.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the person everyone has been waiting for finally walks in. Before any plan begins, the atmosphere itself changes.
ramayan::476.insight: It frames divine authority as calm presence, not agitation or display.

ramayan::477.verse_sanskrit: त्वान्नियोक्ष्यामहे विष्णो लोकानां हितकाम्यया । 1 राज्ञो दशरथस्य त्वमयोध्याधिपते: प्रभो: । । 11518 । धर्मज्ञस्य वदान्यस्य महर्षिसमतेजस: । 18तस्य भार्यासु तिसृषु ह्रीश्रीकीर्त्युपमासु च । । 11519 । । विष्णो पुत्रत्वमागच्छ कृत्वाऽऽत्मानं चतुर्विधम् । 1
ramayan::477.verse_hindi: O Visnu we pray for the welfare of all the worlds. The sovereign of Ayodhya, king Dasaratha is a righteous, virtuous and  generous king equal with rishis in lusture. Pray form into four and incarnate in the of four sons of his three wives, resembling hri (modesty), shree (auspiciousness), kirti (fame).
ramayan::477.english_translation: O Vishnu, for the welfare of all the worlds, we ask you to be born as the son of King Dasharatha, ruler of Ayodhya, a righteous and generous king equal in splendour to great sages. Take four forms and enter the three wives, becoming their four sons.
ramayan::477.translation_literal: त्वाम् (you) / नियोक्ष्यामहे (we shall request) / विष्णो (O Vishnu) / लोकानाम् (of the worlds) / हितकाम्यया (for the welfare-desiring) / राज्ञः (of the king) / दशरथस्य (Dasharatha's) / त्वम् (you) / अयोध्याधिपतेः (of the ruler of Ayodhya) / प्रभोः (of the lord) / धर्मज्ञस्य (of the righteous) / वदान्यस्य (of the generous) / महर्षिसमतेजसः (of splendour equal to great sages) / तस्य (his) / भार्यासु (in the wives) / तिसृषु (three) / ह्रीश्रीकीर्त्युपमासु (resembling modesty, auspiciousness, and fame) / च (and) / विष्णो (O Vishnu) / पुत्रत्वम् (sonhood) / आगच्छ (come) / कृत्वा (having made) / आत्मानम् (yourself) / चतुर्विधम् (fourfold)
ramayan::477.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::477.essence: The divine answer to disorder is to enter human limits on purpose.
ramayan::477.simple_meaning: The devas ask Vishnu to take birth as Dasharatha's four sons, because the worlds need protection from Ravana.
ramayan::477.simple_insight: Sometimes the highest answer is not escape, but entering the world to heal it.
ramayan::477.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the devas stand before Vishnu after seeing Ravana's power grow unbearable. They ask him to be born in Ayodhya as Dasharatha's sons, so the burden of restoring order can be carried from within human life.
ramayan::477.modern_relevance: When a family, team, or city is under strain, the cleanest fix is not from outside. Sometimes the needed person must step into the mess, take a form everyone can meet, and carry the repair from inside the system.
ramayan::477.insight: It shifts the mind from waiting for rescue to recognising that repair may require embodied participation.

ramayan::478.verse_sanskrit: तत्र त्वं मानुषो भूत्वा प्रवृद्धं लोककण्टकम् । अवध्यं दैवतैर्विष्णो समरे जहि रावणम् । । 11520 । ।
ramayan::478.verse_hindi: O Visnu assuring human form, kill Ravana in the battle. He has become a source of torment to the worlds and is invincible by gods.
ramayan::478.english_translation: O Visnu, taking human form, kill Ravana in battle. He has become a torment to the worlds and cannot be slain by the radiant beings.
ramayan::478.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / त्वं (you) / मानुषः (having become human) / भूत्वा (having become) / प्रवृद्धम् (grown powerful) / लोककण्टकम् (thorn to the worlds) / अवध्यम् (unslayable) / दैवतैः (by the radiant beings) / विष्णो (O Vishnu) / समरे (in battle) / जहि (slay) / रावणम् (Ravana)
ramayan::478.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::478.essence: The world’s deepest wound needs a human answer.
ramayan::478.simple_meaning: The divine beings ask Vishnu to take human form and destroy Ravana, who has become unbearable to the world and cannot be defeated by them.
ramayan::478.simple_insight: Some problems can only be answered from inside the world they disturb.
ramayan::478.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the radiant beings have gathered to seek relief from Ravana’s growing violence. They ask Vishnu to enter human life, because Ravana cannot be defeated by divine force alone. This is the moment the incarnation is requested.
ramayan::478.modern_relevance: When a problem keeps defeating every obvious fix, the answer may require stepping closer, not standing apart. Sometimes the only way through is to enter the mess in a human way.
ramayan::478.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract power to embodied response.

ramayan::479.verse_sanskrit: स हि देवांश्च गन्धर्वान्सिद्धांश्च मुनिसत्तमान् । राक्षसो रावणो मूर्खो वीर्योत्सेकेन बाधते । । 11521 । ।
ramayan::479.verse_hindi: That stupid rakshasa, Ravana, with his haughty prowess, is terrorising the gods, gandharvas, siddhas and great rishis.
ramayan::479.english_translation: That stupid rakshasa, Ravana, with his haughty prowess, is terrorising the gods, gandharvas, siddhas and great rishis.
ramayan::479.translation_literal: सः (he) / हि (indeed) / देवान् (the gods) / च (and) / गन्धर्वान् (the gandharvas) / सिद्धान् (the perfected beings) / च (and) / मुनिसत्तमान् (the best of sages) / राक्षसः (the rakshasa) / रावणः (Ravana) / मूर्खः (foolish) / वीर्योत्सेकेन (with arrogant prowess) / बाधते (harasses)
ramayan::479.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::479.essence: Power without humility becomes a threat to everyone.
ramayan::479.simple_meaning: Ravana is abusing his power to torment the beings of the higher realms and the great sages.
ramayan::479.simple_insight: Unchecked pride turns strength into harm.
ramayan::479.detailed_meaning: The sages are petitioning Vishnu because Ravana has become a threat to the whole cosmic order. They describe his arrogance as the reason he now terrorises gods, celestial beings, and holy seers, making intervention necessary.
ramayan::479.modern_relevance: A talented person starts using influence to intimidate everyone around them. What once looked like strength now feels like a threat, and the damage spreads far beyond the original target.
ramayan::479.insight: It shifts attention from raw power to the moral cost of pride.

ramayan::480.verse_sanskrit: ऋषयश्च ततस्तेन गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा । क्रीडन्तो नन्दनवने क्रूरेण किल हिंसिता: । । 11522 । ।
ramayan::480.verse_hindi: It is reported that a cruel rakshasa with his haughty prowess has tortured rishis, gandharvas and apsaras sporting in Nandana groves.
ramayan::480.english_translation: It is reported that a cruel rakshasa with his haughty prowess has tortured rishis, gandharvas and apsaras sporting in Nandana groves.
ramayan::480.translation_literal: ऋषयः (sages) / च (and) / ततः (then) / तेन (by him) / गन्धर्व-अप्सरसः (gandharvas and apsaras) / तथा (also) / क्रीडन्तः (sporting) / नन्दन-वने (in Nandana grove) / क्रूरेण (by the cruel one) / किल (indeed / it is said) / हिंसिताः (were harmed)
ramayan::480.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::480.essence: His power has become a public wound, not a private triumph.
ramayan::480.simple_meaning: The cruel rakshasa has harmed sages, gandharvas, and apsaras even while they were enjoying themselves in Nandana grove.
ramayan::480.simple_insight: Unchecked arrogance eventually turns even beauty and joy into targets.
ramayan::480.detailed_meaning: The gods are describing Ravana’s growing violence. He has not only threatened warriors; he has attacked sages and celestial beings in peaceful places like Nandana grove. This verse adds weight to the case for ending his rule.
ramayan::480.modern_relevance: A bully who starts by mocking people in private soon poisons the whole room. The harm spreads from obvious targets to anyone who simply wants to live in peace.
ramayan::480.insight: It shifts attention from Ravana’s strength to the damage his arrogance causes everywhere.

ramayan::481.verse_sanskrit: वधार्थं वयमायातास्तस्य वै मुनिभिस्सह । सिद्धगन्धर्वयक्षाश्च ततस्त्वां शरणं गता: । । 11523 । ।
ramayan::481.verse_hindi: We siddhas, gandharvas and yakshas along with ascetics, have hence come here to devise ways of his death. We take refuge in you.
ramayan::481.english_translation: We siddhas, gandharvas and yakshas along with ascetics, have hence come here to devise ways of his death. We take refuge in you.
ramayan::481.translation_literal: वधार्थम् (for the death) / वयम् (we) / आयाताः (have come) / तस्य (of that one) / वै (indeed) / मुनिभिः (with ascetics) / सह (together with) / सिद्धगन्धर्वयक्षाः (siddhas, gandharvas, and yakshas) / च (and) / ततः (therefore) / त्वाम् (to you) / शरणम् (refuge) / गताः (have gone)
ramayan::481.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::481.essence: Even the mighty bow when danger has no other answer.
ramayan::481.simple_meaning: The afflicted beings have come to Vishnu for shelter and ask him to destroy Ravana.
ramayan::481.simple_insight: True refuge is not weakness; it is the place even the powerful turn when force fails.
ramayan::481.detailed_meaning: The suffering gods and celestial beings have already described Ravana's terror. Now they gather before Vishnu, not merely complaining, but asking for rescue and a way to end the threat. This verse marks the plea that sets the incarnation in motion.
ramayan::481.modern_relevance: When a problem has spread beyond what you can manage alone, you finally ask for help. That moment is not defeat. It is the first honest step toward change.
ramayan::481.insight: It shifts the mind from private struggle to rightful surrender and collective response.

ramayan::482.verse_sanskrit: त्वं गति: परमा देव सर्वेषां न: परन्तप: । वधाय देवशत्रूणां नृणां लोके मन: कुरु । । 11524 । ।
ramayan::482.verse_hindi: O tormentor of enemies, O Visnu, you are the supreme, refuge for all of us. Resolve to be born in the world of men for the destruction of enemies of the gods (rakshasas).
ramayan::482.english_translation: O tormentor of enemies, O Vishnu, you are the supreme refuge for all of us. Resolve to be born in the world of men for the destruction of the enemies of the radiant beings.
ramayan::482.translation_literal: त्वं (you) / गति: (refuge) / परमा (supreme) / देव (radiant one) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / नः (of us) / परन्तप (tormentor of enemies) / वधाय (for the destruction) / देवशत्रूणाम् (of the enemies of the radiant beings) / नृणाम् (in the world of men) / लोके (in the world) / मनः (mind) / कुरु (make)
ramayan::482.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::482.essence: True refuge may have to enter the world it saves.
ramayan::482.simple_meaning: The devas ask Vishnu to become human and destroy the rakshasas, because he alone is their highest refuge.
ramayan::482.simple_insight: Sometimes help arrives not from distance, but by stepping fully into the world’s struggle.
ramayan::482.detailed_meaning: The gods, sages, and celestial beings have already described Ravana’s violence and taken shelter together. Now they turn to Vishnu and ask him to enter human life, because only that descent can restore order and end the threat.
ramayan::482.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels too large to fix, you still need someone willing to step down into the mess and carry the burden. Real rescue often looks ordinary from the outside.
ramayan::482.insight: It shifts the mind from waiting for distant rescue to recognising that protection may require embodied action.

ramayan::483.verse_hindi: Visnu, the lord of the celestials, foremost among the gods and bowed by all in the worlds addressed the assembled devatas who were guided by the law of righteousness and were led by the grand sire, Brahma.
ramayan::483.english_translation: Thus addressed, Vishnu, lord of the gods, foremost among the radiant beings, bowed to by all worlds, spoke to the gathered gods led by Brahma, the grandsire.
ramayan::483.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus addressed) / तु (indeed) / देवेशः (lord of the gods) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / त्रिदशपुङ्गवः (foremost among the gods) / पितामहपुरोगान् (led by the grandsire) / तान् (those) / सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः (bowed to by all worlds) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / त्रिदशान् (to the gods) / सर्वान् (all) / समेतान् (assembled) / धर्मसंहितान् (aligned with righteousness)
ramayan::483.speaker: Vishnu
ramayan::483.essence: The one with power answers only after hearing the whole need.
ramayan::483.simple_meaning: Vishnu, honored by all worlds, spoke to the assembled gods led by Brahma.
ramayan::483.simple_insight: Power here is not loud; it listens before it acts.
ramayan::483.detailed_meaning: The gods have already asked for help against Ravana. Vishnu, addressed as the lord of the celestials and bowed to by all worlds, turns to the assembled deities led by Brahma. This verse is the formal opening of his response.
ramayan::483.modern_relevance: A room full of people is waiting for the one person who can decide what happens next. Before speaking, that person first receives the situation fully.
ramayan::483.insight: It shows that true authority begins with calm attention, not impulse.

ramayan::484.verse_sanskrit: भयं त्यजत भद्रं वो हितार्थं युधि रावणम् । सपुत्रपौत्रं सामात्यं समित्रज्ञातिबान्धवम् । । 11527 । । हत्वा क्रूरं दुरात्मानं देवर्षीणां भयावहम् । दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च । वत्स्यामि मानुषे लोके पालयन्पृथिवीमिमाम् । । 11528 । ।
ramayan::484.verse_hindi: भयं त्यजत भद्रं वो हितार्थं युधि रावणम् । सपुत्रपौत्रं सामात्यं समित्रज्ञातिबान्धवम् । । 11527 । । हत्वा क्रूरं दुरात्मानं देवर्षीणां भयावहम् । दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च । वत्स्यामि मानुषे लोके पालयन्पृथिवीमिमाम् । । 11528 । ।
ramayan::484.english_translation: Cast off fear, for your good: in battle, kill Ravana with his sons, grandsons, ministers, friends, and kin. After destroying the cruel, evil-minded one who terrifies sages and seers, I will dwell in the world of men for eleven thousand years, protecting this earth.
ramayan::484.translation_literal: भयं (fear) / त्यजत (abandon) / भद्रं (good fortune) / वो (for you) / हितार्थं (for the sake of good) / युधि (in battle) / रावणम् (Ravana) / सपुत्रपौत्रं (with sons and grandsons) / सामात्यं (with ministers) / समित्रज्ञातिबान्धवम् (with friends, relatives, and kin) / हत्वा (having slain) / क्रूरं (cruel) / दुरात्मानं (evil-minded) / देवर्षीणां (of sages and seers) / भयावहम् (causing fear) / दशवर्षसहस्राणि (ten thousand years) / दशवर्षशतानि (and one hundred years) / च (and) / वत्स्यामि (I will dwell) / मानुषे (in the human) / लोके (world) / पालयन् (protecting) / पृथिवीम् (the earth) / इमाम् (this)
ramayan::484.speaker: Vishnu
ramayan::484.essence: The fight is only the beginning; protection is the real vow.
ramayan::484.simple_meaning: The divine asks the gods to stop fearing. Ravana will be destroyed, and then the divine will live among humans for a long time to protect the earth.
ramayan::484.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when you see the larger work your life is here to serve.
ramayan::484.detailed_meaning: The gods have just begged Vishnu to stop Ravana. In response, Vishnu promises a human birth: first the enemy must be destroyed, then he will remain on earth for eleven thousand years to protect it. This is the divine plan taking shape.
ramayan::484.modern_relevance: You’re staring at a problem that feels too large to touch. This verse says courage is not just for winning the fight — it is for carrying the responsibility that comes after.
ramayan::484.insight: It shifts action from panic to mission: remove the threat, then stay to protect what remains.

ramayan::485.verse_sanskrit: एवं दत्वा वरं देवो देवानां विष्णुरात्मवान् । मानुषे चिन्तयामास जन्मभूमिमथात्मन: । । 11529 । ।
ramayan::485.verse_hindi: Lord Visnu, supreme soul having given boon to devatas in this manner, reflected as to the place where he should take birth as a man in this world of men.
ramayan::485.english_translation: Having thus granted the boon to the gods, Vishnu reflected on where he should take birth as a man in the world of men.
ramayan::485.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / दत्वा (having given) / वरम् (boon) / देवः (the god) / देवानाम् (of the gods) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / आत्मवान् (self-possessed) / मानुषे (in human) / चिन्तयामास (reflected) / जन्मभूमिम् (birth-place) / अथ (then) / आत्मनः (of himself)
ramayan::485.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::485.essence: Rescue begins when power chooses a human form.
ramayan::485.simple_meaning: Vishnu gives the gods their boon, then turns his attention to where he will be born as a human among humans.
ramayan::485.simple_insight: The divine plan moves quietly toward human life, not away from it.
ramayan::485.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked Vishnu to end Ravana's tyranny. After granting them reassurance, he begins considering his own birth among humans. This is the turning point where cosmic rescue starts taking human form.
ramayan::485.modern_relevance: After you finally agree to help with a crisis, the next question is not applause — it is where you will actually show up and do the work.
ramayan::485.insight: It shifts attention from abstract promise to concrete incarnation and action.

ramayan::486.verse_sanskrit: तत: पद्मपलाशाक्ष: कृत्वाऽऽत्मानं चतुर्विधम् । पितरं रोचयामास तथा दशरथन्नृपम् । । 11530 । ।
ramayan::486.verse_hindi: Thereafter, the Lord with eyes like the lotus petal was pleased to transform himself into four forms and to choose king Dasaratha as his father.
ramayan::486.english_translation: Thereafter, the lotus-eyed Lord divided himself into four forms and chose King Dasharatha as his father.
ramayan::486.translation_literal: तत: (thereafter) / पद्मपलाशाक्ष: (lotus-petal-eyed) / कृत्वा (having made) / आत्मानं (himself) / चतुर्विधम् (fourfold) / पितरं (father) / रोचयामास (chose/desired) / तथा (thus) / दशरथन् (Dasharatha) / नृपम् (king)
ramayan::486.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::486.essence: The eternal steps into a human family by choice.
ramayan::486.simple_meaning: The supreme being chose to take birth as Rama, entering the world through Dasharatha.
ramayan::486.simple_insight: What looks like an ordinary birth can hide a vast purpose.
ramayan::486.detailed_meaning: The gods have already asked for relief, and Vishnu has decided to descend. In this verse, he takes on four forms and selects Dasharatha as the father of his earthly birth, turning cosmic intention into the opening of Rama's human story.
ramayan::486.modern_relevance: A family announcement changes everything: a new child is coming, and with it a life no one can fully predict. Some arrivals feel ordinary only until you see the scale of what they begin.
ramayan::486.insight: It shifts attention from random event to deliberate incarnation.

ramayan::487.verse_hindi: Then along with gandharvas, groups of apsaras, rishis, rudras and devatas sang in praise of the Lord Slayer of Madhu, with hymns of celestial beauty.
ramayan::487.english_translation: Then, along with gandharvas, groups of apsaras, sages, rudras, and radiant beings, they praised Madhusudana with celestial hymns.
ramayan::487.translation_literal: तदा (then) / देवर्षि (divine sages) / गन्धर्वाः (gandharvas) / सरुद्राः (with rudras) / साप्सरोगणाः (with groups of apsaras) / स्तुतिभिः (with praises) / दिव्यरूपाभिः (with celestial forms) / तुष्टुवुः (praised) / मधुसूदनम् (Madhusudana)
ramayan::487.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::487.essence: The heavens recognize the weight of his descent.
ramayan::487.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings joined together in praise of Vishnu with beautiful, divine hymns.
ramayan::487.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of meaning that even the radiant beings respond with praise.
ramayan::487.detailed_meaning: After Vishnu has chosen to take birth among humans, the heavens answer. Sages, gandharvas, apsaras, rudras, and other radiant beings gather in praise. This is not the main request itself, but the celestial response that confirms the moment’s sacred weight.
ramayan::487.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone makes a choice that changes everything. The response is not argument, but recognition — everyone feels that something immense has just begun.
ramayan::487.insight: It frames the incarnation as a cosmic event, not a private decision.

ramayan::488.verse_sanskrit: तमुद्धतं रावणमुग्रतेजसंप्रवृद्धदर्पं त्रिदशेश्वरद्विषम् । विरावणं साधुतपस्विकण्टकंतपस्विनामुद्धर तं भयावहम् । । 11532 । ।
ramayan::488.verse_hindi: Therefore, uproot that mighty Ravana possessing frightful prowess, inflamed pride, limitless insolence causing agony to the three worlds, a source of vexation to ascetics and  a dreadful enemy of Indra.
ramayan::488.english_translation: Therefore, uproot that mighty Ravana, blazing with fierce power, swollen with pride, hateful to the lords of the gods, a terror to holy ascetics and a dreadful enemy of Indra.
ramayan::488.translation_literal: तम् (that one) / उद्धतम् (uplifted, arrogant) / रावणम् (Ravana) / उग्रतेजसम् (of fierce radiance, mighty power) / प्रवृद्धदर्पम् (with greatly increased pride) / त्रिदशेश्वरद्विषम् (hater of the lord of the gods) / विरावणम् (making the world cry out, dreadful) / साधुतपस्विकण्टकम् (thorn to holy ascetics) / तपस्विनाम् (of ascetics) / उद्धर (uproot, remove) / तम् (that) / भयावहम् (fear-causing, terrifying)
ramayan::488.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::488.essence: Pride has made Ravana a threat that must be removed.
ramayan::488.simple_meaning: The divine beings ask Vishnu to destroy Ravana, who has become a terrifying threat through pride and violence.
ramayan::488.simple_insight: Unchecked arrogance turns power into a danger for everyone around it.
ramayan::488.detailed_meaning: The gods have already praised Vishnu and now turn to the real problem: Ravana. They describe him as proud, violent, and unbearable to sages and rulers alike. This verse is part of their plea for intervention, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::488.modern_relevance: A person who keeps getting rewarded for intimidation can become impossible to stop until someone names the damage clearly. This verse captures that moment before consequences arrive.
ramayan::488.insight: It frames arrogance as a public threat, not a private flaw.

ramayan::489.verse_sanskrit: तमेव हत्वा सबलं सबान्धवंविरावणं रावणमग्य्रपौरुषम् । स्वर्लोकमागच्छ गतज्वरश्चिरंसुरेन्द्रगुप्तं गतदोषकल्मषम् । । 11533 । ।
ramayan::489.verse_hindi: Kill Ravana, the cause of distress in the worlds, kill his forces and relatives. Them return to heaven  protected by Indra after freeing from distress, faults and sins.
ramayan::489.english_translation: Kill Ravana, along with his forces and relatives. Then return to heaven, freed from distress, and cleansed of faults and impurities.
ramayan::489.translation_literal: तमेव (that very one) / हत्वा (having slain) / सबलं (with his army) / सबान्धवम् (with his relatives) / विरावणं (the Ravana) / रावणम् (Ravana) / अग्र्यपौरुषम् (of foremost manliness) / स्वर्लोकम् (to heaven) / आगच्छ (come) / गतज्वरः (free from distress) / चिरम् (for long) / सुरेन्द्रगुप्तम् (protected by Indra) / गतदोषकल्मषम् (free from faults and impurities)
ramayan::489.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::489.essence: Ending a great harm is framed as rescue, not revenge.
ramayan::489.simple_meaning: The devas ask for Ravana and his allies to be destroyed so the world can be relieved and peace restored.
ramayan::489.simple_insight: Some harms are so large that ending them becomes an act of protection.
ramayan::489.detailed_meaning: The gods have gathered in distress and are pleading for relief from Ravana’s rule. They ask that he and his supporters be destroyed so the burden on the worlds can end and cosmic order can recover.
ramayan::489.modern_relevance: A harmful pattern has spread through a family, team, or city, and everyone knows it. Sometimes the first real mercy is to stop what keeps injuring everything around it.
ramayan::489.insight: It shifts the focus from tolerating damage to restoring order at the source.

ramayan::490.verse_sanskrit: ततो नारायणो देवो नियुक्तस्सुरसत्तमै: । जानन्नपि सुरानेवं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 1161 । ।
ramayan::490.verse_hindi: Although Omniscient lord Narayana knew the means to be employed, when he was requested by the best of devatas he spoke to them softly:
ramayan::490.english_translation: Although Omniscient Narayana knew the means to be employed, when he was requested by the best of devatas he spoke to them softly.
ramayan::490.translation_literal: ततः (then) / नारायणः (Narayana) / देवः (the radiant one) / नियुक्तः (being requested) / सुरसत्तमैः (by the best among the radiant beings) / जानन्नपि (even while knowing) / सुरान् (the radiant beings) / एवम् (thus) / श्लक्ष्णम् (softly) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::490.speaker: Narayana
ramayan::490.essence: Power can speak softly without losing authority.
ramayan::490.simple_meaning: Narayana already knew the answer, but he still answered the radiant beings gently and respectfully.
ramayan::490.simple_insight: Knowing the answer does not cancel humility.
ramayan::490.detailed_meaning: The radiant beings approach Narayana and ask how Ravana can be destroyed. He already knows the plan, but he does not answer with pride or urgency. He speaks softly, showing calm authority before the strategy is even named.
ramayan::490.modern_relevance: Someone asks you a question in a tense meeting, and you already know the answer. You do not need to prove it. You can still answer with calm, measured words.
ramayan::490.insight: It teaches you to combine certainty with gentleness, not dominance.

ramayan::491.verse_sanskrit: उपाय: को वधे तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मन: । यमहं तं समास्थाय निहन्यामृषिकण्टकम् । । 1162 । ।
ramayan::491.verse_hindi: What strategies should be adopted in the matter of destruction of that evilminded Ravana who is a thorn to the sages?.
ramayan::491.english_translation: What strategy should be used to kill that evil-minded Ravana, the thorn in the side of the sages?
ramayan::491.translation_literal: उपायः (strategy/means) / को (what) / वधे (in killing) / तस्य (of that) / रावणस्य (of Ravana) / दुरात्मनः (evil-minded) / यम् (which) / अहम् (I) / तम् (that) / समास्थाय (having adopted) / निहन्याम् (may destroy) / ऋषिकण्टकम् (thorn to the sages)
ramayan::491.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::491.essence: Victory begins with asking the right way, not rushing into force.
ramayan::491.simple_meaning: The gods are not asking for blind force. They want to know the right method for defeating Ravana, who harms the sages.
ramayan::491.simple_insight: It reminds you that power without right means is still confusion.
ramayan::491.detailed_meaning: The gods have already gathered to deal with Ravana, but brute force is not enough. Before action begins, they pause to ask what method will truly end the threat to the sages. The verse turns the crisis into a question of wise means.
ramayan::491.modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that keeps coming back, and anger is not making you smarter. Before you push harder, ask what approach actually solves it.
ramayan::491.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting against a problem to choosing the most effective means.

ramayan::492.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तास्सुरास्सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्विष्णुमव्ययम् । मानुषीं तनुमास्थाय रावणं जहि संयुगे । । 1163 । ।
ramayan::492.verse_hindi: When the devatas were thus addressed by the imperishable Visnu, they replied him saying, You may assume the form of a human being and slay Ravana in the battle.
ramayan::492.english_translation: When the devatas were thus addressed by the imperishable Vishnu, they replied, “Assume a human form and kill Ravana in battle.”
ramayan::492.translation_literal: एवमुक्ताः (thus addressed) / सुराः (the devas) / सर्वे (all) / प्रत्यूचुः (replied) / विष्णुम् (to Vishnu) / अव्ययम् (the imperishable) / मानुषीं (human) / तनुम् (form) / आस्थाय (having assumed) / रावणम् (Ravana) / जहि (slay) / संयुगे (in battle)
ramayan::492.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::492.essence: The highest power chooses a human form to restore order.
ramayan::492.simple_meaning: The divine beings ask Vishnu to be born as a human and defeat Ravana in war.
ramayan::492.simple_insight: Great power does not always arrive in a grand form. Sometimes it comes through restraint, humility, and timing.
ramayan::492.detailed_meaning: The devas have already identified Ravana as a danger that cannot be ignored. Now they ask Vishnu to enter the world as a human, not as a cosmic force, and defeat him in battle. This is the turning point where divine purpose takes human shape.
ramayan::492.modern_relevance: A crisis lands on your desk, and the obvious solution would be brute force. But the wiser answer may be quieter, smaller, and more human than anyone expected.
ramayan::492.insight: It shifts the mind from expecting force to respecting the right form of action.

ramayan::493.verse_sanskrit: स हि तेपे तपस्तीव्रं दीर्घकालमरिन्दम । येन तुष्टोऽभवद्ब्रह्मा लोककृल्लोकपूर्वज: । । 1164 । ।
ramayan::493.verse_hindi: O destroyer of foes Lord Brahma was very pleased with Ravanas intense penance over a long time৷৷
ramayan::493.english_translation: O destroyer of foes, Lord Brahma was very pleased with Ravana's intense penance over a long time.
ramayan::493.translation_literal: सः (he) / हि (indeed) / तेपे (performed austerities) / तपः (austerity) / तीव्रम् (severe) / दीर्घकालम् (for a long time) / अरिन्दम (O destroyer of foes) / येन (by which) / तुष्टः (pleased) / अभवत् (became) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / लोककृत् (creator of the worlds) / लोकपूर्वजः (ancient ancestor of the worlds)
ramayan::493.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::493.essence: Severe discipline can win power before it reveals the flaw inside it.
ramayan::493.simple_meaning: Ravana performed severe penance for a long time, and Brahma was pleased by it.
ramayan::493.simple_insight: Power can grow from discipline, even when the heart behind it is flawed.
ramayan::493.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked how Ravana can be defeated. This verse explains the source of his power: years of severe austerity that even Brahma found pleasing. It sets up the boon that will soon make Ravana nearly untouchable.
ramayan::493.modern_relevance: You can spend years building something real through discipline, and still become trapped by what you wanted from it.
ramayan::493.insight: It shifts attention from the achievement itself to the motive and cost behind it.

ramayan::494.verse_sanskrit: सन्तुष्ट: प्रददौ तस्मै राक्षसाय वरं प्रभु: । 04नानाविधेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो भयं नान्यत्र मानुषात् । । 1165 । । अवज्ञाता: पुरा तेन वरदाने हि मानवा: । 105
ramayan::494.verse_hindi: Pleased, with the rakshasa Brahma granted a boon to the effect that except from men, there was, for him, no fear of death from any other living beings. Ravana ignored men while seeking the boon.
ramayan::494.english_translation: Pleased, Brahma granted the rakshasa a boon: no living being except men could cause his death. Ravana had dismissed men while asking for the boon.
ramayan::494.translation_literal: सन्तुष्टः (pleased) / प्रददौ (gave) / तस्मै (to him) / राक्षसाय (to the rakshasa) / वरम् (boon) / प्रभुः (the lord) / नानाविधेभ्यः (from various) / भूतेभ्यः (beings) / भयम् (fear) / न (not) / अन्यत्र (except) / मानुषात् (from men) / अवज्ञाताः (disregarded) / पुरा (before) / तेन (by him) / वरदाने (in the granting of the boon) / हि (indeed) / मानवाḥ (men)
ramayan::494.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::494.essence: Pride protects itself with a loophole and calls it strength.
ramayan::494.simple_meaning: Ravana asked for protection from all beings except humans, because he thought humans were beneath him. That blind spot became the opening for his downfall.
ramayan::494.simple_insight: Arrogance often hides in what you refuse to take seriously.
ramayan::494.detailed_meaning: Brahma, pleased by Ravana’s severe penance, grants him a deadly loophole: no being except a human can kill him. Ravana, proud of his power, dismisses humans as insignificant. That contempt becomes the crack in his armor.
ramayan::494.modern_relevance: You skip over the person you think is too small to matter, and that is exactly where your blind spot lives. What you dismiss can become the place your whole plan breaks.
ramayan::494.insight: It teaches you to respect the small, overlooked weakness that pride wants to ignore.

ramayan::495.verse_sanskrit: एवं पितामहात्तस्माद्वरं प्राप्य स दर्पित: । । 1166 । । उत्सादयति लोकान्त्रीन् स्त्रियश्चाप्यपकर्षति । तस्मात्तस्य वधो दृष्टो मानुषेभ्य: परन्तप । । 1167 । ।
ramayan::495.verse_hindi: Having obtained the boon from Brahma, Ravana, greed and arrogant went on bringing  destruction to the three worlds. He carried away women by violence. O destroyer of foes his death is possible by men only.
ramayan::495.english_translation: Having obtained the boon from Brahma, Ravana, greedy and arrogant, went on destroying the three worlds. He carried away women by force. Therefore, O destroyer of foes, his death would come only through men.
ramayan::495.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / पितामहात् (from the grandfather) / तस्मात् (from that one) / वरम् (boon) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / सः (he) / दर्पितः (arrogant) / उत्सादयति (destroys) / लोकान् (the worlds) / त्रीन् (three) / स्त्रियः (women) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अपकर्षति (carries away by force) / तस्मात् (therefore) / तस्य (of him) / वधः (death) / दृष्टः (seen as possible) / मानुषेभ्यः (from men) / परन्तप (O destroyer of foes)
ramayan::495.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::495.essence: His immunity becomes the very reason his destruction must come.
ramayan::495.simple_meaning: Ravana misused Brahma's boon, became arrogant, ravaged the worlds, and abducted women. Because of that boon, only a human being could kill him.
ramayan::495.simple_insight: Power without restraint turns protection into a trap.
ramayan::495.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just granted Ravana a dangerous boon: immunity from death except at human hands. This verse shows what Ravana does with that advantage — he grows arrogant, terrorises the worlds, and violates women. The story is now setting up why Rama must be born.
ramayan::495.modern_relevance: Someone gets promoted, gains influence, and starts using it to humiliate others. The problem is never just power; it is what unguarded power reveals.
ramayan::495.insight: It shifts attention from Ravana's strength to the moral corruption that makes his downfall necessary.

ramayan::496.verse_sanskrit: इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुराणां विष्णुरात्मवान् । पितरं रोचयामास तदा दशरथं नृपम् । । 1168 । ।
ramayan::496.verse_hindi: Having heard the words of devatas, selfpossessed Visnu chose king Dasaratha as his father.
ramayan::496.english_translation: Having heard the words of the devas, self-possessed Vishnu chose King Dasharatha as his father.
ramayan::496.translation_literal: इत्येतत् (having heard this) / वचनं (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सुराणाम् (of the devas) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / आत्मवान् (self-possessed) / पितरम् (father) / रोचयामास (chose) / तदा (then) / दशरथम् (Dasharatha) / नृपम् (king)
ramayan::496.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::496.essence: The rescue of the world begins with a chosen birth.
ramayan::496.simple_meaning: After hearing the devas' plea, Vishnu decided to be born as Dasharatha's son.
ramayan::496.simple_insight: Great help often begins by entering ordinary family life, not by escaping it.
ramayan::496.detailed_meaning: The devas have just described Ravana's growing terror. In response, Vishnu calmly chooses Dasharatha as his father, setting the whole Ramayana in motion. The rescue of the world begins with a deliberate birth.
ramayan::496.modern_relevance: A child is born into a family already carrying pain, expectation, and unfinished history. Sometimes the work of healing starts by stepping into that exact inheritance, not avoiding it.
ramayan::496.insight: It frames incarnation as a chosen descent into human responsibility.

ramayan::497.verse_sanskrit: स चाप्यपुत्रो नृपतिस्तस्मिन्काले महाद्युति: । अयजत्पुत्रियामिष्टिं पुत्रेप्सुररिसूदन: । । 1169 । ।
ramayan::497.verse_hindi: At that time, the brilliant king (Dasaratha), destroyer of enemies, who had no sons was performing a sacrifice for sons.
ramayan::497.english_translation: At that time, the brilliant king Dasharatha, destroyer of enemies, who had no sons, was performing a sacrifice for sons.
ramayan::497.translation_literal: स (that) / चाप्यपुत्रः (and childless) / नृपतिः (the king) / तस्मिन् काले (at that time) / महाद्युतिḥ (of great splendor) / अयजत् (performed a sacrifice) / पुत्रियाम् (for sons) / इष्टिम् (sacred rite) / पुत्रेप्सुः (desiring sons) / अरिसूदनः (destroyer of enemies)
ramayan::497.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::497.essence: A childless king turns to ritual when ordinary power cannot answer longing.
ramayan::497.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha, still without sons, performs a ritual to seek children.
ramayan::497.simple_insight: Some prayers begin only after human effort has reached its limit.
ramayan::497.detailed_meaning: After the devas ask Vishnu to be born among humans, Dasharatha is shown in Ayodhya as a childless king turning to a son-seeking sacrifice. This is the quiet human step that sets the larger divine plan in motion.
ramayan::497.modern_relevance: You have done everything you can, and the silence remains. So you make one more honest attempt, not from panic, but from need.
ramayan::497.insight: It shifts attention from passive waiting to purposeful action when life feels incomplete.

ramayan::498.verse_sanskrit: स कृत्वा निश्चयं विष्णुरामन्त्र्य च पितामहम् । अन्तर्धानं गतो देवै: पूज्यमानो महर्षिभि: । । 11610 । ।
ramayan::498.verse_hindi: After Visnu had decided (to incarnate) and he was worshipped by devatas and maharshis he disappeared bidding farewell to Brahma.
ramayan::498.english_translation: After Vishnu had decided to incarnate, and after being worshipped by the devas and great sages, he took leave of Brahma and disappeared.
ramayan::498.translation_literal: स (he) / कृत्वा (having made) / निश्चयं (the decision) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / आमन्त्र्य (having bid farewell) / च (and) / पितामहम् (to Brahma, the grandfather) / अन्तर्धानम् (disappearance) / गतः (gone) / देवैः (by the devas) / पूज्यमानः (being worshipped) / महर्षिभिः (by the great sages)
ramayan::498.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::498.essence: The hidden decision comes first; the visible descent follows.
ramayan::498.simple_meaning: Vishnu makes his decision, takes leave of Brahma, receives honor from the devas and sages, and vanishes.
ramayan::498.simple_insight: Some departures are not losses; they are the beginning of a greater arrival.
ramayan::498.detailed_meaning: The devas have asked for rescue, and Vishnu has already chosen the king who will become his father. After honoring Brahma and receiving worship from the devas and sages, he withdraws from sight. The next verse shows the divine birth beginning.
ramayan::498.modern_relevance: A decision is made in a quiet room, the meeting ends, and everyone walks out knowing something irreversible has already begun. The visible part comes later.
ramayan::498.insight: It marks the moment a cosmic decision turns toward manifestation in the world.

ramayan::499.verse_sanskrit: तो वै यजमानस्य पावकादतुलप्रभम् । प्रादुर्भूतं महद्भूतं महावीर्यं महाबलम् । । 11611 । । कृष्णं रक्ताम्बरधरं रक्तास्यं दुन्दुभिस्वनम् । स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रुप्रवरमूर्धजम् । । 11612 । । शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नं दिव्याभरणभूषितम् । शैलशृङ्गसमुत्सेथं दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम् । । 11613 । । दिवाकरसमाकारं दीप्तानलशिखोपमम् । तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीं राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम् । । 11614 । । दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णां पात्रीं पत्नीमिव प्रियाम् । प्रगृह्य विपुलां दोर्भ्यां स्वयं मायामयीमिव । । 11615 । ।
ramayan::499.verse_hindi: During the sacrifice, there emerged from the sacrificial fire a mighty being with unmatched splendour, his prowess and strength. He wore a black and crimson garment. He had a red face. His voice was similar to the sounds of a drum. He had whiskers of soft and shining tawny hair resembling the mane of a lion He had fine hair on his head. He was endowed with auspicious signs and adorned with splendid divine ornaments. His height resembled a mountain peak. He walked with the strides of a ferocious tiger. Similar to the Sun in radiance, he looked like the crest of a blazing fire. This divine being held like his beloved wife both hands, a large vessel made of gold purified, in fire, covered with a silver lid and filled with payasam (a preparation of rice in milk and sugar). It looked as though it was created  by magic.
ramayan::499.english_translation: During the sacrifice, there emerged from the sacrificial fire a mighty being with unmatched splendour, power, and strength. He wore black and red garments, had a red face, a voice like a drum, lion-like tawny hair, auspicious marks, divine ornaments, a mountain-like height, and tiger-like stride. Radiant like the sun and blazing fire, he held a golden vessel filled with payasam as if by magic.
ramayan::499.translation_literal: तो (then) / वै (indeed) / यजमानस्य (of the sacrificer) / पावकात् (from the fire) / अतुलप्रभम् (of unmatched splendour) / प्रादुर्भूतम् (manifested) / महद्भूतम् (a great being) / महावीर्यम् (of great prowess) / महाबलम् (of great strength) / कृष्णम् (black) / रक्ताम्बरधरम् (wearing red garments) / रक्तास्यम् (red-faced) / दुन्दुभिस्वनम् (drum-sounding) / स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रु (soft tawny body-hair and beard) / प्रवरमूर्धजम् (excellent head-hair) / शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नम् (endowed with auspicious marks) / दिव्याभरणभूषितम् (adorned with divine ornaments) / शैलशृङ्गसमुत्सेथम् (raised like a mountain peak) / दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम् (with the stride of a proud tiger) / दिवाकरसमाकारम् (sun-like in form) / दीप्तानलशिखोपमम् (like a blazing fire-flame) / तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीम् (made of refined gold) / राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम् (with a silver lid) / दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णाम् (filled with divine payasam) / पात्रीम् (vessel) / पत्नीम् इव (like a beloved wife) / प्रियाम् (dear) / प्रगृह्य (holding) / विपुलाम् (large) / दोर्भ्याम् (with both arms) / स्वयं (himself) / मायामयीम् इव (as if magical)
ramayan::499.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::499.essence: The answer arrives in fire, before anyone understands it.
ramayan::499.simple_meaning: A radiant being appears from the sacrificial fire carrying a vessel of sacred food. He is described in dazzling, otherworldly detail, but he has not yet spoken or revealed his purpose.
ramayan::499.simple_insight: Some arrivals change a life before a single word is spoken.
ramayan::499.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha’s son-seeking sacrifice has reached its turning point. From the fire rises a wondrous being, brilliant and formidable, carrying the sacred payasam that will lead to Rama’s birth. The scene is pure revelation before explanation.
ramayan::499.modern_relevance: You can feel the room shift before anyone explains why. A moment arrives carrying consequences, and everyone knows something irreversible has begun.
ramayan::499.insight: It frames a divine intervention as a visible, bodily event rather than an abstract promise.

ramayan::500.verse_sanskrit: समवेक्ष्याब्रवीद्वाक्यमिदं दशरथं नृपम् । प्राजापत्यं नरं विद्धि मामिहाभ्यागतं नृप । । 11616 । ।
ramayan::500.verse_hindi: Having seen king Dasaratha, he said, O King you know I have been sent by Prjapati (Brahma), and I am here.
ramayan::500.english_translation: Having seen King Dasharatha, he said, "O King, know that I am a being sent by Prajapati, and I have come here."
ramayan::500.translation_literal: समवेक्ष्य (having seen) / अब्रवीत् (said) / वाक्यम् (speech) / इदम् (this) / दशरथम् (Dasharatha) / नृपम् (king) / प्राजापत्यम् (sent by Prajapati) / नरम् (being) / विद्धि (know) / माम् (me) / इह (here) / अभ्यागतम् (arrived)
ramayan::500.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::500.essence: A sacred plan enters human life through a messenger.
ramayan::500.simple_meaning: A divine messenger appears before Dasharatha and identifies himself as sent by Brahma.
ramayan::500.simple_insight: Great events often begin with a quiet announcement, not a thunderclap.
ramayan::500.detailed_meaning: After Vishnu has resolved to take birth and the gods have vanished, a radiant being emerges from the sacrificial fire before Dasharatha. He identifies himself as Brahma’s envoy, setting the stage for the request that will change Rama’s life.
ramayan::500.modern_relevance: A message arrives that changes everything — a call, an email, a knock at the door — and you realise your old plans are already over.
ramayan::500.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the turning point: the real change begins with a formal arrival.

ramayan::501.verse_sanskrit: तत: परं तदा राजा प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलि: । भगवन् स्वागतं तेऽस्तु किमहं करवाणि ते । । 11617 । ।
ramayan::501.verse_hindi: With folded palms the king replied, O revered lord. Welcome to you. What can I do
ramayan::501.english_translation: Then the king, with folded palms, replied, "Revered one, welcome to you. What can I do for you?"
ramayan::501.translation_literal: तत: परम् (then after that) / तदा (then) / राजा (the king) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / कृताञ्जलि: (with folded palms) / भगवन् (revered one) / स्वागतं (welcome) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may there be) / किम् (what) / अहम् (I) / करवाणि (should do) / ते (for you)
ramayan::501.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::501.essence: Courtesy comes before the request is even known.
ramayan::501.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha greets the mysterious visitor respectfully and asks how he can help.
ramayan::501.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before the real request is even spoken.
ramayan::501.detailed_meaning: At Dasharatha’s sacrifice, a radiant messenger has just revealed that he comes from Prajapati. The king answers with folded hands, welcoming him and offering service. This is the courteous pause before the divine request is finally made.
ramayan::501.modern_relevance: A stranger arrives with urgent news, and you instinctively straighten up, lower your voice, and ask how you can help before you know the full story.
ramayan::501.insight: It models respectful readiness: receive first, then respond.

ramayan::502.verse_sanskrit: अथो पुनरिदं वाक्यं प्राजापत्यो नरोऽब्रवीत् । राजन्नर्चयता देवानद्य प्राप्तमिदं त्वया । । 11618 । ।
ramayan::502.verse_hindi: Thereafter the one who came from Prajapati answered, O King you have obtained this payasam today in return for the worship offered to the devatas.
ramayan::502.english_translation: Thereafter the one who came from Prajapati answered, O King, you have obtained this payasam today in return for the worship offered to the devas.
ramayan::502.translation_literal: अथो (thereafter) / पुनरिदं (this again) / वाक्यं (speech) / प्राजापत्यो (the one from Prajapati) / नरोऽब्रवीत् (the man spoke) / राजन् (O king) / अर्चयता (by worshipping) / देवान् (the devas) / अद्य (today) / प्राप्तम् (obtained) / इदम् (this) / त्वया (by you)
ramayan::502.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::502.essence: Reverent action brings back a blessing in its own time.
ramayan::502.simple_meaning: The messenger tells King Dasharatha that the sacred sweet rice he has received comes as a reward for his worship of the devas.
ramayan::502.simple_insight: What you honor with sincerity can return to you in unexpected form.
ramayan::502.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, a divine messenger answers Dasharatha after the king greets him respectfully. He explains that the sacred payasam has come because the king honored the devas, setting up the blessing that will change Dasharatha's life.
ramayan::502.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for what matters, even when no result is visible yet. Then one day, the return arrives in a form you never predicted.
ramayan::502.insight: It links reverent action to received blessing, preparing the king for a life-changing gift.

ramayan::503.verse_sanskrit: इदं तु नृपशार्दूल पायसं देवनिर्मितम् । प्रजाकरं गृहाण त्वं धन्यमारोग्यवर्धनम् । । 11619 । ।
ramayan::503.verse_hindi: O Lion among kings, receive this payasam prepared by gods, conferring progeny, bestowing affluence and improving health.
ramayan::503.english_translation: O Lion among kings, receive this payasam prepared by the gods, granting progeny, prosperity, and health.
ramayan::503.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / तु (indeed) / नृपशार्दूल (O tiger among kings) / पायसम् (payasam) / देवनिर्मितम् (made by the gods) / प्रजाकरम् (bringing offspring) / गृहाण (receive) / त्वम् (you) / धन्यम् (auspicious) / आरोग्यवर्धनम् (increasing health)
ramayan::503.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::503.essence: A blessing arrives as something to be received, not debated.
ramayan::503.simple_meaning: A divine messenger offers the king a sacred drink that will bring children, prosperity, and good health.
ramayan::503.simple_insight: Some gifts arrive with a purpose larger than comfort.
ramayan::503.detailed_meaning: In King Dasharatha's sacrifice, a divine messenger appears with sacred payasam from the fire. The offering is not the teaching itself but the blessed result of the ritual, meant to be shared with the queens so the long-awaited sons can be born.
ramayan::503.modern_relevance: A doctor hands you a treatment plan after months of hoping for answers. The relief is real, but so is the instruction: take it exactly as given, because it carries the outcome you asked for.
ramayan::503.insight: It shifts attention from the ritual to the sacred result it is meant to produce.

ramayan::504.verse_sanskrit: भार्याणामनुरूपाणामश्नीतेति प्रयच्छ वै । तासु त्वं प्राप्स्यसे पुत्रान्यदर्थं यजसे नृप । । 11620 । ।
ramayan::504.verse_hindi: O King you are performing this sacrifice for the sake of sons. Give this to your  worthy consorts to consume it. They will bear you sons.
ramayan::504.english_translation: O King, give this to your worthy consorts to eat. Through them, you will obtain the sons for whom you have performed this sacrifice.
ramayan::504.translation_literal: भार्याणाम् (of wives) / अनुरूपाणाम् (worthy, suitable) / अश्नीतेति (let [them] eat) / प्रयच्छ (give) / वै (indeed) / तासु (through them) / त्वम् (you) / प्राप्स्यसे (will obtain) / पुत्रान् (sons) / यदर्थम् (for which purpose) / यजसे (you are sacrificing) / नृप (O king)
ramayan::504.speaker: Prajapati's messenger
ramayan::504.essence: The blessing reaches its goal only when it is given onward.
