ramayan::504.simple_meaning: The sacred food should be given to the king's wives, and through them he will have the sons he seeks.
ramayan::504.simple_insight: What he has prayed for is arriving through a careful, ordered gift.
ramayan::504.detailed_meaning: A divine messenger has come to Dasharatha after the sacrifice. The promised offering is not for the king alone; it must be shared with his queens. This verse gives the practical instruction that will lead to the birth of Rama and his brothers.
ramayan::504.modern_relevance: You may be holding something precious for a goal you cannot reach alone. Sometimes the next step is not force, but giving it to the right hands.
ramayan::504.insight: It shifts attention from personal possession to the proper channel through which fulfillment comes.

ramayan::505.verse_sanskrit: तथेति नृपति: प्रीतश्शिरसा प्रतिगृह्यताम् । पात्रीं देवान्नसम्पूर्णां देवदत्तां हिरण्मयीम् । । 11621 । ।
ramayan::505.verse_hindi: Dasaratha was pleased to receive respectfully the golden vessel filled with the payasam  prepared and bestowed by devatas.
ramayan::505.english_translation: Dasaratha was pleased to receive respectfully the golden vessel filled with the payasam prepared and bestowed by the devas.
ramayan::505.translation_literal: तथेति (so be it) / नृपति: (the king) / प्रीतः (pleased) / शिरसा (with the head) / प्रतिगृह्यताम् (received) / पात्रीं (the vessel) / देवान्नसम्पूर्णां (filled with divine food) / देवदत्तां (given by the devas) / हिरण्मयीम् (golden)
ramayan::505.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::505.essence: A sacred gift is accepted before its real cost is known.
ramayan::505.simple_meaning: Dasaratha gladly accepts the golden bowl of sacred food from the divine messenger.
ramayan::505.simple_insight: Some gifts arrive carrying a future you cannot yet see.
ramayan::505.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasaratha has just been told how to share the sacred payasam that will bring sons. He accepts the golden vessel with reverence, while the real turning point is still just ahead: the distribution of the gift that will shape the royal family.
ramayan::505.modern_relevance: You finally get the email, the signed papers, the key in your hand. The moment is small, but you know something irreversible has just begun.
ramayan::505.insight: It prepares the scene for the next decisive act, where a received gift becomes a life-changing consequence.

ramayan::506.verse_sanskrit: अभिवाद्य च तद्भूतमद्भुतं प्रियदर्शनम् । मुदा परमया युक्तश्चकाराभिप्रदक्षिणम् । । 11622 । ।
ramayan::506.verse_hindi: Overwhelmed with great joy, he, walked around that wonderful being of pleasant  countenance again and again and saluated him respectfully.
ramayan::506.english_translation: Overwhelmed with great joy, he walked around that wonderful being of pleasant countenance again and again and saluted him respectfully.
ramayan::506.translation_literal: अभिवाद्य (having saluted) / च (and) / तद् (that) / भूतम् (being) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful) / प्रियदर्शनम् (pleasant to look at) / मुदा (with joy) / परमया (supreme) / युक्तः (filled) / चकार (did) / अभिप्रदक्षिणम् (circumambulation respectfully)
ramayan::506.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::506.essence: Gratitude comes before the gift is even opened.
ramayan::506.simple_meaning: Dasharatha bows to a wondrous, beautiful being and circles him respectfully, filled with joy.
ramayan::506.simple_insight: Joy can make reverence feel natural, not forced.
ramayan::506.detailed_meaning: In the sacrificial hall, Dasharatha has just received the divine offering that will grant him sons. Before taking it, he honours the wondrous messenger who brought it, moving around him in reverence. The verse shows gratitude before gratification.
ramayan::506.modern_relevance: You finally get the thing you have been waiting for, but you pause first to honour the person who helped it arrive.
ramayan::506.insight: It teaches you to meet good fortune with gratitude before possession.

ramayan::507.verse_sanskrit: ततो दशरथ: प्राप्य पायसं देवनिर्मितम् । बभूव परमप्रीत: प्राप्य वित्तमिवाधन: । । 11623 । ।
ramayan::507.verse_hindi: Dasaratha who received the payasam prepared by devatas was highly pleased like a poor man who received wealth.
ramayan::507.english_translation: Dasaratha, having received the payasam made by the devas, became deeply pleased, like a poor man who has found wealth.
ramayan::507.translation_literal: ततः (then) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / प्राप्य (having received) / पायसम् (payasam) / देवनिर्मितम् (made by the devas) / बभूव (became) / परमप्रीतः (deeply pleased) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / वित्तम् (wealth) / इव (like) / अधनः (a poor man)
ramayan::507.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::507.essence: Joy can feel like wealth when longing is finally answered.
ramayan::507.simple_meaning: Dasaratha receives the divine payasam and feels intense joy, like a poor man suddenly finding wealth.
ramayan::507.simple_insight: Even a small gift can feel immense when it answers a long longing.
ramayan::507.detailed_meaning: The divine being has just handed Dasaratha the sacred payasam. He accepts it with reverence and is overwhelmed with joy, as if sudden wealth had come to a poor man. The verse simply marks his emotional response before the story moves on.
ramayan::507.modern_relevance: You open a message that changes everything and just stare at it for a moment. Relief and disbelief arrive together.
ramayan::507.insight: It shows how a long-awaited blessing can flood the mind before words catch up.

ramayan::508.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं भूतं परमभास्वरम् । संवर्तयित्वा तत्कर्म तत्रैवान्तरधीयत । । 11624 । ।
ramayan::508.verse_hindi: Then that effulgent figure of wonderful form having given the bowl of payasam vanished from there.
ramayan::508.english_translation: Then that effulgent being of wonderful form, after completing that task, vanished from there.
ramayan::508.translation_literal: ततः (then) / तत् (that) / अद्भुत-प्रख्यम् (wonderfully radiant) / भूतम् (being) / परम-भास्वरम् (most effulgent) / संवर्तयित्वा (having completed) / तत् (that) / कर्म (task) / तत्रैव (there itself) / अन्तर्धीयत (vanished)
ramayan::508.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::508.essence: What changes your life may vanish the moment it delivers its gift.
ramayan::508.simple_meaning: A radiant, wondrous being gave the sacred food to Dasharatha and then disappeared.
ramayan::508.simple_insight: Some blessings arrive briefly, do their work, and leave without explanation.
ramayan::508.detailed_meaning: In Dasharatha’s palace, a divine figure has just delivered the sacred payasam that will shape the fate of Ayodhya. The task is complete, and the figure disappears at once, leaving the king with a gift whose consequences will unfold through the whole epic.
ramayan::508.modern_relevance: A message arrives, changes everything, and then the sender is gone. You are left holding the consequence long after the moment itself has passed.
ramayan::508.insight: It turns a miracle into a passing event, shifting attention to what the gift will cause next.

ramayan::509.verse_hindi: The inner apartment, brightened with rays of happiness, shone like the autumnal sky in the glow of the moon.
ramayan::509.english_translation: The inner apartment, brightened with rays of happiness, shone like the autumn sky in the glow of the moon.
ramayan::509.translation_literal: हर्षरश्मिभि: (with rays of joy) / उद्योतम् (brightened) / तस्य (his) / अन्त:पुरम् (inner apartment) / आबभौ (shone) / शारदस्य (of autumn) / अभिरामस्य (beautiful) / चन्द्रस्य (of the moon) / इव (like) / नभः-अंशुभि: (with sky-rays)
ramayan::509.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::509.essence: Joy had already arrived before the gift was named.
ramayan::509.simple_meaning: The royal inner chambers were filled with joy and looked bright and beautiful, like the autumn sky lit by the moon.
ramayan::509.simple_insight: Even a palace feels different when hope enters it.
ramayan::509.detailed_meaning: After the divine being gives Dasaratha the sacred payasam, joy spreads through the royal household. The inner apartment of Ayodhya glows with happiness before the real news is even spoken, preparing the scene for Kausalya to receive the gift of a son.
ramayan::509.modern_relevance: A house goes quiet after a long wait, and then one small message changes everything. The air itself feels lighter before anyone has said the words out loud.
ramayan::509.insight: It shows how hope can transform a whole space before the event is fully known.

ramayan::510.verse_sanskrit: सोऽन्त:पुरं प्रविश्यैव कौसल्यामिदमब्रवीत् । पायसं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पुत्रीयं त्विदमात्मन: । । 11626 । ।
ramayan::510.verse_hindi: He entered the inner apartment and addressing queen Kausalya said, Receive this payasam which has the power to give you sons.
ramayan::510.english_translation: He entered the inner apartment and addressing Kausalya said, Receive this payasam that will grant you a son.
ramayan::510.translation_literal: सः (he) / अन्तःपुरम् (inner apartment) / प्रविश्य एव (having entered indeed) / कौसल्याम् (to Kausalya) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said) / पायसम् (payasam) / प्रतिगृह्णीष्व (receive) / पुत्रीयम् (son-giving) / तु (indeed) / इदम् (this) / आत्मनः (of oneself)
ramayan::510.speaker: Dasaratha
ramayan::510.essence: A hidden gift begins the royal line.
ramayan::510.simple_meaning: Dasaratha brings a sacred sweet drink to Kausalya and asks her to accept it so she may bear a son.
ramayan::510.simple_insight: Some moments in a family change the future before anyone can see it.
ramayan::510.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has received a divine offering and now enters Kausalya’s chamber to share it. This is the quiet beginning of the royal children’s birth, a private moment that sets the whole epic in motion.
ramayan::510.modern_relevance: A doctor calls you into a small room and says the next choice matters more than it looks. A family’s future can begin with one careful handoff.
ramayan::510.insight: It turns a private offering into the first step of a larger destiny.

ramayan::511.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्यायै नरपति: पायसार्धं ददौ तदा । अर्धादर्धं ददौ चापि सुमित्रायै नराधिप: । । 11627 । । कैकेय्यै चावशिष्टार्धं ददौ पुत्रार्थकारणात् । प्रददौ चावशिष्टार्धं पायसस्यामृतोपमम् । । 11628 । । अनुचिन्त्य सुमित्रायै पुनरेव महीपति: । एवं तासां ददौ राजा भार्याणां पायसं पृथक् । । 11629 । ।
ramayan::511.verse_hindi: Then Dasaratha gave half the portion of payasam to Kausalya, half of the remaining half to Sumitra, half of the remaining portion (oneeighth of original) to Kaikeyi for the sake of a son. On further thinking, he gave the remaining oneeighth portion to Sumitra. In this manner the king divided and distributed the payasam among his wives separately.
ramayan::511.english_translation: Then Dasaratha gave half the portion of payasam to Kausalya, half of the remaining half to Sumitra, half of the remaining portion (one-eighth of the original) to Kaikeyi for the sake of a son. On further thinking, he gave the remaining one-eighth portion to Sumitra. In this manner the king divided and distributed the payasam among his wives separately.
ramayan::511.translation_literal: कौसल्यायै (to Kausalya) / नरपति: (the king) / पायसार्धं (half of the payasam) / ददौ (gave) / तदा (then) / अर्धादर्धं (half of the remaining half) / ददौ (gave) / च (and) / अपि (also) / सुमित्रायै (to Sumitra) / नराधिप: (the ruler) / कैकेय्यै (to Kaikeyi) / च (and) / अवशिष्टार्धं (the remaining half) / ददौ (gave) / पुत्रार्थकारणात् (for the sake of a son) / प्रददौ (gave) / च (and) / अवशिष्टार्धं (the remaining half) / पायसस्य (of the payasam) / अमृतोपमम् (like nectar) / अनुचिन्त्य (after considering) / सुमित्रायै (to Sumitra) / पुनरेव (again) / महीपति: (the king) / एवम् (thus) / तासां (to them) / ददौ (gave) / राजा (the king) / भार्याणां (of the wives) / पायसं (payasam) / पृथक् (separately)
ramayan::511.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::511.essence: A hoped-for gift becomes a measured act of royal responsibility.
ramayan::511.simple_meaning: Dasaratha divides the sacred rice pudding among his three wives, giving each a separate share so each can bear a son.
ramayan::511.simple_insight: Even a king’s hope for heirs is shaped by careful, unequal human choices.
ramayan::511.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has received the divine rice pudding meant to bring him sons. In the quiet of the inner chamber, he carefully portions it among Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi, then thinks again and adjusts the shares. The scene prepares the birth of Rama and his brothers.
ramayan::511.modern_relevance: You finally bring home something precious meant to change your family’s future, then find yourself dividing it with care, worry, and hope.
ramayan::511.insight: It shows how a single hoped-for blessing can become a carefully managed family decision.

ramayan::512.verse_sanskrit: तास्त्वेतत्पायसं प्राप्य नरेन्द्रस्योत्तमास्स्त्रय: । सम्मानं मेनिरे सर्वां: प्रहर्षोदितचेतस: । । 11630 । ।
ramayan::512.verse_hindi: The virtuous wives of the king were exceedingly delighted and felt honoured after receiving the payasam .
ramayan::512.english_translation: The king’s noble wives felt honoured and overjoyed after receiving the payasam.
ramayan::512.translation_literal: ताः (those women) / तु (indeed) / एतत् (this) / पायसम् (payasam) / प्राप्य (having received) / नरेन्द्रस्य (of the king) / उत्तमाः (excellent) / स्त्रियः (women/wives) / सम्मानम् (honour) / मेनिरे (they considered) / सर्वाः (all) / प्रहर्ष-उदित-चेतसः (with minds risen in delight)
ramayan::512.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::512.essence: Being received with honour can fill the heart before anything else happens.
ramayan::512.simple_meaning: The king’s wives received the sacred sweet rice and felt honoured and joyful.
ramayan::512.simple_insight: Joy can arrive as honour, not just as pleasure.
ramayan::512.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just divided the sacred payasam among his three queens. This verse pauses on their response: Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi feel honoured and filled with delight as the gift reaches them before the coming conception scene.
ramayan::512.modern_relevance: A message lands in the family group chat and suddenly everyone feels chosen, remembered, included. Sometimes the deepest joy is simply being counted with care.
ramayan::512.insight: It shifts attention from the object received to the dignity of being remembered and included.

ramayan::513.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तु ता: प्राश्य तदुत्तमास्त्रियो महीपतेरुत्तमपायसं पृथक् । हुताशनादित्यसमानतेजसोऽचिरेण गर्भान्प्रतिपेदिरे तदा । । 11631 । ।
ramayan::513.verse_hindi: Then the excellent consorts of the king who glowed like fire and the Sun, having consumed the choicest payasam, became pregnant in a short time.
ramayan::513.english_translation: Then the excellent consorts of the king, radiant like fire and the Sun, having eaten the finest payasam, became pregnant in a short time.
ramayan::513.translation_literal: ततस्तु (then) / ता: (those women) / प्राश्य (having eaten) / तदुत्तमास्त्रिय: (those excellent women) / महीपतेर् (of the king) / उत्तमपायसं (the finest payasam) / पृथक् (separately) / हुताशनादित्यसमानतेजसोः (of radiance equal to fire and the Sun) / अचिरेण (in a short time) / गर्भान् (pregnancies) / प्रतिपेदिरे (obtained) / तदा (then)
ramayan::513.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::513.essence: A hidden blessing begins changing everything before anyone can see it.
ramayan::513.simple_meaning: The king's three wives ate the sacred food and soon conceived children.
ramayan::513.simple_insight: Some moments are quiet on the surface and world-changing underneath.
ramayan::513.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha's queens have just received the sacred payasam. This verse records the result: the blessing takes root quickly, and the royal household moves from hope to fulfilled promise.
ramayan::513.modern_relevance: A doctor hands you a test result after weeks of waiting. The change is invisible at first, but your life has already shifted.
ramayan::513.insight: It marks the turning point where a long-awaited blessing begins to take form.

ramayan::514.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तु राजा प्रसमीक्ष्य ता: स्त्रिय:प्ररूढगर्भा: प्रतिलब्धमानस: । बभूव हृष्टस्त्रिदिवे यथा हरि:सुरेन्द्रसिद्धर्षिगणाभिपूजित: । । 11632 । ।
ramayan::514.verse_hindi: The king now regained his composure of mind on seeing his pregnant wives. He looked delighted like Visnu worshipped by Indra, and hosts of siddhas and rishis.
ramayan::514.english_translation: Then the king, seeing those women now with child, regained his composure and became joyful, like Vishnu in heaven, worshipped by Indra and hosts of perfected sages and seers.
ramayan::514.translation_literal: ततः (then) / तु (indeed) / राजा (the king) / प्रसमीक्ष्य (having observed clearly) / ता: (those) / स्त्रिय: (women) / प्ररूढगर्भा: (with developed pregnancy) / प्रतिलब्धमानस: (one whose mind was regained) / बभूव (became) / हृष्ट: (joyful) / त्रिदिवे (in heaven) / यथा (like) / हरि: (Vishnu) / सुरेन्द्र (by Indra) / सिद्धर्षिगणाभिपूजित: (worshipped by hosts of perfected beings and sages)
ramayan::514.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::514.essence: Hope visible at last restores the heart at once.
ramayan::514.simple_meaning: Dasaratha feels peace and joy again when he sees that his wives are pregnant. The moment is compared to Vishnu being honored in heaven.
ramayan::514.simple_insight: Relief returns when hope becomes visible in front of you.
ramayan::514.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has been waiting for the promise of sons after years of longing. Now he sees his queens carrying children, and his troubled mind settles at once. The comparison to Vishnu honored in heaven lifts the moment into sacred joy.
ramayan::514.modern_relevance: You finally get the message that the test came back positive, and your chest loosens. The fear that sat in your body all week gives way to relief.
ramayan::514.insight: It shifts attention from anxious waiting to the relief of fulfilled hope.

ramayan::515.verse_sanskrit: पुत्रत्वं तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञस्तस्य सुमहात्मन: । उवाच देवतास्सर्वास्स्वयम्भूर्भगवानिदम् । । 1171 । ।
ramayan::515.verse_hindi: When Visnu had decided to be born as the son of that great king (Dasaratha), the selfborn Lord (Brahma), addressed all devatas :
ramayan::515.english_translation: When Vishnu had decided to be born as the son of that great king, the self-born Lord Brahma spoke these words to all the radiant beings:
ramayan::515.translation_literal: पुत्रत्वं (sonhood / birth as a son) / तु (indeed) / गते (having gone / having been resolved) / विष्णौ (when Vishnu) / राज्ञः (of the king) / तस्य (of that) / सुमहात्मनः (great-souled) / उवाच (spoke) / देवताः (the radiant beings) / सर्वाः (all) / स्वयम्भूः (the self-born) / भगवान् (the blessed Lord) / इदम् (this)
ramayan::515.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::515.essence: The divine plan enters history by choosing a human birth.
ramayan::515.simple_meaning: Vishnu has chosen to be born as the king's son, and Brahma now speaks to the other radiant beings.
ramayan::515.simple_insight: Even the cosmic plan begins with a deliberate descent into human life.
ramayan::515.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasaratha's sacrifice has already borne fruit. The queen has conceived, and now Brahma announces to the other radiant beings that Vishnu has chosen to take birth as the king's son. This is the pivot from prayer to incarnation.
ramayan::515.modern_relevance: A family has waited years for a child, and the news finally lands. What looks like a private joy is also the beginning of a much larger unfolding.
ramayan::515.insight: It shifts attention from human events as random to human events as part of a larger design.

ramayan::516.verse_sanskrit: सत्यसन्धस्य वीरस्य सर्वेषान्नो हितैषिण: । विष्णोस्सहायान्बलिनस्सृजध्वं कामरूपिण: । । 1172 । ।
ramayan::516.verse_hindi: Create strong and powerful beings capable of assuming forms at free will to extend support to Visnu who is  true to his word, heroic and benevolent.
ramayan::516.english_translation: Create strong and powerful beings capable of assuming forms at will to support Vishnu, who is true to his word, heroic, and benevolent.
ramayan::516.translation_literal: सत्यसन्धस्य (of the one true to his word) / वीरस्य (of the heroic one) / सर्वेषाम् (for all) / नो (of us) / हितैषिणः (well-wisher) / विष्णोः (of Vishnu) / सहायान् (helpers) / बलिनः (strong ones) / सृजध्वम् (create) / कामरूपिणः (able to assume forms at will)
ramayan::516.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::516.essence: Even Vishnu's mission needs powerful allies.
ramayan::516.simple_meaning: Brahma asks the other divine beings to create powerful helpers who can change form at will, because Vishnu is about to come down to help the world.
ramayan::516.simple_insight: Some tasks are so large they require allies who can rise to them.
ramayan::516.detailed_meaning: The gods have gathered after learning that Vishnu will be born as Dasharatha's son. Brahma now asks them to create mighty, shape-shifting beings who can assist Vishnu in the coming struggle. This is the planning behind the epic's central descent.
ramayan::516.modern_relevance: A hard project lands on your desk and you realise one person cannot carry it alone. The right response is not pride — it is gathering the right people with the right strengths.
ramayan::516.insight: It shifts the mind from lone effort to coordinated support around a worthy mission.

ramayan::517.verse_sanskrit: मायाविदश्च शूरांश्च वायुवेगसमाञ्जवे । नयज्ञान्बुद्धिसम्पन्नान्विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमान् । । 1173 । । असंहार्यानुपायज्ञान् दिव्यसंहननान्वितान् । सर्वास्त्रगुणसम्पन्नानमृतप्राशनानिव । । 1174 । । अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु गन्धर्वाणां तनूषु च । सृजध्वं हरिरूपेण पुत्रांस्तुल्यपराक्रमान् । । 1175 । ।
ramayan::517.verse_hindi: Incarnate as monkeys in the womb of  chiefs of apsarasas and gandharvas. Create sons who have the knowledge of deceitful tricks, who are brave, who match wind in speed, who are endowed with intellect and statecraft, who are determined, who are  knowledgeable in various means of achieving victory, who are supernatural  bodies, who possess capability of employing and resisting weapons, who resemble those who subsist on amrita (immortals) and are equal (to Visnu) in prowess.
ramayan::517.english_translation: Create sons who have the knowledge of deceitful tricks, who are brave, who match wind in speed, who are endowed with intellect and statecraft, who are determined, who are knowledgeable in various means of achieving victory, who have supernatural bodies, who possess capability of employing and resisting weapons, who resemble those who subsist on amrita and are equal in prowess to Vishnu. Incarnate them as monkeys in the wombs of chief apsaras and gandharvas.
ramayan::517.translation_literal: मायाविदः (knowers of illusion/trickery) / च (and) / शूरान् (brave ones) / च (and) / वायुवेगसमान् (equal to wind in speed) / जवे (in swiftness) / नयज्ञान् (knowers of strategy/statecraft) / बुद्धिसम्पन्नान् (endowed with discernment) / विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमान् (equal to Vishnu in prowess) / असंहार्यान् (unconquerable) / उपायज्ञान् (knowers of means) / दिव्यसंहननान्वितान् (endowed with divine bodies) / सर्वास्त्रगुणसम्पन्नान् (fully equipped with the qualities of all weapons) / अमृतप्राशनानिव (as if drinkers of nectar) / अप्सरस्सु (in the wombs of apsaras) / च (and) / मुख्यासु (chief) / गन्धर्वाणां (of gandharvas) / तनूषु (in bodies/wombs) / च (and) / सृजध्वं (create) / हरिरूपेण (in the form of Hari) / पुत्रान् (sons) / तुल्यपराक्रमान् (of equal prowess)
ramayan::517.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::517.essence: The mission requires allies built for speed, strategy, and impossible work.
ramayan::517.simple_meaning: Brahma tells the other divine beings to create powerful monkey-born allies for Vishnu’s mission. They must be fast, intelligent, brave, hard to defeat, and skilled in every kind of strategy and weapon.
ramayan::517.simple_insight: Great work needs the right allies: speed, intelligence, courage, and adaptability all matter together.
ramayan::517.detailed_meaning: Brahma has already accepted Vishnu’s descent as Dasharatha’s son. Now he instructs the divine beings to prepare support for that mission by creating extraordinary monkey allies through the lineages of apsaras and gandharvas. This verse lists the qualities Hanuman and the vanara hosts will embody.
ramayan::517.modern_relevance: A team is being assembled for a mission no single person can carry alone. You do not need only strength; you need speed, judgment, flexibility, and people who can adapt when the plan breaks.
ramayan::517.insight: It shifts attention from raw power to a complete support system: courage, intelligence, and tactical skill together.

ramayan::518.verse_sanskrit: पूर्वमेव मया सृष्टो जाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गव: । जृम्भमाणस्य सहसा मम वक्त्रादजायत । । 1176 । ।
ramayan::518.verse_hindi: Earlier Jambavan, the foremost among bears was suddenly emerged out of my face while I was yawning.
ramayan::518.english_translation: Jambavan, the foremost among bears, had already been created by me; he was born suddenly from my mouth while I was yawning.
ramayan::518.translation_literal: पूर्वमेव (already before) / मया (by me) / सृष्टः (created) / जाम्बवान् (Jambavan) / ऋक्षपुङ्गवः (foremost among bears) / जृम्भमाणस्य (while yawning) / सहसा (suddenly) / मम (my) / वक्त्रात् (from the mouth) / अजायत (was born)
ramayan::518.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::518.essence: Even a yawn can become the birth of a protector.
ramayan::518.simple_meaning: Brahma says Jambavan was created earlier and emerged from his mouth while he yawned.
ramayan::518.simple_insight: Great helpers can appear in the strangest ways, already prepared before the moment you notice them.
ramayan::518.detailed_meaning: Brahma is describing how the forest allies of Vishnu are being brought into being. Jambavan is not introduced as a random bear, but as one of the first powerful beings already formed for the coming struggle, born in an uncanny divine moment.
ramayan::518.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, then later realize they were built for a crucial role all along.
ramayan::518.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to hidden readiness: support may already exist before the crisis begins.

ramayan::519.verse_sanskrit: ते तथोक्ता भगवता तत्प्रतिश्रुत्य शासनम् । जनयामासुरेवं ते पुत्रान्वानररूपिण: । । 1177 । ।
ramayan::519.verse_hindi: Instructed by Brahma in that manner, all of them gave birth to sons in the form of monkeys.
ramayan::519.english_translation: Instructed by Brahma in that manner, all of them gave birth to sons in the form of monkeys.
ramayan::519.translation_literal: ते (they) / तथोक्ता (thus instructed) / भगवता (by the Lord Brahma) / तत् (that) / प्रतिश्रुत्य (having heard and accepted) / शासनम् (the command) / जनयामासुः (gave birth) / एवम् (thus) / ते (they) / पुत्रान् (sons) / वानररूपिणः (in monkey form)
ramayan::519.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::519.essence: The alliance is born before the battle begins.
ramayan::519.simple_meaning: Brahma’s command is carried out, and the celestial beings give birth to sons in monkey form.
ramayan::519.simple_insight: Great events begin with unseen preparations long before the hero appears.
ramayan::519.detailed_meaning: After Brahma instructs the assembled beings to aid the coming struggle, they obey and begin producing sons in monkey form. This is not yet the action itself, but the hidden setup for the allies who will later serve Rama.
ramayan::519.modern_relevance: A project looks impossible until the right people quietly appear, each carrying the exact skill the moment needs. What seems sudden is often the result of earlier coordination.
ramayan::519.insight: It shifts attention from the visible event to the preparation that makes it possible.

ramayan::520.verse_hindi: Distinguished rishis, siddhas, vidhyadharas, uragas, charanas procreated (in the form of monkeys) heroic sons who became forestdwellers.
ramayan::520.english_translation: Distinguished rishis, siddhas, vidhyadharas, uragas, and charanas procreated heroic sons who became forest dwellers.
ramayan::520.translation_literal: ऋषयः (sages) / च (and) / सुतान् (sons) / वीरान् (heroic) / ससृजुः (procreated) / वनचारिणः (forest-wanderers) / महात्मानः (great-souled) / सिद्धविद्याधरोरगाः (siddhas, vidhyadharas, and uragas) / चारणाः (charanas)
ramayan::520.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::520.essence: The forest allies of Rama are born from many exalted lineages.
ramayan::520.simple_meaning: Many exalted beings gave birth to heroic sons who took the form of forest-dwellers.
ramayan::520.simple_insight: Greatness can show up in unexpected forms, even in the next generation.
ramayan::520.detailed_meaning: Brahma’s creative order continues as different classes of exalted beings bring forth monkey-born sons. This verse is one link in a larger account of how the vanara leaders came into being, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::520.insight: It completes the origin story of the vanara warriors by showing their many divine lineages.

ramayan::521.verse_sanskrit: वानरेन्द्रं महेन्द्राभमिन्द्रो वालिनमूर्जितम् । सुग्रीवं जनयामास तपनस्तपतां वर: । । 1179 । ।
ramayan::521.verse_hindi: Indra gave birth to Vali, chief of monkeys resembling Mahendra mountain and having a mighty body. Sun, great among those producing heat, begot Sugriva.
ramayan::521.english_translation: Indra gave birth to Vali, chief of monkeys resembling Mahendra mountain and having a mighty body. The Sun, greatest among those who produce heat, begot Sugriva.
ramayan::521.translation_literal: वानरेन्द्रम् (chief of monkeys) / महेन्द्राभम् (resembling Mahendra) / इन्द्रः (Indra) / वालिनम् (Vali) / ऊर्जितम् (mighty) / सुग्रीवम् (Sugriva) / जनयामास (begot) / तपनः (the Sun) / तपताम् (among the hot ones) / वरः (the best)
ramayan::521.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::521.essence: Two mighty rivals are introduced through their radiant origins.
ramayan::521.simple_meaning: Indra fathered Vali, and the Sun fathered Sugriva. The verse is naming the origins of these monkey chiefs.
ramayan::521.simple_insight: Some figures enter the story already marked by immense force.
ramayan::521.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the births of the great monkey leaders. Indra gives rise to Vali, and the Sun gives rise to Sugriva. The verse serves as background for the alliance and rivalry that will shape the coming search for Sita.
ramayan::521.modern_relevance: A team is being introduced in a room before the real conflict begins. You are not yet watching the drama — you are learning who carries the force that will later collide.
ramayan::521.insight: It prepares the story by showing that these leaders are not ordinary beings.

ramayan::522.verse_hindi: Brihaspati begot the intelligent monkey Tara who  had none to surpass him among the monkey chiefs.
ramayan::522.english_translation: Brihaspati begot Tara, the great monkey, the most intelligent of all the chief monkeys.
ramayan::522.translation_literal: बृहस्पतिः (Brihaspati) / तु (indeed) / अजनयत् (begot) / तारम् (Tara) / नाम (named) / महाहरिम् (great monkey) / सर्ववानरमुख्यानाम् (of all the chief monkeys) / बुद्धिमन्तम् (intelligent) / अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed)
ramayan::522.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::522.essence: A brilliant leader is introduced as part of the coming alliance.
ramayan::522.simple_meaning: Brihaspati is said to have fathered Tara, a monkey chief known for unmatched intelligence.
ramayan::522.simple_insight: Great ability can appear in unexpected forms and unexpected families.
ramayan::522.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the origins of the monkey leaders before the great alliance takes shape. Here, Tara is introduced as one of the remarkable sons born from the gods into monkey form, setting up the larger gathering of forces.
ramayan::522.modern_relevance: A team roster is being announced before the big project begins, and one name stands out for sharp judgment. The verse is introducing talent, not teaching a principle.
ramayan::522.insight: It frames Tara as part of the epic’s cast, not as a separate teaching.

ramayan::523.verse_sanskrit: धनदस्य सुतश्श्रीमान् वानरो गन्धमादन: । विश्वकर्मात्वजनयन्नलं नाम महाहरिम् । । 11711 । ।
ramayan::523.verse_hindi: Kubera begot glorious Gandhamadana and Viswakarma begot a great monkey Nala.
ramayan::523.english_translation: Kubera begot the glorious monkey Gandhamadana, and Vishvakarma begot Nala, the great monkey.
ramayan::523.translation_literal: धनदस्य (of Kubera) / सुतः (son) / श्रीमान् (glorious) / वानरः (monkey) / गन्धमादनः (Gandhamadana) / विश्वकर्मा (Vishvakarma) / तु (and) / अजनयत् (begot) / नलम् (Nala) / नाम (named) / महाहरिम् (great monkey)
ramayan::523.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::523.essence: The epic widens by naming the powers behind its heroes.
ramayan::523.simple_meaning: Kubera and Vishvakarma are named as the fathers of two powerful monkeys, Gandhamadana and Nala.
ramayan::523.simple_insight: Even great beings are shown as part of a larger family and order.
ramayan::523.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the origins of the monkey chiefs before the great alliance and war. This verse names Gandhamadana and Nala as sons of Kubera and Vishvakarma, adding grandeur to the gathering force without yet making a teaching of it.
ramayan::523.insight: It functions as background, not instruction, building the scale of the coming alliance.

ramayan::524.verse_sanskrit: पावकस्य सुतश्श्रीमान् नीलोऽग्निसदृशप्रभ: । तेजसा यशसा वीर्यादत्यरिच्यत वानरान् । । 11712 । ।
ramayan::524.verse_hindi: Neela, the prosperous son of Agni the firegod who equalled him in glow surpassed other monkeys in energy, renown and prowess.
ramayan::524.english_translation: Neela, the prosperous son of Agni, who shone like fire, surpassed the other monkeys in energy, renown, and prowess.
ramayan::524.translation_literal: पावकस्य (of Agni) / सुतः (son) / श्रीमान् (prosperous, splendid) / नीलः (Neela) / अग्निसदृशप्रभः (with fire-like radiance) / तेजसा (in energy) / यशसा (in fame) / वीर्यात् (in prowess) / अत्यरिच्यत (surpassed) / वानरान् (the monkeys)
ramayan::524.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::524.essence: Neela's brilliance is presented as inherited and unmistakable.
ramayan::524.simple_meaning: Neela is described as a radiant, powerful monkey who outshines the others in strength, fame, and valor.
ramayan::524.simple_insight: Some beings stand out not by rank, but by the force they naturally carry.
ramayan::524.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the origins and qualities of the great monkey leaders. After naming Tara, Gandhamadana, and Nala, he introduces Neela as the shining son of Agni, marked by extraordinary brilliance and strength. It is a descriptive detail in a larger catalog, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::524.insight: It highlights lineage and innate excellence as part of the epic's world-building, not as a lesson to apply.

ramayan::525.verse_sanskrit: रूपद्रविणसम्पन्नावश्विनौ रूपसम्मतौ । मैन्दं च द्विविदं चैव जनयामासतुस्स्वयम् । । 11713 । ।
ramayan::525.verse_hindi: Aswini devatas, endowed with wealth and beauty, procreated Mainda and Dwivida who were highly esteemed for their beauty.
ramayan::525.english_translation: The twin Asvins, rich in beauty and themselves admired for their form, begot Mainda and Dwivida.
ramayan::525.translation_literal: रूपद्रविणसम्पन्नौ (endowed with beauty and wealth) / अश्विनौ (the two Asvins) / रूपसम्मतौ (approved for beauty) / मैन्दं (Mainda) / च (and) / द्विविदं (Dwivida) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / जनयामासतुः (begot) / स्वयम् (themselves)
ramayan::525.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::525.essence: Two more warriors are introduced through their divine lineage.
ramayan::525.simple_meaning: The Asvins are named as the parents of Mainda and Dwivida, two monkeys noted for their beauty.
ramayan::525.simple_insight: It is a genealogy verse, showing where two heroic monkey brothers came from.
ramayan::525.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the origins of the monkey leaders gathered for the coming war. After naming Nala and Nila, he now identifies Mainda and Dwivida as sons of the radiant Asvins. The verse adds lineage, not teaching.
ramayan::525.modern_relevance: A family tree at the end of a program can matter for the story, but it does not change your day. This verse simply places two more figures in the epic map.
ramayan::525.insight: It gives background, not guidance: a quiet inventory of who belongs to the alliance.

ramayan::526.verse_sanskrit: वरुणो जनयामास सुषेणं वानरर्षभम् । शरभं जनयामास पर्जन्यस्तु महाबलम् । । 11714 । ।
ramayan::526.verse_hindi: Varuna begot the monkey warrior Sushena and Parjanya, Sarabha of great strength.
ramayan::526.english_translation: Varuna begot the monkey warrior Sushena, and Parjanya begot Sarabha of great strength.
ramayan::526.translation_literal: वरुणो (Varuna) / जनयामास (begot) / सुषेणं (Sushena) / वानरर्षभम् (bull among monkeys) / शरभं (Sarabha) / जनयामास (begot) / पर्जन्यस्तु (and Parjanya) / महाबलम् (of great strength)
ramayan::526.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::526.essence: The gathering force is being named, one ally at a time.
ramayan::526.simple_meaning: Varuna is said to be the father of Sushena, and Parjanya is said to be the father of Sarabha, both powerful monkey warriors.
ramayan::526.simple_insight: The verse is introducing more allied warriors, not giving a teaching.
ramayan::526.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the origins of the monkey warriors who will join the great campaign. After naming Neela and the Ashvins' sons, he continues with Sushena and Sarabha, showing the scale and variety of the forces gathering before the war.
ramayan::526.insight: It adds names and lineage to the army before the larger action unfolds.

ramayan::527.verse_hindi: Vayu, the windgod, begot a son named Hanuman, mighty and graceful, having a body as hard as a diamond and speed equal to Garudas.
ramayan::527.english_translation: Vayu, the windgod, begot a son named Hanuman, mighty and graceful, having a body as hard as a diamond and speed equal to Garudas.
ramayan::527.translation_literal: मारुतस्य (of Vayu) / आत्मजः (son) / श्रीमान् (graceful, illustrious) / हनुमान् (Hanuman) / नाम (named) / वीर्यवान् (mighty) / वज्रसंहनन-उपेतः (endowed with a diamond-hard body) / वैनतेय-समः (equal to Garuda) / जवे (in speed)
ramayan::527.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::527.essence: Hanuman is introduced as strength made swift.
ramayan::527.simple_meaning: Hanuman is introduced as Vayu's son, powerful, beautiful, hard-bodied, and incredibly fast.
ramayan::527.simple_insight: Great deeds often begin with a clear introduction to the strength behind them.
ramayan::527.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the extraordinary beings born to the gods. After naming other vanara heroes, he introduces Hanuman as Vayu's son: beautiful, immensely strong, and swift as Garuda. It is a character introduction, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::527.modern_relevance: A team bio opens with the person everyone will depend on in the hardest moment. Before the action begins, the story quietly tells you who can carry the weight.
ramayan::527.insight: It sets up Hanuman as the force whose power and speed will make impossible missions possible.

ramayan::528.verse_sanskrit: ते सृष्टा बहुसाहस्रा दशग्रीववधे रता: । अप्रमेयबला वीरा विक्रान्ता: कामरूपिण: । । 11716 । ।
ramayan::528.verse_hindi: Thousands of warriors possessing immeasurable strength and courage and capable of assuming any form at will were created to kill Ravana.
ramayan::528.english_translation: Thousands of warriors of immeasurable strength and courage, able to take any form at will, were created to kill Ravana.
ramayan::528.translation_literal: ते (those) / सृष्टा (created) / बहुसाहस्रा (many-thousand) / दशग्रीववधे (for the killing of Ravana) / रता: (intent on) / अप्रमेयबला (of immeasurable strength) / वीरा: (heroes) / विक्रान्ता: (valiant) / कामरूपिण: (shape-shifters)
ramayan::528.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::528.essence: Ravana's defeat was already being assembled in advance.
ramayan::528.simple_meaning: A vast host of powerful shape-shifting warriors was created for Ravana's defeat.
ramayan::528.simple_insight: The scale of the coming war is being assembled before your eyes.
ramayan::528.detailed_meaning: The poem shifts from naming Hanuman to describing the larger forces gathered against Ravana. These are not ordinary fighters but countless shape-shifting warriors, built for one purpose: his defeat. The verse adds size and momentum to the war scene.
ramayan::528.modern_relevance: A project suddenly becomes bigger than one person can handle. You realize the challenge needs a whole force, not a lone hero.
ramayan::528.insight: It frames Ravana's fall as a cosmic mobilization, not a random clash.

ramayan::529.verse_hindi: Endowed with bodies similar to the Meru and Mandara mountains and having  great strength, bears, monkeys, monkeys with cowtails quickly came into being.
ramayan::529.english_translation: Endowed with bodies like the Meru and Mandara mountains, and possessing great strength, bears, monkeys, and monkeys with cowtails quickly came into being.
ramayan::529.translation_literal: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा (resembling Meru and Mandara) / वपुष्मन्तः (bodied, embodied beings) / महाबलाः (of great strength) / ऋक्षवानरगोपुच्छाः (bears, monkeys, and cow-tailed monkeys) / क्षिप्रमेव (very quickly) / अभिजज्ञिरे (came into being)
ramayan::529.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::529.essence: Powerful allies emerged quickly for the coming war.
ramayan::529.simple_meaning: Bears and monkeys with mountain-like bodies and great strength appeared quickly.
ramayan::529.simple_insight: The scene is about the sudden creation of powerful allies, not a teaching you need to apply directly.
ramayan::529.detailed_meaning: The gods have already been gathering forces for the coming struggle with Ravana. Here, Valmiki describes the swift appearance of bears and monkey warriors, each with immense bodies and strength. It is part of the larger preparation, not a standalone lesson.
ramayan::529.insight: It serves as scene-setting for the birth of an army, not a separate principle.

ramayan::530.verse_sanskrit: यस्य देवस्य यद्रूपं वेषो यश्च पराक्रम: । अजायत समस्तेन तस्य तस्य सुत: पृथक् । । 11718 । ।
ramayan::530.verse_hindi: The sons of devatas retained characteristics like beauty, form and prowess of their procreator (gods).
ramayan::530.english_translation: The sons of the devas each arose with the form, appearance, and prowess of the deity who fathered them.
ramayan::530.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / देवस्य (of the radiant being) / यत्-रूपम् (whatever form) / वेषः (appearance) / यः (which) / च (and) / पराक्रमः (prowess) / अजायत (was born) / समस्तेन (with all of that) / तस्य तस्य (of each one) / सुतः (son) / पृथक् (separately)
ramayan::530.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::530.essence: Each son carried the force and form of his father.
ramayan::530.simple_meaning: Each son of a radiant being was born carrying the same appearance, form, and strength as the father.
ramayan::530.simple_insight: Power and character often echo through what gives rise to them.
ramayan::530.detailed_meaning: In the gods' own making of allies against Ravana, Valmiki pauses to explain the kind of beings being born. These sons are not random warriors; each one inherits the visible mark and force of the one who fathered him.
ramayan::530.modern_relevance: A child picks up a parent's habits before anyone has named them. The shape of a family often shows up in the way someone stands, speaks, or fights.
ramayan::530.insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuals to the qualities passed down through origin and lineage.

ramayan::531.verse_sanskrit: गोलाङ्गूलीषु चोत्पन्ना: केचित्सम्मतविक्रमा: । ऋक्षीषु च तथा जाता वानरा: किन्नरीषु च । । 11719 । ।
ramayan::531.verse_hindi: Some monkeys with acknowledged, valour were born to female monkeys with tails         Similarly some other monkeys were born to female bears and female kinnaras.
ramayan::531.english_translation: Some monkeys of acknowledged valor were born to female monkeys with tails. Similarly, some others were born to female bears and female kinnaras.
ramayan::531.translation_literal: गोलाङ्गूलीषु (to female monkeys with tails) / च (and) / उत्पन्नाः (were born) / केचित् (some) / सम्मत-विक्रमाḥ (of acknowledged valor) / ऋक्षीषु (to female bears) / च (and) / तथा (likewise) / जाताḥ (were born) / वानराः (monkeys) / किन्नरीषु (to female kinnaras) / च (and)
ramayan::531.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::531.essence: A genealogy of forest beings is being laid out before the action begins.
ramayan::531.simple_meaning: Different kinds of monkey warriors are described as being born from female monkeys, bears, and kinnaras.
ramayan::531.simple_insight: It is a lineage listing, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::531.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the origins of the many beings who will later join the search for Sita and the war against Ravana. This verse continues the catalog of their births and forms, adding more detail to the larger genealogy.
ramayan::531.insight: It supplies background for the assembled forces, not a standalone lesson.

ramayan::532.verse_sanskrit: देवा महर्षिगन्धर्वास्तार्क्ष्या यक्षा यशस्विन: । नागा: किम्पुरुषाश्चैव सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा: । । 11720 । । बहवो जनयामासुर्हृष्टास्तत्र सहस्रश: । वानरान्सुमहाकायान्सर्वान्वै वनचारिण: । । 11721 । । अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु तथा विद्याधरीषु च । नागकन्यासु च तथा गन्धर्वीणां तनूषु च । । 11722 । ।
ramayan::532.verse_hindi: The devatas, rishis, gandharvas, garudas, yakshas, kimpurushas, siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas and many others were immensely pleased. Thousands of gigantic monkeys wandering in forests were procreated from principal apsarasas  vidhyadaris, nagas, and  gandharvas.
ramayan::532.english_translation: The devatas, rishis, gandharvas, garudas, yakshas, kimpurushas, siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas, and many others were immensely pleased. Thousands of gigantic monkeys wandering in forests were born from principal apsaras, vidyadharis, nagas, and gandharvas.
ramayan::532.translation_literal: देवा: (radiant beings) / महर्षिगन्धर्वा: (great sages and gandharvas) / तार्क्ष्या: (garudas) / यक्षा: (yakshas) / यशस्विन: (glorious ones) / नागा: (serpents) / किम्पुरुषा: (kimpurushas) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा: (siddhas, vidyadharas, and uragas) / बहव: (many) / जनयामासु: (caused to be born) / हृष्टा: (delighted) / तत्र (there) / सहस्रश: (in thousands) / वानरान् (monkeys) / सुमहाकायान् (very large-bodied) / सर्वान् (all) / वै (indeed) / वनचारिण: (forest wanderers) / अप्सरस्सु (from apsaras) / च (and) / मुख्यासु (principal) / तथा (also) / विद्याधरीषु (from vidyadharis) / च (and) / नागकन्यासु (from serpent maidens) / च (and) / तथा (also) / गन्धर्वीणां (of gandharvi women) / तनूषु (from bodies) / च (and)
ramayan::532.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::532.essence: The vanara race begins as a wondrous, shared creation of many realms.
ramayan::532.simple_meaning: Many celestial beings rejoice as thousands of huge forest-dwelling monkeys are born from celestial women and other nonhuman mothers.
ramayan::532.simple_insight: Great events can begin from hidden, unusual origins.
ramayan::532.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the extraordinary birth of the vanara race. Celestial beings rejoice as different groups and beings bring forth these huge forest-dwelling monkeys. The verse adds mythic background, not a teaching or turning point.
ramayan::532.insight: It supplies the epic's origin story for the vanaras, showing their mixed and wondrous lineage.

ramayan::533.verse_sanskrit: कामरूपबलोपेता यथाकामं विचारिण: । सिंहशार्दूलसदृशा दर्पेण च बलेन च । । 11723 । ।
ramayan::533.verse_hindi: They were endowed with the powers to assume any form at will. They possessed enormous strength and power to freely wander in forests. They were like lions and tigers in pride and prowess.
ramayan::533.english_translation: They were endowed with the power to assume any form at will. They roamed freely wherever they wished, and in pride and strength they were like lions and tigers.
ramayan::533.translation_literal: कामरूप-बल-उपेता: (endowed with the power to assume any form at will) / यथाकामम् (as desired, freely) / विचारिण: (roaming, wandering) / सिंह-शार्दूल-सदृशा: (like lions and tigers) / दर्पेण (in pride) / च (and) / बलेन (in strength) / च (and)
ramayan::533.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::533.essence: Powerful beings are being gathered, not yet a lesson being taught.
ramayan::533.simple_meaning: These beings could change form at will, roam freely, and were fierce in pride and strength.
ramayan::533.simple_insight: It paints a world of wild power, not ordinary creatures.
ramayan::533.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the many beings born across the world as the monkey hosts take shape. This verse adds their abilities and ferocity, building the scale of the coming alliance rather than making a separate teaching.
ramayan::533.modern_relevance: A crowded room can suddenly feel charged when one person walks in with total confidence. That kind of presence changes the whole atmosphere before a word is spoken.
ramayan::533.insight: It shifts attention from individual names to the collective force being assembled.

ramayan::534.verse_sanskrit: शिलाप्रहरणास्सर्वे सर्वे पादपयोधिन: । । 11724 । । नखदंष्ट्रायुधास्सर्वे सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकोविदा: ।
ramayan::534.verse_hindi: They all could strike with rocks, use nails and teeth and trees as weapons. They were skilled in the use of all kinds of weapons.
ramayan::534.english_translation: They all could strike with rocks, use nails and teeth and trees as weapons. They were skilled in the use of all kinds of weapons.
ramayan::534.translation_literal: शिला (rocks) / प्रहरणाः (weapons for striking) / सर्वे (all) / सर्वे (all) / पादप (trees) / योधिनः (fighters) / नख (nails) / दंष्ट्रा (teeth) / आयुधाः (weapons) / सर्वे (all) / सर्वैः (all) / अस्त्र (weapons) / कोविदाः (skilled)
ramayan::534.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::534.essence: Even ordinary things become dangerous in the hands of the fiercely armed.
ramayan::534.simple_meaning: These beings could fight with rocks, trees, nails, and teeth. They were also trained in every kind of weapon.
ramayan::534.simple_insight: Power can be raw and wild, yet still fully capable of organized force.
ramayan::534.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the extraordinary beings born in this world: not just strong, but adaptable in combat, able to turn anything around them into a weapon. The verse builds their terrifying capability before the story moves on to their scale and speed.
ramayan::534.modern_relevance: A crowd turns ugly in seconds, and suddenly chairs, bottles, even bare hands become weapons. This verse captures how quickly force can become improvised and total.
ramayan::534.insight: It shifts attention from polished tools to the dangerous versatility of raw aggression.

ramayan::535.verse_hindi: They could shake mountains and uproot deeprooted trees. With their speed they could cause disturbance to Samudra, the lord of the rivers.
ramayan::535.english_translation: They could shake mountains and uproot deep-rooted trees. With their speed they could disturb the ocean, lord of the rivers.
ramayan::535.translation_literal: विचालयेयुः (they could shake) / शैलेन्द्रान् (mountain-kings, mountains) / भेदयेयुः (they could split, break apart) / स्थिरान् (firm, fixed) / द्रुमान् (trees) / क्षोभयेयुः (they could agitate, disturb) / च (and) / वेगेन (with speed) / समुद्रम् (the ocean) / सरिताम् (of rivers) / पतिम् (lord)
ramayan::535.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::535.essence: Their strength is so great that even nature cannot stand still.
ramayan::535.simple_meaning: They had such strength and speed that even mountains, trees, and the ocean could be shaken by them.
ramayan::535.simple_insight: It leaves no doubt about their power: nothing vast or firm can resist them.
ramayan::535.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the extraordinary strength of the monkey warriors before the search and battle intensify. This verse is one link in a chain of images showing how immense, wild, and physically impossible their capabilities are.
ramayan::535.modern_relevance: A room full of people underestimates you until the moment your work lands with force. Some abilities are so large they only become visible when pressure arrives.
ramayan::535.insight: It builds the scale of the army by showing power through impossible physical feats.

ramayan::536.verse_sanskrit: दारयेयु: क्षितिं पद्भ्यामाप्लवेयुर्महार्णवम् । नभ:स्थलम् विशेयुश्च गृह्णीयुरपि तोयदान् । । 11726 । ।
ramayan::536.verse_hindi: They could cause cleavage to this earth with their feet, cross the mighty ocean with one leap and enter the sky and even seize the clouds.
ramayan::536.english_translation: They could cleave the earth with their feet, leap across the mighty ocean, enter the sky, and even seize the clouds.
ramayan::536.translation_literal: दारयेयुः (they could cleave) / क्षितिम् (the earth) / पद्भ्याम् (with their feet) / आप्लवेयुः (they could leap across) / महार्णवम् (the great ocean) / नभःस्थलम् (the sky-space) / विशेयुः (they could enter) / च (and) / गृह्णीयुः (they could seize) / अपि (even) / तोयदान् (the clouds)
ramayan::536.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::536.essence: Their strength is so vast it seems to break the limits of nature.
ramayan::536.simple_meaning: These beings are described as so powerful and swift that they could crack the ground, jump over the ocean, move through the sky, and seize clouds.
ramayan::536.simple_insight: The passage builds a sense of overwhelming force and impossible physical power.
ramayan::536.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is still describing the extraordinary strength of the vanara hosts. After saying they can hurl rocks, use trees as weapons, and shake mountains, he adds more feats to show their scale before the war begins.
ramayan::536.modern_relevance: A team arrives already tested, already hardened, already able to do what others would call impossible. The point is not swagger — it is capacity built before the crisis.
ramayan::536.insight: It shifts attention from individual heroics to the sheer scale of the force being assembled.

ramayan::537.verse_sanskrit: गृह्णीयुरपि मातङ्गान्मत्तान्प्रव्रजतो वने । नर्दमानाश्च नादेन पातयेयुर्विहङ्गमान् । । 11727 । ।
ramayan::537.verse_hindi: They could capture wild elephants sojourning in the forest and make the flying birds drop down screaming.
ramayan::537.english_translation: They could capture wild elephants roaming in the forest and make flying birds fall down with their roar.
ramayan::537.translation_literal: गृह्णीयुः (they could seize) / अपि (even) / मातङ्गान् (elephants) / मत्तान् (intoxicated, wild) / प्रव्रजतो (roaming) / वने (in the forest) / नर्दमानाः (roaring) / च (and) / नादेन (with sound) / पातयेयुः (they could make fall) / विहङ्गमान् (birds)
ramayan::537.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::537.essence: Their strength is so immense that even forest giants and birds cannot resist it.
ramayan::537.simple_meaning: These beings are so powerful that they can seize wild elephants in the forest and bring down birds with their roar.
ramayan::537.simple_insight: Some forces are described by the scale of what they can overwhelm.
ramayan::537.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the extraordinary strength of the monkey hosts. After saying they can shake mountains, cross the ocean, and reach the sky, he adds this image of raw force: even wild elephants and birds cannot withstand them.
ramayan::537.modern_relevance: A room full of noise can make everyone go quiet before the meeting even starts. Some people or situations carry that same overwhelming force.
ramayan::537.insight: It reinforces the sheer physical power of the vanara army before the war begins.

ramayan::538.verse_sanskrit: ईदृशानां प्रसूतानि हरीणां कामरूपिणाम् । शतं शतसहस्राणि यूथपानां महात्मनाम् । । 11728 । ।
ramayan::538.verse_hindi: A crore of monkeys capable of assuming any form at will, great monkeys and commanders of monkey forces were created.
ramayan::538.english_translation: A crore of monkeys capable of assuming any form at will, great monkeys and commanders of monkey forces were created.
ramayan::538.translation_literal: ईदृशानाम् (of such) / प्रसूतानि (born) / हरीणाम् (of monkeys) / कामरूपिणाम् (shape-shifting) / शतम् (a hundred) / शतसहस्राणि (hundred-thousands) / यूथपानाम् (of troop-leaders) / महात्मनाम् (great-souled)
ramayan::538.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::538.essence: Power is multiplying fast, and the force is becoming vast.
ramayan::538.simple_meaning: Countless shape-shifting monkeys and their great leaders came into being.
ramayan::538.simple_insight: The army is not ordinary. It is vast, strange, and beyond normal limits.
ramayan::538.detailed_meaning: The verse continues the catalogue of extraordinary monkey forces. After describing their power in the previous lines, Valmiki now names their sheer number: countless shape-shifting troops and noble commanders, all part of the growing alliance that will later serve Rama.
ramayan::538.modern_relevance: A team suddenly grows beyond what you expected, and the scale itself changes the mood in the room. What was once a plan now feels like a force.
ramayan::538.insight: It adds scale to the gathering army, showing that strength here is both magical and collective.

ramayan::539.verse_sanskrit: ते प्रधानेषु यूथेषु हरीणां हरियूथपा: । बभूवुर्यूथपश्रेष्ठा वीरांश्चाजनयन् हरीन् । । 11729 । ।
ramayan::539.verse_hindi: Those monkey commanders created heroic monkeys among the chief monkey clans who later proved the best among clanleaders.
ramayan::539.english_translation: Those monkey commanders created heroic monkeys among the chief monkey clans, and those monkeys became the best clan leaders.
ramayan::539.translation_literal: ते (those) / प्रधानेषु (among the chief) / यूथेषु (among the clans) / हरीणां (of monkeys) / हरियूथपा: (monkey commanders) / बभूवुः (became) / यूथपश्रेष्ठा: (best among clan leaders) / वीरान् (heroic) / च (and) / अजनयन् (they produced) / हरीन् (monkeys)
ramayan::539.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::539.essence: Power spreads when leaders create more leaders.
ramayan::539.simple_meaning: The monkey commanders produced strong, heroic monkeys within the main clans, and those offspring became leading clan chiefs.
ramayan::539.simple_insight: Great forces grow through capable leaders who create more capable leaders.
ramayan::539.detailed_meaning: Vali and Sugriva’s world is being described in terms of vast monkey armies. This verse is not a teaching moment; it continues the catalogue of their strength, showing how chief leaders generated new heroic leaders within the clans.
ramayan::539.modern_relevance: A team grows when experienced people raise others who can lead, not just follow. Strong organizations multiply leadership instead of hoarding it.
ramayan::539.insight: It shifts attention from raw numbers to how leadership reproduces itself across a group.

ramayan::540.verse_sanskrit: अन्ये ऋक्षवत: प्रस्थानवतस्थु स्सहस्रश: । अन्ये नानाविधान्शैलान्भेजिरे काननानि च । । 11730 । ।
ramayan::540.verse_hindi: Thousands of monkeys dwelt on the plateaus on the top of mountains abounding in bears. Some others inhabited various hills and forests.
ramayan::540.english_translation: Thousands of monkeys dwelt on the plateaus on the top of mountains abounding in bears. Some others inhabited various hills and forests.
ramayan::540.translation_literal: अन्ये (others) / ऋक्षवत: (with bears) / प्रस्थानवतस्थुः (stood on plateaus) / सहस्रशः (in thousands) / अन्ये (others) / नानाविधान् (various) / शैलान् (mountains) / भेJिरे (occupied) / काननानि (forests) / च (and)
ramayan::540.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::540.essence: The army is being spread across the landscape, not yet put to use.
ramayan::540.simple_meaning: The monkey forces spread out across mountains, plateaus, hills, and forests in great numbers.
ramayan::540.simple_insight: Not every line carries a lesson; some simply widen the world around it.
ramayan::540.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the vast monkey host after its leaders have been formed. The forces now spread across mountain plateaus, hills, and forests, showing the scale of Sugriva's army before the alliance with Rama is fully revealed.
ramayan::540.modern_relevance: A crowd fills the station, some waiting on the platform, others spilling into the concourse and stairwells. The point is not advice — it is scale, movement, and a world preparing for what comes next.
ramayan::540.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to scene, letting the story breathe before the next turn.

ramayan::541.verse_sanskrit: सूर्यपुत्रं च सुग्रीवं शक्रपुत्रं च वालिनम् । भ्रातरावुपतस्थुस्ते सर्व एव हरीश्वरा: । । 11731 । । नलं नीलं हनूमन्तमन्यांश्च हरियूथपान् । 3
ramayan::541.verse_hindi: All those leaders, Nala, Neela, Hanuman and others dwelt near those two brothers Sugriva, the offspring of Surya and Vali, the son of Indra.
ramayan::541.english_translation: All the monkey chiefs gathered around the two brothers Sugriva, the son of Surya, and Vali, the son of Indra. Nala, Neela, Hanuman, and the other commanders were among them.
ramayan::541.translation_literal: सूर्यपुत्रम् (the son of Surya) / च (and) / सुग्रीवम् (Sugriva) / शक्रपुत्रम् (the son of Indra) / च (and) / वालिनम् (Vali) / भ्रातरौ (the two brothers) / उपतस्थुः (gathered around) / ते (those) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / हरीश्वराः (monkey lords) / नलम् (Nala) / नीलम् (Neela) / हनूमन्तम् (Hanuman) / अन्यान् (others) / च (and) / हरियूथपान् (monkey commanders)
ramayan::541.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::541.essence: The commanders gather before the real action begins.
ramayan::541.simple_meaning: The monkey leaders gathered around Sugriva and Vali, and many commanders like Nala, Neela, and Hanuman were there too.
ramayan::541.simple_insight: Great efforts often begin with people gathering around shared leadership.
ramayan::541.detailed_meaning: After the monkey clans are organized, the chief leaders assemble around Sugriva and Vali, with Nala, Neela, Hanuman, and others among them. The verse is setting the scene for the alliance, not making a teaching of its own.
ramayan::541.modern_relevance: A team crowds around two founders before a risky launch, waiting for orders, roles, and direction. The verse simply shows the gathering before action begins.
ramayan::541.insight: It frames the alliance as a coordinated force, ready for the next move.

ramayan::542.verse_hindi: Endowed with the might of Garuda and wellversed in warfare, all of them  moving around tormented ferouious lions, tigers and mighty serpents .
ramayan::542.english_translation: Endowed with the might of Garuda and skilled in warfare, they roamed about, overpowering lions, tigers, and great serpents in pride.
ramayan::542.translation_literal: ते (they) / तार्क्ष्य-बल-संपन्नाः (endowed with Garuda's strength) / सर्वे (all) / युद्ध-विशारदाः (skilled in warfare) / विचरन्तः (roaming about) / अर्दयन् (crushed, tormented) / दर्पात् (in pride) / सिंह-व्‍याघ्र-महोरगान् (lions, tigers, and great serpents)
ramayan::542.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::542.essence: Their strength is shown first in the wild, before the war even begins.
ramayan::542.simple_meaning: The monkey warriors were extraordinarily powerful and skilled in battle. They roamed through the wilderness, overpowering fierce animals with pride and strength.
ramayan::542.simple_insight: Raw strength becomes visible when it moves through the world without fear.
ramayan::542.detailed_meaning: The allied monkey forces have gathered in the mountain regions under Sugriva and Vali. Valmiki pauses to show their nature: these are not ordinary beings, but fierce warriors whose strength lets them dominate wild creatures before the larger conflict begins.
ramayan::542.modern_relevance: A group of friends charges onto a rough hiking trail, joking as they go, and the wild terrain feels smaller around them. This verse captures that untamed confidence before a bigger test arrives.
ramayan::542.insight: It builds the image of a force already hardened for war, setting up the alliance’s military power.

ramayan::543.verse_sanskrit: तांश्च सर्वान्महाबाहुर्वाली विपुलविक्रम: । जुगोप भुजवीर्येण ऋक्षगोपुच्छवानरान् । । 11733 । ।
ramayan::543.verse_hindi: Mighty armed leader Vali endowed  with immense prowess  protected, with his strong arms all those bears, gopuchhas(cowtailed) and monkeys.
ramayan::543.english_translation: Mighty-armed Vali, endowed with immense prowess, protected all those bears, cow-tailed beings, and monkeys with the strength of his arms.
ramayan::543.translation_literal: तांश्च (those also) / सर्वान् (all) / महाबाहुः (mighty-armed) / वाली (Vali) / विपुलविक्रमः (of vast prowess) / जुगोप (protected) / भुजवीर्येण (with arm-strength) / ऋक्षगोपुच्छवानरान् (bears, cow-tailed beings, and monkeys)
ramayan::543.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::543.essence: His strength was great enough to protect, not merely overpower.
ramayan::543.simple_meaning: Vali used his great strength to protect the bears, cow-tailed beings, and monkeys around him.
ramayan::543.simple_insight: Power can be used to shelter others, not only to dominate them.
ramayan::543.detailed_meaning: In Kishkindha, the monkey leaders and their followers are being described as a powerful social world around Vali and Sugriva. This line is not a teaching on its own; it is a supporting detail showing Vali's physical dominance and protective reach among the forest beings.
ramayan::543.modern_relevance: A strong manager can either intimidate the whole team or make everyone feel safe. This verse only shows the second kind of strength: power that protects.
ramayan::543.insight: It frames strength as guardianship, not just force.

ramayan::544.verse_hindi: Born in many forms  wih various characteristics (relating to the body and tribe), they pervaded this earth with its mountains, forests and seas.
ramayan::544.english_translation: With those brave ones, the earth — with its mountains, forests, and oceans — was filled by many kinds, marked by many forms and signs.
ramayan::544.translation_literal: तैः (with those) / इयम् (this) / पृथिवी (earth) / शूरैः (with brave ones) / स-पर्वत-वन-अर्णवा (with mountains, forests, and oceans) / कीर्णा (scattered / filled) / विविध-संस्थानैः (with various forms) / नाना-व्यञ्जन-लक्षणैः (with many distinguishing marks and signs)
ramayan::544.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::544.essence: A whole world can be filled by one force.
ramayan::544.simple_meaning: The earth is covered with brave beings of many forms and kinds, spread across mountains, forests, and seas.
ramayan::544.simple_insight: The world is vast, and courage appears in many forms.
ramayan::544.detailed_meaning: Vali’s warriors and their kin are being described as a mighty presence spread across the whole world. This is not a teaching verse; it enlarges the scene by showing how far their strength and variety extend.
ramayan::544.insight: It widens the frame from individual fighters to a world filled with varied strength.

ramayan::545.verse_hindi: In order to assist Rama, this earth was filled with commanders of those who led the monkey forces resembling masses of clouds and mountains. They loan endowed with immense strength and fearful forms and countenances.
ramayan::545.english_translation: In order to assist Rama, the earth was filled with monkey commanders, vast as clouds and mountain peaks, with immense strength and terrible forms.
ramayan::545.translation_literal: तैः (by them) / मेघबृन्द (mass of clouds) / अचलकूट (mountain peaks) / कल्पैः (resembling) / महाबलैः (mighty) / वानरयूथपालैः (by monkey troop-leaders) / बभूव (became) / भूः (the earth) / भीमशरीररूपैः (with terrible bodies and forms) / समावृता (covered) / रामसहायहेतोः (for the purpose of helping Rama)
ramayan::545.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::545.essence: Rama's cause drew an army of strength to the earth.
ramayan::545.simple_meaning: The earth was crowded with powerful monkey leaders, all gathered to help Rama.
ramayan::545.simple_insight: Great help can arrive in overwhelming numbers when a worthy cause calls.
ramayan::545.detailed_meaning: Valmiki describes the gathering of the monkey commanders: huge, fierce, and immensely strong beings filling the earth because Rama needs allies. It is a scene of mobilisation, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::545.modern_relevance: A crisis hits, and suddenly the room fills with people who can actually help. No speeches, no hesitation — just capable hands showing up when the work is bigger than one person.
ramayan::545.insight: It shifts attention from one hero to the force that gathers around a righteous mission.

ramayan::546.verse_sanskrit: निर्वृत्ते तु क्रतौ तस्मिन्हयमेधे महात्मन: । प्रतिगृह्य सुरा भागान्प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम् । । 1181 । ।
ramayan::546.verse_hindi: Completed by the magnanimous king (Dasaratha). The aswamedha and putreshti sacrifices, the devatas received their share of havis and returned to their respective  abodes.
ramayan::546.english_translation: When that great sacrifice was completed, the devas received their portions and returned to their own abodes.
ramayan::546.translation_literal: निर्वृत्ते (having been completed) / तु (indeed) / क्रतौ (sacrifice) / तस्मिन् (that) / हयमेधे (horse-sacrifice) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / सुराः (the devas) / भागान् (shares) / प्रतिजग्मुः (returned) / यथागतम् (as they had come)
ramayan::546.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::546.essence: The sacrifice ends, and the world quietly returns to normal.
ramayan::546.simple_meaning: The horse sacrifice ended, the gods received their offerings, and they went back to their own realms.
ramayan::546.simple_insight: Some moments simply complete their course. What was offered has been received.
ramayan::546.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha's great horse sacrifice has finished. The offerings have been given, the deities have taken their shares, and the sacred gathering dissolves as everyone returns to where they came from. The verse marks the closing of the ritual, not its lesson.
ramayan::546.modern_relevance: The ceremony is over, the room is empty, and the last guest has left. What mattered was not the noise of the event, but that it was carried through completely.
ramayan::546.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of ritual to its completion and closure.

ramayan::547.verse_sanskrit: समाप्तदीक्षानियम: पत्नीगणसमन्वित: । प्रविवेश पुरीं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहन: । । 1182 । ।
ramayan::547.verse_hindi: Having completed the prescribed vows (in respect of aswamedha), king Dasaratha together with his queens returned to the city of Ayodhya accompanied by his attendants, army and chariots.
ramayan::547.english_translation: Having completed the prescribed vows for the horse sacrifice, King Dasharatha returned to the city of Ayodhya with his queens, attendants, army, and chariots.
ramayan::547.translation_literal: समाप्तदीक्षानियम: (having completed the vows and restraints) / पत्नीगणसमन्वित: (together with the group of queens) / प्रविवेश (entered) / पुरीं (the city) / राजा (the king) / सभृत्यबलवाहन: (with attendants, army, and vehicles)
ramayan::547.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::547.essence: Duty ends, and the king returns home.
ramayan::547.simple_meaning: Dasharatha returns to Ayodhya after finishing the rituals of the horse sacrifice, bringing his queens and full royal retinue with him.
ramayan::547.simple_insight: A completed duty brings closure, and life moves back into motion.
ramayan::547.detailed_meaning: The horse sacrifice has ended. Dasharatha, accompanied by his queens, servants, army, and chariots, enters Ayodhya again. The verse simply marks the king's return after the rite, setting up the next turn in the palace story.
ramayan::547.modern_relevance: You finish the ceremony, the deadline, the long obligation — and only then do you finally drive home with everyone silent in the car.
ramayan::547.insight: It marks the shift from sacred task to ordinary life, showing that completion has its own moment of return.

ramayan::548.verse_sanskrit: यथार्हं पूजितास्तेन राज्ञा वै पृथिवीश्वरा: । मुदिता: प्रययुर्देशान्प्रणम्य मुनिपुङ्गवम् । । 1183 । ।
ramayan::548.verse_hindi: Having been honoured by the king (Dasaratha) in a be fitting manner, the highly pleased lords of the earth (kings) made obeisance to the best of sages (Vasishta) and returned to their own countries.
ramayan::548.english_translation: Having been honoured by King Dasharatha in due form, the pleased kings bowed to the great sage Vasishta and returned to their own lands.
ramayan::548.translation_literal: यथार्हम् (as was fitting) / पूजिताः (honoured) / तेन (by him) / राज्ञा (by the king) / वै (indeed) / पृथिवीश्वराः (lords of the earth) / मुदिताः (pleased) / प्रययुः (departed) / देशान् (to their own lands) / प्रणम्य (bowing) / मुनिपुङ्गवम् (to the best of sages)
ramayan::548.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::548.essence: Proper respect lets people part in peace.
ramayan::548.simple_meaning: Dasharatha respectfully honours the visiting kings, and they leave for home after bowing to Vasishta.
ramayan::548.simple_insight: Respect leaves no bitterness behind; even formal gatherings can end in goodwill.
ramayan::548.detailed_meaning: After the sacrifices at Ayodhya, the visiting kings are properly honoured by Dasharatha. They bow to Vasishta, feel pleased, and return to their own kingdoms. The verse simply marks the dignified close of the royal gathering.
ramayan::548.modern_relevance: After a wedding, conference, or family ceremony, the guests finally head home with full hearts and tired smiles. The event is over, but the respect shown there travels with them.
ramayan::548.insight: It shows how honour and courtesy can close an occasion cleanly, leaving everyone content.

ramayan::549.verse_sanskrit: श्रीमतां गच्छतां तेषां स्वपुराणि पुरात्तत: । बलानि राज्ञां शुभ्राणि प्रहृष्टानि चकाशिरे । । 1184 । ।
ramayan::549.verse_hindi: When the army of the kings left the city (Ayodhya) for their own, the armed forces shone bright and cheerfl.
ramayan::549.english_translation: When the kings departed for their own cities, their bright armies shone with joy.
ramayan::549.translation_literal: श्रीमतां (of the prosperous / illustrious ones) / गच्छतां (going) / तेषां (of them) / स्वपुराणि (to their own cities) / पुरात्तत: (from the city) / बलानि (armies) / राज्ञां (of the kings) / शुभ्राणि (bright / shining) / प्रहृष्टानि (delighted) / चकाशिरे (shone)
ramayan::549.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::549.essence: Departure can still carry the glow of honour.
ramayan::549.simple_meaning: The visiting kings leave Ayodhya, and their armies depart looking bright and cheerful.
ramayan::549.simple_insight: A good reception leaves even departing guests carrying warmth with them.
ramayan::549.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has finished the sacrificial rite and honoured the gathered rulers well. Now those kings are returning to their own cities, and their armies depart in good spirits. It is a brief scene of closure before Dasaratha himself re-enters Ayodhya.
ramayan::549.modern_relevance: After a wedding weekend ends and the guests pack their bags, the house feels different. Everyone leaves lighter because they were welcomed well, and the host's duty is not yet done.
ramayan::549.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to aftermath: how people leave matters as much as how they arrive.

ramayan::550.verse_sanskrit: गतेषु पृथिवीशेषु राजा दशरथस्तदा । प्रविवेश पुरीं श्रीमान् पुरस्कृत्य द्विजोत्तमान् । । 1185 । ।
ramayan::550.verse_hindi: After the departure of the rulers, the exalted king Dasaratha preceded by the foremost of brahmins entered the city (of Ayodhya).
ramayan::550.english_translation: After the departure of the rulers, the exalted king Dasaratha, preceded by the foremost of brahmins, entered the city of Ayodhya.
ramayan::550.translation_literal: गतेषु (having departed) / पृथिवीशेषु (the remaining rulers of the earth) / राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / तदा (then) / प्रविवेश (entered) / पुरीम् (the city) / श्रीमान् (the glorious one) / पुरस्कृत्य (preceded by) / द्विजोत्तमान् (the foremost of brahmins)
ramayan::550.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::550.essence: The courtly gathering ends, and the king returns to the city.
ramayan::550.simple_meaning: After the visiting kings leave, Dasaratha returns to Ayodhya in royal procession with respected brahmins leading the way.
ramayan::550.simple_insight: A formal moment of departure and return, not a teaching. The scene simply resets the story’s movement.
ramayan::550.detailed_meaning: The guest kings have been honoured and sent away. Dasaratha, still surrounded by brahmins and ceremony, re-enters Ayodhya. The verse marks the close of one public event and the transition to the next.
ramayan::550.insight: It marks a change of scene, not a moral instruction.

ramayan::551.verse_sanskrit: शान्तया प्रययौ सार्धमृश्यशृङ्गस्सुपूजित: । अन्वीयमानो राज्ञाऽथ सानुयात्रेण धीमता । । 1186 । ।
ramayan::551.verse_hindi: Having been duly honoured by king Dasaratha, sage Rsyasringa with his wife Santa  accompanied by the wise king Romapada and his followers set out for his country.
ramayan::551.english_translation: Having been duly honoured by king Dasaratha, sage Rsyasringa with his wife Santa accompanied by the wise king Romapada and his followers set out for his country.
ramayan::551.translation_literal: शान्तया (with Śānta) / प्रययौ (departed) / सार्धम् (together with) / ऋश्यशृङ्गः (Rsyasringa) / सुपूजितः (duly honoured) / राज्ञा (by the king) / अथ (then) / सानुयात्रेण (with attendants / followers) / धीमता (by the wise)
ramayan::551.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::551.essence: The guests depart, and Dasaratha is left with his hope.
ramayan::551.simple_meaning: Rsyasringa, honored by Dasaratha, leaves with Śānta and the king of Romapada, along with their retinue.
ramayan::551.simple_insight: A formal visit ends, and everyone returns home.
ramayan::551.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has welcomed the sage Rsyasringa and his company with honor. Now the guests depart for their own kingdom, escorted by King Romapada and his followers. The scene is a quiet transition before Dasaratha turns inward toward his long-awaited wish.
ramayan::551.modern_relevance: After the guests leave and the house goes quiet, you finally turn to the one hope you've been carrying in private.
ramayan::551.insight: It marks the end of the visit and clears the stage for Dasaratha's next resolve.

ramayan::552.verse_sanskrit: एवं विसृज्य तान्सर्वान्राजा सम्पूर्णमानस: । उवास सुखितस्तत्र पुत्रोत्पत्तिं विचिन्तयन् । । 1187 । ।
ramayan::552.verse_hindi: When they (guests) all departed in this manner, Dasaratha with his desire fulfilled, his thought centred on begetting sons lived happily.
ramayan::552.english_translation: When they all departed in this manner, Dasaratha, his wish fulfilled, lived there happily, thinking only of begetting sons.
ramayan::552.translation_literal: एवं (in this manner) / विसृज्य (having sent away) / तान् सर्वान् (all those) / राजा (the king) / सम्पूर्ण-मानसः (with mind fulfilled) / उवास (dwelt) / सुखितः (happy) / तत्र (there) / पुत्र-उत्पत्तिम् (the birth of sons) / विचिन्तयन् (thinking about)
ramayan::552.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::552.essence: Fulfilled desire still leaves you waiting for the result.
ramayan::552.simple_meaning: Dasaratha sent the guests away, felt satisfied, and stayed there happily, focused on having sons.
ramayan::552.simple_insight: A long-awaited wish can quiet the mind, even before it is fully complete.
ramayan::552.detailed_meaning: The sacrifice has just been arranged, the honored guests have left, and Dasaratha remains behind in Ayodhya. His heart is full because the ritual he hoped would lead to sons is now underway. This verse simply pauses on his relieved waiting.
ramayan::552.modern_relevance: You finally hit send after months of planning, then sit in the quiet after everyone leaves. The relief is real, but your mind is already on what comes next.
ramayan::552.insight: It shifts attention from the public moment to the private waiting that follows fulfilled effort.
