ramayan::553.verse_sanskrit: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ऋतूनां षट्समत्ययु: । ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ । । 1188 । । नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु पञ्चसु । ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पताविन्दुना सह । । 1189 । । प्रोद्यमाने जगन्नाथं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् । कौसल्याऽजनयद्रामं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् । । 11810 । । विष्णोरर्धं महाभागं पुत्रमैक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम् ।
ramayan::553.verse_hindi: Six seasons (one year) passed after the completion of the sacrifice. In the twelfth month of Chaitra on the ninth day (of the bright fortnight), with Aditi as presiding deity when the star Punarvasu was in the ascendent and the five planets Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus, were exalted in their own house in karkata lagna, when Brihaspati was in conjunction with the Moon, Kausalya gave birth to a son: a facet of Visnu, Lord of the entire universe who received obeisance from all the worlds and was adorned with all auspicious signs, the venerable one  to perpetuate the Ikshvaku race.
ramayan::553.english_translation: Six seasons passed after the sacrifice was completed. Then, in the twelfth month, on the ninth day of Chaitra, under the star ruled by Aditi, with the five planets exalted in their own signs, in Cancer rising, and Jupiter conjoined with the Moon, Kausalya gave birth to Rama, a son who was a part of Vishnu, the delight of the Ikshvaku line, endowed with all auspicious marks, and honored by all worlds.
ramayan::553.translation_literal: ततः (then) / यज्ञे (the sacrifice) / समाप्ते (having been completed) / तु (indeed) / ऋतूनाम् (of the seasons) / षट् (six) / समत्ययुः (passed) / ततः (then) / च (and) / द्वादशे (in the twelfth) / मासे (month) / चैत्रे (in Chaitra) / नावमिके (on the ninth day) / तिथौ (on the lunar day) / नक्षत्रे (in the constellation) / अदितिदैवत्ये (ruled by Aditi) / स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु (placed in exaltation) / पञ्चसु (five) / ग्रहेषु (planets) / कर्कटे (in Cancer) / लग्ने (in the ascendant) / वाक्पतौ (with Brihaspati) / इन्दुना (with the Moon) / सह (together) / प्रोद्यमाने (rising) / जगन्नाथम् (Lord of the world) / सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् (honored by all worlds) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / अजनयत् (gave birth) / रामम् (to Rama) / सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् (endowed with all auspicious marks) / विष्णोः (of Vishnu) / अर्धम् (a part) / महाभागम् (the highly glorious one) / पुत्रम् (son) / ऐक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम् (the increaser of the Ikshvaku line)
ramayan::553.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::553.essence: A long wait ends in a birth that changes a kingdom.
ramayan::553.simple_meaning: After the sacrifice, the long wait ended. Kausalya gave birth to Rama under an auspicious alignment of time and stars, and he was marked as a glorious son of Vishnu.
ramayan::553.simple_insight: Some arrivals feel larger than a birth. They feel like a whole order of life turning.
ramayan::553.detailed_meaning: The sacrifice has ended, months have passed, and the court of Ayodhya is still waiting for its answer. Then, under a sky described in perfect auspicious detail, Kausalya gives birth to Rama — the child who will carry the future of the Ikshvaku line.
ramayan::553.modern_relevance: You wait through months of uncertainty after a hard-won beginning, and then one quiet morning changes everything. Some moments are not just personal news; they feel like history finally moving.
ramayan::553.insight: It shifts attention from the waiting to the significance of what finally arrives.

ramayan::554.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या शुशुभे तेन पुत्रेणामिततेजसा । । 11811 । । यथा वरेण देवानामदितिर्वज्रपाणिना ।
ramayan::554.verse_hindi: Kausalya glowed with the undiminished lustre of her son, just as Aditi with  her son Indra, the foremost among the gods and  the wielder of thunder.
ramayan::554.english_translation: Kausalya glowed with the undiminished lustre of her son, just as Aditi with her son Indra, the foremost among the gods and the wielder of thunder.
ramayan::554.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kausalya) / शुशुभे (shone, glowed) / तेन (with that) / पुत्रेण (with son) / अमिततेजसा (of immeasurable brilliance) / यथा (as) / वरेण (with the boon-given) / देवानाम् (of the radiant beings) / अदितिः (Aditi) / वज्रपाणिना (with the thunderbolt-holder)
ramayan::554.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::554.essence: Greatness makes a mother radiant too.
ramayan::554.simple_meaning: Kausalya shines with the brilliance of her son, just as Aditi shines through Indra. The verse simply compares a mother’s glory to her extraordinary child.
ramayan::554.simple_insight: A child’s greatness can make a mother radiant with pride.
ramayan::554.detailed_meaning: Rama has just been born in Ayodhya after the long sacrifice. Valmiki pauses on Kausalya, showing how her joy is not private alone: her son’s brilliance makes her shine, just as Aditi is glorified by Indra.
ramayan::554.modern_relevance: You watch your child walk onstage, heart pounding, and suddenly your own face lights up. Their strength, talent, or courage feels like it has reached back and touched you.
ramayan::554.insight: It shifts attention from the birth itself to the shared glory between parent and child.

ramayan::555.verse_sanskrit: भरतो नाम कैकेय्यां जज्ञे सत्यपराक्रम: । । 11812 । । साक्षाद्विष्णोश्चतुर्भागस्सर्वैस्समुदितो गुणै: ।
ramayan::555.verse_hindi: As an incarnation of the  fourth part of Visnu, imbued with all virtues, and armed with truth Bharata was born to Kaikeyi.
ramayan::555.english_translation: Bharata, truthful and mighty in valor, was born to Kaikeyi as a partial incarnation of Vishnu, endowed with all virtues.
ramayan::555.translation_literal: भरतः (Bharata) / नाम (by name) / कैकेय्याम् (to Kaikeyi) / जज्ञे (was born) / सत्यपराक्रमः (truthful and mighty in valor) / साक्षात् (directly) / विष्णोः (of Vishnu) / चतुर्भागः (a fourth part) / सर्वैः (with all) / समुदितः (endowed) / गुणैः (with virtues)
ramayan::555.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::555.essence: Bharata enters the world already marked by truth and completeness.
ramayan::555.simple_meaning: Bharata is introduced as a man of truth and courage, born with complete virtue and marked as a partial divine incarnation.
ramayan::555.simple_insight: Greatness can arrive quietly, before anyone has seen a single deed.
ramayan::555.detailed_meaning: After the sacrifice and the birth of Rama, the poem turns to Bharata. Valmiki does not introduce him as a mere prince, but as someone already filled with truth and virtue, with a divine portion behind his human life.
ramayan::555.modern_relevance: A child is born into a family already carrying expectations, gifts, and burdens no one can yet name. Some people seem to arrive with a steadiness that others spend years trying to build.
ramayan::555.insight: It frames Bharata as inherently aligned with truth, not shaped by later achievement.

ramayan::556.verse_sanskrit: अथ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ सुमित्राऽजनयत्सुतौ । । 11813 । । वीरौ सर्वास्त्रकुशलौ विष्णोरर्धसमन्वितौ ।
ramayan::556.verse_hindi: Sumitra gave birth to Lakshmana and Satrughna who were heroic, skilled in the use of all weapons and endowed with the facets of Visnu.
ramayan::556.english_translation: Then Sumitra gave birth to Lakshmana and Shatrughna, heroic, skilled in all weapons, and endowed with a half of Vishnu.
ramayan::556.translation_literal: अथ (then) / लक्ष्मण-शत्रुघ्नौ (Lakshmana and Shatrughna) / सुमित्रा (Sumitra) / अजनयत् (gave birth) / सुतौ (the two sons) / वीरौ (heroic) / सर्व-अस्त्र-कुशलौ (skilled in all weapons) / विष्णोः (of Vishnu) / अर्ध-समन्वितौ (endowed with a half / portion)
ramayan::556.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::556.essence: Some people enter life already carrying the force to protect others.
ramayan::556.simple_meaning: Sumitra gives birth to Lakshmana and Shatrughna, and the verse describes them as heroic, weapon-skilled, and marked by Vishnu’s presence.
ramayan::556.simple_insight: Greatness can be born quietly, before the world ever sees it.
ramayan::556.detailed_meaning: The births of Rama’s brothers are being described one by one. After Bharata, this verse turns to Sumitra’s sons, Lakshmana and Shatrughna, and marks them as heroic protectors with exceptional martial skill. It is part of the larger royal genealogy, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::556.modern_relevance: A family gathers around a newborn and everyone is already trying to guess who this child will become. This verse holds that same hush: some lives arrive carrying strength before they can speak.
ramayan::556.insight: It frames character as something present from the beginning, not only built later.

ramayan::557.verse_sanskrit: पुष्ये जातस्तु भरतो मीनलग्ने प्रसन्नधी: । । 11814 । । सार्पे जातौ च सौमित्री कुलीरेऽभ्युदिते रवौ ।
ramayan::557.verse_hindi: Bharata endowed with pure intellect was born in meena lagna when pushya was in the ascendant. Lakshmana and Satrughna were born in karkata lagna with the star aslesha .
ramayan::557.english_translation: Bharata, endowed with pure intellect, was born under Pushya in Meena lagna. Lakshmana and Satrughna were born under Aslesha in Karkata lagna, with the sun risen.
ramayan::557.translation_literal: पुष्ये (under Pushya) / जातः (was born) / तु (indeed) / भरतः (Bharata) / मीनलग्ने (in Meena lagna) / प्रसन्नधीः (pure-minded) / सार्पे (under Aslesha) / जातौ (were born) / च (and) / सौमित्री (the sons of Sumitra) / कुलीरे (in Karkata) / अभ्युदिते (having risen) / रवौ (the sun)
ramayan::557.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::557.essence: Birth details matter here more than interpretation.
ramayan::557.simple_meaning: Bharata, Lakshmana, and Satrughna are described by the stars and signs under which they were born.
ramayan::557.simple_insight: Some verses simply mark a sacred arrival, not a lesson to apply.
ramayan::557.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the auspicious birth details of Dasharatha’s sons. Bharata’s birth under Pushya and the twins’ birth under Aslesha completes the family portrait begun in the previous verse, before the poem moves on to their qualities and lineage.
ramayan::557.modern_relevance: A family keeps the baby announcement card, the horoscope, the exact time, the name of the star. This verse lives in that register: a careful record of arrival, not a teaching.
ramayan::557.insight: It asks you to notice how epic poetry can pause for lineage and omens before the story moves on.

ramayan::558.verse_sanskrit: राज्ञ: पुत्रा महात्मानश्चत्वारो जज्ञिरे पृथक् । । 11815 । । गुणवन्तोऽनुरूपाश्च रुच्या प्रोष्ठपदोपमा: ।
ramayan::558.verse_hindi: Four worthy sons were successively born to the noble king (Dasaratha), endowed with all virtuous, resembling purvabhadra and uttarabhadra  stars in brightness.
ramayan::558.english_translation: Four worthy sons were successively born to the noble king Dasharatha, virtuous and radiant like the bright stars of the season.
ramayan::558.translation_literal: राज्ञः (of the king) / पुत्राः (sons) / महात्मानः (great-souled, noble) / चत्वारः (four) / जज्ञिरे (were born) / पृथक् (separately, one by one) / गुणवन्तः (possessing virtues) / अनुरूपाः च (and fitting, worthy) / रुच्या (in radiance) / प्रोष्ठपदोपमाः (like the Proshthapada stars)
ramayan::558.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::558.essence: Four remarkable sons are born to a king whose house is about to change forever.
ramayan::558.simple_meaning: Dasharatha had four noble sons, each born separately and each marked by virtue and brilliance.
ramayan::558.simple_insight: Great lives often begin quietly, before anyone knows what they will become.
ramayan::558.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharatha's house is blessed with four sons born one after another: Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Satrughna. The verse pauses to mark their excellence and radiance, but it is still part of the larger birth sequence, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::558.modern_relevance: A family photo is taken after years of waiting, and the room feels suddenly larger than before. Something important has arrived, but its meaning will only unfold over time.
ramayan::558.insight: It frames the brothers as a destined royal line, preparing the reader for the story's central relationships.

ramayan::559.verse_sanskrit: जगु: कलं च गन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणा: । । 11816 । । देवदुन्दुभयो नेदु: पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता । उत्सवश्च महानासीदयोध्यायां जनाकुल: । । 11817 । ।
ramayan::559.verse_hindi: The gandharvas sang melodiously. Groups of apsaras danced. Celestial kettledrums were sounded. Flowers were showered from the sky. Men througed to Ayodhya to witness the festivities.
ramayan::559.english_translation: The gandharvas sang melodiously. Groups of apsaras danced. Celestial kettledrums sounded. Flowers fell from the sky. Ayodhya was filled with a great festival and crowds of people.
ramayan::559.translation_literal: जगु: (sang) / कलं (sweetly) / च (and) / गन्धर्वा: (gandharvas) / ननृतु: (danced) / च (and) / अप्सरोगणा: (groups of apsaras) / देवदुन्दुभय: (celestial kettledrums) / नेदु: (sounded) / पुष्पवृष्टि: (shower of flowers) / च (and) / खात् (from the sky) / च्युता (fallen) / उत्सव: (festival) / च (and) / महान् (great) / आसीत् (was) / अयोध्यायाम् (in Ayodhya) / जनाकुल: (crowded with people)
ramayan::559.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::559.essence: Joy so full it overflows into the sky.
ramayan::559.simple_meaning: Ayodhya erupts in celebration: heavenly singers, dancers, drums, and flowers mark the birth of Dasaratha’s sons, while people gather everywhere to rejoice.
ramayan::559.simple_insight: Some moments are too joyful to stay private; the whole world seems to join in.
ramayan::559.detailed_meaning: After the births of Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, Ayodhya turns into a living festival. Even the heavens seem to respond, with music, dancers, drums, and flowers, while the city fills with people swept up in the joy.
ramayan::559.modern_relevance: A hospital waiting room finally breaks into tears of relief when the baby cries. The news is bigger than one family now — joy spills outward and everyone nearby feels it.
ramayan::559.insight: It marks a shared celebration rather than a private event, showing how great joy spreads through a whole community.

ramayan::560.verse_sanskrit: रथ्याश्च जनसम्बाधा नटनर्तकसङ्कुला: । गायनैश्च विराविण्यो वादनैश्च तथाऽपरै: । । 11818 । ।
ramayan::560.verse_hindi: The highways were crowded with men, thronged by actors and dancers. The voices of singers, performers on different instruments, eulogists and genealogists reverberated.
ramayan::560.english_translation: The highways were crowded with men, thronged by actors and dancers. The voices of singers, performers on different instruments, eulogists and genealogists reverberated.
ramayan::560.translation_literal: रथ्याः (highways) / च (and) / जनसम्बाधाः (crowded with people) / नटनर्तकसङ्कुलाः (filled with actors and dancers) / गायनैः (with singers) / च (and) / विराविण्यः (resounding) / वादनैः (with instrumental performers) / च (and) / तथा (thus) / अपरैः (with others)
ramayan::560.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::560.essence: Public joy filled every street after the royal birth.
ramayan::560.simple_meaning: The streets were packed with people, performers, singers, and praise-singers as the city celebrated.
ramayan::560.simple_insight: Joy can spill into public life and turn the whole city into a shared celebration.
ramayan::560.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha's city is overflowing with celebration after the birth of his sons. Streets are packed, performers fill the air with sound, and public joy becomes visible everywhere. This verse adds texture to the festival, not a new teaching.
ramayan::560.modern_relevance: You walk out of a wedding hall into a street still humming with music, strangers smiling for no reason you need to explain. The whole place seems to breathe relief.
ramayan::560.insight: It shows how a great joy changes the atmosphere of an entire city.

ramayan::561.verse_sanskrit: प्रदेयांश्च ददौ राजा सूतमागधवन्दिनाम् । ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ वित्तं गोधनानि सहस्रश: । । 11819 । ।
ramayan::561.verse_hindi: The king distributed deserving gifts to priests, euologists and genealogists. He gave
ramayan::561.english_translation: The king gave fitting gifts to the bards, minstrels, and genealogists. He also gave wealth and thousands of cows to the priests.
ramayan::561.translation_literal: प्रदेयांश्च (worthy of gifts) / ददौ (gave) / राजा (the king) / सूत-मागध-वन्दिनाम् (to bards, minstrels, and praise-singers) / ब्राह्मणेभ्यः (to the priests) / ददौ (gave) / वित्तम् (wealth) / गोधनानि (cattle wealth) / सहस्रशः (in thousands)
ramayan::561.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::561.essence: Joy in Ayodhya turns into generosity toward everyone who helped.
ramayan::561.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha rewards the people involved in the celebration and gives generous gifts to the priests and others.
ramayan::561.simple_insight: A great occasion is also measured by how generously it honours everyone who serves it.
ramayan::561.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is alive with celebration after Rama’s birth. The king is not thinking of himself; he is distributing gifts to the singers, praise-poets, and priests who have made the ceremony complete. It is a detail inside the larger joy of the naming rites.
ramayan::561.modern_relevance: After a family ceremony, you make sure the helpers, hosts, and elders are thanked properly. Small acts of generosity reveal whether joy is real or only performed.
ramayan::561.insight: It shows that celebration becomes complete only when gratitude is shared outward.

ramayan::562.verse_sanskrit: अतीत्यैकादशाहं तु नामकर्म तथाऽकरोत् । ज्येष्ठं रामं महात्मानं भरतं कैकयीसुतम् । । 11820 । । सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणमिति शत्रुघ्नमपरं तथा । वसिष्ठ: परमप्रीतो नामानि कृतवान् तदा । । 11821 । ।
ramayan::562.verse_hindi: After a lapse of eleven days, the naming ceremony was performed. Highly delighted preceptor Vasishta named Kausalyas son Rama, Kaikeyis son Bharata, one son of Sumitra, Lakshmana and the other Satrughna.
ramayan::562.english_translation: After eleven days, the naming ceremony was performed. The greatly delighted priest Vasishta then gave names to Kausalya's son Rama, Kaikeyi's son Bharata, Sumitra's son Lakshmana, and the other, Shatrughna.
ramayan::562.translation_literal: अतीत्य (after passing) / एकादशाहं (eleven days) / तु (then) / नामकर्म (naming ceremony) / तथाऽकरोत् (thus performed) / ज्येष्ठं (eldest) / रामं (Rama) / महात्मानं (great-souled) / भरतं (Bharata) / कैकयीसुतम् (Kaikeyi's son) / सौमित्रिं (Sumitra's son) / लक्ष्मणमिति (as Lakshmana) / शत्रुघ्नमपरं (the other Shatrughna) / तथा (also) / वसिष्ठ: (Vasishta) / परमप्रीतो (greatly pleased) / नामानि (names) / कृतवान् (made/gave) / तदा (then)
ramayan::562.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::562.essence: The boys receive their names, and their long story begins.
ramayan::562.simple_meaning: After eleven days, Vasishta named the four boys Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna.
ramayan::562.simple_insight: Some moments are important because they quietly mark the beginning of a whole life.
ramayan::562.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the birth celebrations continue, the priest Vasishta performs the naming ceremony for Dasharatha's four sons. This verse simply records the formal moment when each child receives his name, setting the stage for the larger royal story ahead.
ramayan::562.modern_relevance: A family gathers around a newborn, and everyone waits for the name that will follow him for life. The ceremony matters, but the verse is mainly marking the moment before the story begins.
ramayan::562.insight: It shifts attention from event to sequence: first comes birth, then naming, then the life that follows.

ramayan::563.verse_sanskrit: ब्राह्मणान्भोजयामास पौराञ्जानपदानपि । अददाद्ब्रह्मणानां च रत्नौघममितं बहु । । 11822 । । तेषां जन्मक्रियादीनि सर्वकर्माण्यकारयत् ।
ramayan::563.verse_hindi: Brahmins as well as inhabitants of the city and rural areas were feasted. (Dasaratha) bestowed on brahmins unlimited and abundant jewels in charity. The rites at the time of birth and all other rites (associated with the newborn) were duly performed.
ramayan::563.english_translation: Brahmins, city people, and villagers were all feasted. Dasaratha gave the brahmins countless and abundant jewels in charity. All the birth rites and every other rite for the newborns were performed properly.
ramayan::563.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणान् (the brahmins) / भोजयामास (caused to be fed) / पौरान् (city dwellers) / जानपदान् (country people) / अपि (also) / अददात् (gave) / ब्रह्मणानाम् (to the brahmins) / च (and) / रत्नौघम् (a flood of jewels) / अमितम् (immeasurable) / बहु (much) / तेषाम् (of them) / जन्मक्रियादीनि (birth rites and such) / सर्वकर्माणि (all rites) / अकारयत् (had performed)
ramayan::563.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::563.essence: A king's joy becomes communal through generosity and proper rites.
ramayan::563.simple_meaning: Dasaratha celebrates the births with public feasting, generous gifts, and proper rituals for the newborns.
ramayan::563.simple_insight: Joy becomes complete when gratitude is shared openly and the right rites are honored.
ramayan::563.detailed_meaning: After the princes are born and named, Dasaratha turns the whole kingdom into a celebration. He feeds priests, townspeople, and villagers, gives lavish gifts, and ensures every newborn rite is completed. The verse supports the larger scene of royal joy, not a standalone teaching.
ramayan::563.modern_relevance: A family announces a long-awaited birth and the house fills with food, gifts, and relatives. The moment feels larger than private happiness because it is being honored properly.
ramayan::563.insight: It shows how public gratitude and ritual can mark a life event with dignity.

ramayan::564.verse_sanskrit: तेषां केतुरिव ज्येष्ठो रामो रतिकर: पितु: । । 11823 । । बभूव भूयो भूतानां स्वयम्भूरिव सम्मत: ।
ramayan::564.verse_hindi: Among them, Rama like the exalted flag, became dear to his father like Brahma he was highly respected by all living beings.
ramayan::564.english_translation: Among them, Rama, like an exalted flag, became dear to his father and was respected by all beings like Brahma.
ramayan::564.translation_literal: तेषाम् (among them) / केतुरिव (like a banner) / ज्येष्ठः (the eldest) / रामः (Rama) / रतिकरः (delighting) / पितुः (of his father) / बभूव (became) / भूयः (again / greatly) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / स्वयम्भूरिव (like Brahma) / सम्मतः (esteemed)
ramayan::564.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::564.essence: True greatness makes itself loved before it is explained.
ramayan::564.simple_meaning: Rama stood out among his brothers. He was beloved by his father and honoured by everyone around him.
ramayan::564.simple_insight: Quiet excellence draws love and respect without needing to announce itself.
ramayan::564.detailed_meaning: After the naming ceremony in Ayodhya, the poem pauses to show what kind of child Rama is becoming. He is the eldest, cherished by Dasharatha, and already held in esteem by all. The verse sets up the family’s harmony before the later fracture.
ramayan::564.modern_relevance: In a family gathering, one child quietly puts elders at ease while others compete for attention. Without trying to dominate the room, that person becomes the one everyone trusts.
ramayan::564.insight: It frames Rama as naturally admirable, preparing the reader for the larger story of his worth.

ramayan::565.verse_sanskrit: सर्वे वेदविदश्शूरास्सर्वे लोकहिते रता: । । 11824 । । सर्वे ज्ञानोपसम्पन्नास्सर्वे समुदिता गुणै: ।
ramayan::565.verse_hindi: All the sons (of Dasaratha) became wellversed in the Vedas. They were heroic, endowed with knowledge  and virtues and were devoted to the welfare of the people.
ramayan::565.english_translation: All the sons of Dasharatha were learned in the Vedas, heroic, devoted to the welfare of the people, rich in knowledge, and endowed with every virtue.
ramayan::565.translation_literal: सर्वे (all) / वेदविदः (knowers of the Vedas) / शूराः (heroic) / सर्वे (all) / लोकहिते (in the welfare of the people) / रताः (delighted, devoted) / सर्वे (all) / ज्ञानोपसम्पन्नाः (endowed with knowledge) / सर्वे (all) / समुदिताः (assembled, full) / गुणैः (with virtues)
ramayan::565.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::565.essence: Skill, courage, and virtue matter most when they serve others.
ramayan::565.simple_meaning: Dasharatha’s sons were not just princes. They were learned, brave, virtuous, and committed to the good of others.
ramayan::565.simple_insight: Real strength includes knowledge, courage, and concern for others.
ramayan::565.detailed_meaning: After Dasharatha’s generosity and the praise of Rama, Valmiki pauses to describe all four sons. They are trained, noble, and socially useful, setting up why Rama alone will soon stand out as the fullest embodiment of these qualities.
ramayan::565.modern_relevance: A parent watches children who have done everything right on paper — top grades, discipline, talent — yet the real test is whether they care about anyone beyond themselves.
ramayan::565.insight: It shifts attention from achievement alone to character that serves the wider world.

ramayan::566.verse_sanskrit: तेषामपि महातेजा रामस्सत्यपराक्रम: । । 11825 । । इष्टस्सर्वस्य लोकस्य शशाङ्क इव निर्मल: ।
ramayan::566.verse_hindi: Among them  the highly lustrous and truly mighty Rama was stainless (in character).
ramayan::566.english_translation: Among them, the highly lustrous and truly mighty Rama was stainless in character, dear to all the people like the spotless moon.
ramayan::566.translation_literal: तेषाम् (among them) / अपि (also) / महातेजा (highly lustrous) / रामः (Rama) / सत्यपराक्रमः (true in prowess) / इष्टः (dear) / सर्वस्य (of all) / लोकस्य (of the people) / शशाङ्कः इव (like the moon) / निर्मलः (spotless)
ramayan::566.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::566.essence: True greatness can be radiant without ever becoming stained.
ramayan::566.simple_meaning: Rama stands out among his brothers as radiant, truly brave, and morally pure. His greatness is not just power; it is clean character that wins everyone's affection.
ramayan::566.simple_insight: Real strength does not need corruption to prove itself.
ramayan::566.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha's sons are being described before the story's great fracture begins. After naming their learning and virtues, Valmiki singles out Rama: radiant, courageous, and untouched in character, loved by everyone like a clear moon in the night sky.
ramayan::566.modern_relevance: In a room where everyone is trying to look impressive, the person people trust most is usually the one who stays clean. Rama's shine came from character, not performance.
ramayan::566.insight: It shifts admiration from display to moral cleanliness and steady conduct.

ramayan::567.verse_sanskrit: गजस्कन्धेऽश्वपृष्ठे च रथचर्यासु सम्मत: । । 11826 । । धनुर्वेदे च निरत: पितृशुश्रूषणे रत: ।
ramayan::567.verse_hindi: Accepted as skilled in mounting elephants, riding horses, driving chariots and also in archery, he was always emgaged in the service of his parents.
ramayan::567.english_translation: He was skilled in riding elephants, horses, and chariots, expert in archery, and always devoted to serving his parents.
ramayan::567.translation_literal: गजस्कन्धे (on elephant-back) / अश्वपृष्ठे (on horseback) / च रथचर्यासु (and in chariot-driving) / सम्मत: (approved/skilled) / धनुर्वेदे (in archery) / च (and) / निरत: (engaged) / पितृशुश्रूषणे (in serving his parents) / रत: (devoted)
ramayan::567.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::567.essence: His strength was complete because it never left service behind.
ramayan::567.simple_meaning: Rama is trained in weapons, riding, and chariot-driving, but his real character shows in his steady service to his parents.
ramayan::567.simple_insight: Real excellence includes humility and care, not just talent.
ramayan::567.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing Rama before the exile begins: a prince admired for martial skill, yet never separated from filial service. The verse shows that his greatness is not only ability, but disciplined devotion to his parents.
ramayan::567.modern_relevance: You can be brilliant at your craft, fast on your feet, and still be measured by how you treat the people who shaped you.
ramayan::567.insight: It shifts success from raw ability to character expressed through care and obedience.

ramayan::568.verse_sanskrit: बाल्यात्प्रभृति सुस्निग्धो लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मिवर्धन: । । 11827 । । रामस्य लोकरामस्य भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य नित्यश: ।
ramayan::568.verse_hindi: Right from his very childhood Lakshmana, an enhancer of fortune, always remained very  attached to his eldest brother Rama, the delight of the world.
ramayan::568.english_translation: From childhood itself, Lakshmana, the enhancer of fortune, was always deeply attached to Rama, his elder brother and the delight of the world.
ramayan::568.translation_literal: बाल्यात् (from childhood) / प्रभृति (beginning) / सुस्निग्धः (deeply affectionate) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / लक्ष्मिवर्धनः (enhancer of fortune) / रामस्य (of Rama) / लोकरामस्य (of the delight of the world) / भ्रातुः (brother's) / ज्येष्ठस्य (elder) / नित्यशः (always)
ramayan::568.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::568.essence: Loyalty can become a person's defining strength before life even tests it.
ramayan::568.simple_meaning: Lakshmana's love for Rama was not recent or conditional. It had been steady since childhood and shaped his whole identity.
ramayan::568.simple_insight: Some bonds are not chosen late; they are lived so early they become part of who you are.
ramayan::568.detailed_meaning: Valmiki pauses to describe Lakshmana before the exile crisis fully unfolds. He is not just Rama's younger brother; from childhood onward, he has been unwaveringly devoted to Rama, the elder brother who holds the family's center.
ramayan::568.modern_relevance: You know the friend who has stood beside you since school, before ambition and image changed everything. That kind of loyalty is not a mood — it is a history you keep choosing.
ramayan::568.insight: It shifts attention from temporary affection to loyalty formed over time and proven by constancy.

ramayan::569.verse_sanskrit: सर्वप्रियकरस्तस्य रामस्यापि शरीरत: । । 11828 । । लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मिसम्पन्नो बहि:प्राण इवापर: ।
ramayan::569.verse_hindi: Lakshmana,  possessed of fortune, was the dearest to his brother than his own body. As though he was his life without.
ramayan::569.english_translation: Lakshmana, endowed with good fortune, was dear to Rama even more than his own body, like another life outside himself.
ramayan::569.translation_literal: सर्वप्रियकरः (most dear) / तस्य (to him) / रामस्य (of Rama) / अपि (even) / शरीरत: (than the body) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / लक्ष्मिसम्पन्नः (endowed with fortune) / बहिःप्राणः (life outside) / इव (like) / अपरः (another)
ramayan::569.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::569.essence: Some bonds are so close they feel like a second life.
ramayan::569.simple_meaning: Lakshmana was so close to Rama that he felt like another life outside Rama's own body.
ramayan::569.simple_insight: Real loyalty can feel less like company and more like breathing.
ramayan::569.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing Lakshmana's bond with Rama before the exile's full pain unfolds. He is not just a brother nearby; he is the one Rama cannot imagine without, the companion who feels like an extension of his own life.
ramayan::569.modern_relevance: You have one person whose absence changes the shape of your whole day. You don't just miss their company — you feel less complete without them.
ramayan::569.insight: It shifts love from sentiment to inseparable presence.

ramayan::570.verse_sanskrit: न च तेन विना निद्रां लभते पुरुषोत्तम: । । 11829 । । मृष्टमन्नमुपानीतमश्नाति न हि तं विना ।
ramayan::570.verse_hindi: Rama, the greatest among men would not sleep without Lakshmanas company. He would not partake even the choicest food minus to him.
ramayan::570.english_translation: Rama, the greatest among men, would not sleep without Lakshmana's company. He would not even eat the finest food without him.
ramayan::570.translation_literal: न च (not) / तेन विना (without him) / निद्राम् (sleep) / लभते (obtains) / पुरुषोत्तमः (the greatest among men) / मृष्ट-अन्नम् (fine food) / उपानीतम् (brought near) / अश्नाति (eats) / न हि (indeed not) / तम् विना (without him)
ramayan::570.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::570.essence: True closeness shows up in the smallest routines.
ramayan::570.simple_meaning: Rama is so close to Lakshmana that he cannot rest or enjoy food without him nearby.
ramayan::570.simple_insight: Deep loyalty changes even the smallest habits of life.
ramayan::570.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is not just a brother in the background; he is Rama's constant companion. Valmiki shows their bond through ordinary needs — sleep and food — to reveal how completely Rama depends on his presence.
ramayan::570.modern_relevance: You notice it most in the quiet routines: the empty seat at dinner, the missed goodnight message, the room that feels off when one person is absent.
ramayan::570.insight: It turns affection into something measurable in daily life: presence, not words, becomes the sign of love.

ramayan::571.verse_sanskrit: यदा हि हयमारूढो मृगयां याति राघव: । । 11830 । । तदैनं पृष्ठतोऽन्वेति सधनु: परिपालयन् ।
ramayan::571.verse_hindi: Whenever Raghava (Rama) went hunting into the forest, riding the horse, Lakshmana used to follow him holding bow and arrows (in his hand).
ramayan::571.english_translation: Whenever Rama rode out hunting into the forest, Lakshmana followed behind him, carrying bow and arrows and guarding him.
ramayan::571.translation_literal: यदा (whenever) / हि (indeed) / हयमारूढः (mounted on a horse) / मृगयाम् (to hunting) / याति (goes) / राघवः (Rama) / तदा (then) / एनम् (him) / पृष्ठतः (from behind) / अन्वेति (follows) / सधनुः (with bow) / परिपालयन् (guarding)
ramayan::571.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::571.essence: Real loyalty stays close and stays armed.
ramayan::571.simple_meaning: Lakshmana stayed close behind Rama on hunting trips, armed and ready to protect him.
ramayan::571.simple_insight: Love can look like vigilance, not just affection.
ramayan::571.detailed_meaning: The poem is describing the brothers' bond in practical terms. When Rama goes out hunting, Lakshmana does not stay back; he follows with bow in hand, always ready to guard him. The next verse extends the same pattern to Bharata and Shatrughna.
ramayan::571.modern_relevance: You walk your friend to the car after a late-night event, keys in hand, not because danger is certain but because care is active.
ramayan::571.insight: It shows devotion as protective presence, not passive feeling.

ramayan::572.verse_sanskrit: भरतस्यापि शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणावरजो हि स: । । 11831 । । प्राणै: प्रियतरो नित्यं तस्य चासीत्तथा प्रिय: ।
ramayan::572.verse_hindi: In a similar manner Satrughna, younger brother of Lakshmana, became dearer than his own life to Bharata. Similarly, Bharata also was dear to Satrughna.
ramayan::572.english_translation: In a similar manner Satrughna, younger brother of Lakshmana, became dearer than his own life to Bharata. Similarly, Bharata also was dear to Satrughna.
ramayan::572.translation_literal: भरतस्य (to Bharata) / अपि (also) / शत्रुघ्नः (Satrughna) / लक्ष्मण-अवरजः (younger brother of Lakshmana) / हि (indeed) / सः (he) / प्राणैः (than life) / प्रियतरो (dearer) / नित्यम् (always) / तस्य (to him) / च (and) / आसीत् (was) / तथा (similarly) / प्रियः (dear) /
ramayan::572.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::572.essence: Brotherly love here is reciprocal, total, and quietly central.
ramayan::572.simple_meaning: Bharata and Shatrughna love each other deeply, just as Rama and Lakshmana do. The verse is showing the brothers' mutual affection.
ramayan::572.simple_insight: Some bonds are so strong they become part of your identity.
ramayan::572.detailed_meaning: The poem pauses to show the four brothers as a single, bonded family. After describing Rama and Lakshmana, Valmiki adds Bharata and Shatrughna: each is dear to the other beyond ordinary affection. It strengthens the picture of Ayodhya's harmony before exile tears it apart.
ramayan::572.modern_relevance: You know that one sibling who still feels like home, no matter how long it's been. This verse captures that kind of mutual loyalty before life pulls people in different directions.
ramayan::572.insight: It shifts attention from individual character to the web of love holding the family together.

ramayan::573.verse_sanskrit: स चतुर्भिर्महाभागै:पुत्रैर्दशरथ: प्रियै: । । 11832 । । बभूव परमप्रीतो देवैरिव पितामह: ।
ramayan::573.verse_hindi: With his very fortunate sons, Dasaratha was highly pleased like Brahma was with the gods.
ramayan::573.english_translation: With his very fortunate sons, Dasaratha was highly pleased like Brahma was with the gods.
ramayan::573.translation_literal: स (he) / चतुर्भिः (with four) / महाभागैः (very fortunate) / पुत्रैः (with sons) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / प्रियैः (dear) / बभूव (became) / परमप्रीतः (greatly pleased) / देवैः (with the gods) / इव (like) / पितामहः (Brahma)
ramayan::573.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::573.essence: His happiness came from seeing all four sons flourish together.
ramayan::573.simple_meaning: Dasaratha felt deep joy because all four of his sons were noble and beloved, just as Brahma is pleased with the gods.
ramayan::573.simple_insight: A parent's happiness deepens when every child reflects virtue and promise.
ramayan::573.detailed_meaning: The four princes have grown into admired, gifted sons, and Dasaratha looks on with pride. This verse pauses the story to show the king's joy before the later crisis begins to unravel it.
ramayan::573.modern_relevance: You watch your children stand together, each carrying grace you hoped for but could not force. For one brief moment, your heart feels fully answered.
ramayan::573.insight: It shifts attention from royal power to the quiet joy of seeing children embody their upbringing.

ramayan::574.verse_sanskrit: ते यदा ज्ञानसम्पन्नास्सर्वैस्समुदिता गुणै: । । 11833 । । ह्रीमन्त: कीर्तिमन्तश्च सर्वज्ञा दीर्घदर्शिन: । तेषामेवं प्रभावानां सर्वेषां दीप्ततेजसाम् । । 11834 । । पिता दशरथो हृष्टो ब्रह्मा लोकाधिपो यथा ।
ramayan::574.verse_hindi: All his sons were enriched  with knowledge and endowed  with all virtues. They were modest, renowned, omniscient and farsighted. Dasaratha rejoiced at the sight of those glorious sons with such faculties and looked like Brahma, Lord of the worlds.
ramayan::574.english_translation: All his sons were enriched with knowledge and endowed with all virtues. They were modest, renowned, farsighted, and all-knowing. Dasaratha rejoiced at the sight of those glorious sons and looked like Brahma, lord of the worlds.
ramayan::574.translation_literal: ते (they) / यदा (when) / ज्ञानसम्पन्नाः (endowed with knowledge) / सर्वैः (with all) / समुदिताः (endowed) / गुणैः (with virtues) / ह्रीमन्तः (modest) / कीर्तिमन्तः (renowned) / च (and) / सर्वज्ञाः (all-knowing) / दीर्घदर्शिनः (far-seeing) / तेषाम् (of them) / एवम् (thus) / प्रभावानाम् (of the glorious) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / दीप्ततेजसाम् (of radiant splendour) / पिता (father) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / हृष्टः (rejoicing) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / लोकाधिपः (lord of the worlds) / यथा (like)
ramayan::574.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::574.essence: True royal greatness begins with virtue, and a father's joy comes from seeing it.
ramayan::574.simple_meaning: Dasharatha's sons are described as wise, virtuous, modest, famous, farsighted, and radiant. Their excellence fills their father with joy.
ramayan::574.simple_insight: A parent's happiness deepens when children grow into character, not just achievement.
ramayan::574.detailed_meaning: Valmiki pauses before the exile begins to describe Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna at their best: learned, disciplined, and shining with virtue. Dasharatha's joy is complete because his sons seem to embody the ideal royal household.
ramayan::574.modern_relevance: You watch your child speak with kindness, think clearly, and carry themselves well. The pride you feel is not about status — it's about seeing your values become real in another person.
ramayan::574.insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the deeper joy of seeing character mature.

ramayan::575.verse_sanskrit: ते चापि मनुजव्याघ्रा वैदिकाध्ययने रता: । । 11835 । । पितृशुश्रूषणरता धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठिता: ।
ramayan::575.verse_hindi: They (like) tigers among men, were fond of the study of the Vedas  and were always
ramayan::575.english_translation: They, too, like tigers among men, delighted in studying the Vedas, served their father, and were firmly skilled in the art of archery.
ramayan::575.translation_literal: ते (they) / चापि (and also) / मनुजव्याघ्रा: (tigers among men) / वैदिकाध्ययने (in Vedic study) / रता: (delighted, devoted) / पितृशुश्रूषणरता: (devoted to serving their father) / धनुर्वेदे (in the science of archery) / च (and) / निष्ठिता: (firmly established, skilled)
ramayan::575.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::575.essence: Greatness here comes from study, service, and mastery.
ramayan::575.simple_meaning: Rama and his brothers were disciplined, respectful, and well trained. They studied sacred learning, served their father, and mastered archery.
ramayan::575.simple_insight: Real strength grows from learning, service, and steady training.
ramayan::575.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharatha’s sons are being described before the marriage discussion begins. They are not just princely in birth; they are formed by study, obedience, and martial skill. This verse builds the case for why they are worthy heirs.
ramayan::575.modern_relevance: A teenager wakes before dawn for practice, then helps at home without being asked. The verse values that combination: learning, service, and skill, not talent alone.
ramayan::575.insight: It shifts attention from status to formation: character, duty, and competence make a worthy person.

ramayan::576.verse_sanskrit: अथ राजा दशरथस्तेषां दारक्रियां प्रति । । 11836 । । चिन्तयामास धर्मात्मा सोपाध्यायस्सबान्धव: ।
ramayan::576.verse_hindi: Then the virtuous king Dasaratha deliberated with his priests and kinsmen about the marriage of his sons.
ramayan::576.english_translation: Then the virtuous king Dasharatha deliberated with his priests and kinsmen about the marriage of his sons.
ramayan::576.translation_literal: अथ (then) / राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasharatha) / तेषाम् (of those) / दारक्रियां (marriage arrangements) / प्रति (regarding) / चिन्तयामास (deliberated) / धर्मात्मा (virtuous in nature) / सोपाध्यायः (with his priests) / सबान्धवः (with his kinsmen)
ramayan::576.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::576.essence: Wise rulers pause and consult before shaping a family’s future.
ramayan::576.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha sat with his priests and relatives to think through his sons’ marriages.
ramayan::576.simple_insight: Big family decisions are made with counsel, not impulse.
ramayan::576.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharatha has raised four accomplished sons and now turns to their future marriages. He consults priests and kinsmen as a responsible king, while the next verse prepares the arrival of Vishvamitra and a far greater turning point.
ramayan::576.modern_relevance: You’re sitting at the dining table, weighing a major family decision and trying not to rush it. The wisest next step is often to gather the right people and think before you move.
ramayan::576.insight: It shows leadership as consultation: important choices should be weighed with trusted counsel.

ramayan::577.verse_sanskrit: तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य मन्त्रिमध्ये महात्मन: । । 11837 । । अभ्यगच्छन्महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: ।
ramayan::577.verse_hindi: While the nobleminded king was thus deliberating in the midst of his counsellors,  there arrived the effulgent ascetic Viswamitra.
ramayan::577.english_translation: While the nobleminded king was thus deliberating in the midst of his counsellors, there arrived the effulgent ascetic Viswamitra.
ramayan::577.translation_literal: तस्य (of him) / चिन्तयमानस्य (while thinking, deliberating) / मन्त्रिमध्ये (in the midst of counsellors) / महात्मनः (of the noble-minded one) / अभ्यगच्छत् (arrived) / महातेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (the great ascetic)
ramayan::577.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::577.essence: A quiet arrival can overturn the plans already in motion.
ramayan::577.simple_meaning: As King Dasharatha was discussing matters with his advisers, Viswamitra arrived.
ramayan::577.simple_insight: Some turning points enter quietly, right in the middle of ordinary planning.
ramayan::577.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha is in council, still weighing what to do about his sons' marriages, when Viswamitra appears. The scene shifts from family planning to a larger destiny, but this verse itself only marks the arrival that changes everything.
ramayan::577.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of planning something ordinary when a message, call, or visitor changes the whole day.
ramayan::577.insight: It trains attention to notice how one arrival can redirect an entire life.

ramayan::578.verse_sanskrit: स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी द्वाराध्यक्षानुवाच ह । । 11838 । । शीघ्रमाख्यात मां प्राप्तं कौशिकं गाधिनस्सुतम् ।
ramayan::578.verse_hindi: Desirous of seeing the king (Dasaratha) he accosted the doorkeepers, saying Inform the king quickly about the arrival of Viswamitra, the son of Gadhi born in the line of
ramayan::578.english_translation: Desirous of seeing the king, he said to the doorkeepers: 'Quickly tell him that I, Vishvamitra, son of Gadhi, have arrived.'
ramayan::578.translation_literal: सः (he) / राज्ञः (of the king) / दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी (desiring to see) / द्वाराध्यक्षान् (to the doorkeepers) / उवाच (said) / ह (indeed) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / आख्यात (announce) / माम् (me) / प्राप्तम् (having arrived) / कौशिकम् (Koushika) / गाधिनः (of Gadhi) / सुतम् (son)
ramayan::578.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::578.essence: Power still enters by waiting at the door.
ramayan::578.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra asks the guards to announce his arrival to King Dasharatha.
ramayan::578.simple_insight: Even great sages must still enter through the ordinary gates of court.
ramayan::578.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has reached Ayodhya and wants an audience with Dasharatha. He speaks to the palace guards, asking them to announce him at once. The moment is a formal arrival, not a teaching scene; it simply moves the story toward the meeting.
ramayan::578.modern_relevance: You arrive at a locked office, waiting room, or private event and have to be announced before you can proceed. Even important people still depend on someone at the door.
ramayan::578.insight: It shows how important encounters often begin with simple, formal access.

ramayan::579.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं त्रासाद्राज्ञो वेश्म प्रदुद्रुवु: । । 11839 । । सम्भ्रान्तमनसस्सर्वे तेन वाक्येन चोदिता: ।
ramayan::579.verse_hindi: On hearing those words (of Viswamitra) all of them prompted by fear because of left for the royal apartment with excited minds and hurried steps.
ramayan::579.english_translation: On hearing those words, all of them, stirred by fear and with confused minds, rushed to the king's residence.
ramayan::579.translation_literal: तच्छ्रुत्वा (having heard that) / वचनं (speech) / त्रासात् (from fear) / राज्ञो (of the king) / वेश्म (residence) / प्रदुद्रुवुः (ran off) / सम्भ्रान्तमनसः (with confused minds) / सर्वे (all) / तेन (by that) / वाक्येन (by the speech) / चोदिताः (impelled)
ramayan::579.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::579.essence: Fear makes servants run before they understand.
ramayan::579.simple_meaning: The king's attendants hear Visvamitra's message, become alarmed, and hurry to inform Dasaratha.
ramayan::579.simple_insight: Panic spreads fast when something urgent arrives unexpectedly.
ramayan::579.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just arrived and asked to see Dasaratha. His message unsettles the court servants, who rush to the royal chambers in confusion. The verse simply moves the scene forward; it is a bridge, not a teaching.
ramayan::579.insight: It advances the plot by showing the court's immediate alarm and haste.

ramayan::580.verse_sanskrit: ते गत्वा राजभवनं विश्वामित्रमृषिं तदा । । 11840 । । प्राप्तमावेदयामासुर्नृपायैक्ष्वाकवे तदा ।
ramayan::580.verse_hindi: Having reached the royal hall, they reported to the king (Dasaratha), descendant of the Ikshvakus about the arrival of sage Viswamitra.
ramayan::580.english_translation: Having reached the royal hall, they reported to King Dasaratha, descendant of the Ikshvakus, about the arrival of sage Viswamitra.
ramayan::580.translation_literal: ते (they) / गत्वा (having gone) / राजभवनं (the royal hall) / विश्वामित्रमृषिं (sage Viswamitra) / तदा (then) / प्राप्तम् (arrived) / आवेदयामासुः (reported) / नृपाय (to the king) / ऐक्ष्वाकवे (to the Ikshvaku descendant) / तदा (then)
ramayan::580.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::580.essence: A report arrives that changes the king's next move.
ramayan::580.simple_meaning: The messengers went to King Dasaratha and told him that sage Viswamitra had arrived.
ramayan::580.simple_insight: A single report can open the door to a life-changing meeting.
ramayan::580.detailed_meaning: The doorkeepers hurry from the entrance to Dasaratha's hall and announce that Viswamitra has come. This is only the messenger's report, not the teaching itself, but it sets the royal meeting in motion.
ramayan::580.modern_relevance: A message lands in your inbox saying someone important has arrived. Nothing has happened yet, but your whole day is about to change.
ramayan::580.insight: It shifts the scene from waiting to response, preparing the king for action.

ramayan::581.verse_sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सपुरोधास्समाहित: । । 11841 । । प्रत्युज्जगाम तं हृष्टो ब्रह्माणमिव वासव: ।
ramayan::581.verse_hindi: Having heard their words, Dasaratha in great joy went forth together with his preceptors to receive him like Indra receiving Brahma.
ramayan::581.english_translation: Having heard their words, Dasaratha in great joy went forth together with his preceptors to receive him like Indra receiving Brahma.
ramayan::581.translation_literal: तेषाम् (their) / तद्वचनम् (that word) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सपुरोधाः (together with his priests/preceptors) / समाहितः (composed, attentive) / प्रत्युज्जगाम (went forth to receive) / तम् (him) / हृष्टः (joyful) / ब्रह्माणम् इव (like Brahma) / वासवः (Indra)
ramayan::581.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::581.essence: True honor shows itself in how quickly you rise to meet the worthy.
ramayan::581.simple_meaning: Dasaratha joyfully goes out with his priests to welcome Viswamitra, showing honor and readiness.
ramayan::581.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before any request is even spoken.
ramayan::581.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arrived at Ayodhya, and the messengers have brought the news to Dasaratha. The king immediately rises with his priests and goes out to receive the sage, honoring him with the same grandeur as Indra greeting Brahma.
ramayan::581.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with an unexpected message from someone important, and you stop what you are doing. You know some arrivals deserve immediate respect.
ramayan::581.insight: It trains you to respond with composure and honor when a worthy person arrives.

ramayan::582.verse_sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा ज्वलितं दीप्त्या तापसं संशितव्रतम् । । 11842 । । प्रहृष्टवदनो राजा ततोऽर्घ्यमुपहारयत् ।
ramayan::582.verse_hindi: Seeing Viswamitra, shining with the power of his penance fulfilled the king with a cheerful countenance made offerings with due respect.
ramayan::582.english_translation: Seeing Viswamitra, blazing with the power of his disciplined vow, the king approached him with a cheerful face and offered him respectful gifts.
ramayan::582.translation_literal: तं (him) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / ज्वलितं (blazing) / दीप्त्या (with brilliance) / तापसं (the ascetic) / संशितव्रतम् (of firm vow) / प्रहृष्टवदनो (with a joyful face) / राजा (the king) / ततः (then) / अर्घ्यम् (a respectful offering) / उपहारयत् (offered)
ramayan::582.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::582.essence: Honor comes first when a worthy guest arrives.
ramayan::582.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha greets Viswamitra with honor and offers him respectful hospitality.
ramayan::582.simple_insight: Respect begins with how you receive someone who has earned it.
ramayan::582.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has come out with his priests to welcome Viswamitra, whose ascetic power is visible in his presence. The king meets him joyfully and offers the traditional respectful gift before their conversation begins.
ramayan::582.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose discipline has clearly changed them, and your first response is not small talk but respect.
ramayan::582.insight: It shows the etiquette of receiving a revered guest before any request or discussion begins.

ramayan::583.verse_sanskrit: स राज्ञ: प्रतिगृह्यार्घ्यं शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा । । 11843 । । कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव पर्यपृच्छन्नराधिपम् । 2
ramayan::583.verse_hindi: Viswamitra received the offerings as ordained in the scriptures and enquired from the king about the welfare and prosperity of his kingdom.
ramayan::583.english_translation: Viswamitra received the offerings as ordained in the scriptures and enquired from the king about the welfare and prosperity of his kingdom.
ramayan::583.translation_literal: स (he) / राज्ञः (of the king) / प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / अर्घ्यम् (the offering of honor) / शास्त्रदृष्टेन (according to what is seen in the scriptures) / कर्मणा (by conduct) / कुशलम् (about welfare) / च (and) / अव्ययम् (lasting prosperity) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / पर्यपृच्छत् (asked) / नराधिपम् (the lord of men)
ramayan::583.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::583.essence: Proper respect opens the way for serious conversation.
ramayan::583.simple_meaning: Viswamitra accepted the king’s respectful offering in the proper way and then asked about the kingdom’s welfare.
ramayan::583.simple_insight: Respect is shown not just by receiving honor, but by speaking with care afterward.
ramayan::583.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has come forward with honor to greet Viswamitra. The sage accepts the offering exactly as custom requires, then turns immediately to the king’s welfare. The moment is courteous, formal, and marks the beginning of an important meeting.
ramayan::583.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone senior has made time for you. Before any agenda, you notice the courtesy, the formality, and the quiet respect that sets everything else in motion.
ramayan::583.insight: It models how to begin serious meetings with ritual, respect, and concern for the other person’s well-being.

ramayan::584.verse_sanskrit: पुरे कोशे जनपदे बान्धवेषु सुहृत्सु च । । 11844 । । कुशलं कौशिको राज्ञ: पर्यपृच्छत्सुधार्मिक: ।
ramayan::584.verse_hindi: The exceedingly virtuous sage Viswamitra enquired from the king about the treasury welfare of his subjects living in cities and villages, and the well being of his friends and relatives.
ramayan::584.english_translation: The exceedingly virtuous sage Viswamitra asked the king about the welfare of the people in the cities and villages, and about his friends and relatives.
ramayan::584.translation_literal: पुरे (in the city) / कोशे (in the treasury) / जनपदे (in the kingdom) / बान्धवेषु (among relatives) / सुहृत्सु (among friends) / च (and) / कुशलं (welfare) / कौशिकः (Viswamitra) / राज्ञः (of the king) / पर्यपृच्छत् (asked in turn) / सुधार्मिकः (the highly righteous one)
ramayan::584.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::584.essence: A wise visitor begins by caring for the king's whole world.
ramayan::584.simple_meaning: Viswamitra politely asks the king how everything is going: the city, the kingdom, the treasury, and the people close to him.
ramayan::584.simple_insight: Real respect begins with asking after the whole life, not just the public role.
ramayan::584.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arrived at Dasharatha's court and accepted the king's offerings. Before turning to the purpose of his visit, he asks after every layer of the kingdom: city, treasury, countryside, friends, and relatives. The scene is calm, formal, and politically careful.
ramayan::584.modern_relevance: You meet someone after months apart and ask about their parents, work, and home, not just their latest achievement. That kind of attention tells them they are seen as a whole person.
ramayan::584.insight: It shifts attention from status to the full human network that supports a life.

ramayan::585.verse_sanskrit: अपि ते सन्नतास्सर्वे सामन्ता रिपवो जिता: । । 11845 । । दैवं च मानुषं चापि कर्म ते साध्वनुष्ठितम् ।
ramayan::585.verse_hindi: Are the tributary kings submissive to you? Have you conquered your enemies? Are the rites for propitiating gods and the services to humanity  performed rightly?
ramayan::585.english_translation: Are all your tributary kings submissive? Have you conquered your enemies? Have you performed both divine rites and human duties properly?
ramayan::585.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / ते (your) / सन्नताः (submissive) / सर्वे (all) / सामन्ताः (tributary kings) / रिपवः (enemies) / जिताः (conquered) / दैवम् (divine) / च (and) / मानुषम् (human) / च (and) / अपि (also) / कर्म (actions, duties) / ते (your) / साधु (properly) / अनुष्ठितम् (performed)
ramayan::585.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::585.essence: Good rule means enemies checked and duties kept.
ramayan::585.simple_meaning: Viswamitra asks the king whether his rule is secure, his enemies are defeated, and both sacred and worldly duties are being carried out well.
ramayan::585.simple_insight: A ruler is measured by how well he protects order, not by titles alone.
ramayan::585.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just been welcomed by the king and has asked after the kingdom's welfare. Now he checks the real signs of a healthy reign: loyal allies, defeated enemies, and proper fulfilment of both sacred and human responsibilities. It is a formal inquiry, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::585.modern_relevance: A leader walks into a tense review meeting and is asked the questions that matter most: Is the team stable? Are threats handled? Are responsibilities actually being met?
ramayan::585.insight: It frames leadership as the steady fulfilment of duty across both moral and practical life.

ramayan::586.verse_sanskrit: वसिष्ठं च समागम्य कुशलं मुनिपुङ्गव: । । 11846 । । ऋषींश्च तान्यथान्यायं महाभागानुवाच ह ।
ramayan::586.verse_hindi: The foremost of ascetis, Viswamitra approached Vasishta and all other distinguised sages following the protocal and enquired about their welfare.
ramayan::586.english_translation: The foremost of ascetics, Viswamitra, met Vasishta and the other great sages, greeted them properly, and asked after their welfare.
ramayan::586.translation_literal: वसिष्ठं (Vasishta) / च (and) / समागम्य (having met) / कुशलं (after welfare) / मुनिपुङ्गव: (the foremost of sages) / ऋषींश्च (and the sages) / तान् (those) / यथान्यायं (properly, according to protocol) / महाभागान् (the greatly fortunate, noble ones) / उवाच (spoke) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::586.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::586.essence: Courtesy comes first, even when larger matters are waiting.
ramayan::586.simple_meaning: Viswamitra meets Vasishta and the other respected sages and greets them with proper courtesy before speaking to them.
ramayan::586.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before any deeper conversation can begin.
ramayan::586.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has come to the royal court as an honoured guest. After greeting King Dasharatha, he now meets Vasishta and the other sages with full protocol. The scene is still formal and courteous; the real request has not yet begun.
ramayan::586.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where old tensions still exist, and you choose courtesy first. That small act can soften a whole conversation before the hard part starts.
ramayan::586.insight: It teaches you to begin difficult exchanges with dignity and social care.

ramayan::587.verse_sanskrit: ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसस्तस्य राज्ञो निवेशनम् । । 11847 । । विविशु: पूजितास्तत्र निषेदुश्च यथार्हत: ।
ramayan::587.verse_hindi: All of them with gladdened hearts entered the royal palace and sat down, in accordance with their position after having been duly honoured by the king.
ramayan::587.english_translation: All of them, with delighted minds, entered that king's palace and sat down there, duly honored, each according to his rank.
ramayan::587.translation_literal: ते (they) / सर्वे (all) / हृष्टमनसः (with delighted minds) / तस्य (that) / राज्ञः (of the king) / निवेशनम् (dwelling/palace) / विविशुः (entered) / पूजिताः (honored) / तत्र (there) / निषेदुः (sat down) / च (and) / यथार्हतः (according to due worth/rank)
ramayan::587.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::587.essence: Honor settles the room before any words are spoken.
ramayan::587.simple_meaning: The sages and guests enter the king's palace joyfully and take their seats with proper honor and rank.
ramayan::587.simple_insight: Respect creates ease; even formal gatherings can feel warm when people are received well.
ramayan::587.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arrived at Dasharatha's court with the sages. After the greetings, everyone enters the royal palace, is honored properly, and sits in order. The verse simply sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
ramayan::587.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where the host has already noticed your arrival, made space for you, and put you at ease before anyone speaks.
ramayan::587.insight: It shifts attention from the speech itself to the dignity of welcome that makes honest conversation possible.

ramayan::588.verse_sanskrit: अथ हृष्टमना राजा विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् । । 11848 । । उवाच परमोदारो हृष्टस्तमभिपूजयन् ।
ramayan::588.verse_hindi: Then the munificent king, very much (at Viswamitras arrival) pleased offered him a happy hospitality and spoke:
ramayan::588.english_translation: Then the munificent king, delighted at Viswamitra's arrival, honoured him with joy and spoke.
ramayan::588.translation_literal: अथ (then) / हृष्टमना (with a delighted mind) / राजा (the king) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / महामुनिम् (the great sage) / उवाच (spoke) / परमौदारः (most generous) / हृष्टः (delighted) / तम् (him) / अभिपूजयन् (honouring)
ramayan::588.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::588.essence: True welcome is shown before the first sentence.
ramayan::588.simple_meaning: King Janaka welcomes Viswamitra with joy and honour.
ramayan::588.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before any words do.
ramayan::588.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arrived with the sages and entered Janaka's palace. The king rises in delight, receives the great seer properly, and begins the formal exchange that will lead into praise and hospitality.
ramayan::588.modern_relevance: A guest you deeply respect walks into your home after a long journey. You stop everything, greet them well, and let the welcome itself speak first.
ramayan::588.insight: It shifts attention from mere speech to the dignity of receiving another well.

ramayan::589.verse_sanskrit: यथाऽमृतस्य सम्प्राप्तिर्यथावर्षमनूदके । यथा सदृशदारेषु पुत्रजन्माऽप्रजस्य च । । 11849 । । प्रणष्टस्य यथालाभो यथा हर्षो महोदये । तथैवागमनं मन्ये स्वागतं ते महामुने । । 11850 । ।
ramayan::589.verse_hindi: O great sage, welcome to you Your arrival, to me, is like nectar (to a human being), rains to the parched land, birth of a son to the childless through his worthy wife, recovery of lost properity and festive joy in a great achievemnt.
ramayan::589.english_translation: O great sage, your arrival is like nectar to one who is thirsty, rain to parched ground, a son’s birth to the childless through a worthy wife, finding lost wealth, and joy after great success. In the same way, I consider your coming a welcome blessing.
ramayan::589.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / अमृतस्य (of nectar) / सम्प्राप्तिः (attainment, arrival) / यथा (just as) / वर्षम् (rain) / अनूदके (for the waterless, parched) / यथा (just as) / सदृश-दारेषु (in worthy wives) / पुत्र-जन्म (birth of a son) / अप्रजस्य (for the childless) / च (and) / प्रणष्टस्य (of the lost) / यथा (just as) / लाभः (gain, recovery) / यथा (just as) / हर्षः (joy) / महा-उदये (in great success) / तथा एव (just so) / आगमनम् (arrival) / मन्ये (I consider) / स्वागतम् (welcome) / ते (to you) / महामुने (O great sage)
ramayan::589.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::589.essence: A true welcome can feel like life returning.
ramayan::589.simple_meaning: Dasharatha welcomes Vishwamitra by saying his arrival feels like the best possible relief: like rain, nectar, a child’s birth, or recovering something lost.
ramayan::589.simple_insight: Some people enter your life like relief after a long thirst.
ramayan::589.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha greets Vishwamitra after the sage enters Ayodhya with honor. The king piles up images of relief and joy to show how deeply he values the visit before the real request is even spoken.
ramayan::589.modern_relevance: A friend texts back after weeks of silence, and your chest loosens before you even read the words. Some people do that — they don’t add noise, they restore what was fraying.
ramayan::589.insight: It turns welcome into a sacred act of recognition, not just politeness.

ramayan::590.verse_sanskrit: पूर्वं राजर्षिशब्देन तपसा द्योतितप्रभः । ब्रह्मर्षित्वमनुप्राप्त: पूज्योऽसि बहुधा मया । । 11853 । ।
ramayan::590.verse_hindi: Earlier you were rajarshi, a warrior sage. By your austerities you have obtained the brilliance that lends radiance even to the Sun and the Moon you have gained the status of a brahmrshi. In several ways you are worthy of my worship.
ramayan::590.english_translation: Earlier you were a royal sage. Through austerity you have gained a brilliance that outshines the Sun and Moon, and you have attained the rank of a sage among sages. In many ways, you are worthy of my worship.
ramayan::590.translation_literal: पूर्वम् (earlier) / राजर्षिशब्देन (by the name/title of royal sage) / तपसा (through austerity) / द्योतितप्रभः (one whose brilliance is illuminated) / ब्रह्मर्षित्वम् (the state of a sage among sages) / अनुप्राप्तः (attained) / पूज्यः (worthy of worship) / असि (you are) / बहुधा (in many ways) / मया (by me)
ramayan::590.speaker: King Janaka
ramayan::590.essence: A title is small beside the radiance earned through austerity.
ramayan::590.simple_meaning: Janaka honors Vishwamitra by saying that his austerity has transformed him from a royal sage into a higher sage, making him worthy of deep respect.
ramayan::590.simple_insight: Real greatness is earned by inner discipline, not by title alone.
ramayan::590.detailed_meaning: King Janaka welcomes Vishwamitra with reverence and praise. He says the sage's former status was only the beginning; through austerity, Vishwamitra has reached a far higher spiritual stature. The moment deepens Janaka's hospitality into recognition of earned greatness.
ramayan::590.modern_relevance: Someone introduces you in a room full of people, but the respect you actually carry comes from years of quiet discipline, not the label on your name badge.
ramayan::590.insight: It shifts attention from social rank to the inner work that makes respect real.

ramayan::591.verse_sanskrit: तदद्भुतमिदं ब्रह्मन्पवित्रं परमं मम । शुभक्षेत्रगतश्चाहं तव सन्दर्शनात्प्रभो । । 11854 । ।
ramayan::591.verse_hindi: O Brahman your arrival has caused surprise to me. It has conferred great purity on me. O Lord by your very presence here, I feel I haved acquired the merits of a          pilgrimage.
ramayan::591.english_translation: O Brahman, your arrival is astonishing and supremely purifying to me. By seeing you, O Lord, I feel as though I have gained the merit of a sacred pilgrimage.
ramayan::591.translation_literal: तद् (that) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful) / इदम् (this) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahman) / पवित्रम् (purifying) / परमम् (supreme) / मम (to me) / शुभक्षेत्रगतः (gone to a holy place) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / तव (your) / सन्दर्शनात् (by sight) / प्रभो (O Lord)
ramayan::591.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::591.essence: True presence can purify before any teaching begins.
ramayan::591.simple_meaning: The speaker welcomes the sage's arrival as something extraordinary and deeply purifying, like the merit gained from visiting a holy place.
ramayan::591.simple_insight: Some presences lift you before a single word is spoken.
ramayan::591.detailed_meaning: A sage has arrived, and the speaker responds with reverence rather than formality. He says the visit itself is wondrous and cleansing, as if standing in a sacred place. The next verse asks why the sage has come, so this is a respectful opening, not the main teaching.
ramayan::591.modern_relevance: Someone you deeply respect walks into the room, and the whole atmosphere changes before the conversation begins. Their presence steadies you, as if it has already done part of the work.
ramayan::591.insight: It frames holy company as something that transforms you simply by being near it.

ramayan::592.verse_sanskrit: ब्रूहि यत्प्रार्थितं तुभ्यं कार्यमागमनं प्रति । इच्छाम्यनुगृहीतोऽहं त्वदर्थपरिवृद्धये । । 11855 । ।
ramayan::592.verse_hindi: Be pleased to tell me the purpose of your visit. I desire to be given the privilege of
ramayan::592.english_translation: Please tell me what you have come to ask for. I wish to be blessed by serving your purpose and helping it grow.
ramayan::592.translation_literal: ब्रूहि (tell) / यत् (what) / प्रार्थितम् (requested) / तुभ्यम् (to you) / कार्यम् (task, purpose) / आगमनम् (coming) / प्रति (regarding) / इच्छामि (I wish) / अनुगृहीतः (blessed) / अहम् (I) / त्वदर्थ (for your sake) / परिवृद्धये (for increase, growth)
ramayan::592.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::592.essence: You honor someone by asking what they truly need.
ramayan::592.simple_meaning: Rama asks Vishwamitra to state his purpose plainly, and says he feels blessed to help him succeed.
ramayan::592.simple_insight: True generosity starts by asking what another person actually needs.
ramayan::592.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has come to Ayodhya, and Rama meets him with full respect. Instead of guessing, he asks directly what task brought him here and offers himself to help. The moment shows noble readiness before the request is even spoken.
ramayan::592.modern_relevance: Someone you respect finally says, “Can I ask you something?” and you stop performing, stop guessing, and listen. Real support begins there.
ramayan::592.insight: It teaches you to meet a request with readiness, not ego, and to serve the need before trying to control it.

ramayan::593.verse_sanskrit: कार्यस्य न विमर्शं च गन्तुमर्हसि कौशिक । कर्ता चाहमशेषेण दैवतं हि भवान्मम । । 11856 । ।
ramayan::593.verse_hindi: O Viswamitra you need not hesitatate to tell me what ought to be performed. I shall accomplish that act in every possible special way. You are a god to me.
ramayan::593.english_translation: O Viswamitra, you need not hesitate to tell me what must be done. I shall accomplish that task in every possible way. You are a radiant being to me.
ramayan::593.translation_literal: कार्यस्य (of the task) / न (not) / विमर्शं (hesitation or deliberation) / च (and) / गन्तुमर्हसि (you ought to go) / कौशिक (O Kaushika) / कर्ता (doer) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / अशेषेण (completely, without remainder) / दैवतं (radiant being) / हि (indeed) / भवान् (you) / मम (to me)
ramayan::593.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::593.essence: Trust turns hesitation into immediate service.
ramayan::593.simple_meaning: Rama tells Viswamitra to ask for anything without hesitation and promises to complete it fully. He treats Viswamitra with deep reverence.
ramayan::593.simple_insight: Real trust makes room for directness, not caution.
ramayan::593.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has come to Rama with a purpose. After welcoming him, Rama removes all hesitation: whatever task is needed, he will do it completely. The moment shows immediate trust, readiness, and reverence toward the teacher.
ramayan::593.modern_relevance: A mentor finally says, “I need your help with something hard.” You stop performing politeness and answer cleanly: tell me what needs doing, and I’ll handle it all.
ramayan::593.insight: It shifts you from polite uncertainty to wholehearted readiness in service.

ramayan::594.verse_sanskrit: मम चायमनुप्राप्तो महानभ्युदयो द्विज । तवागमनज: कृत्स्नो धर्मश्चानुत्तमो मम । । 11857 । ।
ramayan::594.verse_hindi: O Brahmin I have attained this high foutune today. My great merit has been realised as a result of your arrival.
ramayan::594.english_translation: O Brahmin, today I have attained a great blessing. Your arrival has brought me the fullest fulfillment of duty.
ramayan::594.translation_literal: मम (my) / च (and) / अयम् (this) / अनुप्राप्तः (attained) / महान् (great) / अभ्युदयः (blessing, rise) / द्विज (O Brahmin) / तव (your) / आगमन-जः (born from arrival) / कृत्स्नः (complete, whole) / धर्मः (duty, right order) / च (and) / अनुत्तमः (highest) / मम (my)
ramayan::594.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::594.essence: Serving the worthy can feel like the reward itself.
ramayan::594.simple_meaning: Rama says that Vishvamitra's arrival has brought him great good fortune and made his highest duty feel fulfilled.
ramayan::594.simple_insight: Right company can turn obligation into blessing.
ramayan::594.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has come to Rama and asked for help. Rama answers with humility, saying the sage's arrival itself is a great gain and that serving him is the highest duty. The moment shows reverence before action.
ramayan::594.modern_relevance: A mentor finally answers your message after weeks of silence, and the whole room seems to shift. Their presence alone changes what feels possible, and your responsibility suddenly feels meaningful instead of heavy.
ramayan::594.insight: It shifts duty from burden to privilege, so service feels like fulfillment rather than loss.

ramayan::595.verse_sanskrit: इति हृदयसुखं निशम्य वाक्यं श्रुतिसुखमात्मवता विनीतमुक्तम् । प्रथितगुणयशा गुणैर्विशिष्ट:परमऋषि: परमं जगाम हर्षम् । । 11858 । ।
ramayan::595.verse_hindi: On hearing the words spoken in such an humble manner by the prudent king words pleasing  to the mind and to the ears, the great rishi of  celebrated virtues and fame, of sterling qualities experienced deep delight.
ramayan::595.english_translation: On hearing the king's humble words, pleasing to the heart and to the ear, the great sage, famed for his virtues, felt deep delight.
ramayan::595.translation_literal: इति (thus) / हृदयसुखं (heart-pleasing) / निशम्य (having heard) / वाक्यं (speech) / श्रुतिसुखम् (ear-pleasing) / आत्मवता (by the self-possessed one) / विनीतम् (humble) / उक्तम् (spoken) / प्रथितगुणयशाः (one whose virtues and fame are renowned) / गुणैः (by virtues) / विशिष्टः (distinguished) / परमऋषिः (great sage) / परमम् (greatly) / जगाम (went to) / हर्षम् (delight)
ramayan::595.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::595.essence: Humility makes true character immediately visible.
ramayan::595.simple_meaning: Viswamitra is moved by Rama's humble, thoughtful reply and feels great joy.
ramayan::595.detailed_meaning: Rama has just spoken to Viswamitra with restraint, humility, and readiness to serve. The sage, famous for his own virtues, hears not just polite words but the mark of a worthy disciple. His delight shows that character can be felt instantly.
ramayan::595.modern_relevance: You answer a difficult message without defensiveness, and the other person softens at once. Calm, respectful speech can change the whole atmosphere before the real work even begins.
ramayan::595.insight: It shows that humility and steadiness can win trust before any action starts.

ramayan::596.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::596.essence: The moment pauses before the sage answers.
ramayan::596.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has just spoken with humility and warmth, and Viswamitra is about to answer. This verse is only the narrative bridge into his reply, not a teaching on its own.

ramayan::597.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा राजसिंहस्य वाक्यमद्भुतविस्तरम् । हृष्टरोमा महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत । । 1191 । ।
ramayan::597.verse_hindi: Having heard these wonderful words of Dasaratha, the lion among kings, the brilliant Viswamitra with hair on end replied:
ramayan::597.english_translation: Having heard those wonderful words of the lion among kings, Dasaratha, the brilliant Visvamitra, with hairs standing on end, replied.
ramayan::597.translation_literal: तत् (that) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राजसिंहस्य (of the lion among kings) / वाक्यम् (speech) / अद्भुतविस्तरम् (wonderfully expansive) / हृष्टरोमा (with hairs standing on end) / महातेजा (the greatly radiant one) / विश्वामित्रः (Visvamitra) / अभ्यभाषत (spoke)
ramayan::597.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::597.essence: True nobility can move even a great sage to awe.
ramayan::597.simple_meaning: Visvamitra is moved by Dasaratha's words and answers with respect and wonder.
ramayan::597.simple_insight: Even great sages can be struck silent by sincere, noble speech.
ramayan::597.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has spoken humbly and at length before the sage Visvamitra. Moved by the king's words, Visvamitra reacts with visible awe and then replies. The verse is a bridge in their conversation, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::597.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such honesty that your own defenses drop. For a moment, admiration comes before reply.
ramayan::597.insight: It shifts attention from argument to the moral force of humble speech.

ramayan::598.verse_sanskrit: सदृशं राजशार्दूल तवैतद्भुवि नान्यथा । महावंशप्रसूतस्य वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिन: । । 1192 । ।
ramayan::598.verse_hindi: O Tiger among kings having been born on earth in an illustrious lineage and initiated by Vasishta, this way (of speaking) befits you. It cannot be any other way.
ramayan::598.english_translation: O tiger among kings, this is fitting for you on earth and could not be otherwise, born in a great lineage and guided by Vasishta.
ramayan::598.translation_literal: सदृशम् (fitting) / राजशार्दूल (O tiger among kings) / तव (for you) / एतत् (this) / भुवि (on earth) / न (not) / अन्यथा (otherwise) / महावंशप्रसूतस्य (of one born in a great lineage) / वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिनः (of one instructed by Vasishta)
ramayan::598.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::598.essence: True nobility shows itself in the way you answer pressure.
ramayan::598.simple_meaning: Viswamitra says that this response suits Dasharatha's noble birth and training under Vasishta. A king like him should speak and act with that kind of dignity.
ramayan::598.simple_insight: Your training should show in your choices, especially when the stakes are high.
ramayan::598.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just heard Dasharatha's gracious reply. Before revealing why he has come, he acknowledges the king's nobility: a ruler from a great line, shaped by Vasishta, should answer with honor. It prepares the ground for the harder request that follows.
ramayan::598.modern_relevance: A senior colleague answers your difficult message with calm, measured respect instead of panic. You feel the difference immediately: character is not what you claim when life is easy, but how you speak under pressure.
ramayan::598.insight: It frames noble conduct as something visible in speech, not just status.

ramayan::599.verse_sanskrit: यत्तु मे हृद्गतं वाक्यं तस्य कार्यस्य निश्चयम् । कुरूष्व राजशार्दूल भव सत्यप्रतिश्रव: । । 1193 । ।
ramayan::599.verse_hindi: O Tiger among kings I shall unfold the purpose conceived in my mind. Take a decision and be truthful to your promise.
ramayan::599.english_translation: O Tiger among kings, I shall unfold the purpose conceived in my mind. Take a decision and be truthful to your promise.
ramayan::599.translation_literal: यत् (which) / तु (indeed) / मे (my) / हृद्गतम् (held in the heart) / वाक्यम् (speech) / तस्य (of that) / कार्यस्य (of the task) / निश्चयम् (decision, certainty) / कुरूष्व (do) / राजशार्दूल (O tiger among kings) / भव (be) / सत्यप्रतिश्रवः (true to your promise)
ramayan::599.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::599.essence: A noble promise becomes real only when you choose to stand by it.
ramayan::599.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra asks Dasharatha to make a firm decision and stay faithful to his promise.
