ramayan::791.modern_relevance: After a long night before an important exam, your mentor finally smiles and says, 'Now we begin.' The tension breaks, and the real work starts.
ramayan::791.insight: It marks the transition from waiting to instruction, showing that guidance often begins after patience.

ramayan::792.verse_sanskrit: परितुष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः । प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः । । 1272 । ।
ramayan::792.verse_hindi: O prince of great renown, I am extremely pleased. May you prosper Out of great love and affection for you I shall make over all the weapons.
ramayan::792.english_translation: O prince of great renown, I am extremely pleased. May you prosper. Out of great love and affection for you, I shall give you all the weapons.
ramayan::792.translation_literal: परितुष्टः (fully pleased) / अस्मि (I am) / भद्रम् (good fortune) / ते (to you) / राजपुत्र (prince) / महायशः (greatly renowned) / प्रीत्या (with affection) / परमया (supreme) / युक्तः (endowed) / ददामि (I give) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / सर्वशः (completely)
ramayan::792.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::792.essence: Earned trust brings greater power, not praise alone.
ramayan::792.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra tells Rama that he is pleased with him and will now give him all the weapons he has promised.
ramayan::792.simple_insight: Recognition can open the next door. Readiness is often rewarded with greater trust.
ramayan::792.detailed_meaning: After Rama has protected the sacrifice and proved his steadiness, Vishwamitra smiles and speaks with approval. The sage now gives the prince divine weapons, preparing him for the larger struggles ahead.
ramayan::792.modern_relevance: You finish the hard assignment no one else wanted. Then the mentor who has been watching quietly says, 'Now I can trust you with more.'
ramayan::792.insight: It shifts the focus from proving yourself to receiving responsibility after earned trust.

ramayan::793.verse_sanskrit: देवासुरगणान्वापि सगन्धर्वोरगानपि । यैरमित्रान् प्रसह्याजौ वशीकृत्य जयिष्यसि । । 1273 । । तानि दिव्यानि भद्रं ते ददाम्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः ।
ramayan::793.verse_hindi: With the help of these celestial weapons, you will vanquish even gods and demons, serpents together with gandharvas if they challenge you to a battle as enemies and take them as captives. I shall confer on you all such weapons. May you prosper
ramayan::793.english_translation: With these celestial weapons, you will defeat even gods, demons, serpents, and gandharvas in battle. I give you all these weapons. May you prosper.
ramayan::793.translation_literal: देवासुरगणान् (the groups of devas and asuras) / वा (also) / अपि (even) / सगन्धर्वोरगान् (together with gandharvas and serpents) / अपि (also) / यैः (by which) / अमित्रान् (enemies) / प्रसह्य (forcibly) / आजौ (in battle) / वशीकृत्य (having brought under control) / जयिष्यसि (you will conquer) / तानि (those) / दिव्यानि (celestial) / भद्रं ते (may good be to you) / ददामि (I give) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / सर्वशः (all)
ramayan::793.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::793.essence: Great power can be given before it is tested.
ramayan::793.simple_meaning: Viswamitra is giving Rama divine weapons that can overpower any enemy, even beings from the higher realms and lower realms.
ramayan::793.simple_insight: Power is being handed over, not earned in this moment.
ramayan::793.detailed_meaning: After a night of testing, Viswamitra smiles at Rama and begins bestowing celestial weapons. This verse is part of a larger initiation: the teacher arms the student for dangers ahead, and the gift is still unfolding in the next line.
ramayan::793.modern_relevance: A mentor forwards you the final tool, the access key, the contact list — everything you need for the hard part ahead.
ramayan::793.insight: It shifts attention from personal strength to received capability and preparation.

ramayan::794.verse_sanskrit: दण्डचक्रं महद्दिव्यं तव दास्यामि राघव । । 1274 । । धर्मचक्रं ततो वीर कालचक्रं तथैव च । विष्णुचक्रं तथात्युग्रमैन्द्रमस्त्रं तथैव च । । 1275 । । वज्रमस्त्रं नरश्रेष्ठ शैवं शूलवरं तथा । अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरश्चैव ऐषीकमपि राघव । । 1276 । । ददामि ते महाबाहो ब्राह्ममस्त्रमनुत्तमम् ।
ramayan::794.verse_hindi: Mighty armed, heroic Rama I shall grant you the great celestial dandachakra. O best among men I shall grant you dharmachakra, kalachakra, visnuchakra, indraastra, vajraastra and the great, trident of Siva, brahmashirastra, ishika astra and highly superior brahmaastra.
ramayan::794.english_translation: Mighty-armed Rama, I shall grant you the great celestial Dandachakra. Then, O hero, I shall give you Dharmachakra, Kalachakra, Vishnuchakra, Indra's weapon, Vajraastra, Shiva's excellent trident, Brahmashirastra, Ishikaastra, and the unsurpassed Brahmaastra.
ramayan::794.translation_literal: दण्डचक्रम् (Dandachakra) / महत् (great) / दिव्यम् (celestial) / तव (to you) / दास्यामि (I shall give) / राघव (Raghava) / धर्मचक्रम् (Dharmachakra) / ततः (then) / वीर (hero) / कालचक्रम् (Kalachakra) / तथैव (likewise) / च (and) / विष्णुचक्रम् (Vishnuchakra) / तथा (also) / अत्युग्रम् (very fierce) / ऐन्द्रमस्त्रम् (Indra-weapon) / तथैव (likewise) / च (and) / वज्रमस्त्रम् (Vajraastra) / नरश्रेष्ठ (best among men) / शैवम् (of Shiva) / शूलवरम् (excellent trident) / तथा (and) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / ब्रह्मशिरः (Brahmashiras) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / ऐषीकम् (Ishikaastra) / अपि (also) / राघव (Raghava) / ददामि (I give) / ते (to you) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / ब्राह्ममस्त्रम् (Brahmaastra) / अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed)
ramayan::794.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::794.essence: Great power is being handed over before the real test begins.
ramayan::794.simple_meaning: A divine teacher is handing Rama a long list of powerful celestial weapons, including the supreme Brahmaastra.
ramayan::794.simple_insight: Power is being placed in his hands, but it is still only a tool.
ramayan::794.detailed_meaning: A divine weapons-master is arming Rama with weapon after weapon: cosmic discs, thunderbolt-like force, Shiva's trident, and the unmatched Brahmaastra. The scene is about preparation for war, not reflection. It builds the arsenal before the coming struggle.
ramayan::794.modern_relevance: A mentor drops a stack of advanced tools into your lap before a high-stakes project. The real question is not what you can hold, but whether you can use power without being used by it.
ramayan::794.insight: It shifts attention from the glamour of power to the responsibility of wielding it.

ramayan::795.verse_sanskrit: गदे द्वे चैव काकुत्स्थ मोदकी शिखरी उभे । । 1277 । । प्रदीप्ते नरशार्दूल प्रयच्छामि नृपात्मज ।
ramayan::795.verse_hindi: Born in the race of kakutstha and a tiger among men, O Rama I shall also grant two  shining maces known as modaki and shikhari.
ramayan::795.english_translation: Born in the race of Kakutstha and tiger among men, O Rama, I shall also grant you two blazing maces named Modaki and Shikhari.
ramayan::795.translation_literal: गदे (maces) / द्वे (two) / चैव (also) / काकुत्स्थ (Kakutstha-born) / मोदकी (Modaki) / शिखरी (Shikhari) / उभे (both) / प्रदीप्ते (blazing) / नरशार्दूल (tiger among men) / प्रयच्छामि (I grant) / नृपात्मज (O son of a king)
ramayan::795.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::795.essence: A gift of weapons continues, each one widening Rama's reach.
ramayan::795.simple_meaning: More divine weapons are being given to Rama, including two blazing maces.
ramayan::795.simple_insight: The scene is still building power, not delivering a teaching.
ramayan::795.detailed_meaning: A sage is arming Rama with celestial weapons one by one. After listing several destructive powers, he adds two blazing maces. This is part of a larger gift of weapons, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::795.insight: It adds another weapon to the larger arming of Rama.

ramayan::796.verse_sanskrit: धर्मपाशमहं राम कालपाशं तथैव च । । 1278 । । पाशं वारुणमस्त्रं च ददाम्यहमनुत्तमम् ।
ramayan::796.verse_hindi: Rama, I shall grant dharmapasa, kalapasa, varuna pasa, too unique weapons.
ramayan::796.english_translation: Rama, I shall grant you dharmapasa, kalapasa, and varunapasa as well, O unmatched one.
ramayan::796.translation_literal: धर्मपाशम् (bond of dharma) / अहम् (I) / राम (Rama) / कालपाशम् (bond of time/death) / तथैव च (and likewise) / पाशम् (noose) / वारुणम् (of Varuna) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / च (and) / ददामि (I give) / अहम् (I) / अनुत्तमम् (unmatched)
ramayan::796.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::796.essence: More force is being entrusted before the real work begins.
ramayan::796.simple_meaning: The speaker offers Rama more divine weapons, including the bonds of dharma, time, and Varuna.
ramayan::796.simple_insight: Power is being handed over in full, with no hesitation.
ramayan::796.detailed_meaning: A celestial giver is listing extraordinary weapons for Rama one after another. This verse is part of that inventory, not a separate teaching: it continues the formal bestowal of divine armaments before the larger exchange moves on.
ramayan::796.modern_relevance: A mentor keeps naming tools you did not know existed, each one more precise than the last. The moment is about being equipped, not yet about using what you have received.
ramayan::796.insight: It frames strength as something received in order, not seized in panic.

ramayan::797.verse_sanskrit: अशनी द्वे प्रयच्छामि शुष्कार्द्रे रघुनन्दन । । 1279 । । ददामि चास्त्रं पैनाकमस्त्रं नारायणं तथा ।
ramayan::797.verse_hindi: O descendant of Raghu I shall grant you two thunderbolts named shuska and ardra (dry and wet), painaka astra and narayanaastra.
ramayan::797.english_translation: O descendant of Raghu, I shall grant you two thunderbolts, called dry and wet, along with the Pinaaka weapon and the Narayana weapon.
ramayan::797.translation_literal: अशनी (two thunderbolts) / द्वे (two) / प्रयच्छामि (I grant) / शुष्कार्द्रे (dry and wet) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of Raghu's line) / ददामि (I give) / च (and) / अस्त्रं (weapon) / पैनाकम् (Pinaaka) / अस्त्रं (weapon) / नारायणम् (Narayana) / तथा (also)
ramayan::797.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::797.essence: Sacred power is being placed into disciplined hands.
ramayan::797.simple_meaning: The divine weapons are being handed over to Rama, including the thunderbolts, Pinaaka, and Narayana weapon.
ramayan::797.simple_insight: Power becomes safe only when it is given to the right hands.
ramayan::797.detailed_meaning: In Vishvamitra’s instruction of Rama, the sage is not just naming weapons but transferring sacred force. This verse continues the long list of divine missiles Rama receives, marking his preparation for the trials ahead.
ramayan::797.modern_relevance: A mentor finally trusts you with the tool everyone else hesitated to hand over. The real test is not owning power, but carrying it without distortion.
ramayan::797.insight: It shifts attention from raw force to rightful stewardship.

ramayan::798.verse_sanskrit: आग्नेयमस्त्रं दयितं शिखरं नाम नामतः । । 12710 । । वायव्यं प्रथनं नाम ददामि च तवानघ ।
ramayan::798.verse_hindi: O blemishless Rama I shall grant you agneyaastra known as sikhara which is my
ramayan::798.english_translation: O blemishless Rama, I grant you the Agneya weapon, named Shikhara, and the Vayavya weapon, named Prathana.
ramayan::798.translation_literal: आग्नेयमस्त्रम् (Agneya weapon) / दयितम् (beloved) / शिखरम् (Shikhara) / नाम (by name) / नामतः (by name) / वायव्यम् (Vayavya) / प्रथनम् (Prathana) / नाम (by name) / ददामि (I give) / च (and) / तव (to you) / अनघ (blemishless)
ramayan::798.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::798.essence: Another weapon is added to Rama’s arsenal.
ramayan::798.simple_meaning: A heavenly weapon of fire and another of wind are being given to Rama, along with their names.
ramayan::798.simple_insight: Power is being handed over piece by piece, not all at once.
ramayan::798.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a long transfer of divine weapons, the giver continues listing the arms Rama will receive. This verse is not a new teaching or turning point; it is one item in a larger inventory of power being bestowed before the next stage of the story.
ramayan::798.modern_relevance: A mentor is still walking you through the tools, one by one, before the real test begins.
ramayan::798.insight: It shows preparation as a careful handing over of capability, not a dramatic leap.

ramayan::799.verse_sanskrit: अस्त्रं हयशिरो नाम क्रौञ्चमस्त्रं तथैव च । शक्तिद्वयं च काकुत्स्थ ददामि तव राघव । । 12711 । ।
ramayan::799.verse_hindi: O Rama bron in the Kakutstha race, I shall grant you two powers named hayasira (Horse head) and kraunchaastra.
ramayan::799.english_translation: O Rama, born in the Kakutstha race, I shall grant you the weapon called Hayashira, the Krauncha weapon, and two powers.
ramayan::799.translation_literal: अस्त्रम् (weapon) / हयशिरः (Hayashira) / नाम (called) / क्रौञ्चम् (Krauncha) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / तथा एव च (and likewise) / शक्तिद्वयम् (two powers) / च (and) / काकुत्स्थ (O Kakutstha) / ददामि (I give) / तव (to you) / राघव (O descendant of Raghu)
ramayan::799.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::799.essence: More weapons are being added to prepare Rama for war.
ramayan::799.simple_meaning: A celestial giver is listing more weapons for Rama: Hayashira, Krauncha, and two powers. It is part of a larger gift of weapons, not a teaching by itself.
ramayan::799.simple_insight: The scene is about preparation, not philosophy. Power is being handed over piece by piece.
ramayan::799.detailed_meaning: A divine armorer is still listing weapons to Rama, adding Hayashira, Krauncha, and two special powers to the growing arsenal. The verse continues a sequence of grants, so it supports the larger scene rather than standing alone.
ramayan::799.insight: It shifts the moment from action to inventory: the hero is being equipped for what comes next.

ramayan::800.verse_sanskrit: कङ्कालं मुसलं घोरं कापालमथ कङ्कणम् । धारयन्त्यसुरा यानि ददाम्येतानि सर्वशः । । 12712 । ।
ramayan::800.verse_hindi: I shall grant all these weapons, the dreadful kankala, pestle kapala and kankana used by asuras.
ramayan::800.english_translation: I shall grant you all these dreadful weapons: the kankala, the pestle, the kapala, and the kankana used by the asuras.
ramayan::800.translation_literal: कङ्कालम् (kankala) / मुसलम् (pestle) / घोरम् (dreadful) / कापालम् (kapala) / अथ (and then) / कङ्कणम् (kankana) / धारयन्ति (bear) / असुराः (asuras) / यानि (which) / ददामि (I grant) / एतानि (these) / सर्वशः (all together)
ramayan::800.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::800.essence: More weapons are named as the gift continues.
ramayan::800.simple_meaning: Rama is being given a set of terrible weapons associated with asuras. The passage is part of a larger list, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::800.simple_insight: Some verses simply extend the scene instead of delivering a lesson.
ramayan::800.detailed_meaning: A teacher is still listing powerful astras for Rama, one after another. This verse adds another cluster of fearsome weapons, all part of the same transfer of martial power. It supports the larger sequence rather than standing on its own.
ramayan::800.insight: It continues the inventory of weapons without adding a separate principle.

ramayan::801.verse_sanskrit: वैद्याधरं महास्त्रं च नन्दनं नाम नामतः । असिरत्नं महाबाहो ददामि च नृपात्मज । । 12713 । ।
ramayan::801.verse_hindi: O mightyarmed prince, I shall grant mahaastra, vaidyadhara and and an excellent scimitar  known as nandana.
ramayan::801.english_translation: O mighty-armed prince, I shall grant the great weapon Vaidyadhara and an excellent sword called Nandana.
ramayan::801.translation_literal: वैद्याधरम् (Vaidyadhara) / महास्त्रम् (great weapon) / च (and) / नन्दनम् (Nandana) / नाम (called) / नामतः (by name) / असिरत्नम् (excellent sword) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / ददामि (I grant) / च (and) / नृपात्मज (O prince)
ramayan::801.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::801.essence: More weapons are being bestowed before the larger conflict.
ramayan::801.simple_meaning: A speaker is listing more powerful weapons and granting them to Rama.
ramayan::801.simple_insight: Some verses are not teachings; they simply move the story forward.
ramayan::801.detailed_meaning: A divine armorer is still naming weapons for Rama, adding another great weapon and a prized sword to the growing arsenal. The verse is part of a longer grant of celestial weapons, not a self-contained teaching.
ramayan::801.insight: It adds to the inventory of weapons rather than offering a standalone lesson.

ramayan::802.verse_sanskrit: गान्धर्वमस्त्रं दयितं मानवं नाम नामतः । प्रस्वापनप्रशमने दद्मि सौरं च राघव । । 12714 । ।
ramayan::802.verse_hindi: Rama, I shall grant two much favoured weapons namely gandharvaastras, manava  astra, which induce and suppress sleep and sauraastra as well.
ramayan::802.english_translation: Rama, I shall grant the much-favoured gandharva weapon, the manava weapon, and the saura weapon as well.
ramayan::802.translation_literal: गान्धर्वम् (gandharva) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / दयितम् (much-favoured) / मानवम् (human) / नाम (called) / नामतः (by name) / प्रस्वापन-प्रशमने (for inducing sleep and for calming) / दद्मि (I grant) / सौरम् (solar) / च (and) / राघव (Rama)
ramayan::802.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::802.essence: More weapons are being named in the same ongoing grant.
ramayan::802.simple_meaning: A divine weapon-giver offers Rama several special weapons, including ones linked with sleep, calming, and solar power.
ramayan::802.simple_insight: Power is being handed over in a precise, formal way.
ramayan::802.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a larger exchange, a weapon-giver lists more astras for Rama: one tied to gandharvas, one called manava, and one linked to the sun. The verse is part of a sequence of offerings, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::802.modern_relevance: A senior expert is still naming tools one by one in a long briefing. You are hearing the inventory, not the strategy.
ramayan::802.insight: It adds to a continuing list of weapons rather than delivering a new principle.

ramayan::803.verse_sanskrit: दर्पणं शोषणं चैव सन्तापनविलापने । मदनं चैव दुर्धर्षं कन्दर्पदयितं तथा । । 12715 । । पैशाचमस्त्रं दयितं मोहनं नाम नामतः । प्रतीच्छ नरशार्दूल राजपुत्र महायशः । । 12716 । ।
ramayan::803.verse_hindi: O renowned prince, best among men, receive these astras known as darpana, soshana, santhapana, vilapana, madana astra, the unassailable one favoured by kamadeva  and the paisacha astra known as mohana favoured by demons.
ramayan::803.english_translation: O renowned prince, best among men, receive these astras known as darpana, shoshana, santapana, vilapana, madana, the unassailable one favoured by Kamadeva, and the paisacha astra known as mohana, favoured by demons.
ramayan::803.translation_literal: दर्पणं (darpana) / शोषणं (drying up) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सन्तापनविलापने (causing torment and lamentation) / मदनं (madana) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / दुर्धर्षं (hard to withstand) / कन्दर्पदयितं (dear to Kamadeva) / तथा (also) / पैशाचमस्त्रं (paisacha weapon) / दयितं (beloved) / मोहनं (causing delusion) / नाम (by name) / नामतः (by name) / प्रतीच्छ (receive) / नरशार्दूल (tiger among men) / राजपुत्र (prince) / महायशः (greatly renowned)
ramayan::803.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::803.essence: Power is being assembled, not yet used.
ramayan::803.simple_meaning: These are names of powerful weapons being handed over to Rama. The verse lists more astras and invites him to receive them.
ramayan::803.simple_insight: Some moments are only preparation. The real action is still coming.
ramayan::803.detailed_meaning: A weapon-keeper is still cataloguing divine and fearsome astras for Rama. The exchange is part of a larger transfer of power, not a finished teaching. This verse adds to the inventory before the decisive use of those weapons.
ramayan::803.modern_relevance: You are still in the briefing room, not the battlefield. Tools are being named, handed over, and made ready for what comes next.
ramayan::803.insight: It shows the verse as part of a larger sequence of armaments, not a complete lesson on its own.

ramayan::804.verse_sanskrit: तामसं नरशार्दूल सौमनं च महाबल । संवर्धं चैव दुर्धर्षं मौसलं च नृपात्मज । । 12717 । । सत्यमस्त्रं महाबाहो तथा मायाधरं परम् । घोरं तेजः प्रभं नाम परतेजोऽपकर्षणम् । । 12718 । । सौम्यास्त्रं शिशिरं नाम त्वष्टुरस्त्रं सुदामनम् । दारुणं च भगस्यापि शितेषु मथ मानवम् । । 12719 । ।
ramayan::804.verse_hindi: O tiger among men mighty prince, accept tamasa and saumanaastras, the unassailable, samavardha weapon, mausala, satyaastra, the supreme mayadhara astra, the terrible tejaprabhaastra capable of removing the energy of the opponent, a soft weapon called sisira, supremely formidable twashtus astra, Bhagas terrible shiteshuastra (sharp arrowed one) and manava astra.
ramayan::804.english_translation: O tiger among men and mighty prince, accept the tamasa and saumana astras, the unassailable samavardha weapon, the mausala, the satya astra, the supreme mayadhara astra, the terrible tejaprabha astra that can strip an opponent of power, the gentle sisira astra, the formidable twashtu astra, the terrible shiteshu astra of Bhaga, and the manava astra.
ramayan::804.translation_literal: तामसं (tamasa) / नरशार्दूल (tiger among men) / सौमनं (saumana) / च (and) / महाबल (mighty) / संवर्धं (samavardha) / चैव (and indeed) / दुर्धर्षं (unassailable) / मौसलं (mausala) / च (and) / नृपात्मज (son of a king) / सत्यमस्त्रं (satya weapon) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / तथा (also) / मायाधरं (mayadhara) / परम् (supreme) / घोरं (terrible) / तेजः प्रभं (tejaprabha) / नाम (called) / परतेजोऽपकर्षणम् (removing another's power) / सौम्यास्त्रं (gentle weapon) / शिशिरं (sisira) / नाम (called) / त्वष्टुरस्त्रं (Twashtru's weapon) / सुदामनम् (sudamana) / दारुणं (terrible) / च (and) / भगस्य (of Bhaga) / अपि (also) / शितेषु (sharp-arrowed) / मथ (and) / मानवम् (manava weapon)
ramayan::804.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::804.essence: Power here is not force alone, but the right weapon for each force.
ramayan::804.simple_meaning: A list of powerful weapons is being given to Rama. The verse names several astras and describes their special effects.
ramayan::804.simple_insight: Sometimes preparation is the real protection: know what tools exist before the crisis arrives.
ramayan::804.detailed_meaning: In the war against Ravana, Rama is being equipped with a long sequence of divine weapons. This verse continues the inventory, naming more astras and their powers. It is part of a larger ritual of arming, not a self-contained teaching.
ramayan::804.modern_relevance: Before a high-stakes presentation, you mentally rehearse every possible interruption, backup file, and answer. That quiet preparation is what this verse feels like: a hero being fully armed before the real test.
ramayan::804.insight: It shifts attention from the battle itself to the discipline of being fully equipped for it.

ramayan::805.verse_sanskrit: एतान् राम महाबाहो कामरूपान् महाबलान् । गृहाण परमोदारान् क्षिप्रमेव नृपात्मज । । 12720 । ।
ramayan::805.verse_hindi: O Rama mightyarmed prince, receive these mighty and highly exalted  astras capable of assuming at once any form at will.
ramayan::805.english_translation: O Rama, mighty-armed prince, receive these mighty and highly exalted astras capable of assuming any form at will at once.
ramayan::805.translation_literal: एतान् (these) / राम (O Rama) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed) / कामरूपान् (having any form at will) / महाबलान् (mighty) / गृहाण (receive) / परमौदारान् (highly exalted) / क्षिप्रमेव (at once) / नृपात्मज (O prince)
ramayan::805.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::805.essence: Rama is being equipped for a battle that has not yet begun.
ramayan::805.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra tells Rama to receive these powerful weapons that can take any form instantly.
ramayan::805.simple_insight: Power is being handed over with precision, not drama.
ramayan::805.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra stands before Rama and begins passing on divine weapons. This verse is part of a larger instruction, not a complete teaching by itself. The focus is on transfer: Rama is being prepared for the dangers ahead.
ramayan::805.modern_relevance: A mentor sends you a toolkit before the hard part begins. The moment is not about applause — it is about readiness.
ramayan::805.insight: It shifts attention from the weapon itself to the disciplined handing-down of capability.

ramayan::806.verse_sanskrit: स्थितस्तु प्राङ्मुखो भूत्वा शुचिर्मुनिवरस्तदा । ददौ रामाय सुप्रीतो मन्त्रग्राममनुत्तमम् । । 12721 । ।
ramayan::806.verse_hindi: Viswamitra, the greatest ascetic after the purification ritual stood with his face turned  east and happily, conferred on Rama collection of the unique mantras.
ramayan::806.english_translation: Then the pure sage, standing east-facing, gladly gave Rama the unsurpassed collection of mantras.
ramayan::806.translation_literal: स्थितस्तु (then standing) / प्राङ्मुखः (east-facing) / भूत्वा (having become) / शुचिः (pure) / मुनिवरः (great sage) / तदा (then) / ददौ (gave) / रामाय (to Rama) / सुप्रीतः (very pleased) / मन्त्रग्रामम् (collection of mantras) / अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed)
ramayan::806.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::806.essence: Power is given only after purity and readiness are proven.
ramayan::806.simple_meaning: Viswamitra, after purification, stood facing east and joyfully gave Rama a priceless set of mantras.
ramayan::806.simple_insight: Some gifts are not objects at all, but power handed on with trust.
ramayan::806.detailed_meaning: After testing Rama and Lakshmana, Viswamitra stands purified and east-facing like a priest completing a sacred handover. He then gives Rama the mantras for divine weapons. The moment matters because this is the transfer that prepares Rama for the trials ahead.
ramayan::806.modern_relevance: A mentor finally hands you the key system after weeks of watching you prove yourself. The real gift is not the tool — it is the trust behind it.
ramayan::806.insight: It shows that readiness is recognized by the one who teaches, not claimed by the one who receives.

ramayan::807.verse_sanskrit: सर्वसङ्ग्रहणं येषां दैवतैरपि दुर्लभम् । तान्यस्त्राणि तदा विप्रो राघवाय न्यवेदयत् । । 12722 । ।
ramayan::807.verse_hindi: The sage offered Rama the complete collection of those weapons which even the celestials find it difficult to acquire.
ramayan::807.english_translation: The sage offered Rama the complete collection of those weapons which even the celestials find it difficult to acquire.
ramayan::807.translation_literal: सर्वसङ्ग्रहणं (complete collection) / येषां (of which) / दैवतैरपि (even by the celestials) / दुर्लभम् (hard to obtain) / तानि (those) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / तदा (then) / विप्रः (the sage) / राघवाय (to Rama) / न्यवेदयत् (offered)
ramayan::807.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::807.essence: Rare power is given only when the receiver is ready.
ramayan::807.simple_meaning: Viswamitra gives Rama the full set of rare divine weapons, the kind even heavenly beings struggle to get.
ramayan::807.simple_insight: Great power is being placed in the hands of someone ready to bear it responsibly.
ramayan::807.detailed_meaning: After the purification ritual, Viswamitra stands before Rama and formally hands over the full collection of rare astras. This is part of Rama’s training under the sage, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::807.modern_relevance: A mentor finally trusts you with the tool everyone else treats like a prize. The gift matters less than the readiness it assumes.
ramayan::807.insight: It shifts attention from the rarity of power to the responsibility of receiving it well.

ramayan::808.verse_sanskrit: जपतस्तु मुनेस्तस्य विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः । उपतस्थुर्महार्हाणि सर्वाण्यस्त्राणि राघवम् । । 12723 । ।
ramayan::808.verse_hindi: While the sagacious ascetic Viswamitra was muttering the mystic terms of these venerable astras (addressing their respective deities), all these weapons (with their mystic power) attended on Rama.
ramayan::808.english_translation: While the wise ascetic Vishvamitra was reciting the sacred formulas, all those great weapons came to Raghava.
ramayan::808.translation_literal: जपतस्तु (while muttering) / मुनेः (of the ascetic) / तस्य (his) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Vishvamitra) / धीमतः (wise) / उपतस्थुः (approached) / महार्हाणि (highly venerable) / सर्वाणि (all) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / राघवम् (to Rama)
ramayan::808.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::808.essence: Sacred force comes when the right words are spoken rightly.
ramayan::808.simple_meaning: As Vishvamitra chanted the mantras, the sacred weapons revealed themselves and came to Rama.
ramayan::808.simple_insight: Power answers when it is called with purity and precision.
ramayan::808.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just handed Rama the secret formulas for divine weapons. As he chants, the weapons themselves gather around Rama. The scene is still part of the initiation, not the teaching itself: the sage is transferring power to the prince before the next test begins.
ramayan::808.modern_relevance: A mentor finishes the instructions, and the room goes quiet before the real challenge starts. The tools are in your hands now, but they only work if you can meet them with steadiness.
ramayan::808.insight: It shows that disciplined invocation can make hidden power available at the right moment.

ramayan::809.verse_sanskrit: ऊचुश्च मुदितास्सर्वे रामं प्राञ्जलयस्तदा । इमे स्म परमोदाराः किङ्करास्तव राघव । । 12724 । ।
ramayan::809.verse_hindi: The munificient presiding deities of the weapons with folded palms addressed these words to Rama saying, Here we are, at you disposal .
ramayan::809.english_translation: The generous presiding deities of the weapons, with folded hands, spoke to Rama: “Here we are, at your service, O Raghava.”
ramayan::809.translation_literal: ऊचुः (spoke) / च (and) / मुदिताः (delighted) / सर्वे (all) / रामम् (to Rama) / प्राञ्जलयः (with folded hands) / तदा (then) / इमे (these) / स्म (indeed) / परमोदाराः (most generous) / किङ्कराः (servants) / तव (your) / राघव (O Raghava)
ramayan::809.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::809.essence: Even great powers bow when they meet rightful use.
ramayan::809.simple_meaning: The deities linked to the weapons joyfully bow to Rama and offer themselves as his servants.
ramayan::809.simple_insight: Power becomes obedient when it meets the right holder.
ramayan::809.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just handed Rama the sacred weapons. As the rites complete, the presiding powers of those weapons appear before Rama with folded hands and declare themselves his servants. The verse marks their willing submission before Rama receives and commands them.
ramayan::809.modern_relevance: A tool you finally mastered stops feeling like a mystery and starts feeling like an extension of your hand. Skill changes the relationship: what once seemed powerful now answers to your intent.
ramayan::809.insight: It shifts the mind from owning power to being worthy of it.

ramayan::810.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च काकुत्स्थः समालभ्य च पाणिना । मानसा मे भविष्यध्वमिति तानभ्यचोदयत् । । 12725 । ।
ramayan::810.verse_hindi: Rama received the astras he felt with his hands and commanded them saying, Live in my mind (serve me whenever I remember you).
ramayan::810.english_translation: Rama received the astras, touched them with his hand, and told them, "Live in my mind and serve me whenever I remember you."
ramayan::810.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / च (and) / काकुत्स्थः (Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / समालभ्य (touching) / च (and) / पाणिना (with the hand) / मानसा (in the mind) / मे (my) / भविष्यध्वम् (become) / इति (thus) / तान् (those) / अभ्यचोदयत् (he directed/commanded)
ramayan::810.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::810.essence: True mastery keeps power obedient to the mind.
ramayan::810.simple_meaning: Rama accepts the divine weapons with respect and asks them to stay ready in his mind, under his control, whenever needed.
ramayan::810.simple_insight: Power stays clean when you hold it with restraint, not hunger.
ramayan::810.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just invoked the sacred astras, and their presiding powers appear before Rama with folded hands. Rama receives them not as trophies, but as trusted forces. He asks them to remain present in his mind, ready only when dharma calls.
ramayan::810.modern_relevance: You finally get access to the tool everyone wanted, but you do not rush to show it off. You keep it close, calm, and ready for the moment it truly matters.
ramayan::810.insight: It teaches you to hold capability with discipline, not possessiveness.

ramayan::811.verse_sanskrit: ततः प्रीतमना रामो विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् । अभिवाद्य महातेजा गमनायोपचक्रमे । । 12726 । ।
ramayan::811.verse_hindi: Thereafter, the cheerful Rama, bowed to the mighty ascetic Viswamitra and commenced his journey.
ramayan::811.english_translation: Thereafter, the cheerful Rama bowed to the mighty ascetic Viswamitra and set out on his journey.
ramayan::811.translation_literal: ततः (thereafter) / प्रीत-मनाः (with a pleased mind) / रामः (Rama) / विश्वामित्रम् (Viswamitra) / महामुनिम् (the great ascetic) / अभिवाद्य (having bowed) / महा-तेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / गमनाय (for departure) / उपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::811.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::811.essence: He moves on with gratitude after receiving what he came for.
ramayan::811.simple_meaning: Rama respectfully bows to Viswamitra and then continues on his way, pleased and ready to move forward.
ramayan::811.simple_insight: Respect and readiness can travel together.
ramayan::811.detailed_meaning: After receiving the weapons, Rama does not linger in pride. He bows to Viswamitra, the sage who has guided him, and resumes the journey with a cheerful mind. The verse marks a clean transition, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::811.modern_relevance: You finish the meeting, thank the mentor who helped you, and walk back into the day without clinging to the moment.
ramayan::811.insight: It shows how to leave a turning point with gratitude, not self-importance.

ramayan::812.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य ततोऽस्त्राणि प्रहृष्टवदनश्शुचि: । गच्छन्नेव च काकुत्स्थो विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत् । । 1281 । ।
ramayan::812.verse_hindi: After performing the purificatory rites, Rama received the weapons with a cheerful face. In the way Rama said to Viswamitra.
ramayan::812.english_translation: After performing the purificatory rites, Rama received the weapons with a cheerful face. While walking, Rama then spoke to Viswamitra.
ramayan::812.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / ततः (then) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / प्रहृष्टवदनः (with a delighted face) / शुचिः (pure, purified) / गच्छन् एव (while going) / च (and) / काकुत्स्थः (Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / अथ (then) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::812.speaker: Rama
ramayan::812.essence: He receives strength, then immediately asks how to hold it rightly.
ramayan::812.simple_meaning: Rama receives the weapons cleanly and happily, then continues walking with Viswamitra and begins to speak.
ramayan::812.simple_insight: Preparation and motion continue together; he stays composed as the next lesson begins.
ramayan::812.detailed_meaning: Rama has just accepted the sacred weapons from Viswamitra after purification. Still walking beside the sage, he turns to speak. The verse is a bridge: the gift has been received, and the next instruction is about to unfold.
ramayan::812.modern_relevance: You finish the hard part, wipe your hands, and keep moving into the next conversation. The work is not over just because one step is complete.
ramayan::812.insight: It keeps the scene moving from receiving power to asking how that power should be used.

ramayan::813.verse_sanskrit: गृहीतास्त्रोऽस्मि भगवन् दुराधर्षस्सुरैरपि । अस्त्राणां त्वहमिच्छामि संहारं मुनिपुङ्गव । । 1282 । ।
ramayan::813.verse_hindi: O venerable one, having received these weaponsI have become unassailable even by the celestials. O best of ascetics, May I know the way to withdraw these weapons.
ramayan::813.english_translation: O venerable one, having received these weapons I have become unassailable even by the celestials. O best of ascetics, may I know the way to withdraw these weapons.
ramayan::813.translation_literal: गृहीतास्त्रः (having received weapons) / अस्मि (I am) / भगवन् (venerable one) / दुराधर्षः (hard to assail) / सुरैः अपि (even by the celestials) / अस्त्राणाम् (of weapons) / तु (but) / अहम् (I) / इच्छामि (wish) / संहारम् (withdrawal) / मुनिपुङ्गव (best of ascetics)
ramayan::813.speaker: Rama
ramayan::813.essence: True strength includes knowing how to withdraw force.
ramayan::813.simple_meaning: Rama has received powerful weapons, but he asks Viswamitra how to withdraw them. Real mastery includes knowing how to stop what you have learned to use.
ramayan::813.simple_insight: Power feels safer when it comes with a clear off-switch.
ramayan::813.detailed_meaning: Rama has just received celestial weapons from Viswamitra. Instead of boasting, he immediately asks how to withdraw them. The moment shows a young warrior learning that force without control is dangerous.
ramayan::813.modern_relevance: You learn a powerful tool, a sharp reply, or a new skill—and the real question is whether you know how to put it down cleanly.
ramayan::813.insight: It shifts the mind from possession of power to responsibility for its restraint.

ramayan::814.verse_sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । संहारं व्याजहाराथ धृतिमान् सुव्रतश्शुचि: । । 1283 । ।
ramayan::814.verse_hindi: To these words spoken by Rama, maharshi Viswamitra who was patient practitioner of vows and pure taught the withdrawl mantra.
ramayan::814.english_translation: To these words spoken by Rama, the great sage Viswamitra, steadfast in vows and purity, then taught the withdrawal mantra.
ramayan::814.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / ब्रुवति (speaking) / काकुत्स्थे (to Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (great sage) / संहारम् (withdrawal, recalling) / व्याजहार (uttered, taught) / अथ (then) / धृतिमान् (steadfast) / सुव्रतः (well-vowed) / शुचिः (pure)
ramayan::814.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::814.essence: True mastery includes the power to withdraw what you can unleash.
ramayan::814.simple_meaning: Viswamitra answers Rama by teaching him the mantra that withdraws the weapons he has just received.
ramayan::814.simple_insight: Power is not only about releasing force; it is also about knowing how to stop it.
ramayan::814.detailed_meaning: Rama has just received divine weapons from Viswamitra and asks for the means to draw them back. The sage, calm and disciplined, responds by teaching the withdrawal mantra. This is a practical moment in Rama's training, not a teaching statement on its own.
ramayan::814.modern_relevance: You learn a powerful tool, then realize you also need the discipline to shut it down cleanly.
ramayan::814.insight: It teaches that mastery includes restraint, not just acquisition.

ramayan::815.verse_sanskrit: सत्यवन्तं सत्यकीर्तिं धृष्टं रभसमेव च । प्रतिहारतरं नाम पराङ्मुखमवाङ्मुखम् । । 1284 । । लक्षाक्षविषमौ चैव दृढनाभसुनाभकौ । दशाक्षशतवक्त्रौ च दशशीर्षशतोदरौ । । 1285 । । पद्मनाभमहानाभौ दुन्दुनाभसुनाभकौ । ज्योतिषं कृशनं चैव नैराश्यविमलावुभौ । । 1286 । । योगन्धरहरिद्रौ च दैत्यप्रशमनौतथा । सार्चिर्माली धृतिर्माली वृत्तिमान् रुचिरस्तथा । । 1287 । । पितृसौमनसं चैव विधूतमकरावुभौ । करवीरकरं चैव धनधान्यौ च राघव । । 1288 । । कामरूपं कामरुचिं मोहमावरणं तथा । जृम्भकं सर्वनाभं च सन्तानवरणौ तथा । । 1289 । । भृशाश्वतनयान् राम भास्वरान्कामरूपिण: । प्रतीच्छ मम भद्रं ते पात्रभूतोऽसि राघव । । 12810 । ।
ramayan::815.verse_hindi: O Rama the descendant of Raghu, receive from me the effulgent weapons who are the sons of Bhrusasva and who are capable of changing forms at will. They are  Satyavanta, Satyakirti, Dhrishta, Rabhasa, Pratiharatara, Paranmukha (turned back wards), Avanmukha (turned downwards), Lakshaksha, Vishama, Drudhanabha and Sunabha, Dasaksha, Satavaktra, Dasasheersha and Satodara, Padamanabha and Mahanabha, Dundunabha and Sunabhaka, Jyotisha, Krusanam, both Nairasya and  Vimala, Yogandhara, Haridradaitya, Prasamana, Sarchirmali, Dhri, Mali, Vrtiimanta, also Ruchira, Pitrusaumanasa, bothVidhuta Makara, Karaveera Kara, Dhana, Dhanya, Kama Roopa, Kamaruchi, Moha, also Avarana, Jrumbhaka, Sarvanabha, also Santhana and Varuna. You are worthy of receiving these weapons. May you prosper.
ramayan::815.english_translation: O Rama, descendant of Raghu, receive from me these radiant weapons, the sons of Bhrigusva, who can change form at will: Satyavanta, Satyakirti, Dhrishta, Rabhasa, Pratiharatara, Paranmukha, Avanmukha, Lakshaksha, Vishama, Drudhanabha, Sunabha, Dasaksha, Satavaktra, Dasasheersha, Satodara, Padmanabha, Mahanabha, Dundunabha, Sunabhaka, Jyotisha, Krishana, Nairasya, Vimala, Yogandhara, Haridra, Prasamana, Sarchirmali, Dhriti, Mali, Vrittimanta, Ruchira, Pitrusaumanasa, Vidhuta-makara, Karaveera-kara, Dhana, Dhanya, Kamarupa, Kamaruchi, Moha, Avarana, Jrumbhaka, Sarvanabha, Santhana, and Varuna. You are worthy of receiving these weapons. May you prosper.
ramayan::815.translation_literal: सत्यवन्तम् (truthful) / सत्यकीर्तिम् (true-famed) / धृष्टम् (bold) / रभसम् (impetuous) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / प्रतिहारतरम् (warding-off) / नाम (by name) / पराङ्मुखम् (facing away) / अवाङ्मुखम् (facing downward) / लक्षाक्षविषमौ (Lakshaksha and Vishama) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / दृढनाभसुनाभकौ (Drudhanabha and Sunabha) / दशाक्षशतवक्त्रौ (ten-eyed and hundred-faced) / च (and) / दशशीर्षशतोदरौ (ten-headed and hundred-bellied) / पद्मनाभमहानाभौ (Padmanabha and Mahanabha) / दुन्दुनाभसुनाभकौ (Dundunabha and Sunabhaka) / ज्योतिषम् (radiance) / कृशनम् (dark) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / नैराश्यविमलौ (despair-free and pure) / उभौ (both) / योगन्धरहरिद्रौ (Yogandhara and Haridra) / च (and) / दैत्यप्रशमनौ (subduers of beings of shadow) / तथा (and) / सार्चिर्माली (with garlands of flame) / धृतिमाली (garlanded with steadfastness) / वृत्तिमान् (endowed with conduct) / रुचिरः (beautiful) / तथा (also) / पितृसौमनसम् (father-pleasing) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / विधूतमकरौ (shaken-crocodile) / उभौ (both) / करवीरकरम् (oleander-handed) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / धनधान्यौ (wealth and grain) / च (and) / राघव (O descendant of Raghu) / कामरूपम् (form-changing) / कामरुचिम् (desire-forming) / मोहम् (delusion) / आवरणम् (covering) / तथा (and) / जृम्भकम् (yawning) / सर्वनाभम् (all-navelled) / च (and) / सन्तानवरणौ (progeny-covering) / तथा (and) / भृशाश्वतनयान् (sons of Bhrusasva) / राम (O Rama) / भास्वरान् (radiant) / कामरूपिणः (shape-shifting) / प्रतीच्छ (receive) / मम (from me) / भद्रम् (good fortune) / ते (to you) / पात्रभूतः (fit recipient) / असि (you are) / राघव (O descendant of Raghu)
ramayan::815.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::815.essence: A worthy student is given power only after proving readiness.
ramayan::815.simple_meaning: Viswamitra names a long set of radiant, shape-shifting weapons and offers them to Rama, saying Rama is worthy to receive them. The passage is the handover itself, not the teaching around it.
ramayan::815.simple_insight: Power is being entrusted, not praised from a distance.
ramayan::815.detailed_meaning: After Rama asks for the withdrawal of the weapons, Viswamitra begins naming the astras one by one and offering them to him. The moment is ceremonial and practical: the teacher is placing dangerous power into the hands of a student who has earned it.
ramayan::815.modern_relevance: A mentor stops explaining and finally hands you the responsibility. The praise matters less than the trust behind it.
ramayan::815.insight: It marks the transfer of capability from teacher to student, showing readiness through trust received.

ramayan::816.verse_sanskrit: बाढमित्येव काकुत्स्थ: प्रहृष्टेनान्तारात्मना । दिव्यभास्वरदेहाश्च मूर्तिमन्तस्सुखप्रदा: । । 12811केचिदङ्गारसदृशा: केचिद्धूमोपमास्तथा । चन्द्रार्कसदृशा: केचित्प्रह्वाञ्जलिपुटास्तथा । । 12812 । । रामं प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वाऽब्रुवन् मधुरभाषिण: । इमे स्म नरशार्दूल शाधि किं करवाम ते । । 12813 । ।
ramayan::816.verse_hindi: Certainly said Rama, and with a delighted heart received the astras. Some of the astra devatas were coat black, some like smoke, some resembled rays of Sun or Moon. Assuming corporal forms, with shining, divine bodies, those weapons the their bodies bent down and palms folder they spoke to Rama in a gentle voice: O tiger among men, here we are, What can we do for you?
ramayan::816.english_translation: Certainly, said Rama, and with a delighted heart received the astras. Some of the astras appeared dark as charcoal, some like smoke, some like the sun and moon. Taking bodily forms with shining, wondrous bodies, they stood with folded hands and said to Rama in a gentle voice: "O tiger among men, here we are. What can we do for you?"
ramayan::816.translation_literal: बाढम् (certainly) / इति (thus) / एव (indeed) / काकुत्स्थः (Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / प्रहृष्टेन (with delighted) / अन्तरात्मना (inner being/mind) / दिव्यभास्वरदेहाः (having radiant divine bodies) / च (and) / मूर्तिमन्तः (embodied) / सुखप्रदाः (bringing ease) / केचित् (some) / अङ्गारसदृशाः (like charcoal) / केचित् (some) / धूमोपमाः (like smoke) / तथा (and so) / चन्द्रार्कसदृशाः (like the moon and sun) / केचित् (some) / प्रह्वाञ्जलिपुटाः (bowed with folded hands) / तथा (likewise) / रामम् (to Rama) / प्राञ्जलयः (with folded hands) / भूत्वा (having become) / अब्रुवन् (they spoke) / मधुरभाषिणः (speaking sweetly) / इमे (here we are) / स्म (indeed) / नरशार्दूल (tiger among men) / शाधि (command) / किम् (what) / करवाम (shall we do) / ते (for you)
ramayan::816.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::816.essence: Even great power becomes humble when it serves dharma.
ramayan::816.simple_meaning: Rama gladly accepts the divine weapons, and the weapons themselves appear before him in radiant forms, asking how they may serve him.
ramayan::816.simple_insight: Power is most trustworthy when it bows to right purpose.
ramayan::816.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just handed Rama the sacred weapons. Rama receives them with joy, and the weapons personify themselves as shining beings. They do not dominate him; they stand ready to serve, showing that true power answers to dharma.
ramayan::816.modern_relevance: A new tool, title, or responsibility lands in your hands, and it could easily inflate you. The better sign is whether it makes you more accountable, not more arrogant.
ramayan::816.insight: It shifts power from possession to service: strength is meant to be directed, not hoarded.

ramayan::817.verse_sanskrit: मानसा: कार्यकालेषु साहाय्यं मे करिष्यथ । गम्यतामिति तानाह यथेष्टं रघुनन्दन: । । 12814 । ।
ramayan::817.verse_hindi: Rama spoke to them (astra devatas) saying, Reside in my mind and render assistance  in times of need. Now you can go according to your will.
ramayan::817.english_translation: Rama spoke to them, saying, "Reside in my mind and help me in times of need. Now go as you wish."
ramayan::817.translation_literal: मानसा: (in the mind) / कार्यकालेषु (in times of need) / साहाय्यम् (help) / मे (to me) / करिष्यथ (you will do) । / गम्यताम् (let it go) / इति (thus) / तान् (to them) / आह (said) / यथेष्टम् (as desired) / रघुनन्दनः (Rama, delight of the Raghu line)
ramayan::817.speaker: Rama
ramayan::817.essence: Keep what is needed in mind, and release the rest.
ramayan::817.simple_meaning: Rama asks the astras to stay with him in memory and help when needed, then sends them away freely.
ramayan::817.simple_insight: True help does not need possession. What matters is readiness, not control.
ramayan::817.detailed_meaning: Rama has just received the divine weapons from their living presences. Instead of clinging to them, he asks them to remain available in his mind for the right moment. Then he releases them, showing calm mastery rather than greed.
ramayan::817.modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation and stop rehearsing it. You keep the lesson, not the grip. What helps you most is what you can call on without clinging.
ramayan::817.insight: It shifts you from holding tools tightly to trusting readiness at the right moment.

ramayan::818.verse_sanskrit: अथ ते राममामन्त्ऱ्य कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम् । एवमस्त्विति काकुत्स्थमुक्त्वाजग्मुर्यथाऽगतम् । । 12815 । ।
ramayan::818.verse_hindi: Thereafter those devatas having said, Be it so, circumambulated Rama, took leave of him and returned to their respective abodes from where they had come.
ramayan::818.english_translation: Thereafter those radiant weapon-powers took leave of Rama, circled him in reverence, said, "So be it," and returned as they had come.
ramayan::818.translation_literal: अथ (then) / ते (those) / रामम् (to Rama) / आमन्त्र्य (having taken leave) / कृत्वा (having done) / च (and) / अपि (also) / प्रदक्षिणम् (circumambulation) / एवम् (thus) / अस्तु (so be it) / इति (saying) / काकुत्स्थम् (to the descendant of Kakutstha) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / जग्मुः (they went) / यथागतम् (as they had come)
ramayan::818.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::818.essence: Power is handed over, then quietly withdraws.
ramayan::818.simple_meaning: The weapon-powers respectfully leave Rama and go back to where they came from.
ramayan::818.simple_insight: Some gifts are meant to be carried lightly, not clutched.
ramayan::818.detailed_meaning: After Rama receives the divine weapons from the astra-devatas, they bow to him, grant their assent, and depart. The scene closes the brief exchange and prepares for the next step in Vishwamitra's instruction.
ramayan::818.modern_relevance: A meeting ends, the decision is made, and everyone stands up from the table. The real work begins only after the formalities are over.
ramayan::818.insight: It marks a transition: received power must now be used under guidance, not admired.

ramayan::819.verse_sanskrit: स च तान् राघवो ज्ञात्वा विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् । गच्छन्नेवाथ मधुरं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 12816 । ।
ramayan::819.verse_hindi: After having acquired the knowledge of the weapons Rama addressed maharshi Viswamitra in gentle and soft words while walking along with him.
ramayan::819.english_translation: After gaining knowledge of the weapons, Rama spoke to the great sage Vishwamitra in gentle, soft words as he walked along with him.
ramayan::819.translation_literal: स (he) / च (and) / तान् (those) / राघवः (Raghava, Rama) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / विश्वामित्रम् (Vishvamitra) / महामुनिम् (great sage) / गच्छन् (walking) / एव (indeed) / अथ (then) / मधुरम् (sweetly) / श्लक्ष्णम् (softly/gently) / वचनम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::819.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::819.essence: Strength remains noble when it speaks gently.
ramayan::819.simple_meaning: Rama, walking with Vishvamitra, spoke gently after understanding the weapons he had received.
ramayan::819.simple_insight: Power does not need harshness. Even after gaining strength, you can remain gentle.
ramayan::819.detailed_meaning: Rama has just received the divine weapons and watched the powers depart. Still walking beside Vishvamitra, he speaks softly, showing that new power has not made him proud or loud. The moment is a small sign of his steady character.
ramayan::819.modern_relevance: You finally got the promotion, the praise, the authority you wanted — and the first thing you notice is whether your voice has changed. Real strength does not need to announce itself.
ramayan::819.insight: It shows that true capability can stay calm, courteous, and controlled.

ramayan::820.verse_sanskrit: किन्न्वेतन्मेघसङ्काशं पर्वतस्याविदूरत: । वृक्षषण्डमितो भाति परं कौतूहलं हि मे । । 12817 । । दर्शनीयं मृगाकीर्णं मनोरममतीव च । नानाप्रकारैश्शकुनैर्वल्गुनादैरलङ्कृतम् । । 12818 । ।
ramayan::820.verse_hindi: From this side of the mountain, not  faroff from here stand shining and goodlooking trees resembling clouds. It is replete scattered with animals, pleasing to the mind and extremely beautiful. It is adorned with various kinds of birds singing sweetly. What could be this? I am very curious to know.
ramayan::820.english_translation: From here, not far from the mountain, I can see a cluster of trees shining like clouds. It is full of deer, beautiful to look at, and adorned with many kinds of birds singing sweetly. What could this be? I am very curious to know.
ramayan::820.translation_literal: किम् (what) / नु (indeed) / एतत् (this) / मेघ-सङ्काशम् (cloud-like) / पर्वतस्य (of the mountain) / अविदूरतः (not far) / वृक्ष-षण्डम् (cluster of trees) / इतः (from here) / भाति (shines) / परम् (very) / कौतूहलम् (curiosity) / हि (indeed) / मे (to me) / दर्शनीयम् (worth seeing) / मृग-आकीर्णम् (filled with deer) / मनोरमम् (pleasing to the mind) / अतीव (extremely) / च (and) / नाना-प्रकारैः (of many kinds) / शकुनैः (with birds) / वल्गु-नादैः (with sweet sounds) / अलङ्कृतम् (adorned)
ramayan::820.speaker: Rama
ramayan::820.essence: Wonder begins when you stop assuming you already know.
ramayan::820.simple_meaning: Rama notices a beautiful grove near the mountain and asks what it is. He is curious, not certain, and turns to his guide for an explanation.
ramayan::820.simple_insight: Curiosity can be the first sign that you are paying attention instead of rushing past what is in front of you.
ramayan::820.detailed_meaning: Rama is travelling with Vishwamitra when he spots a striking grove near the mountain — full of deer, birds, and dense trees. He pauses and asks what place this is, showing his alertness and wonder before the teacher answers.
ramayan::820.modern_relevance: You’re on a long drive, half-tired, and something unexpected catches your eye beyond the road. Instead of scrolling past it in your head, you stop and ask what you’re really looking at.
ramayan::820.insight: It shifts the mind from automatic passing to attentive questioning.

ramayan::821.verse_sanskrit: निस्सृता: स्म मुनिश्रेष्ठ कान्ताराद्रोमहर्षणात् । अनया त्ववगच्छामि देशस्य सुखवत्तया । । 12819 । । सर्वं मे शंस भगवन् कस्याश्रमपदं त्विदम् ।
ramayan::821.verse_hindi: O best of acetics, I think we have come out of that  awesome (horripilating) forest because of the pleasant feeling experienced in this region. Whose hermitage is this? O Revered one tell me.
ramayan::821.english_translation: O best of ascetics, I think we have come out of that dreadful forest because this region feels pleasant. Tell me everything, Lord: whose hermitage is this?
ramayan::821.translation_literal: निस्सृता: (come out) / स्म (indeed) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (O best of ascetics) / कान्तारात् (from the forest) / रोमहर्षणात् (hair-raising, dreadful) / अनया (by this) / तु (indeed) / अवगच्छामि (I understand) / देशस्य (of the place) / सुखवत्तया (by its pleasantness) / सर्वम् (everything) / मे (to me) / शंस (tell) / भगवन् (Lord, revered one) / कस्य (whose) / आश्रमपदम् (hermitage) / तु (indeed) / इदम् (this)
ramayan::821.speaker: Rama
ramayan::821.essence: Peaceful surroundings can signal safety after fear.
ramayan::821.simple_meaning: Rama notices the landscape has changed from frightening forest to a calmer, welcoming place, and he asks whose hermitage they have reached.
ramayan::821.simple_insight: A peaceful place can feel like a threshold after fear.
ramayan::821.detailed_meaning: Rama and Vishwamitra are moving through the forest after a dangerous stretch of travel. The harshness gives way to a gentler atmosphere, and Rama senses they have entered sacred ground. He asks whose hermitage they have reached.
ramayan::821.modern_relevance: After hours of tense driving through dark roads, you suddenly reach a quiet lane with lights and trees. Your body knows before your mind does: the danger has eased.
ramayan::821.insight: It trains you to read the atmosphere around you and notice when danger has passed.

ramayan::822.verse_sanskrit: सम्प्राप्ता यत्र ते पापा ब्रह्मघ्ना दुष्टचारिण: । । 12820 । । तव यज्ञस्य विघ्नाय दुरात्मानो महामुने । भगवन् तस्य को देशस्सा यत्र तव याज्ञिकी । । 12821 । । रक्षितव्या क्रिया ब्रह्मन्मया वध्याश्च राक्षसा: । एतत्सर्वं मुनिश्रेष्ठ श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो । । 12822 । ।
ramayan::822.verse_hindi: O great ascetic, O venerable brahmana, from where do those slayers of brahmanas, doers of cruel acts, wickedminded and sinful persons come from and cause obstacles to your sacrifice? Where is that sacrificial place required to be protected by me? Where are these rakshasas required to be slain? O best of ascetics, I would like to hear from you.
ramayan::822.english_translation: O great ascetic, O venerable brahmana, from where do those slayers of brahmanas, doers of cruel acts, wicked-minded and evil persons come from and obstruct your sacrifice? Where is the sacrificial place that I must protect? Where are those rakshasas to be slain? O best of ascetics, I wish to hear all this from you.
ramayan::822.translation_literal: सम्प्राप्ता (have come) / यत्र (where) / ते (those) / पापा (evil ones) / ब्रह्मघ्ना (slayers of brahmanas) / दुष्टचारिण: (of evil conduct) / तव (your) / यज्ञस्य (of sacrifice) / विघ्नाय (for obstruction) / दुरात्मानो (wicked-minded ones) / महामुने (O great ascetic) / भगवन् (O venerable one) / तस्य (of that) / को (what) / देशस्सा (place) / यत्र (where) / तव (your) / याज्ञिकी (sacrificial) / रक्षितव्या (to be protected) / क्रिया (rite) / ब्रह्मन् (O brahmana) / मया (by me) / वध्याश्च (and to be slain) / राक्षसा: (rakshasas) / एतत्सर्वं (all this) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (O best of ascetics) / श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं (I wish to hear) / प्रभो (O lord)
ramayan::822.speaker: Rama
ramayan::822.essence: Duty starts by asking where you must stand and what you must defend.
ramayan::822.simple_meaning: Rama asks Viswamitra where the demons come from, where the sacrifice must be protected, and where he should fight them.
ramayan::822.simple_insight: Clear duty begins with clear questions. You cannot protect what you have not understood.
ramayan::822.detailed_meaning: Rama is with Viswamitra in the forest, just after noticing that they have reached a calmer region. He now asks the sage where the sacrificial work is threatened, where he must stand guard, and where the rakshasas should be fought.
ramayan::822.modern_relevance: Before the meeting starts, you ask the senior colleague exactly where the problem is and what you are responsible for. Real help begins when you stop guessing and define the task.
ramayan::822.insight: It shifts action from vague concern to precise responsibility.

ramayan::823.verse_sanskrit: अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य तद्वनं परिपृच्छत: । विश्वामित्रो महातेजा व्याख्यातुमुपचक्रमे । । 1291 । ।
ramayan::823.verse_hindi: The highly lustrous Viswamitra heard the words of Rama of immeasurable prowess. On his (Ramas) query about the forest, Viswamitra explains.
ramayan::823.english_translation: The highly lustrous Viswamitra, hearing Rama's question about that forest, began to explain.
ramayan::823.translation_literal: अथ (then) / तस्य (his) / अप्रमेयस्य (of immeasurable) / तद्वनं (that forest) / परिपृच्छत: (of the one asking about) / विश्वामित्रो (Viswamitra) / महातेजा (highly lustrous) / व्याख्यातुम् (to explain) / उपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::823.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::823.essence: A question opens the door to the forest's hidden story.
ramayan::823.simple_meaning: Viswamitra begins explaining the forest after Rama asks about it.
ramayan::823.simple_insight: Curiosity opens the next layer of the story.
ramayan::823.detailed_meaning: Rama asks Viswamitra about the forest they have reached. The sage, radiant and attentive, begins to explain what this place means and why it matters. The verse simply turns the conversation toward revelation.
ramayan::823.modern_relevance: You ask a careful question in the middle of a journey, and someone finally names what you are standing in front of. That is how understanding begins.
ramayan::823.insight: It marks the shift from travel to explanation, not a teaching in itself.

ramayan::824.verse_sanskrit: इह राम महाबाहो विष्णुर्देववर: प्रभु: । वर्षाणि सुबहूनीह तथा युगशतानि च । । 1292 । । तपश्चरणयोगार्थमुवास सुमहातपा: ।
ramayan::824.verse_hindi: O mightyarmed Rama Lord Visnu, the foremost among the gods, and master the great ascetic lived here carrying out yogic practices and penance for innumerable years  constituting hundreds of yugas.
ramayan::824.english_translation: O mighty-armed Rama, Lord Vishnu, the foremost among the gods, and master, the great ascetic lived here for many years, even for hundreds of ages, practicing severe austerities.
ramayan::824.translation_literal: इह (here) / राम (Rama) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / देववरः (foremost among the gods) / प्रभुः (master) / वर्षाणि (years) / सुबहूनीह (many here) / तथा (and) / युगशतानि (hundreds of ages) / च (and) / तपश्चरणयोगार्थम् (for the purpose of ascetic practice and yoga) / उवास (lived) / सुमहातपाः (the great ascetic)
ramayan::824.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::824.essence: Even Vishnu is remembered here as one who chose austerity.
ramayan::824.simple_meaning: This place is sacred because Vishnu himself once lived here for ages doing severe penance.
ramayan::824.simple_insight: Power and restraint are not opposites; sometimes the highest presence is shown through discipline.
ramayan::824.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is answering Rama’s question about the forest. He identifies this place as the former hermitage of Vishnu, where the great ascetic stayed for countless years in penance. The setting becomes holy because the divine presence once practiced austerity here.
ramayan::824.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone once rebuilt their life in silence. The space feels different, not because of decoration, but because of what was endured there.
ramayan::824.insight: It shifts attention from sacred place to sacred practice, showing that discipline can make a location luminous.

ramayan::825.verse_sanskrit: एष पूर्वाश्रमो राम वामनस्य महात्मन: । । 1293 । । सिद्धाश्रम इति ख्यातस्सिद्धो ह्यत्र महातपा: ।
ramayan::825.verse_hindi: O Rama this was the hermitage of glorious Vamana. The great sage her performed his ascetic pratices here, hence it is known as siddhashrama.
ramayan::825.english_translation: O Rama, this was the former hermitage of the glorious Vamana. The great ascetic attained success here, so it is known as Siddhashrama.
ramayan::825.translation_literal: एष (this) / पूर्वाश्रमो (former hermitage) / राम (O Rama) / वामनस्य (of Vamana) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / सिद्धाश्रमः (Siddhashrama) / इति (thus) / ख्यातः (known) / सिद्धः (successful/attained) / हि (indeed) / अत्र (here) / महातपाः (great ascetic)
ramayan::825.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::825.essence: A place becomes sacred through fulfilled effort.
ramayan::825.simple_meaning: This hermitage is called Siddhashrama because a great ascetic completed his practice here and made the place renowned.
ramayan::825.simple_insight: Your effort can transform a place, and leave a lasting mark long after you move on.
ramayan::825.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra is leading Rama through a forest tied to sacred history. He points out that this hermitage once belonged to Vamana, who completed intense practice here. The place is remembered because spiritual striving succeeded here.
ramayan::825.modern_relevance: You return to a room where you once broke through fear, finished a hard project, or changed your habits. The room feels different because you changed there.
ramayan::825.insight: It shifts attention from the place itself to the discipline that gave the place its meaning.

ramayan::826.verse_sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु राजा वैरोचनिर्बलि: । । 1294 । । निर्जित्य दैवतगणान् सेन्द्रांश्च समरुद्गणान् । कारयामास तद्राज्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुत: । । 1295 । ।
ramayan::826.verse_hindi: During the period Visnu (in the incarnation of Vamana) was observing austerities at this hermitage, king Bali, son of Virochana, having vanquished Indra and maruts and devatas ruled this kingdom and became famous in all the three worlds (for his prowess and generosity.)
ramayan::826.english_translation: During the period Vishnu, in the incarnation of Vamana, was observing austerities at this hermitage, king Bali, son of Virochana, having vanquished Indra, the Maruts, and the devas, ruled this kingdom and became famous in all the three worlds for his prowess and generosity.
ramayan::826.translation_literal: एतस्मिन् (in this) / एव (only) / काले (time) / तु (indeed) / राजा (king) / वैरोचनिः (son of Virochana) / बलिः (Bali) / निर्जित्य (having conquered) / दैवतगणान् (groups of deities) / सेन्द्रान् (with Indra) / च (and) / समरुद्गणान् (with the Marut hosts) / कारयामास (caused to be ruled) / तद्राज्यम् (that kingdom) / त्रिषु (in the three) / लोकेषु (worlds) / विश्रुतः (famous)
ramayan::826.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::826.essence: Great power can peak just before it meets its limit.
ramayan::826.simple_meaning: Bali had already conquered the gods and was ruling the three worlds when Vamana was doing austerities there.
ramayan::826.simple_insight: Power can be at its height just before it is tested.
ramayan::826.detailed_meaning: At Vamana's hermitage, the story shifts to the other side of the balance: Bali, grandson of Prahlada, has defeated Indra and the celestial hosts and now rules the three worlds. The verse sets the stage for the coming encounter by showing how complete his power already is.
ramayan::826.modern_relevance: You can be at the top of your game, publicly admired, and still be standing on the edge of a turning point you cannot yet see.
ramayan::826.insight: It frames success as temporary context, not final security.

ramayan::827.verse_sanskrit: बलेस्तु यजमानस्य देवास्साग्निपुरोगमा: । समागम्य स्वयं चैव विष्णुमूचुरिहाश्रमे । । 1296 । ।
ramayan::827.verse_hindi: While Bali was performing the sacrifice (to confirm his position as lord of the three worlds), the devas got together with Agni in the forefront and approached Lord Visnu
ramayan::827.english_translation: While Bali was performing the sacrifice, the devas, with Agni at their head, gathered and approached Vishnu in the hermitage.
ramayan::827.translation_literal: बलेः (of Bali) / तु (indeed) / यजमानस्य (while sacrificing) / देवाः (the devas) / स अग्नि-पुरोगमाḥ (with Agni at the front) / समागम्य (having gathered) / स्वयं (themselves) / च एव (and indeed) / विष्णुम् (to Vishnu) / ऊचुः (spoke) / इह (here) / आश्रमे (in the hermitage)
ramayan::827.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::827.essence: The devas seek help before Bali’s ritual reaches its end.
ramayan::827.simple_meaning: The devas, led by Agni, came together and went to Vishnu while Bali was in the middle of a sacrifice.
ramayan::827.simple_insight: Great events often begin with a quiet gathering before the decisive request is made.
ramayan::827.detailed_meaning: At Siddhashrama, Bali is carrying out a powerful sacrifice after defeating the devas. The devas, led by Agni, gather and approach Vishnu to ask for help before the ritual is complete. This verse is a setup for the appeal that follows.
ramayan::827.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the team makes the one request that changes everything. The real turning point often happens in the approach, not the answer.
ramayan::827.insight: It frames crisis as collective action: when force fails, the wise seek a higher resolution before the moment closes.

ramayan::828.verse_sanskrit: बलिर्वैरोचनिर्विष्णो यजते यज्ञमुत्तमम् । असमाप्ते क्रतौ तस्मिन् स्वकार्यमभिपद्यताम् । । 1297 । ।
ramayan::828.verse_hindi: O Visnu son of Virochana is performing a great sacrifice. Before its completion, our purpose ought to be achieved.
ramayan::828.english_translation: O Vishnu, son of Virochana, is performing a great sacrifice. Before its completion, our purpose ought to be achieved.
ramayan::828.translation_literal: बलिः (Bali) / वैरोचनिः (son of Virochana) / विष्णो (O Vishnu) / यजते (is performing sacrifice) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / उत्तमम् (great) / असमाप्ते (unfinished) / क्रतौ (in the sacrifice) / तस्मिन् (in that) / स्वकार्यं (our own task) / अभिपद्यताम् (let it be undertaken)
ramayan::828.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::828.simple_meaning: The gods say they should act now, before Bali's sacrifice is finished and his power becomes secure.
ramayan::828.simple_insight: Timing matters: some chances vanish if you wait too long.
ramayan::828.detailed_meaning: The devas have gathered with Vishnu while Bali's sacrifice is underway. They know his ritual is granting him immense power, so they urge action before the rite is complete and his position becomes unshakable.
ramayan::828.modern_relevance: You see the opening before a difficult meeting begins, before the room hardens against you. If you wait until everything is settled, your chance may already be gone.
ramayan::828.insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to seizing the right moment before conditions close.

ramayan::829.verse_sanskrit: ये चैनमभिवर्तन्ते याचितार इतस्तत: । यच्च यत्र यथावच्च सर्वं तेभ्य: प्रयच्छति । । 1298 । ।
ramayan::829.verse_hindi: He is granting the seekers whatever, wherever and in whichever maner they, coming from here and there approach him for favour.
ramayan::829.english_translation: He grants seekers whatever they ask for, wherever they ask, and in whatever way they ask.
ramayan::829.translation_literal: ये (who) / च (and) / एनम् (him) / अभिवर्तन्ते (approach) / याचितारः (seekers) / इतस्तत: (from here and there) / यत् (what) / च (and) / यत्र (where) / यथा (how) / च (and) / सर्वम् (everything) / तेभ्य: (to them) / प्रयच्छति (gives)
ramayan::829.speaker: Devas
ramayan::829.essence: True generosity gives fully, without narrowing the request.
ramayan::829.simple_meaning: He gives people whatever they ask for, no matter where they come from or how they ask.
ramayan::829.simple_insight: Real generosity answers need without making it small.
ramayan::829.detailed_meaning: The devas are pleading over Bali's sacrifice and praising Vishnu's readiness to respond to every seeker. This line supports their request for Vishnu to act for the world's welfare by showing his boundless willingness to give.
ramayan::829.modern_relevance: Someone messages you from three different apps, each with a different need, and you still respond with care. The verse points to a generosity that does not get tired of being asked.
ramayan::829.insight: It shifts the mind from guarding resources to meeting need openly.

ramayan::830.verse_sanskrit: स त्वं सुरहितार्थाय मायायोगमुपागत: । वामनत्वं गतो विष्णो कुरु कल्याणमुत्तमम् । । 1299 । ।
ramayan::830.verse_hindi: O Visnu perform this supreme, auspicious act assuming the form of a dwarf through, the power of illusion for the welfare of the devatas.
ramayan::830.english_translation: O Vishnu, for the welfare of the radiant beings, assume the dwarf form through the power of illusion and do this supreme auspicious act.
ramayan::830.translation_literal: स (that) / त्वं (you) / सुरहितार्थाय (for the welfare of the radiant beings) / मायायोगम् (the power of illusion) / उपागत: (having taken up) / वामनत्वम् (dwarf-hood) / गतः (gone, assumed) / विष्णो (O Vishnu) / कुरु (do) / कल्याणम् (auspicious good) / उत्तमम् (supreme)
ramayan::830.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::830.essence: True power can choose a smaller form to accomplish a larger good.
ramayan::830.simple_meaning: Vishnu is asked to take the form of a dwarf and act for the welfare of the radiant beings.
ramayan::830.simple_insight: Real power does not need to look grand. It can work quietly for the good of others.
ramayan::830.detailed_meaning: The radiant beings have already asked Vishnu to intervene against Bali's sacrifice. Now the request becomes specific: take the dwarf form, use maya, and complete the rescue. This is the moment the divine plan turns into a deliberate descent.
ramayan::830.modern_relevance: You walk into a room knowing your ego wants to look impressive, but the real task is to help quietly. Sometimes the best move is to become less visible so something larger can happen.
ramayan::830.insight: It shifts attention from status to effective service: the right form is the one that lets the good happen.

ramayan::831.verse_sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम कश्यपोऽग्निसमप्रभ: । अदित्या सहितो राम दीप्यमान इवौजसा । । 12910 । । देवीसहायो भगवान् दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रकम् । व्रतं समाप्य वरदं तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् । । 12911 । ।
ramayan::831.verse_hindi: O Rama in the mean time revered Kasyapa resplendent like the god of fire radiating lustre with Aditi who had completed a thousand divine years of austerities pleased (with her penance) the conferer of boons, Lord Madhusudana (Visnu) (And she said to Visnu):
ramayan::831.english_translation: Meanwhile, Rama, Kasyapa, brilliant like fire, came with Aditi. Having completed a thousand divine years of austerity, the goddess, accompanied by the divine, pleased the boon-giver, Madhusudana.
ramayan::831.translation_literal: एतस्मिन् (in this meanwhile) / अन्तरे (interval) / राम (O Rama) / कश्यपः (Kasyapa) / अग्निसमप्रभः (resplendent like fire) / अदित्या (with Aditi) / सहितः (accompanied) / राम (O Rama) / दीप्यमानः (shining) / इव (like) / ओजसा (with splendour) / देवीसहायः (accompanied by the divine) / भगवान् (the blessed one) / दिव्यम् (divine) / वर्षसहस्रकम् (thousand years) / व्रतम् (austerity) / समाप्य (having completed) / वरदम् (boon-giver) / तुष्टाव (praised) / मधुसूदनम् (Madhusudana)
ramayan::831.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::831.essence: A long austerity ends in reverent recognition of Vishnu's power.
ramayan::831.simple_meaning: Kasyapa and Aditi appear after long austerity to praise Vishnu, the giver of boons.
ramayan::831.simple_insight: Long discipline can end in a clear, reverent recognition of what you have sought.
ramayan::831.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the gods' appeal, Kasyapa appears blazing with Aditi after a thousand divine years of penance. Their long discipline has reached its fruit: they stand before Vishnu and praise him as the boon-giver, preparing the request that follows.
ramayan::831.modern_relevance: After years of showing up before dawn, your practice finally feels less like effort and more like recognition. The waiting itself has been shaping the one who can finally see clearly.
ramayan::831.insight: It shifts attention from asking for results to honoring the discipline that makes insight possible.

ramayan::832.verse_sanskrit: तपोमयं तपोराशिं तपोमूर्तिं तपात्मकम् । तपसा त्वां सुतप्तेन पश्यामि पुरुषोत्तमम् । । 12912 । ।
ramayan::832.verse_hindi: You are all ascetism, a mass of tapas, and an embodiment of tapas. Your soul is tapas. O Purushottama I am beholding you after a rigorous penance.
ramayan::832.english_translation: You are all ascetic power, a mass of ascetic power, and an embodiment of ascetic power. Through severe penance, I behold you, O Supreme Person.
ramayan::832.translation_literal: तपोमयम् (made of tapas) / तपोराशिम् (mass of tapas) / तपोमूर्तिम् (embodiment of tapas) / तपात्मकम् (consisting of tapas) / तपसा (by penance) / त्वाम् (you) / सुतप्तेन (well-seared, severe) / पश्यामि (I behold) / पुरुषोत्तमम् (Supreme Person)
ramayan::832.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::832.essence: Only severe penance lets you recognise the highest reality.
ramayan::832.simple_meaning: Rama is seen as the very form of intense spiritual effort, and only deep penance makes this vision possible.
ramayan::832.simple_insight: Real seeing is earned through discipline, not borrowed from opinion.
ramayan::832.detailed_meaning: Brahma is speaking in a divine revelation to Rama after the gods have petitioned for intervention. He does not just praise Rama; he recognizes him as the living form of tapas itself, visible only to one purified by severe penance.
ramayan::832.modern_relevance: After months of discipline, a pattern finally becomes visible: the habit, the fear, the truth you could not name before. Some things only reveal themselves to a mind that has been forged by effort.
ramayan::832.insight: It shifts you from casual looking to earned vision through disciplined effort.

ramayan::833.verse_sanskrit: शरीरे तव पश्यामि जगत्सर्वमिदं प्रभो । त्वमनादिरनिर्देश्यस्त्वामहं शरणं गत: । । 12913 । ।
ramayan::833.verse_hindi: O Lord I am beholding this entire universe in your body. You are beginningless and  indescribable. I take refuge in you.
ramayan::833.english_translation: O Lord, I see this entire universe in your body. You are beginningless and beyond description. I take refuge in you.
ramayan::833.translation_literal: शरीरे (in the body) / तव (of you) / पश्यामि (I see) / जगत्-सर्वम् (the whole universe) / इदम् (this) / प्रभो (O Lord) / त्वम् (you) / अनादिः (beginningless) / अनिर्देश्यः (indescribable) / त्वाम् (to you) / अहम् (I) / शरणम् (refuge) / गतः (gone)
ramayan::833.speaker: Kashyapa
ramayan::833.essence: When reality is vast enough, surrender becomes the clearest response.
ramayan::833.simple_meaning: Kashyapa sees the entire universe within Vishnu's body and recognises him as beyond beginning and description. In that awareness, he fully surrenders.
ramayan::833.simple_insight: There is relief in letting something vast carry what your mind cannot hold alone.
ramayan::833.detailed_meaning: Kashyapa stands before Vishnu after severe tapas. What he sees is not just a radiant form but the whole universe contained within that body. Faced with that vastness, he stops trying to stand apart and takes refuge completely.
ramayan::833.modern_relevance: You reach the end of your own explanations — after the loss, the diagnosis, the decision that was bigger than you. In that moment, control loosens and surrender becomes the only honest response.
ramayan::833.insight: It shifts the mind from managing reality to trusting what exceeds it.

ramayan::834.verse_sanskrit: तमुवाच हरि: प्रीत: कश्यपं धूतकल्मषम् । वरं वरय भद्रं ते वरार्होऽसि मतो मम । । 12914 । ।
ramayan::834.verse_hindi: Addressing Kasyapa whose sins had been washed clean, Lord Visnu pleased (with his penance) said: Be prosperous you are dear to me. Worthy of a boon. Ask.
ramayan::834.english_translation: Addressing Kasyapa, whose impurities had been washed away, Vishnu, pleased, said: "Be blessed. You are dear to me and worthy of a boon. Ask for one."
ramayan::834.translation_literal: तम् (to him) / उवाच (said) / हरि: (Vishnu) / प्रीत: (pleased) / कश्यपं (to Kasyapa) / धूतकल्मषम् (whose impurities were washed away) / वरम् (a boon) / वरय (ask) / भद्रं ते (blessings to you) / वरार्होऽसि (you are worthy of a boon) / मतो मम (considered by me)
ramayan::834.speaker: Vishnu
ramayan::834.essence: Penance does not just impress the divine; it makes you ready for blessing.
ramayan::834.simple_meaning: Vishnu is pleased with Kasyapa's austerity and tells him to ask for a boon, because his inner impurities have been washed away.
ramayan::834.simple_insight: Real effort can make you ready to receive what you could not demand before.
ramayan::834.detailed_meaning: After Kasyapa's severe tapas, Vishnu appears pleased and speaks to him with honor. This is the reward for purification: the seeker is no longer asking as a beggar, but as someone whose discipline has made him fit to receive.
ramayan::834.modern_relevance: After months of showing up before sunrise, you finally sit in the review meeting with a steadier mind. You did not just want the result — you became the kind of person who could hold it.
ramayan::834.insight: It shifts effort from mere striving to purification that prepares you for grace.

ramayan::835.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य मारीच: कश्यपोऽब्रवीत् । अदित्या देवतानां च मम चैवानुयाचत: । । 12915 । । वरं वरद सुप्रीतो दातुमर्हसि सुव्रत ।
ramayan::835.verse_hindi: Having heard those words of Vishnu, Kasyapa, son of Maricha, replied, O bestower of boons, O great practitioner of austerities Be pleased to grant a boon for Aditi, devatas and for myself.
ramayan::835.english_translation: Having heard those words of Vishnu, Kasyapa replied: O boon-giver, O great ascetic, please grant a boon for Aditi, the devas, and for me.
