ramayan::835.translation_literal: तत्-श्रुत्वा (having heard that) / वचनम् (speech) / तस्य (of that one) / मारीचः कश्यपः (Maricha-Kashyapa) / अब्रवीत् (said) / अदित्याः (for Aditi) / देवतानाम् (for the devas) / च (and) / मम (for me) / च (and) / एव (also) / अनुयाचतः (for the one asking) / वरम् (a boon) / वरद (boon-giver) / सुप्रीतः (very pleased) / दातुम् (to give) / अर्हसि (you are fit) / सुव्रत (of excellent vow)
ramayan::835.speaker: Kashyapa
ramayan::835.essence: A worthy boon is asked for the wider good, not just personal gain.
ramayan::835.simple_meaning: Kashyapa asks Vishnu to grant a boon for Aditi, the devas, and himself.
ramayan::835.simple_insight: Even a great request begins with humble asking.
ramayan::835.detailed_meaning: Vishnu has just been pleased by Kashyapa's austerities and offered a boon. Kashyapa responds not for himself alone, but for Aditi and the devas too. The moment is still part of the larger divine exchange that will lead to Vishnu's incarnation.
ramayan::835.modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for something important, and you do not make it only about yourself. The best requests widen the circle.
ramayan::835.insight: It shifts desire from private gain to a request that serves many.

ramayan::836.verse_sanskrit: पुत्रत्वं गच्छ भगवन्नदित्या मम चानघ । । 12916 । । भ्राता भव यवीयांस्त्वं शक्रस्यासुरसूदन । शोकार्तानां तु देवानां साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि । । 12917 । ।
ramayan::836.verse_hindi: O Sinless Lord, Be born son to Aditi and to me, O Destroyer of asuras, be the younger brother to Indra. You can help these sorrowstricken devatas.
ramayan::836.english_translation: O sinless Lord, be born as the son of Aditi and of me. O destroyer of asuras, be the younger brother of Indra. You can help the sorrow-stricken devas.
ramayan::836.translation_literal: पुत्रत्वं (sonhood) / गच्छ (go) / भगवन् (O Lord) / अदित्या (of Aditi) / मम (of me) / च (and) / अनघ (sinless) / भ्राता (brother) / भव (become) / यवीयान् (younger) / त्वम् (you) / शक्रस्य (of Indra) / असुरसूदन (O destroyer of asuras) / शोकार्तानाम् (of the sorrow-stricken) / तु (indeed) / देवानाम् (of the devas) / साहाय्यम् (help) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you are fit)
ramayan::836.speaker: Kasyapa
ramayan::836.essence: The supreme being is asked to enter the world as aid for the suffering.
ramayan::836.simple_meaning: Kasyapa asks Vishnu to take birth among the devas, join Indra's family, and come to their aid against the asuras.
ramayan::836.simple_insight: Real strength is not self-display; it is appearing where others are overwhelmed and need rescue.
ramayan::836.detailed_meaning: The devas are crushed by the asuras, and Kasyapa is speaking to Vishnu after years of austerity. He does not ask for personal gain. He asks the supreme being to enter family and history so suffering beings can be helped.
ramayan::836.modern_relevance: A room full of people is quietly panicking because one crisis has broken everyone’s focus. The strongest person is not the loudest one — it is the one who steps in, takes a place, and steadies the whole room.
ramayan::836.insight: It shifts attention from power as status to power as service under pressure.

ramayan::837.verse_sanskrit: अयं सिद्धाश्रमो नाम प्रसादा त्ते भविष्यति । सिद्धे कर्मणि देवेश उत्तिष्ठ भगवन्नित: । । 12918 । ।
ramayan::837.verse_hindi: O Lord of the celestials, with my penance accomplished (here) this place will be known as siddhaashrama by your grace. O Lord arise from here.
ramayan::837.english_translation: O Lord of the celestials, by your grace this place will become known as Siddhashrama. When my penance is complete, O blessed one, rise from here.
ramayan::837.translation_literal: अयं (this) / सिद्धाश्रमो (Siddhashrama) / नाम (by name) / प्रसादात् (by grace) / ते (of you) / भविष्यति (will become) / सिद्धे (when accomplished) / कर्मणि (in the act/work) / देवेश (Lord of the celestials) / उत्तिष्ठ (arise) / भगवन् (blessed one) / इतः (from here)
ramayan::837.speaker: Vishnu
ramayan::837.essence: Penance turns an ordinary place into the site of divine arrival.
ramayan::837.simple_meaning: The sage says this place will be called Siddhashrama because the divine grace will make his penance fruitful, and then the Lord should arise from there.
ramayan::837.simple_insight: Some places become sacred because a hard inner effort is finally answered.
ramayan::837.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just asked Vishnu to be born as Aditi's son and help the devas. In reply, the divine presence is told that this forest will become Siddhashrama through grace, and that the waiting here is only until the penance is complete and the Lord rises forth.
ramayan::837.modern_relevance: You keep showing up to the same quiet practice, even when nothing seems to move. Then one day the place where you struggled becomes the place where everything changes.
ramayan::837.insight: It links disciplined effort with a transformed setting, showing that sustained practice can sanctify a place and prepare the next step.

ramayan::838.verse_sanskrit: अथ विष्णुर्महातेजा अदित्यां समजायत । वामनं रूपमास्थाय वैरोचनिमुपागमत् । । 12919 । ।
ramayan::838.verse_hindi: Then the resplendent Visnu, born from the womb of Aditi and assuming the form of Vamana, approached, the son of Virochana (Bali).
ramayan::838.english_translation: Then the resplendent Vishnu was born from Aditi and, taking the form of Vamana, approached Bali, the son of Virochana.
ramayan::838.translation_literal: अथ (then) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / महातेजाः (the greatly resplendent one) / अदित्याम् (in Aditi) / समजायत (was born) / वामनम् (Vamana) / रूपम् (form) / आस्थाय (having assumed) / वैरोचनिम् (to Bali, son of Virochana) / उपागमत् (approached)
ramayan::838.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::838.essence: The supreme reality arrives small, and that is how balance is restored.
ramayan::838.simple_meaning: Vishnu is born from Aditi and takes the form of Vamana to meet Bali.
ramayan::838.simple_insight: The divine enters the world in a small form to restore balance.
ramayan::838.detailed_meaning: Aditi has asked for help, and Vishnu answers by taking birth as Vamana. The moment shifts from prayer to action: the cosmic protector steps into the story in a humble form and walks toward Bali, setting up the famous three-steps episode.
ramayan::838.modern_relevance: When the answer to a huge problem arrives in an ordinary-looking form, it is easy to overlook. This verse reminds you that real power can come quietly, without announcing itself.
ramayan::838.insight: It shifts attention from outward size to the force hidden inside humble action.

ramayan::839.verse_sanskrit: त्रीन् क्रमानथ भिक्षित्वा प्रतिगृह्य च मानद: । आक्रम्य लोकान् लोकात्मा सर्वभूतहिते रत: । । 12920 । । महेन्द्राय पुन: प्रादान्नियम्य बलिमोजसा । त्रैलोक्यं स महातेजाश्चक्रे शक्रवशं पुन: । । 12921 । ।
ramayan::839.verse_hindi: Thereafter, Visnu, soul of the universe who restores respect (for the righeous), and renders the welfare of all living beings, having begged from Bali, and been granted three places to put his footsteps on occupied the (three) worlds and by restraining Bali with his energy, gave (it) back to Mahendra. In this manner the highly lustrous Visnu, gave  possession of the three worlds to Mahendra.
ramayan::839.english_translation: Thereafter, Vishnu, the soul of the universe and friend of all beings, asked Bali for three steps of land. Having received them, he covered the three worlds, restrained Bali by his power, and restored the worlds to Indra. The mighty one thus placed the three worlds under Indra's rule again.
ramayan::839.translation_literal: त्रीन् (three) / क्रमन् (steps) / अथ (then) / भिक्षित्वा (having begged) / प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / च (and) / मानदः (giver of honor) / आक्रम्य (having stepped over) / लोकान् (worlds) / लोकात्मा (soul of the worlds) / सर्वभूतहिते (in the welfare of all beings) / रत: (delighted) / महेन्द्राय (to Mahendra/Indra) / पुनः (again) / प्रादात् (gave back) / नियम्य (having restrained) / बलिम् (Bali) / ओजसा (by power) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / सः (he) / महातेजाः (highly lustrous) / चक्रे (made) / शक्रवशम् (under Indra's rule) / पुनः (again)
ramayan::839.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::839.essence: He takes everything, then gives rightful order back.
ramayan::839.simple_meaning: Vishnu asks for three steps of land, then takes back the three worlds and returns them to Indra.
ramayan::839.simple_insight: Power here serves balance, not possession.
ramayan::839.detailed_meaning: The gods have already appealed for help, and Vishnu has come as Vamana. He asks Bali for three steps, then expands to cover the worlds, subdues Bali, and restores cosmic order by returning the realms to Indra. This is a decisive divine act, not a teaching line.
ramayan::839.modern_relevance: A powerful person can win more than enough and still choose to restore what was taken. The real test is not force, but what you do after you have it.
ramayan::839.insight: It shows authority used to correct imbalance, not to hoard control.

ramayan::840.verse_sanskrit: तेनैष पूर्वमाक्रान्त आश्रमश्श्रमनाशन: । मयापि भक्तय तस्यैष वामनस्योपभुज्यते । । 12922 । ।
ramayan::840.verse_hindi: This asrama, which relieves fatigue, previously under the possession of Vamana, has come under my occoupation for my devotion to him.
ramayan::840.english_translation: This ashram, which relieves fatigue, was once occupied by Vamana. I now enjoy it out of devotion to him.
ramayan::840.translation_literal: तेन (by him) / एषः (this) / पूर्वम् (earlier) / आक्रान्तः (occupied) / आश्रमः (ashram) / श्रमनाशनः (destroying fatigue) / मया अपि (by me also) / भक्त्या (with devotion) / तस्य (to him) / एषः (this) / वामनस्य (of Vamana) / उपभुज्यते (is enjoyed / used)
ramayan::840.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::840.essence: Devotion can make even possession feel like worship.
ramayan::840.simple_meaning: The speaker says this ashram was once occupied by Vamana, and he now uses it as an act of devotion to Vamana.
ramayan::840.simple_insight: Love can change how you receive a place, making use feel like reverence.
ramayan::840.detailed_meaning: Vamana has already crossed the worlds and claimed this sacred place. Now the speaker explains that he occupies the same ashram not as a conqueror, but as a devotee. The verse turns possession into homage.
ramayan::840.modern_relevance: You move into a room where someone you admire once lived, and you feel it immediately. The space is ordinary, but your care for the person changes how you treat every corner.
ramayan::840.insight: It shifts possession into gratitude and use into reverence.

ramayan::841.verse_sanskrit: एतमाश्रममायान्ति राक्षसा विघ्नकारिण: । अत्रैव पुरुषव्याघ्र हन्तव्या दुष्टचारिण: । । 12923 । ।
ramayan::841.verse_hindi: O tiger among men, wicked rakshasas who prowl about the asram and cause
ramayan::841.english_translation: Wicked rakshasas who disturb this hermitage come here. O tiger among men, these evil-doers must be slain right here.
ramayan::841.translation_literal: एतम् (this) / आश्रमम् (hermitage) / आयान्ति (come) / राक्षसा: (rakshasas) / विघ्नकारिण: (troublemakers) / अत्रैव (right here) / पुरुषव्याघ्र (tiger among men) / हन्तव्या: (must be slain) / दुष्टचारिण: (evil-doers)
ramayan::841.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::841.essence: Repeated harm must be stopped at the source.
ramayan::841.simple_meaning: The speaker says that evil beings keep coming to disturb the hermitage, and they should be killed there itself.
ramayan::841.simple_insight: Some places need protection, not negotiation.
ramayan::841.detailed_meaning: In the hermitage of Siddhashrama, the sage is explaining its need for protection. After speaking of the sacred ground and its former guardianship, he points to the rakshasas who keep troubling the place and says they must be destroyed there.
ramayan::841.modern_relevance: A quiet home, a classroom, or a workplace can be spoiled by one person who keeps crossing the line. Sometimes protecting a good space means stopping the harm at once.
ramayan::841.insight: It shifts attention from idealism to necessary protection when repeated harm threatens a sacred or fragile space.

ramayan::842.verse_sanskrit: अद्य गच्छामहे राम सिद्धाश्रममनुत्तमम् । तदाश्रमपदं तात तवाप्येतद्यथा मम । । 12924 । ।
ramayan::842.verse_hindi: O Rama, now lets go to the unparalleled Siddhashrama. O child this asrama is the same to you as it is to me (treat this as your own).
ramayan::842.english_translation: O Rama, now let us go to the unequalled Siddhashrama. O child, this hermitage is as much yours as it is mine.
ramayan::842.translation_literal: अद्य (now) / गच्छामहे (let us go) / राम (Rama) / सिद्धाश्रमम् (to Siddhashrama) / अनुत्तमम् (unequalled) । तदाश्रमपदम् (that hermitage-place) / तात (O child) / तव (your) / अपि (also) / एतत् (this) / यथा (as) / मम (mine) ।
ramayan::842.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::842.essence: A place becomes yours when you are trusted to guard it.
ramayan::842.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra invites Rama to continue to Siddhashrama and tells him to treat the hermitage as his own home.
ramayan::842.simple_insight: True welcome makes you belong before you have earned a place.
ramayan::842.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has brought Rama and Lakshmana to the edge of a sacred hermitage threatened by hostile forces. After explaining the danger, he now invites Rama onward, making the place feel shared and entrusted rather than merely visited.
ramayan::842.modern_relevance: You arrive somewhere new and someone says, “Treat this place like your own.” That simple trust can change how you carry yourself.
ramayan::842.insight: It frames sacred duty as shared ownership and asks Rama to enter as a protector, not a guest.

ramayan::843.verse_sanskrit: प्रविशन्नाश्रमपदं व्यरोचत महामुनि: । शशीव गतनीहार: पुनर्वसुसमन्वित: । । 12925 । ।
ramayan::843.verse_hindi: While enetering the hermitage the great ascetic appeared resplendent (in the company of Rama and Lakshmana) like the moon in conjunction with Punarvasu star emerging out of  the mist.
ramayan::843.english_translation: While entering the hermitage, the great ascetic shone brilliantly, like the moon with Punarvasu after the mist has cleared.
ramayan::843.translation_literal: प्रविशन् (entering) / आश्रमपदम् (the hermitage) / व्यरोचत (shone brightly) / महामुनिः (the great ascetic) / शशी (the moon) / इव (like) / गतनीहारः (with mist gone) / पुनर्वसुसमन्वितः (joined with Punarvasu)
ramayan::843.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::843.essence: Clear presence can make a place feel whole again.
ramayan::843.simple_meaning: Visvamitra enters the hermitage with Rama and Lakshmana, shining with renewed splendour like the moon after mist clears.
ramayan::843.simple_insight: Some presences seem to brighten a whole place just by arriving.
ramayan::843.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra leads Rama and Lakshmana into Siddhashrama after warning them about the rakshasas there. The verse pauses on his radiance, comparing him to the moon emerging from mist before the sages greet him.
ramayan::843.modern_relevance: A respected teacher walks into a room after a tense silence, and everyone straightens without a word. Some people carry a calm that makes the whole space feel ordered again.
ramayan::843.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how presence itself can restore dignity to a place.

ramayan::844.verse_sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा मुनयस्सर्वे सिद्धाश्रमनिवासिन: । उत्पत्त्योत्पत्त्य सहसा विश्वामित्रमपूजयन् । । 12926 । ।
ramayan::844.verse_hindi: At the sight of Viswamitra all the ascetics, inmates of Siddhashrama, jumped out instantly and offered him their worship.
ramayan::844.english_translation: At the sight of Viswamitra, all the ascetics living in Siddhashrama rose up at once and honoured him.
ramayan::844.translation_literal: तम् (him) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / मुनयः (ascetics) / सर्वे (all) / सिद्धाश्रमनिवासिनः (residents of Siddhashrama) / उत्पत्त्य-उत्पत्त्य (rising up again and again) / सहसा (suddenly, at once) / विश्वामित्रम् (Viswamitra) / अपूजयन् (honoured, worshipped)
ramayan::844.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::844.essence: True stature is recognised before it is announced.
ramayan::844.simple_meaning: The sages of Siddhashrama immediately rose and honoured Viswamitra when they saw him.
ramayan::844.simple_insight: Respect can be shown quickly and without hesitation when someone worthy enters the room.
ramayan::844.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra arrives at Siddhashrama with Rama and Lakshmana beside him. The resident ascetics recognise him at once and rise in honour. This verse simply marks that respectful reception before the next scene of hospitality unfolds.
ramayan::844.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone who knows your work stands up before you speak. That instant recognition is what this verse captures.
ramayan::844.insight: It shows how presence alone can command reverence before any words are spoken.

ramayan::845.verse_sanskrit: यथार्हं चक्रिरे पूजां विश्वामित्राय धीमते । तथैव राजपुत्राभ्यामकुर्वन्नतिथिक्रियाम् । । 12927 । ।
ramayan::845.verse_hindi: They extended hospitality to both the princes in the same way they offered their worship to the sagacious Viswamitra.
ramayan::845.english_translation: They extended hospitality to both princes in the same way they offered their worship to the sagacious Viswamitra.
ramayan::845.translation_literal: यथार्हम् (as was proper) / चक्रिरे (they performed) / पूजाम् (honour, worship) / विश्वामित्राय (to Viswamitra) / धीमते (the wise one) / तथा (in that same way) / एव (indeed) / राजपुत्राभ्याम् (to the two princes) / अकुर्वन् (they made) / अतिथिक्रियाम् (hospitality, guest-reception)
ramayan::845.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::845.essence: Hospitality extends the honour given to the wise one.
ramayan::845.simple_meaning: The sages welcomed Rama and Lakshmana with the same respect they showed Viswamitra. The princes were treated as honoured guests, not outsiders.
ramayan::845.simple_insight: Respect is shown not only to the teacher, but to those who travel with him.
ramayan::845.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra arrives at Siddhashrama with Rama and Lakshmana beside him. The resident sages first honour the great seer, then offer the same hospitality to the two princes. It is a scene of formal welcome, not teaching or revelation.
ramayan::845.modern_relevance: You bring someone important to a gathering, and the room notices them because of how they are received. Courtesy toward the people beside the honoured guest says everything.
ramayan::845.insight: It highlights proper guest-reception and equal respect, before the next conversation begins.

ramayan::846.verse_sanskrit: मुहूर्तमथ विश्रान्तौ राजपुत्रावरिन्दमौ । प्राञ्जली मुनिशार्दूलमूचतू रघुनन्दनौ । । 12928 । ।
ramayan::846.verse_hindi: The two princes of the lineage of Raghu, destroyers of foes rested a while and then said to Viswamitra, a tiger amon sages:
ramayan::846.english_translation: The two princes of the Raghu line, destroyers of foes, rested for a moment and then spoke to Viswamitra, tiger among sages, with folded hands.
ramayan::846.translation_literal: मुहूर्तम् (for a moment) / अथ (then) / विश्रान्तौ (having rested) / राजपुत्रौ (the two princes) / अरिन्दमौ (destroyers of foes) / प्राञ्जली (with folded hands) / मुनिशार्दूलम् (to the tiger among sages) / ऊचतुः (spoke) / रघुनन्दनौ (the two delight of the Raghu line)
ramayan::846.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::846.essence: Honor comes first; the request follows.
ramayan::846.simple_meaning: After resting briefly, Rama and Lakshmana stood with folded hands and addressed Viswamitra respectfully.
ramayan::846.simple_insight: Respect begins before the words do.
ramayan::846.detailed_meaning: At Siddhashrama, Viswamitra has just been welcomed by the ascetics. Rama and Lakshmana pause after the journey, then turn to the sage with folded hands. The verse simply sets up the respectful request that follows.
ramayan::846.modern_relevance: You arrive at a meeting tired, but you still straighten up before speaking. The pause, the posture, the respect — they shape what comes next.
ramayan::846.insight: It shows that even princes begin with restraint and reverence before making a request.

ramayan::847.verse_sanskrit: अद्यैव दीक्षां प्रविश भद्रं ते मुनिपुङ्गव । सिद्धाश्रमोऽयं सिद्धस्स्यात् सत्यमस्तु वचस्तव । । 12929 । ।
ramayan::847.verse_hindi: O foremost of ascetics Get initialed today. You will prosper and this asram will attain its fulfilment. Your words shall come true.
ramayan::847.english_translation: O foremost of ascetics, enter the initiation rite today itself. May you be blessed. Then this hermitage will become truly fulfilled, and your words will prove true.
ramayan::847.translation_literal: अद्यैव (today itself) / दीक्षाम् (initiation rite) / प्रविश (enter) / भद्रम् (blessed) / ते (to you) / मुनिपुङ्गव (foremost of ascetics) / सिद्धाश्रमः (the Siddha hermitage) / अयम् (this) / सिद्धः (fulfilled) / स्यात् (may become) / सत्यम् (true) / अस्तु (may it be) / वचः (word) / तव (your)
ramayan::847.speaker: Rama
ramayan::847.essence: Immediate action is what turns a sacred intention into completion.
ramayan::847.simple_meaning: Rama urges Viswamitra to begin the sacred initiation at once, wishing him well and saying the hermitage will be fulfilled when his promise comes true.
ramayan::847.simple_insight: There is power in starting without delay when the moment is ripe.
ramayan::847.detailed_meaning: After resting, Rama and Lakshmana speak to Viswamitra at the Siddha hermitage. They ask him to begin the consecration immediately, bless him, and affirm that the place will be complete when his undertaking succeeds.
ramayan::847.modern_relevance: You have a project sitting in limbo because everyone is waiting for the perfect moment. Sometimes the work becomes real only when someone finally says, 'Start now.'
ramayan::847.insight: It shifts attention from delay to decisive commencement, treating timely action as what fulfills a promise.

ramayan::848.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महान् ऋषि: । प्रविवेश तदा दीक्षां नियतो नियतेन्द्रिय: । । 12930 । ।
ramayan::848.verse_hindi: Saying this, Viswamitra, the great saint effulgent and self trained engaged himself in the  initiation ceremony.
ramayan::848.english_translation: Saying this, Viswamitra, the great saint, radiant and self-controlled, entered the initiation ceremony.
ramayan::848.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (having been spoken to thus) / महातेजाः (great-radiance) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महान् (great) / ऋषिः (sage) / प्रविवेश (entered) / तदा (then) / दीक्षाम् (the initiation ceremony) / नियतः (self-controlled) / नियतेन्द्रियः (with controlled senses)
ramayan::848.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::848.essence: Power becomes useful only when it submits to discipline.
ramayan::848.simple_meaning: Viswamitra accepted the initiation rite and entered it with discipline and self-control.
ramayan::848.simple_insight: Real readiness shows up as calm obedience, not hesitation.
ramayan::848.detailed_meaning: After Rama and Lakshmana urge him to begin at once, Viswamitra finally steps into the initiation rite. The scene is less about drama than about readiness: a powerful sage agrees to be governed by discipline so the larger work can proceed.
ramayan::848.modern_relevance: You finally stop circling the decision and begin the hard process you kept delaying. The moment feels quieter than you expected — and more serious.
ramayan::848.insight: It shifts the mind from delay to disciplined entry.

ramayan::849.verse_sanskrit: कुमारावपि तां रात्रिमुषित्वा सुसमाहितौ । प्रभातकाले चोत्थाय पूर्वां सन्ध्यामुपास्य च । । 12931 । । स्पृष्टोदकौ शुची जप्यं समाप्य नियमेन च । हुताग्निहोत्रमासीनं विश्वामित्रमवन्दताम् । । 12932 । ।
ramayan::849.verse_hindi: The two princes spent the right comfortably and woke up at daybreak. They  performed morning in accordance with the prescribed rule, ablutions, said their prayers and paid their respects to Viswamitra seated at the kindled firesacrifice.
ramayan::849.english_translation: The two princes spent the night in composure. At daybreak they rose, performed the morning rites, washed, completed their prayers, and bowed to Vishvamitra, who was seated beside the fire offering.
ramayan::849.translation_literal: कुमारौ (the two princes) / अपि (indeed) / तां रात्रिम् (that night) / उषित्वा (having spent) / सुसमाहितौ (well-composed, focused) / प्रभातकाले (at daybreak) / च (and) / उत्थाय (having risen) / पूर्वाम् (earlier, morning) / सन्ध्याम् (twilight prayer) / उपास्य (having worshipped) / च (and) / स्पृष्टोदकौ (having touched water, purified) / शुची (pure) / जप्यम् (recitation) / समाप्य (having completed) / नियमेन (according to rule) / च (and) / हुताग्निहोत्रम् (with the fire sacrifice completed) / आसीनम् (seated) / विश्वामित्रम् (Vishvamitra) / अवन्दताम् (they bowed)
ramayan::849.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::849.essence: Readiness begins with discipline before the day asks anything of you.
ramayan::849.simple_meaning: The two princes wake early, cleanse themselves, finish their prayers, and respectfully bow to Vishvamitra.
ramayan::849.simple_insight: Small disciplines reveal character before any great test begins.
ramayan::849.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have spent the night under Vishvamitra's guidance. At dawn, before speaking of the day's task, they rise with discipline, complete their morning rites, and bow to the sage seated by the sacred fire. The scene shows their readiness to learn.
ramayan::849.modern_relevance: You wake before the house is fully alive, wash your face, and begin the day without reaching for your phone. That quiet order can say more about you than any speech.
ramayan::849.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the habits that prepare a person for duty.

ramayan::850.verse_sanskrit: अथ तौ देशकालज्ञौ राजापुत्रावरिन्दमौ । देशे काले च वाक्यज्ञावब्रूतां कौशिकं वच: । । 1301 । ।
ramayan::850.verse_hindi: Thus spoke the two princes to Viswamitra. They were conscious of place and time to speak and capable of conquering enemies.
ramayan::850.english_translation: Thus the two princes, who knew the right place and the right time and knew how to speak, addressed Viswamitra.
ramayan::850.translation_literal: अथ (then) / तौ (those two) / देश-काल-ज्ञौ (knowing place and time) / राज-पुत्रौ (the two princes) / अरिन्दमौ (subduers of foes) / देशे (in place) / काले (in time) / च (and) / वाक्य-ज्ञौ (knowing speech) / अब्रूताम् (they spoke) / कौशिकं (to Kaushika) / वचः (words)
ramayan::850.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::850.essence: Right speech begins with knowing when to speak.
ramayan::850.simple_meaning: The two princes waited for the right moment and then spoke respectfully to Viswamitra.
ramayan::850.simple_insight: Good timing and respectful speech matter as much as courage.
ramayan::850.detailed_meaning: After the night of preparation, Rama and Lakshmana approach Viswamitra with care. They do not interrupt or rush; they choose the right moment and the right words before asking about the danger to the sacrifice.
ramayan::850.modern_relevance: You know the message is important, but you wait until the room is ready to hear it. That restraint can make the difference between being heard and being ignored.
ramayan::850.insight: It teaches you to match your words to the moment instead of forcing them out impulsively.

ramayan::851.verse_sanskrit: भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छावो यस्मिन् काले निशाचरौ । संरक्षणीयौ तौ ब्रह्मन्नातिवर्तेत तत्क्षणम् । । 1302 । ।
ramayan::851.verse_hindi: O adorable Brahmarshi, we want to know around what time the rakshasas will make their appearance so that the sacrifice can be protected. Let  not that moment pass.
ramayan::851.english_translation: O adorable Brahmarshi, we want to know around what time the rakshasas will make their appearance so that the sacrifice can be protected. Let not that moment pass.
ramayan::851.translation_literal: भगवन् (O adorable one) / श्रोतुमिच्छावः (we wish to hear) / यस्मिन् काले (at which time) / निशाचरौ (the night-roamers) / संरक्षणीयौ (to be protected) / तौ (those two) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahmarshi) / अति-वर्तेत (should pass by) / तत्-क्षणम् (that moment)
ramayan::851.speaker: Rama and Lakshmana
ramayan::851.essence: Protection begins with knowing exactly when danger will arrive.
ramayan::851.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana ask Vishwamitra exactly when the demons will appear so they can protect the ritual at the right time.
ramayan::851.simple_insight: Readiness is not vague concern; it is knowing when action must begin.
ramayan::851.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are with Vishwamitra at the sacrifice site. The sages need protection from marauding rakshasas, and the princes want the exact hour of attack so they can stand guard without missing it.
ramayan::851.modern_relevance: You are waiting outside a hospital room, phone in hand, because one message will change how you move next. The question is not whether you care — it is whether you know the moment to act.
ramayan::851.insight: It shifts duty from general intention to precise timing and alert response.

ramayan::852.verse_sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणौ काकुत्स्थौ त्वरमाणौ युयुत्सया । सर्वे ते मुनय: प्रीता: प्रशशंसुर्नृपात्मजौ । । 1303 । ।
ramayan::852.verse_hindi: The sages (of the asrama) were very pleased. They extolled the princes of Kakustha dynasty, who were eager to fight the rakshasas.
ramayan::852.english_translation: The sages of the ashram were very pleased. They praised the princes of the Kakustha line, who were eager to fight the rakshasas.
ramayan::852.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / ब्रुवाणौ (speaking) / काकुत्स्थौ (the two Kakusthas) / त्वरमाणौ (hastening) / युयुत्सया (with the desire to fight) / सर्वे (all) / ते (those) / मुनयः (sages) / प्रीताः (pleased) / प्रशशंसुः (praised) / नृपात्मजौ (the two princes)
ramayan::852.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::852.essence: Readiness itself becomes a form of protection.
ramayan::852.simple_meaning: The sages were pleased that Rama and Lakshmana were ready to face the rakshasas and protect the sacrifice.
ramayan::852.simple_insight: Courage can earn trust before a single battle begins.
ramayan::852.detailed_meaning: At Vishwamitra's hermitage, Rama and Lakshmana answer without hesitation when asked to guard the sacrifice. Their readiness reassures the sages, who praise the two princes for meeting danger without fear.
ramayan::852.modern_relevance: You step forward when everyone else is still measuring the risk. That quiet readiness can earn trust faster than any speech.
ramayan::852.insight: It shows that calm readiness, not noise, is what convinces others you can be relied on.

ramayan::853.verse_sanskrit: अद्यप्रभृति षड्रात्रं रक्षतं राघवौ युवाम् । दीक्षां गतो ह्येष मुनिर्मौनित्वं च गमिष्यति । । 1304 । ।
ramayan::853.verse_hindi: O sons of Raghus lineage protect the sacrifice for six nights from today. With the ceremoney initiated, the sage would  observe silence said the inmates.
ramayan::853.english_translation: O sons of the Raghu line, protect the sacrifice for six nights from today. Once the rite has begun, this sage will keep silence.
ramayan::853.translation_literal: अद्यप्रभृति (from today) / षड्रात्रं (for six nights) / रक्षतं (protect) / राघवौ (O two descendants of Raghu) / युवाम् (you two) / दीक्षां (the rite / initiation) / गतः (having entered) / हि (indeed) / एषः (this) / मुनिः (sage) / मौनित्वं (silence) / च (and) / गमिष्यति (will go / will observe)
ramayan::853.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::853.essence: Protection is the price of sacred work.
ramayan::853.simple_meaning: The sages ask Rama and Lakshmana to guard the sacrifice for six nights while the sage observes silence during the rite.
ramayan::853.simple_insight: Some duties are temporary, but they still demand your full presence.
ramayan::853.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra’s hermitage, the sages have welcomed Rama and Lakshmana just in time. The sacrifice has begun, the sage is now silent, and the brothers are asked to stand guard for six nights against the rakshasas.
ramayan::853.modern_relevance: A friend asks you to stay awake through the night because something fragile depends on you. No applause, no glamour — just six nights of being the shield.
ramayan::853.insight: It shifts attention from personal comfort to protective responsibility taken on at the right time.

ramayan::854.verse_sanskrit: तौ तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रौ यशस्विनौ । अनिद्रौ षडहोरात्रं तपोवनमरक्षताम् । । 1305 । ।
ramayan::854.verse_hindi: At these words of the sages the illustrious princes got ready to protect the tapovana for six days and six nights without sleep.
ramayan::854.english_translation: At these words of the sages, the illustrious princes guarded the forest hermitage for six days and six nights without sleep.
ramayan::854.translation_literal: तौ (those two) / तु (indeed) / तद्वचनं (that instruction) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राजपुत्रौ (the two princes) / यशस्विनौ (illustrious) / अनिद्रौ (without sleep) / षडहोरात्रं (six days and nights) / तपोवनम् (the forest hermitage) / अरक्षताम् (protected)
ramayan::854.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::854.essence: They protected what mattered by giving up comfort completely.
ramayan::854.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana obey the sages and guard the hermitage day and night without sleeping for six days.
ramayan::854.simple_insight: Real protection often means staying alert long after comfort is gone.
ramayan::854.detailed_meaning: The sages have asked Rama and Lakshmana to protect the hermitage during the sacrifice. The princes accept at once and keep watch for six days and nights without sleep. This verse shows their disciplined exertion before the larger conflict begins.
ramayan::854.modern_relevance: You stay up through the night because someone depends on you being awake. No applause, no shortcut — just steady watchfulness when the moment calls for it.
ramayan::854.insight: It shifts action from occasional effort to sustained vigilance for a sacred responsibility.

ramayan::855.verse_hindi: The two mighty, heroic archers (Rama and Lakshmana), destroyers of enemies
ramayan::855.english_translation: The two mighty heroes, the supreme archers, protected the great sage Vishvamitra.
ramayan::855.translation_literal: उपासाञ्चक्रतुḥ (they attended upon) / वीरौ (the two heroes) / यतौ (restrained, vigilant) / तौ (those two) / परमधन्विनौ (the two supreme archers) / ररक्षतुḥ (protected) / मुनिवरम् (the best of sages) / विश्वामित्रम् (Vishvamitra) / अरिन्दमौ (the two enemy-subduers)
ramayan::855.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::855.essence: Strength becomes service when it stands guard for another.
ramayan::855.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana stayed alert and guarded Vishvamitra.
ramayan::855.simple_insight: Real strength is often quiet protection, not display.
ramayan::855.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has brought Rama and Lakshmana into the forest to guard his sacrifice. The two princes do not complain or sleep; they stand watch as disciplined protectors, making the sage's ritual possible.
ramayan::855.modern_relevance: You stay awake beside someone who needs you, even when no one is applauding. Protection itself can be the work.
ramayan::855.insight: It shifts attention from heroics to faithful guardianship.

ramayan::856.verse_sanskrit: अथ काले गते तस्मिन् षष्ठेऽहनि समागते । सौमित्रिमब्रवीद्रामो यत्तो भव समाहित: । । 1307 । ।
ramayan::856.verse_hindi: Time passed. When the sixth day arrived Rama cautioned Lakshmana to be vigilant.
ramayan::856.english_translation: When that time had passed and the sixth day arrived, Rama said to Lakshmana, 'Be alert and composed.'
ramayan::856.translation_literal: अथ (then) / काले (when time) / गते (had passed) / तस्मिन् (that) / षष्ठेऽहनि (on the sixth day) / समागते (having arrived) / सौमित्रिम् (to Lakshmana) / अब्रवीत् (said) / रामः (Rama) / यत्तः (vigilant) / भव (be) / समाहितः (composed)
ramayan::856.speaker: Rama
ramayan::856.essence: Readiness is calm attention before action begins.
ramayan::856.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana to remain alert and composed as the sixth day arrives. The waiting is over; now they must be ready.
ramayan::856.simple_insight: Calm readiness matters more than panic when the decisive moment comes.
ramayan::856.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have guarded the sages' forest retreat through six tense days and nights. As the sixth day begins, Rama tells Lakshmana to stay vigilant and collected, because the test is not just strength but readiness.
ramayan::856.modern_relevance: The call comes right before a difficult presentation, a hospital waiting room update, or the moment a family argument finally turns serious. You do not need frenzy; you need clear attention.
ramayan::856.insight: It teaches you to meet pressure with alert calm, not scattered reaction.

ramayan::857.verse_sanskrit: रामस्यैवं ब्रुवाणस्य त्वरितस्य युयुत्सया । प्रजज्वाल ततो वेदिस्सोपाध्यायपुरोहिता । । 1308 । ।
ramayan::857.verse_hindi: While he was fracing up for a fight, the fire on the sacrificial altar with the officiating priests and spiritual guides suddenly brightened.
ramayan::857.english_translation: While Rama was speaking like this, eager for combat, the sacrificial altar with the priests and teachers suddenly blazed forth.
ramayan::857.translation_literal: रामस्य (of Rama) / एवम् (thus) / ब्रुवाणस्य (while speaking) / त्वरितस्य (eager, hastening) / युयुत्सया (with desire to fight) / प्रजज्वाल (blazed up) / ततः (then) / वेदिः (the sacrificial altar) / स-उपाध्याय-पुरोहिता (with teachers and priests)
ramayan::857.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::857.essence: The scene brightens as Rama’s resolve hardens.
ramayan::857.simple_meaning: As Rama spoke with battle on his mind, the sacrificial fire suddenly flared up along with the altar and the priests.
ramayan::857.simple_insight: The moment of resolve is met by a sign that the path is opening.
ramayan::857.detailed_meaning: Rama has just urged Lakshmana to stay alert as the sixth day of Vishwamitra’s rites arrives. In that charged pause, the altar and its priests blaze brighter. The verse is a scene detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::857.modern_relevance: You are waiting for the right moment to act, and then everything suddenly sharpens: the room, the task, your own resolve. The signal is in the timing.
ramayan::857.insight: It shifts attention from inner readiness to the outward sign that action is now unfolding.

ramayan::858.verse_sanskrit: सदर्भचमसस्रुक्का ससमित्कुसुमोच्चया । विश्वामित्रेण सहिता वेदिर्जज्वाल सर्त्विजा । । 1309 । ।
ramayan::858.verse_hindi: The altar with Viswamitra and the officiating priests, kusa grass, ladles and square
ramayan::858.english_translation: The altar blazed with Viswamitra, the priests, and the sacred ritual items.
ramayan::858.translation_literal: सदर्भ-चमस-स्रुक्का (with darbha grass, ladles, and spoon) / स-समित्-कुसुम-उच्चया (heaped with firewood and flowers) / विश्वामित्रेण (with Viswamitra) / सहिता (accompanied) / वेदिः (the altar) / जज्वाल (blazed) / स-र्त्विजा (with the officiating priests)
ramayan::858.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::858.essence: The rite is ready, and the air is charged before anything happens.
ramayan::858.simple_meaning: The sacrificial altar blazed brightly, surrounded by Viswamitra, the priests, and the ritual materials.
ramayan::858.simple_insight: The scene is being set for a sacred rite, not a teaching.
ramayan::858.detailed_meaning: Rama has warned Lakshmana to stay alert as the sixth day begins. Viswamitra and the priests stand ready around the altar, which blazes with ritual items in place. This verse simply completes the scene before the sacrifice unfolds.
ramayan::858.modern_relevance: You can feel the moment before a ceremony begins: everything arranged, everyone ready, and the air holding its breath.
ramayan::858.insight: It keeps the focus on preparation and atmosphere before the event itself.

ramayan::859.verse_sanskrit: मन्त्रवच्च यथान्यायं यज्ञोऽसौ सम्प्रवर्तते । आकाशे च महान् शब्द: प्रादुरासीद्भयानक: । । 13010 । ।
ramayan::859.verse_hindi: While the sacrifice was being performed in accordance with mantras, a great sound causing fear emerged from the sky.
ramayan::859.english_translation: While the sacrifice was being performed in accordance with the mantras, a great and frightening sound arose from the sky.
ramayan::859.translation_literal: मन्त्रवत् (according to the mantras) / च (and) / यथान्यायम् (properly, in due order) / यज्ञः (the sacrifice) / असौ (this) / सम्प्रवर्तते (is proceeding) / आकाशे (in the sky) / च (and) / महान् (great) / शब्दः (sound) / प्रादुरासीत् (appeared) / भयानकः (terrifying)
ramayan::859.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::859.essence: Order can be shattered the moment it seems complete.
ramayan::859.simple_meaning: The sacrifice is underway exactly as it should be, but a terrifying sound suddenly comes from the sky.
ramayan::859.simple_insight: Even a sacred act can be interrupted by danger without warning.
ramayan::859.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra’s sacrifice has begun with priests, offerings, and careful ritual order. Just as the ceremony settles into rhythm, a terrifying sound erupts from the sky, signaling that unseen forces are about to attack the rite.
ramayan::859.modern_relevance: You finally get the room quiet, the plan in place, and the work moving — then something outside your control breaks in without warning.
ramayan::859.insight: It shifts attention from ritual order to the sudden arrival of disruption.

ramayan::860.verse_sanskrit: आवार्य गगनं मेघो यथा प्रावृषि निर्गत: । तथामायां विकुर्वाणौ राक्षसावभ्यधावताम् । । 13011 । ।
ramayan::860.verse_hindi: Like the clouds in the rainy season, the two rakshasas (Maricha and Subahu), covering the sky through their power of illusion, came running (to the sacrificial place).
ramayan::860.english_translation: Like the clouds in the rainy season, the two rakshasas, using illusion to cover the sky, rushed toward the sacrifice.
ramayan::860.translation_literal: आवार्य (covering) / गगनं (the sky) / मेघो (like clouds) / यथा (as) / प्रावृषि (in the rainy season) / निर्गत: (emerged) / तथामायां (through illusion) / विकुर्वाणौ (displaying) / राक्षसौ (the two rakshasas) / अभ्यधावताम् (rushed forward)
ramayan::860.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::860.essence: The attack begins by swallowing the sky.
ramayan::860.simple_meaning: Two demons used illusion to darken the sky and rush at the sacrifice like storm clouds.
ramayan::860.simple_insight: Some threats arrive by overwhelming the senses before they strike.
ramayan::860.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra's sacrifice is underway when a fearsome sound rises from the sky. Maricha and Subahu appear with magical force, blotting out the heavens and charging toward the ritual place. The verse is a scene-setting attack, not a teaching.
ramayan::860.insight: It sets up the assault on the sacrifice by showing the attackers' deceptive power and speed.

ramayan::861.verse_sanskrit: मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च तयोरनुचराश्च ये । आगम्य भीमसङ्काशा रुधिरौघमवासृजन् । । 13012 । ।
ramayan::861.verse_hindi: Maricha and Subahu of fearful appearance arrived with their followers and rained streams of blood (on the sacrificial altar).
ramayan::861.english_translation: Maricha and Subahu, along with their followers, arrived in terrible form and poured out streams of blood.
ramayan::861.translation_literal: मारीचः (Maricha) / च (and) / सुबाहुः (Subahu) / च (and) / तयोः (of those two) / अनुचराः (followers) / च (and) / ये (who) / आगम्य (having come) / भीमसङ्काशाः (terrible-looking) / रुधिरौघम् (a stream of blood) / अवासृजन् (they released)
ramayan::861.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::861.essence: The ritual is attacked by a violent force.
ramayan::861.simple_meaning: Maricha, Subahu, and their followers came in frightening forms and spilled blood across the sacrifice.
ramayan::861.simple_insight: Some threats arrive not as ideas, but as violent disruption.
ramayan::861.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra’s sacrifice, the rakshasas return to ruin the ritual. Maricha and Subahu arrive with their followers, grotesque and hostile, and shower the altar with blood. The verse is a vivid attack scene, not a teaching.
ramayan::861.modern_relevance: A carefully prepared moment gets shattered by sudden sabotage, and everyone sees how fragile order can be.
ramayan::861.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the force that tries to destroy it.

ramayan::862.verse_sanskrit: सा तेन रुधिरौघेण वेदिर्जज्वाल मण्डिता । सहसाऽभिद्रुतो रामस्तानपश्य त्ततो दिवि । । 13013 । ।
ramayan::862.verse_hindi: Flames rose on the sacrificial altar drenched by the stream of blood. Immediately Rama rushed forward and beheld them in the sky.
ramayan::862.english_translation: Flames rose on the sacrificial altar drenched by the stream of blood. Immediately Rama rushed forward and beheld them in the sky.
ramayan::862.translation_literal: सा (that) / तेन (by that) / रुधिरौघेण (by a stream of blood) / वेदिḥ (the sacrificial altar) / जज्वाल (blazed) / मण्डिता (adorned) / सहसा (suddenly) / अभिद्रुतः (rushed forward) / रामः (Rama) / तान् (them) / अपश्यत् (saw) / ततः (then) / दिवि (in the sky)
ramayan::862.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::862.essence: He sees the threat and moves before it can spread.
ramayan::862.simple_meaning: Blood drenches the sacrificial altar, and Rama immediately rushes forward to confront the attackers in the sky.
ramayan::862.simple_insight: When the moment turns violent, he moves at once.
ramayan::862.detailed_meaning: Maricha and Subahu have attacked Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flooding the altar with blood. The sacred fire now burns against a scene of desecration, and Rama springs forward to meet the threat before the next verse turns to his response.
ramayan::862.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and realize something precious is being ruined in front of you. There is no time to overthink; you move.
ramayan::862.insight: It shows the instant when duty becomes action, before hesitation can enter.

ramayan::863.verse_sanskrit: तावापतन्तौ सहसा दृष्ट्वा राजीवलोचन: । लक्ष्मणं त्वभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य रामो वचनमब्रवीत् । । 13014 । ।
ramayan::863.verse_hindi: Having seen them (Maricha and Subahu) suddenly advancing the lotuseyed Rama gazed at Lakshmana and said:
ramayan::863.english_translation: Having seen them suddenly advancing, the lotus-eyed Rama looked at Lakshmana and said:
ramayan::863.translation_literal: तौ (those two) / आपतन्तौ (rushing forward) / सहसा (suddenly) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / राजीवलोचनः (lotus-eyed) / लक्ष्मणं (Lakshmana) / तु (then) / अभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य (looking toward) / रामः (Rama) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::863.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::863.essence: He sees the threat first, then chooses his response.
ramayan::863.simple_meaning: Rama sees the two attackers rushing in and turns to Lakshmana before speaking.
ramayan::863.simple_insight: A calm response begins with seeing clearly before acting.
ramayan::863.detailed_meaning: Maricha and Subahu have begun their assault on Vishvamitra’s sacrifice. After the altar blazes with blood, Rama spots them rushing in. He turns to Lakshmana and prepares to answer the threat, but this line is only the opening movement of that response.
ramayan::863.modern_relevance: You notice the problem coming in fast, and your first move is not panic — it is a quick look to the person beside you.
ramayan::863.insight: It frames action as deliberate response, not blind reaction.

ramayan::864.verse_sanskrit: पश्य लक्ष्मण दुर्वृत्तान् राक्षसान् पिशिताशनान् । मानवास्त्रसमाधूताननिलेन यथा घनान् । । 13015 । ।
ramayan::864.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, behold, by manavaastra I shall chase, like clouds scattered by winds those wicked rakshasas who eat human flesh.
ramayan::864.english_translation: O Lakshmana, behold those wicked rakshasas who eat human flesh. I will scatter them with the Manavaastra, like clouds driven apart by wind.
ramayan::864.translation_literal: पश्य (behold) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / दुर्वृत्तान् (wicked) / राक्षसान् (rakshasas) / पिशिताशनान् (flesh-eaters) / मानवास्त्रसमाधूतान् (scattered by the Manavaastra) / अनिलेन (by wind) / यथा (like) / घनान् (clouds)
ramayan::864.speaker: Rama
ramayan::864.essence: He names the threat and moves to end it at once.
ramayan::864.simple_meaning: Rama points out the attacking demons to Lakshmana and says he will drive them away with a powerful weapon, like wind scattering clouds.
ramayan::864.simple_insight: Clear force can end a threat fast when restraint is no longer enough.
ramayan::864.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra's sacrifice, Maricha and Subahu rush in to ruin the rite. Rama turns to Lakshmana, names them as wicked flesh-eaters, and prepares to strike. The verse is a sharp prelude to the weapon he is about to unleash.
ramayan::864.modern_relevance: A threat keeps interrupting what matters, and you finally stop explaining yourself. You name the problem clearly and act before it spreads.
ramayan::864.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive response when protection is required.

ramayan::865.verse_sanskrit: मानवं परमोदारमस्त्रं परमभास्वरम् । चिक्षेप परमक्रुद्धो मारीचोरसि राघव: । । 13016 । ।
ramayan::865.verse_hindi: The inflamed Rama hurled the highly powerful and effulgent Manavaastra on the chest of Maricha.
ramayan::865.english_translation: The inflamed Rama hurled the highly powerful and effulgent Manavaastra on the chest of Maricha.
ramayan::865.translation_literal: मानवम् (manava) / परम-उदारम् (supremely generous, exalted) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / परम-भास्वरम् (highly radiant) / चिक्षेप (hurled) / परम-क्रुद्धः (greatly enraged) / मारीच-उरसि (on Maricha's chest) / राघवः (Raghava, Rama)
ramayan::865.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::865.essence: Rama answers danger with immediate, focused force.
ramayan::865.simple_meaning: Rama, burning with anger, launches a radiant weapon straight at Maricha.
ramayan::865.simple_insight: Sometimes the next right move is immediate and forceful.
ramayan::865.detailed_meaning: Maricha and Subahu rush toward the sacrifice. Rama, standing with Lakshmana, stops speaking and acts. He releases the Manavaastra directly at Maricha’s chest, turning warning into decisive force.
ramayan::865.modern_relevance: A threat is closing in and there is no time for debate. You see the problem clearly, act once, and end the hesitation.
ramayan::865.insight: It shows the shift from warning to decisive intervention when danger is already at the door.

ramayan::866.verse_sanskrit: स तेन परमास्त्रेण मानवेन समाहित: । संपूर्णं योजनशतं क्षिप्तस्सागरसम्प्लवे । । 13017 । ।
ramayan::866.verse_hindi: Smitten by that powerful Manavaastra, Maricha was thrown to a full distance of hundred yojanas into the surging high seas.
ramayan::866.english_translation: Smitten by that powerful Manavaastra, Maricha was thrown a full hundred yojanas into the surging sea.
ramayan::866.translation_literal: स (he) / तेन (by that) / परमास्त्रेण (by the supreme weapon) / मानवेन (with the Manava) / समाहितः (struck, hit) / संपूर्णम् (entire) / योजनशतम् (hundred yojanas) / क्षिप्तः (thrown) / सागरसम्प्लवे (into the surging sea)
ramayan::866.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::866.essence: One strike sends deception crashing out of reach.
ramayan::866.simple_meaning: Rama's weapon sends Maricha flying an immense distance into the sea.
ramayan::866.simple_insight: Some moments end all argument. Force can make a warning impossible to ignore.
ramayan::866.detailed_meaning: Rama has just released the Manavaastra at Maricha, the rakshasa who helped draw Sita away from safety. The weapon lands with such force that Maricha is hurled far into the sea, showing the sheer power of Rama's response.
ramayan::866.modern_relevance: A lie has finally been exposed in the meeting, and the room goes silent. One clear response can scatter a whole web of manipulation.
ramayan::866.insight: It shows how decisive action can cut through a dangerous threat before it spreads further.

ramayan::867.verse_sanskrit: विचेतनं विघूर्णन्तं शीतेषु बलताडितम् । निरस्तं दृश्य मारीचं रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् । । 13018 । ।
ramayan::867.verse_hindi: Having seen Maricha beaten by the power of that coolarrowed astra, thrown to a distance, reeling and lying unconscious, Rama spoke to Lakshmana:
ramayan::867.english_translation: Having seen Maricha beaten by the force of that cool-arrowed weapon, thrown far away, reeling and lying unconscious, Rama spoke to Lakshmana:
ramayan::867.translation_literal: विचेतनम् (unconscious) / विघूर्णन्तम् (reeling) / शीतेषु (cool-arrowed) / बलताडितम् (struck by force) / निरस्तम् (thrown away) / दृश्य (having seen) / मारीचम् (Maricha) / रामः (Rama) / लक्ष्मणम् (to Lakshmana) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::867.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::867.essence: The blow lands; the explanation comes after.
ramayan::867.simple_meaning: Rama sees Maricha stunned and thrown far away, then turns to Lakshmana to speak.
ramayan::867.simple_insight: A decisive blow has landed, and the next lesson is about to begin.
ramayan::867.detailed_meaning: Maricha has just been struck by Rama's weapon and hurled away, unconscious and reeling. Rama turns to Lakshmana in the aftermath, using the scene as proof of the weapon's force before explaining what it means.
ramayan::867.modern_relevance: You watch the problem finally collapse after all that effort, and only then do you understand what actually worked.
ramayan::867.insight: It marks the aftermath of action, not the teaching itself.

ramayan::868.verse_sanskrit: पश्य लक्ष्मण शीतेषुं मानवं धर्मसंहितम् । मोहयित्वा नयत्येनं न च प्राणैर्व्ययुज्यत । । 13019 । ।
ramayan::868.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana behold this Manavaastra associated with righteousness employing a cool arrow, which carries him away by making him unconscious and yet not taking his life.
ramayan::868.english_translation: O Lakshmana, behold this Manavaastra joined with righteousness: it carries him away into unconsciousness, yet does not separate him from life.
ramayan::868.translation_literal: पश्य (behold) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / शीतेषुं (cool-arrowed) / मानवं (Manavaastra) / धर्मसंहितम् (joined with righteousness) / मोहयित्वा (having made unconscious) / नयति (carries away) / एनं (him) / न (not) / च (and) / प्राणैः (with life-breaths) / व्ययुज्यत (separates)
ramayan::868.speaker: Rama
ramayan::868.essence: True strength can disable without destroying.
ramayan::868.simple_meaning: A righteous weapon can knock someone out without killing them.
ramayan::868.simple_insight: Real strength knows how to stop harm without becoming harm.
ramayan::868.detailed_meaning: Rama has just seen Maricha hurled far into the sea by his weapon. He turns to Lakshmana and points out the strange precision of that force: it overwhelms without killing. The moment highlights controlled power before the next violent response.
ramayan::868.modern_relevance: You shut down a harmful conversation without humiliating the other person. The strongest response is sometimes the one that ends the danger and leaves dignity intact.
ramayan::868.insight: It teaches you to use force with restraint, aiming to neutralize harm rather than destroy the person.

ramayan::869.verse_sanskrit: इमानपि वधिष्यामि निर्घृणान् दुष्टचारिण: । राक्षसान् पापकर्मस्थान् यज्ञघ्नान् रुधिराशनान् । । 13020 । ।
ramayan::869.verse_hindi: I shall slay these merciless, wicked doors of sinful acts destroyers of sacrifices and blood rakshasas.
ramayan::869.english_translation: I shall slay these merciless, wicked beings of evil conduct, destroyers of sacrifices, and drinkers of blood.
ramayan::869.translation_literal: इमान् (these) / अपि (also) / वधिष्यामि (I shall slay) / निर्घृणान् (merciless) / दुष्टचारिणः (wicked in conduct) / राक्षसान् (rakshasas) / पापकर्मस्थान् (abodes of sinful deeds) / यज्ञघ्नान् (destroyers of sacrifices) / रुधिराशनान् (blood-eaters)
ramayan::869.speaker: Rama
ramayan::869.essence: Rama does not only answer one attack; he commits to ending the source of it.
ramayan::869.simple_meaning: Rama vows to kill the cruel rakshasas who spoil sacrifices and live on violence.
ramayan::869.simple_insight: Some threats are answered not with debate, but with decisive protection.
ramayan::869.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has just seen Maricha struck down by a divine weapon. He turns to Lakshmana and names the larger evil behind the attack: rakshasas who interrupt sacred rites and prey on others. This line is his vow before the next strike.
ramayan::869.modern_relevance: You see the pattern, not just the person: the same cruelty keeps showing up in different masks, and you finally decide to stop it.
ramayan::869.insight: It shifts you from reacting to one incident to confronting the whole source of harm.

ramayan::870.verse_sanskrit: सङ्गृह्यास्त्रं ततो रामो दिव्यमाग्नेयमद्भुतम् । सुबाहूरसि चिक्षेप सविद्ध: प्रापतद्भुवि । । 13021 । ।
ramayan::870.verse_hindi: Then Rama took hold of the celestial, marvellous Agneya weapon and hurled it into the chest of Subahu. Struck, Subahuhe fell down on the ground.
ramayan::870.english_translation: Then Rama took hold of the celestial, marvellous Agneya weapon and hurled it into the chest of Subahu. Struck, Subahu fell down on the ground.
ramayan::870.translation_literal: सङ्गृह्य (taking hold of) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / ततः (then) / रामः (Rama) / दिव्यम् (celestial) / आग्नेयम् (of fire) / अद्भुतम् (marvellous) / सुबाहोः (of Subahu) / असि (into the chest) / चिक्षेप (threw) / सविद्धः (struck) / प्रापतत् (fell down) / भुवि (on the ground)
ramayan::870.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::870.essence: Rama acts decisively to protect a sacred act from disruption.
ramayan::870.simple_meaning: Rama uses a divine fire weapon against Subahu, and Subahu falls to the ground.
ramayan::870.simple_insight: Power is only as clean as the purpose behind it.
ramayan::870.detailed_meaning: In Vishvamitra's sacrifice, Rama has already seen the danger: rakshasas are trying to ruin a sacred rite. He answers without hesitation, drawing a celestial fire weapon and striking Subahu down. The scene moves the rescue forward, not the teaching.
ramayan::870.modern_relevance: You see the threat clearly, act fast, and end it before it spreads. Some moments do not ask for reflection; they ask for decisive force.
ramayan::870.insight: It shows force used in service of protection, not aggression.

ramayan::871.verse_sanskrit: शेषान् वायव्यमादाय निजघान महायशा: । राघव: परमोदारो मुनीनां मुदमावहन् । । 13022 । ।
ramayan::871.verse_hindi: Illustrious and highly generous Rama killed the  remaining rakshasas  with the Vayavya weapon to the delight of the ascetics.
ramayan::871.english_translation: Illustrious and highly generous Rama killed the remaining rakshasas with the Vayavya weapon, delighting the ascetics.
ramayan::871.translation_literal: शेषान् (the remaining) / वायव्यम् (the Vayavya weapon) / आदाय (taking up) / निजघान (he struck down) / महायशाः (the highly illustrious one) / राघवः (Rama) / परमोदारः (highly generous) / मुनीनाम् (of the ascetics) / मुदम् (joy) / आवहन् (bringing)
ramayan::871.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::871.essence: Protecting others sometimes requires ending the threat completely.
ramayan::871.simple_meaning: Rama used the Vayavya weapon to destroy the remaining demons, and the ascetics were pleased.
ramayan::871.simple_insight: Sometimes protection means decisive force, not hesitation.
ramayan::871.detailed_meaning: Rama has already begun clearing the forest of the rakshasas who disrupt the sages' rites. After striking Subahu, he now finishes the remaining attackers with the Vayavya weapon, and the ascetics feel relief as their sacrifices are finally safe.
ramayan::871.modern_relevance: A room is finally quiet after weeks of one person poisoning every meeting. You do not need more patience; you need the courage to end what keeps harming everyone else.
ramayan::871.insight: It shifts the mind from passive tolerance to protective action.

ramayan::872.verse_sanskrit: स हत्वा राक्षसान् सर्वान् यज्ञघ्नान् रघुनन्दन: । ऋषिभि: पूजितस्तत्र यथेन्द्रो विजये पुरा । । 13023 । ।
ramayan::872.verse_hindi: Having killed the rakshasas, obstructors of sacrifices, Rama was worshipped by the hermits like Indra was honoured in the past when he was victorious.
ramayan::872.english_translation: Having killed the rakshasas, obstructors of sacrifices, Rama was worshipped by the hermits like Indra was honoured in the past when he was victorious.
ramayan::872.translation_literal: सः (he) / हत्वा (having killed) / राक्षसान् (rakshasas) / सर्वान् (all) / यज्ञघ्नान् (sacrifice-obstructors) / रघुनन्दनः (Rama, delight of Raghu) / ऋषिभिः (by the sages) / पूजितः (honoured) / तत्र (there) / यथा (like) / इन्द्रः (Indra) / विजये (in victory) / पुरा (formerly) /
ramayan::872.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::872.essence: Victory matters here because it lets sacred work continue.
ramayan::872.simple_meaning: Rama destroys the demons who disrupt the sacrifice, and the sages honor him in gratitude.
ramayan::872.simple_insight: Some victories are measured by the peace they restore, not by the enemies they defeat.
ramayan::872.detailed_meaning: At Vishwamitra’s sacrifice, Rama has just slain Subahu and the other rakshasas attacking the ritual. With the threat gone, the hermits honor him like a victorious Indra. The verse closes the action before Vishwamitra speaks again.
ramayan::872.modern_relevance: You finish the hard part of protecting something fragile, and only then do people feel safe enough to thank you.
ramayan::872.insight: It turns a battle result into a sign of restored order, not personal glory.

ramayan::873.verse_sanskrit: अथ यज्ञे समाप्ते तु विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । निरीतिका दिशो दृष्टवा काकुत्स्थमिदमब्रवीत् । । 13024 । ।
ramayan::873.verse_hindi: Thereafter, when the sacrifice was completed, maharshi Viswamitra beholding all the directions  bereft of evils, said to Rama:
ramayan::873.english_translation: Thereafter, when the sacrifice was completed, the great sage Vishwamitra, seeing that all directions were now free of disturbance, said to Rama:
ramayan::873.translation_literal: अथ (thereafter) / यज्ञे (in the sacrifice) / समाप्ते (having been completed) / तु (then) / विश्वामित्रो (Vishvamitra) / महामुनि: (the great sage) / निरीतिका (free from disturbance) / दिशो (the directions) / दृष्टवा (having seen) / काकुत्स्थम (to Kakutstha/Rama) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::873.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::873.essence: The danger is gone, and the next instruction can finally be given.
ramayan::873.simple_meaning: The sacrifice is over, the land is safe again, and Vishvamitra turns to Rama to speak.
ramayan::873.simple_insight: Some battles end quietly, with relief settling over everyone at once.
ramayan::873.detailed_meaning: Rama has just destroyed the rakshasas who were disturbing Vishvamitra's sacrifice. With the ritual complete and the directions now peaceful, the sage turns to Rama to continue the journey. This verse simply marks that turning point.
ramayan::873.modern_relevance: You finally close the door on a hard task, and only then do you notice how tense the room had been.
ramayan::873.insight: It marks the shift from crisis to conversation, after protection has been restored.

ramayan::874.verse_sanskrit: अथ तां रजनीं तत्र कृतार्थौ रामलक्ष्मणौ । ऊषतुर्मुदितौ वीरौ प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना । । 1311 । ।
ramayan::874.verse_hindi: There, with their purpose fulfilled the heroes, Rama and Lakshmana, full of joy in their hearts spent the night.
ramayan::874.english_translation: There, with their purpose fulfilled, the heroes Rama and Lakshmana spent the night in joy, their inner hearts delighted.
ramayan::874.translation_literal: अथ (then) / तां (that) / रजनीं (night) / तत्र (there) / कृतार्थौ (having accomplished their aim) / रामलक्ष्मणौ (Rama and Lakshmana) / मुदितौ (joyful) / वीरौ (the two heroes) / प्रहृष्टेन (with delighted) / अन्तरात्मना (inner heart) / ऊषतुḥ (spent / passed the night)
ramayan::874.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::874.essence: Completed duty can turn danger into rest.
ramayan::874.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana had finished the task before them, so they passed the night in happiness.
ramayan::874.simple_insight: Peace comes after right action is completed.
ramayan::874.detailed_meaning: After Vishwamitra's sacrifice is protected and the threat is gone, Rama and Lakshmana stay the night there. The brothers are no longer tense or alert; their task has been fulfilled, and the relief shows in their joy.
ramayan::874.modern_relevance: You finally shut the laptop after the hardest part is done. The room is quiet, your shoulders drop, and for once you can feel the relief of having finished well.
ramayan::874.insight: It shifts attention from struggle to the calm that follows fulfilled duty.

ramayan::875.verse_sanskrit: प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां कृतपौर्वाह्णिकक्रियौ । विश्वामित्रमृषींश्चान्यान् सहितावभिजग्मतु: । । 1312 । ।
ramayan::875.verse_hindi: As the night dawned, both the brothers performed the morning rites and approached Viswamitra and other rishis.
ramayan::875.english_translation: As night gave way to dawn, both brothers completed their morning rites and went together to Viswamitra and the other sages.
ramayan::875.translation_literal: प्रभातायाम् (at dawn) / तु (then) / शर्वर्याम् (in the night) / कृत-पौर्वाह्णिक-क्रियौ (having done the morning rites) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / ऋषीन् (the sages) / च (and) / अन्यान् (others) / सहितौ (together) / अभिजग्मतुः (they went)
ramayan::875.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::875.essence: They begin the day by restoring order before action.
ramayan::875.simple_meaning: At dawn, Rama and Lakshmana finish their morning duties and go together to Viswamitra and the other sages.
ramayan::875.simple_insight: Even in a sacred journey, the day begins with order and discipline.
ramayan::875.detailed_meaning: After the night of fulfilled purpose, Rama and Lakshmana rise at dawn, complete their morning rites, and go with Viswamitra to meet the gathered sages. The verse simply moves the story forward from rest to renewed readiness.
ramayan::875.modern_relevance: You wake before the day starts, wash, breathe, and do what grounds you before checking your phone. The first move is not noise — it is readiness.
ramayan::875.insight: It shifts attention from rushing ahead to beginning with disciplined preparation.

ramayan::876.verse_sanskrit: अभिवाद्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् । ऊचतुर्मधुरोदारं वाक्यं मधुरभाषिणौ । । 1313 । ।
ramayan::876.verse_hindi: Sweettongued, they visited with folded hands the best of ascetics Viswamitra who was shining like a flaming fire and addressed him  thus in sweet and generous words:
ramayan::876.english_translation: After bowing to the great sage, shining like blazing fire, the two sweet-tongued brothers spoke to him in gentle, noble words.
ramayan::876.translation_literal: अभिवाद्य (having bowed to) / मुनिश्रेष्ठं (the best of ascetics) / ज्वलन्तमिव (like blazing) / पावकम् (fire) / ऊचतुḥ (they spoke) / मधुरोदारं (sweet and noble) / वाक्यं (words) / मधुरभाषिणौ (the sweet-speaking pair)
ramayan::876.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::876.essence: Humility comes first; even heroes bow before the teacher.
ramayan::876.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana bow to Vishvamitra and speak to him with respect and sweetness.
ramayan::876.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before any request is made.
ramayan::876.detailed_meaning: After a night of success, Rama and Lakshmana go to Vishvamitra, the sage who has guided them. They bow first, then speak with care. The verse shows the brothers’ humility before the teacher who is about to send them onward.
ramayan::876.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has earned your trust, and you do not rush to speak. You begin with respect, because the next conversation depends on it.
ramayan::876.insight: It teaches you to approach guidance with humility before asking for anything.

ramayan::877.verse_sanskrit: इमौ स्म मुनिशार्दूल किङ्करौ समुपस्थितौ । आज्ञापय यथेष्टं वै शासनं करवाव किम् । । 1314 । ।
ramayan::877.verse_hindi: O tiger among ascetics, we  two are at your  service. Command whatever you want and we shall execute it.
ramayan::877.english_translation: O tiger among ascetics, we two are at your service. Command whatever you want, and we shall carry out your order.
ramayan::877.translation_literal: इमौ (these two) / स्म (indeed) / मुनिशार्दूल (tiger among ascetics) / किङ्करौ (servants) / समुपस्थितौ (present, standing ready) / आज्ञापय (command) / यथेष्टं (as you wish) / वै (indeed) / शासनं (order) / करवाव (let us do) / किम् (what)
ramayan::877.speaker: Rama and Lakshmana
ramayan::877.essence: True service begins before you know the assignment.
ramayan::877.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana tell Vishwamitra that they are ready to serve and will do whatever he asks.
ramayan::877.simple_insight: Real readiness means being available before the task is named.
ramayan::877.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have just approached Vishwamitra after their morning rites. Standing before the sage, they bow and offer themselves completely, asking for his command. This moment opens their training under the teacher.
ramayan::877.modern_relevance: You’ve shown up to a meeting early, phone away, notes open, ready to be useful before anyone asks. That quiet availability changes the room.
ramayan::877.insight: It teaches you to meet responsibility with readiness, not resistance.

ramayan::878.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ता स्ततस्ताभ्यां सर्व एव महर्षय: । विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य रामं वचनमब्रुवन् । । 1315 । ।
ramayan::878.verse_hindi: Addressed, thus by both of them, Viswamitra ahead of all the sages, spoke to Rama.
ramayan::878.english_translation: Then, all the great sages, with Viswamitra leading them, spoke to Rama.
ramayan::878.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्ताः (addressed) / ततः (then) / ताभ्याम् (by the two of them) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / महर्षयः (great sages) / विश्वामित्रम् (Viswamitra) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front) / रामम् (to Rama) / वचनम् (words) / अब्रुवन् (spoke)
ramayan::878.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::878.essence: The conversation turns toward Rama, and the real purpose of the visit begins.
ramayan::878.simple_meaning: The sages, with Viswamitra at the front, turn to Rama and begin speaking.
ramayan::878.simple_insight: A new instruction is about to begin, and Rama is being drawn into the next step.
ramayan::878.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just been welcomed by Rama and Lakshmana. Now the gathered sages step forward with him and address Rama directly. The verse is a transition: it prepares the ground for the request that follows about Janaka’s sacrifice.
ramayan::878.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after introductions, and everyone turns toward the one person who must now decide what happens next.
ramayan::878.insight: It shifts the scene from greeting to instruction, setting up the sages’ request to Rama.

ramayan::879.verse_sanskrit: मैथिलस्य नरश्रेष्ठ जनकस्य भविष्यति । यज्ञ: परमधर्मिष्ठस्तस्य यास्यामहे वयम् । । 1316 । ।
ramayan::879.verse_hindi: O foremost of men, Janaka, king of Mithila, is performing a great religious sacrifice. We shall go there.
ramayan::879.english_translation: O foremost of men, Janaka, king of Mithila, is performing a great religious sacrifice. We shall go there.
ramayan::879.translation_literal: मैथिलस्य (of the king of Mithila) / नरश्रेष्ठ (O foremost among men) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / भविष्यति (is taking place) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / परमधर्मिष्ठः (most righteous, greatly devoted to dharma) / तस्य (there) / यास्यामहे (we shall go) / वयम् (we)
ramayan::879.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::879.essence: The next step is a journey to the place where everything will change.
ramayan::879.simple_meaning: Janaka is holding a great sacrifice in Mithila, and the sages decide to go there.
ramayan::879.simple_insight: Sometimes a journey begins because a sacred event is happening somewhere else.
ramayan::879.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has asked for Rama's help, and the sages are now setting the route. They mention Janaka's great sacrifice in Mithila as the place they will travel to next, leading directly toward the bow that will change Rama's life.
ramayan::879.modern_relevance: A friend says, “Come with us — there’s something important happening there.” You don’t yet know the full reason, but the path is already opening.
ramayan::879.insight: It shifts the mind from waiting at home to moving toward the place where destiny unfolds.

ramayan::880.verse_sanskrit: त्वं चैव नरशार्दूल सहास्माभिर्गमिष्यसि । अद्भुतं धनुरत्नं च तत्र तद्रष्टुमर्हसि । । 1317 । ।
ramayan::880.verse_hindi: O tiger among men, come along with us. You ought to see there the wonderful  jewel of a bow.
ramayan::880.english_translation: O tiger among men, come along with us. You ought to see there the wonderful jewel of a bow.
ramayan::880.translation_literal: त्वं (you) / च (also) / एव (indeed) / नरशार्दूल (tiger among men) / सह (with) / अस्माभिः (us) / गमिष्यसि (you will go) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful) / धनुरत्नम् (jewel of a bow) / च (and) / तत्र (there) / तत् (that) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अर्हसि (you ought)
ramayan::880.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::880.essence: The invitation matters because it leads Rama to the bow that will change his life.
ramayan::880.simple_meaning: The sages invite Rama to come with them and see Janaka's extraordinary bow.
ramayan::880.simple_insight: Some moments matter because they open the door to what will change everything.
ramayan::880.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra and the sages are leading Rama toward Mithila for Janaka's sacrifice. This line is only the invitation: they want Rama to come and witness the famed bow that will soon define the next turning point.
ramayan::880.modern_relevance: A friend says, “Come with me, you need to see this,” and you go without knowing the day will split in two. Some invitations are really thresholds.
ramayan::880.insight: It frames the bow as a signpost to a larger destiny, not just an object to be admired.

ramayan::881.verse_sanskrit: तद्धि पूर्वं नरश्रेष्ठ दत्तं सदसि दैवतै: । अप्रमेयबलं घोरं मखे परमभास्वरम् । । 1318 । ।
ramayan::881.verse_hindi: O best among men, this bow of immeasurable energy. dreadful and highly lustrous was bestowed on king Janaka by devatas in a sacrificial  assembly in the past.
ramayan::881.english_translation: O best among men, this bow of immeasurable energy, dreadful and highly lustrous, was once bestowed on Janaka by the divine beings in a sacrificial assembly.
ramayan::881.translation_literal: तत् (that) / हि (indeed) / पूर्वम् (formerly) / नरश्रेष्ठ (O best among men) / दत्तम् (given) / सदसि (in the assembly) / दैवतैः (by the divine beings) / अप्रमेय-बलम् (of immeasurable power) / घोरम् (dreadful) / मखे (in the sacrifice) / परम-भास्वरम् (highly lustrous)
ramayan::881.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::881.essence: The bow’s history makes the coming test feel impossible.
ramayan::881.simple_meaning: The bow was given to Janaka long ago by the divine beings during a sacrifice. It is so powerful and radiant that it inspires awe.
ramayan::881.simple_insight: Some objects carry a history so heavy that even touching them feels like a test.
ramayan::881.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra is leading Rama and Lakshmana toward Janaka’s sacrifice and the famous bow. He explains that the weapon was not ordinary: it came from the divine beings in an ancient ritual gathering. The point is to prepare them for the challenge ahead.
ramayan::881.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone goes quiet because one object on the table has become the whole challenge. Its story matters before you even touch it.
ramayan::881.insight: It frames the bow as a sacred obstacle, raising the stakes before the attempt to lift it.

ramayan::882.verse_sanskrit: नास्य देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरा न च राक्षसा: । कर्तुमारोपणं शक्ता न कथञ्चन मानुषा: । । 1319 । ।
ramayan::882.verse_hindi: Neither devas, nor gandharvas, nor asuras nor human, are capable of stringing the bow by any means.
ramayan::882.english_translation: Neither devas, nor gandharvas, nor asuras, nor human beings are capable of stringing the bow by any means.
ramayan::882.translation_literal: न (not) / अस्य (of this) / देवा: (devas) / न (nor) / गन्धर्वा: (gandharvas) / न (nor) / असुरा: (asuras) / न (nor) / च (and) / राक्षसा: (rakshasas) / कर्तुं (to do) / आरोपणं (the stringing) / शक्ता: (able) / न (not) / कथञ्चन (by any means) / मानुषा: (humans)
ramayan::882.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::882.essence: The bow defeats every claimant before Rama even touches it.
ramayan::882.simple_meaning: No one can string this bow, not even the powerful beings who might seem capable of it.
ramayan::882.simple_insight: Some things are meant to be impossible until the right person arrives.
ramayan::882.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, Vishwamitra has brought Rama and Lakshmana to see the bow that no one has been able to lift, let alone string. This line heightens the challenge before Rama is asked to prove himself.
ramayan::882.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the hardest task in the building lands on your desk. Everyone knows others have failed. The question becomes whether you will even try.
ramayan::882.insight: It builds suspense by showing the task's impossibility before the decisive test begins.

ramayan::883.verse_sanskrit: धनुषस्तस्य वीर्यं तु जिज्ञासन्तो महीक्षित: । न शेकुरारोपयितुं राजपुत्रा महाबला: । । 13110 । ।
ramayan::883.verse_hindi: Mighty princes and kings have failed to string it, in their attempt to know its strength.
ramayan::883.english_translation: Mighty princes and kings, trying to test its strength, could not string that bow.
ramayan::883.translation_literal: धनुषः (of the bow) / तस्य (its) / वीर्यम् (strength) / तु (indeed) / जिज्ञासन्तः (desiring to know) / महीक्षितः (kings) / न (not) / शेकुः (were able) / आरोपयितुम् (to string) / राजपुत्राः (princes) / महाबलाः (mighty)
ramayan::883.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::883.essence: Raw power is useless when the task demands more than force.
ramayan::883.simple_meaning: Even powerful princes and kings could not lift and string the bow while trying to test how strong it was.
ramayan::883.simple_insight: Pride meets its limit fast when power is only borrowed.
ramayan::883.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court, the great bow has already defeated devas, gandharvas, asuras, and human warriors. Now even mighty princes and kings try to prove themselves against it, but none can string it. The scene builds the impossible standard that Rama alone will meet.
ramayan::883.modern_relevance: A room full of confident people keeps trying the same impossible fix, each one sure he can force it. The problem does not yield to force.
ramayan::883.insight: It shifts attention from proving strength to recognizing a challenge that cannot be conquered by ego.

ramayan::884.verse_sanskrit: तद्धनुर्नरशार्दूल मैथिलस्य महात्मन: । तत्र द्रक्ष्यसि काकुत्स्थ यज्ञं चाद्भुतदर्शनम् । । 13111 । ।
ramayan::884.verse_hindi: O best of men, O descendent of Kakustha, there you will see the bow that belongs to the magnanimous king of Mithila and the wonderful sacrifice at that place.
ramayan::884.english_translation: O best of men, O descendant of Kakustha, there you will see the bow of the magnanimous king of Mithila and the wondrous sacrifice there.
ramayan::884.translation_literal: तत् (that) / धनुः (bow) / नरशार्दूल (best of men) / मैथिलस्य (of the king of Mithila) / महात्मनः (of the magnanimous one) / तत्र (there) / द्रक्ष्यसि (you will see) / काकुत्स्थ (O descendant of Kakustha) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / च (and) / अद्भुतदर्शनम् (wonderful to behold)
ramayan::884.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::884.essence: The real test is waiting in the next room.
ramayan::884.simple_meaning: You will see the famous bow of Mithila and the remarkable sacrifice held there.
ramayan::884.simple_insight: Some moments matter because they lead into a turning point, not because they teach a lesson on their own.
