ramayan::982.verse_hindi: O Rama Himavans beloved of beautiful waist, wellknown by the name of Manorama is the daughter of Mount Meru. She is the mother to both the daughters.
ramayan::982.english_translation: O Rama, her mother was the beautiful-waisted Manorama, the beloved wife of Himavan, daughter of Meru.
ramayan::982.translation_literal: या (who) / मेरुदुहिता (daughter of Meru) / राम (Rama) / तयोः (of the two) / माता (mother) / सुमध्यमा (beautiful-waisted) / नाम्ना (by name) / मनोरमा (Manorama) / नाम (named) / पत्नी (wife) / हिमवत: (of Himavan) / प्रिया (beloved)
ramayan::982.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::982.essence: A lineage detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::982.simple_meaning: Manorama, daughter of Meru and beloved wife of Himavan, was the mother of the two daughters being described.
ramayan::982.simple_insight: The verse adds family detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::982.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is tracing the origin of the river Ganga for Rama. After naming Himavan and his daughters, he adds that their mother was Manorama, daughter of Meru and beloved of Himavan. It is a genealogical link in the larger origin story.
ramayan::982.modern_relevance: Someone is telling a family story at a gathering and pauses to add one more ancestor's name. The detail matters to the lineage, but it is still part of the unfolding tale, not a lesson on its own.
ramayan::982.insight: It keeps the genealogy clear so the next verse can identify the daughters.

ramayan::983.verse_sanskrit: तस्यां गङ्गेयमभवज्ज्येष्ठा हिमवतस्सुता । उमा नाम द्वितीयाभून्नाम्ना तस्यैव राघव । । 13516 । ।
ramayan::983.verse_hindi: O son of the Raghus this Ganga was born to Manorama as Himavans eldest daughter. A second one  born to him was wellknown by the name of Uma.
ramayan::983.english_translation: O son of the Raghus, Ganga was the eldest daughter born to Manorama, the daughter of Mount Meru. The second daughter was known by the name Uma.
ramayan::983.translation_literal: तस्याम् (in her) / गङ्गेयम् (Ganga) / अभवत् (became was born) / ज्येष्ठा (eldest) / हिमवत्सुता (daughter of Himavan) / उमा (Uma) / नाम (by name) / द्वितीया (second) / अभूत् (became) / नाम्ना (by name) / तस्याः (of her) / एव (indeed) / राघव (O Raghava)
ramayan::983.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::983.essence: These are not random names; they belong to a sacred lineage.
ramayan::983.simple_meaning: Ganga and Uma are identified here as the two daughters of Himavan, with Ganga the elder and Uma the younger.
ramayan::983.simple_insight: Some names carry lineage, not just identity.
ramayan::983.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing the family line of the mountain king Himavan. First he names the parents, then he identifies their two daughters: Ganga and Uma. The verse is setting up genealogy, not teaching a doctrine.
ramayan::983.modern_relevance: You hear a family story that seems to be only names, but it quietly places someone in a larger lineage. Some identities arrive already connected to a history bigger than the person.
ramayan::983.insight: It shifts attention from the individual name to the ancestry and meaning behind it.

ramayan::984.verse_sanskrit: अथ ज्येष्ठां सुरास्सर्वे देवतार्थचिकीर्षया । शैलेन्द्रं वरयामासुर्गङ्गां त्रिपथगां नदीम् । । 13517 । ।
ramayan::984.verse_hindi: Thereupon all the devatas desirous of deriving some advantage proposed that the eldest daughter of the king of mountains, Ganga, flowing in three directions be given to them.
ramayan::984.english_translation: Thereupon all the devas, seeking a benefit for the world of the gods, asked for Ganga, the eldest daughter of the mountain king, who flows in three paths.
ramayan::984.translation_literal: अथ (then) / ज्येष्ठाम् (the eldest) / सुराः (the devas) / सर्वे (all) / देवतार्थचिकीर्षया (with the wish to do benefit for the devas) / शैलेन्द्रम् (to the mountain king) / वरयामासुः (requested) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / त्रिपथगाम् (flowing in three paths) / नदीम् (the river)
ramayan::984.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::984.essence: A single request can set a world-changing river in motion.
ramayan::984.simple_meaning: The devas asked for Ganga, the eldest daughter of Himavan, because they wanted her for their own good.
ramayan::984.simple_insight: Great events often begin with a request that changes everything.
ramayan::984.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the origin of Ganga in the mountain king's family. After naming her sisters, he shows the devas approaching Himavan and asking for Ganga, because her descent will serve a larger cosmic purpose.
ramayan::984.modern_relevance: A family decision can become a turning point for many lives. What seems like one request can carry consequences far beyond the room where it is made.
ramayan::984.insight: It shifts attention from a private choice to the wider consequences that follow it.

ramayan::985.verse_sanskrit: ददौ धर्मेण हिमवान् तनयां लोकपावनीम् । स्वच्छन्दपथगां गङ्गां त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया । । 13518 । ।
ramayan::985.verse_hindi: In order to do good to the three worlds Himavan, rooted in dharma gifted his eldest daughter Ganga who sanctifies the whole world by flowing at her free will৷৷
ramayan::985.english_translation: For the good of the three worlds, Himavan, grounded in dharma, gave his daughter Ganga, who purifies the world by flowing freely.
ramayan::985.translation_literal: ददौ (gave) / धर्मेण (through dharma; in righteousness) / हिमवान् (Himavan) / तनयाम् (daughter) / लोकपावनीम् (world-purifying) / स्वच्छन्दपथगाम् (going by her own free course) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया (with the wish for the welfare of the three worlds)
ramayan::985.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::985.essence: True giving releases what can serve a wider good.
ramayan::985.simple_meaning: Himavan gives Ganga for the welfare of all worlds. The gift is righteous because it benefits more than one person.
ramayan::985.simple_insight: There is dignity in giving what can bless many, even when it is precious to you.
ramayan::985.detailed_meaning: The mountain king Himavan gives his daughter Ganga to the devas for the welfare of all three worlds. The verse pauses on the nobility of a gift made through dharma, not possession, so the cosmos itself can be helped.
ramayan::985.modern_relevance: You let a talented friend move cities for a chance that will help many people, even though it leaves a gap in your own life. Some gifts are larger than keeping.
ramayan::985.insight: It shifts the mind from possession to stewardship: what you hold is not always meant to stay with you.

ramayan::986.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य ततो देवास्त्रिलोकहितकारिण: । गङ्गामादाय तेऽगच्छन् कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना । । 13519 । ।
ramayan::986.verse_hindi: The devatas having received Ganga committed to the welfare of the three worlds went back to their abodes with a sense of fulfilment in their mind.
ramayan::986.english_translation: The devatas, having received Ganga for the welfare of the three worlds, returned to their own realms with hearts full of fulfillment.
ramayan::986.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / ततः (then) / देवाः (the devatas) / त्रिलोकहितकारिणः (welfare-doing for the three worlds) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / आदाय (having taken) / ते (they) / अगच्छन् (went) / कृतार्थेन (with fulfilled purpose) / अन्तरात्मना (with inner self)
ramayan::986.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::986.essence: A task ends cleanly when it reaches the right hands.
ramayan::986.simple_meaning: The devatas take Ganga and return satisfied, because their purpose has been fulfilled.
ramayan::986.simple_insight: Fulfilment comes when the right thing is done for the larger good.
ramayan::986.detailed_meaning: The devatas have secured Ganga from Himavan for the welfare of the three worlds. Their task is complete, so they leave with a settled, fulfilled mind. The verse closes this brief exchange before the story moves on to Ganga's other mountain-sister.
ramayan::986.modern_relevance: You finally send the proposal, make the call, or hand over the work that was never meant to stay with you. The relief is not in keeping it — it's in knowing the right place received it.
ramayan::986.insight: It shifts attention from possession to rightful transfer.

ramayan::987.verse_sanskrit: या चान्या शैलदुहिता कन्यासीद्रघुनन्दन । उग्रं सा व्रतमास्थाय तपस्तेपे तपोधना । । 13520 । ।
ramayan::987.verse_hindi: O Delight of the Raghus The other daughter of the mountain Himavan was a maiden whose wealth was tapas. She pursued a vow and observed severe austerities.
ramayan::987.english_translation: O Delight of the Raghus, the other daughter of the mountain Himavan was a maiden whose wealth was tapas. She undertook a fierce vow and performed severe austerities.
ramayan::987.translation_literal: या (who) / चान्या (and another) / शैलदुहिता (daughter of the mountain) / कन्या (maiden) / आसीत् (was) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu dynasty) / उग्रम् (fierce) / सा (she) / व्रतम् (vow) / आस्थाय (having undertaken) / तपः (austerity) / तेपे (performed) / तपोधनाः (one rich in austerity)
ramayan::987.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::987.essence: Her worth is shown first through disciplined austerity, not through a name.
ramayan::987.simple_meaning: The mountain king's other daughter was devoted to severe discipline and lived by a hard vow.
ramayan::987.simple_insight: Greatness can be built quietly, through steady self-restraint.
ramayan::987.detailed_meaning: After Ganga is given away for the welfare of the worlds, the poem turns to Himavan's other daughter. Before she is named, she is described by her tapas: a life of vow, heat, and discipline. This verse prepares for her union with Rudra.
ramayan::987.modern_relevance: When everyone else sees only the finished result, they miss the years of private discipline that made it possible. The real preparation often happens where no applause reaches.
ramayan::987.insight: It shifts attention from outcome to the hidden discipline that creates readiness.

ramayan::988.verse_sanskrit: उग्रेण तपसा युक्तां ददौ शैलवरस्सुताम् । रुद्रायाप्रतिरूपाय उमां लोकनमस्कृताम् । । 13521 । ।
ramayan::988.verse_hindi: Himavan the best of mountains gave his daughter Uma associated with severe
ramayan::988.english_translation: The best of mountains gave his daughter Uma, endowed with severe tapas, to Rudra, who was like no ordinary being and was honored by the world.
ramayan::988.translation_literal: उग्रेण (severe) / तपसा (by tapas) / युक्ताम् (endowed with) / ददौ (gave) / शैलवरः (the best of mountains) / सुताम् (daughter) / रुद्राय (to Rudra) / अप्रतिरूपाय (to the unmatched one) / उमाम् (Uma) / लोकनमस्कृताम् (honored by the world)
ramayan::988.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::988.essence: Worth shaped by tapas is fit for sacred union.
ramayan::988.simple_meaning: Himavan gave Uma, who had won her worth through severe tapas, to Rudra, a being beyond ordinary comparison and revered by all.
ramayan::988.simple_insight: Great union is not casual here; it is earned through discipline, worth, and recognition.
ramayan::988.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the mountain king Himavan and his daughter Uma, just after the account of Ganga. Uma is not introduced as a passive bride but as one whose tapas has made her radiant and worthy. The verse marks her giving in marriage to Rudra.
ramayan::988.modern_relevance: A family watches a daughter become someone’s partner after years of discipline, restraint, and character. What looks like a simple marriage carries the weight of all she has become.
ramayan::988.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony to the inner worth that makes such a union fitting.

ramayan::989.verse_sanskrit: एते ते शैलराजस्य सुते लोकनमस्कृते । गङ्गा च सरितां श्रेष्ठा उमादेवी च राघव । । 13522 । ।
ramayan::989.verse_hindi: O son of the Raghus Ganga, the holiest of rivers and Uma devi  are two daughters of the king of the mountains, (Himavan). They are worshipped by the entire world.
ramayan::989.english_translation: O son of the Raghus, Ganga, the holiest of rivers, and Uma Devi are those two daughters of the king of the mountains, honored by the whole world.
ramayan::989.translation_literal: एते (these) / ते (those) / शैलराजस्य (of the king of mountains) / सुते (two daughters) / लोकनमस्कृते (honored by the world) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / च (and) / सरितां (of rivers) / श्रेष्ठा (the foremost) / उमादेवी (Uma Devi) / च (and) / राघव (O Raghava)
ramayan::989.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::989.essence: Two revered daughters share one mountain-born source.
ramayan::989.simple_meaning: Ganga and Uma are both daughters of Himavan, and both are revered by everyone.
ramayan::989.simple_insight: Greatness can be born in more than one form from the same source.
ramayan::989.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is explaining the lineage of sacred figures to Rama. After mentioning Uma, he adds Ganga as another daughter of Himavan, emphasizing that both are honored by the world. The verse is part of a continuing explanation, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::989.modern_relevance: Someone tells you a family story and names two siblings who each became remarkable in different ways. The point is not comparison, but recognition: one source can give rise to more than one kind of greatness.
ramayan::989.insight: It shifts attention from a single sacred figure to the wider sacred family and shared origin behind them.

ramayan::990.verse_sanskrit: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथा त्रिपथगा नदी । खं गता प्रथमं तात गतिं गतिमतां वर । । 13523 । ।
ramayan::990.verse_hindi: O child with a marvellous gait I have related to you about Ganga flowing across the three worlds, Ganga who reached the heaven first and all that.
ramayan::990.english_translation: O child with a marvellous gait, I have told you everything about the river that flows across the three worlds, the river that first reached the sky, best of those who move.
ramayan::990.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / ते (to you) / सर्वम् (everything) / आख्यातम् (has been told) / यथा (how) / त्रिपथगा (flowing through three paths / the three worlds) / नदी (river) / खम् (sky) / गता (gone) / प्रथमम् (first) / तात (dear one) / गतिमताम् (of those who move) / वर (best)
ramayan::990.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::990.essence: The account is complete, but the river’s full journey still unfolds.
ramayan::990.simple_meaning: Valmiki finishes explaining Ganga’s journey across the three worlds, saying he has told Rama all of it, including how she first reached the sky.
ramayan::990.simple_insight: Some stories are complete because they have been fully traced, not because they are simple.
ramayan::990.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is still explaining Ganga’s descent and path to Rama, continuing the sacred geography from the previous verses. This line is a bridge, not the climax: it closes the explanation before the next verse describes Ganga’s heavenly rise.
ramayan::990.modern_relevance: You’ve heard the whole backstory, but the meaning still isn’t finished. Some things only become clear when every step of the path is named.
ramayan::990.insight: It marks a transition from explanation to completion, preparing the listener for the next detail.

ramayan::991.verse_sanskrit: सैषा सुरनदी रम्या शैलेन्द्रस्य सुता तदा । सुरलोकं समारूढा विपापा जलवाहिनी । । 13524 । ।
ramayan::991.verse_hindi: The divine Ganga, daughter of Himavan, beautiful and sinless, carrying a large volume of water ascended the heavens.
ramayan::991.english_translation: The divine Ganga, daughter of Himavan, beautiful and sinless, carrying a large volume of water ascended the heavens.
ramayan::991.translation_literal: सा एषा (this indeed) / सुरनदी (the river of the radiant beings) / रम्या (beautiful) / शैलेन्द्रस्य (of the king of mountains) / सुता (daughter) / तदा (then) / सुरलोकम् (to the world of the radiant beings) / समारूढा (ascended) / विपापा (sinless) / जलवाहिनी (water-bearer, river)
ramayan::991.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::991.essence: Ganga is not just a river; she is a living lineage of purity and ascent.
ramayan::991.simple_meaning: Ganga is described as the beautiful, sinless daughter of the mountain king who rose up to the heavenly world.
ramayan::991.simple_insight: A sacred place can be understood as a living presence, not just a location.
ramayan::991.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is explaining Ganga’s origin to Rama and Lakshmana. He describes her as the lovely, pure daughter of Himavan who rose to the heavenly realm, continuing the sacred genealogy of the river before the story moves onward.
ramayan::991.modern_relevance: A river you crossed as a child can become part of your family story, your memory, your identity. Some places are not scenery; they are lineage.
ramayan::991.insight: It shifts attention from geography to sacred origin and continuity.

ramayan::992.verse_sanskrit: उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन्नुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ । प्रतिनन्द्य कथां वीरावूचतुर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् । । 1361 । ।
ramayan::992.verse_hindi: While Viswamitra preeminent ascetic among the sages was telling the story (of Ganga) to the heroic Rama and Lakshmana, they extolled it and enquired:
ramayan::992.english_translation: While the sage Vishwamitra was telling the story of Ganga, the heroic Rama and Lakshmana praised it and then spoke to the best of sages.
ramayan::992.translation_literal: उक्तवाक्ये (while the speech was being spoken) / मुनौ (by the sage) / तस्मिन् (in that) / उभौ (both) / राघवलक्ष्मणौ (Rama and Lakshmana) / प्रतिनन्द्य (having praised) / कथाम् (the story) / वीरौ (the heroic ones) / ऊचतुḥ (spoke) / मुनिपुङ्गवम् (to the best of sages)
ramayan::992.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::992.essence: They honor the story first, then invite it to go deeper.
ramayan::992.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana listen to Vishwamitra's story, praise it, and ask him to continue.
ramayan::992.simple_insight: Respectful listening is part of wisdom too.
ramayan::992.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra is narrating the story of Ganga to Rama and Lakshmana. The two princes respond with praise and a question, showing their humility and eagerness before the sage. The verse mainly moves the conversation forward.
ramayan::992.modern_relevance: You hear someone explain something beautiful, and instead of rushing past it, you pause, appreciate it, and ask for more.
ramayan::992.insight: It models attentive listening before asking deeper questions.

ramayan::993.verse_sanskrit: धर्मयुक्तमिदं ब्रह्मन् कथितं परमं त्वया । दुहितुश्शैलराजस्य ज्येष्ठाया वक्तुमर्हसि । । 1362 । । विस्तरं विस्तरज्ञोऽसि दिव्यमानुषसम्भवम् ।
ramayan::993.verse_hindi: O Brahman sage, this excellent story set in righteousness has been narrated by you.
ramayan::993.english_translation: O Brahman sage, this excellent story set in righteousness has been narrated by you.
ramayan::993.translation_literal: धर्मयुक्तम् (set in righteousness) / इदम् (this) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahman sage) / कथितम् (narrated) / परमम् (excellent, supreme) / त्वया (by you) / दुहितुः (of the daughter) / शैलराजस्य (of the mountain king) / ज्येष्ठायाः (of the elder) / वक्तुम् (to speak) / अर्हसि (you are worthy) / विस्तरम् (in विस्तार, in detail) / विस्तरज्ञः (knower of detail) / असि (you are) / दिव्यमानुषसम्भवम् (the divine-human origin)
ramayan::993.speaker: Rama
ramayan::993.essence: Respectful inquiry opens the next layer of truth.
ramayan::993.simple_meaning: Rama praises Vishwamitra’s account of Ganga’s sacred origin and asks him to explain the elder daughter of the mountain king in more detail.
ramayan::993.simple_insight: Curiosity can be reverent. Asking for more is not doubt; it is respect.
ramayan::993.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has begun recounting Ganga’s descent and divine origin to Rama and Lakshmana. Rama listens with attention, praises the account, and asks for the fuller story of the elder daughter of the mountain king. The scene turns from narration to inquiry.
ramayan::993.modern_relevance: You hear part of a story that matters, and you don’t rush past it. You ask for the fuller truth because careful listening is its own kind of respect.
ramayan::993.insight: It teaches you to stay curious when something important is only partly revealed.

ramayan::994.verse_sanskrit: त्रीन् पथो हेतुना केन प्लावयेल्लोकपावनी । । 1363 । । कथं गङ्गा त्रिपथगा विश्रुता सरिदुत्तमा । त्रिषु लोकेषु धर्मज्ञ कर्मभि: कैस्समन्विता । । 1364 । ।
ramayan::994.verse_hindi: Why does Ganga, the purifier of the worlds overflow the three paths (worlds)? O knower of dharma what deed made, Tripathaga (flowing in three directions) Ganga wellknown in the three worlds as the best (holiest) of all rivers?
ramayan::994.english_translation: Why does Ganga, the purifier of the worlds, flow along the three paths? O knower of dharma, by what deed did the best of rivers become famed as Tripathaga in the three worlds?
ramayan::994.translation_literal: त्रीन् (three) / पथो (paths) / हेतुना (by cause) / केन (by what) / प्लावयेत् (would overflow / flow through) / लोकपावनी (world-purifying) / कथं (how) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / त्रिपथगा (flowing in three paths) / विश्रुता (renowned) / सरिदुत्तमा (best of rivers) / त्रिषु (in three) / लोकेषु (worlds) / धर्मज्ञ (knower of dharma) / कर्मभिः (by deeds) / कैः (by what) / समन्विता (endowed with)
ramayan::994.speaker: Rama
ramayan::994.essence: True understanding begins when you ask what caused the wonder.
ramayan::994.simple_meaning: Rama asks how Ganga came to flow through three realms and what deed made her famous as the greatest river.
ramayan::994.simple_insight: Curiosity can open the door to deeper meaning instead of settling for surface awe.
ramayan::994.detailed_meaning: Rama, still listening to Vishwamitra, hears the story of Ganga and interrupts with a question. He wants not just the tale, but the reason behind Ganga’s extraordinary fame and threefold course.
ramayan::994.modern_relevance: You hear a story everyone else accepts and still ask, ‘Why did this happen?’ That question can uncover the real meaning hiding under the legend.
ramayan::994.insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to active inquiry.

ramayan::995.verse_sanskrit: तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे विश्वामित्रस्तपोधन: । निखिलेन कथां सर्वामृषिमध्ये न्यवेदयत् । । 1365 । ।
ramayan::995.verse_hindi: Having heard the words of the son of the Kakusthas, Viswamitra, vested with the wealth of asceticism, revealed the complete story in detail in the presence of the sages.
ramayan::995.english_translation: Having heard the words of the son of the Kakusthas, Viswamitra, vested with the wealth of asceticism, revealed the complete story in detail in the presence of the sages.
ramayan::995.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / ब्रुवति (speaking) / काकुत्स्थे (to the Kakutstha) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / तपोधनः (one rich in ascetic power) / निखिलेन (completely) / कथाम् (story) / सर्वाम् (entire) / ऋषिमध्ये (among the sages) / न्यवेदयत् (revealed)
ramayan::995.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::995.essence: A single question draws out the whole story.
ramayan::995.simple_meaning: Viswamitra then told the full story clearly to the gathered sages after hearing Rama's question.
ramayan::995.simple_insight: A question opened the way for a fuller truth.
ramayan::995.detailed_meaning: In the assembly of sages, Rama's question prompts Viswamitra to continue. He does not answer briefly; he unfolds the entire account in detail, setting up the sacred story that follows.
ramayan::995.modern_relevance: You ask one honest question in a room, and suddenly the whole hidden story starts coming out.
ramayan::995.insight: It shifts the moment from inquiry to narration, showing that a sincere question can unlock a deeper teaching.

ramayan::996.verse_sanskrit: पुरा राम कृतोद्वाहो नीलकण्ठो महातपा: । दृष्ट्वा च स्पृहया देवीं मैथुनायोपचक्रमे । । 1366 । ।
ramayan::996.verse_hindi: O Rama, in ancient times, great ascetic the blueneck Lord Siva got married to goddess Uma charmed with her beauty he indulged in sexual enjoyment with intense
ramayan::996.english_translation: O Rama, in ancient times, the great ascetic, the blue-throated Lord Shiva, saw Uma and, drawn by desire, entered into union with her.
ramayan::996.translation_literal: पुरा (in ancient times) / राम (O Rama) / कृतोद्वाहः (having been married) / नीलकण्ठः (blue-throated one) / महातपाः (great ascetic) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / स्पृहया (with desire) / देवीं (the goddess) / मैथुनाय (for union) / उपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::996.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::996.essence: Desire can arise even in the most disciplined life.
ramayan::996.simple_meaning: Shiva, after marrying Uma, was overcome by desire and turned toward union with her.
ramayan::996.simple_insight: Even a great ascetic can be moved by desire.
ramayan::996.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is explaining the origin of Ganga’s descent through the three worlds. He reaches back to Shiva and Uma’s union, showing how a divine marriage led into a larger cosmic event. This line is a supporting detail in that explanation, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::996.modern_relevance: A person who has built a disciplined life can still be pulled sideways by attraction. Strength does not erase human longing; it only makes the pull more visible.
ramayan::996.insight: It reminds you that restraint is a practice, not a permanent state.

ramayan::997.verse_sanskrit: शितिकण्ठस्य देवस्य दिव्यं वर्षशतं गतम् । न चापि तनयो राम तस्यामासीत् परन्तप । । 1367 । ।
ramayan::997.verse_hindi: O Rama, tormentor of enemies, while Lord Siva was thus absorbed in sexual enjoyment, a hundred (celestial) years passed but no son was born to them.
ramayan::997.english_translation: O Rama, tormentor of enemies, a hundred divine years passed for the Lord with the blue throat, and no son was born.
ramayan::997.translation_literal: शितिकण्ठस्य (of the blue-throated one) / देवस्य (of the radiant lord) / दिव्यम् (divine) / वर्षशतम् (hundred years) / गतम् (passed) / न (not) / च (and) / अपि (also) / तनयः (son) / राम (Rama) / तस्याम् (in that) / आसीत् (was) / परन्तप (tormentor of enemies)
ramayan::997.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::997.essence: Even divine union can remain fruitless for a long time.
ramayan::997.simple_meaning: A hundred divine years passed, but Shiva and Uma still had no son.
ramayan::997.simple_insight: Some events take immense time, and even that may not bring the result you expect.
ramayan::997.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is explaining Shiva and Uma's marriage to Rama. After their union, a vast stretch of divine time passes, yet no child is born. The delay matters because the next verse turns this into a cosmic concern for the gods.
ramayan::997.modern_relevance: You can wait through months of effort, hope, and pressure, and still see nothing happen. The silence itself can become the burden.
ramayan::997.insight: It shifts attention from immediate expectation to the weight of delayed consequence.

ramayan::998.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवास्समुद्विग्ना: पितामहपुरोगमा: । यदिहोत्पद्यते भूतं कस्तत्प्रतिसहिष्यते । । 1368 । ।
ramayan::998.verse_hindi: Then the devatas led by Brahma were exceedingly alarmed. Who will be able to bear the power of the offspring if it is born here and now, they reflected.
ramayan::998.english_translation: Then the devas, led by Brahma, were deeply alarmed: "If such a being is born here, who will be able to withstand him?"
ramayan::998.translation_literal: ततः (then) / देवाः (the devas) / समुद्विग्नाः (greatly alarmed) / पितामह-पुरोगमाः (led by Brahma) / यत् (that) / इह (here) / उत्पद्यते (is born) / भूतम् (a being) / कः (who) / तत् (that) / प्रतिसहिष्यते (will be able to withstand)
ramayan::998.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::998.essence: Power can frighten even those who understand it first.
ramayan::998.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings panic at the thought of a child being born with overwhelming power. They fear no one will be able to face him.
ramayan::998.simple_insight: Some arrivals are so vast that even the wise feel small before them.
ramayan::998.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the devas have just seen Shiva consumed by desire and the possibility of a child from that union. Alarm spreads among them. The verse captures their fear that such a being, once born, could become unstoppable.
ramayan::998.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone says, "If this goes wrong, who can handle it?" That flash of dread is what the devas feel here — before the crisis has even taken shape.
ramayan::998.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the scale of its consequences.

ramayan::999.verse_sanskrit: अभिगम्य सुरास्सर्वे प्रणिपत्येदमब्रुवन् । देव देव महादेव लोकस्यास्य हिते रत । । 1369 । । सुराणां प्रणिपातेन प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।
ramayan::999.verse_hindi: All devatas approached Siva and paying their obeisance said, O God of the gods engaged in the welfare of all O Mahadeva accept our salutations Be king which you can be (if you will).
ramayan::999.english_translation: All the devas approached Shiva and, bowing down, said: O God of gods, devoted to the welfare of the world, please accept our salutations and grant us your favor.
ramayan::999.translation_literal: अभिगम्य (having approached) / सुराः सर्वे (all the devas) / प्रणिपत्य (bowing down) / इदम् (this) / अब्रुवन् (said) / देव देव (O god of gods) / महादेव (O great god) / लोकस्य अस्य (of this world) / हिते (in the welfare) / रत (delighting) / सुराणाम् (of the devas) / प्रणिपातेन (by prostration) / प्रसादम् (favor) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you are worthy)
ramayan::999.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::999.essence: Humility becomes strength when the welfare of all is on the line.
ramayan::999.simple_meaning: The devas bow to Shiva and ask him to show favor, because they need his help for the world's welfare.
ramayan::999.simple_insight: Even the powerful must bow when the order of the world is at stake.
ramayan::999.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the devas are alarmed by the consequences of Shiva's austerity and the power it may produce. They approach him together, bow low, and ask him to show favor. This verse is part of their plea, not the final answer.
ramayan::999.modern_relevance: A room full of people can sense when a decision is bigger than their pride. In that moment, the wise move is not to posture — it is to ask clearly, humbly, and together.
ramayan::999.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to humble request when the stakes are larger than ego.

ramayan::1000.verse_sanskrit: न लोका धारयिष्यन्ति तव तेजस्सुरोत्तम । । 13610 । । ब्राह्मेण तपसा युक्तो देव्या सह तपश्चर । त्रैलोक्यहितकामार्थं तेजस्तेजसि धारय । । 13611 । ।
ramayan::1000.verse_hindi: O best among the gods, the worlds cannot contain your energy (the son born of your energy) You may engage yourself in penance in the company of Uma in conformity with the Vedas. Retain your energy in your body for the  welfare of the three worlds.
ramayan::1000.english_translation: O best among the gods, the worlds cannot contain your energy. Practise penance with Uma according to the Vedas. Hold your energy within yourself for the welfare of the three worlds.
ramayan::1000.translation_literal: न (not) / लोका (the worlds) / धारयिष्यन्ति (will contain) / तव (your) / तेजः (energy, splendour) / सुरोत्तम (O best among the gods) / ब्राह्मेण (with Vedic) / तपसा (by penance) / युक्तः (joined, engaged) / देव्या (with the goddess) / सह (together) / तपश्चर (practise penance) / त्रैलोक्यहितकामार्थं (for the welfare of the three worlds) / तेजः (energy) / तेजसि (in energy, within yourself) / धारय (hold, retain)
ramayan::1000.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1000.essence: Power becomes blessing only when it is held with restraint.
ramayan::1000.simple_meaning: The worlds cannot bear your power. You are asked to restrain it through penance with Uma, so it can remain for the welfare of all three worlds.
ramayan::1000.simple_insight: Great power is not always meant to be released at once; sometimes it must be held for a larger good.
ramayan::1000.detailed_meaning: The devas, alarmed by the force of Shiva's seed, appeal to him directly. Brahma's words ask Shiva to contain that power through austerity with Uma, so it can serve the welfare of the three worlds instead of overwhelming them.
ramayan::1000.modern_relevance: You feel the urge to pour everything out now — the anger, the talent, the force. But some power serves better when it is held, shaped, and released with care.
ramayan::1000.insight: It shifts you from immediate discharge to disciplined containment for a larger purpose.

ramayan::1001.verse_hindi: Mahadeva, ruler of the all the worlds, having heard the words of devatas, said Be it so Further:
ramayan::1001.english_translation: Mahadeva, ruler of all the worlds, having heard the words of the devas, said, "So be it," and spoke again.
ramayan::1001.translation_literal: देवतानाम् (of the devas) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः (lord of all the worlds) / बाढम् (so be it) / इति (thus) / अब्रवीत् (said) / सर्वान् (to all) / पुनः (again) / च एवम् (and thus) / उवाच (spoke)
ramayan::1001.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1001.essence: He hears the request and gives his consent at once.
ramayan::1001.simple_meaning: Shiva hears the devas’ request and agrees to help.
ramayan::1001.simple_insight: Sometimes the right answer is simple consent to a larger need.
ramayan::1001.detailed_meaning: The devas have approached Shiva and asked him to act for the welfare of the worlds. He hears their plea and immediately agrees, setting up the next step in the cosmic plan.
ramayan::1001.modern_relevance: A team asks you to step in for something bigger than your preference. You listen, recognize the need, and say yes without making it about yourself.
ramayan::1001.insight: It shows the power of responsive leadership: hearing a genuine need and answering without resistance.

ramayan::1002.verse_sanskrit: धारयिष्याम्यहं तेजस्तेजस्येव सहोमया । त्रिदशा: पृथिवी चैव निर्वाणमधिगच्छतु । । 13613 । ।
ramayan::1002.verse_hindi: Together with Uma I will preserve the semen in my body thereby the devatas and also the earth will have peace.
ramayan::1002.english_translation: Together with Uma, I will preserve my energy in myself, so that the gods and the earth may find peace.
ramayan::1002.translation_literal: धारयिष्यामि (I will preserve) / अहम् (I) / तेजः (energy) / तेजस्या (with energy) / एव (indeed) / सह (together with) / उमा (Uma) / इया (with me) / त्रिदशाः (the gods) / पृथिवी (the earth) / च (and) / एव (also) / निर्वाणम् (peace, relief) / अधिगच्छतु (may attain)
ramayan::1002.speaker: Shiva
ramayan::1002.essence: Power becomes sacred when you can contain it for the sake of others.
ramayan::1002.simple_meaning: Shiva agrees to contain his intense energy with Uma, so the gods and the earth can be safe and peaceful.
ramayan::1002.simple_insight: Real strength sometimes means holding back what you could unleash.
ramayan::1002.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked Shiva to restrain his overwhelming power for the sake of the worlds. He accepts, saying he will hold it with Uma so the heavens and the earth are not burned by it.
ramayan::1002.modern_relevance: You feel anger rising in a meeting and know one sharp sentence could change everything. The strongest move may be to hold it in and protect the room.
ramayan::1002.insight: It shifts power from expression to restraint, showing that self-control can serve the wider good.

ramayan::1003.verse_sanskrit: यदिदं क्षुभितं स्थानान्मम तेजो ह्यनुत्तमम् । धारयिष्यति कस्तन्मे ब्रुवन्तु सुरसत्तमा: । । 13614 । ।
ramayan::1003.verse_hindi: Who will contain this exceptional vital fluid of mine if shaken from its own place? O best of devatas tell me.
ramayan::1003.english_translation: Who will contain this exceptional vital force of mine if it is shaken from its place? O best of the radiant beings, tell me.
ramayan::1003.translation_literal: यत् (which) / इदम् (this) / क्षुभितम् (shaken) / स्थानात् (from its place) / मम (my) / तेजः (vital force) / हि (indeed) / अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed) / धारयिष्यति (will contain) / कः (who) / तत् (that) / मे (to me) / ब्रुवन्तु (let them tell) / सुरसत्तमाः (best of the radiant beings)
ramayan::1003.speaker: Shiva
ramayan::1003.essence: Power this great needs a fitting container.
ramayan::1003.simple_meaning: Shiva asks who can hold his unmatched power if it is disturbed and released from its place.
ramayan::1003.simple_insight: Some forces are so immense that even containing them becomes a cosmic task.
ramayan::1003.detailed_meaning: The radiant beings have asked Shiva to keep his energy steady for the welfare of the worlds. He agrees, but then asks who could possibly contain that force if it moves. The question sets up the earth's role in the next verse.
ramayan::1003.modern_relevance: You know that feeling when a huge surge of anger, grief, or drive is barely contained. The verse captures the question beneath every pressure point: what can safely hold this force if it breaks loose?
ramayan::1003.insight: It points attention to containment before release: powerful energy must be held by something equally stable.

ramayan::1004.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तास्सुरास्सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्वृषभध्वजम् । यत्तेज: क्षुभितं ह्येतत्तद्धरा धारयिष्यति । । 13615 । ।
ramayan::1004.verse_hindi: Thus questioned, all the devatas replied to the bearer of the flag with bull as its symbol (Siva), saying, The earth will contain the disturbed vital fluid.
ramayan::1004.english_translation: Thus questioned, all the devas replied to the bearer of the bull-banner, saying, "The earth will contain that disturbed vital fluid."
ramayan::1004.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्ताः (questioned) / सुराः (the devas) / सर्वे (all) / प्रत्यूचुः (replied) / वृषभध्वजम् (to the bull-bannered one) / यत् (that which) / तेजः (vital radiance) / क्षुभितम् (disturbed) / हि (indeed) / एतत् (this) / तद्धरा (the earth will) / धारयिष्यति (contain)
ramayan::1004.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1004.essence: Even divine force needs a ground that can hold it.
ramayan::1004.simple_meaning: The devas answer Shiva that the earth itself will hold the disturbed vital power he is asking about.
ramayan::1004.simple_insight: A great force is not lost; it is redirected into the world that can bear it.
ramayan::1004.detailed_meaning: The devas have been asked who can contain Shiva's overflowing energy. They answer that the earth will receive it. This is a mythic setup verse, preparing for the release of that power onto the ground below.
ramayan::1004.modern_relevance: A conversation ends with the only practical answer left: put the pressure somewhere solid enough to hold it. Not every force can stay contained; some must be grounded.
ramayan::1004.insight: It frames overwhelming energy as something that must be given a vessel, not suppressed.

ramayan::1005.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्सुरपति: प्रमुमोच महीतले । तेजसा पृथिवी येन व्याप्ता सगिरिकानना । । 13616 । ।
ramayan::1005.verse_hindi: Thus replied by the devatas, the god of the gods released his vital fluid  on earth. It
ramayan::1005.english_translation: Thus replied by the devatas, the god of the gods released his vital fluid on earth. It filled the earth, mountains, and forests with his radiance.
ramayan::1005.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्तः (having been spoken to) / सुरपतिः (lord of the radiant beings) / प्रमुमोच (released) / महीतले (on the surface of the earth) / तेजसा (with radiance) / पृथिवी (the earth) / येन (by which) / व्याप्ता (pervaded) / सगिरिकानना (with mountains and forests)
ramayan::1005.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1005.essence: A single release of power can flood the whole world.
ramayan::1005.simple_meaning: The lord of the radiant beings releases his power onto the earth, and that power spreads everywhere.
ramayan::1005.simple_insight: Some forces are so vast they reshape the whole world around them.
ramayan::1005.detailed_meaning: The radiant beings have asked Shiva to release the power held within him. After their request, he lets that force fall upon the earth, and its brilliance spreads across mountains and forests. This is a mythic transition, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::1005.modern_relevance: A room changes the moment someone with real authority walks in. Their presence alone can alter the mood, the pace, and what everyone else dares to do.
ramayan::1005.insight: It frames power as something that can overflow and transform the whole field around it.

ramayan::1006.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवा: पुनरिदमूचुश्चाथ हुताशनम् । प्रविश त्वं महातेजो रौद्रं वायुसमन्वित: । । 13617 । ।
ramayan::1006.verse_hindi: Then, the devatas said to the firegod, Enter this energy (creative power) related to Rudra followed by the windgod.
ramayan::1006.english_translation: Then the devatas said to the firegod, "Enter that mighty radiance of Rudra, accompanied by Vayu."
ramayan::1006.translation_literal: ततः (then) / देवा: (the devatas) / पुनः (again) / इदम् (this) / ऊचुः (said) / च (and) / अथ (then) / हुताशनम् (to the firegod) / प्रविश (enter) / त्वम् (you) / महातेजः (of great radiance) / रौद्रम् (the Rudra-related) / वायुसमन्वितः (accompanied by Vayu)
ramayan::1006.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1006.essence: Creation begins when separate powers are joined in the right order.
ramayan::1006.simple_meaning: The devatas ask the fire deity to enter Rudra's radiant power, joined by wind, so the divine energy can take form.
ramayan::1006.simple_insight: Some forces must combine before new life can appear.
ramayan::1006.detailed_meaning: The devatas have already released their power onto the earth. Now they turn to Agni and tell him to enter Rudra's blazing energy, with Vayu present too. This is a mythic setup for the birth that follows.
ramayan::1006.modern_relevance: A team has done its part, but the final result still needs the right forces to meet. The breakthrough comes when separate energies are brought together in the right order.
ramayan::1006.insight: It frames creation as coordinated power, not isolated effort.

ramayan::1007.verse_sanskrit: तदग्निना पुनर्व्याप्तं सञ्जातश्श्वेतपर्वत: । दिव्यं शरवणं चैव पावकादित्यसन्निभम् । । 13618 । । यत्र जातो महातेजा: कार्तिकेयोऽग्निसम्भव: ।
ramayan::1007.verse_hindi: That energy pervaded by fire was transformed into the White Mountain. It turned the forest of reeds (Saravana) (blazing) like the fire or the Sun. From that fire was born the glorious Kartikeya.
ramayan::1007.english_translation: That energy pervaded by fire became the White Mountain and the radiant reed-forest. From that fire was born the mighty Kartikeya.
ramayan::1007.translation_literal: तद् (that) / अग्निना (by fire) / पुनर्व्याप्तम् (pervaded again) / सञ्जातः (became born, arose) / श्वेतपर्वतः (White Mountain) / दिव्यम् (divine) / शरवणम् (reed-forest) / च एव (and indeed) / पावकादित्यसन्निभम् (resembling fire and the sun) / यत्र (where) / जातः (was born) / महातेजाः (very radiant, mighty in splendor) / कार्तिकेयः (Kartikeya) / अग्निसम्भवः (fire-born)
ramayan::1007.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1007.essence: Kartikeya’s birth is shown as a blaze of transformed power.
ramayan::1007.simple_meaning: Fire fills the place, the reed-forest becomes radiant, and Kartikeya is born there.
ramayan::1007.simple_insight: Some births are presented as cosmic events, not ordinary beginnings.
ramayan::1007.detailed_meaning: The gods have just acted to create a sacred birth-place. Fire enters the force they invoked, the land becomes the White Mountain and the blazing reed-forest, and Kartikeya appears there as a radiant power born from fire.
ramayan::1007.modern_relevance: A room can feel charged before a life-changing announcement, like everyone sensing something bigger than the moment itself. This verse turns birth into a threshold where the whole atmosphere seems to ignite.
ramayan::1007.insight: It shifts attention from a child’s arrival to the sacred power that makes the arrival possible.

ramayan::1008.verse_sanskrit: अथोमां च शिवं चैव देवास्सर्षिगणास्तदा । पूजयामासुरत्यर्थं सुप्रीतमनसस्तत: । । 13619 । ।
ramayan::1008.verse_hindi: Thereafter highly pleased with the event the devatas along with the saints worshipped Siva and goddess Uma with deep devotion.
ramayan::1008.english_translation: Thereafter, highly pleased with the event, the devas along with the sages worshipped Shiva and Uma with deep devotion.
ramayan::1008.translation_literal: अथो (thereafter) / इमाम् (this) / च (and) / शिवम् (Shiva) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / देवा (the devas) / सर्षिगणाः (along with the groups of sages) / तदा (then) / पूजयामासुः (worshipped) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / सुप्रीतमनसः (with delighted minds) / ततः (thereafter)
ramayan::1008.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1008.essence: Joy after a sacred event becomes worship.
ramayan::1008.simple_meaning: The devas and the sages, filled with joy, offered worship to Shiva and Uma after the event.
ramayan::1008.simple_insight: Shared wonder can become reverence when something sacred has just been revealed.
ramayan::1008.detailed_meaning: After the blazing force has taken form in the forest of reeds, the devas and sages respond with worship. This is not the main teaching of the passage; it is the immediate devotional reaction before Uma speaks and turns the moment toward her own anger.
ramayan::1008.modern_relevance: After a long hospital wait, everyone finally exhales when the doctor says the operation succeeded. Relief naturally turns into gratitude before anyone even speaks.
ramayan::1008.insight: It shows how awe can move a group from watching to honoring.

ramayan::1009.verse_sanskrit: अथ शैलसुता राम त्रिदशानिदमब्रवीत् । समन्युरशपत्सर्वान् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचना । । 13620 । ।
ramayan::1009.verse_hindi: Rama thereafter Uma, daughter of the mountain (Himavan) with her eyes red with anger cursed all of them:
ramayan::1009.english_translation: Then the mountain-born Uma, her eyes red with anger, spoke to the gods and cursed them all.
ramayan::1009.translation_literal: अथ (then) / शैलसुता (the mountain-born daughter) / राम (Rama) / त्रिदशान् (the gods) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said) / समन्युः (angry) / अशपत् (cursed) / सर्वान् (all) / क्रोध-संरक्त-लोचना (with eyes reddened by anger)
ramayan::1009.speaker: Uma
ramayan::1009.essence: Anger spoken in a sacred moment becomes a curse.
ramayan::1009.simple_meaning: Uma, the daughter of the mountain, became angry and cursed the gods.
ramayan::1009.simple_insight: Some moments of anger become irreversible words.
ramayan::1009.detailed_meaning: After the gods and sages worship Shiva and Uma, the scene turns sharp. Uma, still burning with anger, speaks a curse against the gods. The verse is part of a larger divine origin story, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::1009.modern_relevance: A furious text lands in the group chat before you can stop it. The damage is already moving faster than your regret.
ramayan::1009.insight: It shows how unchecked anger can turn a response into a lasting consequence.

ramayan::1010.verse_sanskrit: यस्मान्निवारिता चैव सङ्गति: पुत्रकाम्यया । अपत्यं स्वेषु दारेषु तस्मान्नोत्पादयिष्यथ । । 13621 । ।
ramayan::1010.verse_hindi: यस्मान्निवारिता चैव सङ्गति: पुत्रकाम्यया । अपत्यं स्वेषु दारेषु तस्मान्नोत्पादयिष्यथ । । 13621 । ।
ramayan::1010.english_translation: Because you were prevented from union by the wish for a son, you will not produce offspring in your own wives.
ramayan::1010.translation_literal: यस्मात् (because) / निवारिता (prevented) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सङ्गति: (union) / पुत्रकाम्यया (by desire for a son) / अपत्यम् (offspring) / स्वेषु (in your own) / दारेषु (in wives) / तस्मात् (therefore) / नोत्पादयिष्यथ (you will not produce)
ramayan::1010.speaker: Uma
ramayan::1010.essence: Trying to control fertility for your own aim brings barrenness back to you.
ramayan::1010.simple_meaning: Uma curses the assembled beings: because they interfered with her union out of desire for a son, they will be denied children in their own marriages.
ramayan::1010.simple_insight: Interference born from desire can return as a wound you never expected.
ramayan::1010.detailed_meaning: After the gods and sages honor Shiva and Uma, Uma turns in anger against them. She condemns the very beings who blocked her union for the sake of a son, and declares that they will lose the fruit of children in their own marriages.
ramayan::1010.modern_relevance: A family makes choices for someone else’s future, convinced they know best. Years later, the cost shows up in their own home. Control can boomerang.
ramayan::1010.insight: It shows how controlling another person's life can rebound into your own loss.

ramayan::1011.verse_sanskrit: अद्यप्रभृति युष्माकमप्रजास्सन्तु पत्नय: । । 13622 । । एवमुक्त्वासुरान् सर्वान् शशाप पृथिवीमपि ।
ramayan::1011.verse_hindi: From today onwards your wives will become childless cursed Uma. The devatas
ramayan::1011.english_translation: From this day onward, your wives will be childless. Having spoken thus, she cursed the asuras and the earth itself.
ramayan::1011.translation_literal: अद्यप्रभृति (from today onward) / युष्माकम् (of you) / अप्रजाः (childless) / सन्तु (let them be) / पत्नयः (wives) / एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / असुरान् (the asuras) / सर्वान् (all) / शशाप (cursed) / पृथिवीम् (the earth) / अपि (also)
ramayan::1011.speaker: Uma
ramayan::1011.essence: Anger rarely stays where it began.
ramayan::1011.simple_meaning: Uma curses the asuras and even the earth, declaring that their wives will no longer bear children.
ramayan::1011.simple_insight: A curse can spread beyond the target and touch the whole world around it.
ramayan::1011.detailed_meaning: Uma, angered by the refusal she faced, turns her fury outward. After cursing the asuras, she also curses the earth itself. This verse is part of a chain of curses, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::1011.modern_relevance: A hurt person lashes out and the damage does not stop at the original wound. The anger spills into families, homes, and everything nearby.
ramayan::1011.insight: It shows how unresolved anger can turn into harm that reaches far beyond the first offense.

ramayan::1012.verse_sanskrit: अवने नैकरूपा त्वं बहुभार्या भविष्यसि । । 13623 । । न च पुत्रकृतां प्रीतिं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता । प्राप्स्यसि त्वं सुदुर्मेधे मम पुत्रमनिच्छती । । 13624 । ।
ramayan::1012.verse_hindi: O Earth you will assume many forms and become wife of many masters. O evilminded one, you did not want me to bear a son. Having been fouled as a result of my anger, you will not have the pleasure of having  a son, cursed Uma.
ramayan::1012.english_translation: O Earth, you will take many forms and become the wife of many masters. O foolish one, because you did not want me to have a son, you will not enjoy the joy of bearing one, made impure by my anger.
ramayan::1012.translation_literal: अवने (O Earth) / नैकरूपा (of many forms) / त्वं (you) / बहुभार्या (having many husbands) / भविष्यसि (will become) / न च (and not) / पुत्रकृतां (caused by a son) / प्रीतिं (joy) / मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता (made impure by my anger) / प्राप्स्यसि (you will obtain) / त्वं (you) / सुदुर्मेधे (O very foolish one) / मम (my) / पुत्रम् (son) / अनिच्छती (not wanting)
ramayan::1012.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1012.essence: Anger here becomes a curse that reshapes an entire future.
ramayan::1012.simple_meaning: A curse is being spoken against Earth: she will take many forms and have many husbands, but she will not get the joy of bearing a son because she opposed the speaker.
ramayan::1012.simple_insight: Some words carry the force of irreversible loss, not just anger.
ramayan::1012.detailed_meaning: A divine curse is unfolding after the gods are humiliated. Earth is singled out and condemned for not wanting the speaker's son. The verse is one line in that larger curse, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::1012.modern_relevance: A heated argument can spill into words that outlive the moment. What you say in anger can become the part everyone remembers.
ramayan::1012.insight: It shows how anger turns speech into punishment, not dialogue.

ramayan::1013.verse_sanskrit: तान् सर्वान् व्रीडितान् दृष्ट्वा सुरान्सुरपतिस्तदा । गमनायोपचक्राम दिशं वरुणपालिताम् । । 13625 । ।
ramayan::1013.verse_hindi: The god of the gods (Mahesvara), seeing all the devatas humiliated began to depart in the westerly direction presided over by Varuna.
ramayan::1013.english_translation: Seeing all the devas humiliated, the lord of the gods then set out toward the western direction ruled by Varuna.
ramayan::1013.translation_literal: तान् (those) / सर्वान् (all) / व्रीडितान् (humiliated) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / सुरान् (the devas) / सुरपतिः (lord of the devas) / तदा (then) / गमनाय (for departure) / उपचक्राम (began) / दिशम् (direction) / वरुणपालिताम् (ruled by Varuna)
ramayan::1013.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1013.essence: Humiliation ends one scene and sends the next one into motion.
ramayan::1013.simple_meaning: After seeing the devas shamed, Maheshvara turned to leave toward the west.
ramayan::1013.simple_insight: A humiliation can end a confrontation, but it can also set a larger turning in motion.
ramayan::1013.detailed_meaning: The devas have just been cursed and shamed. Maheshvara sees their disgrace and turns away, heading west under Varuna's direction. The verse is a transition, not the teaching itself; it moves the scene toward his next act of penance.
ramayan::1013.modern_relevance: You watch a room go quiet after the wrong person has been exposed. The moment is not the argument anymore — it is the decision to step away and do what comes next.
ramayan::1013.insight: It shifts attention from the insult itself to the response that follows it.

ramayan::1014.verse_sanskrit: स गत्वा तप आतिष्ठत्पार्श्वे तस्योत्तरे गिरौ । हिमवत्प्रभवे शृङ्गे सह देव्या महेश्वर: । । 13626 । ।
ramayan::1014.verse_hindi: Mahesvara along with goddess Uma, went north of the Himavat mountain and performed penance on a peak.
ramayan::1014.english_translation: Mahesvara, along with goddess Uma, went north of Mount Himavat and performed penance on a peak.
ramayan::1014.translation_literal: स (he) / गत्वा (having gone) / तपः (austerity) / आतिष्ठत् (undertook) / पार्श्वे (on the side) / तस्य (of that) / उत्तर (north) / गिरौ (on the mountain) / हिमवत्प्रभवे (born of Himavat) / शृङ्गे (on the peak) / सह (together with) / देव्या (with the goddess) / महेश्वरः (Mahesvara)
ramayan::1014.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1014.essence: Power here is shown by choosing austerity, not display.
ramayan::1014.simple_meaning: Mahesvara and Uma withdrew to a mountain peak and practiced austerity together.
ramayan::1014.simple_insight: Even the mighty turn inward when the moment demands it.
ramayan::1014.detailed_meaning: After the devas are humiliated, Mahesvara leaves and goes with Uma to a peak north of Himavat. The verse is a scene-setting detail in the larger story of Parvati’s origin and the mountain’s sacred power, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::1014.modern_relevance: A life can look settled from the outside while, inside, you are quietly climbing toward a harder, truer discipline.
ramayan::1014.insight: It shifts attention from outer status to inward discipline and sacred withdrawal.

ramayan::1015.verse_sanskrit: एष ते विस्तरो राम शैलपुत्र्या निवेदित: । गङ्गाया: प्रभवं चैव शृणु मे सहलक्ष्मण: । । 13627 । ।
ramayan::1015.verse_hindi: O Rama this story of the daughter of the mountain has been narrated to you. Now listen with Lakshmana the tale of the birth of Ganga:
ramayan::1015.english_translation: O Rama, this account of the daughter of the mountain has been told to you. Now listen with Lakshmana to the origin of Ganga.
ramayan::1015.translation_literal: एष (this) / ते (to you) / विस्तरः (account) / राम (O Rama) / शैलपुत्र्या (of the daughter of the mountain) / निवेदितः (has been told) / गङ्गायाः (of Ganga) / प्रभवम् (origin) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / शृणु (listen) / मे (to me) / सहलक्ष्मणः (with Lakshmana)
ramayan::1015.speaker: Maheshvara
ramayan::1015.essence: The present story is only a doorway to a deeper origin.
ramayan::1015.simple_meaning: Rama has heard the story so far, and now he is being asked to listen to the origin of Ganga along with Lakshmana.
ramayan::1015.simple_insight: Some teachings open by pointing back before they go forward.
ramayan::1015.detailed_meaning: Maheshvara has withdrawn to the northern peak with Uma after seeing the devas humiliated. From there, he tells Rama that the story of the mountain-born one has been explained, and now the account will move to Ganga's origin. The verse acts as a bridge in the larger telling.
ramayan::1015.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a story and realize the real explanation still lies ahead. Some moments only make sense when you hear what came before them.
ramayan::1015.insight: It shifts attention from the immediate event to the larger chain of causes behind it.

ramayan::1016.verse_sanskrit: तप्यमाने तपो देवे देवा: सर्षिगणा: पुरा । सेनापतिमभीप्सन्त: पितामहमुपागमन् । । 1371 । ।
ramayan::1016.verse_hindi: In olden days when Iswara was engaged in austerities, the devatas together with the ascetics, approached Lord Brahma for an army general.
ramayan::1016.english_translation: In ancient times, when the divine was engaged in austerities, the devas together with the sages approached Brahma, seeking a commander for their armies.
ramayan::1016.translation_literal: तप्यमाने (while engaged in austerities) / तपो देवे (the divine in austerities) / देवा: (the devas) / सर्षिगणा: (together with the groups of sages) / पुरा (long ago) / सेनापतिम् (a commander of armies) / अभीप्सन्त: (desiring) / पितामहम् (to the grandsire Brahma) / उपागमन् (approached)
ramayan::1016.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1016.essence: When power withdraws, the world looks for a new guide.
ramayan::1016.simple_meaning: The devas and sages went to Brahma because they wanted a commander for their forces while Shiva was in austerities.
ramayan::1016.simple_insight: Big cosmic events still begin with a clear request for help.
ramayan::1016.detailed_meaning: The story has moved into a divine crisis: Shiva is absorbed in austerity, and the celestial order needs leadership. So the devas and sages go to Brahma to ask for a commander. This verse is a setup, not the full turning point.
ramayan::1016.modern_relevance: A team is stuck because its strongest person has gone unavailable, and everyone is waiting for direction. The first move is not panic — it is to ask clearly for the help the moment requires.
ramayan::1016.insight: It shifts attention from the problem itself to the need for right leadership.

ramayan::1017.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽब्रुवन् सुरास्सर्वे भगवन्तं पितामहम् । प्रणिपत्य सुरास्सर्वे सेन्द्रास्साग्निपुरोगमा: । । 1372 । ।
ramayan::1017.verse_hindi: Then led by Indra and the Firegod all devatas approached Lord Brahma, the grandsire saluted him (with folded hands) and spoke.
ramayan::1017.english_translation: Then all the devatas, led by Indra and Agni, approached Lord Brahma, bowed to him with folded hands, and spoke.
ramayan::1017.translation_literal: ततः (then) / अब्रुवन् (spoke) / सुराः (the devatas) / सर्वे (all) / भगवन्तम् (the venerable one) / पितामहम् (Brahma, the grandsire) / प्रणिपत्य (having bowed down) / सुराः (the devatas) / सर्वे (all) / स-इन्द्राः (led by Indra) / स-अग्नि-पुरोगमाः (with Agni at their head)
ramayan::1017.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1017.essence: Real help begins when pride steps aside.
ramayan::1017.simple_meaning: The devatas, with Indra and Agni leading them, bowed to Brahma and began to speak.
ramayan::1017.simple_insight: Respect opens the way before any request can be made.
ramayan::1017.detailed_meaning: The heavenly beings are in crisis and need Brahma's help. They come together, led by Indra and Agni, and bow before the grandsire. This verse is the formal opening of their plea, not the plea itself.
ramayan::1017.modern_relevance: You walk into a hard conversation knowing you need help, not control. The first move is humility, not argument.
ramayan::1017.insight: It shows that serious requests begin with deference and shared purpose.

ramayan::1018.verse_sanskrit: यो न स्सेनापतिर्देव दत्तो भगवता पुरा । तप: परममास्थाय तप्यते स्म सहोमया । । 1373 । ।
ramayan::1018.verse_hindi: O Lord in ancient times your lordship gave us an army general (at the time of
ramayan::1018.english_translation: O Lord, in ancient times your lordship gave us a commander-in-chief, who, after undertaking the highest austerity, still torments himself along with me.
ramayan::1018.translation_literal: य: (who) / न: (our) / सेनापति: (commander-in-chief) / देवदत्त: (given by the divine) / भगवता (by the Lord) / पुरा (long ago) / तप: (austerity) / परमम् (highest) / आस्थाय (having undertaken) / तप्यते स्म (was practicing austerity / was tormenting himself) / सहोमया (together with me)
ramayan::1018.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1018.essence: A promised leader is still lost in austerity, and the devas remain unprotected.
ramayan::1018.simple_meaning: The devas tell Brahma that the commander once given to them is still doing severe austerity with them.
ramayan::1018.simple_insight: Even a granted support can remain withdrawn, leaving a group still struggling for help.
ramayan::1018.detailed_meaning: The devas, led by Indra and Agni, have approached Brahma with folded hands. They remind him that the commander they once received is still absorbed in severe austerity, and they are still without the leadership they need. This verse is a supporting plea in their request.
ramayan::1018.modern_relevance: You were promised help, but the person meant to lead is still unavailable. The group keeps waiting, carrying the strain longer than anyone expected.
ramayan::1018.insight: It frames the problem as unfinished support, not a new request.

ramayan::1019.verse_sanskrit: यदत्रानन्तरं कार्यं लोकानां हितकाम्यया । संविधत्स्व विधानज्ञ त्वं हि न: परमा गति: । । 1374 । ।
ramayan::1019.verse_hindi: O Knower of law and order O Grandsire verily you are our supreme refuge committed to the welfare of the worlds. Tell us what we should do in this matter (now that we cannot procreate a general on account of Umas curse).
ramayan::1019.english_translation: O Knower of law and order, O Grandsire, verily you are our supreme refuge, committed to the welfare of the worlds. Tell us what we should do in this matter now that we cannot produce a general because of Uma's curse.
ramayan::1019.translation_literal: यत् (what) / अत्र (here) / अनन्तरम् (next) / कार्यम् (to be done) / लोकानाम् (of the worlds) / हितकाम्यया (with desire for welfare) / संविधत्स्व (arrange) / विधानज्ञ (knower of law and order) / त्वम् (you) / हि (indeed) / नः (our) / परमा (supreme) / गति: (refuge)
ramayan::1019.speaker: Devas
ramayan::1019.essence: When the problem is bigger than you, wisdom becomes the next action.
ramayan::1019.simple_meaning: The devas ask Brahma to decide the next course of action for the good of the worlds, because they cannot solve the problem themselves.
ramayan::1019.simple_insight: Even powerful people need guidance when the situation is bigger than them.
ramayan::1019.detailed_meaning: The devas have already bowed to Brahma and explained their crisis: a curse has blocked the birth of a war leader. Now they ask him to act for the welfare of all worlds and tell them the right next move.
ramayan::1019.modern_relevance: Your team hits a problem no one can solve, and everyone looks to the one person who sees the whole board. This verse is that moment: stop improvising and ask for the next right step.
ramayan::1019.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to asking for clear direction.

ramayan::1020.verse_hindi: Hearing the words of the devatas, Brahma, the Grandsire of all the worlds consoled the devatas with sweet words, saying:
ramayan::1020.english_translation: Hearing the words of the devas, Brahma, the Grandsire of all the worlds, consoled the devas with sweet words, saying:
ramayan::1020.translation_literal: देवतानां (of the devas) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सर्वलोकपितामहः (the Grandsire of all the worlds) / सान्त्वयन् (consoling) / मधुरैः (with sweet) / वाक्यैः (words) / त्रिदशान् (the devas) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1020.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1020.essence: Clear guidance often begins with words that steady fear.
ramayan::1020.simple_meaning: Brahma listens to the devas and reassures them before answering their request.
ramayan::1020.simple_insight: Sometimes the first gift is not a solution, but calm words that steady everyone.
ramayan::1020.detailed_meaning: The devas have approached Brahma with a crisis. After hearing them, the Grandsire does not dismiss their fear; he soothes them with gentle speech before revealing the next step. This verse is the bridge into the divine response.
ramayan::1020.modern_relevance: A team comes to you panicked after a bad meeting. Before solving anything, you lower the temperature in the room so people can think again.
ramayan::1020.insight: It shows that wise leadership begins by calming fear before giving direction.

ramayan::1021.verse_sanskrit: शैल पुत्र्या यदुक्तं तन्न प्रजास्यथ पत्निषु । तस्या वचनमक्लिष्टं सत्यमेतन्न संशय: । । 1376 । ।
ramayan::1021.verse_hindi: शैल पुत्र्या यदुक्तं तन्न प्रजास्यथ पत्निषु । तस्या वचनमक्लिष्टं सत्यमेतन्न संशय: । । 1376 । ।
ramayan::1021.english_translation: What the daughter of the mountain has said will not happen to his wives. Her word is pure and true; there is no doubt about it.
ramayan::1021.translation_literal: शैल-पुत्र्या (by the daughter of the mountain) / यत् (what) / उक्तम् (was said) / तत् (that) / न (not) / प्रजास्यथ (will happen) / पत्निषु (among wives) / तस्याः (her) / वचनम् (word) / अक्लिष्टम् (unsullied) / सत्यम् (true) / एतत् (this) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::1021.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1021.essence: A true statement ends confusion before the story moves forward.
ramayan::1021.simple_meaning: Brahma confirms that the mountain-born woman's statement is true: the child will not come from the wives of the gods.
ramayan::1021.simple_insight: Some truths are settled before anyone can argue with them.
ramayan::1021.detailed_meaning: The devatas have asked Brahma how the promised destroyer of Ravana will be born. Brahma answers by ruling out one possibility at once: the mountain-born woman's words are true, and the child will not be born through the wives of the gods.
ramayan::1021.modern_relevance: A room full of people is guessing, debating, and second-guessing the plan. Then someone with real sight cuts through the noise and says what is actually settled.
ramayan::1021.insight: It shifts the mind from speculation to recognition of what is already fixed.

ramayan::1022.verse_sanskrit: इयमाकाशगा गङ्गा यस्यां पुत्रं हुताशन: । जनयिष्यति देवानां सेनापतिमरिन्दमम् । । 1377 । ।
ramayan::1022.verse_hindi: Ganga keeps flowing in the celestial regions. Through Ganga the Firegod will beget a son who will be capable of destroying enemies. He will become the army general of the gods.
ramayan::1022.english_translation: This celestial Ganga will bear the son whom Fire will father. He will become the gods' commander and destroy their enemies.
ramayan::1022.translation_literal: इयम् (this) / आकाशगा (flowing in the sky, celestial) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / यस्याम् (in whom) / पुत्रम् (son) / हुताशनः (Fire) / जनयिष्यति (will beget) / देवानाम् (of the gods) / सेनापतिम् (army commander) / अरिन्दमम् (enemy-destroyer)
ramayan::1022.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1022.essence: A great outcome depends on the right meeting of exact conditions.
ramayan::1022.simple_meaning: Brahma says that the celestial Ganga will be the mother of Agni's son, and that son will lead the gods' army against their enemies.
ramayan::1022.simple_insight: Even cosmic plans move through exact conditions, not vague miracles.
ramayan::1022.detailed_meaning: Brahma is explaining the divine arrangement behind a future birth: the celestial Ganga will carry the son of Agni, and that child will become the gods' commander. This is one step in a larger plan, not the full point of the passage.
ramayan::1022.modern_relevance: A team is waiting on one final approval, one missing signature, one person saying yes. What looks like delay is often a chain of exact conditions falling into place.
ramayan::1022.insight: It shifts attention from random events to precise causes and coordinated outcomes.

ramayan::1023.verse_sanskrit: ज्येष्ठा शैलेन्द्रदुहिता मानयिष्यति तत्सुतम् । उमायास्तद्बहुमतं भविष्यति न संशय: । । 1378 । ।
ramayan::1023.verse_hindi: Ganga, the eldest daughter of the king of the mountains, will tend that son of Agni. This will be totally acceptable to Uma. No doubt.
ramayan::1023.english_translation: Ganga, the eldest daughter of the king of the mountains, will tend that son of Agni. This will be totally acceptable to Uma. No doubt.
ramayan::1023.translation_literal: ज्येष्ठा (eldest) / शैलेन्द्रदुहिता (daughter of the king of mountains) / मानयिष्यति (will tend / will honour) / तत्सुतम् (that son) / उमायाः (to Uma's) / तद् (that) / बहुमतं (greatly acceptable) / भविष्यति (will become) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::1023.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1023.essence: Great change begins only when every force is in accord.
ramayan::1023.simple_meaning: Ganga will care for the son born from Agni, and Uma will fully approve of it. The arrangement is certain.
ramayan::1023.simple_insight: Even the highest powers must align before great things can begin.
ramayan::1023.detailed_meaning: The devas have asked Brahma for help against Ravana. Brahma is explaining the conditions for a future divine birth: Ganga will receive and tend the child, and Uma will consent. This verse is one link in the larger plan, not the full teaching itself.
ramayan::1023.modern_relevance: A project finally moves after the right people quietly agree behind the scenes. The visible step is small, but the real breakthrough is that everyone essential is aligned.
ramayan::1023.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the hidden agreement that makes the event possible.

ramayan::1024.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कृतार्था रघुनन्दन । प्रणिपत्य सुरास्सर्वे पितामहमपूजयन् । । 1379 । ।
ramayan::1024.verse_hindi: O son of the Raghus having heard Brahmas words all the devatas considered themselves successful in their mission. They saluted him with folded hands and offered their worship.
ramayan::1024.english_translation: O son of the Raghus, having heard Brahma's words, all the devas felt their mission was accomplished. They bowed with joined hands and worshipped the grandfather.
ramayan::1024.translation_literal: तत् (that) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / वचनं (the words) / तस्य (his) / कृतार्था (having achieved their purpose) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghus) / प्रणिपत्य (having bowed down) / सुराः (the devas) / सर्वे (all) / पितामहम् (the grandfather) / अपूजयन् (worshipped)
ramayan::1024.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1024.essence: Their request is answered, and worship follows relief.
ramayan::1024.simple_meaning: The devas hear Brahma's assurance, feel their purpose is fulfilled, bow to him, and worship him.
ramayan::1024.simple_insight: Relief comes when a burden finally has an answer.
ramayan::1024.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just explained how the devas' plan will unfold through Ganga, Shiva, and the Firegod. Hearing this, the assembled devas know their request has been accepted. They bow to Brahma in gratitude before the next step begins.
ramayan::1024.modern_relevance: You finally get the email that says the plan is approved. The tension drops, not because everything is done, but because the hardest part — being heard — is over.
ramayan::1024.insight: It shifts attention from anxious waiting to grateful release once the path is confirmed.

ramayan::1025.verse_sanskrit: ते गत्वा पर्वतं राम कैलासं धातुमण्डितम् । अग्निं नियोजयामासु: पुत्रार्थं सर्वदेवता: । । 13710 । ।
ramayan::1025.verse_hindi: All the devatas, went to mount Kailasa, adorned with minerals, and urged the Firegod for a son.
ramayan::1025.english_translation: All the devatas went to Mount Kailasa, adorned with minerals, and urged the Firegod for a son.
ramayan::1025.translation_literal: ते (they) / गत्वा (having gone) / पर्वतम् (to the mountain) / राम (O Rama) / कैलासम् (Kailasa) / धातुमण्डितम् (adorned with minerals) / अग्निम् (Firegod) / नियोजयामासुः (urged/assigned) / पुत्रार्थम् (for the sake of a son) / सर्वदेवताः (all the devatas)
ramayan::1025.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1025.essence: The devas seek help in layers, because the task exceeds any one power.
ramayan::1025.simple_meaning: The devas went to Mount Kailasa and asked Agni to help bring about the birth of a son.
ramayan::1025.simple_insight: When a task is larger than any one being, even the radiant ones gather and ask for help.
ramayan::1025.detailed_meaning: The devas have already gone to Brahma with their plea. Now they travel to Kailasa and turn to Agni, because the birth they seek will require a chain of divine action. This verse is a supporting step in that larger cosmic request.
ramayan::1025.modern_relevance: A team has done everything it can, and the problem still needs one more person with the right power. Sometimes progress comes from asking the right source, not pushing harder.
ramayan::1025.insight: It shows that even urgent cosmic needs move through cooperation, not force.

ramayan::1026.verse_sanskrit: देवकार्यमिदं देव संविधत्स्व हुताशन । शैलपुत्र्यां महातेजो गङ्गायां तेज उत्सृज । । 13711 । ।
ramayan::1026.verse_hindi: O lustrous Firegod, accomplish this divine work. O god, possessed of mighty energy, release the vital fluid of Iswara in Ganga, daughter of the king of mountains.
ramayan::1026.english_translation: O lustrous Firegod, accomplish this divine work. O mighty one, release Shiva's energy into Ganga, the daughter of the mountain.
ramayan::1026.translation_literal: देवकार्यं (divine work) / इदम् (this) / देव (O divine one) / संविधत्स्व (accomplish, arrange) / हुताशन (Firegod) / शैलपुत्र्यां (in the daughter of the mountain) / महातेजः (O mighty-energy one) / गङ्गायाम् (in Ganga) / तेजः (energy, vital power) / उत्सृज (release)
ramayan::1026.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1026.essence: The higher plan still needs exact action to become real.
ramayan::1026.simple_meaning: The devas ask Fire to carry Shiva's power into Ganga so a needed child can be born.
ramayan::1026.simple_insight: Great purposes sometimes require every force to cooperate without hesitation.
ramayan::1026.detailed_meaning: The devas have already won Brahma's approval and now turn to Fire. They ask him to carry Shiva's power into Ganga, daughter of the mountain, so the long-awaited child can be born. This is a cosmic setup, not the climax.
ramayan::1026.modern_relevance: A team finally gets the green light after weeks of planning, and now the real work begins: each person must do their part cleanly, without ego or delay.
ramayan::1026.insight: It shifts attention from wishing for results to arranging the right conditions.

ramayan::1027.verse_sanskrit: देवतानां प्रतिज्ञाय गङ्गामभ्येत्य पावक: । गर्भं धारय वै देवि देवतानामिदं प्रियम् । । 13712 । ।
ramayan::1027.verse_hindi: The Firegod gave his consent. The devatas approached Ganga and said, O goddess bear the energy of Siva (inyour world) since this cause is dear to the gods.
ramayan::1027.english_translation: The Firegod gave his consent. The devas approached Ganga and said, O goddess, bear the energy of Shiva, for this cause is dear to the devas.
ramayan::1027.translation_literal: देवतानाम् (of the devas) / प्रतिज्ञाय (having promised) / गङ्गाम् (to Ganga) / अभ्येत्य (having approached) / पावकः (the Firegod) / गर्भम् (the seed/embryo) / धारय (bear/hold) / वै (indeed) / देवि (O goddess) / देवतानाम् (of the devas) / इदम् (this) / प्रियम् (dear/pleasing)
ramayan::1027.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1027.essence: Even a sacred plan needs the right vessel.
ramayan::1027.simple_meaning: The devas ask Ganga to hold Shiva's energy after the Firegod agrees to their request.
ramayan::1027.simple_insight: Some tasks are so urgent that even the forces of nature are asked to cooperate.
ramayan::1027.detailed_meaning: The devas have gone to Mount Kailasa to secure a son for the greater cosmic purpose. Fire has agreed to carry Shiva's power, and now the devas turn to Ganga, asking her to receive and hold it. The verse is a step in a larger divine arrangement, not the main teaching.
ramayan::1027.modern_relevance: A team has finally agreed to the plan, and now the real logistics begin. The idea is set; what matters next is whether the right people can carry it without breaking it.
ramayan::1027.insight: It shifts attention from the wish itself to the careful coordination needed to make it real.

ramayan::1028.verse_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दिव्यं रूपमधारयत् । दृष्ट्वा तन्महिमानं स समन्तादवकीर्यत । । 13713 । ।
ramayan::1028.verse_hindi: Hearing the words of the Firegod, Ganga assumed a divine form. Beholding her glory, the god of fire pervaded her from all sides.
ramayan::1028.english_translation: Hearing the Firegod's words, Ganga assumed a divine form. Seeing her majesty, the Firegod spread through her from every side.
ramayan::1028.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / तद्वचनं (that word) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / दिव्यं (divine) / रूपम् (form) / अधारयत् (assumed) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तन्महिमानं (that glory) / सः (he) / समन्तात् (from all sides) / अवकीर्यत (was pervaded/spread)
ramayan::1028.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1028.essence: Power enters only when the vessel is ready.
ramayan::1028.simple_meaning: Ganga changes form when asked, and the Firegod fills her completely. The verse continues the sacred transmission of power, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::1028.simple_insight: Some moments are only about carrying something greater than yourself.
ramayan::1028.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked Fire to carry Shiva's energy into Ganga. After hearing the request, Ganga takes on a divine form, and Fire enters her from every side. The scene is still unfolding toward the birth of the child.
ramayan::1028.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after a difficult request is made, and everyone feels the weight of what must happen next. This verse stays inside that moment of transition.
ramayan::1028.insight: It shows a sacred process in motion, where form changes to hold power.

ramayan::1029.verse_sanskrit: समन्ततस्तदा देवीमभ्यषिञ्चत पावक: । सर्वस्रोतांसि पूर्णानि गङ्गाया रघुनन्दन । । 13714 । ।
ramayan::1029.verse_hindi: O Rama then, the Firegod discharged the vital fluid of Iswara, preserved in his body, which pervaded all sides of Ganga and all her streams were filled with (the fluid).
ramayan::1029.english_translation: O Rama, then the Firegod discharged the vital fluid of Iswara, and it filled Ganga and all her streams on every side.
ramayan::1029.translation_literal: समन्ततः (on all sides) / तदा (then) / देवीम् (the goddess) / अभ्यषिञ्चत (bathed / poured over) / पावकः (the Firegod) / सर्वस्रोतांसि (all streams) / पूर्णानि (filled) / गङ्गायाḥ (of Ganga) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line)
ramayan::1029.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1029.essence: Power that enters fully also fills everything around it.
ramayan::1029.simple_meaning: The Firegod’s energy spread through Ganga and filled all her streams.
ramayan::1029.simple_insight: Some moments are too powerful to contain; they overflow into everything around them.
ramayan::1029.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked Ganga to receive Shiva’s force. The Firegod now releases that sacred energy into her, and it spreads through every stream of her body. This is a transitional moment in the divine conception, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1029.modern_relevance: A room can feel charged after a hard conversation, and everyone senses it before anyone speaks. Some events don’t stay in one place; they spread through the whole atmosphere.
ramayan::1029.insight: It shows a force so intense that it cannot remain localized; it saturates the whole vessel.

ramayan::1030.verse_sanskrit: तमुवाच ततो गङ्गा सर्वदेवपुरोहितम् । अशक्ता धारणे देव तव तेज स्समुद्धतम् । दह्यमानाग्निना तेन सम्प्रव्यथितचेतना । । 13715 । ।
