ramayan::1030.verse_hindi: Ganga addressing the Firegod standing ahead of all the devatas said O god of fire, I am incapable of holding your everincreasing splendour. The fiery fluid is burning me. My consciousness is overwhelmed.
ramayan::1030.english_translation: Ganga said to the Firegod, who stands before all the devas: 'O god of fire, I cannot bear your rising brilliance. The fiery seed burns me, and my mind is overwhelmed.'
ramayan::1030.translation_literal: तम् (him) / उवाच (said) / ततः (then) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / सर्वदेवपुरोहितम् (the priest of all devas) / अशक्ता (unable) / धारणे (to bear) / देव (O radiant one) / तव (your) / तेजः (splendour) / समुद्धतम् (rising, intense) / दह्यमानाग्निना (by the burning fire) / तेन (by that) / सम्प्रव्यथितचेतना (with a mind greatly distressed)
ramayan::1030.speaker: Ganga
ramayan::1030.essence: Power needs a vessel that can hold it.
ramayan::1030.simple_meaning: Ganga cannot contain the Firegod's intense energy, so she asks him to place the embryo elsewhere.
ramayan::1030.simple_insight: Even sacred power must be received in the right way and the right place.
ramayan::1030.detailed_meaning: Ganga has just received the divine seed carried by the Firegod. But its heat is too great for her to hold. She speaks in distress, not rejection, and the scene prepares for the transfer of the embryo to a safer place.
ramayan::1030.modern_relevance: You may be carrying something important that is still too intense to hold alone. Even the right thing can overwhelm you before it finds its proper form.
ramayan::1030.insight: It shows that force without fit can become unbearable, even when the purpose is sacred.

ramayan::1031.verse_sanskrit: अथाब्रवीदिदं गङ्गां सर्वदेवहुताशन: । इह हैमवती पादे गर्भोऽयं सन्निवेश्यताम् । । 13716 । ।
ramayan::1031.verse_hindi: Thereafter the Firegod who is the partaker of oblations offered to all deities said to Ganga Place this embryo on this slope of Mountain Himavan.
ramayan::1031.english_translation: Then the Firegod, the one who receives offerings for all the radiant beings, said to Ganga: "Place this embryo on the slope of Mount Himavan."
ramayan::1031.translation_literal: अथ (then) / अब्रवीत् (said) / इदम् (this) / गङ्गाम् (to Ganga) / सर्वदेवहुताशनः (the firegod who receives offerings for all the radiant beings) / इह (here) / हैमवती (of Himavan) / पादे (on the slope) / गर्भः (embryo) / अयम् (this) / सन्निवेश्यताम् (be placed)
ramayan::1031.speaker: Agni
ramayan::1031.essence: What cannot be held must be set where it can grow.
ramayan::1031.simple_meaning: The Firegod tells Ganga to place the embryo on Mount Himavan's slope.
ramayan::1031.simple_insight: Some moments simply carry what is ready to be born.
ramayan::1031.detailed_meaning: Ganga can no longer hold the blazing embryo she has received. The Firegod, who has safeguarded it, now directs her to place it on Mount Himavan. This is a transfer, not a teaching: the child is about to be set down where he can emerge.
ramayan::1031.modern_relevance: You carry something too intense for one container — a secret, a responsibility, a new beginning. At some point, it must be placed where it can take form.
ramayan::1031.insight: It shifts attention from holding to releasing at the right place.

ramayan::1032.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा त्वग्निवचो गङगा तं गर्भमतिभास्वरम् । उत्ससर्ज महातेज स्स्रोतोभ्यो हि तदानघ । । 13717 । ।
ramayan::1032.verse_hindi: O glorious, sinless one, (Rama) hearing the words of the Firegod, Ganga then expelled that resplendent embryo from her streams.
ramayan::1032.english_translation: O glorious, sinless one, hearing the Firegod's words, Ganga then released that radiant embryo from her streams.
ramayan::1032.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तु (then) / अग्निवचः (the words of Firegod) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / तम् (that) / गर्भम् (embryo) / अतिभास्वरम् (very radiant) / उत्ससर्ज (released) / महातेजः (greatly radiant one) / स्रोतोभ्यः (from the streams) / हि (indeed) / तदा (then) / अनघ (sinless one)
ramayan::1032.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1032.essence: What must be carried is not always meant to stay.
ramayan::1032.simple_meaning: After hearing the Firegod, Ganga releases the radiant embryo from her waters.
ramayan::1032.simple_insight: Sometimes release is not loss; it is the right handoff at the right time.
ramayan::1032.detailed_meaning: Ganga cannot hold the blazing embryo any longer. After the Firegod instructs her, she lets it pass from her streams. The next verse will show what that release becomes on earth, so this line serves the unfolding miracle rather than a complete teaching.
ramayan::1032.modern_relevance: You can carry something only until the moment it must move on. Holding it longer is not care; it is resistance.
ramayan::1032.insight: It shifts attention from possession to timely release.

ramayan::1033.verse_sanskrit: यदस्या निर्गतं तस्मात्तप्तजाम्बूनदप्रभम् । काञ्चनं धरणीं प्राप्तं हिरण्यममलं शुभम् । । 13718 । ।
ramayan::1033.verse_hindi: The embryo that emerged from Ganga reached the earth. It resembled the lustre of molten gold. It furned into gold auspicious, bright and pure.
ramayan::1033.english_translation: The embryo that came out of Ganga reached the earth. It shone like molten gold, pure, bright, and auspicious.
ramayan::1033.translation_literal: यत् (which) / अस्याः (of her) / निर्गतम् (came out) / तस्मात् (from that) / तप्त-जाम्बूनद-प्रभम् (having the radiance of molten Jambu gold) / काञ्चनम् (golden) / धरणीम् (the earth) / प्राप्तम् (reached) / हिरण्यम् (gold) / अमलम् (spotless) / शुभम् (auspicious)
ramayan::1033.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1033.essence: What falls to earth still carries its blazing origin.
ramayan::1033.simple_meaning: The embryo that Ganga released touched the earth and appeared like pure, glowing gold.
ramayan::1033.simple_insight: Some moments arrive already radiant, carrying a force beyond ordinary life.
ramayan::1033.detailed_meaning: Ganga has just released the blazing embryo at Firegod's command. This verse describes what happened as it touched the earth: it shone like pure gold. The line is part of a larger origin story, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1033.insight: It completes the scene by showing the embryo's divine radiance as it enters the world.

ramayan::1034.verse_sanskrit: ताम्रं कार्ष्णायसं चैव तैक्ष्ण्यादेवाभ्यजायत । । 13719 । । मलं तस्याभवत्तत्र त्रपु सीसकमेव च । तदेतद्धरणीं प्राप्य नानाधातुरवर्धत । । 13720 । ।
ramayan::1034.verse_hindi: There copper and iron were produced from its acidity, zinc and lead from its residue. Various minerals were formed when that embryo reached the earth.
ramayan::1034.english_translation: Copper and iron arose from its sharpness; its residue became tin and lead. When that embryo reached the earth, many kinds of minerals grew there.
ramayan::1034.translation_literal: ताम्रम् (copper) / कार्ष्णायसम् (iron) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तैक्ष्ण्यात् (from sharpness) / एव (indeed) / अभ्यजायत (arose) / मलम् (residue) / तस्य (of that) / अभवत् (became) / तत्र (there) / त्रपु (tin) / सीसकम् (lead) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / तत् (that) / एतत् (this) / धरणीम् (earth) / प्राप्य (having reached) / नाना (various) / धातुः (metals/minerals) / अवर्धत (grew)
ramayan::1034.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1034.essence: The embryo's touch turns into the earth's hidden metals.
ramayan::1034.simple_meaning: The embryo that fell to earth changed into different metals and minerals. The verse is describing a miraculous transformation, not giving a teaching.
ramayan::1034.simple_insight: Some moments are too strange for explanation; they simply become what they become.
ramayan::1034.detailed_meaning: Ganga has just released the blazing embryo after hearing the Fire-god's words. As it touches the earth, Valmiki describes the physical fallout: copper, iron, tin, lead, and other minerals appear. The scene is still unfolding, so this is supporting detail in a miracle sequence.
ramayan::1034.modern_relevance: A lab sample fails, then changes color, then starts behaving unlike anything the team expected. The moment is not a lesson yet — it is the strange event that forces everyone to stop and look again.
ramayan::1034.insight: It keeps attention on the transformation itself, before any meaning is drawn from it.

ramayan::1035.verse_sanskrit: निक्षिप्तमात्रे गर्भे तु तेजोभिरभिरञ्जितम् । सर्वं पर्वतसन्नद्धं सौवर्णमभवद्वनम् । । 13721 । ।
ramayan::1035.verse_hindi: When the embryo was placed (in Ganga) it spread on all sides of the forest on the mountain. Irradiated with lustre the forest appeared golden.
ramayan::1035.english_translation: When the embryo was placed in Ganga, its radiance spread through the mountain forest, and the whole wood seemed golden.
ramayan::1035.translation_literal: निक्षिप्तमात्रे (when just placed) / गर्भे (in the embryo) / तु (indeed) / तेजोभिः (with radiances) / अभिरञ्जितम् (tinted all around) / सर्वम् (entire) / पर्वतसन्नद्धम् (on the mountain-bound) / सौवर्णम् (golden) / अभवत् (became) / वनम् (forest)
ramayan::1035.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1035.essence: Its radiance turned the whole forest golden.
ramayan::1035.simple_meaning: The embryo’s brilliance filled the forest and made it look golden.
ramayan::1035.simple_insight: Some presences change the whole atmosphere around them.
ramayan::1035.detailed_meaning: The sages are describing the strange, radiant aftermath of the embryo’s descent into Ganga. As the story moves through the earth’s transformation, this verse adds a visual detail: the mountain forest itself seems turned to gold by that power.
ramayan::1035.insight: It shows how intense energy can alter everything around it without a word.

ramayan::1036.verse_sanskrit: जातरूपमिति ख्यातं तदा प्रभृति राघव । सुवर्णं पुरुषव्याघ्र हुताशनसमप्रभम् । । 13722 । । तृणवृक्षलतागुल्मं सर्वं भवति काञ्चनम् ।
ramayan::1036.verse_hindi: O tiger among men, O scion of the Raghus Then onwards gold which is effulgent like fire, became wellknown as Jatarupa (pure form). The grass, shrubs, creepers and trees of that forest looked golden.
ramayan::1036.english_translation: O tiger among men, O scion of the Raghus, from that time onward gold, radiant like fire, came to be known as Jatarupa. The grass, shrubs, creepers, and trees of that forest all turned golden.
ramayan::1036.translation_literal: जातरूपम् (jatarupa, pure gold) / इति (thus) / ख्यातम् (known) / तदा (then) / प्रभृति (from that time onward) / राघव (O Raghava) / सुवर्णम् (gold) / पुरुषव्याघ्र (O tiger among men) / हुताशनसमप्रभम् (radiant like fire) / तृणवृक्षलतागुल्मम् (grass, trees, creepers, shrubs) / सर्वम् (all) / भवति (becomes) / काञ्चनम् (golden)
ramayan::1036.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1036.essence: Radiance can remake everything around it.
ramayan::1036.simple_meaning: The forest around the divine child turned golden, and gold itself was said to have taken its pure form from that radiance.
ramayan::1036.simple_insight: Some presence changes the world around it without effort or announcement.
ramayan::1036.detailed_meaning: The sages are describing the extraordinary birth of Kumara from Ganga. As the child’s radiance spreads, the mountain forest transforms: minerals, plants, and even gold take on a new brilliance. This verse names that wonder and marks the moment the world seems touched by a sacred fire.
ramayan::1036.modern_relevance: A room can feel different the moment someone enters with calm, clarity, and warmth. Nothing is forced, yet everything around them seems brighter and more ordered.
ramayan::1036.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to the transforming power of presence.

ramayan::1037.verse_sanskrit: तं कुमारं ततो जातं सेन्द्रास्सह मरुद्गणा: । । 13723 । । क्षीरसंभावनार्थाय कृत्तिकास्समयोजन् ।
ramayan::1037.verse_hindi: Thereafter Kumara was born (out of Gangas womb). The gods together with Indra arranged six nymphs (stars) to act  as nurses to suckle Kumara as their own offspring.
ramayan::1037.english_translation: Thereafter Kumara was born. The gods, together with Indra, arranged the Krittikas to nurse him.
ramayan::1037.translation_literal: तं (that) / कुमारं (Kumara) / ततः (then) / जातं (born) / सेन्द्राः (with Indra) / सह (together with) / मरुद्गणाः (the host of Maruts) / क्षीरसंभावनार्थाय (for the purpose of nursing with milk) / कृत्तिकाः (the Krittikas) / समयोजन् (arranged)
ramayan::1037.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1037.essence: His birth is so important that even the gods become his nurses.
ramayan::1037.simple_meaning: Kumara is born, and the gods arrange for the Krittika stars to nurse him.
ramayan::1037.simple_insight: A divine child is welcomed with care before he can even speak.
ramayan::1037.detailed_meaning: The scene stays in the cosmic birth of Kumara. After his emergence, Indra and the other gods arrange the Krittikas to feed and raise him, showing how the heavens themselves gather around the child as his caretakers.
ramayan::1037.modern_relevance: A newborn arrives, and every adult in the room quietly rearranges life around that tiny breath. Some arrivals are so important that even power steps back to nurture them.
ramayan::1037.insight: It shifts attention from the birth itself to the responsibility that follows it.

ramayan::1038.verse_sanskrit: ता: क्षीरं जातमात्रस्य कृत्वा समयमुत्तमम् । । 13724 । । ददु: पुत्रोऽयमस्माकं सर्वासामिति निश्चिता: ।
ramayan::1038.verse_hindi: Those krittikas, having decided among themselves and having made an agreement with the gods saying This boy shall become a son to all of us fed the newborn with their milk (breast milk).
ramayan::1038.english_translation: Those Krittikas, having made a firm agreement among themselves, fed the newborn with their milk, saying, 'This boy shall be a son to all of us.'
ramayan::1038.translation_literal: ता: (those) / क्षीरं (milk) / जातमात्रस्य (of the just-born) / कृत्वा (having made) / समयम् (agreement) / उत्तमम् (excellent, firm) / ददु: (gave) / पुत्रोऽयम् (this son) / अस्माकम् (of us) / सर्वासामिति (to all of us, thus) / निश्चिता: (being निश्चित, resolved)
ramayan::1038.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1038.essence: Shared care can create a child’s first belonging.
ramayan::1038.simple_meaning: The Krittikas agreed that the newborn would belong to all of them, and they fed him with their milk.
ramayan::1038.simple_insight: A child can be claimed by many hearts at once.
ramayan::1038.detailed_meaning: The gods have just arranged the newborn Kumara’s care. The Krittikas make a shared promise and nurse him together, turning a miraculous birth into a collective bond. The verse is a supporting detail in the larger account of his divine origin.
ramayan::1038.modern_relevance: A baby arrives into a family where more than one person steps forward to care for him. The first gift is not possession, but shared responsibility.
ramayan::1038.insight: It shifts attention from ownership to collective nurture.

ramayan::1039.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तु देवता स्सर्वा: कार्तिकेय इति ब्रुवन् । । 13725 । । पुत्रस्त्रैलोक्यविख्यातो भविष्यति न संशय: । 4
ramayan::1039.verse_hindi: Thereafter, all the gods said, This son shall become renowned in the three worlds as Karttikeya, (son of krittikas). There is no doubt .
ramayan::1039.english_translation: Thereafter, all the gods said, 'This son will surely become known in the three worlds as Karttikeya.'
ramayan::1039.translation_literal: ततस्तु (thereafter) / देवता: (the gods) / सर्वा: (all) / कार्तिकेय इति (Karttikeya thus) / ब्रुवन् (said) / पुत्रः (son) / त्रैलोक्य-विख्यातः (famous in the three worlds) / भविष्यति (will become) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::1039.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1039.essence: The child is named before his story begins.
ramayan::1039.simple_meaning: The gods name the newborn child Karttikeya and declare that his fame will spread through all three worlds.
ramayan::1039.simple_insight: Some births are so charged with meaning that everyone present can feel their future before it arrives.
ramayan::1039.detailed_meaning: Kumara has just been born from Ganga, and the gods have arranged the Krittikas to nurture him. Now they declare his name and future fame. This is still the naming and blessing, not the deeper teaching of the passage.
ramayan::1039.modern_relevance: A room full of people watches a baby and already speaks about the life ahead. The moment is about recognition, not instruction.
ramayan::1039.insight: It frames the child’s arrival as a public acknowledgment of destined greatness.

ramayan::1040.verse_sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा स्कन्नं गर्भपरिस्रवे । । 13726 । । स्नापयन् परया लक्ष्म्या दीप्यमानं यथानलम् ।
ramayan::1040.verse_hindi: Hearing the words of the gods, the krittikas bathed the baby that descended from the womb of Ganga resembling flaming fire and shining with great beauty.
ramayan::1040.english_translation: Hearing the gods' words, the krittikas bathed the baby who had emerged from Ganga's womb, shining with great beauty like blazing fire.
ramayan::1040.translation_literal: तेषाम् (their) / तत्-वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / स्कन्नम् (descended) / गर्भ-परिस्रवे (from the womb's flow) / स्नापयन् (bathing) / परया (with supreme) / लक्ष्म्या (splendor) / दीप्यमानम् (shining) / यथा (like) / अनलम् (fire)
ramayan::1040.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1040.essence: A newborn's radiance is confirmed through ritual care.
ramayan::1040.simple_meaning: The krittikas bathe the newborn after hearing the gods' words, and the child shines with radiant beauty.
ramayan::1040.simple_insight: A sacred beginning is marked by care, recognition, and wonder.
ramayan::1040.detailed_meaning: The gods have just named the child Karttikeya and declared his future glory. Now the krittikas bathe the newborn, who has emerged from Ganga and shines like fire. The verse is a brief ceremonial detail in the larger birth narrative.
ramayan::1040.modern_relevance: A newborn is lifted from the bath, and everyone in the room goes quiet for a second. Some moments feel larger than the people holding them.
ramayan::1040.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the meaning others place on it.

ramayan::1041.verse_sanskrit: स्कन्द इत्यब्रुवन् देवा: स्कन्नं गर्भपरिस्रवात् । । 13727 । । कार्तिकेयं महाभागं काकुत्स्थ ज्वलनोपमम् ।
ramayan::1041.verse_hindi: O scion of the Kakusthas, Karttikeya lustrous like flaming fire, was very fortunate Descended from the womb of the Ganga, he is named Skanda by the gods.
ramayan::1041.english_translation: The gods said, "He descended from the womb, so he is Skanda"—Karttikeya, the great one, O scion of the Kakusthas, blazing like fire.
ramayan::1041.translation_literal: स्कन्द (Skanda) / इति (thus) / अब्रुवन् (they said) / देवा: (the gods) / स्कन्नं (one who has descended) / गर्भपरिस्रवात् (from the flow of the womb) / कार्तिकेयं (Karttikeya) / महाभागं (the greatly fortunate one) / काकुत्स्थ (O scion of the Kakusthas) / ज्वलनोपमम् (like blazing fire)
ramayan::1041.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1041.essence: His name records the miracle of his birth.
ramayan::1041.simple_meaning: The gods give the child a name based on how he came into the world and praise his radiant greatness.
ramayan::1041.simple_insight: Some names are born from wonder, not convention.
ramayan::1041.detailed_meaning: The gods have just celebrated the extraordinary birth of Karttikeya. After describing his emergence from the womb and his blazing brilliance, they now name him Skanda. The verse is part of the naming sequence, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::1041.modern_relevance: A family gathers around a newborn and debates the name that will carry the child forward. The moment is intimate, but the name also holds memory, hope, and awe.
ramayan::1041.insight: It shows how a name can preserve the story of a person's arrival.

ramayan::1042.verse_sanskrit: प्रादुर्भूतं तत: क्षीरं कृत्तिकानामनुत्तमम् । । 13728 । । षण्णां षडाननो भूत्वा जग्राह स्तनजं पय: ।
ramayan::1042.verse_hindi: Then excellent milk surged in the breasts of krittikas. Assuming six mouths, he sucked the milk.
ramayan::1042.english_translation: Then excellent milk surged in the breasts of the Krittikas. Assuming six mouths, he sucked the milk.
ramayan::1042.translation_literal: प्रादुर्भूतम् (became manifest) / ततः (then) / क्षीरम् (milk) / कृत्तिकानाम् (of the Krittikas) / अनुत्तमम् (excellent) / षण्णाम् (of six) / षडाननो (six-faced one) / भूत्वा (having become) / जग्राह (he grasped/sucked) / स्तनजम् (from the breast) / पयः (milk)
ramayan::1042.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1042.essence: Even a tender body can hold overwhelming force.
ramayan::1042.simple_meaning: Milk appeared in the Krittikas, and the six-faced child drank from them with all six mouths.
ramayan::1042.simple_insight: Great strength can arrive in a form that still looks small and tender.
ramayan::1042.detailed_meaning: The Krittikas have just bathed the radiant child born from Ganga. Now milk appears in their breasts, and the infant who has become six-faced drinks from all of them at once. The verse marks his miraculous nourishment before his future power is shown.
ramayan::1042.insight: It links hidden power with a body that still appears delicate.

ramayan::1043.verse_sanskrit: गृहीत्वा क्षीरमेकाह्ना सुकुमारवपुस्तदा । । 13729 । । अजयत्स्वेन वीर्येण दैत्यसेनागणान् विभु: ।
ramayan::1043.verse_hindi: Drinking milk just for a day and with a body still tender he could vanquish hosts of demons by his inborn prowess so capable be was
ramayan::1043.english_translation: Drinking milk for just one day, still tender-bodied, he defeated hosts of demons by his own prowess.
ramayan::1043.translation_literal: गृहीत्वा (having taken) / क्षीरम् (milk) / एकाह्ना (in one day) / सुकुमारवपुः (with a tender body) / तदा (then) / अजयत् (he conquered) / स्वेन (by his own) / वीर्येण (prowess) / दैत्यसेनागणान् (hosts of demon-armies) / विभुः (the mighty one)
ramayan::1043.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1043.essence: Tenderness and power can exist in the same body.
ramayan::1043.simple_meaning: He was still very young and delicate, yet his own power was enough to defeat entire armies of demons.
ramayan::1043.simple_insight: Real strength is not always visible in the body that carries it.
ramayan::1043.detailed_meaning: The gods have just praised Karttikeya’s birth and miraculous feeding by the Krittikas. Now the verse turns to his first proof of power: even with a tender body and only a day of nourishment, he overcomes demon hosts by innate force.
ramayan::1043.modern_relevance: A child barely trained suddenly handles a crisis better than everyone expected. What looks fragile can still hold astonishing force when the moment arrives.
ramayan::1043.insight: It shifts attention from outward weakness to latent capability.

ramayan::1044.verse_hindi: With the Firegod in the forefront, all the gods assembled and installed Karttikeya, shining on unsurpassed brilliant, as commander of the gods forces.
ramayan::1044.english_translation: With Agni in the lead, the gods assembled and installed Karttikeya, the commander of the divine forces, whose brilliance was unmatched.
ramayan::1044.translation_literal: सुरगणा: (the gods) / समेत्य (having assembled together) / अग्निपुरोगमा: (with Agni at the front) / ततः (then) / तम् (him) / अतुलद्युतिम् (of unmatched brilliance) / सुरसेनागणपतिम् (the commander of the divine army) / अभ्यषिञ्चन् (anointed / installed)
ramayan::1044.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1044.essence: Power becomes authority when it is publicly recognised.
ramayan::1044.simple_meaning: The gods gathered with Agni leading them and formally installed Karttikeya as their army commander.
ramayan::1044.simple_insight: Greatness is recognised when a community entrusts responsibility to the one who has earned it.
ramayan::1044.detailed_meaning: After Karttikeya's miraculous rise and victory over the demons, the gods gather with Agni at their head. They formally anoint the radiant young warrior as commander of their forces, sealing his place after his extraordinary feat.
ramayan::1044.modern_relevance: A team watches the quiet new hire solve the problem everyone else avoided. By the end of the week, the title changes because the reality already had.
ramayan::1044.insight: It shows that proven strength naturally becomes entrusted leadership.

ramayan::1045.verse_sanskrit: एष ते राम गङ्गाया विस्तरोऽभिहितो मया । । 13731 । । कुमारसम्भवश्चैव धन्य: पुण्यस्तथैव च ।
ramayan::1045.verse_hindi: O Rama this story of Ganga and that of the  birth of Kumara, who was fortunate and auspicious, has been related to you in detail.
ramayan::1045.english_translation: O Rama, this detailed account of Ganga and the auspicious birth of Kumara has now been told to you.
ramayan::1045.translation_literal: एष (this) / ते (to you) / राम (Rama) / गङ्गाया (of Ganga) / विस्तरः (detailed account) / अभिहितः (has been spoken) / मया (by me) / कुमारसम्भवः (the birth of Kumara) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / धन्यः (auspicious) / पुण्यः (holy) / तथा (also) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
ramayan::1045.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1045.essence: The story is complete; the next lesson can begin.
ramayan::1045.simple_meaning: Valmiki tells Rama that he has finished recounting the story of Ganga and Kumara's auspicious birth.
ramayan::1045.simple_insight: Some teachings arrive as a complete story, not a single line.
ramayan::1045.detailed_meaning: Valmiki turns back to Rama after narrating the tale of Ganga and Kartikeya's birth. This line simply marks the close of that account, preparing the listener for the next teaching rather than offering a teaching itself.
ramayan::1045.modern_relevance: You finish telling a long story and pause, knowing the real point will come next.
ramayan::1045.insight: It marks a transition, not a conclusion of thought.

ramayan::1046.verse_sanskrit: भक्तश्च य: कार्तिकेये काकुत्स्थ भुवि मानवः । आयुष्मान् पुत्रपौत्रैश्च स्कन्दसालोक्यतां व्रजेत् । । 13732 । ।
ramayan::1046.verse_hindi: O son of the Kakusthas whosoever reveres Kartikeya on this earth with devotion and faith, shall have a long life, sons and grandsons and after death will reach the world of
ramayan::1046.english_translation: O son of the Kakusthas, whoever reveres Kartikeya on this earth with devotion and faith will enjoy long life, sons and grandsons, and after death will reach the world of Skanda.
ramayan::1046.translation_literal: भक्तः (devoted) / च (and) / यः (whoever) / कार्तिकेये (in Kartikeya) / काकुत्स्थ (O Kakutstha) / भुवि (on earth) / मानवः (a human being) / आयुष्मान् (long-lived) / पुत्र-पौत्रैः (with sons and grandsons) / च (and) / स्कन्द-सालोक्यताम् (the state of being in Skanda's world) / व्रजेत् (would go)
ramayan::1046.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1046.essence: Faith in Skanda is said to bless life now and beyond death.
ramayan::1046.simple_meaning: Devotion to Kartikeya is said to bring long life, family blessing, and a blessed afterlife.
ramayan::1046.simple_insight: Faith is not small; it can shape how you live, what you receive, and how you are remembered.
ramayan::1046.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just told Rama the sacred story of Kartikeya's birth. He ends with a blessing: devotion to Skanda is not empty ritual, but a force that is believed to protect life, family, and the journey beyond death.
ramayan::1046.modern_relevance: You light a lamp before a hard exam, a surgery, or your child's fever, hoping your devotion reaches farther than your fear. This verse speaks to that hope.
ramayan::1046.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to a lived trust that asks for protection and blessing.

ramayan::1047.verse_sanskrit: तां कथां कौशिको रामे निवेद्य कुशिकात्मज: । पुनरेवापरं वाक्यं काकुत्स्थ मिदमब्रवीत् । । 1381 । ।
ramayan::1047.verse_hindi: Viswamitra, an offspring of Kusika having related the story (of Karthikeya) to the son of the Kakusthas (Rama) said again.
ramayan::1047.english_translation: Having related that story to Rama, Viswamitra, son of Kusika, spoke again to the descendant of Kakustha.
ramayan::1047.translation_literal: तां (that) / कथां (story) / कौशिकः (Viswamitra, son of Kusika) / रामे (to Rama) / निवेद्य (having related) / कुशिकात्मजः (son of Kusika) / पुनरेव (again indeed) / अपरं (another) / वाक्यम् (speech) / काकुत्स्थम् (to the Kakustha descendant) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1047.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1047.essence: The teacher pauses, then opens the next story.
ramayan::1047.simple_meaning: Viswamitra finishes telling Rama the story and then begins another one.
ramayan::1047.simple_insight: Some moments are just transitions. Not every line carries a lesson; some simply move the story forward.
ramayan::1047.detailed_meaning: After finishing the account of Kartikeya, Viswamitra turns back to Rama and prepares to tell another ancient story. This verse is a bridge, not the teaching itself. The real content comes in the next lines, where Sagara and the lineage of Ayodhya are introduced.
ramayan::1047.modern_relevance: You finish one conversation and the other person leans in to begin the next thread. The pause matters, but the meaning is still ahead.
ramayan::1047.insight: It marks a transition, reminding you that context can matter more than the line itself.

ramayan::1048.verse_sanskrit: अयोध्याधिपति श्शूर: पूर्वमासीन्नराधिप: । सगरो नाम धर्मात्मा प्रजाकामस्स चाप्रज: । । 1382 । ।
ramayan::1048.verse_hindi: In olden days there lived a brave and righteous king named Sagara who was ruler of Ayodhya. He was childless and desired to have children,
ramayan::1048.english_translation: In olden days there lived a brave and righteous king named Sagara who was ruler of Ayodhya. He was childless and desired to have children.
ramayan::1048.translation_literal: अयोध्याधिपतिḥ (ruler of Ayodhya) / श्शूरः (brave) / पूर्वम् (formerly, in olden times) / आसीत् (there was) / नराधिपः (king) / सगरः (Sagara) / नाम (by name) / धर्मात्मा (righteous-souled) / प्रजाकामः (desiring offspring) / सः (he) / अप्रजः (childless)
ramayan::1048.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1048.essence: A righteous king can still be defined by what he lacks.
ramayan::1048.simple_meaning: A brave, righteous king named Sagara ruled Ayodhya. He had no children and longed for them.
ramayan::1048.simple_insight: Even a powerful ruler can feel the ache of childlessness.
ramayan::1048.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has begun a story for Rama by naming Sagara, the ancient king of Ayodhya. The verse introduces his character and his lack of heirs, setting up the family line and the later events that will follow.
ramayan::1048.modern_relevance: A family photo sits on the table, but one chair is always empty. Behind public strength, there can be a private ache that shapes everything that comes next.
ramayan::1048.insight: It shifts attention from status to longing, showing that greatness does not erase human need.

ramayan::1049.verse_sanskrit: वैदर्भदुहिता राम केशिनी नाम नामत: । ज्येष्ठा सगरपत्नी सा धर्मिष्ठा सत्यवादिनी । । 1383 । ।
ramayan::1049.verse_hindi: O Rama the daughter of the king of Vidarbha by name Kesini was Sagaras eldest wife who was righteous and truthful.
ramayan::1049.english_translation: O Rama, Kesini, the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, was Sagara's eldest wife. She was righteous and truthful.
ramayan::1049.translation_literal: वैदर्भदुहिता (daughter of the king of Vidarbha) / राम (O Rama) / केशिनी (Kesini) / नामत: (by name) / ज्येष्ठा (eldest) / सगरपत्नी (Sagara's wife) / सा (she) / धर्मिष्ठा (righteous) / सत्यवादिनी (truthful)
ramayan::1049.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1049.essence: A key figure is introduced before the story's deeper consequences arrive.
ramayan::1049.simple_meaning: Kesini, Sagara's eldest wife, is introduced as a righteous and truthful woman from Vidarbha.
ramayan::1049.simple_insight: Some verses simply establish the people who make the story possible.
ramayan::1049.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is explaining Sagara's family line to Rama. Before the larger story can move forward, Valmiki pauses to name Kesini, Sagara's eldest wife, and to mark her virtue. It is a supporting detail in the genealogy.
ramayan::1049.modern_relevance: A family tree gets explained before the real story begins. You are being told who belonged where, because later choices will depend on it.
ramayan::1049.insight: It trains you to notice how lineage and character are introduced before major events unfold.

ramayan::1050.verse_sanskrit: अरिष्टनेमेर्दुहिता रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि । द्वितीया सगरस्यासीत्पत्नी सुमतिसंज्ञिता । । 1384 । ।
ramayan::1050.verse_hindi: The daughter of Arishtanemi named Sumati was the second wife of Sagara and  none surpassed her in charm on earth.
ramayan::1050.english_translation: The daughter of Arishtanemi named Sumati was Sagara's second wife, and none on earth surpassed her in beauty.
ramayan::1050.translation_literal: अरिष्टनेमेः (of Arishtanemi) / दुहिता (daughter) / रूपेण (in beauty) / अप्रतिमा (unmatched) / भुवि (on earth) / द्वितीया (second) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / आसीत् (was) / पत्नी (wife) / सुमतिसंज्ञिता (named Sumati)
ramayan::1050.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1050.essence: A royal story begins by naming the women around the king.
ramayan::1050.simple_meaning: Sagara's second wife was Sumati, daughter of Arishtanemi, and she was famous for unmatched beauty.
ramayan::1050.simple_insight: Some verses simply place the people before the story begins.
ramayan::1050.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is introducing King Sagara's family line. After naming his first wife, he adds Sumati, his second wife, and notes her unmatched beauty. The verse builds the royal background before Sagara's austerities begin.
ramayan::1050.modern_relevance: A family history meeting starts with names, titles, and one quiet detail that matters later. Before the real event begins, you need to know who stands in the frame.
ramayan::1050.insight: It frames the coming episode by establishing Sagara's household and lineage.

ramayan::1051.verse_sanskrit: ताभ्यां सह महाराज: पत्नीभ्यां तप्तवांस्तप: । हिमवन्तं समासाद्य भृगुप्रस्रवणे गिरौ । । 1385 । ।
ramayan::1051.verse_hindi: The king (Sagara) accompanied by his wives reached Himavat mountain and engaged  himself in severe austerities on a peak called Bhriguprasravana.
ramayan::1051.english_translation: The king Sagara, together with his two wives, reached Mount Himavat and performed severe austerities on the peak called Bhriguprasravana.
ramayan::1051.translation_literal: ताभ्यां (with those two) / सह (together with) / महाराजः (the great king) / पत्नीभ्यां (with the two wives) / तप्तवान् (performed austerities) / तपः (austerity) / हिमवन्तम् (Himavat) / समासाद्य (having reached) / भृगुप्रस्रवणे (at Bhriguprasravana) / गिरौ (on the mountain)
ramayan::1051.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1051.essence: A future blessing is earned through long, unseen severity.
ramayan::1051.simple_meaning: Sagara and his two wives went to Mount Himavat and practiced harsh austerity on Bhriguprasravana.
ramayan::1051.simple_insight: Great outcomes often begin with quiet endurance no one sees.
ramayan::1051.detailed_meaning: Sagara has come with his two wives to a mountain peak and taken up severe austerity. This is not the result yet, only the hard preparation before the blessing arrives in the next verse.
ramayan::1051.modern_relevance: You move to a new city, give up comfort, and keep showing up before anything changes. The real work is happening long before the reward appears.
ramayan::1051.insight: It shifts attention from the blessing to the disciplined waiting that makes blessing possible.

ramayan::1052.verse_sanskrit: अथ वर्षशते पूर्णे तपसाऽराधितो मुनि: । सगराय वरं प्रादाद्भृगुस्सत्यवतां वर: । । 1386 । ।
ramayan::1052.verse_hindi: When Sagara completed a hundred years in austerities, highly pleased by his performance, ascetic Bhrugu, the best among the truthful granted him a boon.
ramayan::1052.english_translation: When Sagara completed a hundred years in austerities, highly pleased by his performance, ascetic Bhrugu, the best among the truthful, granted him a boon.
ramayan::1052.translation_literal: अथ (then) / वर्षशते (in a hundred years) / पूर्णे (completed) / तपसा (by austerities) / आराधितः (pleased, propitiated) / मुनिः (the sage) / सगराय (to Sagara) / वरम् (a boon) / प्रादात् (gave) / भृगुः (Bhrigu) / सत्यवताम् (among the truthful) / वरः (best)
ramayan::1052.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1052.essence: Long austerity finally earns the blessing.
ramayan::1052.simple_meaning: After a hundred years of austerity, Bhrigu is pleased and grants Sagara a boon.
ramayan::1052.simple_insight: Patient, sustained effort can open a door that force never could.
ramayan::1052.detailed_meaning: Sagara has spent a hundred years in severe austerity on Mount Himavat with his wives. Only after that long discipline does Bhrigu, the truthful sage, appear pleased enough to grant him a boon. The verse is a transition into the reward that follows.
ramayan::1052.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn, long after motivation fades. One day the work itself changes you, and the result finally arrives.
ramayan::1052.insight: It shifts attention from quick gain to long formation and earned readiness.

ramayan::1053.verse_sanskrit: अपत्यलाभस्सुमहान् भविष्यति तवानघ । कीर्तिं चाप्रतिमां लोके प्राप्स्यसे पुरुषर्षभ । । 1387 । ।
ramayan::1053.verse_hindi: O sinless one, you will get a very great progeny, O best among men you will acquire unparalleled fame in this world.
ramayan::1053.english_translation: O sinless one, you will have a great lineage, and you will win unmatched fame in the world, best among men.
ramayan::1053.translation_literal: अपत्यलाभः (gain of offspring) / सुमहान् (very great) / भविष्यति (will be) / तव (your) / अनघ (sinless one) / कीर्तिम् च (and fame) / अप्रतिमाम् (unmatched) / लोके (in the world) / प्राप्स्यसि (you will attain) / पुरुषर्षभ (best among men)
ramayan::1053.speaker: Bhrigu
ramayan::1053.essence: True success is a life that keeps echoing after you.
ramayan::1053.simple_meaning: Bhrigu blesses Sagara with two gifts: many descendants and lasting fame.
ramayan::1053.simple_insight: Some blessings are bigger than comfort — they shape what remains after you are gone.
ramayan::1053.detailed_meaning: After a hundred years of austerity on Mount Himavat, Sagara receives Bhrigu's boon. The sage promises him not just children, but a lineage and a reputation that will spread across the world.
ramayan::1053.modern_relevance: You pour years into work no one notices, wondering if any of it will matter. Then one day you realize you are building a name, a family, or a legacy that will outlast the effort.
ramayan::1053.insight: It shifts attention from immediate reward to the long arc of what your life leaves behind.

ramayan::1054.verse_sanskrit: एका जनयिता तात पुत्रं वंशकरं तव । षष्ठिं पुत्रसहस्राणि अपरा जनयिष्यति । । 1388 । ।
ramayan::1054.verse_hindi: O child, one wife will beget a son who will perpetuate your race and the other, sixty thousand sons, said Bhrugu.
ramayan::1054.english_translation: O child, one wife will bear you a son who will continue your line, and another will bear sixty thousand sons, said Bhrugu.
ramayan::1054.translation_literal: एका (one) / जनयिता (will bear) / तात (O child) / पुत्रं (a son) / वंशकरं (line-continuing) / तव (your) / षष्ठिं (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / अपरा (the other) / जनयिष्यति (will beget)
ramayan::1054.speaker: Bhrugu
ramayan::1054.essence: One child preserves the line; many children extend the name.
ramayan::1054.simple_meaning: Bhrugu blesses Sagara with two kinds of offspring: one wife will bear a son who continues the family line, and another will bear sixty thousand sons.
ramayan::1054.simple_insight: Great power can arrive in different forms: one child can carry a lineage, while many can carry a name.
ramayan::1054.detailed_meaning: Sagara has completed a hundred years of austerity, and Bhrugu has just granted him a blessing. This line specifies the shape of that blessing: one wife will give him the heir who preserves the family line, while the other will bear sixty thousand sons.
ramayan::1054.modern_relevance: You may want success to arrive in one clear form, but life often gives you both a single heir of meaning and a wide spread of achievement.
ramayan::1054.insight: It shifts attention from quantity alone to the different roles children can play in carrying forward a family.

ramayan::1055.verse_sanskrit: भाषमाणं महात्मानं राजपुत्र्यौ प्रसाद्य तम् । ऊचतु: परमप्रीते कृताञ्जलिपुटे तदा । । 1389 । ।
ramayan::1055.verse_hindi: Thereafter, both the daughters of the king were exceedingly delighted. Having propitiated  that magnanimous asectic both of them with folded hands in supplication, said:
ramayan::1055.english_translation: Thereafter, both princesses, greatly pleased, approached that great soul, and then, with folded hands, said to him in supplication:
ramayan::1055.translation_literal: भाषमाणं (speaking) / महात्मानं (the great-souled one) / राजपुत्र्यौ (the two princesses) / प्रसाद्य (having propitiated) / तम् (him) / ऊचतु: (they said) / परमप्रीते (greatly pleased) / कृताञ्जलिपुटे (with folded hands) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1055.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1055.essence: Joyful news can still leave you asking for clarity.
ramayan::1055.simple_meaning: The two princesses are delighted by the sage's words and respectfully ask him more, with folded hands.
ramayan::1055.simple_insight: Even sacred answers can open into more questions when your heart wants certainty.
ramayan::1055.detailed_meaning: Bhrigu has just spoken of the children that will be born. The two royal women are pleased by his blessing, but the moment is not complete yet. They bow to the great sage and prepare to ask which of them will bear which destiny.
ramayan::1055.modern_relevance: You hear news that sounds promising, but you still need the details before you can breathe easily. Relief and uncertainty can live in the same moment.
ramayan::1055.insight: It shows how blessing leads naturally to a deeper question about what will actually happen.

ramayan::1056.verse_sanskrit: एक: कस्यास्सुतो ब्रह्मन् का बहून् जनयिष्यति । श्रोतुमिच्छावहे ब्रह्मन् सत्यमस्तु वचस्तव । । 13810 । ।
ramayan::1056.verse_hindi: O knower of Brahman which of us will beget one, and who many sons? O Brahmarshi we wish to hear. Let your words come true.
ramayan::1056.english_translation: O knower of Brahman, which of us will beget one son, and who many sons? O Brahmarshi, we wish to hear. Let your words come true.
ramayan::1056.translation_literal: एकः (one) / कस्याः (of which one) / सुतः (son) / ब्रह्मन् (O knower of Brahman) / का (which one) / बहून् (many) / जनयिष्यति (will beget) / श्रोतुम् (to hear) / इच्छावहे (we wish) / ब्रह्मन् (O knower of Brahman) / सत्यम् (true) / अस्तु (let it be) / वचः (word) / तव (your)
ramayan::1056.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1056.essence: They ask for certainty where only a blessing has been given.
ramayan::1056.simple_meaning: The two women ask Bhrigu which of them will bear one son and which will bear many, and they ask for his words to prove true.
ramayan::1056.simple_insight: Some questions are really about the future you are hoping to receive.
ramayan::1056.detailed_meaning: After Bhrigu’s blessing, the two princesses bow with folded hands and ask him to clarify the result: which one will bear a single son, and which will bear many. Their hope and curiosity turn a blessing into a specific promise.
ramayan::1056.modern_relevance: You want a clear answer before you commit to the uncertainty ahead. That anxious need to know is exactly what this royal question carries.
ramayan::1056.insight: It shows how people try to turn blessing into certainty before they can rest.

ramayan::1057.verse_sanskrit: तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भृगु: परमधार्मिक: । उवाच परमां वाणीं स्वच्छन्दोऽत्र विधीयताम् । । 13811 । ।
ramayan::1057.verse_hindi: Hearing their words, highly virtuous Bhrugu made an excellent statement saying, In this matter, you may exercise your free will.
ramayan::1057.english_translation: Hearing their words, the highly virtuous Bhrigu spoke a noble reply: In this matter, let free choice be made.
ramayan::1057.translation_literal: तयोः (of those two) / तद्-वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / भृगुः (Bhrigu) / परम-धार्मिकः (highly virtuous) / उवाच (spoke) / परमाम् (excellent) / वाणीम् (speech) / स्वच्छन्दः (free will) / अत्र (here) / विधीयताम् (let be made / let be applied)
ramayan::1057.speaker: Bhrigu
ramayan::1057.essence: True guidance leaves room for your own will.
ramayan::1057.simple_meaning: Bhrigu tells the women they may choose freely in this matter instead of being forced into one fixed outcome.
ramayan::1057.simple_insight: There is dignity in being allowed to choose your own path.
ramayan::1057.detailed_meaning: Bhrigu, asked to resolve a question about offspring, answers without imposing a command. He leaves the decision to the two women, showing that even sacred authority can honor personal choice when the future is being decided.
ramayan::1057.modern_relevance: You are being pushed to decide quickly: yes or no, stay or leave, accept or refuse. A wise voice can still make room for your own will before the door closes.
ramayan::1057.insight: It shifts the mind from obedience under pressure to conscious choice with dignity.

ramayan::1058.verse_sanskrit: एको वंशकरो वाऽस्तु बहवो वा महाबला: । कीर्तिमन्तो महोत्साहा: का वा कं वरमिच्छति । । 13812 । ।
ramayan::1058.verse_hindi: What would you wish? One son who perpetuates the race or many possessed of mighty strength endowed with fame and perseverance? (asked Bhrugu).
ramayan::1058.english_translation: What would you wish? One son who perpetuates the race or many possessed of mighty strength endowed with fame and perseverance?
ramayan::1058.translation_literal: एकः (one) / वंशकरः (lineage-continuing son) / वा (or) / अस्तु (let there be) / बहवः (many) / वा (or) / महाबलाः (greatly strong) / कीर्तिमन्तः (famous) / महोत्साहाः (greatly energetic) / काः (which) / वा (or) / कम् (whom) / वरम् (boon) / इच्छति (desires)
ramayan::1058.speaker: Bhrigu
ramayan::1058.essence: The boon asks you to choose between lineage and abundance.
ramayan::1058.simple_meaning: Bhrigu asks the king to choose between one heir who continues the family line or many sons who are strong, famous, and full of drive.
ramayan::1058.simple_insight: Some choices are about continuity; others are about power and abundance.
ramayan::1058.detailed_meaning: Bhrigu has been asked to decide a boon for Sagara's wives. He presents the choice plainly: one son to carry the lineage, or many sons with strength, fame, and energy. The next verse shows the decision.
ramayan::1058.modern_relevance: You sit with a hard family decision: one secure future, or a larger, riskier one with more possibilities. The question is not abstract — it changes everything that follows.
ramayan::1058.insight: It frames a life choice as a tradeoff between inheritance and expansion.

ramayan::1059.verse_sanskrit: मुनेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा केशिनी रघुनन्दन । पुत्रं वंशकरं राम जग्राह नृपसन्निधौ । । 13813 । ।
ramayan::1059.verse_hindi: O Rama, delight of the descendants of Raghus, on hearing the words of the  ascetic in the presence of king Sagara, Kesini chose the boon to have a son who perpetuates the race.
ramayan::1059.english_translation: O Rama, delight of the descendants of Raghu, on hearing the words of the ascetic in the presence of king Sagara, Kesini chose the boon to have a son who perpetuates the race.
ramayan::1059.translation_literal: मुनेः (of the ascetic) / तु (then) / वचनं (the words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / केशिनी (Kesini) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line) / पुत्रं (a son) / वंशकरं (who continues the lineage) / राम (O Rama) / जग्राह (chose / took) / नृपसन्निधौ (in the presence of the king)
ramayan::1059.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1059.essence: A single boon begins a long chain of consequences.
ramayan::1059.simple_meaning: Kesini chose to receive a son who would continue her family line.
ramayan::1059.simple_insight: Some choices are simple, but they shape everything that follows.
ramayan::1059.detailed_meaning: At Sagara's court, the sage offers a choice of boons to the king's wives. After hearing him, Kesini asks for a son who will carry on the family line. This is one step in the larger birth story of Sagara's sons.
ramayan::1059.modern_relevance: A family sits in a hospital waiting room, deciding what matters most in a life-changing moment. A single wish can set an entire future in motion.
ramayan::1059.insight: It shows how a small request can determine the shape of an entire lineage.

ramayan::1060.verse_sanskrit: षष्ठिं पुत्रसहस्राणि सुपर्णभगिनी तदा । महोत्साहान् कीर्तिमतो जग्राह सुमति: सुतान् । । 13814 । ।
ramayan::1060.verse_hindi: Then, Sumati (the other wife) sister of Suparna (Garuda) obtained the boon of sixty thousand sons endowed with fame and great perseverance.
ramayan::1060.english_translation: Then Sumati, the sister of Garuda, obtained sixty thousand sons, all famed and full of great resolve.
ramayan::1060.translation_literal: षष्ठिं (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousands of sons) / सुपर्णभगिनी (sister of Suparna/Garuda) / तदा (then) / महोत्साहान् (of great resolve) / कीर्तिमतः (famed) / जग्राह (obtained) / सुमति: (Sumati) / सुतान् (sons)
ramayan::1060.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1060.essence: A granted boon multiplies into an entire future.
ramayan::1060.simple_meaning: Sumati, the other wife, received a boon for sixty thousand sons who would be famous and full of energy.
ramayan::1060.simple_insight: Great outcomes often begin as a simple granted wish.
ramayan::1060.detailed_meaning: Bhrigu has just offered a choice between one son who preserves the line and many mighty sons. After Kesini's choice, Sumati, the sister of Garuda, receives the other boon: sixty thousand sons. This is still setup, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1060.modern_relevance: A family discussion turns into a life-shaping decision, and one choice quietly sets the scale of everything that follows.
ramayan::1060.insight: It shifts attention from the wish itself to the consequences a single choice can unleash.

ramayan::1061.verse_sanskrit: प्रदक्षिणमृषिं कृत्वा शिरसाऽभिप्रणम्य च । जगाम स्वपुरं राजा सभार्यो रघुनन्दन । । 13815 । ।
ramayan::1061.verse_hindi: O son of the Raghus the king along with his wives, having circumambulated saint Bhrugu, bowed his head in reverence, saluted him with folded hands and returned to his capital.
ramayan::1061.english_translation: O son of the Raghus, the king along with his wives, having circumambulated saint Bhrugu, bowed his head in reverence, saluted him with folded hands and returned to his capital.
ramayan::1061.translation_literal: प्रदक्षिणम् (circumambulation) / ऋषिम् (the sage) / कृत्वा (having done) / शिरसा (with the head) / अभिप्रणम्य (having bowed reverently) / च (and) / जगाम (went) / स्वपुरम् (to his own city) / राजा (the king) / सभार्यः (along with his wives) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line)
ramayan::1061.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1061.essence: Honor is complete only when you leave with humility.
ramayan::1061.simple_meaning: The king respectfully circled the sage, bowed, and then returned home with his wives.
ramayan::1061.simple_insight: Respect is shown not only in words, but in the way you leave a sacred encounter.
ramayan::1061.detailed_meaning: After receiving the sage's blessing, King Sagara performs the proper courtly and ritual gestures before departing with his wives. The scene closes the exchange cleanly and prepares for the next event: the birth of the sons that will shape the story.
ramayan::1061.modern_relevance: You finish a difficult conversation, lower your voice, and leave with dignity intact. The real respect is in how you exit, not just how you enter.
ramayan::1061.insight: It teaches you to close a sacred or serious moment with humility and composure.

ramayan::1062.verse_sanskrit: अथ काले गते तस्मिन् ज्येष्ठा पुत्रं व्यजायत । असमञ्ज इति ख्यातं केशिनी सगरात्मजम् । । 13816 । ।
ramayan::1062.verse_hindi: After lapse of some time, the eldest wife Kesini gave birth to a son wellknown by name Asamanjasa.
ramayan::1062.english_translation: After some time had passed, the eldest wife Kesini gave birth to a son named Asamanjasa, the son of Sagara.
ramayan::1062.translation_literal: अथ (then) / काले (in time) / गते (having passed) / तस्मिन् (that) / ज्येष्ठा (eldest) / पुत्रं (a son) / व्यजायत (gave birth) / असमञ्ज इति (Asamanjasa thus) / ख्यातं (known) / केशिनी (Kesini) / सगरात्मजम् (Sagara's son)
ramayan::1062.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1062.essence: The first son arrives, and the family's future begins to take shape.
ramayan::1062.simple_meaning: After some time, Kesini, the elder queen, gave birth to a son named Asamanjasa.
ramayan::1062.simple_insight: A royal line continues, but this child will matter for more than birth alone.
ramayan::1062.detailed_meaning: After Bhrigu blesses Sagara and his queens, the story moves forward to the first birth in that house. Kesini, the elder queen, bears a son named Asamanjasa. It is a quiet setup for the larger fate of Sagara's lineage.
ramayan::1062.modern_relevance: A family waits for news after a long stretch of uncertainty, and the first birth changes the whole atmosphere. The story is still only beginning, but the line of consequence has started moving.
ramayan::1062.insight: It marks the beginning of a chain of events that will shape Sagara's house.

ramayan::1063.verse_sanskrit: सुमतिस्तु नरव्याघ्र गर्भतुम्बं व्यजायत । षष्ठि: पुत्रसहस्राणि तुम्बभेदाद्विनि:सृता: । । 13817 । ।
ramayan::1063.verse_hindi: O best among men, Sumati gave birth to a gourdlike foetus and when it burst open, sixty thousand sons emerged.
ramayan::1063.english_translation: O best among men, Sumati gave birth to a gourdlike foetus, and when it burst open, sixty thousand sons emerged.
ramayan::1063.translation_literal: सुमतिः (Sumati) / तु (indeed) / नरव्याघ्र (best among men) / गर्भतुम्बम् (gourdlike foetus) / व्यजायत (gave birth) / षष्ठिः (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / तुम्बभेदात् (from the bursting of the gourd) / विनिःसृताः (came forth)
ramayan::1063.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1063.essence: A legendary birth expands the royal line to sixty thousand sons.
ramayan::1063.simple_meaning: Sumati gave birth to a gourd-shaped foetus, and when it split open, sixty thousand sons came out.
ramayan::1063.simple_insight: The verse simply marks an extraordinary birth, setting up the next part of the story.
ramayan::1063.detailed_meaning: After the eldest wife has already borne Asamanjasa, the story turns to Sumati. Her pregnancy ends in a strange, legendary birth: a gourd-like mass bursts open and sixty thousand sons emerge. The verse is a lineage detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::1063.modern_relevance: A family story can suddenly turn strange and unforgettable, but this verse is only recording the next piece of the lineage.
ramayan::1063.insight: It establishes the king’s vast line of sons before the narrative moves on.

ramayan::1064.verse_sanskrit: घृतपूर्णेषु कुम्भेषु धात्र्यस्तान् समवर्धयन् । कालेन महता सर्वे यौवनं प्रतिपेदिरे । । 13818 । ।
ramayan::1064.verse_hindi: Nurses placed all of them in pots filled with clarified butter and fostered them. They attained adolescence after a long time.
ramayan::1064.english_translation: The nurses raised all of them in pots filled with clarified butter. In time, they all reached youth.
ramayan::1064.translation_literal: घृतपूर्णेषु (in clarified-butter-filled) / कुम्भेषु (in pots) / धात्र्यः (the nurses) / तान् (them) / समवर्धयन् (raised) / कालेन (by time) / महता (great) / सर्वे (all) / यौवनम् (youth) / प्रतिपेदिरे (attained)
ramayan::1064.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1064.essence: Great numbers still need patient care before they can mature.
ramayan::1064.simple_meaning: The infants were kept in pots of clarified butter and carefully raised until they became young men.
ramayan::1064.simple_insight: Some lives are carried forward quietly, long before they are ready to stand on their own.
ramayan::1064.detailed_meaning: Sagara’s sixty thousand sons have just been born in an extraordinary way. The nurses keep them alive in pots filled with clarified butter and raise them over time. This verse simply marks their growth, not a teaching or turning point.
ramayan::1064.modern_relevance: A child spends years under steady care before anyone sees the adult they will become. Most of that forming happens out of sight, in patient hands and ordinary repetition.
ramayan::1064.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic beginnings to the slow care that makes growth possible.

ramayan::1065.verse_sanskrit: अथ दीर्घेण कालेन रूपयौवनशालिन: । षष्टि: पुत्रसहस्राणि सगरस्याभवंस्तदा । । 13819 । ।
ramayan::1065.verse_hindi: Then, after a long time Sagaras sixty thousand sons attained beauty and youth.
ramayan::1065.english_translation: Then, after a long time, Sagara's sixty thousand sons attained beauty and youth.
ramayan::1065.translation_literal: अथ (then) / दीर्घेण (by a long) / कालेन (time) / रूपयौवनशालिनः (endowed with beauty and youth) / षष्टिः (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / अभवन् (became) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1065.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1065.essence: Time has quietly turned miracle into consequence.
ramayan::1065.simple_meaning: Sagara's sixty thousand sons grew up over time and became handsome young men.
ramayan::1065.simple_insight: Some stories move slowly before they turn tragic.
ramayan::1065.detailed_meaning: After being raised in pots of clarified butter, Sagara's sixty thousand sons finally grow into handsome young men. The scene is still calm, but the story is building toward the next disaster involving Asamanjasa and the boys by the Sarayu.
ramayan::1065.modern_relevance: A child you once worried over is suddenly grown, capable, and hard to recognize. Time has done its quiet work before anyone has had a chance to notice.
ramayan::1065.insight: It marks the passage from extraordinary birth to the next stage of the story.

ramayan::1066.verse_sanskrit: स च ज्येष्ठो नरश्रेष्ठ सगरस्यात्मसम्भव: । बालान् गृहीत्वा तु जले सरय्वा रघुनन्दन । । 13820 । । प्रक्षिप्य प्रहसन्नित्यं मज्जतस्तान् समीक्ष्य वै ।
ramayan::1066.verse_hindi: O best among men, delight of the Raghus (in the mean time) sagaras eldest son  Asamanjasa, used to seize hold of children and throw them into the waters of river Sarayu. And while they were drowning, he was laughing.
ramayan::1066.english_translation: O best among men, delight of the Raghus, Sagara's eldest son Asamanjasa used to seize children, throw them into the waters of the Sarayu, and laugh as they drowned.
ramayan::1066.translation_literal: स (he) / च (and) / ज्येष्ठो (eldest) / नरश्रेष्ठ (best among men) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / आत्मसम्भव: (born of himself) / बालान् (children) / गृहीत्वा (having seized) / तु (but) / जले (into water) / सरय्वा (of Sarayu) / प्रक्षिप्य (having thrown) / प्रहसन्नित्यं (laughing constantly) / मज्जतस्तान् (while they were drowning them) / समीक्ष्य (seeing) / वै (indeed)
ramayan::1066.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1066.essence: Cruelty becomes unmistakable when suffering is treated as entertainment.
ramayan::1066.simple_meaning: Asamanjasa, Sagara's eldest son, cruelly threw children into the Sarayu river and laughed as they drowned.
ramayan::1066.simple_insight: Some actions are so cruel they reveal a person has lost all moral restraint.
ramayan::1066.detailed_meaning: After the princes of Sagara have grown up, the epic turns to the dark conduct of the eldest son, Asamanjasa. He seizes children and throws them into the Sarayu for amusement, making his corruption impossible to ignore.
ramayan::1066.modern_relevance: A person in authority treats smaller, weaker people like toys, then smiles when they panic. The shock is not only the cruelty — it is how normal the cruelty feels to him.
ramayan::1066.insight: It shows how unchecked power and delight in harm destroy any claim to goodness.

ramayan::1067.verse_sanskrit: एवं पापसमाचारस्सज्जनप्रतिबाधक: । । 13821 । । पौराणामहिते युक्त: पुत्रो निर्वासित: पुरात् ।
ramayan::1067.verse_hindi: Thus this son inclined towards evil and formenting the good citizens was banished (of the king) from the capital for his indulgence in malevolent acts.
ramayan::1067.english_translation: Thus that son, inclined toward evil and obstructing good people, was banished from the capital for his harmful conduct.
ramayan::1067.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / पापसमाचारः (one of evil conduct) / सज्जनप्रतिबाधकः (obstructor of good people) / पौराणाम् (of the citizens) / अहिते (in harm) / युक्तः (engaged) / पुत्रः (son) / निर्वासितः (banished) / पुरात् (from the city)
ramayan::1067.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1067.essence: Repeated harm eventually costs you your place.
ramayan::1067.simple_meaning: A son who behaved badly, harmed good people, and caused trouble for the citizens was sent away from the capital.
ramayan::1067.simple_insight: Harmful conduct eventually removes even the privileged from the center of life.
ramayan::1067.detailed_meaning: In Sagara's line, Asamanjasa has already been shown frightening children and disturbing the city. This verse closes that episode: his misconduct has become so intolerable that the king expels his own son from the capital.
ramayan::1067.modern_relevance: A family keeps covering for one person’s cruelty until the damage becomes impossible to ignore. At that point, love does not mean enabling the harm anymore.
ramayan::1067.insight: It shows that public order sometimes requires removing a person who keeps injuring the common good.

ramayan::1068.verse_sanskrit: तस्य पुत्रोंऽशुमान्नाम असमञ्जस्य वीर्यवान् । । 13822 । । सम्मत स्सर्वलोकस्य सर्वस्यापि प्रियंवद: ।
ramayan::1068.verse_hindi: Asamanjasas son was Anshuman. He was valiant, beloved and courteous to every one in the world.
ramayan::1068.english_translation: Asamanjasa's son was Anshuman. He was valiant, beloved, and courteous to everyone in the world.
ramayan::1068.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / पुत्रः (son) / अंशुमान् नाम (named Anshuman) / असमञ्जस्य (of Asamanjasa) / वीर्यवान् (valiant) / सम्मतः (approved) / सर्वलोकस्य (by all the world) / सर्वस्य अपि (by everyone indeed) / प्रियंवदः (sweet-spoken, courteous)
ramayan::1068.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1068.essence: A son can restore what a father damaged.
ramayan::1068.simple_meaning: Asamanjasa's son was Anshuman, a brave and well-liked man who spoke kindly to everyone.
ramayan::1068.simple_insight: Character can redeem a family name; goodness is visible in how you treat people.
ramayan::1068.detailed_meaning: After Asamanjasa is banished for cruel behavior, the story pauses to name his son, Anshuman. The point is not action but lineage: from a troubling father comes a son admired by everyone, setting up the larger Sagara episode.
ramayan::1068.modern_relevance: A family reputation can feel heavy when your name is already associated with trouble. Then one person shows up calm, respectful, and reliable, and people begin to see a different future.
ramayan::1068.insight: It shifts attention from inherited shame to earned respect through conduct.

ramayan::1069.verse_sanskrit: तत: कालेन महता मतिस्समभिजायत । । 13823 । । सगरस्य नरश्रेष्ठ यजेयमिति निश्चिता ।
ramayan::1069.verse_hindi: O best among men after a long time, a thought came to the mind of Sagara to definitely perform a sacrifice.
ramayan::1069.english_translation: O best among men, after a long time, a firm thought arose in Sagara's mind: 'I will perform a sacrifice.'
ramayan::1069.translation_literal: तत: (then/after that) / कालेन (with time / after a long time) / महता (great/long) / मतिः (thought / intention) / समभिजायत (arose fully) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / नरश्रेष्ठ (O best among men) / यजेयम् (I will perform a sacrifice) / इति (thus) / निश्चिता (firmly decided)
ramayan::1069.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1069.essence: A sacrifice begins when intention finally hardens into resolve.
ramayan::1069.simple_meaning: After a long time, King Sagara formed a firm intention to perform a sacrifice.
ramayan::1069.simple_insight: A great act begins long before the ritual starts — with a settled intention.
ramayan::1069.detailed_meaning: Sagara, the king, has a long-delayed resolve to begin a sacrifice. This verse is only the inner decision before the ritual itself; the next verse shows him moving into the actual preparations.
ramayan::1069.modern_relevance: You sit with the idea for months before finally booking the venue, calling the teacher, or making the first payment. The real beginning was the moment you decided.
ramayan::1069.insight: It shifts attention from outward ceremony to the quiet moment when resolve becomes action.

ramayan::1070.verse_sanskrit: स कृत्वा निश्चयं राम सोपाध्यायगणस्तदा । । 13824 । । यज्ञकर्मणि वेदज्ञो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे ।
ramayan::1070.verse_hindi: O Rama having determined to perform a sacrifice, he (Sagara) versed in the Vedas, started the initiatory rites for the sacrifice in the company of high priests.
ramayan::1070.english_translation: O Rama, having resolved to perform a sacrifice, Sagara, learned in the Vedas, began the preparatory rites with his priests.
ramayan::1070.translation_literal: स (he) / कृत्वा (having made) / निश्चयं (a resolve) / राम (O Rama) / सोपाध्याय-गणः (with a group of priests) / तदा (then) / यज्ञ-कर्मणि (in sacrifice-work) / वेद-ज्ञः (knower of the Vedas) / यष्टुम् (to sacrifice) / समुपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::1070.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1070.essence: A resolved intention becomes real only when preparation begins.
ramayan::1070.simple_meaning: Sagara decides to perform a sacrifice and begins the ritual preparations with learned priests.
ramayan::1070.simple_insight: Big undertakings begin with a clear decision and careful preparation.
ramayan::1070.detailed_meaning: Sagara, king of Ayodhya, has already formed the resolve to perform a great sacrifice. Now, with priests skilled in Vedic ritual, he begins the formal preparations. The verse is scene-setting for the larger story that follows.
ramayan::1070.modern_relevance: You finally commit to the thing you've been postponing, then spend the evening gathering forms, names, and people. The real beginning is the moment you stop wavering.
ramayan::1070.insight: It shifts attention from desire alone to the disciplined start of action.

ramayan::1071.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रवचश्श्रुत्वा कथाऽन्ते रघुनन्दन: । उवाच परमप्रीतो मुनिं दीप्तमिवानलम् । । 1391 । ।
ramayan::1071.verse_hindi: Immensely pleased with the words of Viswamitra, to the ascetic flaming bright like fire, Rama spoke towards the end of the narration:
ramayan::1071.english_translation: Immensely pleased with the words of Viswamitra, Rama spoke to the ascetic, bright like fire, at the end of the narration.
ramayan::1071.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रवचः (the words of Viswamitra) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / कथाऽन्ते (at the end of the narration) / रघुनन्दनः (Rama, delight of the Raghu line) / उवाच (spoke) / परमप्रीतः (greatly pleased) / मुनिम् (to the ascetic) / दीप्तम् इव अनलम् (shining like fire)
ramayan::1071.speaker: Rama
ramayan::1071.essence: Delight becomes inquiry when understanding is still unfolding.
ramayan::1071.simple_meaning: Rama, pleased by Viswamitra's words, turns to the sage and speaks after the story ends.
ramayan::1071.simple_insight: Curiosity opens the next door. A receptive mind asks for more.
ramayan::1071.detailed_meaning: After hearing Viswamitra's account, Rama is delighted and immediately addresses the radiant sage. The next verse shows that his response is a request to hear the story in fuller detail, making this line a bridge into inquiry rather than a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::1071.modern_relevance: A mentor finishes explaining something and you lean forward instead of pretending you already understand. Real learning begins when you ask for the fuller story.
ramayan::1071.insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to active, respectful inquiry.

ramayan::1072.verse_sanskrit: श्रोतुमिच्छामि भद्रं ते विस्तरेण कथामिमाम् । पूर्वको मे कथं ब्रह्मन् यज्ञं वै समुपाहरत् । । 1392 । ।
ramayan::1072.verse_hindi: O Brahman I wish to listen in detail as to how my ancestors made preparations for the sacrifice? Prosperity to you.
ramayan::1072.english_translation: O Brahman, I wish to hear this story in detail. How did my ancestors prepare the sacrifice? Prosperity to you.
ramayan::1072.translation_literal: श्रोतुम् (to hear) / इच्छामि (I wish) / भद्रम् (prosperity, auspiciousness) / ते (to you) / विस्तरेण (in detail) / कथा (story) / इमाम् (this) / पूर्वकः (ancestor, predecessor) / मे (my) / कथम् (how) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahman) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / वै (indeed) / समुपाहरत् (prepared, arranged)
ramayan::1072.speaker: Rama
ramayan::1072.essence: Real understanding begins when you ask for the whole story.
ramayan::1072.simple_meaning: Rama asks Vishwamitra to explain the old sacrifice story in full detail. He wants to understand how his ancestors carried it out.
ramayan::1072.simple_insight: Curiosity can be humble, not weak. Asking well is often the beginning of real understanding.
ramayan::1072.detailed_meaning: Rama has just listened to Vishwamitra and is eager for more. He turns to the sage and asks how his forefathers arranged the sacrifice. The moment opens the deeper story behind the ritual and the curse tied to Sagara's line.
ramayan::1072.modern_relevance: You hear a half-explained story in a meeting and feel the urge to nod along. Rama does the opposite: he asks for the full context before moving on.
ramayan::1072.insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to active inquiry.

ramayan::1073.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रस्तु काकुत्स्थमुवाच प्रहसन्निव । श्रूयतां विस्तरो राम सगरस्य महात्मन: । । 1393 । ।
ramayan::1073.verse_hindi: Viswamitra addressing the son of the Kakusthas (Rama) with a smile said, O Rama hear in detail the story of the magnanimous king Sagara.
ramayan::1073.english_translation: Viswamitra, smiling, said to Rama: Listen in detail to the story of the great king Sagara.
ramayan::1073.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / तु (indeed) / काकुत्स्थम् (to Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / उवाच (said) / प्रहसन्निव (as if smiling) / श्रूयताम् (let it be heard) / विस्तरः (in detail) / राम (Rama) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled)
ramayan::1073.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1073.essence: A long story begins because the answer needs its roots.
ramayan::1073.simple_meaning: Viswamitra invites Rama to hear the full story of King Sagara, beginning the account of his ancestors.
ramayan::1073.simple_insight: Some lessons arrive through patient listening before they can become clear.
ramayan::1073.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has won Rama’s attention and now begins the ancestral story Rama asked for. He smiles and invites Rama to listen to the full account of King Sagara, opening a long narrative about lineage and sacrifice.
ramayan::1073.modern_relevance: Someone starts telling you the long backstory behind a family pattern, a conflict, or an old promise. You realise the real meaning only comes when you stay and listen all the way through.
ramayan::1073.insight: It shifts attention from the present question to the deeper history that explains it.

ramayan::1074.verse_sanskrit: शङ्करश्वशुरो नाम हिमवानचलोत्तम: । विंध्यपर्वतमासाद्य निरीक्षेते परस्परम् । । 1394 । ।
ramayan::1074.verse_hindi: Sankaras fatherinlaw named Himavan is the greatest mountain. Himavan and Vindhya came close and began looking at one another. (because both are of extreme height and in between them there was no obstruction).
ramayan::1074.english_translation: Himavan, the great mountain and father-in-law of Shankara, and Vindhya came close and looked at each other.
ramayan::1074.translation_literal: शङ्करश्वशुरः (Shankara's father-in-law) / नाम (named) / हिमवान् (Himavan) / अचलोत्तमः (the best of mountains) / विंध्यपर्वतम् (Vindhya mountain) / आसाद्य (having approached) / निरीक्षेते (looked at each other) / परस्परम् (mutually)
ramayan::1074.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1074.essence: The verse simply sets the physical stage for the sacrifice.
ramayan::1074.simple_meaning: Two towering mountains stood so close that they seemed to face each other across the space between them.
ramayan::1074.simple_insight: Some places are shaped by scale alone; the landscape itself becomes part of the story.
ramayan::1074.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is explaining the setting of Sagara's sacrifice to Rama. Before the ritual begins, he points out the vast mountains of Himavan and Vindhya standing opposite each other, framing the land where the event will unfold. It is a geographic detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::1074.modern_relevance: You drive through a narrow mountain pass and suddenly the cliffs feel alive, as if they are watching each other. The verse is that kind of scene-setting: vast, physical, and purely contextual.
ramayan::1074.insight: It trains the mind to notice setting before meaning, so the scene stays clear and grounded.

ramayan::1075.verse_sanskrit: तयोर्मध्ये प्रवृत्तोऽभूद्यज्ञ स्सपुरुषोत्तम । स हि देशो नरव्याघ्र प्रशस्तो यज्ञकर्मणि । । 1395 । ।
ramayan::1075.verse_hindi: O best of men, the sacrifice took place in the region in between these two  mountains. O tiger among men the region was appropriate for conducting sacrificial acts.
ramayan::1075.english_translation: O best of men, the sacrifice took place in the region between those two mountains. O tiger among men, that land was fit for sacrificial rites.
ramayan::1075.translation_literal: तयोः (of those two) / मध्ये (in the middle) / प्रवृत्तः-आभूत् (came to be conducted) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / सः (that) / पुरुषोत्तम (best of men) / सः (that) / हि (indeed) / देशः (region) / नरव्याघ्र (tiger among men) / प्रशस्तः (praised / suitable) / यज्ञकर्मणि (for sacrificial rites)
ramayan::1075.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1075.essence: Right action needs the right ground.
ramayan::1075.simple_meaning: The sacrifice happened in the land between two mountains, and that place was considered especially fit for ritual work.
ramayan::1075.simple_insight: Some places are chosen because they support what must be done well.
ramayan::1075.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is explaining the setting of King Sagara's sacrifice to Rama. He points out the land between two mountains and says it was regarded as especially suitable for ritual action, setting up the larger story of the sacrifice.
ramayan::1075.modern_relevance: You walk into a room that feels right for the work ahead — quiet, steady, undisturbed. Some tasks need the right ground before they can begin.
ramayan::1075.insight: It shifts attention from the ritual itself to the conditions that make right action possible.

ramayan::1076.verse_sanskrit: तस्याश्वचर्यां काकुत्स्थ दृढधन्वा महारथ: । अंशुमानकरोत्तात सगरस्य मते स्थित: । । 1396 । ।
ramayan::1076.verse_hindi: O child, O son of the Kakutsthas, the great charioteer Anshuman (who can fight with eleven thousand charioteers), wielding a strong bow  followed the  sacrificial horse (in order to protect it) in compliance with Sagaras wish.
ramayan::1076.english_translation: O child of the Kakutsthas, the great charioteer Anshuman, strong in battle, followed the sacrificial horse in obedience to Sagara's wish.
ramayan::1076.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / अश्वचर्याम् (the horse's following / guarding) / काकुत्स्थ (O descendant of Kakutstha) / दृढधन्वा (strong-bowed) / महारथः (great charioteer) / अंशुमान् (Anshuman) / अकरोत् (did) / तात (O child) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / मते (in the wish / view) / स्थितः (standing / abiding)
ramayan::1076.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1076.essence: He protects the entrusted task because obedience matters more than display.
ramayan::1076.simple_meaning: Anshuman, a powerful warrior, stayed with the sacrificial horse and protected it because Sagara had ordered it.
ramayan::1076.simple_insight: Some duties are simple: stay with what has been entrusted to you and do not let it be lost.
ramayan::1076.detailed_meaning: The sacrificial horse has been set loose as part of Sagara's ritual. Anshuman, described as a mighty warrior, follows it closely and guards it because he is acting in line with his grandfather's command. The verse is a supporting detail in the larger sacrifice story.
ramayan::1076.modern_relevance: You are asked to watch over something fragile overnight — a child, a project, a promise. The job is not glamorous. It is simply yours to keep safe.
ramayan::1076.insight: It shifts attention from heroics to faithful guardianship of a task already given.

ramayan::1077.verse_sanskrit: तस्य पर्वणि तं यज्ञं यजमानस्य वासव: । राक्षसीं तनुमास्थाय यज्ञीयाश्वमपाहरत् । । 1397 । ।
ramayan::1077.verse_hindi: On the concluding day of the fortnight (full moon day) while the sacrifice was being performed, Vasava (Indra) assuming the form of rakshasa, had stolen away Sagaras sacrificial horse.
ramayan::1077.english_translation: On the concluding day of the fortnight, while the sacrifice was being performed, Vasava assumed the form of a rakshasa and stole away Sagara's sacrificial horse.
ramayan::1077.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / पर्वणि (on the festival day, on the concluding day) / तं (that) / यज्ञं (sacrifice) / यजमानस्य (of the sacrificer) / वासवः (Vasava, Indra) / राक्षसीं (demonic) / तनुम् (form/body) / आस्थाय (having assumed) / यज्ञीय-अश्वम् (sacrificial horse) / अपाहरत् (stole away)
ramayan::1077.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1077.essence: A hidden theft turns a completed rite into the start of disaster.
ramayan::1077.simple_meaning: Indra, taking a disguised form, stole King Sagara's sacrificial horse on the final day of the rite.
ramayan::1077.simple_insight: A sacred effort can be interrupted by forces you did not invite.
ramayan::1077.detailed_meaning: Sagara's horse sacrifice is underway, and the priests are watching for the ritual's completion. On the final day, Indra slips in disguised and steals the horse, setting the entire epic chain of events in motion.
ramayan::1077.modern_relevance: You have nearly finished something important, and then one hidden problem appears and changes everything. The work was real, but the interruption was real too.
ramayan::1077.insight: It shows how one concealed act can derail an entire undertaking and trigger a larger crisis.

ramayan::1078.verse_sanskrit: ह्रियमाणे तु काकुत्स्थ तस्मिन्नश्वे महात्मन: । उपाध्यायगणास्सर्वे यजमानमथाब्रुवन् । । 1398 । ।
ramayan::1078.verse_hindi: O son of the Kakutsthas, when the magnanimous king Sagaras sacrificial horse was stolen away, all the high priests addressing the performer of the sacrifice said:
ramayan::1078.english_translation: O son of the Kakutsthas, when the magnanimous king Sagara's sacrificial horse was stolen away, all the high priests addressing the performer of the sacrifice said:
ramayan::1078.translation_literal: ह्रियमाणे (being carried off) / तु (indeed) / काकुत्स्थ (O son of Kakutstha) / तस्मिन् (that) / अश्वे (horse) / महात्मनः (of the magnanimous one) / उपाध्याय-गणाः (groups of priests) / सर्वे (all) / यजमानम् (to the sacrificer) / अथ (then) / अब्रुवन् (said)
ramayan::1078.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1078.essence: The sacrifice is interrupted, and the priests move to respond.
ramayan::1078.simple_meaning: As the sacrificial horse was being taken away, the priests turned to the king and spoke.
ramayan::1078.simple_insight: Some moments are only the turn before the real crisis begins.
ramayan::1078.detailed_meaning: King Sagara's sacrifice is underway when the chosen horse disappears. The priests, seeing the rite disrupted, immediately turn to the sacrificer and speak. This verse is only the setup for the urgent command that follows.
ramayan::1078.modern_relevance: The meeting is already going wrong when someone notices the missing file, the vanished guest, the broken plan. The real response comes next.
ramayan::1078.insight: It functions as a scene change, not a teaching, preparing the demand that follows.
