ramayan::1079.verse_sanskrit: अयं पर्वणि वेगेन यज्ञियाश्वोऽपनीयते । हर्तारं जहि काकुत्स्थ हयश्चैवोपनीयताम् । । 1399 । ।
ramayan::1079.verse_hindi: O Kakutstha on this auspicious (fullmoon) day the sacrificial horse has been stolen away suddenly and forcibly. Slay the thief and bring back the horse.
ramayan::1079.english_translation: O Kakutstha, on this auspicious full-moon day the sacrificial horse has been stolen away suddenly and forcibly. Slay the thief and bring back the horse.
ramayan::1079.translation_literal: अयं (this) / पर्वणि (on the full-moon day) / वेगेन (swiftly, forcibly) / यज्ञियाश्वः (sacrificial horse) / अपनीयते (is being carried away, stolen) / हर्तारम् (the thief) / जहि (slay) / काकुत्स्थ (O Kakutstha) / हयः (the horse) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / उपनीयताम् (let it be brought back)
ramayan::1079.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1079.essence: A broken rite demands swift repair, not delay.
ramayan::1079.simple_meaning: The priests tell Kakutstha that the sacrificial horse has been stolen during the ritual and must be recovered by killing the thief.
ramayan::1079.simple_insight: Some moments leave no room for hesitation; the right response is immediate and decisive.
ramayan::1079.detailed_meaning: In Sagara’s horse sacrifice, the priests discover that the ritual horse has been seized mid-ceremony. They urgently instruct Kakutstha to kill the thief and restore the horse, because the sacrifice cannot continue while this breach remains.
ramayan::1079.modern_relevance: A critical system crashes halfway through a live launch, and everyone turns to you for the fastest fix. The moment demands action, not reflection.
ramayan::1079.insight: It frames duty as immediate repair of what has been broken, before the larger work can continue.

ramayan::1080.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञच्छिद्रं भवत्येतत्सर्वेषामशिवाय न: । तत्तथा क्रियतां राजन् यथाऽच्छिद्र: क्रतुर्भवेत् । । 13910 । ।
ramayan::1080.verse_hindi: This flaw in sacrifice will be inauspicious for all of us. Hence O king do everything which will ensure flawlessness to this sacrifice.
ramayan::1080.english_translation: This flaw in sacrifice will be inauspicious for all of us. Hence, O king, do everything that will ensure this sacrifice remains flawless.
ramayan::1080.translation_literal: यज्ञच्छिद्रम् (a flaw in sacrifice) / भवति (becomes) / एतत् (this) / सर्वेषाम् (for all) / अशिवाय (for inauspiciousness) / नः (for us) / तत् (therefore) / तथा (thus) / क्रियताम् (let it be done) / राजन् (O king) / यथा (so that) / अच्छिद्रः (flawless) / क्रतुः (sacrifice) / भवेत् (may become)
ramayan::1080.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1080.essence: A small flaw can contaminate a whole act of duty.
ramayan::1080.simple_meaning: A ritual flaw is dangerous for everyone involved, so the king must make sure the sacrifice is completed without any mistake.
ramayan::1080.simple_insight: Carelessness in a sacred duty affects more than you alone.
ramayan::1080.detailed_meaning: The priests see a problem in Sagara's horse sacrifice and warn him that any flaw will bring harm to everyone present. They urge the king to act at once so the ritual can be completed properly.
ramayan::1080.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a ceremony, a presentation, or a family promise, and one careless gap could undo the whole effort. This verse pushes you to protect the integrity of what you started.
ramayan::1080.insight: It shifts attention from finishing fast to finishing cleanly.

ramayan::1081.verse_sanskrit: उपाध्यायवच श्श्रुत्वा तस्मिन् सदसि पार्थिव: । षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह । । 13911 । ।
ramayan::1081.verse_hindi: Having heard the words of the officiating priests, the king (Sagara) addressed his sixty thousand sons in the sacrificial assembly, saying:
ramayan::1081.english_translation: Having heard the words of the officiating priests, the king (Sagara) addressed his sixty thousand sons in the sacrificial assembly, saying:
ramayan::1081.translation_literal: उपाध्याय-वचः (the words of the officiating priests) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तस्मिन् (in that) / सदसि (assembly) / पार्थिवः (the king) / षष्टिं (sixty) / पुत्र-सहस्राणि (thousand sons) / वाक्यम् (speech) / एतत् (this) / उवाच (spoke) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::1081.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1081.essence: The king is about to command a costly response.
ramayan::1081.simple_meaning: King Sagara, after hearing the priests, spoke to his sixty thousand sons in the sacrificial gathering.
ramayan::1081.simple_insight: A command is about to be given. The scene is still moving toward its real meaning.
ramayan::1081.detailed_meaning: In the sacrificial hall, King Sagara listens to the priests and turns to his sixty thousand sons. This verse is only the setup for the order that follows; the pressure of the ritual and the royal command are about to collide.
ramayan::1081.modern_relevance: A manager finishes hearing the problem in a tense meeting and turns to the whole team. The real decision has not come yet; the room is waiting for the next sentence.
ramayan::1081.insight: It frames the moment before action, not the action itself.

ramayan::1082.verse_sanskrit: गतिं पुत्रा: न पश्यामि रक्षसां परुषर्षभा: । मन्त्रपूतैर्महाभागैरास्थितो हि महाक्रतु: । । 13912 । ।
ramayan::1082.verse_hindi: O Best among men, O sons I do not the hand of rakshasas in this as this great sacrifice is consecrated by mantras (to prevent any interruption) and is presided over by eminent priests.
ramayan::1082.english_translation: O sons, best among men, I do not see any way the rakshasas can interfere here, for this great sacrifice has been consecrated by mantras and is being conducted by eminent priests.
ramayan::1082.translation_literal: गतिम् (way) / पुत्राः (sons) / न (not) / पश्यामि (I see) / रक्षसाम् (of rakshasas) / परुषर्षभाः (best among men) / मन्त्रपूतैः (sanctified by mantras) / महाभागैः (by eminent ones) / आस्थितः (presided over) / हि (indeed) / महाक्रतुः (great sacrifice)
ramayan::1082.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1082.essence: What feels fully secured can still hide a fatal gap.
ramayan::1082.simple_meaning: Sagara tells his sons that he sees no way for the rakshasas to disturb the sacrifice, because it has been properly protected by sacred chants and skilled priests.
ramayan::1082.simple_insight: Confidence can make you miss the one danger you never considered.
ramayan::1082.detailed_meaning: King Sagara has already been warned that the sacrifice must remain flawless. After hearing the priests, he reassures his sixty thousand sons that no rakshasa can spoil it. That confidence sets up the command to search the earth.
ramayan::1082.modern_relevance: You lock the office, triple-check the slides, and assume the launch is safe. Then the one thing no checklist covered slips through.
ramayan::1082.insight: It shows how certainty can become blind spots when a task feels fully controlled.

ramayan::1083.verse_sanskrit: तद्गच्छत विचिन्वध्वं पुत्रका: भद्रमस्तु व: । समुद्रमालिनीं सर्वां पृथिवीमनुगच्छत । । 13913 । ।
ramayan::1083.verse_hindi: Therefore my sons, go and search this entire earth surrounded by oceans. May you be safe.
ramayan::1083.english_translation: Therefore, my sons, go and search this entire earth surrounded by oceans. May you be safe.
ramayan::1083.translation_literal: तद् (therefore) / गच्छत (go) / विचिन्वध्वं (search) / पुत्रका: (my sons) / भद्रम् (well-being) / अस्तु (may there be) / व: (for you) / समुद्र-मालिनीम् (encircled by oceans) / सर्वाम् (entire) / पृथिवीम् (earth) / अनुगच्छत (go over / traverse)
ramayan::1083.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1083.essence: A father-king sends his sons across the world to search.
ramayan::1083.simple_meaning: Sagara orders his sons to search the whole earth, promising them safety as they go.
ramayan::1083.simple_insight: A king’s grief can turn into a command that sends others into danger.
ramayan::1083.detailed_meaning: At the sacrifice, Sagara learns that the horse is missing and suspects foul play. He turns to his sixty thousand sons and orders them to search the entire earth, from one ocean to the other, to find it. The verse is a command within a larger chain of action.
ramayan::1083.modern_relevance: A manager sends the whole team into a frantic search after one critical item disappears before a deadline. The order is urgent, but the situation is still unfolding.
ramayan::1083.insight: It pushes the reader to see this as a directive in a larger sequence, not a complete teaching.

ramayan::1084.verse_sanskrit: एकैकयोजनं पुत्रा विस्तारमधिगच्छत । यावत्तुरगसन्दर्श: तावत् खनत मेदिनीम् । तं चैव हयहर्तारं मार्गमाणा ममाज्ञया । । 13914 । ।
ramayan::1084.verse_hindi: O sons, acquiring yojana by yojana the length and breadth of the earth, search for the  thief of the horse. Excavate the earth till the time the horse is found. This is my command.
ramayan::1084.english_translation: O sons, travel across the earth one yojana at a time. Keep digging until you find the horse. This is my command.
ramayan::1084.translation_literal: एकैकयोजनम् (one yojana at a time) / पुत्रा (sons) / विस्तारम् (spread, extent) / अधिगच्छत (go across, traverse) / यावत् (until) / तुरगसन्दर्शः (sight of the horse) / तावत् (until then) / खनत (dig) / मेदिनीम् (the earth) / तम् (that) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / हयहर्तारम् (horse-thief) / मार्गमाणाः (searching for) / मम (my) / आज्ञया (by command)
ramayan::1084.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1084.essence: The search becomes total when what was lost matters this much.
ramayan::1084.simple_meaning: The king orders his sons to search the whole earth and dig everywhere until the stolen horse is found.
ramayan::1084.simple_insight: Some losses are treated like emergencies: you search every corner until the matter is settled.
ramayan::1084.detailed_meaning: King Sagara has lost the sacrificial horse, and his ritual is at risk. He commands his sons to sweep the earth in every direction, digging wherever needed, until the thief and the horse are found. The verse is part of a larger search order, not the main teaching itself.
ramayan::1084.modern_relevance: A missing package, a broken process, and everyone in the office starts tearing through folders, messages, and storage rooms until the mistake is found.
ramayan::1084.insight: It shows relentless pursuit of a problem, not reflection or philosophy.

ramayan::1085.verse_sanskrit: दीक्षित: पौत्रसहितस्सोपाध्यायगणो ह्यहम् । इह स्थास्यामि भद्रं वो यावत्तुरगदर्शनम् । । 13915 । ।
ramayan::1085.verse_hindi: Having been initiated into the sacrifice, I, along with my grandson, Anshuman and  other spiritual preceptors will stay here till such time the horse is found. May you be safe
ramayan::1085.english_translation: Having been initiated into the sacrifice, I, along with my grandson and the other teachers, will stay here until the horse is found. May you be safe.
ramayan::1085.translation_literal: दीक्षित: (initiated into the sacrifice) / पौत्र-सहितः (together with grandson) / स उपाध्याय-गणः (with the group of teachers) / हि (indeed) / अहम् (I) / इह (here) / स्थास्यामि (will stay) / भद्रम् (well-being) / वः (to you) / यावत् (until) / तुरग-दर्शनम् (seeing of the horse)
ramayan::1085.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1085.essence: Some duties are fulfilled by waiting in place.
ramayan::1085.simple_meaning: Sagara says he will remain at the sacrifice site with his grandson and priests until the missing horse is found.
ramayan::1085.simple_insight: A leader does not abandon the ritual or the search; he holds the center while others act.
ramayan::1085.detailed_meaning: King Sagara has sent his sons across the earth to recover the stolen sacrificial horse. Here he stays behind at the ritual site with his grandson and priests, keeping the sacrifice alive until the horse is found. It is a practical command, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::1085.modern_relevance: A parent stays awake in the hospital waiting room while the family searches everywhere else. Someone has to remain steady at the center until the missing thing is found.
ramayan::1085.insight: It shows that responsibility can mean staying put and holding the situation together while others search.

ramayan::1086.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्ता हृष्टमनसो राजपुत्रा महाबला: । जग्मुर्महीतलं राम पितुर्वचनयन्त्रिता: । । 13916 । ।
ramayan::1086.verse_hindi: O Rama thus commanded by Sagara, the highly powerful princes with cheeful hearts departed in obedience to their fathers command in quest of the horse on earth.
ramayan::1086.english_translation: Having been commanded, the mighty princes, their hearts cheerful, set out across the earth, held to their father's word, O Rama.
ramayan::1086.translation_literal: इत्युक्ता (having thus said) / हृष्टमनसः (with joyful minds) / राजपुत्राः (the princes) / महाबलाः (the very powerful) / जग्मुः (went) / महीतलम् (to the earth's surface) / राम (O Rama) / पितुः-वचन-यन्त्रिताः (restrained by their father's word)
ramayan::1086.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1086.essence: They moved because their father's word still bound them.
ramayan::1086.simple_meaning: Sagara's powerful sons left joyfully and obeyed their father's command to search the earth for the stolen horse.
ramayan::1086.simple_insight: Keeping a promise can be a matter of family honor, not just duty.
ramayan::1086.detailed_meaning: Sagara has ordered his sons and grandsons to search the earth for the missing sacrificial horse. After hearing him, the princes depart at once, glad to obey their father's command. The verse marks the beginning of their vast search, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1086.modern_relevance: You leave a family meeting with a task nobody wants, but everyone knows must be done. The decision is bigger than convenience; it belongs to the word your family gave.
ramayan::1086.insight: It shows obedience as inherited responsibility, not reluctant compliance.

ramayan::1087.verse_hindi: O Tiger among men each one of them occupying one yojana in length and breadth of ground, dug up the earth with their nails that were sharp as diamonds.
ramayan::1087.english_translation: Each one, measuring a yojana in length and breadth, tore into the earth with nails as hard as diamonds.
ramayan::1087.translation_literal: योजनायामविस्तारम् (a yojana in length and breadth) / एकैकः (each one) / धरणीतलम् (the surface of the earth) / बिभिदुः (they split / tore open) / परुषव्याघ्र (rough, tiger-like) / वज्रस्पर्शसमैः (equal to diamond-touch) / नखैः (with nails)
ramayan::1087.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1087.essence: Their strength is so vast it seems almost elemental.
ramayan::1087.simple_meaning: The princes were so huge and powerful that each one dug into the earth with nails as hard as diamonds.
ramayan::1087.simple_insight: The scale of the beings matters here: this is pure force, not strategy.
ramayan::1087.detailed_meaning: Sagara's sons have gone down to the earth in search of the sacrificial horse. This verse does not teach a principle; it heightens the scene by showing their immense size and brute strength as they tear into the ground.
ramayan::1087.modern_relevance: A story sometimes pauses on sheer scale before the real action begins — the kind of moment where you feel the force in the room before anyone speaks.
ramayan::1087.insight: It sets the physical stakes by showing overwhelming power at work.

ramayan::1088.verse_sanskrit: शूलैरशनिकल्पैश्च हलैश्चापि सुदारुणै: । भिद्यमाना वसुमती ननाद रघुनन्दन । । 13918 । ।
ramayan::1088.verse_hindi: O Son of the Raghus (Rama) dreadful sounds emanated while the earth was being broken open by  ploughs and lances similar to thunderbolt.
ramayan::1088.english_translation: O Son of the Raghus, dreadful sounds arose as the earth was being broken open by spears and ploughs like thunderbolts.
ramayan::1088.translation_literal: शूलैः (with spears) / अशनिकल्पैः (like thunderbolts) / च (and) / हलैः (with ploughs) / च (and) / अपि (also) / सुदारुणैः (very terrible) / भिद्यमाना (being split) / वसुमती (the earth) / ननाद (roared) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line)
ramayan::1088.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1088.essence: Violence against the earth is heard before it is seen.
ramayan::1088.simple_meaning: The earth groaned as it was violently broken open by powerful tools and weapons.
ramayan::1088.simple_insight: Some acts are so forceful they make the world itself seem to cry out.
ramayan::1088.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara are digging through the earth in their search, each one carving into it with immense force. The ground splits and roars under spears and ploughs. This verse is a vivid sound-image, supporting the larger story rather than carrying a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1088.modern_relevance: A machine bites into frozen ground before dawn, and the whole site shudders with the impact. Some efforts are so forceful they announce themselves before the work is even done.
ramayan::1088.insight: It sharpens the scene into sound, making physical effort feel immense and unstoppable.

ramayan::1089.verse_sanskrit: नागानां मथ्यमानानामसुराणां च राघव । राक्षसानां च दुर्धर्षस्सत्त्वानां निनदोऽभवत् । । 13919 । ।
ramayan::1089.verse_hindi: O descendant of Raghu when the earth was being churned, an irrepressible sound of serpents, demons and rakshasas --of all creatures emerged.
ramayan::1089.english_translation: O descendant of Raghu, when the earth was being churned, a terrible sound arose from serpents, asuras, and rakshasas.
ramayan::1089.translation_literal: नागानां (of serpents) / मथ्यमानानाम् (being churned) / असुराणाम् (of asuras) / च राघव (and, O descendant of Raghu) / राक्षसानाम् (of rakshasas) / च (and) / दुर्धर्षस्सत्त्वानाम् (of irresistible beings) / निनदः (sound) / अभवत् (arose)
ramayan::1089.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1089.essence: The deeper they dig, the louder the buried world answers.
ramayan::1089.simple_meaning: As the earth was churned open, a fierce roar rose from the beings below it.
ramayan::1089.simple_insight: Some forces are so deep that disturbing the ground itself brings them to the surface.
ramayan::1089.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara are tearing into the earth with impossible force. As the layers break, the hidden world below responds with terrifying sound. This verse is part of the same excavation scene, adding the noise of the beings disturbed by the digging.
ramayan::1089.insight: It stays with the scene rather than offering a separate teaching.

ramayan::1090.verse_sanskrit: योजनानां सहस्राणि षष्टिं तु रघुनन्दन । बिभिदुर्धरणीं वीरा: रसातलमनुत्तमम् । । 13920 । ।
ramayan::1090.verse_hindi: O Descendant of the Raghus the heroic sons of Sagara excavated sixty thousand yojanas of earth reaching the nether world (one of the several regions below the earth).
ramayan::1090.english_translation: O Descendant of the Raghus, the heroic sons of Sagara excavated sixty thousand yojanas of earth, reaching the nether world.
ramayan::1090.translation_literal: योजनानां (of yojanas) / सहस्राणि (thousands) / षष्टिं (sixty) / तु (indeed) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line) / बिभिदुः (they split open) / धरणीम् (the earth) / वीराः (the heroic ones) / रसातलम् (the nether world) / अनुत्तमम् (the unsurpassed)
ramayan::1090.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1090.essence: They dug so far that the earth itself gave way.
ramayan::1090.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara dug through sixty thousand yojanas of earth and reached the lower world.
ramayan::1090.simple_insight: Some efforts are so vast they become legend.
ramayan::1090.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the legendary digging of Sagara's sons as they search beneath the earth. The verse is not teaching a principle; it is measuring the impossible scale of their labor and how far their excavation went.
ramayan::1090.modern_relevance: A crew keeps digging through rock long after everyone said the project was impossible. The point is not advice — it is the sheer scale of human persistence.
ramayan::1090.insight: It frames the story as an epic feat, not a moral instruction.

ramayan::1091.verse_sanskrit: एवं पर्वतसम्बाधं जम्बूद्वीपं नृपात्मजा: । खनन्तो नरशार्दूल सर्वत: परिचक्रमु: । । 13921 । ।
ramayan::1091.verse_hindi: O Foremost among men (Rama) the princes while thus excavating Jambu dweepa,  in
ramayan::1091.english_translation: O foremost among men, the princes, while thus excavating Jambudvipa, moved all around it where the mountains blocked them.
ramayan::1091.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / पर्वत-सम्बाधम् (obstructed by mountains) / जम्बूद्वीपम् (Jambudvipa) / नृपात्मजाः (the king's sons, princes) / खनन्तः (digging) / नरशार्दूल (O tiger among men) / सर्वतः (on all sides) / परिचक्रमुः (circled around)
ramayan::1091.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1091.essence: They kept going, even when the earth itself resisted them.
ramayan::1091.simple_meaning: The princes kept digging around Jambudvipa from every side wherever mountains blocked the way.
ramayan::1091.simple_insight: No obstacle stops steady effort when the task is large enough.
ramayan::1091.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara are still at work, digging out the earth in every direction. The land is packed with mountains, so they move around them rather than stop. This is a continuation of the great search for the buried horse.
ramayan::1091.modern_relevance: You hit a wall in a project and keep circling it, testing every angle. Progress sometimes looks like stubborn movement around the obstacle, not through it.
ramayan::1091.insight: It shifts attention from a blocked path to persistent, adaptive effort.

ramayan::1092.verse_hindi: Then the gods together with the gandharvas, asuras and serpents in bewildered minds approached Lord Brahma.
ramayan::1092.english_translation: Then the gods together with the gandharvas, asuras, and serpents, bewildered in mind, approached Brahma.
ramayan::1092.translation_literal: ततः (then) / देवाः (the gods) / सगन्धर्वाः (together with the gandharvas) / सासुराः (together with the asuras) / सहपन्नगाः (together with the serpents) / सम्भ्रान्तमनसः (with bewildered minds) / सर्वे (all) / पितामहम् (Brahma) / उपागमन् (approached)
ramayan::1092.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1092.essence: When confusion spreads everywhere, even the mighty look for a steadier mind.
ramayan::1092.simple_meaning: The gods and other cosmic beings, shaken and confused, went to Brahma for help.
ramayan::1092.simple_insight: Even the powerful seek guidance when the situation goes beyond them.
ramayan::1092.detailed_meaning: The earth has been dug up far beyond ordinary limits by the sons of Sagara. The disturbance is so vast that gods, gandharvas, asuras, and serpents all lose their composure and go together to Brahma, the one who can judge the crisis.
ramayan::1092.modern_relevance: A problem keeps growing until the people who usually act confident finally admit they are out of their depth and call in the person who can see the whole picture.
ramayan::1092.insight: It shifts the mind from private panic to seeking wiser counsel when a crisis exceeds your control.

ramayan::1093.verse_sanskrit: ते प्रसाद्य महात्मानं विषण्णवदनास्तदा । ऊचु: परमसन्त्रस्ता पितामहमिदं वच: । । 13923 । ।
ramayan::1093.verse_hindi: With highly agitated minds and meloncholic faces, all of them approached magnanimous Brahma and having propitiated him said:
ramayan::1093.english_translation: With highly agitated minds and sorrowful faces, all of them approached the great Brahma and, after honoring him, spoke these words:
ramayan::1093.translation_literal: ते (they) / प्रसाद्य (having propitiated) / महात्मानं (the great-souled one) / विषण्णवदनाः (with sorrowful faces) / तदा (then) / ऊचुः (said) / परमसन्त्रस्ताः (greatly frightened) / पितामहम् (to Brahma, the grandsire) / इदम् (this) / वचः (speech)
ramayan::1093.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1093.essence: Fear drives the powerful to ask for help.
ramayan::1093.simple_meaning: The frightened gods, sages, and other beings go to Brahma and speak to him with concern.
ramayan::1093.simple_insight: When a crisis grows too large, even powerful beings seek help from the one who can see the whole picture.
ramayan::1093.detailed_meaning: The gods, gandharvas, asuras, and serpents have just seen the earth being dug up by the sons of Sagara. Alarmed, they gather before Brahma, bow to him, and prepare to explain the danger. This verse is the tense lead-in to their complaint.
ramayan::1093.modern_relevance: A problem keeps growing in a group chat, and everyone finally stops guessing and calls the one person who can untangle the mess. Panic becomes a request for guidance.
ramayan::1093.insight: It shifts you from private worry to seeking wise counsel before the situation worsens.

ramayan::1094.verse_sanskrit: भगवन् पृथिवी सर्वा खन्यते सगरात्मजै: । बहवश्च महात्मानो हन्यन्ते तलवासिन: । । 13924 । ।
ramayan::1094.verse_hindi: O Venerable one the entire earth is being excavated by the sons of Sagara. Many great beings living in the lower worlds are being killed.
ramayan::1094.english_translation: O Venerable one, the entire earth is being excavated by the sons of Sagara. Many great beings living in the lower worlds are being killed.
ramayan::1094.translation_literal: भगवन् (O venerable one) / पृथिवी (earth) / सर्वा (entire) / खन्यते (is being dug up) / सगरात्मजै: (by the sons of Sagara) / बहवः (many) / च (and) / महात्मानः (great beings) / हन्यन्ते (are being killed) / तलवासिनः (those dwelling in the lower worlds)
ramayan::1094.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1094.essence: Single-minded pursuit can become violence when restraint is lost.
ramayan::1094.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara are digging up the earth so widely that beings in the lower worlds are being harmed.
ramayan::1094.simple_insight: A reckless search can spread damage far beyond its original aim.
ramayan::1094.detailed_meaning: The gods have come to Brahma in fear. They are describing the chaos caused by Sagara's sons as they search for the stolen horse. This line is one part of their complaint, showing how their act is disturbing the whole cosmic order.
ramayan::1094.modern_relevance: A frantic search through every drawer, folder, and memory can wreck more than it fixes. What starts as one urgent mission can spill into everything around it.
ramayan::1094.insight: It frames the search as destructive overreach, not heroic effort.

ramayan::1095.verse_sanskrit: अयं यज्ञहरोऽस्माकमनेनाश्वोऽपनीयते । इति ते सर्वभूतानि निघ्नन्ति सगरात्मजा: । । 13925 । ।
ramayan::1095.verse_hindi: This one  is the destroyer of our sacrifice. He  has stolen away our horse saying so the sons of Sagara are slaying all living beings.
ramayan::1095.english_translation: This one is the destroyer of our sacrifice. He has stolen away our horse; saying this, the sons of Sagara are slaying all living beings.
ramayan::1095.translation_literal: अयम् (this one) / यज्ञहरः (destroyer of sacrifice) / अस्माकम् (our) / अनेन (by this one) / अश्वः (horse) / अपनीयते (is being carried away) / इति (thus) / ते (they) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / निघ्नन्ति (are slaying) / सगरात्मजाः (the sons of Sagara)
ramayan::1095.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1095.essence: A false accusation turns sacred purpose into violence.
ramayan::1095.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara believe their sacrificial horse has been stolen, and in anger they begin killing all beings around them.
ramayan::1095.simple_insight: Anger can turn a ritual concern into blind destruction.
ramayan::1095.detailed_meaning: The gods have already gone to Brahma in fear. Now the story shows why: the sons of Sagara, convinced their horse has been taken by the sacrifice's enemy, lash out violently and start killing every being they find.
ramayan::1095.modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a hunt for someone to blame, and the anger spreads faster than the facts. Once outrage takes over, everyone nearby can become collateral damage.
ramayan::1095.insight: It shows how a mistaken accusation can unleash indiscriminate harm.

ramayan::1096.verse_sanskrit: देवतानां वचश्श्रुत्वा भगवान्वै पितामह: । प्रत्युवाच सुसन्त्रस्तान्कृतान्तबलमोहितान् । । 1401 । ।
ramayan::1096.verse_hindi: Having heard the devatas, extremely frightened, and deprived of their sensual perception by the prowess of fate. The adorable grandsire (Brahma) replied:
ramayan::1096.english_translation: Having heard the devas, the adorable grandsire Brahma, frightened and bewildered by the force of fate, replied:
ramayan::1096.translation_literal: देवतानां (of the devas) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / भगवान् (the adorable one) / वै (indeed) / पितामहः (the grandsire) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / सुसन्त्रस्तान् (to the greatly frightened ones) / कृतान्तबलमोहितान् (bewildered by the power of fate)
ramayan::1096.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1096.essence: Even Brahma pauses when fate’s force becomes visible.
ramayan::1096.simple_meaning: Brahma hears the frightened devas and answers them, shaken by the force of fate.
ramayan::1096.simple_insight: Even the highest powers can be startled when a larger force moves.
ramayan::1096.detailed_meaning: The devas have just reported the devastation caused by Sagara's sons. In response, Brahma, the grandsire, speaks to them in fear and confusion. This verse is a bridge into his explanation, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1096.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with panic after a crisis hits, and even the person everyone expects to know the answer pauses before replying.
ramayan::1096.insight: It shifts attention from the immediate alarm to the deeper order behind events.

ramayan::1097.verse_sanskrit: यस्येयं वसुधा कृत्स्ना वासुदेवस्य धीमत: । कापिलं रूपमास्थाय धारयत्यनिशं धराम् । । 1402 । । तस्य कोपाग्निना दग्धा भविष्यन्ति नृपात्मजा: ।
ramayan::1097.verse_hindi: This whole earth belongs to sagacious Vasudeva. He always supports the earth assuming the form of Kapila. The princes will be burnt by the fire of his wrath.
ramayan::1097.english_translation: This whole earth belongs to the wise Vasudeva. He always sustains the earth by assuming the form of Kapila. The princes will be burned by the fire of his anger.
ramayan::1097.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / इयम् (this) / वसुधा (earth) / कृत्स्ना (whole) / वासुदेवस्य (of Vasudeva) / धीमतः (of the wise one) / कापिलम् (Kapila) / रूपम् (form) / आस्थाय (having assumed) / धारयति (sustains) / अनिशम् (always) / धराम् (the earth) / तस्य (of that one) / कोप-अग्निना (by the fire of anger) / दग्धाः (burned) / भविष्यन्ति (will become) / नृपात्मजाः (the princes)
ramayan::1097.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1097.essence: The earth is held by a higher order, and arrogance burns itself up.
ramayan::1097.simple_meaning: The whole earth is sustained by Vasudeva, who appears as Kapila. Because of that power, the princes who acted wrongly will be destroyed by divine anger.
ramayan::1097.simple_insight: Power is not random here; it answers arrogance with consequences.
ramayan::1097.detailed_meaning: The gods have complained to Brahma about the sons of Sagara. Brahma answers that the earth itself belongs to Vasudeva, who sustains it in Kapila’s form. Against that cosmic order, the princes’ violence will be consumed by wrath.
ramayan::1097.modern_relevance: You can feel untouchable after breaking rules in a room full of silence. Then one clear consequence arrives, and the whole atmosphere changes. Some forces were never yours to push around.
ramayan::1097.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing power as human control to seeing it as larger order.

ramayan::1098.verse_sanskrit: पृथिव्याश्चापि निर्भेदोऽदृष्ट एव सनातन: । । 1403 । । सगरस्य च पुत्राणां विनाशोऽदीर्घजीविनाम् ।
ramayan::1098.verse_hindi: The excavation of this earth and the destruction of the short lived sons of Sagara is predestined since eternity.
ramayan::1098.english_translation: The breaking open of the earth and the destruction of Sagara's short-lived sons were fixed from ancient time.
ramayan::1098.translation_literal: पृथिव्याः (of the earth) / च (and) / अपि (also) / निर्भेदः (breaking open, excavation) / अदृष्टः (unseen, unperceived) / एव (indeed) / सनातनः (eternal, ancient) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / च (and) / पुत्राणाम् (of the sons) / विनाशः (destruction) / अदीर्घजीविनाम् (of the short-lived)
ramayan::1098.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1098.essence: What looks sudden was already unfolding long before you noticed.
ramayan::1098.simple_meaning: The earth's opening and the loss of Sagara's sons were already fixed long ago.
ramayan::1098.simple_insight: Some events unfold as part of a larger order, beyond any single person's control.
ramayan::1098.detailed_meaning: Brahma is answering the frightened devas about the ancient cause behind their fear. He says the earth's excavation and the doom of Sagara's sons were already established in the deep order of events, not created by chance in this moment.
ramayan::1098.modern_relevance: You may only see the crisis when it breaks open in front of you, but the forces behind it were set in motion long before your panic began.
ramayan::1098.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate blame to the longer chain of causes already in motion.

ramayan::1099.verse_hindi: O Destroyer of enemies (Rama) On hearing the words of the grandsire (Brahma), the  thirtythree gods, exceedingly delighted returned the way they had come.
ramayan::1099.english_translation: O destroyer of enemies, on hearing the words of the grandsire, the thirty-three gods, greatly delighted, returned the way they had come.
ramayan::1099.translation_literal: पितामहवचः (the grandsire's words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / त्रयस्त्रिंशत् (thirty-three) / अरिन्दम (enemy-destroyer) / देवा: (the gods) / परमसंहृष्टा: (greatly delighted) / पुनः (again) / जग्मुः (went) / यथागतम् (as they had come)
ramayan::1099.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1099.essence: The gods leave because the burden has been understood.
ramayan::1099.simple_meaning: After Brahma spoke, the thirty-three gods left happily, having heard that the earth's burden would be addressed.
ramayan::1099.simple_insight: Relief comes when a burden is finally placed into capable hands.
ramayan::1099.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just explained the fate of Sagara's sons and the earth's disturbance. The thirty-three gods listen, feel reassured, and depart in joy. This verse simply closes that celestial consultation and moves the story onward.
ramayan::1099.modern_relevance: You finally hear from the person who can actually fix the problem. The room loosens, the tension drops, and everyone leaves knowing the next step is no longer theirs to carry.
ramayan::1099.insight: It marks the end of divine consultation, not the beginning of a teaching.

ramayan::1100.verse_sanskrit: सगरस्य च पुत्राणां प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनाम् । । 1405 । । पृथिव्यां भिद्यमानायां निर्घातसमनिस्वन: ।
ramayan::1100.verse_hindi: A sound like the resembling of thunder emanated while the earth was being riven by the noble sons of Sagara.
ramayan::1100.english_translation: A sound like thunder arose as the earth was being split by the noble sons of Sagara.
ramayan::1100.translation_literal: सगरस्य (of Sagara) / च (and) / पुत्राणां (of the sons) / प्रादुरासीत् (arose) / महात्मनाम् (of the noble ones) / पृथिव्यां (in the earth) / भिद्यमानायाम् (while being split) / निर्घातसमनिस्वनः (a sound like thunder)
ramayan::1100.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1100.essence: The breakthrough arrives with force, but it is only one step in a larger fate.
ramayan::1100.simple_meaning: As Sagara's noble sons broke through the earth, a thunder-like sound filled the scene.
ramayan::1100.simple_insight: The moment feels immense, but it is still only part of a larger unfolding.
ramayan::1100.detailed_meaning: Brahma has already spoken about the fate of Sagara's line. Now the sons themselves break through the earth, and the world answers with a thunderous sound. This verse is a vivid bridge between the divine pronouncement and the next action.
ramayan::1100.modern_relevance: A wall finally gives way after hours of drilling, and the whole room shudders. The breakthrough is real, but it is still only the middle of the story.
ramayan::1100.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the larger chain of cause and consequence around it.

ramayan::1101.verse_sanskrit: ततो भित्वा महीं सर्वे कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम् । । 1406 । । सहिता स्सगरास्सर्वे पितरं वाक्यमब्रुवन् । 0
ramayan::1101.verse_hindi: Afterwards, all the sons of Sagara, having riven the earth approached their father and circumamulating him said:
ramayan::1101.english_translation: Afterwards, all the sons of Sagara, having riven the earth, approached their father and, circling him respectfully, said:
ramayan::1101.translation_literal: ततः (then) / भित्वा (having broken) / महीम् (the earth) / सर्वे (all) / कृत्वा (having done) / चाभिप्रदक्षिणम् (respectful circumambulation) / सहिताः (together) / सगराः (the sons of Sagara) / सर्वे (all) / पितरम् (to their father) / वाक्यम् (words) / अब्रुवन् (said)
ramayan::1101.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1101.essence: The search has reached its next turning point.
ramayan::1101.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara broke through the earth, returned together, and spoke respectfully to their father.
ramayan::1101.simple_insight: The scene is moving forward, but no teaching is complete yet.
ramayan::1101.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara have dug through the earth in their search. After breaking through, they return in a respectful circle to their father and report back. This verse mainly moves the story into the next revelation.
ramayan::1101.modern_relevance: You finish the hard part, walk back to the person waiting, and report what you found. The real answer is still just ahead.
ramayan::1101.insight: It shifts attention from the search itself to the report that follows.

ramayan::1102.verse_sanskrit: परिक्रान्ता मही सर्वा सत्त्ववन्तश्च सूदिता: । । 1407 । । देवदानवरक्षांसि पिशाचोरगकिन्नरा: । न च पश्यामहेऽश्वं तमश्वहर्तारमेव च । । 1408 । । किं करिष्याम भद्रं ते बुद्धिरत्र विचार्यताम् ।
ramayan::1102.verse_hindi: The entire earth was ransacked. Mighty devatas, demons, rakshasas, pisachas, uragas and kinnaras were killed. (Yet) we could neither see the horse nor the thief of the horse. Reflect over this matter and direct us. Prosperity to you
ramayan::1102.english_translation: The whole earth has been searched. Mighty devas, demons, rakshasas, pisachas, uragas, and kinnaras have been slain. Yet we still cannot find the horse or the horse thief. Think over this matter and guide us. May you prosper.
ramayan::1102.translation_literal: परिक्रान्ता (circled/searching) / मही (earth) / सर्वा (entire) / सत्त्ववन्तः (powerful beings) / च (and) / सूदिताः (slain) / देवदानवरक्षांसि (devas-danavas-rakshasas) / पिशाचोरगकिन्नरा: (pisachas-uragas-kinnaras) / न (not) / च (and) / पश्यामहे (we see) / अश्वं (horse) / तम् (that) / अश्वहर्तारम् (horse-thief) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / किं (what) / करिष्याम (shall we do) / भद्रं ते (may good be to you) / बुद्धिः (judgment) / अत्र (here) / विचार्यताम् (be considered)
ramayan::1102.speaker: Sagara's sons
ramayan::1102.essence: Force alone cannot recover what confusion has hidden.
ramayan::1102.simple_meaning: Sagara's sons have searched everywhere and destroyed many powerful beings, but they still cannot find the stolen horse. They ask their father what to do next.
ramayan::1102.simple_insight: Even huge effort can fail without clear direction.
ramayan::1102.detailed_meaning: Sagara's sons return after tearing through the earth and killing countless beings in their search for the sacrificial horse. They stand before their father empty-handed, admitting failure and asking him to think through the next step.
ramayan::1102.modern_relevance: You have chased the same missing thing through every corner of your life and still come back empty. At some point, brute force stops helping and clear judgment has to begin.
ramayan::1102.insight: It shifts the mind from blind force to thoughtful reassessment.

ramayan::1103.verse_sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुत्राणां राजसत्तम: । । 1409 । । समन्युरब्रवीद्वाक्यं सगरो रघुनन्दन ।
ramayan::1103.verse_hindi: O Rama incensed to fury at the words of his sons, magnanimous king Sagara replied:
ramayan::1103.english_translation: Hearing the words of his sons, the best of kings Sagara, filled with anger, spoke to them, O Rama.
ramayan::1103.translation_literal: तेषाम् (of them) / तत्-वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / पुत्राणाम् (of the sons) / राज-सत्तमः (best of kings) / समन्युः (angrily) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / वाक्यम् (words) / सगरः (Sagara) / रघुनन्दन (O Rama)
ramayan::1103.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1103.essence: A king’s anger turns a setback into the next order.
ramayan::1103.simple_meaning: Sagara heard his sons and answered in anger.
ramayan::1103.simple_insight: Anger can sharpen a reply, but it also narrows the mind.
ramayan::1103.detailed_meaning: Sagara’s sons have searched the earth for the stolen horse and returned empty-handed. Hearing their report, the king’s temper rises. This verse only sets up his command in the next line, so it functions as a bridge in the story.
ramayan::1103.modern_relevance: You get a disappointing update after a long search, and your first instinct is to snap. The moment before you answer decides the tone of everything that follows.
ramayan::1103.insight: It marks the turn from failed effort to an angry command.

ramayan::1104.verse_sanskrit: भूय: खनत भद्रं वो निर्भिद्य वसुधातलम् । । 14010 । । अश्वहर्तारमासाद्य कृतार्थाश्च निवर्तथ ।
ramayan::1104.verse_hindi: Rive the earth again and excavate, capture the one who has stolen the horse and return after having accomplished the purpose.  Safety to you
ramayan::1104.english_translation: Rive the earth again and excavate; find the horse-thief, and return only after you have accomplished your task. Be safe.
ramayan::1104.translation_literal: भूयः (again) / खनत (dig) / भद्रम् (safety; be well) / वः (to you) / निर्भिद्य (having split open) / वसुधातलम् (the surface of the earth) / अश्वहर्तारम् (the horse-thief) / आसाद्य (having found; having reached) / कृतार्थाः (those who have achieved the aim) / च (and) / निवर्तथ (return)
ramayan::1104.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1104.essence: Effort matters most when the task is still unfinished.
ramayan::1104.simple_meaning: Sagara orders his sons to keep digging through the earth until they find the stolen horse, and only then come back.
ramayan::1104.simple_insight: There is dignity in finishing what you were sent to do.
ramayan::1104.detailed_meaning: King Sagara, angry that his sacrificial horse is missing, sends his sons back to the search with one clear command: keep digging, find the thief, and do not return empty-handed. The verse turns anger into relentless action.
ramayan::1104.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a hard fix, tempted to stop and call it enough. But the problem is still there, and you know it. This verse speaks to finishing the search, not just starting it.
ramayan::1104.insight: It shifts the mind from frustration to sustained, goal-directed action.

ramayan::1105.verse_sanskrit: पितुर्वचनमासाद्य सगरस्य महात्मन: । । 14011 । । षष्टि: पुत्रसहस्राणि रसातलमभिद्रवन् ।
ramayan::1105.verse_hindi: Receiving the command of their father, the magnanimous Sagara, his sixty thousand sons ran towards Rasatala (nether world).
ramayan::1105.english_translation: Receiving the command of their father, the magnanimous Sagara, his sixty thousand sons ran towards Rasatala, the nether world.
ramayan::1105.translation_literal: पितुर्वचनम् (father's command) / आसाद्य (having received) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / महात्मनः (of the magnanimous one) / षष्टिः (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / रसातलम् (Rasatala, the nether world) / अभिद्रवन् (ran toward)
ramayan::1105.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1105.essence: Command received, they rushed forward without pause.
ramayan::1105.simple_meaning: Sagara's sixty thousand sons obey their father at once and rush toward the underworld.
ramayan::1105.simple_insight: Obedience can become blind momentum when no one stops to question the command.
ramayan::1105.detailed_meaning: Sagara has ordered his sons to search beneath the earth for the stolen horse. They do not hesitate or reflect; they surge toward Rasatala as one force. This is a movement scene, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::1105.modern_relevance: A group chat lights up with one urgent instruction, and everyone moves before asking why. The speed feels impressive until you realize no one checked the cost.
ramayan::1105.insight: It shows how collective action can become automatic when authority is obeyed without reflection.

ramayan::1106.verse_sanskrit: खन्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन् ददृशु: पर्वतोपमम् । । 14012 । । दिशागजं विरूपाक्षं धारयन्तं महीतलम् ।
ramayan::1106.verse_hindi: Then while they were excavating the region they beheld the elephant of the quarter named Virupaksha equal in size to a mountain, supporting the earth.
ramayan::1106.english_translation: Then while they were excavating the region they beheld the elephant of the quarter named Virupaksha, equal in size to a mountain, supporting the earth.
ramayan::1106.translation_literal: खन्यमाने (while being excavated) / ततस् (then) / तस्मिन् (in that) / ददृशुः (they saw) / पर्वतोपमम् (mountain-like) / दिशागजम् (the elephant of the quarter) / विरूपाक्षम् (Virupaksha) / धारयन्तम् (supporting) / महीतलम् (the earth's surface)
ramayan::1106.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1106.essence: The search stops when you meet the force holding the ground itself.
ramayan::1106.simple_meaning: As the ground was dug up, the sons of Sagara saw a huge guardian elephant named Virupaksha holding up the earth.
ramayan::1106.simple_insight: Some things are larger than your search, and they hold the world together while you do not notice.
ramayan::1106.detailed_meaning: Sagara's sons are digging through the earth in their search for the stolen horse. Instead of finding what they want, they encounter Virupaksha, a colossal guardian elephant supporting the earth itself. The scene pauses the chase to show the scale of the world beneath them.
ramayan::1106.modern_relevance: You keep digging for the answer you want, then discover the situation is held together by forces far bigger than your search.
ramayan::1106.insight: It shifts attention from the object of pursuit to the hidden structure already sustaining everything.

ramayan::1107.verse_sanskrit: सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं रघुनन्दन । । 14013 । । शिरसा धारयामास विरूपाक्षो महागज: ।
ramayan::1107.verse_hindi: O descendant of Raghu the  mighty elephant Virupaksha was holding on its head the entire earth with its mountains and forests.
ramayan::1107.english_translation: O descendant of Raghu, the mighty elephant Virupaksha was holding on its head the entire earth with its mountains and forests.
ramayan::1107.translation_literal: सपर्वतवनाम् (with mountains and forests) / कृत्स्नाम् (entire) / पृथिवीम् (earth) / रघुनन्दन (O descendant of Raghu) / शिरसा (with the head) / धारयामास (was holding) / विरूपाक्षः (Virupaksha) / महागजः (mighty elephant)
ramayan::1107.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1107.essence: A single movement by the guardian elephant can shake the world.
ramayan::1107.simple_meaning: The giant elephant Virupaksha is said to hold the whole earth, along with its mountains and forests, on its head.
ramayan::1107.simple_insight: It gives a mythic image of vast, impossible strength.
ramayan::1107.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara have dug deep into the lower regions and now see Virupaksha, a colossal guardian elephant. The verse describes him as bearing the whole earth, setting up the next line where his head movement is said to cause earthquakes.
ramayan::1107.insight: It builds a cosmic scale for the coming disturbance.

ramayan::1108.verse_sanskrit: यदा पर्वणि काकुत्स्थ विश्रमार्थं महागज: । । 14014 । । खेदाच्चालयते शीर्षं भूमिकम्पस्तदाभवेत् ।
ramayan::1108.verse_hindi: O descendant of Kakustha when that mighty elephant shakes its head for rest from weariness on certain sacred days earthquake occurs.
ramayan::1108.english_translation: O descendant of Kakustha, when that mighty elephant shakes its head for rest from weariness on sacred days, an earthquake occurs.
ramayan::1108.translation_literal: यदा (when) / पर्वणि (on a sacred day) / काकुत्स्थ (O descendant of Kakustha) / विश्रमार्थं (for rest) / महागजः (the mighty elephant) / खेदात् (from weariness) / अालयते (shakes) / शीर्षम् (the head) / भूमिकम्पः (earthquake) / तत् (then) / आभवेत् (occurs)
ramayan::1108.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1108.essence: What seems immovable can tremble when its burden shifts.
ramayan::1108.simple_meaning: A giant elephant supports the earth. When it shakes its head from fatigue, the earth trembles.
ramayan::1108.simple_insight: Even cosmic stability can be pictured as resting on something that grows tired.
ramayan::1108.detailed_meaning: Rama and the others have gone beneath the earth and discovered Virupaksha, a colossal guardian elephant holding up the world. This verse explains that its brief movement from weariness is what causes earthquakes, deepening the wonder of the scene.
ramayan::1108.modern_relevance: A system can look solid for years, then wobble because the thing holding it together is exhausted. Sometimes the tremor is not random at all.
ramayan::1108.insight: It turns a natural disaster into a reminder that hidden supports matter.

ramayan::1109.verse_sanskrit: तं ते प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा दिशापालं महागजम् । । 14015 । । मानयन्तो हि ते राम जग्मुर्भित्त्वा रसातलम् ।
ramayan::1109.verse_hindi: O Rama having circumabulated and honoured that mighty elephant, the protector of the quarter they reached the Rasatala by riving the earth.
ramayan::1109.english_translation: O Rama, having circumambulated and honoured that mighty elephant, the guardian of the quarter, they reached Rasatala by riving the earth.
ramayan::1109.translation_literal: तम् (that) / ते (they) / प्रदक्षिणम् (circumambulation) / कृत्वा (having done) / दिशापालम् (guardian of a direction) / महागजम् (mighty elephant) / मानयन्तः (honouring) / हि (indeed) / ते (they) / राम (O Rama) / जग्मुः (went) / भित्त्वा (splitting) / रसातलम् (the nether region)
ramayan::1109.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1109.essence: The descent continues after a gesture of respect.
ramayan::1109.simple_meaning: They honoured a mighty elephant, then broke through the earth and went down into the lower world.
ramayan::1109.simple_insight: Some passages are pure movement: honour first, then descent.
ramayan::1109.detailed_meaning: Rama is being told of a strange underworld scene: a colossal elephant stands as guardian, and the beings below show it respect before continuing their journey. The verse is a descriptive link in a larger sequence of subterranean exploration, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1109.insight: It advances the journey by showing reverence before crossing into deeper territory.

ramayan::1110.verse_sanskrit: तत: पूर्वां दिशं भित्त्वा दक्षिणां बिभिदु: पुन: । । 14016 । । दक्षिणस्यामपि दिशि ददृशुस्ते महागजम् । महापद्मं महात्मानं सुमहत्पर्वतोपमम् । । 14017 । । शिरसा धारयन्तं ते विस्मयं जग्मुरुत्तमम् ।
ramayan::1110.verse_hindi: Subsequently, having dug the eastern region, they went on to southern and dug it too. In the southern region, they beheld a mighty elephant, magnanimous Mahapadma, resembling a great mountain. To their astonishment, they saw that elephant holding
ramayan::1110.english_translation: Then they dug through the eastern direction and again through the southern. In the southern direction they saw a mighty elephant, the great-souled Mahapadma, huge as a mountain, and they were struck with wonder at the sight of it holding up the earth.
ramayan::1110.translation_literal: तत: (then) / पूर्वाम् (eastern) / दिशम् (direction) / भित्त्वा (having pierced or dug through) / दक्षिणाम् (southern) / बिभिदुः (they dug through) / पुनः (again) / दक्षिणस्याम् (in the southern) / अपि (also) / दिशि (in the direction) / ददृशुः (they saw) / ते (they) / महागजम् (mighty elephant) / महापद्मम् (Mahapadma) / महात्मानम् (great-souled one) / सुमहत् (very great) / पर्वतोपमम् (mountain-like) / शिरसा (with its head) / धारयन्तम् (holding up) / ते (they) / विस्मयम् (wonder) / जग्मुः (went into) / उत्तमम् (greatest)
ramayan::1110.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1110.essence: Even wonder can be only a step deeper into the mystery.
ramayan::1110.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara keep digging through the directions and discover another giant elephant holding up the earth. The scene is awe-filled, but it is still part of the larger search.
ramayan::1110.simple_insight: Some moments are meant to deepen wonder, not deliver the final answer.
ramayan::1110.detailed_meaning: Sagara's sons have already gone below the earth in search of the lost horse. They keep breaking through one direction after another and now discover Mahapadma, a vast elephant supporting the world. Their amazement grows, but the quest is still unfolding.
ramayan::1110.modern_relevance: You keep pushing through one layer after another, sure the next breakthrough will explain everything. Instead, you find another hidden support beneath the surface.
ramayan::1110.insight: It shows that discovery can reveal more structure, not immediate resolution.

ramayan::1111.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा सगरस्य महात्मन: । । 14018 । । षष्टि: पुत्रसहस्राणि पश्चिमां बिभिदुर्दिशम् ।
ramayan::1111.verse_hindi: Thereafter, illustrious Sagaras sixty thousand sons, having circumabulated the elephant of the western region dug up that region.
ramayan::1111.english_translation: Thereafter, the sixty thousand illustrious sons of Sagara, after circumambulating the great elephant, broke open the western direction.
ramayan::1111.translation_literal: तत: (thereafter) / प्रदक्षिणं (circumambulation) / कृत्वा (having done) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / महात्मन: (of the illustrious one) / षष्टि: (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / पश्चिमां (western) / बिभिदुः (broke open) / दिशम् (direction)
ramayan::1111.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1111.essence: The search continues as the sons break through another direction.
ramayan::1111.simple_meaning: Sagara's sixty thousand sons moved on to the western direction, honoring the guardian elephant there before breaking through the earth.
ramayan::1111.simple_insight: No inner lesson is being taught here; the verse simply carries the action forward.
ramayan::1111.detailed_meaning: The search continues underground. After finding the guardian elephants in other directions, Sagara's sons reach the western quarter, show respect, and then break through it too. This is another step in the larger descent that is still unfolding.
ramayan::1111.insight: It advances the sequence of discovery and digging without pausing for reflection.

ramayan::1112.verse_sanskrit: पश्चिमायामपि दिशि महान्तमचलोपमम् । । 14019 । । दिशागजं सौमनसं ददृशुस्ते महाबला: ।
ramayan::1112.verse_hindi: Possessed of great strength, they beheld also in the western quarter a  great elephant of the quarter named Saumanasa resembling a mountain.
ramayan::1112.english_translation: Possessed of great strength, they beheld also in the western quarter a great elephant of the quarter named Saumanasa, resembling a mountain.
ramayan::1112.translation_literal: पश्चिमायाम् (in the western quarter) / अपि (also) / दिशि (in the direction) / महान्तम् (great) / अचलोपमम् (mountain-like) / दिशागजम् (elephant of the quarter) / सौमनसम् (Saumanasa) / ददृशुः (they saw) / ते (they) / महाबलाः (the very strong ones)
ramayan::1112.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1112.essence: Each new direction reveals another guardian, not the end of the search.
ramayan::1112.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara kept digging and reached the western direction, where they found another great elephant-like guardian of that quarter.
ramayan::1112.simple_insight: Some journeys are about discovery, not conclusion.
ramayan::1112.detailed_meaning: Sagara’s sixty thousand sons have already crossed east and south, digging through the earth in search of the lost horse. In the western direction they find another immense quarter-elephant, Saumanasa, so the search continues without resolution.
ramayan::1112.modern_relevance: You keep pushing through one obstacle after another, thinking the next one will be the last. Instead, you find another barrier and have to keep going.
ramayan::1112.insight: It keeps the search moving forward, showing that each discovery leads to another step.

ramayan::1113.verse_sanskrit: तं ते प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पृष्ट्वा चापि निरामयम् । खनन्त स्समुपक्रान्ता दिशं हैमवतीं तत: । । 14020 । ।
ramayan::1113.verse_hindi: Having paid homage and enquiring as to his wellbeing, they arrived at the northern  region by digging the earth.
ramayan::1113.english_translation: Having paid homage and asking after his wellbeing, they then began digging toward the northern quarter.
ramayan::1113.translation_literal: तम् (him) / ते (they) / प्रदक्षिणं (circumambulation) / कृत्वा (having done) / पृष्ट्वा (having asked) / च (and) / अपि (also) / निरामयम् (free from illness, well) / खनन्तः (digging) / समुपक्रान्ताः (having set out) / दिशम् (direction, quarter) / हैमवतीम् (northern, snowy) / ततः (then)
ramayan::1113.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1113.essence: Respect comes first, then the work continues.
ramayan::1113.simple_meaning: The sons respectfully checked on the being they found, then continued digging northward.
ramayan::1113.simple_insight: Even a task driven by force can still begin with respect.
ramayan::1113.detailed_meaning: The sixty thousand sons of Sagara have already found one quarter-guardian elephant and moved on. After circling it and asking after its wellbeing, they keep digging toward the northern direction. The verse is a bridge in the sequence, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1113.modern_relevance: You can move through a task with force and still pause long enough to show respect before continuing.
ramayan::1113.insight: It shows that ritual respect can coexist with relentless action.

ramayan::1114.verse_sanskrit: उत्तरस्यां रघुश्रेष्ठ ददृशुर्हिमपाण्डुरम् । । 14021 । । भद्रं भद्रेण वपुषा धारयन्तं महीमिमाम् ।
ramayan::1114.verse_hindi: O Rama in the northern region, they beheld an auspicious elephant named Bhadra, who was white like snow, was holding that quater.
ramayan::1114.english_translation: In the northern region, O Rama, they saw an auspicious elephant named Bhadra, white like snow, upholding that quarter with a beautiful form.
ramayan::1114.translation_literal: उत्तरस्याम् (in the northern) / रघुश्रेष्ठ (O best of the Raghu line) / ददृशुः (they saw) / हिमपाण्डुरम् (snow-white) / भद्रम् (auspicious Bhadra) / भद्रेण (with beautiful) / वपुषा (form) / धारयन्तम् (upholding) / महीम् इमाम् (this earth / this quarter)
ramayan::1114.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1114.essence: A directional landmark is being named before the journey continues.
ramayan::1114.simple_meaning: They saw the northern guardian elephant Bhadra, white as snow, standing as the protector of that direction.
ramayan::1114.simple_insight: Some verses simply paint the world around the action, and this is one of them.
ramayan::1114.detailed_meaning: The sixty thousand sons are moving through the directions beneath the earth, paying respect to each guardian elephant before continuing. This verse only identifies the northern one, Bhadra, as the next landmark in their descent.
ramayan::1114.modern_relevance: You are reading a map, not a message. The scene is moving forward, and this line simply marks where the travelers are now.
ramayan::1114.insight: It keeps the narrative grounded in place and sequence rather than teaching a separate principle.

ramayan::1115.verse_sanskrit: समालभ्य तत स्सर्वे कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम् । । 14022 । । षष्टि: पुत्रसहस्राणि बिभिदुर्वसुधातलम् ।
ramayan::1115.verse_hindi: Then all sixty thousand sons having touched the elephant and circumambulated it, penetrated the earth.
ramayan::1115.english_translation: Then all sixty thousand sons, after touching the elephant and circumambulating it, penetrated the earth.
ramayan::1115.translation_literal: समालभ्य (having touched) / ततः (then) / सर्वे (all) / कृत्वा (having done) / च (and) / एनम् (it) / प्रदक्षिणम् (circumambulation) / षष्टिः (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / बिभिदुः (pierced) / वसुधातलम् (the earth's surface)
ramayan::1115.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1115.essence: Respect can still lead you deeper into a fateful search.
ramayan::1115.simple_meaning: The sixty thousand sons honored the elephant and then went down into the earth.
ramayan::1115.simple_insight: Some actions are only steps in a larger, irreversible chain.
ramayan::1115.detailed_meaning: Sagara's sons have found the sacred elephant in the north. After showing it respect, the sixty thousand continue the strange quest by entering the earth itself. The verse is a movement in the story, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1115.modern_relevance: You follow a clue one step farther than you meant to, and suddenly the whole day has changed direction.
ramayan::1115.insight: It keeps the focus on sequence and consequence, not on a separate lesson.

ramayan::1116.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा सागरा: प्रथितां दिशम् । । 14023 । । रोषादभ्यखनन् सर्वे पृथिवीं सगरात्मजा: ।
ramayan::1116.verse_hindi: Subsequently, the sons of Sagara, having gone towards the celebrated northeastern region began to dig with wrath.
ramayan::1116.english_translation: Then the sons of Sagara went toward the famed northeastern direction and, in anger, began to dig the earth.
ramayan::1116.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रागुत्तराम् (toward the northeast) / गत्वा (having gone) / सागरा: (the sons of Sagara) / प्रथिताम् (famed) / दिशम् (direction) / रोषात् (in anger) / अभ्यखनन् (dug up) / सर्वे (all) / पृथिवीम् (the earth) / सगरात्मजा: (the sons of Sagara)
ramayan::1116.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1116.essence: Anger made them dig harder, not see clearer.
ramayan::1116.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara marched northeast and started digging the earth in anger.
ramayan::1116.simple_insight: Uncontrolled anger can drive people into blind, destructive action.
ramayan::1116.detailed_meaning: The sixty thousand sons of Sagara have just broken through the earth in search of the missing horse. Moving toward the northeastern region, they keep digging furiously, unaware that this search is leading them into disaster.
ramayan::1116.modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a hunt for someone to blame, and everyone keeps digging deeper instead of stopping. Rage feels productive until it destroys the ground beneath you.
ramayan::1116.insight: It shows how anger narrows judgment and turns effort into self-defeat.

ramayan::1117.verse_sanskrit: ते तु सर्वे महात्मानो भीमवेगा महाबला: । । 14024 । । ददृशु: कपिलं तत्र वासुदेवं सनातनम् । हयं च तस्य देवस्य चरन्तमविदूरत: । । 14025 । । प्रहर्षमतुलं प्राप्तास्सर्वे ते रघुनन्दन ।
ramayan::1117.verse_hindi: Great sons of  Sagara terribly swiftfooted and exceedingly powerful beheld the eternal Visnu in (sage) Kapila and not far away from him the horse grazing. O descendant of Raghu they all experienced unparalleled joy.
ramayan::1117.english_translation: The mighty sons of Sagara saw the eternal Vishnu in sage Kapila, and nearby the horse grazing. O descendant of Raghu, they all felt unmatched joy.
ramayan::1117.translation_literal: ते (they) / तु (indeed) / सर्वे (all) / महात्मानः (great-souled) / भीमवेगाः (terribly swift) / महाबलाः (very powerful) / ददृशुः (saw) / कपिलम् (Kapila) / तत्र (there) / वासुदेवम् (Vasudeva) / सनातनम् (eternal) / हयम् (horse) / च (and) / तस्य (his) / देवस्य (of the radiant being) / चरन्तम् (grazing) / अविदूरतः (not far away) / प्रहर्षम् (joy) / अतुलम् (unmatched) / प्राप्ताः (having attained) / सर्वे (all) / ते (they)
ramayan::1117.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1117.essence: Joy can arrive at the exact edge of catastrophe.
ramayan::1117.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara find both Kapila and the missing horse, and their joy rises at once.
ramayan::1117.simple_insight: A long search can end in a single instant of relief.
ramayan::1117.detailed_meaning: The sixty thousand sons of Sagara have forced their way underground in search of the sacrificial horse. At last they see Kapila and the horse nearby, and joy floods them before disaster strikes.
ramayan::1117.modern_relevance: You finally spot what you were chasing after weeks of strain. Relief hits first, before you notice the danger still waiting in the room.
ramayan::1117.insight: It marks the moment search turns into false triumph, just before ruin.

ramayan::1118.verse_sanskrit: ते तं हयवरं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणा: । । 14026 । । खनित्रलाङ्गलधरा नानावृक्षशिलाधरा: । अभ्यधावन्त सङ्क्रुद्धास्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रुवन् । । 14027 । ।
ramayan::1118.verse_hindi: They recognised that best of horses. Their eyes were red with anger. Armed with spades, ploughshares and every kind of tree and stone and furious with wrath, they rushed towards Kapila shouting, wait, wait
ramayan::1118.english_translation: They recognised that best of horses. Their eyes were red with anger. Armed with spades, ploughshares and every kind of tree and stone and furious with wrath, they rushed towards Kapila shouting, wait, wait.
ramayan::1118.translation_literal: ते (they) / तं (that) / हयवरं (best horse) / ज्ञात्वा (having recognized) / क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणा: (with eyes agitated by anger) / खनित्रलाङ्गलधरा: (bearing spades and ploughshares) / नानावृक्षशिलाधरा: (bearing various trees and stones) / अभ्यधावन्त (they rushed) / सङ्क्रुद्धा: (enraged) / तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति (saying "stop, stop") / च (and) / अब्रुवन् (they said)
ramayan::1118.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1118.essence: Rage makes you charge before you understand what you see.
ramayan::1118.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara see their missing horse, lose control, and charge forward in rage, shouting for Kapila to stop.
ramayan::1118.simple_insight: Anger narrows the mind until even a sacred search becomes a blind rush.
ramayan::1118.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara have already found the horse and now see it near Kapila. Instead of pausing to understand what they are seeing, they surge forward with tools and weapons in hand, driven by fury. The scene shows how quickly outrage can turn a search into a disaster.
ramayan::1118.modern_relevance: You spot the email that feels unfair, and your pulse jumps before your mind does. In that second, you are already moving toward a fight you have not understood.
ramayan::1118.insight: It shows how anger can override judgment and turn perception into attack.

ramayan::1119.verse_sanskrit: अस्माकं त्वं हि तुरगं यज्ञीयं हृतवानसि । दुर्मेधस्त्वं हि सम्प्राप्तान् विद्धि नस्सगरात्मजान् । । 14028 । ।
ramayan::1119.verse_hindi: O Wickedminded one you have stolen our sacrificial horse. Know that those of us who have come here are the sons of Sagara.
ramayan::1119.english_translation: O wicked-minded one, you have stolen our sacrificial horse. Know that those who have come here are the sons of Sagara.
ramayan::1119.translation_literal: अस्माकम् (our) / त्वम् (you) / हि (indeed) / तुरगम् (horse) / यज्ञीयम् (fit for sacrifice) / हृतवानसि (you have stolen) / दुर्मेधः (wicked-minded one) / त्वम् (you) / हि (indeed) / सम्प्राप्तान् (those who have arrived) / विद्धि (know) / नः (us) / सगरात्मजान् (sons of Sagara)
ramayan::1119.speaker: Sagara's sons
ramayan::1119.essence: Anger makes accusation feel like certainty.
ramayan::1119.simple_meaning: The sons of Sagara accuse Kapila of stealing their sacrificial horse and identify themselves before confronting him.
ramayan::1119.simple_insight: A tense accusation can turn a search into a catastrophe.
ramayan::1119.detailed_meaning: The sons of Sagara have found their missing sacrificial horse near Kapila. Blinded by anger, they accuse him of theft and announce their lineage. This line is part of the confrontation that leads directly into Kapila's furious response.
ramayan::1119.modern_relevance: You rush into a room convinced you know who ruined everything. The first words you throw out can harden confusion into disaster.
ramayan::1119.insight: It shows how anger narrows perception and makes you speak before you understand.

ramayan::1120.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां कपिलो रघुनन्दन । रोषेण महताऽऽविष्टो हुङ्कारमकरोत्तदा । । 14029 । ।
ramayan::1120.verse_hindi: O descendant of Raghu Kapila, having heard their words, overwhelmed with great wrath, uttered the sound Hm.
ramayan::1120.english_translation: O descendant of Raghu, Kapila heard their words and, seized by great anger, then gave a sharp hum.
ramayan::1120.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तु (then) / वचनं (words) / तेषां (of them) / कपिलः (Kapila) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line) / रोषेण (by anger) / महता (great) / आविष्टः (possessed) / हुङ्कारम् (the sound Hm) / अकरोत् (made) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1120.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1120.essence: Anger can turn a misunderstanding into disaster in a single breath.
ramayan::1120.simple_meaning: Kapila hears the sons of Sagara accuse him of stealing the sacrificial horse, and he responds with a furious hum.
ramayan::1120.simple_insight: Anger can answer before words do.
ramayan::1120.detailed_meaning: Kapila stands before the sons of Sagara after they accuse him of taking the sacrificial horse. Their rage meets his, and he answers not with explanation but with a thunderous hum, a moment that pushes the conflict toward destruction.
ramayan::1120.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with blame before they have understood the facts. Your first reaction is not always your wisest one.
ramayan::1120.insight: It shows how a single flash of anger can harden a situation before any real dialogue begins.

ramayan::1121.verse_sanskrit: पुत्रांश्चिरगतान् ज्ञात्वा सगरो रघुनन्दन । नप्तारमब्रवीद्राजा दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । । 1411 । ।
ramayan::1121.verse_hindi: O Delight of the Raghus, king Sagara, realising that his sons had left long ago  said to his grandson Anshuman resplendent with his own lustre:
ramayan::1121.english_translation: O Delight of the Raghus, king Sagara, realising that his sons had gone long ago, spoke to his grandson Anshuman, who shone with his own brilliance:
ramayan::1121.translation_literal: पुत्रान् (sons) / चिरगतान् (gone long ago) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / सगरः (Sagara) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghus) / नप्तारम् (to the grandson) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / राजा (the king) / दीप्यमानम् (shining) / स्वतेजसा (with his own brilliance)
ramayan::1121.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1121.essence: The burden moves to the grandson who still has strength.
ramayan::1121.simple_meaning: Sagara, seeing that his sons had been gone for a long time, spoke to his brilliant grandson Anshuman.
ramayan::1121.simple_insight: A family tragedy is turning into a task only the next generation can carry.
ramayan::1121.detailed_meaning: King Sagara has already lost his sons to the consequences of their own reckless search. Now he turns to Anshuman, the grandson who still has strength and clarity. This verse only sets up the instruction that follows.
ramayan::1121.modern_relevance: A parent looks at the one child who still has steadiness after everyone else has scattered. The real message is still coming, but the weight is already in the room.
ramayan::1121.insight: It prepares the next command by showing that responsibility is passing to the one who can still act.

ramayan::1122.verse_sanskrit: शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च पूर्वैस्तुल्योऽसि तेजसा । पितृ़णां गतिमन्विच्छ येन चाश्वोऽपवाहित: । । 1412 । ।
ramayan::1122.verse_hindi: You are valiant. You have acquired knowledge (in various fields). You are illustrious like  your ancestors. Pursue the track taken by your uncles and by the thief who ran away with the horse.
ramayan::1122.english_translation: You are valiant. You have acquired knowledge in many fields. You shine like your ancestors. Follow the track taken by your uncles and by the thief who carried off the horse.
ramayan::1122.translation_literal: शूरः (valiant) / च (and) / कृतविद्यः (learned) / च (and) / पूर्वैः (like the ancestors) / तुल्यः (equal) / असि (you are) / तेजसा (in radiance) / पितृणाम् (of the fathers/uncles) / गतिम् (the path) / अन्विच्छ (follow/search out) / येन (by whom) / च (and) / अश्वः (the horse) / अपवाहितः (was carried off)
ramayan::1122.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1122.essence: Your strengths become a summons when the family line is at stake.
ramayan::1122.simple_meaning: Sagara praises Anshuman's courage, learning, and lineage, then sends him to trace the path of his lost uncles and recover the stolen horse.
ramayan::1122.simple_insight: Respect and responsibility can arrive together: your gifts are meant to be used in a hard task, not just admired.
ramayan::1122.detailed_meaning: King Sagara speaks to his grandson Anshuman after learning that the sacrificial horse has been stolen and his sons are gone. He names Anshuman's strengths, then gives him the burden of following the trail of the missing horse and the lost uncles.
ramayan::1122.modern_relevance: A senior leader calls you into a quiet room and says, 'You have the skill for this, and the mess is now yours to untangle.' Praise becomes a summons.
ramayan::1122.insight: It turns talent into obligation: what you can do is now what you must try to do.

ramayan::1123.verse_sanskrit: अन्तर्भौमानि सत्त्वानि वीर्यवन्ति महान्ति च । तेषां त्वं प्रतिघातार्थं सास्त्रं गृह्णीष्व कार्मुकम् । । 1413 । ।
ramayan::1123.verse_hindi: Creatures in the depths of the earth are powerful and mighty. Carry with you a bow and weapons to counter their attack.
ramayan::1123.english_translation: Creatures in the depths of the earth are powerful and mighty. Carry with you a bow and weapons to counter their attack.
ramayan::1123.translation_literal: अन्तर्भौमानि (dwelling beneath the earth) / सत्त्वानि (beings) / वीर्यवन्ति (powerful) / महान्ति (great) / च (and) / तेषाम् (of them) / त्वम् (you) / प्रतिघातार्थम् (for repelling, for countering) / स-शस्त्रम् (with weapons) / गृह्णीष्व (take) / कार्मुकम् (the bow)
ramayan::1123.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1123.simple_meaning: The beings under the earth are strong, so Sagara tells Anshuman to take weapons and a bow to defend himself.
ramayan::1123.simple_insight: Some tasks require preparation, not hope alone.
ramayan::1123.detailed_meaning: King Sagara has learned that his sons are gone and sends his grandson Anshuman to continue the search. Before he leaves, Sagara warns him that the beings beneath the earth are powerful, and that he must go armed if he is to face them safely.
ramayan::1123.modern_relevance: You walk into a situation that looks simple, but hidden resistance is real. Before you push forward, make sure you are actually equipped for what may answer back.
ramayan::1123.insight: It shifts action from naïve confidence to prepared readiness.

ramayan::1124.verse_sanskrit: अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांस्त्वं हत्वा विघ्नकरानपि । सिद्धार्थस्सन्निवर्तस्व मम यज्ञस्य पारग: । । 1414 । ।
ramayan::1124.verse_hindi: Honour those who deserve it. Kill those who cause obstacles to sacrifice. Come back with your mission accomplishing. And ensure the (successful) completion of my  sacrifice.
ramayan::1124.english_translation: Honor those who deserve honor. Kill those who create obstacles to the sacrifice. Return after completing your mission and bringing my sacrifice to a successful close.
ramayan::1124.translation_literal: अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांस्त्वं (honoring those worthy of honor) / हत्वा (having killed) / विघ्नकरान् (those who make obstacles) / अपि (also) / सिद्धार्थः (one whose aim is accomplished) / सन् (being) / निवर्तस्व (return) / मम (my) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / पारगः (one who has crossed through, brought to completion)
ramayan::1124.speaker: Sagara
ramayan::1124.essence: Complete the mission by removing the obstacle, not by stopping halfway.
ramayan::1124.simple_meaning: Sagara sends Anshuman to recover the horse, remove whatever blocks the ritual, and return only after the sacrifice is completed successfully.
ramayan::1124.simple_insight: A task becomes complete only when you clear the way for others too.
ramayan::1124.detailed_meaning: King Sagara is trying to complete a sacred sacrifice that has been interrupted. He sends Anshuman out with clear instructions: show respect where it is due, destroy the force causing the obstruction, and return only when the rite is finished.
ramayan::1124.modern_relevance: You are halfway through something important, and one hidden problem keeps blocking everything. This verse speaks to the person who must clear the obstruction, finish the job properly, and not rush back before the work is truly complete.
ramayan::1124.insight: It shifts attention from partial success to full completion, including the removal of whatever blocks the larger aim.

ramayan::1125.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तोंऽशुमान्सम्यक् सगरेण महात्मना । धनुरादाय खड्गं च जगाम लघुविक्रम: । । 1415 । ।
ramayan::1125.verse_hindi: Having been throughly instructed by the highsouled Sagara in this way, Anshuman  left with rapid strides carrying a scimitar and a bow.
ramayan::1125.english_translation: Having been thoroughly instructed by the highsouled Sagara in this way, Anshuman left with rapid strides carrying a bow and a sword.
ramayan::1125.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (having been thus spoken to) / अंशुमान् (Anshuman) / सम्यक् (properly, thoroughly) / सगरेण (by Sagara) / महात्मना (by the highsouled one) / धनुः (bow) / आदाय (having taken) / खड्गम् (sword) / च (and) / जगाम (went) / लघुविक्रमः (with swift stride)
ramayan::1125.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1125.essence: He leaves prepared, because the task has already been set in motion.
ramayan::1125.simple_meaning: After receiving Sagara’s instructions, Anshuman set out quickly with weapons in hand.
ramayan::1125.simple_insight: Preparation matters before a difficult descent into the unknown.
ramayan::1125.detailed_meaning: Sagara has just ordered Anshuman to confront the hidden danger below the earth and continue the family mission. Anshuman obeys at once, taking bow and sword and moving out swiftly. The verse is a transition, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1125.modern_relevance: You get the call, check your gear, and step into the hard part without drama. The real work begins after the instruction ends.
ramayan::1125.insight: It marks the shift from instruction to action, showing readiness before the real challenge begins.

ramayan::1126.verse_sanskrit: स खातं पितृभिर्मार्गमन्तर्भौमं महात्मभि: । प्रापद्यत नरश्रेष्ठ तेन राज्ञाऽभिचोदित: । । 1416 । ।
ramayan::1126.verse_hindi: O Best among men directed by the king (Sagara), Anshuman followed the path taken by his noble uncles into the depths of the earth.
ramayan::1126.english_translation: O best among men, directed by the king, Anshuman entered the path his noble uncles had taken into the depths of the earth.
ramayan::1126.translation_literal: स (he) / खातं (dug out, hollowed) / पितृभिः (by the fathers/ancestors) / मार्गम् (path) / अन्तर्भौमं (subterranean, under the earth) / महात्मभिः (by the noble ones) / प्रापद्यत (entered, followed) / नरश्रेष्ठ (O best among men) / तेन (by that) / राज्ञा (by the king) / अभिचोदितः (urged, directed)
ramayan::1126.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1126.essence: He enters the unknown because his king has asked it of him.
ramayan::1126.simple_meaning: Anshuman, sent by King Sagara, followed the underground route his ancestors had taken.
ramayan::1126.simple_insight: Some journeys are not chosen for glory, only because love and duty demand them.
ramayan::1126.detailed_meaning: Sagara has sent Anshuman into a dangerous search for the lost path of his ancestors. The verse simply shows him obeying and descending into the earth, setting up the larger quest that follows.
ramayan::1126.modern_relevance: You take the assignment no one else wants because the family, team, or promise depends on it. The real work begins when the path disappears.
ramayan::1126.insight: It frames obedience as the first step into uncertainty, not a guarantee of success.
