ramayan::1175.english_translation: Ganga, the goddess who was extremely hard to restrain, thought, 'I will enter the lower regions of the earth by carrying Shiva along with my current.'
ramayan::1175.translation_literal: अचिन्तयत् (thought) / च (and) / सा (she) / देवी (the goddess) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / परमदुर्धरा (extremely difficult to restrain) / विशामि (I will enter) / अहम् (I) / हि (indeed) / पातालम् (the lower regions) / स्रोतसा (by the current) / गृह्य (seizing) / शङ्करम् (Shiva)
ramayan::1175.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1175.essence: Even sacred power becomes dangerous when it starts to overreach.
ramayan::1175.simple_meaning: Ganga, unable to be held back, decides to force her way downward with Shiva carried in her current.
ramayan::1175.simple_insight: Power without restraint can turn even a holy force into pride.
ramayan::1175.detailed_meaning: Ganga has already begun her descent from the heavens after Shiva agreed to receive her flow. In this moment, her force swells into a proud intention: she thinks she can drag Shiva itself into the lower regions. The next verse shows Shiva responding.
ramayan::1175.modern_relevance: You feel momentum building and start believing nothing can stop you. That is often the exact moment restraint matters most.
ramayan::1175.insight: It shows how force, once inflated by pride, can become self-defeating.

ramayan::1176.verse_sanskrit: तस्यावलेपनं ज्ञात्वा क्रुद्धस्तु भगवान् हर: । । 1436 । । तिरोभावयितुं बुद्धिं चक्रे त्रिनयनस्तदा ।
ramayan::1176.verse_hindi: Then the threeeyed Lord Siva, aware of her proud intentions applied his intelligence to conceal her.
ramayan::1176.english_translation: Then the three-eyed Lord Shiva, aware of her proud intention, became angry and resolved to conceal her.
ramayan::1176.translation_literal: तस्य (her) / अवलेपनं (pride, arrogance) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / क्रुद्धः (angry) / तु (indeed) / भगवान् (the blessed lord) / हरः (Shiva) / तिरोभावयितुम् (to make disappear, to conceal) / बुद्धिम् (plan, intelligence) / चक्रे (made, applied) / त्रिनयनः (the three-eyed one) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1176.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1176.essence: Power is greatest when it contains itself.
ramayan::1176.simple_meaning: Shiva sees Ganga's pride and decides to hide her before she can plunge onward.
ramayan::1176.simple_insight: Pride meets a calm, stronger intelligence and loses its force.
ramayan::1176.detailed_meaning: Ganga has rushed down from the heavens, intent on forcing her way into the lower regions. Seeing that she means to sweep everything aside, Shiva responds with quiet power: he plans to contain her in his matted locks rather than let her pass unchecked.
ramayan::1176.modern_relevance: Someone storms into a conversation convinced they already know the answer. The strongest response is not louder force, but the steadier mind that can absorb the surge and redirect it.
ramayan::1176.insight: It shifts the mind from reactive anger to controlled, strategic restraint.

ramayan::1177.verse_sanskrit: सा तस्मिन् पतिता पुण्या पुण्ये रुद्रस्य मूर्धनि । । 1437 । । हिमवत्प्रतिमे राम जटामण्डलगह्वरे ।
ramayan::1177.verse_hindi: O Rama that sacred river (Ganga), descended on to the depths of the matted locks on the holy head of Siva resembling the mount Himavan.
ramayan::1177.english_translation: That sacred Ganga fell onto the holy head of Rudra, into the hollow of the matted locks, O Rama, like Mount Himavan.
ramayan::1177.translation_literal: सा (she) / तस्मिन् (on that) / पतिता (fallen) / पुण्या (sacred) / पुण्ये (on the holy) / रुद्रस्य (of Rudra) / मूर्धनि (head) / हिमवत्प्रतिमे (resembling Himavan) / राम (O Rama) / जटामण्डलगह्वरे (in the hollow of the matted locks)
ramayan::1177.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1177.essence: Even the greatest descent needs a place to be held.
ramayan::1177.simple_meaning: The sacred river Ganga fell onto Shiva's holy head and settled deep inside his matted locks, like a mountain hollow.
ramayan::1177.simple_insight: Some forces are so vast they still need to be received, not resisted.
ramayan::1177.detailed_meaning: Valmiki describes the moment Ganga descends toward Shiva. Her force is immense, but Shiva's matted locks become the place that contains her fall. The verse is a vivid scene detail in the larger story of Ganga's descent.
ramayan::1177.modern_relevance: A crisis lands in your life all at once — a message, a bill, a diagnosis, a flood of emotion. Before you can move, you have to hold it without breaking.
ramayan::1177.insight: It shifts attention from force alone to the vessel that can receive force safely.

ramayan::1178.verse_sanskrit: सा कथञ्चिन्महीं गन्तुं नाशक्नोद्यत्नमास्थिता । । 1438 । । नैव निर्गमनं लेभे जटामण्डलमोहिता ।
ramayan::1178.verse_hindi: Trapped in the matted locks, she (Ganga) could not come out. With all her efforts she could not reach the earth.
ramayan::1178.english_translation: Trapped in the matted locks, she could not somehow reach the earth. Striving with all her might, she found no way out, bewildered by the tangled locks.
ramayan::1178.translation_literal: सा (she) / कथञ्चित् (somehow) / महीम् (the earth) / गन्तुम् (to go) / न अशक्नोत् (was not able) / यत्नम् (effort) / आस्थिता (having undertaken) / नैव (not at all) / निर्गमनम् (exit) / लेभे (obtained) / जटामण्डल (mass of matted locks) / मोहिता (bewildered, deluded)
ramayan::1178.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1178.essence: Effort alone cannot overcome a blocked path.
ramayan::1178.simple_meaning: Ganga gets stuck in Shiva’s matted hair and cannot get out to reach the earth, despite trying hard.
ramayan::1178.simple_insight: Even great force can fail when the path itself is blocked.
ramayan::1178.detailed_meaning: Ganga has descended onto Shiva’s head, but the fall is not complete. Caught in the tangled mass of his matted locks, she struggles to continue downward and cannot reach the earth. This verse is a brief, vivid pause before Bhagiratha’s effort continues.
ramayan::1178.modern_relevance: You keep pushing, checking, and trying to force a door that simply will not open. Sometimes the obstacle is not your effort — it is the path itself.
ramayan::1178.insight: It shifts attention from pushing harder to noticing what is actually obstructing movement.

ramayan::1179.verse_sanskrit: तत्रैवाबम्भ्रमद्देवी संवत्सरगणान् बहून् । । 1439 । । तामपश्यन्पुनस्तत्र तप: परममास्थित: ।
ramayan::1179.verse_hindi: There the golden Ganga wandered about for many years. Bhagiratha not finding Ganga, once again resorted to great penance.
ramayan::1179.english_translation: There the golden Ganga wandered about for many years. Bhagiratha, not finding Ganga, once again took up great penance.
ramayan::1179.translation_literal: तत्रैव (there itself) / अबम्भ्रमत् (wandered about) / देवी (the radiant one) / संवत्सर-गणान् (groups of years) / बहून् (many) / ताम् (her) / अपश्यन् (not seeing) / पुनः (again) / तत्र (there) / तपः (austerity) / परमम् (supreme) / आस्थितः (taken up)
ramayan::1179.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1179.essence: What is blocked often yields only to renewed effort.
ramayan::1179.simple_meaning: Ganga kept moving around for years, and Bhagiratha, still unable to find her, returned to intense penance.
ramayan::1179.simple_insight: Progress often comes from returning to disciplined effort after disappointment.
ramayan::1179.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has already drawn Ganga down from the heavens, but the river is still trapped in Shiva's matted locks. Years pass. He cannot give up, so he goes back to penance with even greater resolve, because only sustained effort can finish what started.
ramayan::1179.modern_relevance: You send the email, hear nothing, and then sit back down to write the next one. The breakthrough usually belongs to the person who can begin again without bitterness.
ramayan::1179.insight: It shifts you from reacting to delay toward renewing effort with steadiness.

ramayan::1180.verse_sanskrit: अनेन तोषितश्चाभूदत्यर्थं रघुनन्दन । । 14310 । । विससर्ज ततो गङ्गां हरो बिन्दुसर: प्रति ।
ramayan::1180.verse_hindi: O Son of the Raghus (Rama) Siva was immensely pleased with the penace and thereafter released Ganga (drop by drop) forming Bindusara.
ramayan::1180.english_translation: O Son of the Raghus, Shiva was immensely pleased with the penance and thereafter released Ganga drop by drop toward Bindusara.
ramayan::1180.translation_literal: अनेन (by this) / तोषितः (pleased) / च (and) / अभूत् (became) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghu line) / विससर्ज (released) / ततः (then) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / हरः (Shiva) / बिन्दुसरः (to Bindusara) / प्रति (toward)
ramayan::1180.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1180.essence: Steady penance can unlock what force cannot.
ramayan::1180.simple_meaning: Shiva was pleased by the penance and let Ganga flow out toward Bindusara.
ramayan::1180.simple_insight: Great effort can open what seemed impossible.
ramayan::1180.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha’s long penance has finally moved Shiva. In response, Shiva releases Ganga in a controlled stream toward the earth, preparing the way for her descent. This verse marks the turning point after the struggle, not the full teaching.
ramayan::1180.modern_relevance: You keep working on something that feels blocked for months, then one small opening appears. The breakthrough often comes only after the pressure has already done its work.
ramayan::1180.insight: It shows that persistence can soften even the hardest resistance.

ramayan::1181.verse_sanskrit: तस्यां विसृज्यमानायां सप्तस्रोतांसि जज्ञिरे । । 14311 । । ह्लादिनी पावनी चैव नलिनी च तथाऽपरा । तिस्र: प्राचीं दिशं जग्मु: गङ्गाश्शिवजलाश्शुभा: । । 14312 । ।
ramayan::1181.verse_hindi: As she (Ganga) was released, she branched out into seven streams. Three streams
ramayan::1181.english_translation: As Ganga was released, seven streams arose. Three streams, bright and purifying, flowed eastward.
ramayan::1181.translation_literal: तस्यां (in her) / विसृज्यमानायां (being released) / सप्तस्रोतांसि (seven streams) / जज्ञिरे (were born) / ह्लादिनी (Hladini) / पावनी (Purifying) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / नलिनी (Nalini) / च (and) / तथा (likewise) / अपरा (another) / तिस्रः (three) / प्राचीं (eastward) / दिशं (direction) / जग्मुः (went) / गङ्गाः (the streams of Ganga) / शिवजलाः (with auspicious water) / शुभाः (auspicious)
ramayan::1181.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1181.essence: What is released can become many streams without losing its purity.
ramayan::1181.simple_meaning: When Ganga was released, she divided into seven streams. Three of those streams flowed eastward.
ramayan::1181.simple_insight: Some releases do not diminish power; they let it spread farther.
ramayan::1181.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha's penance has moved Shiva, and Ganga is finally being released from heaven. This verse simply describes the river splitting into seven streams and beginning its course, continuing the sacred geography of Bhagiratha's success.
ramayan::1181.modern_relevance: A long-delayed project finally opens up, and what looked like one tight channel becomes several workable paths. The release is not chaos; it is movement.
ramayan::1181.insight: It shifts attention from the miracle itself to the unfolding consequence of release.

ramayan::1182.verse_sanskrit: सुचक्षुश्चैव सीता च सिन्धुश्चैव महानदी । तिस्रस्त्वेता दिशं जग्मु: प्रतीचीं तु शुभोदका: । । 14313 । ।
ramayan::1182.verse_hindi: Auspicious Suchakshu, Sita and a great river Sindhu, these three great rivers flowed  westwards.
ramayan::1182.english_translation: Auspicious Suchakshu, Sita, and the great river Sindhu—these three pure rivers flowed westward.
ramayan::1182.translation_literal: सुचक्षुः (Suchakshu) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सीता (Sita) / च (and) / सिन्धुः (Sindhu) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / महानदी (great river) / तिस्रः (three) / तु (indeed) / एताḥ (these) / दिशम् (direction) / जग्मुः (went) / प्रतीचीम् (western) / तु (but) / शुभोदकाः (pure-watered)
ramayan::1182.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1182.essence: The river's branching is being traced, not interpreted.
ramayan::1182.simple_meaning: Three pure rivers are named as flowing westward. It is a descriptive detail in the larger account of Ganga's branching.
ramayan::1182.simple_insight: Some verses simply carry the scene forward, without asking you to act or reflect yet.
ramayan::1182.detailed_meaning: Ganga has been released and divided into streams. This verse names three of them—Suchakshu, Sita, and Sindhu—as flowing westward, while the wider passage continues mapping the river's many paths.
ramayan::1182.modern_relevance: A map app splits one river into several routes, and you only need the next turn. Some moments in a story are there to orient you, not to instruct you.
ramayan::1182.insight: It keeps the narrative moving by identifying one branch of the river's course.

ramayan::1183.verse_sanskrit: सप्तमी चान्वगात्तासां भगीरथमथो नृपम् । भगीरथोऽपि राजर्षिर्दिव्यं स्यन्दनमास्थित: । । 14314 । । प्रायादग्रे महातेजा गङ्गा तं चाप्यनुव्रजत् ।
ramayan::1183.verse_hindi: The seventh stream among them followed Bhagiratha. The most brilliant rajarshi Bhagiratha also mounting on divine chariot raced forward and Ganga followed him.
ramayan::1183.english_translation: The seventh stream followed Bhagiratha. The brilliant king-sage rode ahead in a divine chariot, and Ganga followed him.
ramayan::1183.translation_literal: सप्तमी (seventh) / चान्वगात् (followed) / तासां (among them) / भगीरथम् (Bhagiratha) / अथो (then) / नृपम् (the king) / भगीरथः (Bhagiratha) / अपि (also) / राजर्षिः (king-sage) / दिव्यम् (divine) / स्यन्दनम् (chariot) / आस्थितः (mounted) / प्रायात् (went forward) / अग्रे (ahead) / महातेजाः (of great brilliance) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / तम् (him) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अनुव्रजत् (followed)
ramayan::1183.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1183.essence: Even a miracle needs a guide.
ramayan::1183.simple_meaning: Bhagiratha rides ahead in a divine chariot, and Ganga follows him as the seventh stream. The verse continues the river's descent, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1183.simple_insight: Great effort still needs guidance; even sacred momentum must be led step by step.
ramayan::1183.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has already brought Ganga down in divided streams. Now he rides ahead in a divine chariot, and the seventh stream follows him. The scene is still unfolding, carrying the river toward its final descent.
ramayan::1183.modern_relevance: You finally get the opportunity you fought for, but the hardest part is still steering it well.
ramayan::1183.insight: It shows that even a great breakthrough must be carried forward with disciplined direction.

ramayan::1184.verse_sanskrit: गगनाच्छङ्करशिरस्ततो धरणिमाश्रिता । । 14315 । । व्यसर्पत जलं तत्र तीव्रशब्दपुरस्कृतम् ।
ramayan::1184.verse_hindi: From the sky on to the head of Shankara and thence Ganga resorted to the earth. There it flowed forward with a roaring sound.
ramayan::1184.english_translation: From the sky to Shankara's head, and then to the earth, Ganga descended. There she flowed onward with a roaring sound.
ramayan::1184.translation_literal: गगनात् (from the sky) / शङ्कर-शिरः (Shankara's head) / ततः (then) / धरणिम् (to the earth) / आश्रिता (having resorted) / व्यसर्पत (flowed onward) / जलम् (the water) / तत्र (there) / तीव्र-शब्द-पुरस्कृतम् (accompanied by a fierce sound)
ramayan::1184.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1184.essence: Power becomes life only after it is safely received.
ramayan::1184.simple_meaning: Ganga came down from the sky to Shiva's head and then to the earth, rushing forward with a loud roar.
ramayan::1184.simple_insight: Great force can be beautiful when it is received and guided.
ramayan::1184.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha's long penance has finally brought Ganga down from the heavens. In this moment, the river strikes Shankara's head first, then pours onto the earth in a thunderous rush. The verse shows the power of the descent, not a teaching.
ramayan::1184.modern_relevance: Rainwater pounds onto a rooftop after months of heat, and you hear the whole house answer. Some things arrive with such force that they need a steady place to land.
ramayan::1184.insight: It shifts attention from the miracle itself to the force needing containment before release.

ramayan::1185.verse_hindi: Then the earth looked bright with the fallen and falling shoals of fish, turtles and multitudes  of other seaanimals.
ramayan::1185.english_translation: Then the earth shone with shoals of fish, turtles, and many other sea creatures, both falling and fallen.
ramayan::1185.translation_literal: मत्स्यकच्छपसङ्घैः (with shoals of fish and turtles) / च (and) / शिंशुमारगणैः (with groups of sea creatures) / तदा (then) / पतद्भिः (with those falling) / पतितैः (with those fallen) / च (and) / अन्यैः (with others) / व्यरोचत (shone brightly) / वसुन्धरा (the earth)
ramayan::1185.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1185.essence: The river's descent turns the whole earth into a living spectacle.
ramayan::1185.simple_meaning: As Ganga descended, the earth shone with fish, turtles, and other sea creatures carried along in the flood.
ramayan::1185.simple_insight: The scale of the descent is so vast that even the earth seems lit by the falling river.
ramayan::1185.detailed_meaning: Ganga is rushing down from the sky after touching Shiva's head. Along with her torrent come fish, turtles, and other creatures, falling and flowing with the current. This verse is a vivid detail in the larger scene of the river's descent.
ramayan::1185.insight: It adds a physical detail to the cosmic descent, not a teaching or decision.

ramayan::1186.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवर्षिगन्धर्वा यक्षसिद्धगणास्तदा । । 14317 । । व्यलोकयन्त ते तत्र गगनाद्गां गतां तथा ।
ramayan::1186.verse_hindi: Then devarshis, gandharvas, yakshas and hosts of siddhas looked on with astonishment at Ganga falling from the sky and descending on the earth.
ramayan::1186.english_translation: Then the seer-gods, gandharvas, yakshas, and hosts of siddhas looked on in wonder as Ganga came down from the sky to the earth.
ramayan::1186.translation_literal: ततः (then) / देवर्षिगन्धर्वा (seer-gods and gandharvas) / यक्षसिद्धगणाः (hosts of yakshas and siddhas) / तदा (then) / व्यलोकयन्त (looked on) / ते (they) / तत्र (there) / गगनात् (from the sky) / गां (Ganga) / गताम् (descended) / तथा (thus)
ramayan::1186.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1186.essence: A cosmic event makes even the celestial beings stop and stare.
ramayan::1186.simple_meaning: The celestial beings watched in amazement as Ganga descended from the sky to the earth.
ramayan::1186.simple_insight: Some moments are so vast that even the heavens stop to watch.
ramayan::1186.detailed_meaning: Ganga is pouring down from the sky, following Shiva’s head to the earth. Around that cosmic descent, seer-gods, gandharvas, yakshas, and siddhas gather as stunned witnesses. The verse pauses on their wonder, not on action.
ramayan::1186.modern_relevance: You can stand in a crowd and still feel small when something larger than you is unfolding. Some events deserve silence before interpretation.
ramayan::1186.insight: It shifts attention from doing to witnessing, from control to awe.

ramayan::1187.verse_hindi: Then, gods in a state of excitement in their aerial chariots as large as cities, on horses and on big elephants were stationed there (in the sky).
ramayan::1187.english_translation: Then the gods stood there in their aerial chariots shaped like cities, on horses and great elephants, all in excited motion.
ramayan::1187.translation_literal: विमानैः (with aerial chariots) / नगर-आकारैः (city-shaped) / हयैः (with horses) / गज-वरैः (with great elephants) / तदा (then) / पारिप्लव-गतैः (moving in agitation) / च (and) / अपि (also) / देवताः (the gods) / तत्र (there) / विष्ठिताः (stationed)
ramayan::1187.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1187.essence: The scene is so vast that even the gods gather to watch.
ramayan::1187.simple_meaning: The gods gathered in the sky, riding splendid vehicles and animals, all stirred by the sight below.
ramayan::1187.simple_insight: Even the highest beings are drawn to witness something extraordinary.
ramayan::1187.detailed_meaning: As Ganga begins her descent, celestial beings crowd the sky in flying chariots, on horses, and on elephants. This verse adds to the scene’s vastness, showing the heavens itself leaning in before the river’s arrival.
ramayan::1187.modern_relevance: A crowd gathers outside a hospital entrance, phones raised, all waiting for one moment to happen. Some events pull every eye toward them before they even fully arrive.
ramayan::1187.insight: It frames the moment as so powerful that even the heavens pause to watch.

ramayan::1188.verse_sanskrit: तदद्भुततमं लोके गङ्गापतनमुत्तमम् । । 14319 । । दिदृक्षवो देवगणा: समीयुरमितौजस: ।
ramayan::1188.verse_hindi: Gods with great lustre arrived to witness the most wonderful, grand descent of Ganga.
ramayan::1188.english_translation: The radiant gods gathered to witness the most wondrous descent of Ganga in the world.
ramayan::1188.translation_literal: तद् (that) / अद्भुततमम् (most wondrous) / लोके (in the world) / गङ्गा-पतनम् (the descent of Ganga) / उत्तमम् (excellent, supreme) / दिदृक्षवः (wishing to see) / देव-गणाः (hosts of gods) / समीयुः (gathered together) / अमित-ओजसः (of immeasurable radiance)
ramayan::1188.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1188.essence: Even the gods came to witness a descent too vast to ignore.
ramayan::1188.simple_meaning: The gods, full of radiance, came together to see Ganga descend from the sky. The moment was so extraordinary that even celestial beings were drawn to it.
ramayan::1188.simple_insight: Some moments are so vast that even the highest beings pause to watch.
ramayan::1188.detailed_meaning: As Ganga begins her descent, the heavens stir. Devarshis, gandharvas, yakshas, siddhas, and now the gods themselves gather above the scene. Valmiki pauses the story to show that this is not an ordinary event but a cosmic wonder.
ramayan::1188.modern_relevance: A child’s first performance, a wedding procession, a funeral pyre, a once-in-a-lifetime eclipse — everyone stops and looks. Some moments pull attention out of habit and into awe.
ramayan::1188.insight: It trains attention toward wonder, reminding you that greatness can be recognized before it is understood.

ramayan::1189.verse_hindi: The cloudless sky shone with the radiance of the ornaments of the gods alighting speedily to witness Ganga. It appeared as though the sky was filled with a hundred Suns.
ramayan::1189.english_translation: The cloudless sky shone with the radiance of the ornaments of the gods alighting speedily to witness Ganga. It appeared as though the sky was filled with a hundred Suns.
ramayan::1189.translation_literal: सम्पतद्भिः (alighting quickly) / सुरगणैः (by the hosts of the gods) / तेषाम् (of them) / च (and) / आभरणौजसा (by the radiance of ornaments) / शतादित्यम् (like a hundred suns) / इव (as if) / आभाति (shone) / गगनम् (the sky) / गततोयदम् (cloudless)
ramayan::1189.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1189.essence: The sky itself seems to burn with anticipation.
ramayan::1189.simple_meaning: The sky looked blazing bright as the gods rushed down in their shining ornaments to see Ganga descend.
ramayan::1189.simple_insight: Even a sacred event can make the whole world seem lit from within.
ramayan::1189.detailed_meaning: The gods are arriving in the sky to witness Ganga's descent. Their jeweled bodies make the cloudless heavens blaze like a hundred suns. This verse is not teaching a doctrine; it heightens the wonder of the scene before the river's arrival.
ramayan::1189.modern_relevance: A crowd gathers on a rooftop before sunrise, phones raised, faces bright with expectation. The moment matters so much that even the air seems to glow before anything happens.
ramayan::1189.insight: It shifts attention from action itself to the charged atmosphere that surrounds a sacred moment.

ramayan::1190.verse_hindi: The sky strewn with lightnings appeared as if it was inhabited by seaanimals, serpents and fishes fickle.
ramayan::1190.english_translation: The sky, streaked with lightning, looked as if it were filled with whales, serpents, and darting fish.
ramayan::1190.translation_literal: शिंशुमारोरगगणैः (with groups of crocodiles and serpents) / मीनैः (with fish) / अपि च (and also) / चञ्चलैः (fickle, darting) / विद्युद्भिः इव (like lightning) / विक्षिप्तम् (scattered) / आकाशम् (the sky) / अभवत् (became) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1190.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1190.essence: The sky itself becomes part of the wonder.
ramayan::1190.simple_meaning: The sky looked wildly patterned, like it was filled with moving sea creatures and flashes of lightning.
ramayan::1190.simple_insight: Nature can feel alive and immense, even in a passing moment.
ramayan::1190.detailed_meaning: As Ganga descends, the heavens crowd with gods and dazzling motion. This verse adds another layer to the scene: the sky itself seems broken into flickering forms, matching the restless energy of the sacred event.
ramayan::1190.modern_relevance: You look up during a thunderstorm and the whole sky seems alive, split by flashes. Some moments are so charged they make the world feel transformed.
ramayan::1190.insight: It shifts attention from literal description to vivid perception, showing how wonder reshapes what you see.

ramayan::1191.verse_hindi: White foams of water were scattered in a thousand ways. It appeared as if the sky was  spread over with autumnal clouds flocks of swans.
ramayan::1191.english_translation: White foams of water were scattered in a thousand ways. It looked as if the sky were covered with autumn clouds and flocks of swans.
ramayan::1191.translation_literal: पाण्डरैः (with white) / सलिलोत्पीडैः (with masses of water foam) / कीर्यमाणैः (being scattered) / सहस्रधा (in a thousand ways) / शारदाभ्रैः (with autumn clouds) / इव (as if) / आकीर्णम् (covered) / गगनम् (the sky) / हंससम्प्लवैः (with flocks of swans)
ramayan::1191.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1191.essence: The river turns the sky into a living picture.
ramayan::1191.simple_meaning: The rushing water broke into white foam everywhere, making the sky seem filled with autumn clouds and swans.
ramayan::1191.simple_insight: Nature can look almost unreal when movement, light, and spray merge into one scene.
ramayan::1191.detailed_meaning: The river Ganga is descending in a dazzling rush. Valmiki pauses the story to describe the sight: white spray, cloudlike brightness, and swanlike motion filling the sky. It is a visual bridge between the heavens and the earth.
ramayan::1191.modern_relevance: You stand by a waterfall and forget to check your phone because the spray, light, and motion have taken over your attention.
ramayan::1191.insight: It trains the mind to notice atmosphere, not just movement.

ramayan::1192.verse_sanskrit: क्वचिद्द्रुततरं याति कुटिलं क्वचिदायतम् । । 14323 । । विनतं क्वचिदुद्धूतं क्वचिद्याति शनैश्शनै: ।
ramayan::1192.verse_hindi: Ganga was flowing now rapid, now slow, now wide, now meandering, now low, now high.
ramayan::1192.english_translation: The Ganga moved at one place very fast, at another bent and winding, at another broad, at another low, at another high, and at another very slowly.
ramayan::1192.translation_literal: क्वचित् (at one place) / द्रुततरम् (very fast) / याति (goes) / कुटिलम् (crooked, winding) / क्वचित् (at one place) / आयतम् (extended, broad) / विनतम् (low, bent down) / क्वचित् (at one place) / उद्धूतम् (raised up) / क्वचित् (at one place) / याति (goes) / शनैः शनैः (very slowly)
ramayan::1192.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1192.essence: The river’s power is seen in its constant change.
ramayan::1192.simple_meaning: The Ganga’s surface kept changing shape and speed as it flowed, showing the force and variety of the flood.
ramayan::1192.simple_insight: Even a river in flood does not move in one fixed way.
ramayan::1192.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing the swollen Ganga in flood. The river surges, bends, widens, dips, rises, and slows in different places, creating a vivid picture of untamed water before the scene moves on to the next detail.
ramayan::1192.modern_relevance: A storm drain after heavy rain does the same thing — racing in one stretch, slowing in another, then swelling and dipping again. The line is pure observation, not teaching.
ramayan::1192.insight: It trains attention on motion and variation rather than on a single static image.

ramayan::1193.verse_sanskrit: सलिलेनैव सलिलं क्वचिदभ्याहतं पुन: । । 14324 । । मुहुरूर्ध्वमुखं गत्वा पपात वसुधातलम् ।
ramayan::1193.verse_hindi: Sometimes waves dashed against waves. They rose repeatedly upwards and fell down on the ground.
ramayan::1193.english_translation: Sometimes waves dashed against waves. They rose repeatedly upward and then fell to the earth.
ramayan::1193.translation_literal: सलिलेन (by water) / एव (indeed) / सलिलं (water) / क्वचित् (sometimes) / अभ्याहतम् (struck against) / पुनः (again) / मुहुः (again and again) / ऊर्ध्वमुखम् (with upward face) / गत्वा (having gone) / पपात (fell) / वसुधातलम् (to the earth's surface)
ramayan::1193.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1193.essence: The river’s force is shown through its own collisions.
ramayan::1193.simple_meaning: The river’s water kept striking itself, surging up and then falling back down.
ramayan::1193.simple_insight: It paints motion, not teaching: pure force, rise, and fall in the river’s flow.
ramayan::1193.detailed_meaning: The Ganga is being described in vivid motion. After the earlier lines compare its spread to clouds and its flow to shifting currents, this verse adds another image of turbulence: water striking water, rising, and falling, as the river rushes toward Shiva’s head.
ramayan::1193.modern_relevance: A floodwater surge hits the bridge pillar, climbs, breaks, and drops back. The image matters more than any lesson here: movement itself is the point.
ramayan::1193.insight: It slows the scene down so you can see the river’s power in detail.

ramayan::1194.verse_sanskrit: तच्छङ्करशिरोभ्रष्टं भ्रष्टं भूमितले पुन: । । 14325 । । व्यरोचत तदा तोयं निर्मलं गतकल्मषम् ।
ramayan::1194.verse_hindi: The waters of Ganga descended on Shankaras head and from there to the earth. Freed from all impurities, the waters looked pure and clean.
ramayan::1194.english_translation: The waters of Ganga fell from Shankara's head to the earth, and then shone pure, free from all impurity.
ramayan::1194.translation_literal: तत् (that) / शङ्कर-शिरः (Shankara's head) / भ्रष्टम् (fallen) / भ्रष्टम् (fallen) / भूमितले (onto the earth's surface) / पुनः (again) / व्यरोचत (shone brightly) / तदा (then) / तोयम् (the water) / निर्मलम् (pure) / गत-कल्मषम् (freed from impurity)
ramayan::1194.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1194.essence: Descent did not dirty what was already pure.
ramayan::1194.simple_meaning: Ganga fell from Shiva's head to the earth, and the water remained pure and radiant.
ramayan::1194.simple_insight: What touches the divine stays holy, even after a long descent.
ramayan::1194.detailed_meaning: Ganga has already struck Shiva's head and then fallen to the earth. Valmiki pauses on the river’s appearance: despite the violent descent, the water still shines clean. The next verse turns that image into reverence.
ramayan::1194.modern_relevance: A difficult season can leave you shaken, but not diminished. You may feel battered by the fall and still carry something clear inside.
ramayan::1194.insight: It shifts attention from the force of the fall to the purity that remains.

ramayan::1195.verse_sanskrit: तत्र देवर्षिगन्धर्वा वसुधातलवासिन: । । 14326 । । भवाङ्गपतितं तोयं पवित्रमिति पस्पृशु: ।
ramayan::1195.verse_hindi: Considering the waters fallen from the head of Siva sacred, devatas, rishis and gandharvas and those living on earth touched it (with reverence).
ramayan::1195.english_translation: There the celestial sages, gandharvas, and beings living on earth touched the water reverently, calling it sacred because it had fallen from Shiva's body.
ramayan::1195.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / देवर्षिगन्धर्वा (celestial sages and gandharvas) / वसुधातलवासिन: (those dwelling on the earth) / भवाङ्गपतितं (fallen from Shiva's body) / तोयं (water) / पवित्रम् इति (as sacred) / पस्पृशु: (touched)
ramayan::1195.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1195.essence: Sacredness is revealed by the way everyone responds to it.
ramayan::1195.simple_meaning: People from heaven and earth treated the water with reverence because they believed it was sacred.
ramayan::1195.simple_insight: Reverence changes how you meet even ordinary water.
ramayan::1195.detailed_meaning: The Ganga has just fallen from Shiva's head and become pure again on earth. In that sacred moment, devas, sages, gandharvas, and people touch the water with reverence, showing how holiness is recognised before it is explained.
ramayan::1195.modern_relevance: You step into a temple tank or river after a long journey, and everyone around you lowers their voice. The place itself has changed how people move.
ramayan::1195.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the reverence it awakens.

ramayan::1196.verse_sanskrit: शापात्प्रपतिता ये च गगनाद्वसुधातलम् । । 14327 । । कृत्वा तत्राभिषेकं ते बभूवुर्गतकल्मषा: ।
ramayan::1196.verse_hindi: Those cursed to fall from heaven to earth were absolved of their sins after bathing there (in the waters of Ganga).
ramayan::1196.english_translation: Those cursed to fall from heaven to earth were absolved of their impurities after bathing there in the waters of the Ganga.
ramayan::1196.translation_literal: शापात् (from a curse) / प्रपतिता (fallen down) / ये (those who) / च (and) / गगनात् (from the sky) / वसुधातलम् (to the earth) / कृत्वा (having done) / तत्र (there) / अभिषेकम् (ritual bathing) / ते (they) / बभूवुः (became) / गतकल्मषाः (freed from impurities)
ramayan::1196.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1196.essence: Even the fallen can be restored by sacred contact.
ramayan::1196.simple_meaning: Even those who had fallen from heaven because of a curse became cleansed after bathing in the Ganga.
ramayan::1196.simple_insight: Some places are so sacred they are spoken of as capable of cleansing even the heaviest burden.
ramayan::1196.detailed_meaning: The Ganga has just fallen from Shiva's head to the earth. Celestial beings, sages, and earthly beings gather around it. This verse adds that even those cast down from heaven by a curse are purified there, showing the river's extraordinary sanctity.
ramayan::1196.modern_relevance: A person comes home after years of carrying shame, and a single act of honest repentance feels like a reset. Some moments do not just comfort you — they change what you can return to.
ramayan::1196.insight: It shifts the mind from permanent taint to the possibility of complete cleansing.

ramayan::1197.verse_sanskrit: धूतपापा: पुनस्तेन तोयेनाथ सुभास्वता । । 14328 । । पुनराकाशमाविश्य स्वान् लोकान् प्रतिपेदिरे ।
ramayan::1197.verse_hindi: Cleansed of their sins by the sparkling waters, they ascended through the sky once
ramayan::1197.english_translation: Cleansed of their sins by the sparkling waters, they rose through the sky and returned to their own worlds.
ramayan::1197.translation_literal: धूतपापा: (sins washed away) / पुनः (again) / तेन (by that) / तोयेन (water) / अथ (then) / सुभास्वता (sparkling) / पुनः (again) / आकाशम् (the sky) / आविश्य (entering) / स्वान् (their own) / लोकान् (worlds) / प्रतिपेदिरे (they reached)
ramayan::1197.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1197.essence: Purification is complete when the fallen can return home.
ramayan::1197.simple_meaning: The waters purified them, and after bathing, they rose back into the sky to their own realms.
ramayan::1197.simple_insight: Some places do more than cleanse the body; they restore what was lost.
ramayan::1197.detailed_meaning: This is a continuation of the Ganga passage. Beings who had fallen from heaven bathe in the sacred water, are purified, and then rise back through the sky to their own worlds. The verse completes the miracle, not the argument.
ramayan::1197.insight: It closes the scene by showing purification as a return to one's rightful place.

ramayan::1198.verse_sanskrit: मुमुदे मुदितो लोकस्तेन तोयेन भास्वता । । 14329 । । कृताभिषेको गङ्गायां बभूव विगतक्लम: ।
ramayan::1198.verse_hindi: People rejoiced at the sight of those shining waters. They were happy  to have a dip in Ganga and their fatigue was gone.
ramayan::1198.english_translation: The people rejoiced at those shining waters. After bathing in the Ganga, they became free of fatigue.
ramayan::1198.translation_literal: मुमुदे (rejoiced) / मुदितः (gladdened) / लोकः (the people) / तेन (by that) / तोयेन (water) / भास्वता (shining) / कृताभिषेकः (having bathed) / गङ्गायाम् (in the Ganga) / बभूव (became) / विगतक्लमः (free from fatigue)
ramayan::1198.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1198.essence: Pure waters can lift fatigue and brighten the heart.
ramayan::1198.simple_meaning: The shining waters of the Ganga delighted everyone. A bath there left people refreshed and free of weariness.
ramayan::1198.simple_insight: Cleanse the body, and the mind often follows with relief.
ramayan::1198.detailed_meaning: As Bhagiratha brings the Ganga down to earth, people gather around the sacred water. Its brightness and purity inspire joy, and those who bathe in it feel their exhaustion vanish. The verse dwells on the immediate blessing before the river moves on.
ramayan::1198.modern_relevance: After a long day of heat, dust, and bad news, you step into cool water and feel your shoulders drop. Some relief is so complete it needs no explanation.
ramayan::1198.insight: It shifts attention from effort to renewal, showing that sacred contact can restore what strain has worn down.

ramayan::1199.verse_sanskrit: भगीरथोऽपि राजार्षिर्दिव्यं स्यन्दनमास्थित: । प्रायादग्रे महातेजास्तं गङ्गा पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात् । । 14330 ।
ramayan::1199.verse_hindi: Most brilliant rajarshi Bhagiratha also mounting the divine chariot moved forward and Ganga followed him.
ramayan::1199.english_translation: Most brilliant king-sage Bhagiratha mounted the divine chariot and moved ahead, while Ganga followed behind him.
ramayan::1199.translation_literal: भगीरथः (Bhagiratha) / अपि (also) / राजार्षिः (king-sage) / दिव्यम् (divine) / स्यन्दनम् (chariot) / आस्थितः (mounted) / प्रायात् (moved on) / अग्रे (ahead) / महातेजाः (greatly radiant) / तम् (him) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / पृष्ठतः (from behind) / अन्वगात् (followed)
ramayan::1199.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1199.essence: His resolve is so steady that even Ganga follows.
ramayan::1199.simple_meaning: Bhagiratha rides ahead on a divine chariot, and Ganga follows him from behind.
ramayan::1199.simple_insight: Great effort can draw even the impossible into motion.
ramayan::1199.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga down to earth, and the sacred river now moves after him as he leads the way. The verse is a vivid step in the procession, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1199.modern_relevance: You finally get the project moving, and then the momentum starts following you. The hard part was not speed — it was making the first path open.
ramayan::1199.insight: It shows that determined leadership can pull a vast task into order.

ramayan::1200.verse_sanskrit: देवास्सर्षिगणा: सर्वे दैत्यदानवराक्षसा: । । 14331 । । गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवरास्सकिन्नरमहोरगा: । सर्वाश्चाप्सरसो राम भगीरथरथानुगाम् । । 14332 । । गङ्गामन्वगमन् प्रीतास्सर्वे जलचराश्च ये ।
ramayan::1200.verse_hindi: O Rama besides acquatic beings, rishis, devatas, daityas, danavas, rakshasas along with kinnaras, serpents, foremost of gandharvas, yakshas and apsaras all followed the chariot of Bhagiratha. They were happy to follow Ganga.
ramayan::1200.english_translation: O Rama, besides aquatic beings, rishis, devas, daityas, danavas, rakshasas, the foremost gandharvas, yakshas, kinnaras, serpents, apsaras, and all other creatures joyfully followed the chariot of Bhagiratha, along with Ganga.
ramayan::1200.translation_literal: देवाः (devas) / सर्षिगणाः (along with groups of rishis) / सर्वे (all) / दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः (daityas, danavas, and rakshasas) / गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवराः (foremost gandharvas and yakshas) / स किन्नरमहोरगाः (with kinnaras and great serpents) / सर्वाः च (and all) / अप्सरसः (apsaras) / राम (O Rama) / भगीरथरथानुगाम् (following Bhagiratha's chariot) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / अन्वगमन् (followed) / प्रीताः (joyfully) / सर्वे (all) / जलचराः (aquatic beings) / च (and) / ये (whoever)
ramayan::1200.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1200.essence: Bhagiratha's resolve is so great that all beings follow in its wake.
ramayan::1200.simple_meaning: All kinds of beings, from gods and sages to demons, spirits, serpents, celestial singers, and water creatures, joyfully followed Bhagiratha and the Ganga.
ramayan::1200.simple_insight: Great acts can gather even opposites into one movement.
ramayan::1200.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has drawn Ganga down to earth, and the whole cosmos seems to move with her. Valmiki lists every kind of being to show the scale of the moment: heaven, earth, and the underworld all following one king's resolve.
ramayan::1200.modern_relevance: A single funeral procession, protest march, or pilgrimage can suddenly include strangers who would never stand together otherwise. Some moments are so large that they briefly gather everyone into one line of movement.
ramayan::1200.insight: It shifts attention from individual identities to the shared force that can move them together.

ramayan::1201.verse_sanskrit: यतो भगीरथो राजा ततो गङ्गायशस्विनी । । 14333 । । जगाम सरितां श्रेष्ठा सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी ।
ramayan::1201.verse_hindi: Ganga, famous and foremost of rivers, destroyer of all sins, flowed in the direction  king Bhagiratha moved.
ramayan::1201.english_translation: Ganga, famous and foremost of rivers, destroyer of all sins, flowed in the direction Bhagiratha moved.
ramayan::1201.translation_literal: यतः (in the direction of) / भगीरथः (Bhagiratha) / राजा (the king) / ततः (then) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / यशस्विनी (famous) / जगाम (went) / सरिताम् (of rivers) / श्रेष्ठा (the best) / सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी (destroyer of all sins)
ramayan::1201.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1201.essence: Bhagiratha's resolve draws even the river after him.
ramayan::1201.simple_meaning: Ganga followed Bhagiratha as he moved forward, flowing like the greatest of rivers behind the king.
ramayan::1201.simple_insight: Great forces can be guided by steady purpose.
ramayan::1201.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has already set the divine river in motion, and Ganga now follows his path. The verse simply marks her movement after him, preparing for the next event when her descent reaches Jahnu's sacrificial ground.
ramayan::1201.modern_relevance: You start moving first, and the world often follows later. A clear purpose can pull even huge forces into motion.
ramayan::1201.insight: It shifts attention from the river itself to the momentum Bhagiratha has created.

ramayan::1202.verse_sanskrit: ततो हि यजमानस्य जह्नोरद्भुतकर्मण: । । 14334 । । गङ्गा सम्प्लावयामास यज्ञवाटं महात्मन: ।
ramayan::1202.verse_hindi: Then while Ganga was flowing, it inundated the sacrificial ground of the great sage Jahnu. Jahnu who used to work wonders was performing a sacrifice.
ramayan::1202.english_translation: Then Ganga flooded the sacrificial ground of the great sage Jahnu, while he was performing his sacrifice.
ramayan::1202.translation_literal: ततो (then) / हि (indeed) / यजमानस्य (of the sacrificer) / जह्नोः (of Jahnu) / अद्भुतकर्मणः (of wondrous deeds) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / सम्प्लावयामास (flooded) / यज्ञवाटम् (the sacrificial ground) / महात्मनः (of the great soul / great sage)
ramayan::1202.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1202.essence: A sacred effort is interrupted by a force too vast to contain.
ramayan::1202.simple_meaning: Ganga reaches Jahnu's sacrifice and floods the ritual ground.
ramayan::1202.simple_insight: Great events can still interrupt sacred work.
ramayan::1202.detailed_meaning: As Ganga descends toward Bhagiratha's goal, she overflows into the sacrificial ground of the great sage Jahnu. The verse is a scene-setting link in the river's journey, leading into Jahnu's response in the next line.
ramayan::1202.modern_relevance: You are halfway through something important when a force you didn't plan for spills into the middle of it.
ramayan::1202.insight: It sets up the next reaction, showing how a single disruption changes the course of the story.

ramayan::1203.verse_sanskrit: तस्यावलेपनं ज्ञात्वा क्रुद्धो यज्वा तु राघव । । 14335 । । अपिबच्च जलं सर्वं गङ्गाया: परमाद्भुतम् ।
ramayan::1203.verse_hindi: O Descendant of the Raghu dynasty sage Jahnu who was performing the sacrifice, observed her pride and grew  furious. And astonishingly drank the entire waters of Ganga.
ramayan::1203.english_translation: Knowing her pride, the sacrificial sage Jahnu grew angry and drank up all of Ganga's wondrous waters.
ramayan::1203.translation_literal: तस्य (her) / अवलेपनं (pride, arrogance) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / क्रुद्धः (angry) / यज्वा (the sacrificer, sacrificial sage) / तु (indeed) / राघव (O descendant of Raghu) / अपिबत् (drank) / च (and) / जलं (water) / सर्वं (all) / गङ्गायाः (of Ganga) / परमाद्भुतम् (most astonishing)
ramayan::1203.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1203.essence: Arrogance is met with a force that absorbs it completely.
ramayan::1203.simple_meaning: Jahnu sees Ganga's pride, becomes angry, and swallows all her waters in an astonishing act.
ramayan::1203.simple_insight: Pride meets a force that will not bend.
ramayan::1203.detailed_meaning: Ganga has rushed over Jahnu's sacrifice and disturbed his ritual ground. Seeing her arrogance, the sage reacts instantly and drinks up the river. The next verse shows the astonishment this causes among the gods and sages.
ramayan::1203.modern_relevance: Someone storms into a room assuming everything will adjust around them. One calm person refuses to yield, and the whole atmosphere changes at once.
ramayan::1203.insight: It shows how unchecked pride can be met by decisive restraint, not negotiation.

ramayan::1204.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवास्सगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च सुविस्मिता: । । 14336 । । पूजयन्ति महात्मानं जह्नुं पुरुषसत्तमम् । गङ्गां चापि नयन्ति स्म दुहितृत्वे महात्मन: । । 14337 । ।
ramayan::1204.verse_hindi: Devatas, rishis and gandharvas stood amazed (at this act). They worshipped the magnanimous Jahnu, noblest among men. The devatas entreated the illustrious Jahnu to treat Ganga as his daughter.
ramayan::1204.english_translation: The devas, gandharvas, and sages were astonished. They honoured the great-souled Jahnu, best among men, and asked him to accept Ganga as his daughter.
ramayan::1204.translation_literal: ततः (then) / देवाः (the devas) / सगन्धर्वाः (along with the gandharvas) / ऋषयः (the sages) / च (and) / सुविस्मिताः (greatly astonished) / पूजयन्ति (they honour) / महात्मानम् (the great-souled one) / जह्नुम् (Jahnu) / पुरुषसत्तमम् (best among men) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / च (and) / अपि (also) / नयन्ति स्म (they led) / दुहितृत्वे (into daughterhood) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one)
ramayan::1204.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1204.essence: Power becomes noble when it is acknowledged and redirected.
ramayan::1204.simple_meaning: The celestial beings and sages honour Jahnu after he swallows Ganga, and they ask him to receive her as a daughter.
ramayan::1204.simple_insight: Great power earns reverence, but restraint gives it dignity.
ramayan::1204.detailed_meaning: Jahnu has just swallowed the river Ganga after she disturbed his sacrifice. Now the devas, gandharvas, and sages stand in awe before him, honouring his greatness and asking him to accept Ganga in a new, filial bond. The verse marks the resolution before her release.
ramayan::1204.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after someone handles a disruptive moment with calm authority. People do not just notice control — they respect the person who can hold it without cruelty.
ramayan::1204.insight: It shifts attention from shock to reverence, showing how force can be transformed into relationship.

ramayan::1205.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तुष्टो महातेजाश्श्रोत्राभ्यामसृजत् पुन: । । 14338 । । तस्माज्जह्नुसुता गङ्गा प्रोच्यते जाह्नवीतिच ।
ramayan::1205.verse_hindi: The brilliant (Jahnu) was pleased. He released her through both his both ears. Hence Ganga is called Jahnavi, daughter of Jahnu.
ramayan::1205.english_translation: The brilliant Jahnu was pleased. He released her through both his ears. Hence Ganga is called Jahnavi, daughter of Jahnu.
ramayan::1205.translation_literal: ततः (then) / तुष्टः (pleased) / महातेजाः (the brilliant one) / श्रोत्राभ्याम् (through both ears) / असृजत् (released) / पुनः (again) / तस्मात् (therefore) / जह्नुसुता (daughter of Jahnu) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / प्रोच्यते (is called) / जाह्नवी (Jahnavi) / इति (thus) / च (and)
ramayan::1205.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1205.essence: A clash becomes a lineage when anger gives way to release.
ramayan::1205.simple_meaning: Jahnu lets Ganga go after swallowing her, and that is why she receives the name Jahnavi.
ramayan::1205.simple_insight: Even a powerful force can be released with honor, not only control.
ramayan::1205.detailed_meaning: Jahnu has swallowed Ganga in anger after she disturbed his sacrifice. Now he is appeased and releases her through his ears, turning a crisis into a name. The verse explains the origin of Ganga's title, Jahnavi, and closes the episode.
ramayan::1205.modern_relevance: A tense family conflict cools after someone finally softens. The same relationship that felt like a battle can become a shared story with a new name attached to it.
ramayan::1205.insight: It shifts attention from punishment to reconciliation and from event to meaning.

ramayan::1206.verse_sanskrit: जगाम च पुनर्गङ्गा भगीरथरथानुगा । सागरं चापि सम्प्राप्ता सा सरित्प्रवरा तदा । । 14339 । । रसातलमुपागच्छत्सिद्ध्यर्थं तस्य कर्मण: ।
ramayan::1206.verse_hindi: Ganga, best among rivers, following the chariot of Bhagiratha, reached the ocean. She entered the nether regions of the earth in order to fulfil his mission (salvation of the sons of Sagara).
ramayan::1206.english_translation: Ganga, best among rivers, following the chariot of Bhagiratha, reached the ocean. She entered the nether regions of the earth in order to fulfil his mission.
ramayan::1206.translation_literal: जगाम (went) / च (and) / पुनर्गङ्गा (Ganga again) / भगीरथरथानुगा (following Bhagiratha's chariot) / सागरं (the ocean) / च (and) / अपि (also) / सम्प्राप्ता (having reached) / सा (she) / सरित्प्रवरा (best among rivers) / तदा (then) / रसातलम् (the nether regions) / उपागच्छत् (went down) / सिद्ध्यर्थम् (for the fulfilment) / तस्य (of that) / कर्मणः (task)
ramayan::1206.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1206.essence: A sacred effort matters only when it reaches the end.
ramayan::1206.simple_meaning: Ganga follows Bhagiratha all the way to the ocean and down into the underworld so his mission can be completed.
ramayan::1206.simple_insight: Great causes sometimes need total follow-through, not partial help.
ramayan::1206.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has finally brought Ganga down from heaven, but the task is not finished. She must keep moving with his chariot until she reaches the ocean and the lower regions, because only then can his ancestors be freed. This verse is a continuation of that long rescue.
ramayan::1206.modern_relevance: You got the approval, but the real work still waits in the second half of the project. The hard part is not starting; it is carrying the task all the way through.
ramayan::1206.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic beginnings to complete follow-through.

ramayan::1207.verse_sanskrit: भगीरथोऽपि राजर्षि: गङ्गामादाय यत्नत: । पितामहान् भस्मकृतानपश्यद्दीनचेतन: । । 14340 । ।
ramayan::1207.verse_hindi: Rajarshi Bhagiratha, having brought Ganga with supreme efforts, saw with a sad heart his grandfathers reduced to ashes.
ramayan::1207.english_translation: Rajarshi Bhagiratha, having brought Ganga with great effort, saw his grandfathers reduced to ashes, and his heart was heavy with sorrow.
ramayan::1207.translation_literal: भगीरथः (Bhagiratha) / अपि (also) / राजर्षिः (royal sage) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / आदाय (having brought) / यत्नत: (with effort) / पितामहान् (grandfathers) / भस्मकृतान् (reduced to ashes) / अपश्यत् (saw) / दीनचेतनः (with a saddened heart)
ramayan::1207.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1207.essence: Success does not erase the wound that made it necessary.
ramayan::1207.simple_meaning: Bhagiratha finally brings Ganga to the place of his ancestors, but he sees only their ashes. His success is real, yet grief still remains.
ramayan::1207.simple_insight: Even a hard-won victory can arrive with sorrow still intact.
ramayan::1207.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has completed his long effort and led Ganga to the land of his ancestors. But when he looks, he finds only the ashes of his grandfathers. The verse pauses on the emotional cost of a rescue that is still not complete.
ramayan::1207.modern_relevance: You spent months fixing what your family could not. The problem is solved, but when you finally look back, the ache is still there.
ramayan::1207.insight: It shows that effort can achieve the task without erasing grief; completion and sorrow can exist together.

ramayan::1208.verse_sanskrit: अथ तद्भस्मनां राशिं गङ्गासलिलमुत्तमम् । प्लावयद्धूतपाप्मानस्स्वर्गं प्राप्ता रघूत्तम । । 14341 । ।
ramayan::1208.verse_hindi: O Best of the Raghus thereafter the holy waters of Ganga inundated those heaps of ashes and the sons of Sagara, purged of their sins, reached heaven (said Viswamitra).
ramayan::1208.english_translation: Then, O best of the Raghus, the holy waters of Ganga flooded those heaps of ashes, and the sons of Sagara, freed from impurity, reached the higher realm.
ramayan::1208.translation_literal: अथ (then) / तद्भस्मनां (of those ashes) / राशिं (heap) / गङ्गासलिलम् (Ganga-water) / उत्तमम् (supreme) / प्लावयत् (flooding) / धूतपाप्मानः (those whose impurities were washed away) / स्वर्गम् (higher realm) / प्राप्ता (reached) / रघूत्तम (O best of the Raghus)
ramayan::1208.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1208.essence: What seemed only ashes became release when Ganga arrived.
ramayan::1208.simple_meaning: Ganga's waters washed over the ashes, and the sons of Sagara were released from their burden and reached the higher realm.
ramayan::1208.simple_insight: Even the deepest loss can be transformed when what is sacred finally reaches it.
ramayan::1208.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga down, and he now sees his ancestors' ashes before him. Viswamitra marks the turning point: the river floods the remains, their burden is washed away, and the long suffering of Sagara's sons is finally resolved.
ramayan::1208.modern_relevance: You return to something you thought was finished—a grave, a message, a memory—and find that healing has finally reached it.
ramayan::1208.insight: It shifts attention from grief alone to the moment purification completes what effort began.

ramayan::1209.verse_sanskrit: स गत्वा सागरं राजा गङ्गयाऽनुगतस्तदा । प्रविवेश तलं भूमेर्यत्र ते भस्मसात्कृता: । । 1441 । ।
ramayan::1209.verse_hindi: Thereupon that king followed by Ganga reached the ocean and entered the lower regions of the earth where the sons of Sagara were found reduced to ashes.
ramayan::1209.english_translation: Thereupon that king followed by Ganga reached the ocean and entered the lower regions of the earth where the sons of Sagara were found reduced to ashes.
ramayan::1209.translation_literal: स (that) / गत्वा (having gone) / सागरम् (the ocean) / राजा (the king) / गङ्गया (with Ganga) / अनुगतः (followed) / तदा (then) / प्रविवेश (entered) / तलम् (the lower region) / भूमेः (of the earth) / यत्र (where) / ते (those) / भस्मसात्कृताः (made into ashes)
ramayan::1209.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1209.essence: He reaches the buried wound only after years of effort.
ramayan::1209.simple_meaning: Bhagiratha reached the ocean with Ganga and entered the nether region of the earth to find the ashes of Sagara's sons.
ramayan::1209.simple_insight: Great effort sometimes leads you into places no one else can reach.
ramayan::1209.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga down through immense effort. Now he reaches the ocean and descends into the lower world to find the ashes of his ancestors. This verse is a bridge in the rescue sequence, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1209.modern_relevance: You finally get access to the thing you fought for, only to discover the real work begins in the hidden place beneath it.
ramayan::1209.insight: It marks the movement from effort to discovery, as Bhagiratha reaches the place where the past must be transformed.

ramayan::1210.verse_sanskrit: भस्मन्यथाऽप्लुते राम गङ्गायास्सलिलेन वै । सर्वलोकप्रभुर्ब्रह्मा राजानमिदमब्रवीत् । । 1442 । ।
ramayan::1210.verse_hindi: After the ashes were inundated by the waters of Ganga, Brahma, lord of the world,   appeared before king Bhagiratha and said:
ramayan::1210.english_translation: After the ashes were inundated by the waters of Ganga, Brahma, lord of the world, appeared before king Bhagiratha and said:
ramayan::1210.translation_literal: भस्मनि (in the ashes) / अथ (then) / अप्लुते (having been flooded) / राम (O Rama) / गङ्गायाः (of Ganga) / सलिलेन (with the water) / वै (indeed) / सर्वलोकप्रभुः (lord of all worlds) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / राजानम् (to the king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1210.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1210.essence: Completion itself draws recognition from the highest witness.
ramayan::1210.simple_meaning: Once Ganga's waters cover the ashes, Brahma appears and speaks to Bhagiratha. The rescue of Sagara's sons is complete enough for the divine witness to respond.
ramayan::1210.simple_insight: Some acts are so complete that even silence gives way to recognition.
ramayan::1210.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga down and washed over the ashes of Sagara's sons. At that moment Brahma, lord of the worlds, appears before him and speaks. The verse is a transition: the deed is done, and the cosmic acknowledgment begins.
ramayan::1210.modern_relevance: You finally finish the hard thing no one believed would work. The message, the apology, the rescue, the closure — only then do you hear the first real response.
ramayan::1210.insight: It marks the moment effort becomes fulfilled action, and the world finally answers back.

ramayan::1211.verse_sanskrit: तारिता नरशार्दूल दिवं याताश्च देववत् । षष्ठि: पुत्रसहस्राणि सगरस्य महात्मन: । । 1443 । ।
ramayan::1211.verse_hindi: O Tiger among men sixty thousand sons of illustrious Sagara having been liberated, had gone towards heaven like devatas.
ramayan::1211.english_translation: O tiger among men, the sixty thousand sons of noble Sagara, once freed, went to the higher realm like radiant beings.
ramayan::1211.translation_literal: तारिता (having been liberated) / नरशार्दूल (O tiger among men) / दिवं (to the higher realm) / याताः (gone) / च (and) / देववत् (like radiant beings) / षष्ठि: (sixty) / पुत्रसहस्राणि (thousand sons) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / महात्मन: (of the noble-minded)
ramayan::1211.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1211.essence: Their long bondage ends only when another carries the burden for them.
ramayan::1211.simple_meaning: Sagara’s sixty thousand sons have been freed from their curse and reached the higher realm like radiant beings.
ramayan::1211.simple_insight: Release can come even after terrible loss.
ramayan::1211.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga’s waters down to the ashes of Sagara’s sons. Brahma has already spoken. This verse simply marks the result: the long-delayed liberation of the dead princes, now shown as complete.
ramayan::1211.modern_relevance: You finally clear the last task tied to an old family burden. The relief is real, but it arrives after the cost has already been paid.
ramayan::1211.insight: It completes the rescue by showing the dead sons finally freed.

ramayan::1212.verse_sanskrit: सागरस्य जलं लोके यावत्स्थास्यति पार्थिव । सगरस्यात्मजास्तावत्स्वर्गे स्थास्यन्ति देववत् । । 1444 । ।
ramayan::1212.verse_hindi: O King as long as the waters in the ocean exist in this world, shall the sons of Sagara, live in heavens like gods.
ramayan::1212.english_translation: O king, as long as the waters of the ocean remain in this world, the sons of Sagara will dwell in the higher realm like radiant beings.
ramayan::1212.translation_literal: सागरस्य (of Sagara) / जलं (waters) / लोके (in the world) / यावत् (as long as) / स्थास्यति (will remain) / पार्थिव (O king) / सगरस्य (of Sagara) / आत्मजाः (sons) / तावत् (until then) / स्वर्गे (in the higher realm) / स्थास्यन्ति (will dwell) / देववत् (like radiant beings)
ramayan::1212.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1212.essence: A single act of rescue can echo until the world itself changes.
ramayan::1212.simple_meaning: Brahma blesses Bhagiratha: the freed sons of Sagara will remain in the higher realm as long as the ocean's waters endure.
ramayan::1212.simple_insight: A fulfilled act can carry a family’s honor far beyond one lifetime.
ramayan::1212.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought the sacred river down to purify his ancestors. After the ashes are washed, Brahma appears and confirms the result: Sagara’s sons are freed and granted a lasting place in the higher realm. This verse seals that blessing with a cosmic condition.
ramayan::1212.modern_relevance: You finish something your family never could: a debt paid, a name restored, a wound finally closed. The relief is bigger than you, and it outlives you.
ramayan::1212.insight: It turns private effort into ancestral release and lasting consequence.

ramayan::1213.verse_sanskrit: इयं च दुहिता ज्येष्ठा तव गङ्गा भविष्यति । त्वत्कृतेन च नाम्नाऽथ लोके स्थास्यति विश्रुता । । 1445 । ।
ramayan::1213.verse_hindi: This Ganga will become your eldest daughter and from now on she will be wellknown in this world (as Bhagirathi) after your name.
ramayan::1213.english_translation: This Ganga will become your eldest daughter, and from now on she will be well known in the world by your name.
ramayan::1213.translation_literal: इयं (this) / च (and) / दुहिता (daughter) / ज्येष्ठा (eldest) / तव (your) / गङ्गा (Ganga) / भविष्यति (will become) / त्वत्कृतेन (by your doing / because of you) / च (and) / नाम्ना (by name) / अथ (now) / लोके (in the world) / स्थास्यति (will remain / be known) / विश्रुता (famous, well known)
ramayan::1213.speaker: Bhagiratha
ramayan::1213.essence: Your devoted act can become something the world remembers by your name.
ramayan::1213.simple_meaning: Ganga will be joined to Bhagiratha's family line and become famous in the world through his deed.
ramayan::1213.simple_insight: A single act of devotion can reshape how the world remembers you.
ramayan::1213.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga down to redeem his ancestors. In this moment, the blessing is named: the river becomes his daughter in a lasting, public sense, and his effort will be remembered through her very name.
ramayan::1213.modern_relevance: You spend years fixing something no one else could see, and later people attach your name to the result. Quiet effort can become a public legacy.
ramayan::1213.insight: It shifts attention from personal effort to the lasting form that effort can take in the world.

ramayan::1214.verse_sanskrit: गङ्गा त्रिपथगा राजन् दिव्या भागीरथीति च । त्रीन् पथो भावयन्तीति ततस्त्रिपथगा स्मृता । । 1446 । ।
ramayan::1214.verse_hindi: O King divine Ganga will be called Tripathaga as well as Bhagirathi. Since she flows in the three worlds (heaven, earth and the lower world: Patala), she will be known as
ramayan::1214.english_translation: O King, divine Ganga will be called Tripathaga and Bhagirathi. Because she flows through the three worlds, she will be known as Tripathaga.
ramayan::1214.translation_literal: गङ्गा (Ganga) / त्रिपथगा (one who flows through three paths/worlds) / राजन् (O King) / दिव्या (divine) / भागीरथी (Bhagirathi) इति (thus) / च (and) / त्रीन् (three) / पथः (paths/worlds) / भावयन्ती (flowing through) इति (thus) / ततः (therefore) / त्रिपथगा (Tripathaga) / स्मृता (is called/remembered)
ramayan::1214.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1214.essence: She is remembered by the worlds she passes through.
ramayan::1214.simple_meaning: Ganga is named Tripathaga and Bhagirathi because she flows through heaven, earth, and the lower world.
ramayan::1214.simple_insight: Greatness is sometimes remembered through the path it touches, not just the name it bears.
ramayan::1214.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has already won Ganga’s descent for his ancestors. Now the sage explains her names to King Sagara’s line: she is Bhagirathi because of Bhagiratha, and Tripathaga because she moves through three realms. The verse supports the larger promise, not the final ritual itself.
ramayan::1214.modern_relevance: You carry a name because of what you move through. A family, a project, or a difficult season can mark you so deeply that people remember you by it.
ramayan::1214.insight: It links identity to the breadth of one’s reach, not to a single place or moment.

ramayan::1215.verse_sanskrit: पितामहानां सर्वेषां त्वमत्र मनुजाधिप । कुरुष्व सलिलं राजन् प्रतिज्ञामपवर्जय । । 1447 । ।
ramayan::1215.verse_hindi: O Lord of men O King you may offer the waters of  Ganga here to all your ancestors and thereby fulfil your vow.
ramayan::1215.english_translation: O Lord of men, O King, you may offer the waters of Ganga here to all your ancestors and thereby fulfil your vow.
ramayan::1215.translation_literal: पितामहानाम् (of ancestors) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / त्वम् (you) / अत्र (here) / मनुजाधिप (lord of men) / कुरुष्व (do) / सलिलम् (water-offering) / राजन् (O king) / प्रतिज्ञाम् (vow) / अपवर्जय (fulfil, complete)
ramayan::1215.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1215.essence: A vow is only honoured when you finish what it demanded.
ramayan::1215.simple_meaning: The king is told to offer the sacred waters now, so his vow can be completed and his ancestors honoured.
ramayan::1215.simple_insight: A promise matters most when you finally do what it asked of you.
ramayan::1215.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought Ganga down to earth after immense effort. Now the sage tells King Sagara's line to perform the water offering for the ancestors at once, because the long-delayed vow can finally be fulfilled in this sacred moment.
ramayan::1215.modern_relevance: You finally have the document signed, the apology ready, the visit arranged, and the thing you kept postponing can now be completed. Relief comes not from intention, but from doing what your word required.
ramayan::1215.insight: It shifts you from carrying a promise to completing it.

ramayan::1216.verse_sanskrit: पूर्वकेण हि ते राजंस्तेनातियशसा तदा । धर्मिणां प्रवरेणापि नैष प्राप्तो मनोरथ: । । 1448 । ।
ramayan::1216.verse_hindi: O King by the highly renowned ancestors of yours, the foremost among righteous ones (even Sagara) this desire has not been fulfilled.
ramayan::1216.english_translation: O King, even by your highly renowned ancestors, the foremost among the righteous, this desire was not fulfilled.
ramayan::1216.translation_literal: पूर्वकेण (by the earlier) / हि (indeed) / ते (your) / राजन् (O king) / तेन (by that one) / अतियशसा (highly renowned) / तदा (then) / धर्मिणाम् (of the righteous) / प्रवरेण (by the foremost) / अपि (even) / न (not) / एषः (this) / प्राप्तः (attained) / मनोरथः (wish)
ramayan::1216.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1216.essence: Greatness can be inherited, but completion still asks for one living hand.
ramayan::1216.simple_meaning: Even your great and righteous ancestors never completed this goal. The task has remained unfinished across generations.
ramayan::1216.simple_insight: Some burdens are inherited, not chosen — and they can still wait for one person to complete them.
ramayan::1216.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Ganga story, a sage reminds the king that this long-pending wish has resisted even the most famous and righteous ancestors. The point is not praise alone; it is the weight of an unfinished family duty now landing on one man.
ramayan::1216.modern_relevance: You inherit a family project, a broken promise, or a responsibility everyone before you postponed. Their effort matters, but the unfinished work still arrives in your hands.
ramayan::1216.insight: It shifts you from admiring ancestral effort to seeing your own responsibility to complete what they could not.

ramayan::1217.verse_sanskrit: तथैवांशुमता तात लोकेऽप्रतिमतेजसा । गङ्गां प्रार्थयतानेतुं प्रतिज्ञा नापवर्जिता । । 1449 । ।
ramayan::1217.verse_hindi: O Child similarly though Anshuman possessed unparalleled prowess in this world his prayer to Ganga, his vow could not be fulfilled.
ramayan::1217.english_translation: O Child, similarly, though Anshuman possessed unparalleled prowess in this world, his prayer to bring Ganga did not fulfil his vow.
ramayan::1217.translation_literal: तथैव (similarly) / अंशुमता (by Anshuman) / तात (O child) / लोके (in the world) / अप्रतिम-तेजसा (by one of unmatched brilliance) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / प्रार्थयता (while praying) / नेतुम् (to bring) / प्रतिज्ञा (the vow) / न (not) / अपवर्जिता (fulfilled / completed)
ramayan::1217.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1217.essence: Great power still fails when the task exceeds one lifetime.
ramayan::1217.simple_meaning: Anshuman was powerful and worthy, but even he could not complete the vow to bring Ganga down.
ramayan::1217.simple_insight: Even great ability may not be enough when a task belongs to a larger chain of effort.
ramayan::1217.detailed_meaning: In the story of Bhagiratha's ancestors, the sage is showing how long this family has carried one unfinished duty. Sagara's line had power and virtue, yet even Anshuman could not bring Ganga. Bhagiratha's effort will continue that broken promise.
ramayan::1217.modern_relevance: You may be the capable one in the family, the team, or the company, and still inherit a task no single person can finish. Some promises outlive the person who first made them.
ramayan::1217.insight: It shifts attention from personal talent to the larger work that may need generations of persistence.

ramayan::1218.verse_sanskrit: राजर्षिणा गुणवता महर्षिसमतेजसा । मत्तुल्यतपसा चैव क्षत्रधर्मस्थितेन च । । 14410 । । दिलीपेन महाभाग तव पित्राऽति तेजसा । पुनर्न शङ्किताऽनेतुं गङ्गां प्रार्थयताऽनघ । । 14411 । ।
ramayan::1218.verse_hindi: O Sinless one (Bhagiratha) O Distinguished one on the part of Dilipa brilliant your father who had the virtuous of a rajarshi, who was equal to a maharshi in splendour, and to me in austerities and abiding to the duties of a kshatriya it was even not possible to bring Ganga through prayer.
ramayan::1218.english_translation: O sinless one, your brilliant father Dilipa, who had the virtues of a royal sage, the radiance of a great sage, my own austerity, and the steadfastness of a kshatriya, still could not bring Ganga down by prayer.
ramayan::1218.translation_literal: राजर्षिणा (by a royal sage) / गुणवता (possessed of virtues) / महर्षिसमतेजसा (equal in splendour to a great sage) / मत्तुल्यतपसा (with austerity equal to mine) / चैव (and also) / क्षत्रधर्मस्थितेन (established in the duty of a kshatriya) / च (and) / दिलीपेन (by Dilipa) / महाभाग (O highly fortunate one) / तव (your) / पित्रा (by father) / अति तेजसा (exceedingly brilliant) / पुनः न (again not) / शङ्किता (possible) / आनेतुं (to bring) / गङ्गाम् (Ganga) / प्रार्थयता (by praying) / अनघ (O sinless one)
ramayan::1218.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1218.essence: Even the worthy can fail when the task exceeds human reach.
ramayan::1218.simple_meaning: Even a great, righteous king like Dilipa could not achieve this impossible task through prayer alone.
ramayan::1218.simple_insight: Some goals demand more than merit; humility begins where control ends.
ramayan::1218.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha is being told that his ancestor Dilipa was no ordinary king: righteous, radiant, disciplined, and noble. Even so, he failed to bring Ganga down. The speech builds the weight of Bhagiratha's vow by showing how difficult the task has always been.
ramayan::1218.modern_relevance: You have done everything right, and the result still won't move. A family problem, a stalled project, a long apology — effort and goodness matter, but they do not guarantee control.
ramayan::1218.insight: It shifts you from expecting virtue to guarantee outcomes to respecting the limits of effort and prayer.

ramayan::1219.verse_sanskrit: सा त्वया समनुक्रान्ता प्रतिज्ञा पुरुषर्षभ । प्राप्तोऽसि परमं लोके यश: परमसम्मतम् । । 14412 । ।
ramayan::1219.verse_hindi: O Best among men you have fulfilled that vow. You have achieved supreme renown
ramayan::1219.english_translation: O best among men, you have fulfilled that vow. You have achieved supreme renown.
ramayan::1219.translation_literal: सा (that) / त्वया (by you) / समनुक्रान्ता (undertaken, carried through) / प्रतिज्ञा (vow) / पुरुषर्षभ (best among men) / प्राप्तोऽसि (you have attained) / परमं (supreme) / लोके (in the world) / यशः (renown, fame) / परमसम्मतम् (most honoured, most esteemed)
ramayan::1219.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1219.essence: A vow fulfilled becomes a person's lasting name.
ramayan::1219.simple_meaning: Bhagiratha is praised for fulfilling the vow he took to bring the Ganga down to earth. Because he kept that promise, he earns the highest honour.
ramayan::1219.simple_insight: A kept promise can outlive everything else you do.
ramayan::1219.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has completed the impossible task his ancestors began: winning the Ganga's descent to earth. The speaker praises him not for power, but for carrying a vow all the way through until it became history.
ramayan::1219.modern_relevance: You said yes to something months ago, and now the work is hard, slow, and thankless. This verse remembers that finishing what you promised can matter more than looking impressive.
ramayan::1219.insight: It shifts attention from talent to follow-through, showing that fulfilled commitment becomes lasting honour.

ramayan::1220.verse_sanskrit: यच्च गङ्गावतरणं त्वया कृतमरिन्दम । अनेन च भवान् प्राप्तो धर्मस्यायतनं महत् । । 14413 । ।
ramayan::1220.verse_hindi: O Destroyer of enemies by bringing about the descent of Ganga, you have secured a great abode in dharma.
ramayan::1220.english_translation: O destroyer of enemies, by bringing about the descent of the Ganga, you have secured a great abode in dharma.
ramayan::1220.translation_literal: यत् (which) / च (and) / गङ्गावतरणं (the descent of the Ganga) / त्वया (by you) / कृतम् (done) / अरिन्दम (O destroyer of enemies) / अनेन (by this) / च (and) / भवान् (you) / प्राप्तः (have attained) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / आयतनं (abode) / महत् (great)
ramayan::1220.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1220.essence: A fulfilled vow becomes a permanent standing in dharma.
ramayan::1220.simple_meaning: Bringing the Ganga down is treated as a supreme act that gives Bhagiratha a lasting place in dharma.
ramayan::1220.simple_insight: A noble deed does more than solve a problem; it becomes part of who you are.
ramayan::1220.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has fulfilled the vow that brought the Ganga to earth and rescued his ancestors. The speaker praises that achievement as more than success: it has established Bhagiratha in a great place within dharma itself.
ramayan::1220.modern_relevance: You spent years carrying one promise through setbacks, paperwork, and doubt. When it finally landed, people saw the result — but the deeper reward was that the act changed who you had become.
ramayan::1220.insight: It shifts attention from achievement alone to the moral stature created by fulfilling a hard vow.

ramayan::1221.verse_sanskrit: प्लावयस्व त्वमात्मानं नरोत्तम सदोचिते । सलिले पुरुषव्याघ्र शुचि: पुण्यफलो भव । । 14414 । ।
ramayan::1221.verse_hindi: O Best among men O Tiger among men take a dip in the eternally sacred waters,  purify yourself and acquire holiness.
ramayan::1221.english_translation: O best among men, O tiger among men, take a dip in these sacred waters. Purify yourself and become blessed with holy merit.
ramayan::1221.translation_literal: प्लावयस्व (immerse yourself) / त्वम् (you) / आत्मानम् (yourself) / नरोत्तम (best among men) / सदोचिते (in ever-appropriate) / सलिले (in water) / पुरुषव्याघ्र (tiger among men) / शुचिः (pure) / पुण्यफलः (having holy merit) / भव (become)
ramayan::1221.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1221.essence: Victory is not complete until it is ritually closed.
ramayan::1221.simple_meaning: Rama is told to bathe in the sacred river water, cleanse himself, and gain holy merit.
ramayan::1221.simple_insight: Even after victory, there is a need to pause, cleanse, and honour what comes next.
ramayan::1221.detailed_meaning: After the Ganga has been brought down and Rama's vow has been fulfilled, the speaker urges him to bathe in the sacred waters. It is a ritual close to a great act, preparing him for the next duty.
ramayan::1221.modern_relevance: After the project ends and everyone cheers, you still need the quiet ritual that marks completion — a shower, a prayer, a breath, a reset before the next task.
ramayan::1221.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to purification and transition.

ramayan::1222.verse_sanskrit: पितामहानां सर्वेषां कुरुष्व सलिलक्रियाम् । स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि स्वं लोकं गम्यतां नृप । । 14415 । ।
ramayan::1222.verse_hindi: O King perform the rites of all your forefathers with the waters (of Ganga), farewell. I shall return to my world (now). Go back, O King (said Grandsire)
ramayan::1222.english_translation: O King, perform the rites for all your forefathers with this water. Farewell. I shall return to my own world now. Go back, O King.
ramayan::1222.translation_literal: पितामहानाम् (of forefathers) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / कुरुष्व (do) / सलिलक्रियाम् (water-rites) / स्वस्ति (farewell, may there be well-being) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may it be) / गमिष्यामि (I shall go) / स्वम् (own) / लोकम् (world) / गम्यताम् (let it be gone to) / नृप (O king)
ramayan::1222.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1222.essence: Completion matters as much as the miracle itself.
ramayan::1222.simple_meaning: The divine river has finished its task. Bhagiratha is told to offer the funeral rites, then return home.
ramayan::1222.simple_insight: Some journeys end by restoring order, not by staying forever.
ramayan::1222.detailed_meaning: Bhagiratha has brought the Ganga down to earth and purified his ancestors. Now the grandsire tells him to complete the final rites for his forefathers, then depart. The great work is done; this is the closing blessing before return.
ramayan::1222.modern_relevance: You finish the hard thing, clean up the last details, and feel the quiet shift when the task is truly complete.
ramayan::1222.insight: It marks the end of a sacred mission and the return to ordinary life.

ramayan::1223.verse_sanskrit: भगीरथोऽपि राजर्षि: कृत्वा सलिलमुत्तमम् । यथाक्रमं यथान्यायं सागराणां महायशा: । । 14417 । । कृतोदकश्शुची राजा स्वपुरं प्रविवेश ह । समृद्धार्थो रघुश्रेष्ठ स्वराज्यं प्रशशास ह । । 14418 । ।
ramayan::1223.verse_hindi: The illustrious rajarshi Bhagiratha, performed the rites of offering the sacred water of Ganga, in accordance with proper order and tradition for the sons of Sagara. Purified with the ablutions entered his own city. O Best of the Raghus his desire thus fulfilled he continued to rule the kingdom thereafter.
ramayan::1223.english_translation: The illustrious king Bhagiratha performed the sacred rites for the sons of Sagara in proper order and with proper law. Purified by the waters, the king entered his own city. O best of the Raghus, having fulfilled his aim, he then ruled his kingdom.
