ramayan::1318.detailed_meaning: Ahalya has already crossed a dangerous line with Indra. Now, in the charged silence after the act, she speaks from a mind that has been satisfied and unsettled at once. Her words are urgent: leave, and do not let Gautama find us.
ramayan::1318.modern_relevance: A message sent too late can’t be unsent. The thrill is gone, and what remains is the fear of being seen.
ramayan::1318.insight: It shows how private transgression quickly becomes self-protection.

ramayan::1319.verse_sanskrit: इन्द्रस्तु प्रहसन् वाक्यमहल्यामिदमब्रवीत् । सुश्रोणि परितुष्टोऽस्मि गमिष्यामि यथाऽगतम् । 14822 । ।
ramayan::1319.verse_hindi: Indra smilingly said to Ahalya, O One with lovely hips, I am  gratified. I shall go away the way I have come.
ramayan::1319.english_translation: Indra, smiling, said to Ahalya, "O one with lovely hips, I am satisfied. I shall leave the way I came."
ramayan::1319.translation_literal: इन्द्रः (Indra) / तु (but) / प्रहसन् (smiling) / वाक्यम् (words) / अहल्याम् (to Ahalya) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said) / सुश्रोणि (O one with lovely hips) / परितुष्टः (satisfied) / अस्मि (I am) / गमिष्यामि (I shall go) / यथा (as) / आगतम् (I came)
ramayan::1319.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1319.essence: The smile hides a breach already in motion.
ramayan::1319.simple_meaning: Indra tells Ahalya that he is satisfied and will leave the same way he came, but the scene is only a brief step in the larger encounter.
ramayan::1319.simple_insight: Some moments are only the middle of a mistake, not the meaning of it.
ramayan::1319.detailed_meaning: In Gautama's hermitage, Indra has already entered Ahalya's space under false pretenses. He speaks lightly, smiling and declaring himself satisfied, but the verse is only a passing detail in the unfolding transgression and its aftermath.
ramayan::1319.modern_relevance: A conversation that sounds casual can still sit inside a choice you will regret later. The tone may be light; the consequences are not.
ramayan::1319.insight: It keeps attention on the immediate scene, while the real moral weight remains in the surrounding action.

ramayan::1320.verse_sanskrit: एवं सङ्गम्य तु तया निश्चक्रामोटजात्तत: । । स सम्भ्रमात्त्वरन् राम शङ्कितो गौतमं प्रति । 14823 । ।
ramayan::1320.verse_hindi: O Rama he (Indra) came out of the leafhut quickly after his union with her, apprehensive of Gautama.
ramayan::1320.english_translation: After uniting with her, he quickly came out of the leaf-hut, fearful of Gautama.
ramayan::1320.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / सङ्गम्य (having united with) / तु (but) / तया (with her) / निश्चक्राम (came out) / उटजात् (from the leaf-hut) / ततः (then) / सः (he) / सम्भ्रमात् (in haste/confusion) / त्वरन् (hurrying) / राम (O Rama) / शङ्कितः (afraid/suspicious) / गौतमं (of Gautama) / प्रति (toward)
ramayan::1320.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1320.essence: He fled as soon as pleasure ended, already afraid of the truth.
ramayan::1320.simple_meaning: After being with Ahalya, Indra hurried out of the hut, afraid of Gautama.
ramayan::1320.simple_insight: Desire made him reckless, and fear made him flee.
ramayan::1320.detailed_meaning: In Gautama's hermitage, Indra has just violated trust and is rushing away from the leaf-hut before the sage returns. The verse is a brief movement beat, not the moral climax; it simply shows his panic after the act.
ramayan::1320.modern_relevance: You make a choice in secret, then rush to escape its consequences before anyone notices.
ramayan::1320.insight: It shows how wrongdoing often turns into panic the moment accountability feels near.

ramayan::1321.verse_sanskrit: गौतमं तं ददर्शाथ प्रविशन्तं महामुनिम् । देवदानवदुर्धर्षं तपोबलसमन्वितम् । । 14824 । । तीर्थेंदकपरिक्लिन्नं दीप्यमानमिवानलम् । गृहीतसमिधं तत्र सकुशं मुनिपुङ्गवम् । । 14825 । ।
ramayan::1321.verse_hindi: Subsequently, Indra beheld the great ascetic Gautama, unassailable by devatas and danavas, endowed with the power of ascetism, drenched with sacrifical waters,  shining like flaming fire, carrying sacrificial firewood and Kusha grass and preeminent  among sages, entering that leaf hut.
ramayan::1321.english_translation: Then Indra saw the great ascetic Gautama entering the leaf hut—unassailable by devas and asuras, endowed with the power of austerity, drenched with sacred waters, shining like fire, and carrying sacrificial fuel and kusa grass.
ramayan::1321.translation_literal: गौतमं (Gautama) / तं (that) / ददर्श (saw) / अथ (then) / प्रविशन्तं (entering) / महामुनिम् (great ascetic) / देवदानवदुर्धर्षं (hard to assail by devas and asuras) / तपोबलसमन्वितम् (endowed with ascetic power) / तीर्थेंदकपरिक्लिन्नं (drenched with sacred waters) / दीप्यमानमिव (as if shining) / अनलम् (fire) / गृहीतसमिधं (holding fuel) / तत्र (there) / सकुशं (with kusa grass) / मुनिपुङ्गवम् (best among sages)
ramayan::1321.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1321.essence: The one who has been wronged returns stronger than the one who acted.
ramayan::1321.simple_meaning: Indra sees Gautama returning to his hut, carrying the signs of ritual life and glowing with ascetic power.
ramayan::1321.simple_insight: The man Indra wronged is not weak at all.
ramayan::1321.detailed_meaning: After his secret act with Ahalya, Indra looks up and sees Gautama returning to the leaf hut. The sage is soaked from ritual waters, carrying sacrificial fuel and kusa grass, and appears blazing with tapas. The scene builds the fear that will follow.
ramayan::1321.modern_relevance: You can feel the moment when someone you wronged walks back in, calm and unbroken. The body may look ordinary; the force behind it is not.
ramayan::1321.insight: It sets up the confrontation by showing Gautama's moral and spiritual strength before Indra's fear.

ramayan::1322.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा सुरपतिस्त्रस्तो विवर्णवदनोऽभवत् । अथ दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षं मुनिवेषधरं मुनि: । । 14826 । । दुर्वृत्तं वृत्तसम्पन्नो रोषाद्वचनमब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1322.verse_hindi: On seeing him, the face of the Lord of the gods (Indra) turned pale with fear. Having seen the wicked Indra with a thousandeyed in the guise of an ascetic the gentle sage Gautama got enraged and said:
ramayan::1322.english_translation: On seeing him, the face of the Lord of the gods turned pale with fear. Having seen the thousand-eyed one in the guise of an ascetic, the virtuous sage Gautama grew angry and spoke.
ramayan::1322.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / सुरपतिः (the lord of the gods) / त्रस्तः (frightened) / विवर्णवदनः (with pale face) / अभवत् (became) / अथ (then) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / सहस्राक्षम् (the thousand-eyed one) / मुनिवेषधरम् (wearing the guise of an ascetic) / मुनिः (the sage) / दुर्वृत्तम् (the wicked one) / वृत्तसम्पन्नः (endowed with virtue) / रोषात् (from anger) / वचनम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1322.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1322.essence: Hidden wrongdoing turns to fear the moment it is seen.
ramayan::1322.simple_meaning: Indra is frightened when Gautama appears, and Gautama becomes angry on seeing Indra disguised as an ascetic.
ramayan::1322.simple_insight: Deception may win a moment, but it cannot hide from the one it wounds.
ramayan::1322.detailed_meaning: After Indra takes Ahalya in disguise, Gautama returns and catches him. The scene turns instantly from secret desire to exposed shame: Indra pales, Gautama burns with anger, and the curse that follows becomes inevitable.
ramayan::1322.modern_relevance: You can tell when someone has crossed a line and knows it. The room changes before anyone speaks, and the truth lands in the silence.
ramayan::1322.insight: It shows how wrongdoing collapses under direct sight and triggers immediate moral consequence.

ramayan::1323.verse_sanskrit: मम रूपं समास्थाय कृतवानसि दुर्मते । । 14827 । । अकर्तव्यमिदं तस्माद्विफलस्त्वं भविष्यसि ।
ramayan::1323.verse_hindi: O Wicked natured one assuming my form you have done a forbidden act. For that reason you shall be devoid of  scrotum.
ramayan::1323.english_translation: O wicked one, assuming my form, you have done a forbidden act. Therefore you will be left fruitless.
ramayan::1323.translation_literal: मम (my) / रूपं (form) / समास्थाय (having assumed) / कृतवानसि (you have done) / दुर्मते (O wicked-minded one) / अकर्तव्यम् (not to be done / forbidden) / इदम् (this) / तस्मात् (therefore) / विफलः (fruitless) / त्वम् (you) / भविष्यसि (will become)
ramayan::1323.speaker: Gautama
ramayan::1323.essence: Disguised wrongdoing still brings its own loss.
ramayan::1323.simple_meaning: Indra took Gautama’s form and committed a forbidden act. Gautama curses him, saying the act will leave him diminished and fruitless.
ramayan::1323.simple_insight: Wrong done in disguise still harms the one who chose it.
ramayan::1323.detailed_meaning: Gautama catches Indra entering in disguise after deceiving Ahalya. The sage sees through the act immediately and speaks a curse, turning divine misconduct into irreversible loss. The moment exposes the cost of abusing power.
ramayan::1323.modern_relevance: You use a fake account, a borrowed identity, or a hidden angle to get what you want. The damage may be delayed, but the act still shapes who you become.
ramayan::1323.insight: It shifts attention from cleverness to consequence, especially when wrongdoing hides behind a mask.

ramayan::1324.verse_sanskrit: गौतमेनैवमुक्तस्य सरोषेण महात्मना । । 14828 । । पेततुर्वृषणै भूमौ सहस्राक्षस्य तत्क्षणात् ।
ramayan::1324.verse_hindi: Cursed thus out of anger by eminent Gautama the  testicles of Indra immediately dropped down on the earth.
ramayan::1324.english_translation: Cursed in anger by the great Gautama, Indra's testicles fell to the earth at once.
ramayan::1324.translation_literal: गौतमेन (by Gautama) / एवम् (thus) / उक्तस्य (having been spoken to) / सरोषेण (in anger) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one) / पेततुः (fell) / वृषणौ (the two testicles) / भूमौ (to the earth) / सहस्राक्षस्य (of the thousand-eyed one) / तत्क्षणात् (at that moment)
ramayan::1324.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1324.essence: The curse lands instantly, and power cannot stop the consequence.
ramayan::1324.simple_meaning: Gautama's curse takes effect immediately, and Indra is shamed by the loss of his virility.
ramayan::1324.simple_insight: A forbidden act can bring instant ruin, even for the powerful.
ramayan::1324.detailed_meaning: Gautama has just discovered Indra in his own form, after the deception around Ahalya. In a burst of righteous anger, he pronounces a curse, and this verse shows the curse landing at once.
ramayan::1324.modern_relevance: A lie at work gets exposed in one email thread, and the fallout is immediate. Power does not soften consequences when the breach is clear.
ramayan::1324.insight: It shows that hidden wrongdoing can collapse the moment it is named.

ramayan::1325.verse_sanskrit: तथा शप्त्वा स वै शक्रमहल्यामपि शप्तवान् । । 14829 । । इह वर्षसहस्राणि बहूनि त्वं निवत्स्यसि । वायुभक्षा निराहारा तप्यन्ती भस्मशायिनी । । 14830 । । अदृश्या सर्वभूतानां आश्रमेऽस्मिन्निवत्स्यसि ।
ramayan::1325.verse_hindi: Having thus cursed Indra, he also cursed Ahalya: You will be staying here for thousands of years without food and subsisting on air, lying down in ashes, doing penance, without being seen by any living beings in this ashrama.
ramayan::1325.english_translation: Having thus cursed Indra, he also cursed Ahalya: You will dwell here for thousands of years, living on air, without food, performing austerity, lying on ashes, unseen by all beings in this hermitage.
ramayan::1325.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / शप्त्वा (having cursed) / सः (he) / वै (indeed) / शक्रम् (Indra) / अहल्याम् (Ahalya) / अपि (also) / शप्तवान् (cursed) / इह (here) / वर्षसहस्राणि (thousands of years) / बहूनि (many) / त्वम् (you) / निवत्स्यसि (will dwell) / वायुभक्षा (air-eating) / निराहारा (without food) / तप्यन्ती (performing austerity) / भस्मशायिनी (lying on ashes) / अदृश्या (unseen) / सर्वभूतानाम् (of all beings) / आश्रमे अस्मिन् (in this hermitage) / निवत्स्यसि (you will dwell)
ramayan::1325.speaker: Gautama
ramayan::1325.essence: The punishment is not just pain; it is years of being unseen.
ramayan::1325.simple_meaning: Gautama also curses Ahalya to remain in the hermitage for a long time, fasting, enduring austerity, and unseen by anyone.
ramayan::1325.simple_insight: Some consequences isolate you completely before release comes.
ramayan::1325.detailed_meaning: After catching Indra in his deception, Gautama turns to Ahalya and pronounces her punishment too. She must remain in the hermitage for ages, living on air, without food, unseen by all, until Rama later arrives.
ramayan::1325.modern_relevance: A mistake at home can leave someone living inside silence for years. The damage is not only in the act itself, but in the long afterlife of shame and separation.
ramayan::1325.insight: It shows how a single breach can turn into prolonged isolation and austerity.

ramayan::1326.verse_sanskrit: यदा चैतद्वनं घोरं रामो दशरथात्मज: । । 14831 । । आगमिष्यति दुर्धर्षस्तदा पूता भविष्यसि ।
ramayan::1326.verse_hindi: When the son of Dasaratha, the unassailable Rama enters this dreadful forest, you will be cleansed (of this sin).
ramayan::1326.english_translation: When the son of Dasaratha, the unassailable Rama, enters this dreadful forest, you will be cleansed.
ramayan::1326.translation_literal: यदा (when) / च (and) / एतत् (this) / वनम् (forest) / घोरम् (dreadful) / रामः (Rama) / दशरथात्मजः (son of Dasaratha) / आगमिष्यति (will come) / दुर्धर्षः (unassailable) / तदा (then) / पूता (purified) / भविष्यसि (you will become)
ramayan::1326.speaker: Gautama
ramayan::1326.essence: Rama's arrival can end what punishment began.
ramayan::1326.simple_meaning: Ahalya is told that when Rama comes to this forest, she will be purified and released from the curse.
ramayan::1326.simple_insight: Even long punishment can end the moment grace arrives.
ramayan::1326.detailed_meaning: Gautama has cursed Ahalya to remain in the forest for ages. But he also names the condition for her release: the arrival of Rama, Dasaratha's son, whose presence will restore her. The curse is not final.
ramayan::1326.modern_relevance: You can carry shame for years and still not be beyond repair. One clean encounter, one true act, one person who sees clearly can change everything.
ramayan::1326.insight: It shifts the mind from permanent condemnation to the possibility of restoration.

ramayan::1327.verse_sanskrit: तस्यातिथ्येन दुर्वुत्ते लोभमोहविवर्जिता । । 14832 । । मत्सकाशे मुदा युक्ता स्वं वपुर्धारयिष्यसि ।
ramayan::1327.verse_hindi: O Wickednatured one by offering hospitality to Rama, without covetousness and passion, you will happily live with me by regaining your present form.
ramayan::1327.english_translation: By offering hospitality to Rama, you will be freed from greed and delusion, and you will gladly regain your own body and live with me.
ramayan::1327.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / आतिथ्येन (by hospitality) / दुर्वृत्ते (O wicked-natured one) / लोभ-मोह-विवर्जिता (free from greed and delusion) / मत्-सकाशे (in my presence) / मुदा (with joy) / युक्ता (joined) / स्वम् (own) / वपुः (body, form) / धारयिष्यसि (you will regain/hold)
ramayan::1327.speaker: Gautama
ramayan::1327.essence: A true welcome can become the moment of release.
ramayan::1327.simple_meaning: Ahalya will be purified when Rama is received as an honored guest, and she will regain her form and joy.
ramayan::1327.simple_insight: Even after ruin, sincere welcome can become the beginning of restoration.
ramayan::1327.detailed_meaning: Gautama has already cursed Ahalya and named the condition for release: when Rama enters this forest and is received properly, her long punishment ends. The verse turns hospitality into the doorway back to dignity.
ramayan::1327.modern_relevance: You return home after saying the wrong thing and feeling the room go cold. Then someone still offers you tea, a chair, and a chance to begin again.
ramayan::1327.insight: It shifts you to see welcome as an act that can heal shame and reopen a broken life.

ramayan::1328.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा गौतमो दुष्टचारिणीम् । । 14833 । । इममाश्रममुत्सृज्य सिद्धचारणसेविते । हिमवच्छिखरे पुण्ये तपस्तेपे महातपा: । । 14834 । ।
ramayan::1328.verse_hindi: Highly powerful Gautama who had performed rigid austerities thus cursed the wicked Ahalya and left this hermitage, for the peaks of Himavat mountain served by siddhas and charanas. Here he performed austerities(said Viswamitra).
ramayan::1328.english_translation: Having spoken thus, the mighty Gautama left that wicked woman and went to the sacred peak of Himavat, frequented by siddhas and charanas, where the great ascetic performed austerities.
ramayan::1328.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / महातेजा (the highly radiant one) / गौतमो (Gautama) / दुष्टचारिणीम् (the wicked woman) / इमम् (this) / आश्रमम् (hermitage) / उत्सृज्य (having left) / सिद्धचारणसेविते (frequented by siddhas and charanas) / हिमवच्छिखरे (on the peak of Himavat) / पुण्ये (sacred) / तपः (austerity) / तेपे (performed)
ramayan::1328.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1328.essence: Betrayal ends one life; disciplined withdrawal begins another.
ramayan::1328.simple_meaning: Gautama curses Ahalya, leaves the hermitage, and goes to a sacred mountain peak to continue his austerities.
ramayan::1328.simple_insight: Some wounds end a place forever. He leaves, and the life he had there is over.
ramayan::1328.detailed_meaning: After cursing Ahalya, Gautama abandons the hermitage where betrayal has shattered trust. He goes to the sacred heights of Himavat, beyond ordinary life, and resumes severe austerity. The verse marks his withdrawal from broken domestic life into ascetic discipline.
ramayan::1328.modern_relevance: You walk out of a home after one betrayal too many. The room is still there, but the life you built inside it is gone, and you choose silence over staying.
ramayan::1328.insight: It shifts attention from punishment to withdrawal: when trust breaks, he turns away and recommits to austerity.

ramayan::1329.verse_hindi: Deprived of testicles, Indra with a frightened face addressed hordes of rishis and charanas with agni in the forefront.
ramayan::1329.english_translation: Then Indra, now impotent and frightened, addressed the gods, with Agni in the lead, along with the groups of sages and celestial singers.
ramayan::1329.translation_literal: अफलः (deprived of testicles / impotent) / ततो (then) / शक्रः (Indra) / देवान् (the gods) / अग्निपुरोगमान् (with Agni in the forefront) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / त्रस्तवदनः (with frightened face) / सर्षिस्सङ्घान् (to the groups of sages) / सचारणान् (and charanas)
ramayan::1329.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1329.essence: Power without restraint ends in public shame.
ramayan::1329.simple_meaning: Indra, humiliated and afraid, turns to the gods and the assembled sages for help.
ramayan::1329.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when consequences finally arrive.
ramayan::1329.detailed_meaning: After Gautama's curse has taken effect, Indra is left shamed and powerless. With Agni leading the assembly of gods, sages, and celestial singers, he speaks in fear. The verse is a scene of reaction, not teaching.
ramayan::1329.modern_relevance: You get called out in front of everyone, and the confidence drains from your face. The room knows before you speak that the damage is real.
ramayan::1329.insight: It shows the collapse that follows hidden wrongdoing being exposed.

ramayan::1330.verse_sanskrit: कुर्वता तपसो विघ्नं गौतमस्य महात्मन: । क्रोधमुत्पाद्य हि मया सुरकार्यमिदं कृतम् । । 1492 । ।
ramayan::1330.verse_hindi: I have accomplished the objective of the devatas by creating obstacles to Gautamas  austerities, evoking in consequence the wrath of the magnanimous sage.
ramayan::1330.english_translation: I have accomplished the objective of the devas by creating an obstacle to Gautama's austerities and thereby arousing the wrath of the great sage.
ramayan::1330.translation_literal: कुर्वता (by creating) / तपसः (of austerity) / विघ्नम् (obstacle) / गौतमस्य (of Gautama) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / क्रोधम् (anger) / उत्पाद्य (having aroused) / हि (indeed) / मया (by me) / सुर-कार्यम् (the devas' task) / इदम् (this) / कृतम् (done)
ramayan::1330.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1330.essence: A hidden motive can turn service into betrayal.
ramayan::1330.simple_meaning: Indra admits that he disrupted Gautama's austerity in order to help the devas, and that this provoked the sage's anger.
ramayan::1330.simple_insight: Pursuing a hidden aim can leave a trail of harm and shame.
ramayan::1330.detailed_meaning: After the curse has already struck, Indra confesses his role in the deception. He says he interrupted Gautama's austerities, not by accident but to serve the devas' purpose, and that his act triggered the sage's wrath. The verse is part of a confession, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::1330.modern_relevance: You cut a corner to protect your own advantage, then watch the fallout spread farther than you meant. The damage is real even when your excuse sounds noble.
ramayan::1330.insight: It reveals how self-justifying motives can disguise harm until the consequences arrive.

ramayan::1331.verse_sanskrit: अफलोऽस्मि कृतस्तेन क्रोधात्सा च निराकृता । शापमोक्षेण महता तपोऽस्यापहृतं मया । । 1493 । ।
ramayan::1331.verse_hindi: By his (Gautamas) wrath I have been deprived of my testicles. She (Ahalya) has  been deserted by him. He has lost his ascetic energy through the pronouncement of this great curse.
ramayan::1331.english_translation: By Gautama's wrath I was left without testicles. Ahalya was abandoned by him. Through this great curse, he lost the power of his austerity.
ramayan::1331.translation_literal: अफलः (without fruit / powerless) / अस्मि (I am) / कृतः (made) / तेन (by him) / क्रोधात् (through anger) / सा (she) / च (and) / निराकृता (cast off / abandoned) / शापमोक्षेण (by the release of the curse) / महता (great) / तपः (austerity power) / अस्य (his) / अपहृतम् (taken away) / मया (by me)
ramayan::1331.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1331.essence: A single act of interference leaves three lives wounded.
ramayan::1331.simple_meaning: Indra admits that Gautama's anger has cost him his virility, Ahalya has been cast aside, and Gautama's austerity has been damaged by the curse.
ramayan::1331.simple_insight: A selfish act can leave everyone diminished, including the one who caused it.
ramayan::1331.detailed_meaning: Indra is confessing the damage caused by his interference in Gautama's austerities. Ahalya has been abandoned, Gautama's ascetic power has been broken by the curse, and Indra himself has been mutilated. The verse is part of his plea to the assembled beings.
ramayan::1331.modern_relevance: You meddled where you had no right to, and now everyone is carrying the damage. The harm spreads farther than the original mistake.
ramayan::1331.insight: It shifts attention from personal advantage to the wider ruin caused by violating another's discipline.

ramayan::1332.verse_sanskrit: तस्मात्सुरवरास्सर्वे सर्षिस्सङ्घास्सचारणा: । सुरसाह्यकरं सर्वे सफलं कर्तुमर्हथ । । 1494 । ।
ramayan::1332.verse_hindi: For that reason, O rishis, charanas and great devatas it is your duty to restore my testicles for the benefit I have given you.
ramayan::1332.english_translation: Therefore, O best of the radiant beings, all rishis, charanas, and devas should complete this task that helps the radiant beings.
ramayan::1332.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / सुरवराः (O best of the radiant beings) / सर्वे (all) / सर्षिस्सङ्घाः (with groups of rishis) / सचारणा: (and charanas) / सुरसाह्यकरं (helping the radiant beings) / सर्वे (all) / सफलं (successful / fruitful) / कर्तुम् (to do / complete) / अर्हथ (you should / are worthy to)
ramayan::1332.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1332.simple_meaning: Indra asks the assembled radiant beings, sages, and celestial singers to finish a task that will help him and the other radiant beings.
ramayan::1332.simple_insight: Help given in crisis is a shared responsibility, not a private favour.
ramayan::1332.detailed_meaning: Indra, speaking after his loss and anger, turns to the assembled rishis, charanas, and devas. He is no longer making a complaint; he is asking them to complete the work that will restore what was taken and support the wider order of the radiant beings.
ramayan::1332.modern_relevance: A team knows the project is stuck, and one person cannot fix it alone. This is the moment someone says, clearly, that the repair belongs to everyone who benefited from the work.
ramayan::1332.insight: It shifts attention from personal grievance to collective repair.

ramayan::1333.verse_hindi: Hearing Indra, all the devatas accompanied by maruts. Lead by the Firegod devatas approached and said:
ramayan::1333.english_translation: Hearing Indra, all the devatas, led by Agni, approached the ancestors and said this together with the Maruts.
ramayan::1333.translation_literal: शतक्रतोः (of Indra) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / देवाः (the devatas) / अग्नि-पुरोगमाः (led by Agni) / पितृ-देवान् (to the ancestral deities) / उपेत्य (having approached) / आहुः (said) / सह (together) / सर्वैः (with all) / मरुत्-गणैः (with the groups of Maruts)
ramayan::1333.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1333.essence: The request has been heard, and the response is already moving.
ramayan::1333.simple_meaning: The devatas, led by Agni and joined by the Maruts, go to the ancestors after hearing Indra's request.
ramayan::1333.simple_insight: Some problems need the whole community to answer, not one voice alone.
ramayan::1333.detailed_meaning: Indra has just asked the gods to restore what was lost. In response, the devatas, led by Agni and accompanied by the Maruts, move together toward the ancestral deities. The verse is a bridge in the larger exchange, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1333.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with replies after one urgent message lands. Everyone knows the request matters, but the real action begins when the right people gather and move together.
ramayan::1333.insight: It marks the shift from complaint to collective response.

ramayan::1334.verse_sanskrit: अयं मेषस्सवृषणश्शक्रो ह्यवृषण: कृत: । मेषस्य वृषणौ गृह्य शक्रायाऽशु प्रयच्छथ । । 1496 । ।
ramayan::1334.verse_hindi: This ram (which has received the share of your sacrificial offerings) has testicles. As
ramayan::1334.english_translation: This ram, which has received a share of your sacrificial offerings, has testicles. Quickly take the ram's testicles and give them to Indra.
ramayan::1334.translation_literal: अयं (this) / मेषः (ram) / सवृषणः (with testicles) / शक्रः (Indra) / हि (indeed) / अवृषणः (without testicles) / कृतः (made) / मेषस्य (of the ram) / वृषणौ (the two testicles) / गृह्य (taking) / शक्राय (to Indra) / आशु (quickly) / प्रयच्छथ (give)
ramayan::1334.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1334.essence: A cosmic problem is solved by a blunt, practical substitution.
ramayan::1334.simple_meaning: The gods need to restore Indra's lost testicles by taking them from a ram that already received sacrificial shares.
ramayan::1334.simple_insight: Some remedies are strange, but the demand for balance still stands.
ramayan::1334.detailed_meaning: The gods, led by Agni, have come to answer Indra's plea after his testicles were cut off. They identify a sacrificial ram as the source of replacement and instruct the gods to restore Indra immediately. This verse is a practical step in a larger mythic repair.
ramayan::1334.modern_relevance: A team discovers the fix is awkward, improvised, and not at all elegant — but the problem still has to be solved now.
ramayan::1334.insight: It shows how mythic stories often move through concrete, procedural acts rather than abstract explanation.

ramayan::1335.verse_sanskrit: अफलस्तु कृतो मेष: परां तुष्टिं प्रदास्यति । भवतां हर्षणार्थाय ये च दास्यन्ति मानवा: । । 1497 । ।
ramayan::1335.verse_hindi: अफलस्तु कृतो मेष: परां तुष्टिं प्रदास्यति । भवतां हर्षणार्थाय ये च दास्यन्ति मानवा: । । 1497 । ।
ramayan::1335.english_translation: The ram, made infertile, will grant great satisfaction and bring joy to those humans who offer it.
ramayan::1335.translation_literal: अफलस्तु (made infertile) / कृतो (made) / मेषः (ram) / पराम् (greatest) / तुष्टिम् (satisfaction) / प्रदास्यति (will give) / भवताम् (of you all) / हर्षणार्थाय (for delight) / ये (those who) / च (and) / दास्यन्ति (will offer) / मानवाḥ (humans)
ramayan::1335.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1335.essence: A ritual fix is being made so the offering can be accepted.
ramayan::1335.simple_meaning: The ram is being altered so it can satisfy the ritual and please the people who offer it.
ramayan::1335.simple_insight: Even a strange ritual act is framed as something meant to restore order and satisfaction.
ramayan::1335.detailed_meaning: The gods and ancestors are gathered around a sacrifice. A problem has appeared in the offering, and the Firegod is explaining how to correct it. This line is part of that technical exchange, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1335.insight: It shows a ritual correction being justified as necessary for the sacrifice to work properly.

ramayan::1336.verse_sanskrit: अग्नेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा पितृदेवास्समागता: । उत्पाट्य मेषवृषणौ सहस्राक्षे न्यवेशयन् । । 1498 । ।
ramayan::1336.verse_hindi: Hearing the words of the Firegod the pitrudevatas assembled, uprooted the testicles of the ram and grafted them on to Indra.
ramayan::1336.english_translation: Hearing the words of the Firegod, the ancestral deities assembled, uprooted the ram's testicles, and grafted them onto Indra.
ramayan::1336.translation_literal: अग्नेः (of the Firegod) / तु (then) / वचनम् (word) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / पितृदेवाः (the ancestral deities) / समागताः (assembled) / उत्पाट्य (having uprooted) / मेषवृषणौ (the ram's testicles) / सहस्राक्षे (onto Indra, the thousand-eyed one) / न्यवेशयन् (placed / grafted)
ramayan::1336.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1336.essence: A ritual anomaly is resolved through divine intervention.
ramayan::1336.simple_meaning: The ancestral deities followed the Firegod's instruction and transferred the ram's testicles to Indra.
ramayan::1336.simple_insight: It is a ritual explanation, not a moral lesson.
ramayan::1336.detailed_meaning: In a sacrificial story, the Firegod's words are obeyed by the ancestral deities. They act on a strange ritual problem by removing the ram's testicles and attaching them to Indra, setting up the custom explained in the next verse.
ramayan::1336.insight: It explains the ritual origin of a sacrificial practice.

ramayan::1337.verse_sanskrit: तदा प्रभृति काकुत्स्थ पितृदेवास्समागता: । अफलान् भुञ्जते मेषान् फलैस्तेषामयोजयन् । । 1499 । ।
ramayan::1337.verse_hindi: O Son of the Kakutsthas from then on the pitrudevatas have been accepting rams  without testicles as offerings in a sacrifice, with rams testicles fitted on to Indra.
ramayan::1337.english_translation: O Son of the Kakutsthas, from then on the pitrudevatas have been accepting rams without testicles as offerings in sacrifice, with the rams' testicles fitted to Indra.
ramayan::1337.translation_literal: तदा प्रभृति (from then on) / काकुत्स्थ (O Son of the Kakutsthas) / पितृदेवाः (the pitrudevatas) / समागताः (assembled) / अफलान् (without fruits/testicles) / भुञ्जते (eat/accept) / मेषान् (rams) / फलैः (with fruits/testicles) / तेषाम् (their) / अयोजयन् (fitted/attached)
ramayan::1337.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1337.essence: A sacrifice changes shape, but the ritual order is preserved.
ramayan::1337.simple_meaning: From that time onward, the ancestral deities accepted sacrificial rams without testicles, after the missing parts were attached to Indra's ram.
ramayan::1337.simple_insight: No ritual loss is permanent; even what is taken away can be restored in another form.
ramayan::1337.detailed_meaning: In a mythic explanation of sacrifice, the pitrudevatas gather after hearing Fire's words and agree to accept rams without testicles. The missing parts are then attached to Indra's ram, establishing a ritual rule for future offerings.
ramayan::1337.insight: It explains a ritual exception by tracing how the missing part was reassigned.

ramayan::1338.verse_sanskrit: इन्द्रस्तु मेषवृषणस्तदाप्रभृति राघव । गौतमस्य प्रभावेन तपसश्च महात्मन: । । 14910 । ।
ramayan::1338.verse_hindi: O Son of the Raghus illustrious Gautamas power of ascetism was such that thenceforth Indra possessed the testicles of a ram.
ramayan::1338.english_translation: O Rama, from that time onward Indra had the testicles of a ram because of Gautama's power and that great ascetic's austerity.
ramayan::1338.translation_literal: इन्द्रस्तु (Indra indeed) / मेषवृषणः (ram-testicled) / तदा-प्रभृति (from then onward) / राघव (O Rama) / गौतमस्य (of Gautama) / प्रभावेन (by the power) / तपसः (of austerity) / च (and) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one)
ramayan::1338.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1338.essence: Gautama's austerity left a mark even on Indra.
ramayan::1338.simple_meaning: Indra was marked by the result of Gautama's curse and ascetic power. The verse explains why the gods later accepted ram offerings.
ramayan::1338.simple_insight: Powerful actions leave consequences that do not fade quietly.
ramayan::1338.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is explaining the strange ritual detail behind Ahalya's story. Gautama's austerity had such force that even Indra was made to bear a ram's mark. The verse supports the larger scene, where Rama is about to enter the hermitage and restore what was broken.
ramayan::1338.modern_relevance: A careless act can leave a mark that everyone notices later. Some consequences are not dramatic in the moment, but they reshape how the whole story is remembered.
ramayan::1338.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the lasting consequence of violated restraint.

ramayan::1339.verse_sanskrit: तदागच्छ महातेज आश्रमं पुण्यकर्मण: । तारयैनां महाभागामहल्यां देवरूपिणीम् । । 14911 । ।
ramayan::1339.verse_hindi: Most brilliant Rama therefore enter the hermitage of the pious (Gautama) and liberate  this fortunate Ahalya of divine appearance (from the curse).
ramayan::1339.english_translation: Therefore, O most radiant Rama, enter the hermitage of the man of holy deeds and free the blessed Ahalya, who has a divine form.
ramayan::1339.translation_literal: तदा (therefore/then) / आगच्छ (come/enter) / महातेजः (O most radiant one) / आश्रमम् (hermitage) / पुण्यकर्मणः (of the one of holy deeds) / तारय (liberate/ferry across) / एनाम् (her) / महाभागाम् (blessed one) / अहल्याम् (Ahalya) / देवरूपिणीम् (of divine appearance)
ramayan::1339.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1339.essence: True radiance shows itself by freeing the one who has been held back.
ramayan::1339.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra asks Rama to go into Gautama's hermitage and free Ahalya from the curse that has held her there.
ramayan::1339.simple_insight: Real strength is not only conquest; it is restoring someone who has been trapped.
ramayan::1339.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has brought Rama and Lakshmana to a haunted hermitage where Ahalya still waits under a curse. He now asks Rama to enter the place and release her, turning a test of courage into an act of rescue.
ramayan::1339.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has been blamed for years, and everyone else has already moved on. The brave thing is not to judge faster — it is to help restore them.
ramayan::1339.insight: It shifts action from proving power to using power for repair.

ramayan::1340.verse_hindi: In response to the words of Viswamitra Rama and Lakshmana entered the  hermitage, Viswamitra in front.
ramayan::1340.english_translation: Hearing Vishvamitra's words, Rama and Lakshmana entered the hermitage with Vishvamitra leading the way.
ramayan::1340.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रवचः (Vishvamitra's words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राघवः (Rama) / सहलक्ष्मणः (together with Lakshmana) / विश्वामित्रम् (Vishvamitra) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front) / तम् (that) / आश्रमम् (hermitage) / अथ (then) / अविशत् (entered)
ramayan::1340.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1340.essence: Real change begins when you follow the right guide without delay.
ramayan::1340.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana followed Vishvamitra into the hermitage after hearing his instruction.
ramayan::1340.simple_insight: Some moments matter only because you were willing to follow without hesitation.
ramayan::1340.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just told Rama why Ahalya must be freed. Rama and Lakshmana do not argue or delay; they follow him straight into the hermitage. The verse simply moves the scene forward toward the meeting with Ahalya.
ramayan::1340.modern_relevance: You get the message, stop asking for more proof, and walk into the difficult conversation with the person who knows the way.
ramayan::1340.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to obedient movement: hear clearly, then step forward.

ramayan::1341.verse_sanskrit: ददर्श च महाभागां तपसा द्योतितप्रभाम् । लोकैरपि समागम्य दुर्निरीक्ष्यां सुरासुरै: । । 14913 । । प्रयत्नान्निर्मितां धात्रा दिव्यां मायामयीमिव । स तुषारावृतां साभ्रां पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव । । 14914 । । मध्येंऽभसो दुराधर्षां दीप्तां सूर्यप्रभामिव ।
ramayan::1341.verse_hindi: Rama beheld the highly fortunate Ahalya, shining brilliantly with the power of her asceticism. She could not be seen even by men, suras or asuras joined together. She looked  divine and illusory as if created with special efforts by Brahma. Though not clearly visible, she was shining bright like the light of the full Moon muffled by mists in the sky and like the inviolable light of the Sun reflected in the water.
ramayan::1341.english_translation: Rama saw the highly fortunate Ahalya, whose brilliance shone through her ascetic power. No one could easily behold her, not even gods or demons together. She seemed divinely fashioned, like a full moon veiled by mist and like the sun reflected in water.
ramayan::1341.translation_literal: ददर्श (saw) / च (and) / महाभागाम् (highly fortunate) / तपसा (by ascetic power) / द्योतितप्रभाम् (whose brilliance was illuminated) / लोकैः (by beings) / अपि (even) / समागम्य (having come together) / दुर्निरीक्ष्याम् (hard to behold) / सुरासुरैः (by gods and demons) / प्रयत्नात् (with effort) / निर्मिताम् (fashioned) / धात्रा (by the creator) / दिव्याम् (divine) / मायामयीम् (seeming illusory) / इव (as if) / सः (he) / तुषारावृताम् (covered by mist) / साभ्राम् (with clouds) / पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभाम् (like the radiance of the full moon) / इव (as if) / मध्ये (in the middle) / अश्भसः (of water) / दुराधर्षाम् (hard to assail / inviolable) / दीप्ताम् (shining) / सूर्यप्रभाम् (like the sun's radiance) / इव (as if)
ramayan::1341.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1341.essence: Long endurance can make a person radiant and nearly impossible to see clearly.
ramayan::1341.simple_meaning: Ahalya is shown as radiant, hard to behold, and almost otherworldly. The verse compares her to moonlight, sunlight, and something crafted by the creator with great care.
ramayan::1341.simple_insight: Some presence is so refined that ordinary seeing cannot reach it.
ramayan::1341.detailed_meaning: Rama has entered Gautama’s hermitage and now sees Ahalya after her long stillness. Valmiki lingers on her transformed presence: brilliant, difficult to behold, and beyond ordinary sight. The moment prepares for release, not just recognition.
ramayan::1341.modern_relevance: You meet someone after years of quiet endurance and realize they have not been diminished. They have become harder to read, not easier to overlook.
ramayan::1341.insight: It shifts attention from physical appearance to the force created by long discipline and restraint.

ramayan::1342.verse_sanskrit: सा हि गौतमवाक्येन दुर्निरीक्ष्या बभूव ह । । 14915 । । त्रयाणामपि लोकानां यावद्रामस्य दर्शनम् ।
ramayan::1342.verse_hindi: By the words of Gautama, she became invisible to the three worlds till the appearance of Rama.
ramayan::1342.english_translation: By Gautama's words, she became impossible to behold by the three worlds until Rama's arrival.
ramayan::1342.translation_literal: सा (she) / हि (indeed) / गौतमवाक्येन (by Gautama's word) / दुर्निरीक्ष्या (hard to behold) / बभूव (became) / ह (indeed) / त्रयाणाम् (of three) / अपि (even) / लोकानाम् (worlds) / यावत् (until) / रामस्य (of Rama) / दर्शनम् (sight)
ramayan::1342.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1342.essence: A curse can hide someone until the moment meant to reveal them.
ramayan::1342.simple_meaning: Ahalya remained beyond ordinary sight because of Gautama's curse, until Rama came near.
ramayan::1342.simple_insight: Some suffering lasts until the right moment arrives to end it.
ramayan::1342.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana enter Gautama's hermitage with Vishwamitra. They see Ahalya, hidden from the sight of all beings by her husband's curse. This line explains her unseen state just before Rama's arrival breaks it.
ramayan::1342.modern_relevance: You can live for years inside a condition you did not choose, waiting for the moment that changes everything.
ramayan::1342.insight: It frames the curse as a temporary veil that only the right encounter can lift.

ramayan::1343.verse_sanskrit: शापस्यान्तमुपागम्य तेषां दर्शनमागता । । 14916 । । राघवौ तु ततस्तस्या: पादौ जगृहतुस्तदा ।
ramayan::1343.verse_hindi: With the expiry of the period of the curse, the Raghavas (Rama and Lakshmana) speared and she became perceptible when Rama touched her feet.
ramayan::1343.english_translation: With the curse ended, the Raghavas approached her, and then they took hold of her feet.
ramayan::1343.translation_literal: शापस्य (of the curse) / अन्तम् (end) / उपागम्य (having reached) / तेषाम् (of them) / दर्शनम् (sight) / आगता (having become visible) / राघवौ (the two Raghavas) / तु (and) / ततः (then) / तस्याः (of her) / पादौ (feet) / जगृहतुः (took hold of)
ramayan::1343.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1343.essence: Ending the curse does not erase humility.
ramayan::1343.simple_meaning: When the curse ended, Rama and Lakshmana came near Ahalya and bowed to her feet.
ramayan::1343.simple_insight: Respect is shown first through humility, not words.
ramayan::1343.detailed_meaning: Ahalya has remained hidden by Gautama's curse until Rama arrives. When the curse ends, Rama and Lakshmana approach her not as conquerors, but with reverence, taking her feet in respect before the next act of hospitality unfolds.
ramayan::1343.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone after a long silence, and the first thing you do is lower your pride. Real respect begins there.
ramayan::1343.insight: It shifts the moment from rescue to reverence.

ramayan::1344.verse_sanskrit: स्मरन्ती गौतमवच: प्रतिजग्राह सा च तौ । । 14917 । । पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथाऽऽतिथ्यं चकार सुसमाहिता । प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थो विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा । । 14918 । ।
ramayan::1344.verse_hindi: Recalling the words of Gautama, she received them with water to wash their feet and offerings made with due devotion Rama accepted her hospitality extended in accordance tradition.
ramayan::1344.english_translation: Recalling Gautama's words, she received them with water for washing the feet and with proper hospitality. Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, accepted that hospitality in accordance with the prescribed way.
ramayan::1344.translation_literal: स्मरन्ती (recalling) / गौतमवच: (Gautama's words) / प्रतिजग्राह (received) / सा (she) / च (and) / तौ (them) / पाद्यम् (water for the feet) / अर्घ्यम् (offering) / तथा (and) / आतिथ्यम् (hospitality) / चकार (performed) / सुसमाहिता (with careful devotion) / प्रतिजग्राह (accepted) / काकुत्स्थो (the descendant of Kakutstha) / विधिदृष्टेन (as laid down by rule) / कर्मणा (by conduct)
ramayan::1344.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1344.essence: Restoration begins with the smallest act done rightly.
ramayan::1344.simple_meaning: A woman remembers a sage's words, welcomes the visitors properly, and Rama accepts her hospitality in the proper way.
ramayan::1344.simple_insight: Even in a sacred reunion, respect is shown through simple, exact actions.
ramayan::1344.detailed_meaning: Ahalya has been released from the curse and made visible again. Remembering Gautama's instruction, she greets Rama and Lakshmana with ritual hospitality. Rama accepts it as proper conduct, and the moment becomes a quiet restoration of order after long injustice.
ramayan::1344.modern_relevance: You meet someone after years of silence, and the first thing you do is make the moment respectful. Before any big conversation, small acts of care set the tone.
ramayan::1344.insight: It teaches you that right relationship begins with proper conduct, not dramatic emotion.

ramayan::1345.verse_hindi: Amidst sounds of celestial kettledrums, devatas showered flowers, gandharvas sang and apsarasa danced. There was a great assemblage (of divinities).
ramayan::1345.english_translation: Amidst sounds of celestial kettledrums, the radiant beings showered flowers; gandharvas and apsarasa gathered in a great assembly.
ramayan::1345.translation_literal: पुष्पवृष्टिः (shower of flowers) / महती (great) / आसीत् (was) / देवदुन्दुभि-निस्वनैः (with the sounds of celestial kettledrums) / गन्धर्व-अप्सरसाम् (of gandharvas and apsarasa) / च एव (and indeed) / महान् (great) / आसीत् (was) / समागमः (assembly, gathering)
ramayan::1345.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1345.essence: A restored life draws celebration from the whole world.
ramayan::1345.simple_meaning: The heavens respond with celebration as Ahalya is restored and honored. The verse is a scene of divine rejoicing, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1345.simple_insight: Some moments are so right that even the sky seems to celebrate.
ramayan::1345.detailed_meaning: Ahalya has just been restored to sight after the curse ends, and Rama and Lakshmana stand before her. As the next verse shows the radiant beings praising her, this line simply marks the heavenly celebration around that turning point.
ramayan::1345.modern_relevance: When a long, painful season finally breaks, the relief is almost physical — like the whole room suddenly exhaling with you.
ramayan::1345.insight: It marks a scene of cosmic celebration around a completed restoration.

ramayan::1346.verse_sanskrit: साधु साध्विति देवास्तामहल्यां समपूजयन् । तपोबलविशुद्धाङ्गी गौतमस्य वशानुगाम् । । 14920 । ।
ramayan::1346.verse_hindi: On seeing Ahalya, her body purified by the power of penance at Gautamas command, the devatas worshipfully exclaimed, Excellent, Excellent
ramayan::1346.english_translation: The radiant beings praised Ahalya: "Excellent, excellent," seeing her, whose body had been purified by the power of penance and who had followed Gautama's command.
ramayan::1346.translation_literal: साधु साधु (excellent, excellent) / इति (thus) / देवाः (the radiant beings) / ताम् (her) / अहल्याम् (Ahalya) / समपूजयन् (praised respectfully) / तपोबलविशुद्धाङ्गी (whose body was purified by the power of penance) / गौतमस्य (of Gautama) / वशानुगाम् (one who followed the command)
ramayan::1346.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1346.essence: Purity after suffering deserves recognition, not pity.
ramayan::1346.simple_meaning: The radiant beings praised Ahalya because her suffering and discipline had purified her, and she had remained faithful to Gautama.
ramayan::1346.simple_insight: Endurance with integrity can leave you more luminous than before the fall.
ramayan::1346.detailed_meaning: After Rama's presence restores Ahalya to public honor, the radiant beings shower praise on her. The verse does not begin a new teaching; it confirms the greatness already revealed in the scene and prepares for Gautama's return.
ramayan::1346.modern_relevance: After a long, humiliating period, someone finally sees your effort, your restraint, and the cost you carried quietly. Recognition feels different when it comes after purification, not applause.
ramayan::1346.insight: It frames recovery as earned dignity, not mere rescue.

ramayan::1347.verse_sanskrit: गौतमोऽपि महातेजा अहल्यासहितस्सुखी । रामं सम्पूज्य विधिवत्तपस्तेपे महातपा: । । 14921 । ।
ramayan::1347.verse_hindi: Brilliant Gautam, the great ascetic, along with Ahalya, worshipped Rama  according to tradition, with delight and continued with his austerities.
ramayan::1347.english_translation: Brilliant Gautama, the great ascetic, lived happily with Ahalya. He worshipped Rama properly and then resumed his austerities.
ramayan::1347.translation_literal: गौतमः (Gautama) / अपि (also) / महातेजाः (brilliant, great in power) / अहल्यासहितः (together with Ahalya) / सुखी (happy) / रामम् (Rama) / सम्पूज्य (having worshipped) / विधिवत् (according to proper rite) / तपः (austerity) / तेपे (practised) / महातपाः (the great ascetic)
ramayan::1347.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1347.essence: Reconciliation is complete only when reverence becomes ordinary again.
ramayan::1347.simple_meaning: Gautama and Ahalya were reunited in peace. After honouring Rama properly, Gautama returned to his ascetic practice.
ramayan::1347.simple_insight: Some wounds close quietly. Reverence and right action can restore what was broken.
ramayan::1347.detailed_meaning: After Ahalya is restored and honoured by the gods, Gautama stands with her again, free of the old sorrow that shaped their story. He bows to Rama with proper ritual, then returns to the life of austerity that defines him.
ramayan::1347.modern_relevance: After a long family rupture, everyone finally sits in the same room and speaks carefully. The apology is real, the respect is real, and life goes on with a little more humility than before.
ramayan::1347.insight: It shows that healing does not end responsibility; gratitude and discipline continue together.

ramayan::1348.verse_sanskrit: रामोऽपि परमां पूजां गौतमस्य महामुने: । सकाशाद्विधिवत्प्राप्य जगाम मिथिलां तत: । । 14922 । ।
ramayan::1348.verse_hindi: Having received due hospitality from the great ascetic Gautama Rama also set out towards Mithila.
ramayan::1348.english_translation: Having received due hospitality from the great ascetic Gautama, Rama set out towards Mithila.
ramayan::1348.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / अपि (also) / परमाम् (highest, due) / पूजाम् (hospitality, honor) / गौतमस्य (of Gautama) / महामुनेः (of the great sage) / सकाशात् (from the presence of) / विधिवत् (properly, according to custom) / प्राप्य (having received) / जगाम (went) / मिथिलाम् (to Mithila) / ततः (then)
ramayan::1348.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1348.essence: Respect the moment fully, then move on without residue.
ramayan::1348.simple_meaning: Rama accepted Gautama's proper hospitality and then continued on to Mithila.
ramayan::1348.simple_insight: Even a brief stop can be marked by respect before moving on.
ramayan::1348.detailed_meaning: After Ahalya is honoured and Gautama has received Rama with proper respect, the journey resumes. Nothing dramatic happens here; the verse simply closes the episode and sends Rama onward toward Mithila, where the next major event awaits.
ramayan::1348.modern_relevance: You finish a difficult visit, thank your host properly, and then keep moving. Not every moment needs a speech; some moments are about closing with grace and continuing the journey.
ramayan::1348.insight: It teaches you to leave each encounter cleanly, with respect intact.

ramayan::1349.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह । विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञवाटमुपागमत् । । 1501 । ।
ramayan::1349.verse_hindi: Rama accompanied by Lakshmana with Viswamitra ahead proceeded in northeasterly direction and reached the sacrificial ground.
ramayan::1349.english_translation: Rama, with Lakshmana beside him and Viswamitra leading the way, went northeast and reached the sacrificial ground.
ramayan::1349.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रागुत्तरां (northeastward) / गत्वा (having gone) / रामः (Rama) / सौमित्रिणा (with Lakshmana) / सह (together) / विश्वामित्रं (Viswamitra) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front) / यज्ञवाटम् (to the sacrificial ground) / उपागमत् (approached)
ramayan::1349.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1349.essence: Arrival itself can be the first act of dharma.
ramayan::1349.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana travel with Viswamitra to the place where the sacrifice is being held.
ramayan::1349.simple_insight: Sometimes the next right step is simply to arrive where duty calls.
ramayan::1349.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana follow Viswamitra northeast until they reach the sacrificial ground at Janaka's domain. The verse is a movement scene, carrying the story from travel into the setting where the next encounter will unfold.
ramayan::1349.modern_relevance: You leave the car, cross the parking lot, and walk into the meeting you have been avoiding. The real change begins when you actually show up.
ramayan::1349.insight: It shifts attention from planning to arrival: the task begins by entering the right place at the right time.

ramayan::1350.verse_sanskrit: रामस्तु मुनिशार्दूलमुवाच सहलक्ष्मण: । साध्वी यज्ञसमृद्धिर्हि जनकस्य महात्मन: । । 1502 । ।
ramayan::1350.verse_hindi: Rama with Lakshmana told the tiger among ascetics Viswamitra that the preparations or the sacrifice by the illustrious king Janaka were excellent.
ramayan::1350.english_translation: Rama, together with Lakshmana, said to the tiger among ascetics, Viswamitra, that King Janaka's sacrificial preparations were excellent.
ramayan::1350.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / तु (indeed) / मुनि-शार्दूलम् (to the tiger among ascetics) / उवाच (said) / सह-लक्ष्मणः (together with Lakshmana) / साध्वी (excellent) / यज्ञ-समृद्धिः (the sacrificial preparations) / हि (indeed) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / महात्मनः (of the illustrious one)
ramayan::1350.speaker: Rama
ramayan::1350.essence: Respectful speech can open the next moment cleanly.
ramayan::1350.simple_meaning: Rama tells Viswamitra that Janaka's sacrificial arrangements are splendid.
ramayan::1350.simple_insight: Polite recognition matters. Good conduct begins with seeing and naming what is worthy.
ramayan::1350.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have reached Janaka's sacrificial grounds with Viswamitra. Before the larger events begin, Rama acknowledges the scale and order of the king's arrangements. It is a small, courteous moment in a scene that is still unfolding.
ramayan::1350.modern_relevance: You arrive at a well-run event and notice the care behind it before anything begins. A respectful word can set the tone for everything that follows.
ramayan::1350.insight: It models courteous attention before action. You learn to acknowledge order and effort without rushing past them.

ramayan::1351.verse_sanskrit: बहूनीह सहस्राणि नानादेशनिवासिनाम् । ब्राह्मणानां महाभाग वेदाध्ययनशालिनाम् । । 1503 । । ऋषिवाटाश्च दृश्यन्ते शकटीशतसङ्कुला: । देशो विधीयतां ब्रह्मन् यत्र वत्स्यामहे वयम् । । 1504 । ।
ramayan::1351.verse_hindi: O Illustrious sage thousands of brahmins living in different countries and versed in  the study of the vedas have assembled here. The shelters for ascetics are thronged with hundreds of carts. O Great ascetic let us choose a place where we can stay.
ramayan::1351.english_translation: O illustrious sage, thousands of brahmins from many regions, learned in the study of the Vedas, are gathered here. The ascetics' shelters are crowded with hundreds of carts. O great ascetic, let us choose a place where we can stay.
ramayan::1351.translation_literal: बहूनि (many) / इह (here) / सहस्राणि (thousands) / नानादेशनिवासिनाम् (of those living in different regions) / ब्राह्मणानाम् (of brahmins) / महाभाग (O illustrious one) / वेदाध्ययनशालिनाम् (of those skilled in Vedic study) / ऋषिवाटाः (ascetics' shelters) / च (and) / दृश्यन्ते (are seen) / शकटीशतसङ्कुलाः (crowded with hundreds of carts) / देशः (place) / विधीयताम् (let be chosen) / ब्रह्मन् (O great ascetic) / यत्र (where) / वत्स्यामहे (we shall stay) / वयम् (we)
ramayan::1351.speaker: Rama
ramayan::1351.essence: He sees the crowd and asks where they can fit.
ramayan::1351.simple_meaning: Rama notices that the area is packed with sages, scholars, and carts, so he asks Viswamitra to choose a place for them to stay.
ramayan::1351.simple_insight: Sometimes wisdom begins with simply noticing when space is full.
ramayan::1351.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana arrive with Viswamitra at a crowded sacrificial area. Rama sees the thousands of learned brahmins and the packed shelters, then respectfully asks where they should stay. It is a practical moment, not a teaching.
ramayan::1351.modern_relevance: You arrive at a festival ground, parking lot, or train platform and instantly see there is no room left. Before anything else, you need to notice the situation clearly and ask for the right place.
ramayan::1351.insight: It trains attention toward conditions on the ground before making a move.

ramayan::1352.verse_sanskrit: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । निवेशमकरोद्देशे विविक्ते सलिलायुते । । 1505 । ।
ramayan::1352.verse_hindi: Great ascetic Viswamitra, hearing Ramas words, chose a nottoocrowded place near a watersource for encampment.
ramayan::1352.english_translation: Hearing Rama's words, the great ascetic Viswamitra chose a secluded place with water for his camp.
ramayan::1352.translation_literal: रामस्य (of Rama) / वचनं (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / विश्वामित्रो (Viswamitra) / महामुनि: (great ascetic) / निवेशम् (camping/encampment) / अकरोत् (made/chose) / देशे (in a place) / विविक्ते (secluded) / सलिलायुते (endowed with water)
ramayan::1352.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1352.essence: A wise guide first creates the right setting.
ramayan::1352.simple_meaning: Viswamitra hears Rama and sets up camp in a quiet place with water nearby.
ramayan::1352.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response is simple: listen, settle, and choose the place that supports the work.
ramayan::1352.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have arrived with Viswamitra at Janaka's sacrifice. After hearing Rama speak, the sage quietly selects a secluded, water-rich spot for the group to stay. It is a practical scene, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::1352.modern_relevance: You arrive at a crowded retreat center after a long drive, and the first thing you do is look for the quiet corner near water and shade. Some moments call for arrangement, not reflection.
ramayan::1352.insight: It shifts attention from meaning-making to simple, effective preparation.

ramayan::1353.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रमनुप्राप्तं श्रुत्वा स नृपतिस्तदा । शतानन्दं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोहितमनिन्दितम् । । 1506 । । प्रत्युज्जगाम सहसा विनयेन समन्वित: ।
ramayan::1353.verse_hindi: When the king heard of the arrival of Viswamitra he went forward with Satananda, the blemishless family priest walking ahead in order to welcome him with humility.
ramayan::1353.english_translation: When the king heard of Viswamitra's arrival, he quickly went out with humility, placing the blemishless family priest Shatananda in front to welcome him.
ramayan::1353.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रम् (Viswamitra) / अनुप्राप्तम् (having arrived) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सः (he) / नृपतिः (the king) / तदा (then) / शतानन्दम् (Shatananda) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front) / पुरोहितम् (the family priest) / अनिन्दितम् (blemishless) / प्रत्युज्जगाम (went forward to welcome) / सहसा (quickly) / विनयेन (with humility) / समन्वितः (endowed with)
ramayan::1353.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1353.essence: Respect is shown by how you receive someone.
ramayan::1353.simple_meaning: The king welcomes Viswamitra with respect and humility, and he makes sure the family priest leads the reception.
ramayan::1353.simple_insight: Respect becomes visible in how you receive someone, not just in what you say.
ramayan::1353.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arrived, and the king immediately goes out to greet him. He does not act alone; he places Shatananda, the respected family priest, in front. The moment shows courtly honour and careful ritual order.
ramayan::1353.modern_relevance: A senior guest arrives and everyone in the room watches how the host responds. You can feel the difference between a polite greeting and real respect in that first movement toward the door.
ramayan::1353.insight: It teaches you to honour greatness with speed, humility, and proper order.

ramayan::1354.verse_sanskrit: ऋत्विजोऽपि महात्मानस्त्वर्घ्यमादाय सत्वरम् । । 1507 । । विश्वामित्राय धर्मेण ददुर्मंन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् ।
ramayan::1354.verse_hindi: Eminent officiating priests speedily brought the offerings of worship and paid obeisance to Viswamitra with prayers.
ramayan::1354.english_translation: The eminent officiating priests quickly brought offerings and respectfully honored Viswamitra with prayers.
ramayan::1354.translation_literal: ऋत्विजः (officiating priests) / अपि (also) / महात्मानः (great-souled) / तु (indeed) / अर्घ्यम् (offering of honor) / आदाय (having taken) / सत्वरम् (quickly) / विश्वामित्राय (to Viswamitra) / धर्मेण (according to proper conduct) / ददुः (gave) / मन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् (preceded by prayers)
ramayan::1354.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1354.essence: Formal respect comes first, before any real discussion can begin.
ramayan::1354.simple_meaning: The priests hurried to greet Viswamitra properly, bringing offerings and reciting prayers.
ramayan::1354.simple_insight: Respect opens the meeting before any words do.
ramayan::1354.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra arrives at Janaka’s place for the sacrifice, and the king’s priests move at once to receive him with formal honor. The verse simply sets the scene for the respectful welcome before the real conversation begins.
ramayan::1354.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where people are already standing to greet someone important. The moment is about respect, not debate.
ramayan::1354.insight: It shows ceremonial honor before the deeper exchange begins.

ramayan::1355.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां जनकस्य महात्मन: । । 1508 । । पप्रच्छ कुशलं राज्ञो यज्ञस्य च निरामयम् ।
ramayan::1355.verse_hindi: Viswamitra received illustrious king Janakas worship and enquired about the welfare of the king and the conduct of the sacrifice.
ramayan::1355.english_translation: Viswamitra received illustrious king Janaka's worship and enquired about the welfare of the king and the conduct of the sacrifice.
ramayan::1355.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having received) / च (and) / ताम् (that) / पूजाम् (worship) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled) / पप्रच्छ (asked) / कुशलम् (about wellbeing) / राज्ञः (of the king) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / च (and) / निरामयम् (freedom from trouble / welfare)
ramayan::1355.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1355.essence: Courtesy comes first; even a sage begins by asking after wellbeing.
ramayan::1355.simple_meaning: Viswamitra accepts Janaka's welcome and asks how the king and the sacrifice are doing.
ramayan::1355.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before any deeper conversation begins.
ramayan::1355.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra arrives at Janaka's sacrificial gathering and is greeted with honour. He accepts the welcome, then immediately asks about Janaka's wellbeing and whether the sacrifice is proceeding without trouble. It is a courteous transition, not the main teaching.
ramayan::1355.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where tension is high, but you still begin with respect. Before solving anything, you first notice the person and the situation.
ramayan::1355.insight: It models respectful attention before action or inquiry.

ramayan::1356.verse_sanskrit: स तांश्चापि मुनीन् पृष्ट्वा सोपाध्यायपुरोधस: । । 1509 । । यथान्यायं ततस्सर्वैस्समागच्छत्प्रहृष्टवत् ।
ramayan::1356.verse_hindi: Viswamitra duly enquired the wellbeing of the sages and the spiritual teachers, priests in right order. And thereafter the rest joined them in great delight.
ramayan::1356.english_translation: Viswamitra duly enquired about the wellbeing of the sages, teachers, and priests, and then all gathered together in delight.
ramayan::1356.translation_literal: स (he) / तान् (those) / च (also) / अपि (indeed) / मुनीन् (sages) / पृष्ट्वा (having asked) / सोपाध्यायपुरोधसः (with teachers and priests) / यथान्यायम् (according to proper order) / ततः (then) / सर्वैः (by all) / समागच्छत् (came together) / प्रहृष्टवत् (with great joy)
ramayan::1356.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1356.essence: Courtesy creates the space for everything that follows.
ramayan::1356.simple_meaning: Viswamitra politely asked after the wellbeing of the sages, teachers, and priests, and everyone came together happily.
ramayan::1356.simple_insight: Respect begins with simple care for everyone present.
ramayan::1356.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s sacrificial gathering, Viswamitra first greets the assembled sages, teachers, and priests in proper order. This is a social bridge, not a teaching verse: it shows the formal courtesy that clears the way for the king’s next words.
ramayan::1356.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is waiting, and the first thing you do is notice people, not your agenda. That small courtesy changes the whole atmosphere.
ramayan::1356.insight: It models respectful attention before important conversation begins.

ramayan::1357.verse_sanskrit: अथ राजा मुनिश्रेष्ठं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत । । 15010 । । आसने भगवानास्तां सहैभिर्मुनिपुङ्गवै: ।
ramayan::1357.verse_hindi: The king then folded his hands in supplication to the foremost of ascetics, Viswamitra, saying O Venerable one please be seated along with the eminent ascetics.
ramayan::1357.english_translation: Then the king, with folded hands, spoke to the foremost of ascetics: “O venerable one, please be seated here with these eminent sages.”
ramayan::1357.translation_literal: अथ (then) / राजा (the king) / मुनिश्रेष्ठम् (to the foremost of ascetics) / कृताञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / अभाषत (spoke) / आसने (on the seat) / भगवान् (venerable one) / आस्ताम् (please sit) / सह (with) / एभिः (these) / मुनिपुङ्गवैः (with the eminent sages)
ramayan::1357.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1357.essence: A king honors the sage by making room for him.
ramayan::1357.simple_meaning: King Janaka respectfully invites Viswamitra to sit with the other sages.
ramayan::1357.simple_insight: Respect begins with making space for the worthy.
ramayan::1357.detailed_meaning: Janaka has already welcomed Viswamitra and asked after the guests' welfare. Now, with folded hands, he offers the sage a seat among the assembled seers and priests. The moment is courteous ceremony, not teaching.
ramayan::1357.modern_relevance: You stand at the head of a long table and notice the quiet elder still standing. Before the meeting moves on, you make room and invite him in.
ramayan::1357.insight: It models formal respect, not philosophical instruction.

ramayan::1358.verse_sanskrit: जनकस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा निषसाद महामुनि: । । 15011 । । पुरोधा ऋत्विजश्चैव राजा च सह मन्त्रिभि: ।
ramayan::1358.verse_hindi: In response to Janakas words, great sage Viswamitra occupied his seat. Thereafter the family priests, officiationg priests of the sacrifice, counsellors and also the king occupied their seats according to their rank.
ramayan::1358.english_translation: In response to Janaka's words, the great sage Viswamitra took his seat. Then the family priests, officiating priests, the king, and the ministers also sat down in their proper order.
ramayan::1358.translation_literal: जनकस्य (of Janaka) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / निषसाद (sat down) / महामुनिः (great sage) / पुरोधाः (family priests) / ऋत्विजः (sacrificial priests) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / राजा (king) / च (and) / सह (with) / मन्त्रिभिः (ministers)
ramayan::1358.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1358.essence: Proper order creates the space for important speech.
ramayan::1358.simple_meaning: After Janaka spoke, Viswamitra sat down, and the priests, king, and ministers took their places in order.
ramayan::1358.simple_insight: Order matters. Even in a royal gathering, everyone settles into the right place before the next step begins.
ramayan::1358.detailed_meaning: Janaka has welcomed Viswamitra and spoken with respect. The sage sits, and the court follows proper rank: priests, officiants, king, and ministers. It is a quiet ceremonial pause before the real exchange begins.
ramayan::1358.modern_relevance: A conference room goes silent after the senior guest finishes speaking. No one rushes in. People wait, sit, and let the room settle before the decision begins.
ramayan::1358.insight: It teaches you to respect sequence and role before action.

ramayan::1359.verse_sanskrit: आसनेषु यथान्यायमुपविष्टान् समन्तत: । । 15012 । । दृष्ट्वा स नृपतिस्तत्र विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1359.verse_hindi: Thereafter the king looked on all sides and  saw all of them seated  according to their rank and addressed Viswamitra saying:
ramayan::1359.english_translation: Thereafter the king looked on all sides and saw all of them seated according to their rank and addressed Viswamitra saying:
ramayan::1359.translation_literal: आसनेषु (on seats) / यथान्यायम् (according to proper order) / उपविष्टान् (seated) / समन्तत: (all around) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / स (he) / नृपतिः (the king) / तत्र (there) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / अथ (then) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1359.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1359.essence: Proper order prepares the way for sacred speech.
ramayan::1359.simple_meaning: King Janaka sees everyone seated in proper order and turns to speak to Viswamitra.
ramayan::1359.simple_insight: Order matters before sacred work begins.
ramayan::1359.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s sacrificial hall, Viswamitra, the priests, and the king’s ministers have all taken their seats in proper order. Janaka now turns to Viswamitra, preparing to speak after the assembly has settled.
ramayan::1359.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where every chair, name tag, and place setting has been arranged with care. Before the main conversation begins, the atmosphere already tells you this moment matters.
ramayan::1359.insight: It shows that reverence begins with right order and attention to place.

ramayan::1360.verse_sanskrit: अद्य यज्ञसमृध्दिर्मे सफला दैवतै: कृता । । 15013 । । अद्य यज्ञफलं प्राप्तं भगवद्दर्शनान्मया ।
ramayan::1360.verse_hindi: Today my sacrifice has been rendered fruitful by the devatas. I have reaped the fruit of my sacrifice today by your venerable presence.
ramayan::1360.english_translation: Today my sacrifice has been made fruitful by the radiant beings. I have received the reward of my sacrifice through your sacred presence.
ramayan::1360.translation_literal: अद्य (today) / यज्ञसमृध्दिः (success/completion of sacrifice) / मे (of mine) / सफला (fruitful) / दैवतैः (by the radiant beings) / कृता (made) । / अद्य (today) / यज्ञफलं (fruit of sacrifice) / प्राप्तम् (obtained) / भगवद्दर्शनात् (from the holy sight/presence) / मया (by me) ।
ramayan::1360.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1360.essence: Sacred presence can complete what effort alone begins.
ramayan::1360.simple_meaning: Janaka says the sacrifice has truly succeeded because Vishwamitra has arrived and been seen there. The ritual's reward is not just the fire offering, but the honored presence of the holy guest.
ramayan::1360.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that sincere effort feels complete when it is witnessed with respect.
ramayan::1360.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's sacrifice, Vishwamitra has arrived with the sages and taken his seat. Seeing the assembly in order, Janaka turns to the sage and says the rite has now borne fruit, because the honored presence of such a holy guest has sanctified it.
ramayan::1360.modern_relevance: You prepare for days, then the one person whose respect matters walks in and the whole room changes. The work was already done — but their presence makes it feel complete.
ramayan::1360.insight: It shifts attention from ritual performance to the transforming power of honored presence.

ramayan::1361.verse_sanskrit: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुङ्गव । । 15014 । । यज्ञोपसदनं ब्रह्मन् प्राप्तोऽसि मुनिभि: सह ।
ramayan::1361.verse_hindi: O Preeminent among ascetics O brahmana you have come to my sacrificial mandap along with these ascetics Blessed am I Obliged am I.
ramayan::1361.english_translation: O preeminent among ascetics, O brahmana, you have come to my sacrificial mandap along with these ascetics. Blessed am I. Obliged am I.
ramayan::1361.translation_literal: धन्यः (blessed) / अस्मि (I am) / अनुगृहीतः (favoured, graced) / अस्मि (I am) / यस्य (whose) / मे (my) / मुनिपुङ्गव (preeminent among ascetics) / यज्ञोपसदनं (to the sacrificial enclosure) / ब्रह्मन् (O brahmana) / प्राप्तः (arrived) / असि (you are) / मुनिभिः (with ascetics) / सह (together)
ramayan::1361.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1361.essence: Honor turns a ritual into something fulfilled.
ramayan::1361.simple_meaning: King Dasharatha welcomes Vishvamitra with deep gratitude, saying his sacrifice has been blessed by the sage's arrival with the other ascetics.
ramayan::1361.simple_insight: A worthy guest can turn effort into blessing.
ramayan::1361.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has seated his guests properly and now sees Vishvamitra arrive with fellow ascetics. The king feels his sacrifice has become complete simply because such a revered teacher has come to witness it.
ramayan::1361.modern_relevance: You finish preparing a gathering, then the one person you hoped would come finally walks in. The room changes because their presence matters more than the event itself.
ramayan::1361.insight: It highlights reverence for the right company and the sense that sacred work becomes complete through noble presence.

ramayan::1362.verse_sanskrit: द्वादशाहं तु ब्रह्मर्षे शेषमाहुर्मनीषिण: । । 15015 । । ततो भागार्थिनो देवान् द्रष्टुमर्हसि कौशिक ।
ramayan::1362.verse_hindi: O Brahmarshi learned men say, only twelve days remain for completion of this acrifice. Thereafter O Viswamitra you should see devatas claiming their shares.
ramayan::1362.english_translation: O Brahmarshi, learned men say that only twelve days remain for completion of this sacrifice. After that, O Kaushika, you should see the devas claiming their shares.
ramayan::1362.translation_literal: द्वादशाहम् (twelve days) / तु (indeed) / ब्रह्मर्षे (O Brahmarshi) / शेषम् (remaining) / आहुः (they say) / मनीषिणः (the wise) / ततः (then) / भागार्थिनः (seeking their share) / देवान् (the devas) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अर्हसि (you should) / कौशिक (O Kaushika)
ramayan::1362.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1362.essence: Completion comes only after the remaining days are fulfilled.
ramayan::1362.simple_meaning: Only twelve days remain before the sacrifice is complete. After that, the devas who are due their share should be seen.
ramayan::1362.simple_insight: Some things have their own timing. You cannot force a sacred process before it is ready.
ramayan::1362.detailed_meaning: Janaka is speaking to Vishwamitra after welcoming him and the sages to his sacrifice. He explains that the rite still needs twelve more days before the devas can receive their portion, setting the ritual timeline before the next exchange.
ramayan::1362.modern_relevance: You are halfway through something important and want the result now, but the process still has its own clock. Rushing it only breaks what you came to complete.
ramayan::1362.insight: It teaches you to respect sequence instead of demanding immediate completion.

ramayan::1363.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा मुनिशार्दूलं प्रहृष्टवदनस्तदा । । 15016 । । पुनस्तं परिपप्रच्छ प्राञ्जलि: प्रणतो नृप: ।
ramayan::1363.verse_hindi: Having said this, the king (Janaka) with a cheerful countenance and saluting with folded palms again asked that tiger among ascetics (Viswamitra):
ramayan::1363.english_translation: Having said this, the king Janaka, with a cheerful face and folded hands, bowed and asked that tiger among ascetics, Vishwamitra, again.
ramayan::1363.translation_literal: इत्युक्त्वा (having said thus) / मुनिशार्दूलं (to the tiger among ascetics) / प्रहृष्टवदनस्तदा (then with a delighted face) / पुनः (again) / तं (him) / परिपप्रच्छ (asked) / प्राञ्जलिः (with folded palms) / प्रणतः (bowed) / नृपः (the king)
ramayan::1363.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1363.essence: A humble question can follow even deep honor.
ramayan::1363.simple_meaning: Janaka, pleased and respectful, asked Vishwamitra another question with folded hands.
ramayan::1363.simple_insight: Respect opens the way for honest questions.
ramayan::1363.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s sacrificial hall, Vishwamitra has arrived with the two princes. Janaka bows again, smiling and humble, and prepares to ask who they are. The verse simply turns the scene from welcome into inquiry.
ramayan::1363.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems important, and instead of posturing, you ask with genuine respect. That kind of humility keeps the conversation open.
ramayan::1363.insight: It shows how reverence and curiosity can coexist in the same moment.

ramayan::1364.verse_sanskrit: इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ । । 15017 । । गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ । पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ । । 15018 । । अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ । यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ । । 15019 । । कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने ।
ramayan::1364.verse_hindi: O Sage (Viswamitra), be blessed. Who are these two young men with the prowess of the celestials the gait of an elephant or a lion? They resemble a tiger or a bull in courage. They have large eyes like lotuspetals. They are armed with scimitars bows and quivers. With their approaching youth, they resemble the Aswinikumaras in beauty. They look like gods who have descended on earth from heaven out of their free will. Whose sons are they? How did they come here on foot? And for what purpose?
ramayan::1364.english_translation: O Sage, may you be blessed. Who are these two young men, endowed with power like the divine beings, moving with the gait of an elephant or a lion? Brave as a tiger or bull, with lotus-like eyes, bearing swords, quivers, and bows. Beautiful like the twin Ashvins, as if youth itself has taken form. They seem like immortal beings who have come from the heavenly realm by choice. Whose sons are they, how did they arrive here on foot, and for what purpose?
ramayan::1364.translation_literal: इमौ (these two) / कुमारौ (young men) / भद्रं ते (blessings to you) / देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ (with power equal to the divine beings) / गजसिंहगती (with the gait of an elephant and a lion) / वीरौ (the brave ones) / शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ (comparable to a tiger and a bull) / पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ (with eyes wide like lotus petals) / खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ (bearers of sword, quiver, and bow) / अश्विनाविव (like the Ashvins) / रूपेण (in beauty) / समुपस्थितयौवनौ (with youth fully arrived) / यदृच्छया (by their own will) / एव (indeed) / गां (earth) / प्राप्तौ (having reached) / देवलोकात् (from the heavenly realm) / इव (as if) / अमरौ (immortals) / कथं (how) / पद्भ्याम् (by feet) / इह (here) / प्राप्तौ (have come) / किमर्थं (for what reason) / कस्य (whose) / वा (or) / मुने (O sage)
ramayan::1364.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1364.essence: Their presence is so striking that even a king stops to ask who they are.
ramayan::1364.simple_meaning: Janaka is struck by Rama and Lakshmana's extraordinary appearance and asks who they are, where they came from, and why they have arrived on foot.
ramayan::1364.simple_insight: Sometimes presence itself announces something important before a single word is spoken.
ramayan::1364.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Vishwamitra has arrived with two unknown princes. Their beauty, weapons, and calm power astonish the king. This verse is Janaka's first response: admiration mixed with curiosity as he tries to understand who these remarkable youths are.
ramayan::1364.modern_relevance: You meet two strangers in a room, and something about their calm makes everyone look up. Before names or titles, their presence already changes the atmosphere.
ramayan::1364.insight: It teaches you to notice character through presence before explanation.

ramayan::1365.verse_sanskrit: वरायुधधरौ वीरौ कस्य पुत्रौ महामुने । । 15020 । । भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम् । परस्परस्य सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितै: । । 15021 । । काकपक्षधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वत: ।
