ramayan::1365.verse_hindi: Great ascetic, these two young men with hair falling on their temples like the wings of a crow, each of them resemble the other in personality, expressions and gestures. Wielding excellent weapons they adorn this land like the Moon and the Sun deck the sky. Whose sons are they? I wish truly to hear about these heroes.
ramayan::1365.english_translation: Great ascetic, these two young men with hair falling on their temples like the wings of a crow, each of them resemble the other in personality, expressions and gestures. Wielding excellent weapons they adorn this land like the Moon and the Sun deck the sky. Whose sons are they? I wish truly to hear about these heroes.
ramayan::1365.translation_literal: वरायुधधरौ (bearing excellent weapons) / वीरौ (the two heroes) / कस्य (whose) / पुत्रौ (sons) / महामुने (O great sage) / भूषयन्तौ (adorning) / इमं (this) / देशं (land) / चन्द्रसूर्यौ (the Moon and the Sun) / इव (like) / अम्बरम् (the sky) / परस्परस्य (of each other) / सदृशौ (similar) / प्रमाण (in stature) / ईङ्गित (in gestures) / चेष्टितैः (in movements) / काकपक्षधरौ (wearing crow-like locks of hair) / वीरौ (the two heroes) / श्रोतुम् (to hear) / इच्छामि (I wish) / तत्त्वतः (truly)
ramayan::1365.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1365.essence: Wonder opens the door to a deeper recognition.
ramayan::1365.simple_meaning: Janaka asks who the two heroic young men are, admiring their appearance, weapons, and striking similarity.
ramayan::1365.simple_insight: Sometimes recognition begins with wonder before it becomes understanding.
ramayan::1365.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just seen two extraordinary young warriors arrive with Vishvamitra. Their beauty, weapons, and matching bearing catch his eye. He bows to the sage and asks who they are, setting up the introduction of Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayan::1365.modern_relevance: You spot two strangers in a room and feel the pull of curiosity before anyone speaks. Their presence tells you something important is about to be named.
ramayan::1365.insight: It frames the next revelation by turning attention from appearance to identity.

ramayan::1366.verse_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा जनकस्य महात्मन: । । 15022 । । न्यवेदयन्महात्मानौ पुत्रौ दशरथस्य तौ ।
ramayan::1366.verse_hindi: Hearing the words of the magnanimous Janaka, Viswamitra presented them to him saying that they were the illustrious sons of Dasaratha.
ramayan::1366.english_translation: Hearing the words of the magnanimous Janaka, Viswamitra presented them to him, saying that they were the illustrious sons of Dasaratha.
ramayan::1366.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / तद्वचनं (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / महात्मनः (of the magnanimous one) / न्यवेदयन् (he presented, announced) / महात्मानौ (the two great-souled ones) / पुत्रौ (sons) / दशरथस्य (of Dasaratha) / तौ (those two)
ramayan::1366.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1366.essence: Identity is announced before the real meeting begins.
ramayan::1366.simple_meaning: Viswamitra identifies Rama and Lakshmana to Janaka as Dasaratha's noble sons.
ramayan::1366.simple_insight: Names and lineage matter here, but only as a bridge to the meeting that follows.
ramayan::1366.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, Viswamitra answers the king's curiosity about the two radiant youths standing beside him. He identifies them plainly as Dasaratha's sons, preparing the way for the deeper exchange that follows.
ramayan::1366.modern_relevance: At a formal introduction, someone finally says who the two quiet newcomers are. The room shifts, not because of drama, but because identity has been named.
ramayan::1366.insight: It marks the moment when strangers become known and the next part of the encounter can begin.

ramayan::1367.verse_sanskrit: सिद्धाश्रमनिवासं च राक्षसानां वधं तथा । । 15023 । । तच्चागमनमव्यग्रं विशालायाश्च दर्शनम् । अहल्यादर्शनं चैव गौतमेन समागमम् । । 15024 । । महाधनुषि जिज्ञासां कर्तुमागमनं तथा । एतत्सर्वं महातेजा जनकाय महात्मने । । 15025 । । निवेद्य विररामाथ विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: ।
ramayan::1367.verse_hindi: The great ascetic Viswamitra, who was highly powerful related to the distinguished Janaka in full their undaunted journey to Siddhashrama and the slaughter of rakshasas there, the view of the city of Vishala, meeting with Ahalya and Gautama and the inquisitiveness about the great bow which brought them to Mithila and then kept quiet.
ramayan::1367.english_translation: The great ascetic Viswamitra, full of power, then told the noble Janaka everything: their fearless journey to Siddhashrama, the killing of the rakshasas there, the sight of Vishala, Ahalya's meeting with Gautama, and their coming to see the great bow. Then that great sage fell silent.
ramayan::1367.translation_literal: सिद्धाश्रमनिवासम् (dwelling at Siddhashrama) / च (and) / राक्षसानाम् (of the rakshasas) / वधम् (killing) / तथा (and also) / तत् (that) / चागमनम् (and the coming) / अव्यग्रम् (untroubled) / विशालायाः (of Vishala) / दर्शनम् (sight) / अहल्यादर्शनम् (seeing Ahalya) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / गौतमेन (with Gautama) / समागमम् (meeting) / महाधनुषि (about the great bow) / जिज्ञासाम् (curiosity) / कर्तुम् (to make) / आगमनम् (coming) / तथा (and) / एतत् सर्वम् (all this) / महातेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / जनकाय (to Janaka) / महात्मने (to the noble one) / निवेद्य (having reported) / विरराम (fell silent) / अथ (then) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (the great sage)
ramayan::1367.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1367.essence: A whole journey is carried in a few spoken facts, then left hanging in silence.
ramayan::1367.simple_meaning: Viswamitra briefly recounts to Janaka the journey, the battles, the meeting with Ahalya, and the reason they have come to Mithila.
ramayan::1367.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for speech; even a great teacher can only pause after telling the whole story.
ramayan::1367.detailed_meaning: Janaka has asked who these two remarkable princes are. Viswamitra answers by summarizing everything they have passed through together: Siddhashrama, the destruction of the rakshasas, Vishala, Ahalya, Gautama, and the great bow that drew them to Mithila. The verse ends with his silence, as if the tale itself now stands before Janaka.
ramayan::1367.modern_relevance: After a long drive, you finally reach the person who needs the full story, and you realize no summary can carry the weight of what happened.
ramayan::1367.insight: It shows how a journey can be condensed into a few decisive facts without losing its force.

ramayan::1368.verse_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रस्य धीमत: । हृष्टरोमा महातेजाश्शतानन्दो महातपा: । । 1511 । । गौतमस्य सुतो ज्येष्ठस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभ: । रामसन्दर्शनादेव परं विस्मयमागत: । । 1512 । ।
ramayan::1368.verse_hindi: Satananda the eldest son of Gautama, a great sage who looked brilliant with the power of austerities was thrilled to hear the words of Viswamitra the intellectual and experienced great astonishment on beholding Rama.
ramayan::1368.english_translation: Satananda, the eldest son of Gautama, a great ascetic radiant through austerity, was delighted to hear Viswamitra's words and was filled with wonder at seeing Rama.
ramayan::1368.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / तत्-वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Viswamitra) / धीमतः (of the wise one) / हृष्ट-रोमा (with hair standing on end) / महा-तेजाः (highly radiant) / शतानन्दः (Satananda) / महा-तपाः (great ascetic) / गौतमस्य (of Gautama) / सुतः (son) / ज्येष्ठः (eldest) / तपसा (by austerity) / द्योतित-प्रभः (whose splendour was brightened) / राम-सन्दर्शनात् (from seeing Rama) / एव (indeed) / परम् (great) / विस्मयम् (wonder) / आगतः (arrived)
ramayan::1368.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1368.essence: Wonder can arrive before understanding does.
ramayan::1368.simple_meaning: Satananda is overwhelmed by Viswamitra's words and by the sight of Rama. The moment is one of awe and recognition, not teaching.
ramayan::1368.simple_insight: Some meetings leave you speechless before you even understand why.
ramayan::1368.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has brought Rama and Lakshmana into Janaka's world, and the old tensions around the sacrifice are beginning to soften. Satananda, Gautama's son, hears Viswamitra and then sees Rama, and wonder rises in him before any speech can begin.
ramayan::1368.modern_relevance: You meet someone and feel the room change before a single sentence lands. Sometimes recognition arrives as silence first, explanation later.
ramayan::1368.insight: It frames awe as a bodily response to a presence that exceeds ordinary expectation.

ramayan::1369.verse_sanskrit: स तौ निषण्णौ सम्प्रेक्ष्य सुखासीनौ नृपात्मजौ । शतानन्दो मुनिश्रेष्ठं विश्वामित्रमथामब्रवीत् । । 1513 । ।
ramayan::1369.verse_hindi: Satananda saw the two princes comfortably seated nearby and said to Viswamitra, the foremost of the ascetics:
ramayan::1369.english_translation: Seeing the two princes seated comfortably nearby, Shatananda then said to Viswamitra, the foremost of ascetics:
ramayan::1369.translation_literal: सः (he) / तौ (those two) / निषण्णौ (seated) / सम्प्रेक्ष्य (having observed) / सुखासीनौ (comfortably seated) / नृपात्मजौ (the two princes) / शतानन्दः (Shatananda) / मुनि-श्रेष्ठम् (to the foremost of ascetics) / विश्वामित्रम् (Viswamitra) / अथ (then) / अमब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1369.speaker: Shatananda
ramayan::1369.essence: The scene pauses just long enough for the next question to begin.
ramayan::1369.simple_meaning: Shatananda notices Rama and Lakshmana seated comfortably and turns to speak to Viswamitra.
ramayan::1369.simple_insight: A quiet moment of recognition can open the next conversation.
ramayan::1369.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s realm, after Viswamitra has brought the princes to the hermitage, Shatananda sees Rama and Lakshmana seated in ease. His attention shifts to the sage, and this line simply sets up the exchange that follows.
ramayan::1369.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and notice two people have already settled in. Before anyone speaks, the next question is already forming.
ramayan::1369.insight: It marks a transition from arrival to conversation, with no teaching of its own.

ramayan::1370.verse_sanskrit: अपि ते मुनिशार्दूल मम माता यशस्विनी । दर्शिता राजपुत्राय तपो दीर्घमुपागता । । 1514 । ।
ramayan::1370.verse_hindi: O Tiger among ascetics, was my renowned mother who had been practising intense austerities for long shown to the prince (Rama)?
ramayan::1370.english_translation: O tiger among ascetics, was my renowned mother, who had long practised severe austerities, shown to the prince?
ramayan::1370.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / ते (to you) / मुनिशार्दूल (tiger among ascetics) / मम (my) / माता (mother) / यशस्विनी (renowned) / दर्शिता (shown) / राजपुत्राय (to the prince) / तपः (austerity) / दीर्घम् (for a long time) / उपागता (having undertaken)
ramayan::1370.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1370.essence: A son asks whether his austere mother was properly presented.
ramayan::1370.simple_meaning: Satananda asks whether his mother, known for long austerity, was shown to Rama.
ramayan::1370.simple_insight: The verse carries a family concern, not a teaching. It simply asks whether a revered woman was presented to the prince.
ramayan::1370.detailed_meaning: Satananda, Gautama's eldest son, speaks to Viswamitra after seeing the princes seated nearby. He asks whether his mother, famed for long austerity, was shown to Rama. The verse is a small step in their conversation, not the main point.
ramayan::1370.modern_relevance: You hear a name from your family’s past and want to know whether the person you admire was properly acknowledged.
ramayan::1370.insight: It keeps the scene moving by checking whether a respected figure was introduced to Rama.

ramayan::1371.verse_sanskrit: अपि रामे महातेजा मम माता यशस्विनी । वन्यैरुपाहरत्पूजां पूजार्हे सर्वदेहिनाम् । । 1515 । ।
ramayan::1371.verse_hindi: Did my highly lustrous and celebrated mother offer homage to Rama, worthy of reverence by all living beings, with things available in the forest?
ramayan::1371.english_translation: Did my highly lustrous and celebrated mother offer homage to Rama, worthy of reverence by all living beings, with things available in the forest?
ramayan::1371.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / रामे (to Rama) / महातेजा (highly lustrous) / मम माता (my mother) / यशस्विनी (famous, celebrated) / वन्यैः (with forest-born things) / उपाहरत् (offered) / पूजाम् (worship, homage) / पूजाअर्हे (to one worthy of reverence) / सर्वदेहिनाम् (of all embodied beings)
ramayan::1371.speaker: Shatananda
ramayan::1371.essence: Real reverence is measured by what you offer, not what you say.
ramayan::1371.simple_meaning: Shatananda asks whether his mother honored Rama with forest offerings, recognizing Rama as worthy of reverence from all beings.
ramayan::1371.simple_insight: Even a small act of reverence matters when it is offered to someone truly worthy.
ramayan::1371.detailed_meaning: Shatananda is speaking to Vishwamitra after seeing the two princes seated nearby. He asks whether his mother, long known for her austerity, had welcomed and honored Rama with forest offerings. The verse is a respectful check within a larger exchange, not the main teaching itself.
ramayan::1371.modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly important and wonder whether you treated them with enough care. The question itself shows reverence: did you honor what deserved honor?
ramayan::1371.insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to whether your welcome matched the worth of the person before you.

ramayan::1372.verse_sanskrit: अपि रामाय कथितं यथावृत्तं पुरातनम् । मम मातुर्महातेजो दैवेन दुरनुष्ठितम् । । 1516 । ।
ramayan::1372.verse_hindi: O highly powerful sage, was Rama told the old story about the misdeed of god (Indra) to my mother?
ramayan::1372.english_translation: O highly powerful sage, was Rama told the old story about the misdeed done by the divine being to my mother?
ramayan::1372.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / रामाय (to Rama) / कथितं (was told) / यथावृत्तं (the true account) / पुरातनम् (ancient) / मम (my) / मातुः (mother's) / महातेजः (O highly powerful one) / दैवेन (by the divine being) / दुरनुष्ठितम् (misdeed done)
ramayan::1372.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1372.essence: A question about an old wrong, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::1372.simple_meaning: The speaker is asking whether Rama was told an old story about an offense done to his mother by a divine being.
ramayan::1372.simple_insight: The verse is a question, not a teaching. It depends on the surrounding conversation for its meaning.
ramayan::1372.detailed_meaning: A sage is being asked about an old family incident involving the speaker's mother and a divine being. The question wonders whether Rama ever heard that story. It is a small link in a larger exchange, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::1372.modern_relevance: A conversation can hinge on one missing backstory. Before reacting, you sometimes need to know the old wound everyone else is already carrying.
ramayan::1372.insight: It keeps attention on context, reminding you that present events often rest on an older, unseen story.

ramayan::1373.verse_sanskrit: अपि कौशिक भद्रं ते गुरुणा मम सङ्गता । मम माता मुनिश्रेष्ठ रामसन्दर्शनादित: । । 1517 । ।
ramayan::1373.verse_hindi: O Son of Kushika (Viswamitra) be blessed. O the best among the ascetics, as a result of beholding Rama, was my mother united with my father?
ramayan::1373.english_translation: O son of Kushika, may you be well. O best among ascetics, was my mother united with my father because of seeing Rama?
ramayan::1373.translation_literal: अपि (indeed) / कौशिक (O son of Kushika) / भद्रं ते (may good be to you) / गुरुणा (by the teacher) / मम (my) / सङ्गता (joined together) / मम माता (my mother) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (O best among ascetics) / रामसन्दर्शनादित: (because of seeing Rama)
ramayan::1373.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1373.essence: A single sight of Rama is treated as enough to reshape a family’s fate.
ramayan::1373.simple_meaning: The speaker asks whether his mother and father were brought together because they saw Rama.
ramayan::1373.simple_insight: Sometimes a single sacred encounter is believed to shape an entire family line.
ramayan::1373.detailed_meaning: In a conversation with Vishvamitra, the speaker asks about an old family connection: whether his mother and father were united through the blessing of seeing Rama. It is part of a larger inquiry into how divine encounter alters human lives.
ramayan::1373.modern_relevance: You hear a story about how one meeting changed everything for a family, and you start wondering which encounters in your own life quietly redirected the whole line of your choices.
ramayan::1373.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary cause to the unseen force that binds lives together.

ramayan::1374.verse_sanskrit: अपि मे गुरुणा राम: पूजित: कुशिकात्मज । इहागतो महातेजा: पूजां प्राप्तो महात्मन: । । 1518 । ।
ramayan::1374.verse_hindi: O Son of Kushika was Rama honoured by my father? Was my most brilliant father  honoured by illustrious Rama when he arrived?
ramayan::1374.english_translation: O Son of Kushika, was Rama honoured by my father when he arrived here? Was my illustrious father honoured by noble Rama?
ramayan::1374.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / मे (my) / गुरुणा (by the teacher) / रामः (Rama) / पूजितः (honoured) / कुशिकात्मज (O son of Kushika) / इहागतः (having arrived here) / महातेजाः (very brilliant) / पूजाम् (honour) / प्राप्तः (received) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one)
ramayan::1374.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1374.essence: Noble people reveal themselves in how they honour each other.
ramayan::1374.simple_meaning: Sita asks whether Rama and her father honored each other properly when they met.
ramayan::1374.simple_insight: Respect between noble people matters as much as the meeting itself.
ramayan::1374.detailed_meaning: Sita is speaking with Vishvamitra and asking about the first meeting between Rama and her father. She wants to know whether Rama was properly received and whether her father honored Rama in return, showing how carefully she measures noble conduct.
ramayan::1374.modern_relevance: You can tell a lot from how two people greet each other. Sita is checking whether dignity was preserved on both sides.
ramayan::1374.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the quality of mutual respect.

ramayan::1375.verse_sanskrit: अपि शान्तेन मनसा गुरुर्मे कुशिकात्मज । इहाऽगतेन रामेण प्रयतेनाभिवादित: । । 1519 । ।
ramayan::1375.verse_hindi: O Kushikas son did pious Rama welcome my father with a tranquil mind when he arrived?
ramayan::1375.english_translation: O son of Kushika, did noble Rama welcome my father with a tranquil mind when he arrived?
ramayan::1375.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / शान्तेन (with tranquil) / मनसा (mind) / गुरुः (teacher) / मे (my) / कुशिकात्मज (son of Kushika) / इहाऽगतेन (by having come here) / रामेण (by Rama) / प्रयतेन (respectfully) / अभिवादितः (greeted)
ramayan::1375.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1375.essence: True respect includes a calm, intentional mind.
ramayan::1375.simple_meaning: Satananda asks whether Rama greeted his father respectfully and with a calm mind.
ramayan::1375.simple_insight: Respect is measured not just by words, but by the mind behind them.
ramayan::1375.detailed_meaning: At Viswamitra’s arrival, Satananda turns to how Rama behaved toward his father, testing whether the prince showed true courtesy and inner composure. The verse is part of a courteous exchange, not a self-contained teaching.
ramayan::1375.modern_relevance: You can say the right thing and still miss the real test: whether your tone, attention, and calm made the other person feel honoured.
ramayan::1375.insight: It shifts attention from formal greeting to the quality of presence behind it.

ramayan::1376.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । प्रत्युवाच शतानन्दं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकोविदम् । । 15110 । ।
ramayan::1376.verse_hindi: Great sage Viswamitra equipped with the knowledge of words heard Satananda who was proficient in speech. And replied:
ramayan::1376.english_translation: Hearing that, the great sage Vishvamitra, master of speech and words, replied to Shatananda.
ramayan::1376.translation_literal: तत् (that) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / वचनम् (the words) / तस्य (his) / विश्वामित्रः (Vishvamitra) / महामुनिः (the great sage) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / शतानन्दम् (to Shatananda) / वाक्यज्ञः (knower of speech) / वाक्यकोविदम् (skilled in words)
ramayan::1376.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::1376.essence: The conversation turns, and Vishvamitra begins his reply.
ramayan::1376.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra hears Shatananda and answers him directly.
ramayan::1376.simple_insight: Some verses simply move the conversation forward without adding a new teaching.
ramayan::1376.detailed_meaning: Shatananda has just questioned whether Rama honored Vishvamitra properly. Hearing this, Vishvamitra answers him in the midst of the Ahalya episode. The verse only marks the turn in dialogue; the substance comes in the next line.
ramayan::1376.modern_relevance: A meeting pauses, someone finishes speaking, and the room turns to the person with the clearest answer. This line is that pivot — the moment before the real reply begins.
ramayan::1376.insight: It signals a shift in dialogue, not a new principle.

ramayan::1377.verse_sanskrit: नातिक्रान्तं मुनिश्रेष्ठ यत्कर्तव्यं कृतं मया । सङ्गता मुनिना पत्नी भार्गवेणेव रेणुका । । 15111 । ।
ramayan::1377.verse_hindi: O Best of ascetics (Satananda) All that is required to be done has been done and nothing was omitted. Ahalya was united with sage Gautama like Renuka with Jamadagni.
ramayan::1377.english_translation: O best of ascetics, I have done all that needed to be done and left nothing undone. Ahalya was reunited with her husband, as Renuka was with Jamadagni.
ramayan::1377.translation_literal: नातिक्रान्तं (not transgressed) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (O best of ascetics) / यत्कर्तव्यं (what was to be done) / कृतं (done) / मया (by me) / सङ्गता (reunited) / मुनिना (with the sage) / पत्नी (wife) / भार्गवेण (with Bhargava) / इव (like) / रेणुका (Renuka)
ramayan::1377.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1377.essence: What needed repair was fully restored; nothing was left incomplete.
ramayan::1377.simple_meaning: The task was completed fully, with nothing left unfinished. Ahalya has been restored to her husband, just as Renuka was restored to Jamadagni.
ramayan::1377.simple_insight: Completeness brings quiet relief: what had to be repaired has been repaired.
ramayan::1377.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just described how Rama’s presence and power transformed Ahalya’s fate. Satananda answers with gratitude and certainty: the work is complete, the restoration is real, and nothing required by dharma was left undone.
ramayan::1377.modern_relevance: You finally send the message, make the apology, or finish the repair that has sat in your chest for weeks. Relief comes not from perfection, but from having done what was required.
ramayan::1377.insight: It teaches you to recognise completion instead of reopening what has already been set right.

ramayan::1378.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य विश्वामित्रस्य भाषितम् । शतानन्दो महातेजा रामं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 15112 । ।
ramayan::1378.verse_hindi: Having heard Viswamitra the highly brilliant Satananda said to Rama:
ramayan::1378.english_translation: Having heard Viswamitra, the highly brilliant Shatananda spoke to Rama.
ramayan::1378.translation_literal: तच्छ्रुत्वा (having heard that) / वचनं (the words) / तस्य (of him) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Vishvamitra) / भाषितम् (spoken) / शतानन्दो (Shatananda) / महातेजा (highly brilliant) / रामं (to Rama) / वचनम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1378.speaker: Shatananda
ramayan::1378.essence: The real meeting begins only after the explanation ends.
ramayan::1378.simple_meaning: Shatananda heard Vishvamitra and turned to speak directly to Rama.
ramayan::1378.simple_insight: The moment shifts from explanation to welcome.
ramayan::1378.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just finished explaining Ahalya's release. Shatananda, the sage of this hermitage, now turns from listening to addressing Rama himself. The verse is a transition into welcome, not the welcome itself.
ramayan::1378.modern_relevance: You finish hearing the background and finally turn to the person who arrived. The story moves from explanation to direct encounter.
ramayan::1378.insight: It marks the handoff from narration to personal greeting.

ramayan::1379.verse_sanskrit: स्वागतं ते नरश्रेष्ठ दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि राघव । विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षिमपराजितम् । । 15113 । ।
ramayan::1379.verse_hindi: O Best of men O Son of the Raghus you are fortunate to have come here following
ramayan::1379.english_translation: Welcome to you, best of men. How fortunate that you have come here, with the unconquered sage Vishwamitra at your head.
ramayan::1379.translation_literal: स्वागतम् (welcome) / ते (to you) / नरश्रेष्ठ (best of men) / दिष्ट्या (by good fortune) / प्राप्तः (arrived) / असि (you are) / राघव (Raghava) / विश्वामित्रम् (Vishvamitra) / पुरस्कृत्य (placing in front, leading) / महर्षिम् (great sage) / अपराजितम् (unconquered)
ramayan::1379.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1379.essence: A worthy guide makes your arrival mean more.
ramayan::1379.simple_meaning: Satananda warmly welcomes Rama and notes his good fortune in arriving with Vishvamitra leading the way.
ramayan::1379.simple_insight: Recognition itself can be a blessing: the right guide changes how arrival feels.
ramayan::1379.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra's side, Rama reaches the hermitage where Ahalya has just been freed. Satananda greets him with honor, naming both Rama and the unconquered sage who brought him there. It is a courteous welcome, not a teaching.
ramayan::1379.modern_relevance: You walk into a room with the one person who vouched for you. Before anyone else speaks, that introduction changes everything.
ramayan::1379.insight: It frames arrival through respect and the authority of a trusted guide.

ramayan::1380.verse_sanskrit: अचिन्त्यकर्मा तपसा ब्रह्मर्षिरतुलप्रभ: । विश्वामित्रो महातेजा वेत्स्येनं परमां गतिम् । । 15114 । ।
ramayan::1380.verse_hindi: Highly lustrous Viswamitra has performed deeds which defy all imagination. By his austerities, he became Brahmarshi and possesses unparalleled radiance. Know him to be the supreme resort.
ramayan::1380.english_translation: Highly lustrous Viswamitra has performed deeds which defy all imagination. By his austerities, he became Brahmarshi and possesses unparalleled radiance. Know him to be the supreme resort.
ramayan::1380.translation_literal: अचिन्त्यकर्मा (whose deeds are beyond thought) / तपसा (by austerity) / ब्रह्मर्षिः (a Brahmarshi) / अतुलप्रभः (of unmatched radiance) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महातेजाः (highly brilliant) / वेत्स्येनम् (know him) / परमां गतिम् (the supreme resort)
ramayan::1380.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1380.essence: Austerity can turn a human life into a refuge.
ramayan::1380.simple_meaning: Viswamitra's intense discipline transformed him into a great sage of unmatched brilliance. He is to be seen as a supreme refuge.
ramayan::1380.simple_insight: Real transformation can make someone worthy of deep trust.
ramayan::1380.detailed_meaning: Satananda is welcoming Rama and praising Viswamitra before the sage's presence becomes the bridge into the next stage of Rama's journey. The verse elevates Viswamitra from a former king into a realized sage whose austerity has changed his very standing.
ramayan::1380.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm is unmistakable — not because they were born that way, but because they earned it through years of discipline. Their presence feels like shelter.
ramayan::1380.insight: It shifts respect from status to transformation: what you become matters more than what you were born as.

ramayan::1381.verse_sanskrit: नास्ति धन्यतरो राम त्वत्तोऽन्यो भुवि कश्चन । गोप्ता कुशिकपुत्रस्ते येन तप्तं महत्तप: । । 15115 । ।
ramayan::1381.verse_hindi: Rama Son of Kushika (Viswamitra) who has performed great austerities is your protector. Therefore, there is none on this earth more fortunate than you.
ramayan::1381.english_translation: Rama, there is no one on earth more fortunate than you, for the son of Kushika, who has performed great austerities, is your protector.
ramayan::1381.translation_literal: नास्ति (there is not) / धन्यतरः (more fortunate) / राम (Rama) / त्वत्तः (than you) / अन्यः (another) / भुवि (on earth) / कश्चन (anyone) / गोप्ता (protector) / कुशिकपुत्रः (the son of Kushika) / ते (of you) / येन (by whom) / तप्तम् (was performed) / महत् (great) / तपः (austerity)
ramayan::1381.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1381.essence: Fortune is having earned strength on your side.
ramayan::1381.simple_meaning: Rama is called the most fortunate person on earth because Visvamitra, who earned great power through austerity, is his protector.
ramayan::1381.simple_insight: It feels reassuring to be backed by someone whose strength was earned, not borrowed.
ramayan::1381.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just been welcomed as Rama's guide and protector. Valmiki pauses to praise the depth of that protection: this is no ordinary escort, but a sage whose austerity has made him formidable. Rama is blessed because such a man stands with him.
ramayan::1381.modern_relevance: You are about to walk into a hard conversation, and one steady person says, 'I’m with you.' The fear doesn’t vanish, but your footing changes because the support is real.
ramayan::1381.insight: It shifts attention from personal luck to the quality of the support standing beside you.

ramayan::1382.verse_sanskrit: श्रूयतां चाभिधास्यामि कौशिकस्य महात्मन: । यथा बलं यथा वृत्तं तन्मे निगदत: श्रुणु । । 15116 । ।
ramayan::1382.verse_hindi: I shall tell you about the power and achievement of the magnanimous son of Kushika Viswamitra. Listen
ramayan::1382.english_translation: I shall tell you about the power and achievement of the magnanimous son of Kushika, Viswamitra. Listen.
ramayan::1382.translation_literal: श्रूयताम् (let it be heard) / च (and) / अभिधास्यामि (I will tell) / कौशिकस्य (of Kushika's) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / यथा (how) / बलम् (power) / यथा (how) / वृत्तम् (conduct/achievement) / तत् (that) / मे (by me) / निगदतः (speaking) / श्रुणु (listen)
ramayan::1382.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1382.essence: Greatness deserves to be introduced before it is explained.
ramayan::1382.simple_meaning: Valmiki pauses to introduce Viswamitra's greatness and asks the listener to pay attention.
ramayan::1382.simple_insight: Some stories need a pause before they can be understood.
ramayan::1382.detailed_meaning: After praising Viswamitra's austerity, Valmiki turns to explain who this former king has become. He invites the listener to hear about Viswamitra's power and character before the story of his deeds unfolds.
ramayan::1382.modern_relevance: Before someone tells you a life-changing story, they often stop and frame why it matters. This verse is that pause — a signal that the next part will reveal a person forged by struggle.
ramayan::1382.insight: It shifts attention from the summary to the person behind the summary.

ramayan::1383.verse_sanskrit: राजाऽभूदेष धर्मात्मा दीर्घकालमरिन्दम: । धर्मज्ञ: कृतविद्यश्च प्रजानां च हिते रत: । । 15117 । ।
ramayan::1383.verse_hindi: This righteousminded sage, subduer of enemies, knower of dharma knowledgeable in
ramayan::1383.english_translation: He was a righteous king, long a conqueror of enemies, one who knew dharma, was learned, and delighted in the welfare of his people.
ramayan::1383.translation_literal: राजा (king) / आभूत् (was) / एषः (this) / धर्मात्मा (righteous in nature) / दीर्घकालम् (for a long time) / अरिन्दमः (subduer of enemies) / धर्मज्ञः (knower of dharma) / कृतविद्यः (learned) / च (and) / प्रजानाम् (of the people) / च (and) / हिते (in welfare) / रतঃ (delighted)
ramayan::1383.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1383.essence: True power serves the welfare of those it governs.
ramayan::1383.simple_meaning: He was a righteous king who knew dharma, was learned, and cared for his people’s welfare.
ramayan::1383.simple_insight: Leadership becomes noble when power is used for the people, not for the ruler’s pride.
ramayan::1383.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is introducing his lineage and the moral stature of the kings in it. He describes a ruler whose strength, learning, and command were joined to righteousness and public welfare, setting up a family line shaped by duty.
ramayan::1383.modern_relevance: A manager takes credit for the team’s success but forgets who stayed late to finish the work. This verse points to the opposite kind of authority: strong, informed, and measured by how well it serves others.
ramayan::1383.insight: It shifts leadership from self-display to service and responsibility.

ramayan::1384.verse_sanskrit: प्रजापतिसुतश्चासीत्कुशो नाम महीपति: । कुशस्य पुत्रो बलवान् कुशनाभस्सुधार्मिक: । । 15118 । ।
ramayan::1384.verse_hindi: There was a king named Kusa who was the son of Brahma. His son was Kusanabha who was supremely righteous and strong.
ramayan::1384.english_translation: There was a king named Kusa, son of Brahma. His son was Kusanabha, who was strong and deeply righteous.
ramayan::1384.translation_literal: प्रजापति-सुतः (son of the creator) / च (and) / आसीत् (was) / कुशः (Kusa) / नाम (named) / महीपतिḥ (king) / कुशस्य (of Kusa) / पुत्रः (son) / बलवान् (strong) / कुशनाभः (Kusanabha) / सु-धार्मिकः (very righteous)
ramayan::1384.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1384.essence: A noble lineage is being laid out before Viswamitra appears.
ramayan::1384.simple_meaning: Kusa was a king descended from Brahma, and his son Kusanabha was powerful and righteous.
ramayan::1384.simple_insight: Lineage matters here because it prepares the ground for Viswamitra's family story.
ramayan::1384.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing Viswamitra’s ancestry step by step. He names Kusa, then Kusanabha, to show an honorable royal line before introducing Gadhi and, next, Viswamitra himself. The verse is a bridge, not the climax.
ramayan::1384.modern_relevance: A family history comes up at a gathering, and suddenly everyone is placing names, roles, and inheritances into order. Some details matter because they explain the person who appears next.
ramayan::1384.insight: It shifts attention from the person in front of you to the line of causes that shaped him.

ramayan::1385.verse_sanskrit: कुशनाभसुतस्त्वासीद्गाधिरित्येव विश्रृत: । गाधे: पुत्रो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । । 15119 । ।
ramayan::1385.verse_hindi: Wellknown Gadhi was the son of Kusanabha. Highly lustrous and mighty ascetic Viswamitra is the son of Gadhi.
ramayan::1385.english_translation: Wellknown Gadhi was the son of Kusanabha. Highly lustrous and mighty ascetic Viswamitra is the son of Gadhi.
ramayan::1385.translation_literal: कुशनाभसुतः (son of Kusanabha) / तु (indeed) / आसीत् (was) / गाधिः (Gadhi) / इति एव (thus indeed) / विश्रुतः (well-known) / गाधेः (of Gadhi) / पुत्रः (son) / महातेजाः (highly lustrous) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (great ascetic/sage)
ramayan::1385.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1385.essence: A king's son can become a great sage.
ramayan::1385.simple_meaning: Gadhi was Kusanabha's son, and Viswamitra was Gadhi's son. The verse simply places Viswamitra in his royal lineage.
ramayan::1385.simple_insight: Great teachers can emerge from royal lines and still choose a different life.
ramayan::1385.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing Viswamitra's ancestry through the kings of Kusa's line. After naming Kusanabha, he identifies Gadhi and then Viswamitra, preparing the reader for the king who will later become a great sage.
ramayan::1385.modern_relevance: A family tree gets mentioned in the middle of a story, and then everything changes: the child of kings becomes the one who walks away from kingship itself.
ramayan::1385.insight: It frames Viswamitra as someone whose authority comes from both lineage and transformation.

ramayan::1386.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रो महातेजा: पालयामास मेदिनीम् । बहुवर्षसहस्राणि राजा राज्यमकारयत् । । 15120 । ।
ramayan::1386.verse_hindi: Highly lustrous Viswamitra ruled the earth. As a king he ruled over his kingdom for  thousands of years.
ramayan::1386.english_translation: Highly lustrous Viswamitra ruled the earth. As a king he ruled over his kingdom for thousands of years.
ramayan::1386.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महातेजाः (highly lustrous) / पालयामास (ruled, protected) / मेदिनीम् (the earth) / बहुवर्षसहस्राणि (for many thousands of years) / राजा (as a king) / राज्यम् (the kingdom) / अकारयत् (caused to be ruled, governed)
ramayan::1386.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1386.essence: He ruled long enough to know power, then outgrew it.
ramayan::1386.simple_meaning: Viswamitra once ruled the earth as a king and governed his kingdom for many thousands of years.
ramayan::1386.simple_insight: Great power can last a long time and still leave a person unfinished.
ramayan::1386.detailed_meaning: After naming Viswamitra's lineage, the poem pauses to show his former life as a king. Before he became the great sage, he held the earth in rule for thousands of years. The next verse will move the story forward from that royal past.
ramayan::1386.modern_relevance: A person who has spent years running a company, family, or public role can still feel the ache of a life not yet fully lived. Titles may last; transformation can still call.
ramayan::1386.insight: It frames Viswamitra's later renunciation against the scale of the power he once held.

ramayan::1387.verse_sanskrit: कदाचित्तु महातेजा योजयित्वा वरूथिनीम् । अक्षौहीणीपरिवृत: परिचक्राम मेदिनीम् । । 15121 । ।
ramayan::1387.verse_hindi: Once that highly lustrous Viswamitra having assembled his army of the magnitude of akshauhini went round the earth.
ramayan::1387.english_translation: Once that highly lustrous Viswamitra, having assembled a mighty army, went around the earth.
ramayan::1387.translation_literal: कदाचित् (once) / तु (indeed) / महातेजा (highly lustrous) / योजयित्वा (having assembled) / वरूथिनीम् (an army) / अक्षौहीणी-परिवृतः (surrounded by an akshauhini-sized force) / परिचक्राम (went around) / मेदिनीम् (the earth)
ramayan::1387.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1387.essence: A king in full power is being shown before his life turns.
ramayan::1387.simple_meaning: Viswamitra once travelled across the earth with a huge army behind him.
ramayan::1387.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is still being introduced as a powerful king before his turn toward renunciation. The verse simply describes him moving across the earth with an enormous army, setting the stage for the next meeting with Rama and the larger shift in his life.
ramayan::1387.insight: It sets the scene for Viswamitra’s worldly power before his transformation begins.

ramayan::1388.verse_sanskrit: नगराणि सराष्ट्राणि सरितश्च तथा गिरीन् । आश्रमान्क्रमशो राम विचरन्नाजगाम ह । । 15122 । । वसिष्ठस्याश्रमपदं नानावृक्षसमाकुलम् । नानामृगगणाकीर्णं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् । । 15123 । । देवदानवगन्धर्वै: किन्नरैरुपशोभितम् । प्रशान्तहरिणाकीर्णं द्विजसङ्घनिषेवितम् । । 15124 । । ब्रह्मर्षिगणसङ्कीर्णं देवर्षिगणसेवितम् । तपश्चरणसंसिद्धैरग्निकल्पैर्महात्मभि: । । 15125 । । अब्भक्षैर्वायुभक्षैश्च शीर्णपर्णाशनैस्तथा । फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैर्जितरोषैर्जितेन्द्रियै: । । 15126 । । ऋषिभिर्वालखिल्यैश्च जपहोमपरायणै: । अन्यैर्वैखानसैश्चैव समन्तादुपशोभितम् । । 15127 । ।
ramayan::1388.verse_hindi: Rama while Viswamitra was wandering about kingdoms, cities, rivers, mountains and  hermitages, he gradually reached the ashram of Vasishta. That hermitage afounded in a variety of trees, species of animals, siddhas, charanas, devatas, danavas, gandharvas and kinnaras, multitudes of birds and resting deer. It was inhabited by brahmarshis and devarishis, by sages who had attained perfection through austerities, by those resembling fire in brightness, by the magnanimous and the selfrestrained, by those who had conquered anger and controlled their senses, who was devoted to prayers and offerings of libations. Some of them subsisted on water, some on air. Some lived on fallen leaves, some on fruits and roots. The hermitage looked bedecked with valakhilyas (born from Vala of Brahma ) and vaikhanasas (born from the nails of Brahma).
ramayan::1388.english_translation: Rama, while Viswamitra was wandering through kingdoms, cities, rivers, mountains, and hermitages, gradually reached the ashram of Vasishta. The hermitage was filled with many kinds of trees, animals, siddhas, charanas, devas, danavas, gandharvas, kinnaras, birds, and peaceful deer. It was inhabited by brahmarshis and devarshis, sages perfected by austerity, radiant as fire, magnanimous, self-controlled, free from anger, and devoted to prayers and offerings. Some lived on water, some on air, some on fallen leaves, some on fruits and roots. It was adorned on all sides by valakhilyas and vaikhanasas.
ramayan::1388.translation_literal: नगराणि (cities) / सराष्ट्राणि (with kingdoms) / सरितः (rivers) / तथा (and) / गिरीन् (mountains) / आश्रमान् (hermitages) / क्रमशः (gradually) / राम (Rama) / विचरन् (wandering) / आजगाम (reached) / ह (indeed) । / वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / आश्रमपदम् (hermitage) / नाना-वृक्ष-समाकुलम् (filled with many kinds of trees) / नाना-मृग-गण-आकीर्णम् (crowded with many kinds of animals) / सिद्ध-चारण-सेवितम् (served by siddhas and charanas) । / देव-दानव-गन्धर्वैः (by devas, danavas, gandharvas) / किन्नरैः (and kinnaras) / उपशोभितम् (adorned) / प्रशान्त-हरिण-आकीर्णम् (filled with peaceful deer) / द्विज-सङ्घ-निषेवितम् (frequented by groups of birds) । / ब्रह्मर्षि-गण-सङ्कीर्णम् (crowded with groups of brahmarshis) / देवर्षि-गण-सेवितम् (served by groups of devarshis) / तपः-चरण-संसिद्धैः (by those perfected through austerity) / अग्नि-कल्पैः (fire-like) / महात्मभिः (great-souled beings) । / अब्भक्षैः (water-eaters) / वायुभक्षैः (air-eaters) / च (and) / शीर्ण-पर्ण-आशनैः (leaf-eaters) / तथा (also) / फल-मूल-आशनैः (fruit-and-root-eaters) / दान्तैः (self-controlled) / जित-रोषैः (conquered anger) / जितेन्द्रियैः (sense-conquered) । / ऋषिभिः (by sages) / वालखिल्यैः (valakhilyas) / च (and) / जप-होम-परायणैः (devoted to chanting and sacrifice) / अन्यैः (by others) / वैखानसैः (vaikhanasas) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / समन्तात् (all around) / उपशोभितम् (adorned)
ramayan::1388.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1388.essence: A holy place reveals the character of the people who live there.
ramayan::1388.simple_meaning: Rama reaches Vasishta’s hermitage, a place alive with sages, ascetics, animals, birds, and sacred stillness.
ramayan::1388.simple_insight: Some places carry the discipline of a thousand lives. You feel it the moment you enter.
ramayan::1388.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been travelling with Rama through the land and finally arrives at Vasishta’s hermitage. The scene lingers on the place itself: its trees, animals, sages, ascetics, and sacred order. It is a descriptive pause before the deeper meeting begins.
ramayan::1388.modern_relevance: You walk into a place where everyone has already lowered their voice. Nothing dramatic happens, but the air itself tells you this space was built by discipline.
ramayan::1388.insight: It trains attention to notice the atmosphere created by long practice and self-mastery.

ramayan::1389.verse_sanskrit: वसिष्ठस्याश्रमपदं ब्रह्मलोकमिवापरम् । ददर्श जयतां श्रेष्ठो विश्वामित्रो महाबल: । । 15128 । ।
ramayan::1389.verse_hindi: Highly powerful Viswamitra, foremost among the conquerors, (thus) saw the hermitage of Vasishta which looked like another Brahmaloka.
ramayan::1389.english_translation: Highly powerful Viswamitra, foremost among the conquerors, thus saw the hermitage of Vasishta, which looked like another Brahmaloka.
ramayan::1389.translation_literal: वसिष्ठस्याश्रमपदम् (the hermitage of Vasishta) / ब्रह्मलोकमिवापरम् (like another Brahmaloka) / ददर्श (saw) / जयतां श्रेष्ठः (foremost among conquerors) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महाबलः (greatly powerful)
ramayan::1389.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1389.essence: A pure place announces the meeting before any words are spoken.
ramayan::1389.simple_meaning: Viswamitra arrives at Vasishta's hermitage and sees it as something holy and radiant, like a second Brahmaloka.
ramayan::1389.simple_insight: Some places feel so pure they change your mood before you speak.
ramayan::1389.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has travelled with Rama through kingdoms, rivers, mountains, and hermitages. At last he sees Vasishta’s ashram, and its beauty and sanctity strike him at once. The verse mainly sets the scene for the meeting that follows.
ramayan::1389.modern_relevance: You walk into a place where the air feels different before anyone says a word. The room is quiet, ordered, and alive with discipline — and you know something important is about to happen.
ramayan::1389.insight: It prepares the mind for reverence by showing how holiness can be recognized instantly.

ramayan::1390.verse_sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रो महाबल: । प्रणतो विनयाद्वीरो वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम् । । 1521 । ।
ramayan::1390.verse_hindi: Overwhelmed with joy the mighty, heroic Viswamitra upon seeing Vasishta, the greatest among ascetics, was and offered respectful salutations.
ramayan::1390.english_translation: Seeing Vasishta, the mighty and heroic Viswamitra was filled with great delight and bowed to the best of ascetics with humility.
ramayan::1390.translation_literal: स (he) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / परमप्रीतो (greatly delighted) / विश्वामित्रो (Visvamitra) / महाबलः (mighty) / प्रणतः (bowed) / विनयात् (out of humility) / वीरः (the heroic one) / वसिष्ठम् (to Vasishta) / जपतां वरम् (best among those who recite/mantra-practitioners)
ramayan::1390.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1390.essence: True greatness can bow without losing anything.
ramayan::1390.simple_meaning: Viswamitra sees Vasishta, feels deep joy, and bows respectfully to him.
ramayan::1390.simple_insight: Even great pride can melt into reverence when humility is real.
ramayan::1390.detailed_meaning: After traveling to Vasishta's hermitage, Viswamitra finally sees the sage he has come to meet. The powerful warrior-sage, despite his stature, bows with humility. The moment simply marks respectful arrival before the two begin their exchange.
ramayan::1390.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone you once underestimated has become the person you most need to learn from. Your first move is respect, not performance.
ramayan::1390.insight: It shows that strength becomes cleaner when it can bow without resistance.

ramayan::1391.verse_sanskrit: स्वागतं तव चेत्युक्तो वसिष्ठेन महात्मना । आसनं चास्य भगवान् वसिष्ठो व्यादिदेश ह । । 1522 । ।
ramayan::1391.verse_hindi: Adorable Vasishta received Viswamitra with words of welcome and ordered a seat for him.
ramayan::1391.english_translation: Adorable Vasishta received Viswamitra with words of welcome and ordered a seat for him.
ramayan::1391.translation_literal: स्वागतम् (welcome) / तव (to you) / इति (thus) / उक्तः (having said) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one) / आसनम् (a seat) / च (and) / अस्य (for him) / भगवान् (the venerable one) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / व्यादिदेश (ordered) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::1391.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1391.essence: A gracious welcome can disarm old hostility before it speaks.
ramayan::1391.simple_meaning: Vasishta greets Viswamitra warmly and has a seat brought for him.
ramayan::1391.simple_insight: Respect can soften old rivalry before a single word of debate begins.
ramayan::1391.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra reaches Vasishta's hermitage after a long, charged journey. The two men once stood as rivals, yet Vasishta answers with welcome, not suspicion, and has a seat arranged. The verse simply shows hospitality before the deeper conversation begins.
ramayan::1391.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where the history is complicated, and someone still says, 'Come in, sit down.' That small courtesy can change everything that follows.
ramayan::1391.insight: It shifts the mind from old tension to deliberate respect.

ramayan::1392.verse_sanskrit: उपविष्टाय च तदा विश्वामित्राय धीमते । यथान्यायं मुनिवर: फलमूलमुपाहरत् । । 1523 । ।
ramayan::1392.verse_hindi: With the sagacious Viswamitra seated the great ascetic, duly offered him fruits and roots.
ramayan::1392.english_translation: With the sagacious Viswamitra seated, the great ascetic duly offered him fruits and roots.
ramayan::1392.translation_literal: उपविष्टाय (having been seated) / च (and) / तदा (then) / विश्वामित्राय (to Viswamitra) / धीमते (the wise one) / यथान्यायं (properly, according to custom) / मुनिवरः (the great ascetic) / फलमूलम् (fruits and roots) / उपाहरत् (offered)
ramayan::1392.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1392.essence: Courtesy can soften even old rivalry.
ramayan::1392.simple_meaning: Vasishta receives Viswamitra respectfully and offers him simple food according to custom.
ramayan::1392.simple_insight: Respect begins with small, careful gestures.
ramayan::1392.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra arrives at Vasishta's hermitage after their earlier meeting. Once he is seated, Vasishta follows proper hospitality and offers fruits and roots. The verse is a quiet detail in a larger scene of reconciliation and courtesy.
ramayan::1392.modern_relevance: You pour tea for someone you once competed with. No speech is needed; the way you serve them says the relationship has changed.
ramayan::1392.insight: It shifts attention from status to respectful conduct.

ramayan::1393.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजां वसिष्ठाद्राजसत्तम: । तपोग्निहोत्रशिष्येषु कुशलं पर्यपृच्छत । । 1524 । । विश्वामित्रो महातेजा वनस्पतिगणे तथा । सर्वत्र कुशलं चाह वसिष्ठो राजसत्तमम् । । 1525 । ।
ramayan::1393.verse_hindi: Foremost among kings, the brilliant Viswamitra, having received  hospitality from Vasishta, enquired about his welbeing his austerities, his firesacrifices, his disciples and trees (in his hermitage). Vasishta, too, informed him of the welfare of all.
ramayan::1393.english_translation: Viswamitra, foremost among kings, accepted Vasishta's hospitality and asked about his welfare, austerities, fire sacrifices, disciples, and the trees in the hermitage. Vasishta, too, asked after the welfare of everything there.
ramayan::1393.translation_literal: प्रतिगृह्य (having accepted) / तु (indeed) / ताम् (that) / पूजाम् (hospitality, honor) / वसिष्ठात् (from Vasishta) / राजसत्तमः (foremost among kings) / तपः (austerity) / अग्निहोत्र (fire sacrifice) / शिष्येषु (among disciples) / कुशलम् (welfare) / पर्यपृच्छत (asked in return) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महातेजाः (greatly brilliant) / वनस्पतिगणे (in the group of trees) / तथा (and also) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / कुशलम् (welfare) / च (and) / आह (said) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / राजसत्तमम् (to the foremost among kings)
ramayan::1393.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1393.essence: Courtesy can hold even old rivalry without strain.
ramayan::1393.simple_meaning: After receiving Vasishta's hospitality, Viswamitra asks about the wellbeing of the hermitage, and Vasishta returns the same courtesy.
ramayan::1393.simple_insight: Respect is shown not only to people, but to everything that supports a life of discipline.
ramayan::1393.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arrived at Vasishta's hermitage, and the tension between former rivals is softened by ritual courtesy. Instead of old pride, both men exchange careful questions about austerity, offerings, disciples, and even the trees that sustain the place.
ramayan::1393.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where old tension could easily surface, but you begin by asking after the other person's work, people, and home. That small courtesy changes the whole atmosphere.
ramayan::1393.insight: It teaches you to meet even rivalry with measured respect and attention to what sustains another person's life.

ramayan::1394.verse_sanskrit: सुखोपविष्टं राजानं विश्वामित्रं महातपा: । पप्रच्छ जपतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणस्सुत: । । 1526 । ।
ramayan::1394.verse_hindi: Vasishta, son of Brahma, the greatest among those who recite prayers and possess rich asceticism enquired of king Viswamitra comfortably seated (before him):
ramayan::1394.english_translation: Vasishta, son of Brahma, the greatest among those who recite prayers and possess rich asceticism, asked king Viswamitra, who was comfortably seated:
ramayan::1394.translation_literal: सुखोपविष्टं (comfortably seated) / राजानं (the king) / विश्वामित्रं (Viswamitra) / महातपाः (great ascetic) / पप्रच्छ (asked) / जपतां श्रेष्ठः (best among those who recite prayers) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / ब्रह्मणः सुतः (son of Brahma)
ramayan::1394.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1394.essence: Courtesy opens the door before any real dialogue can begin.
ramayan::1394.simple_meaning: Vasishta respectfully asks Viswamitra about his well-being while Viswamitra is seated comfortably.
ramayan::1394.simple_insight: Respect can live beside old rivalry when both people choose civility.
ramayan::1394.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has come to Vasishta’s place, and the great sage receives him with courtesy. Before any deeper exchange begins, Vasishta asks after his welfare. The verse is a formal opening, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1394.modern_relevance: You meet someone you once competed with, and the first thing you offer is basic respect. Before the hard conversation starts, you choose dignity.
ramayan::1394.insight: It shows how a serious exchange begins with courtesy, not force.

ramayan::1395.verse_sanskrit: कच्चित्ते कुशलं राजन् कच्चिद्धर्मेण रञ्जयन् । प्रजा: पालयसे वीर राजवृत्तेन धार्मिक । । 1527 । ।
ramayan::1395.verse_hindi: O King, is it all well with you? O righteous one O  heroic one are you ruling (your subjects) in accordance with the duties enjoined upon the king? Do you rule them in conformity with the code of moralit in order to make them happy.
ramayan::1395.english_translation: O King, is it all well with you? O righteous one, O heroic one, are you ruling your people according to the duties of a king, and making them happy through just conduct?
ramayan::1395.translation_literal: कच्चित् (is it?) / ते (your) / कुशलम् (well-being) / राजन् (O king) / कच्चित् (is it?) / धर्मेण (by righteousness / according to duty) / रञ्जयन् (delighting / pleasing) / प्रजा: (the people) / पालयसे (you protect / govern) / वीर (O heroic one) / राजवृत्तेन (by the conduct of a king) / धार्मिक (O righteous one)
ramayan::1395.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1395.essence: A ruler's real duty is to protect people through righteous conduct.
ramayan::1395.simple_meaning: A king should govern by righteousness, protect his people, and make them happy through just rule.
ramayan::1395.simple_insight: Leadership is measured by how safely others live under your care.
ramayan::1395.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is speaking to King Viswamitra after welcoming him. The conversation turns from hospitality to governance: a ruler must protect the people, follow the kingly code, and bring them happiness through justice. The verse measures power by moral responsibility.
ramayan::1395.modern_relevance: You manage a team, a family, or a small community, and people quietly feel the shape of your decisions. This verse asks whether your authority makes life steadier, fairer, and less fearful for those who depend on you.
ramayan::1395.insight: It shifts leadership from control to responsibility for others' welfare.

ramayan::1396.verse_sanskrit: कच्चित्ते सम्भृता भृत्या: कच्चित्तिष्ठन्ति शासने । कच्चित्ते विजितास्सर्वे रिपवो रिपुसूदन । । 1528 । ।
ramayan::1396.verse_hindi: Are your servants provided well with their requirements? Do they abide by your command? O Destroyer of foes have all your enemies been conquered ?
ramayan::1396.english_translation: Are your servants properly maintained? Do they remain under your command? O destroyer of foes, have all your enemies been conquered?
ramayan::1396.translation_literal: कच्चित् (whether) / ते (your) / सम्भृताḥ (well-provided) / भृत्याः (servants) / कच्चित् (whether) / तिष्ठन्ति (remain) / शासने (in command) / कच्चित् (whether) / ते (your) / विजिताः (conquered) / सर्वे (all) / रिपवः (enemies) / रिपुसूदन (O destroyer of foes)
ramayan::1396.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1396.essence: A ruler is only as sound as the people and order he sustains.
ramayan::1396.simple_meaning: A king is being checked on the basics of rule: whether his servants are cared for, obedient, and whether his enemies have been subdued.
ramayan::1396.simple_insight: Leadership is measured by care, order, and the ability to protect what depends on you.
ramayan::1396.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is questioning King Viswamitra like a royal elder would question a ruler after a long stay. He asks whether the king’s servants are supported, whether they obey, and whether his enemies have been defeated. It is part of a larger check on the health of the kingdom.
ramayan::1396.modern_relevance: Before a board meeting, you realize the team is exhausted, confused, and quietly drifting. The real question is not your title — it is whether the people under you are supported and aligned.
ramayan::1396.insight: It shifts attention from image to stewardship: a leader must keep people secure, ordered, and cared for.

ramayan::1397.verse_sanskrit: कच्चिद्बलेषु कोशेषु मित्रेषु च परन्तप । कुशलं ते नरव्याघ्र पुत्रपौत्रे तवानघ । । 1529 । ।
ramayan::1397.verse_hindi: O Tormentor of enemies O Sinless one O Tiger among men is it all well with your army, treasury, friends, sons and grandsons?
ramayan::1397.english_translation: O tormentor of enemies, O sinless one, O tiger among men, is it all well with your army, treasury, friends, sons, and grandsons?
ramayan::1397.translation_literal: कच्चित् (is it) / बलेषु (in the armies) / कोशेषु (in the treasuries) / मित्रेषु (in the friends) / च (and) / परन्तप (O tormentor of enemies) / कुशलं (well-being) / ते (of you) / नरव्याघ्र (O tiger among men) / पुत्रपौत्रे (in sons and grandsons) / तव (of yours) / अनघ (O sinless one)
ramayan::1397.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1397.essence: Well-being is not single-layered; it includes strength, support, and family.
ramayan::1397.simple_meaning: The speaker is asking whether the king's military strength, wealth, allies, children, and grandchildren are all prospering.
ramayan::1397.simple_insight: True leadership is checked in every part of life, not just the throne.
ramayan::1397.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra is speaking to Rama in a courteous, formal way. Before any teaching begins, he asks after Rama’s whole condition: army, treasury, allies, children, and grandchildren. It is a respectful inquiry, not a philosophical statement.
ramayan::1397.modern_relevance: A friend asks about your job, savings, relationships, and family in one breath. Real care looks at the whole life, not just the part that is publicly visible.
ramayan::1397.insight: It reminds you to assess well-being broadly, across security, support, and family stability.

ramayan::1398.verse_sanskrit: सर्वत्र कुशलं राजा वसिष्ठं प्रत्युदाहरत् । विश्वामित्रो महातेजा वसिष्ठं विनयान्वित: । । 15210 । ।
ramayan::1398.verse_hindi: Highly brilliant king Viswamitra, humbly informed Vasishta that all was well.
ramayan::1398.english_translation: The highly brilliant Viswamitra, humble and courteous, replied to Vasishta that everything was well.
ramayan::1398.translation_literal: सर्वत्र (everywhere) / कुशलं (well-being) / राजा (king) / वसिष्ठं (to Vasishta) / प्रत्युदाहरत् (replied) / विश्वामित्रो (Viswamitra) / महातेजा (highly brilliant) / वसिष्ठं (to Vasishta) / विनयान्वितः (endowed with humility and courtesy)
ramayan::1398.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1398.simple_meaning: Viswamitra answers Vasishta politely and says that everything is fine.
ramayan::1398.simple_insight: Even great power can speak with humility.
ramayan::1398.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra, the powerful royal sage, is in conversation with Vasishta. Instead of pride, he answers with courtesy and calm. The verse simply marks that exchange, showing the respectful tone between two great figures.
ramayan::1398.modern_relevance: You finally get a message from someone you respect, and you choose warmth instead of proving yourself. That restraint changes the whole tone.
ramayan::1398.insight: It shows that status does not need to become arrogance.

ramayan::1399.verse_sanskrit: कृत्वोभौ सुचिरं कालं धर्मिष्ठौ ता: कथा: शुभा: । मुदा परमया युक्तौ प्रीयेतां तौ परस्परम् । । 15211 । ।
ramayan::1399.verse_hindi: Both the righteous personalities dwelt at length on various matters and interesting anecdotes with great delight and derived mutual pleasure.
ramayan::1399.english_translation: Both righteous men spent a long time speaking of auspicious matters and pleasant stories, and they took great delight in each other’s company.
ramayan::1399.translation_literal: कृत्वा (having done) / उभौ (both) / सुचिरम् (for a long time) / कालम् (time) / धर्मिष्ठौ (the two righteous ones) / ताः (those) / कथाः (stories / conversations) / शुभाः (auspicious, pleasant) / मुदा (with joy) / परमया (supreme) / युक्तौ (joined, endowed) / प्रीयेताम् (they delighted) / तौ (those two) / परस्परम् (mutually / each other)
ramayan::1399.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1399.essence: Peace between wise people can be shown by ordinary delight.
ramayan::1399.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra and Vasishta spent a long time in warm, joyful conversation, sharing good stories and enjoying each other’s company.
ramayan::1399.simple_insight: Even great people need unguarded conversation and mutual ease.
ramayan::1399.detailed_meaning: After the formal greetings between Vishwamitra and Vasishta, the two sages settle into a long, pleasant exchange. Nothing doctrinal is being argued here; Valmiki is simply showing reconciliation, ease, and shared delight before the next important turn in the meeting.
ramayan::1399.modern_relevance: You finally sit down with someone after years of tension, and the first hour is just easy laughter, old stories, and relief. Not every healing needs a speech.
ramayan::1399.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to restored human ease and quiet reconciliation.

ramayan::1400.verse_sanskrit: ततो वसिष्ठो भगवान् कथाऽन्ते रघुनन्दन । विश्वामित्रमिदं वाक्यमुवाच प्रहसन्निव । । 15212 । ।
ramayan::1400.verse_hindi: O Descendent of Raghu at the end of the conversation, venerable Vasishta, smiling as
ramayan::1400.english_translation: Then Vasishta, smiling, said this to Viswamitra at the end of the conversation: "Raghu's descendant..."
ramayan::1400.translation_literal: ततः (then) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / भगवान् (venerable) / कथा-अन्ते (at the end of the conversation) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of Raghu) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / इदम् (this) / वाक्यम् (speech) / उवाच (said) / प्रहसन्-इव (as if smiling)
ramayan::1400.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1400.essence: The conversation ends, and respect turns into hospitality.
ramayan::1400.simple_meaning: Vasishta smiles and begins speaking to Viswamitra after their conversation ends.
ramayan::1400.simple_insight: A calm exchange is about to turn into a meaningful offer of respect.
ramayan::1400.detailed_meaning: After a long, friendly conversation between Vasishta and Viswamitra, the sage smiles and turns to speak again. This verse is only the lead-in to his offer of hospitality, so it supports the next line rather than standing alone.
ramayan::1400.modern_relevance: After a tense meeting finally softens, someone says, “Let me take care of you now.” The real shift is not in the words, but in the warmth behind them.
ramayan::1400.insight: It prepares the reader for an act of honour, not a new teaching.

ramayan::1401.verse_sanskrit: आतिथ्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि बलस्यास्य महाबल । तव चैवाप्रमेयस्य यथार्हं सम्प्रतीच्छ मे । । 15213 । ।
ramayan::1401.verse_hindi: O Highy powerful Viswamitra I wish to offer appropriate hospitality to you and to your incomparable army. Be pleased to accept it.
ramayan::1401.english_translation: O highly powerful Vishwamitra, I wish to offer proper hospitality to your incomparable army. Please accept it from me.
ramayan::1401.translation_literal: आतिथ्यम् (hospitality) / कर्तुम् (to do) / इच्छामि (I wish) / बलस्य (of the army) / अस्य (this) / महाबल (O greatly powerful one) / तव (your) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / अप्रमेयस्य (of the immeasurable one) / यथार्हम् (as is fitting) / सम्प्रतीच्छ (please accept) / मे (from me)
ramayan::1401.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1401.essence: True respect is proved by how you receive someone.
ramayan::1401.simple_meaning: Vasishta asks Vishwamitra to accept proper hospitality for him and his army.
ramayan::1401.simple_insight: Respect is shown through action, not just words.
ramayan::1401.detailed_meaning: After a long, pleasant exchange, Vasishta turns to Vishwamitra and his army and offers them proper hospitality. The moment matters because it shows honour in practice: a host must receive even a powerful guest with care and dignity.
ramayan::1401.modern_relevance: You have a guest in your home after a tense conversation, and you still choose warmth. Real respect shows up in what you offer, not what you feel privately.
ramayan::1401.insight: It shifts honour from sentiment to concrete welcome.

ramayan::1402.verse_sanskrit: सत्क्रियां तु भवानेतां प्रतीच्छतु मयोद्यताम् । राजा त्वमतिथिश्रेष्ठ: पूजनीय: प्रयत्नत: । । 15214 । ।
ramayan::1402.verse_hindi: Please accept the honour I extend. Being a king, you are a distinguished guest. you deserve to be treated respectfully in all possible ways.
ramayan::1402.english_translation: Please accept the honour I extend. Being a king, you are a distinguished guest and deserve respectful treatment in every possible way.
ramayan::1402.translation_literal: सत्क्रियाम् (honourable treatment) / तु (indeed) / भवान् (you) / एताम् (this) / प्रतीच्छतु (please accept) / मया (by me) / उद्यताम् (offered) / राजा (king) / त्वम् (you) / अतिथि-श्रेष्ठः (best among guests) / पूजनीयः (worthy of honour) / प्रयत्नतः (with effort)
ramayan::1402.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1402.essence: Honor can disarm tension before words do.
ramayan::1402.simple_meaning: Vasishta asks Viswamitra to accept his hospitality and honour him properly as an honoured guest and king.
ramayan::1402.simple_insight: Respect opens the way where pride could have closed it.
ramayan::1402.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just welcomed Viswamitra and his army after a tense meeting. Instead of rivalry, he offers hospitality with full respect, calling Viswamitra a king and a guest worthy of honour. The verse keeps the scene moving toward reconciliation.
ramayan::1402.modern_relevance: You meet someone after a long, awkward silence and choose courtesy first. That single act can soften a room that was ready for conflict.
ramayan::1402.insight: It shifts the response from status tension to gracious hospitality.

ramayan::1403.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन विश्वामित्रो महामति: । कृतमित्यब्रवीद्राजा प्रियवाक्येन मे त्वया । । 15215 । ।
ramayan::1403.verse_hindi: To these words of Vasishta, the great intellectual Viswamitra said, you have spoken pleasing words. This in itself is hospitality for me.
ramayan::1403.english_translation: To these words of Vasishta, the great-minded Viswamitra said, “You have spoken pleasing words. This itself is hospitality to me.”
ramayan::1403.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus spoken to) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामतिः (great-minded) / कृतमिति (it is done) / अब्रवीत् (said) / राजा (the king) / प्रियवाक्येन (with pleasing words) / मे (to me) / त्वया (by you)
ramayan::1403.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1403.essence: Respectful words can be hospitality enough.
ramayan::1403.simple_meaning: Viswamitra accepts Vasishta's courteous words as hospitality itself. The honor is not in food or gifts, but in respectful speech.
ramayan::1403.simple_insight: Kind words can be a real offering when they are sincere.
ramayan::1403.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has come to Vasishta's hermitage with his army, and Vasishta is offering welcome with full respect. In this verse, Viswamitra responds that Vasishta's gracious words already count as hospitality, showing mutual honor rather than conflict.
ramayan::1403.modern_relevance: You walk into a room tense with status and expectations, and one person softens everything by speaking with genuine respect. Sometimes that alone is the welcome.
ramayan::1403.insight: It shifts attention from formal gifts to the dignity carried in speech.

ramayan::1404.verse_sanskrit: फलमूलेन भगवन् विद्यते यत्तवाश्रमे । पाद्येनाचमनीयेन भगवद्दर्शनेन च । । 15216 । । सर्वथा च महाप्राज्ञ पूजार्हेण सुपूजित: । गमिष्यामि नमस्तेऽस्तु मैत्रेणेक्षस्व चक्षुषा । । 15217 । ।
ramayan::1404.verse_hindi: O Worshipful one O Profoundly wise one you are worthy of homage. You have excellently honoured me in all possible ways with whatever fruits and roots available in your hermitage, with water for washing feet and for sipping. You have permitted me darshan with your revered self. I shall leave (now). My regards Look upon me with eyes of friendship.
ramayan::1404.english_translation: O worshipful one, profoundly wise one, you are worthy of honour. You have honoured me well with fruits, roots, water for washing the feet, water for sipping, and your revered presence. I shall depart now. My respects to you; look upon me with friendly eyes.
ramayan::1404.translation_literal: फलमूलेन (with fruits and roots) / भगवन् (O worshipful one) / विद्यते (there is) / यत् (whatever) / तव (your) / आश्रमे (in the hermitage) / पाद्येन (with water for the feet) / आचमनीयेन (with water for sipping) / भगवद्दर्शनेन (with seeing the revered one) / च (and) / सर्वथा (in every way) / च (and) / महाप्राज्ञ (O profoundly wise one) / पूजार्हेण (with what is worthy of worship) / सुपूजितः (well honoured) / गमिष्यामि (I shall go) / नमस्तेऽस्तु (let there be my respects to you) / मैत्रेण (with friendliness) / ईक्षस्व (look) / चक्षुषा (with the eye)
ramayan::1404.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1404.essence: Respect is shown by receiving well and leaving well.
ramayan::1404.simple_meaning: Viswamitra thanks Vasishta for the hospitality of the hermitage and prepares to leave respectfully.
ramayan::1404.simple_insight: True respect includes gratitude, humility, and a clean farewell.
ramayan::1404.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been received in Vasishta's hermitage with simple offerings and honour. After accepting the welcome, he responds with courtesy, acknowledges the kindness, and prepares to depart. The verse closes the exchange with mutual respect.
ramayan::1404.modern_relevance: You leave a friend's home after they fed you from a nearly empty kitchen. You notice the care, thank them properly, and don't make the moment awkward by overstaying.
ramayan::1404.insight: It teaches you to receive kindness gracefully and exit without clinging.

ramayan::1405.verse_sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवन्तं राजानं वसिष्ठ:पुनरेव हि । न्यमन्त्रयत धर्मात्मा पुन:पुनरुदारधी: । । 15218 । ।
ramayan::1405.verse_hindi: As the king was addressing thus the righteous and generous Vasishta, repeatedly requested him to accept his hospitality.
ramayan::1405.english_translation: As the king was speaking thus, the righteous and generous Vasishta again and again invited him to accept his hospitality.
ramayan::1405.translation_literal: एवं (thus) / ब्रुवन्तं (speaking) / राजानं (the king) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / पुनरेव (again indeed) / हि (certainly) / न्यमन्त्रयत (invited) / धर्मात्मा (righteous-souled) / पुनःपुनः (again and again) / उदारधीः (generous-minded)
ramayan::1405.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1405.essence: True welcome keeps returning until the guest feels safe to accept.
ramayan::1405.simple_meaning: Vasishta keeps urging King Vishvamitra to stay and accept the welcome offered to him.
ramayan::1405.simple_insight: Hospitality is not a one-time offer; it is repeated with sincerity.
ramayan::1405.detailed_meaning: After Vishvamitra praises Vasishta's welcome, the sage does not let the moment end. He insists again and again that the king accept the hospitality of his hermitage, showing the warmth and dignity of a host who will not let a guest depart unheard.
ramayan::1405.modern_relevance: Someone declines your help twice, and you still offer it a third time because you mean it. Real generosity does not disappear after the first refusal.
ramayan::1405.insight: It shows how genuine hospitality keeps inviting without pride or impatience.

ramayan::1406.verse_sanskrit: बाढमित्येव गाधेयो वसिष्ठं प्रत्युवाच ह । यथा प्रियं भगवतस्तथाऽस्तु मुनिपुङ्गव । । 15219 । ।
ramayan::1406.verse_hindi: The son of Gadhi said to Vasishta, O Preeminent among sages, be it so, O venerable one they will be done.
ramayan::1406.english_translation: The son of Gadhi said to Vasishta, “So be it, O best of sages. Let it be as you wish.”
ramayan::1406.translation_literal: बाढम् (so be it) / इति एव (thus indeed) / गाधेयः (the son of Gadhi) / वसिष्ठम् (to Vasishta) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / ह (indeed) / यथा (as) / प्रियम् (pleasing) / भगवतः (of the venerable one) / तथा (so) / अस्तु (let it be) / मुनिपुङ्गव (O best among sages)
ramayan::1406.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::1406.essence: Respect ends resistance when the other person’s wish is honoured.
ramayan::1406.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra agrees to Vasishta’s request and yields to his wishes.
ramayan::1406.simple_insight: Sometimes wisdom looks like simple consent, not argument.
ramayan::1406.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has been repeatedly invited and honoured at Vishvamitra’s hermitage. After all the respectful urging, Vishvamitra finally answers with calm acceptance, telling the sage that whatever pleases him should be done. The moment simply moves the conversation forward.
ramayan::1406.modern_relevance: A host keeps insisting you stay, and after the third refusal you finally say yes because the other person’s wish matters more than your own plan.
ramayan::1406.insight: It shows how respect can end a negotiation without friction.

ramayan::1407.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो महातेजा वसिष्ठो जपतां वर: । आजुहाव तत: प्रीत: कल्माषीं धूतकल्मष: । । 15220 । ।
ramayan::1407.verse_hindi: Vasishta who was highly brilliant the greatest among those who meditate (on Brahman) and free from sins was pleased. Thereafter he called the speckled cow (Kamadhenu):
ramayan::1407.english_translation: Vasishta, highly brilliant and the best among those who recite mantras, was pleased. Then, purified of all taint, he called out to the speckled cow.
ramayan::1407.translation_literal: एवमुक्तो (thus spoken to) / महातेजा (highly brilliant) / वसिष्ठो (Vasishta) / जपतां वरः (best among reciters) / आजुहाव (called out) / ततः (then) / प्रीतः (pleased) / कल्माषीं (the speckled one) / धूतकल्मषः (one whose taint was shaken off)
ramayan::1407.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1407.essence: Hospitality becomes real only when generosity is put into action.
ramayan::1407.simple_meaning: Pleased by the request, Vasishta called the divine cow to come forward.
ramayan::1407.simple_insight: A generous act begins with a calm, willing heart.
ramayan::1407.detailed_meaning: King Vishvamitra has asked to be hosted, and Vasishta has agreed. Pleased by the exchange, the sage calls Kamadhenu, the speckled cow, so she can provide the feast that will test the scale of his generosity.
ramayan::1407.modern_relevance: You finally say yes to hosting everyone, and then the real work begins. First comes willingness; then comes what that willingness can actually provide.
ramayan::1407.insight: It shifts attention from the invitation itself to the readiness needed to fulfil it.

ramayan::1408.verse_sanskrit: एह्येहि शबले क्षिप्रं श्रृणु चापि वचो मम । सबलस्यास्य राजर्षे:कर्तुं व्यवसितोऽस्म्यहम् । । 15221 । । भोजनेन महार्हेण सत्कारं संविधत्स्व मे ।
ramayan::1408.verse_hindi: O Sabala, come on quick Listen to my words. I have decided to honour this royal saint and his army with excellent food. Make necessary arrangemets.
ramayan::1408.english_translation: O Sabala, come quickly and listen to my words. I have decided to honour this royal sage and his army with excellent food. Arrange the hospitality for me.
ramayan::1408.translation_literal: एह्येहि (come, come) / शबले (O Sabala) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / श्रृणु (listen) / च (and) / अपि (also) / वचः (words) / मम (my) / सबलस्य (of the one with an army) / अस्य (this) / राजर्षेः (royal sage) / कर्तुम् (to do) / व्यवसितः (resolved) / अस्मि (I am) / अहम् (I) / भोजनेन (with food) / महार्हेण (excellent) / सत्कारम् (honour) / संविधत्स्व (arrange) / मे (for me)
ramayan::1408.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1408.essence: Generosity becomes real only when it is made practical.
ramayan::1408.simple_meaning: Vasishta asks Sabala to hurry and prepare a lavish meal to honour the royal sage and his army.
ramayan::1408.simple_insight: True welcome means making room for others with generosity, not just words.
ramayan::1408.detailed_meaning: Gadhi's son has agreed to Vasishta's request. Pleased, Vasishta turns to Sabala, the wish-fulfilling cow, and asks her to prepare rich food for Vishvamitra and his army. The verse is a practical instruction, not the central teaching itself.
ramayan::1408.modern_relevance: A guest arrives with people depending on him, and you do not just offer tea — you open the fridge, call for help, and make the whole place ready.
ramayan::1408.insight: It shifts attention from polite intention to concrete hospitality.

ramayan::1409.verse_sanskrit: यस्य यस्य यथाकामं षड्रसेष्वभिपूजितम् । तत्सर्वं कामधुक्क्षिप्रमभिवर्ष कृते मम । । 15222 । ।
ramayan::1409.verse_hindi: O Kamadhenu quickly entertain them for my sake with the food of six kinds of tastes (varieties of rich dishes) as desired by each.
ramayan::1409.english_translation: O Kamadhenu, quickly entertain them for my sake with the food of six kinds of tastes, each as desired.
ramayan::1409.translation_literal: यस्य यस्य (of each one) / यथाकामम् (as desired) / षड्रसेषु (in the six tastes) / अभिपूजितम् (honoured) / तत् सर्वम् (all that) / कामधुक् (Kamadhenu) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / अभिवर्ष (pour forth) / कृते मम (for my sake)
ramayan::1409.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1409.essence: True hospitality gives each person what suits them best.
ramayan::1409.simple_meaning: Kamadhenu is asked to quickly provide every kind of rich food, suited to each guest's desire.
ramayan::1409.simple_insight: Abundance can be summoned in service of hospitality, not hoarded for status.
ramayan::1409.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has welcomed Rama's royal party and now turns to Sabala, the wish-fulfilling cow. This verse is not a teaching on its own; it is the command that begins a miraculous feast, with every guest to be served according to taste and need.
ramayan::1409.modern_relevance: You are hosting people after a long day, and you want every plate to feel considered. This verse lives in that instinct to feed others well, not merely to feed them fast.
ramayan::1409.insight: It frames generosity as precise care, not generic plenty.

ramayan::1410.verse_sanskrit: रसेनान्नेन पानेन लेह्यचोष्येण संयुतम् । अन्नानां निचयं सर्वं सृजस्व शबले त्वर । । 15223 । ।
ramayan::1410.verse_hindi: O Sabala create at once all food items consisting of liquids and solids for drinking, tasting and siping.
ramayan::1410.english_translation: O Sabala, create at once all kinds of food and drink, both liquid and solid, for tasting and chewing.
ramayan::1410.translation_literal: रसेन (with liquid foods) / अन्नेन (with solid food) / पानेन (with drink) / लेह्यचोष्येण (with what is licked and chewed) / संयुतम् (combined) / अन्नानाम् (of foods) / निचयम् (a heap, abundance) / सर्वम् (all) / सृजस्व (create) / शबले (O Sabala) / त्वर (quickly)
ramayan::1410.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1410.essence: Every kind of nourishment is summoned at once.
ramayan::1410.simple_meaning: Vasishta asks Sabala to produce every kind of food and drink immediately.
ramayan::1410.simple_insight: Abundance can arrive in an instant when the right source is called upon.
