ramayan::1410.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has welcomed a royal guest and his army. After asking Sabala to provide a feast, he now specifies the full spread: drinks, liquids, solids, and every kind of edible item. The verse is a practical instruction, not a teaching.
ramayan::1410.modern_relevance: You are rushing to feed unexpected guests, and the table has to appear now. This is the language of immediate provision, not reflection.
ramayan::1410.insight: It shows a command for complete hospitality, down to every category of food.

ramayan::1411.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ता वसिष्ठेन शबला शत्रुसूदन । विदधे कामधुक्कामान्यस्य यस्य यथेप्सितम् । । 1531 । ।
ramayan::1411.verse_hindi: O Destroyer of foes (Rama) addressed thus by Vasishta the wishfulfilling Sabala satisfied each ones  desires.
ramayan::1411.english_translation: Addressed thus by Vasishta, Sabala, the wish-fulfilling cow, satisfied each person's desire as desired.
ramayan::1411.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्ता (spoken to) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / शबला (Sabala) / शत्रुसूदन (O destroyer of foes) / विदधे (produced, made) / कामधुक् (wish-fulfilling) / कामान् (desires) / अस्य (of this one) / यस्य (of whom) / यथा-इप्सितम् (as desired)
ramayan::1411.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1411.essence: Sabala instantly turned desire into abundance.
ramayan::1411.simple_meaning: Sabala, told by Vasishta, produced whatever each person wanted.
ramayan::1411.simple_insight: Abundance appears when the right source is invoked.
ramayan::1411.detailed_meaning: Vasishta calls Sabala, the wish-fulfilling cow, and she begins providing whatever each guest desires. The verse is a bridge in the scene, showing the miracle in motion before the food and drinks are listed next.
ramayan::1411.modern_relevance: A host opens the door and suddenly the table is overflowing before the guests even sit down. The verse pauses on that moment of effortless abundance before naming what arrives.
ramayan::1411.insight: It shifts attention from the miracle itself to the act of meeting every need at once.

ramayan::1412.verse_sanskrit: इक्षून्मधूं स्तथा लाजान्मैरेयांश्च वरासनान् । पानानि च महार्हाणि भक्ष्यांश्चोच्चावचां स्तथा । । 1532 । ।
ramayan::1412.verse_hindi: Sugarcane, honey and fried grain, invigorating liquors in good containers, excellent drinks and varieties of food (were served).
ramayan::1412.english_translation: Sugarcane, honey and fried grain, invigorating liquors in good containers, excellent drinks and varieties of food were served.
ramayan::1412.translation_literal: इक्षून् (sugarcane) / मधून् (honey) / तथा (and) / लाजान् (fried grain) / मैरेयान् (intoxicating drinks) / च (and) / वरासनान् (excellent seats/containers) / पानानि (drinks) / च (and) / महार्हाणि (highly valuable) / भक्ष्यान् (eatables) / च (and) / उच्चावचान् (varied kinds) / तथा (and)
ramayan::1412.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1412.essence: The miracle shows itself as plenty, not spectacle.
ramayan::1412.simple_meaning: A lavish spread of sweets, drinks, and many kinds of food was prepared and served.
ramayan::1412.simple_insight: Abundance can be a form of welcome, not excess.
ramayan::1412.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has asked Sabala to provide whatever is needed, and the wish-fulfilling cow responds at once. This verse simply lists the rich food and drinks that appear, showing the scale of the miraculous feast rather than teaching a separate lesson.
ramayan::1412.modern_relevance: At a wedding buffet laid out in perfect rows, the variety itself becomes the message: someone wanted every guest to feel fully received.
ramayan::1412.insight: It shifts attention from the miracle to its visible generosity.

ramayan::1413.verse_sanskrit: उष्णाढ्यस्योदनस्यात्र राशय: पर्वतोपमा: । मृष्टान्नानि च सूपाश्च दधिकुल्यास्तथैव च । । 1533 । । नानास्वादुरसानां च षाडबानां तथैव च । भाजनानि सुपूर्णानि गौडानि च सहस्रश: । । 1534 । ।
ramayan::1413.verse_hindi: Heaps of hot rice as high as mountains, savoury food, condiments and on abundance of curd, various kinds of soups, containers in their thousands completely filled with edibles with all six tastes and preparations made of jaggery (were distributed).
ramayan::1413.english_translation: Heaps of hot rice like mountains, savoury dishes, soups, curd in abundance, many drinks with every taste, and thousands of brimming vessels filled with jaggery preparations were distributed.
ramayan::1413.translation_literal: उष्णाढ्यस्य (of hot) / उदनस्य (rice) / अत्र (here) / राशय: (heaps) / पर्वतोपमा: (mountain-like) / मृष्टान्नानि (delicious foods) / च (and) / सूपाश्च (soups also) / दधिकुल्यास्तथैव च (streams of curd likewise) / नानास्वादुरसानां च (of various sweet tastes also) / षाडबानां तथैव च (of shadava drinks likewise) / भाजनानि (vessels) / सुपूर्णानि (completely full) / गौडानि (jaggery preparations) / च (and) / सहस्रश: (in thousands)
ramayan::1413.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1413.essence: Generosity becomes visible when everything is given in plenty.
ramayan::1413.simple_meaning: The feast was overflowing with rice, soups, curd, drinks, and sweets, all prepared in huge quantities.
ramayan::1413.simple_insight: Abundance can be real and generous, not merely symbolic.
ramayan::1413.detailed_meaning: Vasistha is feeding Viswamitra’s large retinue at Rama’s request. This verse lingers on the scale of the meal itself: mountains of rice, rivers of curd, and vessels filled to the brim. It is a scene of royal hospitality, not teaching.
ramayan::1413.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall where servers keep bringing out tray after tray, you feel the quiet power of generosity made visible.
ramayan::1413.insight: It shows hospitality as a concrete act of overflowing care, not a vague sentiment.

ramayan::1414.verse_hindi: O Rama, Vasistha entertained everybody in Viswamitras army to their full satisfaction. They were all wellfed and happy.
ramayan::1414.english_translation: O Rama, Vasistha fed and satisfied all of Viswamitra's army. Everyone was well-fed, delighted, and fully content.
ramayan::1414.translation_literal: सर्वम् (all) / आसीत् (was) / सुसन्तुष्ठम् (fully satisfied) / हृष्ट-पुष्ट-जन-आयुतम् (crowded with delighted and nourished people) / विश्वामित्र-बलम् (Viswamitra's army) / राम (O Rama) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasistha) / अभितर्पितम् (fully fed and satisfied)
ramayan::1414.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1414.essence: Full stomachs can soften even a tense gathering.
ramayan::1414.simple_meaning: Vasistha made sure Viswamitra's whole army was fed well and left happy.
ramayan::1414.simple_insight: Small acts of care can settle an entire crowd.
ramayan::1414.detailed_meaning: After the feast is prepared, Vasistha’s hospitality reaches every member of Viswamitra’s force. The army leaves full, pleased, and at ease. The verse simply records the completed scene, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::1414.modern_relevance: You host a room full of tired guests, and the relief is visible when everyone finally eats. Care can quiet tension faster than argument.
ramayan::1414.insight: It highlights the quiet power of generous hospitality in easing conflict.

ramayan::1415.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रोऽपि राजर्षिर्हृष्ट: पुष्टस्तदाभवत् । सान्त:पुरवरो राजा सब्राह्मणपुरोहित: । । 1536 । ।
ramayan::1415.verse_hindi: King Viswamitra along with ladies, priests and brahmins including the royal sage were fully satisfied and delighted.
ramayan::1415.english_translation: King Viswamitra, the royal sage, was delighted and well satisfied, along with the women of the inner apartments, priests, and brahmins.
ramayan::1415.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / अपि (also) / राजर्षिः (royal sage) / हृष्टः (delighted) / पुष्टः (well nourished, satisfied) / तदा (then) / अभवत् (became) / सान्तःपुरवरो (with the women of the inner apartments) / राजा (king) / सब्राह्मणपुरोहितः (with brahmins and priests)
ramayan::1415.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1415.essence: Careful hospitality turns rivalry into goodwill.
ramayan::1415.simple_meaning: Viswamitra and everyone with him were fed well and left happy after Vasistha's hospitality.
ramayan::1415.simple_insight: Generosity can dissolve tension faster than argument.
ramayan::1415.detailed_meaning: Vasistha has welcomed Viswamitra's visiting force and fed them lavishly. After the meal, the royal sage, his attendants, priests, and brahmins are all pleased. This verse simply records the success of the hospitality before the next exchange begins.
ramayan::1415.modern_relevance: You host people who arrived guarded and tired, then watch their shoulders drop after a good meal. Sometimes warmth changes the whole mood before a single word does.
ramayan::1415.insight: It shows how generous treatment can soften pride and open the way for dialogue.

ramayan::1416.verse_sanskrit: सामात्यो मन्त्रिसहितस्सभृत्य: पूजितस्तदा । युक्त: परमहर्षेण वसिष्ठमिदमब्रवीत् । । 1537 । ।
ramayan::1416.verse_hindi: Having received the hospitality along with his counsellors, ministers and attendants, Viswamitra, filled with great delight, said to Vasishta:
ramayan::1416.english_translation: Having received the hospitality along with his counsellors, ministers and attendants, Viswamitra, filled with great delight, said to Vasishta:
ramayan::1416.translation_literal: सामात्यः (with counsellors) / मन्त्रिसहितः (with ministers together) / सभृत्यः (with attendants) / पूजितः (honoured) / तदा (then) / युक्तः (filled) / परमहर्षेण (with great delight) / वसिष्ठम् (to Vasishta) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1416.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1416.essence: Respect received well can dissolve rivalry for a moment.
ramayan::1416.simple_meaning: Viswamitra, along with his whole retinue, was treated with great honour and joyfully spoke to Vasishta.
ramayan::1416.simple_insight: Being received with care can soften pride and open the heart.
ramayan::1416.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just fed and honoured Viswamitra’s entire company. Satisfied by that generous welcome, the royal sage turns to Vasishta in delight. The verse simply sets up the grateful speech that follows.
ramayan::1416.modern_relevance: You walk into a home after a long, difficult journey and find the table already set for everyone with you. That quiet generosity changes the mood before anyone speaks.
ramayan::1416.insight: It shifts attention from status to gratitude before the real exchange begins.

ramayan::1417.verse_sanskrit: पूजितोऽहं त्वया ब्रह्मन् पूजार्हेण सुसत्कृत: । श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि वाक्यं वाक्यविशारद । । 1538 । ।
ramayan::1417.verse_hindi: O Brahman you are worthy of worship. I was received with reverence and wellentertained by you. O Sage conversant with speech listen.
ramayan::1417.english_translation: O Brahman, you are worthy of worship. I was received with reverence and well entertained by you. O sage skilled in speech, listen; I will now speak.
ramayan::1417.translation_literal: पूजितः (honored) / अहम् (I) / त्वया (by you) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahman) / पूजार्हेण (by one worthy of honor) / सुसत्कृतः (well treated) / श्रूयताम् (let it be heard) / अभिधास्यामि (I will speak) / वाक्यम् (a statement) / वाक्यविशारद (skilled in speech)
ramayan::1417.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::1417.essence: Courtesy prepares the ground for a serious demand.
ramayan::1417.simple_meaning: Visvamitra thanks Vasistha for the respectful welcome and asks him to listen to what he is about to say.
ramayan::1417.simple_insight: Respect opens the door, but the real conversation begins after it.
ramayan::1417.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has been received with honor in Vasistha's home. Still pleased from the hospitality, he addresses Vasistha respectfully and asks him to listen before he makes his request. The verse serves as a courteous opening to the demand for Sabala that follows.
ramayan::1417.modern_relevance: You’ve been welcomed into a room where the mood is warm, but the real ask is still coming. Good manners can soften a difficult request, not erase it.
ramayan::1417.insight: It shows how to frame a hard request with dignity before speaking plainly.

ramayan::1418.verse_sanskrit: गवां शतसहस्रेण दीयतां शबला मम । रत्नं हि भगवन्नेतद्रत्नहारी च प्रार्थिव: । । 1539 । । तस्मान्मे शबलां देहि ममैषा धर्मतो द्विज ।
ramayan::1418.verse_hindi: I shall give you a hundred thousand cows in exchange for Sabala. O Respectable one this cow is a gem. A king (along) has a right on jewels, O Brahmin, for that reason, Sabala rightfully belongs to me. Therefore, give this cow.
ramayan::1418.english_translation: I shall give you a hundred thousand cows in exchange for Sabala. O venerable one, this cow is a jewel. A king has a claim on jewels, O Brahmin; therefore, give me Sabala. She rightfully belongs to me.
ramayan::1418.translation_literal: गवां (of cows) / शतसहस्रेण (by a hundred thousand) / दीयतां (let be given) / शबला (Sabala) / मम (to me) / रत्नं (a jewel) / हि (indeed) / भगवन् (venerable one) / एतत् (this) / रत्नहारी (one who takes jewels) / च (and) / प्रार्थिवः (a king) / तस्मात् (therefore) / मे (to me) / शबलाम् (Sabala) / देहि (give) / मम (my) / एषा (this) / धर्मतः (by right) / द्विज (twice-born one)
ramayan::1418.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1418.essence: Want can sound lawful when it is hungry enough.
ramayan::1418.simple_meaning: Viswamitra offers vast wealth and argues that the sacred cow Sabala should belong to him because a king has a right to precious things.
ramayan::1418.simple_insight: Desire can dress itself as fairness. The mind becomes very persuasive when it wants something badly.
ramayan::1418.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been welcomed by Vasishta, but now he sees Sabala, the miraculous cow in the hermitage. Instead of admiring her from afar, he tries to buy her with wealth and then claims her by royal right. This is the first crack in the meeting.
ramayan::1418.modern_relevance: You see something beautiful in someone else’s life and start explaining why you deserve it. The argument sounds noble, but the wanting is doing the real talking.
ramayan::1418.insight: It exposes how entitlement borrows the language of justice to justify craving.

ramayan::1419.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान्वसिष्ठो मुनिसत्तम: । विश्वामित्रेण धर्मात्मा प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम् । । 15310 । ।
ramayan::1419.verse_hindi: Addressed the by Viswamitra venerable and righteous Vasishta who was of the earth  ascetic replied:
ramayan::1419.english_translation: Thus addressed by Vishwamitra, the venerable and righteous Vasishta replied to the king.
ramayan::1419.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus addressed) / तु (indeed) / भगवान् (venerable one) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / मुनिसत्तमः (best of sages) / विश्वामित्रेण (by Vishvamitra) / धर्मात्मा (righteous) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / महीपतिम् (to the king)
ramayan::1419.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1419.essence: The real stand comes in the next sentence.
ramayan::1419.simple_meaning: Vasishta, addressed by Vishvamitra, answered the king.
ramayan::1419.simple_insight: The reply is about to begin; the real argument comes next.
ramayan::1419.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has just demanded Vasishta's wish-fulfilling cow, Sabala, offering huge wealth in return. This verse simply marks Vasishta's response beginning. The substance of his refusal arrives in the next line.
ramayan::1419.modern_relevance: You can feel the room tighten before someone says the thing that matters. This line is the breath before the refusal.
ramayan::1419.insight: It marks the start of a decisive answer, not the answer itself.

ramayan::1420.verse_sanskrit: नाहं शतसहस्रेण नापि कोटिशतैर्गवाम् । राजन् दास्यामि शबलां राशिभी रजतस्य च । । 15311 । ।
ramayan::1420.verse_hindi: O King I shall not exchange Sabala for a hundred thousand for even or a hundred crore cows or heaps of silver.
ramayan::1420.english_translation: O King, I shall not give away Sabala for a hundred thousand cows, nor even for a hundred crore cows, nor for heaps of silver.
ramayan::1420.translation_literal: नाहम् (I will not) / शतसहस्रेण (by a hundred thousand) / नापि (nor even) / कोटिशतैः (by hundreds of crores) / गवाम् (of cows) / राजन् (O king) / दास्यामि (I will give) / शबलाम् (Sabala) / राशिभिः (by heaps) / रजतस्य (of silver) / च (and)
ramayan::1420.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1420.essence: What is sacred cannot be traded, no matter the price.
ramayan::1420.simple_meaning: Vasishta refuses to sell Sabala, no matter how large the offer. Some things are not for trade.
ramayan::1420.simple_insight: Not everything valuable can be priced. Some bonds are beyond bargaining.
ramayan::1420.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has offered vast wealth for Vasishta’s sacred cow, Sabala. Standing firm, Vasishta rejects the offer completely. This refusal turns a bargaining scene into a clash of pride, value, and spiritual power.
ramayan::1420.modern_relevance: A company offers you a bigger title, more money, and a polished exit — but it would cost the one commitment you made with your whole heart. Vasishta’s refusal shows that some things cannot be bought.
ramayan::1420.insight: It teaches you to recognize what must never be reduced to a transaction.

ramayan::1421.verse_sanskrit: न परित्यागमर्हेयं मत्सकाशादरिन्दम । शाश्वती शबला मह्यं कीर्तिरात्मवतो यथा । । 15312 । ।
ramayan::1421.verse_hindi: O Suppressor of enemies Viswamitra it is not proper to separate this cow from me. The relationship between Sabala and me is permanent like the relationship between a  righteous man and his fame.
ramayan::1421.english_translation: O suppressor of enemies, Viswamitra, it is not right to separate this cow from me. Sabala is permanently mine, like fame belongs to a righteous man.
ramayan::1421.translation_literal: न परित्यागमर्हेयम् (is not fit to be abandoned) / मत्सकाशात् (from my side) / अरिन्दम (O suppressor of enemies) / शाश्वती (permanent) / शबला (Sabala) / मह्यम् (to me) / कीर्तिः (fame) / आत्मवतः (of the self-possessed / righteous one) / यथा (as)
ramayan::1421.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1421.essence: Some things cannot be traded because they are woven into who you are.
ramayan::1421.simple_meaning: Vasishta refuses to give up Sabala. He says the bond between them is lasting, like a good person's reputation.
ramayan::1421.simple_insight: Some relationships are not possessions to trade; they are responsibilities that define you.
ramayan::1421.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has demanded Sabala, but Vasishta stands firm. He says the cow cannot be separated from him, because their bond is enduring. In this clash, the issue is not price but rightful belonging.
ramayan::1421.modern_relevance: Someone asks you to give up the one relationship, tool, or commitment that has held your life together. The pressure is practical, but your refusal comes from knowing this is not something you can casually hand over.
ramayan::1421.insight: It shifts the mind from bargaining over value to recognising an unbreakable bond of responsibility.

ramayan::1422.verse_sanskrit: अस्यां हव्यं च कव्यं च प्राणयात्रा तथैव च । आयत्तमग्निहोत्रं च बलिर्होमस्तथैव च । । 15313 । ।
ramayan::1422.verse_hindi: For havyam (oblations to gods) and kavyam (oblations to ancestors), for fulfilling the necessities of life, maintenance of the sacred fire and offering oblations to all spirits of created beings, and for offerings made to the Firegod I depend on this cow.
ramayan::1422.english_translation: For offerings to the gods and ancestors, for sustaining life, for the sacred fire, and for offerings to the fire, I depend on this cow.
ramayan::1422.translation_literal: अस्याम् (in this) / हव्यं (offering to the gods) / च (and) / कव्यं (offering to the ancestors) / च (and) / प्राणयात्रा (livelihood, maintenance of life) / तथा एव (likewise) / च (and) / आयत्तम् (dependent) / अग्निहोत्रं (the sacred fire rite) / च (and) / बलिः (offering) / होमः (fire oblation) / तत् तथा एव (likewise)
ramayan::1422.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1422.essence: One loss can unravel many forms of sacred order.
ramayan::1422.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra says this cow is needed for ritual offerings, daily living, sacred fire rites, and fire oblations.
ramayan::1422.simple_insight: What sustains a whole life can be hidden in one ordinary form.
ramayan::1422.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra is pressing his case before King Janaka and others by listing everything that depends on Sabala. He is not making a sentimental claim; he is showing that this cow supports ritual, household life, and sacred obligations.
ramayan::1422.modern_relevance: You only notice what supports everything after it is threatened. A single steady source can be carrying your routines, your work, and your obligations without applause.
ramayan::1422.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the network of duties it quietly supports.

ramayan::1423.verse_sanskrit: स्वाहाकारवषट्कारौ विद्याश्च विविधा स्तथा । आयत्तमत्र राजर्षे सर्वमेतन्न संशय: । । 15314 । ।
ramayan::1423.verse_hindi: O Royal saint swaha and vashat and various branches of learning are all dependent on this cow. No doubt about it.
ramayan::1423.english_translation: O royal sage, the offering cries, the sacred exclamation, and many branches of learning all depend on this cow. There is no doubt about it.
ramayan::1423.translation_literal: स्वाहाकारवषट्कारौ (the exclamation svaha and the exclamation vashat) / विद्याः (branches of learning) / च (and) / विविधाः (various) / तथा (also) / आयत्तम् (dependent) / अत्र (here) / राजर्षे (O royal sage) / सर्वम् (all this) / एतत् (this) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::1423.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1423.essence: What looks like one cow is being shown as a whole foundation.
ramayan::1423.simple_meaning: This cow is said to support sacred offerings, ritual recitations, and many kinds of learning. The speaker insists that its value is beyond doubt.
ramayan::1423.simple_insight: Some things quietly hold an entire world together without being seen.
ramayan::1423.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is trying to claim Sabala, and Vasistha is answering with the cow’s hidden importance. He says her presence supports ritual, study, and daily life itself, making this a supporting argument in a larger refusal.
ramayan::1423.modern_relevance: A family heirloom, a notebook, a tool, a person — something small turns out to be carrying more of your life than you realized.
ramayan::1423.insight: It shifts attention from possession to dependence: what seems ordinary may be sustaining everything around it.

ramayan::1424.verse_sanskrit: सर्वस्वमेतत्सत्येन मम तुष्टिकरी सदा । कारणैर्बहुभी राजन्न दास्ये शबलां तव । । 15315 । ।
ramayan::1424.verse_hindi: This one is truly my whole possession, it always gives me contentment. O King for various reasons, I will not give Sabala to you.
ramayan::1424.english_translation: This is truly my whole possession, and it always gives me contentment. O king, for many reasons, I will not give Sabala to you.
ramayan::1424.translation_literal: सर्वस्वम् (all wealth / whole possession) / एतत् (this) / सत्येन (truly) / मम (my) / तुष्टिकरी (contentment-giving) / सदा (always) / कारणैः (for reasons) / बहुभिः (many) / राजन् (O king) / न (not) / दास्ये (I will give) / शबलाम् (Sabala) / तव (to you)
ramayan::1424.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1424.essence: What sustains your life is sometimes the right thing to refuse.
ramayan::1424.simple_meaning: Vasishta says Sabala is not just a cow to him; she is the source of his comfort and livelihood, so he will not give her away.
ramayan::1424.simple_insight: Not everything valuable can be handed over, even under pressure.
ramayan::1424.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has demanded Sabala, the wish-fulfilling cow, after hearing of her powers. Vasishta now refuses plainly: she is his whole support and constant source of contentment, and he will not surrender her, no matter how strongly the king presses.
ramayan::1424.modern_relevance: Someone asks you to give up the one thing that keeps your home steady, your work possible, or your mind intact. You can understand their desire and still say no.
ramayan::1424.insight: It teaches you to protect the foundation that sustains your responsibilities, even when others want access to it.

ramayan::1425.verse_hindi: To there words of Vasishta, Viswamitra who is skilful in conversation reacted with extreme excitement:
ramayan::1425.english_translation: When Vasishta spoke these words, the eloquent Visvamitra answered with great agitation.
ramayan::1425.translation_literal: वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / एवम् (thus) / उक्तः (spoken to) / तु (then) / विश्वामित्रः (Visvamitra) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / ततः (then) / संरब्धतरम् (more fiercely) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / वाक्यम् (speech) / वाक्यविशारदः (skilled in speech)
ramayan::1425.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::1425.essence: Pride turns a negotiation into a test of will.
ramayan::1425.simple_meaning: Visvamitra, provoked by Vasishta's words, answered with intense agitation.
ramayan::1425.simple_insight: Strong feelings can turn a discussion into a contest of pride.
ramayan::1425.detailed_meaning: At Vasishta's refusal, the exchange between the two sages sharpens. Visvamitra, proud and quick to answer, reacts with visible anger. This verse is the turning point before he raises the stakes with a far greater offer.
ramayan::1425.modern_relevance: You hear a calm refusal, and your chest tightens before you can think. The conversation is no longer about the issue — it is now about wounded pride.
ramayan::1425.insight: It shows how quickly ego can hijack a practical exchange.

ramayan::1426.verse_sanskrit: हैरण्यकक्ष्याग्रैवेयान् सुवर्णाङ्कुशभूषितान् । ददामि कुञ्जरांस्तेषां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश । । 15317 । ।
ramayan::1426.verse_hindi: I shall give fourteen thousand elephants with gold trappings around the neck and girth,  and with goads made of gold.
ramayan::1426.english_translation: I shall give fourteen thousand elephants with gold trappings around the neck and girth, and with goads made of gold.
ramayan::1426.translation_literal: हैरण्यकक्ष्याग्रैवेयान् (with gold trappings at the neck and girth) / सुवर्णाङ्कुशभूषितान् (adorned with golden goads) / ददामि (I shall give) / कुञ्जरान् (elephants) / तेषाम् (of them) / सहस्राणि (thousands) / चतुर्दश (fourteen)
ramayan::1426.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::1426.essence: More wealth is offered, but the real dispute remains untouched.
ramayan::1426.simple_meaning: Visvamitra offers a vast number of richly adorned elephants as payment or tribute.
ramayan::1426.simple_insight: Even great wealth cannot settle a conflict of principle.
ramayan::1426.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra, angered by Vasishta's refusal, begins listing immense riches and royal gifts he is willing to offer. This verse is one item in a larger exchange of pride and bargaining, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1426.modern_relevance: You keep raising the offer, hoping more value will solve a refusal. But some no amount of money can buy.
ramayan::1426.insight: It shows how bargaining can become a test of pride, not just a transaction.

ramayan::1427.verse_sanskrit: हैरण्यानां रथानां च श्वेताश्वानां चतुर्युजाम् । ददामि ते शतान्यष्टौ किङ्किणीकविभूषितान् । । 15318 । ।
ramayan::1427.verse_hindi: I shall give you eight hundred chariots made of gold and decorated with small tinkling bells, each chariot yoked with four white horses.
ramayan::1427.english_translation: I shall give you eight hundred chariots made of gold and decorated with small tinkling bells, each chariot yoked with four white horses.
ramayan::1427.translation_literal: हैरण्यानाम् (made of gold) / रथानाम् (of chariots) / च (and) / श्वेताश्वानाम् (of white horses) / चतुर्युजाम् (yoked with four) / ददामि (I give) / ते (to you) / शतानि (hundreds) / अष्टौ (eight) / किङ्किणीकविभूषितान् (decorated with small bells)
ramayan::1427.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1427.essence: The promise keeps growing, item by item.
ramayan::1427.simple_meaning: Viswamitra continues listing gifts he will give: eight hundred golden chariots, each drawn by four white horses and decorated with bells.
ramayan::1427.simple_insight: Some verses are not teachings; they simply show the scale of a lavish promise.
ramayan::1427.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is in the middle of a grand offer, piling up wealth and war equipment as he tries to secure cooperation. This line is one more item in that escalating inventory, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::1427.modern_relevance: You hear a friend or client listing numbers so fast they blur together: vehicles, staff, budgets, extras. The point is not reflection — it is sheer scale.
ramayan::1427.insight: It keeps attention on the sequence of gifts, not on a moral principle.

ramayan::1428.verse_sanskrit: हयानां देशजातानां कुलजानां महौजसाम् । सहस्रमेकं दश च ददामि तव सुव्रत । । 15319 । ।
ramayan::1428.verse_hindi: O Maharshi of auspicious vows I shall give you eleven thousand mighty horses of good breed born in good countries.
ramayan::1428.english_translation: O Maharshi of auspicious vows I shall give you eleven thousand mighty horses of good breed born in good countries.
ramayan::1428.translation_literal: हयानाम् (of horses) / देशजातानाम् (born in good countries) / कुलजानाम् (of noble breed) / महौजसाम् (of great strength) / सहस्रम् (a thousand) / एकम् (one) / दश (ten) / च (and) / ददामि (I give) / तव (to you) / सुव्रत (O one of auspicious vows)
ramayan::1428.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::1428.essence: Lavish gifts can still be a form of pressure.
ramayan::1428.simple_meaning: Ravana offers eleven thousand strong, well-bred horses as part of a larger bargain.
ramayan::1428.simple_insight: Even lavish gifts can be just bargaining when desire is driving them.
ramayan::1428.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to win over a sage with extravagant wealth: elephants, chariots, horses, and cows. This line is one item in that escalating offer, not the main teaching. The real tension is the bargain itself, as Ravana tries to purchase consent.
ramayan::1428.modern_relevance: You pile on perks, promises, and bonuses to get someone to agree. The real question is not how much you offered, but what you are trying to buy.
ramayan::1428.insight: It shifts attention from the size of the gift to the motive behind it.

ramayan::1429.verse_sanskrit: नानावर्णविभक्तानां वयस्स्थानां तथैव च । ददाम्येकां गवां कोटिं शबला दीयतां मम । । 15320 । ।
ramayan::1429.verse_hindi: I shall give one crore young cows of various colours. Give me Sabala.
ramayan::1429.english_translation: I shall give one crore young cows of various colours. Give me Sabala.
ramayan::1429.translation_literal: नानावर्णविभक्तानां (of various colours and separated by different hues) / वयस्स्थानां (of different ages) / तथैव (and likewise) / च (and) / ददामि (I give) / एकाम् (one) / गवाम् (of cows) / कोटिम् (ten million) / शबला (Sabala) / दीयताम् (let be given) / मम (to me)
ramayan::1429.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::1429.essence: Wealth cannot purchase what another person will not release.
ramayan::1429.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra offers a vast wealth of cows in exchange for Sabala, the wish-fulfilling cow he wants from Vasistha.
ramayan::1429.simple_insight: Some things cannot be bought, no matter how much wealth you offer.
ramayan::1429.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra is trying to obtain Sabala from Vasistha. He piles up an enormous offer of wealth—cows, gold, and jewels—to persuade the sage. The verse is part of a bargaining exchange, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::1429.modern_relevance: You can offer more money, more status, more promises — and still fail to get what belongs to trust, not trade.
ramayan::1429.insight: It shows the limits of bargaining when the real issue is attachment and refusal.

ramayan::1430.verse_sanskrit: यावदिच्छसि रत्नं वा हिरण्यं वा द्विजोत्तम । तावद्ददामि तत्सर्वं शबला दीयतां मम । । 15321 । ।
ramayan::1430.verse_hindi: O Best of brahmins I shall offer you jewels or gold as much as you desire. I shall give you everything. Give this Sabala to me.
ramayan::1430.english_translation: O Best of brahmins, I shall offer you jewels or gold as much as you desire. I shall give you everything. Give this Sabala to me.
ramayan::1430.translation_literal: यावत् (as much as) / इच्छसि (you desire) / रत्नं (jewel) / वा (or) / हिरण्यं (gold) / वा (or) / द्विजोत्तम (O best of brahmins) / तावत् (to that extent) / ददामि (I give) / तत् (that) / सर्वम् (all) / शबला (Sabala) / दीयताम् (let be given) / मम (to me)
ramayan::1430.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1430.essence: Wealth can be offered for everything except what is beyond price.
ramayan::1430.simple_meaning: Viswamitra offers Vasishta any wealth he wants, but only if Vasishta gives him Sabala in return.
ramayan::1430.simple_insight: Some things matter more than wealth, no matter how much you offer.
ramayan::1430.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already named horses and cows as gifts, and now he raises the offer to jewels and gold. He is trying to win Sabala from Vasishta, but the exchange is no longer about price. It is about attachment, power, and what a person will not part with.
ramayan::1430.modern_relevance: You can throw money, praise, and leverage at a problem and still fail to move the one thing that matters. Some loyalties cannot be negotiated.
ramayan::1430.insight: It shifts the mind from bargaining for value to recognising what cannot be reduced to value.

ramayan::1431.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान् विश्वामित्रेण धीमता । न दास्यामीति शबलां प्राह राजन् कथञ्चन । । 15322 । ।
ramayan::1431.verse_hindi: To these words of sagacious Viswamitra the adorable Vasishta replied: O King I shall not give Sabala.
ramayan::1431.english_translation: To these words of sagacious Viswamitra, the venerable Vasishta replied: O King, I shall not give Sabala.
ramayan::1431.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus spoken to) / तु (then) / भगवान् (the venerable one) / विश्वामित्रेण (by Viswamitra) / धीमता (by the wise) / न दास्यामि (I will not give) / इति (thus) / शबलाम् (Sabala) / प्राह (said) / राजन् (O king) / कथञ्चन (in any way)
ramayan::1431.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1431.essence: Some bonds cannot be bought, no matter the price.
ramayan::1431.simple_meaning: Vasishta refuses to hand over Sabala, no matter how richly Viswamitra offers to pay.
ramayan::1431.simple_insight: Some things are not for sale, even to power and wealth.
ramayan::1431.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already offered cows, jewels, gold, and anything else Vasishta might want. In this tense exchange, Vasishta answers with a flat refusal. The next line will reveal why Sabala cannot be bought.
ramayan::1431.modern_relevance: A buyer keeps raising the price, sure the seller will fold. But some things are held by loyalty, not market value.
ramayan::1431.insight: It teaches you that attachment can be deeper than wealth and that not everything can be exchanged.

ramayan::1432.verse_sanskrit: एतदेव हि मे रत्नमेतदेव हि मे धनम् । एतदेव हि सर्वस्वमेतदेव हि जीवितम् । । 15323 । ।
ramayan::1432.verse_hindi: This is verily my jewel, my wealth my very life. This is allinall for me.
ramayan::1432.english_translation: This is verily my jewel, my wealth, my very life. This is all in all for me.
ramayan::1432.translation_literal: एतत् (this) एव (indeed) हि (verily) मे (my) रत्नम् (jewel) / एतत् (this) एव (indeed) हि (verily) मे (my) धनम् (wealth) / एतत् (this) एव (indeed) हि (verily) सर्वस्वम् (all possessions) / एतत् (this) एव (this) हि (indeed) जीवितम् (life)
ramayan::1432.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1432.essence: What you cherish can outweigh every offer.
ramayan::1432.simple_meaning: Vasishta says Sabala is not just a cow to him. She is his treasure, his support, and the center of his life.
ramayan::1432.simple_insight: Love can make one possession feel larger than wealth itself.
ramayan::1432.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has offered gold and jewels to take Sabala away, but Vasishta refuses. He is not bargaining now; he is declaring what this cow means to his life, his rites, and his whole sense of worth.
ramayan::1432.modern_relevance: You keep one worn object from a parent, and it is worth more than anything expensive. Not because of price — because it carries your whole history.
ramayan::1432.insight: It shows how attachment can turn a single object into a stand-in for identity and purpose.

ramayan::1433.verse_sanskrit: दर्शश्च पूर्णमासश्च यज्ञाश्चैवाप्तदक्षिणा: । एतदेव हि मे राजन् विविधाश्च क्रियास्तथा । । 15324 । ।
ramayan::1433.verse_hindi: O King verily this Sabala is useful for my darsa and purnamasa sacrifices, for appropriate gifts and various rites.
ramayan::1433.english_translation: O King, this Sabala is useful for my darsa and purnamasa sacrifices, for appropriate gifts and various rites.
ramayan::1433.translation_literal: दर्शः (new-moon sacrifice) / च (and) / पूर्णमासः (full-moon sacrifice) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / आप्तदक्षिणाः (with proper offerings) / एतत् (this) / एव (indeed) / हि (for) / मे (my) / राजन् (O king) / विविधाः (various) / च (and) / क्रियाः (ritual acts) / तथा (likewise)
ramayan::1433.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1433.essence: What looks like property is really the foundation of his sacred work.
ramayan::1433.simple_meaning: Vasishta says Sabala is not just precious to him; she is necessary for his sacrifices, offerings, and many ritual duties.
ramayan::1433.simple_insight: What you rely on is often what quietly holds your whole life together.
ramayan::1433.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has demanded Sabala from Vasishta, and Vasishta refuses. Now he explains why: this cow is not a luxury, but the support of his sacrificial life, his offerings, and every ritual he performs. The refusal is rooted in duty and dependence, not sentiment.
ramayan::1433.modern_relevance: You only notice the value of something after you realize how many parts of your life rest on it. A person, habit, or tool can quietly hold together everything you keep calling your own.
ramayan::1433.insight: It shifts attention from ownership to dependence: what seems like a possession may actually sustain your entire practice.

ramayan::1434.verse_sanskrit: अदोमूला: क्रियास्सर्वा मम राजन्न संशय: । बहुना किं प्रलापेन न दास्ये कामदोहिनीम् । । 15325 । ।
ramayan::1434.verse_hindi: O King this (cow) is undoubtedly the source of all my actions. Why these useless
ramayan::1434.english_translation: O King, this cow is undoubtedly the source of all my rites. Why speak at length? I will not give away the wish-fulfilling cow.
ramayan::1434.translation_literal: अदोमूला: (root/source of this) / क्रियास्सर्वा: (all rites) / मम (my) / राजन् (O King) / न (not) / संशय: (doubt) / बहुना (by much) / किं (what) / प्रलापेन (with talk) / न (not) / दास्ये (I will give) / कामदोहिनीम् (the wish-fulfilling cow)
ramayan::1434.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1434.essence: What sustains your life is not up for bargaining.
ramayan::1434.simple_meaning: Vasishta tells the king that the cow is essential to his rituals, so there is no need for more argument: he will not give it away.
ramayan::1434.simple_insight: Some things are not negotiable once you know their value.
ramayan::1434.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has already explained that Sabala is priceless to his sacrificial life. In this line, he cuts off further pleading and refuses to part with her, setting up the conflict that will drive Vishwamitra to seize the cow by force.
ramayan::1434.modern_relevance: You’ve already explained why this matters, and someone keeps pushing. At some point, clarity becomes a boundary: you know what you cannot hand over.
ramayan::1434.insight: It teaches you to name what is essential and stop apologising for protecting it.

ramayan::1435.verse_sanskrit: कामधेनुं वसिष्ठोऽपि यदा न त्यज्यते मुनि: । तदास्य शबलां राम विश्वामित्रोऽन्वकर्षत । । 1541 । ।
ramayan::1435.verse_hindi: O Rama when sage Vasishta did not consent to part with the wishfulfilling cow, Viswamitra dragged Sabala by force.
ramayan::1435.english_translation: O Rama, when sage Vasishta would not part with the wish-fulfilling cow, Viswamitra dragged Sabala away by force.
ramayan::1435.translation_literal: कामधेनुम् (the wish-fulfilling cow) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / अपि (even) / यदा (when) / न (not) / त्यज्यते (was willing to give up) / मुनिः (the sage) / तदा (then) / अस्य (his) / शबलाम् (Sabala) / राम (O Rama) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / अन्वकर्षत (dragged away)
ramayan::1435.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1435.essence: Refusal met by force turns desire into conflict.
ramayan::1435.simple_meaning: Vasishta refused to give up the wish-fulfilling cow, so Viswamitra seized her by force.
ramayan::1435.simple_insight: Possession without consent turns desire into violence.
ramayan::1435.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already demanded Sabala from Vasishta. When the sage refuses, the dispute stops being about a cow and becomes a test of power. Viswamitra then drags Sabala away, setting the conflict in motion.
ramayan::1435.modern_relevance: A meeting has gone cold because someone will not let go of what they want. The moment persuasion fails, pressure begins. This verse shows how quickly desire can become force.
ramayan::1435.insight: It shifts the focus from wanting something to seeing how wanting can override restraint.

ramayan::1436.verse_sanskrit: नीयमाना तु शबला राम राज्ञा महात्मना । दु:खिता चिन्तयामास रुदन्ती शोककर्शिता । । 1542 । ।
ramayan::1436.verse_hindi: O Rama when she was being taken away by the powerful king the distressed Sabala thus reflected choked with sorrow:
ramayan::1436.english_translation: O Rama, when the powerful king was taking Sabala away, the grieving cow, choked with sorrow and tears, reflected in pain.
ramayan::1436.translation_literal: नीयमाना (being taken away) / तु (indeed) / शबला (Sabala) / राम (O Rama) / राज्ञा (by the king) / महात्मना (by the great-souled) / दुःखिता (distressed) / चिन्तयामास (she reflected) / रुदन्ती (weeping) / शोककर्शिता (worn down by grief)
ramayan::1436.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1436.essence: Being taken away, she feels the loss before she can stop it.
ramayan::1436.simple_meaning: Sabala is being dragged away from Vasishta, and she grieves as she realizes what is happening to her.
ramayan::1436.simple_insight: Even a powerless being feels the pain of being torn from what is familiar.
ramayan::1436.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has seized Sabala from Vasishta, and the cow is now being led away against her will. In this moment of helpless sorrow, she begins to think through her loss, setting up the plea she voices next.
ramayan::1436.modern_relevance: You know that feeling when something safe is being taken from you and you can only watch. The hurt begins before the loss is complete.
ramayan::1436.insight: It shifts attention from force itself to the inner grief force creates.

ramayan::1437.verse_sanskrit: परित्यक्ता वसिष्ठेन किमहं सुमहात्मना । याहं राजभटैर्दीना ह्रियेय भृशदु:खिता । । 1543 । ।
ramayan::1437.verse_hindi: I am being carried away by attendants of the king in this greatly distressed and pitiable condition. Have I been abandoned by the magnanimous Vasishta?
ramayan::1437.english_translation: I am being carried away by the king's attendants in this greatly distressed and pitiable condition. Have I been abandoned by the magnanimous Vasishta?
ramayan::1437.translation_literal: परित्यक्ता (abandoned) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / किम् (whether?) / अहम् (I) / सुमहात्मना (by the greatly noble one) / या (who) / अहम् (I) / राजभटैः (by the king's attendants) / दीना (distressed) / ह्रियेय (am being carried away) / भृश-दुःखिता (greatly sorrowful)
ramayan::1437.speaker: Sabala
ramayan::1437.essence: Loss can feel like abandonment before it feels like change.
ramayan::1437.simple_meaning: Sabala, being dragged away by force, feels abandoned by Vasishta and mourns her helpless condition.
ramayan::1437.simple_insight: Being taken from what you trust can feel like betrayal, even when you cannot explain why.
ramayan::1437.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has seized Vasishta's cow Sabala by force. As king's attendants drag her away, she cries out in grief, wondering whether the great sage has truly abandoned her. The verse deepens the emotional rupture before her plea in the next line.
ramayan::1437.modern_relevance: You get pulled out of a place that once felt safe, and your first thought is not logic but betrayal.
ramayan::1437.insight: It captures the shock of losing protection before you can even understand the reason.

ramayan::1438.verse_sanskrit: किं मयाऽपकृतं तस्य महर्षेर्भावितात्मन: । यन्मामनागसं भक्तामिष्टां त्यजति धार्मिक: । । 1544 । ।
ramayan::1438.verse_hindi: What harm have I done to the pious maharshi, a compassionate soul? Why does he  forsake me, his auspicious one, despite my innocence and devotion?
ramayan::1438.english_translation: What harm have I done to the pious maharshi, a compassionate soul? Why does he forsake me, his innocent and devoted one?
ramayan::1438.translation_literal: किम् (what) / मया (by me) / अपकृतम् (wrong done) / तस्य (to him) / महर्षेः (of the great sage) / भावितात्मनः (of the purified-minded one) / यत् (that) / माम् (me) / अनागसम् (innocent) / भक्ताम् (devoted) / इष्टाम् (dear) / त्यजति (forsakes) / धार्मिकः (the righteous one)
ramayan::1438.speaker: Shabala
ramayan::1438.simple_meaning: Shabala, the cow, feels innocent and abandoned. She cannot understand why the sage who cared for her is now letting her go.
ramayan::1438.simple_insight: Even faithful care can feel like betrayal when separation arrives without explanation.
ramayan::1438.detailed_meaning: Vasishtha’s cow Shabala is being taken away by royal attendants. Choked with grief, she asks what fault she has committed that the righteous sage would abandon her despite her innocence and devotion. The verse deepens her sorrow before she breaks free and runs back to him.
ramayan::1438.modern_relevance: A pet carrier is waiting by the door, and your dog keeps looking back at you. You know the move is necessary, but the look says everything: trust can hurt before it understands.
ramayan::1438.insight: It captures the pain of being removed from what felt like home, even when no blame exists.

ramayan::1439.verse_sanskrit: इति सा चिन्तयित्वा तु विनिश्श्वस्य पुन:पुन: । निर्धूय तांस्तदा भृत्यान् शतशश्शत्रुसूदन । जगामानिलवेगेन पादमूलं महात्मन: । । 1545 । ।
ramayan::1439.verse_hindi: O Destroyer of enemies thus thinking and repeatedly sighing, that cow shook off those attendants who were in hundreds and ran towards the feet of the illustrious Vasishta with the speed of the wind.
ramayan::1439.english_translation: Thinking this over and sighing again and again, Sabala shook off the attendants in hundreds and ran with wind-like speed to the feet of the great Vasishta.
ramayan::1439.translation_literal: इति (thus) / सा (she) / चिन्तयित्वा (having thought) / तु (indeed) / विनिश्श्वस्य (having sighed deeply) / पुन:पुन: (again and again) / निर्धूय (shaking off) / तान् (those) / तदा (then) / भृत्यान् (attendants) / शतशश् (in hundreds) / शत्रुसूदन (O destroyer of enemies) / जगाम (went) / अनिलवेगेन (with wind-speed) / पादमूलं (to the feet) / महात्मन: (of the great one)
ramayan::1439.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1439.essence: Loyalty can break through force and run home.
ramayan::1439.simple_meaning: Sabala, after thinking and sighing, broke free from the attendants and rushed to Vasishta as fast as the wind.
ramayan::1439.simple_insight: Even under force, loyalty can pull you toward the one you trust.
ramayan::1439.detailed_meaning: Sabala, the cow tied to Vasishta, has just sensed separation and distress. Surrounded by attendants trying to take her away, she struggles free and runs back toward her master. The verse shows instinctive loyalty before she speaks.
ramayan::1439.modern_relevance: A child clings to the teacher who made them feel safe, even while adults try to pull them away. Some bonds are stronger than pressure.
ramayan::1439.insight: It shows loyalty as an immediate movement of the heart, not a reasoned decision.

ramayan::1440.verse_sanskrit: शबला सा रुदन्ती च क्रोशन्ती चेदमब्रवीत् । वसिष्ठस्याग्रतस्स्थित्वा मेघदुन्दुभिराविणी । । 1546 । ।
ramayan::1440.verse_hindi: Lowing and moaning, standing before Vasishta, roaring like thunder and of kettledrum, Sabala said:
ramayan::1440.english_translation: Lowing and moaning, Sabala stood before Vasishta and spoke in a voice like thunder and drums.
ramayan::1440.translation_literal: शबला (Sabala) / सा (she) / रुदन्ती (weeping) / च (and) / क्रोशन्ती (crying out) / च (and) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / अग्रतः (in front of) / स्थित्वा (standing) / मेघदुन्दुभिराविणी (resounding like thunder and kettledrum)
ramayan::1440.speaker: Sabala
ramayan::1440.essence: A loyal bond is breaking, and the protest is just beginning.
ramayan::1440.simple_meaning: Sabala, crying loudly, stood before Vasishta and began to speak in a thunderous voice.
ramayan::1440.simple_insight: Even a loyal presence can protest when being taken away from what it trusts.
ramayan::1440.detailed_meaning: Sabala, the cherished cow of Vasishta, has just realized she is being taken from his hermitage. Standing before him, she cries out in distress. This verse is the dramatic setup for her plea in the next line, not the full teaching itself.
ramayan::1440.modern_relevance: You can feel the shock when something loyal and familiar is suddenly being removed from your life.
ramayan::1440.insight: It sets up a plea of separation, not a complete teaching on its own.

ramayan::1441.verse_sanskrit: भगवन् किं परित्यक्ता त्वयाऽहं ब्रह्मणस्सुत । यस्माद्राजभृता मां हि नयन्ते त्वत्सकाशत: । । 1547 । ।
ramayan::1441.verse_hindi: O Brahmas son O Venerable one you have abandoned me? For what reason the servants of the king are taking me away from you?
ramayan::1441.english_translation: O son of Brahma, have you abandoned me? Why are the king's servants taking me away from you?
ramayan::1441.translation_literal: भगवन् (O venerable one) / किं (why) / परित्यक्ता (abandoned) / त्वया (by you) / अहम् (I) / ब्रह्मणः (of Brahma) / सुत (son) / यस्मात् (because) / राजभृताः (king's servants) / माम् (me) / हि (indeed) / नयन्ते (are taking away) / त्वत्सकाशतः (from your presence)
ramayan::1441.speaker: Sabala
ramayan::1441.essence: Being pulled away from safety feels like abandonment.
ramayan::1441.simple_meaning: Sabala, the cow of Vasishta, cries out in pain as royal servants pull her away. She feels abandoned and asks why she is being taken from the sage who protected her.
ramayan::1441.simple_insight: Even a loyal being feels the wound of separation when protection is taken away.
ramayan::1441.detailed_meaning: Sabala stands before Vasishta, weeping as the king's men seize her. She speaks like a child being torn from home, asking why the sage has let this happen. The moment shows the pain of forced separation before the larger conflict unfolds.
ramayan::1441.modern_relevance: You watch someone you depend on step back while others move in to take what felt safe. The shock is not just loss — it is the feeling of being unprotected all at once.
ramayan::1441.insight: It turns attention to the emotional violence of separation and helplessness.

ramayan::1442.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु ब्रह्मर्षिरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । शोकसन्तप्तहृदयां स्वसारमिव दु:खिताम् । । 1548 । ।
ramayan::1442.verse_hindi: Addressed thus, Bramharshi said to Sabala, like to  a sister whose heart is afflicted with sorrow:
ramayan::1442.english_translation: Addressed thus, the Brahmarshi spoke to Sabala, as to a sorrow-stricken sister whose heart was afflicted with grief.
ramayan::1442.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus addressed) / तु (indeed) / ब्रह्मर्षिः (the Brahmarshi) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / शोकसन्तप्तहृदयाम् (with a grief-burned heart) / स्वसारम् इव (like a sister) / दुःखिताम् (sorrowful)
ramayan::1442.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1442.essence: Sorrow should be answered like family, not like a problem.
ramayan::1442.simple_meaning: Vasishta responds to Sabala with tenderness, speaking to her as if she were his sorrowful sister.
ramayan::1442.simple_insight: Grief is met first with compassion, not argument.
ramayan::1442.detailed_meaning: Sabala, the sacred cow, is being taken away by the king's men. She cries out to Vasishta, accusing him of abandoning her. In this verse, Vasishta answers her with grief-aware tenderness before explaining the king's force in the next line.
ramayan::1442.modern_relevance: A friend is crying in front of you, and your first job is not to fix the situation. It is to meet their pain with human warmth before anything else.
ramayan::1442.insight: It teaches you to respond to distress with recognition, not cold explanation.

ramayan::1443.verse_sanskrit: न त्वां त्यजामि शबले नापि मेऽपकृतं त्वया । एष त्वां नयते राजा बलोन्मत्तो महाबल: । । 1549 । ।
ramayan::1443.verse_hindi: O Sabala I am not forsaking you. You have done me no harm. This highly powerful king is forcibly carrying you away from me.
ramayan::1443.english_translation: O Sabala, I am not forsaking you. You have done me no harm. This highly powerful king is forcibly carrying you away from me.
ramayan::1443.translation_literal: न (not) / त्वाम् (you) / त्यजामि (I forsake) / शबले (O Sabala) / न (not) / अपि (also) / मे (to me) / अपकृतम् (wrong done) / त्वया (by you) / एष (this) / त्वाम् (you) / नयते (is taking away) / राजा (the king) / बलोन्मत्तः (maddened by strength) / महाबलः (highly powerful)
ramayan::1443.speaker: Brahmarshi
ramayan::1443.essence: Force can separate what loyalty never meant to break.
ramayan::1443.simple_meaning: The sage tells Sabala that he is not abandoning her. She has harmed him in no way; a powerful king is simply taking her away by force.
ramayan::1443.simple_insight: Not every separation is a betrayal. Sometimes force, not choice, is what tears people apart.
ramayan::1443.detailed_meaning: Sabala, grief-stricken, thinks she has been abandoned. The Brahmarshi answers with calm sorrow: he has not rejected her, and she has wronged him in nothing. He is powerless before a king driven by strength and arrogance.
ramayan::1443.modern_relevance: A friend is being pulled into a decision they never wanted, and you can only watch. The pain is real, but not every loss comes from disloyalty.
ramayan::1443.insight: It separates moral failure from helplessness, so grief does not turn into blame.

ramayan::1444.verse_sanskrit: न हि तुल्यं बलं मह्यं राजा त्वद्य विशेषत: । बली राजा क्षत्रियश्च पृथिव्या: पतिरेव च । । 15410 । ।
ramayan::1444.verse_hindi: I am no match for his strength, especially he is a king. Being king, he is a warrior, powerful and lord of the earth.
ramayan::1444.english_translation: I am no match for his strength, especially he is a king. Being king, he is a warrior, powerful and lord of the earth.
ramayan::1444.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / तुल्यं (equal) / बलं (strength) / मह्यं (to me) / राजा (king) / त्वद्य (than you) / विशेषत: (especially) / बली (powerful) / राजा (king) / क्षत्रियश्च (and a warrior) / पृथिव्या: (of the earth) / पतिरेव (indeed lord) / च (and)
ramayan::1444.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1444.essence: Power decides the immediate outcome, not moral rightness alone.
ramayan::1444.simple_meaning: No one should expect equal resistance from me here. This king has greater strength, greater authority, and the backing of royal power.
ramayan::1444.simple_insight: Some fights are unequal from the start, and wisdom begins by seeing that clearly.
ramayan::1444.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is speaking in the middle of a tense encounter around Sabala. He explains that he cannot oppose the king directly because the king is stronger, armed with royal authority, and backed by the force of rulership. The verse supports the larger argument that force is being used against the weak.
ramayan::1444.modern_relevance: You are being pressured by someone with status, money, and a crowd behind them. Before you blame yourself for not pushing back harder, you first need to see the imbalance clearly.
ramayan::1444.insight: It shifts the mind from heroic fantasy to clear-eyed assessment of power.

ramayan::1445.verse_sanskrit: इयमक्षौहिणी पूर्णा सवाजिरथसङ्कुला । हस्तिध्वजसमाकीर्णा तेनासौ बलवत्तर: । । 15411 । ।
ramayan::1445.verse_hindi: He has an entire akshauhini composed of horses, chariots, elephants and banners. Hence he is stonger.
ramayan::1445.english_translation: He has an entire akshauhini of horses, chariots, elephants, and banners. Therefore, he is stronger.
ramayan::1445.translation_literal: इयम् (this) / अक्षौहिणी (akshauhini, a full battle formation) / पूर्णा (filled) / सवाजिरथसङ्कुला (crowded with horses and chariots) / हस्तिध्वजसमाकीर्णा (covered with elephants and banners) / तेन (therefore) / असौ (that one) / बलवत्तरः (stronger)
ramayan::1445.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1445.essence: Numbers matter when force is about to decide everything.
ramayan::1445.simple_meaning: The side he commands is larger and better equipped, so he has the advantage in strength.
ramayan::1445.simple_insight: Raw numbers can tilt power before a single blow is struck.
ramayan::1445.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is answering a challenge with plain battlefield logic: one side has a full army formation packed with horses, chariots, elephants, and banners. The point is not philosophy, only scale — this is why the other king is stronger.
ramayan::1445.modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting already outnumbered, outspent, and outgunned. Before anyone speaks, the imbalance is visible.
ramayan::1445.insight: It trains you to read power realistically, without romanticising your chances.

ramayan::1446.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ता वसिष्ठेन प्रत्युवाच विनीतवत् । वचनं वचनज्ञा सा ब्रह्मर्षिममितप्रभम् । । 15412 । ।
ramayan::1446.verse_hindi: To these words of  brahmarshi Vasishta armed with immeasurable power, Sabala, who knew the use of words, replied with humility:
ramayan::1446.english_translation: To these words of the brahmarshi Vasishta, armed with immeasurable power, Sabala, who knew the use of words, replied with humility.
ramayan::1446.translation_literal: एवमुक्ता (thus spoken to) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / विनीतवत् (with humility) / वचनं (speech) / वचनज्ञा (knowing words) / सा (she) / ब्रह्मर्षिम् (to the brahmarshi) / अमितप्रभम् (of immeasurable power)
ramayan::1446.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1446.essence: Humility can answer power without losing its own force.
ramayan::1446.simple_meaning: Sabala answers Vasishta respectfully and with careful, humble speech.
ramayan::1446.simple_insight: Even in a tense exchange, dignity can stay soft and restrained.
ramayan::1446.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just argued that a king's strength is not the highest strength. Sabala, the cow of divine origin, responds not with anger but with measured humility. The verse sets up the deeper teaching that follows.
ramayan::1446.modern_relevance: Someone interrupts you in a meeting and you feel your pride rise. You can still answer carefully, without letting defensiveness take over.
ramayan::1446.insight: It shows that real strength can speak without aggression or ego.

ramayan::1447.verse_sanskrit: न बलं क्षत्रियस्याहुर्ब्राह्मणो बलवत्तर: । ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मबलं दिव्यं क्षत्रात्तु बलवत्तरम् । । 15413 । ।
ramayan::1447.verse_hindi: O Best of brahmins it is held that the strength of a kshatriya is no greater than a brahmins. A brahmin possesses great strength his strength is divine. It is greater than that of a kshatriya.
ramayan::1447.english_translation: O best of brahmins, it is said that the strength of a kshatriya is not greater than a brahmin's. A brahmin's strength is divine and greater than a kshatriya's.
ramayan::1447.translation_literal: न (not) / बलं (strength) / क्षत्रियस्य (of a kshatriya) / आहुḥ (they say) / ब्राह्मणः (a brahmin) / बलवत्तरः (stronger) / ब्रह्मन् (O brahmin) / ब्रह्मबलं (brahmin-strength) / दिव्यम् (divine) / क्षत्रात् (than a kshatriya) / तु (indeed) / बलवत्तरम् (stronger)
ramayan::1447.speaker: Sabala
ramayan::1447.essence: Inner power can exceed brute force.
ramayan::1447.simple_meaning: Physical force is not the only kind of strength. Spiritual or inner power can be greater than martial power.
ramayan::1447.simple_insight: You may be stronger than what looks strongest. Real power is not always visible.
ramayan::1447.detailed_meaning: Sabala is answering Vasishta after the sage points to an army as proof of strength. She draws a sharper line: a kshatriya's power is not the highest power. Brahmin power, rooted in spiritual force, is greater.
ramayan::1447.modern_relevance: A room full of loud confidence can still be outmatched by the person who stays calm, clear, and unshaken. The strongest presence is not always the most aggressive one.
ramayan::1447.insight: It shifts respect from physical dominance to disciplined inner force.

ramayan::1448.verse_sanskrit: अप्रमेयबलं तुभ्यं न त्वया बलवत्तर: । विश्वामित्रो महावीर्यस्तेज स्तव दुरासदम् । । 15414 । ।
ramayan::1448.verse_hindi: Your power is immeasurable. Even though highly valiant, Viswamitra is not greater than you in strength. Your power is unequalled.
ramayan::1448.english_translation: Your power is immeasurable. Even though highly valiant, Viswamitra is not greater than you in strength. Your power is unequalled.
ramayan::1448.translation_literal: अप्रमेयबलम् (of immeasurable strength) / तुभ्यम् (to you) / न (not) / त्वया (by you) / बलवत्तरः (stronger) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महावीर्यः (highly valiant) / तेजः (splendour/power) / तव (your) / दुरासदम् (hard to approach, unequalled)
ramayan::1448.speaker: Sabala
ramayan::1448.essence: True power needs no comparison; it stands beyond challenge.
ramayan::1448.simple_meaning: Sabala praises Vasishta's limitless power and says that even mighty Viswamitra is not stronger than him.
ramayan::1448.simple_insight: Real strength does not need to announce itself; it is simply there, beyond comparison.
ramayan::1448.detailed_meaning: After Vasishta speaks, Sabala answers with reverence and confidence. She acknowledges that Viswamitra is powerful, but insists that Vasishta's strength is greater and beyond measure. The verse continues the exchange that leads into her offer to help.
ramayan::1448.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone tries to intimidate the one person who never needed to posture. The strongest presence often belongs to the person who does not compete.
ramayan::1448.insight: It shifts attention from visible force to the deeper authority that cannot be measured by rivalry.

ramayan::1449.verse_sanskrit: नियुङ्क्ष्व मां महाभाग त्वद्ब्रह्मबलसम्भृताम् । तस्य दर्पबलं यत्तन्नाशयामि दुरात्मन: । । 15415 । ।
ramayan::1449.verse_hindi: O Highly fortunate one I am possessed of your brahminic power. Command me. I will destroy the insolent and power of that wickedminded one.
ramayan::1449.english_translation: O highly fortunate one, command me. I am empowered by your spiritual strength. I will destroy the arrogance and force of that wicked-minded one.
ramayan::1449.translation_literal: नियुङ्क्ष्व (command) / माम् (me) / महाभाग (highly fortunate one) / त्वद्ब्रह्मबलसम्भृताम् (endowed with your brahminic power) / तस्य (of that one) / दर्पबलम् (arrogant force) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / नाशयामि (I will destroy) / दुरात्मनः (of the wicked-minded one)
ramayan::1449.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1449.essence: Power becomes clean when it waits for command.
ramayan::1449.simple_meaning: The speaker asks to be given the task and says she will destroy the proud power of the wicked one.
ramayan::1449.simple_insight: True strength is ready to serve a righteous command, not to boast.
ramayan::1449.detailed_meaning: The exchange is still building. After Vasishta is praised for his immense power, the speaker steps forward and asks for an order, offering to destroy the enemy's arrogance. The verse is a supporting pledge, not the main teaching.
ramayan::1449.modern_relevance: Someone in the room says, “Give me the task.” They are not asking for praise, only direction, because they want their strength to serve something clean.
ramayan::1449.insight: It shifts strength from self-display to obedient service.

ramayan::1450.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्तस्तु तया राम वसिष्ठ स्सुमहायशा: । सृजस्वेति तदोवाच बलं परबलार्दनम् । । 15416 । ।
ramayan::1450.verse_hindi: O Rama to this, glorious Vasishta replied: Create an army capable of crushing the enemy power.
ramayan::1450.english_translation: Then glorious Vasishta said to Rama: "Create an army that can crush the enemy force."
ramayan::1450.translation_literal: इत्युक्तस्तु (having been spoken to thus) / तया (by her) / राम (Rama) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / स्सुमहायशाः (the greatly renowned) / सृजस्व (create) / इति (thus) / तदा (then) / उवाच (said) / बलम् (an army/force) / परबलार्दनम् (crushing the enemy force)
ramayan::1450.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1450.essence: The answer to danger is to summon strength, not panic.
ramayan::1450.simple_meaning: Vasishta tells Rama to create a force strong enough to destroy the enemy army.
ramayan::1450.simple_insight: Sometimes the next step is not hesitation, but the right force applied at the right time.
ramayan::1450.detailed_meaning: Vasishta responds to the plea for protection by instructing Rama to create a force that can overwhelm the enemy. The verse is a bridge in the scene: the request has been made, and the practical answer is about to take shape.
ramayan::1450.modern_relevance: A crisis lands on your desk and everyone looks at you for the next move. Before the fix appears, someone has to call for the kind of help that can actually change the outcome.
ramayan::1450.insight: It shifts the mind from fear to decisive preparation.

ramayan::1451.verse_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुरभिस्साऽसृजत्तदा । । 15417 । । तस्या हुम्भारवोत्सृष्टा: पप्लवाश्शतशो नृप । नाशयन्ति बलं सर्वं विश्वामित्रस्य पश्यत: । । 15418 । ।
ramayan::1451.verse_hindi: Hearing his words Kamadhenu created an army. O Rama her lowing brought into being Paplavas in hundreds who destroyed the entire army of Viswamitra, while he looked on helplessly.
ramayan::1451.english_translation: Hearing his words, Kamadhenu created an army. O Rama, her lowing brought forth hundreds of Paplavas, who destroyed the entire army of Vishvamitra while he looked on helplessly.
ramayan::1451.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / तत्-वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सुरभिः (Surabhi) / सा (she) / असृजत् (created) / तदा (then) / तस्याः (her) / हुम्भा-रव-उत्सृष्टाः (released from the lowing sound) / पप्लवाः (Paplavas) / शतशः (in hundreds) / नृप (O king) / नाशयन्ति (destroy) / बलम् (army) / सर्वम् (entire) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Vishvamitra) / पश्यत: (while watching)
ramayan::1451.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1451.essence: A threatened army is destroyed before its leader can respond.
ramayan::1451.simple_meaning: Kamadhenu responded to Vasishta by producing a force that destroyed Vishvamitra's army before his eyes.
ramayan::1451.simple_insight: Power can collapse in an instant when it meets a force it cannot understand.
ramayan::1451.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just refused Vishvamitra's demand and called on Kamadhenu's power. In the next moment, the sacred cow manifests a host that wipes out the king's army while Vishvamitra watches helplessly. The verse is a battle event, not a teaching.
ramayan::1451.insight: It advances the battle by showing Vishvamitra's military power being overwhelmed.

ramayan::1452.verse_sanskrit: बलं भग्नं ततो दृष्ट्वा रथेनाक्रम्य कौशिक: । स राजा परमक्रुद्धो रोषविस्फारितेक्षण: । पप्लवान्नाशयामास शस्त्रैरुच्चावचैरपि । । 15419 । ।
ramayan::1452.verse_hindi: Thereafter the king (Viswamitra), having seen his army thus routed, flew into a fury.
ramayan::1452.english_translation: Seeing his army shattered, King Viswamitra mounted his chariot and, eyes blazing with anger, attacked the Paplavas with every kind of weapon.
ramayan::1452.translation_literal: बलं (army) / भग्नं (broken) / ततः (then) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / रथेन (by chariot) / आक्रम्य (having attacked) / कौशिकः (Kausika, Viswamitra) / सः (that) / राजा (king) / परमक्रुद्धः (deeply enraged) / रोषविस्फारितेक्षणः (with eyes widened by fury) / पप्लवान् (the Paplavas) / नाशयामास (destroyed) / शस्त्रैः (with weapons) / उच्चावचैः (of various kinds) / अपि (also)
ramayan::1452.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1452.essence: Wounded pride turns defeat into retaliation.
ramayan::1452.simple_meaning: Viswamitra sees his army broken and responds with fierce, weapon-filled retaliation.
ramayan::1452.simple_insight: Anger can turn a setback into a harsher escalation.
ramayan::1452.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already seen Kamadhenu's created forces destroy his troops. In this next beat, he loses control, leaps into the fight from his chariot, and lashes back at the Paplavas in fury. The verse shows escalation, not wisdom.
ramayan::1452.modern_relevance: You get cut off in traffic, then answer with a harsher move, and suddenly the whole morning is poisoned. A small hit becomes a bigger one when anger takes the wheel.
ramayan::1452.insight: It shows how quickly wounded pride can convert defeat into retaliation.

ramayan::1453.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रार्दितान् दृष्ट्वा पप्लवाञ्छतशस्तदा । भूय एवासृजत्कोपाच्छकान् यवनमिश्रितान् । । 15420 । ।
ramayan::1453.verse_hindi: Having seen hundreds of Paplavas crushed by Viswamitra, once again she created out of anger. Sakas mixed with Yavanas.
ramayan::1453.english_translation: Having seen hundreds of Paplavas crushed by Viswamitra, once again she created out of anger. Sakas mixed with Yavanas.
ramayan::1453.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रार्दितान् (crushed by Viswamitra) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / पप्लवाञ्छतश्तदा (hundreds of Paplavas then) / भूयः (again) / एवासृजत् (created) / कोपात् (from anger) / शकान् (Sakas) / यवनमिश्रितान् (mixed with Yavanas)
ramayan::1453.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1453.essence: Anger does not end defeat; it breeds a larger one.
ramayan::1453.simple_meaning: Seeing her first force destroyed, she responded by creating another, stronger force out of anger.
ramayan::1453.simple_insight: Escalation born from anger only multiplies the conflict.
ramayan::1453.detailed_meaning: In Vishwamitra’s clash with Kamadhenu, one wave of strange warriors has already been destroyed. Instead of stopping, the cow creates another mixed host in fury. The verse is a rapid battlefield escalation, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::1453.modern_relevance: A harsh reply in a group chat turns into a longer argument, and then a second thread, and then screenshots. Anger keeps inventing new battlefields.
ramayan::1453.insight: It shows how reactive anger keeps generating fresh opposition instead of ending the conflict.

ramayan::1454.verse_hindi: Sakas mixed with Yavanas, resembling golden filaments possessing brilliance and supreme bravery, covered the earth.
ramayan::1454.english_translation: Sakas mixed with Yavanas, resembling golden filaments possessing brilliance and supreme bravery, covered the earth.
ramayan::1454.translation_literal: तैः (by them) / आसीत् (was) / संवृता (covered) / भूमि (the earth) / श्शकैः (by Sakas) / यवनमिश्रितैः (mixed with Yavanas) / प्रभावद्भिः (brilliant) / महावीर्यैः (of great valor) / हेमकिञ्जल्कसन्निभैः (resembling golden filaments)
ramayan::1454.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1454.essence: The battlefield is swallowed by a glittering host.
ramayan::1454.simple_meaning: The earth was covered by a force of Sakas and Yavanas, shining and fierce in battle.
ramayan::1454.simple_insight: The scene is about overwhelming force, not a lesson to carry forward.
ramayan::1454.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra’s attack has already unleashed wave after wave of strange warrior-hosts. Here the poet pauses to describe their appearance: Sakas mixed with Yavanas, bright, fierce, and countless, spreading across the ground before the next blow falls.
ramayan::1454.insight: It keeps the focus on battlefield scale and momentum rather than inner teaching.

ramayan::1455.verse_sanskrit: दीर्घासिपट्टिशधरैःमवर्णाम्बरावृतै: । निर्दग्धं तद्बलं सर्वं प्रदीप्तैरिव पावकै: । । 15422 । ।
ramayan::1455.verse_hindi: Sakas and Yavanas, armed with swords and lances, clad in yellow apparel, looking  like flaming fire destroyed the entire army.
ramayan::1455.english_translation: The Sakas and Yavanas, armed with swords and lances and clad in yellow garments, burned up the entire army like blazing fire.
ramayan::1455.translation_literal: दीर्घासिपट्टिशधरैः (bearing long swords and lances) / मवर्णाम्बरावृतैः (covered in yellow garments) / निर्दग्धं (burned up) / तत् (that) / बलं (army) / सर्वं (entire) / प्रदीप्तैः (blazing) / इव (like) / पावकैः (fires)
ramayan::1455.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1455.essence: A force like fire can consume resistance completely.
ramayan::1455.simple_meaning: The enemy force was overwhelmed by fierce Sakas and Yavanas, who fought like fire and wiped it out.
ramayan::1455.simple_insight: Some moments in a battle leave no room for recovery — only total collapse.
ramayan::1455.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been confronting waves of hostile tribes in a violent clash. After the previous verse names their appearance and strength, this line shows the result: the army is consumed by their attack. It is battlefield description, not teaching.
ramayan::1455.insight: It records the force of the attack, not a principle to apply.

ramayan::1456.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽस्त्राणि महातेजा विश्वामित्रो मुमोच ह । तैस्तैर्यवनकाम्भोजा: पप्लवाश्चाकुलीकृता: । । 15423 । ।
ramayan::1456.verse_hindi: Thereafter, most brilliant Viswamitra released weapons. With these weapons, the Yavanas, Kambhojas and Paplavas were scattered.
ramayan::1456.english_translation: Thereafter, most brilliant Viswamitra released weapons. With these weapons, the Yavanas, Kambhojas and Paplavas were scattered.
ramayan::1456.translation_literal: ततः (thereafter) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / महातेजाः (most brilliant) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / मुमोच (released) / ह (indeed) / तैः (by those) / तैः (those) / यवनकाम्भोजाः (Yavanas and Kambhojas) / पप्लवाः (Paplavas) / च (and) / आकुलीकृताः (scattered, thrown into confusion)
ramayan::1456.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1456.essence: One decisive strike can break a whole formation.
ramayan::1456.simple_meaning: Viswamitra unleashed powerful weapons, and the enemy forces of Yavanas, Kambhojas, and Paplavas were thrown into confusion and scattered.
ramayan::1456.simple_insight: Power without control can break an army in moments.
ramayan::1456.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Viswamitra answers resistance by releasing his weapons. The enemy groups are not just defeated; they are thrown into disorder and scattered. The verse is a combat detail inside a larger sequence of warfare.
ramayan::1456.modern_relevance: A crisis meeting turns sharp and tense, and one decisive move changes the room completely. Some moments are not about debate — they are about the force that ends confusion.
ramayan::1456.insight: It shows how overwhelming force can instantly dismantle organized resistance.

ramayan::1457.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तानाकुलान् दृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रास्त्रमोहितान् । वसिष्ठश्चोदयामास कामधुक् सृज योगत: । । 1551 । ।
ramayan::1457.verse_hindi: Thereafter, Vasishta having seen the forces tortured and overpowered by the weapons of Viswamitra said, O Kamadhenu create additional forces through your yogic power.
ramayan::1457.english_translation: Thereafter, Vasishta, seeing the forces troubled and bewildered by Viswamitra's weapons, urged Kamadhenu to create more forces through her yogic power.
ramayan::1457.translation_literal: ततः (then) / तान् (those) / आकुलान् (distressed, confused) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / विश्वामित्र-अस्त्र-मोहितान् (bewildered by Viswamitra's weapons) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / चोदयामास (urged, prompted) / कामधुक् (Kamadhenu) / सृज (create) / योगतः (through yogic power)
ramayan::1457.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1457.essence: A battle turns when one side calls on a deeper force.
ramayan::1457.simple_meaning: Vasishta sees his side overwhelmed by Viswamitra's weapons and asks Kamadhenu to produce more forces through her power.
ramayan::1457.simple_insight: When ordinary strength fails, the story turns to a deeper source of power.
ramayan::1457.detailed_meaning: In the clash between Viswamitra and Vasishta, Viswamitra's weapons have thrown the opposing forces into confusion. Seeing that pressure, Vasishta turns to Kamadhenu and calls on her yogic power to create fresh troops. The verse moves the battle forward, not the teaching.
ramayan::1457.modern_relevance: A project is collapsing, the team is rattled, and someone reaches for an emergency workaround instead of a clean solution. The moment is about escalation, not reflection.
ramayan::1457.insight: It shifts attention from the visible fight to the hidden source of power being summoned behind it.

ramayan::1458.verse_sanskrit: तस्याहुम्भारवाज्जाता: काम्भोजा रविसन्निभा: । ऊधसस्त्वथ सञ्जाता: पप्लवाश्शस्त्रपाणय: । । 1552 । । योनिदेशाच्च यवनाश्शकृद्देशाच्छका स्तथा । रोमकूपेषु च म्लेच्छा हारीतास्सकिरातका: । । 1553 । ।
ramayan::1458.verse_hindi: From her lowing Kambhojas bright like the Sun, from the udder Paplavas, weapons in  hand, from the vagina Yavanas, from the anus Sakas, from the roots of the hair Mlecchas along with Kiratas and Haritas were born.
ramayan::1458.english_translation: From her lowing, Kambhojas bright like the sun were born; from the udder, Paplavas armed with weapons; from the vagina, Yavanas; from the anus, Shakas; and from the roots of the hair, Mlecchas along with Kiratas and Haritas were born.
ramayan::1458.translation_literal: तस्याः (from her) / हुंभारवात् (from the lowing sound) / जाताः (were born) / काम्भोजाः (Kambhojas) / रविसन्निभाः (sun-like) / ऊधसः (from the udder) / अथ (then) / सञ्जाताः (were born) / पप्लवाः (Paplavas) / शस्त्रपाणयः (weapon-in-hand) / योनिदेशात् (from the genital region) / च (and) / यवनाः (Yavanas) / शकृद्देशात् (from the anus region) / शकाः (Shakas) / तथा (also) / रोमकूपेषु (from the hair pores) / च (and) / म्लेच्छाः (Mlecchas) / हारीताः (Haritas) / स किरातकाः (along with Kiratas)
ramayan::1458.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1458.essence: A mythic counterattack appears, but the verse mainly advances the battle.
ramayan::1458.simple_meaning: Kamadhenu produces warriors and peoples from different parts of her body as Vasishta responds to Viswamitra’s attack.
ramayan::1458.simple_insight: Power can answer violence with overwhelming force, but the scene is still part of a larger conflict.
ramayan::1458.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already unleashed weapons against Vasishta. In response, Vasishta calls on Kamadhenu, and her body gives rise to many fierce peoples and armed forces. The verse is a vivid, mythic detail in the middle of that larger contest.
ramayan::1458.modern_relevance: A conflict has already escalated past reason, and the response is no longer polite. This is the moment when a situation stops being a debate and becomes a force meeting force.
ramayan::1458.insight: It shows escalation as part of a larger chain, not a standalone teaching.

ramayan::1459.verse_sanskrit: तैस्तैर्निषूदितं सर्वं विश्वामित्रस्य तत्क्षणात् । सपदातिगजं साश्वं सरथं रघुनन्दन । । 1554 । ।
ramayan::1459.verse_hindi: O descendant of the Raghus, Viswamitras army consisting of infantry, elephants, horses, chariots has been entirely destroyed by them instantly.
ramayan::1459.english_translation: O descendant of the Raghus, Viswamitra's army of infantry, elephants, horses, and chariots was destroyed instantly.
ramayan::1459.translation_literal: तैस्तैः (by those very ones) / निषूदितम् (destroyed) / सर्वम् (all) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Viswamitra) / तत्क्षणात् (instantly) / सपदातिगजम् (with infantry and elephants) / साश्वम् (with horses) / सरथम् (with chariots) / रघुनन्दन (O descendant of the Raghu line)
ramayan::1459.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1459.essence: An entire army falls in an instant.
ramayan::1459.simple_meaning: Viswamitra's whole army was wiped out at once, including foot soldiers, elephants, horses, and chariots.
