ramayan::1459.simple_insight: Power can vanish in a single moment when it meets a greater force.
ramayan::1459.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just summoned forces from Kamadhenu to answer Viswamitra's attack. In the next instant, the entire army is gone—foot soldiers, elephants, horses, and chariots. The verse is a battle detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::1459.insight: It shifts attention to the speed with which a force can be undone.

ramayan::1460.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा निषूदितं सैन्यं वसिष्ठेन महात्मना । विश्वामित्रसुतानां च शतं नानाविधायुधम् । । 1555 । । अभ्यधावत्सुसङ्कृद्धं वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम् । हुङ्कारेणैव तान् सर्वान् ददाह भगवान् ऋषि: । । 1556 । ।
ramayan::1460.verse_hindi: Having seen the army destroyed by the powerful Vasishta, one hundred sons of Viswamitra became extremely furious and armed with various kinds of weapons rushed towards Vasishta, the best among ascetics. Adorable sage Vasishta, reduced them to ashes with just a humkara (the loud hum sound produced with the mouth)
ramayan::1460.english_translation: Having seen the army destroyed by the powerful Vasishta, one hundred sons of Viswamitra became extremely furious and armed with various kinds of weapons rushed towards Vasishta, the best among ascetics. The venerable sage Vasishta reduced them all to ashes with a single humkara.
ramayan::1460.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / निषूदितं (destroyed) / सैन्यं (army) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / वसिष्ठेन महात्मना (by the great-souled Vasishta) / विश्वामित्रसुतानां (of Visvamitra's sons) / च (and) / शतं (hundred) / नानाविधायुधम् (with various weapons) / अभ्यधावत् (rushed at) / सुसङ्कृद्धं (greatly enraged) / वसिष्ठं (Vasishta) / जपतां वरम् (best among ascetics) / हुङ्कारेण (with a humkara) / एव (indeed) / तान् (them) / सर्वान् (all) / ददाह (burned) / भगवान् ऋषि: (the venerable sage)
ramayan::1460.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1460.essence: Rage charges in; serene force ends it at once.
ramayan::1460.simple_meaning: Visvamitra's sons attack Vasishta in anger after seeing their army destroyed, and Vasishta burns them all with a single sound.
ramayan::1460.simple_insight: Pride rushes forward; calm power ends the fight before it begins.
ramayan::1460.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has already destroyed Visvamitra's army. Enraged, Visvamitra's hundred sons charge him with weapons. The sage does not wrestle or strike back in ordinary combat; he answers with a single humkara and turns them to ash.
ramayan::1460.modern_relevance: Someone humiliates your side in front of everyone, and the urge to strike back surges up instantly. This verse shows how raw anger runs into a power that does not need to escalate.
ramayan::1460.insight: It shifts the mind from reactive force to the cost of uncontrolled anger.

ramayan::1461.verse_sanskrit: ते साश्वरथपादाता वसिष्ठेन महात्मना । भस्मीकृता मुहूर्तेन विश्वामित्रसुता स्तदा । । 1557 । ।
ramayan::1461.verse_hindi: Then one hundred sons of Viswamitra together with their horses, chariots and foot soldiers were reduced to ashes in a moment by the powerful Vasishta.
ramayan::1461.english_translation: Then one hundred sons of Viswamitra, together with their horses, chariots, and foot soldiers, were reduced to ashes in a moment by the powerful Vasishta.
ramayan::1461.translation_literal: ते (those) / साश्वरथपादाता (with horses, chariots, and foot soldiers) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one) / भस्मीकृता (were reduced to ashes) / मुहूर्तेन (in a moment) / विश्वामित्रसुता (the sons of Viswamitra) / स्तदा (then)
ramayan::1461.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1461.essence: One instant of force turns an army to ash.
ramayan::1461.simple_meaning: Vasishta destroys Viswamitra’s hundred sons and their entire force in an instant.
ramayan::1461.simple_insight: Power can end a conflict so completely that only shock remains.
ramayan::1461.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra’s sons rush forward with their full force, but Vasishta answers with overwhelming power. In a single moment, the attack is wiped out. The verse is part of the unfolding clash, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1461.modern_relevance: A fight escalates in seconds, and everything you thought would take hours collapses into one irreversible moment.
ramayan::1461.insight: It shows how quickly pride and aggression can be consumed by greater force.

ramayan::1462.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा विनाशितान् पुत्रान् बलं च सुमहायशा: । सव्रीडश्चिन्तयाऽविष्टो विश्वामित्रोऽभवत्तदा । । 1558 । ।
ramayan::1462.verse_hindi: Seeing his sons and army destroyed the illustrious Viswamitra was filled with shame and anxiety.
ramayan::1462.english_translation: Seeing his sons and army destroyed, the illustrious Viswamitra was filled with shame and anxiety.
ramayan::1462.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / विनाशितान् (destroyed) / पुत्रान् (sons) / बलं (army, force) / च (and) / सुमहायशाः (highly illustrious one) / सव्रीडः (filled with shame) / चिन्तया (by anxiety) / आविष्टः (overcome) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / अभवत् (became) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1462.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1462.essence: Power cannot hide the pain of total defeat.
ramayan::1462.simple_meaning: Viswamitra sees that his sons and fighting force have been destroyed, and shame and worry overwhelm him.
ramayan::1462.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when power cannot protect what you love.
ramayan::1462.detailed_meaning: After Vasishta burns down the sons of Viswamitra and their army, the great king-turned-sage stands stunned. His strength has failed, and the loss hits him as shame and anxious grief before the next image of defeat appears.
ramayan::1462.modern_relevance: You watch a project collapse after weeks of force and planning. The embarrassment lands first, then the worry: all that effort, and still nothing held.
ramayan::1462.insight: It shows the instant when outer power breaks and the mind turns inward to shame.

ramayan::1463.verse_sanskrit: समुद्र इव निर्वेगो भग्नदंष्ट्र इवोरग: । उपरक्त इवादित्यस्सद्यो निष्प्रभतां गत: । । 1559 । ।
ramayan::1463.verse_hindi: Like the ocean without waves or the snake bereft of fangs or the Sun eclipsed by Rahu, suddenly (Viswamitra) looked cheerless and dull.
ramayan::1463.english_translation: Like the ocean without waves or the snake bereft of fangs or the Sun eclipsed by Rahu, Viswamitra suddenly looked cheerless and dull.
ramayan::1463.translation_literal: समुद्र इव (like the ocean) / निर्वेगः (without waves, motionless) / भग्नदंष्ट्रः इव (like one with broken fangs) / उरगः (a serpent) / उपरक्तः इव (like one obscured) / आदित्यः (the Sun) / सद्यः (suddenly) / निष्प्रभताम् (dullness, lack of brilliance) / गतः (gone, become)
ramayan::1463.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1463.essence: Power can vanish in a single blow, leaving only stunned silence.
ramayan::1463.simple_meaning: Viswamitra lost his fierce energy and looked powerless, like a wave-less ocean, a snake without fangs, or a dimmed sun.
ramayan::1463.simple_insight: Even the strongest can be shaken when everything they built collapses.
ramayan::1463.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just watched his sons and army burn to ash before Vasistha. This verse does not teach a new principle; it shows the immediate collapse of his force and pride, using three images to mark how completely his power has been drained.
ramayan::1463.modern_relevance: You open the email that proves your best effort failed, and your body goes flat. The fight leaves first; the mind follows later.
ramayan::1463.insight: It shifts attention from outward power to the moment that power disappears under shock.

ramayan::1464.verse_sanskrit: हतपुत्रबलो दीनो लूनपक्ष इव द्विज: । हतदर्पो हतोत्साहो निर्वेदं समपद्यत । । 15510 । ।
ramayan::1464.verse_hindi: Having lost his sons and the army, like a bird with wings clipped, wretched, with pride vanished and confidence shattered Viswamitra fell into despondency.
ramayan::1464.english_translation: Having lost his sons and the army, like a bird with clipped wings, wretched, with pride gone and courage broken, Viswamitra fell into despondency.
ramayan::1464.translation_literal: हतपुत्रबलः (with sons and army slain) / दीनः (wretched) / लूनपक्षः इव (like one with clipped wings) / द्विजः (a bird) / हतदर्पः (whose pride is destroyed) / हतोत्साहः (whose zeal is destroyed) / निर्वेदम् (despondency) / समपद्यत (fell into)
ramayan::1464.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1464.essence: Pride and force collapse instantly when their support is gone.
ramayan::1464.simple_meaning: Viswamitra is crushed after losing his sons and army. His pride and energy collapse, and he falls into despair.
ramayan::1464.simple_insight: Even great strength can break when everything familiar is taken away.
ramayan::1464.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has watched his sons and army be destroyed. The mighty sage-king who once stood fearless now feels stripped bare, like a bird with clipped wings. This verse shows the collapse before his next decision.
ramayan::1464.modern_relevance: You can hold everything together until one blow takes away your confidence, your plan, and your footing at once.
ramayan::1464.insight: It shows the moment power turns into helplessness when pride and momentum are stripped away.

ramayan::1465.verse_sanskrit: स पुत्रमेकं राज्याय पालयेति नियुज्य च । पृथिवीं क्षत्रधर्मेण वनमेवान्वपद्यत । । 15511 । ।
ramayan::1465.verse_hindi: Viswamitra, having entrusted one of his remaining sons to rule the kingdom in accordance with the kshatriya tradition reached the forest.
ramayan::1465.english_translation: Having entrusted one son to rule the kingdom according to the duty of a warrior, Viswamitra went to the forest.
ramayan::1465.translation_literal: स (he) / पुत्रम् (son) / एकम् (one) / राज्याय (for the kingdom) / पालयेति (let [him] rule) / नियुज्य (having entrusted) / च (and) / पृथिवीम् (the earth/kingdom) / क्षत्रधर्मेण (by the duty of a kshatriya) / वनम् (forest) / एव (only) / अन्वपद्यत (he went)
ramayan::1465.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1465.essence: He lets go of rule and walks toward transformation.
ramayan::1465.simple_meaning: Viswamitra handed over the kingdom to one son and left for the forest.
ramayan::1465.simple_insight: Sometimes a turning point is quiet: you hand off what you can no longer hold and walk on.
ramayan::1465.detailed_meaning: After losing his sons and the strength of his rule, Viswamitra makes a final handover of the kingdom to one remaining son. Then he turns away from royal life and heads into the forest, where the next stage of his transformation will begin.
ramayan::1465.modern_relevance: You sign over a project, close the office door, and leave the role that once defined you. The next chapter begins only after you stop clinging to the old one.
ramayan::1465.insight: It shows the moment when worldly authority is relinquished so a deeper path can begin.

ramayan::1466.verse_sanskrit: स गत्वा हिमवत्पार्श्वं किन्नरोरगसेवितम् । महादेवप्रसादार्थं तपस्तेपे महातपा: । । 15512 । ।
ramayan::1466.verse_hindi: Mighty ascetic Viswamitra, reached the slopes of the Himavat mountain inhabited by kinnaras and uragas (serpents) and performed  austerities in order to propitiate lord Mahadeva.
ramayan::1466.english_translation: Mighty ascetic Viswamitra reached the slopes of Mount Himavat, inhabited by kinnaras and serpents, and performed austerities to win Mahadeva's favor.
ramayan::1466.translation_literal: स (he) / गत्वा (having gone) / हिमवत्पार्श्वं (to the side of Himavat) / किन्नरोरगसेवितम् (served by kinnaras and serpents) / महादेवप्रसादार्थं (for the favor of Mahadeva) / तपस्तेपे (performed austerities) / महातपा: (the great ascetic)
ramayan::1466.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1466.essence: He turns grief into austerity and seeks power through restraint.
ramayan::1466.simple_meaning: Viswamitra goes to the Himalayan slopes and undertakes severe austerity to please Mahadeva.
ramayan::1466.simple_insight: Great change begins with disciplined effort in a lonely place.
ramayan::1466.detailed_meaning: After losing his sons and his pride, Viswamitra leaves behind ordinary life and climbs to the remote slopes of Himavat. Among kinnaras and serpents, he begins harsh austerity to win Mahadeva's favor, setting up the next divine response.
ramayan::1466.modern_relevance: You reach for silence after a collapse, not comfort. When life has stripped you bare, real transformation often begins in a place no one else sees.
ramayan::1466.insight: It shifts the mind from wounded reaction to deliberate spiritual discipline.

ramayan::1467.verse_sanskrit: केनचित्त्वथ कालेन देवेशो वृषभध्वज: । दर्शयामास वरदो विश्वामित्रं महाबलम् । । 15513 । ।
ramayan::1467.verse_hindi: After some time, lord of the gods, bestower of boons, Maheswara with the symbol of the bull on the banner  appeared before mighty Viswamitra.
ramayan::1467.english_translation: After some time, Maheshvara, the lord of the gods and giver of boons, with the bull on his banner, appeared before mighty Vishvamitra.
ramayan::1467.translation_literal: केनचित् (after some) / अथ (then) / कालेन (by time) / देवेशः (lord of the gods) / वृषभध्वजः (bull-bannered one) / दर्शयामास (showed himself) / वरदः (boon-giver) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Vishvamitra) / महाबलम् (mighty)
ramayan::1467.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1467.essence: Long effort can summon what force never can.
ramayan::1467.simple_meaning: After a long period of austerity, Shiva appears before Vishvamitra and offers to grant him a boon.
ramayan::1467.simple_insight: Patient effort can ripen into a meeting you cannot force.
ramayan::1467.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has left kingship, climbed to the Himalayan slopes, and endured severe penance to win divine favor. After that long strain, Shiva finally appears before him. This verse is the arrival, not the request itself.
ramayan::1467.modern_relevance: You keep showing up to the same hard practice for months, with nothing visible to prove it. Then one day the work answers back.
ramayan::1467.insight: It marks the turning point where disciplined austerity meets divine response.

ramayan::1468.verse_sanskrit: किमर्थं तप्यसे राजन् ब्रूहि यत्ते विवक्षितम् । वरदोऽस्मि वरो यस्ते काङ्क्षितस्सोऽभिधीयताम् । । 15514 । ।
ramayan::1468.verse_hindi: O King what are you performing the penance for? Tell me what you want? I am bestower of boons. Speak out you desire (said Lord Siva).
ramayan::1468.english_translation: O King, why are you performing penance? Tell me what you want. I am the giver of boons; speak the desire you seek.
ramayan::1468.translation_literal: किमर्थं (for what reason) / तप्यसे (are you performing penance) / राजन् (O king) / ब्रूहि (tell) / यत् (what) / ते (your) / विवक्षितम् (intended desire) / वरदः (boon-giver) / अस्मि (I am) / वरः (boon) / यः (which) / ते (for you) / काङ्क्षितः (desired) / सः (that) / अभिधीयताम् (let it be spoken)
ramayan::1468.speaker: Shiva
ramayan::1468.essence: The first step toward receiving help is naming what you want.
ramayan::1468.simple_meaning: Shiva asks Vishwamitra why he is doing penance and tells him to say clearly what boon he wants.
ramayan::1468.simple_insight: There is relief in being invited to speak honestly about what you need.
ramayan::1468.detailed_meaning: On the Himalayan slopes, Vishwamitra’s austerity has drawn Shiva’s attention. The god appears and invites him to stop hiding behind effort and name the real desire behind the penance. This is the opening of a sacred exchange.
ramayan::1468.modern_relevance: You keep circling the issue in your head, hoping someone will understand without you saying it. This verse cuts through that hesitation: state the need, clearly and without disguise.
ramayan::1468.insight: It shifts you from indirect striving to clear self-expression.

ramayan::1469.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन विश्वामित्रो महातपा: । प्रणिपत्य महादेवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 15515 । ।
ramayan::1469.verse_hindi: Having heard this from the god, Viswamitra who performed the great austerities prostrated before Mahadeva and said these words.
ramayan::1469.english_translation: Having heard this from the divine being, Viswamitra, the great ascetic, bowed to Mahadeva and spoke these words.
ramayan::1469.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (having been thus spoken to) / तु (indeed) / देवेन (by the divine being) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महातपाः (great ascetic) / प्रणिपत्य (having bowed down) / महादेवम् (to Mahadeva) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1469.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1469.simple_meaning: Viswamitra bows to Mahadeva and responds after being invited to ask for a boon.
ramayan::1469.simple_insight: Respect can come before request. Humility often opens the door to what you seek.
ramayan::1469.detailed_meaning: Mahadeva appears before Viswamitra and offers a boon. The great ascetic does not rush in with pride; he bows first, then speaks. The verse is a transition into the request that follows, not the request itself.
ramayan::1469.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to ask for help in a room that matters. Before speaking, you steady yourself, lower your pride, and begin with respect.
ramayan::1469.insight: It shows that true asking begins with humility, not entitlement.

ramayan::1470.verse_sanskrit: यदि तुष्टो महादेव धनुर्वेदो ममानघ । साङ्गोपाङ्गोपनिषदस्सरहस्य: प्रदीयताम् । । 15516 । ।
ramayan::1470.verse_hindi: O Irreproachable one O Mahadeva if you are pleased with me, make me an expert in Dhanurveda, the science of archery with all it secrets, angas (branches), upangas (subdivisions) and Upanishads.
ramayan::1470.english_translation: O irreproachable Mahadeva, if you are pleased with me, grant me mastery of Dhanurveda, with all its branches, sub-branches, and secret teachings.
ramayan::1470.translation_literal: यदि (if) / तुष्टः (pleased) / महादेव (Mahadeva) / धनुर्वेदः (the science of archery) / मम (for me) / अनघ (irreproachable one) / साङ्गोपाङ्गोपनिषद्-सः (with branches, sub-branches, and secret teachings) / सरहस्यः (with secrets) / प्रदीयताम् (may it be granted)
ramayan::1470.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::1470.essence: True readiness means learning the whole art, not one useful trick.
ramayan::1470.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra asks Mahadeva not just for skill, but for complete mastery of archery, including its hidden principles and deeper knowledge.
ramayan::1470.simple_insight: Real growth asks for the whole discipline, not a quick advantage.
ramayan::1470.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has bowed before Mahadeva and now makes his request. He does not ask for a single weapon or a narrow blessing, but for full mastery of archery and its secret foundations, because his coming mission needs complete readiness.
ramayan::1470.modern_relevance: You can learn one shortcut for a presentation, or you can learn the craft so well that pressure no longer shakes you. Vishvamitra asks for the second kind of mastery.
ramayan::1470.insight: It shifts the mind from wanting a result to wanting deep competence.

ramayan::1471.verse_sanskrit: यानि देवेषु चास्त्राणि दानवेषु महर्षिषु । गन्धर्वयक्षरक्षस्सु प्रतिभान्तु ममानघ । । 15517 । ।
ramayan::1471.verse_hindi: O Irreproachable one whatever weapons are known to devatas, danavas, maharshis, gandharvas, yakshas, rakshasas, be revealed to me.
ramayan::1471.english_translation: O irreproachable one, whatever weapons are known among the gods, the danavas, the great sages, the gandharvas, the yakshas, and the rakshasas, let them become known to me.
ramayan::1471.translation_literal: यानि (whatever) / देवेषु (among the gods) / च (and) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / दानवेषु (among the danavas) / महर्षिषु (among the great sages) / गन्धर्वयक्षरक्षस्सु (among the gandharvas, yakshas, and rakshasas) / प्रतिभान्तु (let them appear / become known) / ममानघ (to me, O irreproachable one)
ramayan::1471.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1471.essence: True mastery asks for the whole field, not a convenient subset.
ramayan::1471.simple_meaning: Viswamitra asks Shiva to reveal every kind of weapon known across all realms and beings.
ramayan::1471.simple_insight: Real mastery begins with wanting the full picture, not a partial advantage.
ramayan::1471.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already bowed to Mahadeva and asked for the science of archery. Now he widens the request: he wants every weapon known to every class of beings. The moment shows his hunger for complete mastery, not a limited lesson.
ramayan::1471.modern_relevance: You take one course and realize it only scratched the surface. Instead of pretending that is enough, you go back and ask for the full subject, the hidden methods, the complete range.
ramayan::1471.insight: It shifts you from narrow competence to disciplined inquiry for total understanding.

ramayan::1472.verse_sanskrit: तव प्रसादाद्भवतु देवदेवममेप्सितम् । एवमस्त्विति देवेशो वाक्यमुक्त्वा गतस्तदा । । 15518 । ।
ramayan::1472.verse_hindi: O Lord of the gods by your favour let my desire be fulfilled. Lord Mahadeva having said: Be it so vanished.
ramayan::1472.english_translation: O Lord of the gods, by your favour let my desire be fulfilled. Lord Mahadeva, having said, 'So be it,' then disappeared.
ramayan::1472.translation_literal: तव (your) / प्रसादात् (by favour) / भवतु (let it be) / देवदेव (O lord of the gods) / मम (my) / एप्सितम् (desired) / एवम् (so) / अस्तु (be it) / इति (thus) / देवेशः (lord of the gods) / वाक्यम् (words) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / गतः (gone) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1472.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1472.essence: The blessing is given, and the story moves on to its consequences.
ramayan::1472.simple_meaning: Mahadeva grants Visvamitra's request for mastery in weapons, then leaves after saying yes.
ramayan::1472.simple_insight: A sincere request can be answered fully, but the real test comes after the blessing is received.
ramayan::1472.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just asked Mahadeva for mastery of divine weapons and sacred knowledge. Mahadeva agrees and disappears at once. The verse closes the exchange before the next line shows what that gift does to Visvamitra.
ramayan::1472.modern_relevance: You finally get the approval, the training, the access you wanted — and the moment is over before you can hold it. What matters next is how you use it.
ramayan::1472.insight: It marks the completion of a request, not the teaching itself, and sets up the consequences that follow.

ramayan::1473.verse_sanskrit: प्राप्य चास्त्राणि राजर्षिर्विश्वामित्रो महाबल: । दर्पेण महता युक्तो दर्पपूर्णोऽभवत्तदा । । 15519 । ।
ramayan::1473.verse_hindi: Rajarshi Viswamitra endowed with supreme power became very haughty. Having obtained the weapons, his insolence was greatly accentuated.
ramayan::1473.english_translation: Rajarshi Viswamitra, having obtained the weapons, became filled with great pride. His arrogance rose even higher.
ramayan::1473.translation_literal: प्राप्य (having obtained) / च (and) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / राजर्षिः (the royal sage) / विश्वामित्रः (Visvamitra) / महाबलः (of great strength) / दर्पेण (with pride) / महता (great) / युक्तः (endowed with) / दर्पपूर्णः (full of arrogance) / अभवत् (became) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1473.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1473.essence: Power without restraint quickly turns into arrogance.
ramayan::1473.simple_meaning: Visvamitra gained powerful weapons, and that success fed his pride. The verse shows power making his ego swell.
ramayan::1473.simple_insight: Strength can sharpen pride instead of wisdom.
ramayan::1473.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just received divine weapons after invoking Mahadeva. Instead of becoming steadier, he grows arrogant. The next verse compares his rising power to a swelling sea, showing how quickly achievement can inflate the sense of separate self.
ramayan::1473.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the praise, the leverage — and suddenly your patience thins. The very thing you wanted can also make you harder to live with.
ramayan::1473.insight: It warns you to watch the ego surge that can follow success.

ramayan::1474.verse_sanskrit: विवर्धमानो वीर्येण समुद्र इव पर्वणि । हतमेव तदा मेने वसिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम् । । 15520 । ।
ramayan::1474.verse_hindi: Like the sea during the full moon, with his increased power (blessed with the invincible strength of the weapons) Viswamitra thought the foremost of ascetics Vasishta was (already) slain. (It shows the height of the kings ignorance and arrogance).
ramayan::1474.english_translation: Like the sea at full moon, Viswamitra, swollen with new power, thought the great sage Vasishta had already been slain.
ramayan::1474.translation_literal: विवर्धमानो (growing) / वीर्येण (by strength) / समुद्रः इव (like the sea) / पर्वणि (at full moon) / हतं (slain) / एव (indeed) / तदा (then) / मेने (he thought) / वसिष्ठम् (Vasishta) / ऋषि-सत्तमम् (the best of sages)
ramayan::1474.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1474.essence: Growing power can make you imagine victory before it exists.
ramayan::1474.simple_meaning: Viswamitra grows more powerful, but that very rise makes him wrongly believe Vasishta is already defeated.
ramayan::1474.simple_insight: Strength without humility can distort judgment and make you mistake confidence for truth.
ramayan::1474.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just gained great weapons and feels unstoppable. Instead of seeing clearly, he inflates his own power and assumes the sage Vasishta is finished. The verse marks the danger of pride at the peak of success.
ramayan::1474.modern_relevance: You get a promotion, a bigger budget, or a string of wins — and suddenly you start believing your own reach is proof of your rightness. This verse warns how quickly momentum can turn into blindness.
ramayan::1474.insight: It shifts the mind from inflated certainty to humble self-checking before judgment.

ramayan::1475.verse_sanskrit: ततो गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदं मुमोचास्त्राणि पार्थिव: । यैस्तत्तपोवनं सर्वं निर्दग्धं चास्त्रतेजसा । । 15521 । ।
ramayan::1475.verse_hindi: Thereafter king Viswamitra having proceeded towards the hermitage (of Vasishta) and released the weapons by the energy of which the entire forest of the ascetics was burnt down.
ramayan::1475.english_translation: Thereafter king Viswamitra proceeded to the hermitage and unleashed the weapons that had burned the whole forest of ascetics with their blazing force.
ramayan::1475.translation_literal: ततः (thereafter) / गत्वा (having gone) / आश्रमपदम् (to the hermitage) / मुमोच (released, unleashed) / अस्त्राणि (the weapons) / पार्थिवः (the king) / यैः (by which) / तत् (that) / तपोवनम् (forest of ascetics) / सर्वम् (entire) / निर्दग्धम् (burned down) / च (and) / अस्त्रतेजसा (by the force of the weapons)
ramayan::1475.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1475.essence: Strength without restraint turns into fire.
ramayan::1475.simple_meaning: Viswamitra went to Vasishta’s hermitage and released the weapons that had already scorched the ascetics’ forest.
ramayan::1475.simple_insight: Power can be turned into destruction in a single moment.
ramayan::1475.detailed_meaning: After Viswamitra’s pride has swollen with new weapons, he marches toward Vasishta’s hermitage and unleashes them. The verse is not the lesson itself, but the violent proof of how far his anger has carried him.
ramayan::1475.modern_relevance: You finally have the authority you wanted, and the first thing it can do is burn what once resisted you.
ramayan::1475.insight: It shows how quickly trained power becomes ruin when guided by wounded pride.

ramayan::1476.verse_sanskrit: उदीर्यमाणमस्त्रं तद्विश्वामित्रस्य धीमत: । दृष्ट्वा विप्रद्रुतास्सर्वे मुनयश्शतशो दिश: । । 15522 । ।
ramayan::1476.verse_hindi: On seeing the weapons discharged by the intelligent Viswamitra saints in hundreds fled in all directions.
ramayan::1476.english_translation: On seeing the weapons discharged by the intelligent Viswamitra, the saints fled in hundreds in all directions.
ramayan::1476.translation_literal: उदीर्यमाणमस्त्रम् (the weapon being discharged) / तत् (that) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Viswamitra) / धीमतः (of the wise one) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / विप्रद्रुताः (fled in panic) / सर्वे (all) / मुनयः (ascetics) / शतशः (in hundreds) / दिशः (towards directions)
ramayan::1476.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1476.essence: Raw power makes even the innocent run.
ramayan::1476.simple_meaning: Viswamitra unleashes his weapon, and the surrounding sages panic and run in every direction.
ramayan::1476.simple_insight: Power changes the atmosphere instantly; fear spreads before anyone can think.
ramayan::1476.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already turned his fury toward Vasishta’s hermitage. As his weapon is released, the peaceful forest becomes a place of terror. The surrounding sages see the force rising and flee in every direction, showing how quickly sacred calm can collapse.
ramayan::1476.modern_relevance: A room can go silent in a second when one person loses control. Even people who meant no harm start looking for the nearest exit.
ramayan::1476.insight: It shows how unchecked force creates panic and breaks the safety around it.

ramayan::1477.verse_sanskrit: वसिष्ठस्य च ये शिष्यास्तथैव मृगपक्षिण: । विद्रवन्ति भयाद्भीता नानादिग्भ्यस्सहस्रश: । । 15523 । ।
ramayan::1477.verse_hindi: The disciples of Vasishta as well as animals and birds got terrified by the fear and fled in their thousands in all directions.
ramayan::1477.english_translation: Vasishta's disciples, along with the animals and birds, were terrified and fled in thousands in every direction.
ramayan::1477.translation_literal: वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / च (and) / ये (those who) / शिष्याः (disciples) / तथा एव (likewise) / मृग-पक्षिणः (animals and birds) / विद्रवन्ति (flee) / भयात् (from fear) / भीताः (terrified) / नाना-दिग्भ्यः (from many directions) / सहस्रशः (in thousands)
ramayan::1477.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1477.essence: Fear turns a living place into empty ground.
ramayan::1477.simple_meaning: Vasishta's students, along with the forest animals and birds, panicked and ran away in every direction.
ramayan::1477.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast enough to empty even a sacred place.
ramayan::1477.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already released his weapons near Vasishta's hermitage. The force of that display terrifies everyone there — students, animals, and birds alike — and they scatter in all directions. This verse is part of the immediate aftermath, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1477.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one sharp outburst, and everyone looks for the exit. Fear does that: it clears the space before anyone has time to think.
ramayan::1477.insight: It shows how overwhelming force can scatter even the innocent around it.

ramayan::1478.verse_hindi: The greatsoul Vasishtas hermitage became deserted and silent in an instant like a barren field.
ramayan::1478.english_translation: The great sage Vasishta's hermitage became empty and silent in an instant, like a barren field.
ramayan::1478.translation_literal: वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / आश्रमपदम् (hermitage) / शून्यम् (empty) / आसीत् (became) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / मुहूर्तम् इव (like for a moment) / निश्शब्दम् (silent) / आसीत् (was) / इरिण-सन्निभम् (like barren ground)
ramayan::1478.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1478.essence: Fear can turn a living place into emptiness at once.
ramayan::1478.simple_meaning: Vasishta's hermitage was suddenly emptied out. The place fell silent, as if life had been drained from it.
ramayan::1478.simple_insight: Fear can empty even a sacred place in seconds.
ramayan::1478.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra's force has just been released, and the uproar spreads through Vasishta's hermitage. Saints, students, birds, and animals flee. In this verse, the once-living ashrama is left deserted and still, showing the immediate shock before Vasishta speaks again.
ramayan::1478.modern_relevance: A room can go quiet in the second after bad news lands. What felt stable a moment ago suddenly feels hollow, and everyone looks for safety first.
ramayan::1478.insight: It shows how quickly panic can erase order, leaving even a sacred space stripped bare.

ramayan::1479.verse_sanskrit: वदतो वै वसिष्ठस्य मा भैरिति मुहुर्मुहु: । नाशयाम्यद्य गाधेयं नीहारमिव भास्कर: । । 15525 । ।
ramayan::1479.verse_hindi: Even while Vasistha was repeatedly  assuring  the saints saying Do not fear, I will now
ramayan::1479.english_translation: Even while Vasistha was repeatedly assuring the saints, saying, 'Do not fear,' he declared, 'Today I will destroy the son of Gadhi like the sun dissolving mist.'
ramayan::1479.translation_literal: वदतो (speaking) / वै (indeed) / वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasistha) / मा भैरिति (do not fear) / मुहुर्मुहु: (again and again) / नाशयामि (I will destroy) / अद्य (today) / गाधेयं (the son of Gadhi) / नीहारमिव (like mist) / भास्कर: (the sun)
ramayan::1479.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1479.essence: Reassurance and wrath can live in the same breath.
ramayan::1479.simple_meaning: Vasishta calms the frightened saints, but he also vows to destroy Vishwamitra right away, like the sun scattering mist.
ramayan::1479.simple_insight: A calm voice can still carry fierce resolve.
ramayan::1479.detailed_meaning: In Vasishta's hermitage, terror has just driven away the disciples, animals, and birds. The sacred place stands emptied. While he tells the frightened saints not to fear, Vasishta turns toward Vishwamitra and vows immediate destruction, setting up the clash that follows.
ramayan::1479.modern_relevance: You may be reassuring everyone in the room while anger is already hardening inside you. The words sound calm; the decision behind them is not.
ramayan::1479.insight: It shows how quickly protection can turn into retaliation when pride is wounded.

ramayan::1480.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा वसिष्ठो जपतां वर: । विश्वामित्रं तदा वाक्यं सरोषमिदमब्रवीत् । । 15526 । ।
ramayan::1480.verse_hindi: The infuriated Vasishta who was highly brilliant, foremost among those who meditate said to Viswamitra:
ramayan::1480.english_translation: Having said this, the highly radiant Vasishta, best among those who pray, then spoke this angry word to Vishvamitra.
ramayan::1480.translation_literal: एवमुक्त्वा (having said thus) / महातेजा (highly radiant) / वसिष्ठो (Vasishta) / जपतां (of those who pray) / वरः (best) / विश्वामित्रं (to Vishvamitra) / तदा (then) / वाक्यं (word/speech) / सरोषम् (angrily) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1480.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1480.essence: A warning turns into a direct accusation.
ramayan::1480.simple_meaning: Vasishta turns from warning the sages to addressing Vishvamitra directly, and he speaks in anger.
ramayan::1480.simple_insight: A calm warning has become a personal confrontation.
ramayan::1480.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just tried to steady the frightened sages in his hermitage after Vishvamitra’s attack. Now, still blazing with force, he turns from reassurance to accusation and speaks directly to Vishvamitra. The verse sets up the rebuke that follows.
ramayan::1480.modern_relevance: You try to keep a room calm, but one person has pushed too far. The tone changes instantly from reassurance to direct confrontation.
ramayan::1480.insight: It marks the moment restraint gives way to open rebuke.

ramayan::1481.verse_sanskrit: आश्रमं चिरसम्वृद्धं यद्विनाशितवानसि । दुराचारोऽसि तन्मूढ तस्मात्त्वं न भविष्यसि । । 15527 । ।
ramayan::1481.verse_hindi: O Fool this hermitage has been developed over a long time. Why did you destroy it?  On account of your wickedness you will not live long.
ramayan::1481.english_translation: O fool, this hermitage has been built up over a long time. Why did you destroy it? Because of your wickedness, you will not live long.
ramayan::1481.translation_literal: आश्रमं (hermitage) / चिरसम्वृद्धं (grown over a long time) / यत् (which) / विनाशितवान् असि (you have destroyed) । / दुराचारः (of wicked conduct) / असि (you are) / तत् (therefore) / मूढ (fool) / तस्मात् (therefore) / त्वम् (you) / न भविष्यसि (will not exist / will not live long)
ramayan::1481.speaker: Vasistha
ramayan::1481.essence: Destruction done in anger exposes the destroyer more than the damage.
ramayan::1481.simple_meaning: Vasistha angrily rebukes Viswamitra for destroying the hermitage and says such wickedness will bring his downfall.
ramayan::1481.simple_insight: Cruel acts do not stay hidden; they carry their own ruin.
ramayan::1481.detailed_meaning: Vasistha has just tried to calm the sages, but Viswamitra's attack has pushed him past restraint. Standing before the ruined hermitage, he turns on Viswamitra with fury, condemning both the destruction and the character behind it.
ramayan::1481.modern_relevance: You walk into a place someone has carefully built, then tear it apart in one angry moment. The damage is immediate, but the real cost is what it reveals about you.
ramayan::1481.insight: It shifts attention from the act itself to the character that made the act possible.

ramayan::1482.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा परमक्रुद्धो दण्डमुद्यम्य सत्वर: । विधूममिव कालाग्निं यमदण्डमिवापरम् । । 15528 । ।
ramayan::1482.verse_hindi: Exceedingly furious Vasishta quickly lifted up his staff which looked like the staff of Yama (the od of death), like smokeless fire at the time of destruction of the worlds.
ramayan::1482.english_translation: Exceedingly furious Vasishta quickly lifted up his staff, like the staff of Yama and like smokeless fire at the end of the world.
ramayan::1482.translation_literal: इत्युक्त्वा (having said thus) / परमक्रुद्धः (exceedingly furious) / दण्डम् (staff) / उद्यम्य (lifting up) / सत्वरः (quickly) / विधूमम् (smokeless) / इव (like) / कालाग्निम् (fire of destruction) / यमदण्डम् (staff of Yama) / इव (like) / अपरम् (another)
ramayan::1482.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1482.essence: Raw anger can make restraint look like death itself.
ramayan::1482.simple_meaning: Vasishta, angered by the destruction of the hermitage, raised his staff at once. His force looked like death itself and like the fire that ends a world.
ramayan::1482.simple_insight: Some anger is so absolute it feels cosmic.
ramayan::1482.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just condemned Viswamitra for destroying the hermitage built over many years. In this instant, the sage does not answer with words alone. He lifts his staff in fury, and the scene shifts from insult to imminent spiritual and physical conflict.
ramayan::1482.modern_relevance: You reach the point where a boundary has been crossed and your body knows it before your mind does. The response comes up fast, hot, and total.
ramayan::1482.insight: It shows how quickly outrage can turn into action when sacred limits are violated.

ramayan::1483.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन विश्वामित्रो महाबल: । आग्नेयमस्त्रमुत्क्षिप्य तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् । । 1561 । ।
ramayan::1483.verse_hindi: Thus said Vasishta. Mighty Viswamitra lifted up agneya astra (shaft of fire) and discharging it said, stay, stay.
ramayan::1483.english_translation: Thus said Vasishta. Mighty Viswamitra lifted the fire weapon and, as he released it, said, “Stand, stand.”
ramayan::1483.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus spoken to) / वसिष्ठेन (by Vasishta) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महाबलः (mighty) / आग्नेयम् (fiery) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / उत्क्षिप्य (having lifted up) / तिष्ठ (stand) / तिष्ठ (stand) / इति (thus) / च (and) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1483.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1483.essence: Power in anger only deepens the clash.
ramayan::1483.simple_meaning: Viswamitra, angered by Vasishta, raises the fire weapon and commands it to strike or stop the opponent.
ramayan::1483.simple_insight: The moment shows how quickly wounded pride can turn into destructive force.
ramayan::1483.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just condemned the destruction of his hermitage. In response, Viswamitra, the powerful king-turned-sage, raises the fire weapon in fury and commands it forward. The verse is a tense step in a larger escalation, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1483.modern_relevance: A heated message thread can turn into a full-blown fight in seconds. One sharp reply, sent in anger, can turn a disagreement into damage.
ramayan::1483.insight: It shows how anger escalates conflict before reason can return.

ramayan::1484.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मदण्डं समुत्क्षिप्य कालदण्डमिवाऽपरम् । वसिष्ठो भगवान् क्रोधादिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 1562 । ।
ramayan::1484.verse_hindi: Venerable Vasishta, in fury lifted the Brahmadanda which was like another rod of death. And spoke these words:
ramayan::1484.english_translation: Venerable Vasishta, in fury lifted the Brahmadanda which was like another rod of death. And spoke these words:
ramayan::1484.translation_literal: ब्रह्मदण्डम् (the Brahma-staff) / समुत्क्षिप्य (having lifted up) / कालदण्डम् (the rod of death) / इव (like) / अपरम् (another) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / भगवान् (the venerable one) / क्रोधात् (out of anger) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1484.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1484.essence: The argument has reached the point where restraint is about to fail.
ramayan::1484.simple_meaning: Vasishta, angered by Viswamitra, raised a powerful staff and began to speak.
ramayan::1484.simple_insight: Even sages can be pulled into fury when pride is challenged.
ramayan::1484.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already answered Vasishta's challenge with a fire weapon. Now Vasishta, enraged, lifts the Brahmadanda like a staff of death and prepares to retaliate. The verse is a bridge into the confrontation, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1484.modern_relevance: A harsh email lands in your inbox, and your first instinct is to fire back immediately. The moment before you reply is where the whole outcome still hangs.
ramayan::1484.insight: It marks the instant a conflict crosses from words into irreversible action.

ramayan::1485.verse_sanskrit: क्षत्रबन्धो स्थितोस्म्येष यद्बलं तद्विदर्शय । नाशयाम्यद्य ते दर्पं शस्त्रस्य तव गाधिज । । 1563 । ।
ramayan::1485.verse_hindi: O wicked kshatriya O son of Gadhi here I stand. Show me your strength and the pride of your arms. I will destroy them now.
ramayan::1485.english_translation: O wicked kshatriya, O son of Gadhi, here I stand. Show me your strength and the pride of your arms. I will destroy them now.
ramayan::1485.translation_literal: क्षत्रबन्धो (O wicked kshatriya) / स्थितः (standing) / अस्मि (I am) / एषः (here) / यत् (whatever) / बलम् (strength) / तत् (that) / विदर्शय (show) / नाशयामि (I will destroy) / अद्य (now) / ते (your) / दर्पम् (pride) / शस्त्रस्य (of weapons) / तव (your) / गाधिज (O son of Gadhi)
ramayan::1485.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1485.essence: Power meets power, but pride is the first thing Vasishta aims to break.
ramayan::1485.simple_meaning: Vasishta stands his ground and challenges Vishwamitra to prove his power. He says he will crush the pride behind Vishwamitra's weapons.
ramayan::1485.simple_insight: Raw force cannot intimidate a mind rooted in higher power.
ramayan::1485.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has raised a fiery weapon, and Vasishta answers without stepping back. The sage who lives by spiritual power refuses to yield to royal force, turning the clash into a test of strength, pride, and authority.
ramayan::1485.modern_relevance: Someone tries to bully you with status, volume, or credentials. You don't have to match their noise to remain unshaken.
ramayan::1485.insight: It frames the conflict as a contest between weapon power and spiritual power, not just two angry men.

ramayan::1486.verse_sanskrit: क्व च ते क्षत्रियबलं क्व च ब्रह्मबलं महत् । पश्य ब्रह्मबलं दिव्यं मम क्षत्रियपांसन । । 1564 । ।
ramayan::1486.verse_hindi: O mean kshatriya where does your energy of a kshatriya stand in comparison with the great energy of Brahma? Behold my Brahmabala (Brahmans energy).
ramayan::1486.english_translation: O mean kshatriya, where does your kshatriya power stand beside the great power of Brahma? Behold my divine Brahma-power.
ramayan::1486.translation_literal: क्व (where) / च (and) / ते (your) / क्षत्रियबलं (kshatriya power) / क्व (where) / च (and) / ब्रह्मबलं (Brahma-power) / महत् (great) / पश्य (behold) / ब्रह्मबलं (Brahma-power) / दिव्यं (divine) / मम (my) / क्षत्रियपांसन (O mean kshatriya)
ramayan::1486.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1486.essence: Louder strength bows before deeper power.
ramayan::1486.simple_meaning: Vasishta challenges Vishvamitra, saying a warrior's strength is nothing beside the greater force of sacred power.
ramayan::1486.simple_insight: Raw force can look strong, but deeper discipline can stop it cold.
ramayan::1486.detailed_meaning: Vasishta stands enraged with the Brahmadanda raised against Vishvamitra. After mocking Vishvamitra's warrior pride, he points to a higher power that does not depend on weapons. The verse is part of the clash before his sacred force overwhelms Vishvamitra's attack.
ramayan::1486.modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready to win by volume, status, or force. Then someone calmer, steadier, and more grounded stops you without raising their voice.
ramayan::1486.insight: It shifts the mind from visible power to the strength that comes from mastery and restraint.

ramayan::1487.verse_sanskrit: तस्यास्त्रं गाधिपुत्रस्य घोरमाग्नेयमुद्यतम् । ब्रह्मदण्डेन तच्छान्तमग्नेर्वेग इवाम्भसा । । 1565 । ।
ramayan::1487.verse_hindi: The Brahmadanda (released by Vasishta) put down the dreadful agneya astra released by Gadhis son just like the force of fire is extinguished by water.
ramayan::1487.english_translation: Vasishta's Brahmadanda quelled the dreadful fire weapon of Vishvamitra's son, just as water extinguishes fire.
ramayan::1487.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / गाधिपुत्रस्य (of the son of Gadhi) / घोरम् (dreadful) / आग्नेयम् (fiery) / उद्यतम् (raised) / ब्रह्मदण्डेन (with the Brahmadanda) / तत् (that) / शान्तम् (was calmed) / अग्नेः (of fire) / वेगः (force) / इव (like) / अम्भसा (by water)
ramayan::1487.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1487.essence: A greater force ends the clash without becoming violent itself.
ramayan::1487.simple_meaning: Vasishta's forceful spiritual weapon stops Vishvamitra's fire weapon instantly, like water putting out flames.
ramayan::1487.simple_insight: Some conflicts are ended not by louder force, but by a higher force that contains it.
ramayan::1487.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has challenged Vasishta, and the air is thick with rival power. Vishvamitra releases a terrifying fire weapon, but Vasishta answers with the Brahmadanda. The blazing attack is stopped at once, showing the superiority of disciplined spiritual power over raw aggression.
ramayan::1487.modern_relevance: Two people are escalating a fight in front of everyone, each trying to outdo the other. Then one calm response cuts through the whole thing. Some situations are not won by matching heat with heat.
ramayan::1487.insight: It shifts attention from aggressive escalation to the quiet authority that can end it.

ramayan::1488.verse_sanskrit: वारुणं चैव रौद्रं च ऐन्द्रं पाशुपतं तथा । ऐषीकं चापि चिक्षेप कुपितो गाधिनन्दन: । । 1566 । ।
ramayan::1488.verse_hindi: The incensed son of Gadhi employed varuna, raudra, aindra, pasupata and aishika  weapons.
ramayan::1488.english_translation: The incensed son of Gadhi released the varuna, raudra, aindra, pasupata, and aishika weapons.
ramayan::1488.translation_literal: वारुणं (varuna) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / रौद्रं (raudra) / च (and) / ऐन्द्रं (aindra) / पाशुपतं (pasupata) / तथा (and so) / ऐषीकं (aishika) / च (and) / अपि (also) / चिक्षेप (threw/released) / कुपितो (angered) / गाधिनन्दनः (son of Gadhi)
ramayan::1488.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1488.essence: Anger keeps reaching for stronger force.
ramayan::1488.simple_meaning: Angry Vishvamitra unleashes several powerful weapons in battle.
ramayan::1488.simple_insight: Power under anger only multiplies danger.
ramayan::1488.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra, the son of Gadhi, has been pushed into open conflict with Vasishta. After one weapon is checked, he answers with another, releasing a series of fearsome astras. The verse is part of the escalating battle, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1488.modern_relevance: A heated text thread turns into a flood of sharper replies. Each new message feels stronger, but it only deepens the damage.
ramayan::1488.insight: It shows how anger escalates conflict instead of resolving it.

ramayan::1489.verse_sanskrit: मानवं मोहनं चैव गान्धर्वं स्वापनं तथा । जृम्भणं मादनं चैव संतापनविलापने । । 1567 । । शोषणं दारणं चैव वज्रमस्त्रं सुदुर्जयम् । ब्रह्मपाशं कालपाशं वारुणं पाशमेव च । । 1568 । । पैनाकास्त्रं च दयितं शुष्कार्द्रे अशनी उभे । दण्डास्त्रमथ पैशाचं क्रौञ्चमस्त्रं तथैव च । । 1569 । । धर्मचक्रं कालचक्रं विष्णुचक्रं तथैव च । वायव्यं मथनं चैव अस्त्रं हयशिरस्तथा । । 15610 । । शक्तिद्वयं च चिक्षेप कङ्कालं मुसलं तथा । 560वैद्याधरं महास्त्रं च कालास्त्रमथ दारुणम् । । 15611 । । त्रिशूलमस्त्रं घोरं च कापालमथ कङ्कणम् । एतान्यस्त्राणि चिक्षेप सर्वाणि रघुनन्दन । । 15612 । । वसिष्ठे जपतां श्रेष्ठे तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
ramayan::1489.verse_hindi: O Descendent of Raghu Viswamitra employed weapons like manava, mohana, gandharva, swapana, jrimbhana, madana, santapana, vilapana, shoshana, darana, vajra weapons, Brahma, kala and varuna pasas, the favourite painaka, daita, shushka, ardra vajras, danda, paisacha, krauncha, weapons, dharmachakra, kalachakra, vishnuchakras, vayavya, mathana, hayasira weapons, kanakala, musala powers,
ramayan::1489.english_translation: O Descendent of Raghu, Viswamitra employed weapons like manava, mohana, gandharva, swapana, jrimbhana, madana, santapana, vilapana, shoshana, darana, vajra weapons, Brahma, kala and varuna pasas, the favourite painaka, daita, shushka, ardra vajras, danda, paisacha, krauncha, weapons, dharmachakra, kalachakra, vishnuchakras, vayavya, mathana, hayasira weapons, kanakala, musala powers,
ramayan::1489.translation_literal: मानवं (human) / मोहनं (bewildering) / चैव (and) / गान्धर्वं (gandharva) / स्वापनं (sleep-inducing) / तथा (and so on) / जृम्भणं (yawning) / मादनं (intoxicating) / चैव (and) / संतापनविलापने (causing distress and lamentation) / शोषणं (drying) / दारणं (splitting) / चैव (and) / वज्रमस्त्रं (thunderbolt-weapon) / सुदुर्जयम् (hard to conquer) / ब्रह्मपाशं (Brahma noose) / कालपाशं (time noose) / वारुणं (Varuna) / पाशमेव (noose indeed) / च (and) / पैनाकास्त्रं (Pinaka-weapon) / च (and) / दयितं (favoured) / शुष्कार्द्रे (dry and wet) / अशनी (lightnings) / उभे (both) / दण्डास्त्रम् (staff-weapon) / अथ (then) / पैशाचं (ghostly) / क्रौञ्चमस्त्रं (krauncha-weapon) / तथैव (likewise) / च (and) / धर्मचक्रं (wheel of dharma) / कालचक्रं (wheel of time) / विष्णुचक्रं (Vishnu wheel) / तथैव (likewise) / च (and) / वायव्यं (wind-born) / मथनं (churning) / चैव (and) / अस्त्रं (weapon) / हयशिरस्तथा (horse-head weapon also) / शक्तिद्वयं (two spears) / च (and) / चिक्षेप (he hurled) / कङ्कालं (skeleton) / मुसलं (mace) / तथा (and) / वैयाधरं (vaidyadhara) / महास्त्रं (great weapon) / च (and) / कालास्त्रम् (time-weapon) / अथ (then) / दारुणम् (terrible) / त्रिशूलमस्त्रं (trident-weapon) / घोरं (fierce) / च (and) / कापालम् (kapala) / अथ (then) / कङ्कणम् (bracelet-weapon) / एतानि (these) / अस्त्राणि (weapons) / चिक्षेप (he hurled) / सर्वाणि (all) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of Raghu) / वसिष्ठे (at Vasishta) / जपतां (among those reciting prayers) / श्रेष्ठे (the best) / तद् (that) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful) / इव (as if) / अभवत् (became)
ramayan::1489.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1489.essence: A flood of force can still fail against steadiness.
ramayan::1489.simple_meaning: Viswamitra unleashes a vast array of magical weapons against Vasishta, but the scene is only a buildup to their failure. The real point is the sheer scale of force he brings, not a teaching on how to live.
ramayan::1489.simple_insight: Not every display of power changes the outcome. Sometimes force only reveals its own limits.
ramayan::1489.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra, once a king and now a fierce ascetic, hurls every weapon he knows at Vasishta in a contest of power and austerity. The verse piles up the names of those weapons to show how overwhelming the assault is before Vasishta answers it.
ramayan::1489.modern_relevance: A person can send every sharp message, every argument, every clever move, and still not touch the deeper calm of the other side. Some conflicts only expose how much force is being wasted.
ramayan::1489.insight: It shows escalation, not resolution, and prepares for the greater power that will answer it.

ramayan::1490.verse_sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि दण्डेन ग्रसते ब्रह्मणस्सुत: । । 15613 । । तेषु शान्तेषु ब्रह्मास्त्रं क्षिप्तवान् गाधिनन्दन: ।
ramayan::1490.verse_hindi: Vasishta son of Brahma, swallowed all those weapons with his staff. When those weapons were humbled, son of Gadhi employed Brahmastra.
ramayan::1490.english_translation: Vasishta, son of Brahma, swallowed all those weapons with his staff. When those weapons were subdued, the son of Gadhi launched the Brahmastra.
ramayan::1490.translation_literal: तानि (those) / सर्वाणि (all) / दण्डेन (with a staff) / ग्रसते (swallows) / ब्रह्मणस्सुत: (the son of Brahma) / तेषु (when those) / शान्तेषु (having become calm/subdued) / ब्रह्मास्त्रं (Brahmastra) / क्षिप्तवान् (cast) / गाधिनन्दन: (the son of Gadhi)
ramayan::1490.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1490.essence: Steady force can absorb violence without breaking.
ramayan::1490.simple_meaning: Vasishta neutralizes every weapon with his staff, and only then does Vishwamitra release the Brahmastra.
ramayan::1490.simple_insight: Power loses its edge when it meets steadiness.
ramayan::1490.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has already thrown every kind of divine weapon he knows. Vasishta, calm and immovable, absorbs them all with his staff. Only after that failure does Vishwamitra reach for the Brahmastra, raising the conflict to an even higher level.
ramayan::1490.modern_relevance: A heated argument keeps escalating: one text, then another, then a sharper insult. Someone refuses to flinch, and the whole exchange changes shape. This verse shows how calm can outmatch force.
ramayan::1490.insight: It shifts the mind from escalating force to composed restraint.

ramayan::1491.verse_sanskrit: तदस्त्रमुद्यतं दृष्ट्वा देवास्साग्निपुरोगमा: । । 15614 । । देवर्षयश्च सम्भ्रान्तागन्धर्वास्समहोरगा: । त्रैलोक्यमासीत्सन्तप्तं ब्रह्मास्त्रे समुदीरिते । । 15615 ।
ramayan::1491.verse_hindi: All the devatas, with Agni in the forefront, divine rishis, great uragas and gandharvas were agitated seeing the Brahmastra raised. When Brahmastra was discharged, the  three worlds became distressed.
ramayan::1491.english_translation: Seeing the Brahmastra raised, all the devas led by Agni, the divine sages, gandharvas, and great serpents were agitated. When the Brahmastra was released, the three worlds were distressed.
ramayan::1491.translation_literal: तदस्त्रम् (that weapon) / उद्यतम् (raised) / दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / देवाः (the devas) / स अग्निपुरोगमाः (with Agni in front) / देवर्षयः (divine sages) / च (and) / सम्भ्रान्ताः (agitated) / गन्धर्वाः (gandharvas) / स महोरगाः (with great serpents) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / आसीत् (was) / सन्तप्तम् (distressed) / ब्रह्मास्त्रे (in the Brahmastra) / समुदीरिते (when released)
ramayan::1491.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1491.essence: Power without restraint makes the whole world tremble.
ramayan::1491.simple_meaning: The release of the Brahmastra shakes every level of existence. Even celestial beings tremble when such force is unleashed.
ramayan::1491.simple_insight: Some actions are so vast that they disturb far more than the person who starts them.
ramayan::1491.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra's weapon has just been answered by Vasishta's power, and the conflict has escalated beyond ordinary combat. The devas, sages, gandharvas, and serpents all recoil as the Brahmastra rises, because this is no longer a duel — it threatens the balance of the three worlds.
ramayan::1491.modern_relevance: A single message sent in anger can spread through an entire family, team, or community before anyone can stop it. Some escalations are bigger than the moment that triggered them.
ramayan::1491.insight: It shifts attention from winning a clash to noticing the wider damage that force can unleash.

ramayan::1492.verse_sanskrit: तदप्यस्त्रं महाघोरं ब्रह्मं ब्राह्मेण तेजसा । वसिष्ठो ग्रसते सर्वं ब्रह्मदण्डेन राघव । । 15616 । ।
ramayan::1492.verse_hindi: O Descendant of Raghu Vasishta who possessed the energy of Brahma swallowed that very dreadful Brahmastra entirely with the help of Brahmadanda.
ramayan::1492.english_translation: O descendant of Raghu, Vasishta, endowed with the energy of Brahma, swallowed that dreadful Brahmastra completely with the Brahmadanda.
ramayan::1492.translation_literal: तत् (that) / अपि (also) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / महाघोरम् (very dreadful) / ब्रह्मम् (Brahma) / ब्राह्मेण (with Brahma's) / तेजसा (energy) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / ग्रसते (swallowed) / सर्वम् (entirely) / ब्रह्मदण्डेन (with the Brahmadanda) / राघव (O descendant of Raghu)
ramayan::1492.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1492.essence: Greater force can absorb even the most terrible weapon.
ramayan::1492.simple_meaning: Vasishta completely neutralized the terrible Brahmastra by using the power of his Brahmadanda.
ramayan::1492.simple_insight: Some forces are stopped not by force, but by greater stillness and authority.
ramayan::1492.detailed_meaning: A deadly Brahmastra has been released, and even the gods are shaken. Vasishta, carrying Brahma's own force, absorbs the weapon with his staff, showing that a higher power can contain overwhelming destruction.
ramayan::1492.modern_relevance: A crisis escalates in a room, and everyone waits for it to explode. One person stays steady, speaks once, and the whole atmosphere changes. Real authority does not always shout.
ramayan::1492.insight: It shifts attention from panic to the presence that can contain panic.

ramayan::1493.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मास्त्रं ग्रसमानस्य वसिष्ठस्य महात्मन: । त्रैलोक्यमोहनं रौद्रं रूपमासीत्सुदारुणम् । । 15617 । ।
ramayan::1493.verse_hindi: While swallowing Brahmastra  the great Vasishta looked fierce and  terrible causing the three worlds to faint.
ramayan::1493.english_translation: While swallowing the Brahmastra, the great Vasishta looked fierce and terrible, and the three worlds were left stunned.
ramayan::1493.translation_literal: ब्रह्मास्त्रं (Brahmastra) / ग्रसमानस्य (of swallowing) / वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / महात्मन: (of the great-souled one) / त्रैलोक्यमोहनं (bewildering the three worlds) / रौद्रं (fierce) / रूपमासीत् (there was a form) / सुदारुणम् (very terrible)
ramayan::1493.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1493.essence: Containing great force can make the protector look terrible.
ramayan::1493.simple_meaning: Vasishta's power became so intense while absorbing the weapon that even the three worlds were shaken by his terrible form.
ramayan::1493.simple_insight: Great power can look frightening even when it is being used to restore balance.
ramayan::1493.detailed_meaning: The two celestial weapons have already been raised, and even the gods are alarmed. Vasishta now absorbs the Brahmastra through his own spiritual force, and the strain of that act makes him appear terrifying enough to unsettle all creation.
ramayan::1493.modern_relevance: You may be the calm person in the room while handling something explosive. The effort to contain chaos can make you look harsh, even when you are protecting everyone else.
ramayan::1493.insight: It shifts attention from the weapon itself to the cost of containing it.

ramayan::1494.verse_sanskrit: रोमकूपेषु सर्वेषु वसिष्ठस्य महात्मन: । मरीच्य इव निष्पेतुरग्नेर्धूमाकुलार्चिष: । । 15618 । ।
ramayan::1494.verse_hindi: From every pore of the great Vasishtas body flames resembling rays of light with smoke emerged.
ramayan::1494.english_translation: From every pore of the great Vasishta's body, flames like smoky rays burst forth.
ramayan::1494.translation_literal: रोमकूपेषु (in the pores of the body) / सर्वेषु (in all) / वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / मरीच्यः इव (like rays) / निष्पेतुः (burst forth) / अग्नेः (of fire) / धूमाकुल-अर्चिषः (with smoke-filled flames)
ramayan::1494.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1494.essence: His power is shown through fire, not explanation.
ramayan::1494.simple_meaning: Vasishta's body blazed so intensely that flames and smoke seemed to pour from every pore.
ramayan::1494.simple_insight: Some moments are too powerful to describe normally — even the body seems to become fire.
ramayan::1494.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just swallowed the terrifying Brahmastra with his own Brahma-powered staff. The force of that act is so immense that his body erupts with fiery radiance, showing the scale of the sage's spiritual power rather than offering a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1494.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when someone absorbs a crisis without flinching. The pressure is still there, but their presence makes it look small.
ramayan::1494.insight: It adds visual force to the sage's power, but it does not shift the reader into a new teaching.

ramayan::1495.verse_sanskrit: प्राज्वलद्ब्रह्मदण्डश्च वसिष्ठस्य करोद्यत: । विधूम इव कालाग्निर्यमदण्ड इवापर: । । 15619 । ।
ramayan::1495.verse_hindi: The staff of Brahma in Vasishtas hand, resembling smokeless fire at the end of the dissolution of the worlds inflamed like another rod of death.
ramayan::1495.english_translation: The staff of Brahma in Vasishta's hand blazed like smokeless fire at the end of the world, like another rod of death.
ramayan::1495.translation_literal: प्राज्वलत् (blazed) / ब्रह्मदण्डः (Brahma's staff) / च (and) / वसिष्ठस्य (of Vasishta) / कर-उद्यतः (raised in his hand) / विधूमः इव (like smokeless) / कालाग्निः (the fire of dissolution) / यमदण्डः इव (like Yama's rod) / अपरः (another) ।
ramayan::1495.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1495.essence: Hidden restraint can blaze like cosmic destruction when fully revealed.
ramayan::1495.simple_meaning: Vasishta's raised staff flares with immense, destructive power, like cosmic fire and the staff of death.
ramayan::1495.simple_insight: Some power is so overwhelming it feels larger than any human conflict.
ramayan::1495.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just swallowed the Brahmastra and revealed a terrifying force within himself. His raised staff now burns like the fire that ends worlds, shocking everyone present. This verse intensifies the scene before the sages begin praising his power.
ramayan::1495.modern_relevance: A calm person suddenly reveals a force you never expected — and everyone in the room goes silent. Some restraint hides a power that, once released, changes the atmosphere instantly.
ramayan::1495.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to the latent force hidden beneath it.

ramayan::1496.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽस्तुवन् मुनिगणा वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम् । अमोघं ते बलं ब्रह्मन् तेजो धारय तेजसा । । 15620 । ।
ramayan::1496.verse_hindi: Then hosts of saints praised Vasishta, the best among sages, saying O Brahmin, your energy is infallible, hold your energy by your enegy.
ramayan::1496.english_translation: Then the hosts of sages praised Vasishta, best among those who recite prayers: “Brahmin, your power is unfailing. Hold your radiance with your own radiance.”
ramayan::1496.translation_literal: तत: (then) / अस्तुवन् (praised) / मुनिगणा (hosts of sages) / वसिष्ठम् (Vasishta) / जपताम् (among those who recite prayers) / वरम् (best) / अमोघम् (unfailing) / ते (your) / बलम् (power) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahmin) / तेजः (radiance) / धारय (hold) / तेजसा (with radiance)
ramayan::1496.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1496.simple_meaning: The sages praise Vasishta after seeing his immense force, and ask him to contain that power with his own radiance.
ramayan::1496.simple_insight: Real strength can be vast, but it still needs restraint.
ramayan::1496.detailed_meaning: Vasishta has just revealed a terrifying spiritual force against Vishvamitra. Seeing that blazing power, the assembled sages stop the conflict by praising him and begging him to contain it. The verse is part of their plea, not the main teaching itself.
ramayan::1496.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after a sharp exchange, and everyone feels the heat still hanging in the air. What matters next is not who won the moment, but who can steady the force they unleashed.
ramayan::1496.insight: It shifts attention from raw power to the discipline needed to hold it.

ramayan::1497.verse_sanskrit: निगृहीतस्त्वया ब्रह्मन् विश्वामित्रो महातपा: । प्रसीद जपतां श्रेष्ठ लोकास्सन्तु गतव्यथा: । । 15621 । ।
ramayan::1497.verse_hindi: O Brahman great ascetic Viswamitra was controlled by you. O Best of ascetics be
ramayan::1497.english_translation: O Brahman, the great ascetic Viswamitra was restrained by you. Be gracious, best of those who recite, and let the worlds be free of distress.
ramayan::1497.translation_literal: निगृहीतस्त्वया (restrained by you) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahman) / विश्वामित्रो (Viswamitra) / महातपा: (great ascetic) / प्रसीद (be gracious) / जपतां (of those who recite) / श्रेष्ठ (best) / लोकास्सन्तु (let the worlds be) / गतव्यथा: (free of distress)
ramayan::1497.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1497.essence: Even righteous power must know when to stop.
ramayan::1497.simple_meaning: The sages praise Vasishta for overpowering Viswamitra, then ask him to calm down so the world can be free of fear.
ramayan::1497.simple_insight: Power is not only in force; it is in knowing when to let the conflict end.
ramayan::1497.detailed_meaning: After Vasishta's blazing staff stops Viswamitra's assault, the gathered sages praise Vasishta's force and then urge him to soften. The moment is still part of the clash between two great ascetics, and the world itself hangs in the balance.
ramayan::1497.modern_relevance: A family argument has already escalated past reason, and everyone in the room is waiting for the first person to lower their voice. Real strength now is ending the spiral, not winning the last point.
ramayan::1497.insight: It shifts attention from victory to restoration: the aim is to end harm, not prolong dominance.

ramayan::1498.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो महातेजाश्शमं चक्रे महातपा: । विश्वामित्रोऽपि निकृतो विनिश्वस्येदमब्रवीत् । । 15622 । ।
ramayan::1498.verse_hindi: At this, Vasishta the most brilliant ascetic became quiet. The humiliated Viswamitra heaved a sigh and spoke these words:
ramayan::1498.english_translation: At this, Vasishta the most brilliant ascetic became quiet. The humiliated Viswamitra heaved a sigh and spoke these words:
ramayan::1498.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus spoken to) / महातेजाः (most brilliant) / शमं (into calm) / चक्रे (made) / महातपाः (great ascetic) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / अपि (also) / निकृतः (humiliated) / विनिश्वस्य (having sighed) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1498.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1498.essence: Defeat lands first as silence, then as speech.
ramayan::1498.simple_meaning: Vasishta falls silent after the praise, and Viswamitra, humbled, sighs before speaking again.
ramayan::1498.simple_insight: Even victory can leave a person shaken and quiet.
ramayan::1498.detailed_meaning: The sages have just praised Vasishta for overpowering Viswamitra. Vasishta falls silent, and Viswamitra, defeated and humiliated, breathes out before answering. The verse is a bridge into his next admission.
ramayan::1498.modern_relevance: You lose the argument in a room full of witnesses, and your chest tightens before you can speak. The silence after humiliation says as much as the words that follow.
ramayan::1498.insight: It marks the emotional pause before Viswamitra turns defeat into a new confession.

ramayan::1499.verse_sanskrit: धिग्बलं क्षत्रियबलं ब्रह्मतेजो बलं बलम् । एकेन ब्रह्मदण्डेन सर्वास्त्राणि हतानि मे । । 15623 । ।
ramayan::1499.verse_hindi: Shame Where is the might of a kshatriya? The energy of a brahmin is the real  energy. The staff of Brahma has singly destroyed all my weapons.
ramayan::1499.english_translation: Shame! Where is the might of a kshatriya? The energy of a brahmin is the real power. The staff of Brahma has alone destroyed all my weapons.
ramayan::1499.translation_literal: धिग् (shame) / बलम् (might) / क्षत्रियबलम् (the might of a kshatriya) / ब्रह्मतेजः (brahmin energy) / बलम् (power) / बलम् (power) / एकेन (by one) / ब्रह्मदण्डेन (with the staff of Brahma) / सर्वास्त्राणि (all weapons) / हतानि (destroyed) / मे (my)
ramayan::1499.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1499.essence: Brute strength collapses before disciplined inner power.
ramayan::1499.simple_meaning: Viswamitra realises that ordinary warrior strength is powerless against spiritual force. His weapons have been defeated by the staff of Brahma, and that humiliation changes how he sees power.
ramayan::1499.simple_insight: Humiliation can become clarity when it strips away false confidence.
ramayan::1499.detailed_meaning: After Vasishta’s calm defeats his attack, Viswamitra stands shaken. His weapons are useless against the staff of Brahma, and the proud warrior suddenly sees that disciplined inner force outruns brute force. That shock turns him toward penance.
ramayan::1499.modern_relevance: You prepared the perfect comeback, and then one quiet sentence exposed how fragile your whole posture was. The moment stings — but it can also reveal what is actually strong.
ramayan::1499.insight: It shifts the mind from external power to the deeper force that cannot be overpowered by force alone.

ramayan::1500.verse_sanskrit: तदेतत्समवेक्ष्याहं प्रसन्नेन्द्रियमानस: । तपो महत्समास्थास्ये यद्वै ब्रह्मत्वकारणम् । । 15624 । ।
ramayan::1500.verse_hindi: Now I have realised the reason. With clear mind and senses, I shall undertake intense penance which will earn me brahminhood.
ramayan::1500.english_translation: Now I have understood the reason. With a calm mind and senses, I will undertake great penance that will bring me brahminhood.
ramayan::1500.translation_literal: तत् एतत् (this) / समवेक्ष्य (having understood) / अहम् (I) / प्रसन्न-इन्द्रिय-मानसः (with calm senses and mind) / तपः (penance) / महत् (great) / समास्थास्ये (will undertake) / यत् (which) / वै (indeed) / ब्रह्मत्व-कारणम् (the cause of brahminhood)
ramayan::1500.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1500.essence: Defeat becomes fuel when you answer it with disciplined effort.
ramayan::1500.simple_meaning: Viswamitra sees the cause of his defeat and decides to answer it with intense penance, keeping his mind and senses calm.
ramayan::1500.simple_insight: Setbacks can become a turning point when you respond with discipline instead of resentment.
ramayan::1500.detailed_meaning: After Vasishta has defeated him, Viswamitra stands humbled. Instead of clinging to anger, he sees what he lacks and resolves to undertake severe penance. This is the moment he turns humiliation into a new path.
ramayan::1500.modern_relevance: You get corrected in front of everyone, and your first impulse is to defend yourself. But one honest look at the failure can turn embarrassment into a training ground.
ramayan::1500.insight: It shifts the mind from wounded pride to deliberate self-transformation.

ramayan::1501.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सन्तप्तहृदय: स्मरन्निग्रहमात्मन: । विनिश्श्वस्य विनिश्श्वस्य कृतवैरो महत्मना । । 1571 । । स दक्षिणां दिशं गत्वा महिष्या सह राघव । तताप परमं घोरं विश्वामित्रो महत्तप: । । 1572 । । फलमूलाशनो दान्तश्चकार सुमहत्तप: ।
ramayan::1501.verse_hindi: O Descendant of Raghu (Rama) having created enmity between himself and the magnanimous Vasishta, Viswamitra recollecting the disgrace and repeatedly sighing with a distressed heart  went with his eldest wife towards southern quarter to perform  rigorous penance. Subsisting on fruits and roots and his senses underfull control he performed the most rigid austerities.
ramayan::1501.english_translation: Then, heart-sick and remembering how he had been restrained by his own self-control, the great-souled Viswamitra, repeatedly sighing, went south with his wife and performed a terrible penance. Living on fruits and roots and keeping his senses under control, he undertook severe austerities.
ramayan::1501.translation_literal: ततस्सन्तप्तहृदयः (then, with a heart burned with grief) / स्मरन्निग्रहम् (remembering restraint) / आत्मनः (of himself) / विनिश्श्वस्य विनिश्श्वस्य (sighing again and again) / कृतवैरो (having made an enemy) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one) / सः (he) / दक्षिणां दिशम् (the southern direction) / गत्वा (having gone) / महिष्या सह (with his wife) / राघव (O Rama) / तताप (performed austerity) / परमम् (supreme) / घोरम् (terrible) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महत्तपः (great penance) / फलमूलाशनः (eating fruits and roots) / दान्तः (self-controlled) / चकार (did) / सुमहत्तपः (very great austerity)
ramayan::1501.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1501.essence: Wounded pride becomes strength only when it is disciplined.
ramayan::1501.simple_meaning: Viswamitra feels the cost of his conflict with Vasishta, but he does not collapse. He leaves, controls his senses, lives simply, and turns his pain into severe discipline.
ramayan::1501.simple_insight: Pain does not have to scatter you; it can be gathered into practice.
ramayan::1501.detailed_meaning: After his clash with Vasishta, Viswamitra is shaken and ashamed. He leaves with his wife, goes south, and answers wounded pride with severe penance. The verse shows the moment hurt becomes disciplined transformation.
ramayan::1501.modern_relevance: You get cut off in traffic, replay the insult all evening, and feel the heat rise again. Viswamitra shows another response: let the hurt sharpen your practice instead of your anger.
ramayan::1501.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to injury toward using injury as fuel for restraint.

ramayan::1502.verse_sanskrit: अथास्य जज्ञिरे पुत्रास्सत्यधर्मपरायणा: । हविष्यन्दो मधुष्यन्दो दृढनेत्रो महारथ: । । 1573 । ।
ramayan::1502.verse_hindi: After some time, four sons, Havishyanda, Madhushyanda, Drudhanetra and Maharatha, who (later) wer wedded to truth and duty, were born.
ramayan::1502.english_translation: After some time, four sons were born to him: Havishyanda, Madhushyanda, Drudhanetra, and Maharatha, men devoted to truth and dharma.
ramayan::1502.translation_literal: अथ (then) / अस्य (his) / जज्ञिरे (were born) / पुत्राः (sons) / सत्यधर्मपरायणाः (devoted to truth and dharma) / हविष्यन्दः (Havishyanda) / मधुष्यन्दः (Madhushyanda) / दृढनेत्रः (Drudhanetra) / महारथः (Maharatha)
ramayan::1502.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1502.essence: His long discipline is reflected in the character of his sons.
ramayan::1502.simple_meaning: Viswamitra eventually had four sons, and they were known for living by truth and duty.
ramayan::1502.simple_insight: A life shaped by discipline leaves its mark even in the next generation.
ramayan::1502.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been pursuing severe penance to transform himself. After that long effort, his four sons are born. The verse simply records the result of that austerity before Brahma appears in the next line.
ramayan::1502.modern_relevance: You work for years to become steadier, kinder, and less reactive. Then one day you notice the people around you are living inside the standard you kept.
ramayan::1502.insight: It shows how sustained inner discipline can shape a family line, not just a single life.

ramayan::1503.verse_sanskrit: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु ब्रह्मा लोकपितामह: । अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम् । । 1574 । ।
ramayan::1503.verse_hindi: A thousand years passed. The Grandsire of the worlds, Brahma, appeared. He spoke to Viswamitra, the great ascetic, these pleasant words:
ramayan::1503.english_translation: A thousand years passed. Brahma, the Grandsire of the worlds, spoke these gentle words to the great ascetic Vishwamitra.
ramayan::1503.translation_literal: पूर्णे (completed) / वर्षसहस्रे (thousand years) / तु (indeed) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / लोकपितामहः (Grandsire of the worlds) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / मधुरम् (sweet) / वाक्यम् (words) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Vishwamitra) / तपोधनम् (wealthy in austerity)
ramayan::1503.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1503.essence: Enduring effort can end in recognition.
ramayan::1503.simple_meaning: After a thousand years of austerity, Brahma appears and speaks kindly to Vishwamitra.
ramayan::1503.simple_insight: Long effort can ripen into recognition.
ramayan::1503.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has endured a thousand years of severe tapas. At last, Brahma, the creator and elder of the worlds, appears and addresses him gently. The verse is a turning point, but only as the prelude to Brahma’s fuller blessing in the next line.
ramayan::1503.modern_relevance: You keep showing up when no one is applauding. Then, one day, the thing you’ve been building quietly finally gets named.
ramayan::1503.insight: It marks the moment discipline begins to receive its fruit and confirmation.

ramayan::1504.verse_sanskrit: चिता राजर्षिलोकास्ते तपसा कुशिकात्मज । अनेन तपसा त्वां तु राजर्षिरिति विद्महे । । 1575 । ।
ramayan::1504.verse_hindi: O Son of Kushika with your austerities you have won the worlds of the rajarshis. On account of your austerities, you are acknowledged a rajarshi.
ramayan::1504.english_translation: O Son of Kushika, by your austerities you have won the worlds of the rajarshis. Because of this austerity, we know you as a rajarshi.
ramayan::1504.translation_literal: चिताः (won) / राजर्षिलोकाः (the worlds of the royal sages) / ते (your) / तपसा (by austerity) / कुशिकात्मज (O son of Kushika) / अनेन (by this) / तपसा (austerity) / त्वाम् (you) / तु (indeed) / राजर्षिः इति (as a royal sage) / विद्महे (we know)
ramayan::1504.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1504.essence: Austerity can elevate you until even the highest recognize your worth.
ramayan::1504.simple_meaning: Through long austerity, Viswamitra has earned the status of a royal sage. His effort has transformed how even the highest beings recognize him.
ramayan::1504.simple_insight: Real change is not claimed; it is earned until others can see it too.
ramayan::1504.detailed_meaning: Brahma appears after Viswamitra's thousand-year austerity and names the result aloud. The struggle is over, and the ascetic who began as a king is now publicly recognized as a rajarshi. This is the turning point where effort becomes identity.
ramayan::1504.modern_relevance: You kept showing up when nobody was clapping, and slowly the work changed your reputation, your habits, and your sense of self.
ramayan::1504.insight: It teaches you that sustained discipline can remake your standing and your identity over time.

ramayan::1505.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा जगाम सह दैवतै: । त्रिविष्टपं ब्रह्मलोकं लोकानां परमेश्वर: । । 1576 । ।
ramayan::1505.verse_hindi: Having said this the glorious (Brahma), supreme lord of the worlds, left for his abode
ramayan::1505.english_translation: Having said this, the glorious Brahma, supreme lord of the worlds, departed with the other radiant beings for the highest heaven, Brahma's realm.
ramayan::1505.translation_literal: एवमुक्त्वा (having said thus) / महातेजा (the greatly radiant one) / जगाम (departed) / सह (together with) / दैवतैः (the radiant beings) / त्रिविष्टपं (to the threefold heaven) / ब्रह्मलोकं (Brahma's realm) / लोकानां (of the worlds) / परमेश्वरः (the supreme lord)
ramayan::1505.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1505.essence: The blessing is complete; the speaker departs, and the silence begins.
ramayan::1505.simple_meaning: Brahma finishes speaking to Viswamitra and returns to his own realm with the radiant beings.
ramayan::1505.simple_insight: Some moments close not with resolution, but with a higher voice moving on.
ramayan::1505.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just acknowledged Viswamitra's immense austerity and granted him a new standing among the seers. After speaking, he leaves with the radiant beings for Brahma's realm. The verse is a transition, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1505.modern_relevance: A meeting ends, the senior person stands up, and the room is left with the weight of what was just said. The real impact lands only after the speaker has gone.
ramayan::1505.insight: It marks the close of Brahma's blessing and the shift back to Viswamitra's inner response.
