ramayan::1553.translation_literal: ते (those) / च (and) / शिष्या: (disciples) / समागम्य (having gathered together) / मुनिं (to the sage) / ज्वलिततेजसम् (of blazing splendour) / ऊचु: (said) / च (and) / वचनं (the words) / सर्वे (all) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / ब्रह्मवादिनाम् (of the expounders of the Vedas)
ramayan::1553.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1553.essence: The message returns; the real decision still lies ahead.
ramayan::1553.simple_meaning: The disciples returned and told the radiant sage what the Vedic scholars had said.
ramayan::1553.simple_insight: Some moments matter only because they move the larger story forward.
ramayan::1553.detailed_meaning: The sage had sent his disciples out to gather learned brahmins. They return to him and report the replies they received. The verse is a bridge in the scene, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1553.modern_relevance: You wait for news after sending people in different directions, and all you get back is a report that changes what happens next.
ramayan::1553.insight: It marks the relay of information, not a settled conclusion.

ramayan::1554.verse_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा ते वचनं सर्वे समायान्ति द्विजातय: । सर्वदेशेषु चागच्छन् वर्जयित्वा महोदयम् । । 15911 । ।
ramayan::1554.verse_hindi: Having heard your words, all brahmins except Mahodaya have arrived from all countries.
ramayan::1554.english_translation: Having heard your words, all brahmins except Mahodaya have arrived from all countries.
ramayan::1554.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) / ते (your) / वचनं (words) / सर्वे (all) / समायान्ति (have arrived) / द्विजातय: (twice-born ones, brahmins) / सर्वदेशेषु (from all countries) / च (and) / आगच्छन् (came) / वर्जयित्वा (excepting) / महोदयम् (Mahodaya)
ramayan::1554.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1554.essence: The summons has worked, but one figure still remains absent.
ramayan::1554.simple_meaning: Brahmins came from every region after hearing the invitation, except Mahodaya.
ramayan::1554.simple_insight: Some calls reach almost everyone, but one person can still remain absent.
ramayan::1554.detailed_meaning: The sage’s messengers have gone out, and learned brahmins are now arriving from across the land. The only exception is Mahodaya. This verse is a report of who has come, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1554.modern_relevance: You send the message, and people start showing up from everywhere. Still, one important person may stay away for reasons you cannot control.
ramayan::1554.insight: It marks the gathering of witnesses before the next stage of the story.

ramayan::1555.verse_sanskrit: वासिष्ठं तच्छतं सर्वं क्रोधपर्याकुलाक्षरम् । यदाह वचनं सर्वं शृणु त्वं मुनिपुङ्गव । । 15912 । ।
ramayan::1555.verse_hindi: O Preeminent among ascetics Here is what the hundred sons of Vasishta spoke in anger.
ramayan::1555.english_translation: O preeminent among ascetics, hear all that the hundred sons of Vasishta said, their words shaken by anger.
ramayan::1555.translation_literal: वासिष्ठम् (of Vasishta) / तत् (that) / शतम् (hundred) / सर्वम् (all) / क्रोध-पर्याकुल-अक्षरम् (words agitated by anger) / यत् (what) / आह (said) / वचनम् (speech) / सर्वम् (all) / शृणु (hear) / त्वम् (you) / मुनि-पुङ्गव (O best of sages)
ramayan::1555.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1555.essence: Anger has already entered the words before the argument begins.
ramayan::1555.simple_meaning: The speaker asks a sage to listen to the angry words spoken by Vasishta's hundred sons.
ramayan::1555.simple_insight: Anger can distort even learned speech into something sharp and unreliable.
ramayan::1555.detailed_meaning: The sages have gathered around a heated dispute. A report is being passed along: Vasishta's hundred sons have spoken in anger, and their words now need to be heard as part of the larger argument about sacrifice and conduct.
ramayan::1555.modern_relevance: You hear the message after the argument has already turned bitter. The facts may still matter, but the tone has begun to poison them.
ramayan::1555.insight: It shifts attention from the content of speech to the state of mind behind it.

ramayan::1556.verse_sanskrit: क्षत्रियो याजको यस्य चण्डालस्य विशेषत: । कथं सदसि भोक्तारो हविस्तस्य सुरर्षय: । । 15913 । ।
ramayan::1556.verse_hindi: When a kshatriya acts as a priest for the sacrifice, particularly for a chandala, how can gods and sages partake the offerings?
ramayan::1556.english_translation: When a kshatriya acts as a priest for the sacrifice, particularly for a chandala, how can gods and sages partake the offerings?
ramayan::1556.translation_literal: क्षत्रियः (a kshatriya) / याजकः (a priest) / यस्य (whose) / चण्डालस्य (of a chandala) / विशेषत: (especially) / कथम् (how) / सदसि (in the assembly) / भोक्तारः (partakers) / हविः (offering) / तस्य (of that) / सुरर्षयः (gods and sages)
ramayan::1556.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1556.essence: Prejudice can make even sacred offerings seem unacceptable.
ramayan::1556.simple_meaning: The speaker questions whether sacred offerings can remain pure when the ritual is performed by someone seen as unfit, especially for a person of low status.
ramayan::1556.simple_insight: Social judgment can poison even a sacred act in the eyes of those who cling to status.
ramayan::1556.detailed_meaning: Vasishta’s sons are attacking Viswamitra’s conduct after hearing how he accepted and protected people they despise. Their criticism turns to ritual purity: they argue that if a kshatriya serves as priest for a sacrifice involving a chandala, even gods and sages should not accept the offering.
ramayan::1556.modern_relevance: A group chat decides someone is “not the right fit,” and suddenly every contribution they make gets treated as tainted. The verse shows how quickly status anxiety can corrupt judgment.
ramayan::1556.insight: It exposes how prejudice can distort moral and ritual reasoning, turning exclusion into a supposed principle.

ramayan::1557.verse_sanskrit: ब्राह्मणा वा महात्मानो भुक्त्वा चण्डालभोजनम् । कथं स्वर्गं गमिष्यन्ति विश्वामित्रेण पालिता: । । 15914 । ।
ramayan::1557.verse_hindi: Joining Viswamitra, (in chanting the mantras during the yaga) how will the great brahmins attain heaven after partaking the food offered by of Chandala?
ramayan::1557.english_translation: How will the great brahmins, fed on food offered by a chandala while protected by Vishvamitra, attain heaven?
ramayan::1557.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणा: (brahmins) / वा (or) / महात्मान: (great-souled) / भुक्त्वा (having eaten) / चण्डालभोजनम् (food of a chandala) / कथम् (how) / स्वर्गम् (heaven) / गमिष्यन्ति (will go) / विश्वामित्रेण (by Vishvamitra) / पालिता: (protected)
ramayan::1557.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1557.essence: Their anger turns ritual purity into a way to shame others.
ramayan::1557.simple_meaning: The sons of Vasishta mock Vishvamitra by saying that brahmins who eat food from a chandala cannot reach heaven.
ramayan::1557.simple_insight: Anger can twist people into judging purity more harshly than character.
ramayan::1557.detailed_meaning: Vasishta's sons are still attacking Vishvamitra after the dispute over the sacrifice. In their anger, they insult both him and the brahmins associated with him, claiming that sharing food from a chandala has ruined their spiritual standing.
ramayan::1557.modern_relevance: A group chat turns cruel after one person is blamed, and suddenly everyone is measuring who is clean enough, worthy enough, acceptable enough.
ramayan::1557.insight: It exposes how resentment turns moral language into a weapon.

ramayan::1558.verse_sanskrit: एतद्वचननैष्ठुर्यमूचु स्संरक्तलोचना: । वासिष्ठा मुनिशार्दूल सर्वे ते समहोदया: । । 15915 । ।
ramayan::1558.verse_hindi: O Best among ascetics all the sons of Vasishta along with Mahodaya with their eyes reddened in anger spoke these harsh words:
ramayan::1558.english_translation: O best among ascetics, all the sons of Vasishta, along with Mahodaya, their eyes reddened in anger, spoke these harsh words.
ramayan::1558.translation_literal: एतद् (this) / वचन (speech) / नैष्ठुर्यम् (harshness) / ऊचुः (spoke) / संरक्त-लोचनाः (with reddened eyes) / वासिष्ठाः (the sons of Vasishta) / मुनि-शार्दूल (O tiger among ascetics) / सर्वे (all) / ते (they) / सम-ओदयाः (together with Mahodaya)
ramayan::1558.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1558.essence: Anger speaks first, and wisdom is pushed aside.
ramayan::1558.simple_meaning: Vasishta’s sons, furious and red-eyed, answered Viswamitra with harsh words.
ramayan::1558.simple_insight: Anger makes even learned people speak beneath themselves.
ramayan::1558.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just challenged the insult around the sacrifice. Now Vasishta’s sons, including Mahodaya, flare up together and answer with contempt. The verse is not the teaching itself, only the charged moment before Viswamitra responds.
ramayan::1558.modern_relevance: A group chat turns sharp after one comment crosses a line. Everyone starts defending status instead of hearing the issue. This verse captures the instant anger takes over the room.
ramayan::1558.insight: It shows how quickly wounded pride turns a disagreement into hostility.

ramayan::1559.verse_sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां मुनिपुङ्गव: । क्रोधसंरक्तनयन स्सरोषमिदमब्रवीत् । । 15916 । ।
ramayan::1559.verse_hindi: On hearing the words (of the hundred sons of Vasishta uttered in anger) Viswamitra, preeminent among ascetics, spoke furiously with eyes reddened in anger.
ramayan::1559.english_translation: On hearing the angry words of all of them, the great sage Viswamitra spoke back in fury, his eyes red with anger.
ramayan::1559.translation_literal: तेषाम् (of them) / तद्वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / मुनिपुङ्गवः (foremost among sages) / क्रोधसंरक्तनयनः (with eyes reddened by anger) / सः (he) / रोषम् (in anger) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1559.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1559.essence: Humiliation can ignite even the disciplined mind.
ramayan::1559.simple_meaning: Viswamitra hears the insult and answers in anger. The verse shows the moment his restraint breaks.
ramayan::1559.simple_insight: Even a great sage can be wounded by contempt.
ramayan::1559.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has brought the sacrifice into danger by defending his authority and the value of his penance. After the sons of Vasishta mock him, he turns on them in anger. This verse is the breath before his curse.
ramayan::1559.modern_relevance: You hear the group chat turn cruel about you, and your chest tightens before you type back. The reaction comes fast when respect has been denied.
ramayan::1559.insight: It shows how quickly injury becomes retaliation when pride is touched.

ramayan::1560.verse_sanskrit: ये दूषयन्त्यदुष्टं मां तप उग्रं समास्थितम् । भस्मीभूता दुरात्मानो भविष्यन्ति न संशय: । । 15917 । ।
ramayan::1560.verse_hindi: I am blameless. I have practised rigorous penance. These wicked ones who have abused (a sage like me) will be reduced to ashes.
ramayan::1560.english_translation: Those who abuse me, though I am blameless and have practised severe penance, will surely be reduced to ashes.
ramayan::1560.translation_literal: ये (those who) / दूषयन्ति (abuse) / अदुष्टं (blameless) / माम् (me) / तपः (penance) / उग्रम् (severe) / समास्थितम् (practising) / भस्मीभूताः (turned to ashes) / दुरात्मानः (wicked ones) / भविष्यन्ति (will become) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::1560.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1560.essence: Severe discipline gives even silence a dangerous weight.
ramayan::1560.simple_meaning: A sage says he has done nothing wrong, yet anyone who insults him after such intense penance will face terrible consequences.
ramayan::1560.simple_insight: Deep practice changes your power; not every attack can land the same way.
ramayan::1560.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just heard the sons of Vasishta insult him in anger. Standing before their words, he answers not with apology but with the authority earned through fierce penance. The next verse shows the curse that follows.
ramayan::1560.modern_relevance: You have done the hard, private work for months, and someone still talks to you like you are nothing. The verse remembers that discipline changes the ground beneath your feet.
ramayan::1560.insight: It shifts attention from insult to earned inner force.

ramayan::1561.verse_sanskrit: अद्य ते कालपाशेन नीता वैवस्वतक्षयम् । सप्तजातिशतान्येव मृतपस्सन्तु सर्वश: । । 15918 । ।
ramayan::1561.verse_hindi: Caught by the noose of death this day, they shall be brought  to the abode of Yama  and for seven hundred births, feed on corpses.
ramayan::1561.english_translation: Caught by the noose of death this day, they shall be brought to the abode of Yama, and for seven hundred births they shall feed on corpses.
ramayan::1561.translation_literal: अद्य (today) / ते (they) / कालपाशेन (by the noose of death) / नीता (led) / वैवस्वतक्षयम् (to the abode of Yama) / सप्तजातिशतानि (seven hundred births) / एव (indeed) / मृतपः (corpse-eaters) / सन्तु (let them be) / सर्वशः (in every way)
ramayan::1561.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1561.essence: Anger now becomes suffering for many lives ahead.
ramayan::1561.simple_meaning: Viswamitra curses the hostile sons of Vasishta: they will die now, go to Yama's realm, and be reborn for many lives as corpse-eaters.
ramayan::1561.simple_insight: Anger can turn a moment into a long chain of ruin.
ramayan::1561.detailed_meaning: After the sons of Vasishta insult Viswamitra, the sage's restraint breaks. He answers their abuse with a terrible curse, sending them to death and miserable rebirths. The verse is part of that escalating curse, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::1561.modern_relevance: A furious message sent in five seconds can reshape years of consequences. Words spoken in heat can outlive the argument that triggered them.
ramayan::1561.insight: It shows how unchecked anger escalates from insult to irreversible harm.

ramayan::1562.verse_sanskrit: श्वमांसनियताहारा मुष्टिका नाम निर्घृणा: । विकृताश्च विरूपाश्च लोकाननुचरन्त्विमान् । । 15919 । ।
ramayan::1562.verse_hindi: Reborn as the merciless race of mushtikas, feeding on the flesh of dogs, hideous and deformed, they shall wander in these worlds.
ramayan::1562.english_translation: Reborn as the merciless race of mushtikas, feeding on the flesh of dogs, hideous and deformed, they shall wander in these worlds.
ramayan::1562.translation_literal: श्वमांस-नियताहारा (whose food is fixed as dog-flesh) / मुष्टिका नाम (named mushtikas) / निर्घृणा: (merciless) / विकृताः (distorted) / च (and) / विरूपाः (deformed) / च (and) / लोकान् (the worlds) / अनुचरन्तु (let them wander) / इमान् (these)
ramayan::1562.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1562.essence: Cruel speech tries to make the wound permanent.
ramayan::1562.simple_meaning: The speaker curses the offenders to be reborn as a cruel, ugly race that survives on dog meat and wanders the world.
ramayan::1562.simple_insight: Hurt pride turns into a harsh curse, showing how quickly anger can deform judgment.
ramayan::1562.detailed_meaning: A furious sage has already declared punishment for those who insulted him. This verse adds the specific form of that curse: they will be reborn among the mushtikas, marked by cruelty and deformity, condemned to roam the world in shame.
ramayan::1562.modern_relevance: After a humiliating argument, you can feel the urge to say something cruel enough to leave a scar. This verse shows how vengeance tries to make suffering mirror the wound.
ramayan::1562.insight: It shows how anger seeks matching punishment instead of measured justice.

ramayan::1563.verse_sanskrit: महोदयस्तु दुर्बुद्धिर्मामदूष्यं ह्यदूषयत् । दूषित स्सर्वलोकेषु निषादत्वं गमिष्यति । । 15920 । ।
ramayan::1563.verse_hindi: The wicked Mahodaya, who blamed a sage like me so faultless shall be reborn in the race of the nishadas vulnerable to abuse by all.
ramayan::1563.english_translation: The wicked Mahodaya, who blamed a faultless sage like me, will be reborn in the Nishada race, where others will treat him with contempt.
ramayan::1563.translation_literal: महोदयः (Mahodaya) / तु (but) / दुर्बुद्धिः (foolish-minded, wicked) / माम् (me) / अदूष्यम् (faultless, blameless) / हि (indeed) / अदूषयत् (he defiled, blamed) / दूषितः (defiled) / सर्वलोकेषु (among all people) / निषादत्वम् (Nishada status/race) / गमिष्यति (will go, will be reborn into)
ramayan::1563.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1563.essence: False blame returns as a life of public contempt.
ramayan::1563.simple_meaning: Mahodaya insulted a faultless sage, so he will be reborn into a lowly condition where others treat him badly.
ramayan::1563.simple_insight: Cruel speech and false blame return as a life marked by humiliation.
ramayan::1563.detailed_meaning: A sage is pronouncing the consequences of wrongdoing. Mahodaya has blamed someone who was blameless, and the curse is specific: he will fall into the Nishada race and live under public contempt. The verse is one link in a larger chain of punishment.
ramayan::1563.modern_relevance: You spread blame in a group chat and think it disappears. It doesn't. Words that stain someone else can come back and stain your own life.
ramayan::1563.insight: It turns careless accusation into a cause with lasting consequences.

ramayan::1564.verse_sanskrit: प्राणातिपातनिरतो निरनुक्रोशतां गत: । दीर्घकालं मम क्रोधाद्दुर्गतिं वर्तयिष्यति । । 15921 । ।
ramayan::1564.verse_hindi: As a consequence of my anger that Mahodaya, devoid of mercy and  taking pleasure in depriving others of their life, will pursue a wretched life for a long time.
ramayan::1564.english_translation: As a consequence of my anger, that Mahodaya, devoid of mercy and taking pleasure in depriving others of their life, will pursue a wretched life for a long time.
ramayan::1564.translation_literal: प्राणातिपातनिरतः (devoted to taking life) / निरनुक्रोशतां (to mercilessness) / गतः (gone) / दीर्घकालं (for a long time) / मम (of my) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / दुर्गतिं (wretched state) / वर्तयिष्यति (will undergo)
ramayan::1564.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1564.essence: Anger can keep cruelty alive far beyond the moment that sparked it.
ramayan::1564.simple_meaning: Violent cruelty and anger do not end quickly; they drag a person into a long, miserable state.
ramayan::1564.simple_insight: It leaves you wary of anger’s long shadow, not just its immediate heat.
ramayan::1564.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just pronounced punishments on the arrogant Mahodaya and the others who insulted him. Here he explains that Mahodaya’s cruelty and his own anger will bind that man to a miserable existence for a long time.
ramayan::1564.modern_relevance: You send one furious message and feel relief for ten seconds. Then the resentment keeps working in the background, shaping the relationship long after the moment has passed.
ramayan::1564.insight: It shifts you to see anger as a force that prolongs harm instead of resolving it.

ramayan::1565.verse_sanskrit: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं विश्वामित्रो महातपा: । विरराम महातेजा ऋषिमध्ये महामुनि: । । 15922 । ।
ramayan::1565.verse_hindi: The most powerful sage Viswamitra of fierce asceticism fell silent after after uttering
ramayan::1565.english_translation: Having said this much, the great ascetic Vishvamitra, blazing with power, fell silent among the sages.
ramayan::1565.translation_literal: एतावत् (this much) / उक्त्वा (having said) / वचनम् (speech) / विश्वामित्रः (Vishvamitra) / महातपाः (great ascetic) / विरराम (fell silent) / महातेजाः (blazing with power) / ऋषिमध्ये (among the sages) / महामुनिः (great sage)
ramayan::1565.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1565.essence: His words end; the force of them remains in silence.
ramayan::1565.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra finished speaking and became silent among the sages.
ramayan::1565.simple_insight: Sometimes the weight of a statement is carried by the silence that follows it.
ramayan::1565.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just spoken a fierce judgment about Mahodaya's fate. After delivering the full force of his words before the gathered sages, he stops. The verse marks the end of his pronouncement, not a new teaching.
ramayan::1565.modern_relevance: You say the hard thing in the room, and then the air changes. Sometimes the silence after your words says more than the words themselves.
ramayan::1565.insight: It marks a pause after judgment, not a new principle to apply.

ramayan::1566.verse_sanskrit: तपोबलहतान् कृत्वा वासिष्ठान् समहोदयान् । ऋषिमध्ये महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत । । 1601 । ।
ramayan::1566.verse_hindi: The most brilliant Viswamitra, having destroyed the sons of Vasishta including Mahodaya by his ascetic power, said this in the midst of saints:
ramayan::1566.english_translation: The brilliant Vishvamitra, having destroyed the sons of Vasishta, including Mahodaya, by his ascetic power, spoke among the sages.
ramayan::1566.translation_literal: तपोबलहतान् (struck down by ascetic power) / कृत्वा (having made) / वासिष्ठान् (the sons of Vasishta) / समहोदयान् (including Mahodaya) / ऋषिमध्ये (in the midst of sages) / महातेजा (the very brilliant one) / विश्वामित्रः (Vishvamitra) / अभ्यभाषत (spoke)
ramayan::1566.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1566.essence: Power without restraint can still leave the real conflict unresolved.
ramayan::1566.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra is described as speaking after defeating Vasishta's sons through the force of his austerities.
ramayan::1566.simple_insight: Power gained through discipline can still be used in a conflict-driven way.
ramayan::1566.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the sages, Vishvamitra is shown after a long struggle with Vasishta's line. His ascetic power has already brought down their sons, and now he turns to speak again. The verse mainly sets up the next part of the story.
ramayan::1566.modern_relevance: You can win a long battle and still not have reached peace. Sometimes the hardest part is what you do after proving your power.
ramayan::1566.insight: It shifts attention from victory itself to the moral weight of what follows.

ramayan::1567.verse_sanskrit: अयमिक्ष्वाकुदायादस्त्रिशंकुरिति विश्रुत: । धर्मिष्ठश्च वदान्यश्च मां चैव शरणं गत: । । 1602 । । तेनानेन शरीरेण देवलोकजिगीषया ।
ramayan::1567.verse_hindi: This religious and generous king born in the Ikshvaku race, wellknown as Trisanku sought my refuge to gain heaven with his physical body,
ramayan::1567.english_translation: This righteous and generous king of the Ikshvaku line, known as Trisanku, came to me for refuge, wanting to reach the heavenly realm in his own body.
ramayan::1567.translation_literal: अयम् (this) / इक्ष्वाकुदायादः (descendant of Ikshvaku) / त्रिशङ्कुः (Trisanku) / इति (thus) / विश्रुतः (well-known) / धर्मिष्ठः (most righteous) / च (and) / वदान्यः (generous) / च (and) / माम् (to me) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / शरणम् (refuge) / गतः (gone) / तेन (by that) / अनेन (this) / शरीरेण (with body) / देवलोकजिगीषया (with the desire to conquer the heavenly realm)
ramayan::1567.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::1567.essence: A desperate wish becomes possible only after someone takes refuge.
ramayan::1567.simple_meaning: Trisanku, a righteous and generous king, came to Vishvamitra seeking refuge so he could reach the heavenly realm without giving up his body.
ramayan::1567.simple_insight: Even impossible hopes begin with someone brave enough to ask for help.
ramayan::1567.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra is speaking in the middle of a larger story about his conflict with the sons of Vasishta. He introduces Trisanku as a righteous king who came to him for protection and asked for a bodily ascent to the heavenly realm, setting up the extraordinary sacrifice that follows.
ramayan::1567.modern_relevance: A friend calls you late at night with a request that sounds impossible, but their voice is steady and sincere. The first step toward any rare change is the courage to ask clearly.
ramayan::1567.insight: It frames transformation as a request for refuge before it becomes an action.

ramayan::1568.verse_sanskrit: यथाऽयं स्वशरीरेण स्वर्गलोकं गमिष्यति । । 1603 । । तथा प्रवर्त्यतां यज्ञे भवद्भिश्च मया सह ।
ramayan::1568.verse_hindi: Join me in the performance of this sacrifice in a manner by which he (Trisanku) attains  heaven with his physical body.
ramayan::1568.english_translation: Join me in the sacrifice so that Trisanku may ascend to heaven in his physical body.
ramayan::1568.translation_literal: यथा (so that) / अयम् (this one) / स्वशरीरेण (with his own body) / स्वर्गलोकम् (to the world of heaven) / गमिष्यति (will go) / तथा (in that way) / प्रवर्त्यताम् (let it be begun) / यज्ञे (in the sacrifice) / भवद्भिः (by you all) / च (and) / मया (by me) / सह (together)
ramayan::1568.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1568.essence: A king's impossible wish becomes a public challenge.
ramayan::1568.simple_meaning: Viswamitra asks the assembled sages to help perform a sacrifice so Trisanku can reach heaven in his own body.
ramayan::1568.simple_insight: A desperate wish can turn into a collective test of limits.
ramayan::1568.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has taken Trisanku's impossible plea as his own cause. Standing before the gathered sages, he asks them to join a sacrifice that will send Trisanku upward without leaving his body behind. The moment is still part of a larger negotiation, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::1568.modern_relevance: You bring a request to a room full of people, and everyone can feel how impossible it sounds. The real question is whether anyone will help you try anyway.
ramayan::1568.insight: It frames the sacrifice as a shared attempt to make the impossible happen.

ramayan::1569.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रवच श्श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षय: । । 1604 । । ऊचुस्समेत्य सहिता धर्मज्ञा धर्मसंहितम् ।
ramayan::1569.verse_hindi: Agreeing to these words of Viswamitra all the rishis, knowers of spiritual order and endowed with righteousness assembled there said:
ramayan::1569.english_translation: Hearing Vishvamitra's words, all the great sages gathered together, righteous and versed in dharma, spoke in agreement.
ramayan::1569.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रवचः (the words of Vishvamitra) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / महर्षयः (great sages) / ऊचुः (said) / समेत्य (having gathered) / सहिताḥ (together) / धर्मज्ञाः (knowers of dharma) / धर्मसंहितम् (in agreement with dharma)
ramayan::1569.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1569.essence: Shared righteousness gives a hard task enough strength to begin.
ramayan::1569.simple_meaning: All the gathered sages agree with Vishvamitra and accept his proposal as righteous.
ramayan::1569.simple_insight: Good counsel gains force when wise people recognise it together.
ramayan::1569.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has asked the other sages to help him make Trishanku ascend with his body intact. After hearing him, the assembled sages confer and respond in agreement. This verse is the collective approval before the ritual begins.
ramayan::1569.modern_relevance: A difficult decision lands in a room full of experts, and everyone falls quiet before nodding. The right course often needs shared courage, not just one strong voice.
ramayan::1569.insight: It shows how righteous action becomes stronger when wise people align behind it.

ramayan::1570.verse_sanskrit: अयं कुशिकदायादो मुनि: परमकोपन: । । 1605 । । यदाह वचनं सम्यगेतत्कार्यं न संशय: । अग्निकल्पो हि भगवान् शापं दास्यति रोषित: । । 1606 । ।
ramayan::1570.verse_hindi: Born in the line of Kusika, this sage is extremely cholerictempered. Whatever he says must be properly carried out. There should be no resitation on this score. The venerable sage is like fire. He will curse us if angered.
ramayan::1570.english_translation: Born in the line of Kusika, this sage is extremely wrathful. Whatever he says must be carried out properly, without doubt. The venerable sage is like fire; if angered, he will curse us.
ramayan::1570.translation_literal: अयं (this) / कुशिकदायादः (descendant of Kusika) / मुनिः (sage) / परमकोपनः (extremely wrathful) / यत् (whatever) / आह (says) / वचनम् (word) / सम्यक् (properly) / एतत् (this) / कार्यम् (to be done) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / अग्निकल्पः (like fire) / हि (indeed) / भगवान् (venerable one) / शापम् (curse) / दास्यति (will give) / रोषितः (angered)
ramayan::1570.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1570.essence: Ignore his warning, and you invite fire.
ramayan::1570.simple_meaning: The sages agree that Vishvamitra is dangerous to ignore. His words must be followed exactly, because angering him could bring a curse.
ramayan::1570.simple_insight: Respect the force of a person’s word when the stakes are sacred.
ramayan::1570.detailed_meaning: The other sages have just agreed to help Vishvamitra with Trisanku’s sacrifice. Now they remind one another who Vishvamitra is: a former king turned blazing ascetic whose command cannot be treated lightly. Their caution explains why they submit.
ramayan::1570.modern_relevance: A team hears the senior expert say, “Do it this way,” and nobody wants to be the one who shrugs it off. Some people’s warnings are not suggestions; they are the cost of not listening.
ramayan::1570.insight: It teaches you to recognise when resistance will only deepen trouble and when careful compliance is the wiser move.

ramayan::1571.verse_sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रवर्त्यतां यज्ञ स्सशरीरो यथा दिवम् । गच्छेदिक्ष्वाकुदायादो विश्वामित्रस्य तेजसा । । 1607 । । तथा प्रवर्त्यतां यज्ञ स्सर्वे समधितिष्ठत ।
ramayan::1571.verse_hindi: Hence let the sacrifice be performed in such a manner that the descendant of the Ikshvakus would attain heaven with his physical body through the spiritual power of Viswamitra. All of you commence the sacrifice.
ramayan::1571.english_translation: Hence let the sacrifice be performed in such a manner that the descendant of the Ikshvakus would attain heaven with his physical body through the spiritual power of Viswamitra. All of you commence the sacrifice.
ramayan::1571.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / प्रवर्त्यताम् (let it be set in motion) / यज्ञः (the sacrifice) / सशरीरः (with the body intact) / यथा (so that) / दिवम् (heaven) / गच्छेत् (may go) / इक्ष्वाकुदायादः (the descendant of Ikshvaku) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Viswamitra) / तेजसा (by the power) / तथा (thus) / प्रवर्त्यताम् (let it be set in motion) / यज्ञः (the sacrifice) / सर्वे (all) / समधितिष्ठत (take your places)
ramayan::1571.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1571.essence: Right action here means exact preparation, not enthusiasm alone.
ramayan::1571.simple_meaning: The sacrifice should begin now, arranged so Viswamitra's power can carry the Ikshvaku descendant onward.
ramayan::1571.simple_insight: Great outcomes often depend on precise preparation, not just intention.
ramayan::1571.detailed_meaning: The sages have accepted Viswamitra's warning and are preparing the ritual. This verse is a practical instruction: start the sacrifice correctly, because Rama's safety and the rite's success depend on exact order, collective action, and Viswamitra's spiritual force.
ramayan::1571.modern_relevance: A team is finally aligned before a high-stakes launch, and every step has to be exact. The moment succeeds only if everyone takes their place and does the work in order.
ramayan::1571.insight: It shifts attention from grand purpose to correct execution under guidance.

ramayan::1572.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महर्षयः चक्रुस्तास्ता:क्रियास्तदा । । 1608 । । याजकश्च महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभवत्क्रतौ ।
ramayan::1572.verse_hindi: The maharshis having resolved performed their respective activities relating to the sacrifice. The brilliant Viswamitra acted as the chief officiating priest.
ramayan::1572.english_translation: The great sages then carried out all the required rites, and the radiant Vishvamitra became the chief priest for the sacrifice.
ramayan::1572.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / महर्षयः (the great sages) / चक्रुः (did) / ताः ताः (those) / क्रियाः (rites, actions) / तदा (then) / याजकः (the officiating priest) / च (and) / महातेजाः (very radiant) / विश्वामित्रः (Vishvamitra) / अभवत् (became) / क्रतौ (in the sacrifice)
ramayan::1572.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1572.essence: The warning ends; disciplined action begins.
ramayan::1572.simple_meaning: The sages immediately began the ritual tasks, and Vishvamitra took charge as the main priest.
ramayan::1572.simple_insight: Some moments call for precise action, not hesitation.
ramayan::1572.detailed_meaning: The sacrifice is now underway. After Vishvamitra’s warning about the danger, the assembled sages do not debate further; they begin the ritual work at once. Vishvamitra himself takes the central priestly role, showing his authority and urgency in the rite.
ramayan::1572.modern_relevance: The meeting ends and everyone moves into execution mode: roles are assigned, the checklist opens, and the person leading the project steps in without drama.
ramayan::1572.insight: It shifts attention from discussion to coordinated execution.

ramayan::1573.verse_sanskrit: ऋत्विजश्चानुपूर्व्येण मन्त्रवन्मन्त्रकोविदा: । । 1609 । । चक्रु: कर्माणि सर्वाणि यथाकल्पं यथाविधि ।
ramayan::1573.verse_hindi: The officiating priests proficient in chanting mantras performed in order of their respective ranks all the rites in accordance with the Yojanakalpa adhering to codes and traditions.
ramayan::1573.english_translation: The officiating priests, skilled in mantra and ritual, performed every rite in proper order, according to established procedure and rule.
ramayan::1573.translation_literal: ऋत्विजः (the officiating priests) / च (and) / अनुपूर्व्येण (in due order) / मन्त्रवत् (with mantras) / मन्त्रकोविदाः (skilled in mantra) / चक्रुः (performed) / कर्माणि (rites) / सर्वाणि (all) / यथाकल्पं (according to the prescribed procedure) / यथाविधि (according to rule)
ramayan::1573.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1573.essence: Sacred work succeeds through exactness, not excitement.
ramayan::1573.simple_meaning: The priests carried out the sacrifice exactly as prescribed, each in the proper order and with full ritual knowledge.
ramayan::1573.simple_insight: Careful order matters when a sacred task depends on many hands.
ramayan::1573.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra’s sacrifice is now fully underway. The priests take up their assigned roles, each trained in mantra and ritual procedure, and complete every step exactly as prescribed. The verse pauses on precision, not drama.
ramayan::1573.modern_relevance: A wedding, memorial, or major ceremony runs smoothly because everyone knows their role and respects the sequence. When the order is right, the whole event holds together.
ramayan::1573.insight: It shifts attention from improvisation to disciplined execution.

ramayan::1574.verse_sanskrit: तत: कालेन महता विश्वामित्रो महातपा: । । 16010 । । चकारावाहनं तत्र भागार्थं सर्वदेवता: ।
ramayan::1574.verse_hindi: Long after, the mighty ascetic Viswamitra  invoked all the gods to partake their share of offerings.
ramayan::1574.english_translation: Long after, the mighty ascetic Viswamitra invoked all the gods to receive their share of the offerings.
ramayan::1574.translation_literal: तत: (then) / कालेन (after time) / महता (great) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महातपाः (the greatly ascetic one) / चकार (made) / आवाहनम् (invocation) / तत्र (there) / भागार्थम् (for the share) / सर्वदेवताः (all the gods)
ramayan::1574.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1574.essence: A proper invitation can still meet complete refusal.
ramayan::1574.simple_meaning: Viswamitra called the gods to come and receive their share of the sacrificial offering.
ramayan::1574.simple_insight: A ritual can be exact and still be rejected when others fail to respond.
ramayan::1574.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is conducting a sacrifice with the help of priests. After the rites are prepared, he formally calls the gods to accept their portion of the offering. This verse sets up the next crisis: the invocation is made, but the gods do not come.
ramayan::1574.modern_relevance: You do everything properly, send the invitation, set the table, and wait. The silence that follows is its own kind of answer.
ramayan::1574.insight: It prepares the turning point by showing a rightful call met with absence.

ramayan::1575.verse_sanskrit: नाभ्यागमंस्तदाहूता भागार्थं सर्वदेवता: । । 16011 । । तत: क्रोधसमाविष्टो विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । स्रुवमुद्यम्य सक्रोधस्त्रिशङ्कुमिदमब्रवीत् । । 16012 । ।
ramayan::1575.verse_hindi: When, the gods invited by him did not come to receive their share of offerings, the great ascetic Viswamitra seized with anger lifted the sacrificial ladle and said to Trisanku:
ramayan::1575.english_translation: When the gods invited by him did not come to receive their share of offerings, the great ascetic Viswamitra, seized with anger, lifted the sacrificial ladle and said to Trisanku:
ramayan::1575.translation_literal: नाभ्यागमन् (did not come) / तदाहूता (those invited) / भागार्थं (for the share) / सर्वदेवताः (all the deities) / ततः (then) / क्रोधसमाविष्टः (filled with anger) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (the great sage) / स्रुवम् (the sacrificial ladle) / उद्यम्य (lifting) / सः (he) / क्रोधात् (in anger) / त्रिशङ्कुम् (Trisanku) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1575.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1575.essence: A slight to sacred order can turn even great discipline into anger.
ramayan::1575.simple_meaning: The gods did not come for their sacrificial share, and Viswamitra became angry and raised the ladle to speak to Trisanku.
ramayan::1575.simple_insight: A sacred ritual can turn sharp when pride, will, and disappointment collide.
ramayan::1575.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has arranged a grand sacrifice, but the invited deities refuse to appear and accept their offerings. Offended and furious, he lifts the ritual ladle and turns to Trisanku. The scene is a hinge: restraint is giving way to force.
ramayan::1575.modern_relevance: You planned everything carefully, and the people you counted on simply did not show up. The disappointment is real — and so is the choice of what you do next.
ramayan::1575.insight: It shows how quickly a disciplined ritual can become a test of ego and resolve.

ramayan::1576.verse_sanskrit: पश्य मे तपसो वीर्यं स्वार्जितस्य नरेश्वर । एष त्वां सशरीरेण नयामि स्वर्गमोजसा । । 16013 । । दुष्प्रापं सशरीरेण दिवं गच्छ नराधिप ।
ramayan::1576.verse_hindi: O King behold the prowess of my selfearned asceticism. With my spiritual might, I shall send you to heaven with your physical body O King go to heaven with physical body which is not possible for anybody to accomplish.
ramayan::1576.english_translation: O King, behold the power of my earned austerity. By my force, I will send you to the higher realm in your physical body. Go to the higher realm with your body, though that is difficult for anyone to do.
ramayan::1576.translation_literal: पश्य (behold) / मे (my) / तपसः (of austerity) / वीर्यम् (power) / स्वार्जितस्य (self-earned) / नरेश्वर (O king) / एष (this) / त्वाम् (you) / सशरीरेण (with body) / नयामि (I will lead) / स्वर्गम् (to the higher realm) / ओजसा (by force) / दुष्प्रापम् (hard to attain) / सशरीरेण (with body) / दिवम् (to the higher realm) / गच्छ (go) / नराधिप (O ruler of men)
ramayan::1576.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1576.essence: Earned discipline can do what ordinary effort cannot.
ramayan::1576.simple_meaning: Viswamitra tells the king to witness the power gained through his own austerity. He claims that this hard-earned inner force can send a person to the higher realm even in the physical body.
ramayan::1576.simple_insight: Real discipline builds power that can carry you beyond ordinary limits.
ramayan::1576.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been angered when the invited radiant beings refuse his offering. In that charged moment, he turns to King Trishanku and declares that his austerity has become real power — power strong enough to lift a living body to the higher realm.
ramayan::1576.modern_relevance: You spend years training, saving, or healing, and then one impossible request arrives. This verse speaks to the kind of force that comes from long discipline: not wishful thinking, but earned capacity.
ramayan::1576.insight: It shifts attention from status to the power created by sustained self-restraint.

ramayan::1577.verse_sanskrit: स्वार्जितं किञ्चिदप्यस्ति मया हि तपस:फलम् । । 16014 । । राजन् स्वतेजसा तस्य सशरीरो दिवं व्रज ।
ramayan::1577.verse_hindi: By the power of what little fruit of austerities I have earned, I shall send to heaven with your body.
ramayan::1577.english_translation: By the power of what little fruit of austerities I have earned, I shall send you to heaven with your body.
ramayan::1577.translation_literal: स्वार्जितम् (self-earned) / किञ्चिदपि (even a little) / अस्ति (is) / मया (by me) / हि (indeed) / तपसःफलम् (fruit of austerity) / राजन् (O king) / स्वतेजसा (by my own power) / तस्य (that) / सशरीरः (with body) / दिवम् (to heaven) / व्रज (go)
ramayan::1577.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1577.essence: Even a little earned discipline can carry you beyond ordinary limits.
ramayan::1577.simple_meaning: Viswamitra says his hard-earned austerity has given him enough power to send the king to a higher realm while still in his body.
ramayan::1577.simple_insight: Real discipline creates force that can change what seems impossible.
ramayan::1577.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just been insulted by the gods who refused his offering. Burning with restrained fury, he reveals the power of his tapas to King Trishanku: even this small fruit of austerity is enough to send him upward in bodily form.
ramayan::1577.modern_relevance: You keep showing up to practice when nobody applauds, and one day that quiet discipline becomes real force. What looked small to others can move your whole life.
ramayan::1577.insight: It shifts attention from external approval to the power built by sustained effort.

ramayan::1578.verse_sanskrit: उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन् सशरीरो नरेश्वर: । । 16015 । । दिवं जगाम काकुत्स्थ मुनीनां पश्यतां तदा ।
ramayan::1578.verse_hindi: O Descendant of Kakustha (Rama) when the sage had said these words, the king with his physical body ascended to heaven in the presence of the sages.
ramayan::1578.english_translation: O Descendant of Kakustha, when the sage had said these words, the king ascended to heaven in his physical body before the sages watched.
ramayan::1578.translation_literal: उक्तवाक्ये (when these words had been spoken) / मुनौ (by the sage) / तस्मिन् (that) / सशरीरः (with the body) / नरेश्वरः (king) / दिवम् (to heaven) / जगाम (went) / काकुत्स्थ (O descendant of Kakustha) / मुनीनां (of the sages) / पश्यताम् (watching) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1578.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1578.essence: The promise becomes real the moment everyone sees it happen.
ramayan::1578.simple_meaning: After the sage finished speaking, King Trisanku rose to heaven in his body while the sages watched.
ramayan::1578.simple_insight: Some moments are so extraordinary they become the story itself.
ramayan::1578.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just declared his power to send Trisanku upward despite the gods' refusal. In front of the assembled sages, the king's body rises to heaven, proving the force of the sage's tapas and setting up the next clash with the celestial order.
ramayan::1578.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after someone makes an impossible promise. Then the thing actually happens, and everyone in the room has to rethink what they believed was possible.
ramayan::1578.insight: It shifts attention from the claim to the visible consequence that follows it.

ramayan::1579.verse_sanskrit: देवलोकगतं दृष्ट्वा त्रिशङ्कुं पाकशासन: । । 16016 । । सह सर्वैस्सुरगणैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1579.verse_hindi: On ascending to heaven Trisanku saw Indra (destroyer of Paka) along with hosts of  gods. Indra said to him:
ramayan::1579.english_translation: On ascending to heaven, Trisanku saw Indra along with all the hosts of the gods, and Indra spoke these words:
ramayan::1579.translation_literal: देवलोकगतं (having gone to the world of the gods) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / त्रिशङ्कुम् (Trisanku) / पाकशासनः (Indra) / सह (along with) / सर्वैः (all) / सुरगणैः (with the hosts of gods) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (word) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1579.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1579.simple_meaning: Trisanku reached heaven and saw Indra there with the other gods. Indra then spoke to him.
ramayan::1579.simple_insight: A new scene opens, but the real message comes in the rejection that follows.
ramayan::1579.detailed_meaning: Trisanku has been lifted to heaven by the sage's power, but the ascent is not the end of the story. Indra appears with the other gods and prepares to challenge Trisanku's claim to that place. This verse simply sets up the confrontation.
ramayan::1579.modern_relevance: You finally get the seat, the invite, the access — and then someone higher up questions whether you belong there.
ramayan::1579.insight: It marks the transition from miraculous ascent to divine rejection.

ramayan::1580.verse_sanskrit: त्रिशङ्को गच्छ भूयस्त्वं नासि स्वर्गकृतालय: । । 16017 । । गुरुशापहतो मूढ पत भूमिमवाक्छिरा: ।
ramayan::1580.verse_hindi: O Trisanku you are not fit to inhabit heaven. Go back, you fool Doomed by the curse of your spiritual preceptor, fall on earth, head down.
ramayan::1580.english_translation: O Trisanku, go back. You are not fit to dwell in heaven. Fool, struck by your guru's curse, fall to earth headfirst.
ramayan::1580.translation_literal: त्रिशङ्को (O Trisanku) / गच्छ (go) / भूयस्त्वम् (back again) / न (not) / असि (you are) / स्वर्ग-कृत-आलयः (fit for heaven as a dwelling) / गुरु-शाप-हतः (struck by the guru's curse) / मूढ (fool) / पत (fall) / भूमिम् (to the earth) / अवाक्-शिराः (head downward)
ramayan::1580.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1580.essence: A higher place cannot hold someone whose inner fault still rules him.
ramayan::1580.simple_meaning: Indra rejects Trisanku from heaven and commands him to fall back to earth, headfirst, because a curse has made him unfit for the higher realm.
ramayan::1580.simple_insight: Pride can lift you briefly, but unresolved wrongdoing still pulls you back down.
ramayan::1580.detailed_meaning: Trisanku has been sent upward by Viswamitra's power and now stands among the radiant beings of heaven. Indra sees him there and refuses him entry, declaring that a man under his guru's curse cannot remain in that realm. The moment turns the ascent into a fall.
ramayan::1580.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the seat, the access — and still feel out of place because the old pattern never changed. Some arrivals expose what hasn't been resolved.
ramayan::1580.insight: It shifts attention from external ascent to the inner condition that can sustain it.

ramayan::1581.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो महेन्द्रेण त्रिशङ्कुरपतत्पुन: । । 16018 । । विक्रोशमानस्त्राहीति विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम् ।
ramayan::1581.verse_hindi: Thus spoken to by Indra, Trisanku crying, O Viswamitra, Protect me, Protect me started falling down.
ramayan::1581.english_translation: Thus spoken to by Indra, Trisanku crying, 'Protect me, protect me, O Viswamitra,' started falling down again.
ramayan::1581.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्तः (spoken to) / महेन्द्रेण (by Indra) / त्रिशङ्कुः (Trisanku) / अपतत् (fell) / पुनः (again) / विक्रोशमानः (crying out) / त्राहीति (protect me) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / तपोधनम् (the ascetic-rich one)
ramayan::1581.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1581.essence: Rejection can send you falling even after you have risen.
ramayan::1581.simple_meaning: Trisanku, rejected from heaven, falls again while crying out to Viswamitra for protection.
ramayan::1581.simple_insight: Even after reaching high places, fear can pull you down in an instant.
ramayan::1581.detailed_meaning: Trisanku has been lifted toward heaven by Viswamitra’s power, but Indra rejects him. As he falls back down, he calls out to Viswamitra for rescue. The verse keeps the tension moving toward Viswamitra’s furious response.
ramayan::1581.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance you fought for, and then one message, one setback, one cold word makes it feel like everything is slipping again.
ramayan::1581.insight: It shows how fragile borrowed elevation is when fear returns.

ramayan::1582.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य क्रोशमानस्य कौशिक: । । 16019 । । रोषमाहारयत्तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1582.verse_hindi: Having heard the wailing Trisanku, the enraged Viswamitra shouted, Stay, Stay.
ramayan::1582.english_translation: Having heard Trisanku’s cry, Visvamitra was filled with fierce anger and shouted, “Stay! Stay!”
ramayan::1582.translation_literal: तच्छ्रुत्वा (having heard that) / वचनं (the cry) / तस्य (of him) / क्रोशमानस्य (wailing) / कौशिकः (Kausika, Visvamitra) / रोषम् (anger) / आहारयत् (brought upon himself) / तीव्रम् (fierce) / तिष्ठ (stay) / तिष्ठ (stay) / इति (thus) / च (and) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1582.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::1582.essence: His anger becomes the force that stops the fall.
ramayan::1582.simple_meaning: Visvamitra hears Trisanku calling for help, becomes furious, and commands him to stop falling.
ramayan::1582.simple_insight: Protective anger can become action in a single instant.
ramayan::1582.detailed_meaning: Trisanku has been rejected from heaven and is falling back down while crying out for rescue. Hearing him, Visvamitra’s rage flares. This verse is the turning point before he answers that cry with a forceful act.
ramayan::1582.modern_relevance: You hear someone panic on the other end of the phone, and your calm breaks. In that instant, care turns into action.
ramayan::1582.insight: It shows how fierce concern can interrupt helplessness and trigger intervention.

ramayan::1583.verse_sanskrit: ऋषिमध्ये स तेजस्स्वी प्रजापतिरिवापर: । । 16020 । । सृजन् दक्षिणमार्गस्थान् सप्तर्षीनपरान् पुन: । नक्षत्रमालामपरामसृजत्क्रोधमूर्च्छित: । । 16021 । । दक्षिणां दिशमास्थाय मुनिमध्ये महायशा: ।
ramayan::1583.verse_hindi: Standing in the midst of the ascetics, that  mighty sage who conjured up a constellation of seven new rishis (stars) looked like another creator Brahma. Overcome by anger the illustrious sage created a new group of stars in the southern direction.
ramayan::1583.english_translation: Standing among the ascetics, that radiant sage looked like another creator, Brahma. Overcome by anger, the illustrious sage created another set of seven stars in the southern sky.
ramayan::1583.translation_literal: ऋषिमध्ये (among the ascetics) / सः (that one) / तेजस्वी (radiant, powerful) / प्रजापतिः (creator) / इव (like) / अपरः (another) / सृजन् (creating) / दक्षिणमार्गस्थान् (placed in the southern path) / सप्तर्षीन् (seven sages) / अपरान् (other) / पुनः (again) / नक्षत्रमालाम् (garland of stars) / अपराम् (another) / असृजत् (created) / क्रोधमूर्च्छितः (overcome by anger) / दक्षिणाम् (southern) / दिशम् (direction) / आस्थाय (taking position) / मुनिमध्ये (among the sages) / महायशाः (greatly renowned)
ramayan::1583.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1583.essence: Power used in anger becomes a display, not wisdom.
ramayan::1583.simple_meaning: Viswamitra, furious and powerful, creates a new set of seven stars in the southern sky, looking like another creator among the sages.
ramayan::1583.simple_insight: Unchecked anger can turn even greatness into spectacle.
ramayan::1583.detailed_meaning: Trisanku is still falling, and Viswamitra’s rage has not cooled. In front of the assembled sages, he answers insult with cosmic force, creating a new constellation in the southern sky. The verse heightens his power, but it is still part of the unfolding scene.
ramayan::1583.modern_relevance: A heated argument pushes you to do something dramatic just to prove you can. The moment may look powerful from the outside, but it still comes from being ruled by anger.
ramayan::1583.insight: It shows how anger can drive creation that is impressive but unstable.

ramayan::1584.verse_sanskrit: सृष्ट्वा नक्षत्रवंशं च क्रोधेन कलुषीकृत: । । 16022 । । अन्यमिन्द्रं करिष्यामि लोको वा स्यादनिन्द्रक: । दैवतान्यपि स क्रोधा त्स्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे । । 16023 । ।
ramayan::1584.verse_hindi: Having created a constellation of stars, Viswamitra out of anger said, I will create  another Indra or this world will be without Indra and commenced to create even gods.
ramayan::1584.english_translation: Having created a constellation of stars, Viswamitra, angered, said, 'I will create another Indra, or this world will be without Indra.' He then began to create even the gods.
ramayan::1584.translation_literal: सृष्ट्वा (having created) / नक्षत्रवंशं (a lineage/constellation of stars) / च (and) / क्रोधेन (with anger) / कलुषीकृत: (made impure/disturbed) / अन्यम् (another) / इन्द्रम् (Indra) / करिष्यामि (I will make) / लोको (world) / वा (or) / स्यात् (may be) / अनिन्द्रकः (without Indra) / दैवतानि (gods) / अपि (even) / सः (he) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / स्रष्टुम् (to create) / समुपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::1584.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1584.essence: Power without restraint turns into cosmic defiance.
ramayan::1584.simple_meaning: Angered by the moment, Viswamitra claims he can remake the cosmic order itself, even to the point of creating new rulers and divine beings.
ramayan::1584.simple_insight: Unchecked anger can make even great power feel reckless.
ramayan::1584.detailed_meaning: After Trishanku's plea, Viswamitra has already forced a new star-pattern into the sky. Now his fury swells further: he threatens to create another Indra and even new gods. This is a display of power pushed to the edge of pride.
ramayan::1584.modern_relevance: You send one furious message, then start imagining how to burn the whole bridge down. The mind in anger always reaches for bigger destruction than the moment requires.
ramayan::1584.insight: It shows how anger escalates from one grievance into grandiose, dangerous overreach.

ramayan::1585.verse_sanskrit: तत: परमसम्भ्रान्तास्सर्षिसङ्घास्सुरासुरा: । विश्वामित्रं महात्मानमूचु: सानुनयं वच: । । 16024 । ।
ramayan::1585.verse_hindi: Struck with wonder and fear, hosts of rishis, suras and asuras humbly addressed Viswamitra.
ramayan::1585.english_translation: Struck with wonder and fear, hosts of rishis, suras and asuras humbly addressed Viswamitra.
ramayan::1585.translation_literal: तत: (then) / परमसम्भ्रान्ताः (greatly astonished and alarmed) / सर्षिसङ्घाः (the hosts of rishis) / सुरासुरा: (the suras and asuras) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / महात्मानम् (the great-souled one) / ऊचुः (said) / सानुनयम् (with humility and conciliation) / वचः (words)
ramayan::1585.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1585.essence: His anger was so vast that even the heavens stepped carefully.
ramayan::1585.simple_meaning: Rishis, radiant beings, and shadow beings were amazed and frightened, so they spoke to Viswamitra with humility.
ramayan::1585.simple_insight: Even the powerful can be shaken when someone’s force crosses a line.
ramayan::1585.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just created a new set of stars in anger, showing power that unsettles the cosmic order. Now rishis, radiant beings, and shadow beings gather around him, astonished and alarmed, and try to calm him before his wrath reshapes the world further.
ramayan::1585.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after one person’s anger changes the whole atmosphere. Everyone who felt safe a moment ago now speaks carefully, trying to cool what has already been set in motion.
ramayan::1585.insight: It shows how unchecked force can make even strong people plead for restraint.

ramayan::1586.verse_sanskrit: अयं राजा महाभाग गुरुशापपरिक्षत: । सशरीरो दिवं यातुं नार्हत्येव तपोधन । । 16025 । ।
ramayan::1586.verse_hindi: O Glorious maharshi, this king cursed by his spiritual preceptor is not worthy of going to heaven with his physical body.
ramayan::1586.english_translation: O glorious great sage, this king cursed by his teacher is not worthy of going to heaven with his physical body.
ramayan::1586.translation_literal: अयं (this) / राजा (king) / महाभाग (O glorious one) / गुरु-शाप-परिक्षत: (struck by the teacher's curse) / स-शरीर: (with the body) / दिवं (to heaven) / यातुं (to go) / नार्हति (is not fit) / एव (indeed) / तपोधन (O treasure of austerity)
ramayan::1586.speaker: Devas
ramayan::1586.essence: A damaged condition cannot be carried untouched into a higher state.
ramayan::1586.simple_meaning: A king who has been cursed by his teacher cannot enter the higher realm in his present body.
ramayan::1586.simple_insight: Some consequences cannot be bypassed, even by power or status.
ramayan::1586.detailed_meaning: The gods are trying to prevent Viswamitra from forcing a mortal king into the higher realm in bodily form. They object that this ruler has been struck by his teacher's curse, and that his present condition makes such an ascent impossible.
ramayan::1586.modern_relevance: You try to skip the hard part and keep the old version of yourself intact. But some transitions demand that you change before you can cross over.
ramayan::1586.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding exceptions to respecting the conditions of transformation.

ramayan::1587.verse_sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां मुनिपुङ्गव: । अब्रवीत्सुमहद्वाक्यं कौशिक: सर्वदेवता: । । 16026 । ।
ramayan::1587.verse_hindi: The son of Kushika (Viswamitra), the preeminent ascetic heard the gods and said these praiseworthy words:
ramayan::1587.english_translation: The son of Kushika, the great ascetic, heard the gods and spoke these noble words.
ramayan::1587.translation_literal: तेषाम् (of them) / तत्-वचनम् (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / देवानाम् (of the gods) / मुनि-पुङ्गवः (the foremost ascetic) / अब्रवीत् (said) / सुमहत्-वाक्यम् (a very great statement) / कौशिकः (Koushika) / सर्व-देवता: (to all the gods)
ramayan::1587.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1587.essence: A true promise holds even when powerful voices object.
ramayan::1587.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra hears the gods and responds with dignity. He is about to explain why he will not break his promise to Trishanku.
ramayan::1587.simple_insight: A noble word matters because it can hold even against pressure from above.
ramayan::1587.detailed_meaning: The gods and sages have gathered around Trishanku’s impossible request. Vishwamitra listens to their appeal, then answers as the one who made the promise. This line sets up his refusal to abandon the vow he has already given.
ramayan::1587.modern_relevance: You made a promise under pressure, and now everyone wants you to quietly retract it. The hardest part is not speaking — it is staying faithful after the applause changes.
ramayan::1587.insight: It shifts attention from persuading others to keeping your own word intact.

ramayan::1588.verse_sanskrit: सशरीरस्य भद्रं वस्त्रिशङ्कोरस्य भूपते: । आरोहणं प्रतिज्ञाय नानृतं कर्तुमुत्सहे । । 16027 । ।
ramayan::1588.verse_hindi: I wish you well Having promised king Trisanku ascent to heaven with his  physical form, I do not wish to go back on my word.
ramayan::1588.english_translation: Having promised King Trishanku ascent to heaven in his physical body, I do not wish to speak falsely.
ramayan::1588.translation_literal: सशरीरस्य (of one with the body) / भद्रं (may it be well) / वस्त्रिशङ्कोरस्य (of Trishanku) / भूपतेः (of the king) / आरोहणं (ascent) / प्रतिज्ञाय (having promised) / न (not) / अनृतं (falsehood) / कर्तुम् (to do) / उत्सहे (I am willing)
ramayan::1588.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1588.essence: A promise becomes sacred the moment you refuse to betray it.
ramayan::1588.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra refuses to take back his promise to Trishanku, even though the promise is difficult to fulfill.
ramayan::1588.detailed_meaning: The gods have objected to Trishanku's bodily ascent to heaven, but Vishwamitra has already given his word. Facing pressure, he chooses truthfulness over retreat, and the next verse shows him turning that promise into a new heaven.
ramayan::1588.modern_relevance: You told someone you would stand by them, then reality got expensive. The easy move is to soften the promise. This verse remembers the dignity of not doing that.
ramayan::1588.insight: It teaches you to protect your word when circumstances become inconvenient.

ramayan::1589.verse_sanskrit: स्वर्गोऽस्तु सशरीरस्य त्रिशङ्कोरस्य शाश्वत: । नक्षत्राणि च सर्वाणि मामकानि ध्रुवाण्यथ । । 16028 । । यावल्लोका धरिष्यन्ति तिष्ठन्त्वेतानि सर्वश: । मत्कृतानि सुरा स्सर्वे तदनुज्ञातुमर्हथ । । 16029 । ।
ramayan::1589.verse_hindi: Let this heaven be an eternal abode for Trisanku in his physical form All these stars created by me shall endure as long as the worlds survive. O gods it behoves of you to accord consent to this.
ramayan::1589.english_translation: Let this heaven be an eternal abode for Trisanku in his physical form. All these stars created by me shall endure as long as the worlds survive. O gods, it behoves you to give your consent.
ramayan::1589.translation_literal: स्वर्गोऽस्तु (let heaven be) / सशरीरस्य (for the embodied) / त्रिशङ्कोः (of Trisanku) / अस्य (of this one) / शाश्वतः (eternal) / नक्षत्राणि (stars) / च (and) / सर्वाणि (all) / मामकानि (created by me) / ध्रुवाणि (fixed) / अथ (also) / यावत् (as long as) / लोकाः (worlds) / धरिष्यन्ति (will endure) / तिष्ठन्तु (let them remain) / एतानि (these) / सर्वशः (in every way) / मत्कृतानि (made by me) / सुराः (gods) / सर्वे (all) / तत् (that) / अनुज्ञातुम् (to approve) / अर्हथ (you ought)
ramayan::1589.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1589.essence: A promise kept with force can reorder what seemed unchangeable.
ramayan::1589.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra refuses to let his promise fail. He asks the gods to make room for Trisanku and to let the new celestial order remain.
ramayan::1589.simple_insight: A committed promise can be strong enough to alter what seems fixed.
ramayan::1589.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already declared that he will not lie to Trisanku. Now, before the gods, he pushes that resolve to its limit: if the old heaven will not accept the king, then a new order must be held together by truth and will.
ramayan::1589.modern_relevance: You told someone you would show up when it mattered, and now the cost is real. Vishwamitra’s answer is not to soften the promise — it is to make reality bend around it.
ramayan::1589.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting convenience to protecting a vow, even when the vow demands a larger change.

ramayan::1590.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ता: सुरास्सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् । एवं भवतु भद्रं ते तिष्ठन्त्वेतानि सर्वश: । । 16030 । । गगने तान्यनेकानि वैश्वानरपथाद्बहि: । नक्षत्राणि मुनिश्रेष्ठ तेषु ज्योतिष्षु जाज्वलन् । । 16031 । । अवाक्छिरास्त्रिशङ्कुश्च तिष्ठत्वमरसन्निभ: ।
ramayan::1590.verse_hindi: Thus addressed, all the gods, replied to the preeminent ascetic, O Best among sages, be blessed let thy will be donel. Those many celebrated stars shall stay on all sides outside the path of Vaisvanara (zodiac) in the firmament. Amidst those stars, Trisanku, shining brilliantly like an immortal, shall stay on, head down.
ramayan::1590.english_translation: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to the great sage: "So be it. Blessings to you. Let all these stars remain as they are. In the sky, many stars shall stay outside the path of Vaisvanara, and among those lights, Trisanku shall shine brilliantly, hanging head downward like an immortal."
ramayan::1590.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्ताः (having been spoken to) / सुराः (the gods) / सर्वे (all) / प्रत्यूचुः (replied) / मुनि-पुङ्गवम् (to the foremost sage) / एवम् (so) / भवतु (let it be) / भद्रम् (blessing) / ते (to you) / तिष्ठन्तु (let them remain) / एतानि (these) / सर्वशः (in every way) / गगने (in the sky) / तानि (those) / अनेकानि (many) / वैश्वानर-पथात् (from the path of Vaisvanara) / बहिः (outside) / नक्षत्राणि (stars) / मुनि-श्रेष्ठ (O best of sages) / तेषु (among them) / ज्योतिषु (among lights) / जाज्वलन् (shining brilliantly) / अवाक्-शिराः (head downward) / त्रिशङ्कुः (Trisanku) / च (and) / तिष्ठतु (let him remain) / अमर-सन्निभः (like an immortal)
ramayan::1590.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1590.essence: A promise so strong that even the sky is rearranged to keep it.
ramayan::1590.simple_meaning: The gods agree to Vishvamitra's request: Trisanku will remain in the sky in his body, and the stars will also be placed there around him.
ramayan::1590.simple_insight: Even the impossible can be made real when a vow is answered fully.
ramayan::1590.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has demanded that his promise to Trisanku not be broken. The gods finally yield and reshape the sky itself: stars are fixed in new positions, and Trisanku is left hanging there in his body, blazing like an immortal. The passage completes the strange bargain.
ramayan::1590.modern_relevance: You make a promise that seems too large to keep, then discover the cost of honouring it. The shape of your world changes because you refused to lie.
ramayan::1590.insight: It shows that a vow can force reality to bend around it, not the other way around.

ramayan::1591.verse_sanskrit: अनुयास्यन्ति चैतानि ज्योतींषि नृपसत्तमम् । । 16032 । । कृतार्थं कीर्तिमन्तं च स्वर्गलोकगतं यथा ।
ramayan::1591.verse_hindi: These stars will follow this illustrious one (Trisanku), the best of kings who gained his object, as if he had attained heaven.
ramayan::1591.english_translation: These stars will follow this illustrious one, the best of kings who gained his object, as if he had attained heaven.
ramayan::1591.translation_literal: अनुयास्यन्ति (will follow) / च (and) / एतानि (these) / ज्योतींषि (stars) / नृपसत्तमम् (the best of kings) / कृतार्थम् (one who has achieved his aim) / कीर्तिमन्तम् (the illustrious one) / च (and) / स्वर्गलोकगतं (gone to the world of heaven) / यथा (as if)
ramayan::1591.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1591.essence: A fulfilled vow can make even the sky change its course.
ramayan::1591.simple_meaning: The stars will follow Trisanku, the king who has achieved his aim, as if he has reached heaven.
ramayan::1591.simple_insight: Even impossible wishes can be honored when a great vow is upheld.
ramayan::1591.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just forced the gods to make room for Trisanku, the king suspended between earth and heaven. This line adds the final marvel: the stars themselves will accompany him, sealing the sage’s promise in cosmic form.
ramayan::1591.modern_relevance: You asked for something impossible and someone finally made room for it. The relief is not just getting the result — it is seeing the world rearrange itself around a vow kept.
ramayan::1591.insight: It turns a private wish into a public cosmic honor.

ramayan::1592.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रस्तु धर्मात्मा सर्वदेवैरभिष्टुत: । । 16033 । । ऋषिभिश्च महातेजा बाढमित्याह देवता: ।
ramayan::1592.verse_hindi: In this manner extolled by all devatas and rishis, mighty and righteous Viswamitra said, well let it be so.
ramayan::1592.english_translation: Extolled by all the gods and sages, the righteous and mighty Viswamitra said, “So be it.”
ramayan::1592.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / तु (indeed) / धर्मात्मा (righteous in nature) / सर्वदेवैः (by all the gods) / अभिष्टुतः (praised) / ऋषिभिः (by sages) / च (and) / महातेजाः (of great splendor) / बाढम् (so be it) / इति (thus) / आह (said) / देवताः (the gods)
ramayan::1592.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1592.essence: Agreement ends the tension; the sacrifice can now move forward.
ramayan::1592.simple_meaning: After the gods and sages praised him, Viswamitra agreed and gave his consent.
ramayan::1592.simple_insight: Sometimes the right answer is simple acceptance after everyone has spoken.
ramayan::1592.detailed_meaning: The gods and sages have just praised Viswamitra and accepted the result of the sacrifice. Viswamitra, honored as righteous and radiant, gives his brief assent. The verse closes the exchange rather than offering a teaching of its own.
ramayan::1592.modern_relevance: A long meeting finally ends, everyone has weighed in, and the person leading it simply says, “Fine, let it be.” The moment is not dramatic — it is closure.
ramayan::1592.insight: It marks the settling of a decision after collective approval.

ramayan::1593.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवा महात्मानो मुनयश्च तपोधना: । जग्मुर्यथाऽऽगतं सर्वे यज्ञस्यान्ते नरोत्तम । । 16034 । ।
ramayan::1593.verse_hindi: O Best among men (Rama) then at the conclusion of the sacrifice the great gods and saints went the way they had come.
ramayan::1593.english_translation: O best among men, then at the end of the sacrifice, the great gods and the sages, rich in austerity, all returned the way they had come.
ramayan::1593.translation_literal: ततः (then) / देवा (the gods) / महात्मानः (great-souled ones) / मुनयः (sages) / च (and) / तपोधनाः (rich in austerity) / जग्मुः (went) / यथाऽऽगतम् (as they had come) / सर्वे (all) / यज्ञस्य अन्ते (at the end of the sacrifice) / नरोत्तम (best among men)
ramayan::1593.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1593.essence: The sacred gathering ends, and everyone returns unchanged.
ramayan::1593.simple_meaning: The sacrifice is over, and the gods and sages leave just as they arrived.
ramayan::1593.simple_insight: Some moments end cleanly: what gathered for a purpose can simply depart.
ramayan::1593.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra’s sacrifice has been completed after the gods and sages praised the result and accepted the outcome. Now, at the close of the ritual, the divine visitors and holy men turn back and leave as they came. It is a scene of closure, not instruction.
ramayan::1593.modern_relevance: After the last guest leaves and the hall goes quiet, the work is complete. No speech is needed; the event has already done what it came to do.
ramayan::1593.insight: It marks the ritual’s completion and the calm return of all who witnessed it.

ramayan::1594.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रो महात्माथ प्रस्थितान् प्रेक्ष्य तानृषीन् । अब्रवीन्नरशार्दूलस्सर्वांस्तान्वनवासिन: । । 1611 । ।
ramayan::1594.verse_hindi: O Tiger among men (Rama) thereafter great Viswamitra seeing the departing sages of the forest said:
ramayan::1594.english_translation: Then great Viswamitra, seeing the sages of the forest depart, said to them all:
ramayan::1594.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रो (Viswamitra) / महात्मा (great-souled) / अथ (then) / प्रस्थितान् (those who had departed) / प्रेक्ष्य (seeing) / तान् (those) / ऋषीन् (sages) / अब्रवीत् (said) / नरशार्दूलः (tiger among men) / सर्वान् (to all) / तान् (those) / वनवासिनः (forest dwellers)
ramayan::1594.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1594.essence: The scene pauses just long enough for the next turn to begin.
ramayan::1594.simple_meaning: Viswamitra notices the sages leaving and speaks to them. The verse is a scene transition, not a teaching.
ramayan::1594.simple_insight: Sometimes a story simply turns a corner and moves on.
ramayan::1594.detailed_meaning: At the end of the sacrifice, the forest sages begin to depart. Viswamitra watches them go and addresses them before the next step of the journey. The verse sets up his reply in the following line.
ramayan::1594.modern_relevance: The meeting ends, people stand up, chairs scrape back, and the room shifts into the next agenda item. Nothing is being argued here yet — only the moment before the real conversation begins.
ramayan::1594.insight: It marks a transition, preparing the listener for Viswamitra's next statement.

ramayan::1595.verse_sanskrit: महान्विघ्न: प्रवृत्तोऽयं दक्षिणामास्थितो दिशम् । दिशमन्यां प्रपत्स्यामस्तत्र तप्स्यामहे तप: । । 1612 । ।
ramayan::1595.verse_hindi: महान्विघ्न: प्रवृत्तोऽयं दक्षिणामास्थितो दिशम् । दिशमन्यां प्रपत्स्यामस्तत्र तप्स्यामहे तप: । । 1612 । ।
ramayan::1595.english_translation: A great obstacle has arisen in this southern direction. Let us go to another direction and perform austerities there.
ramayan::1595.translation_literal: महान् (great) / विघ्नः (obstacle) / प्रवृत्तः (has arisen) / अयम् (this) / दक्षिणाम् (southern) / आस्थितः (situated in) / दिशम् (direction) / दिशम् (direction) / अन्याम् (another) / प्रपत्स्यामहे (let us go) / तत्र (there) / तप्स्यामहे (we shall perform austerities) / तपः (austerity)
ramayan::1595.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1595.essence: When one direction is blocked, disciplined people simply begin again elsewhere.
ramayan::1595.simple_meaning: The sages decide to leave this southern region because a major obstacle has appeared, and continue their austerities elsewhere.
ramayan::1595.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response is not force, but a clean change of place and purpose.
ramayan::1595.detailed_meaning: After the sacrifice ends, Viswamitra sees the forest sages preparing to depart. He tells them that a great obstacle has risen in the south, so they should move to another region and continue their austerities there.
ramayan::1595.modern_relevance: You realize the place you chose for focus has turned noisy, hostile, or blocked. Instead of fighting the whole environment, you move, reset, and keep going.
ramayan::1595.insight: It teaches you to adapt your setting when obstacles make practice impossible.

ramayan::1596.verse_sanskrit: पश्चिमायां विशालायां पुष्करेषु महात्मन: । सुखं तपश्चरिष्याम: परं तद्धि तपोवनम् । । 1613 । ।
ramayan::1596.verse_hindi: O Highsouled sages, there is lake Pushkara in the vast western region. There in the forest fit for austerities we shall practise penance peacefully.
ramayan::1596.english_translation: O Highsouled sages, there is lake Pushkara in the vast western region. There in the forest fit for austerities we shall practise penance peacefully.
ramayan::1596.translation_literal: पश्चिमायां (in the western) / विशालायां (vast) / पुष्करेषु (at Pushkara) / महात्मन: (of the high-souled ones) / सुखं (peacefully) / तपश्चरिष्याम: (we shall practise austerity) / परं (excellent) / तत् (that) / हि (indeed) / तपोवनम् (forest of penance)
ramayan::1596.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::1596.essence: A disrupted practice survives by finding a better place, not by giving up.
ramayan::1596.simple_meaning: Visvamitra tells the sages to move to Pushkara, where they can continue their austerities in peace.
ramayan::1596.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response to disruption is simply to move and continue your practice.
ramayan::1596.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra sees the sages leaving after an obstacle has disrupted their rites. Rather than abandon their discipline, he directs them to Pushkara in the west, a forest suited for penance, where they can continue their austerities without disturbance.
ramayan::1596.modern_relevance: Your meditation room is noisy, the neighbors are drilling, and the day has already gone sideways. Instead of quitting, you find a quieter corner and keep going.
ramayan::1596.insight: It shifts you from reacting to interruption toward protecting the practice itself.

ramayan::1597.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा: पुष्करेषु महामुनि: । तप उग्रं दुराधर्षं तेपे मूलफलाशन: । । 1614 । ।
ramayan::1597.verse_hindi: With this the most powerful sage Viswamitra reached Pushkara where living on fruits and roots, he carried out intense, unsurpassable,  austerities.
ramayan::1597.english_translation: With this, the most radiant great sage Vishwamitra stayed in Pushkara, living on roots and fruits, and performed fierce austerities that were hard to withstand.
ramayan::1597.translation_literal: एवमुक्त्वा (having said thus) / महातेजाः (great-radiant) / पुष्करेषु (in Pushkara) / महामुनिः (great sage) / तपः (austerity) / उग्रम् (fierce) / दुराधर्षम् (hard to withstand) / तेपे (performed) / मूलफलाशनः (one eating roots and fruits)
ramayan::1597.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1597.essence: Power grows where comfort is deliberately refused.
ramayan::1597.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra goes to Pushkara and begins severe austerities, surviving on roots and fruits.
ramayan::1597.simple_insight: Real transformation often begins with quiet discipline, not dramatic speeches.
ramayan::1597.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has already decided where to go. Now the sage reaches Pushkara and throws himself into severe austerity, living only on roots and fruits. This is a scene of preparation, not revelation; the larger change comes through the practice that follows.
ramayan::1597.modern_relevance: You move to a new city, delete distractions, and wake before sunrise to rebuild yourself. The change starts long before anyone else notices.
ramayan::1597.insight: It shows that inner power is built through sustained restraint and repeated effort.

ramayan::1598.verse_sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु अयोध्याधिपतिर्नृप: । अम्बरीष इति ख्यातो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे । । 1615 । ।
ramayan::1598.verse_hindi: At this time Ambarisha, a wellknown king of Ayodhya, launched preparations for a  sacrifice.
ramayan::1598.english_translation: At this time Ambarisha, a well-known king of Ayodhya, began preparations for a sacrifice.
ramayan::1598.translation_literal: एतस्मिन् (at this) / एव (indeed) / काले (time) / तु (but) / अयोध्याधिपतिḥ (lord of Ayodhya) / नृपः (king) / अम्बरीषः (Ambarisha) / इति (thus) / ख्यातः (known) / यष्टुम् (to sacrifice) / समुपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::1598.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1598.essence: A royal ritual begins, and trouble is already moving toward it.
ramayan::1598.simple_meaning: King Ambarisha of Ayodhya began arranging a sacrifice at that same time.
ramayan::1598.simple_insight: Great events often begin with ordinary preparations.
ramayan::1598.detailed_meaning: While Vishwamitra is deep in austerity at Pushkara, the story shifts to Ayodhya. King Ambarisha starts a sacrifice, setting in motion the next chain of events that will soon draw the divine order and human effort into conflict.
ramayan::1598.modern_relevance: You are setting something important in motion, not knowing what will interfere. A plan can look clean right up until the first hidden obstacle appears.
ramayan::1598.insight: It frames the sacrifice as the starting point of a larger disruption, not a finished act.

ramayan::1599.verse_sanskrit: तस्य वै यजमानस्य पशुमिन्द्रो जहार ह । प्रणष्टे तु पशौ विप्रो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् । । 1616 । ।
ramayan::1599.verse_hindi: While he was performing the sacrifice Indra stole away the sacrificial animal. The animal could not be traced. Hence the priest said to the king:
ramayan::1599.english_translation: While he was performing the sacrifice, Indra stole away the sacrificial animal. When the animal was lost, the priest spoke to the king.
ramayan::1599.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / वै (indeed) / यजमानस्य (of the sacrificer) / पशुम् (the sacrificial animal) / इन्द्रः (Indra) / जहार (stole away) / ह (indeed) / प्रणष्टे (when lost) / तु (but) / पशौ (the animal) / विप्रः (the priest) / राजानम् (to the king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1599.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1599.essence: A sacrifice is interrupted before it can be completed.
ramayan::1599.simple_meaning: During King Ambarisha's sacrifice, Indra took away the sacrificial animal. When it disappeared, the priest informed the king.
ramayan::1599.simple_insight: Even a solemn ritual can be interrupted by forces beyond your control.
ramayan::1599.detailed_meaning: King Ambarisha has begun a sacrifice in Ayodhya. Before the rite can proceed, Indra steals the sacrificial animal, and the priest must report the loss. The verse is a plot turn that sets up the king’s next decision.
ramayan::1599.modern_relevance: You prepare everything carefully, and then one missing piece stops the whole plan. The interruption is real, and now you have to decide what comes next.
ramayan::1599.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to consequence, showing how quickly order can be broken.

ramayan::1600.verse_sanskrit: पशुरद्य हृतो राजन् प्रणष्टस्तव दुर्नयात् । अरक्षितारं राजानं घ्नन्ति दोषा नरेश्वर । । 1617 । ।
ramayan::1600.verse_hindi: O King the animal has been stolen away and because of your inability to enforce law, it could not be traced. O Lord of men the king who fails to protect (his dependents)
ramayan::1600.english_translation: O King, the animal has been stolen away and, because you failed to protect it, it is lost. O lord of men, faults destroy a king who cannot protect those under his care.
