ramayan::1648.english_translation: As time passed, the great ascetic Viswamitra became as if ashamed, consumed by worry and sorrow.
ramayan::1648.translation_literal: अथ (then) / काले (in time) / गते (having passed) / तस्मिन् (that) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (great ascetic) / सव्रीडः इव (as if ashamed) / सम्वृत्तः (became) / चिन्ताशोकपरायणः (devoted to worry and sorrow)
ramayan::1648.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1648.essence: A single attachment can undo years of discipline.
ramayan::1648.simple_meaning: Time passes, and Viswamitra is left uneasy, ashamed, and grief-stricken.
ramayan::1648.simple_insight: Even great discipline can be shaken by desire and regret.
ramayan::1648.detailed_meaning: Menaka has stayed in Viswamitra's hermitage for years, and the ascetic who once seemed unshakable is now undone by the passage of time. His inner state turns to worry, sorrow, and a kind of shame, setting up the realization that his focus has been broken.
ramayan::1648.modern_relevance: You told yourself it would be a small distraction, and then weeks were gone. Now the unfinished work sits beside the regret.
ramayan::1648.insight: It shows how desire can quietly erode discipline until regret arrives.

ramayan::1649.verse_sanskrit: बुद्धिर्मुनेस्समुत्पन्ना सामर्षा रघुनन्दन । सर्वं सुराणां कर्मैतत्तपोपहरणं महत् । । 16310 । ।
ramayan::1649.verse_hindi: O Delight of the Raghus (Rama) a sense of indignation filled the mind of the ascetic. All this is the conspiracy of the gods to deprive me of my great austerities, he thought.
ramayan::1649.english_translation: O Delight of the Raghus, indignation arose in the mind of the ascetic: “All this is the work of the radiant beings to rob me of my great austerities.”
ramayan::1649.translation_literal: बुद्धिः (thought) / मुनेः (of the ascetic) / समुत्पन्ना (arose) / सा (that) / अमर्षा (indignation) / रघुनन्दन (O delight of the Raghus) / सर्वम् (all) / सुराणाम् (of the radiant beings) / कर्म (work) / एतत् (this) / तपः-उपहरणम् (depriving of austerity) / महत् (great)
ramayan::1649.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1649.essence: Resentment can invade even the mind of a great ascetic.
ramayan::1649.simple_meaning: Viswamitra feels anger rise when he thinks the radiant beings are blocking his austerities and wasting his long effort.
ramayan::1649.simple_insight: Even deep discipline can be shaken by resentment; noticing that reaction is part of mastery.
ramayan::1649.detailed_meaning: After years in his hermitage, Viswamitra senses his austerities being interrupted. Instead of staying calm, he blames the radiant beings and feels indignation rise. This verse shows the first crack in his restraint before the next line explains his frustration.
ramayan::1649.modern_relevance: You’ve kept a hard practice going for months, then one interruption makes you furious. The real test is not the setback itself, but the story your mind builds around it.
ramayan::1649.insight: It teaches you to notice how quickly frustration can hijack disciplined effort.

ramayan::1650.verse_sanskrit: अहोरात्रापदेशेन गतास्संवत्सरा दश । काममोहाभिभूतस्य विघ्नोऽयं समुपस्थित: । । 16311 । ।
ramayan::1650.verse_hindi: Night and day deluded by lust I have wasted ten years. A hindrance has been posed (to my tapas).
ramayan::1650.english_translation: Night and day, deluded by desire, I have wasted ten years. A hindrance has now arisen against my austerity.
ramayan::1650.translation_literal: अहोरात्रापदेशेन (under the pretext of day and night) / गताः (passed) / संवत्सराः (years) / दश (ten) / काममोहाभिभूतस्य (of one overcome by desire and delusion) / विघ्नः (obstacle) / अयम् (this) / समुपस्थितः (has arisen)
ramayan::1650.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1650.essence: Unchecked desire can quietly destroy years of disciplined effort.
ramayan::1650.simple_meaning: Viswamitra admits that desire and delusion have stolen ten years of his austerity, and he sees the present obstacle as the result.
ramayan::1650.simple_insight: It hurts to realize how quietly distraction can undo years of effort.
ramayan::1650.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been delayed in his mission, and the delay has become unbearable. Looking back, he sees ten years lost to desire and confusion. The verse marks his frustration as he recognises that his own weakened resolve has allowed the obstacle to arise.
ramayan::1650.modern_relevance: You open your phone for a minute and look up to find an hour gone. The bigger loss is not the time — it is the practice you meant to protect.
ramayan::1650.insight: It shifts attention from blaming obstacles to noticing how desire erodes long-term discipline.

ramayan::1651.verse_sanskrit: विनिश्श्वसन्मुनिवर: पश्चात्तापेन दु:खित: । भीतामप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा वेपन्तीं प्राञ्जलिं स्थिताम् । । 16312 । । मेनकां मधुरैर्वाक्यैर्विसृज्य कुशिकात्मज: । उत्तरं पर्वतं राम विश्वामित्रो जगाम ह । । 16313 । ।
ramayan::1651.verse_hindi: O Rama Viswamitra, the best of ascetics sighed with repentance, distressed with grief. On seeing him, the apsara started trembling in fear. She stood before him with folded palms. (But) with sweet words the son of Kushika left her and proceeded
ramayan::1651.english_translation: The best of ascetics, Viswamitra, sighed in repentance and grief. Seeing him trembling in fear, the apsara stood with folded palms. With gentle words, the son of Kushika sent Menaka away and went on to the northern mountain.
ramayan::1651.translation_literal: विनिश्श्वसन् (sighing deeply) / मुनिवरः (the best of ascetics) / पश्चात्तापेन (with repentance) / दुःखितः (grieved) / भीताम् (the frightened one) / अप्सरसम् (the apsara) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / वेपन्तीम् (trembling) / प्राञ्जलिम् (with folded palms) / स्थिताम् (standing) / मेनाकाम् (Menaka) / मधुरैः (with sweet) / वाक्यैः (words) / विसृज्य (having dismissed) / कुशिकात्मजः (the son of Kushika) / उत्तरं (northern) / पर्वतम् (mountain) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / जगाम (went)
ramayan::1651.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1651.essence: Repentance becomes strength when it sends you back to the path.
ramayan::1651.simple_meaning: Viswamitra feels remorse after being tempted, and Menaka stands frightened before him. He dismisses her gently and continues his austerity.
ramayan::1651.simple_insight: A lapse can become a turning point when you return to discipline instead of self-pity.
ramayan::1651.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just realised that desire has interrupted years of austerity. Menaka stands before him trembling, and he answers not with anger but with restraint. This brief moment shows the cost of temptation and the decision to keep going.
ramayan::1651.modern_relevance: You notice the streak you were proud of has broken. Instead of spiralling, you breathe, reset, and return to the work with less drama and more honesty.
ramayan::1651.insight: It shows how quickly remorse can be converted into renewed discipline.

ramayan::1652.verse_sanskrit: स कृत्वा नैष्ठिकीं बुद्धिं जेतुकामो महायशा: । कौशिकीतीरमासाद्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम् । । 16314 । ।
ramayan::1652.verse_hindi: Illustrious Viswamitra took a vow of celibacy in order to control his senses. And performed rigid austerities on reaching the bank of river Kausiki.
ramayan::1652.english_translation: Illustrious Viswamitra took a vow of celibacy in order to control his senses. On reaching the bank of the Kausiki, he performed severe austerities.
ramayan::1652.translation_literal: स (he) / कृत्वा (having made) / नैष्ठिकीं (firm, vowed) / बुद्धिं (resolve) / जेतुकामो (desiring to conquer) / महायशाः (the greatly renowned one) / कौशिकीतीरम् (the bank of the Kausiki) / आसाद्य (having reached) / तपः (austerity) / तेपे (performed) / सुदारुणम् (very severe)
ramayan::1652.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1652.essence: Power begins when you stop negotiating with your senses.
ramayan::1652.simple_meaning: Viswamitra resolves to control his senses, then begins severe austerity by the Kausiki river.
ramayan::1652.simple_insight: Real strength starts when desire no longer runs the mind.
ramayan::1652.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been shaken by temptation and regret. Instead of collapsing, he turns back to discipline: a firm vow, a riverbank, and hard austerity. This is the moment he stops reacting and starts remaking himself.
ramayan::1652.modern_relevance: You delete the app, mute the chat, and still feel the pull. The real turning point comes when you make a firm decision and build a harder routine around it.
ramayan::1652.insight: It shifts discipline from an idea into a concrete act of self-mastery.

ramayan::1653.verse_sanskrit: तस्य वर्षसहस्रं तु घोरं तप उपासत: । उत्तरे पर्वते राम देवतानामभूद्भयम् । । 16315 । ।
ramayan::1653.verse_hindi: O Rama while he was performing rigorous penance for a thousand years on the northern mountains, the gods were gripped with fear. (lest he should exceed them).
ramayan::1653.english_translation: O Rama, while he was performing rigorous penance for a thousand years on the northern mountains, the gods were gripped with fear.
ramayan::1653.translation_literal: तस्य (of him) / वर्षसहस्रं (a thousand years) / तु (indeed) / घोरं (terrible, rigorous) / तपः (austerity) / उपासतः (while practising) / उत्तरे (northern) / पर्वते (on the mountain) / राम (O Rama) / देवतानाम् (of the gods) / अभूत् (became) / भयम् (fear)
ramayan::1653.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1653.essence: A thousand years of discipline made even the gods uneasy.
ramayan::1653.simple_meaning: Viswamitra kept up severe austerity for a thousand years on the northern mountain, and even the gods became afraid of his power.
ramayan::1653.simple_insight: Steady discipline can become so strong that it changes the balance around you.
ramayan::1653.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has withdrawn to the northern mountain and is grinding through an immense vow of austerity. The next verse shows why this matters: his practice has become so formidable that even the gods fear what it may produce.
ramayan::1653.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before sunrise, long after motivation has vanished. Over time, that quiet consistency can become powerful enough to unsettle even your own limits.
ramayan::1653.insight: It shifts attention from intensity to endurance: repeated restraint can transform character and capability.

ramayan::1654.verse_sanskrit: आमन्त्रयन् समागम्य सर्वे सर्षिगणा स्सुरा: । महर्षिशब्दं लभतां साध्वयं कुशिकात्मज: । । 16316 । ।
ramayan::1654.verse_hindi: After consultations the gods and sages decided that this son of Kushika (Viswamitra)  deserved the status of a Maharshi.
ramayan::1654.english_translation: After consulting together, all the gods and sages said, "Let this son of Kushika be given the title of Maharshi."
ramayan::1654.translation_literal: आमन्त्रयन् (consulting together) / समागम्य (having gathered) / सर्वे (all) / सर्षिगणाः (along with groups of sages) / सुराः (the gods) / महर्षिशब्दम् (the title Maharshi) / लभताम् (let him receive) / साधु (properly / rightly) / अयम् (this) / कुशिकात्मजः (son of Kushika)
ramayan::1654.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1654.essence: Long practice eventually earns a new identity.
ramayan::1654.simple_meaning: The gods and sages agree that Viswamitra has earned the title of great sage.
ramayan::1654.simple_insight: Real transformation is recognized by the world only after long discipline has changed you.
ramayan::1654.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already endured severe austerities for a thousand years. Now the gods and sages gather and formally acknowledge what his practice has made him: a Maharshi. The verse is a recognition step, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1654.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn, long after the excitement is gone. Then one day, the people who once doubted you quietly admit you've become someone else.
ramayan::1654.insight: It shifts attention from striving alone to the moment discipline becomes visible character.

ramayan::1655.verse_sanskrit: देवतानां वच श्शृत्वा सर्वलोकपितामह: । अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम् । । 16317 । ।
ramayan::1655.verse_hindi: Having heard the gods, the Grandsire of the worlds (Brahma) addressed  Viswamitra whose wealth was his ascetism in these sweet words.
ramayan::1655.english_translation: Having heard the gods, the Grandsire of the worlds, Brahma, addressed Vishvamitra, whose wealth was his austerity, in sweet words.
ramayan::1655.translation_literal: देवतानाम् (of the gods) / वचः (words) / शृत्वा (having heard) / सर्वलोकपितामहः (the Grandsire of all worlds) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / मधुरम् (sweet) / वाक्यम् (words) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Vishvamitra) / तपोधनम् (whose wealth is austerity)
ramayan::1655.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1655.essence: Austerity can earn the highest recognition without asking for it.
ramayan::1655.simple_meaning: Brahma hears the gods and speaks kindly to Vishvamitra, honoring the power of his austerity.
ramayan::1655.simple_insight: Deep effort changes how even the highest powers respond to you.
ramayan::1655.detailed_meaning: The gods have already agreed that Vishvamitra has earned a higher status through severe penance. Now Brahma, the Grandsire, turns to him directly. This verse is the formal opening of that recognition, just before the blessing is spoken.
ramayan::1655.modern_relevance: You keep showing up when no one is clapping, and then one day the room changes around you. The work itself has been quietly building your stature.
ramayan::1655.insight: It shifts attention from status-seeking to the inner force that earns true recognition.

ramayan::1656.verse_sanskrit: महर्षे स्वागतं वत्स तपसोग्रेण तोषित: । महत्त्वमृषिमुख्यत्वं ददामि तव कौशिक । । 16318 । ।
ramayan::1656.verse_hindi: O Maharshi O Child welcome Pleased with your intense austerities, O Son of Kushika I confer upon you the eminent rank of a great rishi (maharshi).
ramayan::1656.english_translation: O Maharshi, welcome, my child. Pleased by your intense austerities, O Kaushika, I grant you the status and eminence of the foremost among sages.
ramayan::1656.translation_literal: महर्षे (O great sage) / स्वागतं (welcome) / वत्स (my child) / तपसोग्रेण (by intense austerity) / तोषित: (pleased) / महत्त्वम् (greatness) / ऋषिमुख्यत्वम् (foremost rank among sages) / ददामि (I give) / तव (to you) / कौशिक (O Kaushika)
ramayan::1656.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1656.essence: Austere practice can elevate you beyond your original name.
ramayan::1656.simple_meaning: Brahma welcomes Vishwamitra and says his fierce austerities have earned him the highest rank among sages.
ramayan::1656.simple_insight: Real transformation is recognized, not claimed.
ramayan::1656.detailed_meaning: Brahma has already heard the gods and sages agree that Vishwamitra has earned a new standing. Now he publicly welcomes him, naming the change as the fruit of severe tapas and confirming his rise among the great rishis.
ramayan::1656.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn while no one is watching. Months later, the person you’ve become is obvious to everyone else — because your discipline has already done its work.
ramayan::1656.insight: It shifts success from status-seeking to inner formation through disciplined practice.

ramayan::1657.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मणस्स वचश्श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकेश्वरस्य ह । न विषण्णो न सन्तुष्टो विश्वामित्रस्तपोधन: । । 16319 । ।
ramayan::1657.verse_hindi: Having heard the words Brahman, the lord of all the worlds, Viswamitra whose wealth was his asceticism was neither dejected nor delighted.
ramayan::1657.english_translation: Having heard the words of Brahma, the lord of all the worlds, Viswamitra, rich in austerity, was neither dejected nor delighted.
ramayan::1657.translation_literal: ब्रह्मणः (of Brahma) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सर्वलोकेश्वरस्य (of the lord of all worlds) / ह (indeed) / न (not) / विषण्णः (dejected) / न (not) / सन्तुष्टः (delighted) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / तपोधनः (rich in austerity)
ramayan::1657.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1657.essence: Recognition need not disturb a mind that is already whole.
ramayan::1657.simple_meaning: Viswamitra receives Brahma's praise and gift without losing his balance. He neither craves more nor collapses into disappointment.
ramayan::1657.simple_insight: Real strength is staying unchanged when recognition arrives.
ramayan::1657.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just praised Viswamitra's austerity and granted him a great status. Instead of swelling with pride or sinking into need, Viswamitra remains steady. The moment reveals a mind no longer ruled by approval.
ramayan::1657.modern_relevance: You finally get the email that confirms your work mattered. Your chest tightens, but you don't need the praise to define you. You can receive it cleanly and stay yourself.
ramayan::1657.insight: It teaches you to receive success without attachment and without emotional whiplash.

ramayan::1658.verse_sanskrit: प्राञ्जलि: प्रणतो भूत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहम् । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाचं विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । । 16320 । ।
ramayan::1658.verse_hindi: Then the mighty ascetic Viswamitra bowed to Brahma, the Grandsire of all the worlds with folded hands and replied:
ramayan::1658.english_translation: Then the mighty ascetic Viswamitra bowed to Brahma, the Grandsire of all the worlds, with folded hands and replied.
ramayan::1658.translation_literal: प्राञ्जलि: (with folded hands) / प्रणतः (bowed) / भूत्वा (having become) / सर्वलोकपितामहम् (the grandsire of all worlds) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / ततः (then) / वाचम् (speech) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (the great sage)
ramayan::1658.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1658.essence: Honor lands cleanly only when humility receives it.
ramayan::1658.simple_meaning: Viswamitra responds respectfully to Brahma after hearing the honor Brahma offers him.
ramayan::1658.simple_insight: Even great achievement can be answered with humility.
ramayan::1658.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just praised Viswamitra’s severe austerities and granted him a lofty rank. Instead of swelling with pride, Viswamitra folds his hands and answers with reverence. The moment shows a seeker receiving honor without losing his restraint.
ramayan::1658.modern_relevance: You finally get the recognition you worked years for, and the first thing you do is breathe before speaking. That pause matters more than the praise.
ramayan::1658.insight: It models humility at the exact moment pride could take over.

ramayan::1659.verse_sanskrit: महर्षिशब्दमतुलं स्वार्जितै: कर्मभिश्शुभै: । यदि मे भगवानाह ततोऽहं विजितेन्द्रिय: । । 16321 । ।
ramayan::1659.verse_hindi: O Adorable one, if you have conferred the incomparable title of Maharshi earned by my auspicious deeds, I feel I have conquered the senses.
ramayan::1659.english_translation: O Adorable one, if you have conferred the incomparable title of Maharshi earned by my auspicious deeds, I feel I have conquered the senses.
ramayan::1659.translation_literal: महर्षिशब्दम् (the title Maharshi) / अतुलम् (incomparable) / स्वार्जितैः (earned by my own) / कर्मभिः (deeds) / शुभैः (auspicious) / यदि (if) / मे (to me) / भगवान् (the Adorable one) / आह (has said) / ततः (then) / अहम् (I) / विजितेन्द्रियः (one who has conquered the senses)
ramayan::1659.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1659.essence: Honor means little until your senses no longer pull you around.
ramayan::1659.simple_meaning: Real honor is not the title itself, but the inner control that makes such honor deserved.
ramayan::1659.simple_insight: Praise feels real only when your impulses no longer run your life.
ramayan::1659.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra bows before Brahma and hears himself addressed as Maharshi. He does not celebrate the title; he measures it against self-mastery. In this moment, the true test is whether his ascetic effort has actually conquered desire and impulse.
ramayan::1659.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the praise, the public recognition — and still wonder whether you've really changed. The deeper question is not who applauded you, but whether your cravings still control you.
ramayan::1659.insight: It shifts success from external recognition to inner restraint.

ramayan::1660.verse_sanskrit: तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा न तावत् त्त्वं जितेन्द्रिय: । यतस्व मुनिशार्दूल इत्युक्त्वा त्रिदिवं गत: । । 16322 । ।
ramayan::1660.verse_hindi: Then Brahma said to him, You have not conquered the senses yet. O Tiger among
ramayan::1660.english_translation: Then Brahma said to him, “You have not yet conquered the senses. Strive on, O tiger among ascetics,” and then departed to the higher realm.
ramayan::1660.translation_literal: तम् (to him) / उवाच (said) / ततः (then) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / न (not) / तावत् (yet) / त्वम् (you) / जितेन्द्रियः (one who has conquered the senses) / यतस्व (strive) / मुनिशार्दूल (tiger among ascetics) / इति (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / त्रिदिवम् (to the higher realm) / गतः (gone)
ramayan::1660.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1660.essence: Praise is not the same as completion; self-mastery still remains.
ramayan::1660.simple_meaning: Even after great achievement, Viswamitra is told that self-mastery is not complete. He must keep striving until the senses are fully conquered.
ramayan::1660.simple_insight: Real progress is measured by restraint, not praise.
ramayan::1660.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has just asked Brahma whether he has earned the title of great sage. Brahma grants the honor, but not final completion: the senses are still not fully mastered. The blessing becomes a challenge, not a finish line.
ramayan::1660.modern_relevance: You finally get praised after months of work, but the habit that distracts you is still there. The compliment is real — and so is the next round of practice.
ramayan::1660.insight: It shifts success from recognition to inner mastery.

ramayan::1661.verse_sanskrit: विप्रस्थितेषु देवेषु विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । ऊर्ध्वबाहुर्निरालम्बो वायुभक्षस्तपश्चरन् । । 16323 । ।
ramayan::1661.verse_hindi: After the departure of the gods, mighty ascetic Viswamitra raised his arms up, stood without support, subsisting on air, continuing with his austerities.
ramayan::1661.english_translation: After the departure of the gods, mighty ascetic Viswamitra raised his arms up, stood without support, subsisting on air, continuing with his austerities.
ramayan::1661.translation_literal: विप्रस्थितेषु (after having departed) / देवेषु (the gods) / विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / महामुनिः (the great sage) / ऊर्ध्वबाहुः (with arms raised upward) / निरालम्बः (without support) / वायुभक्षः (feeding on air) / तपश्चरन् (practising austerity)
ramayan::1661.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1661.essence: Lasting power is built by refusing comfort again and again.
ramayan::1661.simple_meaning: Viswamitra continues severe austerities after the gods leave, standing with raised arms and living on air.
ramayan::1661.simple_insight: Real change comes from what you repeat, not what you promise once.
ramayan::1661.detailed_meaning: The gods have departed, but Viswamitra does not stop. Alone, upright, and unmoving, he keeps his body in harsh restraint and continues his penance. The verse shows the quiet force of sustained discipline before the next stage of his transformation.
ramayan::1661.modern_relevance: You keep showing up at dawn for the practice no one applauds. The body complains, the mind bargains, but you stay with it anyway.
ramayan::1661.insight: It teaches you to value sustained restraint over dramatic effort.

ramayan::1662.verse_sanskrit: घर्मे पञ्चतपा भूत्वा वर्षास्वाकाशसंश्रय: । शिशिरे सलिलस्थायी रात्र्यहानि तपोधन: । । 16324 । । एवं वर्षसहस्रं हि तपो घोरमुपागमत् ।
ramayan::1662.verse_hindi: Viswamitra whose wealth was his penance carried on his rigid austerities for a thousand years amidst five fires, in summer, under the open sky in monsoon, and   immersed in ater night and day in winter.
ramayan::1662.english_translation: Viswamitra, whose wealth was his penance, practised terrible austerity for a thousand years: in summer among five fires, in the rains under the open sky, and in winter standing in water night and day.
ramayan::1662.translation_literal: घर्मे (in summer heat) / पञ्चतपा (with five fires) / भूत्वा (having become) / वर्षासु (in the rains) / आकाशसंश्रय: (sheltering under the open sky) / शिशिरे (in winter) / सलिलस्थायी (standing in water) / रात्र्यहानि (night and day) / तपोधन: (one whose wealth is austerity) / एवं (thus) / वर्षसहस्रं (for a thousand years) / हि (indeed) / तप: (austerity) / घोरम् (terrible) / उपागमत् (he undertook)
ramayan::1662.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1662.essence: What changes you is not passion alone, but years of chosen hardship.
ramayan::1662.simple_meaning: Viswamitra endured extreme conditions for a thousand years. He kept going through heat, rain, and winter without giving up.
ramayan::1662.simple_insight: Endurance becomes powerful when you stop bargaining with discomfort.
ramayan::1662.detailed_meaning: After the gods leave, Viswamitra keeps standing in fierce austerity. He takes on heat, rain, and winter without shelter, turning his own body into a proving ground. This verse shows the scale of the effort that forces heaven to notice him.
ramayan::1662.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for the same hard practice when no one is clapping: early runs, silent prayer, rehab exercises, one more honest conversation. Progress often belongs to the person who stays.
ramayan::1662.insight: It shifts attention from intensity to consistency: transformation comes from sustained restraint and repetition.

ramayan::1663.verse_sanskrit: तस्मिन् सन्तप्यमाने तु विश्वामित्रे महामुनौ । । 16325 । । सम्भ्रमस्सुमहानासीत्सुराणां वासवस्य च ।
ramayan::1663.verse_hindi: When the mighty asetic Viswamitra was peforming penance, the gods as well as Indra  got deeply perturbed.
ramayan::1663.english_translation: When the mighty ascetic Viswamitra was performing penance, the gods and Indra became deeply alarmed.
ramayan::1663.translation_literal: तस्मिन् (in that) / सन्तप्यमाने (while being scorched by austerity) / तु (indeed) / विश्वामित्रे (in Viswamitra) / महामुनौ (the great sage) / सम्भ्रमः (alarm) / सुमहान् (very great) / आसीत् (was) / सुराणाम् (of the gods) / वासवस्य (of Indra) / च (and)
ramayan::1663.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1663.essence: His penance was so fierce it made the heavens uneasy.
ramayan::1663.simple_meaning: Viswamitra's severe penance was so intense that even the gods and Indra grew anxious.
ramayan::1663.simple_insight: Great inner intensity can disturb even the powers that seem untouchable.
ramayan::1663.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been standing in extreme austerity for years, feeding on air and enduring heat, rain, and cold. His force is so severe that the gods and Indra themselves feel threatened. This verse sets up their reaction in the next line.
ramayan::1663.modern_relevance: You keep showing up with fierce discipline, and the room starts to change around you. Even people who seemed unshaken begin to notice your resolve.
ramayan::1663.insight: It frames discipline as a force that can unsettle complacency and provoke response.

ramayan::1664.verse_sanskrit: रम्भामप्सरसं शक्र स्सह सर्वैर्मरुद्गणै: । उवाचात्महितं वाक्यमहितं कौशिकस्य च । । 16326 । ।
ramayan::1664.verse_hindi: Indra along with all the maruts spoke to the celestial nymph Rambha, words that augured well for them and not for kaushika (Viswamitra).
ramayan::1664.english_translation: Indra, together with all the Maruts, spoke to the celestial nymph Rambha words that were beneficial for them and harmful to Kaushika.
ramayan::1664.translation_literal: रम्भाम् (to Rambha) / अप्सरसम् (the celestial nymph) / शक्रः (Indra) / सह (together with) / सर्वैः (all) / मरुद्गणैः (with the Maruts) / उवाच (spoke) / आत्महितम् (beneficial for themselves) / वाक्यम् (words) / अहितम् (harmful) / कौशिकस्य (for Kaushika) / च (and)
ramayan::1664.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1664.essence: Fearful power tries to weaken discipline before it becomes unstoppable.
ramayan::1664.simple_meaning: Indra and the Maruts ask Rambha to act in a way that will help them and hinder Viswamitra.
ramayan::1664.simple_insight: Power here is afraid of discipline and tries to break it by distraction.
ramayan::1664.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra's severe penance has shaken the heavens. Indra, worried about losing his position, turns to Rambha and the Maruts and sends her as a temptation. The verse is a setup for the larger attempt to interrupt Viswamitra's austerity.
ramayan::1664.modern_relevance: A group chat lights up when someone at work starts outperforming everyone. Instead of improving themselves, people look for ways to distract or derail the one who is focused.
ramayan::1664.insight: It shows how insecurity can turn into sabotage when someone else's discipline threatens your comfort.

ramayan::1665.verse_sanskrit: सुरकार्यमिदं रम्भे कर्तव्यं सुमहत्त्वया । लोभनं कौशिकस्येह काममोहसमन्वितम् । । 1641 । ।
ramayan::1665.verse_hindi: O Rambha you must entice Viswamitra by lust and passion. This important work
ramayan::1665.english_translation: O Rambha, you must lure Vishvamitra with desire and passion. This is a great task for you.
ramayan::1665.translation_literal: सुरकार्यम् (task of the gods) / इदम् (this) / रम्भे (O Rambha) / कर्तव्यम् (to be done) / सुमहत्त्वया (by you, who are very great) / लोभनम् (enticing) / कौशिकस्य (of Kaushika/Vishvamitra) / इह (here) / काममोहसमन्वितम् (accompanied by desire and delusion)
ramayan::1665.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1665.essence: Power tries to weaken discipline by turning attention into temptation.
ramayan::1665.simple_meaning: Indra orders Rambha to distract Vishvamitra by awakening desire in him. It is a strategic, not spiritual, moment in the story.
ramayan::1665.simple_insight: Desire is being used as a weapon, not a feeling.
ramayan::1665.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra’s austerities have alarmed the gods, especially Indra. To protect their own position, Indra instructs Rambha to seduce the sage and break his concentration. The verse is part of a tactical exchange, not a teaching.
ramayan::1665.modern_relevance: A room full of people quietly decides to derail the one person who is finally getting serious. The verse captures how fear can turn into manipulation.
ramayan::1665.insight: It shows how insecurity looks when it becomes interference.

ramayan::1666.verse_sanskrit: तथोक्ता साऽप्सरा राम सहस्राक्षेण धीमता । व्रीडिता प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं प्रत्युवाच सुरेश्वरम् । । 1642 । ।
ramayan::1666.verse_hindi: O Rama, to these words of the sagacious, thousandeyed Lord of the gods (Indra) that apsara with folded hands bashfully replied:
ramayan::1666.english_translation: Then that apsara, addressed by the wise thousand-eyed Indra, bashfully replied with folded hands to the lord of the gods.
ramayan::1666.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / उक्ता (spoken to) / सा (she) / अप्सरा (apsara) / राम (O Rama) / सहस्राक्षेण (by the thousand-eyed one) / धीमता (by the wise one) / व्रीडिता (ashamed) / प्राञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / वाक्यम् (speech) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / सुरेश्वरम् (to the lord of the gods)
ramayan::1666.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1666.essence: She answers under pressure, knowing the request is dangerous.
ramayan::1666.simple_meaning: Rambha, shy and respectful, answers Indra after he orders her to approach Vishwamitra.
ramayan::1666.simple_insight: Even a brief reply can carry fear, shame, and the weight of what comes next.
ramayan::1666.detailed_meaning: Indra has just instructed Rambha to distract Vishvamitra for the sake of the gods. This verse only shows her reaction: she stands before him, ashamed, hands folded, and begins to answer. The real action comes in the next line.
ramayan::1666.modern_relevance: You get a message from someone powerful, and your stomach drops before you even reply. The pause, the folded hands, the careful words — all of it is already part of the pressure.
ramayan::1666.insight: It shows how obedience can begin with hesitation, not confidence.

ramayan::1667.verse_sanskrit: अयं सुरपते घोरो विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । घोरमुत्सृजते क्रोधं मयि देव न संशय: । । 1643 । । ततो हि मे भयं देव प्रासादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।
ramayan::1667.verse_hindi: Lord of the devatas this mighty ascetic Viswamitra is a terrible person. He will ceratinly release on his dreadful anger (curse me). O Lord this is my apprehension. You should excuse me.
ramayan::1667.english_translation: Lord of the devas, this great ascetic Vishvamitra is terrible. He will surely unleash dreadful anger on me. I fear that, divine one; you should pardon me.
ramayan::1667.translation_literal: अयं (this) / सुरपते (O lord of the devas) / घोरः (terrible) / विश्वामित्रः (Vishvamitra) / महामुनिः (great ascetic) / घोरम् (dreadful) / उत्सृजते (will release) / क्रोधम् (anger) / मयि (on me) / देव (divine one) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / ततः (therefore) / हि (indeed) / मे (my) / भयम् (fear) / देव (divine one) / प्रासादम् (pardon) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you should)
ramayan::1667.speaker: Rambha
ramayan::1667.essence: A forced task becomes terrifying when you know the cost.
ramayan::1667.simple_meaning: Rambha is afraid of Vishvamitra's anger and asks Indra to forgive her for the task he assigned.
ramayan::1667.simple_insight: Fear makes even a small mistake feel enormous.
ramayan::1667.detailed_meaning: Indra has ordered Rambha to distract Vishvamitra. She hesitates, knowing the sage's power and wrath. This verse is her plea of fear to Indra, not a teaching on its own, but a step in the larger episode.
ramayan::1667.modern_relevance: You realize too late that a request from authority could cost you more than you expected. The apology comes after the fear has already arrived.
ramayan::1667.insight: It shows how obedience to pressure can collide with conscience and fear.

ramayan::1668.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तया राम रम्भया भीतया तदा । । 1644 । । तामुवाच सहस्राक्षो वेपमानां कृताञ्जलिम् ।
ramayan::1668.verse_hindi: O Rama having heard Rambha trembling in fear and standing with folded palms, Indra spoke:
ramayan::1668.english_translation: O Rama, having heard Rambha trembling in fear and standing with folded palms, Indra spoke:
ramayan::1668.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (having been spoken to thus) / तया (by her) / राम (O Rama) / रम्भया (by Rambha) / भीतया (by the frightened one) / तदा (then) / ताम् (to her) / उवाच (spoke) / सहस्राक्षः (the thousand-eyed one, Indra) / वेपमानाम् (trembling) / कृताञ्जलिम् (with folded hands)
ramayan::1668.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1668.essence: The real message comes after the silence, not before it.
ramayan::1668.simple_meaning: Rambha stands before Indra, frightened and trembling with folded hands, and Indra answers her.
ramayan::1668.simple_insight: Fear changes the whole tone of a conversation.
ramayan::1668.detailed_meaning: Rambha, shaken by what she has heard, stands before Indra with folded hands. This verse is only the transition into his reply, not the teaching itself. It sets the emotional scene for the next line.
ramayan::1668.modern_relevance: You can feel the shift in a room before anyone speaks. A trembling voice, folded hands, and one careful reply change everything.
ramayan::1668.insight: It prepares the listener for the next statement rather than delivering the point itself.

ramayan::1669.verse_sanskrit: माभैषी रम्भे भद्रं ते कुरुष्व मम शासनम् । । 1645 । । कोकिलो हृदयग्राही माधवे रुचिरद्रुमे । अहं कन्दर्पसहित स्स्थास्यामि तव पार्श्वत: । । 1646 । ।
ramayan::1669.verse_hindi: O Rambha have no fear. Feel safe. Carry out my order. When the trees look so beautiful in spring I shall in captivating the form of a cuckoo, stay by your side in the company of Kamadeva (Cupid).
ramayan::1669.english_translation: O Rambha, do not be afraid. All will be well. Carry out my command. In the beautiful spring forest, I will remain beside you with Kama, taking the alluring form of a cuckoo.
ramayan::1669.translation_literal: मा भैषीः (do not fear) / रम्भे (O Rambha) / भद्रं (well-being) / ते (for you) / कुरुष्व (do) / मम (my) / शासनम् (command) / कोकिलः (cuckoo) / हृदयग्राही (heart-seizing) / माधवे (in spring) / रुचिरद्रुमे (in the beautiful trees) / अहम् (I) / कन्दर्पसहितः (with Kama) / स्थास्यामि (will stay) / तव (your) / पार्श्वतः (by the side)
ramayan::1669.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1669.essence: Reassurance becomes manipulation when desire is in control.
ramayan::1669.simple_meaning: Indra reassures Rambha and tells her to obey him. He promises to stay near her in the spring forest, taking an alluring form to help his plan.
ramayan::1669.simple_insight: Charm can be used as a weapon when desire is steering the mind.
ramayan::1669.detailed_meaning: Rambha is trembling after warning Indra about Viswamitra's anger. Indra answers not with restraint, but with seduction and strategy, ordering her to distract the ascetic. This is the moment the episode turns from warning into manipulation.
ramayan::1669.modern_relevance: Someone smiles and says, “Don’t worry, just do this for me,” while asking you to help cover a bad decision. The comfort sounds gentle; the motive is not.
ramayan::1669.insight: It reveals how desire can dress itself as reassurance and command others into harm.

ramayan::1670.verse_sanskrit: त्वं हि रूपं बहुगुणं कृत्वा परमभास्वरम् । तमृषिं कौशिकं रम्भे भेदयस्व तपस्विनम् । । 1647 । ।
ramayan::1670.verse_hindi: O Rambha displaying many (romantic) gestures and assuming a fascinating form, distract the mighty ascetic, Kausika (Viswamitra).
ramayan::1670.english_translation: O Rambha, taking on a radiant and irresistible form, distract the ascetic Vishvamitra.
ramayan::1670.translation_literal: त्वम् (you) / हि (indeed) / रूपम् (form) / बहुगुणम् (full of many qualities) / कृत्वा (having made) / परमभास्वरम् (supremely radiant) / तम् (that) / ऋषिम् (sage) / कौशिकम् (Kausika) / रम्भे (O Rambha) / भेदयस्व (distract, break apart) / तपस्विनम् (the ascetic)
ramayan::1670.speaker: Indra
ramayan::1670.essence: Fear attacks strength by sending distraction in beautiful form.
ramayan::1670.simple_meaning: Indra orders Rambha to use her beauty to disturb Vishvamitra, the ascetic.
ramayan::1670.simple_insight: Desire can be used as a weapon against discipline.
ramayan::1670.detailed_meaning: Indra, afraid of Vishvamitra's growing power, sends Rambha to break his austerity. This verse is the command itself: create a dazzling form and unsettle the ascetic. The real conflict is not romance but fear of spiritual force.
ramayan::1670.modern_relevance: A colleague sees your focus and tries to pull you into gossip, drama, or distraction. The pressure is not random — it targets the very discipline that makes you strong.
ramayan::1670.insight: It shows how insecurity tries to sabotage discipline by weaponising attraction and distraction.

ramayan::1671.verse_sanskrit: सा श्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कृत्वा रूपमनुत्तमम् । लोभयामास ललिता विश्वामित्रं शुचिस्मिता । । 1648 । ।
ramayan::1671.verse_hindi: At these words (of Indra), Rambha, assumed any form of excellent beauty and with a bright smile set out to allure Viswamitra.
ramayan::1671.english_translation: At these words of Indra, Rambha assumed a form of excellent beauty and, with a bright smile, set out to allure Viswamitra.
ramayan::1671.translation_literal: सा (she) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / वचनं (the words) / तस्य (of him) / कृत्वा (having made) / रूपम् (form) / अनुत्तमम् (supreme, excellent) / लोभयामास (began to allure) / ललिता (graceful, charming) / विश्वामित्रम् (Viswamitra) / शुचिस्मिता (with a pure smile)
ramayan::1671.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1671.essence: Beauty here is not grace; it is strategy.
ramayan::1671.simple_meaning: Rambha hears Indra's command, changes her appearance, and goes to distract Viswamitra.
ramayan::1671.simple_insight: Not every beautiful thing is innocent; some beauty is sent to disturb your focus.
ramayan::1671.detailed_meaning: Indra has decided that Viswamitra must be interrupted. Rambha obeys, takes on a dazzling form, and moves toward the ascetic as a deliberate distraction. The verse is a step in a larger trap, not its teaching.
ramayan::1671.modern_relevance: A flattering message arrives just when you're finally focused. The interruption is not random — it is designed to pull your attention away from what matters.
ramayan::1671.insight: It shows how desire can be used as a weapon against discipline.

ramayan::1672.verse_sanskrit: कोकिलस्य च शुश्राव वल्गु व्याहरत: स्वनम् । सम्प्रहृष्टेन मनसा तत एनामुदैक्षत । । 1649 । ।
ramayan::1672.verse_hindi: Excited by the charming warble of the cuckoo, Viswamitra opened his eyes.
ramayan::1672.english_translation: Excited by the charming warble of the cuckoo, Vishwamitra opened his eyes.
ramayan::1672.translation_literal: कोकिलस्य (of the cuckoo) / च (and) / शुश्राव (heard) / वल्गु (charming) / व्याहरत: (speaking or warbling) / स्वनम् (sound) / सम्प्रहृष्टेन (with delighted) / मनसा (mind) / ततः (then) / एनाम् (her) / उदैक्षत (looked at)
ramayan::1672.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1672.essence: Even a disciplined mind can be nudged open by beauty.
ramayan::1672.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra, hearing the cuckoo's sweet call, became delighted and looked toward Rambha.
ramayan::1672.simple_insight: A single pleasant sound can loosen even hard discipline for a moment.
ramayan::1672.detailed_meaning: Indra has sent Rambha to disturb Vishwamitra's austerity. The verse shows the first crack: a cuckoo's sweet call lifts his attention and turns his mind outward, making him look at her. It is a small sensory opening before the larger temptation takes hold.
ramayan::1672.modern_relevance: You are deep in focus, then one soft notification, one attractive voice note, one familiar song pulls your attention off course.
ramayan::1672.insight: It shows how distraction often begins with a tiny, pleasant shift in attention.

ramayan::1673.verse_sanskrit: अथ तस्य च शब्देन गीतेनाप्रतिमेन च । दर्शनेन च रम्भाया मुनिस्सन्देहमागत: । । 16410 । ।
ramayan::1673.verse_hindi: On hearing the sound of the incomparable song of the cuckoo along with the  sight of Rambha, a doubt arose in the mind of the ascetic.
ramayan::1673.english_translation: On hearing the sound of the incomparable song of the cuckoo along with the sight of Rambha, a doubt arose in the mind of the ascetic.
ramayan::1673.translation_literal: अथ (then) / तस्य (for him) / च (and) / शब्देन (by the sound) / गीतेन (by the song) / अप्रतिमेन (incomparable) / च (and) / दर्शनेन (by the sight) / च (and) / रम्भाया (of Rambha) / मुनिः (the ascetic) / सन्देहम् (doubt) / आगतः (came upon)
ramayan::1673.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1673.essence: A single moment of beauty can crack a disciplined mind.
ramayan::1673.simple_meaning: The ascetic became uncertain when he heard the cuckoo's song and saw Rambha.
ramayan::1673.simple_insight: Attraction can unsettle even a disciplined mind in an instant.
ramayan::1673.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already been tempted by Indra's plan. Rambha appears with beauty and the cuckoo's song fills the air. In that charged moment, uncertainty enters the sage's mind before anger follows.
ramayan::1673.modern_relevance: You are focused, then one message, one face, one sound breaks the spell. The mind wavers before you even notice what pulled it.
ramayan::1673.insight: It shows how sensory beauty can interrupt concentration and create inner confusion before reason catches up.

ramayan::1674.verse_sanskrit: सहस्राक्षस्य तत्कर्म विज्ञाय मुनिपुङ्गव: । रम्भां क्रोधसमाविष्ट श्शशाप कुशिकात्मज: । । 16411 । ।
ramayan::1674.verse_hindi: Son of Kushika, the eminent ascetic knew it was the work of Indra. Seized with anger,
ramayan::1674.english_translation: Knowing it was Indra's doing, the great sage, son of Kushika, seized by anger, cursed Rambha.
ramayan::1674.translation_literal: सहस्राक्षस्य (of the thousand-eyed one, Indra's) / तत् (that) / कर्म (deed, act) / विज्ञाय (having known) / मुनि-पुङ्गवः (the foremost sage) / रम्भाम् (Rambha) / क्रोध-समाविष्टः (filled with anger) / शशाप (cursed) / कुशिकात्मजः (son of Kushika)
ramayan::1674.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1674.essence: A tested mind can still be shaken when temptation comes dressed as beauty.
ramayan::1674.simple_meaning: Viswamitra realizes that Indra sent Rambha to disturb him, and in anger he curses her.
ramayan::1674.simple_insight: Even disciplined minds can flare when tested at the edge of desire.
ramayan::1674.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has been drawn out of his meditation by Rambha's presence and the cuckoo's song. In this moment, he sees Indra's hand behind the temptation and, angered by the interruption, curses her.
ramayan::1674.modern_relevance: You finally spot who was stirring the room, and your calm breaks. The reaction is human, even for someone trained to stay above it.
ramayan::1674.insight: It shows how quickly unresolved desire can turn into anger when restraint is challenged.

ramayan::1675.verse_sanskrit: यन्मां लोभयसे रम्भे कामक्रोधजयैषिणम् । दशवर्षसहस्राणि शैली स्थास्यसि दुर्भगे । । 16412 । ।
ramayan::1675.verse_hindi: O luckless Rambha, since you have endeavoured to distract me from my desire to conquer  wrath and passion, you shall turn into a rock and remain so for ten thousand years.
ramayan::1675.english_translation: O luckless Rambha, since you have tried to tempt me away from my resolve to conquer desire and anger, you shall become a stone and remain so for ten thousand years.
ramayan::1675.translation_literal: यत् (since) / माम् (me) / लोभयसे (you tempt) / रम्भे (O Rambha) / काम-क्रोध-जयैषिणम् (one seeking victory over desire and anger) / दश-वर्ष-सहस्राणि (ten thousand years) / शैली (as a stone) / स्थास्यसि (you will remain) / दुर्भगे (O unfortunate one)
ramayan::1675.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1675.essence: A steady vow treats temptation as a real threat, not a harmless interruption.
ramayan::1675.simple_meaning: Trying to distract a person who is committed to mastering desire and anger brings severe consequences. The verse shows how seriously ascetic discipline is guarded.
ramayan::1675.simple_insight: Self-mastery is not fragile when it is real; distractions lose their power against a steady vow.
ramayan::1675.detailed_meaning: Rambha has tried to disturb the sage's austerity. The sage sees the temptation as an attack on his hard-won control over desire and anger, and he curses her to become stone for ten thousand years.
ramayan::1675.modern_relevance: You finally get into a good rhythm with meditation, training, or therapy, and then one message, one flirtation, one old habit tries to yank you back. The verse treats that interruption as serious.
ramayan::1675.insight: It teaches you to protect long practice from the first pull of temptation.

ramayan::1676.verse_sanskrit: ब्राह्मण स्सुमहातेजा स्तपोबलसमन्वित: । उद्धरिष्यति रम्भे त्वां मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृताम् । । 16413 । ।
ramayan::1676.verse_hindi: O Rambha an effulgent brahmin, endowed with the power of asceticism, will liberate you from this state into which you have fallen on account of my anger.
ramayan::1676.english_translation: O Rambha, a radiant brahmin, endowed with the power of austerity, will free you from the state into which you have fallen because of my anger.
ramayan::1676.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणः (brahmin) / स्सुमहातेजाः (very radiant) / तपोबलसमन्वितः (endowed with the power of austerity) / उद्धरिष्यति (will lift out, will free) / रम्भे (O Rambha) / त्वाम् (you) / मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृताम् (made impure by my anger)
ramayan::1676.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1676.essence: Anger harms first, and discipline must clean up its wake.
ramayan::1676.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra says another radiant ascetic will free Rambha from the harm caused by his anger.
ramayan::1676.simple_insight: Unchecked anger spreads harm, and even a great sage must answer for it.
ramayan::1676.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has just cursed Rambha after Indra sent her to distract him. In his anger, he admits that another ascetic, stronger in austerity, will eventually release her from the condition his fury has caused. The moment shows his loss of control.
ramayan::1676.modern_relevance: You said something sharp in a flash of anger, and now you can already see the damage. Even a disciplined person has to face what rage leaves behind.
ramayan::1676.insight: It shifts the mind from righteous fury to responsibility for its consequences.

ramayan::1677.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । अशक्नुवन् धारयितुं क्रोधं सन्तापमागत: । । 16414 । ।
ramayan::1677.verse_hindi: The brilliant Viswamitra, the great ascetic, now experienced remorse for his inability to contain anger.
ramayan::1677.english_translation: Having spoken thus, the brilliant great sage Vishvamitra was unable to restrain his anger and was overcome with distress.
ramayan::1677.translation_literal: एवमुक्त्वा (having spoken thus) / महातेजा (very brilliant) / विश्वामित्रो (Vishvamitra) / महामुनिः (great sage) / अशक्नुवन् (being unable) / धारयितुम् (to restrain) / क्रोधम् (anger) / सन्तापम् (distress) / आगत: (came upon)
ramayan::1677.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1677.essence: A moment of anger can undo years of self-mastery.
ramayan::1677.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra speaks in anger, then immediately feels the pain of not being able to control it.
ramayan::1677.simple_insight: Even great strength can be shaken by anger when restraint fails.
ramayan::1677.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just cursed Rambha after she tried to distract him. In the next instant, the great sage feels the sting of his own anger and the loss of self-command. The verse shows the cost of a mind that breaks its own discipline.
ramayan::1677.modern_relevance: You send the sharp message, then sit staring at the screen, already regretting it. The wound is not just what you said — it is losing command of yourself.
ramayan::1677.insight: It shifts attention from anger's target to the damage done by losing restraint.

ramayan::1678.verse_sanskrit: तस्य शापेन महता रम्भा शैली तदाऽभवत् । वचश्शृत्वा च कन्दर्पो महर्षेस्स च निर्गत: । । 16415 । ।
ramayan::1678.verse_hindi: This mighty curse, of the great saint transformed Rambha into a rock and sent Kamadeva and Indra to their heels.
ramayan::1678.english_translation: By that great curse, Rambha became a stone. Hearing those words, Kamadeva and Indra withdrew from the great sage.
ramayan::1678.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / शापेन (by the curse) / महता (great) / रम्भा (Rambha) / शैली (stone-like) / तदा (then) / अभवत् (became) / वचः (words) / शृत्वा (having heard) / च (and) / कन्दर्पः (Kamadeva) / च (and) / निर्गतः (departed/withdrew) / महर्षेः (from the great sage)
ramayan::1678.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1678.essence: Unchecked anger turns speech into irreversible force.
ramayan::1678.simple_meaning: Rambha is cursed and turned to stone, and the heavenly beings withdraw after hearing the sage's words.
ramayan::1678.simple_insight: A single uncontrolled moment can harden into lasting consequence.
ramayan::1678.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra's anger has just been provoked, and his curse lands with force. Rambha is turned into stone, while Kamadeva and Indra recoil from the power of the sage's words. The verse shows the immediate aftermath of his loss of restraint.
ramayan::1678.modern_relevance: One harsh message sent in anger can freeze a relationship for years. The damage is not abstract — it lands immediately and changes what comes next.
ramayan::1678.insight: It shifts attention from emotion to consequence: anger does not stay inside; it alters the world around you.

ramayan::1679.verse_sanskrit: कोपेन स महातेजास्तपोऽपहरणे कृते । इन्द्रियैरजितै राम न लेभे शान्तिमात्मन: । । 16416 । ।
ramayan::1679.verse_hindi: O Rama highly powerful Viswamitra was deprived of his ascetic merit due to his
ramayan::1679.english_translation: O Rama, the mighty Visvamitra, angered and deprived of the fruit of his austerity, could not find peace within himself because his senses were still unconquered.
ramayan::1679.translation_literal: कोपेन (by anger) / सः (he) / महातेजाः (highly powerful one) / तपः-अपहरणे (when the fruit of austerity was taken away) / कृते (having been done) / इन्द्रियैः (by the senses) / अजितैः (unconquered) / राम (O Rama) / न (not) / लेभे (found) / शान्तिम् (peace) / आत्मनः (of his own self)
ramayan::1679.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1679.essence: Unmastered senses can undo even hard-won strength.
ramayan::1679.simple_meaning: Visvamitra lost his inner peace because anger and uncontrolled senses overpowered him after his austerity was disrupted.
ramayan::1679.simple_insight: Even great discipline can be shaken when anger gets the upper hand.
ramayan::1679.detailed_meaning: After Rambha’s curse and the disturbance of his austerities, Visvamitra stands in remorse before Rama. His power is real, but so is his weakness: uncontrolled anger has broken his inner steadiness. The verse shows the cost of failing to master the senses.
ramayan::1679.modern_relevance: You hold your tongue all day, then one sharp message undoes you in a minute. Strength is not having power — it is keeping your center when provoked.
ramayan::1679.insight: It teaches you that spiritual or personal power means little without control over reaction.

ramayan::1680.verse_sanskrit: बभूवास्य मनश्चिन्ता तपोऽपहरणे कृते । नैव क्रोधं गमिष्यामि न च वक्ष्ये कथञ्चन । । 16417 । ।
ramayan::1680.verse_hindi: Having been deprived of his ascetic merit, he resolved not to lose his temper nor ever breathe a word.
ramayan::1680.english_translation: Having been deprived of his ascetic merit, he resolved not to lose his temper nor ever breathe a word.
ramayan::1680.translation_literal: बभूव (became) / अस्य (his) / मनःचिन्ता (mental concern) / तपः-अपहरणे (when ascetic merit was taken away) / कृते (having been done) / नैव (not at all) / क्रोधम् (anger) / गमिष्यामि (I shall go into) / न (not) / च (and) / वक्ष्ये (I shall speak) / कथञ्चन (in any way)
ramayan::1680.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1680.essence: He answers injury with restraint, not retaliation.
ramayan::1680.simple_meaning: Viswamitra, angered by the loss of his ascetic power, decides not to lose control or speak rashly.
ramayan::1680.simple_insight: Real strength can look like restraint when provoked.
ramayan::1680.detailed_meaning: After Rambha is cursed and the gods retreat, Viswamitra feels the wound of losing hard-earned ascetic power. In that charged moment, he makes a hard choice: no anger, no impulsive speech, only discipline.
ramayan::1680.modern_relevance: Your message gets ignored after weeks of effort, and the first urge is to fire back. This verse points to the harder victory: hold your tongue when pride wants release.
ramayan::1680.insight: It teaches you to interrupt reactivity before it becomes words or action.

ramayan::1681.verse_sanskrit: अथवा नोच्छवसिष्यामि संवत्सरशतान्यपि । अहं विशोषयिष्यामि ह्यात्मानं विजितेन्द्रिय: । । 16418 । ।
ramayan::1681.verse_hindi: Further, I shall not even inhale for hundreds of years. I shall conquer my senses and dry up this body.
ramayan::1681.english_translation: Further, I shall not even inhale for hundreds of years. I shall conquer my senses and dry up this body.
ramayan::1681.translation_literal: अथवा (further) / न (not) / उच्छवसिष्यामि (I shall inhale/breathe) / संवत्सरशतान्यपि (even hundreds of years) / अहम् (I) / विशोषयिष्यामि (shall dry up) / हि (indeed) / आत्मानम् (myself/body) / विजितेन्द्रियः (having conquered the senses)
ramayan::1681.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1681.essence: He answers inner defeat with even fiercer discipline.
ramayan::1681.simple_meaning: Viswamitra resolves to endure extreme austerity, even to the point of stopping his breath, until he fully masters his senses.
ramayan::1681.simple_insight: Real strength can mean refusing every impulse until the mind is no longer ruled by them.
ramayan::1681.detailed_meaning: After losing the merit of his austerities, Viswamitra does not soften. He hardens his resolve instead, vowing to stop breathing and wear down his body until his senses are fully conquered.
ramayan::1681.modern_relevance: You are angry after being cut off in traffic, and your chest is hot with the urge to react. This verse points to a harder freedom: not feeding the impulse at all until it loses power.
ramayan::1681.insight: It shifts attention from immediate reaction to long-term self-mastery through restraint.

ramayan::1682.verse_sanskrit: तावद्यावद्धि मे प्राप्तं ब्राह्मण्यं तपसाऽऽर्जितम् । अनुच्छवसन्नभुञ्जान स्तिष्ठेयं शाश्वतीस्समा: । । 16419 । । न हि मे तप्यमानस्य क्षयं यास्यन्ति मूर्तय: ।
ramayan::1682.verse_hindi: Until brahminhood is obtained by my austerities, I shall stay without breathing or eating for innumerable years. While performing penance, my limbs shall not undergo deterioration.
ramayan::1682.english_translation: Until brahminhood is obtained by my austerities, I shall stay without breathing or eating for innumerable years. While performing penance, my limbs shall not undergo deterioration.
ramayan::1682.translation_literal: तावत् (until then) / यावत् (as long as) / हि (indeed) / मे (for me) / प्राप्तम् (attained) / ब्राह्मण्यम् (brahminhood) / तपसा (by austerity) / आर्जितम् (earned) / अनुच्छवसन् (without breathing) / अभुञ्जान (without eating) / तिष्ठेयम् (I shall remain) / शाश्वतीः (endless) / समाः (years) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / मे (for me) / तप्यमानस्य (while undergoing penance) / क्षयम् (deterioration) / यास्यन्ति (will go) / मूर्तयः (limbs/bodies)
ramayan::1682.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1682.essence: A vow becomes real when comfort is no longer the measure.
ramayan::1682.simple_meaning: He vows to continue severe austerity without food or breath until he achieves the spiritual status he seeks.
ramayan::1682.simple_insight: Real change asks for endurance, not convenience.
ramayan::1682.detailed_meaning: A great ascetic has already resolved not to lose his temper, speak, eat, or even breathe. Now he pushes the vow further: he will stay in penance for endless years until he earns brahminhood, and he trusts that the practice will not destroy him.
ramayan::1682.modern_relevance: You start a hard training plan, then every part of you wants relief by day three. This verse speaks to the part of you that keeps the promise after the excitement is gone.
ramayan::1682.insight: It shifts effort from short-term comfort to long-term transformation.

ramayan::1683.verse_sanskrit: एवं वर्षसहस्रस्य दीक्षां स मुनिपुङ्गव: । । 16420 । । चकाराप्रतिमां लोके प्रतिज्ञां रघुनन्दन ।
ramayan::1683.verse_hindi: O Descendant of Raghu in this way that eminent ascetic took an unprecedented vow to practise penance for a thousand years.
ramayan::1683.english_translation: In this way, that eminent ascetic made an unprecedented vow to practise penance for a thousand years, O descendant of Raghu.
ramayan::1683.translation_literal: एवम् (in this way) / वर्षसहस्रस्य (of a thousand years) / दीक्षाम् (vow of discipline) / सः (that) / मुनिपुङ्गवः (eminent ascetic) / चकार (made) / अप्रतिमाम् (unprecedented) / लोके (in the world) / प्रतिज्ञाम् (vow) / रघुनन्दन (O descendant of Raghu)
ramayan::1683.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1683.essence: A true vow is measured by what it costs over time.
ramayan::1683.simple_meaning: Visvamitra takes a vow to undergo severe penance for a thousand years. It is an extraordinary commitment, unlike anything seen before.
ramayan::1683.simple_insight: Some promises are so serious they reshape a whole life.
ramayan::1683.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has already declared that he will conquer hunger, breath, and bodily weakness through austerity. Here, the vow is formally sealed: a thousand years of penance, unmatched in the world. The moment shows the scale of his resolve before the longer ordeal begins.
ramayan::1683.modern_relevance: You decide, in one quiet moment, to stop drifting and commit for real. The calendar looks ordinary, but your life is already changing shape.
ramayan::1683.insight: It shows how a single vow can turn intention into a long, disciplined practice.

ramayan::1684.verse_sanskrit: अथ हैमवतीं राम दिशं त्यक्त्वा महामुनि: । पूर्वां दिशमनुप्राप्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम् । । 1651 । ।
ramayan::1684.verse_hindi: O Rama thereafter the great ascetic (Viswamitra), abandoning the north of the Himavat mountain reached the eastern quarter and performed rigorous austerities.
ramayan::1684.english_translation: O Rama, thereafter the great ascetic Vishwamitra left the northern region of Himavat, reached the eastern quarter, and performed severe austerities.
ramayan::1684.translation_literal: अथ (thereafter) / हैमवतीं (of Himavat, northern) / राम (O Rama) / दिशं (region/quarter) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / महामुनि: (the great ascetic) / पूर्वां (eastern) / दिशम् (quarter/region) / अनुप्राप्य (having reached) / तपः (austerity) / तेपे (performed) / सुदारुणम् (very severe)
ramayan::1684.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1684.essence: He carried his austerity wherever he went.
ramayan::1684.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra moved from the northern region to the east and continued his harsh austerities there.
ramayan::1684.simple_insight: Great discipline does not stop when the place changes.
ramayan::1684.detailed_meaning: After his long vow, Vishwamitra leaves the northern Himalaya region and goes east to continue his austerities. The verse is a transition, not the teaching itself: it shows his relentless movement and the severity of the penance that prepares the ground for Rama's training.
ramayan::1684.modern_relevance: You change cities, routines, even whole seasons of life — and the unresolved work still follows you. The place shifts, but the discipline has to travel with you.
ramayan::1684.insight: It shifts attention from location to continuity of practice.

ramayan::1685.verse_sanskrit: मौनं वर्षसहस्रस्य कृत्वा व्रतमनुत्तमम् । चकाराप्रतिमं राम तप: परमदुष्करम् । । 1652 । ।
ramayan::1685.verse_hindi: Having observed a unique vow of silence for a thousand years, O Rama he practised unprecedented and extremely difficult austerities.
ramayan::1685.english_translation: Having observed a unique vow of silence for a thousand years, O Rama, he practised unprecedented and extremely difficult austerities.
ramayan::1685.translation_literal: मौनं (silence) / वर्षसहस्रस्य (of a thousand years) / कृत्वा (having done) / व्रतम् (vow) / अनुत्तमम् (supreme) / चकार (did) / अप्रतिमम् (matchless) / राम (O Rama) / तपः (austerity) / परमदुष्करम् (extremely difficult)
ramayan::1685.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1685.essence: Silence and austerity can become a force stronger than impulse.
ramayan::1685.simple_meaning: He kept complete silence for a thousand years and carried out severe austerities of unmatched difficulty.
ramayan::1685.simple_insight: Great discipline is often invisible before it becomes powerful.
ramayan::1685.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has already left the Himalayas and taken up his penance in the eastern direction. This verse adds the scale of his restraint: a thousand years of silence and severe austerity, showing the extraordinary force of his resolve before the next result appears.
ramayan::1685.modern_relevance: You delete the message, close the app, and sit with the discomfort instead of reacting. That quiet restraint is its own strength.
ramayan::1685.insight: It shows that steady restraint can be more powerful than dramatic action.

ramayan::1686.verse_sanskrit: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु काष्ठभूतं महामुनिम् । विघ्नैर्बहुभिराधूतं क्रोधो नान्तर आविशत् । । 1653 । । स कृत्वा निश्चयं राम तप आतिष्टदव्ययम् ।
ramayan::1686.verse_hindi: After completion of a thousand years the great ascetic became a piece of wood. In spite of many impediments, he was unshaken, anger did not enter into his mind. O Rama with firm determination he practised  austerities.
ramayan::1686.english_translation: After a thousand years, the great ascetic had become like a piece of wood. Though many obstacles shook him, anger never entered his mind. With firm resolve, he continued his undying austerity.
ramayan::1686.translation_literal: पूर्णे (completed) / वर्षसहस्रे (a thousand years) / तु (then) / काष्ठभूतं (become like wood) / महामुनिम् (the great ascetic) / विघ्नैः (by obstacles) / बहुभिः (many) / आधूतं (shaken) / क्रोधः (anger) / न (not) / अन्तरे (inside) / आविशत् (entered) / सः (he) / कृत्वा (having made) / निश्चयम् (firm resolve) / राम (O Rama) / तपः (austerity) / आतिष्टत् (practised) / अव्ययम् (undying)
ramayan::1686.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1686.essence: Steady resolve can make even anger powerless.
ramayan::1686.simple_meaning: Viswamitra's years of austerity had made him completely steady. No obstacle could shake him, and anger never entered his mind.
ramayan::1686.simple_insight: Real discipline makes you less reactive, not just more productive.
ramayan::1686.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has spent a thousand years in severe austerity after leaving the Himalayan region and turning eastward. Now, in the midst of repeated obstacles, he remains unmoved. This verse marks the inner victory that makes his vow complete.
ramayan::1686.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for meditation, training, or recovery even when nothing feels dramatic. The real win is not intensity — it is becoming someone who no longer breaks under delay, irritation, or resistance.
ramayan::1686.insight: It shifts attention from short bursts of effort to the character built by sustained restraint.

ramayan::1687.verse_sanskrit: तस्य वर्षसहस्रस्य व्रते पूर्णे महाव्रत: । । 1654 । । भोक्तुमारब्धवानन्नं तस्मिन् काले रघूत्तम । इन्द्रो द्विजातिर्भूत्वा तं सिद्धमन्नमयाचत । । 1655 । ।
ramayan::1687.verse_hindi: O Best of Raghus dynasty (Rama) when the thousandyearold vow was over (Viswamitra) the great practitioner of vows began to partake cooked rice. At this moment Indra assumed the guise of a brahmin and asked him for the rice (he was going to eat).
ramayan::1687.english_translation: O Rama, when the thousand-year vow was complete, the great ascetic began to eat. At that moment, Indra took the form of a brahmin and asked for the cooked rice.
ramayan::1687.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / वर्षसहस्रस्य (of a thousand years) / व्रते (vow) / पूर्णे (when completed) / महाव्रत: (the great vow-holder) / भोक्तुमारब्धवान् (began to eat) / अन्नम् (food/rice) / तस्मिन् काले (at that time) / इन्द्रो (Indra) / द्विजातिर्भूत्वा (having become a brahmin) / तं (him) / सिद्धम् (prepared/cooked) / अन्नम् (cooked food) / अयाचत (asked for)
ramayan::1687.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1687.essence: Relief arrives, and the test begins again.
ramayan::1687.simple_meaning: Viswamitra finally ends his thousand-year vow and starts to eat, but Indra appears as a brahmin and asks for the food first.
ramayan::1687.simple_insight: Even the moment of relief can be interrupted by duty and testing.
ramayan::1687.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has completed an immense vow after a thousand years of austerity. Just as he begins to eat, Indra arrives disguised as a brahmin and asks for the prepared food. The scene sets up Viswamitra's next act of restraint and generosity.
ramayan::1687.modern_relevance: You finally sit down after a brutal stretch and take the first bite — then someone needs you again. The pause you wanted never arrives cleanly.
ramayan::1687.insight: It shifts attention from private reward to the next demand of dharma.

ramayan::1688.verse_sanskrit: तस्मै दत्वा तदा सिद्धं सर्वं विप्राय निश्चित: । निश्शेषितेऽन्ने भगवानभुक्तैव महातपा: । । 1656 । । न किञ्चिदवदद्विप्रं मौनव्रतमुपस्थित: । अथ वर्षसहस्रं वै नोच्छ्वसन्मुनिपुङ्गव: । । 1657 । ।
ramayan::1688.verse_hindi: This mighty, adorable ascetic having adopted a vow of silence decided to give all the cooked rice to the Brahmin. The brahmin finished all the rice. Viswamitra went without food but did not utter a single word to the brahmin. Thereafter the distinguished ascetic practised austerities for another period of thousand years, his breath suspended.
ramayan::1688.english_translation: Having given all the cooked food to the Brahmin, the mighty ascetic said nothing. He observed a vow of silence and remained without breathing for a thousand years.
ramayan::1688.translation_literal: तस्मै (to him) / दत्वा (having given) / तदा (then) / सिद्धं (cooked/ready) / सर्वं (all) / विप्राय (to the Brahmin) / निश्चित: (resolved) / निश्शेषिते (when exhausted) / अन्ने (food) / भगवान् (the venerable one) / अभुक्ता (having not eaten) / एव (indeed) / महातपा: (great ascetic) । न (not) / किञ्चिद् (anything) / अवदत् (spoke) / द्विप्रम् (to the Brahmin) / मौनव्रतम् (vow of silence) / उपस्थित: (having undertaken) । अथ (then) / वर्षसहस्रम् (a thousand years) / वै (indeed) / न (not) / उच्छ्वसन् (breathing) / मुनिपुङ्गव: (best of sages)
ramayan::1688.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1688.essence: A vow becomes real when hunger does not break it.
ramayan::1688.simple_meaning: Visvamitra gives the prepared food away, says nothing, and continues his austerity without breathing for another thousand years.
ramayan::1688.simple_insight: Real strength can look like restraint, not display.
ramayan::1688.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has finished a thousand-year vow and is about to eat. Then a Brahmin arrives, the food is gone, and the sage does not protest. He gives up the meal, keeps his silence, and returns to austerity with even greater resolve.
ramayan::1688.modern_relevance: You finally sit down to eat after a brutal day, and someone else needs you again. You hand it over without complaint. The harder victory is not getting what you want — it's staying steady when you don't.
ramayan::1688.insight: It trains you to meet interruption without losing inner control.

ramayan::1689.verse_sanskrit: तस्यानुच्छ्वसमानस्य मूर्ध्नि धूमो व्यजायत । त्रैलोक्यं येन सम्भ्रान्तमादीपितमिवाभवत् । । 1658 । ।
ramayan::1689.verse_hindi: While his breath, was suspended, smoke emanated from his head which frightened the three worlds. It appeared as though they were on fire.
ramayan::1689.english_translation: While his breath was suspended, smoke rose from his head, and the three worlds were shaken as if they were on fire.
ramayan::1689.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / अनुच्छ्वसमानस्य (while not breathing freely) / मूर्ध्नि (on the head) / धूमः (smoke) / व्यजायत (arose) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / येन (by which) / सम्भ्रान्तम् (confused, shaken) / आदीपितम् इव (as if set on fire) / अभवत् (became)
ramayan::1689.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1689.essence: His austerity was so fierce it seemed to set the worlds ablaze.
ramayan::1689.simple_meaning: His breath was held so long that smoke rose from his head, and even the three worlds seemed shaken by the intensity of his austerity.
ramayan::1689.simple_insight: Deep concentration can become so intense it feels larger than the body itself.
ramayan::1689.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra is deep in severe austerity after his vow. His breath is restrained so completely that smoke seems to rise from his head, and the heavens react in alarm. The verse is a vivid sign of his ascetic power, not a teaching by itself.
ramayan::1689.modern_relevance: You have seen someone so locked into discipline that the room changes around them. This verse captures that kind of force: focus so intense it feels almost dangerous.
ramayan::1689.insight: It shows how extreme tapas can be read as visible power, not just private effort.

ramayan::1690.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवास्सगन्धर्वा: पन्नगोरगराक्षसा: । मोहितास्तेजसा तस्य तपसा मन्दरश्मय: । । 1659 । । कश्मलोपहता स्सर्वे पितामहमथाब्रुवन् ।
ramayan::1690.verse_hindi: Thereupon devatas along with gandharvas, pannagas, uragas, and rakshasas, stood bewildered by his ascetic energy. Their own glory was dimmed in his lustre. Afflicted with anguish, they spoke to the Grandsire (Brahma):
ramayan::1690.english_translation: Thereupon the devas, along with gandharvas, pannagas, uragas, and rakshasas, stood bewildered by his ascetic energy. Their own glory was dimmed by his radiance. Afflicted with anguish, they spoke to the Grandsire, Brahma:
ramayan::1690.translation_literal: ततः (thereupon) / देवाः (the devas) / सगन्धर्वाः (along with gandharvas) / पन्नगोरगराक्षसाः (pannagas, uragas, and rakshasas) / मोहिताः (bewildered) / तेजसा (by radiance) / तस्य (of him) / तपसा (by ascetic power) / मन्दरश्मयः (their rays dimmed) / कश्मलोपहताः (afflicted with anguish) / सर्वे (all) / पितामहम् (to the Grandsire) / अथ (then) / अब्रुवन् (spoke)
ramayan::1690.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1690.essence: Steady austerity can outshine even celestial power.
ramayan::1690.simple_meaning: The force of Vishvamitra's austerity overwhelms even the celestial beings, and they turn to Brahma in distress.
ramayan::1690.simple_insight: Great inner discipline can shake even the powers that seem untouchable.
ramayan::1690.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra's austerity has become so intense that the devas and other powerful beings lose their composure. Blinded by his radiance, they gather before Brahma, alarmed that his tapas is changing the balance of the world.
ramayan::1690.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone who has trained for years walks in and says nothing. Their presence alone changes the temperature. That is the force of sustained discipline.
ramayan::1690.insight: It shows how disciplined effort can become a power others cannot ignore.

ramayan::1691.verse_sanskrit: बहुभि: कारणैर्देव विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । । 16510 । । लोभित: क्रोधितश्चैव तपसा चाभिवर्धते ।
ramayan::1691.verse_hindi: O Lord the great sage Viswamitra was lured and angered in various ways. But his austerities continued to grow:
ramayan::1691.english_translation: O lord, the great sage Vishvamitra was tempted and angered in many ways, yet his austerity only grew stronger.
ramayan::1691.translation_literal: बहुभि: (by many) / कारणै: (by causes) / देव (O lord) / विश्वामित्रो (Vishvamitra) / महामुनि: (the great sage) / लोभित: (tempted) / क्रोधित: (angered) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तपसा (by austerity) / च (and) / अभिवर्धते (grows stronger)
ramayan::1691.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1691.essence: What tries to shake you can become the reason you grow stronger.
ramayan::1691.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra is tested by temptation and anger, but he does not weaken. His austerity keeps increasing instead.
ramayan::1691.simple_insight: Real strength is not avoiding disturbance; it is becoming steadier because of it.
ramayan::1691.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra is in the middle of severe austerities, and forces around him try to provoke or distract him. Instead of breaking, he grows even more intense. The verse highlights the kind of discipline that turns resistance into fuel.
ramayan::1691.modern_relevance: You get mocked in a group chat, then feel the urge to answer sharply. Or you are tempted to quit after one bad review. This verse points to the person who uses pressure to become steadier, not more reactive.
ramayan::1691.insight: It teaches you to convert provocation into deeper restraint rather than immediate reaction.

ramayan::1692.verse_sanskrit: न ह्यस्य वृजिनं किञ्चिद्दृश्यते सूक्ष्ममप्यथ । । 16511 । । न दीयते यदि त्वस्य मनसा यदभीप्सितम् । विनाशयति त्रैलोक्यं तपसा सचराचरम् । । 16512 । ।
ramayan::1692.verse_hindi: His penance was flawless. If his wishes were not granted, he will  surely destroy by his austerities the three worlds with all movables and immovables.
ramayan::1692.english_translation: His penance was flawless. If what his mind desired was not granted, he would destroy the three worlds, with all moving and unmoving beings, by his austerities.
ramayan::1692.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / अस्य (of him) / वृजिनम् (fault, flaw) / किञ्चित् (any) / दृश्यते (is seen) / सूक्ष्मम् (subtle) / अपि (even) / अथ (also) / न (not) / दीयते (is given) / यदि (if) / तु (indeed) / अस्य (of him) / मनसा (by the mind) / यत् (what) / अभीप्सितम् (desired) / विनाशयति (destroys) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / तपसा (by austerity) / सचराचरम् (with moving and unmoving beings)
ramayan::1692.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1692.essence: Perfect discipline can become catastrophic when desire is denied.
ramayan::1692.simple_meaning: His austerity is so intense that even a tiny flaw cannot be found. If his desire is blocked, his penance could shake and destroy the whole cosmos.
ramayan::1692.simple_insight: Unchecked power can become dangerous when desire is frustrated.
ramayan::1692.detailed_meaning: Valmiki describes Vishwamitra’s tapas growing so fierce that even the gods feel threatened. This is not praise alone; it is a warning. A sage’s disciplined energy, if bent by frustration, can turn cosmic.
ramayan::1692.modern_relevance: You know that colleague or parent who stays calm until one more refusal tips everything over. Pressure does not always soften people; sometimes it concentrates their force.
ramayan::1692.insight: It warns you to see how disciplined power can turn destructive when desire is obstructed.

ramayan::1693.verse_sanskrit: व्याकुलाश्च दिशस्सर्वा न च किञ्चित्प्रकाशते । सागरा: क्षुभितास्सर्वे विशीर्यन्ते च पर्वता: । । 16513 । ।
ramayan::1693.verse_hindi: There is bewilderment everywhere. It is dark all over. The oceans are disturbed. The mountains have cracked.
ramayan::1693.english_translation: There is bewilderment everywhere. It is dark all over. The oceans are disturbed. The mountains have cracked.
ramayan::1693.translation_literal: व्याकुलाः (agitated, bewildered) / च (and) / दिशः (directions) / सर्वाः (all) / न (not) / च (and) / किञ्चित् (anything) / प्रकाशते (is visible, shines) / सागराः (oceans) / क्षुभिताः (agitated) / सर्वे (all) / विशीर्यन्ते (are breaking apart) / च (and) / पर्वताः (mountains)
ramayan::1693.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1693.essence: His austerity is so intense it seems to shake creation itself.
ramayan::1693.simple_meaning: The world itself seems to be falling apart: every direction is confused, light is gone, the oceans churn, and the mountains crack.
ramayan::1693.simple_insight: Some moments feel so overwhelming that even the world seems to lose its shape.
ramayan::1693.detailed_meaning: As Vishwamitra's austerities intensify, the disturbance spreads beyond him into the cosmos. The directions blur, light disappears, seas churn, and mountains crack. This is not a teaching verse on its own but a vivid sign of the pressure his penance has placed on creation.
ramayan::1693.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a crisis and feel it instantly: no one is steady, every conversation is fractured, and even simple things seem unstable.
ramayan::1693.insight: It shows how inner unrest can be imagined as outer collapse, making the scale of the disturbance unmistakable.

ramayan::1694.verse_sanskrit: प्रकम्पते च पृथिवी वायुर्वाति भृशाकुल: । बृह्मन्न प्रतिजानीमोनास्तिको जायते जन: । । 16514 । ।
ramayan::1694.verse_hindi: O Brahma the earth trembles. The wind blows fiercely. The people have ceased to believe in God. We do not know the way out.
ramayan::1694.english_translation: O Brahma, the earth trembles. The wind blows fiercely. People have lost faith, and we do not know what to do.
ramayan::1694.translation_literal: प्रकम्पते (trembles) / च (and) / पृथिवी (the earth) / वायुः (the wind) / वाति (blows) / भृशाकुलः (fiercely agitated) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahma) / न (not) / प्रतिजानीमः (we know) / नास्तिकः (without faith) / जायते (becomes) / जनः (the people)
ramayan::1694.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1694.essence: Unchecked austerity can shake the world before anyone answers it.
ramayan::1694.simple_meaning: The whole world is shaken by the force of this sage's penance. Even nature feels unstable, and the people are losing faith because the situation has become overwhelming.
ramayan::1694.simple_insight: Some actions are so intense they seem to unmake the world around them.
ramayan::1694.detailed_meaning: The sages are describing the pressure created by Maricha's extreme austerities. Earth quakes, winds lash the world, and public faith collapses under the fear of what may happen if his wish is denied. This verse deepens the crisis before Brahma responds.
ramayan::1694.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when one person’s rage or desperation starts changing everyone’s mood. You can feel the whole space tilting, and nobody knows how to steady it.
