ramayan::1694.insight: It shows how unchecked intensity spreads fear outward until even the environment feels unstable.

ramayan::1695.verse_sanskrit: सम्मूढमिव त्रैलोक्यं सम्प्रक्षुभितमानसम् । भास्करो निष्प्रभश्चैव महर्षेस्तस्य तेजसा । । 16515 । ।
ramayan::1695.verse_hindi: The people of all the three worlds are agitated and confused in mind. The Sun, too, looks pale before the brilliance of the Maharshi.
ramayan::1695.english_translation: The three worlds seem bewildered and deeply disturbed in mind. Even the sun looks dim before the brilliance of that great sage.
ramayan::1695.translation_literal: सम्मूढमिव (as if bewildered) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / सम्प्रक्षुभितमानसम् (with a deeply disturbed mind) / भास्करः (the sun) / निष्प्रभः (dim, without radiance) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / महर्षेः (of the great sage) / तस्य (his) / तेजसा (by the brilliance)
ramayan::1695.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1695.essence: His brilliance is so great that even the sun fades.
ramayan::1695.simple_meaning: The whole cosmos is shaken by the sage's power. Even the sun seems faded beside his brilliance.
ramayan::1695.simple_insight: Some presence is so intense that it unsettles everything around it.
ramayan::1695.detailed_meaning: The sky, earth, oceans, and people have already been described as shaken by the sage's force. Here the scene reaches its peak: the three worlds are agitated, and even the sun loses its brightness before his radiance. The verse prepares the plea that follows.
ramayan::1695.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone walks in carrying unbearable anger or authority. Everyone feels it before a word is spoken.
ramayan::1695.insight: It shows power so overwhelming that the world itself seems to lose balance.

ramayan::1696.verse_sanskrit: बुद्धिं न कुरुते यावन्नाशे देव महामुनि: । तावत्प्रसाद्यो भगवा नग्निरूपोमहाद्युति: । । 16516 । ।
ramayan::1696.verse_hindi: O Lord before this mighty, venerable ascetic, effulgent like fire decides to destroy the three worlds, he should be appeased.
ramayan::1696.english_translation: O Lord, before this mighty, venerable ascetic, effulgent like fire, decides to destroy the three worlds, he should be appeased.
ramayan::1696.translation_literal: बुद्धिं (resolve) / न (not) / कुरुते (makes) / यावत् (until) / नाशे (for destruction) / देव (O lord) / महामुनिः (great ascetic) / तावत् (then/so long) / प्रसाद्यः (to be appeased) / भगवान् (the venerable one) / अग्निरूपः (fire-shaped) / महाद्युतिः (greatly radiant)
ramayan::1696.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1696.essence: Stop the blaze before it becomes a vow.
ramayan::1696.simple_meaning: The gods should placate this blazing sage before he hardens into a resolve to destroy everything.
ramayan::1696.simple_insight: Small delays matter when anger is still forming.
ramayan::1696.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the gods are alarmed by a great ascetic whose heat is shaking the worlds. This line is part of their urgent response: act now, before his anger settles into a destructive vow.
ramayan::1696.modern_relevance: A tense group chat is spiraling, and one person is about to send the message that changes everything. The wise move is to cool the moment before it becomes irreversible.
ramayan::1696.insight: It teaches you to intervene early, before emotion turns into action.

ramayan::1697.verse_sanskrit: कालाग्निना यथापूर्वं त्रैलोक्यं दह्यतेऽखिलम् । देवराज्यं चिकीर्षेत दीयतामस्य यन्मतम् । । 16517 । ।
ramayan::1697.verse_hindi: All the three worlds are burning as though with the fire Pralaya (dissolution). His desire may be granted even if he wants to rule the kingdom of the gods.
ramayan::1697.english_translation: The whole three worlds are burning like the fire of dissolution. If he wishes even the rule of the gods, let that wish be granted.
ramayan::1697.translation_literal: कालाग्निना (by the fire of dissolution) / यथा (as) / पूर्वम् (before) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / दह्यते (is being burned) / अखिलम् (entirely) / देवराज्यम् (the rule of the gods) / चिकीर्षेत (may desire) / दीयताम् (let it be given) / अस्य (to him) / यत् (whatever) / मतम् (wish)
ramayan::1697.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1697.essence: His austerity is so fierce that even the heavens would rather yield than resist.
ramayan::1697.simple_meaning: The sage's power is so overwhelming that it feels like the whole cosmos is burning. The gods are ready to grant him even their own kingdom if that will calm him.
ramayan::1697.simple_insight: Some force is so intense that everyone around it yields immediately.
ramayan::1697.detailed_meaning: The gods are panicking before Viswamitra's blazing austerity. They fear that his anger could scorch the worlds themselves, so they decide to appease him at once, even if it means offering him the kingdom of the gods.
ramayan::1697.modern_relevance: A room goes silent because one person's anger has changed the air. Everyone stops arguing and starts thinking about how to calm the situation before it spreads.
ramayan::1697.insight: It shows how overwhelming power can force immediate concession, even from the highest powers.

ramayan::1698.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सुरगणास्सर्वे पितामहपुरोगमा: । विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं मधुरं वाक्यमब्रुवन् । । 16518 । ।
ramayan::1698.verse_hindi: Thereafter, with Brahma in the forefront, the gods spoke to Viswamitra in pleasing words:
ramayan::1698.english_translation: Thereafter, with Brahma in the forefront, the gods spoke to Viswamitra in pleasing words:
ramayan::1698.translation_literal: ततस् (thereafter) / सुरगणाः (the groups of gods) / सर्वे (all) / पितामह-पुरोगमाः (with Brahma in front) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Viswamitra) / महात्मानम् (the great-souled one) / मधुरम् (sweet) / वाक्यम् (words) / अब्रुवन् (spoke)
ramayan::1698.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1698.essence: Power met with respect can avert catastrophe.
ramayan::1698.simple_meaning: The gods, led by Brahma, addressed Viswamitra with kind and respectful words.
ramayan::1698.simple_insight: Respect opens the way where force cannot.
ramayan::1698.detailed_meaning: The gods have gathered because Viswamitra's tapas is shaking the order of the worlds. Brahma stands before them as they approach the sage, not to fight him, but to speak gently and prevent disaster. This verse sets up their appeal.
ramayan::1698.modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet before the senior person speaks. When someone has earned real power through discipline, the first move is respect, not resistance.
ramayan::1698.insight: It shifts the response from confrontation to honoring the force behind the demand.

ramayan::1699.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मर्षे स्वागतं तेऽस्तु तपसा स्म सुतोषिता: । ब्राह्मण्यं तपसोग्रेण प्राप्तवानसि कौशिक । । 16519 । ।
ramayan::1699.verse_hindi: Welcome, O Brahmarshi. We are immensely pleased with your austerities. O Kausika you have attained brahminhood by means of your intense penance.
ramayan::1699.english_translation: Welcome, O Brahmarshi. We are immensely pleased with your austerities. O Kausika, you have attained brahminhood by means of your intense penance.
ramayan::1699.translation_literal: ब्रह्मर्षे (O Brahmarshi) / स्वागतं (welcome) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may it be) / तपसा (by austerity) / स्म (indeed) / सुतोषिता: (greatly pleased) / ब्राह्मण्यं (brahminhood) / तपसः (by penance) / उग्रेण (intense) / प्राप्तवानसि (you have attained) / कौशिक (O Kausika)
ramayan::1699.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1699.essence: Intense penance can remake who you are.
ramayan::1699.simple_meaning: The gods welcome Vishwamitra and recognize that his severe penance has transformed him into a Brahmarshi.
ramayan::1699.simple_insight: Real change is earned through sustained inner discipline, not claimed by status.
ramayan::1699.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the gods speak to Vishwamitra after his long austerities. They welcome him as a Brahmarshi and acknowledge that his intense penance has raised him to brahminhood. The moment crowns a hard-won transformation.
ramayan::1699.modern_relevance: After months of showing up before sunrise, your mind finally feels steadier than your moods. No one handed you that steadiness — your repeated effort built it.
ramayan::1699.insight: It shifts attention from inherited identity to earned realization through disciplined practice.

ramayan::1700.verse_sanskrit: दीर्घमायुश्च ते ब्रह्मन् ददामि समरुद्गण: । स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भद्रं ते गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम् । । 16520 । ।
ramayan::1700.verse_hindi: O Brahmana I along with the maruts grant you long life. May you prosper O Gentle one now you may go happily.
ramayan::1700.english_translation: O Brahmana, I along with the Maruts grant you long life. May you prosper, O gentle one; now you may go happily.
ramayan::1700.translation_literal: दीर्घम् (long) / आयुः (life) / च (and) / ते (to you) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahmana) / ददामि (I grant) / समरुद्गणः (together with the Maruts) / स्वस्ति (well-being) / प्राप्नुहि (may you obtain) / भद्रम् (prosperity) / ते (to you) / गच्छ (go) / सौम्य (O gentle one) / यथासुखम् (as happily as you wish)
ramayan::1700.speaker: Brahma
ramayan::1700.essence: True achievement is sealed by blessing, not by struggle alone.
ramayan::1700.simple_meaning: Brahma blesses Viswamitra with long life, well-being, and a happy return after his austerities.
ramayan::1700.simple_insight: Recognition can arrive as blessing: your effort is seen, and the road ahead can open gently.
ramayan::1700.detailed_meaning: The gods, led by Brahma, have just praised Viswamitra for winning brahminhood through severe austerity. In this verse, Brahma completes the honor by blessing him with long life and safe passage, closing the celestial welcome before Viswamitra responds.
ramayan::1700.modern_relevance: After months of discipline, someone finally says, “You’ve done enough.” The relief is not just praise — it is permission to move forward without strain.
ramayan::1700.insight: It turns hard-won effort into honored completion, not endless proving.

ramayan::1701.verse_sanskrit: पितामहवचश्शृत्वा सर्वेषां च दिवौकसाम् । कृत्वा प्रणामं मुदितो व्याजहार महामुनि: । । 16521 । ।
ramayan::1701.verse_hindi: Mighty ascetic Viswamitra was delighted to hear the words of the Grandsire and the gods. Bowing to all of them he thus spoke:
ramayan::1701.english_translation: Mighty ascetic Viswamitra was delighted to hear the words of the Grandsire and the gods. Bowing to all of them he thus spoke:
ramayan::1701.translation_literal: पितामहवचः (the words of the Grandsire) / शृत्वा (having heard) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / च (and) / दिवौकसाम् (of the gods) / कृत्वा (having made) / प्रणामम् (a bow) / मुदितः (delighted) / व्याजहार (spoke) / महामुनिः (the great sage)
ramayan::1701.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1701.essence: Recognition becomes complete only when pride gives way to gratitude.
ramayan::1701.simple_meaning: Viswamitra bows to Brahma and the gods, then speaks with joy after receiving their blessing.
ramayan::1701.simple_insight: Honor and humility can arrive together when ambition is purified by grace.
ramayan::1701.detailed_meaning: Brahma and the gods have just granted Viswamitra long life and recognition. Now the great ascetic bows to them in gratitude, and his next words begin the final step of his transformation from king to brahmarshi.
ramayan::1701.modern_relevance: You finally get the recognition you worked for, and your first move is not triumph. It is a quiet bow to everyone who helped you get there.
ramayan::1701.insight: It shifts success from self-assertion to grateful humility.

ramayan::1702.verse_sanskrit: ब्राह्मण्यं यदि मे प्राप्तं दीर्घमायुस्तथैव च । ओङ्कारश्च वषट्कारो वेदाश्च वरयन्तु माम् । । 16522 । ।
ramayan::1702.verse_hindi: If brahminhood and long life have been acquired by me by your grace, Omkara, Vashatkara and the Vedas shall accept me as Brahmarshi. (I shall acquire the right to interpret the Vedas and to perform sacrifices.)
ramayan::1702.english_translation: If I have truly gained brahminhood and long life by your grace, then let Om, Vashat, and the Vedas accept me.
ramayan::1702.translation_literal: ब्राह्मण्यं (brahminhood) / यदि (if) / मे (to me) / प्राप्तं (obtained) / दीर्घम् (long) / आयुः (life) / तथा (also) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / ओङ्कारः (Om) / च (and) / वषट्कारः (Vashatkara) / च (and) / वेदाः (the Vedas) / च (and) / वरयन्तु (may choose/accept) / माम् (me)
ramayan::1702.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::1702.essence: True status comes only when your becoming is complete.
ramayan::1702.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra asks the divine powers to recognize him as a true brahmarshi if he has truly earned brahminhood and long life.
ramayan::1702.simple_insight: Real stature is not claimed; it is confirmed by what you have become.
ramayan::1702.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just been blessed by Brahma and the gods. Instead of celebrating, he asks for a harder honor: let the sacred sounds and the Vedas themselves acknowledge him as a brahmarshi. The moment reveals his hunger for true standing, not applause.
ramayan::1702.modern_relevance: You finish years of work and still feel unfinished. The certificate is in your hand, but you want the deeper recognition that your character has actually changed.
ramayan::1702.insight: It shifts ambition from external approval to inner qualification.

ramayan::1703.verse_sanskrit: क्षत्रवेदविदां श्रेष्ठो ब्रह्मवेदविदामपि । ब्रह्मपुत्रो वसिष्ठो मामेवं वदतु देवता: । । 16523 । । यद्ययं परम: काम: कृतो यान्तु सुरर्षभा: ।
ramayan::1703.verse_hindi: O gods let the son of Brahma and eminent Vasishta who is knowledgeable in the vedas worthy of brahmins and archery worthy of kshatriyas address me as Brahmarshi. If this supreme desire is granted, O Best of devatas all of you can go.
ramayan::1703.english_translation: O gods, let Vasishta, son of Brahma and best among those who know the Vedas and archery, speak of me as a Brahmarshi. If this highest wish is fulfilled, O best of the radiant beings, you may all depart.
ramayan::1703.translation_literal: क्षत्रवेदविदाम् (of those knowing the Veda of warriors) / श्रेष्ठः (best) / ब्रह्मवेदविदाम् (of those knowing the Veda of brahmins) / अपि (also) / ब्रह्मपुत्रः (son of Brahma) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / माम् (me) / एवम् (thus) / वदतु (may speak) / देवताः (radiant beings) / यदि (if) / अयम् (this) / परमः (highest) / कामः (wish) / कृतः (fulfilled) / यान्तु (may go) / सुरर्षभाः (best of the radiant beings)
ramayan::1703.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramayan::1703.essence: True arrival still longs for recognition from the hardest judge.
ramayan::1703.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra asks the gods to let Vasishta acknowledge him as a Brahmarshi. He is willing to let them leave only after that highest recognition is granted.
ramayan::1703.simple_insight: Even great achievement can still long for rightful recognition.
ramayan::1703.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has already won the gods' approval, but he is not satisfied until Vasishta, the sage whose judgment truly matters, names him a Brahmarshi. This is the turning point where effort seeks confirmation from the one authority he cannot ignore.
ramayan::1703.modern_relevance: You can win the award, get the title, and still feel unfinished until the person you respect most acknowledges what you became.
ramayan::1703.insight: It shifts ambition from public success to the deeper need for earned recognition.

ramayan::1704.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रसादितो देवैर्वसिष्ठो जपतां वर: । । 16524 । । सख्यं चकार ब्रह्मर्षिरेवमस्त्विति चाब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1704.verse_hindi: Thereupon, pleased by the gods, Vasishta, the best among ascetics, lovingly said to Viswamitra You are a Brahmarshi, let it be so.
ramayan::1704.english_translation: Thereupon, pleased by the gods, Vasishta, the best among ascetics, lovingly said to Viswamitra, “You are a Brahmarshi; let it be so.”
ramayan::1704.translation_literal: तत: (thereupon) / प्रसादितो (being pleased) / देवैः (by the gods) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / जपतां वरः (best among ascetics) / सख्यं (friendship) / चकार (made) / ब्रह्मर्षिः (Brahmarshi) / एवम् (thus) / अस्तु (let it be) / इति (thus) / च (and) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1704.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1704.essence: True growth becomes real when it is openly recognized.
ramayan::1704.simple_meaning: Vasishta accepts Viswamitra’s transformation and formally recognizes him as a great sage.
ramayan::1704.simple_insight: There is relief in being seen for who you have become.
ramayan::1704.detailed_meaning: The gods have gathered around Viswamitra’s hard-won transformation. Vasishta, once his rival, is pleased and offers the recognition that seals the change: Viswamitra is now a Brahmarshi. The struggle ends in acknowledgment.
ramayan::1704.modern_relevance: After years of study, therapy, or rebuilding your life, someone finally names the change you already felt inside. Recognition can be its own completion.
ramayan::1704.insight: It shifts the mind from striving for approval to receiving the truth of earned growth.

ramayan::1705.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मर्षिस्त्वं न सन्देहस्सर्वं सम्पत्स्यते तव । । 16525 । । इत्युक्त्वा देवताश्चापि सर्वा जग्मुर्यथागतम् ।
ramayan::1705.verse_hindi: You are a Brahmarshi, no doubt. You will achieve ascetic perfection, said the gods
ramayan::1705.english_translation: You are a Brahmarshi, without doubt. Everything you seek will be fulfilled. Having said this, all the gods returned as they had come.
ramayan::1705.translation_literal: ब्रह्मर्षिः (a Brahmarshi) / त्वम् (you) / न (not) / सन्देहः (doubt) / सर्वम् (everything) / सम्पत्स्यते (will be attained) / तव (for you) / इति (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / देवताः (the gods) / च (and) / अपि (also) / सर्वाः (all) / जग्मुः (went) / यथागतम् (as they had come)
ramayan::1705.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1705.essence: What he sought outside himself was finally recognized within him.
ramayan::1705.simple_meaning: The gods declare that Vishwamitra has become a Brahmarshi and that his long spiritual effort has succeeded fully.
ramayan::1705.simple_insight: Deep effort changes who you are, not just what you get.
ramayan::1705.detailed_meaning: The gods have come to Vasishta to settle Vishwamitra's claim. After their approval, Vasishta confirms the title, and the heavens themselves acknowledge Vishwamitra's completion. This verse seals the transformation that years of tapas had been building toward.
ramayan::1705.modern_relevance: After years of practice, a mentor finally says, 'You are ready.' The relief is not just in praise — it is in hearing that the person you became matches the work you did.
ramayan::1705.insight: It shifts attention from external approval to the inner completion that disciplined striving creates.

ramayan::1706.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रोऽपि धर्मात्मा लब्ध्वा ब्राह्मण्यमुत्तमम् । । 16526 । । पूजयामास ब्रह्मर्षिं वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम् ।
ramayan::1706.verse_hindi: Virtuous Viswamitra also, having attained excellent brahminhood, worshipped  Brahmrshi Vasishta who was the best of those who recite hymns.
ramayan::1706.english_translation: Virtuous Viswamitra, having attained excellent brahminhood, worshipped the Brahmarshi Vasishta, best among those who recite hymns.
ramayan::1706.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / अपि (also) / धर्मात्मा (virtuous in nature) / लब्ध्वा (having attained) / ब्राह्मण्यम् (brahminhood) / उत्तमम् (excellent) / पूजयामास (worshipped) / ब्रह्मर्षिम् (the Brahmarshi) / वसिष्ठम् (Vasishta) / जपताम् (of those who recite hymns) / वरम् (best)
ramayan::1706.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1706.essence: He wins the title, then bows to the man who made him earn it.
ramayan::1706.simple_meaning: Viswamitra, after reaching a higher spiritual standing, showed respect to Vasishta. The former rival now honours the sage he once opposed.
ramayan::1706.simple_insight: Real growth shows up as humility, not victory.
ramayan::1706.detailed_meaning: The gods have just confirmed Viswamitra as a Brahmarshi, and Vasishta has accepted him. In that settled moment, Viswamitra bows to Vasishta. The passage marks reconciliation after a long struggle, not a new teaching.
ramayan::1706.modern_relevance: After a long rivalry at work, you finally get the title you wanted. The real test is whether you can still respect the person who once blocked you.
ramayan::1706.insight: It shifts the mind from proving yourself to honouring what you have become.

ramayan::1707.verse_sanskrit: कृतकामो महीं सर्वां चचार तपसि स्थित: । । 16527 । । एवं त्वनेन ब्राह्मण्यं प्राप्तं राम महात्मना ।
ramayan::1707.verse_hindi: This illustrious sage having fulfilled his desire, wandered over the earth fixed in asceticism. O Rama  thus he acquired brahminhood.
ramayan::1707.english_translation: This illustrious sage, having fulfilled his desire, wandered over the earth fixed in ascetic practice. O Rama, thus he attained brahminhood.
ramayan::1707.translation_literal: कृतकामः (having fulfilled his desire) / महीम् (the earth) / सर्वाम् (all) / चचार (wandered) / तपसि (in ascetic practice) / स्थितः (firmly placed) / एवं (thus) / तु (indeed) / अनेन (by this one) / ब्राह्मण्यम् (brahminhood) / प्राप्तम् (attained) / राम (O Rama) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one)
ramayan::1707.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1707.essence: Fulfilled desire did not end his practice; it deepened it.
ramayan::1707.simple_meaning: Visvamitra became spiritually mature through disciplined ascetic practice and gained the status of a revered sage.
ramayan::1707.simple_insight: Real transformation comes from sustained practice, not from wanting recognition.
ramayan::1707.detailed_meaning: The gods have just praised Visvamitra before Rama. Now the narration explains how he earned that stature: after fulfilling his earlier aim, he roamed the earth in steady austerity until he attained brahminhood. It prepares for the fuller praise that follows.
ramayan::1707.modern_relevance: You finally get what you wanted, but you do not stop there. You keep showing up, keep practicing, and let character deepen after the win.
ramayan::1707.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to the discipline that makes achievement worthy.

ramayan::1708.verse_sanskrit: एष राम मुनिश्रेष्ठ एष विग्रहवांस्तप: । । 16528 । । एष धर्मपरो नित्यं वीर्यस्यैष परायणम् ।
ramayan::1708.verse_hindi: O Rama he is the foremost of ascetics, an embodiment of asceticism, always intent on virtue. He is the ultimate repository of ascetic energy.
ramayan::1708.english_translation: O Rama, he is the foremost of ascetics, an embodiment of asceticism, always intent on virtue. He is the ultimate repository of ascetic energy.
ramayan::1708.translation_literal: एष (this is) / राम (Rama) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (foremost among sages) / एष (this is) / विग्रहवांस्तपः (embodied asceticism) / एष (this is) / धर्मपरः (devoted to virtue) / नित्यम् (always) / वीर्यस्य (of strength/ascetic power) / एष (this is) / परायणम् (the highest refuge/repository)
ramayan::1708.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1708.essence: True strength is power disciplined by virtue.
ramayan::1708.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as someone whose whole life is disciplined, virtuous, and full of inner strength.
ramayan::1708.simple_insight: Real strength is not loud. It shows up as steady self-control and a life aligned with what is right.
ramayan::1708.detailed_meaning: Satananda is introducing Viswamitra’s greatness to Rama and Lakshmana. He says this sage has already fulfilled his purpose through austerity and now stands as a living example of discipline, virtue, and spiritual force.
ramayan::1708.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm presence changes the room, because every choice they make has been trained by years of restraint. Their power feels earned, not performed.
ramayan::1708.insight: It shifts admiration from raw power to power shaped by disciplined virtue.

ramayan::1709.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा विरराम द्विजोत्तम: । । 16529 । । शतानन्दवच: श्रुत्वा रामलक्ष्मणसन्निधौ । जनक: प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच कुशिकात्मजम् । । 16530 । ।
ramayan::1709.verse_hindi: Having thus spoken, the most brilliant and best among brahmins (Satananda) became silent. In the presence of Rama and Lakshmana, Janaka listened to the words of Satananda. And with folded palms said to the son of Kushika (Viswamitra):
ramayan::1709.english_translation: Having thus spoken, the most brilliant and best among brahmins, Satananda, fell silent. Hearing Satananda's words in the presence of Rama and Lakshmana, Janaka folded his palms and spoke to the son of Kushika, Vishwamitra:
ramayan::1709.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / महातेजा (most brilliant) / विरराम (became silent) / द्विजोत्तमः (best among brahmins) / शतानन्दवचः (Satananda's words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / रामलक्ष्मणसन्निधौ (in the presence of Rama and Lakshmana) / जनकः (Janaka) / प्राञ्जलिः (with folded palms) / वाक्यम् (speech) / उवाच (spoke) / कुशिकात्मजम् (to the son of Kushika)
ramayan::1709.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1709.essence: Praise ends, and the king answers with folded hands.
ramayan::1709.simple_meaning: Satananda finishes speaking, and Janaka respectfully turns to Vishwamitra with folded hands.
ramayan::1709.simple_insight: Respectful silence can be the bridge between praise and response.
ramayan::1709.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's sacrifice, Satananda has just praised Vishwamitra in front of Rama and Lakshmana. The speech ends, the room falls quiet, and Janaka prepares to answer. The verse simply marks that transition into the king's gratitude.
ramayan::1709.modern_relevance: A meeting ends, the room goes quiet, and everyone waits for the host to respond. The real moment is not the praise itself, but how you receive it.
ramayan::1709.insight: It marks the shift from spoken praise to formal reply, showing courtly restraint.

ramayan::1710.verse_sanskrit: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुङ्गव । यज्ञं काकुत्स्थसहित: प्राप्तवानसि धार्मिक । । 16531 । ।
ramayan::1710.verse_hindi: O Righteous one O Preeminent among ascetics you have come to my sacrifice accompanied by the descendants of Kakustha (Rama and Lakshmana). I am  blessed by your presence and am   highly favoured.
ramayan::1710.english_translation: O righteous one, O foremost among ascetics, I am blessed and deeply favored that you have come to my sacrifice accompanied by the descendants of Kakustha.
ramayan::1710.translation_literal: धन्यः (blessed) / अस्मि (I am) / अनुगृहीतः (favored, shown grace) / अस्मि (I am) / यस्य (because) / मे (my) / मुनि-पुङ्गव (foremost among ascetics) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / काकुत्स्थ-सहितः (accompanied by Kakustha's descendants) / प्राप्तवान् असि (you have arrived) / धार्मिक (righteous one)
ramayan::1710.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1710.essence: Your presence can sanctify what is already in motion.
ramayan::1710.simple_meaning: Janaka welcomes Rama and Lakshmana to his sacrifice with gratitude and reverence. Their arrival is a blessing to him.
ramayan::1710.simple_insight: True honor is knowing who makes a sacred moment complete.
ramayan::1710.detailed_meaning: Janaka speaks in the middle of a formal welcome at the sacrifice. After the praise of Rama's virtue, he turns to gratitude: Rama and Lakshmana have arrived at the very place where Janaka's ritual and hopes converge.
ramayan::1710.modern_relevance: A host sees the right person walk into a room and feels the whole evening settle into place. Some arrivals do not just fill space; they dignify what was already underway.
ramayan::1710.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the presence that gives ceremony meaning.

ramayan::1711.verse_sanskrit: पावितोऽहं त्वया ब्रह्मन् दर्शनेन महामुने । गुणा बहुविधा: प्राप्तास्तव सन्दर्शनान्मया । । 16532 । ।
ramayan::1711.verse_hindi: O Excellent ascetic O Brahmana I am sanctified with your presence. I have derived immense benefits from your visit.
ramayan::1711.english_translation: O excellent ascetic, O Brahmana, I am purified by your presence. I have received many blessings from merely seeing you.
ramayan::1711.translation_literal: पावितः (purified) / अहम् (I) / त्वया (by you) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahmana) / दर्शनेन (by the sight) / महामुने (O great sage) / गुणाः (qualities, blessings) / बहुविधाः (many kinds) / प्राप्ताः (have been obtained) / तव (of you) / सन्दर्शनात् (from seeing) / मया (by me)
ramayan::1711.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1711.essence: A worthy presence can purify you without a single instruction.
ramayan::1711.simple_meaning: Janaka tells the sage that simply seeing him has made him feel purified and deeply blessed.
ramayan::1711.simple_insight: Right company can lift you before any words are spoken.
ramayan::1711.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s sacrifice hall, Rama and Lakshmana stand beside the sage. After hearing Satananda speak, Janaka greets the visiting ascetic with reverence, saying his mere presence has purified him and brought many blessings.
ramayan::1711.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the room before they say a word. Their presence steadies you, and you leave feeling clearer than when you arrived.
ramayan::1711.insight: It shifts attention from status to the transforming effect of noble company.

ramayan::1712.verse_sanskrit: विस्तरेण च ते ब्रह्मन् कीर्त्यमानं महत्तप: । श्रुतं मया महातेजो रामेण च महात्मना । । 16533 । ।
ramayan::1712.verse_hindi: O powerful  Brahmarshi distinguished Rama and I have heard your great austerities which were related in detail (by Satananda).
ramayan::1712.english_translation: O Brahmarshi, powerful and distinguished one, I have heard in detail of your great austerities from Rama, the great-souled one.
ramayan::1712.translation_literal: विस्तरेण (in detail) / च (and) / ते (of you) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahmana) / कीर्त्यमानं (being spoken of, praised) / महत्तपः (great austerity) / श्रुतं (heard) / मया (by me) / महातेजः (O greatly radiant one) / रामेण (by Rama) / च (and) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one)
ramayan::1712.speaker: Satananda
ramayan::1712.essence: Your austerity is already known through the people who speak of you.
ramayan::1712.simple_meaning: Satananda tells the visiting sage that he has heard of his great austerities in detail from Rama.
ramayan::1712.simple_insight: Your character is known not by claims, but by what others rightly recount.
ramayan::1712.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s sacrifice, the assembled sages greet Vishvamitra with honor. Satananda, speaking for the court, says Rama has already described Vishvamitra’s severe austerities in detail. The verse continues the formal welcome, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::1712.modern_relevance: A room full of people already knows what you have carried through. Before you even speak, your discipline has reached them through someone else’s praise.
ramayan::1712.insight: It shifts attention from self-presentation to the reputation earned through lived discipline.

ramayan::1713.verse_sanskrit: सदस्यै: प्राप्य च सद: श्रुतास्ते बहवो गुणा: । अप्रमेयं तपस्तुभ्यमप्रमेयं च ते बलम् । । 16534 । । अप्रमेया गुणाश्चैव नित्यं ते कुशिकात्मज ।
ramayan::1713.verse_hindi: Many of your virtues have been heard by the members of the assembly present at the  sacrifice. Your austerities are immeasurable, your power is immense. O Son of Kushika (Viswamitra), your virtues cannot be measured.
ramayan::1713.english_translation: Many of your virtues have been heard by the members of the assembly present at the sacrifice. Your austerities are immeasurable, your power is immense. O Son of Kushika, your virtues cannot be measured.
ramayan::1713.translation_literal: सदस्यैः (by the members of the assembly) / प्राप्य (having been heard) / च (and) / सदः (the assembly hall) / श्रुताः (heard) / ते (your) / बहवः (many) / गुणाः (qualities) / अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable) / तपः (austerity) / तुभ्यम् (for you) / अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable) / च (and) / ते (your) / बलम् (strength) / अप्रमेयाः (immeasurable) / गुणाः (qualities) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / नित्यम् (always) / ते (your) / कुशिकात्मज (O son of Kushika)
ramayan::1713.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1713.essence: His strength and virtue are too vast to count.
ramayan::1713.simple_meaning: The speaker praises Viswamitra in front of the assembly: his virtues, austerity, strength, and qualities are beyond measure.
ramayan::1713.simple_insight: True greatness needs no exaggeration; it simply overflows every measure.
ramayan::1713.detailed_meaning: At the sacrifice, the gathered sages have already heard of Viswamitra's renunciation and power. This verse is part of a formal praise, not the climax itself. It adds another layer of reverence before the speaker continues.
ramayan::1713.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone finishes speaking, and the praise is not polite filler. It is the rare moment when everyone present knows the person before them has changed by discipline.
ramayan::1713.insight: It frames greatness as the result of sustained austerity, not a single dramatic act.

ramayan::1714.verse_sanskrit: तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे विभो । । 16535 । । कर्मकालो मुनिश्रेष्ठ लम्बते रविमण्डलम् ।
ramayan::1714.verse_hindi: O Lord I am never tired of listening to your marvellous deeds. O Excellent among ascetics the Sun has set and it is time for evening prayers.
ramayan::1714.english_translation: O Lord, I am never tired of hearing your marvellous deeds. O best among ascetics, the sun has already set, and it is time for evening prayers.
ramayan::1714.translation_literal: तृप्तिः (satisfaction) / आश्चर्य-भूतानाम् (of wondrous) / कथानाम् (stories) / नास्ति (is not) / मे (for me) / विभो (O Lord) / कर्म-कालः (time for action / ritual duty) / मुनि-श्रेष्ठ (O best among ascetics) / लम्बते (has passed / hangs on) / रवि-मण्डलम् (the sun's disk)
ramayan::1714.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1714.simple_meaning: Valmiki says he can listen to the sage's wondrous stories forever, but the day has ended and evening prayers must begin.
ramayan::1714.simple_insight: Even the sweetest conversation must bow to the rhythm of duty.
ramayan::1714.detailed_meaning: Valmiki has been listening to the sage's extraordinary account and does not want it to end. But the sun has set, and the sacred evening rites now take priority. The verse simply pauses the exchange so the meeting can continue tomorrow.
ramayan::1714.modern_relevance: You are deep in a conversation that feels too important to stop, but the room is dimming and your next responsibility is already waiting.
ramayan::1714.insight: It teaches you to end even meaningful engagement when the next duty arrives.

ramayan::1715.verse_sanskrit: श्व: प्रभाते महातेजो द्रष्टुमर्हसि मां पुन: । । 16536 । । स्वागतं तपतां श्रेष्ठ मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।
ramayan::1715.verse_hindi: O Sage of great austerities come to me tomorrow at dawn. O Excellent ascetic welcome And allow me to leave.
ramayan::1715.english_translation: O Sage of great austerities, come to me tomorrow at dawn. O excellent ascetic, be welcome, and allow me to leave.
ramayan::1715.translation_literal: श्वः (tomorrow) / प्रभाते (at dawn) / महातेजः (greatly radiant one) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अर्हसि (you should) / माम् (me) / पुनः (again) / स्वागतम् (welcome) / तपताम् (of ascetics) / श्रेष्ठ (best) / माम् (me) / अनुज्ञातुम् (to permit to leave) / अर्हसि (you should)
ramayan::1715.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1715.essence: Honor the moment, then let it end cleanly.
ramayan::1715.simple_meaning: Janaka asks the sage to meet him again at dawn, welcomes him respectfully, and asks permission to depart.
ramayan::1715.simple_insight: Respect can be firm and graceful at the same time.
ramayan::1715.detailed_meaning: After hearing Vishwamitra's wondrous account, Janaka sees that night has fallen. He invites the sage to return at daybreak, greets him with honor, and asks leave to withdraw. The moment is courteous transition, not teaching.
ramayan::1715.modern_relevance: A long conversation has run late, and you can feel the room thinning with fatigue. You still end it with grace, not abruptness.
ramayan::1715.insight: It shows how to close an important exchange without losing dignity or warmth.

ramayan::1716.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रभाते विमले कृतकर्मा नराधिप: । विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं आजुहाव सराघवम् । । 1661 । ।
ramayan::1716.verse_hindi: The day dawned bright and clear when the king (Janaka) performed his daily routine rites and welcomed the great Viswamitra with the two Raghavas (Rama and Lakshmana).
ramayan::1716.english_translation: Then, at clear dawn, the king, having finished his rites, summoned great Viswamitra together with Rama.
ramayan::1716.translation_literal: तत: (then) / प्रभाते (at dawn) / विमले (clear, pure) / कृतकर्मा (having done his rites) / नराधिप: (the king) / विश्वामित्रं (Viswamitra) / महात्मानं (the great-souled one) / आजुहाव (summoned) / सराघवम् (together with the Raghava)
ramayan::1716.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1716.essence: Morning order quietly prepares the next decisive meeting.
ramayan::1716.simple_meaning: At dawn, King Janaka finished his morning rites and called for Viswamitra along with Rama.
ramayan::1716.simple_insight: A calm, orderly morning opens the next step of the meeting.
ramayan::1716.detailed_meaning: After the previous evening's conversation, dawn breaks over Mithila. Janaka completes his ritual duties and sends for Viswamitra, bringing Rama into the next stage of the encounter. The verse mainly moves the scene forward.
ramayan::1716.modern_relevance: You finish your morning routine, then call the people who matter before the day gets busy. The moment feels small, but it sets everything in motion.
ramayan::1716.insight: It shifts attention from drama to sequence: first the rites, then the summons, then the meeting.

ramayan::1717.verse_sanskrit: तमर्चयित्वा धर्मात्मा शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा । राघवौ च महात्मानौ तदा वाक्यमुवाच ह । । 1662 । ।
ramayan::1717.verse_hindi: The virtuous Janaka paid respects to Viswamitra and the highsouled Rama and Lakshmana in accordance with the sastras and spoke:
ramayan::1717.english_translation: The virtuous Janaka honored Viswamitra and the noble Rama and Lakshmana according to scripture and then spoke.
ramayan::1717.translation_literal: तम् (him) / अर्चयित्वा (having honored) / धर्मात्मा (the virtuous one) / शास्त्रदृष्टेन (according to scripture) / कर्मणा (by action) / राघवौ (Rama and Lakshmana) / च (and) / महात्मानौ (the high-souled ones) / तदा (then) / वाक्यम् (words) / उवाच (spoke) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::1717.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1717.essence: Honor comes first; speech follows after.
ramayan::1717.simple_meaning: Janaka first receives Viswamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana with proper ritual respect, then begins speaking to them.
ramayan::1717.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before any important conversation can begin.
ramayan::1717.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court, the king follows the proper order: he honors Viswamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana with exact ritual care, then addresses them. The verse is a bridge into the dialogue, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1717.modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you can feel the room change when someone is greeted properly, seated well, and treated with dignity. That small discipline makes truth easier to hear.
ramayan::1717.insight: It shifts attention to the etiquette that prepares a serious exchange.

ramayan::1718.verse_sanskrit: भगवन् स्वागतं तेऽस्तु किं करोमि तवानघ । भवानाज्ञापयतु मामाज्ञाप्यो भवता ह्यहम् । । 1663 । ।
ramayan::1718.verse_hindi: Welcome, O Venerable one O Irreproachable one what can I do for you? Worthy of being commanded, I seek your orders.
ramayan::1718.english_translation: Welcome, O venerable one. O irreproachable one, what can I do for you? Please command me; I am under your orders.
ramayan::1718.translation_literal: भगवन् (venerable one) / स्वागतं (welcome) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may it be) / किं (what) / करोमि (shall I do) / तव (of you) / अनघ (irreproachable one) / भवान् (you) / आज्ञापयतु (may command) / माम् (me) / आज्ञाप्यः (fit to be commanded) / भवता (by you) / हि (indeed) / अहम् (I)
ramayan::1718.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1718.essence: Real honor begins when you place yourself in service.
ramayan::1718.simple_meaning: Janaka welcomes Vishwamitra with deep respect and asks what service he can offer, placing himself ready to receive instructions.
ramayan::1718.simple_insight: True respect listens first and makes room before speaking.
ramayan::1718.detailed_meaning: Janaka has welcomed Vishwamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana with formal honor. Now he turns to the sage himself, offering complete readiness to serve. The verse shows royal humility before the teacher who has arrived with a sacred purpose.
ramayan::1718.modern_relevance: Someone senior walks into your office, and you stop performing importance. You ask what they need, not what you want to prove.
ramayan::1718.insight: It trains the mind to meet wisdom with humility, not self-assertion.

ramayan::1719.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्स धर्मात्मा जनकेन महात्मना । प्रत्युवाच मुनिर्वीरं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारद: । । 1664 । ।
ramayan::1719.verse_hindi: At the words of the magnanimous Janaka, the virtuous sage wellversed in speech replied to the heroic king:
ramayan::1719.english_translation: At the words of the magnanimous Janaka, the virtuous sage, skilled in speech, replied to the heroic king:
ramayan::1719.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus spoken to) / धर्मात्मा (virtuous) / जनकेन (by Janaka) / महात्मना (by the magnanimous one) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / मुनिः (the sage) / वीरम् (to the heroic one) / वाक्यविशारदः (skilled in speech)
ramayan::1719.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1719.essence: The meeting turns from courtesy to purpose.
ramayan::1719.simple_meaning: The sage replies to Janaka after being received with honor.
ramayan::1719.simple_insight: Respect opens the way for a meaningful conversation.
ramayan::1719.detailed_meaning: Janaka has welcomed Vishwamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana with proper honor. After that formal greeting, the sage answers the king. The verse is a bridge, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::1719.modern_relevance: You finish the introductions, and the real conversation can finally begin.
ramayan::1719.insight: It marks the transition from formal welcome to the next decisive exchange.

ramayan::1720.verse_sanskrit: पुत्रौ दशरथस्येमौ क्षत्रियौ लोकविश्रुतौ । द्रुष्टुकामौ धनु श्श्रेष्ठं यदेतत्वयि तिष्ठति । । 1665 । ।
ramayan::1720.verse_hindi: Dasarathas sons, (Rama and Lakshmana), kshatriyas renowned in the world are eager to see that great bow in your possession.
ramayan::1720.english_translation: The two sons of Dasaratha, famous kshatriyas, want to see the finest bow that is with you.
ramayan::1720.translation_literal: पुत्रौ (the two sons) / दशरथस्य (of Dasaratha) / इमौ (these two) / क्षत्रियौ (kshatriyas) / लोकविश्रुतौ (world-famous) / द्रुष्टुकामौ (desiring to see) / धनुःश्रेष्ठम् (the finest bow) / यत् (that which) / एतत् (this) / त्वयि (with you) / तिष्ठति (stands)
ramayan::1720.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1720.essence: The request is simple, but the challenge it points to is not.
ramayan::1720.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana, the famous sons of Dasaratha, want to see the great bow in Janaka's possession.
ramayan::1720.simple_insight: Sometimes the whole moment is just a respectful request before a decisive test.
ramayan::1720.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, the king has welcomed Vishvamitra and the two princes. Now the sage explains why Rama and Lakshmana have come: they want to see the great bow kept there. This is the calm before the swayamvara's decisive challenge.
ramayan::1720.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone knows something important is about to happen. Before the test begins, all you can do is ask to see what you are being asked to meet.
ramayan::1720.insight: It frames the bow as the object of the princes' deliberate attention, setting up the coming trial.

ramayan::1721.verse_sanskrit: एतद्दर्शय भद्रं ते कृतकामौ नृपात्मजौ । दर्शनादस्य धनुषो यथेष्टं प्रतियास्यत: । । 1666 । ।
ramayan::1721.verse_hindi: Be blessed. Show this great bow to the princes. This is their desire. Once it is fulfilled, they will go back.
ramayan::1721.english_translation: Be blessed. Show this great bow to the princes. This is their desire. Once it is fulfilled, they will go back.
ramayan::1721.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / दर्शय (show) / भद्रम् ते (may good be to you) / कृतकामौ (having accomplished their desire) / नृपात्मजौ (the king's sons) / दर्शनात् (from seeing) / अस्य (of this) / धनुषः (bow) / यथेष्टम् (as desired) / प्रतियास्यत: (will return)
ramayan::1721.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1721.essence: The request is only a step toward the larger test.
ramayan::1721.simple_meaning: Janaka asks Vishvamitra to show the bow to Rama and Lakshmana. Once they have seen it, their wish will be complete and they can return.
ramayan::1721.simple_insight: Sometimes the whole moment is just a doorway to the next one.
ramayan::1721.detailed_meaning: Janaka has heard that Dasaratha's sons want to see the great bow in his court. He politely agrees and tells Vishvamitra to show it to them. This is a small bridge in the larger scene before the bow challenge begins.
ramayan::1721.modern_relevance: You open the cabinet, hand over the file, and let the meeting move forward. The real test has not started yet.
ramayan::1721.insight: It simply advances the scene, setting up the bow's reveal without adding a teaching of its own.

ramayan::1722.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु जनक: प्रत्युवाच महामुनिम् । श्रूयतामस्य धनुषो यदर्थमिह तिष्ठति । । 1667 । ।
ramayan::1722.verse_hindi: Thus addressed by the mighty ascetic Janaka replied, I shall tell you how this bow came to be deposited here.
ramayan::1722.english_translation: Thus addressed, Janaka replied to the great ascetic: "Listen to why this bow has been kept here."
ramayan::1722.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus addressed) / तु (indeed) / जनकः (Janaka) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / महामुनिम् (to the great ascetic) / श्रूयताम् (let it be heard) / अस्य (of this) / धनुषः (of the bow) / यदर्थम् (for what reason) / इह (here) / तिष्ठति (stands)
ramayan::1722.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1722.essence: The bow is not just kept here; it carries a buried history.
ramayan::1722.simple_meaning: Janaka begins explaining the bow's origin and why it has been kept in his court.
ramayan::1722.simple_insight: Some questions open the door to a much older story.
ramayan::1722.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have asked to see Shiva's bow. Janaka answers the sage and the princes by starting the bow's history, leading into the story of how it came to be guarded in Mithila.
ramayan::1722.modern_relevance: Someone asks where an old family rule came from, and the answer reaches back through generations. What looked like a simple object turns out to carry a whole inheritance.
ramayan::1722.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the story and duty behind it.

ramayan::1723.verse_sanskrit: देवरात इति ख्यातो निमेष्षष्ठो महीपति: । न्यासोऽयं तस्य भगवन् हस्ते दत्तो महात्मना । । 1668 । ।
ramayan::1723.verse_hindi: O Adorable one there was a famous king named Devarata, sixth in line from Nimi. This bow was kept with him in trust by the exalted lord (Shiva).
ramayan::1723.english_translation: O Adorable one, there was a famous king named Devarata, sixth in line from Nimi. This bow was kept with him in trust by the exalted lord (Shiva).
ramayan::1723.translation_literal: देवरातः (Devarata) / इति (thus) / ख्यातः (famous) / निमेष्षष्ठः (sixth in the line of Nimi) / महीपतिः (king) / न्यासः (a trust / deposit) / अयम् (this) / तस्य (with him) / भगवन् (O revered one) / हस्ते (in the hand) / दत्तः (given) / महात्मना (by the great being)
ramayan::1723.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1723.essence: What is held in trust carries its own sacred weight.
ramayan::1723.simple_meaning: Janaka explains that a king named Devarata once received this bow as a sacred trust from Shiva.
ramayan::1723.simple_insight: Some things are not owned; they are held with responsibility until the right moment.
ramayan::1723.detailed_meaning: Janaka is answering the sages’ question before Sita’s swayamvara. He traces the bow’s history back to Devarata, showing that it is no ordinary weapon but a revered trust handed down through generations. The explanation prepares the ground for the bow’s test.
ramayan::1723.modern_relevance: You open a family safe and find something precious that was never really yours to keep. It was only passed to you for the right moment.
ramayan::1723.insight: It frames possession as stewardship, not entitlement.

ramayan::1724.verse_sanskrit: दक्षयज्ञवधे पूर्वं धनुरायम्य वीर्यवान् । रुद्रस्तु त्रिदशान् रोषात्सलीलमिदमब्रवीत् । । 1669 । ।
ramayan::1724.verse_hindi: Earlier at the time of destruction of Dakshas sacrifice, Rudra endowed with  great
ramayan::1724.english_translation: Earlier, at the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice, mighty Rudra drew his bow and, in anger, said this playfully to the gods.
ramayan::1724.translation_literal: दक्षयज्ञवधे (at the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice) / पूर्वं (earlier) / धनुः (bow) / आयम्य (having drawn) / वीर्यवान् (the mighty one) / रुद्रः (Rudra) / तु (indeed) / त्रिदशान् (to the gods) / रोषात् (from anger) / सलीलम् (playfully) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1724.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1724.essence: The bow's history begins in divine anger, not ceremony.
ramayan::1724.simple_meaning: Rudra once drew his bow during Daksha's sacrifice and spoke to the gods in angry play.
ramayan::1724.simple_insight: Power can turn terrifying when anger starts to play with it.
ramayan::1724.detailed_meaning: Janaka is explaining the bow's origin to Vishvamitra. He traces it back to the violent aftermath of Daksha's sacrifice, when Rudra, angered, drew this very bow before the gods. The verse is a supporting detail in the bow's history.
ramayan::1724.modern_relevance: A person in power makes one cutting remark, and the whole room goes still. The force is real, but the verse is only explaining where that force came from.
ramayan::1724.insight: It adds background to the bow's sacred and dangerous history, not a complete teaching.

ramayan::1725.verse_sanskrit: यस्माद्भागार्थिनो भागान्नाकल्पयत मे सुरा: । वराङ्गाणि महार्हाणि धनुषा शातयामि व: । । 16610 । ।
ramayan::1725.verse_hindi: O gods in your anxiety to partake your share of the sacrifie, you have failed to provide mine in the sacrificial offerings. Therefore, I shall sever your jewelled heads and beautiful limbs with this bow.
ramayan::1725.english_translation: O gods, because you did not assign my share among the sacrificial portions, I shall cut off your splendid heads and limbs with this bow.
ramayan::1725.translation_literal: यस्मात् (because) / भागार्थिनः (those desiring a share) / भागात् (from the share) / न (not) / अकल्पयत (you arranged) / मे (for me) / सुराः (gods) / वराङ्गाणि (beautiful limbs) / महार्हाणि (highly precious) / धनुषा (with the bow) / शातयामि (I shall cut off) / वः (your)
ramayan::1725.speaker: Rudra
ramayan::1725.essence: Excluded honor turns into a threat of ruin.
ramayan::1725.simple_meaning: Rudra warns the gods that because they withheld his share in the sacrifice, he will strike back with his bow.
ramayan::1725.simple_insight: Neglect and insult can turn quickly into destructive rage.
ramayan::1725.detailed_meaning: At Daksha's sacrifice, Rudra has been excluded from his rightful share. Standing armed before the gods, he speaks in anger and threatens them. This verse is not the teaching itself, but the sharp edge of the conflict that forces the gods to seek peace.
ramayan::1725.modern_relevance: You get left out of the credit, the invitation, the reward — and the hurt turns hot fast. This is what insult looks like before it becomes retaliation.
ramayan::1725.insight: It shows how wounded pride can escalate into violence when respect is denied.

ramayan::1726.verse_sanskrit: ततो विमनसस्सर्वे देवा वै मुनिपुङ्गव । प्रसादयन्ति देवेशं तेषां प्रीतोऽभवद्भव: । । 16611 । ।
ramayan::1726.verse_hindi: O Eminent ascetic thereafter all the gods with agitated minds propitiated lord of the gods, Siva and he was pleased with them.
ramayan::1726.english_translation: Then all the gods, O best of sages, with troubled minds, propitiated the Lord of the gods, and Bhava became pleased with them.
ramayan::1726.translation_literal: ततः (then) / विमनसः (troubled-minded) / सर्वे (all) / देवाः (the gods) / वै (indeed) / मुनिपुङ्गव (O best of sages) / प्रसादयन्ति (propitiated) / देवेशम् (the Lord of the gods) / तेषाम् (of them) / प्रीतः (pleased) / अभवत् (became) / भवः (Bhava)
ramayan::1726.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1726.essence: Troubled pride yields only when it learns humility.
ramayan::1726.simple_meaning: The gods, shaken and uneasy, turned to Shiva and sought his favor. Their appeal worked, and he became pleased with them.
ramayan::1726.simple_insight: Even powerful beings must soften, ask, and repair what they have broken.
ramayan::1726.detailed_meaning: After Shiva threatens the gods for excluding his share from Daksha's sacrifice, they lose their composure and come forward to appease him. This verse marks the turning point where their propitiation succeeds and Shiva's anger begins to ease.
ramayan::1726.modern_relevance: You said something careless, and the room went cold. Pride will not fix it; only a sincere apology can.
ramayan::1726.insight: It shows that harm can be answered only by humility and repair, not force.

ramayan::1727.verse_sanskrit: प्रीतियुक्तस्स सर्वेषां ददौ तेषां महात्मनाम् । तदेतद्देवदेवस्य धनूरत्नं महात्मन: । न्यासभूतं तदा न्यस्तमस्माकं पूर्व के विभो । । 16612 । ।
ramayan::1727.verse_hindi: O Lord that gem of a bow belonging to Siva was given to the great gods who in turn got it deposited in trust with our ancestor.
ramayan::1727.english_translation: O Lord, that gem among bows, belonging to Shiva, was given to the great gods, who then placed it in trust with our ancestor.
ramayan::1727.translation_literal: प्रीतियुक्तः (pleased) / सः (he) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / ददौ (gave) / तेषाम् (to them) / महात्मनाम् (of the great-souled ones) / तत् (that) / एतत् (this) / देवदेवस्य (of the god of gods) / धनूरत्नम् (gem of a bow) / महात्मनः (of the great one) / न्यासभूतम् (held in trust) / तदा (then) / न्यस्तम् (placed) / अस्माकम् (of ours) / पूर्वके (to the ancestor) / विभो (O lord)
ramayan::1727.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::1727.essence: The bow matters because it was entrusted, not merely owned.
ramayan::1727.simple_meaning: Shiva's great bow was once handed to the gods, and the gods later entrusted it to an ancestor of Ravana's line.
ramayan::1727.simple_insight: It is a lineage claim, not a teaching: Ravana is establishing the bow's sacred custody and his own right to speak of it.
ramayan::1727.detailed_meaning: Ravana is explaining the bow's origin to Parashurama. After the gods pleased Shiva, Shiva gave them the bow, and they placed it in trust with Ravana's ancestor. The verse serves the argument that this weapon has a long, honored history.
ramayan::1727.modern_relevance: Someone in a family argument reaches for old records, old promises, and inherited objects to prove a point. The real issue is not the object alone, but who has the right to claim it.
ramayan::1727.insight: It shifts attention from the weapon itself to the chain of trust behind it.

ramayan::1728.verse_sanskrit: अथ मे कृषत: क्षेत्रं लाङ्गूलादुत्थिता मया । क्षेत्रं शोधयता लब्धा नाम्ना सीतेति विश्रुता । । 16613 । ।
ramayan::1728.verse_hindi: Thereupon while I was ploughing and cleaing the (sacrificial) ground, Sita, a wellknown name, was lifted up by the blade of the plough. Thus she was obtained by
ramayan::1728.english_translation: Thereupon, while I was ploughing and clearing the sacrificial ground, Sita was raised up by the blade of the plough and became known by that name.
ramayan::1728.translation_literal: अथ (thereupon) / मे (by me) / कृषत: (while ploughing) / क्षेत्रं (the field) / लाङ्गूलात् (by the ploughshare) / उत्थिता (raised up) / मया (by me) / क्षेत्रं (the field) / शोधयता (while clearing) / लब्धा (found) / नाम्ना (by name) / सीता (Sita) / इति (thus) / विश्रुता (well-known)
ramayan::1728.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1728.essence: Sita is found, not born in the usual way.
ramayan::1728.simple_meaning: Janaka says he found Sita while ploughing and clearing the sacrificial ground. She rose from the earth and became known as Sita.
ramayan::1728.simple_insight: Some lives arrive as gifts, not possessions.
ramayan::1728.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's account of Sita's origin, he recalls ploughing the sacrificial field when the earth yielded a child. The verse explains her name and miraculous emergence, setting up her later role as Janaka's adopted daughter.
ramayan::1728.modern_relevance: A family story gets told again at a naming ceremony: where did she come from, why that name, what made her special? This verse is that origin story, not its deeper meaning.
ramayan::1728.insight: It grounds Sita's identity in emergence and discovery, not ordinary birth.

ramayan::1729.verse_sanskrit: भूतलादुत्थिता सा तु व्यवर्धत ममात्मजा । वीर्यशुल्केति मे कन्या स्थापितेयमयोनिजा । । 16614 । ।
ramayan::1729.verse_hindi: Arisen from the earth and not from a mothers womb, she grew up as my daughter. I made a stipulation that (this shall be the means to win this maiden as a gift) this shall be given in marriage only to the prince whose prowess is fully tried.
ramayan::1729.english_translation: Arisen from the earth and not from a mother's womb, she grew up as my daughter. I set the condition that she would be given in marriage only to the prince whose prowess was fully proven.
ramayan::1729.translation_literal: भूतलात् (from the earth) / उत्थिता (arisen) / सा (she) / तु (indeed) / व्यवर्धत (grew up) / मम (my) / आत्मजा (daughter) / वीर्य-शुल्का (with prowess as the price) / इति (thus) / मे (my) / कन्या (maiden daughter) / स्थापिता (was established) / इयम् (this one) / अयोनिजा (not born from a womb)
ramayan::1729.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1729.essence: What is most precious deserves proof before possession.
ramayan::1729.simple_meaning: Janaka says Sita, though found in the earth and raised as his daughter, was promised only to a prince whose strength had been tested.
ramayan::1729.simple_insight: What is truly precious should not be handed over casually.
ramayan::1729.detailed_meaning: Janaka is speaking about Sita’s extraordinary origin and the vow he made for her marriage. Found while ploughing the field, she grew up in his care, and he set a severe test: only a prince who could prove his prowess could win her.
ramayan::1729.modern_relevance: You have seen people ask for commitment without offering any proof of character. This verse honours a higher standard: when something matters deeply, it deserves real testing before trust is given.
ramayan::1729.insight: It shifts the mind from casual choice to earned responsibility.

ramayan::1730.verse_sanskrit: भूतलादुत्थितां तां तु वर्धमानां ममात्मजाम् । वरयामासुरागम्य राजानो मुनिपुंगव । । 16615 । ।
ramayan::1730.verse_hindi: O Eminent ascetic arisen from the earth and reared as my daughter, she has been sought after in marriage by many princes.
ramayan::1730.english_translation: O eminent ascetic, the maiden who arose from the earth and grew up as my daughter was sought in marriage by many princes.
ramayan::1730.translation_literal: भूतलादुत्थितां (arisen from the earth) / तां (that) / तु (indeed) / वर्धमानां (growing up) / ममात्मजाम् (my daughter) / वरयामासुः (sought in marriage) / आगम्य (having come) / राजानः (kings) / मुनिपुंगव (O foremost among sages)
ramayan::1730.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1730.essence: Many wanted her; Janaka still guarded what was worthy of her.
ramayan::1730.simple_meaning: Sita, who was found in the earth and raised as Janaka's daughter, had already been desired in marriage by many kings.
ramayan::1730.simple_insight: Her value was known widely, but her heart and fate were still being tested.
ramayan::1730.detailed_meaning: Janaka is explaining Sita's extraordinary status to the sage. She was found in the earth, raised as his daughter, and had already attracted many royal suitors. This verse supports his larger explanation of why her marriage is no ordinary matter.
ramayan::1730.modern_relevance: A family knows their daughter is remarkable long before the world does. Suitors, praise, and attention can come early — but that does not settle what kind of life will truly honor her.
ramayan::1730.insight: It shifts attention from public admiration to the deeper question of worthiness.

ramayan::1731.verse_sanskrit: तेषां वरयतां कन्यां सर्वेषां पृथिवीक्षिताम् । वीर्यशुल्केति भगवन् न ददामि सुतामहम् । । 16616 । ।
ramayan::1731.verse_hindi: O Worshipful one all those monarchs sought this maiden but I did not offer my daughter saying that the marriage offer could be made only through the tried and tested prowess of a suitor.
ramayan::1731.english_translation: O Worshipful one, all those monarchs sought this maiden, but I did not offer my daughter, saying that her hand could be won only through proven prowess.
ramayan::1731.translation_literal: तेषां (of them) / वरयताम् (seeking in marriage) / कन्याम् (the maiden) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / पृथिवीक्षिताम् (of the earth's rulers) / वीर्यशुल्का (with prowess as the bride-price) / इति (thus) / भगवन् (O worshipful one) / न (not) / ददामि (I give) / सुताम् (my daughter) / अहम् (I)
ramayan::1731.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1731.essence: True worth is proved, not requested.
ramayan::1731.simple_meaning: Janaka says he did not give Sita to the kings who asked for her. He set a condition: only a suitor whose strength and skill were proven could win her.
ramayan::1731.simple_insight: Worth is not claimed by status; it is shown through action.
ramayan::1731.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, King Janaka has raised Sita as his daughter and watched many kings ask for her hand. He refuses them all. This moment explains why the swayamvara will become a test of strength, not a mere marriage proposal.
ramayan::1731.modern_relevance: A family watches one candidate after another talk confidently in a living room, but the decision still hangs on character, not charm. Some doors open only when you can actually meet the standard.
ramayan::1731.insight: It shifts judgment from reputation to demonstrated capability.

ramayan::1732.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सर्वे नृपतय स्समेत्य मुनिपुंगव । मिथिलामभ्युपागम्य वीर्यजिज्ञासवस्तदा । । 16617 । ।
ramayan::1732.verse_hindi: O Preeminent among ascetics thereafter many kings together came to Mithila to test their prowess.
ramayan::1732.english_translation: Then all those kings gathered together, O best of ascetics, and came to Mithila to test their strength.
ramayan::1732.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / सर्वे (all) / नृपतयः (kings) / समेत्य (having gathered) / मुनिपुंगव (O best among ascetics) / मिथिलाम् (to Mithila) / अभ्युपागम्य (having come) / वीर्यजिज्ञासवः (desiring to test strength) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1732.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1732.essence: The contest begins when proud kings arrive to prove themselves.
ramayan::1732.simple_meaning: Many kings came together to Mithila because they wanted to test their strength.
ramayan::1732.simple_insight: Great challenges draw in those who want to prove themselves.
ramayan::1732.detailed_meaning: Janaka has announced Sita's swayamvara and set a condition based on strength. In response, kings from many lands gather in Mithila, eager to try their power. This verse simply sets the scene before the bow is brought out.
ramayan::1732.modern_relevance: A room fills before a competition, each person pretending not to care too much. The real test has not started yet, but everyone already feels it coming.
ramayan::1732.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd to the moment when strength will actually be measured.

ramayan::1733.verse_sanskrit: तेषां जिज्ञासमानानां वीर्यं धनुरुपाहृतम् । न शेकुर्ग्रहणे तस्य धनुषस्तोलनेऽपि वा । । 16618 । ।
ramayan::1733.verse_hindi: The bow was brought and placed before those who were curious to test their strength
ramayan::1733.english_translation: The bow was brought before those who had come to test their strength, but none could lift it or even move it.
ramayan::1733.translation_literal: तेषां (of them) / जिज्ञासमानानां (of those wishing to know/test) / वीर्यम् (strength) / धनुः (the bow) / उपाहृतम् (was brought forward) / न (not) / शेकुः (they were able) / ग्रहणे (in taking hold) / तस्य (of that) / धनुषः (bow) / तोलने (in lifting) / अपि (even) / वा (or)
ramayan::1733.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1733.essence: Pride meets reality before a single boast can matter.
ramayan::1733.simple_meaning: The bow was brought out for the kings to test, but none of them could even lift it, much less string it.
ramayan::1733.simple_insight: Some challenges reveal your limits before you speak a word.
ramayan::1733.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, many kings have gathered to win Sita by proving their strength. Janaka has the great bow brought before them, and the test begins. This verse shows the silence after pride meets an impossible task.
ramayan::1733.modern_relevance: You walk into a room thinking your résumé will carry you. Then the real test appears, and your confidence has to answer to reality.
ramayan::1733.insight: It shifts attention from boasting about strength to facing what you can actually do.

ramayan::1734.verse_sanskrit: तेषां वीर्यवतां वीर्यमल्पं ज्ञात्वा महामुने । प्रत्याख्याता नृपतयस्तन्निबोध तपोधन । । 16619 । ।
ramayan::1734.verse_hindi: O great ascetic I knew those mighty kings had little strength, so rejected them.
ramayan::1734.english_translation: O great ascetic, knowing that the strength of those mighty kings was small, I rejected them. Understand this, O treasure of austerity.
ramayan::1734.translation_literal: तेषां (of them) / वीर्यवतां (of the strong) / वीर्यम् (strength) / अल्पम् (small) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / महामुने (O great ascetic) / प्रत्याख्याता (rejected) / नृपतयः (the kings) / तद् (that) / निबोध (understand) / तपोधन (O treasure of austerity)
ramayan::1734.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1734.essence: Strength must be real before pride can prove anything.
ramayan::1734.simple_meaning: The speaker says he recognized the kings had little strength, so he turned them away.
ramayan::1734.simple_insight: Not every challenge deserves a test you are not ready for.
ramayan::1734.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, many kings have come to test the great bow. The speaker explains to the sage why they were refused: their strength was too little to even lift it, let alone string it. The verse is a supporting explanation, not the main teaching.
ramayan::1734.modern_relevance: You can watch people rush into a task they cannot yet carry, then blame the task when they fail. Sometimes the honest answer is to name the mismatch early.
ramayan::1734.insight: It shifts the mind toward honest assessment before pride turns effort into humiliation.

ramayan::1735.verse_sanskrit: तत: परमकोपेन राजानो नृपपुङ्गव । न्यरुंधन्मिथिलां सर्वे वीर्यसंदेहमागता: । । 16620 । ।
ramayan::1735.verse_hindi: O Mighty ascetic, thereafter all the kings doubting their own strength in stringing the bow were inflamed with anger and laid siege on Mithila.
ramayan::1735.english_translation: Then, enraged, all the kings who had begun to doubt their strength laid siege to Mithila.
ramayan::1735.translation_literal: तत: (then) / परमकोपेन (with great anger) / राजानो (the kings) / नृपपुङ्गव (O best among kings) / न्यरुंधन् (besieged) / मिथिलाम् (Mithila) / सर्वे (all) / वीर्यसंदेहमागता: (having come to doubt their strength)
ramayan::1735.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1735.essence: Wounded pride often attacks what exposed it.
ramayan::1735.simple_meaning: The kings, embarrassed by their failure to string the bow, grew furious and surrounded Mithila.
ramayan::1735.simple_insight: Pride can turn quickly into aggression when strength is questioned.
ramayan::1735.detailed_meaning: The assembled kings had tried and failed to lift or string Shiva's bow. Their public humiliation hardened into rage, and instead of accepting defeat they turned against Mithila itself. This is a scene of wounded pride, not wisdom.
ramayan::1735.modern_relevance: A group chat goes silent after your idea gets ignored, and the next message comes back sharp. What was really hurt was pride, not the issue itself.
ramayan::1735.insight: It shows how humiliation can harden into retaliation instead of self-examination.

ramayan::1736.verse_sanskrit: आत्मानमवधूतं ते विज्ञाय नृपपुङ्गवा: । रोषेण महताऽऽविष्टा: पीडयन्मिथिलां पुरीम् । । 16621 । ।
ramayan::1736.verse_hindi: Those eminent kings felt humiliated. Inflamed with anger, they tormented the city of Mithila.
ramayan::1736.english_translation: Those eminent kings felt humiliated. Inflamed with anger, they tormented the city of Mithila.
ramayan::1736.translation_literal: आत्मानम् (themselves) / अवधूतम् (insulted, humiliated) / ते (they) / विज्ञाय (having understood) / नृपपुङ्गवा: (bulls among kings) / रोषेण (with anger) / महता (great) / आविष्टा: (possessed, seized) / पीडयन् (tormenting) / मिथिलाम् (Mithila) / पुरीम् (the city)
ramayan::1736.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1736.essence: Humiliation turned the kings' disappointment into cruelty.
ramayan::1736.simple_meaning: The kings took the rejection as an insult. Angry and wounded, they lashed out at the city of Mithila.
ramayan::1736.detailed_meaning: The contest for Sita's hand has already exposed the kings' limits. After failing at Shiva's bow, they do not bow out gracefully; they react with wounded pride and begin troubling Mithila itself.
ramayan::1736.modern_relevance: You were turned down, and the sting made you want to punish the whole room. That impulse says more about your pride than the rejection.
ramayan::1736.insight: It shows how bruised ego can spread suffering beyond the original slight.

ramayan::1737.verse_sanskrit: ततस्संवत्सरे पूर्णे क्षयं यातानि सर्वश: । साधनानि मुनिश्रेष्ठ ततोऽहं भृशदु:खित: । । 16622 । ।
ramayan::1737.verse_hindi: O Best among ascetics thus one year passed. Everywhere in the city all the means of living were exhausted. I felt deeply sad over this situation.
ramayan::1737.english_translation: O Best among ascetics, thus one year passed. Everywhere in the city all the means of living were exhausted. I felt deeply sad over this situation.
ramayan::1737.translation_literal: ततस्संवत्सरे (then, after a year) / पूर्णे (having been completed) / क्षयं (depletion, exhaustion) / यातानि (had gone to) / सर्वशः (in every way, everywhere) / साधनानि (means, resources) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (O best among ascetics) / ततः (then) / अहम् (I) / भृशदुःखितः (deeply saddened)
ramayan::1737.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1737.essence: A long delay can empty both a city and the heart watching it.
ramayan::1737.simple_meaning: A year passed, the city’s resources ran out, and the speaker felt deep grief over the hardship.
ramayan::1737.simple_insight: Long waiting can drain a whole place, not just a single heart.
ramayan::1737.detailed_meaning: The city has been under strain for a full year, and every resource has been used up. The speaker, watching the exhaustion spread through Mithila, feels sorrow before the next turn in the story brings a new response.
ramayan::1737.modern_relevance: You keep patching things together for months, and then one morning you see the cupboard empty, the bills stacked, and the strain everywhere at once.
ramayan::1737.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the slow exhaustion that builds before a crisis breaks.

ramayan::1738.verse_sanskrit: ततो देवगणान् सर्वान् तपसाऽहं प्रसादयम् । ददुश्च परमप्रीता श्चतुरङ्गबलं सुरा: । । 16623 । ।
ramayan::1738.verse_hindi: Thereafter, I propitiated the gods by my austerities. Highly pleased, they gave me an army of four divisions (chariots, elephants, horses and infantry ).
ramayan::1738.english_translation: Thereafter, I propitiated the gods by my austerities. Highly pleased, they gave me an army of four divisions: chariots, elephants, horses, and infantry.
ramayan::1738.translation_literal: ततस् (thereafter) / देवगणान् (the hosts of gods) / सर्वान् (all) / तपसा (by austerity) / अहम् (I) / प्रसादयम् (propitiated) / ददुः (gave) / च (and) / परमप्रीताः (highly pleased) / चतुरङ्गबलम् (an army of four divisions) / सुराः (the gods)
ramayan::1738.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1738.essence: Austerity can turn exhaustion into unexpected support.
ramayan::1738.simple_meaning: By severe effort, the speaker won the favor of the divine beings, who then granted a powerful four-part army.
ramayan::1738.simple_insight: Hard effort can draw help when you’ve exhausted your own strength.
ramayan::1738.detailed_meaning: The sage is describing a crisis in Mithila after a year of strain and depletion. Having won over the divine beings through austerity, he receives a fourfold army of chariots, elephants, horses, and foot soldiers. It is a practical turning point, not a philosophical teaching.
ramayan::1738.modern_relevance: You’ve pushed through months of pressure, and suddenly the support you needed arrives. The breakthrough feels earned because you kept going when everything was running out.
ramayan::1738.insight: It highlights perseverance under scarcity and the arrival of aid after sustained discipline.

ramayan::1739.verse_sanskrit: ततो भग्ना नृपतयो हन्यमाना दिशो ययु: । अवीर्या वीर्यसन्दिग्धा स्सामात्या: पापकर्मण: । । 16624 । ।
ramayan::1739.verse_hindi: Then those wicked kings who were exhausted were doubtful about their energy. They were beaten and defeated. They fled away along with their ministers in different directions.
ramayan::1739.english_translation: Then those wicked kings, worn out in battle, lost all confidence in their strength. Defeated and struck down, they fled in every direction with their ministers.
ramayan::1739.translation_literal: ततः (then) / भग्नाः (broken, defeated) / नृपतयः (kings) / हन्यमानाः (being struck down) / दिशः (directions) / ययुः (went, fled) / अवीर्याः (without strength) / वीर्यसन्दिग्धाः (doubtful about their valor) / सः (those) / अमात्याः (with ministers) / पापकर्मणः (of wicked deeds)
ramayan::1739.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1739.essence: Defeat exposes how fragile borrowed strength really is.
ramayan::1739.simple_meaning: The enemy kings were beaten so badly that they lost courage and ran away with their ministers.
ramayan::1739.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when strength is no longer enough.
ramayan::1739.detailed_meaning: A battle has gone against the opposing kings. Their forces are broken, their confidence in their own power is gone, and they scatter in fear with their ministers. The verse simply marks the collapse before the next action begins.
ramayan::1739.modern_relevance: A team meeting falls apart after the numbers are shown, and the people who were loudest an hour ago suddenly have nothing to say. The truth of the moment strips away the performance.
ramayan::1739.insight: It shows how quickly false confidence disappears when reality pushes back.

ramayan::1740.verse_sanskrit: तदेतन्मुनिशार्दूल धनु: परमभास्वरम् । रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि दर्शयिष्यामि सुव्रत । । 16625 । ।
ramayan::1740.verse_hindi: O Sage you are a tiger among asceties, you are faithful to your vows, I shall show this effulgent bow to your Rama and Lakshmana .
ramayan::1740.english_translation: O tiger among sages, devoted to your vows, I shall show this dazzling bow to Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayan::1740.translation_literal: तत् (that) / एतत् (this) / मुनि-शार्दूल (tiger among sages) / धनुः (bow) / परम-भास्वरम् (supremely radiant) / राम-लक्ष्मणयोः (to Rama and Lakshmana) / च (and) / अपि (also) / दर्शयिष्यामि (I shall show) / सुव्रत (O one of good vows)
ramayan::1740.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1740.essence: The bow is shown first; the real challenge comes next.
ramayan::1740.simple_meaning: Janaka tells the sage that he will show Rama and Lakshmana a radiant bow.
ramayan::1740.simple_insight: The challenge is being set in motion, but the real test is still ahead.
ramayan::1740.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, after the defeated kings have scattered, he turns to Vishvamitra with formal respect. He points to the radiant bow and says he will show it to Rama and Lakshmana. This is the opening move before the marriage test is revealed.
ramayan::1740.modern_relevance: Someone says, “Let me show you what this really takes,” just before the hard part begins.
ramayan::1740.insight: It sets up a public test of worth before the true condition is stated.

ramayan::1741.verse_sanskrit: यद्यस्य धनुषो राम: कुर्यादारोपणं मुने । सुतामयोनिजां सीतां दद्यां दाशरथेरहम् । । 16626 । ।
ramayan::1741.verse_hindi: O Sage if Rama could lift and string this bow I shall give my daughter Sita, not born from a woman, to him (son of Dasaratha).
ramayan::1741.english_translation: O Sage, if Rama can string this bow, I will give my daughter Sita, who was not born of a woman, to that son of Dasaratha.
ramayan::1741.translation_literal: यदि (if) अस्य (this) धनुषः (of the bow) रामः (Rama) कुर्यात् (should do) आरोपणम् (stringing / lifting) मुने (O sage) । सुताम् (daughter) अयोनिजाम् (not born from a womb) सीताम् (Sita) दद्याम् (I would give) दाशरथेः (of Dasaratha's son) अहम् (I) ।
ramayan::1741.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1741.essence: Worth is proved by what you can actually bear and do.
ramayan::1741.simple_meaning: Janaka sets the condition for Sita's marriage: if Rama can string the great bow, he will give Sita to him.
ramayan::1741.simple_insight: A single test can decide a life-changing bond.
ramayan::1741.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janaka speaks before the gathered sages and princes. Vishvamitra has brought Rama to see the great bow, and Janaka declares the marriage condition: only the man who can string it may win Sita. This verse is the challenge itself, not the deeper teaching.
ramayan::1741.modern_relevance: A father watches quietly as one person’s skill, steadiness, and worth are about to be tested in public. One decisive moment will change two lives.
ramayan::1741.insight: It frames marriage as a test of readiness, not mere desire.

ramayan::1742.verse_sanskrit: जनकस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । धनुर्दर्शय रामाय इति होवाच पार्थिवम् । । 1671 । ।
ramayan::1742.verse_hindi: At the words of Janaka, great ascetic Viswamitra said to the king, Let the bow be shown to Rama.
ramayan::1742.english_translation: At the words of Janaka, the great ascetic Vishwamitra said to the king, "Show the bow to Rama."
ramayan::1742.translation_literal: जनकस्य (of Janaka) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / विश्वामित्रः (Vishvamitra) / महामुनिः (great ascetic) / धनुः (the bow) / दर्शय (show) / रामाय (to Rama) / इति (thus) / ह उवाच (indeed said) / पार्थिवम् (to the king)
ramayan::1742.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1742.essence: The real test begins when the bow is brought forward.
ramayan::1742.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra tells Janaka to bring the bow and show it to Rama.
ramayan::1742.simple_insight: The next step is simple: let the test begin.
ramayan::1742.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, the bow has become the measure of Rama's worth. Vishvamitra, who brought Rama here, now tells the king to present it to him. The scene is still preparing the decisive moment, not delivering the teaching itself.
ramayan::1742.modern_relevance: A hiring manager finally says, “Bring in the candidate.” The room goes quiet because the real test is about to begin.
ramayan::1742.insight: It moves the story from discussion to challenge, setting up the proof that will matter.

ramayan::1743.verse_sanskrit: ततस्स राजा जनक: सामन्तान्व्यादिदेश ह । धनुरानीयतां दिव्यं गन्धमाल्यविभूषितम् । । 1672 । ।
ramayan::1743.verse_hindi: Thereafter king Janaka said to his feudatories, Let the divine bow adorned with flowers and sandalpaste be brought.
ramayan::1743.english_translation: Thereafter King Janaka said to his attendants, "Let the divine bow, adorned with flowers and sandal paste, be brought here."
