ramayan::1743.translation_literal: ततस् (thereafter) / राजा (king) / जनकः (Janaka) / सामन्तान् (to his attendants) / व्यादिदेश (commanded) / ह / धनुः (the bow) / आनीयताम् (let it be brought) / दिव्यम् (divine) / गन्धमाल्यविभूषितम् (adorned with sandal paste and garlands)
ramayan::1743.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1743.essence: A promise becomes real only when the test is brought forward.
ramayan::1743.simple_meaning: Janaka orders his attendants to bring the sacred bow, decorated with flowers and sandal paste, so Rama can try it.
ramayan::1743.simple_insight: A decisive moment is coming, and everyone feels it.
ramayan::1743.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janaka has just said he will give Sita to Rama if Rama can string the bow. Viswamitra has asked for the bow to be shown. Now Janaka orders his men to bring it out, setting the trial in motion.
ramayan::1743.modern_relevance: Someone finally says, “Bring it here,” and the room goes quiet. A promise is no longer abstract; it is about to be tested in front of everyone.
ramayan::1743.insight: It moves the scene from agreement to action, where words must face reality.

ramayan::1744.verse_sanskrit: जनकेन समादिष्टा: सचिवा प्राविशन् पुरीम् । तद्धनु: पुरत: कृत्वा निर्जग्मु: पार्थिवाज्ञया । । 1673 । ।
ramayan::1744.verse_hindi: Commanded by (king) Janaka, the ministers went to the city, put the bow in front of them and carried it as per the orders of the king.
ramayan::1744.english_translation: Commanded by Janaka, the ministers entered the city, placed the bow before them, and brought it out by the king's order.
ramayan::1744.translation_literal: जनकेन (by Janaka) / समादिष्टाः (commanded) / सचिवाः (ministers) / प्राविशन् (entered) / पुरीम् (the city) / तत्-धनुः (that bow) / पुरतः (in front) / कृत्वा (having made) / निर्जग्मुः (went out) / पार्थिव-आज्ञया (by the king's order)
ramayan::1744.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1744.essence: The bow is brought out, and the test begins to take shape.
ramayan::1744.simple_meaning: Janaka's ministers go into the city and carry out the great bow exactly as ordered. It is a moving step in the larger scene, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1744.simple_insight: Sometimes the most important moments are the ones that simply move the story forward.
ramayan::1744.detailed_meaning: After Janaka's command, his ministers enter the city, place the divine bow before them, and carry it out. The scene is preparing the way for Rama to face the bow; this verse is a logistical step in that larger test.
ramayan::1744.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet while people shift the heavy object everyone has been waiting to see. The real moment is coming, but first someone has to carry it into place.
ramayan::1744.insight: It shows how epic events often depend on small, obedient actions before the decisive moment.

ramayan::1745.verse_sanskrit: नृणां शतानि पञ्चाशद्व्यायतानां महात्मनाम् । मञ्जूषामष्टचक्रां तां समूहुस्ते कथञ्चन । । 1674 । ।
ramayan::1745.verse_hindi: Five thousand mighty stalwarts drew with great difficulty the eightwheeled cart on which the bow was placed in a box.
ramayan::1745.english_translation: Five thousand mighty stalwarts drew with great difficulty the eight-wheeled cart on which the bow was placed in a box.
ramayan::1745.translation_literal: नृणाम् (of men) / शतानि (hundreds) / पञ्चाशत् (fifty) / व्यायतानाम् (of strong-built) / महात्मनाम् (of great-souled) / मञ्जूषाम् (box/casket) / अष्टचक्राम् (eight-wheeled) / ताम् (that) / समूहुः (drew together) / ते (they) / कथञ्चन (with difficulty)
ramayan::1745.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1745.essence: Even moving the bow’s casket demands extraordinary force.
ramayan::1745.simple_meaning: Five thousand strong men could barely pull the cart carrying the bow.
ramayan::1745.simple_insight: Some burdens are so heavy that even strength must strain together.
ramayan::1745.detailed_meaning: Janaka has ordered the divine bow brought out for the contest. Even before anyone tries the challenge itself, five thousand powerful men struggle just to move the cart carrying its casket. The verse builds the bow’s impossible weight, not the lesson.
ramayan::1745.modern_relevance: A team heaves a stuck machine down a corridor, muscles tight, faces red, and still it barely moves. Some things announce their weight before the real test even begins.
ramayan::1745.insight: It sets up the bow as an object beyond ordinary human power, raising the stakes for the contest.

ramayan::1746.verse_sanskrit: तामादाय तु मञ्जूषामायसीं यत्र तद्धनु: । सुरोपमं ते जनकमूचुर्नृपतिमन्त्रिण: । । 1675 । ।
ramayan::1746.verse_hindi: The counsellors of the king, brought the iron casket containing the bow and said these words to Janaka comparable to a celestial:
ramayan::1746.english_translation: The king's counsellors brought the iron casket containing the bow and spoke to Janaka, who shone like a celestial being.
ramayan::1746.translation_literal: ताम् (that) / आदाय (having taken) / तु (then) / मञ्जूषाम् (casket) / आयसीम् (iron) / यत्र (where) / तत् (that) / धनुः (bow) / सुरोपमम् (celestial-like) / ते (they) / जनकम् (to Janaka) / ऊचुः (said) / नृपति-मन्त्रिणः (king's counsellors)
ramayan::1746.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1746.essence: The bow is brought forward, but the real test is still coming.
ramayan::1746.simple_meaning: Janaka's ministers carried the iron casket with the bow and addressed him respectfully.
ramayan::1746.simple_insight: A great task is unfolding, but this line is only the delivery of the bow, not the teaching.
ramayan::1746.detailed_meaning: Janaka's ministers have finally hauled the enormous casket containing Shiva's bow into place after great effort. Now they carry it before their king and speak to him with reverence. The real significance comes in the next verse, where the bow is formally presented.
ramayan::1746.modern_relevance: A heavy crate finally arrives after hours of effort, but the real moment is still ahead. This verse is the careful handoff before the decisive reveal.
ramayan::1746.insight: It marks the transition from effort to presentation, not the climax itself.

ramayan::1747.verse_sanskrit: इदं धनुर्वरं राजन् पूजितं सर्वराजभि: । मिथिलाधिप राजेन्द्र दर्शनीयं यदिच्छसि । । 1676 । ।
ramayan::1747.verse_hindi: O Indra among kings O lord of Mithila here is the great bow, worshipped by all kings,
ramayan::1747.english_translation: O king, O lord of Mithila, here is the great bow, honored by all kings and worthy of your sight if you wish.
ramayan::1747.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / धनुर्वरम् (best bow) / राजन् (O king) / पूजितम् (honored) / सर्वराजभि: (by all kings) / मिथिलाधिप (O lord of Mithila) / राजेन्द्र (O king among kings) / दर्शनीयम् (worthy of seeing) / यत् (which) / इच्छसि (you wish)
ramayan::1747.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1747.essence: The bow is introduced as a revered challenge, not just a weapon.
ramayan::1747.simple_meaning: Janaka is being shown the magnificent bow, praised by kings and worthy of admiration.
ramayan::1747.simple_insight: Great power can also be something people stop to honor in awe.
ramayan::1747.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the king's ministers present the iron casket and announce the bow inside to Janaka. They are setting the stage for the test that will reveal who can lift it and win Sita's hand.
ramayan::1747.modern_relevance: A room falls quiet when someone brings out the object everyone has heard about but no one has handled. Before the challenge begins, the whole atmosphere changes.
ramayan::1747.insight: It frames the bow as a revered object before the real test begins.

ramayan::1748.verse_sanskrit: तेषां नृपो वच: श्रुत्वा कृताञ्जलिरभाषत । विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं तौ चोभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ । । 1677 । ।
ramayan::1748.verse_hindi: Having heard this, the king with folded hands said to the great soul Viswamitra sitting with the two princes Rama and Lakshmana:
ramayan::1748.english_translation: Having heard this, the king with folded hands said to the great soul Viswamitra sitting with the two princes Rama and Lakshmana:
ramayan::1748.translation_literal: तेषाम् (their) / नृपः (the king) / वचः (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / कृताञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / अभाषत (spoke) / विश्वामित्रम् (to Vishvamitra) / महात्मानम् (the great-souled one) / तौ (those two) / च (and) / उभौ (both) / रामलक्ष्मणौ (Rama and Lakshmana)
ramayan::1748.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1748.essence: Power becomes graceful when it bows first.
ramayan::1748.simple_meaning: King Janaka listens respectfully and responds to Vishvamitra in the presence of Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayan::1748.simple_insight: True dignity begins with humility, even for a king.
ramayan::1748.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just had the sacred bow brought before Vishvamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana. Hearing the reply, he folds his hands and speaks with reverence. The verse simply marks the king's respectful turn in the ceremony before the bow's challenge is explained.
ramayan::1748.modern_relevance: You are in a room where everyone is waiting for your answer, and you choose respect before explanation. That pause changes the whole tone.
ramayan::1748.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that authority can speak humbly.

ramayan::1749.verse_sanskrit: इदं धनुर्वरं ब्रह्मन् जनकैरभिपूजितम् । राजभिश्च महावीर्यै: अशक्तै: पूरितुं पुरा । । 1678 । ।
ramayan::1749.verse_hindi: O Brahman in the olden days, this great bow was worshipped by my forefathers. Powerful kings failed to string this bow.
ramayan::1749.english_translation: O Brahman, this great bow was honored by my forefathers. In earlier times, powerful kings could not string it.
ramayan::1749.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / धनुर्वरम् (best of bows) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahman) / जनकैः (by the Janakas, by my forefathers) / अभिपूजितम् (highly honored) / राजभिः (by kings) / च (and) / महावीर्यैः (very powerful) / अशक्तैः (unable) / पूरितुम् (to string) / पुरा (formerly, in the past)
ramayan::1749.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1749.essence: The bow’s history already warns that ordinary strength will not be enough.
ramayan::1749.simple_meaning: Janaka tells Vishwamitra that this sacred bow was revered by his ancestors, and even mighty kings once failed to string it.
ramayan::1749.simple_insight: Some challenges are meant to reveal who is ready, not just who is strong.
ramayan::1749.detailed_meaning: King Janaka speaks before Vishwamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana, explaining the bow’s ancient prestige. He reminds them that this was never an ordinary weapon: even powerful rulers could not bend it. The statement builds the tension before the test.
ramayan::1749.modern_relevance: You inherit a task everyone says is impossible. Before you touch it, you already feel the weight of all the people who failed before you.
ramayan::1749.insight: It frames the bow as a threshold: only the truly worthy can pass it.

ramayan::1750.verse_sanskrit: नैतत्सुरगणास्सर्वे नासुरा न च राक्षसा: । गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवरा: सकिन्नरमहोरगा: । । 1679 । ।
ramayan::1750.verse_hindi: Hosts of devatas, asuras, rakhasas, kinnaras and great serpents, the best of gandharvas and yakshas, also failed (to wield this bow).
ramayan::1750.english_translation: All the hosts of devas, asuras, rakshasas, gandharvas, yakshas, kinnaras, and great serpents failed to wield this bow.
ramayan::1750.translation_literal: नैतत् (not this) / सुरगणाः (hosts of devas) / सर्वे (all) / न (not) / असुराः (asuras) / न (not) / च (and) / राक्षसाः (rakshasas) / गन्धर्व-यक्ष-प्रवराः (the best of gandharvas and yakshas) / सकिन्नर-महोरगाः (kinnaras and great serpents)
ramayan::1750.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1750.essence: Even the greatest powers had failed this test.
ramayan::1750.simple_meaning: No mighty being, human or nonhuman, had been able to string this bow.
ramayan::1750.simple_insight: Some challenges are meant to humble pride before they can reveal worth.
ramayan::1750.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, the great bow of his ancestors stands as a test no one has conquered. He tells Vishwamitra and the two princes that even devas, asuras, rakshasas, gandharvas, yakshas, kinnaras, and great serpents have failed before this impossible task.
ramayan::1750.modern_relevance: A room full of experts says a problem has beaten everyone before you. The scale of the challenge is the point: it shows who can meet it without boasting.
ramayan::1750.insight: It frames the bow as a limit that exposes who is ready for the next step.

ramayan::1751.verse_sanskrit: क्व गतिर्मानुषाणां च धनुषोऽस्य प्रपूरणे । आरोपणे समायोगे वेपने तोलनेऽपि वा । । 16710 । ।
ramayan::1751.verse_hindi: How then can men bend, string, fix the arrow, pull the string and lift it?
ramayan::1751.english_translation: How then can men bend, string, fix the arrow, pull the string and lift it?
ramayan::1751.translation_literal: क्व (where) / गतिः (ability, success) / मानुषाणां (of men) / च (and) / धनुषः (of the bow) / अस्य (this) / प्रपूरणे (in stringing, in filling) / आरोपणे (in placing on, stringing) / समायोगे (in fitting, joining) / वेपने (in drawing, shaking) / तोलने (in lifting, weighing) / अपि (even) / वा (or)
ramayan::1751.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1751.essence: Human strength means nothing before what this bow demands.
ramayan::1751.simple_meaning: No ordinary person can even handle this bow, let alone string it, fit the arrow, draw it, or lift it.
ramayan::1751.simple_insight: Some challenges are so beyond human strength that humility is the only honest response.
ramayan::1751.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, the ancient bow has already defeated kings, gods, and mighty beings. Now the speaker asks the obvious question: if all of them failed, what chance do ordinary men have? The line heightens the suspense before Rama and Lakshmana are asked to try.
ramayan::1751.modern_relevance: You stare at a task everyone else has already called impossible. Before you force it, you have to admit how heavy it really is.
ramayan::1751.insight: It frames the bow as a test of scale, not technique, and prepares the listener for a miracle.

ramayan::1752.verse_sanskrit: तदेतद्धनुषां श्रेष्ठमानीतं मुनिपुङ्गव । दर्शयैतन्महाभाग अनयो: राजपुत्रयो: । । 16711 । ।
ramayan::1752.verse_hindi: O Eminent ascetic such heaviest bow is brought here, O Highly accomplished sage show this to the two princes.
ramayan::1752.english_translation: O eminent sage, this finest bow has been brought here. O highly accomplished one, show it to these two princes.
ramayan::1752.translation_literal: तत् (that) / एतत् (this) / धनुषाम् (of bows) / श्रेष्ठम् (the finest) / आनीतम् (brought) / मुनिपुङ्गव (O best among sages) / दर्शय (show) / एतत् (this) / महाभाग (O greatly fortunate one) / अनयोः (of these two) / राजपुत्रयोः (princes)
ramayan::1752.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1752.essence: The challenge is revealed, and the princes are finally called forward.
ramayan::1752.simple_meaning: King Janaka asks Vishvamitra to show Rama and Lakshmana the great bow that no one else could handle.
ramayan::1752.simple_insight: The challenge is now in front of them; the room is waiting to see who can meet it.
ramayan::1752.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s court, the impossible bow has been brought out after many mighty beings failed to handle it. He turns to Vishvamitra and asks him to present it to Rama and Lakshmana, setting up the moment that will test their worth.
ramayan::1752.modern_relevance: A heavy task lands on the table and everyone goes quiet. The real question is no longer whether the task is hard, but who can meet it without flinching.
ramayan::1752.insight: It shifts attention from the object’s weight to the readiness of the one who will face it.

ramayan::1753.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रस्तु धर्मात्मा श्रुत्वा जनकभाषितम् । वत्स राम धनु: पश्य इति राघवमब्रवीत् । । 16712 । ।
ramayan::1753.verse_hindi: Having heard the words of Janaka, the righteous Viswamitra said: O Child O Descendant of Raghu look at this bow.
ramayan::1753.english_translation: Having heard Janaka's words, the righteous Viswamitra said: O child, O descendant of Raghu, look at this bow.
ramayan::1753.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Viswamitra) / तु (then) / धर्मात्मा (righteous-minded) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / जनकभाषितम् (Janaka's words) / वत्स (O child) / राम (Rama) / धनुः (bow) / पश्य (look) / इति (thus) / राघवम् (to the descendant of Raghu) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1753.speaker: Viswamitra
ramayan::1753.essence: The challenge is no longer abstract; Rama is being brought face to face with it.
ramayan::1753.simple_meaning: After hearing Janaka, Viswamitra tells Rama to look at the bow.
ramayan::1753.simple_insight: A great test is being placed before Rama, but the real challenge is still ahead.
ramayan::1753.detailed_meaning: Janaka has already set the impossible standard: whoever can handle this bow may win Sita. Viswamitra now turns to Rama and points him toward the bow, quietly moving the story from announcement to action.
ramayan::1753.modern_relevance: Someone finally says, “Here it is — the real challenge.” The room goes quiet before the first move.
ramayan::1753.insight: It prepares the moment of testing by directing attention to the object of proof.

ramayan::1754.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मर्षेर्वचनाद्रामो यत्र तिष्ठति तद्धनु: । मञ्जूषां तामपावृत्य दृष्ट्वा धनुरथाब्रवीत् । । 16713 । ।
ramayan::1754.verse_hindi: At the words of the great rishi Viswamitra, Rama opened the casket, beheld  the bow and said:
ramayan::1754.english_translation: At the words of the great rishi Viswamitra, Rama opened the casket, saw the bow, and said:
ramayan::1754.translation_literal: ब्रह्मर्षेः (of the great rishi) / वचनात् (at the words) / रामः (Rama) / यत्र (where) / तिष्ठति (is placed) / तत् (that) / धनुः (bow) / मञ्जूषाम् (the casket) / ताम् (that) / अपावृत्य (having opened) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / धनुः (the bow) / अथ (then) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1754.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1754.essence: Rama meets the challenge with calm readiness.
ramayan::1754.simple_meaning: Rama opens the casket, sees the bow, and prepares to speak. The real test comes in the next line, where he offers to handle it.
ramayan::1754.simple_insight: The moment before action can be as charged as the action itself.
ramayan::1754.detailed_meaning: Janaka has brought out Shiva's bow before the gathered princes. Vishwamitra tells Rama to look at it. Rama opens the casket and beholds the weapon, but this line only sets up the decisive response that follows: his calm willingness to try.
ramayan::1754.modern_relevance: You open the email, see the hard request, and pause before replying. The decision is still forming, but your whole future tone is already there.
ramayan::1754.insight: It marks the threshold between seeing a challenge and accepting it.

ramayan::1755.verse_sanskrit: इदं धनुर्वरं ब्रह्मन् संस्पृशामीह पाणिना । यत्नवांश्च भविष्यामि तोलने पूरणेऽपि वा । । 16714 । ।
ramayan::1755.verse_hindi: O Brahmarshi, shall I touch this great bow with my hands lift and string it.
ramayan::1755.english_translation: O Brahmarshi, shall I touch this great bow with my hands, and will I try to lift it and string it too?
ramayan::1755.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / धनुर्वरम् (great bow) / ब्रह्मन् (O Brahmarshi) / संस्पृशामि (shall I touch) / इह (here) / पाणिना (with hand) / यत्नवान् (making effort) / च (and) / भविष्यामि (shall I be) / तोलने (in lifting) / पूरणे (in stringing) / अपि (also) / वा (or)
ramayan::1755.speaker: Rama
ramayan::1755.essence: Real strength begins with a simple first touch.
ramayan::1755.simple_meaning: Rama asks permission to touch the great bow and says he will try to lift and string it.
ramayan::1755.simple_insight: Confidence can be quiet. You can begin before you know the outcome.
ramayan::1755.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Vishwamitra has brought Rama to the bow that no other prince could move. Rama does not boast. He simply asks to begin, ready to test himself in front of everyone.
ramayan::1755.modern_relevance: You stand in front of a task that looks too large to touch, let alone finish. The first honest move is not bravado — it is to begin with your hands on it.
ramayan::1755.insight: It teaches you to meet a daunting task with calm, direct effort instead of dramatic confidence.

ramayan::1756.verse_sanskrit: बाढमित्येव तं राजा मुनिश्च समभाषत । लीलया स धनुर्मध्ये जग्राह वचनान्मुने: । । 16715 ।
ramayan::1756.verse_hindi: The king as also the rishi said Be it so. At the words of the sage (Viswamitra), he (Rama) took hold of the bow by the its middle with ease:
ramayan::1756.english_translation: The king and the sage both said, “Be it so.” At the sage’s words, Rama took hold of the bow by its middle with ease.
ramayan::1756.translation_literal: बाढम् (be it so) / इति (thus) / एव (indeed) / तं (that) / राजा (the king) / मुनिः (the sage) / च (and) / समभाषत (spoke together) / लीलया (with ease, playfully) / सः (he) / धनुः (the bow) / मध्ये (in the middle) / जग्राह (took hold of) / वचनात् (at the word) / मुनेः (of the sage)
ramayan::1756.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1756.essence: Real readiness looks effortless before the decisive act begins.
ramayan::1756.simple_meaning: Rama calmly takes the bow exactly as instructed, showing no strain or hesitation.
ramayan::1756.simple_insight: True strength can look effortless when it is fully mastered.
ramayan::1756.detailed_meaning: In Vishwamitra’s presence, Rama has already asked permission to touch the great bow. The king and the sage agree. Rama then grips the bow at its center without effort, a quiet moment that prepares the way for the far greater feat to come.
ramayan::1756.modern_relevance: You finally get the difficult tool in your hands after weeks of waiting. No drama, no proving — just the calm touch of someone who is ready.
ramayan::1756.insight: It shows mastery through composure, not strain.

ramayan::1757.verse_sanskrit: पश्यतां नृपसहस्राणां बहूनां रघुनन्दन: । आरोपयत्स धर्मात्मा सलीलमिव तद्धनु: । । 16716 । ।
ramayan::1757.verse_hindi: Virtuous Rama, the delight of the Raghus, in the presence of several thousands of men fixed the string to the bow and drew it as though with ease.
ramayan::1757.english_translation: Virtuous Rama, the delight of the Raghus, in the presence of several thousands of men fixed the string to the bow and drew it as though with ease.
ramayan::1757.translation_literal: पश्यतां (while watching) / नृपसहस्राणां (of thousands of kings) / बहूनां (of many) / रघुनन्दनः (the delight of the Raghu line) / आरोपयत् (placed on) / सः (he) / धर्मात्मा (righteous one) / सलीलम् (playfully, with ease) / इव (as if) / तत् (that) / धनुः (bow)
ramayan::1757.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1757.essence: Real mastery looks effortless to everyone else.
ramayan::1757.simple_meaning: Rama strung the great bow easily, right in front of thousands of watching kings.
ramayan::1757.simple_insight: True strength is calm enough to look effortless.
ramayan::1757.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra’s command, Rama has taken up Janaka’s impossible bow in the crowded court. Thousands of kings are watching for failure, but he strings it without strain. The moment proves he is the one chosen for Sita’s hand.
ramayan::1757.modern_relevance: You step onto a stage, a courtroom, or a boardroom with everyone measuring you. The task looks impossible until you do it so cleanly that the room goes silent.
ramayan::1757.insight: It shows mastery as quiet control, not visible struggle.

ramayan::1758.verse_sanskrit: आरोपयित्वा धर्मात्मा पूरयामास तद्धनु: । तद्बभञ्ज धनुर्मध्ये नरश्रेष्ठो महायशा: । । 16717 । ।
ramayan::1758.verse_hindi: Rama, the best among men, righteous and famous lifted the bow. Stringing it with a twang he drew it and broke it into two in the middle.
ramayan::1758.english_translation: Rama, the best among men, righteous and famous lifted the bow. Stringing it with a twang he drew it and broke it into two in the middle.
ramayan::1758.translation_literal: आरोपयित्वा (having strung up) / धर्मात्मा (the righteous one) / पूरयामास (he filled, tightened) / तत् (that) / धनुः (bow) / तत् (that) / बभञ्ज (broke) / धनुः (bow) / मध्ये (in the middle) / नरश्रेष्ठः (best among men) / महायशाः (greatly famous one)
ramayan::1758.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1758.essence: A single clean act can end a lifetime of doubt.
ramayan::1758.simple_meaning: Rama strings the bow, pulls it tight, and breaks it cleanly in the middle.
ramayan::1758.simple_insight: Some acts settle a whole contest in a single motion.
ramayan::1758.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, thousands watch as Rama takes up Shiva's bow. Viswamitra has brought him here to prove his worth and win Sita. The bow does not hold; Rama breaks it in the center, and the room changes forever.
ramayan::1758.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to prove yourself in front of everyone. One steady action does what hours of arguing never could.
ramayan::1758.insight: It shifts the focus from talk and display to decisive action under pressure.

ramayan::1759.verse_sanskrit: तस्य शब्दो महानासीत् निर्घातसमनिस्वन: । भूमिकम्पश्च सुमहान् पर्वतस्येव दीर्यत: । । 16718 । ।
ramayan::1759.verse_hindi: It generated a loud sound like the clap of thunder, like the trembling of the earth and the splitting of a mountain.
ramayan::1759.english_translation: It made a great sound, like thunder, and the earth shook as if a mountain were splitting.
ramayan::1759.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / शब्दः (sound) / महान् (great) / आसीत् (was) / निर्घात-समनिस्वनः (with a thunder-like roar) / भूमिकम्पः (earth-shaking) / च (and) / सुमहान् (very great) / पर्वतस्य (of a mountain) / इव (like) / दीर्यतः (splitting)
ramayan::1759.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1759.essence: His single act shook the whole gathering.
ramayan::1759.simple_meaning: The bow breaks with a thunderous crash, and the ground shakes like a mountain splitting apart.
ramayan::1759.simple_insight: The moment is so forceful that everyone feels it in their body before they understand it.
ramayan::1759.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Rama has just strung and broken Shiva's bow. The victory is not quiet; it lands like thunder. This verse focuses on the physical shock of that impossible act, which stuns everyone around him.
ramayan::1759.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after your decision lands. The impact is felt before anyone finds words, and everyone knows something irreversible has just happened.
ramayan::1759.insight: It shifts the mind from ceremony to consequence: real power changes the whole atmosphere.

ramayan::1760.verse_sanskrit: निपेतुश्च नरा स्सर्वे तेन शब्देन मोहिता: । वर्जयित्वा मुनिवरं राजानं तौ च राघवौ । । 16719 । ।
ramayan::1760.verse_hindi: On hearing the sound, except Janaka, Viswamitra and the two raghavas (Rama and Lakshmana) the rest of the people around fell down and fainted.
ramayan::1760.english_translation: On hearing the sound, everyone except Janaka, Vishvamitra, and the two Raghavas fell down, stunned.
ramayan::1760.translation_literal: निपेतुः (fell down) / च (and) / नरा: (men) / सर्वे (all) / तेन (by that) / शब्देन (by sound) / मोहिता: (bewildered, stunned) / वर्जयित्वा (excepting) / मुनिवरम् (the best of sages) / राजानम् (the king) / तौ (those two) / च (and) / राघवौ (the two Raghavas)
ramayan::1760.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1760.essence: The bow’s sound stunned everyone in the hall.
ramayan::1760.simple_meaning: The bow’s sound was so overwhelming that everyone nearby lost consciousness, except Janaka, Vishvamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana.
ramayan::1760.simple_insight: Some moments are so powerful they stop a crowd in its tracks.
ramayan::1760.detailed_meaning: Rama has just broken Shiva’s bow in Janaka’s court. The impact is so immense that the assembly collapses in shock, leaving only Janaka, Vishvamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana standing. This is a scene-setting reaction, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::1760.insight: It marks the physical shock that follows Rama’s feat, setting up the court’s next response.

ramayan::1761.verse_sanskrit: प्रत्याश्वस्ते जने तस्मिन्राजा विगतसाध्वस: । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो मुनिपुङ्गवम् । । 16720 । ।
ramayan::1761.verse_hindi: When the people recovered the king skilful in the use  of words addressed the eminent ascetic  without apprehension with folded palms in the following words:
ramayan::1761.english_translation: When the people recovered, the king, fearless and skilled in speech, addressed the great ascetic with folded hands.
ramayan::1761.translation_literal: प्रत्याश्वस्ते (having recovered) / जने (the people) / तस्मिन् (in that) / राजा (king) / विगतसाध्वसः (free from fear) / उवाच (said) / प्राञ्जलिः (with folded palms) / वाक्यं (speech) / वाक्यज्ञः (skilled in words) / मुनिपुङ्गवम् (to the foremost ascetic)
ramayan::1761.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1761.essence: Calm speech can hold a shaken room together.
ramayan::1761.simple_meaning: After the crowd calms down, King Janaka speaks respectfully to Vishwamitra with folded hands.
ramayan::1761.simple_insight: Composure and respect matter even after a moment of shock.
ramayan::1761.detailed_meaning: The crowd has just been shaken by a tremendous sound and then steadied. Janaka, unlike the others, remains composed. With Rama and Lakshmana present beside Vishwamitra, he turns to the sage and begins a formal response to what has just happened.
ramayan::1761.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet after a sudden announcement, and everyone is still catching their breath. You wait, gather yourself, and speak with care instead of reacting from the shock.
ramayan::1761.insight: It shows how to answer a startling moment with dignity rather than panic.

ramayan::1762.verse_sanskrit: भगवन् दृष्टवीर्यो मे रामो दशरथात्मज: । अत्यद्भुतमचिन्त्यं च न तर्कितमिदं मया । । 16721 । ।
ramayan::1762.verse_hindi: O Worshipful one I have witnessed the prowess of Rama, son of Dasaratha. I had not
ramayan::1762.english_translation: O worshipful one, I have witnessed the prowess of Rama, son of Dasaratha. I had not imagined such an astonishing and unthinkable feat.
ramayan::1762.translation_literal: भगवन् (O worshipful one) / दृष्टवीर्यः (seen his prowess) / मे (by me) / रामः (Rama) / दशरथात्मजः (son of Dasaratha) / अत्यद्भुतम् (most astonishing) / अचिन्त्यम् (unthinkable) / च (and) / न (not) / तर्कितम् (imagined) / इदम् (this) / मया (by me)
ramayan::1762.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1762.essence: Rama's strength makes even a wise king admit he had underestimated reality.
ramayan::1762.simple_meaning: Janaka says Rama's strength has exceeded anything he could have imagined. What he has seen is astonishing and beyond ordinary reasoning.
ramayan::1762.simple_insight: Real greatness can surprise you into humility.
ramayan::1762.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just watched Rama perform the feat that decides Sita's marriage. The king, now steady again, speaks to Vishwamitra with wonder: Rama's strength is not merely impressive, but beyond what he could have predicted.
ramayan::1762.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a room and assume you understand their limits. Then they handle the hardest thing with quiet ease, and your whole estimate of them changes.
ramayan::1762.insight: It shifts the mind from confident judgment to humbled recognition when reality exceeds expectation.

ramayan::1763.verse_sanskrit: जनकानां कुले कीर्तिमाहरिष्यति मे सुता । सीता भर्तारमासाद्य रामं दशरथात्मजम् । । 16722 । ।
ramayan::1763.verse_hindi: By receiving Rama, son of Dasaratha, as her husband, my daughter Sita will bring glory to my dynasty.
ramayan::1763.english_translation: By receiving Rama, son of Dasaratha, as her husband, my daughter Sita will bring glory to my dynasty.
ramayan::1763.translation_literal: जनकानां (of Janaka's) / कुले (in the lineage) / कीर्तिम् (fame, glory) / आहरिष्यति (will bring) / मे (my) / सुता (daughter) / सीता (Sita) / भर्तारम् (as husband) / आसाद्य (having obtained, receiving) / रामम् (Rama) / दशरथात्मजम् (son of Dasaratha)
ramayan::1763.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1763.essence: A true match elevates both people and the family behind them.
ramayan::1763.simple_meaning: Janaka says that Sita marrying Rama will bring honor to his family line.
ramayan::1763.simple_insight: A marriage can feel larger than two people when it reflects shared worth and character.
ramayan::1763.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just seen Rama's extraordinary strength and steadiness. Speaking to Vishvamitra, he says that giving Sita to Rama will not only fulfill the marriage contest, but also bring lasting honor to his lineage.
ramayan::1763.modern_relevance: You meet someone who makes your family relax, not because they are impressive, but because they are solid. Janaka recognizes that kind of worth instantly.
ramayan::1763.insight: It shifts attention from attraction to the deeper honor a relationship can create.

ramayan::1764.verse_sanskrit: मम सत्या प्रतिज्ञा च वीर्यशुल्केति कौशिक । सीता प्राणैर्बहुमता देया रामाय मे सुता । । 16723 । ।
ramayan::1764.verse_hindi: O Son of Kausika I announce Sita to be the Reward of prowess. My vow has come true. She is more valuable than my life and fit to be given to Rama.
ramayan::1764.english_translation: O Son of Kausika, I declare Sita to be the reward of prowess. My vow has come true. She is dearer to me than life itself and worthy of being given to Rama, my daughter.
ramayan::1764.translation_literal: मम (my) / सत्या (true) / प्रतिज्ञा (vow) / च (and) / वीर्यशुल्का (the prize for prowess) / इति (thus) / कौशिक (O Kausika) / सीता (Sita) / प्राणैः (with life) / बहुमता (greatly valued) / देया (to be given) / रामाय (to Rama) / मे (my) / सुता (daughter)
ramayan::1764.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1764.essence: A vow becomes real only when keeping it costs you something.
ramayan::1764.simple_meaning: Janaka says his vow has been fulfilled: Sita is the prize for true valor, dearer than his own life, and she should be given to Rama.
ramayan::1764.simple_insight: There is dignity in a promise kept at personal cost.
ramayan::1764.detailed_meaning: Janaka, speaking to Vishwamitra, has just seen Rama's strength and heard Sita praised as worthy of him. Now he confirms the vow he made before the contest: Sita will be given to Rama, because the promise, her worth, and the marriage all align.
ramayan::1764.modern_relevance: You made a promise when it felt ceremonial. Then life made it expensive. This verse remembers the moment when keeping your word becomes more important than protecting your comfort.
ramayan::1764.insight: It shifts attention from desire to obligation fulfilled, showing that integrity is measured by costly follow-through.

ramayan::1765.verse_sanskrit: भवतोऽनुमते ब्रह्मन् शीघ्रं गच्छन्तु मन्त्रिण: । मम कौशिक भद्रं ते अयोध्यां त्वरिता रथै: । । 16724 । ।
ramayan::1765.verse_hindi: O Brahmarshi Kausika, be blessed With your consent my ministers will take the chariots to Ayodhya immediately.
ramayan::1765.english_translation: O Brahmarshi Kausika, be blessed. With your consent, my ministers will immediately take the chariots to Ayodhya.
ramayan::1765.translation_literal: भवतः (your) / अनुमते (with approval) / ब्रह्मन् (O brahmarshi) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / गच्छन्तु (let them go) / मन्त्रिणः (ministers) / मम (my) / कौशिक (O Kausika) / भद्रम् (well-being) / ते (to you) / अयोध्याम् (to Ayodhya) / त्वरिताः (hastily) / रथैः (with chariots)
ramayan::1765.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1765.essence: A vow becomes real only when it starts moving.
ramayan::1765.simple_meaning: Janaka asks Vishvamitra's approval and says his ministers should quickly go to Ayodhya with chariots.
ramayan::1765.simple_insight: A decision becomes real only when it turns into action.
ramayan::1765.detailed_meaning: Janaka has already declared Sita's marriage to Rama. Now he turns to Vishvamitra for approval and immediately orders his ministers to travel to Ayodhya. The verse is a practical bridge between vow and announcement.
ramayan::1765.modern_relevance: You finally decide, and the next step is logistics: the call, the message, the booking, the move. A real commitment leaves the room of thought and enters motion.
ramayan::1765.insight: It shifts the mind from declaration to execution.

ramayan::1766.verse_sanskrit: राजानं प्रश्रितैर्वाक्यैरानयन्तु पुरं मम । प्रदानं वीर्यशुल्काया: कथयन्तु च सर्वश: । । 16725 । ।
ramayan::1766.verse_hindi: That Sita, the reward of prowess is to be given to Rama be reventially communicated in detail to king Dasaratha and he may be conveyed here.
ramayan::1766.english_translation: Let King Dasharatha be respectfully brought to this city. Tell him everything about the giving of the maiden won by prowess.
ramayan::1766.translation_literal: राजानम् (the king) / प्रश्रितैः (with respectful) / वाक्यैः (words) / आनयन्तु (let them bring) / पुरम् (to the city) / मम (my) / प्रदानम् (the giving) / वीर्यशुल्काया: (of the maiden won by prowess) / कथयन्तु (let them tell) / च (and) / सर्वश: (in full)
ramayan::1766.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1766.essence: Honor the decision by bringing the other side in respectfully.
ramayan::1766.simple_meaning: Dasharatha should be brought to the city, and the full account of Sita's marriage should be told to him with respect.
ramayan::1766.simple_insight: Big public commitments need clear, respectful communication.
ramayan::1766.detailed_meaning: After Janaka declares Sita as the prize of Rama's strength, he immediately shifts to the practical next step: Dasharatha must be invited and informed properly. The marriage is no longer a contest; it is becoming an alliance that must be carried out with honor.
ramayan::1766.modern_relevance: You’ve made a major decision in front of everyone, and now the message has to travel cleanly. The next step is not drama — it is careful, respectful follow-through.
ramayan::1766.insight: It shifts attention from celebration to responsible completion and formal communication.

ramayan::1767.verse_sanskrit: मुनिगुप्तौ च काकुत्स्थौ कथयन्तु नृपाय वै । प्रीयमाणं तु राजानमानयन्तु सुशीघ्रगा: । । 16726 । ।
ramayan::1767.verse_hindi: The welfare of the descendant of Kausika (Rama and Lakshmana) under the protection of sage (Viswamitra) be reported to the king. The king who will be happy to hear this
ramayan::1767.english_translation: Report to the king that the two Kakutsthas are safe under the protection of the sage. Let the king be brought back quickly, pleased by the news.
ramayan::1767.translation_literal: मुनिगुप्तौ (protected by the sage) / च (and) / काकुत्स्थौ (the two Kakutsthas) / कथयन्तु (let [them] tell) / नृपाय (to the king) / वै (indeed) / प्रीयमाणं (becoming pleased) / तु (but/indeed) / राजानम् (the king) / आनयन्तु (let [them] bring) / सुशीघ्रगा: (swift-moving ones)
ramayan::1767.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1767.essence: Safety, once confirmed, becomes the news that matters most.
ramayan::1767.simple_meaning: The messengers are told to inform the king that Rama and Lakshmana are safe with Viswamitra, and to return quickly with the good news.
ramayan::1767.simple_insight: Sometimes the first relief is simply hearing that your loved ones are safe.
ramayan::1767.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has secured Rama and Lakshmana, and the focus shifts to Ayodhya. The messengers are instructed to report their safety to King Dasharatha and hurry back, because the king’s heart is waiting on that news.
ramayan::1767.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone after a family member travels alone. One message saying they reached safely changes the whole day.
ramayan::1767.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the human need for reassurance and safe return.

ramayan::1768.verse_sanskrit: कौशिकश्च तथेत्याह राजा चाभाष्य मन्त्रिण: । । 16727 । । अयोध्यां प्रेषयामास धर्मात्मा कृतशासनान् । यथावृत्तं समाख्यातुमानेतुं च नृपं तदा । । 16728 । ।
ramayan::1768.verse_hindi: The son of Kausika (Viswamitra) also said, So be it. The virtuous king, having consulted his ministers, despatched counsellors to Ayodhya to communicate to king Dasaratha all that had taken place and bring him (to Mithila).
ramayan::1768.english_translation: Kausika also said, “So be it.” Then the virtuous king consulted his ministers and sent trusted envoys to Ayodhya to report everything that had happened and bring King Dasharatha there.
ramayan::1768.translation_literal: कौशिकः (Kausika) / च (and) / तथा (so) / इति (thus) / आह (said) / राजा (the king) / च (and) / आभाष्य (having consulted) / मन्त्रिणः (the ministers) / अयोध्याम् (to Ayodhya) / प्रेषयामास (sent) / धर्मात्मा (the virtuous one) / कृतशासनान् (trusted envoys) / यथावृत्तम् (what had happened) / समाख्यातुम् (to report) / आनेतुम् (to bring) / च (and) / नृपम् (the king) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1768.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1768.essence: After the decision, the real work is carrying it home with dignity.
ramayan::1768.simple_meaning: Janaka agrees, consults his ministers, and sends messengers to Ayodhya to tell Dasharatha what happened and invite him there.
ramayan::1768.simple_insight: Big events still move through careful words, trusted people, and clear reporting.
ramayan::1768.detailed_meaning: At Mithila, the marriage contest has been decided and the court is turning from challenge to ceremony. Janaka accepts the outcome, consults his ministers, and sends reliable envoys to Ayodhya so Dasharatha can be informed and brought to witness what has taken place.
ramayan::1768.modern_relevance: A major decision is made in a meeting room, and now someone has to call the other side, explain the outcome clearly, and keep the process dignified.
ramayan::1768.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic victory to orderly follow-through and respectful communication.

ramayan::1769.verse_sanskrit: जनकेन समादिष्टा दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहना: । त्रिरात्रमुषिता मार्गे तेऽयोध्यां प्राविशन् पुरीम् । । 1681 । ।
ramayan::1769.verse_hindi: Commanded by Janaka the messengers travelled for three days, rested for three nights on the way and entered the city of Ayodhya along with their horses tired.
ramayan::1769.english_translation: Commanded by Janaka, the messengers travelled for three days, rested for three nights on the way, and entered the city of Ayodhya with their horses exhausted.
ramayan::1769.translation_literal: जनकेन (by Janaka) / समादिष्टा (instructed) / दूताः (messengers) / ते (they) / क्लान्तवाहनाः (with tired horses) / त्रिरात्रम् (for three nights) / उषिताः (having stayed) / मार्गे (on the road) / ते (they) / अयोध्याम् (to Ayodhya) / प्राविशन् (entered) / पुरीम् (the city)
ramayan::1769.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1769.essence: Important news still has to travel the hard way.
ramayan::1769.simple_meaning: Janaka's messengers took three days to reach Ayodhya because the journey was long and their horses were exhausted.
ramayan::1769.simple_insight: Some messages matter enough to cross distance, delay, and fatigue.
ramayan::1769.detailed_meaning: Janaka has sent messengers back to Ayodhya after hearing that Rama and Lakshmana are safe with Vishvamitra. They travel hard for three days and nights, worn out but determined, because the news must reach Dasharatha quickly.
ramayan::1769.modern_relevance: You finally get the update out after a long, tiring journey across trains, calls, and waiting rooms. The message still matters enough to keep going.
ramayan::1769.insight: It highlights the physical cost of carrying urgent news and the persistence needed to deliver it.

ramayan::1770.verse_sanskrit: राज्ञो भवनमासाद्य द्वारस्थानिदमब्रुवन् । शीघ्रं निवेद्यतां राज्ञे दूतान्नो जनकस्य च । । 1682 । ।
ramayan::1770.verse_hindi: Reaching the kings palace the messengers said to the doorkeepers, Let king
ramayan::1770.english_translation: Reaching the king's palace, the messengers said to the doorkeepers, 'Quickly inform the king about our arrival and about Janaka's messengers.'
ramayan::1770.translation_literal: राज्ञः (of the king) / भवनम् (palace) / आसाद्य (having reached) / द्वारस्थान् (to the doorkeepers) / इदम् (this) / अब्रुवन् (they said) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / निवेद्यताम् (let it be announced) / राज्ञे (to the king) / दूतान् (messengers) / नः (our) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / च (and)
ramayan::1770.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1770.essence: The message has arrived; the court has not heard it yet.
ramayan::1770.simple_meaning: The messengers arrive at the palace and ask the doorkeepers to announce them to the king at once.
ramayan::1770.simple_insight: Some moments only move the story forward. This is one of them.
ramayan::1770.detailed_meaning: Janaka's messengers, after days on the road, reach Ayodhya's palace and speak to the gatekeepers. They ask for immediate announcement to the king, preparing the way for the news that will change the royal household.
ramayan::1770.modern_relevance: You finally reach the front desk after a long trip, and the next few minutes decide everything. This is the breath before the message lands.
ramayan::1770.insight: It keeps attention on the arrival of news, not on the news itself.

ramayan::1771.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्ता द्वारपालास्ते राघवाय न्यवेदयन् । ते राजवचनाद्दूता राजवेश्मप्रवेशिता: । ददृशुर्देवसङ्काशं वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम् । । 1683 । ।
ramayan::1771.verse_hindi: Having heard their words, the doorkeepers informed the descendant of Raghu (king Dasaratha). Thereafter, with the the kings permission, the messengers entered the royal palace  and beheld the aged king Dasaratha who shone like a god.
ramayan::1771.english_translation: Having heard their words, the doorkeepers informed the descendant of Raghu. Then, with the king's permission, the messengers entered the royal palace and beheld the aged king Dasaratha, who shone like a god.
ramayan::1771.translation_literal: इत्युक्ता (having been thus spoken to) / द्वारपालाः (the doorkeepers) / ते (they) / राघवाय (to the descendant of Raghu) / न्यवेदयन् (informed) / ते (they) / राजवचनात् (by the king's command) / दूताः (the messengers) / राजवेश्मप्रवेशिताः (made to enter the royal palace) / ददृशुः (they saw) / देवसङ्काशम् (god-like) / वृद्धम् (aged) / दशरथम् (Dasaratha) / नृपम् (the king)
ramayan::1771.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1771.essence: The message is important because the king himself is finally in view.
ramayan::1771.simple_meaning: The messengers are admitted into the palace and see the aged king Dasaratha.
ramayan::1771.simple_insight: Sometimes the real weight of a meeting is in the silence before the first words.
ramayan::1771.detailed_meaning: Janaka's messengers have finally reached Ayodhya and asked to see the king. The doorkeepers report them, permission is granted, and they enter the royal chamber. Their first sight is Dasaratha, old and radiant, just before they speak their message.
ramayan::1771.modern_relevance: You wait outside a closed office, rehearsing what you came to say. Then the door opens, and the first look tells you this conversation will matter.
ramayan::1771.insight: It sets the scene for the message, showing that the meeting begins with formal access and visible royal presence.

ramayan::1772.verse_sanskrit: बद्धाञ्जलिपुटा स्सर्वे दूता विगतसाध्वसा: । राजानं प्रयता वाक्यमब्रुवन्मधुराक्षरम् । । 1684 । ।
ramayan::1772.verse_hindi: All the messengers, hands folded free from apprehensions, reverentially addressed the king in sweet words.
ramayan::1772.english_translation: All the messengers, hands folded, free from fear, reverentially addressed the king in sweet words.
ramayan::1772.translation_literal: बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः (with folded hands) / सर्वे (all) / दूताः (messengers) / विगतसाध्वसाः (free from fear) / राजानम् (to the king) / प्रयताः (reverently) / वाक्यम् (words) / अब्रुवन् (spoke) / मधुराक्षरम् (with sweet words)
ramayan::1772.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1772.essence: Respectful speech lowers fear and makes hard news receivable.
ramayan::1772.simple_meaning: The messengers speak respectfully to the king, calm and unafraid, using gentle words.
ramayan::1772.simple_insight: Respect can steady a difficult conversation before it even begins.
ramayan::1772.detailed_meaning: The envoys from Mithila have been admitted into Dasharatha’s palace. Standing before the king, they fold their hands, lose their fear, and begin speaking carefully. This is the formal opening of Janaka’s message.
ramayan::1772.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where the stakes are high, but your tone decides the shape of everything that follows.
ramayan::1772.insight: It shows how humility and composure can open a tense exchange.

ramayan::1773.verse_sanskrit: मैथिलो जनको राजा साग्निहोत्रपुरस्कृतम् । कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव सोपाध्यायपुरोहितम् । । 1685 । । मुहुर्मुहुर्मधुरया स्नेहसंयुक्तया गिरा । जनकस्त्वां महाराज पृच्छते सपुरस्सरम् । । 1686 । ।
ramayan::1773.verse_hindi: O Great monarch Mithilas lord, king Janaka, with the sacred fire in front again and again enquires about your health and the spiritual wellbeing of your preceptors, priests and attendants in words filled with sweetness and affection.
ramayan::1773.english_translation: O great monarch, Janaka, king of Mithila, with the sacred fire before him, repeatedly asks about your welfare and the wellbeing of your teachers, priests, and attendants in sweet, affectionate words.
ramayan::1773.translation_literal: मैथिलः (of Mithila) / जनकः (Janaka) / राजा (king) / साग्निहोत्रपुरस्कृतम् (with the sacred fire in front) / कुशलम् (welfare) / च (and) / अव्ययम् (undiminished) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सोपाध्यायपुरोहितम् (with teachers and priests) / मुहुर्मुहुः (again and again) / मधुरया (with sweet) / स्नेहसंयुक्तया (joined with affection) / गिरा (with speech) / जनकः (Janaka) / त्वाम् (you) / महाराज (great monarch) / पृच्छते (asks) / सपुरस्सरम् (with due respect)
ramayan::1773.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1773.essence: Respectful speech can carry real affection without losing dignity.
ramayan::1773.simple_meaning: Janaka sends respectful greetings and asks after Dasharatha’s health, along with the wellbeing of his teachers, priests, and attendants.
ramayan::1773.simple_insight: Even formal messages can carry real warmth when respect is sincere.
ramayan::1773.detailed_meaning: Messengers stand before Dasharatha in Ayodhya and relay Janaka’s courteous inquiry. The line is part of a larger diplomatic exchange between two royal houses, not a teaching in itself, but a polished moment of friendship and protocol.
ramayan::1773.modern_relevance: A message arrives from someone you have not spoken to in months, and it begins with genuine concern before business. That small kindness changes the whole tone of the conversation.
ramayan::1773.insight: It reminds you that courtesy is strongest when it includes care for others, not just status.

ramayan::1774.verse_sanskrit: पृष्ट्वा कुशलमव्यग्रं वैदेहो मिथिलाधिप: । कौशिकानुमते वाक्यं भवन्तमिदमब्रवीत् । । 1687 । ।
ramayan::1774.verse_hindi: Janaka, the king of Mithila with the enquiry about your welfare, with the permission of the son of Kausika (Viswamitra) sends you this message:
ramayan::1774.english_translation: Janaka, the king of Mithila, after inquiring about your welfare, with the permission of the son of Kausika, sends you this message:
ramayan::1774.translation_literal: पृष्ट्वा (having asked) / कुशलम् (welfare) / अव्यग्रम् (without anxiety) / वैदेहः (the king of Videha) / मिथिलाधिपः (lord of Mithila) / कौशिकानुमते (with the permission of Kausika's son) / वाक्यम् (message) / भवन्तम् (you) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1774.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1774.essence: A courteous message opens the way for a decisive challenge.
ramayan::1774.simple_meaning: Janaka sends a respectful message after asking about your well-being, and he speaks with Vishvamitra's approval.
ramayan::1774.simple_insight: Respectful words can carry the weight of a serious turning point.
ramayan::1774.detailed_meaning: Janaka’s messengers are still speaking in the court scene. They have greeted the king politely and now deliver Janaka’s formal reply, approved by Vishvamitra. The verse mainly prepares the ground for the bow-swayamvara announcement that follows.
ramayan::1774.modern_relevance: You get a message that sounds polite, but you can feel a major decision behind it. The real news is coming next.
ramayan::1774.insight: It sets up the formal announcement that will change the course of the gathering.

ramayan::1775.verse_sanskrit: पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञा विदिता वीर्यशुल्का ममात्मजा । राजानश्च कृतामर्षानिर्वीर्या विमुखीकृता: । । 1688 । ।
ramayan::1775.verse_hindi: O King It is wellknown that formerly I had vowed to give my daughter to a groom as a reward for prowess. Disappointed when proved powerless, the kings became indignant and opposed me.
ramayan::1775.english_translation: O king, it is well known that I once vowed to give my daughter as the prize for valor. The kings were angered and turned away when they found themselves powerless.
ramayan::1775.translation_literal: पूर्वं (formerly) / प्रतिज्ञा (vow) / विदिता (known) / वीर्यशुल्का (as the price for valor) / ममात्मजा (my daughter) / राजानश्च (and the kings) / कृतामर्षान् (made angry) / निर्वीर्या (powerless) / विमुखीकृताः (turned away)
ramayan::1775.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1775.essence: A promise made to valor exposes who is truly worthy.
ramayan::1775.simple_meaning: Janaka reminds everyone that his daughter was promised to whoever proved his worth, and the proud kings withdrew when they could not meet the challenge.
ramayan::1775.simple_insight: Real honor survives only when it is tested.
ramayan::1775.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janaka speaks before Viswamitra and the gathered kings. He recalls the vow that Sita would marry only a man of true valor, and how other rulers recoiled when they failed the test. This sets up Rama's arrival as the one who can meet that standard.
ramayan::1775.modern_relevance: You set a high standard, and people call it unfair until they have to meet it. The moment pressure exposes weakness, pride often turns into resentment.
ramayan::1775.insight: It shifts the mind from social status to proven worth.

ramayan::1776.verse_sanskrit: सेयं मम सुता राजन् विश्वामित्रपुरस्सरै: । यदृच्छयागतैर्वीरैर्निर्जिता तव पुत्रकै: । । 1689 । ।
ramayan::1776.verse_hindi: O King that this daughter of mine has been won by your heroic son Rama  who has come here casually led by Viswamitra.
ramayan::1776.english_translation: O King, this daughter of mine has been won by your heroic son Rama, who came here by chance led by Vishvamitra.
ramayan::1776.translation_literal: सा (this) / इयम् (this) / मम (my) / सुता (daughter) / राजन् (O king) / विश्वामित्रपुरस्सरैः (led by Vishvamitra) / यदृच्छया (by chance) / आगतैः (having come) / वीरैः (by the heroic one) / निर्जिता (won) / तव (your) / पुत्रकैः (by your son)
ramayan::1776.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1776.essence: The contest ends in a marriage that no one could force.
ramayan::1776.simple_meaning: Janaka tells Dasharatha that Sita has been won by Rama, who arrived with Vishvamitra.
ramayan::1776.simple_insight: A marriage can begin as a contest and end as a joining of destinies.
ramayan::1776.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janaka addresses Dasharatha after the bow challenge. He acknowledges that Sita has been won by Rama, the heroic son who arrived with Vishvamitra. This line is part of Janaka's formal announcement, not the deeper teaching of the scene.
ramayan::1776.modern_relevance: You watch a life-changing moment arrive through what looked like a random invitation. Later you realise it was the doorway that changed everything.
ramayan::1776.insight: It marks the turning point where effort, arrival, and recognition meet in public.

ramayan::1777.verse_sanskrit: तच्च राजन् धनुर्दिव्यं मध्ये भग्नं महात्मना । रामेण हि महाराज महत्यां जनसंसदि । । 16810 । ।
ramayan::1777.verse_hindi: O Great king, Dasaratha the divine bow with its limitless glory was broken in the middle by the great self Rama in the assembly of people.
ramayan::1777.english_translation: O Great king, the divine bow of immense glory was broken in the middle by the great-souled Rama in the public assembly.
ramayan::1777.translation_literal: तत् (that) / च (and) / राजन् (O king) / धनुः (bow) / दिव्यम् (divine) / मध्ये (in the middle) / भग्नम् (broken) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one) / रामेण (by Rama) / हि (indeed) / महाराज (O great king) / महत्याम् (in the great) / जनसंसदि (assembly of people)
ramayan::1777.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1777.essence: Rama's strength is proven by action, not assertion.
ramayan::1777.simple_meaning: Janaka tells Dasaratha that Rama broke the great divine bow in front of everyone.
ramayan::1777.simple_insight: Public proof matters: the right person does not need to boast; the act itself speaks.
ramayan::1777.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, the contest for Sita has become a public test of worth. Rama steps forward and breaks the impossible bow in front of the assembled kings. Janaka now explains the feat to Dasaratha as the decisive proof that Rama has won Sita.
ramayan::1777.modern_relevance: You finally do the thing everyone said could not be done, and the room goes quiet. No speech is needed after that.
ramayan::1777.insight: It shifts attention from claims and status to visible proof of capability.

ramayan::1778.verse_sanskrit: अस्मै देया मया सीता वीर्यशुल्का महात्मने । प्रतिज्ञां कर्तुमिच्छामि तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि । । 16811 । ।
ramayan::1778.verse_hindi: Sita is fit to be given in marriage to this eminent Rama as a reward for his prowess. I request you to give your consent to fulfil my vow.
ramayan::1778.english_translation: Sita is fit to be given in marriage to this eminent Rama as a reward for his prowess. I request you to give your consent to fulfil my vow.
ramayan::1778.translation_literal: अस्मै (to this one) / देया (to be given) / मया (by me) / सीता (Sita) / वीर्यशुल्का (with prowess as the price) / महात्मने (to the great-souled one) / प्रतिज्ञां (vow) / कर्तुम् (to make) / इच्छामि (I wish) / तत् (that) / अनुज्ञातुम् (to permit) / अर्हसि (you are fit)
ramayan::1778.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1778.essence: Strength has already answered; now the promise must follow.
ramayan::1778.simple_meaning: Janaka says Sita should be given to Rama because Rama has proven his worth, and he asks Dasharatha to allow the marriage vow to be completed.
ramayan::1778.simple_insight: A rightful promise becomes sacred once courage has earned it.
ramayan::1778.detailed_meaning: After Rama breaks Shiva's bow in Janaka's court, the king turns to Dasharatha. He says Sita belongs with the hero who proved his strength, and asks permission to complete the promise he has already made before the assembled court.
ramayan::1778.modern_relevance: A parent watches someone show up with real character, not just good words. The decision is no longer about preference or pride — it is about honoring what has already been proven.
ramayan::1778.insight: It shifts attention from personal desire to the obligation created by public commitment and proven merit.

ramayan::1779.verse_sanskrit: सोपाध्यायो महाराज पुरोहितपुरस्सर: । शीघ्रमागच्छ भद्रं ते द्रष्टुमर्हसि राघवौ । । 16812 । ।
ramayan::1779.verse_hindi: O Mighty king be blessed. Come here soon with your preceptors and priest. You ought to be reumitd with Rama amd Lakshmana.
ramayan::1779.english_translation: O mighty king, be blessed. Come here quickly with your teachers and priest. You should be reunited with Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayan::1779.translation_literal: सोपाध्यायः (with teachers) / महाराज (great king) / पुरोहित-पुरस्सरः (with the priest at the front) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / आगच्छ (come) / भद्रम् ते (good fortune to you) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अर्हसि (you ought) / राघवौ (the two Raghus, Rama and Lakshmana)
ramayan::1779.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1779.essence: The moment has arrived to come, witness, and proceed.
ramayan::1779.simple_meaning: The king is invited to come at once with his teachers and priest so he can meet Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayan::1779.simple_insight: Sometimes the next right step is simple: gather the right people and go see what must be seen.
ramayan::1779.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, the bow has been broken and the marriage proposal for Sita is taking shape. This line is part of the formal invitation to Dasaratha: come with your learned men and priest, and witness the meeting that will seal the alliance.
ramayan::1779.modern_relevance: You finally get the message that the meeting cannot be postponed anymore. You call the people who should stand beside you, and you go face the moment together.
ramayan::1779.insight: It shifts action from delay to immediate, supported presence.

ramayan::1780.verse_sanskrit: प्रीतिं च मम राजेन्द्र निर्वर्तयितुमर्हसि । पुत्रयोरुभयोरेव प्रीतिं त्वमपि लप्स्यसे । । 16813 । ।
ramayan::1780.verse_hindi: O Indra among kings you will not only bring me pleasure, you will also be happy to see your sons.
ramayan::1780.english_translation: O Indra among kings, you will not only bring me pleasure, you will also be happy to see your sons.
ramayan::1780.translation_literal: प्रीतिं (pleasure / joy) / च (and) / मम (my) / राजेन्द्र (O best among kings) / निर्वर्तयितुम् (to bring about) / अर्हसि (you are worthy / should) / पुत्रयोः (of the two sons) / उभयोः (of both) / एव (indeed) / प्रीतिं (joy) / त्वम् (you) / अपि (also) / लप्स्यसे (will obtain)
ramayan::1780.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1780.essence: A meeting meant for one king's joy will satisfy two fathers.
ramayan::1780.simple_meaning: Janaka tells Dasharatha that meeting Rama and Lakshmana will delight both fathers. The reunion will bring joy to everyone involved.
ramayan::1780.simple_insight: A long-awaited meeting can heal more than one heart at once.
ramayan::1780.detailed_meaning: Janaka has invited Dasharatha to see Rama and Lakshmana after the bow-swayamvara. He gently says the meeting will please him and also delight Dasharatha through his sons, turning a formal royal visit into a shared moment of joy.
ramayan::1780.modern_relevance: You finally bring your parents to meet the people your life has become. The relief is bigger than one family — everyone feels the warmth of what was once only hoped for.
ramayan::1780.insight: It frames reunion as mutual blessing, not one-sided gain.

ramayan::1781.verse_sanskrit: एवं विदेहाधिपतिर्मधुरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । । 16814 । । विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञात श्शतानन्दमते स्थित: । इत्युक्त्वा विरता दूता राजगौरवशङ्किता: । । 16815 । ।
ramayan::1781.verse_hindi: The king of Videha (Janaka) with Viswamitras approval and in line with Satanandas thinking has conveyed these sweet words. The messengers having said so concluded  out of respect for their king (afraid that they might look overtalkative).
ramayan::1781.english_translation: Thus the king of Videha, with Vishvamitra's approval and in line with Shatananda's counsel, spoke these gentle words. The messengers, having said this, fell silent out of respect for their king.
ramayan::1781.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / विदेहाधिपतिः (the lord of Videha) / मधुरम् (sweetly) / वाक्यम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञात (approved by Vishvamitra) / श्शतानन्दमते (in Shatananda's opinion) / स्थितः (standing) / इत्युक्त्वा (having said thus) / विरता (stopped) / दूता (the messengers) / राजगौरवशङ्किताः (respectful of the king's dignity)
ramayan::1781.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1781.essence: Respect can matter as much as the message itself.
ramayan::1781.simple_meaning: Janaka speaks politely, with approval from Vishvamitra and guidance from Shatananda. After speaking, the messengers stop, careful not to overstep their respect for the king.
ramayan::1781.simple_insight: Even good news can be carried with restraint and dignity.
ramayan::1781.detailed_meaning: Janaka’s messengers have come with a careful invitation to Rama and Lakshmana. This verse simply shows them finishing their message with formal respect, while Janaka stands ready to receive the response.
ramayan::1781.modern_relevance: You send the final message after a tense family conversation, then stop. Sometimes respect means knowing exactly when to leave words alone.
ramayan::1781.insight: It shows how formal speech and restraint preserve dignity in a delicate exchange.

ramayan::1782.verse_sanskrit: दूतवाक्यं च तच्छ्रुत्वा राजा परमहर्षित: । वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च मन्त्रिणोऽन्यांश्च सोऽब्रवीत् । । 16816 । ।
ramayan::1782.verse_hindi: Exceedingly happy to hear the words of the messengers, the king said to Vasishta, Vamadeva and other ministers.
ramayan::1782.english_translation: Hearing the messengers' words, the king was greatly delighted and spoke to Vasishta, Vamadeva, and the other ministers.
ramayan::1782.translation_literal: दूतवाक्यं (the messengers' words) / च (and) / तत् (that) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राजा (the king) / परमहर्षितः (greatly delighted) / वसिष्ठं (to Vasishta) / वामदेवं (to Vamadeva) / च (and) / मन्त्रिणः (ministers) / अन्यान् (others) / च (and) / सः (he) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1782.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1782.essence: Joy arrives first; interpretation comes next.
ramayan::1782.simple_meaning: The king feels great joy after hearing the messengers and turns to his trusted advisors to speak.
ramayan::1782.simple_insight: A single message can change the mood of an entire court.
ramayan::1782.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, the messengers' report has just arrived. The king is overjoyed and immediately turns to Vasishta, Vamadeva, and the other ministers. The verse simply marks his reaction before the next exchange begins.
ramayan::1782.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with news you've been waiting for, and your first instinct is to turn to the people who help you decide what it means.
ramayan::1782.insight: It shows how important news moves from private feeling into shared counsel.

ramayan::1783.verse_sanskrit: गुप्त: कुशिकपुत्रेण कौसल्यानन्दवर्धन: । लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा विदेहेषु वसत्यसौ । । 16817 । ।
ramayan::1783.verse_hindi: The enhancer of the joy of Kausalya (Rama) along with hs brother Lakshmana under the protection of  Viswamitra  is now staying in the coutry of the Videhas.
ramayan::1783.english_translation: Rama, the delight of Kausalya, is staying in the land of the Videhas with his brother Lakshmana under Vishwamitra's protection.
ramayan::1783.translation_literal: गुप्तः (protected) / कुशिकपुत्रेण (by the son of Kushika, Vishwamitra) / कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः (the increaser of Kausalya's joy) / लक्ष्मणेन (with Lakshmana) / सह (together) / भ्रात्रा (with his brother) / विदेहेषु (in the land of the Videhas) / वसति (is dwelling) / असौ (that one)
ramayan::1783.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1783.essence: Rama's arrival quietly sets the marriage in motion.
ramayan::1783.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are staying in Videha under Vishwamitra's protection.
ramayan::1783.simple_insight: Sometimes the story pauses to place you in the scene before the real turning point arrives.
ramayan::1783.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just heard the messengers and turns to his ministers. This verse simply locates Rama and Lakshmana in Videha, guarded by Vishwamitra, setting up the coming decision to join Rama and Sita.
ramayan::1783.modern_relevance: You hear that someone important has arrived in town, and everyone starts moving differently. Before the announcement, there is only the quiet fact of where they are and who is protecting them.
ramayan::1783.insight: It frames the next action by fixing Rama's presence and status in Videha.

ramayan::1784.verse_sanskrit: दृष्टवीर्यस्तु काकुत्स्थो जनकेन महात्मना । सम्प्रदानं सुतायास्तु राघवे कर्तुमिच्छति । । 16818 । ।
ramayan::1784.verse_hindi: Illustrious Janaka desires to bestow his daughter on the descendat of Kakustha (Rama) whose prowess he has witnessed.
ramayan::1784.english_translation: Illustrious Janaka desires to bestow his daughter on the descendant of Kakustha, Rama, because he has witnessed his prowess.
ramayan::1784.translation_literal: दृष्टवीर्यः (having seen prowess) / तु (indeed) / काकुत्स्थः (the descendant of Kakustha) / जनकेन (by Janaka) / महात्मना (the great-souled one) / सम्प्रदानम् (giving in marriage) / सुतायाः (of his daughter) / तु (indeed) / राघवे (to Rama) / कर्तुम् इच्छति (wishes to do)
ramayan::1784.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1784.essence: Janaka chooses Rama because proven strength matters more than rank.
ramayan::1784.simple_meaning: Janaka wants to give his daughter to Rama because he has seen Rama's greatness and strength.
ramayan::1784.simple_insight: Respect can turn into trust when character proves itself.
ramayan::1784.detailed_meaning: After hearing the messengers, King Janaka learns that Rama is safely staying with Vishvamitra in Mithila. Seeing Rama's proven strength, he decides that this is the right match for Sita, and the court moves quickly toward the wedding.
ramayan::1784.modern_relevance: A parent meets someone who has shown steadiness under pressure, not just charm. That proof changes everything about whether they can be trusted with your child.
ramayan::1784.insight: It shifts attention from status or appearance to demonstrated worth.

ramayan::1785.verse_sanskrit: यदि वो रोचते वृत्तं जनकस्य महात्मन: । पुरीं गच्छामहे शीघ्रं मा भूत्कालस्य पर्यय: । । 16819 । ।
ramayan::1785.verse_hindi: If you approve the action, of the distinguished Janaka, let us hurry to the city of Mithila. Let there be no delay.
ramayan::1785.english_translation: If you approve the action of the distinguished Janaka, let us hurry to the city of Mithila. Let there be no delay.
ramayan::1785.translation_literal: यदि (if) / वो (you) / रोचते (approve, please) / वृत्तं (the action, conduct) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / पुरीं (to the city) / गच्छामहे (let us go) / शीघ्रं (quickly) / मा (not) / भूत् (let there be) / कालस्य (of time) / पर्ययः (delay, lapse)
ramayan::1785.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1785.essence: A right moment can be lost to delay.
ramayan::1785.simple_meaning: If Janaka's plan is acceptable, they should go to Mithila at once and avoid any delay.
ramayan::1785.simple_insight: Good timing matters when a decisive moment arrives.
ramayan::1785.detailed_meaning: Janaka has seen Rama's worth and wants to offer Sita in marriage. The moment is moving forward, and the speaker urges the others to act quickly and not let the opportunity slip away.
ramayan::1785.modern_relevance: You finally get the message everyone has been waiting for, and the next step is clear. The only real danger now is hesitation.
ramayan::1785.insight: It shifts attention from discussion to immediate movement before the moment passes.

ramayan::1786.verse_sanskrit: ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां सोपाध्याय: सबान्धव: । राजा दशरथो हृष्ट स्सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत् । । 1691 । ।
ramayan::1786.verse_hindi: With the passing of the night king Dasaratha, accompanied by spiritual preceptors and relatives said to Sumantra:
ramayan::1786.english_translation: When the night had passed, King Dasaratha, accompanied by his teachers and relatives, said this to Sumantra:
ramayan::1786.translation_literal: ततो (then) / रात्र्यां (at night) / व्यतीतायां (having passed) / स-उपाध्यायः (together with teachers) / स-बान्धवः (together with relatives) / राजा दशरथः (King Dasaratha) / हृष्टः (joyful) / सुमन्त्रम् (to Sumantra) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::1786.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1786.essence: The night ends, and the king is ready to act.
ramayan::1786.simple_meaning: After the night passed, Dasaratha, joined by his teachers and relatives, spoke joyfully to Sumantra.
ramayan::1786.simple_insight: The scene is moving forward; the king is about to send someone with an important message.
ramayan::1786.detailed_meaning: After Janaka's proposal and the call to hurry, the scene shifts to Dasaratha at daybreak. Surrounded by teachers and relatives, he turns to Sumantra. The verse sets up the next command, not a teaching of its own.
ramayan::1786.modern_relevance: A family meeting ends and the room shifts into action. Someone who has been waiting all night finally speaks, and everyone knows the next few words will set things in motion.
ramayan::1786.insight: It marks the transition from decision to instruction, moving the story into motion.

ramayan::1787.verse_sanskrit: अद्य सर्वे धनाध्यक्षा धनमादाय पुष्कलम् । व्रजन्त्वग्रे सुविहिता नानारत्नसमन्विता: । । 1692 । ।
ramayan::1787.verse_hindi: Let all the officers of the treasury furnished with enough wealth and a variety gems go in advance under escort.
ramayan::1787.english_translation: Let all the officers of the treasury, well-provided with ample wealth and many jewels, go ahead under escort.
ramayan::1787.translation_literal: अद्य (today) / सर्वे (all) / धनाध्यक्षा (treasury officers) / धनम् (wealth) / आदाय (taking) / पुष्कलम् (ample) / व्रजन्तु (let go) / अग्रे (in front) / सुविहिता (well-escorted) / नानारत्नसमन्विता: (accompanied by various jewels)
ramayan::1787.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1787.essence: A king's resolve becomes action through careful preparation.
ramayan::1787.simple_meaning: Dasharatha orders the treasury officers to move ahead with plenty of wealth and jewels, properly guarded.
ramayan::1787.simple_insight: It shows a king preparing carefully, not casually, for a major journey or ceremony.
ramayan::1787.detailed_meaning: At dawn in Ayodhya, Dasharatha is making rapid preparations after the previous night's decision. He instructs the treasury officials to set out first with wealth and jewels, showing that this is an organized royal movement, not a private errand.
ramayan::1787.modern_relevance: Before a family wedding, a move, or a major public event, someone has to coordinate the valuables, the people, and the timing. This is that careful, practical kind of leadership.
ramayan::1787.insight: It shifts attention to the logistics that make a royal decision real.

ramayan::1788.verse_sanskrit: चतुरङ्गबलं चापि शीघ्रं निर्यातु सर्वश: । ममज्ञासमकालं च यानयुग्यमनुत्तमम् । । 1693 । ।
ramayan::1788.verse_hindi: Let the four divisions of the army from all the four quarters with elegant palanquins
ramayan::1788.english_translation: Let the four divisions of the army set out at once from every quarter, along with the finest conveyances.
ramayan::1788.translation_literal: चतुरङ्गबलम् (the four-part army) / च (and) / अपि (also) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / निर्यातु (let go out) / सर्वशः (from all sides) / ममज्ञासमकालम् (at the same time as my command) / च (and) / यानयुग्यम् (suitable conveyances) / अनुत्तमम् (excellent)
ramayan::1788.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1788.essence: Royal departure begins with immediate, coordinated action.
ramayan::1788.simple_meaning: Dasharatha orders his army and royal transport to move out immediately, along with the treasury and attendants preparing for departure.
ramayan::1788.simple_insight: Some moments demand total readiness, not hesitation.
ramayan::1788.detailed_meaning: King Dasharatha is preparing a grand departure. After ordering wealth, gems, and attendants to move ahead, he now commands the fourfold army and the finest vehicles to set out at once. The verse is logistical, part of a larger royal procession.
ramayan::1788.modern_relevance: You are packing the house before dawn, and every person has a task. This is the voice of a move that cannot wait for later.
ramayan::1788.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to coordination: when the moment comes, everything must move together.

ramayan::1789.verse_sanskrit: वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिरथ काश्यप: । मार्कण्डेयश्च दीर्घायु:ऋषि: कात्यायनस्तथा । । 1694 । । एते द्विजा: प्रयान्त्वग्रे स्यन्दनं योजयस्व मे । यथा कालात्ययो न स्या द्दूता हि त्वरयन्ति माम् । । 1695 । ।
ramayan::1789.verse_hindi: Let brahmins like Vasishta, Vamadeva, Jabali, Kasyapa, Markandeya endowed with long life, and rishi Katyayana depart in advance. My chariot be yoked and kept ready. Let there be no delay. The messengers (from Janaka) are hastening me up.
ramayan::1789.english_translation: Let brahmins like Vasishta, Vamadeva, Jabali, Kasyapa, Markandeya endowed with long life, and rishi Katyayana depart in advance. My chariot be yoked and kept ready. Let there be no delay. The messengers from Janaka are hastening me up.
ramayan::1789.translation_literal: वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / वामदेवः (Vamadeva) / च (and) / जाबालिः (Jabali) / अथ (also) / काश्यपः (Kasyapa) / मार्कण्डेयः (Markandeya) / च (and) / दीर्घायुः (long-lived) / ऋषिः (sage) / कात्यायनः (Katyayana) / तथा (likewise) / एते (these) / द्विजाः (twice-born) / प्रयान्तु (let go) / अग्रे (in advance) / स्यन्दनम् (chariot) / योजयस्व (yoke) / मे (my) / यथा (so that) / कालात्ययः (delay) / न (not) / स्यात् (may be) / दूताः (messengers) / हि (indeed) / त्वरयन्ति (are urging) / माम् (me)
ramayan::1789.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1789.essence: A king leaves at once when duty and summons demand it.
ramayan::1789.simple_meaning: Dasharatha asks the sages to go ahead, orders his chariot prepared, and insists on leaving without delay because Janaka's messengers are urging him on.
ramayan::1789.simple_insight: Some moments leave no room for hesitation. When the call comes, you move.
ramayan::1789.detailed_meaning: At Ayodhya, King Dasharatha is being summoned by Janaka. He sends respected sages ahead, asks for his chariot at once, and refuses delay. The verse is part of a travel sequence, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::1789.modern_relevance: The car is already running, your phone keeps buzzing, and someone is waiting on a decision you promised to make today. This verse is the pressure of being called forward.
ramayan::1789.insight: It shifts attention to urgency and orderly departure, not reflection or doctrine.

ramayan::1790.verse_sanskrit: वचनात्तु नरेन्द्रस्य सा सेना चतुरङ्गिणी । राजानमृषिभि स्सार्धं व्रजन्तं पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात् । । 1696 । ।
ramayan::1790.verse_hindi: While the Indra among kings (Dasaratha) proceeded with the sages, the four divisions of the army followed them at the command of the king.
ramayan::1790.english_translation: At the king's command, the fourfold army followed behind as Dasharatha moved on with the sages.
ramayan::1790.translation_literal: वचनात् (at the command) / तु (indeed) / नरेन्द्रस्य (of the king) / सा (that) / सेना (army) / चतुरङ्गिणी (fourfold) / राजानम् (the king) / ऋषिभिः (with the sages) / सार्धम् (together with) / व्रजन्तम् (proceeding) / पृष्ठतः (from behind) / अन्वगात् (followed)
ramayan::1790.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1790.essence: The king moves first; the army follows.
ramayan::1790.simple_meaning: Dasharatha moves forward with the sages, and his four-part army follows behind him on his command.
ramayan::1790.simple_insight: Some moments are not speeches or choices — just the movement of power, duty, and people in its wake.
ramayan::1790.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha is on the road with the sages, heading toward Janaka's land. At his command, the four divisions of his army follow behind him. The verse simply marks the royal procession and the scale of the escort.
ramayan::1790.modern_relevance: A convoy pulls out before dawn, and everyone moves because one person gave the word. Some scenes are about momentum, not meaning.
ramayan::1790.insight: It keeps the focus on the procession itself, not on any inner decision or teaching.

ramayan::1791.verse_sanskrit: गत्वा चतुरहं मार्गं विदेहानभ्युपेयिवान् । राजा तु जनक श्श्रीमान् श्श्रुत्वा पूजामकल्पयत् । । 1697 । ।
ramayan::1791.verse_hindi: Covering the distance in four days, they arrived in the country of the Videhas. The fortunate king Janaka, having heard about these tidings, made arangements to extend to them reverential hospitality.
ramayan::1791.english_translation: Covering the distance in four days, they arrived in the country of the Videhas. The fortunate king Janaka, having heard about these tidings, made arrangements to extend to them reverential hospitality.
ramayan::1791.translation_literal: गत्वा (having gone) / चतुरहं (four days) / मार्गं (the road) / विदेहान् (the Videhas) / अभ्युपेयिवान् (arrived) / राजा (the king) / तु (then) / जनकः (Janaka) / श्रीमान् (fortunate / illustrious) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / पूजाम् (honour / reverential hospitality) / अकल्पयत् (made arrangements)
ramayan::1791.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1791.essence: Arrival itself can call forth honour before any meeting begins.
