ramayan::1791.simple_meaning: After four days of travel, the party reached Videha. King Janaka heard of their arrival and prepared respectful hospitality for them.
ramayan::1791.simple_insight: Some arrivals matter enough to change how a whole kingdom receives you.
ramayan::1791.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha and the sages are travelling toward Videha for the great meeting with Janaka. This verse simply marks their arrival and Janaka’s immediate preparation to receive them properly, setting the stage for the alliance and Sita’s swayamvara.
ramayan::1791.modern_relevance: You hear that an important guest is coming, and the whole house shifts. Beds are made, food is prepared, and respect becomes visible before a single word is spoken.
ramayan::1791.insight: It shifts attention from travel itself to the dignity of receiving others well.

ramayan::1792.verse_sanskrit: ततो राजानमासाद्य वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम् । जनको मुदितो राजा हर्षं च परमं ययौ । । 1698 । ।
ramayan::1792.verse_hindi: King Janaka approached the aged ruler of men, Dasaratha, and experienced great delight.
ramayan::1792.english_translation: King Janaka approached the aged ruler of men, Dasaratha, and experienced great delight.
ramayan::1792.translation_literal: ततः (then) / राजानम् (the king) / आसाद्य (having approached) / वृद्धम् (the aged) / दशरथम् (Dasaratha) / नृपम् (king) / जनकः (Janaka) / मुदितः (joyful) / राजा (king) / हर्षम् (delight) / च (and) / परमम् (greatest) / ययौ (went to; experienced)
ramayan::1792.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1792.essence: Joy rises when rightful guests finally meet.
ramayan::1792.simple_meaning: Janaka meets the elderly King Dasaratha and feels deep joy at the sight of him.
ramayan::1792.simple_insight: Warm recognition can arrive before any words are spoken.
ramayan::1792.detailed_meaning: Janaka has come out to receive Dasaratha after the journey to Videha. Seeing the aged king before him, he is filled with delight. The verse simply marks the meeting point before the formal welcome and marriage arrangements begin.
ramayan::1792.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person you’ve been hearing about for months, and the tension drops. Sometimes respect becomes real the moment you stand face to face.
ramayan::1792.insight: It frames the scene as a meeting of honor, setting a gracious tone for what follows.

ramayan::1793.verse_sanskrit: उवाच च नरश्रेष्ठो नरश्रेष्ठं मुदाऽन्वित: । स्वागतं ते महाराज दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि राघव । । 1699 । । पुत्रयोरुभयो: प्रीतिं लप्स्यसे वीर्यनिर्जिताम् ।
ramayan::1793.verse_hindi: Filled with joy the best of men (Janaka) addreseed the best of men Dasaratha: O Descendant of the Raghus, O Great king welcome I am fortunate to have you, you will experience the pleasure of both your sons having won the  reward for their prowess.
ramayan::1793.english_translation: Filled with joy, the best of men Janaka addressed the best of men Dasaratha: "Welcome, great king. I am fortunate that you have arrived, O descendant of the Raghus. You will experience the joy of both your sons winning the prize through their own valor."
ramayan::1793.translation_literal: उवाच (said) / च (and) / नरश्रेष्ठः (best of men) / नरश्रेष्ठम् (to the best of men) / मुदा-अन्वितः (filled with joy) / स्वागतम् (welcome) / ते (to you) / महाराज (great king) / दिष्ट्या (by good fortune) / प्राप्तः असि (you have arrived) / राघव (O descendant of Raghu) / पुत्रयोः (of the two sons) / उभयोः (both) / प्रीतिम् (joy) / लप्स्यसे (you will obtain) / वीर्य-निर्जिताम् (won by valor)
ramayan::1793.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1793.essence: Victory will soon bring joy to both fathers.
ramayan::1793.simple_meaning: Janaka warmly welcomes Dasaratha and says he is blessed to have come. He also says Dasaratha will soon feel the joy of both sons proving their worth.
ramayan::1793.simple_insight: Joy can come from seeing courage honored, not just from winning yourself.
ramayan::1793.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has arrived in Mithila for the great meeting around Sita's swayamvara. Janaka greets him with warmth and respect, speaking as a host and fellow king. His words point toward the coming contest, where the sons of both kings will be tested.
ramayan::1793.modern_relevance: You open the door to a room full of pressure, and someone greets you with real warmth. Even before the outcome is known, respect can soften the edge of competition.
ramayan::1793.insight: It frames achievement as something shared by families and communities, not just individuals.

ramayan::1794.verse_sanskrit: दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो महातेजा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषि: । । 16910 । । सह सर्वैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठैर्देवैरिव शतक्रतु: ।
ramayan::1794.verse_hindi: Most brilliant and adorable ascetic Vasishta surrounded by the foremost of brahmins like Indra by the gods has also arrived by the grace of God.
ramayan::1794.english_translation: By good fortune, the brilliant sage Vasishta has arrived, accompanied by the foremost brahmins, like Indra among the radiant beings.
ramayan::1794.translation_literal: दिष्ट्या (by good fortune) / प्राप्तः (arrived) / महातेजाः (of great brilliance) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / भगवान् (venerable) / ऋषिः (sage) / सह (with) / सर्वैः (all) / द्विजश्रेष्ठैः (foremost of brahmins) / देवैः (with the radiant beings) / इव (like) / शतक्रतुः (Indra)
ramayan::1794.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1794.essence: Respect changes the mood before anyone speaks.
ramayan::1794.simple_meaning: Janaka is delighted that Vasishta has arrived with the leading brahmins, shining among them like Indra among the radiant beings.
ramayan::1794.simple_insight: Some arrivals change the whole atmosphere of a room.
ramayan::1794.detailed_meaning: Janaka has come to greet Dasharatha after the wedding arrangements. Now Vasishta, the royal teacher, arrives with the chief brahmins. The verse simply marks the honor and joy of his entrance before the larger exchange continues.
ramayan::1794.modern_relevance: The person everyone trusts finally walks into the room, and the tension drops before a word is spoken.
ramayan::1794.insight: It marks the arrival of respected authority before the next ceremonial exchange.

ramayan::1795.verse_sanskrit: दिष्ट्या मे निर्जिता विघ्ना दिष्ट्या मे पूजितं कुलम् । । 16911 । । राघवै स्सह सम्बन्धाद्वीर्यश्रेष्ठैर्महात्मभि: ।
ramayan::1795.verse_hindi: By the grace of god, I have overcome all impediments. By the grace of God my race  has been honoured through alliance with the house of the Raghus distinguished by their valour.
ramayan::1795.english_translation: By the grace of the divine, I have overcome all obstacles. By the grace of the divine, my family has been honoured through alliance with the house of the Raghus, whose great men are foremost in valour.
ramayan::1795.translation_literal: दिष्ट्या (by good fortune / by grace) / मे (my) / निर्जिता (conquered) / विघ्ना (obstacles) / दिष्ट्या (by good fortune / by grace) / मे (my) / पूजितं (honoured) / कुलम् (family / lineage) / राघवैः (by the Raghus) / सह (with) / सम्बन्धात् (through alliance) / वीर्यश्रेष्ठैः (by those श्रेष्ठ in valour) / महात्मभिः (by great-souled ones)
ramayan::1795.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1795.essence: A rightful alliance can remove obstacles and restore honour at once.
ramayan::1795.simple_meaning: Janaka says his obstacles are gone and his family is honoured because of the alliance with Rama's noble house.
ramayan::1795.simple_insight: A good alliance can lift a whole family’s standing and ease long-standing burdens.
ramayan::1795.detailed_meaning: Janaka welcomes Dasharatha and sees Vasishta arrive with the sages. In this moment of public honour before Sita’s swayamvara, he speaks with relief: the obstacles are gone, and his house is dignified by its bond with the Raghus.
ramayan::1795.modern_relevance: You finally get the call that confirms the partnership, the admission, the marriage, the deal. The pressure that sat on your family name or your future loosens at once.
ramayan::1795.insight: It frames honour and relief as something shared through rightful association, not private achievement alone.

ramayan::1796.verse_sanskrit: श्व: प्रभाते नरेन्द्रेन्द्र निर्वर्तयितुमर्हसि । । 16912 । । यज्ञस्यान्ते नरश्रेष्ठ विवाहमृषिसम्मतम् ।
ramayan::1796.verse_hindi: O Foremost of men, O Best of kings, tomorrow at dawn after the completion of the sacrifice, you should perform the marriage with approval by the sages.
ramayan::1796.english_translation: O foremost of men, O best of kings, tomorrow at dawn, after the sacrifice is complete, you should perform the marriage approved by the sages.
ramayan::1796.translation_literal: श्वः (tomorrow) / प्रभाते (at dawn) / नरेन्द्रेन्द्र (O foremost of kings) / निर्वर्तयितुम् (to carry out) / अर्हसि (you should) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / अन्ते (at the end) / नरश्रेष्ठ (O best of men) / विवाहम् (the marriage) / ऋषिसम्मतम् (approved by the sages)
ramayan::1796.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1796.essence: A completed rite creates the moment for the next duty.
ramayan::1796.simple_meaning: After the sacrifice is finished, Dasharatha is told to hold the marriage ceremony the next morning, with the sages' approval.
ramayan::1796.simple_insight: Right timing matters too. A sacred act can prepare the ground for the next responsibility.
ramayan::1796.detailed_meaning: Vasishta stands among the sages after the sacrifice and instructs Dasharatha to complete the wedding at dawn. The moment turns a sacred gathering into a binding royal duty: the king must now act on what the ritual has made possible.
ramayan::1796.modern_relevance: You finally close the big meeting, and everyone turns to the thing you said would happen next. The first task is done; now you have to carry the promise across the finish line.
ramayan::1796.insight: It teaches you to move from preparation into action without delay once the moment is ripe.

ramayan::1797.verse_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ऋषिमध्ये नराधिप: । । 16913 । । वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठ: प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम् ।
ramayan::1797.verse_hindi: At these words, the most eloquent king (Dasaratha) made his reply in the midst of sages:
ramayan::1797.english_translation: At these words, the king replied in the midst of the sages.
ramayan::1797.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / तद्वचनं (that speech) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / ऋषिमध्ये (in the midst of sages) / नराधिपः (the king) / वाक्यं-वाक्यविदां (among speakers, the best) / श्रेष्ठः (the best) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / महीपतिम् (to the great ruler)
ramayan::1797.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1797.essence: A king's reply can carry the weight of the whole moment.
ramayan::1797.simple_meaning: Dasharatha hears the sage's words and answers respectfully in front of the assembled sages.
ramayan::1797.simple_insight: Some moments matter because a king chooses courtesy before everyone watching.
ramayan::1797.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a sacred gathering, Dasharatha hears the sage's proposal and answers as a king should. The verse is a bridge: it moves the scene from the sage's request to the king's decision.
ramayan::1797.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after a proposal you didn't expect. You take a breath, choose your words carefully, and answer with the dignity the moment deserves.
ramayan::1797.insight: It shifts attention from the content of the reply to the poise with which it is given.

ramayan::1798.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिग्रहो दातृवश श्श्रृतमेतन्मया पुरा । । 16914 । । यथा वक्ष्यसि धर्मज्ञ तत्करिष्यामहे वयम् ।
ramayan::1798.verse_hindi: I have heard that acceptance of a gift from the righteous is a pleasure. So we will act upon your word.
ramayan::1798.english_translation: I have heard long ago that accepting a gift from the righteous is proper. So, O knower of dharma, we will do as you say.
ramayan::1798.translation_literal: प्रतिग्रहः (acceptance / receiving) / दातृवशः (under the giver's control) / श्रुतम् (heard) / एतत् (this) / मया (by me) / पुरा (long ago) / यथा (as) / वक्ष्यसि (you will say) / धर्मज्ञ (O knower of dharma) / तत् (that) / करिष्यामहे (we will do) / वयम् (we)
ramayan::1798.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1798.essence: True respect is shown by doing what you say.
ramayan::1798.simple_meaning: Dasharatha agrees to follow the sage's instruction and says he will act according to what has been said.
ramayan::1798.simple_insight: A good word matters only when it becomes action.
ramayan::1798.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's sacrificial gathering, Dasharatha hears the proposal for Sita's marriage and answers with respect. He does not bargain or delay. The moment matters because a king's response now sets the course of Rama and Sita's future.
ramayan::1798.modern_relevance: You promised a friend, a partner, or a team that you would show up. Now the moment has come, and your reply will decide whether your word meant anything.
ramayan::1798.insight: It links honour to follow-through: once you assent, your action must match your speech.

ramayan::1799.verse_sanskrit: धर्मिष्ठं च यशस्यं च वचनं सत्यवादिन: । । 16915 । । श्रुत्वा विदेहाधिपति: परं विस्मयमागत: । ।
ramayan::1799.verse_hindi: Janaka was filled with extreme admiration to hear one who was truthful, righteous and famous (this Dasaratha).
ramayan::1799.english_translation: Janaka was filled with extreme admiration to hear one who was truthful, righteous, and renowned.
ramayan::1799.translation_literal: धर्मिष्ठं (most righteous) / च (and) / यशस्यं (famous) / च (and) / वचनं (speech) / सत्यवादिनः (of the truth-speaker) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / विदेहाधिपतिः (the king of Videha, Janaka) / परं (great) / विस्मयम् (wonder) / आगतः (reached)
ramayan::1799.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1799.essence: Truthful speech can still leave greatness speechless.
ramayan::1799.simple_meaning: Janaka is deeply impressed when he hears Dasaratha speak with truth, righteousness, and honor.
ramayan::1799.simple_insight: A person of integrity can move even a great king to wonder.
ramayan::1799.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's assembly, Dasaratha has just spoken with the weight of a man bound to truth and dharma. Janaka, hearing that voice, is struck with admiration. The verse pauses on that response before the sages continue their joyful gathering.
ramayan::1799.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with rare honesty in a room full of polished words, and it stops you cold. Integrity still has the power to command respect.
ramayan::1799.insight: It highlights how truthful speech itself can create trust and awe.

ramayan::1800.verse_sanskrit: तत स्सर्वे मुनिगणा: परस्परसमागमे । 16916 । हर्षेण महता युक्तास्तां निशामवसन् सुखम् । ।
ramayan::1800.verse_hindi: Thereupon hosts of sages in one anothers company, filled with great delight spent the night comfortably.
ramayan::1800.english_translation: Thereupon the gathered sages, delighted to meet one another, spent the night in comfort.
ramayan::1800.translation_literal: ततस् (thereupon) / सर्वे (all) / मुनिगणा: (groups of sages) / परस्परसमागमे (in mutual meeting) / हर्षेण (with delight) / महता (great) / युक्ता: (endowed) / तां (that) / निशाम् (night) / अवसन् (spent) / सुखम् (comfortably)
ramayan::1800.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1800.essence: Joy in good company turns waiting into ease.
ramayan::1800.simple_meaning: The sages met each other happily and passed the night in comfort.
ramayan::1800.simple_insight: Shared joy can make even an ordinary night feel complete.
ramayan::1800.detailed_meaning: After Janaka and Dasharatha’s exchange of honor and praise, the assembled sages rejoice in one another’s company. Nothing decisive happens here; the scene simply settles into calm before the next morning’s royal reunion.
ramayan::1800.modern_relevance: A long, tense gathering finally loosens after the formal words are done, and everyone can breathe again. Sometimes the real relief is just being together without strain.
ramayan::1800.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, marking a pause after social and ceremonial tension.

ramayan::1801.verse_sanskrit: राजा च राघवौ पुत्रौ निशाम्य परिहर्षित: । । 16917 । । उवास परमप्रीतो जनकेन सुपूजित: ।
ramayan::1801.verse_hindi: The king (Dasaratha) was greatly delighted on being reunited with his sons Rama and Lakshmana. Honoured by Janaka, he spent the night with supreme satisfaction.
ramayan::1801.english_translation: The king was greatly delighted to see his two sons, Rama and Lakshmana. Honoured by Janaka, he spent the night in supreme happiness.
ramayan::1801.translation_literal: राजा (the king) / च (and) / राघवौ (the two Raghava princes) / पुत्रौ (sons) / निशाम्य (having seen) / परिहर्षितः (greatly delighted) / उवास (dwelt/spent the night) / परमप्रीतः (supremely pleased) / जनकेन (by Janaka) / सुपूजितः (well honoured)
ramayan::1801.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1801.essence: Reunion matters more than royal ceremony.
ramayan::1801.simple_meaning: Dasharatha sees Rama and Lakshmana again, feels deep joy, and stays the night as Janaka’s honoured guest.
ramayan::1801.simple_insight: Some moments are simple: seeing your children safe can undo an entire heart.
ramayan::1801.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court, the formal tension of the bow contest has passed. Dasharatha sees Rama and Lakshmana again, is overwhelmed with relief, and remains honoured by Janaka through the night. The verse simply records that shared ease after a difficult public moment.
ramayan::1801.modern_relevance: You finally spot your child in the crowd after a long day. The knot in your chest loosens before you even speak.
ramayan::1801.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to relief: the real victory here is reunion, not ceremony.

ramayan::1802.verse_sanskrit: जनकोऽपि महातेजा: क्रियां धर्मेण तत्त्ववित् । । 16918 । । यज्ञस्य च सुताभ्यां च कृत्वा रात्रिमुवास ह ।
ramayan::1802.verse_hindi: Mighty philosopher Janaka also performed the  sacrificial rites and spent the night (there where the sacrificial ceremony was performed) with both his daughters.
ramayan::1802.english_translation: Mighty and wise Janaka performed the sacrificial rites according to dharma, and spent the night there with his daughters.
ramayan::1802.translation_literal: जनकः (Janaka) / अपि (also) / महातेजाः (mighty, radiant) / क्रियाम् (the rite) / धर्मेण (according to dharma) / तत्त्ववित् (knower of truth) / यज्ञस्य (of the sacrifice) / च (and) / सुताभ्याम् (with the two daughters) / च (and) / कृत्वा (having done) / रात्रिम् (the night) / उवास (spent) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::1802.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1802.essence: Wisdom shows itself in calm, proper action.
ramayan::1802.simple_meaning: Janaka completed the sacrificial rites properly and stayed there through the night with his daughters.
ramayan::1802.simple_insight: Right action can be steady, quiet, and fully present.
ramayan::1802.detailed_meaning: After the reunion of the kings and sages at Janaka’s sacrificial gathering, the scene settles into order. Janaka, known for wisdom and power, completes the ritual properly and remains there with Sita and her sister through the night, holding the dignity of the moment.
ramayan::1802.modern_relevance: You finish the ceremony, the family gathering, or the long day’s obligation, then stay present instead of rushing away. Some moments ask for quiet endurance, not performance.
ramayan::1802.insight: It teaches you to complete what is required and remain grounded in the aftermath.

ramayan::1803.verse_sanskrit: तत: प्रभाते जनक: कृतकर्मा महर्षिभि: । उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञ श्शतानन्दं पुरोहितम् । । 1701 । ।
ramayan::1803.verse_hindi: Thereafter at dawn after the maharshis had performed their daily (sacrificial) rites the eloquent Janaka said to the chief priest Satananda:
ramayan::1803.english_translation: Thereafter at dawn, after the great sages had completed the rites, Janaka, master of speech, spoke to the chief priest Shatananda.
ramayan::1803.translation_literal: तत: (thereafter) / प्रभाते (at dawn) / जनक: (Janaka) / कृतकर्मा (having completed the rites) / महर्षिभि: (by the great sages) / उवाच (spoke) / वाक्यं (a speech) / वाक्यज्ञ (knower of speech) / श्शतानन्दं (to Shatananda) / पुरोहितम् (the chief priest)
ramayan::1803.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1803.essence: The ritual has ended; the next conversation begins.
ramayan::1803.simple_meaning: At dawn, after the ritual duties were finished, Janaka spoke to Shatananda, the chief priest.
ramayan::1803.simple_insight: Some moments simply move the story forward without carrying a deeper teaching.
ramayan::1803.detailed_meaning: At dawn in Janaka's sacrificial court, the sages have finished their rites. Janaka, already established in ritual order, turns to his priest Shatananda and begins the next step of the gathering. The verse sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
ramayan::1803.modern_relevance: A ceremony ends, the room settles, and someone finally speaks to begin the real discussion. This line is the quiet hinge between ritual completion and the next decision.
ramayan::1803.insight: It marks a transition from sacred action to spoken instruction.

ramayan::1804.verse_sanskrit: भ्राता मम महातेजा यवीयानतिधार्मिक: । कुशध्वज इति ख्यात: पुरीमध्यवसच्छुभाम् । । 1702 । । वार्याफलकपर्यन्तां पिबन्निक्षुमतीं नदीम् । साङ्काश्यां पुण्यसङ्काशां विमानमिव पुष्पकम् । । 1703 । ।
ramayan::1804.verse_hindi: The extremely righteous, renowned and most brilliant Kusadhwaja, my younger brother is (at present) ruling the sacred kingdom of Sankasya, which is like the aerial chariot Pushpaka, with darts planted in water as boundary on the bank of the auspicious, sacred river Ikshumati.
ramayan::1804.english_translation: The extremely righteous, renowned and most brilliant Kusadhwaja, my younger brother, is ruling the sacred kingdom of Sankasya, which is like the aerial chariot Pushpaka, with darts planted in water as its boundary on the bank of the auspicious, sacred river Ikshumati.
ramayan::1804.translation_literal: भ्राता (brother) / मम (my) / महातेजा (very brilliant) / यवीयान् (younger) / अतिधार्मिकः (highly righteous) / कुशध्वजः (Kushadhvaja) / इति (thus) / ख्यातः (known) / पुरीमध्यवसत् (dwells in the city) / शुभाम् (auspicious) / वार्याफलकपर्यन्ताम् (with water-planks as boundary) / पिबन् (drinking / flowing through) / इक्षुमतीम् (Ikshumati) / नदीम् (river) / साङ्काश्याम् (Sankasya) / पुण्यसङ्काशाम् (holy-looking) / विमानमिव (like a flying chariot) / पुष्पकम् (Pushpaka)
ramayan::1804.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1804.essence: A royal introduction prepares the way for a personal request.
ramayan::1804.simple_meaning: Janaka identifies his younger brother Kusadhwaja and describes his prosperous, sacred city by the Ikshumati River.
ramayan::1804.simple_insight: Family, status, and place are being named before a larger request is made.
ramayan::1804.detailed_meaning: Janaka is speaking to Shatananda after completing the rites. He introduces his younger brother Kusadhwaja, a righteous ruler of Sankasya, and paints the city in vivid, royal terms. The verse sets up the family connection before Janaka asks to see him.
ramayan::1804.modern_relevance: You mention a sibling's name, title, and home before asking for a favor. The details matter because they prepare trust and show respect.
ramayan::1804.insight: It frames the coming request through kinship and recognition, not abrupt demand.

ramayan::1805.verse_sanskrit: तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि यज्ञगोप्ता स मे मत: । प्रीतिं सोऽपि महातेजा इमां भोक्ता मया सह । । 1704 । ।
ramayan::1805.verse_hindi: I desire to see Kusadhwaja who I have accepted as the protector of the sacrifice. I want that my glorious brother should share this pleasure, with me.
ramayan::1805.english_translation: I desire to see Kusadhwaja, whom I have accepted as the protector of the sacrifice. I want my glorious brother to share this joy with me.
ramayan::1805.translation_literal: तम् (him) / अहम् (I) / द्रष्टुम् इच्छामि (wish to see) / यज्ञ-गोप्ता (protector of the sacrifice) / सः (he) / मे (to me) / मतः (is regarded) / प्रीतिम् (joy) / सः अपि (he also) / महा-तेजाः (very radiant) / इमाम् (this) / भोक्ता (to enjoy) / मया सह (with me)
ramayan::1805.speaker: Janaka
ramayan::1805.essence: Shared joy matters more than private success.
ramayan::1805.simple_meaning: Janaka says he wants to see his brother Kusadhwaja and share the joy of the sacrifice with him.
ramayan::1805.simple_insight: Joy feels fuller when it is shared with family.
ramayan::1805.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's sacrifice, the rites are complete and the king turns to family. He speaks of Kusadhwaja, his younger brother, as the protector of the ritual and asks to see him so they can share the moment together.
ramayan::1805.modern_relevance: You finish something important and immediately want the person who helped hold it together beside you. The win feels incomplete until you can share it.
ramayan::1805.insight: It highlights how accomplishment becomes meaningful when it is offered back into relationship.

ramayan::1806.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ते तु वचने शतानन्दस्य सन्निधौ । आगता: केचिदव्यग्रा जनकस्तान् समादिशत् । । 1705 । ।
ramayan::1806.verse_hindi: Janaka having said so in the presence of Satananda gave instructions to a few faithful  attendants who were present.
ramayan::1806.english_translation: Then, after Janaka had spoken those words in Satananda's presence, a few calm attendants arrived, and Janaka gave them instructions.
ramayan::1806.translation_literal: एवमुक्ते (thus having been spoken) / तु (then) / वचने (when the words) / शतानन्दस्य (of Satananda) / सन्निधौ (in the presence) / आगता: (arrived) / केचिद् (some) / अव्यग्रा (untroubled, calm) / जनकः (Janaka) / तान् (to them) / समादिशत् (gave instructions)
ramayan::1806.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1806.essence: A king's words become action through immediate instruction.
ramayan::1806.simple_meaning: Janaka gives instructions to his attendants after speaking with Satananda.
ramayan::1806.simple_insight: Small actions still matter when a larger plan is already in motion.
ramayan::1806.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, after he has spoken before Satananda, a few composed attendants come forward. Janaka immediately gives them directions. The verse simply moves the scene toward the next step in the search for Kusadhwaja.
ramayan::1806.modern_relevance: You finish the conversation and immediately call the person who needs to move next. The decision is already made; now someone has to carry it out.
ramayan::1806.insight: It shifts attention from the decision itself to the practical handoff that makes it real.

ramayan::1807.verse_sanskrit: शासनात्तु नरेन्द्रस्य प्रययुश्शीघ्रवाजिभि: । समानेतुं नरव्याघ्रं विष्णुमिन्द्राज्ञया यथा । । 1706 । ।
ramayan::1807.verse_hindi: In obedience to the command of Indra among men (king Janaka), the messengers rode away on swift horses to bring king Kusadhwaja, a tiger among men just like fetching Visnu by the orders of Indra.
ramayan::1807.english_translation: By the king's command, the messengers quickly rode swift horses to bring the tiger among men, just as Indra's order would bring Vishnu.
ramayan::1807.translation_literal: शासनात् (by command) / तु (indeed) / नरेन्द्रस्य (of the king) / प्रययुः (went) / शीघ्रवाजिभिः (with swift horses) / समानेतुम् (to bring) / नरव्याघ्रम् (tiger among men) / विष्णुम् (Vishnu) / इन्द्राज्ञया (by Indra's command) / यथा (as)
ramayan::1807.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1807.essence: A king's will becomes motion the moment he speaks.
ramayan::1807.simple_meaning: Janaka's messengers quickly ride out on fast horses to bring Kusadhwaja to him.
ramayan::1807.simple_insight: Some moments are only movement: a command given, a task carried out, a person brought into the story.
ramayan::1807.detailed_meaning: Janaka has decided he wants Kusadhwaja present. In the royal court, he gives the order, and trusted messengers immediately depart on swift horses. This verse simply marks the urgency of that errand before the meeting takes place.
ramayan::1807.modern_relevance: A text arrives: "Please come now." You drop what you were doing, book the cab, and head out because someone important needs you there.
ramayan::1807.insight: It shifts attention from the decision to the execution, showing how authority becomes action through trusted messengers.

ramayan::1808.verse_sanskrit: साङ्काश्यां ते समागत्य ददृशुश्च कुशध्वजम् । न्यवेदयन्यथावृत्तं जनकस्य च चिन्तितम् । । 1707 । ।
ramayan::1808.verse_hindi: The messengers reached Sankasya, met Kusadhwaja and related to him what had happened. They informed him the intention of (king) Janaka.
ramayan::1808.english_translation: The messengers reached Sankasya, met Kusadhwaja, and told him what had happened. They conveyed Janaka's intention.
ramayan::1808.translation_literal: साङ्काश्यां (to Sankasya) / ते (they) / समागत्य (having arrived) / ददृशुः (saw) / च (and) / कुशध्वजम् (Kusadhwaja) / न्यवेदयन् (reported) / यथावृत्तम् (what had happened) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / च (and) / चिन्तितम् (intention)
ramayan::1808.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1808.essence: The message is delivered so the next step can begin.
ramayan::1808.simple_meaning: The messengers arrive, meet Kusadhwaja, and report Janaka's message and the events that led to it.
ramayan::1808.simple_insight: Some moments only move the story forward. This is one of them.
ramayan::1808.detailed_meaning: Janaka has already sent trusted messengers ahead. They reach Sankasya, find Kusadhwaja, and repeat the whole situation and Janaka's intention. The verse simply carries the message across, preparing the next meeting.
ramayan::1808.modern_relevance: You send the text, wait for the reply, and keep the chain moving. Sometimes all that matters is getting the message to the right person.
ramayan::1808.insight: It shifts attention from drama to transmission: the verse exists to connect one decision to the next.

ramayan::1809.verse_sanskrit: तद्वृत्तं नृपति श्शृत्वा दूतश्रेष्ठैर्महाबलै: । अज्ञायाऽथ नरेन्द्रस्य आजगाम कुशध्वज: । । 1708 । ।
ramayan::1809.verse_hindi: Kusadhwaja having heard the events from the loyal, mighty messengers set out for Mithila in compliance with the request of the king (Janaka).
ramayan::1809.english_translation: Kusadhwaja, having heard the account from the loyal, mighty messengers, set out for Mithila in compliance with King Janaka's request.
ramayan::1809.translation_literal: तद्वृत्तं (that account) / नृपतिः (the king) / शृत्वा (having heard) / दूतश्रेष्ठैः (from the best messengers) / महाबलैः (mighty) / अज्ञाय (having understood) / अथ (then) / नरेन्द्रस्य (of the king) / आजगाम (came) / कुशध्वजः (Kusadhwaja)
ramayan::1809.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1809.essence: He heard the request and came at once.
ramayan::1809.simple_meaning: Kusadhwaja hears the messengers, understands Janaka's request, and goes to Mithila.
ramayan::1809.simple_insight: A prompt, respectful response can move events forward without delay.
ramayan::1809.detailed_meaning: Janaka's messengers have already spoken to Kusadhwaja about the situation. After hearing them, he does not hesitate or argue; he accepts the request and travels to Mithila. The verse simply advances the meeting that will follow.
ramayan::1809.modern_relevance: A message lands in your inbox that changes the day. You read it once, understand what is being asked, and get moving instead of stalling in indecision.
ramayan::1809.insight: It shows how quickly a responsible person answers a legitimate call.

ramayan::1810.verse_sanskrit: स ददर्श महात्मानं जनकं धर्मवत्सलम् । सोऽभिवाद्य शतानन्दं राजानं चापि धार्मिकम् । । 1709 । । राजार्हं परमं दिव्यमासनं चाऽध्यरोहत ।
ramayan::1810.verse_hindi: There he saw the highsouled Janaka devoted to righteousness. Having paid his regards to Satananda and the virtuous king he occupied an exalted seat befitting a
ramayan::1810.english_translation: There he saw the high-souled Janaka devoted to righteousness. Having paid his respects to Shatananda and the righteous king, he sat on an exalted seat worthy of a king.
ramayan::1810.translation_literal: स (he) / ददर्श (saw) / महात्मानं (the high-souled) / जनकं (Janaka) / धर्मवत्सलम् (devoted to righteousness) / सोऽभिवाद्य (having bowed to) / शतानन्दं (Shatananda) / राजानं (the king) / च (and) / अपि (also) / धार्मिकम् (the righteous) / राजार्हं (worthy of a king) / परमं (supreme) / दिव्यम् (divine) / आसनं (seat) / च (and) / आऽध्यरोहत (ascended)
ramayan::1810.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1810.simple_meaning: Kusadhwaja arrives and respectfully meets Janaka and Shatananda. After greeting them, he takes a royal seat.
ramayan::1810.simple_insight: Respect opens the meeting before any serious business begins.
ramayan::1810.detailed_meaning: Kusadhwaja has come to Mithila after hearing the message. He sees Janaka, greets Shatananda and the righteous king with honor, and sits on a fitting royal seat. The verse simply sets the scene before the real discussion begins.
ramayan::1810.modern_relevance: You enter a room for a difficult conversation and pause before speaking. The way you acknowledge people first can shape everything that follows.
ramayan::1810.insight: It teaches you to begin important meetings with humility and proper regard.

ramayan::1811.verse_sanskrit: उपविष्टावुभौ तौ तु भ्रातरावतितेजसौ । । 17010 । । प्रेषयामासतुर्वीरौ मन्त्रिश्रेष्ठं सुदामनम् ।
ramayan::1811.verse_hindi: The two heroic brothers endowed with great splendour seated beside each other, despatched Sudamana the wisest of ministers (to Dasaratha).
ramayan::1811.english_translation: The two heroic brothers, both radiant with great splendour, sat together and sent the best minister, Sudamana.
ramayan::1811.translation_literal: उपविष्टौ (seated) / उभौ (both) / तौ (those two) / तु (indeed) / भ्रातरौ (the two brothers) / अतितेजसौ (exceedingly radiant) / प्रेषयामासतुः (sent forth) / वीरौ (the heroic ones) / मन्त्रिश्रेष्ठम् (the best of ministers) / सुदामनम् (Sudamana)
ramayan::1811.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1811.essence: A messenger is sent; the diplomatic exchange begins.
ramayan::1811.simple_meaning: The two brothers sat together and sent their trusted minister on an errand.
ramayan::1811.simple_insight: Some moments matter only because they move the story forward.
ramayan::1811.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the two radiant brothers sit together after meeting Janaka’s court. They send Sudamana, the chief minister, as an envoy to Dasaratha. The verse simply marks the dispatch of a messenger before the next royal exchange.
ramayan::1811.modern_relevance: A meeting ends, and someone is chosen to carry the message across town. The real work now happens through careful delegation.
ramayan::1811.insight: It shifts attention from the scene to the next step in the negotiation.

ramayan::1812.verse_sanskrit: गच्छ मन्त्रिपते शीघ्रमैक्ष्वाकुममितप्रभम् । । 17011 । । आत्मजैस्सह दुर्धर्षमानयस्व समन्त्रिणम् ।
ramayan::1812.verse_hindi: O Foremost among counsellors, go speedily and bring along with his ministers and sons the invincible Dasaratha of the Ikshvakus dynasty whose splendour is immeasurable.
ramayan::1812.english_translation: O foremost among counsellors, go quickly and bring the invincible Dasaratha of the Ikshvaku line, along with his ministers and sons, whose splendour is immeasurable.
ramayan::1812.translation_literal: गच्छ (go) / मन्त्रिपते (O lord of ministers) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / ऐक्ष्वाकुम् (the Ikshvaku one) / अमितप्रभम् (of immeasurable splendour) / आत्मजैः (with sons) / सह (together) / दुर्धर्षम् (invincible) / आनयस्व (bring) / समन्त्रिणम् (with ministers)
ramayan::1812.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::1812.essence: A royal summons moves the scene forward.
ramayan::1812.simple_meaning: The messenger is told to hurry and bring Dasaratha, along with his sons and ministers, to the assembly.
ramayan::1812.simple_insight: Some verses simply move the scene forward. Their job is to show who is being summoned and how important he is.
ramayan::1812.detailed_meaning: Janaka and the assembled kings are in place. Now the host sends Sudamana to fetch Dasaratha, bringing him with his sons and ministers. The verse is a formal summons, not a teaching, and it sets up the next exchange.
ramayan::1812.modern_relevance: A meeting is waiting, and someone important still has to be fetched from another room. The verse is just the handoff that keeps the scene moving.
ramayan::1812.insight: It marks a transition, not a lesson: the story advances by formal invitation.

ramayan::1813.verse_sanskrit: औपकार्यां स गत्वा तु रघूणां कुलवर्धनम् । । 17012 । । ददर्श शिरसा चैनमभिवाद्येदमब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1813.verse_hindi: Having reached the tent, he (Sudamana) saw Dasaratha, perpetuator of the race of the
ramayan::1813.english_translation: Having reached the tent, he saw Dasaratha, the increaser of Raghu's line, and bowed to him with his head before speaking.
ramayan::1813.translation_literal: औपकार्याम् (to the tent) / सः (he) / गत्वा (having gone) / तु (indeed) / रघूणाम् (of the Raghus) / कुलवर्धनम् (the increaser of the line) / ददर्श (saw) / शिरसा (with head) / च (and) / एनम् (him) / अभिवाद्य (having bowed) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1813.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1813.essence: A messenger enters with humility before speaking.
ramayan::1813.simple_meaning: Sudamana goes to the tent, sees Dasaratha, bows his head, and begins his message.
ramayan::1813.simple_insight: Respect opens the way for the message that follows.
ramayan::1813.detailed_meaning: Sudamana reaches the temporary camp where Dasaratha is staying, sees the king, and bows before speaking. The verse is a brief scene-setting step before Janaka's request is delivered.
ramayan::1813.modern_relevance: You walk into a room knowing you must deliver news carefully. Before the message, your manner already speaks for you.
ramayan::1813.insight: It shows that formal respect frames serious communication.

ramayan::1814.verse_sanskrit: अयोध्याधिपते वीर वैदेहो मिथिलाधिप: । । 17013 । । स त्वां द्रष्टुं व्यवसितस्सोपाध्यायपुरोहितम् ।
ramayan::1814.verse_hindi: O Heroic lord of Ayodhya, Janaka, the lord of Mithila desires to see you along with preceptors and priest.
ramayan::1814.english_translation: O heroic lord of Ayodhya, the king of Mithila desires to see you along with your preceptors and priests.
ramayan::1814.translation_literal: अयोध्याधिपते (O lord of Ayodhya) / वीर (heroic) / वैदेहः (the king of Videha) / मिथिलाधिपः (lord of Mithila) / सः (he) / त्वाम् (you) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / व्यवसितः (has resolved) / सः (he) / उपाध्याय-पुरोहितम् (with preceptors and priests)
ramayan::1814.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1814.essence: Two royal courts are now moving toward one another.
ramayan::1814.simple_meaning: Janaka, the king of Mithila, wants to meet Dasaratha with his teachers and priests.
ramayan::1814.simple_insight: A formal summons can carry the weight of kingdoms meeting each other.
ramayan::1814.detailed_meaning: A messenger has reached Dasaratha's camp near Mithila. After the formal greeting, he delivers Janaka's request: the king of Mithila wants to see the lord of Ayodhya with his learned attendants. The verse simply moves the meeting forward.
ramayan::1814.modern_relevance: A message arrives saying the other side is ready to meet, and suddenly the room changes. Before the conversation begins, the relationship has already shifted.
ramayan::1814.insight: It advances the plot by signaling the formal meeting between two royal houses.

ramayan::1815.verse_sanskrit: मंत्रिश्रेष्ठवच श्शृत्वा राजा सर्षिगणस्तदा । । 17014 । । सबंधुरगमत्तत्र जनको यत्र वर्तते ।
ramayan::1815.verse_hindi: King Dasaratha on hearing the words of the best of the counsellors reached the place
ramayan::1815.english_translation: On hearing the words of the chief counsellor, King Dasaratha went there with the sages and his relatives to where Janaka was staying.
ramayan::1815.translation_literal: मंत्रिश्रेष्ठवचः (the words of the best counsellor) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / राजा (the king) / सर्षिगणः (with the group of sages) / तदा (then) / सबंधुः (with relatives) / अगमत् (went) / तत्र (there) / जनकः (Janaka) / यत्र (where) / वर्तते (is staying)
ramayan::1815.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1815.essence: The king moves straight to the meeting.
ramayan::1815.simple_meaning: Dasaratha goes to Janaka after hearing the counsellor’s message, bringing sages and relatives with him.
ramayan::1815.simple_insight: A decision is made, and the king moves at once.
ramayan::1815.detailed_meaning: A messenger has brought Janaka’s request. Dasaratha does not delay; he sets out with sages and family to meet the Mithila king. The verse simply moves the scene from message to meeting.
ramayan::1815.modern_relevance: You get the call, gather the right people, and go. Some moments ask for movement, not debate.
ramayan::1815.insight: It marks the king’s immediate response to an invitation, not a teaching about how to live.

ramayan::1816.verse_sanskrit: स राजा मन्त्रिसहित स्सोपाध्याय: सबान्धव: । । 17015 । । वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठो वैदेहमिदमब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::1816.verse_hindi: The king (Dasaratha), skilled in speech, accompanied by counsellors and kins said to Janaka,the lord of the Videhas:
ramayan::1816.english_translation: King Dasharatha, skilled in speech, accompanied by counsellors, teachers, and relatives, spoke to Janaka, lord of the Videhas:
ramayan::1816.translation_literal: स (that) / राजा (king) / मन्त्रिसहितः (with counsellors) / स उपाध्यायः (with teachers) / सबान्धवः (with relatives) / वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः (the best among speakers) / वैदेहम् (to the Videha king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::1816.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1816.essence: The king is about to speak; this verse only opens the moment.
ramayan::1816.simple_meaning: Dasharatha arrives with his court and begins speaking to Janaka. The verse only sets up the conversation that follows.
ramayan::1816.simple_insight: Some verses are the doorway, not the message itself.
ramayan::1816.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha has come to Mithila with his ministers, priests, teachers, and relatives. He is about to speak to Janaka, but this line only introduces the speech. The real teaching comes in the verses that follow.
ramayan::1816.modern_relevance: You open a difficult conversation with all the right people beside you, then pause before the first real sentence.
ramayan::1816.insight: It frames the scene without delivering a teaching, so the reader waits for the actual exchange.

ramayan::1817.verse_sanskrit: विदितं ते महाराज इक्ष्वाकुकुलदैवतम् । । 17016 । । वक्ता सर्वेषु कृत्येषु वसिष्ठो भगवानृषि: ।
ramayan::1817.verse_hindi: O Great king venerable Vasishta is the spiritual protector of the Ikshvakus race and it is known that for all ceremonies he is our spokesman.
ramayan::1817.english_translation: O great king, venerable Vasishta is the spiritual protector of the Ikshvaku line, and for every ceremony he is our spokesman.
ramayan::1817.translation_literal: विदितम् (known) / ते (to you) / महाराज (O great king) / इक्ष्वाकुकुलदैवतम् (the family protector of the Ikshvaku line) / वक्ता (speaker) / सर्वेषु (in all) / कृत्येषु (in duties/rites) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / भगवान् (venerable) / ऋषिः (sage)
ramayan::1817.speaker: Dasaratha
ramayan::1817.essence: Vasishta is the Ikshvaku family's trusted voice in sacred matters.
ramayan::1817.simple_meaning: Dasaratha tells Janaka that Vasishta is the revered family guide of the Ikshvaku line and the one who speaks for them in ritual matters.
ramayan::1817.simple_insight: Some people carry a whole family’s authority with calm dignity.
ramayan::1817.detailed_meaning: Dasaratha has arrived with his ministers and relatives to speak with Janaka. Before the marriage negotiations begin, he introduces Vasishta as the trusted sage who represents the Ikshvaku house in sacred matters. It is a formal, preparatory line, not the main teaching.
ramayan::1817.modern_relevance: Before a major family ceremony, everyone waits for the elder who knows the customs, can speak clearly, and keeps the moment from turning chaotic.
ramayan::1817.insight: It shows how legitimacy in public life often rests on trusted tradition and clear representation.

ramayan::1818.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञातस्सह सर्वैर्महर्षिभि: । । 17017 । । एष वक्ष्यति धर्मात्मा वसिष्ठो मे यथाक्रमम् ।
ramayan::1818.verse_hindi: Having been permitted by Viswamitra, along with all maharshis virtuous Vasishta will tell you in detail about my race.
ramayan::1818.english_translation: Having been permitted by Viswamitra, along with all the great sages, virtuous Vasishta will tell you in detail about my race.
ramayan::1818.translation_literal: विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञातः (permitted by Viswamitra) / सह (along with) / सर्वैः (all) / महर्षिभिः (great sages) / एषः (this one) / वक्ष्यति (will speak) / धर्मात्मा (virtuous, righteous) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / मे (my) / यथाक्रमम् (in due order, in detail)
ramayan::1818.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::1818.essence: The right person should speak, in the right order.
ramayan::1818.simple_meaning: Dasharatha says that Vasishta, approved by Viswamitra and the other sages, will explain his lineage in proper order.
ramayan::1818.simple_insight: Some truths are best carried forward by the right witness, in the right order.
ramayan::1818.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Dasharatha has come with ministers, relatives, and sages to speak about Rama's marriage. Before the formal account begins, he points to Vasishta, the royal priest, as the one who will explain the Ikshvaku lineage clearly and properly.
ramayan::1818.modern_relevance: You hand the meeting to the one person who knows the history, the rules, and the stakes. Not every moment needs a speech from you; sometimes it needs the right voice.
ramayan::1818.insight: It shifts attention from self-assertion to orderly transmission through an authorised guide.

ramayan::1819.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा नरश्रेष्ठे राज्ञां मध्ये महात्मनाम् । । 17018 । । तूष्णींभूते दशरथे वसिष्ठो भगवानृषि: । उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो वैदेहं सपुरोधसम् । । 17019 । ।
ramayan::1819.verse_hindi: Having said this amidst the best of men and the most distinguished among kings, Dasaratha remained silent. Then Vasishta, the venerable sage, wellversed in speech
ramayan::1819.english_translation: Having said this amidst the best of men and the most distinguished among kings, Dasaratha remained silent. Then Vasishta, the venerable sage, well-versed in speech, addressed Vaideha and his priest.
ramayan::1819.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / नरश्रेष्ठे (among the best of men) / राज्ञां (of kings) / मध्ये (in the midst) / महात्मनाम् (of the great-souled) / तूष्णींभूते (having become silent) / दशरथे (Dasharatha) / वसिष्ठः (Vasishta) / भगवान् (venerable) / ऋषिः (sage) / उवाच (spoke) / वाक्यज्ञः (knower of speech) / वैदेहम् (to the Vaideha) / सपुरोधसम् (together with his priest)
ramayan::1819.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1819.essence: The scene shifts from silence into Vasishta's speech.
ramayan::1819.simple_meaning: Dasharatha falls silent, and Vasishta begins speaking to Janaka and his priest.
ramayan::1819.simple_insight: Some moments are only a doorway; the real teaching comes next.
ramayan::1819.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, after the opening exchange among kings and sages, Dasharatha falls silent. Vasishta, the family priest and guiding elder of Ayodhya, then turns to Janaka and the assembled company. This verse simply moves the scene into the next speech.
ramayan::1819.modern_relevance: You can feel the room settle after someone finishes speaking, and everyone waits for the elder to begin. This verse is that pause before the real explanation starts.
ramayan::1819.insight: It marks a transition, not a teaching. The verse prepares you for the next argument or genealogy.

ramayan::1820.verse_sanskrit: अव्यक्तप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य अव्यय: । तस्मान्मरीचि स्संजज्ञे मरीचे: काश्यप: सुत: । । 17020 । ।
ramayan::1820.verse_hindi: From the unmanifest was born the eternal, the constant, the imperishable Brahma. To him was born Marichi and to Marichi, Kasyapa.
ramayan::1820.english_translation: From the unmanifest was born the eternal, the constant, the imperishable Brahma. From him was born Marichi, and from Marichi, Kasyapa.
ramayan::1820.translation_literal: अव्यक्तप्रभवः (born from the unmanifest) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / शाश्वतः (eternal) / नित्यः (constant) / अव्ययः (imperishable) / तस्मात् (from him) / मरीचिः (Marichi) / संजज्ञे (was born) / मरीचेः (from Marichi) / काश्यपः (Kasyapa) / सुतः (son)
ramayan::1820.speaker: Vasishta
ramayan::1820.essence: Lineage here is presented as a descent from the unmanifest source.
ramayan::1820.simple_meaning: The verse traces a sacred lineage backward to the unmanifest source, then forward through Brahma, Marichi, and Kasyapa.
ramayan::1820.simple_insight: Some beginnings are older than names. The line of descent points back to a reality beyond form.
ramayan::1820.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is explaining the origin of Rama's solar lineage to Dasaratha and the gathered sages. He begins not with a king, but with the cosmic source: the unmanifest, eternal Brahma, then the chain of descent through Marichi and Kasyapa.
ramayan::1820.modern_relevance: When you ask where your family story really began, the answer is never just a name on a document. Every inheritance reaches back through layers you did not choose.
ramayan::1820.insight: It shifts attention from personal identity to the larger chain of origin behind it.

ramayan::1821.verse_sanskrit: विवस्वान् काश्यपाज्जज्ञे मनुर्वैवस्वत स्स्मृत: । मनु: प्रजापति: पूर्वमिक्ष्वाकुस्तु मनोस्सुत: । । 17021 । ।
ramayan::1821.verse_hindi: Kasyapa begot Vivasvan and Vivasvan, Manu. Ikshavaku was the son of Manu
ramayan::1821.english_translation: Kasyapa begot Vivasvan, Vivasvan begot Manu, and Manu's son was Ikshvaku.
ramayan::1821.translation_literal: विवस्वान् (Vivasvan) / काश्यपात् (from Kashyapa) / जज्ञे (was born) / मनुः (Manu) / वैवस्वतः (son of Vivasvan) / स्मृतः (known as) / मनुः (Manu) / प्रजापतिः (progenitor) / पूर्वम् (earlier) / इक्ष्वाकुः (Ikshvaku) / तु (and) / मनोः (of Manu) / सुतः (son)
ramayan::1821.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1821.essence: Rama's house is shown as part of an ancient royal line.
ramayan::1821.simple_meaning: A royal lineage is being traced from Kashyapa to Vivasvan to Manu to Ikshvaku.
ramayan::1821.simple_insight: Some families are introduced through ancestry, not action.
ramayan::1821.detailed_meaning: Vasishta is explaining the ancient solar line to Dasaratha. He traces the ancestry from Kashyapa to Vivasvan, then to Manu, then to Ikshvaku, preparing the ground for Rama's royal inheritance rather than giving a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1821.modern_relevance: A family tree gets read out at a wedding or memorial, and suddenly every name matters because it explains how the present came to be.
ramayan::1821.insight: It shifts attention from the individual king to the long line of inheritance behind him.

ramayan::1822.verse_sanskrit: तमिक्ष्वाकुमयोध्यायां राजानं विद्धि पूर्वकम् । इक्ष्वाकोस्तु सुतश्श्रीमान् कुक्षिरित्येव विश्रुत: । । 17022 । ।
ramayan::1822.verse_hindi: It may be noted that Ikshvaku was the first ancestral king of Ayodhya whose son was the wellknown, glorious Kukshi.
ramayan::1822.english_translation: Know that Ikshvaku was the first ancestral king of Ayodhya. His glorious son was Kukshi, who became well known.
ramayan::1822.translation_literal: तम् (that) / इक्ष्वाकुम् (Ikshvaku) / अयोध्यायाम् (in Ayodhya) / राजानम् (king) / विद्धि (know) / पूर्वकम् (first/earliest) । / इक्ष्वाकोः (of Ikshvaku) / तु (indeed) / सुतः (son) / श्रीमान् (glorious) / कुक्षिः (Kukshi) / इति (thus) / एव (indeed) / विश्रुतः (well known)
ramayan::1822.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1822.essence: A royal line is being named, not a lesson being given.
ramayan::1822.simple_meaning: Ikshvaku was the first ancestral king of Ayodhya, and his famous son was Kukshi.
ramayan::1822.simple_insight: Some lines simply place you in the lineage before the story moves on.
ramayan::1822.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing the royal line of Ayodhya backward through ancient kings. Ikshvaku stands as the founding ancestor in this chain, and Kukshi is named as his son. The verse is a link in the genealogy, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::1822.modern_relevance: A family tree gets opened at a reunion, and everyone leans in for the names before anyone tells the real story. This verse is that kind of pause.
ramayan::1822.insight: It teaches you to read the epic's lineage as part of its world-building, not its message.

ramayan::1823.verse_sanskrit: कुक्षेरथात्मज: श्रीमान् विकुक्षिरुदपद्यत । विकुक्षेस्तु महातेजा बाण: पुत्र: प्रतापवान् । । 17023 । ।
ramayan::1823.verse_hindi: Prosperous Vikukshi was Kukshis son, who brought forth brilliant and powerful Bana.
ramayan::1823.english_translation: Prosperous Vikukshi was Kukshi's son, who fathered brilliant and powerful Bana.
ramayan::1823.translation_literal: कुक्षेः (of Kukshi) / अथ (then) / आत्मजः (son) / श्रीमान् (prosperous) / विकुक्षिः (Vikukshi) / उदपद्यत (was born) / विकुक्षेः (of Vikukshi) / तु (and) / महातेजाः (brilliant) / बाणः (Bana) / पुत्रः (son) / प्रतापवान् (powerful) (was born)
ramayan::1823.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1823.essence: Rama's story rises from a long chain of kings.
ramayan::1823.simple_meaning: Vikukshi was born to Kukshi, and Bana was born to Vikukshi. It continues the list of early kings in Rama's lineage.
ramayan::1823.simple_insight: Great lineages are built one generation at a time.
ramayan::1823.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing the royal ancestry of Ayodhya before Rama's birth. After naming Ikshvaku and Kukshi, he moves on to Vikukshi and then Bana, continuing the unbroken chain of kings that leads toward Rama.
ramayan::1823.modern_relevance: A family tree on paper can look dry, but it carries the weight of everything that came before you. Your name sits inside a long chain of choices, inheritances, and responsibilities.
ramayan::1823.insight: It places Rama within a remembered royal line, not as an isolated figure.

ramayan::1824.verse_sanskrit: बाणस्य तु महातेजा अनरण्य: प्रतापवान् । अनरण्यात्पृथुर्जज्ञे त्रिशङ्कुस्तु पृथोस्सुत: । । 17024 । ।
ramayan::1824.verse_hindi: Banas son was the most brilliant and valiant Anaranya whose son Pruthu was succeeded by Trisanku.
ramayan::1824.english_translation: Bana's son was the most brilliant and valiant Anaranya, whose son was Pruthu, and Pruthu's son was Trisanku.
ramayan::1824.translation_literal: बाणस्य (of Bana) / तु (indeed) / महातेजा (most brilliant) / अनरण्यः (Anaranya) / प्रतापवान् (valiant) / अनरण्यात् (from Anaranya) / पृथुः (Pruthu) / जज्ञे (was born) / त्रिशङ्कुः (Trisanku) / तु (indeed) / पृथोः (of Pruthu) / सुतः (son)
ramayan::1824.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1824.essence: A royal lineage is being traced, not a lesson being taught.
ramayan::1824.simple_meaning: This is a genealogy verse listing the descendants of Ikshvaku's line, naming Bana, Anaranya, Pruthu, and Trisanku.
ramayan::1824.simple_insight: It reminds you that great stories are rooted in long family lines, not isolated moments.
ramayan::1824.detailed_meaning: Valmiki continues the royal genealogy of Ayodhya's ancient line. After naming Bana, he lists Anaranya, then Pruthu, then Trisanku. The verse serves as a bridge in the lineage, not a teaching or turning point.
ramayan::1824.modern_relevance: You're reading a family tree in an old record, not a dramatic scene. It matters because the epic keeps anchoring kings, choices, and later events in a remembered line of inheritance.
ramayan::1824.insight: It gives context by placing later rulers inside a continuous ancestral chain.

ramayan::1825.verse_hindi: Trisankus famous son was Dundumara also known as Yuvanashva whose son was king Mandhata.
ramayan::1825.english_translation: Trisanku's famous son was Dundumara, also known as Yuvanashva, and his son was King Mandhata.
ramayan::1825.translation_literal: त्रिशङ्कोः (of Trisanku) / अभवत् (was born) / पुत्रः (son) / दुन्दुमारः (Dundumara) / महायशाः (famous, greatly renowned) / युवनाश्व-सुतः (son of Yuvanashva) / तु (indeed) / आसीत् (was) / मान्धाता (Mandhata) / पृथिवीपतिः (lord of the earth, king)
ramayan::1825.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1825.essence: A king's name matters here as a link in an unbroken line.
ramayan::1825.simple_meaning: This line continues the royal genealogy, naming Trisanku's son and then Mandhata as the next ruler in the line.
ramayan::1825.simple_insight: Some verses simply place a person in a long chain of inheritance and history.
ramayan::1825.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing the solar dynasty step by step. After Trisanku comes Dundumara, also called Yuvanashva, and then Mandhata. The verse is a link in the lineage, not a teaching or turning point.
ramayan::1825.modern_relevance: A family tree on paper can feel dry, but it carries memory, identity, and inheritance. Sometimes the only thing a verse does is remind you that you come from a long line of lives before yours.
ramayan::1825.insight: It shifts attention from drama to lineage, showing how epic history is built through succession.

ramayan::1826.verse_sanskrit: मान्धातुस्तु सुत श्श्रीमान् सुसन्धिरुदपद्यत । सुसन्धेरपि पुत्रौ द्वौ ध्रुवसन्धि: प्रसेनजित् । । 17026 । ।
ramayan::1826.verse_hindi: Mandhatas son was prosperous Susandhi who brought forth two sons Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit.
ramayan::1826.english_translation: Mandhata's son was the prosperous Susandhi, who gave birth to two sons, Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit.
ramayan::1826.translation_literal: मान्धातुस्तु (of Mandhata) / सुतः (son) / श्रीमान् (prosperous) / सुसन्धिः (Susandhi) / उदपद्यत (was born) / सुसन्धेः (of Susandhi) / अपि (also) / पुत्रौ (two sons) / द्वौ (two) / ध्रुवसन्धिः (Dhruvasandhi) / प्रसेनजित् (Prasenajit)
ramayan::1826.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1826.essence: The royal line continues through another generation.
ramayan::1826.simple_meaning: Mandhata's line continues through Susandhi, who had two sons named Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit.
ramayan::1826.simple_insight: Some verses simply keep the lineage moving, showing how one royal house flows into the next.
ramayan::1826.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing the solar dynasty before Rama's line appears. After Mandhata comes Susandhi, and from him come Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit. The verse is a genealogical link, not a teaching or turning point.

ramayan::1827.verse_sanskrit: यशस्वी ध्रुवसन्धेस्तु भरतो नाम नामत: । भरतात्तु महातेजा असितो नाम जातवान् । । 17027 । ।
ramayan::1827.verse_hindi: To Dhruvasandhi was born the wellknown Bharata who begot the vigorous Asita.
ramayan::1827.english_translation: To Dhruvasandhi was born the wellknown Bharata who begot the vigorous Asita.
ramayan::1827.translation_literal: यशस्वी (well-known / famous) / ध्रुवसन्धेः (of Dhruvasandhi) / तु (indeed) / भरतः (Bharata) / नाम (by name) / नामतः (by name) / भरतात् (from Bharata) / तु (and) / महातेजाः (very radiant / vigorous) / असितः (Asita) / नाम (by name) / जातवान् (was born)
ramayan::1827.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1827.essence: A royal name is placed into the ancestral chain.
ramayan::1827.simple_meaning: Bharata, son of Dhruvasandhi, had a son named Asita. The verse is part of a royal genealogy, not a teaching.
ramayan::1827.simple_insight: Sometimes a verse simply places a person in the long line of a family.
ramayan::1827.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is listing the kings in Rama’s ancestral line. After Dhruvasandhi comes Bharata, and from Bharata comes Asita. The passage is building lineage, not making a moral point.

ramayan::1828.verse_sanskrit: यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शत्रव: । हैहयास्तालजंघाश्च शूराश्च शशिबिन्दव: । । 17028 । ।
ramayan::1828.verse_hindi: Valiant kings belonging to the races of the Haihayas, Talaiangha, and Sasibindus   became  the enemies to Asita.
ramayan::1828.english_translation: Valiant kings of the Haihaya, Talajangha, and Shashibindu lines became enemies of Asita.
ramayan::1828.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / एते (these) / प्रतिराजानः (hostile kings) / उदपद्यन्त (arose) / शत्रवः (enemies) / हैहयाः (the Haihayas) / तालजंघाः (the Talajanghas) / च (and) / शूराः (the valiant ones) / च (and) / शशिबिन्दवः (the Shashibindus)
ramayan::1828.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1828.essence: Multiple enemies gather before the fall is even named.
ramayan::1828.simple_meaning: Powerful enemy kings arose against Asita from several royal lineages.
ramayan::1828.simple_insight: Sometimes a ruler is surrounded before the real defeat even begins.
ramayan::1828.detailed_meaning: The genealogy has reached Asita, son of Bharata. Now Valmiki notes that several fierce royal houses rose up against him. This verse is only a bridge into Asita's defeat and exile in the next line.
ramayan::1828.modern_relevance: A problem can start as a cluster of rivals, not one obvious opponent. By the time you notice the pressure, it has already spread across the whole field.
ramayan::1828.insight: It sets up the conflict that will push Asita out of power.

ramayan::1829.verse_sanskrit: तांस्तु स प्रतियुध्यन् वै युद्धे राजा प्रवासित: । हिमवन्तमुपागम्य भृगुप्रस्रवणेऽवसत् । । 17029 । । असितोऽल्पबलो राजा मन्त्रिभिस्सहितस्तदा ।
ramayan::1829.verse_hindi: The king Asita who was a weakling was defeated in the conflict against the kings and was exiled. Along with his counsellors he lived at on the Bhriguprasravana Himavat mountain.
ramayan::1829.english_translation: King Asita, though weak in battle, fought those kings and was driven into exile. With his ministers he then lived at Bhriguprasravana on Mount Himavat.
ramayan::1829.translation_literal: तांस्तु (those) / सः (he) / प्रतियुध्यन् (fighting back) / वै (indeed) / युद्धे (in battle) / राजा (the king) / प्रवासितः (driven into exile) / हिमवन्तम् (to the Himalaya) / उपागम्य (having gone) / भृगुप्रस्रवणे (at Bhriguprasravana) / अवसत् (dwelt) / असितः (Asita) / अल्पबलः (weak in strength) / राजा (the king) / मन्त्रिभिः (with ministers) / सहितः (accompanied) / तदा (then)
ramayan::1829.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1829.essence: Defeat sends him away, but it does not end the line.
ramayan::1829.simple_meaning: Asita fought his enemies, lost, and was forced into exile. He then lived in the Himalayas with his ministers.
ramayan::1829.simple_insight: Sometimes defeat does not end the story; it only changes where the story continues.
ramayan::1829.detailed_meaning: Asita, ancestor in the royal line, is defeated by stronger enemies and pushed out of his realm. He retreats with his ministers to a Himalayan refuge. The verse sets up the exile and family line that follow, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::1829.modern_relevance: You lose the post, the deal, the argument, and suddenly your old life is gone. What remains is where you go next, and who stays with you.
ramayan::1829.insight: It frames setback as a turning point, not a full stop.

ramayan::1830.verse_sanskrit: द्वे चास्य भार्ये गर्भिण्यौ बभूवतुरिति श्रुतम् । । 17030 । । एका गर्भविनाशाय सपत्न्यै सगरं ददौ ।
ramayan::1830.verse_hindi: It is said that his (Asitas) two wives were pregnant. One gave food mixed with poison to the other with the intention of destroying her embryo.
ramayan::1830.english_translation: It is said that his two wives were pregnant. One gave food mixed with poison to the other with the intention of destroying her embryo.
ramayan::1830.translation_literal: द्वे (two) / च (and) / अस्य (his) / भार्ये (two wives) / गर्भिण्यौ (pregnant) / बभूवतुः (were) / इति (thus) / श्रुतम् (it is heard) / एका (one) / गर्भविनाशाय (for destroying the embryo) / सपत्न्यै (to the co-wife) / सगरम् (poisoned food) / ददौ (gave)
ramayan::1830.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1830.essence: Jealousy inside a home can poison the next generation.
ramayan::1830.simple_meaning: His two wives were both pregnant, and one secretly gave the other poisoned food to harm the unborn child.
ramayan::1830.simple_insight: Jealousy can turn even motherhood into cruelty.
ramayan::1830.detailed_meaning: This is part of Asita’s troubled family story. After his defeat and exile, the focus shifts to his household, where rivalry between the two pregnant wives turns poisonous. The verse sets up the birth crisis that follows.
ramayan::1830.modern_relevance: A family group chat turns cold after one person feels overlooked, and suddenly every small message carries suspicion. Resentment grows quietly before it ever becomes open harm.
ramayan::1830.insight: It shows how rivalry can corrupt the most intimate bonds before anyone notices the damage.

ramayan::1831.verse_sanskrit: तत श्शैलवरं रम्यं बभूवाभिरतो मुनि: । । 17031 । । भार्गवश्च्यवनो नाम हिमवन्तमुपाश्रित: ।
ramayan::1831.verse_hindi: At that time Chyavana of the family of Bhrigu liked to stay at Himavat, the great, pleasant mountain.
ramayan::1831.english_translation: At that time, the sage Chyavana of the Bhrigu line took delight in the beautiful mountain of Himavat and lived there.
ramayan::1831.translation_literal: तत (then) / श्शैलवरम् (the best mountain) / रम्यम् (delightful) / बभूव (became) / अभिरतः (delighted) / मुनिः (sage) / भार्गवः (of the Bhrigu line) / च्यवनः (Chyavana) / नाम (named) / हिमवन्तम् (Himavat) / उपाश्रितः (having taken refuge in)
ramayan::1831.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1831.essence: The story pauses to place its next turning point.
ramayan::1831.simple_meaning: The sage Chyavana, from the Bhrigu lineage, settled on Mount Himavat and found it pleasing.
ramayan::1831.simple_insight: Some verses simply place the story in motion, showing where the next event will unfold.
ramayan::1831.detailed_meaning: After Asita is driven out and his family’s troubles are introduced, the scene shifts to Chyavana, a revered sage of the Bhrigu line, who takes up residence on Mount Himavat. The verse sets the location for the next development, where Kalindi will approach him.
ramayan::1831.modern_relevance: A story often begins with someone quietly choosing a place that will change everything. Before the big event, there is always a setting — a mountain, a room, a pause — where the next decision becomes possible.
ramayan::1831.insight: It teaches you to notice setup before climax: location, timing, and context shape what happens next.

ramayan::1832.verse_sanskrit: तत्रैका तु महाभागा भार्गवं देववर्चसम् । । 17032 । । ववन्दे पद्मपत्राक्षी काङ्क्षन्ती सुतमात्मन: ।
ramayan::1832.verse_hindi: That the lotuseyed and highly accomplished Kalindi, offered herself for a son to
ramayan::1832.english_translation: There, one highly fortunate, lotus-eyed woman bowed to the radiant descendant of Bhrigu, longing for a son of her own.
ramayan::1832.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / एका (one) / तु (indeed) / महाभागा (highly fortunate) / भार्गवम् (to the descendant of Bhrigu) / देववर्चसम् (radiant, resplendent) / ववन्दे (bowed) / पद्मपत्राक्षी (lotus-eyed) / काङ्क्षन्ती (longing for) / सुतम् (son) / आत्मनः (of her own)
ramayan::1832.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1832.essence: Wanting deeply can still begin with respect.
ramayan::1832.simple_meaning: Kalindi approaches the sage Chyavana with reverence, asking for a son of her own.
ramayan::1832.simple_insight: Deep longing can become humble enough to bow.
ramayan::1832.detailed_meaning: Chyavana is living in the Himalayas when Kalindi comes to him. She is not arguing or demanding; she bows first, carrying the ache of childlessness into a moment of reverence. The scene sets up her request for a son.
ramayan::1832.modern_relevance: You have wanted something for years, and you finally stand before someone who might help. Before the request comes the humility: you bow, because the longing is real.
ramayan::1832.insight: It shows desire meeting reverence, not entitlement.

ramayan::1833.verse_sanskrit: तमृषिं साऽभ्युपागम्य कालिंदी चाभ्यवादयत् । । 17033 । । स तामभ्यवदद्विप्र: पुत्रेप्सुं पुत्रजन्मनि ।
ramayan::1833.verse_hindi: Having approached the ascetic. Kalindi paid obeisance to him who said:
ramayan::1833.english_translation: Having approached the ascetic, Kalindi bowed to him. The learned sage then spoke to her, who longed for a son and was seeking the birth of a child.
ramayan::1833.translation_literal: तम् (that) / ऋषिम् (ascetic) / सा (she) / अभ्युपागम्य (having approached) / कालिंदी (Kalindi) / च (and) / अभ्यवादयत् (paid obeisance) / स (he) / ताम् (to her) / अभ्यवदत् (spoke) / द्विप्रः (the learned brahmin) / पुत्रेप्सुम् (one desiring a son) / पुत्रजन्मनि (regarding the birth of a son)
ramayan::1833.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1833.essence: A humble request opens the way for a blessing.
ramayan::1833.simple_meaning: Kalindi approaches the sage and bows to him. The sage responds to her longing for a child.
ramayan::1833.simple_insight: Some requests begin with humility before they can become fulfilled.
ramayan::1833.detailed_meaning: Kalindi has come to Chyavana on Mount Himavat, hoping for a son. She bows before the sage, and he answers her as a respectful seeker, setting up the blessing that follows in the next verse.
ramayan::1833.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying a private longing you can barely name. Before the answer comes, you have to stand there honestly and ask.
ramayan::1833.insight: It shows that asking rightly matters before receiving anything at all.

ramayan::1834.verse_sanskrit: तव कुक्षौ महाभागे सुपुत्रस्सुमहाबल: । । 17034 । । महावीर्यो महातेजा अचिरात्सञ्जनिष्यति । गरेण सहित श्श्रीमान् मा शुच: कमलेक्षणे । । 17035 । ।
ramayan::1834.verse_hindi: O Great lady a child of high prowess, lustre and virtues is growing in your womb. In a short time this glorious son carrying with him the poison (administered to you) will be born. O Lotuseyed lady, do not grieve.
ramayan::1834.english_translation: O great lady, a son of great strength, great brilliance, and great virtue is growing in your womb. Very soon, this glorious son, along with the poison you took, will be born. O lotus-eyed one, do not grieve.
ramayan::1834.translation_literal: तव (in your) / कुक्षौ (in the womb) / महाभागे (O fortunate one) / सुपुत्रः (a noble son) / सुमहाबलः (of very great strength) / महावीर्यः (of great prowess) / महातेजाः (of great brilliance) / अचिरात् (soon) / सञ्जनिष्यति (will be born) / गरेण (with poison) / सहितः (together with) / श्रीमान् (glorious) / मा (do not) / शुचः (grieve) / कमलेक्षणे (O lotus-eyed one)
ramayan::1834.speaker: Cyavana
ramayan::1834.essence: A feared beginning can still carry a strong and blessed outcome.
ramayan::1834.simple_meaning: A holy man tells Kalindi that her unborn son will be strong, brilliant, and virtuous, and that she should not grieve because the birth is near.
ramayan::1834.simple_insight: Even in pain and fear, reassurance can still reach the heart.
ramayan::1834.detailed_meaning: Kalindi has approached Cyavana seeking a child. He answers her with a blessing: the child already growing in her womb will be exceptional, and the poison she carries will not prevent the birth. The verse is part of a larger exchange, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::1834.modern_relevance: You are waiting for news after a frightening hospital visit, and someone finally says the outcome is not as dark as you feared.
ramayan::1834.insight: It shifts attention from panic to trust in what is already unfolding.

ramayan::1835.verse_sanskrit: च्यवनं तु नमस्कृत्य राजपुत्री पतिव्रता । पतिशोकातुरा तस्मात्पुत्रं देवी व्यजायत । । 17036 । ।
ramayan::1835.verse_hindi: This eldest queen who was a devoted wife, afflicted with sorrow due to loss of her
ramayan::1835.english_translation: The devoted princess bowed to Cyavana, and in grief for her husband she gave birth to that son.
ramayan::1835.translation_literal: च्यवनं (Cyavana) / तु (indeed) / नमस्कृत्य (having bowed) / राजपुत्री (the princess) / पतिव्रता (devoted to her husband) / पतिशोकातुरा (afflicted by sorrow for her husband) / तस्मात् (from that) / पुत्रम् (a son) / देवी (the lady) / व्यजायत (gave birth)
ramayan::1835.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1835.essence: Grief does not stop life; it can become the place life arrives.
ramayan::1835.simple_meaning: A faithful queen bows to the ascetic and, overwhelmed by grief for her husband, gives birth to a son.
ramayan::1835.simple_insight: Love and loss can shape the body itself, turning grief into new life.
ramayan::1835.detailed_meaning: Kalindi has sought out Cyavana after hearing that a son will be born to her. She bows before the sage, and in the shadow of her husband’s loss and sorrow, she bears the child who will matter to the story that follows.
ramayan::1835.modern_relevance: You keep functioning after heartbreak, even while something inside you is still mourning. Life does not wait for grief to finish before it asks you to continue.
ramayan::1835.insight: It shows how duty, sorrow, and new life can exist together in one moment.

ramayan::1836.verse_sanskrit: सपत्न्या तु गरस्तस्यै दत्तो गर्भजिघांसया । सह तेन गरेणैव जात: स सगरोऽभवत् । । 17037 । ।
ramayan::1836.verse_hindi: Since poison was given to her by  her rival queen with the intention of destroying the   embryo, the son was born with poison and so came to be known as Sagara.
ramayan::1836.english_translation: Since poison was given to her by her rival queen with the intention of destroying the embryo, the son was born with poison and so came to be known as Sagara.
ramayan::1836.translation_literal: सपत्न्या (by the rival queen) / तु (indeed) / गरः (poison) / तस्यै (to her) / दत्तः (was given) / गर्भजिघांसया (with the intent to destroy the embryo) / सह (together) / तेन (with that) / गरैः (poison) / एव (indeed) / जातः (born) / सः (he) / सगरः (Sagara) / अभवत् (became)
ramayan::1836.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1836.essence: What was meant to destroy him became his name.
ramayan::1836.simple_meaning: A rival queen tried to kill the unborn child by giving poison to the mother, but the child survived and was named Sagara because he was born with poison.
ramayan::1836.simple_insight: Even an attempt to destroy life can become part of its identity.
ramayan::1836.detailed_meaning: This is a brief genealogical detail in the line of Sagara. The verse explains how a rival queen’s poison failed to kill the unborn child and instead gave him his name, linking the child’s identity to the very danger meant to end him.
ramayan::1836.modern_relevance: A coworker tries to sabotage a project before it launches, but the launch still succeeds. Sometimes the thing meant to ruin you becomes part of the story people remember.
ramayan::1836.insight: It turns a family conflict into a naming story, showing how survival can redefine harm.

ramayan::1837.verse_sanskrit: सगरस्यासमञ्जस्तु असमञ्जात्तथांऽशुमान् । दिलीपोंऽशुमत: पुत्रो दिलीपस्य भगीरथ: । । 17038 । ।
ramayan::1837.verse_hindi: Asamanja was the son of Sagara and to him was born Anshuman. Dilipa was the son of Anshuman and father of Bhagiratha.
ramayan::1837.english_translation: Asamanja was the son of Sagara, and from Asamanja came Anshuman. Anshuman's son was Dilipa, and Dilipa's son was Bhagiratha.
ramayan::1837.translation_literal: सगरस्य (of Sagara) / असमञ्जः (Asamanja) / तु (indeed) / असमञ्जात् (from Asamanja) / तथा (thus) / अंशुमान् (Anshuman) / दिलीपः (Dilipa) / अंशुमतः (of Anshuman) / पुत्रः (son) / दिलीपस्य (of Dilipa) / भगीरथः (Bhagiratha)
ramayan::1837.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1837.essence: Bhagiratha’s greatness is rooted in a long ancestral line.
ramayan::1837.simple_meaning: This verse lists the royal lineage from Sagara to Bhagiratha: Sagara, Asamanja, Anshuman, Dilipa, and Bhagiratha.
ramayan::1837.simple_insight: Some verses simply preserve the chain that makes the story possible.
ramayan::1837.detailed_meaning: Valmiki pauses the story to trace the Solar dynasty’s line from Sagara through Asamanja, Anshuman, and Dilipa to Bhagiratha. It is a genealogical bridge, not a teaching verse, preparing the reader for the later greatness of Bhagiratha.
ramayan::1837.modern_relevance: A family tree on a funeral card, a name passed down in a ceremony, a child asking who came before them — some moments matter because they place a life inside a longer line.
ramayan::1837.insight: It shifts attention from the individual figure to the ancestral chain behind him.

ramayan::1838.verse_sanskrit: भगीरथात्ककुत्स्थश्च ककुत्स्थस्य रघुस्सुत: । रघोस्तु पुत्रस्तेजस्वी प्रवृद्ध: पुरुषादक: । । 17039 । । कल्माषपादो ह्यभवत्तस्माज्जातस्तु शंखण: ।
ramayan::1838.verse_hindi: Bhagiratha begot Kakustha whose son was Raghu. Powerful Pravriddha was Raghus son. He became Purushadaka (cannibal), on the curse of Vasistha. He grasped water in order to retaliate Vasishta but was prevented by  his wife. The water fell on his feet and he came to be known as Kalmashapada (feet polluted with water). Samkhana was born to him.
ramayan::1838.english_translation: Bhagiratha begot Kakustha, whose son was Raghu. Raghu's son was the powerful Pravriddha, who became known as Purushadaka after Vasistha's curse. He tried to seize water in anger, but his wife stopped him; the water fell on his feet, and he came to be called Kalmashapada. Samkhana was born to him.
ramayan::1838.translation_literal: भगीरथात् (from Bhagiratha) / ककुत्स्थः (Kakustha) / च (and) / ककुत्स्थस्य (of Kakustha) / रघुः (Raghu) / सुतः (son) / रघोः (of Raghu) / तु (indeed) / पुत्रः (son) / तेजस्वी (powerful) / प्रवृद्धः (Pravriddha) / पुरुषादकः (Purushadaka, man-eater) / कल्माषपादः (Kalmashapada) / हि (indeed) / अभवत् (became) / तस्मात् (from him) / जातः (born) / तु (and) / शंखणः (Samkhana)
ramayan::1838.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1838.essence: Lineage survives, but one cursed moment can redefine a name.
ramayan::1838.simple_meaning: This is a genealogy line: Bhagiratha's descendants are named, and one ancestor is described as cursed and renamed after a strange incident.
ramayan::1838.simple_insight: Sometimes a family line is remembered not just for birth, but for the turning points that marked it.
ramayan::1838.detailed_meaning: Valmiki continues the royal genealogy of Rama's line, moving from Bhagiratha through Kakustha and Raghu to Pravriddha. In the middle of the list, one ancestor's curse and strange act explain how he received the name Kalmashapada. The verse mainly preserves lineage, not teaching.
ramayan::1838.modern_relevance: A family tree on old paper can suddenly carry a story of shame, curse, and renaming in one line. Some names survive because a moment changed how everyone remembered a person.
ramayan::1838.insight: It keeps the dynasty's succession intact while showing how reputation can become part of identity.

ramayan::1839.verse_sanskrit: सुदर्शन: शङ्घणस्य अग्निवर्ण स्सुदर्शनात् । । 17040 । । शीघ्रगस्त्वग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगस्य मरु स्सुत: । मरो: प्रशुश्रुकस्त्वासीदम्बरीष: प्रशुश्रृकात् । । 17041 । ।
ramayan::1839.verse_hindi: Sudarsana was the son of Samkhana. His son was Agnivarna. To Agnivarna was  born Sighraga and to Sighraga, Maru. To Maru, was born Prasusruka and to Prasrusuka, Ambarisha.
ramayan::1839.english_translation: Sudarsana was the son of Samkhana. His son was Agnivarna. To Agnivarna was born Sighraga and to Sighraga, Maru. To Maru was born Prasusruka, and to Prasusruka, Ambarisha.
ramayan::1839.translation_literal: सुदर्शनः (Sudarsana) / शङ्घणस्य (of Samkhana) / अग्निवर्णः (Agnivarna) / सुदर्शनात् (from Sudarsana) / शीघ्रगः (Sighraga) / तु (indeed) / अग्निवर्णस्य (of Agnivarna) / शीघ्रगस्य (of Sighraga) / मरुः (Maru) / सुतः (son) / मरोः (of Maru) / प्रशुश्रुकः (Prasusruka) / तु (indeed) / आसीत् (was) / अम्बरीषः (Ambarisha) / प्रशुश्रृकात् (from Prasusruka)
ramayan::1839.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::1839.essence: A royal line is being carefully preserved.
ramayan::1839.simple_meaning: This is a genealogy list, naming one king after another in a royal line.
ramayan::1839.simple_insight: Some verses simply preserve the chain of inheritance that holds a kingdom together.
ramayan::1839.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is tracing the solar royal lineage through a sequence of kings: Sudarsana, Agnivarna, Sighraga, Maru, Prasusruka, and Ambarisha. The verse serves as a bridge in the genealogy, not a teaching or dramatic moment.
