ramayan::7028.translation_literal: ते (they) / तु (indeed) / इदानीम् (now) / जनस्थाने (in Janasthana) / वसमानाः (dwelling) / महाबलाः (very powerful) / सङ्गताः (assembled, met) / परमायत्ताः (fully prepared, dependent on) / रामेण (with Rama) / सह (together, with) / संयुगे (in battle) / नानाप्रहरणोपेताः (equipped with many weapons) / खरप्रमुखराक्षसाः (the demons led by Khara)
ramayan::7028.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7028.essence: The battle becomes real the moment both sides meet.
ramayan::7028.simple_meaning: Khara's powerful demons, armed and ready in Janasthana, came together to face Rama in battle.
ramayan::7028.simple_insight: Sometimes the turning point is simply when both sides finally meet.
ramayan::7028.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Khara's armed forces gather and close in on Rama. The verse is not teaching yet; it is the tense setup before violence breaks open in the next line.
ramayan::7028.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the argument starts. Everyone knows the issue is no longer avoidable; the two sides have finally come face to face.
ramayan::7028.insight: It marks the moment conflict becomes direct and unavoidable.

ramayan::7029.verse_sanskrit: तेन सञ्जातरोषेण रामेण रणमूर्धनि । अनुक्त्वा परुषं किञ्चिच्छरैर्व्यापारितं धनुः । । 3367 । ।
ramayan::7029.verse_hindi: With his wrath generated, Rama, without even speaking anything, used his bow and the arrows.
ramayan::7029.english_translation: With anger aroused, Rama, on the battlefield, said nothing harsh and used his bow and arrows.
ramayan::7029.translation_literal: तेन (by that) / सञ्जातरोषेण (with anger arisen) / रामेण (by Rama) / रणमूर्धनि (on the battlefield) / अनुक्त्वा (without speaking) / परुषं (harsh words) / किञ्चिच् (anything) / शरैः (with arrows) / व्यापारितं (used, employed) / धनुः (bow)
ramayan::7029.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7029.essence: Anger need not become cruelty; it can become action.
ramayan::7029.simple_meaning: Rama became angry in battle, but he did not insult anyone. He answered with his bow and arrows instead of harsh words.
ramayan::7029.simple_insight: Strength can stay clean when anger does not turn into speech.
ramayan::7029.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Rama faces Khara's forces. The fighting has begun, but this line focuses on Rama's restraint: he does not waste his fury in abuse. He channels it straight into action, setting up the slaughter that follows.
ramayan::7029.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in front of everyone, and the first rush is to snap back. This verse points to a different power: let action answer without letting anger make you cruel.
ramayan::7029.insight: It shifts anger away from verbal harm and into disciplined action.

ramayan::7030.verse_sanskrit: चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसामुग्रतेजसाम् । निहतानि शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मानुषेण पदातिना । । 3368 । ।
ramayan::7030.verse_hindi: Being a human being who fought on foot, he killed fourteen thousand ferocious demons with his sharp arrows.
ramayan::7030.english_translation: Being a human being who fought on foot, he killed fourteen thousand ferocious demons with his sharp arrows.
ramayan::7030.translation_literal: चतुर्दश (fourteen) / सहस्राणि (thousands) / रक्षसाम् (of demons) / उग्रतेजसाम् (of fierce power) / निहतानि (were killed) / शरैः (with arrows) / तीक्ष्णैः (sharp) / मानुषेण (by a human) / पदातिना (on foot)
ramayan::7030.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7030.essence: One man on foot brought down an army.
ramayan::7030.simple_meaning: Rama, fighting as a man on foot, destroyed fourteen thousand fierce demons with sharp arrows.
ramayan::7030.simple_insight: Great strength can live inside ordinary human form.
ramayan::7030.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Rama has already entered battle against Khara and his forces. This verse measures the scale of the slaughter: a lone man on foot cuts down fourteen thousand fierce demons. It is part of the larger battle account, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7030.modern_relevance: It belongs to the kind of day when one person carries a burden meant for many and keeps going anyway.
ramayan::7030.insight: It underscores the overwhelming force of Rama's response before the battle's final names are given.

ramayan::7031.verse_sanskrit: खरश्च निहतस्सङ्ख्ये दूषणश्च निपातितः । हतश्च त्रिशिराश्चापि निर्भया दण्डकाः कृताः । । 3369 । ।
ramayan::7031.verse_hindi: Khara, Dusana and Trisira were killed in war.The residents of Dandaka forest are rendered safe and fearless.
ramayan::7031.english_translation: Khara, Dusana, and Trisira were killed in battle. The people of Dandaka forest were made safe and fearless.
ramayan::7031.translation_literal: खरः (Khara) / च (and) / निहतः (killed) / सङ्ख्ये (in battle) / दूषणः (Dushana) / च (and) / निपातितः (laid low) / हतः (killed) / च (and) / त्रिशिराः (Trisira) / च (and) / अपि (also) / निर्भयाः (fearless) / दण्डकाः (the people of Dandaka) / कृताः (made)
ramayan::7031.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7031.essence: The defeat of violent power restores safety to the land.
ramayan::7031.simple_meaning: Khara, Dushana, and Trisira are slain, and the people of Dandaka are left safe and unafraid.
ramayan::7031.simple_insight: When violence ends, fear can leave with it.
ramayan::7031.detailed_meaning: After Rama's fury cuts down Khara, Dushana, and Trisira, the verse notes the wider effect: the Dandaka forest is no longer under terror. It is a battlefield result, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7031.insight: It closes the battle’s immediate consequence: the threat is removed and the forest can breathe again.

ramayan::7032.verse_sanskrit: पित्रा निरस्तः क्रुद्धेन सभार्यः क्षीणजीवितः । स हन्ता तस्य सैन्यस्य रामः क्षत्रियपांसनः । । 33610 । ।
ramayan::7032.verse_hindi: Rama, a victim of his fathers anger, banished into the forest with his wife, a shortlived mortal and a calumny on the kshatriyas has killed the army of demons.
ramayan::7032.english_translation: Rama, driven out by his angry father, exiled with his wife and thought to be short-lived, has slain that army of demons.
ramayan::7032.translation_literal: पित्रा (by father) / निरस्तः (cast out) / क्रुद्धेन (by the angry one) / सभार्यः (together with wife) / क्षीणजीवितः (having little life left) / सः (he) / हन्ता (slayer) / तस्य (of that) / सैन्यस्य (army) / रामः (Rama) / क्षत्रियपांसनः (scum of the kshatriyas)
ramayan::7032.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7032.essence: Even a mocked exile can still defeat what others feared.
ramayan::7032.simple_meaning: Rama is described as a man exiled by his father, living in hardship with Sita, yet still destroying the demon army.
ramayan::7032.simple_insight: Even when insulted and cast aside, he remains capable of decisive action.
ramayan::7032.detailed_meaning: This is not a teaching verse but a hostile description in the middle of an argument. Someone is mocking Rama as exiled, weakened, and dishonoured, while also admitting that he has still destroyed the demon army.
ramayan::7032.modern_relevance: A colleague dismisses you as finished after a setback, then watches you quietly solve the problem anyway. The insult does not stop reality from changing.
ramayan::7032.insight: It frames victory as the answer to contempt, not as a response to praise.

ramayan::7033.verse_sanskrit: दुश्शीलः कर्कशस्तीक्ष्णो मूर्खो लुब्धोऽजितेन्द्रियः । । 33611 । । त्यक्तधर्मो ह्यधर्मात्मा भूतानामहिते रतः ।
ramayan::7033.verse_hindi: He is a man of bad conduct, harsh, sharptonged, stupid, miserly and a slave to his senses. He is immoral and unrighteous, one who is busy harming others.
ramayan::7033.english_translation: He is a man of bad conduct, harsh, sharp-tongued, foolish, miserly, and a slave to his senses. He has abandoned dharma, is rooted in wrongdoing, and delights in harming others.
ramayan::7033.translation_literal: दुश्शीलः (of bad conduct) / कर्कशः (harsh) / तीक्ष्णः (sharp) / मूर्खः (foolish) / लुब्धः (miserly) / अजितेन्द्रियः (one whose senses are not controlled) / त्यक्तधर्मः (one who has abandoned dharma) / हि (indeed) / अधर्मात्मा (one whose nature is unrighteous) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / अहिते (in harm) / रतः (delighted)
ramayan::7033.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7033.essence: A powerful person becomes dangerous when self-control and dharma are gone.
ramayan::7033.simple_meaning: Ravana is being described as cruel, uncontrolled, and harmful. The point is not just that he is powerful, but that his character is rotten.
ramayan::7033.simple_insight: Power without restraint becomes a danger to everyone around it.
ramayan::7033.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a fierce argument about Ravana, his nature is laid bare. The speaker strips away royal power and speaks of conduct: harshness, greed, lack of self-control, and a taste for harming others. The verse prepares the case against him.
ramayan::7033.modern_relevance: When someone keeps winning arguments by belittling others, the damage is already visible. The real problem is not their sharpness — it is the character behind it.
ramayan::7033.insight: It shifts attention from external strength to the moral quality of the person using it.

ramayan::7034.verse_sanskrit: येन वैरं विनाऽरण्ये सत्वमाश्रित्य केवलम् । । 33612 । । कर्णनासापहरणाद्भगिनी मे विरूपिता । तस्यभार्यां जनस्थानात्सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम् । 33613 । । आनयिष्यामि विक्रम्य सहायस्तत्र मे भव ।
ramayan::7034.verse_hindi: With no enmity whatsoever, merely because he has strength, he cut off the nose and ears of my sister and mutilated her. His wife Sita  is like the daughter of heaven. I would like to abduct her with force from Janasthana for which you should be my accomplice.
ramayan::7034.english_translation: With no enmity whatsoever, merely because he had strength, he mutilated my sister by cutting off her nose and ears. I will abduct his wife, Sita, who is like the daughter of the heavens, from Janasthana by force. Be my accomplice there.
ramayan::7034.translation_literal: येन (by whom) / वैरम् (enmity) / विनाऽरण्ये (in the forest, without) / सत्वम् (strength) / आश्रित्य (having relied on) / केवलम् (only) / कर्णनासापहरणात् (by cutting off the ears and nose) / भगिनी (sister) / मे (my) / विरूपिता (mutilated) / तस्य (his) / भार्याम् (wife) / जनस्थानात् (from Janasthana) / सीताम् (Sita) / सुरसुतोपमाम् (like the daughter of the gods) / आनयिष्यामि (I will bring, I will abduct) / विक्रम्य (by force, having overpowered) / सहायः (helper, accomplice) / तत्र (there) / मे (my) / भव (be)
ramayan::7034.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7034.essence: Hurt pride seeks revenge by harming the innocent.
ramayan::7034.simple_meaning: Ravana recalls how Surpanakha was mutilated and vows to seize Sita in revenge, asking for help in the attack.
ramayan::7034.simple_insight: Wounded pride can turn pain into cruelty.
ramayan::7034.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Ravana hears of Surpanakha’s humiliation and does not seek justice — he turns grievance into a plan for retaliation. He fixes on Sita, not as a person, but as a target to hurt Rama through violence.
ramayan::7034.modern_relevance: Someone insults your family, and suddenly every boundary feels negotiable. The hurt starts sounding like justification. This verse shows how quickly injury can become vengeance.
ramayan::7034.insight: It exposes how resentment hijacks judgment and turns another person into a weapon.

ramayan::7035.verse_sanskrit: त्वया ह्यहं सहायेन पार्श्वस्थेन महाबल । । 33614 । । भ्रातृभिश्च सुरान्युद्धे समग्रान्नाभिचिन्तये । तत्सहायो भव त्वं मे समर्थो ह्यसि राक्षस । । 33615 । ।
ramayan::7035.verse_hindi: You are mighty. I do not care to fight even the gods when you and my brothers are by my side. Therefore, O demon, be my accomplice. (I know) you are capable of that.
ramayan::7035.english_translation: You are mighty. I would not fear even the gods in battle if you stood beside me with my brothers. Therefore, O demon, become my ally; you are capable of that.
ramayan::7035.translation_literal: त्वया (by you) / हि (indeed) / अहम् (I) / सहायेन (with help, as ally) / पार्श्वस्थेन (standing at my side) / महाबल (greatly strong one) / भ्रातृभिः (with brothers) / च (and) / सुरान् (the gods) / युद्धे (in battle) / समग्रान् (all together) / न अभिचिन्तये (do not fear, do not consider) / तत् (therefore) / सहायः (helper, ally) / भव (become) / त्वम् (you) / मे (for me) / समर्थः (capable) / हि (indeed) / असि (you are) / राक्षस (O demon)
ramayan::7035.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7035.essence: Even arrogance will flatter when it needs an ally.
ramayan::7035.simple_meaning: Ravana flatters Vibhishana and asks him to side with him, saying that with such powerful support he would not fear even the gods in battle.
ramayan::7035.simple_insight: A proud mind can turn even loyalty into a tool.
ramayan::7035.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to pull Vibhishana into his side. After insulting and dismissing moral restraint in the previous lines, he now praises Vibhishana's strength and asks him to become an ally, revealing how badly he wants support before the coming war.
ramayan::7035.modern_relevance: A leader who knows he is wrong still reaches for the smartest person in the room to make his side look stronger.
ramayan::7035.insight: It exposes manipulation disguised as admiration, and the way ego recruits help without changing course.

ramayan::7036.verse_sanskrit: वीर्ये युद्धे च दर्पे च न ह्यस्ति सदृशस्तव । उपायज्ञो महान्शूरस्सर्वमायाविशारदः । । 33616 । ।
ramayan::7036.verse_hindi: In valour,  in war and in conceit there is no one equal to you. You know all means (of success). You are great. You are brave. You are an expert in all deceitful arts.
ramayan::7036.english_translation: In valour, in war and in conceit there is no one equal to you. You know all means of success. You are great. You are brave. You are an expert in every deceitful art.
ramayan::7036.translation_literal: वीर्ये (in valour) / युद्धे (in war) / च (and) / दर्पे (in pride) / च (and) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / अस्ति (is) / सदृशः (equal) / तव (to you) / उपायज्ञः (knower of means) / महान् (great) / शूरः (brave) / सर्वमायाविशारदः (expert in all deceitful arts)
ramayan::7036.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7036.essence: Pride is being fed here so obedience will come more easily.
ramayan::7036.simple_meaning: Ravana flatters another demon, saying no one matches his strength, battle skill, boldness, or cunning.
ramayan::7036.simple_insight: Praise can be a weapon when it is used to recruit pride.
ramayan::7036.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to an ally after recalling how his sister was mutilated. He builds the other man's ego by praising his strength, war skill, and cunning, then uses that praise to draw him into helping with Sita.
ramayan::7036.modern_relevance: Someone messages you with just enough admiration to make you lower your guard. The compliment feels generous, but it is really a hook.
ramayan::7036.insight: It shows how flattery can be used to enlist support before asking for a favor.

ramayan::7037.verse_sanskrit: एतदर्थमहं प्राप्तस्त्वत्समीपं निशाचर । शृणु तत्कर्म साहाय्ये यत्कार्यं वचनान्मम । । 33617 । ।
ramayan::7037.verse_hindi: I have come to you for this purpose seeking your help. Listen to  my words on what you should do:
ramayan::7037.english_translation: I have come to you for this purpose, O night-wanderer, seeking your help. Listen to my words about the task you must do for me.
ramayan::7037.translation_literal: एतदर्थम् (for this purpose) / अहम् (I) / प्राप्तः (have come) / त्वत्समीपम् (near you) / निशाचर (O night-wanderer) / शृणु (listen) / तत् (that) / कर्म (task) / साहाय्ये (in help) / यत् (which) / कार्यम् (is to be done) / वचनात् (from the word) / मम (of me)
ramayan::7037.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7037.essence: The request matters less than the scheme behind it.
ramayan::7037.simple_meaning: Ravana has come to someone and is about to explain a task that requires help. The verse is a setup for the actual instruction that follows.
ramayan::7037.simple_insight: The real message is still coming; this line only opens the door.
ramayan::7037.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Maricha in a calculated exchange. After praising his power, he says he has come for a specific purpose and is about to give the instruction that will pull Maricha into the plot against Rama and Sita.
ramayan::7037.modern_relevance: You know that moment when someone says, “I need your help,” and you can already feel the request coming? This is the breath before the ask.
ramayan::7037.insight: It functions as a lead-in to the actual command, not the command itself.

ramayan::7038.verse_sanskrit: सौवर्णस्त्वं मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजतबिन्दुभिः । आश्रमे तस्य रामस्य सीतायाः प्रमुखे चर । । 33618 । ।
ramayan::7038.verse_hindi: Be a wonderful golden deer dappled with silver dots and roam in front of Sita in Ramas hermitage.
ramayan::7038.english_translation: Be a wonderful golden deer, marked with silver spots, and roam before Sita in Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7038.translation_literal: सौवर्णः (golden) / त्वम् (you) / मृगः (deer) / भूत्वा (having become) / चित्रः (variegated, wonderful) / रजतबिन्दुभिः (with silver spots) / आश्रमे (in the hermitage) / तस्य (of that) / रामस्य (of Rama) / सीतायाः (of Sita) / प्रमुखे (in front) / चर (roam)
ramayan::7038.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7038.essence: Beauty is being used here as bait.
ramayan::7038.simple_meaning: Ravana orders a demon to take the form of a beautiful golden deer and move near Sita so she will notice it.
ramayan::7038.simple_insight: Deception often begins with something that looks harmless and beautiful.
ramayan::7038.detailed_meaning: Ravana is planning Sita's abduction. After praising Maricha's skill, he gives the trap: become a dazzling deer and wander before Sita in Rama's forest home. The verse is a tactical instruction, not a teaching.
ramayan::7038.modern_relevance: A message arrives that looks playful, harmless, even flattering. Behind it is a setup designed to pull your attention exactly where someone else wants it.
ramayan::7038.insight: It shows how temptation is often built as a distraction, not a direct attack.

ramayan::7039.verse_sanskrit: त्वां तु निस्संशयं सीता दृष्ट्वा तु मृगरूपिणम् । गृह्यतामिति भर्तारं लक्ष्मणं चाभिधास्यति । । 33619 । ।
ramayan::7039.verse_hindi: Seeing you in the form of a deer, Sita will undoubtedly ask her husband and Lakshmana to capture you.
ramayan::7039.english_translation: Seeing you in the form of a deer, Sita will undoubtedly ask her husband and Lakshmana to capture you.
ramayan::7039.translation_literal: त्वाम् (you) / तु (indeed) / निस्संशयम् (without doubt) / सीता (Sita) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तु (indeed) / मृगरूपिणम् (in deer-form) / गृह्यताम् (let it be caught) / इति (thus) / भर्तारम् (her husband) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / च (and) / अभिधास्यति (will say)
ramayan::7039.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7039.essence: The bait works because it makes love step away from safety.
ramayan::7039.simple_meaning: Ravana explains that if Maricha appears as a deer, Sita will ask Rama and Lakshmana to catch it.
ramayan::7039.simple_insight: A single lure can set the whole tragedy in motion.
ramayan::7039.detailed_meaning: Ravana is planning Sita’s abduction and instructing Maricha to become the golden deer. He knows Sita will be drawn to it, which will pull Rama and Lakshmana away from the hut and open the way for the kidnapping.
ramayan::7039.modern_relevance: A distraction is placed right where someone’s attention is most tender. The trap works because it pulls the right people out of position at the right moment.
ramayan::7039.insight: It shows how manipulation often begins by creating a harmless-looking desire that moves others exactly where you want them.

ramayan::7040.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तयोरपाये तु शून्ये सीतां यथासुखम् । निराबाधो हरिष्यामि राहुश्चन्द्रप्रभामिव । । 33620 । ।
ramayan::7040.verse_hindi: Then during their absence it will be easy for me to abduct Sita in an isolated place without obstruction, like Rahu eclipsing the light of the moon.
ramayan::7040.english_translation: Then, when they are gone and the place is empty, I will abduct Sita without obstruction, as Rahu eclipses the moon’s radiance.
ramayan::7040.translation_literal: ततः (then) / तयोः (of those two) / अपाये (at the departure) / तु (indeed) / शून्ये (when empty) / सीताम् (Sita) / यथासुखम् (as easily / at will) / निराबाधः (without obstruction) / हरिष्यामि (I will carry off) / राहुः (Rahu) / चन्द्रप्रभाम् (the moon’s radiance) / इव (like)
ramayan::7040.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7040.essence: Wanting begins to sound like inevitability when judgment is already gone.
ramayan::7040.simple_meaning: Ravana plans to take Sita once Rama and Lakshmana are gone, imagining the theft will be easy and unopposed.
ramayan::7040.simple_insight: Delusion grows when desire starts calling itself strategy.
ramayan::7040.detailed_meaning: Hidden in the forest, Ravana watches the trap he has set for Rama and Lakshmana. He imagines their absence will leave Sita exposed, and he speaks as if abduction were as effortless as an eclipse swallowing moonlight.
ramayan::7040.modern_relevance: You start rehearsing how easy it will be once the room is empty, once the guard is distracted, once no one can stop you. Desire always makes the lie sound efficient.
ramayan::7040.insight: It exposes how craving turns people into planners of harm, mistaking opportunity for permission.

ramayan::7041.verse_sanskrit: ततः पश्चात्सुखं रामे भार्याहरणकर्शिते । विस्रब्धः प्रहरिष्यामि कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना । । 33621 । ।
ramayan::7041.verse_hindi: Thereafter, when Rama with his soul afflicted due to his wifes abduction. I can freely, happily, successfully strike him down.
ramayan::7041.english_translation: Thereafter, when Rama is tormented by the abduction of his wife, I will freely and happily strike him down, feeling fully accomplished.
ramayan::7041.translation_literal: ततः (thereafter) / पश्चात् (afterward) / सुखम् (easily, happily) / रामे (at Rama) / भार्याहरणकर्शिते (when tormented by the abduction of his wife) / विस्रब्धः (confidently, without fear) / प्रहरिष्यामि (I will strike) / कृतार्थेन (with the feeling of having achieved my aim) / अन्तरात्मना (with my inner self)
ramayan::7041.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7041.essence: He thinks grief will make his victory easy.
ramayan::7041.simple_meaning: Ravana is planning to attack Rama only after Rama is weakened by Sita's abduction. He believes that grief will make Rama easy to kill.
ramayan::7041.simple_insight: Cruelty often waits for weakness, then mistakes it for victory.
ramayan::7041.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in the middle of his scheme against Sita and Rama. He imagines that once Sita is gone and Rama is crushed by grief, he can attack without fear and finish the matter. The verse reveals his calculating arrogance.
ramayan::7041.modern_relevance: Someone waits until you are already exhausted, then calls their timing clever. They mistake your pain for their advantage.
ramayan::7041.insight: It exposes how ego plans to exploit another person's heartbreak instead of facing them honestly.

ramayan::7042.verse_sanskrit: तस्य रामकथां श्रुत्वा मारीचस्य महात्मनः । शुष्कं समभवद्वक्त्रं परितप्ता बभूव ह । । 33622 । ।
ramayan::7042.verse_hindi: At the mention of Ramas name, great Marichas mouth dried up and he became concerned.
ramayan::7042.english_translation: At the mention of Rama's name, the great Maricha's mouth dried up, and he became distressed.
ramayan::7042.translation_literal: तस्य (of him) / रामकथां (Rama's story) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / मारीचस्य (of Maricha) / महात्मनः (great-souled) / शुष्कं (dry) / समभवत् (became) / वक्त्रं (mouth) / परितप्ता (distressed) / बभूव (became) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7042.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7042.essence: Rama's name alone is enough to unsettle a man already trapped in danger.
ramayan::7042.simple_meaning: Hearing Rama's name made Maricha uneasy and physically dry-mouthed. The fear is immediate and involuntary.
ramayan::7042.simple_insight: Some names carry the memory of consequences before any blow is struck.
ramayan::7042.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been plotting Sita's abduction and the attack on Rama. When Maricha hears Rama mentioned, his body betrays him at once: his mouth dries, and distress rises before he even answers. The scene shows how dangerous this plan already feels to him.
ramayan::7042.modern_relevance: You hear one person's name and your stomach tightens before they even arrive. Your body remembers what your mind tries to dismiss.
ramayan::7042.insight: It shows fear as a bodily warning, not just an emotion. The verse prepares you for Maricha's reluctance before he speaks.

ramayan::7043.verse_sanskrit: ओष्ठौ परिलिहञ्चुष्कौ नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव । मृतभूत इवार्तस्तु रावणं समुदैक्षत । । 33623 । ।
ramayan::7043.verse_hindi: Licking his dried up lips, as though his eyes stopped winking like those of the dead, Maricha stared at Ravana, distressed.
ramayan::7043.english_translation: Licking his dried up lips, as though his eyes stopped winking like those of the dead, Maricha stared at Ravana, distressed.
ramayan::7043.translation_literal: ओष्ठौ (lips) / परिलिहन् (licking) / चुष्कौ (dry) / नेत्रैः (with eyes) / अनिमिषैः (unblinking) / इव (as if) / मृतभूतः (like one dead) / इव (as if) / आर्तः (distressed) / तु (but) / रावणम् (at Ravana) / समुदैक्षत (looked)
ramayan::7043.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7043.essence: Fear silences the body before it can speak.
ramayan::7043.simple_meaning: Maricha stands frozen in fear before Ravana. His body shows distress before he even speaks.
ramayan::7043.simple_insight: Fear can seize the body before the mind finds words.
ramayan::7043.detailed_meaning: Maricha has just heard Ravana speak of attacking Rama. The boast that sounded clever a moment ago now turns deadly in Maricha's mind. Before he answers, his fear shows in his dry lips and unblinking stare.
ramayan::7043.modern_relevance: You hear a plan in a meeting and suddenly realise it could ruin everything. Your mouth goes dry before you find the words to object.
ramayan::7043.insight: It shows fear as a visible reaction, preparing the reader for Maricha's warning to Ravana.

ramayan::7044.verse_sanskrit: स रावणं त्रस्तविषण्णचेता महावने रामपराक्रमज्ञः । कृताञ्जलिस्तत्वमुवाच वाक्यं हितं च तस्मै हितमात्मनश्च । । 33624 । ।
ramayan::7044.verse_hindi: Maricha who knows of Ramas valour was frightened and depressed at heart. He revealed to Ravana with folded hands some facts for mutual benefit.
ramayan::7044.english_translation: Maricha, who knew Rama's valour, was frightened and downcast at heart. With folded hands, he spoke words of counsel for Ravana's good and his own.
ramayan::7044.translation_literal: सः (he) / रावणम् (to Ravana) / त्रस्तविषण्ण-चेताः (frightened and depressed in heart) / महावने (in the great forest) / राम-पराक्रम-ज्ञः (knower of Rama's valour) / कृताञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / तत् (that) / उवाच (spoke) / वाक्यम् (speech) / हितम् (beneficial) / च (and) / तस्मै (for him) / हितम् (beneficial) / आत्मनः (of his own) / च (and)
ramayan::7044.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7044.essence: Fear makes Maricha speak truth before disaster closes in.
ramayan::7044.simple_meaning: Maricha is terrified of Rama's strength, yet still speaks carefully to Ravana for both their sakes.
ramayan::7044.simple_insight: Fear can make you honest when pride would rather stay blind.
ramayan::7044.detailed_meaning: In the great forest, Maricha has just heard Ravana press him into a dangerous scheme. Knowing Rama's power, Maricha is shaken and anxious. He folds his hands and begins to answer with caution, trying to protect both Ravana and himself.
ramayan::7044.modern_relevance: You know a plan is reckless, but the room is full of people who want to hear yes. Your throat tightens, and you finally speak carefully instead of pretending confidence.
ramayan::7044.insight: It shows the moment when fear becomes clear warning, not blind obedience.

ramayan::7045.verse_sanskrit: तच्छृत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः । प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो मारीचो राक्षसेश्वरम् । । 3371 । ।
ramayan::7045.verse_hindi: Having heard the words of Ravana, lord of the demons, wise Maricha who was also an eloquent speaker replied:
ramayan::7045.english_translation: Having heard the words of Ravana, lord of the demons, wise Maricha who was also an eloquent speaker replied:
ramayan::7045.translation_literal: तच्छृत्वा (having heard that) / राक्षसेन्द्रस्य (of the lord of the demons) / वाक्यं (speech) / वाक्यविशारदः (skilled in speech) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / महाप्राज्ञः (very wise) / मारीचः (Maricha) / राक्षसेश्वरम् (to the lord of the demons)
ramayan::7045.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7045.essence: A wise reply matters most when power is listening.
ramayan::7045.simple_meaning: Maricha, a wise and skilled speaker, heard Ravana and replied.
ramayan::7045.simple_insight: Sometimes the real turning point is not action, but the reply that follows hard truth.
ramayan::7045.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, Maricha has already been pressed into a dangerous conversation. This verse only marks the moment before his warning begins: he listens, gathers himself, and answers the king of Lanka with intelligence and caution.
ramayan::7045.modern_relevance: You can feel the room tighten when someone powerful asks for agreement and the honest answer is risky. This is the breath before that answer.
ramayan::7045.insight: It sets up a warning: wisdom begins by refusing to flatter power.

ramayan::7046.verse_sanskrit: सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः । अप्रियस्य तु पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः । । 3372 । ।
ramayan::7046.verse_hindi: O king, it is always easy to find men who speak pleasing words, but it is difficult to get a speaker and a listener who use words unpleasant (to the ears) but beneficial (in life).
ramayan::7046.english_translation: O king, it is always easy to find men who speak pleasing words, but it is difficult to get a speaker and a listener who use words unpleasant to the ears but beneficial in life.
ramayan::7046.translation_literal: सुलभाः (easy to find) / पुरुषा (men) / राजन् (O king) / सततं (always) / प्रियवादिनः (those who speak pleasing words) / अप्रियस्य (of the unpleasant) / तु (but) / पथ्यस्य (beneficial, wholesome) / वक्ता (speaker) / श्रोता (listener) / च (and) / दुर्लभः (rare, hard to find)
ramayan::7046.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7046.essence: What helps is often the hardest thing to say and hear.
ramayan::7046.simple_meaning: People who say what you want to hear are easy to find. Far rarer are people who speak hard truths that actually help, and people willing to hear them.
ramayan::7046.simple_insight: Real growth begins when you welcome the truth that stings a little.
ramayan::7046.detailed_meaning: Maricha, warning Ravana in the forest, pauses the chase and names a hard fact: flattery is common, but useful truth is scarce. He is trying to save Ravana by saying what Ravana does not want to hear.
ramayan::7046.modern_relevance: In a meeting, everyone nods at the risky plan because nobody wants to be the difficult voice. The person who speaks plainly may be the only one protecting the whole room.
ramayan::7046.insight: It shifts you from seeking approval to seeking useful truth, even when it feels uncomfortable.

ramayan::7047.verse_sanskrit: न नूनं बुध्यसे रामं महावीर्यं गुणोन्नतम् । अयुक्तचारश्चपलो महेन्द्रवरुणोपमम् । । 3373 । ।
ramayan::7047.verse_hindi: You  are fickleminded.  You have employed no spy ( who could have told you the truth about Ramas character). Rama is very brave and virtuous comparable to Indra and Varuna. Surely you are not able to know what Rama is.
ramayan::7047.english_translation: You do not truly understand Rama, who is immensely powerful and exalted in virtue, who moves with purpose, and who is like Indra and Varuna. Surely you have not learned what Rama really is.
ramayan::7047.translation_literal: न नूनं (surely not) / बुध्यसे (you understand) / रामं (Rama) / महावीर्यं (of great power) / गुणोन्नतम् (raised in virtue) / अयुक्तचारः (one without proper spies) / चपलः (fickle-minded) / महेन्द्रवरुणोपमम् (equal to Indra and Varuna)
ramayan::7047.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7047.essence: Blindness to greatness is often the start of ruin.
ramayan::7047.simple_meaning: Maricha warns Ravana that he has badly misunderstood Rama. Rama is not ordinary; he is powerful, virtuous, and far beyond Ravana's grasp.
ramayan::7047.simple_insight: Misreading someone powerful can be fatal.
ramayan::7047.detailed_meaning: Maricha answers Ravana after being asked for counsel. He says Ravana is fickle and blind to Rama's true nature. The warning is not abstract: Ravana is underestimating the man who will later destroy his plans.
ramayan::7047.modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room because they are not loud. You call them harmless, then discover they were the only one seeing the whole field.
ramayan::7047.insight: It shifts you from casual judgment to careful seeing before you act.

ramayan::7048.verse_sanskrit: अपि स्वस्ति भवेत्तात सर्वेषां भुवि रक्षसाम् । अपि रामो नासङ्क्रुद्धः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसम् । । 3374 । ।
ramayan::7048.verse_hindi: O dear may there be good to all the demons in the world. If Rama gets enraged, he will make this world demonless.
ramayan::7048.english_translation: O dear, may there be well-being for all the demons in the world. If Rama grows angry, he will make the world free of demons.
ramayan::7048.translation_literal: अपि (may it be) / स्वस्ति (well-being) / भवेत् (may there be) / तात (dear one) / सर्वेषाम् (for all) / भुवि (in the world) / रक्षसाम् (of demons) / अपि (even) / रामः (Rama) / नासङ्क्रुद्धः (not enraged) / कुर्यात् (would make) / लोकम् (the world) / अराक्षसम् (without demons)
ramayan::7048.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7048.essence: Rama's anger would erase the very beings who underestimate him.
ramayan::7048.simple_meaning: Ravana speaks with a bitter warning: even the demons should wish for peace, because if Rama is provoked, he can wipe out their kind from the world.
ramayan::7048.simple_insight: Unchecked anger in the right person can end an entire order.
ramayan::7048.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in the middle of a tense exchange about Rama's power. He warns his listener that even the demons should hope for safety, because Rama's wrath could leave the world without any demons at all.
ramayan::7048.modern_relevance: You dismiss someone as harmless, then one hard boundary wakes them fully. The version of them you ignored was never the whole story.
ramayan::7048.insight: It shifts attention from mocking strength to respecting the cost of provoking it.

ramayan::7049.verse_sanskrit: अपि ते जीवितान्ताय नोत्पन्ना जनकात्मजा । अपि सीतानिमित्तं च न भवेद्व्यसनं मम । । 3375 । ।
ramayan::7049.verse_hindi: Hope the daughter of Janaka is not born to put an end to your life. Hope I will not face any disaster on account of Sita.
ramayan::7049.english_translation: Hope the daughter of Janaka is not born to put an end to your life. Hope I will not face any disaster on account of Sita.
ramayan::7049.translation_literal: अपि (may it be that) / ते (your) / जीवितान्ताय (for the end of life) / न (not) / उत्पन्ना (born) / जनकात्मजा (the daughter of Janaka) / अपि (may it be that) / सीतानिमित्तं (because of Sita) / च (and) / न (not) / भवेत् (may there be) / व्यसनं (disaster) / मम (for me)
ramayan::7049.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7049.essence: His taunt carries the fear of the ruin he has invited.
ramayan::7049.simple_meaning: Ravana is tauntingly hoping that Sita was not born to bring about the end of Rama's life, and that he himself will not suffer disaster because of her.
ramayan::7049.simple_insight: Pride can sound like a prayer while it hides fear.
ramayan::7049.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in Lanka, gloating over Sita’s abduction and still trying to sound in control. He frames his fear as a wish: that Sita will not become the cause of Rama’s death or of Ravana’s own ruin. The line reveals how close his confidence already is to anxiety.
ramayan::7049.modern_relevance: You make a cruel joke to cover the fact that you are already uneasy. The mouth sounds bold, but the mind is bracing for consequences.
ramayan::7049.insight: It exposes how arrogance often masks dread of the damage already in motion.

ramayan::7050.verse_sanskrit: अपि त्वामीश्वरं प्राप्य कामवृत्तं निरङ्कुशम् । न विनश्येत्पुरी लङ्का त्वया सह सराक्षसा । । 3376 । ।
ramayan::7050.verse_hindi: I hope the city of Lanka along with the (entire) race of demons will not be destroyed, with a dictator like you who is a slave to sensual pleasure.
ramayan::7050.english_translation: I hope the city of Lanka, along with the entire race of demons, will not be destroyed because of you, who are a ruler without restraint and a slave to sensual desire.
ramayan::7050.translation_literal: अपि (may it be) / त्वाम् (you) / ईश्वरम् (ruler) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / कामवृत्तम् (one whose conduct is driven by desire) / निरङ्कुशम् (unrestrained) / न (not) / विनश्येत् (may be destroyed) / पुरी (city) / लङ्का (Lanka) / त्वया सह (together with you) / सराक्षसा (along with the demons)
ramayan::7050.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7050.essence: Unrestrained desire in a leader destroys everyone under him.
ramayan::7050.simple_meaning: A ruler ruled by desire brings ruin not only on himself, but on his city and people too.
ramayan::7050.simple_insight: Unchecked appetite in power turns private weakness into public disaster.
ramayan::7050.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a warning is being spoken to Ravana. The speaker sees that his uncontrolled desire and lack of restraint are not personal flaws alone — they threaten the city, the demon race, and everything around him. This line sharpens the warning into a direct prediction of collapse.
ramayan::7050.modern_relevance: A leader who treats every craving like a command can sink an entire team. What feels private in him becomes public damage for everyone around him.
ramayan::7050.insight: It turns personal self-control into a political responsibility.

ramayan::7051.verse_sanskrit: त्वद्विधः कामवृत्तो हि दुश्शीलः पापमन्त्रितः । आत्मानं स्वजनं राष्ट्रं स राजा हन्ति दुर्मतिः । । 3377 । ।
ramayan::7051.verse_hindi: A king  who is a slave to passion, who is of bad conduct, of wicked thoughts, advised in evil ways destroys himself, his kith and kin and the entire kingdom.
ramayan::7051.english_translation: A king who is a slave to passion, of bad conduct and wicked counsel, destroys himself, his family, and his kingdom.
ramayan::7051.translation_literal: त्वद्विधः (one like you) / कामवृत्तः (driven by desire) / हि (indeed) / दुश्शीलः (of bad conduct) / पापमन्त्रितः (advised in evil ways) / आत्मानम् (himself) / स्वजनम् (his own people) / राष्ट्रम् (the kingdom) / सः (that) / राजा (king) / हन्ति (destroys) / दुर्मतिः (of crooked mind)
ramayan::7051.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7051.essence: A ruler's private vice becomes a nation's collapse.
ramayan::7051.simple_meaning: A leader ruled by desire, bad habits, and bad advice brings ruin on himself, his family, and the whole state.
ramayan::7051.simple_insight: Power without self-control turns inward first, then spills outward.
ramayan::7051.detailed_meaning: Ravana is pressing his case in Lanka, and the warning is sharp: a king who gives himself to desire and corrupt counsel does not just fail privately. He drags down his household, his people, and the whole realm with him.
ramayan::7051.modern_relevance: A manager keeps ignoring warning signs because the flattering voices around him feel easier than the truth. By the time the damage is visible, the whole team is paying for one person's appetite.
ramayan::7051.insight: It shifts attention from private impulse to public consequence, showing how inner corruption becomes collective harm.

ramayan::7052.verse_sanskrit: न च पित्रा परित्यक्तो नामर्यादः कथञ्चन । न लुब्धो न च दुश्शीलो न च क्षत्रियपांसनः । । 3378 । । न च धर्मगुणैर्हीनः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः । न तीक्ष्णो न च भूतानां सर्वेषामहिते रतः । । 3379 । ।
ramayan::7052.verse_hindi: Rama, the delight of Kausalya, has not forsaken by his father. He has never crossed the limits of dharma. He is not miserly. He has no  bad conduct. He is not a slur on the kshatriyas. He does not lack in righteousness. He is not cruel nor is he engaged in doing harm to others.
ramayan::7052.english_translation: Rama, the delight of Kausalya, has not been abandoned by his father. He has never crossed the bounds of dharma. He is not miserly, not ill-behaved, not a disgrace to the warrior class. He lacks no virtue, is not cruel, and takes no delight in harming any being.
ramayan::7052.translation_literal: न च (not) / पित्रा (by father) / परित्यक्तः (abandoned) / नामर्यादः (without bounds of dharma) / कथञ्चन (in any way) / न (not) / लुब्धः (greedy) / न च (and not) / दुश्शीलः (ill-behaved) / न च (and not) / क्षत्रियपांसनः (disgrace to warriors) / न च (not) / धर्मगुणैः (with virtues of dharma) / हीनः (devoid) / कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः (the increaser of Kausalya's joy) / न (not) / तीक्ष्णः (harsh) / न च (and not) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / अहिते (in harm) / रतः (delighting)
ramayan::7052.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7052.essence: His greatness lies in the harm he never chose.
ramayan::7052.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as a man who stayed within dharma, avoided greed and cruelty, and never brought shame on his warrior duty.
ramayan::7052.simple_insight: Real nobility is measured by what you do not become.
ramayan::7052.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Rama is being defended as the opposite of a selfish ruler. The speaker lists his restraint, virtue, and harmlessness to show that his exile is not failure but proof of character.
ramayan::7052.modern_relevance: When people are gossiping about you after a hard decision, your real defense is not noise. It is the record of how you have lived when no one was clapping.
ramayan::7052.insight: It shifts attention from image to conduct: a good life is built by refusing greed, harshness, and harm.

ramayan::7053.verse_sanskrit: वञ्चितं पितरं दृष्ट्वा कैकेय्या सत्यवादिनम् । करिष्यामीति धर्मात्मा तात प्रव्रजितो वनम् । । 33710 । ।
ramayan::7053.verse_hindi: O dear, seeing that his truthful father was going to be deceived by Kaikeyi, righteous Rama himself offered to fulfil the promise of his father and came away to the forest.
ramayan::7053.english_translation: Seeing his truthful father being deceived by Kaikeyi, righteous Rama said, 'I will do it,' and went to the forest.
ramayan::7053.translation_literal: वञ्चितं (deceived) / पितरं (father) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / कैकेय्या (by Kaikeyi) / सत्यवादिनम् (truth-speaking) / करिष्यामि (I will do) / इति (thus) / धर्मात्मा (righteous one) / तात (dear one) / प्रव्रजितो (went forth) / वनम् (to the forest)
ramayan::7053.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7053.essence: He saved his father’s honor by giving up his own home.
ramayan::7053.simple_meaning: Rama saw that his father was being deceived, and he chose to honor the promise anyway by leaving for the forest.
ramayan::7053.simple_insight: Love becomes real when you protect someone else's word, even at your own expense.
ramayan::7053.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Rama sees King Dasharatha caught in Kaikeyi's cruel demand. Rather than let his father be shamed by broken words, Rama steps forward and accepts exile himself. The verse marks the moment he turns filial love into action.
ramayan::7053.modern_relevance: You realize a parent is about to be cornered by a promise they can’t escape. You could protest, bargain, or leave. Instead, you quietly take the harder road so their word remains intact.
ramayan::7053.insight: It shifts duty from obligation to chosen sacrifice.

ramayan::7054.verse_sanskrit: कैकेय्याः प्रियकामार्थं पितुर्दशरथस्य च । हित्वा राज्यं च भोगांश्च प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम् । । 33711 । ।
ramayan::7054.verse_hindi: To satisfy the desire of Kaikeyi and to fulfil his fathers word he came to Dandaka forest,  leaving the kingdom and all royal pleasures, behind.
ramayan::7054.english_translation: To satisfy Kaikeyi's desire and to keep King Dasharatha's word, he left the kingdom and royal comforts and entered Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7054.translation_literal: कैकेय्याः (of Kaikeyi) / प्रियकामार्थं (for the sake of pleasing the desire) / पितुः (of the father) / दशरथस्य (of Dasharatha) / च (and) / हित्वा (having abandoned) / राज्यं (the kingdom) / च (and) / भोगांश्च (and pleasures) / प्रविष्टः (entered) / दण्डकावनम् (Dandaka forest)
ramayan::7054.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7054.essence: He gave up everything visible to preserve a promise.
ramayan::7054.simple_meaning: Rama gave up the throne and every royal comfort to honour his father's promise and Kaikeyi's wish.
ramayan::7054.simple_insight: Real nobility is shown by what you willingly give up.
ramayan::7054.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Rama is already walking the path of exile. He has left behind the palace, the throne, and every pleasure because Dasharatha's word must stand and Kaikeyi's demand must be met. The verse highlights the cost of his obedience.
ramayan::7054.modern_relevance: You were offered comfort, status, and an easier path, but keeping your word mattered more. The loss was real, and you chose it anyway.
ramayan::7054.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting comfort to protecting commitment.

ramayan::7055.verse_sanskrit: न रामः कर्कशस्तात नाविद्वान्नाजितेन्द्रियः । अनृतं दुश्श्रुतं चैव नैव त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि । । 33712 । ।
ramayan::7055.verse_hindi: O my dear, Rama is not harsh nor ignorant. It is not that he has no control over the senses. It is not proper  for you to say what is false. You are illinformed.
ramayan::7055.english_translation: O my dear, Rama is not harsh nor ignorant. He is not uncontrolled by his senses. It is not proper for you to speak falsely. You are misinformed.
ramayan::7055.translation_literal: न रामः (Rama is not) / कर्कशः (harsh) / तात (dear one) / न (not) / अविद्वान् (ignorant) / न (not) / अजितेन्द्रियः (one whose senses are not conquered) / अनृतम् (falsehood) / दुश्श्रुतम् (badly heard / misinformed) / च एव (and indeed) / नैव (certainly not) / त्वम् (you) / वक्तुम् अर्हसि (ought to say)
ramayan::7055.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7055.essence: False speech collapses when you look at Rama clearly.
ramayan::7055.simple_meaning: Rama is not cruel, foolish, or uncontrolled. The speaker insists that the accusation is false and based on bad information.
ramayan::7055.simple_insight: Misjudgment spreads fast; clear seeing protects both truth and dignity.
ramayan::7055.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Rama’s exile is being defended against suspicion and distortion. The speaker corrects a false picture of Rama: he is disciplined, intelligent, and self-controlled. This line pushes back against gossip before the fuller praise arrives in the next verse.
ramayan::7055.modern_relevance: A rumor lands in a family group chat, and everyone starts reacting before checking the facts. This verse reminds you that a careless claim can wound a good person before truth has a chance to speak.
ramayan::7055.insight: It shifts you from repeating hearsay to testing what you say against reality.

ramayan::7056.verse_sanskrit: रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मस्साधुस्सत्यपराक्रमः । राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवानां मघवानिव । । 33713 । ।
ramayan::7056.verse_hindi: Rama is dharma incarnate. He is pious. His strength is truth. He is king of all the worlds like Indra to the gods.
ramayan::7056.english_translation: Rama is dharma embodied. He is noble and his strength is truth. He is king of all the worlds, like Indra among the gods.
ramayan::7056.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / विग्रहवान् (embodied) / धर्मः (dharma) / साधुः (noble, virtuous) / सत्यपराक्रमः (whose power is truth) / राजा (king) / सर्वस्य (of all) / लोकस्य (worlds) / देवानाम् (of the gods) / मघवान् (Indra) / इव (like)
ramayan::7056.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7056.essence: Truth is not Rama's rule; it is his power.
ramayan::7056.simple_meaning: Rama is described as the living form of righteousness. His power comes from truth, and his rule is compared to Indra's among the gods.
ramayan::7056.simple_insight: Real authority does not need forceful self-assertion; it rests on character that never splits from truth.
ramayan::7056.detailed_meaning: Vibhishana is defending Rama's character before Ravana's court. After saying Rama left everything behind to honour his father's word, he adds the deeper claim: Rama himself is the shape of dharma, and his power comes from truth.
ramayan::7056.modern_relevance: In a room where everyone is trying to sound powerful, the person who stays clean, precise, and honest often has the most authority. This verse names that kind of strength.
ramayan::7056.insight: It shifts you from admiring power to recognising truth-backed authority as the highest form of strength.

ramayan::7057.verse_sanskrit: कथं त्वं तस्य वैदेहीं रक्षितां स्वेन तेजसा । इच्छसि प्रसभं हर्तुं प्रभामिव विवस्वतः । । 33714 । ।
ramayan::7057.verse_hindi: Sita is protected by the strength of her character. How do you desire to carry her away forcibly (from Rama) ? Can any one separate the radiance of the Sun from the Sun itself ?
ramayan::7057.english_translation: Sita is protected by the strength of her character. How do you desire to carry her away forcibly from Rama? Can anyone separate the radiance of the Sun from the Sun itself?
ramayan::7057.translation_literal: कथम् (how) / त्वम् (you) / तस्य (of him) / वैदेहीम् (Sita, daughter of Videha) / रक्षिताम् (protected) / स्वेन (by own) / तेजसा (radiance, power) / इच्छसि (you desire) / प्रसभम् (forcibly) / हर्तुम् (to take away) / प्रभाम् (radiance) / इव (like) / विवस्वतः (of the Sun)
ramayan::7057.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7057.essence: What is truly joined cannot be torn apart by force.
ramayan::7057.simple_meaning: Sita cannot be taken by force because she is already protected by Rama's power. The verse compares that bond to the Sun and its radiance.
ramayan::7057.simple_insight: Some things are held so completely that force only reveals your helplessness.
ramayan::7057.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the speaker warns that Sita is not an isolated captive. She is guarded by Rama's power and belonging to him in a way force cannot undo. The image of the Sun and its radiance makes the separation impossible.
ramayan::7057.modern_relevance: You try to control a relationship by pressure, threats, or leverage, but the bond is already elsewhere. What is truly held with care cannot be seized by force.
ramayan::7057.insight: It shifts attention from possession to relationship: some bonds are not objects to be grabbed.

ramayan::7058.verse_sanskrit: शरार्चिषमाधृष्यं चापखङ्गेन्धनं रणे । रामाग्निं सहसा दीप्तं न प्रवेष्टुं त्वमर्हसि । । 33715 । ।
ramayan::7058.verse_hindi: You should not enter into the unquenchable fire that is  Rama,  the fire that has the  arrows (of Rama) as its flames and his sword and bow as fuel.
ramayan::7058.english_translation: You should not rush into Rama, the blazing fire whose flames are arrows and whose fuel is bow and sword.
ramayan::7058.translation_literal: शरार्चिषम् (whose flames are arrows) / अधृष्यम् (unassailable) / चापखङ्गेन्धनम् (with bow-and-sword as fuel) / रणे (in battle) / रामाग्निम् (Rama-fire) / सहसा (suddenly) / दीप्तम् (blazing) / न (not) / प्रवेष्टुम् (to enter) / त्वम् (you) / अर्हसि (are fit)
ramayan::7058.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7058.essence: Do not mistake rage for strength; some battles consume the one who starts them.
ramayan::7058.simple_meaning: Rama is being compared to a fire that cannot be approached carelessly. Ravana is warned that attacking him head-on will end in ruin.
ramayan::7058.simple_insight: Some forces punish arrogance instantly. Wisdom is knowing when not to charge forward.
ramayan::7058.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the warning grows sharper. Rama is described as a blazing fire in battle, with arrows as flames and bow and sword as fuel. The speaker is not teaching a principle so much as pressing Ravana to see the danger before he rushes into disaster.
ramayan::7058.modern_relevance: You know that moment when pride says, “I can handle this,” but every sign says stop. This verse is that warning before the collision.
ramayan::7058.insight: It shifts the mind from bravado to caution when confronting a force you cannot overrun.

ramayan::7059.verse_sanskrit: धनुर्व्यादितदीप्तास्यं शरार्चिषममर्षणम् । चापबाणधरं तीक्ष्णं शत्रुसैन्यप्रहारिणम् । । 33716 । । राज्यं सुखं च सन्त्यज्य जीवितं चेष्टमात्मनः । नात्यासादयितुं तात रामान्तकमिहार्हसि । । 33717 । ।
ramayan::7059.verse_hindi: You should not give up happiness,your dear life and kingdom and come to Rama who is a variable god of death. His bow is  like on open burning mouth, and his flaming arrows are like fire. He is all anger. He is wielder of bow and arrows. He can strike the enemy army (alone).
ramayan::7059.english_translation: You should not give up kingdom, pleasure, and your own life to approach Rama here. His open bow is a blazing mouth, his arrows are flames, and he destroys enemy armies.
ramayan::7059.translation_literal: धनुः (bow) / व्यादित (opened wide) / दीप्त-आस्यम् (with a blazing mouth) / शर-अर्चिषम् (with arrows as flames) / अमर्षणम् (unbearable in anger) / चाप-बाण-धरम् (holding bow and arrows) / तीक्ष्णम् (sharp, fierce) / शत्रु-सैन्य-प्रहारिणम् (striker of enemy armies) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / सुखम् (pleasure) / च (and) / सन्त्यज्य (having abandoned) / जीवितम् (life) / च ईष्टम् (dear) / आत्मनः (of oneself) / न (not) / अति-आसादयितुम् (to approach too closely) / तात (dear one) / राम-अन्तकम् (Rama, the ender of life) / इह (here) / अर्हसि (you are fit / should)
ramayan::7059.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7059.essence: Pride is fatal when it mistakes fire for weakness.
ramayan::7059.simple_meaning: Rama is being described as a fearsome warrior no one should rush toward. His weapons burn like fire, and anyone who comes against him risks everything.
ramayan::7059.simple_insight: Some forces are not meant to be tested by pride.
ramayan::7059.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a warning to Ravana, the speaker piles image on image: Rama's bow is a blazing mouth, his arrows are fire, and his anger is unstoppable. The point is not praise alone, but to make Ravana feel the cost of underestimating him.
ramayan::7059.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the threat, or force the meeting. But the other side is not a soft target, and your confidence may be the danger.
ramayan::7059.insight: It shifts the mind from reckless challenge to sober respect for power.

ramayan::7060.verse_sanskrit: अप्रमेयं हि तत्तेजो यस्य सा जनकात्मजा । न त्वं समर्थस्तां हर्तुं रामचापाश्रयं वने । । 33718 । ।
ramayan::7060.verse_hindi: Immeasurable indeed is the power of Rama to whom Sita, daughter of Janaka belongs. You are not competent to kidnap her, for she is under the refuge of Ramas bow in the forest.
ramayan::7060.english_translation: Indeed, the power of Rama is immeasurable, for Sita, the daughter of Janaka, belongs to him. You are not capable of abducting her, because she is under the protection of Rama's bow in the forest.
ramayan::7060.translation_literal: अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable) / हि (indeed) / तत् (that) / तेजः (power, splendour) / यस्य (whose) / सा (that) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka) / न (not) / त्वम् (you) / समर्थः (capable) / ताम् (her) / हर्तुम् (to seize, abduct) / रामचापाश्रयम् (under the refuge of Rama's bow) / वने (in the forest)
ramayan::7060.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7060.essence: Some targets are unreachable because their protection is already in place.
ramayan::7060.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that Sita cannot be taken, because Rama's power protects her even in the forest.
ramayan::7060.simple_insight: Not everything vulnerable is helpless. Some things are held by a strength you cannot see at first.
ramayan::7060.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being confronted with the reality of whom Sita belongs to and what it means to challenge Rama. The forest is not a place of weakness here; it is the place where Rama's protection still reaches her, making abduction both impossible and reckless.
ramayan::7060.modern_relevance: You think a boundary is soft because no one is shouting. Then you learn the person you crossed is backed by a strength you didn't account for.
ramayan::7060.insight: It shifts the mind from opportunism to respect for hidden protection and force.

ramayan::7061.verse_sanskrit: तस्य सा नरसिंहस्य सिंहोरस्कस्य भामिनी । प्राणेभ्योऽपि प्रियतरा भार्या नित्यमनुव्रता । । 33719 । ।
ramayan::7061.verse_hindi: Beautiful Sita happens to be the wife of Rama who is like a lion among men. Rama
ramayan::7061.english_translation: That lovely woman is the wife of that lion among men, the lion-chested Rama, and she is more dear to him than life itself, always faithful to him.
ramayan::7061.translation_literal: तस्य (of that one) / सा (she) / नरसिंहस्य (of the lion among men) / सिंहोरस्कस्य (of the lion-chested one) / भामिनी (the lovely woman) / प्राणेभ्यः (than life-breaths) / अपि (even) / प्रियतरा (dearer) / भार्या (wife) / नित्यम् (always) / अनुव्रता (faithfully following)
ramayan::7061.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7061.essence: Their bond is stronger than mere possession; it is faithful belonging.
ramayan::7061.simple_meaning: Sita is Rama's wife, and he values her more than his own life. She remains faithfully devoted to him.
ramayan::7061.simple_insight: Love here is not casual affection. It is loyalty so deep that life itself becomes secondary.
ramayan::7061.detailed_meaning: Ravana's warning is building toward a moral boundary: Sita is not a prize to be taken. She belongs to Rama, the lion among men, and their bond is marked by mutual fidelity and value beyond life. This verse strengthens the case that follows.
ramayan::7061.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses a committed relationship as if it were easy to break. This verse reminds you that real bonds are not accessories — they are chosen loyalties with weight.
ramayan::7061.insight: It frames Sita not as an object in a dispute, but as someone held within a bond of unwavering fidelity.

ramayan::7062.verse_sanskrit: न सा धर्षयितुं शक्या मैथिल्योजस्विनः प्रिया । दीप्तस्येव हुताशस्य शिखा सीता सुमध्यमा । । 33720 । ।
ramayan::7062.verse_hindi: Sita is the darling of mighty Rama. With her slender waist, she is like the leaping flames of blazing fire and it is not possible  for you to touch her.
ramayan::7062.english_translation: Sita is the darling of mighty Rama. With her slender waist, she is like the leaping flames of blazing fire, and it is not possible for you to touch her.
ramayan::7062.translation_literal: न सा (she not) / धर्षयितुं (to violate, to touch forcibly) / शक्या (possible) / मैथिल्यः (of Maithili, Sita) / ओजस्विनः (of the powerful one) / प्रिया (beloved) / दीप्तस्य (of the blazing) / इव (like) / हुताशस्य (of fire) / शिखा (flame) / सीता (Sita) / सुमध्यमा (slender-waisted)
ramayan::7062.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7062.simple_meaning: Sita cannot be violated. She belongs to Rama, and her brilliance is compared to a flame that cannot be touched.
ramayan::7062.simple_insight: Some things are protected by their own radiance, not by force.
ramayan::7062.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned again and again that Sita is not an easy prize. Her beauty, dignity, and Rama’s power make her untouchable. This verse strengthens the argument before the final threat is stated.
ramayan::7062.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing past your no, pretending persistence is charm. This verse draws a hard line: dignity is not available for conquest.
ramayan::7062.insight: It reinforces that desire does not create permission. The mind must respect limits before action becomes harm.

ramayan::7063.verse_sanskrit: किमुद्यममिमं व्यर्थं कृत्वा ते राक्षसाधिप । दृष्टश्चेत्वं रणे तेन तदन्तं तव जीवितम् । । 33721 । ।
ramayan::7063.verse_hindi: O chief of the demons, why do you make this futile attempt ? The moment you are seen by Rama in war will be the last of your life.
ramayan::7063.english_translation: O chief of the demons, why do you make this futile attempt? The moment you are seen by Rama in war will be the last of your life.
ramayan::7063.translation_literal: किम् (why) / उद्यमम् (effort) / इमम् (this) / व्यर्थम् (futile) / कृत्वा (having made) / ते (your) / राक्षसाधिप (chief of the demons) / दृष्टः (seen) / चेद् (if) / त्वम् (you) / रणे (in battle) / तेन (by him) / तत्-अन्तम् (that end) / तव (your) / जीवितम् (life)
ramayan::7063.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7063.essence: Facing Rama in battle means the end of everything you are risking.
ramayan::7063.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that attacking Rama is pointless, because being seen by Rama in battle will mean death.
ramayan::7063.simple_insight: Some fights are already lost before they begin.
ramayan::7063.detailed_meaning: In the war outside Lanka, someone is warning Ravana not to push further. Rama is not just a rival warrior; he is the force Ravana cannot survive facing. This verse sharpens the threat into a final warning before the larger argument continues.
ramayan::7063.modern_relevance: You keep forcing a conversation, even though you already know where it ends. Some doors close the moment you walk through them.
ramayan::7063.insight: It pushes the mind to see when persistence has become self-destruction.

ramayan::7064.verse_sanskrit: जीवितं च सुखं चैव राज्यं चैव सुदुर्लभम् । यदीच्छसि चिरं भोक्तुं मा कृथा रामविप्रियम् । । 33722 । ।
ramayan::7064.verse_hindi: If you want to enjoy your life, happiness and even the kingdom which is not easily attainable for long, do not incur the displeasure of Rama.
ramayan::7064.english_translation: If you want to enjoy your life, happiness, and even the kingdom for a long time, do not incur Rama's displeasure.
ramayan::7064.translation_literal: जीवितम् (life) / च (and) / सुखम् (happiness) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सुदुर्लभम् (very hard to obtain) / यदि (if) / इच्छसि (you wish) / चिरम् (for long) / भोक्तुम् (to enjoy) / मा (do not) / कृथाः (do) / रामविप्रियम् (what is displeasing to Rama)
ramayan::7064.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7064.essence: Ravana's real enemy is the pride that risks everything he already has.
ramayan::7064.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned that his life, happiness, and hard-won kingdom can last only if he avoids provoking Rama.
ramayan::7064.simple_insight: Power feels secure until one wrong move exposes how fragile it really is.
ramayan::7064.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned that Rama is not an enemy he can casually offend. The speaker reminds him that life, pleasure, and even kingship are rare and fragile things, and that continuing this path will bring ruin.
ramayan::7064.modern_relevance: You know that one text, one email, one stubborn reply could turn a manageable situation into a disaster. This verse lands on that edge: some choices cost more than pride is worth.
ramayan::7064.insight: It shifts the mind from swagger to consequence, showing that reckless defiance can destroy what you most want to keep.

ramayan::7065.verse_sanskrit: स सर्वैस्सचिवैस्सार्धं विभीषणपुरोगमैः । मन्त्रयित्वा तु धर्मिष्ठैः कृत्वा निश्चयमात्मनः । । 33723 । । दोषाणां च गुणानां च सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलम् । आत्मनश्च बलं ज्ञात्वा राघवस्य च तत्वतः । । 33724 । । हिताहितं विनिश्चित्य क्षमं त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि ।
ramayan::7065.verse_hindi: After consulting all your ministers and the righteous persons led by Vibhisana, you may take a decision. Assess the real strength and weakness, merits and demerits  of your own and of Rama. Decide what is good or bad for you and then take steps you deem proper.
ramayan::7065.english_translation: After consulting all your ministers and the righteous persons led by Vibhishana, take your decision. Weigh the merits and faults, the strength and weakness of your side and of Rama's side. Decide what is truly good or harmful for you, and then act as you find fit.
ramayan::7065.translation_literal: सः (he) / सर्वैः (with all) / सचिवैः (with ministers) / सार्धम् (together with) / विभीषण-पुरोगमैः (with Vibhishana as leader) / मन्त्रयित्वा (having consulted) / तु (indeed) / धर्मिष्ठैः (with the righteous) / कृत्वा (having made) / निश्चयम् (a decision) / आत्मनः (of his own) / दोषाणाम् (of faults) / च (and) / गुणानाम् (of merits) / च (and) / सम्प्रधार्य (having fully considered) / बल-अबलम् (strength and weakness) / आत्मनः च (and of his own side) / बलम् (strength) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / राघवस्य च (and of Rama) / तत्त्वतः (truly) / हित-अहितम् (what is beneficial and harmful) / विनिश्चित्य (having determined) / क्षमम् (proper) / त्वम् (you) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you should)
ramayan::7065.speaker: Vibhishana
ramayan::7065.essence: Real judgment begins when you measure yourself honestly against reality.
ramayan::7065.simple_meaning: Before acting, you should consult wise advisers, examine both strengths and weaknesses, and decide what truly helps or harms you.
ramayan::7065.simple_insight: Clear judgment begins when ego stops rushing ahead.
ramayan::7065.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned by Vibhishana and other counselors. The issue is no longer pride but survival: he must compare his own strength with Rama's, hear honest advice, and choose with full awareness of the cost.
ramayan::7065.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, sign the contract, or make the call that cannot be undone. This verse asks you to slow down, check the facts, and hear the people who disagree with you.
ramayan::7065.insight: It teaches you to replace impulse with honest comparison and counsel before making a hard decision.

ramayan::7066.verse_sanskrit: अहं तु मन्ये तव न क्षमं रणे समागमं कोसलराजसूनुना । इदं हि भूयश्श़ृणु वाक्यमुत्तमं क्षमं च युक्तं च निशाचरेश्वर । । 33725 । ।
ramayan::7066.verse_hindi: O Ravana  I think it is not good on your part to confront the prince of Kosala in a war. Listen to my words and consider what is good for you.
ramayan::7066.english_translation: O Ravana, I think it is not right for you to meet the prince of Kosala in battle. Listen to my words and consider what is good for you, O lord of the night-dwellers.
ramayan::7066.translation_literal: अहम् (I) / तु (however) / मन्ये (think) / तव (for you) / न (not) / क्षमम् (proper) / रणे (in battle) / समागमम् (encounter) / कोसलराजसूनुना (with the son of the king of Kosala) / इदम् (this) / हि (indeed) / भूयः (further) / शृणु (listen) / वाक्यम् (speech) / उत्तमम् (excellent) / क्षमम् (proper) / च (and) / युक्तम् (appropriate) / च (and) / निशाचरेश्वर (lord of night-dwellers)
ramayan::7066.speaker: Vibhishana
ramayan::7066.essence: Pride can make a doomed battle feel necessary.
ramayan::7066.simple_meaning: Vibhishana warns Ravana not to fight Rama. He says the battle is not wise or fitting, and urges Ravana to listen carefully and choose what is truly beneficial.
ramayan::7066.simple_insight: Sometimes the bravest move is to stop before pride turns into ruin.
ramayan::7066.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana stands before Ravana and the war that is coming. He has already urged caution and counsel. Now he says plainly that meeting Rama in battle is not wise, because Ravana is heading toward a fight he cannot safely survive.
ramayan::7066.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the call, or walk into the meeting even though every part of you knows it will escalate things. Wisdom sometimes sounds like a warning you do not want to hear.
ramayan::7066.insight: It teaches you to accept hard counsel before ego turns a preventable conflict into disaster.

ramayan::7067.verse_sanskrit: कदाचिदप्यहं वीर्यात्पर्यटन्पृथिवीमिमाम् । बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्पर्वतोपमः । । 3381 । । नीलजीमूतसङ्काशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः । भयं लोकस्य जनयन्किरीटी परिघायुधः । । 3382 । । व्यचरं दण्डकारण्ये ऋषिमांसानि भक्षयन् ।
ramayan::7067.verse_hindi: Once I was roaming the earth, like a mountain possessing the  strength of a thousand elephants, like a dark cloud, wearing bright gold earrings and crown,holding a spear in hand, terrorising the people. I was wandering in Dandaka forest feeding on the flesh of ascetics.
ramayan::7067.english_translation: Once I was roaming the earth, like a mountain with the strength of a thousand elephants, dark as a rain cloud, wearing bright gold earrings and a crown, holding a spear, terrifying the people. I wandered through Dandaka forest, feeding on the flesh of ascetics.
ramayan::7067.translation_literal: कदाचित् (once) / अपि (also) / अहम् (I) / वीर्यात् (from strength) / पर्यटन् (wandering) / पृथिवीम् (the earth) / इमाम् (this) / बलम् (strength) / नागसहस्रस्य (of a thousand elephants) / धारयन् (bearing) / पर्वतोपमः (mountain-like) / नीलजीमूतसङ्काशः (resembling a dark cloud) / तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः (with bright golden earrings) / भयं (fear) / लोकस्य (of the people) / जनयन् (causing) / किरीटी (crowned) / परिघायुधः (with a spear as weapon) / व्यचरम् (I roamed) / दण्डकारण्ये (in Dandaka forest) / ऋषिमांसानि (the flesh of ascetics) / भक्षयन् (eating)
ramayan::7067.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7067.essence: He mistakes terror for greatness and treats cruelty as proof of strength.
ramayan::7067.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts about his former power and cruelty, describing himself as a terrifying wanderer who once hunted and ate ascetics in Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7067.simple_insight: Pride can turn violence into self-image, making cruelty sound like greatness.
ramayan::7067.detailed_meaning: Ravana is answering counsel with a boast. He recalls the time when he roamed the earth in fearsome form, armed and unstoppable, and even preyed on ascetics in Dandaka. The verse is not teaching restraint; it reveals the scale of his arrogance.
ramayan::7067.modern_relevance: Someone in a group chat keeps retelling the worst thing they ever did as if it proved strength. The room goes quiet, because the story is really about how far pride can distort a person.
ramayan::7067.insight: It shows how ego glorifies past harm instead of learning from it.

ramayan::7068.verse_sanskrit: विश्वामित्रोऽथ धर्मात्मा मद्वित्रस्तो महामुनिः । । 3383 । । स्वयं गत्वा दशरथं नरेन्द्रमिदमब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::7068.verse_hindi: Hence the great sage, righteous Visvamitra afraid of me, went to king Dasaratha  and said:
ramayan::7068.english_translation: Then the righteous great sage Visvamitra, afraid of me, went himself to King Dasaratha and said this.
ramayan::7068.translation_literal: विश्वामित्रः (Visvamitra) / अथ (then) / धर्मात्मा (righteous) / मद्वित्रस्तः (afraid of me) / महामुनिः (great sage) / स्वयं (himself) / गत्वा (having gone) / दशरथम् (to Dasaratha) / नरेन्द्रम् (king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::7068.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7068.essence: The verse is a setup, not the heart of the teaching.
ramayan::7068.simple_meaning: Visvamitra, filled with fear, went to King Dasaratha himself and spoke to him.
ramayan::7068.simple_insight: Some moments are only a bridge. What matters is the request that follows.
ramayan::7068.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra, the great sage, is described as going to Dasaratha in person after fearing Ravana's power. This line only sets up the real appeal that comes next: asking for Rama's protection during the sacrifice.
ramayan::7068.modern_relevance: A tense meeting begins with someone swallowing pride and asking for help. The real issue is still waiting to be spoken aloud.
ramayan::7068.insight: It shifts attention from the messenger to the urgent plea he is about to make.

ramayan::7069.verse_sanskrit: अद्य रक्षतु मां रामः पर्वकाले समाहितः । । 3384 । । मारीचान्मे भयं घोरं समुत्पन्नं नरेश्वर ।
ramayan::7069.verse_hindi: O king Maricha has created in me a great fear. Spare the self possessed Rama to protect me while I do the sacrifice.
ramayan::7069.english_translation: O king, Maricha has created a terrible fear in me. Let self-possessed Rama protect me today during the sacrificial rite.
ramayan::7069.translation_literal: अद्य (today) / रक्षतु (let protect) / मां (me) / रामः (Rama) / पर्वकाले (at the time of the rite) / समाहितः (self-possessed, focused) / मारीचान् (from Maricha) / मे (for me) / भयम् (fear) / घोरम् (terrible) / समुत्पन्नम् (has arisen) / नरेश्वर (O king)
ramayan::7069.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::7069.essence: A righteous task needs protection before it can be completed.
ramayan::7069.simple_meaning: Visvamitra asks Dasaratha to send Rama as protection for his sacrifice, because Maricha has frightened him.
ramayan::7069.simple_insight: Even a great sage needs protection when a vow is under threat.
ramayan::7069.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has gone to Dasaratha after being troubled by Maricha and other forces that disrupt his sacrificial work. He asks for Rama, calm and focused, to guard the rite. The verse is a practical request inside a larger appeal.
ramayan::7069.modern_relevance: You finally start the work you promised yourself, and one loud interruption threatens the whole thing. What you need is not more theory — just the right protection at the right time.
ramayan::7069.insight: It frames help as a duty to protect sacred work from disruption.

ramayan::7070.verse_sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्तो धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्तदा । । 3385 । । प्रत्युवाच महाभागं विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् ।
ramayan::7070.verse_hindi: When the great, venerable sage Visvamitra said so, the righteous king Dasaratha replied:
ramayan::7070.english_translation: When the great, venerable sage Visvamitra said so, the righteous king Dasaratha replied:
ramayan::7070.translation_literal: इत्येवम् (thus) / उक्तः (spoken to) / धर्मात्मा (righteous) / राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / तदा (then) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / महाभागम् (to the venerable) / विश्वामित्रम् (Visvamitra) / महामुनिम् (great sage)
ramayan::7070.speaker: Dasaratha
ramayan::7070.essence: A king answers, but his heart is already divided.
ramayan::7070.simple_meaning: Dasaratha answers Visvamitra after hearing his request.
ramayan::7070.simple_insight: A reply is only the beginning of a much harder choice.
ramayan::7070.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has asked for Rama to guard his sacrifice from Maricha. Dasaratha, the king and father, now answers the revered sage. This verse is the turning point before he reveals the conflict between a royal duty and a father's fear.
ramayan::7070.modern_relevance: You hear a request that pulls against your fear for your child. The answer comes next, but the cost is already in the room.
ramayan::7070.insight: It sets up the clash between personal attachment and the obligation that follows a promise.

ramayan::7071.verse_sanskrit: बालो द्वादशवर्षोऽयमकृतास्त्रश्च राघवः । । 3386 । । कामं तु मम यत्सैन्यं मया सह गमिष्यति ।
ramayan::7071.verse_hindi: My son Rama is only twelve. He is not experienced in the use of weapons. I shall accompany you with my army.
ramayan::7071.english_translation: My son Rama is only twelve. He is not experienced in the use of weapons. I shall accompany you with my army.
ramayan::7071.translation_literal: बालः (a boy) / द्वादशवर्षः (twelve years old) / अयम् (this one) / अकृतास्त्रः (untrained in weapons) / च (and) / राघवः (Raghava) / कामम् (indeed) / तु (but) / मम (my) / यत् (whatever) / सैन्यम् (army) / मया (with me) / सह (together) / गमिष्यति (will go)
ramayan::7071.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::7071.essence: A father offers himself when his son is still too young for war.
ramayan::7071.simple_meaning: Dasharatha says Rama is too young and untrained for battle, so he offers to go with Visvamitra using his own army.
ramayan::7071.simple_insight: Love can make you step in front of danger, even when the real sacrifice is yours.
ramayan::7071.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has asked for Rama to protect his sacrifice from Maricha and other threats. Dasharatha, hearing this, sees his twelve-year-old son being asked to face danger and tries to substitute himself and his army instead.
ramayan::7071.modern_relevance: Your child is being pushed into something too harsh too soon, and every part of you wants to take their place. The instinct is human; the cost of that protection is real.
ramayan::7071.insight: It shifts the mind from heroic demand to parental protection, showing how duty is tested by love.

ramayan::7072.verse_sanskrit: बलेन चतुरङ्गेण स्वयमेत्य निशाचरान् । । 3387 । । वधिष्यामि मुनिश्रेष्ठ शत्रूंस्ते मनसेप्सितान् ।
ramayan::7072.verse_hindi: O distinguished sage with the four divisions of my army I will slay the enemies you want me to.
ramayan::7072.english_translation: O distinguished sage, with the four divisions of my army I will myself go and slay the night-roaming enemies you wish to defeat.
ramayan::7072.translation_literal: बलेन (with [my] force) / चतुरङ्गेण (with the four-limbed [army]) / स्वयम् (myself) / एत्य (having come) / निशाचरान् (the night-roamers) / वधिष्यामि (I will slay) / मुनिश्रेष्ठ (O best of sages) / शत्रून् (the enemies) / ते (your) / मनसा-इप्सितान् (desired in mind)
ramayan::7072.speaker: Dasharatha
ramayan::7072.essence: Strength is useless if it misses the real request.
ramayan::7072.simple_meaning: Dasharatha offers to go with his army and destroy the enemies Visvamitra has in mind.
ramayan::7072.simple_insight: You can mean well and still miss what is actually needed.
ramayan::7072.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has asked for help, and King Dasharatha answers with royal confidence. He offers his full army and his own presence, ready to fight the enemies himself. But the sage is leading toward a different need, so this becomes a misunderstanding, not the solution.
ramayan::7072.modern_relevance: A friend says they need help moving through a breakup, and you immediately offer money, advice, and a plan. You mean it sincerely, but you may still be answering the wrong need.
ramayan::7072.insight: It shows the gap between eager help and the specific help a situation requires.

ramayan::7073.verse_sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्तस्समुनी राजानमिदमब्रवीत् । । 3388 । । रामान्नान्यद्बलं लोके पर्याप्तं तस्य रक्षसः ।
ramayan::7073.verse_hindi: When  the king thus responded to the sage,  he told him that none other than Rama in this world is a match for that demon.
ramayan::7073.english_translation: Then the sage said to the king: in this world, no one except Rama is strong enough for that demon.
ramayan::7073.translation_literal: इत्येवम् (thus) / उक्तः (having spoken) / सः (he) / मुनिः (the sage) / राजानम् (to the king) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said) / रामात् (from Rama) / न (not) / अन्यत् (other) / बलम् (strength) / लोके (in the world) / पर्याप्तम् (sufficient) / तस्य (for that) / रक्षसः (demon's)
ramayan::7073.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramayan::7073.essence: The need is so precise that only one person can answer it.
ramayan::7073.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra tells King Dasharatha that only Rama has the strength needed to face the demon.
ramayan::7073.simple_insight: Sometimes the right help is specific, not general.
ramayan::7073.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has come to Ayodhya asking for help against a demon threatening his sacrifice. Dasharatha offers his army and his own strength, but the sage narrows the need to one person: Rama. The moment shifts the whole request onto the prince.
ramayan::7073.modern_relevance: You are offered ten forms of help, but only one solves the real problem. The hardest part is hearing that the answer is specific, not bigger.
ramayan::7073.insight: It shifts attention from broad support to the exact person or action required.

ramayan::7074.verse_sanskrit: देवतानामपि भवान् समरेष्वभिपालकः । । 3389 । । आसीत्तव कृतं कर्म त्रिलोके विदितं नृप ।
ramayan::7074.verse_hindi: O king, you have protected even gods in wars and have been a guardian. Your deeds are very wellknown in the three worlds.
ramayan::7074.english_translation: O king, you have protected even the gods in battles. Your deeds are known throughout the three worlds.
