ramayan::7074.translation_literal: देवतानाम् (of the gods) / अपि (even) / भवान् (you) / समरेषु (in battles) / अभिपालकः (protector) / आसीत् (were) / तव (your) / कृतम् (done, accomplished) / कर्म (deed) / त्रिलोके (in the three worlds) / विदितम् (known) / नृप (O king)
ramayan::7074.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7074.essence: His protection is so proven that even the heavens know his name.
ramayan::7074.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as a warrior so renowned that even the gods have been protected by him, and his deeds are famous everywhere.
ramayan::7074.simple_insight: Greatness is not private; it becomes known through what it protects.
ramayan::7074.detailed_meaning: A sage is speaking to a king about Rama’s unmatched strength. He reminds him that Rama has already defended even the gods in battle and that his fame reaches across the three worlds. It is praise, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7074.modern_relevance: A recommendation lands on your desk that is less about the words and more about the reputation behind them. Some people arrive with proof already living in the room before they do.
ramayan::7074.insight: It frames Rama as a figure whose reputation is established by real action, not claim.

ramayan::7075.verse_sanskrit: काममस्तु महत्सैन्यं तिष्ठत्विह परन्तप । । 33810 । । बालोऽप्येष महातेजास्समर्थस्तस्य निग्रहे । गमिष्ये राममादाय स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु परन्तप । । 33811 । ।
ramayan::7075.verse_hindi: O scourge of foes as you wish, let your great army wait here. Even though Rama is young he is glorious, and capable of subduing the enemy. I will take him. Be blessed.
ramayan::7075.english_translation: O scourge of foes, as you wish, let your great army wait here. Even though Rama is young, he is glorious and able to subdue the enemy. I will take him. Be blessed.
ramayan::7075.translation_literal: कामम् (as you wish) / अस्तु (let it be) / महत्-सैन्यम् (great army) / तिष्ठतु (let it wait) / इह (here) / परन्तप (scourge of foes) / बालः अपि (even though young) / एषः (this one) / महा-तेजाः (of great splendour) / समर्थः (capable) / तस्य (of that) / निग्रहे (in restraining) / गमिष्ये (I will go) / रामम् (Rama) / आदाय (taking) / स्वस्ति (blessing, well-being) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may there be)
ramayan::7075.speaker: Visvamitra
ramayan::7075.essence: The needed force is not always the largest one.
ramayan::7075.simple_meaning: Visvamitra tells the king to leave the army behind. He says young Rama is powerful enough to handle the threat, and he will take Rama with him.
ramayan::7075.simple_insight: You can trust strength that has not yet been proven by age.
ramayan::7075.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has come to Dasharatha for help against dangerous forces in the forest. Instead of asking for soldiers, he asks for Rama alone, saying the boy is already powerful enough for the task. The moment tests the king's trust and Rama's readiness.
ramayan::7075.modern_relevance: You’re about to overbuild the solution, gather more people, and make it heavier than it needs to be. Then someone calm says: the right person is already here.
ramayan::7075.insight: It shifts you from relying on scale to recognising capacity.

ramayan::7076.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु स मुनिस्तमादाय नृपात्मजम् । जगाम परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रस्स्वमाश्रमम् । । 33812 । ।
ramayan::7076.verse_hindi: Sage Visvamitra saying so took the son of the king and went back very happily to his hermitage.
ramayan::7076.english_translation: Having said this, the sage Visvamitra took the king's son and returned to his hermitage, greatly pleased.
ramayan::7076.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / तु (indeed) / सः (he) / मुनिः (the sage) / तम् (him) / आदाय (taking) / नृपात्मजम् (the king's son) / जगाम (went) / परमप्रीतः (greatly pleased) / विश्वामित्रः (Visvamitra) / स्वम् (his own) / आश्रमम् (hermitage)
ramayan::7076.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7076.essence: The agreement is done; the next trial can begin.
ramayan::7076.simple_meaning: Visvamitra takes Rama with him and returns to his hermitage feeling very pleased.
ramayan::7076.simple_insight: Some moments are just movement between scenes, not teachings.
ramayan::7076.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has secured Dasharatha's agreement and now leaves with Rama, the king's son. The verse simply carries the action forward: the sage departs happily with the boy, setting up the next stage of training.
ramayan::7076.modern_relevance: You finish the conversation, stand up, and walk out with the plan settled. The real work starts after the agreement, not during it.
ramayan::7076.insight: It moves the story from negotiation to preparation.

ramayan::7077.verse_sanskrit: तं तदा दण्डकारण्ये यज्ञमुद्दिश्य दीक्षितम् । बभूवोपस्थितो रामश्चित्रं विष्फारयन्धनुः । । 33813 । ।
ramayan::7077.verse_hindi: Then Rama was initiated for the protection of sacrifices and stood on guard, stretching his wonderful bow.
ramayan::7077.english_translation: Then Rama, consecrated for the protection of sacrifices in the Dandaka forest, stood ready, drawing his wondrous bow.
ramayan::7077.translation_literal: तं (him) / तदा (then) / दण्डकारण्ये (in the Dandaka forest) / यज्ञम् (for the sacrifice) / उद्दिश्य (with reference to) / दीक्षितम् (consecrated) / बभूवोपस्थितः (stood present/ready) / रामः (Rama) / चित्रम् (wonderful) / विष्फारयन् (stretching) / धनुः (bow)
ramayan::7077.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7077.essence: He does not merely arrive; he arrives ready to guard what is sacred.
ramayan::7077.simple_meaning: Rama arrives in the Dandaka forest to protect a sacrifice and stands ready with his bow drawn.
ramayan::7077.simple_insight: Readiness matters when something sacred is under threat.
ramayan::7077.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has just brought Rama to his hermitage. Now, in the Dandaka forest, Rama takes his place as protector of the sacrifice, bow in hand. The verse is scene-setting, showing him ready for the duty ahead.
ramayan::7077.modern_relevance: You arrive at the venue before sunrise, phone off, sleeves rolled up, because people are counting on you to hold the line.
ramayan::7077.insight: It shifts attention from arrival to readiness: you show up prepared to protect what matters.

ramayan::7078.verse_sanskrit: अजातव्यञ्जनश्रीमान्पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणः । एकवस्त्रधरो धन्वी शिखी कनकमालया । । 33814 । । शोभयन् दण्डकारण्यं दीप्तेन स्वेन तेजसा । अदृश्यत ततो रामो बालचन्द्र इवोदितः । । 33815 । ।
ramayan::7078.verse_hindi: Thereafter, handsome Rama, with eyes like lotus petals, beards ungrown, clad in a single garment with knotted hair on the head, wielding a bow, with a chain of gold, luminous with his own lustre enhanced the glory of Dandaka forest by looking like the young moon just risen.
ramayan::7078.english_translation: Thereafter, handsome Rama, with eyes like lotus petals, beards ungrown, clad in a single garment with knotted hair on the head, wielding a bow, with a chain of gold, luminous with his own lustre enhanced the glory of Dandaka forest by looking like the young moon just risen.
ramayan::7078.translation_literal: अजात-व्यञ्जन-श्रीमान् (one whose beauty had not yet fully matured) / पद्म-पत्र-निभ-ईक्षणः (with eyes like lotus petals) / एक-वस्त्र-धरः (wearing a single garment) / धन्वी (bow-bearing) / शिखी (with knotted hair) / कनक-मालया (with a golden garland) / शोभयन् (illuminating) / दण्डकारण्यम् (the Dandaka forest) / दीप्तेन (with radiant) / स्वेन (his own) / तेजसा (splendour) / अदृश्यत (was seen) / ततः (then) / रामः (Rama) / बाल-चन्द्रः इव (like the young moon) / उदितः (risen)
ramayan::7078.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7078.essence: His presence alone turns exile into splendour.
ramayan::7078.simple_meaning: Rama appears in the forest, young and radiant, carrying his bow and wearing simple clothes. His presence makes the whole forest seem brighter.
ramayan::7078.simple_insight: Even in exile, dignity can make a place feel alive.
ramayan::7078.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has brought Rama into Dandaka to protect the sacrificial rites. After the initiation, Rama stands there as a young, armed prince in simple dress, glowing with his own presence. The verse pauses on his appearance before the next threat arrives.
ramayan::7078.modern_relevance: You walk into a room with nothing to prove, only quiet presence. Without trying to impress anyone, you change the atmosphere.
ramayan::7078.insight: It shifts attention from what Rama does to the moral radiance he carries into danger.

ramayan::7079.verse_hindi: Then looking like a dark cloud, wearing bright golden earrings, proud of power bestowed on me with boons, I arrived at the hermitage.
ramayan::7079.english_translation: Then, looking like a dark cloud, wearing bright golden earrings, strong and swollen with pride from boons, I arrived at that hermitage.
ramayan::7079.translation_literal: ततः (then) / अहम् (I) / मेघ-सङ्काशः (cloud-like) / तप्त-काञ्चन-कुण्डलः (with heated-gold earrings) / बली (strong) / दत्त-वर-उदर्पात् (from pride due to granted boons) / आजगाम (came) / तद्-आश्रमम् (to that hermitage)
ramayan::7079.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7079.essence: Boons made him bold, and boldness carried him straight into restraint.
ramayan::7079.simple_meaning: Ravana says he came to the hermitage in a fearsome form, proud of the power his boons had given him.
ramayan::7079.simple_insight: Power can make you feel untouchable right before it leads you into danger.
ramayan::7079.detailed_meaning: Ravana describes his own arrival at the hermitage where Rama was guarding the sages. He comes armed, proud, and overconfident, setting up the clash that follows in the next verse.
ramayan::7079.modern_relevance: You walk into a room certain that your status will carry you through. The air changes the moment you meet someone who is calmer, steadier, and harder to shake than you expected.
ramayan::7079.insight: It shows how pride blinds strength and pushes conflict toward its own undoing.

ramayan::7080.verse_sanskrit: तेन दृष्टः प्रविष्टोऽहं सहसैवोद्यतायुधः । मां तु दृष्ट्वा धनुस्सज्यमसम्भ्रान्तश्चकार सः । । 33817 । ।
ramayan::7080.verse_hindi: I entered at once and lifted my weapons. Rama saw me and unperturbed, started stringing his bow.
ramayan::7080.english_translation: I entered at once and lifted my weapons. Rama saw me and, unperturbed, started stringing his bow.
ramayan::7080.translation_literal: तेन (by him) / दृष्टः (seen) / प्रविष्टः (entered) / अहम् (I) / सहसा एव (at once) / उद्यत-आयुधः (with raised weapons) / माम् (me) / तु (but) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / धनुः सज्यम् (the bow strung) / असम्भ्रान्तः (unshaken) / चकार (made) / सः (he)
ramayan::7080.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7080.essence: Rama meets sudden violence without losing his composure.
ramayan::7080.simple_meaning: Ravana rushed in with weapons ready, but Rama stayed calm and immediately prepared his bow.
ramayan::7080.simple_insight: Real strength is the ability to stay composed when someone else comes at you hard.
ramayan::7080.detailed_meaning: Ravana is describing his own charge into the scene. He enters with weapons raised, expecting fear or hesitation. Instead, Rama sees him and responds without confusion, calmly stringing his bow. The verse is a combat detail, not a teaching.
ramayan::7080.modern_relevance: Someone cuts into your space with anger, and your whole body wants to react. This verse is the image of meeting force without losing your center.
ramayan::7080.insight: It shows how steadiness can answer aggression before panic takes over.

ramayan::7081.verse_sanskrit: अवजानन्नहं मोहाद्बालोऽयमिति राघवम् । विश्वामित्रस्य तां वेदिमभ्यधावं कृतत्वरः । । 33818 । ।
ramayan::7081.verse_hindi: Out of my delusion I underestimated the young boy, and screaming, ran towards Visvamitras sacrificial altar.
ramayan::7081.english_translation: Out of delusion, I underestimated Rama as only a boy and rushed toward Vishwamitra's sacrificial altar in haste.
ramayan::7081.translation_literal: अवजानन् (underestimating) / अहम् (I) / मोहात् (out of delusion) / बालः (a boy) / अयम् (this one) / इति (thus) / राघवम् (Rama) / विश्वामित्रस्य (of Vishvamitra) / ताम् (that) / वेदिम् (sacrificial altar) / अभ्यधावम् (I rushed toward) / कृतत्वरः (hastily)
ramayan::7081.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7081.essence: He lost the moment he mistook power for youth.
ramayan::7081.simple_meaning: Ravana admits that he misjudged Rama because of his own confusion and rushed forward too quickly.
ramayan::7081.simple_insight: Underestimating someone can be more dangerous than their strength.
ramayan::7081.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recounting his own defeat. He remembers seeing Rama at Vishvamitra's sacrificial altar, dismissing him as a mere boy, and charging ahead in arrogance. The verse shows the exact mistake that led to his downfall.
ramayan::7081.modern_relevance: You brush past the quiet person in the room, assuming they are harmless. By the time you realise your mistake, the damage is already done.
ramayan::7081.insight: It exposes how delusion turns judgment into reckless action.

ramayan::7082.verse_sanskrit: तेन मुक्तस्ततो बाणः शितश्शत्रुनिबर्हणः । तेनाहं त्वाहतः क्षिप्तस्समुद्रे शतयोजने । । 33819 । ।
ramayan::7082.verse_hindi: Then Rama released a sharp arrow that could kill the enemy. It struck me and threw me at a distance of hundred yojanas into the sea.
ramayan::7082.english_translation: Then Rama released a sharp arrow that could kill the enemy. It struck me and threw me a hundred yojanas into the sea.
ramayan::7082.translation_literal: तेन (by that) / मुक्तः (released) / ततः (then) / बाणः (arrow) / शितः (sharp) / शत्रु-निबर्हणः (destroying enemies) / तेन (by that) / अहम् (I) / तु (indeed) / आहतः (struck) / क्षिप्तः (thrown) / समुद्रे (into the sea) / शत-योजने (hundred yojanas)
ramayan::7082.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7082.essence: One arrow ended Ravana's certainty and sent him flying.
ramayan::7082.simple_meaning: Rama shot a deadly arrow, and it hurled the speaker far into the sea.
ramayan::7082.simple_insight: A single, precise act can end overconfidence in an instant.
ramayan::7082.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recalling the moment he rushed at Rama in the forest and was met with a devastating arrow. The verse is not teaching a principle on its own; it is part of Ravana's account of how quickly Rama overpowered him.
ramayan::7082.modern_relevance: You charge in certain you have the upper hand, and one clean response sends you back stunned. Pride rarely survives first contact with reality.
ramayan::7082.insight: It shows how arrogance collapses when it meets disciplined force.

ramayan::7083.verse_sanskrit: नेच्छता तात मां हन्तुं तदा वीरेण रक्षितः । रामस्य शरवेगेन निरस्तोऽहमचेतनः । । 33820 । ।
ramayan::7083.verse_hindi: O dear being thrown away by the speed of his dart I lost my consciousness. I was protected by Rama who did not want to kill me.
ramayan::7083.english_translation: Rama did not want to kill me. His arrow’s force hurled me away, and I lost consciousness.
ramayan::7083.translation_literal: नेच्छता (not wanting) / तात (dear one) / माम् (me) / हन्तुम् (to kill) / तदा (then) / वीरेण (by the heroic one) / रक्षितः (protected) / रामस्य (Rama's) / शरवेगेन (by the speed of the arrow) / निरस्तः (thrown away) / अहम् (I) / अचेतनः (unconscious)
ramayan::7083.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7083.essence: Rama’s blow was strong enough to stop him, yet not meant to kill.
ramayan::7083.simple_meaning: Rama did not intend to kill Ravana here. The force of his arrow flung Ravana away so violently that he lost consciousness.
ramayan::7083.simple_insight: Even in battle, Rama’s restraint is greater than his force.
ramayan::7083.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recounting his first clash with Rama near Vishvamitra’s sacrifice. After underestimating the boy and charging in, he is struck and hurled away. This line is a supporting detail in his own account of defeat, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::7083.modern_relevance: You can be overwhelmed by someone’s response and still realize they were holding back. Not every defeat comes from full force.
ramayan::7083.insight: It shifts attention from raw power to restrained power: strength guided by intention, not rage.

ramayan::7084.verse_sanskrit: पातितोऽहं तदा तेन गम्भीरे सागराम्भसि । प्राप्य संज्ञां चिरात्तात लङ्कां प्रतिगतः पुरीम् । । 33821 । ।
ramayan::7084.verse_hindi: O dear I was thrown into the deep sea and after a long time regained consciousness and  returned to the city of Lanka.
ramayan::7084.english_translation: I was thrown into the deep sea by him, and after a long time I regained consciousness and returned to the city of Lanka.
ramayan::7084.translation_literal: पातितः (thrown down) / अहम् (I) / तदा (then) / तेन (by him) / गम्भीरे (into the deep) / सागराम्भसि (in the waters of the sea) / प्राप्य (having regained) / संज्ञाम् (consciousness) / चिरात् (after a long time) / तात (dear one) / लङ्काम् (to Lanka) / प्रतिगतः (returned) / पुरीम् (to the city)
ramayan::7084.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7084.essence: A single strike can leave you adrift before you find yourself again.
ramayan::7084.simple_meaning: He was hurled into the deep sea, lost consciousness, and only later made it back to Lanka.
ramayan::7084.simple_insight: Survival can be a long, stunned return after one hard blow.
ramayan::7084.detailed_meaning: This is part of a warrior’s account of being struck by Rama’s arrow and cast far away. He describes sinking into the sea, recovering much later, and returning to Lanka. The verse supports the larger claim that Rama’s strike was overwhelming.
ramayan::7084.modern_relevance: After a brutal setback, you may not recover at once. Sometimes you come back only after shock, distance, and time have done their work.
ramayan::7084.insight: It shifts attention from the blow itself to the slow process of regaining composure.

ramayan::7085.verse_sanskrit: एवमस्मि तदा मुक्तस्सहायास्तु निपातिताः । अकृतास्त्रेण बालेन रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । । 33822 । ।
ramayan::7085.verse_hindi: That way I was spared by the young boy who was not versed in archery and who could still accomplish the task with ease.Those who accompanied me were destroyed.
ramayan::7085.english_translation: I was spared by that young boy who was not skilled in weapons, while my companions were struck down by Rama, who could accomplish hard tasks without strain.
ramayan::7085.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / अस्मि (I was) / तदा (then) / मुक्तः (released/spared) / सहायाः (companions) / तु (indeed) / निपातिताः (were struck down) / अकृतास्त्रेण (by one untrained in weapons) / बालेन (by the young one) / रामेण (by Rama) / अक्लिष्टकर्मणा (by one whose actions are effortless)
ramayan::7085.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7085.essence: Youth and inexperience did not weaken Rama's force.
ramayan::7085.simple_meaning: Ravana says he survived Rama's attack, but the companions around him were killed. He admits Rama was young, yet still effective and effortless in action.
ramayan::7085.simple_insight: Even a wounded ego can tell the truth: the opponent was stronger than expected.
ramayan::7085.detailed_meaning: Ravana is warning others after surviving an encounter with Rama. He recalls being thrown into the sea while the men around him were destroyed. The verse is part of a larger argument meant to stop reckless conflict with Rama.
ramayan::7085.modern_relevance: You dismiss someone as inexperienced, then realize they handled the crisis better than anyone expected. That quiet competence can be more dangerous than obvious force.
ramayan::7085.insight: It shifts the mind from underestimating appearance to respecting actual capability.

ramayan::7086.verse_sanskrit: तन्मया वार्यमाणस्त्वं यदि रामेण विग्रहम् । करिष्यस्यापदं घोरां क्षिप्रं प्राप्स्यसि रावण । । 33823 । ।
ramayan::7086.verse_hindi: If you pick up conflict with Rama even while being warned by me you will soon face a
ramayan::7086.english_translation: If you choose to fight Rama even after I have warned you, Ravana, you will quickly meet a terrible calamity.
ramayan::7086.translation_literal: तत् (that) / मया (by me) / वार्यमाणः (being warned, being restrained) / त्वम् (you) / यदि (if) / रामेण (with Rama) / विग्रहम् (conflict, battle) / करिष्यसि (you will do, you will undertake) / आपदं (disaster, calamity) / घोराम् (terrible, fierce) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / प्राप्स्यसि (you will obtain, you will meet) / रावण (Ravana)
ramayan::7086.speaker: Vibhishana
ramayan::7086.essence: Ignoring clear warning turns a bad choice into a fast ruin.
ramayan::7086.simple_meaning: Vibhishana warns Ravana that if he continues toward battle with Rama, he will quickly meet disaster.
ramayan::7086.simple_insight: Pride can make danger obvious and still unbearable to hear.
ramayan::7086.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Vibhishana has already tried to stop Ravana from walking into ruin. Ravana refuses to listen. This verse is the warning sharpened into a final prediction: Rama is not a fight Ravana can survive.
ramayan::7086.modern_relevance: You can feel the collapse coming in a relationship, a deal, or a habit — and still keep pushing. This verse names the cost of refusing the warning you already understand.
ramayan::7086.insight: It shifts the mind from stubborn momentum to honest self-check before disaster hardens.

ramayan::7087.verse_sanskrit: क्रीडारतिविधिज्ञानां समाजोत्सवशालिनाम् । रक्षसां चैव सन्तापमनर्थं चाहरिष्यसि । । 33824 । ।
ramayan::7087.verse_hindi: You will bring grief and disaster into the lives of demons who are sporting in love and who are in the habit of celebrating community festivals with joy.
ramayan::7087.english_translation: You will bring grief and disaster into the lives of demons who are sporting in love and who are in the habit of celebrating community festivals with joy.
ramayan::7087.translation_literal: क्रीडारति (sporting in love) / विधिज्ञानाम् (those who know the proper ways) / समाजोत्सवशालिनाम् (those who delight in community festivals) / रक्षसाम् (of the demons) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सन्तापम् (grief) / अनर्थम् (disaster) / च (and) / आहरिष्यसि (you will bring)
ramayan::7087.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7087.essence: One violent choice can shatter an entire community.
ramayan::7087.simple_meaning: Rama's opposition will not just hurt Ravana. It will also bring sorrow and ruin to the lives and celebrations of the people around him.
ramayan::7087.simple_insight: A selfish choice never stays private; it spreads pain into the whole world around it.
ramayan::7087.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been warned that fighting Rama will end in ruin. The warning widens here: the consequences will not stop with Ravana himself, but will spill into Lanka's people, their pleasures, and their public life. This is part of a tightening argument, not the final teaching.
ramayan::7087.modern_relevance: You make one reckless decision, and suddenly the whole house feels it — the mood, the plans, the people who had no say in it.
ramayan::7087.insight: It shifts the mind from personal impulse to the wider damage it creates.

ramayan::7088.verse_sanskrit: हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधां नानारत्नविभूषिताम् । द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं पुरीं लङ्कां विनष्टां मैथिलीकृते । । 33825 । ।
ramayan::7088.verse_hindi: You will see the city of Lanka dotted with magnificent royal mansions embellished  with different kinds of gems ruined for the sake of Sita.
ramayan::7088.english_translation: You will see the city of Lanka, filled with palaces and glittering with many kinds of jewels, ruined because of Sita.
ramayan::7088.translation_literal: हर्म्य-प्रासाद-सम्बाधाम् (crowded with mansions and palaces) / नाना-रत्न-विभूषिताम् (adorned with many kinds of jewels) / द्रक्ष्यसि (you will see) / त्वम् (you) / पुरीम् (the city) / लङ्काम् (Lanka) / विनष्टाम् (destroyed) / मैथिली-कृते (for the sake of Maithili / Sita)
ramayan::7088.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7088.essence: Splendor means nothing when one obsession brings everything down.
ramayan::7088.simple_meaning: Lanka, once full of splendid palaces and jewels, will be destroyed because of Sita.
ramayan::7088.simple_insight: A city’s beauty cannot protect it when arrogance drives it toward ruin.
ramayan::7088.detailed_meaning: A warning is being delivered to Ravana after his refusal to listen. The speaker points to Lanka itself: a glittering city of palaces and jewels that will be reduced to ruin because of its king’s obsession with Sita. The threat is no longer abstract.
ramayan::7088.modern_relevance: You can build something dazzling and still lose it by one stubborn choice. A company, a family, a reputation — beauty does not protect what pride keeps breaking.
ramayan::7088.insight: It shifts attention from outward splendor to the cost of one destructive fixation.

ramayan::7089.verse_sanskrit: अकुर्वन्तोऽपि पापानि शुचयः पापसंश्रयात् । परपापैर्विनश्यन्ति मत्स्या नागह्रदे यथा । । 33826 । ।
ramayan::7089.verse_hindi: Even without committing any sin those pure souls because they keep company with sinners will be destroyed for the sins of others just like fishes in a pool of serpents.
ramayan::7089.english_translation: Even without committing any sin, pure people who stay in the company of the wicked are destroyed by others' wrongdoing, like fish in a pool of serpents.
ramayan::7089.translation_literal: अकुर्वन्तः (not doing) / अपि (even) / पापानि (sins) / शुचयः (the pure) / पापसंश्रयात् (from association with evil) / परपापैः (by others' sins) / विनश्यन्ति (are destroyed) / मत्स्याः (fish) / नागह्रदे (in a serpent-pool) / यथा (like)
ramayan::7089.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7089.essence: Even innocence can be destroyed by the company it keeps.
ramayan::7089.simple_meaning: Even a good person can be ruined by staying close to harmful people. Other people's wrongdoing can pull you down too.
ramayan::7089.simple_insight: Not every fall begins with your own mistake; sometimes proximity is enough.
ramayan::7089.detailed_meaning: Ravana is warning Sita that Lanka is a dangerous place and that even the innocent can be harmed by the moral corruption around them. He compares pure beings to fish trapped in a serpent pool: surrounded by danger, they do not survive.
ramayan::7089.modern_relevance: You keep showing up to a group chat that turns cruel, and after a few weeks you feel heavier, sharper, less like yourself. The damage may not start with you, but it still reaches you.
ramayan::7089.insight: It shifts attention from personal innocence alone to the danger of the moral environment you choose.

ramayan::7090.verse_hindi: You will see the demons who smear their limbs with sandal paste and unguents, who are adorned with excellent ornaments slain and laid on the ground for your mistakes.
ramayan::7090.english_translation: You will see the demons who smear their limbs with sandal paste and unguents, who are adorned with excellent ornaments, slain and laid on the ground because of your own fault.
ramayan::7090.translation_literal: दिव्यचन्दन (divine sandal paste) / दिग्धाङ्गान् (limbs smeared) / दिव्याभरण (excellent ornaments) / भूषितान् (adorned) / द्रक्ष्यसि (you will see) / अभिहतान् (struck down) / भूमौ (on the ground) / तव (your) / दोषात् (because of fault) / तु (indeed) / राक्षसान् (demons)
ramayan::7090.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7090.essence: Adornment cannot shield you from the ruin your choices create.
ramayan::7090.simple_meaning: The demons will be seen dead on the ground, despite their luxury and ornaments, because of Ravana's own wrongdoing.
ramayan::7090.simple_insight: Beauty and status do not protect anyone from the consequences of harmful choices.
ramayan::7090.detailed_meaning: The warning to Ravana continues: Lanka's richly adorned demons will be cut down and left on the ground. Their polish, ornaments, and wealth will not save them, because the ruin comes from Ravana's own fault and the war he has brought on.
ramayan::7090.modern_relevance: You can dress a bad decision in polish, status, and confidence. When the consequences arrive, the surface still falls away.
ramayan::7090.insight: It shifts attention from appearances to consequences.

ramayan::7091.verse_sanskrit: हृतदारान् सदारांश्च दश विद्रवतो दिशः । हतशेषानशरणान्द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं निशाचरान् । । 33828 । ।
ramayan::7091.verse_hindi: You will see the rest of the demons with their wives gone or fleeing in all directions helplessly with none to take care of them.
ramayan::7091.english_translation: You will see the remaining demons, with their wives taken or fleeing in all directions, helpless and without protection.
ramayan::7091.translation_literal: हृतदारान् (with wives taken away) / सदारान् (with wives) / च (and) / दश (in ten) / विद्रवतः (fleeing) / दिशः (directions) / हतशेषान् (the remnants of the slain) / अशरणान् (helpless, without refuge) / द्रक्ष्यसि (you will see) / त्वम् (you) / निशाचरान् (night-roamers, demons)
ramayan::7091.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7091.essence: Violence leaves even the survivors without shelter.
ramayan::7091.simple_meaning: The remaining demons will be scattered, their households broken, and they will have no protection left.
ramayan::7091.simple_insight: Power built on harm collapses into fear and helplessness.
ramayan::7091.detailed_meaning: In this part of the war prophecy, the speaker describes what Lanka will look like after Ravana's defeat. The surviving demons will be scattered, stripped of family stability, and left with nowhere to turn. It is a grim detail in a larger vision of total ruin.
ramayan::7091.modern_relevance: A crowd that once looked untouchable can unravel overnight when the thing holding it together is gone. What seemed like strength can turn into panic, scattering, and silence.
ramayan::7091.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing violent power to seeing its fragility.

ramayan::7092.verse_sanskrit: शरजालपरिक्षिप्तामग्निज्वालासमावृताम् । प्रदग्धभवनां लङ्कां द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं न संशयः । । 33829 । ।
ramayan::7092.verse_hindi: You will undoubtedly see Lanka filled with arrows, surrounded by flames of fire and its buildings on fire.
ramayan::7092.english_translation: You will undoubtedly see Lanka filled with arrows, surrounded by flames of fire and its buildings on fire.
ramayan::7092.translation_literal: शरजालपरिक्षिप्ताम् (surrounded by a net of arrows) / अग्निज्वालासमावृताम् (enveloped by flames of fire) / प्रदग्धभवनाम् (with burned buildings) / लङ्काम् (Lanka) / द्रक्ष्यसि (you will see) / त्वम् (you) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::7092.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7092.essence: Wrong action can turn a whole city into ash.
ramayan::7092.simple_meaning: Lanka will be attacked so fiercely that arrows and fire will cover the city, and its buildings will burn.
ramayan::7092.simple_insight: Some consequences arrive as total destruction, not a warning.
ramayan::7092.detailed_meaning: The warning continues as the enemy city is described in ruins: arrows everywhere, flames rising, homes burning. It is part of a larger threat meant to shake Ravana before the final moral judgment lands.
ramayan::7092.modern_relevance: A careless choice can keep building until the damage is no longer private. Then the collapse is visible to everyone.
ramayan::7092.insight: It sharpens the cost of wrongdoing by showing its public, irreversible aftermath.

ramayan::7093.verse_sanskrit: परदाराभिमर्शात्तु नान्यत्पापतरं महत् । प्रमदानां सहस्रं च तव राजन्परिग्रहः । । 33830 । ।
ramayan::7093.verse_hindi: O king there is no sin greater than violating the chastity of others wives, when you have married a thousand lovely women.
ramayan::7093.english_translation: O king, there is no greater wrong than violating another man's wife. You already possess a thousand women.
ramayan::7093.translation_literal: परदाराभिमर्शात् (from touching another's wife) / तु (indeed) / न (not) / अन्यत् (other) / पापतरम् (more sinful) / महत् (great) / प्रमदानाम् (of women) / सहस्रम् (a thousand) / च (and) / तव (your) / राजन् (O king) / परिग्रहः (possession)
ramayan::7093.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7093.essence: Having plenty does not excuse taking what is forbidden.
ramayan::7093.simple_meaning: Taking another man's wife is presented as a grave wrong, especially when you already have many women of your own.
ramayan::7093.simple_insight: Desire becomes ruin when it ignores boundaries.
ramayan::7093.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned after Sita's abduction. The warning is sharp and personal: a king who already has countless women has crossed a line that will bring destruction on himself and his kingdom.
ramayan::7093.modern_relevance: You know the moment when wanting turns into entitlement — the text stops you there. It says some choices are not just unwise; they are corrosive to your character and your world.
ramayan::7093.insight: It shifts attention from appetite to restraint, showing that power without limits becomes self-destruction.

ramayan::7094.verse_sanskrit: भव स्वदारनिरतस्वकुलं रक्ष राक्षस । मानमृद्धिं च राज्यं च जीवितं चेष्टमात्मनः । । 33831 । ।
ramayan::7094.verse_hindi: Enjoy with your wives. Protect your race, prestige, kingdom, prosperity and your own dear life.
ramayan::7094.english_translation: Enjoy with your own wives, O demon. Protect your family line, honor, kingdom, prosperity, and your own dear life.
ramayan::7094.translation_literal: भव (be) / स्वदारनिरत (devoted to your own wives) / स्वकुलं (your own family line) / रक्ष (protect) / राक्षस (O demon) / मानम् (honor) / ऋद्धिं (prosperity) / च (and) / राज्यं (kingdom) / च (and) / जीवितं (life) / च (and) / इष्टम् (dear) / आत्मनः (of yourself)
ramayan::7094.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7094.essence: Pride can put your whole life at risk for one wrong desire.
ramayan::7094.simple_meaning: Ravana is warned to stay with his own wives and protect everything he values: his family, honor, kingdom, wealth, and life.
ramayan::7094.simple_insight: Some choices cost too much to keep making. Protect what remains before pride destroys it.
ramayan::7094.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already been warned that Lanka will burn if he keeps Sita. This line sharpens the warning: if he wants to preserve his family, status, kingdom, and life, he must stop provoking Rama. It is a final practical appeal before ruin.
ramayan::7094.modern_relevance: You know the conversation has turned dangerous when someone says, 'Protect what you still have.' That is the last warning before pride starts taking everything.
ramayan::7094.insight: It turns the issue from desire to consequences: one stubborn act can endanger every other good you still possess.

ramayan::7095.verse_sanskrit: कलत्राणि च सौम्यानि मित्रवर्गं तथैव च । यदीच्छसि चिरं भोक्तं मा कृथा रामविप्रियम् । । 33832 । ।
ramayan::7095.verse_hindi: If you wish to enjoy your beautiful wives and your good friends for long, do not create enmity with Rama.
ramayan::7095.english_translation: If you wish to enjoy your beautiful wives and your good friends for long, do not create enmity with Rama.
ramayan::7095.translation_literal: कलत्राणि (wives) / च (and) / सौम्यानि (pleasant, beautiful) / मित्रवर्गं (circle of friends) / तथैव (just so, likewise) / च (and) / यदि (if) / इच्छसि (you wish) / चिरं (for a long time) / भोक्तं (to enjoy) / मा (do not) / कृथा (do) / रामविप्रियम् (Rama-displeasure, enmity with Rama)
ramayan::7095.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7095.essence: Rama's anger is not worth the ruin it can bring.
ramayan::7095.simple_meaning: Ravana warns that anyone who wants to keep his wives and friends for long should not provoke Rama.
ramayan::7095.simple_insight: Some enemies are too costly to make.
ramayan::7095.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to stop his own people from crossing a line. After warning that harming another man's wife is a grave wrong, he adds that enmity with Rama will destroy a man's home, friendships, and future. The verse is part of a warning, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::7095.modern_relevance: You are about to send that message that turns a small clash into a lasting feud. Sometimes the real wisdom is knowing which conflict will cost you more than it can ever win.
ramayan::7095.insight: It shifts the mind from impulsive provocation to seeing the long cost of conflict.

ramayan::7096.verse_sanskrit: निवार्यमाणस्सुहृदा मया भृशं प्रसह्य सीतां यदि धर्षयिष्यसि । गमिष्यसि क्षीणबलस्सबान्धवो यमक्षयं रामशरात्तजीवितः । । 33833 । ।
ramayan::7096.verse_hindi: If you violate Sita forcibly notwithstanding my friendly warning, your life will be drained by the arrows of Rama and you will reach the abode of Yama with your kith and kin, your strength depleted.
ramayan::7096.english_translation: If you violate Sita forcibly despite my friendly warning, Rama's arrows will drain your strength and you will go to Yama with your kin.
ramayan::7096.translation_literal: निवार्यमाणः (being restrained) / सुहृदा (by a friend) / मया (by me) / भृशम् (strongly) / प्रसह्य (forcibly) / सीताम् (Sita) / यदि (if) / धर्षयिष्यसि (you will violate) / गमिष्यसि (you will go) / क्षीणबलः (with strength exhausted) / स-बान्धवः (together with your relatives) / यमक्षयम् (to Yama's abode) / रामशरात्तजीवितः (your life taken by Rama's arrows)
ramayan::7096.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7096.essence: Ignoring a clear warning turns desire into ruin.
ramayan::7096.simple_meaning: Ravana warns that if Sita is harmed, Rama will destroy the offender and his family.
ramayan::7096.simple_insight: Some warnings are not threats — they are the last chance to turn back.
ramayan::7096.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned by a well-wisher before the final disaster. The speaker says that forcing Sita will bring Rama's arrows, ruin strength, and end in death for Ravana and his kin. It is part of a larger argument, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::7096.modern_relevance: A friend tells you, one last time, that a reckless choice will wreck everything. You hear the warning, but your pride keeps talking.
ramayan::7096.insight: It frames disregard for restraint as the point where consequences become irreversible.

ramayan::7097.verse_sanskrit: एवमस्मि तदा मुक्तः कथञ्चित्तेन संयुगे । इदानीमपि यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणुष्व निरुत्तरम् । । 3391 । ।
ramayan::7097.verse_hindi: I was somehow saved by him this way in the combat.Listen without any reply to what has taken place recently.
ramayan::7097.english_translation: I was somehow saved by him in that battle. Now listen, without interruption, to what happened afterward.
ramayan::7097.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / अस्मि (I was) / तदा (then) / मुक्तः (saved/released) / कथञ्चित् (somehow) / तेन (by him) / संयुगे (in battle) / इदानीम् (now) / अपि (also) / यत् (what) / वृत्तम् (happened) / तत् (that) / शृणुष्व (listen) / निरुत्तरम् (without reply)
ramayan::7097.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7097.essence: Survival is only the opening; the rest still demands to be heard.
ramayan::7097.simple_meaning: The speaker says he survived a battle thanks to someone else, and now asks the listener to hear the rest of the story without interrupting.
ramayan::7097.simple_insight: Sometimes the real story begins after survival, not before it.
ramayan::7097.detailed_meaning: The speaker is continuing a story of danger and rescue. He says he was saved in battle, then immediately asks for silence so he can recount what happened next. The verse is a bridge, not the main teaching.
ramayan::7097.modern_relevance: Someone cuts in while you're finally explaining what happened. You need one clean sentence of patience before the rest of the story can be told.
ramayan::7097.insight: It shifts attention from the rescue itself to the sequence of events that follows.

ramayan::7098.verse_sanskrit: राक्षसाभ्यामहं द्वाभ्यामनिर्विण्णस्तथा कृतः । सहितो मृगरूपाभ्यां प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम् । । 3392 । ।
ramayan::7098.verse_hindi: Having done so, I picked up courage and entered Dandaka forest, accompanied by the two other demons in the form of deer .
ramayan::7098.english_translation: Having done so, I gathered my courage and entered Dandaka forest with the two deer-shaped demons.
ramayan::7098.translation_literal: राक्षसाभ्याम् (with two demons) / अहम् (I) / द्वाभ्याम् (by two) / अनिर्विण्णः (not discouraged) / तथा (thus) / कृतः (made) / सहितः (accompanied) / मृगरूपाभ्याम् (by two in deer form) / प्रविष्टः (entered) / दण्डकावनम् (Dandaka forest)
ramayan::7098.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7098.essence: He mistook surviving once for being safe.
ramayan::7098.simple_meaning: Ravana says he entered Dandaka forest, no longer shaken, with two deer-shaped companions.
ramayan::7098.simple_insight: The line shows a mind hardening itself after danger, not learning from it.
ramayan::7098.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recounting his own actions after surviving an earlier clash. He says he regained courage and went into Dandaka forest with two demons disguised as deer. The verse is a step in his story, not a teaching.
ramayan::7098.modern_relevance: You get through one hard encounter and immediately move into the next, still carrying the same blind spot.
ramayan::7098.insight: It shows how confidence can return without wisdom, pushing you back into danger.

ramayan::7099.verse_sanskrit: दीप्तजिह्वो महाकायस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रो महाबलः । व्यचरं दण्डकारण्यं मांसभक्षो महामृगः । । 3393 । ।
ramayan::7099.verse_hindi: I wandered in Dandaka forest in the form of a huge animal with a big and strong body, a flaming red tongue and sharp teeth feeding on flesh.
ramayan::7099.english_translation: I wandered through Dandaka forest as a huge flesh-eating beast, with a blazing tongue, massive body, and sharp fangs.
ramayan::7099.translation_literal: दीप्तजिह्वः (with blazing tongue) / महाकायः (huge-bodied) / तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः (sharp-fanged) / महाबलः (very powerful) / व्यचरम् (I wandered) / दण्डकारण्यम् (Dandaka forest) / मांसभक्षः (flesh-eating) / महामृगः (great beast)
ramayan::7099.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7099.essence: Might without restraint becomes something feral.
ramayan::7099.simple_meaning: Ravana describes himself moving through Dandaka forest in a terrifying beast-form, feeding on flesh.
ramayan::7099.simple_insight: Power without restraint turns a being into a threat, not a protector.
ramayan::7099.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recounting his own dreadful roaming in Dandaka forest. He is not teaching a principle here; he is describing the fear he spread while moving in monstrous form among the sages and forests of exile.
ramayan::7099.modern_relevance: A person who enters a room already angry can feel larger than life and still be deeply out of control.
ramayan::7099.insight: It frames brute force as a sign of inner corruption, not strength.

ramayan::7100.verse_sanskrit: अग्निहोत्रेषु तीर्थेषु चैत्यवृक्षेषु रावण । अत्यन्तघोरो व्यचरं तापसान्सम्प्रधर्षयन् । । 3394 । ।
ramayan::7100.verse_hindi: O Ravana, assuming a very dreadful form, I wandered about sacrificial spots, sacred places, river banks, under huge trees planted at quadranglestorturing the ascetics.
ramayan::7100.english_translation: O Ravana, assuming a very dreadful form, I wandered about sacrificial spots, sacred places, river banks, and under huge trees, tormenting the ascetics.
ramayan::7100.translation_literal: अग्निहोत्रेषु (in sacrificial fires) / तीर्थेषु (at sacred places) / चैत्यवृक्षेषु (under sacred trees) / रावण (O Ravana) / अत्यन्तघोरः (extremely dreadful) / व्यचरम् (I wandered about) / तापसान् (ascetics) / सम्प्रधर्षयन् (tormenting, assaulting)
ramayan::7100.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7100.essence: Violence does not stay outside holy places; it invades them.
ramayan::7100.simple_meaning: A fearsome being roamed through holy places and tormented ascetics wherever they gathered.
ramayan::7100.simple_insight: Cruelty spreads even into places meant for prayer and peace.
ramayan::7100.detailed_meaning: The speaker is describing his own monstrous wandering in Dandaka forest. He moved through sacrificial grounds, sacred spots, riverbanks, and holy trees, attacking ascetics there. The verse is part of a grim sequence showing escalating violence, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7100.modern_relevance: A person who enjoys humiliating others will not stop at public spaces, workplaces, or homes. The urge to dominate can poison even places meant for rest and reverence.
ramayan::7100.insight: It shows how unchecked aggression turns sacred spaces into targets.

ramayan::7101.verse_sanskrit: निहत्य दण्डकारण्ये तापसान्धर्मचारिणः । रुधिराणि पिबंस्तेषां तथा मांसानि भक्षयन् । । 3395 । ।
ramayan::7101.verse_hindi: I wandered  about the Dandaka forest slaying righteous ascetics, drinking their blood and eating their flesh.
ramayan::7101.english_translation: I wandered about the Dandaka forest, slaying righteous ascetics, drinking their blood, and eating their flesh.
ramayan::7101.translation_literal: निहत्य (having slain) / दण्डकारण्ये (in Dandaka forest) / तापसान् (ascetics) / धर्मचारिणः (who follow dharma) / रुधिराणि (bloods) / पिबन् (drinking) / तेषाम् (of them) / तथा (and) / मांसानि (flesh) / भक्षयन् (eating)
ramayan::7101.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7101.simple_meaning: A terrifying being boasts that he roamed the forest killing holy men and feeding on their blood and flesh.
ramayan::7101.simple_insight: Unchecked cruelty turns power into corruption.
ramayan::7101.detailed_meaning: Ravana is describing his own monstrous roaming in Dandaka, where he attacked ascetics who lived by discipline and ritual. The verse is not teaching a principle; it deepens his self-portrait as a force of violation before the larger story of his downfall.
ramayan::7101.modern_relevance: A person in power who starts enjoying the harm they cause has crossed a dangerous line. The damage is no longer accidental — it has become identity.
ramayan::7101.insight: It shows how violence can become self-image when restraint is gone.

ramayan::7102.verse_hindi: While thus roaming, I harmed the wanderers of the forest. Intoxicated with their blood
ramayan::7102.english_translation: While roaming like this, I terrified the forest dwellers. Drunk on blood, I moved about as a destroyer of righteousness.
ramayan::7102.translation_literal: ऋषिमांसाशनः (one who eats sages' flesh) / क्रूरः (cruel) / त्रासयन् (frightening) / वनगोचरान् (forest wanderers) / तथा (thus) / रुधिरमत्तः (intoxicated with blood) / अहम् (I) / विचरन् (roaming) / धर्मदूषकः (corrupting righteousness)
ramayan::7102.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7102.simple_meaning: Ravana is describing his own violent past in the forest: he terrorized holy men and forest dwellers, feeding on blood and destroying righteous life.
ramayan::7102.simple_insight: Unchecked violence turns a person into a danger even to their own mind.
ramayan::7102.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recounting his own actions in Dandaka forest: he hunted ascetics, drank their blood, and terrified anyone living there. This is not a teaching verse but part of a self-revealing speech that shows the scale of his cruelty before the next encounter with Rama.
ramayan::7102.modern_relevance: A person who keeps feeding anger until cruelty feels normal eventually scares everyone around them — and stops noticing what they have become.
ramayan::7102.insight: It shows how repeated violence hardens into identity.

ramayan::7103.verse_sanskrit: आसादयं तदा रामं तापसं धर्मचारिणम् । वैदेहीं च महाभागां लक्ष्मणं च महारथम् । । 3397 । ।
ramayan::7103.verse_hindi: I encountered again the righteous Rama who was in the form of an ascetic, with venerable Sita and the great warrior Lakshmana.
ramayan::7103.english_translation: I encountered Rama, the righteous ascetic, together with noble Sita and Lakshmana, the great warrior.
ramayan::7103.translation_literal: आसादयम् (I encountered) / तदा (then) / रामम् (Rama) / तापसम् (ascetic) / धर्मचारिणम् (one who follows righteousness) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi, Sita) / च (and) / महाभागाम् (noble, fortunate) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / च (and) / महारथम् (great warrior)
ramayan::7103.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7103.essence: The meeting is named before the wound is explained.
ramayan::7103.simple_meaning: Ravana says he came upon Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana in the forest.
ramayan::7103.simple_insight: The encounter is being set up, not explained yet.
ramayan::7103.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recalling the moment he came upon Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana in the forest. The verse only names who was present; the next lines explain how he judged Rama and why that meeting turned into hostility.
ramayan::7103.modern_relevance: You remember the moment before everything changed: the person, the place, the look that made the next choice inevitable.
ramayan::7103.insight: It sets the scene for Ravana's remembered grievance, before the judgment and violence unfold.

ramayan::7104.verse_sanskrit: तापसं नियताहारं सर्वभूतहिते रतम् । सोऽहं वनगतं रामं परिभूय महाबलम् । । 3398 । । तापसोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् । अभ्यधावं हि संक्रुद्धस्तीक्ष्ण शृङ्गो मृगाकृतिः । । 3399 । । जिघांसुरकृतप्रज्ञस्तं प्रहारमनुस्मरन् ।
ramayan::7104.verse_hindi: Although Rama was very strong, he was living on restricted diet, engaged in the welfare of all beings. Treating him as a mere ascetic living in the forest, remembering my past hostility with him and disregarding his (fatal) blow, I ran towards him angrily, assuming the form of a sharphorned animal with an intention to kill him.
ramayan::7104.english_translation: Although Rama was very strong, he was living on restricted diet, engaged in the welfare of all beings. Treating him as a mere ascetic living in the forest, remembering my past hostility with him and disregarding his fatal blow, I ran towards him angrily, assuming the form of a sharp-horned animal with an intention to kill him.
ramayan::7104.translation_literal: तापसम् (ascetic) / नियताहारम् (with restricted food) / सर्वभूतहिते (in the welfare of all beings) / रतम् (engaged) / सः (he) / अहम् (I) / वनगतम् (gone to the forest) / रामम् (Rama) / परिभूय (disregarding) / महाबलम् (very strong) / तापसः (ascetic) / अयम् (this) / इति (thus) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / पूर्ववैरम् (previous hostility) / अनुस्मरन् (remembering) / अभ्यधावम् (I ran) / हि (indeed) / संक्रुद्धः (angry) / तीक्ष्णशृङ्गः (sharp-horned) / मृगाकृतिः (having the form of a deer) / जिघांसुः (desiring to kill) / अकृतप्रज्ञः (without wisdom) / तम् (him) / प्रहारम् (the blow) / अनुस्मरन् (remembering)
ramayan::7104.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7104.essence: Knowing the danger, he ran at it anyway.
ramayan::7104.simple_meaning: Maricha admits that he saw Rama's strength and holiness, but still rushed at him in anger, driven by old hatred and a desire to kill.
ramayan::7104.simple_insight: Anger can make you ignore what you clearly see.
ramayan::7104.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha remembers Rama's earlier blow, but pride and old hostility overtake caution. Seeing Rama as an ascetic, he still charges in deer form, choosing revenge over judgment. This is the moment that seals his own ruin.
ramayan::7104.modern_relevance: You know someone is stronger, wiser, or steadier than you are — and you still pick the fight because an old wound is driving you.
ramayan::7104.insight: It shows how resentment can overpower clear perception and push you into self-destructive action.

ramayan::7105.verse_sanskrit: तेन मुक्तास्त्रयो बाणाश्शिताश्शत्रुनिबर्हणाः । । 33910 । । विकृष्य बलवच्चापं सुपर्णानिलनिस्स्वनाः ।
ramayan::7105.verse_hindi: His mighty bow drawn, Rama released three sharp darts that came whizzing like Garuda or the wind. They could destroy the enemy.
ramayan::7105.english_translation: His mighty bow drawn, Rama released three sharp darts that came whizzing like Garuda or the wind. They could destroy the enemy.
ramayan::7105.translation_literal: तेन (by him) / मुक्ताः (released) / त्रयः (three) / बाणाः (arrows) / शिताः (sharp) / शत्रुनिबर्हणाः (enemy-destroying) / विकृष्य (having drawn back) / बलवत् (powerfully) / चापम् (bow) / सुपर्णानिलनिस्स्वनाः (with the sound of Garuda and wind)
ramayan::7105.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7105.essence: Clean force matters more than noise in decisive moments.
ramayan::7105.simple_meaning: Rama draws his bow and fires three deadly arrows with great force and speed.
ramayan::7105.simple_insight: Skill matters when action must be exact, not merely strong.
ramayan::7105.detailed_meaning: In the battle against Ravana's forces, Rama stands with his bow fully drawn and looses three sharp arrows. The verse lingers on their force and sound, showing the precision and violence of the war, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7105.modern_relevance: A problem lands on your desk and you stop talking. You make one clean move, and it has to count.
ramayan::7105.insight: It shifts attention from drama to precise execution under pressure.

ramayan::7106.verse_sanskrit: ते बाणा वज्रसङ्काशास्सुमुक्ता रक्तभोजनाः । आजग्मुस्सहितास्सर्वे त्रयस्सन्नतपर्वणः । । 33911 । ।
ramayan::7106.verse_hindi: All the three tightly jointed, welltargetted darts, strong as thunderbolt, and which could feed on blood came together all at once.
ramayan::7106.english_translation: All the three tightly jointed, well-targeted darts, strong as thunderbolt, and which could feed on blood came together all at once.
ramayan::7106.translation_literal: ते (those) / बाणाः (arrows) / वज्रसङ्काशाः (thunderbolt-like) / सुमुक्ताः (well released) / रक्तभोजनाः (blood-feeding) / आजग्मुः (came) / सहिताः (together) / सर्वे (all) / त्रयः (three) / सन्नतपर्वणः (with bent joints)
ramayan::7106.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7106.essence: The arrows mattered because they were precise, not because they were many.
ramayan::7106.simple_meaning: The three arrows Rama released flew together with devastating force.
ramayan::7106.simple_insight: Sometimes a single, precise act is enough to end what seemed unstoppable.
ramayan::7106.detailed_meaning: Rama has already drawn his bow and loosed three deadly arrows at the enemy. This verse simply describes their terrifying speed and force as they strike together, carrying the battle forward rather than offering a separate teaching.
ramayan::7106.modern_relevance: A problem you've been circling for weeks suddenly meets one clean, decisive move. The force matters less than the precision.
ramayan::7106.insight: It keeps the focus on exact action, not on dramatic struggle.

ramayan::7107.verse_sanskrit: पराक्रमज्ञो रामस्य शठो दृष्टभयः पुरा । समुद्भान्तस्ततोमुक्तस्तावुभौ राक्षसौ हतौ । । 33912 । ।
ramayan::7107.verse_hindi: Having known Ramas prowess earlier and experienced tremendous fear, I ran away in a bewildered state as I was deceitful. The other two demons (who had accompanied me) succumbed.
ramayan::7107.english_translation: Having known Rama's prowess earlier and already filled with fear, I fled in confusion as a deceitful one; the other two demons were slain.
ramayan::7107.translation_literal: पराक्रमज्ञः (knower of prowess) / रामस्य (of Rama) / शठः (deceitful one) / दृष्टभयः (one who has seen fear) / पुरा (earlier) / समुद्भान्तः (thrown into confusion) / ततः (then) / मुक्तः (escaped) / तावुभौ (those two) / राक्षसौ (demons) / हतौ (were slain)
ramayan::7107.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7107.essence: He survived by fleeing, while his companions fell.
ramayan::7107.simple_meaning: A demon who already knew Rama's power panicked, fled in confusion, and survived while his two companions were killed.
ramayan::7107.simple_insight: Fear can break even a hardened enemy before the blow lands.
ramayan::7107.detailed_meaning: Rama's arrows have just struck in battle. One demon admits he had already learned Rama's strength and ran in terror, while the other two fell. The verse is part of a combat sequence, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7107.insight: It shows how fear and confusion can decide the outcome before open defeat.

ramayan::7108.verse_sanskrit: शरेण मुक्तो रामस्य कथञ्चित्प्राप्य जीवितम् । इह प्रव्राजितो युक्तस्तापसोऽहं समाहितः । । 33913 । ।
ramayan::7108.verse_hindi: With my escape from Ramas darts I somehow got a fresh lease of life. Now I am composed. I have started living the life of a recluse here. I have turned an ascetic.
ramayan::7108.english_translation: With my escape from Rama's arrows I somehow got a fresh lease of life. Now I am composed. I have taken up the life of an ascetic here.
ramayan::7108.translation_literal: शरेण (by an arrow) / मुक्तः (released, escaped) / रामस्य (of Rama) / कथञ्चित् (somehow) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / जीवितम् (life) / इह (here) / प्रव्राजितः (gone forth, become a wanderer) / युक्तः (fit, proper, composed) / तापसः (ascetic) / अहम् (I) / समाहितः (settled, composed)
ramayan::7108.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7108.essence: Survival made him change his dress, not his nature.
ramayan::7108.simple_meaning: Ravana says he survived Rama's arrows, calmed himself, and now lives as an ascetic in the forest.
ramayan::7108.simple_insight: Fear can force a proud mind into humility, at least outwardly.
ramayan::7108.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking after being struck by Rama's power and escaping with his life. He admits the shock changed him enough to live like an ascetic, but the next verse shows this is still haunted, unstable speech rather than true transformation.
ramayan::7108.modern_relevance: After a public failure, you can announce a new beginning and still be running from the same wound. The costume changes faster than the mind.
ramayan::7108.insight: It shows how fear can produce a temporary change in behaviour without real inner surrender.

ramayan::7109.verse_sanskrit: वृक्षे वृक्षे च पश्यामि चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरम् । गृहीतधनुषं रामं पाशहस्तमिवान्तकम् । । 33914 । ।
ramayan::7109.verse_hindi: I see Rama in every tree, clad in bark and deerskin, wielding the bow, holding a noose in hand like the god of death.
ramayan::7109.english_translation: I see Rama in every tree, clad in bark and deerskin, wielding the bow, holding a noose in hand like the god of death.
ramayan::7109.translation_literal: वृक्षे वृक्षे (in every tree) / च (and) / पश्यामि (I see) / चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरम् (clad in bark and deerskin) / गृहीतधनुषम् (holding a bow) / रामम् (Rama) / पाशहस्तमिव (as if holding a noose in hand) / अन्तकम् (the ender / death)
ramayan::7109.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7109.essence: Fear turns one man into the whole forest.
ramayan::7109.simple_meaning: Ravana says he sees Rama everywhere in the forest, armed and terrifying, as if death itself were near.
ramayan::7109.simple_insight: Fear can make one enemy seem to fill the whole world.
ramayan::7109.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking after narrowly escaping Rama. Shaken by fear, he projects Rama onto every tree and shadow in the forest, seeing the exiled prince not as a man but as a force of death closing in on him.
ramayan::7109.modern_relevance: After a bad meeting, you walk past every doorway expecting another blow. One sharp fear can make the whole day look hostile.
ramayan::7109.insight: It shows how fear magnifies one threat until everything feels dangerous.

ramayan::7110.verse_sanskrit: अपि रामसहस्राणि भीतः पश्यामि रावण । रामभूतमिदं सर्वमरण्यं प्रतिभाति मे । । 33915 । ।
ramayan::7110.verse_hindi: O Ravana I see in my fear thousands of Ramas. The entire forest appears to me as though filled with Rama.
ramayan::7110.english_translation: O Ravana, in my fear I see thousands of Ramas. The whole forest seems filled with Rama to me.
ramayan::7110.translation_literal: अपि (even) / रामसहस्राणि (thousands of Ramas) / भीतः (afraid) / पश्यामि (I see) / रावण (O Ravana) / रामभूतम् (as though made of Rama) / इदम् (this) / सर्वम् (all) / अरण्यम् (forest) / प्रतिभाति (appears) / मे (to me)
ramayan::7110.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7110.essence: Fear turns one enemy into the whole world.
ramayan::7110.simple_meaning: Fear makes Rama seem to be everywhere. Ravana feels surrounded by him even in the forest.
ramayan::7110.simple_insight: Terror can shrink your world until one presence seems to fill everything.
ramayan::7110.detailed_meaning: Ravana has fled after surviving Rama's arrows. Shaken and no longer composed, he tells himself that Rama appears in every tree and patch of forest. This is not a teaching verse but a frightened man’s confession of being mentally overrun.
ramayan::7110.modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you replay one person’s face in every quiet corner of the day. Fear can make a single presence feel inescapable.
ramayan::7110.insight: It shows how fear projects the same threat onto everything around you.

ramayan::7111.verse_sanskrit: राममेव हि पश्यामि रहिते राक्षसाधिप । दृष्ट्वा स्वप्नगतं राममुद्भ्रमामि विचेतनः । । 33916 । ।
ramayan::7111.verse_hindi: O king of the demons  I see only Rama even in solitude. When I see him in a dream  I lose my senses in a state of bewilderment.
ramayan::7111.english_translation: O king of the demons, I see only Rama even in solitude. When I see him in a dream, I lose my senses in bewilderment.
ramayan::7111.translation_literal: राममेव (Rama alone) / हि (indeed) / पश्यामि (I see) / रहिते (in solitude) / राक्षसाधिप (O lord of the demons) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / स्वप्नगतं (in a dream) / रामम् (Rama) / उद्भ्रमामि (I become confused) / विचेतनः (senseless)
ramayan::7111.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7111.essence: Fear has already conquered the mind before the battle begins.
ramayan::7111.simple_meaning: Ravana says that Rama fills his mind even when he is alone, and even dreams of Rama leave him shaken and confused.
ramayan::7111.simple_insight: What you fear most can keep living in your mind after the moment has passed.
ramayan::7111.detailed_meaning: Ravana is already unsettled by Rama's presence. In this exchange, he admits that Rama haunts his solitude and even his dreams. The verse deepens his fear, showing that the real battle is already inside his mind.
ramayan::7111.modern_relevance: You replay one hard conversation in bed, then again in the shower, then again in a dream. The body is quiet, but the mind keeps meeting what it cannot settle.
ramayan::7111.insight: It shows how fear can dominate attention until even rest becomes restless.

ramayan::7112.verse_sanskrit: रकारादीनि नामानि रामत्रस्तस्य रावण । रत्नानि च रथाश्चैव त्रासं संजनयन्ति मे । । 33917 । ।
ramayan::7112.verse_hindi: O Ravana, every name beginning with the letter Ra, such as Ratna (gems), Ratha (chariot), etc. strike terror in me.
ramayan::7112.english_translation: O Ravana, every name beginning with the letter Ra, such as Ratna (gems), Ratha (chariots), and the like, terrify me.
ramayan::7112.translation_literal: रकारादीनि (beginning with Ra) / नामानि (names) / रामत्रस्तस्य (of the one terrified by Rama) / रावण (O Ravana) / रत्नानि (gems) / च (and) / रथाश्चैव (chariots also) / त्रासं (fear) / संजनयन्ति (generate) / मे (in me)
ramayan::7112.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7112.essence: His fear has become so total that even syllables unsettle him.
ramayan::7112.simple_meaning: Ravana says that anything beginning with the sound “Ra” now frightens him, because Rama dominates his mind so completely.
ramayan::7112.simple_insight: Fear has narrowed his world until even ordinary words feel like omens.
ramayan::7112.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in a tense exchange after Rama has become an all-consuming presence in his mind. He admits that even harmless things like gems and chariots, simply because they begin with "Ra," now fill him with dread. It shows how thoroughly Rama has unsettled him.
ramayan::7112.modern_relevance: You hear a name, a place, or a reminder and your body tightens before your mind can explain why. Old fear can make harmless things feel charged.
ramayan::7112.insight: It shows how obsession can distort perception until the mind mistakes ordinary details for threats.

ramayan::7113.verse_sanskrit: अहं तस्य प्रभावज्ञो न युद्धं तेन ते क्षमम् । बलिं वा नमुचिं वापि हन्याद्धि रघुनन्दनः । । 33918 । ।
ramayan::7113.verse_hindi: I know his power.It is not proper to wage a war with him. Rama, delight of the Raghu dynasty, can slay even Bali or Namuchi.
ramayan::7113.english_translation: I know his power. It is not proper to wage a war with him. Rama, delight of the Raghu dynasty, can slay even Bali or Namuchi.
ramayan::7113.translation_literal: अहम् (I) / तस्य (his) / प्रभाव-ज्ञः (knower of power) / न (not) / युद्धम् (war) / तेन (with him) / ते (for you) / क्षमम् (proper) / बलिम् (Bali) / वा (or) / नमुचिम् (Namuchi) / वा (or) / अपि (even) / हन्यात् (would slay) / हि (indeed) / रघुनन्दनः (Rama, delight of Raghu)
ramayan::7113.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7113.essence: Honest fear can see what pride refuses to admit.
ramayan::7113.simple_meaning: Ravana admits that Rama is too powerful to fight directly. He says Rama could defeat even the greatest warriors, so war would be foolish.
ramayan::7113.simple_insight: Real strength begins with honest recognition of what you are facing.
ramayan::7113.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking under pressure, still trying to sound composed while fear leaks through his words. He admits that Rama's power is beyond ordinary opponents and warns that open war would be a mistake, because Rama can defeat even legendary foes.
ramayan::7113.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that starts a fight you cannot finish. Part of you already knows the other side is stronger, and this verse names that uneasy clarity before disaster.
ramayan::7113.insight: It teaches you to assess power honestly before escalating conflict.

ramayan::7114.verse_sanskrit: रणे रामेण युद्ध्यस्व क्षमां वा कुरु राक्षस । न ते रामकथा कार्या यदि मां द्रष्टुमिच्छसि । । 33919 । ।
ramayan::7114.english_translation: Fight with Rama in battle, or make peace, O Rakshasa. If you wish to see me, do not speak of Rama again.
ramayan::7114.translation_literal: रणे (in battle) / रामेण (by Rama) / युद्ध्यस्व (fight) / क्षमां (peace/forgiveness) / वा (or) / कुरु (do) / राक्षस (O Rakshasa) / न (not) / ते (your) / रामकथा (talk of Rama) / कार्या (to be done) / यदि (if) / माम् (me) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / इच्छसि (you wish)
ramayan::7114.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7114.essence: Fear wants silence, not more reminder.
ramayan::7114.simple_meaning: Ravana tells the enemy to either fight Rama or make peace, but not to keep talking about Rama if he wants to see him.
ramayan::7114.simple_insight: When fear is real, even words about the feared person can feel unbearable.
ramayan::7114.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking from fear and pride at once. He tells his messenger that if he wants Ravana to listen, he must stop repeating Rama's name and choose either battle or peace. The verse shows Ravana's growing unease.
ramayan::7114.modern_relevance: You know that feeling when one person's name keeps landing like a blow in the middle of a tense conversation. Sometimes the mind is already cornered before any decision is made.
ramayan::7114.insight: It shows how fear can make even discussion feel like defeat, pushing the mind toward immediate action or denial.

ramayan::7115.verse_sanskrit: बहवस्साधवो लोके युक्ता धर्ममनुष्ठिताः । परेषामपराधेन विनष्ठास्सपरिच्छदाः । । 33920 । ।
ramayan::7115.verse_hindi: There were many pious men in this world who practise yoga and dharma .They have been destroyed along with their retinue due to mistakes committed by others.
ramayan::7115.english_translation: Many good people in this world, devoted to dharma and disciplined practice, have been destroyed along with their followers because of other people's wrongdoing.
ramayan::7115.translation_literal: बहवः (many) / साधवः (good people) / लोके (in the world) / युक्ताः (disciplined, devoted) / धर्मम् (dharma) / अनुष्ठिताः (practising) / परेषाम् (of others) / अपराधेन (by wrongdoing) / विनष्ठाः (destroyed) / सपरिच्छदाः (along with their retinue)
ramayan::7115.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7115.essence: Other people's wrongdoing can bring down the innocent.
ramayan::7115.simple_meaning: Good people can be ruined by mistakes they did not make. Their discipline and virtue do not always protect them from another person's wrongdoing.
ramayan::7115.simple_insight: It softens blame and sharpens compassion for people hurt by circumstances beyond their control.
ramayan::7115.detailed_meaning: Ravana is pressing Sita to submit, and she answers with moral clarity. She points out that many disciplined, righteous people in the world have already been destroyed because of someone else's offence. Her suffering is real, but she refuses to treat it as proof of weakness.
ramayan::7115.modern_relevance: You did everything right, and still the project collapsed because someone else cut corners. This verse names that unfairness without pretending virtue always shields you from damage.
ramayan::7115.insight: It shifts blame away from the victim and toward the real source of harm.

ramayan::7116.verse_sanskrit: सोऽऽहं तवापराधेन विनश्येयं निशाचर । कुरु यत्ते क्षमं तत्त्वमहं त्वा नानुयामि ह । । 33921 । ।
ramayan::7116.verse_hindi: O demon   As such, I will perish due to your offence. You may do anything you deem appropriate. I will not follow you.
ramayan::7116.english_translation: O demon, I will perish because of your offence. Do whatever you think fit; I will not follow you.
ramayan::7116.translation_literal: सः (that one/I) / अहम् (I) / तव (your) / अपराधेन (because of offence) / विनश्येयम् (may perish) / निशाचर (O night-walker) / कुरु (do) / यत् (whatever) / ते (to you) / क्षमम् (fit) / तत् (that) / अहम् (I) / त्वा (you) / न (not) / अनुयामि (follow) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7116.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7116.essence: You may suffer for another’s wrongdoing, but you need not join it.
ramayan::7116.simple_meaning: He says he may suffer because of the demon’s wrongdoing, but he will not submit or go along with it.
ramayan::7116.simple_insight: You can refuse to cooperate with harm, even when it costs you.
ramayan::7116.detailed_meaning: In Ravana’s court, the pressure is tightening around the captive speaker. He answers without pleading: if the other man chooses wrong, the ruin is his own. He will not be dragged into it or made to comply.
ramayan::7116.modern_relevance: A colleague pressures you to sign off on something you know is crooked. You may lose favor, but you do not have to become part of the lie.
ramayan::7116.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to clean refusal.

ramayan::7117.verse_sanskrit: रामश्च हि महातेजा महासत्त्वो महाबलः । । 33922 । । अपि राक्षसलोकस्य न भवेदन्तकोऽपि सः ।
ramayan::7117.verse_hindi: Rama is brilliant, powerful and strong. I hope he will not be the god of death for the world of demons.
ramayan::7117.english_translation: Rama is brilliant, powerful, and strong. May he not become the destroyer of the demon world.
ramayan::7117.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / च (and) / हि (indeed) / महातेजाः (greatly brilliant) / महासत्त्वः (of great strength) / महाबलः (very powerful) / अपि (even) / राक्षसलोकस्य (of the demon world) / न (not) / भवेत् (may he be) / अन्तकः (destroyer) / अपि (even) / सः (he)
ramayan::7117.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7117.essence: Rama’s strength is so great it makes his enemies speak in fear.
ramayan::7117.simple_meaning: Rama is described as brilliant, strong, and powerful, with the hope that he will not become the destroyer of the demon world.
ramayan::7117.simple_insight: Power can be praised even while fear follows it.
ramayan::7117.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a tense exchange, Ravana speaks about Rama’s force and brilliance. The line is not a teaching on its own; it is part of a larger argument about Rama’s threat to the demon world and the speaker’s fear of his power.
ramayan::7117.modern_relevance: You can hear respect in someone’s voice even when they are warning themselves. A person may look calm on the outside and still feel the pressure of a force they cannot ignore.
ramayan::7117.insight: It frames Rama’s strength as real enough to alter the balance of power, not just a compliment.

ramayan::7118.verse_sanskrit: यदि शूर्पणखाहेतोर्जनस्थानगतः खरः । । 33923 । । अतिवृत्तो हतः पूर्वं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । अत्र ब्रूहि यथातत्त्वं को रामस्य व्यतिक्रमः । । 33924 । ।
ramayan::7118.verse_hindi: For the sake of Surpanakha, Khara of Janasthana committed excesses and got killed by Rama who can accomplish things with ease.Tell me truly if Rama did violate anything here.
ramayan::7118.english_translation: For the sake of Surpanakha, Khara of Janasthana committed excesses and was killed by Rama, who acts without strain. Tell me truly: what fault of Rama was there here?
ramayan::7118.translation_literal: यदि (if) / शूर्पणखा-हेतोः (for Surpanakha's sake) / जनस्थान-गतः (gone to Janasthana) / खरः (Khara) / अतिवृत्तः (acted excessively) / हतः (killed) / पूर्वम् (before) / रामेण (by Rama) / अक्लिष्ट-कर्मणा (by the one whose actions are effortless) / अत्र (here) / ब्रूहि (speak) / यथातत्त्वम् (truly) / कः (what) / रामस्य (of Rama) / व्यतिक्रमः (fault / transgression)
ramayan::7118.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7118.essence: Rama's response is justified because Khara crossed the line first.
ramayan::7118.simple_meaning: Ravana argues that Khara attacked because of Surpanakha, and Rama only responded. He challenges anyone to name a real fault in Rama's actions.
ramayan::7118.simple_insight: It can be easier to blame the response than face the original wrongdoing.
ramayan::7118.detailed_meaning: Ravana is defending Khara after his defeat in Janasthana. He says Khara acted wildly for Surpanakha's sake and was killed by Rama without strain. The point is sharp: Ravana wants to prove Rama did nothing wrong, exposing how thin the case against him is.
ramayan::7118.modern_relevance: A fight starts in a group chat, someone pushes too far, and then complains about being blocked. You know the real question isn't who reacted hardest — it's who crossed the line first.
ramayan::7118.insight: It shifts attention from outrage over consequences to the original act that caused them.

ramayan::7119.verse_sanskrit: इदं वचो बन्धुहितार्थिनामया यथोच्यमानं यदि नाभिपत्स्यसे । सबान्धवस्त्यक्ष्यसि जीवितं रणे हतोऽऽद्य रामेण शरैरजिह्मगैः । । 33925 । ।
ramayan::7119.verse_hindi: If you do not follow my advice given for the welfare of our kith and kin, O Ravana, you are killed today. With your relations you will succumb to his straightmoving arrows.
ramayan::7119.english_translation: If you do not follow my advice given for the welfare of our kith and kin, O Ravana, you are killed today. With your relations you will succumb to his straight-moving arrows.
ramayan::7119.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / वचः (speech) / बन्धु-हित-अर्थिनाम् (of those seeking the welfare of relatives) / अया (by me) / यथा-उच्यमानम् (as being spoken) / यदि (if) / न (not) / अभिपत्स्यसे (you will accept) / स-आ-बन्धवः (with your relatives) / त्यक्ष्यसि (you will abandon) / जीवितम् (life) / रणे (in battle) / हतः (killed) / अद्य (today) / रामेण (by Rama) / शरैः (with arrows) / अजिह्मगैः (straight-moving)
ramayan::7119.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7119.essence: Pride survives only until it ignores the warning that could save it.
ramayan::7119.simple_meaning: Maricha warns Ravana that if he ignores this advice, he and his relatives will die in battle at Rama's hands.
ramayan::7119.simple_insight: Ignoring wise warning can turn pride into a fatal mistake.
ramayan::7119.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Maricha tries one last time to shake Ravana out of his obsession. He speaks as a relative concerned for the family’s survival, warning that Rama’s arrows will destroy them all if Ravana refuses to listen.
ramayan::7119.modern_relevance: A friend tells you, plainly, that a decision is heading toward disaster. You hear the warning, feel the ego flare, and still have to choose whether to listen before the damage becomes irreversible.
ramayan::7119.insight: It shows how refusal to heed clear counsel can make destruction feel inevitable.

ramayan::7120.verse_sanskrit: मारीचेन तु तद्वाक्यं क्षमं युक्तं च निशाचरः । उक्तो न प्रतिजग्राह मर्तुकाम इवौषधम् । । 3401 । ।
ramayan::7120.verse_hindi: The demon Ravana did not heed the appropriate advice of the competent Maricha just like a man wishing to die refuses medicine.
ramayan::7120.english_translation: Ravana did not accept Maricha's wise and fitting advice, just as a man who wants to die refuses medicine.
ramayan::7120.translation_literal: मारीचेन (by Maricha) / तु (indeed) / तद्वाक्यं (that advice) / क्षमं (appropriate) / युक्तं च (and fitting) / निशाचरः (the night-walker) / उक्तो (spoken to) / न प्रतिजग्राह (did not accept) / मर्तुकाम इव (like one desiring death) / औषधम् (medicine)
ramayan::7120.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7120.essence: Pride can make you reject the very help that could save you.
ramayan::7120.simple_meaning: Ravana ignores Maricha's sensible warning, even though it could save him. Pride can make a person reject what would help most.
ramayan::7120.simple_insight: Not every refusal is strength. Sometimes it is the first sign that harm has already begun.
ramayan::7120.detailed_meaning: Maricha has just given Ravana careful, practical counsel about the danger ahead. Ravana, already driven by desire and arrogance, rejects it outright. Valmiki compares him to someone who refuses medicine while wanting death, showing how self-deception blocks rescue.
ramayan::7120.modern_relevance: You get a message from someone who has seen the pattern before, but you dismiss it because it bruises your ego. The warning was never the problem; your refusal was.
ramayan::7120.insight: It teaches you to notice when pride is making you reject useful correction.

ramayan::7121.verse_sanskrit: तं पथ्यहितवक्तारं मारीचं राक्षसाधिपः । अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यमयुक्तं कालचोदितः । । 3402 । ।
ramayan::7121.verse_hindi: The king of the demons, driven by fate, replied with improper and harsh words to Maricha whose advice was salutary and beneficial to him :
ramayan::7121.english_translation: The king of the demons, driven by fate, replied with improper and harsh words to Maricha whose advice was salutary and beneficial to him.
ramayan::7121.translation_literal: तं (to him) / पथ्यहितवक्तारं (the speaker of beneficial advice) / मारीचं (Maricha) / राक्षसाधिपः (the lord of the demons) / अब्रवीत् (said) / परुषं (harsh) / वाक्यम् (words) / अयुक्तं (unfitting) / कालचोदितः (driven by fate)
ramayan::7121.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7121.essence: Refusing good advice is often the first sign of collapse.
ramayan::7121.simple_meaning: Ravana answers Maricha with harsh, unfit words instead of listening to useful advice.
ramayan::7121.simple_insight: Pride can make good counsel feel like an insult.
ramayan::7121.detailed_meaning: Maricha has just warned Ravana that this path will end in ruin. Ravana, the ruler of Lanka, is already under the pressure of his own choices and the pull of destruction. Instead of pausing, he lashes back with harsh words, rejecting the very advice meant to save him.
ramayan::7121.modern_relevance: Someone texts you a careful warning, and you fire back before reading it fully. The real danger is not the advice — it is the pride that cannot receive it.
ramayan::7121.insight: It shows how self-deception turns helpful counsel into something the mind attacks.

ramayan::7122.verse_sanskrit: यत्किलैतदयुक्तार्थं मारीच मयि कथ्यते । वाक्यं निष्फलमत्यर्थमुप्तं बीजमिवोषरे । । 3403 । ।
ramayan::7122.verse_hindi: O Maricha, the words addressed to me are not appropriate.Your advice is extremely fruitless like a seed sown in saline, barren soil.
ramayan::7122.english_translation: O Maricha, the words addressed to me are not appropriate. Your advice is extremely fruitless, like a seed sown in saline, barren soil.
ramayan::7122.translation_literal: यत्किल (indeed what) / एतत् (this) / अयुक्तार्थम् (not fitting the matter) / मारीच (Maricha) / मयि (to me) / कथ्यते (is spoken) / वाक्यम् (speech) / निष्फलम् (fruitless) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / उप्तम् (sown) / बीजम् इव (like a seed) / ऊषरे (in barren soil)
ramayan::7122.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7122.essence: A proud mind treats rescue as useless before the fall.
ramayan::7122.simple_meaning: Ravana dismisses Maricha’s warning as useless and says it will bear no result, like seed thrown into barren ground.
ramayan::7122.simple_insight: Pride can make even good advice feel like waste.
