ramayan::7122.detailed_meaning: Maricha has already warned Ravana not to pursue his plan. Ravana answers with contempt, comparing the warning to seed thrown on barren soil. This moment shows his mind closing itself off just before disaster.
ramayan::7122.modern_relevance: You know that moment when someone is trying to stop you from a bad choice, and you hear only irritation? Ravana is that moment made fatal.
ramayan::7122.insight: It shows how self-will turns helpful counsel into something the mind refuses to receive.

ramayan::7123.verse_sanskrit: त्वद्वाक्यैर्न तु मां शक्यं भेत्तुं रामस्य संयुगे । पापशीलस्य मूर्खस्य मानुषस्य विशेषतः । । 3404 । ।
ramayan::7123.verse_hindi: It is not possible to dissuade me from my encounter with Rama who is sinful, foolish and especially an ordinary human being.
ramayan::7123.english_translation: It is not possible to dissuade me from my encounter with Rama who is sinful, foolish and especially an ordinary human being.
ramayan::7123.translation_literal: त्वद्वाक्यैः (by your words) / न (not) / तु (indeed) / माम् (me) / शक्यम् (possible) / भेत्तुम् (to break away) / रामस्य (of Rama) / संयुगे (in battle) / पापशीलस्य (of sinful nature) / मूर्खस्य (of a fool) / मानुषस्य (of a human) / विशेषतः (especially)
ramayan::7123.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7123.essence: Arrogance makes a real threat look trivial.
ramayan::7123.simple_meaning: Ravana refuses Maricha's advice and insists on facing Rama, dismissing Rama as merely human and unworthy of fear.
ramayan::7123.simple_insight: Pride can make danger look small right up to the moment it destroys you.
ramayan::7123.detailed_meaning: Maricha has warned Ravana against provoking Rama, but Ravana rejects the warning with contempt. He reduces Rama to an ordinary man and treats wise counsel as weakness, revealing the blindness that will carry him toward ruin.
ramayan::7123.modern_relevance: A friend tells you the risk is real, but you brush it off because your ego wants the bigger story. That is how people walk straight into avoidable disaster.
ramayan::7123.insight: It shows how arrogance blocks good counsel and turns clear warning into noise.

ramayan::7124.verse_sanskrit: यस्त्यक्त्वा सुहृदो राज्यं मातरं पितरं तथा । स्त्रीवाक्यं प्राकृतं श्रुत्वा वनमेकपदे गतः । । 3405 । ।
ramayan::7124.verse_hindi: On hearing the casual words of a woman, (this) Rama came to the forest at once, leaving his friends, kingdom, mother and father.
ramayan::7124.english_translation: On hearing the casual words of a woman, Rama came to the forest at once, leaving his friends, kingdom, mother and father.
ramayan::7124.translation_literal: यः (who) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / सुहृदः (friends) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / मातरम् (mother) / पितरम् (father) / तथा (and so) / स्त्रीवाक्यम् (a woman's words) / प्राकृतम् (ordinary) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / वनम् (to the forest) / एकपदे (at once) / गतः (went)
ramayan::7124.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7124.essence: He walked away from power because his word was heavier than a throne.
ramayan::7124.simple_meaning: Rama gave up family, kingdom, and comfort to go to the forest immediately after hearing the command that bound him.
ramayan::7124.simple_insight: Real strength can look like surrendering everything except your word.
ramayan::7124.detailed_meaning: Ravana is mocking Rama before the war, calling him a man who abandoned friends, parents, and a kingdom for a woman's words. The insult only sharpens the truth underneath: Rama went into exile without hesitation because duty had already become larger than comfort.
ramayan::7124.modern_relevance: You get the call that changes everything: a parent needs you, a promise needs keeping, or a move must happen today. The easy life is still there, but your word is not.
ramayan::7124.insight: It shifts attention from status and comfort to the cost of keeping a promise.

ramayan::7125.verse_sanskrit: अवश्यन्तु मया तस्य संयुगे खरघातिनः । प्राणैः प्रियतरा सीता हर्तव्या तव सन्निधौ । । 3406 । ।
ramayan::7125.verse_hindi: In your very presence I will surely abduct Sita, wife of Rama who killed Khara in war,
ramayan::7125.english_translation: In your very presence I will surely abduct Sita, wife of Rama who killed Khara in war.
ramayan::7125.translation_literal: अवश्यम् (surely) / तु (indeed) / मया (by me) / तस्य (his) / संयुगे (in battle) / खरघातिनः (of the slayer of Khara) / प्राणैः (than life) / प्रियतरा (dearer) / सीता (Sita) / हर्तव्या (is to be abducted) / तव (your) / सन्निधौ (in presence)
ramayan::7125.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7125.essence: Desire has made him fearless in the wrong direction.
ramayan::7125.simple_meaning: Ravana declares to Maricha that he will abduct Sita right in Rama's presence, no matter the danger.
ramayan::7125.simple_insight: Arrogance can turn danger into a challenge instead of a warning.
ramayan::7125.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Maricha, pressing ahead with his plan after mocking Rama's human limits. He says he will take Sita even before Rama's eyes, revealing how desire has hardened into reckless certainty.
ramayan::7125.modern_relevance: You can hear this voice when someone decides to cross a line just to prove they can. The warning signs are clear, but ego makes them sound like invitations.
ramayan::7125.insight: It shows how obsession blinds judgment and turns restraint into contempt.

ramayan::7126.verse_sanskrit: एवं मे निश्चिता बुद्धिर्हृदि मारीच वर्तते । न व्यावर्तयितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः । । 3407 । ।
ramayan::7126.verse_hindi: O Maricha  I have made up my mind that way. Even demons or deities including Indra cannot alter this decision of mine.
ramayan::7126.english_translation: O Maricha, I have made up my mind. Even Indra and all the gods and demons together cannot change this decision.
ramayan::7126.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / मे (my) / निश्चिता (fixed, resolved) / बुद्धिः (mind, decision) / हृदि (in the heart) / मारीच (O Maricha) / वर्तते (is placed, stands) / न (not) / व्यावर्तयितुं (to turn back, to alter) / शक्या (able) / सेन्द्रैः (with Indra) / अपि (even) / सुरासुरैः (by gods and demons)
ramayan::7126.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7126.essence: Once desire takes over, even truth sounds powerless.
ramayan::7126.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Maricha that his decision is fixed and cannot be changed, even by the strongest beings.
ramayan::7126.simple_insight: A mind locked onto desire stops hearing reason.
ramayan::7126.detailed_meaning: Ravana is pressing Maricha into helping him abduct Sita. He declares that his resolve is now fixed in his heart and that no force, not even Indra with all the gods and demons, can change it. The verse shows the hardening of his will before disaster.
ramayan::7126.modern_relevance: You already know the choice is reckless, but you keep defending it anyway. By then, advice sounds like an attack, not help.
ramayan::7126.insight: It shows how stubborn certainty can shut out every warning, even when disaster is near.

ramayan::7127.verse_sanskrit: दोषं गुणं वा सम्पृष्टस्त्वमेवं वक्तुमर्हसि । अपायं वाप्युपायं वा कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चये । । 3408 । ।
ramayan::7127.verse_hindi: If I asked you the merits or demerits, the risks involved or the way out while deciding a case, you should have said what you did.
ramayan::7127.english_translation: If I asked you about the merits or faults, the risks or the remedy in deciding this matter, you should have spoken.
ramayan::7127.translation_literal: दोषं (fault) / गुणं (merit) / वा (or) / सम्पृष्टः (having been asked) / त्वम् (you) / एवम् (thus) / वक्तुम् अर्हसि (should speak) / अपायं (danger) / वा (or) / उपायं (remedy) / वा (or) / कार्यस्य (of the matter) / अस्य (this) / विनिश्चये (in deciding)
ramayan::7127.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7127.essence: Asked counsel must include both the danger and the remedy.
ramayan::7127.simple_meaning: A wise adviser should speak clearly when a king asks for judgment about a decision, including its risks and possible remedies.
ramayan::7127.simple_insight: Being consulted carries responsibility; holding back the needed truth is a failure of care.
ramayan::7127.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already fixed his mind on abducting Sita, and Maricha has warned him. Now Ravana rebukes him: if a king asks for counsel, the counsellor must speak about good and bad, danger and remedy. The scene turns from plotting to the ethics of advice.
ramayan::7127.modern_relevance: A manager asks for honest feedback before a bad launch decision. You know the risks, but you soften the truth to stay comfortable. This verse says that being invited to speak means you owe clarity, not politeness.
ramayan::7127.insight: It shifts you from guarded approval to honest counsel when someone has explicitly asked for your judgment.

ramayan::7128.verse_sanskrit: सम्पृष्टेन तु वक्तव्यं सचिवेन विपश्चिता । उद्यताञ्जलिना राज्ञे य इच्छेद्भूतिमात्मनः । । 3409 । ।
ramayan::7128.verse_hindi: A wise counsellor should give advice to the king only when his opinion is sought and that too with folded hands, if he wishes his own prosperity.
ramayan::7128.english_translation: A wise counsellor should give advice to the king only when his opinion is sought and that too with folded hands, if he wishes his own prosperity.
ramayan::7128.translation_literal: सम्पृष्टेन (when asked) / तु (indeed) / वक्तव्यम् (to be spoken) / सचिवेन (by a minister) / विपश्चिता (by the wise) / उद्यताञ्जलिना (with folded hands) / राज्ञे (to the king) / यः (who) / इच्छेत् (would desire) / भूतिम् (prosperity) / आत्मनः (of himself)
ramayan::7128.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7128.essence: Wisdom works best when it is invited and delivered humbly.
ramayan::7128.simple_meaning: A wise advisor should speak to a king only when asked, and do it humbly. Respect and timing protect both the advice and the advisor.
ramayan::7128.simple_insight: Not every true thought needs immediate expression. Humility makes wisdom usable.
ramayan::7128.detailed_meaning: Ravana is pressing Maricha for counsel, and the exchange turns into a lesson on courtly conduct. A minister who wants his own good must wait to be asked, then speak with folded hands and careful respect.
ramayan::7128.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense meeting, and everyone is talking over each other. The sharpest point in the room may still fail if it arrives without timing, humility, or invitation.
ramayan::7128.insight: It teaches you to match truth with tact, and to offer advice in a way the listener can actually receive.

ramayan::7129.verse_sanskrit: वाक्यमप्रितकूलं तु मृदुपूर्वं हितं शुभम् । उपचारेण युक्तं च वक्तव्यो वसुधाधिपः । । 34010 । ।
ramayan::7129.verse_hindi: A king should be addressed with politeness and decorum, with words not unfavourble intended for his good luck and wellbeing.
ramayan::7129.english_translation: A king should be addressed with politeness and decorum, with words that are not disagreeable but are meant for his good and welfare.
ramayan::7129.translation_literal: वाक्यम् (speech) / अप्रितकूलम् (not disagreeable) / तु (but) / मृदुपूर्वम् (preceded by gentleness) / हितम् (beneficial) / शुभम् (auspicious) / उपचारेण (with courteous conduct) / युक्तम् (joined) / च (and) / वक्तव्यः (should be spoken to) / वसुधाधिपः (lord of the earth, king)
ramayan::7129.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7129.essence: Truth lands better when it is wrapped in respect.
ramayan::7129.simple_meaning: When speaking to a king, or anyone in authority, the words should be respectful, gentle, and meant for their good.
ramayan::7129.simple_insight: Respect is not weakness; it helps truth be heard.
ramayan::7129.detailed_meaning: In the court, a wise minister is being told how to advise a ruler. The point is not to flatter power, but to speak in a way that protects dignity while still serving the king’s welfare.
ramayan::7129.modern_relevance: You’re about to send a blunt message to your manager, parent, or partner. The truth may be right, but if your delivery wounds first, it may never be heard.
ramayan::7129.insight: It shifts you from blunt correction to respectful, effective speech.

ramayan::7130.verse_sanskrit: सावमर्दं तु यद्वाक्यं मारीच हितमुच्यते । नाभिनन्दति तद्राजा मानार्हो मानवर्जितम् । । 34011 । ।
ramayan::7130.verse_hindi: A king who deserves honour does not feel happy to hear even good words of advice if said in disrespectful or authoritarian way, O Maricha
ramayan::7130.english_translation: A king who deserves honour does not feel pleased by even good advice when it is spoken with contempt, O Maricha.
ramayan::7130.translation_literal: सावमर्दम् (with contempt) / तु (indeed) / यत्-वाक्यम् (that speech) / मारीच (O Maricha) / हितम् (beneficial) / उच्यते (is said) / न (not) / अभिनन्दति (rejoices in) / तत् (that) / राजा (king) / मान-अर्हः (worthy of honour) / मानवर्जितम् (when stripped of respect)
ramayan::7130.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7130.essence: Truth spoken without respect loses its power.
ramayan::7130.simple_meaning: Even helpful advice loses its force when spoken disrespectfully. A worthy king will not welcome truth wrapped in contempt.
ramayan::7130.simple_insight: Right words need the right tone, or they land as resistance instead of help.
ramayan::7130.detailed_meaning: A counsellor is being instructed on how to speak to a king. The point is not the advice itself, but the manner of delivery: even beneficial words are rejected if they come with disrespect. The passage builds the case for disciplined speech before moving on to royal power.
ramayan::7130.modern_relevance: You finally tell your manager what needs fixing, but your voice is sharp and your timing is wrong. The message may be true, yet the disrespect makes it hard to receive.
ramayan::7130.insight: It teaches you to pair truth with humility so correction can actually be heard.

ramayan::7131.verse_sanskrit: पञ्च रूपाणि राजानो धारयन्त्यमितौजसः । अग्नेरिन्द्रस्य सोमस्य वरुणस्य यमस्य च । । 34012 । ।
ramayan::7131.verse_hindi: Very powerful kings assume five forms like fire, Indra, Moon, Varuna and Yama.
ramayan::7131.english_translation: Very powerful kings assume five forms like fire, Indra, the Moon, Varuna, and Yama.
ramayan::7131.translation_literal: पञ्च (five) / रूपाणि (forms) / राजानः (kings) / धारयन्ति (bear) / अमितौजसः (of limitless power) / अग्नेः (of fire) / इन्द्रस्य (of Indra) / सोमस्य (of the Moon) / वरुणस्य (of Varuna) / यमस्य (of Yama) / च (and)
ramayan::7131.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7131.essence: True authority can be fierce, calm, just, and restrained at once.
ramayan::7131.simple_meaning: A capable king must hold several qualities at once: intensity, courage, calm, control, and firmness.
ramayan::7131.simple_insight: Leadership is steadier when strength has range, not just force.
ramayan::7131.detailed_meaning: The sage is teaching how a ruler should speak and lead. A king cannot be only harsh or only gentle; he must carry fire, courage, calm, command, and restraint together. That balance is what makes authority worthy.
ramayan::7131.modern_relevance: You're in a tense meeting and need to correct someone without crushing them. The moment calls for firmness, not fury; calm, not weakness. Good leadership changes shape without losing its center.
ramayan::7131.insight: It shifts leadership from one-dimensional power to disciplined versatility.

ramayan::7132.verse_sanskrit: औष्ण्यं तथा विक्रमं च सौम्यं दण्डं प्रसन्नताम् । धारयन्ति महात्मानो राजानः क्षणदाचर । । 34013 । । तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु मान्याः पूज्याश्च पार्थिवाः ।
ramayan::7132.verse_hindi: Great kings possess heat, (of the firegod), valour (of Indra), coolness (of the Moon), command (of Varuna) and grace (of the Lord of death). Therefore kings at all stages deserve respect and reverence.
ramayan::7132.english_translation: Great kings possess heat, valour, coolness, command, and grace. Therefore, kings at all times deserve respect and reverence.
ramayan::7132.translation_literal: औष्ण्यम् (heat) / तथा (and) / विक्रमम् (valour) / च (and) / सौम्यम् (coolness) / दण्डम् (command) / प्रसन्नताम् (grace) / धारयन्ति (they possess) / महात्मानः (great-souled ones) / राजानः (kings) / क्षणदाचर (O night-wanderer) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वासु (in all) / अवस्थासु (states) / मान्याः (worthy of honour) / पूज्याः (worthy of reverence) / च (and) / पार्थिवाः (earthly rulers)
ramayan::7132.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7132.essence: Real authority earns respect by balancing force with composure.
ramayan::7132.simple_meaning: A true king must combine strength, calmness, discipline, and dignity. Because of that balance, rulers deserve respect in every situation.
ramayan::7132.simple_insight: Power becomes trustworthy when it is balanced by restraint and grace.
ramayan::7132.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a proud speaker is being corrected about how kings should be treated. The verse explains that real rulers are not just forceful; they also carry calmness and dignity, so they deserve honour in every condition.
ramayan::7132.modern_relevance: A manager who can fire someone, calm a room, and still speak kindly earns real trust. Authority without balance feels dangerous; authority with steadiness feels worthy of respect.
ramayan::7132.insight: It shifts you to judge leadership by character, not just control.

ramayan::7133.verse_sanskrit: त्वं तु धर्ममविज्ञाय केवलं मोहमास्थितः । अभ्यागतं मां दौरात्म्यात्परुषं वक्तुमिच्छसि । । 34014 । ।
ramayan::7133.verse_hindi: You do not know your rightful duty.Because of delusion and an evil mind, you want to speak only harsh words to me, a guest who has come to you.
ramayan::7133.english_translation: You do not know your rightful duty. Because of delusion and an evil mind, you want to speak only harsh words to me, a guest who has come to you.
ramayan::7133.translation_literal: त्वं (you) / तु (indeed) / धर्मम् (duty) / अविज्ञाय (not knowing) / केवलम् (only) / मोहम् (delusion) / आस्थितः (established in) / अभ्यागतम् (arrived as guest) / माम् (me) / दौरात्म्यात् (from evil-mindedness) / परुषम् (harsh) / वक्तुम् (to speak) / इच्छसि (you want)
ramayan::7133.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7133.essence: Delusion makes you violate duty and mistake cruelty for power.
ramayan::7133.simple_meaning: A guest rebukes his host for speaking harshly out of confusion and moral blindness instead of showing proper respect.
ramayan::7133.simple_insight: Harsh words often reveal confusion, not strength.
ramayan::7133.detailed_meaning: A guest has arrived seeking shelter, but the host answers with insult. The speaker calls out that failure directly: this is not strength, but ignorance of duty and a mind clouded by delusion.
ramayan::7133.modern_relevance: You send the sharp reply before checking what the other person actually needs. In that instant, pride speaks louder than decency, and you can feel the break it causes.
ramayan::7133.insight: It shifts attention from reaction to responsibility, especially in moments where courtesy and restraint matter most.

ramayan::7134.verse_sanskrit: गुणदोषौ न पृच्छामि क्षमं चात्मनि राक्षस । मयोक्तं तव चैतावत्संप्रत्यमितविक्रमः । । 34015 । ।
ramayan::7134.verse_hindi: O demon  O extremely valiant demon  I ask you(to do) this much now. I am not asking you whether it is good or bad or whether it is for my welfare or not.
ramayan::7134.english_translation: O demon, O extremely valiant demon, I ask you only this much now. I am not asking whether it is good or bad, or whether it is for my welfare.
ramayan::7134.translation_literal: गुणदोषौ (good and bad) / न (not) / पृच्छामि (I ask) / क्षमं (welfare) / च (and) / आत्मनि (for myself) / राक्षस (O demon) / मया (by me) / उक्तं (said) / तव (to you) / च (and) / एतावत् (this much) / संप्रति (now) / अमितविक्रमः (O one of limitless valor)
ramayan::7134.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7134.essence: Clear need matters more than flattering the listener.
ramayan::7134.simple_meaning: Rama says he is not judging the request by whether it is good for him. He is simply asking the other person to help with the task at hand.
ramayan::7134.simple_insight: Sometimes the right request is simple: ask for needed help without overexplaining or bargaining.
ramayan::7134.detailed_meaning: Rama is speaking to Ravana in Lanka, after refusing to be dragged into abuse. He strips the exchange down to one urgent demand: help with the mission. The verse shows his firmness, clarity, and refusal to let ego distract from the task.
ramayan::7134.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense room, and every sentence is being weighed for hidden motives. This verse gives you the courage to say the real request cleanly, without dressing it up or apologising for needing help.
ramayan::7134.insight: It shifts you from defending yourself to stating the task directly.

ramayan::7135.verse_sanskrit: अस्मिंस्तु त्वं महाकृत्ये साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि । शृणु तत्कर्म साहाय्ये यत्कार्यं वचनान्मम । । 34016 । ।
ramayan::7135.verse_hindi: You have to help me in accomplishing this great task .Hear me on the kind of work you have to do.
ramayan::7135.english_translation: You have to help me in accomplishing this great task. Hear me: this is the work you must do for me.
ramayan::7135.translation_literal: अस्मिन् (in this) / तु (indeed) / त्वं (you) / महाकृत्ये (in the great task) / साहाय्यम् (help) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you are fit / ought) / शृणु (listen) / तत् (that) / कर्म (work) / साहाय्ये (in help) / यत् (what) / कार्यम् (to be done) / वचनात् (from the word) / मम (my)
ramayan::7135.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7135.essence: A huge plan begins by assigning one exact job.
ramayan::7135.simple_meaning: Ravana asks the listener to help him with a major task and says he will now explain exactly what work is needed.
ramayan::7135.simple_insight: Big goals become possible when the next required action is made clear.
ramayan::7135.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already dismissed moral objections and is pressing forward with his plan. In the middle of that urgent command, he tells the demon to listen closely because the next step matters: this is the specific work needed to carry out the larger scheme.
ramayan::7135.modern_relevance: Someone hands you a difficult project and skips the philosophy. They need one clear helper, one clear task, and no confusion about what comes next.
ramayan::7135.insight: It shifts attention from debate to execution by naming the immediate responsibility.

ramayan::7136.verse_sanskrit: सौवर्णस्त्वं मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजतबिन्दुभिः । आश्रमे तस्य रामस्य सीतायाः प्रमुखे चर । । 34017 । ।
ramayan::7136.english_translation: Become a golden deer, beautiful with silver spots, and move before Sita in Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7136.translation_literal: सौवर्णः (golden) / त्वं (you) / मृगः (deer) / भूत्वा (having become) / चित्रः (variegated, beautiful) / रजतबिन्दुभिः (with silver spots) / आश्रमे (in the hermitage) / तस्य (of that) / रामस्य (of Rama) / सीतायाः (of Sita) / प्रमुखे (in front) / चर (move about)
ramayan::7136.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7136.essence: Beauty is used here as bait for harm.
ramayan::7136.simple_meaning: Ravana orders a demon to take the form of a beautiful golden deer with silver spots and wander before Sita at Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7136.simple_insight: Deception often begins with something that looks harmless and beautiful.
ramayan::7136.detailed_meaning: Ravana is instructing Maricha in a calculated plot against Rama and Sita. The shape-shifting deer is not the goal itself but the lure meant to draw Sita's attention and separate her from protection, setting the abduction in motion.
ramayan::7136.modern_relevance: A message arrives that looks playful, harmless, even flattering. You click before you notice the trap was designed to catch your attention first.
ramayan::7136.insight: It shows how temptation can be engineered to distract you from what protects you.

ramayan::7137.verse_sanskrit: सौवर्णस्त्वं मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजतबिन्दुभिः । आश्रमे तस्य रामस्य सीतायाः प्रमुखे चर । प्रलोभयित्वा वैदेहीं यथेष्टं गन्तुमर्हसि । । 34018 । ।
ramayan::7137.verse_hindi: Transform yourself into a wonderful golden deer with silver spots and move about in front of Sita at the hermitage of Rama. After fascinating her, you may go whereever you desire.
ramayan::7137.english_translation: Transform yourself into a wonderful golden deer with silver spots and move about in front of Sita at Rama's hermitage. After fascinating her, go wherever you wish.
ramayan::7137.translation_literal: सौवर्णः (golden) / त्वं (you) / मृगः (deer) / भूत्वा (having become) / चित्रः (variegated) / रजतबिन्दुभिः (with silver spots) / आश्रमे (in the hermitage) / तस्य (of that) / रामस्य (of Rama) / सीतायाः (of Sita) / प्रमुखे (in front) / चर (move about) / प्रलोभयित्वा (having enticed) / वैदेहीं (Sita, daughter of Videha) / यथेष्टम् (as desired) / गन्तुम् (to go) / अर्हसि (you should)
ramayan::7137.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7137.essence: Beauty can be used as bait for harm.
ramayan::7137.simple_meaning: Ravana orders the demon Maricha to become a golden deer with silver spots, wander before Sita, and lure her away from Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7137.simple_insight: Deception often begins as something beautiful.
ramayan::7137.detailed_meaning: Ravana is laying out the trap that will separate Rama and Sita. He tells Maricha to become a dazzling golden deer, appear before Sita at the hermitage, and draw her attention so the abduction can begin.
ramayan::7137.modern_relevance: A polished offer lands in your feed and feels harmless at first. The danger is not ugliness; it is how beautifully distraction can dress itself.
ramayan::7137.insight: It shows how temptation works by first capturing attention, then weakening judgment.

ramayan::7138.verse_sanskrit: त्वां तु मायामृगं दृष्ट्वा काञ्चनं जातविस्मया । आनयैनमिति क्षिप्रं रामं वक्ष्यति मैथिली । । 34019 । ।
ramayan::7138.verse_hindi: Seeing the illusory golden deer, Sita, wonderstruck, will at once ask Rama to get the
ramayan::7138.english_translation: Seeing the illusory golden deer, Sita, wonderstruck, will at once ask Rama to get it.
ramayan::7138.translation_literal: त्वाम् (you) / तु (but) / मायामृगम् (illusory deer) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / काञ्चनम् (golden) / जातविस्मया (filled with wonder) / आनय (bring) / एनम् (it) / इति (thus) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / रामम् (Rama) / वक्ष्यति (will say) / मैथिली (Sita)
ramayan::7138.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7138.essence: Wonder can become the opening through which danger enters.
ramayan::7138.simple_meaning: Sita sees the magical golden deer and, amazed, tells Rama to bring it quickly.
ramayan::7138.simple_insight: A single moment of wonder can open the door to danger.
ramayan::7138.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, Maricha is being sent in the form of a dazzling deer. The plan is to draw Sita's attention and pull Rama away. This verse shows the bait working: Sita's surprise will make her ask Rama to fetch it.
ramayan::7138.modern_relevance: You spot something dazzling and want it immediately, before you ask whether it is real. That first pull can change everything.
ramayan::7138.insight: It shows how fascination can trigger a choice before caution has time to speak.

ramayan::7139.verse_sanskrit: अपक्रान्ते तु काकुत्स्थे दूरं यात्वाप्युदाहर । हा सीते लक्ष्मणेत्येवं रामवाक्यानुरूपकम् । । 34020 । ।
ramayan::7139.verse_hindi: Divert Rama to a faroff place and cry, Alas, Sita, Alas, Lakshmana,  imitating the voice of Rama.
ramayan::7139.english_translation: Divert Rama to a far-off place and cry, 'Alas, Sita! Alas, Lakshmana!' while imitating Rama's voice.
ramayan::7139.translation_literal: अपक्रान्ते (when gone away) / तु (indeed) / काकुत्स्थे (Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / दूरं (far) / यात्वा (having gone) / अपि (even) / उदाहर (cry out) / हा (alas) / सीते (O Sita) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / इति (thus) / एवम् (in this way) / रामवाक्यानुरूपकम् (matching Rama's voice)
ramayan::7139.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7139.essence: False urgency can split even the closest bonds.
ramayan::7139.simple_meaning: Ravana instructs the disguised deer to lure Rama away and call out in Rama's voice, so Sita and Lakshmana will be misled.
ramayan::7139.simple_insight: Deception works best when it borrows the voice of trust.
ramayan::7139.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already set the trap in the forest. He wants the golden deer to pull Rama far from the hermitage, then cry out in Rama's own voice so Sita and Lakshmana panic. This is the precise step that turns suspicion into separation.
ramayan::7139.modern_relevance: A message arrives sounding exactly like someone you trust, and you react before checking. The danger is not just the lie — it is how closely it copies the real voice.
ramayan::7139.insight: It shows how manipulation uses familiarity to break judgment and split attention.

ramayan::7140.verse_sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा रामपदवीं सीतया च प्रचोदितः । अनुगच्छति सम्भ्रान्तः सौमित्रिरपि सौहृदात् । । 34021 । ।
ramayan::7140.verse_hindi: On hearing you, Lakshmana will be bewildered. Urged by Sita and out of love for Rama, Lakshmana will follow the same track as Rama.
ramayan::7140.english_translation: On hearing you, Lakshmana will be bewildered. Urged by Sita and out of love for Rama, Lakshmana will follow the same track as Rama.
ramayan::7140.translation_literal: तच्छ्रुत्वा (on hearing that) / रामपदवीं (Rama's track) / सीतया (by Sita) / च (and) / प्रचोदितः (urged) / अनुगच्छति (follows) / सम्भ्रान्तः (bewildered) / सौमित्रिः (Lakshmana) / अपि (also) / सौहृदात् (out of affection)
ramayan::7140.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7140.essence: Loyalty can pull you forward even when confusion clouds your judgment.
ramayan::7140.simple_meaning: Lakshmana is so loyal to Rama that, once Sita urges him, he follows Rama’s path even while confused.
ramayan::7140.simple_insight: Love can make you move before your mind has fully caught up.
ramayan::7140.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana is setting his trap. Sita’s words will send Lakshmana away from Rama’s side, and his own affection for Rama will pull him after Rama’s path even in confusion. This verse shows the brief opening before the abduction.
ramayan::7140.modern_relevance: A friend calls in a panic, and you leave without thinking through the consequences. Loyalty can be noble, but it can also be the crack through which disaster enters.
ramayan::7140.insight: It shows how affection can override hesitation and move someone into action, even when the situation is already dangerous.

ramayan::7141.verse_sanskrit: अपक्रान्ते च काकुत्स्थे लक्ष्मणे च यथासुखम् । आनयिष्यामि वैदेहीं सहस्राक्षश्शचीमिव । । 34022 । ।
ramayan::7141.verse_hindi: When Rama and Lakshmana are away I will comfortably abduct Vaidehi like the thousandeyed Indra brought Sachi.
ramayan::7141.english_translation: When Rama and Lakshmana are away, I will comfortably abduct Vaidehi like Indra brought Shachi.
ramayan::7141.translation_literal: अपक्रान्ते (having gone away) / च (and) / काकुत्स्थे (when Kakutstha/Rama) / लक्ष्मणे (and Lakshmana) / च (and) / यथासुखम् (at ease) / आनयिष्यामि (I will bring) / वैदेहीं (Vaidehi/Sita) / सहस्राक्षः (the thousand-eyed one, Indra) / शचीम् (Shachi) / इव (like)
ramayan::7141.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7141.essence: Cruelty feels easy when ego has already justified it.
ramayan::7141.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that once Rama and Lakshmana are gone, he will seize Sita easily, just as Indra carried off Shachi.
ramayan::7141.simple_insight: Arrogance makes cruelty feel effortless to the mind that plans it.
ramayan::7141.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Maricha, laying out the scheme that will separate Rama from Sita and leave Lakshmana diverted. This is not a teaching verse but a calculated boast, showing the vanity and confidence behind the abduction plot.
ramayan::7141.modern_relevance: A person starts treating someone else’s life like a problem to solve, then talks themselves into it with a polished excuse. The danger begins long before the harm.
ramayan::7141.insight: It reveals how desire turns another person's dignity into a strategy.

ramayan::7142.verse_sanskrit: एवं कृत्वा त्विदं कार्यं यथेष्टं गच्छ राक्षस । राज्यस्यार्धं प्रयच्छामि मारीच तव सुव्रत । । 34023 । ।
ramayan::7142.verse_hindi: You may go wherever you want after accomplishing this task. I will give you, O demon of determination half my kingdom.
ramayan::7142.english_translation: You may go wherever you want after accomplishing this task. I will give you, O demon of determination, half my kingdom.
ramayan::7142.translation_literal: एवं (thus) / कृत्वा (having done) / तु (indeed) / इदम् (this) / कार्यम् (task) / यथेष्टम् (as you wish) / गच्छ (go) / राक्षस (O demon) / राज्यस्य (of the kingdom) / अर्धम् (half) / प्रयच्छामि (I give) / मारीच (Maricha) / तव (to you) / सुव्रत (O one of good vows)
ramayan::7142.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7142.essence: Desire pays well when it needs another hand.
ramayan::7142.simple_meaning: Ravana promises Maricha freedom and half his kingdom if Maricha completes the task.
ramayan::7142.simple_insight: Power can be used as a bribe when desire needs help.
ramayan::7142.detailed_meaning: Ravana has decided to use Maricha to carry out his plan against Rama and Sita. He offers reward and freedom as bait, trying to turn another being's skill into an instrument of his desire.
ramayan::7142.modern_relevance: A powerful person offers a bonus, a title, or a favor to get someone else to do the dirty work. The promise sounds generous, but it is really leverage.
ramayan::7142.insight: It reveals how desire recruits others by dressing manipulation as generosity.

ramayan::7143.verse_sanskrit: गच्छ सौम्य शिवं मार्गं कार्यस्यास्य विवृद्धये । अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि सरथो दण्डकावनम् । । 34024 । ।
ramayan::7143.verse_hindi: Go and accomplish this task. Let your path be auspicious. I will follow you on the chariot into the Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7143.english_translation: Go and accomplish this task. Let your path be auspicious. I will follow you on the chariot into the Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7143.translation_literal: गच्छ (go) / सौम्य (gentle one) / शिवं (auspicious) / मार्गं (path) / कार्यस्य (of the task) / अस्य (of this) / विवृद्धये (for the increase) / अहं (I) / त्वा (you) / अनुगमिष्यामि (will follow) / सरथः (with a chariot) / दण्डकावनम् (to the Dandaka forest)
ramayan::7143.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7143.essence: Polite language can hide a ruthless plan.
ramayan::7143.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Maricha to go ahead, wishes him well, and says he will follow by chariot into the Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7143.simple_insight: A plot can sound polite while carrying cruelty underneath.
ramayan::7143.detailed_meaning: Ravana is persuading Maricha to help him abduct Sita. He speaks calmly, even warmly, as he sends him toward the Dandaka forest. The verse is a step in the conspiracy, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::7143.modern_relevance: Someone can sound considerate while asking you to help them do harm. The soft tone does not change the intent underneath.
ramayan::7143.insight: It trains you to notice when pleasant words are covering manipulation.

ramayan::7144.verse_sanskrit: प्राप्य सीतामयुद्धेन वञ्चयित्वा तु राघवम् । लङ्कां प्रतिगमिष्यामि कृतकार्यस्सह त्वया । । 34025 । ।
ramayan::7144.verse_hindi: I will deceive Rama and obtain Sita, without waging a war. With the work done, I will return to Lanka along with you.
ramayan::7144.english_translation: I will deceive Rama and obtain Sita, without waging a war. With the work done, I will return to Lanka along with you.
ramayan::7144.translation_literal: प्राप्य (obtaining) / सीताम् (Sita) / अयुद्धेन (without battle) / वञ्चयित्वा (deceiving) / तु (but) / राघवम् (Rama) / लङ्काम् (to Lanka) / प्रतिगमिष्यामि (I will return) / कृतकार्यः (task completed) / सह (with) / त्वया (you)
ramayan::7144.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7144.essence: Victory sought through deceit already carries its own ruin.
ramayan::7144.simple_meaning: Ravana says he will trick Rama, take Sita, and return to Lanka after the plan succeeds.
ramayan::7144.simple_insight: A mind driven by desire starts treating deceit as strategy.
ramayan::7144.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Maricha, pressing him into a plot against Rama. He wants Sita taken by deception, not open battle, and promises to return to Lanka once the scheme succeeds. The verse reveals the scheme before the coercion that follows.
ramayan::7144.modern_relevance: Someone proposes a shortcut that depends on hiding the truth, not earning trust. The plan sounds clever until you see how much integrity it already costs.
ramayan::7144.insight: It exposes how desire turns manipulation into a plan and calls it efficiency.

ramayan::7145.verse_sanskrit: न चेत्करोषि मारीच हन्मि त्वामहमद्य वै । एतत्कार्यमवश्यं मे बलादपि करिष्यसि । राज्ञो हि प्रतिकूलस्थो न जातु सुखमेधते । । 34026 । ।
ramayan::7145.verse_hindi: O Maricha if you do not do this, I will kill you now. Or, by force make you do this work. No one who goes against the king lives in comfort.
ramayan::7145.english_translation: O Maricha, if you do not do this, I will kill you now. Or else, by force, you will do this task. No one who stands against a king ever lives in comfort.
ramayan::7145.translation_literal: न (not) / चेत् (if) / करोषि (you do) / मारीच (Maricha) / हन्मि (I kill) / त्वाम् (you) / अहम् (I) / अद्य (now) / वै (indeed) / एतत्-कार्यम् (this task) / अवश्यम् (certainly) / मे (my) / बलात् (by force) / अपि (even) / करिष्यसि (you will do) / राज्ञः (of a king) / हि (indeed) / प्रतिकूल-स्थः (standing against) / न (not) / जातु (ever) / सुखम् (comfort) / एधते (thrives)
ramayan::7145.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7145.essence: Power backed by fear can compel action, but it cannot earn loyalty.
ramayan::7145.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens Maricha: either obey the plan or die. He says resistance to a king brings no peace.
ramayan::7145.simple_insight: Coercion can force obedience, but it always reveals fear underneath.
ramayan::7145.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana corners Maricha and orders him into the scheme against Rama and Sita. The threat is blunt: comply or die. This is not a teaching verse so much as the pressure that drives the abduction plot forward.
ramayan::7145.modern_relevance: A manager says, “Do it my way or you’re out,” and the room goes silent. Power can demand compliance, but it cannot create trust.
ramayan::7145.insight: It shows how domination works: by fear, not wisdom. The verse advances the plot by exposing Ravana's rule-by-threat mindset.

ramayan::7146.verse_sanskrit: आसाद्य तं जीवितसंशयस्ते मृत्युर्ध्रुवो ह्यद्य मया विरुध्य । एतद्यथावत्प्रतिगृह्य बुद्ध्या यदत्र पथ्यं कुरु तत्तथा त्वम् । । 34027 । ।
ramayan::7146.verse_hindi: Your survival is doubtful after facing Rama in combat. But your death is certain if you oppose me now. Think carefuly and do whatever is desirable for you in the present circumstances.
ramayan::7146.english_translation: Your survival is doubtful after facing Rama in combat. But your death is certain if you oppose me now. Think carefully and do whatever is desirable for you in the present circumstances.
ramayan::7146.translation_literal: आसाद्य (having approached) / तम् (him) / जीवितसंशयः (doubt about survival) / ते (your) / मृत्युः (death) / ध्रुवः (certain) / हि (indeed) / अद्य (today) / मया (by me) / विरुध्य (by opposing) / एतत् (this) / यथावत् (properly) / प्रतिगृह्य (having understood) / बुद्ध्या (with intelligence) / यत् (what) / अत्र (here) / पथ्यम् (beneficial) / कुरु (do) / तत् (that) / तथा (so) / त्वम् (you)
ramayan::7146.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7146.essence: Threat can sound like advice when fear is in charge.
ramayan::7146.simple_meaning: Ravana warns Maricha that fighting Rama may still leave room for survival, but disobeying him now will certainly lead to death. He tells Maricha to think clearly and choose what is safest.
ramayan::7146.simple_insight: Fear can corner you into choices that are not wise, only urgent.
ramayan::7146.detailed_meaning: Ravana is pressuring Maricha into helping with Sita's abduction. He frames the choice as immediate death by disobedience and uncertain survival in battle, using threat to force obedience. The verse is part of a coercive argument, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::7146.modern_relevance: A boss corners you in a late-night call: say yes now, or lose the project. The pressure feels practical, but it is still coercion dressed as urgency.
ramayan::7146.insight: It exposes how fear can masquerade as reason and push you into compliance.

ramayan::7147.verse_sanskrit: आज्ञप्तो राजवद्वाक्यं प्रतिकूलं निशाचरः । अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं मारीचो राक्षसाधिपम् । । 3411 । ।
ramayan::7147.verse_hindi: At this royal command which was against his interest Maracha used harsh words to the demonking:
ramayan::7147.english_translation: At this royal command, which was against his interest, Maricha spoke harshly to the demon king.
ramayan::7147.translation_literal: आज्ञप्तः (commanded) / राजवत् (like a king) / वाक्यम् (speech) / प्रतिकूलम् (unfavorable) / निशाचरः (night-roamer) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / परुषम् (harsh) / वाक्यम् (words) / मारीचः (Maricha) / राक्षसाधिपम् (to the lord of demons)
ramayan::7147.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7147.essence: Coercion drew out a harsh reply, not obedience.
ramayan::7147.simple_meaning: Maricha answered Ravana harshly after being ordered to do something he did not want to do.
ramayan::7147.simple_insight: Pressure can turn a conversation into open resistance.
ramayan::7147.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just threatened Maricha and forced the issue. This verse marks Maricha’s angry reply before he explains the danger of the plan. It is a brief narrative bridge, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::7147.modern_relevance: A manager corners someone in a meeting and demands agreement. The reply is sharp because the demand itself was already a warning sign.
ramayan::7147.insight: It sets up the conflict by showing Maricha’s refusal before his warning begins.

ramayan::7148.verse_sanskrit: केनायमुपदिष्टस्ते विनाशः पापकर्मणा । सपुत्रस्य सराष्ट्रस्य सामात्यस्य निशाचर । । 3412 । ।
ramayan::7148.verse_hindi: Who is that sinner who has given you this advice which will spell destruction on you, your sons, your kingdom and your ministers ?
ramayan::7148.english_translation: Who is that sinner who has given you this advice which will spell destruction on you, your sons, your kingdom and your ministers?
ramayan::7148.translation_literal: केन (by whom) / अयम् (this) / उपदिष्टः (advised) / ते (to you) / विनाशः (destruction) / पापकर्मणा (by an evil-doer) / सपुत्रस्य (with sons) / सराष्ट्रस्य (with kingdom) / सामात्यस्य (with ministers) / निशाचर (O night-wanderer)
ramayan::7148.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7148.essence: One reckless counsel can ruin an entire house.
ramayan::7148.simple_meaning: Maricha angrily asks who advised the king in a way that will ruin him, his family, his kingdom, and his ministers.
ramayan::7148.simple_insight: Bad counsel can destroy far more than a single decision.
ramayan::7148.detailed_meaning: Maricha, forced into a dangerous royal command, lashes out at Ravana. He blames the advisor behind this plan, saying the advice will bring ruin not only to Ravana but to his sons, kingdom, and ministers.
ramayan::7148.modern_relevance: A friend forwards a reckless plan in a group chat and everyone nods along. One bad voice can drag an entire family, team, or company into disaster.
ramayan::7148.insight: It warns you to question advice that flatters impulse but endangers everything around it.

ramayan::7149.verse_sanskrit: कस्त्वया सुखिना राजन्नाभिनन्दति पापकृत् । केनेदमुपदिष्टं ते मृत्युद्वारमुपायतः । । 3413 । ।
ramayan::7149.verse_hindi: Which sinner is not able to see you happy? O king by whom is this gate of death
ramayan::7149.english_translation: Which sinner is not able to see you happy? O king, by whom was this gate of death devised for you through deceit?
ramayan::7149.translation_literal: कः (who) / त्वया (by you) / सुखिना (happy) / राजन् (O king) / न (not) / अभिनन्दति (rejoices in) / पापकृत् (sinner) / केन (by whom) / इदम् (this) / उपदिष्टम् (instructed/devised) / ते (for you) / मृत्युद्वारम् (gate of death) / उपायतः (through deceit/strategy)
ramayan::7149.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7149.essence: A clever scheme can be a doorway to death.
ramayan::7149.simple_meaning: Maricha asks who could possibly want the king to be happy, then says someone has deceitfully shown him a path that leads to death.
ramayan::7149.simple_insight: Deceit often looks like advice until it has already led you into danger.
ramayan::7149.detailed_meaning: Maricha is warning Ravana after being ordered to help with a dangerous plan. He sees the trap behind the request and speaks sharply, saying this scheme is not protection but a doorway to death for Ravana and his kingdom.
ramayan::7149.modern_relevance: A friend urges you into a deal that feels clever but smells wrong. The warning signs are already there; this verse is the voice that names the trap before you step into it.
ramayan::7149.insight: It pushes you to question advice that flatters ambition but quietly leads to ruin.

ramayan::7150.verse_sanskrit: शत्रवस्तव सुव्यक्तं हीनवीर्या निशाचराः । इच्छन्ति त्वां विनश्यन्तमुपरुद्धं बलीयसा । । 3414 । ।
ramayan::7150.verse_hindi: This is clear that your enemy demons are now powerless. Hence they want you to be engaged with a stronger power and be destroyed.
ramayan::7150.english_translation: It is clear, O night-roaming king, that your enemies, now powerless, want you trapped by a stronger force and destroyed.
ramayan::7150.translation_literal: शत्रवः (enemies) / तव (your) / सुव्यक्तम् (very clearly) / हीनवीर्याः (deprived of strength) / निशाचराः (night-roamers) / इच्छन्ति (want) / त्वाम् (you) / विनश्यन्तम् (one being destroyed) / उपरुद्धम् (blocked, trapped) / बलीयसा (by a stronger one)
ramayan::7150.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7150.essence: Weak enemies often win by luring you into a stronger trap.
ramayan::7150.simple_meaning: Ravana is being warned that his enemies, though weak, want to get him trapped by a stronger force and ruined.
ramayan::7150.simple_insight: Not every counsel is meant to protect you; some advice is a disguised push toward your collapse.
ramayan::7150.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, his own people are speaking sharply against the advice that has led him toward disaster. They see that his enemies are too weak to defeat him directly, so they are steering him into a trap where a stronger power will finish the job.
ramayan::7150.modern_relevance: A friend says, “Just ignore it, you’ll be fine,” while quietly pushing you into a situation that will expose you. The danger is not always the attack — sometimes it is the advice that makes you walk into it.
ramayan::7150.insight: It sharpens discernment: you learn to test advice by its likely result, not by its tone.

ramayan::7151.verse_sanskrit: केनेदमुपदिष्टं ते क्षुद्रेणाहितवादिना । यस्त्वामिच्छति नश्यन्तं स्वकृतेन निशाचर । । 3415 । ।
ramayan::7151.verse_hindi: O Ravana by which mean fellow is this advice given against your welfare? Who wants you to be destroyed by your own action.
ramayan::7151.english_translation: O Ravana, by which mean fellow was this harmful advice given against your welfare? Who wants you to be destroyed by your own action?
ramayan::7151.translation_literal: केन (by whom) / इदम् (this) / उपदिष्टम् (advised) / ते (to you) / क्षुद्रेण (by a mean fellow) / अहितवादिना (by one speaking what is harmful) / यः (who) / त्वाम् (you) / इच्छति (wants) / नश्यन्तम् (destroyed) / स्वकृतेन (by your own doing) / निशाचर (O night-walker)
ramayan::7151.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7151.essence: The real enemy may be the advice you keep obeying.
ramayan::7151.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told that someone has given him harmful advice, and that this advice is leading him toward destruction through his own actions.
ramayan::7151.simple_insight: It feels like a warning to check who is shaping your choices before their influence becomes your downfall.
ramayan::7151.detailed_meaning: Ravana has ignored wiser counsel and moved deeper into wrong action. Here, an observer names the real danger: not just Rama, but the bad advice feeding Ravana's own self-destruction. The verse exposes how ego listens only to what flatters it.
ramayan::7151.modern_relevance: A friend keeps telling you to double down on a bad decision because backing out would look weak. The danger is not just the decision — it is the voice that keeps feeding it.
ramayan::7151.insight: It shifts attention from the visible problem to the influence behind it, teaching you to question the counsel you follow.

ramayan::7152.verse_sanskrit: वध्याः खलु न हन्यन्ते सचिवास्तव रावण । ये त्वामुत्पथमारूढं न निगृह्णन्ति सर्वशः । । 3416 । ।
ramayan::7152.verse_hindi: O Ravana the ministers should have prevented you by all means from adopting this  wrong path. Since they have not done so, they deserve to be spain.
ramayan::7152.english_translation: O Ravana, the ministers should have restrained you in every way when you took the wrong path. Since they did not, they deserve blame.
ramayan::7152.translation_literal: वध्याः (deserving punishment) / खलु (indeed) / न (not) / हन्यन्ते (are killed) / सचिवाः (ministers) / तव (your) / रावण (O Ravana) / ये (who) / त्वाम् (you) / उत्पथम् (wrong path) / आरूढम् (mounted upon) / न (not) / निगृह्णन्ति (restrain) / सर्वशः (in every way)
ramayan::7152.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7152.essence: Silence around wrongdoing can make the bystanders guilty too.
ramayan::7152.simple_meaning: A ruler on a wrong path should be firmly restrained by wise ministers. If they stay silent, they become part of the wrongdoing.
ramayan::7152.simple_insight: It reminds you that loyalty is not flattery. Sometimes care means stopping someone before they go too far.
ramayan::7152.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already chosen the path of desire and arrogance. In this exchange, the speaker turns from Ravana himself to the ministers around him, saying they failed in their duty to restrain him. Their silence is treated as a moral failure.
ramayan::7152.modern_relevance: You watch a friend, boss, or sibling making a choice that will wreck everything, and everyone in the room politely stays quiet. This verse says silence can be complicity when someone is headed straight for disaster.
ramayan::7152.insight: It shifts responsibility from passive approval to active intervention when someone is drifting into harm.

ramayan::7153.verse_sanskrit: अमात्यैः कामवृत्तो हि राजा कापथमाश्रितः । निग्राह्यस्सर्वथा सदभिर्न निग्राह्यो निगृह्यसे । । 3417 । ।
ramayan::7153.verse_hindi: Good ministrers should always prevent a lustful king from taking resourse to an evil path. Why were you not stopped, even though you deserve to be checked.
ramayan::7153.english_translation: Good ministers should always restrain a lustful king from taking an evil path. Why were you not stopped, even though you deserved to be checked?
ramayan::7153.translation_literal: अमात्यैः (by ministers) / कामवृत्तः (one ruled by desire) / हि (indeed) / राजा (a king) / कापथम् (evil path) / आश्रितः (having taken refuge in) / निग्राह्यः (to be restrained) / सर्वथा (in every way) / सदभिः (by the good) / न (not) / निग्राह्यः (to be restrained) / निगृह्यसे (you are being restrained)
ramayan::7153.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7153.essence: Wise people stop power before desire turns it into ruin.
ramayan::7153.simple_meaning: A ruler who is driven by desire should be restrained by wise ministers before he goes further into wrongdoing.
ramayan::7153.simple_insight: It feels safer when someone wise can interrupt your worst impulse before it becomes a disaster.
ramayan::7153.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being rebuked by the voice of counsel around him. The point is not punishment but prevention: a king lost to desire should have been checked by ministers who cared about order, not flattered into ruin.
ramayan::7153.modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry message, sign the reckless deal, or say yes to the thing you already know is wrong. The people around you matter when they stop you in time.
ramayan::7153.insight: It shifts responsibility from blind impulse to wise restraint, showing that real support sometimes means saying no.

ramayan::7154.verse_sanskrit: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च यशश्च जयतां वर । स्वामिप्रसादात्सचिवाः प्राप्नुवन्ति निशाचर । । 3418 । ।
ramayan::7154.verse_hindi: O Ravana  the best among the successful ministers attain piety, prosperity, pleasures and fame by the grace of the king.
ramayan::7154.english_translation: O Ravana, the best among successful ministers attain dharma, wealth, desire, and fame by the king's grace.
ramayan::7154.translation_literal: धर्मम् (dharma) / अर्थम् (wealth) / च (and) / कामम् (desire) / च (and) / यशः (fame) / च (and) / जयताम् वर (best among the victorious) / स्वामिप्रसादात् (by the king's grace) / सचिवाः (ministers) / प्राप्नुवन्ति (attain) / निशाचर (O night-roamer)
ramayan::7154.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7154.essence: When a ruler is right, everyone around him can thrive.
ramayan::7154.simple_meaning: A good minister gains duty, prosperity, pleasure, and honor through the ruler's favor.
ramayan::7154.simple_insight: Loyal service is not empty; it can lift your whole life.
ramayan::7154.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned about rule and counsel. The speaker says that ministers flourish when they support a rightful king, because a ruler's grace brings duty, wealth, enjoyment, and honor. Good governance benefits everyone around it.
ramayan::7154.modern_relevance: You work under someone whose choices shape your day, your team, and your future. When leadership is steady and fair, the people who serve it can grow with dignity instead of just surviving.
ramayan::7154.insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the conditions created by wise leadership.

ramayan::7155.verse_sanskrit: विपर्यये तु तत्सर्वं व्यर्थं भवति रावण । व्यसनं स्वामिवैगुण्यात्प्राप्नुवन्तीतरे जनाः । । 3419 । ।
ramayan::7155.verse_hindi: Otherwise evrything will become useless, O Ravana  Others will suffer calamities on account of their masters vices.
ramayan::7155.english_translation: Otherwise, everything becomes useless, O Ravana. Other people suffer calamity because of the faults of their ruler.
ramayan::7155.translation_literal: विपर्यये (in the opposite case) / तु (indeed) / तत् (that) / सर्वम् (all) / व्यर्थम् (wasted, useless) / भवति (becomes) / रावण (O Ravana) / व्यसनम् (calamity, ruin) / स्वामि-वैगुण्यात् (because of the master's faults) / प्राप्नुवन्ति (they obtain, they suffer) / इतरः जनाः (other people)
ramayan::7155.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7155.essence: A leader's faults turn everyone else's work into waste.
ramayan::7155.simple_meaning: When a leader goes wrong, all the good around them is wasted, and others suffer for it.
ramayan::7155.simple_insight: Power is never private; your choices can damage people who never chose them.
ramayan::7155.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, a minister warns that a king's corruption ruins not only himself but the whole system around him. The warning is blunt: when the ruler goes astray, the damage spreads outward and everyone else bears it.
ramayan::7155.modern_relevance: A manager cuts corners, and the team spends weeks cleaning up the mess. One person's poor judgment can drain time, trust, and energy from everyone around them.
ramayan::7155.insight: It shifts responsibility upward: leadership is measured by the harm or stability it creates for others.

ramayan::7156.verse_sanskrit: राजमूलो हि धर्मश्च जयश्च जयतां वर । तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु रक्षितव्या नराधिपाः । । 34110 । ।
ramayan::7156.verse_hindi: O Ravana, the best among the victorious indeed the king is at the root of righteousness and victory.Therefore, the king should be protected by all at every stage.
ramayan::7156.english_translation: O Ravana, the best among the victorious, righteousness and victory depend on the king. Therefore, kings must be protected in every circumstance.
ramayan::7156.translation_literal: राजमूलः (rooted in the king) / हि (indeed) / धर्मः (righteousness) / च (and) / जयः (victory) / च (and) / जयताम् (of the victorious) / वर (O best) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वासु (in all) / अवस्थासु (situations) / रक्षितव्याः (must be protected) / नराधिपाः (kings)
ramayan::7156.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7156.essence: Protect the ruler, and the whole order survives.
ramayan::7156.simple_meaning: Righteous order and victory depend on the king, so the king must be protected in every situation.
ramayan::7156.simple_insight: Leadership is not optional decoration; it is the hinge on which order turns.
ramayan::7156.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned that a kingdom rises or falls with its ruler. The verse argues that the king is the source of order, success, and protection, so ministers and subjects must safeguard him in every condition.
ramayan::7156.modern_relevance: A team collapses when everyone treats the leader like a target instead of a responsibility. The same is true in a family, a company, or a community that forgets who carries the burden.
ramayan::7156.insight: It shifts attention from private advantage to the shared duty of preserving the structure that protects everyone.

ramayan::7157.verse_sanskrit: राज्यं पालयितुं शक्यं न तीक्ष्णेन निशाचर । न चापि प्रतिकूलेन नाविनीतेन राक्षस । । 34111 । ।
ramayan::7157.verse_hindi: O nightwalking demon  a kingdom cannnot be governed by a king who is rude or hostile or impolite.
ramayan::7157.english_translation: O night-walking demon, a kingdom cannot be governed by a king who is rude, hostile, or impolite.
ramayan::7157.translation_literal: राज्यम् (kingdom) / पालयितुम् (to govern) / शक्यम् (possible) / न (not) / तीक्ष्णेन (by the sharp/rude one) / निशाचर (night-walker) / न (not) / चापि (and also not) / प्रतिकूलेन (by the hostile one) / न (not) / अविनीतेन (by the impolite/untrained one) / राक्षस (O demon)
ramayan::7157.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7157.essence: A harsh ruler ruins the very kingdom he tries to protect.
ramayan::7157.simple_meaning: A ruler cannot hold a kingdom together through harshness, hostility, or bad manners. Leadership needs self-control and steady conduct.
ramayan::7157.simple_insight: Real authority comes from restraint. Force may command fear, but it cannot sustain order.
ramayan::7157.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned that a kingdom survives only when its ruler has discipline. The surrounding verses say the king is the root of righteousness and victory, and this line sharpens that point: a harsh, hostile ruler destroys the very realm he tries to hold.
ramayan::7157.modern_relevance: You snapped at your team, then wondered why everything felt tense. People do not follow force for long; they follow steadiness, respect, and control.
ramayan::7157.insight: It shifts leadership from domination to self-mastery. The ruler's inner conduct becomes the condition for outer order.

ramayan::7158.verse_sanskrit: ये तीक्ष्णमन्त्रास्सचिवा भज्यन्ते सह तेन वै । विषमे तुरगा श्शीघ्रा मन्दसारथयो यथा । । 34112 । ।
ramayan::7158.verse_hindi: Ministers who adopt improper strategies go down along with the king just like swift horses driven by a slow charioteer on a rugged terrain.
ramayan::7158.english_translation: Ministers who adopt improper strategies go down along with the king just like swift horses driven by a slow charioteer on a rugged terrain.
ramayan::7158.translation_literal: ये (those who) / तीक्ष्ण-मन्त्राः (sharp-strategy / improper-counsel) / सचिवाः (ministers) / भज्यन्ते (are broken down) / सह (together with) / तेन (that king) / वै (indeed) / विषमे (on rough ground) / तुरगाः (horses) / शीघ्राः (swift) / मन्द-सारथयः (with slow charioteers) / यथा (just as)
ramayan::7158.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7158.essence: Bad strategy takes the leader down with the advisors.
ramayan::7158.simple_meaning: A ruler is only as steady as the advice around him. If ministers give bad guidance, both they and the king suffer together.
ramayan::7158.simple_insight: The people who advise you shape the damage as much as the decision itself.
ramayan::7158.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned about how a kingdom collapses. A king cannot survive on force alone; if his ministers use reckless strategy, the whole court falls together, like fast horses stumbling under a careless driver on bad ground.
ramayan::7158.modern_relevance: A team is racing toward a launch, but the plan is sloppy and nobody wants to say it. One bad strategy from the people in charge can sink the whole effort, not just the leader.
ramayan::7158.insight: It teaches you to judge leadership by the quality of counsel it accepts and the discipline it keeps.

ramayan::7159.verse_sanskrit: बहवस्साधवो लोके युक्ता धर्ममनुष्ठिताः । परेषामपराधेन विनष्टास्सपरिच्छदाः । । 34113 । ।
ramayan::7159.verse_hindi: Persons who walk the righteous path go down in this world along with their kith and kin due to the mistakes committed by others .
ramayan::7159.english_translation: Many good people in the world, devoted to righteous conduct, are ruined along with their families because of the faults of others.
ramayan::7159.translation_literal: बहवः (many) / साधवः (good people) / लोके (in the world) / युक्ताः (joined, devoted) / धर्मम् (righteous conduct) / अनुष्ठिताः (practising) / परेषाम् (of others) / अपराधेन (by fault) / विनष्टाः (ruined) / सपरिच्छदाः (with family and dependents)
ramayan::7159.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7159.essence: Good conduct does not shield you from the fallout of others’ mistakes.
ramayan::7159.simple_meaning: Even good, dutiful people can suffer because of someone else’s wrongdoing. The cost of another person’s failure can spread to an entire family.
ramayan::7159.simple_insight: It reminds you that righteousness does not always protect you from collateral damage.
ramayan::7159.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned that a king’s harshness harms everyone under him. The point widens: when power fails, even decent people and their households are dragged into the ruin caused by others.
ramayan::7159.modern_relevance: You do everything right, yet one reckless decision from a manager, parent, or partner ripples through everyone around them. The pain is unfair, but it is real.
ramayan::7159.insight: It shifts attention from personal merit to the shared consequences of other people’s choices.

ramayan::7160.verse_sanskrit: स्वामिना प्रतिकूलेन प्रजास्तीक्ष्णेन रावण । रक्ष्यमाणा न वर्धन्ते मेषा गोमायुना यथा । । 34114 । ।
ramayan::7160.verse_hindi: O Ravana, people who are ruled by a cruel and hostile king will not grow like the sheep protected by a jackal.
ramayan::7160.english_translation: O Ravana, people ruled by a cruel and hostile king do not prosper, just as sheep guarded by a jackal do not grow.
ramayan::7160.translation_literal: स्वामिना (by the ruler) / प्रतिकूलेन (hostile, adverse) / प्रजाः (subjects, people) / तीक्ष्णेन (cruel, harsh) / रावण (O Ravana) / रक्ष्यमाणा (being protected, being guarded) / न (not) / वर्धन्ते (grow, prosper) / मेषाः (sheep) / गोमायुना (by a jackal) / यथा (as, like)
ramayan::7160.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7160.essence: A hostile ruler destroys the very people he claims to protect.
ramayan::7160.simple_meaning: People do not flourish under a cruel, hostile ruler. Even if they are protected, that protection is unsafe and cannot help them grow.
ramayan::7160.simple_insight: Leadership is not just control; it must create safety for others to thrive.
ramayan::7160.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, the warning grows sharper: bad leadership does not merely hurt the ruler, it poisons everyone beneath him. Valmiki compares such protection to a jackal guarding sheep — a safeguard that is really a threat.
ramayan::7160.modern_relevance: You can feel this in a team where the manager rules through fear. People stop taking initiative, shrink their voice, and survive instead of growing.
ramayan::7160.insight: It shifts attention from power to responsibility: authority is judged by whether it lets others flourish.

ramayan::7161.verse_sanskrit: अवश्यं विनशिष्यन्ति सर्वे रावण राक्षसाः । येषां त्वं कर्कशो राजा दुर्बुद्धिरजितेन्द्रियः । । 34115 । ।
ramayan::7161.verse_hindi: Under a rude, crooked king whose senses are not under his control the demons will surely perish.
ramayan::7161.english_translation: Under a rude, crooked king whose senses are not under his control, the demons will surely perish.
ramayan::7161.translation_literal: अवश्यम् (surely) / विनशिष्यन्ति (will perish) / सर्वे (all) / रावण (O Ravana) / राक्षसाः (demons) / येषाम् (whose) / त्वम् (you) / कर्कशः (rude, harsh) / राजा (king) / दुर्बुद्धिः (crooked-minded) / अजितेन्द्रियः (one whose senses are uncontrolled)
ramayan::7161.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7161.essence: A leader who cannot govern himself will destroy what he governs.
ramayan::7161.simple_meaning: A harsh ruler who cannot control his senses brings destruction on everyone under him.
ramayan::7161.simple_insight: Power without self-mastery does not stay contained; it spills outward and harms others.
ramayan::7161.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned that his own character is dooming his people. The issue is not only enemy strength; it is the inner disorder of a king whose senses rule him instead of his judgment.
ramayan::7161.modern_relevance: A manager who lashes out in meetings, changes direction on impulse, and never checks his temper slowly breaks the whole team. People do not just suffer the leader's moods — they suffer the leader's lack of restraint.
ramayan::7161.insight: It shifts responsibility from external threats to the ruler's own discipline and conduct.

ramayan::7162.verse_sanskrit: तदिदं काकतालीयं घोरमासादितं मया । अत्र किं शोचनीयस्त्वं ससैन्यो विनशिष्यसि । । 34116 । ।
ramayan::7162.verse_hindi: I am faced with  this dreadful disaster accidentally. You will not only be in a miserable state because of your misdeeds, you will perish along with your army.
ramayan::7162.english_translation: I am faced with this dreadful disaster by chance. Why should I grieve for you? You and your army will perish.
ramayan::7162.translation_literal: तत् (that) / इदम् (this) / काकतालीयम् (by chance, like a crow and palm-fruit coincidence) / घोरम् (terrible) / आसादितम् (has been encountered) / मया (by me) / अत्र (here) / किम् (why) / शोचनीयः (to be grieved for) / त्वम् (you) / ससैन्यः (with army) / विनशिष्यसि (will perish)
ramayan::7162.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7162.essence: A cornered mind calls disaster chance and answers with contempt.
ramayan::7162.simple_meaning: Ravana says this disaster has come on him by chance, so he sees no reason to mourn for his enemy. He predicts that the enemy and his army will be destroyed.
ramayan::7162.simple_insight: Panic can turn into cold contempt when someone feels cornered.
ramayan::7162.detailed_meaning: Ravana speaks in the middle of a collapsing situation, refusing pity and turning the moment into a threat. He dismisses the enemy's fate and insists that both the enemy and his army are headed for destruction.
ramayan::7162.modern_relevance: A person gets backed into a corner in a meeting and suddenly talks harder, louder, and colder than before. Fear often hides itself as certainty.
ramayan::7162.insight: It shows how a trapped mind can mask fear with threats and certainty.

ramayan::7163.verse_sanskrit: मां निहत्य तु रामश्च न चिरात्त्वां वधिष्यति । अनेन कृतकृत्योऽस्मि म्रियेयमरिणा हतः । । 34117 । ।
ramayan::7163.verse_hindi: Rama will kill you not long after killing me.Hence even if I die in the hands of the enemy, my desire will be fulfilled.
ramayan::7163.english_translation: Rama will kill you not long after killing me. Hence even if I die in the hands of the enemy, my purpose will be fulfilled.
ramayan::7163.translation_literal: मां (me) / निहत्य (having killed) / तु (but) / रामः (Rama) / च (and) / न चिरात् (not long after) / त्वाम् (you) / वधिष्यति (will kill) / अनेन (by this) / कृतकृत्यः (one who has accomplished his task) / अस्मि (I am) / म्रियेयम् (I may die) / अरिणा (by the enemy) / हतः (struck)
ramayan::7163.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7163.essence: Even death cannot interrupt a consequence already in motion.
ramayan::7163.simple_meaning: Ravana says that even if Rama kills him first, Rama will soon kill the other person too. So Ravana feels his mission is complete even in death.
ramayan::7163.simple_insight: A person can face death without panic when the larger outcome is already clear.
ramayan::7163.detailed_meaning: Ravana is taunting and warning his enemy in the middle of a deadly exchange. He says Rama will soon kill him and then finish the rest. Even if he dies first, he believes the larger result is already sealed.
ramayan::7163.modern_relevance: You can be in the middle of a conflict and still know the larger pattern. When the consequences are already set in motion, panic changes nothing.
ramayan::7163.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate fear to the larger chain of consequences.

ramayan::7164.verse_sanskrit: दर्शनादेव रामस्य हतं मामवधारय । आत्मानं च हतं विद्धि हृत्वा सीतां सबान्धवम् । । 34118 । ।
ramayan::7164.verse_hindi: Yu most understand that if I die at the very sight of Rama, you along with your relatives will perish with the abduction of Sita.
ramayan::7164.english_translation: Understand that I am already as good as dead at the sight of Rama. And know that you and your relatives are ruined by taking Sita away.
ramayan::7164.translation_literal: दर्शनात् (by sight) / एव (indeed) / रामस्य (of Rama) / हतम् (killed) / माम् (me) / अवधारय (understand) / आत्मानम् (yourself) / च (and) / हतम् (killed) / विद्धि (know) / हृत्वा (having taken away) / सीताम् (Sita) / सबान्धवम् (with relatives)
ramayan::7164.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7164.essence: Wrong action carries its own collapse from the beginning.
ramayan::7164.simple_meaning: Ravana warns that just seeing Rama will mean his own death, and abducting Sita will bring ruin on Ravana and his family.
ramayan::7164.simple_insight: Some actions carry their punishment inside them from the start.
ramayan::7164.detailed_meaning: Ravana is cornered and still defiant. He tells his ally that Rama's mere presence is enough to finish him, and that stealing Sita will destroy the thief and his whole line. The verse turns arrogance into a warning.
ramayan::7164.modern_relevance: You know that message, lie, or shortcut will cost more than it gives — but you reach for it anyway. This is the moment when the future punishment is already visible.
ramayan::7164.insight: It shifts the mind from short-term gain to the hidden ruin built into wrongdoing.

ramayan::7165.verse_sanskrit: आनयिष्यसि चेत्सीतामाश्रमात्सहितो मया । नैवत्वमसि नाहं च नैव लङ्का न राक्षसाः । । 34119 । ।
ramayan::7165.verse_hindi: If you bring Sita from the hermitage with my assistance, know that none of us will surviveyou nor I, nor Lanka , nor the demons.
ramayan::7165.english_translation: If you bring Sita from the hermitage with my help, know that none of us will survive: neither you nor I, nor Lanka, nor the demons.
ramayan::7165.translation_literal: आनयिष्यसि (you will bring) / चेत् (if) / सीताम् (Sita) / आश्रमात् (from the hermitage) / सहितः (together with) / मया (by me/with my help) / नैव (not at all) / त्वम् (you) / असि (will exist) / न (not) / अहम् (I) / च (and) / नैव (not at all) / लङ्का (Lanka) / न (nor) / राक्षसाः (the demons)
ramayan::7165.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7165.essence: Desire that ignores warning ends by destroying its own world.
ramayan::7165.simple_meaning: Ravana warns that if Sita is taken from the hermitage, destruction will follow for everyone involved. The act will ruin both sides, not just one person.
ramayan::7165.simple_insight: Unchecked wanting does not stay private; it spreads ruin outward.
ramayan::7165.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to the one person who still tries to warn him. The abduction of Sita has already begun to poison everything around him, and this verse makes the cost plain: not just personal defeat, but the collapse of Lanka itself.
ramayan::7165.modern_relevance: You keep pushing for something you know will break trust in your home, your team, or your marriage. The damage never stays confined to the one thing you wanted.
ramayan::7165.insight: It shifts the mind from short-term desire to the wider fallout of obsession.

ramayan::7166.verse_sanskrit: निवार्यमाणस्तु मया हितैषिणा न मृष्यसे वाक्यमिदं निशाचर । परेतकल्पा हि गतायुषो नरा हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम् । । 34120 । ।
ramayan::7166.verse_hindi: O Ravana, you do not understand this word of warning coming from your wellwisher. Men who are going to die do not heed the advice given by their friends.
ramayan::7166.english_translation: O Ravana, you do not understand this warning from your well-wisher. People whose lives are nearing their end do not accept the good counsel spoken by friends.
ramayan::7166.translation_literal: निवार्यमाणः (being restrained) / तु (but) / मया (by me) / हितैषिणा (by one wishing your good) / न (not) / मृष्यसे (you will tolerate/accept) / वाक्यम् (word/speech) / इदम् (this) / निशाचर (O night-wanderer) / परेतकल्पाः (like the dead) / हि (indeed) / गतायुषः (those whose life is gone) / नराः (people) / हितम् (beneficial counsel) / न (not) / गृह्णन्ति (they accept) / सुहृद्भिः (by friends) / ईरितम् (spoken)
ramayan::7166.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7166.essence: Pride makes even lifesaving advice feel intolerable.
ramayan::7166.simple_meaning: A person headed toward destruction stops listening, even to sincere warning from a friend.
ramayan::7166.simple_insight: It’s sobering to notice how pride can make guidance feel unbearable right when it’s needed most.
ramayan::7166.detailed_meaning: Maricha, terrified by Ravana’s plan, speaks as a friend trying to pull him back from disaster. He warns that a person already rushing toward death stops recognizing help, even when it comes from goodwill. The verse is a last attempt to break Ravana’s blindness.
ramayan::7166.modern_relevance: You’re about to send the angry text, even after the friend who knows you best says stop. In that moment, warning can feel insulting — exactly when it matters most.
ramayan::7166.insight: It shifts the mind to notice when ego is rejecting useful feedback because the outcome is already headed downhill.

ramayan::7167.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं मारीचो रावणं ततः । गच्छावेत्यब्रवीद्दीनो भयाद्रात्रिंचरप्रभोः । । 3421 । ।
ramayan::7167.verse_hindi: Having thus spoken to the demonking, the distressed Maricha said out of fear, Let both of us go.
ramayan::7167.english_translation: Having thus spoken to the demon-king, the distressed Maricha said out of fear, "Let both of us go."
ramayan::7167.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / तु (indeed) / वचनम् (the words) / मारीचः (Maricha) / रावणम् (to Ravana) / ततः (then) / गच्छाव (let us go) / इति (thus) / अब्रवीत् (said) / दीनः (distressed) / भयात् (out of fear) / रात्रिंचरप्रभोः (of the lord of the night-walkers)
ramayan::7167.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7167.essence: Fearful wisdom still cannot save a stubborn man.
ramayan::7167.simple_meaning: Maricha, terrified of Rama, tells Ravana that they should leave instead of pushing ahead.
ramayan::7167.simple_insight: Fear makes clear what pride refuses to hear.
ramayan::7167.detailed_meaning: Maricha has just warned Ravana that abducting Sita will end in disaster. Here he breaks further from Ravana's certainty and, shaken by fear, urges retreat. It is not a teaching verse but a turning point in Ravana's bad decision.
ramayan::7167.modern_relevance: You can feel the alarm in your body before your ego admits it. Sometimes the first wise move is simply to leave.
ramayan::7167.insight: It shows how danger can be recognized clearly, even when the other person refuses to listen.

ramayan::7168.verse_sanskrit: दृष्टश्चाहं पुनस्तेन शरचापासिधारिणा । मद्वधोद्यतशस्त्रेऽण विनष्टं जीवितं च मे । । 3422 । ।
ramayan::7168.verse_hindi: If that warrior Rama carrying bow, arrows and sword sees me once again he will raise his weapon to kill me, and I will cease to be.
ramayan::7168.english_translation: If Rama, armed with bow, arrows, and sword, sees me again, he will raise his weapon to kill me, and my life will end.
ramayan::7168.translation_literal: दृष्टः (seen) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / पुनः (again) / तेन (by him) / शर-चाप-असि-धारिणा (the one bearing arrows, bow, and sword) / मद्-वध-उद्यत-शस्त्रे (with weapon raised for my killing) / विनष्टम् (destroyed) / जीवितम् (life) / च (and) / मे (my)
ramayan::7168.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7168.essence: One more sight of Rama means death for him.
ramayan::7168.simple_meaning: Maricha says that if Rama sees him again, Rama will attack and kill him.
ramayan::7168.simple_insight: Fear sharpens his honesty: he knows one more encounter will end him.
ramayan::7168.detailed_meaning: Maricha has already warned Ravana that Rama will not spare him. Now he explains why he wants to flee: if Rama sees him again, armed and ready, Maricha expects certain death. The verse is a fearful supporting detail in his attempt to escape.
ramayan::7168.modern_relevance: You know the meeting is over before it starts. One more look, one more conversation, and the whole thing collapses.
ramayan::7168.insight: It shows how clear-eyed fear can cut through denial and force retreat.

ramayan::7169.verse_sanskrit: न हि रामं पराक्रम्य जीवन्प्रतिनिवर्तते । वर्तते प्रतिरूपोऽसौ यमदण्डहतस्य ते । । 3423 । ।
ramayan::7169.verse_hindi: No one who exhibits his heroism before Rama will come back alive. To you, already hit by Yamas staff, he is another form of the same Yama.
ramayan::7169.english_translation: No one who shows his strength before Rama comes back alive. To you, already struck by Yama's staff, he is another form of Yama.
ramayan::7169.translation_literal: न हि (not indeed) / रामम् (Rama) / पराक्रम्य (having displayed heroism before) / जीवन् (living) / प्रतिनिवर्तते (returns back) । / वर्तते (is) / प्रतिरूपः (a likeness / another form) / असौ (that one) / यमदण्डहतस्य (of one struck by Yama's staff) / ते (to you) ।
ramayan::7169.speaker: Maricha
ramayan::7169.essence: Against Rama, raw bravado is already a death wish.
ramayan::7169.simple_meaning: Mārīca warns Rāvaṇa that anyone who confronts Rama in battle does not return alive. To Rāvaṇa, Rama is already like death itself.
ramayan::7169.detailed_meaning: Mārīca has been trapped by Rāvaṇa's plan and knows what Rama is capable of. He warns that approaching Rama with force is not a contest but a death sentence, and he speaks from fear, not theory.
ramayan::7169.modern_relevance: You are about to send the sharp reply, the risky email, the grand challenge. But something in you knows this fight will not flatter your ego. Some battles only expose how fragile bravado is.
ramayan::7169.insight: It shifts the mind from proving strength to recognising when strength will only be punished.

ramayan::7170.verse_sanskrit: किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुमेवं त्वयि दुरात्मनि । एष गच्छाम्यहं तात स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु निशाचर । । 3424 । ।
ramayan::7170.verse_hindi: What can I do if you remain evilminded? O dear demon, I am going. May your path be auspicious
ramayan::7170.english_translation: What can I do if you remain evil-minded? O dear demon, I am going. May your path be auspicious.
ramayan::7170.translation_literal: किम् (what) / नु (indeed) / शक्यम् (possible) / मया (by me) / कर्तुम् (to do) / एवम् (thus) / त्वयि (in you) / दुरात्मनि (evil-minded one) / एषः (this) / गच्छामि (I am going) / अहम् (I) / तात (dear one) / स्वस्ति (well-being) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may it be) / निशाचर (night-wanderer)
ramayan::7170.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7170.essence: You cannot rescue someone who chooses blindness.
ramayan::7170.simple_meaning: He gives up trying to change someone who is bent on wrongdoing and leaves with a final blessing.
ramayan::7170.simple_insight: Sometimes the cleanest response to stubborn harm is to step away without carrying hatred.
