ramayan::7170.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been warned that attacking Rama will lead to death. Instead of arguing further, the speaker turns away from him and offers a formal farewell. The moment is less about persuasion than about accepting that some minds will not change.
ramayan::7170.modern_relevance: You have said the same careful thing three times, and the other person still twists it. At some point, leaving without bitterness is the only honest move.
ramayan::7170.insight: It teaches you to stop forcing understanding where only refusal remains.

ramayan::7171.verse_sanskrit: प्रहृष्टस्त्वभवत्तेन वचनेन स रावणः । परिष्वज्य सुसंश्लिष्टमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 3425 । ।
ramayan::7171.verse_hindi: Ravana was so overwhelmed with joy to hear those words that he embraced him tightly and said:.
ramayan::7171.english_translation: Ravana was so overwhelmed with joy to hear those words that he embraced him tightly and said:
ramayan::7171.translation_literal: प्रहृष्टः (delighted) / अभवत् (became) / तेन (by that) / वचनेन (by the speech) / सः (he) / रावणः (Ravana) / परिष्वज्य (embracing) / सुसंश्लिष्टम् (very tightly) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (word/speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7171.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7171.essence: Pleasure at agreement can make a reckless mind lean in further.
ramayan::7171.simple_meaning: Ravana is delighted by the reply, embraces the other person, and begins speaking warmly.
ramayan::7171.simple_insight: A flattering response can make even a dangerous mind open up.
ramayan::7171.detailed_meaning: After Maricha warns him that challenging Rama means death, Ravana hears a reply that pleases him. He immediately embraces Maricha and answers with renewed confidence, setting up the next manipulation in their exchange.
ramayan::7171.modern_relevance: A person finally says what you wanted to hear, and your guard drops instantly. The conversation turns, not because the truth changed, but because your pride got fed.
ramayan::7171.insight: It shows how praise can override judgment and pull you deeper into bad decisions.

ramayan::7172.verse_sanskrit: एतच्छौण्डीर्ययुक्तं ते मच्छन्दवशवर्तिनः । इदानीमसि मारीचः पूर्वमन्यो निशाचरः । । 3426 । ।
ramayan::7172.verse_hindi: Act according to my wish. It befits your valour. You were a different demon earlier. Now you are Maricha.
ramayan::7172.english_translation: Act according to my wish. It befits your valour. You were a different demon earlier. Now you are Maricha.
ramayan::7172.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / शौण्डीर्ययुक्तम् (joined with valour) / ते (your) / मच्छन्दवशवर्तिनः (one who follows my wish) / इदानीम् (now) / असि (you are) / मारीचः (Maricha) / पूर्वम् (earlier) / अन्यः (another) / निशाचरः (night-roamer, demon)
ramayan::7172.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7172.essence: Praise becomes a tool for control.
ramayan::7172.simple_meaning: Ravana flatters Maricha, telling him to follow his command and praising his bravery, while reminding him of his past identity.
ramayan::7172.simple_insight: No insight is offered here; the verse is part of a manipulative exchange.
ramayan::7172.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just won Maricha over with harsh words and praise. He now seals the manipulation by calling Maricha brave, obedient, and transformed. The scene is not a teaching moment but the tightening of Ravana's scheme.
ramayan::7172.modern_relevance: A person finally gives in after hours of pressure, and the other side instantly calls it loyalty. The compliment is not kindness — it is control dressed as approval.
ramayan::7172.insight: It shows how flattery can be used to bend someone into compliance.

ramayan::7173.verse_sanskrit: आरुह्यतामयं शीघ्रं रथो रत्नविभूषितः । मया सह तथा युक्तः पिशाचवदनैः खरैः । । 3427 । ।
ramayan::7173.verse_hindi: Ascend quickly with me this chariot encrusted with gems and yoked with donkeys with devils faces৷৷
ramayan::7173.english_translation: Ascend quickly with me this gem-adorned chariot yoked with donkey-faced monsters.
ramayan::7173.translation_literal: आरुह्यताम् (ascend) / अयम् (this) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / रथः (chariot) / रत्नविभूषितः (adorned with gems) / मया सह (with me) / तथा (thus) / युक्तः (yoked) / पिशाचवदनैः (with demon-faced) / खरैः (donkeys)
ramayan::7173.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7173.essence: A glittering invitation can be the first step in a cruel plan.
ramayan::7173.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Maricha to get into his gem-studded chariot, which is drawn by monstrous donkeys.
ramayan::7173.simple_insight: The verse is just the setup for Ravana's scheme, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::7173.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already won Maricha over with flattery. Now he orders him to climb into a jeweled chariot pulled by grotesque creatures, the first step in a plan to lure Sita and trap Rama. The verse is part of the manipulation, not the moral point.
ramayan::7173.modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person pulls you into a flashy plan before you can see the trap. The danger is not the vehicle — it is the person inviting you in.
ramayan::7173.insight: It shows how persuasion can hide coercion behind luxury and speed.

ramayan::7174.verse_sanskrit: प्रलोभयित्वा वैदेहीं यथेष्टं गन्तुमर्हसि । तां शून्ये प्रसभं सीतामानयिष्यामि मैथिलीम् । । 3428 । ।
ramayan::7174.verse_hindi: You may go whereever you like after tempting Vaidehi. When the princess of Mithila  is alone, I will bring her by force.
ramayan::7174.english_translation: You may go wherever you like after tempting Vaidehi. When the princess of Mithila is alone, I will bring Sita by force.
ramayan::7174.translation_literal: प्रलोभयित्वा (having tempted) / वैदेहीं (Vaidehi) / यथेष्टम् (as desired) / गन्तुम् (to go) / अर्हसि (you are fit) / ताम् (her) / शून्ये (when alone) / प्रसभम् (forcibly) / सीताम् (Sita) / आनयिष्यामि (I will bring) / मैथिलीम् (the princess of Mithila)
ramayan::7174.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7174.essence: Cruelty becomes easier once the victim is made alone.
ramayan::7174.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Maricha to distract Sita and leave. Once Sita is isolated, Ravana says he will seize her by force.
ramayan::7174.simple_insight: Manipulation often begins with distraction, not violence.
ramayan::7174.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has already lured Maricha into a cruel scheme. He now explains the next step: tempt Sita, create a moment of isolation, and then abduct her. The verse shows the cold planning behind the abduction.
ramayan::7174.modern_relevance: A person keeps talking just long enough to separate you from support, then makes the real move. The danger is rarely announced in advance.
ramayan::7174.insight: It teaches you to notice how coercion is prepared through distraction and isolation.

ramayan::7175.verse_sanskrit: ततो रावणमारीचौ विमानमिव तं रथम् । आरुह्य ययतुश्शीघ्रं तस्मादाश्रममण्डलात् । । 3429 । ।
ramayan::7175.verse_hindi: Thereafter Ravana and Maricha ascended the chariot, which was like an aerial car, and quickly departed from that cluster of hermitages.
ramayan::7175.english_translation: Thereafter Ravana and Maricha ascended the chariot, which was like an aerial car, and quickly departed from that cluster of hermitages.
ramayan::7175.translation_literal: ततः (thereafter) / रावणमारीचौ (Ravana and Maricha) / विमानमिव (like an aerial car) / तं रथम् (that chariot) / आरुह्य (having mounted) / ययतुः (they departed) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / तस्मात् (from that) / आश्रममण्डलात् (cluster of hermitages)
ramayan::7175.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7175.essence: The scheme is no longer talk; it is now in motion.
ramayan::7175.simple_meaning: Ravana and Maricha get into the chariot and leave the hermitage area quickly.
ramayan::7175.simple_insight: A plot is moving forward, but no lesson is being stated yet.
ramayan::7175.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already pressed Maricha into helping him trap Sita. After the temptation and threat, both men mount the gem-studded chariot and leave the hermitage district at speed. The verse simply moves the scene into action.
ramayan::7175.modern_relevance: You watch two people leave a room after making a bad plan. The real damage begins not in the argument, but in the decision to go through with it.
ramayan::7175.insight: It shifts attention from moral debate to the consequences of chosen action.

ramayan::7176.verse_sanskrit: तथैव तत्र पश्यन्तौ पत्तनानि वनानि च । गीरींश्च सरितस्सर्वा राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च । । 34210 । ।
ramayan::7176.verse_hindi: And likewise, they went past towns, forests, mountains, streams, states and cities.
ramayan::7176.english_translation: And likewise, they went past towns, forests, mountains, streams, states and cities.
ramayan::7176.translation_literal: तथैव (likewise) / तत्र (there) / पश्यन्तौ (seeing) / पत्तनानि (towns) / वनानि (forests) / च (and) / गिरीन् (mountains) / च (and) / सरितः (streams) / सर्वाḥ (all) / राष्ट्राणि (states) / नगराणि (cities) / च (and)
ramayan::7176.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7176.essence: The journey continues through every kind of terrain.
ramayan::7176.simple_meaning: They moved onward, passing over every kind of landscape and settlement along the way.
ramayan::7176.simple_insight: The journey keeps going until the destination is reached.
ramayan::7176.detailed_meaning: Ravana and Maricha are still in motion, crossing through many lands on their way toward Rama's hermitage. Nothing decisive happens here; this verse simply stretches the journey before the next arrival.
ramayan::7176.insight: It marks travel and transition, not a teaching or decision.

ramayan::7177.verse_sanskrit: समेत्य दण्डकारण्यं राघवस्याश्रमं ततः । ददर्श सह मारीचो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । । 34211 । ।
ramayan::7177.verse_hindi: Ravana, king of the demons, accompanied by Maricha, then reached Dandaka forest and saw Ramas hermitage.
ramayan::7177.english_translation: Ravana, king of the demons, accompanied by Maricha, then reached Dandaka forest and saw Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7177.translation_literal: समेत्य (having reached) / दण्डकारण्यम् (Dandaka forest) / राघवस्य (of Raghava) / आश्रमम् (hermitage) / ततः (then) / ददर्श (saw) / सह (together with) / मारीचः (Maricha) / रावणः (Ravana) / राक्षसाधिपः (lord of the rakshasas)
ramayan::7177.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7177.essence: The threat has reached the threshold of Rama's refuge.
ramayan::7177.simple_meaning: Ravana and Maricha arrive at Rama's hermitage in Dandaka forest and see it for themselves.
ramayan::7177.simple_insight: The danger has reached the place it came to disturb.
ramayan::7177.detailed_meaning: Ravana has crossed into Dandaka forest with Maricha after the long flight from the hermitage. They now stand before Rama's retreat, the quiet center of a coming deceit. This is only the arrival before the trap is set.
ramayan::7177.modern_relevance: You can feel the moment before a disruption lands: the message has been sent, the door is opening, and the calm space you trusted is about to be entered.
ramayan::7177.insight: It marks the arrival of conflict, not the conflict itself.

ramayan::7178.verse_sanskrit: अवतीर्य रथात्तस्मात्ततः काञ्चनभूषणात् । हस्ते गृहीत्वा मारीचं रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । । 34212 । ।
ramayan::7178.verse_hindi: Then Ravana got off the chariot decorated with golden embellishments and, holding Marichas hand, said:.
ramayan::7178.english_translation: Then Ravana got down from his chariot, bright with gold ornaments, took Maricha by the hand, and spoke:
ramayan::7178.translation_literal: अवतीर्य (having descended) / रथात् (from the chariot) / तस्मात् (from that) / ततः (then) / काञ्चनभूषणात् (gold-adorned) / हस्ते (by the hand) / गृहीत्वा (having taken) / मारीचं (Maricha) / रावणः (Ravana) / वाक्यम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7178.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7178.essence: The scene pauses just before Ravana gives the order.
ramayan::7178.simple_meaning: Ravana gets down from his gold-decorated chariot, takes Maricha by the hand, and speaks to him.
ramayan::7178.simple_insight: A decisive move often begins with a simple gesture.
ramayan::7178.detailed_meaning: Ravana has reached the forest with Maricha and now steps down from his chariot to address him directly. The verse only sets up the next instruction, showing the moment before the plan is revealed.
ramayan::7178.modern_relevance: You pull someone aside before making the ask that changes everything. The real turning point is still one sentence away.
ramayan::7178.insight: It prepares the reader for action by showing the exact moment before the plan is spoken.

ramayan::7179.verse_sanskrit: एतदाश्रमपदं दृश्यते कदलीवृतम् । क्रियतां तत्सखे शीघ्रं यदर्थं वयमागताः । । 34213 । ।
ramayan::7179.verse_hindi: O friend here is the site of the hermitage surrounded by banana plants. Quickly get to work on the purpose for which we have come.
ramayan::7179.english_translation: O friend, here is the hermitage site, surrounded by banana plants. Quickly do what we came here to do.
ramayan::7179.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / आश्रमपदम् (hermitage site) / दृश्यते (is seen) / कदलीवृतम् (surrounded by banana plants) / क्रियताम् (let it be done) / तत् (that) / सखे (O friend) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / यत्-अर्थम् (for which purpose) / वयम् (we) / आगताः (have come)
ramayan::7179.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7179.essence: Finding the place is only the beginning; the real act starts now.
ramayan::7179.simple_meaning: Ravana points out Rama's hermitage and urges Maricha to act quickly on their plan.
ramayan::7179.simple_insight: Some moments are only about execution. Once the target is found, hesitation can ruin everything.
ramayan::7179.detailed_meaning: Ravana has reached Dandaka forest with Maricha and now stands before Rama's hermitage. He spots the place, names the mission, and presses Maricha to begin at once. The verse is a setup for the deception that follows.
ramayan::7179.modern_relevance: You finally find the house, the office, the exact place you came for — and now the next move has to be immediate. Planning ends when the moment arrives.
ramayan::7179.insight: It shifts attention from locating the target to carrying out the next step without delay.

ramayan::7180.verse_sanskrit: स रावणवचश्श्रुत्वा मारीचो राक्षसस्तदा । मृगो भूत्वाऽश्रमद्वारि रामस्य विचचार ह । । 34214 । ।
ramayan::7180.verse_hindi: Hearing Ravanas words, Maricha transformed himself into a deer and started moving at the entrance of Ramas hermitage.
ramayan::7180.english_translation: Hearing Ravana's words, the demon Maricha transformed himself into a deer and moved about at the entrance of Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7180.translation_literal: सः (he) / रावणवचः (Ravana's words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / मारीचः (Maricha) / राक्षसः (the demon) / तदा (then) / मृगः (deer) / भूत्वा (having become) / आश्रमद्वारि (at the hermitage gate) / रामस्य (of Rama) / विचचार (moved about) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7180.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7180.essence: A trap begins when beauty is used to hide intent.
ramayan::7180.simple_meaning: Maricha obeys Ravana and takes the form of a deer outside Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7180.simple_insight: A trap can begin with a beautiful disguise.
ramayan::7180.detailed_meaning: Ravana has brought Maricha to the forest and pointed him toward Rama's hermitage. Maricha hears the command, changes shape, and takes his place at the gate as bait. The verse is a step in the setup, not the lesson itself.
ramayan::7180.modern_relevance: Someone smiles, makes the request sound harmless, and suddenly you are helping set a trap you did not design. The danger often arrives dressed as something attractive.
ramayan::7180.insight: It shows how deception often works through obedience and disguise, not force.

ramayan::7181.verse_hindi: Maricha assumed the form of a wonderful and magnificent deer with his antlers studded with the most precious gems, his face dappled with luminous spots of white and  black.
ramayan::7181.english_translation: Maricha assumed the form of a wonderful and magnificent deer with his antlers studded with the most precious gems, his face dappled with luminous spots of white and black.
ramayan::7181.translation_literal: सः (he) / तु (indeed) / तत्-रूपम् (that form) / आस्थाय (having assumed) / महत् (great) / अद्भुत-दर्शनम् (wonderful to behold) / मणि-प्रवर-शृङ्ग-अग्रः (with the foremost tips of the horns studded with jewels) / सित-असित-मुख-आकृतिः (with a face patterned in white and black)
ramayan::7181.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7181.essence: Beauty can be the disguise that makes betrayal work.
ramayan::7181.simple_meaning: Maricha changed himself into a striking deer, with jewel-like antlers and a face marked in white and black.
ramayan::7181.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Rama's hermitage, Ravana's plan is already in motion. Maricha obeys and takes the form of an extraordinary deer, becoming the bait that will draw Rama and Lakshmana away from Sita.
ramayan::7181.modern_relevance: A message, offer, or opportunity can look dazzling on the surface while carrying a trap underneath. The beauty is exactly what makes it dangerous.
ramayan::7181.insight: It shifts attention from the appearance of wonder to the hidden intent behind it.

ramayan::7182.verse_hindi: The deers face was like a pink lotus, his ears were like blue lotus. His neck slightly raised, his lips were like petals of blue lotus.
ramayan::7182.english_translation: The deer’s face was like a pink lotus, his ears like blue lotuses. His neck was slightly raised, and his lips were like blue lotus petals.
ramayan::7182.translation_literal: रक्तपद्मोत्पलमुखः (with a face like red lotus and blue lotus) / इन्द्रनीलोत्पलश्रवाः (with ears like blue lotuses) / किंचित् (slightly) / अभ्युन्नतग्रीवः (raised neck) / इन्द्रनीलदलाधरः (with lips like blue lotus petals)
ramayan::7182.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7182.essence: Beauty here is part of the trap, not proof of safety.
ramayan::7182.simple_meaning: Maricha’s deer form is being described in vivid detail, with lotus-like features and a graceful raised neck.
ramayan::7182.detailed_meaning: Maricha has already taken the dazzling shape of a magical deer outside Rama’s hermitage. This verse lingers on the creature’s beauty, painting its face, ears, neck, and lips so the reader feels how irresistible the illusion is before the trap closes.
ramayan::7182.modern_relevance: A message arrives polished, elegant, and impossible to ignore. The more beautiful the surface looks, the more carefully you need to ask what it is hiding.
ramayan::7182.insight: It trains you to notice when appearance is being used to lure attention away from reality.

ramayan::7183.verse_sanskrit: कुन्देन्दुवज्रसङ्काशमुदरं चास्य भास्वरम् । मधूकनिभपार्श्वश्च पद्मकिञ्जल्कसन्निभः । । 34217 । । वैडूर्यसङ्काशखुरस्तनुजङ्घस्सुसंहतः ।
ramayan::7183.verse_hindi: His bright belly was shining like kunda flowers or the Moon or diamond. His flanks were like the golden madhuka flowers. comparable to the filaments of lotus. His hooves were like vaidurya, and his legs were slim and willshaped.
ramayan::7183.english_translation: His bright belly shone like kunda flowers, the moon, or a diamond. His flanks were like madhuka flowers, his body like lotus filaments, his hooves like vaidurya, and his legs were slender and well-formed.
ramayan::7183.translation_literal: कुन्देन्दुवज्रसङ्काशम् (shining like kunda, moon, and diamond) / उदरम् (belly) / च (and) / अस्य (his) / भास्वरम् (bright, shining) / मधूकनिभपार्श्वः (with flanks like madhuka flowers) / च (and) / पद्मकिञ्जल्कसन्निभः (resembling lotus filaments) / वैडूर्यसङ्काशखुरः (with hooves resembling vaidurya) / तनुजङ्घः (slender-legged) / सुसंहतः (well-formed, compact)
ramayan::7183.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7183.essence: Beauty here is a weapon, built to distract before it deceives.
ramayan::7183.simple_meaning: The deer’s body is described in vivid, jewel-like detail: bright belly, flower-like sides, lotus-like body, and graceful hooves and legs.
ramayan::7183.simple_insight: Sometimes beauty is so intense it feels unreal.
ramayan::7183.detailed_meaning: Maricha has transformed himself into a dazzling golden deer to lure Sita. This verse lingers on the animal’s body, piling image upon image to make the illusion irresistible before the trap closes.
ramayan::7183.modern_relevance: A glossy ad, a perfect profile photo, a polished pitch — everything looks too refined to question. The danger often arrives dressed as beauty.
ramayan::7183.insight: It trains you to notice how appearance can be engineered to disarm judgment.

ramayan::7184.verse_hindi: His tail stood up looking magnificent like a colourful rainbow. Bedecked with various gems, he shone beautiful.
ramayan::7184.english_translation: His tail stood up looking magnificent like a colourful rainbow. Bedecked with various gems, he shone beautiful.
ramayan::7184.translation_literal: इन्द्रायुधसवर्णेन (like a rainbow) / पुच्छेन (with a tail) / ऊर्ध्वं (upward) / विराजता (shining) / मनोहरः (beautiful) / स्निग्धवर्णः (with a smooth lustrous colour) / रत्नैः (with gems) / नानाविधैः (of various kinds) / वृतः (surrounded)
ramayan::7184.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7184.essence: Beauty here is bait, not innocence.
ramayan::7184.simple_meaning: The deer is described as dazzling and jewel-like, with a tail raised high like a rainbow.
ramayan::7184.simple_insight: Beauty can be so vivid it feels almost unreal.
ramayan::7184.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is describing Maricha in the form of a golden deer. The verse lingers on the animal’s beauty—tail, colour, and gemlike brilliance—because that appearance is the lure meant to draw Rama and Sita into danger.
ramayan::7184.modern_relevance: A message arrives with perfect wording, glossy design, and just enough charm to lower your guard. The danger is not loud; it often looks beautiful first.
ramayan::7184.insight: It trains you to notice that appearance can be engineered to mislead.

ramayan::7185.verse_sanskrit: क्षणेन राक्षसो जातो मृगः परमशोभनः । । 34219 । । वनं प्रज्वलयन्रम्यं रामाश्रमपदं च तत् ।
ramayan::7185.verse_hindi: Transformed into a most beautiful deer in a moment, Maricha brightened the beautiful forest and Ramas hermitage.
ramayan::7185.english_translation: In a moment, the demon became a most beautiful deer, lighting up the lovely forest and Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7185.translation_literal: क्षणेन (in a moment) / राक्षसः (the demon) / जातः (became) / मृगः (a deer) / परमशोभनः (most beautiful) / वनं (the forest) / प्रज्वलयन् (lighting up) / रम्यम् (lovely) / रामाश्रमपदम् (Rama's hermitage) / च (and) / तत् (that)
ramayan::7185.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7185.essence: A beautiful form can hide a deadly purpose.
ramayan::7185.simple_meaning: Maricha instantly took the form of a beautiful deer and moved through the forest near Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7185.simple_insight: Some dangers arrive looking beautiful and harmless.
ramayan::7185.detailed_meaning: Maricha, Ravana's ally, changes himself into a dazzling deer beside Rama's forest dwelling. The verse is a visual setup for the trap aimed at Sita, so it serves the larger deception rather than standing alone.
ramayan::7185.modern_relevance: A message arrives looking harmless, almost elegant, and you almost trust it before noticing the hook inside it.
ramayan::7185.insight: It trains you to notice that beauty can be used as bait.

ramayan::7186.verse_sanskrit: मनोहरं दर्शनीयं रूपं कृत्वा स राक्षसः । । 34220 । । प्रलोभनार्थं वैदेह्या नानाधातुविचित्रितम् । विचरन्गच्छते तस्माच्छाद्वलानि समन्ततः । । 34221 । ।
ramayan::7186.verse_hindi: Transfigured into a beautiful, magnificent form painted with the colours of different minerals in order to tempt Sita, Maricha roamed all around the grassland.
ramayan::7186.english_translation: Transfigured into a beautiful, magnificent form painted with the colours of different minerals in order to tempt Sita, Maricha roamed all around the grassland.
ramayan::7186.translation_literal: मनोहरम् (beautiful) / दर्शनीयम् (worth seeing) / रूपम् (form) / कृत्वा (having made) / सः (he) / राक्षसः (the demon) / प्रलोभनार्थम् (for tempting) / वैदेह्याः (of Sita) / नानाधातुविचित्रितम् (adorned with various mineral-colours) / विचरन् (roaming) / गच्छते (goes) / तस्मात् (from there) / छाद्वलानि (the grasslands) / समन्ततः (all around)
ramayan::7186.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7186.essence: Beauty can be the mask that makes danger believable.
ramayan::7186.simple_meaning: Maricha changes into a dazzling deer form to lure Sita, then wanders through the grassland.
ramayan::7186.simple_insight: Deception often begins by looking harmless and beautiful.
ramayan::7186.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Rama's hermitage, Maricha has already taken the form of a striking golden deer to bait Sita. This verse adds the movement: he roams the grassland, keeping the illusion alive and drawing the trap tighter.
ramayan::7186.modern_relevance: A message arrives with a polished photo, perfect wording, and just enough charm to lower your guard. The danger is not loud; it comes dressed to be desired.
ramayan::7186.insight: It shows how temptation works through attractive disguise, not obvious force.

ramayan::7187.verse_sanskrit: रूप्यैर्बिन्दुशतैश्चित्रो भूत्वा स प्रियदर्शनः । विटपीनां किसलयान्भङ्त्क्वाऽदन्विचचार ह । । 34222 । ।
ramayan::7187.verse_hindi: That deer with hundreds of silver spots on the body appeared enchanting and pleasing to the eyes while he wandered about nibbling the tender leaves of trees.
ramayan::7187.english_translation: That deer, marked with hundreds of silver spots, looked enchanting and pleasing to the eye as it wandered about nibbling the tender leaves of trees.
ramayan::7187.translation_literal: रूप्यैः (with silver) / बिन्दुशतैः (with hundreds of spots) / चित्रः (marked, varied) / भूत्वा (having become) / सः (that) / प्रियदर्शनः (pleasing to look at) / विटपीनाम् (of trees) / किसलयान् (tender leaves) / भङ्त्वा (breaking, nibbling) / अदन् (eating) / विचचार (wandered about) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7187.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7187.essence: Beauty can be the mask of a trap.
ramayan::7187.simple_meaning: The deer looks beautiful and harmless while it moves through the trees and eats tender leaves.
ramayan::7187.simple_insight: Appearances can be carefully crafted to hide danger.
ramayan::7187.detailed_meaning: Maricha has taken the form of a dazzling golden deer to lure Sita away from Rama's hermitage. This verse lingers on the animal's beauty and gentle movement, showing how the trap works by seeming harmless and enchanting.
ramayan::7187.modern_relevance: A message arrives with perfect wording, a polished profile, and just enough charm to lower your guard. The danger is not loud; it is attractive.
ramayan::7187.insight: It teaches you to distrust what is merely pleasing to the eye when the stakes are high.

ramayan::7188.verse_hindi: The deer went wandering about the banana groves surrounding Ramas hermitage and moved slowly towards the karnikara trees in order to catch the attention of Sita.
ramayan::7188.english_translation: The deer went wandering about the banana groves surrounding Rama's hermitage and moved slowly towards the karnikara trees in order to catch Sita's attention.
ramayan::7188.translation_literal: कदलीगृहकं (banana grove) / गत्वा (having gone) / कर्णिकारान् (karnikara trees) / इतस्ततः (here and there) / समाश्रयन् (moving toward, taking shelter near) / मन्दगतिः (slow-moving) / सीता-सन्दर्शनं (for Sita's attention/sight) / तथा (thus)
ramayan::7188.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7188.essence: Beauty becomes a snare when it is used to mislead.
ramayan::7188.simple_meaning: The enchanted deer moves slowly through the grove near Rama's hermitage, deliberately drawing Sita's attention.
ramayan::7188.simple_insight: A distraction can be beautiful on purpose.
ramayan::7188.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Rama's hermitage, the golden deer keeps circling through the trees, pretending to wander casually while actually luring Sita's gaze. It is part of Ravana's trap, not a random sighting.
ramayan::7188.modern_relevance: A polished message, a flattering profile, a perfectly timed temptation — it doesn't arrive by accident. Sometimes the thing that catches your eye is designed to.
ramayan::7188.insight: It shows how attraction can be engineered to divert attention from what matters.

ramayan::7189.verse_sanskrit: राजीवचित्रपृष्ठस्स विरराज महामृगः । रामाश्रमपदाभ्याशे विचचार यथासुखम् । । 34224 । ।
ramayan::7189.verse_hindi: That magnificent deer glittered with the colour of blue lotus on its back, wandered merrily in the vicinity of Ramas hermitage.
ramayan::7189.english_translation: That magnificent deer, with a back colored like a blue lotus, shone and wandered freely near Rama's hermitage.
ramayan::7189.translation_literal: राजीव-चित्र-पृष्ठः (with a back colored like a blue lotus) / सः (he) / विरराज (shone) / महा-मृगः (great deer) / राम-आश्रम-पद-आभ्याशे (near Rama's hermitage) / विचचार (wandered about) / यथासुखम् (as he pleased)
ramayan::7189.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7189.essence: Beauty can be the first step of a trap.
ramayan::7189.simple_meaning: A beautiful deer wandered near Rama's hermitage, shining with unusual colours and moving freely.
ramayan::7189.simple_insight: Some temptations arrive as beauty first, not danger.
ramayan::7189.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Rama's hermitage, the magical deer appears in full splendour, moving at ease and drawing the eye. This is not the teaching itself, only the lure that sets the coming deception in motion.
ramayan::7189.modern_relevance: A polished message, a perfect image, a too-good-to-be-true offer — it glides in looking harmless before you notice how much attention it has taken.
ramayan::7189.insight: It sets up the lure that distracts Sita and begins the trap.

ramayan::7190.verse_sanskrit: पुनर्गत्वा निवृत्तश्च विचचार मृगोत्तमः । गत्वा मुहूर्तं त्वरया पुनः प्रतिनिवर्तते । । 34225 । ।
ramayan::7190.verse_hindi: The wonderful deer moved to and fro, now disappearing and now swiftly returning.
ramayan::7190.english_translation: The wonderful deer moved to and fro, now disappearing and now swiftly returning.
ramayan::7190.translation_literal: पुनर्गत्वा (going again) / निवृत्तः (having returned) / च (and) / विचचार (wandered about) / मृगोत्तमः (the best of deer) / गत्वा (having gone) / मुहूर्तं (for a moment) / त्वरया (swiftly) / पुनः (again) / प्रतिनिवर्तते (returns back)
ramayan::7190.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7190.essence: The deer’s restless motion is the bait before the trap.
ramayan::7190.simple_meaning: The deer keeps circling back and forth, vanishing and reappearing near the hermitage.
ramayan::7190.simple_insight: Sometimes a scene is just movement, building tension without saying a word.
ramayan::7190.detailed_meaning: In Rama's forest hermitage, the golden deer keeps slipping away and returning, luring attention by its restless, playful motion. This verse is part of the scene-setting that draws the eye toward the coming deception, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::7190.modern_relevance: A child keeps darting in and out of the room while everyone tries to focus. The motion itself creates the pull, even before anyone knows why.
ramayan::7190.insight: It shows a distracting pattern that keeps pulling attention away from stillness.

ramayan::7191.verse_sanskrit: विक्रीडंश्च क्वचिद्भूमौ पुनरेव निषीदति । आश्रमद्वारमागम्य मृगयूथानि गच्छति । । 34226 । ।
ramayan::7191.verse_hindi: The deer is now sporting, now sitting on the ground, now standing at the entrance of
ramayan::7191.english_translation: The deer is now sporting, now sitting on the ground, now standing at the entrance of the hermitage and moving toward the herds of deer.
ramayan::7191.translation_literal: विक्रीडन् (sporting) / च (and) / क्वचिद् (at some place) / भूमौ (on the ground) / पुनः (again) / एव (indeed) / निषीदति (sits down) / आश्रमद्वारम् (the hermitage entrance) / आगम्य (having come) / मृगयूथानि (toward the herds of deer) / गच्छति (goes)
ramayan::7191.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7191.essence: Restless movement can be the first sign of a trap.
ramayan::7191.simple_meaning: The deer keeps changing its behavior, moving playfully from place to place near the hermitage.
ramayan::7191.simple_insight: Some things are meant to distract you by staying just out of reach.
ramayan::7191.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Rama's hermitage, the golden deer keeps circling, sitting, rising, and wandering toward the other deer. Its strange, playful movement is part of the larger trap being set in motion.
ramayan::7191.modern_relevance: A notification keeps pulling your attention back just as you try to focus. You open it, close it, then check again. The mind can be led around exactly like this deer.
ramayan::7191.insight: It shows how distraction works through movement, novelty, and repeated return.

ramayan::7192.verse_sanskrit: मृगयूथैरनुगतः पुनरेव निवर्तते । सीतादर्शनमाकांक्षन्राक्षसो मृगतां गतः । । 34227 । । परिभ्रमति चित्राणि मण्डलानि विनिष्पतन् ।
ramayan::7192.verse_hindi: Followed by herds of deer and coming back to see Sita again and again, the deer cavorted and pranced and frisked in circles in a wonderful way.
ramayan::7192.english_translation: Followed by herds of deer and coming back to see Sita again and again, the deer cavorted and pranced and frisked in circles in a wonderful way.
ramayan::7192.translation_literal: मृगयूथैः (by herds of deer) / अनुगतः (followed) / पुनः (again) / एव (only) / निवर्तते (turns back) / सीतादर्शनम् (seeing Sita) / आकांक्षन् (desiring) / राक्षसः (the demon) / मृगतां (deerhood) / गतः (gone) / परिभ्रमति (wanders around) / चित्राणि (wonderful) / मण्डलानि (circles) / विनिष्पतन् (leaping out)
ramayan::7192.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7192.essence: The lure works because it keeps returning just when you think it has gone.
ramayan::7192.simple_meaning: The deer keeps circling back toward Sita, as if driven by a hidden lure, moving playfully and strangely through the forest.
ramayan::7192.simple_insight: Not every attraction is innocent; some beauty is a trap in motion.
ramayan::7192.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Rama's hermitage, Maricha has taken the form of a golden deer to draw Sita's attention. He circles, returns, and dances in front of the hut, making the illusion irresistible. The scene is part of Ravana's larger deception.
ramayan::7192.modern_relevance: You keep opening the same profile, the same message, the same temptation, telling yourself it's harmless. The pull feels playful, but it is already steering you.
ramayan::7192.insight: It shows how desire can disguise itself as harmless fascination and keep drawing attention back.

ramayan::7193.verse_sanskrit: समुद्वीक्ष्य च ते सर्वे मृगा ह्यन्ये वनेचराः । । 34228 । । उपागम्य समाघ्राय विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश ।
ramayan::7193.verse_hindi: Seeing the deer, other animals wandering in the forest come near and sniffing him run away in all ten directions.
ramayan::7193.english_translation: Seeing the deer, other animals wandering in the forest come near, sniff him, and then run away in all ten directions.
ramayan::7193.translation_literal: समुद्वीक्ष्य (having seen clearly) / च (and) / ते (those) / सर्वे (all) / मृगाः (deer) / हि (indeed) / अन्ये (other) / वनेचराः (forest-dwellers) / उपागम्य (having approached) / समाघ्राय (having sniffed) / विद्रवन्ति (run away) / दिशः (directions) / दश (ten)
ramayan::7193.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7193.essence: Something unnatural makes even the forest recoil.
ramayan::7193.simple_meaning: Other forest animals come close, smell the deer, and then scatter in every direction.
ramayan::7193.simple_insight: A strange presence changes the whole atmosphere around it.
ramayan::7193.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the deer’s odd behavior has already begun to draw attention. Other animals approach, sniff, sense something is off, and flee. The verse is a small descriptive step in a larger scene, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7193.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone feels the tension before anyone speaks. The mood shifts first; the explanation comes later.
ramayan::7193.insight: It shows how hidden danger or deception can be sensed before it is named.

ramayan::7194.verse_sanskrit: राक्षसस्सोऽपि तान्वन्यान्मृगान्मृगवधे रतः । । 34229 । । प्रच्छादनार्थं भावस्य न भक्षयति संस्पृशन् ।
ramayan::7194.verse_hindi: The demon who was interested in killing wild deer touched and felt them but did not
ramayan::7194.english_translation: The demon, eager to kill wild deer, touched and handled them only to conceal his true intent; he did not eat them.
ramayan::7194.translation_literal: राक्षसः (the demon) / सः (he) / अपि (even) / तान् (those) / वन्यान् (forest-dwelling) / मृगान् (deer) / मृगवधे (in killing deer) / रतः (delighted) / प्रच्छादन-अर्थं (for the sake of concealment) / भावस्य (of intention) / न (not) / भक्षयति (eats) / संस्पृशन् (touching)
ramayan::7194.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7194.essence: A false touch can hide a violent purpose.
ramayan::7194.simple_meaning: He pretended harmless curiosity while hiding violent intent. The touching was only a cover; he was not there to feed or care for the deer.
ramayan::7194.simple_insight: A concealed motive can make even gentle contact unsafe.
ramayan::7194.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Sita, the disguised demon moves among the deer. He handles them as if harmless, but his real purpose is violence. This verse is a small, tense detail in the approach to Sita's meeting with him.
ramayan::7194.modern_relevance: Someone smiles too long at the edge of a conversation, asks personal questions, and seems friendly. Your body notices what your mind wants to excuse: the gesture may be a mask.
ramayan::7194.insight: It trains you to read behavior beneath appearance and notice when contact is being used to hide intent.

ramayan::7195.verse_sanskrit: तस्मिन्नेव ततः काले वैदेही शुभलोचना । । 34230 । । कुसुमावचयव्यग्रा पादपानभ्यवर्तत ।
ramayan::7195.verse_hindi: In the mean time Sita who, with her auspicious looks, was busy plucking flowers drew near the trees.
ramayan::7195.english_translation: In the meantime, Sita, with her beautiful eyes, was busy plucking flowers and moved toward the trees.
ramayan::7195.translation_literal: तस्मिन् (in that) / एव (indeed) / ततः (then) / काले (time) / वैदेही (Sita, daughter of Videha) / शुभलोचना (with auspicious eyes) / कुसुमावचय-व्यग्रा (busy with flower-picking) / पादपान् (to the trees) / अभ्यवर्तत (moved toward)
ramayan::7195.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7195.essence: Sita moves calmly through the forest, absorbed in a simple task.
ramayan::7195.simple_meaning: Sita was moving through the forest, focused on gathering flowers from the trees.
ramayan::7195.simple_insight: Even in a tense setting, ordinary actions continue with quiet grace.
ramayan::7195.detailed_meaning: While the forest scene unfolds around her, Sita turns toward the trees, intent on gathering flowers. The verse is not teaching or arguing; it simply places her in motion, preparing the next moment of the encounter.
ramayan::7195.modern_relevance: You are folding laundry while your mind is elsewhere, or picking up groceries after a hard call. Small tasks still carry you forward even when life feels unsettled.
ramayan::7195.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the quiet dignity of ordinary movement.

ramayan::7196.verse_sanskrit: कर्णिकारानशोकांश्च चूतांश्च मदिरेक्षणा । । 34231 । । कुसुमान्यवचिन्वन्ती चचार रुचिरानना ।
ramayan::7196.verse_hindi: With her bewitching eyes and beautiful face, Sita, went about plucking flowers from karnikara, ashoka and mango trees.
ramayan::7196.english_translation: With her bewitching eyes and beautiful face, Sita went about plucking flowers from karnikara, ashoka, and mango trees.
ramayan::7196.translation_literal: कर्णिकारान् (karnikara trees) / अशोकान् (ashoka trees) / चूतान् (mango trees) / च (and) / मदिरेक्षणा (with intoxicating eyes) / कुसुमानि (flowers) / अवचिन्वन्ती (plucking) / चचार (wandered) / रुचिरानना (with a beautiful face)
ramayan::7196.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7196.essence: Her calm beauty fills the forest before danger arrives.
ramayan::7196.simple_meaning: Sita moves through the forest, gathering flowers from several trees, described with beauty and grace.
ramayan::7196.simple_insight: Even in exile, she carries herself with quiet elegance.
ramayan::7196.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is not idle; she is moving among the trees, plucking flowers while the scene builds toward the appearance of the enchanted deer. The verse mainly paints her presence and beauty, preparing the next turn in the story.
ramayan::7196.modern_relevance: You’re doing something ordinary in a place you never expected to be, and still your presence changes the whole scene.
ramayan::7196.insight: It slows the reader down and frames the forest moment before the temptation appears.

ramayan::7197.verse_sanskrit: अनर्हाऽरण्यवासस्य सा तं रत्नमयं मृगम् । । 34232 । । मुक्तामणि विचित्राङ्गं ददर्श परमाङ्गना ।
ramayan::7197.verse_hindi: The great lady Sita, unworthy of dwelling in the forest, saw the wonderful deer decked with gems, with  spots of pearls all over the body.
ramayan::7197.english_translation: Sita, the noble lady unfit for forest life, saw that marvelous deer, its body patterned with pearls and gems.
ramayan::7197.translation_literal: अनर्हा (unfit) / अरण्यवासस्य (for forest dwelling) / सा (she) / तम् (that) / रत्नमयम् (made of jewels) / मृगम् (deer) / मुक्तामणि (pearls and gems) / विचित्राङ्गम् (variegated-bodied) / ददर्श (saw) / परमाङ्गना (the noble lady)
ramayan::7197.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7197.essence: Beauty can distract you before you know what it costs.
ramayan::7197.simple_meaning: Sita notices a strangely beautiful deer while she is in the forest.
ramayan::7197.simple_insight: A single moment of wonder can open the door to danger.
ramayan::7197.detailed_meaning: Sita is gathering flowers in the forest when a dazzling deer appears before her. Its impossible beauty interrupts the calm of the scene and draws her attention, setting up the lure that will soon change everything.
ramayan::7197.modern_relevance: You spot something dazzling that feels almost too perfect to be real. That first pull of wonder can make you step closer before you notice the trap.
ramayan::7197.insight: It shows how attraction begins with innocent attention before judgment has caught up.

ramayan::7198.verse_sanskrit: सा तं रुचिरदन्तोष्ठी रूप्यधातुतनूरुहम् । । 34233 । । विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयना सस्नेहं समुदैक्षत ।
ramayan::7198.verse_hindi: A lady with beautiful teeth and lips, Sita saw the deer having silver and mineral coloured hair on the body. She gazed at the animal with wonder and joy and love.
ramayan::7198.english_translation: Sita, with beautiful teeth and lips, gazed lovingly and wonderingly at the deer with silver-hued hair.
ramayan::7198.translation_literal: सा (she) / तम् (that) / रुचिरदन्तोष्ठी (with beautiful teeth and lips) / रूप्यधातुतनूरुहम् (with silver-hued body-hair) / विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयना (with wonder-filled, wide-open eyes) / सस्नेहम् (lovingly) / समुदैक्षत (looked at)
ramayan::7198.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7198.essence: Wonder makes her vulnerable to the trap.
ramayan::7198.simple_meaning: Sita looks at the strange deer with wonder, affection, and delight.
ramayan::7198.simple_insight: Curiosity can open the door to danger before you notice it.
ramayan::7198.detailed_meaning: While gathering flowers in the forest, Sita notices a deer unlike any ordinary animal. Its beauty catches her attention completely. This moment matters because her wonder draws her toward the illusion that will soon separate her from safety.
ramayan::7198.modern_relevance: You stop scrolling because something looks too perfect to ignore. That small pull toward beauty can be the first step toward trouble.
ramayan::7198.insight: It shows how fascination can override caution in a single glance.

ramayan::7199.verse_sanskrit: स च तां रामदयितां पश्यन्मायामयो मृगः । । 34234 । । विचचार पुनश्चित्रं दीपयन्निव तद्वनम् ।
ramayan::7199.verse_hindi: That illusory deer saw Ramas wife and moved around wonderfully as if illuminating the forest with his radiance.
ramayan::7199.english_translation: That illusory deer saw Rama's wife and moved around wonderfully, as if illuminating the forest with his radiance.
ramayan::7199.translation_literal: स (that) / च (and) / ताम् (her) / रामदयिताम् (Rama's beloved) / पश्यन् (seeing) / मायामयः (made of illusion) / मृगः (deer) / विचचार (moved about) / पुनः (again) / चित्रम् (wonderfully) / दीपयन् इव (as if illuminating) / तत् (that) / वनम् (forest)
ramayan::7199.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7199.essence: Illusion wins by looking beautiful before it looks dangerous.
ramayan::7199.simple_meaning: The magical deer kept circling Sita, dazzling the forest as it moved.
ramayan::7199.simple_insight: A beautiful distraction can feel like light, even when it leads you away.
ramayan::7199.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has already been drawn toward the strange, gem-like deer. Here the creature notices her and continues its dazzling display, pulling her attention deeper into the illusion. This is a supporting scene in the larger trap around her.
ramayan::7199.modern_relevance: You open one harmless-looking tab, then another, and suddenly your whole evening is gone. Some things do not attack you directly; they simply shine until you follow them.
ramayan::7199.insight: It shows how desire works through attraction first, not force.

ramayan::7200.verse_sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वं तं दृष्ट्वा नानारत्नमयं मृगम् । । 34235 । । विस्मयं परमं सीता जगाम जनकात्मजा ।
ramayan::7200.verse_hindi: Seeing such  an unprecedented deer decorated with different gems, Sita, daughter of Janaka, stood amazed.
ramayan::7200.english_translation: Seeing such an unprecedented deer decorated with different gems, Sita, daughter of Janaka, stood amazed.
ramayan::7200.translation_literal: अदृष्टपूर्वम् (never seen before) / तम् (that) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / नानारत्नमयम् (made of many gems) / मृगम् (deer) / विस्मयम् (wonder) / परमम् (greatest) / सीता (Sita) / जगाम (went into) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka)
ramayan::7200.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7200.essence: Wonder can make you lower your guard.
ramayan::7200.simple_meaning: Sita sees a deer unlike any she has ever seen and is filled with wonder.
ramayan::7200.simple_insight: A beautiful surprise can open the door to danger.
ramayan::7200.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita spots a deer unlike anything she has ever seen, glittering as if made of jewels. The sight overwhelms her with wonder. This moment matters because the enchanted animal is the lure that begins the chain leading to her separation from Rama.
ramayan::7200.modern_relevance: You notice something dazzling on your feed, in a shop window, or in a stranger's promise. The first feeling is wonder. That feeling can also be the opening a trap needs.
ramayan::7200.insight: It teaches you to pause before trusting what only looks extraordinary.

ramayan::7201.verse_sanskrit: सा तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य सुश्रोणी कुसुमान्यपचिन्वती । हेमराजतवर्णाभ्यां पार्श्वाभ्यामुपशोभितम् । । 3431 । । प्रहृष्टा चानवद्याङ्गी मृष्टहाटकवर्णिनी । भर्तारमपि चक्रन्द लक्ष्मणं चापि सायुधम् । । 3432 । ।
ramayan::7201.verse_hindi: Sita while plucking flowers Sita who had fine hips, flawless beautiful limbs and pure golden complexion felt delighted to see the deer with gold and silver colours on both sides of his body. She called out to Rama and Lakshmana who were equipped with arms.
ramayan::7201.english_translation: Sita, while plucking flowers, saw the deer with gold and silver-colored flanks. Delighted, she called Rama and Lakshmana, who were armed.
ramayan::7201.translation_literal: सा (she) / तं (that) / सम्प्रेक्ष्य (having looked closely) / सुश्रोणी (of fine hips) / कुसुमानि (flowers) / अपचिन्वती (plucking) / हेम-राजत-वर्णाभ्याम् (with gold and silver colors) / पार्श्वाभ्याम् (with flanks/sides) / उपशोभितम् (adorned) / प्रहृष्टा (delighted) / च (and) / अनवद्याङ्गी (with flawless limbs) / मृष्ट-हाटक-वर्णिनी (with pure gold complexion) / भर्तारम् (her husband) / अपि (also) / चक्रन्द (called out) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / च (and) / अपि (also) / सायुधम् (armed)
ramayan::7201.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7201.essence: Beauty distracts her just long enough for danger to begin.
ramayan::7201.simple_meaning: Sita sees the strange, beautiful deer while gathering flowers and calls Rama and Lakshmana over to look at it.
ramayan::7201.simple_insight: A moment of wonder can pull attention off guard and set everything in motion.
ramayan::7201.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is gathering flowers when the dazzling deer appears before her. Its beauty catches her completely, and she calls Rama and Lakshmana to come see it. This is a small but crucial turning point before the trap closes.
ramayan::7201.modern_relevance: You spot something dazzling on a walk and stop everything to show someone else. A small distraction can open the door to a much larger mistake.
ramayan::7201.insight: It shows how curiosity and delight can interrupt caution and redirect the whole scene.

ramayan::7202.verse_sanskrit: तयाऽऽहूतौ नरव्याघ्रौ वैदेह्या रामलक्ष्मणौ । वीक्षमाणौ तु तौ देशं तदा ददृशतुर्मृगम् । । 3433 । ।
ramayan::7202.verse_hindi: When Sita called Rama and Lakshmana, the two tigers among men, they looked around and saw the deer.
ramayan::7202.english_translation: When Sita called Rama and Lakshmana, the two tigers among men, they looked around and saw the deer.
ramayan::7202.translation_literal: तया (by her) / आहूतौ (called) / नरव्याघ्रौ (the two tigers among men) / वैदेह्या (by the princess of Videha) / रामलक्ष्मणौ (Rama and Lakshmana) / वीक्षमाणौ (looking around) / तु (indeed) / तौ (they two) / देशम् (the place) / तदा (then) / ददृशतुः (saw) / मृगम् (the deer)
ramayan::7202.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7202.essence: A single look begins the chain that will split the forest scene apart.
ramayan::7202.simple_meaning: Sita called Rama and Lakshmana over, and they turned to look at the strange deer.
ramayan::7202.simple_insight: A small moment of attention can open the door to a much larger loss.
ramayan::7202.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is drawn to the dazzling deer and calls Rama and Lakshmana to look. They turn, see it, and the next step of the tragedy begins. This verse is the quiet hinge before suspicion and separation.
ramayan::7202.modern_relevance: You spot something unusual on a walk and call someone over to see it. That one shared glance can change the whole direction of the day.
ramayan::7202.insight: It shows how curiosity can redirect attention before judgment has time to settle.

ramayan::7203.verse_sanskrit: शङ्कमानस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणो राममब्रवीत् । तमेवैनमहं मन्ये मारीचं राक्षसं मृगम् । । 3434 । ।
ramayan::7203.verse_hindi: Seeing the deer, Lakshmana suspected him to be Maricha and said this to Rama.
ramayan::7203.english_translation: Seeing the deer, Lakshmana suspected him to be Maricha and said this to Rama.
ramayan::7203.translation_literal: शङ्कमानः (suspecting) / तु (but) / तम् (that) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / रामम् (to Rama) / अब्रवीत् (said) / तम् (that one) / एव (indeed) / एनम् (him) / अहम् (I) / मन्ये (think) / मारीचम् (Maricha) / राक्षसम् (demon) / मृगम् (deer)
ramayan::7203.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7203.essence: What looks enchanting may be a trap in disguise.
ramayan::7203.simple_meaning: Lakshmana warns Rama that the beautiful deer may be Maricha in disguise.
ramayan::7203.simple_insight: Not every beautiful thing is safe; caution can save you from a trap.
ramayan::7203.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has just pointed Rama and Lakshmana toward a strange golden deer. Lakshmana watches it closely and remembers Maricha's old tricks. He warns Rama before the chase begins.
ramayan::7203.modern_relevance: You spot the perfect opportunity that feels a little too polished. A quieter part of you says, 'Check again before you chase it.'
ramayan::7203.insight: It trains you to question appearances before acting on excitement.

ramayan::7204.verse_sanskrit: चरन्तोमृगयां हृष्टाः पापेनोपाधिना वने । अनेन निहता राजन् राजानः कामरूपिणा । । 3435 । ।
ramayan::7204.verse_hindi: Many kings, while on hunting expedition in the forest, have been deceitfully killed by malicious Maricha, who could assume any form at his free will.
ramayan::7204.english_translation: Many kings, while hunting in the forest, have been deceitfully killed by malicious Maricha, who could assume any form at will.
ramayan::7204.translation_literal: चरन्तः (roaming) / मृगयाम् (on a hunt) / हृष्टाः (delighted) / पापेन (by the evil one) / उपाधिना (through a deceptive guise) / वने (in the forest) / अनेन (by this one) / निहताः (killed) / राजन् (O king) / राजानः (kings) / कामरूपिणा (by the one who can take any form)
ramayan::7204.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7204.essence: Beauty can be bait when deception knows how to change form.
ramayan::7204.simple_meaning: Lakshmana warns Rama that this deer may be a trap, because Maricha has deceived and killed kings before by changing form.
ramayan::7204.simple_insight: Not every beautiful thing is safe to trust.
ramayan::7204.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama and Lakshmana have stopped to look at the strange deer Sita has noticed. Lakshmana remembers Maricha’s old trick: he has used shifting forms to lure kings into danger. He speaks to warn Rama before the trap closes.
ramayan::7204.modern_relevance: You spot something dazzling in a feed, a deal, a person, a shortcut — and your first impulse is to reach. Then a quieter voice remembers how often charm hides danger.
ramayan::7204.insight: It trains you to pause before trusting what looks attractive, especially when it has a history of deception.

ramayan::7205.verse_sanskrit: अस्य मायाविदो मायामृगरूपमिदं कृतम् । भानुमत्पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्वपुरसन्निभम् । । 3436 । ।
ramayan::7205.verse_hindi: O tiger among men, this deceitful demon (Maricha) has been transformed into the illusory form of a radiant deer which does not exist.
ramayan::7205.english_translation: O tiger among men, this deceitful being has taken the form of an illusory deer, bright as the sun and like a city of the gandharvas.
ramayan::7205.translation_literal: अस्य (of this) / मायाविदः (of the deceitful one) / मायामृगरूपम् (the form of an illusory deer) / इदम् (this) / कृतम् (has been made) / भानुमत् (sun-bright) / पुरुषव्याघ्र (O tiger among men) / गन्धर्वपुरसन्निभम् (resembling the city of the gandharvas)
ramayan::7205.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7205.essence: Beauty can be engineered to hide danger.
ramayan::7205.simple_meaning: Lakshmana warns Rama that the deer is not real. It is a magical disguise, dazzling on purpose to deceive.
ramayan::7205.simple_insight: Not every beautiful thing is safe to trust.
ramayan::7205.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama sees a radiant deer and Lakshmana immediately grows wary. He identifies it as Maricha in disguise, a trick meant to lure them off guard. This verse adds the reason for his suspicion: the beauty itself is part of the deception.
ramayan::7205.modern_relevance: A message arrives with perfect timing, polished language, and exactly the bait you wanted to hear. The shine can be the trap.
ramayan::7205.insight: It trains you to question what dazzles you before you follow it.

ramayan::7206.verse_sanskrit: मृगो ह्येवंविधो रत्नविचित्रो नास्ति राघव । जगत्यां जगतीनाथ मायैषा हि न संशयः । । 3437 । ।
ramayan::7206.verse_hindi: O Rama, lord of the world nowhere on earth does exist this kind of wonderful deer sparkling with gems. That it is a mere trick, an illusion there is no doubt.
ramayan::7206.english_translation: O Rama, lord of the world, nowhere on earth does there exist a deer like this, sparkling with gems. There is no doubt that this is a trick, an illusion.
ramayan::7206.translation_literal: मृगः (deer) / हि (indeed) / एवंविधः (of this kind) / रत्नविचित्रः (adorned with jewels) / न अस्ति (does not exist) / राघव (O Rama) / जगत्याम् (on earth) / जगतीनाथ (lord of the world) / माया (illusion, trick) / एषा (this) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::7206.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7206.essence: What dazzles you most may be the thing meant to mislead you.
ramayan::7206.simple_meaning: This deer is not real. It is a deceptive illusion, and Rama is being warned not to trust what he sees.
ramayan::7206.simple_insight: You do not have to obey every beautiful thing that catches your eye.
ramayan::7206.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha has taken the form of a dazzling deer to lure Rama away. Sita is already captivated, but the warning here is clear: nothing on earth could naturally be this strange. The scene turns on whether Rama trusts appearance or discernment.
ramayan::7206.modern_relevance: You spot a deal online that looks impossibly perfect: flawless specs, unreal price, glowing photos. Something in you knows it is a setup before you can explain why. That first clear seeing can save you.
ramayan::7206.insight: It trains you to question appearances before acting on them.

ramayan::7207.verse_sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं काकुत्स्थं प्रतिवार्य शुचिस्मिता । उवाच सीता संहृष्टा चर्मणा हृतचेतना । । 3438 । ।
ramayan::7207.verse_hindi: Sita was too enchanted by the skin of the deer to retain her sense of discrimination. Intervening, she said to Rama joyfully with a pure smile on her face:
ramayan::7207.english_translation: Sita, with a pure smile and a heart carried away by the deer’s skin, stopped Rama and said this joyfully.
ramayan::7207.translation_literal: एवं (thus) / ब्रुवाणं (speaking) / काकुत्स्थं (to Rama) / प्रतिवार्य (stopping) / शुचिस्मिता (with a pure smile) / उवाच (said) / सीता (Sita) / संहृष्टा (delighted) / चर्मणा (by the skin) / हृतचेतना (with mind carried away)
ramayan::7207.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7207.essence: Beauty can silence judgment before danger is named.
ramayan::7207.simple_meaning: Sita stops Rama and speaks with delight, drawn in by the beauty of the deer’s skin and losing her usual discernment.
ramayan::7207.simple_insight: Charm can pull the mind off course before caution has time to speak.
ramayan::7207.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has already warned Sita that the deer is suspicious. She interrupts him anyway, smiling and captivated by its beauty. This small moment turns the hunt toward tragedy, because enchantment is now stronger than judgment.
ramayan::7207.modern_relevance: You see something beautiful online and want it immediately, even after your better judgment has already whispered no. The wanting arrives faster than discernment.
ramayan::7207.insight: It shows how attraction can override clear seeing before you notice the risk.

ramayan::7208.verse_sanskrit: आर्यपुत्राभिरामोऽसौ मृगो हरति मे मनः । आनयैनं महाबाहो क्रीडार्थं नो भविष्यति । । 3439 । ।
ramayan::7208.verse_hindi: O prince O longarmed one, this deer has captivated my mind. Fetch him for  me.This  will be our playmate.
ramayan::7208.english_translation: O prince, O long-armed one, this deer has captured my mind. Fetch him for me. He will be our playmate.
ramayan::7208.translation_literal: आर्यपुत्र (noble husband/prince) / अभिरामः (delightful) / असौ (this) / मृगः (deer) / हरति (steals/captivates) / मे (my) / मनः (mind) / आनय (bring) / एनम् (him) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / क्रीडार्थम् (for play) / नः (for us) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::7208.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7208.essence: A beautiful distraction can open the door to disaster.
ramayan::7208.simple_meaning: Sita is so enchanted by the golden deer that she asks Rama to bring it to her for play.
ramayan::7208.simple_insight: Desire can make something dangerous feel harmless.
ramayan::7208.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, Sita sees the strange deer and loses her caution. She speaks to Rama with delight, asking him to fetch it as a companion for play. Her request sets the next turning point of the exile.
ramayan::7208.modern_relevance: You spot something charming online and want it immediately, before asking what it will cost you.
ramayan::7208.insight: It shows how fascination can override judgment and pull attention away from what matters most.

ramayan::7209.verse_hindi: Here at the hermitage there are many lovely deer, yaks and antelopes wandering in herds.
ramayan::7209.english_translation: Here in our hermitage, many beautiful deer, yaks, and antelopes roam together.
ramayan::7209.translation_literal: इह (here) / आश्रमपदे (in the hermitage) / अस्माकं (of ours) / बहवः (many) / पुण्यदर्शनाः (beautiful to see) / मृगाः (deer) / चरन्ति (wander) / सहिताः (together) / चमराः (yaks) / सृमराः (antelopes) / तथा (and so on)
ramayan::7209.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7209.essence: Beauty can distract you before you notice it.
ramayan::7209.simple_meaning: Sita points out that the hermitage is full of gentle animals moving together. She is trying to persuade Rama with the beauty of the place.
ramayan::7209.simple_insight: Attraction can begin with beauty, even before reason catches up.
ramayan::7209.detailed_meaning: Sita, already captivated by the golden deer, keeps describing the hermitage as a place alive with beautiful animals. Her words are not a teaching but part of the moment that draws Rama toward the illusion unfolding before him.
ramayan::7209.modern_relevance: You are walking through a quiet park and something beautiful catches your eye before caution does. The first pull is often not logic — it is delight.
ramayan::7209.insight: It shows how beauty can soften judgment and carry the mind toward desire.

ramayan::7210.verse_sanskrit: ऋक्षाः पृषतसङ्घाश्च वानराः किन्नरास्तथा । विचरन्ति महाबाहो रुपश्रेष्ठा मनोहराः । । 34311 । ।
ramayan::7210.verse_hindi: O longarmed one, most beautiful animals like bears, antelopes and groups of monkeys and kinneras are wandering here.
ramayan::7210.english_translation: O long-armed one, beautiful beings like bears, herds of antelopes, monkeys, and kinnaras roam here.
ramayan::7210.translation_literal: ऋक्षाः (bears) / पृषतसङ्घाश्च (and herds of antelopes) / वानराः (monkeys) / किन्नरास्तथा (and kinnaras) / विचरन्ति (wander) / महाबाहो (O long-armed one) / रुपश्रेष्ठा (of excellent form) / मनोहराः (delightful)
ramayan::7210.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7210.essence: Beauty is already all around you; desire just narrows your sight.
ramayan::7210.simple_meaning: Sita is describing the creatures that roam around the hermitage, pointing out its beauty and variety.
ramayan::7210.simple_insight: Even a quiet place can feel alive and wondrous when you truly notice it.
ramayan::7210.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, Sita speaks to Rama while describing the gentle life around them. She lists the animals and celestial beings that move through the woods, building the setting before she points to the rare deer that has caught her attention.
ramayan::7210.modern_relevance: You walk through a park after a hard week and suddenly notice the whole place is alive — birds, dogs, children, trees, movement everywhere.
ramayan::7210.insight: It shifts attention from a single desire to the richness already present around you.

ramayan::7211.verse_sanskrit: न चास्य सदृशो राजन्दृष्टपूर्वो मृगो मया । तेजसा क्षमया दीप्त्या यथाऽयं मृगसत्तमः । । 34312 । ।
ramayan::7211.verse_hindi: O prince  this kind of beautiful, tame and glittering deer I have never seen before.
ramayan::7211.english_translation: O prince, I have never seen a deer like this before, so radiant, gentle, and bright.
ramayan::7211.translation_literal: न च (and not) / अस्य (of this) / सदृशः (equal) / राजन् (O prince) / दृष्टपूर्वः (seen before) / मृगः (deer) / मया (by me) / तेजसा (by radiance) / क्षमया (by gentleness) / दीप्त्या (by brilliance) / यथा (as) / अयम् (this) / मृगसत्तमः (best of deer)
ramayan::7211.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7211.essence: A single deer stands out as too radiant to ignore.
ramayan::7211.simple_meaning: The speaker says this deer is unlike any deer ever seen before, because of its radiance, gentleness, and brilliance.
ramayan::7211.simple_insight: Sometimes beauty feels too unusual to trust.
ramayan::7211.detailed_meaning: In the hermitage forest, the deer and other animals have already been described. Now the speaker pauses over one deer in particular, noticing its unmatched beauty and calm presence. This is a descriptive detail that prepares the scene, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::7211.modern_relevance: You spot something beautiful in a quiet place and instinctively slow down, unsure why it feels different from everything around it.
ramayan::7211.insight: It sharpens attention to unusual beauty before the next event unfolds.

ramayan::7212.verse_hindi: Its body glittering with different colours, speckled with gems of different kinds, is like the Moon shining and illuminating the forest.
ramayan::7212.english_translation: Its body, marked with many colors and dotted with jewel-like spots, shines like the moon and lights up the quiet forest.
ramayan::7212.translation_literal: नानावर्णविचित्राङ्गः (with body of many colors and varied limbs) / रत्नबिन्दुसमाचितः (covered with jewel-like spots) / द्योतयन् (shining, illuminating) / वनम् (the forest) / अव्यग्रम् (quiet, undisturbed) / शोभते (shines, is beautiful) / शशिसन्निभः (moon-like)
ramayan::7212.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7212.essence: Its beauty is so unusual it makes the forest itself seem brighter.
ramayan::7212.simple_meaning: The deer has a dazzling, moonlike body with many colors and jewel-like spots, and it makes the forest look brighter.
ramayan::7212.simple_insight: Some beauty feels unreal at first glance, as if it belongs to another world.
ramayan::7212.detailed_meaning: Sita has spotted a strange deer in the forest and is describing it to Rama. After noting its beauty and rarity, she lingers on its shining body here, as if the sight itself is enough to stop the forest.
ramayan::7212.modern_relevance: You catch sight of something so striking on a quiet walk that you stop mid-step. Before you can name it, the whole scene feels changed.
ramayan::7212.insight: It captures how beauty can interrupt attention and pull the mind outward.

ramayan::7213.verse_sanskrit: अहो रूपमहो लक्ष्मीस्स्वरसम्पच्च शोभना । मृगोऽद्भुतो विचित्राङ्गो हृदयं हरतीव मे । । 34314 । ।
ramayan::7213.verse_hindi: Oh what a beauty, Oh what rich call  what delightful, wonderful, graceful limbs  This deer captivates my heart.
ramayan::7213.english_translation: Oh, what beauty! Oh, what grace and splendour! This wondrous, many-hued deer is stealing my heart.
ramayan::7213.translation_literal: अहो (oh) / रूपम् (beauty) / अहो (oh) / लक्ष्मीः (splendour, grace) / स्वरसम्पद् (rich beauty, lovely form) / च (and) / शोभना (beautiful) / मृगः (deer) / अद्भुतः (wonderful) / विचित्राङ्गः (many-hued-bodied) / हृदयम् (heart) / हरति (steals) / इव (as if) / मे (my)
ramayan::7213.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7213.essence: Beauty can seize the heart before reason has time to answer.
ramayan::7213.simple_meaning: Sita is struck by the deer's extraordinary beauty and feels her heart drawn toward it.
ramayan::7213.simple_insight: Beauty can disarm judgment before you notice it.
ramayan::7213.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita sees the strange golden deer and is captivated by its impossible beauty. Her wonder deepens the trap already forming around Rama, Lakshmana, and her own fate.
ramayan::7213.modern_relevance: You spot something glittering online and want it before thinking. The pull is real, and that first rush can hide the cost.
ramayan::7213.insight: It shows how charm can override caution and lead desire to speak before discernment.

ramayan::7214.verse_sanskrit: यदि ग्रहणमभ्येति जीवन्नेव मृगस्तव । आश्चर्यभूतं भवति विस्मयं जनयिष्यति । । 34315 । ।
ramayan::7214.verse_hindi: If this deer can be caught  alive, it will be thrilling, it will work wonders.
ramayan::7214.english_translation: If this deer can be caught alive, it will be thrilling, it will work wonders.
ramayan::7214.translation_literal: यदि (if) / ग्रहणम् (catching) / अभ्येति (reaches, comes to) / जीवन् एव (alive only) / मृगः (deer) / तव (your) / आश्चर्य-भूतम् (a wonder) / भवति (becomes) / विस्मयम् (astonishment) / जनयिष्यति (will produce)
ramayan::7214.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7214.essence: Beauty can become a trap when desire starts naming it a prize.
ramayan::7214.simple_meaning: Rama is admiring the deer and imagining how remarkable it would be to capture it alive.
ramayan::7214.simple_insight: Curiosity can make something dangerous feel like a prize.
ramayan::7214.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama sees a deer of extraordinary beauty and begins to desire it as a living wonder. This is not a teaching verse; it is part of the moment that draws attention away from caution and toward the bait that will soon separate him from Sita.
ramayan::7214.modern_relevance: You spot something dazzling and start imagining how special it would look if you could keep it. That excitement can make you miss the trap hidden inside the shine.
ramayan::7214.insight: It shows how fascination can override caution and pull attention toward the wrong thing.

ramayan::7215.verse_sanskrit: समाप्तवनवासानां राज्यस्थानां च नः पुनः । अन्तःपुरविभूषार्थो मृग एष भविष्यति । । 34316 । ।
ramayan::7215.verse_hindi: After the completion  of exile in the forest, when we are back in the kingdom, this deer will add beauty to the harem.
ramayan::7215.english_translation: After the forest exile ends and we return to the kingdom, this deer will adorn the inner quarters.
ramayan::7215.translation_literal: समाप्तवनवासानां (for those whose forest exile has ended) / राज्यस्थानां (for those placed in the kingdom) / च (and) / नः (for us) / पुनः (again) / अन्तःपुरविभूषार्थो (for the adornment of the inner quarters) / मृगः (deer) / एषः (this) / भविष्यति (will become)
ramayan::7215.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7215.essence: He turns temptation into a future excuse.
ramayan::7215.simple_meaning: Ravana imagines the deer as a future ornament for the royal women after exile ends and everyone returns home.
ramayan::7215.simple_insight: Desire can dress itself up as harmless pleasure and make danger look like a gift.
ramayan::7215.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana is already captivated by the golden deer. He keeps justifying the chase by imagining it as a gift for the women of the palace once exile is over. The verse shows how attraction starts building its own excuses.
ramayan::7215.modern_relevance: You tell yourself a risky choice is harmless because you can explain it later. That is how temptation gets permission before you notice the cost.
ramayan::7215.insight: It exposes the mind's habit of rationalizing desire by borrowing a future benefit.

ramayan::7216.verse_sanskrit: भरतस्यार्यपुत्रस्य श्वश्रूणां मम च प्रभो । मृगरूपमिदं व्यक्तं विस्मयं जनयिष्यति । । 34317 । ।
ramayan::7216.verse_hindi: O king this deer will create amazement in Bharata, in mothersinlaw, in you and in me as well.
ramayan::7216.english_translation: O king, this deer will create amazement in Bharata, in my mothers-in-law, in you, and in me as well.
ramayan::7216.translation_literal: भरतस्य (of Bharata) / आर्यपुत्रस्य (of the noble son) / श्वश्रूणां (of the mothers-in-law) / मम (of me) / च (and) / प्रभो (O lord) / मृगरूपम् (deer-shaped) / इदम् (this) / व्यक्तम् (clearly) / विस्मयम् (amazement) / जनयिष्यति (will produce)
ramayan::7216.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7216.essence: What looks delightful can become the bait that changes everything.
ramayan::7216.simple_meaning: The deer is so remarkable that it will amaze Bharata, the queens, Rama, and Sita alike.
ramayan::7216.simple_insight: A beautiful distraction can pull everyone in, even when it is not important.
ramayan::7216.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita sees the golden deer and imagines the delight it would bring back in Ayodhya. She speaks to Rama and Lakshmana with playful certainty, treating the deer as a marvel worth catching, not yet knowing it will draw them toward disaster.
ramayan::7216.modern_relevance: You spot something shiny and start imagining how it will impress everyone else. That little thrill can hide the cost of chasing it.
ramayan::7216.insight: It shows how charm can override caution and turn attention away from what matters.

ramayan::7217.verse_sanskrit: जीवन्न यदि तेऽभ्येति ग्रहणं मृगसत्तमः । अजिनं नरशार्दूल रुचिरं मे भविष्यति । । 34318 । ।
ramayan::7217.verse_hindi: O best among men, if this great deer cannot be captured alive, I will wear its beautiful skin.
ramayan::7217.english_translation: O best among men, if this great deer cannot be captured alive, I will wear its beautiful skin.
ramayan::7217.translation_literal: जीवन् (alive) / यदि (if) / ते (by you) / अभ्येति (is brought) / ग्रहणं (capture) / मृगसत्तमः (best of deer) / अजिनं (skin) / नरशार्दूल (best among men) / रुचिरं (beautiful) / मे (for me) / भविष्यति (will become)
ramayan::7217.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7217.essence: Wanting does not stop when the object becomes damaged.
ramayan::7217.simple_meaning: Ravana says that if the deer cannot be taken alive, its skin will still be useful to him.
ramayan::7217.simple_insight: A desire can stay fixed even when the object slips away.
ramayan::7217.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana is speaking about the golden deer that has caught everyone's attention. He is still focused on possessing it, even if only as a skin. The line is a small step in the larger trap that draws Rama and Lakshmana away from Sita.
ramayan::7217.modern_relevance: You want something so badly that even a ruined version of it still feels worth taking. The craving itself has already narrowed your judgment.
ramayan::7217.insight: It shows how desire keeps bargaining even after reality has changed.

ramayan::7218.verse_hindi: If this animal is killed and its golden skin is spread on a tender grass cushion, there will I like to sit.
ramayan::7218.english_translation: If this animal is killed and its golden skin is spread on a tender grass cushion, there I would like to sit.
ramayan::7218.translation_literal: निहतस्य (of the killed) / अस्य (of this) / सत्त्वस्य (creature) / जाम्बूनदमयत्वचि (on a skin like gold) / शष्पबृस्याम् (on a cushion of tender grass) / विनीतायाम् (spread, made ready) / इच्छामि (I wish) / अहम् (I) / उपासितुम् (to sit, to rest)
ramayan::7218.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7218.essence: A beautiful wish can open the door to disaster.
ramayan::7218.simple_meaning: Sita says she wants the deer's golden skin laid on soft grass so she can sit on it.
ramayan::7218.simple_insight: A small desire can reveal a whole mood of longing and delight.
ramayan::7218.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita sees a magnificent golden deer and speaks with delight about its skin. She imagines it killed, spread on soft grass, and used as a seat. The moment is part of the lure that draws Rama away from the cottage.
ramayan::7218.modern_relevance: You spot something beautiful in a shop window and want it instantly, before you’ve asked what it will cost.
ramayan::7218.insight: It shows how desire can fixate on appearance and ignore consequence.

ramayan::7219.verse_sanskrit: कामवृत्तमिदं रौद्रं स्त्रीणामसदृशं मतम् । वपुषा त्वस्य सत्त्वस्य विस्मयो जनितो मम । । 34320 । ।
ramayan::7219.verse_hindi: This kind of request arising out of a womans desire may sound terrible, still then the beauty of this animals skin has produced in me a wonder.
ramayan::7219.english_translation: This kind of request arising out of a woman's desire may sound terrible, yet the beauty of this animal's skin has produced wonder in me.
ramayan::7219.translation_literal: कामवृत्तम् (arising from desire) / इदम् (this) / रौद्रम् (terrible) / स्त्रीणाम् (of women) / असदृशम् (unfitting) / मतम् (considered) / वपुषा (by form/beauty) / तु (yet) / अस्य (of this) / सत्त्वस्य (creature) / विस्मयः (wonder) / जनितः (produced) / मम (in me)
ramayan::7219.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7219.essence: Wonder can weaken judgment before danger is obvious.
ramayan::7219.simple_meaning: The speaker says the request seems harsh and unseemly, but the deer's beauty has filled him with wonder.
ramayan::7219.simple_insight: Beauty can soften judgment, even when the mind knows better.
ramayan::7219.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the golden deer has already caught everyone's attention. The speaker admits that the request feels fierce and improper, yet the animal's extraordinary beauty has stirred awe. It is a small but crucial moment of enchantment before the larger deception unfolds.
ramayan::7219.modern_relevance: You scroll past something beautiful and feel yourself leaning in, even though a small voice says, be careful. That split between caution and wonder is where mistakes begin.
ramayan::7219.insight: It shows how fascination can override clear judgment before you notice it happening.

ramayan::7220.verse_sanskrit: तेन काञ्चनवर्णेन मणिप्रवरशृङ्गिणा । तरुणादित्यवर्णेन नक्षत्रपथवर्चसा । । 34321 । । बभूव राघवस्यापि मनो विस्मयमागतम् ।
ramayan::7220.verse_hindi: By his golden colour resembling the rising Sun, by  his horns with excellent gems shining like the milkyway, even Ramas mind was wonderstruck.
ramayan::7220.english_translation: By his golden colour resembling the rising Sun, by his horns with excellent gems shining like the Milky Way, even Rama's mind was wonderstruck.
ramayan::7220.translation_literal: तेन (by that) / काञ्चनवर्णेन (with golden colour) / मणिप्रवरशृङ्गिणा (with horns of excellent gems) / तरुणादित्यवर्णेन (with the colour of the rising sun) / नक्षत्रपथवर्चसा (with the splendour of the path of stars) / बभूव (became) / राघवस्य (of Rama) / अपि (also) / मनः (mind) / विस्मयम् (wonder) / आगतम् (came)
ramayan::7220.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7220.essence: Even a disciplined mind can be startled by beauty.
ramayan::7220.simple_meaning: Even Rama was amazed by the deer’s golden beauty and jewel-like horns.
ramayan::7220.simple_insight: Beauty can stop even a steady mind for a moment.
ramayan::7220.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has just urged Rama to look at the wondrous deer. Its golden body and shining horns are so unusual that even Rama pauses in surprise. This is the moment before desire begins to cloud judgment.
ramayan::7220.modern_relevance: You spot something so polished, rare, and irresistible that your careful mind slips for a second. That tiny pause can be the start of a costly mistake.
ramayan::7220.insight: It shows how dazzling appearance can interrupt clear judgment before you notice it.

ramayan::7221.verse_sanskrit: एवं सीतावचः श्रुत्वा तं दृष्ट्वा मृगमद्भुतम् । । 34322 । । लोभितस्तेन रूपेण सीतया च प्रचोदितः । उवाच राघवो हृष्टो भ्रातरं लक्ष्मणं वचः । । 34323 । ।
ramayan::7221.verse_hindi: On hearing Sitas words and seeing the wonderful deer, Rama was tempted by its appearance.Prompted by Sita,he joyfully said this to Lakshmana:
ramayan::7221.english_translation: On hearing Sita's words and seeing the wonderful deer, Rama was tempted by its appearance. Prompted by Sita, he joyfully said this to Lakshmana.
ramayan::7221.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / सीतावचः (Sita's words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तम् (that) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / मृगम् (deer) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful) / लोभितः (enticed) / तेन (by that) / रूपेण (by appearance) / सीतया (by Sita) / च (and) / प्रचोदितः (urged) / उवाच (said) / राघवः (Raghava) / हृष्टः (delighted) / भ्रातरम् (to the brother) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / वचः (words)
ramayan::7221.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7221.essence: A beautiful distraction can open the door to ruin.
ramayan::7221.simple_meaning: Rama sees the beautiful deer, feels drawn to it, and speaks happily to Lakshmana after Sita encourages him.
ramayan::7221.simple_insight: Desire can begin with a small, beautiful distraction.
ramayan::7221.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita notices the dazzling deer and Rama is captivated by it. He turns to Lakshmana with delight, not yet seeing the trap forming around them. This is the moment attraction starts to pull the story off course.
