ramayan::7221.modern_relevance: You spot the perfect-looking option and feel the pull before you’ve thought it through. The charm is real; so is the risk.
ramayan::7221.insight: It shows how attraction can override caution before the consequences are visible.

ramayan::7222.verse_sanskrit: पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्याः स्पृहां मृगगतामिमाम् । रूपश्रेष्ठतया ह्येष मृगोऽद्य न भविष्यति । । 34324 । । न वने नन्दनोद्धेशे न चैत्ररथसंश्रये । कुतःपृथिव्यां सौमित्रे योऽस्य कश्चित्समो मृगः । । 34325 । ।
ramayan::7222.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, see the eagerness of Sita. Such a deer of exceptional beauty will not be found in this forest. There is no equal to this animal even in the Nandan garden of Indra, or the Chaitraratha, the garden of Kubera. Where can such an animal be found on earth?
ramayan::7222.english_translation: O Lakshmana, see Sita's eagerness for this deer. Such a deer of exceptional beauty will not be found in this forest. There is no equal to this animal even in Indra's Nandana garden or Kubera's Chaitraratha. Where on earth could such a deer be found?
ramayan::7222.translation_literal: पश्य (see) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / वैदेह्याः (of Sita) / स्पृहाम् (desire, eagerness) / मृगगताम् (directed toward the deer) / इमाम् (this) / रूपश्रेष्ठतया (by supreme beauty) / हि (indeed) / एषः (this) / मृगः (deer) / अद्य (today) / न (not) / भविष्यति (will be) / न (not) / वने (in the forest) / नन्दनोद्धेशे (in Nandana garden) / न (not) / चैत्ररथसंश्रये (in Chaitraratha) / कुतः (how, where) / पृथिव्याम् (on earth) / सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra, Lakshmana) / यः (who) / अस्य (of this) / कश्चित् (any) / समः (equal) / मृगः (deer)
ramayan::7222.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7222.essence: A beautiful object can awaken desire before reason catches up.
ramayan::7222.simple_meaning: Rama points out to Lakshmana how intensely Sita wants the beautiful deer. He says no forest, not even heavenly gardens, has an animal like this one.
ramayan::7222.simple_insight: Beauty can pull attention so strongly that judgment slips for a moment.
ramayan::7222.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is captivated by the golden deer, and Rama notices her longing. He tells Lakshmana that its beauty is unmatched even by the famed gardens of the gods. The moment matters because desire is already bending the course of the exile.
ramayan::7222.modern_relevance: You see something dazzling online and suddenly want it badly. Before you know it, the wanting itself is steering your choices.
ramayan::7222.insight: It shows how fascination begins before action, and how desire can quietly redirect attention.

ramayan::7223.verse_sanskrit: प्रतिलोमानुलोमाश्च रुचिरा रोमराजयः । शोभन्ते मृगमाश्रित्य चित्राः कनकबिन्दवः । । 34326 । ।
ramayan::7223.verse_hindi: The stretches of hair on the deers body bent both in the natural order and in the opposite direction look beautiful. The spots of gold on the skin are wonderful.
ramayan::7223.english_translation: The stretches of hair on the deer’s body, flowing both with and against the grain, look beautiful. The golden spots on its skin are lovely.
ramayan::7223.translation_literal: प्रतिलोम (against the grain) / अनुलोम (with the grain) / च (and) / रुचिराः (beautiful) / रोमराजयः (lines of hair) / शोभन्ते (shine) / मृगम् (the deer) / आश्रित्य (taking as support) / चित्राः (variegated) / कनकबिन्दवः (golden spots)
ramayan::7223.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7223.essence: Beauty can blind you when desire has already taken hold.
ramayan::7223.simple_meaning: Rama is admiring the deer’s markings and hair, describing them as beautiful and striking.
ramayan::7223.simple_insight: Desire can make even a dangerous distraction look enchanting.
ramayan::7223.detailed_meaning: Rama, already drawn in by the golden deer, keeps praising its beauty to Lakshmana. He notices the markings, the hair, and the strange charm of the animal. The verse deepens the spell that will pull him away from Sita and toward Ravana’s trap.
ramayan::7223.modern_relevance: You keep zooming in on the one detail that makes the temptation look harmless. The mind can turn a warning into a fascination.
ramayan::7223.insight: It shows how attraction narrows judgment and makes the alluring object feel worthy of pursuit.

ramayan::7224.verse_sanskrit: पश्यास्य जृम्भमाणस्य दीप्तामग्निशिखोपमाम् । जिह्वां मुखान्निस्सरन्तीं मेघादिव शतह्रदाम् । । 34327 । ।
ramayan::7224.verse_hindi: Look at his tongue stretched out of the mouth while yawning. It is glowing like flaming fire. It is like the lightning sparkling in the cloud.
ramayan::7224.english_translation: Look at his tongue stretched out of the mouth while yawning. It is glowing like flaming fire. It is like lightning sparkling in a cloud.
ramayan::7224.translation_literal: पश्य (look) / अस्य (of this) / जृम्भमाणस्य (of the yawning) / दीप्ताम् (glowing) / अग्निशिखोपमाम् (like a flame) / जिह्वाम् (tongue) / मुखात् (from the mouth) / निस्सरन्तीम् (coming out) / मेघात् इव (like from a cloud) / शतह्रदाम् (lightning)
ramayan::7224.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7224.essence: A beautiful object can seize the mind before reason notices.
ramayan::7224.simple_meaning: The speaker is describing the deer’s yawning tongue as bright and lightning-like, adding to its striking beauty.
ramayan::7224.simple_insight: Beauty can be so vivid it pulls attention before thought catches up.
ramayan::7224.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is captivated by a golden deer and points out its every dazzling feature to Lakshmana. This verse is part of that close, enchanted gaze, where the animal’s yawn is turned into another detail of irresistible beauty.
ramayan::7224.modern_relevance: You stop scrolling because a passing image is strangely perfect, and your attention lingers longer than you meant it to.
ramayan::7224.insight: It shows how desire can dress itself as innocent admiration and quietly take hold.

ramayan::7225.verse_sanskrit: मसारगल्लर्कमुखश्शङ्खमुक्तानिभोदरः । कस्य नामाभिरूप्योऽसौ न मनो लोभयेन्मृगः । । 34328 । ।
ramayan::7225.verse_hindi: His face is a drinking pot of emerald, the belly is a conch or a pearl. Whose mind will not be attracted by this indescribable beauty ?
ramayan::7225.english_translation: His face is like a vessel of emerald; his belly is like a conch or a pearl. Whose mind would not be drawn to such unmatched beauty?
ramayan::7225.translation_literal: मसारगल्लर्कमुखः (emerald-vessel-faced) / शङ्खमुक्तानिभोदरः (conch-pearl-like-bellied) / कस्य (whose) / नाम (indeed) / अभिरूप्यः (beautiful) / असौ (that) / न (not) / मनः (mind) / लोभयेत् (would entice) / मृगः (deer)
ramayan::7225.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7225.essence: Beauty can enchant the mind before it asks permission.
ramayan::7225.simple_meaning: The deer is so strikingly beautiful that anyone would be drawn to it.
ramayan::7225.simple_insight: Some things pull attention so strongly that they bypass reason.
ramayan::7225.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the golden deer appears before Sita and the others, dazzling with impossible beauty. The poet lingers on its features to show why it is so tempting. This is part of the lure that will soon lead to disaster.
ramayan::7225.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and ten minutes later you're still scrolling. Some attractions are designed to catch you before you can think.
ramayan::7225.insight: It shows how beauty can become a trap when desire moves faster than discernment.

ramayan::7226.verse_sanskrit: कस्य रूपमिदं दृष्ट्वा जाम्बूनद मयप्रभम् । नानारत्नमयं दिव्यं न मनो विस्मयं व्रजेत् । । 34329 । ।
ramayan::7226.verse_hindi: Whose mind will not be filled with wonder on seeing this divine beauty glittering like lustrous gold and studded with a variety of gems ?
ramayan::7226.english_translation: Whose mind will not be filled with wonder on seeing this divine beauty glittering like lustrous gold and studded with a variety of gems?
ramayan::7226.translation_literal: कस्य (whose) / रूपम् (form, beauty) / इदम् (this) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / जाम्बूनद-मय-प्रभम् (gold-like lustre) / नाना-रत्न-मयम् (made of many gems) / दिव्यम् (divine, splendid) / न (not) / मनः (mind) / विस्मयम् (wonder) / व्रजेत् (would go, would attain)
ramayan::7226.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7226.essence: Beauty this intense leaves the mind speechless.
ramayan::7226.simple_meaning: Anyone would be amazed by this radiant, gem-like form. Its beauty is so striking that the mind naturally falls into wonder.
ramayan::7226.simple_insight: Some things overwhelm ordinary judgement and leave only awe.
ramayan::7226.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshmana is describing a being whose body seems made of gold and jewels. The surrounding verses build a vivid image piece by piece, and this line completes the praise by asking who could possibly remain unmoved.
ramayan::7226.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone so striking that your mind stops arguing and simply stares. Beauty can silence analysis before it even begins.
ramayan::7226.insight: It shifts attention from naming features to recognising the force of astonishment itself.

ramayan::7227.verse_sanskrit: मांसहेतोरपि मृगान्विनोदार्थं च धन्वनः । घ्नन्ति लक्ष्मण राजानो मृगयायां महावने । । 34330 । ।
ramayan::7227.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana kings who wield  bows  in hunting expeditions kill deer in the forest for
ramayan::7227.english_translation: O Lakshmana, kings who wield bows kill deer in great forests during hunting, for food and for sport.
ramayan::7227.translation_literal: मांसहेतोरपि (even for meat) / मृगान् (deer) / विनोदार्थं (for amusement) / च (and) / धन्वनः (of bowmen) / घ्नन्ति (they kill) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / राजानः (kings) / मृगयायां (in hunting) / महावने (in the great forest)
ramayan::7227.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7227.essence: Forest life includes both beauty and human appetite.
ramayan::7227.simple_meaning: Kings hunt deer in the forest both for food and for sport.
ramayan::7227.simple_insight: A royal hunt is being described plainly, without moral judgment.
ramayan::7227.detailed_meaning: The sage is describing the beauty and abundance of the great forest to Lakshmana. He notes that kings also enter such forests to hunt deer, sometimes for meat and sometimes for sport, as part of ordinary royal life.
ramayan::7227.modern_relevance: A guide points out deer tracks on a trail, and someone mentions how people once came here to hunt. The verse is simply naming a common practice in a forested world.
ramayan::7227.insight: It keeps the passage grounded in the real uses people made of the forest.

ramayan::7228.verse_sanskrit: धनानि व्यवसायेन विचीयन्ते महावने । धातवो विविधाश्चापि मणिरत्नसुवर्णिनः । । 34331 । ।
ramayan::7228.verse_hindi: From huge forests a variety of mineral wealth consisting of gems, stones and gold are collected with great effort.
ramayan::7228.english_translation: From huge forests, a variety of mineral wealth consisting of gems, stones, and gold are collected with great effort.
ramayan::7228.translation_literal: धनानि (wealths) / व्यवसायेन (with effort, by enterprise) / विचीयन्ते (are gathered, are sought out) / महावने (in the great forest) / धातवः (minerals, ores) / विविधाः (various) / च (and) / अपि (also) / मणि-रत्न-सुवर्णिनः (containing gems, jewels, and gold)
ramayan::7228.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7228.essence: Hidden wealth is real, but only effort brings it to light.
ramayan::7228.simple_meaning: Treasure can be extracted from the forest, but only through hard effort and search.
ramayan::7228.simple_insight: Even hidden wealth yields only to persistence and work.
ramayan::7228.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is being shown that a great forest is not empty or useless. It holds wealth in hidden forms, but only those who search carefully and work hard can bring it out. The point supports a larger argument about the value of the wilderness.
ramayan::7228.modern_relevance: You can walk past an overlooked place and see nothing, or keep digging until value appears. The difference is effort, not luck.
ramayan::7228.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to the labor needed to uncover value.

ramayan::7229.verse_sanskrit: तत्सारमखिलं नृ़णां धनं निचयवर्धनम् । मनसा चिन्तितं सर्वं यथा शुक्रस्य लक्ष्मण । । 34332 । ।
ramayan::7229.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana the essence of forest wealth is mineral wealth, which helps the growth of the treasury. It is conceived mentally as in the case of Venus.
ramayan::7229.english_translation: O Lakshmana, the essence of all wealth for people is the wealth that grows a treasury. It is imagined in the mind, as with Venus.
ramayan::7229.translation_literal: तत्सारम् (that essence) / अखिलम् (all) / नृणाम् (of people) / धनम् (wealth) / निचयवर्धनम् (increasing the treasury) / मनसा (by the mind) / चिन्तितम् (conceived) / सर्वम् (all) / यथा (as) / शुक्रस्य (of Venus) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana)
ramayan::7229.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7229.essence: Wealth matters here because it can keep growing.
ramayan::7229.simple_meaning: The main value of wealth is its ability to increase more wealth. The mind imagines and plans this kind of gain.
ramayan::7229.simple_insight: It reminds you to think beyond possession and notice what can create lasting abundance.
ramayan::7229.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is being told how kings think about forest resources: not as scenery, but as value that can be turned into treasury strength. The point is not beauty, but the logic of accumulation.
ramayan::7229.modern_relevance: You look at a half-empty plot of land, a stalled business, or a skill you have not used yet, and ask what it could become. The mind starts pricing possibility before anyone else sees it.
ramayan::7229.insight: It shifts attention from raw assets to their capacity to generate future gain.

ramayan::7230.verse_sanskrit: अर्थी येनार्थकृत्येन संव्रजत्यविचारयन् । तमर्थमर्थशास्त्रज्ञाः प्राहुरर्थ्याश्च लक्ष्मण । । 34333 । ।
ramayan::7230.verse_hindi: A materialist moves about thoughtlessly for making money. Economists call it material wealth.
ramayan::7230.english_translation: A person who seeks wealth moves about thoughtlessly for the sake of gain. Experts in economics call that material wealth, Lakshmana.
ramayan::7230.translation_literal: अर्थी (one seeking wealth) / येन (by which) / अर्थकृत्येन (for the work of gain) / संव्रजति (moves about) / अविचारयन् (without thinking) / तम् (that) / अर्थम् (wealth) / अर्थशास्त्रज्ञाः (experts in economics) / प्राहुः (call) / अर्थ्याः (those seeking wealth) / च (and) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7230.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7230.essence: Blind pursuit of gain can masquerade as success.
ramayan::7230.simple_meaning: People often run after money without thinking clearly. That kind of restless chasing is only called wealth by convention.
ramayan::7230.simple_insight: You can spend your life pursuing something and still never know why.
ramayan::7230.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshmana hears a hard truth about human desire: people chase money blindly and call it success. The verse strips wealth down to restless pursuit, warning that accumulation can become a kind of confusion.
ramayan::7230.modern_relevance: You refresh your bank app three times before bed, hoping the number will quiet you. The verse points out how easily money-seeking becomes mindless motion instead of a real life.
ramayan::7230.insight: It shifts attention from accumulation to intention, asking whether your pursuit is actually serving your life.

ramayan::7231.verse_sanskrit: एतस्य मृगरत्नस्य परार्ध्ये काञ्चनत्वचि । उपवेक्ष्यति वैदेही मया सह सुमध्यमा । । 34334 । ।
ramayan::7231.verse_hindi: एतस्य मृगरत्नस्य परार्ध्ये काञ्चनत्वचि । उपवेक्ष्यति वैदेही मया सह सुमध्यमा । । 34334 । ।
ramayan::7231.english_translation: On this incomparable golden-skinned deer, the slender Vaidehi will recline with me.
ramayan::7231.translation_literal: एतस्य (of this) / मृगरत्नस्य (of the jewel among deer) / परार्ध्ये (on the priceless) / काञ्चनत्वचि (golden-skinned) / उपवेक्ष्यति (will recline) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / मया सह (with me) / सुमध्यमा (the slender-waisted one)
ramayan::7231.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7231.essence: Craving makes a beautiful object into a promise of possession.
ramayan::7231.simple_meaning: Ravana imagines Sita resting beside him on the skin of a rare golden deer, showing his desire and the lure of the illusion before him.
ramayan::7231.simple_insight: Desire can make a fantasy feel more real than reality.
ramayan::7231.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana is already speaking as if Sita were his. He admires the golden deer not for its beauty alone, but for the pleasure he imagines it will bring. The line reveals the mind that turns wonder into possession.
ramayan::7231.modern_relevance: You start wanting an object, a status, or a person so badly that your mind builds a whole scene around it. The fantasy begins to feel like fact.
ramayan::7231.insight: It exposes how craving turns imagination into possession before anything is truly gained.

ramayan::7232.verse_sanskrit: न कादली न प्रियकी न प्रवेणी न चाविकी । भवेदेतस्य सदृशी स्पर्शनेनेति मे मतिः । । 34335 । ।
ramayan::7232.verse_hindi: The skins of various types of deer like Priyaki, Kadali or goats or sheep cannot be compared in softness to the skin of this deer.
ramayan::7232.english_translation: The skins of deer like Kadali, Priyaki, Praveni, or sheep cannot match the softness of this one, in my view.
ramayan::7232.translation_literal: न (not) / कादली (of Kadali) / न (not) / प्रियकी (of Priyaki) / न (not) / प्रवेणी (of Praveni) / न (not) / च (and) / आविकी (of sheep/goats) / भवेत् (would be) / एतस्य (of this) / सदृशी (equal) / स्पर्शनेन (in softness/touch) / इति (thus) / मे (my) / मतिः (opinion)
ramayan::7232.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7232.essence: Craving makes one object seem unmatched.
ramayan::7232.simple_meaning: Ravana judges that no ordinary deer skin is as soft as this extraordinary golden deer.
ramayan::7232.simple_insight: A single desire can make something ordinary feel priceless.
ramayan::7232.detailed_meaning: Ravana is describing the magical deer he wants for Sita. He compares its skin to other kinds of deer and finds none equal in softness. The verse is a small step in his larger plan to lure Sita away.
ramayan::7232.modern_relevance: You spot a rare thing and start justifying why you need it. The mind can dress up craving as comparison, then call it reason.
ramayan::7232.insight: It shows how desire narrows judgment and turns fascination into pursuit.

ramayan::7233.verse_sanskrit: एष चैव मृगश्श्रीमान् यश्च दिव्यो नभश्चरः । उभावेतौ मृगौ दिव्यौ तारामृगमहीमृगौ । । 34336 । ।
ramayan::7233.verse_hindi: This majestic deer and the deer flying in heaven (the deers figure seen in the Moon called Mrgasira)  both the deer of the star in the sky and the deer of the earth are divine.
ramayan::7233.english_translation: This majestic deer and the deer that moves in the sky are both wondrous. The deer among the stars and the deer on earth are alike divine.
ramayan::7233.translation_literal: एष (this) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / मृगः (deer) / श्रीमान् (splendid) / यः (which) / च (and) / दिव्यः (heavenly) / नभश्चरः (moving in the sky) / उभौ (both) / एतौ (these two) / मृगौ (deer) / दिव्यौ (divine) / तारा-मृग-महीमृगौ (the star-deer and the earth-deer)
ramayan::7233.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7233.essence: Beauty can be real and still lead you into a trap.
ramayan::7233.simple_meaning: Rama is marveling at the beauty of the golden deer and linking it to the celestial deer he imagines in the sky.
ramayan::7233.simple_insight: Wonder can make danger look beautiful before it reveals itself.
ramayan::7233.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama sees Maricha's shimmering golden form and is captivated by its impossible beauty. He compares it to the heavenly deer of the stars, not yet seeing the trap hidden inside the wonder. This moment deepens the lure that will pull him away from Sita.
ramayan::7233.modern_relevance: You spot something dazzling online, in a shop window, or in a stranger's life and want it instantly. Beauty can be real and still be bait.
ramayan::7233.insight: It teaches you to notice when admiration is blinding discernment.

ramayan::7234.verse_sanskrit: यदि वाऽयं तथा यन्मां भवेद्वदसि लक्ष्मण । मायैषा राक्षसस्येति कर्तव्योस्य वधो मया । । 34337 । ।
ramayan::7234.verse_hindi: Lakshmana, as you say, if it is the illusion of a demon, even then it should be killed by me.
ramayan::7234.english_translation: Lakshmana, as you say, if it is the illusion of a demon, even then it should be killed by me.
ramayan::7234.translation_literal: यदि (if) / वा (or) / अयम् (this) / तथा (so) / यत् (that) / माम् (me) / भवेत् (may be) / वदसि (you say) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / माया (illusion) / एषा (this) / राक्षसस्य (of the demon) / इति (thus) / कर्तव्यः (to be done) / अस्य (of this) / वधः (killing) / मया (by me)
ramayan::7234.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7234.essence: Even uncertainty cannot excuse you from acting when danger may be real.
ramayan::7234.simple_meaning: Rama says that even if the deer is only an illusion, he still must kill it himself. He treats the threat as his responsibility.
ramayan::7234.simple_insight: You do not wait for perfect certainty when something dangerous is in front of you.
ramayan::7234.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshmana warns Rama that the golden deer may be a trick. Rama does not retreat into hesitation. If the threat is real or only an illusion, he says the burden of dealing with it is still his.
ramayan::7234.modern_relevance: You notice a strange message, a fake account, or a scam that might be harmless — or might not. You do not freeze in analysis. You act on the responsibility in front of you.
ramayan::7234.insight: It shifts you from debating appearances to taking direct responsibility for a possible threat.

ramayan::7235.verse_sanskrit: एतेन हि नृशंसेन मारीचेनाकृतात्मना । वने विचरता पूर्वं हिंसिता मुनिपुङ्गवाः । । 34338 । ।
ramayan::7235.verse_hindi: The great sages were tortured and killed earlier by this cruel, evilminded Maricha while wandering in the forest.
ramayan::7235.english_translation: The great sages were tortured and killed earlier by this cruel, evil-minded Maricha while wandering in the forest.
ramayan::7235.translation_literal: एतेन (by this) / हि (indeed) / नृशंसेन (by the cruel one) / मारीचेन (by Maricha) / अकृतात्मना (by the one without self-control) / वने (in the forest) / विचरता (wandering) / पूर्वं (earlier) / हिंसिताः (were harmed) / मुनिपुङ्गवाः (great sages)
ramayan::7235.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7235.essence: A familiar danger deserves no innocence just because it has changed shape.
ramayan::7235.simple_meaning: Rama points to Maricha as a known threat: this same cruel being has already harmed and killed great sages in the forest.
ramayan::7235.simple_insight: Past violence is enough reason to treat a threat seriously.
ramayan::7235.detailed_meaning: Rama is tracking the deer with Lakshmana beside him, trying to decide whether it is real or a trick. He recalls Maricha's earlier crimes against forest sages, using that memory to justify his suspicion and the need to destroy the danger.
ramayan::7235.modern_relevance: You ignore a warning sign because the person looks harmless now. But your mind remembers the pattern: this is not the first time they have hurt someone.
ramayan::7235.insight: It shifts judgment from appearance to known pattern of harm.

ramayan::7236.verse_sanskrit: उत्थाय बहवो येन मृगयायां जनाधिपाः । निहताः परमेष्वासास्तस्माद्वध्यस्त्वयं मृगः । । 34339 । ।
ramayan::7236.verse_hindi: Many kings who were great archers who set out on hunting expedition were killed by him. Therefore, this animal deserves to be killed.
ramayan::7236.english_translation: Many kings who were great archers, while out on hunting expeditions, were killed by him. Therefore, this deer should be killed.
ramayan::7236.translation_literal: उत्थाय (having risen) / बहवः (many) / येन (by whom) / मृगयायाम् (in hunting) / जनाधिपाः (kings) / निहताः (were killed) / परमेष्वासाः (great archers) / तस्मात् (therefore) / वध्यः (to be killed) / तु (indeed) / अयम् (this) / मृगः (deer)
ramayan::7236.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7236.essence: Past violence makes present trust impossible.
ramayan::7236.simple_meaning: Lakshmana argues that the deer must be killed because it has already killed many kings and skilled archers during hunts.
ramayan::7236.simple_insight: A threat is judged by its history, not its appearance.
ramayan::7236.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama and Lakshmana are reacting to the strange golden deer that has drawn their attention away from Sita. Lakshmana reminds Rama that this creature has already killed powerful hunters, so it cannot be treated as harmless.
ramayan::7236.modern_relevance: A problem looks harmless in the chat window, but you remember the damage it caused last time. Experience makes caution feel less like fear and more like wisdom.
ramayan::7236.insight: It shifts judgment from surface appearance to proven pattern.

ramayan::7237.verse_sanskrit: पुरस्तादिह वातापिः परिभूय तपस्विनः । उदरस्थो द्विजान्हन्तिस्वगर्भोऽश्वतरीमिव । । 34340 । ।
ramayan::7237.verse_hindi: Earlier in this forest, Vatapi used to humiliate the ascetic brahmins and to kill them by entering into their stomach like a womb killing the female mule.
ramayan::7237.english_translation: Earlier in this forest, Vatapi used to humiliate the ascetic brahmins and kill them by entering their stomachs, like a female mule destroys her own womb.
ramayan::7237.translation_literal: पुरस्तात् (earlier) / इह (here, in this place) / वातापिः (Vatapi) / परिभूय (having humiliated) / तपस्विनः (ascetics) / उदरस्थः (being inside the belly) / द्विजान् (brahmins) / हन्ति (kills) / स्वगर्भः (one's own womb) / अश्वतरीम् इव (like a female mule)
ramayan::7237.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7237.essence: Hidden cruelty is more terrifying than open attack.
ramayan::7237.simple_meaning: Vatapi had already been terrorizing ascetic brahmins in this forest by entering their bodies and killing them from within.
ramayan::7237.simple_insight: Some harms are hidden, intimate, and deadly — they destroy from the inside before anyone can react.
ramayan::7237.detailed_meaning: The sages are explaining why this creature must be destroyed. They recall Vatapi's old cruelty in the forest: he humiliated holy men and killed them from within their own bodies. The verse is a grim supporting detail in the case against him.
ramayan::7237.modern_relevance: A smile in the meeting, then a private message that tears someone apart. Some damage is not loud; it works from inside trust, safety, and belonging.
ramayan::7237.insight: It sharpens the warning against concealed harm and shows why the sages see no innocence in the creature.

ramayan::7238.verse_sanskrit: स कदाचिच्चिराल्लोभादाससाद महामुनिम् । अगस्त्यं तेजसा युक्तं भक्षस्तस्य बभूव ह । । 34341 । ।
ramayan::7238.verse_hindi: That Vatapi after a long time, once greedily entered into the stomach of the great lustrous sage Agastya and became his food.
ramayan::7238.english_translation: After a long time, Vatapi greedily entered the great sage Agastya, radiant with power, and became his food.
ramayan::7238.translation_literal: सः (he) / कदाचित् (once) / चिरात् (after a long time) / लोभात् (out of greed) / आससाद (approached/entered) / महामुनिम् (the great sage) / अगस्त्यम् (Agastya) / तेजसा (with radiance/power) / युक्तम् (endowed) / भक्षः (food) / तस्य (his) / बभूव (became) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7238.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7238.essence: Greed entered the wrong body and never came back out.
ramayan::7238.simple_meaning: Vatapi, driven by greed, entered Agastya and became his meal.
ramayan::7238.simple_insight: Greed can walk straight into its own end.
ramayan::7238.detailed_meaning: The forest tale of Vatapi and Ilvala is reaching its trap. After earlier boasting and killing ascetics, Vatapi finally enters Agastya himself. The moment matters because the trick that once fed on others is now undone by the sage's power.
ramayan::7238.modern_relevance: A scam keeps working until it meets someone who sees through it completely. What looked like clever appetite turns into its own undoing.
ramayan::7238.insight: It shows how greed and predation can collapse under a stronger, clearer presence.

ramayan::7239.verse_sanskrit: समुत्थाने व तद्रूपं कर्तुकामं समीक्ष्य तम् । उत्स्मयित्वा तु भगवान्वातापिमिदमब्रवीत् । । 34342 । ।
ramayan::7239.verse_hindi: When the venerable sage Agastya got up (after eating), he observed Vatapi wishing to turn into his real form. So smiling at him, he said:
ramayan::7239.english_translation: When the venerable sage Agastya got up after eating, he saw Vatapi trying to regain his original form. Smiling, Agastya then spoke to him.
ramayan::7239.translation_literal: समुत्थाने (on rising up) / व (and) / तद्रूपं (that form, original form) / कर्तुकामं (wishing to do) / समीक्ष्य (having observed) / तम् (him) / उत्स्मयित्वा (having smiled) / तु (but) / भगवान् (the venerable one) / वातापिम् (to Vatapi) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (said)
ramayan::7239.speaker: Agastya
ramayan::7239.essence: Clear seeing ends the trick before it can begin again.
ramayan::7239.simple_meaning: Agastya notices Vatapi trying to return to his original form after being eaten, and he smiles before speaking to him.
ramayan::7239.simple_insight: Some victories are quiet: you see the threat clearly, and it no longer controls the moment.
ramayan::7239.detailed_meaning: After the feast, Agastya rises and notices that Vatapi is trying to re-form inside the story's deadly trick. This verse is the calm pause before Agastya delivers the blow of truth in the next line.
ramayan::7239.modern_relevance: You catch someone trying to slip back into the same old pattern just after they think they've escaped it. You don't rush. You see clearly first.
ramayan::7239.insight: It trains you to notice a manipulative pattern before responding to it.

ramayan::7240.verse_sanskrit: त्वयाऽविगण्य वातापे परिभूतास्स्वतेजसा । जीवलोके द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तस्मादसि जरां गतः । । 34343 । ।
ramayan::7240.verse_hindi: O Vatapi you killed the best of brahmins living in this world, disregarding them because of your power. Hence you were digested by me.
ramayan::7240.english_translation: O Vatapi, you killed the best of brahmins living in this world, disregarding them because of your power. Hence you were digested by me.
ramayan::7240.translation_literal: त्वया (by you) / अविगण्य (disregarding) / वातापे (O Vatapi) / परिभूताः (oppressed) / स्वतेजसा (by your own power) / जीवलोके (in the world of the living) / द्विजश्रेष्ठाः (best of brahmins) / तस्मात् (therefore) / असि (you are) / जरां गतः (gone to digestion, digested)
ramayan::7240.speaker: Agastya
ramayan::7240.simple_meaning: Agastya tells Vatapi that he abused his power against holy men, so he was consumed and destroyed.
ramayan::7240.simple_insight: Power that humiliates others eventually turns back and ruins itself.
ramayan::7240.detailed_meaning: After Vatapi tries to return to his original form, Agastya smiles and speaks with calm finality. He names Vatapi's cruelty toward brahmins and explains that the same arrogance that harmed others has now brought about his destruction.
ramayan::7240.modern_relevance: Someone weaponizes status in a meeting, humiliating people who cannot answer back. Later, that same arrogance becomes the reason trust disappears and the room closes around them.
ramayan::7240.insight: It warns that cruelty powered by arrogance plants the seed of self-destruction.

ramayan::7241.verse_sanskrit: तदेवं न भवेद्रक्षोवातापिरिव लक्ष्मण । मद्विधं योऽतिमन्येत धर्मनित्यं जितेन्द्रियम् । । 34344 । । भवेद्धतोऽयं वातापिरगस्त्येनेव मां गतः ।
ramayan::7241.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana just like Vatapi, this demon will not live. Whoever violates a person of my kind who is ever righteous and selfcontrolled will be killed
ramayan::7241.english_translation: O Lakshmana, just like Vatapi, this demon will not live. Whoever insults a person like me, who is ever righteous and self-controlled, will be slain. This Vatapi will meet the same end that met him before at Agastya's hands.
ramayan::7241.translation_literal: तदेवं (thus) / न (not) / भवेत् (will be) / रक्षः (demon) / वातापिः (Vatapi) / इव (like) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / मद्विधम् (one like me) / यः (who) / अतिमन्येत (would insult / disregard) / धर्मनित्यम् (ever-righteous) / जितेन्द्रियम् (self-controlled) / भवेत् (will be) / हतः (killed) / अयम् (this) / वातापिः (Vatapi) / अगस्त्येन (by Agastya) / इव (like) / माम् (me) / गतः (met his end)
ramayan::7241.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7241.essence: Contempt for discipline brings your own downfall.
ramayan::7241.simple_meaning: A self-controlled, righteous person is not someone to dismiss lightly. Treating such a person with contempt brings ruin on the one who does it.
ramayan::7241.simple_insight: There is safety in humility and danger in arrogance.
ramayan::7241.detailed_meaning: Agastya has just destroyed Vatapi, and the warning now turns to Lakshmana. The speaker says that anyone who looks down on a disciplined, righteous person meets the same fate. The lesson is about the cost of contempt.
ramayan::7241.modern_relevance: You roll your eyes at the calm person in the room, the one who never performs but always holds the line. Later, you realize you mistook restraint for weakness.
ramayan::7241.insight: It shifts attention from outward force to the power of self-mastery.

ramayan::7242.verse_sanskrit: इह त्वं भव सन्नद्दो यन्त्रितो रक्ष मैथिलीम् । । 34345 । । अस्यामायत्तमस्माकं यत्कृत्यं रघुनन्दन ।
ramayan::7242.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, delight of the Raghu dynasty, be very alert and restrained and protect Sita. Whatever duty we have to perform depends on her protection.
ramayan::7242.english_translation: O Lakshmana, delight of the Raghu dynasty, be very alert and restrained and protect Sita. Whatever duty we have to perform depends on her protection.
ramayan::7242.translation_literal: इह (here) / त्वं (you) / भव (become) / सन्नद्दः (fully armed, prepared) / यन्त्रितः (restrained, controlled) / रक्ष (protect) / मैथिलीम् (Sita of Mithila) / अस्याम् (in her) / आयत्तम् (dependent) / अस्माकम् (our) / यत् (whatever) / कृत्यम् (task, duty) / रघुनन्दन (delight of the Raghu dynasty)
ramayan::7242.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7242.essence: Your next duty depends on guarding what cannot guard itself.
ramayan::7242.simple_meaning: Lakshmana is told to stay ready, stay controlled, and guard Sita, because their next action depends on her safety.
ramayan::7242.simple_insight: Real responsibility begins with protecting what everything else depends on.
ramayan::7242.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama prepares to leave Lakshmana behind with Sita. The moment is fragile: one lapse could cost everything. He orders Lakshmana to stand armed, restrained, and vigilant, because the whole mission now hangs on Sita's protection.
ramayan::7242.modern_relevance: You leave your child with a neighbour for ten minutes and still keep checking your phone. Some responsibilities are not abstract; they rest on one person's steady care.
ramayan::7242.insight: It shifts duty from broad intention to immediate protection of the vulnerable.

ramayan::7243.verse_sanskrit: अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ग्रहीष्याम्यपि वा मृगम् । । 34346 । । यावद्गच्छामि सौमित्रे मृगमानयितुं द्रुतम् ।
ramayan::7243.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana I will go quickly and either kill the deer or catch it.  Now let me go.
ramayan::7243.english_translation: O Lakshmana, I will quickly go and either kill this deer or catch it. Let me go at once to bring the deer back.
ramayan::7243.translation_literal: अहम् (I) / एनम् (this) / वधिष्यामि (will kill) / ग्रहीष्यामि (will catch) / अपि (or even) / वा (or) / मृगम् (deer) / यावत् (until) / गच्छामि (I go) / सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra, Lakshmana) / मृगम् (deer) / आनयितुम् (to bring) / द्रुतम् (quickly)
ramayan::7243.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7243.essence: A brief chase becomes the turning point that breaks protection.
ramayan::7243.simple_meaning: Rama says he will quickly go after the deer, either to kill it or bring it back alive.
ramayan::7243.simple_insight: A small desire can redirect an entire day when it slips past caution.
ramayan::7243.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has been drawn to the golden deer and Lakshmana is guarding the hermitage. Rama decides to chase it himself, speaking as if it is a simple errand. That choice opens the door to the tragedy that follows.
ramayan::7243.modern_relevance: You spot something shiny and harmless-looking, and suddenly your whole attention tilts toward it. One quick impulse can pull you away from what was actually important.
ramayan::7243.insight: It shows how desire can disguise itself as a harmless task and quietly derail duty.

ramayan::7244.verse_sanskrit: पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेहीं मृगत्वचि गतस्पृहाम् । । 34347 । । त्वचा प्रधानया ह्येष मृगोऽद्य न भविष्यति ।
ramayan::7244.verse_hindi: See, how Vaidehi ardently longs for the skin of this deer  I will not let the animal live, O Lakshmana
ramayan::7244.english_translation: See, how Vaidehi ardently longs for the skin of this deer. I will not let the animal live, O Lakshmana.
ramayan::7244.translation_literal: पश्य (see) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / वैदेहीं (Vaidehi) / मृगत्वचि (for the deer-skin) / गतस्पृहाम् (having desire gone toward) / त्वचा (with skin) / प्रधानया (as the main thing) / हि (indeed) / एषः (this) / मृगः (deer) / अद्य (today) / न (not) / भविष्यति (will be) /
ramayan::7244.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7244.essence: A passing desire becomes the excuse for a fatal chase.
ramayan::7244.simple_meaning: Rama points out Sita’s wish for the deer skin and says he will kill the deer now.
ramayan::7244.simple_insight: A small desire becomes the spark that sends the whole scene toward disaster.
ramayan::7244.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has just reassured Lakshmana and gone after the golden deer. Looking back at Sita, he notices her interest in the animal’s skin and uses that as the reason to press on. The moment is a hinge in the abduction plot.
ramayan::7244.modern_relevance: You spot something beautiful in a market window and say, just for a moment, that you want it. That tiny wanting can change the whole direction of the day.
ramayan::7244.insight: It shows how desire can be read as permission, even when the cost is hidden.

ramayan::7245.verse_sanskrit: अप्रमत्तेन ते भाव्यमाश्रमस्थेन सीतया । । 34348 । । यावत्पृषतमेकेन सायकेन निहन्म्यहम् । हत्वैतच्चर्म चादाय शीघ्रमेष्यामि लक्ष्मण । । 34349 । ।
ramayan::7245.verse_hindi: Keep vigil over Sita at the hermitage, O Lakshmana  I will certainly kill the speckled antelope with a single arrow, get his skin and come back quickly.
ramayan::7245.english_translation: Keep vigil over Sita at the hermitage, O Lakshmana. I will certainly kill the speckled antelope with a single arrow, get his skin, and come back quickly.
ramayan::7245.translation_literal: अप्रमत्तेन (with vigilance) / ते (for you) / भाव्यम् (it should be) / आश्रमस्थेन (while staying at the hermitage) / सीतया (with Sita) / यावत् (until) / पृषतम् (the speckled one) / एकेन (with one) / सायकेन (with an arrow) / निहन्मि (I kill) / अहम् (I) / हत्वा (having killed) / एतत् (this) / चर्म (skin) / च आदाय (and having taken) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / एष्यामि (I will come) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana)
ramayan::7245.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7245.essence: One careless errand can demand a second pair of watchful eyes.
ramayan::7245.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana to protect Sita carefully while he goes to kill the deer, take its skin, and return quickly.
ramayan::7245.simple_insight: Real responsibility means doing one thing well while someone else guards what you cannot.
ramayan::7245.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is distracted by the golden deer and asks Lakshmana to stay vigilant with Sita at the hermitage. He sets out to kill the animal and bring back its skin, a small errand that will soon open the door to disaster.
ramayan::7245.modern_relevance: You leave your phone on the table and step outside for two minutes, asking someone to watch the child. A tiny lapse, a harmless errand, and everything depends on whether vigilance holds.
ramayan::7245.insight: It teaches you to separate the immediate task from the duty of protection, and to treat vigilance as part of action.

ramayan::7246.verse_sanskrit: प्रदक्षिणेनातिबलेन पक्षिणा जटायुषा बुद्धिमता च लक्ष्मण । भवाप्रमत्तः परिगृह्य मैथिलीं प्रतिक्षणं सर्वत एव शङ्कितः । । 34350 । ।
ramayan::7246.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, be vigilant in guarding Sita, suspecting danger every moment from all directions. Take the help of Jatayu, the mighty and wise bird who will be on his rounds.
ramayan::7246.english_translation: O Lakshmana, be vigilant in guarding Sita, suspecting danger every moment from all directions. Take the help of Jatayu, the mighty and wise bird who will be on his rounds.
ramayan::7246.translation_literal: प्रदक्षिणेन (from all directions) / अतिबलेन (very powerful) / पक्षिणा (by the bird) / जटायुषा (by Jatayu) / बुद्धिमता (wise) / च (and) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana) / भव (be) / अप्रमत्तः (vigilant) / परिगृह्य (guarding) / मैथिलीं (Maithili, Sita) / प्रतिक्षणं (every moment) / सर्वतः (from everywhere) / एव (indeed) / शङ्कितः (suspicious, wary)
ramayan::7246.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7246.essence: What you love most demands your sharpest attention.
ramayan::7246.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana to guard Sita carefully and stay alert for danger from every direction.
ramayan::7246.simple_insight: Love is not only feeling; it is watchfulness, especially when someone precious is exposed to harm.
ramayan::7246.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has just sent Lakshmana to protect Sita while he hunts the deer. This is not casual caution. He knows the slightest lapse can open the door to disaster, so he orders constant vigilance.
ramayan::7246.modern_relevance: You leave a child with a trusted relative and still glance at your phone every few minutes. Care does not relax just because the setting looks safe.
ramayan::7246.insight: It teaches you to protect what matters with active attention, not assumed safety.

ramayan::7247.verse_sanskrit: तथा तु तं समादिश्य भ्रातरं रघुनन्दनः । बबन्धासिं महातेजा जाम्बूनदमयत्सरुम् । । 3441 । ।
ramayan::7247.verse_hindi: The brilliant Rama, delight of the Raghu dynasty, thus instructed his brother and fastened a sword with a golden handle to his waist.
ramayan::7247.english_translation: The brilliant Rama, delight of the Raghu dynasty, thus instructed his brother and fastened a sword with a golden handle to his waist.
ramayan::7247.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / तु (indeed) / तम् (that) / समादिश्य (having instructed) / भ्रातरम् (brother) / रघुनन्दनः (the delight of the Raghu line) / बबन्ध (fastened) / असिम् (sword) / महातेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / जाम्बूनदमयत्सरुम् (with a golden-hilted scabbard)
ramayan::7247.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7247.simple_meaning: Rama gives Lakshmana instructions and then straps on his sword, ready to act.
ramayan::7247.simple_insight: Preparation matters when the moment has already arrived.
ramayan::7247.detailed_meaning: Rama has already told Lakshmana to guard Sita carefully. Now, in the same charged moment, he arms himself with a golden-hilted sword. The verse is a small but vivid bridge from instruction to action.
ramayan::7247.modern_relevance: You finish the warning, check the lock, and reach for the keys. The conversation is over; now the responsibility turns physical.
ramayan::7247.insight: It shows the shift from speaking about danger to meeting it directly.

ramayan::7248.verse_sanskrit: तत स्त्र्यवनतं चापमादायाऽत्मविभूषणम् । आबध्य च कलापौ द्वौ जगामोदग्रविक्रमः । । 3442 । ।
ramayan::7248.verse_hindi: A man of indomitable prowess, he took the bow with three curves that was like an ornament to him, tied two quivers at the back and left.
ramayan::7248.english_translation: A man of indomitable prowess, he took the bow with three curves that was like an ornament to him, tied two quivers at the back and left.
ramayan::7248.translation_literal: तत् (then) / स्त्र्यवनतम् (three-bent) / चापम् (bow) / आदाय (taking) / आत्मविभूषणम् (his own ornament) / आबध्य (tying on) / च (and) / कलापौ (two quivers) / द्वौ (two) / जगाम (went) / उदग्रविक्रमः (with exalted prowess)
ramayan::7248.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7248.essence: He arms himself and goes, already carrying the coming danger.
ramayan::7248.simple_meaning: Rama takes up his bow, straps on two quivers, and sets out with calm confidence.
ramayan::7248.simple_insight: Readiness can be quiet. The right action begins before the crisis fully arrives.
ramayan::7248.detailed_meaning: Rama has just ordered Lakshmana to guard Sita and taken up his sword. Now he shoulders his bow and quivers and leaves the hut, already moving toward the forest that will test everything. The verse is a visual bridge, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::7248.modern_relevance: You grab your bag, check your phone, and step out the door knowing the day may turn rough. Before the hard moment arrives, you are already preparing to meet it.
ramayan::7248.insight: It shifts attention from anxiety to readiness: gather your tools, then move.

ramayan::7249.verse_sanskrit: तं वञ्चयानो राजेन्द्रमापतन्तं निरीक्ष्यवै । बभूवान्तर्हितस्त्रासात्पुनस्सन्दर्शनेऽभवत् । । च3443 । । बद्धासिर्धनुरादाय प्रदुद्राव यतो मृगः ।
ramayan::7249.verse_hindi: On seeing Rama approaching him, the deer disappeared due to fear and again came within sight. With his sword and the bow, Rama chased wherever the deer ran.
ramayan::7249.english_translation: On seeing Rama approaching him, the deer disappeared from fear and appeared again. With sword and bow in hand, Rama chased wherever the deer ran.
ramayan::7249.translation_literal: तं (him) / वञ्चयानः (deceiving) / राजेन्द्रम् (the lord of kings) / आपतन्तम् (approaching) / निरीक्ष्य वै (indeed seeing) / बभूव (became) / अन्तर्हितः (hidden) / त्रासात् (from fear) / पुनः (again) / सन्दर्शने (in sight) / अभवत् (became) / बद्धासिः (with sword fastened) / धनुः आदाय (taking the bow) / प्रदुद्राव (ran after) / यतः (wherever) / मृगः (the deer)
ramayan::7249.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7249.essence: A glittering distraction pulls you forward by staying just out of reach.
ramayan::7249.simple_meaning: The deer keeps slipping out of sight and appearing again, drawing Rama deeper into the chase. This is the moment the hunt turns into a trap.
ramayan::7249.simple_insight: Not every pursuit is what it first appears to be.
ramayan::7249.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama sees the golden deer vanish in fear and reappear at a distance. He arms himself and follows it through the woods. The verse is a moving step in the larger deception that will pull him away from Sita.
ramayan::7249.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing a message thread because the other person stays just out of reach. The chase feels urgent, but the thing pulling you forward may be leading you away from what matters.
ramayan::7249.insight: It shows how desire and distraction can turn attention into pursuit before judgment catches up.

ramayan::7250.verse_sanskrit: तं स्म पश्यति रूपेण द्योतमानमिवाग्रतः । । 3444 । । अवेक्ष्यावेक्ष्य धावन्तं धनुष्पाणिर्महावने । अतिवृत्तमिषोः पाताल्लोभयानं कदाचन । । 3445 । । शङ्कितन्तु समुद्भ्रान्तमुत्पतन्तमिवाम्बरे । दृश्यमानमदृश्यं च वनोद्देशेषु केषुचित् । । 3446 । । छिन्नाभ्रैरिव संवीतं शारदं चन्द्रमण्डलम् ।
ramayan::7250.verse_hindi: Rama, wielder of the bow, saw that splendid animal ahead of him. Holding the bow he saw the deer running away, bewldered into the great forest looking at him again and again. The deer was getting out of the range of his arrow, while it enticed him now and then. Suspecting that he might be caught,  the deer was, as though jumping into the sky. Now it came within sight and now out of sight in the huge forest. It looked like the autumnal moon surrounded by clouds. (The clouds muffle the Moon and reveal him now and then).
ramayan::7250.english_translation: Rama, wielder of the bow, saw the splendid deer ahead of him. The deer ran through the great forest, looking back again and again, slipping beyond the range of the arrow, then seeming to leap into the sky. It appeared and vanished among the trees, like the autumn moon hidden by clouds.
ramayan::7250.translation_literal: तं (that one) / स्म (indeed) / पश्यति (sees) / रूपेण (by form) / द्योतमानम् (shining) / इव (like) / अग्रतः (ahead) / अवेक्ष्यावेक्ष्य (looking again and again) / धावन्तम् (running) / धनुष्पाणिः (bow in hand) / महावने (in the great forest) / अतिवृत्तम् (gone beyond) / इषोः (of the arrow) / पातात् (from the fall) / लोभयानम् (enticing) / कदाचन (sometimes) / शङ्कितम् (suspicious) / तु (but) / समुद्भ्रान्तम् (confused) / उत्पतन्तम् (leaping up) / इव (as if) / अम्बरे (in the sky) / दृश्यमानम् (visible) / अदृश्यमानम् (invisible) / च (and) / वनोद्देशेषु (in forest tracts) / केषुचित् (in some) / छिन्नाभ्रैः (by broken clouds) / इव (like) / संवीतम् (covered) / शारदम् (autumnal) / चन्द्रमण्डलम् (moon-disc)
ramayan::7250.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7250.essence: What dazzles you most may be leading you away from what matters.
ramayan::7250.simple_meaning: Rama keeps seeing the deer as it darts in and out of view, always just beyond reach. The animal’s strange, teasing movement makes the chase feel uncertain and deceptive.
ramayan::7250.simple_insight: Not everything that appears before you is meant to be trusted.
ramayan::7250.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama follows a dazzling deer that keeps slipping away and returning to view. Its beauty and movement are part of a trap set by Maricha. The verse lingers on the deception before the real danger is revealed.
ramayan::7250.modern_relevance: You keep checking the screen because the message appears, disappears, then appears again. That flicker can hook your attention before you even notice you're being pulled along.
ramayan::7250.insight: It trains you to notice how attraction can disguise danger and draw attention off course.

ramayan::7251.verse_sanskrit: मुहुर्तादेव ददृशे मुहुर्दूरात्प्रकाशते । । 3447 । । दर्शनादर्शनादेवं सोऽपाकर्षत राघवम् । सुदूरमाश्रमस्यास्य मारीचो मृगतां गतः । । 3448 । ।
ramayan::7251.verse_hindi: Maricha, transformed into a deer, was seen now near, now faroff. He pulled Rama away from the hermitage through his exits and entrances.
ramayan::7251.english_translation: Maricha, transformed into a deer, was seen now near, now far off. He drew Rama far away from the hermitage by appearing and disappearing.
ramayan::7251.translation_literal: मुहुर्तात् (for a moment) / एव (indeed) / ददृशे (was seen) / मुहुः (again and again) / दूरात् (from far away) / प्रकाशते (shines / appears) / दर्शनादर्शनात् (by appearing and not appearing) / एवम् (thus) / सः (he) / अपाकर्षत (drew away) / राघवम् (Raghava, Rama) / सुदूरम् (very far) / आश्रमस्य (from the hermitage) / अस्य (of this) / मारीचः (Maricha) / मृगताम् (deerhood) / गतः (having gone)
ramayan::7251.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7251.essence: Appearing and disappearing is enough to lead attention astray.
ramayan::7251.simple_meaning: Maricha kept appearing near and far, luring Rama away from the hermitage.
ramayan::7251.simple_insight: Distraction works best when it keeps changing shape.
ramayan::7251.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha has taken the form of a deer to deceive Rama. By appearing and vanishing, he pulls Rama farther from the hermitage, setting up the trap that will separate Rama from Sita and Lakshmana.
ramayan::7251.modern_relevance: A notification pings, then disappears. You check once, then again. The bait is not the message itself — it is the way it keeps pulling your attention back.
ramayan::7251.insight: It shows how repeated allure can move you farther from where you meant to stay.

ramayan::7252.verse_sanskrit: आसीत् क्रुद्धस्तु काकुत्स्थो विवशस्तेन मोहितः । अथावतस्थे संभ्रान्तश्चायामाश्रित्य शाद्वले । । 3449 । ।
ramayan::7252.verse_hindi: Deluded by that deer, Rama got tired, perplexed and angry. Then bewidered, he waited on a grassland under a shade.
ramayan::7252.english_translation: Deluded by that deer, Rama became angry, helpless, and bewildered. Then, confused, he stopped and rested under the shade on the grass.
ramayan::7252.translation_literal: आसीत् (became) / क्रुद्धः (angry) / तु (indeed) / काकुत्स्थः (Rama) / विवशः (helpless) / तेन (by that) / मोहितः (deluded) / अथ (then) / अवतस्थे (he stood still) / संभ्रान्तः (confused) / च (and) / आयाम् (shade) / आश्रित्य (having taken refuge in) / शाद्वले (on the grass)
ramayan::7252.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7252.essence: A clever distraction can turn resolve into confusion.
ramayan::7252.simple_meaning: Rama is thrown off balance by the golden deer. He grows angry and confused, then stops to rest in the shade.
ramayan::7252.simple_insight: Even the steady can be shaken when desire and confusion pull at the mind.
ramayan::7252.detailed_meaning: Maricha has lured Rama away from the hermitage by appearing as a dazzling deer. Rama, already pulled into the chase, now feels anger, fatigue, and confusion at once. He pauses under a tree, unaware that this moment is part of Ravana's trap.
ramayan::7252.modern_relevance: You keep chasing a dazzling distraction until your own mind feels hot and split. Then you sit down, drained, and only later realise it was designed to pull you off course.
ramayan::7252.insight: It shows how deception works through fatigue and agitation, not just through lies.

ramayan::7253.verse_sanskrit: स तमुन्मादयामास मृगरूपो निशाचरः । मृगैः परिवृतो वन्यैरदूरात्प्रत्यदृश्यत । । 34410 । ।
ramayan::7253.verse_hindi: That demon transformed himself into a deer and, surrounded by the animals of the forest at close range, attracted his attention.
ramayan::7253.english_translation: That night-roaming demon, in the form of a deer, drew him on; surrounded by wild forest animals, he appeared again from near by.
ramayan::7253.translation_literal: सः (he) / तम् (that one) / उन्मादयामास (made mad, drew on) / मृगरूपः (in deer-form) / निशाचरः (night-roaming being) / मृगैः (by deer/animals) / परिवृतः (surrounded) / वन्यैः (forest-dwelling) / अदूरात् (from not far) / प्रत्यदृश्यत (was seen again)
ramayan::7253.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7253.essence: A trap survives by staying just visible.
ramayan::7253.simple_meaning: The demon, disguised as a deer, kept drawing Rama's attention from nearby, surrounded by other forest animals.
ramayan::7253.simple_insight: Distraction often works by looking harmless and staying just out of reach.
ramayan::7253.detailed_meaning: Maricha has already lured Rama away from the hermitage. Now he keeps appearing near the edge of sight, disguised as a deer and ringed by forest creatures, deepening the trap and keeping Rama fixated on him.
ramayan::7253.modern_relevance: A harmless-looking notification keeps popping up while you're trying to focus, and before you know it, your attention has been pulled somewhere it shouldn't go.
ramayan::7253.insight: It shows how deception sustains itself by repeatedly reappearing and keeping the mind hooked.

ramayan::7254.verse_hindi: Seeing Ramas  intention to catch him, the deer ran away once again out of fear and disappeared in a moment.
ramayan::7254.english_translation: Seeing Rama's intention to catch him, the deer ran away once again out of fear and disappeared in a moment.
ramayan::7254.translation_literal: गृहीतुकामम् (wishing to catch) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / एवम् (thus) / पुनः एव (again) / अभ्यधावत (ran toward) / तत्क्षणात् (at that moment) / एव (indeed) / संत्रासात् (from fear) / पुनः (again) / अन्तर्हितः (hidden) / अभवत् (became)
ramayan::7254.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7254.essence: The trap works by retreating the moment you reach for it.
ramayan::7254.simple_meaning: The deer saw that Rama was about to catch him, fled again in fear, and vanished at once.
ramayan::7254.simple_insight: Panic can make a deception slip out of sight in an instant.
ramayan::7254.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the golden deer has already drawn Rama off balance. The moment it senses pursuit, it bolts away again and disappears, keeping the trap alive and pushing Rama deeper into error.
ramayan::7254.modern_relevance: A misleading message looks clear for one second, then slips away before you can pin it down. The chase itself keeps you from seeing what is really happening.
ramayan::7254.insight: It shows how deception survives by staying just out of reach, keeping attention locked on the wrong target.

ramayan::7255.verse_sanskrit: पुनरेव ततो दूराद्वृक्षषण्डाद्विनिस्सृतम् । दृष्ट्वा रामो महातेजास्तं हन्तुं कृतनिश्चयः । । 34412 । ।
ramayan::7255.verse_hindi: Resplendent Rama saw the deer coming out of a cluster of trees at a distance and determined to kill him.
ramayan::7255.english_translation: Resplendent Rama saw the deer coming out of a cluster of trees at a distance and determined to kill him.
ramayan::7255.translation_literal: पुनरेव (again) / ततः (then) / दूरात् (from a distance) / वृक्षषण्डात् (from a cluster of trees) / विनिस्सृतम् (having come out) / दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / रामः (Rama) / महातेजाः (greatly resplendent) / तम् (that one) / हन्तुम् (to kill) / कृतनिश्चयः (with a fixed resolve)
ramayan::7255.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7255.essence: A brief decision in the forest begins the collapse.
ramayan::7255.simple_meaning: Rama sees the deer again from far away and decides to kill it.
ramayan::7255.simple_insight: A split-second decision can set the whole tragedy in motion.
ramayan::7255.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the golden deer keeps appearing and disappearing, pulling Rama's attention toward it. Seeing it emerge again from the trees, Rama fixes on killing it. This moment is one step in the trap that will separate him from Sita.
ramayan::7255.modern_relevance: You spot the same problem again after thinking it was gone. In that instant, your next move can carry far more weight than it seems.
ramayan::7255.insight: It shows how a single sharpened intention can move a story toward irreversible loss.

ramayan::7256.verse_sanskrit: भूयस्तु शरमुद्धृत्य कुपितस्तत्र राघवः । सूर्यरश्मिप्रतीकाशं ज्वलन्तमरिमर्दनः । । 34413 । । सन्धाय सुदृढे चापे विकृष्य बलवद्बली । तमेव मृगमुद्दिश्य श्वसन्तमिव पन्नगम् । । 34414 । । मुमोच ज्वलितं दीप्तमस्त्रं ब्रह्मविनिर्मितम् ।
ramayan::7256.verse_hindi: Powerful Rama, destroyer of foes, lifted in a rage his arrow blazing like the light of  the Sun, strung it to his sturdy bow and drew it with all his force. He then aimed at the deer and released the shining  arrow created by Brahma which went hissing like a  serpent.
ramayan::7256.english_translation: Powerful Rama, destroyer of foes, lifted in a rage his arrow blazing like the light of the Sun, strung it to his sturdy bow and drew it with all his force. He then aimed at the deer and released the shining arrow created by Brahma which went hissing like a serpent.
ramayan::7256.translation_literal: भूयस् (again) / तु (but) / शरम् (arrow) / उद्धृत्य (having lifted) / कुपितः (angry) / तत्र (there) / राघवः (Raghava) / सूर्यरश्मिप्रतीकाशम् (like sun-rays) / ज्वलन्तम् (blazing) / अरिमर्दनः (crusher of enemies) / सन्धाय (having fitted) / सुदृढे (on the firm) / चापे (bow) / विकृष्य (drawing back) / बलवत् (strongly) / बली (mighty one) / तम् (that) / एव (indeed) / मृगम् (deer) / उद्दिश्य (aiming at) / श्वसन्तम् इव (as if breathing) / पन्नगम् (serpent) / मुमोच (released) / ज्वलितम् (burning) / दीप्तम् (shining) / अस्त्रम् (weapon) / ब्रह्मविनिर्मितम् (made by Brahma)
ramayan::7256.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7256.essence: Anger makes the hand move before clarity returns.
ramayan::7256.simple_meaning: Rama, angered by the deer, fits a blazing arrow to his bow, draws with full force, and releases a divine weapon at it.
ramayan::7256.simple_insight: A single moment of anger can turn intention into irreversible action.
ramayan::7256.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has already decided the deer must be struck. He lifts a blazing arrow, draws his bow hard, and sends a weapon forged by Brahma toward the fleeing form. The next verse reveals the hidden truth behind that target.
ramayan::7256.modern_relevance: You refresh the message one more time, then send the sharp reply before thinking. The damage is already in motion.
ramayan::7256.insight: It shows how quickly judgment hardens into action once anger takes the lead.

ramayan::7257.verse_sanskrit: शरीरं मृगरूपस्य विनिर्भिद्य शरोत्तमः । । 34415 । । मारीचस्यैव हृदयं बिभेदाशनिसन्निभः ।
ramayan::7257.verse_hindi: The great arrow which was like a thunderbolt first pierced into the body of Maricha who had assumed the form of a deer and then tore his heart.
ramayan::7257.english_translation: The great arrow, like a thunderbolt, pierced Maricha's deer body and then split his heart.
ramayan::7257.translation_literal: शरीरम् (body) / मृगरूपस्य (of the deer-form) / विनिर्भिद्य (piercing through) / शरोत्तमः (the excellent arrow) / मारीचस्य (of Maricha) / एव (indeed) / हृदयम् (heart) / बिभेद (split) / अशनिसन्निभः (thunderbolt-like)
ramayan::7257.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7257.essence: False appearance falls the moment truth meets force.
ramayan::7257.simple_meaning: Rama's arrow strikes Maricha in his deer form, piercing his body and heart.
ramayan::7257.simple_insight: A disguise cannot protect what has already chosen its end.
ramayan::7257.detailed_meaning: Rama has already recognized the golden deer as a trap. He draws, releases, and the arrow tears through Maricha's false form and into his heart. This is the moment the deception begins to collapse.
ramayan::7257.modern_relevance: You can sense when a situation is off, but still have to act. Some disguises look beautiful right up until the moment they break.
ramayan::7257.insight: It shows how quickly a false appearance can be cut through by decisive action.

ramayan::7258.verse_hindi: And, hurt by the dart, Maricha roared frighteningly, leaped as high as a  palm tree  and dropped down on earth almost dead.
ramayan::7258.english_translation: And, hurt by the dart, Maricha roared frighteningly, leaped as high as a palm tree and dropped down on earth almost dead.
ramayan::7258.translation_literal: तालमात्रम् (as high as a palm tree) / अथ (then) / उत्प्लुत्य (having leaped up) / न्यपतत् (fell down) / सः (he) / शरातुरः (wounded by the arrow) / विनदन् (roaring) / भैरवम् (terrifying) / नादम् (sound) / धरण्याम् (on the earth) / अल्पजीवितः (with life nearly gone)
ramayan::7258.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7258.essence: Deception cannot survive a direct strike for long.
ramayan::7258.simple_meaning: Maricha, wounded by Rama's arrow, leapt high, roared in terror, and fell to the ground nearly dead.
ramayan::7258.simple_insight: A sudden blow can topple even a cunning enemy.
ramayan::7258.detailed_meaning: Rama has just struck Maricha, who came disguised as a deer to lure him away. The arrow pierces the disguise and the body beneath it. Maricha screams, jumps, and collapses, nearly dead, setting up his final thoughts in the next verse.
ramayan::7258.modern_relevance: A plan built on deception can collapse in a single moment. The body may keep moving for a while, but the false shape cannot hold forever.
ramayan::7258.insight: It shows the immediate ruin that follows a hidden attack, preparing the ground for Maricha's last realization.

ramayan::7259.verse_sanskrit: म्रियमाणस्तु मारीचो जहौ तां कृत्रिमां तनुम् । । 34417 । । स्मृत्वा तद्वचनं रक्षो दध्यौ केन तु लक्ष्मणम् । इह प्रस्थापयेत्सीता शून्ये तां रावणो हरेत् । । 34418 । ।
ramayan::7259.verse_hindi: Maricha gave up his false form of the deer and before breathing his last, remembered the words of Ravana. He thought over the means through which Sita could send Lakshmana to this spot so that  Ravana would abduct her when she is alone.
ramayan::7259.english_translation: Maricha gave up his false deer form as he was dying. He remembered Ravana's words and thought about how to get Lakshmana away so Sita would be left alone for Ravana to seize.
ramayan::7259.translation_literal: म्रियमाणः (dying) / तु (but) / मारीचः (Maricha) / जहौ (gave up) / ताम् (that) / कृत्रिमाम् (artificial) / तनुम् (body/form) / स्मृत्वा (remembering) / तत् (that) / वचनम् (word) / रक्षः (the demon) / दध्यौ (he thought) / केन (by what means) / तु (indeed) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / इह (here) / प्रस्थापयेत् (should send away) / सीता (Sita) / शून्ये (when alone) / ताम् (her) / रावणः (Ravana) / हरेत् (would seize)
ramayan::7259.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7259.essence: Separation is the first step of the abduction.
ramayan::7259.simple_meaning: Maricha drops his disguise as he dies and thinks through Ravana's plan: separate Lakshmana from Sita so Ravana can abduct her.
ramayan::7259.simple_insight: A trap often begins with a small separation.
ramayan::7259.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha has been struck down by Rama's arrow. As his life fades, he abandons the deer disguise and remembers Ravana's instructions. The verse shows the last calculation behind the abduction plot: Sita must be left alone.
ramayan::7259.modern_relevance: A harmless-looking request can be the first move in a larger trap. By the time you notice the pattern, the separation has already begun.
ramayan::7259.insight: It trains you to notice how manipulation often works by isolating one person from support.

ramayan::7260.verse_sanskrit: स प्राप्तकालमाज्ञाय चकार च तत स्वनम् । सदृशं राघवस्येह हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च । । 34419 । ।
ramayan::7260.verse_hindi: Then Maricha realised that the appropriate time had come. In a voice similar to Ramas, he shouted loudly Alas Sita, Alas Lakshmana
ramayan::7260.english_translation: Then Maricha realised that the right moment had come, and he cried out in a voice like Rama's: “Alas, Sita! Alas, Lakshmana!”
ramayan::7260.translation_literal: सः (he) / प्राप्तकालम् (the right time) / आज्ञाय (having known) / चकार (made) / च (and) / तत् (that) / स्वनम् (sound/cry) / सदृशम् (similar) / राघवस्य (of Rama) / इह (here) / हा (alas) / सीते (O Sita) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana) / इति (thus) / च (and)
ramayan::7260.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7260.essence: False urgency can wear a trusted voice.
ramayan::7260.simple_meaning: Maricha sees the moment to act and uses Rama's voice to deceive Sita and Lakshmana.
ramayan::7260.simple_insight: A lie can work best when it sounds like trust.
ramayan::7260.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha is dying from Rama's arrow. Knowing Ravana's plan must now move forward, he imitates Rama's voice and cries out to Sita and Lakshmana. The verse is a small but crucial link in the chain that draws them apart.
ramayan::7260.modern_relevance: A message lands in your phone sounding exactly like someone you trust. You react before thinking, and that split second is all the manipulation needed.
ramayan::7260.insight: It shows how deception borrows the shape of trust to trigger instant panic.

ramayan::7261.verse_sanskrit: तेन मर्मणि निर्विद्धं शरेणानुपमेन हि । मृगरूपं तु तत्त्यक्त्वा राक्षसं रूपमास्थितः । । 34420 । । चक्रे स सुमहाकायं मारीचो जीवितं त्यजन् ।
ramayan::7261.verse_hindi: Struck in the vital part by Ramas matchless dart, Maricha gave up the form of the deer and assumed his huge body of the demon.
ramayan::7261.english_translation: Struck in the vital part by Rama's matchless dart, Maricha gave up the form of the deer and assumed his huge body of the demon.
ramayan::7261.translation_literal: तेन (by that) / मर्मणि (in the vital part) / निर्विद्धं (pierced) / शरेण (by arrow) / अनुपमेन (matchless) / हि (indeed) / मृगरूपं (deer-form) / तु (but) / तत् (that) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / राक्षसं (demon) / रूपम् (form) / आस्थितः (having assumed) / चक्रे (made) / सः (he) / सुमहाकायम् (of huge body) / मारीचः (Maricha) / जीवितम् (life) / त्यजन् (giving up)
ramayan::7261.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7261.essence: A convincing disguise ends the moment truth pierces it.
ramayan::7261.simple_meaning: Maricha is hit in a fatal spot, drops the deer disguise, and reveals his true monstrous form as he dies.
ramayan::7261.simple_insight: Even a mask cannot survive the moment truth finally strikes.
ramayan::7261.detailed_meaning: Maricha has lured Rama into the trap by wearing the golden deer form. Now Rama's arrow lands in a fatal place, and the deception collapses. In his last moments, Maricha drops the false body and reveals the demon beneath.
ramayan::7261.modern_relevance: The polished version of a lie can hold only until pressure reaches the weak point. One hard truth, one unavoidable consequence, and the performance ends.
ramayan::7261.insight: It shows how false appearances fall apart when reality finally hits them.

ramayan::7262.verse_sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं भूमौ राक्षसं घोरदर्शनम् । । 34421 । । रामो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं चेष्टमानं महीतले । जगाम मनसा सीतां लक्ष्मणस्य वचस्स्मरन् । । 34422 । ।
ramayan::7262.verse_hindi: Seeing that terrific demon fallen on the ground, drenched in blood, and strring his limbs, Rama thought of Lakshmanas words and reached Sita mentally (thought of her).
ramayan::7262.english_translation: Seeing that terrific demon fallen on the ground, drenched in blood and writhing on the earth, Rama remembered Lakshmana's warning and turned his mind to Sita.
ramayan::7262.translation_literal: तं (that one) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / पतितं (fallen) / भूमौ (on the ground) / राक्षसं (demon) / घोरदर्शनम् (terrible-looking) / रामो (Rama) / रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं (with limbs soaked in blood) / चेष्टमानं (writhing) / महीतले (on the earth) / जगाम (went) / मनसा (with the mind) / सीतां (to Sita) / लक्ष्मणस्य (of Lakshmana) / वचस्स्मरन् (remembering the words)
ramayan::7262.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7262.essence: A warning remembered too late still changes everything.
ramayan::7262.simple_meaning: Rama sees Maricha dying and immediately thinks of Sita, remembering Lakshmana's warning.
ramayan::7262.simple_insight: Even in battle, the mind can snap back to what matters most.
ramayan::7262.detailed_meaning: Maricha has just been struck down after using his trick to lure Rama away. Seeing the demon writhing in blood, Rama does not linger on the kill. Lakshmana's warning returns at once, and his mind races toward Sita.
ramayan::7262.modern_relevance: You get the bad news, and your mind is already three steps ahead to the person who might be in danger. Some moments don't let you stay where you are.
ramayan::7262.insight: It shows how a sudden clue can redirect attention from the immediate scene to a deeper threat.

ramayan::7263.verse_sanskrit: मारीचस्य तु मायैषा पूर्वोक्तं लक्ष्मणेन तु । तत्तथा ह्यभवच्चाद्य मारीचोऽयं मया हतः । । 34423 । ।
ramayan::7263.verse_hindi: This is an illusion created by Maricha. It happened exactly the way Lakshmana had said earlier. Maricha is now killed.
ramayan::7263.english_translation: This is an illusion created by Maricha. It happened exactly the way Lakshmana had said earlier. Maricha is now killed.
ramayan::7263.translation_literal: मारीचस्य (of Maricha) / तु (indeed) / माया (illusion, trick) / एषा (this) / पूर्वोक्तं (said earlier) / लक्ष्मणेन (by Lakshmana) / तु (indeed) / तत् (that) / तथा (so) / हि (indeed) / अभवत् (happened) / च (and) / अद्य (today, now) / मारीचः (Maricha) / अयम् (this one) / मया (by me) / हतः (killed)
ramayan::7263.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7263.essence: The trick is exposed only after it has already done its work.
ramayan::7263.simple_meaning: Rama recognizes that Maricha's deception has worked exactly as Lakshmana warned, and confirms that Maricha has been killed.
ramayan::7263.simple_insight: A warning ignored can become a costly truth.
ramayan::7263.detailed_meaning: After Rama shoots Maricha in the forest, the dying demon reveals the trick behind the golden deer. Rama sees that Lakshmana had been right all along, and the trap has now begun to unfold against Sita.
ramayan::7263.modern_relevance: You dismissed the warning because the situation looked harmless. Only after the damage starts do you see how precise the warning was.
ramayan::7263.insight: It shifts attention from the visible event to the hidden manipulation behind it.

ramayan::7264.verse_sanskrit: हा सीते लक्ष्मणेत्येवमाक्रुश्य च महास्वरम् । ममार राक्षसस्सोऽयं श्रुत्वा सीता कथं भवेत् । । 34424 । । लक्ष्मणश्च महाबाहुः कामवस्थां गमिष्यति । इति सञ्चिन्त्य धर्मात्मा रामो हृष्टतनूरुहः । । 34425 । ।
ramayan::7264.verse_hindi: This demon Maricha screamed aloud saying, Alas, Sita, Alas, Lakshmana. He is now dead. How would Sita react to this voice? What would be the condition of Lakshmana? While righteous Rama reflected on this, his hair stood on end.
ramayan::7264.english_translation: Maricha cried out, "Alas, Sita! Alas, Lakshmana!" Thinking of what Sita would do on hearing that cry, and what would become of mighty Lakshmana, righteous Rama felt his hair stand on end.
ramayan::7264.translation_literal: हा (alas) / सीते (O Sita) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana) / इति एवम् (thus) / आक्रुश्य (crying out) / च (and) / महास्वरम् (with a great voice) / ममार (died) / राक्षसः (the demon) / सः अयम् (this one) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / सीता (Sita) / कथम् (how) / भवेत् (would be) / लक्ष्मणः च (and Lakshmana) / महाबाहुः (mighty-armed) / काम-अवस्थाम् (that condition of desire/confusion) / गमिष्यति (will go) / इति (thus) / सञ्चिन्त्य (thinking) / धर्म-आत्मा (righteous-souled) / रामः (Rama) / हृष्ट-तनूरुहः (with hair standing on end)
ramayan::7264.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7264.essence: A false cry can shake even the steadfast when love is on the line.
ramayan::7264.simple_meaning: Rama hears the false cry and instantly worries for Sita and Lakshmana. Even before fear fully forms, his body reacts.
ramayan::7264.simple_insight: Love makes you vulnerable; concern can strike the body before reason steadies it.
ramayan::7264.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha dies in his deceptive deer form and shouts the names of Sita and Lakshmana to lure Rama into panic. Rama immediately imagines their danger. The verse captures the split second when concern overwhelms calm.
ramayan::7264.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with a voice note that sounds wrong, and your chest tightens before you even know why. Love and fear often arrive together, faster than explanation.
ramayan::7264.insight: It shows how quickly the mind can jump from a sound to worst-case fear, especially when people you love may be at risk.

ramayan::7265.verse_sanskrit: तत्र रामं भयं तीव्रमाविवेश विषादजम् । राक्षसं मृगरूपं तं हत्वा श्रुत्वा च तत्स्वरम् । । 34426 । ।
ramayan::7265.verse_hindi: After killing the demon in the figure of a deer and hearing his voice, Rama was overtaken by intense fear born of despair.
ramayan::7265.english_translation: After killing the demon in the figure of a deer and hearing his voice, Rama was overtaken by intense fear born of despair.
ramayan::7265.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / रामम् (Rama) / भयम् (fear) / तीव्रम् (intense) / आविवेश (entered / overtook) / विषादजम् (born of despair) / राक्षसम् (demon) / मृगरूपम् (in deer form) / तम् (that) / हत्वा (having killed) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / च (and) / तत् (that) / स्वरम् (voice)
ramayan::7265.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7265.essence: The trap is clear only after the damage is done.
ramayan::7265.simple_meaning: After killing the deer-shaped demon and hearing its cry, Rama is suddenly struck by deep fear and despair.
ramayan::7265.simple_insight: Even a steady heart can be shaken when a hidden trap reveals itself.
ramayan::7265.detailed_meaning: In the forest at Panchavati, Rama has killed the strange deer that was really Maricha. The cry he hears after the blow confirms the trick. That realization hits him with sudden dread, because Sita is now exposed and the danger is real.
ramayan::7265.modern_relevance: You realize the message was a trap only after you have already answered. The calm breaks instantly, and your mind rushes to the person left unprotected.
ramayan::7265.insight: It shows how quickly certainty can collapse when a deceptive situation is exposed.

ramayan::7266.verse_sanskrit: निहत्य पृषतं चान्यं मांसमादाय राघवः । त्वरमाणो जनस्थानं ससाराभिमुखस्तदा । । 34427 । ।
ramayan::7266.verse_hindi: Then Rama killed another deer, collected the venison and hastened to Janasthana.
ramayan::7266.english_translation: Then Rama killed another deer, collected the venison, and hastened toward Janasthana.
ramayan::7266.translation_literal: निहत्य (having killed) / पृषतं (the deer) / च (and) / अन्यं (another) / मांसम् (meat) / आदाय (having taken) / राघवः (Rama) / त्वरमाणः (hastening) / जनस्थानम् (toward Janasthana) / ससार (ran) / अभिमुखः (toward) / तदा (then)
ramayan::7266.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7266.essence: Rama moves quickly; the verse only advances the scene.
ramayan::7266.simple_meaning: Rama quickly killed another deer, took the meat, and headed back toward Janasthana.
ramayan::7266.simple_insight: The motion is urgent and practical, not reflective.
ramayan::7266.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has just been drawn off balance by Maricha's deceit and cries. This line only shows the next physical movement: he kills another deer, takes the meat, and rushes back toward Janasthana.
ramayan::7266.modern_relevance: A sudden interruption breaks your focus, and you go straight back to the task you were in the middle of.
ramayan::7266.insight: It tracks the immediate return to action after a distraction, without adding any teaching.

ramayan::7267.verse_sanskrit: आर्तस्वरं तु तं भर्तुर्विज्ञाय सदृशं वने । उवाच लक्ष्मणं सीता गच्छ जीनीहि राघवम् । । 3451 । ।
ramayan::7267.verse_hindi: On hearing the voice in distress and recognising that it was similar to her husbands voice, Sita said to Lakshmana, Go and find out Ramas whereabouts.
ramayan::7267.english_translation: Recognising the distressed voice as like her husband's, Sita said to Lakshmana, "Go and find out where Rama is."
ramayan::7267.translation_literal: आर्तस्वरम् (distressed voice) / तु (indeed) / तम् (that) / भर्तुः (of the husband) / विज्ञाय (having recognised) / सदृशम् (similar) / वने (in the forest) / उवाच (said) / लक्ष्मणम् (to Lakshmana) / सीता (Sita) / गच्छ (go) / जीनीहि (find out) / राघवम् (Rama)
ramayan::7267.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7267.essence: Love recognises distress and acts before certainty arrives.
ramayan::7267.simple_meaning: Sita hears a voice in distress and immediately senses it is Rama's. She asks Lakshmana to go find him.
ramayan::7267.simple_insight: Love becomes alert before the mind has proof.
ramayan::7267.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita hears a cry that sounds like Rama's. The sound cuts through her immediately. She turns to Lakshmana and sends him to search, because fear for the person she loves has already taken hold.
ramayan::7267.modern_relevance: You hear a shaky voice note from someone you love and know something is wrong before you can explain why. Care moves faster than certainty.
ramayan::7267.insight: It trains attention to respond to another's distress without delay or denial.

ramayan::7268.verse_sanskrit: न हि मे हृदयं स्थाने जीवितं वाऽवतिष्ठति । क्रोशतः परमार्तस्य श्रुतश्शब्दो मया भृशम् । । 3452 । । आक्रन्दमानं तु वने भ्रातरं त्रातुमर्हसि ।
ramayan::7268.verse_hindi: I clearly heard Rama calling out in great distress. Indeed, my heart as well as my life is not in its place (restless). You ought to go and protect your brother who is crying in pain in the forest.
ramayan::7268.english_translation: I clearly heard Rama calling out in great distress. Indeed, my heart as well as my life is not in its place. You ought to go and protect your brother who is crying in pain in the forest.
ramayan::7268.translation_literal: न हि (indeed not) / मे (my) / हृदयं (heart) / स्थाने (in its place) / जीवितं (life) / वा (or) / अवतिष्ठति (remains) / क्रोशतः (of one crying out) / परमार्तस्य (of one in great distress) / श्रुतः (heard) / शब्दः (sound/voice) / मया (by me) / भृशम् (greatly) / आक्रन्दमानं (crying out) / तु (indeed) / वने (in the forest) / भ्रातरं (brother) / त्रातुम् (to protect) / अर्हसि (you ought)
ramayan::7268.speaker: Sita
