ramayan::7268.essence: Urgency overrides fear when someone you love is in danger.
ramayan::7268.simple_meaning: Sita tells Lakshmana that she heard Rama's cry of distress and cannot stay calm. She urges him to go immediately and protect his brother in the forest.
ramayan::7268.simple_insight: Love becomes urgent when someone you care about is in danger.
ramayan::7268.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita hears what she believes is Rama's cry for help. Her own fear turns into command: Lakshmana must leave at once and protect his brother. This moment begins the chain that leads to her abduction.
ramayan::7268.modern_relevance: You hear your partner’s voice crack over the phone, and your body knows before your mind does. In that instant, hesitation feels impossible.
ramayan::7268.insight: It shifts you from passive listening to immediate protective action when distress is unmistakable.

ramayan::7269.verse_sanskrit: तं क्षिप्रमभिधाव त्वं भ्रातरं शरणैषिणम् । । 3453 । । रक्षसां वशमापन्नं सिंहानामिव गोवृषम् ।
ramayan::7269.verse_hindi: Like a bull caught by lions, your brother is seeking help caught by demons. You should run at once to your brother.
ramayan::7269.english_translation: Run to your brother at once. He has fallen under the power of demons and is seeking refuge, like a bull surrounded by lions.
ramayan::7269.translation_literal: तं (him) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / अभिधाव (run toward) / त्वम् (you) / भ्रातरम् (brother) / शरणैषिणम् (seeking refuge) / रक्षसाम् (of demons) / वशम् (power) / आपन्नम् (fallen into) / सिंहानाम् (of lions) / इव (like) / गोवृषम् (a bull)
ramayan::7269.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7269.essence: Refusing to delay can be the most loving act.
ramayan::7269.simple_meaning: Sita urges Lakshmana to hurry to Rama, who is in danger and seeking help. The moment demands immediate action, not hesitation.
ramayan::7269.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it turns into swift help.
ramayan::7269.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has heard Rama's cry and knows he is in trouble. She tells Lakshmana to run to his brother at once, describing Rama as helpless before enemies. Her urgency drives the next turn of the exile story.
ramayan::7269.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with a message from someone you love: "Call me now." You do not need a perfect plan. You need to move before fear turns into delay.
ramayan::7269.insight: It shifts you from caution to immediate response when someone is in danger.

ramayan::7270.verse_sanskrit: न जगाम तथोक्तस्तु भ्रातुराज्ञाय शासनम् । । 3454 । । तमुवाच ततस्तत्र कुपिता जनकात्मजा ।
ramayan::7270.verse_hindi: When he did not budge in obedience to his brothers order (to protect Sita), the daughter of Janaka in a rage said :
ramayan::7270.english_translation: When he did not move in obedience to his brother's order to protect Sita, Janaka's daughter, angered, spoke there.
ramayan::7270.translation_literal: न (not) / जगाम (went) / तथा (thus) / उक्तः (spoken to) / तु (but) / भ्रातुः (brother's) / आज्ञाय (order) / शासनम् (command) / तम् (to him) / उवाच (said) / ततः (then) / तत्र (there) / कुपिता (angry) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka)
ramayan::7270.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7270.essence: Loyalty can be mistaken for betrayal when fear is in charge.
ramayan::7270.simple_meaning: Lakshmana refuses to leave, even after Rama's command. Sita, seeing his refusal, speaks in anger.
ramayan::7270.simple_insight: Even noble restraint can look like betrayal when someone you love is in danger.
ramayan::7270.detailed_meaning: Rama has sent Lakshmana away to help him, but Lakshmana stays fixed beside Sita. Watching that refusal, Sita loses patience and speaks sharply. The moment matters because her fear for Rama turns his loyalty into something she can misread.
ramayan::7270.modern_relevance: You ask someone to help the person you love, and they stay where they are. In that instant, their silence can feel like abandonment, even if their heart is loyal.
ramayan::7270.insight: It shows how fear can turn another person's duty into apparent disloyalty.

ramayan::7271.verse_sanskrit: सौमित्रे मित्ररूपेण भ्रातुस्त्वमसि शत्रुवत् । । 3455 । । यस्त्वमस्यामवस्थायां भ्रातरं नाभिपत्स्यसे ।
ramayan::7271.verse_hindi: Since you, O son of Sumitra,  are not reaching out to your brother in this situation, you are an enemy to your brother in the guise of a friend৷৷
ramayan::7271.english_translation: Since you, O son of Sumitra, are not reaching out to your brother in this situation, you are an enemy to your brother in the guise of a friend.
ramayan::7271.translation_literal: सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra) / मित्ररूपेण (in the form of a friend) / भ्रातुः (of the brother) / त्वम् (you) / असि (are) / शत्रुवत् (like an enemy) / यः (who) / त्वम् (you) / अस्यां (in this) / अवस्थायाम् (situation) / भ्रातरम् (brother) / न (not) / अभिपत्स्यसे (you will reach/protect)
ramayan::7271.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7271.essence: Failing to help your own brother turns friendship into disguise.
ramayan::7271.simple_meaning: Sita rebukes Lakshmana for not going to Rama's aid. She says that in a crisis, refusing to help your brother makes you look like an enemy.
ramayan::7271.simple_insight: Real loyalty is proved by response, not intention.
ramayan::7271.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita sees Lakshmana hesitate while Rama is in danger. Her anger is sharp because the stakes are absolute: a brother's safety, a wife's fear, and the collapse of trust if help does not come immediately.
ramayan::7271.modern_relevance: Your sibling calls from the roadside after a flat tire, and you keep delaying because it is inconvenient. This verse cuts through excuses: the people closest to you are measured by whether you show up.
ramayan::7271.insight: It shifts loyalty from sentiment to immediate support in a crisis.

ramayan::7272.verse_sanskrit: इच्छसि त्वं विनश्यन्तं रामं लक्ष्मण मत्कृते । । 3456 । । लोभात्त्वं मत्कृते नूनं नानुगच्छसि राघवम् ।
ramayan::7272.verse_hindi: It is possess me that you wish Ramas death. You do not rush to him certainly because of greed for me.
ramayan::7272.english_translation: You want Rama to perish for my sake. Out of desire for me, you do not go to Raghava.
ramayan::7272.translation_literal: इच्छसि (you wish) / त्वं (you) / विनश्यन्तं (perishing) / रामं (Rama) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / मत्कृते (for my sake) / लोभात् (from greed) / त्वं (you) / मत्कृते (for my sake) / नूनं (indeed) / न (not) / अनुगच्छसि (you go after) / राघवम् (Raghava)
ramayan::7272.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7272.essence: Wanting can make you fail the person who needs you most.
ramayan::7272.simple_meaning: Sita accuses Lakshmana of staying back because he wants her, not because he is loyal to Rama. She sees his hesitation as selfish desire, not care.
ramayan::7272.simple_insight: Desire can disguise itself as concern and still pull you away from what matters most.
ramayan::7272.detailed_meaning: In the forest after Sita is left with Lakshmana, she turns on him sharply. Rama is in danger, yet Lakshmana still hesitates. Sita interprets that hesitation as greed for her presence, not brotherly loyalty.
ramayan::7272.modern_relevance: You keep delaying the hard call because staying close feels easier than doing what your role demands. The excuse sounds noble, but the real pull is personal wanting.
ramayan::7272.insight: It exposes how attachment can twist duty into hesitation and make inaction look like care.

ramayan::7273.verse_sanskrit: व्यसनं ते प्रियं मन्ये स्नेहो भ्रातरिनास्तिते । । 3457 । । तेन तिष्ठसि विश्रब्धंतमपश्यन्महाद्युतिम् ।
ramayan::7273.verse_hindi: I think Ramas adversity is welcome to you. You do not have any love towards your brother. It is for this that you stand unconcerned instead of proceeding to help your brilliant brother.
ramayan::7273.english_translation: I think Rama's adversity is welcome to you. You have no love for your brother. That is why you stand unconcerned instead of going to help your brilliant brother.
ramayan::7273.translation_literal: व्यसनम् (adversity) / ते (to you) / प्रियम् (dear, welcome) / मन्ये (I think) / स्नेहः (love) / भ्रातरि (for the brother) / न अस्ति ते (there is not in you) / तेन (for that reason) / तिष्ठसि (you stand) / विश्रब्धम् (confidently, unconcerned) / तम् (him) / अपश्यन् (not seeing) / महाद्युतिम् (the greatly radiant one)
ramayan::7273.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7273.essence: Real love does not stay still when the person you cherish is in danger.
ramayan::7273.simple_meaning: Sita rebukes Lakshmana for staying back instead of rushing to Rama's aid. She sees his hesitation as proof that he does not truly love his brother.
ramayan::7273.simple_insight: Love is proven by movement, not excuses.
ramayan::7273.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is in danger and Lakshmana has not yet gone to him. Sita, anxious and fierce with loyalty, reads his delay as betrayal. Her words sharpen the pressure: this is not a small hesitation, but a test of brotherly love.
ramayan::7273.modern_relevance: Your sibling calls from the hospital and you keep finding reasons to wait. The delay itself starts to feel like the answer.
ramayan::7273.insight: It exposes how quickly concern becomes action when loyalty is real.

ramayan::7274.verse_sanskrit: किं हि संशयमापन्ने तस्मिन्निह मया भवेत् । । 3458 । । कर्तव्यमिह तिष्ठन्त्या यत्प्रधानस्त्वमागतः ।
ramayan::7274.verse_hindi: When he for whose service you have primary come here, has met with difficulty, what is the use of your being here? What purpose you serve by staying here with me ?
ramayan::7274.english_translation: When the one you came here to serve is in trouble, what use is your staying here with me? What purpose do you serve by remaining here?
ramayan::7274.translation_literal: किं (what) / हि (indeed) / संशयमापन्ने (having fallen into difficulty) / तस्मिन् (in that one) / इह (here) / मया (with me) / भवेत् (would be) / कर्तव्यम् (to be done) / इह (here) / तिष्ठन्त्या (by staying) / यत् (what) / प्रधानः (chief) / त्वम् (you) / आगतः (have come)
ramayan::7274.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7274.essence: Real duty can require leaving the person who wants you most.
ramayan::7274.simple_meaning: Sita tells Lakshmana that if Rama is in trouble, Lakshmana should not remain with her. His real duty is to go to Rama.
ramayan::7274.simple_insight: Love becomes clear when duty is tested under pressure.
ramayan::7274.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is frightened and grieving, but she still thinks with moral precision. Lakshmana has come to protect her, yet Rama is the one in danger. She presses him to leave her side and go where his real obligation lies.
ramayan::7274.modern_relevance: You’re comforting one person while another crisis waits across town. The harder truth is that your presence may be needed elsewhere, even if leaving feels cruel.
ramayan::7274.insight: It shifts loyalty from comfort to obligation, showing that protection must follow the real need.

ramayan::7275.verse_sanskrit: इति ब्रुवाणां वैदेहीं बाष्पशोकपरिप्लुताम् । । 3459 । । अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणस्त्रस्तां सीतां मृगवधूमिव ।
ramayan::7275.verse_hindi: While Sita thus spoke, flooded with tears of sorrow, frightened like a doe, Lakshmana replied :
ramayan::7275.english_translation: While Sita thus spoke, flooded with tears of sorrow, frightened like a doe, Lakshmana replied:
ramayan::7275.translation_literal: इति (thus) / ब्रुवाणाम् (speaking) / वैदेहीम् (Sita) / बाष्प-शोक-परिप्लुताम् (overwhelmed with tears and sorrow) / मृग-वधूम् इव (like a doe) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / त्रस्ताम् (frightened) / सीताम् (to Sita)
ramayan::7275.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7275.essence: Her fear is so raw that even the reply must arrive gently.
ramayan::7275.simple_meaning: Lakshmana speaks to Sita while she is overwhelmed by grief and fear, like a frightened deer.
ramayan::7275.simple_insight: Even in panic, the scene stays human, fragile, and painfully real.
ramayan::7275.detailed_meaning: Sita has just spoken in fear and sorrow, pressing Lakshmana with desperate questions. Valmiki pauses to show her state first: tears, grief, and the vulnerability of a doe. Then Lakshmana begins his reply, setting up the next part of their exchange.
ramayan::7275.modern_relevance: Someone is crying across from you, asking the same question three times because panic has narrowed everything. Before the answer comes, you feel the room tighten around their fear.
ramayan::7275.insight: It shifts attention from the content of the reply to the emotional weight of the moment.

ramayan::7276.verse_sanskrit: पन्नगासुरगन्धर्वदेवमानुषराक्षसैः । । 34510 । । अशक्यस्तव वैदेहि भर्ता जेतुं न संशयः ।
ramayan::7276.verse_hindi: O Vaidehi there is no doubt that pannagas, asuras, gandharvas, gods, men or even demons cannot defeat him.
ramayan::7276.english_translation: O Vaidehi, there is no doubt that your husband cannot be defeated by pannagas, asuras, gandharvas, gods, men, or even demons.
ramayan::7276.translation_literal: पन्नगासुरगन्धर्वदेवमानुषराक्षसैः (by serpents, asuras, gandharvas, gods, men, and demons) / अशक्यः (impossible) / तव (your) / वैदेहि (Vaidehi) / भर्ता (husband) / जेतुं (to conquer) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::7276.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7276.essence: Rama's strength is beyond every enemy Sita can imagine.
ramayan::7276.simple_meaning: Lakshmana reassures Sita that Rama cannot be conquered by any being, from gods to demons.
ramayan::7276.simple_insight: Fear loosens when someone you love is larger than the danger.
ramayan::7276.detailed_meaning: Sita is grieving and afraid in the forest. Lakshmana answers her fear by naming every kind of being imaginable and saying none can defeat Rama. He is trying to steady her heart by restoring trust in Rama's strength.
ramayan::7276.modern_relevance: You are waiting for a message after a hard night, and your mind keeps inventing worst-case endings. This verse reminds you that panic grows fastest where trust has gone thin.
ramayan::7276.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of collapse to confidence in protection.

ramayan::7277.verse_sanskrit: देवि देवमनुष्येषु गन्धर्वेषु पतत्रिषु । । 34511 । । राक्षसेषु पिशाचेषु किन्नरेषु मृगेषु च । दानवेषु च घोरेषु स न विद्येत शोभने । । 34512 । । यो रामं प्रतियुध्येत समरे वासवोपमम् ।
ramayan::7277.verse_hindi: O brilliant Devi  none  among gods or men, gandharvas, birds or goblins kinnaras, wild animals or dreadful demons can encounter Rama in war.
ramayan::7277.english_translation: O brilliant Devi, none among gods or men, gandharvas, birds, goblins, kinnaras, wild animals, or dreadful demons can face Rama in war.
ramayan::7277.translation_literal: देवि (O देवी) / देव-मनुष्येषु (among gods and men) / गन्धर्वेषु (among gandharvas) / पतत्रिषु (among birds) / राक्षसेषु (among demons) / पिशाचेषु (among goblins) / किन्नरेषु (among kinnaras) / मृगेषु (among wild animals) / च (and) / दानवेषु (among dreadful demons) / च (and) / घोरेषु (terrible ones) / सः (he) / न (not) / विद्येत (would be found) / शोभने (O lovely one) / यः (who) / रामम् (Rama) / प्रतियुध्येत (would fight against) / समरे (in battle) / वासवोपमम् (Indra-like)
ramayan::7277.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7277.essence: No force in any realm can match Rama in battle.
ramayan::7277.simple_meaning: Lakshmana says that no being in any realm could stand against Rama in battle.
ramayan::7277.simple_insight: Some protection is beyond measure; you do not need to prove it again and again.
ramayan::7277.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is answering Sita’s fear in the forest. He insists that Rama is beyond defeat, naming every kind of being to show the scale of that certainty. The verse strengthens his promise, but it is still part of a larger exchange.
ramayan::7277.modern_relevance: When you are trying to calm someone who is spiralling, you may reach for absolute reassurance. This is that moment: not a teaching, but a forceful promise meant to steady a frightened heart.
ramayan::7277.insight: It reinforces certainty by listing every possible challenger and dismissing them all.

ramayan::7278.verse_sanskrit: अवध्यस्समरे रामो नैवं त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि । । 34513 । । न त्वामस्मिन्वने हातुमुत्सहे राघवं विना ।
ramayan::7278.verse_hindi: Rama is indestructible in war. It is not proper for you to say what you said. When he is not here I do not wish to leave you alone here in the forest.
ramayan::7278.english_translation: Rama is indestructible in war. It is not proper for you to say what you said. When he is not here I do not wish to leave you alone here in the forest.
ramayan::7278.translation_literal: अवध्यः (indestructible) / समरे (in battle) / रामः (Rama) / न (not) / एवम् (thus) / त्वम् (you) / वक्तुम् (to say) / अर्हसि (are fit) / न (not) / त्वाम् (you) / अस्मिन् (in this) / वने (forest) / हातुम् (to abandon) / उत्सहे (I am willing) / राघवम् (Raghava) / विना (without)
ramayan::7278.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7278.essence: True loyalty refuses to leave the vulnerable alone.
ramayan::7278.simple_meaning: Rama is said to be unbeatable in battle, and the speaker refuses to leave Sita alone in the forest without him.
ramayan::7278.simple_insight: Love shows up as protection, not just words.
ramayan::7278.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the speaker answers Sita's doubts by insisting that Rama cannot be overcome in battle. But the real weight of the verse is personal: without Rama present, the speaker will not leave Sita exposed in that lonely place.
ramayan::7278.modern_relevance: You are about to walk away from someone vulnerable after a hard conversation, but something in you says no. Not because you can fix everything — because leaving them alone would be wrong.
ramayan::7278.insight: It shifts loyalty from argument to presence: when someone is exposed, staying matters more than proving a point.

ramayan::7279.verse_sanskrit: अनिवार्यं बलं तस्य बलैर्बलवतामपि । । 34514 । । त्रिभिर्लोकैस्समुद्युक्तैस्सेश्वरैरपि सामरैः ।
ramayan::7279.verse_hindi: He cannot be stopped by the strength of the mighty, or by Indra supported by gods or by the wellequipped armies of all the three worlds.
ramayan::7279.english_translation: He cannot be stopped by the strength of the mighty, or by Indra supported by the gods, or by the well-equipped armies of all the three worlds.
ramayan::7279.translation_literal: अनिवार्यम् (unstoppable) / बलम् (strength) / तस्य (of him) / बलैः (by the strengths) / बलवताम् (of the powerful) / अपि (even) / त्रिभिः (by the three) / लोकैः (worlds) / समुद्युक्तैः (assembled) / स इश्वरैः (with lords) / अपि (even) / सामरैः (with the gods)
ramayan::7279.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7279.essence: No force in the three worlds can overpower him.
ramayan::7279.simple_meaning: His force cannot be checked, not even by the strongest beings or by all the armies of the three worlds.
ramayan::7279.simple_insight: Some power is so complete that resistance only proves how little it can be moved.
ramayan::7279.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the speaker is defending Rama's unmatched strength after hearing fear about leaving him. The claim is not a teaching about conduct but a dramatic reassurance: no force in the cosmos can overpower Rama here.
ramayan::7279.modern_relevance: When you are afraid of one person, one deadline, or one confrontation, your mind can make the threat feel cosmic. This verse cuts that fear down: not every danger is as absolute as it feels.
ramayan::7279.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to proportion, reminding you that fear often exaggerates what can actually harm you.

ramayan::7280.verse_sanskrit: हृदयं निर्वृतं तेऽस्तुसन्तापस्त्यज्यतामयम् । । 34515 । । आगमिष्यति ते भर्ता श्रीघ्रं हत्वा मृगोत्तमम् ।
ramayan::7280.verse_hindi: May your heart be relieved (of this fear)  Give up this grief. Your husband will soon return with the excellent deer killed.
ramayan::7280.english_translation: May your heart be relieved of this fear. Give up this grief. Your husband will soon return with the excellent deer killed.
ramayan::7280.translation_literal: हृदयं (heart) / निर्वृतं (relieved, at ease) / ते (your) / अस्तु (may it be) / सन्तापः (grief, burning pain) / त्यज्यताम् (be given up) / अयम् (this) / आगमिष्यति (will come back) / ते (your) / भर्ता (husband) / श्रीघ्रम् (soon) / हत्वा (having killed) / मृगोत्तमम् (the best deer)
ramayan::7280.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7280.essence: False comfort can hide the beginning of ruin.
ramayan::7280.simple_meaning: The speaker tries to calm Sita, saying her fear and grief should end because Rama will soon return after killing the deer.
ramayan::7280.simple_insight: Comfort can sound certain even when disaster is already near.
ramayan::7280.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita grows uneasy after Rama goes after the golden deer. Someone tries to soothe her by promising that Rama will return quickly with the deer slain. The reassurance is tragically false, making this a moment of deceptive calm before abduction.
ramayan::7280.modern_relevance: You get a reassuring text: “I’m on my way.” You breathe again, not knowing the delay is already turning into a different kind of loss.
ramayan::7280.insight: It shows how fragile relief becomes when it rests on a false promise.

ramayan::7281.verse_sanskrit: न च तस्य स्वरो व्यक्तं मायया केन चित्कृतः । गन्धर्वनगरप्रख्या माया सा तस्य रक्षसः । । 34516 । ।
ramayan::7281.verse_hindi: Surely it is not his voice. It is contrived by some ones illusory power. It is the illusion created by that demon, like the city of the gandharvas. (which does not exist.)
ramayan::7281.english_translation: Surely it is not his voice. It is a trick of illusion created by that demon, like a city of the gandharvas that seems real but does not exist.
ramayan::7281.translation_literal: न (not) / च (and not) / तस्य (his) / स्वरः (voice) / व्यक्तम् (clearly) / मायया (by illusion) / केनचित् (by someone) / कृतः (made) / गन्धर्वनगरप्रख्या (like the city of the gandharvas) / माया (illusion) / सा (that) / तस्य (his) / रक्षसः (of the demon)
ramayan::7281.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7281.essence: What sounds familiar can still be a trap.
ramayan::7281.simple_meaning: The sound Sita hears is not truly Rama’s voice. It is a false appearance, a deceptive trick made by Ravana.
ramayan::7281.simple_insight: Not every familiar voice is safe to trust.
ramayan::7281.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita hears a voice that seems to be Rama’s. The speaker here corrects that hope: the sound is only Ravana’s deception, as unreal as a shimmering city in the sky. It sets up the trap that follows.
ramayan::7281.modern_relevance: You hear a message that sounds exactly like someone you trust, but something feels off. That small doubt can save you from a costly mistake.
ramayan::7281.insight: It trains you to question appearances before you react.

ramayan::7282.verse_sanskrit: न्यासभूतासि वैदेहि न्यस्ता मयि महात्मना । । 34517 । । रामेण त्वं वरारोहे न त्वां त्यक्तुमिहोत्सहे ।
ramayan::7282.verse_hindi: O best of women Vaidehi  great Rama has entrusted your safty to me. I do not wish to leave you here alone.
ramayan::7282.english_translation: O Vaidehi, the noble Rama entrusted you to me. I do not wish to leave you here alone.
ramayan::7282.translation_literal: न्यासभूता (entrusted as a trust) / असि (you are) / वैदेहि (O Vaidehi) / न्यस्ता (entrusted) / मयि (to me) / महात्मना (by the great-souled one) / रामेण (by Rama) / त्वं (you) / वरारोहे (O fair-browed one) / न (not) / त्वाम् (you) / त्यक्तुम् (to abandon) / इह (here) / उत्सहे (I am willing)
ramayan::7282.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7282.essence: Being entrusted with someone makes leaving them a moral failure.
ramayan::7282.simple_meaning: Lakshmana says Sita was placed in his care by Rama, so he will not abandon her there.
ramayan::7282.simple_insight: Real loyalty means staying when leaving would be easier.
ramayan::7282.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita hears a voice that sounds like Rama and fears the worst. Lakshmana reassures her that Rama entrusted her to him, and that he cannot walk away from that responsibility.
ramayan::7282.modern_relevance: A friend leaves you in someone’s care before a hard night, and that person stays when it would be easier to step away. Honor is shown in that choice.
ramayan::7282.insight: It shifts duty from abstract promise to concrete protection of someone placed in your care.

ramayan::7283.verse_sanskrit: कृतवैराश्च वैदेहि वयमेतैर्निशाचरैः । । 34518 । । खरस्य निधनादेव जनस्थानवधं प्रति ।
ramayan::7283.verse_hindi: O Vaidehi since the killing of Khara and the residents of Janasthana we have developed enmity with the demons.
ramayan::7283.english_translation: O Vaidehi, ever since Khara was slain and Janasthana was destroyed, we have become enemies of these night-roamers.
ramayan::7283.translation_literal: कृतवैराः (made into enemies) / च (and) / वैदेहि (O Vaidehi) / वयम् (we) / एतैः (with these) / निशाचरैः (night-roamers) / खरस्य (of Khara) / निधनात् (from the killing) / एव (indeed) / जनस्थानवधं (the destruction of Janasthana) / प्रति (because of)
ramayan::7283.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7283.essence: Old wounds turn into new enemies.
ramayan::7283.simple_meaning: The speakers tell Sita that their conflict with the demons began after Khara was killed and Janasthana was destroyed.
ramayan::7283.simple_insight: Some enmities are born from violence and never fully disappear.
ramayan::7283.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the companions explain to Sita why the night-roaming demons are now hostile. They trace the hatred back to Rama’s killing of Khara and the destruction of Janasthana, turning a local victory into a larger feud.
ramayan::7283.modern_relevance: A small act of retaliation can ripple outward long after the original event is over. What seemed like one finished conflict can become a lasting pattern of hostility.
ramayan::7283.insight: It shows how one violent act can harden an entire relationship into open enmity.

ramayan::7284.verse_sanskrit: राक्षसा विविधा वाचो विसृजन्ति महावने । । 34519 । । हिंसाविहारा वैदेहि न चिन्तयितुमर्हसि ।
ramayan::7284.verse_hindi: These demons wander about tormenting others and spreading rumours of all kinds.
ramayan::7284.english_translation: These demons roam the great forest, speaking in many voices. Vaidehi, they live for violence; you should not worry about them.
ramayan::7284.translation_literal: राक्षसाः (demons) / विविधाः (various) / वाचः (words, voices) / विसृजन्ति (let loose, utter) / महावने (in the great forest) / हिंसाविहाराः (those whose play is violence) / वैदेहि (Vaidehi) / न (not) / चिन्तयितुम् (to worry) / अर्हसि (you are fit, should)
ramayan::7284.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7284.essence: Loud threats are still only threats.
ramayan::7284.simple_meaning: Lakshmana is telling Sita not to fear the demons. He says they roam the forest, speak in many ways, and are used to violence.
ramayan::7284.simple_insight: Fear shrinks when you remember the threat is loud, not all-powerful.
ramayan::7284.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is trying to steady Sita after warning her about the dangers around them. He describes the demons as violent forest-dwellers who spread many kinds of talk, then tells her not to let them trouble her mind.
ramayan::7284.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with nasty speculation, and your mind starts running ahead of the facts. This verse reminds you that not every loud voice deserves your fear.
ramayan::7284.insight: It shifts attention from imagined danger to the speaker's violent nature and empty noise.

ramayan::7285.verse_sanskrit: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्ता सा क्रुद्धा संरक्तलोचना । । 34520 । । अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यवादिनम् ।
ramayan::7285.verse_hindi: Addressed thus by Lakshmana, Sita got mighty angry. Her eyes turned red and she spoke harshly to truthful Lakshmana
ramayan::7285.english_translation: Addressed thus by Lakshmana, Sita got mighty angry. Her eyes turned red and she spoke harshly to truthful Lakshmana.
ramayan::7285.translation_literal: लक्ष्मणेन (by Lakshmana) / एवम् (thus) / उक्ता (addressed) / सा (she) / क्रुद्धा (angry) / संरक्त-लोचना (with reddened eyes) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / परुषं (harsh) / वाक्यम् (speech) / लक्ष्मणम् (to Lakshmana) / सत्य-वादिनम् (truth-speaking)
ramayan::7285.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7285.essence: Pain can turn a truthful warning into a harsh exchange.
ramayan::7285.simple_meaning: Lakshmana's words anger Sita, and she answers him sharply.
ramayan::7285.simple_insight: Even noble people can speak from hurt when fear and grief are pressed too hard.
ramayan::7285.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshmana tries to explain the danger around them to Sita. His warning lands badly. Sita, already shaken by Rama's absence, flares in anger and answers him harshly, setting up the painful exchange that follows.
ramayan::7285.modern_relevance: You hear a warning when you are already exhausted, and it lands like an accusation. The reply comes sharper than you meant, because fear is already in the room.
ramayan::7285.insight: It shows how distress can distort even truthful speech into conflict.

ramayan::7286.verse_sanskrit: अनार्याकरणारम्भ नृशंस कुलपांसन । । 34521 । । अहं तव प्रियं मन्ये रामस्य व्यसनं महत् ।
ramayan::7286.verse_hindi: O ignoble, cruel Lakshmana, you are a disgrace to your family. I think this great disaster of Rama is a pleasure to you.
ramayan::7286.english_translation: O ignoble, cruel Lakshmana, you are a disgrace to your family. I think this great disaster of Rama is a pleasure to you.
ramayan::7286.translation_literal: अनार्य-करण-आरम्भ (ignoble in conduct) / नृशंस (cruel) / कुल-पांसन (disgrace to the family) / अहम् (I) / तव (your) / प्रियम् (pleasure) / मन्ये (I think) / रामस्य (of Rama) / व्यसनम् (misfortune) / महत् (great)
ramayan::7286.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7286.essence: Fear can make you accuse the very person trying to protect you.
ramayan::7286.simple_meaning: Sita angrily accuses Lakshmana of being cruel and dishonourable, and says Rama's suffering seems to please him.
ramayan::7286.simple_insight: Pain can make even love sound like accusation.
ramayan::7286.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has already been warned about the dangers around her. Lakshmana's words have struck her in fear and anger, and she lashes back at him, accusing him of cruelty and of secretly enjoying Rama's misfortune.
ramayan::7286.modern_relevance: A tense conversation can twist fear into blame. When someone feels cornered, they may attack the person closest to them, even if that person is trying to help.
ramayan::7286.insight: It shows how fear distorts judgment and turns protection into suspicion.

ramayan::7287.verse_sanskrit: रामस्य व्यसनं दृष्ट्वा तेनैतानि प्रभाषसे । । 34522 । । नैतच्चित्रं सपत्नेषु पापं लक्ष्मण यद्भवेत् । त्वद्विधेषु नृशंसेषु नित्यं प्रच्छन्नचारिषु । । 34523 । ।
ramayan::7287.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana,do you speak such words seeing the disaster of Rama?  No wonder that cruel men who always move like you in disguise will thus resort to sinful action against rivals.
ramayan::7287.english_translation: O Lakshmana, do you speak such words seeing Rama's disaster? No wonder that cruel men who move in disguise always resort to sinful action against rivals.
ramayan::7287.translation_literal: रामस्य (of Rama) / व्यसनं (disaster) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तेन (by that) / एतानि (these) / प्रभाषसे (you speak) । नैतत् (not this) / चित्रं (surprising) / सपत्नेषु (among rivals) / पापं (evil) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / यत् (that) / भवेत् (may be) । त्वद्विधेषु (in those like you) / नृशंसेषु (cruel) / नित्यं (always) / प्रच्छन्नचारिषु (moving in disguise) ।
ramayan::7287.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7287.essence: Fear makes even loyalty look like treachery.
ramayan::7287.simple_meaning: Sita accuses Lakshmana of speaking cruelly while seeing Rama's misfortune, and says such hidden, hostile behavior is no surprise from enemies.
ramayan::7287.simple_insight: Hurt can turn suspicion sharp, making every word sound like betrayal.
ramayan::7287.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has already been pushed into fear and anger. Lakshmana's words only deepen her suspicion, and she lashes out, reading his speech as the work of an enemy. This verse is part of her accusation, not a finished teaching.
ramayan::7287.modern_relevance: A tense message lands at the worst possible time, and you read contempt into every line. In a frightened mind, even care can look like attack.
ramayan::7287.insight: It shows how fear can distort interpretation and turn a trusted person into a suspected enemy.

ramayan::7288.verse_sanskrit: सुदुष्टस्त्वं वने राममेकमेकोऽनुगच्छसि । मम हेतोः प्रतिच्छन्नः प्रयुक्तोभरतेन वा । । 34524 । ।
ramayan::7288.verse_hindi: You are very wicked. You are hiding your true identity, and employed by Bharata, you are following Rama in the forest as he is alone.
ramayan::7288.english_translation: You are very wicked. You are hiding your true identity, and, sent by Bharata, you are following Rama in the forest while he is alone.
ramayan::7288.translation_literal: सुदुष्टः (very wicked) / त्वम् (you) / वने (in the forest) / रामम् (Rama) / एकम् (alone) / एकः (alone) / अनुगच्छसि (you follow) / मम (my) / हेतोः (for the sake) / प्रतिच्छन्नः (disguised, hidden) / प्रयुक्तः (sent, employed) / भरतेन (by Bharata) / वा (or)
ramayan::7288.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7288.essence: A suspicious mind turns loyalty into evidence of betrayal.
ramayan::7288.simple_meaning: Ravana accuses Lakshmana of being a hidden agent, sent by Bharata to follow Rama alone in the forest.
ramayan::7288.simple_insight: Suspicion can twist loyalty into conspiracy in the mind that cannot trust.
ramayan::7288.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana is already speaking from jealousy and deceit. Seeing Lakshmana near Rama, he assumes hidden motives and turns brotherly loyalty into a sinister plot. The verse is one step in his attempt to undermine trust before making his move.
ramayan::7288.modern_relevance: When you are already hurt, even ordinary care can look like manipulation. A mind full of suspicion turns every loyal act into a hidden agenda.
ramayan::7288.insight: It shows how a corrupted mind projects its own schemes onto others.

ramayan::7289.verse_sanskrit: तन्नसिध्यति सौमित्रे तव वा भरतस्य वा । कथमिन्दीवरश्यामं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणम् । । 34525 । । उपसंश्रित्य भर्तारं कामयेयं पृथग्जनम् ।
ramayan::7289.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana such intention of yours or even of Bharatas will not be fulfilled. I have held the hands of Rama who has eyes like the lotus petal, who has the complexion of the blue lotus. How can I prefer some other man?
ramayan::7289.english_translation: O Lakshmana, such intention of yours or even Bharata's will not be fulfilled. I have held the hand of Rama, whose eyes are like lotus petals and whose complexion is like the blue lotus. How can I prefer another man?
ramayan::7289.translation_literal: तत् (that) / न (not) / सिध्यति (succeeds) / सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra, Lakshmana) / तव (your) / वा (or) / भरतस्य (of Bharata) / वा (or) / कथम् (how) / इन्दीवर-श्यामम् (blue-lotus-hued) / पद्म-पत्र-निभ-ईक्षणम् (lotus-petal-like-eyed) / उपसंश्रित्य (having taken refuge in) / भर्तारम् (husband/master) / कामयेयम् (would desire) / पृथग्जनम् (another man)
ramayan::7289.speaker: Surpanakha
ramayan::7289.essence: Once the heart has chosen, every other offer falls away.
ramayan::7289.simple_meaning: She says Lakshmana and Bharata cannot succeed. She has already chosen Rama and cannot desire another man.
ramayan::7289.simple_insight: Some choices close every other door. Love becomes unmistakable when it is no longer negotiable.
ramayan::7289.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Surpanakha answers Lakshmana with sharp certainty. She says Rama has already won her desire, and neither Lakshmana nor Bharata can change that. The verse turns attraction into refusal: she has chosen, and that choice now governs her.
ramayan::7289.modern_relevance: You know that moment when someone keeps trying to redirect your heart, but the answer is already settled? This is that firmness — the point where preference becomes commitment.
ramayan::7289.insight: It shifts the mind from casual attraction to irreversible commitment.

ramayan::7290.verse_sanskrit: समक्षं तव सौमित्रे प्राणांस्त्यक्षे न संशयः । रामं विना क्षणमपि न हि जीवामि भूतले । । 34526 । ।
ramayan::7290.verse_hindi: I will undoubtedly give up my life in your presence.I will not live even for a moment on earth without Rama, O son of Sumitra
ramayan::7290.english_translation: I will undoubtedly give up my life in your presence. I will not live even for a moment on earth without Rama, O son of Sumitra.
ramayan::7290.translation_literal: समक्षं (in the presence) / तव (of you) / सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra) / प्राणान् (life-breaths) / त्यक्षे (I will give up) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / रामं (Rama) / विना (without) / क्षणम् (for a moment) / अपि (even) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / जीवामि (I live) / भूतले (on the earth)
ramayan::7290.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7290.essence: Rama’s absence makes life unbearable; that is how complete her love is.
ramayan::7290.simple_meaning: Sita says she would rather die than live even briefly without Rama. Her bond with him is so complete that life itself has no meaning apart from his presence.
ramayan::7290.simple_insight: Love can become so total that separation feels like erasure.
ramayan::7290.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is speaking under pressure to Lakshmana after harsh words and suspicion. She answers with absolute clarity: if Rama is absent, life itself has no hold on her. The verse shows the depth of her devotion and grief.
ramayan::7290.modern_relevance: You’ve sat in a quiet room after a breakup, staring at your phone, knowing one absence has changed everything. Sita names that kind of emptiness without softening it.
ramayan::7290.insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to total dependence, showing how love can define the whole meaning of living.

ramayan::7291.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्तः परुषं वाक्यं सीतया रोमहर्षणम् । । 34527 । । अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणस्सीतां प्राञ्जलिर्विजितेन्द्रियः ।
ramayan::7291.verse_hindi: The selfcontrolled Lakshmana with folded palms replied to Sitas harsh, horripilating words:
ramayan::7291.english_translation: The self-controlled Lakshmana, with folded palms, replied to Sita’s harsh, hair-raising words.
ramayan::7291.translation_literal: इत्युक्तः (having been spoken to thus) / परुषम् (harsh) / वाक्यम् (speech) / सीतया (by Sita) / रोमहर्षणम् (hair-raising) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / सीताम् (to Sita) / प्राञ्जलिः (with folded palms) / विजितेन्द्रियः (one who has conquered the senses)
ramayan::7291.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7291.essence: Self-mastery lets you answer pain without becoming cruel.
ramayan::7291.simple_meaning: Lakshmana answers Sita respectfully, even after hearing her painful words.
ramayan::7291.simple_insight: Even in hurt, he keeps his restraint and dignity.
ramayan::7291.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has spoken sharply to Lakshmana after rejecting his plea. Lakshmana, though shaken, stands before her with folded hands and self-mastery. This verse marks his controlled reply before he explains himself.
ramayan::7291.modern_relevance: You get blamed in a tense conversation and feel the heat rise. This is the moment to keep your hands open, your voice steady, and answer without losing yourself.
ramayan::7291.insight: It teaches you to respond with restraint instead of matching hurt with hurt.

ramayan::7292.verse_sanskrit: उत्तरं नोत्सहे वक्तुं दैवतं भवती मम । । 34528 । । वाक्यमप्रतिरूपं तु न चित्रं स्त्रीषु मैथिलि । स्वभावस्त्वेष नारीणामेवं लोकेषु दृश्यते । । 34529 । ।
ramayan::7292.verse_hindi: O princess from Mithila, I do not want to use such harsh words. To me you are a deity (worthy of adoration). It is not surprising that women of the world use such undeserving words. It is their nature.
ramayan::7292.english_translation: O princess from Mithila, I do not want to use such harsh words. To me you are worthy of reverence. It is not surprising that women of the world speak in ways that are unbecoming; that is how their nature appears in the world.
ramayan::7292.translation_literal: उत्तरं (reply) / न (not) / उत्सहे (I wish) / वक्तुं (to speak) / दैवतं (a deity; worthy of reverence) / भवती (you) / मम (to me) / वाक्यम् (speech) / अप्रतिरूपं (unseemly, unbecoming) / तु (but) / न (not) / चित्रम् (surprising) / स्त्रीषु (among women) / मैथिलि (O princess of Mithila) / स्वभावः (nature) / तु (indeed) / एषः (this) / नारीणाम् (of women) / एवम् (thus) / लोकेषु (in the world) / दृश्यते (is seen)
ramayan::7292.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7292.essence: Restraint and resentment can live in the same sentence.
ramayan::7292.simple_meaning: Lakshmana refuses to answer Sita with more cruelty. He says he sees her as worthy of reverence, though he also repeats a harsh generalisation about women.
ramayan::7292.simple_insight: Even in anger, speech can reveal restraint, respect, and damage all at once.
ramayan::7292.detailed_meaning: Sita has just spoken to Lakshmana with cutting words, accusing him of abandoning Rama. Folded in grief and anger, Lakshmana answers carefully. He tries to hold back harsher speech, but his reply still carries resentment and a sweeping judgment about women.
ramayan::7292.modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you start a reply, stop, and realise your next sentence could wound for years. Restraint matters, but so does the bias hidden inside it.
ramayan::7292.insight: It shows how partial self-control can still carry prejudice, even when the speaker is trying not to escalate.

ramayan::7293.verse_sanskrit: विमुक्तधर्माश्चपलास्तीक्ष्णा भेदकराः स्त्रियः । न सहे हीदृशं वाक्यं वैदेहि जनकात्मजे । । 34530 । । श्रोत्रयोरुभयोर्मेद्य तप्तनाराचसन्निभम् ।
ramayan::7293.verse_hindi: Women devoid dharma are fickle and inconsistent. They use sharp, piercing words. O daughter of Janaka, O princess from Videha, your words pierce my ears like redhot darts.I cannot tolerate them.
ramayan::7293.english_translation: Women devoid of dharma are fickle and inconsistent. They use sharp, piercing words. O daughter of Janaka, O princess from Videha, your words pierce my ears like red-hot darts. I cannot tolerate them.
ramayan::7293.translation_literal: विमुक्तधर्माः (devoid of dharma) / चपलाः (fickle) / तीक्ष्णाः (sharp) / भेदकराः (divisive) / स्त्रियः (women) / न (not) / सहे (I endure) / हीदृशम् (such) / वाक्यम् (speech) / वैदेहि (O Vaidehi) / जनकात्मजे (daughter of Janaka) / श्रोत्रयोः (of the ears) / उभयोः (both) / मे (my) / द्युतम् (piercing) / तप्तनाराचसन्निभम् (like red-hot arrows)
ramayan::7293.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7293.essence: Painful words can make even restraint sound like accusation.
ramayan::7293.simple_meaning: Lakshmana says he cannot bear Sita's harsh words. He describes them as painfully sharp and says such speech is like red-hot arrows in his ears.
ramayan::7293.simple_insight: When hurt turns into speech, even love can feel attacked.
ramayan::7293.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has spoken sharply to Lakshmana, and he answers with hurt pride and restraint. He insists he is not speaking cruelly, but defending himself against words that feel unbearable. The exchange deepens the emotional fracture before Rama's return.
ramayan::7293.modern_relevance: A text arrives after midnight, and you read it twice because the tone stings more than the content. Before you answer, you can feel how quickly hurt becomes a weapon.
ramayan::7293.insight: It shows how wounded pride can turn a conversation into a clash of injuries instead of understanding.

ramayan::7294.verse_sanskrit: उपशृण्वन्तु मे सर्वे साक्षिभूता वनेचराः । । 34531 । । न्यायवादी यथान्यायमुक्तोऽहं परुषं त्वया ।
ramayan::7294.verse_hindi: I speak what is just while you use harsh and unjust words. Let all beings who move in the forest bear witness.
ramayan::7294.english_translation: Let all the forest-dwellers hear me as witnesses. I have spoken justly; you have spoken harshly and unfairly.
ramayan::7294.translation_literal: उपशृण्वन्तु (let hear) / मे (my) / सर्वे (all) / साक्षिभूता (become witnesses) / वनेचराः (forest-dwellers) / न्यायवादी (speaking justly) / यथान्यायम् (according to justice) / उक्तः (spoken) / अहम् (I) / परुषम् (harshly) / त्वया (by you)
ramayan::7294.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7294.essence: A mind in denial calls itself just and the other person harsh.
ramayan::7294.simple_meaning: Ravana calls the forest beings to witness his claim that he has spoken fairly and Sita has spoken harshly.
ramayan::7294.simple_insight: Pride often turns a refusal to listen into a claim of justice.
ramayan::7294.detailed_meaning: In the Ashoka grove, Ravana keeps pressing Sita after she rejects him. He tries to recast himself as the reasonable one and her words as cruelty, appealing to the forest-dwellers as witnesses. The verse is part of his escalating attempt to justify coercion.
ramayan::7294.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a tense conversation and then says, 'Be honest, I was calm and you were the one being rude.' The need to win the story matters more than the truth.
ramayan::7294.insight: It exposes how self-justification can disguise pressure as fairness.

ramayan::7295.verse_sanskrit: धिक्त्वामद्य प्रणश्य त्वं यन्मामेवं विशङ्कसे । स्त्रीत्वलदुष्टं स्वभावेन गुरुवाक्ये व्यवस्थितम् । । 34532 । ।
ramayan::7295.verse_hindi: Fie upon you. Like a woman of wicked nature you doubt me when I stood firm by my brothers words. You will go to ruin.
ramayan::7295.english_translation: Fie upon you. May you perish today. Why do you distrust me like this? By nature I stand firm in my brother's word.
ramayan::7295.translation_literal: धिक् (fie upon) / त्वाम् (you) / अद्य (today) / प्रणश्य (perish) / त्वम् (you) / यत् (why) / माम् (me) / एवम् (thus) / विशङ्कसे (distrust) / स्त्रीत्वलदुष्टम् (corrupted by womanhood) / स्वभावेन (by nature) / गुरुवाक्ये (in the elder/brother's word) / व्यवस्थितम् (firmly placed / standing)
ramayan::7295.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7295.essence: Wounded pride turns doubt into insult.
ramayan::7295.simple_meaning: Ravana angrily curses Sita for doubting him and insists that he stands by his brother's word.
ramayan::7295.simple_insight: Anger often turns fear into accusation before the truth is even heard.
ramayan::7295.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to force Sita into submission after she rejects him. Her distrust wounds his pride, and he answers with insult and a curse, revealing how quickly wounded ego turns into cruelty.
ramayan::7295.modern_relevance: Someone questions your promise in the middle of a tense argument, and you snap back with contempt instead of answering clearly. The real injury is not the doubt — it's the pride underneath it.
ramayan::7295.insight: It shows how ego protects itself by attacking the other person's character instead of addressing the concern.

ramayan::7296.verse_sanskrit: गमिष्ये यत्र काकुत्स्थ स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु वरानने । । 34533 । । रक्षन्तु त्वां विशालाक्षि समग्रा वनदेवताः ।
ramayan::7296.verse_hindi: O beautiful lady, I will go to Rama wherever he may be. Be happy. O largeeyed one, may  all the deities of the forest protect you.
ramayan::7296.english_translation: O beautiful lady, I will go to Rama wherever he may be. Be happy. O large-eyed one, may all the deities of the forest protect you.
ramayan::7296.translation_literal: गमिष्ये (I will go) / यत्र (wherever) / काकुत्स्थ (Rama, descendant of Kakutstha) / स्वस्ति (well-being) / ते (to you) / अस्तु (may it be) / वरानने (O beautiful-faced one) / रक्षन्तु (may protect) / त्वाम् (you) / विशालाक्षि (O large-eyed one) / समग्रा (all) / वनदेवताः (forest deities)
ramayan::7296.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7296.essence: He chooses Rama over comfort and leaves Sita with a blessing.
ramayan::7296.simple_meaning: Lakshmana tells Sita he will go wherever Rama is and asks the forest powers to protect her.
ramayan::7296.simple_insight: Love can look like leaving, not clinging.
ramayan::7296.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Lakshmana answers Sita after harsh words and suspicion. He declares that his place is with Rama, not beside comfort, and leaves Sita under the care of the forest powers. The moment carries the pain of separation inside devotion.
ramayan::7296.modern_relevance: You have to step away from someone you care about, even while wishing them safety. The hardest goodbye is the one that still honors your duty.
ramayan::7296.insight: It shifts loyalty from personal comfort to chosen duty, even when that choice creates separation.

ramayan::7297.verse_sanskrit: निमित्तानि च घोराणि यानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति मे । । 34534 । । अपि त्वां सह रामेण पश्येयं पुनरागतः । न वेत्येतन्न जानामि वैदेहि जनकात्मजे । । 34535 । ।
ramayan::7297.verse_hindi: O daughter of Janaka O princess from Videha, I see dreadful omens. I do not know whether I will see you when I am back with Rama.
ramayan::7297.english_translation: O daughter of Janaka, O princess of Videha, I see dreadful omens. I do not know whether I will see you again when I return with Rama.
ramayan::7297.translation_literal: निमित्तानि (omens) / च (and) / घोराणि (terrible) / यानि (which) / प्रादुर्भवन्ति (are appearing) / मे (to me) / अपि (whether) / त्वां (you) / सह (with) / रामेण (with Rama) / पश्येयम् (I may see) / पुनरागतः (having returned again) / न वा (or not) / इति एतत् (this) / न जानामि (I do not know) / वैदेहि (O daughter of Videha) / जनकात्मजे (O daughter of Janaka)
ramayan::7297.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7297.essence: He speaks as if goodbye may already have begun.
ramayan::7297.simple_meaning: Lakshmana senses bad omens and tells Sita he does not know whether he will return and see her again with Rama.
ramayan::7297.simple_insight: Sometimes the heart knows danger before the mind can explain it.
ramayan::7297.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is speaking to Sita before leaving the forest. He has already promised to go after Rama, but now he sees signs of danger in the world around him. His words carry fear, urgency, and the ache of possible separation.
ramayan::7297.modern_relevance: You lock the door before leaving for a long trip and suddenly feel it: the strange quiet, the bad feeling, the sense that this goodbye may last longer than you want.
ramayan::7297.insight: It teaches you to name risk honestly instead of pretending everything is certain.

ramayan::7298.verse_sanskrit: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्ता सा रुदन्ती जनकात्मजा । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं तीव्रं बाष्पपरिप्लुता । । 34536 । ।
ramayan::7298.verse_hindi: At these words of Lakshmana Sita started crying. With eyes filled with tears she replied with harshness :
ramayan::7298.english_translation: At these words of Lakshmana, Sita began to weep. With tears streaming, she answered with fierce words.
ramayan::7298.translation_literal: लक्ष्मणेन (by Lakshmana) / एवम् (thus) / उक्ता (spoken to) / सा (she) / रुदन्ती (weeping) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / ततः (then) / वाक्यम् (speech) / तीव्रम् (fierce) / बाष्पपरिप्लुता (flooded with tears)
ramayan::7298.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7298.essence: Pain rises first as tears, then as fierce words.
ramayan::7298.simple_meaning: Sita breaks into tears when Lakshmana speaks, then answers with intense emotion.
ramayan::7298.simple_insight: Grief can sharpen the voice; pain does not always make a person silent.
ramayan::7298.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana has just offered to go find Rama and admitted the bad omens around him. Sita, already overwhelmed by separation, cannot hold back her tears. This verse marks the moment before her desperate reply.
ramayan::7298.modern_relevance: You hear one more line that confirms your fear, and your throat tightens before you can even answer.
ramayan::7298.insight: It shows how distress can move straight from tears into urgent speech.

ramayan::7299.verse_sanskrit: गोदावरीं प्रवेक्ष्यामि विना रामेण लक्ष्मण । अबन्धिष्येऽथवा त्यक्ष्ये विषमे देहमात्मनः । । 34537 । ।
ramayan::7299.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana without Rama I will drown myself in Godavari or hang myself or leap from a cliff into death.
ramayan::7299.english_translation: O Lakshmana, without Rama I will enter the Godavari, or I will bind myself, or I will abandon this body on a dangerous cliff.
ramayan::7299.translation_literal: गोदावरीं (to the Godavari) / प्रवेक्ष्यामि (I will enter) / विना (without) / रामेण (Rama) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / अबन्धिष्ये (I will bind myself) / अथवा (or) / त्यक्ष्ये (I will abandon) / विषमे (on a dangerous) / देहम् (body) / आत्मनः (of myself)
ramayan::7299.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7299.essence: Rama's absence feels worse than death to her.
ramayan::7299.simple_meaning: Sita says she cannot bear life without Rama. She would rather die than live separated from him.
ramayan::7299.simple_insight: Separation can feel so complete that survival itself seems empty.
ramayan::7299.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana has warned Sita that bad omens surround Rama's return. Grief spills over into defiance: Sita declares that without Rama she would rather destroy her body than continue alone. Her love is absolute, and the pain is immediate.
ramayan::7299.modern_relevance: You get a message saying the person you rely on may not come back, and your chest tightens before your mind can speak. Sita gives that panic a voice.
ramayan::7299.insight: It reveals how love can become the measure of whether life still feels livable.

ramayan::7300.verse_sanskrit: पिबाम्यहं विषं तीक्ष्णं प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम् । न त्वहं राघवादन्यं पदापि पुरुषं स्पृशे । । 34538 । ।
ramayan::7300.verse_hindi: I will drink deadly poison or enter fire and die, but will not touch any other man even with my feet.
ramayan::7300.english_translation: I will drink deadly poison or enter fire and die, but will not touch any other man even with my feet.
ramayan::7300.translation_literal: पिबामि (I will drink) / अहम् (I) / विषम् (poison) / तीक्ष्णम् (deadly) / प्रवेक्ष्यामि (I will enter) / हुताशनम् (fire) / न (not) / तु (but) / अहम् (I) / राघवादन्यम् (other than Rama) / पदापि (even with the foot) / पुरुषम् (man) / स्पृशे (touch)
ramayan::7300.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7300.essence: Love can become a vow so strong that even death feels easier.
ramayan::7300.simple_meaning: Sita declares that she would rather die than break her fidelity to Rama by touching any other man.
ramayan::7300.simple_insight: Integrity can be stronger than fear, even when everything around you is collapsing.
ramayan::7300.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana has urged Sita to leave the shelter of the grove. In her anguish, she answers with fierce clarity: she would rather face poison or fire than violate her loyalty to Rama. Her fidelity becomes her strength.
ramayan::7300.modern_relevance: Someone pressures you to compromise your boundaries, then acts shocked when you refuse. In that moment, Sita's answer reminds you that self-respect can be louder than panic.
ramayan::7300.insight: It shifts the mind from survival at any cost to fidelity at any cost.

ramayan::7301.verse_sanskrit: इति लक्ष्मणमाक्रुश्य सीता दुःखसमन्विता । पाणिभ्यां रुदती दुःखादुदरं प्रजघान ह । । 34539 । ।
ramayan::7301.verse_hindi: Thus Sita cried in distress, sadly hitting her belly with both the hands, blaming Lakshmana (all the time).
ramayan::7301.english_translation: Thus Sita cried in distress, blaming Lakshmana, and struck her own belly with both hands.
ramayan::7301.translation_literal: इति (thus) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / आक्रुश्य (having reproached) / सीता (Sita) / दुःखसमन्विता (filled with grief) / पाणिभ्याम् (with both hands) / रुदती (weeping) / दुःखात् (from sorrow) / उदरम् (the belly) / प्रजघान (struck) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7301.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7301.essence: Grief overwhelms reason before comfort can reach her.
ramayan::7301.simple_meaning: Overcome by grief, Sita lashes out at Lakshmana and beats her own body in despair.
ramayan::7301.simple_insight: Grief can become physical when the heart can no longer hold it.
ramayan::7301.detailed_meaning: Sita has just spoken of death and separation from Rama. In that raw moment, she blames Lakshmana and strikes her own belly with both hands, showing how unbearable exile and fear have become before Lakshmana tries to soothe her.
ramayan::7301.modern_relevance: You read one message too late, and the mind starts spiraling. The body feels the panic before the words can explain it.
ramayan::7301.insight: It shows how overwhelming sorrow can turn inward and erupt as self-striking, not calm speech.

ramayan::7302.verse_sanskrit: तामार्तरूपां विमना रुदन्तीं सौमित्रिरालोक्य विशालनेत्राम् । आश्वासयामास न चैव भर्तु स्तं भ्रातरंकिञ्चिदुवाच सीता । । 34540 । ।
ramayan::7302.verse_hindi: Saumitri saw  the largeeyed, dejected Sita crying in distress.He pacified and consoled her but she did not say anything at all to her husbands brother.
ramayan::7302.english_translation: Saumitri saw the large-eyed, dejected Sita crying in distress. He pacified and consoled her, but she did not say anything at all to her husband's brother.
ramayan::7302.translation_literal: ताम् (her) / आर्तरूपाम् (in a distressed state) / विमना (downcast, dejected) / रुदन्तीम् (weeping) / सौमित्रिः (Saumitri) / आलोक्य (having seen) / विशालनेत्राम् (large-eyed) / आश्वासयामास (consoled, reassured) / न (not) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / भर्तुः (of her husband) / स्तम् (brother) / भ्रातरम् (brother) / अ-किञ्चित् (nothing) / उवाच (said) / सीता (Sita)
ramayan::7302.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7302.essence: Grief can leave even comfort unanswered.
ramayan::7302.simple_meaning: Lakshmana sees Sita in deep distress and tries to comfort her, but she says nothing to him.
ramayan::7302.simple_insight: Silence can carry more pain than words can fix.
ramayan::7302.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has just spoken harshly to Lakshmana in grief. He sees her crying, tries to soothe her, and waits for a response. But she remains silent, caught in hurt and fear, and the moment hangs in painful stillness.
ramayan::7302.modern_relevance: You reach out after a fight, trying to calm the room, and the other person gives you nothing back. The silence hurts because it says the wound is still open.
ramayan::7302.insight: It shifts attention from argument to emotional rupture, showing how distress can block speech itself.

ramayan::7303.verse_sanskrit: तया परुषमुक्तस्तु कुपितो राघवानुजः । स विकाङ्क्षन्भृशं रामं प्रतस्थे नचिरादिव । । 3461 । ।
ramayan::7303.verse_hindi: Lakshmana, brother of Rama, hurt by the harsh words of Sita, hastened with Ramas wellbeing in mind.
ramayan::7303.english_translation: Lakshmana, the younger brother of Rama, angered by Sita's harsh words, set out quickly, thinking only of Rama's welfare.
ramayan::7303.translation_literal: तया (by that) / परुष-मुक्तः (spoken harshly to) / तु (indeed) / कुपितः (angered) / राघव-अनुजः (Raghava's younger brother) / सः (he) / विकाङ्क्षन् (desiring) / भृशम् (greatly) / रामम् (Rama) / प्रतस्थे (set out) / नचिरात् इव (as if without delay)
ramayan::7303.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7303.essence: Personal injury fades when loyalty is stronger.
ramayan::7303.simple_meaning: Lakshmana, stung by Sita's harsh words, left at once, still thinking of Rama's safety.
ramayan::7303.simple_insight: Even hurt feelings can be overtaken by loyalty.
ramayan::7303.detailed_meaning: Sita has just spoken in grief, and Lakshmana has been blamed. He feels the sting, but he does not stay to defend himself. Instead, he turns at once toward Rama's welfare, and that split second opens the door for Ravana's approach.
ramayan::7303.modern_relevance: You were just criticized by someone you were trying to help. The impulse to withdraw is real, but loyalty can still move you toward what matters most.
ramayan::7303.insight: It shows how devotion can outrun personal hurt and keep the mind fixed on the larger duty.

ramayan::7304.verse_sanskrit: तदासाद्य दशग्रीवः क्षिप्रमन्तरमास्थितः । अभिचक्राम वैदेहीं परिव्राजकरूपधृक् । । 3462 । ।
ramayan::7304.verse_hindi: The tenheaded Ravana who was in hiding assumed the guise of a wandering mendicant and approached Sita.
ramayan::7304.english_translation: The ten-headed Ravana, hiding nearby, approached Sita in the guise of a wandering mendicant.
ramayan::7304.translation_literal: तदा (then) / आसाद्य (having approached) / दशग्रीवः (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / अन्तरम् (an opening, a chance) / आस्थितः (having taken) / अभिचक्राम (approached) / वैदेहीम् (Sita, daughter of Videha) / परिव्राजक-रूप-धृक् (wearing the form of a wandering mendicant)
ramayan::7304.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7304.essence: Harm moves in only after it finds an opening.
ramayan::7304.simple_meaning: Ravana seizes a chance and comes toward Sita disguised as a wandering ascetic.
ramayan::7304.simple_insight: Deception often arrives wearing the face of safety.
ramayan::7304.detailed_meaning: Sita is alone and shaken after Lakshmana leaves. Ravana spots the opening immediately. He hides his true form, takes on the dress of a wandering mendicant, and moves toward her. The verse sets up the trap, not the full deception.
ramayan::7304.modern_relevance: Someone shows up gentle, respectful, and harmless right after your guard drops. The danger is not loud; it often arrives polished and well-timed.
ramayan::7304.insight: It trains you to notice how opportunism waits for vulnerability.

ramayan::7305.verse_sanskrit: श्लक्ष्णकाषायसंवीतश्शिखी छत्री उपानही । वामे चांसेऽवसज्याथ शुभे यष्टिकमण्डलू । । 3463 । । परिव्राजकरूपेण वैदेहीमन्वपद्यत ।
ramayan::7305.verse_hindi: And then Ravana wearing fine orange robes, with hair knotted on the head, carrying a parasol, wearing sandals, hanging a kamandalu (waterpot), and a staff on the auspicious left shoulder walked towards Vaidehi like a mendicant.
ramayan::7305.english_translation: And then Ravana, wearing fine orange robes, with hair knotted on the head, carrying a parasol, wearing sandals, and hanging a waterpot and staff from his left shoulder, approached Vaidehi in the guise of a mendicant.
ramayan::7305.translation_literal: श्लक्ष्ण-काषाय-संवीतः (clad in fine orange robes) / शिखी (with knotted hair) / छत्री (with a parasol) / उपानही (with sandals) / वामे चांसे (on the left shoulder) / अवसज्य (hanging) / अथ (then) / शुभे यष्टि-कमण्डलू (a staff and waterpot) / परिव्राजक-रूपेण (in the form of a mendicant) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / अन्वपद्यत (approached)
ramayan::7305.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7305.essence: False holiness can be the perfect disguise for harm.
ramayan::7305.simple_meaning: Ravana disguises himself as a wandering ascetic and moves toward Sita. The verse is mainly about his appearance and approach, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::7305.simple_insight: A dangerous intention can hide behind the right clothes.
ramayan::7305.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita is alone. Ravana has already chosen deceit, and now he completes the disguise: robes, staff, waterpot, sandals, even the look of a renunciant. The verse sets up the moment before he speaks to her.
ramayan::7305.modern_relevance: Someone shows up polished, calm, and harmless, but the feeling in your body says otherwise. This verse catches the moment before charm turns into manipulation.
ramayan::7305.insight: It shows how appearance can be used to mask predatory intent.

ramayan::7306.verse_sanskrit: तामाससादातिबलो भ्रातृभ्यां रहितां वने । । 3464 । । रहितां चन्द्रसूर्याभ्यां सन्ध्यामिव महत्तमः ।
ramayan::7306.verse_hindi: Mighty Ravana approached Sita deprived of both the brothers, Like darkness encompasses the evening twilight in the absence of the Sun and the Moon.
ramayan::7306.english_translation: Mighty Ravana approached Sita, who was alone in the forest, like deep twilight without the sun and moon.
ramayan::7306.translation_literal: ताम् (her) / आससाद (approached) / अति-बलः (very mighty) / भ्रातृभ्याम् (from the two brothers) / रहिताम् (deprived, alone) / वने (in the forest) / रहिताम् (deprived) / चन्द्र-सूर्याभ्याम् (of the moon and sun) / सन्ध्याम् इव (like twilight) / महत्तमः (great darkness)
ramayan::7306.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7306.essence: Power becomes menace when protection is absent.
ramayan::7306.simple_meaning: Ravana came upon Sita while she was alone in the forest. The verse compares her helpless isolation to twilight swallowed by darkness when the sun and moon are gone.
ramayan::7306.simple_insight: Isolation can make danger feel larger than it is.
ramayan::7306.detailed_meaning: Ravana has disguised himself and reached Sita in the forest. Rama and Lakshmana are absent, and the verse slows to show the moral imbalance of the moment: a powerful predator facing a woman left alone. The image of twilight swallowed by darkness prepares the threat.
ramayan::7306.modern_relevance: You step away for one minute and the room changes. A message arrives, a voice gets too close, and the absence of support suddenly feels physical.
ramayan::7306.insight: It frames vulnerability as the real force in the scene, not Ravana's strength.

ramayan::7307.verse_sanskrit: तामपश्यत्ततो बालां रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम् । । 3465 । । रोहिणीं शशिना हीनां ग्रहवद्भृशदारुणः ।
ramayan::7307.verse_hindi: The extremely cruel Ravana saw the illustrious young wife of Rama just as Ketu looks at Rohini star in the absence of the Moon.
ramayan::7307.english_translation: The extremely cruel Ravana saw the illustrious young wife of Rama just as Ketu looks at Rohini star in the absence of the Moon.
ramayan::7307.translation_literal: ताम् (her) / अपश्यत् (saw) / ततः (then) / बालाम् (young woman) / रामपत्नीम् (Rama's wife) / यशस्विनीम् (illustrious) / रोहिणीम् (Rohini) / शशिना (by the Moon) / हीनाम् (deprived of) / ग्रहवत् (like a planet) / भृश-दारुणः (extremely cruel)
ramayan::7307.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7307.essence: The first look already carries the violence to come.
ramayan::7307.simple_meaning: Ravana finally sees Sita, Rama's wife, in the forest. The line compares his gaze to a dark, threatening force fixed on a vulnerable star.
ramayan::7307.simple_insight: Some moments are not neutral seeing — they are the beginning of harm.
ramayan::7307.detailed_meaning: Ravana, disguised as a wandering ascetic, has reached Sita in the forest while Rama and Lakshmana are absent. Valmiki pauses on the instant of first sight: the powerful king sees the unprotected woman, and the scene turns ominous before a single word is spoken.
ramayan::7307.modern_relevance: A stranger keeps staring after the room goes quiet, and everyone feels the shift before anything is said. The danger was already present in the looking.
ramayan::7307.insight: It teaches you to notice predatory attention before it becomes action.

ramayan::7308.verse_sanskrit: तमुग्रतेजःकर्माणं जनस्थानरूहा द्रुमाः । । 3466 । । समीक्ष्य सम्प्रकम्पन्ते न प्रवाति च मारुतः ।
ramayan::7308.verse_hindi: Seeing the ferocious Ravana, the huge trees at Janasthana shook vidently. Even the wind ceased to blow.
ramayan::7308.english_translation: Seeing the fierce Ravana, the trees of Janasthana trembled, and the wind did not blow.
ramayan::7308.translation_literal: तम् (him) / उग्र-तेजः-कर्माणम् (one whose deeds are fierce in power) / जनस्थान-रूहाः (the trees of Janasthana) / द्रुमाः (trees) / समीक्ष्य (having seen) / सम्प्रकम्पन्ते (tremble greatly) / न (not) / प्रवाति (blows) / च (and) / मारुतः (the wind)
ramayan::7308.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7308.essence: His violence is so heavy that nature itself flinches.
ramayan::7308.simple_meaning: Ravana's presence is so terrifying that even trees tremble and the wind stops.
ramayan::7308.simple_insight: Some presences feel so violent that the whole world seems to recoil.
ramayan::7308.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Ravana has just approached Sita after the brothers are absent. The forest itself reacts to his fierce force: the trees shake and the wind falls still. This is a scene-setting verse, building fear before the next movement.
ramayan::7308.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the conversation dies. Before anyone speaks, everyone has already felt the pressure in the air.
ramayan::7308.insight: It heightens Ravana as an overwhelming threat before the encounter even begins.

ramayan::7309.verse_sanskrit: शीघ्रस्रोताश्च तं दृष्ट्वा वीक्षन्तं रक्तलोचनम् । । 3467 । । स्तिमितं गन्तुमारेभे भयाद्गोदावरी नदी ।
ramayan::7309.verse_hindi: Seeing Ravana with his bloodred eyes, the swiftflowing river Godavari slowed down out of fear.
ramayan::7309.english_translation: Seeing Ravana with his bloodred eyes, the swiftflowing river Godavari slowed down out of fear.
ramayan::7309.translation_literal: शीघ्रस्रोताः (swift-flowing) / च (and) / तम् (him) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / वीक्षन्तम् (looking) / रक्तलोचनम् (red-eyed) / स्तिमितम् (became still) / गन्तुम् (to go) / आरेभे (began) / भयात् (out of fear) / गोदावरी (Godavari) / नदी (river)
ramayan::7309.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7309.essence: His fearsome presence unsettles even the river before he moves.
ramayan::7309.simple_meaning: Even the Godavari river seems to freeze in fear when it sees Ravana’s red-eyed, terrifying gaze.
ramayan::7309.simple_insight: Some presences disturb the whole world around them before they even act.
ramayan::7309.detailed_meaning: Ravana has entered the forest near Janasthana while seeking Sita. The trees have already shuddered at his presence. Now even the Godavari, usually swift and moving, seems to lose its flow before his fearsome gaze. The scene builds Ravana’s menace before his next move.
ramayan::7309.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the conversation thins before you speak. The tension is not in your words yet — it is in what your presence has already announced.
ramayan::7309.insight: It shows how inner violence can radiate outward and unsettle the environment before any direct action begins.

ramayan::7310.verse_sanskrit: रामस्य त्वन्तरप्रेप्सुर्दशग्रीवस्तदन्तरे । । 3468 । । उपतस्थे च वै देहीं भिक्षुरूपेण रावणः ।
ramayan::7310.verse_hindi: The tenheaded Ravana who was waiting for Ramas absence now got it. Disguised as a mendicant he stepped toward to where Sita was.
ramayan::7310.english_translation: Ravana, waiting for Rama to be away, seized the opening and approached Sita in the guise of a mendicant.
ramayan::7310.translation_literal: रामस्य (of Rama) / तु (indeed) / अन्तरप्रेप्सुः (seeking the interval/absence) / दशग्रीवः (the ten-necked one, Ravana) / तदन्तरे (in that gap) / उपतस्थे (approached) / च (and) / वै (indeed) / देहीं (the woman, Sita) / भिक्षुरूपेण (in the form of a mendicant) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7310.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7310.essence: Wrongness slips in when vigilance is gone.
ramayan::7310.simple_meaning: Ravana notices Rama is absent and uses that chance to approach Sita while disguised as a holy beggar.
ramayan::7310.simple_insight: A dangerous person often waits for the exact moment your guard is down.
ramayan::7310.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana sees his opening. Rama is away, Sita is alone, and the enemy chooses deception over force. This verse is a turning point in the abduction sequence, showing the trap being set rather than the full act itself.
ramayan::7310.modern_relevance: You step away for one minute, and someone uses that gap to push a boundary. The danger is not always force; sometimes it is timing, disguise, and patience.
ramayan::7310.insight: It teaches you to notice how harm often enters through opportunity and appearance, not open attack.

ramayan::7311.verse_sanskrit: अभव्यो भव्यरूपेण भर्तारमनुशोचतीम् । । 3469 । । अभ्यवर्तत वैदेहीं चित्रामिव शनैश्चरः ।
ramayan::7311.verse_hindi: The evilminded Ravana in the guise of a holy man, like Saturn moves towards Chitra
ramayan::7311.english_translation: The evil-minded Ravana, disguised as a holy man, moved toward Vaidehi, like Saturn approaching Chitra.
ramayan::7311.translation_literal: अभव्यः (evil-minded) / भव्यरूपेण (with a holy appearance) / भर्तारम् (her husband) / अनुशोचतीम् (one who was grieving) / अभ्यवर्तत (moved toward) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / चित्राम् (Chitra) / इव (like) / शनैश्चरः (Saturn)
ramayan::7311.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7311.essence: A sacred-looking mask can hide predatory intent.
ramayan::7311.simple_meaning: Ravana approaches Sita while pretending to be a holy man. The verse compares his slow approach to Saturn moving toward a star.
ramayan::7311.simple_insight: A false appearance can hide a harmful intent.
ramayan::7311.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has finally found the moment he was waiting for: Rama is absent, and Sita is alone in grief. He comes dressed as a mendicant, using holiness as a mask. The verse captures his stealthy approach before he speaks.
ramayan::7311.modern_relevance: Someone shows up gentle, careful, and polished, but something in the room feels off. You notice the mismatch between the face they wear and the motive moving underneath it.
ramayan::7311.insight: It teaches you to watch actions, not appearances.

ramayan::7312.verse_sanskrit: स पापो भव्यरूपेण तृणैः कूप इवावृतः । । 34610 । । अतिष्ठत्प्रेक्ष्य वैदेहीं रामपत्निं यशस्विनीम् ।
ramayan::7312.verse_hindi: Just like a well is concealed by an overgrowth of grass, Ravana guised as a holy man stood looking at illustrious Sita, the wife of Rama.
ramayan::7312.english_translation: The wicked Ravana, hidden by a holy disguise like a well covered with grass, stood staring at illustrious Sita, Rama's wife.
ramayan::7312.translation_literal: सः (he) / पापः (wicked one) / भव्यरूपेण (with a holy appearance) / तृणैः (with grasses) / कूपः इव (like a well) / आवृतः (covered) / अतिष्ठत् (stood) / प्रेक्ष्य (looking at) / वैदेहीम् (Sita of Videha) / रामपत्निम् (Rama's wife) / यशस्विनीम् (illustrious)
ramayan::7312.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7312.essence: Deception becomes most dangerous when it looks harmless.
ramayan::7312.simple_meaning: Ravana hides his true nature behind a holy look and watches Sita from close by.
ramayan::7312.simple_insight: A false appearance can be more dangerous than open force.
ramayan::7312.detailed_meaning: In the forest hut, Sita sits alone while Rama and Lakshmana are away. Ravana has taken the disguise of a mendicant and moved close enough to watch her. This verse pauses on the danger of his deception before the approach continues.
ramayan::7312.modern_relevance: Someone arrives at your door with a calm voice, careful clothes, and perfect manners. The danger is not loud; it is concealed.
ramayan::7312.insight: It teaches you to notice when charm is covering intent.

ramayan::7313.verse_sanskrit: शुभां रुचिरदन्तोष्ठीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् । । 34611 । । आसीनां पर्णशालायां बाष्पशोकाभिपीडिताम् । स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं पीतकौशेयवासिनीम् । । 34612 । । अभ्यगच्छत वैदेहीं दुष्टचेता निशाचरः ।
ramayan::7313.verse_hindi: The wicked demon came close to that auspicious princess from Videha sitting in the cottage Her face was like the full moon. Her teeth and lips were lovely. She was clad in yellow silk. Her eyes were like lotus petals tormented by tears of grief.
ramayan::7313.english_translation: The wicked demon approached Vaidehi, who was sitting in the cottage, her face like the full moon, her teeth and lips lovely, her eyes like lotus petals, and her mind pressed by tears and sorrow.
ramayan::7313.translation_literal: शुभाम् (auspicious) / रुचिर-दन्त-ओष्ठीम् (lovely-teethed-and-lipped) / पूर्ण-चन्द्र-निभ-आनाम् (full-moon-like-faced) / आसीनाम् (sitting) / पर्ण-शालायाम् (in the leaf-hut) / बाष्प-शोक-अभिपीडिताम् (pressed by tears and grief) / सः (he) / ताम् (her) / पद्म-पलाश-अक्षीम् (lotus-petal-eyed) / पीत-कौशेय-वासिनीम् (yellow-silk-clad) / अभ्यगच्छत (approached) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / दुष्ट-चेता (wicked-minded) / निशाचरः (night-roaming being)
ramayan::7313.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7313.essence: Cruel intent often approaches beauty first.
ramayan::7313.simple_meaning: Ravana, filled with evil intent, approached Sita where she sat in the forest hut, beautiful yet overwhelmed by sorrow.
ramayan::7313.simple_insight: Beauty and vulnerability can coexist, and cruelty often moves toward both.
ramayan::7313.detailed_meaning: In the forest hut at Panchavati, Sita sits grieving in exile, still radiant despite her tears. Ravana, disguised and driven by dark desire, steps closer. The verse slows the scene so the reader feels the danger before he speaks.
ramayan::7313.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with a polite smile while you are already exhausted and hurt. The danger is not always loud; sometimes it walks in beautifully dressed.
ramayan::7313.insight: It sharpens your awareness of predatory intent hidden behind charm and appearance.

ramayan::7314.verse_sanskrit: स मन्मथशराविष्टो ब्रह्मघोषमुदीरयन् । । 34613 । । अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं रहिते राक्षसाधिपः ।
ramayan::7314.verse_hindi: स मन्मथशराविष्टो ब्रह्मघोषमुदीरयन् । । 34613 । । अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं रहिते राक्षसाधिपः ।
ramayan::7314.english_translation: Ravana, overwhelmed by desire and speaking in a Brahmin-like voice, addressed her with a humble speech in the deserted place.
ramayan::7314.translation_literal: सः (he) / मन्मथ-शर-आविष्टः (pierced by the arrows of desire) / ब्रह्म-घोषम् (a Brahmin-like voice) / उदीरयन् (uttering) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / प्रश्रितम् (humble) / वाक्यम् (speech) / रहिते (in a deserted place) / राक्षस-अधिपः (the lord of the rakshasas)
ramayan::7314.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7314.essence: Desire can sound respectful while hiding its real aim.
ramayan::7314.simple_meaning: Ravana, consumed by desire, spoke to Sita in a soft, respectful tone in the lonely forest hut.
ramayan::7314.simple_insight: Charm can hide predatory intent; a gentle voice is not always a safe one.
ramayan::7314.detailed_meaning: Ravana has found Sita alone in the forest hut. Inflamed by desire, he disguises his approach in respectful speech. This verse marks the moment before he begins his deceitful attempt to win her trust.
ramayan::7314.modern_relevance: A polished message arrives in your inbox, full of respect and urgency. The tone feels safe, but the pressure underneath it is real. Not every gentle voice deserves your trust.
ramayan::7314.insight: It trains you to notice when courtesy is being used as a mask for manipulation.

ramayan::7315.verse_sanskrit: तामुत्तमां स्त्रियं लोके पद्महीनामिव श्रियम् । । 34614 । । विभ्राजमानां वपुषा रावणः प्रशशंस ह ।
ramayan::7315.verse_hindi: Sita was the most lovely lady of the world shining in beauty. She was like the goddess of wealth (Laxmi) without her lotus. Ravana praised her thus:
ramayan::7315.english_translation: Ravana praised that unmatched woman in the world, shining in beauty like wealth without its lotus.
ramayan::7315.translation_literal: ताम् (that) / उत्तमाम् (supreme, unmatched) / स्त्रियम् (woman) / लोके (in the world) / पद्महीनाम् (without a lotus) / इव (like) / श्रियम् (wealth, splendour) / विभ्राजमानाम् (shining) / वपुषा (with her body, in form) / रावणः (Ravana) / प्रशशंस (praised)
ramayan::7315.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7315.essence: Beauty is being used here as a doorway to coercion.
ramayan::7315.simple_meaning: Ravana looked at Sita and praised her unmatched beauty. The verse is part of his approach to her, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::7315.simple_insight: Some verses simply reveal the moment before a choice turns dangerous.
ramayan::7315.detailed_meaning: In the Ashoka grove, Ravana stands before Sita after approaching her alone. He is struck by her beauty and praises her as the most splendid woman in the world, like wealth missing its lotus. The line sets up his attempt to win her over.
ramayan::7315.modern_relevance: A person says the right words too smoothly in a quiet room, and you can feel the pressure before the request even comes.
ramayan::7315.insight: It frames the scene as seduction and threat, not reflection, so the next verse lands with full force.

ramayan::7316.verse_sanskrit: का त्वं काञ्चनवर्णाभे पीतकौशेयवासिनि । । 34615 । । कमलानां शुभां मालां पद्मिनीव हि बिभ्रती ।
ramayan::7316.verse_hindi: Who are you with a golden complexion, clad in yellow silk, and looking like a lotuspond and wearing an auspicious lotus garland?
