ramayan::7364.verse_sanskrit: लङ्कानाम समुद्रस्य मम मध्ये महापुरी । सागरेण परिक्षिस्ता निविष्टा नगमूर्धनि । । 34729 । ।
ramayan::7364.verse_hindi: My great city  called Lanka is on the peak of a mountain surrounded by, and in the middle of, the sea.
ramayan::7364.english_translation: My great city called Lanka is on the peak of a mountain, surrounded by the sea and set in its midst.
ramayan::7364.translation_literal: लङ्कानाम (of Lanka) / समुद्रस्य (of the sea) / मम (my) / मध्ये (in the middle) / महापुरी (great city) / सागरेण (by the sea) / परिक्षिस्ता (surrounded) / निविष्टा (situated) / नगमूर्धनि (on the mountain-peak)
ramayan::7364.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7364.essence: He tries to seduce with power by turning his city into a promise.
ramayan::7364.simple_meaning: Ravana describes Lanka as a great city set on a mountain peak, ringed by the sea.
ramayan::7364.simple_insight: Power often speaks by showing off what it owns.
ramayan::7364.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to dazzle Sita with the splendour and security of Lanka. He paints his city as vast, elevated, and unreachable, using its geography as proof of his power and as part of his pressure to win her over.
ramayan::7364.modern_relevance: Someone gives you a tour of their penthouse, their contacts, their status, and their security system, as if success itself should persuade you. Ravana is doing that here.
ramayan::7364.insight: It reveals how ego uses grandeur and possession to control the room.

ramayan::7365.verse_sanskrit: तत्र सीते मया सार्धं वनेषु विहरिष्यसि । न चास्यारण्यवासस्य स्पृहयिष्यसि भामिनि । । 34730 । ।
ramayan::7365.verse_hindi: O Sita, you can stroll with me in my pleasuregardens. O  beautiful lady, you will not like living in the forest (thereafter).
ramayan::7365.english_translation: O Sita, you can stroll with me in my pleasure gardens. O beautiful lady, you will not long for life in the forest.
ramayan::7365.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / सीते (O Sita) / मया (with me) / सार्धं (together) / वनेषु (in gardens/forests) / विहरिष्यसि (you will wander) / न (not) / च (and) / अस्य (of this) / अरण्य-वासस्य (forest dwelling) / स्पृहयिष्यसि (you will desire/long for) / भामिनि (O beautiful lady)
ramayan::7365.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7365.essence: Luxury is being offered as a trap, not a gift.
ramayan::7365.simple_meaning: Ravana tempts Sita with luxury and companionship, claiming she will forget the forest life if she joins him.
ramayan::7365.simple_insight: Charm can be used to disguise coercion.
ramayan::7365.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to seduce Sita in Lanka by painting a future of comfort, beauty, and ease. He offers himself, his city, and pleasure as a replacement for her exile with Rama. This line is part of his pressure, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7365.modern_relevance: Someone flatters you with comfort right after ignoring your boundaries. The promise sounds generous, but it is really a way to make refusal feel unreasonable.
ramayan::7365.insight: It reveals how persuasion can become manipulation when desire is used to override consent.

ramayan::7366.verse_sanskrit: पञ्च दास्यस्सहस्राणि सर्वाभरणभूषिताः । सीते परिचरिष्यन्ति भार्या भवसि मे यदि । । 34731 । ।
ramayan::7366.verse_hindi: O Sita  if you become my wife, five thousand female attendants adorned with all ornaments will attend on you.
ramayan::7366.english_translation: O Sita, if you become my wife, five thousand female attendants adorned with all ornaments will attend on you.
ramayan::7366.translation_literal: पञ्च (five) / दास्यः (female attendants) / सहस्राणि (thousands) / सर्वाभरणभूषिताः (adorned with all ornaments) / सीते (O Sita) / परिचरिष्यन्ति (will attend upon) / भार्या (wife) / भवसि (you become) / मे (my) / यदि (if)
ramayan::7366.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7366.essence: Luxury offered as bait cannot hide coercion.
ramayan::7366.simple_meaning: Ravana tempts Sita with luxury, promising her attendants and royal comfort if she becomes his wife.
ramayan::7366.simple_insight: Charm and comfort can be used as traps when someone wants control.
ramayan::7366.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to soften Sita's resistance by offering splendor instead of force: gardens, comfort, and thousands of attendants. The verse is part of his attempt to persuade her before her fierce reply.
ramayan::7366.modern_relevance: Someone praises your future with them by listing all the things they can give you — status, convenience, attention — while ignoring your refusal.
ramayan::7366.insight: It exposes how power often disguises coercion as generosity.

ramayan::7367.verse_sanskrit: रावणेनैवमुक्ता तु कुपिता जनकात्मजा । प्रत्युवाचानवद्याङ्गी तमनादृत्य राक्षसम् । । 34732 । ।
ramayan::7367.verse_hindi: Thus addressed by Ravana, Janaki, a lady of blemishless limbs, got enraged and replied without caring for the demon:
ramayan::7367.english_translation: Thus addressed by Ravana, Janaki, a lady of blemishless limbs, became enraged and replied without caring for the demon.
ramayan::7367.translation_literal: रावणेन (by Ravana) / एवम् (thus) / उक्ता (spoken to) / तु (indeed) / कुपिता (angered) / जनकात्मजा (Janaka's daughter) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / अनवद्याङ्गी (blemishless-limbed one) / तम् (to him) / अनादृत्य (without respecting) / राक्षसम् (the demon)
ramayan::7367.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7367.essence: Respect is not owed to someone using power to violate dignity.
ramayan::7367.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to tempt Sita with comfort and power, but she responds with anger and refuses to honor him.
ramayan::7367.simple_insight: Your dignity can stay intact even under pressure.
ramayan::7367.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just offered Sita luxury, attendants, and a life beside him. Instead of softening, she burns with anger and answers him as he deserves. This is the moment her inner strength becomes unmistakable.
ramayan::7367.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with flattery, pressure, or a deal that feels dirty. You do not owe them politeness when they are trying to buy your surrender.
ramayan::7367.insight: It teaches you to meet coercion with moral clarity, not compliance.

ramayan::7368.verse_hindi: I am devoted to Rama, my husband, who is unshakeable like a huge mountain, is comparable to lord Indra and is imperturbable like the mighty ocean.
ramayan::7368.english_translation: I am devoted to Rama, my husband, who is unshakeable like a huge mountain, comparable to Indra, and as imperturbable as the mighty ocean.
ramayan::7368.translation_literal: महागिरिमिव (like a great mountain) / अकम्प्यम् (unshakable) / महेन्द्रसदृशम् (like Mahendra/Indra) / पतिम् (husband) / महोदधिमिव (like the great ocean) / अक्षोभ्यम् (unperturbable) / अहम् (I) / राममनुव्रता (devoted to Rama)
ramayan::7368.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7368.essence: Devotion stays firm because it has already chosen.
ramayan::7368.simple_meaning: Sita declares her loyalty to Rama and describes him as steady, vast, and unmovable, like a mountain and the ocean.
ramayan::7368.simple_insight: Real devotion does not depend on comfort; it stays firm under pressure.
ramayan::7368.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just tried to tempt Sita with luxury and power. She answers by naming Rama's greatness and her own unwavering loyalty. In the enemy's palace, she refuses fear and turns the insult into a declaration of fidelity.
ramayan::7368.modern_relevance: Someone pressures you to trade loyalty for comfort, status, or safety. Sita's answer shows what it looks like to hold your ground without shouting: you remember who you belong to, and you do not move.
ramayan::7368.insight: It shifts loyalty from a feeling to a steady, chosen stance.

ramayan::7369.verse_hindi: I am the loyal wife of venerable Rama who is endowed with all excellences, a refuge to all like  a spreading banyan tree, and a votary of truth.
ramayan::7369.english_translation: I am devoted to Rama, my husband, who is endowed with all excellences, broad and sheltering like a banyan tree, and steadfast in truth.
ramayan::7369.translation_literal: सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नम् (endowed with all excellences) / न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलम् (broad and round like a banyan tree) / सत्यसन्धम् (steadfast in truth) / महाभागम् (great-souled, venerable) / अहम् (I) / रामम् (Rama) / अनुव्रता (devoted wife, faithful follower)
ramayan::7369.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7369.essence: Faithfulness becomes unbreakable when it rests on known greatness.
ramayan::7369.simple_meaning: Sita says she belongs to Rama, who is noble, all-accomplished, protective, and completely true to his word.
ramayan::7369.simple_insight: Love here is not sentiment; it is steadfast recognition of a man’s character.
ramayan::7369.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana presses Sita to abandon Rama. She answers by naming Rama’s qualities one by one: his excellence, his protective greatness, and his truthfulness. This verse deepens her refusal by showing why her loyalty cannot be shaken.
ramayan::7369.modern_relevance: Someone asks why you still trust the person others have given up on. You answer not with excuses, but with the exact qualities that made your trust real in the first place.
ramayan::7369.insight: It shifts loyalty from blind attachment to clear-eyed commitment grounded in character.

ramayan::7370.verse_sanskrit: महाबाहुं महोरस्कं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम् । नृसिंहं सिंहसङ्काशमहं राममनुव्रता । । 34735 । ।
ramayan::7370.verse_hindi: I am the faithful wife of the longarmed, broadchested  Rama,  a lion among men. His gait is the gait of an advancing, invincible lion.
ramayan::7370.english_translation: I am the faithful wife of Rama, the long-armed, broad-chested man who moves with a lion’s stride and looks like a lion among men.
ramayan::7370.translation_literal: महाबाहुम् (long-armed) / महोरस्कम् (broad-chested) / सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम् (moving with lion-like stride) / नृसिंहम् (lion among men) / सिंहसङ्काशम् (lion-like) / अहम् (I) / राममनुव्रता (faithful wife of Rama)
ramayan::7370.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7370.essence: Loyalty here rests on seeing strength and steadiness clearly.
ramayan::7370.simple_meaning: Sita praises Rama’s physical strength and fearless bearing, calling herself his devoted wife.
ramayan::7370.simple_insight: Love can see strength clearly and still choose loyalty without hesitation.
ramayan::7370.detailed_meaning: In this sequence, Sita is listing Rama’s qualities one by one: unshakeable, noble, strong, truthful, and now lion-like in body and movement. It is a praise of the man she chose and the steadiness of her devotion.
ramayan::7370.modern_relevance: You remember the person who made you feel safe: not just kind, but steady, strong, and unmistakably present.
ramayan::7370.insight: It shifts attention from abstract praise to the lived experience of trust in a partner.

ramayan::7371.verse_sanskrit: पूर्णचन्द्राननं रामं राजवत्सं जितेन्द्रियम् । पृथुकीर्तिं महात्मानमहं राममनुव्रता । । 34736 । ।
ramayan::7371.verse_hindi: I am the devoted wife of great Rama, whose face is like a fullmoon, who is the son of a king, who has conquered his senses and whose fame is widespread (on earth).
ramayan::7371.english_translation: I am the devoted wife of Rama, whose face is like the full moon, who is the son of a king, who has conquered his senses, and whose fame is spread far and wide.
ramayan::7371.translation_literal: पूर्णचन्द्राननम् (having a full-moon face) / रामम् (Rama) / राजवत्सम् (son of a king) / जितेन्द्रियम् (one who has conquered the senses) / पृथुकीर्तिम् (of wide fame) / महात्मानम् (great-souled) / अहम् (I) / राममनुव्रता (devoted wife to Rama)
ramayan::7371.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7371.essence: She measures a man by character, then refuses the lesser claim.
ramayan::7371.simple_meaning: Sita names Rama’s qualities to show why she belongs to him and why Ravana cannot claim her.
ramayan::7371.simple_insight: Love can be rooted in clear sight, not confusion.
ramayan::7371.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana by naming Rama’s virtues one by one: his beauty, royal birth, self-control, greatness, and fame. She is not pleading; she is drawing a line between the man she chose and the man who threatens her.
ramayan::7371.modern_relevance: Someone tries to flatter you into lowering your standards, and you quietly remember what real character looks like. Sita does not forget the difference.
ramayan::7371.insight: It shifts the mind from coercion to discernment: you can name what is worthy and refuse what is not.

ramayan::7372.verse_sanskrit: त्वं पुनर्जम्बुकस्सिंहीं मामिच्छसि सुदुर्लभाम् । नाहं शक्या त्वया स्प्रष्टुमादित्यस्य प्रभा यथा । । 34737 । ।
ramayan::7372.verse_hindi: You are a jackal, and you want a lioness like me who is difficult to win. I am like the Suns radiance whom you cannot even touch.
ramayan::7372.english_translation: You are a jackal, and you want a lioness like me, who is hard to win. I am like the radiance of the sun, which you cannot even touch.
ramayan::7372.translation_literal: त्वम् (you) / पुनः (again) / जम्बुकः (jackal) / सिंहीम् (lioness) / माम् (me) / इच्छसि (you desire) / सुदुर्लभाम् (hard to win) / न (not) / अहम् (I) / शक्या (able to be) / त्वया (by you) / स्प्रष्टुम् (to touch) / आदित्यस्य (of the sun) / प्रभा (radiance) / यथा (like)
ramayan::7372.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7372.essence: Wanting someone does not make you worthy of them.
ramayan::7372.simple_meaning: Sita rejects Ravana completely. She says he is unworthy of her and cannot touch her, just as no one can touch the sun’s radiance.
ramayan::7372.simple_insight: Dignity can be a boundary. Not every desire deserves access.
ramayan::7372.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana’s demand with sharp refusal. She compares herself to the sun’s radiance and him to a jackal, making clear that his desire does not grant him any right over her. The moment is a defense of her honor.
ramayan::7372.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing past your no, acting as if wanting you is the same as deserving you. Sita’s words remind you that desire is not entitlement.
ramayan::7372.insight: It teaches you to name the boundary clearly and refuse false claims to your attention, body, or trust.

ramayan::7373.verse_sanskrit: पादपान्काञ्चनान्नूनं बहून्पश्यसि मन्दभाक् । राघपस्य प्रियां भार्यां यस्त्वमिच्छसि रावण । । 34738 । ।
ramayan::7373.verse_hindi: O luckless Ravana  you want the beloved wife of Rama.You will, for sure, see golden trees. (which those close to death do).
ramayan::7373.english_translation: O luckless Ravana, you want the beloved wife of Rama. You will, for sure, see golden trees.
ramayan::7373.translation_literal: पादपान् (trees) / काञ्चनान् (golden) / नूनम् (surely) / बहून् (many) / पश्यसि (you see) / मन्दभाक् (luckless one) / राघवस्य (of Rama) / प्रियां (beloved) / भार्याम् (wife) / यः (who) / त्वम् (you) / इच्छसि (desire) / रावण (Ravana)
ramayan::7373.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7373.essence: Desire does not make the impossible yours.
ramayan::7373.simple_meaning: Sita mocks Ravana for desiring Rama's wife. She says his wish is as impossible as seeing golden trees.
ramayan::7373.simple_insight: Some desires are so blind they expose the person who wants them.
ramayan::7373.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana's coercion with sharp, fearless contempt. After declaring her devotion to Rama, she turns his desire into a humiliation, comparing it to an impossible sight. The verse is part of a taunting refusal, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7373.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing past your no, acting as if enough pressure will change reality. Sita's answer is the kind that draws a hard line without apology.
ramayan::7373.insight: It shows how to refuse violation with clarity, not confusion.

ramayan::7374.verse_sanskrit: क्षुधितस्य हि सिंहस्य मृगशत्रोस्तरस्विनः । आशीविषस्य मुखाद्दंष्ट्रामादातुमिच्छसि । । 34739 । ।
ramayan::7374.verse_hindi: You are seeking to pull the teeth from  the mouth of a hungry and powerful lion who is considered the enemy of the deer(which you are). You intend to pull the fang of a poisonous snake.
ramayan::7374.english_translation: You are trying to pull a fang from the mouth of a hungry, powerful lion, the enemy of deer. You are trying to seize a snake's tooth.
ramayan::7374.translation_literal: क्षुधितस्य (of the hungry) / हि (indeed) / सिंहस्य (of the lion) / मृगशत्रोः (of the enemy of deer) / तरस्विनः (powerful, fierce) / आशीविषस्य (of the poisonous snake) / मुखात् (from the mouth) / दंष्ट्राम् (fang, tooth) / आदातुम् (to take, to pull out) / इच्छसि (you desire)
ramayan::7374.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7374.essence: Desire turns foolish when it mistakes danger for opportunity.
ramayan::7374.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told that his desire is reckless and impossible. Trying to take Sita from Rama is like trying to pull a fang from a hungry lion or a poisonous snake.
ramayan::7374.simple_insight: Some dangers cannot be negotiated with. Pride makes them look conquerable until it is too late.
ramayan::7374.detailed_meaning: Sita is rebuking Ravana after he has tried to claim her. She piles up fierce images to show how impossible his plan is: he is facing not a harmless victim, but a force that will tear him apart if he reaches in.
ramayan::7374.modern_relevance: You keep pushing a boundary someone has already made clear. The more you treat their warning like bluff, the more dangerous your own move becomes.
ramayan::7374.insight: It warns you to read danger correctly before you act, instead of confusing desire with power.

ramayan::7375.verse_sanskrit: मन्दरं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं पाणिना हर्तुमिच्छसि । कालकूटं विषं पीत्वा स्वस्तिमान्गन्तुमिच्छसि । । 34740 । ।
ramayan::7375.verse_hindi: You are trying to carry the greatest of mountains, the Mandara, with one hand. You are wishing to go safe after drinking deadly poison (produced from the churning of the ocean).
ramayan::7375.english_translation: You are trying to carry the greatest of mountains, Mandara, with one hand. You are wishing to go safely after drinking deadly poison.
ramayan::7375.translation_literal: मन्दरं (Mandara) / पर्वतश्रेष्ठं (the greatest mountain) / पाणिना (with the hand) / हर्तुम् (to carry) / इच्छसि (you wish) / कालकूटं (deadly poison) / विषं (poison) / पीत्वा (having drunk) / स्वस्तिमान् (safe, unharmed) / गन्तुम् (to go) / इच्छसि (you wish)
ramayan::7375.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7375.essence: You cannot grab the unbearable and still come away unharmed.
ramayan::7375.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told that his desire is impossible and self-destructive, like lifting a mountain with one hand and surviving poison.
ramayan::7375.simple_insight: Some desires are not just risky — they are impossible to survive.
ramayan::7375.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned that taking Sita is not a bold act but a fatal overreach. The speaker piles up impossible images to show the scale of his delusion: he is reaching for what cannot be held and inviting destruction at the same time.
ramayan::7375.modern_relevance: You keep saying yes to one more impossible thing, as if force can make it safe. This is the moment before a collapse you can already feel coming.
ramayan::7375.insight: It shifts the mind from bravado to sober self-check: not every desire is worth the cost.

ramayan::7376.verse_sanskrit: अक्षि सूच्या प्रमृजसि जिह्वया लेक्षि च क्षुरम् । राघवस्य प्रियां भार्यां योऽधिगन्तुं त्वमिच्छसि । । 34741 । ।
ramayan::7376.verse_hindi: You wish to violate the loving wife of Rama. You are rubbing your eyes with a needle and licking the razor with your tongue.
ramayan::7376.english_translation: You wish to violate Rama's beloved wife. You are rubbing your eyes with a needle and licking a razor with your tongue.
ramayan::7376.translation_literal: अक्षि (eye) / सूच्या (with a needle) / प्रमृजसि (you rub) / जिह्वया (with the tongue) / लेक्षि (you lick) / च (and) / क्षुरम् (the razor) / राघवस्य (of Rama) / प्रियां (beloved) / भार्यां (wife) / यः (who) / अधिगन्तुम् (to obtain / to approach) / त्वम् (you) / इच्छसि (wish)
ramayan::7376.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7376.essence: Forbidden desire can be a form of self-harm.
ramayan::7376.simple_meaning: Trying to take Rama's wife is as foolish and self-harming as rubbing your eyes with a needle and licking a razor.
ramayan::7376.simple_insight: Some desires are not just wrong — they are self-destructive from the start.
ramayan::7376.detailed_meaning: In the enemy city, the warning continues to Ravana. The speaker piles up images of impossible, painful acts to show how insane it is to pursue Sita. This verse is one sharp link in that larger rebuke.
ramayan::7376.modern_relevance: You know that urge that would wreck your life, yet it still tempts you. This is that moment before the damage, when warning still sounds like insult.
ramayan::7376.insight: It turns desire into a clear self-injury, making the cost impossible to ignore.

ramayan::7377.verse_sanskrit: अवसज्य शिलां कण्ठे समुद्रं तर्तुमिच्छसि । सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ चोभौ पाणिभ्यां हर्तुमिच्छसि । । 34742 । । यो रामस्य प्रियां भार्यां प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छसि ।
ramayan::7377.verse_hindi: You want to assault Ramas dear wife. It is like girding a stone round the neck and trying to cross the sea.It is like intending to take the Sun and the Moon with both your hands.
ramayan::7377.english_translation: You want to assault Rama's dear wife. It is like tying a stone to your neck and trying to cross the sea. It is like trying to seize the Sun and the Moon with both hands.
ramayan::7377.translation_literal: अवसज्य (having tied) / शिलाम् (a stone) / कण्ठे (around the neck) / समुद्रम् (the sea) / तर्तुम् इच्छसि (you wish to cross) / सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ (the Sun and Moon) / च (and) / उभौ (both) / पाणिभ्याम् (with the hands) / हर्तुम् इच्छसि (you wish to seize) / योऽधिगन्तुम् इच्छसि (you who wish to obtain) / रामस्य (of Rama) / प्रियाम् (dear) / भार्याम् (wife) / प्रधर्षयितुम् (to violate)
ramayan::7377.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7377.essence: Desire can become so blind that it carries its own ruin.
ramayan::7377.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told that trying to violate Rama's wife is impossible and self-destructive. The image is of someone making a foolish, doomed attempt against something far beyond his reach.
ramayan::7377.simple_insight: Some actions are not just wrong — they are impossible to carry without ruining yourself.
ramayan::7377.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, the warnings around Ravana are sharpening into open contempt. The speaker piles up impossible images: crossing the sea with a stone tied to your neck, grabbing the Sun and Moon by hand. The point is not just that Sita is protected, but that Ravana's desire has become absurdly self-destructive.
ramayan::7377.modern_relevance: You already know that message you should not send, that boundary you should not cross, that person you should not corner. The urge may feel powerful; the consequences will be heavier.
ramayan::7377.insight: It turns reckless desire into a picture of guaranteed collapse, forcing restraint through shame and scale.

ramayan::7378.verse_sanskrit: अग्निं प्रज्वलितं दृष्ट्वा वस्त्रेणाहर्तुमिच्छसि । । 34743 । । काल्याणवृत्तां रामस्य यो भार्यांहर्तुमिच्छसि ।
ramayan::7378.verse_hindi: You intend to assaut the wife of Rama, who is a lady of virtuous conduct. You wish to hold blazing fire in your cloth.
ramayan::7378.english_translation: You intend to assault the wife of Rama, who is a woman of virtuous conduct. You wish to hold blazing fire in your cloth.
ramayan::7378.translation_literal: अग्निं (fire) / प्रज्वलितं (blazing) / दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / वस्त्रेण (with a cloth) / आहर्तुम् (to hold) / इच्छसि (you wish) / काल्याणवृत्तां (of virtuous conduct) / रामस्य (of Rama's) / यो (who) / भार्याम् (wife) / आहर्तुम् (to seize) / इच्छसि (you wish)
ramayan::7378.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7378.essence: Desire for what should not be taken destroys the taker first.
ramayan::7378.simple_meaning: Trying to take Rama’s righteous wife is as impossible and dangerous as holding blazing fire in a cloth.
ramayan::7378.simple_insight: Some acts burn the one who reaches for them first.
ramayan::7378.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a warning is being hurled at Ravana. The speaker piles up impossible images to show the folly of desiring Sita: crossing the sea with a stone, grabbing the sun and moon, now holding fire in cloth. The verse is one link in that escalating rebuke.
ramayan::7378.modern_relevance: You reach for something you know will ruin you, then call it desire. This verse strips away the glamour and shows the cost before the damage is done.
ramayan::7378.insight: It turns craving into a visible danger, not a private temptation.

ramayan::7379.verse_sanskrit: अयोमुखानां शूलानामग्रे चरितुमिच्छसि । । 34744 । । रामस्य सदृशीं भार्यां योऽधिगन्तुं त्वमिच्छसि ।
ramayan::7379.verse_hindi: You want to acquire Ramas worthy wife. You wish to walk on sharp ironheaded spear.
ramayan::7379.english_translation: You want to win Rama's worthy wife. You wish to walk onto the points of sharp iron spears.
ramayan::7379.translation_literal: अयोमुखानाम् (iron-tipped) / शूलानाम् (spears) / अग्रे (in front of) / चरितुम् (to walk) / इच्छसि (you wish) / रामस्य (Rama's) / सदृशीम् (worthy, like) / भार्याम् (wife) / यः (who) / अधिगन्तुम् (to obtain) / त्वम् (you) / इच्छसि (wish)
ramayan::7379.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7379.essence: What you want may already be the thing that wounds you.
ramayan::7379.simple_meaning: Wanting to take Rama's wife is as impossible and deadly as walking onto spear points.
ramayan::7379.simple_insight: Some desires are not just wrong; they are self-destroying from the start.
ramayan::7379.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is speaking in Lanka, condemning Ravana's desire for Sita. The verse is part of a chain of harsh comparisons meant to show that taking Rama's wife is not merely forbidden — it is like stepping into certain pain.
ramayan::7379.modern_relevance: You keep reaching for something that would cut you open if you got it. The warning is not moralistic; it is practical.
ramayan::7379.insight: It shifts desire from temptation to danger, making the cost impossible to ignore.

ramayan::7380.verse_sanskrit: यदन्तरं सिंहशृगालयोर्वने यदन्तरं स्यन्दिनिका समुद्रयोः । सुराग्र्य सौवीरकयोर्यदन्तरं तदन्तरं वै तव राघवस्य च । । 34745 । ।
ramayan::7380.verse_hindi: The difference between you and Rama is the difference between a jackal and a lion in the forest, between a ditch and the sea, and between sour gruel and the best of wines.
ramayan::7380.english_translation: The difference between you and Rama is the difference between a jackal and a lion in the forest, between a ditch and the sea, and between sour gruel and the best of wines.
ramayan::7380.translation_literal: यत्-अन्तरम् (the difference) / सिंह-शृगालयोः (between a lion and a jackal) / वने (in the forest) / यत्-अन्तरम् (the difference) / स्यन्दिनिका-समुद्रयोः (between a ditch and the sea) / सुराग्र्य-सौवीरकयोः (between the finest wine and sour gruel) / यत्-अन्तरम् (the difference) / तत्-अन्तरम् (that difference) / वै (indeed) / तव (between you) / राघवस्य (and Rama)
ramayan::7380.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7380.essence: Pride collapses when the real distance is named.
ramayan::7380.simple_meaning: The speaker says the gap between this person and Rama is enormous, like lion and jackal, sea and ditch, or fine wine and sour drink.
ramayan::7380.simple_insight: Some comparisons are meant to humble pride completely.
ramayan::7380.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned in harsh, unforgettable images. The speaker says that comparing Ravana to Rama is like comparing a jackal to a lion, a ditch to the sea, or sour gruel to the finest wine. The point is total moral and natural mismatch.
ramayan::7380.modern_relevance: Someone finally tells you, plainly, that you are not in the same league as the person you keep underestimating. Pride can survive criticism; it cannot survive comparison.
ramayan::7380.insight: It forces the mind to see scale clearly and drop inflated self-regard.

ramayan::7381.verse_sanskrit: यदन्तरं काञ्चनसीसलोहयोर्यदन्तरं चन्दनवारिपङ्कयोः । यदन्तरं हस्तिबिडालयोर्वने तदन्तरं दाशरथेस्तवैव च । । 34746 । ।
ramayan::7381.verse_hindi: The difference between you and Rama is the difference  between gold and lead, sandal and slime, an elephant and a cat of the forest.
ramayan::7381.english_translation: The difference between you and Rama is the difference between gold and lead, sandal and slime, an elephant and a cat of the forest.
ramayan::7381.translation_literal: यदन्तरं (the difference) / काञ्चन (gold) / सीस (lead) / लोहयोः (between metals) / यदन्तरं (the difference) / चन्दन (sandalwood) / वारि (water) / पङ्कयोः (between mud) / यदन्तरं (the difference) / हस्ति (elephant) / बिडालयोः (of cat and) / वने (in the forest) / तदन्तरं (that difference) / दाशरथेः (of Dasharatha's son) / तव (between you and) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
ramayan::7381.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7381.essence: Rama and Ravana stand worlds apart in nature and worth.
ramayan::7381.simple_meaning: Rama and Ravana are not equals at all. Their difference is as vast as gold and lead, sandalwood and mud, an elephant and a cat.
ramayan::7381.simple_insight: Some comparisons are not insults; they are reality made visible.
ramayan::7381.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, the speaker piles up images to show the distance between the two men. Each comparison makes the gap sharper: purity and weight, fragrance and filth, strength and smallness. It is part of a larger rebuke, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7381.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone tries to compare themselves to a person who has spent years earning trust. The gap is not about status — it is about character, steadiness, and what each life has been made of.
ramayan::7381.insight: It shifts the mind from rivalry to honest comparison of character and conduct.

ramayan::7382.verse_sanskrit: यदन्तरं वायसवैनतेययोर्यदन्तरं मद्गुमयूरयोरपि । यदन्तरं सारसगृध्रयोर्वने तदन्तरं दाशरथेस्तवैव च । । 34747 । ।
ramayan::7382.verse_hindi: The difference between you and Dasarathas son is the difference between a crow and Garuda, a watercrane and a peacock, a vulture and a swan in the forest.
ramayan::7382.english_translation: The difference between you and Dasaratha's son is the difference between a crow and Garuda, a watercrane and a peacock, a vulture and a swan in the forest.
ramayan::7382.translation_literal: यदन्तरं (the difference) / वायस-वैनतेययोः (between crow and Garuda) / यदन्तरं (the difference) / मद्गु-मयूरयोः (between watercrane and peacock) / अपि (also) / यदन्तरं (the difference) / सारस-गृध्रयोः (between swan and vulture) / वने (in the forest) / तदन्तरं (that difference) / दाशरथेः (of Dasaratha's son) / तव (of you) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
ramayan::7382.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7382.essence: Rama and Ravana are not on the same level at all.
ramayan::7382.simple_meaning: Rama is being described as vastly superior to the enemy, using sharp animal comparisons to show the gap between them.
ramayan::7382.simple_insight: Some differences are so large that comparison itself becomes humiliation.
ramayan::7382.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is speaking in a run of insults and comparisons aimed at Ravana. He piles image upon image—crow and Garuda, watercrane and peacock, vulture and swan—to show that Ravana and Rama belong to utterly different orders of being. The point is not teaching, but fierce poetic condemnation.
ramayan::7382.modern_relevance: When someone tries to measure themselves against a person they have already wronged, the comparison can become its own rebuke.
ramayan::7382.insight: It turns rivalry into a moral contrast, not a contest of equals.

ramayan::7383.verse_sanskrit: तस्मिन्सहस्राक्षसमप्रभावे रामे स्थिते कार्मुकबाणपाणौ । हृतापि तेहं न जरां गमिष्ये वज्रं यथा मक्षिकयावगीर्णम् । । 34748 । ।
ramayan::7383.verse_hindi: So long Rama, equal in prowess to the thousandeyed Indra stands with bow and arrows in hand, I will not, although abducted, wither away like a diamond gulped by an insect (fly).
ramayan::7383.english_translation: So long as Rama, equal in prowess to the thousand-eyed Indra, stands with bow and arrows in hand, I will not, though abducted, wither away like a diamond swallowed by an insect.
ramayan::7383.translation_literal: तस्मिन् (in that) / सहस्राक्षसमप्रभावे (equal in prowess to the thousand-eyed one) / रामे (Rama) / स्थिते (standing) / कार्मुकबाणपाणौ (with bow and arrows in hand) / हृतापि (though abducted) / ते (your) / अहं (I) / न (not) / जरां गमिष्ये (will go to decay) / वज्रम् (diamond) / यथा (like) / मक्षिकया (by an insect) / अवगूर्णम् (swallowed)
ramayan::7383.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7383.essence: Abduction cannot break her while Rama still stands.
ramayan::7383.simple_meaning: Sita says she will not be broken by abduction while Rama still lives and stands ready with his bow.
ramayan::7383.simple_insight: Real strength can come from trust that refuses to collapse under pain.
ramayan::7383.detailed_meaning: Sita answers Ravana from Lanka, still held captive but not defeated. She measures herself against Rama's living strength and refuses Ravana's attempt to reduce her to helplessness. Her endurance is tied to her faith in Rama's return.
ramayan::7383.modern_relevance: You are in a room where everything feels stolen from you, yet you still know who stands for you. That knowledge can keep you from collapsing inward.
ramayan::7383.insight: It shifts the mind from humiliation to inward steadiness rooted in trust.

ramayan::7384.verse_sanskrit: इतीव तद्वाक्यमदुष्टभावा सुदुष्टमुक्त्वा रजनीचरं तम् । गात्रप्रकम्पाद्व्यथिता बभूव वातोद्धता सा कदलीव तन्वी । । 34749 । ।
ramayan::7384.verse_hindi: Having said thus to the wicked nightwalker Ravana, Sita, pure in thought remained  distressed.Her slender body started trembling like a banana plant becomes shaken by a violent wind.
ramayan::7384.english_translation: Having said thus to the wicked nightwalker Ravana, Sita, pure in thought, remained distressed. Her slender body began trembling like a banana plant shaken by a violent wind.
ramayan::7384.translation_literal: इतीव (thus) / तद्वाक्यम् (that speech) / अदुष्टभावा (pure in thought) / सुदुष्टम् (to the very wicked one) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / रजनीचरम् (nightwalker) / तम् (that) / गात्रप्रकम्पात् (from trembling of the body) / व्यथिता (distressed) / बभूव (became) / वातोद्धता (shaken by wind) / सा (she) / कदलीव (like a banana plant) / तन्वी (slender-bodied)
ramayan::7384.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7384.essence: Purity can remain intact even when fear shakes the body.
ramayan::7384.simple_meaning: Sita has answered Ravana, but his words still leave her shaken. Even while remaining pure in mind, her body trembles with distress.
ramayan::7384.simple_insight: Courage does not always look calm. You can stay pure and still feel shaken.
ramayan::7384.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just answered Ravana without losing her moral clarity. But his presence and words still disturb her body. Valmiki shows both her inner purity and the real cost of standing alone before a dangerous man.
ramayan::7384.modern_relevance: You hold your ground in a tense conversation, then your hands shake after it ends. The fear was real, even though you did not give in to it.
ramayan::7384.insight: It separates inner integrity from outward composure, showing that fear can shake the body without conquering the mind.

ramayan::7385.verse_sanskrit: तां वेपमानामुपलक्ष्य सीतां स रावणो मृत्युसमप्रभावः । कुलं बलं नाम च कर्म चात्मनः समाचचक्षे भयकारणार्थम् । । 34750 । ।
ramayan::7385.verse_hindi: Beholding Sita who was trembling, Ravana, powerful like death, started telling about himself, his clan, his strength and his deeds to instil more fear in her.
ramayan::7385.english_translation: Seeing Sita trembling, Ravana, powerful like death, began boasting of his clan, strength, name, and deeds to frighten her further.
ramayan::7385.translation_literal: ताम् (her) / वेपमानाम् (trembling) / उपलक्ष्य (having observed) / सीताम् (Sita) / सः (he) / रावणः (Ravana) / मृत्युसमप्रभावः (equal in power to death) / कुलम् (clan) / बलम् (strength) / नाम (name) / च (and) / कर्म (deeds) / च (and) / आत्मनः (his own) / समाचचक्षे (began to narrate) / भयकारणार्थम् (for the purpose of causing fear)
ramayan::7385.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7385.essence: When fear meets refusal, ego reaches for boasting.
ramayan::7385.simple_meaning: Ravana sees Sita shaking and tries to scare her by boasting about his lineage, power, name, and exploits.
ramayan::7385.simple_insight: Fear often makes people inflate themselves instead of speaking plainly.
ramayan::7385.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita stands before Ravana, visibly shaken but still refusing him. Ravana notices her fear and answers not with reason, but with self-display: he recites his lineage, power, and achievements to overwhelm her resistance.
ramayan::7385.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting and starts listing titles, credentials, and past wins instead of addressing your point. The volume is meant to intimidate because the argument is weak.
ramayan::7385.insight: It shows how ego uses self-praise as a weapon when it cannot win by truth.

ramayan::7386.verse_sanskrit: एवं बृवन्त्यां सीतायां संरब्दः परुषं वचः । ललाटे भृकुटीं कृत्वा रावणः प्रत्युवाच ह । । 3481 । ।
ramayan::7386.verse_hindi: Addressed thus by Sita, Ravana, his anger roused, knitted his eyebrows with a frown on his forehead and replied to her harshly:
ramayan::7386.english_translation: Thus addressed by Sita, Ravana, angered, knitted his brows in a frown on his forehead and replied harshly.
ramayan::7386.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / ब्रुवन्त्याम् (while speaking) / सीतायाम् (to Sita) / संरब्दः (angered) / परुषम् (harsh) / वचः (speech) / ललाटे (on the forehead) / भृकुटीम् (a frown) / कृत्वा (having made) / रावणः (Ravana) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7386.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7386.essence: Wounded pride speaks before understanding can begin.
ramayan::7386.simple_meaning: Ravana answers Sita with anger and harsh words, his face darkening with a frown.
ramayan::7386.simple_insight: When pride is threatened, it answers with force instead of listening.
ramayan::7386.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just spoken with courage to Ravana. Instead of hearing her, he hardens himself, frowns, and answers with cruelty. The moment shows how far his ego has closed his ears.
ramayan::7386.modern_relevance: Someone questions you honestly, and your first impulse is to snap back. That split-second defensiveness tells the truth before your words do.
ramayan::7386.insight: It shows how anger turns a conversation into a display of ego.

ramayan::7387.verse_sanskrit: भ्राता वैश्रवणस्याहं सापत्न्यो वरवर्णिनि । रावणो नाम भद्रं ते दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान् । । 3482 । ।
ramayan::7387.verse_hindi: O paragon of beauty  I am the halfbrother of Kubera, born of his stepmother. I am known as the tenheaded, powerful Ravana. Be blessed
ramayan::7387.english_translation: O paragon of beauty, I am the half-brother of Kubera, born of his stepmother. I am known as the ten-headed, powerful Ravana. Be blessed.
ramayan::7387.translation_literal: भ्राता (brother) / वैश्रवणस्य (of Kubera) / अहम् (I am) / सापत्न्यः (born of a stepmother; half-brother) / वरवर्णिनि (O beautiful one) / रावणः (Ravana) / नाम (by name) / भद्रम् ते (be blessed) / दशग्रीवः (ten-necked, ten-headed) / प्रतापवान् (powerful)
ramayan::7387.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7387.essence: He tries to conquer resistance with a résumé of power.
ramayan::7387.simple_meaning: Ravana introduces himself to Sita, boasting of his lineage, name, and power in an attempt to intimidate her.
ramayan::7387.simple_insight: Pride can sound like confidence, but it often hides fear.
ramayan::7387.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita stands before Ravana after rejecting him. He answers her with a self-presentation full of rank, lineage, and force, trying to overwhelm her resistance. This line is part of his intimidation, not the verse's main teaching.
ramayan::7387.modern_relevance: Someone starts listing titles, connections, and achievements the moment they feel rejected. The louder the self-praise, the more fragile the ego usually is.
ramayan::7387.insight: It shows how insecurity turns into self-advertisement instead of honest dialogue.

ramayan::7388.verse_sanskrit: यस्य देवास्सगन्धर्वाः पिशाचपतगोरगाः । विद्रवन्ति भयाद्भीता मृत्योरिव सदा प्रजाः । । 3483 । ।
ramayan::7388.verse_hindi: Just as people get scared of death, all (creatures) including gandharvas, gods, evil spirits, birds and snakes run away from me.
ramayan::7388.english_translation: All beings, including gods, gandharvas, spirits, birds, and snakes, flee from me in fear, just as people flee from death.
ramayan::7388.translation_literal: यस्य (of whom) / देवाः (the gods) / सगन्धर्वाः (along with gandharvas) / पिशाचपतगोरगाः (spirits, birds, and snakes) / विद्रवन्ति (flee) / भयात् (from fear) / भीताः (terrified) / मृत्योः इव (like death) / सदा (always) / प्रजाः (creatures)
ramayan::7388.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7388.essence: Fear becomes his proof of greatness, and that is his blindness.
ramayan::7388.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that every kind of being runs away from him in terror, the way people fear death.
ramayan::7388.simple_insight: Pride can make fear feel like power, but it only reveals how isolated you are.
ramayan::7388.detailed_meaning: Sita has rejected Ravana, and he answers not with humility but with self-exalting menace. He lists gods, celestial beings, spirits, birds, and snakes as fleeing from him, trying to overwhelm her with his reputation before he escalates the threat.
ramayan::7388.modern_relevance: Someone walks into a room and starts naming all the people who fear him, hoping the room itself will shrink. That kind of intimidation is often a mask for insecurity.
ramayan::7388.insight: It exposes how ego tries to win by frightening others instead of persuading them.

ramayan::7389.verse_sanskrit: येन वैश्रवणो राजा द्वैमात्रः कारणान्तरे । द्वन्द्वमासादितः क्रोधाद्रणे विक्रम्य निर्जितः । । 3484 । ।
ramayan::7389.verse_hindi: For some reason or other a duel took place between me and king Kubera. With my prowess, I defeated him in the duel.
ramayan::7389.english_translation: For some reason or other a duel took place between me and King Kubera. By force in battle, I defeated him.
ramayan::7389.translation_literal: येन (by whom/with whom) / वैश्रवणो (Kubera) / राजा (king) / द्वैमात्रः (for some reason or other; by a two-mother relation) / कारणान्तरे (for another cause) / द्वन्द्वम् (duel) / आसादितः (was brought about) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / रणे (in battle) / विक्रम्य (having displayed prowess) / निर्जितः (defeated)
ramayan::7389.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7389.essence: Victory becomes vanity when you need everyone to hear it.
ramayan::7389.simple_meaning: Ravana says he once fought Kubera in a duel and defeated him through force and anger.
ramayan::7389.simple_insight: Pride can turn victory into self-display instead of wisdom.
ramayan::7389.detailed_meaning: Ravana is boasting to Sita, listing his conquests to impress and intimidate her. He recalls defeating Kubera in battle, not as a moral example but as proof of his power. The verse supports his larger claim of fearsome dominance.
ramayan::7389.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting keeps retelling old wins, hoping the room will mistake volume for strength. The story sounds impressive, but it mostly reveals how much approval they still need.
ramayan::7389.insight: It shifts attention from conquest to the ego that needs to announce it.

ramayan::7390.verse_sanskrit: यद्भयार्तः परित्यज्य स्वमधिष्ठानमृद्धिमत् । कैलासं पर्वतश्रेष्ठमध्यास्ते नरवाहनः । । 3485 । ।
ramayan::7390.verse_hindi: Out of fear for me, Kubera is residing on the mighty mount Kailasa, leaving his own earlier prosperous place of residence.
ramayan::7390.english_translation: Out of fear for me, Kubera is residing on the mighty mount Kailasa, leaving his own earlier prosperous place of residence.
ramayan::7390.translation_literal: यद्भयार्तः (made fearful) / परित्यज्य (having abandoned) / स्वमधिष्ठानम् (his own abode) / ऋद्धिमत् (prosperous, abundant) / कैलासम् (Kailasa) / पर्वतश्रेष्ठम् (best of mountains) / अध्यास्ते (dwells upon) / नरवाहनः (the one whose vehicle is a man, Kubera)
ramayan::7390.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7390.essence: Fear has driven a king from his own palace.
ramayan::7390.simple_meaning: Kubera has left his rich home and now lives on Mount Kailasa because he fears Ravana.
ramayan::7390.simple_insight: Power can force even the mighty to retreat.
ramayan::7390.detailed_meaning: Ravana is boasting to Sita about his victories over Kubera. He says Kubera abandoned his splendid home and fled to Kailasa in fear. The line is one link in Ravana’s larger self-glorifying speech, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::7390.modern_relevance: Someone keeps reminding you of every win, every person who backed down, every door they forced open. The point is not wisdom — it is intimidation.
ramayan::7390.insight: It shows how conquest turns into bragging when ego needs an audience.

ramayan::7391.verse_sanskrit: यस्य तत्पुष्पकं नाम विमानं कामगं शुभम् । वीर्यादेवार्जितं भद्रे येन यामि विहायसम् । । 3486 । ।
ramayan::7391.verse_hindi: O noble lady  with my valour I gained over from Kubera the aerial chariot Pushpaka,
ramayan::7391.english_translation: O noble lady, with my valour I won the auspicious aerial chariot named Pushpaka from Kubera, and with it I travel through the sky.
ramayan::7391.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / तत् (that) / पुष्पकम् (Pushpaka) / नाम (named) / विमानम् (aerial chariot) / कामगम् (moving at will) / शुभम् (auspicious) / वीर्यात् (by valour) / एव (indeed) / अर्जितम् (obtained) / भद्रे (O noble lady) / येन (by which) / यामि (I go) / विहायसम् (through the sky)
ramayan::7391.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7391.essence: Power becomes empty when it is used only to dominate.
ramayan::7391.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he won the Pushpaka aerial chariot through his own strength and now travels in it across the sky.
ramayan::7391.simple_insight: Pride can turn a victory into a story you keep telling yourself.
ramayan::7391.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Sita in Lanka, listing his powers and possessions to overwhelm her with his grandeur. After mentioning Kubera and the mountain of fear, he points to the Pushpaka chariot as proof of his might. The verse is part of his coercive boast, not a teaching.
ramayan::7391.modern_relevance: Someone keeps listing their achievements in a meeting, hoping the room will mistake volume for worth. The need to impress is doing the talking.
ramayan::7391.insight: It shows how self-importance turns real success into an instrument of intimidation.

ramayan::7392.verse_sanskrit: मम सञ्जातरोषस्य मुखं दृष्ट्वैव मैथिलि । विद्रवन्ति परित्रस्तास्सुराश्शक्रपुरोगमाः । । 3487 । ।
ramayan::7392.verse_hindi: O Princess from Mithila, seeing my angry face  even gods led by Indra take to their heels in fear.
ramayan::7392.english_translation: O Princess from Mithila, seeing my angry face, even gods led by Indra run away in fear.
ramayan::7392.translation_literal: मम (my) / सञ्जात-रोषस्य (of one whose anger has arisen) / मुखं (face) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / एव (indeed) / मैथिलि (O princess of Mithila) / विद्रवन्ति (run away) / परित्रस्ताः (frightened) / सुराः (the gods) / शक्र-पुरोगमाः (led by Indra)
ramayan::7392.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7392.essence: Power without restraint becomes a weapon of intimidation.
ramayan::7392.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his anger is so terrifying that even the gods flee when they see his face.
ramayan::7392.simple_insight: Pride can make fear your only language.
ramayan::7392.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to overwhelm Sita with intimidation. He boasts about his own terrifying power, claiming that even Indra and the gods flee when he is angry. The verse is part of his coercive display, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::7392.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with loud confidence, trying to make their anger feel like authority. The performance is meant to shrink you before they even touch you.
ramayan::7392.insight: It shows how raw ego turns strength into threat and uses fear to dominate others.

ramayan::7393.verse_sanskrit: यत्र तिष्ठाम्यहं तत्र मारुतो वाति शङ्कितः । तीव्रांशुश्शिशिरांशुश्च भयात्सम्पद्यते रविः । । 3488 । ।
ramayan::7393.verse_hindi: Wherever I am, the Windgod blows with hesitation. So are the Sun and the Moon afraid of me. Afraid of me the Sun duly discharges his duties.
ramayan::7393.english_translation: Wherever I am, the Windgod blows with hesitation. The Sun and the Moon are afraid of me and do their work in fear.
ramayan::7393.translation_literal: यत्र (where) / तिष्ठामि (I stand) / अहम् (I) / तत्र (there) / मारुतः (the Windgod) / वाति (blows) / शङ्कितः (hesitantly, with fear) / तीव्रांशुः (the Sun) / शिशिरांशुः (the Moon) / च (and) / भयात् (from fear) / सम्पद्यते (performs, carries out) / रविः (the Sun)
ramayan::7393.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7393.essence: He mistakes fear for authority, and the world only obeys because it must.
ramayan::7393.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his presence terrifies even the wind, sun, and moon, forcing the natural world to behave differently around him.
ramayan::7393.simple_insight: Pride can make fear feel like power, but it still leaves you alone.
ramayan::7393.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to impress Sita by describing his terrifying force. He claims that even the wind, sun, and moon act differently in his presence. The verse is part of a larger boast, not a teaching on its own.
ramayan::7393.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting keeps talking louder than everyone else, trying to sound unstoppable. The room goes quiet, but not from respect — from discomfort. That kind of dominance is what Ravana is performing here.
ramayan::7393.insight: It reveals how ego turns intimidation into a false measure of greatness.

ramayan::7394.verse_sanskrit: निष्कम्पपत्रास्तरवो नद्यश्च स्तिमितोदकाः । भवन्ति यत्र यत्राहं तिष्ठामि विचरामि च । । 3489 । ।
ramayan::7394.verse_hindi: Wherever I stay or move about, the leaves of trees do not shake, and the waters in rivers remain still.
ramayan::7394.english_translation: Wherever I stay or move about, the leaves of trees do not shake, and the waters in rivers remain still.
ramayan::7394.translation_literal: निष्कम्पपत्राः (with unmoving leaves) / तरवः (trees) / नद्यः (rivers) / च (and) / स्तिमितोदकाः (with still waters) / भवन्ति (become) / यत्र यत्र (wherever) / अहम् (I) / तिष्ठामि (stand) / विचरामि (move about) / च (and)
ramayan::7394.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7394.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his presence is so terrifying that even trees and rivers seem to go still around him.
ramayan::7394.simple_insight: Fear can make you imagine your own power is absolute.
ramayan::7394.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to impress Sita with his might. He claims that when he stands or walks anywhere, even nature freezes in fear. This is part of his larger boast about his terrifying presence.
ramayan::7394.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting starts speaking like the room should revolve around them, and everyone falls quiet. That silence can feed a false sense of power.
ramayan::7394.insight: It exposes the psychology of intimidation: dominance can silence others without proving real strength.

ramayan::7395.verse_sanskrit: मम पारे समुद्रस्य लङ्का नाम पुरी शुभा । सम्पूर्णा राक्षसैर्घोरैर्यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती । । 34810 । ।
ramayan::7395.verse_hindi: My city known as Lanka, teeming with terrific demons, is on the other side of the sea. It is  beautiful like the city of Indras Amaravati.
ramayan::7395.english_translation: My city called Lanka lies beyond the sea, crowded with fearsome beings, and it is beautiful like Indra’s Amaravati.
ramayan::7395.translation_literal: मम (my) / पारे (on the far side) / समुद्रस्य (of the sea) / लङ्का (Lanka) / नाम (named) / पुरी (city) / शुभा (beautiful) / सम्पूर्णा (filled) / राक्षसैः (with rakshasas) / घोरैः (terrible) / यथा (like) / इन्द्रस्य (of Indra) / अमरावती (Amaravati)
ramayan::7395.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7395.essence: Ravana’s splendour is real, but so is the menace beneath it.
ramayan::7395.simple_meaning: Ravana describes Lanka as his beautiful city across the sea, full of terrible beings, and compares it to Indra’s celestial city.
ramayan::7395.simple_insight: Power can build beauty, but it can also make a place feel dangerous.
ramayan::7395.detailed_meaning: From Lanka, Ravana points to his island capital beyond the ocean. He boasts of its splendour and its fearsome inhabitants, setting the stage for Hanuman’s secret entry and the larger clash between Ravana’s pride and Rama’s resolve.
ramayan::7395.modern_relevance: You can look at a place you built with pride and still miss the fear it inspires in others.
ramayan::7395.insight: It frames Lanka as both magnificent and threatening, revealing Ravana’s pride before the coming conflict.

ramayan::7396.verse_sanskrit: प्राकारेण परिक्षिप्ता पाण्डुरेण विराजता । हेमकक्ष्या पुरी रम्या वैढूर्यमयतोरणा । । 34811 । ।
ramayan::7396.verse_hindi: The beautiful city of Lanka  shines with its pale white ramparts and golden interiors. The entrance gates are encrusted with vaidurya (catseye).
ramayan::7396.english_translation: The beautiful city of Lanka shines with its pale white ramparts and golden interiors. The entrance gates are encrusted with vaidurya (catseye).
ramayan::7396.translation_literal: प्राकारेण (with ramparts) / परिक्षिप्ता (surrounded) / पाण्डुरेण (with pale-white) / विराजता (shining) / हेमकक्ष्या (golden inner chambers) / पुरी (city) / रम्या (beautiful) / वैढूर्यमयतोरणा (with vaidurya-made gates)
ramayan::7396.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7396.essence: Beauty and power can be displayed as one image.
ramayan::7396.simple_meaning: Lanka is described as a splendid city with white walls, golden interiors, and jeweled gates.
ramayan::7396.simple_insight: Some places announce power before anyone speaks a word.
ramayan::7396.detailed_meaning: Ravana is describing his own island capital to the listener. After naming its location beyond the sea, he paints Lanka as dazzling and fortified: white ramparts, golden chambers, and jewel-studded gates. The verse is part of a larger boastful description, not a teaching.
ramayan::7396.modern_relevance: You walk into a lobby with marble floors, gold trim, and guarded doors. Before anyone explains the company, the building has already told you who thinks it matters.
ramayan::7396.insight: It trains attention on setting and power, not on inner meaning.

ramayan::7397.verse_hindi: It is crowded with elephants, horses and chariots. It resounds with the music of trumpets. The trees in the delightful pleasuregardens yield fruits in all seasons.
ramayan::7397.english_translation: It is crowded with elephants, horses and chariots. It resounds with the music of trumpets. The trees in the delightful pleasure gardens yield fruits in all seasons.
ramayan::7397.translation_literal: हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधा (crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots) / तूर्यनादविनादिता (filled with the sound of trumpets) / सर्वकालफलैः (with fruits in all seasons) / वृक्षैः (by trees) / सङ्कुलोद्द्यानशोभिता (adorned with crowded pleasure gardens)
ramayan::7397.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7397.essence: Splendor can be used to disguise captivity.
ramayan::7397.simple_meaning: Lanka is described as a bustling, beautiful city with animals, chariots, music, and gardens that bear fruit all year.
ramayan::7397.simple_insight: Not every dazzling place is safe; beauty can be part of temptation.
ramayan::7397.detailed_meaning: Ravana is praising Lanka to Sita, painting it as a rich, vibrant capital full of power, music, and abundance. He is building the case for why she should accept life there with him, turning the city itself into a lure.
ramayan::7397.modern_relevance: A glossy apartment tour, a luxury car, and a perfectly staged dinner can all hide what life there will actually cost you.
ramayan::7397.insight: It shows how seduction often begins with spectacle, not honesty.

ramayan::7398.verse_sanskrit: तत्र त्वं वसती सीते राजपुत्रि मया सह । न स्मरिष्यसि नारीणां मानुषीणां मनस्विनि । । 34813 । ।
ramayan::7398.verse_hindi: O highminded princess, O Sita while living with me, you will not even think of other women.
ramayan::7398.english_translation: O high-minded princess, O Sita, while living with me, you will not even think of other women.
ramayan::7398.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / त्वं (you) / वसती (dwelling) / सीते (O Sita) / राजपुत्रि (O princess) / मया (with me) / सह (together) / न (not) / स्मरिष्यसि (you will remember) / नारीणां (of women) / मानुषीणां (of human) / मनस्विनि (O high-minded one)
ramayan::7398.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7398.essence: Seduction here is really an attempt to overwrite loyalty.
ramayan::7398.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts to Sita that if she stays with him, she will forget all other women and live only with him.
ramayan::7398.simple_insight: Charm and power can still be a prison when they are used to possess.
ramayan::7398.detailed_meaning: In Lanka's shining city, Ravana keeps trying to break Sita's resolve. Surrounded by wealth and splendor, he tempts her with comfort and status, claiming his company will erase all memory of Rama and other women. The verse is part of his pressure, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7398.modern_relevance: Someone floods your inbox with gifts, praise, and promises, hoping attention will wear down your boundaries. The pressure is the point.
ramayan::7398.insight: It shows how desire speaks as certainty, trying to replace consent with persuasion.

ramayan::7399.verse_sanskrit: भुञ्जाना मानुषान्भोगान्दिव्यांश्च वरवर्णिनि । न स्मरिष्यसि रामस्य मानुषस्य गतायुषः । । 34814 । ।
ramayan::7399.verse_hindi: O blessed lady of fine complexion, while enjoying both human and heavenly  pleasures with me there, you will not remember Rama who is a mortal of short lifespan.
ramayan::7399.english_translation: O blessed lady of fine complexion, while enjoying both human and heavenly pleasures with me there, you will not remember Rama who is a mortal of short lifespan.
ramayan::7399.translation_literal: भुञ्जाना (enjoying) / मानुषान् (human) / भोगान् (pleasures) / दिव्यान् (heavenly) / च (and) / वरवर्णिनि (O blessed lady of fine complexion) / न (not) / स्मरिष्यसि (you will remember) / रामस्य (of Rama) / मानुषस्य (of the mortal) / गतायुषः (whose life is spent / short-lived)
ramayan::7399.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7399.essence: Ravana mistakes luxury for power over the heart.
ramayan::7399.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that Sita will forget Rama because she will live in luxury with him instead.
ramayan::7399.simple_insight: Arrogance always assumes comfort can erase love.
ramayan::7399.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands in Lanka, trying to break Sita with seduction and status. He promises pleasures beyond human measure and dismisses Rama as merely mortal and short-lived. The verse is part of his attempt to replace devotion with desire.
ramayan::7399.modern_relevance: Someone tries to win you over by offering comfort, status, and certainty, while belittling the person or principle you still hold dear.
ramayan::7399.insight: It exposes how desire speaks when it thinks possession can replace loyalty.

ramayan::7400.verse_sanskrit: स्थापयित्वा प्रियं पुत्रं राज्ञा दशरथेन यः । मन्दवीर्यस्सुतो ज्येष्ठस्ततः प्रस्थापितो वनम् । । 34815 । ।
ramayan::7400.verse_hindi: Considering the eldest son a weakling, king Dasaratha has sent him away to the forest so that he could consecrate his dear son(Bharata).
ramayan::7400.english_translation: Having set aside his beloved son, King Dasharatha sent his eldest son, whom he considered weak, into the forest.
ramayan::7400.translation_literal: स्थापयित्वा (having set aside) / प्रियम् (beloved) / पुत्रम् (son) / राज्ञा (by the king) / दशरथेन (by Dasharatha) / यः (who) / मन्दवीर्यः (weak in strength) / सुतः (son) / ज्येष्ठः (eldest) / ततः (then) / प्रस्थापितः (sent forth) / वनम् (to the forest)
ramayan::7400.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7400.essence: A wound becomes sharper when someone names it as betrayal.
ramayan::7400.simple_meaning: Dasharatha sent his eldest son away to the forest, treating him as unfit while favoring Bharata.
ramayan::7400.simple_insight: A cruel judgment can turn family love into exile.
ramayan::7400.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Sita in Lanka, twisting Rama’s exile into an insult. He claims Dasharatha pushed aside his eldest son, judged him weak, and sent him to the forest to secure Bharata’s place. It is part of a manipulative argument, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::7400.modern_relevance: Someone takes a family wound and retells it as proof that nobody valued you. The facts get bent until pain sounds like truth.
ramayan::7400.insight: It shows how grievance can be weaponized by reframing a painful event as deliberate rejection.

ramayan::7401.verse_sanskrit: तेन किं भ्रष्टराज्येन रामेण गतचेतसा । करिष्यसि विशालाक्षि तापसेन तपस्विना । । 34816 । ।
ramayan::7401.verse_hindi: O largeeyed Sita dislodged from the kingdom, Rama has lost his capacity to think. He is doing penance, assuming an ascetic role. What can he do (for you)?
ramayan::7401.english_translation: O large-eyed Sita, what can Rama do for you now? He has lost the kingdom and his mind is turned away. He is living as an ascetic, devoted to penance.
ramayan::7401.translation_literal: तेन (by him) / किं (what) / भ्रष्टराज्येन (with the kingdom lost) / रामेण (by Rama) / गतचेतसा (with the mind gone) / करिष्यसि (will do) / विशालाक्षि (O large-eyed one) / तापसेन (as an ascetic) / तपस्विना (by the one practising austerity)
ramayan::7401.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7401.essence: He tries to make Rama look too broken to save anyone.
ramayan::7401.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Rama as powerless: stripped of his kingdom and living like an ascetic, he cannot help Sita now.
ramayan::7401.simple_insight: Arrogance often speaks loudest when it feels threatened.
ramayan::7401.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to break Sita’s resolve. He sneers that Rama has lost his kingdom, his mind is scattered, and he now lives like a penitent in the forest. The line is not teaching truth; it is pressure, meant to make Sita doubt rescue.
ramayan::7401.modern_relevance: Someone cornered in an argument starts attacking your partner’s worth instead of facing the real issue. The insult is meant to make you doubt the person you trust.
ramayan::7401.insight: It shows how manipulation works by shrinking the other person’s power before asking for surrender.

ramayan::7402.verse_sanskrit: सर्वराक्षसभर्तारं कामात्स्वयमिहागतम् । न मन्मथशराविष्टं प्रत्याख्यातुं त्वमर्हसि । । 34817 । ।
ramayan::7402.verse_hindi: I am lord of all the demons. You should not reject me I am here (only because I am) overcome by the arrows of the god of love.
ramayan::7402.english_translation: I am the lord of all the demons. You should not reject me. I have come here only because I am pierced by the arrows of desire.
ramayan::7402.translation_literal: सर्वराक्षसभर्तारम् (lord of all the demons) / कामात् (from desire) / स्वयम् (myself) / इह (here) / आगतम् (come) / न (not) / मन्मथशराविष्टम् (pierced by the arrows of the god of love) / प्रत्याख्यातुम् (to reject) / त्वम् (you) / अर्हसि (you ought)
ramayan::7402.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7402.essence: Wanting something does not make it rightful.
ramayan::7402.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Sita not to refuse him. He claims his desire brought him here and uses that as a reason she should accept him.
ramayan::7402.simple_insight: Desire can make a person speak as if wanting something gives them entitlement.
ramayan::7402.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana stands before Sita and tries to turn his own lust into an argument. He presents himself as powerful, then hides behind desire, hoping to make force sound like fate. This verse is part of his pressure, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7402.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with a smile and calls their pushiness attraction, as if wanting you gives them the right to ignore your no.
ramayan::7402.insight: It exposes how ego dresses up craving as justification, and how pressure can be disguised as romance.

ramayan::7403.verse_sanskrit: प्रत्याख्याय हि मां भीरु परितापं गमिष्यसि । चरणेनाभिहत्येव पुरूरवसमूर्वशी । । 34818 । ।
ramayan::7403.verse_hindi: O timid lady if you reject me, you will regret like Urvasi who kicked Pururava and regretted later.
ramayan::7403.english_translation: O timid lady, if you reject me, you will suffer regret like Urvashi did after kicking Pururava.
ramayan::7403.translation_literal: प्रत्याख्याय (having rejected) / हि (indeed) / माम् (me) / भीरु (timid one) / परितापम् (regret, torment) / गमिष्यसि (you will go into) / चरणेन (with the foot) / अभिहत्य (having struck, having kicked) / इव (like) / पुरूरवसम् (Pururava) / ऊर्वशी (Urvashi)
ramayan::7403.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7403.essence: Fear is being used here to disguise coercion.
ramayan::7403.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens Sita, saying that if she refuses him, she will later feel deep regret, just as Urvashi regretted insulting Pururava.
ramayan::7403.simple_insight: A threat can sound persuasive only when fear has already replaced clarity.
ramayan::7403.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressuring Sita after boasting that Rama is powerless. He tries to frighten her with a story of Urvashi and Pururava, turning insult into manipulation. The verse is one move in his larger attempt to break her resistance.
ramayan::7403.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a message thread and says you’ll regret saying no, as if fear is proof. The pressure is the point.
ramayan::7403.insight: It exposes coercion dressed up as counsel, and shows how manipulation uses shame to force consent.

ramayan::7404.verse_sanskrit: अङ्गुल्या न समो रामो मम युद्धे स मानुषः । तव भाग्येन सम्प्राप्तं भजस्व वरवर्णिनि । । 34819 । ।
ramayan::7404.verse_hindi: O lady of fine complexion, Rama is a (mere) mortal. In war he is no match (even) for my finger. It is your good fortune that you have got me here. Take refuge in me.
ramayan::7404.english_translation: O lady of fine complexion, Rama is a mere mortal. In war he is no match even for my finger. It is your good fortune that you have got me here. Take refuge in me.
ramayan::7404.translation_literal: अङ्गुल्या (by the finger) / न (not) / समः (equal) / रामः (Rama) / मम (to me) / युद्धे (in battle) / सः (he) / मानुषः (a human) / तव (your) / भाग्येन (by fortune) / सम्प्राप्तम् (obtained/come upon) / भजस्व (take refuge in / seek) / वरवर्णिनि (O lady of fine complexion)
ramayan::7404.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7404.essence: False greatness always needs to diminish what it cannot match.
ramayan::7404.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts to Sita that Rama is only human and no match for him in battle, then urges her to accept him instead.
ramayan::7404.simple_insight: Pride can turn strength into blindness.
ramayan::7404.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to break Sita’s resolve by belittling Rama and magnifying himself. He turns desire into insult, claiming victory before any battle is fought. The verse is part of his pressure, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7404.modern_relevance: Someone tries to impress you by tearing down what you value and inflating their own power. The louder the brag, the clearer the insecurity underneath.
ramayan::7404.insight: It reveals how arrogance speaks when it has no real ground.

ramayan::7405.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही क्रुद्धा संरक्तलोचना । अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं रहिते राक्षसाधिपम् । । 34820 । ।
ramayan::7405.verse_hindi: Thus addressed, Sita was enraged and her eyes turned red. She replied in harsh words to the chief of the demons in that solitary place:.
ramayan::7405.english_translation: Thus addressed, Sita was enraged and her eyes turned red. She replied in harsh words to the chief of the demons in that solitary place.
ramayan::7405.translation_literal: एवमुक्ता (thus addressed) / तु (indeed) / वैदेही (Sita, daughter of Videha) / क्रुद्धा (angry) / संरक्तलोचना (with reddened eyes) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / परुषं (harsh) / वाक्यं (speech) / रहिते (in a lonely place) / राक्षसाधिपम् (to the lord of the demons)
ramayan::7405.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7405.essence: Humiliation does not erase dignity; it can sharpen it.
ramayan::7405.simple_meaning: Sita, angered by Ravana's taunts, answers him sharply in the empty place where he has trapped her.
ramayan::7405.simple_insight: Even in helplessness, your dignity can answer back.
ramayan::7405.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Grove, Ravana keeps pressing Sita to accept him and abandon Rama. His words provoke her, and she turns on him with anger and clarity. This verse marks the moment her silence breaks into defiance.
ramayan::7405.modern_relevance: When someone corners you with pressure and flattery, your body may shake before your voice does. Sita shows that refusal can still be fierce.
ramayan::7405.insight: It shifts you from passive endurance to clear resistance when your boundaries are crossed.

ramayan::7406.verse_sanskrit: कथं वैश्रवणं देवं सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम् । भ्रातरं व्यपदिश्य त्वमशुभं कर्तुमिच्छसि । । 34821 । ।
ramayan::7406.verse_hindi: Why do you wish to do something inauspicious by calling Lord Kubera who is worshipped by all beings your brother ?
ramayan::7406.english_translation: Why do you wish to do something inauspicious by calling Lord Kubera, worshipped by all beings, your brother?
ramayan::7406.translation_literal: कथं (how) / वैश्रवणं (Kubera) / देवं (the radiant one) / सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम् (worshipped by all beings) / भ्रातरं (brother) / व्यपदिश्य (calling by name) / त्वम् (you) / अशुभं (inauspicious act) / कर्तुम् (to do) / इच्छसि (you wish)
ramayan::7406.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7406.essence: A revered name cannot make an ugly act clean.
ramayan::7406.simple_meaning: Sita rebukes Ravana for trying to justify an evil act by using a respected name. She says a holy or honored relation cannot make wrongdoing acceptable.
ramayan::7406.simple_insight: A polished excuse does not change the moral weight of what you are doing.
ramayan::7406.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has tried to flatter and pressure Sita by boasting about himself and using family language to blur the truth. Sita cuts through the manipulation and refuses to let a sacred name cover an ugly intention.
ramayan::7406.modern_relevance: Someone calls a harmful decision “for the family,” “for the company,” or “for everyone’s good,” but the damage is still there. Sita’s clarity refuses that kind of moral laundering.
ramayan::7406.insight: It teaches you to separate labels from actions and judge the act itself.

ramayan::7407.verse_sanskrit: अवश्यं विनशिष्यन्ति सर्वे रावण राक्षसाः । येषां त्वं कर्कशो राजा दुर्बुद्धिरजितेन्द्रियः । । 34822 । ।
ramayan::7407.verse_hindi: O Ravana ,you are cruel and evilminded. You have no control over your senses. (And yet) you are the ruler of your breed. Surely they are going to be destroyed.
ramayan::7407.english_translation: O Ravana, all the demons under a cruel, evil-minded, and uncontrolled ruler are surely headed for destruction.
ramayan::7407.translation_literal: अवश्यं (surely) / विनशिष्यन्ति (will be destroyed) / सर्वे (all) / रावण (O Ravana) / राक्षसाः (the demons) / येषाम् (of whom) / त्वम् (you) / कर्कशः (cruel) / राजा (king) / दुर्बुद्धिः (evil-minded) / अजितेन्द्रियः (uncontrolled in the senses)
ramayan::7407.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7407.essence: A ruler without self-mastery destroys everyone he leads.
ramayan::7407.simple_meaning: A harsh, self-controlled leader drags everyone around him toward ruin. Sita is telling Ravana that his own condition is already destroying his people.
ramayan::7407.simple_insight: It is sobering to see that private disorder never stays private.
ramayan::7407.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita stands alone before Ravana and answers his insults without fear. She sees through his power: he is not a strong king but a man ruled by appetite and anger. Because he leads that way, his whole race is heading toward destruction.
ramayan::7407.modern_relevance: A manager lashes out in meetings, then wonders why the whole team is tense and failing. The damage was never just personal; everyone was living inside his moods.
ramayan::7407.insight: It shifts attention from power itself to the character governing that power.

ramayan::7408.verse_sanskrit: अपहृत्य शचीं भार्यां शक्यमिन्द्रस्य जीवितुम् । न च रामस्य भार्यां मामपनीयास्ति जीवितम् । । 34823 । ।
ramayan::7408.verse_hindi: It may be possible (for some one) to live after abducting Indras wife, Sachi, but it is not possible for any one to live after kidnapping the wife of Rama.
ramayan::7408.english_translation: It may be possible for someone to live after abducting Indra's wife, Sachi, but it is not possible for anyone to live after kidnapping the wife of Rama.
ramayan::7408.translation_literal: अपहृत्य (having abducted) / शचीं (Sachi) / भार्यां (wife) / शक्यम् (possible) / इन्द्रस्य (of Indra) / जीवितुम् (to live) / न (not) / च (and) / रामस्य (of Rama) / भार्यां (wife) / माम् (me) / अपनीय (having taken away) / अस्ति (there is) / जीवितम् (life)
ramayan::7408.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7408.essence: Some violations are so grave they make survival impossible.
ramayan::7408.simple_meaning: Ravana says some crimes can still leave you alive, but taking Sita, Rama's wife, will not.
ramayan::7408.simple_insight: Some acts cross a line so severe that they destroy the one who commits them.
ramayan::7408.detailed_meaning: In Ravana's court, he is being warned about the consequences of his actions. He answers with grim certainty: abducting Sita is not like offending any ordinary king. By naming Rama's wife, he declares that this choice has made survival impossible.
ramayan::7408.modern_relevance: You know the moment you cross a line and cannot pretend it is harmless anymore. Some choices do not just create trouble — they change the whole future of the person who made them.
ramayan::7408.insight: It shifts the mind from casual wrongdoing to irreversible consequence.

ramayan::7409.verse_sanskrit: जीवेच्चिरं वज्रधरस्य हस्ताच्छचीं प्रधृष्याप्रतिरूपरूपाम् । न मादृशीं राक्षस दूशयित्वा पीतामृतस्यापि तवास्ति मोक्षः । । 34824 । ।
ramayan::7409.verse_hindi: O demon, you may live long after forcibly snatching the most beautiful Sachi, from the hands of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, but after abusing a woman like me, you will not be released from death even if you drink nectar.
ramayan::7409.english_translation: O demon, you may live long after forcibly snatching the most beautiful Sachi from the hands of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, but after abusing a woman like me, you will not be released from death even if you drink nectar.
ramayan::7409.translation_literal: जीवेच्चिरम् (may live long) / वज्रधरस्य (of the thunderbolt-bearer) / हस्तात् (from the hand) / शचीम् (Sachi) / प्रधृष्य (having forcibly seized) / अप्रतिरूपरूपाम् (of unmatched beauty) / न (not) / मादृशीम् (a woman like me) / राक्षस (O demon) / दूशयित्वा (having violated) / पीतामृतस्य (even of one who has drunk nectar) / अपि (even) / तव (for you) / अस्ति (there is) / मोक्षः (release)
ramayan::7409.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7409.essence: Violating the innocent carries a cost even power cannot cancel.
ramayan::7409.simple_meaning: Sita tells Ravana that even if he once harmed a celestial queen and survived, violating a woman like her will still bring his death.
ramayan::7409.simple_insight: Cruel power is not immunity. Some acts seal their own ruin.
ramayan::7409.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana without fear. He has boasted of his strength and past conquests, but she draws a hard line: what he has done to her crosses every limit. Her words turn his arrogance into a sentence.
ramayan::7409.modern_relevance: A bully at work thinks past success protects him from consequences. Then one line, one complaint, one exposed pattern ends the illusion.
ramayan::7409.insight: It shifts the mind from intimidation to moral consequence: power does not erase the cost of violation.

ramayan::7410.verse_sanskrit: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवाम् । हस्ते हस्तं समाहत्य चकार सुमहद्वपुः । । 3491 । ।
ramayan::7410.verse_hindi: On hearing the Sitas words, the powerful Ravana struck his palms one over the other and assumed a huge form (original figure).
ramayan::7410.english_translation: On hearing Sita's words, the powerful Ravana struck his palms together and assumed a huge form.
ramayan::7410.translation_literal: सीतायााः (of Sita's) / वचनं (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / दशग्रीवः (Ravana, the ten-headed one) / प्रतापवाम् (powerful) / हस्ते (in the hands) / हस्तं (hand) / समाहत्य (striking together) / चकार (made) / सुमहद्वपुः (a very huge body)
ramayan::7410.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7410.essence: He answers truth with spectacle, not understanding.
ramayan::7410.simple_meaning: Ravana hears Sita and responds with swagger, making himself look even larger and more imposing.
ramayan::7410.simple_insight: Pride often answers truth with performance instead of change.
ramayan::7410.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just spoken with fearless clarity. Ravana does not soften or reflect; he reacts by swelling himself with display, trying to intimidate her before speaking again. The verse shows his ego hardening under challenge.
ramayan::7410.modern_relevance: Someone points out your blind spot in a meeting, and you respond by talking louder, sitting taller, and trying to dominate the room.
ramayan::7410.insight: It shows how wounded pride turns feedback into a power display instead of a moment of self-checking.

ramayan::7411.verse_sanskrit: स मैथिलीं पुनर्वाक्यं बभाषे च ततो भृशम् । नोन्मत्तया श्रुतौ मन्ये मम वीर्यपराक्रमौ । । 3492 । ।
ramayan::7411.verse_hindi: Ravana again said to that princess from Mithila, I suppose you are too insane to disregard my strength and valour.
ramayan::7411.english_translation: Ravana again said to the princess from Mithila, "I think you must be mad if you ignore my strength and valour."
ramayan::7411.translation_literal: सः (he) / मैथिलीं (to the princess from Mithila) / पुनः (again) / वाक्यम् (speech) / बभाषे (spoke) / च (and) / ततः (then) / भृशम् (strongly) / नो (not) / उन्मत्तया (by one who is mad) / श्रुतौ (in hearing) / मन्ये (I think) / मम (my) / वीर्य-पराक्रमौ (strength and valour)
ramayan::7411.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7411.essence: Ego hears refusal and answers with louder self-importance.
ramayan::7411.simple_meaning: Ravana reacts to Sita's refusal by boasting that her rejection cannot erase his power. He treats her disbelief as madness.
ramayan::7411.simple_insight: Pride can make force feel like truth, even when it is only fear in disguise.
ramayan::7411.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has answered Ravana with fearless refusal. Instead of hearing her dignity, he turns to self-display, trying to overwhelm her with boasts about his own might. The verse shows arrogance hardening into delusion.
ramayan::7411.modern_relevance: Someone keeps talking over your boundary, as if repetition will turn pressure into consent. Ravana's mistake is familiar: confusing intimidation with authority.
ramayan::7411.insight: It exposes how ego tries to replace persuasion with spectacle.

ramayan::7412.verse_sanskrit: उद्वहेयं भुजाभ्यां तु मेदिनीमम्बरे स्थितः । आपिबेयं समुद्रं च हन्यां मृत्युं रणे स्थितः । । 3493 । ।
ramayan::7412.verse_hindi: Standing in the sky, I can  lift the earth with my arms.  I can drink the oceans. I can kill even the god of death in a combat.
ramayan::7412.english_translation: Standing in the sky, I can lift the earth with my arms. I can drink the oceans. I can kill even the god of death in combat.
