ramayan::7412.translation_literal: उद्वहेयम् (I could lift) / भुजाभ्याम् (with my arms) / तु (indeed) / मेदिनीम् (the earth) / अम्बरे (in the sky) / स्थितः (standing) / आपिबेयम् (I could drink up) / समुद्रम् (the ocean) / च (and) / हन्याम् (I could strike down) / मृत्युम् (death) / रणे (in battle) / स्थितः (standing)
ramayan::7412.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7412.essence: Boasting tries to sound like power when it is really fear.
ramayan::7412.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he can lift the earth, drink the oceans, and defeat death itself in battle.
ramayan::7412.simple_insight: Pride can make power sound limitless, even when it is already blind.
ramayan::7412.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to intimidate Sita after she rejects him. He inflates his strength into impossible feats, turning brute force into a claim of total invincibility. The verse is one step in his coercive argument, not a self-contained teaching.
ramayan::7412.modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts listing everything they can do, every resource they control, every way they could win. The volume rises because the insecurity underneath is already showing.
ramayan::7412.insight: It exposes how boasting can become a substitute for real persuasion.

ramayan::7413.verse_sanskrit: अर्कं ऱुन्ध्यां शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विभिन्द्या हि महीतलम् । कामरूपिणमुन्मत्ते पश्य मां कामदं पतिम् । । 3494 । ।
ramayan::7413.verse_hindi: I can obstruct the Sun and shatter the earth with my sharp arrows. O mad woman I am a husband who can fulfil your desires, and can assume any form at my own free will. Look at me.
ramayan::7413.english_translation: I can obstruct the Sun and shatter the earth with my sharp arrows. O mad woman, I am a husband who can fulfil your desires and can assume any form at will. Look at me.
ramayan::7413.translation_literal: अर्कं (the Sun) / ऱुन्ध्यां (I can obstruct) / शरैः (with arrows) / तीक्ष्णैः (sharp) / विभिन्द्याम् (I can shatter) / हि (indeed) / महीतलम् (the earth's surface) / कामरूपिणम् (one who can take any desired form) / उन्मत्ते (O mad woman) / पश्य (look) / माम् (me) / कामदम् (desire-granting) / पतिम् (husband/lord)
ramayan::7413.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7413.essence: Power without self-mastery becomes ugly pleading.
ramayan::7413.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he can block the Sun, break the earth, change form at will, and satisfy any desire. He is trying to overwhelm Sita with sheer display of power.
ramayan::7413.simple_insight: Pride can sound like strength while it is really desperation.
ramayan::7413.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressuring Sita after she rejects him. He piles up impossible claims about his power and shape-shifting, trying to turn force into attraction. The scene shows how desire, ego, and humiliation have hardened into menace.
ramayan::7413.modern_relevance: Someone floods your phone with grand promises after you say no, trying to make volume feel like value. Ravana's speech is that pattern turned monstrous.
ramayan::7413.insight: It exposes how ego tries to replace consent with intimidation.

ramayan::7414.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तवतस्तस्य सूर्यकल्पे शिखिप्रभे । क्रुद्धस्य हरिपर्यन्ते रक्ते नेत्रे बभूवतुः । । 3495 । ।
ramayan::7414.verse_hindi: As Ravana exploded in anger, his ambercoloured eyes turned red like the radiance of the flaming fire, and almost as bright as the Sun.
ramayan::7414.english_translation: As Ravana exploded in anger, his ambercoloured eyes turned red like the radiance of the flaming fire, and almost as bright as the Sun.
ramayan::7414.translation_literal: एवमुक्तवतस् (having spoken thus) / तस्य (his) / सूर्यकल्पे (sun-like) / शिखिप्रभे (fire-bright) / क्रुद्धस्य (of the angered one) / हरिपर्यन्ते (at the corners of the eyes) / रक्ते (red) / नेत्रे (eyes) / बभूवतुः (became)
ramayan::7414.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7414.essence: His rage is visible before his next move.
ramayan::7414.simple_meaning: Ravana's anger made his eyes turn red and fierce.
ramayan::7414.simple_insight: Unchecked anger changes even the face you present to the world.
ramayan::7414.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just boasted of his power before the woman he wants to overpower. This verse does not advance an argument; it simply shows the bodily sign of his rage, setting up his next shift in form and intention.
ramayan::7414.modern_relevance: You say one sharp thing in a heated argument, and your whole face changes before you even notice it.
ramayan::7414.insight: It shows how anger announces itself before action, exposing the mind's loss of control.

ramayan::7415.verse_sanskrit: सद्यस्सौम्यं परित्यज्य भिक्षुरूपं स रावणः । स्वं रूपं कालरूपाभं भेजे वैश्रवणानुजः । । 3496 । ।
ramayan::7415.verse_hindi: Ravana, brother of Kubera, shed the gentle figure of a mendicant and assumed the form of the god of death.
ramayan::7415.english_translation: Ravana, brother of Kubera, shed the gentle figure of a mendicant and assumed the form of the god of death.
ramayan::7415.translation_literal: सद्यस् (at once) / सौम्यम् (gentle, mild) / परित्यज्य (having abandoned) / भिक्षुरूपम् (mendicant form) / सः (he) / रावणः (Ravana) / स्वम् (own) / रूपम् (form) / कालरूपाभम् (resembling the form of death) / भेजे (assumed) / वैश्रवणानुजः (Kubera's younger brother)
ramayan::7415.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7415.essence: A wounded ego drops its disguise the moment it is challenged.
ramayan::7415.simple_meaning: Ravana drops his disguise and shows a terrifying form, revealing how quickly anger strips away restraint.
ramayan::7415.simple_insight: Anger can erase the mask you were using to seem harmless.
ramayan::7415.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been posing as a gentle mendicant, but the insult has ignited him. In this instant he throws off the disguise and reveals a death-like form, showing how quickly wounded pride turns into menace.
ramayan::7415.modern_relevance: Someone smiles through a tense conversation, then one sharp comment makes the whole room change. The mask drops, and the real temperature of the moment appears.
ramayan::7415.insight: It shows how rage can instantly replace composure with threat.

ramayan::7416.verse_sanskrit: संरक्तनयनश्श्रीमांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः । क्रोधेन महताविष्टो नीलजीमूतसन्निभः । । 3497 । । दशास्यः कार्मुकी बाणी बभूव क्षणदाचरः ।
ramayan::7416.verse_hindi: Overcome by intense anger, Ravanas eyes reddened. The nightranger, stood armed with bow and arrows and shining with glittering gold ornaments, appeared like a black cloud.
ramayan::7416.english_translation: Overcome by intense anger, Ravana's eyes reddened. The night-ranger, armed with bow and arrows and shining with glittering gold ornaments, appeared like a black cloud.
ramayan::7416.translation_literal: संरक्तनयनः (with reddened eyes) / श्रीमान् (splendid, adorned) / तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः (with heated-gold ornaments) / क्रोधेन (by anger) / महता (great) / आविष्टः (possessed, overcome) / नीलजीमूतसन्निभः (resembling a dark rain cloud) / दशास्यः (the ten-faced one, Ravana) / कार्मुकी (bow-armed) / बाणी (with arrows) / बभूव (became) / क्षणदाचरः (the night-ranger)
ramayan::7416.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7416.essence: Anger can arm you before it has reasoned with you.
ramayan::7416.simple_meaning: Ravana is consumed by anger, armed for battle, and described as dark, glittering, and terrifying.
ramayan::7416.simple_insight: Rage can make someone look powerful while shrinking their judgment.
ramayan::7416.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just been provoked and the scene turns physical: his eyes redden, his ornaments blaze, and he takes up bow and arrows. Valmiki pauses to show the force of his fury before the next movement in the confrontation.
ramayan::7416.modern_relevance: You feel your face heat in an argument, and suddenly everything in you wants to strike back. The body looks ready before the mind has any wisdom.
ramayan::7416.insight: It shows how anger overtakes perception before action even begins.

ramayan::7417.verse_sanskrit: स परिव्राजकच्छद्म महाकायो विहाय तत् । । 3498 । । प्रतिपद्य स्वकं रूपं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । संरक्तनयनः क्रोधाज्जीमूतनिचयप्रभः । । 3499 । । रक्ताम्बरधरस्तस्थौ स्त्रीरत्नं प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम् ।
ramayan::7417.verse_hindi: Ravana, chief of the demons, shed the mendicants form and assumed his real self. Clad in red garments, his eyes turned red in anger. Looking like layers of clouds, he stood in front of Sita, a gem among women.
ramayan::7417.english_translation: Ravana, chief of the demons, shed the mendicant disguise and assumed his own form. Clad in red garments, his eyes red with anger, he stood before Sita, the jewel among women.
ramayan::7417.translation_literal: स (he) / परिव्राजकच्छद्म (mendicant disguise) / महाकायः (great-bodied one) / विहाय (having cast off) / तत् (that) / प्रतिपद्य (having assumed) / स्वकम् (his own) / रूपम् (form) / रावणः (Ravana) / राक्षसाधिपः (chief of the rakshasas) / संरक्तनयनः (red-eyed) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / जीमूतनिचयप्रभः (cloud-mass-like in splendour) / रक्ताम्बरधरः (wearing red garments) / तस्थौ (stood) / स्त्रीरत्नम् (jewel among women) / प्रेक्ष्य (having seen) / मैथिलीम् (Sita of Mithila)
ramayan::7417.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7417.essence: The disguise falls, and the real hunger stands exposed.
ramayan::7417.simple_meaning: Ravana drops his disguise, returns to his true form, and stands enraged before Sita.
ramayan::7417.simple_insight: A mask can fall in a second, but desire and anger remain exposed.
ramayan::7417.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has come to Sita pretending to be a holy mendicant. The disguise is now gone. He reveals his real form, burning with anger and desire, and stands before her. This is the moment before he speaks.
ramayan::7417.modern_relevance: The polite tone in a message can vanish the moment someone is denied what they want. What remains underneath is the real person.
ramayan::7417.insight: It shows how quickly self-control collapses when craving is blocked.

ramayan::7418.verse_sanskrit: स तामसितकेशान्तां भास्करस्य प्रभामिव । । 34910 । । वसनाभरणोपेतां मैथिलीं रावणोऽब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::7418.verse_hindi: Ravana said to the princess from Mithila, whose black hair was shining, who was luminous like the Sun and was clad in the best of cothes and ornaments.
ramayan::7418.english_translation: Ravana said to the princess from Mithila, whose black hair shone and who was radiant like the sun, and who was adorned with clothes and ornaments.
ramayan::7418.translation_literal: सा (that woman) / ताम् (to that) / असितकेशान्ताम् (with black hair) / भास्करस्य (of the sun) / प्रभाम् इव (like the radiance) / वसनाभरणोपेताम् (endowed with garments and ornaments) / मैथिलीम् (the woman from Mithila) / रावणः (Ravana) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7418.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7418.essence: Beauty can be the first step of a trap.
ramayan::7418.simple_meaning: Ravana addresses Sita, describing her beauty and radiance before speaking his temptation.
ramayan::7418.simple_insight: Not every flattering voice is safe to trust.
ramayan::7418.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has abandoned disguise and stands before Sita in his true form. He first fixes his gaze on her beauty, then begins the speech that will try to bend her will. This verse is the opening of that coercive appeal.
ramayan::7418.modern_relevance: Someone praises your beauty a little too carefully, a little too soon, and you feel the pressure underneath the compliment. Ravana begins exactly there.
ramayan::7418.insight: It frames the next verse as manipulation, not admiration.

ramayan::7419.verse_sanskrit: त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यदि भर्तारमिच्छसि । । 34911 । । मामाश्रय वरारोहे तवाहं सदृशः पतिः ।
ramayan::7419.verse_hindi: O beautiful lady  if you desire a husband who is famous in the three worlds, take refuge in me. I am fit to be your husband.
ramayan::7419.english_translation: O beautiful lady, if you desire a husband famed in the three worlds, take refuge in me. I am a fitting husband for you.
ramayan::7419.translation_literal: त्रिषु लोकेषु (in the three worlds) / विख्यातं (famous) / यदि (if) / भर्तारम् (husband) / इच्छसि (you desire) / माम् (me) / आश्रय (take refuge) / वरारोहे (O beautiful lady) / तव (for you) / अहम् (I) / सदृशः (fit, suitable) / पतिः (husband)
ramayan::7419.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7419.essence: Power tries to rename desire as suitability.
ramayan::7419.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to seduce Sita by praising himself as a famous and worthy husband, and urging her to choose him instead of Rama.
ramayan::7419.simple_insight: Flattery can be a mask for arrogance and harm.
ramayan::7419.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has abandoned his disguise and now speaks directly to Sita, trying to justify his desire with grand words. This is not wisdom but coercion dressed as praise, and the next verse continues the pressure.
ramayan::7419.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with polished compliments that are really a demand. The tone is smooth, but the message is simple: choose me, ignore your own judgment.
ramayan::7419.insight: It exposes how ego can dress itself as worthiness and call that love.

ramayan::7420.verse_sanskrit: मां भजस्व चिराय त्वमहं श्लाघ्यः प्रियस्तव । । 34912 । । नैव चाहं क्वचिद्भद्रे करिष्ये तव विप्रियम् । त्यज्यतां मानुषे भावो मयि भावः प्रणीयताम् । । 34913 । ।
ramayan::7420.verse_hindi: I am your praiseworthy husband. I will not cause any unpleasantness to you at any time. Abandon on your inclination towards, a (mere) mortal. Divert your love to me.
ramayan::7420.english_translation: Be devoted to me for a long time. I am a husband worthy of praise and will never do anything unpleasant to you. Give up your attachment to a human being and turn your heart toward me.
ramayan::7420.translation_literal: माम् (me) / भजस्व (be devoted to) / चिराय (for a long time) / त्वम् (you) / अहम् (I) / श्लाघ्यः (praiseworthy) / प्रियः (dear) / तव (your) / नैव (never) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / क्वचिद् (at any time) / भद्रे (O fortunate one) / करिष्ये (will do) / तव (to you) / विप्रियम् (what is unpleasant) / त्यज्यताम् (let be given up) / मानुषे (in a human) / भावः (attachment) / मयि (in me) / भावः (feeling) / प्रणीयताम् (let be placed)
ramayan::7420.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7420.essence: A demand for love can hide a bid for control.
ramayan::7420.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to win Sita by promising safety and praise, asking her to abandon her love for Rama and choose him instead.
ramayan::7420.simple_insight: Charm can be a mask for possession.
ramayan::7420.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands before Sita in Lanka and tries to seduce her with status, safety, and flattery. He presents himself as the better choice and urges her to drop her bond with Rama. This is one step in his larger attempt to break her resolve.
ramayan::7420.modern_relevance: Someone who wants control may sound generous at first: praise, promises, reassurance. The pressure often comes wrapped as care.
ramayan::7420.insight: It reveals how manipulation works by replacing devotion with convenience.

ramayan::7421.verse_sanskrit: राज्याच्च्युतमसिद्धार्थं रामं परिमितायुषम् । कैर्गुणैरनुरक्तासि मूढे पण्डितमानिनि । । 34914 । । यः स्त्रिया वचनाद्राज्यं विहाय ससुहृज्जनम् । अस्मिन्व्यालानुचरिते वने वसति दुर्मतिः । । 34915 । ।
ramayan::7421.verse_hindi: O stupid woman you think you are very wise. What is there in Rama so that you are attached to him ? He has left the kingdom and his kith and kin due to the words of a woman. He has not accomplished anything (in life). He has a limited life span and now lives in this forest haunted by wild animals.
ramayan::7421.english_translation: O foolish woman, you think yourself wise. What qualities make you attached to Rama? He has lost his kingdom and failed to achieve his aim. He has a short life left and now lives in a forest haunted by wild creatures. A man who abandons a kingdom with his friends because of a woman's words and lives in such a forest is surely misguided.
ramayan::7421.translation_literal: राज्यात् (from the kingdom) / च्युतम् (fallen) / असिद्धार्थम् (one who has not achieved his aim) / रामम् (Rama) / परिमित-आयुषम् (of limited life span) / कैः (by what) / गुणैः (qualities) / अनुरक्ता (attached) / असि (you are) / मूढे (O foolish woman) / पण्डित-मानिनि (you who think yourself wise) / यः (who) / स्त्रिया (by a woman) / वचनात् (at the words) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / विहाय (having abandoned) / ससुहृद्-जनम् (with friends and kin) / अस्मिन् (in this) / व्याल-अनुचरिते (traversed by wild beasts) / वने (forest) / वसति (lives) / दुर्मतिः (a misguided man)
ramayan::7421.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7421.essence: Ravana attacks Rama's worth to shake Sita's faith.
ramayan::7421.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Sita and tries to shame her attachment to Rama by pointing to Rama's exile, lost kingdom, and forest life.
ramayan::7421.simple_insight: Pride can twist reality until weakness looks like wisdom.
ramayan::7421.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps trying to break Sita's resolve. Here he sneers at Rama as a defeated exile with little time left, living among wild beasts after giving up his kingdom. The verse is part of Ravana's coercive argument, not a self-contained teaching.
ramayan::7421.modern_relevance: Someone under pressure may list every practical reason your choice is foolish, hoping your values will collapse under their confidence.
ramayan::7421.insight: It shows how contempt is used to erode loyalty and make steadfast love seem irrational.

ramayan::7422.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं वाक्यं प्रियार्हां प्रियवादिनीम् । अभिगम्य सुदुष्टात्मा राक्षसः काममोहितः । । 34916 । । जग्राह रावणस्सीतां बुधः खे रोहिणीमिव ।
ramayan::7422.verse_hindi: Just as Budha (planet Mercury) catches Rohini (a cluster of five stars) in the sky, the evilminded, infatuated Ravana advanced towards the pitiable, pleasing Sita and caught hold of her.
ramayan::7422.english_translation: Having said this to Maithili, the evil-minded Rakshasa, overcome by desire and delusion, approached and seized Sita, just as Budha seizes Rohini in the sky.
ramayan::7422.translation_literal: इत्युक्त्वा (having said thus) / मैथिलीं (to Maithili) / वाक्यं (speech) / प्रियार्हां (worthy of affection) / प्रियवादिनीम् (sweet-speaking) / अभिगम्य (approaching) / सुदुष्टात्मा (evil-minded) / राक्षसः (Rakshasa) / काममोहितः (deluded by desire) / जग्राह (seized) / रावणः (Ravana) / सीताम् (Sita) / बुधः (Budha) / खे (in the sky) / रोहिणीम् (Rohini) / इव (like)
ramayan::7422.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7422.essence: Unchecked desire crosses the line into force.
ramayan::7422.simple_meaning: Ravana ignores Sita's dignity, approaches her in desire, and seizes her by force.
ramayan::7422.simple_insight: Desire without restraint becomes violence in a single step.
ramayan::7422.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just tried to persuade Sita to abandon Rama. She refuses. In this moment, words fail him and lust takes over. He moves from argument to assault, revealing the full collapse of restraint.
ramayan::7422.modern_relevance: A conversation turns sour, and someone stops listening. The shift from persuasion to pressure is the moment you see what they really wanted all along.
ramayan::7422.insight: It shows how quickly entitlement turns into coercion when desire is not checked.

ramayan::7423.verse_sanskrit: वामेन सीतां पद्माक्षीं मूर्धजेषु करेण सः । । 34917 । । ऊर्वोस्तु दक्षिणेनैव परिजग्राह पाणिना ।
ramayan::7423.verse_hindi: Ravana seized with his left hand the lotuseyed Sita by the hair and lifted her by the thighs with his right hand.
ramayan::7423.english_translation: Ravana seized Sita, lotus-eyed and helpless, with his left hand by the hair and lifted her by the thighs with his right hand.
ramayan::7423.translation_literal: वामेन (with the left) / सीताम् (Sita) / पद्माक्षीम् (lotus-eyed) / मूर्धजेषु (by the hair) / करेण (with the hand) / सः (he) / ऊर्वोः (by the thighs) / तु (indeed) / दक्षिणेन (with the right) / एव (only) / परिजग्राह (seized) / पाणिना (with the hand)
ramayan::7423.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7423.essence: Desire here becomes force, and force exposes its own ugliness.
ramayan::7423.simple_meaning: Ravana grabbed Sita violently, holding her by the hair with one hand and lifting her by the thighs with the other.
ramayan::7423.simple_insight: Some acts are not passion at all — they are force stripped of dignity.
ramayan::7423.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just spoken to Sita and then lunges at her. This line shows the assault itself: he grabs her by the hair and lifts her bodily, turning persuasion into violence in a single brutal motion.
ramayan::7423.modern_relevance: A conversation can turn ugly in one second, and the body knows it before the mind does. This verse captures that sudden crossing of a line.
ramayan::7423.insight: It shifts attention from words to the moment power becomes physical coercion.

ramayan::7424.verse_sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा मृत्युसङ्काशं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रं महाभुजम् । । 34918 । । प्राद्रवन्गिरिसङ्काशं भयार्ता वनदेवताः ।
ramayan::7424.verse_hindi: The sylvan deities fled out of fear on seeing the dreadful appearance of Ravana who had sharp teeth and mighty arms. He looked like a mountain, a veritable god of death.
ramayan::7424.english_translation: The sylvan deities fled in fear on seeing Ravana, dreadful as death, with sharp teeth and mighty arms, mountain-like in form.
ramayan::7424.translation_literal: तम् (him) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / मृत्युसङ्काशम् (death-like) / तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रम् (sharp-teethed) / महाभुजम् (mighty-armed) / प्राद्रवन् (ran away) / गिरिसङ्काशम् (mountain-like) / भयार्ताः (stricken with fear) / वनदेवताः (forest deities)
ramayan::7424.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7424.essence: Even the forest recoils when violence arrives in full force.
ramayan::7424.simple_meaning: The forest spirits were terrified by Ravana’s terrifying form and fled at once.
ramayan::7424.simple_insight: Power can look overwhelming before it ever touches you.
ramayan::7424.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just seized Sita in the forest. As he stands there, huge, sharp-toothed, and fearsome, the forest deities themselves flee in terror. The verse heightens the horror of the abduction before the next scene continues.
ramayan::7424.modern_relevance: You can feel a room change when someone furious walks in. Before a word is spoken, fear has already done its work.
ramayan::7424.insight: It deepens the scene’s menace by showing even nature recoiling from Ravana.

ramayan::7425.verse_sanskrit: स च मायामयो दिव्यः खरयुक्तः खरस्वनः । । 34919 । । प्रत्यदृश्यत हेमाङ्गो रावणस्य महारथः ।
ramayan::7425.verse_hindi: There arrived the great  golden chariot of Ravana, illusive and wonderful, harnessed with donkeys and braying like donkeys.
ramayan::7425.english_translation: There arrived Ravana's great golden chariot, wondrous and illusory, harnessed with donkeys and sounding like donkeys.
ramayan::7425.translation_literal: सः (he) / च (and) / मायामयः (made of illusion) / दिव्यः (wonderful) / खरयुक्तः (harnessed with donkeys) / खरस्वनः (braying like donkeys) / प्रत्यदृश्यत (appeared) / हेमाङ्गः (golden-bodied / with golden parts) / रावणस्य (of Ravana) / महारथः (great chariot)
ramayan::7425.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7425.essence: Splendor can still be a mask for ugliness.
ramayan::7425.simple_meaning: Ravana's splendid chariot appears, but its beauty is deceptive and noisy, marked by donkeys instead of nobility.
ramayan::7425.simple_insight: Outward grandeur can still carry something absurd and hollow.
ramayan::7425.detailed_meaning: Sita has just been seized, and the forest spirits have fled in terror from Ravana's terrifying presence. Now his great golden chariot appears, dazzling but false, underscoring the violence of the moment as he prepares to carry her away.
ramayan::7425.modern_relevance: A polished entrance, a luxury car, a perfect profile, a confident voice — and yet something in it feels off. This verse catches the mismatch between glitter and character.
ramayan::7425.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to the quality underneath it.

ramayan::7426.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तां परुषैर्वाक्यैर्भर्त्सयन्स महास्वनः । । 34920 । । अङ्केनादाय वैदेहीं रथमारोपयत्तदा ।
ramayan::7426.verse_hindi: Reproaching the princess from Videha loudly and harshly, Ravana took her on his lap and put her on the chariot.
ramayan::7426.english_translation: Then Ravana, roaring loudly, rebuked Vaidehi with harsh words, took her onto his lap, and placed her on the chariot.
ramayan::7426.translation_literal: ततस्ताम् (then her) / परुषैः (harsh) / वाक्यैः (with words) / भर्त्सयन् (rebuking) / सः (he) / महास्वनः (loud-voiced) / अङ्केन (with lap) / आदाय (having taken) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / रथम् (to the chariot) / आरोपयत् (placed) / तदा (then)
ramayan::7426.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7426.essence: Power here is not persuasion; it is seizure.
ramayan::7426.simple_meaning: Ravana insults Sita, lifts her onto his lap, and puts her on his chariot.
ramayan::7426.simple_insight: Cruelty often begins with words and ends with force.
ramayan::7426.detailed_meaning: Ravana has reached Sita in the forest after terrifying the surrounding beings. He now turns his aggression directly on her, speaking harshly and physically seizing her. This is the moment abduction becomes undeniable.
ramayan::7426.modern_relevance: A conversation turns sharp, then suddenly physical boundaries are crossed. The shift is fast, ugly, and unmistakable.
ramayan::7426.insight: It shows how domination escalates from verbal abuse to bodily control.

ramayan::7427.verse_sanskrit: सा गृहीता विचुक्रोश रावणेन यशस्स्विनी । । 34921 । । रामेति सीता दुःखार्ता रामं दूरगतंवने ।
ramayan::7427.verse_hindi: Seized by Ravana, illustrious Sita screamed aloud Alas, Rama. for one who was far away in the forest.
ramayan::7427.english_translation: Seized by Ravana, illustrious Sita cried out, "Rama!" in her grief, calling to Rama who was far away in the forest.
ramayan::7427.translation_literal: सा (she) / गृहीता (seized) / विचुक्रोश (cried out) / रावणेन (by Ravana) / यशस्स्विनी (illustrious) / रामेति ("Rama!") / सीता (Sita) / दुःखार्ता (stricken with grief) / रामं (to Rama) / दूरगतं (gone far away) / वने (in the forest)
ramayan::7427.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7427.essence: Loss makes absence unbearable in a single cry.
ramayan::7427.simple_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita, and she cries out for Rama, who is far away in the forest.
ramayan::7427.simple_insight: Grief becomes sharper when the person you need is out of reach.
ramayan::7427.detailed_meaning: Ravana has lifted Sita into his chariot and is carrying her away by force. In that instant, with Rama absent and the forest between them, she cries out his name in helpless shock and heartbreak.
ramayan::7427.modern_relevance: You reach for your phone after the bad news, but the one person you want cannot answer. That empty distance is exactly what Sita feels here.
ramayan::7427.insight: It shows how separation can turn a single name into a cry for rescue.

ramayan::7428.verse_sanskrit: तामकामां स कामार्तः पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव । । 34922 । । विवेष्टमानामादाय उत्पपाताथ रावणः ।
ramayan::7428.verse_hindi: Passionate Ravana took hold of Sita who was not willing and was writhing in pain. He seized her  like (an eagle carrying away) a serpent queen and flew up.
ramayan::7428.english_translation: Passionate Ravana took hold of Sita, who was unwilling and writhing in pain, and flew up with her, like an eagle carrying off a serpent queen.
ramayan::7428.translation_literal: ताम् (her) / अकामाम् (unwilling) / सः (he) / कामार्तः (burned by desire) / पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव (like the queen of serpents) / विवेष्टमानाम् (writhing) / आदाय (having seized) / उत्पपात (leapt up) / अथ (then) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7428.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7428.essence: Desire here does not ask; it carries away.
ramayan::7428.simple_meaning: Ravana forcibly lifts Sita, who does not want him, and carries her away into the sky.
ramayan::7428.simple_insight: Desire can turn into violence in a single moment.
ramayan::7428.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already seized Sita and forced her onto his chariot. Here, he lifts her into the sky against her will, while she writhes in pain. The scene marks the terrible point where abduction becomes complete.
ramayan::7428.modern_relevance: A boundary is ignored, then crossed again, then carried farther than you thought possible. This is what entitlement looks like when it stops pretending to be restraint.
ramayan::7428.insight: It shows how unchecked craving becomes force, stripping away consent and dignity.

ramayan::7429.verse_sanskrit: ततस्सा राक्षसेन्द्रेण ह्रियमाणा विहायसा । । 34923 । । भृशं चुक्रोश मत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्ता यथाऽऽतुरा ।
ramayan::7429.verse_hindi: While Sita was being carried off in the sky by the king of demons,   she screamed a lot in agony and anxiety like a mad woman in a bewildered state:
ramayan::7429.english_translation: While Sita was being carried through the sky by the king of demons, she cried out loudly in agony and confusion, like a woman beside herself.
ramayan::7429.translation_literal: ततस् (then) / सा (she) / राक्षसेन्द्रेण (by the king of demons) / ह्रियमाणा (being carried off) / विहायसा (through the sky) / भृशम् (greatly) / चुक्रोश (cried out) / मत्ता इव (like one mad) / भ्रान्तचित्ता (with a bewildered mind) / यथा आतुरा (as if distressed)
ramayan::7429.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7429.essence: Abduction turns shock into helpless cries.
ramayan::7429.simple_meaning: Sita is being carried away through the sky by Ravana and cries out in deep distress, panic, and confusion.
ramayan::7429.simple_insight: Fear can strip away composure in an instant.
ramayan::7429.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is flying away with her through the sky. She is helpless, overwhelmed, and crying out in terror as the abduction becomes real. The verse lingers on her shock, not on any teaching.
ramayan::7429.modern_relevance: You realize too late that the situation has crossed a line, and your voice comes out raw before your mind can catch up.
ramayan::7429.insight: It captures the instant panic of losing control in a crisis.

ramayan::7430.verse_sanskrit: हा लक्ष्मण महाबाहो गुरुचित्तप्रसादक । । 34924 । । ह्रियमाणां न जानीषे रक्षसा माममर्षिणा ।
ramayan::7430.verse_hindi: Alas, O longarmed Lakshmana, you who used to entertain your brother do not know that I am being carried away by this ruthless demon.
ramayan::7430.english_translation: Alas, O long-armed Lakshmana, you who used to delight your brother do not know that I am being carried away by this ruthless demon.
ramayan::7430.translation_literal: हा (alas) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / महाबाहो (O long-armed one) / गुरुचित्तप्रसादक (you who delight your brother's mind) / ह्रियमाणाम् (being carried away) / न (not) / जानीषे (you know) / रक्षसा (by a demon) / माम् (me) / अमर्षिणा (ruthless, furious)
ramayan::7430.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7430.essence: Being seen too late can hurt as much as being taken.
ramayan::7430.simple_meaning: Sita cries out to Lakshmana in terror, saying he does not realize she is being abducted by a ruthless demon.
ramayan::7430.simple_insight: Fear makes the distance between people feel unbearable.
ramayan::7430.detailed_meaning: As Ravana carries Sita through the sky, she cries out in panic to Lakshmana below. Her words are not teaching but desperate lament: she is being taken by force, and the brother who once comforted her and Rama is absent at the worst moment.
ramayan::7430.modern_relevance: You call out for help, but the person you trust is out of reach. In that moment, fear turns every second into a wound.
ramayan::7430.insight: It shows how helplessness speaks when protection arrives too late.

ramayan::7431.verse_sanskrit: जीवितं सुखमर्थांश्च धर्महेतोः परित्यजन् । । 34925 । । ह्रियमाणामधर्मेण मां राघव न पश्यसि ।
ramayan::7431.verse_hindi: O Rama, you have given up your life, pleasure and treasure for the sake of righteousness. Do you not see me carried off by an unrighteous fellow ?
ramayan::7431.english_translation: O Rama, you have given up life, pleasure, and wealth for the sake of righteousness. Do you not see me being carried off by an unrighteous man?
ramayan::7431.translation_literal: जीवितं (life) / सुखम् (pleasure) / अर्थान् (wealth) / च (and) / धर्म-हेतोः (for the sake of righteousness) / परित्यजन् (giving up) / ह्रियमाणाम् (being carried off) / अधर्मेण (by unrighteousness) / माम् (me) / राघव (Raghava, Rama) / न (not) / पश्यसि (you see)
ramayan::7431.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7431.essence: Righteousness is hollow if it does not notice suffering in time.
ramayan::7431.simple_meaning: Sita reminds Rama that he sacrificed comfort and wealth for righteousness, and pleads that he notice her being taken away by injustice.
ramayan::7431.simple_insight: Doing the right thing means nothing if you cannot see the harm unfolding before you.
ramayan::7431.detailed_meaning: Sita is being carried through the sky by Ravana while Rama is elsewhere, separated by distance and shock. In her fear, she calls out to the man who gave up everything for dharma, asking why that same resolve has not yet reached her rescue.
ramayan::7431.modern_relevance: You can be proud of your principles and still miss the person nearest to you who is hurting. This verse lands where conviction has to become attention.
ramayan::7431.insight: It shifts duty from abstract virtue to active protection of the vulnerable in front of you.

ramayan::7432.verse_sanskrit: ननु नामाविनीतानां विनेतासि परन्तप । । 34926 । । कथमेवंविधं पापं न त्वं शासि हि रावणम् ।
ramayan::7432.verse_hindi: O scorcher of enemies you are the chastiser of the haughty. Why do you not punish such a sinner like Ravana.
ramayan::7432.english_translation: O scorcher of enemies, you are the chastiser of the unruly. Why do you not punish such a sinner as Ravana?
ramayan::7432.translation_literal: ननु (indeed) / नाम (surely) / अविनीतानाम् (of the unruly) / विनेतासि (you are the chastiser) / परन्तप (O scorcher of enemies) / कथम् (why) / एवम्-विधम् (such a) / पापम् (sinner) / न (not) / त्वम् (you) / शासि (punish) / हि (indeed) / रावणम् (Ravana)
ramayan::7432.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7432.essence: True strength is measured by whether it confronts obvious wrongdoing.
ramayan::7432.simple_meaning: Sita asks why Rama, who corrects the arrogant, is not punishing Ravana for this evil act.
ramayan::7432.simple_insight: Sometimes the hardest pain is watching power remain unused against obvious wrongdoing.
ramayan::7432.detailed_meaning: Sita, carried off by Ravana, speaks from the height of her helplessness and dignity. She reminds Rama that he is known as the one who restrains the unruly, then asks why that same force has not yet reached Ravana.
ramayan::7432.modern_relevance: You watch someone cross a clear line, and the person who could stop it stays silent. That silence can feel more painful than the wrong itself.
ramayan::7432.insight: It shifts the mind from passive lament to the demand that justice meet abuse of power.

ramayan::7433.verse_sanskrit: ननु सद्योऽविनीतस्य दृश्यते कर्मणःफलम् । । 34927 । । कालोऽप्यङ्गीभवत्यत्र सस्यानामिव पक्तये ।
ramayan::7433.verse_hindi: The effect of arrogant action cannot be seen right away. Just as the crop yields results only after ripening, in the same way it takes time. Time acts as a supporting factor.
ramayan::7433.english_translation: The effect of arrogant action cannot be seen right away. Just as the crop yields results only after ripening, in the same way it takes time. Time acts as a supporting factor.
ramayan::7433.translation_literal: ननु (indeed) / सद्यो (immediately) / अविनीतस्य (of the arrogant) / दृश्यते (is seen) / कर्मणः (of action) / फलम् (the result) / कालः (time) / अपि (also) / अङ्गीभवति (becomes a supporting factor) / अत्र (here) / सस्यानाम् (of crops) / इव (like) / पक्तये (for ripening)
ramayan::7433.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7433.essence: Arrogant action ripens slowly, but its result still comes.
ramayan::7433.simple_meaning: Arrogant actions do not show their results at once. Like crops that need time to ripen, consequences unfold slowly.
ramayan::7433.simple_insight: What looks delayed is still working its way toward you.
ramayan::7433.detailed_meaning: Sita is answering Ravana's boast and complaint from captivity in Lanka. She reminds him that wrongdoing does not always bear fruit instantly; like grain ripening in a field, its result comes in time, with time itself helping it mature.
ramayan::7433.modern_relevance: You send the harsh email in anger and hear nothing back for days. Silence does not mean it vanished; some actions only ripen later.
ramayan::7433.insight: It shifts the mind from expecting instant consequences to respecting delayed moral causality.

ramayan::7434.verse_sanskrit: त्वं कर्म कृतवानेतत्कालोपहतचेतनः । । 34928 । । जीवितान्तकरं घोरं रामाद्व्यसनमाप्नुहि ।
ramayan::7434.verse_hindi: Time has taken a toll of your senses. This has made you do what you have done. A great calamity is awaiting you in the hands of Rama. It will end your life.
ramayan::7434.english_translation: Time has taken a toll of your senses. This has made you do what you have done. A great calamity awaits you in the hands of Rama. It will end your life.
ramayan::7434.translation_literal: त्वं (you) / कर्म (deed) / कृतवान् (have done) / एतत् (this) / कालोपहतचेतनः (one whose mind is struck down by time) / जीवितान्तकरम् (life-ending) / घोरम् (terrible) / रामात् (from Rama) / व्यसनम् (misfortune) / आप्नुहि (you will obtain / meet with)
ramayan::7434.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7434.essence: A clouded mind can still choose the blow that destroys it.
ramayan::7434.simple_meaning: Your judgment has been ruined by time, so you have done this terrible thing. Now Rama will bring a disaster that ends your life.
ramayan::7434.simple_insight: Bad choices can feel clever in the moment and still lead straight to ruin.
ramayan::7434.detailed_meaning: The speaker is warning Ravana after rebuking his arrogance. The point is not theory but consequence: time has clouded his mind, and the path he has chosen now leads toward Rama’s fatal response.
ramayan::7434.modern_relevance: You know the message was reckless the moment you sent it, but pride kept it in motion. Now the fallout is already moving toward you.
ramayan::7434.insight: It shifts the mind from justifying a bad act to facing its inevitable cost.

ramayan::7435.verse_sanskrit: हन्तेदानीं सकामास्तु कैकेयी सह बान्धवैः । । 34929 । । ह्रिये यद्धर्मकामस्य धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनः ।
ramayan::7435.verse_hindi: Alas, the lawful wife of the glorious and righteous Rama is being abducted now. Let
ramayan::7435.english_translation: Alas, now Kaikeyi and her relatives act with selfish desire, while the glorious and righteous Rama's lawful wife is being carried off.
ramayan::7435.translation_literal: हन्त (alas) / इदानीम् (now) / सकामाः (driven by desire) / तु (indeed) / कैकेयी (Kaikeyi) / सह (with) / बान्धवैः (with relatives) / ह्रिये (in shame / alas) / यत् (that) / धर्मकामस्य (of the one who desires righteousness) / धर्मपत्नी (lawful wife) / यशस्विनः (of the glorious one)
ramayan::7435.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7435.essence: Selfish desire can shame an entire household.
ramayan::7435.simple_meaning: The speaker laments that Kaikeyi and her kin are acting from desire while Rama's rightful wife is being seized.
ramayan::7435.simple_insight: A single act of desire can bring shame to an entire house.
ramayan::7435.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the news of Sita's abduction has reached the grieving camp. The speaker does not offer strategy yet; he first names the moral wound: Kaikeyi's desire has helped set disaster in motion, and Rama's righteous household is being dishonoured.
ramayan::7435.modern_relevance: A family group chat turns sour after one selfish decision, and suddenly everyone is carrying the embarrassment. You feel how one person's appetite can stain an entire circle.
ramayan::7435.insight: It frames desire as a force that spreads shame beyond the person who acted.

ramayan::7436.verse_sanskrit: आमन्त्रये जनस्थाने कर्णिकारान्सुपुष्पितान् । । 34930 । । क्षिप्रं रामाय शंसध्वं सीतां हरति रावणः ।
ramayan::7436.verse_hindi: O karnikar trees in full bloom in Janasthana, tell Rama quickly that Ravana is kidnapping Sita.
ramayan::7436.english_translation: O karnikar trees in full bloom in Janasthana, tell Rama quickly that Ravana is kidnapping Sita.
ramayan::7436.translation_literal: आमन्त्रये (I address) / जनस्थाने (in Janasthana) / कर्णिकारान् (to the karnikar trees) / सुपुष्पितान् (full-blooming) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / रामाय (to Rama) / शंसध्वम् (tell) / सीताम् (Sita) / हरति (is carrying off) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7436.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7436.essence: A cry for help, not a lesson, breaks into the forest.
ramayan::7436.simple_meaning: The speaker calls out to the blooming trees in Janasthana and asks them to tell Rama at once that Ravana is taking Sita away.
ramayan::7436.simple_insight: Grief can make even the forest feel like a witness to your loss.
ramayan::7436.detailed_meaning: Sita has just been seized, and the forest is still ringing with the shock of it. In her desperation, she addresses the trees around Janasthana and begs them to carry the message to Rama. The verse is a cry, not a teaching.
ramayan::7436.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a crisis and reach for anything that might carry your message. Panic turns the world into a messenger.
ramayan::7436.insight: It shows raw loss rather than guidance, turning the landscape into a witness to abduction.

ramayan::7437.verse_sanskrit: माल्यवन्तं शिखरिणं वन्दे प्रस्रवणं गिरिम् । । 34931 । । क्षिप्रं रामाय शंस त्वं सीतां हरति रावणः ।
ramayan::7437.verse_hindi: I salute to Malyavan and  Prasravana mountains. Tell Rama at once that Ravana is carrying away Sita.
ramayan::7437.english_translation: I salute Mount Malyavan and Mount Prasravana. Tell Rama at once that Ravana is carrying away Sita.
ramayan::7437.translation_literal: माल्यवन्तं (Malyavan) / शिखरिणं (the mountain) / वन्दे (I salute) / प्रस्रवणं (Prasravana) / गिरिम् (mountain) / क्षिप्रं (quickly) / रामाय (to Rama) / शंस (tell) / त्वं (you) / सीतां (Sita) / हरति (is carrying away) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7437.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7437.essence: Urgency turns the landscape into a messenger.
ramayan::7437.simple_meaning: The speaker salutes the mountains and urgently asks them to tell Rama that Ravana is taking Sita away.
ramayan::7437.simple_insight: Grief can make even nature feel like a messenger.
ramayan::7437.detailed_meaning: Sita has been seized, and the forest itself becomes witness to the loss. The speaker turns to the mountains near Janasthana, asking them to carry the news to Rama immediately. It is a cry of urgency, not a teaching.
ramayan::7437.modern_relevance: You get the text no one wanted to send, and suddenly every second feels heavy. The mind starts looking for anything that can carry the message faster.
ramayan::7437.insight: It captures the shock of helplessness before action is possible.

ramayan::7438.verse_sanskrit: हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णां वन्दे गोदावरीं नदीम् । । 34932 । । क्षिप्रं रामाय शंस त्वं सीतां हरति रावणः ।
ramayan::7438.verse_hindi: O river Godavari abounding in swans and cranes, my salutations to you  Tell Rama immediately that Ravana is taking away Sita.
ramayan::7438.english_translation: O river Godavari abounding in swans and cranes, I salute you. Tell Rama immediately that Ravana is carrying away Sita.
ramayan::7438.translation_literal: हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाम् (abounding in swans and cranes) / वन्दे (I salute) / गोदावरीम् (Godavari) / नदीम् (river) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / रामाय (to Rama) / शंस (tell) / त्वम् (you) / सीताम् (Sita) / हरति (is carrying away) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7438.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7438.essence: She turns to the river because human help is already too far away.
ramayan::7438.simple_meaning: Sita turns to the river Godavari and asks it to carry her message to Rama: Ravana is taking her away.
ramayan::7438.simple_insight: Even in crisis, her mind reaches for help through the world around her.
ramayan::7438.detailed_meaning: Sita is being abducted through the forest. In her fear and urgency, she speaks to the Godavari as a witness and messenger, asking it to tell Rama that Ravana is carrying her away. The verse is part of a flowing cry for help, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7438.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a crisis and reach for anything that can carry your message. The mind grabs for help before it can even fully name the loss.
ramayan::7438.insight: It shows how panic narrows you to one urgent need: be heard before it is too late.

ramayan::7439.verse_sanskrit: दैवतानि च यान्यस्मिन्वने विविधपादपे । । 34933 । । नमस्करोम्यहं तेभ्योभर्तुश्शंसत मां हृताम् ।
ramayan::7439.verse_hindi: I offer my salutations to different deities residing in this forest abounding in trees of many kinds. Tell my husband about me that I am being whisked away.
ramayan::7439.english_translation: I offer my salutations to the deities dwelling in this forest of many kinds of trees. Tell my husband that I am being carried away.
ramayan::7439.translation_literal: दैवतानि (deities) / च (and) / यानि (which) / अस्मिन् (in this) / वने (forest) / विविध-पादपे (with many kinds of trees) / नमस्करोमि (I salute) / अहम् (I) / तेभ्यः (to them) / भर्तुः (to my husband) / शंसत (tell) / माम् (me) / हृताम् (carried away)
ramayan::7439.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7439.essence: She cannot stop the abduction, but she can still send the truth ahead.
ramayan::7439.simple_meaning: Sita, being carried off by Ravana, calls out to the forest deities and asks them to tell Rama what has happened to her.
ramayan::7439.simple_insight: Even in helplessness, she keeps speaking with dignity and purpose.
ramayan::7439.detailed_meaning: Ravana is carrying Sita away through the forest. As she passes the trees, rivers, and unseen presences around her, she turns to them like witnesses and messengers. This is not a teaching verse but a cry inside the flow of her abduction.
ramayan::7439.modern_relevance: You lose sight of the person you trust, and all you can do is send the message through whatever is still listening.
ramayan::7439.insight: It shows how to preserve agency in a moment of powerlessness: speak clearly, name what is happening, and ask for help to carry it forward.

ramayan::7440.verse_sanskrit: यानि कानि चिदप्यत्र सत्त्वानि निवसन्त्युत । । 34934 । । सर्वाणि शरणं यामि मृगपक्षिगणानपि ।
ramayan::7440.verse_hindi: I seek refuge in all those living beings as well as herds of animals and birds in the forest.
ramayan::7440.english_translation: I seek refuge in all the living beings here, and in the herds of animals and birds as well.
ramayan::7440.translation_literal: यानि (whatever) / कानि चिदपि (any and all) / अत्र (here) / सत्त्वानि (living beings) / निवसन्ति (dwelling) / उत (also) / सर्वाणि (all) / शरणं (refuge) / यामि (I go) / मृगपक्षिगणान् (groups of animals and birds) / अपि (also)
ramayan::7440.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7440.essence: Total vulnerability can become the beginning of surrender.
ramayan::7440.simple_meaning: Sita, lost in the forest, turns to every creature around her and asks for refuge. Her helplessness is complete, but so is her humility.
ramayan::7440.simple_insight: Even in helplessness, you can remain open instead of hardening.
ramayan::7440.detailed_meaning: Sita, alone after Ravana's abduction, speaks to the forest itself. After greeting the river and the forest spirits, she turns to every creature around her — animals, birds, and unseen beings — asking them to receive her plea and carry news to Rama.
ramayan::7440.modern_relevance: You are stranded in a place you never meant to be, with no one answering your calls. In that moment, the first victory is not control — it is still being able to ask.
ramayan::7440.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble dependence when circumstances are beyond your control.

ramayan::7441.verse_sanskrit: ह्रियमाणां प्रियां भर्तुः प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसीम् । । 34935 । । विवशाऽपहृता सीता रावणेनेति शंसत ।
ramayan::7441.verse_hindi: Tell Rama that his dear wife Sita whom he loves more than his life is abducted helplessly.
ramayan::7441.english_translation: Tell Rama that his dear wife Sita, whom he loves more than his life, has been helplessly carried off by Ravana.
ramayan::7441.translation_literal: ह्रियमाणाम् (being carried off) / प्रियम् (beloved) / भर्तुः (of the husband) / प्राणेभ्यः अपि (even than life) / गरीयसीम् (dearer, more weighty) / विवशा (helpless) / अपहृता (abducted) / सीता (Sita) / रावणेन (by Ravana) / इति (thus) / शंसत (tell)
ramayan::7441.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7441.essence: Loss becomes unbearable because the bond was real.
ramayan::7441.simple_meaning: Sita asks the forest beings to tell Rama that she has been abducted by Ravana, even though she is more precious to him than life itself.
ramayan::7441.simple_insight: Love is measured by absence too — what is taken reveals what was truly cherished.
ramayan::7441.detailed_meaning: Alone in the forest after Ravana's attack, Sita turns to every living being around her and sends a message to Rama. She is not only reporting the abduction; she is making sure he understands the gravity of what has been lost.
ramayan::7441.modern_relevance: You leave a message after a breakup, an accident, or a sudden disappearance, hoping the right person understands the full weight of what happened. Sita speaks with that same urgency.
ramayan::7441.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the bond the event has shattered.

ramayan::7442.verse_sanskrit: विदित्वा मां महाबाहुरमुत्रापि महाबलः । । 34936 । । आनेष्यति पराक्रम्य वैवस्वतहृतामपि ।
ramayan::7442.verse_hindi: If he knows that I am abducted by Yama, the god of death, that mighty, longarmed hero will save me even from there by virtue of his valour.
ramayan::7442.english_translation: If he knows that I have been taken by Yama himself, that mighty, long-armed hero will still rescue me by his valor.
ramayan::7442.translation_literal: विदित्वा (having known) / माम् (me) / महाबाहुः (the long-armed one) / अमुत्र अपि (even there) / महाबलः (the very powerful one) / आनेष्यति (will bring back) / पराक्रम्य (by exerting valor) / वैवस्वत-हृताम् अपि (even if taken by Yama)
ramayan::7442.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7442.essence: Love so strong it imagines no barrier as final.
ramayan::7442.simple_meaning: Sita believes Rama's strength and love are so great that even death itself would not stop him from rescuing her.
ramayan::7442.simple_insight: Deep trust can steady the heart even in the worst fear.
ramayan::7442.detailed_meaning: Ravana has carried Sita away into Lanka, and she is trying to keep hope alive through the terror. In this moment, she measures Rama not by distance or danger, but by the strength of his resolve. Even death would not be enough to stop him.
ramayan::7442.modern_relevance: You're waiting for a message that could change everything, and fear keeps inventing worst cases. This verse remembers what trust feels like when it is stronger than panic.
ramayan::7442.insight: It shifts the mind from helpless fear to confidence in steadfast love.

ramayan::7443.verse_sanskrit: सा तदा करुणा वाचो विलपन्ती सुदुःखिता । । 34937 । । वनस्पतिगतं गृध्रं ददर्शाऽयतलोचना ।
ramayan::7443.verse_hindi: When the griefstricken, largeeyed Sita was lamenting piteously, she saw the vulture (Jatayu) seated on a tree.
ramayan::7443.english_translation: When the grief-stricken, large-eyed Sita was lamenting piteously, she saw the vulture seated on a tree.
ramayan::7443.translation_literal: सा (she) / तदा (then) / करुणा (piteous) / वाचः (words) / विलपन्ती (lamenting) / सुदुःखिता (deeply sorrowful) / वनस्पति-गतम् (seated on a tree) / गृध्रम् (vulture) / ददर्श (saw) / आयत-लोचना (large-eyed)
ramayan::7443.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7443.essence: Grief can still notice a possible ally.
ramayan::7443.simple_meaning: Sita, overwhelmed by grief and crying out in pain, notices a vulture perched on a tree.
ramayan::7443.simple_insight: Even in panic, the mind still registers a possible sign of help.
ramayan::7443.detailed_meaning: After being seized by Ravana, Sita is crying out in helpless grief. As she laments, her large eyes catch sight of Jatayu perched on a tree. The moment is brief, but it marks the first glimpse of resistance in a scene of abduction.
ramayan::7443.modern_relevance: You are shaking, trying to make sense of a terrible moment, and then you notice one small sign that someone else may still be near.
ramayan::7443.insight: It keeps attention on the scene itself, not on interpretation or resolution.

ramayan::7444.verse_sanskrit: सा तमुद्वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणी रावणस्य वशं गता । 34938 । । समाक्रन्दद्भयपरा दुःखोपहतया गिरा ।
ramayan::7444.verse_hindi: The heavyhipped Sita felt frightened in the grip of Ravana. When she saw Jatayu she screamed, shaken by sorrow:
ramayan::7444.english_translation: Seeing him, Sita, beautiful-waisted and now in Ravana's power, cried out in fear, her voice broken by grief.
ramayan::7444.translation_literal: सा (she) / तम् (him) / उद्वीक्ष्य (having looked up) / सुश्रोणी (beautiful-waisted) / रावणस्य (of Ravana) / वशं (control) / गता (gone) / समाक्रन्दत् (cried out) / भयपरा (filled with fear) / दुःखोपहतया (struck by sorrow) / गिरा (with voice)
ramayan::7444.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7444.essence: Desperation speaks first when rescue suddenly appears.
ramayan::7444.simple_meaning: Sita sees Jatayu and cries out in fear and grief while trapped by Ravana.
ramayan::7444.simple_insight: Fear and sorrow can break the voice before they break the will.
ramayan::7444.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is carrying her away through the forest. When she spots Jatayu, the old vulture who may help her, her grief and fear surge into a cry for rescue. The verse is a vivid reaction, not a teaching.
ramayan::7444.modern_relevance: You catch sight of the one person who might help, and your voice comes out shaken. In that moment, panic and hope arrive together.
ramayan::7444.insight: It shows the instant when fear turns into a cry for help.

ramayan::7445.verse_sanskrit: जटायो पश्य मामद्य ह्रियमाणामनाथवत् । । 34939 । । अनेन राक्षसेन्द्रेण करुणं पापकर्मणा ।
ramayan::7445.verse_hindi: O Jatayu, see me now being carried away by the sinful king of demons in this pitiable condition as though I am an orphan.
ramayan::7445.english_translation: O Jatayu, see me now being carried away by the sinful king of demons in this pitiable condition as though I am an orphan.
ramayan::7445.translation_literal: जटायो (O Jatayu) / पश्य (see) / माम् (me) / अद्य (now) / ह्रियमाणाम् (being carried away) / अनाथवत् (like one without a protector) / अनेन (by this) / राक्षसेन्द्रेण (by the king of demons) / करुणम् (pitiably) / पापकर्मणा (by the one of evil deeds)
ramayan::7445.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7445.essence: Fear becomes clearer when you call it by name.
ramayan::7445.simple_meaning: Sita cries out to Jatayu, begging him to look at her as Ravana carries her away like a helpless orphan.
ramayan::7445.simple_insight: Even in terror, she names the injustice clearly.
ramayan::7445.detailed_meaning: Sita has just seen Jatayu while Ravana carries her through the forest. In her fear, she calls out to the old vulture as her only witness and protector, describing her helpless state before the abduction continues.
ramayan::7445.modern_relevance: You spot the one person who might still help as everything goes wrong. In that instant, you stop pretending and name exactly what is happening.
ramayan::7445.insight: It shows how to speak plainly in crisis instead of collapsing into silence.

ramayan::7446.verse_sanskrit: नैष वारयितुं शक्यस्तव क्रूरो निशाचरः । । 34940 । । सत्त्वाञ्जितकाशी च सायुधश्चैव दुर्मतिः ।
ramayan::7446.verse_hindi: This nightranger is equipped with weapons. Cruel, strong and evilminded, he has won wars. You cannot stop him.
ramayan::7446.english_translation: This cruel night-roamer cannot be stopped by you. He is armed, strong, and wicked-minded, and he has won battles.
ramayan::7446.translation_literal: नैष (this one) / वारयितुं (to be stopped) / शक्यः (able) / तव (by you) / क्रूरः (cruel) / निशाचरः (night-roamer) / सत्त्वाञ्जितकाशी (strong and battle-winning) / च (and) / सायुधः (armed) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / दुर्मतिः (evil-minded)
ramayan::7446.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7446.essence: Clear sight can be braver than resistance.
ramayan::7446.simple_meaning: Sita tells Jatayu that Ravana is too powerful, armed, and cruel to be stopped by him.
ramayan::7446.simple_insight: Sometimes courage is honest enough to admit a stronger force.
ramayan::7446.detailed_meaning: Sita, already seized by Ravana, sees Jatayu trying to resist. She does not flatter the moment with false hope. She names Ravana's weapons, strength, and cruelty, making clear that Jatayu cannot physically stop him.
ramayan::7446.modern_relevance: You see someone rushing at a fight they cannot win. The kindest thing is not false encouragement, but the truth about what they are facing.
ramayan::7446.insight: It shifts the mind from heroic denial to clear-eyed assessment of danger.

ramayan::7447.verse_sanskrit: रामाय तु यथातत्त्वं जटायो हरणं मम । । 34941 । । लक्ष्मणाय च तत्सर्वमाख्यातव्यमशेषतः ।
ramayan::7447.verse_hindi: O Jatayu narrate to Rama and Lakshmana the exact facts of my abduction and all the details without any omission.
ramayan::7447.english_translation: O Jatayu, tell Rama and Lakshmana exactly how I was carried off, and tell them everything without leaving anything out.
ramayan::7447.translation_literal: रामाय (to Rama) / तु (indeed) / यथातत्त्वम् (exactly as it is) / जटायो (O Jatayu) / हरणम् (abduction) / मम (of me) / लक्ष्मणाय (to Lakshmana) / च (and) / तत् (that) / सर्वम् (all) / आख्यातव्यम् (to be told) / अशेषतः (completely, without remainder)
ramayan::7447.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7447.essence: Even in helplessness, she insists on exact truth.
ramayan::7447.simple_meaning: Sita asks Jatayu to tell Rama and Lakshmana the full truth about her abduction, with nothing left out.
ramayan::7447.simple_insight: When you cannot act, clear truth becomes your last strength.
ramayan::7447.detailed_meaning: Ravana has taken Sita by force, and she uses her last moment with Jatayu to leave a precise witness behind. She wants Rama and Lakshmana to know exactly what happened, because the truth itself must travel back to them.
ramayan::7447.modern_relevance: After a bad call, you send the one message that matters: what happened, who was there, what was done. Clarity is how you protect yourself when you cannot protect the moment.
ramayan::7447.insight: It shifts you from panic to precise reporting, so the truth can reach the people who must act.

ramayan::7448.verse_sanskrit: तं शब्दमवसुप्तस्तु जटायुरथ शुश्रुवे । निरीक्ष्य रावणं क्षिप्रं वैदेहीं च ददर्श सः । । 3501 । ।
ramayan::7448.verse_hindi: While reposing, Jatayu heard the cry and at once looked up and saw Ravana and Vaidehi.
ramayan::7448.english_translation: While resting, Jatayu heard the cry and at once looked up and saw Ravana and Vaidehi.
ramayan::7448.translation_literal: तं (that) / शब्दम् (sound) / अवसुप्तः (while asleep, resting) / तु (indeed) / जटायुः (Jatayu) / अथ (then) / शुश्रुवे (heard) / निरीक्ष्य (having looked) / रावणम् (Ravana) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / च (and) / ददर्श (saw) / सः (he)
ramayan::7448.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7448.essence: Alertness turns a quiet moment into a turning point.
ramayan::7448.simple_meaning: Jatayu, resting nearby, hears the noise and quickly sees Ravana carrying Sita.
ramayan::7448.simple_insight: Even a moment of alertness can change the course of a life.
ramayan::7448.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Jatayu is at rest when he hears a sudden cry. He looks up and sees Ravana with Sita. This is the instant the rescue attempt begins, but the verse itself is only the scene-setting before Jatayu speaks.
ramayan::7448.modern_relevance: You hear a strange sound from the next room and look up just in time to catch what is happening. Some moments only matter because someone was awake enough to notice.
ramayan::7448.insight: It shifts attention from passive rest to immediate awareness when something urgent appears.

ramayan::7449.verse_sanskrit: ततः पर्वतकूटाभस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डः खगोत्तमः । वनस्पतिगतश्श्रीमान्व्याजहार शुभां गिरम् । । 3502 । ।
ramayan::7449.verse_hindi: Glorious Jatayu, the best among the birds, looked like the peak of a mountain.
ramayan::7449.english_translation: Then the glorious best of birds, sharp-beaked Jatayu, perched on a tree, spoke a noble line.
ramayan::7449.translation_literal: ततः (then) / पर्वतकूटाभः (mountain-peak-like) / तीक्ष्णतुण्डः (sharp-beaked) / खगोत्तमः (best among birds) / वनस्पतिगतः (perched on a tree) / श्रीमान् (glorious) / व्याजहार (spoke) / शुभाम् (auspicious) / गिरम् (speech)
ramayan::7449.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7449.essence: A noble presence is announced before the brave words arrive.
ramayan::7449.simple_meaning: Jatayu is described as a glorious bird perched on a tree, about to speak.
ramayan::7449.simple_insight: Even a brief description can build the weight of a great act.
ramayan::7449.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita, and Jatayu has seen it happen. Before he answers, Valmiki pauses to show his stature: glorious, mountain-like, sharp-beaked, perched above the forest. The verse is a visual setup for his brave declaration.
ramayan::7449.modern_relevance: You can feel the moment before someone speaks up in a crisis — the silence, the posture, the gathering of courage before the first clear sentence.
ramayan::7449.insight: It frames a speaker as worthy of attention before the speech begins.

ramayan::7450.verse_sanskrit: दशग्रीव स्थितो धर्मे पुराणे सत्यसंश्रयः । जटायुर्नाम नाम्नाहं गृध्रराजो महाबलः । । 3503 । ।
ramayan::7450.verse_hindi: O tenheaded Ravana, I am Jatayu, king of vultures. I am mighty. An eternal follower, of dharma, I am an adherent to truth.
ramayan::7450.english_translation: O ten-headed Ravana, I am Jatayu, king of vultures. I am mighty. I stand with dharma and I hold fast to truth.
ramayan::7450.translation_literal: दशग्रीव (O ten-headed one) / स्थितः (standing) / धर्मे (in dharma) / पुराणे (ancient) / सत्यसंश्रयः (taking refuge in truth) / जटायुः (Jatayu) / नाम (by name) / नाम्ना (by name) / अहम् (I) / गृध्रराजः (king of vultures) / महाबलः (mighty)
ramayan::7450.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7450.essence: Real strength is the willingness to stand with truth against power.
ramayan::7450.simple_meaning: Jatayu declares his identity, strength, and loyalty to dharma and truth before confronting Ravana.
ramayan::7450.simple_insight: Courage becomes noble when it serves what is right, not just what is powerful.
ramayan::7450.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has just seen Ravana seize Sita. From his perch in the forest, the old bird rises and speaks his name with pride. He is not boasting for vanity — he is announcing that his strength belongs to dharma, and he will use it now.
ramayan::7450.modern_relevance: You see something wrong in front of you, and your first instinct is to stay quiet because the other person has more power. Jatayu shows another way: name yourself, name your values, and step forward anyway.
ramayan::7450.insight: It shifts bravery from raw force to moral allegiance.

ramayan::7451.verse_sanskrit: राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः । लोकानां च हिते युक्तो रामो दशरथात्मजः । । 3504 । ।
ramayan::7451.verse_hindi: Rama, Dasarathas son, is the king of the entire world. He is equal to Indra and Varuna. He is ever engaged in the welfare of the entire world.
ramayan::7451.english_translation: Rama, Dasaratha's son, is the king of the entire world. He is equal to Indra and Varuna. He is ever engaged in the welfare of the entire world.
ramayan::7451.translation_literal: राजा (king) / सर्वस्य (of all) / लोकस्य (world) / महेन्द्र-वरुण-उपमः (equal to Indra and Varuna) / लोकानाम् (of the worlds / people) / च (and) / हिते (in welfare) / युक्तः (engaged) / रामः (Rama) / दशरथ-आत्मजः (Dasaratha's son)
ramayan::7451.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7451.essence: Real kingship is power used for everyone's good.
ramayan::7451.simple_meaning: Rama is not just a ruler; his greatness lies in using power for the welfare of everyone.
ramayan::7451.simple_insight: Leadership feels lighter when it is measured by service, not control.
ramayan::7451.detailed_meaning: Jatayu, dying after confronting Ravana, identifies Rama to the abductors as the rightful king of the world. In the middle of this crisis, he defines Rama not by conquest but by universal care and moral authority.
ramayan::7451.modern_relevance: A manager has the title, the corner office, and the loudest voice — but the team only trusts them when decisions protect everyone, not just the powerful.
ramayan::7451.insight: It shifts leadership from dominance to responsibility, and greatness from status to service.

ramayan::7452.verse_sanskrit: तस्यैषा लोकनाथस्य धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनी । सीता नाम वरारोहा यां त्वं हर्तुमिहेच्छसि । । 3505 । ।
ramayan::7452.verse_hindi: The lady you want to abduct from here is the famous Sita, the lawful wife of Rama, the lord of the world.
ramayan::7452.english_translation: The famous Sita, the lawful wife of Rama, the lord of the world, is the one you wish to abduct from here.
ramayan::7452.translation_literal: तस्याः (of that) / एषा (this) / लोकनाथस्य (of the lord of the world) / धर्मपत्नी (lawful wife) / यशस्विनी (famous, glorious) / सीता (Sita) / नाम (by name) / वरारोहा (of noble stature) / याम् (whom) / त्वम् (you) / हर्तुम् (to abduct) / इह (here) / इच्छसि (you wish)
ramayan::7452.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7452.essence: The abduction is not hidden by force; it is exposed by truth.
ramayan::7452.simple_meaning: Jatayu identifies Sita as Rama's honored wife and says Ravana wants to carry her away from there.
ramayan::7452.simple_insight: Some wrongs are made worse by knowing exactly whom they target.
ramayan::7452.detailed_meaning: Jatayu stands before Ravana and names the woman at the center of the crime: Sita, Rama's lawful wife. He is not speaking abstractly; he is marking the moral enormity of abducting a protected woman from the husband who guards the world.
ramayan::7452.modern_relevance: You watch someone twist a vulnerable person's life for desire. Naming who they are and what they deserve can be the first act of resistance.
ramayan::7452.insight: It frames the coming conflict as a direct violation of dharma, not a private desire.

ramayan::7453.verse_sanskrit: कथं राजास्थितो धर्मे परदारान्परामृशेत् । रक्षणीया विशेषेण राजदारा महाबल । । 3506 । ।
ramayan::7453.verse_hindi: How can a king who adheres to righteousness outrage anothers wife ? O powerful one, a kings wife in particular should be protected.
ramayan::7453.english_translation: How can a king who abides in righteousness outrage another man's wife? O mighty one, a king's wives in particular should be protected.
ramayan::7453.translation_literal: कथम् (how) / राजा (king) / आस्थितः (situated, abiding) / धर्मे (in righteousness) / परदारान् (another man's wives) / परामृशेत् (should touch, outrage) / रक्षणीया (to be protected) / विशेषेण (especially) / राजदाराः (king's wives) / महाबल (O mighty one)
ramayan::7453.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7453.essence: Power becomes shameful the moment it stops protecting.
ramayan::7453.simple_meaning: A just ruler should never violate another man's wife. Instead, he should protect women, and especially guard his own household.
ramayan::7453.simple_insight: True strength shows itself through restraint and protection, not through taking what is forbidden.
ramayan::7453.detailed_meaning: Rama is answering the threat against Sita by drawing a hard line around royal conduct. He reminds Ravana that a king bound to righteousness cannot behave like a predator, and that a ruler's first duty is protection, not violation.
ramayan::7453.modern_relevance: A manager with authority corners someone at a late-night office party and thinks no one will challenge him. The verse cuts through that illusion: power is measured by what it refuses to take.
ramayan::7453.insight: It shifts power from entitlement to responsibility, and makes restraint the mark of real authority.

ramayan::7454.verse_sanskrit: निवर्तय मतिं नीचां परदाराभिमर्शनात् । न तत्समाचरेद्धीरो यत्परोऽस्य विगर्हयेत् । । 3507 । । यथात्मनस्तथान्येषां दारा रक्ष्या विपश्चिता ।
ramayan::7454.verse_hindi: Refrain yourself from the vile thought of violating others wives. Wise men do not adopt what is censured by others. Just like ones own, the wise should protect others wives.
ramayan::7454.english_translation: Refrain yourself from the vile thought of violating other men's wives. Wise men do not adopt what is censured by others. Just like one's own, the wise should protect others' wives.
ramayan::7454.translation_literal: निवर्तय (refrain) / मतिम् (mind) / नीचाम् (vile) / परदाराभिमर्शनात् (from violating another man's wife) । न (not) / तत् (that) / समाचरेत् (should do) / धीरः (the wise one) / यत् (what) / परः (another) / अस्य (of him) / विगर्हयेत् (would censure) । यथा (just as) / आत्मनः (one's own) / तथा (so) / अन्येषाम् (of others) / दाराः (wives) / रक्ष्याः (to be protected) / विपश्चिता (by the wise).
ramayan::7454.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7454.essence: Wisdom begins where desire stops excusing itself.
ramayan::7454.simple_meaning: A wise person does not act in a way that would deserve blame. Other men's wives should be treated with the same protection as one's own.
ramayan::7454.simple_insight: Integrity means refusing the very action you would judge harshly in someone else.
ramayan::7454.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been warned that Sita is Rama's wife and that a righteous king must not violate another man's wife. This verse sharpens the warning into a moral rule: wisdom means avoiding what the world rightly condemns and protecting the wives of others as carefully as your own.
ramayan::7454.modern_relevance: You know the line you would never forgive in someone else. The verse asks you to stop before crossing it yourself, especially when desire is trying to rename itself.
ramayan::7454.insight: It shifts judgment inward: your standards must govern your own conduct first.

ramayan::7455.verse_sanskrit: धर्ममर्थं वा कामं वा शिष्टाश्शास्त्रेष्वनागतम् । । 3508 । । व्यवस्यन्त्यनु राजानं धर्मं पौलस्त्यनन्दन ।
ramayan::7455.verse_hindi: O son of Paulastya learned men determine the path of dharma artha and kama,  following a kings conduct even if  they are not declared in sastras.
ramayan::7455.english_translation: O son of Paulastya, learned men determine dharma, wealth, and desire by following a king's conduct, even when the scriptures do not spell it out.
ramayan::7455.translation_literal: धर्मम् (dharma) / अर्थम् (wealth) / वा (or) / कामम् (desire) / वा (or) / शिष्टाः (learned men) / शास्त्रेषु (in the scriptures) / अनागतम् (not arrived / not explicitly stated) / व्यवस्यन्ति (determine) / अनु (following) / राजानम् (the king) / धर्मम् (righteous conduct) / पौलस्त्यनन्दन (son of Paulastya)
ramayan::7455.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7455.essence: Your conduct becomes law for everyone watching.
ramayan::7455.simple_meaning: A ruler's behavior becomes a model for society. When the king acts well, people learn what is right even beyond written rules.
ramayan::7455.simple_insight: Your choices quietly teach others what is normal.
ramayan::7455.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned that a king's example shapes public morality. Learned people take their cue from royal conduct, even where no scripture gives a direct rule. The verse raises the stakes: leadership is not private.
ramayan::7455.modern_relevance: A manager cuts corners on one project, and soon the whole team starts treating shortcuts as normal. People copy the standard you live, not the policy document on the wall.
ramayan::7455.insight: It shifts attention from personal freedom to public responsibility: your behavior becomes a living rule for others.

ramayan::7456.verse_sanskrit: राजा धर्मस्य कामस्य द्रव्याणां चोत्तमो निधिः । । 3509 । । धर्मश्शुभं वा पापं वा राजमूलं प्रवर्तते ।
ramayan::7456.verse_hindi: A king is the best repository of rigteousness, material wealth and pleasures. The king is the root of dharma, virtue and sin.
ramayan::7456.english_translation: A king is the best repository of righteousness, wealth, and desire. Good or bad, what people call dharma grows from the king’s root.
ramayan::7456.translation_literal: राजा (king) / धर्मस्य (of righteousness) / कामस्य (of desire) / द्रव्याणां (of wealth, possessions) / च (and) / उत्तमः (the best) / निधिः (storehouse, repository) । धर्मः (righteousness) / शुभं (good) / वा (or) / पापं (bad) / वा (or) / राजमूलम् (rooted in the king) / प्रवर्तते (proceeds, arises) ।
ramayan::7456.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7456.essence: A ruler’s character becomes the moral climate of everyone beneath him.
ramayan::7456.simple_meaning: A ruler carries responsibility for both prosperity and moral order. A kingdom’s good and bad direction begins with the king.
ramayan::7456.simple_insight: Power is never neutral; it quietly trains everyone around it.
ramayan::7456.detailed_meaning: In Ravana’s court, the argument turns from private restraint to public responsibility. The speaker says a king is the storehouse of wealth, desire, and righteousness, because the ruler’s character sets the moral tone for everyone under him.
ramayan::7456.modern_relevance: A manager normalizes cutting corners, and soon the whole team does it. A parent’s habits become the household atmosphere. What you permit at the top quietly becomes the culture below.
ramayan::7456.insight: It shifts attention from personal authority to the moral patterns authority creates.

ramayan::7457.verse_sanskrit: पापस्वभावश्चपलः कथं त्वं रक्षसां वर । । 35010 । । ऐश्वर्यमभिसम्प्राप्तो विमानमिव दुष्कृतिः ।
ramayan::7457.verse_hindi: O best of demons  by nature you are sinful, and fickleminded. You do all forbidden acts. Otherwise,how could you get this wealth, like the celestial chariot?
ramayan::7457.english_translation: O best of demons, by nature you are sinful and fickle-minded. You do forbidden acts. Otherwise, how could you have gained this wealth, like a celestial chariot?
ramayan::7457.translation_literal: पापस्वभावः (sinful by nature) / चपलः (fickle-minded) / कथम् (how) / त्वम् (you) / रक्षसां वर (best of demons) / ऐश्वर्यम् (wealth, power) / अभिसम्प्राप्तः (having obtained) / विमानम् इव (like a celestial chariot) / दुष्कृतिः (one who does forbidden acts)
ramayan::7457.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7457.essence: Power gained through crookedness reveals the nature that earned it.
ramayan::7457.simple_meaning: Ravana is being called naturally unstable and prone to wrongdoing. His power is seen as proof of that corruption.
ramayan::7457.simple_insight: There is no glamour in tainted success; it carries its own decay.
ramayan::7457.detailed_meaning: A speaker rebukes Ravana directly, calling him the greatest of the demons and pointing to his unstable, harmful nature. His sudden wealth and power are treated not as achievement but as evidence of inner corruption.
ramayan::7457.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, but everyone knows it came through manipulation. The title looks bright from the outside, yet it already feels heavy in your hands.
ramayan::7457.insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the character that produced it.

ramayan::7458.verse_sanskrit: कामं स्वभावो यो यस्य न शक्यः परिमार्जितुम् । । 35011 । । न हि दुष्टात्मनामार्यमावसत्यालये चिरम् ।
ramayan::7458.verse_hindi: Indeed, it is not possible to erase the nature of any one, whatever it be. Prosperity does not rest for long in the house of the evilminded.
ramayan::7458.english_translation: Indeed, it is not possible to erase the nature of any one, whatever it be. Prosperity does not rest for long in the house of the evilminded.
ramayan::7458.translation_literal: कामम् (nature / tendency) / स्वभावः (innate nature) / यः (which) / यस्य (of whom) / न (not) / शक्यः (possible) / परिमार्जितुम् (to erase) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / दुष्टात्मनाम् (of the evilminded) / आर्यम् (prosperity / noble fortune) / आवसति (dwells) / आलये (in the house) / चिरम् (for long)
ramayan::7458.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7458.essence: What you are inside decides how long success can stay.
ramayan::7458.simple_meaning: A person's basic nature is hard to change. Ill-gotten success does not stay long with someone who is inwardly corrupt.
ramayan::7458.simple_insight: It leaves you wary of self-deception: what you are inside eventually shapes what you can keep.
ramayan::7458.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been warned about his conduct toward Rama. Instead of listening, he doubles down on his own logic. The verse becomes a hard truth about character: inner corruption cannot be hidden forever, and unstable success does not remain with it.
ramayan::7458.modern_relevance: You can land the promotion, win the argument, or get the recognition — but if the pattern underneath is rotten, it will show up again. What you are becoming matters more than what you temporarily hold.
ramayan::7458.insight: It shifts attention from outward gain to the inner pattern that determines whether success can last.

ramayan::7459.verse_sanskrit: विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा रामो महाबलः । । 35012 । । नापराध्यति धर्मात्मा कथं तस्यापराध्यसि ।
ramayan::7459.verse_hindi: Powerful and righteous Rama has not offended you, your kingdom or your city. Why do you offend him?
ramayan::7459.english_translation: Powerful and righteous Rama has not offended you, your kingdom, or your city. Why do you offend him?
ramayan::7459.translation_literal: विषये (in [your] territory) / वा (or) / पुरे (in [your] city) / वा (or) / ते (to you) / यदा (when) / रामः (Rama) / महाबलः (mighty) / नापराध्यति (does not offend) / धर्मात्मा (righteous one) / कथं (why) / तस्य (of him) / अपराध्यसि (do you offend)
ramayan::7459.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7459.essence: Do not answer a harmless person with harm.
ramayan::7459.simple_meaning: Rama has done nothing wrong to you. The verse asks why you would still act against him.
ramayan::7459.simple_insight: It feels clearer to stop harming someone who has not harmed you.
ramayan::7459.detailed_meaning: A speaker is defending Rama in the middle of a tense exchange. He points out that Rama has not wronged Ravana in his land, city, or person, and presses the moral question: why attack a righteous man who has given no offense?
ramayan::7459.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in traffic, and your whole body wants to retaliate. This verse interrupts that reflex: not every irritation is an injury, and not every person deserves your counterattack.
ramayan::7459.insight: It shifts the mind from retaliation to moral proportion.

ramayan::7460.verse_sanskrit: यदि शूर्पणखाहेतोर्जनस्थानगतः खरः । । 35013 । । अतिवृत्तो हतः पूर्वं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । अत्र ब्रूहि यथातत्त्वं को रामस्य व्यतिक्रमः । । 35014 । । यस्य त्वं लोकनाथस्य भार्यां हृत्वा गमिष्यसि ।
ramayan::7460.verse_hindi: On account of Surpanakha, Khara trespassed into Janasthana and got killed by Rama, without much effort. Tell me truly, what transgression (of dharma) did he commit for which you are stealing away the wife of Rama who is the lord of this world?.
ramayan::7460.english_translation: On account of Surpanakha, Khara trespassed into Janasthana and got killed by Rama, without much effort. Tell me truly, what transgression did he commit for which you are stealing away the wife of Rama, the lord of this world?
