ramayan::7460.translation_literal: यदि (if) / शूर्पणखाहेतोः (because of Surpanakha) / जनस्थानगतः (having gone to Janasthana) / खरः (Khara) / अतिवृत्तः (having overstepped) / हतः (was slain) / पूर्वं (earlier) / रामेण (by Rama) / अक्लिष्टकर्मणा (by the one whose deeds are effortless) / अत्र (here) / ब्रूहि (tell) / यथातत्त्वम् (truly) / को (what) / रामस्य (of Rama) / व्यतिक्रमः (transgression) / यस्य (whose) / त्वम् (you) / लोकनाथस्य (of the lord of the world) / भार्याम् (wife) / हृत्वा (having stolen) / गमिष्यसि (will go)
ramayan::7460.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7460.essence: Ravana condemns Rama while revealing his own guilt.
ramayan::7460.simple_meaning: Ravana argues that Rama has done nothing wrong, while Ravana himself has already crossed the line by abducting Sita.
ramayan::7460.simple_insight: Self-justification collapses when you compare your act to the harm you condemn in others.
ramayan::7460.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being warned again and again. Instead of listening, he tries to defend himself by pointing to Khara's death and Rama's supposed fault. But the argument exposes him: Rama acted in defense, while Ravana is stealing Sita, the wife of a righteous king.
ramayan::7460.modern_relevance: You can feel the mind trying to win an argument after it has already crossed a line. The facts do not change just because you can speak loudly about someone else's mistake.
ramayan::7460.insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to seeing the moral gap between their defense and your own wrongdoing.

ramayan::7461.verse_sanskrit: क्षिप्रं विसृज वैदेहीं मा त्वा घोरेण चक्षुषा । । 35015 । । दहेद्दहनभूतेन वृत्रमिन्द्राशनिर्यथा ।
ramayan::7461.verse_hindi: Leave Vaidehi at once lest with her fierce looks you should be burnt down like demon Vrtra by the thunderbolt of Indra.
ramayan::7461.english_translation: Leave Vaidehi at once, lest her fierce gaze burn you down like Indra's thunderbolt burned Vrtra.
ramayan::7461.translation_literal: क्षिप्रम् (at once) / विसृज (release) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / मा (lest) / त्वा (you) / घोरेण (with fierce) / चक्षुषा (with gaze) / दहेत् (may burn) / दहनभूतेन (with burning force) / वृत्रम् (Vrtra) / इन्द्राशनिः (Indra's thunderbolt) / यथा (as)
ramayan::7461.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7461.essence: Clinging to what is sacred can turn into self-destruction.
ramayan::7461.simple_meaning: Ravana warns that Sita should be released immediately, because her fierce look could destroy the one who holds her.
ramayan::7461.simple_insight: A warning can carry fear, but it cannot undo the harm already chosen.
ramayan::7461.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still trying to justify keeping Sita. He warns that her gaze itself is dangerous, comparing her power to Indra's thunderbolt striking Vrtra. The line is part of a tense argument urging him to release her before ruin follows.
ramayan::7461.modern_relevance: You keep holding onto something you already know is hurting you. The warning signs are there, but you keep rationalising them away.
ramayan::7461.insight: It pushes you to notice danger early instead of explaining it away.

ramayan::7462.verse_sanskrit: सर्पमाशीविषं बद्ध्वा वस्त्रान्ते नावबुध्यसे । । 35016 । । ग्रीवायां प्रतिसक्तं च कालपाशं न पश्यसि ।
ramayan::7462.verse_hindi: You are not aware that you are tying a venomous snake with the skirt of your cloth. worn by you. You are not able to see the noose of death tightened around your neck.
ramayan::7462.english_translation: You do not realize that you are tying a venomous snake to the edge of your cloth. You do not see the noose of death already tightened around your neck.
ramayan::7462.translation_literal: सर्पम् (snake) / आशीविषम् (venomous) / बद्ध्वा (having tied) / वस्त्रान्ते (at the edge of the cloth) / न (not) / अवबुध्यसे (you understand) । / ग्रीवायाम् (on the neck) / प्रतिसक्तम् (tightened) / च (and) / कालपाशम् (noose of death) / न (not) / पश्यसि (you see)
ramayan::7462.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7462.essence: What you cling to in pride can become the rope that ends you.
ramayan::7462.simple_meaning: Ravana is being warned that keeping Sita is like holding a poisonous snake and a death noose without realizing it.
ramayan::7462.simple_insight: Pride can make danger feel invisible until it is too late.
ramayan::7462.detailed_meaning: Ravana has dismissed every warning and keeps pressing his claim on Sita. In this sharp rebuke, he is told that what he is holding is not a prize but a fatal threat already wrapped around him.
ramayan::7462.modern_relevance: You keep a relationship, habit, or decision because it feels powerful, even while it slowly poisons everything around it. The warning usually arrives before the collapse.
ramayan::7462.insight: It shifts the mind from possession to perception: what feels like control may already be self-destruction.

ramayan::7463.verse_sanskrit: स भारस्सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत् । । 35017 । । तदन्नमपि भोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम् ।
ramayan::7463.verse_hindi: O gentle Ravana one should carry that much of weight which does not tire him. One should eat only that wholesome food which can be easily digested.
ramayan::7463.english_translation: O gentle Ravana, one should carry only the weight that does not tire him. One should eat only wholesome food that can be digested easily.
ramayan::7463.translation_literal: सः (that) / भारः (weight) / सौम्य (gentle one) / भर्तव्यः (to be borne) / यः (which) / नरम् (a person) / न (not) / आवसादयेत् (should tire) / तत् (that) / अन्नम् (food) / अपि (also) / भोक्तव्यम् (to be eaten) / जीर्यते (is digested) / यत् (that which) / अनामयम् (wholesome)
ramayan::7463.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7463.essence: Only burdens within your capacity can be borne safely.
ramayan::7463.simple_meaning: Take on only what does not exhaust you, and choose only what truly suits you. The lesson is about limits, restraint, and what is actually sustainable.
ramayan::7463.simple_insight: You do not prove strength by overloading yourself. Real wisdom knows the measure that keeps you steady.
ramayan::7463.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned not to keep Sita, because she is a burden that will destroy him. The verse turns that warning into a general rule: carry only what you can bear, and take in only what your system can digest.
ramayan::7463.modern_relevance: You keep saying yes to one more project, one more obligation, one more late night. Then your body, your mind, and your relationships start showing the cost. This verse asks you to notice the load before it breaks you.
ramayan::7463.insight: It teaches you to measure capacity before committing, so your choices remain sustainable instead of self-defeating.

ramayan::7464.verse_sanskrit: यत्कृत्वा न भवेद्धर्मो न कीर्तिर्न यशो भुवि । । 35018 । । शरीरस्य भवेत्खेदः कस्तत्कर्म समाचरेत् ।
ramayan::7464.verse_hindi: Who will do such a deed which cannot beget dharma, fame or glory in the world? Who will do such deeds that bring only exhaustion to the body?
ramayan::7464.english_translation: Who would do a deed that brings neither dharma, nor fame, nor glory in the world? Who would do an act that only tires the body?
ramayan::7464.translation_literal: यत् (which) / कृत्वा (having done) / न (not) / भवेत् (would be) / धर्मः (dharma) / न (not) / कीर्तिः (fame) / न (not) / यशः (glory) / भुवि (in the world) / शरीरस्य (of the body) / भवेत् (would be) / खेदः (weariness) / कः (who) / तत् (that) / कर्म (deed) / समाचरेत् (would perform)
ramayan::7464.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7464.essence: A hard action is not noble if it leaves only exhaustion and nothing worthwhile.
ramayan::7464.simple_meaning: Ravana argues that no sensible person should do work that brings no right conduct, no respect, and only bodily exhaustion.
ramayan::7464.simple_insight: Not every effort deserves your energy. Some actions cost too much and give back nothing lasting.
ramayan::7464.detailed_meaning: Ravana is defending his own position in a tense exchange with a warning about burden and consequence. He asks why anyone would choose an act that produces no dharma, no honor, and only fatigue, revealing his practical but self-serving logic.
ramayan::7464.modern_relevance: You are about to say yes to another draining commitment because you want to seem capable. Before you do, ask whether it builds anything worth carrying.
ramayan::7464.insight: It pushes you to test an action by its deeper value, not just by the effort it demands.

ramayan::7465.verse_sanskrit: षष्टिर्वर्षसहस्राणि मम जातस्य रावण । । 35019 । । पितृपैतामहं राज्यं यथावदनुतिष्ठतः ।
ramayan::7465.verse_hindi: Sixty thousand years ago I was born, O Ravana  Since then I have ruled justly my hereditary kingdom.
ramayan::7465.english_translation: Sixty thousand years ago I was born, O Ravana. Since then I have ruled justly my hereditary kingdom.
ramayan::7465.translation_literal: षष्टिः (sixty) / वर्षसहस्राणि (thousand years) / मम (my) / जातस्य (of one born) / रावण (O Ravana) / पितृपैतामहं (ancestral, inherited from father and grandfather) / राज्यं (kingdom) / यथावत् (properly, justly) / अनुतिष्ठतः (of one ruling, carrying out)
ramayan::7465.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7465.essence: Years of rule mean nothing without just conduct.
ramayan::7465.simple_meaning: Ravana claims he has ruled his inherited kingdom properly for a very long time, presenting himself as a rightful and established king.
ramayan::7465.simple_insight: Long possession does not equal moral right; what matters is how you have held power.
ramayan::7465.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to justify his authority in the middle of a tense confrontation. He reminds the listener that he is no newcomer: he has ruled his ancestral kingdom for sixty thousand years and believes that record proves his legitimacy.
ramayan::7465.modern_relevance: You may have held a position for years and start treating tenure like proof. But time in charge is not the same as integrity in charge.
ramayan::7465.insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement based on duration to legitimacy earned through conduct.

ramayan::7466.verse_sanskrit: वृद्धोऽहं त्वं युवा धन्वी सशरः कवची रथी । । 35020 । । तथाप्यादाय वैदेहीं कुशली न गमिष्यसि ।
ramayan::7466.verse_hindi: I am old, you are young, wielding a bow and arrows, with shield to protect and chariot to ride. Even then I will not let you go safe with Vaidehi kidnapped.
ramayan::7466.english_translation: I am old, you are young, wielding a bow and arrows, with shield to protect and chariot to ride. Even then I will not let you go safe with Vaidehi kidnapped.
ramayan::7466.translation_literal: वृद्धः (old) अहम् (I) त्वम् (you) युवा (young) धन्वी (bow-holder) सशरः (with arrows) कवची (armored) रथी (chariot-rider) तथापि (even then) आदाय (having taken) वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) कुशली (safe) न (not) गमिष्यसि (you will go)
ramayan::7466.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7466.essence: Age and weapons mean nothing when resolve refuses surrender.
ramayan::7466.simple_meaning: Even with age against him and weapons on Ravana’s side, the speaker says Ravana will not leave safely with Sita.
ramayan::7466.simple_insight: Strength does not guarantee escape when conscience and courage stand in the way.
ramayan::7466.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita, and the confrontation has become direct. The speaker measures age, weapons, and strength, then rejects Ravana’s confidence outright. This is not a teaching verse but a defiant step in the kidnapping crisis.
ramayan::7466.modern_relevance: A smaller person stands between you and someone being taken advantage of, and the size difference suddenly matters less than resolve. Some moments are decided by refusal, not force.
ramayan::7466.insight: It frames the clash as moral resistance, not mere physical contest.

ramayan::7467.verse_sanskrit: न शक्तस्त्वं बलाद्धर्तुं वैदेहीं मम पश्यतः । । 35021 । । हेतुभिर्न्यायसंसिद्धैद्धृवां वेदश्रुतीमिव ।
ramayan::7467.verse_hindi: You cannot carry Vaidehi by force within my very sight just as the everlasting revelations of the Vedas cannot be robbed by mere logic of reason.
ramayan::7467.english_translation: You cannot carry Vaidehi away by force while I am watching, just as the eternal Vedic revelation cannot be taken away by mere reasoning.
ramayan::7467.translation_literal: न शक्तः (not able) / त्वम् (you) / बलात् (by force) / हर्तुम् (to carry away) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / मम (my) / पश्यतः (while seeing) / हेतुभिः (by reasons) / न्यायसंसिद्धैः (established by logic) / धृवाम् (eternal) / वेदश्रुतीम् (Vedic revelation) / इव (like)
ramayan::7467.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7467.essence: Force cannot take what righteous guardianship refuses to yield.
ramayan::7467.simple_meaning: Ravana cannot abduct Sita by force while Rama is present. The claim is absolute: strength and argument both fail against what is firmly protected.
ramayan::7467.simple_insight: There is steadiness in knowing that some things can be guarded without hesitation.
ramayan::7467.detailed_meaning: Rama stands before Ravana after Sita's abduction. Ravana is powerful, armed, and arrogant, but Rama answers with calm certainty: not even force can take Vaidehi from him while he watches. The verse turns protection into a moral boundary.
ramayan::7467.modern_relevance: Someone tries to pressure you into giving up a boundary you already know is right — in a meeting, a family argument, or a private confrontation. This verse reminds you that calm refusal can be stronger than force.
ramayan::7467.insight: It teaches you to hold a boundary without apology when something precious is under your protection.

ramayan::7468.verse_sanskrit: युद्ध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ रावण । । 35022 । । शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथापूर्वं खरस्तथा ।
ramayan::7468.verse_hindi: O Ravana, if you are brave, fight with me. In a moment, you will be killed like Khara and lie down on the ground.
ramayan::7468.english_translation: O Ravana, if you are brave, fight with me. In a moment, you will be killed like Khara and lie down on the ground.
ramayan::7468.translation_literal: युद्ध्यस्व (fight) / यदि (if) / शूरः (brave) / असि (you are) / मुहूर्तं (for a moment) / तिष्ठ (stay) / रावण (Ravana) / शयिष्यसे (you will lie down) / हतः (killed) / भूमौ (on the ground) / यथा (like) / पूर्वं (before) / खरः (Khara) / तथा (so)
ramayan::7468.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7468.essence: True courage speaks plainly to power and refuses to shrink.
ramayan::7468.simple_meaning: Hanuman challenges Ravana directly and warns that he will fall dead like Khara if he fights.
ramayan::7468.simple_insight: Some threats are not bluster. Courage can be calm, direct, and completely unafraid.
ramayan::7468.detailed_meaning: Hanuman stands before Ravana in Lanka after proving he cannot be intimidated. He rejects Ravana's boastful power and dares him to fight, naming Khara as the reminder of what happens to those who underestimate dharma-backed strength.
ramayan::7468.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, expecting you to fold. You look them in the eye and answer plainly, without shaking or raising your voice.
ramayan::7468.insight: It shows how fearless speech can expose arrogance and stop intimidation before it spreads.

ramayan::7469.verse_sanskrit: असकृत्संयुगे येन निहता दैत्यदानवाः । । 35023 । । नचिराच्चीरवासास्त्वां रामो युधि वधिष्यति ।
ramayan::7469.verse_hindi: Clad in bark garments, Rama, who has often slain demons in the past will soon kill you in war.
ramayan::7469.english_translation: Clad in bark garments, Rama, who has often slain demons in the past, will soon kill you in war.
ramayan::7469.translation_literal: असकृत् (often) / संयुगे (in battle) / येन (by whom) / निहता (slain) / दैत्यदानवाः (demons and titans) / नचिरात् (soon) / चीरवासाः (wearing bark garments) / त्वाम् (you) / रामः (Rama) / युधि (in war) / वधिष्यति (will kill)
ramayan::7469.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7469.essence: Even Ravana names the force that will destroy him.
ramayan::7469.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that Rama, though dressed as an exile, has already destroyed many powerful enemies and will soon kill him too.
ramayan::7469.simple_insight: Pride can still recognize the blade that is about to end it.
ramayan::7469.detailed_meaning: Ravana answers Rama's challenge by dismissing the threat and then revealing it: Rama has already slain many fierce beings, and that same warrior will soon strike him down. The verse sits inside a tense exchange before battle, sharpening Ravana's fear into a boast.
ramayan::7469.modern_relevance: You laugh off a warning, but part of you already knows the person across from you is serious. The bravado is loud; the outcome is already closing in.
ramayan::7469.insight: It turns empty confidence into a sign of impending defeat.

ramayan::7470.verse_sanskrit: किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं गतौदूरं नृपात्मजौ । । 35024 । । क्षिप्रं त्वं नश्यसे नीच तयोर्भीतो न संशयः ।
ramayan::7470.verse_hindi: What can I do? O mean fellow the two princes have gone far away.You will soon be destroyed out of fear for them. There is no doubt.
ramayan::7470.english_translation: What can I do? O mean fellow, the two princes have gone far away. You will soon be destroyed out of fear for them. There is no doubt.
ramayan::7470.translation_literal: किं (what) / नु (indeed) / शक्यं (possible) / मया (by me) / कर्तुं (to do) / गतौदूरं (gone far away) / नृपात्मजौ (the two princes) / क्षिप्रं (soon) / त्वं (you) / नश्यसे (will perish) / नीच (base fellow) / तयोः (of them) / भीतः (afraid) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::7470.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7470.essence: Fear and insult can hide the same weakness.
ramayan::7470.simple_meaning: Ravana taunts his enemy, saying the princes are far away and their fear will soon destroy him.
ramayan::7470.simple_insight: Pride can turn fear into a weapon before the blow even lands.
ramayan::7470.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking after the princes have moved away from the immediate scene. He mocks their absence and tries to break his opponent with contempt, but the real force here is his own arrogance hardening into certainty.
ramayan::7470.modern_relevance: Someone leaves the room, and the other person starts talking louder, meaner, more certain. The confidence is often just fear wearing armor.
ramayan::7470.insight: It shows how arrogance uses contempt to cover vulnerability.

ramayan::7471.verse_sanskrit: न हि मे जीवमानस्य नयिष्यसि शुभामिमाम् । । 35025 । । सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीं रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम् ।
ramayan::7471.verse_hindi: I will not let you take away the auspicious, lotuseyed Sita, the dear consort of Rama as long as I am alive.
ramayan::7471.english_translation: I will not let you take away the auspicious, lotus-eyed Sita, the dear consort of Rama, as long as I am alive.
ramayan::7471.translation_literal: न हि (indeed not) / मे (of me) / जीवमानस्य (while living) / नयिष्यसि (you will take away) / शुभाम् (auspicious) / इमाम् (this) / सीताम् (Sita) / कमलपत्राक्षीम् (lotus-petaled-eyed) / रामस्य (of Rama) / महिषीम् (queen/consort) / प्रियाम् (dear)
ramayan::7471.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7471.essence: Love becomes duty when protection is the only thing left.
ramayan::7471.simple_meaning: He refuses to let anyone take Sita away while he is still alive.
ramayan::7471.simple_insight: Some loyalties are non-negotiable. You stand, or you fall, but you do not hand over what must be protected.
ramayan::7471.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has reached the moment of abduction, and the threat is immediate. Jatayu, already old and outmatched, speaks with total resolve: Sita will not be taken while he still breathes. The verse is the cry of duty under impossible odds.
ramayan::7471.modern_relevance: You see someone being pushed too far and your body moves before your fear does. A younger sibling, a colleague, a stranger on a train — something in you says: not while I’m here.
ramayan::7471.insight: It shifts you from passive concern to active protection when someone vulnerable is under threat.

ramayan::7472.verse_sanskrit: अवश्यं तु मया कार्यं प्रियं तस्य महात्मनः । । 35026 । । जीवितेनापि रामस्य तथा दशरथस्य च ।
ramayan::7472.verse_hindi: I should do this important work of those great souls, Rama and Dasaratha, even if it claims my life.
ramayan::7472.english_translation: I should do the important work of those great souls, Rama and Dasaratha, even if it costs me my life.
ramayan::7472.translation_literal: अवश्यं (certainly) / तु (but) / मया (by me) / कार्यं (work to be done) / प्रियम् (dear/important) / तस्य (of that) / महात्मनः (great soul) / जीवितेन (with life) / अपि (even) / रामस्य (of Rama) / तथा (and so) / दशरथस्य (of Dasharatha) / च (and)
ramayan::7472.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7472.essence: Duty can demand your life and still be non-negotiable.
ramayan::7472.simple_meaning: He knows he must carry out a necessary task for Rama and Dasharatha, even if it means dying for it.
ramayan::7472.simple_insight: Real duty is measured by what you’re willing to lose for it.
ramayan::7472.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands before the abducted Sita, furious and cornered, while Rama and Lakshmana are far away. In that tense moment, he admits that a task tied to Rama and Dasharatha must be done, even at the cost of his own life.
ramayan::7472.modern_relevance: You promised to finish the job after everyone else had gone home. Your body is tired, your pride is tired, but the task still belongs to you.
ramayan::7472.insight: It shifts the mind from self-preservation to responsibility, showing that some obligations outrank comfort and fear.

ramayan::7473.verse_sanskrit: तिष्ठ तिष्ठ दशग्रीव मुहूर्तं पश्य रावण । । 35027 । । युद्धातिथ्यं प्रदास्यामि यथाप्राणं निशाचर । वृन्तादिव फलं त्वां तु पातयेयं रथोत्तमात् । । 35028 । ।
ramayan::7473.verse_hindi: O ten headed Ravana stay, stay for a while. O demon  as long as I am alive I will treat you with the hospitality of war. You will be pulled down from this best of the chariots like a ripe fruit drops from the stalk.
ramayan::7473.english_translation: O ten-headed Ravana, stay, stay for a moment. O night-roamer, I will give you the hospitality of battle as long as I live. I will make you fall from this finest of chariots like a ripe fruit from its stalk.
ramayan::7473.translation_literal: तिष्ठ (stay) / तिष्ठ (stay) / दशग्रीव (ten-headed one) / मुहूर्तं (for a moment) / पश्य (see) / रावण (Ravana) / युद्धातिथ्यं (battle-hospitality) / प्रदास्यामि (I will give) / यथाप्राणं (as long as life lasts) / निशाचर (night-roamer) / वृन्तात् (from the stalk) / इव (like) / फलम् (a fruit) / त्वाम् (you) / तु (indeed) / पातयेयम् (I will make fall) / रथोत्तमात् (from the finest chariot)
ramayan::7473.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7473.essence: Honor can be stronger than survival.
ramayan::7473.simple_meaning: Jatayu challenges Ravana and promises to fight him until death, saying he will knock him down from his chariot like fruit falling from a stalk.
ramayan::7473.simple_insight: Courage can be fierce, even when the odds are hopeless.
ramayan::7473.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already stopped Ravana from carrying Sita away. Bleeding but unbroken, he faces the abductor again and taunts him to stay and fight. This is the proud defiance of an old guardian who knows he may die but will not step aside.
ramayan::7473.modern_relevance: You see someone bullying the weak and your body shakes, but you step in anyway. You may not win, yet you refuse to be silent.
ramayan::7473.insight: It turns resistance into a moral stand, not a calculation of success.

ramayan::7474.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्तस्य यथान्यायं रावणस्य जटायुषा । क्रुद्धस्याग्निनिभास्सर्वा रेजुर्विंशतिदृष्टयः । । 3511 । ।
ramayan::7474.verse_hindi: Ravanas twenty eyes glowed like fire in anger after Jatayu thus rightly said.
ramayan::7474.english_translation: Ravana’s twenty eyes blazed like fire with anger after Jatayu spoke justly.
ramayan::7474.translation_literal: इत्युक्तस्य (having thus spoken) / यथान्यायं (according to what was right) / रावणस्य (of Ravana) / जटायुषा (by Jatayu) / क्रुद्धस्य (of the angry one) / अग्निनिभाः (like fire) / सर्वाः (all) / रेजुः (shone) / विंशतिदृष्टयः (the twenty eyes)
ramayan::7474.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7474.essence: Truth ignites the anger of a proud mind.
ramayan::7474.simple_meaning: Jatayu’s righteous words make Ravana furious, and his twenty eyes flash like fire.
ramayan::7474.simple_insight: Anger often flares hardest when someone has spoken the truth.
ramayan::7474.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has confronted Ravana for abducting Sita. Ravana does not answer with restraint; his rage surges instantly, and Valmiki marks it in a vivid image of twenty blazing eyes. The verse is a reaction, not a teaching.
ramayan::7474.modern_relevance: Someone calls out your wrongdoing in front of you, and your first impulse is to burn with anger. The flash tells you more about your pride than their words do.
ramayan::7474.insight: It shows how exposed ego reacts when corrected.

ramayan::7475.verse_hindi: As the bright gold earrings of the intolerant king of demons glittered, his eyes turned red in rage and he pounced upon Jatayu, the lord of birds.
ramayan::7475.english_translation: As the bright gold earrings of the intolerant king of demons glittered, his eyes turned red in rage and he pounced upon Jatayu, the lord of birds.
ramayan::7475.translation_literal: संरक्तनयनः (with reddened eyes) / कोपात् (from anger) / तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः (with heated-gold earrings) / राक्षसेन्द्रः (the lord of demons) / अभिदुद्राव (rushed upon) / पतगेन्द्रम् (the lord of birds) / अमर्षणः (the intolerant one)
ramayan::7475.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7475.essence: Anger makes even a powerful mind rush blind.
ramayan::7475.simple_meaning: Ravana, furious and blazing with anger, charges at Jatayu.
ramayan::7475.simple_insight: Rage narrows the mind until it becomes pure attack.
ramayan::7475.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Jatayu has challenged Ravana and stalled the abduction of Sita. Ravana's face burns with anger as he lunges at the bird-king. The verse is a bridge into the violent clash that follows.
ramayan::7475.modern_relevance: A sharp comment lands in the middle of an argument, and your whole body wants to strike back. This is the moment before reason disappears.
ramayan::7475.insight: It shows how anger turns a conflict into blind assault.

ramayan::7476.verse_sanskrit: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुल स्तयोस्तस्मिन्महावने । बभूव वातोद्धतयोर्मेघयोर्गगने यथा । । 3513 । ।
ramayan::7476.verse_hindi: The clash between them was tumultuous and it appeared like the clash of two pieces of clouds in the sky raised by stormy winds.
ramayan::7476.english_translation: The clash between them was tumultuous and it appeared like the clash of two pieces of clouds in the sky raised by stormy winds.
ramayan::7476.translation_literal: स (that) / सम्प्रहारः (clash) / तुमुलः (tumultuous) / तयोः (of the two) / तस्मिन् (in that) / महावने (great forest) / बभूव (was) / वात-उद्धतयोः (driven up by wind) / मेघयोः (of clouds) / गगने (in the sky) / यथा (like)
ramayan::7476.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7476.essence: The fight is so fierce it feels like a storm in the sky.
ramayan::7476.simple_meaning: Their fight was fierce and chaotic, like storm clouds smashing together in the sky.
ramayan::7476.simple_insight: Some conflicts are so violent they feel bigger than the people in them.
ramayan::7476.detailed_meaning: In the great forest, Jatayu and Ravana are locked in open combat after Ravana's violent abduction of Sita. Valmiki pauses on the force of the clash itself, comparing their struggle to storm-driven clouds colliding overhead.
ramayan::7476.modern_relevance: Two people are shouting over a decision that has already gone too far. The room feels charged, but the real damage is bigger than the argument in front of you.
ramayan::7476.insight: It shifts attention from the combatants to the sheer force of the collision.

ramayan::7477.verse_hindi: The duel between Ravana and Jatayu looked as though it was a fight between two huge winged mountains of Malyavan range.
ramayan::7477.english_translation: The duel between Ravana and Jatayu looked as though it was a fight between two huge winged mountains of the Malyavan range.
ramayan::7477.translation_literal: तत् (that) / बभूव (became) / अद्भुतम् (marvellous) / युद्धम् (battle) / गृध्र-राक्षसयोः (of the vulture and the demon) / तदा (then) / सपक्षयोः (with wings) / माल्यवतोः (of Malyavan) / महापर्वतयोः (of two great mountains) / इव (like)
ramayan::7477.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7477.essence: Great conflict can make living beings seem like colliding mountains.
ramayan::7477.simple_meaning: Ravana and Jatayu fought so fiercely that the battle seemed like two huge winged mountains crashing together.
ramayan::7477.simple_insight: Some struggles are so vast they feel larger than the beings involved.
ramayan::7477.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita, and Jatayu rises to stop him. In the forest, the old vulture-king and the demon king clash with such force that the scene becomes mountain-like and mythic, a brief image before the fight continues.
ramayan::7477.modern_relevance: Two people argue so hard that the room feels smaller by the second. What is really happening is not noise — it is two wills colliding, each refusing to yield.
ramayan::7477.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of conflict to the sheer force of opposing wills.

ramayan::7478.verse_hindi: Then the mighty Ravana rained sharp, dreadful shafts, spears and Vikarnis at Jatayu,  king of vultures.
ramayan::7478.english_translation: Then the mighty Ravana rained sharp, dreadful shafts, spears, and Vikarnis at Jatayu, king of vultures.
ramayan::7478.translation_literal: ततः (then) / नालीकनाराचैः (with shafts and arrows) / तीक्ष्णाग्रैः (with sharp points) / च (and) / विकर्णिभिः (with vikarnis) / अभ्यवर्षत् (rained down) / महाघोरैः (dreadful) / गृध्रराजम् (at the king of vultures) / महाबलः (the mighty one)
ramayan::7478.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7478.essence: The fight turns savage as Ravana showers Jatayu with weapons.
ramayan::7478.simple_meaning: Ravana attacks Jatayu with a heavy rain of sharp weapons.
ramayan::7478.simple_insight: A brutal confrontation is underway, with no room for hesitation or mercy.
ramayan::7478.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana and Jatayu are locked in a fierce struggle over Sita. After the scene-setting comparison in the previous verses, this line simply shows Ravana unleashing more weapons on the vulture king, pushing the battle forward.
ramayan::7478.modern_relevance: A conflict has already crossed the point of politeness. Words are gone, and the other person is now trying to overwhelm you.
ramayan::7478.insight: It advances the battle by showing Ravana escalating force against Jatayu.

ramayan::7479.verse_sanskrit: स तानि शरजालानि गृध्रः पत्त्ररथेश्वरः । जटायुः प्रतिजग्राह रावणास्त्राणि संयुगे । । 3516 । ।
ramayan::7479.verse_hindi: Jatayu, lord of the birds, faced the arrows and other weapons showered  by Ravana.
ramayan::7479.english_translation: Jatayu, lord of the birds, faced the arrows and other weapons showered by Ravana.
ramayan::7479.translation_literal: स (he) / तानि (those) / शरजालानि (nets of arrows) / गृध्रः (the vulture) / पत्त्ररथेश्वरः (lord of the winged chariot) / जटायुः (Jatayu) / प्रतिजग्राह (received, withstood) / रावणास्त्राणि (Ravana's weapons) / संयुगे (in battle)
ramayan::7479.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7479.essence: He did not outrun the attack; he met it.
ramayan::7479.simple_meaning: Jatayu takes Ravana's attack head-on and absorbs the shower of weapons in battle.
ramayan::7479.simple_insight: Some acts of courage are pure resistance: standing in the blow so someone else can live.
ramayan::7479.detailed_meaning: Ravana is attacking Sita's protector, Jatayu, in the forest. The old vulture does not flee. He meets the rain of arrows and weapons directly, holding the line in a fight that is already turning brutal.
ramayan::7479.modern_relevance: You see a friend being cornered and step in before thinking. You do not have the power to win, only the courage to stand there anyway.
ramayan::7479.insight: It shows courage as direct resistance, not winning. The body becomes a shield before the mind has time to calculate.

ramayan::7480.verse_sanskrit: तस्य तीक्ष्णनखाभ्यां तु चरणाभ्यां महाबलः । चकार बहुधा गात्रे व्रणान्पतगसत्तमः । । 3517 । ।
ramayan::7480.verse_hindi: The mighty, virtuous vulture with his sharp claws wounded many parts of the body of Ravana.
ramayan::7480.english_translation: The mighty, virtuous vulture wounded Ravana in many places with his sharp claws.
ramayan::7480.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / तीक्ष्ण-नखाभ्यां (with sharp claws) / तु (indeed) / चरणाभ्यां (with feet) / महाबलः (the mighty one) / चकार (made) / बहुधा (in many ways) / गात्रे (on the body) / व्रणान् (wounds) / पतग-सत्तमः (the best of birds) ।
ramayan::7480.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7480.essence: Even a wounded defender can strike back with force.
ramayan::7480.simple_meaning: Jatayu struck Ravana hard and left wounds all over his body.
ramayan::7480.simple_insight: Even against a stronger enemy, courage can still leave a mark.
ramayan::7480.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already intercepted Ravana and endured a weapon attack. In this brief moment, the old vulture answers with his claws, tearing Ravana's body before the fight continues. It is a fierce detail inside an ongoing struggle, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7480.modern_relevance: You may not be able to win the whole fight, but you can still land the blow that matters.
ramayan::7480.insight: It highlights resistance in the middle of a losing battle, not a finished victory.

ramayan::7481.verse_sanskrit: अथ क्रोधाद्धशग्रीवो जग्राह दश मार्गणान् । मृत्युदण्डनिभान्घोरान्छत्रुमर्दनकाङ्क्षया । । 3518 । ।
ramayan::7481.verse_hindi: Ravana in a rage took ten dreadful darts (looking) like the staff of death with a desire to crush the enemy.
ramayan::7481.english_translation: Ravana in a rage took ten dreadful darts, like the staff of death, eager to crush his enemy.
ramayan::7481.translation_literal: अथ (then) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / दश (ten) / मार्गणान् (arrows or darts) / जग्राह (he took up) / मृत्युदण्ड-निभान् (death-staff-like) / घोरान् (terrible) / छत्रुमर्दन-काङ्क्षया (with the desire to crush the enemy)
ramayan::7481.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7481.essence: Rage turns defense into a desire to destroy.
ramayan::7481.simple_meaning: Ravana, furious in battle, picked up ten terrible darts and aimed to destroy his opponent.
ramayan::7481.simple_insight: Anger narrows the mind until destruction feels like purpose.
ramayan::7481.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already wounded Ravana with his claws. In response, Ravana seizes ten dreadful arrows, driven by rage and the urge to crush the bird. The verse is a moment in the fight, not a teaching.
ramayan::7481.modern_relevance: A heated argument can turn one sharp comment into a full attack. The mind stops seeing a person and starts seeing a target.
ramayan::7481.insight: It shows how quickly injury can become retaliation when anger takes over.

ramayan::7482.verse_sanskrit: स तैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यः पूर्णमुक्तैरजिह्मगैः । बिभेद निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गृध्रं घोरैश्शिलीमुखैः । । 3519 । ।
ramayan::7482.verse_hindi: The mighty Ravana fully released his dreadful, sharp arrows that went straight and pierced the vulture.
ramayan::7482.english_translation: The mighty Ravana fully released his dreadful, sharp arrows that went straight and pierced the vulture.
ramayan::7482.translation_literal: स (he) / तैः (with those) / बाणैः (with arrows) / महावीर्यः (mighty) / पूर्णमुक्तैः (fully released) / अजिह्मगैः (going straight) / बिभेद (pierced) / निशितैः (sharp) / तीक्ष्णैः (keen) / गृध्रम् (the vulture) / घोरैः (dreadful) / शिलीमुखैः (arrows)
ramayan::7482.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7482.essence: The fight sharpens, but nothing is yet resolved.
ramayan::7482.simple_meaning: Ravana fires sharp, straight arrows at Jatayu and wounds him further.
ramayan::7482.simple_insight: Violence here is only a step in the larger tragedy.
ramayan::7482.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already been wounded by Jatayu's attack while carrying Sita away. Enraged, he answers with a storm of arrows, striking the vulture again. The scene is still moving toward Jatayu's final stand, not toward a teaching.
ramayan::7482.modern_relevance: A conflict can turn brutal in seconds, and each new blow only deepens the damage. This is the moment anger stops arguing and starts cutting.
ramayan::7482.insight: It keeps the focus on the escalating combat, not on any inner lesson.

ramayan::7483.verse_sanskrit: स राक्षसरथे पश्यन्जानकीं बाष्पलोचनाम् । अचिन्तयित्वा तान्बाणान्राक्षसं समभिद्रवत् । । 35110 । ।
ramayan::7483.verse_hindi: Seeing Sita, daughter of Janaka, on the demons chariot with eyes full of tears, Jatayu without minding the arrows renewed his attack.
ramayan::7483.english_translation: Seeing Sita, daughter of Janaka, on the demon's chariot with eyes full of tears, Jatayu rushed at the demon without thinking of the arrows.
ramayan::7483.translation_literal: सः (he) / राक्षस-रथे (on the demon's chariot) / पश्यन् (seeing) / जानकीम् (Sita, daughter of Janaka) / बाष्प-लोचनाम् (with tear-filled eyes) / अचिन्तयित्वा (without thinking of) / तान् (those) / बाणान् (arrows) / राक्षसम् (at the demon) / समभिद्रवत् (rushed / attacked)
ramayan::7483.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7483.essence: He saw her tears and forgot his own danger.
ramayan::7483.simple_meaning: Jatayu sees Sita in Ravana's chariot, ignores the arrows, and attacks at once.
ramayan::7483.simple_insight: Real courage moves before fear can speak.
ramayan::7483.detailed_meaning: Ravana has abducted Sita, and Jatayu spots her riding in the enemy chariot, weeping. He does not pause to protect himself. The sight of her suffering drives him straight into a desperate attack.
ramayan::7483.modern_relevance: You see someone being cornered and your body moves before your mind finishes calculating the risk.
ramayan::7483.insight: It shows how protective action can override self-preservation when injustice is unmistakable.

ramayan::7484.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽस्य सशरं चापं मुक्तामणिविभूषितम् । चरणाभ्यां महातेजा बभञ्ज पतगेश्वरः । । 35111 । ।
ramayan::7484.verse_hindi: The glorious lord of birds crushed with his feet the bow and arrow of Ravana with pearls and gems encrusted.
ramayan::7484.english_translation: Then the glorious lord of birds crushed Ravana's bow and arrows, adorned with pearls and gems, beneath his feet.
ramayan::7484.translation_literal: ततः (then) / अस्य (his) / सशरम् (with arrows) / चापम् (bow) / मुक्तामणि-विभूषितम् (adorned with pearls and gems) / चरणाभ्याम् (with his feet) / महातेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / बभञ्ज (broke, crushed) / पतगेश्वरः (lord of birds)
ramayan::7484.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7484.essence: He answered violence with impossible courage.
ramayan::7484.simple_meaning: Jatayu uses his feet to crush Ravana's bow and arrows in the middle of the attack.
ramayan::7484.simple_insight: Courage can be so complete that it turns defense into dominance.
ramayan::7484.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already thrown himself at Ravana to protect Sita. Ravana answers with arrows, but the bird king meets the assault head-on and smashes the weapon beneath his feet. It is a brief, fierce moment in a larger fight.
ramayan::7484.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with pressure and expects you to fold. Instead, you stand your ground so firmly that their leverage breaks.
ramayan::7484.insight: It shows fearless resistance: protection can be active, not passive.

ramayan::7485.verse_sanskrit: ततोऽन्यद्धनुरादाय रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः । ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । । 35112 । ।
ramayan::7485.verse_hindi: Overcome with anger, Ravana took another bow and rained (on him) hundreds and thousands of arrows.
ramayan::7485.english_translation: Overcome with anger, Ravana took another bow and rained hundreds and thousands of arrows on him.
ramayan::7485.translation_literal: ततः (then) / अन्यत् (another) / धनुः (bow) / आदाय (taking) / रावणः (Ravana) / क्रोध-मूर्छितः (faint with anger) / ववर्ष (rained) / शर-वर्षाणि (showers of arrows) / शतशः (in hundreds) / अथ (and then) / सहस्रशः (in thousands)
ramayan::7485.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7485.essence: Anger does not seek victory; it seeks escalation.
ramayan::7485.simple_meaning: Ravana, furious, picked up another bow and unleashed a flood of arrows.
ramayan::7485.simple_insight: Anger makes force feel like control, even as it narrows judgment.
ramayan::7485.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has just smashed Ravana’s first bow to stop him from carrying Sita away. Enraged, Ravana grabs another weapon and answers with overwhelming arrows. The verse is a combat beat, showing the violence escalating before Jatayu’s suffering is described.
ramayan::7485.modern_relevance: A sharp reply, a slammed door, a flood of texts — anger can make escalation feel like strength.
ramayan::7485.insight: It shows how quickly wounded pride turns into excess force.

ramayan::7486.verse_sanskrit: शरैरावारितस्तस्य संयुगे पतगेश्वरः । कुलायमुपसम्प्राप्तः पक्षीव प्रबभौ तदा । । 35113 । ।
ramayan::7486.verse_hindi: Jatayu, shot with arrows on all sides in the combat, shone like the bird that returned to its nest.
ramayan::7486.english_translation: Jatayu, shot with arrows on all sides in the combat, shone like the bird that returned to its nest.
ramayan::7486.translation_literal: शरैः (with arrows) / आवारितः (covered) / तस्य (his) / संयुगे (in the combat) / पतगेश्वरः (lord of birds) / कुलायम् (to the nest) / उपसम्प्राप्तः (having reached) / पक्षी इव (like a bird) / प्रबभौ (shone) / तदा (then)
ramayan::7486.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7486.essence: Pain does not erase dignity when you keep flying toward duty.
ramayan::7486.simple_meaning: Jatayu is covered in arrows during battle, yet he still shines like a bird returning to its nest.
ramayan::7486.simple_insight: Even wounded, he carries the dignity of purpose.
ramayan::7486.detailed_meaning: In the fight with Ravana, Jatayu is already being torn by arrows. Valmiki does not pause for strategy here; he lingers on the sight of the bird-king still blazing with courage as he presses into danger, just before he strikes back.
ramayan::7486.modern_relevance: You may be exhausted, criticized, and still moving toward what you must protect. The body shows the damage; the will still carries its own light.
ramayan::7486.insight: It shifts attention from injury to steadfast purpose under attack.

ramayan::7487.verse_sanskrit: स तानि शरवर्षाणि पक्षाभ्यां च विधूयच । चरणाभ्यां महातेजा बभञ्जास्य महद्धनुः । । 35114 । ।
ramayan::7487.verse_hindi: Powerful Jatayu scattered the shower of arrows with his wings and broke down the great bow with his claws.
ramayan::7487.english_translation: Powerful Jatayu scattered the shower of arrows with his wings and broke down the great bow with his claws.
ramayan::7487.translation_literal: सः (he) / तानि (those) / शरवर्षाणि (showers of arrows) / पक्षाभ्याम् (with his two wings) / च (and) / विधूय (having shaken off) / चरणाभ्याम् (with his two feet/claws) / महातेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / बभञ्ज (broke) / अस्य (his) / महत् (great) / धनुः (bow)
ramayan::7487.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7487.essence: He turns defense into counterforce without losing his courage.
ramayan::7487.simple_meaning: Jatayu shakes off Ravana's arrows with his wings and breaks Ravana's great bow with his claws.
ramayan::7487.simple_insight: Courage is not the absence of injury; it is meeting force without yielding.
ramayan::7487.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already flooded the sky with arrows, and Jatayu is being battered in midair. Even so, the great bird answers with a fierceness that turns defense into attack, snapping Ravana's bow and holding the line in Sita's rescue.
ramayan::7487.modern_relevance: A barrage of criticism lands on you in a meeting, and you feel the room tilt. You steady yourself, answer cleanly, and refuse to be pushed off your ground.
ramayan::7487.insight: It shows that steadfast resistance can come from the weakest-looking side.

ramayan::7488.verse_sanskrit: तच्चाग्निसदृशं दीप्तं रावणस्य शरावरम् । पक्षाभ्यां स महावीर्यो व्याधुनोत्पतगेश्वरः । । 35115 । ।
ramayan::7488.verse_hindi: Mighty Jatayu, lord of the birds, shattered with his wings the armour of Ravana that was glowing like fire.
ramayan::7488.english_translation: Mighty Jatayu, lord of the birds, shattered with his wings the armour of Ravana that was glowing like fire.
ramayan::7488.translation_literal: तत् (that) / अग्नि-सदृशम् (fire-like) / दीप्तम् (shining) / रावणस्य (of Ravana) / शरावरम् (armour) / पक्षाभ्याम् (with wings) / सः (he) / महावीर्यः (mighty) / व्याधुनोत् (shook off) / पतगेश्वरः (lord of birds)
ramayan::7488.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7488.essence: A wounded defender still lands a blow that matters.
ramayan::7488.simple_meaning: Jatayu used his wings to shake off Ravana’s blazing armour in battle.
ramayan::7488.simple_insight: Even in a losing fight, courage can strike hard and clean.
ramayan::7488.detailed_meaning: Ravana has abducted Sita, and Jatayu blocks his path in the air. Wounded by arrows, the old bird still tears through Ravana’s defence with his wings. This verse is one move inside that desperate rescue battle.
ramayan::7488.modern_relevance: A person stands up in a room where everyone else has gone quiet. They may not win, but their refusal to stay silent still changes the scene.
ramayan::7488.insight: It shows that righteous resistance matters even when the odds are hopeless.

ramayan::7489.verse_hindi: Powerful Jatayu killed in the combat, the splendid, swiftmoving, devilfaced asses with  golden shields yoked to the chariot.
ramayan::7489.english_translation: Powerful Jatayu killed in combat the splendid, swift-moving, devil-faced asses yoked to the chariot with golden shields.
ramayan::7489.translation_literal: काञ्चनोरश्छदान् (with golden breast-shields) / दिव्यान् (splendid, divine) / पिशाचवदनान् (devil-faced) / खरान् (asses) / तान् (those) / च (and) / अस्य (his) / जवसम्पन्नान् (swift-moving) / जघान (killed) / समरे (in battle) / बली (the mighty one)
ramayan::7489.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7489.essence: Even Ravana’s chariot beasts fall before Jatayu’s fury.
ramayan::7489.simple_meaning: Jatayu continued the fight and killed Ravana’s swift, fierce asses in battle.
ramayan::7489.simple_insight: The struggle is so fierce that even the chariot animals become part of the fight.
ramayan::7489.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already shattered Ravana’s weapons and armour. In this verse, the battle tightens further as he kills the fierce, gold-shielded asses pulling Ravana’s chariot. It is another step in a desperate airborne struggle.
ramayan::7489.insight: It keeps the scene moving by showing Jatayu dismantling Ravana piece by piece.

ramayan::7490.verse_sanskrit: वरं त्रिवेणुसम्पन्नं कामगं पावकार्चिषम् । मणिहेमविचित्राङ्गं बभञ्ज च महारथम् । । 35117 । ।
ramayan::7490.verse_hindi: Then he(Jatayu) broke down the great chariot(of Ravana) glowing like fire, glittering with gold and gems, made of three bamboo reeds, and capable of flying wherever the rider willed.
ramayan::7490.english_translation: Then he broke Ravana's great chariot, glowing like fire, glittering with gold and gems, made of three bamboo reeds, and able to fly wherever the rider wished.
ramayan::7490.translation_literal: वरम् (excellent / splendid) / त्रिवेणुसम्पन्नम् (furnished with three bamboo reeds) / कामगम् (going where desired) / पावकार्चिषम् (with fire-like radiance) / मणिहेमविचित्राङ्गम् (with limbs adorned by jewels and gold) / बभञ्ज (broke) / च (and) / महारथम् (great chariot)
ramayan::7490.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7490.essence: Flashing power still falls when courage strikes it.
ramayan::7490.simple_meaning: Jatayu smashed Ravana's splendid flying chariot in the middle of battle.
ramayan::7490.simple_insight: Even a magnificent advantage can be broken when courage meets it head-on.
ramayan::7490.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already torn through Ravana's defenses in the air. Here, the old vulture keeps attacking the demon king's shining flying chariot, smashing the vehicle that carried Sita away. The verse is part of the action, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7490.modern_relevance: A person arrives with polished tools, status, and every visible advantage. Still, one brave refusal can shatter the whole display.
ramayan::7490.insight: It shows courage dismantling power at its most impressive.

ramayan::7491.verse_sanskrit: पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतीकाशं छत्रं च व्यजनैस्सह । पातयामास वेगेन ग्राहिभी राक्षसैस्सह । । 35118 । ।
ramayan::7491.verse_hindi: Jatayu violently pulled down the parasol shining like the full moon and the fans of the chariot along with the demons holding them.
ramayan::7491.english_translation: Jatayu violently pulled down the parasol shining like the full moon and the fans of the chariot along with the demons holding them.
ramayan::7491.translation_literal: पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतीकाशम् (shining like the full moon) / छत्रम् (parasol) / च (and) / व्यजनैः (with fans) / सह (along with) / पातयामास (pulled down) / वेगेन (swiftly, violently) / ग्राहिभिः (by the holders) / राक्षसैः (with demons) / सह (together with)
ramayan::7491.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7491.essence: Powerful resistance strips away the symbols of dominance first.
ramayan::7491.simple_meaning: Jatayu tore down Ravana’s royal canopy and fans, along with the demons holding them, in the heat of battle.
ramayan::7491.simple_insight: It shows how fierce protection can be when someone stands between harm and the innocent.
ramayan::7491.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already smashed Ravana’s chariot and slain its horses. In this moment, the great bird keeps ripping apart the king of Lanka’s pride and symbols of power, while the abduction of Sita continues nearby.
ramayan::7491.modern_relevance: You see someone being dragged into harm’s way, and you stop caring about appearances. In that instant, only protection matters.
ramayan::7491.insight: It shifts attention from status and spectacle to direct intervention against wrongdoing.

ramayan::7492.verse_sanskrit: सारथेश्चास्य वेगेन तुण्डेनैव महच्छिरः । पुनर्व्यपाहरच्छ्रीमान्पक्षिराजो महाबलः । । 35119 । ।
ramayan::7492.verse_hindi: Again the glorious, powerful king of birds swiftly shattered the huge head of the charioteer with his beak.
ramayan::7492.english_translation: Again the glorious, powerful king of birds swiftly shattered the huge head of the charioteer with his beak.
ramayan::7492.translation_literal: सारथेः (of the charioteer) / च (and) / अस्य (his) / वेगेन (swiftly) / तुण्डेन (with his beak) / एव (indeed) / महत्-शिरः (huge head) / पुनः (again) / व्यपाहरत् (shattered) / श्रीमान् (glorious one) / पक्षि-राजः (king of birds) / महा-बलः (powerful)
ramayan::7492.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7492.essence: Jatayu keeps fighting without pause, even as the cost rises.
ramayan::7492.simple_meaning: Jatayu strikes again, this time crushing the charioteer's head with his beak.
ramayan::7492.simple_insight: The fight is still raging, and Jatayu is not backing down.
ramayan::7492.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has already smashed Ravana's chariot and torn down its ornaments. In this moment, the bird-king keeps attacking the crew, crushing the charioteer's head as the rescue effort against Sita turns desperate and violent.
ramayan::7492.insight: It shows relentless resistance: even after one victory, the struggle continues until the threat is stopped.

ramayan::7493.verse_sanskrit: स भग्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः । अङ्केनादाय वैदेहीं पपात भुवि रावणः । । 35120 । ।
ramayan::7493.verse_hindi: With the bow broken, the chariot destroyed, asses (drawing the chariot) and the charioteer dead,  Ravana fell down on the ground holding Vaidehi on his lap.
ramayan::7493.english_translation: With his bow broken, his chariot shattered, his horses and charioteer dead, Ravana fell to the ground holding Vaidehi in his lap.
ramayan::7493.translation_literal: सः (he) / भग्नधन्वा (with the bow broken) / विरथः (without a chariot) / हताश्वः (with the horses killed) / हतसारथिः (with the charioteer killed) / अङ्केन (in the lap) / आदाय (taking) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / पपात (fell) / भुवि (on the ground) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7493.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7493.essence: What looks invincible can fall the moment its supports break.
ramayan::7493.simple_meaning: Ravana is brought down in battle. His weapons, chariot, horses, and driver are gone, and he falls to the ground still holding Sita.
ramayan::7493.simple_insight: Power can collapse in a single instant when its supports are cut away.
ramayan::7493.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has just torn apart Ravana's chariot and killed its driver. In the chaos, Ravana is thrown down to the earth, still clutching Sita. The scene marks the bird's fierce resistance, but it is only one step in the abduction.
ramayan::7493.modern_relevance: A plan that looked unstoppable can unravel fast when the key support disappears. What seemed like control was only a structure propped up by force.
ramayan::7493.insight: It shifts attention from apparent strength to the fragile supports underneath it.

ramayan::7494.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भूमौ रावणं भग्नवाहनम् । साधुसाध्विति भूतानि गृध्रराजमपूजयन् । । 35121 । ।
ramayan::7494.verse_hindi: Seeing Ravana fallen on the ground with his broken chariot, all beings honoured the king of the birds, saying, Well done Well done
ramayan::7494.english_translation: Seeing Ravana fallen on the ground with his broken chariot, all beings honoured the king of the birds, saying, "Well done! Well done!"
ramayan::7494.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / निपतितम् (fallen) / भूमौ (on the ground) / रावणम् (Ravana) / भग्नवाहनम् (with broken vehicle) / साधुसाधु इति (well done, well done) / भूतानि (all beings) / गृध्रराजम् (the king of birds) / अपूजयन् (honoured)
ramayan::7494.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7494.essence: Even a losing fight can earn honor when it is righteous.
ramayan::7494.simple_meaning: Ravana is knocked down, and the beings around the scene praise Jatayu for his courage.
ramayan::7494.simple_insight: Courage matters even when it cannot win.
ramayan::7494.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already been struck hard in the fight with Jatayu. He lies on the ground with his chariot broken, and the world around him responds not with fear but praise for the bird-king who resisted him. The verse marks public recognition of Jatayu's bravery before the struggle continues.
ramayan::7494.modern_relevance: You may not stop the harm completely, but people still notice when you stand up anyway.
ramayan::7494.insight: It shifts attention from victory to moral courage under impossible odds.

ramayan::7495.verse_sanskrit: परिश्रान्तं तु तं दृष्टवा जरया पक्षियूथपम् । उत्पपात पुनर्हृष्टो मैथिलीं गृह्य रावणः । । 35122 । ।
ramayan::7495.verse_hindi: Seeing the lord of the flocks of birds exhausted due to age still fighting, Ravana felt glad. He flew back into the sky taking Sita, princess of Mithila, with him.
ramayan::7495.english_translation: Seeing the bird-king exhausted by age, Ravana became delighted again and lifted Sita, the princess of Mithila, into the sky.
ramayan::7495.translation_literal: परिश्रान्तम् (exhausted) / तु (but) / तम् (him) / दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / जरया (by age) / पक्षियूथपम् (lord of the bird flock) / उत्पपात (rose up) / पुनः (again) / हृष्टः (delighted) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili) / गृह्य (seizing) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7495.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7495.essence: Weakness invites attack when mercy is absent.
ramayan::7495.simple_meaning: Ravana sees that Jatayu is weakened by age, regains confidence, and carries Sita away into the sky.
ramayan::7495.simple_insight: A predator often returns the moment resistance seems to fade.
ramayan::7495.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has fought Ravana hard enough to damage his chariot and stall the abduction. But when Ravana sees the old bird exhausted, he seizes the opening, lifts Sita again, and escapes upward. The scene is a brief turn before Jatayu’s final stand.
ramayan::7495.modern_relevance: You were almost safe, then the person pressuring you noticed you were tired and pushed again.
ramayan::7495.insight: It shows how quickly cruelty exploits weakness when vigilance slips.

ramayan::7496.verse_sanskrit: तं प्रहृष्टं निधायाङ्के गच्छन्तं जनकात्मजाम् । गृध्रराजस्समुत्पत्य समभिद्रुत्य रावणम् । । 35123 । । समावार्य महातेजा जटायुरिदमब्रवीत् ।
ramayan::7496.verse_hindi: Seeing Sita, Janakas daughter, happily carried away into the sky by Ravana on his lap. Jatayu, the mighty king of vultures chased him, and obstructing his path said :
ramayan::7496.english_translation: Seeing Sita, Janaka's daughter, happily carried away into the sky by Ravana on his lap, Jatayu, the mighty king of vultures, rose up, rushed after him, blocked his path, and said this to him.
ramayan::7496.translation_literal: तं (him) / प्रहृष्टं (delighted) / निधाय (placing) / अङ्के (on the lap) / गच्छन्तं (going) / जनकात्मजाम् (Janaka's daughter) / गृध्रराजः (king of vultures) / समुत्पत्य (having risen up) / समभिद्रुत्य (having rushed at) / रावणम् (Ravana) / समावार्य (having obstructed) / महातेजाः (the greatly radiant one) / जटायुः (Jatayu) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7496.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7496.essence: Old age does not cancel the duty to resist cruelty.
ramayan::7496.simple_meaning: Ravana carries Sita away, and Jatayu rises to stop him and challenge him.
ramayan::7496.simple_insight: Courage sometimes means stepping into danger for someone else.
ramayan::7496.detailed_meaning: Ravana is carrying Sita off through the sky after abducting her. Even though Jatayu is old, he launches himself at Ravana and blocks his path. The verse sets up the fierce confrontation that follows.
ramayan::7496.modern_relevance: You see someone being mistreated and your body moves before your fear does. That instant of intervention is what Jatayu embodies.
ramayan::7496.insight: It shifts attention from helpless watching to immediate intervention.

ramayan::7497.verse_sanskrit: वज्रसंस्पर्शबाणस्य भार्यां रामस्य रावण । । 35124 । । अल्पबुद्धे हरस्येनां वधाय खलु रक्षसाम् ।
ramayan::7497.verse_hindi: Foolish Ravana, you are kidnapping this lady, wife of Rama, whose arrows can hit like a thunderbolt. This will lead to the destruction of all demons.
ramayan::7497.english_translation: Foolish Ravana, you are kidnapping the wife of Rama, whose arrows strike like thunderbolts. This will bring destruction upon all the demons.
ramayan::7497.translation_literal: वज्रसंस्पर्शबाणस्य (whose arrows touch like thunderbolts) / भार्यां (wife) / रामस्य (of Rama) / रावण (Ravana) / अल्पबुद्धे (foolish one) / हरस्येनाम् (you are carrying away this woman) / वधाय (for destruction) / खलु (indeed) / रक्षसाम् (of the demons)
ramayan::7497.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7497.essence: Harming what is protected by dharma turns ruin back on the offender.
ramayan::7497.simple_meaning: Jatayu warns Ravana that Sita is Rama's wife and that taking her will lead to the ruin of the demon host.
ramayan::7497.simple_insight: Some acts are so wrong they carry their own destruction.
ramayan::7497.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has intercepted Ravana in the sky while Ravana carries Sita away. Though old and outmatched, he still confronts the abductor and warns him that kidnapping Rama's wife will bring disaster on Ravana and his allies.
ramayan::7497.modern_relevance: You see someone making a choice that will wreck everything around them, and you say it plainly. Some warnings come too late to stop the damage, but not too late to name it.
ramayan::7497.insight: It sharpens the mind to see that power used against dharma becomes self-destructive.

ramayan::7498.verse_hindi: You are drinking poison along with all your friends, relatives, ministers, the army and  your allies. like a thirsty man drinks water.
ramayan::7498.english_translation: You are drinking poison along with all your friends, relatives, ministers, the army, and your allies, like a thirsty man drinks water.
ramayan::7498.translation_literal: स-मित्र-बन्धुः (with friends and relatives) / स-आमात्यः (with ministers) / स-बलः (with the army) / स-परिच्छदः (with attendants and allies) / विषपानम् (poison-drinking) / पिबसि (you drink) / एतत् (this) / पिपासितः इव (like one who is thirsty) / उदकम् (water)
ramayan::7498.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7498.essence: Desire can feel like relief while it is poisoning everyone tied to you.
ramayan::7498.simple_meaning: Ravana is so blindly chasing desire that he is swallowing destruction for himself and everyone around him.
ramayan::7498.simple_insight: Unchecked craving does not stay private; it pulls whole circles into ruin.
ramayan::7498.detailed_meaning: Jatayu confronts Ravana in mid-abduction, with Sita already in his grasp. He warns Ravana that this act is not just theft but self-destruction, and that Ravana’s court, family, army, and allies will be dragged down with him.
ramayan::7498.modern_relevance: You make one reckless choice, and suddenly your partner, team, and family are paying for it too. Desire often feels like relief right before it becomes poison.
ramayan::7498.insight: It frames harmful action as collective self-destruction, not private pleasure.

ramayan::7499.verse_sanskrit: अनुबन्धमजानन्तः कर्मणामविचक्षणाः । । 35126 । । शीघ्रमेव विनश्यन्ति यथा त्वं विनशिष्यसि ।
ramayan::7499.verse_hindi: Fools who do not know the consequences of their action perish soon. Similarly you are going to die soon.
ramayan::7499.english_translation: Fools who do not know the consequences of their actions perish quickly. So you will perish soon as well.
ramayan::7499.translation_literal: अनुबन्धम् (consequences) / अजानन्तः (not knowing) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / अविचक्षणाः (the foolish) / शीघ्रम् एव (very soon) / विनश्यन्ति (perish) / यथा (as) / त्वम् (you) / विनशिष्यसि (will perish)
ramayan::7499.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7499.essence: Ignoring the cost of action is itself the fastest path to ruin.
ramayan::7499.simple_meaning: People who act without understanding the results of their actions destroy themselves quickly. Ravana is being told he is heading toward the same end.
ramayan::7499.simple_insight: Not every urge deserves action; some choices carry their own destruction.
ramayan::7499.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is being warned that his decision is not just immoral but self-destructive. The speaker says that anyone who ignores the consequences of action falls quickly, and Ravana is already trapped in that pattern.
ramayan::7499.modern_relevance: You send the angry text before sleeping on it, then spend the next day cleaning up the damage. The harm was never sudden — it was built into the choice.
ramayan::7499.insight: It shifts the mind from impulse to consequence, making you pause before acting on desire or anger.

ramayan::7500.verse_sanskrit: बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे । । 35127 । । वधाय बडिशं गृह्य सामिषं जलजो यथा ।
ramayan::7500.verse_hindi: You are bound by the noose of death like a fish holding on to the bait of the fishing hook. Where can you go now?
ramayan::7500.english_translation: You are bound by the noose of death like a fish holding on to the bait of the fishing hook. Where can you go now?
ramayan::7500.translation_literal: बद्धः (bound) / त्वम् (you) / कालपाशेन (by the noose of death) / क्व (where) / गतः (gone) / तस्य (of that) / मोक्ष्यसे (will you be freed) / वधाय (for killing) / बडिशं (the hook) / गृह्य (having taken) / सामिषं (with bait) / जलजः (fish) / यथा (like)
ramayan::7500.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7500.essence: Grasping the bait is already the beginning of ruin.
ramayan::7500.simple_meaning: Ravana is told that death has already trapped him, and he cannot escape now. Like a fish that bites the baited hook, he has moved into his own destruction.
ramayan::7500.simple_insight: Some choices feel like power until they become the trap.
ramayan::7500.detailed_meaning: Ravana has ignored warning after warning and dragged his whole side toward ruin. Here, the speaker tells him that death has already closed around him, and his own grasping has become the weapon that will end him.
ramayan::7500.modern_relevance: You keep pressing send on the message that will only deepen the fight. It feels like control for a moment, then you realise you walked straight into the hook.
ramayan::7500.insight: It shifts attention from bravado to consequence: what you seize in desire can become the instrument of your fall.

ramayan::7501.verse_sanskrit: न हि जातु दुराधर्षौ काकुत्स्थौ तव रावण । । 35128 । । धर्षणं चाश्रमस्यास्य क्षमिष्येते तु राघवौ ।
ramayan::7501.verse_hindi: O Ravana  know that Rama and Lakshmana, the Kakutsthas, are invincible. They will not forgive the asssault you have made on their hermitage.
ramayan::7501.english_translation: O Ravana, know that Rama and Lakshmana, the Kakutsthas, are invincible. They will not forgive the assault you have made on their hermitage.
ramayan::7501.translation_literal: न हि (indeed not) / जातु (ever) / दुराधर्षौ (hard to assault, invincible) / काकुत्स्थौ (the two Kakutsthas) / तव (your) / रावण (O Ravana) / धर्षणं (the assault) / च (and) / आश्रमस्य (of the hermitage) / अस्य (this) / क्षमिष्येते (will forgive) / तु (indeed) / राघवौ (the two descendants of Raghu)
ramayan::7501.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7501.essence: Some acts are so grave that even mercy cannot erase them.
ramayan::7501.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana cannot be overpowered, and they will not excuse your attack on the hermitage.
ramayan::7501.simple_insight: Some violations cannot be undone by apology. You have crossed a line that will answer back.
ramayan::7501.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana’s violence has already set consequences in motion. The speaker warns him that Rama and Lakshmana are not weak targets, and that attacking a sacred hermitage is a grave act they will not overlook.
ramayan::7501.modern_relevance: You lash out at someone’s home, their boundary, or their safe place, thinking it will pass. It won’t. Some breaches leave a mark that no explanation can erase.
ramayan::7501.insight: It frames harm as a self-creating consequence, not a clever move that can be forgotten.

ramayan::7502.verse_sanskrit: यथा त्वया कृतं कर्म भीरुणा लोकगर्हितम् । । 35129 । । तस्कराचरितो मार्गो नैव वीरनिषेवितः ।
ramayan::7502.verse_hindi: Your cowardly action will be condemned by the whole world. The path you have chosen is the path of a thief and not of a hero.
ramayan::7502.english_translation: Your cowardly action will be condemned by the whole world. The path you have chosen is the path of a thief and not of a hero.
ramayan::7502.translation_literal: यथा (as) / त्वया (by you) / कृतं (done) / कर्म (action) / भीरुणा (by a coward) / लोकगर्हितम् (condemned by the world) / तस्कराचरितो (followed by thieves) / मार्गो (path) / नैव (not at all) / वीरनिषेवितः (trodden by heroes)
ramayan::7502.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7502.essence: Cowardly gain always exposes itself as dishonour.
ramayan::7502.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told that his deed is cowardly, shameful, and unworthy of a hero.
ramayan::7502.simple_insight: Cowardice may seize power, but it never earns respect.
ramayan::7502.detailed_meaning: Ravana has been warned that Rama and Lakshmana cannot be shaken. In this verse, the rebuke sharpens: his act is not brave conquest but a thief's path, condemned by everyone who knows honour.
ramayan::7502.modern_relevance: You cut a corner, take credit, and call it strategy. Later, the label changes — not in your favor — because people can tell when courage was missing.
ramayan::7502.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justifying aggression to seeing how actions are judged by character.

ramayan::7503.verse_sanskrit: युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि मुहूर्तं तिष्ठरावण । । 35130 । । शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथा भ्राता खरस्तथा ।
ramayan::7503.verse_hindi: O Ravana if you are courageous, tarry awhile and fight with me. Like your brother Khara, you will lie on the ground dead.
ramayan::7503.english_translation: O Ravana, if you are courageous, fight with me for a moment. Like your brother Khara, you will lie dead on the ground.
ramayan::7503.translation_literal: युध्यस्व (fight) / यदि (if) / शूरः असि (you are brave) / मुहूर्तं (for a moment) / तिष्ठ (stay) / रावण (O Ravana) / शयिष्यसे (you will lie down) / हतः (slain) / भूमौ (on the ground) / यथा (as) / भ्राता (brother) / खरः (Khara) / तथा (so)
ramayan::7503.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7503.essence: Bravado ends the moment courage is tested.
ramayan::7503.simple_meaning: Rama dares Ravana to stop boasting and fight, warning that he will end up dead like Khara.
ramayan::7503.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when it is forced to face reality.
ramayan::7503.detailed_meaning: Rama answers Ravana’s threats with a direct challenge. After warning him that his assault is shameful and that both brothers are invincible, Rama says Ravana can prove his courage only by fighting now — and will fall like Khara did.
ramayan::7503.modern_relevance: Someone keeps talking big in a group chat, but the moment they’re asked to act, the bluff shows. This verse cuts through posturing and names the cost of empty bravado.
ramayan::7503.insight: It shifts the mind from intimidation to direct confrontation.

ramayan::7504.verse_sanskrit: परेतकाले पुरुषो यत्कर्म प्रतिपद्यते । । 35131 । । विनाशायात्मनोऽधर्म्यं प्रतिपन्नोऽसि कर्म तत् ।
ramayan::7504.verse_hindi: You have resorted to unrighteous action like a dying man. This will spell your destruction.
ramayan::7504.english_translation: You have taken to unrighteous action like a dying man. That action will destroy you.
ramayan::7504.translation_literal: परेतकाले (at the time of death) / पुरुषः (a person) / यत् (which) / कर्म (action) / प्रतिपद्यते (undertakes) / विनाशाय (for destruction) / आत्मनः (of oneself) / अधर्म्यम् (unrighteous) / प्रतिपन्नः असि (you have undertaken) / कर्म (action) / तत् (that)
ramayan::7504.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7504.essence: Wrong action is already the beginning of your ruin.
ramayan::7504.simple_meaning: Ravana has chosen a wrongful course, and that choice itself is leading him toward ruin.
ramayan::7504.simple_insight: Some actions do not just fail; they poison the person who chooses them.
ramayan::7504.detailed_meaning: Rama stands before Ravana and strips away the arrogance. This is not just a challenge to fight, but a moral warning: Ravana’s choice has already turned inward against him, and the destruction he brings on others is now becoming his own.
ramayan::7504.modern_relevance: You know that text you sent, the one that felt sharp in the moment? The damage started before the reply came back. Some choices begin breaking you the instant you make them.
ramayan::7504.insight: It shifts attention from victory or defeat to the moral cost built into the action itself.

ramayan::7505.verse_sanskrit: पापानुबन्धो वै यस्य कर्मणः कर्मको नु तत् । । 35132 । । कुर्वीत लोकाधिपतिस्स्वयंभूर्भगवानपि ।
ramayan::7505.verse_hindi: If the consequences of an action be sin, who will do it ? Even the selfborn lord of the world may not.
ramayan::7505.english_translation: If the consequence of an action is grave harm, who would do it? Even the self-born lord of the world would not.
ramayan::7505.translation_literal: पापानुबन्धः (followed by harm) / वै (indeed) / यस्य (whose) / कर्मणः (of action) / कर्मकः (doer) / नु (indeed) / तत् (that) / कुर्वीत (would do) / लोकाधिपतिः (lord of the world) / स्वयंभूः (self-born) / भगवान् (the exalted one) / अपि (even)
ramayan::7505.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7505.essence: A wise being refuses actions that carry their own destruction.
ramayan::7505.simple_meaning: A person should not do something that leads to harmful consequences. Even the highest power would avoid such an action.
ramayan::7505.simple_insight: Not every possible act deserves your strength. Some choices are beneath your dignity because they poison the future.
ramayan::7505.detailed_meaning: Jatayu is confronting Ravana after seeing Sita carried off by force. He has already called the act unrighteous and destructive. Now he presses the point: a wise being would never choose an action that carries its own ruin.
ramayan::7505.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will burn a bridge you may need tomorrow. In that pause, this verse asks whether the action is worth its own damage.
ramayan::7505.insight: It trains you to judge actions by their consequences before you commit to them.

ramayan::7506.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा शुभं वाक्यं जटायुस्तस्य रक्षसः । । 35133 । । निपपात भृशं पृष्ठे दशग्रीवस्य वीर्यवान् ।
ramayan::7506.verse_hindi: Brave Jatayu having thus said these cautious words to the demon dashed against his back again and again.
ramayan::7506.english_translation: Brave Jatayu, having said these gentle words to the demon, struck Ravana's back again and again.
ramayan::7506.translation_literal: एवमुक्त्वा (having said thus) / शुभं (gentle, auspicious) / वाक्यं (words) / जटायुः (Jatayu) / तस्य (of that) / रक्षसः (demon's) / निपपात (fell upon, struck) / भृशं (hard, repeatedly) / पृष्ठे (on the back) / दशग्रीवस्य (of Dashagriva, Ravana) / वीर्यवान् (the brave, powerful one)
ramayan::7506.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7506.essence: Gentle words are not weakness when fierce action follows.
ramayan::7506.simple_meaning: Jatayu speaks firmly, then attacks Ravana from behind with full force.
ramayan::7506.simple_insight: Courage is not only words; it becomes action when the moment demands it.
ramayan::7506.detailed_meaning: Ravana has taken Sita and is trying to carry her away. Jatayu, the old vulture king, first warns him with measured words, then hurls himself at Ravana's back. This verse marks the start of his desperate resistance.
ramayan::7506.modern_relevance: You watch someone cross a line you cannot ignore. Your warning is calm, but your body is already moving.
ramayan::7506.insight: It shifts courage from protest to intervention when harm is already underway.

ramayan::7507.verse_sanskrit: तं गृहीत्वा नखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विददार समन्ततः । । 35134 । । अधिरूढो गजारोहो यथा स्याद्दुष्टवारणम् ।
ramayan::7507.verse_hindi: Thereafter, seizing Ravana, Jatayu ascended on his back and pierced his body all over with his sharp claws just as a rider goads an unruly elephant.
ramayan::7507.english_translation: Thereafter, seizing Ravana, Jatayu climbed onto his back and pierced his body all over with his sharp claws, like a rider driving an unruly elephant.
ramayan::7507.translation_literal: तम् (him) / गृहीत्वा (having seized) / नखैः (with claws) / तीक्ष्णैः (sharp) / विददार (he tore) / समन्ततः (all around) / अधिरूढः (mounted) / गजारोहः (an elephant-rider) / यथा (as) / स्यात् (would be) / दुष्टवारणम् (an unruly elephant)
ramayan::7507.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7507.essence: He fights anyway, even though claws cannot win against power.
ramayan::7507.simple_meaning: Jatayu attacks Ravana fiercely, clawing him all over after jumping onto his back.
ramayan::7507.simple_insight: Courage is not always victory; sometimes it is the refusal to yield.
ramayan::7507.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has intercepted Ravana while Sita is being carried away. With no weapon except his body, he leaps onto the demon king and tears at him with his claws. The scene is raw resistance, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7507.modern_relevance: A smaller person steps between harm and someone vulnerable, knowing the cost may be high. The act matters even if the outcome is uncertain.
ramayan::7507.insight: It shows that protection can be fierce even when you are outmatched.

ramayan::7508.verse_sanskrit: विददार नखैरस्य तुण्डं पृष्ठे समर्पयन् । । 35135 । । केशांश्चोत्पाटयामास नखपक्षमुखायुधः ।
ramayan::7508.verse_hindi: Jatayu who had  his claws, wings and beak as the only weapons  pierced and pricked  Ravana all over with his nails by pressing his beak on his back and pulled out his hair.
ramayan::7508.english_translation: Jatayu pressed his beak onto Ravana's back, tore at him with his claws, and pulled out his hair.
ramayan::7508.translation_literal: विददार (pierced) / नखैः (with claws) / अस्य (his) / तुण्डम् (beak) / पृष्ठे (on the back) / समर्पयन् (pressing, applying) / केशान् (hair) / च (and) / उत्पाटयामास (pulled out)
ramayan::7508.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7508.essence: Courage can look desperate when it is protecting someone helpless.
ramayan::7508.simple_meaning: Jatayu attacks Ravana with everything he has: claws, beak, and wings. He tears at the demon's body and hair in a fierce struggle.
ramayan::7508.simple_insight: No protection is too small when you stand up for what must be defended.
ramayan::7508.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has intercepted Ravana as he carries Sita away. In this moment, the old bird throws his whole body into the fight, using claws, beak, and wings against the stronger foe. The verse is a combat detail in a larger rescue scene.
ramayan::7508.modern_relevance: You see someone being pushed around in public, and your voice shakes — but you still step in. Sometimes courage is not elegance; it is using whatever you have.
ramayan::7508.insight: It shows that protecting another person can demand total, improvised courage rather than perfect strength.

ramayan::7509.verse_sanskrit: स तथा गृध्रराजेन क्लिश्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः । । 35136 । । अमर्षस्फुरितोष्ठस्सन्प्राकम्पत च रावणः ।
ramayan::7509.verse_hindi: Thus tormented again and again by the king of vultures, Ravana shook with anger, his lips quivering.
ramayan::7509.english_translation: Thus tormented again and again by the king of vultures, Ravana shook with anger, his lips quivering.
ramayan::7509.translation_literal: स तथा (thus) / गृध्रराजेन (by the king of vultures) / क्लिश्यमानो (being tormented) / मुहुर्मुहुः (again and again) / अमर्षस्फुरितोष्ठः (with quivering lips from anger) / सन् (being) / प्राकम्पत (shook) / च (and) / रावणः (Ravana)
ramayan::7509.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7509.essence: His anger shakes first; the real blow comes next.
ramayan::7509.simple_meaning: Ravana is enraged and shaken after Jatayu keeps attacking him.
ramayan::7509.simple_insight: Rage can make even the powerful lose steadiness for a moment.
ramayan::7509.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has launched himself at Ravana to stop Sita’s abduction. In this moment, the wounded but fearless vulture keeps striking, and Ravana’s composure begins to crack under repeated blows.
ramayan::7509.modern_relevance: Someone keeps challenging your plans, and you feel your temper rise before you can hide it. The body betrays what pride wants to conceal.
ramayan::7509.insight: It shows how pressure exposes anger before action follows.

ramayan::7510.verse_sanskrit: स परिष्वज्य च वैदेहीं वामेनाङ्केन रावणः । । 35137 । । तलेनाभिजघानाशु जटायुं क्रोधमुर्छीतः ।
ramayan::7510.verse_hindi: Losing his senses, with rage, Ravana held Vaidehi (Sita) with his left arm and hit Jatayu with his palm.
ramayan::7510.english_translation: Losing his senses with rage, Ravana held Vaidehi in his left arm and struck Jatayu with his palm.
ramayan::7510.translation_literal: सः (he) / परिष्वज्य (having embraced/held) / च (and) / वैदेहीं (Vaidehi, Sita) / वामेन (with the left) / अङ्केन (with the arm/lap) / रावणः (Ravana) / तलेन (with the palm) / अभिजघान (struck) / आशु (quickly) / जटायुम् (Jatayu) / क्रोधमुर्छीतः (fainted from rage)
ramayan::7510.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7510.essence: Blind rage turns capture into cruelty.
ramayan::7510.simple_meaning: Ravana clutched Sita with one arm and, blinded by anger, struck Jatayu with his hand.
ramayan::7510.simple_insight: Rage makes a person grasp and strike without seeing the cost.
ramayan::7510.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is fighting Jatayu in mid-abduction. Wounded and furious, he tightens his hold on her with one arm while slashing at the bird-king with his hand. The verse is a brutal action beat, not a teaching moment.
