ramayan::7559.verse_sanskrit: खमुत्पतन्तं तं दृष्ट्वा मैथिली जनकात्मजा । दुःखिता परमोद्विग्ना भये महति वर्तिनी । । 3531 । ।
ramayan::7559.verse_hindi: Sita, daughter of Janaka, princess of Mithila felt miserable, looking at Ravana taking off and got very  much agitated out of fear.
ramayan::7559.english_translation: Seeing him rise into the sky, Sita, daughter of Janaka, became miserable and deeply agitated with great fear.
ramayan::7559.translation_literal: खम् (sky) / उत्पतन्तम् (rising up) / तम् (him) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / मैथिली (Maithili, Sita) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka) / दुःखिता (grieved) / परमोद्विग्ना (deeply agitated) / भये (in fear) / महति (great) / वर्तिनी (being in)
ramayan::7559.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7559.essence: Sudden loss can overwhelm you before you even begin to resist.
ramayan::7559.simple_meaning: Sita sees Ravana rising into the sky with her and is overwhelmed by grief and fear.
ramayan::7559.simple_insight: Fear can flood the mind in an instant when everything familiar is suddenly gone.
ramayan::7559.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is carrying her away from the world she knows. As she sees him rise into the sky, her grief turns into intense fear. This verse captures the shock of abduction before her next words of protest.
ramayan::7559.modern_relevance: You look up and realize the situation has already moved beyond your control. The body reacts before the mind can make sense of what just happened.
ramayan::7559.insight: It shows the first wave of trauma: disorientation, grief, and fear before resistance can form.

ramayan::7560.verse_sanskrit: रोषरोदनताम्राक्षी भीमाक्षं राक्षसाधिपम् । रुदन्ती करुणं सीता ह्रियमाणेदमब्रवीत् । । 3532 । ।
ramayan::7560.verse_hindi: While being carried away, Sita wept piteously and her eyes went red with tears of anger and grief. Looking at the frightening eyes of the king of the demons, she said these words :
ramayan::7560.english_translation: While being carried away, Sita wept piteously and her eyes turned red with tears of anger and grief. Looking at the frightening-eyed lord of the demons, she spoke these words.
ramayan::7560.translation_literal: रोषरोदनताम्राक्षी (with eyes reddened by angry tears) / भीमाक्षम् (fearsome-eyed) / राक्षसाधिपम् (lord of the demons) / रुदन्ती (weeping) / करुणम् (piteously) / सीता (Sita) / ह्रियमाणा (being carried away) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7560.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7560.essence: Even in abduction, Sita keeps her voice and her dignity.
ramayan::7560.simple_meaning: Sita, being carried off, cried with anger and sorrow and spoke to Ravana in distress.
ramayan::7560.simple_insight: Pain can still speak with dignity, even in the middle of helplessness.
ramayan::7560.detailed_meaning: Ravana is carrying Sita away through the sky. Terrified, grieving, and furious, she turns her tears toward him and prepares to confront him. This line sets up her direct challenge in the next verse.
ramayan::7560.modern_relevance: You are dragged into a situation you never chose, yet your voice still matters. Even in shock, you can name what is wrong.
ramayan::7560.insight: It shows that emotional collapse and clear protest can exist together.

ramayan::7561.verse_sanskrit: न व्यपत्रपसे नीच कर्मणानेन रावण । ज्ञात्वा विरहितां यन्मां चोरयित्वा पलायसे । । 3533 । ।
ramayan::7561.verse_hindi: O mean Ravana, are you not ashamed of kidnapping me when I was separated (from my husband)?
ramayan::7561.english_translation: O mean Ravana, are you not ashamed of kidnapping me when I was separated from my husband?
ramayan::7561.translation_literal: न (not) / व्यपत्रपसे (do you feel ashamed) / नीच (base, mean) / कर्मणा (by the deed) / अनेन (this) / रावण (Ravana) / ज्ञात्वा (knowing) / विरहिताम् (separated) / यत् (that) / माम् (me) / चोरयित्वा (having stolen, abducted) / पलायसे (you flee)
ramayan::7561.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7561.essence: Vulnerability does not excuse predation; it makes the crime clearer.
ramayan::7561.simple_meaning: Sita confronts Ravana for abducting her when she was already separated from Rama. She calls out his shameful act directly.
ramayan::7561.simple_insight: Cruelty feels smaller when named plainly.
ramayan::7561.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is carrying her away through the sky. In terror and grief, she does not stay silent. She turns on him with moral force, exposing that he has attacked a woman already made vulnerable by separation from her husband.
ramayan::7561.modern_relevance: Someone takes advantage of you when you are already exhausted, lonely, or grieving, then acts as if it was just business. Sita names the cruelty without softening it.
ramayan::7561.insight: It teaches you to name exploitation directly instead of normalising it.

ramayan::7562.verse_sanskrit: त्वयैव नूनं दुष्टात्मन् भीरुणा हर्तुमिच्छता । ममापवाहितो भर्ता मृगरूपेण मायया । । 3534 । ।
ramayan::7562.verse_hindi: O wicked fellow, with an intention to abduct me you enticed my husband to a distance deceitfully in the form of a deer.
ramayan::7562.english_translation: O wicked fellow, with the desire to abduct me, you deceitfully lured my husband away in the form of a deer.
ramayan::7562.translation_literal: त्वया (by you) / एव (indeed) / नूनम् (surely) / दुष्टात्मन् (wicked one) / भीरुणा (cowardly) / हर्तुम् इच्छता (desiring to abduct) / मम (my) / अपवाहितः (led away) / भर्ता (husband) / मृगरूपेण (in the form of a deer) / मायया (by deceit)
ramayan::7562.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7562.essence: Deceit works best after it has pulled protection away.
ramayan::7562.simple_meaning: Sita accuses Ravana of using deceit to separate her from Rama by luring him away as a deer.
ramayan::7562.simple_insight: Deception often begins by creating distance before the harm is visible.
ramayan::7562.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already seized Sita, and she answers him with fearless clarity. She names the trick that made the abduction possible: a false deer used to draw Rama away from her. Her grief is sharp, but her mind is clear.
ramayan::7562.modern_relevance: Someone flatters you, keeps you talking, and quietly pulls your attention away from what matters most. By the time you notice, the damage is already in motion.
ramayan::7562.insight: It teaches you to see manipulation at the moment it creates separation.

ramayan::7563.verse_sanskrit: यो हि मामुद्यतस्त्रातुं सोऽप्ययं विनिपातितः । गृध्रराजः पुराणोऽसौ श्वशुरस्य सखा मम । । 3535 । ।
ramayan::7563.verse_hindi: This Jatayu, an old friend of my fatherinlaw tried to protect me but he too has fallen a prey.
ramayan::7563.english_translation: This Jatayu, an old friend of my father-in-law, tried to protect me, but he too has fallen.
ramayan::7563.translation_literal: यः (who) / हि (indeed) / माम् (me) / उद्यतः (having risen) / त्रातुम् (to protect) / सः अपि (he also) / अयम् (this one) / विनिपातितः (has been struck down) / गृध्रराजः (king of vultures) / पुराणः (ancient) / असौ (that one) / श्वशुरस्य (of father-in-law) / सखा (friend) / मम (of mine)
ramayan::7563.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7563.essence: A failed rescue can still be a noble act.
ramayan::7563.simple_meaning: Jatayu tried to save Sita from Ravana, but he has been killed. She identifies him as an old friend of her father-in-law.
ramayan::7563.simple_insight: Even a desperate rescue can end in loss, and that loss still matters.
ramayan::7563.detailed_meaning: Ravana has carried Sita away, and she sees the wounded Jatayu on the ground. He had risen to defend her, but the cost was fatal. In the middle of her abduction, she honors his courage and grief.
ramayan::7563.modern_relevance: You watch someone step in to help and still get hurt. Even when the rescue fails, your gratitude does not.
ramayan::7563.insight: It teaches you to recognize sacrifice clearly, even when it does not succeed.

ramayan::7564.verse_sanskrit: परमं खलु ते वीर्यं दृश्यते राक्षसाधम । विश्राव्य नामधेयं हि युद्धे नास्मि जिता त्वया । । 3536 । ।
ramayan::7564.verse_hindi: O lowly demon, you have, indeed, shown your heroism  (in killing this old vulture).
ramayan::7564.english_translation: O lowly demon, you have indeed shown your heroism; by making your name known, you have not defeated me in battle.
ramayan::7564.translation_literal: परमं (supreme) / खलु (indeed) / ते (your) / वीर्यम् (heroism) / दृश्यते (is seen) / राक्षसाधम (lowest among demons) / विश्राव्य (having made known) / नामधेयम् (name) / हि (indeed) / युद्धे (in battle) / न (not) / अस्मि (I am) / जिता (defeated) / त्वया (by you)
ramayan::7564.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7564.essence: Violence against the helpless is not victory.
ramayan::7564.simple_meaning: Sita mocks Ravana. She says his only real display of strength was killing the old vulture, not defeating Rama in battle.
ramayan::7564.simple_insight: Cruel power can look bold, yet still reveal weakness.
ramayan::7564.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu falls protecting her, Sita turns on Ravana with fierce clarity. She refuses to call his violence heroic and denies him the dignity of a real victory. Her words cut his pride while honoring the fallen protector.
ramayan::7564.modern_relevance: When someone boasts after hurting a weaker person, their “strength” is already exposed. You do not have to flatter cruelty just because it is loud.
ramayan::7564.insight: It teaches you to name cowardice plainly instead of letting intimidation pass as courage.

ramayan::7565.verse_sanskrit: ईदृशं गर्हितं कर्म कथं कृत्वा न लज्जसे । स्त्रियाश्च हरणं नीच रहिते च परस्य च । । 3537 । ।
ramayan::7565.verse_hindi: O lowly fellow how is it that you are not ashamed of commiting such a despicable act  abducting anothers wife when she is alone ?
ramayan::7565.english_translation: O lowly fellow, how is it that you are not ashamed of committing such a despicable act, abducting another's wife when she is alone?
ramayan::7565.translation_literal: ईदृशम् (such) / गर्हितम् (despicable) / कर्म (act) / कथम् (how) / कृत्वा (having done) / न (not) / लज्जसे (are you ashamed) / स्त्रियाः (of a woman) / च (and) / हरणम् (abduction) / नीच (lowly one) / रहिते (when alone, unprotected) / च (and) / परस्य (of another) / च (and)
ramayan::7565.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7565.essence: True courage is exposed when you prey on the helpless.
ramayan::7565.simple_meaning: Sita confronts Ravana for abducting her while she was alone and undefended, and she calls the act shameful and disgraceful.
ramayan::7565.simple_insight: Moral strength can still speak clearly when power is being abused.
ramayan::7565.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita faces Ravana after Jatayu has already fallen trying to save her. She does not flatter his pride or soften the truth. She names the abduction for what it is: cowardly, shameful, and beneath any claim to honour.
ramayan::7565.modern_relevance: A powerful person corners someone who is alone and calls it victory. Sita's words refuse that lie and name the act exactly as it is.
ramayan::7565.insight: It teaches you to name abuse plainly, without letting the aggressor dress it up as strength.

ramayan::7566.verse_sanskrit: कथयिष्यन्ति लोकेषु पुरुषाः कर्म कुत्सितम् । सुनृशंसमधर्मिष्ठं तव शौण्डीर्यमानिनः । । 3538 । ।
ramayan::7566.verse_hindi: You consider yourself to be brave after committing such a cruel, despicable and unrighteous act for which people of the world will condemn you.
ramayan::7566.english_translation: You consider yourself brave after committing a cruel, despicable, and unrighteous act that people everywhere will condemn.
ramayan::7566.translation_literal: कथयिष्यन्ति (will speak) / लोकेषु (among the people, in the world) / पुरुषाः (men, people) / कर्म (deed, act) / कुत्सितम् (despicable, vile) / सुनृशंसम् (very cruel) / अधर्मिष्ठम् (most unrighteous) / तव (your) / शौण्डीर्यमानिनः (of one proud of valor)
ramayan::7566.speaker: Jatayu
ramayan::7566.essence: Pride cannot redeem a deed the world will rightly condemn.
ramayan::7566.simple_meaning: People will remember this act as cruel and shameful, not heroic. Your pride in bravery cannot hide what you did.
ramayan::7566.simple_insight: Cruelty does not become courage just because you call it strength.
ramayan::7566.detailed_meaning: Jatayu, dying after trying to stop Ravana from abducting Sita, condemns him directly. He says the world will not praise this deed as bravery; it will remember it as vile and unrighteous. The verse deepens the accusation before the rebuke that follows.
ramayan::7566.modern_relevance: You can win the argument, the room, even the moment — and still be remembered for the harm you caused. Calling it strength does not change what it was.
ramayan::7566.insight: It separates real courage from violent self-justification.

ramayan::7567.verse_sanskrit: धिक्ते शौर्यं च सत्त्वं च यत्त्वं कथितवांस्तदा । कुलाक्रोशकरं लोके धिक्ते चारित्रमीदृशम् । । 3539 । ।
ramayan::7567.verse_hindi: Fie upon your heroism and strength about which you boasted. Fie upon your character that would bring calumny to the race and the world. I condemn such behaviour of yours.
ramayan::7567.english_translation: Fie upon your heroism and strength about which you boasted. Fie upon your character that would bring calumny to the race and the world. I condemn such behaviour of yours.
ramayan::7567.translation_literal: धिक् ते (fie upon you) / शौर्यम् (heroism) / च (and) / सत्त्वम् (strength) / च (and) / यत् (which) / त्वम् (you) / कथितवान् (boasted) / तदा (then) / कुलाक्रोश-करम् (bringing shame to the family) / लोके (in the world) / धिक् ते (fie upon you) / चारित्रम् (conduct) / ईदृशम् (such)
ramayan::7567.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7567.essence: Boasted strength means nothing when conduct disgraces you.
ramayan::7567.simple_meaning: Sita rejects Ravana’s boast of strength and calls his conduct shameful to his family and to the world.
ramayan::7567.simple_insight: False strength collapses the moment it is measured against character.
ramayan::7567.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana’s threats without yielding. He has boasted of power and courage; she strips those claims bare, saying his conduct brings disgrace on his lineage and on the world. The verse is part of her sustained moral rebuke.
ramayan::7567.modern_relevance: Someone talks big after crossing a line, then hides behind confidence. You can feel the difference between real strength and loud self-importance in one sentence.
ramayan::7567.insight: It turns bravado into shame by measuring action against character.

ramayan::7568.verse_sanskrit: किं कर्तुं शक्यमेवं हि यज्जवेनैव धावसि । मुहूर्तमपि तिष्ठस्व न जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि । । 35310 । ।
ramayan::7568.verse_hindi: Tarry a little, you will not go back with life. What can be done now since you are running away so swiftly?
ramayan::7568.english_translation: Tarry a little; you will not return alive. What can be done now, since you are running away so swiftly?
ramayan::7568.translation_literal: किम् (what) / कर्तुम् (to do) / शक्यम् (possible) / एवम् (thus) / हि (indeed) / यत् (since) / जवेन (with speed) / एव (indeed) / धावसि (you are running) / मुहूर्तम् (for a moment) / अपि (even) / तिष्ठस्व (stay) / न (not) / जीवन् (alive) / प्रतियास्यसि (you will return)
ramayan::7568.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7568.essence: Running faster cannot undo what is already closing in.
ramayan::7568.simple_meaning: The speaker tells someone to stop running, warning that escape will not save his life.
ramayan::7568.simple_insight: Panic does not create safety; sometimes the danger is already too close.
ramayan::7568.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a tense confrontation, one side taunts the fleeing man and tells him to stop. The warning is plain: running fast will not preserve his life, because the two princes are already close enough to kill him.
ramayan::7568.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone after sending the message, hoping distance will soften what you started. But some moments do not become safer just because you run from them.
ramayan::7568.insight: It shifts the mind from escape fantasy to facing consequences already in motion.

ramayan::7569.verse_sanskrit: न हि चक्षुष्पथं प्राप्य तयोः पार्थिवपुत्रयोः । ससैन्योऽपि समर्थस्त्वं मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम् । । 35311 । ।
ramayan::7569.verse_hindi: If you come within sight of these two princes, it will not be possible for you to live for a moment even if you are with your entire army.
ramayan::7569.english_translation: If you come within sight of these two princes, it will not be possible for you to live for a moment even if you are with your entire army.
ramayan::7569.translation_literal: न हि (indeed not) / चक्षुष्पथं (the path of sight) / प्राप्य (having reached) / तयोः (of those two) / पार्थिवपुत्रयोः (princes, sons of a king) / ससैन्यः अपि (even with an army) / समर्थः (able) / त्वं (you) / मुहूर्तम् अपि (even for a moment) / जीवितुम् (to live)
ramayan::7569.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7569.essence: Their mere sight is enough to end his confidence.
ramayan::7569.simple_meaning: Just seeing these two princes will be enough to end your life, even if you bring your whole army.
ramayan::7569.simple_insight: Some threats are so overwhelming that numbers stop mattering.
ramayan::7569.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a tense exchange, one speaker warns an enemy not to flee or test his luck. He says that if the enemy even comes into sight of the two princes, his army will not save him. The verse sharpens the threat, but it is still part of the warning, not the main teaching.
ramayan::7569.modern_relevance: You walk into a room already rattled, and one calm person makes your whole strategy feel small. Some presences expose how fragile your bluster really is.
ramayan::7569.insight: It shifts attention from force in numbers to force in presence.

ramayan::7570.verse_sanskrit: न त्वं तयोश्शरस्पर्शं सोढुं शक्तः कथञ्चन । वने प्रज्वलितस्येव स्पर्शमग्नेर्विहंगमः । । 35312 । ।
ramayan::7570.verse_hindi: Just as a bird cannot bear the touch of forest fire, you will not be able to endure the mere touch of arrows of the two heroes indeed.
ramayan::7570.english_translation: Just as a bird cannot bear the touch of forest fire, you will not be able to endure the mere touch of arrows of the two heroes indeed.
ramayan::7570.translation_literal: न (not) / त्वं (you) / तयोः (of those two) / शरस्पर्शं (touch of arrows) / सोढुं (to bear) / शक्तः (able) / कथञ्चन (in any way) / वने (in the forest) / प्रज्वलितस्य (of the blazing) / इव (like) / स्पर्शम् (touch) / अग्नेः (of fire) / विहंगमः (bird)
ramayan::7570.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7570.essence: Against such force, pride is only another way to burn.
ramayan::7570.simple_meaning: Ravana cannot survive the arrows of Rama and Lakshmana. Their attack is compared to forest fire touching a bird.
ramayan::7570.simple_insight: Some threats are so overwhelming that resistance only makes the danger clearer.
ramayan::7570.detailed_meaning: In the forest, someone is warning Ravana that Rama and Lakshmana are not ordinary opponents. Their arrows will be as deadly to him as a blazing fire is to a bird. It is a threat inside a larger plea to stop before ruin comes.
ramayan::7570.modern_relevance: You keep pushing into a conflict that is already bigger than your control. Sometimes the bravest move is to hear the warning before the damage becomes irreversible.
ramayan::7570.insight: It sharpens the warning: continued defiance will only lead to destruction.

ramayan::7571.verse_sanskrit: साधु कुर्वाऽऽत्मनः पथ्यं साधु मां मुञ्च रावण । मत्प्रधर्षणरुष्टो हि भ्रात्रा सह पतिर्मम । । 35313 । । विधास्यति विनाशाय त्वं मां यदि न मुञ्चसि ।
ramayan::7571.verse_hindi: O Ravana be good and do whatever is beneficial to you. It is proper for you to release me. If you do not, enraged over my assault, my husband along with his brother, will bring about your destruction.
ramayan::7571.english_translation: O Ravana, be wise and do what is good for you. It is right that you release me. If you do not, my husband, enraged by your outrage, along with his brother, will bring about your destruction.
ramayan::7571.translation_literal: साधु (good / proper) / कुर्व (do) / आत्मनः (for yourself) / पथ्यं (what is beneficial) / साधु (properly) / माम् (me) / मुञ्च (release) / रावण (Ravana) / मत्प्रधर्षण-रुष्टः (angered by my violation) / हि (indeed) / भ्रात्रा (with brother) / सह (together) / पतिः (husband) / मम (my) / विधास्यति (will bring about) / विनाशाय (for destruction) / त्वम् (you) / यदि (if) / न (not) / मुञ्चसि (you release)
ramayan::7571.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7571.essence: Forcing what is not yours plants the seed of your own undoing.
ramayan::7571.simple_meaning: Sita tells Ravana to do what is good for him and let her go. If he refuses, Rama and Lakshmana will destroy him in anger.
ramayan::7571.simple_insight: Forcing what is not yours can turn a victory into your own collapse.
ramayan::7571.detailed_meaning: Sita stands captive in Lanka and speaks to Ravana with calm force. She warns him that abducting her will not end in triumph: Rama, stirred by outrage, will come with Lakshmana and destroy him. Her words are both a warning and a final moral boundary.
ramayan::7571.modern_relevance: You keep pressing a conversation after the other person has clearly said no. The moment may feel powerful, but the cost is already moving toward you.
ramayan::7571.insight: It shifts the mind from possession to consequence: what you seize against dharma returns as destruction.

ramayan::7572.verse_sanskrit: येन त्वं व्यवसायेन बलान्मां हर्तुमिच्छसि । । 35314 । । व्यवसायस्स ते नीच भविष्यति निरर्थकः ।
ramayan::7572.verse_hindi: O vile creature, the effort you are making to abduct me forcibly will be fruitless.
ramayan::7572.english_translation: O vile creature, the effort you are making to abduct me forcibly will be fruitless.
ramayan::7572.translation_literal: येन (by which) / त्वं (you) / व्यवसायेन (with effort / resolve) / बलात् (by force) / माम् (me) / हर्तुम् (to carry away) / इच्छसि (you wish) / व्यवसायः (effort / resolve) / सः (that) / ते (of yours) / नीच (base) / भविष्यति (will become) / निरर्थकः (fruitless)
ramayan::7572.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7572.essence: Force can move you, but it cannot make wrongdoing succeed.
ramayan::7572.simple_meaning: Ravana's attempt to seize Sita by force will not succeed in the way he hopes. She sees his effort as base and empty.
ramayan::7572.simple_insight: You do not have to be conquered just because pressure is strong.
ramayan::7572.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita faces Ravana alone after he has tried threats and persuasion. She does not beg or break; she names his effort for what it is and strips it of power. His force may act on her body, but it cannot give his act meaning.
ramayan::7572.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, pushing you to agree before you are ready. You can feel the pressure without handing over your judgment. Sita shows that force does not automatically become authority.
ramayan::7572.insight: It teaches you to see coercion clearly and refuse to grant it legitimacy.

ramayan::7573.verse_sanskrit: न ह्यहं तमपश्यन्ती भर्तारं विबुधोपमम् । । 35315 । । उत्सहे शत्रुवशगा प्राणान्धारयितुं चिरम् ।
ramayan::7573.verse_hindi: I will not be eager to hold on to my life for long to live at the mercy of the enemy without being able to see my godlike husband.
ramayan::7573.english_translation: I will not be eager to hold on to my life for long to live at the mercy of the enemy without being able to see my godlike husband.
ramayan::7573.translation_literal: न हि (not indeed) / अहम् (I) / तम् (him) / अपश्यन्ती (not seeing) / भर्तारम् (husband) / विबुधोपमम् (godlike) / उत्सहे (I am willing) / शत्रुवशगा (under the control of the enemy) / प्राणान् (life-breaths) / धारयितुम् (to hold on to) / चिरम् (for long)
ramayan::7573.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7573.essence: Separation from what you love can make survival itself feel unbearable.
ramayan::7573.simple_meaning: Sita says she cannot bear to keep living as a captive when she cannot see Rama, whom she calls godlike.
ramayan::7573.simple_insight: Love can make mere survival feel empty when dignity and connection are taken away.
ramayan::7573.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is speaking to Ravana after repeated threats. She refuses to treat captivity as normal life. Her loyalty to Rama is so complete that existence itself feels unbearable without his presence.
ramayan::7573.modern_relevance: You can be surrounded by comfort and still feel trapped when you are cut off from the person or purpose that gives your life shape.
ramayan::7573.insight: It shifts the mind from bare survival to the question of what makes life worth continuing.

ramayan::7574.verse_sanskrit: न नूनं चात्मनः पथ्यं श्रेयो वा समवेक्षसे । । 35316 । । मृत्युकाले यथा मर्त्यो विपरीतानि सेवते ।
ramayan::7574.verse_hindi: At the time of death, mortals behave very differently. They act contrary to their own welfare. Likewise you are not able to foresee what is beneficial and good for you.
ramayan::7574.english_translation: You do not see what is truly good for you. Like mortals at the hour of death, you choose what is harmful.
ramayan::7574.translation_literal: न नूनम् (certainly not) / च (and) / आत्मनः (of yourself) / पथ्यम् (what is beneficial) / श्रेयः वा (or what is good) / समवेक्षसे (you clearly see) / मृत्युकाले (at the time of death) / यथा (as) / मर्त्यः (a mortal) / विपरीतानि (opposite things) / सेवते (serves / chooses)
ramayan::7574.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7574.essence: Want can make you reject your own good.
ramayan::7574.simple_meaning: Sita tells Ravana that he cannot recognize what is good for him. In his blindness, he is choosing the opposite of his own welfare.
ramayan::7574.simple_insight: Self-deception can make harmful choices feel urgent and even reasonable.
ramayan::7574.detailed_meaning: Sita, trapped in Lanka, answers Ravana’s pressure with moral clarity. She warns him that he is acting like a person near death, rejecting what would actually save him. Her words expose his blindness before the next threat lands.
ramayan::7574.modern_relevance: You keep opening the same message thread, even though every reply makes things worse. Part of you knows it, but another part still reaches for it. Sita names that split before it ruins you.
ramayan::7574.insight: It shifts attention from impulse to discernment, showing how desire can invert judgment.

ramayan::7575.verse_sanskrit: मुमूर्षूणां हि सर्वेषां यत्पथ्यं तन्न रोचते । । 35317 । । पश्याम्यद्य हि कण्ठेत्वां कालपाशावपाशितम् ।
ramayan::7575.verse_hindi: Those who wish to die, do not like anything salutary. I see the noose of death wound round your neck now.
ramayan::7575.english_translation: Those who wish to die do not like what is good for them. I see the noose of death wound around your neck now.
ramayan::7575.translation_literal: मुमूर्षूणाम् (of those who wish to die) / हि (indeed) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / यत्पथ्यम् (what is salutary) / तत् (that) / न (not) / रोचते (is pleasing) / पश्यामि (I see) / अद्य (today) / हि (indeed) / कण्ठे (around the neck) / त्वाम् (you) / कालपाशावपाशितम् (bound by the noose of death)
ramayan::7575.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7575.essence: A mind bent on ruin rejects the very thing that could save it.
ramayan::7575.simple_meaning: People who are close to death often reject what would help them. Here, Ravana is being told that death has already closed in on him.
ramayan::7575.simple_insight: Self-destruction often begins as stubborn refusal to listen.
ramayan::7575.detailed_meaning: Ravana has ignored warning after warning in Lanka. The speaker sees that Ravana's mind is already trapped by the force that will destroy him, and that even useful counsel now feels bitter to him.
ramayan::7575.modern_relevance: You keep dismissing the advice that would save your project, your health, or your relationship. By the time the warning feels obvious, the damage is already moving.
ramayan::7575.insight: It shifts you to notice how denial makes even good counsel feel unbearable.

ramayan::7576.verse_sanskrit: यथा चास्मिन्भयस्थाने न बिभेषि दशानन । । 35318 । । व्यक्तं हिरण्मयान् हि त्वं सम्पश्यसि महीरुहान् ।
ramayan::7576.verse_hindi: O tenheaded Ravana, since you do not fear the source of fear, evidently you see golden trees. (a symptom of death).
ramayan::7576.english_translation: O ten-headed Ravana, since you do not fear the source of fear, it is clear that you see golden trees.
ramayan::7576.translation_literal: यथा (since) / च (and) / अस्मिन् (in this) / भय-स्थाने (place of fear) / न (not) / बिभेषि (you fear) / दशानन (O ten-headed one) / व्यक्तम् (clearly) / हिरण्मयान् (golden) / हि (indeed) / त्वम् (you) / सम्पश्यसि (you see) / महीरुहान् (trees)
ramayan::7576.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7576.essence: A mind already lost mistakes danger for beauty.
ramayan::7576.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told that his lack of fear shows he is already seeing things wrongly, as if deadly danger were something beautiful.
ramayan::7576.simple_insight: Self-deception can make danger look harmless, even attractive.
ramayan::7576.detailed_meaning: In the underworld vision of death, the speaker warns Ravana that he is no longer perceiving reality clearly. Because he does not fear this dreadful place, it means his mind is already distorted — he sees golden trees instead of the horrors that await him.
ramayan::7576.modern_relevance: You ignore the warning signs because the situation still feels familiar. By the time danger looks beautiful, judgment has already slipped.
ramayan::7576.insight: It shows how fearlessness can become blindness when the mind has lost its grip on reality.

ramayan::7577.verse_sanskrit: नदीं वैतरणीं घोरां रुधिरौघनिवाहिनीम् । । 35319 । । असिपत्रवनं चैव भीमं पश्यसि रावण ।
ramayan::7577.verse_hindi: O Ravana, you see the dreadful river Vaitarani with torrents of blood flowing and frightening forest of trees with swords as leaves.
ramayan::7577.english_translation: O Ravana, you see the dreadful river Vaitarani with torrents of blood flowing and the frightening forest of trees with swords as leaves.
ramayan::7577.translation_literal: नदीं (river) / वैतरणीं (Vaitarani) / घोरां (dreadful) / रुधिरौघनिवाहिनीम् (carrying torrents of blood) / असिपत्रवनं (the forest of sword-leaves) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / भीमं (terrifying) / पश्यसि (you see) / रावण (Ravana)
ramayan::7577.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7577.essence: Fear has already turned Ravana's vision into punishment.
ramayan::7577.simple_meaning: Ravana is told that his death-like vision is of the terrible river of blood and the forest of sword-leaves.
ramayan::7577.simple_insight: When fear and death are near, the mind can only project torment.
ramayan::7577.detailed_meaning: A voice taunts Ravana as his end approaches, saying he no longer sees the world clearly. Instead, he is seeing the horrors of the afterlife: the blood-filled Vaitarani river and the sword-leaf forest. It is part of a sequence of warnings about death, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7577.modern_relevance: When panic takes over, ordinary reality warps into threat. A tired, cornered mind can turn every sign into a warning of collapse.
ramayan::7577.insight: It shows how terror distorts perception and makes the mind read doom everywhere.

ramayan::7578.verse_sanskrit: तप्तकाञ्चनपुष्पां च वैडूर्यप्रवरच्छदाम् । । 35320 । । द्रक्ष्यसे शाल्मलीं तीक्ष्णामायसैः कण्टकैश्चिताम् ।
ramayan::7578.verse_hindi: You will see a log of salmali tree with bright golden flowers and excellent vaidurya stone with pointed iron thorns.
ramayan::7578.english_translation: You will see the salmali tree, bright with golden flowers and covered with sharp iron thorns.
ramayan::7578.translation_literal: तप्तकाञ्चनपुष्पाम् (with golden flowers) / च (and) / वैडूर्यप्रवरच्छदाम् (with excellent vaidurya-like covering) / द्रक्ष्यसे (you will see) / शाल्मलीम् (the salmali tree) / तीक्ष्णाम् (sharp) / आयसैः (with iron) / कण्टकैः (with thorns) / चिताम् (covered)
ramayan::7578.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7578.essence: Beauty here is only a disguise for pain.
ramayan::7578.simple_meaning: Ravana is being told to imagine a terrible sight in the lower realm: a salmali tree that looks beautiful but is covered in sharp iron thorns.
ramayan::7578.simple_insight: False beauty can hide pain and punishment.
ramayan::7578.detailed_meaning: Ravana is being warned about the consequences of his choice. The speaker piles up images from the lower realm—blood, terror, and a tree that gleams like gold but is laced with iron thorns—to show what awaits someone who harms the noble Rama.
ramayan::7578.modern_relevance: A polished deal looks irresistible on the screen, but the fine print is full of traps. What shines first can still cut deepest.
ramayan::7578.insight: It turns temptation into warning: appearances can be designed to lure you into suffering.

ramayan::7579.verse_sanskrit: न हि त्वमीदृशं कृत्वा तस्यालीकं महात्मनः । । 35321 । । धरितुं शक्ष्यसि चिरं विषं पीत्वेव निर्घृणः ।
ramayan::7579.verse_hindi: You are pitiless. You will not be able to survive for long after deceiving such noble Rama just as man cannot survive after drinking poison.
ramayan::7579.english_translation: You are pitiless. You will not be able to survive for long after deceiving such noble Rama, just as a man cannot survive after drinking poison.
ramayan::7579.translation_literal: न हि (for not) / त्वम् (you) / ईदृशम् (such) / कृत्वा (having done) / तस्य (his) / अलीकम् (falsehood, deceit) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / धरितुम् (to endure, survive) / शक्ष्यसि (you will be able) / चिरम् (for long) / विषम् (poison) / पीत्वा (having drunk) / इव (like) / निर्घृणः (merciless, pitiless)
ramayan::7579.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7579.essence: Deceit against the noble one becomes poison in your own body.
ramayan::7579.simple_meaning: Deceiving a noble person brings ruin. Ravana will not be able to last long after his cruelty, just as poison destroys the one who drinks it.
ramayan::7579.simple_insight: Cruelty carries its own collapse. What you do to others comes back as your own undoing.
ramayan::7579.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana’s threats with unshaken clarity. After describing the horrors awaiting him, she warns that deceiving Rama will not be survivable. Her words sharpen the moral verdict already closing in around Ravana.
ramayan::7579.modern_relevance: You tell a lie that buys you one more week, but the strain starts eating your sleep that same night. Sita names that collapse before it finishes you.
ramayan::7579.insight: It shifts attention from immediate gain to the self-destructive cost of deceit.

ramayan::7580.verse_sanskrit: बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन दुर्निवारेण रावण । । 35322 । । क्वगतो लप्स्यसे शर्म भर्तुर्मम महात्मनः ।
ramayan::7580.verse_hindi: O Ravana you are bound by the inevitable noose of death. Where shall you get away from great Rama, my husband to obtain peace.
ramayan::7580.english_translation: O Ravana, you are bound by the inescapable noose of time. Where will you go to find peace away from my noble husband?
ramayan::7580.translation_literal: बद्धः (bound) / त्वम् (you) / कालपाशेन (by the noose of time) / दुर्निवारेण (inescapable) / रावण (Ravana) / क्व (where) / गतः (gone) / लप्स्यसे (will you obtain) / शर्म (peace) / भर्तुः (of the husband) / मम (my) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one)
ramayan::7580.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7580.essence: You cannot flee the force that has already caught you.
ramayan::7580.simple_meaning: Ravana cannot escape the consequences closing in on him, and peace will not come from fleeing Rama.
ramayan::7580.simple_insight: Some defeats are already decided before the final blow lands.
ramayan::7580.detailed_meaning: Sita, still captive in Lanka, speaks with fearless certainty to Ravana. She names him as already bound by death and says no refuge or peace lies outside Rama. Her words turn fear into moral judgment.
ramayan::7580.modern_relevance: You keep trying to outrun the message, the bill, the apology, the hard conversation. But some consequences are already on the way, and peace comes only through facing them.
ramayan::7580.insight: It shifts the mind from escape to reckoning: you stop bargaining with what is already closing in.

ramayan::7581.verse_sanskrit: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण विना भ्रात्रा महावने । । 35323 । । राक्षसा निहता येन सहस्राणि चतुर्दश । स कथं राघवो वीरस्सर्वास्त्रकुशलो बली । । 35324 । । न त्वां हन्याच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैरिष्टभार्यापहारिणम् ।
ramayan::7581.verse_hindi: Rama has killed fourteen thousand demons alone without his brother within a moment. He is a strong warrior and wellversed in the use of all kinds of weapons. You have stolen his loving wife. How can he live without killing you.
ramayan::7581.english_translation: Rama killed fourteen thousand demons alone in an instant, without his brother. He is a mighty warrior, skilled with every weapon. You have stolen his beloved wife. How could he not kill you with sharp arrows?
ramayan::7581.translation_literal: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण (in just the space of a blink) / विना भ्रात्रा (without his brother) / महावने (in the great forest) / राक्षसा (demons) / निहता (were slain) / येन (by whom) / सहस्राणि (thousands) / चतुर्दश (fourteen) / स (he) / कथम् (how) / राघवः (Raghava) / वीरः (a hero) / सर्वास्त्रकुशलः (skilled in all weapons) / बली (strong) / न (not) / त्वाम् (you) / हन्यात् (would kill) / शरैः (with arrows) / तीक्ष्णैः (sharp) / इष्टभार्यापहारिणम् (the one who stole his beloved wife)
ramayan::7581.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7581.essence: You have not merely offended him; you have awakened his full strength.
ramayan::7581.simple_meaning: Sita argues that Ravana has provoked a warrior who once destroyed fourteen thousand demons alone, so his death is now likely.
ramayan::7581.simple_insight: Cruel actions can awaken consequences you cannot outrun.
ramayan::7581.detailed_meaning: Held captive in Lanka, Sita answers Ravana with fierce clarity. She reminds him that Rama once wiped out fourteen thousand demons alone, then names the real wound: Ravana has stolen Rama's wife. Her words are both warning and judgment.
ramayan::7581.modern_relevance: You break trust with someone who has every reason to act decisively, then act surprised when the cost arrives. Sita names the danger before it becomes fate.
ramayan::7581.insight: It shifts the mind from contempt for the victim to respect for the force you have provoked.

ramayan::7582.verse_sanskrit: तच्चान्यच्च परुषं वैदेही रावणाङ्कगा । । 35325 । । भयशोकसमाविष्टा करुणं विललाप ह ।
ramayan::7582.verse_hindi: Sita, daughter of Videha, full of sorrow and fear under Ravanas grip uttered these partly harsh and partly piteous wordsweeping.
ramayan::7582.english_translation: Sita, daughter of Videha, full of sorrow and fear under Ravana's grip, uttered these partly harsh and partly piteous words, weeping.
ramayan::7582.translation_literal: तच्च (that and) / अन्यच्च (and other) / परुषं (harsh) / वैदेही (the daughter of Videha, Sita) / रावणाङ्कगा (resting on Ravana's lap / in Ravana's grip) / भयशोकसमाविष्टा (filled with fear and grief) / करुणं (piteously, sadly) / विललाप (lamented, wailed) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7582.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7582.essence: Suffering turns even clear speech into a cry.
ramayan::7582.simple_meaning: Sita, seized by Ravana and overwhelmed by fear and grief, cried out in broken lament.
ramayan::7582.simple_insight: Pain can make even a steady voice break into fragments.
ramayan::7582.detailed_meaning: Ravana has carried Sita away into Lanka. In her terror and sorrow, she speaks in a mixed voice of anger, grief, and helplessness. This verse is not a teaching moment; it is the raw sound of abduction.
ramayan::7582.modern_relevance: You realize too late that the room has turned unsafe, and your voice comes out shaken, sharp, and broken all at once.
ramayan::7582.insight: It captures how fear and grief distort speech before they can be controlled.

ramayan::7583.verse_sanskrit: तथा भृशार्तां बहुचैव भाषिणीं विलापपूर्वं करुणं च भामिनीम् । जहार पापः करुणं विचेष्टतीं नृपात्मजामागतगात्रवेपथुम् । । 35326 । ।
ramayan::7583.verse_hindi: Sinful Ravana carried away the beautiful princess trembling with great fear, struggling helplessly, crying pathetically and pleading in many mournful ways.
ramayan::7583.english_translation: Sinful Ravana carried away the beautiful princess trembling with great fear, struggling helplessly, crying pathetically and pleading in many mournful ways.
ramayan::7583.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / भृश-आर्ताम् (deeply afflicted) / बहु-च (and much) / एव (indeed) / भाषिणीम् (speaking) / विलाप-पूर्वम् (with lamentation first) / करुणम् (piteously) / च (and) / भामिनीम् (the beautiful woman) / जहार (carried away) / पापः (the wicked one) / करुणम् (piteously) / विचेष्टतीम् (struggling) / नृप-आत्मजाम् (the king's daughter) / आगत-गात्र-वेपथुम् (with trembling that had come over her body)
ramayan::7583.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7583.essence: Force can carry the body, but it cannot make the act right.
ramayan::7583.simple_meaning: Ravana abducts Sita while she cries, pleads, and trembles in terror. The verse emphasizes her helpless suffering and his cruelty.
ramayan::7583.simple_insight: Cruel power can overwhelm the body, but not the dignity of the one being taken.
ramayan::7583.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita in the forest and is carrying her away by force. She is terrified, pleading, and writhing in helpless protest, while the epic lingers on the violence of the act and the suffering it causes.
ramayan::7583.modern_relevance: A person with power ignores your no, keeps moving, and calls it justified. This verse does not soften that moment: it names the fear, the struggle, and the wrongness of being overpowered.
ramayan::7583.insight: It sharpens attention to coercion and the human cost of domination.

ramayan::7584.verse_sanskrit: ह्रियमाणा तु वैदेही कञ्चिन्नाथमपश्यती । ददर्श गिरिशृङ्गस्थान्पञ्च वानरपुङ्गवान् । । 3541 । ।
ramayan::7584.verse_hindi: While Sita was being kidnapped, she saw no one to protect her. Only five great monkeys stood on the top of a mountain.
ramayan::7584.english_translation: While Sita was being carried away, she saw no protector. Then she saw five great monkeys standing on a mountain peak.
ramayan::7584.translation_literal: ह्रियमाणा (being carried away) / तु (but) / वैदेही (Sita, daughter of Videha) / कञ्चित् (any) / नाथम् (protector) / अपश्यती (not seeing) / ददर्श (she saw) / गिरिशृङ्गस्थान् (standing on a mountain peak) / पञ्च (five) / वानरपुङ्गवान् (great monkeys)
ramayan::7584.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7584.essence: Hope begins when you spot one possible witness.
ramayan::7584.simple_meaning: Sita, being taken away, looked for help and found none. Then she noticed five monkeys on a mountain peak.
ramayan::7584.simple_insight: Even in helplessness, the mind notices the smallest possible sign of rescue.
ramayan::7584.detailed_meaning: Ravana is carrying Sita away through the sky. She searches for any protector and sees none, until her eyes catch five monkeys on a distant mountain peak. This is a tiny but crucial moment before she drops signs for Rama.
ramayan::7584.modern_relevance: You can be overwhelmed and still notice one possible ally in the distance. In the middle of panic, the mind grabs onto the smallest opening.
ramayan::7584.insight: It shifts attention from total helplessness to the first usable sign of support.

ramayan::7585.verse_sanskrit: तेषां मध्ये विशालाक्षी कौशेयं कनकप्रभम् । उत्तरीयं वरारोहा शुभान्याभरणानि च । । 3542 । । मुमोच यदि रामाय शंसेयुरिति मैथिली ।
ramayan::7585.verse_hindi: Largeeyed, bright and beautiful Sita dropped her upper silk garment shining like gold and auspicious ornaments in their midst with a hope they may report this  to Rama.
ramayan::7585.english_translation: Large-eyed, bright and beautiful Sita dropped her upper silk garment, shining like gold, and her auspicious ornaments among them, hoping they would report this to Rama.
ramayan::7585.translation_literal: तेषाम् (among them) / मध्ये (in the midst) / विशालाक्षी (large-eyed one) / कौशेयं (silk cloth) / कनकप्रभम् (golden-bright) / उत्तरीयम् (upper garment) / वरारोहा (beautifully formed woman) / शुभानि (auspicious) / आभरणानि (ornaments) / च (and) / मुमोच (released, dropped) / यदि (if) / रामाय (to Rama) / शंसेयुः (they may report) / इति (thus) / मैथिली (the princess of Mithila)
ramayan::7585.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7585.essence: Hope survives by leaving a trace for the one who must find you.
ramayan::7585.simple_meaning: Sita drops her silk shawl and ornaments in the hope that someone will carry word of her to Rama.
ramayan::7585.simple_insight: Even in captivity, she reaches for the smallest possible bridge back to him.
ramayan::7585.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is carrying her away. She spots five monkeys on a mountain and, in that instant, quietly drops her shining garment and ornaments among them, hoping they will somehow tell Rama where she is.
ramayan::7585.modern_relevance: You lose your phone in a crowded station, but you still leave a note where someone kind might find it. In panic, people still reach for one last thread of connection.
ramayan::7585.insight: It shows how a small, deliberate sign can carry hope when direct help is impossible.

ramayan::7586.verse_sanskrit: वस्त्रमुत्सृज्य तन्मध्ये निक्षिप्तं सहभूषणम् । । 3543 । । सम्भ्रमात्तु दशग्रीवस्तत्कर्म न स बुद्धवान् ।
ramayan::7586.verse_hindi: In his excitement Ravana failed to notice when Sita dropped down that garment along with ornaments in their midst.
ramayan::7586.english_translation: In his excitement, Ravana did not notice when Sita dropped that garment and ornaments among them.
ramayan::7586.translation_literal: वस्त्रम् (garment) / उत्सृज्य (having thrown down) / तत् (that) / मध्ये (in the midst) / निक्षिप्तम् (placed, dropped) / सहभूषणम् (with ornaments) / सम्भ्रमात् (in confusion, excitement) / तु (but) / दशग्रीवः (Ravana) / तत् (that) / कर्म (act) / न (not) / सः (he) / बुद्धवान् (noticed, understood)
ramayan::7586.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7586.essence: Panic can make you blind to the message meant to stop you.
ramayan::7586.simple_meaning: Ravana was so flustered that he did not even notice Sita dropping her garment and ornaments among the monkeys.
ramayan::7586.simple_insight: Panic makes you miss the very signs meant for you.
ramayan::7586.detailed_meaning: Sita is being carried away by Ravana, helpless but still alert. She drops her garment and ornaments so Rama may later find a trace of her. In Ravana's confusion, he misses the signal entirely, and the chance to understand her plea passes him by.
ramayan::7586.modern_relevance: You can be so caught up in getting what you want that you miss the warning signs right in front of you.
ramayan::7586.insight: It shows how desire and haste can blind you to crucial evidence.

ramayan::7587.verse_sanskrit: पिङ्गाक्षास्तां विशालाक्षीं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव । । 3544 । । विक्रोशन्तीं तथा सीतां ददृशुर्वानरर्षभाः ।
ramayan::7587.verse_hindi: The best among the tawneyeyed monkeys gazed, without blinking, at the  largeeyed Sita lamenting.
ramayan::7587.english_translation: The best among the tawny-eyed monkeys gazed, without blinking, at Sita lamenting.
ramayan::7587.translation_literal: पिङ्गाक्षाः (tawny-eyed ones) / ताम् (her) / विशालाक्षीम् (large-eyed) / नेत्रैः (with eyes) / अनिमिषैः इव (as if without blinking) / विक्रोशन्तीम् (lamenting) / तथा (thus) / सीताम् (Sita) / ददृशुः (saw) / वानरर्षभाः (bulls among monkeys)
ramayan::7587.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7587.essence: Witness can be helpless when loss is already in motion.
ramayan::7587.simple_meaning: The monkey leaders stared at Sita as she cried out in distress.
ramayan::7587.simple_insight: Even in helplessness, suffering can hold everyone in silence.
ramayan::7587.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just carried Sita away from the grove, and the monkeys have seen the terrible scene unfold. They stand frozen, watching her lament with unblinking eyes. The verse captures their stunned helplessness before the abduction fully carries her away.
ramayan::7587.modern_relevance: You watch a moment unfold that you cannot stop — a message sent too late, a door closing, someone carried beyond your reach.
ramayan::7587.insight: It fixes the scene of witness: grief is seen clearly, but not yet answered.

ramayan::7588.verse_sanskrit: स च पम्पामतिक्रम्य लङ्कामभिमुखः पुरीम् । । 3545 । । जगाम रुदतीं गृह्य वैदेहीं राक्षसेश्वरः ।
ramayan::7588.verse_hindi: Ravana crossed the lake Pampa and flew towards the city of Lanka carrying with him lamenting daughter of Videha.
ramayan::7588.english_translation: Ravana crossed Pampa and headed toward Lanka, carrying the weeping daughter of Videha.
ramayan::7588.translation_literal: सः (he) / च (and) / पम्पाम् (Pampa) / अतिक्रम्य (having crossed) / लङ्काम् (toward Lanka) / अभिमुखः (facing) / पुरीम् (city) / जगाम (went) / रुदतीम् (weeping) / गृह्य (having seized) / वैदेहीम् (the daughter of Videha) / राक्षसेश्वरः (the lord of the rakshasas)
ramayan::7588.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7588.essence: A single seizure begins a chain that cannot be called back.
ramayan::7588.simple_meaning: Ravana carries Sita away toward Lanka while she weeps.
ramayan::7588.simple_insight: Some moments are not victories at all; they are the beginning of a ruin you cannot yet see.
ramayan::7588.detailed_meaning: After seizing Sita, Ravana turns toward Lanka and leaves the forest behind. Sita is still crying, and the theft is now moving across the landscape. The verse serves as a grim bridge from abduction to the consequences that follow.
ramayan::7588.modern_relevance: A decision made in a flash can keep moving long after the first rush is gone. By the time the harm is visible, it may already be in motion.
ramayan::7588.insight: It shifts attention from the act itself to the irreversible trail it sets in motion.

ramayan::7589.verse_sanskrit: तां जहार सुसंहृष्टो रावणो मृत्युमात्मनः । । 3546 । । उत्सङ्गेनेव भुजगीं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रां महाविषाम् ।
ramayan::7589.verse_hindi: Delighted Ravana, carried off Sita, the very embodiment of his death, like one carrying a highly poisonous sharpfanged female snake on his lap.
ramayan::7589.english_translation: Delighted Ravana carried off Sita, the very embodiment of his death, like one carrying a highly poisonous, sharp-fanged female snake on his lap.
ramayan::7589.translation_literal: तां (her) / जहार (carried off) / सुसंहृष्टो (greatly delighted) / रावणो (Ravana) / मृत्युम् (death) / आत्मनः (of himself) / उत्सङ्गेन (on the lap) / इव (like) / भुजगीम् (female snake) / तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राम् (sharp-fanged) / महाविषाम् (highly poisonous)
ramayan::7589.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7589.essence: Victory already carries the poison that will end it.
ramayan::7589.simple_meaning: Ravana abducted Sita joyfully, but he was really carrying the cause of his own destruction.
ramayan::7589.simple_insight: What feels like victory can already contain the seed of ruin.
ramayan::7589.detailed_meaning: Ravana leaves Lanka with Sita in his grasp, triumphant and unaware of the cost. Valmiki frames the moment as irony: the king thinks he has won, but he has picked up his own death and is carrying it home.
ramayan::7589.modern_relevance: You finally get what you wanted, and the thrill feels clean for one second. Then you realize you dragged home the very thing that will undo you.
ramayan::7589.insight: It turns conquest into warning: desire can feel like triumph while secretly becoming self-destruction.

ramayan::7590.verse_sanskrit: वनानि सरितश्शैलांत्सरांसि च विहायसा । । 3547 । । स क्षिप्रं समतीयाय शरश्चापादिव च्युतः ।
ramayan::7590.verse_hindi: Like an arrow released from the bow, Ravana went through the sky, at once crossing forests, rivers mountains and tanks.
ramayan::7590.english_translation: Like an arrow released from the bow, Ravana went through the sky, at once crossing forests, rivers, mountains, and tanks.
ramayan::7590.translation_literal: वनानि (forests) / सरितः (rivers) / शैलान् (mountains) / सरांसि (lakes) / च (and) / विहायसा (through the sky) / सः (he) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / समतीयाय (crossed over) / शरः (arrow) / चापात् (from the bow) / इव (like) / च्युतः (released)
ramayan::7590.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7590.essence: Ravana moves fast, but the cost of his act moves with him.
ramayan::7590.simple_meaning: Ravana flies rapidly through the sky, crossing every obstacle in his path as if he were an arrow shot from a bow.
ramayan::7590.simple_insight: Speed can carry you forward, but it cannot save you from what you have done.
ramayan::7590.detailed_meaning: After seizing Sita, Ravana rushes toward Lanka through the air, passing forests, rivers, mountains, and lakes in one swift motion. The verse is a visual bridge in the abduction sequence, not a reflective teaching.
ramayan::7590.modern_relevance: A mistake is made, and then everything speeds up: the call, the drive, the excuses, the damage. Some moments move like an arrow — fast enough to outrun thought, not consequence.
ramayan::7590.insight: It shifts attention from the drama of motion to the moral weight of what is being carried away.

ramayan::7591.verse_sanskrit: तिमिनक्रनिकेतं तु वरुणालयमक्षयम् । । 3548 । । सरितां शरणं गत्वा समतीयाय सागरम् ।
ramayan::7591.verse_hindi: Ravana soon crossed the refuge of rivers, the abode of Varuna, god of the sea, inexhaustible ocean, and the home for whales and crocodiles.
ramayan::7591.english_translation: Ravana soon crossed the ocean, the refuge of rivers, the inexhaustible abode of Varuna, home of whales and crocodiles.
ramayan::7591.translation_literal: तिमिनक्रनिकेतम् (home of whales and crocodiles) / तु (but) / वरुणालयम् (abode of Varuna) / अक्षयम् (inexhaustible) / सरिताम् (of rivers) / शरणम् (refuge) / गत्वा (having gone) / समतीयाय (crossed over) / सागरम् (the ocean)
ramayan::7591.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7591.essence: Ravana keeps moving toward the ruin he cannot yet see.
ramayan::7591.simple_meaning: Ravana crossed the ocean quickly after carrying Sita away.
ramayan::7591.simple_insight: The journey is unstoppable once desire has taken hold.
ramayan::7591.detailed_meaning: Ravana has seized Sita and is racing through the sky toward Lanka. This line marks his crossing of the sea itself, a vast natural barrier that even his power can only briefly defy. It is scene-setting, not a teaching.
ramayan::7591.modern_relevance: A decision made in anger or obsession can carry you far before you even feel the cost.
ramayan::7591.insight: It frames the abduction as a swift, irreversible movement toward disaster.

ramayan::7592.verse_sanskrit: सम्भ्रमात्परिवृत्तोर्मी रुद्धमीनमहोरगः । । 3549 । । वैदेह्यां ह्रियमाणायां बभूव वरुणालयः ।
ramayan::7592.verse_hindi: While Sita, princess of Videha was being carried away, the ocean, abode of Varuna
ramayan::7592.english_translation: The ocean, abode of Varuna, was agitated, its waves turning back in confusion, and its fish and great serpents held back, while Sita of Videha was being carried away.
ramayan::7592.translation_literal: सम्भ्रमात् (in confusion) / परिवृत्त-ऊर्मी (with waves turned back) / रुद्ध-मीन-महोरगः (with fish and great serpents restrained) / वैदेह्यां (while the princess of Videha) / ह्रियमाणायां (was being carried away) / बभूव (became) / वरुणालयः (the abode of Varuna, the ocean)
ramayan::7592.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7592.essence: A great wrong is so severe that even the sea seems shaken.
ramayan::7592.simple_meaning: The sea itself seems disturbed as Sita is carried away, with its waves, fish, and great serpents held in turmoil.
ramayan::7592.simple_insight: Even nature seems to recoil when innocence is violated.
ramayan::7592.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already crossed the ocean with Sita in his grasp. As he moves through the sky, Valmiki pauses on the sea below: its waves churn backward, and its creatures are held in agitation. The moment heightens the horror of the abduction.
ramayan::7592.modern_relevance: You watch something wrong happen in silence, and even the room feels different. The air, the water, the whole world seems to know a line has been crossed.
ramayan::7592.insight: It turns a private crime into a cosmic disturbance, making the violation feel unbearable.

ramayan::7593.verse_sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षगता वाचस्ससृजुश्चारणास्तदा । । 35410 । । एतदन्तो दशग्रीव इति सिद्धास्तदाब्रुवन् ।
ramayan::7593.verse_hindi: The charanas and siddhas moving in the sky said, O tenheaded Ravana this is your  end .
ramayan::7593.english_translation: Then the celestial beings moving through the sky spoke words: "O ten-headed Ravana, this is your end."
ramayan::7593.translation_literal: अन्तरिक्षगता (moving through the sky) / वाचः (words) / ससृजुः (they uttered) / चारणाः (the celestial singers) / तदा (then) / एतदन्तः (this is the end) / दशग्रीवः (ten-headed Ravana) / इति (thus) / सिद्धाः (the perfected beings) / तदा (then) / अब्रुवन् (they said)
ramayan::7593.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7593.essence: The moment of triumph already carries the seed of ruin.
ramayan::7593.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings see Ravana’s fate and announce that his end has arrived.
ramayan::7593.simple_insight: Power looks absolute until the moment the world quietly names its fall.
ramayan::7593.detailed_meaning: As Ravana carries Sita toward Lanka, beings in the sky watch the scene unfold. The charanas and siddhas speak aloud what the moment already contains: the abduction itself is the beginning of Ravana’s end.
ramayan::7593.modern_relevance: You can feel a situation turning before it breaks. The room is still moving, but something in it has already crossed the line.
ramayan::7593.insight: It frames Ravana’s triumph as the start of his collapse, not his victory.

ramayan::7594.verse_sanskrit: स तु सीतां विवेष्टन्तीमङ्केनादाय रावणः । । 35411 । । प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां रूपिणीं मृत्युमात्मनः ।
ramayan::7594.verse_hindi: Ravana entered the city of Lanka holding Sita who was tossing from side to side and who was the very embodiment of his death.
ramayan::7594.english_translation: Ravana entered the city of Lanka holding Sita who was tossing from side to side and who was the very embodiment of his death.
ramayan::7594.translation_literal: सः (he) / तु (indeed) / सीताम् (Sita) / विवेष्टन्तीम् (tossing about) / अङ्केन (in his lap/arms) / आदाय (having taken) / रावणः (Ravana) / प्रविवेश (entered) / पुरीम् (the city) / लङ्काम् (Lanka) / रूपिणीम् (embodied) / मृत्युम् (death) / आत्मनः (of his own)
ramayan::7594.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7594.essence: His prize is already the shape of his fall.
ramayan::7594.simple_meaning: Ravana carries Sita into Lanka, but the capture is also the beginning of his own destruction.
ramayan::7594.simple_insight: What you seize in anger can become the shape of your undoing.
ramayan::7594.detailed_meaning: Ravana has crossed the line from desire into irreversible ruin. He brings Sita into Lanka as a trophy, but the poem frames her as his own death already walking beside him. The next verse simply carries him deeper into the consequences.
ramayan::7594.modern_relevance: You finally get what you chased, and the room goes quiet. The victory feels heavy because something in you already knows it will cost more than it gave.
ramayan::7594.insight: It turns possession into consequence: the thing taken in greed becomes the seed of collapse.

ramayan::7595.verse_sanskrit: सोऽभिगम्य पुरीं लङ्कां सुविभक्तमहापथाम् । । 35412 । । संरूढकक्ष्याबहुलं स्वमन्तःपुरमाविशत् ।
ramayan::7595.verse_hindi: Ravana went through the well laidout roads of the city of Lanka and through the well many guarded halls of the palace and entered the inner apartment.
ramayan::7595.english_translation: Ravana went through the well-laid roads of Lanka and entered his inner palace through many guarded chambers.
ramayan::7595.translation_literal: सः (he) / अभिगम्य (having gone to) / पुरीम् (the city) / लङ्काम् (Lanka) / सुविभक्त-महापथाम् (with well-arranged great roads) / संरूढ-कक्ष्या-बहुलम् (full of many guarded chambers) / स्वम् (his own) / अन्तःपुरम् (inner palace) / आविशत् (entered)
ramayan::7595.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7595.essence: Orderly streets can still lead straight into cruelty.
ramayan::7595.simple_meaning: Ravana carried Sita into Lanka and entered his private palace through its guarded corridors.
ramayan::7595.simple_insight: The scene tightens the trap around Sita, showing how power can turn movement into captivity.
ramayan::7595.detailed_meaning: Ravana has crossed into Lanka with Sita in his arms. He moves through the city's ordered roads and heavily guarded palace corridors, not as a king at peace but as a captor returning to his hidden quarters. The next verse will show where he places her.
ramayan::7595.modern_relevance: You can walk through polished hallways and still be carrying something shameful into private space.
ramayan::7595.insight: It shifts attention from grandeur to violation: the city looks orderly, but the act inside it is corrupt.

ramayan::7596.verse_sanskrit: तत्र तामसितापाङ्गां शोकमोहपरायणाम् । । 35413 । । निदधे रावणस्सीतां मयो मायामिवस्त्रियम् ।
ramayan::7596.verse_hindi: Sita, with her dark eye lashes and lost in utter sorrow was kept in the harem by Ravana, like demon Maya kept Mayamayi.
ramayan::7596.english_translation: Ravana placed Sita in the inner women’s quarters, dark-eyed and overcome by grief and confusion, like a deluding illusion hidden away.
ramayan::7596.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / ताम् (her) / असितापाङ्गाम् (dark-eyed) / शोकमोहपरायणाम् (devoted to sorrow and confusion) / निदधे (placed) / रावणः (Ravana) / सीताम् (Sita) / मया (by Maya) / मायाम् इव (like an illusion) / स्त्रियम् (woman)
ramayan::7596.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7596.essence: Taking what cannot be won leads to hiding it away.
ramayan::7596.simple_meaning: Ravana confined Sita inside his palace, where grief and confusion surrounded her.
ramayan::7596.simple_insight: Cruel control often hides fear of what it cannot truly possess.
ramayan::7596.detailed_meaning: Ravana brings Sita into Lanka and hides her in the inner women’s quarters. She is overwhelmed by sorrow, while he treats her like something to be concealed. The next verse shows him tightening control so no one can see her.
ramayan::7596.modern_relevance: Someone locks a painful truth behind closed doors and calls it protection. The secrecy never heals what the taking has broken.
ramayan::7596.insight: It shows how possession turns into concealment, and concealment into deeper harm.

ramayan::7597.verse_sanskrit: अब्रवीच्च दशग्रीवः पिशाचीर्घोरदर्शनाः । । 35414 । । यथा नेमां पुमान् स्त्री वा सीतां पश्यत्यसम्मतः ।
ramayan::7597.verse_hindi: Ravana ordered the female goblins of fearful appearance,Let no outsider whether man or woman, see her, without my permission.
ramayan::7597.english_translation: Ravana ordered the fearsome female goblins: let no man or woman see Sita without my permission.
ramayan::7597.translation_literal: अब्रवीत् (said) / च (and) / दशग्रीवः (the ten-necked one, Ravana) / पिशाचीः (female goblins) / घोर-दर्शनाः (fearful-looking) / यथा (so that) / न (not) / इमाम् (this one) / पुमान् (man) / स्त्री वा (or woman) / सीताम् (Sita) / पश्यति (sees) / असम्मतः (without permission)
ramayan::7597.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7597.essence: Possession turns immediately into secrecy and control.
ramayan::7597.simple_meaning: Ravana orders Sita to be kept hidden so no one can see her without his permission.
ramayan::7597.simple_insight: Control grows stronger when fear replaces trust.
ramayan::7597.detailed_meaning: Ravana has brought Sita into Lanka and placed her in the inner women’s quarters. Now he commands the terrifying female guards to keep her hidden from everyone, tightening his control over her isolation.
ramayan::7597.modern_relevance: Someone locks their phone, changes the passwords, and starts controlling who can speak to whom. Possession always wants secrecy next.
ramayan::7597.insight: It shows how domination isolates its victim before it speaks of care.

ramayan::7598.verse_sanskrit: मुक्तामणिसुवर्णानि वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च । । 35415 । । यद्यदिच्छेत्तदेवास्या देयं मच्छन्दतो यथा ।
ramayan::7598.verse_hindi: Pearls, gems or gold, clothes or ornaments, whatever she desires, be made available to her without any hesitation.
ramayan::7598.english_translation: Pearls, gems, gold, clothes, or ornaments—whatever she desires should be given to her freely, without hesitation.
ramayan::7598.translation_literal: मुक्तामणिसुवर्णानि (pearls, gems, and gold) / वस्त्राणि (clothes) / आभरणानि (ornaments) / च (and) / यद्यत् (whatever) / इच्छेत् (she may desire) / तत् एव (that itself) / अस्याः (to her) / देयम् (should be given) / मच्छन्दतः (according to my will) / यथा (as)
ramayan::7598.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7598.essence: He offers luxury, but keeps the cage closed.
ramayan::7598.simple_meaning: Ravana orders that Sita be given anything she wants—jewels, clothes, or ornaments—without delay.
ramayan::7598.simple_insight: Cruelty can still wear the mask of generosity.
ramayan::7598.detailed_meaning: Ravana has confined Sita in Lanka and barred all outsiders from seeing her. In the same breath, he orders his attendants to supply her with anything she asks for. The verse shows his possessive control disguised as care.
ramayan::7598.modern_relevance: Someone says, "Take whatever you need," while controlling your movements and choices. The gesture sounds generous, but the power behind it tells the real story.
ramayan::7598.insight: It teaches you to notice when provision is being used to hide domination.

ramayan::7599.verse_sanskrit: या च वक्ष्यति वैदेहीं वचनं किञ्चिदप्रियम् । । 35416 । । अज्ञानाद्यदि वा ज्ञानान्न तस्या जीवितं प्रियम् ।
ramayan::7599.verse_hindi: Whoever utters any unpleasant words knowingly or unknowingly to Sita, princess of Videha is not worthy to survive (must be killed).
ramayan::7599.english_translation: Whoever utters any unpleasant words knowingly or unknowingly to Sita, princess of Videha, is not worthy to survive.
ramayan::7599.translation_literal: या (who) / च (and) / वक्ष्यति (will speak) / वैदेहीं (to the princess of Videha) / वचनं (a word) / किञ्चिदप्रियम् (something unpleasant) / अज्ञानात् (out of ignorance) / यदि वा (or even if) / ज्ञानात् (knowingly) / न (not) / तस्या (for that person's) / जीवितं (life) / प्रियम् (dear)
ramayan::7599.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7599.essence: A captive's dignity still demands careful speech.
ramayan::7599.simple_meaning: Sita must be treated with complete care. Ravana orders that even accidental harshness toward her is unacceptable.
ramayan::7599.simple_insight: Respect is shown not only in grand acts, but in the words you allow around someone in pain.
ramayan::7599.detailed_meaning: Ravana has Sita confined in Lanka, yet he still commands his attendants to keep her comfortable and untouched by insult. The passage shows his possessive authority, but also the seriousness with which her dignity is being guarded in this moment.
ramayan::7599.modern_relevance: A family member is already overwhelmed, and one careless comment in the room can cut deeper than the original problem. This verse reminds you that protection includes speech, not just action.
ramayan::7599.insight: It shifts you from passive concern to active protection of another person's dignity.

ramayan::7600.verse_sanskrit: तथोक्त्वा राक्षसीस्तास्तु राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान् । । 35417 । । निष्क्रम्यान्तः पुरात्तस्मात्किंकृत्यमिति चिन्तयन् । ददर्शाष्टौ महावीर्यान्राक्षसान्पिशिताशनान् । । 35418 । ।
ramayan::7600.verse_hindi: The courageous lord of the demons, having said so to the demonesses, came out of the inner apartment. While contemplating the future course of action, he saw eight powerful, carnivorous demons.
ramayan::7600.english_translation: Having said this to the demonesses, the powerful lord of the demons left the inner apartment. Thinking about what should be done next, he saw eight mighty flesh-eating demons.
ramayan::7600.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / राक्षसीः (the demonesses) / ताः (those) / तु (indeed) / राक्षसेन्द्रः (the lord of the demons) / प्रतापवान् (the powerful) / निष्क्रम्य (having come out) / अन्तःपुरात् (from the inner apartment) / तस्मात् (from there) / किंकृत्यम् (what should be done) / इति (thus) / चिन्तयन् (thinking) / ददर्श (he saw) / अष्टौ (eight) / महावीर्यान् (very mighty) / राक्षसान् (demons) / पिशिताशनान् (flesh-eaters)
ramayan::7600.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7600.essence: Ravana keeps moving, but his mind never leaves the hunt for control.
ramayan::7600.simple_meaning: Ravana leaves the inner chambers, still thinking about his next move, and notices eight powerful demons.
ramayan::7600.simple_insight: A mind in motion keeps scanning for its next weapon.
ramayan::7600.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just issued harsh orders about Sita’s safety inside the palace. He steps out of the inner chambers, still calculating what to do next, and notices eight fierce demons nearby. The scene simply moves the action forward.
ramayan::7600.modern_relevance: You finish one difficult conversation and walk out still replaying your next move. Before the mind settles, it is already looking for the next ally, the next tactic, the next threat.
ramayan::7600.insight: It shifts attention from the command just spoken to the strategy still forming.

ramayan::7601.verse_sanskrit: स तान्दृष्ट्वा महावीर्यो वरदानेन मोहितः । उवाचैतानिदं वाक्यं प्रशस्य बलवीर्यतः । । 35419 । ।
ramayan::7601.verse_hindi: The mighty Ravana, deluded by the boons, praised the strength and valour of the demons and said :
ramayan::7601.english_translation: The mighty Ravana, deluded by the boons, praised the strength and valour of the demons and said:
ramayan::7601.translation_literal: सः (he) / तान् (those) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / महावीर्यः (very mighty) / वरदानेन (by the boon-gift) / मोहितः (deluded) / उवाच (said) / एतान् (to these) / इदम् (this) / वाक्यम् (speech) / प्रशस्य (having praised) / बलवीर्यतः (by strength and valour)
ramayan::7601.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7601.essence: Power without clear seeing turns praise into self-deception.
ramayan::7601.simple_meaning: Ravana, swollen by the power of his boons, praises his demon forces and speaks to them.
ramayan::7601.simple_insight: Pride can make strength feel like certainty.
ramayan::7601.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just finished speaking harshly about Sita and steps out of his inner chambers. Seeing his demon forces, he becomes intoxicated by the boons he has received and turns to praise their strength. The verse sets up the command that follows.
ramayan::7601.modern_relevance: You get a little power, and suddenly your own confidence starts sounding like wisdom. That is how poor decisions begin.
ramayan::7601.insight: It shows how power can distort judgment before action even begins.

ramayan::7602.verse_sanskrit: नानाप्रहरणाः क्षिप्रमितो गच्छत सत्वराः । जनस्थानं हतस्थानं भूतपूर्वं खरालयम् । । 35420 । ।
ramayan::7602.verse_hindi: Armed with different weapons, proceed at once to Janasthana where Khara lived and died.
ramayan::7602.english_translation: Armed with different weapons, proceed at once to Janasthana where Khara lived and died.
ramayan::7602.translation_literal: नानाप्रहरणाः (with various weapons) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / इतः (from here) / गच्छत (go) / सत्वराः (hastily) / जनस्थानम् (to Janasthana) / हतस्थानम् (the place of the slain) / भूतपूर्वम् (formerly existing) / खरालयम् (Khara's abode)
ramayan::7602.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7602.essence: Ravana turns loss into another attack.
ramayan::7602.simple_meaning: Ravana orders the demons to go quickly, fully armed, to Janasthana, the place where Khara once lived.
ramayan::7602.simple_insight: The command is about speed, force, and retaliation — not reflection.
ramayan::7602.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just left the inner chambers and, still under the spell of his own power, turns to his demon followers. He sends them armed to Janasthana, the ruined place where Khara was killed, preparing another violent move in the widening conflict.
ramayan::7602.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with angry messages after someone is humiliated. Within minutes, people are ready to rush in armed with opinions and loyalty, not wisdom.
ramayan::7602.insight: It shows how anger quickly becomes mobilisation when ego feels threatened.

ramayan::7603.verse_sanskrit: तत्रोष्यतां जनस्थाने शून्ये निहतराक्षसे । पौरुषं बलमाश्रित्य त्रासमुत्सृज्य दूरतः । । 35421 । ।
ramayan::7603.verse_hindi: Go and there in the desolate Janasthana where all demons had been killed, leaving all your apprehensions and relying on your strength and vigour.
ramayan::7603.english_translation: Go and stay in the deserted Janasthana, where the demons have been slain. Put fear far away and rely on your own strength and courage.
ramayan::7603.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / उष्यतां (let it be stayed) / जनस्थाने (in Janasthana) / शून्ये (desolate) / निहत-राक्षसे (where the demons have been slain) / पौरुषम् (manliness / courage) / बलम् (strength) / आश्रित्य (having relied on) / त्रासम् (fear) / उत्सृज्य (having cast off) / दूरतः (far away)
ramayan::7603.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7603.essence: Pride tells you empty ground is safe ground.
ramayan::7603.simple_meaning: Ravana tells his forces to occupy the empty Janasthana, drop their fear, and depend on their own strength.
ramayan::7603.simple_insight: Confidence can become recklessness when it is built on pride instead of judgment.
ramayan::7603.detailed_meaning: Ravana, swollen by power after the slaughter at Janasthana, urges his followers to move into the emptied forest stronghold. He speaks like a commander who mistakes force for safety, just before the next stage of conflict hardens.
ramayan::7603.modern_relevance: You walk into a project that already burned someone else out, and call it easy because the room is empty now. Pride can make danger look like opportunity.
ramayan::7603.insight: It shows how bravado can replace caution when a mind is intoxicated by victory.

ramayan::7604.verse_sanskrit: बलं हि सुमहद्यन्मे जनस्थाने निवेशितम् । सदूषणखरं युद्धे हतं रामेण सायकैः । । 35422 । ।
ramayan::7604.verse_hindi: I had stationed a great army at Janasthana, who were all killed along with Khara and Dusana by Ramas arrows.
ramayan::7604.english_translation: I had stationed a great army at Janasthana, and Rama killed it there with his arrows, along with Khara and Dusana.
ramayan::7604.translation_literal: बलम् (army) / हि (indeed) / सुमहत् (very great) / यत् (which) / मे (my) / जनस्थाने (at Janasthana) / निवेशितम् (stationed) / सदूषणखरम् (with Sadushana and Khara) / युद्धे (in battle) / हतम् (killed) / रामेण (by Rama) / सायकैः (with arrows)
ramayan::7604.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7604.essence: A battlefield loss becomes the beginning of a dangerous vendetta.
ramayan::7604.simple_meaning: Ravana says his powerful force at Janasthana was wiped out by Rama's arrows, including Khara and Dusana.
ramayan::7604.simple_insight: Power can vanish in a single decisive defeat.
ramayan::7604.detailed_meaning: Ravana is recalling the loss of his forces at Janasthana, where Khara and Dusana were also slain by Rama. This is not a teaching verse but part of his mounting anger, leading into his vow of revenge.
ramayan::7604.modern_relevance: You replay the moment everything went wrong and can still feel the sting. The loss itself is over, but the mind keeps sharpening it into grievance.
ramayan::7604.insight: It frames the defeat as the seed of obsession, not just a military loss.

ramayan::7605.verse_sanskrit: तत क्रोधो ममामर्षाद्धैर्यस्योपरि वर्तते । वैरं च सुमहज्जातं रामं प्रति सुदारुणम् । । 35423 । ।
ramayan::7605.verse_hindi: My anger engineered by my intolerance has crossed the limits of my patience. It has created in me a terrific enmity against Rama.
ramayan::7605.english_translation: My anger, born of intolerable humiliation, has gone beyond my patience. It has formed a terrible enmity toward Rama.
ramayan::7605.translation_literal: तत् (then) / क्रोधः (anger) / मम (my) / अमर्षात् (from intolerance, from wounded pride) / धैर्यस्य (of patience, of endurance) / उपरि (beyond, over) / वर्तते (is moving, is rising) / वैरम् (enmity) / च (and) / सुमहत् (very great) / जातम् (has arisen) / रामम् (toward Rama) / प्रति (against) / सुदारुणम् (terrible, fierce)
ramayan::7605.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7605.essence: Wounded pride is turning into violent enmity.
ramayan::7605.simple_meaning: Ravana admits that wounded pride has turned into anger and fierce hatred for Rama.
ramayan::7605.simple_insight: Unchecked hurt can harden into hatred before you notice it.
ramayan::7605.detailed_meaning: Ravana, stung by the loss of his warriors and the killing of Khara and Dushana, speaks from humiliation rather than clarity. He recognizes that his patience is breaking and that his resentment toward Rama is becoming dangerous.
ramayan::7605.modern_relevance: You replay one insult all night, and by morning it has become a story about revenge. The wound was small; the hatred grew around it.
ramayan::7605.insight: It shows how pride, once injured, can escalate into a resolve to retaliate.

ramayan::7606.verse_sanskrit: निर्यातयितुमिच्छामि तच्च वैरमहं रिपोः । न हि लप्स्याम्यहं निद्रामहत्वा संयुगे रिपुम् । । 35424 । ।
ramayan::7606.verse_hindi: I want to take revenge on my foe. I shall not sleep until I kill him in a combat.
ramayan::7606.english_translation: I want to avenge that enmity against my foe. I shall not sleep until I have killed my enemy in battle.
ramayan::7606.translation_literal: निर्यातयितुम् (to send out / to remove) / इच्छामि (I wish) / तत् (that) / च (and) / वैरम् (enmity / revenge) / अहम् (I) / रिपोः (of the enemy) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / लप्स्यामि (I shall obtain) / अहम् (I) / निद्राम् (sleep) / अहत्वा (without killing) / संयुगे (in battle) / रिपुम् (the enemy)
ramayan::7606.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7606.essence: Revenge promises rest but keeps you awake.
ramayan::7606.simple_meaning: Ravana says he will not rest until he has killed his enemy in battle and settled his revenge.
ramayan::7606.simple_insight: Unchecked anger steals sleep, peace, and judgment.
ramayan::7606.detailed_meaning: Ravana speaks after hearing of Khara and Dushana’s defeat. His outrage has hardened into revenge, and he vows that only Rama’s death will end his unrest. The verse shows desire turning into obsession.
ramayan::7606.modern_relevance: You replay a fight in your head at 2 a.m., building a case instead of sleeping. The mind wants payback, but it only deepens the wound.
ramayan::7606.insight: It exposes how revenge keeps the mind trapped in agitation instead of restoring balance.

ramayan::7607.verse_sanskrit: तं त्विदानीमहं हत्वा खरदूषणघातिनम् । रामं शर्मोपलप्स्यामि धनं लब्ध्वेव निर्धनः । । 35425 । ।
ramayan::7607.verse_hindi: I will be happy only after killing the destroyer of Khara and Dusana, just as a poor man feels happy only on acquiring wealth.
ramayan::7607.english_translation: I will be happy only after killing Rama, the slayer of Khara and Dushana, just as a poor man feels happy only on acquiring wealth.
ramayan::7607.translation_literal: तम् (him) / तु (indeed) / इदानीम् (now) / अहम् (I) / हत्वा (having killed) / खरदूषणघातिनम् (the slayer of Khara and Dushana) / रामम् (Rama) / शर्म (peace/happiness) / उपलप्स्यामि (I will obtain) / धनम् (wealth) / लब्ध्वा (having obtained) / इव (like) / निर्धनः (a poor man)
ramayan::7607.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7607.essence: He mistakes another man's death for his own peace.
ramayan::7607.simple_meaning: Ravana says he will feel relief only after killing Rama, comparing that relief to a poor person suddenly gaining wealth.
ramayan::7607.simple_insight: Obsession can make peace feel impossible until the target is gone.
