ramayan::7607.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still feeding his rage after Khara and Dushana’s death. He speaks like a man possessed, convinced that only Rama’s death will restore his comfort. The verse is one link in his escalating plan for revenge.
ramayan::7607.modern_relevance: You keep replaying one insult, one loss, one person’s success, and tell yourself you can’t relax until it is fixed.
ramayan::7607.insight: It shows how revenge narrows the mind until relief is tied to destruction.

ramayan::7608.verse_sanskrit: जनस्थाने वसद्भिस्तु भवद्भीराममाश्रिता । प्रवृत्तिरुपनेतव्या किञ्करोतीति तत्त्वतः । । 35426 । ।
ramayan::7608.verse_hindi: While dwelling at Janasthana, all of you should collect exact information about the activities of Rama.
ramayan::7608.english_translation: While dwelling at Janasthana, all of you should collect exact information about the activities of Rama.
ramayan::7608.translation_literal: जनस्थाने (in Janasthana) / वसद्भिः (by those dwelling) / तु (but) / भवद्भिः (by you all) / रामम् (Rama) / आश्रिता (having taken refuge in / relying on) / प्रवृत्तिः (news / report) / उपनेतव्या (should be brought / conveyed) / किञ्करोति (what he is doing) / इति (thus) / तत्त्वतः (accurately / in truth)
ramayan::7608.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7608.essence: Ravana wants intelligence before action, because obsession needs constant watching.
ramayan::7608.simple_meaning: Ravana orders his spies to stay in Janasthana and bring him exact reports on what Rama is doing.
ramayan::7608.simple_insight: Obsession makes people monitor what threatens them instead of facing it directly.
ramayan::7608.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already decided to kill Rama. Now, from Janasthana, he tells his followers to watch Rama closely and bring back precise reports of his movements. It is part of a longer scheme of revenge, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::7608.modern_relevance: You keep checking someone’s posts, messages, and status because they unsettle you. The more threatened you feel, the more you start tracking instead of acting.
ramayan::7608.insight: It shows how fear turns into surveillance and keeps attention fixed on an enemy.

ramayan::7609.verse_sanskrit: अप्रमादाच्च गन्तव्यं सर्वैरपि निशाचरैः । कर्तव्यश्च सदा यत्नो राघवस्य वधं प्रति । । 35427 । ।
ramayan::7609.verse_hindi: All of you, O nightrangers, should be on the alert there and it should be always your duty to try to kill Rama.
ramayan::7609.english_translation: All of you, O night-rangers, should stay alert there, and you should always keep trying to kill Rama.
ramayan::7609.translation_literal: अप्रमादात् (with vigilance) / च (and) / गन्तव्यम् (should go) / सर्वैः अपि (by all indeed) / निशाचरैः (night-rangers) / कर्तव्यः (to be done) / च (and) / सदा (always) / यत्नः (effort) / राघवस्य (of Rama) / वधम् (killing) / प्रति (toward)
ramayan::7609.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7609.essence: Ravana turns vigilance into a permanent campaign against Rama.
ramayan::7609.simple_meaning: Ravana orders his followers to stay alert and keep trying to kill Rama at all times.
ramayan::7609.simple_insight: A fixed obsession can turn vigilance into a weapon.
ramayan::7609.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Ravana is directing the night-rangers after gathering reports about Rama. He does not ask for a one-time attack; he commands constant alertness and repeated effort to bring Rama down. The verse is part of his planning, not the passage's main teaching.
ramayan::7609.modern_relevance: A grudge can start running your schedule. You check, track, and plan around one person until your mind belongs to them.
ramayan::7609.insight: It shows how obsession narrows attention and turns every day into pursuit.

ramayan::7610.verse_sanskrit: युष्माकं च बलज्ञोऽहं बहुशो रणमूर्धनि । अतश्चास्मिन् जनस्थाने मया यूयं नियोजिताः । । 35428 । ।
ramayan::7610.verse_hindi: I have seen your strength on many war fronts. That is why you have been assigned this  duty at Janasthana.
ramayan::7610.english_translation: I have seen your strength on many war fronts. That is why you have been assigned this duty at Janasthana.
ramayan::7610.translation_literal: युष्माकं (of you all) / च (and) / बलज्ञः (knower of strength) / अहं (I) / बहुशः (many times) / रणमूर्धनि (at the forefront of battle) / अतः (therefore) / च (and) / अस्मिन् (in this) / जनस्थाने (at Janasthana) / मया (by me) / यूयं (you all) / नियोजिताः (assigned)
ramayan::7610.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7610.essence: Strength becomes real when someone relies on it.
ramayan::7610.simple_meaning: Ravana says he knows these demons' fighting strength, so he has assigned them to guard and act at Janasthana.
ramayan::7610.simple_insight: Capability should be matched with responsibility, not wasted.
ramayan::7610.detailed_meaning: Ravana is directing his demons after ordering Rama's destruction. He tells them he knows their strength from many battles, and that is why he has placed them at Janasthana. It is a tactical assignment, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::7610.modern_relevance: A team lead assigns the hardest client because they know you can handle pressure. The verse is about placement based on proven strength, not inspiration.
ramayan::7610.insight: It shifts attention from praise to deployment: skill is proven by where it is trusted.

ramayan::7611.verse_sanskrit: ततः प्रियं वाक्यमुपेत्य राक्षसा महार्थमष्टावभिवाद्य रावणम् । विहाय लङ्कां सहिताः प्रतस्थिरे यतो जनस्थानमलक्ष्यदर्शनाः । । 35429 । ।
ramayan::7611.verse_hindi: The eight demons were glad to hear the pleasing and meaningful words of Ravana. They offered him salutations and left Lanka in the direction of Janasthana without being seen by any one.
ramayan::7611.english_translation: Then the eight demons, pleased by Ravana's meaningful words, bowed to him and departed from Lanka toward Janasthana, moving unseen.
ramayan::7611.translation_literal: ततः (then) / प्रियम् (pleasing) / वाक्यम् (speech) / उपेत्य (having received) / राक्षसाः (demons) / महार्थम् (weighty, meaningful) / अष्टौ (eight) / अभिवाद्य (having saluted) / रावणम् (Ravana) / विहाय (leaving) / लङ्काम् (Lanka) / सहिताः (together) / प्रतस्थिरे (departed) / यतः (toward) / जनस्थानम् (Janasthana) / अलक्ष्यदर्शनाः (unseen in appearance)
ramayan::7611.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7611.essence: Secret orders turn into motion before anyone sees the harm coming.
ramayan::7611.simple_meaning: Ravana's eight followers accept his orders, bow to him, and leave Lanka secretly for Janasthana.
ramayan::7611.simple_insight: A command can send people into motion long before the real consequences appear.
ramayan::7611.detailed_meaning: After Ravana's instructions, eight rākṣasas bow and slip out of Lanka together. This is not the turning point itself, but the quiet movement that sets the next danger in motion: Sita's abduction is being prepared in secret.
ramayan::7611.modern_relevance: A message lands in a group chat, and people start moving before anyone outside the circle knows what is happening. Quiet coordination can change everything before the room catches up.
ramayan::7611.insight: It shows how hidden planning becomes action through obedience and secrecy.

ramayan::7612.verse_sanskrit: ततस्तु सीतामुपलभ्य रावणः सुसम्प्रहृष्टः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम् । प्रसज्य रामेण च वैरमुत्तमं बभूव मोहान्मुदितस्सराक्षसः । । 35430 । ।
ramayan::7612.verse_hindi: Then the demon Ravana felt greatly happy for getting Sita, princess of Mithila, without knowing in his delusion that he had created the bitterest enmity with Rama.
ramayan::7612.english_translation: Then Ravana felt greatly pleased after seizing Sita, the princess of Mithila, and in his delusion he thought he had secured victory. But he had only created the fiercest enmity with Rama.
ramayan::7612.translation_literal: ततः (then) / तु (indeed) / सीताम् (Sita) / उपलभ्य (having obtained) / रावणः (Ravana) / सुसम्प्रहृष्टः (greatly delighted) / परिगृह्य (having seized) / मैथिलीम् (the princess of Mithila) / प्रसज्य (having incurred) / रामेण (with Rama) / च (and) / वैरम् (enmity) / उत्तमम् (fiercest) / बभूव (became) / मोहात् (from delusion) / मुदितः (pleased) / सः (he) / राक्षसः (the demon)
ramayan::7612.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7612.essence: What looks like victory can be the start of your downfall.
ramayan::7612.simple_meaning: Ravana is overjoyed after abducting Sita, but his happiness is born from delusion. What feels like success is actually the start of ruin.
ramayan::7612.simple_insight: A triumph can be the moment you lose sight of reality.
ramayan::7612.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just carried Sita away and thinks he has won. But the victory is hollow: by taking her, he has crossed into direct conflict with Rama. Valmiki shows the instant where arrogance mistakes disaster for success.
ramayan::7612.modern_relevance: You finally get the thing you wanted, and the rush feels huge. But a few minutes later, you can already sense the damage it set in motion.
ramayan::7612.insight: It shifts the mind from celebrating acquisition to seeing the consequences hidden inside it.

ramayan::7613.verse_sanskrit: सन्दिश्य राक्षसान्घोरान् रावणोऽष्टौ महाबलान् । आत्मानं बुद्धिवैक्लब्यात्कृतकृत्यममन्यत । । 3551 । ।
ramayan::7613.verse_hindi: After ordering the eight most fierce  and powerful demons, Ravana had a sense of accomplishment within himself because of his perverse intellect.
ramayan::7613.english_translation: After ordering the eight fierce, mighty demons, Ravana foolishly thought his task was complete.
ramayan::7613.translation_literal: सन्दिश्य (having ordered) / राक्षसान् (the demons) / घोरान् (fierce) / रावणः (Ravana) / अष्टौ (eight) / महाबलान् (mighty) / आत्मानम् (himself) / बुद्धिवैक्लब्यात् (because of confusion of intellect) / कृतकृत्यम् (task-completed) / अमन्यत (considered)
ramayan::7613.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7613.essence: Confused pride made him mistake motion for victory.
ramayan::7613.simple_meaning: Ravana sent out eight powerful demons and then, blinded by his own confused thinking, believed he had finished what needed to be done.
ramayan::7613.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just given orders to eight fierce demons in the chain of events leading to Sita's capture. Instead of seeing the danger or the moral weight of what he is doing, he mistakes his own impulse for success and feels satisfied too early.
ramayan::7613.modern_relevance: You send the message, delegate the task, and feel oddly relieved before anything is actually done. The mind loves calling itself finished when it has only started.
ramayan::7613.insight: It warns you not to confuse decisive action with genuine completion.

ramayan::7614.verse_sanskrit: स चिन्तयानो वैदेहीं कामबाणसमर्पितः । प्रविवेश गृहं रम्यं सीतां द्रष्टुमभित्वरन् । । 3552 । ।
ramayan::7614.verse_hindi: Thinking about Vaidehi and hit by the arrows of Cupid (the god of love). Ravana hastened to see Sita and entered the beautiful home.
ramayan::7614.english_translation: Thinking of Vaidehi, pierced by the arrows of desire, Ravana hurried to see Sita and entered the beautiful house.
ramayan::7614.translation_literal: स (he) / चिन्तयानः (thinking) / वैदेहीम् (of Vaidehi) / कामबाणसमर्पितः (struck by the arrows of desire) / प्रविवेश (entered) / गृहं (the house) / रम्यम् (beautiful) / सीताम् (Sita) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अभित्वरन् (hastening)
ramayan::7614.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7614.essence: Desire drove him forward faster than wisdom could stop him.
ramayan::7614.simple_meaning: Ravana, overwhelmed by desire for Sita, quickly enters the beautiful house to see her.
ramayan::7614.simple_insight: Unchecked desire makes you hurry toward what will ruin you.
ramayan::7614.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already convinced himself that he has won. Now, burning with longing for Sita, he rushes into the inner house to see her. The next verse will show what he finds: Sita surrounded by demonesses, deep in grief.
ramayan::7614.modern_relevance: You replay someone's face in your head and call it urgency. Before you know it, desire has already started steering your feet.
ramayan::7614.insight: It shows how craving narrows attention and pushes action before judgment can catch up.

ramayan::7615.verse_sanskrit: स प्रविश्य तु तद्वेश्म रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । अपश्यद्राक्षसीमध्ये सीतां शोकपरायणाम् । । 3553 । ।
ramayan::7615.verse_hindi: Ravana, lord of the demons, entered his residence and saw Sita full of grief in the midst of the demonesses.
ramayan::7615.english_translation: Ravana, lord of the demons, entered his residence and saw Sita full of grief in the midst of the demonesses.
ramayan::7615.translation_literal: स (he) / प्रविश्य (having entered) / तु (indeed) / तद्वेश्म (that residence) / रावणः (Ravana) / राक्षसाधिपः (lord of the demons) / अपश्यत् (saw) / राक्षसीमध्ये (amid the demonesses) / सीताम् (Sita) / शोकपरायणाम् (given over to grief)
ramayan::7615.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7615.essence: Grief fills the room before Ravana makes his next move.
ramayan::7615.simple_meaning: Ravana goes into his palace and finds Sita surrounded by demonesses, overwhelmed by sorrow.
ramayan::7615.simple_insight: The scene is still, but the grief is already crushing everything around it.
ramayan::7615.detailed_meaning: Ravana returns to his own residence after moving toward Sita in desire and pride. Inside, he sees Sita trapped among the demonesses, not yielding, only grieving. The verse simply fixes the scene before his next act.
ramayan::7615.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting control, and instead you meet someone's grief. The moment exposes more than your plan ever could.
ramayan::7615.insight: It frames the next movement of the story by showing Sita's suffering before Ravana acts again.

ramayan::7616.verse_sanskrit: अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां शोकभाराभिपीडिताम् । वायुवेगैरिवाक्रान्तां मज्जन्तीं नावमर्णवे । । 3554 । । मृगयूथपरिभ्रष्टां मृगीं श्वभिरिवावृताम् । अधोमुखमुखीं सीतामभ्येत्य च निशाचरः । । 3555 । । तां तु शोकपरां दीनामवशां राक्षसाधिपः । स बलाद्दर्शयामास गृहं देवगृहोपमम् । । 3556 । ।
ramayan::7616.verse_hindi: The demon Ravana forcibly took Sita, her face full of tears, to show her his heavenlike home. Inflicted with grief she looked wretched. She resembled a female deer hounded out of the herd. With her head bent in grief, she looked pathetic like one not under her control, like a boat sinking under the sea driven by the wind.
ramayan::7616.english_translation: Ravana, lord of the demons, forcibly led Sita to show her his palace. Her face was full of tears, she was crushed by grief, and she looked like a deer driven from its herd, like a boat sinking in the sea. With her head bowed and her will broken, he displayed her the house that was like a divine mansion.
ramayan::7616.translation_literal: अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं (with a face full of tears) / दीनाम् (wretched) / शोकभाराभिपीडिताम् (crushed by the burden of grief) / वायुवेगैः (by wind-force) / इव (like) / आक्रान्ताम् (overtaken) / मज्जन्तीम् (sinking) / नावम् (boat) / अर्णवे (in the sea) / मृगयूथपरिभ्रष्टाम् (fallen away from the herd of deer) / मृगीम् (female deer) / श्वभिः (by dogs) / इव (like) / आवृताम् (surrounded) / अधोमुखमुखीम् (with face turned downward) / सीताम् (Sita) / अभ्येत्य (approaching) / च (and) / निशाचरः (the night-wanderer) / ताम् (her) / तु (indeed) / शोकपराम् (given to grief) / दीनाम् (wretched) / अवशाम् (helpless) / राक्षसाधिपः (lord of the demons) / सः (he) / बलात् (by force) / दर्शयामास (showed) / गृहम् (house) / देवगृह-उपमम् (resembling a divine mansion)
ramayan::7616.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7616.essence: Splendor becomes monstrous when it is used to humiliate the helpless.
ramayan::7616.simple_meaning: Ravana drags Sita through his grand palace, but her grief and helplessness make the scene tragic, not triumphant. The verse lingers on her suffering and his force.
ramayan::7616.simple_insight: Power can display wealth, but it cannot hide cruelty.
ramayan::7616.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just entered his own palace and found Sita among the women guarding her. Instead of dignity, the scene reveals her tears, bowed head, and helpless grief. Valmiki slows down here to show the moral ugliness of Ravana's force.
ramayan::7616.modern_relevance: Someone can call the room beautiful, fill it with lights, and still make it feel like a cage. The décor does not change the fear in the person being controlled.
ramayan::7616.insight: It shifts attention from Ravana's grandeur to the violence underneath it.

ramayan::7617.verse_sanskrit: हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधं स्त्रीसहस्रनिषेवितम् । नानापक्षिगणैर्जुष्टं नानारत्नसमन्वितम् । । 3557 । । दान्तकैस्तापनीयैश्च स्फाटिकै राजतैरपि । वज्रवैडूर्यचित्रैश्च स्तम्भैर्दृष्टिमनोहरैः । । 3558 । । दिव्यदुन्दुभिनिर्ह्रादं तप्तकाञ्चनतोरणम् ।
ramayan::7617.verse_hindi: His home was a complex of palaces and mansions served by thousands of women. It was an abode of different flocks of birds. It had captivating pillars studded with gold, crystals, silver, diamonds and vaiduryas. It resounded with wonderful sounds of drums. Its golden entrances were glittering.
ramayan::7617.english_translation: His home was a complex of palaces and mansions served by thousands of women. It was an abode of different flocks of birds. It had captivating pillars studded with gold, crystals, silver, diamonds and vaiduryas. It resounded with wonderful sounds of drums. Its golden entrances were glittering.
ramayan::7617.translation_literal: हर्म्य-प्रासाद-सम्बाधम् (crowded with palaces and mansions) / स्त्री-सहस्र-निषेवितम् (attended by thousands of women) / नाना-पक्षि-गणैः (by many flocks of birds) / जुष्टम् (adorned) / नाना-रत्न-समन्वितम् (endowed with many jewels) / दान्तकैः (with polished ivory) / तापनीयैः (with gold) / च (and) / स्फाटिकैः (with crystal) / राजतैः (with silver) / अपि (also) / वज्र-वैडूर्य-चित्रैः (variegated with diamonds and vaiduryas) / स्तम्भैः (with pillars) / दृष्टि-मनः-हरैः (delighting the eyes and mind) / दिव्य-दुन्दुभि-निर्ह्रादम् (resounding with divine drums) / तप्त-काञ्चन-तोरणम् (with golden gateways)
ramayan::7617.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7617.essence: Wealth can dazzle the eye while revealing nothing of character.
ramayan::7617.simple_meaning: Ravana's palace is described as lavish, crowded, and dazzling, filled with women, birds, jewels, drums, and golden gates.
ramayan::7617.simple_insight: Splendor can hide the emptiness of the person who built it.
ramayan::7617.detailed_meaning: Ravana brings Sita into his own palace and the poet pauses to paint its wealth: palaces, women, birds, jewels, drums, and gold everywhere. The scene is not teaching a lesson yet; it is showing the scale of the place where Sita has been taken.
ramayan::7617.modern_relevance: You walk into a house that looks perfect from the outside: polished floors, expensive lighting, everything arranged to impress. But the shine tells you nothing about the heart of the person inside.
ramayan::7617.insight: It shifts attention from surface luxury to the moral reality behind it.

ramayan::7618.verse_sanskrit: सोपानं काञ्चनं चित्रमारुरोह तया सह । । 3559 । । दान्तका राजताश्चैव गवाक्षाः प्रियदर्शनाः । हेमजालावताश्चासन्स्तत्र प्रासादपङ्क्तयः । । 35510 । ।
ramayan::7618.verse_hindi: He ascended the wonderful golden staircase taking Sita along with him.Beautiful looked the rows of mansions with silver and ivory windows and golden trellis.
ramayan::7618.english_translation: He ascended the wonderful golden staircase with Sita beside him. The rows of mansions looked beautiful, with silver and ivory windows and golden trellis.
ramayan::7618.translation_literal: सोपानं (staircase) / काञ्चनं (golden) / चित्रम् (wonderful) / आरुरोह (ascended) / तया सह (with her) / दान्तकाः (made of ivory) / राजताः (silver) / च एव (and indeed) / गवाक्षाः (windows) / प्रियदर्शनाः (pleasant to look at) / हेमजालावताः (covered with golden trellis) / च आसन् (were) / तत्र (there) / प्रासादपङ्क्तयः (rows of mansions)
ramayan::7618.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7618.essence: Luxury here is part of the violation, not a cover for it.
ramayan::7618.simple_meaning: Ravana leads Sita up a golden staircase into his palace. The place is lavish, with silver, ivory, and gold everywhere.
ramayan::7618.simple_insight: Splendour can hide cruelty. A beautiful place does not make a violent act less violent.
ramayan::7618.detailed_meaning: Ravana has brought Sita into Lanka and now parades her through his palace. The golden stairs and jeweled mansions are not a celebration; they are part of the display of power that surrounds her captivity.
ramayan::7618.modern_relevance: A polished office, a luxury car, or a grand house can still contain coercion, pressure, or humiliation. Beauty on the outside does not cancel harm inside.
ramayan::7618.insight: It separates appearance from moral reality, so you do not confuse luxury with goodness.

ramayan::7619.verse_sanskrit: सुधामणिविचित्राणि भूमिभागानि सर्वशः । दशग्रीवस्स्वभवने प्रादर्शयत मैथिलीम् । । 35511 । ।
ramayan::7619.verse_hindi: The tenheaded Ravana showed Sita, the princess from Mithila the floors with wonderful crystals.
ramayan::7619.english_translation: The ten-headed Ravana showed Sita the floors in his palace decorated with wonderful crystals.
ramayan::7619.translation_literal: सुधामणि-विचित्राणि (decorated with wonderful crystals) / भूमिभागानि (floors, ground-level spaces) / सर्वशः (everywhere, in all directions) / दशग्रीवः (the ten-headed one, Ravana) / स्वभवने (in his own palace) / प्रादर्शयत् (showed) / मैथिलीम् (to Sita of Mithila)
ramayan::7619.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7619.essence: Splendor becomes a weapon when the listener is captive.
ramayan::7619.simple_meaning: Ravana is showing Sita the glittering parts of his palace. The verse is about the tour itself, not a teaching.
ramayan::7619.simple_insight: Some displays are meant to impress, not to comfort.
ramayan::7619.detailed_meaning: Ravana has brought Sita into his palace and is parading its splendor before her. The crystal-studded floors are part of his attempt to dazzle a captive woman who has not chosen to be there.
ramayan::7619.modern_relevance: Someone gives you a polished tour of their success while you are standing there uneasy, already knowing the shine is meant to control the room.
ramayan::7619.insight: It shows how power can use beauty as pressure, not generosity.

ramayan::7620.verse_sanskrit: दीर्घिकाः पुष्करिण्यश्च नानावृक्षसमन्विताः । रावणो दर्शयामास सीतां शोकपरायणाम् । । 35512 । ।
ramayan::7620.verse_hindi: Ravana showed Sita who was overwhelmed with sorrow, stepwells surrrounded by various trees and tanks.
ramayan::7620.english_translation: Ravana showed Sita, overwhelmed with sorrow, the stepwells and tanks surrounded by many kinds of trees.
ramayan::7620.translation_literal: दीर्घिकाः (stepwells) / पुष्करिण्यः (tanks) / च (and) / नानावृक्षसमन्विताः (accompanied by various trees) / रावणः (Ravana) / दर्शयामास (showed) / सीताम् (Sita) / शोकपरायणाम् (overwhelmed with sorrow)
ramayan::7620.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7620.essence: Beauty on display cannot seduce a sorrowful heart.
ramayan::7620.simple_meaning: Ravana is trying to impress Sita by showing her the beauty of his palace grounds, but she remains sunk in sorrow.
ramayan::7620.simple_insight: Charm cannot reach a heart that has already turned away.
ramayan::7620.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps parading the splendor of his palace before Sita, hoping beauty will weaken her resistance. But Sita is already grief-stricken and unmoved. This verse is a small part of that larger attempt to entice her.
ramayan::7620.modern_relevance: Someone sends you photos of a perfect life after you have already seen through the performance. The display is polished, but it cannot touch the grief or clarity you are carrying.
ramayan::7620.insight: It shows how empty display fails when the other person is no longer persuadable.

ramayan::7621.verse_sanskrit: दर्शयित्वा तु वैदेह्याः कृत्स्नं तद्भवनोत्तमम् । उवाच वाक्यं पापात्मा सीतां लोभितुमिच्छया । । 35513 । ।
ramayan::7621.verse_hindi: The sinful Ravana showed Sita, princess of Videha, the best of all his mansions in order to allure her, saying:
ramayan::7621.english_translation: After showing Vaidehi the finest part of his palace, the sinful Ravana spoke words, wanting to tempt Sita.
ramayan::7621.translation_literal: दर्शयित्वा (having shown) / तु (indeed) / वैदेह्याः (of Vaidehi) / कृत्स्नं (entire) / तद्भवनोत्तमम् (that best palace) / उवाच (spoke) / वाक्यं (a speech) / पापात्मा (the sinful one) / सीतां (to Sita) / लोभितुम् (to allure) / इच्छया (with desire)
ramayan::7621.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7621.essence: Display comes first; the pressure follows.
ramayan::7621.simple_meaning: Ravana shows Sita the best parts of his palace and then begins speaking, hoping to tempt her.
ramayan::7621.simple_insight: Charm can be a weapon when desire is trying to disguise itself.
ramayan::7621.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already paraded Sita through his glittering palace. Now, after trying to impress her with luxury, he begins his speech. The verse marks the shift from display to manipulation.
ramayan::7621.modern_relevance: Someone gives you the grand tour, the polished smile, the carefully chosen details — and then starts asking for what they really want. You can feel the pressure change.
ramayan::7621.insight: It reveals how seduction often begins with spectacle before the real demand is spoken.

ramayan::7622.verse_sanskrit: दश राक्षसकोट्यश्च द्वाविंशतिरथापराः । तेषां प्रभुरहं सीते सर्वेषां भीमकर्मणाम् । । 35514 । । वर्जयित्वा जरावृद्धान्बालांश्च रजनीचरान् ।
ramayan::7622.verse_hindi: O Sita, leaving aside children and the aged, I am the lord of crores of nightrangers in addition to ten crore demons and twentytwo crore terrorists.
ramayan::7622.english_translation: O Sita, setting aside the children and the aged, I am the lord of ten crore demons and twenty-two crore more night-walkers.
ramayan::7622.translation_literal: दश (ten) / राक्षसकोट्यश्च (and crores of demons) / द्वाविंशतिः (twenty-two) / अपराः (more) / तेषाम् (of them) / प्रभुः (lord) / अहम् (I) / सीते (O Sita) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / भीमकर्मणाम् (of terrible deeds) / वर्जयित्वा (leaving aside) / जरावृद्धान् (the old) / बालान् (the young) / च (and) / रजनीचरान् (night-walkers)
ramayan::7622.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7622.essence: Raw numbers cannot create the respect Ravana wants.
ramayan::7622.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts to Sita about the vast number of demons under his command, excluding only the very young and the very old.
ramayan::7622.simple_insight: Pride often hides emptiness. Big numbers can be a mask for a small, desperate heart.
ramayan::7622.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps trying to overwhelm Sita with power, wealth, and scale. After showing her his palace, he now boasts of the immense forces he commands, hoping fear will break her resolve. The speech is part of his attempt to win her through intimidation.
ramayan::7622.modern_relevance: Someone floods your inbox with titles, numbers, and achievements to make you feel small. The pressure is real, but it is still just pressure.
ramayan::7622.insight: It exposes how intimidation works: by replacing moral force with sheer display of power.

ramayan::7623.verse_sanskrit: सहस्रमेकमेकस्य मम कार्यपुरस्सरम् । । 35515 । । यदिदं राजतन्त्रं मे त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । जीवितं च विशालाक्षि त्वं मे प्राणैर्गरीयसी । । 35516 । ।
ramayan::7623.verse_hindi: For me alone there are a thousand attendants.The  administration of the kingdom and all my subjects will be under your control. O largeeyed Sita you are dearer to me than my life.
ramayan::7623.english_translation: For me alone there are a thousand attendants. The administration of the kingdom and all my subjects will be under your control. O large-eyed Sita, you are dearer to me than my life.
ramayan::7623.translation_literal: सहस्रम् (a thousand) / एकम् (one) / एकस्य (of one) / मम (my) / कार्यपुरस्सरम् (with duties first) / यद् (which) / इदम् (this) / राजतन्त्रम् (kingdom-administration) / मे (my) / त्वयि (in you) / सर्वम् (all) / प्रतिष्ठितम् (placed) / जीवितम् (life) / च (and) / विशालाक्षि (O large-eyed one) / त्वम् (you) / मे (to me) / प्राणैः (than the life-breaths) / गरीयसी (greater)
ramayan::7623.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7623.essence: Power tries to disguise possession as love.
ramayan::7623.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to impress Sita with his power, wealth, and control, while claiming she matters to him more than his own life.
ramayan::7623.simple_insight: Charm can hide coercion. A flattering voice can still be a threatening one.
ramayan::7623.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already shown Sita his palace and boasted of his power. Now he tries another tactic: offering her the kingdom, servants, and status, while claiming personal devotion. It is not a sincere invitation but part of his pressure.
ramayan::7623.modern_relevance: Someone floods you with compliments, promises influence, and says you matter most — but the pressure underneath is unmistakable. Ravana's language is polished coercion.
ramayan::7623.insight: It teaches you to hear control hiding inside praise and grand promises.

ramayan::7624.verse_sanskrit: बहूनांस्त्रीसहस्राणां मम योऽसौ परिग्रहः । तासां त्वमीश्वरा सीते मम भार्या भव प्रिये । । 35517 । ।
ramayan::7624.verse_hindi: O Sita dear  be my chief queen among the many thousands of women I have married.
ramayan::7624.english_translation: O Sita dear, be my chief queen among the many thousands of women I have married.
ramayan::7624.translation_literal: बहूनाम् (of many) / स्त्रीसहस्राणाम् (thousands of women) / मम (my) / यः (who) / असौ (that) / परिग्रहः (household / possession) / तासाम् (among them) / त्वम् (you) / ईश्वरा (mistress / chief) / सीते (O Sita) / मम (my) / भार्या (wife) / भव (become) / प्रिये (dear one)
ramayan::7624.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7624.essence: Power tries to rename coercion as honour.
ramayan::7624.simple_meaning: Ravana asks Sita to become his chief wife, claiming authority over the many women in his household.
ramayan::7624.simple_insight: Desire can dress itself as invitation, but it is still possession.
ramayan::7624.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to bend Sita with status and persuasion after abduction. He boasts of his household and power, then offers her the place of chief queen. The verse is part of his coercive argument, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7624.modern_relevance: Someone who has already crossed your boundaries may still sound polite, generous, even flattering. The tone can be soft while the pressure underneath is hard.
ramayan::7624.insight: It exposes how control can hide inside praise and promises of privilege.

ramayan::7625.verse_sanskrit: साधु किं तेऽन्यया बुद्ध्या रोचयस्व वचो मम । भजस्वमाभितप्तस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि । । 35518 । ।
ramayan::7625.verse_hindi: Do not think otherwise. Be good and accept my request. I am consumed by thoughts of you. You should be gracious to me.
ramayan::7625.english_translation: Do not think otherwise. Be good and accept my request. I am consumed by thoughts of you. You should be gracious to me.
ramayan::7625.translation_literal: साधु (be good) / किं (why) / ते (for you) / अन्यया (other) / बुद्ध्या (with thought) / रोचयस्व (be pleased) / वचः (word) / मम (my) / भजस्व (accept) / माभितप्तस्य (of the one consumed) / प्रसादम् (grace) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you are fit)
ramayan::7625.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7625.essence: Polite words can still carry coercion.
ramayan::7625.simple_meaning: Ravana begs Sita to accept his words and show him favor. He tries to soften his desire with polite language, but the plea is still a demand.
ramayan::7625.simple_insight: Charm can hide pressure, but it cannot make pressure clean.
ramayan::7625.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Sita in Lanka after offering her power, status, and queenship. He tries to sound gentle and reasonable, but his desire is already tightening the scene. The next verse reminds us that this is a fortified city, not a place of easy escape.
ramayan::7625.modern_relevance: Someone keeps texting after you have not answered, calling it concern, calling it care. The words are polished, but the pressure is still there.
ramayan::7625.insight: It reveals how desire can dress itself as courtesy while still trying to override another person's will.

ramayan::7626.verse_sanskrit: परिक्षिप्ता समुद्रेण लङ्केयं शतयोजना । नेयं धर्षयितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः । । 35519 । ।
ramayan::7626.verse_hindi: This Lanka extending to a hundred yojanas and surrounded by the sea is vulnerable to neither demons nor gods including Indra.
ramayan::7626.english_translation: This Lanka, stretching a hundred yojanas and surrounded by the sea, cannot be taken even by Indra and the gods, much less by demons.
ramayan::7626.translation_literal: परिक्षिप्ता (surrounded) / समुद्रेण (by the sea) / लङ्का (Lanka) / इयम् (this) / शतयोजना (a hundred yojanas in extent) / नेयम् (this is not) / धर्षयितुम् (to be assaulted) / शक्या (able) / सेन्द्रैः (with Indra) / अपि (even) / सुरासुरैः (by gods and demons)
ramayan::7626.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7626.essence: He mistakes a fortress for proof that he cannot fall.
ramayan::7626.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that Lanka is so strongly protected by the sea that no one can attack it, not even the gods with Indra.
ramayan::7626.simple_insight: Pride can turn protection into blindness.
ramayan::7626.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to impress Sita with his power and the city’s invulnerability. He points to the sea, the scale of the fortress, and the strength of its defenses, using fear and status to pressure her into yielding.
ramayan::7626.modern_relevance: Someone lists all the reasons they are untouchable: money, status, security, connections. The louder the boast, the more it reveals the fear underneath.
ramayan::7626.insight: It exposes how power speaks when it wants obedience, not understanding.

ramayan::7627.verse_sanskrit: न देवेषु न यक्षेषु न गन्धर्वेषु पक्षिषु । अहं पश्यामि लोकेषु यो मे वीर्यसमो भवेत् । । 35520 । ।
ramayan::7627.verse_hindi: I do not see any one equal to me in valour among gods, or yakshas or gandharvas or birds.
ramayan::7627.english_translation: I do not see anyone equal to me in valour among gods, yakshas, gandharvas, or birds.
ramayan::7627.translation_literal: न (not) / देवेषु (among gods) / न (not) / यक्षेषु (among yakshas) / न (not) / गन्धर्वेषु (among gandharvas) / पक्षिषु (among birds) / अहं (I) / पश्यामि (see) / लोकेषु (among beings / in the worlds) / यः (who) / मे (my) / वीर्यसमः (equal in valour) / भवेत् (may be / is)
ramayan::7627.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7627.essence: He mistakes his strength for invincibility.
ramayan::7627.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that no being he knows can match his strength and courage.
ramayan::7627.simple_insight: Pride can make a mind stop seeing its own limits.
ramayan::7627.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is still pressing his case and measuring himself against every kind of being he can name. This line is not a teaching but a boast: he believes his strength makes him unmatched, and that confidence is part of the blindness leading to his fall.
ramayan::7627.modern_relevance: You keep listing your advantages in your head after everyone else has left the room. That private tally can become the very thing that blinds you.
ramayan::7627.insight: It shows how unchecked self-regard turns comparison into delusion.

ramayan::7628.verse_sanskrit: राज्यभ्रष्टेन दीनेन तापसेन गतायुषा । किं करिष्यसि रामेण मानुषेणाल्पतेजसा । । 35521 । ।
ramayan::7628.verse_hindi: Of what use is Rama who has lost his kingdom, who is depressed and leads an
ramayan::7628.english_translation: What can Rama, a man who has lost his kingdom, who is miserable, who lives like an ascetic, and whose life is nearly over, do?
ramayan::7628.translation_literal: राज्यभ्रष्टेन (by one deprived of the kingdom) / दीनेन (by the miserable) / तापसेन (by the ascetic) / गतायुषा (by one whose life has gone) / किम् (what) / करिष्यसि (will you do) / रामेण (with Rama) / मानुषेण (by the human) / अल्पतेजसा (of little splendour)
ramayan::7628.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7628.essence: Ravana tries to make weakness sound like final truth.
ramayan::7628.simple_meaning: Ravana mocks Rama as powerless: exiled, weakened, and too human to matter against him.
ramayan::7628.simple_insight: Pride makes a person mistake hardship for weakness.
ramayan::7628.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already boasted that no one equals his strength. Now he turns to Sita and dismisses Rama as a broken exile, trying to strip away her faith by reducing Rama to a weak, ordinary man.
ramayan::7628.modern_relevance: Someone dismisses your partner, your teacher, or your own values because they look small under pressure. Ravana's words sound strong, but they are only contempt speaking.
ramayan::7628.insight: It exposes how arrogance belittles what it cannot understand.

ramayan::7629.verse_sanskrit: भजस्व सीते मामेव भर्ताहं सदृशस्तव । यौवनं ह्यध्रुवं भीरु रमस्वेह मया सह । । 35522 । ।
ramayan::7629.verse_hindi: O Sita take refuge only in me. I am a befitting husband to you. O timid one youth is impermanent. Enjoy (your life) with me while it lasts.
ramayan::7629.english_translation: O Sita, take refuge only in me. I am a husband fit for you. Youth is uncertain, timid one; enjoy life with me while it lasts.
ramayan::7629.translation_literal: भजस्व (take refuge in) / सीते (O Sita) / माम् एव (only me) / भर्ता (husband) / अहम् (I) / सदृशः (fit, equal) / तव (for you) / यौवनम् (youth) / हि (indeed) / अध्रुवम् (unstable, impermanent) / भीरु (timid one) / रमस्व (enjoy yourself) / इह (here) / मया सह (with me together)
ramayan::7629.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7629.essence: Flattery becomes a weapon when it asks you to betray what you know.
ramayan::7629.simple_meaning: Ravana urges Sita to abandon Rama and accept him instead, claiming he is a better match and that youth will not last forever.
ramayan::7629.simple_insight: Charm can hide coercion; a flattering voice can still be a trap.
ramayan::7629.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has Sita captive and is trying to break her loyalty. After boasting of his own greatness, he turns to seduction: forget Rama, choose me, and enjoy life while youth remains. The verse is part of his pressure campaign, not a self-contained teaching.
ramayan::7629.modern_relevance: Someone keeps texting after a breakup, mixing compliments with pressure: “You deserve better, I’m right here.” The sweetness is the strategy; the real aim is to wear down your refusal.
ramayan::7629.insight: It reveals how desire can speak as persuasion, and why flattery must be tested, not trusted.

ramayan::7630.verse_sanskrit: दर्शने माकृथा बुद्धिं राघवस्य वरानने । कास्य शक्तिरिहागन्तुमपि सीते मनोरथैः । । 35523 । ।
ramayan::7630.verse_hindi: O lovely Sita, give up the thought of seeing Rama. Where does he possess the power to reach this place even on the mental plane ?
ramayan::7630.english_translation: O lovely Sita, give up the thought of seeing Rama. Where does he possess the power to reach this place even on the mental plane?
ramayan::7630.translation_literal: दर्शने (in seeing) / मा (do not) / कृथा (make) / बुद्धिम् (the thought) / राघवस्य (of Rama) / वरानने (O lovely-faced one) / का (what) / अस्य (his) / शक्तिः (power) / इह (here) / आगन्तुम् (to come) / अपि (even) / सीते (O Sita) / मनोरथैः (by thoughts)
ramayan::7630.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7630.essence: Despair speaks like certainty when it wants to break your faith.
ramayan::7630.simple_meaning: Ravana tries to crush Sita's hope by saying Rama cannot come to her, not even in imagination. It is a cruel attempt to break her trust.
ramayan::7630.simple_insight: Cruel voices often attack hope first, because hope keeps you free inside.
ramayan::7630.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressing Sita to abandon Rama and accept him instead. After mocking Rama's weakness and exile, he now tries to sever her last inner refuge: the belief that Rama can reach her. The verse is part of a manipulative argument, not a truth.
ramayan::7630.modern_relevance: A message arrives at midnight: 'He won't change. She won't come back. Stop hoping.' Ravana's words sound like certainty, but they are really pressure. The mind that gives up hope too quickly hands power to fear.
ramayan::7630.insight: It reveals how manipulation works by shrinking your imagination before it can reach rescue.

ramayan::7631.verse_sanskrit: न शक्यो वायुराकाशे पाशैर्बद्धुं महाजवः । दीप्यमानस्य वाप्यग्नेर्गृहीतुं विमलां शिखाम् । । 35524 । ।
ramayan::7631.verse_hindi: It is not possible to bind  the wind blowing at high speed in the sky. Similarly it is not possible to catch the brilliant glow of flaming fire.
ramayan::7631.english_translation: It is not possible to bind the wind moving at great speed in the sky, nor to catch the bright flame of a blazing fire.
ramayan::7631.translation_literal: न शक्यो (not possible) / वायुः (the wind) / आकाशे (in the sky) / पाशैः (with ropes) / बद्धुम् (to bind) / महाजवः (great-speeded) / दीप्यमानस्य (of the blazing) / वा अपि (or also) / अग्नेः (of fire) / गृहीतुम् (to grasp) / विमलाम् (pure, bright) / शिखाम् (flame-tip)
ramayan::7631.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7631.essence: Force cannot hold what is naturally ungraspable.
ramayan::7631.simple_meaning: Ravana says Sita cannot be held back any more than wind can be tied up or fire's flame caught.
ramayan::7631.simple_insight: Some things cannot be controlled by force, no matter how much you want them.
ramayan::7631.detailed_meaning: Ravana is trying to break Sita's resolve in Lanka by flattering and threatening her. He compares her to wind and fire: impossible to restrain, impossible to seize. The speech is part of his attempt to make her abandon hope of Rama.
ramayan::7631.modern_relevance: Someone keeps trying to force a decision at the edge of a breakup, as if pressure could create consent. This verse reminds you that force cannot hold what is already moving free.
ramayan::7631.insight: It shifts the mind from possession to restraint: some realities cannot be held by force.

ramayan::7632.verse_sanskrit: त्रयाणामपि लोकानां न तं पश्यामि शोभने । विक्रमेण नयेद्यस्त्वां मद्बाहुपरिपालिताम् । । 35525 । ।
ramayan::7632.verse_hindi: O lovely lady, I do not see any one in these three worlds who can, by his valour, take you away from me guarded by my arms.
ramayan::7632.english_translation: O lovely lady, I do not see anyone in these three worlds who can, by his valour, take you away from me, guarded by my arms.
ramayan::7632.translation_literal: त्रयाणाम् (of the three) / अपि (even) / लोकानाम् (worlds) / न (not) / तम् (that one) / पश्यामि (I see) / शोभने (O lovely one) / विक्रमेण (by valour) / नयेत् (could take away) / यः (who) / त्वाम् (you) / मद्बाहुपरिपालिताम् (protected by my arms)
ramayan::7632.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7632.essence: Power feels absolute until it meets a stronger will.
ramayan::7632.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that no one in the three worlds is strong enough to take Sita away from him while he protects her.
ramayan::7632.simple_insight: Pride can sound like certainty right before it collapses.
ramayan::7632.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to overpower Sita with confidence instead of force. After dismissing Rama's reach, he declares that no warrior in the three worlds can remove her from his protection. The speech shows his arrogance hardening into a threat.
ramayan::7632.modern_relevance: Someone talks big in a meeting, certain their position makes them untouchable. The bravado feels solid until reality answers back.
ramayan::7632.insight: It exposes how domination speaks in the language of inevitability.

ramayan::7633.verse_sanskrit: लङ्कायां सुमहद्राज्यमिदं त्वमनुपालय । त्वत्प्रेष्या मद्विधाश्चैव देवाश्चापि चराचराः । । 35526 । ।
ramayan::7633.verse_hindi: Rule this vast kingdom of Lanka. People like me, even gods and all beings, mobile and immobile, will be at your beck and call.
ramayan::7633.english_translation: Rule this vast kingdom of Lanka. People like me, even gods and all beings, mobile and immobile, will be at your beck and call.
ramayan::7633.translation_literal: लङ्कायाम् (in Lanka) / सुमहत् (very great) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / इदम् (this) / त्वम् (you) / अनुपालय (rule, govern) / त्वत्प्रेष्याः (those sent by you, at your command) / मद्विधाः (people like me) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / देवाः (the radiant beings) / च (and) / अपि (also) / चराचराः (the moving and the unmoving beings)
ramayan::7633.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7633.essence: Power offered as devotion is still possession.
ramayan::7633.simple_meaning: Ravana offers Sita the rule of Lanka and claims that everyone, from beings like him to all other beings, will serve her.
ramayan::7633.simple_insight: Pride can disguise itself as generosity, but control is still control.
ramayan::7633.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to win Sita with power, not tenderness. After boasting that no one can take her away, he offers her his kingdom as if surrendering it, while actually tightening his claim. The verse is part of his coercive persuasion.
ramayan::7633.modern_relevance: Someone says, “Take the lead, I’ll support you,” but every decision still has to pass through them. The offer sounds generous until you notice the control underneath.
ramayan::7633.insight: It exposes false generosity: a gift that keeps the other person trapped.

ramayan::7634.verse_sanskrit: अभिषेकोदकक्लिन्ना तुष्टा च रमयस्व माम् । दुष्कृतं यत्परा कर्म वनवासेन तद्गतम् । । 35527 । । यश्च ते सुकृतो धर्मस्तस्येह फलमाप्नुहि ।
ramayan::7634.verse_hindi: Drenched with the waters of consecration, entertain me. The effect of the bad deeds done in the past are over with your dwelling in the forest. Now enjoy the fruits  of your
ramayan::7634.english_translation: Drenched by the waters of consecration, delight me. The harm done before has ended through your life in the forest. Now enjoy here the fruit of your good conduct.
ramayan::7634.translation_literal: अभिषेक-उदक-क्लिन्ना (drenched with consecration-water) / तुष्टा (satisfied, delighted) / च (and) / रमयस्व (delight, entertain) / माम् (me) / दुष्कृतम् (bad deed, wrongdoing) / यत् (which) / परा (gone beyond, ended) / कर्म (action, deed) / वन-वासेन (by forest-exile) / तत् (that) / गतम् (gone) / यः (which) / च (and) / ते (your) / सुकृतः (good, meritorious) / धर्मः (conduct, duty) / तस्य (of that) / इह (here) / फलम् (fruit, result) / आप्नुहि (obtain, enjoy)
ramayan::7634.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7634.essence: He turns captivity into a gift and calls it her reward.
ramayan::7634.simple_meaning: Ravana urges Sita to stay with him, claiming her exile has finished the old wrong and that she should now enjoy the reward of her virtue.
ramayan::7634.simple_insight: A corrupt mind can dress possession up as reward.
ramayan::7634.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressuring Sita after boasting that no one can take her away. He twists her suffering into permission, trying to make captivity sound like comfort and virtue sound like consent.
ramayan::7634.modern_relevance: Someone who has cornered you may call it care, relief, or even a fresh start. The pressure feels softer when it is dressed as your own good.
ramayan::7634.insight: It exposes how manipulation borrows the language of comfort to erase consent.

ramayan::7635.verse_sanskrit: इह माल्यानि सर्वाणि दिव्यगन्धानि मैथिलि । । 35528 । । भूषणानि च मुख्यानि सेवस्व च मया सह । ।
ramayan::7635.verse_hindi: O princess from Mithila, put on all garlands of wonderful fragrance and finest of jewels here with me.
ramayan::7635.english_translation: O princess from Mithila, put on all garlands of wonderful fragrance and finest jewels here with me.
ramayan::7635.translation_literal: इह (here) / माल्यानि (garlands) / सर्वाणि (all) / दिव्यगन्धानि (of divine fragrance) / मैथिलि (O Maithili) / भूषणानि (ornaments) / च (and) / मुख्यानि (chief / finest) / सेवस्व (enjoy / wear) / च (and) / मया (with me) / सह (together)
ramayan::7635.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7635.essence: Luxury cannot turn coercion into welcome.
ramayan::7635.simple_meaning: Ravana invites Sita to enjoy fragrant garlands and fine ornaments with him in Lanka.
ramayan::7635.simple_insight: Seduction often tries to dress possession up as care.
ramayan::7635.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressing Sita to accept his luxury and company. He speaks as if comfort can replace consent, trying to turn captivity into intimacy. This verse is part of that coercive display, not a teaching in itself.
ramayan::7635.modern_relevance: Someone keeps offering you gifts, attention, or status while ignoring your refusal. The polish is real, but so is the pressure underneath it.
ramayan::7635.insight: It exposes how charm can be used to blur boundaries and disguise control.

ramayan::7636.verse_sanskrit: पुष्पकं नाम सुश्रोणि भ्रातुर्वैश्रवणस्य मे । । 35529 । । विमानं सूर्यसङ्काशं तरसा निर्जितं मया ।
ramayan::7636.verse_hindi: O finehipped lady, I won by my strength from my brother Vaisravana (Kubera) an aerial chariot called Pushpaka shining with the radiance of the Sun.
ramayan::7636.english_translation: O fine-hipped lady, I won by my strength from my brother Vaisravana an aerial chariot called Pushpaka, shining with the radiance of the Sun.
ramayan::7636.translation_literal: पुष्पकं (Pushpaka) / नाम (called) / सुश्रोणि (O fine-hipped one) / भ्रातुः (from the brother) / वैश्रवणस्य (of Vaisravana) / मे (my) / विमानं (aerial chariot) / सूर्यसङ्काशं (sun-like) / तरसा (by strength) / निर्जितं (won) / मया (by me)
ramayan::7636.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7636.essence: Power tries to seduce by turning conquest into luxury.
ramayan::7636.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts to Sita that he won the shining Pushpaka aerial chariot from Kubera through his own strength.
ramayan::7636.simple_insight: Pride often turns even a gift into a trophy of conquest.
ramayan::7636.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to impress Sita with his wealth and power. He points to the Pushpaka chariot, claiming he seized it from Kubera, his half-brother. The verse is part of his attempt to lure her into submission.
ramayan::7636.modern_relevance: Someone keeps listing what they own, what they beat, and what they took. The need to sound powerful often reveals the deepest insecurity.
ramayan::7636.insight: It exposes how boasting can be a mask for craving control and admiration.

ramayan::7637.verse_sanskrit: विशालं रमणीयं च तद्विमानमनुत्तम् । । 35530 । । तत्र सीते मया सार्धं विहरस्व यथासुखम् ।
ramayan::7637.verse_hindi: O Sita that excellent chariot is big and beautiful. Where on you can roam happily along with me.
ramayan::7637.english_translation: O Sita, that excellent aerial chariot is vast and beautiful. There, you can roam happily with me.
ramayan::7637.translation_literal: विशालं (vast) / रमणीयं (beautiful) / च (and) / तत्-विमानम् (that aerial chariot) / अनुत्तम् (excellent) / तत्र (there) / सीते (O Sita) / मया (with me) / सार्धं (together) / विहरस्व (roam) / यथासुखम् (as you wish / happily)
ramayan::7637.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7637.essence: Luxury cannot soften a forced invitation.
ramayan::7637.simple_meaning: Ravana points to the Pushpaka chariot and invites Sita to travel with him in comfort and ease.
ramayan::7637.simple_insight: The invitation sounds generous, but it is still the language of possession.
ramayan::7637.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to tempt Sita with the splendour of the Pushpaka aerial chariot he seized from Kubera. He describes its beauty and invites her to move about with him, but the offer is part of his pressure, not real care.
ramayan::7637.modern_relevance: Someone shows you a polished offer after crossing a boundary you never agreed to. The shine can be real and still hide control.
ramayan::7637.insight: It trains you to notice when comfort is being used to disguise coercion.

ramayan::7638.verse_sanskrit: वदनं पद्मसङ्काशममलं चारुदर्शनम् । शोकार्तंतु वरारोहे न भ्राजति वरानने । । 35531 । ।
ramayan::7638.verse_hindi: O heavyhipped lady your face which is a clean lotus pleasing to the eye has lost its shine, stricken with grief.
ramayan::7638.english_translation: O heavy-hipped lady, your face, clean as a lotus and pleasing to look at, no longer shines, stricken with grief.
ramayan::7638.translation_literal: वदनं (face) / पद्मसङ्काशम् (lotus-like) / अमलम् (spotless) / चारुदर्शनम् (beautiful to look at) / शोकार्तम् (stricken with grief) / तु (but) / वरारोहे (O fine-hipped one) / न (not) / भ्राजति (shines) / वरानने (O beautiful-faced one)
ramayan::7638.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7638.essence: Grief has dimmed the beauty Ravana cannot stop noticing.
ramayan::7638.simple_meaning: Ravana says Sita's beautiful face has lost its radiance because grief has overtaken her.
ramayan::7638.simple_insight: Sorrow can dim even the brightest presence.
ramayan::7638.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps trying to tempt Sita with comfort and luxury. He points to her face and notices what grief has done to it. This is part of his pressure, not a teaching, and it flows into her silent refusal.
ramayan::7638.modern_relevance: Someone keeps talking at you while you sit there exhausted, trying not to show how much the conversation is costing you. Grief changes the face before it changes the words.
ramayan::7638.insight: It shows how suffering can be visible even when you stay silent.

ramayan::7639.verse_sanskrit: एवं वदति तस्मित्सा वस्त्रान्तेन वराङ्गना । पिधायेन्दुनिभं सीता मुखमश्रूण्यवर्तयत् । । 35532 । ।
ramayan::7639.verse_hindi: As Ravana went on speaking thus, Sita covered her beautiful, moonlike face with the edge of her garment and stood shedding tears.
ramayan::7639.english_translation: As Ravana went on speaking thus, Sita covered her beautiful, moonlike face with the edge of her garment and stood shedding tears.
ramayan::7639.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / वदति (speaking) / तस्मिन् (in that) / सा (she) / वस्त्र-अन्तेन (with the edge of her garment) / वर-अङ्गना (beautiful woman) / पिधाय (covering) / इन्दु-निभम् (moon-like) / सीता (Sita) / मुखम् (face) / अश्रूणि (tears) / अवर्तयत् (let flow / shed)
ramayan::7639.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7639.essence: Her silence is not weakness; it is a refusal to yield.
ramayan::7639.simple_meaning: Sita turns away from Ravana's words, hides her face, and cries.
ramayan::7639.simple_insight: Pain can be silent and still fully present.
ramayan::7639.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps speaking to Sita, pressing his case. She does not answer with anger or argument. Instead, she covers her face and lets tears fall, showing both grief and refusal.
ramayan::7639.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing you to respond in a conversation you never wanted. You lower your gaze, hold yourself together, and let the tears come later.
ramayan::7639.insight: It shows grief without surrendering dignity or giving the speaker the reaction he wants.

ramayan::7640.verse_sanskrit: ध्यायन्तीं तामिवास्वस्थां दीनां चिन्ताहतप्रभाम् । उवाच वचनं पापो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः । । 35533 । ।
ramayan::7640.verse_hindi: While Sita was lost in thought, feeling ill at lase, looking wretched with her beauty dulled by her anxiety, the sinful lord of the demons continued :
ramayan::7640.english_translation: While Sita was lost in thought, feeling ill at ease and worn down, her radiance dimmed by grief, Ravana, lord of the demons, spoke.
ramayan::7640.translation_literal: ध्यायन्तीम् (while thinking deeply) / ताम् (her) / इव (as if) / अस्वस्थाम् (unwell) / दीनाम् (wretched) / चिन्ताहतप्रभाम् (her radiance struck down by anxiety) / उवाच (spoke) / वचनम् (words) / पापः (sinful) / रावणः (Ravana) / राक्षसेश्वरः (lord of the demons)
ramayan::7640.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7640.essence: Sita’s grief is visible, and Ravana presses on anyway.
ramayan::7640.simple_meaning: Sita is overwhelmed with grief and anxiety, and Ravana begins speaking to her.
ramayan::7640.simple_insight: Grief can drain even visible strength, but it does not erase inner dignity.
ramayan::7640.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has turned away in sorrow, her face covered and her brightness dimmed by fear and grief. Ravana, standing before her as the ruler of the demons, begins another attempt to pressure her. The verse sets up the moral clash that follows.
ramayan::7640.modern_relevance: You sit in a room after bad news, barely answering texts, while someone keeps pushing for a response you do not owe them.
ramayan::7640.insight: It shifts attention from the speaker’s pressure to the victim’s exhausted state before the next move.

ramayan::7641.verse_sanskrit: अलं व्रीडेन वैदेहि धर्मलोपकृतेन च । । 35534 । । आर्षोऽयं दैवनिष्यन्दो यस्त्वामभिगमिष्यति ।
ramayan::7641.verse_hindi: O Sita you need not feel shamed that it is a violation of righteous conduct. Take it as godsend which has the approval of sages.
ramayan::7641.english_translation: O Sita, do not be ashamed that this violates righteous conduct. Treat it as a fate sent by the divine and approved by the sages.
ramayan::7641.translation_literal: अलम् (enough) / व्रीडेन (with shame) / वैदेहि (O daughter of Videha) / धर्मलोपकृतेन (caused by a breach of righteous conduct) / च (and) / आर्षः (sages' / approved by sages) / अयम् (this) / दैवनिष्यन्दः (downpour of the divine / divine result) / यः (which) / त्वाम् (you) / अभिगमिष्यति (will approach)
ramayan::7641.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7641.essence: Wrongdoing stays wrong even when dressed as approval.
ramayan::7641.simple_meaning: Ravana tells Sita not to feel ashamed about what he is forcing on her, trying to reframe his wrongdoing as something sanctioned by higher powers.
ramayan::7641.simple_insight: A corrupt mind can dress harm in holy language and still remain corrupt.
ramayan::7641.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressing Sita with words after she has already turned away in distress. Instead of hearing her refusal, he tries to rename his violation as something approved by sages and the divine, showing how desire can twist language itself.
ramayan::7641.modern_relevance: Someone crosses your boundary and then calls it “meant to be,” “for your own good,” or “just how things worked out.” The wound is not only the act — it is the lie wrapped around it.
ramayan::7641.insight: It teaches you to see through moral camouflage and name wrongdoing plainly.

ramayan::7642.verse_sanskrit: एतौ पादौ मया स्निग्धौ शिरोभिः परिपीडितौ । । 35535 । । प्रसादं कुरु मे क्षिप्रं वश्यो दासोऽहमस्मिते ।
ramayan::7642.verse_hindi: I am bowing down, pressing my heads at your shining feet. I am at your mercy. Grant me your favourI will remain your slave and remain ever under your control.
ramayan::7642.english_translation: I bow my heads, pressing them to your shining feet. Grant me your favour at once; I am your obedient slave.
ramayan::7642.translation_literal: एतौ (these) / पादौ (feet) / मया (by me) / स्निग्धौ (lovingly) / शिरोभिः (with heads) / परिपीडितौ (pressed down) / प्रसादम् (favour, grace) / कुरु (do) / मे (for me) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / वश्यः (submissive, under control) / दासः (slave, servant) / अहम् (I) / अस्मि (am)
ramayan::7642.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7642.essence: Pride can collapse into surrender when desire finally overpowers it.
ramayan::7642.simple_meaning: Ravana kneels before Sita, touches his head to her feet, and begs for her favour. He claims complete submission and says he will remain under her control.
ramayan::7642.simple_insight: Even pride can collapse into humility when desire becomes unbearable.
ramayan::7642.detailed_meaning: Ravana has crossed from threat to pleading. After trying to shame Sita, he now bows before her and asks for mercy, calling himself her servant. The scene turns his arrogance inside out, but only because he wants something he cannot force.
ramayan::7642.modern_relevance: You rehearse a proud speech, then hear your own voice break when the person across from you will not yield. The need to be seen differently can strip away every mask.
ramayan::7642.insight: It shows how unchecked desire can unravel pride and force a humiliating admission of dependence.

ramayan::7643.verse_sanskrit: इमाश्शून्य मया वाचश्शुष्यमाणेन भाषिताः । । 35536 । । न चापि रावणः काञ्चिन्मूर्ध्ना स्त्रीं प्रणमेत ह ।
ramayan::7643.verse_hindi: My throat has dried up. I have spoken these words in a forlorn state. Ravana has never bowed down to a woman in obeisance.
ramayan::7643.english_translation: My throat has dried up. I have spoken these words in a forlorn state. Ravana has never bowed down to a woman in obeisance.
ramayan::7643.translation_literal: इमाः (these) / शून्य (empty, futile) / मया (by me) / वाचः (words) / शुष्यमाणेन (by one whose throat is drying) / भाषिताः (spoken) / न (not) / च (and) / अपि (even) / रावणः (Ravana) / काञ्चित् (to any) / मूर्ध्ना (with the head) / स्त्रीम् (woman) / प्रणमेत (would bow) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7643.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7643.essence: Pride speaks loudest when it is already losing control.
ramayan::7643.simple_meaning: Ravana says his words have come out in a dry, desperate state. He insists that he has never bowed his head to any woman.
ramayan::7643.simple_insight: Pride can sound like certainty even when it is already cracking.
ramayan::7643.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands before Sita in Lanka, trying to force her submission. His earlier words have not moved her. Now his own strain shows: he admits the dryness of his voice, yet clings to his pride, reminding himself that he has never bowed to any woman.
ramayan::7643.modern_relevance: You keep talking when the room is already against you, trying to sound unshaken. Sometimes the loudest pride is just panic in a royal costume.
ramayan::7643.insight: It reveals a mind defending ego even as its control slips, showing how pride hardens under rejection.

ramayan::7644.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम् । । 35537 । । कृतान्तवशमापन्नो ममेयमिति मन्यते ।
ramayan::7644.verse_hindi: Having said this to the daughter of Janaka, the tenheaded Ravana who had fallen under the control of Yama, lord of death, misconceived that she had become his own.
ramayan::7644.english_translation: Having said this to the daughter of Janaka, the ten-headed Ravana, fallen under death's control, wrongly thought that she had become his own.
ramayan::7644.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / दशग्रीवः (the ten-headed one, Ravana) / मैथिलीं (to the daughter of Mithila) / जनकात्मजाम् (daughter of Janaka) / कृतान्तवशम् (under the control of death) / आपन्नः (fallen) / मम (mine) / इयम् (this one) / इति (thus) / मन्यते (thinks)
ramayan::7644.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7644.essence: He mistakes desire for ownership, even as death is already near.
ramayan::7644.simple_meaning: Ravana speaks to Sita and, blinded by desire and fate, mistakes her for someone he can possess.
ramayan::7644.simple_insight: Desire can make possession feel real even when it is only delusion.
ramayan::7644.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just spoken to Sita after trying to bend her will. Valmiki shows the tragedy plainly: even as death closes in on him, Ravana still mistakes refusal for possession. The moment exposes his blindness more than his power.
ramayan::7644.modern_relevance: Someone hears a polite no and keeps acting as if the answer was yes. The mind can turn rejection into possession when it wants something badly enough.
ramayan::7644.insight: It reveals how craving distorts reality and turns another person into an object.

ramayan::7645.verse_sanskrit: सा तथोक्ता तु वैदेही निर्भया शोककर्शिता । तृणमन्तरतः कृत्वा रावणं प्रत्यभाषत । । 3561 । ।
ramayan::7645.verse_hindi: Thus addressed by Ravana, Sita, immersed in deep sorrow and unafraid of him, placed  a blade of grass between her and him (intending not to speak to him  straight) and replied:
ramayan::7645.english_translation: Thus addressed by Ravana, Sita, immersed in deep sorrow and unafraid of him, placed a blade of grass between herself and him and replied.
ramayan::7645.translation_literal: सा (she) / तथा (thus) / उक्ता (spoken to) / तु (indeed) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / निर्भया (fearless) / शोककर्शिता (worn down by grief) / तृणम् (grass) / अन्तरतः (between) / कृत्वा (having made) / रावणम् (Ravana) / प्रत्यभाषत (spoke back)
ramayan::7645.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7645.essence: Grief need not become surrender; dignity can remain intact.
ramayan::7645.simple_meaning: Sita answers Ravana without fear, even though grief weighs on her. She keeps a blade of grass between them, showing complete refusal of intimacy or submission.
ramayan::7645.simple_insight: Pain does not have to make you small. You can stay dignified even when you are hurting.
ramayan::7645.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana tries to force Sita into submission. Instead of collapsing, she answers from within her sorrow with steady courage. The blade of grass marks her refusal to treat him as equal or acceptable, even in captivity.
ramayan::7645.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, trying to make you flinch, agree, or soften your no. Your voice shakes, but your boundary does not. Sita shows how dignity can survive pressure.
ramayan::7645.insight: It teaches you to protect your boundaries without needing anger or collapse.

ramayan::7646.verse_sanskrit: राजा दशरथो नाम धर्मसेतुरिवाचलः । सत्यसन्धः परिज्ञातो यस्य पुत्रस्सराघवः । । 3562 । ।
ramayan::7646.verse_hindi: Rama is a son of  the renowned king Dasaratha, who was a firm ambankment (protector) of righteousness and was true to his promise.
ramayan::7646.english_translation: Rama is the son of the renowned king Dasaratha, who was a firm embankment of righteousness and true to his promise.
ramayan::7646.translation_literal: राजा (king) / दशरथो (Dasaratha) / नाम (by name) / धर्मसेतुः इव (like a bridge of righteousness) / अचलः (unmoving, firm) / सत्यसन्धः (true to his promise) / परिज्ञातः (well known, renowned) / यस्य (whose) / पुत्रः (son) / सः राघवः (that Rama)
ramayan::7646.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7646.essence: Rama’s greatness is rooted in a father who kept righteousness firm.
ramayan::7646.simple_meaning: Dasaratha is described as a king who stood firm in righteousness and never broke his word. Rama is named as his son.
ramayan::7646.simple_insight: A child can inherit a father's moral stature as much as his name.
ramayan::7646.detailed_meaning: Sita, speaking to Ravana in Lanka, answers with calm dignity. Instead of yielding, she names Rama through his father: Dasaratha, known for righteousness and truthfulness. The line strengthens Rama’s moral standing before the next declaration.
ramayan::7646.modern_relevance: Someone asks who you belong to, and you answer with the kind of home that shaped you. Your name carries the weight of the promises kept before you.
ramayan::7646.insight: It shifts attention from rank or power to the moral ground a person comes from.

ramayan::7647.verse_sanskrit: रामो नाम स धर्मात्मा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः । दीर्घबाहुर्विशालाक्षो दैवतं हि पतिर्मम । । 3563 । ।
ramayan::7647.verse_hindi: The longarmed, largeeyed Rama is famous in all the three worlds. He is my husband, a righteous soul and a god to all.
ramayan::7647.english_translation: Rama is famous in all three worlds. He is my husband, righteous, long-armed, and large-eyed.
ramayan::7647.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / नाम (by name) / सः (he) / धर्मात्मा (righteous in nature) / त्रिषु (in three) / लोकेषु (worlds) / विश्रुतः (widely known) / दीर्घबाहुः (long-armed) / विशालाक्षः (large-eyed) / दैवतं (a radiant being) / हि (indeed) / पतिः (husband) / मम (my)
ramayan::7647.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7647.essence: Her loyalty rests on seeing Rama's character, not on her circumstances.
ramayan::7647.simple_meaning: Sita identifies Rama as her husband and praises his righteousness and fame across all worlds.
ramayan::7647.simple_insight: Love can be steady without being blind; it recognises character, not just closeness.
ramayan::7647.detailed_meaning: Sita, speaking to Ravana from captivity, answers not with fear but with certainty. She names Rama as her husband and as a man known for righteousness, reminding Ravana that her bond is rooted in truth, not weakness.
ramayan::7647.modern_relevance: When someone tries to define your life by the room you're trapped in, you can still remember who stands for you. Sita does not let captivity rewrite her loyalty.
ramayan::7647.insight: It shifts attention from immediate pressure to the deeper truth of relationship and character.

ramayan::7648.verse_sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातस्सिंहस्कन्धो महाद्युतिः । लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा यस्ते प्राणान्हरिष्यति । । 3564 । ।
ramayan::7648.verse_hindi: The brilliant Rama of the Ikshvaku dynasty with the lions shoulders will come with his brother Lakshmana and take away your life.
ramayan::7648.english_translation: Born in the Ikshvaku line, with lion-like shoulders and great radiance, Rama will come with his brother Lakshmana and take your life.
ramayan::7648.translation_literal: इक्ष्वाकूणां (of the Ikshvakus) / कुले (in the line) / जातः (born) / सिंहस्कन्धः (lion-shouldered) / महाद्युतिः (great-radiance) / लक्ष्मणेन (with Lakshmana) / सह (together) / भ्रात्रा (with [his] brother) / यः (who) / ते (your) / प्राणान् (life-breaths) / हरिष्यति (will take away)
ramayan::7648.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7648.essence: Rama’s arrival is not a hope here — it is a threat to wrongdoing.
ramayan::7648.simple_meaning: Sita warns Ravana that Rama, born in the Ikshvaku line and accompanied by Lakshmana, will kill him.
ramayan::7648.simple_insight: A stolen woman is not powerless when the truth of justice stands behind her.
ramayan::7648.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana without fear. She names Rama’s lineage, strength, and the presence of Lakshmana, then warns that the brothers will destroy him. It is a fierce refusal, not a philosophical teaching.
ramayan::7648.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a group chat and expects you to stay quiet. Instead, you speak with calm certainty because you know the people standing with you, and you know what is right.
ramayan::7648.insight: It shows how dignity can become resistance when fear no longer controls your voice.

ramayan::7649.verse_sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं यद्यहं तस्य त्वया स्यां धर्षिता बलात् । शयिता त्वं हतस्संख्ये जनस्थाने यथा खरः । । 3565 । ।
ramayan::7649.verse_hindi: Had you abducted me forcibly in his presence, you would have been lying down dead just as Khara in Janasthana.
ramayan::7649.english_translation: Had you abducted me forcibly in his presence, you would have been lying down dead just as Khara in Janasthana.
ramayan::7649.translation_literal: प्रत्यक्षं (in the presence) / यदि (if) / अहं (I) / तस्य (of him) / त्वया (by you) / स्याम् (were) / धर्षिता (violated/abducted) / बलात् (by force) / शयिता (lying down) / त्वं (you) / हतः (killed) / संख्ये (in battle) / जनस्थाने (in Janasthana) / यथा (like) / खरः (Khara)
ramayan::7649.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7649.essence: Ravana's force would have ended in death before Rama.
ramayan::7649.simple_meaning: Sita says Ravana would have been killed if he had tried to seize her in Rama's presence, just as Khara was killed in Janasthana.
ramayan::7649.simple_insight: Her courage is steady because she trusts Rama's strength completely.
ramayan::7649.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana without fear. She reminds him that Rama is no helpless husband: even Khara, a fearsome foe, fell before him. Her words strip away Ravana's arrogance and measure Rama's power against a known defeat.
ramayan::7649.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with threats, and you stay calm because you know exactly where your protection lies. Sita speaks from that kind of unshaken confidence.
ramayan::7649.insight: It shifts the mind from intimidation to clear-eyed confidence in real strength.

ramayan::7650.verse_sanskrit: य एते राक्षसाः प्रोक्ता घोररूपा महाबलाः । राघवे निर्विषास्सर्वे सुपर्णे पन्नगा यथा । । 3566 । ।
ramayan::7650.verse_hindi: Those dreadful, mighty demons you have described are ineffective in his presence just like the serpents who with their venom are ineffective  in the presence of  Suparna (Garuda).
ramayan::7650.english_translation: Those dreadful, mighty demons you have described are ineffective in Rama's presence, just like serpents are ineffective before Garuda.
ramayan::7650.translation_literal: य (who) / एते (these) / राक्षसाः (demons) / प्रोक्ता (described) / घोररूपा (terrible-looking) / महाबलाः (very powerful) / राघवे (in Rama's presence) / निर्विषाः (without poison, ineffective) / सर्वे (all) / सुपर्णे (before Garuda) / पन्नगाः (serpents) / यथा (just as)
ramayan::7650.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7650.essence: Rama's presence makes terrifying force powerless.
ramayan::7650.simple_meaning: Sita says Ravana's terrible warriors cannot really harm Rama, just as poisonous snakes lose power before Garuda.
ramayan::7650.simple_insight: Real strength makes threats look smaller than they seem.
ramayan::7650.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana's intimidation with calm certainty. She says the demons he boasts of are powerless before Rama, and she compares them to snakes before Garuda. The verse strengthens her defiance, but it is still part of a larger argument.
ramayan::7650.modern_relevance: Someone tries to scare you with their connections, their team, or their power. You remember that not every threat is equal, and some people simply cannot be shaken.
ramayan::7650.insight: It shifts fear into clear judgment: apparent power is not the same as real power.

ramayan::7651.verse_sanskrit: तस्य ज्याविप्रमुक्तास्ते शराः काञ्चनभूषणाः । शरीरं विधमिष्यन्ति गङ्गाकूलमिवोर्मयः । । 3567 । ।
ramayan::7651.verse_hindi: The goldtipped arrows released from his bowstring will shatter your body like the waves erode the banks of river Ganga.
ramayan::7651.english_translation: The gold-tipped arrows released from his bowstring will shatter your body like the waves erode the banks of the Ganga.
ramayan::7651.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / ज्या-विप्रमुक्ताः (released from the bowstring) / ते (those) / शराः (arrows) / काञ्चन-भूषणाः (gold-adorned) / शरीरम् (body) / विधमिष्यन्ति (will shatter) / गङ्गा-कूलम् (the bank of the Ganga) / इव (like) / ऊर्मयः (waves)
ramayan::7651.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7651.essence: Rama's force is not loud, but it is unstoppable.
ramayan::7651.simple_meaning: Rama's gold-tipped arrows will tear through your body just as river waves cut away a bank.
ramayan::7651.simple_insight: Power spoken with certainty can be more frightening than a threat.
ramayan::7651.detailed_meaning: Sita is answering Ravana with calm certainty after he boasts of his strength. She does not plead; she measures Rama's force against him and says his body will not withstand it. The line deepens her warning by making Rama's arrows feel like an unstoppable natural power.
ramayan::7651.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a room, expecting fear, and you answer without raising your voice. You know the difference between bluster and real force.
ramayan::7651.insight: It shifts the mind from intimidation to clear-eyed confidence in what is stronger.

ramayan::7652.verse_sanskrit: असुरैर्वा सुरैर्वा त्वं यद्यवध्योऽसि रावण । उत्पाद्य सुमहद्वैरं जीवंस्तस्य न मोक्ष्यसे । । 3568 । ।
ramayan::7652.verse_hindi: O Ravana, even if you stand invulnerable to gods and demons, you will not come out alive in the combat with Rama with whom you have earned great enmity.
ramayan::7652.english_translation: O Ravana, even if you are invulnerable to gods and demons, you will not come out alive in the combat with Rama, with whom you have earned great enmity.
ramayan::7652.translation_literal: असुरैः (by demons) / वा (or) / सुरैः (by gods) / वा (or) / त्वं (you) / यदि (if) / अवध्यः (invulnerable) / असि (are) / रावण (Ravana) / उत्पाद्य (having created) / सुमहत् (great) / वैरम् (enmity) / जीवन् (alive) / तस्य (with him) / न (not) / मोक्ष्यसे (you will be released)
ramayan::7652.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7652.essence: Great power cannot cancel the cost of your own enmity.
ramayan::7652.simple_meaning: Ravana may be beyond the reach of gods and demons, but not beyond the consequences of his enmity with Rama. This clash will end with his death.
ramayan::7652.simple_insight: No protection can save you from the cost of a chosen enemy.
ramayan::7652.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the war, Rama’s side is speaking with certainty about Ravana’s fate. The issue is no longer whether Ravana is powerful; it is whether his own actions have made survival impossible. This verse sharpens the warning into a verdict.
ramayan::7652.modern_relevance: You can build every defense you want, but some choices still corner you. The person you keep provoking may not need to be stronger than your shields.
ramayan::7652.insight: It shifts attention from raw power to the moral consequences of conflict.

ramayan::7653.verse_sanskrit: स ते जीवितशेषस्य राघवोऽन्तकरो बली । पशोर्यूपगतस्येव जीवितं तव दुर्लभम् । । 3569 । ।
ramayan::7653.verse_hindi: Powerful Rama will put an end to whatever little life you are left with. Just as a beast
ramayan::7653.english_translation: Powerful Rama will put an end to whatever little life you are left with. Just as a beast tied to the sacrificial post has little chance of living, your life is hard to preserve.
ramayan::7653.translation_literal: सः (he) / ते (your) / जीवितशेषस्य (of the remainder of life) / राघवः (Raghava/Rama) / अन्तकरः (end-maker) / बली (strong, powerful) / पशोः (of a beast) / यूपगतस्येव (as if bound to the sacrificial post) / जीवितम् (life) / तव (your) / दुर्लभम् (hard to obtain, difficult to preserve)
ramayan::7653.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7653.essence: Rama is the kind of force that leaves no room for escape.
ramayan::7653.simple_meaning: Rama will finish off the little life you have left. Your chances of surviving him are as slim as a sacrificial animal's.
ramayan::7653.simple_insight: When danger is real, denial becomes impossible.
ramayan::7653.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in the middle of his own threat-filled confidence, describing Rama as the one who will end the demon king’s remaining life. The image of a beast tied for sacrifice makes the warning brutal and immediate, not abstract.
ramayan::7653.modern_relevance: You can still pretend a problem is manageable until the moment it stands before you, undeniable. Then the real question is whether you were honest early enough.
ramayan::7653.insight: It sharpens the mind to face consequences before they arrive.

ramayan::7654.verse_sanskrit: यदि पश्येत्स रामस्त्वां रोषदीप्तेन चक्षुषा । रक्षस्त्वमद्य निर्धग्धो गच्छेस्सद्यः पराभवम् । । 35610 । ।
ramayan::7654.verse_hindi: O demon, you will be completely consumed if Rama looks at you with eyes burning in anger.
ramayan::7654.english_translation: O demon, if Rama looks at you with eyes burning in anger, you will be burned up at once and meet utter defeat.
ramayan::7654.translation_literal: यदि (if) / पश्येत् (should look) / सः (he) / रामः (Rama) / त्वाम् (you) / रोष-दीप्तेन (with anger-blazing) / चक्षुषा (with eyes) / रक्षः (demon) / त्वम् (you) / अद्य (today) / निर्धग्धः (completely burned) / गच्छेः (you would go) / सद्यः (at once) / पराभवम् (defeat)
ramayan::7654.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7654.essence: One look from Rama is said to end the enemy's strength.
ramayan::7654.simple_meaning: Rama's anger alone is enough to destroy the enemy instantly.
ramayan::7654.simple_insight: Real power does not need to shout; its gaze is enough.
ramayan::7654.detailed_meaning: In the war against Ravana, Rama's allies are describing his overwhelming force. This line is not a teaching but a threat inside a larger argument: even Rama's angry glance is said to be enough to burn the enemy and end the fight.
ramayan::7654.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the person with real authority finally looks up. No speech is needed; everyone feels the shift.
