ramayan::7654.insight: It shows Rama as a force of decisive power, not merely a warrior in motion.

ramayan::7655.verse_sanskrit: यश्चन्द्रं नभसो भूमौ पातयेन्नाशयेत वा । सागरं शोषयेद्वापि स सीतां मोचयेदिह । । 35611 । ।
ramayan::7655.verse_hindi: He who can bring down the Moon to the earth from the sky or even dash it down, he who can drain the sea dry will definitely release me from here.
ramayan::7655.english_translation: He who can bring the moon down from the sky to the earth, or even hurl it down, he who can dry up the sea, will surely free me from here.
ramayan::7655.translation_literal: यः (whoever) / चन्द्रम् (the moon) / नभसः (from the sky) / भूमौ (to the earth) / पातयेत् (could make fall) / वा (or) / नाशयेत् (could destroy) / वा (or) / सागरम् (the sea) / शोषयेत् (could dry up) / वा (or) / अपि (even) / सः (he) / सीताम् (Sita) / मोचयेत् (would release) / इह (here)
ramayan::7655.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7655.essence: Only impossible power can break a prison this vast.
ramayan::7655.simple_meaning: Sita says that only someone with impossible power could free her from Lanka.
ramayan::7655.simple_insight: Her hope is not weak; it is measured against the scale of the prison.
ramayan::7655.detailed_meaning: Sita is still trapped in Ravana’s city, speaking with fierce clarity about the scale of her captivity. She says only someone who can overturn the sky or drain the sea could free her, because ordinary strength will not be enough.
ramayan::7655.modern_relevance: You’re facing a problem that no quick fix can touch — a betrayal, a debt, a diagnosis, a trapped feeling. Some situations are so large that only extraordinary help can move them.
ramayan::7655.insight: It shifts the mind from underestimating the obstacle to naming its full size before seeking rescue.

ramayan::7656.verse_sanskrit: गतायुस्त्वं गतश्रीको गतसत्त्व गतेन्द्रियः । लङ्का वैधव्यसंयुक्ता त्वत्कृतेन भविष्यति । । 35612 । ।
ramayan::7656.verse_hindi: Your life is coming to an end. Your fortunes will wane, your strength will be sapped. Your senses will be dissipated. By your deeds Lanka will attain widowhood.
ramayan::7656.english_translation: Your life is coming to an end. Your fortunes will wane, your strength will be sapped. Your senses will be dissipated. By your deeds Lanka will attain widowhood.
ramayan::7656.translation_literal: गतायुः (life ended) / त्वम् (you) / गतश्रीकः (fortune gone) / गतसत्त्वः (strength gone) / गतइन्द्रियः (senses gone) / लङ्का (Lanka) / वैधव्यसंयुक्ता (joined with widowhood) / त्वत्कृतेन (by your doing) / भविष्यति (will become)
ramayan::7656.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7656.essence: Cruelty drains the one who commits it and ruins everything around him.
ramayan::7656.simple_meaning: Ravana is told that his life, power, and senses are nearing collapse, and that his actions will leave Lanka bereft and ruined.
ramayan::7656.simple_insight: Cruel acts do not stay private; they hollow out both the doer and the world around him.
ramayan::7656.detailed_meaning: Sita, held captive in Lanka, answers Ravana with calm force. After warning him that even Rama's anger would destroy him, she says his own life and strength are already fading. His wrongdoing will not only end him; it will leave Lanka devastated.
ramayan::7656.modern_relevance: You can still feel the damage after the apology is impossible. A betrayal may look powerful for a moment, but it quietly strips away the person who committed it.
ramayan::7656.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing wrongdoing as dominance to seeing it as self-destruction.

ramayan::7657.verse_sanskrit: न ते पापमिदं कर्म शुखोदर्कं भविष्यति । याऽहं नीता विनाभावं पतिपार्श्वात्त्वया वने । । 35613 । ।
ramayan::7657.verse_hindi: This evil deed(of abduction) will not yield happy results.You have brought me from my husband from the forest without any forethought.
ramayan::7657.english_translation: This evil deed of abduction will not bring happy results. You have taken me from my husband in the forest without forethought.
ramayan::7657.translation_literal: न (not) / ते (to you) / पापम् (evil deed) / इदम् (this) / कर्म (action) / शुखोदर्कम् (bringing happy result) / भविष्यति (will be) / या (which) / अहम् (I) / नीता (taken) / विनाभावम् (without forethought) / पतिपार्श्वात् (from husband’s side) / त्वया (by you) / वने (in the forest)
ramayan::7657.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7657.essence: Harm done in haste plants its own suffering.
ramayan::7657.simple_meaning: Sita tells Ravana that abducting her from her husband in the forest was a wicked act and will bring no good result.
ramayan::7657.simple_insight: Cruel acts may feel powerful in the moment, but they carry their own ruin.
ramayan::7657.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has seized Sita and is trying to break her resolve. She answers without fear: taking her from Rama was a thoughtless evil, and it will not end in happiness for him. Her words turn the abduction into a moral verdict.
ramayan::7657.modern_relevance: You sent the message, made the move, and crossed the line before thinking. Later, the damage is still there, and no excuse can make it clean.
ramayan::7657.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate gain to the long consequence of harmful action.

ramayan::7658.verse_sanskrit: स हि दैवतसंयुक्तो मम भर्ता महाद्युतिः । निर्भयो वीर्यमाश्रित्य शून्ये वसति दण्डके । । 35614 । ।
ramayan::7658.verse_hindi: My effulgent, valiant husband armed with divine power resides fearlessly in the desolate Dandaka.
ramayan::7658.english_translation: My effulgent, valiant husband, endowed with divine power, lives fearlessly in the lonely Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7658.translation_literal: सः (he) / हि (indeed) / दैवतसंयुक्तः (endowed with divine power) / मम (my) / भर्ता (husband) / महाद्युतिः (greatly radiant) / निर्भयः (fearless) / वीर्यम् (strength) / आश्रित्य (having taken refuge in) / शून्ये (in the empty/desolate place) / वसति (dwells) / दण्डके (in Dandaka)
ramayan::7658.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7658.essence: Exile has not diminished Rama; it has only revealed his fearlessness.
ramayan::7658.simple_meaning: Sita describes Rama as radiant, powerful, and fearless, living in the lonely Dandaka forest.
ramayan::7658.simple_insight: Love sees strength clearly, even in exile and danger.
ramayan::7658.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana’s taunts by turning to Rama’s true stature. She reminds him that the man he has insulted is not helpless: he is radiant, divinely empowered, and unafraid, even while living in the empty forest of Dandaka.
ramayan::7658.modern_relevance: Someone underestimates you because they only see your current situation. The people who know your character remember what still stands beneath the hardship.
ramayan::7658.insight: It shifts attention from outward weakness to inner force and steadiness.

ramayan::7659.verse_sanskrit: स ते दर्पं बलं वीर्यमुत्सेकं च तथाविधम् । अपनेष्यति गात्रेभ्यश्शरवर्षेण संयुगे । । 35615 । ।
ramayan::7659.verse_hindi: He will remove your pride, your power, your valour and haughtiness from your limbs with a shower of arrows in the fight.
ramayan::7659.english_translation: He will remove your pride, your power, your valour and haughtiness from your limbs with a shower of arrows in the fight.
ramayan::7659.translation_literal: स (he) / ते (your) / दर्पं (pride) / बलं (strength) / वीर्यम् (valour) / उत्सेकं च (and haughtiness) / तथाविधम् (of that kind) / अपनेष्यति (will remove) / गात्रेभ्यः (from the limbs) / शरवर्षेण (with a shower of arrows) / संयुगे (in battle)
ramayan::7659.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7659.essence: Pride falls fastest when it meets real force.
ramayan::7659.simple_meaning: Rama will strike you so hard in battle that your pride, strength, courage, and arrogance will be wiped out.
ramayan::7659.simple_insight: Arrogance looks solid until reality meets it.
ramayan::7659.detailed_meaning: Sita, held captive in Lanka, answers Ravana’s threats without fear. She names Rama as the one who will meet his pride with arrows in battle. The verse is a sharp warning, not a teaching.
ramayan::7659.modern_relevance: A person who keeps bullying everyone in the room eventually meets someone who does not flinch. The force that looked untouchable collapses the moment it is truly tested.
ramayan::7659.insight: It shows how unchecked arrogance invites its own undoing.

ramayan::7660.verse_sanskrit: यदा विनाशो भूतानां दृश्यते कालचोदितः । तदा कार्ये प्रमाद्यन्ति नराः कालवशं गताः । । 35616 । ।
ramayan::7660.verse_hindi: When destruction draws near, people being prompted by time start commiting blunders in their deeds.
ramayan::7660.english_translation: When destruction draws near, people prompted by time begin to make mistakes in their actions.
ramayan::7660.translation_literal: यदा (when) / विनाशः (destruction) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / दृश्यते (is seen) / कालचोदितः (prompted by time) / तदा (then) / कार्ये (in action) / प्रमाद्यन्ति (become careless) / नराः (people) / कालवशं (under the sway of time) / गताः (gone)
ramayan::7660.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7660.essence: When ruin is near, judgment begins to fail from within.
ramayan::7660.simple_meaning: When a person's end is near, time itself seems to cloud judgment and cause careless mistakes.
ramayan::7660.simple_insight: There is a grim clarity in seeing that self-destruction often begins before the final fall.
ramayan::7660.detailed_meaning: Sita is speaking to Ravana after warning him of Rama's power. She says that when a being's destruction is already approaching, time pushes that person into careless action. The verse explains Ravana's blindness as the sign of his nearing end.
ramayan::7660.modern_relevance: You keep forcing a decision even as every sign says you're off course. The more pressure rises, the more your own judgment starts betraying you.
ramayan::7660.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming only bad luck to seeing how inner confusion grows when consequences are already closing in.

ramayan::7661.verse_sanskrit: मां प्रधृष्य स ते कालः प्राप्तोऽयं राक्षसाधम । आत्मनो राक्षसानां च वधायान्तःपुरस्य च । । 35617 । ।
ramayan::7661.verse_hindi: You vilest of demons, since you have assaulted me, the time of your death and destruction of all demons and of all women in the harem has drawn near.
ramayan::7661.english_translation: You vilest of demons, since you have assaulted me, the time of your death and destruction of all demons and of all women in the harem has drawn near.
ramayan::7661.translation_literal: मां (me) / प्रधृष्य (having assaulted) / स (that) / ते (your) / कालः (time) / प्राप्तः (has arrived) / अयम् (this) / राक्षसाधम (vilest of demons) / आत्मनः (of yourself) / राक्षसानाम् (of the demons) / च (and) / वधाय (for the destruction) / अन्तःपुरस्य (of the harem) / च (and)
ramayan::7661.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7661.essence: Violation itself sets the punishment in motion.
ramayan::7661.simple_meaning: After assaulting her, the assailant is told that his own destruction, and the destruction tied to his side, has now begun.
ramayan::7661.simple_insight: Harm does not stay hidden forever; it ripens into consequences.
ramayan::7661.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita faces Ravana after his assault on her dignity. She does not collapse into fear; she names the moral law already moving against him. Her words turn the moment from private violence into inevitable reckoning.
ramayan::7661.modern_relevance: You send the message, cross the boundary, and tell yourself it will fade. But the damage has already changed the room, and the future is moving toward you.
ramayan::7661.insight: It shifts the mind from denial to accountability: actions against others begin their own undoing.

ramayan::7662.verse_sanskrit: न शक्या यज्ञमध्यस्था वेदी सृग्भाण्डमण्डिता । द्विजातिमन्त्रपूता च चण्डालेनावमर्दितुम् । । 35618 । ।
ramayan::7662.verse_hindi: The sacrificial altar adorned with ladles and vessels and sanctified by the sacred mantras recited by brahmins cannot be defiled by a chandala (man of lowest caste).
ramayan::7662.english_translation: An altar placed in the middle of a sacrifice, adorned with ladles and vessels and purified by brahmin chants, cannot be defiled by a chandala.
ramayan::7662.translation_literal: न शक्या (cannot be able) / यज्ञमध्यस्था (standing in the middle of a sacrifice) / वेदी (altar) / सृग्भाण्डमण्डिता (adorned with ladles and vessels) / द्विजातिमन्त्रपूता (purified by brahmin mantras) / च (and) / चण्डालेन (by a chandala) / अवमर्दितुम् (to defile)
ramayan::7662.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7662.essence: Purity cannot be destroyed by the one who tries to violate it.
ramayan::7662.simple_meaning: Sita says that just as a sacred altar cannot be polluted by an outcaste, she herself cannot be touched in a way that makes her impure.
ramayan::7662.simple_insight: Her dignity does not depend on what a violator tries to do.
ramayan::7662.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana with a sharp moral image. He has claimed power over her body, but she refuses his logic. She compares herself to a consecrated altar: protected by purity, untouched by the shame he tries to impose.
ramayan::7662.modern_relevance: Someone tries to shame you after crossing a line, as if their action defines you. Sita's reply draws a hard boundary: violation does not rewrite your worth.
ramayan::7662.insight: It shifts the mind from humiliation to inviolable self-respect.

ramayan::7663.verse_sanskrit: तथाऽहं धर्मनित्यस्य धर्मपत्नी पतिव्रता । त्वया स्पृष्टुं न शक्यास्मि राक्षसाधम पापिना । । 35619 । ।
ramayan::7663.verse_hindi: O lowly demon  similarly I am a chaste woman and wife of the ever righteous Rama who cannot be defiled by a sinner like you.
ramayan::7663.english_translation: O lowly demon, I am the devoted wife of the ever-righteous Rama and a chaste woman. A sinner like you cannot defile me.
ramayan::7663.translation_literal: तथा (similarly) / अहम् (I) / धर्म-नित्यस्य (of the ever-righteous) / धर्म-पत्नी (righteous wife) / पतिव्रता (devoted to one husband) / त्वया (by you) / स्पृष्टुम् (to touch) / न शक्या (cannot be able) / अस्मि (I am) / राक्षस-अधम (lowly demon) / पापिना (by the sinful)
ramayan::7663.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7663.essence: A corrupt touch cannot break a devotion already held in purity.
ramayan::7663.simple_meaning: Sita says she is Rama’s faithful wife, and Ravana cannot corrupt her or make her impure.
ramayan::7663.simple_insight: Your dignity is not granted by others; it can remain intact even under pressure.
ramayan::7663.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has cornered Sita and tried to overpower her with force and insult. She answers without fear, grounding her refusal in her loyalty to Rama and in her own moral strength.
ramayan::7663.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with pressure, manipulation, or a crude demand, expecting you to fold. You can refuse without shrinking. Your boundaries are not weakness; they are clarity.
ramayan::7663.insight: It teaches you to hold your ground from inner conviction, not from fear or apology.

ramayan::7664.verse_sanskrit: क्रीडन्ती राजहंसेन पद्मषण्डेषु नित्यदा । हंसी सा तृणषण्डस्थं कथं पश्येत मद्गुकम् । । 35620 । ।
ramayan::7664.verse_hindi: How can a female swan ever sporting in lotusponds in the company of a royal swan look at the watercrow resting on a grassy land?
ramayan::7664.english_translation: How can a female swan ever sporting in lotusponds in the company of a royal swan look at the watercrow resting on a grassy land?
ramayan::7664.translation_literal: क्रीडन्ती (sporting) / राजहंसेन (with a royal swan) / पद्मषण्डेषु (in lotus groves) / नित्यदा (always) / हंसी (female swan) / सा (that) / तृणषण्डस्थम् (resting on a grass patch) / कथम् (how) / पश्येत (would look at) / मद्गुकम् (watercrow)
ramayan::7664.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7664.essence: Your worth does not rise to meet what demeans you.
ramayan::7664.simple_meaning: Sita says Ravana is as unworthy of her attention as a waterbird on grass is to a swan living among lotuses with a royal swan.
ramayan::7664.simple_insight: She refuses to let comparison or insult blur her inner dignity.
ramayan::7664.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps pressing Sita to submit. She answers with a sharp image: she belongs with Rama, the royal swan, not with him. This is part of her firm rejection of Ravana's advances.
ramayan::7664.modern_relevance: Someone keeps sending messages after you have clearly said no, acting as if persistence can erode your standards. Sita's answer is a clean refusal, not an argument.
ramayan::7664.insight: It teaches you to hold your boundaries without apology or self-doubt.

ramayan::7665.verse_sanskrit: इदं शरीरं निस्संज्ञं बन्ध वा खातयस्व वा । नेदं शरीरं रक्षयं मे जीवितं वापि राक्षस । । 35621 । । न तु शक्ष्याम्युपक्रोशं पृथिव्यां दातुमात्मनः ।
ramayan::7665.verse_hindi: O demon  this body has (now) no consciousness. You may bind it or bury it. I do not think that this body or even this life need to be protected. But at no cost can I make this an object of censure on earth (must not be branded an unchaste woman).
ramayan::7665.english_translation: O demon, this body has no consciousness now. You may bind it or bury it. I do not think this body or even this life need to be protected. But I cannot allow myself to be shamed on earth.
ramayan::7665.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / शरीरम् (body) / निस्संज्ञम् (without consciousness) / बन्ध (bind) / वा (or) / खातयस्व (have buried) / वा (or) / न (not) / इदम् (this) / शरीरम् (body) / रक्ष्यम् (to be protected) / मे (my) / जीवितम् (life) / वा (or) / अपि (even) / राक्षस (demon) / न (not) / तु (but) / शक्ष्यामि (I will be able) / उपक्रोशम् (censure/shame) / पृथिव्याम् (on earth) / दातुम् (to give) / आत्मनः (of myself)
ramayan::7665.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7665.essence: Your body can be controlled; your dignity cannot be taken.
ramayan::7665.simple_meaning: Sita says Ravana can do whatever he wants to her body, but she will not accept shame or abandon her dignity.
ramayan::7665.simple_insight: There is strength in refusing to trade your integrity for safety.
ramayan::7665.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita stands before Ravana after rejecting his threat and temptation. Surrounded by force, she declares that even if her body is trapped, her honor is not. This is the moral center of her resistance.
ramayan::7665.modern_relevance: You are cornered in a room where someone can threaten your job, your reputation, or your privacy. The pressure is real, but so is your right to refuse humiliation.
ramayan::7665.insight: It teaches you to separate physical vulnerability from moral consent.

ramayan::7666.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही क्रोधात्सुपरुषं वचः । । 35622 । । रावणं मैथिली तत्र पुनर्नोवाच किञ्चन ।
ramayan::7666.verse_hindi: Having uttered these very harsh words out of anger, the daughter of Videha, the princess from Mithila spoke no more.
ramayan::7666.english_translation: Having uttered these very harsh words out of anger, the daughter of Videha, the princess from Mithila, spoke no more to Ravana there.
ramayan::7666.translation_literal: एवमुक्त्वा (having said thus) / तु (indeed) / वैदेही (the daughter of Videha) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / सुपरुषं (very harsh) / वचः (words) / रावणं (to Ravana) / मैथिली (the princess of Mithila) / तत्र (there) / पुनः (again) / न उवाच (did not speak) / किञ्चन (anything)
ramayan::7666.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7666.essence: A single fierce reply can be enough; after that, silence protects your dignity.
ramayan::7666.simple_meaning: Sita answered Ravana with sharp anger, then fell silent and said nothing more.
ramayan::7666.simple_insight: Sometimes dignity is not in the last word, but in refusing to keep arguing.
ramayan::7666.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has cornered Sita and tried to break her with force and insult. She answers once, fiercely, then stops. The silence matters: she will not keep feeding his cruelty.
ramayan::7666.modern_relevance: Someone keeps pushing your buttons in a group chat, hoping you'll spiral. You answer once, clearly, and then stop. That silence can be strength.
ramayan::7666.insight: It teaches you to answer abuse once and then withdraw your attention.

ramayan::7667.verse_sanskrit: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं रोमहर्षणम् । । 35623 । । प्रत्युवाच ततस्सीतां भयसन्दर्शनं वचः ।
ramayan::7667.verse_hindi: Having heard such harsh, horripilating words from Sita, Ravana replied in a way designed to create fear in her:
ramayan::7667.english_translation: Having heard Sita's harsh, terrifying words, Ravana replied with words meant to frighten her.
ramayan::7667.translation_literal: सीताया (of Sita) / वचनं (words) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / परुषं (harsh) / रोमहर्षणम् (hair-raising, terrifying) / प्रत्युवाच (replied) / ततः (then) / सीतां (to Sita) / भयसन्दर्शनं (fear-inducing) / वचः (speech)
ramayan::7667.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7667.essence: Fear tries to overpower what it cannot persuade.
ramayan::7667.simple_meaning: Ravana answers Sita with speech meant to scare her after hearing her fierce refusal.
ramayan::7667.simple_insight: Cruel words often follow when control is slipping.
ramayan::7667.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has just answered Ravana with fearless contempt and refused him completely. Hearing her defiance, Ravana does not soften; he turns to intimidation. This verse is the pivot before his threat-filled response.
ramayan::7667.modern_relevance: Someone shuts down your boundary with a smirk and a threat disguised as confidence. The moment reveals more about their fear than your weakness.
ramayan::7667.insight: It shows how ego answers refusal with intimidation instead of respect.

ramayan::7668.verse_sanskrit: शृणु मैथिलि मद्वाक्यं मासान्द्वादश भामिनि । । 35624 । । कालेनानेन नाभ्येषि यदि मां चारुहासिनि । ततस्त्वां प्रातराशार्थं सूदाश्छेत्स्यन्ति लेशशः । । 35625 । ।
ramayan::7668.verse_hindi: O comely princess from Mithila, O lady with a sweet smile listen to my words. If you do not accept my hand in the course of twelve months, the cooks will cut you off into small bits for the (my) breakfast.
ramayan::7668.english_translation: Listen, princess of Mithila. If you do not accept me within twelve months, my cooks will cut you into small pieces for breakfast.
ramayan::7668.translation_literal: शृणु (listen) / मैथिलि (O princess of Mithila) / मद्वाक्यम् (my words) / मासान् द्वादश (twelve months) / भामिनि (O lovely lady) / कालेन अनेन (by this time) / न अभ्येषि (you do not come to me) / यदि (if) / माम् (me) / चारुहासिनि (O sweet-smiled one) / ततः (then) / त्वाम् (you) / प्रातराशार्थम् (for breakfast) / सूदाः (the cooks) / छेत्स्यन्ति (will cut) / लेशशः (into bits)
ramayan::7668.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7668.essence: Ravana tries to rule through fear when he cannot win by truth.
ramayan::7668.simple_meaning: Ravana gives Sita a cruel deadline: accept him within twelve months, or he will have her killed and served up for breakfast.
ramayan::7668.simple_insight: Threats lose their power when you see the fear behind them.
ramayan::7668.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just heard Sita answer him with fire. Instead of humility, he answers with menace, trying to crush her resolve by setting a brutal deadline and threatening her life. The verse shows his arrogance and desperation.
ramayan::7668.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with a fake choice: comply now, or face consequences later. The pressure is meant to shrink your will, not clarify your options.
ramayan::7668.insight: It exposes coercion as a tactic of control, not a sign of strength.

ramayan::7669.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं रावणश्शत्रुरावणः । राक्षसीश्च ततः क्रुद्ध इदं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 35626 । ।
ramayan::7669.verse_hindi: Enraged Ravana, who used to make enemies wail, turned to the demonesses and said these words.
ramayan::7669.english_translation: Enraged Ravana, who used to make enemies wail, turned to the demonesses and said these words.
ramayan::7669.translation_literal: इत्युक्त्वा (having said thus) / परुषम् (harsh) / वाक्यम् (speech) / रावणः (Ravana) / शत्रुरावणः (the enemy-frightening Ravana) / राक्षसीः (the demonesses) / च (and) / ततः (then) / क्रुद्धः (angry) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (word) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7669.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7669.essence: Ravana's anger spills from the target to everyone nearby.
ramayan::7669.simple_meaning: Ravana, furious after speaking harshly to Sita, now turns to the demonesses and orders them to act.
ramayan::7669.simple_insight: Anger narrows the mind until cruelty feels like command.
ramayan::7669.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just tried to pressure Sita and failed. Still burning with rage, he turns away from her and addresses the demonesses, preparing them to carry out his threat. The verse is a bridge into the next command, not the command itself.
ramayan::7669.modern_relevance: A conversation goes badly, and instead of cooling down, someone lashes out at the nearest people in the room. The real damage often starts after the argument ends.
ramayan::7669.insight: It shows how wounded pride quickly becomes aggression toward others.

ramayan::7670.verse_sanskrit: शीघ्रमेव हि राक्षस्यो विकृता घोरदर्शनाः । दर्पमस्या विनेष्यध्वं मांसशोणितभोजनाः । । 35627 । ।
ramayan::7670.verse_hindi: Addressing the flesheating, blooddrinking, loathsome and fearful demonesses Ravana said, Humble her pride at once.
ramayan::7670.english_translation: Ravana said, "You fearful, deformed flesh-eaters, crush her pride at once."
ramayan::7670.translation_literal: शीघ्रम् (at once) / एव (indeed) / हि (certainly) / राक्षस्यः (female demons) / विकृताः (deformed) / घोरदर्शनाः (terrifying-looking) / दर्पम् (pride) / अस्याः (of her) / विनेष्यध्वम् (you should crush) / मांसशोणितभोजनाः (you whose food is flesh and blood)
ramayan::7670.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7670.essence: Cruelty begins by trying to break dignity.
ramayan::7670.simple_meaning: Ravana orders the demonesses to break Sita's spirit immediately.
ramayan::7670.simple_insight: Cruel power always tries to humiliate before it harms.
ramayan::7670.detailed_meaning: After threatening Sita himself, Ravana turns to his demonesses and orders them to crush her pride. He is trying to make fear do what force alone has not yet done, and the next verse shows them obeying at once.
ramayan::7670.modern_relevance: A hostile group starts circling the one person who refuses to break. The pressure is no longer just physical — it is meant to humiliate, isolate, and wear down dignity.
ramayan::7670.insight: It shows how intimidation often targets self-respect first, not just the body.

ramayan::7671.verse_sanskrit: वचनादेव तास्तस्य सुघोरा राक्षसीगणाः । कृतप्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा मैथिलीं पर्यवारयन् । । 35628 । ।
ramayan::7671.verse_hindi: No sooner had Ravana said it than the dreadful demonesses offered obeisance to him with folded hands and surrounded Sita.
ramayan::7671.english_translation: No sooner had Ravana said it than the dreadful demonesses offered obeisance to him with folded hands and surrounded Sita.
ramayan::7671.translation_literal: वचनात् (at the word) / एव (indeed, just) / ताः (those) / तस्य (his) / सु-घोराः (very dreadful) / राक्षसी-गणाः (groups of demonesses) / कृताञ्जलयः (with folded hands) / भूत्वा (having become) / मैथिलीम् (Sita, the princess of Mithila) / पर्यवारयन् (surrounded)
ramayan::7671.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7671.essence: Ravana's cruelty becomes real the moment others obey it.
ramayan::7671.simple_meaning: At Ravana's command, the terrifying demonesses bowed and closed in around Sita.
ramayan::7671.simple_insight: Power can turn obedience into cruelty in a single moment.
ramayan::7671.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just ordered the demonesses to crush Sita's pride. They instantly bow and encircle her, showing how completely his will controls the room. The verse is a brief action beat, not the passage's main teaching.
ramayan::7671.modern_relevance: A manager sends one sharp message, and everyone around the room falls into line. The pressure is not physical, but the same fear of power makes people move without questioning.
ramayan::7671.insight: It shows how command can spread cruelty through obedient hands.

ramayan::7672.verse_sanskrit: स ताः प्रोवाच राजा तु रावणो घोरदर्शनः । प्रचाल्य चरणोत्कर्षैर्दारयन्निव मेदिनीम् । । 35629 । ।
ramayan::7672.verse_hindi: Stamping his feet and shaking the ground as if tearing the earth, Ravana said to those fiercelooking demonesses:
ramayan::7672.english_translation: Stamping his feet and shaking the ground as if tearing the earth, Ravana said to those fiercelooking demonesses:
ramayan::7672.translation_literal: स (he) / ताः (those) / प्रोवाच (spoke) / राजा (king) / तु (indeed) / रावणः (Ravana) / घोरदर्शनः (fearful-looking) / प्रचाल्य (shaking) / चरणोत्कर्षैः (with the lifting of his feet) / दारयन्निव (as if tearing) / मेदिनीम् (the earth)
ramayan::7672.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7672.essence: Force is being used here to cover insecurity.
ramayan::7672.simple_meaning: Ravana speaks to his demonesses with violent force, stamping the ground as he gives orders.
ramayan::7672.simple_insight: Power can sound loud and still be brittle underneath.
ramayan::7672.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has already ordered Sita surrounded by his fierce attendants. Now he stamps the ground and speaks like a man trying to make fear do the work of authority. The verse sets up his command to move Sita into the Ashoka grove.
ramayan::7672.modern_relevance: A manager slams a hand on the table and raises their voice to hide uncertainty. The room goes quiet, but everyone can feel the strain behind the display.
ramayan::7672.insight: It shows how domination often depends on performance, not inner steadiness.

ramayan::7673.verse_sanskrit: अशोकवनिकामध्ये मैथिली नीयतामियम् । तत्रेयं रक्ष्यतां गूढं युष्माभिः परिवारिता । । 35630 । ।
ramayan::7673.verse_hindi: Let this Sita be led into the Asoka grove. There sit round her and protect her in secret (her presence there should not be made public).
ramayan::7673.english_translation: Let this Sita be led into the Asoka grove. There sit round her and protect her in secret; her presence there should not be made public.
ramayan::7673.translation_literal: अशोकवनिकामध्ये (into the Asoka grove) / मैथिली (Sita) / नीयताम् (let be led) / इयम् (this) / तत्र (there) / इयम् (her) / रक्ष्यताम् (let be protected) / गूढम् (in secret) / युष्माभिः (by you all) / परिवारिता (surrounded)
ramayan::7673.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7673.essence: Control can wear the mask of protection.
ramayan::7673.simple_meaning: Ravana orders Sita to be taken into the Asoka grove and guarded secretly by the demonesses.
ramayan::7673.simple_insight: Power can hide what it cannot win.
ramayan::7673.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just summoned his fierce attendants and now gives them a cold command. Sita is to be moved into the Asoka grove, surrounded, and kept out of public view. The verse is a tactical instruction, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7673.modern_relevance: A manager quietly moves someone to a corner office and tells others to keep it low-key. The control is real, even when it is dressed up as protection.
ramayan::7673.insight: It shows how coercion often hides behind the language of care and secrecy.

ramayan::7674.verse_sanskrit: तत्रैनां तर्जनैर्घोरैः पुनस्सान्त्वैश्च मैथिलीम् । आनयध्वं वशं सर्वा वन्यां गजवधूमिव । । 35631 । ।
ramayan::7674.verse_hindi: There you all bring her under control through forcing and cajoling as one would do to tame a wild sheelephant.
ramayan::7674.english_translation: There, all of you bring Sita under control through threats and then soothing words, as you would tame a wild she-elephant.
ramayan::7674.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / एनाम् (her) / तर्जनैः (with threats) / घोरैः (terrible) / पुनः (again) / सान्त्वैः (with conciliatory words) / च (and) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili) / आनयध्वम् (bring) / वशम् (under control) / सर्वाः (all) / वन्याम् (wild) / गजवधूमिव (like a female elephant)
ramayan::7674.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7674.essence: Power tries to break dignity by alternating fear and charm.
ramayan::7674.simple_meaning: Ravana orders the demonesses to subdue Sita by alternating threats and soothing words, treating her like a wild animal to be broken.
ramayan::7674.simple_insight: Cruel control often mixes fear and false kindness.
ramayan::7674.detailed_meaning: Ravana has placed Sita in the Asoka grove and now instructs his demon attendants how to handle her. He does not seek understanding or consent; he wants submission, using intimidation and soft speech together to break her resistance.
ramayan::7674.modern_relevance: Someone corners you with pressure, then suddenly switches to sweetness to get you to yield. The tactic changes, but the aim is the same: control.
ramayan::7674.insight: It exposes manipulation as a blend of force and persuasion, and warns you to see through both.

ramayan::7675.verse_sanskrit: इति प्रतिसमादिष्टा राक्षस्यो रावणेन ताः । अशोकवनिकां जग्मुर्मैथिलीं परिगृह्य तु । । 35632 । । सर्वकालफलैर्वृक्षैर्नानापुष्पफलैर्वृताम् । सर्वकालमदैश्चापि द्विजैस्समुपसेविताम् । । 35633 । ।
ramayan::7675.verse_hindi: Thus instructed by Ravana, the demonesses took Sita into the Asoka grove, which was full of perenmal fruits and flowers of different kinds, where trees yielded fruits of all seasons and birds were always cheerful.
ramayan::7675.english_translation: Thus instructed by Ravana, the demonesses took Sita into the Asoka grove, which was full of perennial fruits and flowers of many kinds, and where birds were always cheerful.
ramayan::7675.translation_literal: इति (thus) / प्रतिसमादिष्टाः (having been instructed) / राक्षस्यः (the demonesses) / रावणेन (by Ravana) / ताः (they) / अशोकवनिकाम् (to the Asoka grove) / जग्मुः (went) / मैथिलीम् (Sita) / परिगृह्य (taking) / तु (indeed) / सर्वकालफलैः (with fruits of all seasons) / वृक्षैः (with trees) / नानापुष्पफलैः (with many flowers and fruits) / वृताम् (surrounded) / सर्वकालमदैः (always cheerful) / च (and) / अपि (also) / द्विजैः (by birds) / समुपसेविताम् (served / frequented)
ramayan::7675.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7675.essence: A beautiful place can still be a prison.
ramayan::7675.simple_meaning: Ravana’s attendants lead Sita into the Asoka grove, a beautiful garden filled with fruit, flowers, and birds.
ramayan::7675.simple_insight: Even beauty can feel like a cage when you are not free.
ramayan::7675.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has ordered the demonesses to place Sita in the Asoka grove and keep her guarded. The garden is lush and pleasant, but it is still the place where her captivity is deepened.
ramayan::7675.modern_relevance: You arrive in a beautiful room after being cornered into a choice you never wanted. The setting may be lovely, but your freedom is already gone.
ramayan::7675.insight: It separates outward beauty from inward captivity, showing that comfort does not equal freedom.

ramayan::7676.verse_sanskrit: सा तु शोकपरीताङ्गी मैथिली जनकात्मजा । राक्षसीवशमापन्ना व्याघ्रीणां हरिणी यथा । । 35634 । ।
ramayan::7676.verse_hindi: Sita, daughter of Janaka, engulfed in grief found herself like a doe under the control of tigresses.
ramayan::7676.english_translation: Sita, daughter of Janaka, engulfed in grief found herself like a doe under the control of tigresses.
ramayan::7676.translation_literal: सा (she) / तु (indeed) / शोकपरीताङ्गी (whose body was filled with grief) / मैथिली (Maithili) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka) / राक्षसीवशमापन्ना (fallen under the control of demonesses) / व्याघ्रीणां (of tigresses) / हरिणी (a doe) / यथा (like)
ramayan::7676.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7676.essence: Grief leaves you exposed when cruelty closes in.
ramayan::7676.simple_meaning: Sita is overwhelmed by sorrow and trapped among cruel women, like a helpless deer among tigresses.
ramayan::7676.simple_insight: Grief can make even the strongest person feel cornered and exposed.
ramayan::7676.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita has been seized and placed among Ravana’s demonesses in the Ashoka grove. Valmiki compares her to a doe surrounded by tigresses, showing both her vulnerability and the threat pressing in on her.
ramayan::7676.modern_relevance: You can be in a room full of people and still feel hunted, watched, and powerless. This verse names that raw, cornered feeling.
ramayan::7676.insight: It shifts attention to the emotional violence of captivity, not just the physical act of being held.

ramayan::7677.verse_sanskrit: शोकेन महता ग्रस्ता मैथिली जनकात्मजा । न शर्म लभते भीरुः पाशबद्धा मृगी यथा । । 35635 । ।
ramayan::7677.verse_hindi: Sita, daughter of Janaka, immersed in deep grief knew no peace just like a doe caught in a snare.
ramayan::7677.english_translation: Sita, daughter of Janaka, overwhelmed by great grief, found no peace, like a doe caught in a snare.
ramayan::7677.translation_literal: शोकेन (by grief) / महता (great) / ग्रस्ता (seized, swallowed) / मैथिली (Sita of Mithila) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka) / न (not) / शर्म (peace, comfort) / लभते (finds) / भीरुः (fearful, tender) / पाशबद्धा (bound in a snare) / मृगी (doe) / यथा (like)
ramayan::7677.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7677.essence: Grief can imprison you without ever touching your worth.
ramayan::7677.simple_meaning: Sita is so overwhelmed by grief and fear that she cannot find any peace, just like a deer caught in a trap.
ramayan::7677.simple_insight: Pain can pin you down without taking away your worth.
ramayan::7677.detailed_meaning: In Lanka’s Ashoka grove, Sita has been seized by Ravana’s demonesses and separated from Rama. Valmiki lingers on her inner state: grief has closed in so tightly that even safety feels unreachable. The simile of the trapped doe shows her vulnerability without diminishing her dignity.
ramayan::7677.modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor after bad news, unable to think straight, feeling cornered by what you cannot change. This verse understands that kind of helplessness without calling it weakness.
ramayan::7677.insight: It teaches you to see suffering clearly without confusing suffering with failure.

ramayan::7678.verse_sanskrit: न विन्दते तत्र तु शर्म मैथिली विरूपनेत्राभिरतीव तर्जिता । पतिं स्मरन्ती दयितं च देवतं विचेतनाऽभूद्भयशोकपीडिता । । 35636 । ।
ramayan::7678.verse_hindi: Sita had no peace as she was threatened excessively by those women of deformed  looks. Remembering her beloved husband who was also her god, and overtaken by fear and grief , she fell unconscious.
ramayan::7678.english_translation: Sita had no peace as she was threatened excessively by those women of deformed looks. Remembering her beloved husband, whom she held dear as a deity, and overtaken by fear and grief, she fell unconscious.
ramayan::7678.translation_literal: न विन्दते (did not find) / तत्र (there) / तु (indeed) / शर्म (peace) / मैथिली (Sita of Mithila) / विरूपनेत्राभिः (by women with deformed eyes) / अतीव (greatly) / तर्जिता (threatened) / पतिम् (husband) / स्मरन्ती (remembering) / दयितम् (beloved) / च (and) / देवतम् (deity) / विचेतना (unconscious) / अभूत् (became) / भयशोकपीडिता (afflicted by fear and grief)
ramayan::7678.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7678.essence: Love held in memory cannot always stop collapse under terror.
ramayan::7678.simple_meaning: Sita could find no peace. Harassed by the demon women, she thought of Rama and lost consciousness in fear and grief.
ramayan::7678.simple_insight: Grief can overwhelm even the strongest heart when love feels out of reach.
ramayan::7678.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is surrounded by hostile women who mock and threaten her. She holds on to Rama in memory, but fear and sorrow finally break her composure, and she faints. The verse deepens her suffering rather than advancing the plot.
ramayan::7678.modern_relevance: You keep replaying one cruel conversation while everyone around you keeps pressing for an answer. Your body goes quiet before your mind can catch up.
ramayan::7678.insight: It shows how sustained fear and grief can shut the body down.

ramayan::7679.verse_sanskrit: राक्षसं मृगरूपेण चरन्तं कामरूपिणम् । निहत्य रामो मारीचं तूर्णं पथि न्यवर्तत । । 3571 । ।
ramayan::7679.verse_hindi: Rama killed Maricha, the demon assuming the form of the deer as per his will and swiftly took the return path.
ramayan::7679.english_translation: Rama killed Maricha, the demon who had taken the form of a deer at will, and swiftly turned back on the path.
ramayan::7679.translation_literal: राक्षसं (demon) / मृगरूपेण (in the form of a deer) / चरन्तं (moving) / कामरूपिणम् (shape-shifting) / निहत्य (having killed) / रामः (Rama) / मारीचं (Maricha) / तूर्णं (swiftly) / पथि (on the path) / न्यवर्तत (turned back)
ramayan::7679.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7679.essence: A false lure can cost you the moment you cannot afford to lose.
ramayan::7679.simple_meaning: Rama kills Maricha, who has disguised himself as a deer, and immediately heads back.
ramayan::7679.simple_insight: Some moments demand instant action, not reflection.
ramayan::7679.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha has lured Rama away by taking the form of a deer. Rama strikes him down and turns back at once, but the delay has already served Ravana's plan. The verse is a plot-moving detail, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7679.modern_relevance: You notice too late that the distraction was the trap. By the time you turn back, the real danger has already moved.
ramayan::7679.insight: It shows how a single deceptive lure can pull attention away from what matters most.

ramayan::7680.verse_sanskrit: तस्य सन्त्वरमाणस्य द्रष्टुकामस्य मैथिलीम् । क्रूरस्वनोऽथ गोमायुर्विननादास्य पृष्ठतः । । 3572 । ।
ramayan::7680.verse_hindi: While Rama was hasting to see Sita, he heard from behind the ghastly howl of a jackal.
ramayan::7680.english_translation: While Rama was hurrying to see Sita, he heard behind him the ghastly howl of a jackal.
ramayan::7680.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / सन्त्वरमाणस्य (of one hurrying) / द्रष्टुकामस्य (desiring to see) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili) / क्रूरस्वनः (cruel-sounding) / अथ (then) / गोमायुः (jackal) / विननाद (howled) / अस्य (behind him) / पृष्ठतः (from the rear)
ramayan::7680.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7680.essence: A hopeful return is interrupted by an ominous sign.
ramayan::7680.simple_meaning: Rama is hurrying back to see Sita when a jackal howls behind him.
ramayan::7680.simple_insight: A sudden sign can interrupt even urgent hope.
ramayan::7680.detailed_meaning: After killing Maricha, Rama is hurrying back toward Sita. Before the reunion can happen, a jackal howls behind him, breaking the momentum and hinting at danger. The verse sets up Rama's unease in the next line.
ramayan::7680.modern_relevance: You are almost at the conversation you have been dreading and hoping for. Then one small sound in the room changes everything.
ramayan::7680.insight: It shifts the scene from forward motion to warning, preparing the mind for suspicion.

ramayan::7681.verse_sanskrit: स तस्य स्वरमाज्ञाय दारुणं रोमहर्षणम् । चिन्तयामास गोमायोस्स्वरेण परिशङ्कितः । । 3573 । ।
ramayan::7681.verse_hindi: Rama knew it was the horrible, horripilating cry of a jackal which made him apprehensive . It made him think.
ramayan::7681.english_translation: Rama recognized the dreadful, hair-raising cry and grew anxious at the jackal's sound.
ramayan::7681.translation_literal: स (he) / तस्य (that) / स्वरम् (sound) / आज्ञाय (having recognized) / दारुणम् (terrible) / रोमहर्षणम् (hair-raising) / चिन्तयामास (he thought) / गोमायोः (of the jackal) / स्वरेण (by the sound) / परिशङ्कितः (made apprehensive)
ramayan::7681.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7681.essence: The body can sense danger before the mind can name it.
ramayan::7681.simple_meaning: Rama hears a jackal's cry and immediately feels uneasy. The sound seems like a bad sign.
ramayan::7681.simple_insight: A sudden unease can arrive before you know why. The mind notices danger before the facts are clear.
ramayan::7681.detailed_meaning: Rama is hurrying back after killing Maricha, eager to return to Sita. Then a jackal's harsh cry breaks the moment. He recognizes it at once as disturbing and begins to worry, because the scene feels wrong before anything is explained.
ramayan::7681.modern_relevance: You are walking to meet someone you love, and one strange sound makes your stomach tighten. Before you can explain it, your body already knows something feels off.
ramayan::7681.insight: It shows how instinct can register danger before the mind has a full explanation.

ramayan::7682.verse_sanskrit: अशुभं बत मन्येऽहं गोमायुर्वाश्यते यथा । स्वस्ति स्यादपि वैदेह्या राक्षसैर्भक्षणं विना । । 3574 । ।
ramayan::7682.verse_hindi: The way the jackal is howling appears ominous. May Sita be safe without being eaten up by demons
ramayan::7682.english_translation: The jackal’s cry feels ominous. May Sita remain safe and not be eaten by demons.
ramayan::7682.translation_literal: अशुभम् (inauspicious) / बत (alas) / मन्येऽहम् (I think) / गोमायुर्वाश्यते (the jackal is howling) / यथा (as) / स्वस्ति (safely) / स्यात् (may there be) / अपि (even) / वैदेह्याः (for Vaidehi / Sita) / राक्षसैः (by demons) / भक्षणं (being eaten) / विना (without)
ramayan::7682.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7682.essence: A bad omen becomes unbearable because Sita’s safety is all that matters.
ramayan::7682.simple_meaning: Rama hears the jackal’s cry as a bad sign and immediately worries for Sita’s safety.
ramayan::7682.simple_insight: Love can turn a small sign into urgent fear.
ramayan::7682.detailed_meaning: Rama is hurrying to reach Sita when a jackal howls behind him. He takes it as an ominous sign and, in the middle of that anxious moment, his first thought is whether Sita is safe from the demons.
ramayan::7682.modern_relevance: You hear a strange silence after a missed call, and your mind jumps straight to the person you love. Fear makes even a small sign feel huge.
ramayan::7682.insight: It shows how anxiety narrows attention to the one person you cannot bear to lose.

ramayan::7683.verse_sanskrit: मारीचेन तु विज्ञाय स्वरमालम्ब्य मामकम् । विक्रुष्टं मृगरूपेण लक्ष्मणश्शृणुयाद्यदि । । 3575 । । स सौमित्रिस्स्वरं श्रुत्वा तां च हित्वाच मैथिलीम् । तयेह प्रहितः क्षिप्रं मत्सकाशमिहैष्यति । । 3576 । ।
ramayan::7683.verse_hindi: If  Lakshmana listens to Maricha imitating my voice in the form of a deer, he, sent by Sita will come for me at once, leaving her behind.
ramayan::7683.english_translation: If Lakshmana hears Maricha imitating my voice in the form of a deer, he will leave Sita behind and come to me at once.
ramayan::7683.translation_literal: मारीचेन (by Maricha) / तु (indeed) / विज्ञाय (having known) / स्वरम् (voice) / आलम्ब्य (taking up) / मामकम् (my) / विक्रुष्टम् (cried out) / मृगरूपेण (in deer-form) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / शृणुयात् (should hear) / यदि (if) / सः (he) / सौमित्रिः (Lakshmana, son of Sumitra) / स्वरम् (voice) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / ताम् (her) / च (and) / हित्वा (leaving) / च (also) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili, Sita) / तया (by her) / इह (here) / प्रहितः (sent) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / मत्सकाशम् (to my presence) / इह (here) / एष्यति (will come)
ramayan::7683.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7683.essence: A fake call can move the protector away from what matters most.
ramayan::7683.simple_meaning: Rama foresees that Maricha’s imitation of his voice will lure Lakshmana away from Sita and bring him back quickly.
ramayan::7683.simple_insight: A single false cry can split attention and expose what you were protecting.
ramayan::7683.detailed_meaning: Rama, already suspicious of the golden deer, works out the trap before it fully closes. He sees that if Lakshmana hears his voice called out from the forest, he will rush away from Sita, and that separation is exactly what the enemies want.
ramayan::7683.modern_relevance: You hear your phone ring from another room and leave the child alone for one minute. That is how distraction works: it pulls the protector away at the exact wrong moment.
ramayan::7683.insight: It teaches you to recognize bait that uses urgency to separate you from your responsibility.

ramayan::7684.verse_sanskrit: राक्षसैस्सहितैर्नूनं सीताया ईप्सितो वधः । काञ्चनश्च मृगो भूत्वा व्यपनीयाश्रमात्तु माम् । । 3577 । । दूरं नीत्वा तु मारीचो राक्षसोऽभूच्छरा हतः । हा लक्ष्मण हतोऽस्मीति यद्वाक्यं व्याजहार ह । । 3578 । ।
ramayan::7684.verse_hindi: Hence the murder of Sita must have been jointly planned by the demons. Maricha who had assumed the form of a golden deer, took me away from the hermitage to a faroff place where, killed by my arrows, he turned a demon uttering the words, Alas, Lakshmana, I am killed.
ramayan::7684.english_translation: Hence the murder of Sita must have been jointly planned by the demons. Maricha, who had taken the form of a golden deer, lured me away from the hermitage to a far-off place, where he was struck down by my arrows and cried out, 'Alas, Lakshmana, I am slain.'
ramayan::7684.translation_literal: राक्षसैः (with demons) / सहितैः (together) / नूनम् (surely) / सीतायाः (of Sita) / ईप्सितः (desired) / वधः (killing) / काञ्चनः (golden) / च (and) / मृगः (deer) / भूत्वा (having become) / व्यपनीय (having led away) / आश्रमात् (from the hermitage) / तु (indeed) / माम् (me) / दूरम् (far) / नीत्वा (having taken) / तु (then) / मारीचः (Maricha) / राक्षसः (a demon) / अभूत् (became) / शरैः (by arrows) / हतः (struck) / हा (alas) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / हतः (slain) / अस्मि (I am) / इति (thus) / यत् (which) / वाक्यम् (words) / व्याजहार (uttered) / ह (indeed)
ramayan::7684.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7684.essence: The trap worked by separating protector from the protected.
ramayan::7684.simple_meaning: Rama concludes that the demons must have planned Sita's death together. He recalls how Maricha, disguised as a golden deer, drew him away and then died crying out in a way meant to mislead Lakshmana.
ramayan::7684.simple_insight: Deception works by pulling you away from what you were meant to protect.
ramayan::7684.detailed_meaning: In the forest near the hermitage, Rama pieces together the trap after the golden deer episode. Maricha's dying cry was meant to sound like Rama's voice and draw Lakshmana away, leaving Sita exposed. Rama now sees the larger conspiracy behind the abduction.
ramayan::7684.modern_relevance: You answer one urgent message and miss the real danger unfolding next to you. Later, the pattern is obvious: distraction was the weapon, and separation was the goal.
ramayan::7684.insight: It shifts attention from the bait to the strategy behind it.

ramayan::7685.verse_sanskrit: अपि स्वस्ति भवेत्ताभ्यां रहिताभ्यां महावने । जनस्थाननिमित्तं हि कृतवैरोऽस्मि राक्षसैः । । 3579 । । निमित्तानि च घोराणि दृश्यन्तेऽद्य बहूनि च ।
ramayan::7685.verse_hindi: On account of living in this dense forest in Janasthana I have earned enmity with the demons. Will Lakshmana and Sita be safe without my protection? I see many terrible portents.
ramayan::7685.english_translation: Will Lakshmana and Sita be safe without me in this great forest? I have made enemies among the demons in Janasthana, and today I see many terrible omens.
ramayan::7685.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / स्वस्ति (well-being) / भवेत्ताभ्यां (may there be for those two) / रहिताभ्यां (being without) / महावने (in the great forest) / जनस्थान-निमित्तं (because of Janasthana) / हि (indeed) / कृत-वैरोऽस्मि (I have become one who has made enmity) / राक्षसैः (with the demons) / निमित्तानि (omens) / च (and) / घोराणि (terrible) / दृश्यन्ते (are seen) / अद्य (today) / बहूनि (many)
ramayan::7685.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7685.essence: Love becomes vigilance when the people you protect are out of sight.
ramayan::7685.simple_meaning: Rama worries that Lakshmana and Sita may be unsafe without him. He also senses that the forest and the day itself are full of bad signs.
ramayan::7685.simple_insight: Love does not always feel tender; sometimes it feels like alertness, fear, and responsibility.
ramayan::7685.detailed_meaning: In Janasthana, Rama has already drawn the demons' hostility. As he stands away from Lakshmana and Sita, he suddenly feels the weight of having left them exposed. The verse catches his protective anxiety and his sense that danger is closing in.
ramayan::7685.modern_relevance: You step out for ten minutes and your mind stays with the child asleep at home, the partner driving in rain, the parent who didn't answer the call. Care can make you feel the distance like a wound.
ramayan::7685.insight: It shifts attention from personal safety to protective responsibility for those depending on you.

ramayan::7686.verse_sanskrit: इत्येवं चिन्तयन्रामश्श्रुत्वा गोमायुनिस्स्वनम् । । 35710 । । आत्मनश्चापनयनान्मृगरूपेण रक्षसा । आजगाम जनस्थानं राघवः परिशङ्कितः । । 35711 । ।
ramayan::7686.verse_hindi: On hearing the jackals howl, Rama began thinking how the demon in the form of a deer drew him away. Thus in the midst of apprehensions he reached Janasthana.
ramayan::7686.english_translation: On hearing the jackals howl, Rama began thinking how the demon in the form of a deer had drawn him away. In deep apprehension, he reached Janasthana.
ramayan::7686.translation_literal: इत्येवं (thus) / चिन्तयन् (thinking) / रामः (Rama) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / गोमायु-निस्स्वनम् (the jackals' howl) / आत्मनः (of himself) / च (and) / अप-नयनात् (from being led away) / मृग-रूपेण (in the form of a deer) / रक्षसा (by the demon) / आजगाम (came) / जनस्थानम् (to Janasthana) / राघवः (Raghava) / परिशङ्कितः (full of apprehension)
ramayan::7686.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7686.essence: Unease becomes wisdom when the signs finally fit together.
ramayan::7686.simple_meaning: Rama hears an ominous cry and realizes the deer was a demon's trick. Uneasy, he returns to Janasthana with growing fear.
ramayan::7686.simple_insight: Fear sharpens attention when something is wrong.
ramayan::7686.detailed_meaning: Rama is already uneasy after being lured away by the golden deer. Hearing the jackals cry, he connects the signs and hurries back toward Janasthana, sensing danger at home.
ramayan::7686.modern_relevance: You get one strange message, then another: a missed call, a silence, a feeling in your chest. The mind starts connecting the dots before the facts are fully clear.
ramayan::7686.insight: It shows how intuition gathers scattered signs into caution before disaster fully appears.

ramayan::7687.verse_sanskrit: तं दीनमनसो दीनमासेदुर्मृगपक्षिणः । सव्यं कृत्वा महात्मानं घोरांश्च ससृजुस्स्वरान् । । 35712 । ।
ramayan::7687.verse_hindi: Dejected at heart, the birds and animals piteously kept the great soul (Rama) to the left and produced a dreadful cacophony.
ramayan::7687.english_translation: Dejected at heart, the birds and animals piteously kept the great soul Rama to the left and produced a dreadful cacophony.
ramayan::7687.translation_literal: तम् (that) / दीनमनसः (with dejected mind) / दीनम् (dejected) / आसेदुः (approached) / मृगपक्षिणः (deer and birds) / सव्यं (to the left) / कृत्वा (having made) / महात्मानम् (the great soul) / घोरान् (dreadful) / च (and) / ससृजुः (released) / स्वरान् (sounds)
ramayan::7687.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7687.essence: The forest itself warns him that danger is near.
ramayan::7687.simple_meaning: The animals and birds around Rama gave ominous signs: they moved to his left and made harsh sounds.
ramayan::7687.simple_insight: Sometimes the world seems to warn you before your mind is ready to listen.
ramayan::7687.detailed_meaning: Rama has just been led astray by the deer and now senses danger in Janasthana. Around him, the forest itself turns uneasy: birds and animals crowd to his left and cry out harshly. This is one more ominous sign in a sequence pushing him to turn back.
ramayan::7687.modern_relevance: You step outside and the day feels off before anything has gone wrong. A missed call, a slammed door, a restless dog — your body notices the warning before your thoughts do.
ramayan::7687.insight: It trains attention to early warning signs instead of dismissing unease as nothing.

ramayan::7688.verse_sanskrit: तानि दृष्ट्वा निमित्तानि महाघोराणि राघवः । न्यवर्तताथ त्वरितो जवेनाश्रममात्मनः । । 35713 । ।
ramayan::7688.verse_hindi: On seeing such dreadfu omens at that time, Rama hurried back to his hermitage.
ramayan::7688.english_translation: Seeing those terrible omens, Rama quickly turned back toward his own hermitage.
ramayan::7688.translation_literal: तानि (those) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / निमित्तानि (omens) / महाघोराणि (terrible) / राघवः (Rama) / न्यवर्तत (turned back) / अथ (then) / त्वरितः (quickly) / जवेन (with speed) / आश्रमम् (to the hermitage) / आत्मनः (his own)
ramayan::7688.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7688.essence: He trusted the warning signs and changed direction at once.
ramayan::7688.simple_meaning: Rama sees frightening signs and immediately turns back toward the hermitage.
ramayan::7688.simple_insight: Sometimes the wisest move is to stop and return before things worsen.
ramayan::7688.detailed_meaning: While moving through the forest, Rama notices harsh omens and the cries of animals and birds. He does not push forward blindly. He turns back at once toward his own hermitage, sensing danger before it fully appears.
ramayan::7688.modern_relevance: You step outside and something feels wrong: the air, the silence, the timing. Instead of forcing the plan, you turn back before trouble has a chance to grow.
ramayan::7688.insight: It teaches you to respect warning signs and reverse course before momentum turns costly.

ramayan::7689.verse_sanskrit: सीतां स तु वरारोहां लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम् । आजगाम जनस्थानं चिन्तयन्नेव राघवः । । 35714 । ।
ramayan::7689.verse_hindi: Rama arrived at Janasthana thinking (of the safety) of charming Sita and mighty Lakshmana.
ramayan::7689.english_translation: Rama arrived at Janasthana thinking of the safety of charming Sita and mighty Lakshmana.
ramayan::7689.translation_literal: सीताम् (Sita) / सः (he) / तु (indeed) / वरारोहाम् (the charmingly beautiful one) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / च (and) / महाबलम् (the very strong one) / आजगाम (came) / जनस्थानम् (to Janasthana) / चिन्तयन् (thinking) / एव (only) / राघवः (Raghava/Rama)
ramayan::7689.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7689.essence: His return is driven by worry for the two he loves.
ramayan::7689.simple_meaning: Rama returned to Janasthana while his mind stayed with Sita and Lakshmana. Even in motion, his concern was for their safety.
ramayan::7689.simple_insight: Love keeps watch even when the body is moving on.
ramayan::7689.detailed_meaning: After seeing the dreadful omens, Rama turns back toward Janasthana. He is not thinking of himself or the path ahead; his mind is on Sita and Lakshmana, whose safety now feels urgent in the forest.
ramayan::7689.modern_relevance: You get halfway down the road and suddenly think of the people you left behind. The body keeps moving, but your attention is already with them.
ramayan::7689.insight: It shifts attention from personal movement to protective concern for others.

ramayan::7690.verse_sanskrit: ततो लक्ष्मणमायान्तं ददर्श विगतप्रभम् । ततोऽविदूरे रामेण समीयाय स लक्ष्मणः । । 35715 । । विषण्णस्सुविषण्णेन दुःखितो दुःखभागिना ।
ramayan::7690.verse_hindi: He then saw Lakshmana coming towards him with a cheerless face. When the sad, depressed Lakshmana came near, he saw Rama (equally) despondent and griefstricken.
ramayan::7690.english_translation: He then saw Lakshmana coming toward him with a cheerless face. When the deeply saddened Lakshmana came near, he saw Rama equally despondent and grief-stricken.
ramayan::7690.translation_literal: ततः (then) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / आयान्तम् (coming) / ददर्श (saw) / विगतप्रभम् (without brightness, cheerless) / ततः (then) / अविदूरे (not far away) / रामेण (by Rama) / समीयाय (came near) / सः (he) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / विषण्णः (dejected) / सुविषण्णेन (by the very dejected one) / दुःखितः (grieved) / दुःखभागिना (by the one sharing sorrow)
ramayan::7690.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7690.essence: Shared sorrow can meet before words do.
ramayan::7690.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana meet in shared grief. Each sees the other's sorrow, and that grief deepens the moment.
ramayan::7690.simple_insight: Some pain is so heavy it becomes visible before a word is spoken.
ramayan::7690.detailed_meaning: Rama has rushed back into Janasthana after seeing bad omens. Lakshmana approaches with his own worry already on his face. Before any explanation, the brothers meet in the same sorrow, both carrying the fear of what has happened to Sita.
ramayan::7690.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a bad call, and your brother, partner, or friend already looks wrecked. Before either of you speaks, you both know something has gone wrong.
ramayan::7690.insight: It shows how grief can be shared instantly, without needing explanation.

ramayan::7691.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जगर्हेऽथ तं भ्राता ज्येष्ठो लक्ष्मणमागतम् । । 35716 । । विहाय सीतां विजने वने राक्षससेविते ।
ramayan::7691.verse_hindi: In this situation Rama the elder brother rebuked Lakshmana for having left Sita behind in a desolate forest infested with demons.
ramayan::7691.english_translation: In this situation Rama, the elder brother, rebuked Lakshmana for having left Sita behind in a desolate forest infested with demons.
ramayan::7691.translation_literal: सञ्जगर्हे (rebuked) / अथ (then) / तं (him) / भ्राता (brother) / ज्येष्ठः (elder) / लक्ष्मणम् (Lakshmana) / आगतम् (arrived) / विहाय (having left behind) / सीताम् (Sita) / विजने (desolate) / वने (forest) / राक्षस-सेविते (inhabited by demons)
ramayan::7691.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7691.essence: Leaving someone unprotected can become the wound that changes everything.
ramayan::7691.simple_meaning: Rama rebukes Lakshmana for leaving Sita alone in a lonely forest full of dangerous beings.
ramayan::7691.simple_insight: Love can sound sharp when protection has failed.
ramayan::7691.detailed_meaning: Rama has reached Janasthana and sees Lakshmana return with grief on his face. In that raw moment, the elder brother turns on him for one unbearable fact: Sita was left alone in a wilderness filled with danger. The rebuke carries fear, blame, and helpless love.
ramayan::7691.modern_relevance: You look back and realize someone vulnerable was left alone because you assumed things would be fine. The regret lands before the explanation does.
ramayan::7691.insight: It shows how responsibility sharpens under loss: the mind goes first to who was left unprotected.

ramayan::7692.verse_sanskrit: गृहीत्वा च करं सव्यं लक्ष्मणं रघुनन्दनः । । 35717 । । उवाच मधुरोदर्कमिदं परुषमार्तिमत् ।
ramayan::7692.verse_hindi: Rama, the delight of the Raghus, took hold of Lakshmanas left hand, and in sadness said these sweet harsh words :
ramayan::7692.english_translation: Rama, delight of the Raghu line, took Lakshmana's left hand and, in sorrow, spoke these sweet yet harsh words.
ramayan::7692.translation_literal: गृहीत्वा (having taken hold of) / च (and) / करं (hand) / सव्यं (left) / लक्ष्मणं (Lakshmana) / रघुनन्दनः (Rama, delight of the Raghu line) / उवाच (spoke) / मधुरोदर्कम् (sweet in result / with a gentle ending) / इदम् (this) / परुषम् (harsh) / आर्तिमत् (full of grief)
ramayan::7692.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7692.essence: Grief can make even love sound like reproach.
ramayan::7692.simple_meaning: Rama grips Lakshmana's hand and speaks to him with a voice that is both loving and bitter, driven by grief over Sita's absence.
ramayan::7692.simple_insight: Love can sound severe when fear and sorrow are behind it.
ramayan::7692.detailed_meaning: Rama has just found Lakshmana returning alone after leaving Sita in the forest. Overcome by anguish, he takes Lakshmana's hand and rebukes him. The moment is not teaching a principle but showing grief breaking through brotherly love.
ramayan::7692.modern_relevance: You grab a friend's hand after a terrible mistake and your words come out sharper than you meant. The care is real, but panic is speaking too.
ramayan::7692.insight: It shows how sorrow can turn tenderness into blame in a single breath.

ramayan::7693.verse_sanskrit: अहो लक्ष्मण गर्ह्यं ते कृतं यस्त्वं विहाय ताम् । । 35718 । । सीतामिहाऽगतस्सौम्य कच्चित्स्वस्ति भवेदिह ।
ramayan::7693.verse_hindi: O gentle Lakshmana you are to blame for coming here, leaving Sita behind. Alas will she be safe now?
ramayan::7693.english_translation: O gentle Lakshmana, you are to blame for coming here and leaving Sita behind. Alas, will she be safe now?
ramayan::7693.translation_literal: अहो (alas) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / गर्ह्यम् (blameworthy) / ते (your) / कृतम् (done) / यत् (that) / त्वम् (you) / विहाय (having left) / ताम् (her) / सीताम् (Sita) / इह (here) / आगतः (come) / सौम्य (gentle one) / कच्चित् (whether) / स्वस्ति (safely) / भवेत् (may be) / इह (here)
ramayan::7693.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7693.essence: Grief makes Rama see Lakshmana's return as a failure to protect Sita.
ramayan::7693.simple_meaning: Rama blames Lakshmana for leaving Sita alone and worries whether she is safe in the forest.
ramayan::7693.simple_insight: Love can turn instantly into fear when someone you protect is left exposed.
ramayan::7693.detailed_meaning: Rama has just learned that Lakshmana returned without Sita. In the forest, with danger all around, he turns on his brother in grief and dread. The verse is part of his frantic search for Sita, not a finished teaching.
ramayan::7693.modern_relevance: You step out for ten minutes and realize the child, the phone, or the fragile plan was left unguarded. Panic arrives before logic does.
ramayan::7693.insight: It shows how quickly responsibility becomes fear when someone vulnerable is missing.

ramayan::7694.verse_sanskrit: न मेऽस्ति संशयो वीर सर्वथा जनकात्मजा । । 35719 । । विनष्टा भक्षिता वापि राक्षसैर्वनचारिभिः । अशुभान्येव भूयिष्ठं यथा प्रादुर्भवन्ति मे । । 35720 । ।
ramayan::7694.verse_hindi: O heroic Lakshmana I see many inauspicious omens. I think Sita might have been lost or eaten away by the demons of the forest. There is no doubt about it.
ramayan::7694.english_translation: O heroic Lakshmana, I have no doubt at all that Janaka's daughter has been destroyed, or eaten by the forest-roaming demons. Many inauspicious signs keep appearing to me.
ramayan::7694.translation_literal: न मेऽस्ति (there is not for me) / संशयः (doubt) / वीर (heroic one) / सर्वथा (in every way) / जनकात्मजा (Janaka's daughter) / विनष्टा (destroyed) / भक्षिता (devoured) / वा अपि (or even) / राक्षसैः (by demons) / वनचारिभिः (forest-roaming) / अशुभानि (inauspicious things) / एव (indeed) / भूयिष्ठम् (most abundantly) / यथा (as) / प्रादुर्भवन्ति (appear) / मे (to me)
ramayan::7694.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7694.essence: Fear turns hints into certainty before the facts arrive.
ramayan::7694.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana he is certain Sita has been destroyed or taken by the forest demons, because every sign around him feels ominous.
ramayan::7694.simple_insight: Grief can turn every sign into proof.
ramayan::7694.detailed_meaning: Rama has found only fear and absence in the forest. Holding Lakshmana's hand, he reads every omen as confirmation that Sita is gone. The verse deepens his panic, preparing the search that follows.
ramayan::7694.modern_relevance: You check your phone for one message and find none. Then every silence starts to feel like an answer. Fear can make the mind build certainty from shadows.
ramayan::7694.insight: It shows how anxiety narrows the mind until it mistakes dread for knowledge.

ramayan::7695.verse_sanskrit: अपि लक्ष्मण सीतायास्सामग्र्यं प्राप्नुयावहे । जीवन्त्याः पुरुषव्याघ्र सुताया जनकस्य वै । । 35721 । ।
ramayan::7695.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, a tiger among men, will we be able to see the daughter of Janaka, living in a state of total wellbeing? Will we be able to get her back ?
ramayan::7695.english_translation: O Lakshmana, tiger among men, will we be able to see Janaka's daughter alive and in full wellbeing again?
ramayan::7695.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / सीतायाः (of Sita) / सामग्र्यम् (complete wellbeing) / प्राप्नुयावहे (may we obtain, may we reach) / जीवन्त्याः (of the living) / पुरुषव्याघ्र (tiger among men) / सुतायाः (of the daughter) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / वै (indeed)
ramayan::7695.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7695.essence: Hope is still alive, but fear is already speaking.
ramayan::7695.simple_meaning: Sita is being searched for in the forest, and the speaker wonders whether she is still alive and safe.
ramayan::7695.simple_insight: Fear makes every silence feel like an answer.
ramayan::7695.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are in the forest after Sita's disappearance. The signs around them feel dark, and the speaker voices the deepest fear: whether Janaka's daughter can still be found alive and unharmed. The verse deepens the search with dread, not resolution.
ramayan::7695.modern_relevance: You call a missing person's phone again and again, hoping for one ring. The longer it stays silent, the more your mind fills the gap.
ramayan::7695.insight: It captures how uncertainty turns hope into fear and keeps the mind searching for proof.

ramayan::7696.verse_sanskrit: यथा वै मृगसङ्घाश्च गोमायुश्चैव भैरवम् । वाश्यन्ते शकुनाश्चापि प्रदीप्तामभितो दिशम् । । 35722 । । अपि स्वस्ति भवेत्तस्या राजपुत्र्या महाबल ।
ramayan::7696.verse_hindi: O  mighty Lakshmana  from the way the beasts, jackals and birds too have turned in the bright direction of the Sun, crying in a frightful manner, can we hope princess Sita is safe ?
ramayan::7696.english_translation: O mighty Lakshmana, from the way the beasts, jackals, and birds are crying frightfully toward the bright direction of the sun, can we hope Princess Sita is safe?
ramayan::7696.translation_literal: यथा (as) / वै (indeed) / मृगसङ्घाः (groups of beasts) / च (and) / गोमायुः (jackals) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / भैरवम् (fearfully) / वाश्यन्ते (are crying) / शकुनाः (birds) / च (and) / अपि (also) / प्रदीप्ताम् (bright) / अभितः (around) / दिशम् (the direction) / अपि (perhaps) / स्वस्ति (well-being) / भवेत्तस्या (may there be for her) / राजपुत्र्याः (of the princess) / महाबल (mighty one)
ramayan::7696.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7696.essence: Fearful signs can shake hope, but they cannot prove loss.
ramayan::7696.simple_meaning: Rama notices frightening omens in nature and wonders whether Sita may still be safe. He is reading the world anxiously, searching for any sign that she has survived.
ramayan::7696.simple_insight: Fear can sharpen attention without fully taking away hope.
ramayan::7696.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama and Lakshmana are already straining under uncertainty after Sita’s disappearance. Rama watches jackals, birds, and beasts behaving ominously and asks whether the princess might still be unharmed. The verse shows how grief turns every sign into a question.
ramayan::7696.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone after a message goes unanswered and start reading every silence as evidence. One bad sign can feel like a verdict, even when you still don’t know anything.
ramayan::7696.insight: It teaches you to notice anxiety without letting it become certainty.

ramayan::7697.verse_sanskrit: इदं हि रक्षो मृगसन्निकाशं प्रलोभ्य मां दूरमनुप्रयान्तम् । हतं कथञ्चिन्महता श्रमेण स राक्षसोऽभून्म्रियमाण एव । । 35723 । ।
ramayan::7697.verse_hindi: Appearing in the guise of a deer, this demon allured me to a great distance. With much effort he was somehow killed. but he assumed his demoniac form while dying.
ramayan::7697.english_translation: Appearing in the guise of a deer, this demon lured me far away. I managed to kill him only with great effort, and he died in his true monstrous form.
ramayan::7697.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / हि (indeed) / रक्षः (demon) / मृग-सन्निकाशम् (deer-like) / प्रलोभ्य (having lured) / माम् (me) / दूरम् (far) / अनुप्रयान्तम् (going after) / हतम् (killed) / कथञ्चित् (somehow) / महता (great) / श्रमेण (with effort) / सः (that) / राक्षसः (demon) / अभूत् (became) / म्रियमाणः (dying) / एव (indeed)
ramayan::7697.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7697.essence: A false lure can remove you from the one place you needed to stay.
ramayan::7697.simple_meaning: A demon disguised as a deer drew Rama far away from the others. Rama killed him only after a hard struggle, and the demon revealed his true form while dying.
ramayan::7697.simple_insight: Deception can pull you far from what you were protecting.
ramayan::7697.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha has lured Rama away by taking the form of a golden deer. Rama recalls the trap and the struggle of killing him, because this is the moment that explains how Sita was left exposed and why danger now feels immediate.
ramayan::7697.modern_relevance: You follow a shiny distraction for ten minutes and come back to find the real problem waiting untouched. The cost of being lured away is often paid somewhere else.
ramayan::7697.insight: It shifts attention to how deception creates distance before harm becomes visible.

ramayan::7698.verse_sanskrit: मनश्च मे दीनमिहाप्रहृष्टं चक्षुश्च सव्यं कुरुते विकारम् । असंशयं लक्ष्मण नास्ति सीता हृता मृता वा पथि वर्तते वा । । 35724 । ।
ramayan::7698.verse_hindi: With my heart dejected and depressed, my left eye throbbing, O Lakshmana, I have no doubt that Sita is either abducted or dead or abandoned on the way.
ramayan::7698.english_translation: With my heart dejected and depressed, my left eye throbbing, O Lakshmana, I have no doubt that Sita is either abducted or dead or abandoned on the way.
ramayan::7698.translation_literal: मनः (mind) / च (and) / मे (my) / दीनम् (dejected) / इह (here) / अप्रहृष्टम् (not delighted) / चक्षुः (eye) / च (and) / सव्यम् (left) / कुरुते (does) / विकारम् (disturbance) / असंशयम् (without doubt) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / नास्ति (is not) / सीता (Sita) / हृता (abducted) / मृता (dead) / वा (or) / पथि (on the path) / वर्तते (is staying / wandering) / वा (or)
ramayan::7698.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7698.essence: Distress can warn you that something precious has gone wrong.
ramayan::7698.simple_meaning: Rama feels a deep disturbance in his mind and body. He tells Lakshmana that Sita must have been abducted, killed, or left behind on the road.
ramayan::7698.simple_insight: Grief can show itself before proof arrives.
ramayan::7698.detailed_meaning: After the false deer has lured Rama away, he returns shaken and senses something is terribly wrong. Speaking to Lakshmana, he reads his own disturbed mind and body as signs that Sita is gone, dead, or lost on the path.
ramayan::7698.modern_relevance: You miss one call from someone you love, then notice the silence in your chest before the facts arrive. The body often knows fear before the mind catches up.
ramayan::7698.insight: It teaches you to notice how distress registers in body and thought before certainty appears.

ramayan::7699.verse_sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं दीनं शून्ये दशरथात्मजः । पर्यपृच्छत धर्मात्मा वैदेहीमागतं विना । । 3581 । ।
ramayan::7699.verse_hindi: Rama, son of Dasaratha, the righteous self, saw Lakshmana downcast and dejected. Seeing him  without Sita, Rama enquired:
ramayan::7699.english_translation: Rama, son of Dasaratha, the righteous self, saw Lakshmana downcast and dejected. Seeing him without Sita, Rama asked about Vaidehi.
ramayan::7699.translation_literal: स (he) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / लक्ष्मणं (Lakshmana) / दीनं (downcast, dejected) / शून्ये (in emptiness, alone) / दशरथात्मजः (the son of Dasaratha) / पर्यपृच्छत (asked, inquired) / धर्मात्मा (the righteous one) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi, Sita) / आगतम् (arrived) / विना (without)
ramayan::7699.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7699.essence: Rama sees the absence before he hears the story.
ramayan::7699.simple_meaning: Rama sees Lakshmana looking broken and asks where Sita is.
ramayan::7699.simple_insight: Loss announces itself before words do.
ramayan::7699.detailed_meaning: Rama has returned alone enough to notice what is missing. Lakshmana stands before him, dejected and empty-handed. The sight of his brother without Sita forces the question that confirms Rama’s fear: something has gone terribly wrong.
ramayan::7699.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and know, before anyone speaks, that something is wrong. A face, a silence, an absence tells the truth first.
ramayan::7699.insight: It shows how absence can be read immediately through grief and body language.

ramayan::7700.verse_sanskrit: प्रस्थितं दण्डकारण्यं या मामनुजगाम ह । क्व सा लक्ष्मण वैदेही यां हित्वा त्वमिहागतः । । 3582 । ।
ramayan::7700.verse_hindi: Where is that princess from Videha who accompanied me when I entered Dandaka forest ? Why have you come here leaving her behind ?
ramayan::7700.english_translation: Where is that princess from Videha who accompanied me when I entered Dandaka forest? Why have you come here leaving her behind?
ramayan::7700.translation_literal: प्रस्थितं (having set out) / दण्डकारण्यं (to Dandaka forest) / या (who) / माम् (me) / अनुजगाम (followed) / ह (indeed) / क्व (where) / सा (that) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / वैदेही (the princess from Videha) / याम् (whom) / हित्वा (leaving) / त्वम् (you) / इह (here) / आगतः (have come)
ramayan::7700.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7700.essence: What is most loved is felt most sharply when it disappears.
ramayan::7700.simple_meaning: Rama asks Lakshmana where Sita is, shocked that she is not with him. Her absence tells him something terrible has happened.
ramayan::7700.simple_insight: Love sharpens awareness; when someone matters, their absence becomes immediate and unbearable.
ramayan::7700.detailed_meaning: After Lakshmana returns alone from the forest, Rama sees his grief and asks the question he already fears the answer to. Sita had followed him into Dandaka; now she is missing, and the silence around her becomes the proof of loss.
ramayan::7700.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and know, before anyone speaks, that the person you expected is not coming. The missing chair, the unopened message, the empty side of the bed — absence tells the truth first.
ramayan::7700.insight: It trains the mind to read absence as meaningful, not neutral, and to face loss directly instead of delaying it.

ramayan::7701.verse_sanskrit: राज्यभ्रष्टस्य दीनस्य दण्डकान्परिधावतः । क्व सा दुःखसहाया मे वैदेही तनुमध्यमा । । 3583 । ।
ramayan::7701.verse_hindi: Where is that princess from Videha, a sharer of my sorrows, Sita of slender waist who followed this hapless prince disloged from the kingdom into the Dandaka forest?
ramayan::7701.english_translation: Where is that princess from Videha, a sharer of my sorrows, Sita of slender waist who followed this hapless prince dislodged from the kingdom into the Dandaka forest?
ramayan::7701.translation_literal: राज्यभ्रष्टस्य (of one cast out from the kingdom) / दीनस्य (of the wretched) / दण्डकान् (through Dandaka) / परिधावतः (running about) / क्व (where) / सा (that) / दुःखसहाया (sorrow-sharer) / मे (my) / वैदेही (princess of Videha) / तनुमध्यमा (slender-waisted woman)
ramayan::7701.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7701.essence: Loss hurts most when the one who shared it is gone.
ramayan::7701.simple_meaning: Rama is asking where Sita is, remembering that she shared his hardship and followed him into exile.
ramayan::7701.simple_insight: Love feels most precious when absence makes its companionship visible.
ramayan::7701.detailed_meaning: Rama has found Lakshmana, but Sita is missing. Still reeling from exile, he asks where the woman is who left the palace with him and shared his suffering in the forest. The verse carries the shock of separation.
ramayan::7701.modern_relevance: You come home after a brutal day and instinctively look for the one person who made the day bearable. Their absence doesn't just leave a room empty; it exposes how much you relied on being understood.
ramayan::7701.insight: It shifts attention from the fact of absence to the bond that made endurance possible.

ramayan::7702.verse_sanskrit: यां विना नोत्सहे वीर मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम् । क्व सा प्राणसहाया मे सीता सुरसुतोपमा । । 3584 । ।
ramayan::7702.verse_hindi: O warrior Lakshmana where is that Sita without whom I have no interest to live for a moment, who was like the daughter of a god and a sustainer of my life?
