ramayan::7702.english_translation: O warrior Lakshmana, where is that Sita without whom I have no wish to live even for a moment, that Sita who was like the daughter of a radiant being and the support of my life?
ramayan::7702.translation_literal: यां (whom) / विना (without) / नोत्सहे (I do not wish) / वीर (O warrior) / मुहूर्तम् (for a moment) / अपि (even) / जीवितुम् (to live) / क्व (where) / सा (that) / प्राणसहाया (life-supporting companion) / मे (my) / सीता (Sita) / सुरसुतोपमा (like the daughter of a radiant being)
ramayan::7702.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7702.essence: Without her, even survival feels empty.
ramayan::7702.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that Sita is his life’s support, and without her he cannot bear to live even for a moment.
ramayan::7702.simple_insight: Love can become the very reason life feels livable — and unbearable when absent.
ramayan::7702.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Rama has already lost Sita and is speaking in raw anguish to Lakshmana. He is not debating dharma now; he is confessing how completely Sita has become bound to his breath, making this a cry of separation rather than a lesson in restraint.
ramayan::7702.modern_relevance: You open a chat thread one more time, hoping the name you miss will appear. The day keeps moving, but your mind keeps returning to the person whose absence has changed the shape of everything.
ramayan::7702.insight: It reveals how separation can strip away abstraction and expose the depth of attachment.

ramayan::7703.verse_sanskrit: पतित्वममराणां वा पृथिव्याश्चापि लक्ष्मण । तां विना तपनीयाभां नेच्छेयं जनकात्मजाम् । । 3585 । ।
ramayan::7703.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana I desire no lordship of the gods  or of the entire earth without that daughter of Janaka, that lady of golden complexion.
ramayan::7703.english_translation: O Lakshmana, I would not want the lordship of the gods or even the whole earth without Janaka's daughter, the golden-complexioned one.
ramayan::7703.translation_literal: पतित्वम् (lordship) / अमराणाम् (of the immortals) / वा (or) / पृथिव्याः (of the earth) / च (and) / अपि (even) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana) / ताम् (that one) / विना (without) / तपनीयाभाम् (golden-complexioned) / न इच्छेयम् (I would not desire) / जनकात्मजाम् (Janaka's daughter)
ramayan::7703.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7703.essence: Power is worthless when the heart has already lost what it values most.
ramayan::7703.simple_meaning: Rama says that even the highest power or the whole earth is worthless to him without Sita.
ramayan::7703.simple_insight: Love can make every prize feel hollow when the one you miss is absent.
ramayan::7703.detailed_meaning: Rama, exiled and grieving in the forest, speaks to Lakshmana about Sita. He is not bargaining for comfort or power anymore. Even the rule of the gods or the earth itself cannot replace the one person he has lost.
ramayan::7703.modern_relevance: You got the promotion, the bigger apartment, the title people wanted you to want — and still felt the ache of one missing person. Some victories are too small for the love you carry.
ramayan::7703.insight: It shifts attention from status to attachment, showing that power without love is empty.

ramayan::7704.verse_sanskrit: कच्चिज्जीवति वैदेहि प्राणैः प्रियतरा मम । कच्चित्प्रव्राजनं सौम्य न मे मिथ्या भविष्यति । । 3586 । ।
ramayan::7704.verse_hindi: O gentle Lakshmana I wonder if Vaidehi, who is dearer to me than my life is still alive
ramayan::7704.english_translation: O gentle Lakshmana, I wonder if Vaidehi, who is dearer to me than my life, is still alive. I hope my exile has not been in vain.
ramayan::7704.translation_literal: कच्चित् (whether) / जीवति (is living) / वैदेहि (Vaidehi) / प्राणैः (than life) / प्रियतरा (dearer) / मम (to me) / कच्चित् (whether) / प्रव्राजनं (the exile) / सौम्य (gentle one) / न (not) / मे (my) / मिथ्या (in vain) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::7704.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7704.essence: Love makes exile unbearable, yet still worth enduring.
ramayan::7704.simple_meaning: Rama asks Lakshmana whether Sita is still alive and whether the suffering of exile will have meaning.
ramayan::7704.simple_insight: Love can survive uncertainty, even when all you have is waiting.
ramayan::7704.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are deep in exile, and Rama’s mind keeps returning to Sita. He asks whether she still lives and whether the painful separation has any purpose, showing how grief and love can sit together.
ramayan::7704.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a painful separation, hoping one message will prove the loss meant something. Rama’s question carries that same raw ache.
ramayan::7704.insight: It shifts the mind from numb endurance to honest longing, without pretending the pain is small.

ramayan::7705.verse_sanskrit: सीतानिमित्तं सौमित्रे मृते मयि गते त्वयि । कच्चित्सकामा सुखिता कैकेयी सा भविष्यति । । 3587 । ।
ramayan::7705.verse_hindi: O Saumitri when I am dead on account of Sita, and you are back, Kaikeyi with her desire fulfilled will be happy, indeed.
ramayan::7705.english_translation: O Saumitri, when I am dead because of Sita, and you have returned, will Kaikeyi be happy with her desire fulfilled?
ramayan::7705.translation_literal: सीतानिमित्तं (because of Sita) / सौमित्रे (O Saumitri) / मृते (when dead) / मयि (in me) / गते (having gone) / त्वयि (you) / कच्चित् (whether) / सकामा (with desire fulfilled) / सुखिता (happy) / कैकेयी (Kaikeyi) / सा (she) / भविष्यति (will be)
ramayan::7705.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7705.essence: Fulfilled desire may still leave the heart untouched.
ramayan::7705.simple_meaning: Rama wonders whether Kaikeyi will truly be happy if her wish has cost him his life and sent Lakshmana back.
ramayan::7705.simple_insight: Getting what you want does not always heal what drove you to want it.
ramayan::7705.detailed_meaning: Exiled in the forest, Rama speaks to Lakshmana about the chain Kaikeyi set in motion. Sita is missing, Rama feels as if he may die from the pain, and he wonders whether the queen who demanded his exile will actually feel satisfied.
ramayan::7705.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the move, the victory you pushed so hard for — and the room goes quiet inside you. Rama asks whether getting your wish ever really feeds the hunger that made it.
ramayan::7705.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing desire to questioning whether desire can ever deliver peace.

ramayan::7706.verse_sanskrit: सपुत्रराज्यां सिद्धार्थां मृतपुत्रा तपस्विनी । उपस्थास्यतिकौसल्या कच्चित्सौम्य न केकयीम् । । 3588 । ।
ramayan::7706.verse_hindi: O handsome one  I wonder if that lady of renunciation, Kausalya with her son dead, will have to serve Kaikeyi whose desire would be fulfilled, and who will enjoy the power of the throne in the company of her son
ramayan::7706.english_translation: O handsome one, I wonder if Kausalya, that ascetic woman, with her son dead, will have to serve Kaikeyi, who has achieved her desire and enjoys the throne with her son.
ramayan::7706.translation_literal: सपुत्रराज्यां (with kingdom and son) / सिद्धार्थां (one whose desire is fulfilled) / मृतपुत्रा (with son dead) / तपस्विनी (ascetic woman) / उपस्थास्यति (will serve) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / कच्चित् (whether) / सौम्य (O handsome one) / न (not) / केकयीम् (Kaikeyi)
ramayan::7706.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7706.essence: He fears his mother's grief will be made worse by having to serve her rival.
ramayan::7706.simple_meaning: Rama worries that Kausalya, after losing her son, may be forced to serve Kaikeyi, whose wish has come true and who now holds the power of the throne.
ramayan::7706.simple_insight: Grief deepens when you imagine the humiliation that follows loss.
ramayan::7706.detailed_meaning: Rama is in exile with Lakshmana, and every thought turns back to Ayodhya. He is not only grieving his own banishment; he is imagining the suffering of his mother Kausalya and the triumph of Kaikeyi. The verse carries the ache of a family broken by royal power.
ramayan::7706.modern_relevance: You leave a family meeting and suddenly picture your mother swallowing her hurt while the person who caused it sits at the center of the room. That second wound can hurt more than your own.
ramayan::7706.insight: It shifts attention from personal loss to the social shame that loss can create.

ramayan::7707.verse_sanskrit: यदि जीवति वैदेही गमिष्याम्याश्रमं पुनः । सुवृत्ता यदि वृत्ता प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि लक्ष्मण । । 3589 । ।
ramayan::7707.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, only if Vaidehi is alive will I enter the cottage again or else I will give up
ramayan::7707.english_translation: O Lakshmana, only if Vaidehi is alive will I enter the cottage again; otherwise I will give up my life.
ramayan::7707.translation_literal: यदि (if) / जीवति (is alive) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / गमिष्यामि (I will go) / आश्रमम् (to the cottage) / पुनः (again) / सुवृत्ता (well-conducted) / यदि (if) / वृत्ता (gone) / प्राणान् (life-breaths) / त्यक्ष्यामि (I will give up) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7707.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7707.essence: Without Sita, even home becomes unlivable.
ramayan::7707.simple_meaning: Rama says he will only go back to the hermitage if Sita is alive. If she is dead, he will not continue living.
ramayan::7707.simple_insight: Some losses change what returning even means.
ramayan::7707.detailed_meaning: Rama speaks to Lakshmana in the forest after Sita’s abduction. The hermitage, once their refuge, has become unbearable without her. He ties his own return to her survival, showing how completely his world depends on finding her.
ramayan::7707.modern_relevance: You walk back into a home after a breakup and feel the silence hit before the door closes. The place is still standing, but the life you built there is not.
ramayan::7707.insight: It shifts the mind from routine return to the emotional reality that a place can lose its meaning.

ramayan::7708.verse_sanskrit: यदि मामाश्रमगतं वैदेही नाभिभाषते । पुनः प्रहसिता सीता विनशिष्यामि लक्ष्मण । । 35810 । ।
ramayan::7708.verse_hindi: I will die if Sita, princess from Videha, is not there to speak to me with her sweet smile when I return to the cottage, O Lakshmana
ramayan::7708.english_translation: I will die if Sita, princess from Videha, is not there to speak to me with her sweet smile when I return to the cottage, O Lakshmana.
ramayan::7708.translation_literal: यदि (if) / माम् (me) / आश्रमगतं (returned to the hermitage) / वैदेही (Sita of Videha) / न (not) / अभिभाषते (speaks to) / पुनः (again) / प्रहसिता (smiling) / सीता (Sita) / विनशिष्यामि (I will perish) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana)
ramayan::7708.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7708.essence: A return means nothing if the beloved is missing.
ramayan::7708.simple_meaning: Rama says that returning to the hermitage will mean nothing if Sita is not there to greet him with her smile.
ramayan::7708.simple_insight: Love can make even a safe place feel empty when the beloved is missing.
ramayan::7708.detailed_meaning: Exiled in the forest, Rama is speaking to Lakshmana with Sita still unaccounted for. He imagines returning to the hermitage and finding no smile, no voice, no presence waiting for him. That absence would feel like death.
ramayan::7708.modern_relevance: You come home after a brutal day and the one person who usually softens the room isn't there. The chair is the same, the house is the same, but the place that felt alive suddenly feels hollow.
ramayan::7708.insight: It shifts attention from location to presence: a home is defined by who receives you there.

ramayan::7709.verse_sanskrit: ब्रूहि लक्ष्मण वैदेही यदि जीवति वा न वा । त्वयि प्रमत्ते रक्षोभिर्भक्षिता वा तपस्विनी । । 35811 । ।
ramayan::7709.verse_hindi: Tell me, O Lakshmana   if Sita is alive or not, whether she was eaten up by demons when you were off your guard.
ramayan::7709.english_translation: Tell me, O Lakshmana, whether Vaidehi is alive or not, whether the ascetic woman was devoured by demons when you were off your guard.
ramayan::7709.translation_literal: ब्रूहि (tell) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / यदि (whether) / जीवति (is alive) / वा (or) / न (not) / वा (or) / त्वयि (while you) / प्रमत्ते (were negligent) / रक्षोभिः (by demons) / भक्षिता (devoured) / वा (or) / तपस्विनी (the ascetic woman)
ramayan::7709.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7709.essence: Love under threat becomes unbearable uncertainty.
ramayan::7709.simple_meaning: Rama anxiously asks Lakshmana whether Sita is still alive or has been taken by demons while Lakshmana was careless.
ramayan::7709.simple_insight: Grief makes the mind leap to the worst possible ending.
ramayan::7709.detailed_meaning: Rama is searching for Sita after her abduction. Facing Lakshmana, he cannot bear uncertainty and asks whether she lives or has been killed by demons while Lakshmana was distracted. The verse carries raw panic, not teaching.
ramayan::7709.modern_relevance: You miss one call and your mind fills the silence with disaster. Love can turn a few unanswered minutes into a whole tragedy.
ramayan::7709.insight: It shows how fear can convert absence into catastrophe before any facts are known.

ramayan::7710.verse_sanskrit: सुकुमारी च बाला च नित्यं चादुःखदर्शिनी । मद्वियोगेन वैदेही व्यक्तं शोचति दुर्मनाः । । 35812 । ।
ramayan::7710.verse_hindi: Vaidehi is delicate, young and she has never faced any sorrow.She will be certainly disheartened due to separation from me.
ramayan::7710.english_translation: Vaidehi is delicate, young, and unused to sorrow. Separated from me, she is surely grieving in distress.
ramayan::7710.translation_literal: सुकुमारी (delicate) / च (and) / बाला (young girl) / च (and) / नित्यं (always) / चादुःखदर्शिनी (one who has never seen sorrow) / मद्वियोगेन (by separation from me) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / व्यक्तं (clearly) / शोचति (grieves) / दुर्मनाः (distressed in mind)
ramayan::7710.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7710.essence: Distance hurts most when the heart is already tender.
ramayan::7710.simple_meaning: Sita is young, gentle, and unaccustomed to hardship. Rama believes that being apart from him is surely making her miserable.
ramayan::7710.simple_insight: Love notices vulnerability before it notices itself.
ramayan::7710.detailed_meaning: Rama, stricken by uncertainty in the forest, is trying to imagine Sita's condition after Lakshmana left her alone. He knows her tenderness and inexperience with suffering, so he concludes that separation itself must be breaking her spirit.
ramayan::7710.modern_relevance: You wait for a message that never comes, and your mind goes straight to the person you love most. You know their silence may be carrying more pain than yours.
ramayan::7710.insight: It shifts attention from your own fear to the hidden cost your absence may be causing someone else.

ramayan::7711.verse_sanskrit: सर्वदा रक्षसा तेन जिह्मेन सुदुरात्मना । वदता लक्ष्मणेत्युच्चैस्तवापि जनितं भयम् । । 35813 । ।
ramayan::7711.verse_hindi: The evilminded, wicked demon calling out loudly O Lakshmana must have by all means instilled fear in your mind.
ramayan::7711.english_translation: The evil-minded, crooked demon, calling out loudly “Lakshmana,” must have frightened you too.
ramayan::7711.translation_literal: सर्वदा (always) / रक्षसा (by the demon) / तेन (by that) / जिह्मेन (crooked) / सुदुरात्मना (very evil-minded) / वदता (speaking) / लक्ष्मणेत्युच्चैः (Laxmana, loudly) / तव (your) / अपि (also) / जनितं (caused) / भयम् (fear)
ramayan::7711.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7711.essence: A false cry can break your judgment before you notice.
ramayan::7711.simple_meaning: Rama assumes that a demon called out to Lakshmana in order to frighten him and separate him from Sita.
ramayan::7711.simple_insight: Fear can be planted by a single voice at the wrong moment.
ramayan::7711.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is trying to understand why Lakshmana left Sita alone. He imagines Ravana’s trick: a false cry using Lakshmana’s name, meant to stir panic and pull Lakshmana away. This is part of Rama’s growing anguish.
ramayan::7711.modern_relevance: You hear your name shouted in panic from another room, and your body moves before your mind does. This verse captures how easily fear can hijack judgment.
ramayan::7711.insight: It shows how manipulation works by triggering urgent instinct before clear thought.

ramayan::7712.verse_sanskrit: श्रुतस्तु शङ्के वैदेह्या स स्वरस्सदृशो मम । त्रस्तया प्रेषितस्त्वं च द्रष्टुं मां शीघ्रमागतः । । 35814 । ।
ramayan::7712.verse_hindi: I am afraid, Vaidehi, frightened by hearing the voice which was like mine sent you to see me, and you came all at once.
ramayan::7712.english_translation: I suspect that, frightened by hearing a voice like mine, Vaidehi sent you to see me, and you came quickly.
ramayan::7712.translation_literal: श्रुतः (heard) / तु (but) / शङ्के (I suspect) / वैदेह्या (by Vaidehi) / सः (that) / स्वरः (voice) / सदृशः (like) / मम (mine) / त्रस्तया (by the frightened one) / प्रेषितः (sent) / त्वं (you) / च (and) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / माम् (me) / शीघ्रम् (quickly) / आगतः (came)
ramayan::7712.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7712.essence: A false voice can move you before doubt wakes up.
ramayan::7712.simple_meaning: Ravana thinks Sita heard a voice that sounded like his and sent someone to check on him. He assumes fear and quick movement on her part.
ramayan::7712.simple_insight: Fear can make a false signal feel completely real.
ramayan::7712.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking after Sita has been deceived by a voice that mimicked Rama's. He is trying to explain why she reacted so quickly, revealing both his manipulation and his awareness that the trick worked.
ramayan::7712.modern_relevance: You hear a message that sounds exactly like someone you trust, and you react before thinking. A fake signal can move you faster than the truth.
ramayan::7712.insight: It shows how imitation and fear can override judgment in a single moment.

ramayan::7713.verse_sanskrit: सर्वथा तु कृतं कष्टं सीतामुत्सृजता वने । प्रतिकर्तुं नृशंसानां रक्षसां दत्तमन्तरं । । 35815 । ।
ramayan::7713.verse_hindi: You have definitely done a great mistake by leaving Sita alone in the forest. This has given a chance to the cruel demons to wreak revenge.
ramayan::7713.english_translation: You have definitely done a great mistake by leaving Sita alone in the forest. This has given a chance to the cruel demons to wreak revenge.
ramayan::7713.translation_literal: सर्वथा (certainly) / तु (indeed) / कृतं (done) / कष्टं (a grievous wrong) / सीताम् (Sita) / उत्सृजता (by leaving) / वने (in the forest) / प्रतिकर्तुं (to retaliate) / नृशंसानाम् (of the cruel ones) / रक्षसाम् (of the demons) / दत्तम् (given) / अन्तरम् (an opening)
ramayan::7713.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7713.essence: Leaving someone unprotected can create the very harm you feared.
ramayan::7713.simple_meaning: Ravana says that leaving Sita alone in the forest was a terrible error, because it gave the demons room to strike back.
ramayan::7713.simple_insight: A careless choice can create danger you never meant to invite.
ramayan::7713.detailed_meaning: After Sita is left alone in the forest, Ravana turns that abandonment into blame and threat. He sees the opening it created for the demons’ revenge, and the moment becomes a grim warning about what neglect can unleash.
ramayan::7713.modern_relevance: You leave someone vulnerable and tell yourself it will be fine. Later, the consequences arrive through the exact gap you ignored.
ramayan::7713.insight: It sharpens attention to the cost of leaving responsibility unfinished.

ramayan::7714.verse_sanskrit: दुःखिताः खरघातेन राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः । तैस्सीता निहता घोरैर्भविष्यति न संशयः । 35816 । ।
ramayan::7714.verse_hindi: The dreadful, carnivorous demons aggrieved over my murder of Khara must have undoubtedly killed Sita.
ramayan::7714.english_translation: The dreadful, flesh-eating demons, angered by my killing of Khara, must surely have killed Sita.
ramayan::7714.translation_literal: दुःखिताः (grieved) / खरघातेन (by the killing of Khara) / राक्षसाः (demons) / पिशिताशनाः (flesh-eaters) / तैः (by them) / सीता (Sita) / निहता (killed) / घोरैः (by the dreadful ones) / भविष्यति (will have happened / must have happened) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
ramayan::7714.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7714.essence: Panic turns uncertainty into a fatal story.
ramayan::7714.simple_meaning: Ravana assumes that the demons, furious over Khara’s death, have probably killed Sita.
ramayan::7714.simple_insight: Fear can turn a mind into a courtroom, where every guess feels like proof.
ramayan::7714.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just learned of Khara’s death and the danger around Sita. Instead of seeing clearly, he leaps to the worst conclusion: that the enraged demons have already killed her. The verse shows panic overtaking judgment.
ramayan::7714.modern_relevance: You get one alarming message and your mind finishes the whole disaster before lunch. Fear fills the gaps with certainty.
ramayan::7714.insight: It shows how grief and fear can distort judgment into instant catastrophe.

ramayan::7715.verse_sanskrit: अहोऽस्मिन् व्यसने मग्नस्सर्वथा शत्रुसूदन । किं न्विदानीं करिष्यामि शङ्के प्राप्तव्यमीदृशम् । । 35817 । ।
ramayan::7715.verse_hindi: O destroyer of enemies  I am completely drowned in sorrow. What can I do at this moment. Alas, I am destined to suffer.
ramayan::7715.english_translation: O destroyer of enemies, I am completely drowned in sorrow. What can I do at this moment? Alas, I fear this suffering has come upon me.
ramayan::7715.translation_literal: अहो (alas) / अस्मिन् (in this) / व्यसने (calamity, distress) / मग्नः (submerged) / सर्वथा (completely) / शत्रु-सूदन (destroyer of enemies) / किं (what) / नु (indeed) / इदानीम् (now) / करिष्यामि (shall I do) / शङ्के (I fear, I suspect) / प्राप्तव्यम् (to be encountered) / ईदृशम् (such)
ramayan::7715.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7715.essence: Love can turn victory into panic in a single breath.
ramayan::7715.simple_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by fear that Sita has been killed and feels helpless about what to do next.
ramayan::7715.simple_insight: Even the strongest heart can be shaken when love is at risk.
ramayan::7715.detailed_meaning: After killing Khara, Rama suddenly fears that the enraged demons may have killed Sita in revenge. He is thrown into helpless grief, asking what he can possibly do now. The verse captures a crisis of fear before action resumes.
ramayan::7715.modern_relevance: You check your phone and see no reply after the argument. Your mind fills the silence with the worst possibility, and for a moment you cannot think straight.
ramayan::7715.insight: It shows how fear can collapse clear action into helpless imagining.

ramayan::7716.verse_sanskrit: इति सीतां वरारोहां चिन्तयन्नेव राघवः । आजगाम जनस्थानं त्वरया सह लक्ष्मणः । । 35818 । ।
ramayan::7716.verse_hindi: While thus brooding over the beautiful Sita, the scion of the Raghus along with Lakshmana hurried towards Janasthana.
ramayan::7716.english_translation: While thus brooding over the beautiful Sita, the scion of the Raghus along with Lakshmana hurried towards Janasthana.
ramayan::7716.translation_literal: इति (thus) / सीतां (Sita) / वरारोहां (beautifully built) / चिन्तयन् (brooding over) / एव (indeed) / राघवः (Raghava) / आजगाम (came) / जनस्थानम् (to Janasthana) / त्वरया (hastily) / सह (together with) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7716.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7716.essence: Grief drives him onward before he knows the truth.
ramayan::7716.simple_meaning: Rama, worried about Sita, quickly reached Janasthana with Lakshmana.
ramayan::7716.simple_insight: Grief can narrow your world to one urgent search.
ramayan::7716.detailed_meaning: After fearing that Sita has been killed, Rama cannot stay still. With Lakshmana beside him, he rushes toward Janasthana, driven by worry and the need to find her. This is a movement scene, not a teaching moment.
ramayan::7716.modern_relevance: You replay one bad possibility in your mind and start moving before you have proof. The body follows the fear long before the facts arrive.
ramayan::7716.insight: It shows how worry can push action forward before certainty exists.

ramayan::7717.verse_sanskrit: विगर्हमाणोऽनुजमार्तरूपं क्षुधा श्रमाच्चैव पिपासया च । विनिश्श्वसन् शुष्कमुखो विवर्णः प्रतिश्रयं प्राप्य समीक्ष्य शून्यम् । । 35819 । । स्वमाश्रमं सम्प्रविगाह्य वीरो विहारदेशाननुसृत्य कांश्चित् । एतत्तदित्येव निवासभूमौ प्रहृष्टरोमा व्यथितो बभूव । । 35820 । ।
ramayan::7717.verse_hindi: Thus blaming his dejected brother, the valiant Rama entered the hermitage, sighing deeply, his face pale and his throat dried up with hunger, exhaustion and thirst. Reaching his dwellingplace, he found it empty. He thoroughly searched the hermitage and the places where she used to move about on the premises. And so it has happened, he sadly said to himself, his hair raised on end.
ramayan::7717.english_translation: Thus blaming his dejected brother, the valiant Rama entered the hermitage, sighing deeply, his face pale and his throat dried up with hunger, exhaustion and thirst. Reaching his dwellingplace, he found it empty. He thoroughly searched the hermitage and the places where she used to move about on the premises. And so it has happened, he sadly said to himself, his hair raised on end.
ramayan::7717.translation_literal: विगर्हमाणः (blaming) / अनुजम् (his younger brother) / आर्तरूपम् (in a distressed state) / क्षुधा (by hunger) / श्रमात् (from fatigue) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / पिपासया (by thirst) / च (and) / विनिश्श्वसन् (sighing deeply) / शुष्कमुखः (dry-faced) / विवर्णः (pale) / प्रतिश्रयम् (to the dwelling) / प्राप्य (having reached) / समीक्ष्य (having seen) / शून्यम् (empty) / स्वम् (his own) / आश्रमम् (hermitage) / सम्प्रगाह्य (entering thoroughly) / वीरः (the hero) / विहारदेशान् (the places of wandering) / अनुसृत्य (following) / कांश्चित् (some) / एतत् तत् इति एव (it must be that) / निवासभूमौ (in the dwelling place) / प्रहृष्टरोमा (with hair standing on end) / व्यथितः (distressed) / बभूव (became)
ramayan::7717.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7717.essence: The empty place tells him what words cannot.
ramayan::7717.simple_meaning: Rama enters the empty hermitage, exhausted and shaken, searches for Sita everywhere, and realizes she is gone.
ramayan::7717.simple_insight: Some losses are understood first by the body, before the mind can accept them.
ramayan::7717.detailed_meaning: After failing to find Sita, Rama and Lakshmana rush back to the hermitage. Rama is hungry, thirsty, and furious with grief, but the place is empty. He searches the paths she used to walk and understands the truth before anyone says it aloud.
ramayan::7717.modern_relevance: You come home after a brutal day and know something is wrong before anyone speaks. The silence in the room tells you first.
ramayan::7717.insight: It turns grief into recognition: the absence itself becomes the message, and the mind is forced to face what the heart already knows.

ramayan::7718.verse_sanskrit: अथाश्रमादुपावृत्तमन्तरा रघुनन्दनः । परिपप्रच्छ सौमित्रिं रामो दुःखार्दितं पुनः । । 3591 । ।
ramayan::7718.verse_hindi: Rama, the delight of the Raghus, once again questioned Lakshmana who had come out of the hermitage, deeply hurt:
ramayan::7718.english_translation: Rama, the delight of the Raghus, once again questioned Lakshmana who had come out of the hermitage, deeply hurt:
ramayan::7718.translation_literal: अथ (then) / आश्रमात् (from the hermitage) / उपावृत्तम् (having returned) / अन्तराः (within) / रघुनन्दनः (the delight of the Raghus) / परिपप्रच्छ (questioned repeatedly) / सौमित्रिम् (Lakshmana) / रामः (Rama) / दुःख-आर्दितम् (afflicted by sorrow) / पुनः (again)
ramayan::7718.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7718.essence: Pain makes Rama question the one beside him.
ramayan::7718.simple_meaning: Rama turns back from the hermitage and questions Lakshmana again, while Lakshmana is already in pain and sorrow.
ramayan::7718.simple_insight: Grief makes even a simple question carry blame.
ramayan::7718.detailed_meaning: After reaching the hermitage and finding it empty, Rama turns back to Lakshmana, who has returned in distress. The search for Sita has become urgent and painful, and Rama’s questioning now carries the weight of fear and accusation.
ramayan::7718.modern_relevance: You come home shaken, and the first question lands like blame instead of comfort. When fear is running the room, even concern can sound like accusation.
ramayan::7718.insight: It shows how panic can distort speech and turn care into reproach.

ramayan::7719.verse_sanskrit: तमुवाच किमर्थं त्वमागतोऽपास्य मैथिलीम् । यदा सा तव विश्वासाद्वने विरहिता मया । । 3592 । ।
ramayan::7719.verse_hindi: Why did you come, leaving the princess from Mithila alone in the forest when I had left her under your trust ?
ramayan::7719.english_translation: Why did you come, leaving the princess from Mithila alone in the forest when I had left her under your trust?
ramayan::7719.translation_literal: तम् (him) / उवाच (said) / किमर्थं (for what reason) / त्वम् (you) / आगतः (came) / अपास्य (having left behind) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili) / यदा (when) / सा (she) / तव (your) / विश्वासात् (trust) / वने (in the forest) / विरहिता (separated, left alone) / मया (by me)
ramayan::7719.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7719.essence: Broken trust makes loss feel personal, immediate, and unforgivable.
ramayan::7719.simple_meaning: Rama asks Lakshmana why he left Sita alone in the forest after Rama had placed her under his care.
ramayan::7719.simple_insight: Trust is not abstract; when it is broken, the hurt is immediate and personal.
ramayan::7719.detailed_meaning: Rama has returned to the hermitage and found Sita missing. Shaken and grieving, he turns to Lakshmana and asks why he left her unprotected after Rama had entrusted her to him. The verse carries the first shock of loss.
ramayan::7719.modern_relevance: You asked someone to stay with a parent, a child, or a vulnerable friend, and they walked away. The anger is not just about the outcome — it is about trust that should have held.
ramayan::7719.insight: It shifts attention from blame in general to the specific failure of entrusted care.

ramayan::7720.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वैवाभ्यागतं त्वां मे मैथिलीं त्यज्य लक्ष्मण । शङ्कमानं महत्पापं यत्सत्यं व्यथितं मनः । । 3593 । ।
ramayan::7720.verse_hindi: When I saw you, O Lakshmana, coming without Sita, my mind was oppressed with evil thought which have come true.
ramayan::7720.english_translation: When I saw you, O Lakshmana, coming without Sita, my mind was oppressed by a terrible fear that proved true.
ramayan::7720.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / एव (indeed) / अभ्यागतम् (arrived) / त्वाम् (you) / मे (my) / मैथिलीम् (Sita) / त्यज्य (having left) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / शङ्कमानम् (suspicious / fearing) / महत्पापम् (great evil) / यत् (which) / सत्यम् (true) / व्यथितम् (distressed) / मनः (mind)
ramayan::7720.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7720.essence: A feared loss becomes real the moment he sees Lakshmana alone.
ramayan::7720.simple_meaning: Rama says that seeing Lakshmana return without Sita filled him with dread, and that dread turned out to be right.
ramayan::7720.simple_insight: Some fears are not imagination; they are the mind sensing a real loss before it is spoken.
ramayan::7720.detailed_meaning: Rama sees Lakshmana return from the hermitage alone. In that instant, before any explanation, he feels that something terrible has happened to Sita. This verse captures the shock of intuition becoming knowledge.
ramayan::7720.modern_relevance: You hear footsteps at the door and know, before the words come, that something has gone wrong. The mind sometimes catches reality a moment before the facts arrive.
ramayan::7720.insight: It teaches you to notice when intuition is warning you, instead of dismissing every uneasy feeling as overthinking.

ramayan::7721.verse_sanskrit: स्फुरते नयनं सव्यं बाहुश्च हृदयं च मे । दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मण दूरे त्वां सीताविरहितं पथि । । 3594 । ।
ramayan::7721.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, as I saw you from a distance without Sita, my left eye, my shoulder and my heart throbbed.
ramayan::7721.english_translation: O Lakshmana, as I saw you from a distance without Sita, my left eye, my shoulder and my heart throbbed.
ramayan::7721.translation_literal: स्फुरते (throbs) / नयनम् (eye) / सव्यं (left) / बाहुः (shoulder/arm) / च (and) / हृदयम् (heart) / च (and) / मे (my) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / दूरे (from afar) / त्वाम् (you) / सीता-विरहितम् (deprived of Sita) / पथि (on the path)
ramayan::7721.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7721.essence: The body can feel loss before the mind can name it.
ramayan::7721.simple_meaning: Rama sees Lakshmana return without Sita and feels a painful omen in his body. The sight confirms his fear that something terrible has happened.
ramayan::7721.simple_insight: When fear is real, the body often knows before the mind is ready.
ramayan::7721.detailed_meaning: Rama stands waiting for news in the forest. Lakshmana appears on the path alone, and the sight strikes Rama like a wound. His body trembles before the full truth is spoken: Sita is gone.
ramayan::7721.modern_relevance: You spot a loved one walking toward you with an empty look and no explanation. Before anyone speaks, your body already knows something has gone wrong.
ramayan::7721.insight: It shows how grief announces itself before facts are confirmed.

ramayan::7722.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तन्तु सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणश्शुभलक्षणः । भूयो दुःखसमाविष्टो दुःखितं राममब्रवीत् । । 3595 । ।
ramayan::7722.verse_hindi: Thus addressed, virtuous Lakshmana, overwhelmed with sorrow replied to the grief stricken Rama:
ramayan::7722.english_translation: Thus addressed, virtuous Lakshmana, overwhelmed with sorrow replied to the grief stricken Rama:
ramayan::7722.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्तम् (spoken) / तु (then) / सौमित्रिः (Lakshmana) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / शुभलक्षणः (of auspicious marks) / भूयः (again) / दुःखसमाविष्टः (filled with sorrow) / दुःखितम् (grief-stricken) / रामम् (to Rama) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7722.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7722.essence: Even the answer comes burdened when love has already been wounded.
ramayan::7722.simple_meaning: Lakshmana, already grieving, answered Rama in deep sorrow.
ramayan::7722.simple_insight: Pain can make even a loyal heart speak carefully and heavily.
ramayan::7722.detailed_meaning: After seeing Lakshmana return without Sita, Rama is shaken by fear and grief. Lakshmana, himself broken by the situation, answers his brother with the weight of someone trying to explain an unbearable truth.
ramayan::7722.modern_relevance: You get a message that something has gone terribly wrong, and the person who brings it is almost as shaken as you are. The conversation itself carries the wound.
ramayan::7722.insight: It prepares the next explanation by showing that Lakshmana speaks from grief, not indifference.

ramayan::7723.verse_sanskrit: न स्वयं कामकारेण तां त्यक्त्वाहमिहागतः । प्रचोदित स्तयैवोग्रैस्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः । । 3596 । ।
ramayan::7723.verse_hindi: I did not leave her on my own nor have I  come here of my own accord. I came to you,
ramayan::7723.english_translation: I did not leave her of my own will, nor did I come here on my own. I came to you, driven by those fierce words.
ramayan::7723.translation_literal: न (not) / स्वयम् (by myself) / कामकारेण (according to desire) / ताम् (her) / त्यक्त्वा (having left) / अहम् (I) / इह (here) / आगतः (come) । / प्रचोदितः (driven) / तया (by her) / एव (indeed) / उग्रैः (fierce) / त्वत्सकाशम् (to your presence) / इह (here) / आगतः (come) ।
ramayan::7723.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7723.essence: A terrible choice can still be made under pressure, not from betrayal.
ramayan::7723.simple_meaning: Lakshmana insists that he did not abandon Sita willingly. He says her fierce cries pushed him to come to Rama instead.
ramayan::7723.simple_insight: Not every painful choice is a betrayal; sometimes you are pulled by forces you did not choose.
ramayan::7723.detailed_meaning: Rama, shattered by grief, accuses Lakshmana after seeing him return without Sita. Lakshmana answers with anguish: he did not leave her by choice, but came only because of the terrible cries he heard. The verse defends his loyalty while deepening the tragedy.
ramayan::7723.modern_relevance: You replay the moment you walked away from a hard conversation, wondering if you failed someone. Sometimes you left because another crisis was already pulling you elsewhere.
ramayan::7723.insight: It shifts blame from deliberate neglect to a tragic collision of duties and circumstances.

ramayan::7724.verse_sanskrit: आर्येणेव पराक्रुष्टं हासीते लक्ष्मणेति च । परित्राहीति यद्वाक्यं मैथिल्यास्तच्छ्रुतिं गतम् । । 3597 । ।
ramayan::7724.verse_hindi: Uttered loudly, Alas Sita, Alas, Lakshmana, save me, as if these were the words of your noble self, reached Sitas ears.
ramayan::7724.english_translation: Uttered loudly, "Alas, Sita! Alas, Lakshmana! Save me!" as if these were your own words, reached Sita's ears.
ramayan::7724.translation_literal: आर्येणेव (as if by the noble one) / पराक्रुष्टं (shouted loudly) / हासीते (Alas, Sita) / लक्ष्मणेति (Lakshmana, thus) / च (and) / परित्राहीति (save me) / यद्वाक्यं (which words) / मैथिल्याः (of the princess from Mithila) / तत् (those) / श्रुतिं गतम् (reached the ears)
ramayan::7724.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7724.essence: Fearful words can sound like truth when panic takes over.
ramayan::7724.simple_meaning: Sita heard a cry that sounded like her own voice calling for Lakshmana to save her.
ramayan::7724.simple_insight: A voice can carry fear so clearly that it reaches across distance and confusion.
ramayan::7724.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana explains that the cry of distress, calling out for Sita and Lakshmana and begging for rescue, reached Sita's ears. The verse is part of his account of how he was driven away from her by her terrified words.
ramayan::7724.modern_relevance: You hear panic in a loved one's voice and mistake it for certainty. In that moment, fear itself starts steering the next choice.
ramayan::7724.insight: It shows how distress can distort perception and push people into immediate, irreversible action.

ramayan::7725.verse_sanskrit: सा तमार्तस्वरं श्रुत्वा तव स्नेहेन मैथिली । गच्छ गच्छेति मामाह रुदन्ती भयविह्वला । । 3598 । ।
ramayan::7725.verse_hindi: The princess from Mithila heard this cry of pain and, wild with fear, urged me out of her love for you to go.
ramayan::7725.english_translation: The princess from Mithila heard this cry of pain and, wild with fear, urged me out of her love for you to go.
ramayan::7725.translation_literal: सा (she) / तम् (that) / आर्तस्वरम् (cry of pain) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तव (your) / स्नेहेन (out of love) / मैथिली (the princess from Mithila) / गच्छ (go) / गच्छेति (saying “go, go”) / माम् (me) / आह (said) / रुदन्ती (weeping) / भयविह्वला (overwhelmed by fear)
ramayan::7725.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7725.essence: Her fear and love made her send him back at once.
ramayan::7725.simple_meaning: Sita heard the cry of distress, panicked for Rama's safety, and told Hanuman to go back to him.
ramayan::7725.simple_insight: Love can make fear speak first, even before thought catches up.
ramayan::7725.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman explains to Rama how Sita reacted when she heard the cry of distress. Overcome by fear and love, she urged him to return at once. The verse is a small but revealing detail in Hanuman's report, not the main teaching.
ramayan::7725.modern_relevance: You hear bad news about someone you love and your first words come out before your mind can steady itself.
ramayan::7725.insight: It shows how devotion can become urgent speech under pressure, revealing the depth of Sita's concern for Rama.

ramayan::7726.verse_sanskrit: प्रचोद्यमानेन मया गच्छेति बहुशस्तया । प्रत्युक्ता मैथिली वाक्यमिदं त्वत्प्रत्ययान्वितम् । 3599 । ।
ramayan::7726.verse_hindi: When I was repeated asked to go, I said this in order to instil confidence in the princess from Mithila :
ramayan::7726.english_translation: When I was repeatedly urged to go, I replied with these words to give the princess from Mithila confidence:
ramayan::7726.translation_literal: प्रचोद्यमानेन (being repeatedly urged) / मया (by me) / गच्छेति (to go) / बहुशस् (many times) / तया (by her) / प्रत्युक्ता (answered) / मैथिली (the princess from Mithila) / वाक्यम् (speech) / इदम् (this) / त्वत्प्रत्ययान्वितम् (endowed with trust in you)
ramayan::7726.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7726.essence: He speaks to restore trust before he speaks the truth.
ramayan::7726.simple_meaning: He answered Sita again and again, speaking in a way that would calm her and restore her trust.
ramayan::7726.simple_insight: Sometimes the kindest words are the ones meant to steady someone else’s fear.
ramayan::7726.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita is shaken by fear and urging him to leave. The speaker keeps answering her, not to debate, but to calm her heart. This line is the setup for his reassurance that Rama is beyond danger.
ramayan::7726.modern_relevance: Someone you love is spiraling, and you keep repeating the same calm words because panic does not need facts first — it needs steadiness.
ramayan::7726.insight: It shows how reassurance can be an act of care, not just information.

ramayan::7727.verse_sanskrit: न तत्पश्याम्यहं रक्षो यदस्य भयमावहेत् । निर्वृता भव नास्त्येतत्केनाप्येवमुदाहृतम् । । 35910 । ।
ramayan::7727.verse_hindi: No one  can cause fear in Rama. I do not see any demon who can hold a threat to him. Give up fear. Some one might have said it.
ramayan::7727.english_translation: No demon can frighten Rama. Be calm; no one has ever said such a thing to him.
ramayan::7727.translation_literal: न (not) / तत् (that) / पश्यामि (I see) / अहम् (I) / रक्षः (demon) / यत् (which) / अस्य (of him) / भयम् (fear) / आवहेत् (would cause) । / निर्वृता (at ease) / भव (be) / न (not) / अस्ति (there is) / एतत् (this) / केनापि (by anyone) / एवम् (thus) / उदाहृतम् (spoken)
ramayan::7727.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7727.essence: Rama is beyond the fear Sita imagines.
ramayan::7727.simple_meaning: Hanuman reassures Sita that no demon can frighten Rama, and that she should stop fearing for him.
ramayan::7727.simple_insight: Fear eases when you remember who is truly beyond threat.
ramayan::7727.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Hanuman is answering Sita’s anxious question about Rama’s safety. He reassures her that no demon can threaten Rama and tells her to set aside fear. This line supports his larger promise that Rama will come.
ramayan::7727.modern_relevance: You spiral after a message goes unanswered, imagining the worst. Sometimes the fear is bigger than the facts, and a steady voice is enough to bring you back.
ramayan::7727.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to confidence by naming the threat as unreal.

ramayan::7728.verse_sanskrit: विगर्हितं च नीचं च कथमार्योऽभिधास्यति । त्राहीति वचनं सीते यस्त्रायेत्रिदशानपि । । 35911 । ।
ramayan::7728.verse_hindi: How can Rama who is capable of saving even gods speak such unworthy, demeaning words, Save me, O Sita
ramayan::7728.english_translation: How can Rama, who can save even the radiant beings, speak such unworthy, demeaning words: 'Save me, O Sita'?
ramayan::7728.translation_literal: विगर्हितं (unworthy) / च (and) / नीचं (low, base) / च (and) / कथम् (how) / आर्यः (the noble one) / अभिधास्यति (would speak) / त्राहि (save) / इति (thus) / वचनं (the words) / सीते (O Sita) / यः (who) / त्रायेत् (could save) / त्रिदशान् (the radiant beings) / अपि (even)
ramayan::7728.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7728.essence: Falsehood survives by wearing the shape of trust.
ramayan::7728.simple_meaning: Ravana is mocking the idea that Rama would ever cry out for help. He says a noble, powerful man who could protect even the radiant beings would never speak such a humiliating plea.
ramayan::7728.simple_insight: Pride can twist even obvious truth into denial.
ramayan::7728.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to keep his deception alive by speaking through a false voice. He argues that Rama, the man Sita trusts, would never beg for rescue. The line is part of a larger trick meant to shake her confidence.
ramayan::7728.modern_relevance: You hear a voice message that sounds like someone you love, but the tone is wrong. Your mind wants to believe it anyway. That split second is where manipulation works.
ramayan::7728.insight: It shows how a liar borrows trust by imitating the voice of someone beloved.

ramayan::7729.verse_sanskrit: किं निमित्तं तु केनापि भ्रातुरालम्ब्य मे स्वरम् । राक्षसेनेरितं वाक्यं त्राहि त्राहीति शोभने । । 35912 । ।
ramayan::7729.verse_hindi: O fair lady, for some reason some demon  has uttered these words Save me, save me adapting my brothers voice.
ramayan::7729.english_translation: O fair lady, for some reason some demon has uttered these words, 'Save me, save me,' using my brother's voice.
ramayan::7729.translation_literal: किं निमित्तं (for what reason) / तु (but) / केनापि (by some) / भ्रातुः (brother's) / आलम्ब्य (taking support of) / मे (my) / स्वरम् (voice) / राक्षसेन (by a demon) / ईरितं (spoken) / वाक्यम् (words) / त्राहि त्राहि इति (save, save, thus) / शोभने (O fair lady)
ramayan::7729.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7729.essence: A familiar voice can be used as a trap.
ramayan::7729.simple_meaning: A demon is imitating Rama's brother's voice and crying for help. The speaker tells Sita not to be fooled by it.
ramayan::7729.simple_insight: Not every cry for help is real. Panic can wear a familiar voice.
ramayan::7729.detailed_meaning: In the forest, after Sita hears a desperate cry, Rama explains that the plea is false. A demon has copied Lakshmana's voice to trick her. The warning matters because the whole abduction depends on one moment of mistaken trust.
ramayan::7729.modern_relevance: You hear your sibling's voice on a bad phone line, begging urgently. Your body moves before your mind can check. This verse warns how easily fear can be weaponized through familiarity.
ramayan::7729.insight: It trains you to verify before reacting to emotional pressure.

ramayan::7730.verse_sanskrit: विस्वरं व्याहृतं वाक्यं लक्ष्मण त्राहि मामिति । न भवत्या व्यथा कार्या कुनारीजनसेविता । । 35913 । ।
ramayan::7730.verse_hindi: Lakshmana, save me are the words uttered in an altered tone. Like an ordinary, lowborn woman you are not to feel concerned for this.
ramayan::7730.english_translation: “Lakshmana, save me” are words spoken in a distorted voice. You should not be distressed by the words of a low woman-like person.
ramayan::7730.translation_literal: विस्वरं (in a distorted voice) / व्याहृतं (spoken) / वाक्यं (speech) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / त्राहि मामिति (saying save me) / न (not) / भवत्या (by you) / व्यथा (distress) / कार्या (to be done) / कुनारीजनसेविता (served by low woman-like people)
ramayan::7730.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7730.essence: False reassurance is often the cover for control.
ramayan::7730.simple_meaning: The speaker says the cry for help was spoken in a strange voice, so it should not upset you.
ramayan::7730.simple_insight: Not every alarming sound deserves your fear.
ramayan::7730.detailed_meaning: Inside Lanka, Ravana is trying to steady the woman he has deceived. He dismisses the cry for help as a strange imitation and tells her not to be shaken. The verse is part of his manipulation, not a teaching.
ramayan::7730.modern_relevance: Someone texts you a half-truth and then rushes to explain it away before you can think. The point is not clarity — it is control.
ramayan::7730.insight: It shows how deception tries to sound calm, so you lower your guard before questioning.

ramayan::7731.verse_sanskrit: अलं वैक्लब्यमालम्ब्य स्वस्था भव निरुत्सुका । न सोऽस्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु पुमान्वै राघवं रणे । । 35914 । । जातो वा जायमानो वा संयुगे यः पराजयेत् । न जय्यो राघवो युद्धे देवैश्शक्रपुरोगमैः । । 35915 । ।
ramayan::7731.verse_hindi: You should not feel agitated or dispirited. Be composed. There is no one either born or going to be born in the three worlds who can defeat Rama in war. He cannot be conquered in a battle even by gods led by indra.
ramayan::7731.english_translation: You should not feel agitated or dispirited. Be composed. There is no one either born or going to be born in the three worlds who can defeat Rama in war. He cannot be conquered in a battle even by gods led by Indra.
ramayan::7731.translation_literal: अलम् (enough) / वैक्लब्यम् (despondency) / आलम्ब्य (taking hold of) / स्वस्था (steady) / भव (be) / निरुत्सुका (free from anxiety) / न (not) / सः (he) / अस्ति (is) / त्रिषु (in the three) / लोकेषु (worlds) / पुमान् (man) / वै (indeed) / राघवम् (Rama) / रणे (in battle) / जातः (born) / वा (or) / जायमानः (being born) / वा (or) / संयुगे (in combat) / यः (who) / पराजयेत् (might defeat) / न (not) / जय्यः (conquerable) / राघवः (Rama) / युद्धे (in war) / देवैः (by the gods) / शक्रपुरोगमैः (with Indra at the front)
ramayan::7731.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7731.essence: Rama's strength is beyond ordinary defeat.
ramayan::7731.simple_meaning: Stop panicking and steady yourself. Rama cannot be defeated in battle by anyone in the three worlds, not even the gods with Indra leading them.
ramayan::7731.simple_insight: Fear loses its grip when you remember what is truly unshakable.
ramayan::7731.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, a frightened woman is being reassured after hearing a terrifying voice that seems to imitate Lakshmana. The speaker answers with confidence: Rama cannot be beaten in battle by anyone, now or ever. It is reassurance inside a tense, deceptive moment.
ramayan::7731.modern_relevance: A message arrives late at night, and your mind starts inventing disasters from a few bad words. This verse cuts through that spiral with a steadier view.
ramayan::7731.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to confidence by naming what cannot be overcome.

ramayan::7732.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही परिमोहितचेतना । उवाचाश्रूणि मुञ्चन्ती दारुणं मामिदं वचः । । 35916 । ।
ramayan::7732.verse_hindi: Deluded by her senses, Vaidehi said these words, shedding tears when I  tried to
ramayan::7732.english_translation: Deluded by her senses, Vaidehi said these words, shedding tears.
ramayan::7732.translation_literal: एवमुक्ता (thus spoken to) / तु (indeed) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / परिमोहितचेतना (with mind bewildered) / उवाच (said) / अश्रूणि (tears) / मुञ्चन्ती (releasing) / दारुणं (harsh) / मामिदं (to me this) / वचः (speech)
ramayan::7732.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7732.essence: Tears do not cancel a firm refusal.
ramayan::7732.simple_meaning: Sita, overwhelmed and in tears, responds with harsh words.
ramayan::7732.simple_insight: Even in fear, she refuses to yield her dignity.
ramayan::7732.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has just pressed Sita again after Lakshmana’s words of reassurance. Still shaken and weeping, Vaidehi answers him with a fierce rejection. The verse is a bridge into her refusal, not the full argument itself.
ramayan::7732.modern_relevance: When someone corners you and your voice shakes, the words can still be clear. Fear does not always mean surrender.
ramayan::7732.insight: It shows that distress can sharpen resolve instead of weakening it.

ramayan::7733.verse_sanskrit: भावो मयि तवात्यर्थं पाप एव निवेशितः । विनष्टे भ्रातरि प्राप्तुं न च त्वं मामवाप्स्यसि । । 35917 । ।
ramayan::7733.verse_hindi: You have an extremely sinful intention of getting me  when your brother is dead. But you will not be able to gain me.
ramayan::7733.english_translation: You have an extremely sinful intention of getting me when your brother is dead. But you will not be able to gain me.
ramayan::7733.translation_literal: भावः (intention) / मयि (toward me) / तव (your) / अत्यर्थम् (extremely) / पापः (sinful) / एव (indeed) / निवेशितः (placed) / विनष्टे (when destroyed/dead) / भ्रातरि (brother) / प्राप्तुम् (to obtain) / न (not) / च (and) / त्वम् (you) / माम् (me) / अवाप्स्यसि (will obtain)
ramayan::7733.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7733.essence: Desire that feeds on another’s loss cannot claim what it wants.
ramayan::7733.simple_meaning: Sita rejects Ravana’s attempt to win her after separating her from Rama. She calls the desire sinful and says he will never have her.
ramayan::7733.simple_insight: Cruel advantage does not become love just because it is possible.
ramayan::7733.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita answers Ravana’s pressure with complete moral clarity. He is trying to claim her while Rama is absent, but she names the act for what it is and refuses to soften her stance.
ramayan::7733.modern_relevance: Someone corners you after a breakup, a loss, or a vulnerable moment and calls it “a chance.” You feel the insult immediately: timing does not make exploitation acceptable.
ramayan::7733.insight: It teaches you to name manipulation clearly and refuse false claims on your vulnerability.

ramayan::7734.verse_sanskrit: सङ्केताद्भरतेन त्वं रामं समनुगच्छसि । क्रोशन्तं हि यथात्यर्थं नैवमभ्यवपद्यसे । । 35918 । ।
ramayan::7734.verse_hindi: Since you are not reaching out to Rama who is helplessly crying for his rescue, you must have followed Rama, instructed by Bharata (to do him harm)৷৷
ramayan::7734.english_translation: Since you are not reaching out to Rama, who is crying helplessly for rescue, you must have followed Rama only on Bharata's instruction.
ramayan::7734.translation_literal: सङ्केतात् (by instruction/sign) / भरतेन (by Bharata) / त्वम् (you) / रामम् (Rama) / समनुगच्छसि (follow closely) / क्रोशन्तम् (crying out) / हि (indeed) / यथा (as) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / न (not) / एवम् (thus) / अभ्यवपद्यसे (you are not approaching / taking hold of)
ramayan::7734.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7734.essence: Fear makes even help look like betrayal.
ramayan::7734.simple_meaning: Sita is accusing the speaker of being sent by Bharata and of pretending to help Rama while actually harming her.
ramayan::7734.simple_insight: Fear can turn trust into suspicion in an instant.
ramayan::7734.detailed_meaning: In Ashoka Grove, Sita is cornered, grieving, and under threat. A disguised visitor speaks to her, and she answers with sharp suspicion, reading his silence as proof of betrayal. This verse continues her refusal to be deceived.
ramayan::7734.modern_relevance: A stranger messages you with just enough familiarity to sound safe, but something feels off. Under stress, your mind starts connecting every gap as evidence.
ramayan::7734.insight: It shows how fear can distort perception and make even rescue look like harm.

ramayan::7735.verse_sanskrit: रिपुः प्रच्छन्नचारी त्वं मदर्थमनुगच्छसि । राघवस्यान्तरप्रेप्सुस्तथैनं नाभिपद्यसे । । 35919 । ।
ramayan::7735.verse_hindi: You are an enemy moving in disguise with an interest in me. You are waiting for an opportunity to set aside Rama. That is why you are not rushing to him.
ramayan::7735.english_translation: You are an enemy moving in disguise with an interest in me. You are waiting for an opportunity to set aside Rama. That is why you are not rushing to him.
ramayan::7735.translation_literal: रिपुः (enemy) / प्रच्छन्नचारी (moving in disguise) / त्वं (you) / मदर्थम् (for my sake) / अनुगच्छसि (you follow) । / राघवस्य (of Rama) / अन्तरप्रेप्सुः (seeking an opening) / तथा (thus) / एनम् (him) / न (not) / अभिपद्यसे (you approach)
ramayan::7735.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7735.essence: A false helper reveals himself by avoiding the one he truly targets.
ramayan::7735.simple_meaning: Sita accuses the disguised figure of being an enemy pretending to help her, while really looking for a chance to harm Rama.
ramayan::7735.simple_insight: Not every helper is safe; discernment protects what you love.
ramayan::7735.detailed_meaning: In the hermitage, Sita sees through the disguise. The stranger claims concern for her, but she suspects a hidden motive: he is watching for a chance to strike at Rama. Her refusal is sharp, protective, and immediate.
ramayan::7735.modern_relevance: A stranger online says all the right things, but keeps circling your private details and your partner’s name. Something in you knows the kindness is a cover.
ramayan::7735.insight: It trains you to read motives, not just words, before you trust someone.

ramayan::7736.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तो हि वैदेह्या संरब्धो रक्तलोचनः । क्रोधात्प्रस्फुरमाणोष्ठ आश्रमादभिनिर्गतः । । 35920 । ।
ramayan::7736.verse_hindi: At these words from the princess of Videha, I came out of the hermitage in an agitated mood with my eyes turned red and lips quivering in anger.
ramayan::7736.english_translation: At these words from the princess of Videha, I came out of the hermitage in an agitated mood with my eyes turned red and lips quivering in anger.
ramayan::7736.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus spoken to) / हि (indeed) / वैदेह्या (by the princess of Videha) / संरब्धः (agitated) / रक्तलोचनः (with red eyes) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / प्रस्फुरमाणोष्ठः (with quivering lips) / आश्रमात् (from the hermitage) / अभिनिर्गतः (came out)
ramayan::7736.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7736.essence: Anger can move you before judgment does.
ramayan::7736.simple_meaning: He leaves the hermitage in a fit of anger, his eyes red and lips trembling after hearing those words.
ramayan::7736.simple_insight: Anger can pull you out of your center before you notice it.
ramayan::7736.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, tense words have just been spoken about Rama and his absence. The speaker leaves at once, visibly shaken: eyes red, lips trembling, body driven by anger rather than calm judgment. The verse marks the emotional turn before the next exchange.
ramayan::7736.modern_relevance: A sharp message lands in your phone, and before you think, you’re already standing up, jaw tight, ready to answer. The reaction arrives before the reasoning.
ramayan::7736.insight: It shows how quickly hurt can become action when anger takes over.

ramayan::7737.verse_sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं सौमित्रिं रामस्सन्तापमोहितः । अब्रवीद्दुष्कृतं सौम्य तां विना यत्त्वमागतः । । 35921 । ।
ramayan::7737.verse_hindi: To Lakshmana thus reporting, Rama, overcome with grief, said,(Even then) O noble brother your coming here, leaving her behind, is a wrong step taken.
ramayan::7737.english_translation: To Lakshmana thus reporting, Rama, overcome with grief, said, “Even then, noble brother, your coming here, leaving her behind, was a wrong step.”
ramayan::7737.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / ब्रुवाणम् (speaking) / सौमित्रिम् (to Lakshmana) / रामः (Rama) / सन्ताप-मोहितः (overcome with grief) / अब्रवीत् (said) / दुष्कृतम् (wrong deed) / सौम्य (noble brother) / ताम् (her) / विना (without) / यत् (that) / त्वम् (you) / आगतः (came)
ramayan::7737.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7737.essence: Grief can cloud you, but it cannot make a wrong choice right.
ramayan::7737.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that coming back without Sita was a mistake, even if grief drove the decision.
ramayan::7737.simple_insight: Pain can explain a choice, but it does not automatically justify it.
ramayan::7737.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana has returned from the hermitage in distress, leaving Sita behind after her harsh words. Rama, shaken by grief, immediately sees the deeper fault: his brother came away without protecting her. The moment turns sorrow into moral judgment.
ramayan::7737.modern_relevance: You leave a tense conversation, then realise someone vulnerable is still stranded in the middle of it. Being upset may explain why you acted fast — but it does not erase the cost of leaving.
ramayan::7737.insight: It teaches you to judge actions by their moral weight, not by the emotion that triggered them.

ramayan::7738.verse_sanskrit: जानन्नपि समर्थं मां रक्षसां विनिवारणे । अनेन क्रोधवाक्येन मैथिल्या निस्सृतो भवान् । । 35922 । ।
ramayan::7738.verse_hindi: You have come out of the hermitage provoked by Maithilis angry words, even though you are aware that I am capable of warding off the demons.
ramayan::7738.english_translation: You have come out of the hermitage provoked by Maithili's angry words, even though you know I am capable of warding off the demons.
ramayan::7738.translation_literal: जानन्नपि (even knowing) / समर्थं (capable) / मां (me) / रक्षसां (of demons) / विनिवारणे (in warding off) / अनेन (by this) / क्रोधवाक्येन (angry speech) / मैथिल्या (by Maithili) / निस्सृतो (you came out) / भवान् (you)
ramayan::7738.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7738.essence: Anger can make you abandon the very duty you already knew.
ramayan::7738.simple_meaning: Rama rebukes Lakshmana for leaving Sita because of her angry words, even though Lakshmana knew Rama could handle the danger.
ramayan::7738.simple_insight: Strong feelings can make you abandon what you were meant to protect.
ramayan::7738.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita has spoken sharply, and Lakshmana has stormed away. Rama, shaken by grief, still sees the larger duty: Sita needed protection, not wounded pride. He rebukes Lakshmana because anger has interrupted care.
ramayan::7738.modern_relevance: You leave the room after a cutting text, and suddenly the thing you were supposed to handle is unattended. This verse catches that moment when irritation makes you forget responsibility.
ramayan::7738.insight: It shifts attention from emotional injury back to the obligation that still stands.

ramayan::7739.verse_sanskrit: न हि ते परितुष्यामि त्यक्त्वा यद्यासि मैथिलीम् । क्रुद्धायाः परुषं श्रुत्वा तां विहाय त्वमागतः । । 35923 । ।
ramayan::7739.verse_hindi: I am not happy with you as you have come here deserting Sita on the plea that she was angry and spoke harsh words.
ramayan::7739.english_translation: I am not pleased with you for leaving Sita and coming here because she was angry and spoke harshly.
ramayan::7739.translation_literal: न हि (indeed not) / ते (with you) / परितुष्यामि (I am pleased) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / यत् (because) / यासि (you go) / मैथिलीम् (Sita) / क्रुद्धायाः (of the angry one) / परुषम् (harshly) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / ताम् (her) / विहाय (leaving) / त्वम् (you) / आगतः (have come)
ramayan::7739.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7739.essence: Anger can make you abandon the very person you are meant to protect.
ramayan::7739.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that he is unhappy because Lakshmana left Sita behind after hearing her angry words.
ramayan::7739.simple_insight: Strong feelings can push you into choices that later feel wrong.
ramayan::7739.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshmana returns after leaving Sita alone in anger. Rama, shaken by grief, rebukes him sharply. The issue is not just the quarrel — it is the breach of protection and the cost of acting from hurt.
ramayan::7739.modern_relevance: You storm out after a fight and tell yourself it was justified. Hours later, you realise you left someone vulnerable just to protect your pride.
ramayan::7739.insight: It shifts attention from emotional reaction to the duty you still owe in conflict.

ramayan::7740.verse_sanskrit: सर्वथा त्वविनीतं ते सीतया यत्प्रचोदितः । क्रोधस्य वशमापन्नो नाकरोश्शासनं मम । । 35924 । ।
ramayan::7740.verse_hindi: Provoked by the words of Sita spoken in anger you came without respecting my orders. It is definitely an act of disobedience.
ramayan::7740.english_translation: Provoked by the words of Sita spoken in anger you came without respecting my orders. It is definitely an act of disobedience.
ramayan::7740.translation_literal: सर्वथा (in every way) / त्वम् (you) / अविनीतम् (discourteous; disobedient) / ते (your) / सीतया (by Sita) / यत् (because) / प्रचोदितः (urged; provoked) / क्रोधस्य (of anger) / वशम् (under control) / आपन्नः (having fallen) / न (not) / अकरोः (you did) / शासनम् (command; order) / मम (my)
ramayan::7740.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7740.essence: Anger can explain your action, but it cannot justify breaking your duty.
ramayan::7740.simple_meaning: Rama says Lakshmana acted wrongly by letting anger drive him away from Sita instead of following his command.
ramayan::7740.simple_insight: Strong feelings do not excuse breaking a clear responsibility.
ramayan::7740.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama confronts Lakshmana after Sita's harsh words have pulled him away from the hut. Rama sees the deeper failure: not the emotion itself, but the moment anger overrode obedience and left Sita unprotected.
ramayan::7740.modern_relevance: A text message hits your nerve, and you walk out of the room before thinking. Later you call it honesty, but the real issue was that emotion took the wheel before responsibility could speak.
ramayan::7740.insight: It teaches you to separate emotional provocation from the obligation you still owe.

ramayan::7741.verse_sanskrit: असौ हि राक्षसश्शेते शरेणाभिहतो मया । मृगरूपेण येनाहमाश्रमादपवाहितः । । 35925 । ।
ramayan::7741.verse_hindi: This demon who misled me in the guise of a deer and took me away from the hermitage, lies dead, killed by my arrow.
ramayan::7741.english_translation: This demon who misled me in the guise of a deer and took me away from the hermitage, lies dead, killed by my arrow.
ramayan::7741.translation_literal: असौ (that one) / हि (indeed) / राक्षसः (demon) / शेते (lies) / शरेण (by an arrow) / अभिहतः (struck down) / मया (by me) / मृगरूपेण (in deer-form) / येन (by whom) / अहम् (I) / आश्रमात् (from the hermitage) / अपवाहितः (carried away, led off)
ramayan::7741.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7741.essence: One deception opened the path to everything that followed.
ramayan::7741.simple_meaning: The false deer that lured Rama away from the hermitage has been killed by his arrow.
ramayan::7741.simple_insight: A single deception can trigger a chain of ruin.
ramayan::7741.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama recalls the trick that pulled him away from the hermitage and set Sita’s abduction in motion. The deer was never just an animal; it was the bait that exposed how quickly desire and distraction can open the door to disaster.
ramayan::7741.modern_relevance: You follow one shiny distraction, and suddenly the whole day is gone. The real damage often begins long before you notice the trap.
ramayan::7741.insight: It shifts attention to the first wrong turn, where later suffering is often planted.

ramayan::7742.verse_sanskrit: विकृष्य चापं परिधाय सायकं सलीलबाणेन च ताडितो मया । मार्गीं तनुं त्यज्य स विक्लबस्वरो बभूव केयूरधरस्सराक्षसः । । 35926 । ।
ramayan::7742.verse_hindi: Bending the bow I fixed the arrow and released it at ease. Hit by that arrow he gave up his guise of the deer and assuming the form of a demon with a bracelet on his arm fell down groaning.
ramayan::7742.english_translation: Bending the bow, I fitted the arrow and loosed it with ease. Struck by that arrow, he cast off the deer-form and fell groaning, revealing his demon body with an armlet.
ramayan::7742.translation_literal: विकृष्य (bending) / चापं (the bow) / परिधाय (having fitted on) / सायकं (the arrow) / सलीलबाणेन (with an easy arrow) / च (and) / ताडितः (struck) / मया (by me) / मार्गीं (deer-form) / तनुं (body/form) / त्यज्य (having abandoned) / सः (he) / विक्लबस्वरः (groaning) / बभूव (became) / केयूरधरः (armlet-wearing) / सः राक्षसः (that demon)
ramayan::7742.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7742.essence: One clean shot exposed the lie hiding beneath the disguise.
ramayan::7742.simple_meaning: Rama calmly shoots the deer, and the false form falls away to reveal the demon beneath.
ramayan::7742.simple_insight: A polished disguise can vanish in a single decisive act.
ramayan::7742.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has already realised the golden deer was a trap. He draws his bow, releases one controlled shot, and the illusion breaks. The deer collapses, revealing Maricha in his true demon form.
ramayan::7742.modern_relevance: Someone smiles through a lie, but one clear question exposes everything. The mask does not survive contact with steady attention.
ramayan::7742.insight: It shows how calm, precise action can cut through deception without hesitation.

ramayan::7743.verse_sanskrit: शराहतेनैव तदार्तया गिरा स्वरं समालम्ब्य सुदूरसुश्रवम् । उदाहृतं तद्वचनं सुदारुणं त्वमागतो येन विहाय मैथिलीम् । । 35927 । ।
ramayan::7743.verse_hindi: Hit by the arrow, the demon imitating my voice cried out in desperation which could be clearly audible even from a distance. On hearing the dreadful words you deserted Sita and came here.
ramayan::7743.english_translation: Hit by the arrow, the demon imitating my voice cried out in desperation which could be clearly audible even from a distance. On hearing the dreadful words, you deserted Sita and came here.
ramayan::7743.translation_literal: शराहतेन (by the arrow-struck one) / एव (indeed) / तदा (then) / आर्तया (with distressed) / गिरा (voice) / स्वरम् (sound) / समालम्ब्य (taking up) / सुदूरसुश्रवम् (clearly heard from far away) / उदाहृतम् (uttered) / तत् (that) / वचनम् (speech) / सुदारुणम् (very dreadful) / त्वम् (you) / आगतः (came) / येन (because of which) / विहाय (leaving) / मैथिलीम् (Sita)
ramayan::7743.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7743.essence: False urgency can drag you away from what you were protecting.
ramayan::7743.simple_meaning: The wounded demon used a fake cry to trick Rama. Hearing it, Rama left Sita and rushed away.
ramayan::7743.simple_insight: A single false alarm can split attention and open the door to loss.
ramayan::7743.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Maricha has already been struck and is dying in the shape of a deer. Using his last breath, he imitates Rama's voice so Sita will panic. The line explains how that cry pulled Rama away from Sita and set the tragedy in motion.
ramayan::7743.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with a message that sounds urgent, and you drop everything. Later you realize the panic was the point. One false signal can pull you away from what matters most.
ramayan::7743.insight: It shows how deception works by hijacking concern and forcing a mistaken response.

ramayan::7744.verse_sanskrit: भृशमाव्रजमानस्य तस्याधो वामलोचनम् । प्रास्फुरच्चास्खलद्रामो वेपथुश्चाप्य जायत । । 3601 । ।
ramayan::7744.verse_hindi: As  Rama was returning( to the hermitage), his left eye throbbed repeatedly  and he stumbled and his body trembled.
ramayan::7744.english_translation: As Rama was returning to the hermitage, his left eye throbbed repeatedly, he stumbled, and his body trembled.
ramayan::7744.translation_literal: भृशम् (greatly) / आव्रजमानस्य (while returning) / तस्य (his) / अधः (below / on the left side) / वाम-लोचनम् (left eye) / प्रास्फुरत् (throbbed) / च (and) / अस्खलत् (stumbled) / रामः (Rama) / वेपथुः (trembling) / च (and) / अपि (also) / जायत (arose)
ramayan::7744.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7744.essence: Your body can sense danger before your mind names it.
ramayan::7744.simple_meaning: Rama is returning to the hermitage when his left eye throbs, he stumbles, and his body trembles.
ramayan::7744.simple_insight: Sometimes the body knows distress before the mind does.
ramayan::7744.detailed_meaning: Rama is hurrying back toward the hermitage after the false deer episode. Before he even knows what has happened, his body gives warning signs: a throbbing eye, a stumble, a tremor. The next verse reveals his fear for Sita.
ramayan::7744.modern_relevance: You are walking back from a phone call that felt wrong, and your chest tightens before you can explain why. The mind catches up later; the body noticed first.
ramayan::7744.insight: It trains you to notice warning signs before you force a rational explanation.

ramayan::7745.verse_sanskrit: उपालक्ष्य निमित्तानि सोऽशुभानि मुहुर्मुहुः । अपि क्षेमं नु सीताया इति वै व्याजहार च । । 3602 । ।
ramayan::7745.verse_hindi: As inauspicious omens appeared again and again, doubting if all is well with Sita, he said to himself, Can Sita be safe?
ramayan::7745.english_translation: Noticing bad omens again and again, he said to himself, “Is Sita safe?”
ramayan::7745.translation_literal: उपालक्ष्य (noticing) / निमित्तानि (omens) / सः (he) / अशुभानि (inauspicious) / मुहुः मुहुः (again and again) / अपि (whether) / क्षेमम् (safety/well-being) / नु (indeed?) / सीतायाः (of Sita) / इति (thus) / वै (indeed) / व्याजहार (spoke to himself)
ramayan::7745.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7745.essence: Fear sharpens when the heart knows what the mind cannot yet prove.
ramayan::7745.simple_meaning: Rama notices bad signs and immediately worries about Sita's safety. His mind turns toward her before he knows anything for sure.
ramayan::7745.simple_insight: Sometimes anxiety is not random — it is your mind and body registering that something has shifted.
ramayan::7745.detailed_meaning: Rama is returning to the hermitage after hearing the false cry. His body has already reacted with trembling and a stumbling step. Now the omens around him darken, and his first thought is for Sita. The verse captures the instant fear begins to take shape.
ramayan::7745.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet house and feel something is off before you can name it. Your chest tightens, your eyes scan the room, and one question rises first: is everyone safe?
ramayan::7745.insight: It trains attention to notice warning signs instead of dismissing them as imagination.

ramayan::7746.verse_sanskrit: त्वरमाणो जगामाथ सीतादर्शनलालसः । शून्यमावसथं दृष्ट्वा बभूवोद्विग्नमानसः । । 3603 । ।
ramayan::7746.verse_hindi: Anxious to see Sita, he hastened to the hermitage and finding it empty, became
ramayan::7746.english_translation: Anxious to see Sita, he hastened to the hermitage and, finding it empty, became deeply troubled.
ramayan::7746.translation_literal: त्वरमाणः (hastening) / जगाम (went) / अथ (then) / सीता-दर्शन-लालसः (longing to see Sita) / शून्यम् (empty) / आवसथम् (dwelling) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / बभूव (became) / उद्विग्न-मानसः (troubled in mind)
ramayan::7746.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7746.essence: Empty space can reveal the worst before words do.
ramayan::7746.simple_meaning: Rama rushes back to the hermitage, eager to see Sita. When he finds it empty, fear and distress rise at once.
ramayan::7746.simple_insight: A missing presence can strike harder than any blow.
ramayan::7746.detailed_meaning: Rama returns to the hermitage with urgency, driven by longing and unease. The hut is empty, and that emptiness instantly unsettles him. This verse is a step in the unfolding discovery of Sita's disappearance.
ramayan::7746.modern_relevance: You open the door and the room is wrong — too quiet, too empty, and your body knows before your mind does.
ramayan::7746.insight: It shows how absence can become evidence, turning intuition into alarm before facts arrive.

ramayan::7747.verse_sanskrit: उद्भ्रमन्निव वेगेन विक्षिपन्रघुनन्दनः । तत्र तत्रोटजस्थानमभिवीक्षय समन्ततः । । 3604 । । ददर्श पर्णशालां च रहितां सीतया तदा । श्रिया विरहितां ध्वस्तां हेमन्ते पद्मिनीमिव । । 3605 । ।
ramayan::7747.verse_hindi: Rama, the delight of the Raghu dynasty, hurtled in, turning round, throwing his hands to and fro, casting his looks all around the cottage where she used to move. The cottage, devoid of Sita looked like a lotuspond, the beauty of its lotuses destroyed by winter.
ramayan::7747.english_translation: Rama, the delight of the Raghu dynasty, hurtled in, turning round, throwing his hands to and fro, casting his looks all around the cottage where she used to move. The cottage, devoid of Sita looked like a lotuspond, the beauty of its lotuses destroyed by winter.
ramayan::7747.translation_literal: उद्भ्रमन् (hurtling / whirling) / इव (as if) / वेगेन (with speed) / विक्षिपन् (throwing about) / रघुनन्दनः (Rama, delight of the Raghu dynasty) / तत्र तत्र (here and there) / ओटजस्थानम् (the cottage place) / अभिवीक्षय (looking all around) / समन्ततः (everywhere) / ददर्श (he saw) / पर्णशालाम् (the leaf-hut) / च (and) / रहिताम् (devoid) / सीतया (of Sita) / तदा (then) / श्रिया (of beauty / splendour) / विरहिताम् (stripped) / ध्वस्ताम् (ruined) / हेमन्ते (in winter) / पद्मिनीम् (a lotus pond) / इव (like)
ramayan::7747.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7747.essence: Her absence makes the whole place feel destroyed.
ramayan::7747.simple_meaning: Rama rushes through the hermitage, searching everywhere, and finds Sita's hut empty. The place that held her beauty now feels ruined and lifeless, like a lotus pond after winter.
ramayan::7747.simple_insight: Loss changes a place instantly; what once felt alive can feel empty in a single breath.
ramayan::7747.detailed_meaning: Rama reaches the hermitage and cannot find Sita. He searches in panic, looking everywhere around the leaf-hut. The next verses deepen the scene, showing how her absence drains the whole forest of life.
ramayan::7747.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and know, before anyone speaks, that something is wrong. The silence, the missing object, the changed air — absence can hit harder than news.
ramayan::7747.insight: It turns a search into a visible measure of grief, where absence reshapes the world around it.

ramayan::7748.verse_sanskrit: रुदन्तमिव वृक्षैश्च म्लानपुष्पमृगद्विजम् । श्रिया विहीनं विध्वस्तं सन्त्यक्तवनदेवतम् । । 3606 । । विप्रकीर्णाजिनकुशं विप्रविद्धब्रुसीकटम् । दृष्ट्वा शून्यं निजस्थानं विललाप पुनः पुनः । । 3607 । ।
ramayan::7748.verse_hindi: The trees with flowers withered, the animals and birds turned pale looked as if they
ramayan::7748.english_translation: Seeing his own place empty, stripped of Lakshmana's seat and Sita's presence, Rama wept again and again. The flowers had faded, the animals and birds looked mournful, and the hermitage itself seemed bereft of its glory and guardian.
ramayan::7748.translation_literal: रुदन्तमिव (as if weeping) / वृक्षैः (by the trees) / च (and) / म्लान-पुष्प-मृग-द्विजम् (with faded flowers, animals, and birds) / श्रिया (of splendor) / विहीनम् (deprived) / विध्वस्तम् (ruined) / सन्त्यक्त-वन-देवतम् (abandoned by the forest deity) / विप्रकीर्ण-अजिन-कुशम् (scattered deer-skins and kusa grass) / विप्रविद्ध-ब्रुसीकटम् (thrown about, with broken utensils) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / शून्यम् (empty) / निज-स्थानम् (his own place) / विललाप (lamented) / पुनः पुनः (again and again)
ramayan::7748.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7748.essence: Absence changes the whole world into a witness of grief.
ramayan::7748.simple_meaning: Rama sees the hermitage empty and ruined, with signs that Sita is gone, and he breaks into repeated grief.
ramayan::7748.simple_insight: Love makes absence visible everywhere. Even the place around you can seem to grieve.
ramayan::7748.detailed_meaning: Rama has returned to the hermitage and found Sita missing. The flowers have faded, the birds and animals seem sorrowful, and the simple home he shared with her and Lakshmana is in disarray. The scene turns his fear into open lament.
ramayan::7748.modern_relevance: You come home and notice the cup still on the table, the chair pulled back, the room too quiet. Loss makes even ordinary things feel wounded.
ramayan::7748.insight: It shows how grief spreads into perception, making the whole environment mirror inner loss.

ramayan::7749.verse_sanskrit: हृता मृता वा नष्टा वा भक्षिता वा भविष्यति । निलीनाप्यथवा भीरुरथवा वनमाश्रिता । । 3608 । ।
ramayan::7749.verse_hindi: Timid Sita might have been abducted or dead or crushed or eaten up by demons. Or, she may be hiding for protection in the forest
ramayan::7749.english_translation: Sita might have been abducted, dead, destroyed, eaten, hiding, or sheltering in the forest.
ramayan::7749.translation_literal: हृता (abducted) / मृता (dead) / वा (or) / नष्टा (destroyed) / वा (or) / भक्षिता (eaten up) / वा (or) / भविष्यति (might be) / निलीना (hidden) / अपि अथवा (or even) / भीरुः (timid) / अथवा (or) / वनम् (forest) / आश्रिता (taking refuge in)
ramayan::7749.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7749.essence: Absence turns the mind into a courtroom of fears.
ramayan::7749.simple_meaning: Rama is trying to guess what happened to Sita. He lists every possible fate, from abduction to death to hiding in the forest.
ramayan::7749.simple_insight: Grief makes the mind search every possible explanation, even the painful ones.
ramayan::7749.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in the ruined hermitage after Sita's disappearance, scanning the emptiness for any clue. Unable to know where she is, he voices every fear at once — abducted, dead, hidden, or taking refuge somewhere in the forest.
