ramayan::7749.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the last place you saw them, inventing every explanation because not knowing hurts more than any answer.
ramayan::7749.insight: It shows how love under stress becomes a storm of possibilities, not calm certainty.

ramayan::7750.verse_sanskrit: गता विचेतुं पुष्पाणि फलान्यपि च वा पुनः । अथवा पद्मिनीं याता जलार्थं वा नदीं गता । । 3609 । ।
ramayan::7750.verse_hindi: Maybe she has gone to pluck flowers or fruits. Or to the lotuspond or river to  fetch water.
ramayan::7750.english_translation: Maybe she has gone to pluck flowers or fruits. Or to the lotus pond or river to fetch water.
ramayan::7750.translation_literal: गता (gone) / विचेतुं (to pick) / पुष्पाणि (flowers) / फलानि (fruits) / अपि (also) / च (and) / वा (or) / पुनः (again) / अथवा (or else) / पद्मिनीं (lotus pond) / याता (gone) / जलार्थं (for water) / वा (or) / नदीं (river) / गता (gone)
ramayan::7750.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7750.essence: Hope keeps inventing harmless reasons before fear takes over.
ramayan::7750.simple_meaning: The speaker is listing harmless places Sita might have gone: to gather flowers or fruit, or to fetch water from a pond or river.
ramayan::7750.simple_insight: Grief keeps reaching for ordinary explanations before it accepts fear.
ramayan::7750.detailed_meaning: In the empty forest, the search for Sita has become desperate. The speaker still tries to imagine ordinary reasons for her absence: flowers, fruit, or water. It is a fragile hope before the harsher possibilities take over.
ramayan::7750.modern_relevance: You check the kitchen, the balcony, the parking lot — anywhere she might have gone. Your mind keeps offering ordinary explanations before it admits something feels wrong.
ramayan::7750.insight: It shows the mind clinging to normal possibilities before panic fully sets in.

ramayan::7751.verse_sanskrit: यत्नान्मृगयमाणस्तु नाससाद वने प्रियाम् । शोकरक्तेक्षणश्शोकादुन्मत्त इव लक्ष्यते । । 36010 । ।
ramayan::7751.verse_hindi: He ransacked the forest, yet did not find his beloved. He  appeared like a mad man, his eyes turned red with tears of sorrow.
ramayan::7751.english_translation: He searched the forest carefully, yet did not find his beloved. With eyes red from grief, he looked like a madman.
ramayan::7751.translation_literal: यत्नात् (with effort) / मृगयमाणः (searching for) / तु (but) / न (not) / आससाद (found) / वने (in the forest) / प्रियाम् (his beloved) / शोकरक्तेक्षणः (with grief-red eyes) / शोकात् (from sorrow) / उन्मत्तः इव (like one mad) / लक्ष्यते (is seen)
ramayan::7751.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7751.essence: Searching harder cannot fill the emptiness left by loss.
ramayan::7751.simple_meaning: Rama searched the forest with urgency, but he still could not find Sita. His grief was so intense that he seemed unhinged.
ramayan::7751.simple_insight: Love can make even the strongest person look broken when separation becomes real.
ramayan::7751.detailed_meaning: Rama is still roaming the forest after Sita's disappearance. He searches everywhere, but the trail is empty. The sight of the prince reduced to grief shows how completely the loss has shaken him.
ramayan::7751.modern_relevance: You checked every room, called every number, and still got nothing. The silence itself starts to change your face.
ramayan::7751.insight: It shows how grief can overwhelm even disciplined action, turning search into visible anguish.

ramayan::7752.verse_hindi: Running from tree to tree, hill to hill, and river to river and weeping, Rama was immersed in a sea of sorrow.
ramayan::7752.english_translation: Running from tree to tree, hill to hill, and river to river and weeping, Rama was immersed in a sea of sorrow.
ramayan::7752.translation_literal: वृक्षात् (from tree) / वृक्षम् (to tree) / प्रधावन् (running) / सः (he) / गिरेः (from hill) / च (and) / अद्रिम् (to hill) / नदान् (from river) / नदीम् (to river) / बभूव (became) / विलपन् (lamenting) / रामः (Rama) / शोक-अर्णव-परिप्लुतः (immersed in an ocean of sorrow)
ramayan::7752.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7752.essence: Loss drives him from place to place, but finding her is still beyond him.
ramayan::7752.simple_meaning: Rama searches everywhere for Sita, running from place to place while grieving deeply.
ramayan::7752.simple_insight: Love can turn even strength into frantic searching.
ramayan::7752.detailed_meaning: Sita has vanished from the forest. Rama has already imagined possible places she might have gone, but the search only deepens his grief. He rushes from tree to hill to river, unable to stop the ache of separation.
ramayan::7752.modern_relevance: You check the same rooms twice, then three times, hoping the missing person will appear. Panic makes every familiar place feel like a clue.
ramayan::7752.insight: It shows how grief can scatter attention and turn searching into suffering.

ramayan::7753.verse_sanskrit: अपि काचित्त्वया दृष्टा सा कदम्बप्रिया प्रिया । कदम्ब यदि जानीषे शंस सीतां शुभाननाम् । । 36012 । ।
ramayan::7753.verse_hindi: O Kadamba tree, tell me if you have seen my beloved with a fair face and with love for kadamba flowers.
ramayan::7753.english_translation: O Kadamba tree, tell me if you have seen my beloved with a fair face and with love for kadamba flowers.
ramayan::7753.translation_literal: अपि (whether) / काचित् (some woman) / त्वया (by you) / दृष्टा (seen) / सा (that) / कदम्बप्रिया (fond of kadamba flowers) / प्रिया (beloved) / कदम्ब (O Kadamba tree) / यदि (if) / जानीषे (you know) / शंस (tell) / सीताम् (Sita) / शुभाननाम् (of fair face)
ramayan::7753.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7753.essence: Even in despair, love keeps asking the world for one more sign.
ramayan::7753.simple_meaning: Rama asks a kadamba tree whether it has seen Sita, describing her by her beauty and her love for kadamba flowers.
ramayan::7753.simple_insight: Grief makes even a tree feel like a witness when the person you love is gone.
ramayan::7753.detailed_meaning: Rama is roaming the forest after Sita’s abduction, searching every tree and riverbank with desperate hope. Here he stops before a kadamba tree and pleads for news of her, using the smallest detail of her affection to make the world help him find her.
ramayan::7753.modern_relevance: You replay tiny details after someone disappears from your life — the flower they loved, the corner they stood in, the thing only you would remember.
ramayan::7753.insight: It shows how love under loss turns memory into a search, and the world into a possible clue.

ramayan::7754.verse_sanskrit: स्निग्धपल्लवसङ्काशा पीतकौशेयवासिनी । शंसस्व यदि वा दृष्टा बिल्व बिल्वोपमस्तनी । । 36013 । ।
ramayan::7754.verse_hindi: O Bilva tree, tell me if you have seen a lady delicate like your tender leaf, dressed in yellow silk, a lady whose breasts are round like Bilva fruits.
ramayan::7754.english_translation: O Bilva tree, tell me if you have seen a lady delicate like your tender leaf, dressed in yellow silk, a lady whose breasts are round like Bilva fruits.
ramayan::7754.translation_literal: स्निग्धपल्लवसङ्काशा (resembling tender leaves) / पीतकौशेयवासिनी (wearing yellow silk) / शंसस्व (tell) / यदि (if) / वा (or) / दृष्टा (seen) / बिल्व (O Bilva tree) / बिल्वोपमस्तनी (with Bilva-fruit-like breasts)
ramayan::7754.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7754.essence: He asks the forest itself to become a witness to his loss.
ramayan::7754.simple_meaning: Rama asks a Bilva tree whether it has seen Sita, describing her beauty through the tree's own form.
ramayan::7754.simple_insight: Love makes even the forest feel like a witness.
ramayan::7754.detailed_meaning: Rama, frantic in the forest after Sita's abduction, speaks to trees as if they can answer him. He describes her with tender, intimate details, hoping some part of the forest has seen where she went.
ramayan::7754.modern_relevance: You search every corner after someone you love disappears, and even ordinary places start feeling like they might know something.
ramayan::7754.insight: It shows how grief turns the world into a field of questions.

ramayan::7755.verse_sanskrit: अथवाऽर्जुन शंस त्वं प्रियां तामर्जुनप्रियाम् । जनकस्य सुता भीरुर्यदि जीवति वा न वा । । 36014 । ।
ramayan::7755.verse_hindi: O Arjuna tree, tell me if you know a timid lady, daughter of Janaka and my beloved, fond of Arjuna tree. Is the living or not ?
ramayan::7755.english_translation: O Arjuna tree, tell me whether you have seen that timid daughter of Janaka, my beloved, who loves the Arjuna tree, and whether she lives or not.
ramayan::7755.translation_literal: अथवा (or else) / अर्जुन (Arjuna tree) / शंस (tell) / त्वं (you) / प्रियम् (beloved one) / ताम् (that one) / अर्जुनप्रियाम् (fond of the Arjuna tree) / जनकस्य (of Janaka) / सुता (daughter) / भीरुः (timid) / यदि (if) / जीवति (lives) / वा (or) / न (not) / वा (or)
ramayan::7755.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7755.essence: Love keeps asking the world for what it has lost.
ramayan::7755.simple_meaning: Rama asks an Arjuna tree whether it has seen Sita, the timid daughter of Janaka, and whether she is still alive.
ramayan::7755.simple_insight: The search itself becomes a cry of love when certainty is gone.
ramayan::7755.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has not yet found Sita, and Rama’s longing is being voiced through the forest. He asks the Arjuna tree about Janaka’s daughter, his beloved, as if the trees themselves might know where she is. The verse deepens the ache of separation.
ramayan::7755.modern_relevance: You call someone’s name into an empty room and then ask the silence if it has answers. Love keeps searching even when it has no proof.
ramayan::7755.insight: It turns grief into a searching attention that refuses to stop at silence.

ramayan::7756.verse_sanskrit: ककुभः ककुभोरूं तां व्यक्तं जानाति मैथिलीम् । यथा पल्लवपुष्पाढ्यो भाति ह्येष वनस्पतिः । । 36015 । ।
ramayan::7756.verse_hindi: This Kakubha tree rich with tender leaves and flowers (perhaps)knows Maithili whose thighs are beautiful like the trunk of the Kakubha tree.
ramayan::7756.english_translation: This Kakubha tree, rich with tender leaves and flowers, surely knows Maithili, whose thighs are beautiful like the trunk of the Kakubha tree.
ramayan::7756.translation_literal: ककुभः (the Kakubha tree) / ककुभोरूं (with thighs like the Kakubha tree) / ताम् (her) / व्यक्तम् (clearly) / जानाति (knows) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili) / यथा (just as) / पल्लवपुष्पाढ्यः (rich with leaves and flowers) / भाति (shines) / हि (indeed) / एषः (this) / वनस्पतिः (tree)
ramayan::7756.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7756.essence: Longing makes even a tree feel like a witness.
ramayan::7756.simple_meaning: The speaker points to a Kakubha tree and says it must have seen Sita, since her beauty is like the tree's graceful form.
ramayan::7756.simple_insight: Even in grief, the mind reaches for the living world and turns beauty into a witness.
ramayan::7756.detailed_meaning: Sita has vanished into the forest, and Rama is searching every tree as if the woods themselves might answer. He notices the Kakubha tree and compares its graceful form to Sita's beauty, treating the landscape as a possible witness to her passage.
ramayan::7756.modern_relevance: You walk past a street tree after a painful goodbye and suddenly every ordinary thing feels charged with memory. Grief makes the world look like it knows more than it says.
ramayan::7756.insight: It shows how longing turns the surroundings into clues, and keeps the search alive even when there is no answer.

ramayan::7757.verse_sanskrit: भ्रमरैरुपगीतश्च यथा द्रुमवरो ह्ययम् । एष व्यक्तं विजानाति तिलकस्तिलकप्रियाम् । । 36016 । ।
ramayan::7757.verse_hindi: This great Tilaka tree round which bees bumble surely knows the lady who loves to put tilaka marks on the forehead.
ramayan::7757.english_translation: This great Tilaka tree, ringed by bees, surely knows the lady who loves to wear a tilaka on her forehead.
ramayan::7757.translation_literal: भ्रमरैः (by bees) / उपगीतः (sung around, surrounded) / च (and) / यथा (as) / द्रुमवरः (great tree) / हि (indeed) / अयम् (this) / एषः (this) / व्यक्तम् (surely, clearly) / विजानाति (knows) / तिलकः (Tilaka tree) / तिलकप्रियां (the lady dear to tilaka, or who loves tilaka)
ramayan::7757.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7757.essence: A desperate search can make every detail feel like a clue.
ramayan::7757.simple_meaning: Hanuman keeps asking the trees if they know Sita. Here he notices a Tilaka tree and hopes it can point him toward her.
ramayan::7757.simple_insight: Searching with care means noticing even the smallest clue.
ramayan::7757.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is alone in the forest, asking trees about Sita’s whereabouts. After naming the Arjuna and Kakubha trees, he turns to the Tilaka tree, reading its shape and the bees around it as a possible sign. The verse continues his urgent search, not a complete teaching.
ramayan::7757.modern_relevance: You are scanning old messages, locations, and names for one clue that might change everything. Careful attention can turn a vague search into a real lead.
ramayan::7757.insight: It trains the mind to look for meaningful patterns without losing focus.

ramayan::7758.verse_sanskrit: अशोक शोकापनुद शोकोपहतचेतसम् । त्वन्नामानं कुरु क्षिप्रं प्रियासन्दर्शनेन माम् । । 36017 । ।
ramayan::7758.verse_hindi: O Ashoka tree, dispeller of sorrow, by quickly showing me my darling make me ashoka (free from sorrow) as I am griefstricken at heart.
ramayan::7758.english_translation: O Ashoka tree, dispeller of sorrow, by quickly showing me my darling make me ashoka, for my heart is grief-stricken.
ramayan::7758.translation_literal: अशोक (Ashoka) / शोकापनुद (dispeller of sorrow) / शोकोपहतचेतसम् (one whose mind is struck by sorrow) / त्वन्नामानं (the name of you) / कुरु (make) / क्षिप्रं (quickly) / प्रियासन्दर्शनेन (by the sight of the beloved) / माम् (me)
ramayan::7758.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7758.essence: Even sorrow can be addressed as if it might help you heal.
ramayan::7758.simple_meaning: Hanuman speaks to the Ashoka tree and asks it to end his grief by helping him quickly see Sita.
ramayan::7758.simple_insight: Love becomes bearable when it has a path toward reunion.
ramayan::7758.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is hidden in Lanka, searching for Sita after crossing the ocean alone. He stands among the trees in the Ashoka grove and speaks to one named Ashoka, asking it to live up to its name by ending sorrow through Sita's sight.
ramayan::7758.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, a phone call away from relief, and every minute feels heavy. This verse carries that ache of waiting for one face, one message, one sign that pain can loosen.
ramayan::7758.insight: It turns longing into a direct plea for reunion rather than passive suffering.

ramayan::7759.verse_sanskrit: यदि ताल त्वया दृष्टा पक्वतालफलस्तनी । कथयस्व वरारोहां कारुण्यं यदि ते मयि । । 36018 । ।
ramayan::7759.verse_hindi: O Palmyra tree be kind to me and tell me if you have seen my beautiful beloved who has breasts like ripe palmyra fruit?
ramayan::7759.english_translation: O Palmyra tree, be kind to me and tell me if you have seen my beautiful beloved, whose breasts are like ripe palmyra fruit.
ramayan::7759.translation_literal: यदि (if) / ताल (palmyra tree) / त्वया (by you) / दृष्टा (seen) / पक्व-ताल-फल-स्तनी (one whose breasts are like ripe palmyra fruit) / कथयस्व (tell) / वरारोहाम् (the lovely-bodied woman) / कारुण्यम् (kindness) / यदि (if) / ते (your) / मयि (toward me)
ramayan::7759.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7759.essence: Searching love asks every corner of the world for one answer.
ramayan::7759.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks a palmyra tree whether it has seen Sita and begs it to answer kindly if it knows anything.
ramayan::7759.simple_insight: Longing can make even a tree feel like a witness.
ramayan::7759.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is searching Lanka at night, asking trees about Sita as he moves through enemy ground. This verse is part of his careful, desperate questioning, not a complete teaching by itself.
ramayan::7759.modern_relevance: You keep scanning every face, every message, every clue for the person who matters. Even silence starts to feel like it might answer you.
ramayan::7759.insight: It shows how devotion and urgency can turn searching into a whole way of seeing.

ramayan::7760.verse_sanskrit: यदि दृष्टा त्वया सीता जम्बु जम्बूफलोपमा । प्रियां यदि विजानीषे निःशङ्कं कथयस्व मे । । 36019 । ।
ramayan::7760.verse_hindi: O Jambu tree, do not hesitate to tell me if you know Sita whose body shines lovely like gold.
ramayan::7760.english_translation: O Jambu tree, if you have seen Sita, tell me without hesitation.
ramayan::7760.translation_literal: यदि (if) / दृष्टा (seen) / त्वया (by you) / सीता (Sita) / जम्बु (Jambu tree) / जम्बूफलोपमा (like the fruit of the jambu tree) / प्रियां (the beloved) / यदि (if) / विजानीषे (you know) / निःशङ्कं (without hesitation) / कथयस्व (tell) / मे (to me)
ramayan::7760.speaker: Hanuman
ramayan::7760.essence: Searching itself becomes devotion when nothing else is left.
ramayan::7760.simple_meaning: Hanuman asks a tree whether it has seen Sita and tells it to speak freely if it knows anything.
ramayan::7760.simple_insight: Even in desperation, he keeps searching with focus and hope.
ramayan::7760.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is moving through Lanka at night, asking trees one by one whether they have seen Sita. This is not a teaching verse but part of his urgent search, showing how completely he has taken Rama’s mission as his own.
ramayan::7760.modern_relevance: You have searched every corner of the house and still cannot find what matters. The urgency stays, but you keep asking, keep looking, keep moving.
ramayan::7760.insight: It shows single-minded pursuit under pressure, without losing restraint or purpose.

ramayan::7761.verse_sanskrit: अहो त्वं कर्णिकाराद्य सुपुष्पैश्शोभसे भृशम् । कर्णिकारप्रिया साध्वी शंस दृष्टा प्रिया यदि । । 36020 । ।
ramayan::7761.verse_hindi: O Karnikara tree with flowers in full bloom, tell me if you have seen my faithful beloved who is fond of karnikara flowers.
ramayan::7761.english_translation: O Karnikara tree with flowers in full bloom, tell me if you have seen my faithful beloved who is fond of karnikara flowers.
ramayan::7761.translation_literal: अहो (ah, indeed) / त्वम् (you) / कर्णिकाराद्य (O karnikara-tree) / सुपुष्पैः (with full flowers) / शोभसे (you shine) / भृशम् (greatly) / कर्णिकार-प्रिया (fond of karnikara flowers) / साध्वी (faithful / virtuous one) / शंस (tell) / दृष्टा (seen) / प्रिया (beloved) / यदि (if)
ramayan::7761.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7761.essence: Grief makes even a tree feel like a witness.
ramayan::7761.simple_meaning: Rama speaks to a flowering tree as if it can answer him, asking whether it has seen Sita, who loves those flowers.
ramayan::7761.simple_insight: Love can make even the silent world feel like it might answer.
ramayan::7761.detailed_meaning: Alone in the forest, Rama searches every tree for a sign of Sita. He speaks to the karnikara tree because grief has made every blooming branch feel like a witness. This verse is one step in his desperate search, not the full thought itself.
ramayan::7761.modern_relevance: You catch yourself talking to a place that holds a memory — a street, a bench, a doorway — because the person is gone and your mind still searches.
ramayan::7761.insight: It shows how longing turns the environment into a field of clues, keeping attention fixed on the missing person.

ramayan::7762.verse_sanskrit: चूतनीपमहासालान्पनसान्कुरवान्धवान् । दाडिमाननसान्गत्वा दृष्ट्वा रामो महायशाः । । 36021 । । मल्लिका माधवीश्चैव चम्पकान्केतकीस्तथा । पृच्छन्रामो वने भान्तः उन्मत्त इव लक्ष्यते । । 36022 । ।
ramayan::7762.verse_hindi: Renowned Rama, like a madman confused, approached the Mango, Kadamba , Sal and Jackfruit, Dhava, Champak, Ketaki trees and Pomegranate, Jasmine and Madhavi creepers, in order to make similar queries.
ramayan::7762.english_translation: Renowned Rama, like a madman confused, approached the mango, kadamba, sal, jackfruit, dhava, pomegranate, jasmine, madhavi, champaka, and ketaki trees, asking them the same question.
ramayan::7762.translation_literal: चूत (mango tree) / नीप (kadamba tree) / महासालान् (great sal trees) / पनसान् (jackfruit trees) / कुरवान् (dhava trees) / धवान् (dhava trees) / दाडिमान् (pomegranate trees) / अनसान् (jasmine plants) / गत्वा (having gone) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / रामः (Rama) / महायशाः (highly renowned) / मल्लिका (jasmine) / माधवीः (madhavi creepers) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / चम्पकान् (champaka trees) / केतकीः (ketaki plants) / तथा (also) / पृच्छन् (asking) / रामः (Rama) / वने (in the forest) / भान्तः (shining) / उन्मत्तः इव (as if mad) / लक्ष्यते (is seen)
ramayan::7762.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7762.essence: Longing can make even a noble mind look unhinged.
ramayan::7762.simple_meaning: Rama searches every tree and creeper for Sita, asking each one in turn. His grief makes him look almost mad.
ramayan::7762.simple_insight: Love in separation can make even the strongest person look unsteady.
ramayan::7762.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has already asked one tree after another whether they have seen Sita. He keeps moving from tree to tree, naming flowers and creepers as if they might answer. The scene shows how far his longing has shaken him.
ramayan::7762.modern_relevance: You walk back through the same empty room, checking places they cannot be. Grief makes the mind repeat the search long after reason knows the answer.
ramayan::7762.insight: It shows how loss can scatter attention, making the mind search everywhere for what is missing.

ramayan::7763.verse_sanskrit: अथवा मृगशाबाक्षीं मृग जानासि मैथिलीम् । मृगविप्रेक्षणी कान्ता मृगीभिस्सहिता भवेत् । । 36023 । ।
ramayan::7763.verse_hindi: Or,  O deer do you know about Maithili who has the eyes of a fawn? My beloved who has the restless eyes of a doe may be found in their company.
ramayan::7763.english_translation: Or, O deer, do you know Maithili, the one with fawn-like eyes? My beloved, with the restless eyes of a doe, may be found among your company.
ramayan::7763.translation_literal: अथवा (or) / मृगशाबाक्षीं (fawn-eyed) / मृग (deer) / जानासि (do you know) / मैथिलीम् (Maithili) / मृगविप्रेक्षणी (deer-eyed) / कान्ता (beloved) / मृगीभिस्सहिता (together with does) / भवेत् (may be)
ramayan::7763.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7763.essence: Love in grief starts asking the world impossible questions.
ramayan::7763.simple_meaning: Rama asks a deer whether it has seen Sita, describing her with deer-like eyes and asking if she might be with other deer.
ramayan::7763.simple_insight: Grief can make even a noble mind speak to the forest as if it might answer.
ramayan::7763.detailed_meaning: Alone in the forest after Sita’s disappearance, Rama moves from tree to tree and animal to animal, asking each if it has seen her. This verse is one more desperate question in that search, shaped by love, panic, and the hope that the forest may know what humans do not.
ramayan::7763.modern_relevance: You keep scanning faces in a crowd after losing someone important, hoping the world will somehow return a clue.
ramayan::7763.insight: It shows how longing narrows attention and turns every living thing into a possible witness.

ramayan::7764.verse_sanskrit: गज सा गजनासोरूर्यदि दृष्टा त्वया भवेत् । तां मन्ये विदितां तुभ्यमाख्याहि वरवारण । 36024 । ।
ramayan::7764.verse_hindi: O elephant tell me if you have seen her whose thighs are like the trunk of an elephant. O best of elephants, tell me if you know her.
ramayan::7764.english_translation: O elephant, tell me if you have seen her whose thighs are like an elephant's trunk. O best of elephants, tell me if you know her.
ramayan::7764.translation_literal: गज (elephant) / सा (she) / गजनासोरूरू (with elephant-trunk-like thighs) / यदि (if) / दृष्टा (seen) / त्वया (by you) / भवेत् (may be) / ताम् (her) / मन्ये (I think) / विदिताम् (known) / तुभ्यम् (to you) / आख्याहि (tell) / वरवारण (best of elephants)
ramayan::7764.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7764.essence: Love lost turns a noble man into a seeker of every possible clue.
ramayan::7764.simple_meaning: Rama is asking a passing elephant whether it has seen Sita and can identify her by her elephant-like thighs.
ramayan::7764.simple_insight: Grief can make even a king plead with the forest for answers.
ramayan::7764.detailed_meaning: Rama is wandering through the forest after Sita's abduction, asking animals and trees whether they have seen her. Here he turns to an elephant, describing Sita by her graceful features and begging for any clue that might lead him to her.
ramayan::7764.modern_relevance: You keep asking anyone who might know where she went, replaying her features in your mind because the absence is unbearable.
ramayan::7764.insight: It shows the raw urgency of loss: when love is threatened, even pride gives way to desperate searching.

ramayan::7765.verse_sanskrit: शार्दूल यदि सा दृष्टा प्रिया चन्द्रनिभानना । मैथिली मम विस्रब्धं कथयस्व न ते भयम् । । 36025 । ।
ramayan::7765.verse_hindi: O tiger tell me freely and fearlessly if you have seen my beloved princess from Mithila with a face like the moon.
ramayan::7765.english_translation: O tiger, if you have seen my beloved Maithili, whose face is like the moon, tell me freely and without fear; you have nothing to fear from me.
ramayan::7765.translation_literal: शार्दूल (O tiger) / यदि (if) / सा (she) / दृष्टा (seen) / प्रिया (beloved) / चन्द्रनिभानना (moon-faced) / मैथिली (Maithili) / मम (my) / विस्रब्धं (freely, without fear) / कथयस्व (tell) / न (not) / ते (to you) / भयम् (fear)
ramayan::7765.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7765.essence: Desperation turns every creature into a possible witness.
ramayan::7765.simple_meaning: Rama asks a tiger-like creature whether it has seen Sita and tells it to speak without fear.
ramayan::7765.simple_insight: Grief can make even a king speak to the world as if it might answer.
ramayan::7765.detailed_meaning: In the search for Sita, Rama questions the animals of the forest one by one, describing her by her beauty so they might recognise her. This line is part of that desperate, moving search, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7765.modern_relevance: You repeat the same question to anyone who might know, even when hope is thin. When someone you love is missing, every stranger, every sign, every silence starts to matter.
ramayan::7765.insight: It shows how longing narrows the mind to one urgent need: find the lost person.

ramayan::7766.verse_sanskrit: किं धावसि प्रिये दूरे दृष्टासि कमलेक्षणे । वृक्षैराच्छाद्य चात्मानं किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे । । 36026 । ।
ramayan::7766.verse_hindi: O lotus eyed darling, why are you running away? I have already seen you.  Why are you hiding behind trees and not replying to me?
ramayan::7766.english_translation: O lotus-eyed darling, why are you running away? I have already seen you. Why are you hiding behind trees and not replying to me?
ramayan::7766.translation_literal: किं (why) / धावसि (are you running) / प्रिये (beloved) / दूरे (far away) / दृष्टासि (you have been seen) / कमलेक्षणे (lotus-eyed one) / वृक्षैः (by trees) / आच्छाद्य (covering) / च (and) / आत्मानं (yourself) / किं (why) / मां (me) / न (not) / प्रतिभाषसे (do you answer/speak back)
ramayan::7766.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7766.essence: Recognition comes first; trust follows slowly.
ramayan::7766.simple_meaning: He sees the woman he loves, calls out to her, and asks why she is hiding and not answering him.
ramayan::7766.simple_insight: Even in longing, the heart reaches out before it has certainty.
ramayan::7766.detailed_meaning: Hanuman has found Sita in the Ashoka grove and is trying to speak to her safely from the shadows. She hides behind trees, unsure of him. His words are part reassurance, part urgency, trying to stop her from slipping away.
ramayan::7766.modern_relevance: You spot someone you care about across a crowded street, but they hesitate and look away. The distance is only a few steps, yet trust still has to cross it.
ramayan::7766.insight: It shows how love must often begin by making itself recognizable before it can be received.

ramayan::7767.verse_sanskrit: तिष्ठ तिष्ठ वरारोहे न तेऽस्ति करुणा मयि । नात्यर्थं हास्यशीलासि किमर्थं मामुपेक्षसे । । 36027 । ।
ramayan::7767.verse_hindi: O my beautiful beloved, stay, stay  Have you no compassion for me ? You are so fond of fun. Why do you avoid me?
ramayan::7767.english_translation: O my beautiful beloved, stay, stay. Have you no compassion for me? You are so fond of play. Why do you ignore me?
ramayan::7767.translation_literal: तिष्ठ (stay) / तिष्ठ (stay) / वरारोहे (O beautiful one) / न (not) / ते (your) / अस्ति (is) / करुणा (compassion) / मयि (for me) / न (not) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / हास्यशीलासि (you are fond of play) / किमर्थम् (why) / माम् (me) / उपेक्षसे (you ignore)
ramayan::7767.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7767.essence: Desire makes him chase what he cannot hold.
ramayan::7767.simple_meaning: A man pleads with a woman not to run away from him. He asks why she is ignoring him when he is calling her back.
ramayan::7767.simple_insight: Longing can make even a simple plea sound desperate.
ramayan::7767.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a man spots a woman he believes is Sita and calls after her again and again. He asks her to stop, accuses her of teasing him, and begs for a reply. The verse is part of his urgent attempt to make her turn back.
ramayan::7767.modern_relevance: You send three messages and keep checking your phone, hoping the other person will answer. The silence starts to feel personal, and your own need begins to speak louder than your words.
ramayan::7767.insight: It shows how desire can distort perception and turn pursuit into pleading.

ramayan::7768.verse_sanskrit: पीतकौशेयकेनासि सूचिता वरवर्णिनि । धावन्त्यपि मया दृष्टा तिष्ठ यद्यस्ति सौहृदम् । । 36028 । ।
ramayan::7768.verse_hindi: O lady of lovely complexion, I can see your yellow silk (flying), while you are running away. If you have love for me, stay on.
ramayan::7768.english_translation: O lady of lovely complexion, I can see your yellow silk flying as you run away. If you have love for me, stay on.
ramayan::7768.translation_literal: पीतकौशेयकेन (by the yellow silk garment) / असि (you are) / सूचिता (made visible, indicated) / वरवर्णिनि (O woman of lovely complexion) / धावन्ती (running) / अपि (even) / मया (by me) / दृष्टा (seen) / तिष्ठ (stay) / यदि (if) / अस्ति (there is) / सौहृदम् (friendship, affection)
ramayan::7768.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7768.essence: Even being seen does not become consent.
ramayan::7768.simple_meaning: Ravana tells the woman he can still see her by the flash of her yellow garment as she runs away, and asks her to stop if she cares for him.
ramayan::7768.simple_insight: Desire makes even pursuit sound like pleading.
ramayan::7768.detailed_meaning: In the grove, Ravana keeps calling after the woman he is chasing. He notices the flash of her yellow silk as she flees behind the trees and begs her to stop, trying to turn pursuit into intimacy.
ramayan::7768.modern_relevance: Someone keeps texting after a clear silence, reading every tiny sign as encouragement. Wanting closeness can make you ignore the other person's refusal.
ramayan::7768.insight: It shows how craving can dress itself up as affection and ignore consent.

ramayan::7769.verse_sanskrit: नैव सा नूनमथवा हिंसिता चारुहासिनी । कृच्छ्रप्राप्तं न मां नूनं यथोपेक्षितुमर्हति । । 36029 । ।
ramayan::7769.verse_hindi: O lady with a sweet smile I have never hurt you. When I am in difficulty it does not behove you to ignore me.
ramayan::7769.english_translation: O lady with a sweet smile, I have never hurt you. When I am in difficulty, it does not befit you to ignore me.
ramayan::7769.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) / सा (she) / नूनम् (surely) / अथवा (or else) / हिंसिता (harmed) / चारुहासिनी (sweet-smiling one) / कृच्छ्र-प्राप्तम् (one who has fallen into distress) / न (not) / माम् (me) / नूनम् (surely) / यथा (as) / उपेक्षितुम् (to ignore) / अर्हति (is fit / proper)
ramayan::7769.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7769.essence: Refusal feels unbearable when desire has already turned into self-pity.
ramayan::7769.simple_meaning: Ravana insists he has never harmed Sita and says it is wrong for her to ignore him while he suffers.
ramayan::7769.simple_insight: Desire can twist itself into grievance and call itself wounded innocence.
ramayan::7769.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands before the empty space where Sita should answer him. He has already begged, accused, and pleaded. Now he turns his own distress into an argument, insisting she owes him attention because he claims no harm has been done.
ramayan::7769.modern_relevance: You send three messages and get silence back. Instead of noticing the boundary, your mind starts building a case that you deserve a reply.
ramayan::7769.insight: It exposes how wounded pride can disguise entitlement as pain.

ramayan::7770.verse_sanskrit: व्यक्तं सा भक्षिता बाला राक्षसैः पिशिताशनैः । विभज्याङ्कानि सर्वाणि मया विरहिता प्रिया । । 36030 । ।
ramayan::7770.verse_hindi: It is clear that separated from me, the body of my young beloved is torn off and eaten away by carnivorous demons.
ramayan::7770.english_translation: It is clear that, separated from me, my young beloved has been torn apart and eaten by flesh-eating demons.
ramayan::7770.translation_literal: व्यक्तम् (clearly) / सा (she) / भक्षिता (devoured) / बाला (young woman) / राक्षसैः (by demons) / पिशिताशनैः (flesh-eating) / विभज्य (having torn apart) / अङ्कानि (limbs) / सर्वाणि (all) / मया (from me) / विरहिता (separated) / प्रिया (beloved)
ramayan::7770.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7770.essence: Distance makes Ravana's fear invent a tragedy before any truth is known.
ramayan::7770.simple_meaning: Ravana fears that his beloved has been torn apart and eaten by demons after being separated from him.
ramayan::7770.simple_insight: Grief can turn suspicion into a devastating certainty.
ramayan::7770.detailed_meaning: Separated from Sita, Ravana imagines the worst. He pictures her young body being torn apart by flesh-eating demons, and his panic deepens the sorrow already building in this scene of desperate searching.
ramayan::7770.modern_relevance: You miss a loved one’s call for one night, and your mind races to disaster before any facts arrive.
ramayan::7770.insight: It shows how separation can magnify fear until imagination feels like proof.

ramayan::7771.verse_sanskrit: नूनं तच्छुभदन्तोष्ठं सुनासं चारुकुण्डलम् । पूर्णचन्द्रनिभं ग्रस्तं मुखंनिष्प्रभतां गतम् । । 36031 । ।
ramayan::7771.verse_hindi: Her beautiful face with her sparkling teeth and lips, wellshaped nose, shining earrings has been like the full moon, eclipsed and rendered pale.
ramayan::7771.english_translation: Her beautiful face, with sparkling teeth, lips, a well-shaped nose, and shining earrings, had been like the full moon—now eclipsed and pale.
ramayan::7771.translation_literal: नूनं (surely) / तत् (that) / शुभदन्तोष्ठम् (with beautiful teeth and lips) / सुनासम् (with a fine nose) / चारुकुण्डलम् (with lovely earrings) / पूर्णचन्द्रनिभम् (like the full moon) / ग्रस्तम् (eclipsed / swallowed) / मुखम् (face) / निष्प्रभताम् (paleness) / गतम् (gone to)
ramayan::7771.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7771.essence: He can still see her beauty, and that makes the loss sharper.
ramayan::7771.simple_meaning: Ravana imagines Sita's face, once radiant and beautiful, now dimmed and ruined by the demons.
ramayan::7771.simple_insight: Grief can turn beauty into a wound you keep seeing everywhere.
ramayan::7771.detailed_meaning: In the enemy city, Ravana keeps searching for signs of Sita and speaking as if her body has been torn apart. This verse is part of his anguished imagining: he recalls her face in detail, then sees it as eclipsed and stripped of its former brightness.
ramayan::7771.modern_relevance: You replay a loved one's face after bad news, noticing every detail you once took for granted. Loss makes memory painfully vivid.
ramayan::7771.insight: It turns beauty into evidence of absence, sharpening Ravana's grief into obsessive imagining.

ramayan::7772.verse_sanskrit: सा हि चम्पकवर्णाभा ग्रीवा ग्रैवेयशोभिता । कोमला विलपन्त्यास्तु कान्ताया भक्षिता शुभा । । 36032 । ।
ramayan::7772.verse_hindi: That delicate, beautiful neck of my beloved having the complexion of a champak flower and adorned with necklaces was perhaps eaten up.
ramayan::7772.english_translation: That delicate, beautiful neck of my beloved, the color of a champak flower and adorned with necklaces, was perhaps eaten away.
ramayan::7772.translation_literal: सा (that) / हि (indeed) / चम्पकवर्णाभा (having champak-flower color) / ग्रीवा (neck) / ग्रैवेयशोभिता (adorned with necklaces) / कोमला (delicate) / विलपन्त्याः (of the weeping one) / तु (indeed) / कान्तायाः (of the beloved) / भक्षिता (eaten) / शुभा (beautiful)
ramayan::7772.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7772.essence: Grief turns even beauty into a wound.
ramayan::7772.simple_meaning: The speaker imagines that his beloved's soft, beautiful neck, once adorned with necklaces, has likely been devoured.
ramayan::7772.simple_insight: Grief keeps returning to the body, searching for what it has lost.
ramayan::7772.detailed_meaning: Rama is still trapped in the agony of imagining Sita's fate. After picturing her face and other features in the previous lines, he turns to her neck and necklaces, each detail making the loss more unbearable. This is not a teaching verse; it is grief breaking into fragments.
ramayan::7772.modern_relevance: You keep replaying small details of someone you lost — the necklace, the collar, the tilt of the neck — because grief clings to what it can still picture.
ramayan::7772.insight: It shows how mourning fixates on physical details when the mind cannot bear the whole loss.

ramayan::7773.verse_sanskrit: नूनं विक्षिप्यमाणौ तौ बाहू पल्लवकोमलौ । भक्षितौ वेपमानाग्रौ सहस्ताभरणाङ्गदौ । । 36033 । ।
ramayan::7773.verse_hindi: Her arms, delicate like tender leaves, their tips (fingers) quivering, adorned with armlets and bracelets have surely been eaten away.
ramayan::7773.english_translation: Her delicate arms, like tender leaves, with trembling fingertips and adorned with armlets and bracelets, have surely been eaten away.
ramayan::7773.translation_literal: नूनम् (surely) / विक्षिप्यमाणौ (being tossed or flung about) / तौ (those two) / बाहू (arms) / पल्लवकोमलौ (soft like tender leaves) / भक्षितौ (eaten away) / वेपमानाग्रौ (with trembling tips) / सहस्ताभरणाङ्गदौ (adorned with bracelets and armlets)
ramayan::7773.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7773.essence: Love without answers becomes a search through unbearable possibilities.
ramayan::7773.simple_meaning: Rama imagines Sita's soft arms, trembling and still adorned with bracelets, have been devoured too.
ramayan::7773.simple_insight: Grief turns love into unbearable imagining.
ramayan::7773.detailed_meaning: Alone in the forest after Sita's disappearance, Rama studies every sign and imagines what may have happened to her. He pictures her beautiful arms, once adorned with ornaments, and concludes with dread that they too may have been destroyed.
ramayan::7773.modern_relevance: You replay the last image of someone you love after they vanish from reach, and your mind fills the silence with fear.
ramayan::7773.insight: It shows how loss makes the mind invent painful details when certainty is gone.

ramayan::7774.verse_sanskrit: मया विरहिता बाला रक्षसां भक्षणाय वै । सार्धेनेव परित्यक्ता भक्षिता बहुबान्धवा । । 36034 । ।
ramayan::7774.verse_hindi: The young lady having many relations, forsaken by me, has been (perhaps) picked up by a demon for food and later abandoned halfeaten.
ramayan::7774.english_translation: The young woman, with many loved ones, has been left by me for the demons to devour; perhaps she was only half-eaten and then abandoned.
ramayan::7774.translation_literal: मया (by me) / विरहिता (separated, left alone) / बाला (young woman) / रक्षसां (of demons) / भक्षणाय (for devouring) / वै (indeed) / सार्धेन (half) / इव (as if) / परित्यक्ता (abandoned) / भक्षिता (eaten) / बहुबान्धवा (having many relatives)
ramayan::7774.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7774.essence: Loss makes the mind invent horrors before it knows the facts.
ramayan::7774.simple_meaning: Rama fears that Sita has been left alone, taken by a demon, and perhaps killed after being partly eaten.
ramayan::7774.simple_insight: Grief turns the mind into a place of terrible guesses.
ramayan::7774.detailed_meaning: In the forest after Sita’s disappearance, Rama is consumed by panic and guilt. Seeing no sign of her, he imagines the worst: that she has been seized by a demon and destroyed. The verse is part of his escalating despair.
ramayan::7774.modern_relevance: You miss one call from someone you love, and your mind runs straight to disaster. Fear fills in the blanks faster than facts can.
ramayan::7774.insight: It shows how separation can distort the mind into cruel certainty.

ramayan::7775.verse_sanskrit: हा लक्ष्मण महाबाहो पश्यसि त्वं प्रियां क्वचित् । हा प्रिये क्व गता भद्रे हा सीतेति पुनः पुनः । । 36035 । ।
ramayan::7775.verse_hindi: O longarmed Lakshmana, are you able to see my beloved anywhere? O noble lady, O darling, where have you gone? O Sita  SIta
ramayan::7775.english_translation: O longarmed Lakshmana, can you see my beloved anywhere? O noble lady, O dear one, where have you gone? O Sita!
ramayan::7775.translation_literal: हा (alas) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / महाबाहो (O longarmed one) / पश्यसि (do you see) / त्वं (you) / प्रियां (beloved) / क्वचित् (anywhere) / हा (alas) / प्रिये (O beloved) / क्व (where) / गता (gone) / भद्रे (O noble lady) / हा (alas) / सीतेति (Sita) / पुनः पुनः (again and again)
ramayan::7775.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7775.essence: Grief keeps asking the same question when love cannot find its answer.
ramayan::7775.simple_meaning: Rama cries out to Lakshmana, searching for Sita in anguish and calling her name again and again.
ramayan::7775.simple_insight: Love becomes raw when the person you cherish cannot be found.
ramayan::7775.detailed_meaning: Sita has vanished, and Rama is no longer speaking calmly. He turns to Lakshmana, then to the empty forest itself, calling out in panic and grief. This is the moment his search becomes a cry of loss.
ramayan::7775.modern_relevance: You’ve searched every room, checked every message, and still no reply comes. The mind keeps calling the same name because absence itself has become unbearable.
ramayan::7775.insight: It shows how loss can strip away composure and leave only urgent longing.

ramayan::7776.verse_sanskrit: इत्येवं विलपन्रामः परिधावन्वनाद्वनम् । क्वचिदुद्भ्रमते वेगात्क्वचिद्विभ्रमते बलात् । । 36036 । । क्वचिन्मत्त इवाभाति कान्तान्वेषणतत्परः ।
ramayan::7776.verse_hindi: Rama ran from forest to forest, now jumping, now taking strong strides, but all the time weeping, a madman busy in search of his beloved.
ramayan::7776.english_translation: Rama ran from forest to forest, now jumping, now taking strong strides, but all the time weeping, a madman busy in search of his beloved.
ramayan::7776.translation_literal: इत्येवं (thus) / विलपन् (lamenting) / रामः (Rama) / परिधावन् (running around) / वनात् वनम् (from forest to forest) / क्वचित् (sometimes) / उद्भ्रमते (jumps up) / वेगात् (with speed) / क्वचित् (sometimes) / विभ्रमते (moves wildly) / बलात् (with force) / क्वचित् (sometimes) / मत्तः इव (as if intoxicated) / आभाति (appears) / कान्तान्वेषणतत्परः (intent on searching for his beloved)
ramayan::7776.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7776.essence: Grief can drive even the strongest person into helpless motion.
ramayan::7776.simple_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by grief and runs through the forest searching for Sita, acting like a man beside himself.
ramayan::7776.simple_insight: Love can turn strength into helplessness when loss becomes real.
ramayan::7776.detailed_meaning: After Sita's disappearance, Rama and Lakshmana scour the forest in panic. Rama's grief breaks through royal composure; he rushes wildly from place to place, unable to think clearly, driven only by the need to find her.
ramayan::7776.modern_relevance: You search every room after a sudden breakup, checking places twice, unable to settle. Grief makes even the strongest mind move without rest.
ramayan::7776.insight: It shows how loss can scatter attention and make action frantic instead of effective.

ramayan::7777.verse_sanskrit: स वनानि नदीश्शैलान् गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च । । 36037 । । काननानि च वेगेन भ्रमत्यपरिसंस्थितः ।
ramayan::7777.verse_hindi: He rushed through forests, rivers, hills and mountain streams and through dense jungles with an unstable mind.
ramayan::7777.english_translation: He rushed through forests, rivers, hills, mountain streams, and dense jungles with an unsettled mind.
ramayan::7777.translation_literal: स (he) / वनानि (forests) / नदीः (rivers) / शैलान् (hills) / गिरिप्रस्रवणानि (mountain streams) / च (and) / काननानि (dense jungles) / च (and) / वेगेन (swiftly) / भ्रमति (moves about) / अपरिसंस्थितः (unsettled, unsteady)
ramayan::7777.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7777.essence: Grief drives him onward, but not yet with peace.
ramayan::7777.simple_meaning: Rama moves restlessly through every kind of terrain, driven by grief and unable to stay still.
ramayan::7777.simple_insight: Grief can scatter the mind so completely that even the body cannot rest.
ramayan::7777.detailed_meaning: Sita has vanished, and Rama is tearing through the wilderness in panic. He has already called out to Lakshmana and cried for Sita; now the search becomes frantic motion across forests, rivers, hills, and ravines.
ramayan::7777.modern_relevance: You’ve walked room to room after a painful message, checking the same place twice, unable to settle. The body keeps moving because the mind has not yet caught up.
ramayan::7777.insight: It shows how loss can turn searching into frantic motion instead of clear action.

ramayan::7778.verse_sanskrit: तथा स गत्वा विपुलम् महद्वनं परीत्य सर्वं त्वथ मैथिलीं प्रति । अनिष्ठिताशस्सचकार मार्गणे पुनः प्रियायाः परमं परिश्रमम् । । 36038 । ।
ramayan::7778.verse_hindi: Rama went about the vast forest searching for the princess from Mithila all over not giving up hope of finding her. He continued to make great efforts for searching his beloved.
ramayan::7778.english_translation: Rama went through the vast forest, searching everywhere for Sita, still not giving up hope of finding her. He kept making great effort to search for his beloved.
ramayan::7778.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / सः (he) / गत्वा (having gone) / विपुलम् (vast) / महत्-वनम् (great forest) / परीत्य (going around) / सर्वम् (all) / त्वथ (then) / मैथिलीम् (the princess from Mithila) / प्रति (toward) / अनिष्ठित-आशः (not giving up hope) / सचकार (made) / मार्गणे (in searching) / पुनः (again) / प्रियायाः (of the beloved) / परमम् (greatest) / परिश्रमम् (effort)
ramayan::7778.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7778.essence: Hope keeps love searching after strength is gone.
ramayan::7778.simple_meaning: Rama keeps searching the forest for Sita without losing hope. His love pushes him to keep trying even when the search is exhausting.
ramayan::7778.simple_insight: Love can keep you moving long after your strength should have run out.
ramayan::7778.detailed_meaning: Rama has already abandoned calm and composure and is tearing through the forest after Sita. This verse adds the detail that he keeps circling the vast wilderness, refusing to stop or lose hope, because the search for her has become his only purpose in that moment.
ramayan::7778.modern_relevance: You keep checking one more street, one more message, one more room after the person you love is gone. Exhaustion doesn't stop you, because hope still has hold of you.
ramayan::7778.insight: It shows how longing can turn effort into relentless searching, even after reason says to stop.

ramayan::7779.verse_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वाश्रमपदं शून्यं रामो दशरथात्मजः । रहितां पर्णशालां च विध्वस्तान्यासनानि च । । 3611 । । अदृष्ट्वा तत्र वैदेहीं सन्निरीक्ष्य च सर्वशः । उवाच रामः प्राक्रुश्य प्रगृह्य रुचिरौ भुजौ । । 3612 । ।
ramayan::7779.verse_hindi: Rama, son of Dasaratha, saw the empty cottage devoid of Sita. The mats were displaced. He searched everywhere but unable to see Vaidehi lifted his lovely arms and said:
ramayan::7779.english_translation: Rama, son of Dasaratha, saw the empty cottage without Sita. The mats were scattered. He searched everywhere, and failing to find Vaidehi, he raised his lovely arms and spoke.
ramayan::7779.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / आश्रमपदम् (the hermitage dwelling) / शून्यम् (empty) / रामः (Rama) / दशरथात्मजः (son of Dasaratha) / रहिताम् (devoid of) / पर्णशालाम् (leaf-hut) / च (and) / विध्वस्तानि (scattered, disturbed) / आसनानि (seats, mats) / च (and) / अदृष्ट्वा (not seeing) / तत्र (there) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / सन्निरीक्ष्य (having searched closely) / च (and) / सर्वशः (everywhere) / उवाच (spoke) / रामः (Rama) / प्राक्रुश्य (in anguish) / प्रगृह्य (lifting) / रुचिरौ (beautiful) / भुजौ (arms)
ramayan::7779.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7779.essence: Empty space can wound more sharply than words.
ramayan::7779.simple_meaning: Rama returns to the hermitage and finds it empty. The signs of struggle and Sita’s absence make him search in panic before he speaks out in grief.
ramayan::7779.simple_insight: Loss becomes real the moment the place itself goes silent.
ramayan::7779.detailed_meaning: Rama comes back to the hermitage after searching the forest and finds the cottage empty, the mats disturbed, and Sita gone. The sight breaks his composure. This verse captures the instant before grief turns into desperate questioning.
ramayan::7779.modern_relevance: You come home and know something is wrong before anyone speaks. A chair is out of place, a phone is silent, and your body understands the loss first.
ramayan::7779.insight: It shows how absence can hit before facts do, turning search into anguish.

ramayan::7780.verse_sanskrit: क्व नु लक्ष्मण वैदेही कं वा देशमितो गता । केनाहृता वा सौमित्रे भक्षिता केन वा प्रिया । । 3613 । ।
ramayan::7780.verse_hindi: O son of Sumitra, where is my beloved ? Where did she go? By whom was she abducted? Or, devoured? O Lakshmana
ramayan::7780.english_translation: O son of Sumitra, where is my beloved? Where has the princess of Videha gone from here? By whom has she been carried off, or has she been devoured, my dear one?
ramayan::7780.translation_literal: क्व (where) / नु (indeed) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / वैदेही (Sita, princess of Videha) / कं (to whom) / वा (or) / देशम् (place) / इतः (from here) / गता (gone) / केन (by whom) / आहृता (carried away) / वा (or) / भक्षिता (devoured) / केन (by whom) / वा (or) / प्रिया (beloved)
ramayan::7780.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7780.essence: Grief invents monsters when love cannot find what it lost.
ramayan::7780.simple_meaning: Rama, frantic with grief, asks Lakshmana where Sita has gone and whether someone carried her away or harmed her.
ramayan::7780.simple_insight: Love can turn into panic in a single breath when someone you trust disappears.
ramayan::7780.detailed_meaning: In the empty forest hermitage, Rama has already seen Sita's abandoned seat and searched in vain. Now, overwhelmed by fear, he turns to Lakshmana and asks where she has gone, who took her, or whether some beast devoured her. The verse captures the first shock of her disappearance.
ramayan::7780.modern_relevance: You come home and find the room too quiet, the phone unanswered, the chair still warm. In that instant, your mind races through every terrible possibility before reason can catch up.
ramayan::7780.insight: It shows how fear fills gaps with worst-case stories before facts arrive.

ramayan::7781.verse_sanskrit: वृक्षेणाच्छाद्य यदि मां सीते हसितुमिच्छसि । अलं ते हसितेनाद्य मां भजस्व सुदुःखितम् । । 3614 । ।
ramayan::7781.verse_hindi: O Sita if you intend to make fun by hiding behind a tree, I tell you it is enough. Stop it and come to this extremely sorrowful man.
ramayan::7781.english_translation: If you are hiding behind a tree to tease me, Sita, that is enough. Stop teasing and come to this grief-stricken man.
ramayan::7781.translation_literal: वृक्षेण (with a tree) / आच्छाद्य (having hidden) / यदि (if) / माम् (me) / सीते (Sita) / हसितुम् (to laugh, to tease) / इच्छसि (you wish) / अलम् (enough) / ते (for you) / हसितेन (with teasing/laughter) / अद्य (today) / माम् (me) / भजस्व (come to, approach) / सुदुःखितम् (deeply sorrowful)
ramayan::7781.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7781.essence: Grief makes absence feel like a cruel joke.
ramayan::7781.simple_meaning: Rama, overwhelmed by Sita's disappearance, pleads as if she might be hiding nearby and teasing him. He asks her to stop and come to him.
ramayan::7781.simple_insight: Grief can make even a great man speak to absence as if it were present.
ramayan::7781.detailed_meaning: Rama has reached the empty forest dwelling and found Sita gone. In panic and heartbreak, he calls out as though she might be hiding behind a tree and joking with him. The verse shows how shock distorts speech when love has been suddenly torn away.
ramayan::7781.modern_relevance: You check the empty room twice, then call a name into silence as if the person might answer. Loss can make the mind bargain with reality for one more second.
ramayan::7781.insight: It captures the first stage of loss: the mind reaches for denial before it can accept absence.

ramayan::7782.verse_sanskrit: यैस्सह क्रीडसे सीते विश्वस्तैर्मृगपोतकैः । एते हीनास्त्वया सौम्ये ध्यायन्त्यस्राविलेक्षणाः । । 3615 । ।
ramayan::7782.verse_hindi: O gentle  Sita those fawns who trusted you and played with you, are now separated from you. Brooding over you, their eyes are brimming with tears.
ramayan::7782.english_translation: O gentle Sita, those fawns who trusted you and played with you are now separated from you. Brooding over you, their eyes are brimming with tears.
ramayan::7782.translation_literal: यैः (with whom) / सह (together) / क्रीडसे (you played) / सीते (O Sita) / विश्वस्तैः (trusting) / मृगपोतकैः (with the fawns) / एते (these) / हीनाः (deprived, separated) / त्वया (from you) / सौम्ये (O gentle one) / ध्यायन्ति (they brood, long for) / अस्राविलेक्षणाः (with tear-filled eyes)
ramayan::7782.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7782.essence: Even the creatures around her feel the wound of her absence.
ramayan::7782.simple_meaning: Rama tells Sita that even the young deer she once played with now miss her and seem to grieve her absence.
ramayan::7782.simple_insight: Loss is so complete that even the forest feels the absence.
ramayan::7782.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is searching in anguish for Sita and speaking to her as if she might still be near. He points to the deer that once played around her, saying they too seem stricken by her disappearance, which deepens the scene of separation.
ramayan::7782.modern_relevance: You leave a place, and even the small routines there feel hollow. The chair, the corner, the pet that waited by the door — absence spreads farther than you expect.
ramayan::7782.insight: It turns grief outward, showing how separation alters the whole world around the one who is gone.

ramayan::7783.verse_sanskrit: सीतया रहितोऽहं वै न हि जीवामि लक्ष्मण । मृतं शोकेन महता सीताहरणजेन माम् । । 3616 । । परलोके महाराजो नूनं द्रक्ष्यति मे पिता ।
ramayan::7783.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, I cannot live without Sita. I am filled with deep grief on account of Sitas abduction. My late father, the king will certainly see me in the other world (I will definitely commit suicide).
ramayan::7783.english_translation: O Lakshmana, I cannot live without Sita. I am overcome by the great grief caused by Sita's abduction. My father, the great king, will surely see me in the other world.
ramayan::7783.translation_literal: सीतया (by Sita) / रहितः (separated) / अहम् (I) / वै (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / जीवामि (I live) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / मृतम् (as dead) / शोकेन (by grief) / महता (great) / सीताहरणजेन (born from Sita's abduction) / माम् (me) / परलोके (in the other world) / महाराजः (great king) / नूनम् (surely) / द्रक्ष्यति (will see) / मे (my) / पिता (father)
ramayan::7783.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7783.essence: Love can make separation feel like death before death arrives.
ramayan::7783.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that Sita's absence has left him unable to live, and the grief of her abduction feels like death itself.
ramayan::7783.simple_insight: Some losses hit so hard that they change how life feels immediately.
ramayan::7783.detailed_meaning: Rama, shattered by Sita's abduction, speaks to Lakshmana as if his life has already split in two. He says separation from Sita feels unbearable and even imagines meeting his father after death, showing how total his grief has become.
ramayan::7783.modern_relevance: You get the call that someone you love is missing, and the room goes silent. Your body is still there, but part of you has already fallen away.
ramayan::7783.insight: It names grief as a bodily, immediate collapse, not just a thought or mood.

ramayan::7784.verse_sanskrit: कथं प्रतिज्ञां संश्रुत्य मया त्वमभियोजितः । । 3617 । । अपूरयित्वा तं कालं मत्सकाशमिहागतः । कामवृत्तमनार्यं मां मृषावादिनमेव च । । 3618 । । धिक्त्वामिति परे लोके व्यक्तं वक्ष्यति मे पिता ।
ramayan::7784.verse_hindi: My father say will surely in the other world: Without completing the appointed period of the vow taken, how could you come here ? Fie upon you  You are irresponsible. You are ignoble. You are a liar.
ramayan::7784.english_translation: My father will surely say in the other world: 'Without completing the appointed period of the vow, how could you come here? Fie upon you. You are unrighteous. You are ignoble. You are a liar.'
ramayan::7784.translation_literal: कथम् (how) / प्रतिज्ञाम् (vow) / संश्रुत्य (having promised) / मया (by me) / त्वम् (you) / अभियोजितः (sent away/ordered) / अपूरयित्वा (without completing) / तं कालम् (that period) / मत्सकाशम् (to my presence) / इह (here) / आगतः (come) / कामवृत्तम् (acting by desire) / अनार्यम् (ignoble) / माम् (me) / मृषावादिनम् (speaker of falsehood) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / धिक् त्वाम् (fie upon you) / इति (thus) / परे लोके (in the other world) / व्यक्तम् (clearly) / वक्ष्यति (will say) / मे (my) / पिता (father)
ramayan::7784.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7784.essence: A true promise still binds you when suffering makes it hard.
ramayan::7784.simple_meaning: Rama says he cannot return before the promised time, because his father would blame him for breaking the vow and acting without honour.
ramayan::7784.simple_insight: A painful promise still counts. Integrity matters most when keeping it costs you.
ramayan::7784.detailed_meaning: Exiled in the forest, Rama is speaking through grief to Lakshmana after remembering Sita and his father. He fears the shame of returning before the vow is complete. The verse turns his sorrow into a fierce demand for honour.
ramayan::7784.modern_relevance: You promised someone you would stay the full course, and now quitting early would feel easier. This verse catches that moment when comfort tempts you to break your word.
ramayan::7784.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to honouring the commitment you already made.

ramayan::7785.verse_sanskrit: विवशं शोकसन्तप्तं दीनं भग्नमनोरथम् । । 3619 । । मामिहोत्सृज्य करुणं कीर्तिर्नरमिवानृजुम् । क्व गच्छसि वरारोहे मां नोत्सृज सुमध्यमे । । 36110 । । त्वया विरहितश्चाहं मोक्ष्ये जीवितमात्मनः ।
ramayan::7785.verse_hindi: O lovely lady where have you gone, leaving me here like fame deserting a crook? I am helpless griefstricken, pitiable, pathetic and disappointed. O lady of slender waist, leave me not. Separated from you, I will give up my life.
ramayan::7785.english_translation: O lovely lady, where have you gone, leaving me here like fame deserting a crooked man? I am helpless, grief-stricken, pitiable, and disappointed. O lady of slender waist, do not leave me. Separated from you, I will give up my life.
ramayan::7785.translation_literal: विवशम् (helpless) / शोकसन्तप्तम् (burning with grief) / दीनम् (wretched) / भग्नमनोरथम् (one whose hopes are broken) / माम् (me) / इह (here) / उत्सृज्य (having left) / करुणम् (pitiable) / कीर्तिः (fame) / नरम् इव (like a man) / अनृजुम् (crooked) / क्व (where) / गच्छसि (are you going) / वरारोहे (O lovely lady) / माम् (me) / न उत्सृज (do not abandon) / सुमध्यमे (O lady of slender waist) / त्वया विरहितः (deprived of you) / च अहम् (and I) / मोक्ष्ये (will give up) / जीवितम् (life) / आत्मनः (of myself)
ramayan::7785.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7785.essence: Loss makes even a noble heart speak in despair.
ramayan::7785.simple_meaning: Rama cries out in grief after losing Sita. He feels helpless and broken, begs her not to leave him, and says he cannot keep living without her.
ramayan::7785.simple_insight: Love can make even the strongest person sound completely undone.
ramayan::7785.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in the forest after Sita's disappearance, calling into empty space with no answer. The search has not yet become rescue; it is still raw absence. This line shows the first collapse of his composure.
ramayan::7785.modern_relevance: You call someone’s name in an empty room after they’ve left. The silence makes your body understand what your mind still resists.
ramayan::7785.insight: It reveals how separation strips away status, strength, and control, leaving only grief.

ramayan::7786.verse_sanskrit: इतीव विलपन्रामस्सीतादर्शनलालसः । । 36111 । । न ददर्श सुदुःखार्तो राघवो जनकात्मजाम् ।
ramayan::7786.verse_hindi: Deeply distressed, Rama who was anxious to see Sita, daughter of Janaka, wailed and wailed but could not see her.
ramayan::7786.english_translation: Deeply distressed, Rama, eager to see Sita, wailed and wailed but could not see Janaka's daughter.
ramayan::7786.translation_literal: इतीव (thus) / विलपन् (wailing) / रामः (Rama) / सीतादर्शनलालसः (longing for Sita's sight) / न (not) / ददर्श (saw) / सुदुःखार्तः (deeply afflicted with sorrow) / राघवः (Raghava) / जनकात्मजाम् (Janaka's daughter)
ramayan::7786.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7786.essence: Longing becomes unbearable when the one you seek is gone.
ramayan::7786.simple_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by grief and cannot find Sita anywhere.
ramayan::7786.simple_insight: Love hurts most when you can no longer reach the person you need.
ramayan::7786.detailed_meaning: Rama has returned to the place where Sita should be, but she is gone. He calls out in anguish, searching again and again, and finds only absence. The verse shows the raw collapse of a man who has lost the one person he most longs to see.
ramayan::7786.modern_relevance: You keep checking the empty room, the silent phone, the place where someone should have been. Grief makes even a familiar world feel uninhabited.
ramayan::7786.insight: It shifts attention from search to loss: the pain is not confusion, but absence.

ramayan::7787.verse_sanskrit: अनासादयमानं तं सीतां दशरथात्मजम् । । 36112 । । पङ्कमासाद्य विपुलं सीदन्तमिव कुञ्जरम् । लक्ष्मणो राममत्यर्थमुवाच हितकाम्यया । । 36113 । ।
ramayan::7787.verse_hindi: Lakshmana, dedicated to his wellbeing, spoke to Rama, son of Dasaratha, who was sinking like an elephant into the quagmire, when he failed to trace Sita.
ramayan::7787.english_translation: Lakshmana, devoted to Rama's wellbeing, spoke to Rama, son of Dasaratha, who was sinking like an elephant into a great quagmire after failing to find Sita.
ramayan::7787.translation_literal: अनासादयमानं (not finding) / तम् (him) / सीताम् (Sita) / दशरथात्मजम् (the son of Dasharatha) / पङ्कम् (quagmire) / आसाद्य (having reached) / विपुलम् (great) / सीदन्तम् (sinking) / इव (like) / कुञ्जरम् (an elephant) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / रामम् (Rama) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly) / उवाच (spoke) / हितकाम्यया (with desire for his welfare)
ramayan::7787.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7787.essence: Grief can unseat even Rama; care begins by steadying him.
ramayan::7787.simple_meaning: Lakshmana sees Rama overcome by grief after failing to find Sita and speaks to lift him up.
ramayan::7787.simple_insight: Even the strongest can sink in grief; steady support matters in that moment.
ramayan::7787.detailed_meaning: In the forest search for Sita, Rama has collapsed into sorrow after failing to find her. Lakshmana, moved by concern, steps in to steady him. This verse is a bridge into Lakshmana's counsel, not the counsel itself.
ramayan::7787.modern_relevance: You watch a friend go quiet after a devastating search or bad news. Before advice, they need someone who can stand beside them and keep them moving.
ramayan::7787.insight: It shows the value of calm support before problem-solving begins.

ramayan::7788.verse_sanskrit: मा विषादं महाबाहो कुरु यत्नं मया सह । इदं च हि वनं शूर बहुकन्दरशोभितम् । । 36114 । ।
ramayan::7788.verse_hindi: O longarmed, heroic Rama, do not grieve. This forest is full of caves. Let us try together.
ramayan::7788.english_translation: O long-armed, heroic Rama, do not grieve. Let us make an effort together. This forest is beautiful with many caves.
ramayan::7788.translation_literal: मा (do not) / विषादं (grief) / महाबाहो (O long-armed one) / कुरु (do) / यत्नं (effort) / मया (with me) / सह (together) / इदं (this) / च (and) / हि (indeed) / वनं (forest) / शूर (O heroic one) / बहुकन्दरशोभितम् (adorned with many caves)
ramayan::7788.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7788.essence: Grief loosens when someone stands beside you and keeps moving.
ramayan::7788.simple_meaning: Lakshmana urges Rama not to despair and to keep searching with him. He points to the forest's caves as places where Sita might be found.
ramayan::7788.simple_insight: When grief freezes you, shared effort can keep hope alive.
ramayan::7788.detailed_meaning: Rama has just searched in vain for Sita and collapsed into anguish. Lakshmana, seeing his brother break under the strain, steadies him and offers his own strength. This is the moment he turns sorrow into action.
ramayan::7788.modern_relevance: You are staring at a phone that still has no reply, and your chest is tightening. The right next move may not be certainty — it may be one steady person saying, 'I'll look with you.'
ramayan::7788.insight: It shifts you from helpless sadness to shared, practical searching.

ramayan::7789.verse_sanskrit: प्रियकाननसञ्चारा वनोन्मत्ता च मैथिली । सा वनं वा प्रविष्टा स्यान्नलिनीं वा सुपुष्पिताम् । । 36115 । ।
ramayan::7789.verse_hindi: Sita is madly in love with the forest. She might have entered deep into the jungle or into a fully blossomed lotuspond.
ramayan::7789.english_translation: Sita, who loved wandering in the forest, may have entered the forest or a blooming lotus pond.
ramayan::7789.translation_literal: प्रियकाननसञ्चारा (fond of moving in lovely forests) / वनोन्मत्ता (forest-absorbed) / च (and) / मैथिली (Maithili) / सा (she) / वनं (forest) / वा (or) / प्रविष्टा (entered) / स्यात् (may be) / नलिनीं (lotus pond) / वा (or) / सुपुष्पिताम् (fully blossomed)
ramayan::7789.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7789.essence: Love looks for the missing person by knowing her nature.
ramayan::7789.simple_meaning: Lakshmana is guessing where Sita might have gone, describing her as someone who loves wandering in forests and may have entered a grove or lotus pond.
ramayan::7789.simple_insight: Searching for someone you love often begins with imagining where their heart would naturally go.
ramayan::7789.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is trying to comfort Rama after Sita’s disappearance. He imagines places Sita would enjoy — forests, ponds, rivers — and reasons that she may have wandered there or hidden nearby. It is a hopeful search, not a settled truth.
ramayan::7789.modern_relevance: You lose track of someone in a crowded park and start thinking like this: where would they have gone if they were simply following what they love?
ramayan::7789.insight: It shifts the search from panic to informed guessing, using knowledge of Sita’s nature to narrow the possibilities.

ramayan::7790.verse_sanskrit: सरितं वापि सम्प्राप्ता मीनवञ्जुलसेविताम् । स्नातुकामा निलीना स्याद्धासकामा वने क्वचित् । । 36116 । ।
ramayan::7790.verse_hindi: Maybe she has gone to take a dip in the river full of reeds and fishes  Or has hidden somewhere for the sake of fun.
ramayan::7790.english_translation: Maybe she has gone to take a dip in the river full of reeds and fishes, or has hidden somewhere for the sake of fun.
ramayan::7790.translation_literal: सरितम् (river) / वा (or) / अपि (also) / सम्प्राप्ता (having reached) / मीनवञ्जुलसेविताम् (served by fish and reeds) / स्नातुकामा (wishing to bathe) / निलीना (hidden) / स्यात् (may be) / हासकामा (wishing for play) / वने (in the forest) / क्वचित् (somewhere)
ramayan::7790.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7790.essence: Hope fills the gap before certainty arrives.
ramayan::7790.simple_meaning: Sita may have gone to bathe in a river, or she may be hiding somewhere playfully in the forest.
ramayan::7790.simple_insight: When you cannot find someone you love, the mind starts inventing hopeful possibilities.
ramayan::7790.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are searching the forest for Sita. Trying to make sense of her absence, they imagine she may have gone to a river to bathe or hidden herself for play. It is a searching guess, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::7790.modern_relevance: You replay the last place they were seen, inventing harmless explanations because the real one feels too heavy to hold.
ramayan::7790.insight: It shows a mind grasping for comforting possibilities before facing loss.

ramayan::7791.verse_sanskrit: वित्रासयितुकामा वा लीना स्यात्कानने क्वचित् । जिज्ञासमाना वैदेही त्वां मां च पुरुषर्षभ । । 36117 । । तस्याह्यन्वेषणे श्रीमन् क्षिप्रमेव यतावहे ।
ramayan::7791.verse_hindi: O best of men, maybe Vaidehi has hidden in the forest intending to scare you and me. She wishes to test our love. O blessed Rama let us ransack the forest immediately.
ramayan::7791.english_translation: O best of men, maybe Vaidehi has hidden in the forest intending to scare you and me. She wishes to test our love. O blessed Rama, let us search for her immediately.
ramayan::7791.translation_literal: वित्रासयितुकामा (wishing to frighten) / वा (or) / लीना (hidden) / स्यात् (may be) / कानने (in the forest) / क्वचित् (somewhere) / जिज्ञासमाना (wishing to test) / वैदेही (Vaidehi) / त्वाम् (you) / माम् (me) / च (and) / पुरुषर्षभ (O best of men) / तस्य (of her) / हि (indeed) / अन्वेषणे (in the search) / श्रीमन् (O blessed one) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / एव (indeed) / यतावहे (let us strive)
ramayan::7791.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7791.essence: Uncertainty turns love into urgent searching.
ramayan::7791.simple_meaning: The speaker imagines Sita may be hiding somewhere in the forest and urges Rama to search at once.
ramayan::7791.simple_insight: When fear rises, the mind starts inventing hopeful explanations and urgent plans.
ramayan::7791.detailed_meaning: Hanuman-like searching is not yet here; this is still the anxious speculation of the search party in the forest. They have not found Sita, so they imagine she may be hiding nearby and press Rama to keep looking without delay.
ramayan::7791.modern_relevance: You lose track of someone you care about and your mind starts filling the silence with guesses. Before panic hardens, you keep searching and refuse to stop at fear.
ramayan::7791.insight: It shifts the mind from helpless worry to immediate, directed searching.

ramayan::7792.verse_sanskrit: वनं सर्वं विचिनुवो यत्र सा जनकात्मजा । । 36118 । । मन्यसे यदि काकुत्स्थ मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः ।
ramayan::7792.verse_hindi: O scion of the Kakutsthas, let us search all over the forest if you please. Do not indulge in sorrow.
ramayan::7792.english_translation: O scion of the Kakutsthas, let us search all over the forest if you please. Do not indulge in sorrow.
ramayan::7792.translation_literal: वनम् (forest) / सर्वम् (entire) / विचिनुवः (let us search) / यत्र (where) / सा (she) / जनकात्मजा (daughter of Janaka) / मन्यसे (if you think) / यदि (if) / काकुत्स्थ (O Kakutstha) / मा स्म (do not) / शोके (in sorrow) / मनः (mind) / कृथाः (place/do)
ramayan::7792.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7792.essence: Grief is real, but it must not stop the search.
ramayan::7792.simple_meaning: Lakshmana urges Rama to search the entire forest for Sita and not lose heart in grief.
ramayan::7792.simple_insight: Even in panic, you can choose the next useful step instead of collapsing inward.
ramayan::7792.detailed_meaning: Rama has lost Sita and the forest has become a field of desperate searching. Lakshmana, trying to steady him, says they should search every corner and not let sorrow stop the effort. This is brotherly resolve under pressure.
ramayan::7792.modern_relevance: You’ve checked every room, every message, every place they might have gone. Panic wants to freeze you; this verse says keep moving, keep looking, keep your mind usable.
ramayan::7792.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to focused action under stress.

ramayan::7793.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु सौहार्दाल्लक्ष्मणेन समाहितः । । 36119 । । सह सौमित्रिणा रामो विचेतुमुपचक्रमे ।
ramayan::7793.verse_hindi: When Lakshmana consoled him so affectionately Rama became composed. He continued the search with Lakshmana, son of Sumitra.
ramayan::7793.english_translation: When Lakshmana consoled him so affectionately, Rama became composed. He continued the search with Lakshmana, son of Sumitra.
ramayan::7793.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (being thus spoken to) / तु (indeed) / सौहार्दात् (from affection) / लक्ष्मणेन (by Lakshmana) / समाहितः (became composed) / सह (together with) / सौमित्रिणा (with the son of Sumitra) / रामः (Rama) / विचेतुम् (to search) / उपचक्रमे (began)
ramayan::7793.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7793.essence: Affection steadies grief and turns it back toward action.
ramayan::7793.simple_meaning: Lakshmana's loving words steady Rama, and the two brothers keep searching for Sita together.
ramayan::7793.simple_insight: A caring voice can pull you back from grief and into action.
ramayan::7793.detailed_meaning: After Lakshmana urges him not to sink into sorrow, Rama regains composure. The two brothers then resume their search for Sita in the forest, moving forward together instead of freezing in despair.
ramayan::7793.modern_relevance: You are spiralling after bad news, and a steady friend says just enough to bring you back. The next step is still there, waiting.
ramayan::7793.insight: It shows how supportive words can restore clarity and restart effort.

ramayan::7794.verse_sanskrit: तौ वनानि गिरींश्चैव सरितश्च सरांसि च । । 36120 । । निखिलेन विचिन्वानौ सीतां दशरथात्मजौ ।
ramayan::7794.verse_hindi: The two sons of Dasaratha went on searching for Sita in forests, mountains, rivers, ponds everywhere.
ramayan::7794.english_translation: The two sons of Dasaratha searched everywhere for Sita — in forests, mountains, rivers, and ponds.
ramayan::7794.translation_literal: तौ (those two) / वनानि (forests) / गिरीन् (mountains) / च (and) / एव (also) / सरितः (rivers) / च (and) / सरांसि (ponds) / च (and) / निखिलेन (completely) / विचिन्वानौ (searching) / सीताम् (Sita) / दशरथात्मजौ (the two sons of Dasharatha)
ramayan::7794.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7794.essence: Searching harder cannot undo what has already happened.
ramayan::7794.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana searched every kind of place for Sita, but still could not find her.
ramayan::7794.simple_insight: Some losses cannot be fixed by effort alone.
ramayan::7794.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana move through forests, hills, rivers, and ponds, searching every corner for Sita after her abduction. This verse is part of the search itself, not a teaching moment, showing their urgent but failing effort.
ramayan::7794.modern_relevance: You retrace every step after the missed call, the lost file, the argument, hoping one more look will change the result. Sometimes the search itself is all you have.
ramayan::7794.insight: It captures relentless searching without resolution, before the deeper grief fully lands.

ramayan::7795.verse_sanskrit: तस्य शैलस्य सानूनि गुहाश्च शिखराणि च । । 36121 । । निखिलेन विचिन्वानौ नैव तामभिजग्मतुः ।
ramayan::7795.verse_hindi: They were not able to find Sita even though they searched all over the mountain slopes, caves and peaks.
ramayan::7795.english_translation: They could not find her even after searching every slope, cave, and peak of that mountain.
ramayan::7795.translation_literal: तस्य (of that) / शैलस्य (mountain) / सानूनि (slopes) / गुहाः (caves) / च (and) / शिखराणि (peaks) / च (and) / निखिलेन (completely) / विचिन्वानौ (searching) / नैव (not even) / ताम् (her) / अभिजग्मतुः (they found)
ramayan::7795.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7795.essence: Even exhaustive searching can end in helplessness.
ramayan::7795.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana searched the mountain thoroughly, but Sita was still not found.
ramayan::7795.simple_insight: Sometimes effort meets silence, and the search itself becomes part of the sorrow.
ramayan::7795.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are still combing the mountain where Sita might be hidden. They check slopes, caves, and peaks, but the search brings no relief. This verse simply marks the painful fact that their effort has not yet succeeded.
ramayan::7795.modern_relevance: You’ve checked every room, every message, every place she might be. The answer still isn’t there, and the not-knowing keeps stretching on.
ramayan::7795.insight: It shows the frustration of total effort without result, before the next clue arrives.

ramayan::7796.verse_sanskrit: विचित्य सर्वतश्शैलं रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवित् । । 36122 । । नेह पश्यामि सौमित्रे वैदेहीं पर्वते शुभाम् ।
ramayan::7796.verse_hindi: After searching her all over, Rama said  Saumitri, I am unable to find the noble Vaidehi on the mountain
ramayan::7796.english_translation: After searching the whole mountain, Rama said to Lakshmana, 'I do not see the noble Vaidehi here on the mountain.'
ramayan::7796.translation_literal: विचित्य (having searched) / सर्वतश्शैलं (the whole mountain) / रामः (Rama) / लक्ष्मणम् (to Lakshmana) / अब्रवित् (said) / नेह (not here) / पश्यामि (I see) / सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra) / वैदेहीं (Vaidehi) / पर्वते (on the mountain) / शुभाम् (the noble one)
ramayan::7796.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7796.essence: Searching harder does not always change what is missing.
ramayan::7796.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that, after searching the mountain thoroughly, he still cannot find Sita there.
ramayan::7796.simple_insight: Sometimes effort ends in a hard truth: the search was real, but the answer is still missing.
ramayan::7796.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have already searched forests, rivers, caves, and peaks. On this mountain too, Rama looks again and admits to Lakshmana that Sita is not there. The verse marks the deepening of their helpless search.
ramayan::7796.modern_relevance: You have checked every folder, every message, every corner of the room, and the thing is still gone. Some searches end not with certainty, but with the ache of not finding.
ramayan::7796.insight: It teaches you to face absence directly instead of pretending a thorough search has guaranteed an answer.

ramayan::7797.verse_sanskrit: ततो दुःखाभिसन्तप्तो लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । । 36123 । । विचरन्दण्डकारण्यं भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम् ।
ramayan::7797.verse_hindi: Going about the Dandaka forest Lakshmana, consumed by sorrow, said  to his brother, glowing with brilliance:
ramayan::7797.english_translation: Then Lakshmana, tormented by grief, spoke to his brilliant brother while moving through the Dandaka forest:
ramayan::7797.translation_literal: ततः (then) / दुःखाभिसन्तप्तः (tormented by sorrow) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / वाक्यम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / विचरन् (wandering) / दण्डकारण्यम् (the Dandaka forest) / भ्रातरम् (to his brother) / दीप्ततेजसम् (of radiant brilliance)
ramayan::7797.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7797.essence: Grief does not silence Lakshmana’s loyalty; it sharpens it.
ramayan::7797.simple_meaning: Lakshmana, overwhelmed by grief, speaks to Rama while they continue searching through the forest.
