ramayan::7797.simple_insight: Grief does not stop the loyal from keeping watch and moving forward.
ramayan::7797.detailed_meaning: Rama has searched the mountain and found no trace of Sita. In the middle of that helpless search through Dandaka, Lakshmana, aching with sorrow, turns to his radiant brother and speaks. The next verse carries his reassurance.
ramayan::7797.modern_relevance: You keep walking after bad news, still scanning every corner for a solution. Even when your chest is tight, someone beside you may still need your steady voice.
ramayan::7797.insight: It shows loyalty speaking even in despair, before the answer has arrived.

ramayan::7798.verse_sanskrit: प्राप्स्यसि त्वं महाप्राज्ञ मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम् । । 36124 । । यथा विष्णुर्महाबाहुर्बलिं बद्ध्वा महीमिमाम् ।
ramayan::7798.verse_hindi: O longarmed brother O wise sire  just as Visnu obtained the earth by binding Bali you will obtain Sita certainly.
ramayan::7798.english_translation: O wise, long-armed brother, you will surely obtain Sita, daughter of Janaka, just as Vishnu won this earth by binding Bali.
ramayan::7798.translation_literal: प्राप्स्यसि (you will obtain) / त्वं (you) / महाप्राज्ञ (O very wise one) / मैथिलीं (Maithili) / जनकात्मजाम् (daughter of Janaka) / यथा (just as) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / महाबाहुः (the long-armed one) / बलिं (Bali) / बद्ध्वा (having bound) / महीम् इमाम् (this earth)
ramayan::7798.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7798.essence: Past victory becomes a reason to keep trusting the future.
ramayan::7798.simple_meaning: Lakshmana reassures Rama that Sita will be recovered, comparing it to Vishnu’s victory over Bali.
ramayan::7798.simple_insight: Hope can be steady, not vague. A clear memory of past victory can hold you up in grief.
ramayan::7798.detailed_meaning: Rama has searched the mountain and cannot find Sita. Lakshmana, seeing his brother crushed by sorrow, answers with confidence: just as Vishnu once overcame Bali and regained the earth, Rama too will recover Sita.
ramayan::7798.modern_relevance: You’ve walked every room, checked every message, and still found nothing. In that hollow moment, someone beside you says, “Not yet means not never,” and your breathing changes.
ramayan::7798.insight: It shifts the mind from despair to confident remembrance of what has been possible before.

ramayan::7799.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु सौहार्दाल्लक्ष्मणेन स राघवः । । 36125 । । उवाच दीनया वाचा दुःखाभिहतचेतनः ।
ramayan::7799.verse_hindi: Having been addressed thus by Lakshmana, Raghava with a griefstriken heart said these piteous words :
ramayan::7799.english_translation: Having been addressed thus by Lakshmana, Raghava, with a grief-stricken heart, spoke these piteous words.
ramayan::7799.translation_literal: एवमुक्तः (thus addressed) / तु (indeed) / सौहार्दात् (out of affection) / लक्ष्मणेन (by Lakshmana) / सः (he) / राघवः (Raghava) / उवाच (spoke) / दीनया (pitiful) / वाचा (with voice) / दुःखाभिहतचेतनः (whose mind was struck by sorrow)
ramayan::7799.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7799.essence: Grief can make even a reply sound broken.
ramayan::7799.simple_meaning: Lakshmana spoke to Rama with affection, and Rama answered in a voice heavy with grief.
ramayan::7799.simple_insight: Even the strongest voice can break when sorrow has done its work.
ramayan::7799.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana has just encouraged Rama in the Dandaka forest, reminding him that Sita will be found. Rama, exhausted by grief and still searching, answers not with confidence but with a pained voice. This is a transition verse that leads into his lament.
ramayan::7799.modern_relevance: You get the reassuring text, but your chest is still tight and your mind still circles the same loss. Sometimes grief answers before hope can.
ramayan::7799.insight: It shifts attention from the content of speech to the emotional state that shapes it.

ramayan::7800.verse_sanskrit: वनं सर्वं सुविचितं पद्मिन्यः फुल्लपङ्कजाः । । 36126 । । गिरिश्चायं महाप्राज्ञ बहुकन्दरनिर्झरः । न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीं प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसीम् । । 36127 । ।
ramayan::7800.verse_hindi: O wise Lakshmana I have searched the entire forest, the ponds with fully blossomed lotuses, the mountains with many caves and streams. But could not see Vaidehi who is dearer to me than my life.
ramayan::7800.english_translation: O wise Lakshmana, I have searched the whole forest, the ponds with blooming lotuses, and this mountain with many caves and streams. Yet I do not see Vaidehi, who is dearer to me than my life.
ramayan::7800.translation_literal: वनं (forest) / सर्वं (entire) / सुविचितं (well-searched) / पद्मिन्यः (lotus ponds) / फुल्लपङ्कजाः (with fully-bloomed lotuses) / गिरिः (mountain) / च (and) / अयम् (this) / महाप्राज्ञ (O very wise one) / बहुकन्दरनिर्झरः (with many caves and streams) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / पश्यामि (I see) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / प्राणेभ्यः (than life) / अपि (even) / गरीयसीम् (dearer, greater)
ramayan::7800.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7800.essence: Searching harder cannot fill the hole left by loss.
ramayan::7800.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that he has searched every likely place in the forest, but still cannot find Sita, whom he values more than his own life.
ramayan::7800.simple_insight: Love becomes unbearable when the one you seek is missing.
ramayan::7800.detailed_meaning: After Sita's abduction, Rama and Lakshmana search the forest together. Rama lists the ponds, mountains, caves, and streams they have already checked, but the effort only sharpens his grief. This is the moment his search turns into raw despair.
ramayan::7800.modern_relevance: You have checked every room, every message, every place she might have gone. The silence is the wound. That is what searching feels like when love has already been broken open.
ramayan::7800.insight: It shows how grief narrows the mind into relentless searching and unbearable absence.

ramayan::7801.verse_sanskrit: एवं स विलपन्रामस्सीताहरणकर्शितः । दीनश्शोकसमाविष्टो मुहूर्तं विह्वलोऽभवत् । । 36128 । ।
ramayan::7801.verse_hindi: Thus tormented by the abduction of Sita, Rama felt dejected and cried.Overpowered by grief he lost his consciousness for a moment.
ramayan::7801.english_translation: Thus tormented by the abduction of Sita, Rama felt dejected and cried. Overpowered by grief he lost his consciousness for a moment.
ramayan::7801.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / सः (he) / विलपन् (lamenting) / रामः (Rama) / सीता-हरण (Sita's abduction) / कर्शितः (tormented) / दीनः (dejected) / शोक-समाविष्टः (filled with grief) / मुहूर्तम् (for a moment) / विह्वलः (confused, overcome) / अभवत् (became)
ramayan::7801.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7801.essence: Love can shatter composure when absence becomes real.
ramayan::7801.simple_meaning: Rama breaks under the pain of losing Sita. He cries, grows overwhelmed, and briefly loses his composure.
ramayan::7801.simple_insight: Even the strongest hearts can buckle when love is torn away.
ramayan::7801.detailed_meaning: After searching the forest, Rama receives no relief. The loss of Sita hits him so hard that he can only lament, sink into grief, and lose awareness for a moment. This verse shows the raw human cost of separation before he regathers himself.
ramayan::7801.modern_relevance: You keep calling and there is still no reply. The room gets quiet, your chest tightens, and for a second you cannot think straight.
ramayan::7801.insight: It shows grief as a real force that can interrupt thought, not just an emotion to be managed.

ramayan::7802.verse_sanskrit: सन्तप्तो ह्यवसन्नाङ्गो गतबुद्धिर्विचेतनः । निषसादातुरो दीनो निश्श्वस्याशीतमायतम् । । 36129 । ।
ramayan::7802.verse_hindi: By grief tormented, limbs enervated, intellect atrophied, senses switched off, he felt anxious and depressed and sighed long and hot.
ramayan::7802.english_translation: Tormented by grief, his limbs weakened, his mind dulled, and his senses stunned, he sat down helpless and miserable, breathing a long, hot sigh.
ramayan::7802.translation_literal: सन्तप्तः (tormented) / हि (indeed) / अवसन्नाङ्गः (with weakened limbs) / गतबुद्धिः (with dulled mind) / विचेतनः (unconscious, stunned) / निषसाद (sat down) / आतुरः (distressed) / दीनः (miserable) / निश्श्वस्य (breathing out) / आशीतम् (hot) / आयतम् (long)
ramayan::7802.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7802.essence: Grief can leave even the strongest person unable to stand.
ramayan::7802.simple_meaning: Grief has overwhelmed Rama so completely that his body, mind, and senses all give way. He sits down, exhausted and stunned.
ramayan::7802.simple_insight: Deep loss can drain even the strongest person of strength and clarity.
ramayan::7802.detailed_meaning: After searching the forest for Sita, Rama reaches a breaking point. The pain of her abduction has left him physically weakened, mentally blank, and unable to steady himself. This verse shows the collapse before the next cry of anguish.
ramayan::7802.modern_relevance: You keep searching your phone for one message that never comes, and suddenly your body feels heavy too. Grief does not stay in the mind; it drains everything.
ramayan::7802.insight: It shows how sorrow can shut down thought, energy, and speech all at once.

ramayan::7803.verse_sanskrit: बहुलं स तु निश्श्वस्य रामो राजीवलोचनः । हा प्रियेति विचुक्रोश बहुशो बाष्पगद्गदः । । 36130 । ।
ramayan::7803.verse_hindi: Rama, his throat choked, shed propuse tears, sighing, O my darling.
ramayan::7803.english_translation: Rama, lotus-eyed, sighed again and again. His throat choked with tears, he cried out many times, “Oh, my beloved!”
ramayan::7803.translation_literal: बहुलम् (many times) / सः (he) / तु (indeed) / निश्श्वस्य (having sighed) / रामः (Rama) / राजीवलोचनः (lotus-eyed) / हा (alas) / प्रिये (beloved) / इति (thus) / विचुक्रोश (cried out) / बहुशः (again and again) / बाष्पगद्गदः (with voice choked by tears)
ramayan::7803.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7803.essence: Even the strongest heart can break openly when love is torn away.
ramayan::7803.simple_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by grief for Sita. He keeps sighing and crying out her name, unable to hold himself together.
ramayan::7803.simple_insight: Love can hurt so deeply that even strength breaks into tears.
ramayan::7803.detailed_meaning: After Sita’s abduction, Rama is no longer the steady prince of Ayodhya but a man stunned by loss. He sighs, chokes on tears, and calls out to the one he has lost. Lakshmana will soon try to steady him.
ramayan::7803.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after a message that changes everything. Your chest tightens, and the name you want to say is the one you cannot reach.
ramayan::7803.insight: It shows grief before recovery begins, when feeling itself overwhelms speech and action.

ramayan::7804.verse_sanskrit: तं ततस्सान्त्वयामास लक्ष्मणः प्रियबान्धवः । बहुप्रकारं धर्मज्ञः प्रश्रितं प्रश्रिताञ्जलिः । । 36131 । ।
ramayan::7804.verse_hindi: Then Lakshmana, the knower of dharma and a dear friend offered obeisance most humbly with folded palms and consoled Rama in many ways.
ramayan::7804.english_translation: Then Lakshmana, the knower of dharma and a dear friend, offered obeisance with folded palms and consoled Rama in many ways.
ramayan::7804.translation_literal: तम् (him) / ततः (then) / सान्त्वयामास (consoled) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / प्रियबान्धवः (dear kinsman, dear friend) / बहुप्रकारम् (in many ways) / धर्मज्ञः (knower of dharma) / प्रश्रितम् (humble) / प्रश्रिताञ्जलिः (with folded, humble palms)
ramayan::7804.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7804.essence: Love sometimes means kneeling beside someone who cannot be reasoned with.
ramayan::7804.simple_meaning: Lakshmana bowed humbly and tried many ways to comfort Rama in his grief.
ramayan::7804.simple_insight: Real support is often quiet, humble, and repeated when someone is breaking down.
ramayan::7804.detailed_meaning: Rama has just collapsed into grief over Sita. Lakshmana, his devoted brother, steps forward not with argument or pride, but with folded hands and gentle words. This is the human side of the exile: one brother trying to steady another when reason has already failed.
ramayan::7804.modern_relevance: Your friend is crying in the car after a call that changed everything. You do not fix it with one perfect sentence. You stay, speak gently, and try again.
ramayan::7804.insight: It shifts support from clever advice to humble presence and repeated reassurance.

ramayan::7805.verse_sanskrit: अनादृत्य तु तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणोष्ठपुटाच्च्युतम् । अपश्यंस्तां प्रियां सीतां प्राक्रोशत्स पुनः पुनः । । 36132 । ।
ramayan::7805.verse_hindi: Without caring  for the words from the lips of Lakshmana, Rama sobbed loudly, unable to see his beloved Sita.
ramayan::7805.english_translation: Without heeding Lakshmana's words, Rama sobbed again and again, unable to see his beloved Sita.
ramayan::7805.translation_literal: अनादृत्य (ignoring) / तु (but) / तत्-वाक्यम् (that speech) / लक्ष्मण-ओष्ठ-पुटात्-च्युतम् (fallen from Lakshmana's lips) / अपश्यन् (not seeing) / ताम् (her) / प्रियाम् (beloved) / सीताम् (Sita) / प्राक्रोशत् (cried out) / सः (he) / पुनः पुनः (again and again)
ramayan::7805.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7805.essence: Grief makes even comfort unheard when the beloved is gone.
ramayan::7805.simple_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by grief and cannot be comforted because he cannot see Sita.
ramayan::7805.simple_insight: Some grief is too deep for advice; it only circles back into tears.
ramayan::7805.detailed_meaning: Rama has just broken down in sorrow, and Lakshmana tries to comfort him with respectful words. But Rama cannot take them in. His mind is fixed only on the missing Sita, and his grief keeps returning in waves.
ramayan::7805.modern_relevance: You can hear a friend trying to calm you, but your mind stays on the one absence that hurts most.
ramayan::7805.insight: It shows how loss can shut out even wise counsel and keep attention locked on what is missing.

ramayan::7806.verse_sanskrit: सीतामपश्यन्धर्मात्मा शोकोपहतचेतनः । विललाप महाबाहू रामः कमललोचनः । । 3621 । ।
ramayan::7806.verse_hindi: The righteous, the longarmed,lotuseyed Rama, unable to see Sita wept with his senses overwhilmed by grief.
ramayan::7806.english_translation: The righteous, long-armed, lotus-eyed Rama wept, unable to see Sita, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
ramayan::7806.translation_literal: सीताम् (Sita) / अपश्यन् (not seeing) / धर्मात्मा (righteous-minded) / शोकोपहतचेतनः (with mind struck by grief) / विललाप (lamented) / महाबाहूः (long-armed one) / रामः (Rama) / कमललोचनः (lotus-eyed one)
ramayan::7806.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7806.essence: Loss can overwhelm even the most steadfast person.
ramayan::7806.simple_meaning: Rama breaks down in grief because he cannot find Sita. The verse shows his pain, not a teaching.
ramayan::7806.simple_insight: Even the strongest heart can be undone by separation.
ramayan::7806.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in anguish after losing sight of Sita. Lakshmana has just tried to comfort him, but grief has taken over completely. This verse is part of a flowing lament, showing Rama’s collapse before he speaks again.
ramayan::7806.modern_relevance: You search every room after a painful argument, hoping the person you love will appear. The silence itself starts to feel physical.
ramayan::7806.insight: It turns grief into a visible force that can seize even a disciplined mind.

ramayan::7807.verse_sanskrit: पश्यन्निव च तां सीतामपश्यन्मदनार्दितः । उवाच राघवो वाक्यं विलापाश्रयदुर्वचम् । । 3622 । ।
ramayan::7807.verse_hindi: Under the spell of Cupid, Rama uttered such words in grief which are otherwise unutterable. As if he was seeing Sita (before him) which was not a fact.
ramayan::7807.english_translation: Under the spell of desire and grief, Rama spoke words that were hard to utter, as if he were seeing Sita before him, though he was not.
ramayan::7807.translation_literal: पश्यन्निव (as if seeing) / तां (that) / सीताम् (Sita) / अपश्यन् (not seeing) / मदनार्दितः (struck by desire) / उवाच (spoke) / राघवः (Raghava) / वाक्यम् (speech) / विलापाश्रयदुर्वचम् (hard to utter because it rests in lamentation)
ramayan::7807.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7807.essence: Absence can feel so sharp it masquerades as presence.
ramayan::7807.simple_meaning: Rama is so overwhelmed by longing and grief that he speaks as if Sita were right in front of him, even though she is not.
ramayan::7807.simple_insight: Deep longing can make absence feel like presence.
ramayan::7807.detailed_meaning: Rama has already broken down searching for Sita. Here, Valmiki shows his grief turning almost hallucinatory: he speaks to the empty forest as if she stands before him. This is not a teaching verse but a vivid step in his collapse.
ramayan::7807.modern_relevance: You keep reaching for a phone that has no message, then imagine the person anyway. Grief can make the mind place someone in front of you when they are gone.
ramayan::7807.insight: It shows how longing distorts perception and pulls speech into lament.

ramayan::7808.verse_sanskrit: त्वमशोकस्य शाखाभिः पुष्पप्रियतया प्रिये । आवृणोषि शरीरं ते मम शोकविवर्धिनी । । 3623 । ।
ramayan::7808.verse_hindi: O my beloved  as you love flowers you are hiding your body behind the branches of
ramayan::7808.english_translation: O my beloved, as you love flowers, you hide your body behind the branches of the aśoka tree, increasing my sorrow.
ramayan::7808.translation_literal: त्वम् (you) / अशोकस्य (of the aśoka tree) / शाखाभिः (with branches) / पुष्पप्रियतया (by flower-fondness) / प्रिये (beloved) / आवृणोषि (you cover) / शरीरम् (body) / ते (your) / मम (my) / शोकविवर्धिनी (increasing sorrow)
ramayan::7808.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7808.essence: Even imagined concealment becomes pain when love is searching.
ramayan::7808.simple_meaning: Rama, overcome by longing, speaks to Sita as if she were hidden behind the aśoka tree branches, and that sight only deepens his grief.
ramayan::7808.simple_insight: Longing can make even a glimpse feel like loss.
ramayan::7808.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has lost sight of Sita and is speaking in anguish to the world around him as if it were her. He imagines her hidden behind the aśoka branches, and the imagined concealment only sharpens his heartbreak.
ramayan::7808.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you miss, then realize it was only a passing shape. The almost-seeing hurts more than not seeing at all.
ramayan::7808.insight: It captures how grief projects meaning onto ordinary things and turns them into reminders of absence.

ramayan::7809.verse_sanskrit: कदलीस्कन्धसदृशौ कदल्या संवृतावुभौ । ऊरू पश्यामि ते देवि नासि शक्ता निगूहितुम् । । 3624 । ।
ramayan::7809.verse_hindi: O Devi I can see both your thighs which resemble banana trunk hidden behind a banana plant. It is not possible for you to hide them from me.
ramayan::7809.english_translation: O Devi, I can see both your thighs, like banana trunks hidden behind a banana plant. You cannot conceal them from me.
ramayan::7809.translation_literal: कदली-स्कन्ध-सदृशौ (resembling banana trunks) / कदल्या (by a banana plant) / संवृतौ (covered, hidden) / उभौ (both) / ऊरू (thighs) / पश्यामि (I see) / ते (your) / देवि (O Devi) / न (not) / असि (are) / शक्ता (able) / निगूहितुम् (to conceal)
ramayan::7809.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7809.essence: Longing makes the mind see what is no longer there.
ramayan::7809.simple_meaning: Rama, overcome by longing, tells Sita that her thighs are still visible even when she tries to hide behind the banana plant.
ramayan::7809.simple_insight: Desire makes even a hidden form feel impossible to lose.
ramayan::7809.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is stricken with longing for Sita and speaks as if he can still see her through the leaves. This line is part of his grief-filled search, not a teaching, and its force comes from his inability to bear her absence.
ramayan::7809.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the last glimpse of someone you miss, noticing details that should not matter anymore. Longing makes the mind cling to what it cannot hold.
ramayan::7809.insight: It shows how grief and desire can distort perception, making absence feel almost like presence.

ramayan::7810.verse_sanskrit: कर्णिकारवनं भद्रे हसन्ती देवि सेवसे । अलं ते परिहासेन मम बाधावहेन वै । । 3625 । ।
ramayan::7810.verse_hindi: O gentle one  you are wandering in the karnikara garden, laughing and making fun. Enough of this , that causes my pain.
ramayan::7810.english_translation: O gentle one, you wander in the karnikara grove, laughing and teasing. Enough of this joking, for it only adds to my pain.
ramayan::7810.translation_literal: कर्णिकारवनं (karnikara grove) / भद्रे (gentle one) / हसन्ती (laughing) / देवि (lady) / सेवसे (you wander in, you enjoy) / अलम् (enough) / ते (your) / परिहासेन (with joking) / मम (my) / बाधावहेन (pain-causing) / वै (indeed)
ramayan::7810.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7810.essence: Teasing can wound most when love is already strained.
ramayan::7810.simple_meaning: Rama tells Sita to stop teasing him in the grove, because her joking only increases his distress.
ramayan::7810.simple_insight: Even playful words can hurt when someone is already overwhelmed.
ramayan::7810.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama speaks to Sita with tenderness mixed with strain. She is nearby among the flowering trees, and his longing has made even her teasing feel unbearable. The moment is part of a larger exchange of affectionate complaint, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::7810.modern_relevance: You try to laugh it off with someone who is already exhausted, and the joke lands wrong. Sometimes care means noticing when even harmless teasing will sting.
ramayan::7810.insight: It reminds you to read emotional exhaustion before you joke.

ramayan::7811.verse_sanskrit: परिहासेन किं सीते परिश्रान्तस्य मे प्रिये । अयं स परिहासोऽपि साधु देवि न रोचते । । 3626 । ।
ramayan::7811.verse_hindi: O my dear Sita, why are you joking when I am exhausted? Such fun cannot be relished  now.
ramayan::7811.english_translation: O my dear Sita, why are you joking when I am exhausted? Such fun cannot be enjoyed now.
ramayan::7811.translation_literal: परिहासेन (with joking) / किं (why) / सीते (Sita) / परिश्रान्तस्य (of the exhausted one) / मे (of me) / प्रिये (beloved) / अयं (this) / सः (that) / परिहासः अपि (joke even) / साधु (well / properly) / देवि (devi) / न (not) / रोचते (is pleasing)
ramayan::7811.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7811.simple_meaning: Rama asks Sita not to joke with him while he is tired. Even playful words can feel wrong when someone is exhausted.
ramayan::7811.simple_insight: Care includes timing. Even affection can become painful if it ignores another person's fatigue.
ramayan::7811.detailed_meaning: Rama and Sita are in the forest, speaking playfully. But Rama is weary, and the teasing now feels heavy rather than sweet. The verse turns a light exchange into a lesson about restraint and sensitivity.
ramayan::7811.modern_relevance: You come home worn out, and someone tries to joke you out of your mood. What would have been funny earlier now feels sharp. This verse remembers that tired hearts need gentleness first.
ramayan::7811.insight: It teaches you to notice another person's state before using humor or pressure.

ramayan::7812.verse_sanskrit: विशेषेणाश्रमस्थाने हासोऽयं न प्रशस्यते । अवगच्छामि ते शीलं परिहासप्रियं प्रिये । । 3627 । । आगच्छ त्वं विशालाक्षि शून्योऽयमुटजस्तव ।
ramayan::7812.verse_hindi: O darling  joking specially in a hermitage  is not appreciated. I know your nature.You love fun. O largeeyed Sita, come here. This cottage of yours is empty.
ramayan::7812.english_translation: O darling, joking especially in a hermitage is not appreciated. I know your nature. You love fun. O large-eyed Sita, come here. This cottage of yours is empty.
ramayan::7812.translation_literal: विशेषेण (especially) / आश्रमस्थाने (in a hermitage-place) / हासः (laughter, joking) / अयम् (this) / न (not) / प्रशस्यते (is praised, is appreciated) । अवगच्छामि (I understand) / ते (your) / शीलम् (nature, character) / परिहासप्रियम् (fond of joking) / प्रिये (dear one) । आगच्छ (come) / त्वम् (you) / विशालाक्षि (O large-eyed one) / शून्यः (empty) / अयम् (this) / उटजः (cottage, hut) / तव (your).
ramayan::7812.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7812.essence: Playfulness fades when absence starts speaking.
ramayan::7812.simple_meaning: Joking feels out of place here, especially in a hermitage. Rama tells Sita he knows she likes playful teasing, then calls her to come because her cottage feels empty without her.
ramayan::7812.simple_insight: Even light teasing can carry grief when separation has entered the room.
ramayan::7812.detailed_meaning: Rama is speaking to Sita in the forest hermitage after a moment of teasing. His tone shifts quickly from playful complaint to loneliness: the cottage feels empty without her. The verse sits inside a growing ache of separation, not a finished teaching.
ramayan::7812.modern_relevance: You make a joke in a quiet room, but the other person hears the loneliness underneath it. Sometimes playfulness is just grief looking for a softer shape.
ramayan::7812.insight: It shows how absence can turn ordinary words into signs of longing.

ramayan::7813.verse_sanskrit: सुव्यक्तं राक्षसैस्सीता भक्षिता वा हृतापि वा । । 3628 । । न हि सा विलपन्तं मामुपसम्प्रैति लक्ष्मण ।
ramayan::7813.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana surely Sita is either devoured by demons or abducted. When I am weeping like this she is not coming to me.
ramayan::7813.english_translation: O Lakshmana, Sita has surely been devoured by demons or carried away. She does not come to me when I am weeping like this.
ramayan::7813.translation_literal: सुव्यक्तम् (surely) / राक्षसैः (by demons) / सीता (Sita) / भक्षिता (devoured) / वा (or) / हृता (carried away) / अपि (also) / वा (or) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / सा (she) / विलपन्तम् (weeping) / माम् (me) / उपसम्प्रैति (comes near) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7813.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7813.essence: Fear rushes in where love cannot find an answer.
ramayan::7813.simple_meaning: Rama, overwhelmed by grief, tells Lakshmana that Sita must have been seized or killed, because she is not returning to him even as he cries out.
ramayan::7813.simple_insight: Grief can turn uncertainty into certainty before any proof exists.
ramayan::7813.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has already begun to fear the worst after losing Sita. Speaking to Lakshmana, he imagines two terrible possibilities: she has been eaten by demons or carried off. The line captures the first collapse of hope into panic.
ramayan::7813.modern_relevance: You call again and again, but the silence answers louder each time. In that helpless gap, your mind starts writing the worst ending for you.
ramayan::7813.insight: It shows how panic fills missing facts with the most painful explanation.

ramayan::7814.verse_sanskrit: एतानि मृगयूथानि साश्रुनेत्राणि लक्ष्मण । । 3629 । । शंसन्तीव हि वैदेहीं भक्षितां रजनीचरैः ।
ramayan::7814.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, these herds of deer with their eyes filled with tears are as if telling me that she is eaten away by the demons.
ramayan::7814.english_translation: O Lakshmana, these herds of deer with tears in their eyes seem to be telling me that Vaidehi has been devoured by the night-wanderers.
ramayan::7814.translation_literal: एतानि (these) / मृगयूथानि (herds of deer) / साश्रुनेत्राणि (with tear-filled eyes) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / शंसन्तीव (seem to be telling) / हि (indeed) / वैदेहीं (Vaidehi) / भक्षितां (devoured) / रजनीचरैः (by night-wanderers)
ramayan::7814.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7814.essence: Grief can make even nature seem to confirm your worst fear.
ramayan::7814.simple_meaning: Rama reads the sorrow in the deer around him and takes it as a sign that Sita has been taken or killed.
ramayan::7814.simple_insight: Grief makes the whole world feel like a message of loss.
ramayan::7814.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is already convinced Sita is gone. He points to the deer, their eyes seeming wet with grief, and hears an omen in them. The verse deepens his panic rather than teaching a separate principle.
ramayan::7814.modern_relevance: You lose someone’s phone signal, then every silent corner feels like bad news. Grief starts turning ordinary details into proof of the worst.
ramayan::7814.insight: It shows how fear can project meaning onto the smallest signs and intensify despair.

ramayan::7815.verse_sanskrit: हा ममार्ये क्व यातासि हा साध्वि वरवर्णिनि । । 36210 । । हा सकामा त्वया देवी कैकेयी सा भविष्यति ।
ramayan::7815.verse_hindi: Alas, my noble lady, where have you gone? O chaste lady of excellent complexion, that queen Kaikeyis desire will be fulfilled now.
ramayan::7815.english_translation: Alas, my noble lady, where have you gone? O chaste lady of excellent complexion, Kaikeyi's wish will now be fulfilled.
ramayan::7815.translation_literal: हा (alas) / मम (my) / आर्ये (noble lady) / क्व (where) / यातासि (have you gone) / हा (alas) / साध्वि (chaste lady) / वरवर्णिनि (of excellent complexion) / हा (alas) / सकामा (fulfilled in desire) / त्वया (by you) / देवी (queen) / कैकेयी (Kaikeyi) / सा (that) / भविष्यति (will become)
ramayan::7815.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7815.essence: Her absence makes the old bargain finally hurt.
ramayan::7815.simple_meaning: Rama cries out in grief for Sita, calling her noble and pure. Her absence means Kaikeyi's old wish has now come true.
ramayan::7815.simple_insight: Love feels most unbearable when absence makes every earlier promise come due.
ramayan::7815.detailed_meaning: Rama has returned from exile expecting Sita beside him, but she is gone. In a single cry, he mourns her disappearance and sees the hidden cost of Kaikeyi's boon: the separation has become real, and the house is already hollow.
ramayan::7815.modern_relevance: You come home with one person in mind, and the room answers back with absence. Then you realise what was lost was not just company, but the life you expected to continue.
ramayan::7815.insight: It turns grief into recognition: one missing person can expose the full cost of an old choice.

ramayan::7816.verse_sanskrit: सीतया सह निर्यातो विना सीतामुपागतः । । 36211 । । कथं नाम प्रवेक्ष्यामि शून्यमन्तःपुरं पुनः ।
ramayan::7816.verse_hindi: I left home with Sita. How can I reenter the inner apartment without her ?
ramayan::7816.english_translation: I left home with Sita. How can I reenter the inner apartment without her?
ramayan::7816.translation_literal: सीतया (with Sita) / सह (together) / निर्यातो (having gone out) / विना (without) / सीताम् (Sita) / उपागतः (having come back) / कथम् (how) / नाम (indeed) / प्रवेक्ष्यामि (shall I enter) / शून्यम् (empty) / अन्तःपुरम् (inner apartment) / पुनः (again)
ramayan::7816.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7816.essence: A shared home becomes unenterable when the one who made it whole is gone.
ramayan::7816.simple_meaning: Rama says he cannot return to the palace without Sita, because going back alone would make the home feel empty and broken.
ramayan::7816.simple_insight: Love changes what home means; absence can make even a palace feel hollow.
ramayan::7816.detailed_meaning: After Sita is taken away, Rama stands in grief and imagines the palace without her. The life he left with her cannot simply be resumed alone. This verse shows how loss turns a home into emptiness.
ramayan::7816.modern_relevance: You come back to an apartment after a breakup and notice the shoes by the door, the cup on the shelf, the silence in every room. The place is unchanged, but your life inside it is not.
ramayan::7816.insight: It shifts attention from physical return to emotional reality: some places cannot be re-entered the same way after loss.

ramayan::7817.verse_sanskrit: निर्वीर्य इति लोको मां निर्दयश्चेति वक्ष्यति । । 36212 । । कातरत्वं प्रकाशं हि सीतापनयनेन मे ।
ramayan::7817.verse_hindi: By Sitas abduction it will be  clear to the world that I lack manliness and compassion. My cowardly nature will clearly manifest.
ramayan::7817.english_translation: By Sita's abduction, it will be clear to the world that I lack manliness and compassion. My cowardly nature will clearly be revealed.
ramayan::7817.translation_literal: निर्वीर्यः (without manliness) / इति (thus) / लोकः (the world) / माम् (me) / निर्दयः (without compassion) / च (and) / इति (thus) / वक्ष्यति (will say) / कातरत्वम् (cowardice) / प्रकाशम् (clearly) / हि (indeed) / सीता-अपनयनेन (by Sita's abduction) / मे (my)
ramayan::7817.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7817.essence: Silence in the face of loss can look like weakness.
ramayan::7817.simple_meaning: Rama says that if Sita is taken away, people will think he is weak and heartless. His public honor as a king and husband is at stake.
ramayan::7817.simple_insight: Sometimes the hardest part of duty is knowing your silence will be read as failure.
ramayan::7817.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in the grief of separation and sees the larger cost. If Sita is carried away and he does nothing, the world will judge him as cowardly and cruel. This is the pressure that pushes him toward action.
ramayan::7817.modern_relevance: You see a harmful rumor spreading about someone you protect. Staying quiet feels safer, but it also lets your character be rewritten in public.
ramayan::7817.insight: It shifts the mind from private pain to public responsibility: inaction can become a moral statement.

ramayan::7818.verse_sanskrit: निवृत्तवनवासश्च जनकं मिथिलाधिपम् । । 36213 । । कुशलं परिपृच्छन्तं कथं शक्ष्ये निरीक्षितुम् ।
ramayan::7818.verse_hindi: After completing the period of my exile when Janaka , king of Mithila, enquires of her welfare how can I face him?
ramayan::7818.english_translation: After completing my exile, how can I face Janaka, the king of Mithila, when he asks after her welfare?
ramayan::7818.translation_literal: निवृत्तवनवासः (one who has returned from forest exile) / च (and) / जनकम् (Janaka) / मिथिलाधिपम् (king of Mithila) / कुशलम् (well-being) / परिपृच्छन्तम् (asking in detail) / कथम् (how) / शक्ष्ये (shall I be able) / निरीक्षितुम् (to look at / face)
ramayan::7818.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7818.essence: Love makes absence impossible to explain away.
ramayan::7818.simple_meaning: Rama knows that returning to Janaka without Sita will be unbearable. The shame is not only personal; it will also break the dignity of the meeting.
ramayan::7818.simple_insight: Some losses change how you can face the world at all.
ramayan::7818.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in exile, already imagining the future after Sita's abduction. He knows Janaka, Sita's father, will ask about her with love and concern. The pain is not just separation; it is the humiliation of having to answer for it.
ramayan::7818.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a breakup, and someone kindly asks, “Where is she?” The question is gentle, but it lands like a blow because your absence has a name.
ramayan::7818.insight: It shifts you from private grief to the social weight of loss and shame.

ramayan::7819.verse_sanskrit: विदेहराजो नूनं मां दृष्ट्वा विरहितं तया । । 36214 । । सुतास्नेहेन सन्तप्तो मोहस्य वशमेष्यति ।
ramayan::7819.verse_hindi: If the king of Videha sees me without her, he will surely be distressed and will fall into a swoon for the love of his daughter.
ramayan::7819.english_translation: If the king of Videha sees me without her, he will surely be distressed and will fall into a swoon for the love of his daughter.
ramayan::7819.translation_literal: विदेहराजः (the king of Videha) / नूनम् (surely) / माम् (me) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / विरहितम् (deprived) / तया (of her) / सुतास्नेहेन (with love for his daughter) / सन्तप्तः (distressed) / मोहस्य (of swoon) / वशम् (into the state) / एष्यति (will go)
ramayan::7819.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7819.essence: Absence becomes heavier when a father's love has to witness it.
ramayan::7819.simple_meaning: Rama knows Janaka will be devastated to see him return without Sita. The king's love for his daughter will make her absence unbearable.
ramayan::7819.simple_insight: Separation hurts more when love is shared by everyone involved.
ramayan::7819.detailed_meaning: Rama, still in exile and speaking of Sita's loss, imagines facing Janaka, the king of Mithila and Sita's father. He knows the sight of him alone will wound the father with grief, because this loss is not private.
ramayan::7819.modern_relevance: You bring bad news to a parent whose child is missing, and the room changes before you even speak. Some absences are so large they pass through every heart in the family.
ramayan::7819.insight: It shifts the mind from personal grief to the wider circle of people who carry that grief with you.

ramayan::7820.verse_sanskrit: अथवा न गमिष्यामि पुरीं भरतपालिताम् । । 36215 । । स्वर्गोऽपि सीतया हीनश्शून्य एव मतो मम ।
ramayan::7820.verse_hindi: Or else, I will not go to the city ruled by Bharata. Without Sita even heaven will be empty for me.
ramayan::7820.english_translation: Or else, I will not go to the city ruled by Bharata. Without Sita even heaven would feel empty to me.
ramayan::7820.translation_literal: अथवा (or else) / न (not) / गमिष्यामि (I will go) / पुरीं (to the city) / भरतपालिताम् (ruled by Bharata) / स्वर्गः (heaven) / अपि (even) / सीतया (with Sita) / हीनः (deprived) / शून्यः (empty) / एव (indeed) / मतः (considered) / मम (by me)
ramayan::7820.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7820.essence: What you long for can matter more than paradise.
ramayan::7820.simple_meaning: Rama says he cannot bear returning to Bharata’s city without Sita. Even the highest place would feel empty if she is absent.
ramayan::7820.simple_insight: Love can make every outer reward feel hollow when the one you miss is missing.
ramayan::7820.detailed_meaning: Rama, separated from Sita in the forest, imagines the return to Ayodhya under Bharata’s rule. The throne, the city, even heaven itself lose value for him without her presence. The verse turns grief into a measure of what truly matters.
ramayan::7820.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the apartment, the long-awaited trip — and the person you wanted to share it with is absent. The achievement is real, but it lands like a room with the lights off.
ramayan::7820.insight: It shifts attention from external success to the presence that gives life its meaning.

ramayan::7821.verse_sanskrit: मामिहोत्सृज्य हि वने गच्छायोध्यां पुरीं शुभाम् । । 36216 । । न त्वहं तां विना सीतां जीवेयं हि कथञ्चन ।
ramayan::7821.verse_hindi: Go to the auspicious city of Ayodhya, leaving me here in the woods. I can never live without Sita.
ramayan::7821.english_translation: Go to the auspicious city of Ayodhya, leaving me here in the woods. I can never live without Sita.
ramayan::7821.translation_literal: माम् (me) / इह (here) / उत्सृज्य (leaving) / हि (indeed) / वने (in the forest) / गच्छ (go) / अयोध्यां (to Ayodhya) / पुरीं (city) / शुभाम् (auspicious) / न (not) / तु (but) / अहम् (I) / ताम् (her) / विना (without) / सीताम् (Sita) / जीवेयम् (would live) / हि (indeed) / कथञ्चन (in any way)
ramayan::7821.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7821.essence: Home means nothing when the one you love is missing.
ramayan::7821.simple_meaning: Rama tells his messenger to go to Ayodhya without him. Separated from Sita, he feels life itself has no meaning.
ramayan::7821.simple_insight: Love can make even a rightful home feel unlivable.
ramayan::7821.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama speaks after hearing that Bharata rules Ayodhya. He imagines returning without Sita and rejects the very idea. The verse shows how exile has become bearable, but separation from her has not.
ramayan::7821.modern_relevance: You can have the job, the address, the plan, and still feel absent if the person you love is missing. Some losses change what home means.
ramayan::7821.insight: It shifts attention from outward return to the inner cost of separation.

ramayan::7822.verse_sanskrit: गाढमाश्लिष्य भरतो वाच्यो मद्वचनात्त्वया । । 36217 । । अनुज्ञातोऽसि रामेण पालयेति वसुन्धराम् ।
ramayan::7822.verse_hindi: While embracing Bharata tightly, repeat my words, You are permitted by Rama to rule the earth.
ramayan::7822.english_translation: While embracing Bharata tightly, repeat my words: you are permitted by Rama to rule the earth.
ramayan::7822.translation_literal: गाढम् (tightly) / आश्लिष्य (embracing) / भरतः (Bharata) / वाच्यः (to be said) / मद्वचनात् (from my words) / त्वया (by you) / अनुज्ञातः (permitted) / असि (you are) / रामेण (by Rama) / पालयेति (to rule / to govern) / वसुन्धराम् (the earth)
ramayan::7822.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7822.essence: Power becomes clean when it is given without bitterness.
ramayan::7822.simple_meaning: Rama asks that Bharata be embraced and told he may rule the kingdom in Rama's name.
ramayan::7822.simple_insight: Real authority can be handed over with humility, not seized with pride.
ramayan::7822.detailed_meaning: In exile, Rama refuses the throne for himself but does not reject Bharata's burden. He sends a message of acceptance and legitimacy through an embrace, turning a family wound into a lawful handover of rule.
ramayan::7822.modern_relevance: You step back from a role you could have fought for, then publicly bless the person who must carry it now. That kind of gracious transfer is rare, and unforgettable.
ramayan::7822.insight: It teaches you to release status without resentment and honour the person who must now bear responsibility.

ramayan::7823.verse_sanskrit: अम्बा च मम कैकेयी सुमित्रा च त्वया विभो । । 36218 । । कौसल्या च यथान्यायमभिवाद्या ममाऽज्ञया । रक्षणीया प्रयत्नेन भवता सूक्तकारिणा । । 36219 । ।
ramayan::7823.verse_hindi: My mother Kaikeyi, Sumitra and Kausalya  should also be offered due obeisance. You should protect them with great effort, carrying out my instructions.
ramayan::7823.english_translation: My mother Kaikeyi, Sumitra, and Kausalya should also be offered due obeisance. You should protect them with great effort, carrying out my instructions.
ramayan::7823.translation_literal: अम्बा (mother) / च (and) / मम (my) / कैकेयी (Kaikeyi) / सुमित्रा (Sumitra) / च (and) / त्वया (by you) / विभो (O mighty one) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / च (and) / यथान्यायम् (properly) / अभिवाद्या (to be saluted) / मम (my) / आज्ञया (by command) / रक्षणीया (to be protected) / प्रयत्नेन (with effort) / भवता (by you) / सूक्तकारिणा (by one who does what is well said)
ramayan::7823.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7823.essence: Love still looks after others when everything is falling apart.
ramayan::7823.simple_meaning: Rama asks Lakshmana to honor Kaikeyi, Sumitra, and Kausalya properly and protect them carefully while following his instructions.
ramayan::7823.simple_insight: Even in exile and separation, care for family and respect for elders still come first.
ramayan::7823.detailed_meaning: Before leaving for Ayodhya, Rama gives Lakshmana one more set of duties. He asks him to bow to Kaikeyi, Sumitra, and Kausalya, and to guard them carefully. The moment is tender and heavy: even as one brother goes into the forest, he worries about the women left behind.
ramayan::7823.modern_relevance: You are leaving town after a family crisis, but the last thing on your mind is not your own pain. It is whether the people at home will be treated with dignity and care.
ramayan::7823.insight: It shifts attention from personal loss to the responsibility that remains with the people left behind.

ramayan::7824.verse_sanskrit: सीतायाश्च विनाशोऽयं मम चामित्रकर्शन । विस्तरेण जनन्या मे विनिवेद्यस्त्वया भवेत् । । 36220 । ।
ramayan::7824.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, subduer of the enemy this loss of Sita and me should be explained in detail to my mother.
ramayan::7824.english_translation: O Lakshmana, subduer of the enemy, this loss of Sita and me should be explained in detail to my mother.
ramayan::7824.translation_literal: सीतायाः (of Sita) / च (and) / विनाशः (loss, destruction) / अयम् (this) / मम (of me) / च (and) / अमित्रकर्शन (O subduer of enemies) / विस्तरेण (in detail) / जनन्याः (to [my] mother) / मे (my) / विनिवेद्यः (to be reported) / त्वया (by you) / भवेत् (should be)
ramayan::7824.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7824.essence: Pain must sometimes be carried back to the people who love you.
ramayan::7824.simple_meaning: Rama asks Lakshmana to tell his mother, in full detail, about the loss of Sita and his own suffering.
ramayan::7824.simple_insight: Grief becomes heavier when it must be carried back home.
ramayan::7824.detailed_meaning: After exile, Rama is already speaking like a man who knows his mother will need the truth, however painful. He asks Lakshmana to report Sita's loss and his own condition to Kausalya, making private sorrow into family news.
ramayan::7824.modern_relevance: You have to call home with news you can barely say out loud. The hardest part is not the pain itself, but giving it shape for someone who loves you.
ramayan::7824.insight: It shifts grief from silent shock to responsible witness.

ramayan::7825.verse_sanskrit: इति विलपति राघवे सुदीने वनमुपगम्य तया विना सुकेश्या । भयविकलमुखस्तु लक्ष्मणोऽपि व्यथितमना भृशमातुरो बभूव । । 36221 । ।
ramayan::7825.verse_hindi: When Rama, devoid of  Sita, the lady with beautiful hair, wailed piteously after reaching the forest, Lakshmana too, his face pale out of fear and mind dejected, felt extremely agitated.
ramayan::7825.english_translation: When Rama, devoid of Sita, the lady with beautiful hair, wailed piteously after reaching the forest, Lakshmana too, his face pale out of fear and mind dejected, felt extremely agitated.
ramayan::7825.translation_literal: इति (thus) / विलपति (wailing) / राघवे (when Rama) / सुदीने (deeply sorrowful) / वनम् (forest) / उपगम्य (having reached) / तया (by her, with her) / विना (without) / सुकेश्या (the fair-haired one) / भय-विकल-मुखः (face distressed by fear) / तु (indeed) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / अपि (also) / व्यथित-मनाः (mind afflicted) / भृशम् (greatly) / आतुरः (agitated) / बभूव (became)
ramayan::7825.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7825.essence: Grief is contagious when love is already under strain.
ramayan::7825.simple_meaning: Rama reaches the forest without Sita and breaks down in grief. Lakshmana, seeing his brother's pain, is shaken too and becomes deeply distressed.
ramayan::7825.simple_insight: Grief spreads quickly when someone you love is hurting.
ramayan::7825.detailed_meaning: After the exile has driven Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana into the forest, the separation becomes unbearable. Rama laments Sita's absence, and Lakshmana, who has been trying to stay steady, is shaken by his brother's collapse and falls into distress himself.
ramayan::7825.modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day and try to hold it together, but the person beside you sees the strain immediately. Their pain becomes yours before either of you can speak.
ramayan::7825.insight: It shows how separation wounds not only the one left behind, but everyone who loves them.

ramayan::7826.verse_sanskrit: स राजपुत्रः प्रियया विहीनः शोकेन मोहेन च पीड्यमानः । विषादयन्भ्रातरमार्तरूपो भूयो विषादं प्रविवेश तीव्रम् । । 3631 । ।
ramayan::7826.verse_hindi: Prince Rama, separated from his beloved, lost his senses out of sorrow. Seeing his brother in a distressed state, he sank again into intense grief.
ramayan::7826.english_translation: Prince Rama, separated from his beloved, lost his senses out of sorrow. Seeing his brother in a distressed state, he sank again into intense grief.
ramayan::7826.translation_literal: स (that) / राजपुत्रः (prince) / प्रियया (from the beloved) / विहीनः (separated) / शोकेन (by sorrow) / मोहेन (by delusion) / च (and) / पीड्यमानः (being tormented) / विषादयन् (grieving) / भ्रातरम् (the brother) / आर्तरूपः (in a distressed state) / भूयो (again) / विषादम् (into grief) / प्रविवेश (entered) / तीव्रम् (intense)
ramayan::7826.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7826.essence: Seeing a loved one suffer can pull you deeper into your own pain.
ramayan::7826.simple_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by separation from Sita. His grief is so deep that seeing Lakshmana suffer makes his own sorrow return even more strongly.
ramayan::7826.simple_insight: Grief multiplies when you see it reflected in someone you love.
ramayan::7826.detailed_meaning: Rama has reached the forest without Sita, and the loss has already broken his composure. Now he sees Lakshmana shaken too. Instead of easing, the pain deepens: one brother's suffering feeds the other's, and the scene becomes a spiral of grief.
ramayan::7826.modern_relevance: You get one text from a sibling saying they are not okay, and your own chest tightens. Their pain doesn't stay theirs for long; it enters you too.
ramayan::7826.insight: It shows how shared suffering can intensify distress instead of relieving it.

ramayan::7827.verse_sanskrit: स लक्ष्मणं शोकवशाभिपन्नं शोके निमग्नो विपुले तु रामः । उवाच वाक्यं व्यसनानुरूपमुष्णं विनिश्श्वस्य रुदंत्सशोकम् । । 3632 । ।
ramayan::7827.verse_hindi: Plunged in deep grief, Rama heaved hot sighs and said these words to griefstricken Lakshmanaweeping:
ramayan::7827.english_translation: Plunged in deep grief, Rama heaved hot sighs and said these words to grief-stricken Lakshmana: ...
ramayan::7827.translation_literal: स (that) / लक्ष्मणं (to Lakshmana) / शोकवशाभिपन्नं (overcome by grief) / शोके (in grief) / निमग्नो (immersed) / विपुले तु (indeed deeply) / रामः (Rama) / उवाच (said) / वाक्यं (words) / व्यसनानुरूपमुष्णं (hot, fitting the calamity) / विनिश्श्वस्य (having sighed) / रुदंत्सशोकम् (weeping and sorrowful)
ramayan::7827.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7827.essence: Even Rama cannot speak from grief without carrying it in his breath.
ramayan::7827.simple_meaning: Rama, overwhelmed by sorrow, turned to Lakshmana and spoke through tears and heavy sighs.
ramayan::7827.simple_insight: Grief can leave even the strongest voice shaking.
ramayan::7827.detailed_meaning: Separated from Sita, Rama has already collapsed into sorrow, and Lakshmana is sinking with him. In this moment Rama gathers himself just enough to speak, but his words come from the same wound, not from calm strength.
ramayan::7827.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone you love after bad news, and neither of you has words. Sometimes the first honest response is not a solution, only a broken voice.
ramayan::7827.insight: It shows that pain can be shared so completely that comfort itself becomes difficult to find.

ramayan::7828.verse_sanskrit: न मद्विधो दुष्कृतकर्मकारी मन्ये द्वितीयोऽस्ति वसुन्धरायाम् । शोकेन शोको हि परम्पराया मा मेति भिन्दन्हृदयं मनश्च । । 3633 । ।
ramayan::7828.verse_hindi: I think there is none on earth like me who has performed such forbidden acts.  One grief after the other is successively piercing my heart and my mind.
ramayan::7828.english_translation: I think there is none on earth like me who has performed such forbidden acts. One grief after another is piercing my heart and mind.
ramayan::7828.translation_literal: न (not) / मद्विधः (like me) / दुष्कृतकर्मकारी (one who does forbidden acts) / मन्ये (I think) / द्वितीयः (second) / अस्ति (is) / वसुन्धरायाम् (on the earth) / शोकेन (by grief) / शोकः (grief) / हि (indeed) / परम्परया (in succession) / मा (me) / मेति (piercing) / भिन्दन् (splitting) / हृदयम् (heart) / मनः (mind) / च (and)
ramayan::7828.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7828.essence: Grief has become a second wound, and Rama now blames himself for it.
ramayan::7828.simple_meaning: Rama says he has no equal in wrongdoing and feels grief striking him again and again, breaking both heart and mind.
ramayan::7828.simple_insight: Pain can stack until even your thoughts feel wounded.
ramayan::7828.detailed_meaning: Rama, already crushed by separation from Sita, turns inward and judges himself harshly. In front of Lakshmana, he speaks as a man overwhelmed by sorrow, believing his own past actions have brought this crushing chain of grief.
ramayan::7828.modern_relevance: You replay one mistake, then another, until the whole day feels stained. The mind starts calling the pain proof that you deserve it.
ramayan::7828.insight: It shows how grief can turn into self-condemnation and make suffering feel deserved.

ramayan::7829.verse_sanskrit: पूर्वं मया नूनमभीप्सितानि पापानि कर्माण्यसकृत्कृतानि । तत्रायमद्यापतितो विपाको दुःखेन दुःखं यदहं विशामि । । 3634 । ।
ramayan::7829.verse_hindi: In the past I had certainly done some sinful deeds I often liked the consequences of which have descended on me now as I am experiencing one sorrow after another.
ramayan::7829.english_translation: In the past I had certainly done some sinful deeds I often liked the consequences of which have descended on me now as I am experiencing one sorrow after another.
ramayan::7829.translation_literal: पूर्वं (in the past) / मया (by me) / नूनम् (certainly) / अभीप्सितानि (desired) / पापानि (sinful) / कर्माणि (deeds) / असकृत् (again and again) / कृतानि (done) / तत्र (there) / अयम् (this) / अद्य (today) / आपतितः (fallen upon) / विपाकः (result) / दुःखेन (with sorrow) / दुःखम् (sorrow) / यत् (that) / अहम् (I) / विशामि (enter)
ramayan::7829.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7829.essence: Present suffering can be the return of choices you once kept making.
ramayan::7829.simple_meaning: Rama feels that his present suffering is the result of past harmful actions he once chose and repeated.
ramayan::7829.simple_insight: Pain becomes clearer when you see it as the result of your own earlier choices.
ramayan::7829.detailed_meaning: Rama sits overwhelmed by grief after losing his kingdom, father, and home. Speaking to Lakshmana, he turns inward and sees his suffering as the return of earlier harmful actions. The verse deepens his despair before the next list of losses.
ramayan::7829.modern_relevance: You look back at a relationship, a job, or a habit and suddenly see the pattern: the hurt did not appear from nowhere. It grew from choices you kept repeating.
ramayan::7829.insight: It shifts blame away from fate and toward honest self-accounting for repeated actions.

ramayan::7830.verse_sanskrit: राज्यप्रणाशस्स्वजनैर्वियोगः पितुर्विनाशो जननीवियोगः । सर्वाणि मे लक्ष्मण शोकवेगमापूरयन्ति प्रविचिन्तितानि । । 3635 । ।
ramayan::7830.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, loss of kingdom, separation from kith and kin, death of father, separation from mother--all these thoughts augment my sorrow faster and in greater measure.
ramayan::7830.english_translation: O Lakshmana, loss of kingdom, separation from kith and kin, death of father, separation from mother—all these thoughts increase my sorrow more and more.
ramayan::7830.translation_literal: राज्यप्रणाशः (loss of kingdom) / स्वजनैः (from kith and kin) / वियोगः (separation) / पितुः (of father) / विनाशः (death) / जननीवियोगः (separation from mother) / सर्वाणि (all) / मे (my) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / शोकवेगम् (the force of sorrow) / आपूरयन्ति (fill up, increase) / प्रविचिन्तितानि (thought over, contemplated)
ramayan::7830.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7830.essence: Grief deepens when every loss is remembered together.
ramayan::7830.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that thinking about losing his kingdom, family, father, and mother only makes his grief stronger.
ramayan::7830.simple_insight: Grief can gather power when the mind keeps returning to every loss at once.
ramayan::7830.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Rama speaks to Lakshmana as sorrow keeps rising inside him. He is not naming one wound but many: the lost throne, separation from family, his father's death, and his mother's absence. The verse shows grief becoming heavier through reflection.
ramayan::7830.modern_relevance: At 2 a.m., your mind starts replaying every loss at once: the job that ended, the friend who drifted away, the parent you miss, the home that changed. The sorrow multiplies when nothing is held apart.
ramayan::7830.insight: It shows how one painful thought can trigger a whole chain of grief.

ramayan::7831.verse_sanskrit: सर्वं तु दुःखं मम लक्ष्मणेदं शान्तं शरीरे वनमेत्य शून्यम् । सीतावियोगात्पुनरप्युदीर्णं काष्ठैरिवाग्निस्सहसा प्रदीप्तः । । 3636 । ।
ramayan::7831.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, all this sorrow calmed down when I came to this solitary forest. But with Sitas separation, it was rekindled just as fire blazes forth again with logs of wood.
ramayan::7831.english_translation: O Lakshmana, all my sorrow had calmed when I came to this lonely forest. But with Sita's separation, it has flared up again, like fire suddenly blazing when fed with logs.
ramayan::7831.translation_literal: सर्वम् (all) / तु (but) / दुःखम् (sorrow) / मम (my) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / इदम् (this) / शान्तम् (calmed) / शरीरे (in the body) / वनम् (forest) / एत्य (having come) / शून्यम् (solitary) / सीतावियोगात् (from Sita's separation) / पुनः (again) / अपि (also) / उदीर्णम् (flared up) / काष्ठैः (with logs) / इव (like) / अग्निः (fire) / सहसा (suddenly) / प्रदीप्तः (blazing)
ramayan::7831.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7831.essence: One separation can reignite grief that seemed to have cooled.
ramayan::7831.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that the forest had eased his sorrow, but Sita's absence has brought it back fiercely, like a fire suddenly fed with wood.
ramayan::7831.simple_insight: Loss can stay quiet for a while and still return with full force.
ramayan::7831.detailed_meaning: Rama is in exile, speaking to Lakshmana in the forest. He has endured the fall of his kingdom and the pain of separation from family, but Sita's disappearance has reopened everything. The verse shows grief returning in a deeper, sharper form.
ramayan::7831.modern_relevance: You were doing fine until one empty chair, one unopened message, or one familiar song brought everything back. Some wounds do not vanish; they wait for the smallest spark.
ramayan::7831.insight: It teaches you that emotional pain can resurface when a deeper attachment is threatened.

ramayan::7832.verse_sanskrit: सा नूनमार्या मम राक्षसेन बलाद्दृता खं समुपेत्य भीरुः । अपस्वरं सस्वरविप्रलापा भयेन विक्रन्दितवत्यभीक्ष्णम् । । 3637 । ।
ramayan::7832.verse_hindi: The timid princess of mine forcibly carried away into the sky by a demon must have again and again cried aloud out of fear in a broken voice.
ramayan::7832.english_translation: The timid princess of mine, forcibly carried away by a demon into the sky, must have again and again cried out in fear, her voice broken by terror.
ramayan::7832.translation_literal: सा (she) / नूनम् (surely) / आर्या (noble lady) / मम (my) / राक्षसेन (by the demon) / बलात् (forcibly) / दृता (carried away) / खम् (sky) / समुपेत्य (having reached) / भीरुः (fearful) / अपस्वरम् (in a broken voice) / सस्वरविप्रलापा (crying aloud, lamenting) / भयेन (out of fear) / विक्रन्दितवती (must have cried) / अभीक्ष्णम् (again and again)
ramayan::7832.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7832.essence: Absence makes the mind invent the suffering it cannot see.
ramayan::7832.simple_meaning: Rama imagines Sita being dragged away by Ravana and crying out in fear, her voice breaking as she is carried through the sky.
ramayan::7832.simple_insight: Grief fills in the missing moments with the worst possible images.
ramayan::7832.detailed_meaning: Alone in the forest after Sita's abduction, Rama is not just mourning her absence. He is picturing the exact terror she may have endured in Ravana's grasp. This verse is one more surge in his chain of anguished guesses.
ramayan::7832.modern_relevance: You get one unanswered message and your mind starts writing the worst version of the story. Love under stress often imagines fear before facts arrive.
ramayan::7832.insight: It shows how separation turns love into painful speculation, each thought deepening the wound.

ramayan::7833.verse_sanskrit: तौ लोहितस्य प्रियदर्शनस्य सदोचितावुत्तमचन्दनस्य । वृत्तौ स्तनौ शोणितपङ्कदिग्धौ नूनं प्रियाया मम नाभिभातः । । 3638 । ।
ramayan::7833.verse_hindi: Her captivating copper coloured skin, smeared with the best of red sandal paste would not be surely pleasing now, drenched in blood and mud.
ramayan::7833.english_translation: Her captivating copper-coloured body, smeared with the finest red sandal paste, would no longer delight me now, drenched in blood and mud.
ramayan::7833.translation_literal: तौ (those) / लोहितस्य (of red / copper-coloured) / प्रियदर्शनस्य (pleasing to look at) / सदोचितावुत्तमचन्दनस्य (always fitting with the finest sandal paste) / वृत्तौ (rounded / full) / स्तनौ (breasts) / शोणितपङ्कदिग्धौ (smeared with blood and mud) / नूनं (surely) / प्रियाया (of my beloved) / मम (my) / नाभिभातः (will not shine / will not be pleasing)
ramayan::7833.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7833.essence: Grief sees the beloved already marked by harm.
ramayan::7833.simple_meaning: Rama imagines Sita's beautiful body, once adorned with sandal paste, now soiled by blood and mud. The verse deepens his grief and helplessness.
ramayan::7833.simple_insight: Love makes absence more painful because the mind keeps seeing what suffering has done.
ramayan::7833.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama speaks to Lakshmana after Sita’s abduction. He is not just grieving her loss; he is picturing the violence done to her body and dignity. This verse is one more surge of that unbearable imagining.
ramayan::7833.modern_relevance: You replay the last image of someone you love after a bad call, a hospital visit, or a breakup. The mind keeps returning to what pain might have touched.
ramayan::7833.insight: It shows how grief turns memory into a wound and makes the imagination the site of suffering.

ramayan::7834.verse_sanskrit: तच्छलक्ष्णसुव्यक्तमृदुप्रलापं तस्या मुखं कुञ्चितकेशभारम् । रक्षोवशं नूनमुपागताया न भ्राजते राहुमुखे यथेन्दुः । । 3639 । ।
ramayan::7834.verse_hindi: Her face with her clear, sweet and gentle words and her curly hair falling will no more look bright coming under the grip of demons like the moon eclipsed by Rahu.
ramayan::7834.english_translation: Her face, with its clear, sweet, gentle speech and curly hair, will no longer shine after falling under the grip of the demons, like the moon eclipsed by Rahu.
ramayan::7834.translation_literal: तत् (that) / शलक्ष्ण (clear, smooth) / सुव्यक्त (very distinct) / मृदु (gentle) / प्रलापम् (speech) / तस्या (her) / मुखम् (face) / कुञ्चित-केश-भारम् (with a mass of curled hair) / रक्षो-वशम् (under the control of demons) / नूनम् (surely) / उपागतायाः (of one who has come under) / न (not) / भ्राजते (shines) / राहु-मुखे (in Rahu's mouth) / यथा (like) / इन्दुः (the moon)
ramayan::7834.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7834.essence: Grief makes the beloved's image dim inside your own mind.
ramayan::7834.simple_meaning: Rama imagines Sita's beauty ruined by Ravana's capture. He compares her dimmed face to the moon swallowed by Rahu.
ramayan::7834.simple_insight: Love can make absence feel like a wound you keep seeing everywhere.
ramayan::7834.detailed_meaning: Alone and tormented after Sita's abduction, Rama keeps picturing her in Ravana's power. He remembers her gentle speech and beauty, then imagines that radiance eclipsed, as if the moon had been swallowed by Rahu. The verse is one more turn in his grief.
ramayan::7834.modern_relevance: You replay one image over and over after someone disappears from your life. Your mind keeps adding details, and each one hurts more than the last.
ramayan::7834.insight: It shows how grief turns memory into vivid suffering and keeps the loss alive in the mind.

ramayan::7835.verse_sanskrit: तां हारपाशस्य सदोचिताया ग्रीवां प्रियाया मम सुव्रतायाः । रक्षांसि नूनं परिपीतवन्ति विभिद्य शून्ये रुधिराशनानि । । 36310 । ।
ramayan::7835.verse_hindi: The bloodthirsty demons must have drunk the blood of my faithful beloved in a lonely place breaking her neck that used to wear beautiful necklaces.
ramayan::7835.english_translation: The bloodthirsty demons must have drunk the blood of my faithful beloved in a lonely place, breaking the neck that once wore beautiful necklaces.
ramayan::7835.translation_literal: तां (that woman) / हारपाशस्य (of necklace-strands) / सदोचिताया (of one always fit) / ग्रीवां (neck) / प्रियाया (of the beloved) / मम (my) / सुव्रतायाः (of the faithful one) / रक्षांसि (the demons) / नूनं (surely) / परिपीतवन्ति (have drunk) / विभिद्य (breaking) / शून्ये (in a lonely place) / रुधिराशनानि (blood-eating ones)
ramayan::7835.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7835.essence: Love under terror imagines the worst before truth arrives.
ramayan::7835.simple_meaning: Rama imagines that Sita has been attacked and killed in the forest. He pictures the demons breaking her neck and drinking her blood.
ramayan::7835.simple_insight: Grief can turn love into terrible certainty before any proof exists.
ramayan::7835.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama has lost all trace of Sita. Each detail he notices pushes him toward a worse conclusion. Here he imagines her jeweled neck torn by demons, showing how panic and love can feed each other.
ramayan::7835.modern_relevance: You hear silence from someone you love after a long drive home. Your mind starts writing the worst ending before you have any facts.
ramayan::7835.insight: It shows how absence can magnify fear into vivid, painful certainty.

ramayan::7836.verse_sanskrit: मया विहीना विजने वने या रक्षोभिराहृत्य विकृष्यमाणा । नूनं निनादं कुररीव दीना सा मुक्तवत्यायतकान्तनेत्रा । । 36311 । ।
ramayan::7836.verse_hindi: The lovely, largeeyed lady separated from me in the desolate forest, abducted and dragged by demons must have cried at that time desperately like a female osprey.
ramayan::7836.english_translation: The lovely, large-eyed lady separated from me in the desolate forest, abducted and dragged by demons, must have cried desperately then like a female osprey.
ramayan::7836.translation_literal: मया (by me) / विहीना (deprived of) / विजने (in desolate) / वने (forest) / या (who) / रक्षोभिः (by demons) / आहृत्य (having seized) / विकृष्यमाणा (being dragged) / नूनम् (surely) / निनादम् (a cry) / कुररी इव (like a female osprey) / दीना (wretched) / सा (she) / मुक्तवती (must have cried out) / आयत-कान्त-नेत्रा (large-eyed, lovely-eyed)
ramayan::7836.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7836.essence: Absence makes Rama imagine Sita's suffering as if he were hearing it.
ramayan::7836.simple_meaning: Rama imagines Sita, alone in the forest, seized and dragged by demons, crying out in helpless grief like a bird.
ramayan::7836.simple_insight: Love can turn imagination into pain, making absence feel immediate and unbearable.
ramayan::7836.detailed_meaning: Rama is searching for Sita after her abduction. Looking back at her loss, he pictures her being dragged through the lonely forest and crying out in terror. The verse deepens his grief and shows how vividly he feels her suffering.
ramayan::7836.modern_relevance: You replay the worst moment in your head because you cannot bear not knowing. The mind fills silence with images sharper than facts.
ramayan::7836.insight: It shows how grief reconstructs missing scenes and intensifies attachment into anguish.

ramayan::7837.verse_sanskrit: अस्मिन्मयासार्धमुदारशीला शिलातले पूर्वमुपोपविष्टा । कान्तस्मिता लक्ष्मण जातहासा त्वामाह सीता बहुवाक्यजातम् । । 36312 । ।
ramayan::7837.verse_hindi: On this rock, O Lakshmana, my goodnatured lady with her lovely smile sat with me in the past and chatted with you.
ramayan::7837.english_translation: On this rock, O Lakshmana, my good-natured lady with her lovely smile sat with me in the past and chatted with you.
ramayan::7837.translation_literal: अस्मिन् (on this) / मया (by me) / सार्धम् (together with) / उदारशीला (good-natured) / शिलातले (on the rock-seat) / पूर्वम् (before, formerly) / उपोपविष्टा (sat down) / कान्तस्मिता (with lovely smile) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana) / जातहासा (with laughter arisen) / त्वाम् (you) / आह (said) / सीता (Sita) / बहुवाक्यजातम् (many words, much conversation)
ramayan::7837.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7837.essence: A small remembered moment becomes unbearable after loss.
ramayan::7837.simple_meaning: Rama remembers Sita sitting on this rock with him and speaking cheerfully with Lakshmana. The verse is a grief-stricken memory of a vanished moment.
ramayan::7837.simple_insight: Loss makes ordinary memories ache with unbearable clarity.
ramayan::7837.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in the forest and points to a rock where Sita once sat beside him. He remembers her smiling, speaking freely with Lakshmana, and sharing an ordinary moment that now feels gone forever. The verse deepens his search through memory.
ramayan::7837.modern_relevance: You pass the café where you once laughed with someone who is gone from your life. The place is unchanged, but the memory lands like a wound.
ramayan::7837.insight: It shifts attention from the search itself to the tender evidence of what has been lost.

ramayan::7838.verse_sanskrit: गोदावरीयं सरितां वरिष्ठा प्रिया प्रियाया मम नित्यकालम् । अप्यत्र गच्छेदिति चिन्तयामि नैकाकिनी याति हि सा कदाचित् । । 36313 । ।
ramayan::7838.verse_hindi: Would she have gone to Godavari, the foremost of the rivers so dear at all times to my beloved ? But I think she has not gone there alone at any time.
ramayan::7838.english_translation: Would she have gone to Godavari, the foremost of rivers, so dear at all times to my beloved? But I think she has never gone there alone.
ramayan::7838.translation_literal: गोदावरीयम् (to Godavari) / सरिताम् (of rivers) / वरिष्ठा (foremost) / प्रिया (dear) / प्रियायाः (to the beloved one) / मम (my) / नित्यकालम् (always) / अपि (even) / अत्र (here) / गच्छेत् (would go) / इति (thus) / चिन्तयामि (I think) / नैकाकिनी (not alone) / याति (goes) / हि (indeed) / सा (she) / कदाचित् (at any time)
ramayan::7838.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7838.essence: Love keeps looking for someone in the places they once belonged.
ramayan::7838.simple_meaning: Rama wonders whether Sita may have gone to the Godavari river, but he doubts she would ever go there alone.
ramayan::7838.simple_insight: Grief keeps searching for familiar places, even when reason says the beloved is gone.
ramayan::7838.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is trying to reconstruct Sita's last movements after her abduction. He remembers the river Godavari and her habits, testing each possibility against the woman he knows. The verse shows a mind forced into painful guessing.
ramayan::7838.modern_relevance: You keep checking the places they used to love: the café, the park, the train platform. Loss makes ordinary places feel like clues.
ramayan::7838.insight: It shows how love turns memory into search, and search into sorrow.

ramayan::7839.verse_sanskrit: पद्मानना पद्मविशालनेत्रा पद्मानि वानेतुमभिप्रयाता । तदप्ययुक्तं न हि सा कदाचिन्मया विना गच्छति पङ्कजानि । । 36314 । ।
ramayan::7839.verse_hindi: The lady whose face was like the lotus, whose large eyes were like lotus petals could  have gone to fetch lotuses (but) that also is not possible as she has never gone there without me.
ramayan::7839.english_translation: The lady whose face was like the lotus, whose large eyes were like lotus petals, could have gone to fetch lotuses — but that is not possible, because she has never gone anywhere without me.
ramayan::7839.translation_literal: पद्मानना (lotus-faced) / पद्मविशालनेत्रा (lotus-wide-eyed) / पद्मानि (lotuses) / वानेतुम् (to fetch) / अभिप्रयाता (gone intending) / तत् अपि (that also) / अयुक्तम् (not fitting) / न हि (for not) / सा (she) / कदाचित् (ever) / मया (by me / with me) / विना (without) / गच्छति (goes) / पङ्कजानि (lotuses)
ramayan::7839.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7839.essence: Love notices the smallest habits and knows when they have been broken.
ramayan::7839.simple_meaning: Rama is trying to reason out where Sita might have gone, but he rejects the idea that she went alone to pick lotuses. He knows she never travels without him.
ramayan::7839.simple_insight: Love makes absence feel impossible, even before proof arrives.
ramayan::7839.detailed_meaning: Rama is searching the forest after Sita’s disappearance and retracing every familiar place. He remembers her habits and rules out one possibility after another. Here, his grief sharpens into logic: Sita would not have gone alone to gather lotuses.
ramayan::7839.modern_relevance: You replay a loved one’s last habits after they stop answering the phone. The mind reaches for ordinary explanations first, because the truth feels too large to name.
ramayan::7839.insight: It shows how grief starts by testing familiar patterns, trying to make absence fit memory.

ramayan::7840.verse_sanskrit: कामं त्विदं पुष्पितवृक्षषण्डं नानाविधैः पक्षिगणैरुपेतम् । वनं प्रयाता नु तदप्ययुक्त मेकाकिनी सातिबिभेति भीरुः । । 36315 । ।
ramayan::7840.verse_hindi: Could she have gone to the forest where there are many kinds of trees in full bloom inhabited by a variety of birds? That is also not possible as she is timid and too scared to go there alone.
ramayan::7840.english_translation: Could she have gone to the forest where many kinds of trees are in full bloom, filled with many kinds of birds? That too is impossible, because she is timid and would never go there alone.
ramayan::7840.translation_literal: कामं (perhaps) / तु (indeed) / इदम् (this) / पुष्पित-वृक्ष-षण्डम् (grove of flowering trees) / नानाविधैः (of many kinds) / पक्षि-गणैः (with flocks of birds) / उपेतम् (filled with) / वनम् (forest) / प्रयाता (gone) / नु (indeed) / तत् अपि (that also) / अयुक्तम् (impossible) / एकाकिनी (alone) / सा (she) / अति-बिभेति (is very afraid) / भीरुः (timid one)
ramayan::7840.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7840.essence: Love keeps eliminating impossible places, one by one.
ramayan::7840.simple_meaning: Rama keeps ruling out places where Sita might have gone. Even a beautiful forest seems impossible, because Sita is too fearful to wander there alone.
ramayan::7840.simple_insight: Love notices the smallest details when fear is involved.
ramayan::7840.detailed_meaning: Rama is searching for Sita after her abduction, and each guess is a wound he tries to reason through. He imagines the blooming forest, but rejects it at once: Sita is gentle, frightened, and never walks alone. His grief is turning into desperate deduction.
ramayan::7840.modern_relevance: You replay every place they might have gone, every detail of what they would or would not do. When someone you love is missing, the mind becomes a searchlight that cannot rest.
ramayan::7840.insight: It shows how grief narrows attention into careful, painful logic.

ramayan::7841.verse_sanskrit: आदित्य भो लोककृताकृतज्ञ लोकस्य सत्यानृतकर्मसाक्षिन् । मम प्रिया सा क्व गता हृता वा शंसस्व मे शोकवशस्य नित्यम् । । 36316 । ।
ramayan::7841.verse_hindi: O Sungod, you know all the happenings of the world. You are witness to all the deeds of the people, true and false. Tell me where my beloved Sita has gone or has been carried off. My grief never ceases.
ramayan::7841.english_translation: O Sun, you know all that has been made and all that has not. You witness the true and false deeds of the world. Tell me where my beloved Sita has gone, or whether she has been carried away. My grief never ends.
ramayan::7841.translation_literal: आदित्य (O Sun) / भो (O) / लोककृताकृतज्ञ (knower of what is made and unmade in the world) / लोकस्य (of the world) / सत्यानृतकर्मसाक्षिन् (witness of true and false deeds) / मम (my) / प्रिया (beloved) / सा (she) / क्व (where) / गता (gone) / हृता (carried off) / वा (or) / शंसस्व (tell) / मे (to me) / शोकवशस्य (of one ruled by grief) / नित्यम् (always)
ramayan::7841.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7841.essence: Grief makes even the strongest person plead for one answer.
ramayan::7841.simple_meaning: Rama cries out to the Sun for help, asking whether Sita has gone away or been abducted. He appeals to the Sun's all-seeing nature because grief has left him desperate.
ramayan::7841.simple_insight: When grief is overwhelming, even the most composed person starts asking the world to answer.
ramayan::7841.detailed_meaning: Rama is searching for Sita after her disappearance. Standing in anguish, he turns to the Sun as an all-seeing witness of the world and begs for any clue—whether she left, was taken, or is somewhere hidden. The verse is part of his desperate questioning.
ramayan::7841.modern_relevance: You replay the last place you saw them, then ask anyone who might know. When panic rises, you start pleading with the world for one clear answer.
ramayan::7841.insight: It shows how grief drives the mind to seek certainty from every possible witness.

ramayan::7842.verse_sanskrit: लोकेषु सर्वेषु च नास्ति किञ्चिद्यत्ते न नित्यं विदितं भवेत्तत् । शंसस्व वायो कुलशालिनीं तां हृता मृता वा पथि वर्तते वा । । 36317 । ।
ramayan::7842.verse_hindi: O Windgod, there is nothing that you know not in all the worlds. Do tell me if  that lady of a noble race has been abducted or dead or is on the way.
ramayan::7842.english_translation: O Windgod, there is nothing that you do not know in all the worlds. Tell me whether that lady of noble birth has been abducted, is dead, or is still on the way.
ramayan::7842.translation_literal: लोकेषु (in the worlds) / सर्वेषु (in all) / च (and) / नास्ति (there is not) / किञ्चित् (anything) / यत् (which) / ते (to you) / न (not) / नित्यं (always) / विदितं (known) / भवेत्तत् (would be) / शंसस्व (tell) / वायो (O Windgod) / कुलशालिनीं (of noble race) / तां (that woman) / हृता (abducted) / मृता (dead) / वा (or) / पथि (on the path) / वर्तते (is moving) / वा (or)
ramayan::7842.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7842.essence: Fear calms only when you ask for facts.
ramayan::7842.simple_meaning: Rama appeals to the Windgod as an all-knowing witness and asks whether Sita has been abducted, killed, or is still somewhere on the road.
ramayan::7842.simple_insight: Even in panic, the first need is clear information, not guesswork.
ramayan::7842.detailed_meaning: Rama is overwhelmed by fear after losing Sita. He turns from the Sun to the Wind, asking the cosmic witness for facts: was she taken, did she die, or is she still somewhere on the path? The search begins with inquiry.
ramayan::7842.modern_relevance: Your phone shows one missed call and your mind runs ahead to disaster. Before you spiral, you want one clean answer: what actually happened?
ramayan::7842.insight: It trains the mind to seek direct knowledge before imagination fills the gap.

ramayan::7843.verse_sanskrit: इतीव तं शोकविधेयदेहं रामं विसंज्ञं विलपन्तमेवम् । उवाच सौमित्रिरदीनसत्त्वो न्याये स्थितः कालयुतं च वाक्यम् । । 36318 । ।
ramayan::7843.verse_hindi: While Rama was thus in tears, in a state of sorrow and swoon, Lakshmana who was rational and courageous spoke to him words appropriate to the time :
ramayan::7843.english_translation: While Rama was thus in tears, in a state of sorrow and swoon, Lakshmana, steadfast in right conduct and fearless in spirit, spoke words suited to the moment.
ramayan::7843.translation_literal: इतीव (thus) / तं (that) / शोकविधेयदेहं (whose body was yielded to grief) / रामं (Rama) / विसंज्ञं (unconscious) / विलपन्तमेवम् (wailing thus) / उवाच (spoke) / सौमित्रिः (Lakshmana) / अदीनसत्त्वः (of undaunted spirit) / न्याये स्थितः (established in justice) / कालयुतं (timely) / च (and) / वाक्यम् (words)
ramayan::7843.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7843.essence: Lakshmana's steadiness meets Rama's collapse at the exact moment it is needed.
ramayan::7843.simple_meaning: Rama is overcome by grief, and Lakshmana responds with the right words at the right time.
ramayan::7843.simple_insight: Even in collapse, someone steady can speak the words that help you stand again.
ramayan::7843.detailed_meaning: Rama has fallen into grief after losing sight of Sita. He is exhausted, disoriented, and almost unconscious. Lakshmana, calm and brave, steps in not with emotion but with timing, ready to steady his brother and move the search forward.
ramayan::7843.modern_relevance: Your friend is spiraling after bad news, and you can see panic taking over. This is the moment to be the steady voice, not another wave of fear.
ramayan::7843.insight: It shows how courage can become support: the steadier person carries the moment until the other can move again.

ramayan::7844.verse_sanskrit: शोकं विमुञ्चार्य धृतिं भजस्व सोत्साहता चास्तु विमार्गणेऽस्याः । उत्साहवन्तो हि नरा न लोके सीदन्ति कर्मस्वतिदुष्करेषु । । 36319 । ।
ramayan::7844.verse_hindi: O noble prince, give up grief. Take courage. Show enthusiasm to search and find Sita. Enthusiastic people will not get despondent in carrying out the  most difficult tasks.
