ramayan::7892.english_translation: If Sita has been devoured or kidnapped, none in this world or even the divine can do anything to make me happy, O handsome Lakshmana.
ramayan::7892.translation_literal: भक्षितायाम् (if devoured) / हि (indeed) / वैदेह्याम् (Sita of Videha) / हृतायाम् (if carried off) / अपि (even) / लक्ष्मण (O Lakshmana) / के (who) / हि (indeed) / लोके (in the world) / प्रियम् (pleasant) / कर्तुम् (to do) / शक्ताः (able) / सौम्य (O gentle one) / मम (to me) / ईश्वराः (the divine beings)
ramayan::7892.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7892.essence: Some losses are so total that comfort cannot reach them.
ramayan::7892.simple_meaning: Ravana says that if Sita is dead or taken away, no one can restore his peace or make him feel better. The loss would be complete.
ramayan::7892.simple_insight: Some losses cut so deep that comfort itself feels impossible.
ramayan::7892.detailed_meaning: Ravana, speaking from a place of panic and dread, imagines the worst: Sita may have been eaten or carried off. He tells Lakshmana that if that has happened, no one in the world can undo it or bring him relief. The line reveals how total the crisis feels.
ramayan::7892.modern_relevance: You get the message that changes everything, and suddenly every normal fix feels useless. No explanation, distraction, or reassurance can touch the fact that something irretrievable may have happened.
ramayan::7892.insight: It names the point where a loss becomes too large for consolation and forces complete emotional reckoning.

ramayan::7893.verse_sanskrit: कर्तारमपि लोकानां शूरं करुणवेदिनम् । । 36454 । । अज्ञानादवमन्येरत्सर्वभूतानि लक्ष्मण ।
ramayan::7893.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana even the compassionate and heroic Creator of the worlds will be disrespected by all beings, however ignorantly (if such things are allowed to happen).
ramayan::7893.english_translation: O Lakshmana, all beings would, in ignorance, despise even the heroic and compassionate creator of the worlds.
ramayan::7893.translation_literal: कर्तारम् (creator) / अपि (even) / लोकानाम् (of the worlds) / शूरम् (heroic) / करुणवेदिनम् (knower of compassion) / अज्ञानात् (through ignorance) / अवमन्येरन् (would despise) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7893.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7893.essence: Ignorance can make even greatness look ordinary.
ramayan::7893.simple_meaning: People judge badly when they do not understand. Even the most heroic, compassionate being can be despised through ignorance.
ramayan::7893.simple_insight: It softens quick judgment and reminds you that lack of understanding warps respect.
ramayan::7893.detailed_meaning: Rama is speaking to Lakshmana after fearing Sita may be lost forever. In his grief, he reflects on how ignorance makes beings misread even the noblest power. The line prepares his self-reproach and despair.
ramayan::7893.modern_relevance: You see a leader make one mistake and suddenly every achievement gets erased in the group chat. A mind clouded by fear or resentment can no longer recognize what is still true.
ramayan::7893.insight: It shifts you from snap judgment to clearer seeing, especially when emotion is distorting your view.

ramayan::7894.verse_sanskrit: मृदुं लोकहिते युक्तं दान्तं करुणवेदिनम् । । 36455 । । निर्वीर्य इति मन्यन्ते नूनं मां त्रिदशेश्वराः ।
ramayan::7894.verse_hindi: The gods will certainly consider me a man engaged in the welfare of the world, a man of selfrestraint and compassion, but at the same time a weak man.
ramayan::7894.english_translation: The gods will certainly consider me a man engaged in the welfare of the world, a man of self-restraint and compassion, but at the same time a weak man.
ramayan::7894.translation_literal: मृदुं (gentle) / लोकहिते (in the welfare of the world) / युक्तं (engaged) / दान्तं (self-controlled) / करुणवेदिनम् (one who knows compassion) / निर्वीर्यः इति (as powerless) / मन्यन्ते (they think) / नूनं (certainly) / मां (me) / त्रिदशेश्वराः (the lords of the gods)
ramayan::7894.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7894.essence: Gentleness can be mistaken for weakness, even when it is disciplined strength.
ramayan::7894.simple_meaning: Rama says that even the gods may mistake his gentleness, self-control, and compassion for weakness.
ramayan::7894.simple_insight: It can hurt when your best qualities are misunderstood, but restraint is still strength.
ramayan::7894.detailed_meaning: Rama is speaking to Lakshmana in exile, after fearing Sita may be lost. He reflects on how even the highest beings may misread his calm, compassionate nature as impotence. The verse reveals the cost of choosing restraint over force.
ramayan::7894.modern_relevance: You stay calm in a tense meeting, and someone calls you passive. You keep your temper with your family, and they call you soft. Rama knows that pain: the strongest restraint is often the most misunderstood.
ramayan::7894.insight: It shifts you from defending your image to holding your character steady.

ramayan::7895.verse_sanskrit: मां प्राप्य हि गुणो दोषस्संवृत्तः पश्य लक्ष्मण । । 36456 । । अद्यैव सर्वभूतानां रक्षसामभवाय च । संहृत्यैव शशिज्योत्स्नां महान्सूर्य इवोदितः । । 36457 । । संहृत्यैव गुणान्सर्वान्मम तेजः प्रकाशते ।
ramayan::7895.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana even demerits turn into merits when they come in contact with me. Just as the Sun shines, effacing the moonlight, my brilliance will outshine my demerits of exterminating all (wicked) beings including the demons.
ramayan::7895.english_translation: O Lakshmana, even demerit turns into merit when it comes to me. See: today, for the destruction of all beings and the demons, I rise like the great sun, swallowing moonlight. By swallowing all my qualities, my brilliance shines forth.
ramayan::7895.translation_literal: मां (me) / प्राप्य (having reached) / हि (indeed) / गुणः (merit, virtue) / दोषः (fault, demerit) / संवृत्तः (becomes) / पश्य (see) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / अद्यैव (today itself) / सर्वभूतानाम् (of all beings) / रक्षसाम् (of the demons) / अभवाय (for destruction) / च (and) / संहृत्य (having withdrawn) / एव (indeed) / शशि-ज्योत्स्नाम् (moonlight) / महान् (great) / सूर्यः (sun) / इव (like) / उदितः (risen) / संहृत्य (having withdrawn) / एव (indeed) / गुणान् (qualities) / सर्वान् (all) / मम (my) / तेजः (splendour) / प्रकाशते (shines)
ramayan::7895.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7895.essence: Power can make even flaws seem like strengths.
ramayan::7895.simple_meaning: Rama says his own presence turns faults into strengths, and that his brilliance will now overpower all other qualities as he rises to destroy the demons.
ramayan::7895.simple_insight: Great force changes the meaning of everything around it.
ramayan::7895.detailed_meaning: Rama speaks to Lakshmana in the tense lead-up to war. He declares that his very presence transforms what looks like fault into power, like the sun swallowing moonlight. This is not a teaching in itself, but a forceful boast within a larger argument.
ramayan::7895.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the person everyone underestimated finally speaks with total authority. The moment is not about confidence alone — it is about power changing the meaning of the whole room.
ramayan::7895.insight: It shows how overwhelming presence can eclipse lesser traits and reshape how others judge strength.

ramayan::7896.verse_sanskrit: नैव यक्षा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः । । 36458 । । किन्नरा वा मनुष्या वा सुखं प्राप्स्यन्ति लिक्ष्मण ।
ramayan::7896.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, neither yakshas, nor goblins nor demons nor kinneras nor humans  will be in peace now.
ramayan::7896.english_translation: O Lakshmana, neither yakshas, nor goblins, nor demons, nor kinnaras, nor humans will find peace now.
ramayan::7896.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) / यक्षाः (yakshas) / न (nor) / गन्धर्वाः (gandharvas) / न (nor) / पिशाचाः (goblins) / न (nor) / राक्षसाः (demons) / किन्नराः (kinnaras) (or) / वा (or) / मनुष्याः (humans) / वा (or) / सुखम् (peace) / प्राप्स्यन्ति (will obtain) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7896.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7896.essence: Pride makes one enemy feel like the whole world.
ramayan::7896.simple_meaning: Ravana says his power will disturb every kind of being, not just one enemy group. He is announcing total threat, not a limited battle.
ramayan::7896.simple_insight: Unchecked anger spreads wider than its target.
ramayan::7896.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is speaking to Lakshmana while boasting of the havoc his weapons can unleash. He is not teaching dharma here; he is escalating the threat, claiming that no being across the worlds will be safe from him.
ramayan::7896.modern_relevance: A person in a rage texts three people, then ten, then everyone. What began as one wounded reaction starts shaking every relationship around it.
ramayan::7896.insight: It shows how ego turns a private conflict into a universal threat.

ramayan::7897.verse_sanskrit: ममास्त्रबाणसम्पूर्णमाकाशं पश्य लक्ष्मण । । 36459 । । निस्सम्पातं करिष्यामि ह्यद्य त्रैलोक्यचारिणाम् ।
ramayan::7897.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, just see, I will fill the sky with all my weapons and arrows and make all movements impossible in the three worlds.
ramayan::7897.english_translation: O Lakshmana, just see, I will fill the sky with all my weapons and arrows and make all movement impossible in the three worlds.
ramayan::7897.translation_literal: मम (my) / अस्त्र-बाण-सम्पूर्णम् (filled with weapons and arrows) / आकाशम् (the sky) / पश्य (see) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / निस्सम्पातम् (without movement, with no flying) / करिष्यामि (I will make) / हि (indeed) / अद्य (today) / त्रैलोक्य-चारिणाम् (of those who move through the three worlds)
ramayan::7897.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7897.essence: Arrogance dreams of stopping the whole world.
ramayan::7897.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he will crowd the sky with weapons and arrows until nothing in the three worlds can move freely.
ramayan::7897.simple_insight: Unchecked pride always imagines total control.
ramayan::7897.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to Lakshmana in the middle of a fierce confrontation. He boasts that his weapons will fill the sky and stop all movement across the three worlds, revealing the scale of his arrogance before the battle fully unfolds.
ramayan::7897.modern_relevance: A person in a heated argument starts talking like they can control everyone in the room. The bigger the boast, the clearer the panic underneath.
ramayan::7897.insight: It shows the mind of domination: when ego swells, it tries to freeze everything around it.

ramayan::7898.verse_sanskrit: सन्निरुद्धग्रहगणमावारितनिशाकरम् । । 36460 । । विप्रणष्टानलमरुद्भास्करद्युतिसंवृतम् । विनिर्मथितशैलाग्रं शुष्यमाणजलाशयम् । । 36461 । । ध्वस्तद्रुमलतागुल्मं विप्रणाशितसागरम् । त्रैलोक्यं तु करिष्यामि संयुक्तं कालकर्मणा । । 36462 । ।
ramayan::7898.verse_hindi: I will obstruct the movement of planets and the Moon, destroy the radiance of the Sun, the fire and block the wind crush the mountain tops, dry up the tanks, destroy the trees shrubs and creepers and annihilate the oceans. I shall bring about this fatal change at once in the three worlds.
ramayan::7898.english_translation: I will obstruct the movement of the planets and the Moon, destroy the radiance of the Sun, extinguish fire, block the wind, crush mountain peaks, dry up lakes, destroy trees, shrubs, and creepers, and wipe out the oceans. I will bring ruin to the three worlds at once through the force of time.
ramayan::7898.translation_literal: सन्निरुद्धग्रहगणम् (with the planets obstructed) / आवारितनिशाकरम् (with the Moon covered) / विप्रणष्टानलमरुद्भास्करद्युतिसंवृतम् (with the radiance of fire, wind, and the Sun destroyed and hidden) / विनिर्मथितशैलाग्रम् (with mountain peaks crushed) / शुष्यमाणजलाशयम् (with water-reservoirs drying up) / ध्वस्तद्रुमलतागुल्मम् (with trees, creepers, and shrubs destroyed) / विप्रणाशितसागरम् (with the oceans utterly ruined) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / तु (indeed) / करिष्यामि (I will make) / संयुक्तम् (combined) / कालकर्मणा (by the action of time)
ramayan::7898.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7898.essence: Pride turns fury into a fantasy of cosmic ruin.
ramayan::7898.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he can throw the whole cosmos into disorder, stopping celestial motion and destroying nature itself.
ramayan::7898.simple_insight: Unchecked rage makes a person imagine total destruction as power.
ramayan::7898.detailed_meaning: Ravana speaks to Lakshmana in the middle of his furious threat over Sita. He does not sound measured or wise; he sounds like a ruler whose pride has swollen into cosmic violence, claiming he can unravel the natural order itself.
ramayan::7898.modern_relevance: A person in a rage sends one message too many, then another, each more extreme than the last. In that moment, destruction feels like control.
ramayan::7898.insight: It shows how anger inflates the self until ruin feels like strength.

ramayan::7899.verse_sanskrit: न तां कुशलिनीं सीतां प्रदास्यन्ति ममेश्वराः । अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सौमित्रे मम द्रक्ष्यन्ति विक्रमम् । । 36463 । ।
ramayan::7899.verse_hindi: If the gods do not return my Sita safely to me, O Lakshmana  they will witness my power right now.
ramayan::7899.english_translation: If the lords do not return my Sita safely to me, O Lakshmana, they will witness my power right now.
ramayan::7899.translation_literal: न (not) / तां (that) / कुशलिनीं (safe and well) / सीतां (Sita) / प्रदास्यन्ति (will return) / मम (my) / ईश्वराः (lords) / अस्मिन् (in this) / मुहूर्ते (moment) / सौमित्रे (O Lakshmana) / मम (my) / द्रक्ष्यन्ति (will see) / विक्रमम् (valor)
ramayan::7899.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7899.essence: Restraint ends when what matters is still being withheld.
ramayan::7899.simple_meaning: Rama warns that if Sita is not safely returned at once, his force will become visible immediately.
ramayan::7899.simple_insight: There are moments when calm ends and action must speak for you.
ramayan::7899.detailed_meaning: Rama stands in the middle of a furious vow, speaking to Lakshmana after promising to unleash impossible force. Sita’s safety has become the point at which restraint can no longer continue, and the verse marks the instant before violence erupts.
ramayan::7899.modern_relevance: You’ve held back through one more delay, one more excuse, one more empty promise. Then the line is crossed, and everyone finally sees what you can do.
ramayan::7899.insight: It shifts the mind from passive waiting to decisive response when a limit has been reached.

ramayan::7900.verse_hindi: Lakshmana no beings will be able to move in the sky, blocked by arrows released from my bowstring there will be no space left there.
ramayan::7900.english_translation: Lakshmana, no beings will be able to move in the sky; my arrows loosed from the bowstring will leave no space there.
ramayan::7900.translation_literal: नाकाशम् (not the sky) / उत्पतिष्यन्ति (will fly up) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / मम (my) / चापगुणोन्मुक्तैः (released from the bowstring) / बाणजालैः (by nets of arrows) / निरन्तरम् (without interruption)
ramayan::7900.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7900.essence: Boasting reaches for total control when restraint is already lost.
ramayan::7900.simple_meaning: Ravana is boasting that his arrows will fill the sky so completely that nothing can move there.
ramayan::7900.simple_insight: Pride can sound powerful right before it becomes reckless.
ramayan::7900.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Ravana's furious threat, he turns to Lakshmana and describes a sky choked with arrows. He is not teaching anything here; he is escalating his boast, trying to overwhelm the enemy with the image of total destruction.
ramayan::7900.modern_relevance: Someone in a heated argument starts speaking in absolutes: every option is dead, every boundary will be crossed, nothing can stop them. The volume rises, but clarity is already gone.
ramayan::7900.insight: It shows a mind inflamed by anger, confusing intimidation with strength.

ramayan::7901.verse_sanskrit: अर्दितं मम नाराचैर्ध्वस्तभ्रान्तमृगद्विजम् । समाकुलममर्यादं जगत्पश्याद्य लक्ष्मण । । 36465 । ।
ramayan::7901.verse_hindi: O Lakshmna now beasts and birds will be confused and destroyed by my darts.You will see them crossing all limits of propriety.
ramayan::7901.english_translation: O Lakshmana, now you will see the world struck by my arrows, its beasts and birds thrown into confusion, and all limits of propriety broken.
ramayan::7901.translation_literal: अर्दितं (struck) / मम (by my) / नाराचैः (with arrows) / ध्वस्त (destroyed) / भ्रान्त (confused) / मृग (beasts) / द्विजम् (birds) / समाकुलम् (utterly agitated) / अमर्यादम् (without restraint) / जगत् (the world) / पश्य (see) / अद्य (now) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana)
ramayan::7901.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7901.essence: Unchecked power breaks order before it reaches its target.
ramayan::7901.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that his arrows will throw the world into chaos, disturbing animals and birds and breaking all order.
ramayan::7901.simple_insight: Raw force can shatter order in an instant.
ramayan::7901.detailed_meaning: Rama, grieving and furious after Sita's abduction, speaks to Lakshmana with terrifying resolve. He is not offering a teaching here but showing how far his anger will go: the whole world, even its creatures, will be thrown into disorder.
ramayan::7901.modern_relevance: You hit send while furious and suddenly the room, the chat, the whole day feels poisoned. One burst of force can scatter everything around you.
ramayan::7901.insight: It shows how grief-driven anger can spill beyond its target and disturb the wider world.

ramayan::7902.verse_hindi: For the sake of Maithili I will render this world devoid of goblins and demons with my irresistible arrows pulled up to my ears.
ramayan::7902.english_translation: For the sake of Maithili I will render this world devoid of goblins and demons with my irresistible arrows pulled up to my ears.
ramayan::7902.translation_literal: आकर्णपूर्णैः (drawn to the ear) / इषुभिः (with arrows) / जीवलोकम् (the world of living beings) / दुरावरैः (hard to resist) / करिष्ये (I will make) / मैथिलीहेतोर् (for the sake of Maithili) / अपिशाचम् (without goblins) / अराक्षसम् (without demons)
ramayan::7902.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7902.essence: Love here takes the form of unstoppable retaliation.
ramayan::7902.simple_meaning: Rama vows to use his arrows so fiercely that the world will be cleared of dangerous beings for Sita's sake.
ramayan::7902.simple_insight: Love can become fierce protection when someone you cherish is threatened.
ramayan::7902.detailed_meaning: Rama speaks after Sita's abduction, promising Lakshmana that his arrows, drawn back to his ears, will scour the world of hostile beings. The verse intensifies the resolve already building around Ravana’s crime.
ramayan::7902.modern_relevance: You hear about someone hurting a person you love, and something in you hardens. The urge is no longer debate — it is protection.
ramayan::7902.insight: It shifts resolve from grief into forceful protection.

ramayan::7903.verse_sanskrit: मम रोषप्रयुक्तानां सायकानां बलं सुराः । द्रक्ष्यन्त्यद्य विमुक्तानामतिदूरातिगामिनाम् । । 36467 । ।
ramayan::7903.verse_hindi: Now the gods will witness the power of my arrows released in great rage which can hit distant targets.
ramayan::7903.english_translation: Now the gods will witness the power of my arrows released in great rage, arrows that can strike from very far away.
ramayan::7903.translation_literal: मम (my) / रोष-प्रयुक्तानाम् (driven by rage) / सायकानाम् (of arrows) / बलम् (power) / सुराः (gods) / द्रक्ष्यन्ति (will see) / अद्य (today) / विमुक्तानाम् (released) / अति-दूर-अतिगामिनाम् (going beyond very far)
ramayan::7903.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7903.essence: Power under rage becomes a threat to everything nearby.
ramayan::7903.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that the gods will soon see how powerful his furious arrows are, because they can fly extremely far.
ramayan::7903.simple_insight: Anger can make you feel unstoppable, but it only inflates what is already dangerous.
ramayan::7903.detailed_meaning: Ravana stands in the middle of his own fury, speaking of arrows as if rage itself were a weapon. The surrounding verses escalate into total destruction, so this line is part of a larger threat rather than a complete teaching.
ramayan::7903.modern_relevance: You hit send while furious and feel powerful for ten seconds. The force is real, but so is the damage it can carry farther than you meant.
ramayan::7903.insight: It shows how rage turns skill into menace and pushes speech toward escalation.

ramayan::7904.verse_sanskrit: नैव देवा न दैतेया न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः । भविष्यन्ति मम क्रोधात्त्रैलोक्ये विप्रणाशिते । । 36468 । ।
ramayan::7904.verse_hindi: My anger will destroy all the gods, demons and evil spirits. They will be extinghished from the three worlds.
ramayan::7904.english_translation: My anger will destroy all the gods, demons, and evil spirits. They will be extinguished from the three worlds.
ramayan::7904.translation_literal: नैव (not even) / देवा (the radiant beings) / न (not) / दैतेया (the sons of Diti) / न (not) / पिशाचा (evil spirits) / न (not) / राक्षसाः (demons) / भविष्यन्ति (will remain) / मम (my) / क्रोधात् (from anger) / त्रैलोक्ये (in the three worlds) / विप्रणाशिते (when destroyed)
ramayan::7904.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7904.essence: Rage makes total destruction sound like power.
ramayan::7904.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his rage will wipe out every kind of being across the three worlds.
ramayan::7904.simple_insight: Unchecked anger makes destruction feel total, even when it is only self-deception.
ramayan::7904.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in the heat of pride, promising that his fury will leave no radiant being, demon, or spirit standing anywhere in the three worlds. It is not a teaching, but a display of terrifying arrogance that reveals how far his mind has gone from restraint.
ramayan::7904.modern_relevance: A furious text draft feels righteous for a moment, and then you read it back and see the wreckage it would cause. Rage loves exaggeration; it talks like everything must be burned down.
ramayan::7904.insight: It exposes anger as a force that inflates the self and erases proportion.

ramayan::7905.verse_sanskrit: देवदानवयक्षाणां लोका ये रक्षसामपि । बहुधा न भविष्यन्ति बाणौघैश्शकलीकृताः । । 36469 । ।
ramayan::7905.verse_hindi: The worlds of gods, yakshas or even demons torn into shreds by my arrows will not  survive.
ramayan::7905.english_translation: The worlds of gods, yakshas, and even demons will be shattered by my arrows and will not survive in many pieces.
ramayan::7905.translation_literal: देवदानवयक्षाणाम् (of gods, demons, and yakshas) / लोका (worlds) / ये (which) / रक्षसाम् (of demons) / अपि (even) / बहुधा (in many ways) / न भविष्यन्ति (will not remain) / बाणौघैः (by arrow-streams) / शकलीकृताः (made into pieces)
ramayan::7905.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7905.essence: Rage makes even overwhelming power look like ruin.
ramayan::7905.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that his arrows will shatter the worlds of celestial beings and demons alike.
ramayan::7905.simple_insight: Unchecked rage turns power into destruction, not strength.
ramayan::7905.detailed_meaning: Ravana is still raging after Sita's abduction. He is not reasoning now; he is threatening cosmic ruin, claiming his arrows can tear apart every realm if opposed. The verse is one step in his escalating fury, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramayan::7905.modern_relevance: A furious message thread can start like this: one person decides to scorch everything because they feel cornered. The verse shows how anger inflates the self until destruction feels justified.
ramayan::7905.insight: It warns how anger can make someone confuse devastation with control.

ramayan::7906.verse_sanskrit: निर्मर्यादानिमान्लोकान्करिष्याम्यद्य सायकैः । हृतां मृतां वा सौमित्रे न दास्यन्ति ममेश्वराः । । 36470 । ।
ramayan::7906.verse_hindi: If the gods do not hand over Sita to me either carried away or dead I will transgress these worlds, O Lakshmana
ramayan::7906.english_translation: If the lords of the worlds do not give me Sita, carried away or dead, I will violate these worlds with my arrows, O Lakshmana.
ramayan::7906.translation_literal: निर्मर्यादान् (without bounds / lawless) / इमान् (these) / लोकान् (worlds) / करिष्यामि (I will make) / अद्य (today) / सायकैः (with arrows) / हृताम् (carried away) / मृताम् (dead) / वा (or) / सौमित्रे (O son of Sumitra, Lakshmana) / न (not) / दास्यन्ति (will give) / मम (to me) / ईश्वराः (lords)
ramayan::7906.speaker: Ravana
ramayan::7906.essence: Desire without restraint turns the whole world into a threat.
ramayan::7906.simple_meaning: Ravana threatens to shatter the order of the worlds with his arrows if Sita is not handed over to him.
ramayan::7906.simple_insight: Unchecked rage makes everything feel like an enemy, even the world itself.
ramayan::7906.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana’s fury is rising by the hour. He speaks to Lakshmana with a mind already beyond restraint, threatening to make the worlds lawless if Sita is not returned to him. This verse shows how desire hardens into destruction.
ramayan::7906.modern_relevance: You are furious after being ignored, and suddenly every boundary feels like an insult. In that moment, rage wants to turn the whole world into the target.
ramayan::7906.insight: It shows how obsession turns grievance into a fantasy of total destruction.

ramayan::7907.verse_sanskrit: तथारुपां हि वैदेहीं न दास्यन्ति यदि प्रियाम् । नाशयामि जगत्सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् । । 36471 । ।
ramayan::7907.verse_hindi: If my beloved Vaidehi is not given back to me in her true form I will destroy the three worlds with all animate and inanimate beings.
ramayan::7907.english_translation: If my beloved Vaidehi is not given back to me in her true form I will destroy the three worlds with all animate and inanimate beings.
ramayan::7907.translation_literal: तथारूपाम् (in that form) / हि (indeed) / वैदेहीम् (Vaidehi) / न (not) / दास्यन्ति (they will give) / यदि (if) / प्रियाम् (beloved one) / नाशयामि (I will destroy) / जगत्-सर्वम् (all the world) / त्रैलोक्यम् (the three worlds) / स-चराचरम् (with moving and unmoving beings)
ramayan::7907.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7907.essence: When love is wounded, restraint can collapse into ruin.
ramayan::7907.simple_meaning: Rama says he will destroy the entire cosmos if Sita is not returned to him in the form he wants.
ramayan::7907.simple_insight: Love and rage can fuse into a force that threatens everything.
ramayan::7907.detailed_meaning: Rama has reached the edge of restraint in Lanka. After warning that the worlds will not survive his arrows, he now names the condition: if Vaidehi is not returned, he will wipe out the three worlds. The verse shows fury at its most dangerous.
ramayan::7907.modern_relevance: You finally lose patience after being ignored one too many times. The words come out sharper than you meant, and suddenly the whole room feels at risk.
ramayan::7907.insight: It shows how wounded attachment can turn into totalizing destruction.

ramayan::7908.verse_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा रोषताम्राक्षो रामो निष्पीड्य कार्मुकम् । शरमादाय सन्दीप्तं घोरमाशीविषोपमम् । । 36472 । । सन्धाय धनुषि श्रीमान्रामः परपुरञ्जयः । युगान्ताग्निरिव क्रुद्ध इदं वचनमब्रवीत् । । 36473 । ।
ramayan::7908.verse_hindi: After speaking these words, handsome Rama, his eyes red with anger, pressed his bow, took out the glowing arrow that was dreadful like a poisonous serpent, fixed it to his bow and said these words in a rage like the fire at the time of dissolution of the world.
ramayan::7908.english_translation: After speaking these words, handsome Rama, his eyes red with anger, pressed his bow, took out the glowing arrow that was dreadful like a poisonous serpent, fixed it to his bow and said these words in a rage like the fire at the time of dissolution of the world.
ramayan::7908.translation_literal: इत्युक्त्वा (having said thus) / रोषताम्राक्षः (with anger-red eyes) / रामः (Rama) / निष्पीड्य (pressing) / कार्मुकम् (the bow) / शरम् (arrow) / आदाय (taking) / सन्दीप्तम् (glowing) / घोरम् (terrible) / आशीविषोपमम् (like a poisonous serpent) / सन्धाय (having fitted) / धनुषि (on the bow) / श्रीमान् (the splendid one) / रामः (Rama) / परपुरञ्जयः (conqueror of enemy cities) / युगान्ताग्निः (the fire of the end of an age) / इव (like) / क्रुद्धः (angry) / इदम् (this) / वचनम् (speech) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7908.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7908.essence: Rage has become action, and action now has a weapon.
ramayan::7908.simple_meaning: Rama, furious and ready for battle, draws his bow, fits a blazing arrow, and speaks with terrifying force.
ramayan::7908.simple_insight: Anger can move the body fast, but it still needs restraint.
ramayan::7908.detailed_meaning: Rama has just threatened to destroy the worlds if Sita is not returned. Now he physically readies his bow and arrow, his rage matching the scale of his words. This is a charged battle prelude, not the teaching itself.
ramayan::7908.modern_relevance: Your jaw tightens, your hands move, and the email is almost sent. In that half-second, force is already becoming action.
ramayan::7908.insight: It shows the moment before violence: emotion, weapon, and intent aligning into one dangerous line.

ramayan::7909.verse_sanskrit: यथा जरा यथा मृत्युर्यथा कालो यथा विधिः । नित्यं न प्रतिहन्यन्ते सर्वभूतेषु लक्ष्मण । । 36474 । । तथाहं क्रोधसंयुक्तो न निवार्योऽस्मि सर्वथा ।
ramayan::7909.verse_hindi: Just as all beings in this world cannot avoid age and death, or defy time and fate so also none can prevent me at all when I am  angry, O Lakshmana
ramayan::7909.english_translation: Just as all beings cannot escape old age, death, time, or fate, so too no one can restrain me when I am angry, Lakshmana.
ramayan::7909.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / जरा (old age) / यथा (just as) / मृत्युः (death) / यथा (just as) / कालः (time) / यथा (just as) / विधिः (fate) / नित्यम् (always) / न (not) / प्रतिहन्यन्ते (are resisted) / सर्वभूतेषु (among all beings) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / तथाहम् (so I) / क्रोधसंयुक्तः (joined with anger) / न (not) / निवार्यः (to be restrained) / अस्मि (am) / सर्वथा (in any way)
ramayan::7909.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7909.essence: Anger can make even the restrained feel ungovernable.
ramayan::7909.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that anger can make a person feel as unavoidable as age, death, and fate itself.
ramayan::7909.simple_insight: Unchecked anger can feel absolute, but that is exactly why it needs restraint.
ramayan::7909.detailed_meaning: Rama has just threatened destruction if Sita is not returned. In the heat of grief and rage, he tells Lakshmana that anger has made him impossible to stop, like time or death. The verse shows how powerful emotion can override judgment.
ramayan::7909.modern_relevance: You are in a fight, your pulse is racing, and your words are getting sharper by the second. In that moment, anger can feel like a force nobody can slow down.
ramayan::7909.insight: It warns you to notice anger before it turns into unstoppable action.

ramayan::7910.verse_sanskrit: पुरेव मे चारुदंतीमनिन्दितां दिशन्ति सीतां यदि नाद्य मैथिलीम् । सदेवगन्धर्वमनुष्यपन्नगं जगत्सशैलं परिवर्तयाम्यहम् । । 36475 । ।
ramayan::7910.verse_hindi: I will topsyturvy this entire world including the gods, the gandharvas, human beings, serpents and mountains if they do not show me the princess from Mithila, who is blemishless and whose teeth are beautiful
ramayan::7910.english_translation: I will overturn the whole world, including the gods, gandharvas, humans, serpents, and mountains, if they do not show me Sita of Mithila, the blameless princess with beautiful teeth.
ramayan::7910.translation_literal: पुरेव (the whole world) / मे (for me) / चारुदंतीम् (the one with beautiful teeth) / अनिन्दिताम् (the blameless one) / दिशन्ति (they show) / सीताम् (Sita) / यदि (if) / न (not) / अद्य (today) / मैथिलीम् (the daughter of Mithila) / सदेवगन्धर्वमनुष्यपन्नगम् (with gods, gandharvas, humans, and serpents) / जगत् (world) / सशैलम् (with mountains) / परिवर्तयामि (I will overturn) / अहम् (I)
ramayan::7910.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7910.essence: Loss can make even the whole world feel negotiable.
ramayan::7910.simple_meaning: Rama, consumed by grief and rage, vows to shake the entire world if Sita is not returned to him now.
ramayan::7910.simple_insight: Love can become fierce enough to feel like the world itself must answer.
ramayan::7910.detailed_meaning: Rama has just drawn his bow, his anger burning after Sita’s abduction. Speaking to Lakshmana, he swears that if Sita is not revealed immediately, he will overturn the whole world. This is not strategy; it is grief turned volcanic.
ramayan::7910.modern_relevance: You’ve searched every room, every message, every clue, and the silence keeps growing. When what you love is taken, even the world can feel like it should be forced to answer.
ramayan::7910.insight: It shows how grief can magnify one loss until everything else feels unstable.

ramayan::7911.verse_sanskrit: तप्यमानं तथा रामं सीताहरणकर्शितम् । लोकानामभवे युक्तं सांवर्तकमिवानलम् । । 3651 । । वीक्षमाणं धनुस्सज्यं निश्श्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः । दग्धुकामं जगत्सर्वं युगान्ते च यथा हरम् । । 3652 । । अदृष्टपूर्वं सङ्क्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा रामं तु लक्ष्मणः । अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता । । 3653 । ।
ramayan::7911.verse_hindi: Tormented and emaciated due to Sitas abduction, resembling the fire at the time of dissolution of the creation, ready to destroy the world, Rama looked at his bow strung again and again, breathing hot sighs like Lord Siva at the end of the creation, wishing to burn down the world in a rage. Lakshmana who had never seen Rama in such anger before said to him with folded hands and parched throat.
ramayan::7911.english_translation: Tormented and emaciated by Sita's abduction, Rama looked like the fire of cosmic dissolution. He kept lifting his bow, breathing hot sighs, as if ready to burn the whole world in anger. Seeing Rama in a rage he had never seen before, Lakshmana spoke with folded hands and a parched throat.
ramayan::7911.translation_literal: तप्यमानं (being tormented) / तथा (thus) / रामं (Rama) / सीताहरणकर्शितम् (worn down by Sita's abduction) / लोकानामभवे (at the dissolution of the worlds) / युक्तम् (fitting) / सांवर्तकम् (of cosmic dissolution) / इव (like) / अनलम् (fire) / वीक्षमाणम् (looking) / धनुस्सज्यम् (with bow strung) / निश्श्वसन्तम् (breathing heavily) / पुनः पुनः (again and again) / दग्धुकामम् (wishing to burn) / जगत् (the world) / सर्वम् (all) / युगान्ते (at the end of an age) / च (and) / यथा (like) / हरम् (Shiva) / अदृष्टपूर्वम् (never seen before) / संक्रुद्धम् (angered) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / रामम् (Rama) / तु (indeed) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / प्राञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / वाक्यम् (words) / मुखेन (with mouth) / परिशुष्यता (parched)
ramayan::7911.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7911.essence: Grief can make a restrained man look like destruction itself.
ramayan::7911.simple_meaning: Rama is consumed by grief and rage after Sita's abduction, looking like a force of destruction. Lakshmana, shocked by this change, approaches him respectfully and speaks.
ramayan::7911.simple_insight: Deep grief can make even the strongest person look unrecognizable.
ramayan::7911.detailed_meaning: After Sita is taken, Rama stands exhausted, furious, and almost unearthly, bow in hand as if the world itself is about to end. Lakshmana sees a brother he has never seen before and, alarmed by that change, begins to answer him with care.
ramayan::7911.modern_relevance: You come home after bad news and keep pacing with your phone in your hand, unable to sit still. Grief can turn familiar strength into something fierce and frightening.
ramayan::7911.insight: It frames rage as a visible symptom of unbearable loss, not just a moral failing.

ramayan::7912.verse_sanskrit: पुरा भूत्वा मृदुर्दान्तस्सर्वभूतहिते रतः । न क्रोधवशमापन्नः प्रकृतिं हातुमर्हसि । । 3654 । ।
ramayan::7912.verse_hindi: Earlier you were gentle, self restrained and engaged in the welfare of all beings. (Now) it is not proper for you to give up your natural composure in anger.
ramayan::7912.english_translation: Earlier you were gentle, self-restrained, and devoted to the welfare of all beings. It is not right for you to abandon your natural composure in anger.
ramayan::7912.translation_literal: पुरा (earlier/previously) / भूत्वा (having been) / मृदुः (gentle) / दान्तः (self-restrained) / सर्वभूतहिते (in the welfare of all beings) / रतः (delighted/engaged) / न (not) / क्रोधवशम् (under the control of anger) / आपन्नः (fallen into) / प्रकृतिम् (natural disposition/composure) / हातुम् (to abandon) / अर्हसि (you ought)
ramayan::7912.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7912.essence: Your real strength is the composure anger tries to erase.
ramayan::7912.simple_meaning: Rama is reminded that his true nature is gentleness and self-control, not anger. Even in grief, he should not abandon the calm character that serves all beings.
ramayan::7912.simple_insight: Strength can mean staying composed when pain tries to harden you.
ramayan::7912.detailed_meaning: Rama has been shattered by Sita’s abduction, and those around him see his grief turning toward fury. This verse reminds him of the calm, restrained conduct that once defined him and warns him not to lose himself in anger.
ramayan::7912.modern_relevance: After a brutal argument, you feel your voice rising and your chest tightening. Someone who cares about you may be trying to stop you before anger becomes your new habit.
ramayan::7912.insight: It shifts the mind from reactive fury back to disciplined self-command.

ramayan::7913.verse_sanskrit: चन्द्रे लक्ष्मीः प्रभा सूर्ये गतिर्वायौ भुवि क्षमा । एतत्तु नियतं सर्वं त्वयि चानुत्तमं यशः । । 3655 । ।
ramayan::7913.verse_hindi: In you are always present the grace of the Moon, the radiance of the Sun, the motion of the wind, the forbearance of the earth and reputation.
ramayan::7913.english_translation: The grace of the moon, the radiance of the sun, the movement of the wind, the patience of the earth, and unmatched fame are all fixed in you.
ramayan::7913.translation_literal: चन्द्रे (in the moon) / लक्ष्मीः (grace, radiance) / प्रभा (splendour) / सूर्ये (in the sun) / गतिः (movement) / वायौ (in the wind) / भुवि (on the earth) / क्षमा (forbearance, patience) / एतत् (this) / तु (indeed) / नियतम् (fixed, always present) / सर्वम् (all) / त्वयि (in you) / च (and) / अनुत्तमम् (unmatched) / यशः (fame, reputation)
ramayan::7913.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7913.essence: Your nobility is made of many powers, not one.
ramayan::7913.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as holding the beauty of the moon, the brilliance of the sun, the motion of the wind, the patience of the earth, and unmatched fame.
ramayan::7913.simple_insight: Greatness is not one trait. It is the steady presence of many noble qualities at once.
ramayan::7913.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is praising Rama while trying to steady him after Sita’s abduction. He gathers images from nature—moon, sun, wind, earth—to remind Rama that his greatness has always included beauty, strength, movement, endurance, and fame.
ramayan::7913.modern_relevance: When someone you love is shaken, you may remind them who they have been at their best. Not to flatter them, but to call their strength back into the room.
ramayan::7913.insight: It shifts attention from grief alone to the character that can still hold steady inside grief.

ramayan::7914.verse_sanskrit: एकस्य नापराधेन लोकान् हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि । न तु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नस्साङ्ग्रामिको रथः । । 3656 । । केन वा कस्य वा हेतोस्सायुधस्सपरिच्छदः ।
ramayan::7914.verse_hindi: To destroy the world for the mistake of a single person is not proper. Why and by whom is this warchariot broken with weapons and all its accesories I do not know.
ramayan::7914.english_translation: To destroy the world for the mistake of a single person is not proper. Why and by whom is this war-chariot broken with weapons and all its equipment, I do not know.
ramayan::7914.translation_literal: एकस्य (of one) / न (not) / अपराधेन (by fault) / लोकान् (the worlds / people) / हन्तुम् (to destroy) / त्वम् (you) / अर्हसि (are fit) / न (not) / तु (but) / जानामि (I know) / कस्य (whose) / अयम् (this) / भग्नः (broken) / साङ्ग्रामिकः (battle-ready) / रथः (chariot) / केन (by whom) / वा (or) / कस्य (whose) / वा (or) / हेतोः (for what reason) / सायुधः (with weapons) / सपरिच्छदः (with all equipment)
ramayan::7914.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7914.essence: One person's fault never authorizes indiscriminate destruction.
ramayan::7914.simple_meaning: Harming everyone because one person erred is wrong. The broken war-chariot is also a mystery, and its cause is still unknown.
ramayan::7914.simple_insight: It reminds you to keep blame proportional, not let anger spill onto everyone around the problem.
ramayan::7914.detailed_meaning: In the aftermath of a fierce encounter, the speaker sees a broken war-chariot and the damage of battle. But he refuses collective punishment: one person's fault must not lead to the destruction of all. The verse holds both restraint and uncertainty.
ramayan::7914.modern_relevance: A manager finds one team member made a costly mistake and starts drafting a message that shames the whole department. This verse pulls the hand back before collective anger becomes collective harm.
ramayan::7914.insight: It shifts judgment from sweeping retaliation to measured responsibility.

ramayan::7915.verse_sanskrit: खुरनेमिक्षतश्चायं सिक्तो रुधिरबिन्धुभिः । । 3657 । । देशो निर्वृत्तसङ्ग्रामस्सुघोरः पार्थिवात्मज ।
ramayan::7915.verse_hindi: O prince, this place is damaged by the hooves of the horses and the rims of the chariot. It is soaked with drops of blood.Very dreadful must have been the fight here.
ramayan::7915.english_translation: O prince, this place is damaged by the hooves of the horses and the rims of the chariot. It is soaked with drops of blood. Very dreadful must have been the fight here.
ramayan::7915.translation_literal: खुरनेमि (horse-hoof and chariot-rim) / क्षत (damaged) / च (and) / अयम् (this) / सिक्तः (sprinkled) / रुधिर-बिन्दुभिः (with drops of blood) / देशः (place) / निर्वृत्त-सङ्ग्रामः (where battle has taken place) / सुघोरः (very dreadful) / पार्थिव-आत्मज (O son of a king)
ramayan::7915.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7915.essence: The battlefield itself reveals how fierce the fight was.
ramayan::7915.simple_meaning: The ground shows the signs of a fierce battle: broken tracks, blood, and heavy damage.
ramayan::7915.simple_insight: A battle leaves proof behind even when no one is speaking.
ramayan::7915.detailed_meaning: A close inspection of the battlefield shows churned earth, broken chariot traces, and blood drops scattered across the ground. The speaker is trying to understand what happened here by reading the marks left behind.
ramayan::7915.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after an argument and notice the slammed chair, the silence, the mess. The damage tells the story before anyone does.
ramayan::7915.insight: It shifts attention from rumor to visible evidence.

ramayan::7916.verse_sanskrit: एकस्य तु विमर्धोऽयं न द्वयोर्वदतांवर । । 3658 । । न हि वृत्तं हि पश्यामि बलस्य महतः पदम् ।
ramayan::7916.verse_hindi: O, best of the eloquent  this fight involves only one and not two. I do not see the footprints of a big army.
ramayan::7916.english_translation: O best of the eloquent, this fight involves only one and not two. I do not see the footprints of a large army.
ramayan::7916.translation_literal: एकस्य (of one) / तु (indeed) / विमर्धः (struggle, clash) / अयम् (this) / न (not) / द्वयोः (of two) / वदतांवर (O best of speakers) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / वृत्तम् (tracks, footprints) / हि (indeed) / पश्यामि (I see) / बलस्य (of an army) / महतः (great) / पदम् (footprint, trace)
ramayan::7916.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7916.essence: The evidence points to one fighter, not a whole army.
ramayan::7916.simple_meaning: The speaker says this was not a battle between two armies. It looks like the clash involved only one side, because there are no signs of a large force here.
ramayan::7916.simple_insight: A careful eye can tell when a story of war is being overstated.
ramayan::7916.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, someone examines the wreckage and notices a broken chariot, blood, and signs of only one fighter’s movement. Speaking to a respected listener, he argues that this was not a full army clash but the work of a single warrior.
ramayan::7916.modern_relevance: You arrive after the argument is over and everyone is calling it a huge fight. The room, the messages, the evidence tell a simpler story: one person did the damage, not a crowd.
ramayan::7916.insight: It trains you to look at evidence before accepting dramatic claims.

ramayan::7917.verse_sanskrit: नैकस्य तु कृते लोकान्विनाशयितुमर्हसि । । 3659 । । युक्तदण्डा हि मृदवः प्रशान्ता वसुधाधिपाः ।
ramayan::7917.verse_hindi: To destroy the entire world for one individual is not right. The lords of the earth should remain gentle, peaceful and punish only the deserving.
ramayan::7917.english_translation: To destroy the entire world for one individual is not right. The lords of the earth should remain gentle, peaceful and punish only the deserving.
ramayan::7917.translation_literal: नैकस्य (not for one) / तु (indeed) / कृते (for the sake of) / लोकान् (the worlds) / विनाशयितुम् (to destroy) / अर्हसि (you ought) / युक्तदण्डाः (properly punitive) / हि (indeed) / मृदवः (gentle) / प्रशान्ताः (peaceful) / वसुधाधिपाः (lords of the earth)
ramayan::7917.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7917.essence: Real strength punishes only what is guilty.
ramayan::7917.simple_meaning: A ruler should not bring ruin on everyone because of one person. True power is calm, fair, and measured.
ramayan::7917.simple_insight: Justice feels stronger when it is restrained, not when it spreads damage everywhere.
ramayan::7917.detailed_meaning: Rama is being urged to see the bigger moral picture after the search for Sita. The speaker reminds him that a king must not let one offense justify destruction of the whole world. A ruler’s strength lies in measured punishment, not rage.
ramayan::7917.modern_relevance: You’re furious at one colleague, and suddenly the whole team is about to pay for it. This verse pulls you back before your anger becomes collateral damage.
ramayan::7917.insight: It shifts you from reactive punishment to proportionate response.

ramayan::7918.verse_sanskrit: सदा त्वं सर्वभूतानां शरण्यः परमा गतिः । । 36510 । । को नु दारप्रणाशं ते साधु मन्येत राघव ।
ramayan::7918.verse_hindi: You are the ultimate resort and refuge of all beings. Who would like that your wife should be abducted ?
ramayan::7918.english_translation: You are the ultimate refuge and highest destination of all beings. Who would think it right for your wife to be abducted?
ramayan::7918.translation_literal: सदा (always) / त्वं (you) / सर्वभूतानां (of all beings) / शरण्यः (refuge-worthy) / परमा (highest) / गतिः (destination, resort) / को (who) / नु (indeed) / दारप्रणाशं (wife-abduction, loss of wife) / ते (your) / साधु (rightly) / मन्येत (would think) / राघव (Raghava)
ramayan::7918.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7918.essence: A refuge cannot be made to accept the violation of what he loves.
ramayan::7918.simple_meaning: Rama is being reminded that he is the refuge of all beings, so it is unthinkable that anyone would approve of Sita's abduction.
ramayan::7918.simple_insight: Even the strongest protector can be shaken by loss. The hurt is real because the bond is real.
ramayan::7918.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a serious plea, a speaker reminds Rama of his role as the refuge of all beings. The point is not abstract praise; it is a moral appeal: if Rama stands for protection, then Sita's abduction is a deep violation that no just mind could approve.
ramayan::7918.modern_relevance: When someone you trust is violated, you do not need a lecture about perspective. You need the plain recognition that what happened was wrong, and that the wound matters.
ramayan::7918.insight: It affirms that protection is part of right order, and that betrayal of trust is never trivial.

ramayan::7919.verse_sanskrit: सरितस्सागराश्शैला देवगन्धर्वदानवाः । । 36511 । । नालं ते विप्रियं कर्तुं दीक्षितस्येव साधवः ।
ramayan::7919.verse_hindi: Just as pious men do not do anything disagreeable towards persons who observe religious vows, so also rivers, seas and mountains, gods, gandharvas and demons are not capable of causing unhappiness to you.
ramayan::7919.english_translation: Just as pious men do not do anything disagreeable towards persons who observe vows, so rivers, seas, mountains, radiant beings, and shadow beings are not capable of causing you unhappiness.
ramayan::7919.translation_literal: सरितः (rivers) / सागराः (oceans) / शैलाः (mountains) / देवगन्धर्वदानवाः (radiant beings, gandharvas, and shadow beings) / न (not) / अलम् (able) / ते (to you) / विप्रियम् (displeasure) / कर्तुम् (to do) / दीक्षितस्य इव (like one who has taken a vow) / साधवः (pious people)
ramayan::7919.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7919.essence: No force can truly shake the one who stands in vow.
ramayan::7919.simple_meaning: No force in nature or among powerful beings can truly harm you. The speaker is assuring Rama that his vowed strength and righteousness make him beyond such injury.
ramayan::7919.simple_insight: Your steadiness can make outside forces feel smaller than they are.
ramayan::7919.detailed_meaning: In the midst of Sita's abduction and Rama's grief, a speaker reassures him that even rivers, oceans, mountains, and powerful beings cannot truly bring him low. It is part of a larger argument urging Rama to recover Sita and act.
ramayan::7919.modern_relevance: When everything feels against you — deadlines, family pressure, bad news, and your own fear — this verse reminds you that not every force around you gets to define your collapse.
ramayan::7919.insight: It shifts attention from imagined helplessness to the support already present around you.

ramayan::7920.verse_sanskrit: येन राजन्हृता सीता तमन्वेषितुमर्हसि । । 36512 । । मद्वितीयो धनुष्पाणिस्सहायैः परमर्षिभिः ।
ramayan::7920.verse_hindi: O king bow in hands, followed by me and with the help of great sages you should search for the one who has abducted Sita.
ramayan::7920.english_translation: O king, you should search for the one who abducted Sita, with me as your companion and with the help of great sages.
ramayan::7920.translation_literal: येन (by whom) / राजन् (O king) / हृता (abducted) / सीता (Sita) / तम् (that one) / अन्वेषितुम् (to search for) / अर्हसि (you should) / मद्वितीयः (with me as second) / धनुष्पाणिः (bow-in-hand) / सहायैः (with helpers) / परमर्षिभिः (with great sages)
ramayan::7920.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7920.essence: You keep searching for what was lost, and you do it with help.
ramayan::7920.simple_meaning: Rama is urged to keep searching for Sita’s abductor, with the speaker and great sages helping him.
ramayan::7920.simple_insight: Hard searches become bearable when you know you are not carrying them alone.
ramayan::7920.detailed_meaning: Sita has been taken, and the grief of the forest has turned into a mission. The speaker tells Rama to search for the abductor, not as a lone wounded husband but as a king supported by companions and sages.
ramayan::7920.modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor, phone in hand, trying to find one missing answer. The problem is bigger than you, but the next step still belongs to you.
ramayan::7920.insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to supported action.

ramayan::7921.verse_sanskrit: समुद्रं च विचेष्यामः पर्वतांश्च वनानि च । । 36513 । । गुहाश्च विविधा घोरा नदी पद्मवनानि च ।
ramayan::7921.verse_hindi: We will search oceans, mountains, forests and several dreadful caves, rivers and lotusponds.
ramayan::7921.english_translation: We will search the oceans, mountains, forests, dreadful caves, rivers, and lotus ponds.
ramayan::7921.translation_literal: समुद्रं (the ocean) / च (and) / विचेष्यामः (we will search) / पर्वतान् (mountains) / च (and) / वनानि (forests) / च (and) / गुहाः (caves) / च (and) / विविधाः (various) / घोराः (dreadful) / नदी (rivers) / पद्मवनानि (lotus groves / lotus ponds)
ramayan::7921.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7921.essence: The search is total because the loss is total.
ramayan::7921.simple_meaning: The search will not be limited to one place. Every possible terrain will be checked until Sita's abductor is found.
ramayan::7921.simple_insight: When something matters this much, you do not search halfway.
ramayan::7921.detailed_meaning: Hanuman and the others are speaking to Rama after Sita's abduction. They pledge to search every kind of place—sea, mountain, forest, cave, river, and pond—until they find the one who took her. It is a promise of total pursuit, not a teaching verse.
ramayan::7921.modern_relevance: You retrace every step after a child goes missing, checking parks, stairwells, buses, and back alleys. Panic becomes focus, and nothing gets ignored.
ramayan::7921.insight: It shifts attention from a narrow search to complete, determined action.

ramayan::7922.verse_hindi: We will search relentlessly for the abductor of your wife everywhere including the world of gods and gandharvas till we find her.
ramayan::7922.english_translation: We will search relentlessly through the worlds of the gods and gandharvas until we find the abductor of your wife.
ramayan::7922.translation_literal: देवगन्धर्वलोकान् (the worlds of gods and gandharvas) / च (and) / विचेष्यामः (we will search through) / समाहिताः (with focused minds) / यावत् (until) / न (not) / अधिगमिष्यामः (we will find) / तव (your) / भार्यापहारिणम् (the abductor of your wife)
ramayan::7922.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7922.essence: Nothing less than exhaustive effort will do.
ramayan::7922.simple_meaning: They will search every realm with full focus until Sita's abductor is found.
ramayan::7922.simple_insight: When something precious is lost, real effort means leaving no place untouched.
ramayan::7922.detailed_meaning: Rama and the search party have already committed to combing forests, mountains, rivers, and caves. Now the search widens even further: even the realms of celestial beings will be examined until Sita's abductor is found. It is a pledge of total pursuit, not a teaching by itself.
ramayan::7922.modern_relevance: You have already checked the obvious places, and the answer still is not there. So you widen the search, call in help, and keep going until the missing piece is found.
ramayan::7922.insight: It shifts you from partial searching to total commitment.

ramayan::7923.verse_sanskrit: न चेत्साम्ना प्रदास्यन्ति पत्नीं ते त्रिदशेश्वराः । । 36515 । । कोसलेन्द्र ततः पश्चात्प्राप्तकालं करिष्यसि ।
ramayan::7923.verse_hindi: O lord of Kosala when gods do not restore Sita on request, then you can think of taking action at the appropriate time.
ramayan::7923.english_translation: O lord of Kosala, if the gods do not restore Sita on request, then you can think of taking action at the proper time.
ramayan::7923.translation_literal: न चेत् (if not) / साम्ना (by conciliation) / प्रदास्यन्ति (will give back) / पत्नीं (wife) / ते (your) / त्रिदशेश्वराः (lords of the gods) / कोसलेन्द्र (lord of Kosala) / ततः पश्चात् (then afterward) / प्राप्तकालं (when the proper time has come) / करिष्यसि (you will do)
ramayan::7923.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7923.essence: Right action comes only after gentler means fail.
ramayan::7923.simple_meaning: If persuasion fails, Rama should wait for the right moment and then act. Force comes after peaceful means are exhausted.
ramayan::7923.simple_insight: Not every battle begins with force. First come patience, diplomacy, and timing.
ramayan::7923.detailed_meaning: Hanuman and the allies are planning how to help Rama recover Sita. They say the gods should be asked first, and only if that fails should Rama act at the right time. The verse places force after restraint.
ramayan::7923.modern_relevance: You have one chance to repair the relationship before everything hardens. You speak calmly first, because acting too soon can make the wound permanent.
ramayan::7923.insight: It teaches you to exhaust peaceful means before moving to force.

ramayan::7924.verse_sanskrit: शीलेन साम्ना विनयेन सीतां नयेन न प्राप्स्यसि चेन्नरेन्द्र । ततस्समुत्सादय हेमपुङ्खै र्महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैश्शरौघैः । । 36516 । ।
ramayan::7924.verse_hindi: O king if you fail to get Sita through appeasement, through humility or diplomacy then you destroy (the three worlds) by your goldtipped stream of arrows comparable to Indras thunderbolt.
ramayan::7924.english_translation: O king, if you fail to get Sita through appeasement, humility, or diplomacy, then destroy the enemies with your gold-tipped arrows, like Indra's thunderbolt.
ramayan::7924.translation_literal: शीलेन (through gentleness/character) / साम्ना (through conciliation) / विनयेन (through humility) / सीताम् (Sita) / नयेन (through diplomacy) / न प्राप्स्यसि (you will not obtain) / चेत् (if) / नरेन्द्र (O king) / ततः (then) / समुत्सादय (destroy utterly) / हेमपुङ्खैः (with gold-tipped) / महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैः (like Indra's thunderbolt) / शरौघैः (with a flood of arrows)
ramayan::7924.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7924.essence: Restraint comes first; force is justified only after peace fails.
ramayan::7924.simple_meaning: Try gentleness, conciliation, humility, and diplomacy first. If those fail, respond with overwhelming force.
ramayan::7924.simple_insight: You can be restrained without being weak.
ramayan::7924.detailed_meaning: Rama’s allies are advising him after Sita’s abduction. They tell him to try every peaceful means first, but not to hesitate if Ravana refuses. The verse marks the point where restraint turns into rightful action.
ramayan::7924.modern_relevance: You’ve sent the careful message, made the calm call, and offered a fair way out. If the damage continues, you stop negotiating and protect what matters.
ramayan::7924.insight: It teaches you to exhaust peace before force, then act without guilt when restraint no longer works.

ramayan::7925.verse_sanskrit: तं तथा शोकसन्तप्तं विलपन्तमनाथवत् । मोहेन महताविष्टं परिद्यूनमचेतनम् । । 3661 । । ततस्सौमित्रिराश्वास्य मुहूर्तादिव लक्ष्मणः । रामं सम्बोधयामास चरणौ चाभिपीडयन् । । 3662 । ।
ramayan::7925.verse_hindi: Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, consoling the mighty miserable Rama, who was afflicted with sorrow, and was weeping helplessly like an orphan, drowned in great delusion, devoid of consciousness, pressed his feet and addressed him:
ramayan::7925.english_translation: Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, consoling the mighty miserable Rama, who was afflicted with sorrow, and was weeping helplessly like an orphan, drowned in great delusion, devoid of consciousness, pressed his feet and addressed him:
ramayan::7925.translation_literal: तं (him) / तथा (thus) / शोकसन्तप्तं (tormented by grief) / विलपन्तम् (lamenting) / अनाथवत् (like an orphan) / मोहेन (by delusion) / महता (great) / आविष्टम् (overwhelmed) / परिद्यूनम् (dejected) / अचेतनम् (unconscious) / ततः (then) / सौमित्रिः (Lakshmana, son of Sumitra) / आश्वास्य (having consoled) / मुहूर्तात् (after a moment) / इव (as if) / लक्ष्मणः (Lakshmana) / रामम् (Rama) / सम्बोधयामास (addressed) / चरणौ (feet) / च (and) / अभिपीडयन् (pressing)
ramayan::7925.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7925.essence: Strength sometimes means holding someone else together first.
ramayan::7925.simple_meaning: Lakshmana comforts Rama after seeing him overwhelmed by grief, confusion, and helplessness.
ramayan::7925.simple_insight: Even the strongest person can collapse; steady care matters in that moment.
ramayan::7925.detailed_meaning: Rama has been crushed by sorrow and stands like a man who has lost all bearings. Lakshmana, his younger brother and constant protector, steps in, calms him, presses his feet, and speaks. The verse is a bridge into Lakshmana's consoling counsel.
ramayan::7925.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and see someone you rely on breaking down in silence. Before advice, before solutions, they need steady presence. Lakshmana shows that kind of care.
ramayan::7925.insight: It teaches you to meet another person's collapse with calm support, not panic or distance.

ramayan::7926.verse_sanskrit: महता तपसा राम महता चापि कर्मणा । राज्ञा दशरथेनासि लब्धोऽमृतमिवामरैः । । 3663 । ।
ramayan::7926.verse_hindi: O Rama king Dasaratha begot you by doing a great penance and performing great deeds, just as gods begot the nectar.
ramayan::7926.english_translation: O Rama, King Dasharatha obtained you through great austerity and great deeds, just as the gods obtained nectar.
ramayan::7926.translation_literal: महता (great) / तपसा (by austerity) / राम (O Rama) / महता (great) / चापि (and also) / कर्मणा (by deed) / राज्ञा (by the king) / दशरथेन (by Dasharatha) / असि (you are) / लब्धः (obtained) / अमृतमिव (like nectar) / अमरैः (by the immortals)
ramayan::7926.speaker: Lakshmana
ramayan::7926.essence: What is most precious is often won through sacrifice, then lost through love.
ramayan::7926.simple_meaning: Rama's birth was not ordinary. Dasharatha gained him through intense effort and merit, as if receiving something rare and priceless.
ramayan::7926.simple_insight: What you treasure most often comes after long effort and sacrifice.
ramayan::7926.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana is consoling Rama after his collapse in grief. He reminds him that Dasharatha did not receive such a son by chance; he earned him through severe effort, and now that same father is overwhelmed by separation.
ramayan::7926.modern_relevance: You finally get the role, the child, the relationship, the chance you prayed for — and then you realize it came through years of invisible effort. What was hard-won can still be lost to separation.
ramayan::7926.insight: It shifts attention from entitlement to earned value, and from possession to the fragility of what was gained.

ramayan::7927.verse_sanskrit: तव चैव गुणैर्बद्धस्त्वद्वियोगान्महीपतिः । राजा देवत्वमापन्नो भरतस्य यथाश्रुतम् । । 3664 । ।
ramayan::7927.verse_hindi: King Dasaratha, impelled by your virtues, and separation from you attained godhood as heard from Bharata.
ramayan::7927.english_translation: King Dasaratha, bound by your virtues and by separation from you, attained godhood, as Bharata had heard.
ramayan::7927.translation_literal: तव (your) / चैव (indeed) / गुणैः (by virtues) / बद्धः (bound) / त्वद्वियोगात् (from separation from you) / महीपतिः (the king) / राजा (king) / देवत्वम् (godhood) / आपन्नः (attained) / भरतस्य (of Bharata) / यथाश्रुतम् (as heard)
ramayan::7927.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7927.essence: Separation from what you love can undo even a king.
ramayan::7927.simple_meaning: Dasaratha was so bound to Rama's virtues and so wounded by separation that he died, as Bharata later heard.
ramayan::7927.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that absence becomes unbearable.
ramayan::7927.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the father who sent Rama away cannot survive the cost of that decision. Bharata has heard the story, and this verse names the hidden wound: Dasaratha was conquered not by war, but by separation from his son.
ramayan::7927.modern_relevance: You can hold it together all day, then fall apart in the quiet after someone leaves. Some losses do not look dramatic from outside; they hollow you out slowly.
ramayan::7927.insight: It shifts attention from outward strength to the private cost of separation.

ramayan::7928.verse_sanskrit: यदि दुःखमिदं प्राप्तं काकुत्स्थ न सहिष्यसे । प्राकृतश्चाल्पसत्त्वश्च इतरः कस्सहिष्यति । । 3665 । ।
ramayan::7928.verse_hindi: O Rama, if you cannot bear this sorrow that has befallen you, how can weak and ordinary persons endure (such suffering)?
ramayan::7928.english_translation: O Rama, if you cannot bear this sorrow that has befallen you, how can weak and ordinary persons endure such suffering?
ramayan::7928.translation_literal: यदि (if) / दुःखम् (sorrow) / इदम् (this) / प्राप्तम् (has come) / काकुत्स्थ (O Kakutstha, Rama) / न (not) / सहिष्यसे (you will bear) / प्राकृतः (ordinary) / च (and) / अल्पसत्त्वः (weak-minded, faint-hearted) / च (and) / इतरः (another) / कः (who) / सहिष्यति (will bear)
ramayan::7928.speaker: Bharata
ramayan::7928.essence: Your endurance becomes the measure others use to endure.
ramayan::7928.simple_meaning: Bharata reminds Rama that his strength matters because ordinary people look to him. If Rama cannot endure grief, weaker people will have even less hope.
ramayan::7928.simple_insight: Your composure can become a shelter for others.
ramayan::7928.detailed_meaning: Bharata stands before Rama after the exile has torn Ayodhya apart. He has already spoken of Dasharatha's grief and now presses the deeper point: Rama is not just suffering as a son, but carrying the burden of an ideal that others depend on.
ramayan::7928.modern_relevance: You walk into the room after the bad news, and everyone is watching your face. You do not get to collapse first if others are leaning on you.
ramayan::7928.insight: It shifts responsibility from private feeling to public steadiness.

ramayan::7929.verse_sanskrit: दुःखितो हि भवान्लोकांस्तेजसा यदि धक्ष्यते । आर्ताः प्रजा नरव्याघ्र क्व नु यास्यन्ति निर्वृतिम् । । 3666 । ।
ramayan::7929.verse_hindi: O best of men  if you grieve and burn the world with your brilliance, wherefrom will the (ordinary) afflicted people get relief?
ramayan::7929.english_translation: O best of men, if you grieve and burn the world with your brilliance, where will afflicted people find relief?
ramayan::7929.translation_literal: दुःखितः (grieving) / हि (indeed) / भवान् (you) / लोकान् (the worlds) / तेजसा (with brilliance) / यदि (if) / धक्ष्यते (will burn) / आर्ताः (afflicted) / प्रजाः (people) / नरव्याघ्र (O tiger among men) / क्व (where) / नु (indeed) / यास्यन्ति (will go) / निर्वृतिम् (to relief)
ramayan::7929.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7929.essence: Your sorrow becomes everyone’s burden when you cannot hold yourself together.
ramayan::7929.simple_meaning: If Rama lets sorrow consume him, ordinary people will suffer too. A leader’s inner state affects everyone who depends on him.
ramayan::7929.simple_insight: Your private pain is never fully private when others rely on you.
ramayan::7929.detailed_meaning: Bharata is urging Rama not to collapse into grief over exile. He reminds him that a prince’s sorrow does not stay personal: if Rama burns with anguish, the whole kingdom will feel it. The verse turns emotional restraint into a public responsibility.
ramayan::7929.modern_relevance: You walk into a family dinner after a brutal day, and everyone reads your face before you speak. Your mood changes the room more than your words do.
ramayan::7929.insight: It shifts you from self-contained suffering to responsibility for the emotional climate you create.

ramayan::7930.verse_sanskrit: लोकस्वभाव एवैष ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः । गतश्शक्रेण सालोक्यमनयस्तं समस्पृशत् । । 3667 । ।
ramayan::7930.verse_hindi: It is the go of the world. Yayati, son of Nahusa, shared heaven with Indra but because of his curse (for his bad conduct) suffered misfortune.
ramayan::7930.english_translation: It is the way of the world. Yayati, son of Nahusha, enjoyed heaven with Indra, but a curse later brought him misfortune.
ramayan::7930.translation_literal: लोकस्वभावः (the nature of the world) / एवैषः (indeed this) / ययातिः (Yayati) / नहुषात्मजः (son of Nahusha) / गतः (having gone) / शक्रेण (with Indra) / सालोक्यम् (shared dwelling) / अनयः (misfortune) / तं (him) / समस्पृशत् (touched)
ramayan::7930.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7930.essence: Even the highest fortune can turn without warning.
ramayan::7930.simple_meaning: Even a great king who once shared heaven with Indra later suffered misfortune. No height in life is permanent.
ramayan::7930.simple_insight: What feels secure today can change tomorrow, so you stop clinging to status.
ramayan::7930.detailed_meaning: Rama is being urged to bear sorrow because suffering is part of the world’s pattern. The speaker points to Yayati, son of Nahusha, who once shared Indra’s realm and later fell into misfortune. Even the mighty are not exempt.
ramayan::7930.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the praise, the perfect run of luck — and then one email changes everything. This verse reminds you that no peak is protected from change.
ramayan::7930.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to success toward seeing impermanence as normal.

ramayan::7931.verse_sanskrit: महर्षिर्यो वसिष्ठस्तु यः पितुर्नः पुरोहितः । अह्ना पुत्रशतं जज्ञे तथैवास्य पुनर्हतम् । । 3668 । ।
ramayan::7931.verse_hindi: To sage Vasistha, our fathers priest, were born a hundred sons in a day.But all of them were killed in one day the same way.
ramayan::7931.english_translation: To sage Vasistha, our fathers priest, were born a hundred sons in a day. But all of them were killed in one day the same way.
ramayan::7931.translation_literal: महर्षिः (great sage) / यः (who) / वसिष्ठः (Vasistha) / तु (indeed) / यः (who) / पितुः (of the father) / नः (our) / पुरोहितः (family priest) / अह्ना (in a day) / पुत्रशतम् (a hundred sons) / जज्ञे (were born) / तथा (so) / एव (indeed) / अस्य (his) / पुनः (again) / हतम् (killed)
ramayan::7931.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7931.essence: Greatness does not protect anyone from devastating reversal.
ramayan::7931.simple_meaning: Vasistha once had a hundred sons born in a single day, and all of them were killed in a single day too.
ramayan::7931.simple_insight: Even the greatest households are not spared loss.
ramayan::7931.detailed_meaning: The speaker recalls Vasistha, the family priest, as proof that even a sage can suffer unbearable reversal. A hundred sons came to him in one day, and the same number were taken away in one day. The point is to measure the scale of grief, not to tell a side story.
ramayan::7931.modern_relevance: A family photo sits on the shelf, and one phone call changes everything. Some losses arrive so fast that your mind cannot even keep up with their meaning.
ramayan::7931.insight: It trains the mind to see that no household is exempt from sudden loss.

ramayan::7932.verse_sanskrit: या चेयं जगतां माता देवी लोकनमस्कृता । अस्याश्च चलनं भूमेर्दृश्यते सत्यसंश्रव । । 3669 । ।
ramayan::7932.verse_hindi: You (rigidly) adhere to truth.(Like you) the mother earth who is adored by all the worlds, is unshakeable. Yet she is seen to be shaking at times.
ramayan::7932.english_translation: You rigidly adhere to truth. Like the mother earth adored by all the worlds, you are unshakeable. Yet even she is seen to tremble at times.
ramayan::7932.translation_literal: या (and) / च (also) / इयं (this) / जगताम् (of the worlds) / माता (mother) / देवी (radiant one) / लोकनमस्कृता (worshipped by the worlds) / अस्याः (of her) / च (and) / चलनम् (movement, shaking) / भूमेः (of the earth) / दृश्यते (is seen) / सत्यसंश्रव (one firmly bound to truth)
ramayan::7932.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7932.essence: Truth makes a person steady, though pressure can still make that steadiness visible.
ramayan::7932.simple_meaning: Truthfulness gives a person a steadiness like the earth, which is usually unmoving even though it sometimes shakes.
ramayan::7932.simple_insight: Integrity does not make life motionless, but it gives you a center that survives disturbance.
ramayan::7932.detailed_meaning: The sages are praising a ruler whose word is fixed in truth. They compare him to the earth, revered by all and usually steady, yet still capable of trembling. The point is that even great steadiness can be tested by force.
ramayan::7932.modern_relevance: You keep your promise while everything around you shifts — family pressure, deadlines, fear, doubt. The strain may show, but your word still anchors you.
ramayan::7932.insight: It teaches you to measure strength by steadiness of character, not by the absence of pressure.

ramayan::7933.verse_sanskrit: यौ धर्मौ जगतां नेत्रौ यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । आदित्यचन्द्रौ ग्रहणमभ्युपेतौ महाबलौ । । 36610 । ।
ramayan::7933.verse_hindi: The powerful Sun and Moon, righteous entities, who are the two eyes of these worlds and on whom everything rests firmly, also suffer eclipses sometimes.
ramayan::7933.english_translation: The powerful Sun and Moon, the two eyes of the worlds on whom everything rests, also undergo eclipses.
ramayan::7933.translation_literal: यौ (which two) / धर्मौ (righteous) / जगतां (of the worlds) / नेत्रौ (the two eyes) / यत्र (on whom) / सर्वं (everything) / प्रतिष्ठितम् (is established) / आदित्यचन्द्रौ (the Sun and Moon) / ग्रहणम् (eclipse) / अभ्युपेतौ (have undergone / are subject to) / महाबलौ (the very powerful)
ramayan::7933.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7933.essence: Even the greatest lights in the world are subject to shadow.
ramayan::7933.simple_meaning: Even the most powerful and dependable things in the world can be eclipsed. Nothing that changes stays beyond disturbance.
ramayan::7933.simple_insight: It softens your grip on what looks permanent and reminds you that brilliance still belongs to the changing world.
ramayan::7933.detailed_meaning: Vasistha is pointing to examples that everyone trusts: the sun and moon, the eyes of the world. Even they are covered at times. The argument is building toward a larger truth about the limits of created things.
ramayan::7933.modern_relevance: You trusted the one person who always seemed steady, and then they vanished for a week. The shock hurts because you had made them permanent. This verse warns you not to.
ramayan::7933.insight: It trains you to see that even the strongest forms of stability can be interrupted, so attachment should loosen.

ramayan::7934.verse_sanskrit: सुमहान्त्यपि भूतानि देवाश्च पुरुषर्षभ । न दैवस्य प्रमुञ्चन्ति सर्वभूतानि देहिनः । । 36611 । ।
ramayan::7934.verse_hindi: O best among men  Fate spares none. Great beings, every creature, even the gods cannot escape fate.
ramayan::7934.english_translation: O best among men, fate spares none. Great beings, every creature, even the gods cannot escape fate.
ramayan::7934.translation_literal: सुमहान्ति (very great) / अपि (even) / भूतानि (beings) / देवाः (the gods) / च (and) / पुरुषर्षभ (best among men) / न (not) / दैवस्य (of fate) / प्रमुञ्चन्ति (escape) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / देहिनः (embodied ones)
ramayan::7934.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7934.essence: Even the greatest beings remain within the reach of fate.
ramayan::7934.simple_meaning: No being, however great, can escape the force that governs events. Even the radiant beings are not exempt.
ramayan::7934.simple_insight: It softens pride and fear at once: you are not all-powerful, but you are also not singled out.
ramayan::7934.detailed_meaning: In the midst of a grave exchange, the speaker reminds the listener that even the greatest beings, including the radiant ones, cannot step outside the rule that governs embodied life. The point is not comfort but realism: no one is exempt from consequence.
ramayan::7934.modern_relevance: You can plan every detail of the move, the launch, the apology, and the diagnosis still arrives. This verse meets the moment when life refuses to obey your schedule.
ramayan::7934.insight: It shifts the mind from control fantasies to sober acceptance of limits and consequence.

ramayan::7935.verse_sanskrit: शक्रादिष्वपि देवेषु वर्तमानौ नयानयौ । श्रूयेते नरशार्दूल न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि । । 36612 । ।
ramayan::7935.verse_hindi: It is I heard that Indra and other deities are also governed by the principle of justice. Therefore, you should not bewail, O tiger among men.
ramayan::7935.english_translation: It is heard that Indra and other deities are also governed by the principle of justice. Therefore, you should not grieve, O tiger among men.
ramayan::7935.translation_literal: शक्रादिषु (among Indra and others) / अपि (also) / देवेषु (among the deities) / वर्तमानौ (existing, operating) / नयानयौ (right and wrong, justice and injustice) / श्रूयेते (are heard of) / नरशार्दूल (O tiger among men) / न (not) / त्वं (you) / शोचितुम् (to grieve) / अर्हसि (you should)
ramayan::7935.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7935.essence: Even the mighty are answered by justice, so grief need not rule you.
ramayan::7935.simple_meaning: Even powerful beings are subject to right and wrong, so you should not sink into grief.
ramayan::7935.simple_insight: Your pain feels personal, but the order of things is larger than your fear.
ramayan::7935.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Rama’s sorrow over Sita, the speaker points to a harder law: even Indra and the other radiant beings are not beyond justice. This is meant to steady Rama, not erase his pain.
ramayan::7935.modern_relevance: You replay a mistake at 1 a.m. and feel singled out by life. This verse reminds you that even the powerful are not exempt from consequence or order.
ramayan::7935.insight: It shifts the mind from personal collapse to seeing a larger moral order at work.

ramayan::7936.verse_sanskrit: नष्टायामपि वैदेह्यां हृतायामपि चानघशोचितुं नार्हसे वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा । । 36613 । ।
ramayan::7936.verse_hindi: Even if Vaidehi is killed or abducted, you should not grieve like ordinary men, O
ramayan::7936.english_translation: Even if Vaidehi has been killed or abducted, you should not grieve like an ordinary man, O hero.
ramayan::7936.translation_literal: नष्टायाम् (having been destroyed) / अपि (even) / वैदेह्याम् (Vaidehi) / हृतायाम् (having been seized) / अपि (even) / च (and) / अनघ (sinless one) / शोचितुम् (to grieve) / न (not) / अर्हसे (you should) / वीर (hero) / यथा (like) / अन्यः (another) / प्राकृतः (ordinary man) / तथा (thus)
ramayan::7936.speaker: Unknown
ramayan::7936.essence: Real loss does not require you to abandon your composure.
ramayan::7936.simple_meaning: Even if Sita has been killed or taken away, Rama should not fall into ordinary grief. He is being asked to stand above raw panic and keep his dignity.
ramayan::7936.simple_insight: Pain may be real, but it does not have to erase your steadiness.
ramayan::7936.detailed_meaning: After hearing that fate rules even the mighty, the speaker turns to Rama and says Sita's loss cannot justify collapse. The point is not denial of grief, but the discipline of remaining a hero when everything feels ruined.
ramayan::7936.modern_relevance: You get a call that changes everything, and your hands start shaking. This verse reminds you that even real loss does not have to turn you into panic.
ramayan::7936.insight: It shifts you from emotional collapse to dignified endurance under pressure.

ramayan::7937.verse_sanskrit: त्वव्दिधा न हि शोचन्ति सततं सत्यदर्शिनः । सुमहत्स्वपि कृच्छ्रेषु रामानिर्विण्णदर्शनाः । । 36614 । ।
ramayan::7937.verse_hindi: O Rama, you always see the truth. So  in the face of great difficulties men like you, whose vision is not blurred, should not lose heart.
ramayan::7937.english_translation: O Rama, you always see the truth. So in great difficulties, people like you, whose vision is never clouded, should not lose heart.
ramayan::7937.translation_literal: त्वव्दिधाः (people like you) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / शोचन्ति (grieve) / सततं (always) / सत्यदर्शिनः (truth-seeing ones) / सुमहत्सु (in very great) / अपि (even) / कृच्छ्रेषु (difficulties) / राम (Rama) / अनिर्विण्णदर्शनाः (those whose vision is not dejected/blurred)
ramayan::7937.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7937.essence: Clear seeing keeps you steady when life turns harsh.
ramayan::7937.simple_meaning: People who see reality clearly do not fall into despair, even in severe trouble. Clear sight keeps the mind steady.
ramayan::7937.simple_insight: You can face pain without being swallowed by it.
ramayan::7937.detailed_meaning: Rama is being urged not to break under grief. The speaker reminds him that those who see truth clearly do not sink into despair, even when the situation is crushing. The next line will ask him to judge with discernment.
