ramayan::7986.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7986.essence: The truth arrives too late for the one who carried it.
ramayan::7986.simple_meaning: Jatayu dies just as Rama urgently asks for news of Sita. The scene shows the final moment of a loyal ally who has done his duty.
ramayan::7986.simple_insight: Some loyalty ends in silence, but it is never wasted.
ramayan::7986.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has just revealed Ravana’s identity to Rama and spoken with his last strength. As Rama, hands folded, asks him to tell more, the vulture’s life leaves him. The exchange ends not with comfort, but with a death earned in protection.
ramayan::7986.modern_relevance: You finally reach someone who can explain what happened, but their energy is gone. The truth comes through just as the person who carried it can no longer stay.
ramayan::7986.insight: It shifts attention from the information to the sacrifice behind it.

ramayan::7987.verse_sanskrit: स निक्षिप्य शिरो भूमौ प्रसार्य चरणौ तदा । । 36818 । । विक्षिप्य च शरीरं स्वं पपात धरणीतले ।
ramayan::7987.verse_hindi: Then Jatayu dropped his head down, his feet thrown about, his body outstretched on earth.
ramayan::7987.english_translation: Then Jatayu dropped his head down, his feet thrown about, his body outstretched on earth.
ramayan::7987.translation_literal: स (he) / निक्षिप्य (having placed) / शिरः (head) / भूमौ (on the ground) / प्रसार्य (having stretched out) / चरणौ (feet) / तदा (then) / विक्षिप्य (having flung apart) / च (and) / शरीरं (body) / स्वं (his own) / पपात (fell) / धरणीतले (on the earth's surface)
ramayan::7987.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7987.essence: His body falls where his loyalty stood.
ramayan::7987.simple_meaning: Jatayu collapsed onto the ground, his body falling apart as life left him.
ramayan::7987.simple_insight: Some deaths arrive with dignity intact, even in defeat.
ramayan::7987.detailed_meaning: After telling Rama what happened to Sita, the wounded vulture Jatayu can no longer hold himself up. He lowers his head, stretches his limbs, and falls onto the earth as his life ends. The verse is a physical closing of his sacrifice.
ramayan::7987.modern_relevance: You finally say the hard truth you were holding in, and your body gives out after. The release can feel as heavy as the wound.
ramayan::7987.insight: It shifts attention from heroic speech to the bodily cost of sacrifice.

ramayan::7988.verse_hindi: Stricken with deep grief, his eyes red (with tears) Rama saw the vulture looking like a mountain. Seeing him dead, he said to Lakshmana:
ramayan::7988.english_translation: Seeing the vulture, its red eyes filled with grief, lying dead like a mountain, Rama, overcome with many sorrows, said to Lakshmana:
ramayan::7988.translation_literal: तम् (that) / गृध्रम् (vulture) / प्रेक्ष्य (seeing) / ताम्राक्षम् (red-eyed) / गतासुम् (lifeless) / अचलोपमम् (mountain-like) / रामः (Rama) / सुबहुभिः (by many) / दुःखैः (sorrows) / दीनः (grief-stricken) / सौमित्रिम् (to Lakshmana) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
ramayan::7988.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7988.essence: Grief first silences the one who can bear almost anything.
ramayan::7988.simple_meaning: Rama sees Jatayu dead and is overwhelmed with grief as he turns to Lakshmana.
ramayan::7988.simple_insight: Some losses are so heavy they leave even the strongest speechless for a moment.
ramayan::7988.detailed_meaning: Jatayu has fallen after fighting to protect Sita. Rama stands before the dead bird, red-eyed and shaken, and turns to Lakshmana. This is the instant grief becomes spoken mourning, just before Rama reflects on what Jatayu has done.
ramayan::7988.modern_relevance: You arrive too late and find the one who tried to help you gone. Grief hits first; words come only after.
ramayan::7988.insight: It shows the pause that follows shock, before the mind can make meaning of loss.

ramayan::7989.verse_sanskrit: बहूनि रक्षसां वासे वर्षाणि वसता सुखम् । । 36820 । । अनेन दण्डकारण्ये विशीर्णमिह पक्षिणा ।
ramayan::7989.verse_hindi: Dwelling for many years happily in Dandaka forest, the abode of demons, the bird lost his life (on our account).
ramayan::7989.english_translation: Dwelling for many years happily in Dandaka forest, the abode of demons, the bird lost his life on our account.
ramayan::7989.translation_literal: बहूनि (many) / रक्षसां (of demons) / वासे (in the dwelling) / वर्षाणि (years) / वसता (dwelling) / सुखम् (happily) / अनेन (by this one) / दण्डकारण्ये (in Dandaka forest) / विशीर्णम् (shattered; lost) / इह (here) / पक्षिणा (by the bird)
ramayan::7989.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7989.essence: A long safe life can still end in one noble sacrifice.
ramayan::7989.simple_meaning: The bird lived safely for many years in the dangerous forest, but now he has died because he helped them.
ramayan::7989.simple_insight: Even a life of safety can end in sacrifice when courage is needed.
ramayan::7989.detailed_meaning: Rama, grieving over Jatayu's body, remembers that the vulture had lived long and safely in Dandaka despite its dangers. Now that same bird has died protecting Sita and helping Rama. The line deepens the tragedy of loyal sacrifice.
ramayan::7989.modern_relevance: You may spend years staying out of danger, only to be called into one moment that costs everything. Some acts of loyalty are remembered only after they are gone.
ramayan::7989.insight: It shifts attention from a long safe life to the meaning of a final courageous act.

ramayan::7990.verse_sanskrit: अनेकवार्षिको यस्तु चिरकालसमुत्थितः । । 36821 । । सोऽयमद्य हतश्शेते कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः ।
ramayan::7990.verse_hindi: This Jatayu, who lived for long years, is lying dead now. (The dictate of) destiny is inescapable.
ramayan::7990.english_translation: This Jatayu, who lived for long years, is lying dead now. Time is hard to overcome.
ramayan::7990.translation_literal: अनेकवार्षिकः (of many years) / यः (who) / तु (indeed) / चिरकालसमुत्थितः (long-standing, long-lived) / सः (that one) / अयम् (this one) / अद्य (today) / हतः (killed) / शेते (lies) / कालः (time) / हि (indeed) / दुरतिक्रमः (hard to overcome)
ramayan::7990.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7990.essence: Even a long life ends when time arrives.
ramayan::7990.simple_meaning: Even someone who has lived for many years can die. Time cannot be escaped.
ramayan::7990.simple_insight: Grief becomes clearer when you see how little control you have over loss.
ramayan::7990.detailed_meaning: Rama stands over Jatayu's body in the forest, shaken by the bird's sacrifice for Sita. He sees that age, strength, and loyalty all still end in death, and speaks the hard truth that time overpowers everyone.
ramayan::7990.modern_relevance: You visit someone in the hospital and realize how quickly strength can vanish. A body that carried years of effort can still fail without warning.
ramayan::7990.insight: It shifts the mind from assuming permanence to meeting loss as part of life.

ramayan::7991.verse_sanskrit: पश्य लक्ष्मण गृध्रोऽयमुपकारी हतश्च मे । । 36822 । । सीतामभ्यवपन्नो वै रावणेन बलीयसा ।
ramayan::7991.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana, see this Jatayu, my benefactor, killed by the powerful Ravana while he was reaching out to help Sita.
ramayan::7991.english_translation: O Lakshmana, see this Jatayu, my benefactor, killed by the powerful Ravana while he was reaching out to help Sita.
ramayan::7991.translation_literal: पश्य (see) / लक्ष्मण (Lakshmana) / गृध्रः (the bird) / अयम् (this) / उपकारी (benefactor/helper) / हतः (killed) / च (and) / मे (my) / सीताम् (Sita) / अभ्यवपन्नः (having approached to protect/help) / वै (indeed) / रावणेन (by Ravana) / बलीयसा (by the stronger one)
ramayan::7991.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7991.essence: A helper may fall, but the sacrifice remains sacred.
ramayan::7991.simple_meaning: Rama points out Jatayu to Lakshmana: the bird who tried to help Sita has been killed by Ravana.
ramayan::7991.simple_insight: Goodness can cost everything, yet it still matters.
ramayan::7991.detailed_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana have reached the fallen Jatayu in the forest. Rama recognises the bird as the one who fought to protect Sita and now lies dead after meeting Ravana's strength. The moment deepens the grief and reveals Jatayu's sacrifice.
ramayan::7991.modern_relevance: You find the friend who stepped in for you and took the hit. The fact that they lost does not erase what they tried to do.
ramayan::7991.insight: It shifts attention from victory to sacrifice, and from loss to the value of loyal action.

ramayan::7992.verse_sanskrit: गृध्रराज्यं परित्यज्य पितृपैतामहं महत् । । 36823 । । मम हेतोरयं प्राणान्मुमोच पतगेश्वरः ।
ramayan::7992.verse_hindi: This lord of the birds left his ancestral kingdom of viltures and gave up life for my sake.
ramayan::7992.english_translation: This lord of the birds left his ancestral kingdom of vultures and gave up life for my sake.
ramayan::7992.translation_literal: गृध्रराज्यम् (the kingdom of vultures) / परित्यज्य (having abandoned) / पितृपैतामहम् (ancestral, inherited from father and grandfather) / महत् (great) / मम हेतोः (for my sake) / अयम् (this one) / प्राणान् (life-breaths) / मुमोच (released) / पतगेश्वरः (lord of birds)
ramayan::7992.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7992.essence: Loyalty becomes sacred when it costs the one who gives it.
ramayan::7992.simple_meaning: Jatayu abandoned his own royal place and gave his life for Rama's sake.
ramayan::7992.simple_insight: It reminds you that real loyalty can be costly, even to the point of sacrifice.
ramayan::7992.detailed_meaning: Rama stands over the fallen Jatayu after Sita's abduction. Seeing the bird who tried to stop Ravana, he recognizes a sacrifice that came from pure loyalty, not obligation. The moment turns grief into reverence.
ramayan::7992.modern_relevance: You watch someone step in during a crisis, knowing they may get hurt, and they still do it. Later, when the danger has passed, you realise what courage actually looked like.
ramayan::7992.insight: It shifts attention from status and possession to the willingness to protect another at personal cost.

ramayan::7993.verse_sanskrit: सर्वत्र खलु दृश्यन्ते साधवो धर्मचारिणः । । 36824 । । शूराश्शरण्यास्सौमित्रे तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि ।
ramayan::7993.verse_hindi: O Lakshmana valiant souls and protectors, being righteous and honest are found even among animals and birds.
ramayan::7993.english_translation: O Lakshmana, righteous and brave protectors are found everywhere, even among birds and other creatures.
ramayan::7993.translation_literal: सर्वत्र (everywhere) / खलु (indeed) / दृश्यन्ते (are seen) / साधवः (the righteous) / धर्मचारिणः (those who walk in dharma) / शूराः (brave ones) / शरण्याः (worthy of refuge) / सौमित्रे (O Lakshmana) / तिर्यग्योनिगतेषु (among those in animal forms) / अपि (even)
ramayan::7993.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7993.essence: Courage and righteousness can appear in the least expected form.
ramayan::7993.simple_meaning: Goodness and courage are not limited to humans. Even among animals and birds, there can be noble beings worth trusting and honoring.
ramayan::7993.simple_insight: It softens your pride and widens your respect for life.
ramayan::7993.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu dies protecting Sita, Rama speaks to Lakshmana beside the fallen bird. His grief turns into recognition: noble conduct is not confined to kings or sages. Even a bird can choose courage, loyalty, and protection.
ramayan::7993.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a crisis and assume they will look away. Instead, the quietest person in the room steps forward and helps without hesitation.
ramayan::7993.insight: It trains you to notice virtue wherever it appears, not only in the people you expect to admire.

ramayan::7994.verse_sanskrit: सीताहरणजं दुःखं न मे सौम्य तथाविधम् । । 36825 । । यथा विनाशे गृध्रस्य मत्कृते च परन्तप ।
ramayan::7994.verse_hindi: O scorcher of enemies, O handsome Lakshmana the grief I experience due to Jatayus death on my account is more intense than Sitas abduction.
ramayan::7994.english_translation: O scorcher of enemies, O handsome Lakshmana, the grief I feel at Jatayu's death on my account is greater than the sorrow of Sita's abduction.
ramayan::7994.translation_literal: सीताहरणजं (born of Sita's abduction) / दुःखं (grief) / न (not) / मे (to me) / सौम्य (gentle one) / तथाविधम् (of that kind) / यथा (as) / विनाशे (in the destruction) / गृध्रस्य (of the vulture) / मत्कृते (for my sake) / च (and) / परन्तप (scorcher of enemies)
ramayan::7994.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7994.essence: True grief is for the one who gave everything and died for you.
ramayan::7994.simple_meaning: Rama tells Lakshmana that Jatayu's death, after fighting for him, causes him even deeper pain than Sita's abduction.
ramayan::7994.simple_insight: Love notices sacrifice. The heart remembers who gave everything.
ramayan::7994.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu dies trying to stop Ravana, Rama speaks to Lakshmana in the forest. Sita is still missing, yet Rama says the bird's death for his sake cuts even deeper. The moment reveals how fully he values loyal sacrifice.
ramayan::7994.modern_relevance: You remember the friend who showed up when everything was falling apart. The help mattered, but the cost they paid for you stays with you longer.
ramayan::7994.insight: It teaches you to honour sacrifice as deeply as rescue, and to see loyalty as something sacred.

ramayan::7995.verse_sanskrit: राजा दशरथश्श्रीमान्यथा मम महायशाः । । 36826 । । पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च तथाऽयं पतगेश्वरः ।
ramayan::7995.verse_hindi: This lord of the birds for me is as worthy of reverence and honour as the famous and prosperous king Dasaratha.
ramayan::7995.english_translation: This lord of the birds for me is as worthy of reverence and honour as the famous and prosperous king Dasaratha.
ramayan::7995.translation_literal: राजा (king) / दशरथः (Dasaratha) / श्रीमान् (prosperous, illustrious) / यथा (as) / मम (for me) / महायशाः (very famous, greatly renowned) / पूजनीयः (worthy of reverence) / च (and) / मान्यः (worthy of honour) / च (and) / तथा (so) / अयम् (this) / पतगेश्वरः (lord of birds)
ramayan::7995.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7995.essence: Loyalty can make someone as worthy as a king.
ramayan::7995.simple_meaning: Sita says Jatayu deserves the same respect as King Dasharatha. She is recognizing his courage, loyalty, and sacrifice.
ramayan::7995.simple_insight: True honor is not about rank; it is about who stands with you when it costs them everything.
ramayan::7995.detailed_meaning: Sita, after hearing of Jatayu's death, speaks to Lakshmana with deep gratitude. In the forest, the fallen bird-king is no ordinary creature to her; he is a protector who gave his life trying to save her, and she places him beside Dasharatha in worth.
ramayan::7995.modern_relevance: You remember the person who stayed when leaving would have been easier. In that moment, titles matter less than the one who chose to protect you anyway.
ramayan::7995.insight: It shifts respect from social status to sacrificial loyalty.

ramayan::7996.verse_sanskrit: सौमित्रे हर काष्ठानि निर्मथिष्यामि पावकम् । । 36827 । । गृध्रराजं दिधक्षामि मत्कृते निधनं गतम् ।
ramayan::7996.verse_hindi: O Saumitri  fetch firewood. I shall generate fire by rubbing them and cremate the king of the birds who has laid down his life for my sake.
ramayan::7996.english_translation: O Saumitri, fetch firewood. I shall kindle fire by rubbing them and cremate the king of birds who has laid down his life for my sake.
ramayan::7996.translation_literal: सौमित्रे (O Saumitri) / हर (fetch) / काष्ठानि (firewood) / निर्मथिष्यामि (I shall kindle by rubbing) / पावकम् (fire) / गृध्रराजं (the king of birds) / दिधक्षामि (I wish to cremate) / मत्कृते (for my sake) / निधनं गतम् (gone to death)
ramayan::7996.speaker: Sita
ramayan::7996.essence: A true sacrifice deserves immediate honour, not only sorrow.
ramayan::7996.simple_meaning: Sita asks Lakshmana to gather wood so she can make a fire and cremate Jatayu, who died helping her.
ramayan::7996.simple_insight: Gratitude can become a final act of honour, even in grief.
ramayan::7996.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu has fallen protecting Sita, she speaks with Lakshmana in the forest. Her grief is immediate and practical: the bird who died for her deserves rites, and she will not let his sacrifice go unhonoured.
ramayan::7996.modern_relevance: You stand beside someone who showed up for you at real cost. Before anything else, you want to honour what they gave.
ramayan::7996.insight: It turns grief into responsibility and asks you to repay courage with reverence.

ramayan::7997.verse_sanskrit: नाथं पतगलोकस्य चितामारोप्य राघव । । 36828 । । इमं धक्ष्यामि सौमित्रे हतं रौद्रेण रक्षसा ।
ramayan::7997.verse_hindi: O scion of the Raghus  I will place the body of the lord of the world of birds, killed by the fierce demon, on the funeral pyre and crimate him with honour.
ramayan::7997.english_translation: O scion of the Raghus, I will place the body of the lord of the world of birds, killed by the fierce demon, on the funeral pyre and cremate him with honour.
ramayan::7997.translation_literal: नाथं (lord) / पतगलोकस्य (of the world of birds) / चिताम् (on the funeral pyre) / आरोप्य (having placed) / राघव (O scion of the Raghus) / इमम् (this) / धक्ष्यामि (I will burn) / सौमित्रे (O Saumitri) / हतम् (killed) / रौद्रेण (by the fierce) / रक्षसा (demon)
ramayan::7997.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7997.essence: Grief does not cancel gratitude; it deepens it.
ramayan::7997.simple_meaning: Rama says he will place Jatayu’s body on the pyre and cremate him with honour.
ramayan::7997.simple_insight: Even in grief, respect matters. A noble death deserves a noble farewell.
ramayan::7997.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu falls defending Sita, Rama and Lakshmana stand over the dying bird. Rama refuses to leave him as a corpse in the forest. He orders a proper cremation, treating the wounded ally as a honored protector.
ramayan::7997.modern_relevance: You lose someone who stood by you when it mattered most. Even while hurting, you still choose dignity, care, and a proper farewell.
ramayan::7997.insight: It teaches you to honour sacrifice, even when the helper can no longer be helped.

ramayan::7998.verse_sanskrit: या गतिर्यज्ञशीलानामाहिताग्नेश्च या गतिः । । 36829 । । अपरावर्तिनां या च या च भूमिप्रदायिनाम् । मया त्वं समनुज्ञातो गच्छ लोकाननुत्तमान् । । 36830 । । गृध्रराज महासत्त्व संस्कृतश्च मया व्रज ।
ramayan::7998.verse_hindi: O mighty lord of the birds  by my grace attain the state of those who perform sacrifices, who kindle and maintain sacrificial fires, who beat no retreat from the battlefield and who offer land in charity. Purified by my offering of fire, you may depart for the best of the worlds.
ramayan::7998.english_translation: O mighty lord of the birds, by my grace attain the state of those who perform sacrifices, who kindle and maintain sacrificial fires, who never retreat from battle, and who give land in charity. Purified by my offering of fire, you may go to the highest worlds.
ramayan::7998.translation_literal: या गतिः (the state) / यज्ञशीलानाम् (of those devoted to sacrifice) / आहिताग्नेः च (and of one who maintains the sacred fire) / या गतिः (the state) / अपरावर्तिनाम् (of those who do not turn back) / या च (and the state) / भूमिप्रदायिनाम् (of those who give land) / मया (by me) / त्वम् (you) / समनुज्ञातः (fully permitted) / गच्छ (go) / लोकान् (worlds) / अनुत्तमान् (highest) / गृध्रराज (O king of vultures) / महासत्त्व (great-souled one) / संस्कृतः (purified) / च (and) / मया (by me) / व्रज (depart)
ramayan::7998.speaker: Rama
ramayan::7998.essence: Courage and sacrifice can raise a fallen life to the highest worlds.
ramayan::7998.simple_meaning: Rama blesses Jatayu with the highest worlds, comparing his merit to sacrificial priests, warriors who never flee, and generous donors.
ramayan::7998.simple_insight: A noble death can be honored as a life fully lived.
ramayan::7998.detailed_meaning: Jatayu lies dying after trying to stop Ravana. Rama and Lakshmana are preparing his cremation. Before the pyre is lit, Rama speaks this blessing, honoring Jatayu’s courage as equal to the greatest acts of duty and sacrifice.
ramayan::7998.modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, after someone has fought for what was right and can fight no more, the words matter most: their courage was not wasted. Rama speaks like that here.
ramayan::7998.insight: It teaches you to recognize sacrifice as sacred, even when it ends in death.

ramayan::7999.verse_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा चितां दीप्तामारोप्य पतगेश्वरम् । । 36831 । । ददाह रामो धर्मात्मा स्वबन्धुमिव दुःखितः ।
ramayan::7999.verse_hindi: Thus said, righteous Rama laid him on the pyre and sadly cremated the lord of the birds as one would do to his own relative.
ramayan::7999.english_translation: Thus said, righteous Rama laid him on the blazing pyre and sadly cremated the lord of the birds as one would do to his own relative.
ramayan::7999.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / चिताम् (on the pyre) / दीप्ताम् (blazing) / आरोप्य (having placed) / पतगेश्वरम् (the lord of birds) / ददाह (burned) / रामः (Rama) / धर्मात्मा (righteous in nature) / स्वबन्धुम् इव (like his own relative) / दुःखितः (grieving)
ramayan::7999.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::7999.essence: Grief becomes sacred when you honour the one you lost.
ramayan::7999.simple_meaning: Rama places Jatayu on the blazing pyre and performs his cremation with the grief and care due to family.
ramayan::7999.simple_insight: Love is shown most clearly in the rituals you perform for the one you have lost.
ramayan::7999.detailed_meaning: After Jatayu dies protecting Sita, Rama carries out the final rites himself. The prince who has lost both safety and certainty treats the fallen bird not as an animal, but as a beloved kinsman. The verse closes that act of honour.
ramayan::7999.modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed after the machines go quiet, and your hands still know what care looks like. Grief does not erase dignity; it sharpens it.
ramayan::7999.insight: It teaches you to meet loss with honour, not numbness.

ramayan::8000.verse_sanskrit: रामोऽथ सहसौमित्रिर्वनं गत्वा स वीर्यवान् । । 36832 । । स्थूलान्हत्वा महारोहीननुतस्तार तं द्विजम् ।
ramayan::8000.verse_hindi: Then the mighty Rama, accompanied by Saumitri, got into the forest and killed a huge
ramayan::8000.english_translation: Then the mighty Rama, accompanied by Saumitri, went into the forest and killed a huge deer.
ramayan::8000.translation_literal: रामः (Rama) / अथ (then) / सहसौमित्रिः (together with Saumitri) / वनं (into the forest) / गत्वा (having gone) / सः वीर्यवान् (that mighty one) / स्थूलान् (huge) / हत्वा (having killed) / महारोहीन् (great deer) / अनुतस्तार (cut up / prepared) / तम् द्विजम् (that bird)
ramayan::8000.speaker: Valmiki
ramayan::8000.essence: Love for the dead becomes labor for the living.
ramayan::8000.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana go into the forest, kill a large deer, and prepare its meat for Jatayu's funeral rites.
ramayan::8000.simple_insight: Even grief has to be met with action.
ramayan::8000.detailed_meaning: After cremating Jatayu, Rama and Lakshmana go into the forest to gather what is needed for the funeral offering. The verse is a practical step in the rites, not a separate teaching.
ramayan::8000.modern_relevance: After a funeral, someone still has to gather flowers, arrange food, and do the hard practical tasks. Grief does not pause the world; love shows up in what gets done next.
ramayan::8000.insight: It shows how mourning becomes service through concrete action.

shakti_gita::1.verse_sanskrit:
गुरुदेव ! त्वया मोक्तं पुराणान्यखिलानि यत् ।
विद्यन्ते स्मृतयो नूनं श्रुतितत्त्वप्रकाशिकाः ॥
shakti_gita::1.verse_hindi: हे गुरुदेव ! आपने कहा था कि पुराण सभी वेदों के तात्पर्यप्रकाशक स्मृतियाँ हैं
shakti_gita::1.english_translation: O Guru, you said that the Puranas are all the remembered texts that illuminate the true meaning of the Vedas.
shakti_gita::1.translation_literal: गुरुदेव (O Guru) / त्वया (by you) / मोक्तं (said) / पुराणानि (Puranas) / अखिलानि (all) / यत् (that) / विद्यन्ते (exist) / स्मृतयः (remembered texts) / नूनं (indeed) / श्रुतितत्त्वप्रकाशिकाः (illuminating the essence of the Vedas)
shakti_gita::1.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::1.essence: The Puranas reveal the deeper meaning behind the Vedas as remembered teachings.
shakti_gita::1.simple_meaning: The Puranas are described as texts that explain the true meaning found in the Vedas.
shakti_gita::1.simple_insight: Texts considered ancient often hold deeper explanations of foundational teachings.
shakti_gita::1.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the Guru, recalling that the Puranas are considered the remembered texts that clarify the essential teachings of the Vedas, highlighting their importance beyond just ancient stories.
shakti_gita::1.insight: Recognize that some teachings serve as bridges to deeper understanding rather than standalone knowledge.

shakti_gita::2.verse_sanskrit:
नैकोपनिषदश्चापि पुराणनिचये ननु।
गीतानाम्ना च विख्यातास्सन्ति तत्राऽपि भूरिशः ॥
shakti_gita::2.verse_hindi: और पुराणों में गीता नाम से विख्यात अनेक उपनिषद् भरे हुए हैं
shakti_gita::2.english_translation: Many Upanishads, famous by the name Gita, are also found in the Puranas.
shakti_gita::2.translation_literal: नैका (many) उपनिषद् (Upanishads) च (also) अपि (indeed) पुराणानि (Puranas) ननु (surely) गीता (Gita) नाम्ना (by name) च (also) विख्याताः (famous) सन्ति (are) तत्र (there) अपि (also) भूरिशः (many)
shakti_gita::2.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::2.essence: Many scriptures contain Gita-named Upanishads within the Puranas.
shakti_gita::2.simple_meaning: Many Upanishads named Gita are found within the Puranas as well.
shakti_gita::2.simple_insight: Knowledge is vast and appears in many forms across scriptures.
shakti_gita::2.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that within the vast Puranic texts, many Upanishads known as Gitas are present, showing the richness of spiritual literature beyond just one famous Gita.
shakti_gita::2.modern_relevance: You realize that wisdom is spread across many sources, not just one book or teacher.
shakti_gita::2.insight: It encourages openness to diverse expressions of spiritual knowledge beyond a single text.

shakti_gita::3.verse_sanskrit:
आदिष्टञ्चाऽपि मे देव ! विबुधानां च सन्निधौ ।
प्रादुरासीन्महादेवी स्वयं ब्रह्ममयी पुरा ॥
shakti_gita::3.verse_hindi: हे देव ! आपने यह भी आज्ञा की थी कि पुरा काल में ब्रह्ममयी महादेवी देवताओं के सन्मुख प्रकट हुई थीं
shakti_gita::3.english_translation: O Devi! You also commanded that in ancient times, the great goddess, embodying the supreme reality, appeared before the enlightened beings.
shakti_gita::3.translation_literal: आदिष्टञ्चाऽपि (also commanded) मे (by me) देव (O Devi) ! विबुधानां (of the enlightened beings) च (and) सन्निधौ (in presence) । प्रादुरासीन्महादेवी (appeared the great goddess) स्वयं (herself) ब्रह्ममयी (embodying supreme reality) पुरा (in ancient times) ॥
shakti_gita::3.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::3.essence: The great goddess once appeared before enlightened beings as the supreme reality.
shakti_gita::3.simple_meaning: The great goddess, who is the supreme reality, appeared long ago before enlightened beings as you had commanded.
shakti_gita::3.simple_insight: Sometimes divine presence reveals itself clearly to those ready to receive it.
shakti_gita::3.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates that the goddess, embodying supreme reality, manifested before divine beings in ancient times as previously instructed by Devi. This sets the stage for understanding her cosmic role.
shakti_gita::3.insight: It highlights the sacred moment when deeper truths reveal themselves to prepared awareness.

shakti_gita::4.verse_sanskrit:
रहस्यं शक्तिरूपस्य शक्तिमब्रह्मणो बहु ।
श्रावयित्वा महादेवी देवान साध्वकृतार्थयत् ॥
shakti_gita::4.verse_hindi: और उन्होंने शक्तिमान् ब्रह्म के शक्तिमय स्वरुप के अनेक रहस्य उनको भलीभाँति सुनाकर कृतकृत्य किया था
shakti_gita::4.english_translation: The great Goddess revealed many secrets of the powerful form of the supreme being, satisfying the gods and the sages.
shakti_gita::4.translation_literal: रहस्यं (secret) शक्तिरूपस्य (of the form of power) शक्तिम्-अब्राह्मणो (of the powerful supreme being) बहु (many) । / श्रावयित्वा (having revealed) महादेवी (the great Goddess) देवान (to the gods) साध्वकृतार्थयत् (made the sages satisfied) ॥
shakti_gita::4.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::4.essence: Revealing many secrets of the supreme being fulfilled the gods and sages.
shakti_gita::4.simple_meaning: The great Goddess shared many mysterious teachings about the powerful form of the supreme being, pleasing the gods and sages.
shakti_gita::4.simple_insight: Sharing deep truths can bring fulfillment and connection among seekers.
shakti_gita::4.detailed_meaning: In the Shakti Gita, the narrator recounts how the great Goddess revealed many hidden aspects of her powerful divine nature to gods and sages, who became fully content and grateful upon hearing these profound teachings.
shakti_gita::4.insight: It shows the importance of revealing deep wisdom to those ready to receive it, fostering understanding and gratitude.

shakti_gita::5.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिलोकपावनी दिव्यां शक्तिगीतां सुदुर्लभाम् ।
अतो मां श्रावयेदानी ज्ञानानन्ददयानिधे ! ॥
shakti_gita::5.verse_hindi: अत: कृपा करके हे ज्ञान आनन्द और दया के निधि गुरुदेव ! त्रिलोक पवित्र कर, सुदिव्य और दुर्लभ शक्तिगीता मुझे सुनाइये
shakti_gita::5.english_translation: Therefore, O revered Guru, the treasure of knowledge, bliss, and compassion, please graciously recite to me the divine, rare Shakti Gita that purifies the three worlds.
shakti_gita::5.translation_literal: अतः (therefore) कृपा (grace) करके (doing) हे (O) ज्ञान (knowledge) आनन्द (bliss) और (and) दयानिधे (treasure of compassion) गुरुदेव (revered teacher)! त्रिलोक (three worlds) पावनी (purifying) दिव्यां (divine) शक्तिगीतां (Shakti Gita) सुदुर्लभाम् (rare). अतो (therefore) मां (to me) श्रावयेत (may recite) दानी (now)!
shakti_gita::5.speaker: Unknown
shakti_gita::5.essence: Rare, divine teachings that uplift all worlds are sought from a compassionate teacher.
shakti_gita::5.simple_meaning: A humble request is made to the revered teacher to recite the rare and divine Shakti Gita that purifies all worlds.
shakti_gita::5.simple_insight: There is reverence for rare wisdom that uplifts and purifies beyond ordinary experience.
shakti_gita::5.detailed_meaning: The speaker appeals respectfully to a revered teacher, asking for the recital of the Shakti Gita, a sacred and rare scripture known to purify the three worlds and embody knowledge, bliss, and compassion.
shakti_gita::5.insight: It shows the importance of seeking guidance from a trusted source to access profound and transformative wisdom.

shakti_gita::6.verse_sanskrit:
त्वद्भक्सा सूत ! सद्बुद्धे ! प्रसन्नोऽस्मि न संशयः ।
विशेषतश्च ते मसा विश्वकल्याणसक्तया ॥
shakti_gita::6.verse_hindi: हे सुबुद्धि सूत ! मैं तुम्हारी भक्ति से और विशेषतः तुम्हारी जगत्कल्याण में लगी हुई बुद्धि से अत्यंत प्रसन्न हूँ
shakti_gita::6.english_translation: O wise Suta! I am pleased by your devotion and especially by your wisdom devoted to the welfare of the world.
shakti_gita::6.translation_literal: त्वद्भक्सा (your devotion) / सूत (O Suta) / सद्बुद्धे (wise) / प्रसन्नोऽस्मि (I am pleased) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / विशेषतश्च (especially) / ते (your) / मसा (by) / विश्वकल्याणसक्तया (devoted to world welfare)
shakti_gita::6.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::6.essence: Devotion combined with wisdom focused on universal welfare brings divine delight.
shakti_gita::6.simple_meaning: The goddess expresses her happiness at Suta's devotion and his keen wisdom focused on helping the world.
shakti_gita::6.simple_insight: Your sincere care and clear wisdom naturally draw the divine's pleasure.
shakti_gita::6.detailed_meaning: Devi addresses Suta, acknowledging his dedication and deep understanding directed towards the welfare of all beings, showing divine approval of his mindset and devotion.
shakti_gita::6.insight: Recognizing the divine's pleasure encourages aligning devotion with wisdom aimed at collective good.

shakti_gita::7.verse_sanskrit:
अतः सूत ! समीहेऽहं तुभ्यं श्रावयितुं शनैः ।
पुराणशास्त्रं परमं वेदार्थप्रतिपादकम् ॥
shakti_gita::7.verse_hindi: इसलिये शनैः शनैः वेदार्थ प्रतिपादक पुराण शास्त्र तुम्हें सुनाने की मैं इच्छा रखता हूँ
shakti_gita::7.english_translation: Therefore, Suta said: I wish to slowly recount to you the supreme Purana that explains the meaning of the Vedas.
shakti_gita::7.translation_literal: अतः (therefore) सूत (Suta) ! समीहेऽहं (to you) तुभ्यं (slowly) श्रावयितुं (to recount) शनैः (slowly) । पुराणशास्त्रं (Purana scripture) परमं (supreme) वेदार्थप्रतिपादकम् (Veda-meaning-expounding)
shakti_gita::7.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::7.essence: Deep wisdom requires patient, gradual sharing to be truly understood.
shakti_gita::7.simple_meaning: Suta expresses his wish to slowly narrate the supreme Purana that reveals the meaning of the Vedas.
shakti_gita::7.simple_insight: Sometimes slow, patient sharing is needed to convey deep knowledge clearly.
shakti_gita::7.detailed_meaning: Suta prepares to begin narrating the Shakti Gita, emphasizing the importance of slowly revealing the highest Purana that clarifies Vedic wisdom.
shakti_gita::7.insight: It reminds you that deep wisdom unfolds best with patience and gradual explanation.

shakti_gita::8.verse_sanskrit:
यतस्त्वमेव तच्छास्त्रं नृणामभ्युदयाय वै ।
निःश्रेयसकृते चैव लोके ख्यापयितुं प्रभुः ॥
shakti_gita::8.verse_hindi: क्योंकि तुम उन शास्त्रों को मनुष्यों के अभ्युदय और निःश्रेयस के लिये जगत में प्रकट करने में समर्थ हो
shakti_gita::8.english_translation: Because you alone are capable of manifesting the scriptures among humans for their welfare and ultimate freedom.
shakti_gita::8.translation_literal: यतः (because) त्वम् (you) एव (alone) तत् (that) शास्त्रम् (scripture) नृणाम् (of humans) अभ्युदयाय (for welfare) वै (indeed) । निःश्रेयसकृते (for ultimate freedom) चैव (also) लोके (in the world) ख्यापयितुम् (to manifest) प्रभुः (the lord)
shakti_gita::8.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::8.essence: Only you can manifest teachings that bring true welfare and ultimate freedom to humanity.
shakti_gita::8.simple_meaning: You alone have the power to bring the teachings to people that lead to their well-being and highest freedom.
shakti_gita::8.simple_insight: There is strength and uniqueness in your ability to guide others toward lasting good and freedom.
shakti_gita::8.detailed_meaning: The narrator recognizes the Goddess as uniquely able to manifest sacred teachings that uplift humanity, guiding them to well-being and ultimate freedom beyond suffering.
shakti_gita::8.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed wondering who can truly help others thrive; this reminds you that your unique insight can illuminate lasting good for those around you.
shakti_gita::8.insight: It teaches you to appreciate your unique role in sharing wisdom that serves others' highest welfare and freedom.

shakti_gita::9.verse_sanskrit:
श्रावये शक्तिगीतां नामिदानीं श्रूयतां खलु ।
महादेवीपदाम्भोजचञ्चरीकदा त्वया ॥
shakti_gita::9.verse_hindi: इस समय शक्तिगीता मैं तुम्हें सुनाता हूँ सुनो, क्योंकि तुम्हारा चित्तरूपी भ्रमर महादेवी के पदरूपी कमल में सदा लीन रहता है
shakti_gita::9.english_translation: Now I tell you the Shakti Gita; listen well, for your mind-like bumblebee always dwells in the lotus feet of the great goddess.
shakti_gita::9.translation_literal: श्रावये (I tell) / शक्तिगीतां (Shakti Gita) / नामिदानीं (now) / श्रूयतां (listen) / खलु (indeed) / महादेवीपदाम्भोजचञ्चरीकदा (your mind-like bumblebee in the lotus feet of the great goddess) / त्वया (by you)
shakti_gita::9.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::9.essence: The mind naturally dwells in devotion to the divine, inviting attentive listening now.
shakti_gita::9.simple_meaning: The speaker announces telling the Shakti Gita and asks to listen, describing the listener's mind as always absorbed in the goddess's lotus feet.
shakti_gita::9.simple_insight: Your mind naturally longs to be absorbed in the divine presence, inviting your attention now.
shakti_gita::9.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the beginning of the Shakti Gita, announcing the teaching to come. He describes the listener's mind as a bumblebee always resting in Devi's lotus feet, symbolizing constant devotion and focus, setting the stage for the teachings.
shakti_gita::9.insight: Recognize how your mind often clings to what holds your deepest attention, inviting deliberate focus.

shakti_gita::10.verse_sanskrit:
गीतेयं सारभूताऽस्ति सर्वोपनिषदां हिता।
निष्कर्षः सर्ववेदानां जननी ज्ञानवर्चसाम् ॥
shakti_gita::10.verse_hindi: यह सब उपनिषदों की साररूपा, वेदों का निष्कर्ष और ज्ञानज्योति की जननी है
shakti_gita::10.english_translation: This is the essence of all the Upanishads, the conclusion of all the Vedas, and the source of the light of knowledge.
shakti_gita::10.translation_literal: गीतेयं (this song) सारभूताऽस्ति (is the essence) सर्वोपनिषदां (of all Upanishads) हिता (beneficial). निष्कर्षः (the conclusion) सर्ववेदानां (of all Vedas) जननी (mother/source) ज्ञानवर्चसाम् (of the light of knowledge).
shakti_gita::10.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::10.essence: The deepest wisdom and clarity of all sacred texts comes together here as one source.
shakti_gita::10.simple_meaning: This teaching contains the core truth of all ancient sacred texts and is the source of clear understanding.
shakti_gita::10.simple_insight: You carry within you the foundation of all true knowledge and insight.
shakti_gita::10.detailed_meaning: Devi declares that the wisdom revealed here captures the core message of the Upanishads and Vedas, serving as the origin of illuminating knowledge for seekers.
shakti_gita::10.modern_relevance: When you study a complex subject, you look for the key insight that unlocks everything else—this teaching is that key.
shakti_gita::10.insight: Recognize that profound knowledge can be distilled into a clear, guiding essence that lights your path.

shakti_gita::11.verse_sanskrit:
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे साक्षाब्रह्मस्वरूपिणीम्।
जगदम्वां महादेवीं समाराध्य दिवौकसः ॥
shakti_gita::11.verse_hindi: पुरातन काल में देवताओ ने देवासुर संग्राम में जब साक्षात् ब्रह्म स्वरुपिणी जगन्मात रूपधारिणी महादेवी की
shakti_gita::11.english_translation: In ancient times, during the war between devas and asuras, the divine beings worshipped the great goddess, the mother of the world, who is the very form of Brahman.
shakti_gita::11.translation_literal: पुरा (ancient) देवासुरे (devas and asuras) युद्धे (in the battle) साक्षात् (directly) ब्रह्मस्वरूपिणीम् (who is Brahman herself) जगदम्वां (mother of the world) महादेवीं (the great goddess) समाराध्य (worshipped) दिवौकसः (the divine beings)
shakti_gita::11.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::11.essence: The great goddess embodies supreme reality and is honored by all in cosmic struggle.
shakti_gita::11.simple_meaning: Long ago, the divine beings worshipped the great goddess who is the mother of the world and the very form of the supreme reality during a battle with the shadow forces.
shakti_gita::11.simple_insight: The great goddess is the source and support of all beings, honored even in cosmic conflict.
shakti_gita::11.detailed_meaning: In a legendary ancient battle between radiant beings (devas) and shadowy forces (asuras), the goddess who embodies the supreme reality and motherhood of the universe was honored by all divine beings, showing her central role in cosmic order.
shakti_gita::11.insight: Recognize the source of strength and support beyond conflict and division in your own life.

shakti_gita::12.verse_sanskrit:
विविधैविधिभिः सूत ! विजयं लमिरे यदा ।
अम्बायज्ञमनुष्ठाय ततस्ते विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
shakti_gita::12.verse_hindi: अनेक प्रकार से उपासना करके जय प्राप्त किया था और इस जयलाभ के पश्च्यात विधिपूर्वक अम्बायज्ञ का अनुष्ठान कर
shakti_gita::12.english_translation: O Suta, after gaining victory through many diverse methods, the sacred ritual dedicated to the Mother was then performed according to proper procedures.
shakti_gita::12.translation_literal: विविधैविधिभिः (by many diverse) सूत (O Suta) ! विजयं (victory) लमिरे (obtained) यदा (when) । अम्बायज्ञमनुष्ठाय (performing the Mother-sacrifice) ततस्ते (then) विधिपूर्वकम् (according to proper procedure) ॥
shakti_gita::12.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::12.essence: Victory gained by many means leads to proper ritual honoring the Mother.
shakti_gita::12.simple_meaning: Victory was achieved through many varied methods, and afterward a sacred ritual honoring the Mother was performed properly.
shakti_gita::12.simple_insight: Success often follows diverse efforts and is honored with respectful ritual.
shakti_gita::12.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates that after obtaining victory through various means, the proper ritual to honor the divine Mother was conducted as prescribed, marking a ceremonial act of gratitude or consecration.
shakti_gita::12.insight: Recognize that success often results from multiple efforts and deserves respectful acknowledgment.

shakti_gita::13.verse_sanskrit:
दिक्षाचक्रिरे देवीं विधूतकल्मपास्तदा।
तस्मिन् काले तु देवनारदस्योपदेशतः ॥
shakti_gita::13.verse_hindi: विधूतफल्मष होकर महादेवी के दर्शन लाभ करने की उन्होंने इच्छा की थी, उस समय देवर्षि नारद के उपदेश द्वारा उनको
shakti_gita::13.english_translation: Having removed all faults, they desired to see the Great Goddess then, prompted by sage Narada's teaching.
shakti_gita::13.translation_literal: दिक्षा (initiation) / चक्रिरे (removed) / देवीं (Goddess) / विधूत (removed) / कल्मपास्तदा (faults then) / तस्मिन् (at that) / काले (time) / तु (indeed) / देवनारदस्य (sage Narada's) / उपदेशतः (teaching)
shakti_gita::13.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::13.essence: Purification and sage's advice prepare one to meet the Great Goddess.
shakti_gita::13.simple_meaning: They purified themselves and wished to see the Great Goddess, guided by sage Narada's advice.
shakti_gita::13.simple_insight: Preparation and guidance clear the way to experience the divine.
shakti_gita::13.detailed_meaning: At this moment in the Shakti Gita, those seeking the goddess have purified themselves of faults, inspired by Narada's teaching, setting the stage to meet the Great Goddess.
shakti_gita::13.insight: It shows that preparation and wise guidance are needed before a true spiritual experience.

shakti_gita::14.verse_sanskrit:
विविदुर्विबुधाः सर्वे यन्मणिद्वीपमुनमम।
तैयद्यप्यम्बिकालोकं समासाद्य महेश्वरी ॥
shakti_gita::14.verse_hindi: यह विदित हुआ था कि यद्यपि देवी लोकरूपी मणिद्वीप में जाकर जगन्माता का
shakti_gita::14.english_translation: It is known that even the wise attain the divine light of Ambika upon reaching the jeweled island of the sage.
shakti_gita::14.translation_literal: विविदुर्विबुधाः (wise and learned) / सर्वे (all) / यन्मणिद्वीपमुनमम (upon that jeweled island of the sage) / तैयद्यप्यम्बिकालोकं (still attained Ambika's light) / समासाद्य (having reached) / महेश्वरी (the great queen)
shakti_gita::14.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::14.essence: Even the wisest are illuminated by the Goddess's divine light upon approach.
shakti_gita::14.simple_meaning: Even the most learned reached the divine light of the Goddess upon arriving at the sacred jeweled island.
shakti_gita::14.simple_insight: Approaching the divine opens a light beyond ordinary understanding, even for the wise.
shakti_gita::14.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how all the enlightened beings, despite their wisdom, experienced the profound light of Ambika when they reached the sacred jeweled island, highlighting her supreme presence.
shakti_gita::14.insight: It shows that spiritual experience surpasses intellectual knowledge and can illuminate anyone who approaches with openness.

shakti_gita::15.verse_sanskrit:
द्रष्टुं शक्या तथाऽप्येते सर्वे गन्तुं न शक्नुयुः।
तत्र देवाः कियन्तस्तु किंयन्मात्रर्पयस्तथा ॥
shakti_gita::15.verse_hindi: दर्शन प्राप्त हो सकता है परन्तु वहां सब देवता पहुंच नहीं सकते, केवल कुछ देवता और कुछ ऋषिगण ही
shakti_gita::15.english_translation: All can see there, but not all can reach; only some deities and sages can go there.
shakti_gita::15.translation_literal: द्रष्टुं (to see) शक्या (possible) तथाऽपि (even so) एते (these) सर्वे (all) गन्तुं (to go) न (not) शक्नुयुः (able). तत्र (there) देवाः (deities) कियन्तः (some) तु (but) किंयन् (few) मात्र (only) अर्पयः (offering) तथा (thus).
shakti_gita::15.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::15.essence: Many can witness the sacred, but only few can truly enter it.
shakti_gita::15.simple_meaning: Many can see that place, but only a few divine beings and sages can actually reach it.
shakti_gita::15.simple_insight: Some truths or realms are visible but not accessible to everyone.
shakti_gita::15.detailed_meaning: The Goddess explains that while the sacred realm can be perceived by many, only a select group of divine beings and sages can truly enter or dwell there, highlighting its rarity and sanctity.
shakti_gita::15.insight: Recognize that not all visible opportunities or truths are accessible to everyone; some require special readiness or purity.

shakti_gita::16.verse_sanskrit:
क्षमन्ते गन्तुमेवाऽहो सूत ! तत्राऽप्यपेक्ष्यते ।
महादेव्या दयादृष्टिस्तां विना नैतुमीशते ॥
shakti_gita::16.verse_hindi: पहुँचने का सामर्थ्य रखते हैं, तो भी महादेवी की कृपा सापेक्ष है
shakti_gita::16.english_translation: Even if one has the ability to reach, without the compassionate gaze of the Great Goddess, it is not possible to attain her.
shakti_gita::16.translation_literal: क्षमन्ते (are able) गन्तुम् (to go) एव (indeed) अहो (alas) सूत (O Suta) ! तत्राऽपि (even there) अपेक्ष्यते (is awaited) । महादेव्या (by the Great Goddess) दया (compassion) दृष्टि (gaze) तां (her) विना (without) नैतुम् (to reach) ईशते (is possible) ॥
shakti_gita::16.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::16.essence: Compassion from the divine is essential to truly reach the highest goal, beyond mere ability.
shakti_gita::16.simple_meaning: No matter how capable you are, reaching the divine presence requires her compassionate grace.
shakti_gita::16.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that your efforts alone are not the whole story.
shakti_gita::16.detailed_meaning: Suta speaks here, explaining that even if someone is capable of reaching the Great Goddess, without her compassionate attention, that attainment is impossible. This highlights devotion’s essential role alongside effort.
shakti_gita::16.modern_relevance: You might have all the skills for a goal, but without support or kindness from others, success remains out of reach.
shakti_gita::16.insight: It teaches to open the heart to receive compassion as a vital part of progress, not just rely on personal effort.

shakti_gita::17.verse_sanskrit:
एवं सुविदिते तात ! भगवान देवनायकः ।
विष्णुरूचे तदानीन्तु देवान् सम्बोध्य तानिदम् ॥
shakti_gita::17.verse_hindi: ऐसा विदित होने पर देवनायक भगवान् विष्णु ने सब देवताओ को समझाकर कहा
shakti_gita::17.english_translation: Having thus understood, the divine leader Vishnu then addressed all the deities to explain this matter.
shakti_gita::17.translation_literal: एवं (thus) सुविदिते (understood) तात (O son)! भगवान (divine being) देवनायकः (leader of gods) । विष्णुरूचे (Vishnu then) तदानीन्तु (at that time) देवान् (to the deities) सम्बोध्य (explaining) तानिदम् (this) ॥
shakti_gita::17.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::17.essence: Clear understanding prompts sharing knowledge with others.
shakti_gita::17.simple_meaning: After understanding the situation clearly, Vishnu, the leader of the divine beings, spoke to explain it to the other deities.
shakti_gita::17.simple_insight: Clarity leads to the need to share and guide others with understanding.
shakti_gita::17.detailed_meaning: In the narrative flow of the Shakti Gita, Vishnu comprehends the teachings or situation and proceeds to explain it to the gathered deities, marking a pivotal moment of communication.
shakti_gita::17.insight: Recognize when understanding calls for sharing and guiding others with clarity.

shakti_gita::18.verse_sanskrit:
प्रभवो न यदा गन्तुं निखिलास्तत्र निर्जराः!
शक्नुवन्त्यपि ये गन्तुं देवीलोकं हि तेऽपि च ॥
shakti_gita::18.verse_hindi: जब सब देवतागण देवी लोक में नहीं पहुंच सके और जिनकी वहां पहुंचने की सामर्थ्य भी है वे भी
shakti_gita::18.english_translation: When all radiant beings cannot reach the realm of the Goddess, even those capable of reaching it cannot go there.
shakti_gita::18.translation_literal: प्रभवो (radiant beings) / न (not) / यदा (when) / गन्तुं (to go) / निखिलास्तत्र (all there) / निर्जराः (cannot reach) / शक्नुवन्ति (are capable) / अपि (even) / ये (those who) / गन्तुं (to go) / देवीलोकं (Goddess realm) / हि (indeed) / तेऽपि (they also) / च (and)
shakti_gita::18.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::18.essence: Some realms of the divine remain unreachable even to those capable of reaching them.
shakti_gita::18.simple_meaning: Sometimes, the realm of the divine is unreachable even for those who seem capable of entering it.
shakti_gita::18.simple_insight: There’s a limit to what ability alone can achieve in reaching higher states.
shakti_gita::18.detailed_meaning: Devi teaches that even the most radiant beings, who normally could access divine realms, sometimes cannot enter her realm. This shows that spiritual attainment is not guaranteed by power or capacity alone but depends on deeper factors.
shakti_gita::18.modern_relevance: You might face situations where your skills or efforts can’t open certain doors, reminding you that some things are beyond control.
shakti_gita::18.insight: It shifts perspective from relying solely on ability toward recognizing unseen barriers in spiritual or personal growth.

shakti_gita::19.verse_sanskrit:
क्षमन्ते स्वेच्छया नैतुं जगदम्वादयामृते ।
यदा तु जगदम्बायाः सर्वथाऽपेक्षिता कृपा ॥
shakti_gita::19.verse_hindi: अपनी इच्छा से नहीं पहुंच सकते, अत: जब जगन्माता की कृपा ही सब प्रकार से अपेक्षित है
shakti_gita::19.english_translation: You cannot reach by your own will; thus, the universal mother’s grace is always needed in every way.
shakti_gita::19.translation_literal: क्षमन्ते (can reach) स्वेच्छया (by own will) नैतुं (not) जगदम्वादयामृते (to the universal mother) यदा (when) तु (but) जगदम्बायाः (of universal mother) सर्वथा (in every way) अपेक्षिता (needed) कृपा (grace)
shakti_gita::19.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::19.essence: Your own will can’t reach the sacred; only grace guides fully.
shakti_gita::19.simple_meaning: You cannot reach the divine merely by trying on your own; you always need the universal mother’s grace in every way.
shakti_gita::19.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing divine grace supports you beyond your own efforts.
shakti_gita::19.detailed_meaning: Devi explains that human will alone cannot attain the highest spiritual state; the universal mother's grace is essential and must be sought in every aspect of life.
shakti_gita::19.modern_relevance: You’ve pushed hard but feel stuck—this reminds you that some support beyond effort is essential to move forward.
shakti_gita::19.insight: It shifts your mindset from relying solely on self-will to opening to grace as a necessary companion.

shakti_gita::20.verse_hindi: तो आओ हम सब मिलकर हितकारी और सर्वोत्तम ब्रह्मचक्र का अनुष्ठान करें
shakti_gita::20.english_translation: Come, let us all together perform the beneficial and supreme Brahma-cycle ritual.
shakti_gita::20.translation_literal: सर्वै (all) रागम्यतां (without attachment) तहिं (there) ब्रह्मचक्रम् (Brahma-cycle) अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed) अस्माभि (by us) मिलित (joined) देवैः (with gods) इह (here) अनुष्ठीयतां (let it be performed) हितम् (beneficial)
shakti_gita::20.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::20.essence: The highest beneficial ritual is performed together with unity and devotion.
shakti_gita::20.simple_meaning: Everyone should come together to perform the highest and most beneficial Brahma-cycle ritual.
shakti_gita::20.simple_insight: Unity in sacred action brings collective benefit beyond the individual.
shakti_gita::20.detailed_meaning: Suta invites all present to unite and perform the supreme Brahma-cycle ritual, emphasizing communal participation for a beneficial spiritual purpose.
shakti_gita::20.insight: It highlights the power of collective effort in sacred or meaningful undertakings.

shakti_gita::21.verse_sanskrit:
वयञ्चेद् ब्रह्मचक्रेऽस्मिन् कृतकृत्या भवेम ह ।
अर्मुना ब्रह्मचक्रेण सर्वोत्कृष्टतमेन च ॥
shakti_gita::21.verse_hindi: यदि ब्रह्मचक्र में हम लोग सफल काम होंगे और यदि इस सर्वोत्तम चक्र द्वारा
shakti_gita::21.english_translation: If we become perfect through the supreme Brahmachakra, then indeed we attain completeness.
shakti_gita::21.translation_literal: यदि (if) / ब्रह्मचक्र (supreme wheel of Brahman) / में (in) / हम (we) / लोग (people) / सफल (successful) / काम (work) / होंगे (be) / और (and) / यदि (if) / इस (this) / सर्वोत्तम (supreme) / चक्र (wheel) / द्वारा (by)
shakti_gita::21.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::21.essence: Perfection through the supreme spiritual cycle leads to complete fulfillment.
shakti_gita::21.simple_meaning: Becoming perfect through the highest spiritual practice leads to full completeness.
shakti_gita::21.simple_insight: There is hope in following the highest path to become complete and fulfilled.
shakti_gita::21.detailed_meaning: The Goddess speaks of achieving perfection through the supreme spiritual cycle, implying that dedication to this path results in ultimate completeness.
shakti_gita::21.insight: It encourages committing fully to the highest spiritual discipline to realize your true purpose.

shakti_gita::22.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वेऽभिन्नान्तरात्मानः स्वीयाभिः कम्पशक्तिभिः ।
स्वज्ञानेन स्वभक्त्या च जगन्मातुः पदाम्बुजे ॥
shakti_gita::22.verse_hindi: हम लोग सब एक अन्तःकरण होकर अपनी क्रियाशक्ति, भक्ति और ज्ञान से जग माता के चरणों में
shakti_gita::22.english_translation: All beings are one inner self, united by their power of action, devotion, and wisdom at the feet of the world mother.
shakti_gita::22.translation_literal: सर्वेऽभिन्न (all undivided) अन्तरात्मानः (inner selves) स्वीयाभिः (by their own) कम्पशक्तिभिः (power of action) स्वज्ञानेन (by own wisdom) स्वभक्त्या (by own devotion) च (and) जगन्मातुः (of the world mother) पदाम्बुजे (at the lotus feet)
shakti_gita::22.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::22.essence: All beings share one inner self united by action, devotion, and wisdom toward the world mother.
shakti_gita::22.simple_meaning: All beings share the same inner self and are connected through their own action, devotion, and wisdom to the world mother.
shakti_gita::22.simple_insight: You belong to a shared inner unity that flows through your actions and devotion.
shakti_gita::22.detailed_meaning: The goddess teaches that every being is essentially one inner self, connected not by outward differences but through their own power of action, devotion, and wisdom, all reaching toward her presence as the world mother.
shakti_gita::22.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated, remember your inner self connects you deeply to others through your choices and care.
shakti_gita::22.insight: This verse invites you to recognize your shared inner nature with others, shifting your view from separation to connection.

shakti_gita::23.verse_sanskrit:
शक्नुयाम वयं लब्धुमेकाग्रत्वं परं यदि।
तदा मे दृढविश्वासो वर्तते-विबुधर्षभाः॥
shakti_gita::23.verse_hindi: एकाग्रता प्राप्त कर सकेंगे तो मेरा स्थिर विश्वास है कि
shakti_gita::23.english_translation: If we can attain complete focus, then my firm confidence remains, O best of the wise.
shakti_gita::23.translation_literal: शक्नुयाम (we can) / वयं (we) / लब्धुमेकाग्रत्वं (to attain focus) / परं (supreme) / यदि (if) / तदा (then) / मे (my) / दृढविश्वासो (firm confidence) / वर्तते (exists) / विवुधर्षभाः (O best of the wise)
shakti_gita::23.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::23.essence: Complete focus creates the steady confidence needed to face any challenge.
shakti_gita::23.simple_meaning: When you can focus your mind fully, a strong confidence naturally arises within you.
shakti_gita::23.simple_insight: Feeling steady comes from training your attention to settle deeply in the present.
shakti_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Devi speaks to the importance of concentrated focus as the foundation for firm inner trust. Addressing a wise listener, she asserts that gaining unwavering attention is key to developing confidence and strength in any spiritual or worldly effort.
shakti_gita::23.modern_relevance: When your thoughts scatter during work or study, remember real confidence comes from steady focus, not just wishing for success.
shakti_gita::23.insight: It teaches you to cultivate single-pointed attention as the root of enduring inner trust.

shakti_gita::24.verse_hindi: महादेवी अवश्य यहां ही स्वयं आविर्भूत होकर दर्शन और उपदेश द्वारा हम लोगों को कृतकृत्य करेंगी
shakti_gita::24.english_translation: The great Goddess herself will surely manifest here and graciously bless through her vision and teachings.
shakti_gita::24.translation_literal: यन्नूनं (surely) सा (she) महादेवी (great Goddess) स्वयमाविर्भविष्यति (will manifest herself) । स्वदर्शन (self-vision) उपदेशाभ्याम् (and teachings) अत्रैव (here itself) अनुग्रहीप्यति (graciously blesses) ॥
shakti_gita::24.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::24.essence: The divine will manifest here and bless through direct vision and teaching.
shakti_gita::24.simple_meaning: The great Goddess will appear here in person and bless us by showing herself and giving teachings.
shakti_gita::24.simple_insight: You can trust that the divine presence will come and guide you directly.
shakti_gita::24.detailed_meaning: At this moment, the narrator promises that the great Goddess will personally appear and bless those present by revealing herself and giving direct teachings. This assures the listeners of her imminent guidance and grace.
shakti_gita::24.modern_relevance: When you feel alone or uncertain, trust that a guiding presence can appear anytime to support and teach you.
shakti_gita::24.insight: It encourages opening your heart to trust that guidance and blessings can come directly, not just through distant or indirect means.

shakti_gita::25.verse_sanskrit:
एतच्छुत्वा वचो विष्णोस्तदानीं निखिलाः मुराः ।
विष्णुं चक्रेश्वर कृत्वा भगवन्त रमापतिम् ॥
shakti_gita::25.verse_hindi: इतना भगवान् विष्णु का वचन सुनकर उस समय समस्त देवतागण भगवान विष्णु को
shakti_gita::25.english_translation: Hearing these words of the supreme being Vishnu, at that moment all the radiant beings bowed to Vishnu, the lord of the discus, the divine consort of Lakshmi.
shakti_gita::25.translation_literal: एतत् (this) शुत्वा (having heard) वचः (words) विष्णोः (of Vishnu) तदानीम् (then) निखिलाः (all) मुराः (divine beings) । विष्णुं (Vishnu) चक्रेश्वर (lord of discus) कृत्वा (making) भगवन्त् (divine) रमापतिम् (consort of Lakshmi) ॥
shakti_gita::25.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::25.essence: Clear, authoritative words inspire natural respect and unity among radiant beings.
shakti_gita::25.simple_meaning: After hearing Vishnu's words, all the radiant beings respectfully acknowledged him as the lord of the discus and Lakshmi's consort.
shakti_gita::25.simple_insight: Respect and recognition naturally follow clear and powerful teaching from a true teacher.
shakti_gita::25.detailed_meaning: In this scene, after Vishnu speaks, all the divine beings recognize his authority and grace by bowing to him, showing their reverence and unity under his guidance.
shakti_gita::25.insight: It reveals the power of words to inspire respect and alignment among a community when spoken with clarity and authority.

shakti_gita::26.verse_sanskrit:
पुण्येन ब्रामचक्रेण सर्वश्रेष्ठत्वमंजुषा ।
उपास्तै महादेव्याः प्रवृत्ताः सुसमाहिताः ॥
shakti_gita::26.verse_hindi: चक्रेश्वर बनाकर ब्रह्मचक्र के द्वारा महादेवी की उपासना में सावधान होकर प्रवृत्त हुए
shakti_gita::26.english_translation: By the sacred Brahma-disc, the foremost devotees engaged in worship of the great goddess with full concentration.
shakti_gita::26.translation_literal: पुण्येन (by sacred) ब्रामचक्रेण (by Brahma-disc) सर्वश्रेष्ठत्वम् (foremost position) अंजुषा (with attention) । उपास्तै (worshippers) महादेव्याः (of the great goddess) प्रवृत्ताः (engaged) सुसमाहिताः (well-concentrated) ॥
shakti_gita::26.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::26.essence: Focused, careful worship honors the great goddess with full concentration.
shakti_gita::26.simple_meaning: The best worshippers carefully used the sacred Brahma-disc to focus deeply on worshiping the great goddess.
shakti_gita::26.simple_insight: Devotion focused with care brings deep connection to the divine.
shakti_gita::26.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the foremost devotees prepare to worship Devi using the sacred Brahma-disc, concentrating fully to honor her with care and attention.
shakti_gita::26.insight: It reminds you that focused, respectful attention deepens any sacred practice.

shakti_gita::27.verse_sanskrit:
तनो विहारिणी निसं भक्तमानसमन्दिरे।
आद्या सैव महादेवी करुणैकनिकेतनम् ॥
shakti_gita::27.verse_hindi: भक्त मनोमन्दिर विहारिणी वही करुणामयी आद्या महादेवी
shakti_gita::27.english_translation: The primal great goddess dwells in the temple of the devoted heart, filled with compassion.
shakti_gita::27.translation_literal: तनो (of the body) / विहारिणी (dwelling) / निसं (without) / भक्तमानसमन्दिरे (in the temple of the devoted mind) / आद्या (primordial) / सैव (indeed) / महादेवी (great goddess) / करुणैकनिकेतनम् (the unique abode of compassion)
shakti_gita::27.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::27.essence: The primal goddess lives within the compassionate, devoted heart.
shakti_gita::27.simple_meaning: The primal goddess resides within the heart filled with devotion and compassion.
shakti_gita::27.simple_insight: You can feel the divine presence in your own compassionate, devoted heart.
shakti_gita::27.detailed_meaning: Devi explains that she dwells inside the heart of one who is devoted and compassionate, showing her intimate connection with those who open to her with love and kindness.
shakti_gita::27.modern_relevance: When you feel compassion deeply for someone, you experience a sacred presence within yourself.
shakti_gita::27.insight: Recognize that opening your heart with devotion allows the divine presence to be experienced directly.

shakti_gita::28.verse_sanskrit:
देवग्नुष्टिते तस्मिन् ब्रह्मचक्रे सुदुर्लभे।
देवासिगोचरीभूय दिव्यं तेजस्वितमयम ॥
shakti_gita::28.verse_hindi: सब देवताओं के द्वारा अनुष्ठित ब्रह्मचक्र में  देवताओं के दर्शनेन्द्रियगोचर होकर दिव्य तेजोमय और
shakti_gita::28.english_translation: In the rare sacred circle performed by all the radiant beings, the divine brilliance becomes visible to the senses of the divine beings.
shakti_gita::28.translation_literal: देवग्नुष्टिते (performed by gods) / तस्मिन् (in that) / ब्रह्मचक्रे (sacred circle) / सुदुर्लभे (very rare) / देवासिगोचरीभूय (becoming visible to the senses of gods) / दिव्यं (divine) / तेजस्वितमयम (full of brilliance)
shakti_gita::28.speaker: Unknown
shakti_gita::28.essence: A rare sacred ritual reveals divine brilliance visible only to divine beings.
shakti_gita::28.simple_meaning: A rare sacred ritual performed by divine beings reveals a heavenly brilliance visible to divine senses.
shakti_gita::28.simple_insight: Some sacred moments shine with a light that only higher beings can perceive.
shakti_gita::28.detailed_meaning: The verse describes a rare sacred ritual called the brahmachakra performed by divine beings, where a magnificent divine light manifests, perceptible only to these exalted beings' senses.
shakti_gita::28.insight: It hints that some profound experiences require special readiness or presence to be perceived.

shakti_gita::29.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वसौन्दर्य शोभाढन्यं परमाद्भुतदर्शनम् ।
विभ्राणाऽलौकिक रूपमाविर्भाविमवाप ह ॥
shakti_gita::29.verse_hindi: सब सौन्दर्यों से शोभित अद्भुत रूप में प्रकट हुई
shakti_gita::29.english_translation: She appeared in a form adorned with all beauty, wondrous and supernatural.
shakti_gita::29.translation_literal: सर्वसौन्दर्य (all-beauty) / शोभाढन्यं (adorned) / परमाद्भुतदर्शनम् (supremely wondrous to behold) / विभ्राणाऽलौकिक (radiant, supernatural) / रूपम् (form) / आविर्भाविमवाप (appeared, manifested) / ह (indeed)
shakti_gita::29.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::29.essence: The divine manifests as a form beyond ordinary beauty and wonder.
shakti_gita::29.simple_meaning: She appeared in an extraordinary form, shining with all kinds of beauty and wonder.
shakti_gita::29.simple_insight: The appearance of the divine can inspire awe beyond ordinary experience.
shakti_gita::29.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes the Goddess manifesting herself in a dazzling, supernatural form filled with all beauty. This moment marks the revelation of her supreme and wondrous nature to the listener.
shakti_gita::29.insight: Seeing the divine form shows how appearances can express immense power and inspire devotion.

shakti_gita::30.verse_sanskrit:
दिवौकसोऽखिला अमी पुरस्तदा
व्यलोकयनंखण्डमण्डलाकृति विभिद्य त्रै तमन्ततिम् ।
अखण्डमण्डलात्मकं मुदिव्यमेकमद्भुतं यहः
किमप्यहो परं प्रकाशते स्म दुःसहम् ॥
shakti_gita::30.verse_hindi: उस समय इन सब देवताओं ने देखा कि अन्धकार को भेदन करके एक सुदिव्य, अद्भुत, दुःसह और अखण्ड मण्डलाकार ज्योति उनके सामने प्रकाशित हुई
shakti_gita::30.english_translation: At that time, all the radiant beings saw an unbroken, wondrous, unbearable light shining before them, piercing through the darkness.
shakti_gita::30.translation_literal: दिवौकसोऽखिला (all radiant beings) / अमी (these) / पुरस्तदा (at that time) / व्यलोकयन (saw) / अखण्डमण्डलाकृति (unbroken circle shape) / विभिद्य (piercing) / त्रै (the darkness) / तमन्ततिम् (unbearable) / अखण्डमण्डलात्मकं (unbroken circle-shaped) / मुदिव्यमेकम् (a wondrous light) / अद्भुतं (wondrous) / यहः (which) / किमपि (something) / अहो (oh) / परं (supreme) / प्रकाशते (shines) / स्म (indeed) / दुःसहम् (unbearable)
shakti_gita::30.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::30.essence: A single radiant light can break through the deepest darkness, revealing the supreme.
shakti_gita::30.simple_meaning: All the radiant beings witnessed a single, bright, continuous light that broke through complete darkness.
shakti_gita::30.simple_insight: Some moments reveal such powerful light that darkness feels impossible to hold.
shakti_gita::30.detailed_meaning: As the scene unfolds, all the radiant beings present witness a brilliant, unbroken light that breaks the overwhelming darkness, revealing a supreme and wondrous illumination.
shakti_gita::30.insight: It shows that even the deepest darkness can be pierced by a single, intense clarity.

shakti_gita::31.verse_sanskrit:
अनन्तकोटिसूर्यतेज ओघमोघताकरं 
विभासते स्म तन्महः समुज्ज्वलं मनोहरम् ।
महरततोऽन्तरा गलद्विधरण्यपुञ्जसन्निभा 
समाविरास्त षोडशी समस्तविश्वमोहिनी ॥
shakti_gita::31.verse_hindi: वह ज्योति अनन्त कोटि सूर्यों की तेजोराशि को भी पराभूत करने वाली, समुज्ज्वल, मनोहर और शोभायमान थी। उस ज्योति के बीच से एक गलितकाञ्चन के सदृश और जगत को मुग्धं करने वाली षोडशी स्त्रीमूर्ति प्रकट हुई
shakti_gita::31.english_translation: That radiant light outshone the brilliance of infinite millions of suns, dazzling and beautiful. From within that light appeared a molten-golden form, the enchanting sixteen-armed goddess who captivates the entire world.
shakti_gita::31.translation_literal: अनन्तकोटि (infinite millions) / सूर्यतेज (sun’s brilliance) / ओघ (wave) / मोह (flood) / ताकरं (of fire) / विभासते (shines) / स्म (indeed) / तन्महः (that great) / समुज्ज्वलं (blazing) / मनोहरम् (beautiful) / । / महरततः (from great distance) / अन्तर (within) / अगलत (molten) / विधरण्य (of gold) / पुञ्ज (mass) / सन्निभा (like) / समाविरास्त (appeared) / षोडशी (sixteen-armed goddess) / समस्त (entire) / विश्व (world) / मोहिनी (captivating)
shakti_gita::31.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::31.essence: A radiant light reveals the captivating sixteen-armed form that enchants all.
shakti_gita::31.simple_meaning: A light brighter than millions of suns appeared, revealing the sixteen-armed goddess who captivates the whole world with her golden form.
shakti_gita::31.simple_insight: Some experiences are so radiant they naturally draw your attention and wonder.
shakti_gita::31.detailed_meaning: In this scene, a magnificent light surpassing the brightness of countless suns emerges. From its core, a molten golden sixteen-armed goddess manifests, captivating the entire universe with her dazzling presence. This moment introduces the divine form and power of Devi.
shakti_gita::31.insight: It invites you to notice when something in your life shines so brightly it captures your full attention.

shakti_gita::32.verse_sanskrit:
अपूर्वमूतिरम्विकाऽवलास्वरूपधारिणी 
वभौ समस्तविश्वनव्यभास्वरप्रभाकरा।
सुदिव्यवस्नभूषणैविभूषिता चतुर्भुजैः 
सुपाशमशंक  तथाऽभयं वरंच विभ्रती ॥
shakti_gita::32.verse_hindi: जो स्त्रीरूप धारण करने वाली अपूर्व मूर्ति देवी संसार की नवीन देदीप्यमान सब शोभाओं की छवि रूप से विराज रही है, जो दिव्य वस्त्र और अलंकारों से भूषित है, जो चार हाथों में पाश, अंकुश, अभय और वर को धारण किये हुई
shakti_gita::32.english_translation: The Goddess, in the form of a unique woman, shines as the radiant image of all new glories in the world, adorned with divine garments and ornaments, holding the noose, goad, fearlessness, and boon in her four hands.
shakti_gita::32.translation_literal: अपूर्वमूतिर् (unique form) अम्विका (the Goddess) अवलास्वरूपधारिणी (wearing the form of a woman) वभौ (shines) समस्तविश्वन (all-world's) नव्यभास्वरप्रभाकरा (new radiant light) सुदिव्यवस्नभूषणै (with divine clothes and ornaments) विभूषिता (adorned) चतुर्भुजैः (with four hands) सुपाशम् (a beautiful noose) अशंक (a goad) तथा (also) अभयं (fearlessness) वरं (a boon) च (and) विभ्रती (holding)
shakti_gita::32.speaker: Suta
shakti_gita::32.essence: The Goddess appears as a radiant woman holding symbols of power, protection, and blessing.
shakti_gita::32.simple_meaning: The Goddess is described as a unique woman shining beautifully with divine clothes and ornaments, holding four symbolic items in her hands.
shakti_gita::32.simple_insight: You can see the divine as a powerful presence adorned with symbols of control, protection, and blessing.
shakti_gita::32.detailed_meaning: The narrator, Suta, describes the Goddess Devi manifesting as a radiant woman wearing divine garments and ornaments. She holds in her four hands symbols representing power and protection: a noose, a goad, fearlessness, and a boon. This depiction sets the stage for her cosmic role.
shakti_gita::32.insight: The verse invites you to recognize the divine presence through its symbolic expressions of protection and grace.

shakti_gita::33.verse_sanskrit:
असौ जगद्भवस्थितिप्रणाशकारिणीश्वरी
शिवात्मनः परात्परस्य नाभिपद्यमास्थिता।
शिवोऽपि दिव्यमञ्चमतस्यधिस्वपंस्त्रिदेवयुक्
पितृवज्रपिनिर्जरा यदीयपादरूपिणः ॥
shakti_gita::33.verse_hindi: जगत की उत्पत्ति स्थिति लय करने वाली जगदीश्वरी शिव रूप धारी परमब्रह्म के नाभि कमल पर आसीना है, शिव दिव्य मंच पर सोये हुए हैं जिस मंच के ब्रह्मा, शिव और विष्णु के सहित अनेक पितृ ऋषि और देवता स्वरुप हैं
shakti_gita::33.english_translation: The sovereign lady who causes the creation, preservation, and destruction of the world sits on the navel lotus of the supreme Shiva, the highest true self. Shiva himself rests on her divine throne, surrounded by the three gods, ancestors, sages, and radiant beings.
shakti_gita::33.translation_literal: असौ (she) जगत् (world) भव (creation) स्थिति (preservation) प्रणाशकारिणी (destroyer) ईश्वरी (sovereign lady) शिवात्मनः (of Shiva's true self) परात्परस्य (the supreme) नाभिपद्यम् (navel lotus) आसीता (seated). शिवः (Shiva) अपि (also) दिव्य (divine) मञ्चम् (throne) अचमत् (rests) अस्य (her) अधि (upon) स्वपम् (sleep/rest) त्रिदेवयुक् (with three gods) पितृवज्रपिनः (ancestors, sages, and radiant beings) जरा (shining) यदीयपादरूपिणः (in the form of feet).
shakti_gita::33.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::33.essence: The divine source of all existence rests beyond even the highest true self at the universe's center.
shakti_gita::33.simple_meaning: At the center of the universe sits the divine mother who creates, sustains, and destroys all, with the supreme consciousness resting upon her.
shakti_gita::33.simple_insight: You carry the source of all creation within you, a presence greater than the highest self.
shakti_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Devi describes herself as the fundamental power behind creation, preservation, and destruction, seated on the navel of Shiva, the supreme true self. Shiva and many divine beings rest on her throne, showing her supreme cosmic role beyond even the highest divine self.
shakti_gita::33.modern_relevance: In moments when you feel overwhelmed by life's changes, remember that your true self holds the power to create, sustain, and transform everything around you.
shakti_gita::33.insight: Recognize that your inner being is the foundational source beyond even your highest sense of self, shifting your sense of identity and power.

shakti_gita::34.verse_sanskrit:
गभीरमप्यहोऽम्बिकामुखं सुचारुदर्शनं
जगद्विमोहकारकस्वमन्दहास्यशोभितम् ।
अवाचि संसपि स्वतस्तदाननादुदेति च
जगद्विमोइसाधकः स ओंध्यनिर्निरन्तरम् ॥
shakti_gita::34.verse_hindi: देवी का मुख सुचारु दर्शन और गम्भीर होने पर भी जगन्मुग्धकर मन्द हास्य से सुशोभित है, निर्वाक होने पर भी उनके मुख से जगत् को मुग्ध करने वाली ओंकार ध्वनि स्वतः ही निकल रही है
shakti_gita::34.english_translation: The face of Devi is deeply profound yet beautifully clear, adorned with a gentle smile that enchants the world; though silent, from her mouth flows the captivating Om sound that mesmerizes all beings continuously.
shakti_gita::34.translation_literal: गभीरमपि (deep even) अहोऽम्बिका (ah, Ambika) मुखं (face) सुचारुदर्शनं (beautiful clear sight) जगद्विमोहकारक (world enchantment maker) स्वमन्दहास्यशोभितम् (with own gentle smile adorned) । अवाचि (speechless) संसपि (still) स्वतस्त (spontaneously) दाननात् (from mouth) उदेति (arises) च (and) जगद्विमोइसाधकः (world enchantment accomplisher) स (he) ओंध्य (Om sound) निरन्तरम् (continuously) ॥
shakti_gita::34.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::34.essence: Profound quietness can naturally radiate enchanting power and presence.
shakti_gita::34.simple_meaning: Devi's face is deeply profound and beautifully clear with a gentle smile that enchants the world. Though she is silent, a captivating Om sound flows naturally from her mouth, mesmerizing everyone.
shakti_gita::34.simple_insight: You can be quietly powerful and still captivate the world with your presence.
shakti_gita::34.detailed_meaning: Devi’s face shines with a profound yet clear beauty, smiling gently to enchant the entire world. Even in silence, her mouth naturally utters the sacred Om sound, a continuous vibration that mesmerizes all beings, showing her divine power beyond words.
shakti_gita::34.insight: It reveals how presence and subtle expression can influence and captivate without needing words or noise.

shakti_gita::35.verse_sanskrit:
समस्ततत्त्वतो ध्रुवं बहिर्गताऽप्यसौ शिवा
जगत्स्यदिव्यशक्तिभिश्च येविषयथाऽखिलम् ।
ददाति विश्वशङ्करं परं निरन्तरं मुहुः
प्रसादमात्मनो जगन्निवासिनीवजातये ॥
shakti_gita::35.verse_hindi: वे सर्वतत्त्वातीत होने पर भी अपनी दैवी शक्ति से जगत् में परिव्याप्त होकर संसार के कल्याण कारी उत्कृष्ट अपने प्रसाद को जगनिवासी जीवसमूह को निरन्तर बारम्बार प्रदान कर रही हैं
shakti_gita::35.english_translation: Although transcending all elements, She pervades the world with divine power, continuously granting her grace for the welfare of all beings.
shakti_gita::35.translation_literal: समस्ततत्त्वतो (beyond all elements) / ध्रुवं (unchanging) / बहिर्गतात् (going outside) / अपि (even) / असौ (she) / शिवा (auspicious) / जगत् (world) / स्य (is) / दिव्यशक्ति (divine power) / इष् (wishes) / च (and) / एव (certainly) / विषयथा (pervading) / अखिलम् (all) / ददाति (gives) / विश्वशङ्करं (the universal benefactor) / परं (supreme) / निरन्तरं (continually) / मुहुः (again and again) / प्रसादम् (grace) / आत्मनः (of the self) / जगन्निवासिनी (dwelling in the world) / इव (like) / जातये (arises)
shakti_gita::35.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::35.essence: The divine pervades all and endlessly offers grace to sustain life.
shakti_gita::35.simple_meaning: She is beyond all elements but fills the world with her divine power, continuously giving grace to support all beings.
shakti_gita::35.simple_insight: You can feel connected to a power that constantly supports and blesses life around you.
shakti_gita::35.detailed_meaning: Devi declares that although she transcends all material elements, she pervades the entire world with her divine power, repeatedly offering grace to all living beings, ensuring their welfare and protection.
shakti_gita::35.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by the world's challenges, remember there is a constant, unseen power supporting and blessing life around you.
shakti_gita::35.insight: Recognize that divine power is not distant but actively present, continuously offering support and grace in every moment.

shakti_gita::36.verse_sanskrit:
सदात्मिका चिदात्मिका रसात्मिकाऽद्याऽप्यसौ
 प्रपद्य सच्चीदात्मकं हि भावमात्मनैव तु ।
प्रपंचरूपधारिणी महेश्वरी द्वयात्मिका 
रसात्मकस्वसत्तया समस्तविश्वमाश्नुत ॥
shakti_gita::36.verse_hindi: वह अद्वैत सच्चिदानंदमयी होने पर भी सत् और चित् भाव के आश्रय से द्वैतरूप धारण करती हुई आनन्द भाव से जगत को परिव्याप्त किये हुई हैं
shakti_gita::36.english_translation: Though she is non-dual, composed of existence, consciousness, and bliss, she takes a dual form through the feelings of truth and consciousness and pervades the world with the emotion of bliss.
shakti_gita::36.translation_literal: सदात्मिका (of true existence) / चिदात्मिका (of conscious self) / रसात्मिका (of blissful essence) / अद्य (even now) / अपि (indeed) / असौ (she) / प्रपद्य (takes refuge/assumes) / सच्चीदात्मकं (of existence, consciousness, bliss) / हि (indeed) / भावम् (state/feeling) / आत्मनैव (in herself) / तु (but) / प्रपंचरूपधारिणी (assuming dual form) / महेश्वरी (great sovereign lady) / द्वयात्मिका (of dual nature) / रसात्मकस्वसत्तया (by her blissful own being) / समस्तविश्वमाश्नुत (pervades all the universe)
shakti_gita::36.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita::36.essence: The divine blends unity and duality, filling everything with blissful presence.
shakti_gita::36.simple_meaning: The divine is fundamentally one, made of pure existence, consciousness, and bliss, yet she appears as many through feelings of truth and awareness, filling the entire world with bliss.
shakti_gita::36.simple_insight: You can hold unity and diversity inside you, shining with joyful presence.
shakti_gita::36.detailed_meaning: Devi teaches that although she is the ultimate reality—unchanging and whole—she manifests simultaneously as a duality through the feelings of truth and consciousness, spreading bliss throughout the universe, showing the world’s unity and multiplicity as one.
shakti_gita::36.modern_relevance: Like feeling completely yourself while embracing all your roles and emotions, you can be whole inside yet express many sides, filling your life with joy.
shakti_gita::36.insight: It invites you to see unity beneath apparent differences, embracing complexity without losing your inner wholeness.

shakti_gita::37.verse_sanskrit:
देवीं ब्रह्ममयीं समीक्ष्य पुरतस्त्वेवंविधा निर्जरा 
निप्पन्दा अगिरोऽभवन्निव कियन्मूढा: क्षणं संस्थिताः । 
पश्चान्मोहतयोविमुक्तमतयश्चैतन्यपूर्णाशयाः. शान्ता 
देवगणाः कृताञ्जलिपुटा देवी परां तुष्टुवुः ॥
shakti_gita::37.verse_hindi: देवतागण इस रूप में ब्रह्ममयी देवी का दर्शन करके थोडी देर तक निस्पन्द और निर्वाक् हो विमोहित हो गए, तत्पश्चात् मोहमुक्त होकर पूर्ण चेतनता को प्राप्त होते हुए कृताञ्जलि हो स्तुति करने लगे
shakti_gita::37.english_translation: The divine beings, upon seeing the Goddess as the supreme reality, became still and speechless for a moment; then freed from delusion and full of consciousness, they bowed with joined hands and praised her.
