shambhu_gita::18.modern_relevance: When you decide how to respond to challenges, you realize you alone hold the power to act and shape your path.
shambhu_gita::18.insight: Recognize your unique role as the independent doer with the authority to choose action.

shambhu_gita::19.verse_hindi: जिस धर्म के अत्यन्त प्रभाव से मनुष्य सृष्टि की कर्मो उद्धर्व गामिनी गति निश्चय बनी रहती है और
shambhu_gita::19.english_translation: When the overwhelming power of dharma firmly establishes the natural course of all beings in the world, both men and women abide by it.
shambhu_gita::19.translation_literal: यत् (which) धर्मातिप्रभावेण (by the intense power of dharma) मर्त्यसृष्टे (in mortal creation) गतिर्बुवम (the movement of the earth) क्रमः (order) उदध्वगामिनी (like the ocean's flow) तिष्ठेत् (abides) मानवानाञ्च (and of men) योनितः (and women)
shambhu_gita::19.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::19.essence: Strong dharma creates a steady, natural order for all human lives.
shambhu_gita::19.simple_meaning: The natural order of life and human paths become steady and certain when strongly guided by dharma.
shambhu_gita::19.simple_insight: There is comfort knowing that a deeper order guides all lives steadily onward.
shambhu_gita::19.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how dharma’s overwhelming power sets the unchanging flow of the world and human lives alike, anchoring their paths like a steady current.
shambhu_gita::19.modern_relevance: When you commit to what is right and true, your life’s path gains a steady, reliable flow, easing confusion and doubt.
shambhu_gita::19.insight: It shifts focus from resisting life’s flow to trusting and moving with the natural order dharma creates.

shambhu_gita::20.verse_sanskrit:
प्राणिनः एतनाद्रक्षेद्धर्मो वर्णाश्रमोऽस्त्यसौ ।
नात्र कश्चन सन्देहो विद्यते मृत ! तात ! भोः ॥
shambhu_gita::20.verse_hindi: जीवों को मनुष्ययोनि से  पतन होने नहीं देता वह वर्णाश्रम धर्म है, हे तात सूत ! इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::20.english_translation: The dharma of varna and ashrama protects beings from falling into the human birth; there is no doubt about this, dear Suta.
shambhu_gita::20.translation_literal: प्राणिनः (beings) एतनात् (from this) रक्षेत् (protects) धर्मः (duty) वर्णाश्रमः (varnas and stages of life) अस्ति (exists) असौ (that) । नत्र (there is not) कश्चन (anyone) सन्देहः (doubt) विद्यते (exists) मृत (indeed) तात (dear one) भोः (oh) ॥
shambhu_gita::20.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::20.essence: Living according to your life role prevents falling into lower states of existence.
shambhu_gita::20.simple_meaning: The system of varna and ashrama keeps beings from falling into a lower state by guiding their life roles; this is certain.
shambhu_gita::20.simple_insight: Knowing that following your life role protects your path brings confidence and clarity.
shambhu_gita::20.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the speaker assures Suta that following the established social and spiritual order (varna and ashrama dharma) prevents beings from descending into a lower state of existence. This teaching supports the importance of living according to one's role and stage in life to maintain spiritual progress.
shambhu_gita::20.modern_relevance: When you commit to your responsibilities and life roles, you create stability and protect yourself from confusion or feeling lost.
shambhu_gita::20.insight: It teaches you to respect your natural place and duties to maintain balance and avoid inner or outer downfall.

shambhu_gita::21.verse_sanskrit:
वर्णाश्रमाख्यधर्मेण पितरो वर्द्धिता भृशम् ।
जीवेभ्योऽभ्युदयं शश्वद्ददते नेह संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::21.verse_hindi: वर्णाश्रम धर्म से अत्यन्त संवर्द्धित होकर पितृगण जीवों को सर्वदा अभ्युदय प्रदान किया करते हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::21.english_translation: The ancestors, greatly nurtured by the duties of classes and stages of life, always grant well-being to living beings without doubt.
shambhu_gita::21.translation_literal: वर्णाश्रमाख्यधर्मेण (by duties called classes and stages of life) / पितरो (ancestors) / वर्द्धिता (nurtured) / भृशम् (greatly) / जीवेभ्योऽभ्युदयं (well-being to living beings) / शश्वत् (always) / ददते (give) / नेह (here) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::21.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::21.essence: Ancestors empowered by social duties continuously support the prosperity of living beings.
shambhu_gita::21.simple_meaning: Ancestors, supported by the system of social duties, always bring prosperity and well-being to all living beings.
shambhu_gita::21.simple_insight: There is trust in a timeless order where ancestors continuously support life’s flourishing.
shambhu_gita::21.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how the ancestors, empowered by the social and spiritual duties of classes and life stages, provide ongoing prosperity to living beings, affirming the enduring power of this tradition.
shambhu_gita::21.insight: It highlights the sustaining role of inherited duties and traditions in supporting life and community well-being.

shambhu_gita::22.verse_sanskrit:
वर्णाश्रमाख्यधर्मेषु शैथिल्य समुपस्थिते ।
कर्तुं कर्मोपयुक्तासु स्वाधीनास्वपि सृष्टिषु ॥
shambhu_gita::22.verse_hindi: हे सूत ! वर्णाश्रमधर्म के शिथिल हो जाने से कर्म करने की उपयोगिनी स्वाधीन सृष्टि में
shambhu_gita::22.english_translation: O Suta, when the duties of the social orders and stages of life become lax, even the acts fit for performing become unstable in the created world.
shambhu_gita::22.translation_literal: वर्णाश्रमाख्यधर्मेषु (in the duties called social orders and life stages) शैथिल्य (laxity) समुपस्थिते (when present) ।कर्तुं (to do) कर्मोपयुक्तासु (in acts fit for doing) स्वाधीनास्वपि (even in the independent) सृष्टिषु (in the created world) ॥
shambhu_gita::22.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::22.essence: Weakening clear duties destabilizes even the right actions in the world.
shambhu_gita::22.simple_meaning: When the clear duties of social roles and life stages weaken, even suitable actions become unstable in the world.
shambhu_gita::22.simple_insight: You feel the instability when your responsibilities become unclear or loose.
shambhu_gita::22.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to Suta that when the duties associated with social orders (varna) and life stages (ashrama) become lax or neglected, even the actions that should be performed correctly lose their effectiveness, causing instability in the world.
shambhu_gita::22.modern_relevance: You feel uncertain when your roles at work or home become unclear, making your efforts feel unstable or ineffective.
shambhu_gita::22.insight: Recognize that weakening your commitment to clear duties disrupts your ability to act effectively and confidently.

shambhu_gita::23.verse_sanskrit:
जायते मानवानां भोः सूत  ! नून विषर्ययः ।
स्वाधीनसृष्टिपुजेषु ध्रुवं जाते विषर्यये ॥
shambhu_gita::23.verse_hindi: मानव दृष्टि में भी अवश्य निर्यय होता है, हे सूत ! स्वाधीनसृष्टि समूह में विपर्यय होने से ही सब प्रकार की
shambhu_gita::23.english_translation: O Suta, in human perception, change surely occurs; in the free natural world, change is constant and certain.
shambhu_gita::23.translation_literal: जायते (arises) मानवानां (of humans) भोः (O) सूत (Suta) ! नून (certainly) विषर्ययः (change) । स्वाधीनसृष्टिपुजेषु (in free nature's creations) ध्रुवं (constant) जाते (arises) विषर्यये (change) ॥
shambhu_gita::23.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::23.essence: Change is certain both in human perception and in the free natural world.
shambhu_gita::23.simple_meaning: Human perception always involves change; in the free natural world, change is constant and inevitable.
shambhu_gita::23.simple_insight: You notice everything shifts; nothing stays fixed in your experience or the world around you.
shambhu_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that humans always experience change in their perceptions. The natural world, free and independent, constantly undergoes change, highlighting impermanence as an essential reality.
shambhu_gita::23.modern_relevance: You realize your thoughts, feelings, and surroundings never stay the same, no matter how much you want stability.
shambhu_gita::23.insight: It teaches you to recognize impermanence as a fundamental truth, easing attachment to fixed outcomes.

shambhu_gita::24.verse_sanskrit:
विप्लवः सृष्टिषु प्राज्ञ ! भवेत्सर्वविधास्वपि। 
भीषणोदर्कमेवैतदृदृष्ट्वा पितृगणैः खलु ॥
shambhu_gita::24.verse_hindi: सृष्टि में भी विप्लव होने की अवश्य सम्भावना रहती है; हे प्राज्ञ इसी भीषण परिणाम को देखकर ही पितरों ने
shambhu_gita::24.english_translation: In creation, upheaval is always possible; seeing this terrible consequence, the ancestors indeed...
shambhu_gita::24.translation_literal: विप्लवः (upheaval) सृष्टिषु (in creations) प्राज्ञ (wise one) भवेत् (is possible) सर्वविधास्वपि (in all kinds) । भीषणोदर्कमेव (a terrible consequence indeed) एतदृदृष्ट्वा (having seen this) पितृगैः (by ancestors) खलु (indeed) ॥
shambhu_gita::24.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::24.essence: Upheaval is always possible in creation and demands awareness.
shambhu_gita::24.simple_meaning: Upheaval or disruption can occur in any form of creation; the ancestors recognized this serious danger.
shambhu_gita::24.simple_insight: Recognizing potential danger helps in preparing for inevitable upheavals.
shambhu_gita::24.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the wise, explaining that disturbances are natural in all forms of creation. The ancestors foresaw the terrible results of such upheavals and acted with caution.
shambhu_gita::24.insight: It teaches you to expect change and prepare for difficult consequences in any situation.

shambhu_gita::25.verse_sanskrit:
तपस्तप्तं पुरा घोरं विश्वकल्याणसम्पदे।
स्वतपस्याप्रभावेण तोपितो भगवांश्च तैः ॥
shambhu_gita::25.verse_hindi: विश्वकल्याण-संम्पादन के लिये युग काल में घोर तपस्या की थी और अपनी तपस्या के प्रभाव से उन्होंने
shambhu_gita::25.english_translation: In ages past, intense austerities were undertaken to achieve universal well-being, and by the power of those austerities, the divine was honored.
shambhu_gita::25.translation_literal: तपस्तप्तं (austerity-heated) / पुरा (long ago) / घोरं (intense) / विश्वकल्याणसम्पदे (for universal well-being attainment) / स्वतपस्याप्रभावेण (by the power of self-austerity) / तोपितो (honored) / भगवांश्च (the divine) / तैः (by those)
shambhu_gita::25.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::25.essence: Intense austerity for universal welfare honors the divine through its power.
shambhu_gita::25.simple_meaning: Long ago, powerful austerities were done to bring about universal welfare, and by their power, the divine was honored.
shambhu_gita::25.simple_insight: Great efforts for the good of all have lasting impact beyond their time.
shambhu_gita::25.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates how in ancient times intense austerities were performed aiming at the welfare of the entire world. The power generated from these efforts honored the divine, setting a foundation for cosmic benefit.
shambhu_gita::25.insight: It shows how dedicated effort focused on the greater good influences the world beyond immediate results.

shambhu_gita::26.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वशक्तयालयः शम्भुः सर्वलोकहितमदः।
अन्वभावि तदा तात ! सर्वैः पितृगणैश्च तैः ॥
shambhu_gita::26.verse_hindi: सर्वशक्तिमान् सर्वलोकहितकर भगवान् शम्भु को प्रसन्न किया था। हे तात! उस समय उन सब पितरो ने अनुभव किया कि
shambhu_gita::26.english_translation: Shambhu, the all-powerful and benefactor of all worlds, was pleased. Then, O father, all the forefathers experienced that.
shambhu_gita::26.translation_literal: सर्वशक्तयालयः (all-powerful) शम्भुः (Shambhu) सर्वलोकहितमदः (benefactor of all worlds) अन्वभावि (experienced then) तदा (then) तात (O father) सर्वैः (all) पितृगणैः (forefathers) च (and) तैः (those)
shambhu_gita::26.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::26.essence: The divine's pleasure is felt by all connected ancestral beings.
shambhu_gita::26.simple_meaning: Shambhu, the all-powerful divine being who cares for all worlds, became pleased, and then all the forefathers experienced that joy.
shambhu_gita::26.simple_insight: The divine's pleasure brings a shared experience of joy among those connected to the cosmic order.
shambhu_gita::26.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shambhu (Shiva) is described as all-powerful and caring for all worlds. His pleasure is witnessed and experienced collectively by all the forefathers (pitṛs), indicating a significant cosmic event unfolding.
shambhu_gita::26.insight: It shows how a vital presence's harmony influences the entire community connected to it.

shambhu_gita::27.verse_sanskrit:
सप्तानां स्वरसङ्घानां स्वरूपस्य समष्टितः ।
ओङ्कारध्वनितो दिव्यं कोटिमूर्याधिकप्रभम ॥
shambhu_gita::27.verse_hindi: सप्त स्वरों के रूप की समष्टि रूप ओंकार ध्वनि से एक दिव्य कोटि सूर्य से भी अधिक प्रभावान्
shambhu_gita::27.english_translation: The collective essence of the seven musical notes, in their true form, shines as the divine Om sound, brighter than a million suns.
shambhu_gita::27.translation_literal: सप्तानां (of seven) स्वरसङ्घानां (musical notes' group) स्वरूपस्य (form) समष्टितः (collective) । ओङ्कारध्वनितो (by the Om sound) दिव्यं (divine) कोटिमूर्याधिकप्रभम (million suns more luminous) ॥
shambhu_gita::27.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::27.essence: The seven notes unite as Om, a sound surpassing even immense cosmic radiance.
shambhu_gita::27.simple_meaning: The seven musical notes together form a divine sound, Om, which shines more brightly than millions of suns.
shambhu_gita::27.simple_insight: Sound carries a hidden divine power beyond ordinary perception.
shambhu_gita::27.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes the cosmic significance of sound, revealing that the seven basic musical notes collectively embody the sacred Om sound, which radiates immense divine power surpassing countless suns.
shambhu_gita::27.insight: It reveals that ordinary elements like sound can symbolize vast cosmic power and presence.

shambhu_gita::28.verse_sanskrit:
एकं प्रादुरभूज्ज्योतिरुज्ज्वलं सुमनोहरम ।
तज्ज्योतिरन्तरा शम्भुरासीनः प्रणवासन ॥
shambhu_gita::28.verse_hindi: एक समुज्वल सुमनोहर ज्योतिः प्रकट हुई। उस ज्योति के अन्तर्गत प्रणावासनालीन लोक शंकर महादेव भगवान्
shambhu_gita::28.english_translation: A single radiant and beautiful light appeared. Beneath that light sat Shambhu, the lord of the sacred syllable.
shambhu_gita::28.translation_literal: एकं (one) / प्रादुरभूज् (arose) / ज्योतिः (light) / उज्ज्वलं (bright) / सुमनोहरम् (beautiful) / तज्ज्योतिः (that light) / अन्तरा (underneath) / शम्भुः (Shambhu) / आसीनः (seated) / प्रणव-असन (on the seat of the sacred syllable)
shambhu_gita::28.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::28.essence: A radiant light reveals Shambhu seated within the sacred cosmic sound.
shambhu_gita::28.simple_meaning: A bright, beautiful light appeared, and under it sat Shambhu, the divine being connected with the sacred sound.
shambhu_gita::28.simple_insight: The presence of the divine can be felt as a radiant light that holds all within it.
shambhu_gita::28.detailed_meaning: As the sages gathered, a brilliant light manifested. Within this light sat Shiva, embodying the sacred syllable pranava, symbolizing the cosmic essence and divine presence.
shambhu_gita::28.insight: It invites you to recognize that profound presence often shines quietly beneath all appearances.

shambhu_gita::29.verse_sanskrit:
प्रादुर्भूतो महादेवो भगवाँल्लोकशङ्करः।
शुभैस्तदङ्गवर्णैस्तु गिरयो राजता अलम् ॥
shambhu_gita::29.verse_hindi: शम्भु प्राविभूत हुए। उनके शुभ्र अंग वर्णों से अगणित रजत गिरि अत्यन्त तिरस्कृत हो रहे थे।
shambhu_gita::29.english_translation: Mahadeva, the revered Lord of the world, manifested; countless silver mountains were utterly shamed by his radiant white limbs.
shambhu_gita::29.translation_literal: प्रादुर्भूतो (manifested) महादेवो (Mahadeva) भगवाँल्लोकशङ्करः (revered Lord of the world) । शुभैः (auspicious) तदङ्गवर्णैः (that-limbs-colors) तु (indeed) गिरयः (mountains) राजता (silver) अलम् (utterly) ॥
shambhu_gita::29.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::29.essence: Shiva's radiant form surpasses even countless shining mountains.
shambhu_gita::29.simple_meaning: Shiva appeared in his glorious form, so radiant that countless silver mountains seemed humbled by his brightness.
shambhu_gita::29.simple_insight: The divine presence can outshine even the grandest natural wonders.
shambhu_gita::29.detailed_meaning: In this scene, Shiva appears as the majestic Mahadeva, radiating a brilliant white glow so powerful that countless silver mountains seem diminished in comparison, emphasizing his supreme grandeur.
shambhu_gita::29.insight: Recognize that true greatness shines from within and overshadows external grandeur.

shambhu_gita::30.verse_sanskrit:
अमिता अव्धीर्यन्ते त्रिभिनेत्ररलङ्कृतः ।
विभ्रदिव्यं जटाजूटं भस्मभृपितविग्रहः ॥
shambhu_gita::30.verse_hindi: तीन नेत्रों से सुशोभित थे, दिव्य जटा जूटधारी भस्मभूषितकलेवर
shambhu_gita::30.english_translation: He was adorned with three eyes, divine matted hair, and a body smeared with sacred ash.
shambhu_gita::30.translation_literal: अमिता (countless) / अव्धीर्यन्ते (adorned) / त्रिभिनेत्र (three-eyed) / रटलङ्कृतः (adorned) / विभ्रदि (matted hair) / व्यं (divine) / जटाजूटं (matted hair) / भस्मभृपितविग्रहः (ash-smeared body)
shambhu_gita::30.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::30.essence: The divine appears with three eyes, sacred ash, and matted hair as signs of power.
shambhu_gita::30.simple_meaning: He is described visually by his three eyes, divine matted hair, and a body covered with sacred ash.
shambhu_gita::30.simple_insight: The image evokes reverence, showing the divine's unique and powerful form.
shambhu_gita::30.detailed_meaning: Suta describes Shiva’s appearance to the assembled sages, emphasizing his supernatural features as a symbol of his divine nature and power.
shambhu_gita::30.insight: The verse invites seeing the divine as beyond ordinary form, marked by powerful symbols.

shambhu_gita::31.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिशूलं खर्परं शृङ्गीं दधानो डमरुन्तथा ।
चतुभिर्दिव्यहस्तैः स्वैः नागयज्ञोपवीतवान ॥
shambhu_gita::31.verse_hindi: अपने चारों दिव्य हाथों में डमरू खप्पर त्रिशूल और सींग धारण किये हुये हैं, अनन्त नाग जिनके यज्ञोपवीत है
shambhu_gita::31.english_translation: He holds a drum, a skull, a trident, and a horn in his four divine hands, wearing the sacred thread of the infinite serpent.
shambhu_gita::31.translation_literal: त्रिशूलं (trident) / खर्परं (skull) / शृङ्गीं (horn) / दधानो (holding) / डमरुन्तथा (and drum) / चतुभिर्दिव्यहस्तैः (with four divine hands) / स्वैः (his own) / नागयज्ञोपवीतवान (wearing serpent sacred thread)
shambhu_gita::31.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::31.essence: The divine's power and mystery are shown through sacred symbols held and worn.
shambhu_gita::31.simple_meaning: Shiva is described holding four sacred objects in his four divine hands, wearing the serpent as a sacred thread.
shambhu_gita::31.simple_insight: This image shows the power and mystery embodied by the divine through symbols.
shambhu_gita::31.detailed_meaning: Suta describes Shiva adorned with symbols of power and mystery: four divine hands each holding a sacred object, and the infinite serpent worn like a sacred thread, marking his divine status.
shambhu_gita::31.insight: Symbols can convey deep meaning and presence beyond words or direct description.

shambhu_gita::32.verse_sanskrit:
व्याघ्रचर्माम्बरं दिव्यं वसानः शोभते भृशम् ।
तदवामांके समासीना षोडशी सर्वमुन्दरी ॥
shambhu_gita::32.verse_hindi: दिव्य व्याघ्रचर्म रूपी वस्त्र को पहने हुए हैं जिससे बहुत ही सुशोभित हो रहे हैं। उनके वाम अंक पर बैठी हुई सर्वसुन्दरी
shambhu_gita::32.english_translation: He shines brightly wearing the divine tiger-skin garment; on his left arm sits the most beautiful woman.
shambhu_gita::32.translation_literal: व्याघ्रचर्माम्बरं (tiger-skin garment) / दिव्यं (divine) / वसानः (wearing) / शोभते (shines) / भृशम् (greatly) / तदवामांके (on that left arm) / समासीना (seated) / षोडशी (sixteen-year-old maiden) / सर्वमुन्दरी (most beautiful woman)
shambhu_gita::32.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::32.essence: Shiva’s divine presence shines adorned with tiger skin and a beautiful companion.
shambhu_gita::32.simple_meaning: He wears a divine tiger-skin garment and looks radiant; a beautiful maiden sits on his left arm.
shambhu_gita::32.simple_insight: A vivid scene shows Shiva’s majestic presence and grace with the divine woman.
shambhu_gita::32.detailed_meaning: In this descriptive moment, Shiva is depicted wearing his divine tiger-skin robe, glowing with radiance. Sitting on his left arm is a sixteen-year-old woman, described as the most beautiful, highlighting his majestic and divine companionship.
shambhu_gita::32.insight: The verse invites recognition of divine majesty through symbolic imagery rather than direct teaching.

shambhu_gita::33.verse_sanskrit:
पूर्णशक्तिमयी श्यामा तस्य वैभवपूर्णताम्।
सम्पादयन्ती सततं मनोज्ञा राजतेतराम् ॥
shambhu_gita::33.verse_hindi: पूर्णशक्तिमयी मनोहारिणी षोडशी श्यामा उनके वैभव की पूर्णता को निरन्तर सम्पादित करती हुई अत्यन्त सुशोभित है।
shambhu_gita::33.english_translation: The sixteen-armed dark goddess, full of complete power, continuously manifests the fullness of his splendor, shining beautifully beyond the mind.
shambhu_gita::33.translation_literal: पूर्णशक्तिमयी (full of complete power) / श्यामा (dark/black one) / तस्य (of his) / वैभवपूर्णताम् (fullness of splendor) / सम्पादयन्ती (continuously manifesting) / सततं (always) / मनोज्ञा (mind-pleasing/beautiful) / राजतेतराम् (shines beyond the mind)
shambhu_gita::33.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::33.essence: The divine’s radiant power and beauty continuously shine beyond the limits of the mind.
shambhu_gita::33.simple_meaning: A powerful, beautiful divine figure continuously expresses fullness beyond what your mind can grasp.
shambhu_gita::33.simple_insight: There's awe in sensing that the divine’s beauty and power go beyond your thoughts.
shambhu_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes the sixteen-armed dark goddess Shyama, who embodies complete power and endlessly reveals the fullness of his majestic presence, shining in a way that surpasses ordinary mental perception.
shambhu_gita::33.modern_relevance: You see someone radiating calm strength and beauty that feels beyond what you can fully understand or explain.
shambhu_gita::33.insight: It invites you to open beyond mental limits and appreciate the divine’s fullness as a living presence.

shambhu_gita::34.verse_sanskrit:
पाशाङ्कुशौ च विभ्राणा 'लोचनत्रयभूषिता ।
कल्याणं जंगतां कर्त्तु मन्दस्मितमनोरमा ॥
shambhu_gita::34.verse_hindi: वह पाश और अंकुश को धारण किये हुई हैं, त्रिलोचन से सुशोभित हैं और जगत का कल्याण करने के लिये ईषत् हास्य से शोभायमान है।
shambhu_gita::34.english_translation: She holds a noose and a goad, adorned with three eyes, and with a gentle smile, shines to protect the world.
shambhu_gita::34.translation_literal: पाशाङ्कुशौ (noose and goad) / च (and) / विभ्राणा (wearing) / लोचनत्रयभूषिता (adorned with three eyes) / कल्याणं (welfare) / जंगतां (of the world) / कर्त्तु (to do) / मन्दस्मित (gentle smile) / मनोरमा (pleasing)
shambhu_gita::34.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::34.essence: Power and kindness combine to protect and guide the world.
shambhu_gita::34.simple_meaning: She wears a noose and a goad, has three eyes, and smiles gently to protect the world.
shambhu_gita::34.simple_insight: The divine presence acts with calm control and care to keep the world safe.
shambhu_gita::34.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta describes a divine figure holding symbolic tools and adorned with three eyes, smiling gently, portraying power combined with kindness aimed at the welfare of all beings.
shambhu_gita::34.insight: Symbolic tools represent control over forces; gentle presence balances power with compassion.

shambhu_gita::35.verse_sanskrit:
दिव्यमेवंविधं रूपं सगुणं पितरस्तदा ।
आलोक्याऽऽशान्विताः सन्तो बद्धहस्ताः ययाचिरे ॥
shambhu_gita::35.verse_hindi: उस समय ऐसे दिव्य सगुण रूप को देखकर पितृगण आशान्वित होकर हाथो को जोड़कर प्रार्थना करने लगे।
shambhu_gita::35.english_translation: At that time, seeing such a divine form with qualities, the ancestors, hopeful, joined their hands and began to pray.
shambhu_gita::35.translation_literal: दिव्यमेवम् (divine thus) / विधं (form) / रूपं (appearance) / सगुणं (with qualities) / पितरः (ancestors) / तदा (then) / आलोक्याऽऽशान्विताः (seeing, hopeful) / सन्तः (beings) / बद्धहस्ताः (joined hands) / ययाचिरे (began to pray)
shambhu_gita::35.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::35.essence: Seeing a divine form naturally inspires hopeful reverence and prayer.
shambhu_gita::35.simple_meaning: Ancestors saw a divine form and, filled with hope, folded their hands to pray.
shambhu_gita::35.simple_insight: Hope can arise naturally when you recognize something truly inspiring.
shambhu_gita::35.detailed_meaning: The ancestors witnessed a divine, embodied form and responded reverently by joining their hands in prayer, expressing hopeful devotion at the moment.
shambhu_gita::35.insight: It shows how recognition of something greater naturally invites reverence and hope.

shambhu_gita::36.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वेश्वर ! वयं भाविविश्वदुःखेन कातराः ।
निराकां हि तदुःखमापन्नाः शरणं तव ॥
shambhu_gita::36.verse_hindi: हे विश्वेश्वर ! हम जगत् के भावी दुःख से कातर हो उसके निराकरण के लिये ही आपके शरणागत हुए हैं
shambhu_gita::36.english_translation: O Lord of the universe! We are distressed by the future sufferings of the world and have taken refuge in you to remove that distress.
shambhu_gita::36.translation_literal: विश्वेश्वर (Lord of the universe) / वयं (we) / भावि (future) / विश्वदुःखेन (world's suffering) / कातराः (distressed) / निराकां (removal) / हि (indeed) / तदुःखम् (that suffering) / आपन्नाः (having encountered) / शरणं (refuge) / तव (your)
shambhu_gita::36.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::36.essence: Distress over future suffering leads to seeking refuge in the divine.
shambhu_gita::36.simple_meaning: They express deep worry about the world's future suffering and seek refuge in the divine for relief.
shambhu_gita::36.simple_insight: When overwhelmed by worry, turning to a higher refuge brings comfort.
shambhu_gita::36.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker addresses Shiva as the Lord of the universe, expressing distress over the world's future pain and taking refuge in Shiva to seek relief from that suffering.
shambhu_gita::36.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by the world's problems and seek comfort by connecting to something greater than yourself.
shambhu_gita::36.insight: It teaches you to seek support when faced with fears about the future beyond your control.

shambhu_gita::37.verse_sanskrit:
साम्प्रतं मानवे लोके करुणावरुणालय !।
धर्मे विप्लवसद्भावात् प्रभो ! धर्मस्य तात्त्विकम् ॥
shambhu_gita::37.verse_hindi: हे करुणावरुणा लय प्रभो! इस समय मनुष्य लोक में धर्म विप्लव हो जाने से धर्म का यथार्थ
shambhu_gita::37.english_translation: O Lord of compassion and cosmic law! At this time, in the human world, the true nature of dharma is disturbed by confusion and decline.
shambhu_gita::37.translation_literal: साम्प्रतं (at present) / मानवे (in human) / लोके (world) / करुणावरुणालय (O compassionate ruler of cosmic law) / धर्मे (in dharma) / विप्लवसद्भावात् (due to the state of upheaval) / प्रभो (O Lord) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / तात्त्विकम् (the true essence)
shambhu_gita::37.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::37.essence: Confusion in the human world disrupts the true nature of dharma right now.
shambhu_gita::37.simple_meaning: Right now, in the human world, confusion has disturbed the true meaning of dharma, the natural order and purpose.
shambhu_gita::37.simple_insight: You notice how confusion can shake what holds everything steady.
shambhu_gita::37.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta describes a time when human society faces a crisis: dharma, the guiding principle of right action and order, is in turmoil. This sets the stage for teachings to restore clarity.
shambhu_gita::37.modern_relevance: You see news and social media filled with conflicting values, leaving you unsure about what really matters.
shambhu_gita::37.insight: It highlights how confusion about core values leads to uncertainty and distress in any society or life.

shambhu_gita::38.verse_sanskrit:
सार्वभौमस्वरूपं वै लुप्तमायं प्रजास्वभूत् ।
वर्णाश्रमाख्यधर्मेभ्यः प्रजाश्रद्धोपसंहृतेः ॥
shambhu_gita::38.verse_hindi: सार्वभौमस्वरूप प्रजा प्रायः लुप्त ही हो गया है और 'वर्णाश्रम धर्म की ओर से प्रजा की श्रद्धा उठ जाने से ही
shambhu_gita::38.english_translation: The universal nature is lost among beings because the people have lost faith in the duties of caste and stage of life.
shambhu_gita::38.translation_literal: सार्वभौमस्वरूपं (universal nature) / वै (indeed) / लुप्तमायं (lost) / प्रजास्वभूत् (among beings) / वर्णाश्रमाख्यधर्मेभ्यः (from duties named caste and stage of life) / प्रजाश्रद्धोपसंहृतेः (due to beings' loss of faith)
shambhu_gita::38.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::38.essence: Losing faith in your natural duties causes your sense of universal wholeness to vanish.
shambhu_gita::38.simple_meaning: When people lose faith in their natural duties and roles, their sense of universal order and unity disappears.
shambhu_gita::38.simple_insight: You feel fragmented when you stop trusting the purpose in your role and duties.
shambhu_gita::38.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the universal nature of beings fades when people lose trust in their prescribed duties according to caste and stage of life, causing confusion and disharmony in society and self.
shambhu_gita::38.modern_relevance: You feel lost when you ignore the responsibilities tied to your role, breaking the balance within yourself and others.
shambhu_gita::38.insight: It teaches you to restore trust in your role and duties to regain a sense of unity and purpose.

shambhu_gita::39.verse_sanskrit:
आर्यजातेः किलार्य्यत्वं लुसमायोऽभवञ्च तत् ।
भयभीता वयं जाता अतः शम्भो ! दयार्णव ! ॥
shambhu_gita::39.verse_hindi: आर्य जाति का आर्यत्व लुप्तप्राय हो गया है इस कारण हे दयार्णव शम्भो ! हम भयभीत हुए हैं ।
shambhu_gita::39.english_translation: The noble nature of the noble birth is nearly lost; therefore, O compassionate Shambhu, we have become fearful.
shambhu_gita::39.translation_literal: आर्यजातेः (of noble birth) किल (indeed) आर्य्यत्वं (nobility) लुसमायः (nearly lost) अभवञ्च (became) तत् (that) । भयभीता (fearful) वयं (we) जाता (have become) अतः (therefore) शम्भो (O Shambhu) ! दयार्णव (ocean of compassion) ! ॥
shambhu_gita::39.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::39.essence: Losing noble qualities rooted in birth causes fear that calls for compassionate help.
shambhu_gita::39.simple_meaning: The noble qualities connected with noble birth are nearly gone, causing us to feel afraid.
shambhu_gita::39.simple_insight: You can sense fear when the values you rely on begin to fade away.
shambhu_gita::39.detailed_meaning: The narrator expresses concern that the noble qualities traditionally associated with birth are vanishing, leading to fear and uncertainty before Shiva, called the compassionate ocean of mercy. This reflects a moment of doubt about sustaining dharma.
shambhu_gita::39.modern_relevance: You notice fear rising when the traditions or values you trusted seem to be disappearing around you.
shambhu_gita::39.insight: It highlights how loss of core values triggers fear and calls for seeking compassionate support.

shambhu_gita::40.verse_sanskrit:
कस्मिंश्चित्समये दैव्यां सृष्टौ हि विप्लवे सति ।
यदि देवाप्सरे युद्धेऽसुराणां विजयो भवेत् ॥
shambhu_gita::40.verse_hindi: कालान्तर में दैवी सृष्टि में विप्लव होने पर यदि देवासुर संग्राम में असुरों की विजय हो जाय
shambhu_gita::40.english_translation: At some point in the divine creation, during a great upheaval, if in battle the Asuras were to win against the Devas,
shambhu_gita::40.translation_literal: कस्मिंश्चित्समये (at some time) / दैव्यां (divine) / सृष्टौ (creation) / हि (indeed) / विप्लवे (upheaval) / सति (being) / यदि (if) / देवाप्सरे (Devas and Apsaras) / युद्धेऽसुराणां (in the battle of Asuras) / विजयो (victory) / भवेत् (would be)
shambhu_gita::40.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::40.essence: A battle where shadow beings triumph over radiant beings is a moment in cosmic upheaval.
shambhu_gita::40.simple_meaning: At some moment during the divine creation, if in a battle the forces of shadow were to win against the radiant beings,
shambhu_gita::40.simple_insight: Sometimes events unfold beyond expected order, but these moments alone don't define the whole story.
shambhu_gita::40.detailed_meaning: Suta describes a hypothetical scenario within the divine creation where a great disturbance occurs, and if the Asuras (shadow beings) were to defeat the Devas (radiant beings) in battle, it sets a dramatic stage but is part of a larger cosmic narrative.
shambhu_gita::40.insight: Recognize that conflict and upheaval are part of larger cycles and do not fully determine the outcome.

shambhu_gita::41.verse_sanskrit:
तदा शम्भो ! भवत्यष्टौ भवेन्नूनं विपर्ययः ।
अतस्त्वच्छरणापन्ना वयं भीता अभूम ह ॥
shambhu_gita::41.verse_hindi: तो हे शम्भो! आपकी सृष्टि में अवश्य विपर्याय होगा इस कारण हम भयभीत होकर आपके शरणागत हुए हैं।
shambhu_gita::41.english_translation: O Shambhu! Your creation will surely face disorder; therefore, we have come to your refuge, fearful and helpless.
shambhu_gita::41.translation_literal: तदा (then) शम्भो (Shambhu) ! भवत्यष्टौ (your creation) भवेन्नूनं (will surely be) विपर्ययः (disorder) । अतः (therefore) त्वच्छरणापन्ना (to your refuge surrendered) वयं (we) भीता (fearful) अभूम (became) ह (indeed) ॥
shambhu_gita::41.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::41.essence: Fear of inevitable disorder leads to seeking refuge in the divine.
shambhu_gita::41.simple_meaning: The speaker expresses fear because they believe that disorder will arise in Shambhu's creation, so they seek refuge in him.
shambhu_gita::41.simple_insight: Fear can drive us to seek protection and guidance from a higher source.
shambhu_gita::41.detailed_meaning: The narrator recounts a moment of fear and uncertainty among those devoted to Shiva (Shambhu), who recognize that disorder will come in the world Shiva created, prompting them to seek his protection.
shambhu_gita::41.insight: It highlights how awareness of inevitable challenges motivates turning to support beyond oneself.

shambhu_gita::42.verse_sanskrit:
उपदिश्य, यथायोग्यमस्मानिः साध्वसान कुरु ।
एषा नः प्रार्थना नाथ ! साअलि त्वत्पदाम्बुजे ॥
shambhu_gita::42.verse_hindi: हमको यथायोग्य उपदेश देकर निर्भय करें, हे नाथ ! यही आपके चरणकमलों में हमारी साञ्जलि प्रार्थना है।
shambhu_gita::42.english_translation: Teach us appropriately and make us fearless, O Lord! This is our humble prayer at your lotus feet.
shambhu_gita::42.translation_literal: उपदिश्य (teaching) / यथायोग्यम् (appropriately) / अस्मान् (us) / इः (this) / साध्वसान् (make fearless) / कुरु (do) / एषा (this) / नः (our) / प्रार्थना (prayer) / नाथ (O Lord) / सा (this) / अति (indeed) / त्वत्पदाम्बुजे (at your lotus feet)
shambhu_gita::42.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::42.essence: Asking for teaching that removes fear is a humble, powerful prayer.
shambhu_gita::42.simple_meaning: You ask the divine to teach you properly so you become fearless. This humble request is made at the divine's feet.
shambhu_gita::42.simple_insight: There is strength in asking for clear guidance that removes fear and doubt.
shambhu_gita::42.detailed_meaning: In this verse, a devotee humbly asks Shiva to give teaching suited to their capacity and to make them fearless. This moment is a prayer for courage and clarity before beginning spiritual learning.
shambhu_gita::42.modern_relevance: You feel stuck and unsure, so you quietly ask a trusted mentor for advice that helps you move forward without fear.
shambhu_gita::42.insight: It invites you to approach learning and growth with humility and to seek guidance that builds courage.

shambhu_gita::43.verse_sanskrit:
अपनोदयत स्वीयं चित्तस्थं भयमुल्वणम् ।
उपदेशेषु मे भूयः श्रद्धां कुरुत सत्तमाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::43.verse_hindi: हे महानुभावो! अपने चिर के उत्कट भय को आप दूर करो और मेरे उपदेशों पर श्रद्धान्वित हो।
shambhu_gita::43.english_translation: O noble ones! Remove the intense fear within your own mind and deepen your trust in my teachings.
shambhu_gita::43.translation_literal: अपनोदयत (arise in own) स्वीयं (own) चित्तस्थं (in mind) भयम् (fear) उल्ल्वणम् (intense). उपदेशेषु (in teachings) मे (my) भूयः (more) श्रद्धां (trust) कुरुत (do) सत्तमाः (noble ones)!
shambhu_gita::43.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::43.essence: Deep fear within can be eased by cultivating trust in wise guidance.
shambhu_gita::43.simple_meaning: You are asked to overcome your strong inner fear by placing sincere trust in these teachings.
shambhu_gita::43.simple_insight: Peace grows when you replace fear with trust in guidance.
shambhu_gita::43.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shiva urges his listeners to confront their own profound fears that arise in the mind and instead cultivate sincere trust in his teachings to find strength.
shambhu_gita::43.modern_relevance: When anxious thoughts flood your mind, grounding yourself in trusted guidance can calm your inner storm.
shambhu_gita::43.insight: It teaches you to replace internal fear with faith in reliable wisdom, calming the restless mind.

shambhu_gita::44.verse_sanskrit:
दूरीभूते भये वश्व जगद्गीतिर्विनचति ।
भवन्तो हि यतस्सन्ति स्थूलसृष्टेनियामकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::44.verse_hindi: आपका भय दूर होने पर जगत का भी भय दूर होगा क्योंकि आप लोग ही स्थूल सृष्टि के नियामक हैं ।
shambhu_gita::44.english_translation: When your fear disappears, the world's fear also vanishes because you are the controllers of the gross creation.
shambhu_gita::44.translation_literal: दूरीभूते (when distant/away) भये (fear) वश्व (world) जगद्गीतिः (world's fear) विनचति (is destroyed) । भवन्तो (you all) हि (indeed) यतः (because) सन्ति (are) स्थूलसृष्टेनियामकाः (controllers of the gross creation) ॥
shambhu_gita::44.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::44.essence: Your freedom from fear shapes the fear experienced in the world you govern.
shambhu_gita::44.simple_meaning: When you let go of your fear, the fear in the world also lessens because you influence the physical world around you.
shambhu_gita::44.simple_insight: You carry the power to calm not just yourself but the whole environment by releasing your own fear.
shambhu_gita::44.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that individual fear affects the greater world since people are the regulators of the visible, physical universe. When we overcome our fears, it has a ripple effect on the collective reality.
shambhu_gita::44.modern_relevance: You notice tension rising around you when you feel anxious; calming yourself can ease the atmosphere for everyone nearby.
shambhu_gita::44.insight: It teaches you to see your inner state as a source of wider influence, inspiring responsibility for your emotional balance.

shambhu_gita::45.verse_sanskrit:
स्थूलसृष्टेश्च धात्रयस्ति सूक्ष्मप्टिन संशयः ।
प्राणिनः स्थूलदेहं हि प्राप्तवन्तो यथाविधम ॥
shambhu_gita::45.verse_hindi: स्थूलसृष्टि निःसन्देह सूक्ष्मसृष्टि की धात्री है, जिस प्रकार के स्थूल शरीर को जीव प्राप्त होते हैं
shambhu_gita::45.english_translation: The subtle elements are undoubtedly the source of the gross creation, just as living beings acquire gross bodies in due course.
shambhu_gita::45.translation_literal: स्थूलसृष्टेश्च (gross creation and) / धात्रयस्ति (are the support) / सूक्ष्मप्टिन (subtle elements) / संशयः (without doubt) / प्राणिनः (living beings) / स्थूलदेहं (gross body) / हि (indeed) / प्राप्तवन्तो (have obtained) / यथाविधम (according to proper order)
shambhu_gita::45.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::45.essence: The visible world emerges from subtle elements just as bodies arise naturally.
shambhu_gita::45.simple_meaning: Subtle elements are the foundation of the visible world, just as living beings naturally acquire their physical bodies.
shambhu_gita::45.simple_insight: Everything visible arises from subtle roots; your body is a natural form you take.
shambhu_gita::45.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the visible, gross world depends on subtle elements as its foundation, similar to how living beings receive physical bodies naturally over time.
shambhu_gita::45.insight: It shows the connection between unseen subtle causes and visible effects, helping you see beyond appearances.

shambhu_gita::46.verse_sanskrit:
तांद्दगेव प्रकुर्वन्ति कर्मेह पिनरो ध्रुवम् ।
नात्र कश्चन सन्देहः सत्यं सत्यं वदामि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::46.verse_hindi: पितृगण ! निश्चय उसी श्रेणी के कर्म वह यहां किया करते हैं इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं मैं आपलोगों से सत्य कहता हूँ।
shambhu_gita::46.english_translation: Ancestors certainly perform the same kind of actions here; there is no doubt in this, I tell you the truth.
shambhu_gita::46.translation_literal: तांद्दगेव (certainly the same) प्रकुर्वन्ति (perform) कर्मेह (actions here) पिनरो (ancestors) ध्रुवम् (without doubt) । नात्र (not here) कश्चन (anyone) सन्देहः (doubt) सत्यं (truth) सत्यं (truth) वदामि (I speak) वः (to you) ॥
shambhu_gita::46.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::46.essence: Ancestors unquestionably perform the same kinds of actions in their realm.
shambhu_gita::46.simple_meaning: Ancestors definitely perform the same kinds of actions here; there is no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::46.simple_insight: Knowing that actions continue in a certain way brings certainty amid confusion.
shambhu_gita::46.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the sages about the ancestors (Pitṛgaṇa), affirming that they perform consistent actions in their realm, emphasizing certainty to clarify any doubts about their behavior.
shambhu_gita::46.insight: It reassures that certain patterns of action persist reliably, grounding understanding of cycles beyond immediate perception.

shambhu_gita::47.verse_sanskrit:
भवत्स्वतः प्रसीदत्सु मानवानां निरन्तरम् ।
स्थूलदेहा जनिप्यन्ते नूनं धर्मसहायकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::47.verse_hindi: अतः आप सभी के प्रसन्न होने से निरन्तर ही मनुष्यों के स्थूलशरीर धर्म सहायक उत्पन्न होंगे।
shambhu_gita::47.english_translation: When you remain pleased, humans continually generate gross bodies that support dharma.
shambhu_gita::47.translation_literal: भवत्स्वतः (from you) / प्रसीदत्सु (being pleased) / मानवानां (of humans) / निरन्तरम् (continuously) / स्थूलदेहा (gross bodies) / जनिप्यन्ते (are born) / नूनं (indeed) / धर्मसहायकाः (helpers of dharma)
shambhu_gita::47.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::47.essence: Your inner joy helps life continuously create bodies that support the natural order.
shambhu_gita::47.simple_meaning: Your steady inner happiness helps humans keep forming bodies that support their true purpose.
shambhu_gita::47.simple_insight: Knowing your peace aids life’s natural order brings a quiet confidence and care.
shambhu_gita::47.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when the divine remains pleased, humans continuously take physical form that supports dharma, the natural order, showing how inner states influence outer life cycles.
shambhu_gita::47.modern_relevance: When you feel calm and content, your actions and presence contribute to stability and purpose around you, even beyond what you see.
shambhu_gita::47.insight: It teaches you that your inner state influences the ongoing creation and maintenance of life aligned with dharma.

shambhu_gita::48.verse_sanskrit:
पितरो निश्चितं लोके धर्मगाम्भीर्यलोषतः ।
धार्मिको विप्लवो घोर उपातिष्ठत साम्प्रतम् ॥
shambhu_gita::48.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! संसार में इस समय धर्म का गंभीरता के लोप होने से निश्चय घोर धर्मविप्लव उपस्थित हुआ है
shambhu_gita::48.english_translation: O ancestors, in this world, the severe loss of dharma has surely caused a terrible upheaval of unrighteousness at present.
shambhu_gita::48.translation_literal: पितरो (ancestors) निश्चितं (certainly) लोके (in the world) धर्मगाम्भीर्यलोषतः (from the loss of dharma's seriousness) धार्मिको (righteousness) विप्लवो (upheaval) घोर (terrible) उपातिष्ठत (has arisen) साम्प्रतम् (at present)
shambhu_gita::48.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::48.essence: Loss of seriousness about dharma inevitably leads to deep societal chaos.
shambhu_gita::48.simple_meaning: When people stop taking dharma seriously, severe disorder and unrighteousness arise in the world.
shambhu_gita::48.simple_insight: You sense how fragile order is when respect for dharma disappears.
shambhu_gita::48.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the assembly, declaring that due to the current loss of seriousness toward dharma, a great and terrible upheaval of unrighteousness has appeared, shaking the world’s moral foundation.
shambhu_gita::48.modern_relevance: You notice how a small lapse in shared values can quickly turn a community chaotic and untrustworthy.
shambhu_gita::48.insight: It teaches you to recognize that collective respect for ethical order is crucial to avoid societal collapse.

shambhu_gita::49.verse_sanskrit:
धार्मिके विप्लवे जाने धम्मै गौणं विदन्त्यहो।
अहम्मन्या जनाः सर्वे पापण्डे पण्डिता भृशम् ॥
shambhu_gita::49.verse_hindi: और धर्मविप्लव उपस्थित होने से यहाँ धर्म को अहम्मन्य और पाखण्ड में पण्डित सभी लोग अत्यन्त गौण समझने लगे हैं
shambhu_gita::49.english_translation: When the collapse of dharma occurs, all the learned who are arrogant consider dharma to be insignificant and hypocritical.
shambhu_gita::49.translation_literal: धार्मिके (of dharma) विप्लवे (collapse) जाने (when) धम्मै (dharma) गौणं (insignificant) विदन्त्य (consider) अहो (here) अहम्मन्या (arrogant) जनाः (people) सर्वे (all) पापण्डे (hypocritical) पण्डिता (learned) भृशम् (very much)
shambhu_gita::49.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::49.essence: Arrogance makes even the wise dismiss dharma as meaningless and false.
shambhu_gita::49.simple_meaning: When dharma collapses, even learned people become arrogant and see dharma as unimportant and hypocritical.
shambhu_gita::49.simple_insight: Pride can blind you to the true value of your purpose and ethics.
shambhu_gita::49.detailed_meaning: In a time of crisis when dharma is disrupted, even knowledgeable people become proud and start to see dharma as insignificant and hypocritical, losing respect for their true purpose.
shambhu_gita::49.modern_relevance: You might notice how when core values weaken, even smart people defend harmful shortcuts out of pride.
shambhu_gita::49.insight: It teaches you to watch how arrogance can distort your view of what truly matters.

shambhu_gita::50.verse_sanskrit:
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सार्वभौमस्वरूपकम् ।
जानीयुर्मानवाः किं नु धर्माचर्य्यगणा अपि ॥
shambhu_gita::50.verse_hindi: और शाश्वत धर्म के सार्वभौम स्वरूप को मनुष्य तो, क्या जाने धर्माचार्यों ने भी
shambhu_gita::50.english_translation: Even the dharma teachers do not truly know the universal nature of eternal dharma, so how would ordinary humans?
shambhu_gita::50.translation_literal: शाश्वतस्य (of the eternal) / च (and) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / सार्वभौमस्वरूपकम् (universal nature) / जानीयुर्मानवाः (do humans know) / किं (how) / नु (indeed) / धर्माचर्य्यगणा (even dharma teachers) / अपि (also)
shambhu_gita::50.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::50.essence: Even the most learned cannot fully know the eternal, universal dharma.
shambhu_gita::50.simple_meaning: The true, universal nature of eternal dharma is so vast that even those who teach it cannot fully understand it, let alone ordinary people.
shambhu_gita::50.simple_insight: It’s humbling to know that no one has complete understanding, inviting openness and curiosity.
shambhu_gita::50.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shiva points out how vast and profound eternal dharma is. Even the learned dharma teachers, regarded as authorities, cannot fully grasp its universal essence. This highlights the depth of dharma beyond human comprehension.
shambhu_gita::50.modern_relevance: When you think you’ve mastered a life principle, remember even experts don’t hold all the answers. It invites patience with yourself.
shambhu_gita::50.insight: It shifts your perspective from expecting certainty to embracing ongoing inquiry and humility.

shambhu_gita::51.verse_sanskrit:
अज्ञात्वा तत्स्वरूपं हि पथो निमिरे पृथक् ।
कुमार्गमवलम्बन्ते भ्रान्ता यैरेव मानवाः ॥
shambhu_gita::51.verse_hindi: उसके स्वरूप को न समझकर स्वतन्त्र पन्थ निर्माण किये हैं जिनसे ही भ्रान्त होकर मनुष्य कुपथगामी बनते हैं।
shambhu_gita::51.english_translation: Not knowing the true nature of that, humans create separate paths and, confused by them, stray onto wrong ways.
shambhu_gita::51.translation_literal: अज्ञात्वा (not knowing) तत् (that) स्वरूपं (nature) हि (indeed) पथो (paths) निमिरे (create) पृथक् (separate) कुमार्गम् (wrong path) अवलम्बन्ते (follow) भ्रान्ता (confused) यैः (by those) एव (indeed) मानवाः (humans)
shambhu_gita::51.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::51.essence: Confusion arises when you ignore true nature and build false separate paths.
shambhu_gita::51.simple_meaning: Without understanding the true nature of reality, people create their own separate paths and get confused, leading them away from the right way.
shambhu_gita::51.simple_insight: There's a gentle warning that missing clarity can mislead your whole journey.
shambhu_gita::51.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when humans fail to grasp the true nature of reality, they invent different paths out of confusion. These separate paths cause them to stray from the correct way, showing how ignorance causes misdirection.
shambhu_gita::51.modern_relevance: You might find yourself juggling conflicting advice or beliefs, feeling stuck because you haven't yet seen the core truth that would unify your direction.
shambhu_gita::51.insight: It teaches you to question and seek the true nature behind appearances before choosing your path.

shambhu_gita::52.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मगाम्भीर्यनाशेन मानवानाञ्च बुद्धयः।
बहिर्मुखीनाः सम्वृत्ता इन्द्रियेषु परायणाः ॥
shambhu_gita::52.verse_hindi: और धर्म की गंभीरता का नाश होने से ही मनुष्यों की बुद्धि बहिर्मुखीन और इन्द्रियपरायण हो गई है
shambhu_gita::52.english_translation: When the seriousness of dharma is lost, human intelligence turns outward and becomes enslaved to the senses.
shambhu_gita::52.translation_literal: धर्मगाम्भीर्यनाशेन (by loss of seriousness of dharma) / मानवानाञ्च (and of humans) / बुद्धयः (intelligence) / बहिर्मुखीनाः (turned outward) / सम्वृत्ता (become enclosed) / इन्द्रियेषु (in the senses) / परायणाः (dependent/enslaved)
shambhu_gita::52.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::52.essence: Losing respect for dharma makes the mind restless and enslaved to the senses.
shambhu_gita::52.simple_meaning: When people stop taking their true purpose seriously, their intelligence turns outward and becomes controlled by their senses.
shambhu_gita::52.simple_insight: You feel how losing focus on what matters lets your mind get distracted and restless.
shambhu_gita::52.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when humans forget the importance of dharma—their true purpose and moral seriousness—their wisdom fades. Instead, their attention fixates on sensory pleasures and distractions, losing connection with deeper insight.
shambhu_gita::52.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly on your phone, losing sense of purpose as your attention surrenders to fleeting distractions.
shambhu_gita::52.insight: This verse shifts your focus from external temptations back to honoring your deeper responsibilities and discipline.

shambhu_gita::53.verse_sanskrit:
निमज्जेयुर्यथा पूर्णे सुगभीरे जलाशये ।
अनेकेऽपि गजाः सम्यक् किन्तु तस्य जलं यदि ॥
shambhu_gita::53.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! जिस प्रकार जलपूर्ण सुगंभीर जलाशय में अनेक हस्ती भी अच्छी तरह डूबी जा सकते हैं परन्तु उस जलाशय का जल यदि
shambhu_gita::53.english_translation: Just as many elephants can be fully submerged in a deep, full lake, but the water of that lake...
shambhu_gita::53.translation_literal: निमज्जेयुः (can be submerged) / यथा (just as) / पूर्णे (full) / सुगभीरे (deep) / जलाशये (in the lake) / अनेकेऽपि (many also) / गजाः (elephants) / सम्यक् (properly) / किन्तु (but) / तस्य (of that) / जलं (water) / यदि (if)
shambhu_gita::53.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::53.essence: External pressures can be many, yet the true nature remains unchanged beneath them.
shambhu_gita::53.simple_meaning: Many large elephants can be fully submerged in a deep, full waterbody, yet the water itself remains unaffected.
shambhu_gita::53.simple_insight: Great challenges or pressures can happen without changing the core nature beneath them.
shambhu_gita::53.detailed_meaning: Suta is describing a metaphor where many elephants can be submerged in a deep lake without changing the water itself. This sets up a teaching about how external events do not affect the inner essence.
shambhu_gita::53.insight: It teaches that external circumstances, no matter how overwhelming, do not alter the underlying essence.

shambhu_gita::54.verse_sanskrit:
क्षेत्रे प्रसारयेत्कापि महासीम्नि पितृवजा:।
शशकोऽपि तदा तत्र निमज्जेन्नैव कहिर्चित्त ॥
shambhu_gita::54.verse_hindi: किसी बड़े मैदान में फैला दिया जाय तो उसमें खरगोश भी कभी भी नहीं डूब सकता
shambhu_gita::54.english_translation: If spread over a large field, even a hare would never drown in it.
shambhu_gita::54.translation_literal: क्षेत्रे (in the field) प्रसारयेत् (if spread) कपि (even) महा-सीम्नि (in a great boundary) पितृ-वजा: (possibly 'father's water' or a specific term) शशक: अपि (even a hare) तदा (then) तत्र (there) निमज्जेन् (would immerse) नैव (not) कहि (anywhere) चित्त (mind)
shambhu_gita::54.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::54.essence: Vastness offers safety so even the smallest are never overwhelmed.
shambhu_gita::54.simple_meaning: If something is spread wide enough, even a small creature cannot be overwhelmed or trapped by it.
shambhu_gita::54.simple_insight: There is safety and freedom in vastness that even the smallest can never lose.
shambhu_gita::54.detailed_meaning: This verse uses the image of spreading water over a large field, so large that even a small hare could not drown. It suggests the power of vastness or abundance to protect and support all beings, highlighting an aspect of the divine or nature's generosity.
shambhu_gita::54.modern_relevance: When problems feel overwhelming, remember that expanding your perspective can make even tough challenges manageable.
shambhu_gita::54.insight: It teaches you to see that expanding your space or resources can prevent harm or overwhelm.

shambhu_gita::55.verse_sanskrit:
आसीज्जलाशये यावत्तावदेव जलन्तु तत् ।
किन्तु शक्तौ विपर्यासो भवेदगाम्भीर्यनाशतः ॥
shambhu_gita::55.verse_hindi: वह जल जितना जलाशय में था उतना ही तो रहता है परन्तु उसकी गम्भीरता नष्ट होने से उसकी शक्ति में फेर पड़ जाता है
shambhu_gita::55.english_translation: The water in the lake remains the same in quantity, but its power changes when its depth is lost.
shambhu_gita::55.translation_literal: आसीज्जलाशये (water in the lake) / यावत् (as much as) / तावदेव (only that much) / जलन्तु (remains) / तत् (that) / किन्तु (but) / शक्तौ (in power) / विपर्यासो (change) / भवेद् (happens) / अगाम्भीर्यनाशतः (due to loss of depth)
shambhu_gita::55.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::55.essence: Losing inner depth changes your power even when your external presence stays constant.
shambhu_gita::55.simple_meaning: The amount of water stays the same, but losing depth changes its power.
shambhu_gita::55.simple_insight: You feel how losing inner depth can weaken your true strength.
shambhu_gita::55.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that although the water quantity in a lake remains constant, losing its depth diminishes its power, symbolizing how losing inner depth weakens strength.
shambhu_gita::55.modern_relevance: You seem fine on the surface, but skipping reflection leaves you drained and less effective.
shambhu_gita::55.insight: It teaches you to value inner depth as the source of lasting strength, not just external presence.

shambhu_gita::56.verse_sanskrit:
समष्टिव्याष्टिरूपाभ्यां स्रष्टेः सन्धारिका मम ।
शक्तिनियामिका सैव ध्रुवं धर्मः सनातनः ॥
shambhu_gita::56.verse_hindi: समष्टि और व्यष्टिरूप से, सृष्टि के धारण करने वाली जो मेरी नियमाका शक्ति है उसी को सनातन धर्म कहते हैं
shambhu_gita::56.english_translation: The eternal dharma is the regulating power of my creation that sustains both the collective and the individual forms.
shambhu_gita::56.translation_literal: समष्टि (collective) / एवं (and) / व्यष्टि (individual) / रूपाभ्यां (in forms) / स्रष्टेः (of the creator) / सन्धारिका (sustaining) / मम (my) / शक्तिनियामिका (regulating power) / सैव (indeed) / ध्रुवं (eternal) / धर्मः (dharma) / सनातनः (eternal)
shambhu_gita::56.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::56.essence: Your true purpose is the eternal power sustaining both the universe and yourself.
shambhu_gita::56.simple_meaning: The eternal dharma is the power that sustains both the whole universe and each individual form within it.
shambhu_gita::56.simple_insight: Knowing your true purpose connects you to the timeless force sustaining all life.
shambhu_gita::56.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes dharma as the eternal regulating power that holds together both the vast cosmos and every individual being. This teaching reveals dharma as the foundation of creation's order and balance.
shambhu_gita::56.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic, remember you are part of a timeless power that holds everything steady, both your world and the larger whole.
shambhu_gita::56.insight: It shifts your view from feeling isolated to seeing yourself as part of an enduring, sustaining order.

shambhu_gita::57.verse_sanskrit:
तत्सनातनधर्मस्य पादाश्चत्वार आसते ।
साधारणविशेषौ हि तथाऽसाधारणापदौ ॥
shambhu_gita::57.verse_hindi: उस सनातन धर्म के चार पाद है, यथा-साधारण धर्म, विशेष धर्म, असाधारण धर्म और आपद्धर्म
shambhu_gita::57.english_translation: That eternal dharma has four parts: common dharma, special dharma, extraordinary dharma, and emergency dharma.
shambhu_gita::57.translation_literal: तत् (that) सनातनधर्मस्य (of eternal dharma) पादाः (feet/parts) चत्वार् (four) आसते (are) । साधारणविशेषौ (common and special) हि (indeed) तथा (so) असाधारणापदौ (extraordinary and emergency) ॥
shambhu_gita::57.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::57.essence: Eternal dharma includes four distinct ways to act depending on the situation.
shambhu_gita::57.simple_meaning: Eternal dharma is divided into four types: common, special, extraordinary, and emergency duties or codes.
shambhu_gita::57.simple_insight: Understanding dharma as layered helps you see how different situations call for different responses.
shambhu_gita::57.detailed_meaning: This verse introduces the concept that eternal dharma is not a single rule but consists of four categories, each guiding behavior differently depending on the context, setting a framework for later detailed teachings.
shambhu_gita::57.modern_relevance: You face many roles and challenges; knowing that different situations require different kinds of responsibility can ease confusion.
shambhu_gita::57.insight: It encourages recognizing that ethical living adapts to circumstances, not just one fixed standard.

shambhu_gita::58.verse_sanskrit:
सार्वभौमो यतो धर्मः सर्वलोकहितप्रदः।
ददासभ्युदयं नित्यं सुखं निःश्रेयसन्तथा ॥
shambhu_gita::58.verse_hindi: धर्म सार्वभौम और सर्वलोकहितकर होने से यह निरन्तर अनायास, अभ्युदय और निःश्रेयस प्रदान करता है
shambhu_gita::58.english_translation: When dharma is universal and benefits all worlds, it continuously grants effortless prosperity and true welfare.
shambhu_gita::58.translation_literal: सार्वभौमो (universal) यतो (from which) धर्मः (dharma) सर्वलोकहितप्रदः (benefiting all worlds) ददाति (gives) अभ्युदयं (prosperity) नित्यम् (always) सुखं (happiness) निःश्रेयसन्तथा (and true welfare)
shambhu_gita::58.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::58.essence: Dharma that benefits all brings effortless and lasting prosperity and true welfare.
shambhu_gita::58.simple_meaning: When your actions follow dharma that is universal and benefits all, they naturally bring continuous prosperity, happiness, and true welfare.
shambhu_gita::58.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing that acting for everyone's good creates lasting well-being without struggle.
shambhu_gita::58.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes dharma as a universal principle that supports all beings and worlds. When you act according to such dharma, you naturally foster constant prosperity and ultimate welfare for yourself and others.
shambhu_gita::58.modern_relevance: You volunteer your time at a community event, not for reward but because it helps everyone; that effort creates real, ongoing good.
shambhu_gita::58.insight: It shifts your motivation from personal gain to universal benefit, making your actions naturally fruitful and fulfilling.

shambhu_gita::59.verse_sanskrit:
निखिलं धर्मशक्तचैव विश्वमेतञ्चराचरम्।
क्रमेणाभ्युदयं लब्ध्वा सरत्यग्रे हि माम्प्रति ॥
shambhu_gita::59.verse_hindi: यह स्थावर-जंगमात्मा समस्त विश्व धर्म को शक्ति से ही क्रमशः अभ्युदय प्राप्त करके ही मेरी ओर अग्रसर होता है
shambhu_gita::59.english_translation: The entire universe, moving and unmoving, advances step by step through the power of dharma toward me.
shambhu_gita::59.translation_literal: निखिलं (entire) / धर्मशक्तचैव (and by the power of dharma) / विश्वम् (universe) / एतञ्च (this) / चराचरम् (moving and unmoving) / क्रमेण (step by step) / अभ्युदयं (advancement) / लब्ध्वा (having obtained) / सरति (advances) / अग्रे (forward) / हि (indeed) / माम् (to me) / प्रति (towards)
shambhu_gita::59.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::59.essence: All existence steadily moves toward the divine by following dharma's power.
shambhu_gita::59.simple_meaning: Everything in the world, living or not, moves forward gradually with the power of dharma toward the divine presence.
shambhu_gita::59.simple_insight: There is a steady, natural progress toward what is true and right in all existence.
shambhu_gita::59.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes the universe as composed of all moving and non-moving things that, empowered by dharma, advance gradually toward him, symbolizing cosmic order moving toward its source.
shambhu_gita::59.insight: It shows that all aspects of life progress through dharma's power toward harmony and purpose.

shambhu_gita::60.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानिनो मम भक्ताश्च धर्मशक्तयैव सत्त्वरम्।
तत्त्वज्ञानस्य साहाय्याल्लभन्ते मुक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥
shambhu_gita::60.verse_hindi: और मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तगण धर्म की ही शक्ति द्वारा तत्त्वज्ञान की सहायता से उत्तम निःश्रेयस को शीघ्र प्राप्त होते हैं
shambhu_gita::60.english_translation: My wise devotees swiftly attain the highest freedom through the power of dharma aided by true knowledge.
shambhu_gita::60.translation_literal: ज्ञानिनो (wise) / मम (my) / भक्ताश्च (devotees also) / धर्मशक्तयैव (by dharma's power alone) / सत्त्वरम् (the pure or excellent) / तत्त्वज्ञानस्य (of true knowledge) / साहाय्याल् (with the help) / लभन्ते (attain) / मुक्तिमुत्तमाम् (the highest freedom)
shambhu_gita::60.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::60.essence: True devotion combined with wisdom and dharma power leads quickly to highest freedom.
shambhu_gita::60.simple_meaning: Those who are devoted and wise gain the greatest freedom quickly by following the power of dharma and true understanding.
shambhu_gita::60.simple_insight: You feel encouraged knowing devotion and wisdom together open the fastest path to freedom.
shambhu_gita::60.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that his followers who combine devoted love with wisdom and act according to dharma gain the highest freedom without delay. This teaching highlights the union of Bhakti and Jnana as a powerful means to liberation.
shambhu_gita::60.modern_relevance: You feel stuck between heart and head—this reminds you that combining your sincere care with clear understanding accelerates your growth.
shambhu_gita::60.insight: It teaches you to unite heartfelt devotion with clear knowledge to move swiftly toward inner freedom.

shambhu_gita::61.verse_sanskrit:
शाश्वतस्यास्य धर्मस्य यावत्प्रादुर्भविष्यति ।
सार्वभौमस्वरूपं हे पितरो भाग्यशालिनः! ॥
shambhu_gita::61.verse_hindi: हे भाग्यशाली पितृगण ! इस सनातन धर्म का सार्वभौम स्वरूप जितना प्रकट होगा
shambhu_gita::61.english_translation: O fortunate ancestors! As long as this eternal dharma exists, its universal nature will manifest.
shambhu_gita::61.translation_literal: शाश्वतस्य (of the eternal) अस्य (this) धर्मस्य (dharma) यावत् (as long as) प्रादुर्भविष्यति (will manifest) । सार्वभौमस्वरूपं (universal nature) हे (O) पितरो (ancestors) भाग्यशालिनः (fortunate) ॥
shambhu_gita::61.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::61.essence: The eternal dharma reveals its universal nature as long as it exists.
shambhu_gita::61.simple_meaning: The universal form of the eternal dharma will show itself as long as it exists, says the speaker to the ancestors.
shambhu_gita::61.simple_insight: There is a lasting presence of righteous order that reveals itself through time.
shambhu_gita::61.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the fortunate ancestors, declaring that the eternal dharma's universal nature will continue to manifest as long as dharma endures, setting the stage for teachings about timeless righteousness.
shambhu_gita::61.insight: Recognize that the enduring principles of right conduct reveal themselves continuously through time.

shambhu_gita::62.verse_sanskrit:
जनानां क्षुद्रता लोके तावत्येव विनक्षंयति ।
साधारणस्य धर्मस्य तत्त्वतो हृदयङ्गमम् ॥
shambhu_gita::62.verse_hindi: संसार में मनुष्यों की क्षुद्रता उतनी ही नष्ट होगी। तत्त्वतः. साधारण धर्म का
shambhu_gita::62.english_translation: In the world, the pettiness of humans will be destroyed just as much as the essence of ordinary dharma reaches the heart.
shambhu_gita::62.translation_literal: जनानां (of people) क्षुद्रता (pettiness) लोके (in the world) तावत्येव (just so much) विनक्षंयति (is destroyed) । साधारणस्य (of ordinary) धर्मस्य (dharma) तत्त्वतो (essentially) हृदयङ्गमम् (heart-reaching) ॥
shambhu_gita::62.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::62.essence: True dharma's presence in the heart dissolves human pettiness.
shambhu_gita::62.simple_meaning: Human pettiness decreases as the true essence of simple dharma deeply touches the heart.
shambhu_gita::62.simple_insight: There is hope in knowing that embracing true purpose softens inner smallness.
shambhu_gita::62.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the common human pettiness or small-mindedness diminishes exactly in proportion to how deeply the essential nature of ordinary dharma enters the heart. This means living true to basic righteous conduct transforms inner limitations.
shambhu_gita::62.modern_relevance: When you genuinely follow your basic values, the trivial grudges and small worries that cloud your mind begin to vanish.
shambhu_gita::62.insight: It teaches you to focus on the core of your dharma to naturally overcome petty thoughts and behaviors.

shambhu_gita::63.verse_sanskrit:
सार्वभौमस्वरूपं हि कर्त्तुमह्यै  न संशयः ।
पालनीयाः सदाचारा आर्यजातीयमानवै: ॥
shambhu_gita::63.verse_hindi: सार्वभौम स्वरूप निःसन्देह  हृदयंगम करने योग्य है सदाचार भी आर्य जातीय मनुष्यों से पालन कराने योग्य हैं
shambhu_gita::63.english_translation: There is no doubt that the universal nature can be acted upon by me; righteous conduct must be upheld even by noble people.
shambhu_gita::63.translation_literal: सार्वभौमस्वरूपं (universal nature) / हि (indeed) / कर्त्तुमह्यै (to be done by me) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / पालनीयाः (to be upheld) / सदाचारा (righteous conduct) / आर्यजातीयमानवैः (by noble people)
shambhu_gita::63.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::63.essence: You must act on universal truth and uphold noble conduct without hesitation.
shambhu_gita::63.simple_meaning: You can and should act according to what applies universally. Even noble people must follow righteous conduct.
shambhu_gita::63.simple_insight: You feel responsible to act on what truly matters, respecting good conduct for everyone.
shambhu_gita::63.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that acting upon the universal nature — the common reality underlying all — is without doubt. This calls for everyone, especially noble people, to uphold righteous behavior.
shambhu_gita::63.modern_relevance: You face choices that affect more than yourself. Remember that acting rightly is a responsibility shared by all with integrity.
shambhu_gita::63.insight: It shifts your focus from narrow self-interest to embracing universal responsibility and moral standards.

shambhu_gita::64.verse_sanskrit:
वर्णाश्रमीयधर्मस्य विशेषस्य तथैव च ।
यतो वर्णाश्रमैधर्मेविहींना सर्वथा ननु ॥
shambhu_gita::64.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार वर्णाश्रम सम्बन्धी विशेष धर्म के सदाचार पालन कराने योग्य हैं; क्योकि  वर्णाश्रम धर्म रहित
shambhu_gita::64.english_translation: Similarly, the particular duties related to varna and ashrama ensure proper conduct; without them, complete disorder follows.
shambhu_gita::64.translation_literal: वर्णाश्रमीयधर्मस्य (of varna-ashrama duty) विशेषस्य (particular) तथैव (similarly) च (also) यतो (because) वर्णाश्रमैधर्मे (without varna-ashrama duty) विहींना (devoid) सर्वथा (entirely) ननु (indeed) ।
shambhu_gita::64.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::64.essence: Clear roles and duties are essential to maintain order in conduct and life.
shambhu_gita::64.simple_meaning: Specific duties related to social and life stages guide proper behavior; without these duties, disorder arises.
shambhu_gita::64.simple_insight: You feel grounded when you follow clear responsibilities that shape your actions.
shambhu_gita::64.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that duties connected to one's social role and life stage (varna and ashrama) provide essential structure for right conduct. Without these guiding responsibilities, behavior becomes disordered and chaotic.
shambhu_gita::64.modern_relevance: When your daily roles and responsibilities are unclear, life feels chaotic and your actions lose meaning.
shambhu_gita::64.insight: It teaches you to recognize how defined responsibilities organize your choices and keep your life steady.

shambhu_gita::65.verse_sanskrit:
असौं सृष्टिर्मानवानां कालिकायाः प्रभावतः ।
प्रकृतर्मे लयं याति कुत्रचित्समये स्वतः ॥
shambhu_gita::65.verse_hindi: यह मनुष्य सृष्टि स्वतः मेरी प्रकृति काली के प्रभाव से किसी समयान्तर में सर्वथैव लय को प्राप्त हुआ करती है
shambhu_gita::65.english_translation: This human creation of mine naturally dissolves at some time under the influence of the dark power of time.
shambhu_gita::65.translation_literal: असौं (this) / सृष्टिर्मानवानां (creation of humans) / कालिकायाः (of the dark one - Kali) / प्रभावतः (under the influence) / प्रकृतर्मे (my nature) / लयं (dissolution) / याति (goes) / कुत्रचित्समये (at some time) / स्वतः (naturally)
shambhu_gita::65.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::65.essence: All that arises from nature must dissolve naturally under the influence of time.
shambhu_gita::65.simple_meaning: All human creation arises from my nature and will naturally dissolve eventually because of the power of time.
shambhu_gita::65.simple_insight: Recognizing that all things naturally end brings a quiet acceptance of change.
shambhu_gita::65.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that everything created, including human existence, emerges from his nature but inevitably dissolves by time’s power. This reflects the cosmic cycle of creation and destruction rooted deeply in nature’s flow.
shambhu_gita::65.modern_relevance: You watch a favorite moment fade or a project end, realizing nothing lasts forever despite your efforts.
shambhu_gita::65.insight: It shifts your mind to accept impermanence as a natural and unavoidable part of all things.

shambhu_gita::66.verse_sanskrit:
धत्ते रूपान्तरं वासौ नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
वर्णाश्रमाणां धर्माणां बीजरक्षामभावतः ॥
shambhu_gita::66.verse_hindi: अथवा वह रूपान्तर को धारण कर लिया करती है। इसमें कोई विचार की बात नहीं है। वर्णाश्रम धर्म को बीजरक्षा के प्रभाव से
shambhu_gita::66.english_translation: The inner being adopts different forms without deliberation due to the absence of the seed protection of varna-ashrama dharma.
shambhu_gita::66.translation_literal: धत्ते (adopts) रूपान्तरं (different forms) वासौ (inner being) नात्र (not there) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (deliberation) । वर्णाश्रमाणां (of varna-ashrama) धर्माणां (duties) बीजरक्षा (seed protection) अभावतः (because of absence) ॥
shambhu_gita::66.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::66.essence: The true self changes forms unconsciously when the root of duty and order is absent.
shambhu_gita::66.simple_meaning: The true self naturally takes on different forms without thinking when the foundation of social and spiritual duties is missing.
shambhu_gita::66.simple_insight: There is unrest when the foundation of duty and purpose is lost, causing the self to change uncontrollably.
shambhu_gita::66.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when the protective foundation of varna-ashrama dharma (the social and spiritual order) is absent, the true self takes on changing forms without conscious choice, leading to instability in identity and action.
shambhu_gita::66.modern_relevance: When you lose your core values or sense of purpose, you might find yourself changing roles or behaviors without clarity or control.
shambhu_gita::66.insight: It teaches you to recognize how losing your grounding in purpose leads to reactive shifts in identity and action.

shambhu_gita::67.verse_sanskrit:
मर्त्यानां रक्षितः पन्थाः स्यात् क्रमाभ्युदयपदः ।
शाश्वतस्य हि धर्मस्य ज्ञान स्यात्तेन कहिचित् ॥
shambhu_gita::67.verse_hindi: मनुष्यों की अभ्युदय देनेवाली शैली की रक्षा होती है, उससे किसी समय सनातन धर्म का ज्ञान होता है।
shambhu_gita::67.english_translation: The protected path of humans leads to their prosperity and grants knowledge of the eternal dharma.
shambhu_gita::67.translation_literal: मर्त्यानां (of mortals) / रक्षितः (protected) / पन्थाः (path) / स्यात् (is) / क्रमाभ्युदयपदः (the way to prosperity) / शाश्वतस्य (of the eternal) / हि (indeed) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / ज्ञान (knowledge) / स्यात् (is) / तेन (by it) / कहिचित् (certainly).
shambhu_gita::67.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::67.essence: A steady, protected path leads to lasting growth and eternal understanding.
shambhu_gita::67.simple_meaning: If your path is protected and steady, it will lead you to growth and lasting understanding of your true purpose.
shambhu_gita::67.simple_insight: You can trust that steady, protected effort leads to lasting growth and clarity.
shambhu_gita::67.detailed_meaning: In a moment of teaching, Shiva explains that when a person's path is safeguarded and steady, it naturally leads to their growth and an understanding of eternal dharma, the true purpose that never changes.
shambhu_gita::67.modern_relevance: When you commit to a clear and steady course, even amidst distractions, growth and deeper meaning naturally follow.
shambhu_gita::67.insight: It shifts focus from fleeting actions to sustaining a protected, steady path that reveals deeper purpose over time.

shambhu_gita::68.verse_sanskrit:
वर्णधर्म यतो विज्ञाः प्रवृत्ते रोधकं जगुः ।
निवृत्तेः पोषकञ्चैव धर्ममाश्रमगोचरम् ॥
shambhu_gita::68.verse_hindi: क्योंकि हे विज्ञ पितृगण ! वर्ण धर्म प्रवृत्तिरोधक और आश्रम धर्म निवृत्तिपोषक कहा जाता है।
shambhu_gita::68.english_translation: Learned ancestors say that social duties activated support order, while withdrawal duties nourish renunciation.
shambhu_gita::68.translation_literal: वर्णधर्म (social duties) यतः (because) विज्ञाः (learned) पितृगण (ancestors) प्रवृत्ते (in activity) रोधकं (restraining) जगुः (said) । निवृत्तेः (in withdrawal) पोषकञ्चैव (also nourishing) धर्मम् (duty) आश्रमगोचरम् (stage-of-life related) ॥
shambhu_gita::68.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::68.essence: Active duties maintain order; withdrawal duties nourish inner growth.
shambhu_gita::68.simple_meaning: Active social duties maintain order, while duties in withdrawal support personal growth in stages of life.
shambhu_gita::68.simple_insight: You can find balance by acting to maintain order and withdrawing to nurture yourself.
shambhu_gita::68.detailed_meaning: Suta reports that wise ancestors taught two kinds of duties: active social roles that restrain chaos, and duties in retirement stages that nourish inner growth. This sets the framework for understanding dharma in different life phases.
shambhu_gita::68.modern_relevance: You juggle work and family roles, then need time away to recharge and grow beyond daily tasks.
shambhu_gita::68.insight: It teaches you to recognize when to engage with society and when to step back for personal nourishment.

shambhu_gita::69.verse_sanskrit:
अतो वर्णाश्रमाख्यस्य धर्मस्यैव सुरक्षणात् ।
रक्षिता पितरो वो हि शक्तिः सम्पत्स्यते शुभा ॥
shambhu_gita::69.verse_hindi: इसलिये हे पितृगण ! वर्णाश्रम धर्म की रक्षा के द्वारा ही तुम्हारी ही शुभशक्ति रक्षित होगी।
shambhu_gita::69.english_translation: Therefore, O ancestors, your own auspicious power will be protected only by preserving the dharma of the social orders and stages of life.
shambhu_gita::69.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) वर्णाश्रमाख्यस्य (of the social orders and stages of life) धर्मस्यैव (only of dharma) सुरक्षणात् (by protection) । रक्षिता (protected) पितरो (ancestors) वो (your) हि (indeed) शक्तिः (power) सम्पत्स्यते (will be obtained) शुभा (auspicious) ॥
shambhu_gita::69.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::69.essence: Protecting your true duty is the way to preserve your auspicious power.
shambhu_gita::69.simple_meaning: Your true power and wellbeing depend on protecting your rightful role and duty in life.
shambhu_gita::69.simple_insight: You feel empowered when you honor your responsibilities with care and commitment.
shambhu_gita::69.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, reminding them that their auspicious power depends on protecting the dharma of social roles and life stages. The verse emphasizes that upholding these duties maintains strength and prosperity.
shambhu_gita::69.modern_relevance: When you commit to your responsibilities at work or home, you preserve your inner strength and positive influence.
shambhu_gita::69.insight: It teaches you to see your duty as a source of authentic power, not a burden to resist.

shambhu_gita::70.verse_sanskrit:
साधारणस्य धर्मस्य विशेषस्य तथैव च ।
कियन्तीवर्णयाम्यद्य वृत्तीयुषकमन्तिके ॥
shambhu_gita::70.verse_hindi: अब साधारण धर्म और विशेष धर्म की कुछ वृत्तियों का वर्णन आपलोग के सामने करता हूँ
shambhu_gita::70.english_translation: Now I describe some behaviors of ordinary dharma and special dharma to you all.
shambhu_gita::70.translation_literal: साधारणस्य (of ordinary) धर्मस्य (dharma) विशेषस्य (special) तथैव (also) च (and) । कियन्तीवर्णयामि (some describe/I describe) अद्य (today/now) वृत्तीयुषकमन्तिके (behaviors/actions near the end)
shambhu_gita::70.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::70.essence: Introducing distinctions between ordinary and special dharma behaviors.
shambhu_gita::70.simple_meaning: A description of some common and special duties or behaviors is about to be given.
shambhu_gita::70.simple_insight: Understanding different kinds of dharma helps prepare for deeper teachings.
shambhu_gita::70.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the sages, preparing to explain types of dharma—ordinary and special—highlighting the upcoming focus on specific behaviors.
shambhu_gita::70.insight: Recognizing different categories of duty sets the stage for practical guidance.

shambhu_gita::71.verse_sanskrit:
श्रयन्तां ता भवद्भिस्तु दत्तचित्तैः शनैः शनैः ।
धृतिः क्षमा दमोऽस्तेयं शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ॥
shambhu_gita::71.verse_hindi: आपलोग दत्तचित्त होकर उनको  शनैः शनैः सुने, धृति, क्षमा, दम, अस्तेय, शौच, इन्द्रियनिग्रह
shambhu_gita::71.english_translation: You all should listen to them with a willing heart, slowly and steadily, cultivating endurance, forgiveness, self-control, non-stealing, purity, and control of the senses.
shambhu_gita::71.translation_literal: श्रयन्तां (Let them rely) / ता (those) / भवद्भिस्तु (by you all) / दत्तचित्तैः (with a willing heart) / शनैः शनैः (slowly, steadily) / धृतिः (endurance) / क्षमा (forgiveness) / दमोऽस्तेयं (self-control, non-stealing) / शौचम् (purity) / इन्द्रिय-निग्रहः (control of the senses)
shambhu_gita::71.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::71.essence: Willing, patient listening slowly builds lasting self-discipline and inner strength.
shambhu_gita::71.simple_meaning: Listening patiently and with willingness helps develop endurance, forgiveness, self-control, honesty, purity, and control over your senses.
shambhu_gita::71.simple_insight: Patience and self-control grow naturally when you listen with a willing heart.
