shambhu_gita::71.detailed_meaning: Shiva instructs followers to listen carefully and with willingness to teachings or guidance, which slowly cultivates key qualities like endurance, forgiveness, self-control, honesty, purity, and mastery over the senses, essential for disciplined living.
shambhu_gita::71.modern_relevance: When you take time to listen fully and openly to feedback or advice, your patience and self-control naturally improve.
shambhu_gita::71.insight: It teaches you to cultivate inner qualities through deliberate, patient, and willing attention to guidance.

shambhu_gita::72.verse_sanskrit:
धीर्विद्या सत्यमक्रोध औदार्य समदर्शिता ।
परोपकारनिप्कामभावप्रभृतयः शुभाः ॥
shambhu_gita::72.verse_hindi: धी, विद्या, सत्य, अक्रोध, उदारता, समदर्शिता, परोपकार, निष्कामभाव आदि
shambhu_gita::72.english_translation: Patience, knowledge, truthfulness, absence of anger, generosity, impartiality, selfless service, and desirelessness are all good qualities.
shambhu_gita::72.translation_literal: धीर्विद्या (patience and knowledge) / सत्यम् (truthfulness) / अक्‍रोध (absence of anger) / औदार्य (generosity) / समदर्शिता (impartiality) / परोपकार (helping others) / निष्कामभाव (desirelessness) / प्रभृतयः (qualities) / शुभाः (good)
shambhu_gita::72.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::72.essence: True strength comes from patient, generous, and selfless qualities within you.
shambhu_gita::72.simple_meaning: Good character is made of patience, honesty, generosity, fairness, and helping others without wanting rewards.
shambhu_gita::72.simple_insight: You feel steady and open when you act without craving or anger.
shambhu_gita::72.detailed_meaning: Shiva lists key virtues like patience, truthfulness, and selfless care as the foundation of righteous action. These qualities prepare Arjuna to act with a clear mind and open heart.
shambhu_gita::72.modern_relevance: You stay calm in difficult conversations, give without expecting thanks, and treat everyone fairly at work.
shambhu_gita::72.insight: Focus on cultivating patience and generosity in daily life to act with steady purpose and clear intent.

shambhu_gita::73.verse_hindi: साधारण धर्म की ही शुभ वृत्तियां हैं।
shambhu_gita::73.english_translation: The virtuous actions belong only to ordinary dharma.
shambhu_gita::73.translation_literal: साधारणस्य (ordinary's) धर्मस्य (of dharma) विद्यन्ते (exist) वृत्तयो (actions) ध्रुवम् (fixed, certain)
shambhu_gita::73.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::73.essence: Steady, virtuous actions arise from following ordinary, common dharma.
shambhu_gita::73.simple_meaning: Most good actions come from following ordinary, common principles of right conduct.
shambhu_gita::73.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that simple, steady duties form the foundation of good action.
shambhu_gita::73.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva explains that common, everyday duties—the basic rules of conduct—are the source of stable, virtuous actions. This sets the stage for understanding how higher dharma builds upon this foundation.
shambhu_gita::73.modern_relevance: You rely on regular habits and common sense to guide your daily choices, forming the backbone of your integrity.
shambhu_gita::73.insight: It teaches you to recognize and value simple, consistent duties as the basis of ethical behavior.

shambhu_gita::74.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मचर्यश्च दाम्पत्यं निवासी निर्जने बने ।
त्यागो ह्यध्यापनश्चैव याजनञ्च प्रतिग्रहः ॥
shambhu_gita::74.verse_hindi: और ब्रह्मचर्य, दाम्पत्य, निर्जनवनवास, त्याग, पाठन, याजन, प्रतिग्रह, प्रजापालन
shambhu_gita::74.english_translation: Celibacy, married life, living in a solitary forest, renunciation, study, sacrifice, and acceptance of gifts.
shambhu_gita::74.translation_literal: ब्रह्मचर्यश्च (celibacy and) दाम्पत्यं (married life) निवासी (living) निर्जने (in a solitary) बने (forest) । त्यागो (renunciation) हि (indeed) अध्यापनश्चैव (and study also) याजनञ्च (sacrifice) प्रतिग्रहः (acceptance of gifts) ॥
shambhu_gita::74.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::74.essence: Spiritual life includes multiple valid paths and practices.
shambhu_gita::74.simple_meaning: This verse lists different life stages and practices, including celibacy, marriage, forest dwelling, renunciation, study, sacrifice, and accepting gifts.
shambhu_gita::74.simple_insight: Life includes many paths and practices, each with its own place and purpose.
shambhu_gita::74.detailed_meaning: The verse mentions various traditional lifestyles and spiritual practices without elaboration, showing the diversity of dharmic living. It does not teach a specific lesson but names important ways of life.
shambhu_gita::74.insight: Recognize that spiritual life can take many forms, each valid in its context.

shambhu_gita::75.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मयुद्धं प्रजारक्षा वाणिज्यं सेवनादयः ।
विशेषस्यापि धर्मस्य सन्तीमाः खलु वृत्तयः ॥
shambhu_gita::75.verse_hindi: धर्मयुद्ध, वाणिज्य, सेवा आदि, विशेष धर्म की यह ही वृत्तियां हैं
shambhu_gita::75.english_translation: Protecting the people through righteous war, trade, and service are indeed the main forms of special dharma.
shambhu_gita::75.translation_literal: धर्मयुद्धं (righteous war) / प्रजारक्षा (protection of subjects) / वाणिज्यं (trade) / सेवनादयः (service, etc.) / विशेषस्यापि (also of special) / धर्मस्य (dharma) / सन्तीमाः (main) / खलु (indeed) / वृत्तयः (forms, activities)
shambhu_gita::75.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::75.essence: Protecting, trading, and serving are essential expressions of your special duty.
shambhu_gita::75.simple_meaning: Certain actions like protecting people, trading, and serving are important forms of special duty you must uphold.
shambhu_gita::75.simple_insight: You can find purpose and meaning in fulfilling your specific roles with integrity.
shambhu_gita::75.detailed_meaning: This teaching explains that special dharma includes specific roles such as righteous war to protect people, engaging in trade, and serving others. These are distinct duties that define how one contributes to society.
shambhu_gita::75.modern_relevance: You stand up for your community, keep your business honest, and help those around you — these are your real responsibilities.
shambhu_gita::75.insight: Recognize your unique duties as meaningful ways to live dharma through action and service.

shambhu_gita::76.verse_sanskrit:
साधारणस्य धर्मस्यावयवाः कीर्तिता यथा ।
विशेषस्यापि धर्मस्य तथाङ्गानि पृथक् पृथक् ॥
shambhu_gita::76.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार साधारण धर्म के अंग कहे गये हैं उसी प्रकार विशेष धर्म के भी अलग अलग अंग हैं
shambhu_gita::76.english_translation: Just as the parts of common duty are described, similarly the parts of special duty are also distinct.
shambhu_gita::76.translation_literal: साधारणस्य (common) धर्मस्यावयवाः (parts of duty) कीर्तिता (described) यथा (as) । विशेषस्यापि (special also) धर्मस्य (duty) तथाङ्गानि (parts) पृथक् (distinct) पृथक् (separately) ॥
shambhu_gita::76.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::76.essence: Both common and special duties have distinct, separate parts to fulfill.
shambhu_gita::76.simple_meaning: Both general duties and special duties have their own specific parts or aspects that must be recognized.
shambhu_gita::76.simple_insight: You realize duties are layered, not all the same; your special roles matter distinctly.
shambhu_gita::76.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that just as common duties have defined parts, so do special duties, highlighting the complexity and structure of one's obligations in life.
shambhu_gita::76.modern_relevance: You juggle everyday tasks but also have unique responsibilities that require your specific attention and care.
shambhu_gita::76.insight: Recognize that your unique roles require distinct actions alongside general responsibilities.

shambhu_gita::77.verse_sanskrit:
उपाङ्गान्यपि धर्मस्य वर्तन्ते भूरिशो ध्रुवम् ।
देशकालादिवैचित्र्यादुपाङ्गं ह्येकमेव च ॥
shambhu_gita::77.verse_hindi: धर्म के उपांग भी अनेक ही हैं और देशकाल पात्र की विचित्रता के अनुसार एक ही उपांग
shambhu_gita::77.english_translation: Many subsidiary parts of dharma exist, but due to differences in place, time, and context, only one is chosen.
shambhu_gita::77.translation_literal: उपाङ्गान्यपि (subsidiary parts also) धर्मस्य (of dharma) वर्तन्ते (exist) भूरिशः (many) ध्रुवम् (fixed) । देशकालादि (place, time, etc.) वैचित्र्याद् (due to difference) उपाङ्गं (subsidiary part) हि (indeed) एकमेव (only one) च (also) ॥
shambhu_gita::77.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::77.essence: Only one part of dharma fits your unique place and time.
shambhu_gita::77.simple_meaning: Dharma includes many parts, but only one part applies to you based on your situation.
shambhu_gita::77.simple_insight: You don’t have to follow every rule—only the one that fits your moment.
shambhu_gita::77.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that dharma has many aspects, but because place, time, and circumstances differ, only one particular aspect applies at once. This teaches how to find your immediate duty amidst many possibilities.
shambhu_gita::77.modern_relevance: When choices overwhelm you, remember your true responsibility depends on your current situation—not every option available.
shambhu_gita::77.insight: Focus your effort on the duty that fits your present context instead of trying to do everything.

shambhu_gita::78.verse_sanskrit:
अङ्गानां नन्वनेकपामुपाङ्गं स्याइसंशयम् ।
अत्यन्तं वर्त्तते विज्ञाः ! धर्मस्य गहना गतिः ॥
shambhu_gita::78.verse_hindi: अनेक अंगों का निःसन्देह ही उपांग हो सकता है। हे विज्ञों! धर्म की गति अति गहन है।
shambhu_gita::78.english_translation: Without many parts, a part cannot exist; surely the path of dharma is very profound.
shambhu_gita::78.translation_literal: अङ्गानां (of parts) नन्व (surely not) एकपाम् (one alone) उपाङ्गं (a part) स्य (can be) असंशयम् (without doubt) । अत्यन्तं (extremely) वर्त्तते (exists) विज्ञाः (wise ones) ! धर्मस्य (of dharma) गहना (profound) गतिः (path) ॥
shambhu_gita::78.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::78.essence: No part stands alone; dharma’s path is deeply interconnected and profound.
shambhu_gita::78.simple_meaning: A single part cannot stand alone; the way of dharma is deeply complex and interconnected.
shambhu_gita::78.simple_insight: You sense that dharma’s path is too deep to grasp by looking at just one part.
shambhu_gita::78.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that dharma’s true nature cannot be understood by isolating a single part; it requires seeing the whole complex system of interconnected parts, revealing dharma’s deep and subtle movement.
shambhu_gita::78.modern_relevance: You notice how a team’s success depends on all members working together, not just one person’s effort.
shambhu_gita::78.insight: It teaches you to see your role as part of a larger whole, not in isolation.

shambhu_gita::79.verse_sanskrit:
जायते भावसाहाय्याभूतिदाः ! अन्तरं बहु ।
सर्वधर्मस्वरूपेषु सत्यं सत्यं ब्रवीमि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::79.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! भाव की सहायता से सब धर्मों के स्वरूपो में अनेक अन्तर हो जाया करता है, यह मैं आप लोगों को सत्य कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::79.english_translation: O ancestors! With the support of emotions, many differences arise in the forms of all dharmas; this I tell you truly.
shambhu_gita::79.translation_literal: जायते (arises) / भाव (emotion) / साहाय्य (support) / अभूतिदाः (causes) / अन्तरं (difference) / बहु (many) / सर्वधर्मस्वरूपेषु (in all dharma's forms) / सत्यं (truth) / सत्यं (truly) / ब्रवीमि (I speak) / वः (to you)
shambhu_gita::79.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::79.essence: Emotions create many differences in how people perceive the true nature of their duties.
shambhu_gita::79.simple_meaning: Emotions influence how people understand the true nature of their duties and paths, causing many differences.
shambhu_gita::79.simple_insight: Recognizing that your feelings affect what you see brings clarity and compassion for others' views.
shambhu_gita::79.detailed_meaning: Addressing the ancestors, Shiva explains that emotions affect how people perceive the true nature of dharma, creating many variations in understanding and practice.
shambhu_gita::79.modern_relevance: You notice how your mood changes your view of rules or expectations at work or home, making things seem clearer or confusing.
shambhu_gita::79.insight: It teaches you to notice when emotions influence your judgment and to seek deeper clarity beyond feelings.

shambhu_gita::80.verse_sanskrit:
भावतत्त्वस्य विज्ञानं पूर्णरूपेण वेदितुम् ।
अंत:करणविज्ञानस्वरूपं वच्मि वोऽग्रतः ॥
shambhu_gita::80.verse_hindi: भाव तत्त्व के विज्ञान को पूर्ण रूप से स्पष्ट करने के अर्थ अन्तःकरण विज्ञान का स्वरूप आप लोगों के समीप कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::80.english_translation: I speak to you closely about the inner mind's nature to fully reveal the essence of feeling's knowledge.
shambhu_gita::80.translation_literal: भावतत्त्वस्य (essence of feeling) / विज्ञानं (knowledge) / पूर्णरूपेण (in complete form) / वेदितुम् (to know) / अंत:करणविज्ञानस्वरूपं (inner mind-knowledge-nature) / वच्मि (I speak) / वोऽग्रतः (to you closely)
shambhu_gita::80.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::80.essence: Understanding feelings deeply requires knowing the true nature of the inner mind.
shambhu_gita::80.simple_meaning: The deepest understanding of feeling comes from knowing the nature of your inner mind.
shambhu_gita::80.simple_insight: Knowing your inner mind helps you fully grasp your feelings' true nature.
shambhu_gita::80.detailed_meaning: Shiva prepares to teach about the essence of feeling by explaining the inner mind's nature, inviting close attention to fully understand this subtle knowledge.
shambhu_gita::80.modern_relevance: When emotions feel overwhelming, turning inward to understand your mind helps you see feelings clearly.
shambhu_gita::80.insight: It teaches you to explore your inner mind as the foundation for understanding your feelings completely.

shambhu_gita::81.verse_sanskrit:
मनो बुद्धिरहङ्कारश्चित्तमेतच्चतुर्विधम् ।
अन्तःकरणमस्तीति वित्त यूयं पितृव्रजाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::81.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! अन्तःकरण के चार भेद हैं, ऐसा आपलोग जाने, यथा-मन बुद्धि चित्त और अहङ्कार।
shambhu_gita::81.english_translation: O ancestors, know that the inner instrument has four parts: mind, intellect, sense of I, and inner state.
shambhu_gita::81.translation_literal: मनो (mind) बुद्धि (intellect) अहङ्कार (ego/sense of I) चित्तम् (inner state) एतच्चतुर्विधम् (these four kinds) । अन्तःकरणम् (inner instrument) अस्ति (exists) इति (thus) वित्त (know) यूयं (you) पितृव्रजाः (ancestors) !
shambhu_gita::81.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::81.essence: The inner instrument has four distinct parts shaping your experience.
shambhu_gita::81.simple_meaning: The inner instrument consists of four parts: the mind, intellect, ego, and inner state. This is a foundational classification of how your inner self works.
shambhu_gita::81.simple_insight: Knowing your inner self has parts helps you understand your thoughts and feelings better.
shambhu_gita::81.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the assembled ancestors, explaining that the inner instrument (antahkarana) is made of four parts: mind (manas), intellect (buddhi), ego (ahamkara), and inner state (chitta). This sets the stage for deeper teachings on self and mind.
shambhu_gita::81.modern_relevance: When you reflect on your feelings, thoughts, and self-identity, recognizing these as distinct parts helps you manage your reactions and decisions.
shambhu_gita::81.insight: It teaches you to see your mind’s different layers, helping separate thinking from feeling and self from inner awareness.

shambhu_gita::82.verse_hindi: चित्त मन का अन्तर्विभाग है और अहंकार बुद्धि का अन्तर्विभाग है। संसारी जीवों को जिस प्रकार स्त्री दृढ माया रस्सियों से बांधकर
shambhu_gita::82.english_translation: The inner part of the mind is the inner state, and the sense of separate self is the inner part of the discerning mind; just as worldly beings are firmly bound by the strong ropes of illusion.
shambhu_gita::82.translation_literal: मनसोऽन्तविभागोऽस्ति (mind's inner part is) चित्तञ्च (the inner state also) अहकतिधियः (sense of separate self [is] of discerning mind) । मायापाशैदृढैव (like strong ropes of illusion) ध्या (of intellect) योषित (female) संसारगोचरम् (worldly beings) ॥
shambhu_gita::82.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::82.essence: The sense of separate self tightly binds the mind in strong illusion.
shambhu_gita::82.simple_meaning: Your inner state is part of your mind, and the sense of being separate comes from your discerning mind. This sense traps you like strong ropes of illusion.
shambhu_gita::82.simple_insight: You can feel how your sense of separateness ties your mind to confusion and limits freedom.
shambhu_gita::82.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva explains that your deepest mind includes your inner state (Chitta) and that the sense of 'I' (Ahamkara) comes from the discerning mind (Buddhi). This false sense of separation binds worldly beings as firmly as strong ropes of illusion.
shambhu_gita::82.modern_relevance: When your mind fixates on 'me' and 'mine,' you feel trapped by worries and confusion that pull you away from calm.
shambhu_gita::82.insight: It teaches you to notice how the sense of 'I' traps your mind and to begin loosening that grip.

shambhu_gita::83.verse_sanskrit:
यथा संसारिभिर्जीवैः कार्य कारयतेऽनिशम् ।
तथा चित्तं मनो बुद्धिमहंकारो नियम्य च ॥
shambhu_gita::83.verse_hindi: उनसे अहर्निश संसार का कार्य कराती है उसी प्रकार चित्त मन को और अहङ्कार बुद्धि को नियमन करके
shambhu_gita::83.english_translation: Just as the natural world constantly causes beings to act, similarly the mind, intellect, and sense of self must be controlled.
shambhu_gita::83.translation_literal: यथा (just as) संसारिभिः (by beings of the world) जीवैः (living beings) कार्य (action) कारयते (causes to do) अनिशम् (constantly) । तथा (so) चित्तं (mind) मनः (mind) बुद्धिम् (intellect) अहंकारः (sense of self) नियम्य (controlling) च (and) ॥
shambhu_gita::83.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::83.essence: Controlling mind, intellect, and ego is as essential as nature’s constant driving of action.
shambhu_gita::83.simple_meaning: The world naturally causes beings to act constantly. Similarly, you must control your mind, intellect, and sense of separate self.
shambhu_gita::83.simple_insight: There’s strength in steady self-control, just like nature’s unstoppable flow.
shambhu_gita::83.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that just as the world compels living beings to act without pause, a person must similarly regulate the restless mind, discerning intellect, and ego to act wisely and steadily.
shambhu_gita::83.modern_relevance: When distractions constantly pull your attention, steadying your mind and sense of self helps you stay focused and effective.
shambhu_gita::83.insight: It teaches you to treat your mind and ego like natural forces that need consistent regulation for balanced action.

shambhu_gita::84.verse_sanskrit:
कार्य कारयते शश्वनानावैचित्र्यसङ्कुलम् ।
संस्कारानुचरा जीवा वर्तन्ते सर्वथा खलु ॥
shambhu_gita::84.verse_hindi: निरन्तर माया वैचित्र्यपूर्ण काम कराया करते हैं। जीव सर्वथा ही संस्कारों के दास हैं
shambhu_gita::84.english_translation: The mind constantly compels action full of diverse illusions. The living being is entirely bound by impressions.
shambhu_gita::84.translation_literal: कार्य (action) / कारयते (makes) / शश्वन (always) / अनावैचित्र्यसङ्कुलम् (full of illusions and variety) । / संस्कारानुचरा (following impressions) / जीवा (the living being) / वर्तन्ते (exist) / सर्वथा (completely) / खलु (indeed) ॥
shambhu_gita::84.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::84.essence: Your actions are driven by a restless mind shaped by countless impressions.
shambhu_gita::84.simple_meaning: Your mind is always active, driven by many illusions. Your true self is bound by past impressions shaping your actions.
shambhu_gita::84.simple_insight: There's relief in seeing how deep habits shape your actions beyond your immediate control.
shambhu_gita::84.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how the restless mind, full of illusions, continuously drives action. The living being remains bound by past impressions, which shape all behavior and responses in life.
shambhu_gita::84.modern_relevance: You notice how your habits and past experiences push you to act automatically, even when you want to choose differently.
shambhu_gita::84.insight: It teaches you to recognize how deep impressions steer your reactions, inviting you to cultivate discipline to change them.

shambhu_gita::85.verse_sanskrit:
वासनोत्पन्नसंस्कारा अभिवघ्नन्ति प्राणिनः ।
आसक्तिरेव मूलञ्च बन्धनस्यास्य कारणम् ॥
shambhu_gita::85.verse_hindi: वासना से उत्पन्न संस्कार जीवों को जकड़ रखते हैं, आसक्ति ही इस बन्धन का मूल कारण है
shambhu_gita::85.english_translation: Impressions born from desire bind living beings; attachment is the root cause of this bondage.
shambhu_gita::85.translation_literal: वासना (desires) / से (from) / उत्पन्न (born) / संस्कारा (impressions) / अभिवघ्नन्ति (bind) / प्राणिनः (living beings) / । / आसक्ति (attachment) / एव (indeed) / मूलम् (root) / च (and) / बन्धनस्य (of bondage) / अस्य (this) / कारणम् (cause) / ॥
shambhu_gita::85.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::85.essence: Attachment born from desire creates the mental bonds that trap living beings.
shambhu_gita::85.simple_meaning: Desires create mental impressions that bind living beings, and attachment is the main cause of this bondage.
shambhu_gita::85.simple_insight: You can feel the weight of attachment as the real cause of what holds you back.
shambhu_gita::85.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that desires produce deep mental impressions (samskaras) which trap living beings in cycles of bondage; attachment to these desires is the fundamental cause of this entrapment.
shambhu_gita::85.modern_relevance: You notice how craving something creates habits and patterns that keep you stuck, even when you want freedom.
shambhu_gita::85.insight: Recognize attachment as the source of mental patterns that limit your freedom and start loosening your hold.

shambhu_gita::86.verse_sanskrit:
संस्कारो वासनाजन्यः संस्कारात्कर्म जायते ।
वासनोत्पद्यते भूयः कर्मणो नात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::86.verse_hindi: वासना से संस्कार होता है, संस्कार से कर्म होता है, कर्म से पुनः वासना उत्पन्न होती है.
shambhu_gita::86.english_translation: Desires give rise to impressions; impressions lead to action; and action again produces desires without doubt.
shambhu_gita::86.translation_literal: वासना (desire) / जन्यः (born from) / संस्कारः (impression) / संस्कारात् (from impression) / कर्म (action) / जायते (arises) / वासना (desire) / उत्पद्यते (is produced) / भूयः (again) / कर्मणः (from action) / न (not) / अत्र (here) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::86.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::86.essence: Desire creates impressions, impressions cause actions, and actions regenerate desire endlessly.
shambhu_gita::86.simple_meaning: Desires create mental impressions, impressions lead to actions, and these actions create more desires, forming a continuous cycle.
shambhu_gita::86.simple_insight: Recognizing this cycle reveals how your cravings keep renewing themselves through your actions.
shambhu_gita::86.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how the restless desires (vasanas) form deep impressions (samskaras), which then manifest as actions (karma). These actions again generate fresh desires, creating a cycle that binds beings in reactive patterns.
shambhu_gita::86.modern_relevance: You notice how one craving leads to habits, which prompt more cravings, making it hard to break free from repeating patterns.
shambhu_gita::86.insight: This verse teaches you to see how your actions are not isolated but part of a repeating cycle fueled by desire and impression.

shambhu_gita::87.verse_sanskrit:
वासनायाः पुनर्विज्ञाः ! संस्कारों जायते ध्रुवम् ।
सदैवं वासनाचक्रं जीवानाञ्च गतागतम् ॥
shambhu_gita::87.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञो ! वासना से पुनः संस्कार ही उत्पन्न होता है । इस संसार में इस प्रकार से वासना का चक्र और जीव का आवागमन
shambhu_gita::87.english_translation: O wise one, from desire arises habit again; thus the cycle of desire and the soul's coming and going continues in this world.
shambhu_gita::87.translation_literal: वासनायाः (of desire) पुनर्विज्ञाः (again arises) ! संस्कारों (habit) जायते (is born) ध्रुवम् (certainly) । सदैवं (always) वासनाचक्रं (cycle of desire) जीवानाञ्च (of the soul also) गतागतम् (coming and going) ॥
shambhu_gita::87.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::87.essence: Desire continuously produces habits that keep the soul cycling through life.
shambhu_gita::87.simple_meaning: Desire creates habits, and these habits keep the cycle of the soul's movement continuing endlessly.
shambhu_gita::87.simple_insight: There’s a natural pull where desire leads to habit, keeping you caught in repeating patterns.
shambhu_gita::87.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to a wise listener how desire (vasana) inevitably creates lasting habits (samskara), which bind the soul into a continuous cycle of coming and going in the world.
shambhu_gita::87.modern_relevance: You notice how one craving leads to repeated behaviors, trapping you in familiar ups and downs you want to escape.
shambhu_gita::87.insight: It teaches you to see desire not as isolated but as the seed of habits that sustain your cycle.

shambhu_gita::88.verse_sanskrit:
पूर्णायमानमस्तीह चक्रानेमियथा रथे ।
पूर्वजन्मार्जिता यादृक् कर्मसंस्कारसन्ततिः ॥
shambhu_gita::88.verse_hindi: रथ चक्रनेमि के समान सदा घूर्णायमान रहता है । पूर्व जन्मार्जित कर्मसंस्कार समूह अथवा
shambhu_gita::88.english_translation: Just like the wheel of a chariot always keeps turning, the continuous flow of impressions from past actions keeps moving.
shambhu_gita::88.translation_literal: पूर्णायमानमस्तीह (always turning) चक्रानेमियथा (like the wheel of a chariot) रथे (of the chariot) । पूर्वजन्मार्जिता (acquired in previous birth) यादृक् (such as) कर्मसंस्कारसन्ततिः (continuous flow of impressions of actions) ॥
shambhu_gita::88.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::88.essence: The impressions of past actions keep turning endlessly like a chariot wheel.
shambhu_gita::88.simple_meaning: Your past actions create a continuous flow of impressions that keep influencing your present, like a chariot's wheel always turning.
shambhu_gita::88.simple_insight: There's a steady momentum from what you did before, always moving you forward.
shambhu_gita::88.detailed_meaning: Shiva compares the ongoing influence of past karmic impressions to a chariot wheel that never stops turning, showing how past actions keep affecting the present moment.
shambhu_gita::88.modern_relevance: When you find yourself reacting habitually, it’s the momentum of past choices spinning like a wheel beneath your awareness.
shambhu_gita::88.insight: Recognize how past actions keep driving present habits, so you can consciously change the cycle.

shambhu_gita::89.verse_sanskrit:
एतजन्मकृतानां वा कर्मणां यादृशी स्मृतिः ।
अङ्किता जीवचित्तं स्यादासक्तिः स्याद्धि तादृशी ॥
shambhu_gita::89.verse_hindi: इस जन्म के कर्म की स्मृति जैसी जीव के वित्त में अङ्कित रहती है उसी प्रकार उसको आसक्ति हुआ करती है।
shambhu_gita::89.english_translation: Just as the memory of actions from this life is imprinted on the mind, so too attachment arises accordingly.
shambhu_gita::89.translation_literal: एतजन्मकृतानां (of this birth's actions) / वा (or) / कर्मणां (of actions) / यादृशी (such as the memory) / स्मृतिः (memory) / अङ्किता (imprinted) / जीवचित्तं (on the living mind) / स्याद् (would be) / आसक्तिः (attachment) / स्यात् (would be) / धि (indeed) / तादृशी (of that kind)
shambhu_gita::89.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::89.essence: Your attachments arise naturally from memories imprinted by your past actions.
shambhu_gita::89.simple_meaning: Your mind remembers your actions from this life, and that memory creates your attachments.
shambhu_gita::89.simple_insight: Attachment grows from what your mind holds onto from past actions.
shambhu_gita::89.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that just as memories of your past actions remain engraved in your mind, those same memories create attachment. This shows how the inner mind holds the seeds of craving based on past deeds.
shambhu_gita::89.modern_relevance: When you replay past mistakes or successes in your mind, you feel drawn to or repelled by them, shaping your attachments today.
shambhu_gita::89.insight: It teaches you to see attachment as a natural imprint of past actions, not a fixed identity.

shambhu_gita::90.verse_sanskrit:
तदासक्त्यनुरूपेषु विश्येर्षु निरन्तरम् ।
प्रसज्जन्तेऽभितो जीवाः तदासक्त्यनुसारतः ॥
shambhu_gita::90.verse_hindi: उसी आसक्ति के अनुसार जीव उसी आसक्ति सम्बन्धीय विषयों में निरन्तर चारों ओर से जकड़े रहते हैं
shambhu_gita::90.english_translation: Living beings, bound by their attachments, remain constantly entangled in objects corresponding to those attachments.
shambhu_gita::90.translation_literal: तदा (then) असक्त्य (attachment) अनुरूपेषु (according) विषयेषु (objects) निरन्तरम् (constantly) प्रसज्जन्ते (entangled) अभितः (all around) जीवाः (living beings) तदा असक्त्य अनुसारतः (according to that attachment)
shambhu_gita::90.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::90.essence: Attachments bind living beings continuously to matching objects all around them.
shambhu_gita::90.simple_meaning: You get caught up in things that match your attachments, unable to break free.
shambhu_gita::90.simple_insight: It feels like being surrounded and held by what you desire or cling to.
shambhu_gita::90.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how living beings are continuously caught in objects or situations that match their inner attachments, showing how the mind’s desires keep it bound and restless.
shambhu_gita::90.modern_relevance: You find yourself repeatedly distracted by the same habits or desires, unable to focus because your attachments pull you in every direction.
shambhu_gita::90.insight: Recognize how your attachments create repetitive patterns that keep your mind restless and reactive.

shambhu_gita::91.verse_hindi: आसक्ति चित्त की सहायता से मन में ही उत्पन्न होती है। मन और चित्तरूपी स्त्री पुरुष के संगम से संसार में
shambhu_gita::91.english_translation: Attachment arises certainly in the mind with the help of the mind and consciousness, born from the union of the mind and consciousness in the world.
shambhu_gita::91.translation_literal: आसक्तचित्तसाहाय्यान् (attachment-mind-help) मनस् (mind) उत्पद्यते (arises) ध्रुवम् (certainly) । दम्पत्यः (couple) सङ्गमात् (from union) लोके (in the world) मनः (mind) चित्तस्वरूपयोः (and consciousness-forms) ॥
shambhu_gita::91.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::91.essence: Attachment arises inside your mind from the union of mind and consciousness.
shambhu_gita::91.simple_meaning: Attachment arises in your mind when the restless mind and inner consciousness come together.
shambhu_gita::91.simple_insight: You feel how your own mind and inner state create attachments, not outside things.
shambhu_gita::91.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that attachment is not external but emerges inside us when the restless mind (manas) and consciousness (chitta) unite. This is a key moment revealing the inner origin of emotional bonds in the world.
shambhu_gita::91.modern_relevance: You notice how your worries and desires arise when your busy mind clings to fleeting thoughts and feelings.
shambhu_gita::91.insight: It teaches you to observe that attachment is a product of your own mind mixing with inner awareness, not an external force.

shambhu_gita::92.verse_sanskrit:
आसक्तेजीयते जन्म नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
प्रजातन्तुं यथा पुत्रः संरक्षँसल्लभते पितुः ॥
shambhu_gita::92.verse_hindi: आसक्ति का जन्म होता है। इसमें विचार नहीं करना चाहिये। पुत्र जिस प्रकार पिता के प्रजातन्तु की रक्षा करके
shambhu_gita::92.english_translation: Attachment arises naturally and should not be overanalyzed; just as a son instinctively protects his father's lineage.
shambhu_gita::92.translation_literal: आसक्ते (attachment) जीयते (is born) जन्म (naturally) नात्र (not here) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (thinking) । प्रजातन्तुं (lineage) यथा (just as) पुत्रः (son) संरक्षँस (protects) अल्लभते (attains) पितुः (father's) ॥
shambhu_gita::92.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::92.essence: Attachment arises naturally and cannot be undone by mere reasoning.
shambhu_gita::92.simple_meaning: Attachment naturally arises in the mind and cannot be controlled by reasoning, just as a son instinctively protects his father's family.
shambhu_gita::92.simple_insight: It’s okay to notice attachment without trying to force it away through thought.
shambhu_gita::92.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that attachment is born naturally and is not something to be dismantled by overthinking. Like a son who instinctively guards his father’s lineage, attachment arises without deliberate choice, showing its deep roots in human nature.
shambhu_gita::92.modern_relevance: You feel drawn to something or someone, and trying to analyze or control that feeling only makes it stronger.
shambhu_gita::92.insight: Accept attachment as a natural impulse instead of battling it intellectually, freeing your energy for wiser action.

shambhu_gita::93.verse_sanskrit:
तस्याधिकारमासक्तिविभ्राणा विषयाँस्तथा।
सृष्टिं वर्द्धयते शश्वदिह दैवीश्च मानवीम् ॥
shambhu_gita::93.verse_hindi: पिता के अधिकार को प्राप्त होता है उसी प्रकार आसक्ति इस संसार में विषयों को धारण करती हुई देवी और मानवी सृष्टि को विशेष रूप से अग्रसर करती है
shambhu_gita::93.english_translation: Attachment to rightful authority continuously nurtures both divine and human creation in this world.
shambhu_gita::93.translation_literal: तस्याधिकारम् (to his authority) आसक्ति-विभ्राणा (attachment holding) विषयान् (objects) तथा (thus) सृष्टिं (creation) वर्धयते (nurtures) शश्वत्-इह (always here) दैवी-इश् (divine) च (and) मानवीम् (human)
shambhu_gita::93.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::93.essence: Attachment to rightful responsibility is the force that nurtures all creation.
shambhu_gita::93.simple_meaning: When you hold on to your rightful role with dedication, it supports both divine and human life to grow and thrive.
shambhu_gita::93.simple_insight: There's strength in embracing your rightful place; it supports something greater than yourself.
shambhu_gita::93.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that just as a father’s rightful authority sustains his family, attachment to one's proper role or duty helps both divine and human realms to flourish and progress.
shambhu_gita::93.modern_relevance: You feel the pressure to take responsibility at work or home, and holding steady there creates growth beyond just yourself.
shambhu_gita::93.insight: Recognize that embracing your rightful responsibilities energizes not only your life but also the wider environment around you.

shambhu_gita::94.verse_sanskrit:
बुद्धिराज्यस्य सिद्धान्तमपरं वित्त किन्त्त्व हो ।
बुद्धयहङ्कारसंयोगादभावतत्त्वोदयो भवेत् ॥
shambhu_gita::94.verse_hindi: अहो! किन्तु बुद्धिराज्य का सिद्धान्त और है ऐसा जानो अहङ्कार और बुद्धि के संगम से भावतत्व का उदय होता है
shambhu_gita::94.english_translation: Know that the foundation of the kingdom of the discerning mind is different: it arises from the union of the sense of separate self and discernment, producing the essence of feeling.
shambhu_gita::94.translation_literal: बुद्धिराज्यस्य (of the kingdom of discernment) सिद्धान्तम् (foundation/principle) अपरम् (different/other) वित्त (is known) किन्त्त्व (but indeed) हो (ah) । बुद्धियः (of the discernment) अहङ्कार (sense of separate self) संयोजनाद्भावतत्त्वोदयो (from union arises the essence of feeling) भवेत् (comes to be) ॥
shambhu_gita::94.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::94.essence: Clarity arises as feeling when the separate self and discernment unite.
shambhu_gita::94.simple_meaning: True understanding comes from the union of your sense of self and your discerning mind, creating the essence of feeling or experience.
shambhu_gita::94.simple_insight: You feel clarity when your sense of self and wisdom merge into a deeper experience.
shambhu_gita::94.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva explains that the foundation of true wisdom is not just intellect alone but emerges when the sense of separate self (Ahamkara) combines with discernment (Buddhi), generating the essential feeling that grounds understanding.
shambhu_gita::94.modern_relevance: When you fully engage both your identity and your thoughtful mind, your insights become more meaningful and felt deeply, not just known abstractly.
shambhu_gita::94.insight: It teaches you to recognize that clear understanding arises from the interplay between your self-perception and discriminating mind.

shambhu_gita::95.verse_sanskrit:
भावोऽपि द्विवियो ज्ञेयः शुद्धाशुद्धप्रभेदव:।
भावोऽशुद्धस्तयोबुद्धिं विधत्ते विषयाकृतिम् ॥
shambhu_gita::95.verse_hindi: शुद्ध और अशुद्ध भेद मे भाव भी द्विविध हैं सो जानो। उनमें से अशुद्ध भाव वुद्धि को विषयवत् कर देता है
shambhu_gita::95.english_translation: Feelings too are of two kinds: pure and impure; impure feelings distort the discerning mind like objects do.
shambhu_gita::95.translation_literal: भावोऽपि (feeling also) द्विवियो (twofold) ज्ञेयः (to be known) शुद्धाशुद्धप्रभेदवः (pure and impure distinctions). भावोऽशुद्धः (impure feeling) तयोबुद्धिं (the discerning mind) विधत्ते (distorts) विषयाकृतिम् (like an object).
shambhu_gita::95.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::95.essence: Impure feelings distort the discerning mind just as distracting objects do.
shambhu_gita::95.simple_meaning: Feelings come in two types: pure ones that support clear understanding, and impure ones that confuse the mind like distractions.
shambhu_gita::95.simple_insight: You can notice how your feelings either clarify or cloud your perception right now.
shambhu_gita::95.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that feelings are not all the same—some are pure and support clarity, while impure feelings disturb the discerning mind by acting like distracting objects.
shambhu_gita::95.modern_relevance: In a tense conversation, your feelings may either help you listen clearly or distract you with bias and confusion.
shambhu_gita::95.insight: It teaches you to observe which feelings clarify your mind and which ones confuse it, improving your discernment.

shambhu_gita::96.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धो भावः क्रमाचित्तं कुर्वाणो निर्मलं तथा ।
बुद्धिं ब्रह्मपदं नूनं नयच्छान्ति प्रयच्छति ॥
shambhu_gita::96.verse_hindi: और शुद्ध भाव क्रमशः अन्तःकरण को मल रहित करता हुआ बुद्धि को ब्रह्मपद में पहुंचाकर ही शान्ति प्रदान करता है
shambhu_gita::96.english_translation: A pure attitude gradually cleanses the inner consciousness, leading the discerning mind to the supreme reality and granting peace.
shambhu_gita::96.translation_literal: शुद्धो (pure) भावः (attitude) क्रम (gradually) अचित्तं (mind/unconscious) कुर्वाणो (making) निर्मलं (clean) तथा (thus) बुद्धिं (discerning mind) ब्रह्मपदं (supreme reality) नूनं (indeed) नयच्छन्ति (leads) प्रयच्छति (gives) ।
shambhu_gita::96.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::96.essence: A pure attitude gradually cleanses your mind and leads your wisdom to peace.
shambhu_gita::96.simple_meaning: A pure and sincere attitude slowly cleanses your inner mind, helping your discerning mind reach the supreme reality and find peace.
shambhu_gita::96.simple_insight: You can feel peace grow as your inner state becomes clearer and purer.
shambhu_gita::96.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that a pure attitude gradually cleanses the inner mind (chitta), removing impurities and confusion. This purification allows the discerning mind (buddhi) to reach Brahman, the supreme reality, resulting in true inner peace.
shambhu_gita::96.modern_relevance: When you steadily clear your mental clutter and emotional noise, your mind can settle into clarity, bringing calm and true peace.
shambhu_gita::96.insight: It teaches you to nurture purity in your inner state so your discernment naturally leads to peace.

shambhu_gita::97.verse_sanskrit:
नन्दासक्तेर्वशा जीवा अथवा भावनोदिताः।
एतत्तत्त्वद्रयस्यैव साहाय्यात्कर्म कुर्वते ॥
shambhu_gita::97.verse_hindi: जीव या तो आसक्ति के वशीभूत हो या भावप्रणोदित होकर ही, इन्हीं दो तत्वों की सहायता से ही कर्म करते हैं।
shambhu_gita::97.english_translation: Living beings act either compelled by attachment or driven by emotion, performing actions supported only by these two forces.
shambhu_gita::97.translation_literal: नन्द (attachment) आसक्तेर् (by attachment) वशा (compelled) जीवा (living beings) अथवा (or) भाव (emotion) उदिताः (arisen) एतत् (this) तत्त्व (principle) द्रयस्यैव (only by the two) साहाय्यात् (help) कर्म (action) कुर्वते (do)
shambhu_gita::97.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::97.essence: All actions arise from either attachment or emotional impulse as their foundation.
shambhu_gita::97.simple_meaning: You act because you are either caught by attachment or moved by emotion; these two forces support all your actions.
shambhu_gita::97.simple_insight: Recognizing that attachment and emotion guide your actions brings clarity to your motivations.
shambhu_gita::97.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that all living beings perform actions motivated by either attachment, which binds them, or by arising emotions. These two forces are the fundamental supports behind every action a person takes.
shambhu_gita::97.modern_relevance: You notice how many times your decisions come from wanting something or feeling strongly, even when you don’t realize it.
shambhu_gita::97.insight: It teaches you to observe whether your actions arise from craving attachment or emotional impulse, helping you gain control over your choices.

shambhu_gita::98.verse_sanskrit:
कायिकं याचिकञ्चैव तथा मानसमेव च ।
आसक्तौ किन्तु वैवश्यं भावे स्वातन्त्र्यमस्ति ह ॥
shambhu_gita::98.verse_hindi: शरीरिक, वाचनिक और मानसिक कर्म करते हैं। आसक्ति में विवशता है परन्तु भाव में स्वाधीनता है
shambhu_gita::98.english_translation: The body, speech, and mind perform actions. Attachment creates compulsion, but your inner feelings remain free.
shambhu_gita::98.translation_literal: कायिकं (bodily) / याचिकञ्चैव (and also verbal) / तथा (and) / मानसमेव (mental indeed) / च (also) / आसक्तौ (in attachment) / किन्तु (but) / वैवश्यं (compulsion) / भावे (in feeling) / स्वातन्त्र्यमस्ति (there is freedom) / ह (indeed)
shambhu_gita::98.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::98.essence: Your actions may feel forced but your inner feelings can stay free.
shambhu_gita::98.simple_meaning: Your body, speech, and mind carry out actions. Though attachment makes you feel forced, your inner feelings can stay free.
shambhu_gita::98.simple_insight: You can feel free inside even when your actions are tied to attachments.
shambhu_gita::98.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that while your body, speech, and mind perform actions, attachment to these actions creates a sense of compulsion. Yet, the inner feeling or attitude behind these actions holds freedom from this compulsion.
shambhu_gita::98.modern_relevance: You might feel trapped by daily routines or expectations, but your inner attitude can remain untouched and free.
shambhu_gita::98.insight: Notice that your inner feelings can stay independent of the compulsions your body and mind face.

shambhu_gita::99.verse_sanskrit:
आनन्याद्विषयाणान्तु बहुशाखासमन्विता ।
आसक्तिर्विद्यते नूनं शुद्धो भावो न तादृशः ॥
shambhu_gita::99.verse_hindi: आसक्ति बहु शाखा युक्त ही है क्योंकि विषय अनन्त हैं परन्तु शुद्धभाव वैसा नहीं है
shambhu_gita::99.english_translation: Attachment indeed has many branches because the objects are countless, but pure feeling is not like that.
shambhu_gita::99.translation_literal: आनन्याद्विषयाणान्तु (because of countless objects) बहुशाखासमन्विता (attachment has many branches) । आसक्तिर्विद्यते (attachment exists) नूनं (certainly) शुद्धो (pure) भावो (feeling) न (not) तादृशः (like that) ॥
shambhu_gita::99.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::99.essence: Attachment multiplies with desires; pure feeling remains singular and undivided.
shambhu_gita::99.simple_meaning: Attachment arises because desires are many, but pure feeling is simple and undivided.
shambhu_gita::99.simple_insight: You can feel deeply without being pulled into countless desires.
shambhu_gita::99.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that attachment has many forms because desires are endless. However, a pure inner feeling or state is not fragmented by these desires; it remains whole and undisturbed.
shambhu_gita::99.modern_relevance: You scroll through endless distractions, feeling pulled in every direction, yet a calm, pure feeling can remain untouched by this flood.
shambhu_gita::99.insight: You learn to recognize that many cravings create scattered attachments, but cultivating a pure feeling lets you stay unified and steady.

shambhu_gita::100.verse_sanskrit:
एकाद्वैतदशां नेतुभीष्टेऽसौ नात्र संशयः।
यतो ब्रह्मपदं विज्ञाः ! विद्यनेऽद्वैतमेव हि ॥
shambhu_gita::100.verse_hindi: वह एक अद्वैत दशा को प्राप्त करा सकता है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं; क्योंकि हे विज्ञों! ब्रह्मपद अद्वैत ही है
shambhu_gita::100.english_translation: There is no doubt that one who attains the non-dual state reaches the supreme reality; know, O wise ones, that the supreme reality is indeed non-dual.
shambhu_gita::100.translation_literal: एकाद्वैतदशां (non-dual state) नेतुभीष्टेऽसौ (one who attains) नात्र (there is no) संशयः (doubt) यतो (because) ब्रह्मपदं (supreme reality) विज्ञाः (O wise ones) विद्यनेऽद्वैतमेव (indeed non-dual) हि (is)
shambhu_gita::100.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::100.essence: The supreme reality is nothing other than the non-dual state itself.
shambhu_gita::100.simple_meaning: The highest state you can reach is complete oneness without division, the supreme reality itself.
shambhu_gita::100.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing that ultimate reality is unified and undivided.
shambhu_gita::100.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that achieving the non-dual state—the experience beyond all separation—is the sure path to realizing the supreme reality. This teaching addresses wise seekers, affirming no doubt about this profound truth.
shambhu_gita::100.modern_relevance: When your mind stops dividing experience into 'me' and 'other,' you glimpse the whole, dissolving inner conflict.
shambhu_gita::100.insight: It shifts your view from fragmented self to recognizing an undivided, unified reality.

shambhu_gita::101.verse_sanskrit:
आसत्त्या कार्यकर्त्तारो जीवाः प्रारब्धयोगतः।
श्रीगुरोर्देवतानां वा प्रमादादेव सर्वथा ॥
shambhu_gita::101.verse_hindi: आसक्ति से काम करनेवाले जीव सर्वथा प्रारब्ध की सहायता, श्रीगुरुदेव की कृपा अथवा देवताओं की कृपा से ही
shambhu_gita::101.english_translation: Beings attached to their actions succeed only through past karma, the grace of the revered teacher, or divine beings' favor.
shambhu_gita::101.translation_literal: आसत्त्या (by attachment) कार्यकर्त्तारो (doers of actions) जीवाः (beings) प्रारब्धयोगतः (by past karma) श्रीगुरोः (of the revered teacher) देवतानां (of divine beings) वा (or) प्रमादात् (through grace) एव (only) सर्वथा (completely)
shambhu_gita::101.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::101.essence: Attachment to action means results depend on past karma or grace beyond your control.
shambhu_gita::101.simple_meaning: When you act with attachment, your results depend on past karma, the teacher’s kindness, or divine favor.
shambhu_gita::101.simple_insight: You feel less alone knowing results come from forces beyond your current efforts.
shambhu_gita::101.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that beings attached to their actions do not fully control the outcomes; these depend on past karma, the favor of the revered teacher, or divine beings. This reminds Arjuna that effort alone isn't enough.
shambhu_gita::101.modern_relevance: You push hard on a project but realize success also depends on past work, mentors’ support, or unseen factors.
shambhu_gita::101.insight: You shift from expecting full control to recognizing the wider influences shaping your results.

shambhu_gita::102.verse_sanskrit:
पाशतुल्याद्धि विषयात स्वान्निवर्तयितुं क्षमाः।
अन्यथा विषये तेषां प्रक्तिसत्व  निश्चिता ॥
shambhu_gita::102.verse_hindi: पाशतुल्य विषय से अपने को बचा सकते हैं, नहीं तो उसमें उनका फंसना निश्चित है
shambhu_gita::102.english_translation: Those who are like a noose can free themselves from sense objects; otherwise, their nature surely remains attached to those objects.
shambhu_gita::102.translation_literal: पाशतुल्याद्धि (like a noose) विषयात (from sense objects) स्वान्निवर्तयितुं (to withdraw oneself) क्षमाः (able). अन्यथा (otherwise) विषये (in the objects) तेषां (their) प्रक्तिसत्व (nature) निश्चिता (certain).
shambhu_gita::102.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::102.essence: Only firm self-restraint frees you from attachment; otherwise, your nature remains bound.
shambhu_gita::102.simple_meaning: You can only free yourself from attachment to desires by firmly restraining yourself; otherwise, your nature remains caught in them.
shambhu_gita::102.simple_insight: There's hope in firm resolve — only strong effort can break old attachments.
shambhu_gita::102.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that sense objects can trap people unless they have the strength to hold firm like a noose. Without this firm restraint, their nature inevitably stays bound to desires.
shambhu_gita::102.modern_relevance: You try to stop scrolling but your mind keeps drifting back to distractions unless you firmly decide to resist.
shambhu_gita::102.insight: It teaches you to hold firm mental boundaries against distractions to detach from craving.

shambhu_gita::103.verse_sanskrit:
किन्तु शुद्धस्य भावस्य साहाय्यात्कार्यकारिणः।
भाग्यवन्तो न सज्जन्ते विषयेषु कदाचन ॥
shambhu_gita::103.verse_hindi: परन्तु शुद्ध भाव की सहायता से कर्म करने वाले भाग्यवान को  विषयों में कदापि नहीं फंसना चाहिए
shambhu_gita::103.english_translation: However, the fortunate who act with pure intention should never become entangled in worldly things.
shambhu_gita::103.translation_literal: किन्तु (however) शुद्धस्य (of pure) भावस्य (intention) साहाय्यात्कार्यकारिणः (by the help of those who act) भाग्यवन्तो (the fortunate) न (not) सज्जन्ते (become entangled) विषयेषु (in worldly things) कदाचन (ever)
shambhu_gita::103.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::103.essence: Acting with pure intention protects you from being caught in worldly distractions.
shambhu_gita::103.simple_meaning: Acting with a pure heart and clear intention protects you from being caught in desires or distractions.
shambhu_gita::103.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that pure intentions shield you from getting lost in fleeting things.
shambhu_gita::103.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when someone acts with a pure and focused heart, supported by clear intention, they are fortunate because they avoid getting distracted or trapped by worldly desires and attachments.
shambhu_gita::103.modern_relevance: You start a project with honest purpose, and even when challenges arise, your focus keeps you from getting overwhelmed by irrelevant distractions.
shambhu_gita::103.insight: It teaches you to anchor your actions in purity of intent, which prevents distraction and entanglement with passing desires.

shambhu_gita::104.verse_sanskrit:
उत्तरोत्तरमेतेषां सर्वथोर्दध्वगतिर्भवेत् ।
संगृहीता हि संस्काराः पूर्वजन्माने यादृशाः ॥
shambhu_gita::104.verse_hindi: उत्तरोत्तर उनकी सर्वथा अवगति होती रहती है। जीव ने पूर्व जन्म में जैसे संस्कार संग्रह किये हैं
shambhu_gita::104.english_translation: The impressions from past lives keep accumulating and deeply influence the present.
shambhu_gita::104.translation_literal: उत्तरोत्तर (gradually) मेतेषां (of these) सर्वथा (completely) उर्दध्वगतिर्भवेत् (there is a movement/flow) / संगृहीता (collected) हि (indeed) संस्काराः (impressions) पूर्वजन्माने (from previous births) यादृशाः (such as)
shambhu_gita::104.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::104.essence: Past-life impressions continuously build and shape present experience.
shambhu_gita::104.simple_meaning: Impressions from previous lives build up continuously and shape the present experience.
shambhu_gita::104.simple_insight: You carry a deep history of past experiences shaping who you are now.
shambhu_gita::104.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta explains that the impressions or tendencies formed in past lives accumulate steadily, influencing the current life’s circumstances and reactions.
shambhu_gita::104.modern_relevance: Your habits, fears, and preferences may stem from deep past patterns you never consciously noticed.
shambhu_gita::104.insight: Recognize that many present tendencies come from accumulated past impressions beyond current awareness.

shambhu_gita::105.verse_sanskrit:
आसक्तिस्तादृशी जीवे प्रादुरेप्यनि निश्चितम्।
तस्या एवानुसारेण जीववर्गे जनिप्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::105.verse_hindi: उसी के अनुसार उसमें आसक्ति प्रकट होगी और उसी आसक्ति के अनुसार जीवों में
shambhu_gita::105.english_translation: Attachment definitely arises in a living being according to that same attachment present in its kind.
shambhu_gita::105.translation_literal: आसक्तिस्तादृशी (attachment like that) / जीवे (in the living being) / प्रादुरेप्यनि (surely arises) / निश्चितम् (certainly) / तस्या (of that) / एवानुसारेण (by the same manner) / जीववर्गे (in the class of beings) / जनिप्यते (is born, arises)
shambhu_gita::105.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::105.essence: Attachments arise naturally by reflecting the attachments in the environment you belong to.
shambhu_gita::105.simple_meaning: Attachment in a living being arises following the type of attachment it observes or absorbs from its surroundings or kind.
shambhu_gita::105.simple_insight: You feel how your attachments are shaped by what you live with and see around you.
shambhu_gita::105.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the form of attachment a being experiences is not random but follows the pattern of attachments found in its environment or species. This teaching points to how the mind and emotions are influenced by their context.
shambhu_gita::105.modern_relevance: You notice how your cravings and attachments often echo what people around you value or seek, shaping your desires unconsciously.
shambhu_gita::105.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your attachments are influenced by your environment, helping you question and possibly reshape them.

shambhu_gita::106.verse_sanskrit:
हेयोपादेयताज्ञानं नास्ति कोऽप्यत्र संशयः ।
आसक्तिमूलके चैवमसद्भाचे प्रसज्य वै ॥
shambhu_gita::106.verse_hindi: हेय और उपादेय का विचार उत्पन्न होगा। इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं है और इस प्रकार से आसक्ति मूलक असदुभाव में फंसकर ही
shambhu_gita::106.english_translation: There is no doubt that knowledge must be rejected and avoided here, for it arises from attachment and leads to false existence.
shambhu_gita::106.translation_literal: हेय (to be rejected) / उपादेय (to be avoided) / तै (there) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / नास्ति (is not) / कोऽपि (anyone) / अत्र (here) / संशयः (doubt) / आसक्ति-मूलके (rooted in attachment) / च (and) / एव (certainly) / असद्भाचे (false nature) / प्रसज्य (being born) / वै (indeed)
shambhu_gita::106.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::106.essence: Knowledge rooted in attachment creates falsehood and must be abandoned.
shambhu_gita::106.simple_meaning: Knowledge that arises from attachment should be rejected because it leads to false understanding and illusion.
shambhu_gita::106.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing that some knowledge only traps you deeper in illusion.
shambhu_gita::106.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that certain kinds of knowledge, those born from attachment, must be abandoned because they create false views of existence, binding the seeker to illusion rather than freedom.
shambhu_gita::106.modern_relevance: You notice how some beliefs or ideas you cling to only confuse you and keep you stuck in worry or false hopes.
shambhu_gita::106.insight: It teaches you to question knowledge that deepens attachment and to seek understanding that frees you.

shambhu_gita::107.verse_sanskrit:
जीवो वन्धदशातः स्वं रक्षितुं नैव शक्ष्यति ।
सम्बद्धेन मया साई सद्भावेन तु संयुतः ॥
shambhu_gita::107.verse_hindi: जीव बन्धन दशा से अपने को बचा नहीं सकेगा। परन्तु हे विज्ञों! सत्भाव जिसका सम्बन्ध मेरे साथ है उसके साथ युक्त होकर
shambhu_gita::107.english_translation: A living being cannot free itself from the state of bondage; but one united with me in true nature is connected through goodness.
shambhu_gita::107.translation_literal: जीवो (living being) / वन्धदशातः (from bondage state) / स्वं (self) / रक्षितुं (to protect) / नैव (not) / शक्ष्यति (is able) / सम्बद्धेन (connected) / मया (by me) / साई (that) / सद्भावेन (by true nature) / तु (but) / संयुतः (joined)
shambhu_gita::107.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::107.essence: You cannot escape bondage alone; true connection with the divine changes that.
shambhu_gita::107.simple_meaning: No one can free themselves alone from the cycle of bondage, but those joined in true nature with the divine find connection beyond it.
shambhu_gita::107.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing you don’t have to struggle alone for freedom.
shambhu_gita::107.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that living beings cannot break free from the cycle of bondage by themselves. However, those who unite with him in sincere nature and goodness are joined in a way that transcends this limitation.
shambhu_gita::107.modern_relevance: You might feel stuck in harmful patterns or struggles you can't escape alone; finding a connection beyond yourself brings real support.
shambhu_gita::107.insight: It teaches you to seek support beyond your isolated efforts, embracing connection with something greater.

shambhu_gita::108.verse_sanskrit:
यत्कर्म कुरुते जीवः सततं भावशुद्धित: ।
हेतुतां बहते विज्ञाः ! मुक्तेस्तत्कर्म निश्चितम् ॥
shambhu_gita::108.verse_hindi: निरन्तरं भावशुद्धि द्वारा जो कर्म जीव करता है वह कर्म अवश्य ही मुक्ति का कारण होता है।
shambhu_gita::108.english_translation: Any action performed by a being with constant purity of mind surely leads to freedom.
shambhu_gita::108.translation_literal: यत् (which) / कर्म (action) / कुरुते (does) / जीवः (the living being) / सततं (constantly) / भावशुद्धित: (with purity of mind) / हेतुतां (cause) / बहते (flows) / विज्ञाः (the wise) / मुक्तेः (of freedom) / तत् (that) / कर्म (action) / निश्चितम् (certain)
shambhu_gita::108.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::108.essence: Constant purity of mind ensures every action leads to freedom.
shambhu_gita::108.simple_meaning: When you act with a mind that is always pure and clear, your actions naturally bring you freedom.
shambhu_gita::108.simple_insight: There's power in steady purity—your true freedom grows from it.
shambhu_gita::108.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that a living being who performs actions with continuous purity of mind inevitably causes those actions to become a path to liberation. This teaching comes in a moment emphasizing the essential connection between inner clarity and the result of freedom.
shambhu_gita::108.modern_relevance: You show up to your work or relationships with clear intentions and a calm mind; this steadiness transforms what you do into a source of personal freedom.
shambhu_gita::108.insight: It shifts your focus from external results to maintaining a pure inner state, making every action a step toward freedom.

shambhu_gita::109.verse_sanskrit:
पापकर्माप्यतः पुण्यं सद्भावेन समन्वितम् ।
एष मे निश्चयो विज्ञाः ! एषा ये धारणाऽस्त्यलम् ॥
shambhu_gita::109.verse_hindi: इस कारण सद्भावसे युक्त पापकर्म भी पुण्य हो जाता है हे विज्ञो ! यह मेरा निश्चय है।  और मेरी यही धारणा है।
shambhu_gita::109.english_translation: Therefore, even sinful actions joined with good intention become virtuous, learned one! This is my certainty and firm belief.
shambhu_gita::109.translation_literal: पापकर्मापि (even sinful actions) अथः (therefore) पुण्यं (virtuous) सद्भावेन (with good intention) समन्वितम् (joined) । एष (this) मे (my) निश्चयः (certainty) विज्ञाः (learned one) ! एषा (this) ये (which) धारणा (belief) अस्ति (is) अलम् (firm) ॥
shambhu_gita::109.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::109.essence: Sincere good intention can turn even wrong actions into virtuous ones.
shambhu_gita::109.simple_meaning: Actions that seem wrong can become good if done with sincere, positive intention.
shambhu_gita::109.simple_insight: Knowing your heart’s intention matters more than the act itself brings relief and hope.
shambhu_gita::109.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that even acts considered wrong gain virtue if performed with sincere goodwill. This challenges rigid ideas of good and bad, emphasizing intention over outcome.
shambhu_gita::109.modern_relevance: You made a choice that felt wrong but meant well; this shows your true character, not just the mistake.
shambhu_gita::109.insight: It shifts your focus from judging acts to understanding the intentions behind them, encouraging compassionate self-reflection.

shambhu_gita::110.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मोऽस्ति मम सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मशक्तिः पितृव्रजाः !।
नाऽयं स्थूलपदार्थोऽस्ति निखिलेन्द्रियगोचरः ॥
shambhu_gita::110.verse_hindi: हे पितृवृन्दो ! धर्म मेरी सूक्ष्माति सूक्ष्म शक्ति है, यह सभी इन्द्रियो से जानने योग्य स्थूल पदार्थ नहीं है।
shambhu_gita::110.english_translation: O ancestors, my dharma is an extremely subtle power; it is not a gross object perceived by the senses.
shambhu_gita::110.translation_literal: धर्मोऽस्ति (dharma is) मम (my) सूक्ष्माति-सूक्ष्मशक्तिः (extremely subtle power) पितृव्रजाः (O ancestors) । नाऽयं (not this) स्थूलपदार्थः (gross object) अस्ति (is) निखिलेन्द्रियगोचरः (perceptible by all senses) ॥
shambhu_gita::110.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::110.essence: True purpose is a subtle power beyond physical perception.
shambhu_gita::110.simple_meaning: Your true purpose is a very subtle force, not something physical or detectable by the senses.
shambhu_gita::110.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your deepest purpose is beyond what can be measured or seen.
shambhu_gita::110.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that dharma is not a simple physical thing but an extremely subtle power that cannot be perceived by the senses. This sets the stage for understanding dharma as an inner, transcendent force.
shambhu_gita::110.modern_relevance: You might feel lost measuring your worth by visible achievements, but your deepest purpose is beyond what anyone can see or touch.
shambhu_gita::110.insight: It teaches you to look beyond surface appearances and sense-based judgments to recognize your true calling as subtle and profound.

shambhu_gita::111.verse_sanskrit:
नास्य स्थूलपदार्थेन सम्बन्ध स्थूल इप्यते ।
भावेन हि यदाऽधर्मे धर्मेण परिणम्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::111.verse_hindi: और न इसका स्थूल पदार्थ से स्थूल सम्बन्ध है । जब भाव से ही धर्म अधर्म में
shambhu_gita::111.english_translation: There is no gross connection with gross objects here; when the inner attitude turns from dharma to adharma, that is the real change.
shambhu_gita::111.translation_literal: नास्य (not for this) / स्थूलपदार्थेन (with gross objects) / सम्बन्ध (connection) / स्थूल (gross) / इप्यते (exists) / भावेन (by attitude) / हि (indeed) / यदा (when) / अधर्मे (in adharma) / धर्मेण (from dharma) / परिणम्यते (it turns)
shambhu_gita::111.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::111.essence: Moral change happens in your inner attitude, not through physical things.
shambhu_gita::111.simple_meaning: The real shift from right to wrong happens in your inner attitude, not in physical things.
shambhu_gita::111.simple_insight: You feel that true change is about how you see and feel, not what you physically have.
shambhu_gita::111.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that shifting from dharma to adharma is not about external objects but about an inner change in feeling or attitude. This moment marks where true moral transformation takes place.
shambhu_gita::111.modern_relevance: You might blame your environment for your struggles, but real change happens when your inner feelings shift, not when things around you change.
shambhu_gita::111.insight: It shifts your focus from external conditions to the inner attitude as the source of ethical change.

shambhu_gita::112.verse_sanskrit:
अधर्मस्यापि धर्मे वै परिणामो यदा भवेत् ।
एष एव तदा धर्म-सूक्ष्मत्वपरिचायकः ॥
shambhu_gita::112.verse_hindi: और अधर्म धर्म में निश्चय ही परिणत होता है तो यही धर्म के सूक्ष्म स्वरूप का परिचायक है।
shambhu_gita::112.english_translation: When even unrighteousness inevitably transforms into righteousness, this reveals the subtle nature of dharma.
shambhu_gita::112.translation_literal: अधर्मस्यापि (of unrighteousness also) धर्मे (into righteousness) वै (indeed) परिणामो (transformation/result) यदा (when) भवेत् (happens). एष (this) एव (indeed) तदा (then) धर्म-सूक्ष्मत्वपरिचायकः (indicator of dharma's subtlety) ॥
shambhu_gita::112.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::112.essence: Even apparent wrong leads naturally back to right, revealing dharma’s subtle nature.
shambhu_gita::112.simple_meaning: Sometimes what looks like wrong action naturally turns into right action, showing dharma’s subtle, guiding presence.
shambhu_gita::112.simple_insight: There is hope and trust in the process, even when things seem off track.
shambhu_gita::112.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that dharma is so subtle that even actions appearing wrongful eventually transform into righteousness, revealing the profound interconnectedness of right and wrong in life’s unfolding.
shambhu_gita::112.modern_relevance: After making a tough decision that felt wrong, you see its consequences lead to something good you hadn’t expected.
shambhu_gita::112.insight: It teaches you to see that apparent mistakes can serve the deeper purpose of your life’s path.

shambhu_gita::113.verse_sanskrit:
मम शक्तिर्दिधा भिन्ना विद्याऽविद्यामभेदतः। 
धर्माधर्मसुसम्बन्धस्ताभ्यां सार्द्ध  हि विद्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::113.verse_hindi: मेरी शक्ति के विद्या और अविद्या नामी, दो भेदों के साथ ही धर्म और अधर्म का सम्बन्ध है
shambhu_gita::113.english_translation: My power appears divided as knowledge and ignorance, just as dharma and adharma are closely linked.
shambhu_gita::113.translation_literal: मम (my) शक्तिर्दिधा (power divided) भिन्ना (distinct) विद्याऽविद्या (knowledge-ignorance) अभेदतः (without difference) धर्माधर्मसुसम्बन्धः (dharma-adharma close connection) ताभ्यां (between them) सार्ध (together) हि (indeed) विद्यते (exists)
shambhu_gita::113.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::113.essence: True power includes both knowing and not knowing, inseparably linked.
shambhu_gita::113.simple_meaning: The divine power is not simply knowledge or ignorance but holds both closely connected like right and wrong.
shambhu_gita::113.simple_insight: You can find power in holding opposites together without needing to separate them.
shambhu_gita::113.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that his own power manifests as two states—knowledge and ignorance—which are not truly separate. Similarly, dharma (right conduct) and adharma (wrong conduct) are intertwined, showing the complexity beneath appearances.
shambhu_gita::113.modern_relevance: Sometimes your mind feels torn between clarity and confusion, but both are part of your inner strength working together.
shambhu_gita::113.insight: It shifts your view from seeing knowledge and ignorance as enemies to seeing them as parts of a unified power.

shambhu_gita::114.verse_sanskrit:
एतस्यानुभवं सम्यगधर्मज्ञा एवं कुर्वते ।
संवर्द्धयत आसक्तिर्नन्वसद्भावमलिका ॥
shambhu_gita::114.verse_hindi: इसका धर्मज्ञ व्यक्ति ही सम्यक् अनुभव करते हैं । संसार में असद्भाव  मूलक आसक्ति
shambhu_gita::114.english_translation: Only those who truly know dharma fully experience this; attachment rooted in falsehood grows in the world.
shambhu_gita::114.translation_literal: एतस्यानुभवं (of this experience) सम्यगधर्मज्ञा (truly-knowing dharma) एवं (thus) कुर्वते (do) । संवर्द्धयत (grows) आसक्तिः (attachment) नन्व (otherwise) असद्भावम् (false nature) अलिका (rooted in) ॥
shambhu_gita::114.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::114.essence: True understanding of dharma reveals and dissolves attachments born of falsehood.
shambhu_gita::114.simple_meaning: Only those who deeply understand what is right truly experience this; attachments based on falsehood grow in the world.
shambhu_gita::114.simple_insight: Knowing what is truly right reveals where your attachments are illusions.
shambhu_gita::114.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that only a person who truly understands dharma—the right way to be—can fully experience this truth, while attachments based on false or unstable ideas continue to grow among others.
shambhu_gita::114.modern_relevance: When you face desires that pull you forward, knowing your true values helps you see which attachments are just illusions you can let go.
shambhu_gita::114.insight: It teaches you to recognize attachments rooted in illusion and dissolve them through true understanding.

shambhu_gita::115.verse_sanskrit:
अविद्यायाः सदा विज्ञाः ! प्रभावं भृरिशो भवे।
किन्तु मद्युक्तसद्भावात्मकं कर्म निरन्तरम् ॥
shambhu_gita::115.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञो ! सदा अविद्या के प्रभाव को अत्यन्त ही बढ़ाती है किन्तु मुझसे युक्त सद्भावात्मक कर्म निरन्तर
shambhu_gita::115.english_translation: O wise one! Ignorance always greatly increases its influence, but actions connected to me with true attitude continue steadily.
shambhu_gita::115.translation_literal: अविद्यायाः (of ignorance) सदा (always) विज्ञाः (O wise one) ! प्रभावं (influence) भृरिशो (greatly) भवे (becomes) । किन्तु (but) मद्युक्तसद्भावात्मकं (connected-to-me true-attitude) कर्म (action) निरन्तरम् (continues) ॥
shambhu_gita::115.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::115.essence: True, sincere action connected to the divine persists even as ignorance spreads.
shambhu_gita::115.simple_meaning: Ignorance tends to increase its power, but actions done with true connection to the divine continue steadily without stopping.
shambhu_gita::115.simple_insight: There is strength in steady, sincere action even as confusion grows around you.
shambhu_gita::115.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses a wise listener, explaining that while ignorance can expand its influence, actions performed with sincere connection to Shiva remain constant and unbroken, emphasizing the power of devoted effort amidst confusion.
shambhu_gita::115.modern_relevance: You notice distractions and doubts growing around your work, yet keeping steady and true to your values carries you through.
shambhu_gita::115.insight: It teaches you to maintain steady, sincere effort despite increasing confusion or obstacles.

shambhu_gita::116.verse_sanskrit:
अल वर्द्धयते विद्याप्रभाव जगतीतले।
भावप्रभाव एतावान्महानस्ति पितृव्रजाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::116.verse_hindi: जगत में विद्या के 'प्रभाव को ही वृद्धि करते हैं । हे पितृगण ! भाव का प्रभाव इतना महान् है
shambhu_gita::116.english_translation: The influence of knowledge alone grows on the world's surface. O ancestors, the power of emotion is even greater.
shambhu_gita::116.translation_literal: अल (only) / वर्द्धयते (grows) / विद्याप्रभाव (influence of knowledge) / जगतीतले (on the world's surface) / भावप्रभाव (influence of emotion) / एतावान्महान (so great) / स्ति (is) / पितृव्रजाः (O ancestors)!
shambhu_gita::116.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::116.essence: Emotions influence the world more deeply than knowledge alone.
shambhu_gita::116.simple_meaning: Knowledge changes the world, but emotions influence it even more deeply.
shambhu_gita::116.simple_insight: You feel how your emotions quietly shape everything around you beyond facts.
shambhu_gita::116.detailed_meaning: In a teaching moment, Shiva points out to the ancestors that while knowledge impacts the world, the power of feelings is even greater, highlighting the unseen force emotions hold in shaping reality.
shambhu_gita::116.modern_relevance: You notice how your mood colors your day more than what you know or plan.
shambhu_gita::116.insight: It shifts focus from intellect alone to the profound impact of emotional energy on perception and action.

shambhu_gita::117.verse_sanskrit:
वलादयस्य जड़ो याति चैतन्यं महदद्भुतम् ।
जड़ायामपिमूर्तौ  वै येनैवाविर्भवाम्यहम् ॥
shambhu_gita::117.verse_hindi: कि उसके बल से जड़ महाभुत चैतन्य को प्राप्त होता है जिस कारण से ही मैं जड़ मूर्ति में भी निश्चय प्रकट होता हूं
shambhu_gita::117.english_translation: By that power, the inert great element attains consciousness, through which even in inert form I certainly manifest.
shambhu_gita::117.translation_literal: वलादयस्य (by the power) / जड़ो (inert) / याति (attains) / चैतन्यं (consciousness) / महदद्भुतम् (great element) / जड़ायाम् (in the inert) / अपि (also) / मूर्तौ (form) / वै (indeed) / येनैव (by which alone) / अविर्भवामि (I manifest) / अहम् (I)
shambhu_gita::117.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::117.essence: Consciousness exists even within what appears lifeless, revealing unity of all forms.
shambhu_gita::117.simple_meaning: The power behind all things brings consciousness even to what appears lifeless, and through that power, I appear in all forms.
shambhu_gita::117.simple_insight: There is a hidden life and awareness even in what looks lifeless and still.
shambhu_gita::117.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the great natural element, which seems lifeless, gains consciousness through a divine power. This same power allows Shiva to manifest even within inert forms, revealing the deep unity of life and form.
shambhu_gita::117.modern_relevance: You might see something ordinary and lifeless, but underneath, it holds potential and awareness you don’t immediately notice.
shambhu_gita::117.insight: Recognize that awareness underlies all appearances, shifting how you relate to the world’s forms.

shambhu_gita::118.verse_sanskrit:
अससमापि सत्यं स्यात् क्तं जीवहिताय वै ।
अधर्मों जायते धर्मः पशुहिंसा यथाऽवरे ॥
shambhu_gita::118.verse_hindi: मिथ्या भी सत्य हो जाता है जो कि जीवों के हित के लिये ही कहा गया हो । अधर्म धर्म हो जाता है, यथा-यश में पशुहिंसा
shambhu_gita::118.english_translation: Falsehood becomes true when said for the welfare of living beings. Wrong becomes right, just as harming animals is seen as a sin.
shambhu_gita::118.translation_literal: अस (not) / समापि (completely) / सत्यं (truth) / स्यात् (becomes) / क्तं (spoken words) / जीवहिताय (for living beings' welfare) / वै (indeed) / अधर्मों (unrighteousness) / जायते (arises) / धर्मः (righteousness) / पशुहिंसा (animal harm) / यथा (as) / अवरे (sin)
shambhu_gita::118.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::118.essence: Truth and wrongness depend on whether actions serve the welfare of living beings.
shambhu_gita::118.simple_meaning: Sometimes what seems false can be true if it helps living beings. Similarly, what seems wrong can be right depending on how it affects others.
shambhu_gita::118.simple_insight: You can feel relief in knowing that intent and outcome matter more than rigid rules.
shambhu_gita::118.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that truth and righteousness are not fixed but depend on the welfare of living beings. An act usually considered wrong, like harming animals, can be seen differently when the context or intention changes the meaning of right and wrong.
shambhu_gita::118.modern_relevance: You notice someone bending strict rules to protect a friend or family member, challenging your ideas of right and wrong.
shambhu_gita::118.insight: It shifts your mind from fixed rules to evaluating actions by their impact and intention.

shambhu_gita::119.verse_sanskrit:
यात्येवं भावसम्बन्धञ्चितन्यं जड़तामिह ! ।
सत्यं मिथ्या भवेद्धर्मो जायतेऽधर्मरूपभाक् ॥
shambhu_gita::119.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार इस संसार में भाव के सम्बन्ध से  चैतन्य जड़ सत्य असत्य और धर्म अधर्म हो जाता है
shambhu_gita::119.english_translation: In this world, through attachment to feelings, consciousness becomes inert, truth becomes false, and dharma appears as adharma.
shambhu_gita::119.translation_literal: याति (goes) एवं (thus) भाव (feeling) सम्बन्ध (relation) चित् (consciousness) अन्यं (other) जड़ता (inertia) इह (here) । सत्यं (truth) मिथ्या (false) भवेत् (becomes) धर्मः (dharma) जायते (arises) अधर्मरूप (adharma-form) भाक् (appears) ॥
shambhu_gita::119.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::119.essence: Attachment to feelings clouds awareness, reversing truth and right action.
shambhu_gita::119.simple_meaning: When you get caught in your feelings, your awareness dulls, and what is true and right can seem false and wrong.
shambhu_gita::119.simple_insight: You can feel confused when emotions blur what is real and right.
shambhu_gita::119.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how attachment to feelings can confuse the mind, making pure consciousness seem dull and turning truth into falsehood, and dharma into its opposite, adharma.
shambhu_gita::119.modern_relevance: You react strongly to a situation, and suddenly your clear judgment feels clouded, making good choices seem impossible.
shambhu_gita::119.insight: It teaches you to notice how feelings can distort your perception of truth and ethics.

shambhu_gita::120.verse_sanskrit:
भावशुद्धिसमायुक्तमसत्कर्म्मोप्यतो ध्रुवम् ।
आपद्ध्रमें भजत्येव सद्धर्मत्वं न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::120.verse_hindi: इसी करण भावशुद्धियुक्त असत् कर्म भी आसद्धर्म में निःसन्देह सद्धर्मरूप में परिणत होकर ही
shambhu_gita::120.english_translation: Even actions that seem wrong, when done with pure intention, surely transform into right conduct without doubt.
shambhu_gita::120.translation_literal: भावशुद्धि (with pure intention) / समायुक्तम् (joined) / असत्कर्म्म (wrong action) / उप्यतः (even though) / ध्रुवम् (certainly) / आपद्ध्रमें (in adverse conduct) / भजति (performs) / एव (indeed) / सद्धर्मत्वं (rightness of conduct) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::120.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::120.essence: Pure intention transforms even seemingly wrong actions into unquestionably right conduct.
shambhu_gita::120.simple_meaning: If you act with a pure heart, even actions that seem wrong become right and aligned with true purpose.
shambhu_gita::120.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing your good intentions can redeem your mistakes.
shambhu_gita::120.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that when actions arise from a pure intention, even those that outwardly seem wrong or adverse are transformed into right conduct, showing the power of inner motivation over external appearances.
shambhu_gita::120.modern_relevance: You made a mistake but acted sincerely. That honesty can change the meaning of your choice, making it right in deeper ways.
shambhu_gita::120.insight: It shifts your focus from judging actions by their appearance to valuing the purity of your motivation.

shambhu_gita::121.verse_sanskrit:
विधत्तेऽदश्च जीवानां मङ्गलं परमं सदा ।
गतिः सूक्ष्मास्ति धर्मस्य भवन्तोऽतः पितृवजाः!॥
shambhu_gita::121.verse_hindi: जीवों के लिये सदा परम मङ्गल विधायक होता है। धर्म की गति सूक्ष्म है अतः हे पितृगण!
shambhu_gita::121.english_translation: The highest auspiciousness is always appointed for living beings. The path of dharma is subtle, therefore, O ancestors!
shambhu_gita::121.translation_literal: विधत्तेऽदश्च (appoints always) / जीवानां (of living beings) / मङ्गलं (auspiciousness) / परमं (highest) / सदा (always) / गतिः (path) / सूक्ष्मास्ति (is subtle) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / भवन्तः (you are) / अतः (therefore) / पितृवजाः (O ancestors)!
shambhu_gita::121.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::121.essence: Your highest good is always present, though dharma’s path is subtle and requires trust.
shambhu_gita::121.simple_meaning: There is always a highest good appointed for all living beings. The path of dharma is delicate and not always obvious.
shambhu_gita::121.simple_insight: You can trust that your true well-being is always unfolding, even if you don’t see it clearly.
shambhu_gita::121.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that every living being is guided by a supreme auspiciousness. Dharma’s course is subtle and often hidden, requiring trust and attentiveness to follow it rightly.
shambhu_gita::121.modern_relevance: When life feels confusing or uncertain, remember that your deepest good is quietly being arranged, even if you can’t yet see how.
shambhu_gita::121.insight: It shifts your focus from needing clear signs to trusting subtle guidance toward your highest good.

shambhu_gita::122.verse_sanskrit:
कुर्युश्चेत् कर्मा मचित्ता भावशुद्धिपुरस्सरम् ।
अधिकुर्युस्तदावश्यं पूर्ण धर्म सनातनम् ॥
shambhu_gita::122.verse_hindi: आप सब भावशुद्धि पूर्वक भगतचित्त होकर यदि कर्म करोगे तो अवश्य सनातन धर्म के पूर्णाधिकार को प्राप्त कर सकोगे।
