shambhu_gita::173.english_translation: But, O ancestors, the supreme divine knowledge is subtle, profound, and invincible, filled with the powers of the subtle realm.
shambhu_gita::173.translation_literal: दुर्ज्ञेयैः (by the unknowable) / पितरः (ancestors) / किन्तु (but) / सूक्ष्मराज्यविभूतिभिः (by subtle realm powers) / पूर्णाऽधिदैवविद्याऽत्तिगुह्या (full supreme divine knowledge very secret) / दुर्जेयत्रैभवा (by invincible powers)
shambhu_gita::173.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::173.essence: True divine knowledge is subtle, deeply hidden, and invincible against being grasped prematurely.
shambhu_gita::173.simple_meaning: The supreme divine knowledge is very subtle, hidden, and protected by powerful forces that make it impossible to conquer.
shambhu_gita::173.simple_insight: Some truths are deeply hidden and protected, reminding you that not all knowledge is easily reached.
shambhu_gita::173.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the ancestors, explaining that the supreme divine knowledge is not easily grasped because it is subtle, deeply secret, and guarded by powerful forces from the subtle realm.
shambhu_gita::173.insight: Recognize that some essential wisdom requires patience and readiness before it can be understood or accessed.

shambhu_gita::174.verse_sanskrit:
यस्य किञ्चिद्रहस्यं वः संक्षेपावर्णयाम्यहम् ।
सावधानभवद्भिश्च श्रूयतां पितरोऽधुना ॥
shambhu_gita::174.verse_hindi: जिसका कुछ रहस्य संक्षेप से मैं आपसे कहता हूँ हे पितृगण ! इस समयं आपलोग सावधान होकर सुनो
shambhu_gita::174.english_translation: I briefly reveal a certain secret to you, O ancestors; now listen carefully.
shambhu_gita::174.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) किञ्चित् (some) रहस्यं (secret) वः (to you) संक्षेप (brief) आवर्णयामि (I reveal) अहम् (I) । सावधान (careful) भवद्भिः (by you) इश्रूयतां (let be heard) पितरः (ancestors) अधुना (now) ॥
shambhu_gita::174.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::174.essence: Important knowledge requires focused and careful listening.
shambhu_gita::174.simple_meaning: A speaker announces that a brief secret will now be revealed and asks the listeners to pay close attention.
shambhu_gita::174.simple_insight: There is value in pausing and paying close attention before important knowledge.
shambhu_gita::174.detailed_meaning: The narrator, Suta, prepares the assembly of sages (the ancestors) for an important teaching by Shiva, asking them to listen carefully as he shares a secret.
shambhu_gita::174.insight: It invites you to focus fully before receiving valuable knowledge, highlighting the power of attention.

shambhu_gita::175.verse_sanskrit:
असावेकाऽद्वितीयाऽपि श्यामा में प्रकृतिः सती ।
स्थलात्सूक्ष्मात्तुरीयाच कारणाद्रूपतस्तथा ॥
shambhu_gita::175.verse_hindi: मेरी प्रकृति श्यामा एक और अद्वितीय होकर भी स्थूल सूक्ष्म कारण और तुरीय रूप से
shambhu_gita::175.english_translation: My nature, Shyama, though one and without a second, manifests as gross, subtle, causal, and the fourth state.
shambhu_gita::175.translation_literal: असावेकाऽद्वितीयाऽपि (this one and without second) श्यामा (Shyama) में (in) प्रकृतिः (nature) सती (existing) । स्थलात् (gross) सूक्ष्मात् (subtle) तुरीयाच् (fourth state) कारणाद् (causal) रूपतस् (form) तथा (also) ॥
shambhu_gita::175.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::175.essence: One unique nature expresses as gross, subtle, causal, and transcendent forms simultaneously.
shambhu_gita::175.simple_meaning: Your true nature is one and unique, yet it shows itself in four forms: gross, subtle, causal, and beyond.
shambhu_gita::175.simple_insight: Knowing your nature includes many layers helps you feel connected to all aspects of life.
shambhu_gita::175.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to Shyama that although the divine nature is uniquely one, it manifests in four ways: the physical (gross), the subtle (mind and energy), the causal (origin), and the transcendent fourth state (beyond all forms). This reveals the complexity behind apparent unity.
shambhu_gita::175.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or scattered, remember your true nature is one, expressing in many ways beyond what you see.
shambhu_gita::175.insight: It teaches you to recognize unity within diversity, seeing all experiences as expressions of one true nature.

shambhu_gita::176.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्धा संविभक्ताऽलं राजते विश्वमोहिनी ।
सन्देहो नात्र कर्तव्यो विस्मयो वा कदाचन ॥
shambhu_gita::176.verse_hindi: यह विश्वमोहिनी चतुर्धा विभक्त होकर विराजमान है, इसमें संदेह अथवा विस्मय कभी नहीं करना चाहिये
shambhu_gita::176.english_translation: This cosmic illusion shines divided into four parts; in it, doubt or astonishment must never arise.
shambhu_gita::176.translation_literal: चतुर्धा (fourfold) / संविभक्ताऽलं (divided) / राजते (shines) / विश्वमोहिनी (cosmic illusion) / सन्देहो (doubt) / नात्र (not here) / कर्तव्यो (should be done) / विस्मयो (astonishment) / वा (or) / कदाचन (ever)
shambhu_gita::176.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::176.essence: The cosmic illusion is clearly divided; doubt or surprise is unnecessary.
shambhu_gita::176.simple_meaning: The cosmic illusion is divided into four parts and shines clearly; you should never feel doubt or surprise about it.
shambhu_gita::176.simple_insight: You can trust the cosmic illusion's nature without confusion or uncertainty.
shambhu_gita::176.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the cosmic illusion, which veils reality, is divided into four distinct aspects. He advises that neither doubt nor astonishment should arise when understanding this complex truth.
shambhu_gita::176.modern_relevance: When faced with confusing or overwhelming experiences, you can trust that the complexity you see is structured and not random or baffling.
shambhu_gita::176.insight: It shifts your mind from doubting the nature of illusion to accepting its structured presence.

shambhu_gita::177.verse_sanskrit:
स्थूलायाः प्रकृतेः सप्ताधिकाराः सन्ति सर्वथा। 
तेषामेवाधिकाराणां गूढः शक्तिमयो महान् ॥
shambhu_gita::177.verse_hindi: स्थूल प्रकृति के सर्वथा सप्त अधिकार हैं उन्हीं सप्त  अधिकारों के शक्तिमय महान्
shambhu_gita::177.english_translation: The gross natural world has exactly seven authorities, and the great power resides in those seven alone.
shambhu_gita::177.translation_literal: स्थूलायाः (of gross) प्रकृतेः (nature) सप्ताधिकाराः (seven authorities) सन्ति (are) सर्वथा (entirely). / तेषामेवाधिकाराणां (of those very authorities) गूढः (hidden) शक्तिमयो (full of power) महान् (great).
shambhu_gita::177.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::177.essence: All power in the material world is contained in seven fundamental authorities.
shambhu_gita::177.simple_meaning: The material world is governed by exactly seven main forces, and the great power lies hidden within these forces.
shambhu_gita::177.simple_insight: Understanding that a few core forces shape the whole world brings a sense of order beneath chaos.
shambhu_gita::177.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the visible natural world (gross prakriti) is controlled by seven fundamental authorities. These seven powers are mysterious but contain all the force behind nature's workings, setting the stage for deeper metaphysical teaching.
shambhu_gita::177.insight: It invites you to focus on mastering or understanding the few key forces behind the many changes you see around you.

shambhu_gita::178.verse_hindi: गहन रहस्यसमूह हे पितृगण ! आधिभौतिक ज्ञान के अतिगुह्य विज्ञान विस्तार के प्रकाशक हैं
shambhu_gita::178.english_translation: The ancestors are the secret assembly, the revealers of profound knowledge beyond worldly understanding.
shambhu_gita::178.translation_literal: रहस्यसङ्घः (secret assembly) / पितरो (ancestors) / वर्त्तते (exists) / सम्भकाशकः (revealer) । / आधिभौतिकवोधातिगृहाविज्ञानविस्तृतेः (beyond worldly knowledge, of deep science expansion) ॥
shambhu_gita::178.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::178.essence: Ancestors form a secret group revealing knowledge beyond the physical world.
shambhu_gita::178.simple_meaning: The ancestors form a secret group who reveal knowledge that goes beyond basic worldly understanding.
shambhu_gita::178.simple_insight: There is a hidden lineage of deep wisdom behind the knowledge we see.
shambhu_gita::178.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta describes the ancestors as a secret group who possess and reveal profound knowledge that transcends ordinary worldly understanding and scientific study, emphasizing the hidden depth of this wisdom.
shambhu_gita::178.insight: Recognize that deep wisdom often comes through a hidden lineage beyond surface knowledge.

shambhu_gita::179.verse_sanskrit:
सप्तधा शक्तिविज्ञानं स्थूलायाः प्रकृतेरपि ।
जगत्यां प्रायशो नैव सम्भवेत्सम्मकाशितम् ॥
shambhu_gita::179.verse_hindi: स्थूल प्रकृति के सप्तविध शक्ति विज्ञान का भी जगत में प्रकाशित होना प्रायः सम्भव नहीं ही होता है।
shambhu_gita::179.english_translation: The sevenfold knowledge of powers in the gross nature rarely manifests openly in the world.
shambhu_gita::179.translation_literal: सप्तधा (sevenfold) शक्तिविज्ञानं (knowledge of powers) स्थूलायाः (of the gross) प्रकृतेरपि (nature even) जगत्यां (in the world) प्रायशो (mostly) नैव (not) सम्भवेत् (occurs) सम्मकाशितम् (openly manifested)
shambhu_gita::179.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::179.essence: The deep powers of gross nature rarely reveal themselves clearly in the world.
shambhu_gita::179.simple_meaning: The detailed powers of the gross material nature rarely appear clearly or openly in the world.
shambhu_gita::179.simple_insight: Some deep truths about nature remain hidden and rarely show themselves plainly.
shambhu_gita::179.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the complex sevenfold powers of the gross natural world do not usually reveal themselves in everyday life, suggesting the hidden complexity beneath appearances.
shambhu_gita::179.insight: Recognize that much of reality's deeper forces are subtle and not immediately visible, requiring patient observation.

shambhu_gita::180.verse_sanskrit:
सन्सेवातीव गुह्यानि रहस्यान्यपराणि तु ।
नैवात्र संशयः कोऽपि कर्त्तव्यः पितरो धुधाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::180.verse_hindi: अन्यान्य रहस्य तो अतिगुह ही हैं, हे विज्ञ पितृगणं! इसमें कुछ भी सन्देह नहीं करना चाहिए
shambhu_gita::180.english_translation: Other secrets are indeed deeply hidden; there should be no doubt about this, O wise ancestors!
shambhu_gita::180.translation_literal: सन्सेवातीव (other) गुह्यानि (hidden) रहस्यानि (secrets) अपाराणि (deep) तु (indeed) नैवात्र (not here) संशयः (doubt) कोऽपि (anyone) कर्त्तव्यः (should do) पितरो (ancestors) धुधाः (wise)
shambhu_gita::180.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::180.essence: Some truths are deeply hidden and must be accepted without doubt.
shambhu_gita::180.simple_meaning: There are other secrets that are very deeply hidden, and there is no need to doubt this fact.
shambhu_gita::180.simple_insight: Some truths remain hidden and certain, even if not openly revealed.
shambhu_gita::180.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta addresses the sages, acknowledging that some teachings are deeply concealed and should be accepted without doubt, setting the stage for deeper revelation.
shambhu_gita::180.insight: It teaches you to accept that some knowledge is beyond immediate reach and requires trust in the process.

shambhu_gita::181.verse_sanskrit:
सूक्ष्मकारणयोः शक्तयोविज्ञानौघः समुच्यते ।
आधिदैविकसम्बन्धिज्ञानं नैवात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::181.verse_hindi: सूक्ष्म शक्ति और कारण शक्ति के विज्ञानसमूह आधिदैविक ज्ञान कहाते हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::181.english_translation: The collective knowledge of subtle power and causal power is called higher divine knowledge; there is no doubt in this.
shambhu_gita::181.translation_literal: सूक्ष्म (subtle) / कारण (causal) / यौः (of the two) / शक्तयोः (powers) / विज्ञानौघः (knowledge-collection) / समुच्यते (is called) / आधिदैविक (higher divine) / सम्बन्धि (related) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / नैवात्र (not here) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::181.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::181.essence: Higher wisdom arises from knowing both subtle and causal powers without doubt.
shambhu_gita::181.simple_meaning: Higher divine knowledge means understanding the combined subtle and causal powers behind reality without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::181.simple_insight: You feel confident when you grasp both the subtle and causal roots of existence.
shambhu_gita::181.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that true higher knowledge involves knowing two fundamental forces: subtle power (the fine, unseen energy) and causal power (the origin behind effects). This combined understanding forms the basis of divine wisdom without any uncertainty.
shambhu_gita::181.modern_relevance: When you explore not just surface causes but also subtle influences behind events, your understanding deepens and doubt fades.
shambhu_gita::181.insight: It teaches you to integrate both visible causes and subtle forces to grasp reality fully.

shambhu_gita::182.verse_sanskrit:
शक्तेस्तत्त्वं तुरीयाया वाङ्मनोबुद्धयगोचरम् ।
यदास्ते तद्विजानीत ज्ञानमध्यात्मसंज्ञकम् ॥
shambhu_gita::182.verse_hindi: तुरीय शक्ति का जो मन वचन और बुद्धि से अतीत तत्त्व है उसको अध्यात्म ज्ञान जानना चाहिए
shambhu_gita::182.english_translation: The essence of the supreme power is beyond mind, speech, and intellect; this is called spiritual knowledge.
shambhu_gita::182.translation_literal: शक्तेः (of power) तत्त्वं (essence) तुरीयाया (of the fourth state) वाङ्-मनः-बुद्धयः-आगोचरम् (beyond speech, mind, intellect) यद् (that) अस्ते (exists) तद् (that) विजानीत (should be known) ज्ञानम् (knowledge) अध्यात्म-संज्ञकम् (called spiritual)
shambhu_gita::182.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::182.essence: The deepest power is beyond mind, speech, and intellect—it is true spiritual knowledge.
shambhu_gita::182.simple_meaning: True spiritual knowledge is about the power that is beyond your mind, speech, and intellect.
shambhu_gita::182.simple_insight: You can rest in knowing there's a deeper power beyond your everyday thinking and talking.
shambhu_gita::182.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the highest power, the turiya state beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, transcends the mind, speech, and intellect. This transcendent essence is what real spiritual knowledge is about.
shambhu_gita::182.modern_relevance: When your thoughts and words fail to capture the full truth, you feel the presence of something deeper inside you.
shambhu_gita::182.insight: This verse shifts your understanding from relying on mental concepts to opening to a reality beyond mental limits.

shambhu_gita::183.verse_sanskrit:
अमीषां ज्ञानपुंजनां त्रिविधानामसंशयम् ।
बोधो रहस्यवर्गस्य सुगमो नैव वर्तते ॥
shambhu_gita::183.verse_hindi: इन त्रिविध ज्ञानसमूह के रहस्यों को समझना निःसन्देह ही सहज नहीं है
shambhu_gita::183.english_translation: Understanding the mysteries of these three types of knowledge is certainly not easy.
shambhu_gita::183.translation_literal: अमीषां (these) / ज्ञानपुंजनां (bundles of knowledge) / त्रिविधानाम् (threefold) / असंशयम् (without doubt) / बोधो (understanding) / रहस्यवर्गस्य (of the secret class) / सुगमः (easy) / नैव (not) / वर्तते (exists)
shambhu_gita::183.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::183.essence: Some knowledge’s deepest secrets cannot be easily understood without patient inquiry.
shambhu_gita::183.simple_meaning: The mysteries contained in three kinds of knowledge are not easy to understand without effort and patience.
shambhu_gita::183.simple_insight: It's okay to find some truths difficult; patience opens deeper understanding.
shambhu_gita::183.detailed_meaning: Shiva points out that the threefold categories of knowledge contain deep secrets. They are not straightforward, requiring dedicated inquiry and openness to grasp their meaning.
shambhu_gita::183.modern_relevance: When you face complex ideas or confusing information, it’s natural to feel stuck. Real understanding unfolds slowly with attention and patience.
shambhu_gita::183.insight: It teaches you to approach deep knowledge with openness and sustained questioning rather than expecting quick answers.

shambhu_gita::184.verse_sanskrit:
ममैव ज्ञानिनो भक्ताः शक्नुवन्ति मुखं द्रुतम् ।
रहस्यं ज्ञातुमेतेपां पितरो नात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::184.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! मेरे ज्ञानीभक्त ही इनके रहस्य को अनायास शीघ्र समझने में समर्थ होते हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं है।
shambhu_gita::184.english_translation: O ancestors! Only my wise devotees can quickly and effortlessly understand this secret, there is no doubt in this.
shambhu_gita::184.translation_literal: ममैव (only mine) ज्ञानिनो (wise ones) भक्ताः (devotees) शक्नुवन्ति (are able) मुखं (quickly) द्रुतम् (swiftly) । रहस्यं (secret) ज्ञातुमेतेपां (to know these) पितरो (ancestors) नात्र (in this no) संशयः (doubt) ॥
shambhu_gita::184.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::184.essence: Only wise devotion can swiftly reveal hidden spiritual secrets without doubt.
shambhu_gita::184.simple_meaning: Only those who combine wisdom and devotion to Shiva can quickly understand this secret without difficulty.
shambhu_gita::184.simple_insight: There is confidence that sincere devotion with wisdom leads to fast understanding.
shambhu_gita::184.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, saying that only his devotees who are wise can swiftly and effortlessly grasp the secret teachings he offers. This moment highlights the power of combining devotion with knowledge.
shambhu_gita::184.modern_relevance: When you deeply trust and seek wisely, complex ideas become clear faster than you expect.
shambhu_gita::184.insight: It teaches that devotion alone or wisdom alone is incomplete; together they accelerate deep understanding.

shambhu_gita::185.verse_sanskrit:
श्यामा त्रैगुण्यमव्यास्ते प्रक्रिर्तिर्मे स्वभावतः ।
धर्मोऽस्ति त्रिगुणानाञ्च चाञ्चल्यं श्रुतिसम्मतः ॥
shambhu_gita::185.verse_hindi: मेरी प्रकृति श्यामा स्वभाव से त्रिगुणमयी है और त्रिगुण का धर्म अस्थिरता है यह श्रुतिसम्मत है
shambhu_gita::185.english_translation: My nature is dark and composed of the three qualities; the nature of these three qualities is instability, as the scriptures confirm.
shambhu_gita::185.translation_literal: श्यामा (dark) त्रैगुण्यमव्यास्ते (composed of three qualities) प्रक्रिर्तिर्मे (nature my) स्वभावतः (by nature) । धर्मः (nature) अस्ति (is) त्रिगुणानाम् (of the three qualities) च (and) अञ्च (instability) श्रुतिसम्मतः (scriptures confirmed) ॥
shambhu_gita::185.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::185.essence: Instability and restlessness arise naturally from the three qualities composing all nature.
shambhu_gita::185.simple_meaning: Everything in the natural world is made of three qualities, and these qualities cause constant change and restlessness.
shambhu_gita::185.simple_insight: It’s freeing to see that change and restlessness are natural, not your fault or failure.
shambhu_gita::185.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that his own nature, dark and mysterious, is made of the three qualities (gunas) that cause continuous change. The scriptures confirm that these qualities naturally bring instability, revealing why the natural world is always shifting.
shambhu_gita::185.modern_relevance: When your moods and thoughts keep shifting unpredictably, it helps to know this restlessness is built into your nature, not a personal flaw.
shambhu_gita::185.insight: Recognize restlessness as a natural effect of the three qualities, so you stop blaming yourself and begin observing with clarity.

shambhu_gita::186.verse_sanskrit:
परिणामिन्यतो नित्यं प्रकृतिर्मेऽस्त्यसंशयम् ।
तदा सा पोच्यते विद्या मां यदेवावलोकते ॥
shambhu_gita::186.verse_hindi: इस कारण मेरी प्रकृति निःसन्देह सदा परिणामिनी रहती है। जब वह मेरी तरफ देखती है तब वह विद्या कहलाती है
shambhu_gita::186.english_translation: My nature is certainly always transformative; when it looks upon me, that is called wisdom.
shambhu_gita::186.translation_literal: परिणामिन्यतः (transformative by nature) / नित्यं (always) / प्रकृति: (nature) / मेऽस्ति (is mine) / असंशयम् (without doubt) / तदा (then) / सा (she/it) / पोच्यते (is called) / विद्या (wisdom) / मां (me) / यत् (when) / एव (indeed) / अवलोकते (looks upon)
shambhu_gita::186.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::186.essence: True wisdom is the changing nature recognizing the unchanging true self.
shambhu_gita::186.simple_meaning: Your inner nature is always changing. When this changing nature recognizes your true self, that recognition is called wisdom.
shambhu_gita::186.simple_insight: There is clarity and peace in seeing your true self beyond constant change.
shambhu_gita::186.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that his nature, Prakriti, is always in flux and transformation. When this natural change turns its attention toward the unchanging true self (Purusha), that act of recognition is called wisdom (Vidya). This verse reveals the relationship between change and stable awareness.
shambhu_gita::186.modern_relevance: When your moods shift or circumstances change, wisdom comes from recognizing the steady self beneath those changes.
shambhu_gita::186.insight: It shifts your focus from being lost in constant change to recognizing the stable observer within.

shambhu_gita::187.verse_sanskrit:
यदा बहिर्मुखीनाऽसौ प्रसूते जगद्भतम् ।
तदाऽविद्याभिधानेन नूनमेषाऽभिधीयते ॥
shambhu_gita::187.verse_hindi: जब वह बहिर्मुखीन होकर अद्भुत जगत् प्रसव करती है तब ही वह अविद्या कहाती है
shambhu_gita::187.english_translation: When it turns outward and creates the wondrous world, that is indeed called deep confusion.
shambhu_gita::187.translation_literal: यदा (when) बहिर्मुखीनाऽसौ (it turns outward) प्रसूते (creates) जगद्भतम् (the world) तदा (then) अविद्याभिधानेन (by the term deep confusion) नूनम् (indeed) एषा (this) अभिधीयते (is called)
shambhu_gita::187.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::187.essence: Turning outward to the world causes deep confusion that veils true understanding.
shambhu_gita::187.simple_meaning: Deep confusion arises when your attention moves outward, creating the appearance of the world.
shambhu_gita::187.simple_insight: You feel how looking outside yourself can cloud your clarity and bring confusion.
shambhu_gita::187.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the wondrous world appears when attention shifts outward from the true self. This turning outward causes deep confusion, as the inner being becomes obscured by the illusions of the natural world.
shambhu_gita::187.modern_relevance: When you get lost scrolling endlessly on your phone, your mind turns outward and confusion grows, hiding your true clarity.
shambhu_gita::187.insight: It teaches you to recognize that confusion arises from focusing outside rather than within, prompting a shift inward.

shambhu_gita::188.verse_sanskrit:
प्रेमसात्प्रकृतेः स्वस्याः स्यामहं विश्ववीजदः।
त्रिविधानां हि देवानां भवेयं जनकोऽपि च ॥
shambhu_gita::188.verse_hindi: मैं अपनी प्रकृति के प्रेम के वशीभूत होकर जगत का बीजदाता बन जाता हूँ और मैं ही विविध श्रेणी के देवताओं का जनक भी बन जाता हूँ
shambhu_gita::188.english_translation: By being immersed in the love of my own nature, I become the seed-giver of the universe and the progenitor of the three classes of deities.
shambhu_gita::188.translation_literal: प्रेमसात्प्रकृतेः (from the love of nature) / स्वस्याः (of my own) / स्यामहं (I become) / विश्ववीजदः (the seed-giver of the universe) / त्रिविधानां (of the threefold) / हि (indeed) / देवानां (of the deities) / भवेयं (I become) / जनकोऽपि (also the progenitor) / च (and)
shambhu_gita::188.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::188.essence: Loving your true nature makes you the source of all creation and divine life.
shambhu_gita::188.simple_meaning: By deeply loving my own true nature, I become the source from which everything in the universe arises, including all divine beings.
shambhu_gita::188.simple_insight: There is creative power in embracing your true nature with love and acceptance.
shambhu_gita::188.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks of merging with his own nature so fully that he becomes the origin and father of all creation and divine beings, showing his role as the cosmic source.
shambhu_gita::188.insight: It teaches you that embracing and loving your true nature unlocks your creative potential.

shambhu_gita::189.verse_sanskrit:
त एव त्रिविधा देवा विश्वस्य त्रिविधा गतीः ।
पालयन्ते तथा मृष्टीः सत्यमेतन्न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::189.verse_hindi: वही विविध देवतागण जगत की त्रिविध दृष्टि और गति का संरक्षण करते हैं यह सत्य है इसमें सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::189.english_translation: The various radiant beings protect the world’s threefold vision and threefold movement; this truth is beyond doubt.
shambhu_gita::189.translation_literal: त (that) / एव (indeed) / त्रिविधा (threefold) / देवा (divine beings) / विश्वस्य (of the world) / त्रिविधा (threefold) / गतीः (movements) / पालयन्ते (protect) / तथा (thus) / मृष्टीः (visions) / सत्यमेतन्न् (this truth) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::189.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::189.essence: Multiple radiant beings sustain the world's threefold vision and movement without fail.
shambhu_gita::189.simple_meaning: Different divine beings sustain the world’s three types of vision and movement; this is an unquestionable truth.
shambhu_gita::189.simple_insight: There is certainty in the divine order maintaining the world's diverse functions and perspectives.
shambhu_gita::189.detailed_meaning: As the narrative unfolds, Suta explains how various divine beings uphold the world's threefold ways of seeing and moving, emphasizing that this is a fundamental, undeniable truth in the cosmos.
shambhu_gita::189.insight: It highlights the dependable support sustaining the world's complex systems beyond human control.

shambhu_gita::190.verse_sanskrit:
भिन्ना त्रिगुणवैचित्र्याच्छक्तिद्वैविध्य आत्मना ।
दृष्टिगोचरतामेति श्यामाऽत्र जगतीतले ॥
shambhu_gita::190.verse_hindi: श्यामा त्रिगुण वैचित्र्य से दो प्रकार की शक्ति में विभक्त होकर इस जगत में दिखाई देती है
shambhu_gita::190.english_translation: The dark energy appears in this world divided by three qualities and two types of power.
shambhu_gita::190.translation_literal: भिन्ना (divided) त्रि-गुण (three qualities) वैचित्र्य-आ (variety) शक्ति-द्वैविध्य (two types of power) आत्मना (by the self) दृष्टि-गोचरता-मेति (visible) श्यामाऽत्र (dark energy here) जगतीतले (on the earth)
shambhu_gita::190.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::190.essence: The world’s energy appears divided into three qualities and two powers within the self.
shambhu_gita::190.simple_meaning: The dark energy that fills the world shows up as divided by three qualities and two kinds of power in the self.
shambhu_gita::190.simple_insight: The world’s energy is not one simple thing but a complex mix of qualities and powers.
shambhu_gita::190.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes how the fundamental energy or force behind the world is split into three qualities (gunas) and two powers, making the world’s diversity understandable as an expression of this divided energy.
shambhu_gita::190.insight: It shifts your view from seeing the world as one thing to recognizing multiple forces shaping experience.

shambhu_gita::191.verse_sanskrit:
शक्ती त एव कथ्येते आकर्षणविकर्षणे ।
रागद्वेषौ च पितरो नाऽत्र कश्चन संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::191.verse_hindi: उन्हीं शक्तियों को आकर्षण विकर्षण और राग द्वेष कहते हैं हे पितृगण ! इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::191.english_translation: Those forces are called attraction, repulsion, and attachment and aversion, O ancestors! There is no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::191.translation_literal: शक्ती (forces) / त (those) / एव (indeed) / कथ्येते (are said) / आकर्षणविकर्षणे (attraction and repulsion) / रागद्वेषौ (attachment and aversion) / च (and) / पितरो (O ancestors) / नाऽत्र (not here) / कश्चन (any) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::191.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::191.essence: Attraction, repulsion, attachment, and aversion are undeniable forces shaping experience.
shambhu_gita::191.simple_meaning: These forces are known as attraction, repulsion, attachment, and aversion; there is no doubt about it.
shambhu_gita::191.simple_insight: Recognizing these forces helps you understand how your feelings pull and push you.
shambhu_gita::191.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to the ancestors that certain forces—attraction, repulsion, attachment, and aversion—are fundamental and undeniable aspects influencing beings.
shambhu_gita::191.modern_relevance: You feel drawn to some things and pushed away from others; knowing this helps you see your emotional patterns clearly.
shambhu_gita::191.insight: Naming these forces helps you notice when your mind is pulled by desire or pushed by dislike.

shambhu_gita::192.verse_sanskrit:
आद्ये स्थूलेऽपरौ सूक्ष्मौ विद्यते पितरो ध्रुवम् ।
एतयोर्गुणसम्बन्धः प्रोच्यते साम्मतं मया ॥
shambhu_gita::192.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! प्रथम स्थूल और दूसरी सूक्ष्म ही है। अब मैं इन दोनों शक्तियों का गुण सम्बन्ध कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::192.english_translation: O ancestral beings! First is the gross, and second is the subtle. Now I describe the relationship of qualities between these two powers.
shambhu_gita::192.translation_literal: आद्ये (first) स्थूलेऽपरौ (gross and subtle) सूक्ष्मौ (subtle) विद्यते (exists) पितरो (ancestors) ध्रुवम् (certainly) । एतयोर्गुणसम्बन्धः (this quality relationship) प्रोच्यते (is explained) साम्मतं (approved) मया (by me) ॥
shambhu_gita::192.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::192.essence: Two fundamental powers exist: gross and subtle, linked by qualities.
shambhu_gita::192.simple_meaning: There are two fundamental powers: one gross and one subtle. This verse introduces their relationship.
shambhu_gita::192.simple_insight: Recognizing two fundamental layers beneath experience opens a deeper understanding of reality.
shambhu_gita::192.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestral beings, explaining that there are two primary forces—the gross (physical) and the subtle (energetic or mental). He prepares to explain how these two relate through qualities, setting a foundation for deeper metaphysical teaching.
shambhu_gita::192.insight: It invites you to notice the layers beneath appearances, distinguishing between what is tangible and what is subtle energy or mind.

shambhu_gita::193.verse_sanskrit:
अस्ति रागो रजोमूलस्तथाऽऽकर्पणमेव च।
विकर्षणं तथा द्वेषस्तगोमूलश्च विद्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::193.verse_hindi: आकर्षण और राग रजोमूलक और विकर्षण और द्वेष तमोमूलक हैं
shambhu_gita::193.english_translation: Attraction and attachment come from passion; aversion and hatred arise from darkness.
shambhu_gita::193.translation_literal: अस्ति (exists) / रागो (attachment) / रजोमूलः (rooted in passion) / तथा (and) / आकर्पणम् (attraction) / एव (indeed) / च (also) / विकर्षणं (aversion) / तथा (and) / द्वेषः (hatred) / तगः (darkness) / मूलः (root) / च (also) / विद्यते (exists)
shambhu_gita::193.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::193.essence: Attachment arises from passion; aversion grows from deep darkness within.
shambhu_gita::193.simple_meaning: Attachment and attraction arise from the energy of passion, while aversion and hatred come from deep darkness within.
shambhu_gita::193.simple_insight: You can feel how your likes and dislikes reflect deeper forces inside you, not just personal preference.
shambhu_gita::193.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that our emotional pulls like attraction and attachment have their root in rajas, the quality of passion, while dislikes such as aversion and hatred arise from tamas, the quality of darkness and inertia. Understanding these roots helps us see emotions as natural forces.
shambhu_gita::193.modern_relevance: When you find yourself strongly drawn to something or strongly rejecting it, it's often passion or inner darkness shaping your feelings, not just rational choice.
shambhu_gita::193.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your emotional reactions come from underlying qualities, helping you respond more wisely.

shambhu_gita::194.verse_sanskrit:
समन्वये द्वयोः सत्त्वगुणो नूनं विकाशते ।
अतः समन्वयादेव तयोविश्वस्य धारिका ॥
shambhu_gita::194.verse_hindi: दोनों के समन्वय में ही सत्वगुण का विकास होता है इस कारण आकर्षण विकर्षण के समन्वय से ही जगत की धारक
shambhu_gita::194.english_translation: The quality of harmony arises from the union of the two, and this union alone sustains the entire world.
shambhu_gita::194.translation_literal: समन्वये (in the union) / द्वयोः (of the two) / सत्त्वगुणो (the quality of harmony) / नूनं (indeed) / विकाशते (arises) / अतः (therefore) / समन्वयादेव (from the very union) / तयो (of those two) / विश्वस्य (of the world) / धारिका (the sustainer)
shambhu_gita::194.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::194.essence: The world exists because harmony grows from the union of opposites.
shambhu_gita::194.simple_meaning: Harmony or balance develops when two opposing forces come together, and this union supports the entire world.
shambhu_gita::194.simple_insight: You feel the power of balance that arises when differences come together as one.
shambhu_gita::194.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the world is held together by the balance of two opposing forces. Their union creates harmony, which sustains existence itself.
shambhu_gita::194.modern_relevance: When conflicting feelings or ideas come together in your life, you create a balance that keeps everything stable.
shambhu_gita::194.insight: It teaches you to see opposing elements not as enemies, but as partners whose union creates strength.

shambhu_gita::195.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वं रक्षति मच्छक्तिः सात्त्विकी धर्मरूपिणी।
नित्या सा वर्तते नित्यं विश्वकल्याणकारिणी ॥
shambhu_gita::195.verse_hindi: धर्मरूपिणी मेरी सात्त्विक शक्ति जगत की रक्षा करती है। यह नित्या और सर्वदा विश्व का कल्याण करनेवाली है
shambhu_gita::195.english_translation: My sattvic power, embodying dharma, protects the world. It always exists and continuously brings welfare to all.
shambhu_gita::195.translation_literal: विश्वं (world) / रक्षति (protects) / मच्छक्तिः (my power) / सात्त्विकी (sattvic) / धर्मरूपिणी (embodying dharma) / नित्या (always) / सा (she/it) / वर्तते (exists) / नित्यं (constantly) / विश्वकल्याणकारिणी (world-welfare-doing)
shambhu_gita::195.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::195.essence: Pure, righteous power always protects and benefits the world without interruption.
shambhu_gita::195.simple_meaning: A pure, righteous power that embodies true purpose always protects and benefits the entire world without fail.
shambhu_gita::195.simple_insight: You can trust that your inner strength quietly supports the well-being of all things.
shambhu_gita::195.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes his sattvic (pure) power as embodying dharma, the true ethical principle. This power constantly preserves and benefits the entire world, showing the steady presence of righteous energy sustaining life.
shambhu_gita::195.modern_relevance: When you act with clear, ethical intention, your inner strength naturally supports not just yourself but those around you.
shambhu_gita::195.insight: This verse invites you to see your true strength as a steady, benevolent force aligned with right purpose.

shambhu_gita::196.verse_sanskrit:
आरभ्य पितरोऽनेकग्रहोपाहतोऽखिलम् ।
अण्वन्तं स्थितिमादत्ते तस्मादेव समन्वयात् ॥
shambhu_gita::196.verse_hindi: हे पितरो! उसी समन्वय से अनेक ग्रह उपग्रह से लेकर परमाणु पर्यन्त सब स्थिति भाव को धारण करते हैं
shambhu_gita::196.english_translation: O ancestors! From that same union, many planets, their satellites, and even atoms hold their states of being.
shambhu_gita::196.translation_literal: आरभ्य (starting from) पितरोऽनेकग्रहोपाहतोऽखिलम् (ancestors many planets satellites all) / अण्वन्तं (atoms) स्थितिमादत्ते (state holds) तस्मादेव (from that very) समन्वयात् (union)
shambhu_gita::196.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::196.essence: All existence from atoms to planets is held by one unified principle.
shambhu_gita::196.simple_meaning: All things, from huge planets and their moons to tiny atoms, exist because of one fundamental union.
shambhu_gita::196.simple_insight: Everything shares a common source holding it together, from the largest to the smallest.
shambhu_gita::196.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta describes how the entire cosmos, including ancestors, many planets, their satellites, and even the smallest atoms, maintain their existence through one essential union or binding force.
shambhu_gita::196.insight: See the universe as a seamless whole connected by a single underlying principle.

shambhu_gita::197.verse_sanskrit:
तथा समन्वयस्यैव दशायां द्वेषरागयोः ।
जीवान्तःकरणे सत्त्वगुणस्यैव प्रकाशतः ॥
shambhu_gita::197.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार रागद्वेष के समन्वय की दशा में ही सत्त्वगुण का विकाश जीव के अन्तःकरण में होने से
shambhu_gita::197.english_translation: Similarly, in the state of the union of attachment and aversion, the quality of sattva shines forth within the inner being.
shambhu_gita::197.translation_literal: तथा (similarly) / समन्वयस्यैव (of the union itself) / दशायां (in the state) / द्वेषरागयोः (of hatred and attachment) / जीवान्तःकरणे (in the inner being) / सत्त्वगुणस्यैव (of the quality of sattva itself) / प्रकाशतः (from the shining forth)
shambhu_gita::197.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::197.essence: Clarity can arise within the inner being even amid mixed feelings of attachment and aversion.
shambhu_gita::197.simple_meaning: When attachment and aversion combine inside you, the clear and pure quality of your nature still shines through.
shambhu_gita::197.simple_insight: You can find clarity inside even when your feelings are confused and conflicted.
shambhu_gita::197.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even when strong opposing emotions like attachment and aversion arise together within the mind, the pure quality of sattva—clarity and balance—still manifests in the inner self, showing that confusion does not completely hide your true nature.
shambhu_gita::197.modern_relevance: You feel torn between wanting and resisting something, yet a quiet clarity still lingers inside, helping you find balance.
shambhu_gita::197.insight: It teaches you to recognize the steady clarity beneath conflicting emotions, anchoring your awareness beyond turmoil.

shambhu_gita::198.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानं विकाशते सम्यग् धर्मभाव उदेति च ।
पुण्यः पुण्यप्रवाहो हि बहते नात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::198.verse_hindi: ज्ञान का विकास और धर्मभाव का सम्यक् उदय हुआ करता है, पवित्र पुण्य प्रवाह ही बहता रहता है इसमें सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::198.english_translation: True wisdom grows and the feeling of righteous purpose arises; a pure flow of virtue always continues without doubt.
shambhu_gita::198.translation_literal: ज्ञानं (wisdom) / विकाशते (grows) / सम्यग् (properly) / धर्मभाव (feeling of righteousness) / उदेति (arises) / च (and) / पुण्यः (virtue) / पुण्यप्रवाहो (flow of virtue) / हि (indeed) / बहते (flows) / नात्र (there is no) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::198.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::198.essence: True wisdom awakens a clear, doubtless flow of righteous purpose and virtue.
shambhu_gita::198.simple_meaning: True wisdom develops clearly, awakening a genuine feeling of righteousness, and a continuous, pure flow of virtue follows without hesitation.
shambhu_gita::198.simple_insight: There's calm assurance when your wisdom and sense of purpose naturally guide you forward.
shambhu_gita::198.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva describes how real wisdom unfolds in a person, bringing forth a clear sense of righteous purpose. This inner growth leads to a constant stream of virtuous actions, free from doubt, marking a reliable path to follow.
shambhu_gita::198.modern_relevance: You notice your understanding deepening, and with it, a natural motivation to do what feels genuinely right flows steadily through your day.
shambhu_gita::198.insight: It shifts your view from sporadic effort to trusting a steady, doubt-free flow of right intention and action.

shambhu_gita::199.verse_sanskrit:
द्वे एव भवतः शक्ती आकर्षणविकर्षणे ।
नारीधारासु जीवानां नृधारास्वपि सर्चतः ॥
shambhu_gita::199.verse_hindi: यही दो आकर्षण और विकर्षण शक्तियां जीवों की स्त्री धारा और पुरुष धारा में सर्वत्र वर्तमान हैं
shambhu_gita::199.english_translation: There are only two forces of attraction and repulsion present in all beings, both in the female and male streams everywhere.
shambhu_gita::199.translation_literal: द्वे (two) एव (only) भवतः (are) शक्ती (forces) आकर्षणविकर्षणे (attraction and repulsion) । नारीधारासु (in female streams) जीवानां (of beings) नृधारास्वपि (and in male streams also) सर्चतः (present) ॥
shambhu_gita::199.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::199.essence: All life flows through two universal forces: attraction and repulsion.
shambhu_gita::199.simple_meaning: Two fundamental forces of attraction and repulsion exist universally in all beings, across both male and female life currents.
shambhu_gita::199.simple_insight: You can sense that the push and pull forces shape all life everywhere you look.
shambhu_gita::199.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that every living being is influenced by two fundamental forces: attraction and repulsion. These forces operate equally through both male and female forms of life, underlying all existence.
shambhu_gita::199.insight: Recognizing attraction and repulsion as universal forces helps you see underlying patterns in relationships and nature.

shambhu_gita::200.verse_sanskrit:
आकर्षणस्वरूपं हि शरीरं योषितामिह ।
तथा विकर्षण नृणां शरीरं स्यात्स्वरूपतः ॥
shambhu_gita::200.verse_hindi: इस संसार में स्त्री शरीर आकर्षण रूपी और पुरुष शरीर विकर्षण रूपी ही है
shambhu_gita::200.english_translation: In this world, the female body is naturally of the form of attraction, and the male body is naturally of the form of repulsion.
shambhu_gita::200.translation_literal: आकर्षणस्वरूपं (attraction-form) हि (indeed) शरीरं (body) योषितामिह (of females here) । तथा (thus) विकर्षण (repulsion) नृणां (of men) शरीरं (body) स्यात् (is) स्वरूपतः (by nature) ॥
shambhu_gita::200.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::200.essence: Female and male bodies are described as embodying attraction and repulsion respectively by nature.
shambhu_gita::200.simple_meaning: Female bodies are described as naturally drawing in, while male bodies are described as naturally pushing away.
shambhu_gita::200.simple_insight: It feels like this verse highlights a natural difference in how attraction and repulsion express physically between genders.
shambhu_gita::200.detailed_meaning: This verse reflects a traditional idea from Shambhu Gita about the natural qualities of female and male bodies, framing females as embodying attraction and males as embodying repulsion, illustrating a dualistic view of physical nature.
shambhu_gita::200.insight: It invites reflection on how we perceive natural tendencies but does not instruct action or inner work directly.

shambhu_gita::201.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मानन्दानुभूते: स्याल्लोभाव स्पर्शेन्द्रियेण वै ।
दम्पतीसङ्गमः साक्षात्पवित्रः सात्त्विकः शुभः ॥
shambhu_gita::201.verse_hindi: स्पर्श-इन्द्रिय द्वारा ब्रह्मानन्द अनुभव के लोभ से ही साक्षात् पवित्र सात्विक और शुभ स्त्री पुरुष का संगम होता है ।
shambhu_gita::201.english_translation: The union of a pure, sattvic, and auspicious couple happens directly through the sense of touch fueled by the desire for experiencing bliss of the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::201.translation_literal: ब्रह्मानन्दानुभूते: (for experiencing supreme bliss) / स्यात् (there is) / लोभ: (desire) / स्पर्शेन्द्रियेण (by the sense of touch) / वै (indeed). / दम्पतीसङ्गमः (union of a couple) / साक्षात् (directly) / पवित्रः (pure) / सात्त्विकः (sattvic) / शुभः (auspicious).
shambhu_gita::201.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::201.essence: Pure touch combined with longing for supreme bliss creates a sacred, harmonious union.
shambhu_gita::201.simple_meaning: A truly pure and harmonious union between partners happens through physical touch combined with a sincere desire for the bliss of the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::201.simple_insight: You feel how deep connection arises when touch is joined with true longing for joy beyond the ordinary.
shambhu_gita::201.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when two partners come together with a pure heart and desire to experience the bliss of the supreme reality, their physical union becomes sacred, sattvic, and auspicious, transforming ordinary contact into a spiritual connection.
shambhu_gita::201.modern_relevance: You notice how moments of genuine touch with someone you trust can feel deeply meaningful, as if touching a higher joy beyond daily life.
shambhu_gita::201.insight: It teaches you to see physical connection as a gateway to shared spiritual experience, not just a casual act.

shambhu_gita::202.verse_sanskrit:
सत्त्वभावमयः पुण्यो वर्त्तते सङ्गमक्षणः ।
आधिदैविकपीठस्योत्पादको नात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::202.verse_hindi: संगम का काल अतिपवित्र सत्त्वभावमय और अधिदेवपीठ-उत्पादक है इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::202.english_translation: The moment of union is supremely pure, filled with pure nature, and undoubtedly the source of the divine seat.
shambhu_gita::202.translation_literal: सत्त्वभावमयः (filled with pure nature) / पुण्यो (pure) / वर्त्तते (exists) / सङ्गमक्षणः (moment of union) / आधिदैविकपीठस्य (of the divine seat) / उत्पादको (producer/source) / नात्र (here not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::202.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::202.essence: The moment of union is pure and undeniably the source of divine presence.
shambhu_gita::202.simple_meaning: The time of coming together is extremely pure and is clearly the source of the divine presence; there is no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::202.simple_insight: You sense the sacredness in moments when true connection arises, beyond all doubt.
shambhu_gita::202.detailed_meaning: Suta describes the moment of union or confluence as a supremely pure time charged with sattva (purity), which is undeniably the origin of the divine seat or presence, setting a sacred tone for what follows.
shambhu_gita::202.insight: Recognize that certain moments hold a sacred quality that naturally arises without question or effort.

shambhu_gita::203.verse_sanskrit:
विष्णुस्वरूपमादाय ब्रह्माण्डस्य स्थितिक्षणे ।
ब्रमाण्डेस्मिन यथाऽऽकृष्टो विष्णुपीठस्वरूपिणि ॥
shambhu_gita::203.verse_hindi: जैसे है पितृगण ! ब्रह्माण्ड की स्थिति दशा में मैं विष्णुरूप धारण करके विष्णुपीठ रूपी
shambhu_gita::203.english_translation: At the moment of the universe's preservation, I assumed the form of Vishnu, the seat of the cosmos, just as the ancestors do.
shambhu_gita::203.translation_literal: विष्णुस्वरूपमादाय (assuming form of Vishnu) ब्रह्माण्डस्य (of the universe) स्थितिक्षणे (at the moment of preservation) । ब्रमाण्डेस्मिन (in the universe) यथा (just as) आकृष्टो (attracted) विष्णुपीठस्वरूपिणि (in the form of the Vishnu seat) ॥
shambhu_gita::203.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::203.essence: The supreme manifests as Vishnu to uphold the universe’s stability when needed.
shambhu_gita::203.simple_meaning: At the universe's moment of preservation, I took the form of Vishnu, the cosmic seat, like the ancestors do.
shambhu_gita::203.simple_insight: Divine forms adapt to sustain the cosmos, showing unity in diverse roles.
shambhu_gita::203.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares that at the time when the universe is sustained, he takes on Vishnu's form, embodying the cosmic seat. This reflects the divine's ability to manifest various roles, similar to how ancestors connect with cosmic order.
shambhu_gita::203.insight: It reveals how the supreme takes on different forms to maintain cosmic balance, showing flexible unity.

shambhu_gita::204.verse_sanskrit:
सन्तिष्टे पितरो नूनं दम्पतीसङ्गमे तथा ।
आकृष्यन्ते त्रिधा देवाः पीठस्योत्पादके स्वतः ॥
shambhu_gita::204.verse_hindi: इस ब्रह्माण्ड में आकृष्ट रहता है उसी प्रकार दम्पती की पीठ-उत्पन्नकारी संगम दशा में
shambhu_gita::204.english_translation: Just as ancestors remain present, gods are naturally drawn threefold to the union created by a couple's union.
shambhu_gita::204.translation_literal: सन्तिष्टे (remain) पितरो (ancestors) नूनं (indeed) दम्पतीसङ्गमे (in the couple's union) तथा (thus) । आकृष्यन्ते (are drawn) त्रिधा (threefold) देवाः (gods) पीठस्योत्पादके (to the seat-producer) स्वतः (naturally) ॥
shambhu_gita::204.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::204.essence: Divine presence naturally surrounds the sacred union of a couple.
shambhu_gita::204.simple_meaning: In the world, ancestors and divine beings are naturally attracted to the union formed by a couple.
shambhu_gita::204.simple_insight: The sacred presence around union reminds us that connections hold deeper unseen bonds.
shambhu_gita::204.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how in the universe, just as ancestors remain close, divine forces are naturally drawn to the sacred union of a couple, emphasizing the spiritual significance of partnership.
shambhu_gita::204.insight: It reveals that human relationships are embedded in a larger spiritual context beyond immediate perception.

shambhu_gita::205.verse_sanskrit:
यथाकालं यथादेशं यथापात्रं तदाऽनयाः ।
भवन्तः पितरस्तत्र रजोवीर्य्याश्रयेण हि ॥
shambhu_gita::205.verse_hindi: यथाकाल यथादेश यथापात्र त्रिविध देवतागण स्वतः आकृष्ट हुआ करते हैं
shambhu_gita::205.english_translation: The three groups of deities naturally gather according to the right time, place, and vessel.
shambhu_gita::205.translation_literal: यथा (according to) कालं (time) / यथा (according to) देशं (place) / यथा (according to) पात्रं (vessel) / तदा (then) अनयाः (these) / भवन्तः (are) पितरः (ancestors) / तत्र (there) रजः (passion) वीर्यः (strength) आश्रयेण (by the support) हि (indeed)
shambhu_gita::205.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::205.essence: Certain things come together naturally only when time, place, and form are right.
shambhu_gita::205.simple_meaning: The three groups of divine beings naturally come together exactly at their right time, place, and form.
shambhu_gita::205.simple_insight: Some things happen naturally when conditions are just right, without force or effort.
shambhu_gita::205.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how three groups of divine beings assemble naturally, each arriving according to their proper time, location, and form, emphasizing natural order and timing in cosmic events.
shambhu_gita::205.insight: It teaches to trust natural timing and conditions rather than forcing outcomes.

shambhu_gita::206.verse_sanskrit:
आकृप्यन्ते वपुर्दातुं जीवाय स्थूलमद्रुतम् ।
अन्ये देवगणा नेतुं शरीरैरातिवाहिकैः ॥
shambhu_gita::206.verse_hindi: हे अनघ पितृगण ! उस समय आपलोग रजवीर्य्य की सहायता से ही यथादेश कालपात्र अद्भुत स्थूल शरीर जीव को प्रदान करने के अर्थ उस पीठ में आकृष्ट होते हो । अत्यान्य देवतागण
shambhu_gita::206.english_translation: O sinless ancestors, at that time you gathered on that seat with the aid of Rajaveerya to grant a wondrous, gross, and imperishable body to the living being; many other divine beings came with their bodies in marriage.
shambhu_gita::206.translation_literal: आकृप्यन्ते (are gathered) / वपुर्दातुं (to give body) / जीवाय (to the living being) / स्थूलम् (gross) / अद्रुतम् (imperishable) । / अन्ये (others) / देवगणा (divine groups) / नेतुं (to lead) / शरीरैः (with bodies) / अति-वाहिकैः (exceedingly carried) ॥
shambhu_gita::206.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::206.essence: Many divine beings come together to grant a special body to a living being.
shambhu_gita::206.simple_meaning: Many divine beings gathered together to grant a remarkable physical body to a living being at that time.
shambhu_gita::206.simple_insight: The creation of a body involves the cooperation of many divine forces beyond ordinary sight.
shambhu_gita::206.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates a moment when many divine beings assemble with great power to bestow a special, durable body on a living being, marking a significant event in the story's unfolding.
shambhu_gita::206.insight: Recognizing that complex transformations often require unseen support beyond what we notice.

shambhu_gita::207.verse_sanskrit:
युक्ताञ्जीवगणाँस्तत्र सूक्ष्मदेहावलम्बिनः।
पूर्वेभ्यो भोगलोकेभ्य आकृप्यन्ते न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::207.verse_hindi: आतिपाहिक देह युक्त सूक्ष्मदेहधारी जीवों को पूर्वभोग लोको से वहां पहुंचा देने के लिये निःसन्देह आकृष्ट होते हैं
shambhu_gita::207.english_translation: There is no doubt that subtle-bodied beings attached to gross-bodied beings are drawn there from their previous worlds.
shambhu_gita::207.translation_literal: युक्ताञ्जीवगणाँस्तत्र (attached beings there) / सूक्ष्मदेहावलम्बिनः (subtle-bodied dependent) / पूर्वेभ्यो (from previous) / भोगलोकेभ्यः (worlds of enjoyment) / आकृप्यन्ते (are drawn) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::207.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::207.essence: Subtle beings linked to gross bodies are inevitably drawn from previous worlds.
shambhu_gita::207.simple_meaning: Subtle beings connected to gross-bodied beings are certainly drawn to that place from their earlier worlds.
shambhu_gita::207.simple_insight: Connections from past lives influence where subtle beings go next.
shambhu_gita::207.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that beings with subtle bodies who are linked to those with gross bodies get inevitably drawn to a certain realm, carried over from their experiences in earlier worlds.
shambhu_gita::207.insight: It highlights how past attachments and subtle connections shape present experiences beyond physical life.

shambhu_gita::208.verse_sanskrit:
रज शल्या ततस्तत्र तमःशक्तिः परास्यते ।
तेन पीठे विनष्टे वै रजोजातबलाश्रयात ॥
shambhu_gita::208.verse_hindi: वहां रजशक्ति तमशक्ति को परास्त कर लेती है उससे पीठ का नाश हो जाने पर ही रजोगुण के बल से
shambhu_gita::208.english_translation: There, the quality of passion overcomes the force of darkness; when the base is destroyed, only then does the power of passion persist.
shambhu_gita::208.translation_literal: रज (passion) / शल्या (piercing/overcoming) / ततस्तत्र (there) / तमःशक्तिः (darkness power) / परास्यते (is overcome) / तेन (by that) / पीठे (base) / विनष्टे (destroyed) / वै (indeed) / रजोजातबलाश्रयात (from the strength of passion born)
shambhu_gita::208.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::208.essence: Passion can only arise after the foundation of darkness is destroyed.
shambhu_gita::208.simple_meaning: Passion (rajas) overcomes darkness (tamas) only after the foundation that supports darkness is destroyed.
shambhu_gita::208.simple_insight: You can feel your energy rise when the hidden darkness beneath you breaks away.
shambhu_gita::208.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how the quality of passion (rajas) can surpass the force of darkness (tamas) only after the base or support of darkness is destroyed, revealing the dynamic interplay of inner qualities.
shambhu_gita::208.modern_relevance: When you break free from deep-rooted fears or doubts, your drive and energy can finally emerge stronger.
shambhu_gita::208.insight: It teaches you to dismantle the root causes of inertia before your motivating energy can fully awaken.

shambhu_gita::209.verse_sanskrit:
पतितस्यैव वीर्य्यस्य सहयोगेन सर्वथा ।
नारीदेहे भवन्नूनं गर्भाधानं न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::209.verse_hindi: पतित वीर्य के सर्वथा सहयोग से ही नारीदेह में ही निःसन्देह गर्भाधान हो जाता है
shambhu_gita::209.english_translation: Without the full union of vital energy, conception in a woman's body does not happen without doubt.
shambhu_gita::209.translation_literal: पतितस्यैव (of the vital energy that has fallen) वीर्य्यस्य (of semen) सहयोगेन (by union) सर्वथा (completely) । नारीदेहे (in woman's body) भवन्नूनं (indeed happens) गर्भाधानं (conception) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
shambhu_gita::209.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::209.essence: Complete union is essential for conception; partial effort cannot create new life.
shambhu_gita::209.simple_meaning: Conception in a woman's body requires the full union of vital energy; without it, conception will not happen.
shambhu_gita::209.simple_insight: Some things only happen through complete union and presence, not partial effort.
shambhu_gita::209.detailed_meaning: This verse states a biological fact in the context of ancient teaching: conception requires the complete union of vital energy (semen) within the woman's body, emphasizing that partial or incomplete union cannot produce a child.
shambhu_gita::209.insight: It highlights that certain results need full, committed involvement rather than partial or fragmented effort.

shambhu_gita::210.verse_sanskrit:
यथायोग्यं तदा यूयं जीवानां सूक्ष्मदेहिनाम् ।
सन्निवासोपयुक्तानि स्थूलदेहगृहाण्यहो ॥
shambhu_gita::210.verse_hindi: उस समय आपलोग यथायोग्य' सक्ष्म शरीरधारी जीवों के रहने के उपयोगी यथायोग्य गृहरूपी स्थूल शरीर
shambhu_gita::210.english_translation: At that time, you should provide appropriate gross bodies as residences suitable for the subtle-bodied living beings.
shambhu_gita::210.translation_literal: यथायोग्यं (appropriately) तदा (then) यूयं (you) जीवानां (of living beings) सूक्ष्मदेहिनाम् (subtle-bodied) सन्निवासोपयुक्तानि (suitable for residence) स्थूलदेहगृहाणि (gross body houses) अहो (should provide)
shambhu_gita::210.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::210.essence: Living beings receive fitting physical bodies suited to their subtle inner nature at the right time.
shambhu_gita::210.simple_meaning: You should give living beings appropriate physical bodies suited to their subtle inner nature at the right time.
shambhu_gita::210.simple_insight: There is care in ensuring every being has the proper support for its existence.
shambhu_gita::210.detailed_meaning: Shiva instructs that living beings with subtle inner forms receive suitable gross bodies as homes, showing thoughtful care for their needs in the natural cycle.
shambhu_gita::210.modern_relevance: You notice how people need the right environment or tools to thrive, just like living beings need fitting bodies to live fully.
shambhu_gita::210.insight: Recognize the importance of providing appropriate support aligned with inner nature to enable healthy functioning.

shambhu_gita::211.verse_sanskrit:
संयच्छय नयन्ते च जीवांस्तत्रैव निर्जराः।
पराजितं तमो नैव स्यात्तत्र रजसा यदि ॥
shambhu_gita::211.verse_hindi: प्रदान करते हो और देवतागण जीवों को वहां ही पहुंचा देते हैं। यदि वहां तम को रज परास्त नहीं कर सके
shambhu_gita::211.english_translation: There, the beings are controlled and freed from decay; if darkness is not overcome by passion, it cannot exist there.
shambhu_gita::211.translation_literal: संयच्छय (controlling) नयन्ते (lead) च (and) जीवांस्तत्रैव (beings there itself) निर्जराः (decay-free). पराजितं (defeated) तमो (darkness) नैव (not) स्यात् (becomes) तत्र (there) रजसा (by passion) यदि (if).
shambhu_gita::211.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::211.essence: A realm without decay exists where darkness fails to overcome passion.
shambhu_gita::211.simple_meaning: In that place, living beings are controlled and free from decay; if darkness is not defeated by passion, it does not exist there.
shambhu_gita::211.simple_insight: There is a realm beyond decay where darkness cannot prevail if passion overcomes it.
shambhu_gita::211.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes a realm where beings are maintained without aging or decay. The verse suggests that darkness, symbolizing ignorance or inertia, cannot survive there if passion or energy triumphs.
shambhu_gita::211.insight: It highlights that overcoming inner darkness requires active energy or passion; without it, ignorance cannot persist.

shambhu_gita::212.verse_sanskrit:
रजस्तमोभ्यां पितरो भावशुद्धिपुरस्सरम् ।
अग्रेसरदभ्यां सततं सत्त्वं ज्ञानमयं प्रति ॥
shambhu_gita::212.verse_hindi: और हे पितरो! रज और तम भावशुद्धि पूर्वक ज्ञानमय सत्व की ओर अग्रसर हो
shambhu_gita::212.english_translation: O ancestral beings! Always advance from the qualities of passion and ignorance toward the pure, wisdom-filled quality of goodness.
shambhu_gita::212.translation_literal: रजस्तमोभ्यां (from passion and ignorance) / पितरो (ancestors) / भावशुद्धिपुरस्सरम् (toward purity of quality advancing) / अग्रसरदभ्यां (constantly advancing) / सततं (always) / सत्त्वं (goodness) / ज्ञानमयं (full of wisdom) / प्रति (toward)
shambhu_gita::212.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::212.essence: You can always advance from restless confusion to steady, wise clarity.
shambhu_gita::212.simple_meaning: You can shift your nature from passion and confusion toward a pure, steady state full of wisdom.
shambhu_gita::212.simple_insight: There is hope and power in moving toward clarity and wisdom from confusion.
shambhu_gita::212.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestral beings, urging them to progress from the unstable qualities of passion (rajas) and ignorance (tamas) toward the stable, wisdom-filled quality of goodness (sattva). This teaching highlights a spiritual evolution from confusion to clarity.
shambhu_gita::212.modern_relevance: When your mind feels restless and clouded with doubt, you can choose to move toward calm clarity and wise understanding.
shambhu_gita::212.insight: It teaches you to recognize unstable mental states and intentionally cultivate clarity and wisdom instead.

shambhu_gita::213.verse_sanskrit:
नृनारीभेदरूपाच्च द्वन्द्वधर्मप्रभावतः।
लब्ध्वा बहिर्गनाभ्यां हि पराभक्तिं ममोत्तमाम् ॥
shambhu_gita::213.verse_hindi: और स्त्रीपुरुषभेद रुपी द्वन्द्व धर्म के प्रभाव से बचकर मेरी उत्तम पराभक्ति प्राप्त करके
shambhu_gita::213.english_translation: Escaping the dualities of male and female forms, through external groups, one attains my supreme devoted love.
shambhu_gita::213.translation_literal: नृनारीभेदरूपाच्च (male-female-difference-forms) / द्वन्द्वधर्मप्रभावतः (due to duality-nature's influence) / लब्ध्वा (having obtained) / बहिर्गनाभ्यां (through external groups) / हि (indeed) / पराभक्तिं (supreme devotion) / ममोत्तमाम् (my highest)
shambhu_gita::213.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::213.essence: The highest devotion arises when you go beyond gender and social divisions.
shambhu_gita::213.simple_meaning: The highest devoted love to Shiva is found when you rise above distinctions like male or female and beyond external social groups.
shambhu_gita::213.simple_insight: You feel free from limiting divisions when your love for the divine transcends all labels.
shambhu_gita::213.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that the supreme devotion to him is not bound by social or gender divisions. When a devotee goes beyond these external distinctions and group identities, they reach his highest devoted love.
shambhu_gita::213.modern_relevance: You might notice how social labels or group identities sometimes limit your connection with others or the divine. This teaching invites you to love beyond those boundaries.
shambhu_gita::213.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with outer categories to embracing devotion that transcends all separations.

shambhu_gita::214.verse_sanskrit:
यदि सत्त्वे विलीयेत तह्याकृष्टा महर्षयः ।
रहितं सृष्टिधर्मेण कैवल्यं शाश्वतं, पदम् ॥
shambhu_gita::214.verse_hindi: यदि सत्व में विलीन हो जाये तो ऋषिगण आकृष्ट होकर सृष्टिधर्म से रहित शाश्वत कैवल्यपद
shambhu_gita::214.english_translation: If sages dissolve into pure goodness, they become free from creation’s law and reach eternal freedom.
shambhu_gita::214.translation_literal: यदि (if) सत्त्वे (in pure goodness) विलीयेत (dissolve) तह्याकृष्टा (then attracted) महर्षयः (great sages) । / रहितं (free) सृष्टिधर्मेण (by creation's law) कैवल्यं (freedom) शाश्वतं (eternal), पदम् (state) ॥
shambhu_gita::214.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::214.essence: True freedom is found when you fully merge with pure goodness beyond creation’s laws.
shambhu_gita::214.simple_meaning: When you become completely absorbed in pure goodness, you move beyond the rules of creation and reach lasting freedom.
shambhu_gita::214.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing freedom lies beyond the restless world when you merge with goodness.
shambhu_gita::214.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that when great sages fully dissolve their sense of separate self into pure goodness (sattva), they transcend the laws that govern creation and enter a timeless state of absolute freedom called kaivalya.
shambhu_gita::214.modern_relevance: In moments when you let go of ego and align with your best qualities, you experience freedom beyond everyday struggles and limitations.
shambhu_gita::214.insight: This verse shifts your view from being trapped by external conditions to resting in unchanging inner freedom.

shambhu_gita::215.verse_sanskrit:
अनेनैवाध्वना गम्यमिति संसूचयन्त्यलम् ।
नैवात्र संशयः कोऽपि विद्यते पितृपुङ्गवा ! ॥
shambhu_gita::215.verse_hindi: इसी मार्ग से प्राप्य है ऐसा भलीभांति बता देते हैं। हे पितृश्रेष्ठो । इसमें कोई संशयं नहीं है
shambhu_gita::215.english_translation: They clearly indicate that this very path leads to the goal. There is no doubt in this, O best of ancestors!
shambhu_gita::215.translation_literal: अनेनैवाध्वना (by this very path) / गम्यमिति (to be reached) / संसूचयन्ति (indicate clearly) / अलम् (this) / नैवात्र (not here) / संशयः (doubt) / कोऽपि (anyone) / विद्यते (exists) / पितृपुङ्गवा (O best of ancestors)
shambhu_gita::215.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::215.essence: This very path unmistakably leads to the goal without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::215.simple_meaning: This verse says that the path being taught clearly leads to the goal without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::215.simple_insight: You can trust this teaching as certain and direct.
shambhu_gita::215.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta reassures the assembled sages that the path Shiva describes is certain and free of doubt, emphasizing the confidence in the teaching being presented.
shambhu_gita::215.insight: It affirms trust in the clear guidance given, eliminating hesitation about the path.

shambhu_gita::216.verse_sanskrit:
अधिदेवरहस्येन पूर्णस्यास्य पवित्रता।
पीठविज्ञानयोगस्य यावती प्रचरिप्यति ॥
shambhu_gita::216.verse_hindi: इस संसार में अधिदेव रहस्यपूर्ण इस पीठविज्ञान योग की पवित्रता जितनी प्रचारित होगी
shambhu_gita::216.english_translation: In this world, the sacredness of this secret Adhideva Peethavigyana Yoga spreads as far as it is proclaimed.
shambhu_gita::216.translation_literal: अधिदेवरहस्येन (by the secret of the supreme deity) / पूर्णस्यास्य (of this complete) / पवित्रता (sacredness) / पीठविज्ञानयोगस्य (of Peethavigyana yoga) / यावती (as much as) / प्रचरिप्यति (it spreads)
shambhu_gita::216.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::216.essence: Sacred knowledge's power depends on how widely it is shared.
shambhu_gita::216.simple_meaning: The sacredness of this secret spiritual yoga is known to spread only as much as people share it.
shambhu_gita::216.simple_insight: Sacred knowledge gains power and reach through sharing, not secrecy.
shambhu_gita::216.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how the holy and secret practice of Peethavigyana Yoga depends on how widely it is proclaimed. The verse highlights the connection between spreading sacred wisdom and its recognized purity.
shambhu_gita::216.modern_relevance: Hidden knowledge or wisdom only grows meaningful when you share it openly with others who can benefit.
shambhu_gita::216.insight: It teaches that sacred or deep wisdom requires proclamation to manifest its true influence and sanctity.

shambhu_gita::217.verse_sanskrit:
तावन्मात्रोत्तमणिभुक्तैर्जीवैर्जनिष्यते ।
जगत्यामिह सन्देहो विद्यते न स्वधाभुजः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::217.verse_hindi: उतना ही उत्तम श्रेणी के जीवों का जन्म हो सकेगा हे पितरो! इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::217.english_translation: Only that many highest-class beings will be born here, O ancestors! There is no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::217.translation_literal: तावन्मात्रः (that many only) उत्तम (highest) अणिभुक्तैः (class-eaten/by class) जीवैः (beings) जनिष्यते (will be born) । जगत्याम् (in the world) इहि (here) सन्देहः (doubt) न (not) स्वधाभुजः (O ancestors) !
shambhu_gita::217.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::217.essence: The birth of highest beings in the world is fixed and certain without doubt.
shambhu_gita::217.simple_meaning: Only a limited number of the best beings will be born in this world; there is no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::217.simple_insight: Some things, like the birth of great beings, are certain and not to be questioned.
shambhu_gita::217.detailed_meaning: The narrator Suta addresses the ancestors, affirming that only a definite number of highest beings will be born in this world. This sets a context of order and certainty in cosmic creation.
shambhu_gita::217.insight: It shows acceptance of natural limits and certainty in cosmic design rather than endless chance.

shambhu_gita::218.verse_sanskrit:
उत्तमस्थूलदेहेषु दैवसम्पत्तिधारिणः ।
प्रवेशं कर्तुमर्हन्ति जीवाः सौभाग्यशालिनः ॥
shambhu_gita::218.verse_hindi: उत्तम स्थूल शरीरों में देवीसम्पत्तिधारी सौभाग्यशाली जीव पहुंच सकते हैं
shambhu_gita::218.english_translation: Fortunate beings endowed with divine qualities can enter supreme gross bodies.
shambhu_gita::218.translation_literal: उत्तम (supreme) / स्थूल (gross) / देहेषु (in bodies) / दैवसम्पत्तिधारिणः (endowed with divine qualities) / प्रवेशं (entry) / कर्तुमर्हन्ति (are worthy to do) / जीवाः (living beings) / सौभाग्यशालिनः (fortunate)
shambhu_gita::218.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::218.essence: Only fortunate beings with divine qualities enter supreme physical bodies.
shambhu_gita::218.simple_meaning: Only fortunate living beings who carry divine qualities can enter the best physical bodies.
shambhu_gita::218.simple_insight: Some states of being are available only to those prepared by inner qualities.
shambhu_gita::218.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that only fortunate living beings who possess divine qualities can inhabit the highest forms of physical bodies, indicating a special readiness or merit needed for such an embodiment.
shambhu_gita::218.insight: It highlights that external forms are accessed through inner readiness and qualities, not by chance.

shambhu_gita::219.verse_sanskrit:
तत्वज्ञा एव ते देव्याः सम्पत्तेरधिकारिणः।
नूनं धर्मस्य नित्यस्य सार्वभौमस्वरूपकम् ॥
shambhu_gita::219.verse_hindi: यहां देवीसम्पत्ति के अधिकारी तत्त्वज्ञानी वे जीव ही सनातनधर्म के सार्वभौम स्वरुप को समझने के निःसन्देह अधिकारी हो सकते हैं
shambhu_gita::219.english_translation: Only those who truly know reality are rightly qualified to possess the wealth of the divine feminine and understand the eternal, sovereign nature of dharma.
shambhu_gita::219.translation_literal: तत्वज्ञा (knowers of reality) / एव (alone) / ते (those) / देव्याः (of the divine feminine) / सम्पत्तेरधिकारिणः (are qualified to possess) / नूनं (indeed) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / नित्यस्य (eternal) / सार्वभौमस्वरूपकम् (sovereign nature)
shambhu_gita::219.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::219.essence: True understanding of reality alone grants rightful claim to eternal dharma’s power.
shambhu_gita::219.simple_meaning: Only those who deeply understand reality can truly possess the lasting power of the divine energy and grasp the eternal nature of dharma.
shambhu_gita::219.simple_insight: Knowing reality gives you rightful access to enduring strength and purpose.
shambhu_gita::219.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that the true guardians of the divine feminine's power and the eternal law are those who have realized the essence of reality itself. Without this clear understanding, no one can claim true ownership of lasting dharma.
shambhu_gita::219.modern_relevance: When you seek lasting purpose or power, it comes not from surface actions but from deeply knowing what truly is — your own reality.
shambhu_gita::219.insight: It teaches you to value deep clarity about reality as the foundation for rightful authority and spiritual strength.

shambhu_gita::220.verse_sanskrit:
वेदितुं शक्नुवन्तीह नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
भूयो भेदानराणाञ्च नारीणां वो ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥
shambhu_gita::220.verse_hindi: इसमें कुछ विचार करने की बात नहीं है, पुनः मैं नर नारियों का भेद आपलोगों से कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::220.english_translation: There is no need to consider this further; again I declare to you the distinctions between men and women.
shambhu_gita::220.translation_literal: वेदितुं (to know) शक्नुवन्तीह (here able) नात्र (not here) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (consideration) । / भूयो (again) भेदानराणाञ्च (distinctions of men and women) नारीणां (of women) वो (to you) ब्रवीम्यहम् (I speak) ॥
shambhu_gita::220.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::220.essence: A restatement of gender distinctions is announced without further discussion.
shambhu_gita::220.simple_meaning: I will now again explain the differences between men and women, with no need for further thought.
shambhu_gita::220.simple_insight: Sometimes a clear statement repeats what is already known without elaboration.
shambhu_gita::220.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the audience, signaling he will restate the distinctions between men and women without inviting further debate. This sets up a forthcoming explanation, not a teaching by itself.
shambhu_gita::220.insight: This verse prepares the listener for a detailed explanation rather than giving a direct teaching.

shambhu_gita::221.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिधा ज्ञेया नरा नार्यों भेदात्तैगुण्यगोचरात् ।
भवन्ति पितरस्तेषु सात्त्विका गुणमोहिताः ॥
shambhu_gita::221.verse_hindi: त्रिगुण सम्बन्धी भेद के अनुसार नर और नारी तीन प्रकार के जानने चाहिये, हे पितरो! उनमें से सात्त्विक गुणमोहित
shambhu_gita::221.english_translation: Men and women should be known in three ways, based on the three qualities; among them, the fathers are deluded by the quality of goodness.
shambhu_gita::221.translation_literal: त्रिधा (threefold) ज्ञेया (should be known) नरा (men) नार्यों (and women) भेदात् (due to distinction) तैगुण्य-गोचरात् (due to being objects of three qualities) भवन्ति (are) पितरः (fathers) तेषु (among them) सात्त्विका (of goodness quality) गुण-मोहिताः (deluded)
shambhu_gita::221.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::221.essence: Even goodness can blind those who are attached to it among human types.
shambhu_gita::221.simple_meaning: People are understood in three types based on qualities, but fathers are confused by the quality of goodness.
shambhu_gita::221.simple_insight: Sometimes the best qualities can also cause confusion or misunderstanding.
shambhu_gita::221.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta explains that men and women are classified by the three qualities—sattva, rajas, and tamas—but fathers in particular are misled by the quality of goodness, hinting at a common human confusion regarding pure qualities.
shambhu_gita::221.modern_relevance: You notice how even the kindest intentions can sometimes cloud judgment, leading to confusion in relationships.
shambhu_gita::221.insight: It reveals how attachment to a single quality, even a positive one, can distort clear understanding.

shambhu_gita::222.verse_sanskrit:
राजसा रूपमुग्धाश्च तामसाः काममोहिताः ।
मिथुनीभूतकाले हि जायते त्रिविधा दशा ॥
shambhu_gita::222.verse_hindi: राजसिक रूपमोहित और तामसिक नर नारी काममोहित होते हैं। मिथुनीभूत काल में तीन दशा होती है
shambhu_gita::222.english_translation: Men and women are deluded by passion and desire in the mode of passion and by attachment in the mode of ignorance. In the time of pairing, three states arise.
shambhu_gita::222.translation_literal: राजसा (by passion) रूपमुग्धाश्च (deluded by form) तामसाः (by ignorance) काममोहिताः (deluded by desire) । मिथुनीभूतकाले (in the time of pairing) हि (indeed) जायते (arises) त्रिविधा (threefold) दशा (states) ॥
shambhu_gita::222.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::222.essence: Intimacy often brings three confusing states shaped by passion and attachment.
shambhu_gita::222.simple_meaning: People become confused by desire and attachment during times of intimate union, experiencing three different states.
shambhu_gita::222.simple_insight: Desire and confusion often cloud clarity when close bonds form.
shambhu_gita::222.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that during intimate pairing, humans influenced by passion and ignorance experience three distinct mental states, each clouding perception differently due to desire or attachment.
shambhu_gita::222.modern_relevance: When relationships deepen, you might find your clarity blurred by strong emotions and attachments.
shambhu_gita::222.insight: Recognize how passion and ignorance shape your reactions in close relationships, allowing clearer awareness.

shambhu_gita::223.verse_sanskrit:
प्राकृताऽऽद्या दशैवास्ति द्वितीया विकृतात्मिका । 
तृतीयोन्मादरूपैव सत्यमेतन्न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::223.verse_hindi: यथा प्राकृत दशा, विकृत दशा और उन्माद दशा यह सत्य है इसमें सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::223.english_translation: There are indeed three states: the natural state, the altered state, and the state of madness; this truth is without doubt.
shambhu_gita::223.translation_literal: प्राकृताऽऽद्या (natural first) / दशैवास्ति (states indeed are) / द्वितीया (second) / विकृतात्मिका (altered-natured) / तृतीयोन्मादरूपैव (third madness-like indeed) / सत्यमेतन्न (this truth) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::223.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::223.essence: Experience arises in three fundamental states: natural, distorted, and madness without doubt.
shambhu_gita::223.simple_meaning: There exist three clear states of existence: the original natural state, a distorted state, and a state of madness, and this is certain.
shambhu_gita::223.simple_insight: Recognizing these three states helps you see how your experience shifts beyond mere appearances.
shambhu_gita::223.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that all experience can be categorized into three fundamental conditions: the original natural state of being, an altered or distorted state, and an extreme state of madness or delusion. This classification is presented as an undeniable truth.
shambhu_gita::223.modern_relevance: When your mood swings unexpectedly or your thoughts feel wild, you can identify which state of mind you're in and respond wisely.
shambhu_gita::223.insight: It teaches you to recognize the nature of your mental states instead of being caught by them automatically.

shambhu_gita::224.verse_sanskrit:
प्राकृतस्यैव भावस्य नरा नार्यश्च सात्त्विकाः ।
राजसा विकृतस्यैव ह्युन्मादस्य तु तामसाः ॥
shambhu_gita::224.verse_hindi: सत्त्वगुण के नरनारी प्राकृत, रजोगुण के विकृत और तमोगुण के
shambhu_gita::224.english_translation: Men and women of sattva are natural; those of rajas are distorted; those of tamas are mad.
shambhu_gita::224.translation_literal: प्राकृतस्यैव (natural indeed) भावस्य (nature/state) नरा (men) नार्यश्च (and women) सात्त्विकाः (of sattva) । राजसा (by rajas) विकृतस्यैव (distorted indeed) हि (indeed) उन्मादस्य (madness) तु (but) तामसाः (of tamas) ॥
shambhu_gita::224.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::224.essence: Your true nature is pure; imbalance causes distortion and madness.
shambhu_gita::224.simple_meaning: People who embody sattva (purity) are natural and balanced by nature. Those influenced by rajas (activity) become distorted, and those under tamas (inertia) become confused or mad.
shambhu_gita::224.simple_insight: You can feel grounded knowing your core nature is pure despite confusion or disturbance.
shambhu_gita::224.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that men and women who embody sattva quality are naturally balanced and true to themselves. Those dominated by rajas show distorted behavior, and tamas leads to madness or confusion. This verse helps distinguish inherent nature from temporary states.
shambhu_gita::224.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed or restless, remember these are temporary states; your true nature remains calm and natural beneath.
shambhu_gita::224.insight: Recognize that your core nature is pure and stable, while moods of confusion or restlessness are temporary and caused by shifting qualities.

shambhu_gita::225.verse_sanskrit:
जायन्ते पितरः ! नूनं प्रकृत्या पक्षपातिनः ।
उन्मादरूपाऽवस्था स्यान्नूनं नरकदा तथा ॥
shambhu_gita::225.verse_hindi: हे पितरो! तमोगुण के स्वाभाव ही से उन्मादभाव के पक्षपाती होते हैं । उन्माद नरक प्रद
shambhu_gita::225.english_translation: O ancestors! By their very nature, they are biased toward madness; such madness leads certainly to the lower realm.
shambhu_gita::225.translation_literal: जायन्ते (are born) / पितरः (ancestors) / नूनं (certainly) / प्रकृत्या (by nature) / पक्षपातिनः (biased) / उन्मादरूपाऽवस्था (a state of madness) / स्यान्नूनं (indeed) / नरकदा (leading to the lower realm) / तथा (thus)
shambhu_gita::225.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::225.essence: Natural bias toward madness leads to suffering and descent into the lower realm.
shambhu_gita::225.simple_meaning: Ancestors naturally tend toward a biased state of madness, which leads to suffering in the lower realm.
shambhu_gita::225.simple_insight: Bias rooted in nature can cause uncontrolled states that bring suffering.
