shambhu_gita::225.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses ancestors, saying their natural tendency is to favor madness, a state that results in suffering or the lower realm. It warns of the consequences of such deep confusion and imbalance.
shambhu_gita::225.insight: Recognize how ingrained biases can escalate into harmful mental states and lead to negative consequences.

shambhu_gita::226.verse_sanskrit:
स्वर्गदा विकृताऽवस्था प्राकृता मुक्तिदायिनी ।
यतो नास्त्येव सम्बन्धः सृष्टेरुत्पन्नकारिणः ॥
shambhu_gita::226.verse_hindi: विकृत स्वर्गप्रद और प्राकृत दशा ही मुक्तिप्रद है। क्योंकि विकार और सृष्टि उत्पन्न कारी
shambhu_gita::226.english_translation: The altered heavenly state and the natural state both grant freedom, because there is no attachment to the creator of the manifested world.
shambhu_gita::226.translation_literal: स्वर्गदा (heavenly-giving) विकृताऽवस्था (altered state) प्राकृता (natural) मुक्तिदायिनी (freedom-giving) यतः (because) नास्त्य (there is not) एव (indeed) सम्बन्धः (attachment) सृष्टेः (of creation) उत्पन्नकारिणः (originator/creator)
shambhu_gita::226.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::226.essence: Freedom exists when you have no attachment to the creator of the manifested world.
shambhu_gita::226.simple_meaning: Both an altered divine state and the natural state can bring freedom because freedom comes when you have no attachment to the source of the world.
shambhu_gita::226.simple_insight: Freedom grows when you stop clinging to who or what made everything.
shambhu_gita::226.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that true freedom is found beyond all attachment, whether in a transformed heavenly state or the natural condition, because freedom means not being bound to the creator of all that exists.
shambhu_gita::226.modern_relevance: You feel stuck when you cling to the idea that your identity or success depends on forces outside you, but real freedom comes when you release that need.
shambhu_gita::226.insight: It teaches you to loosen emotional and mental ties to the origin of your circumstances, opening a space for inner freedom.

shambhu_gita::227.verse_sanskrit:
नूनमष्टप्रकारस्य मैथुनस्य तथैव च ।
विकारस्यापि तस्यां वै प्राकृतायां न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::227.verse_hindi: अष्ट प्रकार मैथुन का भी सम्बन्ध प्राकृत दशा में नहीं ही रहता है यह निःसन्देह ही है।
shambhu_gita::227.english_translation: There is no doubt that the eight types of union and their transformations do not persist in the natural state.
shambhu_gita::227.translation_literal: नूनम् (indeed) अष्ट (eight) प्रकारस्य (types) मैथुनस्य (of union) तथैव (also) च (and) विकारस्यापि (of transformation also) तस्यां (in that) वै (certainly) प्राकृतायां (natural) न (no) संशयः (doubt) ।
shambhu_gita::227.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::227.essence: The eight unions and their changes cannot endure in the true natural state.
shambhu_gita::227.simple_meaning: The eight kinds of union and their changes do not continue once things return to their natural state.
shambhu_gita::227.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing complex attachments and changes are not permanent.
shambhu_gita::227.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the eight forms of union (intimate connections or bindings) and their changes cannot persist in the true natural condition of reality. This teaching points to the impermanence of complex states when seen from pure awareness.
shambhu_gita::227.modern_relevance: You notice how intense relationships or states that once seemed permanent eventually fade away when life settles into its natural rhythm.
shambhu_gita::227.insight: It shifts your understanding from clinging to changing states toward seeing their impermanence in the natural flow of existence.

shambhu_gita::228.verse_sanskrit:
अतो हि पितरो यूयं नूनं देवगणस्तथा ।
चाञ्चल्यरहितं शुद्ध सात्त्विकं देवदुर्लभम् ॥
shambhu_gita::228.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! यही कारण है कि देवदुर्लभ चञ्चलतारहित शुद्ध सात्विक
shambhu_gita::228.english_translation: Therefore, ancestors and divine beings, you are indeed pure, steady, and rare in your goodness.
shambhu_gita::228.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) / हि (indeed) / पितरो (ancestors) / यूयं (you) / नूनं (certainly) / देवगणस्तथा (and divine beings) / चाञ्चल्यरहितं (without fickleness) / शुद्ध (pure) / सात्त्विकं (of goodness) / देवदुर्लभम् (rare among divine beings)
shambhu_gita::228.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::228.essence: Steady purity and goodness are rare and treasured qualities among noble beings.
shambhu_gita::228.simple_meaning: Ancestors and divine beings are praised here as pure, steady, and rare in their true goodness.
shambhu_gita::228.simple_insight: Steadiness and purity in character are acknowledged as rare and valuable.
shambhu_gita::228.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the narrator addresses ancestors and divine beings, highlighting their exceptional steadiness and purity, emphasizing these qualities as rare and precious among beings.
shambhu_gita::228.insight: It teaches the value of steady, unwavering purity as a rare and admirable quality.

shambhu_gita::229.verse_sanskrit:
नारीभ्यश्च नरेभ्यश्च ह्याधिकार कथञ्चन ।
कदाचिदेव केभ्यश्चिदीशते दातुमुत्तमम् ॥
shambhu_gita::229.verse_hindi: उत्तम अधिकार आपलोग और देवतागण किन्हीं नर नारियों को किसा प्रकार कदाचित् ही प्रदान कर सकते हैं
shambhu_gita::229.english_translation: Neither men nor women ever truly have the highest authority to grant the supreme.
shambhu_gita::229.translation_literal: नारीभ्यश्च (to women also) / नरेभ्यश्च (to men also) / हि (indeed) / अधिकार (authority) / कथञ्चन (in any way) / कदाचिदेव (ever) / केभ्यश्चिद् (to anyone) / ईशते (gives) / दातुम् (to give) / उत्तमम् (the highest)
shambhu_gita::229.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::229.essence: The highest authority cannot be granted by any human being.
shambhu_gita::229.simple_meaning: Neither men nor women can ever grant the supreme highest authority to anyone.
shambhu_gita::229.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing the greatest power is beyond human control or granting.
shambhu_gita::229.detailed_meaning: In a discussion about supreme authority, the narrator clarifies that no man or woman possesses the ultimate right to grant the highest power or status to others, emphasizing the limits of human control.
shambhu_gita::229.modern_relevance: You might feel pressure to control outcomes or give power, but some things are beyond human authority or influence.
shambhu_gita::229.insight: It shifts your view from trying to control ultimate outcomes to accepting limits on human power.

shambhu_gita::230.verse_sanskrit:
अल्पमैथुनसन्तुष्टौ सात्त्विकौ दम्पती तथा ।
राजसौ कामुकौ किन्तु स्तो विचारसमन्विता ॥
shambhu_gita::230.verse_hindi: सात्त्विक नरनारी अल्प मैथुन से संतुष्ट, राजसिक गण कामुक परन्तु विचारवान्
shambhu_gita::230.english_translation: Sattvic couples are content with little intimacy; Rajasic couples are desire-driven but thoughtful.
shambhu_gita::230.translation_literal: अल्पमैथुनसन्तुष्टौ (content with little intimacy) सात्त्विकौ (sattvic) दम्पती (couples) तथा (also) । राजसौ (rajasic) कामुकौ (desire-driven) किन्तु (but) स्तो (possessing) विचारसमन्विता (thoughtfulness) ॥
shambhu_gita::230.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::230.essence: Contentment with little intimacy and desire with thought can coexist in a balanced relationship.
shambhu_gita::230.simple_meaning: Couples with a pure nature feel satisfied with little intimacy, while those driven by desire still act thoughtfully.
shambhu_gita::230.simple_insight: You can balance simple satisfaction with considered desire without losing harmony.
shambhu_gita::230.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes two types of couples: those with sattvic nature who are content with minimal intimacy, and rajasic couples who desire more but maintain thoughtful behavior. This shows how temperament affects relationships.
shambhu_gita::230.modern_relevance: In relationships, some find joy in simplicity, while others seek more passion but still value respect and thoughtfulness.
shambhu_gita::230.insight: Recognize your natural balance between satisfaction and desire, and act with conscious thought in relationships.

shambhu_gita::231.verse_sanskrit:
अविचारपरौ तौ स्तस्तामसावतिकामुकौ ।
सात्त्विकौ दम्पती नूनं स्यातां ज्ञानरतौ वरौ ॥
shambhu_gita::231.verse_hindi: और तामसिक गण घोर कामासत और अविचारी होते हैं हे पितरो! श्रेष्ठ सात्त्विक नरनारी ही ज्ञान निरत
shambhu_gita::231.english_translation: The tamasic groups are deeply attached to desire and lack discernment. The best couple are the sattvic man and woman, devoted to wisdom.
shambhu_gita::231.translation_literal: अविचारपरौ (without discernment) तौ (those two) स्तः (are) तामसाः (tamasic) अतिकामुकौ (excessively desiring) । सात्त्विकौ (sattvic) दम्पती (couple) नूनं (surely) स्यातां (are) ज्ञानरतौ (engaged in knowledge) वरौ (best) ॥
shambhu_gita::231.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::231.essence: True strength lies in balanced wisdom, not in blind desire or confusion.
shambhu_gita::231.simple_meaning: Some people act without thinking and are lost in strong desires. The best are those who are calm and focused on gaining wisdom together.
shambhu_gita::231.simple_insight: There's strength in pairing clear understanding with balanced desire, not in chasing uncontrolled wants.
shambhu_gita::231.detailed_meaning: Suta explains to sages that tamasic beings are driven by uncontrolled desire and lack discernment. In contrast, the ideal couple lives in harmony through wisdom and balance, representing the sattvic quality.
shambhu_gita::231.modern_relevance: You see couples lost in impulsive wants and confusion, but those who grow together through understanding show the healthiest bond.
shambhu_gita::231.insight: It shifts focus from reacting impulsively to cultivating thoughtful, shared wisdom in relationships.

shambhu_gita::232.verse_sanskrit:
परस्परार्थिनौ तौ हि जायते पितरः ! सदा ।
राजसौ भोगनिरतौ स्वार्थिनौ भवतश्च तौ ॥
shambhu_gita::232.verse_hindi: और सदा ही वे परस्परार्थी होते हैं राजसिक गण भोग निरत और स्वार्थी होते हैं तथा
shambhu_gita::232.english_translation: The fathers are always mutually self-interested; they are rajasic, indulging in enjoyment and self-centeredness.
shambhu_gita::232.translation_literal: परस्परार्थिनौ (mutually self-interested) तौ (they) हि (indeed) जायते (are born) पितरः (fathers) सदा (always) । राजसौ (rajasic) भोगनिरतौ (indulged in enjoyment) स्वार्थिनौ (self-centered) भवतश्च (and also are) तौ (they) ॥
shambhu_gita::232.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::232.essence: Self-interest and desire create constant conflict among those who should support each other.
shambhu_gita::232.simple_meaning: The fathers are always involved in selfish desires, driven by enjoyment and self-interest.
shambhu_gita::232.simple_insight: Recognizing persistent self-interest helps you look beyond surface relationships.
shambhu_gita::232.detailed_meaning: This verse describes a group called the fathers, who are characterized by selfishness and indulgence. They are rajasic, driven by passion and desire, always seeking personal gain rather than harmony.
shambhu_gita::232.modern_relevance: In family or work, you sometimes meet people focused only on their own benefit, caught up in enjoyment and self-interest.
shambhu_gita::232.insight: It teaches you to identify self-centered motives beneath social roles and not be distracted by surface appearances.

shambhu_gita::233.verse_sanskrit:
तामसौ तौ विचारेण राहतौ च प्रमादिनौ।
अनर्थकारिणौ स्यातां कामभोगपरायणौ ॥
shambhu_gita::233.verse_hindi: तामसिकगण विचाररहित प्रमादी कामभोगपरायण और अनर्थ कारी होते हैं।
shambhu_gita::233.english_translation: Those influenced by tamas are careless and lose clarity; they become devoted only to desire and cause harm.
shambhu_gita::233.translation_literal: तामसौ (tamas-influenced) तौ (those) विचारेण (by discernment) राहतौ (free) च (and) प्रमादिनौ (careless) अनर्थकारिणौ (causing harm) स्यातां (may be) कामभोगपरायणौ (devoted to desire and enjoyment)
shambhu_gita::233.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::233.essence: Carelessness born from darkness fuels desire and leads to harmful outcomes.
shambhu_gita::233.simple_meaning: When the mind is clouded by tamas, you lose clear thinking, become careless, and get caught up only in chasing desires that cause harm.
shambhu_gita::233.simple_insight: There's a quiet danger in carelessness fueled by dullness and desire; clarity protects you from harm.
shambhu_gita::233.detailed_meaning: Shiva warns that when someone is overwhelmed by tamas—the quality of darkness and inertia—they lose discernment and become negligent. This carelessness leads them to focus only on fulfilling desires, which ultimately causes problems and harm to themselves and others.
shambhu_gita::233.modern_relevance: When you're tired, distracted, or stuck in bad habits, you might act without thinking and chase short-term pleasures that hurt your well-being.
shambhu_gita::233.insight: This verse teaches you to notice when dullness clouds your mind and to restore clarity to avoid careless harm.

shambhu_gita::234.verse_sanskrit:
रोचते सात्त्विकाभ्यां हि पवित्रं ज्ञानकौशलम्।
तथैव राजसाभ्याञ्च क्रियाकौशलमद्भुतम् ॥
shambhu_gita::234.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! सात्त्विक नरनारी पवित्र ज्ञान कौशल, राजसिक अद्भुत क्रिया कौशल
shambhu_gita::234.english_translation: Pure wisdom skill pleases the true beings of sattva; wonderful skill in action pleases those of rajas.
shambhu_gita::234.translation_literal: रोचते (pleases) सात्त्विकाभ्यां (to the pure beings) हि (indeed) पवित्रं (pure) ज्ञानकौशलम् (skill in wisdom)। तथैव (likewise) राजसाभ्याञ्च (to those of rajas) क्रियाकौशलमद्भुतम् (wonderful skill in action) ॥
shambhu_gita::234.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::234.essence: Different natures delight in either pure wisdom or skillful action.
shambhu_gita::234.simple_meaning: Clear, pure understanding pleases the calm and steady nature; skillful, effective action pleases the active and restless nature.
shambhu_gita::234.simple_insight: You can find joy both in quiet wisdom and in dynamic, skillful doing.
shambhu_gita::234.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that beings dominated by sattva (calm clarity) find joy in pure wisdom, while those dominated by rajas (active energy) find joy in skillful action. This shows how different temperaments appreciate different expressions of excellence.
shambhu_gita::234.modern_relevance: When your mind is calm, you appreciate thoughtful clarity; when restless, you find satisfaction in well-done tasks.
shambhu_gita::234.insight: Recognize whether your nature seeks wisdom or action, then cultivate skill accordingly to find fulfillment.

shambhu_gita::235.verse_sanskrit:
पितरस्तामसाभ्यान्तु भावः पाशविकः सदा ।
नैवात्र विस्मयः कार्यः सन्देहो वा कदाचन ॥
shambhu_gita::235.verse_hindi: और तामसिक पाशवभाव के सदा पक्षपाती होते हैं, इसमें कभी विस्मय अथवा सन्देह नहीं करना चाहिये
shambhu_gita::235.english_translation: Those with a dull, animalistic nature are always biased; there is never cause for wonder or doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::235.translation_literal: पितरः (ancestors/fathers) तामसाभ्यान्तु (from darkness/dullness) भावः (disposition) पाशविकः (animalistic) सदा (always) । नैवात्र (never here) विस्मयः (wonder) कार्यः (should be) सन्देहो (doubt) वा (or) कदाचन (ever) ॥
shambhu_gita::235.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::235.essence: Dull, instinct-driven minds are always biased without cause for surprise or doubt.
shambhu_gita::235.simple_meaning: People dominated by dullness and base instincts always act with bias; it’s natural and no cause for doubt or surprise.
shambhu_gita::235.simple_insight: It’s freeing to accept that some attitudes come from deep nature, not from personal choice.
shambhu_gita::235.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that those influenced by tamas, the quality of dullness and inertia, naturally show animal-like biased behavior. This is a fixed trait, not something to be unexpectedly questioned or doubted in daily interactions.
shambhu_gita::235.modern_relevance: You notice some people always react with stubborn bias and never seem to question their views—it’s just how their mind works.
shambhu_gita::235.insight: Recognize bias rooted in dullness as a fixed inner tendency, reducing frustration and misplaced expectations.

shambhu_gita::236.verse_sanskrit:
सात्त्विकाः स्युर्नरा नार्यो ध्रुवं धीराः स्वभावतः
राजसाश्चञ्चला एवमुन्मादा इव तामसाः ॥
shambhu_gita::236.verse_hindi: सात्त्विक नरनारी स्वभाव से ही धीर, राजसिक चञ्चल और तामसिक उन्मादप्राय होते हैं
shambhu_gita::236.english_translation: People and women of sattva nature are naturally steady, those of rajas are restless, and those of tamas are prone to madness.
shambhu_gita::236.translation_literal: सात्त्विकाः (of sattva) स्युर्नरा (are men) नार्यो (and women) ध्रुवं (steadily) धीराः (wise) स्वभावतः (by nature) राजसाश्चञ्चला (of rajas restless) एवम् (thus) उन्मादा (madness) इव (like) तामसाः (of tamas)
shambhu_gita::236.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::236.essence: People's behavior flows naturally from their dominant quality: steadiness, restlessness, or confusion.
shambhu_gita::236.simple_meaning: People naturally show qualities of steadiness, restlessness, or madness depending on their dominant nature.
shambhu_gita::236.simple_insight: We often act in ways shaped deeply by our basic nature, beyond immediate control.
shambhu_gita::236.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how human behavior varies according to the three qualities: sattva brings steadiness, rajas causes restlessness, and tamas tends toward madness. This sets the stage for understanding how nature influences action and mind.
shambhu_gita::236.modern_relevance: You notice some people stay calm under pressure, others fidget constantly, while some seem overwhelmed and confused.
shambhu_gita::236.insight: Recognizing your dominant nature helps you understand your habitual responses and work with them rather than fight them.

shambhu_gita::237.verse_sanskrit:
प्रेमिकाः सात्त्विका नित्यं राजसाः कुटिलाः स्मृताः । 
निर्लज्जास्तामसा ज्ञेयाः सत्यमेतद्रवीमि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::237.verse_hindi: सात्त्विक नरनारी नित्य प्रेमिक, राजसिक कुटिल और तामसिक निर्लज्ज होते हैं। यह मैं आपलोगों से सत्य कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::237.english_translation: Sattvic men and women are always devoted lovers; rajasic ones are deceitful; tamasic ones are shameless. This I declare to you as truth.
shambhu_gita::237.translation_literal: प्रेमिकाः (lovers) सात्त्विका (pure) नित्यं (always) राजसाः (passionate) कुटिलाः (deceitful) स्मृताः (remembered) । निर्मलज्जास्तामसा (shameless, ignorant) ज्ञेयाः (should be known) सत्यमेतद् (this truth) रवीमि (I say) वः (to you) ॥
shambhu_gita::237.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::237.essence: True devotion reflects pure clarity; deceit and shamelessness arise from restless or dull natures.
shambhu_gita::237.simple_meaning: People with pure qualities love genuinely and constantly; those with restless or dull qualities tend to be deceitful or shameless.
shambhu_gita::237.simple_insight: You feel clarity in knowing true love is sincere and free of deceit or shamelessness.
shambhu_gita::237.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that lovers with sattvic nature are always sincere and devoted. Those with rajasic nature act with cunning, and tamasic individuals behave shamelessly. This teaching clarifies the quality of devotion based on inner nature.
shambhu_gita::237.modern_relevance: You notice how some people love openly and honestly, while others hide motives or behave without respect, reflecting their inner state.
shambhu_gita::237.insight: It teaches you to see love’s quality as a reflection of inner clarity or confusion, helping you choose sincere connections.

shambhu_gita::238.verse_sanskrit:
सात्त्विकाः सङ्गमेऽध्यात्मलक्ष्यकाश्च परस्परम् ।
आनन्ददा राजसास्तु कामसौख्यैकलक्ष्यकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::238.verse_hindi: सात्त्विक नरनारी को संगम दशा में अध्यात्म लक्ष्य और एक दूसरे के आनन्द में तत्परता, और राजसिक गण को एकमात्र कामज सुख लक्ष्य और भोग में तत्परता
shambhu_gita::238.english_translation: In the union of a sattvic man and woman, the focus is on spiritual goals and mutual joy, while rajasic groups seek only sensual pleasure and gratification.
shambhu_gita::238.translation_literal: सात्त्विकाः (sattvic) सङ्गमेऽ (in union) अध्यात्मलक्ष्यकाः (spiritual goal seekers) च (and) परस्परम् (each other) । आनन्ददा (joy-giving) राजसास्तु (rajasic indeed) कामसौख्यैकलक्ष्यकाः (sensual pleasure single goal seekers) ॥
shambhu_gita::238.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::238.essence: Union can be for deep shared joy or merely fleeting sensual pleasure.
shambhu_gita::238.simple_meaning: When two people connect with a pure heart, they share spiritual joy and mutual care, unlike those who focus only on physical pleasure.
shambhu_gita::238.simple_insight: True connection feels uplifting and meaningful beyond temporary desires.
shambhu_gita::238.detailed_meaning: Shiva contrasts two ways of union: sattvic couples unite with spiritual focus and mutual joy, while rajasic groups pursue only sensual pleasure. This highlights how intention shapes the quality of relationships.
shambhu_gita::238.modern_relevance: You might notice relationships around you that either deepen your growth or just chase momentary excitement without lasting meaning.
shambhu_gita::238.insight: It teaches you to distinguish relationships that foster lasting joy from those based solely on desire.

shambhu_gita::239.verse_sanskrit:
रता भोगे तामसास्तु स्वस्वलक्ष्याः प्रमादिनः।
सात्त्विकानां नराणां हि नारीणामपि तादृशाम् ॥
shambhu_gita::239.verse_hindi: और तामसिक गण को केवल अपना अपना लक्ष्य और प्रमाद जनित सुख में तत्परता रहती है। हे पितृगण! सात्विक नरनारियों के चित्त में ही
shambhu_gita::239.english_translation: Those influenced by darkness are absorbed only in their own goals and careless pleasures; even in the minds of pure men and women, such tendencies arise.
shambhu_gita::239.translation_literal: रता (attached) / भोगे (to pleasures) / तामसास्तु (those of darkness) / स्वस्वलक्ष्याः (own goals) / प्रमादिनः (careless) / सात्त्विकानां (of the pure) / नराणां (men) / हि (indeed) / नारीणामपि (also women) / तादृशाम् (such)
shambhu_gita::239.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::239.essence: Even pure minds can fall into careless attachment to selfish pleasures.
shambhu_gita::239.simple_meaning: Some people get caught up in selfish goals and careless pleasures, even good men and women sometimes fall into this.
shambhu_gita::239.simple_insight: You can feel the pull of shallow desires even when your intention is pure.
shambhu_gita::239.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how those dominated by tamas (darkness) focus only on personal gain and careless enjoyment. Even people with good nature (sattva) are not immune to such distractions in their minds.
shambhu_gita::239.modern_relevance: You planned your day well but found yourself distracted by social media and cravings, losing sight of what matters.
shambhu_gita::239.insight: Recognize careless desires early so you can return focus to your true purpose and avoid slipping into distraction.

shambhu_gita::240.verse_sanskrit:
चित्तेष्वेव प्रकाशेत ह्यात्मज्ञानं तथैव च ।
पूर्णस्वरूपं धर्मस्य नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
shambhu_gita::240.verse_hindi: आत्मज्ञान और धर्म का पूर्ण स्वरूप प्रकाशित हो सकता है। इसमें विचार नहीं करना चाहिये
shambhu_gita::240.english_translation: Self-knowledge and the complete nature of dharma shine only in the heart; they should not be subjected to intellectual speculation.
shambhu_gita::240.translation_literal: चित्तेष्वेव (in the heart alone) प्रकाशेत (shines) हि (indeed) आत्मज्ञानं (self-knowledge) तथैव (similarly) च (also) / पूर्णस्वरूपं (complete nature) धर्मस्य (of dharma) नत्र (not here) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (speculation/thinking)
shambhu_gita::240.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::240.essence: True self-knowledge and dharma reveal themselves within, beyond mental speculation.
shambhu_gita::240.simple_meaning: Self-knowledge and the full meaning of your purpose arise clearly in your heart, beyond intellectual thought.
shambhu_gita::240.simple_insight: You can trust your inner knowing without overthinking it.
shambhu_gita::240.detailed_meaning: In a teaching moment, Shiva explains that true understanding of the self and dharma cannot be grasped by mental speculation but is revealed directly in the heart's light.
shambhu_gita::240.modern_relevance: You sit quietly, trying to solve your life's purpose by thinking hard, but the real answer comes from a calm inner awareness, not mental chatter.
shambhu_gita::240.insight: Shift from overanalyzing to sensing your inner truth directly without mental interference.

shambhu_gita::241.verse_sanskrit:
दम्पत्योर्वर्तते नूनं नराणां हि प्रधानता ।
अतो हि पितरः ! सर्वगुणानां संविकाशने ॥
shambhu_gita::241.verse_hindi: स्त्रीपुरुष में पुरुष का ही सर्वथा प्राधान्य है इस कारण हे पितृगण ! सवगुणों के विकास में विद्वानों के द्वारा
shambhu_gita::241.english_translation: Among a married couple, the man holds primary importance for the full development of all virtues, O ancestral beings.
shambhu_gita::241.translation_literal: दम्पत्योर्वर्तते (in a married couple) / नूनं (indeed) / नराणां (of men) / हि (certainly) / प्रधानता (primacy) / अतो (therefore) / हि (indeed) / पितरः (O ancestral beings) / सर्वगुणानां (of all virtues) / संविकाशने (for the development)
shambhu_gita::241.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::241.essence: This verse claims men are foremost in developing virtues within marriage.
shambhu_gita::241.simple_meaning: In a marriage, this verse says the man is considered primarily responsible for the growth of virtuous qualities.
shambhu_gita::241.simple_insight: It feels like a fixed social role defining virtue growth by gender, which may not apply universally.
shambhu_gita::241.detailed_meaning: This verse addresses the traditional view that in a married couple, the man is foremost for cultivating virtues, appealing to ancestral authority. It reflects cultural assumptions rather than universal truths, limiting standalone applicability.
shambhu_gita::241.insight: It shows how social roles can shape expectations about who nurtures virtues, encouraging reflection on these assumptions.

shambhu_gita::242.verse_sanskrit:
कर्त्तव्यं पुरुषाणां वै मन्यतेऽभ्यधिकं बुधैः ।
प्रकृया चं, प्रवृत्त्या च तुल्या धर्मेण चेत्पुनः ॥
shambhu_gita::242.verse_hindi: पुरुष का दायित्व ही अधिक माना गया है। स्त्री, और पुरुष यदि समान प्रकृति, प्रवृत्ति और धर्मवाले होकर
shambhu_gita::242.english_translation: The duty of a person is regarded as supreme by the wise; when nature, disposition, and purpose are equal, duty is the measure.
shambhu_gita::242.translation_literal: कर्त्तव्यं (duty) पुरुषाणां (of persons) वै (indeed) मन्यतेऽभ्यधिकं (considered supreme) बुधैः (by the wise) । प्रकृया (by nature) चं (and) प्रवृत्त्या (disposition) च (and) तुल्या (equal) धर्मेण (by duty/purpose) चेत्पुनः (again) ॥
shambhu_gita::242.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::242.essence: When nature, disposition, and purpose are equal, duty is the supreme guide for action.
shambhu_gita::242.simple_meaning: When a person's nature, inclination, and purpose are alike, their duty is considered most important by the wise.
shambhu_gita::242.simple_insight: You feel clarity when your duty matches your true nature and deepest purpose.
shambhu_gita::242.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that for persons who share equal natural qualities, dispositions, and dharma, their duty becomes the ultimate guide. This clarifies how to prioritize action when internal factors are balanced.
shambhu_gita::242.modern_relevance: You face a choice where your skills, desires, and values align perfectly. Now choosing what to do feels natural and right.
shambhu_gita::242.insight: It teaches you to recognize when your inner qualities align, making your current duty the highest priority.

shambhu_gita::243.verse_sanskrit:
प्रभवेर्युनरा नार्यो धर्तु सात्त्विकलक्षणम् ।
तदर्थ सुलभा मुक्ति का कथाभ्युदयस्य वै ॥
shambhu_gita::243.verse_hindi: सात्विक लक्षणों को धारण कर सके तो उनके लिये अभ्युदय की तो बात ही क्या है मुक्ति भी अति सुलभ है
shambhu_gita::243.english_translation: If one can embody the qualities of sattva, then liberation is extremely easy, and the rise to prosperity is assured.
shambhu_gita::243.translation_literal: प्रभवेर्युनरा (for the rise and prosperity) / नार्यो (for women) / धर्तु (to hold/maintain) / सात्त्विकलक्षणम् (the qualities of sattva) / तदर्थ (for that reason) / सुलभा (easy) / मुक्ति (liberation) / का (what) / कथाभ्युदयस्य (of the rise of the story) / वै (indeed)
shambhu_gita::243.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::243.essence: Embodying pure qualities makes freedom naturally simple and inevitable.
shambhu_gita::243.simple_meaning: Living with pure, sattvic qualities makes liberation very accessible, even effortless.
shambhu_gita::243.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing purity naturally opens the door to freedom.
shambhu_gita::243.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that if a person can sustain the qualities of sattva—purity, harmony, and clarity—they no longer need to struggle for liberation; their spiritual rise and freedom become easy and natural.
shambhu_gita::243.modern_relevance: You notice how staying calm and clear helps you overcome challenges with less resistance and stress.
shambhu_gita::243.insight: It shifts focus to cultivating inner purity as the foundation for effortless spiritual progress.

shambhu_gita::244.verse_sanskrit:
समानधर्मप्रकृतिप्रवृत्ती दम्पती परम् ।
जगत्यां नैव जायते विशिष्टां मत्कृपां बिना ॥
shambhu_gita::244.verse_hindi: परन्तु समान प्रकृति प्रवृत्ति और धर्म के दम्पती संसार में मेरी विशेष कृपा बिना नहीं हो सकता
shambhu_gita::244.english_translation: Still, a couple united by similar nature and duty cannot arise in the world without my special grace.
shambhu_gita::244.translation_literal: समानधर्मप्रकृतिप्रवृत्ती (similar-nature-duty-activity) / दम्पती (couple) / परम् (indeed) / जगत्यां (in the world) / नैव (not at all) / जायते (arises) / विशिष्टां (special) / मत्कृपां (my grace) / बिना (without)
shambhu_gita::244.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::244.essence: Even natural unions rely on a special grace beyond nature and duty.
shambhu_gita::244.simple_meaning: A couple sharing similar nature and duty cannot come into the world without Shiva's special grace.
shambhu_gita::244.simple_insight: Even natural bonds depend on a higher kindness beyond the obvious.
shambhu_gita::244.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even when two people share the same nature and purpose, their coming together as a couple depends on his special grace, highlighting the divine influence behind relationships.
shambhu_gita::244.insight: Recognize that meaningful relationships often depend on unseen support beyond personal effort.

shambhu_gita::245.verse_sanskrit:
प्राप्नुतो जन्म चेत्सन्तौ ज्ञानिभक्ताबुभावपि ।
तदैवैवविधो योगो लोकातीतः प्रजायते ॥
shambhu_gita::245.verse_hindi: यदि दोनों ही मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त होकर जन्मग्रहण करें तब ही ऐसा लोकातीत मेल हो सकता है
shambhu_gita::245.english_translation: Only when one is born both a wise person and a devotee does the transcendental union arise.
shambhu_gita::245.translation_literal: प्राप्नुतो (is attained) जन्म (birth) चेत् (if) सन्तौ (both) ज्ञानि (wise) भक्त (devotee) अभुभावपि (being) तदा (then) एवैव (certainly) विधो (union) योगो (yoga) लोकातीतः (beyond worlds) प्रजायते (is born)
shambhu_gita::245.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::245.essence: Highest freedom arises only when wisdom and devotion unite within you.
shambhu_gita::245.simple_meaning: True spiritual freedom happens only when a person embodies both deep wisdom and devoted love at once.
shambhu_gita::245.simple_insight: You feel complete and free when your understanding and devotion grow together.
shambhu_gita::245.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that the highest spiritual state, beyond all worlds, arises only when a person is both truly wise and truly devoted. This union of wisdom and devotion is rare and leads to transcendence.
shambhu_gita::245.modern_relevance: When you balance clear understanding with heartfelt care, your sense of freedom and peace deepens beyond everyday concerns.
shambhu_gita::245.insight: It shifts your practice from focusing on just knowing or just feeling to integrating both for true inner freedom.

shambhu_gita::246.verse_sanskrit:
यतश्चैवंविधे योगेऽनेक विघ्ना भवन्त्यलम् ।
किञ्चिदत्रापि वक्ष्येऽहं श्रूयतां पितृभिर्बुधैः ॥
shambhu_gita::246.verse_hindi: क्योंकि ऐसे मेल में विघ्न बहुत ही होते हैं इस विषय में मैं कुछ वर्णन करता हूँ विद्वान् पितृगण सुनें
shambhu_gita::246.english_translation: Because in such a union many obstacles arise, I will now describe some; let the wise ancestors hear.
shambhu_gita::246.translation_literal: यतः (because) च (and) एवम् (thus) विधे (in the method) योगे (union) अनेक (many) विघ्ना (obstacles) भवन्ति (arise) अलम् (much) । किञ्चिद् (some) अत्र (here) अपि (also) वक्ष्यामि (I will speak) अहम् (I) श्रूयताम् (let hear) पितृभिः (by ancestors) बुधैः (wise) ॥
shambhu_gita::246.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::246.essence: Many obstacles arise in this practice; recognizing them prepares you to face them.
shambhu_gita::246.simple_meaning: In this kind of union or practice, many difficulties occur. I will explain some of them now for the wise ancestors to hear.
shambhu_gita::246.simple_insight: Recognizing obstacles is the first step to overcoming them with wisdom.
shambhu_gita::246.detailed_meaning: Shiva prepares to teach about the many challenges in this form of yoga or practice. He addresses wise ancestors, signaling the importance and seriousness of the upcoming explanation about obstacles on the spiritual path.
shambhu_gita::246.insight: It teaches you to expect and prepare for challenges when pursuing deeper practice or union.

shambhu_gita::247.verse_sanskrit:
नराणां पितरः ! सन्ति भेदाः षोडशसङ्ख्यकाः ।
तथा भेदाश्च नारीणां षोडशैव प्रचिकीर्ता: ॥
shambhu_gita::247.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! पुरुष और स्त्री के सोलह सोलह भेद कहे गये हैं
shambhu_gita::247.english_translation: O ancestors, sixteen distinctions have been described for men and sixteen for women.
shambhu_gita::247.translation_literal: नराणां (of men) / पितरः (ancestors) / सन्ति (there are) / भेदाः (distinctions) / षोडशसङ्ख्यकाः (sixteen in number) / तथा (also) / भेदाः (distinctions) / च (and) / नारीणां (of women) / षोडशैव (exactly sixteen) / प्रचिकीर्ता: (have been declared)
shambhu_gita::247.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::247.essence: Traditional texts describe sixteen distinctions each for men and women.
shambhu_gita::247.simple_meaning: There are sixteen types of distinctions described for men and sixteen for women.
shambhu_gita::247.simple_insight: Recognizing distinctions can help understand human nature better.
shambhu_gita::247.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the sages, stating that traditional teachings describe sixteen distinct types or categories for men and sixteen for women, setting up a classification but without deeper teaching here.
shambhu_gita::247.insight: This verse highlights the presence of detailed classifications but does not teach a universal principle itself.

shambhu_gita::248.verse_sanskrit:
शशो मृगो वराहोऽश्वो नृणामेताश्चतुर्विधाः।
जातयः खलु वर्तन्ते नात्र कार्योऽतिविस्मयः ॥
shambhu_gita::248.verse_hindi: शश, मृग, वराह और अश्व ये पुरुष की चार जातियां हैं इसमें अति विस्मय न करें
shambhu_gita::248.english_translation: The four classes of men are the hare, the deer, the boar, and the horse; do not be overly surprised by this.
shambhu_gita::248.translation_literal: शशो (hare) / मृगो (deer) / वराहः (boar) / अश्वः (horse) / नृणाम् (of men) / एताः (these) / चतुर्विधाः (four types) / जातयः (classes) / खलु (indeed) / वर्तन्ते (exist) / नात्र (here not) / कार्यः (cause) / अतिविस्मयः (excessive wonder)
shambhu_gita::248.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::248.essence: Men naturally fall into different types symbolized by animals; this is not surprising.
shambhu_gita::248.simple_meaning: There are four types of men symbolized by animals; this classification is normal and not surprising.
shambhu_gita::248.simple_insight: Recognizing different human types helps us accept natural diversity without judgment.
shambhu_gita::248.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes four symbolic classes of men named after animals, implying natural differences in nature and behavior that should not cause surprise or confusion.
shambhu_gita::248.insight: It teaches to accept natural human differences as normal rather than shocking or strange.

shambhu_gita::249.verse_sanskrit:
प्रत्येकमेव प्रत्येकान्तर्भावेनैव जातयः ।
षोडशधा प्रजायन्ते पुरुषाणां न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::249.verse_hindi: प्रत्येक जाति में ही प्रत्येक का अन्तर्भाव होने से ही पुरुष की  सोलह प्रकार को जाति होती है यह निःसन्देह है
shambhu_gita::249.english_translation: Each type exists within every other type, so the sixteen types arise in people without doubt.
shambhu_gita::249.translation_literal: प्रत्येक (each) एव (indeed) प्रत्येकान्तर्भावेनैव (within every other) जातयः (types) । षोडशधा (sixteenfold) प्रजायन्ते (are born) पुरुषाणां (of persons) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
shambhu_gita::249.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::249.essence: Every person fully contains all sixteen types within themselves without exception.
shambhu_gita::249.simple_meaning: Every person includes all sixteen types within themselves completely and without exception.
shambhu_gita::249.simple_insight: You are not just one type; many qualities coexist inside you together.
shambhu_gita::249.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the sixteen classifications or types of people are not separate but fully contained within each individual, revealing the complex nature of human identity beyond simple categories.
shambhu_gita::249.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems one way, but inside, many qualities and contradictions coexist quietly together.
shambhu_gita::249.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself or others as fixed types to recognizing complex, simultaneous inner diversity.

shambhu_gita::250.verse_sanskrit:
पद्मिनी चित्रिणी चैव शङ्खिनी हस्तिनी तथा ।
 एवं चतुर्विधा गीता जातयो योषितामपि ॥
shambhu_gita::250.verse_hindi: पद्मिनी, चित्रिणी शंखिनी  और हस्तिनी स्त्रियों की भी ये चार जातियां प्रसिद्ध हैं
shambhu_gita::250.english_translation: There are also four well-known classes of women: Padmini, Chitrini, Shankhini, and Hastini.
shambhu_gita::250.translation_literal: पद्मिनी (Padmini) / चित्रिणी (Chitrini) / चैव (also) / शङ्खिनी (Shankhini) / हस्तिनी (Hastini) / तथा (and) / एवं (thus) / चतुर्विधा (fourfold) / गीता (classes) / जातयो (types) / योषितामपि (of women also)
shambhu_gita::250.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::250.essence: Ancient texts classify women into four named categories.
shambhu_gita::250.simple_meaning: Four types of women named Padmini, Chitrini, Shankhini, and Hastini are known and recognized.
shambhu_gita::250.simple_insight: This is a descriptive classification without a universal teaching.
shambhu_gita::250.detailed_meaning: Suta, the narrator, lists four categories of women—Padmini, Chitrini, Shankhini, and Hastini—as a known classification in ancient texts, without offering philosophical or ethical teaching here.
shambhu_gita::250.insight: This verse provides a cultural classification without direct guidance or insight for present-day action.

shambhu_gita::251.verse_sanskrit:
अन्तर्भावेन प्रत्येकं जायन्ते ताश्च षोड़श ।
सामानानां समानासु दाम्पत्यप्रेमबन्धनम् ॥
shambhu_gita::251.verse_hindi: प्रत्येक में अन्तर्भाव होने से प्रत्येक के चार चार भेद होकर स्त्री की सोलह जातियां होती हैं यदि इन सोलह प्रकार को पुरुषजाति और सोलह प्रकार की स्त्रीजाति में ठीक ठीक समान श्रेणी में दाम्पत्य प्रेम सम्बन्ध सृष्टि में
shambhu_gita::251.english_translation: Each contains a subtle essence that divides it into sixteen kinds; similarly, sixteen types of women arise, and when matched properly with men, these form harmonious marital love bonds.
shambhu_gita::251.translation_literal: अन्तर्भावेन (by inner essence) प्रत्येकं (each) जायन्ते (are born) ताश्च (and those) षोड़श (sixteen) । सामान्यानां (of common) समानासु (in equals) दाम्पत्यप्रेमबन्धनम् (marital love bond) ॥
shambhu_gita::251.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::251.essence: Subtle inner qualities divide beings into types that form natural love bonds when matched.
shambhu_gita::251.simple_meaning: Each type contains a subtle essence dividing it into sixteen kinds; when men and women match these types, marital love forms.
shambhu_gita::251.simple_insight: Love and relationships can reflect deep, subtle classifications beyond the obvious.
shambhu_gita::251.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that each individual has a subtle inner quality that categorizes them into sixteen types. These sixteen types for women and men form pairs that create harmonious marital love in the natural order.
shambhu_gita::251.insight: Recognize that relationships can involve complex inner compatibilities beyond surface appearances.

shambhu_gita::252.verse_sanskrit:
स्थापितं त्याज्जगत्याचेत्स्तो मोक्षाभ्युदयौ तयोः । 
नारीणामुच्चजाति भवेद्यधुभयोस्तदा ॥
shambhu_gita::252.verse_hindi: स्थापित हो तो दोनों के अभ्युदय और निःश्रेयस होते हैं। दोनो में से यदि स्त्री को जाति उच्च हो तो
shambhu_gita::252.english_translation: If a woman attains a higher caste, then both worldly prosperity and ultimate freedom are established.
shambhu_gita::252.translation_literal: स्थापितं (established) त्याज्जगत्याचेत्स् (worldly prosperity and) तो (then) मोक्षाभ्युदयौ (ultimate freedom and prosperity) तयोः (of both) । नारीणाम् (of women) उच्चजाति (higher caste) भवेत् (is) यधु (if) अभयः (higher) तदा (then) ॥
shambhu_gita::252.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::252.essence: Social caste is linked here to worldly and spiritual success, but this is context-bound.
shambhu_gita::252.simple_meaning: If a woman belongs to a higher social class, then both her worldly success and spiritual progress are established.
shambhu_gita::252.simple_insight: Social caste does not define true spiritual or worldly progress universally.
shambhu_gita::252.detailed_meaning: This verse discusses the impact of caste status on both worldly prosperity and spiritual liberation, focusing on women. It suggests a condition where higher caste leads to better outcomes, reflecting social views rather than universal spiritual truth.
shambhu_gita::252.insight: It reveals how social hierarchy can influence perceived spiritual and worldly advancement, though this is culturally specific and not a universal principle.

shambhu_gita::253.verse_sanskrit:
एतासां प्रकृतिः सप्तश्रेण्यन्तं हि यथाक्रमम् ।
सामञ्जस्यं ध्रुवं रक्षेत्क्रममभ्युदयस्य च ॥
shambhu_gita::253.verse_hindi: सात श्रेणी तक नारी की प्रकृति यथाक्रम सामञ्जस्य की अवश्य रक्षा करती है और अभ्युदय का क्रम बना रहता है
shambhu_gita::253.english_translation: The nature of women follows seven levels in order, always preserving harmony and the sequence of growth.
shambhu_gita::253.translation_literal: एतासां (of these) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / सप्तश्रेण्यन्तं (seven-level) / हि (indeed) / यथाक्रमम् (in order) / सामञ्जस्यं (harmony) / ध्रुवं (constant) / रक्षेत् (protects) / क्रमम् (sequence) / अभ्युदयस्य (of growth) / च (and)
shambhu_gita::253.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::253.essence: Growth unfolds in seven harmonious stages that must be preserved in order.
shambhu_gita::253.simple_meaning: There is a natural progression through seven stages that preserves harmony and the order of growth.
shambhu_gita::253.simple_insight: Growth and harmony unfold in natural stages that support each other.
shambhu_gita::253.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes a natural order consisting of seven progressive levels that maintain harmony and ensure steady growth, emphasizing the importance of preserving this sequence.
shambhu_gita::253.insight: Recognize and respect natural sequences that maintain harmony and enable progress.

shambhu_gita::254.verse_sanskrit:
ततोऽशान्तिश्च दुःखञ्च जायते रोग एव च । 
नराणामुच्चजातिश्चेत्सामञ्जस्यं यथाक्रमम् ॥
shambhu_gita::254.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर अशान्ति दुःख और रोग होता है। यदि पुरुष की जाति उच्च होतो अभ्युदय का यथाक्रम
shambhu_gita::254.english_translation: Then unrest, suffering, and disease arise; if a man's birth is high, his progress follows accordingly.
shambhu_gita::254.translation_literal: ततः (then) अशान्ति (unrest) च (and) दुःखञ्च (suffering) जायते (arises) रोग (disease) एव (also) च (and) । नराणाम् (of men) उच्चजातिश्च (high birth) चेत् (if) सामञ्जस्यं (progress) यथाक्रमम् (according to order) ॥
shambhu_gita::254.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::254.essence: Unrest and suffering arise, but your inherent nature directs your progress.
shambhu_gita::254.simple_meaning: Unrest, suffering, and disease naturally arise in life, but a person's inherent nature guides their progress.
shambhu_gita::254.simple_insight: Even in hardship, who you are determines how you grow and move forward.
shambhu_gita::254.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that life inevitably brings unrest, suffering, and illness. However, a person's inherent qualities or birth influence how they respond and progress through these challenges.
shambhu_gita::254.modern_relevance: You wake up feeling overwhelmed by stress or pain, yet your character and values decide how you navigate the day.
shambhu_gita::254.insight: Recognize that hardship is natural, but your inner nature shapes your response and growth.

shambhu_gita::255.verse_sanskrit:
सम्यगभ्युदयस्यास्ते तर्हि श्रेणीत्रयावधि ।
सामन्जस्यस्य रक्षायां सृष्टेर्वाधा ततो भवेत् ॥
shambhu_gita::255.verse_hindi: सामञ्जस्य तीन श्रेणी तक भलीभांति रहता है तदनन्तर सृष्टि की सामञ्जस्य रक्षा में बाधा होती है
shambhu_gita::255.english_translation: Harmony is well maintained through three levels; after that, obstacles arise in preserving harmony in creation.
shambhu_gita::255.translation_literal: सम्यक् (well) अभ्युदयस्य (of harmony) अस्ते (there are) तर्हि (then) श्रेणीत्रयावधि (up to three levels) । सामन्जस्यस्य (of harmony) रक्षायां (in protection) सृष्टेः (of creation) बाधा (obstacle) ततो (thereafter) भवेत् (arises) ॥
shambhu_gita::255.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::255.essence: Harmony holds well within three levels; exceeding them brings obstacles.
shambhu_gita::255.simple_meaning: Harmony or balance in creation is well maintained within three stages or levels; beyond that, difficulties arise in keeping this harmony intact.
shambhu_gita::255.simple_insight: You feel how balance is delicate and needs care before disruption sets in.
shambhu_gita::255.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva explains that harmony in the universe is preserved through three distinct levels or classes. Once these are exceeded or neglected, obstacles emerge that challenge the ongoing balance of creation.
shambhu_gita::255.modern_relevance: You notice how your team works smoothly in a few clear steps, but adding more complexity soon causes friction and confusion.
shambhu_gita::255.insight: It teaches you to recognize natural limits of harmony and act to protect balance before problems grow.

shambhu_gita::256.verse_sanskrit:
स्वधर्मतश्च्युता नारी स्वधर्मादविच्युतो नरः ।
भवेद्यदि तदा सृष्टेः सामञ्जस्यं न तिष्ठति ॥
shambhu_gita::256.verse_hindi: नारीगण यदि नारी धर्म से च्युत हों और पुरुषगण पुरुषधर्म से च्युत हो तो सृष्टि का सामञ्जस्य नहीं रहता है
shambhu_gita::256.english_translation: If women abandon their own dharma and men abandon theirs, then harmony in creation cannot remain.
shambhu_gita::256.translation_literal: स्वधर्मतश्च्युता (having abandoned own dharma) / नारी (women) / स्वधर्मादविच्युतो (not having abandoned own dharma) / नरः (men) / भवेद्यदि (if there is) / तदा (then) / सृष्टेः (of creation) / सामञ्जस्यं (harmony) / न (not) / तिष्ठति (remains)
shambhu_gita::256.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::256.essence: Abandoning one's natural duty disrupts the harmony of the whole creation.
shambhu_gita::256.simple_meaning: When women and men leave their natural duties, the balance of the world breaks.
shambhu_gita::256.simple_insight: You see how abandoning your role affects the whole community's harmony.
shambhu_gita::256.detailed_meaning: The verse warns that if women and men both neglect their own natural duties, the harmony that holds the world together falls apart, emphasizing the importance of each person fulfilling their appropriate roles.
shambhu_gita::256.modern_relevance: When individuals ignore their responsibilities in families or communities, relationships and social balance suffer.
shambhu_gita::256.insight: It teaches you to recognize the importance of fulfilling your role for collective harmony.

shambhu_gita::257.verse_sanskrit:
तपःप्रधानतामति नारीधर्मों यतः सदा ।
यज्ञमधानतामेवं नृणां धर्म इति श्रुतिः ॥
shambhu_gita::257.verse_hindi: क्योंकि सदा नारीधर्म तपः प्रधान है और पुरुषधर्म यज्ञ प्रधान है यही श्रुति है
shambhu_gita::257.english_translation: Because women’s duty is primarily austerity, and men’s duty is primarily sacrifice, so the scriptures say.
shambhu_gita::257.translation_literal: तपःप्रधानतामति (austerity is primary) / नारीधर्मों (women's duty) / यतः (because) / सदा (always) / यज्ञमधानतामेवं (sacrifice is primary) / नृणां (men's) / धर्म (duty) / इति (thus) / श्रुतिः (scripture)
shambhu_gita::257.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::257.essence: Ancient texts assign austerity to women and sacrifice to men as their main duties.
shambhu_gita::257.simple_meaning: Tradition says women's main duty involves austerity, while men's main duty involves sacrifice.
shambhu_gita::257.simple_insight: This verse reflects traditional roles that divide duties by gender, which may not apply universally.
shambhu_gita::257.detailed_meaning: This verse states a traditional teaching that assigns austerity as the chief duty of women and sacrifice as the chief duty of men, reflecting a cultural belief about gender roles in dharma.
shambhu_gita::257.insight: Recognize how ancient teachings often assigned different duties based on gender, which may conflict with modern views.

shambhu_gita::258.verse_sanskrit:
हीश्च श्रीर्मधुरा वाणी त्रिविधा च पवित्रता।
निःस्वार्थश्च सतीभावो वात्सल्यं सेवनादरः ॥
shambhu_gita::258.verse_hindi: नारी के लिये ही, श्री, मधुर वचन, विविध पवित्रता, स्वार्थरहित पातिव्रत्य, वात्सल्यभाव, सेवापरायणता
shambhu_gita::258.english_translation: For a woman, the divine is sweet speech, threefold purity, selfless chastity, motherly love, and devoted service.
shambhu_gita::258.translation_literal: हीश्च (for woman) श्रीर्मधुरा (divine sweet) वाणी (speech) त्रिविधा (threefold) च (and) पवित्रता (purity) । निःस्वार्थश्च (selfless) सतीभावो (chastity) वात्सल्यं (motherly love) सेवनादरः (devoted service) ॥
shambhu_gita::258.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::258.essence: This verse lists traditional feminine virtues without broader philosophical claim.
shambhu_gita::258.simple_meaning: A woman embodies sweet speech, three kinds of purity, selfless chastity, motherly affection, and devoted service.
shambhu_gita::258.simple_insight: This verse describes qualities traditionally linked to women, without universal philosophical teaching here.
shambhu_gita::258.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes ideal qualities associated with women, including purity and devotion. The focus is on traditional feminine virtues rather than a universal spiritual teaching.
shambhu_gita::258.insight: This verse reflects cultural ideals rather than a universal insight applicable beyond gender roles.

shambhu_gita::259.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुषोचितभावानामङ्गीकारे सदाऽचिः ।
नारीणां हि गुणा अष्टावुत्तमाः कीर्तिता इमे ॥
shambhu_gita::259.verse_hindi: और पुरुषों के उपयोगी भावों में भावित होने में सदा अरुचि ये आठ ही उत्तमगुण कहे गये हैं
shambhu_gita::259.english_translation: Men are always averse to embracing these eight excellent qualities praised in women.
shambhu_gita::259.translation_literal: पुरुषोचितभावानाम् (men's-appropriate feelings) अङ्गीकारे (acceptance) सदाऽचिः (always aversion) । नारीणां (women's) हि (indeed) गुणा (qualities) अष्टावुत्तमाः (eight excellent) कीर्तिता (praised) इमे (these) ॥
shambhu_gita::259.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::259.essence: Resistance to noble qualities doesn’t diminish their true value or praise.
shambhu_gita::259.simple_meaning: Sometimes people resist accepting noble qualities, even when those qualities are praised and valuable.
shambhu_gita::259.simple_insight: There’s a tension between what feels natural to resist and what is truly excellent.
shambhu_gita::259.detailed_meaning: Shiva points out that men often feel aversion to accepting certain noble qualities, here described as eight praised virtues associated with women, highlighting a conflict between social bias and acknowledged excellence.
shambhu_gita::259.modern_relevance: You may notice yourself or others resisting qualities like patience or gentleness, even though these traits bring real strength and harmony.
shambhu_gita::259.insight: It teaches you to notice your resistance to valuable qualities and open to their true worth.

shambhu_gita::260.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुषाणान्तु सर्वेषां पितरः! सन्ततं भृशम् । 
स्वस्ववर्णाश्रमाचारपालनं गुण उत्तमः ॥
shambhu_gita::260.verse_hindi: और हे पितृगण ! सब पुरुषों के लिये सर्वदा अपने अपने वर्णाश्रमाचार का पालन ही उत्तमगुण कहा गया है।
shambhu_gita::260.english_translation: And O ancestors, for all people, always following their own duties and social roles is considered the highest virtue.
shambhu_gita::260.translation_literal: पुरुषाणाम् (of men) अन्तु (indeed) सर्वेषाम् (all) पितरः (ancestors)! सन्ततं (always) भृशम् (greatly) स्वस्व (own) वर्णाश्रमाचारपालनं (observance of caste and stage duties) गुण (virtue) उत्तमः (the best).
shambhu_gita::260.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::260.essence: True virtue arises from faithfully living your own life duties and roles.
shambhu_gita::260.simple_meaning: Always following your own duties and social roles is considered the best quality for every person.
shambhu_gita::260.simple_insight: There is strength and goodness in sincerely living your own role as it is meant to be.
shambhu_gita::260.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestral beings, highlighting that for all people, consistently following their specific social and life duties—varnashramadharma—is regarded as the highest virtue, emphasizing commitment to one's rightful role amid society and life stages.
shambhu_gita::260.modern_relevance: You feel the pressure to compare yourself or live someone else’s life, but your true strength lies in embracing your own responsibilities fully.
shambhu_gita::260.insight: This verse teaches to focus fully on your own path and responsibilities, not to imitate or envy others.

shambhu_gita::261.verse_sanskrit:
योषितां पुरुषाणाश्च परीक्षाऽतीव दुर्गमा ।
ऋतम्भरायुता भक्ता ज्ञानिनो मे यथार्थतः ॥
shambhu_gita::261.verse_hindi: स्त्री और पुरुष परीक्षा बहुत ही कठिन है । ऋतम्भरा युक्त मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त ही यथार्थ रूप से
shambhu_gita::261.english_translation: Testing women and men is extremely difficult; only my true wise devotees who uphold truth endure it fully.
shambhu_gita::261.translation_literal: योषितां (of women) / पुरुषाणाम् (of men) / परीक्षा (test) / अतीव (very) / दुर्गमा (difficult) / ऋतम्भरायुता (upholders of truth) / भक्ता (devotees) / ज्ञानिनः (wise ones) / मे (my) / यथार्थतः (truly)
shambhu_gita::261.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::261.essence: True devotion and wisdom make enduring difficult tests possible.
shambhu_gita::261.simple_meaning: Testing men and women is very hard, but those who are truly devoted and wise overcome these challenges by upholding truth.
shambhu_gita::261.simple_insight: Facing hard challenges feels less heavy when you hold devotion and wisdom as your foundation.
shambhu_gita::261.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that testing both men and women is extremely difficult. Only those who are truly devoted to him and have wisdom, who live by truth, can withstand these tests without faltering.
shambhu_gita::261.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed when life tests your character through relationships and responsibilities, but staying true and devoted helps you stand firm.
shambhu_gita::261.insight: It teaches you to meet life's toughest challenges with steady devotion and unwavering commitment to truth.

shambhu_gita::262.verse_sanskrit:
पितरः ! दम्पती नूनं शक्नुवन्ति परीक्षितुम् ।
अन्यः कोऽपि न शक्नोति सत्यमेतद्भवीमि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::262.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण! स्त्री परीक्षा , और पुरुष परीक्षा करने में समर्थ हैं और कोई भी समर्थ नहीं हो सकता। यह मैं अपलोगों से सत्य कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::262.english_translation: O ancestors! Couples alone are capable of true testing; no one else can truly test you. This I speak to you with truth.
shambhu_gita::262.translation_literal: पितरः (ancestors) / दम्पती (couples) / नूनं (indeed) / शक्नुवन्ति (are capable) / परीक्षितुम् (to test) / अन्यः (any other) / कोऽपि (anyone) / न (not) / शक्नोति (is able) / सत्यमेतद्भवीमि (this is true, I speak) / वः (to you)
shambhu_gita::262.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::262.essence: Only couples have the unique power to truly test and reveal each other.
shambhu_gita::262.simple_meaning: Only couples have the real ability to truly test and understand each other; no one else can do this for them.
shambhu_gita::262.simple_insight: True understanding and testing come only within the bond of a couple, not from outsiders.
shambhu_gita::262.detailed_meaning: The narrator addresses the ancestors, pointing out that only a married couple can genuinely test and understand each other’s true nature, emphasizing the unique intimacy and challenge of that relationship.
shambhu_gita::262.modern_relevance: You might notice only your partner truly sees and challenges who you are in ways no one else can.
shambhu_gita::262.insight: Recognize that deep personal challenges and growth often happen uniquely within intimate partnerships, not from external judgments.

shambhu_gita::263.verse_sanskrit:
सामुद्रिकैस्तथा ज्योति शास्त्रैश्चैव स्वरोदयैः।
एवं बहुविधैांगैः परीक्ष्येतेऽत्र दम्पती ॥
shambhu_gita::263.verse_hindi: इस जगत में सामुद्रिक विद्या, स्वरोदयविद्या और ज्योतिष विद्या से और इस प्रकार के नेक मार्गों से स्त्री पुरुष परीक्षा की जाती है
shambhu_gita::263.english_translation: In this world, couples are tested by palmistry, voice science, astrology, and many such noble methods.
shambhu_gita::263.translation_literal: सामुद्रिकैः (by palmistry) तथा (also) ज्योति (light/astrology) शास्त्रैः (sciences) च (and) एव (indeed) स्वर (voice) उदयैः (rising) / एवं (thus) बहुविधैः (many kinds) अंगैः (methods) परीक्ष्येते (are tested) अत्र (here) दम्पती (couple)
shambhu_gita::263.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::263.essence: Couples are examined through many external traditional methods.
shambhu_gita::263.simple_meaning: Couples are evaluated through various traditional sciences like palmistry, voice analysis, and astrology.
shambhu_gita::263.simple_insight: People often rely on many external methods to understand relationships and character.
shambhu_gita::263.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta describes how, in the world, couples undergo scrutiny by various traditional sciences such as palmistry, voice reading, and astrology. These diverse methods are used to assess compatibility or character.
shambhu_gita::263.modern_relevance: You might notice how people look for signs or tests to judge relationships or personalities before committing.
shambhu_gita::263.insight: It shows how external measures are often used to assess inner qualities, prompting reflection on where true understanding lies.

shambhu_gita::264.verse_sanskrit:
कर्त्तु दाम्पससम्बन्धं कैवल्याभ्युदयेच्छुभिः ।
तेषां नामानि कथ्यन्ते येषाम्हर्या विचारणा ॥
shambhu_gita::264.verse_hindi: दाम्पत्य सम्बन्ध करने के लिये अभ्युदय और कैवल्येच्छुओं को जिन बातों का विचार करना चाहिये उनके नाम कहे जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::264.english_translation: The names of considerations for those seeking marriage and those desiring liberation are described.
shambhu_gita::264.translation_literal:
कर्त्तु (for doing) दाम्पससम्बन्धं (marital relation) कैवल्याभ्युदयेच्छुभिः (for those desiring liberation and prosperity) ।
तेषां (their) नामानि (names) कथ्यन्ते (are told) येषाम्हर्या (whose considerations) विचारणा (consideration) ॥
shambhu_gita::264.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::264.essence: Choosing marriage or liberation requires understanding specific important considerations.
shambhu_gita::264.simple_meaning: This verse lists topics to consider for those wanting marriage or liberation.
shambhu_gita::264.simple_insight: There are clear factors to reflect on before choosing marriage or liberation.
shambhu_gita::264.detailed_meaning: The narrator introduces the subjects of marriage and liberation, outlining that specific considerations or qualities are important for each path, setting the stage for detailed teachings.
shambhu_gita::264.insight: It signals the need to understand key factors before committing to major life paths like marriage or spiritual freedom.

shambhu_gita::265.verse_sanskrit:
कुलं देहो गणो योनिग्रहो राशिदिनन्तथा ।
स्त्रीदीर्घश्चैव माहेन्द्रो राशीशो रज्जुवश्यकौ ॥
shambhu_gita::265.verse_hindi: कुल शरीर, गण, योनि, ग्रह, राशि, दिन, माहेन्द्र, स्त्री दीर्घ, राशि का अधिपति, रज्जु. वश्य
shambhu_gita::265.english_translation: The body, family, groups, origin, planets, constellations, lunar mansions, the lord of constellations, and the bond of control.
shambhu_gita::265.translation_literal: कुलं (family) देहो (body) गणो (groups) योनिग्रहो (origin-planet) राशिदिनन्तथा (constellations, days, and so forth) । स्त्रीदीर्घश्चैव (woman-length also) माहेन्द्रो (lord of the lunar mansion) राशीशो (lord of the constellation) रज्जुवश्यकौ (rope-control) ॥
shambhu_gita::265.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::265.essence: A list of physical, social, and celestial categories without a teaching.
shambhu_gita::265.simple_meaning: Lists various concepts like body, family, groups, origins, planets, constellations, and control mechanisms, without teaching or narrative.
shambhu_gita::265.simple_insight: This verse names elements but offers no standalone insight.
shambhu_gita::265.detailed_meaning: This verse enumerates various categories such as the body, family, celestial influences, and control bonds, likely as part of a larger explanation but does not itself convey a teaching.
shambhu_gita::265.insight: No direct teaching or insight; the verse is descriptive or classificatory.

shambhu_gita::266.verse_sanskrit:
वेधश्च वर्णकूटञ्च भूतलिङ्गाख्यकूटकम् ।
नाड़ी च योगिनीगोत्रं जातिश्च पक्षिकूटकम् ॥
shambhu_gita::266.verse_hindi: वेध, वर्णकूट, नाडी, भूतलिङ्गायकूट योगिनी गोत्र, जाति, पाक्षि कूटक
shambhu_gita::266.english_translation: Vedha, Varnakuta, Nadi, Bhutalingakuta, Yogini gotra, Jati, Pakshi kutakam.
shambhu_gita::266.translation_literal: वेध (Vedha) / च (and) / वर्णकूट (Varnakuta) / च (and) / भूतलिङ्गाख्यकूटकम् (called Bhutalingakuta) / नाड़ी (Nadi) / च (and) / योगिनीगोत्रं (Yogini gotra) / जातिश्च (and caste) / पक्षिकूटकम् (Pakshi kutakam)
shambhu_gita::266.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::266.essence: This verse names various classifications without explanation or teaching.
shambhu_gita::266.simple_meaning: This verse lists various names or categories without further explanation or teaching.
shambhu_gita::266.simple_insight: A list alone does not offer insight without context or explanation.
shambhu_gita::266.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Suta enumerates several terms—Vedha, Varnakuta, Nadi, Bhutalingakuta, Yogini gotra, Jati, Pakshi kutakam—likely classifications or groups, but without additional context or teaching.
shambhu_gita::266.insight: Recognize that not all verses carry direct teachings; some set the stage or catalog concepts.

shambhu_gita::267.verse_sanskrit:
तारा तथा भकूटश्च प्रवृत्तिवृद्धिरेव च ।
इन्द्रियाणां तथा दाढयं भावश्च पञ्चविंशकः ॥
shambhu_gita::267.verse_hindi: तारा, भकूट, प्रवृत्ति, इन्द्रिय दाय, बुद्धि और पच्चीसा भाव
shambhu_gita::267.english_translation: Tara, Bhakoota, Pravrtti, the strength of the senses, intellect, and the twenty-five states.
shambhu_gita::267.translation_literal: तारा (Tara) / तथा (and) / भकूटश्च (Bhakoota also) / प्रवृत्तिवृद्धिरेव (the increase of activity indeed) / च (and) / इन्द्रियाणां (of the senses) / तथा (also) / दाढयं (strength) / भावश्च (and states) / पञ्चविंशकः (twenty-five)
shambhu_gita::267.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::267.essence: Many subtle inner energies and faculties combine to shape experience.
shambhu_gita::267.simple_meaning: This verse lists various subtle energies or states, including Tara, Bhakoota, activity, senses' strength, intellect, and twenty-five elements.
shambhu_gita::267.simple_insight: Complex inner forces combine to shape your experience and understanding.
shambhu_gita::267.detailed_meaning: The verse names subtle inner forces and faculties such as Tara and Bhakoota, the increase of activity (Pravrtti), the power of senses, intellect, and twenty-five states that compose the inner experience, revealing the complex makeup of the mind and body.
shambhu_gita::267.insight: Recognize that your mind and senses involve many interacting layers and states influencing your actions and awareness.

shambhu_gita::268.verse_sanskrit:
अधिकारे समाने चेत्स्थापितः पितरो भवेत् ।
सौम्यो दाम्पससम्बन्धोऽभ्युदयस्य तु का कथा ॥
shambhu_gita::268.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! यदि समान अधिकार में कल्याणकारी दाम्पत्य सम्बन्ध स्थापित हो तो अभ्युदय की तो बात ही क्या है
shambhu_gita::268.english_translation: O ancestors, if a beneficial marital bond is established with equal rights, then what is there to discuss about prosperity?
shambhu_gita::268.translation_literal: अधिकारे (in equal rights) समाने (equal) चेत् (if) स्थापितः (established) पितरो (ancestors) भवेत् (would be) । सौम्यो (beneficial) दाम्पससम्बन्धः (marital relation) अभ्युदयस्य (of prosperity) तु (then) का (what) कथा (talk) ॥
shambhu_gita::268.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::268.essence: Equal and kind relationships naturally lead to shared prosperity.
shambhu_gita::268.simple_meaning: If a fair and kind marital relationship exists with equal rights, prosperity naturally follows without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::268.simple_insight: Harmony in relationships built on equality eases worries about success and well-being.
shambhu_gita::268.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the sages, suggesting that when marital relationships are founded on equal rights and kindness, prosperity is a natural outcome, implying the importance of fairness in social bonds.
shambhu_gita::268.insight: It encourages valuing equality and kindness in relationships as foundations for collective well-being.

shambhu_gita::269.verse_sanskrit:
मोक्षोऽपि सुलभस्ताहि नैव कार्योऽत्र विस्मयः ।
एवंविधै हि दाम्पसे सञ्जते जायते ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::269.verse_hindi: निःश्रेयस भी सुलभ है इसमें, विस्मय नहीं ही करना चाहिये। ऐसा दम्पति सम्बन्ध होने पर ही
shambhu_gita::269.english_translation: Freedom from rebirth is also easy here; there is no need to be surprised. This is certain when such a marital relationship exists.
shambhu_gita::269.translation_literal: मोक्षः (liberation) अपि (also) सुलभः (easy) ताहि (in this) नैव (not at all) कार्यः (cause for) विस्मयः (surprise) । एवंविधै (in such a way) हि (indeed) दाम्पसे (in marital relationship) सञ्जते (arises) जायते (certainly) ध्रुवम् (fixed, definite) ॥
shambhu_gita::269.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::269.essence: Lasting inner freedom naturally arises from a devoted marital relationship.
shambhu_gita::269.simple_meaning: True freedom from the cycle of rebirth is easy to attain through a stable, devoted marital relationship. There is no reason to be surprised by this.
shambhu_gita::269.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing that committed love naturally leads to lasting freedom.
shambhu_gita::269.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva explains that achieving liberation (moksha) is surprisingly accessible when a couple shares a devoted, harmonious relationship. The certainty of freedom arises naturally from such a bond, showing that spiritual progress can come through relational harmony.
shambhu_gita::269.modern_relevance: You notice how deep trust and commitment with your partner creates a calm space where old worries lose their grip and genuine freedom feels possible.
shambhu_gita::269.insight: It shifts your view to see that spiritual freedom can grow through healthy, loving relationships, not just solitary practice.

shambhu_gita::270.verse_sanskrit:
मत्सधानाविभूतीनां देवानां भवतां तथा ।
ऋषीणाञ्चैव सर्वेषां सर्वथैव प्रसन्नता ॥
shambhu_gita::270.verse_hindi: मेरे प्रधान विभूतिरूपी आप लोगों की सब देवताओं की और सब ऋषियों की भी सब प्रकार से ही प्रसन्नता होती है
shambhu_gita::270.english_translation: As the supreme being, I am the cause of all gods' and sages' complete happiness in every way.
shambhu_gita::270.translation_literal: मत्सधानाविभूतीनां (of supreme beings) / देवानां (of gods) / भवतां (your) / तथा (also) / ऋषीणां (of sages) / चैव (and indeed) / सर्वेषां (of all) / सर्वथैव (in every way) / प्रसन्नता (happiness).
shambhu_gita::270.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::270.essence: The supreme being is the source of all beings' complete happiness in every way.
shambhu_gita::270.simple_meaning: You are the supreme presence who brings happiness to all divine beings and sages in every way.
shambhu_gita::270.simple_insight: Knowing you are the source of universal joy brings a deep feeling of connectedness and reverence.
shambhu_gita::270.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares himself as the supreme source of happiness for all deva beings and sages. This moment reveals his cosmic role as the inner cause of their peace and joy.
shambhu_gita::270.modern_relevance: When you recognize that your presence can uplift those around you deeply, you feel more connected and responsible for shared well-being.
shambhu_gita::270.insight: It shifts the view to see yourself as a source of joy and inspiration, not just a separate individual.

shambhu_gita::271.verse_sanskrit:
जन्मभूमिमैवेद्धन्या पवित्रञ्च कुलं तयोः !।
तौ स्वयं ज्ञानिनी सन्ता स्तः सार्वभौमधर्मिणौ ॥
shambhu_gita::271.verse_hindi: उनका कुल पवित्र होता है, जन्मभूमि धन्य होती, है और या तो वे स्वयं शानवान् होकर सार्वभौम धर्म के अधिकारी बनते हैं
shambhu_gita::271.english_translation: Their lineage is pure and their birthplace blessed; they themselves become wise and uphold universal righteousness.
shambhu_gita::271.translation_literal: जन्मभूमिमैव (birthplace only) / एव (indeed) / धन्या (blessed) / पवित्रञ्च (and pure) / कुलं (lineage) / तयोः (of those two) / तौ (they) / स्वयं (themselves) / ज्ञानिनी (wise) / सन्ता (become) / स्तः (are) / सार्वभौमधर्मिणौ (holders of universal righteousness)
shambhu_gita::271.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::271.essence: A pure origin naturally leads to wisdom and rightful conduct.
shambhu_gita::271.simple_meaning: Those with a pure birthplace and lineage become wise and uphold universal righteousness.
shambhu_gita::271.simple_insight: There’s pride and strength in knowing your foundation shapes your character and values.
shambhu_gita::271.detailed_meaning: Shiva praises those whose ancestral home and family are sacred; such people naturally develop wisdom and uphold the highest moral standards in society.
shambhu_gita::271.modern_relevance: You feel grounded and confident when your upbringing and roots support values that guide your choices rightly.
shambhu_gita::271.insight: Recognize how your background influences your sense of duty and encourages living by universal principles.

shambhu_gita::272.verse_sanskrit:
अथवा सन्तति लब्ध्वा पूर्णज्ञानरलकृताम् ।
विश्वमेतत् प्रकुर्वन्तौ धन्यं धन्यौ च तो स्वयम् ॥
shambhu_gita::272.verse_hindi: नहीं तो पूर्ण ज्ञान से अलंकृत सन्तति को प्राप्त करके वह इस जगत् को धन्य करते हुए स्वयं भी धन्य होते हैं।
shambhu_gita::272.english_translation: Or by attaining a lineage adorned with complete knowledge, they bless this entire world and themselves become blessed.
shambhu_gita::272.translation_literal: अथवा (or) सन्तति (lineage/descendants) लब्ध्वा (having obtained) पूर्णज्ञान (complete knowledge) रलकृताम् (adorned) । विश्वमेतत् (this world) प्रकुर्वन्तौ (they make/do) धन्यं (blessed) धन्यौ (blessed) च (and) तो (they) स्वयम् (themselves) ॥
shambhu_gita::272.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::272.essence: Wisdom in your descendants blesses the world and returns blessing to you.
shambhu_gita::272.simple_meaning: If you gain descendants filled with full understanding, you bless the world and yourself through them.
shambhu_gita::272.simple_insight: Knowing your influence flows through your lineage brings a deep sense of lasting blessing.
shambhu_gita::272.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that attaining a lineage enriched with complete knowledge creates a ripple of blessing beyond oneself, affecting the entire world and oneself through that knowledge-bearing family.
shambhu_gita::272.modern_relevance: You see your family's values and wisdom shaping the world around you, knowing your influence carries beyond your lifetime.
shambhu_gita::272.insight: Shift your focus from personal gain to nurturing wisdom that benefits generations and the wider world.

shambhu_gita::273.verse_sanskrit:
क्षेत्ररूपतया नारी पूर्णा धैर्यगुणैः सदा ।
कन्यायाः पितरौ नस्पाद धव्य यौ त्रिविधं सदा ॥
shambhu_gita::273.verse_hindi: नारी क्षेत्र रूपा होने से सदा धैर्यगुणों से पूर्ण है इस कारण जो पिता माता सदा ही कन्या के त्रिविध धैर्य की
shambhu_gita::273.english_translation: A woman is like a field, always full of patience; her parents always honor her threefold patience.
shambhu_gita::273.translation_literal: क्षेत्ररूपतया (like a field) नारी (woman) पूर्णा (full) धैर्यगुणैः (with patience virtues) सदा (always) । कन्यायाः (of the daughter) पितरौ (parents) नस्पाद (honor) धव्य (always) यौ (two) त्रिविधं (threefold) सदा (always) ॥
shambhu_gita::273.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::273.essence: Patience in a woman is likened to fertile ground honored by her parents.
shambhu_gita::273.simple_meaning: A woman is compared to a field, always full of patience, and her parents honor her enduring patience in three ways.
shambhu_gita::273.simple_insight: Patience is honored as a sacred quality within family bonds.
shambhu_gita::273.detailed_meaning: This verse uses the metaphor of a woman as a field, emphasizing her enduring patience. It acknowledges how parents honor this threefold patience in their daughter, highlighting cultural values around feminine endurance and parental respect, without deeper philosophical teaching.
shambhu_gita::273.insight: It shows how patience is seen as a valued virtue within family relationships, but does not present a universal teaching beyond that.

shambhu_gita::274.verse_sanskrit:
रक्षितुं शक्नुतो नूनं तथा कत्तुं समुन्ननम् ।
स्वामिनो ये निजस्त्रीणां धैव्यैवा त्रिविधं सदा ॥
shambhu_gita::274.verse_hindi: रक्षा और उन्नति में समर्थ होते हैं अथवा जो पति सदा अपनी स्त्री के विविध धैर्य को
shambhu_gita::274.english_translation: A husband is always capable of protecting and uplifting his wife through her threefold qualities of endurance.
shambhu_gita::274.translation_literal: रक्षितुं (to protect) शक्नुतो (is capable) नूनं (indeed) तथा (also) कत्तुं (to uplift) समुन्ननम् (exalted) स्वामिनो (of the husband) ये (who) निजस्त्रीणां (own women’s) धैव्यैवा (by endurance qualities) त्रिविधं (threefold) सदा (always)
shambhu_gita::274.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::274.essence: Protection and upliftment arise from honoring a partner’s enduring qualities.
shambhu_gita::274.simple_meaning: A husband can protect and raise his wife by recognizing and supporting her three kinds of endurance.
shambhu_gita::274.simple_insight: Strength grows when endurance is honored and supported in relationships.
shambhu_gita::274.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how a husband can protect and uplift his wife by respecting her threefold endurance. It focuses on qualities needed for sustaining relationships rather than a universal teaching for liberation.
shambhu_gita::274.modern_relevance: In partnerships, understanding and supporting your partner’s resilience builds strength and growth together.
shambhu_gita::274.insight: It shifts the focus from control to honoring the partner’s inner strengths in relationships.

shambhu_gita::275.verse_sanskrit:
स्वयं संयमिनः सन्तो नष्टं कर्तुं न चोद्यताः।
ते सदा प्राप्नुवन्सेव सदगान देवदुर्लभाम् ॥
shambhu_gita::275.verse_hindi: स्वयं संयमी रहते हुए नष्ट करने में उद्यत नहीं होते हैं वे सदा देवदुर्लभ सदगति को ही प्राप्त होते हैं।
shambhu_gita::275.english_translation: Those who control themselves do not engage in destruction and always attain the rare, divine good state.
shambhu_gita::275.translation_literal: स्वयं (self) संयमिनः (controllers) सन्तः (being) नष्टं (destruction) कर्तुं (to do) न (not) चोद्यताः (engaged) । ते (they) सदा (always) प्राप्नुवन् (attain) सेव (rare) सदगान (good state) देवदुर्लभाम् (divine rare) ॥
shambhu_gita::275.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::275.essence: Self-control prevents destructive acts and leads to rare lasting well-being.
shambhu_gita::275.simple_meaning: If you keep control over yourself, you won’t act to destroy what matters and will reach a rare and precious state of well-being.
shambhu_gita::275.simple_insight: You feel steady and safe when you don’t let impulsive destruction take over.
shambhu_gita::275.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that those who master their urges and do not rush into destructive actions achieve a rare and difficult-to-attain state of lasting goodness and peace.
shambhu_gita::275.modern_relevance: You pause instead of reacting in frustration or anger, avoiding damage to your relationships or goals and preserving your well-being.
shambhu_gita::275.insight: It teaches you to hold back destructive impulses and cultivate steady self-control for lasting benefit.

shambhu_gita::276.verse_sanskrit:
भवन्तः पितरः ! तेभ्यः स्ववाञ्छितगुणान्विताम् ।
सन्ततिञ्च बलं स्वास्थ्यं प्रयच्छन्ति स्वयं सदा ॥
shambhu_gita::276.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण! आपलोग उनको अपने वांछित गुणवाली सन्तति, बल और स्वास्थ्य सदा स्वत: प्रदान करते हो।
shambhu_gita::276.english_translation: O ancestors! You always grant them offspring with desired qualities, strength, and health by yourselves.
shambhu_gita::276.translation_literal: भवन्तः (you are) पितरः (ancestors) ! तेभ्यः (to them) स्ववाञ्छितगुणान्विताम् (with desired qualities) । सन्ततिञ्च (offspring also) बलं (strength) स्वास्थ्यं (health) प्रयच्छन्ति (give) स्वयं (by yourselves) सदा (always) ॥
shambhu_gita::276.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::276.essence: Ancestors naturally and continuously bestow desired qualities and vitality on descendants.
shambhu_gita::276.simple_meaning: Ancestors naturally provide their descendants with desired qualities, strength, and health without effort.
shambhu_gita::276.simple_insight: There is a natural flow of life where qualities and vitality are passed on effortlessly.
shambhu_gita::276.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the sages, highlighting that the ancestors inherently grant their descendants qualities, strength, and health, emphasizing the natural continuity of life and lineage without deliberate intervention.
shambhu_gita::276.insight: Recognize the effortless continuity of qualities and life through natural lineage and care.

shambhu_gita::277.verse_sanskrit:
गर्भाधानस्वरूपस्य यौ तु पीठस्य दम्पती ।
स्मरतः पितरः ! नित्यं मर्यादाच पवित्रताम् ॥
shambhu_gita::277.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! जो दम्पती गर्भाधान रुपी पीठ की मर्यादा और पवित्रता को सदा स्मरण रखते हैं
shambhu_gita::277.english_translation: O ancestors! Those couples who always remember the sanctity and dignity of the act of conception.
shambhu_gita::277.translation_literal: गर्भाधानस्वरूपस्य (of the form of conception) / यौ (couples) / तु (indeed) / पीठस्य (of the seat/place) / दम्पती (couples) / स्मरतः (remembering) / पितरः (ancestors) / नित्यं (always) / मर्यादाच (from dignity) / पवित्रताम् (sanctity)
shambhu_gita::277.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::277.essence: Couples who honor the sacredness of conception uphold dignity and purity.
shambhu_gita::277.simple_meaning: Couples who always keep in mind the sacredness and dignity of conception honor its true value.
shambhu_gita::277.simple_insight: Respecting the sacredness of life’s beginnings grounds your relationships deeply.
