shambhu_gita::596.insight: It shifts your attention from fleeting goals to a steady commitment to dharma and inner freedom, stabilizing your actions.

shambhu_gita::597.verse_sanskrit:
पुण्यवन्तस्त एवाहो वाच्यास्तेजस्विनो ननु ।
स्वभावतः प्रसीदन्ति तेषु देवर्षयो ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::597.verse_hindi: पुण्यात्मा तेजस्वी कहलाते हैं और उन पर देवताओं के तथा ऋषियों की स्वभावतः प्रसन्नता होती है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::597.english_translation: Those with virtuous nature and radiance are naturally pleasing to the deities and sages, without doubt.
shambhu_gita::597.translation_literal: पुण्यवन्तः (virtuous) त (indeed) एवाहः (are called) वाच्याः (sayings) तेजस्विनः (radiant) ननु (surely) स्वभावतः (by nature) प्रसीदन्ति (are pleased) तेषु (in them) देवर्षयः (deities and sages) ध्रुवम् (certainly)
shambhu_gita::597.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::597.essence: Virtue and inner radiance naturally attract the goodwill of higher beings.
shambhu_gita::597.simple_meaning: People with virtue and inner brightness naturally attract respect and goodwill from divine beings and wise sages.
shambhu_gita::597.simple_insight: Being virtuous shines like a light that draws respect without effort.
shambhu_gita::597.detailed_meaning: The narrator, Suta, explains that those who possess virtue and radiance naturally gain the favor of deities and sages. This sets a context for understanding the qualities that align a person with higher beings.
shambhu_gita::597.modern_relevance: When you act with genuine goodness and integrity, people around you naturally respond with respect and warmth.
shambhu_gita::597.insight: Recognize that cultivating virtue creates an effortless positive influence on your environment and relationships.

shambhu_gita::598.verse_sanskrit:
अतोऽन्तःकरणेऽध्यात्मरहस्यस्य यथाक्रमम् ।
विकाशो जायते तेषां नान कार्या विचारणा ॥
shambhu_gita::598.verse_hindi: इसी कारण उनके अन्तःकरण में अध्यात्म रहस्य का क्रमविकास होता है और
shambhu_gita::598.english_translation: Therefore, within the inner being, the secret of spirituality unfolds in a precise order of development, not by random thoughts or actions.
shambhu_gita::598.translation_literal: अतः (therefore) अन्तःकरणे (in the inner being) अध्यात्मरहस्यस्य (of the secret of spirituality) यथाक्रमम् (in proper order) विकाशो (development) जायते (arises) तेषां (of them) नान (various) कार्या (actions) विचारणा (considerations)
shambhu_gita::598.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::598.essence: Spiritual secrets unfold naturally within the inner being in an ordered sequence.
shambhu_gita::598.simple_meaning: The inner self gradually reveals spiritual secrets in an orderly way, not through random actions or thoughts.
shambhu_gita::598.simple_insight: Spiritual growth is a natural unfolding, not a scattered or forced effort.
shambhu_gita::598.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how the inner being reveals spiritual truths step by step. This moment highlights that spiritual insight is an ordered process, not chaos.
shambhu_gita::598.modern_relevance: You sense your own growth unfolding step by step, not from rushing or random effort.
shambhu_gita::598.insight: It teaches you to trust the natural sequence of inner growth rather than forcing spiritual understanding.

shambhu_gita::599.verse_sanskrit:
ततस्ते सल्लभन्तेऽन्ते मत्सायुज्यमसंशयम् ।
नैवात्र विस्मयः कार्यों भवद्भिहें स्वधाभुजः ॥
shambhu_gita::599.verse_hindi: अन्त में वे निश्चय ही मेरे सायुज्य को प्राप्त कर लेते हैं; हे पितृगण ! इसमें विस्मय न करें
shambhu_gita::599.english_translation: In the end, they certainly attain union with me; O ancestral spirits, do not be surprised at this.
shambhu_gita::599.translation_literal: ततः (then) ते (they) सल्लभन्ते (attain) अन्ते (at the end) मत् (with me) सायुज्यम् (union) असंशयम् (without doubt) । नैव (never) अत्र (here) विस्मयः (wonder) कार्यः (should be) भवत् (O you) भिहें (ancestors) स्वधाभुजः (O possessors of offerings) ॥
shambhu_gita::599.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::599.essence: Steadfast seekers inevitably unite with the divine; this outcome is certain.
shambhu_gita::599.simple_meaning: Those who follow the path ultimately unite with the divine presence; this is certain and not surprising.
shambhu_gita::599.simple_insight: There is assurance that sincere seekers will reach union, removing doubt and fear.
shambhu_gita::599.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestral spirits, affirming that ultimately those who pursue the spiritual path without wavering achieve union with him. This statement reassures that the final result is certain, inviting no surprise or doubt.
shambhu_gita::599.insight: It reassures you that persistent spiritual effort leads to sure union with your true self, ending uncertainty.

shambhu_gita::600.verse_sanskrit:
वर्तन्ते पितरो यानि भुवनानि चतुर्दश।
ऋषीणामधिकारोऽस्ति सर्वथाऽक्षुण्ण एष्वलम् ॥
shambhu_gita::600.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! ऋषियों का अधिकार चतुर्दश भुवनों में सर्वथा अक्षरण है
shambhu_gita::600.english_translation: O ancestors! The sages' authority over the fourteen worlds is completely unbroken.
shambhu_gita::600.translation_literal: वर्तन्ते (exist) पितरो (ancestors) यानि (which) भुवनानि (worlds) चतुर्दश (fourteen) ऋषीणाम् (of sages) अधिकारः (authority) अस्ति (is) सर्वथा (completely) अक्षुण्ण (unbroken) एष्वलम् (indeed)
shambhu_gita::600.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::600.essence: Sages' authority across all worlds remains unbroken and continuous.
shambhu_gita::600.simple_meaning: The sages hold continuous and complete authority over the fourteen worlds, as declared to the ancestors.
shambhu_gita::600.simple_insight: Authority and influence extend beyond the visible, connecting realms and beings unseen.
shambhu_gita::600.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta declares that the sages maintain uninterrupted authority over all fourteen worlds, addressing the ancestral beings and establishing the cosmic order's spiritual hierarchy.
shambhu_gita::600.insight: It shows the enduring influence of wisdom across multiple layers of existence, beyond immediate perception.

shambhu_gita::601.verse_sanskrit:
यथा देवाधिकारो हि सर्वो सृष्टि समश्नुते ।
देवानुशासिता सा स्यादसुरैर्वाऽनुशासिता ॥
shambhu_gita::601.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार देवताओं का अधिकार सम्पूर्ण सृष्टि में परिव्याप्त है। चाहे दैवी अनुशासन हो, चाहे आसुरी अनुशासन हो
shambhu_gita::601.english_translation: Just as the authority of the radiant beings pervades all creation, so all is governed either by divine order or by shadowy rule.
shambhu_gita::601.translation_literal: यथा (just as) देवाधिकारो (authority of devas) हि (indeed) सर्वो (all) सृष्टि (creation) समश्नुते (pervades) । देव (divine) अनुशासिता (governed) सा (that) स्याद (is) असुरैः (by asuras) वा (or) अनुशासिता (governed) ॥
shambhu_gita::601.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::601.essence: All creation is governed by either radiant order or shadowy control.
shambhu_gita::601.simple_meaning: All of creation is governed by a higher authority, either by radiant beings or shadowy forces.
shambhu_gita::601.simple_insight: You realize everything operates under some form of order, light or shadow.
shambhu_gita::601.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes how the entire universe is under authority — either the rule of radiant beings embodying divine order, or shadowy forces representing disruption. This explains why all actions and events follow some governing principle.
shambhu_gita::601.modern_relevance: You notice systems at work everywhere—some supportive, others disruptive—but all shaping what happens around you.
shambhu_gita::601.insight: Recognize that every situation arises under some form of order, guiding your response to it.

shambhu_gita::602.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्माण्डपिण्डसञजुष्टां जङ्गमस्थावरात्मिकाम् ।
सम्पूर्णा ताम्पारव्याप्य दैवी शक्तिविराजते ॥
shambhu_gita::602.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माण्ड पिण्डात्मक और जड़ चेतनात्मक सब सृष्टि में दैवी शक्ति व्याप्त है, उसी प्रकार
shambhu_gita::602.english_translation: The divine power pervades all creation, both the cosmic whole and all moving and unmoving beings.
shambhu_gita::602.translation_literal: ब्रह्माण्डपिण्डसञजुष्टां (cosmic whole and) / जङ्गमस्थावरात्मिकाम् (moving and unmoving beings) / सम्पूर्णा (entire) / ताम् (that) / पारव्याप्य (pervading) / दैवी (divine) / शक्तिविराजते (power shines)
shambhu_gita::602.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::602.essence: Divine power completely fills both the universe and all beings within it.
shambhu_gita::602.simple_meaning: The divine energy fills everything that exists, including the entire universe and all living and non-living things.
shambhu_gita::602.simple_insight: You can feel the presence of the divine everywhere, in all things around you.
shambhu_gita::602.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes how divine power is not limited but fully present in every part of the universe, both the cosmic entirety and all individual beings, moving or still.
shambhu_gita::602.insight: It shifts your view to see every object and being as infused with the same divine energy.

shambhu_gita::603.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानराज्याधिदैवानामधिकारस्तथैव हि ।
अस्ति व्याप्तः किलषणां भुवनानि चतुर्दश ॥
shambhu_gita::603.verse_hindi: ज्ञान के अधिष्ठातृ देवता ऋषियों का अधिकार, चतुर्दश, भुवन में परिव्याप्त है
shambhu_gita::603.english_translation: The rulers of knowledge and the divine beings preside over the fourteen worlds, encompassing all beings.
shambhu_gita::603.translation_literal: ज्ञानराज्याधिदैवानाम् (of the rulers of knowledge and divine beings) अधिकारः (authority) तथैव (also) हि (indeed) अस्ति (exists) व्याप्तः (pervades) किलषणाम् (of all beings) भुवनानि (worlds) चतुर्दश (fourteen).
shambhu_gita::603.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::603.essence: True knowledge and its guardians have authority over all worlds and beings.
shambhu_gita::603.simple_meaning: The divine beings who represent knowledge hold authority over all fourteen worlds, which include all beings.
shambhu_gita::603.simple_insight: Understanding that wisdom governs everything can make you feel connected and grounded in the vastness of existence.
shambhu_gita::603.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the divine beings associated with wisdom have authority over the fourteen worlds, which together encompass all beings. This shows the vast reach and power of true knowledge across existence.
shambhu_gita::603.modern_relevance: When you realize deep knowledge influences every part of life, you feel less alone and more anchored in a larger whole.
shambhu_gita::603.insight: It shifts your view to see wisdom as a universal force, giving your learning and awareness greater meaning.

shambhu_gita::604.verse_sanskrit:
किन्तु तत्रैव पिण्डेऽलं तेषां कार्य प्रकाशते।
सम्पूर्णैः पञ्चकोषाणां विकाशैर्यः प्रपूरितः ॥
shambhu_gita::604.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे पितरों ! उनका कार्य उसी पिण्ड में प्रकट होता है जो पिण्ड पञ्चकोष के पूर्ण विकास से पूर्ण होकर
shambhu_gita::604.english_translation: But their work manifests in that very body which is fully developed by the complete expansion of the five sheaths.
shambhu_gita::604.translation_literal: किन्तु (but) तत्रैव (in that very) पिण्डेऽलं (body) तेषां (their) कार्य (work/action) प्रकाशते (manifests). सम्पूर्णैः (complete) पञ्चकोषाणां (of five sheaths) विकाशैः (expansions) यः (which) प्रपूरितः (fully filled/expanded).
shambhu_gita::604.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::604.essence: True work appears only when all five inner layers are fully developed within the body.
shambhu_gita::604.simple_meaning: True action or work arises from the body only when all five layers (sheaths) of being are fully developed within it.
shambhu_gita::604.simple_insight: There is a deep completeness required inside you before your true work can be revealed.
shambhu_gita::604.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the true effects or work of beings appear only when the physical body is fully enriched by the development of five internal layers called sheaths, which together form the complete person. This moment of full inner blossoming is crucial for real action to emerge.
shambhu_gita::604.modern_relevance: You may feel stuck, waiting for the right moment; real growth and results come only when your whole being is ready inside.
shambhu_gita::604.insight: This teaching shifts your focus from external effort alone to nurturing complete inner development before expecting your work to manifest.

shambhu_gita::605.verse_sanskrit:
क्षेत्र ज्ञानविकाशस्य प्रजायेत स्वधाभुजः !।
नात्र कश्चन सन्देह ऋषीणां पूजनं ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::605.verse_hindi: ज्ञान विकास का क्षेत्र बन जाता है। परन्तु इसमें सन्देह नहीं कि, ऋषिगण
shambhu_gita::605.english_translation: The field for the growth of knowledge arises within one's own self; there is no doubt that the sages are honored for this.
shambhu_gita::605.translation_literal: क्षेत्र (field) ज्ञानविकाशस्य (of knowledge's growth) प्रजायेत (arises) स्वधाभुजः (within one's own self) । नात्र (there is no) कश्चन (any) सन्देह (doubt) ऋषीणां (of sages) पूजनं (honoring) ध्रुवम् (certain).
shambhu_gita::605.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::605.essence: True knowledge grows within your own self, honored by those who seek wisdom.
shambhu_gita::605.simple_meaning: Knowledge develops from within your own self, and it is certain that sages are respected for this inner growth.
shambhu_gita::605.simple_insight: You feel empowered knowing that wisdom arises from your own inner space, honored by those who seek truth.
shambhu_gita::605.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the true ground for knowledge to develop is the individual's own self, and that the sages are surely revered for cultivating this inner field of wisdom.
shambhu_gita::605.modern_relevance: You realize that your personal growth and understanding come from within, not from external approval or sources.
shambhu_gita::605.insight: It teaches you to trust your inner self as the real place where wisdom unfolds, beyond outside validation.

shambhu_gita::606.verse_sanskrit:
जायते निखिलेप्वेव भुवनेषु प्रतिक्षणम्।
प्रतिष्ठास्थानमास्ते मे यतो हि ज्ञानभूमयः ॥
shambhu_gita::606.verse_hindi: सब भुवनों में ही सदा पूजे जाते हैं। क्योंकि ज्ञान भूमियाँ ही मेरी प्रतिष्ठा का स्थान है
shambhu_gita::606.english_translation: In all worlds, the divine is always revered because the realms of knowledge are the true seat of its presence.
shambhu_gita::606.translation_literal: जायते (arises) / निखिलेप्वेव (in all worlds indeed) / भुवनेषु (in the worlds) / प्रतिक्षणम् (at every moment) / प्रतिष्ठास्थानम् (seat of presence) / आस्ते (exists) / मे (my) / यतः (because) / हि (indeed) / ज्ञानभूमयः (realms of knowledge)
shambhu_gita::606.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::606.essence: True presence is rooted eternally in realms of knowledge, honored everywhere without fail.
shambhu_gita::606.simple_meaning: The divine is always honored everywhere because its true foundation exists in realms of knowledge.
shambhu_gita::606.simple_insight: You belong where understanding and wisdom are alive — that is your true home and honor.
shambhu_gita::606.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares that across all worlds, the divine presence is continuously revered because its true seat is the realm of knowledge. This emphasizes the supreme importance of wisdom as the foundation of all existence and respect.
shambhu_gita::606.modern_relevance: When you are recognized at work or in life, it’s often because your knowledge and understanding form your true value and foundation.
shambhu_gita::606.insight: This shifts your focus from seeking external approval to cultivating knowledge as the lasting source of your true presence.

shambhu_gita::607.verse_sanskrit:
पितरो ज्ञानराज्यस्य विस्तीर्णस्य रहस्यकम् ।
अपूर्व भवतो वच्मि श्रूयतां सुसमाहितः ॥
shambhu_gita::607.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण! ज्ञानराज्य विस्तार का अपूर्व रहस्य मैं आप लोगों से कहता हूँ, ध्यान देकर सुनो
shambhu_gita::607.english_translation: O ancestors! I reveal to you the rare secret of the vast kingdom of wisdom; listen with full attention.
shambhu_gita::607.translation_literal: पितरो (ancestors) / ज्ञानराज्यस्य (of the kingdom of wisdom) / विस्तीर्णस्य (vast, expansive) / रहस्यकम् (secret) / अपूर्व (rare) / भवतो (yours) / वच्मि (I speak) / श्रूयतां (let it be heard) / सुसमाहितः (with good concentration)
shambhu_gita::607.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::607.essence: A rare secret of vast wisdom requires full, concentrated listening.
shambhu_gita::607.simple_meaning: I address the ancestors to share a rare and profound secret about the vast realm of wisdom; listen carefully.
shambhu_gita::607.simple_insight: There is something precious and deep waiting to be heard if you pay close attention.
shambhu_gita::607.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to the ancestors, preparing to reveal a profound and rare secret about the vast kingdom of wisdom, urging them to listen attentively to grasp its full significance.
shambhu_gita::607.insight: It invites you to focus fully and prepare yourself to receive valuable knowledge beyond ordinary understanding.

shambhu_gita::608.verse_hindi: मेरे अध्यात्मज्ञान-मूलक शास्त्रसमूह स्थूल अन्नमय कोष से सम्बन्ध रखने के समय
shambhu_gita::608.english_translation: My spiritual knowledge scriptures are rooted in the gross physical body at the time of establishing connection.
shambhu_gita::608.translation_literal: ममैव (my own) / अध्यात्मिकज्ञानमूलिकाः (spiritual knowledge-based) / शास्त्रराशयः (scripture collections) / स्थूलान्नमयकोषेण (with the gross food-based body) / सम्बन्धस्थापनक्षणे (at the moment of establishing connection)
shambhu_gita::608.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::608.essence: Spiritual knowledge is initially linked to the physical body when establishing understanding.
shambhu_gita::608.simple_meaning: The scriptures of spiritual knowledge I offer are connected to the physical body when establishing a link.
shambhu_gita::608.simple_insight: Spiritual teachings are grounded in the physical body’s experience before deeper truth unfolds.
shambhu_gita::608.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the spiritual knowledge scriptures he provides are initially connected to the physical, gross body level, showing how teachings begin grounded in the material frame before rising to subtler layers.
shambhu_gita::608.insight: Recognize that spiritual teachings often start with the body’s experience before deeper understanding arises.

shambhu_gita::609.verse_sanskrit:
स्थूलाक्षरमयै रूपैर्वर्तेरन् पुस्तकात्मकैः।
अत्र नानाविधैर्नूनं विश्वस्मिन् सम्मकाशिताः ॥
shambhu_gita::609.verse_hindi: इस संसार में अनेक प्रकार से प्रकाशित स्थूल अक्षरमय पुस्तकों के रूप में विद्यमान रहते हैं
shambhu_gita::609.english_translation: In this world, many kinds of gross, letter-based books exist, illuminating knowledge.
shambhu_gita::609.translation_literal: स्थूलाक्षरमयै (with gross letter-based) / रूपैः (forms) / वर्तेरन् (existing) / पुस्तकात्मकैः (like books) / अत्र (here/in this) / नानाविधैः (various types) / नूनं (indeed) / विश्वस्मिन् (in the world) / सम्मकाशिताः (illuminated/present)
shambhu_gita::609.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::609.essence: Many visible, letter-based books exist to share knowledge in this world.
shambhu_gita::609.simple_meaning: Many kinds of physical books made from letters exist in the world, showing varied knowledge.
shambhu_gita::609.simple_insight: The world holds many visible forms of knowledge we can access and learn from.
shambhu_gita::609.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta describes the physical presence of many letter-based books in the world, highlighting the tangible ways knowledge is shared among people.
shambhu_gita::609.insight: Recognize that knowledge appears in many forms, often as physical texts that shape understanding.

shambhu_gita::610.verse_sanskrit:
स्थूलपुस्तकपुंञ्जोऽयं यद्यप्यास्ते विनम्वरः ।
स्थूलाक्षरमयानाञ्च पुस्तकानां यथायथम् ॥
shambhu_gita::610.verse_hindi: यद्यपि स्थूल पुस्तक समूह नाशवान हैं और इस प्रकार के स्थूल अक्षरमय पुस्तक-समूह का
shambhu_gita::610.english_translation: Although this collection of physical books is perishable, the collection of physical letter-based books is likewise so.
shambhu_gita::610.translation_literal: स्थूलपुस्तकपुंञ्जोऽयं (this gross-book-collection) यद्यपि (although) अस्ते (exists) विनम्वरः (perishable) । स्थूलाक्षरमयानाञ्च (physical-letter-based) पुस्तकानां (of books) यथायथम् (likewise)
shambhu_gita::610.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::610.essence: Physical books and their letters are perishable and not eternal.
shambhu_gita::610.simple_meaning: Physical books made of letters are perishable and will eventually decay like all material things.
shambhu_gita::610.simple_insight: Even the knowledge stored in physical form is subject to decay and change.
shambhu_gita::610.detailed_meaning: The narrator Suta explains that collections of physical books, made of letters on material surfaces, are impermanent and will deteriorate over time. This points to the impermanence of physical knowledge carriers.
shambhu_gita::610.insight: Recognize that external physical sources of knowledge are temporary and cannot hold ultimate truth.

shambhu_gita::611.verse_sanskrit:
भवेतामीदृशां देशकालपात्रमभेदतः।
आविर्भारतिरोभावौ यथाकालं न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::611.verse_hindi: देश, काल और पात्र के प्रभेद से समय पर, आविर्भाव और तिरोभाव हुआ करता है,
shambhu_gita::611.english_translation: Manifestation and withdrawal happen according to place, time, and person without doubt.
shambhu_gita::611.translation_literal: भवेतामीदृशां (there would be such) / देशकालपात्रमभेदतः (without distinction of place, time, and person) / आविर्भारतिरोभावौ (manifestation and withdrawal) / यथाकालं (according to the time) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::611.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::611.essence: Manifestation and withdrawal follow place, time, and person without exception.
shambhu_gita::611.simple_meaning: Manifestation and disappearance happen naturally and depend on the place, time, and person involved.
shambhu_gita::611.simple_insight: The timing and context shape every event, beyond our control or certainty.
shambhu_gita::611.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that manifestation and withdrawal of phenomena occur inevitably according to the specific place, time, and person, highlighting the natural flow without doubt or exception.
shambhu_gita::611.modern_relevance: You notice how opportunities or feelings arise and fade depending on where you are and who you are with, not on your will.
shambhu_gita::611.insight: Accept that timing and context shape outcomes beyond your control, reducing frustration.

shambhu_gita::612.verse_sanskrit:
सूक्ष्मराज्ये तु शास्त्राणां नित्यसंस्थितिहेतवे ।
चतुर्विधानि वर्तन्ते पुस्तकान्यपराण्यपि ॥
shambhu_gita::612.verse_hindi: परन्तु सूक्ष्मराज्य में शास्त्रो की नित्य स्थिति रहने के लिये और भी चार प्रकार की  पुस्तके हैं।
shambhu_gita::612.english_translation: In the subtle realm, for the constant existence of the scriptures, there are four more types of books.
shambhu_gita::612.translation_literal: सूक्ष्मराज्ये (in the subtle realm) / तु (but) / शास्त्राणां (of scriptures) / नित्यसंस्थितिहेतवे (for eternal existence) / चतुर्विधानि (four types) / वर्तन्ते (exist) / पुस्तकानि (books) / अपराणि अपि (also others)
shambhu_gita::612.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::612.essence: Sacred knowledge endures through multiple subtle forms beyond visible texts.
shambhu_gita::612.simple_meaning: In the subtle realm, there exist four additional types of books that support the eternal presence of the scriptures.
shambhu_gita::612.simple_insight: There is more beneath the surface keeping sacred knowledge alive beyond what we see.
shambhu_gita::612.detailed_meaning: Suta describes a hidden subtle realm where scriptures persist eternally, maintained by four distinct types of books beyond the usual texts, pointing to a deeper cosmic order behind sacred teachings.
shambhu_gita::612.insight: It invites you to recognize that knowledge and wisdom often have unseen layers sustaining them.

shambhu_gita::613.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्माण्डपिण्डौ नादश्च विन्दुरक्षरमेव च ।
पञ्चप्रकारकाण्याहुः पुस्तकानि पुराविदः ॥
shambhu_gita::613.verse_hindi: इसी कारण पुस्तकों के पांच भेद हैं; यथा, ब्रह्माण्ड, पिण्ड, नाद, बिन्दु और अक्षरमय।
shambhu_gita::613.english_translation: That is why scholars say there are five categories of books: cosmos, individual, sound, point, and imperishable.
shambhu_gita::613.translation_literal: ब्रह्माण्डपिण्डौ (cosmos, individual) / नादश्च (and sound) / विन्दुरक्षरमेव (point and imperishable) / च (also) / पञ्चप्रकारकाणि (five types) / आहुः (they say) / पुस्तकानि (books) / पुराविदः (scholars)
shambhu_gita::613.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::613.essence: Spiritual knowledge is classified into five distinct categories by wise scholars.
shambhu_gita::613.simple_meaning: Scholars classify sacred texts into five types: cosmos, individual, sound, point, and imperishable categories.
shambhu_gita::613.simple_insight: Understanding categories helps organize knowledge and study effectively.
shambhu_gita::613.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta explains that ancient scholars have categorized sacred writings into five distinct types, each representing a level or aspect of spiritual knowledge, helping students understand the vast scope of teachings.
shambhu_gita::613.modern_relevance: When you explore complex topics, sorting information into clear groups makes learning manageable and meaningful.
shambhu_gita::613.insight: Recognizing knowledge categories helps structure your learning and deepens comprehension.

shambhu_gita::614.verse_sanskrit:
श्रुतिर्नादे स्म्रितिर्विन्दौ ब्रह्माण्डे तन्त्रमेव च ।
पिण्डे च वैद्यकं शास्त्रमक्षरेऽन्यदुदाहृतम् ॥
shambhu_gita::614.verse_hindi: इन पांच प्रकार की पुस्तको का एक उदाहरण बताया जाता है। नादमयी पुस्तक का उदाहरण श्रुति है, बिन्दुमयी पुस्तक का उदाहरण स्मृति है, ब्रह्माण्ड मयी पुस्तक का उदाहरण तंत्र है, पिण्डमयी पुस्तक का उदाहरण वैद्यक शास्त्र है और इनसे अतिरिक्त पृथ्वी के अन्यान्य ग्रन्थ अक्षर मयी पुस्तक के उदाहरण हैं
shambhu_gita::614.english_translation: Five types of scriptures are exemplified: sound-based is Shruti, point-based is Smriti, cosmic-based is Tantra, body-based is Ayurveda, and beyond these, other earthly texts are considered letter-based.
shambhu_gita::614.translation_literal: श्रुतिर्नादे (Shruti in sound) स्म्रितिर्विन्दौ (Smriti in point) ब्रह्माण्डे (in cosmos) तन्त्रमेव (Tantra indeed) च (and) । पिण्डे (in body) च (also) वैद्यकं (Ayurveda) शास्त्रम् (science) अक्षरेऽन्यदुदाहृतम् (letter-based other mentioned) ॥
shambhu_gita::614.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::614.essence: Sacred knowledge manifests in five symbolic forms representing distinct paths of wisdom.
shambhu_gita::614.simple_meaning: There are five kinds of scriptures symbolized by different forms: sound, point, cosmos, body, and letters representing various knowledge traditions.
shambhu_gita::614.simple_insight: Knowledge expresses itself in many forms, each guiding us in unique ways.
shambhu_gita::614.detailed_meaning: Suta explains the classification of scriptures into five categories, linking them to different symbolic forms and fields of knowledge, showing the vastness and diversity of sacred teachings.
shambhu_gita::614.modern_relevance: You encounter knowledge in many forms—from spoken words to written texts to holistic health—all shaping your understanding.
shambhu_gita::614.insight: Recognize that wisdom comes through diverse mediums, each offering a unique doorway to deeper understanding.

shambhu_gita::615.verse_sanskrit:
नूनं ज्ञानस्य निसत्वान्नित्याः शास्त्रसमुच्चयाः।
एते पञ्चविधेष्वेषु कापि तिष्ठन्ति पुस्तके ॥
shambhu_gita::615.verse_hindi: ज्ञान नित्य होने के कारण नित्य शास्त्र समूह इन पुस्तको में से किसी पुस्तक में अवश्य विद्यमान रहते हैं
shambhu_gita::615.english_translation: Because wisdom is eternal, the eternal collections of scriptures surely exist in some of these five types of books.
shambhu_gita::615.translation_literal: नूनं (indeed) ज्ञानस्य (of wisdom) निसत्वान्नित्याः (being eternal) शास्त्रसमुच्चयाः (collections of scriptures) एते (these) पञ्चविधेषु (in five types) एषु (in these) कापि (some) तिष्ठन्ति (exist) पुस्तके (in the books).
shambhu_gita::615.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::615.essence: Eternal wisdom is preserved within specific collections of scripture across time.
shambhu_gita::615.simple_meaning: Eternal wisdom is always present within some of these five types of scripture collections.
shambhu_gita::615.simple_insight: True wisdom is timeless and reliably found within established teachings.
shambhu_gita::615.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that because true wisdom never changes, it can always be found across certain classical collections of teachings, categorized into five types of scriptures.
shambhu_gita::615.insight: It helps you trust that deep, timeless wisdom is preserved and accessible through established sources.

shambhu_gita::616.verse_sanskrit:
पञ्चप्रकारकं सर्व पुस्तकं प्रलयक्षणे ।
वेदेषु प्रविलीयैव भजते मां न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::616.verse_hindi: और प्रलयावस्था में भी ये पुस्तकसमूह वेद में लय होकर मुझको प्राप्त होते है।
shambhu_gita::616.english_translation: Even in the state of dissolution, these collections of scriptures merge into the Vedas and reach me without doubt.
shambhu_gita::616.translation_literal: पञ्चप्रकारकं (five types) सर्व (all) पुस्तकं (the book) प्रलयक्षणे (at the time of dissolution) । वेदेषु (in the Vedas) प्रविलीयैव (dissolving/merging) भजते (are attained) मां (me) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
shambhu_gita::616.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::616.essence: Spiritual knowledge transcends cosmic dissolution, remaining eternally accessible.
shambhu_gita::616.simple_meaning: These five types of scriptures merge into the Vedas at dissolution and reach Shiva without doubt.
shambhu_gita::616.simple_insight: The divine wisdom endures beyond cosmic endings, never truly lost.
shambhu_gita::616.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even when the universe dissolves, the five types of sacred scriptures merge back into the Vedas, symbolizing the eternal presence and continuity of spiritual knowledge beyond cosmic cycles.
shambhu_gita::616.insight: It shows that true knowledge transcends endings and continues beyond apparent loss.

shambhu_gita::617.verse_sanskrit:
पञ्चभावप्रपन्नानां पुस्तकानां स्वधाभुजः ।
रक्षका ऋषयो नूनं विद्यन्ते च प्रकाशकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::617.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण! ऋषिगण ही इन पञ्चभावापन्न शास्त्रों के प्रकाशक और रक्षक हैं
shambhu_gita::617.english_translation: The sages are indeed the protectors and illuminators of the scriptures dedicated to the five elements.
shambhu_gita::617.translation_literal: पञ्चभावप्रपन्नानां (of those devoted to five elements) / पुस्तकानां (of the scriptures) / स्वधाभुजः (protectors) / रक्षका (guardians) / ऋषयो (the sages) / नूनं (indeed) / विद्यन्ते (exist) / च (and) / प्रकाशकाः (illuminators)
shambhu_gita::617.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::617.essence: Sages protect and illuminate teachings rooted in the five fundamental elements.
shambhu_gita::617.simple_meaning: Sages are the protectors and teachers of the scriptures focused on the five fundamental elements.
shambhu_gita::617.simple_insight: Respect grows knowing wise beings keep ancient teachings alive and clear.
shambhu_gita::617.detailed_meaning: In the assembly, Suta acknowledges that sages serve as guardians and illuminators of the scriptures that explain the five elements, highlighting their role in preserving essential knowledge.
shambhu_gita::617.insight: Recognize those who preserve and clarify deep knowledge as vital guides for understanding complex truths.

shambhu_gita::618.verse_sanskrit:
अध्यात्मज्ञानमास्ते हि विभक्तं सप्तभूमिषु ।
ऋषिशब्दे यतो ज्ञानभूमिज्ञानप्रकाशके ॥
shambhu_gita::618.verse_hindi: और अध्यात्मज्ञान सप्त भूमिक्षाओं में विभक्त होने के कारण उन ज्ञान भूमियों के ज्ञान के प्रकाशक ऋषियों के शब्दो में
shambhu_gita::618.english_translation: Spiritual knowledge is divided into seven levels, illuminated by the words of sages who reveal the knowledge of these planes.
shambhu_gita::618.translation_literal: अध्यात्मज्ञानमास्ते (spiritual knowledge exists) / हि (indeed) / विभक्तं (divided) / सप्तभूमिषु (in seven planes) / । / ऋषिशब्दे (in sages' words) / यतो (from which) / ज्ञानभूमिज्ञानप्रकाशके (knowledge-planes knowledge-illuminators) / ॥
shambhu_gita::618.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::618.essence: Spiritual knowledge unfolds across seven levels, each revealed by sage teachings.
shambhu_gita::618.simple_meaning: Spiritual knowledge is described as divided into seven distinct levels, each illuminated by the teachings of sages who reveal the understanding of these levels.
shambhu_gita::618.simple_insight: Understanding comes in stages, revealed by wise teachers guiding us through deeper layers.
shambhu_gita::618.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that spiritual knowledge is not one simple thing but divided into seven realms or levels. Each realm has sages whose teachings illuminate the knowledge contained there, highlighting the complexity and layered nature of spiritual wisdom.
shambhu_gita::618.insight: Recognize that spiritual understanding unfolds progressively, guided by trusted teachers revealing deeper layers.

shambhu_gita::619.verse_sanskrit:
भेदोऽवश्यं भवेदत्र संशयावसरः कुतः।
ऋषिप्रवर्तिते स्वच्छे निदिध्यासंवत्र्मनि ॥
shambhu_gita::619.verse_hindi: अवश्य भेद रहता है और ऋषियों के द्वारा प्रवर्ति निदिध्यासन-मार्ग के
shambhu_gita::619.english_translation: Difference is certainly present here; how can there be doubt when sages have established pure meditation on the true self?
shambhu_gita::619.translation_literal: भेदोऽवश्यं (difference certainly) भवेदत्र (exists here) संशयावसरः (doubt possibility) कुतः (from where) । ऋषिप्रवर्तिते (by sages established) स्वच्छे (pure) निदिध्यासंवत्र्मनि (in deep meditation on the self) ॥
shambhu_gita::619.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::619.essence: Apparent difference causes doubt, but deep meditation dispels that doubt.
shambhu_gita::619.simple_meaning: There is definitely difference, but when sages teach pure meditation on the true self, doubt about it disappears.
shambhu_gita::619.simple_insight: You feel your confusion about difference clear as deep meditation unfolds.
shambhu_gita::619.detailed_meaning: Shiva points out that while difference appears real, sages have shown through pure, deep meditation on the true self that doubt about difference can be resolved. This verse sets the stage for exploring unity beyond apparent distinctions.
shambhu_gita::619.modern_relevance: You struggle with conflicting opinions, but when you focus inward deeply, the confusion about opposites begins to clear.
shambhu_gita::619.insight: It shifts your view from clinging to surface differences to trusting deeper insight from sustained meditation.

shambhu_gita::620.verse_sanskrit:
अधिकारप्रभेदाश्च सम्भवेयुर्न संशयः ।
ऋषीणां किन्तु लक्ष्येषु भेदो नास्ति कदाचन ॥
shambhu_gita::620.verse_hindi: अधिकारों में भी अवश्य भेद रहता है, परन्तु ऋषियों के लक्ष्य कदापि भेद नहीं रहता है
shambhu_gita::620.english_translation: There is certainly a difference in roles, but the goals of the sages never differ.
shambhu_gita::620.translation_literal: अधिकारप्रभेदाश्च (difference in roles) / सम्भवेयुर्न (certainly exists) / संशयः (doubt) / ऋषीणां (of sages) / किन्तु (but) / लक्ष्येषु (in goals) / भेदो (difference) / नास्ति (is not) / कदाचन (ever).
shambhu_gita::620.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::620.essence: Different roles do not change the single, shared goal of those seeking truth.
shambhu_gita::620.simple_meaning: People can have different duties, but their ultimate aims can be the same without conflict.
shambhu_gita::620.simple_insight: It feels reassuring that despite varied tasks, we share common higher purposes.
shambhu_gita::620.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that while individuals may act in different roles or responsibilities, the sages—those who seek truth—always share a unified, unwavering goal. This verse highlights harmony despite diversity in action.
shambhu_gita::620.modern_relevance: At work or home, you juggle many roles, yet your core values and hopes remain constant beneath it all.
shambhu_gita::620.insight: It shifts how you see changing duties—not as distractions but as varied expressions of a stable purpose.

shambhu_gita::621.verse_sanskrit: सिद्धान्तेषु स्वकीयेषु विनाऽभ्रान्ति स्वधाभुजः ।            स्वस्वपदर्शितज्ञानमार्गे वा केऽपि नेशते ॥
shambhu_gita::621.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! अपने अपने सिद्धान्त मे और अपने अपने प्रदर्शित ज्ञानपथ मे अभ्रान्त हुए बिना कोई भी
shambhu_gita::621.english_translation: O ancestors! Without becoming confused in your own principles and the paths of knowledge you have shown, no one gets lost.
shambhu_gita::621.translation_literal: सिद्धान्तेषु (in principles) स्वकीयेषु (own) विनाऽभ्रान्ति (without confusion) स्वधाभुजः (one who holds one's own) स्वस्वपदर्शितज्ञानमार्गे (in one's own shown path of knowledge) वा (or) केऽपि (anyone) नेशते (gets lost)
shambhu_gita::621.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::621.essence: Staying true to your clear knowledge prevents you from becoming lost or confused.
shambhu_gita::621.simple_meaning: If you stay committed to your own clear principles and knowledge path, you will not become confused or lost.
shambhu_gita::621.simple_insight: There is safety and confidence in trusting your own clear understanding.
shambhu_gita::621.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, assuring them that as long as they remain anchored in their own established principles and paths of knowledge without confusion, they will not lose their way. This emphasizes the importance of clarity and trust in one's own understanding amid many teachings.
shambhu_gita::621.modern_relevance: When faced with conflicting advice or information, holding on to your clear values and understanding prevents overwhelm and confusion.
shambhu_gita::621.insight: It teaches you to trust your own discernment and not be swayed into confusion by others' opinions.

shambhu_gita::622.verse_sanskrit:
ऋषीणां पदवीं पुण्यां परिलधुं कदाचन।
निश्चितं वित्त पितरो नात्र कश्चन संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::622.verse_hindi: ऋषि पदवी को नहीं प्राप्त कर सकता। हे पितृगण ! इसको निश्चित जानो, इसमें संदेह नहीं है
shambhu_gita::622.english_translation: The exalted position of the sages cannot be attained by anyone; O ancestors, be certain of this without doubt.
shambhu_gita::622.translation_literal: ऋषीणां (of sages) / पदवीं (position) / पुण्यां (exalted) / परिलधुं (to attain) / कदाचन (ever). / निश्चितं (certainly) / वित्त (know) / पितरो (ancestors) / नात्र (here not) / कश्चन (anyone) / संशयः (doubt).
shambhu_gita::622.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::622.essence: The honored rank of sages is unreachable by anyone else, no doubt.
shambhu_gita::622.simple_meaning: The honored status of sages is something no one can achieve; ancestors, be sure of this truth.
shambhu_gita::622.simple_insight: Some heights of virtue are beyond ordinary reach, inviting respect and awe.
shambhu_gita::622.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta addresses the ancestors, emphasizing that the revered status of sages is unreachable for ordinary beings, setting a tone of respect for the spiritual excellence of sages.
shambhu_gita::622.insight: Recognize and honor the exceptional spiritual attainments beyond common experience without trying to possess them.

shambhu_gita::623.verse_sanskrit:
ऋषयो मन्त्रद्रष्टारः कथ्यन्ते नात्र संशयः ।
शब्दास्त एव मन्त्राः स्युर्ये मद्रूपप्रकाशकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::623.verse_hindi: मंत्र के द्रष्टा ऋषि कहते हैं। मेरे रूप का बतानेवाला जो शब्द है उसी को मन्त्र कहते हैं।
shambhu_gita::623.english_translation: The sages who perceive mantras say without doubt that the words revealing my form are the mantras.
shambhu_gita::623.translation_literal: ऋषयो (sages) मन्त्रद्रष्टारः (mantra-seers) कथ्यन्ते (are said) नात्र (there is no) संशयः (doubt) । शब्दास्त (words) एव (indeed) मन्त्राः (mantras) स्युः (are) ये (which) मद्रूप (my form) प्रकाशकाः (revealing) ॥
shambhu_gita::623.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::623.essence: Mantras are words that reveal the form of the divine without doubt.
shambhu_gita::623.simple_meaning: Sages who see mantras say the words that reveal the divine form are called mantras.
shambhu_gita::623.simple_insight: Words can carry the power to reveal deeper truths beyond their surface meaning.
shambhu_gita::623.detailed_meaning: The narrator explains that sages who perceive the essence behind mantras agree that the words which reveal Shiva's form are what define mantras, affirming the power of sacred sound to disclose divine reality.
shambhu_gita::623.insight: It teaches that language can act as a bridge revealing profound inner realities when deeply understood.

shambhu_gita::624.verse_sanskrit:
अतो ये शक्नुवन्तीह मन्त्रान् द्रष्टुं स्वधाभुजः!।
अहो मामपि ते द्रष्टुं क्षमन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::624.verse_hindi: इस कारण जो मन्त्र को देख सकते हैं वह मुझे भी देख सकते हैं
shambhu_gita::624.english_translation: Therefore, those who can perceive the mantra can also perceive me without doubt.
shambhu_gita::624.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) / ये (those who) / शक्नुवन्तीह (can here) / मन्त्रान् (mantras) / द्रष्टुं (to see) / स्वधाभुजः (the self-possessor) / अहो (ah!) / मामपि (me also) / ते (they) / द्रष्टुं (to see) / क्षमन्ते (are able) / नात्र (here not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::624.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::624.essence: Grasping the inner meaning of the mantra reveals the divine without doubt.
shambhu_gita::624.simple_meaning: If you can understand the sacred mantra, you can also understand me without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::624.simple_insight: Understanding the mantra opens the way to perceiving the divine directly.
shambhu_gita::624.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses those who can perceive the mantra's truth, saying that such perception naturally leads to seeing Shiva himself, removing any doubt about his presence.
shambhu_gita::624.modern_relevance: When you grasp the deeper meaning behind a symbol or teaching, you often connect directly to the source it points to.
shambhu_gita::624.insight: It shifts your focus from external forms (mantra) to the essence they reveal (the divine).

shambhu_gita::625.verse_sanskrit:
दुर्दमाया हि मांयायाः प्रभावांत्पितरो ध्रुवम् ।
यद्यपि स्वस्वरूपं मे वाङ्मनोबुद्धयगोचरम् ॥
shambhu_gita::625.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! यद्यपि मेरी दुर्दमनीय माया के प्रभाव से मेरे वाक् मन और बुद्धि से अगोचर स्वस्वरूप
shambhu_gita::625.english_translation: O ancestors! Although my true nature is beyond the reach of speech, mind, and intellect due to the overwhelming power of my difficult-to-conquer illusion.
shambhu_gita::625.translation_literal: दुर्दमाया (difficult to conquer illusion) / हि (indeed) / मांयायाः (of illusion) / प्रभावांत् (power/effect) / पितरो (ancestors) / ध्रुवम् (certainly) / यद्यपि (although) / स्वस्वरूपं (own true form) / मे (my) / वाङ्मनः (speech and mind) / बुद्धयः (intellect) / अगोचरम् (beyond perception)
shambhu_gita::625.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::625.essence: The true self can be hidden beyond mind and speech by a powerful illusion.
shambhu_gita::625.simple_meaning: My true nature is hidden from speech, mind, and intellect because of the strong power of my difficult illusion.
shambhu_gita::625.simple_insight: Some truths are too vast for ordinary thought to grasp or express.
shambhu_gita::625.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that despite their questioning, his real self remains beyond ordinary mental faculties due to a powerful illusion veiling it.
shambhu_gita::625.insight: Recognize that some aspects of your true self are beyond normal thinking or speaking.

shambhu_gita::626.verse_sanskrit:
अथवा चिद्विलासस्य तस्य ज्ञानं यथार्थतः।
नानुभूतं भवेन्नूनं निखिलर्षयन्तरात्मनि ॥
shambhu_gita::626.verse_hindi: अथवा उसके चिद्विलास का ज्ञान सब ऋषियों को सम्यक् प्रकार से अनुभूत न होता हो
shambhu_gita::626.english_translation: Or the true understanding of his divine play is not fully experienced by all sages within their inner selves.
shambhu_gita::626.translation_literal: अथवा (or) चिद्विलासस्य (of divine play) तस्य (its) ज्ञानं (knowledge) यथार्थतः (truly) नानुभूतं (not experienced) भवेन्नूनं (indeed) निखिलर्षयन्तरात्मनि (by all sages within the inner self)
shambhu_gita::626.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::626.essence: The true depth of divine play escapes full experience even by all sages.
shambhu_gita::626.simple_meaning: Not all sages fully experience or understand the true nature of Shiva’s divine play within themselves.
shambhu_gita::626.simple_insight: Sometimes even wise people miss the full truth of the divine’s deeper play.
shambhu_gita::626.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that the profound truth of Shiva's divine play (chidvilasa) is so subtle that even the great sages do not fully grasp or experience it within their inner selves.
shambhu_gita::626.insight: It opens the mind to accept that some truths are beyond even advanced understanding or direct experience.

shambhu_gita::627.verse_sanskrit:
तथापि मन्त्रद्रष्टृत्वात्ते मजूज्ञानावबोधिनः।
भवेयुर्नात्र सन्देहः सत्यमेतब्रवीमि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::627.verse_hindi: परंन्तु वे मंत्रद्रष्टा होने से मेरे ज्ञान के ज्ञाता है, इसमें संदेह नहीं। यह मैं सत्य कहता हूँ।
shambhu_gita::627.english_translation: Yet, because he is the seer of the mantra, he is the knower of my knowledge, there is no doubt in this; I speak the truth to you.
shambhu_gita::627.translation_literal: तथापि (yet) मन्त्रद्रष्टृत्वात् (because of being seer of mantra) ते (he) मजूज्ञानावबोधिनः (of my knowledge-knower) भवेत् (is) नात्र (here not) सन्देहः (doubt) सत्यम् (truth) एत (this) ब्रवीमि (I speak) वः (to you)
shambhu_gita::627.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::627.essence: Direct perception of the mantra reveals complete knowledge without doubt.
shambhu_gita::627.simple_meaning: Because he has the power to see the mantra, he truly understands my knowledge without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::627.simple_insight: Certain insight comes from direct experience, removing any doubt.
shambhu_gita::627.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the one who truly perceives the sacred mantra also directly knows Shiva's knowledge. This clarity leaves no room for doubt, affirming the certainty of this insight.
shambhu_gita::627.insight: Knowing deeply from direct perception removes uncertainty and brings clear understanding.

shambhu_gita::628.verse_sanskrit:
अतः परस्परं तेषां मतं नूनं स्वधाभुजः ।
मयथार्थस्वरूपस्य ज्ञाने नैव विभिद्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::628.verse_hindi: अतः मेरे यथार्थ स्वरूप के ज्ञान में उनके परस्पर यथार्थ रूप से मतभेद हो नहीं सकता है
shambhu_gita::628.english_translation: Therefore, in the true knowledge of my real nature, there can be no genuine disagreement among them.
shambhu_gita::628.translation_literal: अतः (therefore) / परस्परं (mutually) / तेषां (among them) / मतं (opinion) / नूनं (certainly) / स्वधाभुजः (true nature of myself) / मयथार्थस्वरूपस्य (of my true real form) / ज्ञाने (in knowledge) / नैव (not at all) / विभिद्यते (is divided or separated)
shambhu_gita::628.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::628.essence: True knowledge of your real nature leaves no room for genuine disagreement.
shambhu_gita::628.simple_meaning: When you truly understand your real nature, there is no real conflict or disagreement in that knowledge.
shambhu_gita::628.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your deepest truth is beyond dispute.
shambhu_gita::628.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when one attains true knowledge of their real nature, any apparent disagreements among views disappear because the understanding is unified and complete.
shambhu_gita::628.modern_relevance: In moments of inner clarity, you see beyond conflicting opinions and feel a deep sense of unity within yourself.
shambhu_gita::628.insight: It teaches you to recognize that true understanding dissolves apparent contradictions and unites perspectives.

shambhu_gita::629.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुषार्थाधिकाराणां भैदैहि ज्ञानभूमिषु ।
विरोध इव भासेत भूमिभेदैश्च केवलम् ॥
shambhu_gita::629.verse_hindi: केवल भूमिभेद, अधिकारभेद और पुरुषार्थभेद होने के कारण इन ज्ञान भूमियों में विरोधाभास प्रतीत होता है
shambhu_gita::629.english_translation: In fields of knowledge, conflicts appear only due to differences in perspectives, rights, and purposes.
shambhu_gita::629.translation_literal: पुरुषार्थाधिकाराणां (of purposes and rights) / भैदैहि (because of differences) / ज्ञानभूमिषु (in knowledge fields) / विरोध (conflict) / इव (like) / भासेत (appears) / भूमिभेदैश्च (also by differences of fields) / केवलम् (only)
shambhu_gita::629.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::629.essence: Conflicts in knowledge arise only from differing roles, aims, or viewpoints.
shambhu_gita::629.simple_meaning: Conflicts in knowledge arise only when different viewpoints, roles, or goals are mixed and misunderstood.
shambhu_gita::629.simple_insight: Understanding comes when you see conflicts as differences in perspective, not absolute contradictions.
shambhu_gita::629.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that apparent contradictions in knowledge are not true opposites but arise from different goals, rights, or fields, showing that truth varies with context.
shambhu_gita::629.modern_relevance: When people argue at work or online, often it's because they focus on different goals or roles, not because one side is entirely wrong.
shambhu_gita::629.insight: It teaches you to recognize that disagreements often stem from differing contexts or aims, not from fundamental truth clashes.

shambhu_gita::630.verse_sanskrit:
मत्तः पराङ्मुखा एव तत्त्वज्ञानावकण्टके।
पतन्यैवविध गर्ने विरोधभ्रमपङ्किले ॥
shambhu_gita::630.verse_hindi: मुझसे विमुख लोग ही तत्त्वज्ञान के पथ के कण्टक रूपी ऐसे विरोध और भ्रम से भरे हुए गड्ढे में पतित हुआ करते हैं
shambhu_gita::630.english_translation: Only those who turn away from me fall into obstacles and pits full of opposition and confusion on the path of true knowledge.
shambhu_gita::630.translation_literal: मत्तः (from me) / पराङ्मुखा (turned away) / एव (only) / तत्त्वज्ञानावकण्टके (path of true knowledge's thorns) / पतन्यैवविध (fall indeed) / गर्ने (do) / विरोधभ्रमपङ्किले (obstacles filled with opposition and confusion pits)
shambhu_gita::630.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::630.essence: Turning away from the divine leads to confusion and obstacles on the path to true knowledge.
shambhu_gita::630.simple_meaning: Only those who turn away from the divine fall into confusion and obstacles on the path of true knowledge.
shambhu_gita::630.simple_insight: Trusting the divine protects you from confusion and harmful distractions.
shambhu_gita::630.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that turning away from him, the source of true knowledge, leads people into confusion and obstacles that block their spiritual progress.
shambhu_gita::630.modern_relevance: When you ignore your inner guidance, you get caught in doubts and distractions that stall your growth.
shambhu_gita::630.insight: It teaches you to stay open and trusting toward the divine presence to avoid mental and spiritual pitfalls.

shambhu_gita::631.verse_sanskrit:
यथा पर्वतवास्तव्या मानवाः शिक्षयन्त्यहो।
स्वानुरूपां गति विज्ञाः ! समभूमिनिवासिनः ॥
shambhu_gita::631.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञो ! पर्वतवासी मनुष्य जिस प्रकार समतलवासी मनुष्यों के
shambhu_gita::631.english_translation: Just as mountain-dwellers teach those living on flat lands according to their ways, wise people understand the path suited to each.
shambhu_gita::631.translation_literal: यथा (just as) पर्वतवास्तव्या (mountain-dwelling) मानवाः (people) शिक्षयन्ति (teach) अहो (indeed) स्वानुरूपां (their own-suited) गति (path) विज्ञाः (wise) समभूमिनिवासिनः (flat-land dwellers)
shambhu_gita::631.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::631.essence: True wisdom adapts to each person's unique path and needs.
shambhu_gita::631.simple_meaning: Wisdom is about recognizing that different people need guidance suited to their unique situations.
shambhu_gita::631.simple_insight: You feel acceptance knowing that your way is valid and understood by wise ones.
shambhu_gita::631.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that just as mountain people teach flat-land people in ways they can grasp, true wisdom adapts to each individual's nature and circumstances.
shambhu_gita::631.modern_relevance: You notice how advice from someone who truly understands your situation feels more helpful than generic suggestions.
shambhu_gita::631.insight: It teaches you to adapt your understanding and guidance to fit each person's unique context.

shambhu_gita::632.verse_sanskrit:
एकस्या ज्ञानभूमेश्च तथा दर्शनशासनम् ।
स्त्रीयां गति प्रशंसन्तो दूषयन्तश्च तद्गतिम् ॥
shambhu_gita::632.verse_hindi: चलने की शैली का दोष दर्शन करके अपनी गति की प्रशंसा करते हुए
shambhu_gita::632.english_translation: Some, seeing the path of knowledge and vision, praise their own way while criticizing that path.
shambhu_gita::632.translation_literal: एकस्या (of one) ज्ञानभूमेश्च (knowledge ground) तथा (and) दर्शनशासनम् (vision teaching) स्त्रीयां (woman's) गति (movement/path) प्रशंसन्तो (praising) दूषयन्तश्च (criticizing) तद्गतिम् (that path)
shambhu_gita::632.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::632.essence: People often praise their own way while unfairly criticizing true wisdom paths.
shambhu_gita::632.simple_meaning: Some people look at the path of knowledge and insight but praise their own way while criticizing that path.
shambhu_gita::632.simple_insight: We often feel sure about our own path and judge others' ways without full understanding.
shambhu_gita::632.detailed_meaning: This verse points out how some individuals, after encountering teachings on knowledge and insight, still favor their own approach and disparage the alternative path. It reflects human tendency to cling to familiar views while doubting others.
shambhu_gita::632.modern_relevance: You might notice someone dismissing expert advice while praising their own method, even if it’s less effective.
shambhu_gita::632.insight: It teaches you to recognize this bias and remain open to wisdom beyond your current approach.

shambhu_gita::633.verse_sanskrit:
विज्ञानरीतिमन्यस्याः कचिद्विप्रतिपादयेत्।
नास्ति तत्खण्डनं कल्याः ! मतस्यान्यस्य निश्चितम् ॥
shambhu_gita::633.verse_hindi: पर्वत-आरोहण प्रणाली सिखाया करते हैं, ठीक उसी प्रकार एक ज्ञान भूमिका दर्शन दूसरी ज्ञानभूमि के दर्शन शास्त्रो की विज्ञान शैली का कदाचित् खण्डन करता है
shambhu_gita::633.english_translation: Just as a mountain climbing method is taught, similarly one knowledge foundation's view may refute another's scientific style, but no refutation exists for the supreme view.
shambhu_gita::633.translation_literal: विज्ञानरीतिमन्यस्याः (scientific method of another) कचिद् (sometimes) विप्रतिपादयेत् (may refute) । नास्ति (there is not) तत्-खण्डनं (that refutation) कल्याः (of the supreme) ! मतस्य (view) अन्यस्य (of another) निश्चितम् (certain).
shambhu_gita::633.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::633.essence: Some views may challenge others, but the supreme truth cannot be contradicted.
shambhu_gita::633.simple_meaning: Different ways of understanding may challenge each other, but the ultimate truth remains beyond all doubt or refutation.
shambhu_gita::633.simple_insight: There's comfort knowing some truths are steady despite conflicting opinions.
shambhu_gita::633.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that different knowledge systems or methods can challenge one another like different paths up a mountain, but the highest or supreme understanding cannot be disproved or contradicted.
shambhu_gita::633.modern_relevance: You might hear conflicting expert opinions or methods, but some core truths stay steady beneath the noise.
shambhu_gita::633.insight: It shifts your mind to seek the ultimate, unshakable truth beyond temporary disagreements.

shambhu_gita::634.verse_sanskrit:
अपि तु स्वमतस्यास्ति पोषकं सर्वथा यतः।
तत्खण्डनमतो भक्ता ज्ञानिनो मण्डनं विदुः ॥
shambhu_gita::634.verse_hindi: उसको मेरे ज्ञानो भक्त परमत का खण्डन नहीं समझते बल्कि स्वमत को पुष्टि समझते हैं
shambhu_gita::634.english_translation: Even the wise do not see my knowledge as a denial of supreme devotion, but as a confirmation of their own views.
shambhu_gita::634.translation_literal: अपि (even) तु (then) स्वमतस्यास्ति (of one's own view there is) पोषकं (support) सर्वथा (completely) यतः (because) तत्खण्डनम (that denial) अतः (therefore) भक्ता (devotees) ज्ञानिनो (the wise) मण्डनं (condemnation) विदुः (know).
shambhu_gita::634.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::634.essence: True wisdom confirms, never denies, sincere devotion and personal inner truth.
shambhu_gita::634.simple_meaning: True wisdom does not reject devotion as wrong; instead, it supports and confirms each person’s sincere inner faith.
shambhu_gita::634.simple_insight: You can trust that your heartfelt devotion and your wise understanding are not in conflict.
shambhu_gita::634.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that followers who are devoted and those who are wise do not see his teaching as opposing each other. Instead, even the wisest recognize that devotion confirms their own understanding rather than contradicting it.
shambhu_gita::634.modern_relevance: When you deeply believe in something and also seek clear understanding, you realize both can coexist and strengthen each other, not clash.
shambhu_gita::634.insight: It teaches you to see your devotion and your wisdom as complementary, not contradictory parts of your inner journey.

shambhu_gita::635.verse_sanskrit:
यदा सुकवयो नैशमाकाशं वर्णयन्त्यहो ।
दिवाकाशस्तदा नूनं स्वत एवावधीर्य्य्ते ॥
shambhu_gita::635.verse_hindi: कवि जब रात्रि के आकाश का वर्णन करता है तो स्वतः ही दिन के आकाश की निन्दा हो जाती है
shambhu_gita::635.english_translation: When poets describe the night sky, the day sky is naturally criticized without effort.
shambhu_gita::635.translation_literal: यदा (when) सुकवयो (poets) नैशमाकाशं (night sky) वर्णयन्ति (describe) अहो (oh) । दिवाकाशः (day sky) तदा (then) नूनं (indeed) स्वतः (naturally) एव (only) अवधीर्यते (becomes criticized) ॥
shambhu_gita::635.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::635.essence: Praising one thing naturally casts its opposite in a lesser light.
shambhu_gita::635.simple_meaning: When poets praise the night sky, the day sky automatically seems lesser without anyone trying.
shambhu_gita::635.simple_insight: Sometimes praise for one thing feels like a silent criticism of another.
shambhu_gita::635.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Suta uses the example of poets praising the night sky, which naturally causes the day sky to appear flawed by comparison. It shows how focusing on one side can unintentionally bring down its opposite.
shambhu_gita::635.modern_relevance: You notice how complimenting a friend unintentionally makes someone else feel overlooked or less appreciated.
shambhu_gita::635.insight: It reveals how comparisons create unspoken judgments, even when praise is sincere.

shambhu_gita::636.verse_sanskrit:
दिवाकाशप्रशंसायां कृतायां कविभिः खलु ।
व्योम्नो नैशंस्य जायेत स्वत एव पराभवः ॥
shambhu_gita::636.verse_hindi: और जब वह दिन के आकाश का वर्णन करता है तो रात्रि के आकाश की निन्दा स्वतः ही हो जाती है,
shambhu_gita::636.english_translation: When poets praise the sky of day, criticism of the night sky naturally arises.
shambhu_gita::636.translation_literal: दिवाकाशप्रशंसायां (in praise of the day sky) / कृतायां (when done) / कविभिः (by poets) / खलु (indeed) / व्योम्नो (of the sky) / नैशंस्य (of the night sky) / जायेत (arises) / स्वत (naturally) / एव (indeed) / पराभवः (criticism or downfall)
shambhu_gita::636.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::636.essence: Praising one aspect naturally invites criticism of its opposite.
shambhu_gita::636.simple_meaning: Praising the sky during the day naturally leads to criticizing the night sky.
shambhu_gita::636.simple_insight: Highlighting one thing often invites criticism of its opposite.
shambhu_gita::636.detailed_meaning: In describing the beauty of the day sky, poets inadvertently cause the night sky to be seen as lesser. This reflects the natural tendency to compare and contrast, setting up opposites.
shambhu_gita::636.modern_relevance: You post a glowing review of a colleague, and others start pointing out their flaws without you saying a word.
shambhu_gita::636.insight: It shifts awareness to how praise can unintentionally create judgment of the opposite.

shambhu_gita::637.verse_sanskrit:
सप्तानां ज्ञानभूमीनां तथा दर्शनसप्तके।
निन्दकानि चं वाक्यानि स्तवकानि कचित् कचिद् ॥
shambhu_gita::637.verse_hindi: इसी प्रकार निन्दा स्तुति का सम्बन्ध इन सातो ज्ञानभूमियों के दर्शनशास्त्रोम कहीं कहीं
shambhu_gita::637.english_translation: Similarly, among the seven fields of knowledge and the seven systems of philosophy, there are also some statements of criticism and some of praise.
shambhu_gita::637.translation_literal: सप्तानां (of seven) ज्ञानभूमीनां (knowledge fields) तथा (and) दर्शनसप्तके (seven philosophies) निन्दकानि (criticisms) चं (also) वाक्यानि (statements) स्तवकानि (praises) कचित् (some) कचिद् (some)
shambhu_gita::637.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::637.essence: All knowledge systems include both criticism and praise within their teachings.
shambhu_gita::637.simple_meaning: Among the seven knowledge fields and philosophical systems, there are some statements that criticize and some that praise.
shambhu_gita::637.simple_insight: Even deep knowledge areas have both critics and supporters.
shambhu_gita::637.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that within the broad spectrum of seven knowledge fields and seven philosophical traditions, one finds both criticism and praise expressed, showing the diversity of views in philosophy.
shambhu_gita::637.insight: Recognize that every perspective includes both critique and appreciation, enriching understanding.

shambhu_gita::638.verse_sanskrit:
लभ्यन्ते यैर्विमुह्यन्ति मानसान्यल्पमेधसाम् ।
नैवात्र विस्मयः कार्यों भवद्भिः पितृपुङ्गवाः ॥
shambhu_gita::638.verse_hindi: पाया जाता है, जिससे अल्पबुद्धियों का मन घबरा जाता है। हे पितृगण ! इसमें आपलोग विस्मय न करें
shambhu_gita::638.english_translation: That which confuses weak minds is not a cause for wonder for you, O noble ancestors.
shambhu_gita::638.translation_literal: लभ्यन्ते (are attained) / यैः (by those who) / विमुह्यन्ति (are confused) / मानसाः (minds) / अल्पमेधसाम् (of the small-intellect) / नैवात्र (not here) / विस्मयः (wonder) / कार्यः (is to be done) / भवद्भिः (by you) / पितृपुङ्गवाः (noble ancestors)
shambhu_gita::638.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::638.essence: Not all confusion deserves your surprise—steady minds remain unaffected.
shambhu_gita::638.simple_meaning: You should not be surprised or disturbed by things that confuse those with limited understanding.
shambhu_gita::638.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing that confusion is natural for some minds, not for you.
shambhu_gita::638.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses noble ancestors, telling them not to be shocked by things that confuse less discerning minds. This reassures them to remain steady amid bewildering phenomena that unsettle others.
shambhu_gita::638.modern_relevance: When others around you panic or get confused by complex situations, you can stay calm and not be shaken.
shambhu_gita::638.insight: It teaches you to recognize your steadiness when others are unsettled by confusion.

shambhu_gita::639.verse_sanskrit:
केवलं पितरो ज्ञानभूमिपार्थक्यतो ध्रुवम् ।
स्वरूपे चिन्मये तैर्न निरीक्ष्येऽहं पृथक् पृथक् ॥
shambhu_gita::639.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! केवल ज्ञानभूमियों की पृथक्ता से ही मैं चिन्मय स्वरूप में उनको पृथक् पृथक् दिखाई पड़ता हूँ
shambhu_gita::639.english_translation: O forefathers! I appear separate to them only because of their limited knowledge; in reality, I am pure consciousness itself.
shambhu_gita::639.translation_literal: केवलं (only) पितरो (forefathers) ज्ञानभूमिपार्थक्यतो (due to difference in knowledge grounds) ध्रुवम् (certainly) । स्वरूपे (in form) चिन्मये (pure consciousness) तैर्न (by them) निरीक्ष्येऽहं (I am seen) पृथक् (separately) पृथक् (separately) ॥
shambhu_gita::639.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::639.essence: Apparent separation arises only from limited knowledge; the true self is pure consciousness.
shambhu_gita::639.simple_meaning: You appear separate from pure consciousness only because your knowledge is limited. In truth, everything is of the same conscious nature.
shambhu_gita::639.simple_insight: There is relief in realizing separation is just limited seeing, not the true state.
shambhu_gita::639.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the forefathers, explaining that their perception of him as separate arises from their limited understanding. In essence, his true form is pure consciousness, indivisible and unified, beyond apparent distinctions.
shambhu_gita::639.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated or different from others, it’s often your limited perspective, not the true nature of connection.
shambhu_gita::639.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing division to recognizing underlying unity beyond appearances.

shambhu_gita::640.verse_sanskrit:
पार्थक्याज्ञानभूमीनां तत्पार्थक्यं न तत्त्वतः।
यथा सोपानतो मर्त्य एकस्मादपरं क्रमांद ॥
shambhu_gita::640.verse_hindi: वह पृथक्ता ज्ञान भूमि के कारण है, तत्त्वतःनहीं है। जिस प्रकार मनुष्य एक सोपान के बाद दूसरा सोपान आरोहण करता हुआ
shambhu_gita::640.english_translation: Separation is due to ignorance of distinctions, not true reality; like climbing one step after another.
shambhu_gita::640.translation_literal: पार्थक्याज्ञानभूमीनां (of those founded on ignorance of separation) तत्पार्थक्यं (that separation) न (not) तत्त्वतः (in essence). यथा (just as) सोपानतो (from step to step) मर्त्य (a mortal) एकस्मात् (from one) अपरं (another) क्रमांद् (in order).
shambhu_gita::640.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::640.essence: Separation arises from ignorance, not from the true nature of reality.
shambhu_gita::640.simple_meaning: Separation exists only because of ignorance; in truth, everything is connected like steps in a ladder.
shambhu_gita::640.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing separation is just confusion, not the real nature of things.
shambhu_gita::640.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that what appears as separation or difference arises from ignorance. Like climbing steps one after another, distinctions are sequential but not ultimately real.
shambhu_gita::640.modern_relevance: When you feel divided from others or yourself, remember this feeling is like stepping—it arises from confusion, not from who you truly are.
shambhu_gita::640.insight: It shifts your view from seeing separation as real to seeing it as a temporary, layered experience.

shambhu_gita::641.verse_sanskrit:
प्रासादस्य समारोहन पृष्ठमारोहति ध्रुवम् ।
शास्त्रासक्तास्तथा भक्ता लभन्ते सन्निधि मम ॥
shambhu_gita::641.verse_hindi: अन्त में छत पर चढ़ ही जाता है, उसी प्रकार शास्त्रनिरत मेरे भक्त मुझ तक पहुंच ही जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::641.english_translation: Just as one finally climbs to the roof, so too my devotees absorbed in scripture reach my presence surely.
shambhu_gita::641.translation_literal: प्रासादस्य (of the palace) समारोहन (climbing up) पृष्ठमारोहति (ascends to the roof) ध्रुवम् (surely) । शास्त्रासक्तास्तथा (scripture-absorbed thus) भक्ता (devotees) लभन्ते (obtain) सन्निधि (presence) मम (my) ॥
shambhu_gita::641.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::641.essence: Steady devotion and study naturally lead to reaching the divine presence.
shambhu_gita::641.simple_meaning: Those who are devoted and focused on sacred teachings eventually reach the divine presence like climbing to a rooftop.
shambhu_gita::641.simple_insight: There is assurance in steady devotion and study—they naturally bring you closer to what you seek.
shambhu_gita::641.detailed_meaning: Shiva compares the journey of his devotees to climbing a building's roof. Just as climbing is inevitable with steady effort, so is reaching Shiva’s presence for those devoted to scripture and him.
shambhu_gita::641.modern_relevance: You keep returning to your studies or spiritual reading, even when it feels slow. Over time, this steady focus brings you deeper connection.
shambhu_gita::641.insight: It teaches you to trust that persistent devotion and learning naturally bring you closer to the divine presence.

shambhu_gita::642.verse_sanskrit:
शास्त्रान्तरमतानाञ्च भेदोऽप्येवं विबुध्यताम् ।
क्रियतां नात्र सन्देहो विस्मयो न विधीयताम् ॥
shambhu_gita::642.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! शास्त्रान्तरो का मतभेद भी ऐसा ही जानिये, इसमें सन्देह या विस्मय न करिये
shambhu_gita::642.english_translation: O ancestors, understand that differences in other scriptures are similar; do not doubt or be amazed by them.
shambhu_gita::642.translation_literal: हे (O) / पितृगण (ancestors) / शास्त्रान्तरो (of other scriptures) / का (of) / मतभेद (difference) / भी (also) / ऐसा (such) / ही (only) / जानिये (know) / इसमें (in this) / सन्देह (doubt) / या (or) / विस्मय (amazement) / न (not) / करिये (do)
shambhu_gita::642.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::642.essence: Differences in scriptures should not cause doubt or astonishment.
shambhu_gita::642.simple_meaning: Differences in other scriptures are similar; do not be confused or surprised by them.
shambhu_gita::642.simple_insight: It's okay not to fully understand every scripture; confusion is natural but shouldn't stop your trust.
shambhu_gita::642.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the assembled sages, advising them that differences in teachings across scriptures are natural and should not cause doubt or surprise, preparing them to hear Shiva's unified teaching.
shambhu_gita::642.modern_relevance: When you encounter conflicting advice online or in books, remember such differences are normal and don't need to shake your trust in your path.
shambhu_gita::642.insight: It teaches you to accept variation in teachings without losing confidence or becoming unsettled.

shambhu_gita::643.verse_hindi: मेरे अध्यात्मभाव से पूर्ण शास्त्र समूह ऋतम्भरा से उत्पन्न होने के कारण और अधिकारि भेद के लक्ष्य से
shambhu_gita::643.english_translation: The entire collection of scriptures, filled with spiritual meanings, arises from the truth and the aim of distinguishing the qualified.
shambhu_gita::643.translation_literal: भावैराध्यात्मिकै: (filled with spiritual feelings) पूर्णः (complete) शास्त्रपुञ्जो (collection of scriptures) यतः (because) अजनि (arose) । ऋतम्भराख्यबुद्धेश्च (from the truth-called intellect) अधिकारिभेदलक्ष्यतः (due to the aim of differentiating qualified) ॥
shambhu_gita::643.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::643.essence: Scriptures emerge from spiritual truth to clarify different qualifications.
shambhu_gita::643.simple_meaning: The scriptures come from spiritual understanding and the purpose of clarifying who is qualified.
shambhu_gita::643.simple_insight: Scriptures are not random but arise from deep truth and clear aims.
shambhu_gita::643.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that the scriptures are a complete collection filled with spiritual meaning, arising from the eternal truth and intended to clarify different qualifications or levels among practitioners.
shambhu_gita::643.insight: Recognize that spiritual teachings arise from clear intentions and truths, not arbitrary ideas.

shambhu_gita::644.verse_sanskrit:
अतो यथार्थतो नास्ति गिधोऽमुष्य विरोधिता।
मत्याऽप्यनादिकां ब्रह्माश्रयीभूताश्च भूतिदाः! ॥
shambhu_gita::644.verse_hindi: कहे जाने के कारण इनका परस्पर यथार्थ विरोध नहीं है। वेदान्त शास्त्र ने माया को ब्रह्म की आश्रयभूता
shambhu_gita::644.english_translation: Therefore, truly, there is no real contradiction between them. Even illusion, which is dependent on the supreme reality, grants existence.
shambhu_gita::644.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) यथार्थतो (truly) नास्ति (is not) गिधः (contradiction) अमुष्य (between these) विरोधिता (opposed). मत्याऽपि (even illusion) अनादिकां (beginningless) ब्रह्माश्रयीभूताः (dependent on Brahman) च (and) भूतिदाः (givers of existence)!
shambhu_gita::644.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::644.essence: Apparent contradictions vanish when you see that all depends on the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::644.simple_meaning: Apparent conflicts or contradictions between truths do not really exist because everything, including illusion, depends on the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::644.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing contradictions dissolve when seen from the highest truth.
shambhu_gita::644.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that although things may seem opposed, at the deepest level there is no true contradiction. Even illusion (maya) depends on the supreme reality (Brahman) and gives rise to existence, showing unity beneath diversity.
shambhu_gita::644.modern_relevance: When you face conflicting ideas or feelings, you can find peace knowing these opposites are connected at a deeper level.
shambhu_gita::644.insight: This teaching shifts your view to see apparent opposites as expressions of one underlying reality.

shambhu_gita::645.verse_sanskrit:
मायां वैदान्तिकाः सान्तां मन्यन्ते जगतो यतः ।
असत्यत्वं प्रमातुं वै क्षमन्ते स्म न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::645.verse_hindi: अनादि मानकर भी सान्त माना है। इसी कारण यह शास्त्र जगत को मिथ्यारूप प्रमाणित कर सका है
shambhu_gita::645.english_translation: Philosophers consider the world as an illusion because they cannot accept its falsehood as real.
shambhu_gita::645.translation_literal: मायां (illusion) वैदान्तिकाः (philosophers) सान्तां (consider) मन्यन्ते (think) जगतो (of the world) यतः (because) असत्यत्वं (falsehood) प्रमातुं (to accept) वै (indeed) क्षमन्ते (can) स्म (indeed) न (not) संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::645.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::645.essence: The world feels real because you cannot accept its falsehood as true.
shambhu_gita::645.simple_meaning: People who study deep philosophy see the world as an illusion because they cannot truly accept that what appears real is actually false.
shambhu_gita::645.simple_insight: It’s hard to let go of what feels real, even if it’s an illusion.
shambhu_gita::645.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva explains that philosophers call the world an illusion because they cannot fully accept its unreality. This reflects the difficulty in accepting that what we experience as real is actually false or transient.
shambhu_gita::645.modern_relevance: You trust your senses so deeply that doubting the reality of what you see feels impossible, even when reason suggests otherwise.
shambhu_gita::645.insight: It reveals why people cling to appearances—they cannot emotionally accept that the world might be unreal.

shambhu_gita::646.verse_sanskrit:
भक्तिशास्त्रे पुनर्दैवीमीमांसानामके हिते।
मायां तां ब्रह्मणः शक्ति मत्वा भक्तैः प्रकल्प्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::646.verse_hindi: एवं हे पितृगण ! दैवीमीमांसा रूपी उपासना काण्ड सम्बन्धीय भक्ति शास्त्र ने माया को ब्रह्मशक्ति मानकर
shambhu_gita::646.english_translation: Thus, O ancestors, the scripture of devotion considers the illusion as the power of Brahman and presents it to devotees.
shambhu_gita::646.translation_literal: भक्तिशास्त्रे (in devotion scripture) पुनः (again) दैवी (divine) मीमांसानाम् (of inquiries) अके (related) हिते (for benefit) मायां (illusion) तां (that) ब्रह्मणः (of Brahman) शक्ति (power) मत्वा (considering) भक्तैः (by devotees) प्रकल्प्यते (is presented)
shambhu_gita::646.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::646.essence: Devotion interprets illusion as the sacred power of the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::646.simple_meaning: The teachings of devotion regard illusion not as mere falsehood but as the power of the supreme reality, explaining it to devotees as part of their practice.
shambhu_gita::646.simple_insight: Seeing illusion as a sacred power shifts fear into trust and deepens your devotion.
shambhu_gita::646.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the assembled ancestors, explaining that the scriptures focused on devotion interpret illusion (maya) as a manifestation of Brahman's power, thus giving devotees a way to understand and relate to the cosmic veil through loving faith.
shambhu_gita::646.modern_relevance: When confusing or overwhelming experiences arise, you can reframe them as part of a greater power at work, easing resistance and opening your heart.
shambhu_gita::646.insight: It teaches you to view difficult or confusing aspects of life as expressions of a divine power, transforming your relationship with them.

shambhu_gita::647.verse_sanskrit: अभिन्नत्वं तयोः कल्याः ! उभयोब्रह्ममाययोः ।         शक्तिशक्तिमनार्यस्मात् भेदाभाव: प्रसिध्यति ॥
shambhu_gita::647.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म और माया अभेद, बताया है; क्योंकि शक्ति और शक्तिमान में अभेद होना प्रसिद्ध है
shambhu_gita::647.english_translation: The supreme reality and illusion are ultimately not separate; the distinction between power and the powerful is also unreal.
shambhu_gita::647.translation_literal: अभिन्नत्वं (non-difference) / तयोः (of both) / कल्याः (auspicious/true) / उभयो (both) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / माययोः (illusion) / शक्तिः (power) / शक्तिमन् (powerful one) / अनार्यस्मात् (not inferior) / भेदाभावः (absence of difference) / प्रसिध्यति (is established/famous)
shambhu_gita::647.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::647.essence: The supreme reality and its illusion are fundamentally one without real separation.
shambhu_gita::647.simple_meaning: The supreme reality (Brahman) and illusion (Maya) are not actually separate. Similarly, the power and the one who holds power are not two different things.
shambhu_gita::647.simple_insight: You are closer to your true strength than you realize; separation is an illusion.
shambhu_gita::647.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that the highest reality and illusion are not truly divided. Just as power and the powerful cannot be separated, the appearance of difference between the supreme reality and its veil is a misconception.
shambhu_gita::647.modern_relevance: When you feel weak or powerless, remember that your true nature and your strength are not separate—they are one whole.
shambhu_gita::647.insight: This shifts your view from seeing yourself as fragmented to recognizing unity within your being and abilities.

shambhu_gita::648.verse_sanskrit:
लोके शक्तेर्यथा नास्ति भेदः शक्तिमता सह ।
ब्रह्मशक्तेस्तथा नास्ति भेदो वै ब्रह्मणा सह ॥
shambhu_gita::648.verse_hindi: जैसे मैं और मेरी शक्ति, ऐसा कहने में दोनों का अभेद सिद्ध होता है, ऐसे ही ब्रह्म और ब्रह्मशक्ति माया में अभेद है।
shambhu_gita::648.english_translation: Just as there is no difference between me and my power, similarly there is no difference between Brahman and its power, the veil of appearance.
shambhu_gita::648.translation_literal: लोके (in the world) शक्तेः (of power) यथा (just as) नास्ति (there is no) भेदः (difference) शक्तिमता (with power) सह (with) । ब्रह्मशक्तेः (of Brahman's power) तथा (similarly) नास्ति (there is no) भेदः (difference) वै (indeed) ब्रह्मणा (with Brahman) सह (with) ॥
shambhu_gita::648.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::648.essence: The supreme reality and its power are fundamentally one, not two separate things.
shambhu_gita::648.simple_meaning: The true self and its power are not separate; they are one and the same, like you and your own ability.
shambhu_gita::648.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your strength is not apart from who you truly are.
shambhu_gita::648.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that just as a person is inseparable from their power, Brahman and its creative power, the veil of appearance, are also inseparable. This teaching reveals the non-dual nature of ultimate reality and its manifest energy.
shambhu_gita::648.modern_relevance: You often feel your abilities are separate from who you are, but this reminds you that your true self and your strength act as one.
shambhu_gita::648.insight: It shifts your view from seeing power as external to recognizing it as an inseparable part of your true self.

shambhu_gita::649.verse_sanskrit: यथा शक्तिमतः शक्तिस्तत्रैवाऽव्यक्ततां गता।               कदाचिद्व्यक्तिमापन्ना तत्पृथक्त्वेन भासते ॥
shambhu_gita::649.verse_hindi: जैसे शक्तिमान की शक्ति उसमें कभी अव्यक रहती है और कभी उससे प्रकाशित होकर अलग प्रतीत होती है
shambhu_gita::649.english_translation: Just as the power in the powerful sometimes remains unmanifest and sometimes appears separate as manifest,
shambhu_gita::649.translation_literal: यथा (just as) शक्तिमतः (of the powerful) शक्तिः (power) तत्रैव (there itself) अव्यक्ततां (unmanifest state) गता (goes, remains)। कदाचित् (sometimes) व्यक्तिम् (manifest) आपन्ना (attaining) तत् (that) पृथक्त्वेन (in separation) भासते (appears) ॥
shambhu_gita::649.speaker: Shiva
