shambhu_gita::701.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares the core teaching of Vedanta as a rare secret that is hard to find. He urges immediate and clear understanding, emphasizing that grasping this truth swiftly is crucial for liberation.
shambhu_gita::701.modern_relevance: You suddenly understand a complex idea that others struggle with, and this clarity lights your path forward.
shambhu_gita::701.insight: It teaches you to prioritize clear understanding and swift insight over confusion or delay.

shambhu_gita::702.verse_sanskrit:
अपरोक्षानुभूति हि कृत्वैवासादयन्त्यलम् ।
जीवन्मुक्तिपदं भक्ता ज्ञानिनो मे न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::702.verse_hindi: परोक्षानुभव करके मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तगण शीघ्र ही जीवन्मुक्त पदवी को प्राप्त करते हैं; इसमें सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::702.english_translation: By direct experience, my wise devotees quickly attain the state of freedom in this life; I have no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::702.translation_literal: अपरोक्षानुभूति (direct experience) / हि (indeed) / कृत्वैव (by doing alone) / आसादयन्ति (they attain) / अलम् (this) / जीवन्मुक्तिपदं (the state of freedom in life) / भक्ता (devotees) / ज्ञानिनः (wise ones) / मे (my) / न (no) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::702.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::702.essence: Freedom arises immediately through direct experience by devoted, wise seekers.
shambhu_gita::702.simple_meaning: You can reach true freedom in this life through your own direct experience, without doubt.
shambhu_gita::702.simple_insight: There's confidence in knowing your personal experience is the path to freedom.
shambhu_gita::702.detailed_meaning: Shiva assures that his wise devotees who seek with devotion do not rely on hearsay but directly experience freedom in this life, removing all uncertainty about liberation.
shambhu_gita::702.modern_relevance: You’ve felt the shift when a truth clicks inside you, not just from what others say. That inner knowing changes everything.
shambhu_gita::702.insight: Trust your own lived experience as the surest path to freedom, beyond intellectual doubt.

shambhu_gita::703.verse_sanskrit:
देवादिदेव ! सर्वज्ञ ! सर्वज्ञानाश्रयस्थल।
गुरूणां हे गुरो ! नाथ ! कृपया ते कृपाम्बुधे ! ॥
shambhu_gita::703.verse_hindi: हे देवादिदेव ! हे सब ज्ञानो के आश्रयस्थल ! हे सर्वज्ञ ! हे गुरुओ के गुरु ! हे दयासागर!  हे नाथ ! आपकी कृपा से
shambhu_gita::703.english_translation: O Lord of lords! Knower of all! Refuge of all knowledge! Teacher of teachers! Lord! Ocean of compassion! By your grace...
shambhu_gita::703.translation_literal: देवादिदेव (Lord of lords) / सर्वज्ञ (knower of all) / सर्वज्ञानाश्रयस्थल (refuge of all knowledge) / गुरूणां (of teachers) / हे (O) / गुरो (teacher) / नाथ (lord) / कृपया (by grace) / ते (your) / कृपाम्बुधे (ocean of compassion)
shambhu_gita::703.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::703.essence: Ultimate compassion and wisdom guide those who seek with humility.
shambhu_gita::703.simple_meaning: This is a respectful invocation to Shiva, acknowledging him as the ultimate lord, all-knowing, the support of all wisdom, the teacher of teachers, and a boundless source of compassion.
shambhu_gita::703.simple_insight: Recognizing a source greater than ourselves can inspire humility and openness to guidance.
shambhu_gita::703.detailed_meaning: Suta calls upon Shiva with deep reverence, praising his supreme status, infinite knowledge, and compassionate nature. This invocation sets a tone of devotion and respect for the teachings that follow.
shambhu_gita::703.insight: It invites you to open your heart to guidance beyond your current understanding, fostering trust in the learning process.

shambhu_gita::704.verse_sanskrit:
वैदिकज्ञानकाण्इस्य सारं वेदान्तमद्भुतम् ।
गुहातिगृह्यमाकर्ण्य कृतकृत्या अभूम ह ॥
shambhu_gita::704.verse_hindi: हम वैदिक ज्ञान के साररूप वेदान्त का अद्भुत रहस्य सुनकर कृतकृत्य हुए
shambhu_gita::704.english_translation: Hearing the wondrous secret of Vedanta, the essence of Vedic knowledge, I felt deeply grateful.
shambhu_gita::704.translation_literal: वैदिकज्ञानकाण्इस्य (of Vedic knowledge) / सारं (essence) / वेदान्तमद्भुतम् (wondrous Vedanta) / गुहातिगृह्यमाकर्ण्य (having heard the secret beyond the secret) / कृतकृत्या (grateful) / अभूम (I became) / ह (indeed)
shambhu_gita::704.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::704.essence: Hearing the deepest secret of knowledge inspires true gratitude.
shambhu_gita::704.simple_meaning: Hearing the profound secret of Vedanta, which is the essence of Vedic knowledge, fills one with deep gratitude.
shambhu_gita::704.simple_insight: Gratitude arises naturally when profound truths are understood.
shambhu_gita::704.detailed_meaning: Suta recounts hearing the deepest secret of Vedanta, the essence of all Vedic knowledge, and expresses heartfelt gratitude for this rare teaching.
shambhu_gita::704.insight: It shows how receiving deep wisdom invites sincere appreciation beyond words.

shambhu_gita::705.verse_sanskrit: किन्तु यद्भवता प्रोक्तं वेदान्तस्याधिकारिणः ।                 ज्ञानवन्तोऽभिधीयन्ते जीवन्मुक्ता इति प्रभो !॥
shambhu_gita::705.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे प्रभो ! आपने जो वेदान्त के अधिकारी. ज्ञानी व्यक्ति को जीवन्मुक्त नाम से अभिहित किया है वह जीवन्मुक्त पदवी
shambhu_gita::705.english_translation: But, O Lord, the one described by you as the knower of Vedanta is called the truly liberated one.
shambhu_gita::705.translation_literal: किन्तु (but) यत् (that) भवता (by you) प्रोक्तं (said) वेदान्तस्याधिकारिणः (one authorized in Vedanta) । ज्ञानवन्तः (knowers) अभिधीयन्ते (are called) जीवन्मुक्ता (truly liberated) इति (thus) प्रभो (O Lord) ।
shambhu_gita::705.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::705.essence: True liberation is the natural state of those who deeply know the highest truth.
shambhu_gita::705.simple_meaning: A person who truly understands the highest teaching of Vedanta is called truly liberated.
shambhu_gita::705.simple_insight: Freedom is not a distant goal but the result of deep understanding.
shambhu_gita::705.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva affirms that those who have mastered the teachings of Vedanta, the highest wisdom, attain true liberation. It highlights that liberation is not just a hope but a status achieved by deep realization.
shambhu_gita::705.modern_relevance: When you finally grasp the core of your experience, freedom from confusion naturally follows, like a weight lifting.
shambhu_gita::705.insight: It teaches you to link true freedom with deep knowledge rather than external conditions or rituals.

shambhu_gita::706.verse_sanskrit:
सम्भाव्यते कथं होतत्तन्न विद्द्यो वयं विभो !।
अल्पज्ञ ईरितो जीवः सर्वज्ञोऽस्ति भवान् यतः ॥
shambhu_gita::706.verse_hindi: कैसे सम्भव है ? हे विभो ! इसको हमलोग नहीं जानते हैं क्योंकि हे शम्भो ! आप सर्वज्ञ है जीव अल्पज्ञ है,
shambhu_gita::706.english_translation: How can it happen? O Vibhā! We do not know this because, O Shambhu, you are all-knowing while the living being is little-knowing.
shambhu_gita::706.translation_literal: सम्भाव्यते (happens) कथं (how) होतत् (it happens) तन्न (that) विद्द्यो (know) वयं (we) विभो (O Vibhā) ! / अल्पज्ञ (little-knowing) ईरितः (is) जीवः (living being) सर्वज्ञोऽस्ति (all-knowing is) भवान् (you) यतः (because) ॥
shambhu_gita::706.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::706.essence: Limited beings cannot grasp what the all-knowing divine comprehends.
shambhu_gita::706.simple_meaning: The speaker admits not knowing how something can happen, acknowledging that Shambhu is all-knowing while living beings have limited knowledge.
shambhu_gita::706.simple_insight: It's okay to admit our limited understanding compared to the vast knowing of the divine.
shambhu_gita::706.detailed_meaning: In this moment, someone addresses Shambhu as Vibhā, confessing their inability to comprehend a certain matter. They recognize Shambhu's complete knowledge contrasted with their own limited understanding, highlighting the gap between the divine and the living being.
shambhu_gita::706.modern_relevance: You hit a wall trying to understand a complex problem and realize some answers are beyond your current grasp.
shambhu_gita::706.insight: It invites humility to accept that some knowledge is beyond immediate understanding and to trust sources wiser than ourselves.

shambhu_gita::707.verse_hindi: आप देशकाल से अपरिच्छिन्न हैं जीव देश काल से परिच्छिन्न है, आप समदर्शी सबके अन्तर्यामी और अहङ्कारादि से रहित हैं
shambhu_gita::707.english_translation: You are beyond all place and time; the individual being is limited by place and time. You are an impartial witness within all, free from ego and other bindings.
shambhu_gita::707.translation_literal: देशकालापरिच्छिन्नः (not limited by place and time) त्रं (and) जीवः (individual being) च (also) एकदेशिकः (limited to one place) समदर्शी (impartial seer) भव (you are) अनन्ताम् (infinite) अहङ्कारवजितः (free from ego)
shambhu_gita::707.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::707.essence: Your true self is the limitless, impartial witness beyond ego and temporal limits.
shambhu_gita::707.simple_meaning: You exist beyond all limits of place and time. The individual being is tied to specific places and moments. You see everyone impartially and are free from ego.
shambhu_gita::707.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing you are not confined by any moment or identity.
shambhu_gita::707.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that unlike the individual being who experiences life bound to specific places and times, the true self is unlimited, sees all equally, and is untouched by ego or false identities.
shambhu_gita::707.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck by circumstances or overwhelmed by your roles, remember your true self is beyond those limits and remains a steady witness.
shambhu_gita::707.insight: Shift your perspective from identification with your changing roles to the impartial awareness that watches them all.

shambhu_gita::708.verse_sanskrit:
जीवोऽहङ्कारवान् स्थूलासक्तश्चासमदर्शनः ।
जीवः स्वार्थी संदा शम्भो ! परार्थे तु परो भवान् ॥
shambhu_gita::708.verse_hindi: और जीव असमदर्शी दृश्य में आसक्त और अहङ्कारी है, आप परार्थपर हैं और जीव स्वार्थी है,
shambhu_gita::708.english_translation: The individual is ego-bound, attached to the gross, and lacks equal vision; the individual is self-centered, while you are concerned with the welfare of others.
shambhu_gita::708.translation_literal: जीवोऽहङ्कारवान् (the individual is ego-bound) / स्थूलासक्तश्च (and attached to the gross) / असमदर्शनः (lacking equal vision) / जीवः (the individual) / स्वार्थी (self-centered) / संदा (indeed) / शम्भो (O Shambhu) / परार्थे (for the welfare of others) / तु (but) / परो (you are) / भवान् (indeed).
shambhu_gita::708.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::708.essence: Your true self transcends ego and selfish attachment to care for others.
shambhu_gita::708.simple_meaning: You, the true self, care for others, but the individual is caught in ego, selfishness, and attachment to the physical world.
shambhu_gita::708.simple_insight: Feel the relief of knowing your deeper nature is beyond selfish ego and attachments.
shambhu_gita::708.detailed_meaning: Shiva contrasts the individual, who is trapped in ego and attached to the physical world with limited vision, to the divine self that cares for others beyond selfish concerns.
shambhu_gita::708.modern_relevance: When you find yourself caught in selfish thoughts and attachments, remember your true nature cares for others beyond these limits.
shambhu_gita::708.insight: This teaching helps shift your perspective from self-centeredness to recognizing your nature as connected and other-oriented.

shambhu_gita::709.verse_sanskrit:
भवान् विश्वगुरुनूनं सर्वज्ञानखनिस्तथा ।
अस्त्यज्ञः सर्वथा जीवः स्वरूपज्ञानवजितः ॥
shambhu_gita::709.verse_hindi: आप सबके गुरु और सब ज्ञानों की खान है और जीव सर्वथा अज्ञ और स्वरूपज्ञान शून्य है
shambhu_gita::709.english_translation: The divine is the universal teacher and the source of all knowledge, while the living being is entirely ignorant and devoid of self-knowledge.
shambhu_gita::709.translation_literal: भवान् (the divine) / विश्वगुरुनूनं (universal teacher) / सर्वज्ञानखनिस्तथा (and source of all knowledge) / अस्त्यज्ञः (is ignorant) / सर्वथा (completely) / जीवः (living being) / स्वरूपज्ञानवजितः (devoid of self-knowledge)
shambhu_gita::709.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::709.essence: The divine knows everything; you remain completely unaware of your true nature.
shambhu_gita::709.simple_meaning: The divine is the teacher of everything and the source of all knowledge, but you do not yet truly know your own essential nature.
shambhu_gita::709.simple_insight: It feels humbling to realize that your deepest self is still unknown and learning begins from there.
shambhu_gita::709.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva reveals that while the divine is the supreme teacher and the origin of all wisdom, every living being remains fully ignorant of their true self. The moment invites humility and the quest to know oneself more deeply.
shambhu_gita::709.modern_relevance: You may master many skills or facts, yet still feel disconnected from who you truly are deep inside.
shambhu_gita::709.insight: This verse shifts your focus from external knowledge to the importance of awakening self-knowledge within.

shambhu_gita::710.verse_sanskrit:
अतो जीवः कथं शैवीमुत्तमां पदवीं गतः।
जीवन्मुक्तोऽभिधीयत ज्ञानानन्ददयार्णव ! ॥
shambhu_gita::710.verse_hindi: इस कारण हे ज्ञान, आनन्द और दया के सागर ! जीव कैसे उत्तम शिव पदवी को प्राप्त करके जीवन्मुक्त कहा सकता है ?
shambhu_gita::710.english_translation: O knowledge, ocean of bliss and compassion! How can the living being be called liberated after attaining the supreme Shiva state?
shambhu_gita::710.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) जीवः (living being) कथं (how) शैवीमुत्तमां (supreme Shiva) पदवीं (state) गतः (attained)। जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated living being) अभिधीयत (called) ज्ञानानन्ददयार्णव (knowledge-bliss-compassion ocean) ! ॥
shambhu_gita::710.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::710.essence: True liberation is not guaranteed by reaching a supreme state alone.
shambhu_gita::710.simple_meaning: Reaching a supreme divine state alone does not guarantee true liberation or freedom for the living being.
shambhu_gita::710.simple_insight: True freedom is deeper than achieving a high spiritual status or title.
shambhu_gita::710.detailed_meaning: Shiva questions how a living being can claim to be fully liberated simply by attaining the highest Shiva state. This challenges the assumption that reaching a supreme position equals complete freedom.
shambhu_gita::710.modern_relevance: You might have achieved a major goal or status, yet still feel restless inside, realizing success alone doesn’t bring true freedom.
shambhu_gita::710.insight: It shifts the mind from equating titles or achievements with true inner freedom to questioning what genuine liberation really means.

shambhu_gita::711.verse_sanskrit:
शरीरत्रितयोपेतो भवेज्जीवः कथं गुरो !।
शरीरत्रितयातीतो जीवन्मुक्तो महाजनः ॥
shambhu_gita::711.verse_hindi: हे गुरो ! जीव के तीनों शरीर रहते हुए. जीवन्मुक्त महात्मा कैसे शरीरातीत हो सकते हैं ।
shambhu_gita::711.english_translation: O teacher, how can the liberated great soul be beyond the three bodies while still having them?
shambhu_gita::711.translation_literal: शरीरत्रितयोपेतो (having three bodies) भवेत् (can be) जीवः (the living being) कथं (how) गुरो (O teacher) । शरीरत्रितयातीतो (beyond three bodies) जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated soul) महाजनः (great soul) ॥
shambhu_gita::711.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::711.essence: You can live fully with your bodies and still be free beyond them.
shambhu_gita::711.simple_meaning: It asks how someone can be truly free while still existing with their physical, subtle, and causal bodies.
shambhu_gita::711.simple_insight: Freedom can coexist with our living experience, not just after leaving it.
shambhu_gita::711.detailed_meaning: A question is posed to the teacher about how a liberated soul can transcend the three bodies—physical, subtle, and causal—yet still appear to have them, highlighting the paradox of living liberation.
shambhu_gita::711.modern_relevance: You might wonder how to feel truly free while still carrying your daily burdens and identities.
shambhu_gita::711.insight: It invites shifting perspective from being trapped in the bodies to recognizing freedom within them.

shambhu_gita::712.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्भिर्दशभिोकैः स्वकोषैः पञ्चभिस्तथा।
सार्द्ध सम्बन्धयुक्तोऽपि तत्मभावान्वितोऽपि च ॥
shambhu_gita::712.verse_hindi: चतुर्दश भुवन और पञ्चकोश से सम्बन्ध युक्त रहने पर भी और उनका प्रभाव बना रहने पर भी
shambhu_gita::712.english_translation: Even while connected with the fourteen worlds and the five sheaths, and influenced by them, the true nature remains.
shambhu_gita::712.translation_literal: चतुर्भिर्दशभिोकैः (by fourteen worlds) स्वकोषैः (by own sheaths) पञ्चभिस्तथा (and five also) सार्ध (together) सम्बन्धयुक्तः (connected) अपि (also) तत् (that) भावान्वितः (endowed with nature) अपि (also) च (and)
shambhu_gita::712.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::712.essence: Your true self remains unchanged despite connections and influences from many worlds and layers.
shambhu_gita::712.simple_meaning: Even when you are connected with many worlds and layers of existence, your true nature remains unchanged and present.
shambhu_gita::712.simple_insight: You can feel connected to everything and still know your core is steady and untouched.
shambhu_gita::712.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that although the true self relates to the fourteen worlds (the cosmic realms) and five sheaths (layers of existence like the body and mind), it remains unaffected in its essential nature. This teaching comes amid deep metaphysical discussion on the self’s relation to the cosmos.
shambhu_gita::712.modern_relevance: You juggle many roles and influences every day, yet your true self remains steady beneath all that noise and change.
shambhu_gita::712.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with external layers to recognizing the unchanging essence within.

shambhu_gita::713.verse_sanskrit:
जीवन्मुक्तः कथं देव ! पदं मुक्तेरवाप्नुयात् ।
अंघटयंघटनायां सा प्रकृतिस्ते पटीयसी ॥
shambhu_gita::713.verse_hindi: बना रहने पर भी जीवन्मुक्त कैसे मुक्ति पद को प्राप्त कर सकते हैं। आपकी अघटन घटना पटीयसी प्रकृति
shambhu_gita::713.english_translation: O divine one, how can one be liberated while still living? Your nature is unchanging amid all changes.
shambhu_gita::713.translation_literal: जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated while living) कथं (how) देव (O divine one) ! पदं (state) मुक्तेः (of liberation) अवाप्नुयात् (can obtain) । अंघटयंघटनायां (in unchanging-changing) सा (that) प्रकृतिस्ते (your nature) पटीयसी (is stable) ॥
shambhu_gita::713.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::713.essence: You can be fully alive and already free because your true nature never changes.
shambhu_gita::713.simple_meaning: It asks how a person can be free while still alive, pointing out that your true nature remains unchanged despite all changes.
shambhu_gita::713.simple_insight: You can feel steady freedom even while fully living through change.
shambhu_gita::713.detailed_meaning: Shiva questions how liberation is possible without death, affirming that the true self remains constant amid all worldly transformations, suggesting freedom is through recognizing this unchanging nature.
shambhu_gita::713.modern_relevance: You face constant change and challenges but can still feel steady and free at your core, even as life unfolds around you.
shambhu_gita::713.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing freedom as an after-death state to recognizing freedom in the midst of life’s changes.

shambhu_gita::714.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिगुणैर्मोहयन्सास्ते निजैर्जीवांस्तथाप्यहो ।
जीवन्मुक्तो गुणातीतं पदं लन्धुमलं कथम् ॥
shambhu_gita::714.verse_hindi: अपने तीनों गुणों से सब जीवों को मोहित करती रहती है अहो ! तो भी जीवन्मुक्त कैसे गुणातीत पदवी को प्राप्त कर सकते हैं
shambhu_gita::714.english_translation: The three qualities always delude living beings, yet how can the liberated soul attain the state beyond all qualities?
shambhu_gita::714.translation_literal: त्रिगुणैः (by three qualities) मोहयन् (deluding) सास्ते (all beings) निजैः (by their own) जीवांस् (living beings) तथापि (yet) अहो (oh) जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated soul) गुणातीतं (beyond qualities) पदं (state) लन्धु मलम् (attain how)
shambhu_gita::714.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::714.essence: You can be free even while the three qualities continue to influence others.
shambhu_gita::714.simple_meaning: The three qualities always confuse living beings, yet a liberated person can reach a state beyond these qualities.
shambhu_gita::714.simple_insight: You can be free inside even if the world around you remains confusing and colored by nature.
shambhu_gita::714.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the three qualities of nature (sattva, rajas, tamas) constantly hold beings in delusion. Still, one who is liberated transcends these qualities and reaches a pure state untouched by them.
shambhu_gita::714.modern_relevance: You may feel overwhelmed by influences and moods around you, yet your true self can remain untouched and free.
shambhu_gita::714.insight: Shift focus from being caught in moods and influences to witnessing them without being controlled.

shambhu_gita::715.verse_sanskrit:
भवत्तो व्यतिरिक्तं स्यायत्किञ्चिद्विश्वगोलके ।
तत्सर्वं वर्तते नूनं कर्माधीनं न संशयः॥
shambhu_gita::715.verse_hindi: आपके अतिरिक्त विश्व में सब कुछ कर्माधीन है
shambhu_gita::715.english_translation: Everything in the universe except you is certainly subject to the consequence of action.
shambhu_gita::715.translation_literal: भवत्तो (except you) / व्यतिरिक्तं (beyond) / स्यायत् (would be) / किंचित् (anything) / विश्वगोलके (in the universe) / तत् (that) / सर्वं (all) / वर्तते (exists) / नूनं (indeed) / कर्माधीनं (subject to action) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::715.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::715.essence: Your true self is beyond karma; only the universe is bound by it.
shambhu_gita::715.simple_meaning: Everything in the universe except your true self is controlled by the results of actions.
shambhu_gita::715.simple_insight: You can find freedom knowing you are not bound by karma like everything else.
shambhu_gita::715.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva reveals that while the whole universe is governed by karma, your true self stands apart, untouched and free from action's binding effects.
shambhu_gita::715.modern_relevance: When stress rises over outcomes you can't control, remember you are the part that remains free beyond all consequences.
shambhu_gita::715.insight: Shift your view to see yourself apart from reactive consequences, reducing worry and increasing calm in your actions.

shambhu_gita::716.verse_sanskrit:
धर्माधर्मानुसम्बन्धरहितं नैव चास्यहो ।
जीवन्मुक्तो महात्माऽतो दुर्द्दमं कर्मवन्धनम् ॥
shambhu_gita::716.verse_hindi: और धर्माधर्म सबन्ध से रहित नहीं है अतः जीवन्मुक्त महात्मा कैसे अदमनीय कर्मबन्धन
shambhu_gita::716.english_translation: The great liberated being is never free from the connection of right and wrong, so how can the difficult bondage of actions hold him?
shambhu_gita::716.translation_literal: धर्माधर्म (right-wrong) / अनु सम्बंध रहितं (without connection) / नैव (never) / च (also) / अस्य (his) / अहो (indeed) / जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated being) / महात्मा (great soul) / अतः (therefore) / दुर्दमं (difficult) / कर्मबन्धनम् (bondage of actions)
shambhu_gita::716.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::716.essence: Freedom includes acting within right and wrong without being bound by action’s consequences.
shambhu_gita::716.simple_meaning: Even a truly free person remains connected to right and wrong actions and is not bound by the consequences.
shambhu_gita::716.simple_insight: You can stay engaged in right and wrong without being trapped by the results of your actions.
shambhu_gita::716.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even the great liberated souls remain linked to the concepts of right and wrong, yet they are not caught in the difficult bondage of action. This teaching arises in a moment clarifying how freedom coexists with active engagement.
shambhu_gita::716.modern_relevance: You might feel stuck between doing what’s right and avoiding mistakes, yet freedom comes when you act without clinging to outcomes.
shambhu_gita::716.insight: It shifts your view to see freedom as engaging with action consciously without getting caught in its consequences.

shambhu_gita::717.verse_sanskrit:
धर्माधर्ममुसम्बन्धं छित्वा च क्षमते कथम् ।
स्थूलादिदेहसत्त्वेऽपि गन्तुं ब्रह्मस्वरूपताम् ॥
shambhu_gita::717.verse_hindi: और धर्माधर्म के सम्बन्ध से रहित होकर स्थूलादि शरीर रहते हुए भी ब्रह्मीभूत होने में समर्थ होते हैं।
shambhu_gita::717.english_translation: Even while remaining in the gross body, one can transcend notions of right and wrong and attain the nature of the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::717.translation_literal: धर्माधर्मम् (right-wrong) / सम्बन्धं (relation) / छित्वा (cutting off) / च (and) / क्षमते (is able) / कथम् (how) / स्थूलादि (gross and others) / देहसत्त्वेऽपि (even in the body existence) / गन्तुं (to go) / ब्रह्मस्वरूपताम् (to the supreme reality's nature)
shambhu_gita::717.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::717.essence: Your true self transcends moral dualities even while embodied.
shambhu_gita::717.simple_meaning: You can overcome the dual ideas of right and wrong even while living in your physical body and realize your true, divine nature.
shambhu_gita::717.simple_insight: You carry freedom inside you, even amidst everyday dualities and judgments.
shambhu_gita::717.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that a person need not escape the physical body or common notions of right and wrong to realize their true self as supreme reality. Even within the gross body, one can transcend dualities and experience the ultimate nature.
shambhu_gita::717.modern_relevance: When faced with daily moral judgments or personal conflicts, you can remember that your deeper self is untouched by these opposites and remains free.
shambhu_gita::717.insight: It shifts your perspective from being trapped in moral labels to seeing yourself as the unchanging essence beyond them.

shambhu_gita::718.verse_sanskrit:
भवानपि यदा भूमाववतीर्णः कदाचन।
कर्माद्यायत्ततामाप्तो भवत्येवाक्षिगोचरः ॥
shambhu_gita::718.verse_hindi: जब आप भी कभी कभी अवतार धारण करके कर्मादि के अधीन दिखाई पड़ते हैं तो
shambhu_gita::718.english_translation: Even when you sometimes take a form and appear bound by action, you remain the one beyond the senses.
shambhu_gita::718.translation_literal: भवानपि (you also) / यदा (when) / भूमाववतीर्णः (having descended to the earth) / कदाचन (sometimes) / कर्माद्यायत्ततामाप्तो (appearing subject to action, etc.) / भवत्येवाक्षिगोचरः (you alone are visible to the eye)
shambhu_gita::718.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::718.essence: You can appear bound by action yet remain beyond all sensory limits.
shambhu_gita::718.simple_meaning: You may appear involved in actions as if limited by them, but your true nature is beyond all sensory perception.
shambhu_gita::718.simple_insight: It feels freeing to know you are never truly trapped by what you do or how others see you.
shambhu_gita::718.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even when the divine takes a worldly form and seems subject to actions and conditions, the true self remains untouched and unseen by the senses. This shows the difference between form and essence during embodiment.
shambhu_gita::718.modern_relevance: Sometimes you feel caught up in tasks and roles, but this reminds you that your true self is beyond all those appearances.
shambhu_gita::718.insight: This shifts your view from identifying with actions to recognizing your deeper, unchanging presence behind them.

shambhu_gita::719.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानिनस्तार्ह ते भक्ता जीवन्मुक्ताः कृपानिधे ।
शक्नुयुः कथमत्येतुं कर्मप्रभृतिवन्धनम् ॥
shambhu_gita::719.verse_hindi: हे कृपानिधान! आपके ज्ञानी भक्त जीवन्मुक्तगण कैसे, इन सब कर्मादि बन्धन से अतीत हो सकते हैं
shambhu_gita::719.english_translation: O treasure of compassion, how can your wise devotees, who are free while living, transcend all bonds of action?
shambhu_gita::719.translation_literal: ज्ञानिनः (wise ones) तारः (are able) ते (your) भक्ता (devotees) जीवन्मुक्ताः (liberated while living) कृपानिधे (O treasure of compassion) शक्नुयुः (can) कथम् (how) अति (beyond) एतुम् (to go) कर्म (action) प्रभृति (and others) बन्धनम् (bonds)
shambhu_gita::719.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::719.essence: Living wisely means freedom beyond all binding consequences of action.
shambhu_gita::719.simple_meaning: Wise devotees who live fully free themselves from all attachments to actions and their consequences.
shambhu_gita::719.simple_insight: You can live free while acting, untouched by the bonds of your deeds.
shambhu_gita::719.detailed_meaning: At a moment of questioning, someone asks how the wise devotees of the compassionate divine remain free while still living, untouched by the usual bonds that tie others to their actions and outcomes.
shambhu_gita::719.modern_relevance: You wonder how some people seem calm and unburdened despite busy lives full of responsibilities and pressures.
shambhu_gita::719.insight: It shifts your view from seeing actions as chains to seeing wise living as freedom despite action.

shambhu_gita::720.verse_sanskrit:
एवञ्चेत्तेऽवतारेषु ज्ञानिभक्तेषु च प्रभो!।
जीवन्मुक्तेषु को भेदो वर्त्तते भक्तवत्सल ! ॥
shambhu_gita::720.verse_hindi: यदि ऐसा हो तो हे भक्तवत्सल ! आपके अवतारों में और आपके ज्ञानी, भक्त जीवन्मुक्तो में भेद क्या है ?
shambhu_gita::720.english_translation: If that is so, O lover of devotees, what difference is there between your incarnations and your wise, devoted liberated beings?
shambhu_gita::720.translation_literal: एवञ्चेत् (if so) तेऽवतारेषु (in your incarnations) ज्ञानि-भक्तेषु (in wise devotees) च (and) प्रभो (O lord)! जीवन्मुक्तेषु (in liberated beings) को (what) भेदो (difference) वर्त्तते (exists) भक्तवत्सल (lover of devotees)!
shambhu_gita::720.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::720.essence: There may be no real difference between divine incarnations and liberated devotees.
shambhu_gita::720.simple_meaning: You ask what the difference is between divine incarnations and wise, devoted beings who are already liberated.
shambhu_gita::720.simple_insight: Sometimes questions arise about distinctions that may not truly exist.
shambhu_gita::720.detailed_meaning: The bard Suta raises a question to the assembly about what really separates divine incarnations from wise devotees who have attained liberation, inviting deeper exploration.
shambhu_gita::720.insight: It encourages questioning apparent differences between exemplars and enlightened individuals to see underlying unity.

shambhu_gita::721.verse_sanskrit:
एवं विधैश्च नश्चित्तं शङ्कासैर्वीलोड़ितम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वे समाधाय शान्ति तस्मिन् प्रयच्छ नः ॥
shambhu_gita::721.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार की शङ्काओं से हमारे अन्तःकरण आलोदित हो रहे हैं इसलिये हमारी शंकाओं का समाधान करके
shambhu_gita::721.english_translation: Our inner state is troubled by such doubts; therefore, grant us peace by resolving all these doubts.
shambhu_gita::721.translation_literal: एवं (thus) विधैः (by methods) च (and) नः (our) चित्तं (mind) शङ्कासैः (by doubts) वीलोड़ितम् (disturbed) । तस्मात् (therefore) सर्वे (all) समाधाय (having resolved) शान्ति (peace) तस्मिन् (in that) प्रयच्छ (grant) नः (us) ॥
shambhu_gita::721.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::721.essence: Peace arises only when doubts disturbing your mind are fully resolved.
shambhu_gita::721.simple_meaning: Doubts disturb your mind and inner state. When you clear these doubts, peace naturally arises.
shambhu_gita::721.simple_insight: You can feel relief when your restless mind settles through clarity.
shambhu_gita::721.detailed_meaning: The verse expresses how the inner state (Chitta) becomes troubled by doubts and hesitation. It asks for peace to be granted by removing these doubts, highlighting the importance of clarity for calmness.
shambhu_gita::721.modern_relevance: When your mind races with doubts before a big decision, you feel unsettled until clarity brings calm.
shambhu_gita::721.insight: It teaches you to recognize doubts as the source of inner unrest and seek their resolution to restore calm.

shambhu_gita::722.verse_sanskrit:
वयं येन कृतार्थत्वं सद्गुरो ! सँल्लभेमहि ।
मनो येन मिलिन्दो नो भवेत्तव पदाम्बुजे ॥
shambhu_gita::722.verse_hindi: हमें कृतार्थ कीजिये जिससे हमारा मन भ्रमर की तरह आपके चरणकमलों में लग जाय
shambhu_gita::722.english_translation: O true teacher, grant us fulfillment so our minds may settle at your lotus feet like a bee.
shambhu_gita::722.translation_literal: वयं (we) येन (by which) कृतार्थत्वं (fulfillment) सद्गुरो (O true teacher) ! सँल्लभेमहि (may we obtain) । मनो (mind) येन (by which) मिलिन्दो (bee) नो (our) भवेत्तव (may become) पदाम्बुजे (at the lotus feet) ॥
shambhu_gita::722.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::722.essence: True fulfillment draws the restless mind gently to devoted stillness.
shambhu_gita::722.simple_meaning: You ask the true teacher to give you a sense of fulfillment so your restless mind can peacefully focus on the divine.
shambhu_gita::722.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your restless mind can find a place of calm and devotion.
shambhu_gita::722.detailed_meaning: In a moment of humble prayer, the speaker asks the true teacher, likely Shiva, to grant a deep sense of fulfillment that quiets the mind’s restlessness, drawing it like a bee to peaceful devotion at the divine lotus feet.
shambhu_gita::722.modern_relevance: When your mind buzzes with worry and distraction, you long for a place or feeling that settles and centers you completely.
shambhu_gita::722.insight: This verse invites you to seek fulfillment that naturally draws your attention and calms mental agitation.

shambhu_gita::723.verse_sanskrit:
उत्पत्तिश्च विनाशश्च भूतानामागतिं गतिम् ।
वेत्ति विद्यामविद्याञ्च स ज्ञेयो भगवानिति ॥
shambhu_gita::723.verse_hindi: हे पितरों जो उत्पति और विनाश को, जीवों की अगति और गति को एवं विद्या और अविद्या को जानते हो उन्हीं को भगवान जानो
shambhu_gita::723.english_translation: The one who understands creation and destruction, the coming and going of beings, as well as knowledge and ignorance, is known as the divine.
shambhu_gita::723.translation_literal: उत्पत्तिश्च (creation and) / विनाशश्च (destruction also) / भूतानामागतिं (the coming of beings) / गतिम् (and going) / वेत्ति (knows) / विद्यामविद्याञ्च (knowledge and ignorance also) / स (he) / ज्ञेयो (to be known) / भगवानिति (as the divine).
shambhu_gita::723.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::723.essence: Understanding birth, death, knowledge, and ignorance reveals the nature of the divine.
shambhu_gita::723.simple_meaning: Understanding how life begins and ends, how beings come and go, and how knowledge contrasts with ignorance reveals the true divine nature.
shambhu_gita::723.simple_insight: You feel connected when you see life's full cycle and the dance of knowing and not knowing.
shambhu_gita::723.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to the sages, explaining that truly knowing the processes of creation, destruction, and the flow of beings, along with knowledge and ignorance, is how one recognizes the divine presence behind all.
shambhu_gita::723.modern_relevance: When you watch a tree grow, shed leaves, and begin again, or when you learn something new after confusion, you glimpse the deeper pattern behind life.
shambhu_gita::723.insight: It teaches you to see beyond appearances to the underlying cycles and contrasts that reveal deeper truth.

shambhu_gita::724.verse_sanskrit:
भगवच्छन्दवाच्यः स्यामेतैरेवगुणैरहम् ।
ते सर्वे स्म प्रकाशन्ते गुणा भागवते ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::724.verse_hindi: जिन गुणों से मैं भगवान् शब्दवाच्य हूँ वह सब गुण
shambhu_gita::724.english_translation: I am the supreme being spoken of by these very qualities; all qualities certainly shine in the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::724.translation_literal: भगवच्छन्दवाच्यः (spoken of as the supreme being) स्यामेतैरेवगुणैरहम् (I am by these very qualities) । ते सर्वे स्म (all these indeed) प्रकाशन्ते (shine) गुणा (qualities) भागवते (in the supreme reality) ध्रुवम् (certainly) ॥
shambhu_gita::724.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::724.essence: The supreme reality fully embodies and shines through all qualities.
shambhu_gita::724.simple_meaning: The qualities that describe the supreme being are exactly those in which I exist and shine fully.
shambhu_gita::724.simple_insight: Understanding that the supreme reality expresses itself through all qualities brings a sense of awe and unity.
shambhu_gita::724.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares that the qualities attributed to the supreme being are not separate from him; rather, he embodies them fully, revealing the unity between the qualities and the supreme reality itself.
shambhu_gita::724.insight: Recognize that what seems like many traits or qualities are expressions of a singular supreme essence.

shambhu_gita::725.verse_sanskrit:
अतो भागवतस्येह देहिनोऽपि हि तिष्ठतः।
अहो भगवता सार्द्ध कश्चिद्भेदो न विद्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::725.verse_hindi: भागवत में अवश्य प्रकाशित हो जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::725.english_translation: The embodied being who abides in the divine sees no difference from the divine.
shambhu_gita::725.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) / भागवतस्येह (in the divine) / देहिनः (the embodied being) / अपि (also) / हि (indeed) / तिष्ठतः (abiding) / अहो (ah) / भगवता (with the divine) / सार्ध (together) / कश्चित् (anyone) / भेदः (difference) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists)
shambhu_gita::725.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::725.essence: Living within the divine removes all sense of separation.
shambhu_gita::725.simple_meaning: When you live fully connected with the divine, you no longer feel separate from it.
shambhu_gita::725.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing the divine and your true self are not two.
shambhu_gita::725.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when a living being dwells in harmony with the divine presence, the sense of separation vanishes, revealing unity rather than division.
shambhu_gita::725.modern_relevance: In moments when you feel deeply connected to something greater, the usual boundaries between you and others fade away.
shambhu_gita::725.insight: It teaches you to recognize your shared essence with the divine, dissolving feelings of isolation.

shambhu_gita::726.verse_sanskrit: यदा हि ज्ञानिनो भक्ताः सम्माप्ता मत्स्वरूपताम् ।           त्रिभावात्मकरूपस्य सगुणस्य रहस्यकम् ॥
shambhu_gita::726.verse_hindi: इसलिये भगवान् और भागवत में कोई भी भेद नहीं है। अतः जब मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त मेरे स्वरूप में पहुंचकर मेरे त्रिभावमय सगुण
shambhu_gita::726.english_translation: When the devotees who possess knowledge reach the state of unity with my true form, the mystery of my threefold nature manifesting with qualities is revealed.
shambhu_gita::726.translation_literal: यदा (when) हि (indeed) ज्ञानिनो (the knowledgeable ones) भक्ताः (devotees) सम्माप्ता (have reached) मत् (my) स्वरूपताम् (true form) । त्रिभावात्मकरूपस्य (of the threefold nature) सगुणस्य (with qualities) रहस्यकम् (the mystery)
shambhu_gita::726.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::726.essence: True knowledge and devotion together reveal the divine’s threefold, mysterious nature within you.
shambhu_gita::726.simple_meaning: When knowledgeable devotees unite with the true self, they understand the secret of the divine’s threefold nature with qualities.
shambhu_gita::726.simple_insight: There is deep fulfillment in realizing the unity and mystery of the divine within you.
shambhu_gita::726.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to his followers that those who combine knowledge and devotion, upon reaching his true form, perceive the hidden mystery of his threefold nature filled with qualities. This moment reveals the profound unity between the divine and the devotee.
shambhu_gita::726.modern_relevance: You might feel disconnected sometimes, but when insight and love combine, you glimpse the deeper unity behind your experience.
shambhu_gita::726.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing a profound, multifaceted unity with the divine.

shambhu_gita::727.verse_sanskrit:
निर्गुणस्यापि ज्ञात्वैव मद्युक्ता भवितुं सदा ।
शक्नुवन्ति तदा सृष्टेरुत्पत्तिमलयौ ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::727.verse_hindi: निर्गुण रूप का रहस्य जानकर सब समय मुझमे ही युक्त रहने में समर्थ होते हैं उस समय जगत के उत्पत्ति
shambhu_gita::727.english_translation: Knowing the secret of the formless, beings can always remain united with me; then they can certainly understand the world's creation.
shambhu_gita::727.translation_literal: निर्गुणस्यापि (of the formless) ज्ञात्वैव (by knowing certainly) मद्युक्ता (united with me) भवितुं (to be) सदा (always) । शक्नुवन्ति (are able) तदा (then) सृष्टेर् (of creation) उत्पत्तिम् (origin) अलयौ (the foundation) ध्रुवम् (certain) ॥
shambhu_gita::727.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::727.essence: Understanding the formless lets you stay united and clearly see creation's foundation.
shambhu_gita::727.simple_meaning: When you understand the formless essence, you can always stay connected with the divine and then see how the entire world originates.
shambhu_gita::727.simple_insight: Feeling connected to what is beyond form brings clarity about where everything comes from.
shambhu_gita::727.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that those who realize the secret of the formless (the unchanging essence beyond all qualities) can remain constantly united with him and thereby clearly perceive the true origin of the universe.
shambhu_gita::727.modern_relevance: When you stop clinging to appearances and connect to your inner essence, you gain insight into how everything around you truly arises.
shambhu_gita::727.insight: It teaches you to shift focus from surface changes to the unchanging foundation, revealing the world's origin.

shambhu_gita::728.verse_sanskrit:
असेतुं नाहतस्तेषां दृष्टिमार्ग कथञ्चन ।
महात्मानो महामान्यास्ते तदा त्वात्मदर्शिनः ॥
shambhu_gita::728.verse_hindi: और विनाश उनकी दृष्टि से अतीत नहीं हो सकते। आत्मदर्शी महामान्य महापुरुष तब
shambhu_gita::728.english_translation: Those who see the true self do not view others as destroyed or lost.
shambhu_gita::728.translation_literal: असेतुं (not destroyed) / नाहतस्तेषां (by them) / दृष्टिम् (view) / मार्ग (way) / कथञ्चन (in any way) / महात्मनो (great souls) / महामान्यास्ते (highly respected are they) / तदा (then) / त्वात्मदर्शिनः (self-seeing)
shambhu_gita::728.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::728.essence: True seers recognize no one or nothing is ever truly destroyed or lost.
shambhu_gita::728.simple_meaning: People who truly see their own inner being do not regard others as destroyed or lost.
shambhu_gita::728.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing that nothing truly disappears from the perspective of true understanding.
shambhu_gita::728.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva explains that those who have realized their true self see beyond destruction and loss. They are great and respected because their vision transcends the apparent end of things, recognizing the eternal nature beneath.
shambhu_gita::728.modern_relevance: You watch a friendship fade but sense its essence remains, untouched by time or absence.
shambhu_gita::728.insight: It shifts your view from seeing endings to seeing continuity and presence beyond appearances.

shambhu_gita::729.verse_sanskrit:
नूनं जीवप्रवाहस्य समुत्पत्तिञ्च सर्वतः।
चतुर्धाभूतसङ्घस्य प्रसक्षीकुर्वते गतिम् ॥
shambhu_gita::729.verse_hindi: जीवप्रवाह की उत्पत्ति और चतुर्विध भूतसङ्घ की गति को सर्वथा प्रत्यक्ष करते हैं और
shambhu_gita::729.english_translation: They fully reveal the origin of the flow of living beings and the movement of the fourfold elements.
shambhu_gita::729.translation_literal: नूनं (indeed) जीवप्रवाहस्य (of the flow of living beings) समुत्पत्तिञ्च (and origin) सर्वतः (completely) चतुर्धाभूतसङ्घस्य (of the group of four elements) प्रसक्षीकुर्वते (reveal clearly) गतिम् (the movement)
shambhu_gita::729.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::729.essence: The origin and motion of life and elements are fully revealed here.
shambhu_gita::729.simple_meaning: The origin and movement of all living beings and the four basic elements are fully revealed here.
shambhu_gita::729.simple_insight: Understanding the source and flow of life and nature brings clarity about existence.
shambhu_gita::729.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates how the teaching fully unveils the beginning of all living beings and the dynamic movement of the four fundamental elements, setting the stage for deeper philosophical insights.
shambhu_gita::729.insight: It emphasizes that seeing the root and movement of life and nature opens understanding beyond surface appearances.

shambhu_gita::730.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानिभक्तास्तदा ते च प्राप्य मत्प्रकृतेः कृपाम् ।              विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपे द्वे तस्या दृट्वा मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
shambhu_gita::730.verse_hindi: हे पितरो ! तब वे ज्ञानीभक्त मेरी प्रकृति की कृपा को पाकर उसके विद्या भौर अविद्या दोनों रूपों का बार बार दर्शन करके
shambhu_gita::730.english_translation: O ancestors! Then those wise devotees, having received my nature's grace, repeatedly beheld both its forms: knowledge and ignorance.
shambhu_gita::730.translation_literal: हे (O) / पितरो (ancestors) / तब (then) / वे (those) / ज्ञानीभक्त (wise devotees) / मेरी (my) / प्रकृतेः (nature's) / कृपाम् (grace) / विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपे (forms of knowledge and ignorance) / द्वे (both) / तस्या (of that) / दृट्वा (having seen) / मुहुर्मुहुः (again and again)
shambhu_gita::730.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::730.essence: Repeatedly seeing both knowledge and ignorance invites the divine's grace into your life.
shambhu_gita::730.simple_meaning: Wise devotees receive the divine's grace by repeatedly observing both knowledge and ignorance within existence.
shambhu_gita::730.simple_insight: There's strength in embracing both clarity and confusion as parts of your path.
shambhu_gita::730.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that wise devotees gain his grace by continually witnessing the dual aspects of knowledge and ignorance within the natural world and themselves.
shambhu_gita::730.modern_relevance: You find moments of clarity and confusion in your learning; both together deepen your growth when accepted repeatedly.
shambhu_gita::730.insight: This verse encourages you to open your awareness to both understanding and doubt, allowing grace to unfold naturally.

shambhu_gita::731.verse_sanskrit:
स्वयमेव प्रजायन्ते प्रकृतिस्थाः स्वधाभुजः !।
नास्ति कोऽप्यत्र सन्देहः ससं सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥
shambhu_gita::731.verse_hindi: प्रकृतिस्थ हो जाते हैं इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं; मैं सत्य सत्य कहता हूँ
shambhu_gita::731.english_translation: Those established in the natural world are born by themselves; there is no doubt in this, I speak the truth.
shambhu_gita::731.translation_literal: स्वयमेव (by themselves) / प्रजायन्ते (are born) / प्रकृतिस्थाः (those established in nature) / स्वधाभुजः (self-born) / नास्ति (there is not) / कोऽपि (anyone) / तत्र (there) / सन्देहः (doubt) / स (with) / सत्यं (truth) / ब्रवीमि (I speak) / अहम् (I)
shambhu_gita::731.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::731.essence: Natural phenomena arise spontaneously without external cause; this is an undeniable truth.
shambhu_gita::731.simple_meaning: Things that belong to the natural world come into existence by themselves without external cause.
shambhu_gita::731.simple_insight: There is reassurance in knowing that natural processes unfold on their own without needing interference.
shambhu_gita::731.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that everything established in the natural world (Prakriti) arises spontaneously on its own. This teaching reassures Arjuna that natural existence is self-originated without doubt, emphasizing the autonomous nature of material creation.
shambhu_gita::731.modern_relevance: You notice how plants grow and seasons change without your control or effort—life unfolds naturally on its own.
shambhu_gita::731.insight: It shifts your view to see natural events as self-arising, reducing the urge to control or resist what happens.

shambhu_gita::732.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मिन् काले च ते भक्ता आत्मज्ञानाव्धिपारगाः।
मत्सायुज्यं समापन्ना मद्रूपाः स्युः सुनिश्चितम् ॥
shambhu_gita::732.verse_hindi: उस समय वह आत्मज्ञानी भक्त मत्सायुज्य को प्राप्त करके मेरे ही रूप बन जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::732.english_translation: At that time, those devoted who have crossed the ocean of self-knowledge reach union with me and become firmly established in my form.
shambhu_gita::732.translation_literal: तस्मिन् (at that) / काले (time) / च (also) / ते (those) / भक्ता (devotees) / आत्मज्ञानाव्धि (ocean of self-knowledge) / पारगाः (having crossed) / मत्सायुज्यं (union with me) / समापन्ना (arrived) / मद्रूपाः (my form) / स्युः (become) / सुनिश्चितम् (firmly established)
shambhu_gita::732.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::732.essence: Deep devotion and self-knowledge together bring unshakable union with the divine form.
shambhu_gita::732.simple_meaning: When you fully realize your true self through deep devotion and knowledge, you unite completely with the divine and become established in that unity.
shambhu_gita::732.simple_insight: There is profound peace when devotion and self-knowledge merge into oneness with the divine.
shambhu_gita::732.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that devotees who have mastered deep self-knowledge and crossed its vast ocean reach a state of union with him, becoming firmly established in his divine form, symbolizing complete spiritual realization.
shambhu_gita::732.modern_relevance: After long searching and learning about who you truly are, you finally feel fully connected with the highest truth inside you.
shambhu_gita::732.insight: It teaches that spiritual devotion combined with clear self-understanding leads to unwavering unity with the divine form.

shambhu_gita::733.verse_sanskrit:
यदा मे ज्ञानिनो भक्ताः संविदन्तीह मामलम् ।
ब्रह्मणोरुभयोरेव कार्यकारणरूपयोः ॥
shambhu_gita::733.verse_hindi: मेरे ज्ञानीभक्त जब मुझको भलीभांति जान लेते हैं तो कार्यब्रह्म और कारण ब्रह्मा की
shambhu_gita::733.english_translation: When my wise devotees truly know me, they realize I am both the supreme reality and the cause of all causes.
shambhu_gita::733.translation_literal: यदा (when) / मे (my) / ज्ञानिनो (wise ones) / भक्ताः (devotees) / संविदन्तीह (truly know) / मामलम् (me) / ब्रह्मणो (of the supreme reality) / उभयोरिव (of both) / कार्यकारणरूपयोः (form of cause and effect)
shambhu_gita::733.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::733.essence: True devotion recognizes the divine as both the cause and essence of all existence.
shambhu_gita::733.simple_meaning: When devoted seekers truly understand the divine, they see it as both the supreme reality and the cause behind all things.
shambhu_gita::733.simple_insight: Knowing the divine deeply reveals it as both origin and outcome, inspiring devotion beyond separation.
shambhu_gita::733.detailed_meaning: Shiva tells that when his wise devotees fully recognize him, they see him not only as the supreme reality itself but also as the cause behind everything that happens, uniting existence and origin in one.
shambhu_gita::733.modern_relevance: You meet someone who inspires you so deeply that you feel they are both the root and the whole of what matters in life.
shambhu_gita::733.insight: It shifts your view from seeing the divine as distant to recognizing it as intimately both the source and the substance of all experience.

shambhu_gita::734.verse_sanskrit:
तदैक्यं जायते तेषां ध्रुवमेवान्तरात्मनि ।
ब्रह्मरूपा भवन्त्येव तेऽतो नैवात्र संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::734.verse_hindi: एकता उनके अन्तःकरण में हो जाने से वह ब्रह्म रूप ही हो जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::734.english_translation: When their unity arises within the inner self, they truly become the form of the supreme reality; there is no doubt about this.
shambhu_gita::734.translation_literal: तत् (that) / ऐक्यम् (unity) / जायते (arises) / तेषाम् (of them) / ध्रुवम् (certainly) / एव (indeed) / अन्तरात्मनि (in the inner self) / ब्रह्मरूपा (form of the supreme reality) / भवन्ति (become) / एव (indeed) / ते (they) / अतो (therefore) / नै (not) / अत्र (here) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::734.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::734.essence: Your deepest inner unity is unmistakably the supreme reality itself.
shambhu_gita::734.simple_meaning: When all differences dissolve inside your deepest self, you become one with the supreme reality without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::734.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your deepest self is already whole and divine.
shambhu_gita::734.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva explains that when the diverse aspects within a person unify deeply in their inner self, that unity is no less than the supreme reality itself. This teaching reveals the non-dual truth beyond appearances.
shambhu_gita::734.modern_relevance: When your scattered thoughts and feelings settle into harmony inside, you touch a timeless wholeness beyond stress.
shambhu_gita::734.insight: It invites you to recognize your inner unity as the true foundation beneath all change and conflict.

shambhu_gita::735.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वेषु प्राणिपुत्रेषु येपामुत्पद्यते ननु ।
ब्रह्मबुर्धिमहात्मानो जीवन्मुक्ता भवन्ति ते ॥
shambhu_gita::735.verse_hindi: जिनमें सब प्राणीमात्रों पर ब्रह्म बुद्धि उत्पन्न हुई है वह महात्मा जीवन्मुक्त हैं
shambhu_gita::735.english_translation: Those in whom the wisdom of the supreme reality arises for all living beings become great souls freed from rebirth.
shambhu_gita::735.translation_literal: सर्वेषु (in all) / प्राणिपुत्रेषु (living beings) / ये (who) /epam (also) / उत्पद्यते (arises) / ननु (indeed) / ब्रह्मबुर्धिमहात्मानो (of supreme reality wisdom great souls) / जीवन्मुक्ता (free from rebirth) / भवन्ति (become) / ते (they)
shambhu_gita::735.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::735.essence: Freedom arises when you see supreme wisdom present in all living beings.
shambhu_gita::735.simple_meaning: When you develop deep understanding that connects all beings, you become a great soul free from life's cycle.
shambhu_gita::735.simple_insight: Freedom comes with realizing the supreme wisdom within all living beings.
shambhu_gita::735.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that those whose awareness embraces the supreme wisdom in every living being transcend rebirth and become great souls, highlighting the deep unity beyond individual separation.
shambhu_gita::735.modern_relevance: You feel connected to everyone around you, and in that connection, your sense of personal limitation begins to dissolve.
shambhu_gita::735.insight: It teaches you to recognize the shared divine wisdom in all life, which frees you from feeling separate.

shambhu_gita::736.verse_sanskrit:
अपरोक्षं ध्रुवं येषां ब्रह्मज्ञानं प्रजायते ।
ते महापुरुषा लोके जीवन्मुक्ता न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::736.verse_hindi: जिनको अपरोक्ष रूप से ब्रह्मज्ञान उत्पन्न हुआ है वह महापुरुष संसार में जीवन्मुक्त हैं
shambhu_gita::736.english_translation: Those in whom direct, unwavering knowledge of the supreme reality arises are great beings, undoubtedly liberated while alive.
shambhu_gita::736.translation_literal: अपरोक्षं (directly perceived) / ध्रुवं (unwavering) / येषां (in whom) / ब्रह्मज्ञानं (knowledge of the supreme reality) / प्रजायते (arises) / ते (those) / महापुरुषा (great beings) / लोके (in the world) / जीवन्मुक्ता (liberated while alive) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::736.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::736.essence: Direct, unwavering knowledge of the supreme reality grants living liberation.
shambhu_gita::736.simple_meaning: Direct, unwavering knowledge of the supreme reality makes a person truly free in life.
shambhu_gita::736.simple_insight: You can be free now by knowing clearly who you really are beyond appearances.
shambhu_gita::736.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes those who gain direct, certain knowledge of the supreme reality as great beings who are liberated even while living, emphasizing liberation is possible now through wisdom.
shambhu_gita::736.modern_relevance: You realize freedom not after life ends but by seeing clearly what truly is beyond your daily struggles and illusions.
shambhu_gita::736.insight: It teaches you to seek direct, clear understanding instead of relying on indirect beliefs or doubts.

shambhu_gita::737.verse_sanskrit:
देहोऽस्मि पुरुषश्चास्मि शूद्रोऽस्मि ब्राह्मणोऽस्मि च ।
यथेत्थं दृढविश्वासस्तथैव पितृपुङ्गवाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::737.verse_hindi: जैसे मैं देह हूँ, मैं पुरुष हूँ. मैं ब्राह्मण हूँ, मैं शुद्र हूँ, इस प्रकारसे दृढ़ निश्चय होता है
shambhu_gita::737.english_translation: Just as I am the body, I am pure awareness; I am both the highest and the lowest, so firm is the conviction of the forefathers.
shambhu_gita::737.translation_literal: देह (body) अस्मि (am) पुरुष (pure awareness) च (and) अस्मि (am) शूद्र (lowest class) अस्मि (am) ब्राह्मण (highest class) अस्मि (am) च (and) । यथा (just as) एत्थं (thus) दृढ (firm) विश्वासः (conviction) तथा (so) एव (indeed) पितृपुङ्गवाः (forefathers) ।
shambhu_gita::737.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::737.essence: Your true self transcends all labels, roles, and distinctions without contradiction.
shambhu_gita::737.simple_meaning: You are not just one fixed identity like body or social role; your true self includes all, from highest to lowest.
shambhu_gita::737.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you transcend any single label or role assigned by society or mind.
shambhu_gita::737.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to sages that the true self is not limited by physical body or social categories like brahmin or shudra; these are superficial. Firm conviction in this truth comes from ancient wise teachers, revealing the unity beyond apparent divisions.
shambhu_gita::737.modern_relevance: At work or home, you may feel boxed in by roles or expectations. This teaching reminds you that you are much more than any label others apply.
shambhu_gita::737.insight: It shifts your mind from limiting self-identifications to embracing a wider, unified sense of being.

shambhu_gita::738.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं देहो न पुरुषो न शूद्रो ब्राह्मणो न च ।
निजस्वरूपे किन्त्वस्मि सच्चिदानन्दरूपकः ॥
shambhu_gita::738.verse_hindi: वैसे ही मैं देह नहीं हूँ, न पुरुष हूँ, न ब्राह्मण हूँ, न शूद्र हूँ किन्तु अपने स्वरूप में सत्य ज्ञानानन्द (सच्चिदानन्द) स्वरूप,
shambhu_gita::738.english_translation: I am not the body, nor the person, nor the Brahmin, nor the Shudra; in my own nature, I am the form of truth, consciousness, and bliss.
shambhu_gita::738.translation_literal: नाहं (I am not) देहो (body) न (nor) पुरुषो (person) न (nor) शूद्रो (Shudra) ब्राह्मणो (Brahmin) न (nor) च (and) । निजस्वरूपे (in own nature) किन्त्वस्मि (but I am) सच्चिदानन्दरूपकः (truth-consciousness-bliss form) ॥
shambhu_gita::738.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::738.essence: Your true self is beyond body and social identity; it is pure truth and joy.
shambhu_gita::738.simple_meaning: You are not your physical body or social identity. Your true nature is pure existence, awareness, and happiness.
shambhu_gita::738.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your essence is beyond all roles and forms.
shambhu_gita::738.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares that he transcends all physical bodies and social classes like Brahmin or Shudra. His true self is the unchanging reality of truth, consciousness, and bliss, not limited by external identities.
shambhu_gita::738.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by labels or roles at work or home, remember your deeper self is free and unbounded.
shambhu_gita::738.insight: This verse invites you to shift from identifying with external roles to recognizing your unchanging inner nature.

shambhu_gita::739.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकाशरूपः सर्वान्तर्यामी सर्वात्मको विभुः ।
अस्म्यहं सर्वथा नूनं चिदाकाशस्वरूपकः ॥
shambhu_gita::739.verse_hindi: प्रकाशरूप, अन्तर्यामी, सर्वात्मा, विभु और चिदाकाशरूप हूँ
shambhu_gita::739.english_translation: I am the form of light, the inner witness, the all-pervading self, the sovereign, and the nature of conscious space.
shambhu_gita::739.translation_literal: प्रकाशरूपः (form of light) सर्वान्तर्यामी (all-inner-witness) सर्वात्मको (all-self) विभुः (sovereign) अस्म्यहं (I am) सर्वथा (completely) नूनं (indeed) चिदाकाशस्वरूपकः (form of conscious space)
shambhu_gita::739.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::739.essence: The true self is infinite light, inner witness, and pervading conscious space.
shambhu_gita::739.simple_meaning: I am the shining presence that fills all, the inner witness, the all-encompassing self, the supreme ruler, and the form of conscious space.
shambhu_gita::739.simple_insight: Recognizing the self as the infinite light and presence beyond all limits brings deep inner awe.
shambhu_gita::739.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares his identity as the luminous essence that pervades everything, the inner observer within all beings, the universal self that governs all, and the conscious space that is the basis of existence. This verse reveals his cosmic nature and supreme presence.
shambhu_gita::739.insight: It shifts understanding from a limited self to recognizing the boundless inner presence as your true identity.

shambhu_gita::740.verse_sanskrit:
निश्चयो दृढ़ एवं योऽपरोक्षज्ञानमस्ति तत् ।
वोद्धव्यमेतत् पितरोऽपरोक्षज्ञानलक्षणम् ॥
shambhu_gita::740.verse_hindi: ऐसा दृढ़ निश्चय होना अपरोक्ष ज्ञान कहा जाता है, हे पितृगण ! इसको अपरोक्ष ज्ञान का लक्षण समझो
shambhu_gita::740.english_translation: A firm resolve is called direct knowledge; ancestors, recognize this as the mark of direct knowledge.
shambhu_gita::740.translation_literal: निश्चय (resolve) दृढ़ (firm) एवं (and) य: (which) अपरोक्षज्ञानमस्ति (is direct knowledge) तत् (that) । वोद्धव्यमेतत् (should be known) पितरोऽपरोक्षज्ञानलक्षणम् (ancestors, mark of direct knowledge) ॥
shambhu_gita::740.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::740.essence: Firm resolve is the defining sign of direct and clear knowledge.
shambhu_gita::740.simple_meaning: Having a strong and unwavering determination is what is called direct knowledge.
shambhu_gita::740.simple_insight: You feel confident and steady when your understanding is clear and firm.
shambhu_gita::740.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, highlighting that true direct knowledge is marked by an unshakable and firm resolve in understanding.
shambhu_gita::740.modern_relevance: When you make a decision with full confidence and clarity, your mind is free from doubt and hesitation.
shambhu_gita::740.insight: It teaches you to recognize direct knowledge by the firmness of your conviction.

shambhu_gita::741.verse_hindi: "मैं ब्रह्म ही हूँ" इस प्रकार के अपरोक्ष ज्ञान से सभी कर्म बन्धनों की निश्चय निवृत्ति हो जाती है
shambhu_gita::741.english_translation: "I am the supreme reality" — this direct knowledge removes all bondage to actions for sure.
shambhu_gita::741.translation_literal: अहं (I) ब्रह्मास्मि (am supreme reality) इत्येव (thus indeed) अपरोक्षज्ञानयोगतः (from direct knowledge yoga) । सर्वकर्माबलीवन्धनिवृत्तिः (all action bondage cessation) जायते (arises) ध्रुवम् (certainly) ॥
shambhu_gita::741.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::741.essence: Direct knowledge of your true self ends all bondage to actions.
shambhu_gita::741.simple_meaning: Realizing deeply that you are the supreme reality ends all bondage caused by actions.
shambhu_gita::741.simple_insight: There is profound freedom in knowing your true nature beyond all actions.
shambhu_gita::741.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva reveals that direct and unwavering knowledge of being the supreme reality dissolves the binding effects of all actions, freeing the seeker from their consequences and the cycle of reactivity.
shambhu_gita::741.modern_relevance: When you understand who you truly are beneath your roles and tasks, the pressure from daily responsibilities loses its grip.
shambhu_gita::741.insight: It shifts your perspective from being controlled by your actions’ results to resting in your true self beyond them.

shambhu_gita::742.verse_sanskrit:
मारब्धं सञ्चितं कल्याः ! आगामीतिप्रभेदतः ।
मोच्यते त्रिविधं कर्म कर्मतत्त्वविशारदैः ॥
shambhu_gita::742.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! सञ्चित, प्रारब्ध और आगामि ये तीन प्रकार के कर्म कर्मतत्वज्ञों ने कहे हैं
shambhu_gita::742.english_translation: O ancestors! The three types of karma—accumulated, originated, and future—are known by those who understand the essence of karma.
shambhu_gita::742.translation_literal: मारब्धं (originated) सञ्चितं (accumulated) कल्याः (auspicious ones, ancestors) ! आगामीतिप्रभेदतः (future, by distinction) । मोच्यते (is known) त्रिविधं (threefold) कर्म (karma) कर्मतत्त्वविशारदैः (by those who understand the essence of karma) ॥
shambhu_gita::742.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::742.essence: Karma is a threefold process: past accumulated, current active, and future arising actions.
shambhu_gita::742.simple_meaning: Karma exists in three forms: what you have done before, what you are doing now, and what you will do in the future.
shambhu_gita::742.simple_insight: Seeing karma as three parts helps you understand how your actions connect across time.
shambhu_gita::742.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that karma is not just one thing but three: the accumulated past actions, the current actions that bear fruit, and the future actions yet to arise. This classification helps frame how karma operates over time.
shambhu_gita::742.modern_relevance: You feel weighed down by past mistakes, caught in current habits, and anxious about choices ahead; knowing karma works in three stages helps you see your life as a continuous flow.
shambhu_gita::742.insight: It shifts your view of karma from a single cause to an ongoing process unfolding in past, present, and future.

shambhu_gita::743.verse_hindi: जिनका भोग उत्पन्न नहीं हुआ है और जो अनन्त कोटि जन्मो में किये हुए कर्मों के संस्कारभूत हैं
shambhu_gita::743.english_translation: For those whose experience has not arisen and who are imprinted with the karmic impressions accumulated over infinite lifetimes.
shambhu_gita::743.translation_literal: अनन्तकोटि (infinite crores) / जन्म (births) / ओघेऽभुक्तानां (whose experience has not arisen) / कृतकर्मणाम् (of performed actions) / नृनं (of humans) / संस्कारभूतं (formed of impressions) / यदीजवत् (like a cause-effect relation) / कारणान्वयि (connected)
shambhu_gita::743.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::743.essence: Unseen karmic impressions from countless past lives shape present experience.
shambhu_gita::743.simple_meaning: You carry impressions from countless past actions, even if you don’t consciously experience their effects now.
shambhu_gita::743.simple_insight: It feels reassuring to know unseen past patterns influence you but don’t fully define your present.
shambhu_gita::743.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how humans carry deep karmic impressions from infinite past lives. Even if those effects aren’t currently felt, they shape present tendencies and patterns.
shambhu_gita::743.modern_relevance: You may feel stuck by habits or reactions you can’t explain—these come from long-hidden past influences.
shambhu_gita::743.insight: It teaches you to recognize that unseen past actions influence your present without defining it.

shambhu_gita::744.verse_sanskrit:
अस्ति पूर्वार्जितं कर्मजातं तत्कर्म सञ्चितम् ।
जनकं स्थूलदेहस्य देहेऽस्मिन्नेव च प्रदम् ॥
shambhu_gita::744.verse_hindi: एवं बीजवत् कारणरूप जो पूर्वार्जित कर्म है वह सञ्चितकर्म कहलाते हैं । स्थूलशरीर के उत्पादक अर्थात् कारण और
shambhu_gita::744.english_translation: The actions you have performed before are stored as accumulated karma in this same body, which is the cause of the gross physical form.
shambhu_gita::744.translation_literal: अस्ति (there is) पूर्वार्जितं (previously earned) कर्मजातं (born of action) तत् (that) कर्म (action) सञ्चितम् (accumulated) । जनकं (cause) स्थूलदेहस्य (of the gross body) देहेऽस्मिन्नेव (in this very body) च (and) प्रदम् (given) ॥
shambhu_gita::744.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::744.essence: Accumulated past actions cause the formation of your present physical body.
shambhu_gita::744.simple_meaning: Your past actions accumulate and shape your current physical body and life circumstances.
shambhu_gita::744.simple_insight: You feel the presence of your past efforts living within you now.
shambhu_gita::744.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the actions previously performed by a person accumulate as karma, which acts like a seed causing the formation of the current physical body. This shows how past deeds influence the present life.
shambhu_gita::744.modern_relevance: After years of habits and choices, you notice how your current health and situation reflect your past decisions.
shambhu_gita::744.insight: Recognize that your present condition is influenced by past actions, encouraging responsibility and awareness.

shambhu_gita::745.verse_sanskrit:
सुखदुःखादिभोगानामास्ते पूर्वार्जितश्च यत् ।
प्रारब्धं पोच्यते कर्म तदेवाहो स्वधाभुजः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::745.verse_hindi: इसी देह में सुखदुःख आदि भोगों को देनेवाले जो पूर्वजन्मार्जित कर्म है वह ही प्रारब्ध कर्म कहलाते हैं
shambhu_gita::745.english_translation: The pleasures and pains experienced in this body are due to past life's earned karma, called the begun karma.
shambhu_gita::745.translation_literal: सुखदुःखादि (pleasures and pains) भोगानाम् (experiences) आस (there are) ते (those) पूर्वार्जित (previously earned) च (and) यत् (which) प्रारब्धं (begun) पोच्यते (is exhausted) कर्म (karma) तदेव (that indeed) अहो (oh) स्वधाभुजः (the body that enjoys)!
shambhu_gita::745.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::745.essence: Present experiences are the unfolding of past earned actions within this body.
shambhu_gita::745.simple_meaning: The joys and sufferings you experience now come from actions you performed in past lives, which are now playing out.
shambhu_gita::745.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing present experiences are the result of past causes beyond your immediate control.
shambhu_gita::745.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to the sages that the happiness and suffering the body feels now come from karma earned in previous lives. This begun karma shapes current experience and must be endured as part of one’s present journey.
shambhu_gita::745.modern_relevance: When you face unexpected struggles or joys, it helps to remember some results stem from past choices beyond today’s control.
shambhu_gita::745.insight: Recognize current life events as effects of prior actions, shifting focus from blame to understanding.

shambhu_gita::746.verse_sanskrit:
जीवदेहकृतं कर्म पापपुण्यात्मकं किल।
आस्ते यन्नूतनं कर्म तदागामि प्रचक्ष्यते ॥
shambhu_gita::746.verse_hindi: जीव के देह से किये हुए जो पापपुण्यात्मक नये कर्म है वह  अगामी कर्म कहे जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::746.english_translation: Actions done by the living body that are new and involve either harm or benefit are called future actions.
shambhu_gita::746.translation_literal: जीवदेहकृतं (by living body done) / कर्म (action) / पापपुण्यात्मकं (harm-benefit characterized) / किल (indeed) / आस्ते (exists) / यन्नूतनं (which is new) / कर्म (action) / तदागामि (that future) / प्रचक्ष्यते (is called)
shambhu_gita::746.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::746.essence: New actions performed now become the causes of future experiences.
shambhu_gita::746.simple_meaning: New actions performed by your living body, whether good or bad, create future consequences.
shambhu_gita::746.simple_insight: You carry the power to shape what comes next by what you do now.
shambhu_gita::746.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that every new action performed by a living being’s body, whether tending toward harm or benefit, is called a future action because its effects have yet to unfold.
shambhu_gita::746.modern_relevance: When you decide how to respond in a tense conversation, your choice creates the next moment's reality.
shambhu_gita::746.insight: It teaches you to recognize that every new action plants a seed for what you will experience later.

shambhu_gita::747.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मैवाऽस्मीसह कल्याः ! निश्चयात्मकताजुपा।
तत्र ज्ञानामिना कर्म सञ्चितं दह्यते ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::747.verse_hindi: इन तीन प्रकार के कर्मों से ज्ञानी के सञ्चितकर्म " ब्रह्म ही मैं हूँ" ऐसे निश्चयात्मक ज्ञान की अग्नि से जल जाते हैं।
shambhu_gita::747.english_translation: The accumulated actions of the wise are surely burned by the fire of the certain knowledge 'I am Brahman'.
shambhu_gita::747.translation_literal: ब्रह्मैवाऽस्मि (I am Brahman alone) / सह (with) / कल्याः (auspicious) / निश्चयात्मकता (certainty) / जुपा (by fire) / तत्र (there) / ज्ञानामिना (by knowledge) / कर्म (actions) / सञ्चितं (accumulated) / दह्यते (is burned) / ध्रुवम् (certainly)
shambhu_gita::747.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::747.essence: Certain knowledge of your true self burns away all accumulated actions.
shambhu_gita::747.simple_meaning: When you firmly know 'I am the supreme reality,' your past actions no longer bind you.
shambhu_gita::747.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self dissolves past burdens.
shambhu_gita::747.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that a wise person's accumulated actions are destroyed by the firm knowledge of their true nature as Brahman, freeing them from karmic effects.
shambhu_gita::747.modern_relevance: You realize that deep self-understanding can free you from past mistakes and regrets weighing you down.
shambhu_gita::747.insight: It shifts your focus from being burdened by past actions to embodying your true nature, freeing your mind.

shambhu_gita::748.verse_sanskrit:
संस्कारात्मकवीजौघ ग्रास्ते सञ्चितकर्मणाम् ।
चित्ताकाशेपु सर्वेषां प्राणिनां निहितो ननु ॥
shambhu_gita::748.verse_hindi: सञ्चितकर्मसमूह के संस्कार रूप बीज सब प्राणियों के चित्ताकाशक जमा रहते हैं,
shambhu_gita::748.english_translation: The seeds of past accumulated actions dwell in the vast sky of the mind of all beings.
shambhu_gita::748.translation_literal: संस्कारात्मकवीजौघ (in the form of impressions seeds) / ग्रास्ते (are contained) / सञ्चितकर्मणाम् (of accumulated actions) । / चित्ताकाशेपु (in the sky of the mind) / सर्वेषां (of all) / प्राणिनां (living beings) / निहितो (placed) / ननु (indeed) ॥
shambhu_gita::748.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::748.essence: The mind holds seeds of all past actions, shaping every being's inner world.
shambhu_gita::748.simple_meaning: All beings carry within their mind the impressions or seeds of their past actions.
shambhu_gita::748.simple_insight: You are shaped by many unseen impressions held deep inside your mind.
shambhu_gita::748.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains how every living being's mind contains the seeds formed by their past accumulated actions, influencing their present inner state and experiences.
shambhu_gita::748.modern_relevance: You notice how old habits or memories unconsciously influence your feelings and choices, like invisible seeds growing inside your mind.
shambhu_gita::748.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your present mental state is influenced by stored past impressions, not just current events.

shambhu_gita::749.verse_sanskrit:
यदा ज्ञानिमहात्मानोऽपरोक्षज्ञानयोगतः।
पञ्चकोशा अहं नैव तेभ्योऽतीतो ह्यसंशयम् ॥
shambhu_gita::749.verse_hindi: जब ज्ञानी महापुरुष अपरोक्ष ज्ञान से यह जान जाते हैं कि मैं पञ्चकोश नहीं है, मैं पञ्चकोशो से अतीत
shambhu_gita::749.english_translation: When wise great beings directly realize through knowledge that the true self is not the five sheaths, they are undoubtedly beyond them.
shambhu_gita::749.translation_literal: यदा (when) ज्ञानिमहात्मनोऽपरोक्षज्ञानयोगतः (wise great beings through direct knowledge) / पञ्चकोशा (five sheaths) / अहं (I) / नैव (not) / तेभ्यः (from them) / अतीतो (beyond) / हि (indeed) / असंशयम् (without doubt)
shambhu_gita::749.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::749.essence: Your true self is beyond the five layers that seem to define you.
shambhu_gita::749.simple_meaning: You are not your body, mind, or senses—the five layers that seem to cover you. The true self is beyond all of them.
shambhu_gita::749.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true self is beyond your physical and mental layers.
shambhu_gita::749.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that enlightened beings realize through direct knowledge that the true self is not the five coverings (body, breath, mind, intellect, and bliss). This realization places them firmly beyond all these layers, free from confusion.
shambhu_gita::749.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by your thoughts, feelings, and physical worries—this verse reminds you that your true self isn't limited by those layers.
shambhu_gita::749.insight: It teaches you to look past your identity with body and mind, recognizing the deeper self beyond appearances.

shambhu_gita::750.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मा तद्रष्टरूपोऽस्मि शुद्धो बुद्धश्च शाश्वतः ।
इत्थमेव विदन्तीह पञ्चकोशस्थितेषु वै ॥
shambhu_gita::750.verse_hindi: और उनमें द्रष्टा शुद्ध बुद्ध और सनातन आत्मा हूँ तब पञ्चकोश मे स्थित
shambhu_gita::750.english_translation: I am the pure seer, the eternal discerning mind, and the true self residing in the five sheaths.
shambhu_gita::750.translation_literal: आत्मा (true self) / तद्-रष्टरूपः (that-seer-form) / अस्मि (am) / शुद्धः (pure) / बुद्धः (discerning mind) / च (and) / शाश्वतः (eternal) / इति (thus) / इव (like) / विदन्ति (know) / एषु (in these) / पञ्च-कोश-स्थितेषु (situated in the five sheaths) / वै (indeed)
shambhu_gita::750.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::750.essence: Your true self is the pure, eternal seer residing within all layers of experience.
shambhu_gita::750.simple_meaning: You are the pure observer, the eternal discerning mind, and the true self residing within all five layers of your being.
shambhu_gita::750.simple_insight: You carry a calm, unchanging presence inside despite all outer changes.
shambhu_gita::750.detailed_meaning: Shiva reveals to seekers that their true self is not the restless mind or body but the pure, eternal observer dwelling within the five sheaths of existence that veil the true self.
shambhu_gita::750.modern_relevance: When your emotions and thoughts swirl uncontrollably, remember the quiet, pure presence watching it all from inside you.
shambhu_gita::750.insight: This verse shifts how you view yourself—from being your restless thoughts to recognizing your unchanging inner witness.

shambhu_gita::751.verse_sanskrit:
सञ्चिताः कर्मसंस्काराश्चित्ताकाशेषु संस्थिताः।
तिष्ठन्तोऽपि हि तेष्वेव न मुक्तान् बहुमीशते ॥
shambhu_gita::751.verse_hindi: चित्ताकाश में रहने वाले सञ्चित कर्म संस्कार भी पञ्चकोश में ही रह जाते हैं और उन मुक्त आत्माओं को बाँध नहीं कर सकते
shambhu_gita::751.english_translation: Accumulated impressions of past actions reside in the mind's space but cannot bind those who are truly free.
shambhu_gita::751.translation_literal: सञ्चिताः (accumulated) कर्मसंस्काराः (action impressions) चित्ताकाशेषु (in the mind's space) संस्थिताः (reside)। तिष्ठन्तः (remaining) अपि (even) हि (indeed) तेषु (in those) एव (alone) न (not) मुक्तान् (free ones) बहु-ईशते (bind).
shambhu_gita::751.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::751.essence: Accumulated mental impressions cannot bind the truly free self.
shambhu_gita::751.simple_meaning: Impressions from all past actions stay in the mind but cannot bind those who are truly free.
shambhu_gita::751.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your true self remains free despite old mental patterns.
shambhu_gita::751.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that although all past action impressions accumulate in the mind's vast space, they do not have power over those who have attained true freedom beyond the mind.
shambhu_gita::751.modern_relevance: You notice old habits or memories lingering but realize they no longer control your choices or freedom.
shambhu_gita::751.insight: Recognize that accumulated mental patterns do not limit your inner freedom once you see beyond them.

shambhu_gita::752.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानिनामिह मुक्तानां प्राणिनां पितृपुङ्गवाः !।
पारब्धकर्मणां नाशो भोगादेव प्रजायते ॥
shambhu_gita::752.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी मुक्त पुरुषों के प्रारब्ध कर्मों का क्षय भोग से ही होता है
shambhu_gita::752.english_translation: For the liberated wise ones, the exhaustion of past deeds happens only through experience.
