shambhu_gita::803.verse_sanskrit:
देशकालात्मकाः कर्मरूपा अपि विभूतयः।
सन्ति मे प्रकृतेर्मुख्यास्तिस्रस्ताभ्योऽपि मामकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::803.verse_hindi: काल देश और कर्मरूपी जो मेरी प्रकृति की तीन प्रधान विभूतियां हैं उनसे भी मेरे
shambhu_gita::803.english_translation: Among my nature's three principal powers are time, place, and action.
shambhu_gita::803.translation_literal: देशकालात्मकाः (time-and-place-related) / कर्मरूपा (action-shaped) / अपि (also) / विभूतयः (powers) / सन्ति (are) / मे (my) / प्रकृतेः (of nature) / मुख्याः (principal) / तिस्रः (three) / ताभ्यः (from these) / अपि (also) / मामकाः (mine)
shambhu_gita::803.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::803.essence: Time, place, and action are the three main powers shaping all existence.
shambhu_gita::803.simple_meaning: Your nature is influenced by three main powers: time, place, and the actions you perform.
shambhu_gita::803.simple_insight: Understanding your life’s flow comes from seeing how time, place, and action shape you.
shambhu_gita::803.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that within his nature, three fundamental forces govern existence: time, place, and actions. These shape the world and beings, including the divine presence within all things.
shambhu_gita::803.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or changed, it’s often the moment, the environment, and your choices shaping you more than you realize.
shambhu_gita::803.insight: Recognize how your context and behavior form your experience; this helps you navigate change with clarity.

shambhu_gita::804.verse_sanskrit:
भक्ता भवन्त्यतीता हि जीवन्मुक्ता न संशयः।
भूयोऽहं व्यासतो वक्ष्ये सावधाननिशम्यताम् ॥
shambhu_gita::804.verse_hindi: जीवन्मुक्त भक्त अतीत हो जाते हैं इनको मैं और विस्तारपूर्वक कहता हूं सुनो
shambhu_gita::804.english_translation: Devotees who have attained inner freedom have gone beyond all doubts. I will explain this further; listen carefully.
shambhu_gita::804.translation_literal: भक्ता (devotees) भवन्ति (become) अतिता (beyond) हि (indeed) जीवन्मुक्ता (liberated beings) न (not) संशयः (doubt). भूयः (again) अहं (I) व्यासतः (in detail) वक्ष्ये (will explain) सावधाननिशम्यताम् (listen attentively).
shambhu_gita::804.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::804.essence: Devotion leads beyond all doubt to a state of inner freedom.
shambhu_gita::804.simple_meaning: Devotees who have reached true inner freedom no longer have doubts. This teaching will be explained more fully.
shambhu_gita::804.simple_insight: You can find a confident peace through devoted inner freedom.
shambhu_gita::804.detailed_meaning: Shiva tells that those devoted beings who have achieved liberation from the cycle of reaction are beyond all doubts. He prepares to explain this profound state more deeply to the listener.
shambhu_gita::804.modern_relevance: When your trust in your path deepens, your worries and doubts begin to fade, bringing a calm certainty.
shambhu_gita::804.insight: It teaches you to recognize that steady devotion can dissolve uncertainty and bring lasting inner freedom.

shambhu_gita::805.verse_sanskrit:
महाकालश्च कालश्च पिता चैव स्वधाभुजः !।
सगुणस्य स्वरूपस्य सन्तीमा मे विभूतयः ॥
shambhu_gita::805.verse_hindi: हे जिज्ञास्तु पितृगण ! महाकाल, काल और पिता ये मेरी सगुणरूप की विभूतियां हैं
shambhu_gita::805.english_translation: O seekers among the ancestors, Mahakala, Kala, and the father are my manifestations with qualities.
shambhu_gita::805.translation_literal: महाकालश्च (Mahakala and) कालश्च (Kala and) पिता (father) चैव (also) स्वधाभुजः (among the ancestors) ! / सगुणस्य (of the one with qualities) स्वरूपस्य (form) सन्तीमा (manifestations) मे (my) विभूतयः (powers) ॥
shambhu_gita::805.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::805.essence: Cosmic time and ancestral figures are expressions of the divine's manifested qualities.
shambhu_gita::805.simple_meaning: Mahakala, Kala, and the father among ancestors are forms of my manifested qualities.
shambhu_gita::805.simple_insight: The divine appears in many forms connected to time and ancestry.
shambhu_gita::805.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains to seekers among ancestors that Mahakala (great time), Kala (time), and the father as ancestral figures are manifestations of his qualified form, linking cosmic time and lineage as expressions of his power.
shambhu_gita::805.insight: It reveals how divine qualities manifest through cosmic time and ancestral forms, connecting eternity with lineage.

shambhu_gita::806.verse_sanskrit:
देशश्च जन्मभूमिश्च माता चैव बुभुत्सवः !।
मुख्या मत्मकृतेनूर्नमिमाः सन्ति विभूतयः ॥
shambhu_gita::806.verse_hindi: और देश, जन्मभूमि एवं माता यह  मेरी प्रकृति की प्रधान विभूतियां हैं ।
shambhu_gita::806.english_translation: The land, birthplace, and mother are the principal manifestations of my nature.
shambhu_gita::806.translation_literal: देशश्च (land too) जन्मभूमिश्च (birthplace also) माता (mother) चैव (and indeed) बुभुत्सवः (manifestations) । मुख्या (principal) मत्मकृतेनूर्नमिमाः (by my nature) सन्ति (are) विभूतयः (manifestations) ॥
shambhu_gita::806.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::806.essence: Your homeland and mother reveal the divine nature through their presence.
shambhu_gita::806.simple_meaning: Land, birthplace, and mother are the main expressions of the divine nature described here.
shambhu_gita::806.simple_insight: Everything familiar and close to you reflects a part of the divine nature.
shambhu_gita::806.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that fundamental elements of life like the land you live on, your birthplace, and your mother represent key expressions of his cosmic nature, grounding the divine in the everyday world.
shambhu_gita::806.modern_relevance: The place you come from and your family shape your sense of self and connection to the world around you.
shambhu_gita::806.insight: It invites you to see the sacred in your roots and surroundings, recognizing them as expressions of a larger reality.

shambhu_gita::807.verse_hindi: निज अन्तःकरण में ही विविध आकाशरूप से सर्वव्यापक देश का अनुभव होता है
shambhu_gita::807.english_translation: Within your own inner being, you directly experience the all-pervading space in its threefold forms.
shambhu_gita::807.translation_literal: निज (own) / अन्तःकरणे (inner being) / एव (indeed) / त्रिविध (threefold) / आकाशरूपतः (in the form of space) / सर्वव्यापक (all-pervading) / देशः (region) / अयम् (this) / अनुभूयत (is experienced) / एव (only)
shambhu_gita::807.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::807.essence: The infinite, all-encompassing space is directly experienced within your own inner being.
shambhu_gita::807.simple_meaning: Inside your own inner being, you experience the vast, all-encompassing space in three forms.
shambhu_gita::807.simple_insight: You are intimately connected to the infinite space that fills everything.
shambhu_gita::807.detailed_meaning: Shiva reveals that within the inner being exists the experience of the vast all-pervading space in its threefold aspects, inviting a profound realization of the infinite residing within oneself.
shambhu_gita::807.modern_relevance: When you pause and feel deeply inside, you recognize the vast openness and freedom present within you beyond the daily noise.
shambhu_gita::807.insight: It shifts your focus inward to discover that the infinite and boundless qualities you seek are already within you.

shambhu_gita::808.verse_sanskrit:
अतोऽपि स्वशरीराणि मन्यन्ते प्राणिनां कृते ।
योगिनः प्रकृतेर्मुख्यविभूत्यात्मकतः स्वतः ॥
shambhu_gita::808.verse_hindi: इस कारण निज शरीर भी जीव के लिये मेरी प्रकृति की प्रधान विभूतिरूप से योगिगण मानते हैं।
shambhu_gita::808.english_translation: Therefore, yogis naturally regard their own bodies as the primary manifestation of nature for living beings.
shambhu_gita::808.translation_literal: अतोऽपि (therefore also) स्वशरीराणि (own bodies) मन्यन्ते (are regarded) प्राणिनां (of living beings) कृते (for) । योगिनः (yogis) प्रकृतेर्मुख्यविभूति-आत्मतः (by nature as principal manifestation) स्वतः (naturally) ॥
shambhu_gita::808.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::808.essence: Your body is nature’s principal form naturally recognized by those who seek wisdom.
shambhu_gita::808.simple_meaning: Those who practice yoga naturally recognize their own body as the main form of nature for living beings.
shambhu_gita::808.simple_insight: You can feel connected knowing your body is a natural expression of life’s power.
shambhu_gita::808.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that yogis perceive their bodies not as separate but as the foremost visible form of nature itself that sustains all life, highlighting the unity between self and nature.
shambhu_gita::808.modern_relevance: When you feel disconnected from your body during stress, remember it naturally embodies the vital force of life itself.
shambhu_gita::808.insight: It shifts attention to seeing your body as a natural, primary expression of the living world rather than a separate object.

shambhu_gita::809.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः स्पन्दनं यत्स्यात्सम्बन्धाद्देशकालयोः।
कर्म तत् च्यते विज्ञैर्विसर्गात्मकमेव तत् ॥
shambhu_gita::809.verse_hindi: देश और काल के सम्बन्ध से मेरी प्रकृति के स्पन्दन को कर्म कहते है,
shambhu_gita::809.english_translation: The movement of my nature related to place and time is called action by the wise; it is merely a form of release.
shambhu_gita::809.translation_literal: प्रकृतेः (of nature) स्पन्दनं (movement) यत् (that which) स्यात् (exists) सम्बन्धात् (from relation) देशकालयोः (of place and time) । कर्म (action) तत् (that) च्यते (is called) विज्ञैः (by the wise) विसर्गात्मकम् (of the nature of release) एव (indeed) तत् (that) ॥
shambhu_gita::809.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::809.essence: Action is the natural movement of changing nature in relation to time and place.
shambhu_gita::809.simple_meaning: Action is the natural movement of the world connected to time and place, seen by the wise as a release.
shambhu_gita::809.simple_insight: You can see your actions as part of a natural flow, not separate or personal.
shambhu_gita::809.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that what we call actions are just movements of the natural world shaped by time and place. The wise understand these as expressions of the natural release of energy, not as something inherently personal or separate.
shambhu_gita::809.modern_relevance: When you rush to judge your choices as success or failure, remember they are just natural movements shaped by circumstances beyond you.
shambhu_gita::809.insight: It shifts your view from seeing action as personal effort to seeing it as the unfolding of natural forces.

shambhu_gita::810.verse_sanskrit:
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गो विद्यते किल ।
त्रिविधं कथ्यते कर्म सहजादिप्रभेदतः ॥
shambhu_gita::810.verse_hindi: वह भूतभावोद्भव कर विसर्गरूप है । वह कर्म सहजादि रूप से त्रिविध कहाता है ।
shambhu_gita::810.english_translation: The divine is the cause from which all beings arise and dissolve; action is described in three kinds by its nature and origin.
shambhu_gita::810.translation_literal: भूतभावोद्भवकरो (cause of beings' origin) / विसर्गो (dissolution) / विद्यते (exists) / किल (indeed) / त्रिविधं (threefold) / कथ्यते (is described) / कर्म (action) / सहजादि (by nature and origin) / प्रभेदतः (in distinctions)
shambhu_gita::810.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::810.essence: All existence flows from one source; actions naturally divide into three types.
shambhu_gita::810.simple_meaning: Everything that exists comes from one origin and returns there; actions naturally appear in three types.
shambhu_gita::810.simple_insight: You are part of a vast flow where actions have natural, distinct forms.
shambhu_gita::810.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that all beings arise from and return to a single source. He introduces the idea that actions are naturally divided into three types by their origin, setting the foundation for understanding duty and effort.
shambhu_gita::810.modern_relevance: You can feel overwhelmed by choices, but recognizing actions fall into clear types helps you find your place in the flow.
shambhu_gita::810.insight: This verse shifts your view to see your actions as natural expressions arising from a shared origin.

shambhu_gita::811.verse_sanskrit:
अपि तेपामनेकांश्च भेदान कर्मविदो विदुः ।
यदा मे ज्ञानिनो भक्ता जीवन्मुक्तिपदं ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::811.verse_hindi: कर्मतत्वदर्शियों ने उन तीनों के भी अनेक भेद कहे हैं। मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त जब जीवन्मुक्त पदवी को
shambhu_gita::811.english_translation: Even the experts in action describe many distinctions among the three paths. But my wise devotees firmly attain the state of living liberation.
shambhu_gita::811.translation_literal: अपि (even) तेपामनेकांश्च (of the three paths many) भेदान (differences) कर्मविदो (experts in action) विदुः (know) । यदा (when) मे (my) ज्ञानिनो (wise ones) भक्ता (devotees) जीवन्मुक्तिपदं (state of living liberation) ध्रुवम् (certain/firm) ॥
shambhu_gita::811.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::811.essence: Wise devotion transcends distinctions and guarantees living liberation.
shambhu_gita::811.simple_meaning: Different experts describe many distinctions in the three paths, but wise devotees firmly achieve living liberation.
shambhu_gita::811.simple_insight: Knowing your devotion leads you safely beyond confusion brings calm and confidence.
shambhu_gita::811.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that although scholars of action distinguish many subtle differences among the three spiritual paths, his wise devotees who love him achieve steady living liberation.
shambhu_gita::811.modern_relevance: You might hear many opinions about how to grow or find freedom, but your sincere devotion can guide you steadily beyond confusion.
shambhu_gita::811.insight: It shifts focus from debating paths to trusting devotion as the sure way to freedom.

shambhu_gita::812.verse_sanskrit:
प्राप्नुवन्ति तदा देश-कालकर्म्माणि तानहो ।
किञ्चिन्नैवापवाधन्ते सत्यं सत्यं ब्रवीमि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::812.verse_hindi: प्राप्त कर लेते हैं तो देश, काल और कर्म उनको कुछ भी बाधा नहीं दे सकते
shambhu_gita::812.english_translation: Once you attain that, place, time, and actions no longer obstruct you; truly, I tell you this.
shambhu_gita::812.translation_literal: प्राप्नुवन्ति (attain) तदा (then) देश-कालकर्म्माणि (place-time-actions) तानहो (not harm) । किञ्चिन्नैवापवाधन्ते (nothing at all obstructs) सत्यं (truth) सत्यं (truth) ब्रवीमि (I speak) वः (to you) ॥
shambhu_gita::812.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::812.essence: True attainment frees you from all external limitations of time, place, and actions.
shambhu_gita::812.simple_meaning: When you truly reach a certain state, external factors like place, time, or past actions cannot stop you.
shambhu_gita::812.simple_insight: You feel a deep freedom, knowing nothing outside can block your inner progress.
shambhu_gita::812.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to Arjuna about a state of realization where usual obstacles—time, place, and past deeds—lose their power to hinder true progress or freedom.
shambhu_gita::812.modern_relevance: You feel stuck by your circumstances, deadlines, or past mistakes, but this shows you can still move beyond those limits.
shambhu_gita::812.insight: It teaches you to see beyond external conditions and realize your progress is not confined by them.

shambhu_gita::813.verse_sanskrit:
गुणत्रयस्य सम्बन्धादेषां भेदांश्र वर्णये ।
श्रूयन्तां सावधानैस्ते भवद्भिश्च शनैः शनैः ॥
shambhu_gita::813.verse_hindi: त्रिगुण के सम्बन्ध से इनका भेद वर्णन करता हूँ, सुनें ।
shambhu_gita::813.english_translation: I describe the distinctions among the three qualities slowly and attentively; please listen carefully.
shambhu_gita::813.translation_literal: गुणत्रयस्य (of the three qualities) सम्बन्धात् (from the relation) एषां (of these) भेदांश्र (distinctions) वर्णये (I describe) । श्रूयन्तां (let them hear) सावधानैः (with attentiveness) ते (you all) भवद्भि: (by you) च (and) शनैः शनैः (slowly slowly) ॥
shambhu_gita::813.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::813.essence: Clear understanding requires careful, slow explanation of subtle distinctions.
shambhu_gita::813.simple_meaning: I will explain the differences between the three qualities carefully and slowly for you to understand.
shambhu_gita::813.simple_insight: Teaching needs patience and care to reveal subtle distinctions clearly.
shambhu_gita::813.detailed_meaning: Shiva announces that he will carefully explain the distinctions among the three fundamental qualities (gunas). This sets the stage for deeper teaching about nature and behavior.
shambhu_gita::813.modern_relevance: When learning complex ideas, taking time and attention reveals their true meaning clearly.
shambhu_gita::813.insight: It teaches you to approach complex knowledge patiently and attentively for clear understanding.

shambhu_gita::814.verse_sanskrit:
विभ्वनिर्वचनीयौ द्वावतिसूक्ष्मौ गुणान्वयात् ।
शक्यौ देशमहाकालौ विज्ञातुं नैव कहिर्चित ॥
shambhu_gita::814.verse_hindi: सूक्ष्माति सूक्ष्म, विभु और अनिर्वचनीय देश और महाकाल गुण के सम्बन्ध से जाने नहीं जाते
shambhu_gita::814.english_translation: The vast and the indescribable are too subtle and fine to be truly known through qualities or time.
shambhu_gita::814.translation_literal: विभ्व (vast) / अनिर्वचनीयौ (indescribable) / द्वावतिसूक्ष्मौ (exceedingly subtle) / गुणान्वयात् (by qualities) / शक्यौ (possible) / देशमहाकालौ (space and great time) / विज्ञातुं (to know) / नैव (not) / कहिःचित् (anyone)
shambhu_gita::814.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::814.essence: The vast and indescribable cannot be captured by qualities or time.
shambhu_gita::814.simple_meaning: The infinite and indescribable cannot be understood by typical qualities or by measuring time or space.
shambhu_gita::814.simple_insight: You feel the mystery beyond all familiar ways of knowing and measuring.
shambhu_gita::814.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that the supreme reality is so subtle and vast that it cannot be grasped by observing qualities or through concepts of space and time. This moment points to the limits of ordinary knowing.
shambhu_gita::814.modern_relevance: You try to fully understand something immense, but it slips beyond all labels and measures.
shambhu_gita::814.insight: It teaches you to accept that some realities are beyond conceptual grasp and measurement.

shambhu_gita::815.verse_sanskrit:
किन्तु तौ भावसम्बन्धाज्ज्ञातुं शक्यौ न संशयः ।
जीवन्मुक्ता महात्मानः शक्तितो देशकालयोः ॥
shambhu_gita::815.verse_hindi: परन्तु वह भाव के सम्बन्ध से जाने जाते हैं। जीवन्मुक महापुरुष ब्रह्मभाव की धारणा  द्वारा देश और काल की शक्ति से
shambhu_gita::815.english_translation: However, they are known by their connection to feelings; the liberated great beings realize the supreme nature beyond the power of place and time.
shambhu_gita::815.translation_literal: किन्तु (however) तौ (they two) भावसम्बन्धात् (from connection to feeling) ज्ञातुम् (to know) शक्यौ (possible) न (not) संशयः (doubt) । जीवन्मुक्ताः (liberated beings) महात्मानः (great souls) शक्तितः (by power) देशकालयोः (of place and time) ॥
shambhu_gita::815.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::815.essence: True freedom is known through feeling its connection beyond time and place.
shambhu_gita::815.simple_meaning: Great liberated beings are recognized by their connection to deep feelings and the supreme nature beyond all limits of place and time.
shambhu_gita::815.simple_insight: You are more than your surroundings; your true nature connects beyond them.
shambhu_gita::815.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Shiva explains that while some things are known by direct connection to feelings, the great liberated ones perceive the supreme reality untouched by the constraints of place and time.
shambhu_gita::815.modern_relevance: You might feel defined by your environment or schedule, but your true self connects beyond any circumstance or moment.
shambhu_gita::815.insight: It teaches you to see your identity beyond external conditions, recognizing your timeless inner nature.

shambhu_gita::816.verse_sanskrit:
स्वयं धारणयाऽऽत्मानं ब्रह्मभावस्य शुद्धया।
विमोक्तुं शक्नुवन्तीह नात्रास्ते कोऽपि विस्मयः ॥
shambhu_gita::816.verse_hindi: अपने आप को मुक्त कर लेते है इसमें विस्मय नहीं है।
shambhu_gita::816.english_translation: Those who uphold themselves in the pure state of supreme reality can free themselves here; there is no wonder in this.
shambhu_gita::816.translation_literal: स्वयं (oneself) / धारणयाऽऽत्मानं (uphold) / ब्रह्मभावस्य (of the supreme reality) / शुद्धया (pure) / विमोक्तुं (to free) / शक्नुवन्तीह (are able here) / नात्रास्ते (there is not) / कोऽपि (anyone) / विस्मयः (wonder)
shambhu_gita::816.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::816.essence: Steady connection to your pure true self naturally leads to your freedom here and now.
shambhu_gita::816.simple_meaning: When you firmly hold yourself in the pure state of your highest reality, you can free yourself; it is natural and unsurprising.
shambhu_gita::816.simple_insight: There is calm certainty in knowing freedom arises from steady connection to your true nature.
shambhu_gita::816.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that by maintaining unwavering awareness of your pure, supreme nature, you can liberate yourself here and now—this is no mystery but a natural truth.
shambhu_gita::816.modern_relevance: When you stay grounded in your core true self, even amid chaos, freedom from overwhelm naturally arises without surprise.
shambhu_gita::816.insight: It shifts your focus to sustaining pure self-awareness as the key to liberation rather than seeking external change.

shambhu_gita::817.verse_sanskrit:
यदा मे प्रकृतेधीराः ! त्रैगुण्योपाधिसंयुतः।
कल्पमन्वन्तरादीनि नानारूपाणि सन्धरन् ॥
shambhu_gita::817.verse_hindi: महाकाल जब मेरी प्रकृति के त्रिगुण-उपाधि से युक्त होकर कल्प मन्वन्तर आदि अनेक रूपों को धारण करके
shambhu_gita::817.english_translation: When the great time, bound by the three qualities of my nature, takes on many forms through cycles of creation and dissolution.
shambhu_gita::817.translation_literal: यदा (when) / मे (my) / प्रकृति (nature) / धीरा: (bound) / त्रैगुण्य (three qualities) / उपाधि (limiting factors) / संयुतः (joined) / कल्प (aeon) / अन्वन्तरादीनि (cycles and periods) / नानारूपाणि (various forms) / सन्धरन् (assuming)
shambhu_gita::817.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::817.essence: Nature's three qualities shape endless forms through cosmic cycles of time.
shambhu_gita::817.simple_meaning: The great time, connected with the three qualities of nature, takes on many forms through cycles of cosmic creation and destruction.
shambhu_gita::817.simple_insight: Change and many forms arise naturally from the qualities of nature over time.
shambhu_gita::817.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes how the great cosmic time, influenced by the three fundamental qualities (gunas) of nature, manifests in countless forms through vast cycles of creation and dissolution known as kalpas and manvantaras.
shambhu_gita::817.insight: Recognize that the changing world and its many forms arise from underlying natural qualities acting over time.

shambhu_gita::818.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्युगमैहाकाल ऋतुभिः षडभिरेव च ।
प्रत्यक्षत्वं गतो लोके जीववर्गेषु सन्ततम् ॥
shambhu_gita::818.verse_hindi: अन्त में चार युग और छः ऋतुरूप से प्रत्यक्ष होकर जीव पर
shambhu_gita::818.english_translation: In the end, the four ages and six seasons manifest continuously in the cycle of living beings.
shambhu_gita::818.translation_literal: चतुर्युगमै (four ages) / अहाकाल (end time) / ऋतुभिः (by seasons) / षडभिरेव (six indeed) / च (and) / प्रत्यक्षत्वं (manifestation) / गतो (gone) / लोके (in the world) / जीववर्गेषु (among living beings) / सन्ततम् (continually)
shambhu_gita::818.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::818.essence: Life continuously unfolds through repeating cycles of ages and seasons.
shambhu_gita::818.simple_meaning: The four ages and six seasons appear continuously in the world among living beings.
shambhu_gita::818.simple_insight: Time flows unceasingly through all life, shaping every moment.
shambhu_gita::818.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how time unfolds as the four great ages and six seasons, continuously manifesting among living beings, showing the unending flow of natural cycles affecting all life.
shambhu_gita::818.insight: Recognize that life unfolds within constant cycles of change beyond any one individual.

shambhu_gita::819.verse_sanskrit:
प्रभावं तनुते स्वीयं जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनाम् ।
अत्येति निर्मला बुद्धिस्तथाप्युक्तप्रभावतः ॥
shambhu_gita::819.verse_hindi: प्रभाव डालता है किन्तु तब भी जीवन्मुक्त महात्माओं की निर्मल बुद्धि उक्त प्रभावों से भी अतीत हो जाती है।
shambhu_gita::819.english_translation: The influence affects, yet the pure wisdom of the liberated great souls surpasses even such influences.
shambhu_gita::819.translation_literal: प्रभावं (influence) तनुते (affects) स्वीयं (their own) जीवन्मुक्त (liberated) महात्मनाम् (great souls) । अत्येति (surpasses) निर्मला (pure) बुद्धि (wisdom) तथापि (yet) उक्त (spoken) प्रभावतः (influences) ॥
shambhu_gita::819.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::819.essence: Pure wisdom transcends all external influences without being disturbed.
shambhu_gita::819.simple_meaning: Influences may reach you, but pure wisdom in liberated beings goes beyond them.
shambhu_gita::819.simple_insight: You can feel steady and clear even when external forces try to sway you.
shambhu_gita::819.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even though external influences impact beings, those who have attained liberation and pure wisdom transcend these effects, remaining unaffected in their inner clarity.
shambhu_gita::819.modern_relevance: When criticism or pressure tries to cloud your judgment, your clear understanding can still hold steady and true.
shambhu_gita::819.insight: It teaches you to recognize that true clarity in your mind is untouched by external pressures or influences.

shambhu_gita::820.verse_sanskrit:
तथैव प्रकृतेनूनं गुणान् देशो यदा धरन् ।
राशिनक्षत्रसूर्यादिग्रहोपग्रहमुख्यकान् ॥
shambhu_gita::820.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार जब देश प्रकृति गुणो को धारण करके राशि, नक्षत्र, सूर्य, ग्रह और उपग्रह आदि
shambhu_gita::820.english_translation: Similarly, nature takes on qualities according to the region, supporting constellations, sun, planets, and satellites.
shambhu_gita::820.translation_literal: तथैव (similarly) प्रकृतेनूनं (by nature indeed) गुणान् (qualities) देशो (region) यदा (when) धरन् (holding) । राशि (constellation) नक्षत्र (star) सूर्यादि (sun and so on) ग्रह (planets) उपग्रह (satellites) मुख्यकान् (primary)
shambhu_gita::820.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::820.essence: Nature’s qualities change based on cosmic and regional influences.
shambhu_gita::820.simple_meaning: Nature adopts qualities depending on the region and the influence of celestial bodies like stars and planets.
shambhu_gita::820.simple_insight: The world reflects diverse qualities shaped by cosmic influences beyond our control.
shambhu_gita::820.detailed_meaning: The verse describes how nature takes on various qualities based on the influence of regions and celestial bodies such as constellations, the sun, and planets, illustrating the interconnectedness of cosmic forces and natural phenomena.
shambhu_gita::820.insight: It shifts your view to see nature and environment as shaped by larger cosmic patterns rather than isolated factors.

shambhu_gita::821.verse_hindi: अनेक रूपों को धारण करता हुआ,अन्त में मातृभूमि रूप से पार्वत्य, पर्वतप्राय, मरु, ऊषर,
shambhu_gita::821.english_translation: Taking on many forms, finally assuming the form of the motherland—like Parvati, a mountain, desert, and wilderness.
shambhu_gita::821.translation_literal: नानारूपोच्चयान् (various forms taking up) / धृत्वा (holding) / मातृभूरूपतस्ततः (then motherland form) / पार्वत्यपर्वतप्राय्त्मरुदेशोपरादिभिः (like Parvati, like a mountain, desert, wilderness, and so on)
shambhu_gita::821.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::821.essence: The divine manifests in many forms, ultimately as the sacred motherland itself.
shambhu_gita::821.simple_meaning: The divine takes many forms and finally appears as the motherland, including forms like Parvati, mountains, deserts, and wilderness.
shambhu_gita::821.simple_insight: The divine's presence is everywhere, from sacred beings to the land itself.
shambhu_gita::821.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes how the divine manifests in countless forms, ultimately embodying the motherland itself, symbolized by Parvati and various natural landscapes like mountains and deserts, showing omnipresence.
shambhu_gita::821.insight: Recognize the divine in diverse forms around you, including the natural world and homeland.

shambhu_gita::822.verse_hindi: सजल और जलज छः रूप से अथवा ब्राह्मणादि चतुर्वर्णरूपी भूमि भेद से
shambhu_gita::822.english_translation: The earth is described by six forms—water-born and water-containing—or divided by the four varnas starting with Brahmins.
shambhu_gita::822.translation_literal: सजलैजलजैश्च (water-born and water-containing) / अपि (also) / षड़ेृपैर् (by six forms) / उक्तनामकैः (by names said) / ब्राह्मणादि (starting with Brahmin) / चतुर्वर्णरूप (four varna-formed) / भूभेदतः (by earth division) / अथवा (or)
shambhu_gita::822.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::822.essence: The earth can be described in multiple ways reflecting different viewpoints.
shambhu_gita::822.simple_meaning: The earth is described in different ways—by six water-related forms or by its division into four varnas starting with Brahmins.
shambhu_gita::822.simple_insight: Descriptions can reflect different perspectives without one being the absolute truth.
shambhu_gita::822.detailed_meaning: Suta describes the earth with varied classifications: six water-related forms or division by social classes starting with Brahmins, showing diverse ways to see the same reality.
shambhu_gita::822.insight: It teaches that reality can be categorized differently depending on perspective or context.

shambhu_gita::823.verse_hindi: जीव को आसक्ति में बांधता है, वैसा होने पर भी जीवन्मुक्त महात्मा की अव्यभिचारिणी बुद्धि
shambhu_gita::823.english_translation: Attachment binds the living being, yet the liberated soul here has an unwavering intellect.
shambhu_gita::823.translation_literal: जीव (living being) आसक्ति (attachment) में (in) बंधता (binds) है (is), वैसा (such) होने (being) पर (even) भी (also) जीवन्मुक्त (liberated soul) महात्मा (great soul) की (of) अव्यभिचारिणी (unwavering) बुद्धि (intellect).
shambhu_gita::823.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::823.essence: Attachment binds most, but the liberated mind remains steady and unwavering.
shambhu_gita::823.simple_meaning: Attachment ties ordinary beings, but a liberated person’s mind stays steady and never wavers.
shambhu_gita::823.simple_insight: You can feel steady and calm inside, even when outside forces try to hold you back.
shambhu_gita::823.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that while ordinary people are caught by attachments that bind them, a liberated soul (a great being free from illusion) maintains a steady, unwavering intellect. This teaching distinguishes the mind of the truly free from the bound.
shambhu_gita::823.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by desires pulling you every way, yet deep inside, your mind can remain calm and steady, untouched by that chaos.
shambhu_gita::823.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your true mind can stay stable despite external attachments pulling you.

shambhu_gita::824.verse_sanskrit:
नैवापतति कुत्रापि मुदृढ़े तस्य बन्धने । 
जीवन्मुक्तस्थितियस्मात्पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसि ॥
shambhu_gita::824.verse_hindi: उसके सुदृढ़ बन्धन में नहीं पड़ती है क्योंकि जीवन्मुक्तों की स्थिति जल में कमलपत्र के समान होती है
shambhu_gita::824.english_translation: The liberated being does not fall into any strong bondage because their state of freedom is like a lotus leaf on water.
shambhu_gita::824.translation_literal: नैवापतति (does not fall) कुत्रापि (anywhere) मुदृढ़े (firm/strong) तस्य (of that) बन्धने (bondage) । जीवन्मुक्तस्थितियस्मात् (from the state of the liberated being) पद्मपत्रमिव (like a lotus leaf) आम्भसि (on water) ॥
shambhu_gita::824.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::824.essence: True freedom leaves you untouched by any strong bond, like a lotus leaf on water.
shambhu_gita::824.simple_meaning: When you reach true freedom, no strong bond can hold you, just like a lotus leaf stays dry on water.
shambhu_gita::824.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you cannot be caught or weighed down by life’s bindings anymore.
shambhu_gita::824.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that a being who has attained freedom stands beyond all strong attachments or bindings. Like a lotus leaf that rests on water without sinking or getting wet, such a liberated state remains unaffected by worldly bonds.
shambhu_gita::824.modern_relevance: You’ve faced tough challenges, yet you remain unshaken and free, like a lotus leaf floating above the waves.
shambhu_gita::824.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as naturally untouchable by external pressures and attachments.

shambhu_gita::825.verse_sanskrit:
पितृजे मत्यपि स्थूले गुणाधारे वपुष्यहो।
सर्वेषु देशकालेषु जीवन्मुक्तात्मवेदिनाम् ॥
shambhu_gita::825.verse_hindi: और माता पिता से उत्पन्न स्थूल शरीर गुणों का आधार होने पर भी जीवन्मुक्त की प्रतिभा सब देश और काल में
shambhu_gita::825.english_translation: Even though born from parents and having a gross body as the basis of qualities, the brilliance of the liberated true self shines in all places and times.
shambhu_gita::825.translation_literal: पितृजे (from parents) / मत्यपि (even though born) / स्थूले (gross) / गुणाधारे (basis of qualities) / वपुष्यहो (having a body) / सर्वेषु (in all) / देशकालेषु (places and times) / जीवन्मुक्तात्मवेदिनाम् (of the liberated true self’s brilliance)
shambhu_gita::825.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::825.essence: The true self shines beyond body, birth, place, and time.
shambhu_gita::825.simple_meaning: Your true self shines clearly in every place and time, beyond your physical body born of parents.
shambhu_gita::825.simple_insight: You are more than your physical form; your essence shines everywhere and always.
shambhu_gita::825.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that although our bodies arise from parents and are made of qualities, the true self that is liberated shines beyond all local and temporal limits.
shambhu_gita::825.modern_relevance: You may feel tied to your appearance or background, but your deeper self remains bright and free everywhere you go.
shambhu_gita::825.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with body and birth to recognizing the timeless nature of the true self.

shambhu_gita::826.verse_sanskrit:
प्रतिमा निर्मलोक्तस्य स्थूलदेहस्य तैर्गुणैः।
मुद्यते पितरो नैव सत्यमेतद्रवीमि वः ॥
shambhu_gita::826.verse_hindi: निर्मल रहकर उक्त स्थूल शरीर के गुणों से मोहित नहीं होती है, यह मैं सत्य कहता हूं
shambhu_gita::826.english_translation: The true self, pure and untouched, is never deluded by the qualities of the gross body; this I speak as truth to you.
shambhu_gita::826.translation_literal: प्रतिमा (image/likeness) निर्मल (pure) उक्तस्य (spoken/of said) स्थूलदेहस्य (gross body) तैः (by those) गुणैः (qualities) मुद्यते (is deluded) पितरो (fathers/ancestors) नैव (not at all) सत्यमेतद् (this is truth) रवीमि (I say) वः (to you)
shambhu_gita::826.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::826.essence: The true self is pure and never deceived by the body's qualities.
shambhu_gita::826.simple_meaning: Your true self is pure and never confused or affected by the changing qualities of your physical body.
shambhu_gita::826.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your essence is untouched by your body's shifts.
shambhu_gita::826.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that the true self, or inner being, remains pure and unaffected by the changing qualities of the physical body, reassuring Arjuna that identity is deeper than appearance or bodily traits.
shambhu_gita::826.modern_relevance: You may feel overwhelmed by how your body ages or changes, but your true self remains steady and untouched beneath those shifts.
shambhu_gita::826.insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with your body to recognizing your unchanging inner self.

shambhu_gita::827.verse_sanskrit:
सन्ततं मयि युक्तानां जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनाम् ।
जायन्ते सर्वकर्माणि तदर्थं भ्रष्टवीजवत् ॥
shambhu_gita::827.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण! मुझमें सदा युक्त होने से जीवन्मुक्त महात्माओं के सब कर्म उनके लिये भ्रष्ट बीजवत होजाते हैं
shambhu_gita::827.english_translation: For those always united with me, all their actions arise like spoiled seeds, yet they remain liberated in life.
shambhu_gita::827.translation_literal: सन्ततं (always) मयि (in me) युक्तानां (of those united) जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनाम् (liberated beings) । जायन्ते (arise) सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) तदर्थं (for that reason) भ्रष्टवीजवत् (like spoiled seeds) ॥
shambhu_gita::827.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::827.essence: Being continuously united with the divine makes all your actions harmless and frees you in life.
shambhu_gita::827.simple_meaning: If you stay constantly connected to the divine, your actions do not bind you like bad seeds but lead to freedom in life.
shambhu_gita::827.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true connection can make even imperfect actions harmless.
shambhu_gita::827.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that beings who remain always connected to him act in the world, but their actions do not create binding consequences, like spoiled seeds that fail to grow. This frees them from the cycle of reactivity while living.
shambhu_gita::827.modern_relevance: You can make mistakes or face setbacks, yet your rooted connection to what truly matters keeps you free from lasting harm.
shambhu_gita::827.insight: It shifts your view from fearing consequences to trusting your inner alignment dissolves their power.

shambhu_gita::828.verse_sanskrit:
आयस्कान्तगिरेः पोते गच्छत्येवान्तिकं यथा।
पृथग्भवन्ति लौहानि कीलकान्यखिलान्यलम् ॥
shambhu_gita::828.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार चुम्बक के पर्वत के निकट होते ही पोत के शरीर की सब लोहे की कीले
shambhu_gita::828.english_translation: Just as all the iron nails of a ship stick together when near the magnet mountain,
shambhu_gita::828.translation_literal: आयस्कान्तगिरेः (magnet mountain's) / पोते (of the ship) / गच्छत्येवान्तिकं (when approaching nearby) / यथा (just as) / पृथग्भवन्ति (separately become) / लौहानि (iron pieces) / कीलकानि (nails) / अखिलानि (all) / अलम् (together)
shambhu_gita::828.speaker: Unknown
shambhu_gita::828.essence: A strong force naturally unites scattered parts into a single whole.
shambhu_gita::828.simple_meaning: When a ship carrying iron nails comes near a magnet mountain, all the nails come together tightly.
shambhu_gita::828.simple_insight: Some forces naturally bring scattered things into unity without effort.
shambhu_gita::828.detailed_meaning: This verse uses the example of a ship carrying many iron nails that, when near a magnet mountain, all the nails attract and cling together. It illustrates how a strong attracting force can unify separate pieces.
shambhu_gita::828.modern_relevance: Like metal nails drawn together by a magnet, your thoughts or people around you can naturally come into harmony when a strong influence is present.
shambhu_gita::828.insight: It teaches how a powerful presence or influence can unify scattered elements effortlessly.

shambhu_gita::829.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मिन्नेव भवन्त्याशु सलग्नानि धराधरे।
सपोतश्च क्षणे तस्मिंस्तत्रैवाब्धौ निमज्जति ॥
shambhu_gita::829.verse_hindi: पोत से खुलकर उस पर्वत में जा मिलती हैं और वह पोत समुद्रमग्न हो जाता है,
shambhu_gita::829.english_translation: The boats quickly attach to the mountain, and the boat itself sinks into the ocean there.
shambhu_gita::829.translation_literal: तस्मिन्नेव (in that very) भवन्ति (are) आशु (quickly) सलग्नानि (attached) धराधरे (to the mountain). सपोतः (the boat) च (and) क्षणे (in a moment) तस्मिन् (there) तत्रैव (right there) अब्धौ (in the ocean) निमज्जति (sinks).
shambhu_gita::829.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::829.essence: Temporary attachment can lead quickly to complete immersion or loss.
shambhu_gita::829.simple_meaning: Boats quickly stick to the mountain and then sink immediately into the ocean there.
shambhu_gita::829.simple_insight: Sometimes things that seem steady can quickly disappear without warning.
shambhu_gita::829.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how boats cling briefly to a mountain before sinking into the ocean, illustrating a sudden and total submersion. This is a narrative scene setting without explicit teaching.
shambhu_gita::829.insight: Recognizes how appearances of stability can be momentary and misleading.

shambhu_gita::830.verse_sanskrit:
तथैव मयि युक्तानां जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनाम् । 
श्रयन्तेऽखिलकेर्माणि ब्रह्माण्डाकाशमेव वै ॥
shambhu_gita::830.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार मुझमें युक्त जीवन्मुक्तों के सब कर्म ब्रह्माण्डाकाश को आश्रय कर लेते हैं
shambhu_gita::830.english_translation: Similarly, for those united with me, all actions of the liberated great souls rest like the cosmic space.
shambhu_gita::830.translation_literal: तथैव (similarly) मयि (in me) युक्तानां (of those united) जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनाम् (liberated great souls) । / श्रयन्तेऽखिलकेर्माणि (all actions rest) ब्रह्माण्डाकाशमेव (like the cosmic space) वै (indeed) ॥
shambhu_gita::830.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::830.essence: When united with the divine, your actions rest effortlessly like infinite space.
shambhu_gita::830.simple_meaning: When you unite with the divine, your actions settle calmly like the vast cosmic space.
shambhu_gita::830.simple_insight: You can feel your efforts rest naturally when connected deeply within.
shambhu_gita::830.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that souls united with the divine act freely, with their deeds resting peacefully like the infinite cosmic space, symbolizing complete inner freedom and non-attachment.
shambhu_gita::830.modern_relevance: You finish a demanding project and realize your efforts no longer weigh on you—they settle naturally, like space holding everything effortlessly.
shambhu_gita::830.insight: It shifts your view from struggling with outcomes to embodying calm connection, letting your actions flow without clinging.

shambhu_gita::831.verse_sanskrit:
बारिबिन्दुरिवाकाशात्पतितस्ते महार्णवे:।
 जीवन्मुक्ता महात्मानो लयं गच्छन्ति मव्यहो ॥
shambhu_gita::831.verse_hindi: और जीवन्मुक्त आकाशपतित वारिविन्दु के समान मुझमें मिल जाते हैं
shambhu_gita::831.english_translation: Just as water droplets fall from the sky into the great ocean, liberated beings merge into me.
shambhu_gita::831.translation_literal: बारि (water) / बिन्दु (droplet) / इव (like) / आकाशात् (from sky) / पतितः (fallen) / ते (they) / महा (great) / अर्णवे: (in ocean) / जीवन्मुक्ता (liberated beings) / महात्मानो (great souls) / लयम् (merging) / गच्छन्ति (go) / म (into me) / अव्यहो (undivided)
shambhu_gita::831.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::831.essence: Liberated beings lose their separateness and merge completely into the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::831.simple_meaning: Liberated beings lose their separate selves and become one with the supreme reality, like water drops joining an ocean.
shambhu_gita::831.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self ultimately merges with the vast whole.
shambhu_gita::831.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that those who are liberated no longer see themselves as separate. Like water droplets falling from the sky and merging into the vast ocean, these great souls dissolve their individuality into Shiva, the supreme reality.
shambhu_gita::831.modern_relevance: When you release your ego and separate identity, you can find deep peace by feeling connected to something vast and unchanging.
shambhu_gita::831.insight: This verse shifts focus from clinging to a separate self toward embracing unity with the supreme reality.

shambhu_gita::832.verse_sanskrit:
एकैकस्यं गुणस्याथ या वृत्तिद्धयरूपतः।
आहारो मैथुनं निद्रा भयं ज्ञानं सुखैपणा ॥
shambhu_gita::832.verse_hindi: जीव में जो एक एक गुण की दो दो वृत्ति रूप से आहार, निद्रा, भय, मैथुन, ज्ञान और सुखेच्छा
shambhu_gita::832.english_translation: In every individual, each quality has two modes: intake, sleep, fear, desire, knowledge, and pleasure.
shambhu_gita::832.translation_literal: एकैकस्यं (each one's) गुणस्याथ (qualities and) या (which) वृत्तिद्धयरूपतः (in two modes). आहारो (intake) मैथुनं (desire) निद्रा (sleep) भयं (fear) ज्ञानं (knowledge) सुखैपणा (and pleasure).
shambhu_gita::832.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::832.essence: Every quality inside you naturally expresses itself in two opposite ways.
shambhu_gita::832.simple_meaning: Every quality within you appears in two forms, like seeking and resting, or fear and knowledge.
shambhu_gita::832.simple_insight: You can feel how your traits swing between action and stillness, desire and peace.
shambhu_gita::832.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that each quality inside a person appears in two opposite ways — for example, intake and sleep, fear and desire. This teaches how traits are dynamic and dual in nature.
shambhu_gita::832.modern_relevance: You notice how your habits and feelings often come in pairs, like wanting something then resting from it.
shambhu_gita::832.insight: It shifts your view to see qualities as fluid pairs, helping you embrace change in yourself without judgment.

shambhu_gita::833.verse_sanskrit:
इमा षड्वृत्तयः सन्त्यास्थावराज्जीवसङ्घतः।
देवतोन्नतसृष्टयन्तं विद्यमानाः समानतः ॥
shambhu_gita::833.verse_hindi: यह छः वृत्तियां स्थावर आदि जीव से लेकर देवता आदि उन्नत सृष्टि में भी समानता से विद्यमान
shambhu_gita::833.english_translation: These six modes exist equally throughout all beings, from inert matter to living beings to the highest deities.
shambhu_gita::833.translation_literal: इमा (these) षड्वृत्तयः (six modes) सन्ति (are) स्थावर (inert) आर्ज् (and) जीवसङ्घतः (living beings)। देवत (deities) उन्नत (highest) सृष्टयन्तं (creation) विद्यमानाः (present) समानतः (equally)॥
shambhu_gita::833.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::833.essence: Six fundamental qualities exist equally in all beings from lowest to highest.
shambhu_gita::833.simple_meaning: Six qualities or tendencies are found equally in all things, from non-living matter to living beings and even the highest divine beings.
shambhu_gita::833.simple_insight: Everything shares fundamental qualities, connecting all levels of existence.
shambhu_gita::833.detailed_meaning: Suta describes a foundational cosmological idea: six basic qualities or modes are present evenly across all creation, from the simplest matter to the most exalted beings. This sets the stage for understanding universal patterns beyond distinctions.
shambhu_gita::833.insight: Recognize the shared patterns beneath apparent differences among all existence.

shambhu_gita::834.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मजालेषु तान् सर्वानावद्धान कुर्वते च ताः ।
स्थावरान जंगमाञ्जीवान देवमादिकान् ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::834.verse_hindi: रहकर कर्मजाल में उनको नाबद्ध रखती है
shambhu_gita::834.english_translation: The divine binds all beings—immovable, moving, and divine alike—in the net of karma.
shambhu_gita::834.translation_literal: कर्मजालेषु (in the net of karma) / तान् (them) / सर्वानावद्धान (all bound) / कुर्वते (makes) / च (and) / ताः (those) / स्थावरान (immovable beings) / जंगमाञ्जीवान (moving living beings) / देवमादिकान् (divine beings and others) / ध्रुवम् (certainly)
shambhu_gita::834.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::834.essence: All beings, from the smallest to the divine, are entwined in the net of karma.
shambhu_gita::834.simple_meaning: Everything alive, still or moving, and even divine beings are bound by the consequences of their actions.
shambhu_gita::834.simple_insight: Recognizing that all beings share the burden of karma brings humility and shared responsibility.
shambhu_gita::834.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shiva explains that all forms of life—whether immovable like mountains, moving like animals, or divine like radiant beings—are caught in karma's binding net, emphasizing the universal reach of action and consequence.
shambhu_gita::834.modern_relevance: You feel stuck by past choices, seeing how unseen patterns bind you and everyone else, no matter your status.
shambhu_gita::834.insight: Understand that no one exists outside the consequences of their actions, shifting focus from blame to personal responsibility.

shambhu_gita::835.verse_sanskrit:
परन्तु जीवन्मुक्तेपु नूनं स्वाभाविकास्त्रपि।
सतीप्वपि किलैतासु त्यजन्ति स्वगुणान् हि ताः ॥
shambhu_gita::835.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे विज्ञवरो! जीवन्मुक्त में ये स्वाभाविक छः वृत्तियां रहने पर भी अपने स्वाभाविक गुणों को परित्याग कर देती हैं।
shambhu_gita::835.english_translation: However, among those who are truly liberated, even with these natural six tendencies present, they abandon their natural qualities.
shambhu_gita::835.translation_literal: परन्तु (however) जीवन्मुक्ते (in the truly liberated) नूनं (indeed) स्वाभाविका (natural) अस्ति (are) त्रपि (even) सतीप्वपि (even these) किल (indeed) ऐतासु (in these) त्यजन्ति (they abandon) स्वगुणान् (their own qualities) हि (indeed) ताः (they feminine plural).
shambhu_gita::835.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::835.essence: True freedom means releasing attachment to natural traits without erasing them.
shambhu_gita::835.simple_meaning: Even when natural habits or tendencies remain, truly free people let go of being controlled by them.
shambhu_gita::835.simple_insight: Freedom is not about losing who you are but releasing what holds you back.
shambhu_gita::835.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even after full liberation, natural qualities or tendencies remain in a person, but the person no longer clings to or identifies with these qualities. This marks true freedom beyond outward change.
shambhu_gita::835.modern_relevance: You might still feel your usual impulses or moods, yet you can choose not to react or be limited by them.
shambhu_gita::835.insight: It teaches you to recognize habitual patterns without letting them define your actions or identity.

shambhu_gita::836.verse_hindi: आहार और निद्रारूपी तामसिक वृत्तियां केवल उनके स्थूल शरीर के आश्रय से वासनाशून्य होकर जीवित रहती हैं।
shambhu_gita::836.english_translation: The tamasic modes of sleep and eating survive only by residing in the gross body, devoid of desires.
shambhu_gita::836.translation_literal: निद्रा (sleep) / आहारस्वरूपिणि (in the form of eating) / स्तामसिक्यो (tamasic) / हि (indeed) / वृत्तयः (modes) / स्थूलदेहा (gross body) / आश्रयेण (by the shelter) / एषां (of these) / तिष्ठे (they reside) / युर्नष्टवासनाः (without desires)
shambhu_gita::836.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::836.essence: Sleep and hunger exist only with the body; the true self is beyond them.
shambhu_gita::836.simple_meaning: Sleep and eating are tamasic habits that exist only because the physical body supports them; without the body, they vanish.
shambhu_gita::836.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing these urges are tied to your body, not your deeper self.
shambhu_gita::836.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that sleep and eating represent tamasic tendencies relying entirely on the gross physical body. They disappear when desires are gone, showing these urges are not part of the true self but linked to bodily existence.
shambhu_gita::836.modern_relevance: When you notice hunger or tiredness, remember they arise from your body—not your deeper awareness beyond it.
shambhu_gita::836.insight: Recognize urges like hunger and sleep as temporary body-driven events, not your unchanging self.

shambhu_gita::837.verse_sanskrit:
भयमैथुनरूपिण्यो जीवन्मुक्तौघटत्तयः।
राजसिक्यो विलीयन्ते स्वीयेषु कारणेवलम् ॥
shambhu_gita::837.verse_hindi: जीवन्मुक्तों की भय और मैथुन रूपी राजसिक वृत्तियां अपने स्वकारण में लय हो जाती हैं और
shambhu_gita::837.english_translation: In the liberated beings, the fear and passion-like rajasic tendencies dissolve completely in their own source.
shambhu_gita::837.translation_literal: भयमैथुनरूपिण्यो (fear and passion-like) / जीवन्मुक्तौघटत्तयः (liberated beings) / राजसिक्यो (rajasic tendencies) / विलीयन्ते (dissolve) / स्वीयेषु (in their own) / कारणेवलम् (only source)
shambhu_gita::837.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::837.essence: Fears and desires vanish by dissolving naturally into their own origin in liberation.
shambhu_gita::837.simple_meaning: Fear and desire-like tendencies in liberated beings disappear by merging back into their own source.
shambhu_gita::837.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your fears and desires lose power by returning to their origin.
shambhu_gita::837.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that once beings reach liberation, their restless fears and passionate urges, which arise from rajasic qualities, dissolve naturally by merging back into their own source, removing inner turbulence.
shambhu_gita::837.modern_relevance: You notice your anxious thoughts and cravings losing hold as you observe them deeply instead of reacting.
shambhu_gita::837.insight: It teaches you to see fears and desires as temporary waves that calm when you trace them back to their root.

shambhu_gita::838.verse_sanskrit:
सुखेच्छाज्ञानरूपिण्यस्तेषां सात्विकवृत्तयः ।
समं विश्वेन तादात्म्यभाजः सत्यः स्वधाभुजः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::838.verse_hindi: उनकी ज्ञान और मुखेच्छा रूपी सात्त्विक वृत्तियां जगत के साथ तदाकाररूप धारण करके
shambhu_gita::838.english_translation: Their pure knowledge and desire, as sattvic tendencies, share the same essence with the universe and are truly rooted in their own nature.
shambhu_gita::838.translation_literal: सुखेच्छा (pleasant desire) / ज्ञानरूपिण्यः (formed of knowledge) / तेषां (of them) / सात्विकवृत्तयः (pure tendencies) / समं (equal) / विश्वेन (with the universe) / तादात्म्यभाजः (sharing the same essence) / सत्यः (true) / स्वधाभुजः (rooted in own nature)
shambhu_gita::838.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::838.essence: Pure knowledge and desire share the same true essence as the universe.
shambhu_gita::838.simple_meaning: Pure, wise desires and knowledge reflect the same true essence as the entire universe.
shambhu_gita::838.simple_insight: You can feel connected and aligned when your pure thoughts and desires match the universe's essence.
shambhu_gita::838.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when desires and knowledge are pure and sattvic, they do not conflict with the universe but share its essence, revealing a natural harmony between inner nature and cosmic reality.
shambhu_gita::838.modern_relevance: When your honest wishes and clear understanding align with the world, you experience natural peace and belonging.
shambhu_gita::838.insight: This verse shifts your view to see that pure desires and knowledge are not separate from the world but part of its essence.

shambhu_gita::839.verse_sanskrit:
आभिमुख्येन मे नित्यं प्रवहन्ते न संशयः।
एवं मे ज्ञानिनो भक्ताः शक्नुवन्ति जगद्गुरोः ॥
shambhu_gita::839.verse_hindi: मेरी ओर सदा प्रवाहित होती हैं । इस प्रकार से मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त जगद्गुरु
shambhu_gita::839.english_translation: There is no doubt that streams always flow toward me; thus, my wise devotees can reach the world teacher.
shambhu_gita::839.translation_literal: आभिमुख्येन (toward me) / मे (my) / नित्यं (always) / प्रवहन्ते (flow) / न (no) / संशयः (doubt) / एवं (thus) / मे (my) / ज्ञानिनो (wise) / भक्ताः (devotees) / शक्नुवन्ति (are able) / जगद्गुरोः (world teacher)
shambhu_gita::839.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::839.essence: True devotion naturally flows to the genuine teacher without hesitation.
shambhu_gita::839.simple_meaning: Devotion naturally moves toward the divine teacher without hesitation or doubt.
shambhu_gita::839.simple_insight: You can trust that your inner devotion directs you toward true guidance.
shambhu_gita::839.detailed_meaning: Shiva states that streams of devotion always flow toward him without any doubt, showing how his wise devotees naturally connect to the world teacher through their knowledge and love.
shambhu_gita::839.modern_relevance: When you feel a quiet pull toward someone or something that truly inspires you, it shows your inner guidance working without resistance.
shambhu_gita::839.insight: Recognize that genuine devotion flows effortlessly toward what truly supports your growth and clarity.

shambhu_gita::840.verse_sanskrit:
जगतो रंक्षकस्यापि पदमाप्तुमसंशयम्।
इति वो ज्ञानमाख्यातं श्रूयतां वः पुनर्ब्रूवे ॥
shambhu_gita::840.verse_hindi: और जगदरक्षक पदवी को प्राप्त करने में समर्थ होते हैं। इस प्रकार का ज्ञान कहा गया और भी आप लोगों से कहता हूं सुनो।
shambhu_gita::840.english_translation: Those who possess such knowledge undoubtedly attain the status of protector of the world. This knowledge has been named, and I tell you again: listen.
shambhu_gita::840.translation_literal: जगतो (of the world) / रंक्षकस्यापि (also of the protector) / पदमाप्तुम (to attain the position) / असंशयम् (without doubt) / इति (thus) / वो (your) / ज्ञानमाख्यातं (knowledge named) / श्रूयतां (let it be heard) / वः (to you) / पुनर्ब्रूवे (I tell again)
shambhu_gita::840.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::840.essence: Clear knowledge empowers you to become a protector of the world without doubt.
shambhu_gita::840.simple_meaning: When you gain this knowledge, you become confident and capable of protecting the world. This teaching is important and worth hearing again.
shambhu_gita::840.simple_insight: You feel empowered knowing knowledge can give you a vital role beyond yourself.
shambhu_gita::840.detailed_meaning: In a moment of teaching, Shiva emphasizes that understanding this knowledge grants the power and status of a world protector. He repeats this to make sure his listeners grasp its importance and listen carefully.
shambhu_gita::840.modern_relevance: You realize that deep understanding of your purpose can give you strength to face challenges beyond personal limits.
shambhu_gita::840.insight: It shifts your view from small personal concerns to recognizing the power of knowledge to serve greater causes.

shambhu_gita::841.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मैं अपनी इच्छासे ही अपनी ही शक्तिरूपी कर्म और अपने ही अनुशासनरूपी धर्माधर्म की
shambhu_gita::841.english_translation: Although I act by my own will, my actions are the power itself, shaped by my own discipline of dharma and adharma.
shambhu_gita::841.translation_literal: यद्यपि (although) स्वेच्छया (by own will) एव (indeed) अहम् (I) स्वशक्तयात्मककर्मणः (own power-formed actions) स्वानुशासनरूपाया (own discipline-shaped) धमाधर्मव्यवस्थितेः (of dharma and adharma arrangement)
shambhu_gita::841.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::841.essence: Your free will acts through inner power shaped by your own discipline of right and wrong.
shambhu_gita::841.simple_meaning: You act by your own will, but your actions are formed by your own inner power and the discipline of right and wrong you follow.
shambhu_gita::841.simple_insight: You hold the power of action, but it is shaped by your inner discipline and sense of right.
shambhu_gita::841.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even though he acts from his own free will, his actions are expressions of his inherent power, which is itself shaped by his inner order of dharma and adharma. This shows the complex interplay between free will, power, and moral discipline.
shambhu_gita::841.modern_relevance: You decide what to do, but your habits and values shape how your actions really play out in life.
shambhu_gita::841.insight: Recognize that your will alone doesn't determine action; your inner discipline shapes its nature.

shambhu_gita::842.verse_hindi: अधीनता स्वीकार करके इस जगत में इसके कल्याण के लिये जब कभी अवतार धारण करता हूँ।
shambhu_gita::842.english_translation: Accepting submission, whenever I incarnate in this world, it is for its welfare.
shambhu_gita::842.translation_literal: निघ्नताञ्चोररीकृत्य (accepting submission) / जगत्कल्याणहेतवे (for the welfare of the world) / यदा (whenever) / कदाचि (at any time) / विश्वस्मिन् (in the world) / अतीर्णो (having incarnated) / भवामि (I become) / अहो (indeed)
shambhu_gita::842.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::842.essence: Choosing limitation to serve the world's welfare is a conscious act of humility and power.
shambhu_gita::842.simple_meaning: Whenever I take a form in this world, it is by accepting limitation to work for its well-being.
shambhu_gita::842.simple_insight: There is power and humility in choosing to serve the greater good through limitation.
shambhu_gita::842.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that when he incarnates, he accepts the constraint of form and limitation to act compassionately for the welfare of the world. This verse reveals his conscious choice to submit to conditions in order to serve.
shambhu_gita::842.modern_relevance: When you step into a new role or responsibility, you might feel limited but your aim can be to serve something bigger than yourself.
shambhu_gita::842.insight: It teaches you to accept constraints willingly when your purpose is to serve a higher good beyond yourself.

shambhu_gita::843.verse_sanskrit:
जीवन्मुक्तपदप्राप्तान किन्तु भक्तगणानहम्।
सर्वथा कर्मभिर्मुक्तात् विदधे पितरो ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::843.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे पितृगण ! जीवन्मुक्ति पदवी प्राप्त भक्त गण को मैं सब प्रकार के कर्म से मुक्त कर देता हूँ
shambhu_gita::843.english_translation: But O ancestors, I free my devoted followers who have attained the state of living liberation from all kinds of actions.
shambhu_gita::843.translation_literal:
जीवन्मुक्तपदप्राप्तान (attained living liberation state) किन्तु (but) भक्तगणानहम् (my devoted followers) ।
सर्वथा (in all ways) कर्मभिर्मुक्तात् (free from actions) विदधे (I give) पितरो (ancestors) ध्रुवम् (certainly) ॥
shambhu_gita::843.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::843.essence: True devotion combined with living liberation frees you from all binding actions.
shambhu_gita::843.simple_meaning: Those devoted to the divine who have reached living liberation are freed from the binding effect of all actions.
shambhu_gita::843.simple_insight: You feel a deep freedom knowing true devotion frees you from the weight of every action.
shambhu_gita::843.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that devotees who have attained a state of living liberation are completely freed from all karmic binding, marking a profound spiritual achievement beyond ordinary action.
shambhu_gita::843.modern_relevance: You might feel stuck by the consequences of past choices, but devotion and inner freedom can release you from that burden.
shambhu_gita::843.insight: It shifts your understanding from seeing actions as binding to seeing devotion as liberating, changing how you engage with life.

shambhu_gita::844.verse_sanskrit:
नानाविधाश्च जायन्तेऽवतारा मे युगे युगे ।
समष्टिकर्मसादेते सम्पद्यन्ते न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::844.verse_hindi: युग युग में मेरे अवतार अनेक प्रकार के होते हैं वह सब समष्टिका धीन होते हैं।
shambhu_gita::844.english_translation: In every age, many types of my incarnations appear; all arise to fulfill collective karma without doubt.
shambhu_gita::844.translation_literal: नानाविधाश्च (various types) / जायन्तेऽवतारा (are born incarnations) / मे (my) / युगे युगे (in every age) / समष्टिकर्मसादेते (from collective karma) / सम्पद्यन्ते (arise) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
shambhu_gita::844.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::844.essence: The divine manifests repeatedly in many forms to address collective karma across ages.
shambhu_gita::844.simple_meaning: Many forms of my incarnations appear in every age, all arising from collective karma.
shambhu_gita::844.simple_insight: You can trust that the divine acts repeatedly through many forms to restore balance.
shambhu_gita::844.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that throughout time, various incarnations manifest repeatedly, each arising to fulfill the shared consequences of collective actions. This verse situates Shiva as the source of these divine appearances linked to cosmic order.
shambhu_gita::844.insight: It shifts how you see challenges as part of a larger unfolding action beyond individual control.

shambhu_gita::845.verse_sanskrit:
प्राधान्यं त्रिविधानां मे शक्तीनामेव जायते।
ममावतारपुञ्जेषु तेऽतो मच्छत्स्यपक्षकाः ॥
shambhu_gita::845.verse_hindi: मेरे अवतारों में मेरी त्रिविध शक्ति की ही प्रधानता रहती है इस कारण वह मेरी शक्ति सापेक्ष हैं
shambhu_gita::845.english_translation: My threefold powers are foremost among my incarnations; thus, they are relative to my power.
shambhu_gita::845.translation_literal: प्राधान्यं (foremost) त्रिविधानां (of three kinds) मे (my) शक्तीनामेव (powers only) जायते (arise) । ममावतारपुञ्जेषु (in my incarnations) तेऽतो (therefore) मच्छत्स्यपक्षकाः (relative to my power) ॥
shambhu_gita::845.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::845.essence: The threefold powers in incarnations reflect their source in supreme power.
shambhu_gita::845.simple_meaning: My incarnations highlight my three main powers, showing how they relate to my overall strength.
shambhu_gita::845.simple_insight: Seeing the divine powers as connected parts of a whole reveals their true nature.
shambhu_gita::845.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that among his many incarnations, the threefold powers are most prominent, emphasizing their connection as expressions of his supreme power.
shambhu_gita::845.insight: Recognize that different expressions of your power are interconnected aspects of a greater whole.

shambhu_gita::846.verse_sanskrit:
अपेक्षते तु मच्छक्तीर्जीवन्मुक्तेषु कोऽपि न ।
सर्वमुक्ता हि जायन्ते जीवन्मुक्ता न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::846.verse_hindi: परन्तु जीवन्मुक्तगण में से कोई भी मेरी शक्ति की अपेक्षान हीं रखता,
shambhu_gita::846.english_translation: But none among the liberated beings depends on my power; all are liberated, no doubt about it.
shambhu_gita::846.translation_literal: अपेक्षते (expects) तु (but) मच्छक्तीः (my power) जीवन्मुक्तेषु (among liberated beings) कोऽपि (anyone) न (not) । / सर्वमुक्ता (all liberated) हि (indeed) जायन्ते (are born) जीवन्मुक्ता (liberated beings) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
shambhu_gita::846.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::846.essence: True liberation depends on nothing outside the self; it is complete and self-sufficient.
shambhu_gita::846.simple_meaning: Those who are truly free do not depend on Shiva's power or anything else; their freedom is complete and unquestionable.
shambhu_gita::846.simple_insight: You can feel complete independence in your freedom, without needing anything outside you.
shambhu_gita::846.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shiva clarifies that beings who have attained liberation do not rely on his divine energy or any other force. Their freedom is absolute, arising from within themselves, emphasizing true self-sufficiency.
shambhu_gita::846.modern_relevance: You’ve reached a point where you no longer seek external approval or support to feel free in your choices and being.
shambhu_gita::846.insight: It teaches you to recognize freedom as independent of external powers, rooted solely in your own inner state.

shambhu_gita::847.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मज्ञानं यदासाद्य ज्ञानिभक्तगणो मम ।
लभते पितरो नूनं जीवन्मुक्तिपदं परम् ॥
shambhu_gita::847.verse_hindi: हे पितृगणं ! जिस आत्मज्ञान को प्राप्त करके मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तगण उत्तम जीवन्मुक्त पदवी को प्राप्त करते हैं
shambhu_gita::847.english_translation: O ancestors, the wise devotees who attain self-knowledge surely reach the highest state of freedom in life.
shambhu_gita::847.translation_literal: आत्मज्ञानं (self-knowledge) यत् (which) आसाद्य (having attained) ज्ञानि-भक्तगणः (wise devotees) मम (my) । लभते (obtain) पितरो (ancestors) नूनं (certainly) जीवन्मुक्तिपदम् (state of freedom in life) परम् (highest) ॥
shambhu_gita::847.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::847.essence: Wisdom combined with devoted love leads to the highest living freedom.
shambhu_gita::847.simple_meaning: Those who combine wisdom and devoted love to the divine gain the highest freedom in life through self-knowledge.
shambhu_gita::847.simple_insight: You can find deep freedom when wisdom and devotion join in your heart.
shambhu_gita::847.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, explaining that his wise devotees who blend knowledge and devotion achieve the supreme state of liberation while alive, highlighting the power of devotion and insight combined.
shambhu_gita::847.modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard to understand yourself deeply and stay devoted to your values; this leads you to real freedom from inner struggles.
shambhu_gita::847.insight: It teaches you that gaining self-knowledge enriched by devotion shifts you from bondage to freedom in your daily life.

shambhu_gita::848.verse_hindi: उस आत्मज्ञान के आविर्भाव की दशा वेद में तीन श्रेणी की कही गई है। वेदान्त प्रतिपाद्य सच्चिदानन्दमय
shambhu_gita::848.english_translation: The emergence of that self-knowledge is described in the Vedas in three categories. It reveals the true self characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss as taught in Vedanta.
shambhu_gita::848.translation_literal: आविर्भूतेस्तस्य (of that emergence) वेदे (in the Veda) दशात्रैविध्यमीरितम् (threefold categories described) । वेदान्तप्रतिपाद्यस्य (of what Vedanta teaches) सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणः (having the form of existence-consciousness-bliss) ॥
shambhu_gita::848.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::848.essence: Self-knowledge reveals itself in three fundamental forms: existence, consciousness, and bliss.
shambhu_gita::848.simple_meaning: Self-knowledge appears in three forms described in the Vedas, revealing the true self as existence, consciousness, and bliss.
shambhu_gita::848.simple_insight: There is comfort knowing your true self has many clear, timeless expressions.
shambhu_gita::848.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that self-knowledge, the realization of the true self, is categorized into three types in the Vedas. Vedanta teaches this true self as pure existence, consciousness, and bliss, highlighting its profound nature.
shambhu_gita::848.modern_relevance: You may sense different ways your true self shows up in life—through being, awareness, or joy—each pointing to your real nature.
shambhu_gita::848.insight: It guides you to recognize your true self beyond appearances by understanding its three essential qualities.

shambhu_gita::849.verse_sanskrit:
स्वस्वरूपस्य सँल्लब्धावपरोक्षानुभूतितः ।
सत्यां स्वतो विमुच्यन्ते जीवाः संसारबन्धनात् ॥
shambhu_gita::849.verse_hindi: स्वरूप की उपलब्धि अपरोक्षानुभूति द्वारा करते ही जीव बन्धनरहित हो जाता है;
shambhu_gita::849.english_translation: When a being directly experiences its own true nature, it is naturally freed from the bonds of reactivity.
shambhu_gita::849.translation_literal: स्वस्वरूपस्य (of own true nature) सँल्लब्धाव (upon obtaining) अपरोक्षानुभूतितः (direct experience) । सत्यां (truly) स्वतो (by itself) विमुच्यन्ते (are freed) जीवाः (beings) संसारबन्धनात् (from the bonds of reactivity) ॥
shambhu_gita::849.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::849.essence: Direct experience of your true self naturally frees you from reactive bondage.
shambhu_gita::849.simple_meaning: When you directly experience who you truly are, you naturally become free from reactivity and suffering.
shambhu_gita::849.simple_insight: Knowing yourself deeply brings a natural relief from feeling stuck or trapped.
shambhu_gita::849.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that when a being gains a clear, direct experience of its own true nature, that being naturally escapes the cycle of reactive suffering known as reactivity. This moment of direct inner knowing is the key to freedom.
shambhu_gita::849.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in repetitive patterns until a moment of clear self-understanding frees you from old reactions.
shambhu_gita::849.insight: It shifts your focus from trying to escape suffering to directly experiencing your unchanging nature, which dissolves bondage.

shambhu_gita::850.verse_sanskrit:
तेषां पारब्धमावल्याभ्रमत्कौलालचक्रवत् ।
तञ्चित्तस्य तदा किन्तु विक्षेपो नैव नश्यति ॥
shambhu_gita::850.verse_hindi: किन्तु उस समय घूमते हुए कुलाल चक्र के समान उसके चित्त के विक्षेप उसके प्रारब्ध की प्रबलता के कारण दूर नहीं होते हैं
shambhu_gita::850.english_translation: But at that time, the distractions in the mind do not disappear because of the strong force of past karma, like the spinning potter's wheel.
shambhu_gita::850.translation_literal: तेषां (their) पारब्धम् (past karma) आवल्याभ्रमत् (like a spinning wheel) कौलालचक्रवत् (like a potter's wheel) । तञ्चि (that) तस्य (of that) तदा (then) किन्तु (but) विक्षेपो (distraction) नैव (not) नश्यति (disappear) ॥
shambhu_gita::850.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::850.essence: Strong past karma can keep the mind restless despite effort to quiet it.
shambhu_gita::850.simple_meaning: When your past actions have strong influence, your mind's distractions keep spinning like a potter's wheel and don't easily stop.
shambhu_gita::850.simple_insight: It's normal to feel stuck in restless thoughts when past influences are strong.
shambhu_gita::850.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that during deep practice, the mind can remain restless and distracted because the strong force of past karma keeps stirring it like a spinning potter's wheel, showing the challenge in calming the mind.
shambhu_gita::850.modern_relevance: Your mind races uncontrollably when past habits and consequences strongly tug your attention, making focus feel impossible.
shambhu_gita::850.insight: Recognize that past actions can powerfully sustain mental distractions, requiring patient discipline to calm.

shambhu_gita::851.verse_sanskrit:
तव्युत्थानदशा नूनं बाहुल्येन हि जायते।
किन्तु ते भाग्यवन्तो मे भक्ता ज्ञानाब्धिपारगाः ॥
shambhu_gita::851.verse_hindi: और उसकी व्युत्थान दशा अधिकता से बनी रहती है परन्तु यह भाग्यवान् मेरा भक्त
shambhu_gita::851.english_translation: Your state of upheaval is indeed often intense, but fortunate are my devotees who have mastered the ocean of wisdom.
shambhu_gita::851.translation_literal: तव्युत्थानदशा (your state of upheaval) / नूनं (indeed) / बाहुल्येन (with intensity) / हि (certainly) / जायते (arises). / किन्तु (but) / ते (those) / भाग्यवन्तो (fortunate) / मे (my) / भक्ता (devotees) / ज्ञानाब्धिपारगाः (masters of the ocean of wisdom).
shambhu_gita::851.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::851.essence: Devotion paired with deep wisdom makes one fortunate despite life's upheavals.
shambhu_gita::851.simple_meaning: Though your life may often feel chaotic, those devoted and wise are truly fortunate and steady.
shambhu_gita::851.simple_insight: You can feel fortunate even when life feels overwhelming, by holding onto devotion and wisdom.
shambhu_gita::851.detailed_meaning: Shiva acknowledges that life can be full of intense upheaval, but those who are devoted to him and have deep understanding are blessed and strong despite challenges.
shambhu_gita::851.modern_relevance: You face constant stress and upheaval, yet your steady faith and insight keep you grounded and fortunate.
shambhu_gita::851.insight: It teaches you to see devotion and wisdom as anchors that transform turbulent experiences into strength.

shambhu_gita::852.verse_sanskrit:
यान्ति मे तीव्रत्तीनां स्वतः सन्धौ स्वरूपताम् । 
विक्षेपबहुलेनान्तःकरणेन समन्विताः ॥
shambhu_gita::852.verse_hindi: तीव्रवृत्तियों की सन्धि में अपने आप ही मेरे स्वस्वरूप में पहुंच जाया करता है ।
shambhu_gita::852.english_translation: The intense waves of the mind naturally converge into my own true nature.
shambhu_gita::852.translation_literal: यान्ति (go) / मे (my) / तीव्रत्तीनां (of intense waves) / स्वतः (by themselves) / सन्धौ (into union) / स्वरूपताम् (to true nature) / विक्षेपबहुलेन (full of distraction) / अन्तःकरणेन (by the inner instrument) / समन्विताः (accompanied)
shambhu_gita::852.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::852.essence: Even restless mental waves naturally unite in your true self.
shambhu_gita::852.simple_meaning: The mind’s intense and restless thoughts naturally come together in your true self despite distractions.
shambhu_gita::852.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing your busy mind is still connected to your true nature.
shambhu_gita::852.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that even when the mind is full of intense and distracting waves, it ultimately converges back into the true self, revealing the natural connection beneath mental chaos.
shambhu_gita::852.modern_relevance: When your thoughts race and distract you, notice how they still guide you closer to your authentic self.
shambhu_gita::852.insight: It teaches you to see the mind’s turbulence as part of the natural flow toward your true self.

shambhu_gita::853.verse_sanskrit:
सन्तोऽपि स्वस्वरूपस्य ह्यपरोक्षानुभूतितः। 
मुक्तात्मानोऽभिधीयन्ते श्रेणीमाद्यां गता अमी ॥
shambhu_gita::853.verse_hindi: विक्षेप बहुल अन्तःकरण से युक्त होने पर भी स्व स्वरूप की अपरोक्षानुभूति द्वारा वह मुक्तात्मा प्रथम श्रेणी का कहलाता है।
shambhu_gita::853.english_translation: Even when the mind is full of distractions, those who directly experience their true nature are called the liberated, the highest class.
shambhu_gita::853.translation_literal: सन्तः (saints) अपि (also) स्वस्वरूपस्य (of own nature) हि (indeed) अपरोक्षानुभूतितः (direct experience) मुक्तात्मानः (liberated beings) अभिधीयन्ते (are called) श्रेणीम (class) आद्यां (highest) गता (gone) अमी (called)
shambhu_gita::853.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::853.essence: True freedom is knowing your real self directly, even amid mental distractions.
shambhu_gita::853.simple_meaning: Even if your mind is restless and distracted, directly experiencing your true self means you are truly free.
shambhu_gita::853.simple_insight: You can feel deep freedom even when your mind is unsettled and busy.
shambhu_gita::853.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that some seekers, despite having many distractions in their minds, directly experience their true self. These beings are called liberated, belonging to the highest spiritual class, showing that freedom is not about mental stillness alone.
shambhu_gita::853.modern_relevance: Your mind races with thoughts and worries, yet moments arise when you glimpse your true self clearly — that is genuine freedom.
shambhu_gita::853.insight: It shifts the idea that freedom requires perfect mental quiet to understanding it can coexist with distraction.

shambhu_gita::854.verse_sanskrit:
प्राकृतेन कलंकेन  दृश्यासत्या च वर्जिता । 
जगजालविहीनयमवस्था जायते ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::854.verse_hindi: यह अवस्था जगज्जालरहित प्राकृतिक कलंक रहित और दृश्य की आसक्ति से रहित होती है
shambhu_gita::854.english_translation: This state is free from the world's entanglement, natural blemish, and attachment to appearances.
shambhu_gita::854.translation_literal: प्राकृतेन (by nature) कलंकेन (blemish) दृश्यासत्या (attachment to seen) च (and) वर्जिता (free) । जगजालविहीनयमवस्था (state without world-entanglement) जायते (arises) ध्रुवम् (certainly) ॥
shambhu_gita::854.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::854.essence: A stable state arises beyond natural flaws and attachment to appearances.
shambhu_gita::854.simple_meaning: There is a state of being without natural defects, without being caught in the world's illusions or attachments to what you see.
shambhu_gita::854.simple_insight: You can feel a deep freedom beyond flaws and appearances that usually trap your mind.
shambhu_gita::854.detailed_meaning: Shiva describes a pure state of being, free from the natural imperfections and illusions that usually bind living beings. This state is untouched by attachments to the seen world or its confusing entanglements.
shambhu_gita::854.modern_relevance: When your mind stops clinging to surface impressions and flaws, you discover calm beyond everyday distractions.
shambhu_gita::854.insight: It teaches you to see beyond appearances and natural flaws, recognizing a stable, untainted state within.

shambhu_gita::855.verse_sanskrit:
मनोऽपि जायते नूनं सम्यग्भर्जीतवीजवत् ।
तस्मिन दि ज्ञानिभक्तेऽहं मनोमोहात्मकेन वै ॥
shambhu_gita::855.verse_hindi: मन भुने हुए बीज के सदृश्य हो जाता है और उस ज्ञानी भक्त मे मैं तय मनोमोहरुपी
shambhu_gita::855.english_translation: The mind indeed arises like a sprouted seed; in that wise devotee, I reside as the mind's deluding principle.
shambhu_gita::855.translation_literal: मनः (mind) अपि (also) जायते (arises) नूनं (certainly) सम्यग्भर्जीत-वीजवत् (like a properly sprouted seed) । तस्मिन् (in that) दी (wise) ज्ञानि-भक्तेऽहम् (devotee I [am]) मनो-मोह-आत्मकेन (by the mind-delusion-principle) वै (indeed) ॥
shambhu_gita::855.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::855.essence: The divine dwells beyond the restless mind’s illusions in a wise devotee.
