shambhu_gita::953.translation_literal: विद्या (knowledge) / आत्मविद्या (knowledge of the true self) / अस्मि (I am) / मृत्युः (death) / संहारकारिषु (in those who bring destruction) / तेजो (brilliance) / नरेषु (in men) / नारीषु (in women) / पवित्रा (sacred) / श्रीः (prosperity) / स्वधाभुजः (possessing the sacred offerings)
shambhu_gita::953.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::953.essence: The divine manifests uniquely as spiritual knowledge, ending force, vitality, and sacred prosperity.
shambhu_gita::953.simple_meaning: I represent the highest spiritual knowledge, the force of death that ends cycles, the vitality in men, and the sacred prosperity in women.
shambhu_gita::953.simple_insight: The divine expresses as different powers in knowledge, endings, and life’s energy across beings.
shambhu_gita::953.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, declaring his essence as various fundamental powers: spiritual knowledge, the force that destroys, vitality in men, and sacred prosperity in women. This verse shows Shiva’s identification with cosmic principles manifesting diversely.
shambhu_gita::953.insight: Recognize that profound forces shape life differently in knowledge, endings, and vitality, beyond personal identity.

shambhu_gita::954.verse_sanskrit:
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतनांकुसुमाकरः ।
वाराणां सोमवारोऽस्मि निश्चितं पितृपुगवाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::954.verse_hindi: मैं मासों में मार्गशीर्ष, ऋतुओं में वसन्त और वारों में निश्चय सोमवार हूँ
shambhu_gita::954.english_translation: Among months, I am Margashirsha; among seasons, spring; and among days, surely Monday.
shambhu_gita::954.translation_literal: मासानां (among months) मार्गशीर्षोऽहम् (Margashirsha I am) अमृतनांकुसुमाकरः (nectar-cloud-sun) । वाराणां (among days) सोमवारः अस्मि (Monday I am) निश्चितं (certainly) पितृपुगवाः (honored by ancestors) ॥
shambhu_gita::954.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::954.essence: The divine is present as the sacred pulse in time's cycles and rhythms.
shambhu_gita::954.simple_meaning: Shiva identifies himself with the month of Margashirsha, the spring season, and the day Monday, highlighting his presence in time and nature.
shambhu_gita::954.simple_insight: There is a sacred connection between time cycles and the divine presence you can feel in the natural rhythm of life.
shambhu_gita::954.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks about his embodiment in various cycles of time: the month Margashirsha, the spring season known for renewal, and Monday, a day especially dedicated to him, showing his integration with cosmic rhythms.
shambhu_gita::954.insight: Recognize how natural rhythms and cycles can remind you of deeper presence and continuity beyond daily distractions.

shambhu_gita::955.verse_sanskrit:
अहोरात्रेषु पितरोऽस्म्यहं सन्धिचतुष्टयम् ।
उद्यमोऽभ्युदये कार्ये ज्ञानं निःश्रेयसे तथा ॥
shambhu_gita::955.verse_hindi: दिन रात्रि की चारों सन्धि मैं ही हूँ, मैं अभ्युदय की क्रियाओं में उद्यम और निःश्रेयस की क्रिया मै ज्ञान हूँ
shambhu_gita::955.english_translation: In the four junctions of day and night, I am the ancestors; in the actions of progress, I am effort, and in the pursuit of higher good, I am wisdom.
shambhu_gita::955.translation_literal: अहोरात्रेषु (in day and night) पितरोऽस्मि (I am the ancestors) अहं (I) सन्धिचतुष्टयम् (the four junctions) । उद्यमः (effort) अभ्युदये (in progress) कार्ये (in action) ज्ञानं (wisdom) निःश्रेयसे (in the highest good) तथा (also) ॥
shambhu_gita::955.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::955.essence: Every turning point holds effort and wisdom that guide progress toward what is best.
shambhu_gita::955.simple_meaning: You exist in every turning point of day and night. In all progress, you bring effort and in pursuing what is best, you bring wisdom.
shambhu_gita::955.simple_insight: You hold power in every change, combining doing and knowing toward what truly matters.
shambhu_gita::955.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks here about being present at all key transitions—dawn, midday, dusk, midnight—symbolizing life's constant cycles. He claims to embody the ancestors at these junctions and to be the force of effort in progress and wisdom in pursuing the highest good, teaching how our actions and insight are intertwined.
shambhu_gita::955.modern_relevance: You feel the push and pull at every shift in your day—between rest and work, doubt and clarity—and this verse reminds you that effort paired with wisdom moves you toward what truly matters.
shambhu_gita::955.insight: It teaches you to recognize your presence in every moment of change and to bring both active effort and clear understanding to your actions.

shambhu_gita::956.verse_sanskrit:
उद्योगेषु च सर्वेषु विश्वकल्याणकारिषु ।
दण्डरूपो विमार्गिभ्यो गुणिभ्योऽस्म्यादरस्तथा ॥
shambhu_gita::956.verse_hindi: मैं जगत् के कल्याणकारी उद्योग, मै विपथगामी को दण्ड, गुणी का आदर,
shambhu_gita::956.english_translation: In all efforts for the welfare of the world, I am the discipline for the misguided and the respect for the virtuous.
shambhu_gita::956.translation_literal: उद्योगेषु (in efforts) च (and) सर्वेषु (all) विश्वकल्याणकारिषु (for world welfare) । दण्डरूपो (as discipline) विमार्गिभ्यो (to misguided) गुणिभ्यो (to virtuous) अस्मि (I am) आदरः (respect) तथा (also) ॥
shambhu_gita::956.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::956.essence: Firm discipline and respectful honor both serve the world's welfare.
shambhu_gita::956.simple_meaning: In every effort that helps the world, discipline corrects those who stray, and respect supports those with virtue.
shambhu_gita::956.simple_insight: You can be both firm and kind — correction and honor come from the same source.
shambhu_gita::956.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains his role in guiding the world: as a firm discipline to those who have lost their way, and as respectful support to those who live with virtue. This teaching shows how action balances firmness with honor.
shambhu_gita::956.modern_relevance: When you lead a team, you correct mistakes firmly but also honor those who do well, balancing care with accountability.
shambhu_gita::956.insight: It teaches you to balance firm correction with genuine respect in your actions toward others.

shambhu_gita::957.verse_sanskrit:
संयमो नियमश्चाहमास्तिक्यञ्चाऽस्मि भूतिदाः ।
श्वासप्रश्वासरूपेषु सुषुम्ना प्राणकर्मसु ॥
shambhu_gita::957.verse_hindi: संयम, नियम, और आस्तिकता हूं और श्वास प्रश्वास रूपी प्राणक्रिया में सुषुम्ना हूँ ।
shambhu_gita::957.english_translation: I am restraint, discipline, and faith, and the vital force in the breath's flow within the central channel.
shambhu_gita::957.translation_literal: संयमो (restraint) / नियमश्च (and discipline) / अहम् (I am) / आस्तिक्यञ्च (and faith) / अस्मि (am) / भूतिदाः (life-giving) / श्वासप्रश्वासरूपेषु (in the form of inhalation and exhalation) / सुषुम्ना (central energy channel) / प्राणकर्मसु (in vital actions)
shambhu_gita::957.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::957.essence: Discipline, faith, and life flow together as the vital breath within you.
shambhu_gita::957.simple_meaning: You are the power of self-control, daily discipline, and trust that fuels your life force and breath.
shambhu_gita::957.simple_insight: You carry steady strength and faith quietly flowing in every breath you take.
shambhu_gita::957.detailed_meaning: Shiva reveals his essence as the principles of restraint, discipline, and faith that sustain life, embodied in the subtle flow of breath through the vital energy channel called sushumna.
shambhu_gita::957.modern_relevance: When you pause and breathe deeply during stress, you feel the quiet strength of discipline and trust within you.
shambhu_gita::957.insight: Recognize yourself as the source of steady inner strength expressed through mindful control and trust in your life energy.

shambhu_gita::958.verse_sanskrit:
ऐश्वर्ययुक्तं यत्किञ्चित् सम्पत्त्या युक्तमेव वा ।
बलप्रभावादिगुणैः समृद्धं यद्यदेव हि ॥
shambhu_gita::958.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! जो कुछ ऐश्वर्ययुक्त, सम्पत्तियुक्त अथवा प्रभाव बल आदि गुण द्वारा समृद्ध
shambhu_gita::958.english_translation: O ancestors! Whatever is endowed with power, wealth, or qualities such as strength and influence is indeed prosperous.
shambhu_gita::958.translation_literal: ऐश्वर्ययुक्तं (endowed with power) / यत्किञ्चित् (whatever) / सम्पत्त्या (with wealth) / युक्तमेव (indeed endowed) / वा (or) / बलप्रभावादिगुणैः (by strength, influence, and qualities) / समृद्धं (prosperous) / यद्यदेव (whatever indeed)
shambhu_gita::958.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::958.essence: Prosperity is commonly seen as having power, wealth, and strong qualities.
shambhu_gita::958.simple_meaning: Anything that has power, wealth, or qualities like strength and influence is considered prosperous.
shambhu_gita::958.simple_insight: Prosperity is recognized through visible power and qualities, but this is only a surface view.
shambhu_gita::958.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the sages, describing prosperity as being linked to material wealth, power, and qualities like strength and influence, indicating an external view of success.
shambhu_gita::958.insight: It highlights how society often measures prosperity by external power and possessions, inviting reflection beyond appearances.

shambhu_gita::959.verse_sanskrit:
दृश्यते तद्विजानीत मद्विभूतिस्वरूपकम् ।
मां विभूतिषु पश्यन्तोऽनुक्षणं हे स्वधाभुजः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::959.verse_hindi: जहाँ जहाँ देखो वहीं मेरी विभूति है ऐसा जानना चाहिए। हे पितृगण ! आप लोग यदि हर समय मुझ को विभूतियों में दर्शन करते हुए
shambhu_gita::959.english_translation: Wherever you look, know that my manifestations exist there. O ancestors, if you constantly see me in all manifestations,
shambhu_gita::959.translation_literal: दृश्यते (is seen) तद् (that) विजानीत (should be known) मद् (my) विभूति (manifestations) स्वरूपकम् (form/essence) । / मां (me) विभूतिषु (in manifestations) पश्यन्तः (seeing) अनुक्षणं (constantly) हे (O) स्वधाभुजः (ancestors) ।
shambhu_gita::959.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::959.essence: The divine is always visible in all forms if you choose to see it.
shambhu_gita::959.simple_meaning: The divine is present everywhere you look in many forms. When you see constantly with this awareness, you recognize the sacred in all things.
shambhu_gita::959.simple_insight: You feel connected knowing the divine shows up in everything around you.
shambhu_gita::959.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, telling them that his divine presence appears in all forms everywhere. He asks them to recognize this constant presence to deepen their devotion and awareness.
shambhu_gita::959.modern_relevance: Walking through a bustling street or a quiet park, you glimpse the sacred in every face and leaf, feeling connected beyond the surface.
shambhu_gita::959.insight: It teaches you to shift from seeing separate things to seeing the divine essence in all forms around you.

shambhu_gita::960.verse_sanskrit:
यूयं चेन्मद्गतस्वान्ता अथवा पृजया मम ।
मत्परायणतामेत्य रताः कर्तव्यकर्माणि ॥
shambhu_gita::960.verse_hindi: मद्गतचित्त होकर अथवा ,मेरी पूजा द्वारा मत्परायण होकर अपने कर्तव्य कर्म में रत रहोगे
shambhu_gita::960.english_translation: Be absorbed in me or devoted by worship; with that devotion, engage fully in your duties.
shambhu_gita::960.translation_literal: यूयं (you) चेन् (if) मद्गतस्वान्ता (mind absorbed in me) अथवा (or) पृजया (by worship) मम (my) मत्परायणतामेत्य (with devotion to me) रताः (engaged) कर्तव्यकर्माणि (in duties to be done)
shambhu_gita::960.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::960.essence: Devotion to the divine supports wholehearted engagement in your duties.
shambhu_gita::960.simple_meaning: You can either keep your mind absorbed in me or show devotion through worship, and with that, fully engage in your duties.
shambhu_gita::960.simple_insight: Devotion does not pull you away from action; it deepens your engagement with what you must do.
shambhu_gita::960.detailed_meaning: Shiva instructs that whether you focus your mind inwardly on him or express devotion through worship, that dedication should empower you to perform your required duties without distraction or hesitation.
shambhu_gita::960.modern_relevance: When you deeply care about a purpose or value, it becomes easier to stay fully present and committed to your daily responsibilities.
shambhu_gita::960.insight: It shifts your action from mere obligation to a devoted offering, transforming how you experience duty.

shambhu_gita::961.verse_sanskrit:
भवेयुस्तहर्याविश्यं वो विश्वस्याभ्युदयस्य च ।
वहन्तो हेतुतामन्ते मां लभेध्वं न संशयः ॥
shambhu_gita::961.verse_hindi: तो अवश्य ही अपने तथा जगत के अभ्युदय के कारण होगे और अन्त में मुझको प्राप्त होगे, इसमें सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::961.english_translation: You will certainly become the cause of your own and the world's upliftment and ultimately reach me without doubt.
shambhu_gita::961.translation_literal: भवेयुः (you will become) तहर्य (cause) आविश्यं (certainly) वो (your) विश्वस्य (of the world) अभ्युदयस्य (upliftment) च (and) । वहन्तः (carrying) हेतुताम् (cause) अन्ते (in the end) मां (me) लभेध्वं (you will reach) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
shambhu_gita::961.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::961.essence: You become the cause of your and the world's rise and will surely reach the divine.
shambhu_gita::961.simple_meaning: You will definitely become the cause of your own and the world's growth and finally reach the divine without doubt.
shambhu_gita::961.simple_insight: You can trust that your efforts contribute to a greater upliftment and a clear goal.
shambhu_gita::961.detailed_meaning: Shiva assures that those who act with purpose become the driving cause for their own progress and the world's well-being, ultimately reaching the divine presence without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::961.modern_relevance: When you take responsibility for your actions, you influence not just your life but those around you, moving steadily toward your highest goal.
shambhu_gita::961.insight: It shifts your view to see personal effort as inseparable from collective upliftment and spiritual fulfillment.

shambhu_gita::962.verse_sanskrit:
एष चोपनिपत्सारोपदेशः श्रावितो मया ।
शम्भुगीतेतिनाम्नेयं गीता लोके प्रसेत्स्यति ॥
shambhu_gita::962.verse_hindi: मैंने उपनिषदों का साररूप, यह उपदेश तुमको सुनाया है। यह  गीता शम्भुगीता नाम से प्रसिद्ध होकर
shambhu_gita::962.english_translation: I have revealed the essence of the Upanishads; this teaching will be known in the world as the Shambhu Gita.
shambhu_gita::962.translation_literal: एष (this) च (also) उपनिपत्सारोपदेशः (essence-teaching) श्रावितो (heard) मया (by me) । शम्भुगीतेतिनाम्नेयं (named Shambhu Gita) गीता (song/teaching) लोके (in the world) प्रसेत्स्यति (will spread) ॥
shambhu_gita::962.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::962.essence: A timeless essence of ancient teachings is revealed anew as the Shambhu Gita.
shambhu_gita::962.simple_meaning: This teaching is the essence of the Upanishads, revealed here and destined to be known as the Shambhu Gita.
shambhu_gita::962.simple_insight: The deepest wisdom can be passed down in new forms, shining through time.
shambhu_gita::962.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares that he has spoken the core essence of the ancient Upanishads, presenting it freshly as the Shambhu Gita, which will spread widely.
shambhu_gita::962.insight: It shows how timeless wisdom can be re-expressed to remain alive and accessible.

shambhu_gita::963.verse_sanskrit:
कृत्वा त्रयाणां लोकानां मानाञ्च क्रमोन्नतिम् ।
धर्मज्ञानं यथार्थश्च तेषु प्रद्योतयिष्यति ॥
shambhu_gita::963.verse_hindi: त्रिलोक तथा मनुष्य जाति की क्रमोन्नति करके उसमें धर्म के यथार्थ ज्ञान का विकाश करे
shambhu_gita::963.english_translation: By uplifting the three worlds and humanity, it will illuminate the true knowledge of dharma within them.
shambhu_gita::963.translation_literal: कृत्वा (having done) / त्रयाणां (of the three) / लोकानां (worlds) / मानाञ्च (and of humans) / क्रमोन्नतिम् (the gradual uplift) / धर्मज्ञानं (knowledge of dharma) / यथार्थश्च (true/real) / तेषु (in them) / प्रद्योतयिष्यति (will illuminate)
shambhu_gita::963.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::963.essence: True dharma grows by uplifting all worlds and humanity together.
shambhu_gita::963.simple_meaning: You bring progress to the entire world and humanity by revealing the true understanding of dharma within them.
shambhu_gita::963.simple_insight: There is power in awakening true purpose that lifts not just you but everyone around you.
shambhu_gita::963.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks of elevating the three realms—physical, mental, and spiritual—and humanity by unfolding the real knowledge of dharma, guiding all toward authentic growth and order.
shambhu_gita::963.modern_relevance: When you help others find their true purpose, you contribute to a greater progress beyond yourself.
shambhu_gita::963.insight: It shifts focus from personal gain to inspiring collective growth through true dharma knowledge.

shambhu_gita::964.verse_sanskrit:
गीतेयं दैवतत्त्वेप्वविश्वस्तेभ्यः कदाचन ।
गुरुभक्तिविहीनेभ्यो विमुखेभ्यो मदेव हि ॥
shambhu_gita::964.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण ! यह गीता देव तत्वविश्वासहीन, गुरुभकिशन्य , मुझसे विमुख व्यक्ति
shambhu_gita::964.english_translation: O ancestors! This Gita is indeed meant for those who trust the divine reality, have devotion to the Guru, and are not turned away from me.
shambhu_gita::964.translation_literal: गीतेयं (this Gita) / दैवतत्त्वेप्व (in divine reality) / विश्वस्तेभ्यः (to those who trust) / कदाचन (at any time) / गुरुभक्तिविहीनेभ्यो (to those without devotion to the Guru) / विमुखेभ्यो (to those turned away) / मदेव (only from me) / हि (indeed)
shambhu_gita::964.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::964.essence: Deep teachings reveal themselves only to those with trust and devotion, not to the disconnected.
shambhu_gita::964.simple_meaning: This teaching is intended only for those who trust the divine reality, respect their Guru, and remain devoted to the speaker.
shambhu_gita::964.simple_insight: True learning opens only to those ready with trust and devotion, not to those who turn away.
shambhu_gita::964.detailed_meaning: Shiva addresses the ancestors, clarifying that the Gita's wisdom is meant for those who have faith in the divine reality, show devotion to their Guru, and remain connected to him, excluding those who lack these qualities.
shambhu_gita::964.modern_relevance: You won’t absorb deep guidance if you reject trusted teachers or lack faith in what’s greater than yourself.
shambhu_gita::964.insight: It teaches that readiness through trust and devotion is essential before profound teachings can be received and understood.

shambhu_gita::965.verse_sanskrit:
नास्तिकेभ्योऽशुचिभ्यश्च नैव देया स्वधाभुजः !।
गुरौ वेदेषु देवेषु विश्वासं ये प्रकुर्वते ॥
shambhu_gita::965.verse_hindi: अशुचि और परलोक पर विश्वास न रखनेवाले व्यक्ति को देने योग्य नहीं है।
shambhu_gita::965.english_translation: Those who do not trust the Guru, the Vedas, or the divine are not deserving of offerings.
shambhu_gita::965.translation_literal: नास्तिकेभ्यः (from those who do not believe) अशुचिभ्यः (and impure) च (and) नैव (not at all) देया (to be given) स्वधाभुजः (offerings) गुरौ (to the Guru) वेदेषु (in the Vedas) देवेषु (in the divine) विश्वासं (trust) ये (those who) प्रकुर्वते (make)
shambhu_gita::965.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::965.essence: True offerings require genuine trust in the teacher, scriptures, and the divine.
shambhu_gita::965.simple_meaning: Offerings should only be given to those who trust the Guru, sacred texts, and the divine.
shambhu_gita::965.simple_insight: Trust is the foundation that makes offerings meaningful and worthy.
shambhu_gita::965.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that offerings or gifts are meaningful only when given to those who have faith in the Guru, the Vedas, and the divine. Without this trust, giving is empty and undeserved.
shambhu_gita::965.modern_relevance: You hesitate to invest time or respect in someone who doubts the values or guidance you hold dear.
shambhu_gita::965.insight: It teaches you to look for genuine trust before offering your devotion or attention.

shambhu_gita::966.verse_sanskrit:
तेभ्यो जगत्यां भक्तेभ्यः सदाचारिभ्य एव तु ।
निःसन्देहं प्रदातव्या गीतेयं परमाद्भुता ॥
shambhu_gita::966.verse_hindi: सदाचारी, और गुरु देवता और वेद पर विश्वास रखनेवाले मेरे भक्तों को ही यह परम अद्भुत गीता देनी चाहिये
shambhu_gita::966.english_translation: This supreme and wondrous song should undoubtedly be given only to my devotees who are virtuous, revering gurus and the Vedas.
shambhu_gita::966.translation_literal: तेभ्यः (to them) जगत्यां (in the world) भक्तेभ्यः (to devotees) सदाचारिभ्य (to virtuous ones) एव (only) तु (indeed) निःसन्देहं (undoubtedly) प्रदातव्या (to be given) गीतेयं (this song) परमाद्भुता (supreme wondrous)
shambhu_gita::966.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::966.essence: Profound teachings are meant only for virtuous, devoted seekers who honor their guides.
shambhu_gita::966.simple_meaning: This supreme song should be given only to devotees who live virtuously and respect their teachers and scriptures.
shambhu_gita::966.simple_insight: Trust grows when teachings come from those who live what they teach and respect higher wisdom.
shambhu_gita::966.detailed_meaning: Shiva emphasizes that the highest, most wondrous teaching is meant only for those devoted souls who uphold virtuous conduct and honor their spiritual guides and sacred knowledge, highlighting the importance of readiness to receive deep wisdom.
shambhu_gita::966.insight: It encourages valuing integrity and respect as prerequisites for receiving deep teachings.

shambhu_gita::967.verse_sanskrit:
यत्र तिष्ठति गीतेयमङ्गोपाङ्गसमन्विता ।
अपयाति ततो बाधा तमः सूर्योदये यथा ॥
shambhu_gita::967.verse_hindi: यह गीता जिस स्थान पर रहेगी वहाँ से सभी प्रकार की बाधा ऐसे दूर हो जायगी जैसे सूर्य के प्रकाश होते ही अन्धकार दूर होजाता है
shambhu_gita::967.english_translation: Wherever this Gita resides, all obstacles vanish there like darkness at sunrise.
shambhu_gita::967.translation_literal: यत्र (where) तिष्ठति (resides) गीतेयम् (this Gita) अंगोपाङ्गसमन्विता (with all limbs/parts) अपयाति (goes away) ततो (therefrom) बाधा (obstacle) तमः (darkness) सूर्योदये (at sunrise) यथा (like)
shambhu_gita::967.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::967.essence: The presence of true wisdom dissolves all obstacles like sunlight dispels darkness.
shambhu_gita::967.simple_meaning: Wherever the wisdom of this Gita is present, all difficulties disappear as sunlight removes darkness.
shambhu_gita::967.simple_insight: You can feel safe and clear when true wisdom fills your space.
shambhu_gita::967.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how the presence of this teaching removes all troubles like the sun dispels night. This highlights the power of spiritual wisdom to clear confusion and hardship.
shambhu_gita::967.modern_relevance: You notice how a moment of clarity or a wise word can dissolve your worries like morning light chases away night.
shambhu_gita::967.insight: It teaches that wisdom's presence changes your environment by removing obstacles and confusion naturally.

shambhu_gita::968.verse_hindi: सन्ततिहीन व्यक्ति के लिये सुसन्तान प्राप्ति कारक,आसन्न प्रसवा स्त्रियों के लिये सर्वमङ्गल प्रद्
shambhu_gita::968.english_translation: For those without offspring, he grants good children; for women nearing birth, he is the cause of all auspiciousness.
shambhu_gita::968.translation_literal: निस्सन्तानजनेभ्यो (to people without children) हि (indeed) सुसन्तानप्रदायकः (giver of good children) । आसन्नमसवानाञ्च (and to women near delivery) सर्वमंगलकारकः (cause of all auspiciousness) ॥
shambhu_gita::968.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::968.essence: He brings children and blessings to those longing and those about to give birth.
shambhu_gita::968.simple_meaning: He grants children to those without them and brings all good things to women about to give birth.
shambhu_gita::968.simple_insight: There is hope and blessing even in difficult moments of longing and waiting.
shambhu_gita::968.detailed_meaning: Suta describes Shiva's power to bless childless people with offspring and to bring auspiciousness to women in labor, highlighting his role as a protector and benefactor in crucial life moments.
shambhu_gita::968.insight: Recognize that support and blessings arise in times of deep need and transition.

shambhu_gita::969.verse_sanskrit:
अस्याः पाठोऽस्ति रोगिभ्यो धन्वन्तरिसमो भुवि ।
नैवात्र विस्मया कार्यों भवद्भिः पितृपुङ्गवाः !॥
shambhu_gita::969.verse_hindi: और रोगी के लिये धन्वन्तरी सदृश इसका पाठ है, हे पितृवरो! इसमें आप विस्मय नहीं करें
shambhu_gita::969.english_translation: For the sick, this teaching is like Dhanvantari on earth; O noble ancestors, do not be amazed by it.
shambhu_gita::969.translation_literal: अस्याः (of this) पाठोऽस्ति (is the teaching) रोगिभ्यो (for the sick) धन्वन्तरिसमः (like Dhanvantari) भुवि (on the earth) । नैवात्र (not here) विस्मया (with amazement) कार्यः (to be done) भवद्भिः (by you) पितृपुङ्गवाः (O noble ancestors) ॥
shambhu_gita::969.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::969.essence: Healing teachings may seem surprising but serve to restore and comfort.
shambhu_gita::969.simple_meaning: This teaching is like a healing medicine for those who are suffering; don't be surprised by its effect.
shambhu_gita::969.simple_insight: Healing teachings may seem strange but are meant to help without shock.
shambhu_gita::969.detailed_meaning: Suta compares the teaching to Dhanvantari, the divine healer, telling the noble ancestors that this teaching cures like medicine. They are urged not to be surprised or doubtful about its power.
shambhu_gita::969.insight: It encourages openness to healing knowledge, even if it seems unusual or unexpected.

shambhu_gita::970.verse_sanskrit:
एतया पितरः ! शम्भुयागानुष्ठानतो ध्रुवम् ।
पाठतो होमतो वाऽपि यथाविधि निरन्तरम् ॥
shambhu_gita::970.verse_hindi: हे पितृगण! इस गीता के सम्बन्ध से यथाविधि हवनात्मक अथवा पाठात्मक शिवयज्ञ का अनुष्ठान समान रूप से
shambhu_gita::970.english_translation: O ancestors! By properly performing Shiva yajna, whether by reciting or offering fire according to the rules, you are certainly honored.
shambhu_gita::970.translation_literal: एतया (by this) / पितरः (ancestors) / शम्भुयागानुष्ठानतो (by performing Shiva yajna) / ध्रुवम् (certainly) / पाठतो (by reciting) / होमतो (by offering fire) / वा (or) अपि (also) / यथा (according to) / विधि (rules) / निरन्तरम् (continuously)
shambhu_gita::970.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::970.essence: Proper performance of Shiva yajna continuously honors the ancestors.
shambhu_gita::970.simple_meaning: Performing Shiva yajna properly—whether by reciting or offering fire—honors the ancestors consistently.
shambhu_gita::970.simple_insight: Honoring with devotion creates a continuous connection beyond words or rituals.
shambhu_gita::970.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the assembled sages, explaining how proper ritual acts dedicated to Shiva, like chanting or fire offerings, continuously honor the ancestors, emphasizing the power of disciplined ritual acts in the sacred tradition.
shambhu_gita::970.insight: It teaches that sincere, properly performed practices uphold respect and connection across time.

shambhu_gita::971.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्वर्गफलप्राप्तिर्जायते नात्र संशयः ।
विशेषतो गृहस्थानां नित्यपाठविधानतः ॥
shambhu_gita::971.verse_hindi: चतुर्वर्ग फलप्रद है,  विशेषतः हे पितृगण ! गृहस्थाश्रम के कल्याण चाहनेवाले इसके नित्यपाठ द्वारा
shambhu_gita::971.english_translation: There is no doubt that the fourfold goals are attained, especially by householders who regularly study this.
shambhu_gita::971.translation_literal: चतुर्वर्गफलप्राप्तिः (fourfold goals attainment) जायते (happens) नात्र (there is no) संशयः (doubt) । विशेषतः (especially) गृहस्थानां (of householders) नित्यपाठविधानतः (by regular study) ॥
shambhu_gita::971.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::971.essence: Consistent study ensures achieving life’s fourfold goals, especially for householders.
shambhu_gita::971.simple_meaning: Regular study of this text helps householders achieve the four important life goals without doubt.
shambhu_gita::971.simple_insight: Consistent practice supports clear progress toward meaningful aims.
shambhu_gita::971.detailed_meaning: The narrator states confidently that the four key goals of life are assuredly achieved, especially by those living as householders who engage in daily study of the teaching.
shambhu_gita::971.insight: Regular engagement with wise teachings strengthens steady progress toward life’s aims.

shambhu_gita::972.verse_sanskrit:
धनैश्वाणि पुत्राश्च कलत्रं शान्तिरेव च ।
प्रजायते न सन्देहः सत्यमेतत् स्वधाभुजः! ॥
shambhu_gita::972.verse_hindi: धन ऐश्वर्य पुत्र कला और शान्ति के अधिकारी होंगे इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं है।
shambhu_gita::972.english_translation: There is no doubt that wealth, power, children, art, and peace are all rightful possessions of the true self.
shambhu_gita::972.translation_literal: धनैश्वाणि (wealth and power) पुत्राश्च (and children) कलत्रं (art) शान्तिरेव (and peace indeed) च (also) प्रजायते (are born/arise) न (not) सन्देहः (doubt) सत्यमेतत् (this is true) स्वधाभुजः (of the true self/own being)!
shambhu_gita::972.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::972.essence: Wealth, family, talents, and peace naturally belong to your true self without doubt.
shambhu_gita::972.simple_meaning: You inherently deserve wealth, children, artistic skills, and peace as part of your true nature.
shambhu_gita::972.simple_insight: You can feel secure knowing these blessings are naturally part of who you are.
shambhu_gita::972.detailed_meaning: Shiva declares that wealth, power, offspring, artistic talents, and peace naturally arise as rightful qualities of the true self. This verse reassures that these are not random or external gifts but essential aspects of your nature.
shambhu_gita::972.modern_relevance: You may sometimes doubt your worthiness of success or peace, but this reminds you these are natural to your being.
shambhu_gita::972.insight: This shifts your view from scarcity to natural entitlement, encouraging confident, balanced action.

shambhu_gita::973.verse_sanskrit:
साधकानां निवृत्तानामस्याः पाठेन नित्यशः ।
तत्त्वज्ञानाधिकारित्वं स्यानिःश्रेयसमेव च ॥
shambhu_gita::973.verse_hindi: निवृत्तिमार्गगामी साधकगण इसके नित्यपाठ द्वारा तत्वज्ञान के अधिकारी होकर निःश्रेषस प्राप्त करेंगे
shambhu_gita::973.english_translation: Those practitioners who constantly study this will gain the right to true knowledge and attain the highest good.
shambhu_gita::973.translation_literal: साधकानाम् (of practitioners) निवृत्तानाम् (withdrawn) अस्याः (of this) पाठेन (by study) नित्यशः (constantly) तत्त्वज्ञानाधिकारित्वं (right to true knowledge) स्यान् (will be) अःश्रेयसम् (highest good) एव (only) च (and)
shambhu_gita::973.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::973.essence: Consistent study empowers seekers to claim true knowledge and reach the highest good.
shambhu_gita::973.simple_meaning: If you consistently study this teaching with dedication, you become qualified to truly understand reality and achieve the best outcome.
shambhu_gita::973.simple_insight: Steady dedication builds your right to deep understanding and lasting fulfillment.
shambhu_gita::973.detailed_meaning: Shiva instructs that practitioners who have turned away from distractions and engage in regular study of this teaching will rightfully gain deep wisdom and reach the highest benefit possible.
shambhu_gita::973.modern_relevance: You sit down every day to review your goals and values. This steady effort deepens your insight and moves you toward what truly matters.
shambhu_gita::973.insight: It encourages forming a consistent habit of study and reflection to claim the authority to understand and live wisely.

shambhu_gita::974.verse_sanskrit:
अस्याः पाठेन नारीणां सतीत्वं प्रणयोऽनघः ।
दम्पत्योः स्याद्यथाकामं ज्ञानवत्सन्ततिस्तथा ॥
shambhu_gita::974.verse_hindi: इसके पाठ द्वारा स्त्रियों में सतीत्वधर्म और दम्पति में पवित्र प्रेम की प्राप्ति होगी और पिता माता की इच्छा के अनुसार ज्ञानवान् सुसन्तति की उत्पत्ति होगी
shambhu_gita::974.english_translation: By studying this, women will cultivate devoted conduct, couples will nurture pure love, and parents will have a wise and desired offspring.
shambhu_gita::974.translation_literal: अस्याः (of this) / पाठेन (by the study) / नारीणां (of women) / सतीत्वं (devoted conduct) / प्रणयोऽनघः (pure love) / दम्पत्योः (of the couple) / स्याद्यथाकामं (may be as desired) / ज्ञानवत्सन्ततिस्तथा (and a wise offspring likewise)
shambhu_gita::974.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::974.essence: Family harmony grows from devotion, love, and wisdom fulfilled together.
shambhu_gita::974.simple_meaning: Learning this teaching will inspire women toward devoted behavior, couples toward pure love, and parents toward wise children as they wish.
shambhu_gita::974.simple_insight: There is harmony when family roles align with love and wisdom.
shambhu_gita::974.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that this teaching fosters respectful conduct among women, strengthens loving bonds in couples, and blesses parents with wise children, fulfilling family aspirations.
shambhu_gita::974.insight: It highlights how shared values in family nurture love and wisdom across generations.

shambhu_gita::975.verse_sanskrit:
प्रायशो वैदिका यागा लोपमेष्यन्त्यलं कलौ।
त्रिलौहनिम्मितं लिङ्गरूपं मे विग्रहं वरम् ॥
shambhu_gita::975.verse_hindi: कलियुग में प्राचीन वैदिक याग लुप्त प्राय हो जायंगे, उस समय यदि त्रिलौह निर्मित मेरे लिङ्गरूप विग्रह की
shambhu_gita::975.english_translation: In the age of Kali, ancient Vedic sacrifices will mostly disappear; at that time, my best form will be the symbol made of the three metals.
shambhu_gita::975.translation_literal: प्रायशः (mostly) वैदिका (Vedic) यागाः (sacrifices) लोपम (disappearance) एष्यन्ति (will happen) अलं (indeed) कलौ (in Kali age) । त्रि-लौ-ह-निम्मितं (made of three metals) लिङ्गरूपं (symbol form) मे (my) विग्रहं (form) वरम् (best) ॥
shambhu_gita::975.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::975.essence: When old rituals fade, new sacred symbols become the path to the divine.
shambhu_gita::975.simple_meaning: In the dark age, old Vedic rituals will mostly vanish, so the divine's symbol made of three metals will be the best way to worship.
shambhu_gita::975.simple_insight: Even when old ways fade, new forms arise to keep the divine close.
shambhu_gita::975.detailed_meaning: Shiva warns that in the Kali Yuga, traditional Vedic sacrifices will mostly disappear. Instead, He will be worshiped through a sacred symbol, a lingam made of three metals, which represents his best form for that time.
shambhu_gita::975.insight: It teaches that spiritual connection adapts with time, shifting from rituals to symbols.

shambhu_gita::976.verse_sanskrit:
स्थापयित्वा विधानेन तदा वै पितरो ध्रुवम् । 
ऋग्वेदसंहितास्वाहाकारेण सहितं खलु ॥
shambhu_gita::976.verse_hindi: स्थापना पूर्वक तब हे पितरों ऋग्वेद संहिता, स्वाहाकार सहित
shambhu_gita::976.english_translation: After establishing the proper ritual, the ancestors firmly performed it along with the Rigveda and the svaha utterance.
shambhu_gita::976.translation_literal: स्थापयित्वा (establishing) / विधानेन (by the procedure) / तदा (then) / वै (indeed) / पितरो (ancestors) / ध्रुवम् (firmly) / ऋग्वेदसंहितास्वाहाकारेण (with Rigveda collection and svaha utterance) / सहितं (together) / खलु (certainly)
shambhu_gita::976.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::976.essence: Ritual success depends on precise setup and faithful execution by predecessors.
shambhu_gita::976.simple_meaning: The ancestors firmly performed the ritual after setting it up properly, including chanting from the Rigveda and the svaha call.
shambhu_gita::976.simple_insight: Rituals rely on careful preparation and faithful performance by those before us.
shambhu_gita::976.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how the ancestors, after carefully setting the ritual procedure, performed it with certainty using the Rigveda hymns and the svaha invocation, emphasizing tradition and order.
shambhu_gita::976.insight: It shows the importance of preparation and respect for established practice in any meaningful work.

shambhu_gita::977.verse_sanskrit:
विष्णोः सूर्यस्य शक्तेश्च धीशस्यापि यथाविधि।
अस्याः शम्भोश्च गीताया हवनेन समन्वितम् ॥
shambhu_gita::977.verse_hindi: विष्णुगीता, सूर्यगीता,  शक्तिगीता, धीशगीता और इस शम्भुगीता के हवन के साथ
shambhu_gita::977.english_translation: Along with the offerings of Vishnu Gita, Surya Gita, Shakti Gita, and Dhi Gita, this Shambhu Gita is also presented.
shambhu_gita::977.translation_literal: विष्णोः (of Vishnu) / सूर्यस्य (of the sun) / शक्तेश्च (and of power) / धीशस्यापि (also of the lord of intellect) / यथाविधि (according to the method) / अस्याः (of this) / शम्भोश्च (of Shambhu) / गीताया (of the song) / हवनेन (with the offering) / समन्वितम् (accompanied)
shambhu_gita::977.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::977.essence: The Shambhu Gita is offered together with other sacred hymns in ritual.
shambhu_gita::977.simple_meaning: This verse says that the Shambhu Gita is offered along with other sacred hymns like Vishnu Gita and Surya Gita.
shambhu_gita::977.simple_insight: The verse highlights the Shambhu Gita's importance among revered sacred texts.
shambhu_gita::977.detailed_meaning: Suta is explaining that the Shambhu Gita is presented ceremonially alongside other famous sacred chants, showing its revered status among these spiritual songs.
shambhu_gita::977.insight: It shows how spiritual teachings are often honored together in a ritual context, emphasizing tradition and respect.

shambhu_gita::978.verse_sanskrit:
सप्तशत्यास्तथा देवीमाहात्म्यस्यापि निश्चितम् । 
सप्तभिर्ह्ववनैर्युक्तं साङ्गोपाङ्गैः समन्वितम् ॥
shambhu_gita::978.verse_hindi: देवीमाहात्म्य सप्तशती का हवन, इस प्रकार सप्त हवन समन्वित सांगोपांग
shambhu_gita::978.english_translation: The Devi Mahatmya's seven hundred verses include seven complete, interconnected havans.
shambhu_gita::978.translation_literal: सप्तशत्यास्तथा (seven hundred verses also) देवीमाहात्म्यस्यापि (of Devi Mahatmya also) निश्चितम् (certain) । सप्तभिर्ह्ववनैर्युक्तं (joined with seven havans) साङ्गोपाङ्गैः (interconnected) समन्वितम् (assembled) ॥
shambhu_gita::978.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::978.essence: The Devi Mahatmya unites seven hundred verses through seven connected sacred rituals.
shambhu_gita::978.simple_meaning: The Devi Mahatmya scripture contains seven hundred verses divided into seven connected sacred fire rituals.
shambhu_gita::978.simple_insight: Ancient teachings often organize wisdom through ritual and structure, connecting many parts into a whole.
shambhu_gita::978.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates that the Devi Mahatmya text is composed of seven hundred verses and includes seven distinct but linked fire rituals, emphasizing its structured spiritual practice.
shambhu_gita::978.insight: Recognize that deep teachings often come through layered, ritualized expressions, not just words alone.

shambhu_gita::979.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वधारकयागस्यानुष्ठानं मंगलालयम् ।
भक्ता मे ये करिष्यन्ति व्ययशाव्यविवर्जिताः ॥
shambhu_gita::979.verse_hindi: विश्वधारक याग का अनुष्ठान मेरा भक्त करेगा और साथ ही साथ व्ययशाट्यरहित होकर
shambhu_gita::979.english_translation: My devotees will perform the sacred sacrifice that upholds the universe without waste or excess.
shambhu_gita::979.translation_literal: विश्वधारकयागस्य (of the universe-upholding sacrifice) अनुष्ठानं (performance) मंगलालयम् (auspicious place) भक्ता (devotees) मे (my) ये (who) करिष्यन्ति (will do) व्ययशाव्यविवर्जिताः (without waste or excess)
shambhu_gita::979.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::979.essence: Devoted action performed without waste sustains the entire universe.
shambhu_gita::979.simple_meaning: Devotees who perform this sacred action do so without waste, supporting the universe with careful, meaningful effort.
shambhu_gita::979.simple_insight: There is dignity and power in devoted, efficient action that serves the greater whole.
shambhu_gita::979.detailed_meaning: Shiva teaches that performing the great universal sacrifice with devotion and without unnecessary waste is a sacred duty. Devotees who engage in this act contribute to sustaining cosmic order through mindful, purposeful action.
shambhu_gita::979.modern_relevance: You carefully prepare a meaningful offering or project, making sure no resources are wasted but everything serves a worthy purpose.
shambhu_gita::979.insight: It teaches you to engage fully in your responsibilities with devotion while avoiding needless excess or waste.

shambhu_gita::980.verse_sanskrit:
सत्कारं विदुषां सम्यगवाह्मणानाञ्च भोजनम् ।
यथेष्टदान-दीनेभ्यः कृत्वा यज्ञं परात्परम् ॥
shambhu_gita::980.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मण भोजन, विद्वान् ब्राह्मणों का सत्कार और दीन दरिद्रों को यथेष्ट दान करके
shambhu_gita::980.english_translation: Honor the wise with proper hospitality and offer alms to the poor; thus perform the highest sacrifice.
shambhu_gita::980.translation_literal: सत्कारं (hospitality) / विदुषां (of the wise) / सम्यक् (proper) / आह्मणानां (of Brahmins) / च (and) / भोजनम् (food) / यथेष्ट (as desired) / दान-दीनेभ्यः (to the poor needy) / कृत्वा (doing) / यज्ञं (sacrifice) / परात्परम् (highest)
shambhu_gita::980.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::980.essence: Highest sacrifice is honoring the wise and giving freely to those in need.
shambhu_gita::980.simple_meaning: Show respect to the wise with good hospitality and give what you can to the poor. This is the highest form of sacrifice.
shambhu_gita::980.simple_insight: There is dignity in honoring wisdom and generosity in helping those in need.
shambhu_gita::980.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shiva teaches that true sacrifice is not ritual alone, but respecting learned people with hospitality and sharing generously with the poor, blending social care with spiritual practice.
shambhu_gita::980.modern_relevance: You invite a mentor for a meal and donate to a shelter; these simple acts connect you to something greater.
shambhu_gita::980.insight: It shifts your focus from ritual formality to meaningful care expressed through respect and generosity.

shambhu_gita::981.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वधारकनामानं पूरयिष्यन्ति सर्वथा ।
स्वसङ्कल्पानुसारेण वैदिकानां फलं ध्रुवम् ॥
shambhu_gita::981.verse_hindi: विश्वधारक यज्ञ की समाप्ति करेगा तो उसके संकल्प के अनुसार
shambhu_gita::981.english_translation: Those who perform the universal-supporting sacrifice will surely fulfill the results according to their own resolve.
shambhu_gita::981.translation_literal: विश्वधारकनामानं (universal-supporting sacrifice) / पूरयिष्यन्ति (will fulfill) / सर्वथा (completely) / स्वसङ्कल्पानुसारेण (according to own resolve) / वैदिकानां (of the Vedic) / फलं (result) / ध्रुवम् (certain)
shambhu_gita::981.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::981.essence: Your deepest resolve directs the true outcome of your greatest actions.
shambhu_gita::981.simple_meaning: The results of a great, universal action depend fully on your own intention and resolve.
shambhu_gita::981.simple_insight: You have power in your intention; what you truly want shapes your outcomes.
shambhu_gita::981.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shiva explains that when someone completes a great universal sacrifice, the true effect they receive depends entirely on their own inner resolve, highlighting the power of personal intention behind actions.
shambhu_gita::981.modern_relevance: After finishing a big project or commitment, the outcome you experience is shaped by your own clear intention and focus.
shambhu_gita::981.insight: It teaches you to align your inner resolve clearly, knowing it directly influences the results you experience.

shambhu_gita::982.verse_sanskrit:
वाजपेयाश्वमेघादियज्ञानां महतामलम् ।
लप्स्यन्ते ते हि निर्बाधं सन्देहो नाऽत्र कश्चन ॥
shambhu_gita::982.verse_hindi: अश्वमेध वाजपेय आदि सभी प्रकार के वैदिक यज्ञों के
shambhu_gita::982.english_translation: Those who perform great Vedic sacrifices like Ashvamedha and Vajapeya attain their fruits without any doubt.
shambhu_gita::982.translation_literal: वाजपेयाश्वमेघादियज्ञानां (Vajapeya, Ashvamedha, and similar sacrifices) महताम् (of great) अलम् (collection) । लप्स्यन्ते (they attain) ते (those) हि (indeed) निर्बाधं (without obstacle) सन्देहो (doubt) नाऽत्र (not here) कश्चन (anyone) ॥
shambhu_gita::982.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::982.essence: Significant committed actions yield their results clearly and without doubt.
shambhu_gita::982.simple_meaning: Performing great Vedic sacrifices like Ashvamedha and Vajapeya leads to their fruits without any doubt or obstacle.
shambhu_gita::982.simple_insight: There is confidence in knowing sincere, large efforts bring clear results.
shambhu_gita::982.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shiva explains that performing great Vedic sacrifices such as Ashvamedha and Vajapeya guarantees their results without hesitation or doubt, affirming the certainty of sincere, committed action.
shambhu_gita::982.modern_relevance: You put in a big effort on an important project and feel certain it will pay off clearly and surely.
shambhu_gita::982.insight: It teaches you to trust that wholehearted, significant action produces definite results without uncertainty.

shambhu_gita::983.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञो दानञ्च तीर्थञ्च तपो वा तादृशं न हि ।
विश्वधारकयज्ञस्य यत् फलेन सम कलौ ॥
shambhu_gita::983.verse_hindi: फल की उसको प्राप्ति होगी, इसमे सन्देह नहीं
shambhu_gita::983.english_translation: Sacrifice, charity, pilgrimage, and austerity do not yield the fruit of the sacrifice that sustains the world in this age of decline.
shambhu_gita::983.translation_literal: यज्ञो (sacrifice) / दानञ्च (charity and) / तीर्थञ्च (pilgrimage and) / तपो (austerity) / वा (or) / तादृशं (such) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / विश्वधारकयज्ञस्य (of the world-sustaining sacrifice) / यत् (which) / फलेन (by the fruit) / सम (equal) / कलौ (in the age of decline)
shambhu_gita::983.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita::983.essence: Common spiritual acts no longer guarantee the true sustaining result in this age.
shambhu_gita::983.simple_meaning: Common acts like sacrifice, charity, pilgrimage, and austerity don’t produce the highest results in this age.
shambhu_gita::983.simple_insight: You learn that usual spiritual acts may not fulfill the deepest purpose now.
shambhu_gita::983.detailed_meaning: Shiva explains that in the current age of decline, traditional religious acts like sacrifice, charity, pilgrimage, and austerity no longer produce the full benefits they once did, especially the kind of results that uphold the world’s order.
shambhu_gita::983.modern_relevance: You’ve done all the usual good deeds, but still feel something essential is missing or unrewarded.
shambhu_gita::983.insight: It shifts your effort from just repeating rituals to pursuing deeper, sustaining action aligned with higher purpose.

shambhu_gita::984.verse_sanskrit:
भवेन्नैवात्र सन्देहः सत्यसमेतद्रवीमि वः ।
माहात्म्यं शम्भुगीताया मर्त्यलोके प्रचार्य वै ॥
shambhu_gita::984.verse_hindi: ऐसा कोई यज्ञ, ऐसा कोई तीर्थ और ऐसा कोई 'दान और तप नहीं है जिसके फल की तुलना कलियुग में इस विश्व धारक याग के साथ हो सकती हो, यही सत्य है ।
shambhu_gita::984.english_translation: There is no sacrifice, pilgrimage, donation, or austerity whose fruit compares to the world-sustaining sacrifice taught in the Shambhu Gita, this is the truth.
shambhu_gita::984.translation_literal: भवेत् (there is) नै (not) अत्र (here) सन्देहः (doubt) सत्यसमेत (with truth) द्रवीमि (I declare) वः (to you). माहात्म्यं (greatness) शम्भुगीताया (of Shambhu Gita) मर्त्यलोके (in the mortal world) प्रचार्य (spread) वै (indeed).
shambhu_gita::984.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::984.essence: The Shambhu Gita's teaching surpasses all rituals and austerities in true power.
shambhu_gita::984.simple_meaning: No ritual, pilgrimage, gift, or austerity matches the power of the sacrifice taught in the Shambhu Gita in this age.
shambhu_gita::984.simple_insight: True greatness comes from teachings that sustain the whole world, not just isolated acts.
shambhu_gita::984.detailed_meaning: Suta proclaims to the sages that no common religious acts in the mortal world can equal the greatness of the sacrifice described in the Shambhu Gita, emphasizing the unique power of this teaching in the current age.
shambhu_gita::984.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by countless self-improvement methods, recognize some teachings have greater impact than many scattered efforts.
shambhu_gita::984.insight: It highlights that some teachings or practices hold more transformative power than many others combined.

shambhu_gita::985.verse_sanskrit:
लोकद्वयस्य कल्याणं निष्पादयत कल्पदाः।
स्वयं कल्याणमाजश्च यूयं भवत सत्तमाः ! ॥
shambhu_gita::985.verse_hindi: हे श्रेष्ठ पितृगण ! आप इस गीता की महिमा मनुष्यलोक में प्रचारित करके उभय लोक का कल्याण साधन करें और स्वयं कल्याण को प्राप्त हो
shambhu_gita::985.english_translation: O noble ancestors! By spreading the greatness of this Gita among humans, bring welfare to both worlds and attain welfare yourselves.
shambhu_gita::985.translation_literal: लोकद्वयस्य (of both worlds) कल्याणं (welfare) निष्पादयत (bring about) कल्पदाः (O wish-fulfilling trees) । स्वयं (yourself) कल्याणमाजश्च (obtain welfare) यूयं (you all) भवत (become) सत्तमाः (best) !
shambhu_gita::985.speaker: Suta
shambhu_gita::985.essence: Sharing true wisdom blesses both others and yourself simultaneously.
shambhu_gita::985.simple_meaning: You can help both the human and higher realms by sharing this teaching and receive blessings yourself.
shambhu_gita::985.simple_insight: There is joy in knowing your good actions benefit many, including yourself.
shambhu_gita::985.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the venerable ancestors, urging them to spread the Gita's wisdom among humans. By doing so, they will promote well-being in both earthly and higher realms while also gaining blessings themselves.
shambhu_gita::985.modern_relevance: You post a helpful insight online, knowing your words can uplift many and bring you a quiet satisfaction.
shambhu_gita::985.insight: It invites you to share wisdom openly, trusting that spreading good benefits both others and yourself.

tirukkural::1.verse_sanskrit: Agara mudala ezhuththellam adi bagavan mutarrae ulagu.
tirukkural::1.verse_hindi: As the letter 'A' stands first among letters, so the primordial source stands first in the world.
tirukkural::1.english_translation: As the letter 'A' stands first among letters, so the primordial source stands first in the world.
tirukkural::1.translation_literal: Agara (the letter A) + mudala (first/beginning) + ezhuththellam (all letters); adi (primordial/foundational) + bagavan (the source/the exalted) + mutarrae (is the first/is the beginning) + ulagu (world/all things)
tirukkural::1.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::1.essence: Everything flows from its root; know yours first.
tirukkural::1.simple_meaning: Just as the letter 'A' is the foundation upon which all language rests, so there is a primordial ground upon which all of existence rests. Understanding your foundation — what your actions, values, and life are rooted in — is where all genuine endeavor begins.
tirukkural::1.simple_insight: Every structure needs a foundation, and every life needs a grounding principle. The Tirukkural opens by asking: before you say or do anything — what is yours?
tirukkural::1.detailed_meaning: The Tirukkural's very first verse uses a brilliant pedagogical device: the comparison to the letter 'A' (in Tamil, as in Sanskrit, the first vowel, the root of all speech). Just as A is present within every word even when not visible, the primordial source is present within all things. Thiruvalluvar is not making a theological claim so much as a structural one: everything that exists is grounded in something prior to itself. For the purposes of karma and action, this translates to: trace every act to its root, because the root determines the fruit.
tirukkural::1.modern_relevance: Systems thinkers speak of 'leverage points' — places in a system where a small shift produces large downstream effects. The deepest leverage point is always the foundational premise or purpose from which everything else flows. Thiruvalluvar opens the Tirukkural by pointing to exactly this: the ground before the first act. For leaders, practitioners, and anyone in a change process, this is the question that precedes all others.
tirukkural::1.insight: Before you build anything — a habit, a relationship, a business, a practice — the most important question is: what is this standing on?

tirukkural::2.verse_sanskrit: Kural 611: Uzhavarkku ezhupori ullo — tolil vinai seyya viruppe.
tirukkural::2.verse_hindi: Sustained effort is the seed of achievement; without it, even what you have will not stay.
tirukkural::2.english_translation: Sustained effort is the seed of achievement; without it, even what you have will not stay.
tirukkural::2.translation_literal: uzhaipavar (the industrious/those who work) + kai (hand/result) + urugum (will grow/will yield); seyvinam (the work done/the effort applied) + munnar (before/ahead) + thozhilai (one's work/craft) + vinai (action/effort)
tirukkural::2.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::2.essence: Effort does not end at success — it is how success continues.
tirukkural::2.simple_meaning: Effort is not a one-time cost you pay to acquire something. It is the ongoing requirement for both building and keeping. Those who work consistently accumulate; those who stop lose not only what they might have gained but what they already have.
tirukkural::2.simple_insight: Most people think effort is what you do before you succeed. Thiruvalluvar says effort is what you do before, during, and after — or you have not actually succeeded.
tirukkural::2.detailed_meaning: This kural addresses a common delusion: that success, once reached, is stable. Thiruvalluvar observes that wealth, skill, relationships, and reputation all require ongoing effort to maintain. The industrious person (uzhaipavar) does not rest on previous work — they continue, because they understand that all achievements are processes, not destinations. The verse is equally a warning and an encouragement: the path to losing what you have is the same path as never trying — inaction.
tirukkural::2.modern_relevance: Research on skill maintenance shows that expertise decays without deliberate practice. Relationship quality declines without continued investment. Financial health erodes without ongoing management. Even physical fitness reverts within weeks of stopping. Thiruvalluvar's observation is empirically precise: everything worth having requires continued effort to keep. This is not discouraging — it is a practical map of how achievement actually works.
tirukkural::2.insight: The person who works consistently is not doing more than the person who rests on results — they are doing the one thing that actually preserves the results.

tirukkural::3.verse_sanskrit: Kural 616: Aatruvaar aatral peridhu — aataamai maanilai il.
tirukkural::3.verse_hindi: The capable find a way through every obstacle. Ability is the one wealth that cannot be taken.
tirukkural::3.english_translation: The capable find a way through every obstacle. Ability is the one wealth that cannot be taken.
tirukkural::3.translation_literal: aatruvaar (those who are capable/those who can) + aatral (capability/strength) + peridhu (is great/is foremost); aataamai (incapability/inability) + maanilai (honorable state) + il (there is none/does not exist)
tirukkural::3.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::3.essence: True wealth is what you can do, not what you have.
tirukkural::3.simple_meaning: Those who cultivate genuine capability are never truly stuck — they can navigate any obstacle because they bring the capacity to engage with it. Among all forms of wealth, the ability to do is the most secure because it cannot be taken from you.
tirukkural::3.simple_insight: People obsess over outcomes and resources. Thiruvalluvar points to something prior: the capacity to work effectively. Cultivate that and outcomes follow. Neglect it and no amount of resources protects you.
tirukkural::3.detailed_meaning: Aatral (capability, strength, competence) is what Thiruvalluvar identifies as the highest form of wealth in the context of action. Unlike wealth, reputation, or social position, genuine capability is intrinsic — it cannot be confiscated, depreciated by market forces, or lost to the opinion of others. The verse also implies a principle of confidence: the capable person does not fear new situations because they trust their own ability to engage with whatever arises. This is a fundamentally different relationship with uncertainty than one based on the possession of fixed resources.
tirukkural::3.modern_relevance: Economic research on long-term prosperity increasingly focuses on human capital — skills, adaptability, and learning capacity — as the most durable form of wealth in rapidly changing economies. People who lose jobs but have strong capabilities find new ones; those whose identity is tied to a specific position often cannot. Thiruvalluvar identified this principle millennia ago, pointing to capability as the form of wealth that provides real security.
tirukkural::3.insight: The most anxious people are often the most externally successful — because their security is in what they have, not in what they can do. This kural says: invest in what you are capable of.

tirukkural::4.verse_sanskrit: Kural 31: Azhukkarumbu aanaathal ulpada — naanudaiyaar naanku ini.
tirukkural::4.verse_hindi: Whatever harm or shame may come, never violate the code of right conduct.
tirukkural::4.english_translation: Whatever harm or shame may come, never violate the code of right conduct.
tirukkural::4.translation_literal: azhukku (harm/wrongdoing) + arumbu (difficulty/suffering) + aanaathal (even if it becomes) + ula (while existing) + pada (even if it falls/befalls); naanudaiyaar (those who have honor/those of integrity) + naanku (even so/still) + ini (henceforth) + [will not violate right conduct]
tirukkural::4.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::4.essence: Real integrity holds its shape even under pressure.
tirukkural::4.simple_meaning: A person of genuine integrity does not abandon right conduct when circumstances make it difficult or costly. The real test of values is not whether you hold them when it is easy — it is whether you hold them when it hurts.
tirukkural::4.simple_insight: Anyone can be ethical when it costs nothing. What Thiruvalluvar is pointing to is the integrity that holds even when it is inconvenient, costly, or painful. That is the only integrity that counts.
tirukkural::4.detailed_meaning: This kural is in the chapter on 'Naanudaimai' — possessing honor or moral integrity. The verse acknowledges the reality: harm and shame may come anyway — life does not exempt the ethical person from difficulty. But the one who genuinely has integrity does not use difficulty as a justification for abandoning right conduct. The conditional framing is important: Thiruvalluvar is not naive about the costs of virtue. He is saying that those costs, however real, do not justify crossing the line.
tirukkural::4.modern_relevance: Research on organizational ethics consistently finds that the most common rationalization for wrongdoing is situational — 'this time is different,' 'the pressure is too great,' 'everyone does it.' Thiruvalluvar anticipates exactly this rationalization and pre-empts it: the situation being difficult is not a valid reason. Individuals and organizations that cultivate situation-independent integrity consistently outperform those that treat ethics as conditional.
tirukkural::4.insight: The person who compromises under pressure reveals that their integrity was always conditional. This kural is about building integrity that is not conditional.

tirukkural::5.verse_sanskrit: Kural 391: Katka kasadara kattu — kattathu kattaraa vidal.
tirukkural::5.verse_hindi: Learn what is worth learning. Having learned it, act on it without fail.
tirukkural::5.english_translation: Learn what is worth learning. Having learned it, act on it without fail.
tirukkural::5.translation_literal: katka (learn/study) + kasadara (without fault/thoroughly/well) + kattu (having learned/after learning); kattathu (what was learned) + kattaraa (not failing/without fail) + vidal (living it/practicing it/releasing it into action)
tirukkural::5.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::5.essence: Learning not acted on is just decoration.
tirukkural::5.simple_meaning: Choose learning carefully — pursue what is genuinely worth knowing, and pursue it thoroughly. But the second instruction is equally important and often harder: once you have learned something worth knowing, act on it. The learning is not complete until it becomes action.
tirukkural::5.simple_insight: Most people believe their problem is that they don't know enough. Thiruvalluvar identifies the deeper problem: what you already know, you are not living. More knowledge will not fix that.
tirukkural::5.detailed_meaning: Kasadara (without fault, without defect) modifies katka — the instruction is not to accumulate knowledge indiscriminately, but to learn what is worth learning and to learn it well. The second line, kattaraa vidal, is the knife-edge: having learned it, live it without exception. Thiruvalluvar's formulation implies that the purpose of learning is action — knowledge that produces no change in conduct has not been truly learned. This makes 'learning' much more than an intellectual activity; it is a commitment to embodiment.
tirukkural::5.modern_relevance: Behavioral research on the 'knowing-doing gap' — the persistent distance between what people know they should do and what they actually do — is one of the most studied phenomena in organizational psychology. Access to information has never been greater; rates of behavior change remain stubbornly modest. This kural names the problem with precision: learning is incomplete until it changes what you do. The discipline of closing the gap is the actual practice.
tirukkural::5.insight: The hardest part of learning is not understanding — it is the moment you have to live differently because of what you now understand.

tirukkural::6.verse_sanskrit: Kural 203: Tham paavam thamakke aru — tham pavamae thammai visum.
tirukkural::6.verse_hindi: When no one is watching, the inner record-keeper still is. Every action registers — the conscience forgets nothing.
tirukkural::6.english_translation: When no one is watching, the inner record-keeper still is. Every action registers — the conscience forgets nothing.
tirukkural::6.translation_literal: tham (one's own) + paavam (harmful act/wrong) + thamakke (to oneself) + aru (harm/suffering it brings); tham (one's own) + pavamae (the act itself) + thammai (one's self) + visum (harms/wounds/strikes back)
tirukkural::6.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::6.essence: The inner witness sees everything — and never forgets.
tirukkural::6.simple_meaning: Actions that appear to harm only others always leave a mark on the one who performs them. The conscience — the inner awareness — is an observer that forgets nothing. Harm done 'in private' is never truly private because the self that did it must continue living with the self that observed it.
tirukkural::6.simple_insight: People distinguish between actions that others see and actions no one sees. Thiruvalluvar says that distinction is an illusion. The most important witness is the one that cannot be removed from the room.
tirukkural::6.detailed_meaning: This kural operates on two levels. Literally, it says that wrongdoing returns to harm the doer — the inner consequence of harmful action. But more subtly, it points to the mechanism: the inner observer (the conscience, awareness, the part of the mind that knows what it has done) carries every act forward. There is no clean slate through concealment. The psychological burden of hidden wrongdoing — heightened vigilance, reduced cognitive resources, diminished self-respect — is well-documented. Thiruvalluvar frames this not as moralistic judgment but as simple observation of how consciousness works.
tirukkural::6.modern_relevance: Research on moral disengagement and self-deception shows that while people can rationalize individual acts, the cumulative psychological cost of continued wrongdoing appears in anxiety, reduced trust in one's own judgment, and impaired decision-making. The 'inner witness' may not use moralistic language, but it records. Integrity research consistently links honesty — especially when no one is watching — to psychological well-being.
tirukkural::6.insight: Privacy from others is not privacy from yourself. The one witness you can never remove is you.

tirukkural::7.verse_sanskrit: Kural 601: Iddanmaiyin illaamai thondraa — mudippaanavaangum mudiye.
tirukkural::7.verse_hindi: Treat idleness as an enemy and action as a friend. What looks like rest may be the slowest form of ruin.
tirukkural::7.english_translation: Treat idleness as an enemy and action as a friend. What looks like rest may be the slowest form of ruin.
tirukkural::7.translation_literal: iddanmaiyin (from laziness/from inactivity) + illaamai (poverty/lack/nothingness) + thondraa (does not arise/does not appear); mudippaanavaangum (one who can accomplish/capable person) + mudiye (must strive/must initiate)
tirukkural::7.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::7.essence: Idleness costs everything; action costs only effort.
tirukkural::7.simple_meaning: Idleness is not neutral — it is actively working against you. The capable person recognizes this and treats disciplined action not as an obligation but as the natural posture of a life that intends to stay whole.
tirukkural::7.simple_insight: Rest is necessary. Idleness is not rest — it is drift. Thiruvalluvar is pointing to the difference: one restores capacity, the other quietly erodes it.
tirukkural::7.detailed_meaning: This kural is from the chapter on 'Iddanmai' — laziness or idleness. Thiruvalluvar's treatment is characteristically practical: he identifies idleness not as a moral failure but as a strategic one. The capable person (mudippaanavaangum) must initiate — must begin, must stay in motion. The second line implies that the cost of idleness is not dramatic collapse but slow diminishment: poverty, lack, and absence of what could have been. The warning is against comfortable passivity dressed as wisdom or patience.
tirukkural::7.modern_relevance: Behavioral economics identifies 'status quo bias' — the tendency to maintain the current state rather than act — as one of the most powerful forces in human decision-making. Combined with the compounding nature of inaction (small missed opportunities that accumulate into significant gaps), the cost of habitual idleness is enormous and largely invisible until late. This kural treats that bias as an adversary to be recognized and countered.
tirukkural::7.insight: Idleness is a quiet thief. It takes slowly enough that you rarely notice what's gone until you look back.

tirukkural::8.verse_sanskrit: Kural 628: Adharkku avan allaal aLikkum — poruthaar poraadavar.
tirukkural::8.verse_hindi: Bearing insult without retaliating is harder and greater than any austerity. Real strength is what stays quiet.
tirukkural::8.english_translation: Bearing insult without retaliating is harder and greater than any austerity. Real strength is what stays quiet.
tirukkural::8.translation_literal: adharkku (for that/to that) + avan (that person) + allaal (than/other than); aLikkum (grants/gives/is generous with) + poruthaar (those who endure/those who bear patiently) + poraadavar (those who do not fight/those who do not retaliate)
tirukkural::8.speaker: Thiruvalluvar
tirukkural::8.essence: Enduring without breaking — that is the deepest practice.
tirukkural::8.simple_meaning: Enduring provocation, insult, or injury without retaliation is a form of inner discipline greater than any external practice. What looks like inaction is, in fact, the highest form of self-mastery.
tirukkural::8.simple_insight: Retaliation is the easy response — it requires no self-mastery, only reactivity. Not retaliating, when you have the capacity to, is the harder and rarer achievement.
tirukkural::8.detailed_meaning: This kural is from the chapter on 'Poraiyudaimai' — the quality of forbearance or fortitude. Thiruvalluvar's comparison is striking: bearing insult without retaliation is presented as greater than any tapas (austerity). This inverts the conventional hierarchy that prizes external spiritual practice. Why? Because the discipline required to hold equanimity in the face of direct provocation — when every instinct calls for response — is more total and more demanding than any voluntary discomfort one takes on in a controlled setting. Genuine equanimity is tested by exactly the situations where it is most difficult to maintain.
tirukkural::8.modern_relevance: Research on self-regulation shows that inhibiting an automatic response (retaliation, reactive speech, emotional escalation) is metabolically and cognitively demanding — it draws on the same finite resources as any demanding task. The ability to consistently inhibit reactive responses under provocation is one of the strongest predictors of leadership effectiveness, relationship quality, and psychological well-being. This kural validates that capacity as the highest form of inner practice.
tirukkural::8.insight: Anyone can be peaceful when unchallenged. The kural says the one who stays peaceful when directly provoked has achieved something that controlled conditions cannot teach you.

vishnu_gita::1.verse_sanskrit:
यदुक्तं भवता देव ! भगवान् विश्वपालकः।
अपूर्वचिन्मयज्योतीरूपः पूर्ण प्रकाशितः ॥
vishnu_gita::1.verse_hindi: हे देव ! आपने जो कहा कि विश्वपालक,अपूर्व चिन्मय ज्योति रूप, पूर्ण प्रकाशमान श्रीभगवान् ने
vishnu_gita::1.english_translation: O Deva! What you have spoken about is the supreme being, the protector of the universe, uniquely conscious and fully radiant.
vishnu_gita::1.translation_literal: यदुक्तं (what was spoken) भवता (by you) देव (O Deva) ! भगवान् (the supreme being) विश्वपालकः (protector of the universe) अपूर्वचिन्मयज्योतीरूपः (unique conscious light form) पूर्ण (complete) प्रकाशितः (illuminated)
vishnu_gita::1.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::1.essence: The supreme being is uniquely conscious, radiant, and the protector of all.
vishnu_gita::1.simple_meaning: You spoke about the supreme being who protects the world and shines with a unique conscious light.
vishnu_gita::1.simple_insight: Acknowledging the divine as uniquely radiant invites reverence and awe.
vishnu_gita::1.detailed_meaning: In this part, Suta addresses the sages, referring to the divine as described earlier: the supreme protector with a unique conscious, radiant form. It sets a tone of respect and wonder for the teachings that follow.
vishnu_gita::1.insight: It reminds you to recognize and respect the vastness and uniqueness of the divine presence around you.

vishnu_gita::2.verse_sanskrit:
देवलोके हि देवानां भयं सत्यमनाशयत् ।
इच्छामस्तत्समाकर्ण्य वयमाप्तुं कृतार्थताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::2.verse_hindi: देवलोक में देवताओं को भय से मुक्त किया, यह सत्य है परन्तु हम उस वृतांत को सुनकर कृतार्थता को प्राप्त करना चाहते हैं।
vishnu_gita::2.english_translation: It is true that in the divine realm the radiant beings were freed from fear, but we desire to hear that and attain complete fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::2.translation_literal: देवलोके (in the divine realm) / हि (indeed) / देवानां (of the radiant beings) / भयं (fear) / सत्यम् (true) / अनाशयत् (was removed) / इच्छामः (we desire) / तत् (that) / समाकर्ण्य (hearing carefully) / वयम् (we) / आप्तुम् (to attain) / कृतार्थताम् (fulfillment)
vishnu_gita::2.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::2.essence: Hearing how radiant beings overcame fear inspires our desire for fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::2.simple_meaning: The divine beings in their realm are free from fear, and we want to hear about this to feel fulfilled.
vishnu_gita::2.simple_insight: We seek reassurance and fulfillment by learning how fear is overcome.
vishnu_gita::2.detailed_meaning: The verse reflects on the divine realm where radiant beings have cast off fear, expressing a wish to hear such truths and gain fulfillment from them.
vishnu_gita::2.insight: It invites you to listen deeply to truths that can free you from fear and bring fulfillment.

vishnu_gita::3.verse_hindi: मन बुद्धि और वचन से अतीत, चिन्मय ज्योति, प्रकाशमान, कृपालु, परमपुरुष जो आविर्भूत हुए थे वे कौन थे
vishnu_gita::3.english_translation: Who is this supreme being, beyond mind, intellect, and speech, radiant with conscious light and full of compassion?
vishnu_gita::3.translation_literal: मन (mind) / बुद्धि (intellect) / वचः (speech) / अतीतः (beyond) / च (and) / चिन्मय (consciousness-filled) / ज्योतिः (light) / उज्ज्वलः (radiant) / परमः (supreme) / पुरुषः (being) / कः (who) / असौ (that) / आविरासीत् (manifested) / कृपानिधिः (full of compassion)
vishnu_gita::3.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::3.essence: A radiant, compassionate supreme being transcends mind, intellect, and speech.
vishnu_gita::3.simple_meaning: The verse wonders about a supreme being who is beyond mind, intellect, and speech, shining with conscious light and full of compassion.
vishnu_gita::3.simple_insight: There is awe and curiosity toward a being beyond all mental faculties and full of radiant compassion.
vishnu_gita::3.detailed_meaning: Vishnu contemplates a supreme being who transcends ordinary mental faculties and speech, shining with pure consciousness and abundant compassion, evoking wonder about the source of such divine qualities.
vishnu_gita::3.insight: It invites shifting focus from surface thoughts to the radiant conscious source beyond all mental activity.

vishnu_gita::4.verse_sanskrit:
देवानामुपदेशैः कैः स निराकृतवान्भयम् ।
कृपया श्रावयित्वा तद्धन्यानस्मान् कुरु प्रभो ! ॥
vishnu_gita::4.verse_hindi: और किन उपदेशों के द्वारा उन्होंने देवताओं के भय का निराकरण किया था, वह कृपया सुना कर हे प्रभो! हमलोगों को धन्य कीजिए
vishnu_gita::4.english_translation: By which teachings did he remove the gods' fear? Kindly tell us, Lord, and make us blessed.
vishnu_gita::4.translation_literal: देवानामुपदेशैः (by the teachings of the gods) कैः (by whom) स (he) निराकृतवान्भयम् (removed the fear) । कृपया (by kindness) श्रावयित्वा (having told) तद्धन्यानस्मान् (that blessed us) कुरु (do) प्रभो (O Lord) ॥
vishnu_gita::4.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::4.essence: A request to learn which teaching removed fear and brought blessing.
vishnu_gita::4.simple_meaning: They ask the Lord to kindly explain which teachings removed the gods' fear and blessed them.
vishnu_gita::4.simple_insight: There is a humble request for guidance to overcome fear and receive blessings.
vishnu_gita::4.detailed_meaning: The sages ask the Lord Vishnu to explain how he removed the gods' fear through his teachings, seeking blessings through this knowledge.
vishnu_gita::4.insight: It encourages seeking clarity from the divine to overcome fear and find strength.

vishnu_gita::5.verse_sanskrit:
द्वन्द्वात्मकोऽस्ति सर्गोऽयं दिवा रात्र्या च सन्ततम् ।
प्रभया तमसा चाऽपि ज्ञानतोऽज्ञानतो यथा ॥
vishnu_gita::5.verse_hindi: जैसे दिन और रात, प्रकाश और अन्धकार, ज्ञान और अज्ञान आदि से यह संसार निरन्तर द्वन्द्वात्मक है
vishnu_gita::5.english_translation: This world continuously exists as pairs of opposites: day and night, light and darkness, knowledge and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::5.translation_literal: द्वन्द्वात्मकोऽस्ति (is full of pairs of opposites) / सर्गोऽयं (this creation) / दिवा (day) / रात्र्या (night) / च (and) / सन्ततम् (always) / प्रभया (with light) / तमसा (with darkness) / चाऽपि (also) / ज्ञानतोऽज्ञानतो (from knowledge and from ignorance) / यथा (just as).
vishnu_gita::5.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::5.essence: Life continuously unfolds as a play of opposing forces in constant balance.
vishnu_gita::5.simple_meaning: The world you live in is always made of opposing pairs like day and night or knowledge and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::5.simple_insight: You can find peace accepting that life naturally contains opposites that flow continuously.
vishnu_gita::5.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the entire world is woven from continuous pairs of opposites—day and night, light and darkness, knowledge and ignorance—showing how duality forms the fabric of experience.
vishnu_gita::5.modern_relevance: When you face conflicting emotions or decisions, remember that life naturally swings between opposites, making balance a constant challenge.
vishnu_gita::5.insight: Recognize that opposing forces are natural and necessary, helping you accept fluctuations without resistance.

vishnu_gita::6.verse_sanskrit:
सुखदुःखादिभिः सम्यक् स्थूलसूक्ष्मात्मकं खलु ।
ब्रह्माण्डञ्च सदा व्याप्तमनुभूतञ्च भावुकैः ॥
vishnu_gita::6.verse_hindi: वैसे ही स्थूलसूक्ष्मात्मक और अनुभव करने वालों के द्वारा अनुभूत यह ब्रह्माण्ड सदा सुख दुःखादि से सम्यक् परिव्याप्त है
vishnu_gita::6.english_translation: The vast universe, both gross and subtle, is always pervaded completely by experiences of pleasure and pain.
vishnu_gita::6.translation_literal: सुखदुःखादिभिः (by pleasures and pains etc.) / सम्यक् (completely) / स्थूलसूक्ष्मात्मकं (gross and subtle in nature) / खलु (indeed) / ब्रह्माण्डञ्च (the universe) / सदा (always) / व्याप्तम् (pervaded) / अनुभूतञ्च (experienced) / भावुकैः (by experiencers)
vishnu_gita::6.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::6.essence: Every part of existence is always experienced through joy and suffering together.
vishnu_gita::6.simple_meaning: Everything in the universe, both visible and invisible, is always experienced through feelings of happiness and sadness.
vishnu_gita::6.simple_insight: You can feel connected knowing that joy and pain are universal experiences.
vishnu_gita::6.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the universe, including all gross and subtle forms, is always filled with experiences of pleasure and pain felt by living beings, showing the shared nature of existence.
vishnu_gita::6.modern_relevance: When you notice your own ups and downs, remember that all life experiences these feelings constantly, not just you alone.
vishnu_gita::6.insight: It teaches you to see pleasure and pain as part of the universal experience, not personal exceptions.

vishnu_gita::7.verse_sanskrit:
सामञ्जस्यं तथा  सृष्टेर्गत्या द्वन्द्वस्वरूपया।
समन्तात्सवर्वथा पातुं सुरा अप्यसुरा अपि ॥
vishnu_gita::7.verse_hindi: इस संसार का  स्वरूप द्वन्द्वमय होने के कारण सृष्टिकी समता को सब ओर और सब तरह से रक्षा करने के लिये देवता और असुर अति यत्न से
vishnu_gita::7.english_translation: Because the world is inherently full of dualities, both the deities and the shadow beings strive intensely to protect cosmic balance everywhere and in every way.
vishnu_gita::7.translation_literal: सामञ्जस्यं (harmony) तथा (thus) सृष्टेर्गत्या (by the course of creation) द्वन्द्वस्वरूपया (having the nature of duality) समन्तात् (from all sides) सर्वथा (in every way) पातुं (to protect) सुरा (deities) अपि (also) असुरा (shadow beings) अपि (also)
vishnu_gita::7.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::7.essence: Opposites work together to protect harmony throughout the world.
vishnu_gita::7.simple_meaning: The world is full of opposing forces, so both radiant and shadow beings work hard to keep harmony everywhere.
vishnu_gita::7.simple_insight: Even opposing forces play a role in maintaining balance, showing unity beneath conflict.
vishnu_gita::7.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the world as inherently consisting of opposing forces. Both deities and shadow beings exert great effort to maintain cosmic harmony on all sides, emphasizing the balance underlying apparent conflict.
vishnu_gita::7.insight: It shifts the view from seeing conflict as purely negative to recognizing its role in sustaining overall balance.

vishnu_gita::8.verse_sanskrit:
दैवे जगति लिप्सन्ते प्रभुत्वमतियत्नतः।
सुरासुरविरोधस्तत्सूक्ष्मे जगति सर्वदा ॥
vishnu_gita::8.verse_hindi: दैवजगत में अपने अपने प्रभुत्व को चाहते हैं इसी कारण सूक्ष्म जगत् में देवता और असुरो का सर्वदा विरोध रहता है
vishnu_gita::8.english_translation: In the divine world, each desires dominance, which causes the subtle realm to always have conflict between radiant beings and shadow beings.
