vishnu_gita::60.insight: It invites you to trust a source beyond your own confusion and fears, allowing those fears to diminish through that trust.

vishnu_gita::61.verse_sanskrit:
तथोपदेशं याचामो ज्ञातुं स्म ञ्च तत्त्वतः ।
त्वां शताः स्मो यथा मोहे न पतामः पुनः क्वचित् ॥
vishnu_gita::61.verse_hindi: ऐसे उपदेश की हम आपसे याचना करते हैं जिससे हम आपको तत्त्वरूप से जानने को और स्मरण करने को समर्थ हो सकें और पुनः कभी मोह में नहीं पड़ें
vishnu_gita::61.english_translation: We earnestly seek your teaching that helps us truly know and remember you, so we never fall into delusion again.
vishnu_gita::61.translation_literal: तथोपदेशं (such teaching) / याचामो (we request) / ज्ञातुं (to know) / स्म (indeed) / ञ्च (and) / तत्त्वतः (truly) / त्वां (you) / शताः (hundreds) / स्मो (we) / यथा (so that) / मोहे (in delusion) / न (not) / पतामः (we fall) / पुनः (again) / क्वचित् (ever)
vishnu_gita::61.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::61.essence: True teaching frees you from confusion by enabling lasting knowledge and remembrance.
vishnu_gita::61.simple_meaning: We ask for a teaching that helps us truly understand and remember the divine so we never get lost in confusion again.
vishnu_gita::61.simple_insight: There is hope in seeking wisdom that frees you permanently from confusion.
vishnu_gita::61.detailed_meaning: Suta requests a teaching from Vishnu that allows clear understanding and lasting remembrance, aiming to avoid falling into delusion again, showing the quest for clarity and devotion.
vishnu_gita::61.modern_relevance: You long for guidance that helps you understand something deeply and never forget it, so confusion no longer clouds your mind.
vishnu_gita::61.insight: It teaches you to seek knowledge that sticks and protects against repeated confusion.

vishnu_gita::62.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वासो नो ध्रुवो जातो यत्त्वां संस्मरतां सदा ।
अस्माकं निखिला भीतिस्तापोऽभावश्च नक्ष्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::62.verse_hindi: हम लोगों को ठीक विश्वास हो गया है कि आपको सदा स्मरण करने से हमारे सब भय, त्रिविध ताप और अभाव नाश हो जायेंगे
vishnu_gita::62.english_translation: We have firm trust that always remembering you will destroy all our fears, triple sufferings, and lacks.
vishnu_gita::62.translation_literal: विश्वासो (trust) / नो (our) / ध्रुवो (firm) / जातो (has arisen) / यत् (that) / त्वां (you) / संस्मरतां (always remembering) / सदा (always) / अस्माकं (our) / निखिला (all) / भीति (fear) / स्तापः (sufferings) / अभावः (lack) / च (and) / नक्ष्यति (is destroyed)
vishnu_gita::62.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::62.essence: Steady trust in the divine through constant remembrance removes all fears and lacks.
vishnu_gita::62.simple_meaning: You develop a strong trust that always remembering the divine will remove all your fears, sufferings, and deficiencies.
vishnu_gita::62.simple_insight: Trusting deeply that devotion protects you brings calm and relief from inner troubles.
vishnu_gita::62.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker expresses growing confidence that sustained devotion and remembrance of the divine will eliminate all fears and pains that trouble them, marking a turning point from doubt to unwavering faith.
vishnu_gita::62.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by worries and challenges, simply holding trust in a steady caring presence can ease your inner struggles and bring comfort.
vishnu_gita::62.insight: It teaches you to cultivate unwavering faith through steady remembrance, which dissolves fear and suffering over time.

vishnu_gita::63.verse_sanskrit:
त्वां सदा स्मरतां नूनमुद्यमो नः फलिष्यति।
सर्वे मनोरथाः सिद्धा भविष्यन्ति नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
vishnu_gita::63.verse_hindi: आपको सदा स्मरण करनेसे निश्चय ही हमारा पुरुषार्थ सफल होगा और हमारे सभी मनोरथ सिद्ध होंगे, आपको प्रणाम है
vishnu_gita::63.english_translation: By always remembering you, our efforts will surely succeed, and all our desires will be fulfilled; salutations to you.
vishnu_gita::63.translation_literal: त्वां (you) / सदा (always) / स्मरतां (remembering) / नूनम् (certainly) / उद्यमो (effort) / नः (our) / फलिष्यति (will bear fruit) / सर्वे (all) / मनोरथाः (desires) / सिद्धाः (fulfilled) / भविष्यन्ति (will become) / नमः (salutations) / अस्तु (let it be) / ते (to you)
vishnu_gita::63.speaker: Devotee (Unknown)
vishnu_gita::63.essence: Constant remembrance of the divine guarantees that your efforts will succeed and wishes fulfill.
vishnu_gita::63.simple_meaning: If you always keep the divine in your thoughts, your efforts will succeed and your wishes will come true.
vishnu_gita::63.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing consistent remembrance empowers your efforts to bear fruit.
vishnu_gita::63.detailed_meaning: A devotee expresses that constant remembrance of the divine ensures success in all endeavors and fulfillment of desires, showing the power of devotion amid life's challenges.
vishnu_gita::63.modern_relevance: You face a tough project but find strength by recalling what grounds you; this steadies your effort and opens possibilities.
vishnu_gita::63.insight: It teaches you to anchor your actions in steady remembrance, transforming effort into assured success.

vishnu_gita::64.verse_sanskrit:
युष्माकं स्तुतिभिर्देवाः ! प्रसन्नोऽस्मि ततस्त्वहम् ।
श्रेयसे वो यथायोग्यं ब्रवीमि वचनं शुभम् ॥
vishnu_gita::64.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! मैं तुम्हारी स्तुति से प्रसन्न हुआ इस कारण तुम्हारे कल्याण के लिये मैं यथायोग्य शुभ वचन कहता हूँ
vishnu_gita::64.english_translation: O radiant beings, I am pleased by your praise; therefore, I speak auspicious words for your well-being.
vishnu_gita::64.translation_literal: युष्माकं (your) / स्तुतिभिः (by praises) / देवाः (divine beings) / प्रसन्नः अस्मि (I am pleased) / ततः (therefore) / त्वम् (I) / श्रेयसे (for well-being) / वः (your) / यथा (as) / योग्यं (appropriate) / ब्रवीमि (I speak) / वचनं (words) / शुभम् (auspicious)
vishnu_gita::64.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::64.essence: Praise opens the way for blessings and well-being.
vishnu_gita::64.simple_meaning: The divine being feels pleased by your praise and responds by sharing appropriate blessings for your good.
vishnu_gita::64.simple_insight: Gratitude and praise open the way for blessings and well-being.
vishnu_gita::64.detailed_meaning: The divine being expresses pleasure at the praises offered by the radiant beings and promises to speak auspicious words for their benefit, setting a tone of blessing before teaching.
vishnu_gita::64.insight: It shows how acknowledging appreciation can open a heart to respond with care and positivity.

vishnu_gita::65.verse_sanskrit:
सदाचारच्युता यूयं भवथ स्म दिवौकसः।
स्वकर्तव्यं स्वधर्मश्च भवन्तो व्यहमरच्छुभम् ॥
vishnu_gita::65.verse_hindi: तुम लोग सदाचारभ्रष्ट हो गये हो इस कारण तुम मंगलमय निज कर्त्तव्य और स्वधर्मा को भूल गये हो
vishnu_gita::65.english_translation: You have fallen from righteous conduct and therefore forgotten your own duty and true purpose.
vishnu_gita::65.translation_literal: सदाचारच्युता (fallen from righteous conduct) / यूयं (you) / भवथ (have become) / स्म (indeed) / दिवौकसः (mortal beings) / स्वकर्तव्यं (own duty) / स्वधर्मश्च (and own purpose) / भवन्तो (you) / व्यहमरच्छुभम् (have forgotten)
vishnu_gita::65.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::65.essence: Losing sight of your duty means losing your way in life.
vishnu_gita::65.simple_meaning: You have abandoned good conduct and forgotten your own duty and life purpose.
vishnu_gita::65.simple_insight: There is a quiet ache in realizing when you’ve lost your way in what matters.
vishnu_gita::65.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu points out how the listeners, once following righteous conduct, have fallen into confusion and forgotten their personal duties and deeper life purpose, creating a crisis that requires realignment.
vishnu_gita::65.modern_relevance: You’ve been so caught up in distractions that your core responsibilities and values have slipped from view.
vishnu_gita::65.insight: It shifts your focus from external chaos back to your personal responsibility and authentic purpose.

vishnu_gita::66.verse_sanskrit:
अत एव समाक्रामच्चित्तं वो मोहज भयम् ।
त्तापोऽयोग्यप्र्वार्त्युत्थोऽभावो मत्स्मृतिनाशत: ॥
vishnu_gita::66.verse_hindi: इसी से तुम्हारे चित्त पर मोह जनित भय, अयोग्य- प्रवृत्ति जनित ताप और मेरे विस्मरण जनित अभाव, इन सभी ने अधिकार कर लिया है
vishnu_gita::66.english_translation: Because of this, your mind is overwhelmed by delusion-born fear, pain from unworthy actions, and absence caused by forgetting me.
vishnu_gita::66.translation_literal: अत (therefore) एव (indeed) समाक्रामत् (has overwhelmed) चित्तं (mind) वो (your) मोहज (born of delusion) भयम् (fear) । त्तापः (pain) अयोग्य प्रवर्त्त्य (from unworthy actions) उत्पन्नः (arisen) अभावः (absence) मत् (of me) स्मृति (memory) नाशतः (from destruction) ॥
vishnu_gita::66.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::66.essence: Fear and pain arise when you forget your true self and act from confusion.
vishnu_gita::66.simple_meaning: Your mind is overwhelmed by fear caused by confusion, pain from unworthy actions, and emptiness from forgetting your true self.
vishnu_gita::66.simple_insight: There is a deep ache when you lose connection with your true self and get trapped in fear and pain.
vishnu_gita::66.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that Arjuna's mind is overwhelmed by fear born of confusion, suffering caused by wrong actions, and a sense of loss from forgetting the divine presence within him. This moment reveals how losing sight of the true self causes inner turmoil.
vishnu_gita::66.modern_relevance: You’ve felt trapped by anxiety and regret after acting against your values, while feeling disconnected from your deeper source of strength.
vishnu_gita::66.insight: It teaches you to recognize that fear and pain arise from losing touch with your true nature and acting out of confusion.

vishnu_gita::67.verse_hindi: यदि तुम आचारवान् होने से कर्तव्य परायण, स्वधर्मनिरत और मद्गतचित्त हो सकोगे
vishnu_gita::67.english_translation: If you become disciplined, devoted to your duty, absorbed in your own dharma, then you will surely succeed.
vishnu_gita::67.translation_literal: यूयाम् (you) आचार (discipline) च (and) चेत् (if) स्वक (own) कर्तव्य (duty) परायणा: (devoted) स्वधर्म (own duty) निरताश्चाऽपि (engaged also) भवितुं (to become) खलु (indeed) शक्ष्यथ (you will be able)
vishnu_gita::67.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::67.essence: Dedication and discipline in your own duty are the surest paths to success.
vishnu_gita::67.simple_meaning: When you live with discipline, focus on your responsibilities, and stay true to your purpose, success follows.
vishnu_gita::67.simple_insight: There's confidence in knowing steady effort and commitment lead you forward.
vishnu_gita::67.detailed_meaning: Vishnu encourages the listener to cultivate discipline and unwavering dedication to their personal duty, emphasizing that such focus leads to assured success in life's tasks.
vishnu_gita::67.modern_relevance: You wake up and follow your daily routine with quiet focus, knowing this steady path moves you towards your goals.
vishnu_gita::67.insight: It teaches you to anchor your energy in consistent discipline and devotion to your chosen role, fostering progress.

vishnu_gita::68.verse_sanskrit:
माञ्चित्ताश्चेत्तदा यूयं भयात्तापादभावतः ।
विमुक्ताः सर्वकल्याणं लप्स्यध्वे मत्प्रसादतः ॥
vishnu_gita::68.verse_hindi: तभी भय और ताप मुक्त होकर सभी  प्रकार के अभाव को दूर करते हुए मेरी कृपा से यावत् मङ्गल लाभ करोगे
vishnu_gita::68.english_translation: Then, freed from fear and suffering, you will attain all kinds of welfare by my grace.
vishnu_gita::68.translation_literal: माञ्चित्ताः (mind restrained) / चेत्तदा (then if) / यूयं (you) / भयात् (from fear) / तापात् (from suffering) / अभावतः (from absence/lack) / विमुक्ताः (freed) / सर्वकल्याणं (all welfare) / लप्स्यध्वे (will attain) / मत् (my) / प्रसादतः (grace/favour)
vishnu_gita::68.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::68.essence: Releasing fear and pain invites divine grace that grants complete well-being.
vishnu_gita::68.simple_meaning: When you free your mind from fear and suffering, you will receive all kinds of well-being through my grace.
vishnu_gita::68.simple_insight: You can feel safe and cared for even in hardship through trust in the divine's grace.
vishnu_gita::68.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu assures that by releasing fear and pain, the listener will be embraced by divine grace, gaining complete well-being that overcomes all lack and hardship.
vishnu_gita::68.modern_relevance: When anxiety and pain weigh you down, trusting a deeper source can bring unexpected ease and support.
vishnu_gita::68.insight: It teaches you to release fear and suffering to open up to compassionate support beyond your control.

vishnu_gita::69.verse_sanskrit:
आचारः सर्वकल्याणमूलं नूनं दिवौकसः !॥
शक्ष्यन्त्याचारवन्तो हि प्राप्तुं कल्याणसम्पदः ॥
vishnu_gita::69.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! आचार ही सब कल्याणों का मूल है आचारवान ही सब कुछ प्राप्त कर सकते हैं
vishnu_gita::69.english_translation: O divine beings! Conduct is indeed the root of all welfare; those with good conduct attain all prosperity.
vishnu_gita::69.translation_literal: आचारः (conduct) सर्वकल्याणम्ूलं (root of all welfare) नूनं (indeed) दिवौकसः (divine beings) ! / शक्ष्यन्ति (attain) आचारवन्तः (those with conduct) हि (indeed) प्राप्तुं (to obtain) कल्याणसम्पदः (all prosperity) ॥
vishnu_gita::69.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::69.essence: Good conduct is the true root of all lasting welfare and prosperity.
vishnu_gita::69.simple_meaning: Good conduct is the foundation of every blessing and prosperity in life. Only those who live with proper conduct truly gain lasting welfare.
vishnu_gita::69.simple_insight: You feel grounded knowing that your way of living shapes your well-being deeply.
vishnu_gita::69.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, teaching that the way one lives—their conduct—is the source of all true benefits and blessings. This moment highlights that inner discipline and behavior shape the entire outcome of one's life.
vishnu_gita::69.modern_relevance: You notice how your daily choices and behavior set the tone for your success and happiness, even beyond what you expect.
vishnu_gita::69.insight: It teaches you to focus on cultivating consistent good conduct to unlock lasting prosperity, not just chasing results.

vishnu_gita::70.verse_sanskrit:
आचारमूला जातिः स्यादाचारः शास्त्रमूलकः।
वेदवाक्यं शास्त्रमूलं वेदः साधकमूलकः ॥
vishnu_gita::70.verse_hindi: जाति आचार मूलक होती है, प्राचार शास्त्र मूलक होता है, शास्त्र का मूल वेदवाक्य है, वेद का मूल साधक है
vishnu_gita::70.english_translation: Conduct is the root of caste, conduct is based on scripture, scripture is rooted in the Vedic statement, and the Veda's root is the practitioner.
vishnu_gita::70.translation_literal: आचारमूला (conduct root) जातिः (caste) स्यादाचारः (conduct is) शास्त्रमूलकः (based on scripture)। वेदवाक्यं (Vedic statement) शास्त्रमूलं (scripture's root) वेदः (Veda) साधकमूलकः (practitioner's root) ॥
vishnu_gita::70.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::70.essence: Your true role arises from your conduct, rooted in practice beyond scripture.
vishnu_gita::70.simple_meaning: Your behavior defines your social role. This behavior is based on scripture, scripture is based on Vedic teachings, and those teachings are based on the person who practices them.
vishnu_gita::70.simple_insight: Your daily actions and practice ultimately shape your identity more than labels or texts.
vishnu_gita::70.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that social identity (caste) starts with one's conduct, which itself is grounded in scriptural teachings. These scriptures rest on Vedic statements, but ultimately all depend on the practitioner's consistent practice.
vishnu_gita::70.modern_relevance: When you consistently live your values, your true role emerges beyond titles or external labels.
vishnu_gita::70.insight: It shifts focus from external labels to how your consistent behavior and practice shape your true role.

vishnu_gita::71.verse_sanskrit:
साधकश्च क्रियामूलः क्रियाऽपि फलमूलिका।
फलमूलं सुखं देवाः ! सुखमानन्दमूलकम् ॥
vishnu_gita::71.verse_hindi: साधक की मूल क्रिया है, क्रिया का मूल फल है, हे देवगण ! फल का मूल सुख है, सुख का मूल आनन्द है,
vishnu_gita::71.english_translation: The root of a seeker is action; the root of action is its result; the root of result is happiness; and the root of happiness is bliss.
vishnu_gita::71.translation_literal: साधकश्च (seeker also) क्रियामूलः (root of action) क्रियाऽपि (action also) फलमूलिका (root of result) । फलमूलं (root of result) सुखं (happiness) देवाः (O divine beings) ! सुखमानन्दमूलकम् (root of happiness is bliss) ॥
vishnu_gita::71.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::71.essence: Action is the foundation that ultimately leads to bliss through results and happiness.
vishnu_gita::71.simple_meaning: Your efforts start with taking action, which leads to results, then to happiness, and finally to deep joy.
vishnu_gita::71.simple_insight: You feel encouraged knowing every step in action leads toward lasting joy.
vishnu_gita::71.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to seekers that their practice begins with intentional action, which produces results. Those results bring happiness, and at the core of happiness lies bliss — the highest joy beyond ordinary pleasure.
vishnu_gita::71.modern_relevance: You finish a challenging task and feel a small happiness, which can deepen into a profound satisfaction beyond momentary pleasure.
vishnu_gita::71.insight: It shifts your focus to see action as the starting point for a chain leading to true joy, making effort feel meaningful.

vishnu_gita::72.verse_sanskrit:
आनन्दो ज्ञानमूलस्तु ज्ञानं वै ज्ञेयमूलकम् ।
तत्त्वमूलं ज्ञेयमानं तत्वं हि ब्रह्ममूलकम् ॥
vishnu_gita::72.verse_hindi: आनन्द का मूल ज्ञान है, ज्ञान का मूल ज्ञेय है, सकल ज्ञेयों का मूल तत्व है, तत्त्व का मूल ब्रह्म है,
vishnu_gita::72.english_translation: Bliss is rooted in knowledge; knowledge is rooted in the known; the source of all known is the essence; the essence's root is the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::72.translation_literal: आनन्दो (bliss) ज्ञानमूलः (root of knowledge) तु (indeed) ज्ञानं (knowledge) वै (certainly) ज्ञेयमूलकम् (root of the known) तत्त्वमूलं (root of essence) ज्ञेयमानं (that which is known) तत्वं (essence) हि (indeed) ब्रह्ममूलकम् (root of supreme reality)
vishnu_gita::72.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::72.essence: Bliss flows from the essence that underlies knowledge and all that is known.
vishnu_gita::72.simple_meaning: Bliss arises from knowledge, knowledge comes from what is understood, and all understanding is rooted in the essential reality beneath everything.
vishnu_gita::72.simple_insight: Joy feels deeper and more lasting when connected to the true foundation of all understanding.
vishnu_gita::72.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the layered roots of experience: bliss depends on knowledge, knowledge depends on what is known, and what is known ultimately depends on the essential reality, Brahman. This verse unfolds the foundational structure of awareness.
vishnu_gita::72.modern_relevance: When you feel true happiness, it’s often because you understand something real beneath surface distractions, not just facts or fleeting emotions.
vishnu_gita::72.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing facts to connecting with the deeper essence behind all knowledge and joy.

vishnu_gita::73.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मज्ञानं त्वैक्यमूलमैक्यं स्यात्सर्वमूलकम् ।
ऐक्यं तद्धि सुपर्वाणः ! भावातीतं सुनिश्चितम् ॥
vishnu_gita::73.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मज्ञान का मूल ऐक्य है और ऐक्य सबका मूल है, हे देवगण ! वही ऐक्य भावातीत है यह निश्चित है
vishnu_gita::73.english_translation: The root of supreme knowledge is unity, and unity is the root of all; that unity is beyond all emotions and certain, O divine beings!
vishnu_gita::73.translation_literal: ब्रह्मज्ञानं (supreme knowledge) / त्वैकमूलम् (root is unity) / ऐक्यं (unity) / स्यात् (exists) / सर्वमूलकम् (root of all) / ऐक्यं (unity) / तद्धि (that indeed) / सुपर्वाणः (O divine beings) / भावातीतं (beyond emotions) / सुनिश्चितम् (certain)
vishnu_gita::73.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::73.essence: True knowledge is rooted in an unchanging unity beyond all emotions.
vishnu_gita::73.simple_meaning: The deepest knowledge comes from understanding that everything ultimately unites into one, which is beyond any feelings or emotions.
vishnu_gita::73.simple_insight: There's peace in realizing that true knowledge is found in the unchanging unity beyond emotions.
vishnu_gita::73.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches divine beings that the ultimate knowledge, Brahmajnana, comes from realizing the oneness underlying everything. This unity is beyond emotional states and is absolutely certain, pointing to an unchanging reality behind all appearances.
vishnu_gita::73.modern_relevance: When emotions feel overwhelming, you can find steady ground by sensing the unity that connects all things beyond those feelings.
vishnu_gita::73.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing changing feelings to resting in the unchanging unity that underlies all experience.

vishnu_gita::74.verse_sanskrit:
भावातीतमिदं सर्वे प्रकाशये भावमात्रकम ।
नास्त्यत्र संशय: को पि सत्यं सत्यं वदाम्यहम ॥
vishnu_gita::74.verse_hindi: यह सकल संसार प्रकाश रूप से केवल भावमय है परन्तु वस्तुतः भावातीत है, इसमें कोई भी सन्देह नहीं है मैं सत्य सत्य कहता हूँ
vishnu_gita::74.english_translation: All this universe appears as pure light filled only with feeling, yet truly it is beyond feeling; there is no doubt in this, I speak the truth.
vishnu_gita::74.translation_literal: भावातीतमिदं (beyond feeling this) / सर्वे (all) / प्रकाशये (as light) / भावमात्रकम (only consisting of feeling) / नास्त्यत्र (there is not there) / संशय: (doubt) / को (anyone) / पि (at all) / सत्यं (truth) / सत्यं (truth) / वदाम्यहम (I speak)
vishnu_gita::74.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::74.essence: Everything appears as feeling but is truly beyond all feeling.
vishnu_gita::74.simple_meaning: The entire world looks like it is made of light and feeling, but actually it goes beyond any feeling or emotion.
vishnu_gita::74.simple_insight: There's a quiet depth beneath every feeling that nothing can touch or change.
vishnu_gita::74.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that although the universe appears as light filled with feelings, its true nature transcends all emotions and sensations. This teaching invites Arjuna to see beyond appearances to the unchanging reality beneath.
vishnu_gita::74.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by emotions or sensory overload, remember that beneath all feelings there is a calm space that stays untouched.
vishnu_gita::74.insight: It shifts your mind to recognize that appearances of feelings do not define the ultimate nature of reality.

vishnu_gita::75.verse_sanskrit:
अज्ञानदेव भीतीनामुत्पत्तिजायते सुरा : ।
अज्ञानमेव जन्तूनां हेतुस्तापत्रयस्य वै ॥
vishnu_gita::75.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! अज्ञान से ही भय की उत्पत्ति होती है, अज्ञान ही त्रिताप का कारण है
vishnu_gita::75.english_translation: O divine beings, ignorance alone gives rise to fear; ignorance is the cause of the threefold suffering.
vishnu_gita::75.translation_literal: अज्ञानदेव (ignorance alone) / भीतीनाम् (of fears) / उत्पत्ति (origin) / जायते (arises) / सुरा (O divine beings) / अज्ञानम् (ignorance) / एव (alone) / जन्तूनाम् (of beings) / हेतुः (cause) / तापत्रयस्य (of threefold suffering) / वै (indeed)
vishnu_gita::75.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::75.essence: Fear and suffering arise only from ignorance, not from reality itself.
vishnu_gita::75.simple_meaning: Fear and suffering arise from ignorance. When you do not understand, fear appears along with pain.
vishnu_gita::75.simple_insight: Knowing this brings relief: fear is not real but a product of misunderstanding.
vishnu_gita::75.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings explaining that ignorance is the root cause of fear and the three kinds of suffering, highlighting how misunderstanding traps beings in distress.
vishnu_gita::75.modern_relevance: You feel anxious because you don’t see the full picture; confusion feeds your worries and suffering.
vishnu_gita::75.insight: Recognize that fear and suffering are symptoms of ignorance, shifting your focus toward gaining clear understanding.

vishnu_gita::76.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानेन रहिता जीवा: साधुसैभाग्यवंचिता: ।
द्रष्टुं स्मर्तृञ्च मां नित्यं कदाचिदपि नेशते ॥
vishnu_gita::76.verse_hindi: ज्ञानरहित जीव सौभाग्य से वञ्चित हैं और वह मेरे दर्शन लाभ करने में और यहां तक कि मेरे स्मरण करने तक में असमर्थ होते हैं।
vishnu_gita::76.english_translation: Beings without wisdom are deprived of good fortune; they cannot perceive or even remember me.
vishnu_gita::76.translation_literal: ज्ञानेन (by wisdom) / रहिता (deprived) / जीवा: (beings) / साधुसैभाग्यवंचिता: (deprived of good fortune) / द्रष्टुं (to see) / स्मर्तृञ्च (and to remember) / मां (me) / नित्यं (always) / कदाचिदपि (at any time) / नेशते (are not able)
vishnu_gita::76.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::76.essence: Without wisdom, beings fail to perceive or remember the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::76.simple_meaning: Without wisdom, beings lose their chance to connect with the divine and cannot see or remember it.
vishnu_gita::76.simple_insight: There is sadness in being unable to recall or perceive what matters most.
vishnu_gita::76.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that beings who lack wisdom are unfortunate because they cannot perceive or even remember the divine presence, missing the chance for true connection and understanding.
vishnu_gita::76.modern_relevance: You might know something valuable but without clear understanding, you fail to fully appreciate or remember it when it matters.
vishnu_gita::76.insight: It teaches you to cultivate wisdom so you can recognize and hold onto what truly matters.

vishnu_gita::77.verse_sanskrit:
नूनं कर्तव्यनिष्ठो यो निजधर्मपरायणः ।
ज्ञानवान्स भयान्मुक्तः सयमेव ब्रवीमि वः ॥
vishnu_gita::77.verse_hindi: परन्तु मैं तुम्हें सत्य कहता हूँ कि जो कर्तव्यनिष्ठ और स्वधर्मपरायण होते हैं वह अतिसुगमता से ही आत्मज्ञान लाभ करके भयमुक्त हो जाते हैं
vishnu_gita::77.english_translation: But I tell you truly, those devoted to their duty and their own path easily attain self-knowledge and become free from fear.
vishnu_gita::77.translation_literal: नूनं (indeed) कर्तव्यनिष्ठो (devoted to duty) यो (who) निजधर्मपरायणः (devoted to own dharma) । ज्ञानवान्स (knowledgeable) भयान्मुक्तः (fearless) सयमेव (certainly) ब्रवीमि (I say) वः (to you) ॥
vishnu_gita::77.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::77.essence: Steadfast commitment to your true duty naturally brings fearless self-knowledge.
vishnu_gita::77.simple_meaning: Fully committing to your own duty leads naturally to clear understanding and freedom from fear.
vishnu_gita::77.simple_insight: There's confidence in knowing that staying true to your path dissolves fear.
vishnu_gita::77.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when a person dedicates themselves firmly to their immediate duty and their unique life path, they gain clear self-knowledge and lose fear. This moment follows the call for action rooted in dharma amid life's challenges.
vishnu_gita::77.modern_relevance: You face a tough choice at work or home and feel stuck; focusing on what you truly must do clears confusion and calms anxiety.
vishnu_gita::77.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing outcomes to trusting steady commitment to your purpose.

vishnu_gita::78.verse_sanskrit:
तापत्रयं न शक्नोति कदाचित् स्प्रष्टुमेव तम् ।
अचिरेणैव कालेन स मुक्तिमधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::78.verse_hindi: पुनः त्रिताप उनको स्पर्श नहीं कर सकता और वह शीघ्र ही मुक्ति को प्राप्त करते हैं
vishnu_gita::78.english_translation: One who is beyond the threefold suffering can never be touched by it and soon attains freedom.
vishnu_gita::78.translation_literal: तापत्रयं (threefold suffering) / न (not) / शक्नोति (can) / कदाचित् (ever) / स्प्रष्टुमेव (to touch even) / तम् (that) / अचिरेणैव (very soon) / कालेन (by time) / स (he) / मुक्तिमधिगच्छति (attains freedom)
vishnu_gita::78.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::78.essence: Freedom comes swiftly when suffering can no longer touch you.
vishnu_gita::78.simple_meaning: If you rise above the three kinds of suffering, they can no longer affect you, and you quickly reach freedom.
vishnu_gita::78.simple_insight: There’s peace in knowing pain cannot truly touch your deeper being.
vishnu_gita::78.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that those who transcend the threefold suffering—physical, mental, and spiritual pain—are untouched by it and soon gain liberation, highlighting the power of detachment and understanding in overcoming life’s struggles.
vishnu_gita::78.modern_relevance: When overwhelming stress or pain hits, you can find refuge in the part of you that remains untouched, moving you toward freedom.
vishnu_gita::78.insight: This verse shifts the mind from fearing pain to recognizing your deeper self beyond suffering.

vishnu_gita::79.verse_sanskrit:
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाजज्ञानाद्धयानं विशिष्यते ।
ध्यानात् कर्मफलसागस्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥
vishnu_gita::79.verse_hindi: अभ्यास की अपेक्षा ज्ञान श्रेष्ठ है, ज्ञान से ध्यान विशेष माना गया है, ध्यान से कर्मफलों का त्याग श्रेष्ठ है और त्याग के अनंतर ही शान्ति होती है
vishnu_gita::79.english_translation: Practice is inferior to wisdom; wisdom excels over ignorance. Meditation surpasses wisdom; renouncing the fruits of action is higher than meditation. Beyond renunciation alone lies peace.
vishnu_gita::79.translation_literal: श्रेयो (better) हि (indeed) ज्ञानमभ्यासात् (than practice/wisdom) अज्ञानात् (than ignorance) ध्यानं (meditation) विशिष्यते (is superior) । ध्यानात् (than meditation) कर्मफलसागस्य (renunciation of fruits of action) आगच्छन्ति (comes) शान्तिः (peace) अनन्तरम् (immediately after) ॥
vishnu_gita::79.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::79.essence: Peace arises only after you fully renounce attachment to action’s results.
vishnu_gita::79.simple_meaning: Wisdom is more valuable than just practice; meditation is better than wisdom; and giving up attachment to results leads directly to peace.
vishnu_gita::79.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing peace awaits when you stop clinging to outcomes.
vishnu_gita::79.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that while practice builds foundation, true wisdom surpasses mere effort. Meditation deepens this wisdom, but the highest step is renouncing attachment to action's results. This renunciation brings lasting peace beyond all striving.
vishnu_gita::79.modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard on a project, but the real calm comes when you stop worrying about how it will turn out.
vishnu_gita::79.insight: It shifts your focus from constant effort to releasing attachment to outcomes, opening space for inner calm.

vishnu_gita::80.verse_sanskrit:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वञ्च माय पश्यति ।
तस्याऽहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::80.verse_hindi: जो मुझको सर्वत्र देखता है और सबको मुझमें देखता है उसके लिये मैं कभी अन्तर्धान नहीं होता हूँ और वह भी मुझसे अदृश्य नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::80.english_translation: Whoever sees me everywhere and sees everything in me, to them I never disappear, and they never disappear from me.
vishnu_gita::80.translation_literal: यो (who) / मां (me) / पश्यति (sees) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / सर्वञ्च (everything) / माय (in me) / पश्यति (sees) । / तस्याऽहं (to them I) / न (not) / प्रणश्यामि (disappear) / स (and they) / च (also) / मे (from me) / न (not) / प्रणश्यति (disappear) ॥
vishnu_gita::80.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::80.essence: Seeing all as the divine means the divine and you are inseparable.
vishnu_gita::80.simple_meaning: If you see the divine everywhere and recognize everything as part of it, the divine never leaves you, and you never leave the divine.
vishnu_gita::80.simple_insight: There’s comfort in knowing you are always connected and never truly alone.
vishnu_gita::80.detailed_meaning: Vishnu tells that recognizing the divine presence everywhere creates an unbreakable bond. Anyone who sees all things as part of the divine never loses that connection, and the divine never loses them.
vishnu_gita::80.modern_relevance: In moments when you feel isolated, remember that seeing yourself and others as connected to something greater means you are never truly alone.
vishnu_gita::80.insight: It teaches you to experience connection as a constant, dissolving separation and fear of abandonment.

vishnu_gita::81.verse_sanskrit:
देवादिदेव ! सर्वज्ञ ! सृष्टिस्थितिलयप्रभो !
त्वद्विस्मरणतो नूनं दुर्गतिर्नोऽभवत्स्वयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::81.verse_hindi: हे देवादिदेव ! हे सृष्टिस्थितिप्रलयकर्त्ता ! हे सर्वज्ञ ! अब हमलोगों को यह विदित हुआ कि आपको विस्मृत होने से ही हमलोगों की यह दुर्गति हुई है
vishnu_gita::81.english_translation: O lord of all lords, all-knowing, controller of creation, preservation, and dissolution! We have realized that our downfall happened because we forgot you.
vishnu_gita::81.translation_literal: देवादिदेव (lord of lords) / सर्वज्ञ (all-knowing) / सृष्टिस्थितिलयप्रभो (controller of creation, preservation, and dissolution) / त्वद्विस्मरणतो (because of forgetting you) / नूनं (surely) / दुर्गतिर्नः (our downfall) / अभवत् (happened) / स्वयम् (by itself)
vishnu_gita::81.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::81.essence: Forgetting the divine causes downfall and hardship.
vishnu_gita::81.simple_meaning: Forgetting the divine who controls everything caused our difficulties and downfall.
vishnu_gita::81.simple_insight: Recognizing that forgetting the divine leads to hardship brings clarity and responsibility.
vishnu_gita::81.detailed_meaning: The speaker acknowledges Vishnu as the supreme being governing creation, maintenance, and destruction, admitting their troubles arose from forgetting him. This moment marks a realization of dependence on the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::81.modern_relevance: You realize your struggles grew when you stopped acknowledging the bigger support that holds things together.
vishnu_gita::81.insight: It shifts the mind to see forgetting support leads to personal and collective hardship.

vishnu_gita::82.verse_sanskrit:
आज्ञाऽस्ति भवतः सत्या जीवा अभ्यासयोगतः।
निर्भयायां पदव्यान्तु भवन्सग्रेसरा ध्रुवम् ॥
vishnu_gita::82.verse_hindi: आपकी आज्ञा सत्य है कि अभ्यास के द्वारा ही जीव निर्भयपद की ओर अग्रसर होते हैं
vishnu_gita::82.english_translation: Your instruction is true: through practice, beings steadily progress toward the fearless state.
vishnu_gita::82.translation_literal: आज्ञा (instruction) अस्ति (is) भवतः (your) सत्या (true) जीवा (beings) अभ्यासयोगतः (through practice) । निर्भयायां (to fearless) पदव्यान्तु (may they progress) भवन्सग्रेसरा (steadily) ध्रुवम् (firmly) ॥
vishnu_gita::82.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::82.essence: Steady practice is the sure path leading beings to fearless stability.
vishnu_gita::82.simple_meaning: Regular practice is the true way for beings to move steadily toward a fearless state.
vishnu_gita::82.simple_insight: There is confidence in knowing steady effort naturally leads you beyond fear.
vishnu_gita::82.detailed_meaning: Vishnu assures that consistent practice is the reliable path for living beings to reach a fearless state, emphasizing discipline as essential in their spiritual journey.
vishnu_gita::82.modern_relevance: You keep returning to your meditation every day, even when distractions arise; this steady effort quietly builds your inner strength.
vishnu_gita::82.insight: It teaches you to trust the process of repeated effort as the key to overcoming fear.

vishnu_gita::83.verse_sanskrit:
क्रमशो निर्भयाः सन्तस्ते जीवा भाग्यशालिनः ।
अतुलां परमां शान्तिमधिगच्छन्ति सत्वरम् ॥
vishnu_gita::83.verse_hindi: और क्रमशः भयरहित होकर परमभाग्यशाली हो परमशान्ति को शीघ्र प्राप्त करते हैं
vishnu_gita::83.english_translation: Step by step, fearless beings attain supreme fortune and quickly reach the highest peace.
vishnu_gita::83.translation_literal: क्रमशः (step by step) / निर्भयाः (fearless) / सन्तः (beings) / ते (they) / जीवा (living beings) / भाग्यशालिनः (fortunate) / अतुलां (unequalled) / परमां (supreme) / शान्तिम् (peace) / अधिगच्छन्ति (attain) / सत्वरम् (quickly)
vishnu_gita::83.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::83.essence: Fearlessness, taken step by step, quickly leads to supreme peace and fortune.
vishnu_gita::83.simple_meaning: By moving forward without fear, beings steadily become fortunate and quickly find deep peace.
vishnu_gita::83.simple_insight: Fearlessness creates a steady path that leads you swiftly to true calm.
vishnu_gita::83.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how living beings who overcome fear step forward gradually, gaining great fortune and swiftly achieving supreme peace. This teaching encourages courage as the foundation for inner calm and success.
vishnu_gita::83.modern_relevance: You face a difficult change but stay calm and brave, and soon find relief and confidence growing.
vishnu_gita::83.insight: It teaches you to replace hesitation with steady courage, accelerating your progress toward peace.

vishnu_gita::84.verse_sanskrit:
तदुक्तक्त्रमतो देव ! दीनाश्रय ! यथा वयं ।
प्रशांता निर्भया: स्याम कृप्यैव तथाऽऽदिश ॥
vishnu_gita::84.verse_hindi: अतः हे दीनजनों के आश्रयदाता ! आपके कहे हुए क्रम के अनुसार हम शान्ति को प्राप्त करके कैसे भयरहित हो सकते हैं वह कृपया आज्ञा कीजिये
vishnu_gita::84.english_translation: O refuge of the humble! According to your instructions, please kindly teach how we can become peaceful and fearless.
vishnu_gita::84.translation_literal: तत् (that) / उक्त (spoken) / उक्त (spoken) / क्रमतः (in order) / देव (O divine one) / दीनाश्रय (refuge of the humble) / यथा (how) / वयम् (we) / प्रशांता (peaceful) / निर्भया (fearless) / स्याम (may become) / कृप्यैव (by your kindness) / तथा (thus) / आदिश (command/instruct)
vishnu_gita::84.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::84.essence: Peace and fearlessness arise by trusting and following kind guidance.
vishnu_gita::84.simple_meaning: The speaker asks the divine refuge of the humble to kindly explain how to become peaceful and free from fear by following the given instructions.
vishnu_gita::84.simple_insight: There is hope and relief in trusting guidance to overcome fear and find peace.
vishnu_gita::84.detailed_meaning: In a moment of seeking refuge, the speaker addresses the divine protector of the humble, requesting clear guidance on attaining peace and fearlessness as taught by the divine.
vishnu_gita::84.modern_relevance: You feel anxious and uncertain, hoping for clear guidance to find calm and courage in your life.
vishnu_gita::84.insight: It encourages you to place trust in compassionate guidance as a path to inner calm and fearlessness.

vishnu_gita::85.verse_sanskrit:
हे देवाः ! इन्द्रियैर्जीवा विषयेषु निरन्तम् ।
सक्ताः सन्तस्तदाकारवृत्तिभिः स्युः मुदुःखिताः ॥
vishnu_gita::85.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जीव इन्द्रियों की सहायता से विषयों में फँसकर विषयाकार वृत्ति को प्राप्त करता हुआ नाना दुःख प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::85.english_translation: O divine beings! The living being, constantly attached through the senses to objects, experiences various pains due to these attachments.
vishnu_gita::85.translation_literal: हे (O) देवाः (divine beings) ! इन्द्रियैः (by the senses) जीवः (the living being) विषयेषु (to objects) निरन्तम् (constantly) सक्ताः (attached) सन्तः (being) तदा-आकार-वृत्तिभिः (to the form of objects / attachments) स्युः (become) मुदुः (pleasures) दुःखिताः (distressed / suffering)
vishnu_gita::85.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::85.essence: Attachment through the senses causes repeated cycles of pleasure and pain.
vishnu_gita::85.simple_meaning: When you constantly cling to things through your senses, you experience both pleasure and pain because of that attachment.
vishnu_gita::85.simple_insight: Recognizing that attachment to sensory pleasures leads to suffering brings clarity and relief.
vishnu_gita::85.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings explaining that living beings, by constantly engaging their senses with transient objects, become attached and experience a cycle of pleasure and pain. This teaches how attachment through senses causes emotional turbulence.
vishnu_gita::85.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly through social media, chasing likes and updates that feel good briefly but leave you restless and unsatisfied.
vishnu_gita::85.insight: It teaches you to observe how sensory attachments lead to fluctuating moods and suffering.

vishnu_gita::86.verse_sanskrit:
दशेयमेव भीहेतुः स्वर्गादिप्राप्तिकारणम् ।
एषैव विषमा नूनं आवागमनकारणम् ॥
vishnu_gita::86.verse_hindi: यही दशा सब भयों की कारण है, यही दशा स्वर्ग नरक प्रेत पितृ आदि नाना लोकप्राप्ति और आवागमन का मूलकारण है
vishnu_gita::86.english_translation: This very condition is the cause of all fears and the root reason for coming and going across many realms.
vishnu_gita::86.translation_literal: दशेयमेव (this condition itself) / भीहेतुः (cause of fear) / स्वर्गादि (heaven and other realms) / प्राप्तिकारणम् (cause of attainment) / एषैव (this very) / विषमा (unequal/hard) / नूनं (indeed) / आवागमनकारणम् (cause of coming and going)
vishnu_gita::86.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::86.essence: Restlessness and fear cause endless movement through many realms.
vishnu_gita::86.simple_meaning: Your unsettled state creates fear and causes you to move through many states of existence repeatedly.
vishnu_gita::86.simple_insight: There is comfort in seeing fear and restlessness as the roots of endless cycles, not your true nature.
vishnu_gita::86.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the restless, unequal state of the mind causes fear and the endless cycle of rebirth and movement through various realms. Recognizing this helps understand the source of suffering and Samsara.
vishnu_gita::86.modern_relevance: You feel anxious and unsettled, trapped in repeating patterns, as though you keep shifting between different emotional states without rest.
vishnu_gita::86.insight: It teaches you to identify restlessness and fear as the real reasons for your repeating struggles and cycles.

vishnu_gita::87.verse_sanskrit:
ततो विषयवैराग्यैर्यदा शिथिलबन्धनः।
प्रारब्धवान् साधकः स्यात्तदा सफलतालयः ॥
vishnu_gita::87.verse_hindi: अतः विषयवैराग्य द्वारा इस बन्धन को शिथिल करता हुआ अभ्यास की सहायता से प्रारब्धवान् साधक जब सफलता लाभ करता है
vishnu_gita::87.english_translation: When the seeker loosens attachment through dispassion toward sense objects, they begin to attain success.
vishnu_gita::87.translation_literal: ततः (then) विषयवैराग्यैः (by dispassion toward objects) यदा (when) शिथिलबन्धनः (loosened bondage) प्रारब्धवान् (having begun) साधकः (seeker) स्यात् (becomes) तदा (then) सफलतालयः (attaining success)
vishnu_gita::87.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::87.essence: Loosening attachment to desires initiates true progress toward success.
vishnu_gita::87.simple_meaning: By loosening attachment to desires and sense objects, the seeker starts making progress toward success.
vishnu_gita::87.simple_insight: Relief grows when you stop holding tightly to what tempts you.
vishnu_gita::87.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when a seeker practicing yoga lessens their attachment to worldly desires, the binding force of craving weakens. This loosening marks the start of real progress toward success on the spiritual path.
vishnu_gita::87.modern_relevance: You realize your anxiety fades as you stop obsessing over every craving and outcome.
vishnu_gita::87.insight: This verse teaches you to reduce craving as the first step toward meaningful success.

vishnu_gita::88.verse_sanskrit:
तदैव विमलं ज्ञानमासाद्य निर्मलाशयः।
समुन्नताधिकराप्तेरधिकार भवत्यलम् ॥
vishnu_gita::88.verse_hindi: तब ही वह ज्ञानवान् होकर उन्नत अधिकार प्राप्त करने का अधिकारी बनता है
vishnu_gita::88.english_translation: Only then, having attained pure knowledge, does one become worthy of elevated authority.
vishnu_gita::88.translation_literal: तदैव (only then) / विमलं (pure) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / आसाद्य (having attained) / निर्मलाशयः (pure-hearted) / समुन्नताधिकराप्तेः (of elevated authority obtained) / अधिकार (authority) / भवति (becomes) / अलम् (worthy)
vishnu_gita::88.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::88.essence: True authority comes only after achieving pure knowledge and clarity of heart.
vishnu_gita::88.simple_meaning: You become qualified for higher responsibility only when your knowledge is pure and your heart is clear.
vishnu_gita::88.simple_insight: There is confidence in realizing true authority comes from clarity within, not just external position.
vishnu_gita::88.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu teaches that only those who have attained pure knowledge and inner clarity become qualified to hold elevated authority, emphasizing wisdom as the foundation of rightful power.
vishnu_gita::88.modern_relevance: Before taking a leadership role, you realize knowledge and clear intention make your authority meaningful and respected.
vishnu_gita::88.insight: It shifts your view from seeking power to cultivating genuine understanding as the basis of rightful authority.

vishnu_gita::89.verse_sanskrit:
नश्वरस्य शरीरस्य सम्बन्धाद्भवतां भयम् ।
भ्रान्तिमूलं यदेतत्तद्देवाः ! तत्त्वबुभुत्मवः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::89.verse_hindi: हे तत्त्वनिज्ञासु देवतागण ! नश्वर शरीर के सम्बन्ध से आपलोगों का जो भय है सो भ्रममूलक है
vishnu_gita::89.english_translation: O wise beings, the fear you have from the connection to the perishable body is rooted in confusion.
vishnu_gita::89.translation_literal: नश्वरस्य (perishable) शरीरस्य (body) सम्बन्धात् (from connection) भवतां (your) भयः (fear) । भ्रान्तिमूलं (rooted in confusion) यत् (that) एतत् (this) देवाः (wise beings) ! तत्त्वबुभुत्मवः (O knowers of truth) !
vishnu_gita::89.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::89.essence: Fear comes from confusing the lasting self with the perishable body.
vishnu_gita::89.simple_meaning: Fear arises because you mistakenly identify with your mortal body instead of seeing beyond it.
vishnu_gita::89.simple_insight: It feels freeing to know your fear is based on a misunderstanding about who you really are.
vishnu_gita::89.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses wise beings, explaining that their fear comes from confusing their true nature with the perishable body. This teaching helps them disidentify from bodily fears and see beyond temporary forms.
vishnu_gita::89.modern_relevance: When you worry about aging or illness, this teaching reminds you that your true self is not your fragile body.
vishnu_gita::89.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with the body to recognizing fear as a product of that misidentification.

vishnu_gita::90.verse_sanskrit:
इह दृश्यानि सर्वाणि नवराणि भवन्यहो ।
अविवेकमयोऽयं यत्समारोऽतो भयाप्लुतः ॥
vishnu_gita::90.verse_hindi: इस संसार की समस्त वस्तु नश्वर है, विशेषतः यह संसार अज्ञानमय होने के कारण भय से पूर्ण है
vishnu_gita::90.english_translation: Everything seen in this world is perishable and full of fear because it is born of ignorance.
vishnu_gita::90.translation_literal: इह (here) दृश्यानि (things seen) सर्वाणि (all) नवराणि (perishable) भवन्यः (are) अविवेकमयः (full of ignorance) अयम् (this) यत् (because) समारः (fear) अतः (therefore) भयाप्लुतः (full of fear)
vishnu_gita::90.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::90.essence: The world you perceive is fleeting and filled with fear because it arises from ignorance.
vishnu_gita::90.simple_meaning: All things in this world are temporary and come with fear because they arise from ignorance.
vishnu_gita::90.simple_insight: Recognizing the world's impermanence and fear brings a sense of detachment and clarity.
vishnu_gita::90.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that everything visible in the world is subject to decay and is unstable because it is rooted in ignorance, causing fear and uncertainty in those who perceive it.
vishnu_gita::90.modern_relevance: You notice how every plan or possession feels fragile and uncertain, stirring anxiety that comes from not fully understanding the nature of things.
vishnu_gita::90.insight: This shifts your view to see the world’s things as temporary appearances that do not define your true self.

vishnu_gita::91.verse_sanskrit:
अविवेकसमुद्भूतविषयासक्तितः कचित् ।
लब्धुं न कोऽपि शक्रोति निर्भयत्वामिह स्वतः ॥
vishnu_gita::91.verse_hindi: अज्ञानसम्भूत विषय में प्रासक्त रहने से कोई भी भयरहित नहीं हो सक्ता
vishnu_gita::91.english_translation: No one can attain fearlessness while being attached to objects born of ignorance.
vishnu_gita::91.translation_literal: अविवेकसमुद्भूतविषयासक्तितः (attachment to objects born of ignorance) / कचित् (anyone) / लब्धुं (to attain) / न (not) / कोऽपि (anyone) / शक्रोति (can) / निर्भयत्वम् (fearlessness) / इह (here) / स्वतः (by itself).
vishnu_gita::91.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::91.essence: Fearlessness cannot arise while attachment to confusion-born objects remains.
vishnu_gita::91.simple_meaning: You cannot become free from fear if you stay attached to things that arise from confusion or lack of clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::91.simple_insight: There's relief in seeing that fear dissolves when you loosen grip on confusing desires.
vishnu_gita::91.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when the mind clings to objects born from ignorance, fear remains. True fearlessness cannot arise while attachments founded on confusion persist.
vishnu_gita::91.modern_relevance: You feel anxious when you desperately cling to uncertain outcomes or confusing desires that cloud your mind.
vishnu_gita::91.insight: It teaches you to notice how clinging to unclear desires blocks your courage and calm.

vishnu_gita::92.verse_hindi: पुत्र मित्र कलत्रादि स्वजन केवल अपने अपने कर्म भोगने के लिये एक देशकाल में उत्पन्न होकर
vishnu_gita::92.english_translation: Children, friends, spouses, and other loved ones are born together in one place and time only to experience the results of their own actions.
vishnu_gita::92.translation_literal: पुत्रम् (children) मित्र (friends) कलत्रादि (spouses etc.) स्वजनाः (loved ones) स्वस्वकर्मणा (by their own actions) भोगार्थ (for experiencing) युगपन्नूनम् (born together in the same time period) एकत्र (at one place) उत्पत्ति (birth) आश्रिताः (dependent)
vishnu_gita::92.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::92.essence: Loved ones gather only to experience their own actions’ consequences together.
vishnu_gita::92.simple_meaning: People you call family or friends come together only to experience the results of their own actions.
vishnu_gita::92.simple_insight: You realize that everyone is ultimately responsible for their own experiences, even those closest to you.
vishnu_gita::92.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that children, friends, spouses, and other dear ones appear in the same place and time not by chance but to face the consequences of their individual past actions. This shows relationships are tied to karma, not just chance or affection.
vishnu_gita::92.modern_relevance: You notice how even in close relationships, everyone faces their own challenges and outcomes, no one escapes their personal journey.
vishnu_gita::92.insight: It shifts the mind to see relationships as opportunities to meet your own actions’ results, not as escapes or mere attachments.

vishnu_gita::93.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मीयत्वेन राजन्ते ध्रुवं स्वस्वार्थसिद्धये ।
संस्थाप्यानृतसम्बन्धमेषु यान्ति महद्भयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::93.verse_hindi: अपने अपने स्वार्थ सिद्धि के लिये आत्मीय रूप से प्रतीत होते हैं उनमें मिथ्या सम्बन्ध स्थापन करके देही अनेक भयों को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::93.english_translation: Beings appear friendly only to fulfill their own interests, creating false relationships that bring great fear to the embodied self.
vishnu_gita::93.translation_literal: आत्मीयत्वेन (as friendly) / राजन्ते (they reign) / ध्रुवं (certainly) / स्वस्वार्थसिद्धये (for their own benefit) / संस्थाप्यानृतसम्बन्धम् (false relationships established) / एषु (in these) / यान्ति (go) / महद्भयम् (great fear)
vishnu_gita::93.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::93.essence: Friendships based on self-interest create false ties that bring fear to the self.
vishnu_gita::93.simple_meaning: People often act like friends to achieve their own goals, forming false bonds that cause fear inside you.
vishnu_gita::93.simple_insight: It's unsettling to realize some relationships hide self-interest beneath friendliness.
vishnu_gita::93.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that beings appear affectionate only to fulfill their personal desires. These false bonds cause confusion and fear for the embodied self, showing that not all closeness is genuine in the turbulent world.
vishnu_gita::93.modern_relevance: You smile with a colleague who helps only when it benefits them, leaving you uncertain about true trust.
vishnu_gita::93.insight: It teaches you to recognize when relationships are driven by self-interest, helping you protect your inner peace.

vishnu_gita::94.verse_sanskrit:
एतदात्मीयजं दुःखं भयं चाऽज्ञानमूलकम् ।
न जायते सुखं सत्यं नश्वरात्काञ्चनादितः ॥
vishnu_gita::94.verse_hindi: यह सब आत्मीयजनित भय और दुःख अज्ञानमूलक है। नश्वर कामिनी काञ्चन आदि भोगपदार्थ अपनी नश्वरता के कारण कदापि सत्य सुख को उत्पन्न नहीं कर सकते
vishnu_gita::94.english_translation: All suffering and fear born of attachment arise from deep confusion. Fleeting pleasures like gold and others cannot produce true happiness.
vishnu_gita::94.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / आत्मीयजं (born of attachment) / दुःखं (suffering) / भयं (fear) / च (and) / आज्ञानमूलकम् (rooted in ignorance) / न (not) / जायते (arises) / सुखं (happiness) / सत्यं (true) / नश्वरात् (transient) / काञ्चनादितः (from gold and similar things)
vishnu_gita::94.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::94.essence: Fear and pain come from confusion; fleeting things cannot bring true happiness.
vishnu_gita::94.simple_meaning: Fear and suffering arise from deep confusion caused by attachment. Temporary pleasures like gold cannot bring lasting happiness.
vishnu_gita::94.simple_insight: Knowing that pain comes from confusion brings relief from chasing fleeting joys.
vishnu_gita::94.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that suffering and fear rooted in attachment arise from ignorance. Material pleasures like gold are temporary and cannot create true, lasting happiness, urging a deeper understanding beyond worldly allure.
vishnu_gita::94.modern_relevance: You feel restless chasing status or possessions, but they never satisfy you deeply or for long.
vishnu_gita::94.insight: Recognize that clinging to temporary things fuels fear and suffering; true happiness lies beyond them.

vishnu_gita::95.verse_sanskrit:
ईशे नश्वरेऽर्थे हि सक्तो देही निरन्तरम्।
विविधं दुःखमाप्नोति भयञ्चैवाऽधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::95.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार के नश्वर विषयों में फंसकर देही निरन्तर अनेक प्रकार के दुःख और भय प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::95.english_translation: The embodied being, attached to fleeting things, continuously suffers various pains and fears.
vishnu_gita::95.translation_literal: ईशे (in fleeting) नश्वरेऽर्थे (mortal things) हि (indeed) सक्तो (attached) देही (the embodied being) निरन्तरम् (constantly) विविधं (various) दुःखम् (pains) आप्नोति (obtains) भयञ्च (and fear) एव (indeed) अधिगच्छति (attains)
vishnu_gita::95.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::95.essence: Attachment to what fades brings endless fear and suffering to the embodied self.
vishnu_gita::95.simple_meaning: Being attached to temporary and passing things causes continuous suffering and fear.
vishnu_gita::95.simple_insight: You can feel relief by seeing how attachment to impermanence breeds your worries.
vishnu_gita::95.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when the embodied self clings to mortal, temporary things, it continuously experiences various forms of suffering and fear. This insight reveals the root cause of ongoing distress in life.
vishnu_gita::95.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling through social media, hoping to find lasting joy, but every new post fades and leaves you restless.
vishnu_gita::95.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing fleeting things to recognizing how attachment fuels ongoing fear and pain.

vishnu_gita::96.verse_sanskrit:
जरामृत्युभयं देहे पुत्रादौ कालजादिकम्।
राजंतस्करजं द्रव्ये जराजं यौवने भयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::96.verse_hindi: शरीर में जरा और मृत्यु का भय है, पुत्रकलत्रादि में काल और वियोग का भय है, धन में राजा और चोर का भय है, यौवन में वार्द्धक्य का भय है
vishnu_gita::96.english_translation: The body fears old age and death; children and spouses bring fears of separation and time; wealth carries fears of kings and thieves; youth fears growing old.
vishnu_gita::96.translation_literal: जरामृत्युभयं (old-age-death fear) / देहे (in body) / पुत्रादौ (in children and spouse) / कालजादिकम् (time and so on) / राजंतस्करजं (king thief born) / द्रव्ये (in wealth) / जराजं (old-age-born) / यौवने (in youth) / भयम् (fear)
vishnu_gita::96.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::96.essence: Fears arise only from what changes, never from the true self.
vishnu_gita::96.simple_meaning: The body, relationships, wealth, and youth all bring different fears because they are temporary and vulnerable.
vishnu_gita::96.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing these fears come from changeable things, not your inner being.
vishnu_gita::96.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how different parts of life cause specific fears: the body fears aging and death; family fears separation and loss; wealth fears theft and control; youth fears aging. This highlights the impermanence of worldly attachments.
vishnu_gita::96.modern_relevance: You notice your anxiety rising when you think about losing your job, your loved ones drifting away, or your health declining with age.
vishnu_gita::96.insight: Recognize that fears are tied to external, impermanent things, freeing you to detach and focus on what remains constant.

vishnu_gita::97.verse_sanskrit:
जरारोगभयं रूपे वले शत्रुभवं भयम् ।
भोगे रोगभयं नूनं कुले पतन भयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::97.verse_hindi: रूप में जरा और रोग का भय है, बल में शत्रु का भय है, भोग मे रोग का भय है, कुल में पतित होने का भय है
vishnu_gita::97.english_translation: There is fear of old age and disease in appearance, fear of enemies in strength, fear of disease in enjoyment, and fear of downfall in lineage.
vishnu_gita::97.translation_literal: जरारोगभयं (old age-disease-fear) रूपे (in appearance) वले (in strength) शत्रुभवं (enemy-being) भयम् (fear) । भोगे (in enjoyment) रोगभयं (disease-fear) नूनं (indeed) कुले (in lineage) पतन (fall) भयम् (fear) ॥
vishnu_gita::97.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::97.essence: All that seems strong or joyful carries hidden fears that reveal its impermanence.
vishnu_gita::97.simple_meaning: Everything you value—your looks, strength, pleasures, and family—has some hidden fear or weakness.
vishnu_gita::97.simple_insight: Recognizing fear in all you hold dear frees you from clinging to fragile things.
vishnu_gita::97.detailed_meaning: Vishnu points out how people fear aging and sickness in their body, enemies in their power, illness in their pleasures, and ruin in their family line. This reveals the fragile nature of worldly attachments.
vishnu_gita::97.modern_relevance: You might worry about losing your youth, health, influence, or family reputation—this verse shows these fears are natural but reveal impermanence.
vishnu_gita::97.insight: It teaches you to see that all external things are vulnerable, encouraging detachment and deeper stability.

vishnu_gita::98.verse_sanskrit:
दीनताजं भयं माने गुणे खलभयं खलु ।
भयं निन्दकजं शक्तौ विद्यायां वादिनं भयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::98.verse_hindi: मान में दीनता का भय है, गुण में खलों का ही भय है, शक्ति में निन्द का भय है, विद्या में वादी का भय है
vishnu_gita::98.english_translation: In humility, fear of lowliness arises; in virtue, fear of wickedness; in strength, fear of criticism; in knowledge, fear of argument.
vishnu_gita::98.translation_literal: दीनताजं (from humility) / भयं (fear) / माने (in honor) / गुणे (in virtue) / खलभयं (fear of wickedness) / खलु (indeed) / भयं (fear) / निन्दकजं (born of criticism) / शक्तौ (in strength) / विद्यायां (in knowledge) / वादिनं (of the debater) / भयम् (fear)
vishnu_gita::98.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::98.essence: Your best qualities can also be the source of your fears.
vishnu_gita::98.simple_meaning: Fear arises in different qualities: humility fears being seen as weak, virtue fears evil people, strength fears criticism, and knowledge fears argument.
vishnu_gita::98.simple_insight: You might feel afraid even when growing in good qualities, and that’s part of the journey.
vishnu_gita::98.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how different positive qualities—humility, virtue, strength, knowledge—bring their own kinds of fear, showing that growth always faces inner challenges.
vishnu_gita::98.modern_relevance: You may hesitate to show kindness fearing judgment, or doubt your knowledge fearing debate, even when these are your strengths.
vishnu_gita::98.insight: It teaches you to recognize that fear can arise alongside your best qualities, inviting you to face it without retreat.

vishnu_gita::99.verse_hindi: सब लोगों के अभीप्सित स्वर्ग में भी ईष्या और पतन का भय है , केवल उत्तम वैराग्यपद  ही भयरहित है
vishnu_gita::99.english_translation: Even in the most desired higher realms, envy and fear of downfall exist; only the highest state of detachment is truly free of fear.
vishnu_gita::99.translation_literal: स्वर्गेऽपि (even in heaven) प्रार्थ्यमानेऽस्मिन् (desired by many) ईपर्याप्तनज (envy and fear of downfall) भयम् (fear) । वैराग्यपदमेव (only the state of detachment) अत्र (here) तिष्ठति (stands/remains) अभयम् (fearlessness) उत्तमम् (supreme) ॥
vishnu_gita::99.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::99.essence: Only supreme detachment offers complete fearlessness beyond any desired realm.
vishnu_gita::99.simple_meaning: Even the most desired heavenly places have envy and fear of falling; only the highest level of detachment is completely free of fear.
vishnu_gita::99.simple_insight: Relief comes knowing that true safety is found only in letting go completely.
vishnu_gita::99.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that even the most enviable and sought-after heavenly realms contain fear of loss and envy. The only place free from such fear is the supreme state of detachment, where the mind is not bound by desire or attachment.
vishnu_gita::99.modern_relevance: You may achieve many goals and places others envy, yet still feel anxious about losing them. Only letting go fully brings peace.
vishnu_gita::99.insight: This verse shifts your focus from chasing external success to cultivating inner detachment as true security.

vishnu_gita::100.verse_sanskrit:
येनैव हि विचारेण तत्तु लभ्येत निर्जराः !।
जगतां श्रेयसे नूनं तं ब्रवीमि निबोधत ॥
vishnu_gita::100.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! जिस विचार के द्वारा इसकी प्राप्ति निश्चय ही होती है उसको जगत् कल्याण के लिये ही कहता हूँ सो जानो
vishnu_gita::100.english_translation: O divine beings! The thought by which that is surely attained is called the welfare of the world, understand this.
vishnu_gita::100.translation_literal: येनैव (by which alone) हि (indeed) विचारेण (by thought) तत्तु (that) लभ्येत (is attained) निर्जराः (certainly)! जगतां (of the worlds) श्रेयसे (for welfare) नूनं (indeed) तं (that) ब्रवीमि (I say) निबोधत (understand).
vishnu_gita::100.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::100.essence: Focused thought that leads to attainment is the true welfare of the world.
vishnu_gita::100.simple_meaning: The thought or reflection that leads to certain attainment is what brings true welfare to the world.
vishnu_gita::100.simple_insight: You feel inspired knowing that clear, focused thought shapes the wellbeing of all.
vishnu_gita::100.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that the specific kind of thought or inquiry that leads to definite attainment is what truly benefits the entire world. This teaching sets the stage for understanding wisdom's power.
vishnu_gita::100.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by many options, focusing your thinking on what truly benefits everyone guides you to wiser choices.
vishnu_gita::100.insight: It encourages you to focus your mind on clear, purposeful thinking that benefits beyond yourself.

vishnu_gita::101.verse_sanskrit:
देहिनोऽस्मिन् यथा देहे कोमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिधीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::101.verse_hindi: देहाभिमानी जीव का जिस प्रकार इस देह में कौमार यौवन और वार्धक्य है देहान्तरप्राप्ति अर्थात् मृत्यु भी उसी प्रकार है (अवस्थाभेदमात्र है) अतएव ज्ञानी उसमें मोहित नहीं होते हैं
vishnu_gita::101.english_translation: Just as the body experiences childhood, youth, and old age, the wise are not deluded by the body's death.
vishnu_gita::101.translation_literal: देहिनोऽस्मिन् (in the embodied self) / यथा (just as) / देहे (in the body) / कोमारं (childhood) / यौवनं (youth) / जरा (old age) / तथा (similarly) / देहान्तरप्राप्ति (attaining another body - i.e. death) / धीरः (the wise) / तत्र (therein) / न (not) / मुह्यति (deluded)
vishnu_gita::101.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::101.essence: The true self is steady and undeluded despite the body's aging and death.
vishnu_gita::101.simple_meaning: The body passes through stages like childhood, youth, and old age, but the wise know its death is just another change and are not confused by it.
vishnu_gita::101.simple_insight: You can feel steady knowing your true self is beyond the body's changes and death.
vishnu_gita::101.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that just as the body naturally ages through childhood, youth, and old age, death is merely another stage of change. The wise see beyond this physical cycle and are not confused or disturbed by it.
vishnu_gita::101.modern_relevance: You watch a loved one age or face illness, but you sense their true being remains beyond these shifts and endings.
vishnu_gita::101.insight: It teaches you to see your identity beyond physical changes, reducing fear of death and loss.

vishnu_gita::102.verse_hindi: हे श्रेष्ठ देवगण! इन्द्रियों की वृत्ति और उनके साथ इन्द्रियों के विषयो का संयोग ये ही शीतोष्णादि सुख दुःख को देनेवाले हैं। ये सब आगमापायी ( उत्पत्तिनाशविशिष्ट) है अतएव अनित्य हैं उनको सहन करो अर्थात् हर्षविषाद आदि के वशीभूत मत हो
vishnu_gita::102.english_translation: O exalted devas! The contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These experiences arise and pass away; endure them and do not be controlled by joy or sorrow.
vishnu_gita::102.translation_literal: मात्रा (contact) -स्पर्शास्तु (only) -गीर्वाणाः (senses)! शीतोष्ण (cold and heat) -सुख (pleasure) -दुःख (pain) -दाः (giving). आगमापायिनः (arising and passing away) -अनित्याः (impermanent) -ताः (those) -तितिक्षध्वम् (endure) -उत्तमाः (best).
vishnu_gita::102.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::102.essence: Pleasure and pain arise from senses and pass; endurance frees you from their control.
vishnu_gita::102.simple_meaning: Your senses meet things that cause feelings like cold, heat, pleasure, and pain. These feelings come and go, so you should endure them without letting joy or sorrow control you.
vishnu_gita::102.simple_insight: You can find calm by realizing that feelings of pleasure and pain are temporary and should not sway you.
vishnu_gita::102.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses the devas, explaining how their senses' contact with worldly objects creates sensations of pleasure and pain, which arise and disappear. He advises enduring these passing experiences without being ruled by emotional highs or lows.
vishnu_gita::102.modern_relevance: You get a sudden chill or warmth, or a mood swings quickly after a text or news. Recognizing these feelings as temporary helps you stay calm and balanced.
vishnu_gita::102.insight: It teaches you to recognize sensations as temporary and not react by chasing pleasure or avoiding pain.

vishnu_gita::103.verse_sanskrit:
यं हि न व्यथयंत्य्ते पुरुषं विबुर्ध्षभा:।
ममदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
vishnu_gita::103.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्ठो! ये सब (मात्रास्पर्श) सुख दुःख में संभव युक्त जिस धीर व्यक्ति को व्यथा नहीं देते हैं वह अमरत्व प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::103.english_translation: O best of gods! Those great beings who are not disturbed by these joys and sorrows attain immortality.
vishnu_gita::103.translation_literal: यं (whom) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / व्यथयन्ति (disturb) / ते (them) / पुरुषं (person) / विबुर्ध्षभा: (great beings) / मम (my) / दुःखसुखं (sorrow and joy) / धीरं (steady) / सोऽमृतत्वाय (for immortality) / कल्पते (is considered)
vishnu_gita::103.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::103.essence: True strength is staying steady through both joy and sorrow.
vishnu_gita::103.simple_meaning: A person who is not shaken by happiness or sadness is steady and attains freedom from suffering.
vishnu_gita::103.simple_insight: You can find strength in staying calm through life’s ups and downs.
vishnu_gita::103.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses the highest beings who do not let pleasure or pain disturb their inner balance. This steadiness is a sign of deep inner strength and leads to freedom beyond ordinary experience.
vishnu_gita::103.modern_relevance: When you face unexpected praise or criticism, staying steady lets you keep your peace and move forward without losing yourself.
vishnu_gita::103.insight: It teaches you to cultivate a steady mind that neither clings to joy nor rejects pain, leading to lasting freedom.

vishnu_gita::104.verse_sanskrit:
नाऽसतो विद्यते भावो नाऽभावो विद्यते सतः।
उभयोराप दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
vishnu_gita::104.verse_hindi: अनित्य वास्तु स्थायी नहीं है और नित्य वास्तु का विनाश नहीं होता, अर्थात अनित्य शरीर और जगत का अवश्य नाश होगा और नित्य वस्तु आत्मा का क्तिकाल मे विनाश नहीं है । तत्त्वदर्शी लोगों ने इन दोनों का ही तत्त्व देखा है।
vishnu_gita::104.english_translation: The impermanent has no lasting reality; the permanent is never destroyed. The wise have seen the truth of both.
vishnu_gita::104.translation_literal: na (not) asato (impermanent) vidyate (exists) bhavo (being) na (not) abhavo (non-being) vidyate (exists) satah (permanent) ubhayoh (both) ap (indeed) drshtah (seen) antah (inside) tv anayos (of these two) tattvadarsibhih (truth-seeing ones).
vishnu_gita::104.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::104.essence: The temporary disappears; the true self endures forever.
vishnu_gita::104.simple_meaning: Some things in life are temporary and will end, while others are eternal and cannot be destroyed. Wise people understand this difference clearly.
vishnu_gita::104.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that while many things pass, your true self remains unchanged.
vishnu_gita::104.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to seekers that the world and body are temporary and will end, but the true self is eternal and indestructible. Those who see deeply recognize both realities clearly.
vishnu_gita::104.modern_relevance: You watch a relationship or phase end, feeling loss, but deep inside you sense something within that never changes.
vishnu_gita::104.insight: It shifts your view from clinging to changing things toward recognizing your lasting inner reality.

vishnu_gita::105.verse_sanskrit:
अविनाशि तु तद्वित्त येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्याऽस्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति ॥
vishnu_gita::105.verse_hindi: जो  उत्पत्तिनाश शील इन सब  देहादि में व्याप्त है उस आत्मस्वरूप को अविनाशी मानना चाहिए। कोई भी उस अव्यय उत्पत्तिनाशशून्य आत्मा का विनाश नहीं कर सकता
vishnu_gita::105.english_translation: The true self that pervades all creation is indestructible; no one can destroy this imperishable essence.
vishnu_gita::105.translation_literal: अविनाशि (indestructible) / तु (but) / तद्वित्त (knowing that which) / येन (by whom) / सर्वमिदं (all this) / ततम् (is pervaded) / । / विनाशम् (destruction) / अव्ययस्याऽस्य (of the imperishable) / न (not) / कश्चित् (anyone) / कर्तुमर्हति (is able to do) ॥
vishnu_gita::105.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::105.essence: The true self that pervades everything is eternal and cannot be destroyed.
vishnu_gita::105.simple_meaning: Your true self is eternal and cannot be destroyed by anything in the world.
vishnu_gita::105.simple_insight: You can feel secure knowing the deepest part of you is forever safe.
vishnu_gita::105.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the true self, which pervades all things and transcends birth and death, is eternal and cannot be destroyed by anyone or anything.
vishnu_gita::105.modern_relevance: When facing loss or change, knowing your core essence is unbreakable brings calm and strength.
vishnu_gita::105.insight: It shifts your view from fearing loss to recognizing your enduring inner being.

vishnu_gita::106.verse_sanskrit:
यदा वो मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तास्थ निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
vishnu_gita::106.verse_hindi: जब तुम्हारी बुद्धि मोहरूप गहन दुर्ग अर्थात देहादि में आत्मबुद्धि को परित्याग करेगी तब तुम श्रोतव्य और श्रुत अर्थों से वैराग्य प्राप्त होगे
vishnu_gita::106.english_translation: When your intellect crosses beyond the deep darkness of delusion, then detachment arises from both the listener and the heard.
vishnu_gita::106.translation_literal: यदा (when) वो (your) मोहकलिलं (darkness of delusion) बुद्धिः (intellect) व्यतितरिष्यति (crosses beyond) तदा (then) गन्ता (goes) स्थ (place) निर्वेदं (detachment) श्रोतव्यस्य (of what is heard) श्रुतस्य (of the heard) च (and)
vishnu_gita::106.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::106.essence: Detachment arises when your intellect transcends deep delusion and confusion.
vishnu_gita::106.simple_meaning: Your intellect moves beyond deep confusion, and then true detachment arises from understanding both what is heard and the listener.
vishnu_gita::106.simple_insight: There is freedom in seeing clearly beyond confusion and letting go fully.
vishnu_gita::106.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when your mind overcomes the deep darkness of confusion that hides your true self, detachment naturally follows from both hearing teachings and understanding them fully.
vishnu_gita::106.modern_relevance: When your mind stops being clouded by doubt and distraction, you naturally stop clinging to ideas or outcomes.
vishnu_gita::106.insight: It teaches you to recognize and move beyond mental confusion to achieve detachment from external inputs and internal reactions.

vishnu_gita::107.verse_sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना वो यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यथ ॥
vishnu_gita::107.verse_hindi: जब तत्त्वज्ञान सम्बन्धी उपदेशों के सुनने से और उनके मनन के द्वारा तुम्हारी बुद्धि अविचलित होकर समाधि उत्तमरूप से स्थिर रहेगी तब तुम योग प्राप्त होगे।
vishnu_gita::107.english_translation: When your intellect becomes steady and unwavering through listening and reflecting on true knowledge, then you will attain yoga.
vishnu_gita::107.translation_literal: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना (by hearing and reflection) / वो (your) / यदा (when) / स्थास्यति (will become steady) / निश्चला (unwavering) / समाधावचला (like absorbed presence) / बुद्धि (intellect) / तदा (then) / योगमवाप्स्यथ (you will attain yoga)
vishnu_gita::107.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::107.essence: Steady, unwavering intellect through true knowledge is the gateway to yoga.
vishnu_gita::107.simple_meaning: By deeply listening and reflecting, your mind becomes steady and clear, leading you to attain yoga.
vishnu_gita::107.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing steady understanding opens the path to yoga.
vishnu_gita::107.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when the listener’s mind stops wavering through hearing and reflecting on true knowledge, their intellect becomes steady like absorbed presence, enabling them to reach yoga.
vishnu_gita::107.modern_relevance: You’ve read, thought deeply, and now your restless thoughts settle—opening space for clarity and focus.
vishnu_gita::107.insight: It teaches you to cultivate steady intellect through thoughtful reflection, enabling inner stillness and progress.

vishnu_gita::108.verse_sanskrit:
बासस्पर्शेष्वसत्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्माने यत्सुखम् ।
स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा मुखमक्षय्यमश्नुते ॥
vishnu_gita::108.verse_hindi: बाहोन्द्रियों के सभी विषयों में अनासक्तचित्त व्यक्ति, आत्मा में जो शान्ति सुख है उसकी प्राप्ति करता है, वह ब्रह्म में योग के द्वारा युक्तात्मा होकर अक्षय सुख प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::108.english_translation: The self-controlled person, detached from all external senses, finds inner peace and attains imperishable joy through the yoga of Brahman.
vishnu_gita::108.translation_literal: बासस्पर्शेषु (in external senses) असत् (without) आत्मा (self) यत् (that) सुखम् (happiness) विन्दति (finds) आत्माने (in the self) स (that) ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा (joined with Brahman-yoga) मुखम् (imperishable) अक्षयम् (undying) अश्नुते (attains)
vishnu_gita::108.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::108.essence: Detachment from the senses opens the door to lasting inner joy through union with the supreme.
vishnu_gita::108.simple_meaning: When you stop clinging to external things, you find deep peace and lasting joy within yourself through spiritual practice.
vishnu_gita::108.simple_insight: Relief comes from quieting your attachment to outer things and resting in your true self.
vishnu_gita::108.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person who remains unattached to all sensory experiences and turns their focus inward attains a steady, imperishable happiness by uniting with the supreme reality through yoga.
vishnu_gita::108.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly, distracted by notifications and noise. When you detach from this sensory flood, a calm joy emerges from within.
vishnu_gita::108.insight: It shifts your practice from chasing external pleasure to cultivating inner peace through detachment and yoga.

vishnu_gita::109.verse_sanskrit:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।
आद्यन्तवन्तो विबुधाः ! न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
vishnu_gita::109.verse_hindi: विषयजनित जो सब सुख हैं वह निश्चय ही दुःख के हेतु हैं एवं आदि और अन्त विशिष्ट अर्थात् अनित्य हैं इसी कारण हे देवगण ! विवेकी पुरुष इन सब में रत नहीं होते हैं
vishnu_gita::109.english_translation: All pleasures born of contact with the senses are surely causes of suffering; they have a beginning and an end, and the wise do not delight in them.
vishnu_gita::109.translation_literal: ये (these) / हि (indeed) / संस्पर्शजा (born of contact) / भोगा (pleasures) / दुःखयोनय (causes of suffering) / एव (only) / ते (they) / आद्यन्तवन्तो (having a beginning and an end) / विबुधाः (wise ones) / न (not) / तेषु (in them) / रमते (delight) / बुधः (the wise)
vishnu_gita::109.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::109.essence: Pleasures born from senses are temporary and cause suffering; the wise avoid delighting in them.
vishnu_gita::109.simple_meaning: Pleasures that come from sensory contact always cause suffering because they are temporary. Wise people do not get attached to them.
vishnu_gita::109.simple_insight: You can feel peace by not chasing pleasures that will surely end in pain.
vishnu_gita::109.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that all pleasures arising from contact with the senses are temporary and inevitably lead to suffering. Wise beings understand this impermanence and thus do not indulge in such fleeting enjoyments.
vishnu_gita::109.modern_relevance: You scroll social media for quick hits of happiness, but soon feel empty and restless; this teaches you to see those pleasures as temporary distractions.
vishnu_gita::109.insight: Shift your focus from chasing temporary pleasures to seeking lasting inner steadiness beyond sensory experiences.

vishnu_gita::110.verse_sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
vishnu_gita::110.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार मनुष्य जीर्ण वस्त्र परित्याग करके दुसरे नवीन वस्त्र धारण करता है, उसी प्रकार आत्मा जीर्ण शरीर परित्याग करके अन्य नूतन देह धारण करता है
vishnu_gita::110.english_translation: Just as a person discards old clothes and puts on new ones, the true self leaves the old worn-out body and takes on a new one.
vishnu_gita::110.translation_literal: वासांसि (clothes) जीर्णानि (old) यथा (just as) विहाय (leaving) नवानि (new) गृह्णाति (takes) नरोऽपराणि (another person's); तथा (so) शरीराणि (bodies) विहाय (leaving) जीर्णानि (old) अन्यानि (other) संयाति (takes) नवानि (new) देही (the true self)
vishnu_gita::110.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::110.essence: The true self discards old bodies as easily as changing worn clothes.
vishnu_gita::110.simple_meaning: The true self is not the body. When the body gets old, the true self moves on to a new body like changing clothes.
