vishnu_gita::110.simple_insight: You are not limited by your current body; your true self goes beyond physical change.
vishnu_gita::110.detailed_meaning: In this teaching from Vishnu, the true self is compared to a person changing clothes. When one body becomes worn out, the true self leaves it and takes on a new one, showing the difference between the physical and the eternal inner being.
vishnu_gita::110.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by aging or illness, remember your true self is beyond the body’s limits and changes.
vishnu_gita::110.insight: Recognize the distinction between your ever-changing body and your unchanging true self; this shifts your identity beyond physical form.

vishnu_gita::111.verse_sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि निर्जराः ।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव ह्येतदेवावधार्यताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::111.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! सकल भूत प्रारम्भ में अव्यक्त चक्षु आदि के अगोचर हैं, केवल बीच में व्यक्त-प्रकाशित हैं एवं मरणकाल में भी अव्यक्त हैं, यह सब ही आप विचार करें
vishnu_gita::111.english_translation: O divine beings! All creatures begin as unmanifest and imperceptible, become manifest in the middle, and return to unmanifest at death; reflect on this truth.
vishnu_gita::111.translation_literal: अव्यक्तादीनि (from unmanifest origins) / भूतानि (beings) / व्यक्तमध्यानि (manifest in the middle) / निर्जराः (without old age, impermanent) / अव्यक्तनिधनानि (ending unmanifest) / एव (indeed) / हि (certainly) / एते (these) / एव (only) / अवधार्यताम् (should be considered).
vishnu_gita::111.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::111.essence: Life appears briefly between two vast periods of invisibility and change.
vishnu_gita::111.simple_meaning: All beings start hidden and invisible, appear briefly during life, and vanish back into invisibility at death.
vishnu_gita::111.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing that life’s visible moments are just a brief phase within a larger unseen cycle.
vishnu_gita::111.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine assembly, explaining that all living beings originate in an unmanifest state, become visible during their life span, and finally return to that unmanifest state at death, urging reflection on this transient nature of existence.
vishnu_gita::111.modern_relevance: You watch a new project bloom, then fade—realizing the visible phase is just part of a larger hidden process.
vishnu_gita::111.insight: This shifts your view from clinging to appearances toward accepting the deeper unseen cycles of change.

vishnu_gita::112.verse_sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनपाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्याः।
आश्चर्यवच्चैन्मन्य: शृणोति श्रुत्वाऽप्येनं  वेद न चैव कांश्चित ॥
vishnu_gita::112.verse_hindi: कोई इस आत्मा को आश्चर्यवत् देखता है, इसी प्रकार कोई इसको आश्चर्य्यवत् कहता है और कोई इस को आश्चर्य्यवत् सुनता है और कोई सुनकर भी इसको नहीं जानता है
vishnu_gita::112.english_translation: Some see the true self as a wonder, some call it wondrous, others hear of it, yet none truly know it.
vishnu_gita::112.translation_literal: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति (as a wonder sees) कश्चित (someone) एना (thus) अपाश्चर्यवत् (as a wonder) वदति (speaks) तथैव (likewise) च (and) अन्याः (others) आश्चर्यवत् (wondrous) च (also) ऐन (indeed) मन्य: (thinks) शृणोति (hears) श्रुत्वा (having heard) अपि (even) एनं (this) वेद (knows) न (not) चैव (indeed) कांश्चित् (anyone)
vishnu_gita::112.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::112.essence: Many encounter the true self differently, but true understanding is rare.
vishnu_gita::112.simple_meaning: Many encounter the true self in different ways—seeing, speaking, or hearing—but few truly understand it.
vishnu_gita::112.simple_insight: Knowing the true self is a rare and precious experience beyond words or appearances.
vishnu_gita::112.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu highlights how the true self is perceived differently: some see it with wonder, some speak of it with awe, others merely hear about it, yet genuine understanding remains elusive for all.
vishnu_gita::112.modern_relevance: You might hear inspiring ideas or see others talk about deep truths, but truly grasping your own essence remains rare and precious.
vishnu_gita::112.insight: It shifts your focus from passive hearing or speaking to seeking direct, personal understanding of your true self.

vishnu_gita::113.verse_sanskrit:
देवाधिदेव ! हे नाथ ! भवतः कृपयाऽधुना।
ज्ञात्वा वैराग्यमाहात्म्यं तत्स्वरूपच सुस्फुटम् ॥
vishnu_gita::113.verse_hindi: हे देवादिदेव! हे नाथ ! इस समय वैराग्य की महिमा और उसका स्वरूप आपकी कृपा से भलीभांति जानकर
vishnu_gita::113.english_translation: O supreme being, O lord! By your grace now clearly knowing the greatness and true nature of renunciation.
vishnu_gita::113.translation_literal: देवाधिदेव (supreme being) / हे (O) / नाथ (lord) / भवतः (your) / कृपया (by grace) / अधुना (now) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / वैराग्यम् (renunciation) / आहात्म्यम् (greatness) / तत् (that) / स्वरूप (true nature) / सुस्फुटम् (clearly)
vishnu_gita::113.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::113.essence: True renunciation becomes clear and powerful through the grace that reveals it.
vishnu_gita::113.simple_meaning: You can understand how powerful and clear true renunciation is when guided by grace.
vishnu_gita::113.simple_insight: You feel relief and clarity when you see letting go as a profound strength.
vishnu_gita::113.detailed_meaning: At a moment of seeking, the speaker addresses the supreme being, asking for grace to truly grasp the greatness and clear nature of renunciation, highlighting its importance for the path ahead.
vishnu_gita::113.modern_relevance: When you finally understand the strength in releasing control, you find peace amid uncertainty.
vishnu_gita::113.insight: It teaches you to trust that letting go is not loss but a clear power revealed through grace.

vishnu_gita::114.verse_sanskrit:
निर्भया: स्मो वयं जाता देवास्त्वत्पदसेविन: ।
इदानी वर्णयन्सम्यक् सृष्टिप्रकरणं तथा ॥
vishnu_gita::114.verse_hindi: हम सब आपके चरण सेवक देवगण भय से रहित हुए हैं।  अब सृष्टिप्रकरण और
vishnu_gita::114.english_translation: We have become fearless servants at your feet, O divine one. Now, clearly describe the creation process.
vishnu_gita::114.translation_literal: निर्भया: (fearless) स्मो (we have become) वयं (we) जाता (born/become) देवाः (divine beings) त्वत् (your) पदसेविनः (foot-servants) । इदानी (now) वर्णयन् (describing) सम्यक् (clearly) सृष्टि-प्रकरणं (creation process) तथा (also) ॥
vishnu_gita::114.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::114.essence: Fearlessness and devotion prepare the mind to receive knowledge about creation.
vishnu_gita::114.simple_meaning: The divine beings say they are now fearless servants ready to hear a clear explanation of how creation began.
vishnu_gita::114.simple_insight: There is courage in readiness to learn profound truths without fear.
vishnu_gita::114.detailed_meaning: The divine beings address Vishnu, expressing that they have lost all fear and are devoted servants at his feet. They request a clear explanation of the process of creation, marking a pivotal moment before receiving cosmic wisdom.
vishnu_gita::114.insight: It shows that openness and fearlessness are the first steps to understanding complex truths.

vishnu_gita::115.verse_sanskrit:
तद्रहस्यं महाविष्णो ! ज्ञापयन्यच्छ नोऽधुना।
विवेकं तादृशं येन जानीमो विस्तराद्वयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::115.verse_hindi: उसका रहस्य अच्छी तरह वर्णन करके हे महाविष्णो! हमको ऐसा विवेक दीजिए जिससे हम अच्छी तरह समझ सकें
vishnu_gita::115.english_translation: Reveal that secret now, O Mahavishnu, and grant us the discernment to deeply understand it.
vishnu_gita::115.translation_literal: तद् (that) रहस्यं (secret) महा-विष्णो (O great Vishnu) ज्ञापय (reveal) नि (now) अच (give) नोऽ (to us) अधुना (at this moment) विवेकं (discernment) तादृशं (such) येन (by which) जानीमः (we may understand) विस्तरात् (in detail) द्वयम् (two/dual).
vishnu_gita::115.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::115.essence: True understanding comes from seeking clear, guided discernment of hidden truths.
vishnu_gita::115.simple_meaning: Requesting clear guidance to gain the kind of understanding that uncovers hidden truths deeply.
vishnu_gita::115.simple_insight: You can feel hopeful when you seek the right insight—it opens new understanding.
vishnu_gita::115.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker asks the great Vishnu to reveal a secret with clear guidance, hoping to grasp a profound dual teaching fully.
vishnu_gita::115.modern_relevance: When facing confusing situations, asking for clear insight can help you understand complex challenges deeply.
vishnu_gita::115.insight: It teaches you to actively seek clear discernment to truly grasp subtle, important truths.

vishnu_gita::116.verse_sanskrit: का सृष्टिः कश्च सम्बन्धस्तया नस्सह सम्मतः॥
vishnu_gita::116.verse_hindi: की सृष्टि क्या है और सृष्टि के साथ हमारा क्या सम्बन्ध है।
vishnu_gita::116.english_translation: What is creation, and what is our relationship with it?
vishnu_gita::116.translation_literal: का (what) / सृष्टिः (creation) / कश्च (who) / सम्बन्धः (relationship) / तया (with it) / न (not) / सह (together) / सम्मतः (considered)
vishnu_gita::116.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::116.essence: The question of what creation is and how you relate to it opens the path to wisdom.
vishnu_gita::116.simple_meaning: Creation is the world around us, and this asks what connection you have to it.
vishnu_gita::116.simple_insight: Curiosity about your true relationship to the world invites deeper understanding.
vishnu_gita::116.detailed_meaning: Vishnu poses a fundamental question about the nature of creation and our link to it, inviting reflection on existence and the self's place within the cosmos.
vishnu_gita::116.modern_relevance: When you stop to ask what your life really connects to, you open space for meaning beyond daily tasks.
vishnu_gita::116.insight: It encourages shifting from automatic living to consciously exploring your role in the unfolding whole.

vishnu_gita::119.verse_sanskrit:
निर्गुणावस्थितावस्मि खल्वव्यक्तोऽद्वितीयकः ।
आविर्भवति मे शक्तिमर्त्त एव यदा सुराः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::119.verse_hindi: मैं निर्गुण अवस्था में अव्यक्त और अद्वितीय ही रहता हूँ। हे देवता गण ! जब मेरी शक्ति मुझसे ही उत्पन्न होती है
vishnu_gita::119.english_translation: I remain unmanifested, without qualities, and without a second. O deities, my power arises from me alone.
vishnu_gita::119.translation_literal: निर्गुणावस्थितावस्मि (without qualities, situated) / खलु (indeed) / अव्यक्तः (unmanifested) / अद्वितीयकः (without second) / आविर्भवति (arises) / मे (my) / शक्तिः (power) / मर्त्त (from me) / एव (indeed) / यदा (when) / सुराः (deities)
vishnu_gita::119.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::119.essence: The supreme source is unmanifested, unique, and the origin of all power.
vishnu_gita::119.simple_meaning: I exist beyond qualities and form, unique and unmanifested. My power comes forth from me alone.
vishnu_gita::119.simple_insight: There is strength in being the source beyond all forms and qualities.
vishnu_gita::119.detailed_meaning: Vishnu speaks of his supreme nature as the unmanifested, unique reality beyond qualities. He addresses the gods, revealing that all power originates from him, highlighting his ultimate cause role.
vishnu_gita::119.insight: It invites you to see your deepest source as beyond all changing traits, the origin of your own power.

vishnu_gita::120.verse_sanskrit:
महाविष्णुस्तदा भूत्वा सगुणं धारये वपुः।
शक्तिर्मम महामाया द्विधा कृत्वाऽऽत्मनो वपुः ॥
vishnu_gita::120.verse_hindi: तब मैं महाविष्णु होकर सगुणरूप को धारण करता हूँ। मेरी शक्ति महामाया अपने में से दो रूप प्रकट करके वे
vishnu_gita::120.english_translation: Then I become Mahavishnu, adopting a form with qualities; my great power, Mahamaya, manifests two forms from itself.
vishnu_gita::120.translation_literal: महाविष्णुस्तदा (then Mahavishnu) / भूत्वा (becoming) / सगुणं (with qualities) / धारये (I bear) / वपुः (body/ form) / शक्तिर्मम (my power) / महामाया (great illusion) / द्विधा (in two ways) / कृत्वा (having made) / आत्मनो (of self) / वपुः (body/ form)
vishnu_gita::120.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::120.essence: The supreme being manifests diverse forms through its great power of illusion.
vishnu_gita::120.simple_meaning: I take on a form with qualities as Mahavishnu, and my great power, Mahamaya, creates two forms from itself.
vishnu_gita::120.simple_insight: The divine manifests distinct forms through its great power to engage with creation.
vishnu_gita::120.detailed_meaning: Vishnu declares that as Mahavishnu he assumes a qualified form, embodying qualities. His great power, Mahamaya, divides into two separate forms, marking a fundamental cosmic act of manifestation.
vishnu_gita::120.insight: It shows how the supreme being reveals multiplicity from unity by manifesting diverse forms through power.

vishnu_gita::121.verse_sanskrit:
विद्यारूपेण सततं सेवायां रमते मम ।
करोति ज्ञानिनो जीवन्मां प्रत्ग्रेसरंश्च सा ॥
vishnu_gita::121.verse_hindi: विद्यारूप से सदा मेरी सेवा में रत रहती हैं और वे ज्ञानी जीवों को मेरी ओर अग्रसर करती रहती हैं
vishnu_gita::121.english_translation: The form of knowledge is always delighted in my service and guides wise beings toward me.
vishnu_gita::121.translation_literal: विद्यारूपेण (by the form of knowledge) सततं (always) सेवायां (in service) रमते (delights) मम (my) । करोति (does) ज्ञानिनो (to the wise) जीवन्मां (living beings toward me) प्रत्ग्रेसरंश्च (advances) सा (she) ॥
vishnu_gita::121.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::121.essence: Knowledge joyfully serves and leads the wise toward their true self.
vishnu_gita::121.simple_meaning: The form of knowledge happily serves the divine and helps wise beings move closer to their true self.
vishnu_gita::121.simple_insight: You can trust that knowledge lovingly supports your journey toward deeper connection.
vishnu_gita::121.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes knowledge as a joyful presence always devoted to serving him. This presence actively leads wise beings forward, helping them progress on their spiritual journey toward union with the divine.
vishnu_gita::121.modern_relevance: When you study or reflect deeply, that seeking itself becomes a joyful guide moving you closer to your inner truth.
vishnu_gita::121.insight: It teaches you to see knowledge as a living, loving guide that supports your growth rather than just abstract facts.

vishnu_gita::122.verse_sanskrit:
तथाऽविद्यास्वरूपेण सैव जीवानर्निशम ।
अज्ञानबन्धने बद्ध्वा तेषां बंधनकारणम ॥
vishnu_gita::122.verse_hindi: वे ही पुनः अविद्यारूप से जीवों को अज्ञानबन्धन में अहर्निश फंसाकर उनके बन्धन तथा
vishnu_gita::122.english_translation: They continuously bind living beings in the bondage of ignorance, which itself is the nature of ignorance.
vishnu_gita::122.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / अविद्या (ignorance) / स्वरूपेण (by nature) / सैव (indeed) / जीव (living beings) / अनर् निशम् (unceasingly) / अज्ञानबन्धने (in bondage of ignorance) / बद्ध्वा (binding) / तेषां (their) / बन्धनकारणम (cause of bondage)
vishnu_gita::122.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::122.essence: Ignorance itself continuously traps living beings in bondage.
vishnu_gita::122.simple_meaning: Ignorance is the very cause that continuously traps living beings in bondage, preventing freedom.
vishnu_gita::122.simple_insight: There is a persistent force that keeps you unaware and bound, but it is not your true nature.
vishnu_gita::122.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that living beings remain caught in bondage because ignorance itself continuously traps them. This ignorance is the root cause of their binding, making liberation difficult without wisdom.
vishnu_gita::122.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck in recurring mistakes or patterns, it’s often because deep confusion keeps pulling you back, not your true self.
vishnu_gita::122.insight: Recognize that the obstacles you face are caused by persistent misunderstanding, not your essential being.

vishnu_gita::123.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिस्थिथ्योश्च जगत: कारणं भवति ध्रुवम ।
वस्तुतोऽह निजानन्दप्रकाशाय हि केवलम् ॥
vishnu_gita::123.verse_hindi: जगत की सृष्टि स्थिति का निश्चित कारण बनती हैं। हे श्रेष्ठ देवगण ! वास्तव में केवल
vishnu_gita::123.english_translation: The world’s creation and maintenance definitely have a cause. Indeed, it is solely for the true self’s blissful illumination.
vishnu_gita::123.translation_literal: सृष्टि (creation) स्थित्यः (maintenance) च (and) जगतः (world's) कारणं (cause) भवति (is) ध्रुवम् (certain) । वस्तुतः (indeed) अहं (I) निजानन्द (own bliss) प्रकाशाय (for illumination) हि (indeed) केवलम् (only) ॥
vishnu_gita::123.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::123.essence: The world’s existence depends on the true self’s blissful light as its definite cause.
vishnu_gita::123.simple_meaning: The world’s coming into being and staying stable definitely has a cause, which is the true self shining in bliss.
vishnu_gita::123.simple_insight: There is a definite cause behind everything, rooted in the true self’s joyful light.
vishnu_gita::123.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the existence and continuous presence of the world are caused by something unchanging. He reveals this cause is the blissful illumination of the true self, emphasizing the divine source behind all creation and maintenance.
vishnu_gita::123.modern_relevance: When faced with chaos or uncertainty, remembering that a deeper cause supports existence can bring calm and trust.
vishnu_gita::123.insight: It shifts your view to see the world’s phenomenon as expressions of an underlying blissful reality.

vishnu_gita::124.verse_sanskrit:
धरामि द्वैतरूपं तज्जानीत विबुर्ध्षभा: ।
ममानन्दस्य तस्याऽस्ति महामायैव कारणम् ॥
vishnu_gita::124.verse_hindi: अपने आनन्द के प्रकाश के लिये ही मैं द्वैतरूप को धारण करता हूँ, इस बात को जानो । मेरे उस आनन्द का कारण महामाया ही है
vishnu_gita::124.english_translation: Know that I uphold the dual form to manifest my bliss; the great illusion is the cause of that bliss.
vishnu_gita::124.translation_literal: धरामि (I uphold) / द्वैतरूपं (dual form) / तज्जानीत (know that) / विबुर्ध्षभा: (manifestation, radiance) । / मामनन्दस्य (of my bliss) / तस्याऽस्ति (is of that) / महामायैव (the great illusion itself) / कारणम् (cause) ॥
vishnu_gita::124.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::124.essence: Your experience of duality is the stage for bliss born from great illusion.
vishnu_gita::124.simple_meaning: The divine maintains the appearance of two separate forms so that the bliss of existence can be revealed, and this bliss arises because of the great illusion.
vishnu_gita::124.simple_insight: You sense that your experience of separation is a stage where your deeper joy unfolds.
vishnu_gita::124.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that he assumes the appearance of duality—two forms or aspects—so that his own blissful nature can be experienced. This duality is caused by the great illusion (Maya), which creates the play where joy arises. This teaching situates duality as a purposeful expression, not mere confusion.
vishnu_gita::124.modern_relevance: When you feel divided inside or see the world in opposites, remember that this separation can reveal deeper joy hidden beneath appearances.
vishnu_gita::124.insight: It shifts your view from seeing duality as limitation to understanding it as the stage for bliss to manifest.

vishnu_gita::125.verse_sanskrit:
माच्छत्तिरूपां   या प्राहुर्मूलप्रकृतिरित्यापी ।
विदन्ति प्रकृति तां मे त्रिगुणां तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
vishnu_gita::125.verse_hindi: जिसको मेरी शक्तिरूपिणी और मूलप्रकृति भी कहते हैं। उस मेरी प्रकृति को त्रिगुणमय करके तत्त्वदर्शिगण जानते हैं
vishnu_gita::125.english_translation: My energy, which is also called the original nature, is understood by those with true insight as composed of the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::125.translation_literal: माऽच्छत्तिरूपां (my energy form) या (which) प्राहुः (they call) मूलप्रकृतिरिति (original nature) अपि (also). विदन्ति (know) प्रकृतिं (nature) तां (that) मे (my) त्रिगुणां (three qualities) तत्त्वदर्शिनः (those with true insight).
vishnu_gita::125.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::125.essence: The true self’s original nature is a dynamic energy made of three qualities.
vishnu_gita::125.simple_meaning: The divine power is also the original nature of everything, seen by the wise as made of three fundamental qualities.
vishnu_gita::125.simple_insight: There’s clarity in knowing the true self’s nature is a dynamic energy made of three parts.
vishnu_gita::125.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that his power is also the root nature of all things. Those with clear insight understand this nature as formed from three essential qualities, the three gunas, which shape all existence.
vishnu_gita::125.modern_relevance: When you notice your moods shift between calm, active, or resistant states, you’re sensing the three qualities that shape your inner being.
vishnu_gita::125.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as fixed to seeing your nature as a dynamic balance of three forces.

vishnu_gita::126.verse_sanskrit:
नाना तत्त्वविभाक्तां तां केचन ज्ञानिनो विदु: ।
तामेव प्रकृति केचिच्चतुर्विशतिधा जगुः ॥
vishnu_gita::126.verse_hindi: कोई तत्त्वज्ञानी उसको नानातत्त्वों में विभक्त जानते हैं। कोई तत्वज्ञानी उसी प्रकृति को चतुर्विंश भाग में विभक्त कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::126.english_translation: Some wise ones perceive the supreme reality as divided into many aspects; others describe this same nature as divided into twenty-four parts.
vishnu_gita::126.translation_literal: नाना (many) तत्त्वविभाक्तां (divided into principles) तां (that) केचन (some) ज्ञानिनो (wise ones) विदु: (know) । तामेव (that same) प्रकृति (nature) केचि (some) चतुर्विशतिधा (into twenty-four parts) जगुः (say) ॥
vishnu_gita::126.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::126.essence: The same ultimate nature can be seen as many aspects or as twenty-four parts.
vishnu_gita::126.simple_meaning: The supreme reality can be understood in different ways: some see it as many separate aspects, others as twenty-four parts of one nature.
vishnu_gita::126.simple_insight: It's freeing to know there are many valid ways to see the same ultimate reality.
vishnu_gita::126.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that those who seek wisdom perceive the supreme reality differently. Some divide it into many principles, while others classify it specifically into twenty-four parts, showing varied but valid perspectives on the nature of existence.
vishnu_gita::126.modern_relevance: You might find yourself puzzled by different views on truth or meaning; this reminds you that multiple perspectives can all hold value.
vishnu_gita::126.insight: It teaches you to hold space for diverse understandings without insisting on one absolute view.

vishnu_gita::127.verse_sanskrit:
वस्तुतो मेऽष्टधा  भिन्ना प्राधान्यत्प्रकृतिर्मता ।
जगत्प्रविनी शक्तिर्युमाभिरवधार्य्यताम ॥
vishnu_gita::127.verse_hindi: वास्तव में प्रधानतः मेरी शक्तिरूपिणी जगत्प्रसविनी प्रकृति अष्टया विभक्त है, सो आप जानें
vishnu_gita::127.english_translation: In essence, my power that generates the world is primarily divided into eight aspects, now understand this.
vishnu_gita::127.translation_literal: वस्तुतो (in essence) मेऽष्टधा (eightfold) भिन्ना (divided) प्राधान्यत् (primarily) प्रकृतिर्मता (is the nature/opinion) । जगत् (world) प्रविनी (generating) शक्ति (power) युमाभि (by you) अवधार्यताम (be understood) ॥
vishnu_gita::127.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::127.essence: The creative power behind the world divides into eight main aspects.
vishnu_gita::127.simple_meaning: The divine power that creates the world is mainly split into eight different parts. This is important to know.
vishnu_gita::127.simple_insight: Knowing the many sides of creation's power helps you see complexity behind what seems simple.
vishnu_gita::127.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals to his listener that the cosmic creative power responsible for the world is not singular but divided into eight essential aspects. This sets the stage for deeper explanation of these aspects.
vishnu_gita::127.insight: It shifts understanding from a unitary view of creation to recognizing multiple fundamental forces at play.

vishnu_gita::128.verse_sanskrit:
अन्या चेतनमय्यस्ति प्रकृतिर्जीवमुक्तिदा ।
उक्ताष्टप्रकृर्तेर्भिना यां ही पश्यन्ति योगिन: ॥
vishnu_gita::128.verse_hindi: और चेतनमयी प्रकृति जो जीव को मुक्त करती है, वह इससे अलग है जिसको योगी लोग उक्त आठ प्रकार की प्रकृति से भिन्न देखते हैं
vishnu_gita::128.english_translation: The conscious nature that grants liberation is different from the eight types of nature seen by yogis.
vishnu_gita::128.translation_literal: अन्या (different) / चेतनमय्यः (conscious nature) / अस्ति (is) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / जीवम् (living being) / मुक्तिदा (giver of liberation) / उक्त-आष्ट (mentioned eight) / प्रकृर्तेर्भिः (types of nature) / या (which) / हि (indeed) / पश्यन्ति (see) / योगिनः (yogis)
vishnu_gita::128.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::128.essence: True liberation comes from a conscious nature beyond all known types of nature.
vishnu_gita::128.simple_meaning: There is a conscious nature that frees the true self, which is different from the eight types of nature yogis usually recognize.
vishnu_gita::128.simple_insight: Freedom comes from recognizing a deeper reality beyond usual perceptions.
vishnu_gita::128.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the conscious nature which grants liberation differs from the eight material or functional types of nature that yogis observe; this points to a higher transcendent reality beyond common experience.
vishnu_gita::128.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck in familiar patterns or identities, know there is a deeper freedom beyond what you usually perceive.
vishnu_gita::128.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with known natural forms to seeking the transcendent source of liberation.

vishnu_gita::129.verse_sanskrit:
मम प्रकृतिसम्भूतसंसारस्य सुरर्षभाः ।
सृष्टिः प्रवाहरूपेण ह्यनाद्यन्ता प्रकीर्तिता ॥
vishnu_gita::129.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! मेरी प्रकृति से उत्पन्न इस संसार की सृष्टि प्रवाह रूप से ही अनादि अनन्त कही गई है
vishnu_gita::129.english_translation: O divine beings! The creation of this world born from my nature is described as an endless, continuous flow without beginning or end.
vishnu_gita::129.translation_literal: मम (my) / प्रकृतिसम्भूतसंसारस्य (of the world born from nature) / सुरर्षभाः (O foremost of the divine beings) / सृष्टिः (creation) / प्रवाहरूपेण (as a flowing stream) / हि (indeed) / अनाद्यन्ता (without beginning or end) / प्रकीर्तिता (is described)
vishnu_gita::129.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::129.essence: Creation flows endlessly from divine nature without beginning or end.
vishnu_gita::129.simple_meaning: The world created from my nature flows endlessly, having no beginning or end.
vishnu_gita::129.simple_insight: The endless flow of creation invites acceptance of constant change beyond limits.
vishnu_gita::129.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, explaining that the manifest world arises from his nature as an unceasing, eternal flow, highlighting the timeless and infinite character of creation itself.
vishnu_gita::129.insight: Recognize that the world and its changes are part of an infinite, ongoing process beyond your control.

vishnu_gita::130.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माण्डसमूह के अनन्त होने पर भी प्रत्येक ब्रह्माण्ड की ही उत्पत्ति स्थिति और लय,
vishnu_gita::130.english_translation: Even though the cosmic systems are infinite, each has its own cycle of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::130.translation_literal: अपि (even) / ब्रह्माण्डमयस् (cosmic systems) / अनन्तत्वे (in infinity) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / मम (my) / प्रतिब्रह्माण्डम् (each cosmic system) / एव (indeed) / असौ (that) / सृष्टि (creation) / स्थिति (preservation) / लयम् (dissolution) / खलु (indeed)
vishnu_gita::130.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::130.essence: Infinite worlds exist, each with its own cycle of creation and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::130.simple_meaning: Though cosmic systems are infinite, each has its own process of arising, sustaining, and dissolving.
vishnu_gita::130.simple_insight: There's a unique rhythm to every cycle of existence, even within endlessness.
vishnu_gita::130.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that countless universes exist, each with its own cycle of birth, maintenance, and end. This moment reveals the vastness and ordered diversity beyond what we see.
vishnu_gita::130.modern_relevance: You notice how different projects or phases in life begin, grow, and end uniquely, even when many seem endless.
vishnu_gita::130.insight: It teaches you to see cycles as natural and unique, helping you accept change without resistance.

vishnu_gita::131.verse_sanskrit:
स्वयं करोति दुर्जेया जीवैर्मद्वशत्तिनी।
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशानां रूपेणाऽहं सहायवान् ॥
vishnu_gita::131.verse_hindi: जीवों के द्वारा दुर्ज्ञेया यह मेरी प्रकृति मेरे वश में रहकर स्वयं ही करती है।  मैं ही ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश रूप से
vishnu_gita::131.english_translation: My nature acts on its own through living beings who are difficult to control, yet they remain under my influence. I am Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesha in form, the one who supports all.
vishnu_gita::131.translation_literal: स्वयं (self) / करोति (does) / दुर्जेया (difficult to control) / जीवैः (by living beings) / मद्वशत्तिनी (under my control) / ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशानां (of Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesha) / रूपेण (in the form) / अहं (I) / सहायवान् (supporter)
vishnu_gita::131.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::131.essence: Even difficult actions arise through my nature, supported by my cosmic forms.
vishnu_gita::131.simple_meaning: My nature moves through living beings who are hard to control, yet they act within my influence. I am the support in the forms of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesha.
vishnu_gita::131.simple_insight: There is reassurance knowing a greater support guides even what seems uncontrollable.
vishnu_gita::131.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that although living beings act in unpredictable and difficult ways, their actions occur within the scope of his influence. He reveals his cosmic presence as the combined forms of creation, preservation, and transformation, supporting all existence.
vishnu_gita::131.insight: Recognize that your apparent lack of control is still within a larger, supportive reality.

vishnu_gita::132.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिस्थितिलये वर्ते प्रतिब्रह्मंडेव हि ।
स्वस्वशक्तचाश्रयान्नूनं त्रय एते हि हेतवः ॥
vishnu_gita::132.verse_hindi: प्रत्येक ब्रह्माण्ड में सृष्टि स्थिति और लय में सहायक रहता हूँ ! हे श्रेष्ठ देवगण !
vishnu_gita::132.english_translation: I support each universe through creation, maintenance, and dissolution, O supreme radiant beings!
vishnu_gita::132.translation_literal: सृष्टि (creation) / स्थिति (maintenance) / लय (dissolution) / वर्ते (exist) / प्रतिब्रह्मंडे (in each universe) / हि (indeed) / स्वस्वशक्त (own power) / आश्रयन् (support) / नूनं (certainly) / त्रय (three) / एते (these) / हि (indeed) / हेतवः (causes)
vishnu_gita::132.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::132.essence: The divine power continuously sustains all universes through creation, preservation, and destruction.
vishnu_gita::132.simple_meaning: The divine supports every universe through the processes of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::132.simple_insight: Everything around you is sustained by a continuous cycle beyond your sight.
vishnu_gita::132.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes his role sustaining countless universes by overseeing their birth, existence, and destruction, addressing radiant divine beings to reveal the cosmic scale of this support.
vishnu_gita::132.insight: It shows the vast, ongoing cycles that underlie all existence, inviting awe beyond daily concerns.

vishnu_gita::133.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिस्थितिल्याना वै भवन्ति सुरसत्तमा:
ब्रह्मा मच्छक्तिमाश्रित्य जीवकर्मानुसारतः ॥
vishnu_gita::133.verse_hindi: स्थिति और लय के कारण होते हैं। हे देवगण ! ब्रह्मा मेरी शक्ति का आश्रय लेकर जीवों के पूर्वकर्म के अनुसार
vishnu_gita::133.english_translation: Creation, preservation, and destruction arise from me; Brahma acts by my power according to beings' past actions.
vishnu_gita::133.translation_literal: सृष्टि (creation) / स्थिति (preservation) / लय (destruction) / कारण (cause) / होते (are) / हैं (are) / सुरसत्तमा (O best of the gods) / ब्रह्मा (Brahma) / मच्छक्तिमाश्रित्य (taking my power as refuge) / जीवकर्मानुसारतः (according to the beings' karma)
vishnu_gita::133.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::133.essence: Cosmic cycles flow through divine power guided by beings' past actions.
vishnu_gita::133.simple_meaning: Creation, preservation, and destruction happen through the divine power. Brahma works by that power following beings' past actions.
vishnu_gita::133.simple_insight: You see the world changing because of a greater power and past actions influencing the present.
vishnu_gita::133.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the cosmic processes of creation, preservation, and destruction happen through his power. Brahma, the creator god, acts under this power guided by the past actions of living beings. This verse reveals the divine coordination behind cosmic cycles.
vishnu_gita::133.modern_relevance: When you witness change and cycles in life, recognize a greater force at work guiding events beyond your control.
vishnu_gita::133.insight: Understand that actions have consequences operating within a greater cosmic order beyond individual control.

vishnu_gita::134.verse_sanskrit:
तथा स्वाभाविकं कर्माप्रवाहं प्रकृतेः सुराः ।
आश्रित्य तनुते नित्यं स्थावरं जङ्गमं जगत् ॥
vishnu_gita::134.verse_hindi: तथा प्रकृति के स्वाभाविक कर्म-प्रवाह का अवलम्बन करके स्थावर जङ्गमात्मक संसार को सदा विस्तार करते हैं
vishnu_gita::134.english_translation: The radiant beings continuously extend the moving and unmoving world by naturally following the flow of actions of the natural world.
vishnu_gita::134.translation_literal: तथा (thus) / स्वाभाविकं (natural) / कर्माप्रवाहं (flow of actions) / प्रकृतेः (of nature) / सुराः (radiant beings) / आश्रित्य (relying on) / तनुते (extend) / नित्यं (always) / स्थावरं (unmoving) / जङ्गमं (moving) / जगत् (world)
vishnu_gita::134.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::134.essence: Radiant beings sustain the world by naturally following nature’s flow of actions.
vishnu_gita::134.simple_meaning: Radiant beings continuously maintain and expand the world by following the natural flow of nature’s actions.
vishnu_gita::134.simple_insight: There is a steady, natural flow behind how everything in the world keeps moving and growing.
vishnu_gita::134.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how the radiant beings depend on the natural flow of nature’s actions to constantly sustain and expand both the moving and unmoving aspects of the world.
vishnu_gita::134.insight: It shows how aligning with natural rhythms supports ongoing growth and stability in life and surroundings.

vishnu_gita::135.verse_sanskrit:
उद्भिदः स्वेदजस्याथ झण्डजस्य तथा सुराः ।
जरायुजस्य मर्त्ताना पितृणां भवतां तथा ॥
vishnu_gita::135.verse_hindi: हे देव गण ! उद्भिज, स्वेदज, अण्डज, जरायुज, मनुष्य, पितृ, देवता
vishnu_gita::135.english_translation: O divine beings! There are born from sprouts, sweat-born, egg-born, womb-born, human, ancestors, and gods.
vishnu_gita::135.translation_literal: उद्भिदः (sprout-born) / स्वेदजस्याथ (sweat-born too) / झण्डजस्य (egg-born) / तथा (also) / सुराः (gods) / जरायुजस्य (womb-born) / मर्त्ताना (humans) / पितृणां (ancestors) / भवतां (of beings) / तथा (also)
vishnu_gita::135.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::135.essence: Life arises through diverse origins across many forms of beings.
vishnu_gita::135.simple_meaning: There are many kinds of beings born in different ways: from plants, sweat, eggs, wombs, humans, ancestors, and divine beings.
vishnu_gita::135.simple_insight: Life emerges in many forms and origins, showing nature’s vast diversity.
vishnu_gita::135.detailed_meaning: The narrator lists categories of beings based on their birth methods, including plants, sweat-born, egg-born creatures, womb-born humans, ancestors, and gods, illustrating the variety of life forms known in the story.
vishnu_gita::135.insight: Recognize the vast array of life forms and origins beyond just human birth.

vishnu_gita::136.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्वज्ञानोपदेष्ट्रणामृषीणां चैव सर्वशः।
ब्रह्मैव कुरुते सृष्टिं महामायाप्रभावतः ॥
vishnu_gita::136.verse_hindi: और 'तत्वज्ञानोपदेशक ऋषियो की, इन सब प्रकार की सृष्टि को ब्रह्माजी ही महामाया के प्रभाव से करते हैं
vishnu_gita::136.english_translation: All sages who teach knowledge of reality agree: the supreme reality alone creates all existence through great illusion.
vishnu_gita::136.translation_literal: तत्त्वज्ञानोपदेष्ट्रणामृषीणां (of sages who teach knowledge of reality) चैव (and) सर्वशः (completely) ब्रह्मैव (only Brahman/supreme reality) कुरुते (creates) सृष्टिं (creation) महामायाप्रभावतः (by the power of great illusion).
vishnu_gita::136.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::136.essence: The supreme reality alone creates all existence through a powerful cosmic illusion.
vishnu_gita::136.simple_meaning: All great teachers agree that the supreme reality alone creates the entire universe through a powerful veil of illusion.
vishnu_gita::136.simple_insight: There is a shared source behind all things, even if appearances seem many and separate.
vishnu_gita::136.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that every sage who teaches about reality agrees that the supreme reality alone is responsible for all creation, which arises through a powerful cosmic illusion called great illusion (mahamaya). This explains why the world appears diverse though it is rooted in one source.
vishnu_gita::136.modern_relevance: When you see chaos or separation around you, remember that all things come from a single source shaping appearances like a powerful illusion.
vishnu_gita::136.insight: It invites you to see beyond appearances and recognize a unified source behind diversity, shifting your view from fragmentation to oneness.

vishnu_gita::137.verse_sanskrit:
इमे मन्मायया भ्रान्ताः सृष्टिचक्रे भ्रमन्त्यहो।
यूयं सर्वेऽपि मन्मायामोहिताः स्थ विशेषतः ॥
vishnu_gita::137.verse_hindi: अहो ! मेरी माया से भूले हुए ये सब सृष्टिचक्र मे घूमते रहते हैं। आप सब भी मेरी माया से विशेष विमोहित हैं
vishnu_gita::137.english_translation: Alas! All these beings wander confused in the cycle of creation by my illusion. You too are especially deluded by my illusion.
vishnu_gita::137.translation_literal: इमे (these) मन्मायया (by my illusion) भ्रान्ताः (confused) सृष्टिचक्रे (in the cycle of creation) भ्रमन्ति (wander) अहो (alas) । यूयं (you all) सर्वेऽपि (also all) मन्मायामोहिताः (deluded by my illusion) विशेषतः (especially) ॥
vishnu_gita::137.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::137.essence: Confusion and endless wandering arise from being caught in the divine's illusion.
vishnu_gita::137.simple_meaning: All beings are trapped, confused in the cycle of creation due to the divine's illusion, including you especially.
vishnu_gita::137.simple_insight: There is a gentle sadness in seeing how deeply illusion misleads us all.
vishnu_gita::137.detailed_meaning: Vishnu speaks of all beings caught in the cycle of rebirth and confusion caused by his divine illusion. He points out that you, the listener, are particularly caught in this delusion, highlighting the challenge of seeing clearly.
vishnu_gita::137.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck in repetitive patterns and confusion, it’s often because unseen illusions shape your view more than you realize.
vishnu_gita::137.insight: It teaches you to recognize that much confusion comes from unseen illusions shaping perception.

vishnu_gita::138.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिचक्रविवेकन्तु निबोधत समाहिताः ।
यमत्र सन्निधौ देवाः ! भवतां प्रब्रवीम्यहम् ॥
vishnu_gita::138.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! आपलोगों के समीप जिस सृष्टिचक्र के विवेक को मैं यहाँ कहता हूँ उसको सावधान होकर समझो
vishnu_gita::138.english_translation: O beings of light! Attentively understand here the discernment of the cycle of creation I now explain before you.
vishnu_gita::138.translation_literal: सृष्टिचक्रविवेकन्तु (creation-cycle discernment) निबोधत (understand) समाहिताः (composed) यमत्र (here) सन्निधौ (in presence) देवाः (beings of light) भवतां (your) प्रब्रवीम्यहम् (I speak)
vishnu_gita::138.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::138.essence: Calm, focused attention is essential to understand the cycle of creation.
vishnu_gita::138.simple_meaning: Listen carefully with a calm mind to understand the workings of the cycle of creation explained here.
vishnu_gita::138.simple_insight: Calm attention opens the way to truly grasp complex cycles around you.
vishnu_gita::138.detailed_meaning: Before a gathering of radiant beings, Vishnu invites them to calmly and attentively understand the deep truth of creation's recurring cycle he is about to reveal.
vishnu_gita::138.modern_relevance: In a noisy world, pausing with steady focus helps you grasp complex patterns you otherwise miss.
vishnu_gita::138.insight: It teaches you to steady your mind to perceive deeper truths beyond surface distractions.

vishnu_gita::139.verse_sanskrit:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद ब्रह्मणो विदुः।
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः॥
vishnu_gita::139.verse_hindi: सहस्त्रयुग पर्यन्त ब्रह्मा का जो एक दिन उसको जो जानते हैं एवं सहस्त्रयुगान्ता जो रात्रि उसको जो जानते हैं, वह लोग अहोरात्रवेत्ता हैं
vishnu_gita::139.english_translation: Those who know the day of Brahma lasting a thousand yugas and the night ending after a thousand yugas are the true knowers of day and night.
vishnu_gita::139.translation_literal: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तम् (lasting a thousand yugas) / अहस्यद (day) / ब्रह्मणः (of Brahma) / विदुः (know) / रात्रिं (night) / युगसहस्रान्ताम् (ending after a thousand yugas) / ते (those) / अहोरात्रविदः (knowers of day and night) / जनाः (people)
vishnu_gita::139.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::139.essence: True understanding of day and night comes from grasping vast cosmic time cycles.
vishnu_gita::139.simple_meaning: Some people understand that one day and night of Brahma each last thousands of cosmic cycles, showing deeper knowledge of time.
vishnu_gita::139.simple_insight: There's awe and clarity in realizing time is vast and cyclical beyond everyday hours.
vishnu_gita::139.detailed_meaning: This verse reveals that true knowledge of day and night comes from grasping the immense cosmic cycles Brahma experiences, each lasting thousands of yugas, framing human time within vast cosmic rhythms.
vishnu_gita::139.modern_relevance: When feeling pressed by daily deadlines, remembering that time flows in immense, repeating cycles can ease pressure and expand perspective.
vishnu_gita::139.insight: It shifts your mind from short-term urgency to appreciating vast cosmic rhythms and cycles.

vishnu_gita::140.verse_sanskrit:
अव्यक्ताद व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहगगमे ।
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ने तत्रैवाव्यत्तसंज्ञके ॥
vishnu_gita::140.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा के दिन के आरम्भ में अव्यक्त से सब व्यक्त (चराचर प्राणिमात्र ) प्रादुर्भूत होते हैं एवं ब्रह्मा की रात्रि के प्रारम्भ में उसी अव्यक्तस्वरूप में ही लीन हो जाते हैं
vishnu_gita::140.english_translation: At the start of Brahma's day, all manifest from the unmanifest and return to it at nightfall.
vishnu_gita::140.translation_literal: अव्यक्ताद (from the unmanifest) व्यक्तयः (manifest beings) सर्वाः (all) प्रभवन्ति (arise) अहगगमे (at the start of the day) । रात्र्यागमे (at the start of the night) प्रलीयन्ते (dissolve) तत्रैव (there itself) अव्यत्तसंज्ञके (called unmanifest) ॥
vishnu_gita::140.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::140.essence: All existence cycles between the unseen unmanifest and the manifest world repeatedly.
vishnu_gita::140.simple_meaning: All living beings come into existence from the unmanifest state when Brahma's day begins and dissolve back into it at night.
vishnu_gita::140.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing all forms arise and fade back into a deeper reality.
vishnu_gita::140.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the cosmic cycle where all beings manifest from the unmanifest state at the start of Brahma's day and dissolve back into it at night, symbolizing the eternal rhythm of creation and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::140.modern_relevance: You watch the day begin and end, noticing how everything around you appears, changes, and quietly fades away again.
vishnu_gita::140.insight: It shifts your view from clinging to appearances toward seeing all as temporary expressions of a deeper ground.

vishnu_gita::141.verse_sanskrit:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।
रात्रयागमेऽवशो देवाः ! प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
vishnu_gita::141.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! वही व्यक्त सचराचर सब प्राणिवर्ग बारम्बार जन्म ग्रहण करके रात्रि के समागम होने पर लीन होते हैं एवं दिन के प्रारम्भ में अपने अपने कर्मादि के वश होकर उत्पन होते हैं
vishnu_gita::141.english_translation: O radiant beings, all living and non-living beings repeatedly take birth, dissolve at nightfall, and arise again with the dawn, driven by their actions.
vishnu_gita::141.translation_literal: भूतग्रामः (group of beings) स (that) एवायं (indeed) भूत्वा (becoming) भूत्वा (becoming) प्रलीयते (dissolves) । रात्रयागमेऽवशः (at nightfall) देवाः (deities) ! प्रभवत्यहरागमे (arise at daybreak) ॥
vishnu_gita::141.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::141.essence: All beings endlessly dissolve and arise daily, driven by their past actions.
vishnu_gita::141.simple_meaning: All beings continually cycle through birth and death, dissolving each night and arising each day, driven by their actions.
vishnu_gita::141.simple_insight: Life flows in cycles beyond your control, shaped by actions beyond each moment.
vishnu_gita::141.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, describing the endless cycle where all living and non-living forms repeatedly come into existence, dissolve at night, and reappear at dawn, governed by the power of their actions. This sets a cosmic rhythm of birth and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::141.modern_relevance: You notice how every day ends and begins anew, like your thoughts and feelings that dissolve and arise without your bidding.
vishnu_gita::141.insight: Recognize the repetitive cycle of arising and passing beyond your immediate control, shaped by past actions.

vishnu_gita::142.verse_sanskrit:
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तो व्यक्तात्सनातनः ।
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्स्वपि न नश्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::142.verse_hindi: किन्तु उस व्यक्तभाव से भी श्रेष्ठ अतीन्द्रिय अनादि जो एकभाव है वह सकल प्राणियों के नष्ट होने पर भी नष्ट नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::142.english_translation: Beyond the manifest form, there is another unmanifest eternal state that pervades all beings and does not perish even when they perish.
vishnu_gita::142.translation_literal: परस्तस्मात् (beyond that) तु (indeed) भावः (state) अन्यः (another) अव्यक्तः (unmanifest) व्यक्तात् (from the manifest) सनातनः (eternal) यः (who) स (he) सर्वेषु (in all) भूतेषु (beings) नश्यत् (perishes) स्वपि (even) न (not) नश्यति (perishes)
vishnu_gita::142.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::142.essence: An eternal, unmanifest essence pervades all beings and never truly disappears.
vishnu_gita::142.simple_meaning: There is a timeless, unchanging reality beyond everything that appears, which does not vanish even when all living beings perish.
vishnu_gita::142.simple_insight: You can feel steady knowing your true nature is eternal beyond life’s changes.
vishnu_gita::142.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that beyond the visible, changing world, there is an unmanifest eternal essence that persists beyond the death or disappearance of all beings, pointing to a deeper reality beyond physical forms.
vishnu_gita::142.modern_relevance: When everything around you changes or disappears, you can find comfort knowing there is a part of you that never fades.
vishnu_gita::142.insight: This verse shifts your focus from fleeting appearances to the unchanging eternal essence within and beyond all life.

vishnu_gita::143.verse_sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् ।
ये प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
vishnu_gita::143.verse_hindi: जो अव्यक्त अर्थात् अतीन्द्रिय भाव अक्षर कहा गया है उसको परम गति अर्थात् परमपुरुषार्थ कहते हैं, जिसको प्राप्त होकर पुनः प्रत्यावर्तित होना नहीं होता है वह मेरा ही परमधाम है।
vishnu_gita::143.english_translation: That which is unmanifested and imperishable is called the supreme destination; those who attain it do not return. That supreme abode is mine.
vishnu_gita::143.translation_literal: अव्यक्तः (unmanifested) अक्षर (imperishable) इति (thus) उक्तः (called) तम् (that) आहुः (they say) परमाम् (supreme) गतिम् (destination) । ये (those who) प्राप्य (having attained) न (not) निवर्तन्ते (return) तद्धाम् (that abode) परमम् (supreme) मम (mine) ॥
vishnu_gita::143.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::143.essence: The unchanging, unmanifest supreme state is the final destination where return ceases.
vishnu_gita::143.simple_meaning: There is a supreme state beyond all forms and change, eternal and unchanging. Once you reach it, you do not come back to the cycle of change. This supreme state is the highest dwelling, belonging to the divine.
vishnu_gita::143.simple_insight: There is a peaceful, lasting destination beyond all appearances, where returning is no longer needed.
vishnu_gita::143.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the ultimate reality as unmanifest and imperishable, a supreme destination beyond the visible world. Those who realize this highest state transcend the cycle of returning and change. This moment in the scripture reveals the nature of the final, unchanging abode of the divine.
vishnu_gita::143.modern_relevance: When life feels full of constant change and restlessness, knowing there is a final, peaceful place beyond all upheaval brings deep calm and hope.
vishnu_gita::143.insight: It shifts your view from chasing temporary results to seeking lasting, unchanging presence beyond all appearances.

vishnu_gita::144.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुषः स परो देवो भक्तया लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया।
यस्यान्तः स्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
vishnu_gita::144.verse_hindi: हे देव गण! जिसमें भूतगण (प्राणिमात्र) स्थित हैं एवं जो इस सकल जगत् में व्याप्त है वह परमपुरुष एकान्तभक्ति द्वारा ही प्राप्य है
vishnu_gita::144.english_translation: The supreme being, within whom all creatures reside and who pervades the entire universe, is attained only through exclusive devotion.
vishnu_gita::144.translation_literal: पुरुषः (the supreme being) / स (that) / परो (supreme) / देवो (being) / भक्तया (through devotion) / लभ्यः (attainable) / तु (indeed) / अनन्यया (exclusive) / यस्य (whose) / अन्तः (within) / स्थानि (reside) / भूतानि (all creatures) / येन (by whom) / सर्वम् (all) / इदं (this) / ततम् (pervaded)
vishnu_gita::144.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::144.essence: The supreme presence within all is reached only through exclusive devotion.
vishnu_gita::144.simple_meaning: The supreme being who lives within all creatures and fills the entire world can only be reached by wholehearted, exclusive devotion.
vishnu_gita::144.simple_insight: You feel the power of devotion as the unique path to connection with the supreme presence.
vishnu_gita::144.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the supreme being pervades everything and everyone. The only way to truly reach this presence is through singular, devoted love, excluding any divided attention or distractions.
vishnu_gita::144.modern_relevance: When your heart focuses completely on what matters most, you access a deeper connection beyond distractions.
vishnu_gita::144.insight: It shifts your practice from scattered efforts to a focused, exclusive devotion as the key to deeper experience.

vishnu_gita::145.verse_sanskrit:
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि दृश्यतां योग ऐश्वरः।
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥
vishnu_gita::145.verse_hindi: मेरे ऐश्वरीय योग को देखो, सकलप्राणी मुझ में अवस्थित होकर भी अवस्थित नहीं हैं अर्थात् मैं उनसे निर्लिप्त हूँ, मैं भूतधारक और भूतपालक हूँ तथापि भूतगण में मैं अवस्थित नहीं हूँ
vishnu_gita::145.english_translation: Behold my sovereign yoga: all beings abide in me yet are not truly established in me; I sustain and nurture them but am not established among them.
vishnu_gita::145.translation_literal: न (not) / च (and) / मत्स्थानि (in me established) / भूतानि (beings) / दृश्यतां (should be seen) / योग (yoga) / ऐश्वरः (sovereign) / भूतभृन्न (supporter of beings) / च (and) / भूतस्थो (established among beings) / ममात्मा (my self) / भूतभावनः (beings nurturer)
vishnu_gita::145.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::145.essence: You can uphold all beings without being established or trapped among them.
vishnu_gita::145.simple_meaning: Though everything exists within you and you support all life, you remain detached and not limited by them.
vishnu_gita::145.simple_insight: You can care deeply without losing your sense of self or becoming entangled.
vishnu_gita::145.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals his cosmic role: he upholds all living beings but remains untouched and independent from their changing states, showing the divine balance of engagement without attachment.
vishnu_gita::145.modern_relevance: You care for others deeply but stay centered when emotions and demands try to overwhelm you.
vishnu_gita::145.insight: It teaches you to engage fully in supporting life without losing your inner freedom or sense of separateness.

vishnu_gita::146.verse_sanskrit:
यथाकाशस्थिनो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् ।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीन्युपधार्यताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::146.verse_hindi: सर्व व्यापी और महान वायु जिस प्रकार आकाश में नित्य स्थित सकल भूत भी वैस ही मुझमें अवस्थित हैं ऐसा समझो
vishnu_gita::146.english_translation: Just as the vast and eternal wind pervades the sky, all beings also dwell in Me.
vishnu_gita::146.translation_literal: यथा (just as) आकाशस्थिनो (residing in the sky) नित्यं (eternal) वायुः (wind) सर्वत्रगो (moving everywhere) महान् (great) । तथा (so) सर्वाणि (all) भूतानि (beings) मत्स्थानि (in Me residing) उपधार्यताम् (should be understood) ॥
vishnu_gita::146.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::146.essence: All beings dwell within the divine as wind dwells eternally in the vast sky.
vishnu_gita::146.simple_meaning: All living beings exist within the divine presence just as the wind constantly fills the vast sky.
vishnu_gita::146.simple_insight: You are connected to everything, endlessly present like the wind in the sky.
vishnu_gita::146.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the wind, though unseen, pervades the entire sky constantly. Similarly, all beings exist within the divine essence, showing the unity and omnipresence of the true self.
vishnu_gita::146.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated, remember you are as connected and present everywhere as the wind in the open sky.
vishnu_gita::146.insight: It shifts your view from separation to recognizing your presence within all things like the omnipresent wind.

vishnu_gita::147.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वभूतानि गीर्वाणाः ! प्रकृति यान्ति मामिकाम् ।
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥
vishnu_gita::147.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! प्रलयकाल में सब भूतगण मेरी प्रकृति को प्राप्त होते हैं एवं पुनः सृष्टि के प्रारम्भ में मैं उनको उत्पन्न करता हूँ
vishnu_gita::147.english_translation: O divine beings! At the time of dissolution, all beings return to my nature, and at the beginning of creation, I manifest them again.
vishnu_gita::147.translation_literal: सर्वभूतानि (all beings) गीर्वाणाः (O divine beings) ! प्रकृति (nature) यान्ति (go) मामिकाम् (to my own) । कल्पक्षये (at the destruction of the kalpa) पुनः (again) तानि (they) कल्पादौ (at the beginning of the kalpa) विसृजामि (I manifest) अहम् (I) ॥
vishnu_gita::147.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::147.essence: All beings dissolve into and emerge anew from divine nature in endless cycles.
vishnu_gita::147.simple_meaning: All beings dissolve back into the divine nature at the end of a cycle and are recreated by the divine at the next beginning.
vishnu_gita::147.simple_insight: There is a continuous cycle where everything returns and begins anew through the divine nature.
vishnu_gita::147.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, explaining how at the end of cosmic cycles all beings merge back into his nature, and at new beginnings, he brings them forth again, revealing the eternal cycle of dissolution and creation.
vishnu_gita::147.insight: It shows the natural rhythm of endings and beginnings, teaching acceptance of change as part of a greater whole.

vishnu_gita::148.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृति स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः ।
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥
vishnu_gita::148.verse_hindi: मैं अपनी प्रकृति में अधिष्ठान करके स्वभाव वश होकर कर्मादि परवश इन समस्त भूतगण की पुनः पुनः सृष्टि करता रहता हूँ
vishnu_gita::148.english_translation: I establish myself in my own nature and, compelled by it, repeatedly create all these groups of beings through action.
vishnu_gita::148.translation_literal: प्रकृति (nature) स्वाम (own) अवष्टभ्य (establishing) विसृजामि (I create) पुनः पुनः (again and again) । भूतग्राममिमं (these groups of beings) कृत्स्नम् (entire) अवशम् (compelled) प्रकृतेर्वशात् (by nature's power) ॥
vishnu_gita::148.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::148.essence: Creation arises naturally from being established in one's own nature, beyond separate will.
vishnu_gita::148.simple_meaning: The divine establishes itself in its own nature and, driven by that nature, continuously creates all beings through action.
vishnu_gita::148.simple_insight: You can feel the flow of creation moving through you beyond your conscious control.
vishnu_gita::148.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that he rests within his own nature (Prakriti) and from there, compelled by its force, continuously creates all living beings. This shows creation as a natural, ongoing process flowing from the divine's inherent nature, not an act of separate will.
vishnu_gita::148.modern_relevance: When you act and create repeatedly, it often feels less like your individual choice and more like a natural flow beyond your control.
vishnu_gita::148.insight: It shifts your perspective from seeing yourself as a separate doer to recognizing being part of a larger natural process.

vishnu_gita::149.verse_sanskrit:
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति दिवौकसः ।
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥
vishnu_gita::149.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! उन सब कर्मों में अनासक्त और उदासीनवत् अवस्थित मुझको वह सब कर्म बाँध नहीं सकते हैं
vishnu_gita::149.english_translation: O divine beings! Those actions do not bind me, who remain detached and indifferent to them.
vishnu_gita::149.translation_literal: न (not) / च (and) / मां (me) / तानि (those) / कर्माणि (actions) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / दिवौकसः (divine beings) / उदासीनवत् (like indifferent) / उदासीनम् (indifferent) / असक्तं (detached) / तेषु (in them) / कर्मसु (actions)
vishnu_gita::149.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::149.essence: You can be fully active yet remain detached and free from binding consequences.
vishnu_gita::149.simple_meaning: You can act without being attached or emotionally involved, so those actions do not trap or bind you.
vishnu_gita::149.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing you can act fully yet remain unaffected inside.
vishnu_gita::149.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that when one performs actions without attachment or emotional involvement, those actions do not bind or limit the true self. This teaching encourages acting with detachment.
vishnu_gita::149.modern_relevance: You finish a difficult task but don't obsess over praise or failure; your peace stays intact regardless.
vishnu_gita::149.insight: It teaches you to act without emotional investment, separating your identity from outcomes.

vishnu_gita::150.verse_sanskrit:
मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम ।
हेतुनाऽनेन वै देवाः ! जगद्विपरिवर्त्तते ॥
vishnu_gita::150.verse_hindi: मेरे अधिष्ठान से प्रकृति चराचर सहित विश्व को उत्पन्न करती है हे देवगण ! इस कारण जगत् बारम्बार उत्पन्न होता है
vishnu_gita::150.english_translation: Under my guidance, nature creates the moving and unmoving world; for this reason, the world undergoes continual change, O radiant beings.
vishnu_gita::150.translation_literal: मयाऽध्यक्षेण (under my guidance) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / सूयते (creates) / सचराचरम (moving and unmoving) / हेतुनाऽनेन (by this cause) / वै (indeed) / देवाः (O radiant beings) / जगद्विपरिवर्त्तते (the world undergoes change)
vishnu_gita::150.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::150.essence: The world changes endlessly because nature acts under a higher guidance.
vishnu_gita::150.simple_meaning: Nature, guided by the divine, creates all life and matter, causing the world to keep changing endlessly.
vishnu_gita::150.simple_insight: The world’s constant change happens because of a deeper guiding force working through nature.
vishnu_gita::150.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that under his guidance, Prakriti (nature) produces all moving and unmoving things, explaining why the universe continually arises and dissolves.
vishnu_gita::150.insight: Recognize that constant change happens through a guiding source beyond what appears, deepening acceptance.

vishnu_gita::151.verse_sanskrit:
न मे विदर्भवन्तो हि प्रभवं न महर्षयः ।
अहमादिहि वो देवाः ! महीणाञ्च सर्वशः ॥
vishnu_gita::151.verse_hindi: मेरा प्रभव (आविर्भाव) तुमको अवगत नहीं है महर्षिगण को भी अवगत नहीं है क्योंकि मैं हे देवगण ! तुम लोगों का और महर्षिगण का सर्व प्रकार से आदि हूँ
vishnu_gita::151.english_translation: Neither the sages nor the Vidarbha folk know my origin; I am the origin of you all and the sages in every way.
vishnu_gita::151.translation_literal: न (not) मे (my) विदर्भवन्तः (Vidarbha folk) हि (indeed) प्रभवं (origin) न (nor) महर्षयः (great sages) । अहम् (I) आदिः (origin) हि (indeed) वो (you) देवाः (devas) ! महीणाञ्च (and of the sages) सर्वशः (in every way) ॥
vishnu_gita::151.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::151.essence: The ultimate origin is beyond all knowledge, yet it is the source of all beings.
vishnu_gita::151.simple_meaning: No one, including the great sages or the people of Vidarbha, fully knows my origin. I am the source of everything and everyone.
vishnu_gita::151.simple_insight: Knowing that the ultimate origin is beyond even great sages brings humility and wonder.
vishnu_gita::151.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu declares that neither the wise sages nor the people of Vidarbha know his true origin. He asserts that he is the primal source of all beings, including the sages and the divine beings, emphasizing his supreme and mysterious nature.
vishnu_gita::151.insight: It invites you to accept that some truths about existence are beyond complete human understanding.

vishnu_gita::152.verse_sanskrit:
यो मामजमनादिश्च वेति लोकमहेश्वरम् ।
असंमूढः स सर्वत्र सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::152.verse_hindi: जो मुझको अनादि, जन्मरहित, और सकल लोकों का महान् ईश्वर जानता है वह सब जगह मोहरहित होकर सकल पापों से मुक्त हो जाता है
vishnu_gita::152.english_translation: Whoever understands me as unborn, without beginning, and the great lord of all worlds is freed everywhere from all wrongs.
vishnu_gita::152.translation_literal: यो (who) माम् (me) अज (unborn) अनादि (without beginning) इच (knows) वेति (knows) लोक (world) महेश्वरम् (great lord) । असंमूढः (not deluded) स (he) सर्वत्र (everywhere) सर्वपापैः (all wrongs) प्रमुच्यते (is freed) ॥
vishnu_gita::152.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::152.essence: Seeing the divine as unborn and limitless frees you from all faults everywhere.
vishnu_gita::152.simple_meaning: If you understand the divine as eternal and beyond birth, you become free from all faults everywhere.
vishnu_gita::152.simple_insight: There is freedom in seeing the divine as timeless and untouched by beginnings.
vishnu_gita::152.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that recognizing the divine as unborn and without origin frees one from all faults universally. This insight invites seeing beyond the illusion of beginnings and endings to a timeless truth.
vishnu_gita::152.modern_relevance: When you stop labeling yourself and others by beginnings or limits, you feel lighter and free from blame or guilt.
vishnu_gita::152.insight: This shifts your view from seeing life as chained by origins to seeing the divine as an eternal, freeing presence.

vishnu_gita::153.verse_sanskrit:
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा ।
मद्भावा मानला जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥
vishnu_gita::153.verse_hindi: भृगु श्रादि सात महर्षि और उनके पूर्ववर्ती सनकादि चार महर्षि तथा स्वायंभुवादि चौदह मनु ये सभी मेरे प्रभाव से युक्त हैं एवं मेरे हिरण्य गर्भ रूप के सङ्कल्पमात्र से ही उत्पन्न हैं, समस्त संसार के सभी जीव उन्हीं की सृष्टि की हुई प्रजा है
vishnu_gita::153.english_translation: Seven great sages, four ancient Manus, and fourteen progenitors arose from my essence; all beings in the world descend from their creation.
vishnu_gita::153.translation_literal: महर्षयः (great sages) सप्त (seven) पूर्वे (ancient) चत्वारो (four) मनवः (progenitors) तथा (also) । मद्भावा (from my essence) मानला (progenitors) जाता (born) येषाम् (of whom) लोक (world) इमाः (these) प्रजाः (beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::153.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::153.essence: All beings arise from divine essence through ancient sages and progenitors.
vishnu_gita::153.simple_meaning: Seven great sages, four ancient Manus, and fourteen progenitors were born from the divine essence; all living beings come from their creation.
vishnu_gita::153.simple_insight: Everything and everyone arises from a common divine source through these ancient beings.
vishnu_gita::153.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that from his own essence came seven great sages, four ancient Manus, and fourteen progenitors, who in turn created all beings in the world. This verse shows the cosmic origin of life and the divine source behind creation.
vishnu_gita::153.insight: It reveals the interconnected origin of all beings from a shared divine essence, encouraging reverence for life.

vishnu_gita::154.verse_sanskrit:
एतां विभूति योगश्च मम यो वेत्ति नत्त्वतः।
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
vishnu_gita::154.verse_hindi: जो तत्त्वज्ञान के द्वारा मेरी उक्त विभूति एवं योगको जानता है वह अचल समाधि मे युक्त होता है इसमें सन्देह नहीं
vishnu_gita::154.english_translation: Whoever knows my manifested powers and yoga through true knowledge is surely established in unwavering absorbed presence without doubt.
vishnu_gita::154.translation_literal: एतां (this) / विभूति (manifested powers) / योगश्च (and yoga) / मम (my) / यो (who) / वेत्ति (knows) / नत्त्वतः (through true knowledge) / सोऽविकम्पेन (that unshaken) / योगेन (by yoga) / युज्यते (is established) / नात्र (there is not) / संशयः (doubt)
vishnu_gita::154.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::154.essence: Deep knowledge of the divine's power brings unwavering, absorbed steadiness.
vishnu_gita::154.simple_meaning: When you truly understand the divine's powers and yoga, you become steady and fully absorbed without doubt.
vishnu_gita::154.simple_insight: You can rest in calm certainty by deeply knowing the divine's presence and power.
vishnu_gita::154.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that recognizing his manifested powers and the yoga he embodies through clear wisdom leads to a firm, unshakable state of absorbed presence, free from any doubt or wavering.
vishnu_gita::154.modern_relevance: When you fully grasp your own strengths and deeper purpose, you find calm focus even amidst chaos.
vishnu_gita::154.insight: It teaches you to root your awareness in clear knowledge of the true self, creating steady inner absorption.

vishnu_gita::155.verse_sanskrit:
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसम्मोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः ।
सुखं दुःख भवोऽभावो भयञ्चाभयमेव च ॥
vishnu_gita::155.verse_hindi: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव ( उद्भव), अभव (नाश) भय, अभय,
vishnu_gita::155.english_translation: Discerning mind, knowledge, freedom from delusion, patience, truthfulness, self-restraint, tranquility, pleasure, pain, existence, non-existence, fear, and fearlessness.
vishnu_gita::155.translation_literal: बुद्धि (discerning mind) / ज्ञान (knowledge) / असम्मोहः (freedom from delusion) / क्षमा (patience) / सत्यं (truthfulness) / दमः (self-restraint) / शमः (tranquility) / सुखं (pleasure) / दुःख (pain) / भवोऽभावो (existence and non-existence) / भयञ्चाभयमेव च (fear and fearlessness also)
vishnu_gita::155.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::155.essence: True clarity embraces patience, truth, and opposite experiences without confusion.
vishnu_gita::155.simple_meaning: A clear mind embodies qualities like knowledge, patience, truthfulness, calm, and experiences both pleasure and pain, fear and fearlessness.
vishnu_gita::155.simple_insight: You can hold opposites like fear and fearlessness together with calm understanding.
vishnu_gita::155.detailed_meaning: Vishnu lists important qualities of a wise, discerning mind that can recognize truth and remain calm amid opposites like pain and pleasure, fear and courage.
vishnu_gita::155.modern_relevance: When your mind races between stress and calm, remembering these qualities helps you steady your thoughts and emotions.
vishnu_gita::155.insight: It teaches you to recognize both positive and negative experiences without losing your inner balance.

vishnu_gita::156.verse_sanskrit:
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिः स्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः।
भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथविधाः ॥
vishnu_gita::156.verse_hindi: अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश, अयश, प्राणियों के ये सब नाना प्रकार के भाव मुझसे ही उत्पन्न होते हैं
vishnu_gita::156.english_translation: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and dishonor—all these diverse qualities in beings arise from me alone.
vishnu_gita::156.translation_literal: अहिंसा (non-violence) / समता (equanimity) / तुष्टिः (contentment) / स्तपो (austerity) / दानं (charity) / यशः (fame) / अयशः (dishonor) / भवन्ति (arise) / भावा (qualities) / भूतानां (of beings) / मत्त (from me) / एव (alone) / पृथविधाः (various)
vishnu_gita::156.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::156.essence: All diverse qualities in beings arise from one divine source within everything.
vishnu_gita::156.simple_meaning: Every quality you notice in others or yourself—like kindness, pride, or hardship—originates from the divine source within everything.
vishnu_gita::156.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing both your strengths and struggles come from the same inner source.
vishnu_gita::156.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that all qualities seen in living beings—whether good like non-violence and charity, or challenging like dishonor—emanate from him, the source of all existence. This reveals the unity behind all apparent differences.
vishnu_gita::156.modern_relevance: When you feel pride or face criticism, remember both arise from the same inner source, helping you hold balanced perspective.
vishnu_gita::156.insight: It shifts your view to see all experiences as expressions of one underlying reality, removing judgment and fostering acceptance.

vishnu_gita::157.verse_sanskrit:
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्व प्रवर्तते।
इति मन्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥
vishnu_gita::157.verse_hindi: मैं सकल जगत की उत्पत्ति का हेतु हूँ और मुझसे ही सब जगत् प्रवृत्ति को प्राप्त करता है यह जानकर विवेकी गण मेरे भाव को प्राप्त होकर मेरा भजन करते हैं
vishnu_gita::157.english_translation: I am the source of everything; from me, all activity arises. Knowing this, the wise devoted ones worship me with full feeling.
vishnu_gita::157.translation_literal: अहं (I) / सर्वस्य (of everything) / प्रभवो (the origin) / मत्तः (from me) / सर्व (all) / प्रवर्तते (arises) / इति (thus) / मन्वा (knowing) / भजन्ते (worship) / मां (me) / बुधा (the wise) / भावसमन्विताः (with deep feeling)
vishnu_gita::157.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::157.essence: Knowing yourself as the source of all awakens sincere and deep devotion.
vishnu_gita::157.simple_meaning: Everything begins from me, and all activity happens through me. Wise people who understand this worship me with sincere feeling.
vishnu_gita::157.simple_insight: Feeling connected as the source invites a natural, heartfelt devotion.
vishnu_gita::157.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu reveals that he is the origin of all existence and activity. Those wise enough to grasp this truth develop deep devotion and worship him with sincere emotion, seeing their connection beyond just the surface world.
vishnu_gita::157.modern_relevance: When you realize your work and energy come from a deeper source, your efforts become acts of heartfelt devotion, not just tasks.
vishnu_gita::157.insight: It shifts your view from isolated effort to seeing your actions as part of a greater source, inspiring genuine devotion.

vishnu_gita::158.verse_sanskrit:
अनादिदेव ! सृष्टीनां कर्तः ! पालक ! हारक! ।
प्रभो ! विश्वनियन्तनः कृपया कथयाऽधुना ॥
vishnu_gita::158.verse_hindi: हे विश्वनियन्ता ! हे सृष्टि के कर्त्ता पालक और संहारक प्रभो ! अब कृपा करके यह बताइये
vishnu_gita::158.english_translation: O eternal divine! Creator, protector, and destroyer of all creation! O lord, controller of the universe! Please kindly explain now.
vishnu_gita::158.translation_literal:
अनादिदेव (eternal divine) ! सृष्टीनां (of creations) कर्तः (creator) ! पालक (protector) ! हारक (destroyer) ! ।
प्रभो (lord) ! विश्वनियन्तनः (controller of universe) कृपया (kindly) कथयाऽधुना (please tell now) ॥
vishnu_gita::158.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::158.essence: Respectful openness invites guidance from the eternal source of creation and change.
vishnu_gita::158.simple_meaning: A respectful request is made to the eternal divine, creator, protector, and destroyer, asking for a kind explanation.
vishnu_gita::158.simple_insight: Approaching the vast unknown with respect opens the way for deeper understanding.
vishnu_gita::158.detailed_meaning: In this verse, someone addresses the eternal divine, acknowledging its roles as creator, protector, and destroyer of the universe, and asks humbly for an explanation or teaching. It sets a reverent tone before the discourse begins.
vishnu_gita::158.modern_relevance: When facing something vast and unclear, starting with respect and openness invites clarity and guidance.
vishnu_gita::158.insight: It teaches the importance of humility and reverence when seeking profound knowledge or guidance.

vishnu_gita::159.verse_sanskrit:
इयं सृष्टिः किमाधारा तथाऽस्याः को नियामकः ।
आलम्ब्य कमिमे जीवाः परिणाममयीमिमाम् ॥
vishnu_gita::159.verse_hindi: कि यह सृष्टि किस आधार पर स्थित है और सृष्टि का नियामक कौन है और किसको अवलम्बन करके इस परिणाममय
vishnu_gita::159.english_translation: What is the foundation of this creation? Who controls it? On whom do living beings depend for this resulting world?
vishnu_gita::159.translation_literal: इयं (this) / सृष्टिः (creation) / किमाधारा (what foundation) / तथाऽस्याः (and of this) / को (who) / नियामकः (controller) / आलम्ब्य (depending) / कमिमे (on whom) / जीवाः (living beings) / परिणाममयीमिमाम् (this resulting)
vishnu_gita::159.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::159.essence: Creation depends on a foundation and controller that living beings rely upon.
vishnu_gita::159.simple_meaning: This asks what supports the entire creation, who controls it, and on whom living beings rely.
vishnu_gita::159.simple_insight: It invites a deep curiosity about the source and guidance behind everything you see.
vishnu_gita::159.detailed_meaning: The verse raises foundational questions about the nature of creation and its governance, prompting the seeker to consider the ultimate support and controller behind existence.
vishnu_gita::159.modern_relevance: When everything feels uncertain, you may find yourself asking what truly holds your life and who guides your path.
vishnu_gita::159.insight: It encourages shifting from accepting appearances to seeking the deeper underlying reality and its source.

vishnu_gita::160.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिं जयन्तो वहन्ति प्राप्तुं त्वां मोक्षदायिनं ।
ज्ञानानन्दपदं नित्यं भक्ताभीष्टफलप्रदम् ॥
vishnu_gita::160.verse_hindi: सृष्टि को जय करते हुए जीव, ज्ञानानन्दप्रद नित्य भक्ताभीष्ट फल प्रद और मोक्ष दायी आपको प्राप्त कर सकते हैं ।
vishnu_gita::160.english_translation: Living beings who conquer creation can attain you, the giver of liberation, eternal bliss of wisdom, and the desired fruit of devotion.
vishnu_gita::160.translation_literal: सृष्टिं (creation) / जयन्तो (conquering) / वहन्ति (carry/attain) / प्राप्तुं (to obtain) / त्वां (you) / मोक्षदायिनं (giver of liberation) / ज्ञानानन्दपदं (field/realm of wisdom and bliss) / नित्यं (eternal) / भक्ताभीष्टफलप्रदम् (giver of devotee's desired fruit)
vishnu_gita::160.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::160.essence: Overcoming worldly cycles lets you reach the divine who grants eternal joy and devotion’s rewards.
vishnu_gita::160.simple_meaning: Those who overcome the cycle of creation can reach the divine who gives lasting freedom, eternal joy from knowledge, and the rewards of devotion.
vishnu_gita::160.simple_insight: There is hope and power in knowing you can connect with the divine and receive what your heart truly desires.
vishnu_gita::160.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that living beings who overcome worldly cycles can reach him, who grants liberation (moksha), eternal bliss born from wisdom, and the fruits desired by devoted hearts. This verse highlights Vishnu’s role as the ultimate receiver of devotion and source of spiritual fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::160.modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelming, remember you can connect with something greater that offers lasting joy and fulfillment beyond temporary struggles.
vishnu_gita::160.insight: It encourages you to see devotion as a path to lasting freedom and deep fulfillment beyond immediate circumstances.

vishnu_gita::161.verse_sanskrit:
धर्ममाधारा स्थिता सृष्टि: स एवास्या नियामक: ।
केवलं धर्ममेवैकमाश्रित्य जीवजातयः॥
vishnu_gita::161.verse_hindi: सृष्टि धर्म के आधारपर स्थित है, सृष्टि का नियामक धर्म ही है और एकमात्र धर्म को ही अवलम्बन करके ये जीवगण
vishnu_gita::161.english_translation: The creation stands firmly on dharma; dharma alone governs it. All beings rely solely on dharma.
vishnu_gita::161.translation_literal: धर्ममाधारा (on the support of dharma) स्थिता (stands firm) सृष्टि: (creation) स (that) एव (alone) अस्या (of this) नियामक: (regulator) । केवलं (only) धर्ममेवैकम् (dharma alone) आश्रित्य (relying) जीवजातय: (living beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::161.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::161.essence: All creation and life depend solely on living by true purpose.
vishnu_gita::161.simple_meaning: Everything that exists depends on dharma, the true purpose or natural order, and all beings live by relying on it.
vishnu_gita::161.simple_insight: There is strength and stability in living according to your true purpose.
vishnu_gita::161.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that the entire creation is firmly based on dharma, the natural order that governs everything. All living beings depend on this single guiding principle for their existence and conduct.
vishnu_gita::161.modern_relevance: When your work, relationships, or choices feel unstable, grounding yourself in your true purpose can create steady strength.
vishnu_gita::161.insight: This shifts your focus from scattered desires to anchoring actions in your deeper purpose, providing clarity and direction.

vishnu_gita::162.verse_sanskrit:
अग्रेसरा भवन्तीमा मां प्रत्येव न संशयः।
ममानुशासनं धर्म इति तत्त्वविदो विदुः ॥
vishnu_gita::162.verse_hindi: मेरी ओर ही अग्रसर होते हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं है। मेरा अनुशासन धर्म है ऐसा तत्त्वज्ञ समझते हैं
vishnu_gita::162.english_translation: There is no doubt that all who advance turn towards me; true seekers recognize my teaching as dharma.
vishnu_gita::162.translation_literal: अग्रेसरा (foremost/advance) भवन्तीमा (become) मां (towards me) प्रत्येव (indeed) न (not) संशयः (doubt)। मम (my) अनुशासनं (discipline/teaching) धर्म (duty/true way) इति (thus) तत्त्वविदो (truth-knowers) विदुः (know)
vishnu_gita::162.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::162.essence: True seekers naturally turn to the divine’s teaching as their true path.
vishnu_gita::162.simple_meaning: Those who sincerely seek the truth naturally turn towards the divine, recognizing this teaching as the true way.
vishnu_gita::162.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your genuine search draws you closer to what is real.
vishnu_gita::162.detailed_meaning: Vishnu declares that all sincere seekers instinctively come to him, recognizing his teaching as dharma, the true path. This moment confirms the natural pull toward divine guidance for those who truly desire clarity.
