vishnu_gita::162.modern_relevance: When you feel lost or uncertain, your genuine desire to find meaning quietly draws you to trustworthy guidance.
vishnu_gita::162.insight: It shifts your trust from external confusion toward the inner certainty found in devoted seeking.

vishnu_gita::163.verse_sanskrit:
जगन्नियामिका शक्तिर्धर्मरूपाऽस्ति या मम ।
तया ह्यनन्तब्रह्माण्डान्यनन्ता लोकराशयः ॥
vishnu_gita::163.verse_hindi: मेरी जगन्नियामिका शक्तिरूप धर्म से अनन्त ब्रह्माण्डसमूह, अनन्त लोकसमूह और
vishnu_gita::163.english_translation: My power that governs the universe is the form of dharma; by it, infinite universes and countless worlds exist.
vishnu_gita::163.translation_literal: जगन्नियामिका (world-governing) / शक्तिः (power) / धर्मरूपा (in the form of dharma) / अस्ति (is) / या (which) / मम (my) / तया (by that) / हि (indeed) / अनन्त (infinite) / ब्रह्माण्डानि (universes) / अनन्ता (infinite) / लोकराशयः (world-collections)
vishnu_gita::163.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::163.essence: The power sustaining infinite worlds is dharma, the universal governing force.
vishnu_gita::163.simple_meaning: The divine power that controls everything is dharma itself, and through it infinite universes and worlds exist.
vishnu_gita::163.simple_insight: Everything that exists and continues is sustained by a universal order beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::163.detailed_meaning: Vishnu declares that the power governing all existence is dharma itself; this power supports endless universes and countless worlds, emphasizing the vastness and order of creation under his influence.
vishnu_gita::163.insight: Recognize that a universal order underlies all diversity and change, sustaining existence beyond what you see.

vishnu_gita::164.verse_sanskrit:
ऋषयः पितरो यूयं स्वस्वस्थान स्थिताः सदा ।
रक्षन्ति सृश्तिखिलामिति जानीत सत्तमा: ! ॥
vishnu_gita::164.verse_hindi: ऋषि देवता पितृगण अपने अपने स्थान पर सदा स्थित रहकर सम्पूर्ण सृष्टि की रक्षा करते हैं, हे श्रेष्ठ देवगण ! इसको जानो
vishnu_gita::164.english_translation: The sages, deities, and ancestors always remain in their own places, protecting the entire creation, O supreme deities, know this.
vishnu_gita::164.translation_literal: ऋषयः (sages) / पितरो (ancestors) / यूयं (you) / स्वस्वस्थान (own-place) / स्थिताः (situated) / सदा (always) / रक्षन्ति (protect) / सृश्तिखिलामिति (entire-creation) / जानीत (know) / सत्तमा: (best, supreme)
vishnu_gita::164.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::164.essence: Timeless beings remain in place, continuously protecting all creation.
vishnu_gita::164.simple_meaning: Sages, deities, and ancestors always stay in their own places and protect all of creation.
vishnu_gita::164.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that unseen forces watch over the whole world constantly.
vishnu_gita::164.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how sages, divine beings, and ancestors remain steadfast in their realms, continuously guarding all creation. This reassures listeners about the cosmic order maintained by these timeless forces.
vishnu_gita::164.insight: Recognize that some protective forces work quietly and constantly beyond your view.

vishnu_gita::165.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मे धारणरूपा या शक्तिरस्ति दिवौकसः।
तयैव स्वस्वकक्षायामिमे सर्वे स्थिताः सदा ॥
vishnu_gita::165.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! मेरी धर्म की धारिका शक्ति द्वारा ही अपनी अपनी कक्षा में सदा स्थित रहते हैं
vishnu_gita::165.english_translation: O divine beings! By the power that sustains dharma, all always remain in their own realm.
vishnu_gita::165.translation_literal: धर्मे (in dharma) / धारणरूपा (the form of sustaining) / या (which) / शक्तिरस्ति (power exists) / दिवौकसः (divine beings) / तयैव (by that very) / स्वस्वकक्षायाम् (in their own realm) / इमे (these) / सर्वे (all) / स्थिताः (situated) / सदा (always)
vishnu_gita::165.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::165.essence: A sustaining power maintains all beings in their proper realms through dharma.
vishnu_gita::165.simple_meaning: All beings remain constantly in their own respective realms by the power that upholds dharma.
vishnu_gita::165.simple_insight: There is a sustaining power keeping everyone in their rightful place, creating order.
vishnu_gita::165.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that the power sustaining dharma keeps each being in their own specific realm, maintaining cosmic order and balance.
vishnu_gita::165.insight: Recognize that an underlying power maintains order and balance beyond individual control.

vishnu_gita::166.verse_sanskrit:
ग्रहनक्षत्रप्रमुखा लोका ब्रह्माण्डकानि च ।
तयैव पितरो यूयमृषयश्च तथाऽसुराः ॥
vishnu_gita::166.verse_hindi: समस्त ब्रह्माण्ड और सभी ग्रह नक्षत्र आदि लोकसमूह और उसी के द्वारा ऋषि, पितृ, आपलोग और अनुरगण भी
vishnu_gita::166.english_translation: All the worlds including the cosmos, planets, and stars, along with the sages, ancestors, and radiant beings, are part of that same reality.
vishnu_gita::166.translation_literal: ग्रहनक्षत्रप्रमुखा (planets and stars prominent) / लोका (worlds) / ब्रह्माण्डकानि (cosmic bodies) / च (and) / तयैव (by those same) / पितरो (ancestors) / यूयम् (you all) / ऋषयः (sages) / च (and) / तथाऽसुराः (and radiant beings)
vishnu_gita::166.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::166.essence: All cosmic elements and beings are interconnected parts of one reality.
vishnu_gita::166.simple_meaning: The entire cosmos with all its planets, stars, and worlds, along with sages, ancestors, and radiant beings, belong to one interconnected existence.
vishnu_gita::166.simple_insight: Everything visible and invisible is linked, forming one vast, shared reality.
vishnu_gita::166.detailed_meaning: This verse lists the cosmic elements—the planets and stars—and living entities like sages, ancestors, and radiant beings, emphasizing their unity within the universe. It sets the stage by showing the vastness and interconnectedness of all existence.
vishnu_gita::166.insight: Recognize all aspects of existence as interconnected parts of one cosmic whole.

vishnu_gita::167.verse_sanskrit:
रक्षन्तः पदमर्यादा स्वीयां लोकानवन्त्यलम् ।
यदा स्वधर्माच्च्यवथ विप्लबो जायते तदा ॥
vishnu_gita::167.verse_hindi: अपनी अपनी पद मर्यादा की रक्षा करते हुए संसार की रक्षा में भलीभांति प्रवृत्त रहते हैं। आपलोग जब स्वधर्म से च्युत होते हो तभी जगत में विप्लव उपस्थित होता है
vishnu_gita::167.english_translation: By protecting their own ranks and boundaries, beings maintain the world's order; when they forsake their own duty, disorder arises.
vishnu_gita::167.translation_literal: रक्षन्तः (protecting) पदमर्यादा (their own rank-boundaries) स्वीयां (own) लोकानवन्त्यलम् (world/order) । यदा (when) स्वधर्माच्च्यवथ (from own duty falling away) विप्लबो (disorder) जायते (arises) तदा (then) ॥
vishnu_gita::167.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::167.essence: Order depends on each person protecting their own rightful duty and place.
vishnu_gita::167.simple_meaning: Everyone keeps the world in balance by guarding their own role. When you abandon your duty, chaos follows.
vishnu_gita::167.simple_insight: You feel responsible and steady when you honor your part in the whole.
vishnu_gita::167.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that all beings maintain cosmic harmony by respecting their own roles and limits. When someone breaks from their true duty, it causes disorder in the world.
vishnu_gita::167.modern_relevance: At work or home, when you stick to your responsibilities, everything flows smoothly; stepping away can cause disruption.
vishnu_gita::167.insight: It teaches you to focus on fulfilling your role well to support broader harmony and prevent chaos.

vishnu_gita::168.verse_sanskrit:
अत्यन्तं येन लोकेषु नित्यं सीदन्ति प्राणिनः ।
अनन्तकोटिब्रह्माण्डयुक्तदृष्टिप्रवाहकः ॥
vishnu_gita::168.verse_hindi: जिससे लोकों में प्राणिमात्र नित्य अत्यन्त क्लेश पाते हैं, मुझमें स्थित अनन्तकोटि ब्रह्माण्डयुक्त सृष्टिप्रवाह
vishnu_gita::168.english_translation: I am the flow of creation that sustains countless universes, from which all beings constantly suffer minimal distress.
vishnu_gita::168.translation_literal: अत्यन्तं (extreme) / येन (by whom) / लोकेषु (in worlds) / नित्यं (constantly) / सीदन्ति (suffer) / प्राणिनः (beings) / अनन्तकोटिब्रह्माण्डयुक्तदृष्टिप्रवाहकः (the flow that carries infinite crores of universes)
vishnu_gita::168.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::168.essence: The divine is the sustaining flow behind infinite universes where beings face ongoing suffering.
vishnu_gita::168.simple_meaning: The divine is the sustaining flow behind countless worlds where all living beings experience ongoing suffering.
vishnu_gita::168.simple_insight: Even vast creation is a field where beings face constant struggle; this awareness brings humility.
vishnu_gita::168.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes himself as the cosmic flow that supports infinite universes filled with beings who endure continual hardship, highlighting the vast scale and inherent suffering within creation.
vishnu_gita::168.insight: It reveals the vast, interconnected reality that includes both cosmic grandeur and the persistent challenges for all beings.

vishnu_gita::169.verse_sanskrit:
मतिस्थत: केवलं धर्ममेवैकमवल्म्ब्य हि ।
वर्तते धर्म एवातो विश्वधारक ईरितः ॥
vishnu_gita::169.verse_hindi: एकमात्र धर्म को अवलम्बन करके ही स्थित है इसी कारण धर्म विश्वधारक कहा गया है।
vishnu_gita::169.english_translation: Only by firmly adhering to the one true dharma does the world remain sustained; that is why dharma is called the support of the universe.
vishnu_gita::169.translation_literal: मतिस्थत: (firmly settled) केवलं (only) धर्ममेवैकम् (dharma alone) अवल्म्ब्य (by relying) हि (indeed) वर्तते (exists) धर्म (dharma) एव (only) अतः (therefore) विश्वधारक (world-supporting) ईरितः (called)
vishnu_gita::169.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::169.essence: The universe depends on unwavering commitment to one true dharma.
vishnu_gita::169.simple_meaning: Everything in the universe stays steady because it follows one true dharma. That is why dharma supports all.
vishnu_gita::169.simple_insight: You feel the power and responsibility of holding to what is right and steady.
vishnu_gita::169.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the entire universe stays balanced and functioning because of unwavering adherence to one true dharma. This moment highlights dharma as the basis that upholds everything around us.
vishnu_gita::169.modern_relevance: When your choices align with your deepest values, you become a steady force others rely on, even if they don’t see it.
vishnu_gita::169.insight: It shifts your view from isolated acts to seeing your steady values as the foundation for all stability.

vishnu_gita::170.verse_sanskrit:
अनन्ता ये ग्रहाः सर्व्ये तथोपग्रहराशयः ।
ब्रह्माण्डशब्दनिर्बाच्यास्तथैवामरपुङ्गवाः !॥
vishnu_gita::170.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्ठ गण ! अनंत ग्रह उपग्रह्मय ब्रह्माण्ड और
vishnu_gita::170.english_translation: The infinite planets, their satellites, the entire universe, and the immortal foremost beings.
vishnu_gita::170.translation_literal: अनन्ता (infinite) / ये (which) / ग्रहाः (planets) / सर्व्ये (all) / तथ (and) / उपग्रहराशयः (satellites) / ब्रह्माण्ड (universe) / शब्दनिर्बाच्याः (called) / तथैव (likewise) / अमरपुङ्गवाः (immortal foremost beings)
vishnu_gita::170.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::170.essence: The cosmos includes endless worlds, their satellites, and immortal exalted beings.
vishnu_gita::170.simple_meaning: This verse lists vast cosmic entities like infinite planets, their moons, the universe, and immortal exalted beings.
vishnu_gita::170.simple_insight: The vastness of everything shows how much lies beyond our usual view.
vishnu_gita::170.detailed_meaning: Suta describes the immense cosmic scale, including countless planets, their satellites, the whole universe, and immortal exalted beings, setting the stage for a grand teaching.
vishnu_gita::170.insight: It expands your sense of scale, inviting awe at the universe's vastness beyond daily concerns.

vishnu_gita::171.verse_sanskrit:
नानावैचित्र्यसंयुक्ता उद्भिज्जस्वेदजाण्डजाः ।
जरायुजा इमे नूनं भूतसङ्काः समीरिनाः ॥
vishnu_gita::171.verse_hindi: अनन्त विचित्रतापूर्ण उद्विज, स्वदेज, अंडज और जरायुजरुपी चतुर्विध भूतसंघ
vishnu_gita::171.english_translation: Indeed, the beings in the world arise in four diverse forms: those born from sprouts, sweat, eggs, and wombs.
vishnu_gita::171.translation_literal: नानावैचित्र्यसंयुक्ता (with many diversities) / उद्भिज् (sprout-born) / स्वेद (sweat) / जाण्डजाः (egg-born) / जरायुजा (womb-born) / इमे (these) / नूनं (indeed) / भूतसङ्काः (groups of beings) / समीरिनाः (living beings)
vishnu_gita::171.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::171.essence: Life manifests in four distinct forms based on origin.
vishnu_gita::171.simple_meaning: Living beings arise in four different ways: from plants, sweat, eggs, and wombs.
vishnu_gita::171.simple_insight: Life appears in many forms, each with its own origin and nature.
vishnu_gita::171.detailed_meaning: The verse describes the four categories of beings in the world according to their origin: plants and trees (sprout-born), beings born from sweat (perhaps symbolic of spontaneous generation), those born from eggs, and those born from the womb. This classification sets the stage for understanding the diversity of life.
vishnu_gita::171.insight: Recognize that life manifests diversely, beyond a single origin or form.

vishnu_gita::172.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वानेतान्वीनिर्देष्टे नियमे परिचाल्यन ।
एक एवाऽस्ति धर्मोऽतो जगतां स नियामकः ॥
vishnu_gita::172.verse_hindi: इन सबको निर्दिष्ट नियम पर चलने वाला एकमात्र धर्म है इस कारण धर्म को जगन्नियंता कहते हैं ।
vishnu_gita::172.english_translation: The one duty that governs all is to follow the prescribed rules; thus, this duty is the regulator of the world.
vishnu_gita::172.translation_literal: सर्व (all) एतान् (these) विनिर्देष्टे (prescribed) नियम (rules) परिचाल्यन् (following) । एक (one) एव (only) अस्ती (exists) धर्मः (duty) अतो (therefore) जगताम् (of the worlds) स (that) नियामकः (regulator) ॥
vishnu_gita::172.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::172.essence: Following your one true duty maintains the order that governs all existence.
vishnu_gita::172.simple_meaning: There is one essential duty: to follow the rules that govern everything. This duty maintains order in the world.
vishnu_gita::172.simple_insight: You can feel steady knowing your duty connects you to the world’s harmony.
vishnu_gita::172.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that among many instructions, one core duty stands out: following the prescribed rules (dharma) that regulate the world. This teaching comes as a foundation for understanding how individual action fits within cosmic order.
vishnu_gita::172.modern_relevance: When you decide to respect the basic rules at work or in your community, you contribute to a balanced, functioning whole.
vishnu_gita::172.insight: It teaches you to see your responsibilities as part of a larger system that keeps life stable.

vishnu_gita::173.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्मे वशं याता मूढा जीवगणा हि ये।
क्रमशो मां समायान्ति निश्चितं विबुधोत्तमा: ॥
vishnu_gita::173.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्ठगण ! मेरी प्रकृति के अधीन रहकर मूढ़ जीवगण क्रमशः मुझको निश्चित ही प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::173.english_translation: O best of the devas, the deluded living beings, being under my nature, gradually surely come to me.
vishnu_gita::173.translation_literal: प्रकृतेर्मे (by my nature) / वशं (under control) / याता (being) / मूढा (deluded) / जीवगणा (living beings) / हि (indeed) / ये (who) / क्रमशो (gradually) / मां (me) / समायान्ति (come) / निश्चितं (certainly) / विबुधोत्तमा: (best of the wise)
vishnu_gita::173.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::173.essence: Confused beings bound by nature ultimately return to the divine inevitably.
vishnu_gita::173.simple_meaning: Deluded living beings, controlled by my nature, gradually and surely come back to me.
vishnu_gita::173.simple_insight: There is an underlying order in how beings return to the divine despite confusion.
vishnu_gita::173.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the best of the devas, explaining that living beings, though deluded and controlled by the natural world, inevitably return to him over time, showing a cosmic cycle of return despite ignorance.
vishnu_gita::173.insight: It reveals that confusion and delusion do not prevent an ultimate return to the true source.

vishnu_gita::174.verse_sanskrit:
विशिष्टचेतना जीवस्तद्वनमेव चाऽऽश्रिता: ।
मां प्रत्यग्रेसराः सन्तो मामेवायान्ति चै क्रमात् ॥
vishnu_gita::174.verse_hindi: और उसी प्रकार से मुझे ही आश्रय करके विशिष्ट चेतन जीवगण क्रमशः मेरी ओर अग्रसर होते हुए मुझको ही प्राप्त करते हैं।
vishnu_gita::174.english_translation: Distinct conscious beings, relying on that sound, gradually move toward me and finally reach only me.
vishnu_gita::174.translation_literal: विशिष्टचेतना (distinct conscious) / जीवः (beings) / तद्वनम् (that sound) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / आश्रिता: (relying on) / माम् (me) / प्रत्यग्-इरसः (moving forward) / सन्तः (those who are) / माम् (me) / एव (only) / आयान्ति (come) / च (and) / ए (indeed) / क्रमात् (gradually)
vishnu_gita::174.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::174.essence: Trusting a higher sound leads conscious beings gradually to the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::174.simple_meaning: Conscious beings who rely on the true sacred sound gradually approach and finally reach the divine being.
vishnu_gita::174.simple_insight: Trusting a higher sound or truth gently guides you closer to your true self.
vishnu_gita::174.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that conscious beings who depend on the sacred sound naturally progress step by step toward him, symbolizing a devotional journey toward the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::174.modern_relevance: You might feel lost, but trusting a guiding truth or inner voice helps you move steadily toward what truly matters.
vishnu_gita::174.insight: It teaches you to trust a guiding inner truth that naturally draws you closer to your higher purpose.

vishnu_gita::175.verse_sanskrit:
अतः कर्म द्विधा मुख्यं सहजं जैवमेव च ।
तस्मात् कर्मविदो धीरा धर्म कर्मेति सजगुः ॥
vishnu_gita::175.verse_hindi: इसी कारण कर्म सहज और जैव रूप से प्रधानतः दो प्रकार का कहलाता है। कर्म के जानने वाले महापुरुषगण इसी से धर्म को कर्म नाम से अभिहित करते हैं।
vishnu_gita::175.english_translation: Therefore, action is chiefly twofold: natural and biological; wise experts call this dharma as action.
vishnu_gita::175.translation_literal: अतः (therefore) कर्म (action) द्विधा (twofold) मुख्यं (chief) सहजं (natural) जैवमेव (biological) च (also) । तस्मात् (therefore) कर्मविदो (experts in action) धीरा (wise ones) धर्म (dharma) कर्मेति (as action) सजगुः (named) ॥
vishnu_gita::175.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::175.essence: Action is both effortless natural flow and life’s biological expression of purpose.
vishnu_gita::175.simple_meaning: Action has two main types: natural, which happens effortlessly, and biological, which relates to life itself. Wise people call this dharma, or true purpose, action.
vishnu_gita::175.simple_insight: You can recognize that your purpose shows up both naturally and through your living actions.
vishnu_gita::175.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that action divides mainly into two kinds: the effortless natural action and the biological action essential to life. Those who understand action deeply equate dharma with this dual nature of action, setting a foundation for purpose.
vishnu_gita::175.modern_relevance: You notice some work flows easily, while other tasks connect deeply to your life’s purpose—both are true action.
vishnu_gita::175.insight: It shifts your view to see purpose as expressed both naturally and biologically through your actions.

vishnu_gita::176.verse_sanskrit:
एवं यज्ञस्तथा धर्म उभौ पर्यायवाचकौ ।
कथितौ वेद्निष्णतै: शस्त्रज्ञै: शास्त्रविस्तरे ॥
vishnu_gita::176.verse_hindi: इसी प्रकार यज्ञ और धर्म दोनों को पर्यायवाची शब्द हैं, इस बात को वेदनिष्णात शास्त्रों ने शास्त्र विस्तार में कहा है ।
vishnu_gita::176.english_translation: Similarly, sacrifice and duty are synonymous, as explained in detail by the scripture experts well-versed in the Vedas.
vishnu_gita::176.translation_literal: एवं (thus) / यज्ञस्तथा (sacrifice also) / धर्म (duty/righteousness) / उभौ (both) / पर्यायवाचकौ (synonyms) / कथितौ (have been stated) / वेद्निष्णतै: (by those skilled in the Vedas) / शस्त्रज्ञै: (experts in scriptures) / शास्त्रविस्तरे (in detailed scripture)
vishnu_gita::176.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::176.essence: Sacrifice and duty are the same; fulfilling duty is sacred action.
vishnu_gita::176.simple_meaning: Sacrifice and duty mean the same thing; experts in the scriptures have explained this clearly.
vishnu_gita::176.simple_insight: You can feel grounded knowing your duties are acts of sacred offering.
vishnu_gita::176.detailed_meaning: Vishnu clarifies that the concept of yagna (sacrifice) and dharma (duty) are used interchangeably in the scriptures, emphasizing that acting according to duty itself is a form of sacred sacrifice.
vishnu_gita::176.modern_relevance: When you complete your daily tasks with sincerity, you are performing a meaningful offering beyond mere work.
vishnu_gita::176.insight: This shifts your view from seeing duties as chores to acts of spiritual significance.

vishnu_gita::177.verse_sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः मजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।
अनेन जीवा राध्यन्तामसावस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
vishnu_gita::177.verse_hindi: सृष्टि के प्रारम्भ में यज्ञक साथ ही साथ प्रजाओं को उत्पन्न करके प्रजापतिने कहा, “ इससे जीवगण आराधना करें, यह उन लोगों का अभीष्ट प्रदानकारी हो"।
vishnu_gita::177.english_translation: At creation's start, Prajapati said: 'Having created sacrifices and beings, let these beings worship; this grants their heartfelt desires.'
vishnu_gita::177.translation_literal: सहयज्ञाः (together sacrifices) मजाः (beings) सृष्ट्वा (having created) पुरोवाच (spoke first) प्रजापतिः (Prajapati). अनेन (by this) जीवा (beings) राध्यन्ताम (may be worshipped) असौ (these) त्विष्टकामधुक् (granter of desires).
vishnu_gita::177.speaker: Prajapati
vishnu_gita::177.essence: Creation began with sacrifice and beings meant to worship for their desires.
vishnu_gita::177.simple_meaning: In the beginning, Prajapati created sacrifices and beings, instructing that beings worship through sacrifice to receive their desires.
vishnu_gita::177.simple_insight: Creation connects beings and rituals as a means to fulfill heartfelt wishes.
vishnu_gita::177.detailed_meaning: At the dawn of creation, Prajapati established the practice of yajna (sacrifice) alongside the birth of living beings, instructing that beings use this practice to receive what they truly desire.
vishnu_gita::177.insight: It highlights how early teachings linked action (sacrifice) with intention to shape outcomes.

vishnu_gita::178.verse_sanskrit:
भावयन्तु हि वोऽनेन भवन्तो भावयन्तु तान् ।
परस्परम भावयन्त: श्रेयो देवा: ! अवाप्स्यथ ॥
vishnu_gita::178.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जीवगण इसके द्वारा आपलोगों को सम्बर्द्धित करें और आपलोग उनको सम्बर्द्धित करें इसी प्रकार परस्पर सम्बर्द्धित होकर सभी कल्याण प्राप्त करेंगे ।
vishnu_gita::178.english_translation: O radiant beings! By mutually honoring each other, you all will attain higher well-being together.
vishnu_gita::178.translation_literal: भावयन्तु (honor) हि (indeed) वोऽनेन (by that) भवन्तो (you all) भावयन्तु (honor) तान् (them) । परस्परम (mutually) भावयन्त: (honoring) श्रेयो (greater good) देवा: (radiant beings) ! अवाप्स्यथ (will attain) ॥
vishnu_gita::178.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::178.essence: Mutual honoring among beings creates shared growth and well-being.
vishnu_gita::178.simple_meaning: You should honor others and let them honor you in return; this mutual respect brings greater well-being for all.
vishnu_gita::178.simple_insight: There is warmth in knowing that caring for others also nurtures your own growth.
vishnu_gita::178.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, encouraging them to mutually honor one another. This reciprocal honoring creates a shared path to greater well-being and harmony among all beings involved.
vishnu_gita::178.modern_relevance: You notice how a simple act of appreciation from a colleague brightens your day, and your kindness inspires theirs right back.
vishnu_gita::178.insight: It teaches you to see others' success as intertwined with your own, promoting a cycle of mutual support.

vishnu_gita::179.verse_sanskrit:
इष्टान भोगान् भवन्तो हि दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
अदत्त्वा वो भवहत्तान् यो भुंक्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
vishnu_gita::179.verse_hindi: आपलोग यज्ञ से  सम्बर्द्धित होकर उनको अभीलाषित भोग प्रदान करेंगे इसलिए आपके दिए भोगों को आपलोगों के अर्पण किए बिना ही जो भोगता है वह चोर ही है
vishnu_gita::179.english_translation: Those who are devoted to sacrifice receive the desired enjoyments; anyone who enjoys without offering is indeed a thief.
vishnu_gita::179.translation_literal: इष्टान (desired) भोगान् (enjoyments) भवन्तो (are) हि (indeed) दास्यन्ते (given) यज्ञभाविताः (those devoted to sacrifice) । अदत्त्वा (without giving) वो (your) भवहत्तान् (offered) यो (who) भुंक्ते (enjoys) स्तेन (thief) एव (indeed) सः (that one) ॥
vishnu_gita::179.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::179.essence: Receiving is rightful only when preceded by sincere offering.
vishnu_gita::179.simple_meaning: Enjoyments come to those who offer with devotion. Taking without giving is like stealing.
vishnu_gita::179.simple_insight: You feel respect for the flow of giving and receiving, not entitlement or taking.
vishnu_gita::179.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that those who dedicate their enjoyments through sacrifice receive blessings. Anyone who consumes without offering breaks this sacred balance and acts like a thief.
vishnu_gita::179.modern_relevance: When you take from others without contributing, it leaves a sense of imbalance and guilt, unlike when you give first with respect.
vishnu_gita::179.insight: It teaches you to honor the natural cycle of giving before receiving, fostering fairness and integrity.

vishnu_gita::180.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्विषः।
भुजते ते त्वधं पापा ये पचन्सात्मकारणात् ॥
vishnu_gita::180.verse_hindi: यज्ञ का अवशिष्ट भोजन करने वाले सज्जनगण सब पापों से मुक्त हो जाते हैं किन्तु जो अपने ही लिये भोजन बनाते हैं वे पापिगण पाप को ही भोजन करते हैं
vishnu_gita::180.english_translation: Those who eat the remnants of yajna are freed from all faults; but those who cook only for themselves consume sin itself.
vishnu_gita::180.translation_literal: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः (yajna remnants eaters) सन्तो (saints) मुच्यन्ते (are freed) सर्वकिल्विषः (all faults). भुजते (eat) ते (they) त्वधं (below) पापा (sin) ये (who) पचन्स (cooking) आत्मकारणात् (for oneself).
vishnu_gita::180.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::180.essence: Sharing sacred offerings frees you; selfish cooking keeps you bound by harm.
vishnu_gita::180.simple_meaning: Eating food offered in sacred rituals frees you from faults. Cooking only for yourself leads to harm.
vishnu_gita::180.simple_insight: There's a deep relief in knowing sharing nourishes your true self while selfishness causes harm.
vishnu_gita::180.detailed_meaning: In the context of sacred yajna rituals, Vishnu teaches that those who partake in the shared offerings are freed from all faults, symbolizing purity through selflessness. Those who cook and eat only for themselves feed harmful tendencies, remaining bound by negative consequences.
vishnu_gita::180.modern_relevance: You prepare a meal just for yourself, skipping sharing. You feel a quiet heaviness, unlike the lightness you notice when you give food or help others.
vishnu_gita::180.insight: It teaches you to find freedom by acting with generosity rather than serving only your own desires.

vishnu_gita::181.verse_sanskrit:
अन्नाद् भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद् भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
vishnu_gita::181.verse_hindi: जीव समूह अन्न से उत्पन्न होते हैं, अन्न वृष्टि होने से उत्पन्न होता है और यज्ञ से वृष्टि होती है एवं यज्ञ कर्म द्वारा सम्पन्न होता है।
vishnu_gita::181.english_translation: Living beings arise from food; food comes from rain; rain arises from sacrifice; and sacrifice is born of action.
vishnu_gita::181.translation_literal: अन्नाद् (from food) भवन्ति (are born) भूतानि (living beings) पर्जन्याद् (from rain) अन्नसम्भवः (food arises). यज्ञाद् (from sacrifice) भवति (comes) पर्जन्यो (rain) यज्ञः (sacrifice) कर्मसमुद्भवः (is born of action).
vishnu_gita::181.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::181.essence: Your actions start a chain that sustains all life through sacrifice, rain, and food.
vishnu_gita::181.simple_meaning: All living things depend on a cycle: your actions create sacrifice, which brings rain, which grows food, which sustains life.
vishnu_gita::181.simple_insight: Your smallest effort connects you deeply to the whole world’s survival.
vishnu_gita::181.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the natural cycle linking human action to life’s sustenance: actions create sacrificial efforts, which bring rain, feeding food, and thus supporting living beings.
vishnu_gita::181.modern_relevance: When you choose to act responsibly, you help sustain not just yourself but the entire ecosystem around you.
vishnu_gita::181.insight: It teaches you to see your actions as part of a larger natural cycle sustaining life.

vishnu_gita::182.verse_sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं वित्त ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात् सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम ॥
vishnu_gita::182.verse_hindi: कर्म को ब्रह्म (वेद ) द्वारा उत्पन्न समझो और ब्रह्म (वेद) अक्षर (ब्रह्म) से उत्पन्न है इसलिये सर्वव्यापी ब्रह्म यज्ञ में नित्य प्रतिष्ठित है ।
vishnu_gita::182.english_translation: Action originates from the supreme teachings and the supreme teachings arise from the imperishable supreme reality; therefore, the all-pervading supreme reality is eternally established in sacrifice.
vishnu_gita::182.translation_literal: कर्म (action) / ब्रह्मोद्भवं (originated from the supreme teachings) / वित्त (and) / ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् (the supreme teachings arise from the imperishable supreme reality) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वगतं (all-pervading) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / नित्यं (eternally) / यज्ञे (in sacrifice) / प्रतिष्ठितम (established)
vishnu_gita::182.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::182.essence: All actions arise from an eternal supreme reality present in sacred practice.
vishnu_gita::182.simple_meaning: All actions arise from supreme teachings, which themselves come from the eternal supreme reality, and this reality is always present in the act of sacrifice.
vishnu_gita::182.simple_insight: Your actions connect you to an unchanging, all-pervading truth beyond yourself.
vishnu_gita::182.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that all actions (karma) originate from the supreme teachings (brahma), which in turn arise from the imperishable supreme reality (brahma-akshara). This eternal reality is ever-present in the sacred act of sacrifice, linking individual action to cosmic truth.
vishnu_gita::182.modern_relevance: When you commit to your work or service deeply, you participate in a timeless flow that connects you to something greater than yourself.
vishnu_gita::182.insight: It teaches you to see your actions as expressions of a deeper, eternal reality that transcends daily outcomes.

vishnu_gita::183.verse_sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्त्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं देवाः ! स जीवति ॥
vishnu_gita::183.verse_hindi: इस लोक में जो इस प्रकार प्रवर्तित चक्र का अनुसरण नहीं करता है, हे देवगण ! इंद्रियासक्त पापजीवन वह व्यक्ति व्यर्थ जीता है ।
vishnu_gita::183.english_translation: In this world, one who does not follow the established cycle, O radiant beings, lives a wasted life bound by senses and wrongdoing.
vishnu_gita::183.translation_literal: एवं (thus) / प्रवर्तितं (established) / चक्रं (cycle) / नानुवर्त्तयतीह (does not follow here) / यः (who) / अघायुर् (wrongdoing-life) / इन्द्रियारामो (sensual-pleasure-seeker) / मोघं (vainly) / देवाः (O radiant beings) / स (that) / जीवति (lives)
vishnu_gita::183.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::183.essence: Ignoring your natural path leads to a restless, empty life.
vishnu_gita::183.simple_meaning: Living without following your natural role and inner cycle leads to a wasted life of restless desire and harm.
vishnu_gita::183.simple_insight: There is emptiness in chasing only pleasure without living your true purpose.
vishnu_gita::183.detailed_meaning: This verse warns that a person who ignores their inherent natural duties and the order of life, indulging only in sensory pleasures and wrongdoing, lives a life without meaning or fulfillment. The audience is addressed as radiant beings, emphasizing the importance of dharma.
vishnu_gita::183.modern_relevance: You may find yourself caught in distractions or habits that feel good but leave you empty, missing what truly matters.
vishnu_gita::183.insight: It teaches you to recognize when you are off your true path and to realign with your natural responsibilities.

vishnu_gita::184.verse_sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिन: पर्ययृपास्ते।
ब्रह्माग्नादपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥
vishnu_gita::184.verse_hindi: कितने योगिगण देवयज्ञ की ही उपासना करते हैं, कोई कोई यज्ञरूप उपाय द्वारा ब्रह्मरूपी अग्नि में यज्ञ को सम्पन्न करते हैं
vishnu_gita::184.english_translation: Some yogis worship the divine sacrifice; others complete the sacrifice by offering it into the supreme fire of Brahman.
vishnu_gita::184.translation_literal: दैवमेवापरे (some worship only the divine) / यज्ञं (the sacrifice) / योगिन: (yogis) / पर्ययृपास्ते (worship) / ब्रह्माग्नात् (from the fire of Brahman) / अपरे (others) / यज्ञं (the sacrifice) / यज्ञेनैव (by the sacrifice itself) / उपजुह्वति (complete/offer).
vishnu_gita::184.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::184.essence: Offering to the divine or merging with the supreme reality both fulfill the sacred act.
vishnu_gita::184.simple_meaning: Some yogis worship the divine presence itself, while others offer their sacrifice directly into the supreme reality, completing it through that union.
vishnu_gita::184.simple_insight: You can approach the sacred either by heartfelt devotion or by merging fully with the highest reality.
vishnu_gita::184.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how different yogis approach the sacred sacrifice: some worship the divine aspect of the sacrifice, while others see the supreme reality as the fire that consumes and completes their offering, emphasizing two paths of devotion and union.
vishnu_gita::184.modern_relevance: When you give your effort, you might focus on honoring what inspires you or fully merge your work into a greater purpose that transcends individual acts.
vishnu_gita::184.insight: It shifts the mind from separate acts of worship to a deeper union with the greater reality behind all devotion.

vishnu_gita::185.verse_sanskrit:
श्रोतादीनीन्द्रियाष्यन्ते संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
शब्ददीन विषयानन्ये इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
vishnu_gita::185.verse_hindi: और कोई योगी संयमरूपी अग्नि में अपनी श्रवण आदि इन्द्रियों का हवन करते हैं और कितने योगिगण इन्द्रियरूपी अग्नि में शब्द आदि विषयों को हवन करते हैं
vishnu_gita::185.english_translation: Some yogis offer their senses like hearing into the fire of restraint, and many others offer objects like sound into the fire of the senses.
vishnu_gita::185.translation_literal: श्रोतादीनि (hearing and others) इन्द्रियाः (senses) अश् (fire) अन्ते (into) संयम (restraint) अग्निषु (fires) जुह्वति (offer) / शब्द (sound) दीन (objects) विषय (objects) अन्ये (others) इन्द्रिय (senses) अग्निषु (fires) जुह्वति (offer)
vishnu_gita::185.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::185.essence: Discipline is offering senses and their objects into a fire that burns distraction and craving.
vishnu_gita::185.simple_meaning: You can practice self-control by offering your senses and the objects they perceive into the fire of restraint, reducing distraction.
vishnu_gita::185.simple_insight: There's power in consciously directing your senses rather than letting them wander uncontrollably.
vishnu_gita::185.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that some yogis cultivate discipline by controlling their senses like hearing, offering them into the fire of restraint. Others focus on controlling sensory objects like sounds, using the senses themselves as a fire to burn distractions.
vishnu_gita::185.modern_relevance: When notifications and sounds pull your attention everywhere, choosing to focus is like offering your senses into a calming fire of control.
vishnu_gita::185.insight: It teaches you to use discipline as a fire that consumes distractions by consciously managing senses and their objects.

vishnu_gita::186.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे ।
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥
vishnu_gita::186.verse_hindi: कितने योगिगण ज्ञान के द्वारा प्रज्वालित आत्मसंयमरूप योगाग्नि में सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियकर्म और प्राणकर्मों का हवन करते हैं
vishnu_gita::186.english_translation: Many yogis offer all sensory and life-force actions as a sacrifice into the fire of self-discipline kindled by wisdom.
vishnu_gita::186.translation_literal: सर्वाणि (all) इन्द्रियकर्माणि (sensory actions) प्राणकर्माणि (life-force actions) चापरे (also others) आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ (in the fire of self-discipline yoga) जुह्वति (offer) ज्ञानदीपिते (kindled by wisdom)
vishnu_gita::186.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::186.essence: Wisdom lights the fire of self-discipline that transforms all your actions.
vishnu_gita::186.simple_meaning: You can transform all your bodily and breath actions by offering them into self-discipline fueled by wisdom.
vishnu_gita::186.simple_insight: There is power in using wisdom to guide and control your actions and impulses.
vishnu_gita::186.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how yogis bring all their sensory activities and life breaths as offerings into a fire that symbolizes self-discipline, which itself is ignited by deep knowledge. This shows how wisdom fuels control over body and breath.
vishnu_gita::186.modern_relevance: When you focus your mind with clear understanding, even restless impulses and habits can be transformed into deliberate, meaningful actions.
vishnu_gita::186.insight: It teaches you to use wisdom to ignite self-control, turning every action into a conscious practice.

vishnu_gita::187.verse_hindi: कोई कोई द्रव्यदानरूपी यज्ञ, कोई तपोयज्ञ और कोई योगयज्ञ के अनुष्ठाता है तथा नियम में दृढ़ रहने वाले यतिगण स्वाध्याय और ब्रह्मज्ञानरूपी यज्ञ का अनुष्ठान करते हैं।
vishnu_gita::187.english_translation: Some perform sacrifices of material gifts, some perform sacrifices of disciplined austerity, some perform sacrifices of yoga, and some steadfast ascetics perform sacrifices of self-study and knowledge of the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::187.translation_literal: द्रव्ययज्ञाः (material sacrifices) तपोयज्ञा (austerity sacrifices) योगयज्ञा (yoga sacrifices) तथा (and also) अपरे (others) स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाः (sacrifices of self-study and knowledge) यतयः (ascetics) संशितव्रताः (steadfast in vows)
vishnu_gita::187.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::187.essence: Dedication to the divine takes many sincere forms, all are valid sacrifices.
vishnu_gita::187.simple_meaning: People honor the divine in different ways: giving gifts, practicing austerity, doing yoga, or studying sacred knowledge with firm commitment.
vishnu_gita::187.simple_insight: There are many valid ways to express dedication, each equally valuable and sincere.
vishnu_gita::187.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes various types of sacrifices people perform to connect with the divine: material offerings, austerity, disciplined yoga, and study of sacred teachings. This shows the diversity of sincere spiritual effort.
vishnu_gita::187.modern_relevance: You might see people showing commitment differently—some by donating, some by sticking to tough habits, some by meditating, others by learning deeply.
vishnu_gita::187.insight: It teaches you to recognize and respect diverse forms of sincere spiritual effort without judging one as better than another.

vishnu_gita::188.verse_sanskrit:
आपने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥
vishnu_gita::188.verse_hindi: अन्य कोई कोई अपान में प्राण और प्राण में अपान का हवन करते हैं और इस प्रकार से प्राण अपान की गति को जय करके प्राणायाम परायण हो जाते हैं
vishnu_gita::188.english_translation: Some offer the life force into the downward breath or the downward breath into the life force, controlling the flow between them and dedicating themselves to breath control.
vishnu_gita::188.translation_literal: आपने (themselves) / जुह्वति (offer) / प्राणं (life force) / प्राणेऽपानं (into life force, downward breath) / तथाऽपरे (and others) / प्राणापानगती (life force-downward breath movement) / रुद्ध्वा (controlling) / प्राणायामपरायणाः (dedicated to breath control)
vishnu_gita::188.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::188.essence: Controlling breath directs your vital energy and deepens your focused discipline.
vishnu_gita::188.simple_meaning: You can offer your energy by controlling the flow between your inward life force and outward breath, dedicating yourself to breath control.
vishnu_gita::188.simple_insight: There’s power and calm when you learn to master your breathing and energy flow.
vishnu_gita::188.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains how some practitioners dedicate themselves to controlling the vital energies by regulating the life force (prana) and downward breath (apana), using breath control (pranayama) to achieve balance and mastery.
vishnu_gita::188.modern_relevance: When you pause and focus on your breathing during stress, you engage this ancient practice of balancing inner energy and breath.
vishnu_gita::188.insight: It teaches you to channel scattered energy by mastering the natural rhythm between inhalation and exhalation.

vishnu_gita::189.verse_sanskrit:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान् प्राणेषु जुह्वति।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मपाः ॥
vishnu_gita::189.verse_hindi: अन्य कोई कोई नियताहारी होकर प्राण में प्राण को हवन करते हैं। यज्ञ के द्वारा निष्पाप, सभी यज्ञवेत्ता
vishnu_gita::189.english_translation: Some, disciplined in their habits, offer life force into life force. All these knowledgeable in sacrifice are free from faults through sacrifice.
vishnu_gita::189.translation_literal: अपरे (others) नियताहाराः (disciplined in habits) प्राणान् (life forces) प्राणेषु (into life forces) जुह्वति (offer in sacrifice)। सर्वेऽपि (all indeed) एते (these) यज्ञविदो (knowers of sacrifice) यज्ञक्षपितकल्मपाः (sins destroyed by sacrifice) ॥
vishnu_gita::189.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::189.essence: Steady, disciplined action purifies faults and renews your inner life force.
vishnu_gita::189.simple_meaning: People who maintain steady habits offer their life force through disciplined action, which cleanses their faults.
vishnu_gita::189.simple_insight: There is strength and purity in steady, disciplined practice that transforms your inner state.
vishnu_gita::189.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how individuals disciplined in their habits perform sacrifices by offering their life force. This steady practice removes faults and purifies them, showing the power of habitual discipline in spiritual action.
vishnu_gita::189.modern_relevance: You keep a daily routine—whether meditation, exercise, or work—that gradually clears your stress and self-doubt without dramatic effort.
vishnu_gita::189.insight: It shifts your focus from sporadic effort to consistent, disciplined practice as the path to inner cleansing.

vishnu_gita::190.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतमुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यस्त्रिदिवौकसः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::190.verse_hindi: यज्ञ का अवशिष्ट अमृत भोजन करने वाले सनातन ब्रह्म को ही प्राप्त होते हैं। हे देवतागण ! जो लोग यज्ञानुष्ठान से रहित हैं न उनका इहलोक है और न उनका परलोक ही है
vishnu_gita::190.english_translation: Only the eternal supreme reality attains the immortal nectar left from sacrifice; those without sacrifice have neither this world nor the higher realm.
vishnu_gita::190.translation_literal: यज्ञशिष्टामृतमुजो (sacrificial remnants, immortal nectar) / यान्ति (attain) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सनातनम् (eternal) । / नायं (not this) / लोकोऽस्ति (world exists) / अयज्ञस्य (without sacrifice) / कुतः (from where) / अन्यः (any other) / त्रिदिवौकसः (three realms) !
vishnu_gita::190.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::190.essence: True sacrifice is the gateway to eternal fulfillment and higher realms.
vishnu_gita::190.simple_meaning: Only those who engage in true sacrifice receive the immortal essence and reach the eternal supreme reality. Without sacrifice, neither this world nor the higher realm is accessible.
vishnu_gita::190.simple_insight: You feel the importance of sincere offering as the bridge to lasting fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::190.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the immortal nectar left after a true sacrifice is received by the eternal supreme reality. Those who avoid sacrifice have no connection to this world or any higher realm, emphasizing the necessity of selfless action.
vishnu_gita::190.modern_relevance: You give your time and energy to a cause bigger than yourself; this offering nourishes your deepest fulfillment and connection beyond daily life.
vishnu_gita::190.insight: It teaches you that engaging earnestly in selfless acts connects you to lasting reality beyond transient experience.

vishnu_gita::191.verse_sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।
कर्मजान वित्त तान् सनिवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::191.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म के जानने वालों के मुख से इस प्रकार से बहुप्रकार के यज्ञो का विस्तार हुआ है उन सबको कर्म से उत्पन्न जानो, ऐसा जानकर तुम मुक्ति को प्राप्त होगे
vishnu_gita::191.english_translation: From the mouths of those who know the supreme reality, many types of sacrifices have been declared; knowing all these arise from action, you will attain freedom.
vishnu_gita::191.translation_literal: एवं (thus) / बहुविधा (many types) / यज्ञा (sacrifices) / वितता (spread) / ब्रह्मणो (of the supreme reality) / मुखे (mouth) / कर्मजान (born of action) / वित्त (wealth/possessions) / तान् (those) / सनिवं (certainly) / ज्ञात्वा (knowing) / विमोक्ष्यते (one is freed)
vishnu_gita::191.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::191.essence: Understanding that all sacred acts originate in action leads to genuine freedom.
vishnu_gita::191.simple_meaning: Many kinds of sacred actions come from the supreme reality. When you understand these actions arise from effort, you gain freedom.
vishnu_gita::191.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that all actions and their fruits have a clear origin you can understand.
vishnu_gita::191.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that those who truly know the supreme reality declare many types of sacred sacrifices. Recognizing that these arise through action helps the seeker understand how to transcend their effects and gain freedom.
vishnu_gita::191.modern_relevance: You notice how every project, task, or relationship unfolds from your actions. Realizing this gives you control and peace beyond outcomes.
vishnu_gita::191.insight: It teaches you to see all results as products of your actions, which shifts focus from attachment to understanding.

vishnu_gita::192.verse_sanskrit:
श्रेयान् द्रव्यमयाद यज्ञान ज्ञानयज्ञोऽमृतान्धसः ।
सर्व कर्माग्विलं देवाः ! ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::192.verse_hindi: हे अमृत भोजी देवतागण ! द्रव्यमय यज्ञ से ज्ञानयज्ञ श्रेष्ठ है क्योंकि ज्ञान में ही सब कर्मों की पूर्णरूप से परि समाप्ति हुआ करती है
vishnu_gita::192.english_translation: O immortal enjoyers among the radiant beings! The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to the sacrifice of material wealth because through knowledge all actions come to complete fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::192.translation_literal: श्रेयान् (superior) द्रव्यमयाद (than material wealth) यज्ञान (sacrifice) ज्ञानयज्ञः (knowledge sacrifice) अमृतान्धसः (O immortal enjoyers) । सर्व (all) कर्माग्विलं (of actions completely) देवाः (radiant beings) ! ज्ञाने (in knowledge) परिसमाप्यते (comes to completion) ॥
vishnu_gita::192.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::192.essence: Knowledge completes all actions more fully than material offerings.
vishnu_gita::192.simple_meaning: Offering knowledge is better than offering material things because knowledge brings all actions to their full completion.
vishnu_gita::192.simple_insight: You feel the power of wisdom to finish what action alone cannot.
vishnu_gita::192.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that sacrifices made with knowledge surpass those made with material wealth because knowledge brings all actions to their true completion.
vishnu_gita::192.modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard and given your time, but understanding your purpose brings deeper completion than material achievement alone.
vishnu_gita::192.insight: It shifts your focus from external offerings to cultivating inner understanding to fulfill your efforts.

vishnu_gita::193.verse_sanskrit:
अश्रद्दधाना जीवा वै धर्मस्यास्य सुधाशनाः !।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवमनि ॥
vishnu_gita::193.verse_hindi: हे सुधा के पान करने वाले देवतागण ! इस धर्म में अश्रद्धा करने वाले जीवगण मुझको न प्राप्त करके मृत्युमय संसारमार्ग में लौट आते हैं
vishnu_gita::193.english_translation: Those without faith in this dharma do not reach me and return to the death-bound cycle of existence.
vishnu_gita::193.translation_literal: अश्रद्दधाना (without faith) / जीवा (beings) / वै (certainly) / धर्मस्यास्य (of this dharma) / सुधाशनाः (drinkers of nectar) / अप्राप्य (not attaining) / मां (me) / निवर्तन्ते (return) / मृत्युसंसारवमनि (in death-bound cycle of existence)
vishnu_gita::193.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::193.essence: Without trust in the path, you cannot reach the true self and remain trapped in suffering.
vishnu_gita::193.simple_meaning: Those who lack trust in this teaching fail to reach the divine and return to endless suffering.
vishnu_gita::193.simple_insight: Trust feels like a fragile step, but it opens the path beyond suffering.
vishnu_gita::193.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, warning that beings who do not trust this dharma fail to attain him and instead return to the cycle of birth and death. This highlights faith as essential for spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::193.modern_relevance: You hesitate to fully commit to a new path, and so you find yourself stuck repeating old painful patterns.
vishnu_gita::193.insight: It teaches you that trust is not optional—it unlocks progress toward the true self, while doubt keeps you trapped.

vishnu_gita::194.verse_sanskrit:
त्रविद्या मां सोमपाः पृतपापा: यज्ञैरिष्टा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयनते ।
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक पश्नन्ति दिव्यान दिवि देवभोगान ॥
vishnu_gita::194.verse_hindi: वेदत्रय के अनुसार कर्मकाण्डपरायण  सकामकर्मीगण यज्ञ द्वारा मेरा यजन करके यज्ञ शेषरूपी सोमपान करते हुए और निष्पाप होते हुए स्वर्गगति की प्रार्थना करते हैं, वे लोग पुण्यस्वरूप इन्द्रलोक में पहुंच कर वहां दिव्य देवभोग समूह भोग करते हैं।
vishnu_gita::194.english_translation: According to the three Vedas, those devoted to ritual acts perform sacrifices and drink the Soma; being free of sin, they seek heavenly realms and enjoy divine pleasures among the gods.
vishnu_gita::194.translation_literal: त्रविद्या (three Vedas) / मां (me) / सोमपाः (those who drink Soma) / पृतपापा: (free from sin) / यज्ञैरिष्टा (by sacrifices desired) / स्वर्गतिं (heavenly path) / प्रार्थयनते (seek) / । / ते (they) / पुण्यमासाद्य (attaining merit) / सुरेन्द्रलोक (Indra's realm) / पश्नन्ति (enjoy) / दिव्यान (divine) / दिवि (in the sky) / देवभोगान (pleasures of gods) / ॥
vishnu_gita::194.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::194.essence: Ritual actions bring heavenly rewards but do not lead to ultimate freedom.
vishnu_gita::194.simple_meaning: People who follow ritual acts perform sacrifices and drink Soma to become pure and seek to reach heaven, where they enjoy divine pleasures.
vishnu_gita::194.simple_insight: Ritual actions can lead to heavenly rewards, but these are temporary enjoyments in higher realms.
vishnu_gita::194.detailed_meaning: Suta narrates how those devoted to ritualistic duties perform sacrifices and consume Soma, purify themselves, and pray to reach heavenly realms. The verse explains the traditional outcome of ritual karma in the Vedic worldview.
vishnu_gita::194.insight: It highlights the ritual path's temporary goals and rewards, contrasting with deeper spiritual freedom.

vishnu_gita::195.verse_sanskrit:
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति ।
एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुभपन्ना गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥
vishnu_gita::195.verse_hindi: वे उन विपुल स्वर्ग सुख समूह को भोग करने के अनन्तर पुण्य क्षीण होने पर मृत्युलोक में लौट आते हैं और वेदत्रयविहित धर्मों को अवलम्बन करके भोग की इच्छा करते हुए आवागमन चक्र में आया जाया करते हैं
vishnu_gita::195.english_translation: After enjoying the vast pleasures of the higher realm, when their virtue is exhausted, they return to the mortal world and, following the threefold duties, repeatedly come and go driven by desire.
vishnu_gita::195.translation_literal: ते (they) / तं (that) / भुक्त्वा (having enjoyed) / स्वर्गलोकं (the higher realm) / विशालं (vast) / क्षीणे (exhausted) / पुण्ये (virtue) / मर्त्यलोकं (mortal world) / विशन्ति (enter) । / एवं (thus) / त्रयीधर्म (threefold duties) / अनुभपन्ना (following) / गतागतं (coming and going) / कामकामा (desiring pleasure) / लभन्ते (obtain) ॥
vishnu_gita::195.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::195.essence: Desire causes repeated returns to the mortal world despite enjoying higher pleasures.
vishnu_gita::195.simple_meaning: After enjoying happiness in the higher realm, when their merit ends, they return to the mortal world and keep coming back driven by desire, following prescribed duties.
vishnu_gita::195.simple_insight: Desire keeps beings trapped in a cycle of coming and going despite enjoying bliss.
vishnu_gita::195.detailed_meaning: This verse describes souls who, after experiencing pleasures in the higher realm, exhaust their good karma and return to the mortal world. Despite following sacred duties, their desires drive them to repeatedly cycle through birth and death.
vishnu_gita::195.insight: It reveals how desire fuels repeated cycles of action and consequence, even after experiencing joy and rest.

vishnu_gita::196.verse_sanskrit:
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च ।
न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवान्त ते ॥
vishnu_gita::196.verse_hindi: मैं ही सभी यज्ञो का भोक्ता और प्रभु हूँ परन्तु वे लोग मेरे यथार्थ स्वरूप को नहीं जानते हैं इस कारण उनकी पुनरावृत्ति होती है।
vishnu_gita::196.english_translation: I am indeed the recipient and lord of all sacrifices, yet they do not truly know my real nature, and thus they fall back into repetition.
vishnu_gita::196.translation_literal: अहं (I) हि (indeed) सर्वयज्ञानां (of all sacrifices) भोक्ता (recipient/enjoyer) च (and) प्रभुरेव (only lord) च (and) । न (not) तु (but) माम् (me) अभिजानन्ति (know) तत्त्वेन (in true nature) अतः (therefore) च्यवान्त (fall back) ते (they) ॥
vishnu_gita::196.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::196.essence: Not knowing the divine nature behind actions causes endless repetitive cycles.
vishnu_gita::196.simple_meaning: The divine is the true recipient of all sacrifices and actions, but people fail to recognize this reality, causing them to repeat their cycles.
vishnu_gita::196.simple_insight: It feels freeing to realize your actions connect to a deeper truth beyond repetition.
vishnu_gita::196.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals he is the ultimate recipient and lord of all rituals, but humans do not understand his true essence, which causes them to get stuck in repetitive cycles of action and consequence.
vishnu_gita::196.modern_relevance: You keep repeating the same mistakes or habits, unaware that you have not yet seen the deeper truth behind your actions.
vishnu_gita::196.insight: This shifts your focus from external rituals or results to recognizing the deeper presence behind all your actions.

vishnu_gita::197.verse_sanskrit:
सम्पत्तिमासुरी प्राहुग्धर्मस्य विवर्द्धिनीम्।
धर्मप्रवर्द्धिनी देवी सम्पत्तिं तद्वदेव हि ॥
vishnu_gita::197.verse_hindi: आसुरी सम्पत्ति को अधर्म वर्द्धिनी कहते हैं और उसी प्रकार दैवी सम्पत्ति को धर्मवर्द्धिका कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::197.english_translation: Wealth associated with ego is called adharma-increasing, while divine wealth is called dharma-increasing.
vishnu_gita::197.translation_literal: सम्पत्तिम् (wealth) आसुरी (egoistic) प्राहुः (is said) धर्मस्य (of dharma) विवर्द्धिनीम् (increasing) । धर्मप्रवर्द्धिनी (dharma-increasing) देवी (divine) सम्पत्तिं (wealth) तद्वदेव (that is indeed said) हि (indeed) ॥
vishnu_gita::197.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::197.essence: Wealth either increases ego and confusion or supports righteous growth and purpose.
vishnu_gita::197.simple_meaning: There are two kinds of wealth: one that grows ego and leads away from your true purpose, and one that supports and increases righteous living.
vishnu_gita::197.simple_insight: Recognizing the source of your wealth can reveal whether it nourishes your true self or your ego.
vishnu_gita::197.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that not all wealth is equal. Wealth born from ego and selfishness increases confusion and adharma, while wealth aligned with dharma supports righteousness and growth toward one's true purpose.
vishnu_gita::197.modern_relevance: You might receive money or success that either fuels your pride and anxiety or supports your values and well-being.
vishnu_gita::197.insight: You learn to distinguish between possessions that strengthen your purpose and those that inflate ego, shifting how you relate to success.

vishnu_gita::198.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मात्सोव्वौर्हि युष्माभिर्देवैः श्रेयोऽभिकाङ्गिभिः।
कर्तव्य आश्रयो दैव्याः सम्पत्तेरेव सर्वदा ॥
vishnu_gita::198.verse_hindi: इस कारण सर्वदा कल्याण चाहने वाले आप सबको दैवी सम्पत्ति का ही आश्रय लेना उचित है
vishnu_gita::198.english_translation: Therefore, you all who desire well-being should always rely on divine qualities alone.
vishnu_gita::198.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) सोऽव्वौर्हि (you all indeed) युष्माभिः (by you) देवैः (divine) श्रेयोऽभिकाङ्गिभिः (auspicious qualities) कर्तव्य (should be done) आश्रय (support) दैव्याः (divine) सम्पत्तेः (qualities) एव (only) सर्वदा (always)
vishnu_gita::198.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::198.essence: True well-being always rests on relying on divine qualities alone.
vishnu_gita::198.simple_meaning: You should always depend only on divine qualities to achieve true well-being and success.
vishnu_gita::198.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing true well-being comes from inner divine qualities, not external things.
vishnu_gita::198.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs those seeking lasting good to depend solely on divine qualities, not temporary or worldly support, emphasizing the foundation of spiritual strength for enduring well-being.
vishnu_gita::198.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by temporary solutions, you remember that true support comes from your inner strength and values.
vishnu_gita::198.insight: It shifts focus from chasing fleeting external comforts to cultivating reliable inner qualities for well-being.

vishnu_gita::199.verse_sanskrit:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
vishnu_gita::199.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! भयशून्यता, चित्त की प्रसन्नता, आत्मज्ञान के उपायों में निष्ठा, दान, इन्द्रिय संयम, यज्ञ, स्वाध्याय, तप, सरलता,
vishnu_gita::199.english_translation: O divine beings, fearlessness, purity of mind, steady practice of knowledge yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, and straightforwardness are qualities to cultivate.
vishnu_gita::199.translation_literal: अभयं (fearlessness) सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः (mind-purity) ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः (steadiness-in-knowledge-yoga) दानं (charity) दमश्च (self-control) यज्ञश्च (sacrifice) स्वाध्यायः (self-study) तपः (austerity) आर्जवम् (straightforwardness)
vishnu_gita::199.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::199.essence: Steady courage, generosity, and self-control together build true inner discipline.
vishnu_gita::199.simple_meaning: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steady wisdom practice, generosity, control of senses, sacrifice, study, austerity, and honesty help you grow in discipline.
vishnu_gita::199.simple_insight: You feel stronger and clearer when you build steady habits of courage and kindness.
vishnu_gita::199.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, listing essential qualities for inner growth: fearlessness, a pure mind, steady wisdom practice, generosity, control over senses, ritual sacrifice, study, austerity, and honesty. These form a disciplined life foundation.
vishnu_gita::199.modern_relevance: You commit to daily habits like honest effort, learning, and kindness that quietly shape your character over time.
vishnu_gita::199.insight: It teaches you to strengthen yourself through balanced courage, generosity, and steady inner work.

vishnu_gita::200.verse_sanskrit:
अहिंसा सत्यम क्रोधस्त्याग: शांतिरपैशुनम ।
दया भूतेप्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्द्द्वं ह्रीरचापलम ॥
vishnu_gita::200.verse_hindi: अहिंसा, सत्य, क्रोध का न होना, त्याग, शान्ति, खलता का त्याग, सब प्राणियों पर दया, लोभ का त्याग, अहंकार का त्याग ही अर्थात् पापकर्म से लज्जा, चपलता का त्याग,
vishnu_gita::200.english_translation: Non-violence, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, peace, giving up malice, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, humility, shame of wrongful acts, and abandoning restlessness.
vishnu_gita::200.translation_literal: अहिंसा (non-violence) / सत्यम (truth) / क्रोधः (anger) / त्यागः (renunciation) / शान्तिः (peace) / अपैशुनम् (absence of malice) / दया (compassion) / भूतेषु (towards beings) / अवलोलुप्त्वं (freedom from greed) / मार्द्दवं (gentleness) / ह्रीः (modesty) / चापलम् (restlessness)
vishnu_gita::200.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::200.essence: True discipline is letting go of harmful emotions and embracing kindness and peace.
vishnu_gita::200.simple_meaning: Living with kindness, truth, peace, and compassion means letting go of anger, greed, and restlessness.
vishnu_gita::200.simple_insight: You feel lighter and calmer when you release anger, greed, and harshness.
vishnu_gita::200.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that true discipline arises from abandoning harmful emotions like anger and greed while embracing kindness, truth, peace, and humility. This balance leads to a harmonious life and steady character.
vishnu_gita::200.modern_relevance: After a tense argument, you choose calmness and kindness instead of holding onto anger or resentment.
vishnu_gita::200.insight: It shifts your focus from reacting with anger or desire to cultivating gentleness and peacefulness in daily actions.

vishnu_gita::201.verse_sanskrit:
तेज: क्षमा धृति: शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीयभिजातस्य निर्जराः! ॥
vishnu_gita::201.verse_hindi: तेजस्विता, क्षमा, धैर्य, शौच, द्रोह का त्याग और अपने पूज्य होने के अभिमान का अभाव, यह सभी धर्मवृत्तियाँ दैवी संपत्ति वाले व्यक्तियों मे हुआ करती है
vishnu_gita::201.english_translation: Radiance, forgiveness, patience, purity, renouncing betrayal, and absence of pride in being revered are qualities born in those with divine nature.
vishnu_gita::201.translation_literal: तेज: (radiance) क्षमा (forgiveness) धृति: (patience) शौचम् (purity) अध्रोहो (non-betrayal) नातिमानिता (not excessive pride) भवन्ति (are) सम्पदं (qualities) दैवीय-भिजातस्य (of divine-born) निर्जराः (ageless/steadfast)!
vishnu_gita::201.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::201.essence: Steadfast virtues like patience and humility arise naturally in those with divine nature.
vishnu_gita::201.simple_meaning: Certain noble qualities like patience, forgiveness, purity, avoiding betrayal, and humility naturally arise in those connected to the divine nature.
vishnu_gita::201.simple_insight: You feel steadiness and inner strength when you practice patience and humility.
vishnu_gita::201.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a person with divine qualities naturally embodies radiant virtues such as forgiveness, patience, purity, loyalty, and humility without arrogance. These virtues mark a steady and mature character.
vishnu_gita::201.modern_relevance: In a heated argument, choosing forgiveness and humility helps you stay steady and respected, even when others react harshly.
vishnu_gita::201.insight: It teaches you to cultivate steady virtues that build inner strength and steady your character.

vishnu_gita::202.verse_sanskrit:
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।
अज्ञानञ्चाभिजातस्य देवाः ! सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥
vishnu_gita::202.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! दम्भ, दर्प, अहङ्कार, क्रोध, निष्ठुरता, अविवेक, ये सब पाप सम्बन्धीय वृत्तियां बासुरी सम्पत्ति वाले व्यक्तियों में हुआ करती हैं
vishnu_gita::202.english_translation: O divine beings! Hypocrisy, pride, ego, anger, harshness, and ignorance are qualities found in those attached to lower tendencies.
vishnu_gita::202.translation_literal: दम्भो (hypocrisy) / दर्पोऽभिमानश्च (pride and ego) / क्रोधः (anger) / पारुष्यमेव (harshness indeed) / च (and) / अज्ञानञ्चाभिजातस्य (and ignorance of the unlearned) / देवाः (O divine beings) / सम्पदमासुरीम् (qualities of lower nature)
vishnu_gita::202.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::202.essence: Harsh emotions reveal attachment to lower, restless tendencies, not your true self.
vishnu_gita::202.simple_meaning: Pride, ego, anger, harshness, and ignorance are signs of a disturbed mind caught in lower tendencies.
vishnu_gita::202.simple_insight: You can feel how anger and pride cloud your true self and cause inner unrest.
vishnu_gita::202.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that qualities like hypocrisy, pride, ego, anger, harshness, and ignorance belong to those trapped in harmful tendencies. Recognizing these traits helps one move toward inner clarity.
vishnu_gita::202.modern_relevance: When you snap at a loved one or feel proud to prove a point, these feelings reveal your mind’s unrest and block your deeper peace.
vishnu_gita::202.insight: It teaches you to notice harsh emotions as signals of deeper confusion, inviting you to detach and observe.

vishnu_gita::203.verse_sanskrit:
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता।
नैव शोचत भो देवाः ! दैवी सम्पदमास्थिताः ॥
vishnu_gita::203.verse_hindi: देवी सम्पत्तियां मोक्ष का कारण होती हैं और आसुरी सम्पत्तियां बन्धन का कारण हुआ करती है। इस कारण हे देवतागण ! आपलोग चिन्ता ही न करो क्योंकि आपलोग देवी सम्पत्ति में स्थित हो
vishnu_gita::203.english_translation: Divine qualities lead to freedom, while demonic qualities cause bondage. So, beings of light, do not grieve, for you abide in divine qualities.
vishnu_gita::203.translation_literal: दैवी (divine) / सम्पद् (qualities) / विमोक्षाय (for liberation) / निबन्धाय (for bondage) / आसुरी (demonic) / मता (considered) / नैव (never) / शोचत (grieve) / भो (O) / देवाः (beings of light) / दैवी (divine) / सम्पदम् (qualities) / आस्थिताः (abiding)
vishnu_gita::203.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::203.essence: Freedom arises from divine qualities; bondage comes from shadow qualities.
vishnu_gita::203.simple_meaning: Divine qualities lead to freedom, while demonic qualities cause bondage. You should not worry because you possess divine qualities.
vishnu_gita::203.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your true nature is already free and pure.
vishnu_gita::203.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that qualities aligned with the divine nature lead to liberation, while those aligned with ego and shadows cause bondage. He encourages the radiant beings not to grieve, affirming their existence in divine qualities that bring freedom.
vishnu_gita::203.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your darker impulses, remember your true qualities are freeing and can guide you beyond limitation.
vishnu_gita::203.insight: It shifts focus from fearing negative traits to recognizing and resting in your inherent freedom.

vishnu_gita::204.verse_sanskrit:
द्वौ भूतसर्गाौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च।
देवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं शृणुतामराः ॥
vishnu_gita::204.verse_hindi: हे अमरगण ! इस संसार के प्राणियों में देवीभाव और आसुरीभाव रूप से दो प्रकार की सृष्टि है। इनमे से दैवी भाव का विस्तारित विवरण कहा गया है अब आसुरी भाव का विवरण मुझसे सुनो
vishnu_gita::204.english_translation: O immortal beings! In this world, there are two kinds of beings: divine and shadowy. The detailed description of the divine nature has been given; now listen to the description of the shadowy nature from me.
vishnu_gita::204.translation_literal: द्वौ (two) / भूतसर्गाौ (creations of beings) / लोकेऽस्मिन् (in this world) / दैव (divine) / आसुर (shadowy) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / देवो (the divine) / विस्तरशः (in detail) / प्रोक्त (told) / आसुरं (shadowy) / शृणुतामराः (listen, immortals)
vishnu_gita::204.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::204.essence: The world contains two kinds of beings: divine and shadowy, each with distinct qualities.
vishnu_gita::204.simple_meaning: There are two kinds of beings in the world: those with divine qualities and those with shadowy qualities. The divine side has been explained; now the shadowy side will be described.
vishnu_gita::204.simple_insight: Understanding the world involves recognizing both light and shadow aspects in beings.
vishnu_gita::204.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the immortal sages, explaining that all beings fall into two categories: divine and shadowy. He notes that he has already described the divine nature in detail and now will explain the shadowy nature, setting the stage for contrasting qualities.
vishnu_gita::204.insight: It prepares you to see the world as a balance of opposing qualities, not just one-sided.

vishnu_gita::205.verse_sanskrit:
प्रत्तिञ्च निवृत्तिञ्च जना न विदुरासुराः।
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::205.verse_hindi: आसुरी प्रकृत्ति वाले व्यक्तिगण प्रवृत्ति और निवृत्ति दोनों को नहीं जानते हैं इस कारण उनमें न शौच है न आचार है और न सत्य है।
vishnu_gita::205.english_translation: Beings of shadow nature do not understand activity or cessation; in them are no purity, conduct, or truth.
vishnu_gita::205.translation_literal: प्रत्तिञ्च (activity) / निवृत्तिञ्च (cessation) / जना (beings) / न (not) / विदुरासुराः (shadow-natured beings) / न (not) / शौचं (purity) / नापि (also not) / चाचारो (conduct) / न (not) / सत्यं (truth) / तेषु (in them) / विद्यते (exists)
vishnu_gita::205.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::205.essence: Lack of understanding both action and resting causes loss of purity, conduct, and truth.
vishnu_gita::205.simple_meaning: Beings driven by ego and confusion neither understand how to act rightly nor how to stop; they lack purity, proper conduct, and truth.
vishnu_gita::205.simple_insight: Recognizing what you don’t understand about acting and resting frees you from confusion and falsehood.
vishnu_gita::205.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that beings dominated by asuric nature lack awareness of both engagement and withdrawal. Because they cannot grasp these basic principles, they fail to uphold cleanliness, moral behavior, and truthfulness, highlighting their deep confusion.
vishnu_gita::205.modern_relevance: When you rush without pause or avoid necessary action, you lose touch with integrity and honesty in your life.
vishnu_gita::205.insight: It teaches you to recognize the importance of balancing activity with rest to maintain clarity and truthfulness.

vishnu_gita::206.verse_hindi: वे असुरमावापन्न लोग कहते हैं कि यह जगत् असत्य है,धर्म अधर्म व्यवस्थाशून्य अप्रतिष्ठ है, ईश्वर शून्य है, विनापरम्परा सम्बन्ध के यही अचानक उत्पन्न हुआ है, इसका और कुछ भी कारण नहीं है केवल स्त्री पुरुष के काम से उत्पन्न हैं
vishnu_gita::206.english_translation: Those who have fallen into ignorance say the world is unreal, without order or the divine, spontaneously born only from desire and union, with no other cause.
vishnu_gita::206.translation_literal: असत्यम (unreal) अप्रतिष्ठञ्च (without foundation) जगद् (world) आहुः (say) अन ईश्वरम् (no divine) । अपरस्पर (from each other) संभूतं (born) किम् (what) अन्यत् (other) काम (desire) हैूतुकम् (cause) ॥
vishnu_gita::206.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::206.essence: The world is not merely a random product of desire; it has a deeper foundation.
vishnu_gita::206.simple_meaning: Some say the world is unreal and only arose from desire without any deeper cause or divine order.
vishnu_gita::206.simple_insight: It feels unsettling to hear the world called meaningless, but this view overlooks the underlying order.
vishnu_gita::206.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses a common but mistaken belief among those lost in ignorance, who deny the world's reality and divine foundation, claiming it arose randomly from desire alone.
vishnu_gita::206.modern_relevance: When chaos and confusion hit, it’s easy to think everything is random and meaningless, but deeper order often exists beneath the surface.
vishnu_gita::206.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the world as meaningless chance to recognizing a deeper structure beyond desire.

vishnu_gita::207.verse_sanskrit:
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥
vishnu_gita::207.verse_hindi: यह सब अल्पबुद्धि असुरगण ऐसे विचारों को प्राश्रय करके मलिनचित्त उग्रकर्मा और अहितकारी होकर जगत के नाश के लिये उत्पन्न होते हैं
vishnu_gita::207.english_translation: Those with limited understanding, embracing such views, become restless doers harming the world’s well-being and leading to its decay.
vishnu_gita::207.translation_literal: एतां (these) दृष्टिम् (view) अवष्टभ्य (embracing) नष्टात्मनः (lost-self) अल्पबुद्धयः (small-minded) । प्रभवन्ति (arise) उग्रकर्माणः (fierce-actions) क्षयाय (for-destruction) जगतः (world) अहिताः (harmful) ॥
vishnu_gita::207.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::207.essence: Limited understanding fuels harmful actions that damage the world’s wellbeing.
vishnu_gita::207.simple_meaning: Holding onto wrong ideas leads to harmful actions that damage others and the world.
vishnu_gita::207.simple_insight: You feel the weight of how your mindset shapes actions affecting everything around you.
vishnu_gita::207.detailed_meaning: Vishnu warns that those with limited understanding who adopt harmful views generate intense destructive actions. These actions harm the world and cause decay. This teaching is a call to refine one’s perspective to prevent damage.
vishnu_gita::207.modern_relevance: When you fixate on narrow, negative thoughts, you might act out in ways that hurt your relationships or community without realizing it.
vishnu_gita::207.insight: It teaches you to recognize how harmful beliefs fuel destructive behavior, urging a clearer, disciplined mind.

vishnu_gita::208.verse_sanskrit:
कामाश्रित दुष्पूरं दम्भमानम्दान्विता: ।
मोहादगृहीत्वा सद्ग्राहान प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रता: ॥
vishnu_gita::208.verse_hindi: वे लोग पूर्ण नहीं होने वाली कामनाओं को आश्रय लेकर, दम्भ अभिमान और गर्व से युक्त होकर, मोह से दुराग्रहों को धारण करने अपवित्र व्रतों को करते हुए अकार्यों मे प्रवृत हुआ करते हैं
vishnu_gita::208.english_translation: People who cling to unfulfillable desires, filled with pride and arrogance, hold on to wrong attachments out of confusion, and engage in impure practices.
vishnu_gita::208.translation_literal: कामाश्रित (desires-dependent) दुष्पूरं (hard to fulfill) दम्भमानम् (full of deceit/pride) दान्विता: (and arrogance) । मोहात् (from delusion) अगृहीत्वा (not holding) सद्ग्राहान (right attachments) प्रवर्तन्ते (they engage) अशुचिव्रता: (impure vows/practices) ॥
vishnu_gita::208.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::208.essence: Clinging to impossible desires fuels pride and confusion, leading to harmful attachments.
vishnu_gita::208.simple_meaning: Holding on to desires that can never be fulfilled creates pride and confusion, leading you to harmful attachments and impure actions.
vishnu_gita::208.simple_insight: Letting go of impossible desires frees you from pride and confusion that trap you in harmful patterns.
vishnu_gita::208.detailed_meaning: Vishnu warns that people who base their actions on impossible desires become proud and arrogant, and from this confusion, cling to wrong attachments, performing impure or misguided practices. This teaching reveals how desire and ego cloud judgment and lead to suffering.
vishnu_gita::208.modern_relevance: You chase goals that feel out of reach, building pride when you achieve little, and cling to habits that don’t serve you, causing frustration.
vishnu_gita::208.insight: Recognize when your desires are unrealistic and how pride from unmet wants fuels harmful attachments; then shift focus to realistic, wholesome aims.

vishnu_gita::209.verse_hindi: मरणकाल पर्यन्त व्यापिनी अपरिमित चिन्ता को आश्रय करते हुए कामभोग परायण होकर "यह कामभोग ही परमपुरुषार्थ है" ऐसा निश्चय करते हुए
vishnu_gita::209.english_translation: They rely on endless worries until death, certain that satisfying desires is the highest goal.
vishnu_gita::209.translation_literal: चिन्ता (worry) अपरिमेयाञ्च (endless) प्रलयान्ताम् (until the time of destruction/death) उपाश्रिताः (relying on) काम (desires) उपभोग (enjoyment) परमा (supreme) एतावदिति (thus) निश्चिताः (certain)
vishnu_gita::209.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::209.essence: Endless worry and desire are mistaken for the highest purpose until life ends.
vishnu_gita::209.simple_meaning: Many live absorbed in endless worry, believing that fulfilling desires is life's highest achievement.
vishnu_gita::209.simple_insight: It's painful to realize how much endless worry and desire trap you in a false highest goal.
vishnu_gita::209.detailed_meaning: Vishnu points out how people cling to infinite worries and focus solely on fulfilling desires, wrongly believing that this is their ultimate purpose, just until death arrives.
vishnu_gita::209.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly through social media, chasing likes and desires, convinced this will bring lasting happiness.
vishnu_gita::209.insight: It shifts your view from chasing desires as the highest aim to questioning what truly matters beyond worry.

vishnu_gita::210.verse_hindi: सैकड़ों आशारूपी पाशों में बंधकर और काम क्रोध परायण होते हुए, वह लोग कामभोग के लिये अन्यायपूर्वक अर्थ संचय की इच्छा करते हैं
vishnu_gita::210.english_translation: Bound by hundreds of chains of desire and driven by craving and anger, they wrongly accumulate wealth for sensual pleasures.
vishnu_gita::210.translation_literal: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः (bound by hundreds of chains of desire) / कामक्रोधपरायणाः (devoted to desire and anger) / ईहन्ते (they strive) / कामभोगार्थम् (for the purpose of sensual enjoyment) / अन्यायेन (wrongly) / अर्थ (wealth) / संचयान (accumulation)
vishnu_gita::210.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::210.essence: Desire and anger trap you in wrongful craving for fleeting pleasure.
vishnu_gita::210.simple_meaning: People get trapped by many desires and driven by craving and anger, wrongly gathering wealth just for pleasure.
vishnu_gita::210.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing desire and anger are chains you can choose to break.
vishnu_gita::210.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how people become caught in countless desires and controlled by craving and anger. This leads them to unjustly collect wealth only for fleeting pleasures, trapping themselves in suffering.
vishnu_gita::210.modern_relevance: You might find yourself chasing more money or status out of frustration or craving, losing sight of what truly matters.
vishnu_gita::210.insight: Recognize how desire and anger fuel harmful, endless seeking; shifting focus frees your energy.

vishnu_gita::211.verse_sanskrit:
इदमद्य माया लब्धमिदं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम ।
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम ॥
vishnu_gita::211.verse_hindi: आज मुझे यह लाभ हुआ, यह मनोरथ प्राप्त होगा, मेरा यह धन है,  और यह धन भी मेरा होगा,
vishnu_gita::211.english_translation: Today I have gained this, I will obtain this desire, this wealth is mine, and this wealth will be mine again.
vishnu_gita::211.translation_literal: इदम् (this) अद्य (today) माया (illusion/wealth) लब्धम् (obtained) इदम् (this) प्राप्स्ये (will obtain) मनोरथम् (desire) इदम् (this) अस्तीत् (is) इदम् (this) अपि (also) मे (my) भविष्यति (will be) पुनः (again) धनम् (wealth)
vishnu_gita::211.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::211.essence: Attachment to gains and desires binds the mind to temporary possessions.
