vishnu_gita::211.simple_meaning: The speaker talks about having gained something today and expecting to gain more, considering wealth and desires as possessions.
vishnu_gita::211.simple_insight: The focus on possessions and desires shows temporary attachment to what is gained.
vishnu_gita::211.detailed_meaning: The verse expresses a moment of claiming gains and future hopes as personal wealth and desire, reflecting attachment to material success without philosophical reflection.
vishnu_gita::211.insight: It highlights how clinging to possessions and expecting more can anchor the mind in temporary gains.

vishnu_gita::212.verse_sanskrit:
असौ मया इतः शत्रुहनिध्ये चापरानपि ।
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान् मुखी ॥
vishnu_gita::212.verse_hindi: मेरे द्वारा इस शत्रु का नाश हुआ है, और शत्रुओ का भी नाश करूंगा, मैं ईश्वर हूँ, मैं भोगी हूँ, मैं सिद्ध हूँ, मैं बलवान् हूँ, मैं सुखी हूँ,
vishnu_gita::212.english_translation: I have destroyed this enemy, and I will destroy other enemies too; I am the lord, the enjoyer, the accomplished, the strong, the joyful.
vishnu_gita::212.translation_literal: असौ (this) / मया (by me) / इतः (here) / शत्रुहनिध्ये (in enemy destruction) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अन्य (other) / अपि (also) / ईश्वरोऽहम् (I am the lord) / अहं (I) / भोगी (enjoyer) / सिद्धः (accomplished) / अहं (I) / बलवान् (strong) / मुखी (joyful)
vishnu_gita::212.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::212.essence: A victorious being declares strength and joy after defeating enemies.
vishnu_gita::212.simple_meaning: The speaker declares having defeated one enemy and intends to defeat others, claiming to be powerful, accomplished, and joyful.
vishnu_gita::212.simple_insight: This verse expresses confidence and victory but centers on a specific character's claim.
vishnu_gita::212.detailed_meaning: Vishnu proclaims his victory over an enemy and his continued power to defeat others, emphasizing his strength and joy. This verse reflects a situational declaration of triumph rather than a universal teaching.
vishnu_gita::212.insight: It shows a moment of triumph and self-assurance but does not offer a broader teaching for personal growth.

vishnu_gita::213.verse_sanskrit:
आढयोऽभिजनवानसमि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सद्र्श्यो मया ।
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
vishnu_gita::213.verse_hindi: मैं धनवान् हूँ, मैं कुलीन हूँ, मेरे समान और कौन है, मैं यज्ञ करूंगा, मैं दान करूंगा, मैं हर्षको प्राप्त होऊंगा इस प्रकार से वे अज्ञान से विमोहित व्यक्तिगण
vishnu_gita::213.english_translation: I am wealthy, I am noble, who else is like me? I will perform sacrifices, I will give gifts, I will be joyful — thus deluded by ignorance.
vishnu_gita::213.translation_literal: आढयः (wealthy) अभिजनवानसमि (and noble) कोऽन्यः (who else) अस्ति (is) सद्र्श्यो (like) मया (me) । यक्ष्ये (I will perform sacrifices) दास्यामि (I will give) मोदिष्य (I will be joyful) इति (thus) अज्ञानविमोहिताः (deluded by ignorance) ॥
vishnu_gita::213.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::213.essence: Pride in wealth and status deludes and blinds you from true understanding.
vishnu_gita::213.simple_meaning: Thinking 'I am the richest and best' and believing this leads to confusion and blindness to reality.
vishnu_gita::213.simple_insight: You can feel trapped when pride blinds you to your true nature and leads to false joy.
vishnu_gita::213.detailed_meaning: Vishnu points out how people, deluded by ignorance, boast of wealth and status, planning grand acts to prove their worth, unaware that this pride clouds their understanding.
vishnu_gita::213.modern_relevance: You see someone boasting about their achievements or possessions, convinced it makes them superior, yet this pride hides their deeper insecurities.
vishnu_gita::213.insight: It shifts your mind to recognize pride as a form of ignorance that hides your deeper self and true clarity.

vishnu_gita::214.verse_sanskrit:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजाल समावृता
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
vishnu_gita::214.verse_hindi: अनेक विषयों में अपने चित्त को फसाये हुए विक्षिप्त रहते हैं और मोहमय जाल से श्रावृत होकर और कामभोग में आसक्त होकर अपवित्र नरक में पड़ते हैं
vishnu_gita::214.english_translation: Disturbed by many thoughts and trapped in the web of delusion, people fall into the impure lower realm through attachment to desire and pleasure.
vishnu_gita::214.translation_literal: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता (disturbed by many minds) / मोहजाल (web of delusion) / समावृता (covered) / प्रसक्ताः (attached) / कामभोगेषु (in desire-pleasure) / पतन्ति (fall) / नरकेऽशुचौ (into impure lower realm)
vishnu_gita::214.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::214.essence: A restless, desire-bound mind traps you in a web that leads away from freedom.
vishnu_gita::214.simple_meaning: When your mind is restless and caught in illusions, attachment to desires drags you down into an impure state.
vishnu_gita::214.simple_insight: You can feel the heaviness of being trapped by your own desires and confusion.
vishnu_gita::214.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how a distracted mind, overwhelmed by many desires and illusions, becomes trapped in a harmful cycle leading away from purity and freedom. This moment warns against losing clarity through attachment to fleeting pleasures.
vishnu_gita::214.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly, distracted by impulses and cravings, feeling stuck yet pulled toward more momentary pleasures.
vishnu_gita::214.insight: Recognize how distraction and craving cloud your mind and pull your life off course.

vishnu_gita::215.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
vishnu_gita::215.verse_hindi: अपने आप को ही बड़े और पूज्य मानते हुए, अविनयी, धनादिक के अभिमान से अभिमानित और गर्वित होकर वह दम्भ के साथ नाममात्र के यज्ञो द्वारा अविधिपूर्वक यजन किया करते हैं
vishnu_gita::215.english_translation: Considering themselves great and venerable, proud from wealth and arrogance, they perform meaningless rituals with deceit and without true discipline.
vishnu_gita::215.translation_literal: आत्मसम्भाविताः (considering themselves true selves) / स्तब्धाः (stiff/obstinate) / धनमान (pride in wealth) / अदान्विताः (and prideful) / यजन्ते (they perform) / नामयज्ञैः (by nominal rituals) / ते (they) / दम्भेन (with deceit) / अविधिपूर्वकम् (without proper discipline)
vishnu_gita::215.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::215.essence: Empty pride and false rituals block real inner progress.
vishnu_gita::215.simple_meaning: People who see themselves as superior and proud because of wealth perform meaningless rituals with deceit and without real discipline.
vishnu_gita::215.simple_insight: False pride and empty actions create distance from true growth and freedom.
vishnu_gita::215.detailed_meaning: Vishnu points out those who stubbornly consider themselves superior, boasting wealth, yet perform rituals superficially and deceitfully, lacking real commitment or discipline, thus missing true spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::215.modern_relevance: You might see people around who boast or show off wealth but lack genuine effort or sincerity in what they do.
vishnu_gita::215.insight: It shifts attention from external show and pride to sincere, disciplined effort as the path forward.

vishnu_gita::216.verse_sanskrit:
अहंकारं बलं दर्प काम क्रोधश्च संश्रिताः।
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः॥
vishnu_gita::216.verse_hindi: अहङ्कार, बल, दर्प, काम और क्रोध का अवलम्बन करते हुए अपने देह में और औरों के देह में रहनेवाला जो मैं हूँ उससे द्वेष करते हुए सच्चे पथ के चलनेवाले साधु लोगों के गुणों की निन्दा किया करते हैं
vishnu_gita::216.english_translation: Those who rely on ego, strength, pride, desire, and anger hate the true self within themselves and others, criticizing the virtues of sincere seekers.
vishnu_gita::216.translation_literal: अहंकारं (ego) / बलं (strength) / दर्प (pride) / काम (desire) / क्रोधश्च (and anger) / संश्रिताः (relying on) / मामात्मपरदेहेषु (me, the true self, in own and others' bodies) / प्रद्विषन्तः (hate) / अभ्यसूयकाः (the envious)
vishnu_gita::216.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::216.essence: Pride, desire, and anger cause you to hate the true self in yourself and others.
vishnu_gita::216.simple_meaning: People who depend on ego, pride, desire, and anger end up hating the true self in themselves and others, criticizing those who follow a sincere path.
vishnu_gita::216.simple_insight: You feel stuck when pride and anger blind you to your own and others' true nature.
vishnu_gita::216.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that some people, caught in ego, pride, desire, and anger, despise the true self within themselves and others. This leads them to criticize sincere seekers walking the path of truth.
vishnu_gita::216.modern_relevance: When you let pride and frustration take over, you push away your own values and judge others harshly instead of understanding them.
vishnu_gita::216.insight: Recognize how ego and strong emotions distort your perception of yourself and others, opening space for kindness and acceptance.

vishnu_gita::217.verse_sanskrit:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान् संसारे प्राणिनोऽधमान् ।
क्षिपाभ्यजत्रमशुभानामुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
vishnu_gita::217.verse_hindi: मैं संसार में मेरी हिंसा करनेवाले इन सब क्रूर अधम अशुभ व्यक्तियों को आसुरी योनियों में ही निरन्तर गिराया करता हूँ
vishnu_gita::217.english_translation: I cast those cruel, lowest, and inauspicious beings who hate me into demonic births in the cycle of existence again and again.
vishnu_gita::217.translation_literal: तान् (them) अहं (I) द्विषतः (haters) क्रूरान् (cruel) संसारे (in the cycle of existence) प्राणिनः (beings) अधमान् (lowest) क्षिपा (cast) अभ्यजत्र (repeatedly) अशुभानाम् (inauspicious)ूरीषु (in wombs) एव (certainly) योनिषु (births).
vishnu_gita::217.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::217.essence: Cruelty and hatred lead to continued difficult rebirths within the cycle of existence.
vishnu_gita::217.simple_meaning: The divine says that those who act cruelly and oppose the divine cycle experience repeated births in lower, troubled forms.
vishnu_gita::217.simple_insight: There is a natural consequence for cruelty and hatred within the cycle of existence.
vishnu_gita::217.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how beings who oppose or act cruelly towards the divine nature face repeated difficult rebirths, emphasizing the law of consequences within samsara.
vishnu_gita::217.insight: It reminds you that harmful actions lead to difficult consequences, encouraging care in how you treat others.

vishnu_gita::218.verse_sanskrit:
आसुरी योनिमापन्ना मूढ़ा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
मामप्राप्यैव गीर्वाणास्ततो यान्त्यधमाँ गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::218.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! वह मूढ़गण जन्म जन्म में आसुरी योनि प्राप्त करके मुझे प्राप्त न होकर और भी अधमगति को प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::218.english_translation: Those deluded beings, born repeatedly into demonic origins, fail to reach me and instead fall into a lower realm.
vishnu_gita::218.translation_literal: आसुरी (demonic) / योनिम् (origin) / आपन्ना (having obtained) / मूढ़ा (deluded) / जन्मनि (in births) / जन्मनि (in births) / माम् (me) / अप्राप्य (not obtaining) / एव (only) / गीर्वाणाः (those who speak) / ततः (then) / यान्ति (go) / अधमाँ (lower) / गतिम् (state)
vishnu_gita::218.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::218.essence: Repeated confusion and ego-born states block the path to the divine and cause decline.
vishnu_gita::218.simple_meaning: Repeatedly being born into deluded and harmful states keeps beings away from the divine and leads them to worse conditions.
vishnu_gita::218.simple_insight: There is a risk of slipping further into confusion if you don't find the true path.
vishnu_gita::218.detailed_meaning: Vishnu warns that beings born into deluded, ego-driven existences fail to reach the divine and instead descend into lower states of being, highlighting the cost of ignorance and mistaken identity.
vishnu_gita::218.modern_relevance: When you keep repeating harmful patterns without clear purpose, you move farther from your true self and deeper into confusion.
vishnu_gita::218.insight: Recognize that staying trapped in ego and confusion prevents progress toward your inner freedom.

vishnu_gita::219.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
vishnu_gita::219.verse_hindi: काम, क्रोध और लोभ, नरक यह तीन प्रकार के द्वार हैं, यह तीनों आत्मज्ञान के नाशक हैं इस कारण इन तीनों को त्याग कर देना चाहिये
vishnu_gita::219.english_translation: Desire, anger, and greed are the three gates to the lower realm that destroy self-knowledge; therefore, these three must be abandoned.
vishnu_gita::219.translation_literal: त्रिविधं (threefold) / नरकस्य (of the lower realm) / एदम् (this) / द्वारं (gate) / नाशनम् (destroyer) / आत्मनः (of the self) / कामः (desire) / क्रोधः (anger) / तथा (also) / लोभः (greed) / तस्मात् (therefore) / एतत्रयं (these three) / त्यजेत् (should be abandoned)
vishnu_gita::219.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::219.essence: Desire, anger, and greed are gates destroying self-knowledge and must be abandoned.
vishnu_gita::219.simple_meaning: Desire, anger, and greed block your true self-knowledge and lead to suffering. Letting go of them is essential.
vishnu_gita::219.simple_insight: You feel relief in recognizing these feelings block your clarity and peace.
vishnu_gita::219.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that desire, anger, and greed act as dangerous gates leading to the lower realm of confusion. These emotions destroy self-knowledge, so abandoning them is the path to clarity and freedom.
vishnu_gita::219.modern_relevance: When frustration, craving, or jealousy arise during your day, they cloud your judgment and peace. Noticing and releasing them opens clarity.
vishnu_gita::219.insight: This verse shifts focus from chasing wants to noticing and letting go of disruptive emotions.

vishnu_gita::220.verse_sanskrit:
एतैविर्मुक्तो जीवस्तु तमोद्वारैत्रिभिः खलु ।
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::220.verse_hindi: नरक के द्वाररूपी इन तीनो से ही विमुक्त जीव अपना मङ्गल करनेवाला आचरण करता है और तदन्तर परमगतिरूपी मोक्ष को प्राप्त करता है।
vishnu_gita::220.english_translation: A being freed from the three gates of the lower realm acts for its own welfare and then attains the supreme state.
vishnu_gita::220.translation_literal: एतैविर्मुक्तो (thus freed) / जीवस्तु (the living being) / तमोद्वारैः (by the gates of darkness) / त्रिभिः (three) / खलु (indeed) / आचरति (acts) / आत्मनः (for the self) / श्रेयः (welfare) / ततः (then) / याति (goes) / परां (supreme) / गतिम् (state)
vishnu_gita::220.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::220.essence: Freedom comes by acting beyond three gates of darkness toward your true welfare.
vishnu_gita::220.simple_meaning: When a person frees themselves from three harmful entrances of darkness, they act for their own good and reach the highest state.
vishnu_gita::220.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing freedom means moving beyond hidden traps that block your growth.
vishnu_gita::220.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that beings trapped by three metaphorical gates of darkness, representing ignorance or lower impulses, cannot act for true welfare. Once freed from these, they act rightly and attain the highest state of liberation.
vishnu_gita::220.modern_relevance: When you recognize and step beyond three harmful habits or fears, your actions align with your well-being and growth.
vishnu_gita::220.insight: This verse teaches you to identify and release three key inner blocks so your actions become truly beneficial.

vishnu_gita::221.verse_sanskrit:
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्त्तते कामकारतः ।
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::221.verse_hindi: जो व्यक्ति शास्त्रविधि को त्याग करके स्वेच्छानुकूल कार्य में प्रवृत्त होता है वह सिद्धि शान्ति और मोक्ष को प्राप्त नहीं हो सकता
vishnu_gita::221.english_translation: One who abandons scriptural discipline and acts driven by desire does not attain accomplishment, happiness, or ultimate freedom.
vishnu_gita::221.translation_literal: यः (one who) शास्त्रविधिम् (scriptural discipline) उत्सृज्य (abandoning) वर्त्तते (acts) कामकारतः (driven by desire) । न (not) स (he) सिद्धिम् (accomplishment) अवाप्नोति (attains) न (not) सुखं (happiness) न (not) परां (ultimate) गतिम् (freedom) ॥
vishnu_gita::221.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::221.essence: Ignoring disciplined guidance for desire-driven actions blocks lasting success and freedom.
vishnu_gita::221.simple_meaning: Acting without following the right principles and chasing desires prevents real success, peace, and freedom.
vishnu_gita::221.simple_insight: Relief comes knowing that fulfillment requires more than just following what feels good right now.
vishnu_gita::221.detailed_meaning: Vishnu warns that abandoning the guidance of spiritual discipline (scriptural rules) to pursue personal desires leads away from true accomplishment, lasting happiness, and the highest freedom. This teaching comes as a caution against impulsive, self-centered action.
vishnu_gita::221.modern_relevance: You decide to skip your core values to chase quick pleasures, only to feel empty and restless afterward.
vishnu_gita::221.insight: It shifts your mindset from following impulses to honoring steady discipline as the path to true fulfillment.

vishnu_gita::222.verse_sanskrit:
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं वः कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ ।
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हथ ॥
vishnu_gita::222.verse_hindi: इस कारण इस विश्व में यह कार्य है और यह अकार्य है इसकी व्यवस्था करने में शास्त्र ही आपके लिये प्रमाण है । शास्त्र विधानोक्त कर्म को जानकर उसको कर सकते हो
vishnu_gita::222.english_translation: Therefore, scripture is your guide to distinguish what actions should be done and which should not; knowing the scriptural injunctions, you should act accordingly.
vishnu_gita::222.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / शास्त्रं (scripture) / प्रमाणं (authority/guide) / वः (for you) / कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ (in what is to be done and not done) / ज्ञात्वा (knowing) / शास्त्रविधानोक्तं (as prescribed by scripture) / कर्म (action) / कर्तुम् (to do) / इह (here) / आर्हथ (you should).
vishnu_gita::222.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::222.essence: Clear guidance from scripture reveals what actions are right and which are not.
vishnu_gita::222.simple_meaning: Scripture is the reliable guide that helps you know which actions to do and which to avoid. By understanding scriptural instructions, you can act rightly.
vishnu_gita::222.simple_insight: You feel confident when your actions are rooted in clear guidance, not confusion.
vishnu_gita::222.detailed_meaning: At a crucial moment, Vishnu instructs that the source to discern right from wrong action is scripture. This teaching establishes scripture as the authority to guide duty in complex situations.
vishnu_gita::222.modern_relevance: When unsure about a tough choice, you turn to trusted guidelines or principles to decide what you must do and what to avoid.
vishnu_gita::222.insight: It teaches you to rely on trusted principles to clarify your responsibilities and avoid confusion.

vishnu_gita::223.verse_sanskrit:
दैवीभावस्य रक्षायै आसुरीभावतो भयात् ।
मयैव वर्णधर्मस्य कृता सृष्टिर्दिवौकसः ॥
vishnu_gita::223.verse_hindi: हे देव गण! आसुरी भाव के भय से दैवी भाव की रक्षा करने के लिये मैंने ही वणधर्म की सृष्टि की है
vishnu_gita::223.english_translation: O divine beings, to protect the divine nature from the fear of the demonic nature, I alone created the system of classes and duties.
vishnu_gita::223.translation_literal: दैवीभावस्य (of the divine nature) / रक्षायै (for protection) / आसुरीभावतो (from the demonic nature) / भयात् (because of fear) / मयैव (by me alone) / वर्णधर्मस्य (of the system of classes and duties) / कृता (created) / सृष्टिः (creation) / दिवौकसः (of the gods and demons)
vishnu_gita::223.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::223.essence: Social roles exist to protect the good from destructive forces.
vishnu_gita::223.simple_meaning: A system of social roles and duties was created to protect goodness from harmful forces.
vishnu_gita::223.simple_insight: You have a purpose that supports preserving what is right and good.
vishnu_gita::223.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to divine beings that he created social orders and duties to protect the world’s goodness from destructive forces, showing the importance of role and responsibility.
vishnu_gita::223.modern_relevance: When chaos threatens your values, your role and responsibilities act as a shield to uphold what matters.
vishnu_gita::223.insight: Recognize your responsibilities as part of a protective design that sustains what you value.

vishnu_gita::224.verse_hindi: वर्णधर्म प्रवृत्तिरोधक सत्त्वगुण वर्द्धक स्वधर्मरक्षक और दैवीसम्पत्तिप्रवर्तक है
vishnu_gita::224.english_translation: The protector of the duties of caste is the enhancer of goodness, the guardian of one's own duty, and the promoter of divine qualities.
vishnu_gita::224.translation_literal: प्रतिरोधको (protector) वर्णधर्माः (of caste duties) सत्वविवर्द्धकः (enhancer of goodness) स्वधर्मरक्षकः (guardian of own duty) तदेवीसम्पत्प्रवर्तकः (promoter of divine qualities)
vishnu_gita::224.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::224.essence: Protecting your true duties cultivates goodness and fosters divine qualities in you.
vishnu_gita::224.simple_meaning: You protect your true role by performing your duties, which increases goodness and brings divine qualities into your life.
vishnu_gita::224.simple_insight: You feel confident and aligned when you commit to your true responsibilities.
vishnu_gita::224.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu highlights the importance of protecting and fulfilling one's assigned duties (varna-dharma). Doing so nurtures the quality of goodness (sattva) and promotes divine virtues, guiding a person toward spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::224.modern_relevance: When you stay committed to your responsibilities, you naturally cultivate kindness and integrity, which influence your surroundings positively.
vishnu_gita::224.insight: It teaches you to see your duties as a source of inner growth rather than just obligations.

vishnu_gita::225.verse_sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणाञ्च सुधाभुजः !।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वाभावप्रभवैगुणै ॥
vishnu_gita::225.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! ब्राह्मण क्षत्रिय वैश्य और शूद्रगण के कर्मसमूह पूर्व जन्म के संस्कार से उत्पन्न गुण  विशेषरूप से विभक्त हैं
vishnu_gita::225.english_translation: O divine beings! The duties of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras are divided according to the qualities born from their past life's nature.
vishnu_gita::225.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां (of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas) / शूद्राणां (and Shudras) / सुधाभुजः (O divine beings) / कर्माणि (duties) / प्रविभक्तानि (are divided) / स्वाभावप्रभवैगुणै (according to qualities arising from nature)
vishnu_gita::225.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::225.essence: Your true duties flow from qualities shaped by your past nature.
vishnu_gita::225.simple_meaning: Different groups have different duties based on qualities they developed from past lives.
vishnu_gita::225.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your responsibilities suit your true nature.
vishnu_gita::225.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that social roles and duties arise from inherent qualities shaped by past impressions, grounding each person's responsibility in their natural makeup.
vishnu_gita::225.modern_relevance: You notice how your strengths and habits guide what you do best, naturally shaping your role at work or home.
vishnu_gita::225.insight: Recognize that your natural talents and tendencies guide you toward your most fitting actions.

vishnu_gita::226.verse_sanskrit:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
vishnu_gita::226.verse_hindi: शम, दम, तपस्या,शौच,क्षमा,सरलता, ज्ञान विज्ञान और आस्तिकता, यह सब ब्राह्मण गण के स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं
vishnu_gita::226.english_translation: Calmness, self-control, disciplined effort, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, wisdom, discriminating knowledge, and belief in the supreme reality are natural duties of the Brahmin community.
vishnu_gita::226.translation_literal: शमो (calmness) / दमः (self-control) / तपः (disciplined effort) / शौचं (purity) / क्षान्तिः (forgiveness) / आर्जवम् (straightforwardness) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / ज्ञानं (wisdom) / विज्ञानम् (discriminating knowledge) / आस्तिक्यम् (belief in the supreme reality) / ब्रह्मकर्म (duties of the Brahmin) / स्वभावजम् (natural born)
vishnu_gita::226.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::226.essence: Calmness and honest wisdom are natural duties born from your true nature.
vishnu_gita::226.simple_meaning: Certain qualities like calmness, self-discipline, purity, forgiveness, honesty, and wisdom are natural duties for those on a spiritual path.
vishnu_gita::226.simple_insight: Your character shines when you live with calmness and honest wisdom.
vishnu_gita::226.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the essential qualities that naturally arise in those who live by spiritual principles, emphasizing calmness, self-discipline, purity, forgiveness, honesty, wisdom, and faith as their natural actions.
vishnu_gita::226.modern_relevance: When you face daily stress, returning to calmness and honest clarity grounds your choices and actions.
vishnu_gita::226.insight: It teaches you to recognize and cultivate natural, virtuous qualities as your true daily duties.

vishnu_gita::227.verse_sanskrit:
शौर्य तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
vishnu_gita::227.verse_hindi: शौर्य, तेज, धृति, दक्षता, युद्ध से नहीं भागना, दान और प्रभुता की शक्ति, यह सब क्षत्रिय जाति के स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं
vishnu_gita::227.english_translation: Courage, brilliance, steadiness, skill, not fleeing in battle, generosity, and leadership are all natural duties of the warrior class.
vishnu_gita::227.translation_literal: शौर्य (courage) / तेजो (brilliance) / धृति (steadiness) / दक्ष्यं (skill) / युद्धे (in battle) / च (and) / अपलायनम् (not fleeing) / दान (generosity) / ईश्वरभावश्च (and leadership) / क्षात्रं (warrior) / कर्म (duty) / स्वभावजम् (natural-born)
vishnu_gita::227.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::227.essence: Bravery, skill, generosity, and steadfastness are natural duties that define your role.
vishnu_gita::227.simple_meaning: Being brave, skilled, steady, generous, and facing challenges without fleeing are natural duties for a warrior.
vishnu_gita::227.simple_insight: There is confidence in knowing your strengths and responsibilities are part of who you are.
vishnu_gita::227.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the qualities inherent to the warrior class—courage, brilliance, steadiness, skill, bravery in battle, generosity, and leadership—as natural duties shaped by their nature and role in society.
vishnu_gita::227.modern_relevance: When you face tough decisions or pressure, remember your natural strengths and responsibilities guide you to stand firm and act with generosity.
vishnu_gita::227.insight: This verse helps you recognize and own your natural strengths and responsibilities, guiding your actions with confidence.

vishnu_gita::228.verse_sanskrit:
कृषिगोरक्षवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥
vishnu_gita::228.verse_hindi: कृषि, पशुपालन और वाणिज्य, यह वैश्य जाति के स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं और परिचर्यात्मक कर्म शूद्रजाति का भी स्वाभाविक कर्म है
vishnu_gita::228.english_translation: Farming, herding, and trade are the natural duties of the Vaishya class, and service work is the natural duty of the Shudra class.
vishnu_gita::228.translation_literal: कृषिगोरक्षवाणिज्यं (farming-herding-trade) / वैश्यकर्म (Vaishya duty) / स्वभावजम् (natural-born) / परिचर्यात्मकं (service-oriented) / कर्म (action) / शूद्रस्यापि (of Shudra also) / स्वभावजम् (natural-born)
vishnu_gita::228.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::228.essence: Different social groups are described with distinct traditional duties.
vishnu_gita::228.simple_meaning: Different social groups have traditional roles: Vaishyas in farming and trade, Shudras in service work.
vishnu_gita::228.simple_insight: Understanding assigned social duties can clarify personal roles but may limit universal application.
vishnu_gita::228.detailed_meaning: The verse describes traditional social roles assigning farming, herding, and trade to Vaishyas, and service to Shudras. It reflects a social order concept rather than a universal teaching for all individuals.
vishnu_gita::228.insight: Recognize the verse reflects social roles, not personal dharma for everyone; be cautious applying it universally.

vishnu_gita::229.verse_sanskrit:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभतेऽखिलाः।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं श्रूयतां विन्दते यथा ॥
vishnu_gita::229.verse_hindi: अपने अपने कर्म में निष्ठावान् सभी व्यक्ति सिद्धि को प्राप्त करते हैं। स्वकर्म में निरत व्यक्ति जिस प्रकार से  सिद्धि को प्राप्त करते हैं, वह सुनो
vishnu_gita::229.english_translation: Everyone attains perfection by being dedicated to their own action. Listen to how one devoted to their own duty attains perfection.
vishnu_gita::229.translation_literal: स्वे (own) स्वे (own) कर्मणि (in action) अभिरतः (devoted) संसिद्धिं (perfection) लभतेऽखिलाः (all attain)। स्वकर्मनि (own duty) निरतः (engaged) सिद्धिं (perfection) श्रूयतां (listen) विन्दते (attains) यथा (how) ॥
vishnu_gita::229.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::229.essence: True success comes from dedicated focus on your own chosen actions.
vishnu_gita::229.simple_meaning: By focusing sincerely on your own work, you can achieve true success and fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::229.simple_insight: You feel empowered knowing dedication to your own duty leads to achievement.
vishnu_gita::229.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that each person attains success and spiritual perfection by sincerely dedicating themselves to their own responsibilities, instead of imitating others. This moment introduces the principle that true accomplishment arises from personal commitment.
vishnu_gita::229.modern_relevance: You see colleagues rushing to copy others’ tasks, but your own steady focus is what truly builds progress.
vishnu_gita::229.insight: It teaches you to commit fully to your unique responsibilities instead of comparing yourself to others.

vishnu_gita::230.verse_sanskrit:
यतः प्रतिभूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति साधकः
॥
vishnu_gita::230.verse_hindi: जिनसे जीवों की प्रवृत्ति अर्थात् चेष्टा का उदय होता है और जो इस सम्पूर्ण विश्व में व्याप्त हैं, स्वकर्म के द्वारा साधक उनकी अर्चना करके सिद्धि प्राप्त करता है।
vishnu_gita::230.english_translation: From whom all beings' tendencies arise and who pervades the entire universe, the practitioner attains perfection by worshipping through their own actions.
vishnu_gita::230.translation_literal: यतः (from whom) / प्रतिभूतानां (of beings' manifestations) / येन (by whom) / सर्वमिदं (all this) / ततम् (pervaded) / स्वकर्मणा (by own action) / तम् (him) / अभ्यर्च्य (worshipping) / सिद्धिं (perfection) / विन्दति (attains) / साधकः (the practitioner)
vishnu_gita::230.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::230.essence: You gain true success by honoring the universal source through your own actions.
vishnu_gita::230.simple_meaning: You achieve true accomplishment by honoring the origin of all beings through your own committed actions.
vishnu_gita::230.simple_insight: Trust that your sincere actions connect you with the source within everything.
vishnu_gita::230.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how all life and tendencies arise from a central divine source. The practitioner, by engaging sincerely in their own duties and actions, honors that source and attains spiritual success.
vishnu_gita::230.modern_relevance: When you focus fully on your work, recognizing it as part of a greater whole, you find deeper fulfillment beyond results.
vishnu_gita::230.insight: Shift from seeking external rewards to honoring your effort as a form of reverence toward the greater whole.

vishnu_gita::231.verse_sanskrit:
श्रेयान स्वधम्मो विगुणः परश्चान्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
vishnu_gita::231.verse_hindi: अपना धर्म यदि सदोष भी हो तो वह पूर्णरूप से अनुष्ठित परधर्म की अपेक्षा श्रेष्ठ है क्योंकि स्वभाव से निश्चित कर्म को करता हुआ जीव पाप को प्राप्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::231.english_translation: Better is your own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed; performing the duty ordained by your nature, you incur no blame.
vishnu_gita::231.translation_literal: श्रेयान (better) स्वधम्मः (own duty) विगुणः (faulty) परः च (than another) अनुष्ठितात् (performed) । स्वभावनियतं (by nature fixed) कर्म (action) कुर्वन् (doing) आप्नोति (attains) किल्बिषम् (no blame) ॥
vishnu_gita::231.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::231.essence: Doing your own natural duty, even imperfectly, is better than perfect duty not your own.
vishnu_gita::231.simple_meaning: You should follow your own natural duty, even if imperfect, rather than perfectly doing someone else's duty. Acting according to your nature avoids blame.
vishnu_gita::231.simple_insight: There is peace in trusting your own path, even if it feels flawed.
vishnu_gita::231.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu advises that each being has a duty aligned with their nature. Even if this duty is imperfect, it is better to perform it than to flawlessly perform a duty meant for someone else. This ensures freedom from moral fault.
vishnu_gita::231.modern_relevance: You face choices where you might copy others perfectly or follow your own imperfect instincts. Trusting your nature helps you avoid regret and blame.
vishnu_gita::231.insight: It shifts your focus from imitating others to embracing your unique role and natural actions.

vishnu_gita::232.verse_sanskrit:
सहज कर्म विबुधाः ! सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवाटताः ॥
vishnu_gita::232.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! सदोष होने पर भी सहज अर्थात् खभाव से उत्पन्न कर्म का त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये क्योंकि जिस प्रकार अग्नि को धूम ढककर रहता है उसी प्रकार सभी कर्म दोष से आवृत हैं।
vishnu_gita::232.english_translation: O enlightened beings! Even if actions have faults, do not abandon natural spontaneous actions, for just as fire is covered by smoke, all actions are covered by faults.
vishnu_gita::232.translation_literal: सहज (natural/spontaneous) / कर्म (actions) / विबुधाः (wise beings) / सदोषम् (faulty) / अपि (even) / न (not) / त्यजेत् (should abandon) / सर्वारम्भा (all beginnings/actions) / हि (indeed) / दोषेण (by fault) / धूमेन (by smoke) / अग्निः (fire) / इव (like) / आस्तताः (are covered)
vishnu_gita::232.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::232.essence: Natural action is valuable even when flawed; faults don’t justify stopping acting.
vishnu_gita::232.simple_meaning: You should not give up your natural, spontaneous actions just because they contain some faults. Like fire is hidden by smoke, all actions have some flaws.
vishnu_gita::232.simple_insight: It’s comforting to know that natural efforts are valuable even when imperfect.
vishnu_gita::232.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the wise, encouraging them to continue their natural, spontaneous actions despite imperfections. Like fire being obscured by smoke, all actions carry faults, but that does not make the actions worthless or to be abandoned.
vishnu_gita::232.modern_relevance: You tried to do something from your heart, but mistakes happened. Still, stopping because of flaws means losing what’s real and natural about your effort.
vishnu_gita::232.insight: It teaches you to accept imperfection in your natural efforts without abandoning them completely.

vishnu_gita::233.verse_sanskrit:
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धि परमां सन्न्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::233.verse_hindi: सभी विषयों में अनासक्तबुद्धि, जितात्मा और इच्छारहित व्यक्ति सन्न्यास अर्थात् आसक्ति और कर्मफल के त्याग द्वारा परमोन्नत नैष्ककर्मय सिद्धि को प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::233.english_translation: A person with a mind free from attachment, self-conquered and desireless attains the highest perfection of actionlessness through renunciation.
vishnu_gita::233.translation_literal: असक्तबुद्धिः (mind free from attachment) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / जितात्मा (self-conquered) / विगतस्पृहः (desireless) / नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धि (perfection of actionlessness) / परमां (highest) / सन्न्यासेन (through renunciation) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
vishnu_gita::233.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::233.essence: True freedom arises when the mind is free from attachment and desire through renunciation.
vishnu_gita::233.simple_meaning: You can achieve the highest freedom by letting go of attachments, controlling yourself, and giving up desire through renunciation.
vishnu_gita::233.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing freedom comes from releasing what binds your mind.
vishnu_gita::233.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the highest state of actionlessness is reached when a person’s mind is free from attachment, their self is conquered, and desires are absent, achieved through renunciation of craving and the fruits of actions.
vishnu_gita::233.modern_relevance: You feel stuck when wanting things pulls your mind every which way. Letting go of craving opens a path to calm and clarity.
vishnu_gita::233.insight: It teaches you to focus on releasing attachments and desires, which clears the way for inner freedom.

vishnu_gita::234.verse_sanskrit:
विशिष्टचेतना जीवाः सुराः : त्रिगुणभेदतः ।
चतुर्वेवाऽधिकारेषु विभक्ताः सन्ति सर्वदा ॥
vishnu_gita::234.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! त्रिगुण के भेद से विशिष्ट चेतन जीव सर्वदा चार ही अधिकारों में विभक्त हैं
vishnu_gita::234.english_translation: O gods, the distinct conscious beings are always divided into four categories according to the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::234.translation_literal: विशिष्टचेतना (distinct conscious) / जीवाः (beings) / सुराः (gods) / त्रिगुणभेदतः (according to three qualities) / चतुर्वेवाऽधिकारेषु (in four only categories) / विभक्ताः (divided) / सन्ति (are) / सर्वदा (always)
vishnu_gita::234.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::234.essence: Conscious beings are naturally sorted into four groups by three qualities of nature.
vishnu_gita::234.simple_meaning: Distinct conscious beings are always classified into four groups based on the three qualities that define nature.
vishnu_gita::234.simple_insight: Understanding beings as divided by qualities helps see the world’s natural differences clearly.
vishnu_gita::234.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the gods, explaining that living beings with distinct consciousness are continuously grouped into four categories based on the three qualities of nature, setting the stage for deeper philosophical classifications.
vishnu_gita::234.insight: It invites you to recognize that differences among beings arise from natural qualities, not arbitrary separation.

vishnu_gita::235.verse_sanskrit:
राक्षसा असुरा: देवा: कृतविद्याश्च ते मता: ।
केवलं तम आश्रिय विपरीतं प्रकुर्वते ॥
vishnu_gita::235.verse_hindi: उन्हीं को राक्षस असुर देवता और कृतविद्य कहते है। केवल तमोगुण के आश्रित होकर जो विपरीत
vishnu_gita::235.english_translation: Demons, shadow beings, radiant beings, and practitioners of sorcery are all called so because they rely solely on the quality of darkness and act in opposition.
vishnu_gita::235.translation_literal: राक्षसा (demons) / असुरा: (shadow beings) / देवा: (radiant beings) / कृतविद्याश्च (practitioners of sorcery) / ते (they) / मता: (are called) / केवलं (only) / तम (darkness) / आश्रिय (relying) / विपरीतं (opposite) / प्रकुर्वते (act)
vishnu_gita::235.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::235.essence: Beings depending solely on darkness act contrary to harmony and order.
vishnu_gita::235.simple_meaning: Those called demons, shadow beings, radiant beings, and sorcerers act from darkness and follow opposing ways.
vishnu_gita::235.simple_insight: Not all beings act from light or clarity; some follow darkness and opposition.
vishnu_gita::235.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes beings labeled as demons, shadow beings, radiant beings, and sorcerers. These beings act by relying solely on the quality of darkness (tamas) and choose paths contrary to harmony and order.
vishnu_gita::235.insight: It teaches to recognize forces or tendencies that arise from confusion and opposition rather than clarity and harmony.

vishnu_gita::236.verse_sanskrit:
कर्म तानाक्षसानाहुर्गुणभेदविदो बुधाः ।
रजोद्वारेण ये जीवा इन्द्रियासक्तचेतमः ॥
vishnu_gita::236.verse_hindi: कर्म करते हैं उनको गुणभेद के जाननेवाले विद्वान लोग राक्षस कहते हैं। जो जीव इन्द्रियासक्त चित्त होकर रजोगुण के द्वारा
vishnu_gita::236.english_translation: The wise, who understand the distinctions of qualities, call those who act with minds attached to the senses and influenced by the quality of passion as demons.
vishnu_gita::236.translation_literal: कर्म (actions) तानाक्षसानाहुः (those who perform) गुणभेदविदो (knowers of the distinction of qualities) बुधाः (the wise) । रजोद्वारेण (through the gate of passion) ये (those who) जीवा (living beings) इन्द्रियासक्तचेतमः (with minds attached to the senses) ॥
vishnu_gita::236.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::236.essence: Passionate mind attached to senses drives restless, binding actions.
vishnu_gita::236.simple_meaning: Those who understand qualities see that living beings acting with sense-driven passionate minds are caught in rajas, a binding quality.
vishnu_gita::236.simple_insight: Recognizing how passion ties your mind to senses helps you understand your restless actions.
vishnu_gita::236.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to Arjuna that wise people recognize how qualities influence action. Beings whose minds are attached to senses and dominated by passion (rajas) are seen as bound and reactive, limiting their freedom.
vishnu_gita::236.modern_relevance: You notice how your desires and restless mind drive impulsive decisions, trapping you in cycles of dissatisfaction.
vishnu_gita::236.insight: It teaches you to observe when your mind clings to sensory desires and understand that such attachment causes restless, unbalanced action.

vishnu_gita::237.verse_sanskrit:
तम प्रधानं विषयवहुलं कर्म कुर्वते ।
असुरास्ते समाख्याता देवाञ्च्छृणुत देवताः ॥
vishnu_gita::237.verse_hindi: तमोन्मुख विषय बहुल कर्म करते हैं वह असुर हैं। देवाधिकार के जीवों का लक्षण सुनो,
vishnu_gita::237.english_translation: Those who are dominated by darkness perform actions full of attachments; such beings are called shadowed ones. Listen to the traits of beings aligned with the divine.
vishnu_gita::237.translation_literal: तमोन्मुख (darkness-faced) विषय (objects) बहुल (full of) कर्म (actions) कुर्वते (do) । असुरास्ते (shadowed beings are) समाख्याता (called) देवाञ्च्छृणुत (listen to gods and) देवताः (divine beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::237.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::237.essence: Actions driven by craving bind you to darkness and restless confusion.
vishnu_gita::237.simple_meaning: People who act driven by craving and attachments are trapped in darkness. This behavior is called shadowed or ego-driven action.
vishnu_gita::237.simple_insight: You can feel how craving shadows your actions, making them restless and confusing.
vishnu_gita::237.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that beings dominated by darkness (tamas) act with many attachments and desires. These shadowed beings contrast with those aligned with the divine, whose nature will be described next. It sets the stage for choosing between ego-driven and higher action.
vishnu_gita::237.modern_relevance: You notice when your choices come from frustration or craving, making even simple tasks feel heavy and chaotic.
vishnu_gita::237.insight: Recognize craving as the root that darkens your actions; this awareness lets you shift toward clarity.

vishnu_gita::238.verse_sanskrit:
रजःसाहाय्यमाश्रित्य कर्म सत्त्वप्रधानकम् ।
विषयाच्छन्नमतयः कुर्वते ते विचक्षणाः ॥
vishnu_gita::238.verse_hindi: जो विषय वासना रखते हुए रजोगुण की सहायता से सत्वगुण उन्मुख कर्म में प्रवृत्त होते हैं वे विलक्षण व्यक्ति देवता कहलाते हैं
vishnu_gita::238.english_translation: Those who, supported by passion and driven by goodness, perform actions veiled by desires are called wise beings.
vishnu_gita::238.translation_literal: रजःसाहाय्यम् (with passion's help) / आश्रित्य (relying on) / कर्म (actions) / सत्त्वप्रधानकम् (primarily of goodness) / विषयाच्छन्नमतयः (minds covered by desires) / कुर्वते (do) / ते (they) / विचक्षणाः (wise ones)
vishnu_gita::238.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::238.essence: Wise action can arise from passion and goodness, even when desire clouds the mind.
vishnu_gita::238.simple_meaning: People who act with energy and goodness but still have desires are considered wise beings.
vishnu_gita::238.simple_insight: You are wise when your actions stem from goodness, even if desires are present.
vishnu_gita::238.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that some beings act motivated by passion (rajas) and guided mainly by goodness (sattva), even though their minds are clouded by desires. These beings are considered distinctively wise for their balanced nature.
vishnu_gita::238.modern_relevance: You rush to finish a project driven by ambition but keep your values clear—this blend makes your effort wise.
vishnu_gita::238.insight: Recognize that acting with passion and goodness, despite desires, still reflects wisdom.

vishnu_gita::239.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धसत्वे स्थिता ये स्युः कृतविद्या मतास्तु ते ।
अहं तु कृतविधेषु ह्यादर्शोऽस्मि सुरर्षभाः ॥
vishnu_gita::239.verse_hindi: जो शुद्ध सत्त्वगुण में स्थित हैं चे कृतविद्य कहाते हैं। हे देवतागण ! मैं ही कृतविद्योका आदर्श हूँ
vishnu_gita::239.english_translation: Those established in pure goodness are called wise in their actions. O radiant beings, I am the ideal among those wise in action.
vishnu_gita::239.translation_literal: शुद्धसत्वे (in pure goodness) / स्थिता (established) / ये (those who) / स्युः (are) / कृतविद्या (wise in action) / मतास्तु (are called) / ते (they) । / अहं (I) / तु (indeed) / कृतविधेषु (among those wise in action) / हि (certainly) / आदर्शः (ideal) / अस्मि (am) / सुरर्षभाः (O best of the radiant beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::239.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::239.essence: True wisdom is shown by acting from pure goodness; the ideal is embodied in living example.
vishnu_gita::239.simple_meaning: People rooted in pure goodness are called wise because their actions reflect that. I am the perfect example of such wisdom in action.
vishnu_gita::239.simple_insight: You can feel confident knowing that pure goodness in your actions shows true wisdom.
vishnu_gita::239.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that those who act from a pure, good nature are considered wise in how they act. Vishnu presents himself as the perfect model of such wise action, highlighting the ideal to follow.
vishnu_gita::239.modern_relevance: When you choose kindness and integrity in your daily choices, you become wise through your actions, just like a role model you admire.
vishnu_gita::239.insight: It shifts your focus to embodying goodness in every action, making wisdom visible through how you live.

vishnu_gita::240.verse_sanskrit:
यतो विद्या ममाधीना वर्तते सन्ततं ध्रुवम् ।
दृष्टिश्चेद् युष्मदीया मां प्रत्येव सततं भवेत् ॥
vishnu_gita::240.verse_hindi: क्योंकि विद्या सदा मेरे अधीन ही रहती है। हे देवतागण ! यदि आप लोगों की दृष्टि सदा मेरी ही ओर रहे
vishnu_gita::240.english_translation: Because knowledge always remains under my control. O radiant beings! If your gaze always remains fixed on me,
vishnu_gita::240.translation_literal: यतो (because) विद्या (knowledge) ममाधीना (under my control) वर्तते (remains) सन्ततं (always) ध्रुवम् (steady) । दृष्टिश्चेद् (if the gaze) युष्मदीया (your) मां (on me) प्रत्येव (always) सततं (continually) भवेत् (becomes) ॥
vishnu_gita::240.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::240.essence: Steady focus on the divine keeps knowledge constant and unshaken.
vishnu_gita::240.simple_meaning: Steady knowledge stays with the one who keeps their attention continually on the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::240.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that focused attention brings lasting wisdom.
vishnu_gita::240.detailed_meaning: Vishnu declares that true knowledge remains constant under his guidance. He invites radiant beings to keep their focus on him, promising that such devotion secures unwavering wisdom.
vishnu_gita::240.modern_relevance: When you keep your attention on what truly matters, your understanding deepens and becomes steady despite distractions.
vishnu_gita::240.insight: It teaches you to maintain steady focus on your inner guide to keep wisdom stable within.

vishnu_gita::241.verse_sanskrit:
तदा वश्च्यवनं नैव भयं वा न भविष्यति ।
उन्नतिः क्रमशो नूनं युष्माकं च भविष्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::241.verse_hindi: तो आप लोगों का  न पतन होगा और न आपको भय होगा और आप लोगों की क्रमशः उन्नति अवश्य होगी
vishnu_gita::241.english_translation: Then you will have neither downfall nor fear, and your progress will surely grow step by step.
vishnu_gita::241.translation_literal: तदा (then) वश्च्यवनं (fall/downfall) नैव (not at all) भयं (fear) वा (or) न (not) भविष्यति (will happen) । उन्नतिः (progress) क्रमशः (gradually/step by step) नूनं (certainly) युष्माकं (your) च (and) भविष्यति (will happen) ॥
vishnu_gita::241.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::241.essence: Steady effort eliminates fear and guarantees gradual progress.
vishnu_gita::241.simple_meaning: You will not experience failure or fear, and your progress will grow gradually and surely.
vishnu_gita::241.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing steady progress comes without fear or loss.
vishnu_gita::241.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reassures that those who follow the right path will neither fall nor be afraid, promising gradual and certain advancement through disciplined action.
vishnu_gita::241.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or anxious about setbacks, this reminds you that consistent effort removes fear and leads to growth.
vishnu_gita::241.insight: It teaches you to trust steady effort over anxiety about failure, focusing on slow, sure progress.

vishnu_gita::242.verse_sanskrit:
देवादिदेव ! धर्माभिप्रवर्तक : महाप्रभो ।
लोकोत्तरगति तद्वद्रहस्यं परमाद्भुतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::242.verse_hindi: हे देवादिदेव ! हे धर्म के प्रवर्तक ! हे महाप्रभो ! हे विभो! धर्म की लोकोत्तर गति और परम अद्भुत रहस्य
vishnu_gita::242.english_translation: O God of gods! O great lord, the promulgator of dharma! The transcendental goal of dharma and its supreme, wondrous mystery are like that.
vishnu_gita::242.translation_literal: देवादिदेव (god of gods) / धर्माभिप्रवर्तकः (promulgator of dharma) / महाप्रभो (great lord) / लोकोत्तरगति (transcendental goal) / तद्वत् (like that) / रहस्यं (mystery) / परमाद्भुतम् (supreme wondrous)
vishnu_gita::242.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::242.essence: The highest source of dharma leads to a supreme, transcendent mystery beyond the world.
vishnu_gita::242.simple_meaning: This verse praises a supreme being as the source and upholder of dharma, whose ultimate goal and mystery surpass the world.
vishnu_gita::242.simple_insight: There is awe and reverence for a power beyond ordinary understanding guiding true purpose.
vishnu_gita::242.detailed_meaning: The verse extols the divine as the highest lord and the initiator of righteous conduct (dharma), highlighting that the ultimate aim of dharma transcends worldly understanding and remains a supreme mystery.
vishnu_gita::242.insight: It invites respect for the profound, unseen principles that govern purposeful living beyond immediate logic.

vishnu_gita::243.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञात्वा धर्मस्य जाताः स्मः कृतकृत्या वयं विभो ! ।
जगद्गुरो ! चतुर्भेदा भेदतस्त्रिगुणस्य ये ॥
vishnu_gita::243.verse_hindi: समझकर हमलोग कृत्यकृत्य हुए। हे जगद्गुरो ! त्रिगुण के भेद से आपने जो चार भेद
vishnu_gita::243.english_translation: Knowing our dharma, we have become accomplished. O world teacher! From the three qualities, you have made four distinctions.
vishnu_gita::243.translation_literal: ज्ञात्वा (knowing) धर्मस्य (of dharma) जाताः (born/made) स्मः (we are) कृतकृत्या (accomplished) वयं (we) विभो (O lord) ! जगद्गुरो (world teacher) ! चतुर्भेदा (four distinctions) भेदतः (from the division) त्रिगुणस्य (of the three qualities) ये (who)
vishnu_gita::243.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::243.essence: True understanding of dharma reveals clear distinctions beyond superficial qualities.
vishnu_gita::243.simple_meaning: Understanding your true purpose helps you become accomplished. The teacher explains how the three qualities lead to four important distinctions.
vishnu_gita::243.simple_insight: You feel grounded when your purpose becomes clear beyond confusing traits.
vishnu_gita::243.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses how understanding one's dharma leads to mastery. He explains that the three fundamental qualities (gunas) create four distinct categories, revealing deeper clarity beyond surface traits.
vishnu_gita::243.modern_relevance: You finally see your role clearly after sorting through confusing personality traits and expectations.
vishnu_gita::243.insight: It teaches you to look beyond surface traits to find your true purpose and mastery.

vishnu_gita::244.verse_sanskrit:
विशिष्टचेतनापन्नजीवानां कथितास्त्वया।
त्रिगुणानां हि तेषां वै स्वरूपं गुणभेदतः ॥
vishnu_gita::244.verse_hindi: विशिष्ट चेतन जीवों के  वर्णन किये हैं, हे प्रभो ! उन्हीं त्रिगुणों का स्वरूप और त्रिगुणों के विचार से
vishnu_gita::244.english_translation: You have described the distinct conscious beings and the nature of the three qualities based on their differences.
vishnu_gita::244.translation_literal: विशिष्टचेतनापन्नजीवानां (distinct conscious beings) कथितास्त्वया (have been described by you) । त्रिगुणानां (of the three qualities) हि (indeed) तेषां (their) वै (own) स्वरूपं (nature) गुणभेदतः (due to differences in qualities) ॥
vishnu_gita::244.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::244.essence: Distinct conscious beings differ fundamentally by their three qualities.
vishnu_gita::244.simple_meaning: You have explained different conscious beings and how the three qualities vary among them.
vishnu_gita::244.simple_insight: Understanding beings by their qualities helps to see their true nature beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::244.detailed_meaning: The narrator acknowledges that the divine has explained the distinct conscious beings and the nature of the three qualities (gunas), emphasizing differences in these qualities as their true nature.
vishnu_gita::244.insight: It invites recognizing the diversity of consciousness through the lens of qualities shaping identity.

vishnu_gita::245.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मङ्गिानाञ्च सर्वेषामाचाराणां तथा प्रभो !।
वर्णयन्नः प्रधानानां भेदानुपदिशाखिलान् ॥
vishnu_gita::245.verse_hindi: धर्म के सभी अङ्गों और प्रधान आचारों के सम्पूर्ण भेदों का वर्णन करते हुए ऐसा उपदेश दें
vishnu_gita::245.english_translation: O Lord, please teach us by describing all parts of dharma and all the distinctions among its main codes of conduct.
vishnu_gita::245.translation_literal: धर्मङ्गिानाञ्च (all parts of dharma) / सर्वेषामाचाराणां (of all codes of conduct) / तथा (also) / प्रभो (O Lord) /। / वर्णयन्नः (describe us) / प्रधानानां (principal/main) / भेदानुपदिशाखिलान् (all distinctions instruct) / ॥
vishnu_gita::245.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::245.essence: Complete understanding of all parts and distinctions of dharma is essential before teaching.
vishnu_gita::245.simple_meaning: The speaker asks the Lord to explain all aspects and distinctions of dharma and its main rules clearly.
vishnu_gita::245.simple_insight: There is value in understanding all parts and differences within dharma fully before acting.
vishnu_gita::245.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the narrator requests a complete explanation of dharma, its parts, and principal codes of conduct to clarify the complex system for the listeners.
vishnu_gita::245.insight: It encourages seeking thorough understanding of ethical guidance before applying it in life.

vishnu_gita::246.verse_sanskrit:
येन द्रष्टुं वयं सर्वे भवन्तं शक्नुमः सदा।
भावातीतं गुणातीतमवाङ्मनसगोचरम ॥
vishnu_gita::246.verse_hindi: हमको कि जिससे हम सब भावों से अतीत, गुणों से अतीत और मन वाणी से अगोचर आपको हर समय देखने का सामर्थ्य प्राप्त कर सके
vishnu_gita::246.english_translation: By which we all can always see you beyond emotions, beyond qualities, beyond speech and mind.
vishnu_gita::246.translation_literal: येन (by which) / द्रष्टुं (to see) / वयं (we) / सर्वे (all) / भवन्तं (you) / शक्नुमः (can) / सदा (always) / भावातीतं (beyond emotions) / गुणातीतम् (beyond qualities) / अवाङ्मनसगोचरम् (beyond speech and mind, perceivable)
vishnu_gita::246.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::246.essence: You can perceive the true self beyond all emotions, qualities, and mental expressions at all times.
vishnu_gita::246.simple_meaning: You can learn to see the true self beyond all emotions, qualities, and mental expressions at any time.
vishnu_gita::246.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you can perceive without being caught in feelings or words.
vishnu_gita::246.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals a way to perceive the divine that transcends all emotional states, qualities (gunas), speech, and mind, showing how to access a clear, uninterrupted vision beyond ordinary mental limitations.
vishnu_gita::246.modern_relevance: When your mind is overwhelmed by emotions or chatter, this teaching reminds you that you can still see clearly beyond all that noise.
vishnu_gita::246.insight: It teaches you to shift your awareness beyond reactive feelings and mental labels to a pure witnessing of what is.

vishnu_gita::247.verse_sanskrit:
लीनाऽव्यक्तदशायां में प्रकृतिमयि सर्वदा ।
तथा व्यक्तदशायां सा प्रकटीभूय सर्वतः ॥
vishnu_gita::247.verse_hindi: मेरी प्रकृति अव्यक्त दशा में मुझमें सर्वदा लीन रहती है और व्यक्त दशा में यह प्रकट होकर
vishnu_gita::247.english_translation: My nature remains always merged in me in the unmanifest state, and in the manifest state it appears everywhere.
vishnu_gita::247.translation_literal: लीनाऽव्यक्तदशायां (merged in unmanifest state) / में (in me) / प्रकृतिमयि (by nature) / सर्वदा (always) / तथा (and) / व्यक्तदशायां (in manifest state) / सा (it) / प्रकटीभूय (becoming manifest) / सर्वतः (everywhere)
vishnu_gita::247.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::247.essence: True nature is simultaneously hidden within and revealed everywhere.
vishnu_gita::247.simple_meaning: Your essential nature stays hidden within you in quiet moments but shows up clearly in active times all around.
vishnu_gita::247.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing you are both the calm core and the lively world.
vishnu_gita::247.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that his nature remains deeply merged and unexpressed in the unmanifest state, yet becomes fully visible and active in the manifest state, showing a unity between hidden essence and visible form.
vishnu_gita::247.modern_relevance: When you feel quiet and unnoticed, and when you express yourself fully, both are parts of your true nature.
vishnu_gita::247.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing yourself as either hidden or visible to embracing both as your true reality.

vishnu_gita::248.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिगुणानां तरङ्गेशु स्वभावाद्धि तरङ्गाति ।
नैवात्र संशयः कोऽपि वर्तते विबुधर्षभाः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::248.verse_hindi: स्वभाव से ही त्रिगुण तरङ्गले सब ओर तरङ्गित होने लगती है। हे देवतागण ! इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं है।
vishnu_gita::248.english_translation: The waves of the three qualities naturally arise and move everywhere; among the wise, there is no doubt about this.
vishnu_gita::248.translation_literal: त्रिगुणानां (of the three qualities) / तरङ्गेशु (in the waves) / स्वभावाद्धि (from the nature itself) / तरङ्गाति (it flows) / नैवात्र (not here) / संशयः (doubt) / कोऽपि (anyone) / वर्तते (exists) / विबुधर्षभाः (the best among the wise)
vishnu_gita::248.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::248.essence: The three qualities flow naturally; the wisest accept this without doubt.
vishnu_gita::248.simple_meaning: The three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas) naturally arise and move everywhere without interruption, and wise people have no doubt about this fact.
vishnu_gita::248.simple_insight: There is confidence in recognizing the natural flow of qualities within everything around you.
vishnu_gita::248.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the three fundamental qualities—sattva, rajas, and tamas—flow like waves from their very nature throughout existence, and the wisest beings accept this without any hesitation or doubt.
vishnu_gita::248.modern_relevance: When you notice your mood shifting naturally through energy, calm, or inertia, you can trust this flow as part of your nature without resistance.
vishnu_gita::248.insight: It shifts your perspective to accept natural fluctuations as inherent, reducing inner conflict about change.

vishnu_gita::249.verse_sanskrit:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः ।
निबध्नन्ति सुपर्वाणो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
vishnu_gita::249.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! सत्व रज और तम ये तीन गुण प्रकृति से उत्पन्न होकर देहों में स्थित निर्विकार देही को आवद्ध किया करते हैं
vishnu_gita::249.english_translation: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas are qualities born of nature that bind the changeless true self to the body.
vishnu_gita::249.translation_literal: सत्त्वं (goodness) / रजः (passion) / तमः (ignorance) / इति (thus) / गुणाः (qualities) / प्रकृतिसंभवाः (born of nature) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / सुपर्वाणः (the true self) / देहे (in the body) / देहिनम् (the embodied self) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
vishnu_gita::249.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::249.essence: The changeless true self is bound by nature’s three qualities within the body.
vishnu_gita::249.simple_meaning: Three qualities of nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance—bind the unchanging true self to the body.
vishnu_gita::249.simple_insight: There’s a deeper self inside you that remains untouched despite changing qualities around it.
vishnu_gita::249.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to celestial beings that the three qualities—sattva, rajas, and tamas—arise from nature and entangle the imperishable true self within the body, causing it to appear bound and affected by change.
vishnu_gita::249.modern_relevance: You feel stuck or overwhelmed by your moods and impulses, yet your true self remains untouched beneath them all.
vishnu_gita::249.insight: It teaches you to see the difference between your changeless true self and the shifting qualities that influence your experience.

vishnu_gita::250.verse_sanskrit:
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् ।
सुखसङ्गेन बनाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघाः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::250.verse_hindi: हे पाप रहितो! इन तीनों गुणों से निर्मल होने के कारण, प्रकाशक और दोषरहित सत्त्वगुण सुखासनि के द्वारा और ज्ञानसंग के द्वारा बद्ध करता है
vishnu_gita::250.english_translation: Pure sattva, being luminous and free from fault, binds through attachment to pleasure and to knowledge.
vishnu_gita::250.translation_literal: तत्र (there) सत्त्वं (sattva-quality) निर्मलत्वात् (from purity) प्रकाशकम् (illuminating) अनामयम् (without disease/fault) । सुखसङ्गेन (by attachment to pleasure) बन्धति (binds) ज्ञानसङ्गेन (by attachment to knowledge) च (and) अनघाः (sinless/without fault) ॥
vishnu_gita::250.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::250.essence: Pure clarity can bind you when it fuels attachment to pleasure or knowledge.
vishnu_gita::250.simple_meaning: Pure qualities that illuminate and are free of faults can still bind you if you become attached to pleasure or knowledge.
vishnu_gita::250.simple_insight: Even your best qualities can hold you back when mixed with craving.
vishnu_gita::250.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that even sattva—the purest, most luminous quality—is not automatically liberating. When it creates attachment to pleasant experiences or knowledge, it binds the seeker, showing that purity alone is not enough for freedom.
vishnu_gita::250.modern_relevance: You might feel your clarity or learning is freeing, but craving comfort or certainty can still trap you in endless cycles.
vishnu_gita::250.insight: Recognize that attachment can arise even from good qualities, shifting your task to release craving itself.

vishnu_gita::251.verse_sanskrit:
रजो रागात्मकं वित्त तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् ।
तन्निबनाति भो देवाः ! कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
vishnu_gita::251.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! रजोगुण को रागात्मक, और तृष्णासक्ति से उत्पन्न जानना चाहिए, वह देही को कर्म आसक्ति  द्वारा आबद्ध किया करता है।
vishnu_gita::251.english_translation: O radiant beings, know that wealth born of desire and attachment to passion binds the embodied self through attachment to action.
vishnu_gita::251.translation_literal: रजो (of passion) रागात्मकं (filled with attachment) वित्त (wealth) तृष्णा (desire) सङ्ग (attachment) समुत्भवम् (originating) । तन् (that) निबनाति (binds) भो (O) देवाः (radiant beings) कर्म (action) सङ्गेन (by attachment) देहिनम् (the embodied self) ॥
vishnu_gita::251.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::251.essence: Desire-born wealth binds the self through attachment to action.
vishnu_gita::251.simple_meaning: Wealth that arises from desire and attachment binds the true self because it creates attachment to actions and their outcomes.
vishnu_gita::251.simple_insight: You feel how craving wealth can quietly tie you down, limiting your freedom.
vishnu_gita::251.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that wealth born from passion and desire creates attachment that binds the embodied self to ongoing actions and their results, trapping it in cycles of craving and consequence.
vishnu_gita::251.modern_relevance: You chase money driven by craving, only to find it pulls you deeper into stress and endless doing.
vishnu_gita::251.insight: Recognize how craving for outcomes creates bondage; shifting focus away frees your actions.

vishnu_gita::252.verse_sanskrit:
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं वित्त मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
प्रमादालास्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निव्धान्ति निर्जरा ॥
vishnu_gita::252.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! तमोगुण को अज्ञान से उत्पन्न और सब प्राणियों मे भ्रम उत्पन्न करनेवाला जानो, वह प्रमाद अनुद्दम धम और चित्त की अवसन्नता द्वारा देही को आबद्ध करता है।
vishnu_gita::252.english_translation: O beings, know that the quality of darkness born from ignorance causes delusion in all living beings; it binds the embodied self through carelessness, laziness, and drowsiness.
vishnu_gita::252.translation_literal: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं (darkness born of ignorance) / वित्त (cause) / मोहनं (delusion) / सर्वदेहिनाम् (in all embodied beings) / प्रमादालास्यनिद्राभि (through carelessness, laziness, drowsiness) / तन्निव्धान्ति (binds) / निर्जरा (without decay or end)
vishnu_gita::252.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::252.essence: Ignorance-born darkness binds living beings through careless laziness and mental dullness.
vishnu_gita::252.simple_meaning: Darkness arising from ignorance causes confusion and binds living beings through carelessness, laziness, and drowsiness.
vishnu_gita::252.simple_insight: You feel how laziness and carelessness silently hold you back in confusion.
vishnu_gita::252.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how the quality of darkness, born from ignorance, creates delusion and traps all embodied beings. This binding happens through common human weaknesses like carelessness, laziness, and drowsiness, stopping progress toward clarity.
vishnu_gita::252.modern_relevance: You find yourself distracted and stuck, tired yet unable to focus, trapped by your own mental fog and inertia.
vishnu_gita::252.insight: Recognize how carelessness and mental dullness act like chains, and begin to notice these patterns to break free.

vishnu_gita::253.verse_sanskrit:
सत्त्वं सूखे सञ्जयति रजः कणि चामराः।
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥
vishnu_gita::253.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! सत्त्वगुण जीव को सुख में आबद्ध करता है, रजोगुण कर्म में आबद्ध करता है और तमोगुण ज्ञान को आवरण कर के प्रमाद में आबद्ध करता है
vishnu_gita::253.english_translation: The quality of goodness binds the being to happiness, passion binds to action, and ignorance covers knowledge, binding one to negligence.
vishnu_gita::253.translation_literal: सत्त्वं (goodness) / सूखे (to happiness) / सञ्जयति (binds) / रजः (passion) / कणि (to action) / चामराः (binds) / ज्ञानमावृत्य (covering knowledge) / तु (but) / तमः (ignorance) / प्रमादे (to negligence) / सञ्जयत्युत (binds)
vishnu_gita::253.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::253.essence: Your nature's qualities bind you differently—to happiness, to action, or to negligence.
vishnu_gita::253.simple_meaning: Goodness ties you to happiness, passion ties you to action, and ignorance hides knowledge, causing carelessness.
vishnu_gita::253.simple_insight: You can see how your natural tendencies shape what you get stuck in.
vishnu_gita::253.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to divine beings how the three qualities—goodness, passion, and ignorance—bind living beings differently: goodness links to happiness, passion to action, and ignorance conceals knowledge, leading to negligence.
vishnu_gita::253.modern_relevance: You notice sometimes you pursue pleasure, sometimes get caught up in busyness, or overlook important things because your own nature pulls you different ways.
vishnu_gita::253.insight: Recognize which quality influences your current state; this awareness helps you shift toward clarity and care.

vishnu_gita::254.verse_sanskrit:
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं प्रभु भवसलम् ।
रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
vishnu_gita::254.verse_hindi: रज एवं तमोगुण को दबा करके. सत्त्वगुण बलवान होता है, सत्त्व एवं तमोगुण को परास्त करके रजोगुण प्रबल होता है और सत्त्व एवं रजोगुण को दबा कर के तमो गुण प्रबल होता है
vishnu_gita::254.english_translation: By overcoming rajas and tamas, sattva becomes dominant; by overcoming sattva and tamas, rajas becomes dominant; by overcoming sattva and rajas, tamas becomes dominant.
vishnu_gita::254.translation_literal: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय (overcoming rajas and tamas) सत्त्वं (sattva) प्रभु (dominant) भवसलम् (becomes) । रजः (rajas) सत्त्वं (sattva) तमश्चैव (and tamas also) तमः (tamas) सत्त्वं (sattva) रजस्तथा (and rajas likewise) ॥
vishnu_gita::254.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::254.essence: One of the three qualities dominates only when it suppresses the other two.
vishnu_gita::254.simple_meaning: Among the three qualities—activity, inertia, and harmony—one becomes strong only after the other two are overcome within you.
vishnu_gita::254.simple_insight: You can watch how shifting inner qualities shape your experience of yourself.
vishnu_gita::254.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the interplay of the three fundamental qualities (gunas): rajas (activity), tamas (inertia), and sattva (harmony). Each quality becomes dominant only by suppressing the other two. This reveals how inner states fluctuate and influence behavior.
vishnu_gita::254.modern_relevance: When you feel energetic, calm, or dull, it’s because one inner quality is overshadowing the others, shaping how you act and feel.
vishnu_gita::254.insight: It teaches you to recognize which inner quality currently governs your mind and how the others recede, helping you observe your shifting states.

vishnu_gita::255.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन् प्रकाश उपजायते ।
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्चमित्युत ॥
vishnu_gita::255.verse_hindi: जब इस देह में श्रोत्रादि सब द्वारो में ज्ञानमय प्रकाश होता है तब सत्त्वगुण की विशेष वृद्धि हुई है ऐसा समझना चाहिये
vishnu_gita::255.english_translation: When knowledge arises as light in all the senses of this body, it shows a clear growth of the quality of goodness.
vishnu_gita::255.translation_literal: सर्वद्वारेषु (in all doors) देहेऽस्मिन् (in the body) प्रकाश (light) उपजायते (arises) । ज्ञानं (knowledge) यदा (when) तदा (then) विद्याद् (there is) विवृद्धं (growth) सत्चमिति (called goodness) उत (indeed) ॥
vishnu_gita::255.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::255.essence: Knowledge illuminating all senses reveals the blossoming of inner goodness.
vishnu_gita::255.simple_meaning: When knowledge lights up all your senses and awareness, it shows that your inner goodness is growing.
vishnu_gita::255.simple_insight: You can feel your whole being becoming clearer and more virtuous as knowledge grows.
vishnu_gita::255.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when all the sensory gateways of the body are illuminated by knowledge, it signals the flourishing of sattva, the quality of purity and clarity. This moment marks a deepening of inner harmony and wisdom.
vishnu_gita::255.modern_relevance: You notice moments when your perceptions feel sharper, clearer, and more balanced, signaling growth in your character.
vishnu_gita::255.insight: Recognize when your awareness brightens your senses as a sign of increased clarity and goodness within.

vishnu_gita::256.verse_sanskrit:
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा ।
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे विबुधर्षभाः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::256.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! लोभ, प्रवृत्ति अर्थात् सर्वदा सकाम कर्म करने की इच्छा, कर्मों का आरम्भ अर्थात् उद्यम, अशम अर्थात् अशान्ति एवं स्पृहा अर्थात् विषय तृष्णा, यह सब रजोगुण बढ़ने पर उत्पन्न होते हैं
vishnu_gita::256.english_translation: Greed, urge, beginning of action, unrest, and craving arise when the quality of passion grows.
vishnu_gita::256.translation_literal: लोभः (greed) / प्रवृत्तिः (urge) / आरम्भः (beginning) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / अशमः (unrest) / स्पृहा (craving) / रजसः (of passion) / एतानि (these) / जायन्ते (arise) / विवृद्धे (when increased) / विवुधर्षभाः (wise ones)
vishnu_gita::256.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::256.essence: Passion intensifies greed, restless urges, and craving in all your actions.
vishnu_gita::256.simple_meaning: Greed, urges to act, restlessness, and craving come from increasing passion in your mind.
vishnu_gita::256.simple_insight: You can notice how intense desire stirs restlessness and endless wanting in your actions.
vishnu_gita::256.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when the quality of passion (rajas) grows stronger in your nature, it brings greed, impulses to start actions, inner unrest, and craving for objects or results. These affect your ability to act calmly and wisely.
vishnu_gita::256.modern_relevance: You wake up feeling restless and driven by wants, rushing into tasks without peace or clarity.
vishnu_gita::256.insight: This verse helps you see how passion fuels restless desire and action, encouraging you to cultivate calmness.

vishnu_gita::257.verse_sanskrit:
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च ।
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विटद्धे सुरसत्तमाः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::257.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्ठो! विवेकभ्रंश, उद्यमहीनता, कर्तव्य के अनुसन्धान का न रहना और मिथ्या अभिमान यह सभी तमो  गुण के बढ़ने पर उत्पन्न होते हैं
vishnu_gita::257.english_translation: O best of the radiant ones! Loss of discernment, inactivity, neglect of duty, and false pride all arise from the increase of darkness.
vishnu_gita::257.translation_literal: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च (absence of light and activity) / प्रमादो (carelessness) / मोह (delusion) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / तमस्येतानि (from darkness these) / जायन्ते (arise) / विटद्धे (O radiant one) / सुरसत्तमाः (best of the devas)
vishnu_gita::257.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::257.essence: Growing inner darkness causes loss of clarity, laziness, neglect, and false pride.
vishnu_gita::257.simple_meaning: Losing clarity, becoming inactive, ignoring your responsibilities, and falling into false pride come from growing inner darkness.
vishnu_gita::257.simple_insight: You can feel stuck when your inner light dims and false views take over.
vishnu_gita::257.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the radiant divine, explaining that when darkness grows within, it causes loss of discernment, laziness, neglect of duty, and false pride, warning of how inner confusion weakens action.
vishnu_gita::257.modern_relevance: You start doubting yourself and procrastinating when confusion and pride cloud your mind during tough times.
vishnu_gita::257.insight: It teaches you to recognize how inner darkness harms your clarity and motivation to act rightly.

vishnu_gita::258.verse_sanskrit:
यदा सत्त्वे प्रद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान प्रतिपद्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::258.verse_hindi: यदि सत्वगुण के विशेषरूप से बढ़नेपर जीव मृत्युको प्राप्त हो तब वह ब्रह्मवेत्ताओ के प्रकाशमय लोकों को प्राप्त होता है अर्थात् उसकी उत्तम गति होती है
vishnu_gita::258.english_translation: When the body-holder departs by the supreme mode of goodness, they reach the pure realms of the wise.
vishnu_gita::258.translation_literal: यदा (when) सत्त्वे (in goodness) प्रद्धे (increased) तु (then) प्रलयं (destruction/departure) याति (goes) देहभृत् (body-holder) । तदोत्तमविदां (then of supreme wise) लोकान् (worlds) अमलान् (pure) प्रतिपद्यते (obtains) ॥
vishnu_gita::258.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::258.essence: Departing with pure goodness leads the true self to radiant realms of wisdom.
vishnu_gita::258.simple_meaning: When a person's body ends with the highest goodness in their nature, their true being attains pure, wise realms beyond.
vishnu_gita::258.simple_insight: There's hope in knowing that living with goodness leads to peaceful destinations beyond this life.
vishnu_gita::258.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when a being's physical life ends under the influence of the highest quality of goodness (sattva), their essence moves to pure worlds inhabited by the wisest. This teaching points to the rewards of cultivating purity and clarity in life.
vishnu_gita::258.modern_relevance: You notice how peaceful moments after deep kindness or clarity feel like a glimpse of something beyond daily struggles.
vishnu_gita::258.insight: It shifts focus to nurturing goodness in life as a way to prepare for a peaceful transition beyond the body.

vishnu_gita::259.verse_sanskrit:
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसंगिषु जायते ।
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढ़योनिषु जायते ॥
vishnu_gita::259.verse_hindi: रजोगुण की वृद्धि के समय मृत्यु होने पर कर्मासक्त मनुष्य लोक में जन्म होता है एवं तमोगुण बढ़ने पर मृतव्यक्ति (पशु प्रेत आदि) मूढ़ योनियों में जन्म लेता है
vishnu_gita::259.english_translation: When death comes during the increase of rajas, the person attached to actions is born in the human world; when tamas increases, the deceased is born in foolish forms.
vishnu_gita::259.translation_literal: रजसि (in rajas) प्रलयं (death) गत्वा (having gone) कर्मसंगिषु (attached to actions) जायते (is born) । तथा (likewise) प्रलीनः (having increased) तमसि (in tamas) मूढयोनिषु (in foolish births) जायते (is born) ॥
vishnu_gita::259.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::259.essence: Your state of mind at death determines the nature of your next birth.
vishnu_gita::259.simple_meaning: Where your mind is fixed at death shapes your next birth—attachment leads to human life; darkness leads to confused, lower forms.
vishnu_gita::259.simple_insight: Knowing your mindset at death shapes your future brings responsibility and care to your present.
vishnu_gita::259.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that if a person dies while their mind is dominated by rajas (attachment and activity), they are reborn in a human realm tied to actions. If tamas (darkness and ignorance) dominates, rebirth occurs in confused, lower life forms, reflecting the quality of the inner state at death.
vishnu_gita::259.modern_relevance: When you react in frustration or dullness, you shape your mental habits that influence your future wellbeing and choices deeply.
vishnu_gita::259.insight: This teaching shifts focus from external actions to the inner quality of mind at death as key in shaping future experience.

vishnu_gita::260.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् ।
रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥
vishnu_gita::260.verse_hindi: सुकृत अर्थात् सात्त्विक कर्मका सात्त्विक और निर्मल फल है, राजस कर्म को फल दुःख और तामस कर्म का फल अज्ञान अर्थात् मूढ़ता है, ऐसा ज्ञानी लोग कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::260.english_translation: The fruit of pure, virtuous action is called sattvic and is pure; the fruit of passionate action is pain; the fruit of ignorant, dark action is ignorance.
vishnu_gita::260.translation_literal: कर्मणः (of action) सुकृतस्याहुः (of good deeds is said) सात्त्विकं (sattvic) निर्मलं (pure) फलम् (fruit) । रजसस्तु (passionate indeed) फलं (fruit) दुःखम् (pain) अज्ञानं (ignorance) तमसः (of darkness) फलम् (fruit) ॥
vishnu_gita::260.speaker: Unknown
