vishnu_gita::260.essence: The quality of your action shapes whether its result is clarity, pain, or confusion.
vishnu_gita::260.simple_meaning: Actions done with purity and good intention bring clear and good results. Actions done with passion cause pain. Actions done in ignorance lead to confusion.
vishnu_gita::260.simple_insight: You can feel peace when your actions come from clarity, not impulse or confusion.
vishnu_gita::260.detailed_meaning: This verse explains three types of actions and their results: pure and virtuous actions bring clear, positive outcomes; actions driven by passion cause pain; and actions done in ignorance result in confusion. Understanding this helps Arjuna see how his choices shape his experience.
vishnu_gita::260.modern_relevance: You notice that when you act calmly and with good intent, outcomes feel clear. But when driven by stress or confusion, results often cause more pain or frustration.
vishnu_gita::260.insight: It teaches you to recognize how your mindset colors the results of your actions and to choose clarity over impulse.

vishnu_gita::261.verse_sanskrit:
सत्त्वात् संजायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥
vishnu_gita::261.verse_hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञानोत्पत्ति होती है, रज से लोभ उत्पन्न होता है और तमोगुण से प्रमाद अविवेक और अज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है
vishnu_gita::261.english_translation: From sattva arises wisdom, from rajas greed, and from tamas negligence, delusion, and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::261.translation_literal: सत्त्वात् (from sattva) / संजायते (arises) / ज्ञानं (wisdom) / रजसो (from rajas) / लोभ (greed) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / प्रमादमोहौ (negligence and delusion) / तमसो (from tamas) / भवतः (are) / अज्ञानमेव (indeed ignorance) / च (and)
vishnu_gita::261.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::261.essence: Your inner qualities shape your mind into wisdom, greed, or ignorance.
vishnu_gita::261.simple_meaning: Three qualities shape your mind: clarity brings wisdom, restlessness causes greed, and darkness leads to confusion and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::261.simple_insight: You can recognize which inner quality governs your thoughts, guiding you toward wisdom or confusion.
vishnu_gita::261.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how three fundamental qualities—clarity (sattva), activity (rajas), and inertia (tamas)—affect the mind. Clarity produces understanding; restlessness fuels desire; and darkness causes delusion and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::261.modern_relevance: When your mind feels calm and clear, you understand better; when restless, you chase wants; when dull, confusion takes over.
vishnu_gita::261.insight: It helps you to notice whether your mind is clear, restless, or dull to choose wiser responses.

vishnu_gita::262.verse_sanskrit:
उर्दध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।
जघन्यगुणवृतिस्था अघो गछन्ति तामसा: ॥
vishnu_gita::262.verse_hindi: सत्त्वप्रधान व्यक्ति उर्द्ध्वलोक को जाते हैं, रजोगुण प्रधान व्यक्ति मध्यलोक में रहते हैं और निकृष्टगुणावलम्बी तामसिक व्यक्ति अधोलोक में जाते हैं
vishnu_gita::262.english_translation: People dominated by sattva ascend to higher realms, those with rajas dwell in the middle realms, and those bound by tamas descend to lower realms.
vishnu_gita::262.translation_literal: उर्दध्वं (upward) गच्छन्ति (go) सत्त्वस्था (those established in sattva) मध्ये (in the middle) तिष्ठन्ति (stay) राजसाः (those of rajas) जघन्यगुणवृतिस्था (those of heavy/ugly qualities) अघो (downward) गच्छन्ति (go) तामसा: (those of tamas)
vishnu_gita::262.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::262.essence: Your inner qualities determine whether you rise, remain, or fall in existence.
vishnu_gita::262.simple_meaning: People’s qualities influence where they go: purity leads upward, passion keeps one in the middle, and darkness pulls downward.
vishnu_gita::262.simple_insight: You feel your inner nature shapes your journey and where you find yourself.
vishnu_gita::262.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how people’s inner qualities—purity (sattva), passion (rajas), and darkness (tamas)—determine their spiritual and existential position, describing a cosmic hierarchy tied to these traits.
vishnu_gita::262.modern_relevance: You notice how your mindset and habits influence whether you feel uplifted, stuck, or dragged down in daily life.
vishnu_gita::262.insight: Recognize how your dominant qualities shape your experience and direction in life.

vishnu_gita::263.verse_sanskrit:
नान्यं गणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति ।
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::263.verse_hindi: जब ज्ञानी व्यक्ति गुण के अतिरिक्त और किसी को कर्त्ता करके नहीं देखता है और गुण से परे जो गुण का दर्शक आत्मा है उसको जानता है वह मुझको प्राप्त हो जाता है
vishnu_gita::263.english_translation: When a wise person sees no doer beyond the qualities and knows the self that observes these qualities, they attain me.
vishnu_gita::263.translation_literal: नान्यं (no other) / गणैः (qualities) / कर्तारं (doer) / यदा (when) / द्रष्टा (seer) / अनुपश्यति (observes) / गुणैः (qualities) / च (and) / परं (beyond) / वेत्ति (knows) / मद्भावं (my state) / सः (he) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
vishnu_gita::263.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::263.essence: True wisdom is seeing yourself as the observer beyond all qualities and doers.
vishnu_gita::263.simple_meaning: A wise person understands that no one acts independently beyond qualities and recognizes the self that watches these qualities, thus connecting with the divine.
vishnu_gita::263.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing you are the observer, not the doer behind your traits.
vishnu_gita::263.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that knowing the self as the observer beyond all qualities is the key to realizing the divine. The wise see no separate agent acting but only qualities and the self witnessing them.
vishnu_gita::263.modern_relevance: When you notice your moods and habits without blaming a separate 'you,' you start to experience inner freedom beyond your traits.
vishnu_gita::263.insight: It teaches you to shift from identifying as the doer to recognizing yourself as the witness behind all qualities.

vishnu_gita::264.verse_sanskrit:
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन देही देहसमुद्भवान् ।
जन्ममृत्युजरादुः रैविर्मुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥
vishnu_gita::264.verse_hindi: देह से उत्पन्न इन तीनों गुणों को अतिक्रमण करके जन्ममृत्युजरारूप दुःखों से मुक्त होकर देही परमानन्द को प्राप्त हो जाता है
vishnu_gita::264.english_translation: Surpassing the three qualities born from the body, the embodied one becomes free from the sorrows of birth, death, old age, and pain, and attains supreme bliss in the body.
vishnu_gita::264.translation_literal: गुणानेतानतीत्य (surpassing the three qualities) / त्रीन (three) / देही (the embodied one) / देहसमुद्भवान् (born of the body) / जन्ममृत्युजरादुः (birth, death, old age, pain) / रैविः (sorrow) / मुक्तः (free) / अमृतम् (immortality/supreme bliss) / अश्नुते (attains)
vishnu_gita::264.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::264.essence: True bliss arises when you transcend the body’s three qualities and its cycle of suffering.
vishnu_gita::264.simple_meaning: You can go beyond the three qualities that come from your body and be free from birth, death, aging, and pain to experience supreme joy within yourself.
vishnu_gita::264.simple_insight: You carry the possibility of freedom and joy beyond all physical suffering and change.
vishnu_gita::264.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the embodied self, bound by three gunas (qualities) originating from the body, can transcend these to escape the cycle of birth, death, aging, and suffering, thereby reaching immortal bliss even while embodied.
vishnu_gita::264.modern_relevance: When your body feels weak or pain arises, remember you are more than these changes and can find lasting joy beyond them.
vishnu_gita::264.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with bodily qualities to recognizing a transcendent bliss within the embodied experience.

vishnu_gita::265.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकाशश्च प्रवृत्तिश्च मोहमेव च निर्जराः !
न द्वष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्गति ॥
vishnu_gita::265.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! प्रकाश, प्रवृत्ति और मोह (तीनों गुणों के यथाक्रम कार्य) से सब गुणकार्य प्रारम्भ होने पर जो व्यक्ति द्वेष नहीं करता है और इनके निवृत्त होने पर जो इनमें इच्छा नहीं रखता है वह गुणातीत कहलाता है
vishnu_gita::265.english_translation: O radiant beings! When light, activity, and delusion arise, if a person does not hate them, and when they cease, if they hold no desire for them, that person is called beyond the qualities.
vishnu_gita::265.translation_literal: प्रकाशश्च (light also) / प्रवृत्तिश्च (activity also) / मोहमेव (and delusion indeed) / च (and) / निर्जराः (without old age or decay) / न (not) / द्वष्टि (hatred) / सम्प्रवृत्तानि (those that arise) / न (not) / निवृत्तानि (those that cease) / काङ्गति (desire) ॥
vishnu_gita::265.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::265.essence: Freedom arises when you neither hate nor desire the inner qualities as they come and go.
vishnu_gita::265.simple_meaning: You become free from qualities when you neither hate their arising nor desire their passing.
vishnu_gita::265.simple_insight: Peace grows when you stop fighting or chasing your inner impulses.
vishnu_gita::265.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that when light, activity, and delusion arise within, a person who neither hates these qualities nor desires their cessation transcends them, becoming beyond the realm of qualities.
vishnu_gita::265.modern_relevance: When your feelings and impulses arise, you neither reject nor chase them, and peace naturally follows.
vishnu_gita::265.insight: It teaches you to relate to inner forces without resistance or attachment, opening space for freedom.

vishnu_gita::266.verse_sanskrit:
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैयों न विचाल्यते ।
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येवं योऽवतियुति नेङ्गते ॥
vishnu_gita::266.verse_hindi: जो उदासीन अर्थात् केवल साक्षीरूप से स्थित है और गुणों से जो विचलित नहीं होता है और गुणसमूह अपना अपना कार्य करते हैं ऐसा समझकर जो स्थिर रहता है और स्वयं चेष्टा नहीं करता है वह गुणातीत कहलाता है
vishnu_gita::266.english_translation: One who remains indifferent like a witness, unmoved by qualities as they act, and stays steady without engaging, is called beyond qualities.
vishnu_gita::266.translation_literal: उदासीनवदासीनो (like indifferent witness) / गुणैयों (by qualities) / न (not) / विचाल्यते (is disturbed) / गुणा (qualities) / वर्तन्त (exist) / इति (thus) / एवम् (so) / योऽवतियुति (who remains) / न (not) / एङ्गते (engages)
vishnu_gita::266.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::266.essence: Remaining steady and detached like a witness means you are beyond all qualities acting around you.
vishnu_gita::266.simple_meaning: You stay calm and steady like a witness, not disturbed or involved by changing qualities around you.
vishnu_gita::266.simple_insight: You feel peaceful knowing you don't have to react to every change or emotion.
vishnu_gita::266.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a state where a person observes qualities (like emotions or traits) without being disturbed or involved, remaining steady and inactive, illustrating the state beyond the influence of nature's changes.
vishnu_gita::266.modern_relevance: When emotions or moods shift rapidly, you can choose to simply observe without getting swept away by them.
vishnu_gita::266.insight: It teaches you to step back mentally and watch thoughts and feelings without reacting or identifying with them.

vishnu_gita::267.verse_hindi: जिसको सुखदुःख समान हैं, जो आत्मा अवस्थित है, जिसके लिये मिटटी का ढेला पत्थर और सुवर्ण सब समान है, जिसके निकट प्रिय और अप्रिय दोनों समान हैं, जिसने अपनी इन्द्रियों को जीत लिया है और जिसके निकट निन्दा और स्तुति दोनों समान है वह गुणातीत कहलाता है
vishnu_gita::267.english_translation: One who sees pleasure and pain as equal, and values clay, stone, and gold alike, who regards friend and foe the same, has conquered the senses and treats praise and blame equally; such a one is beyond qualities.
vishnu_gita::267.translation_literal: समदुःखसुखः (equal pain and pleasure) स्वस्थः (established) समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः (equal to clay, stone, and gold) तुल्यनियापियो (equal to friend and foe) धीरः (the steady one) तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः (equal to blame and praise)
vishnu_gita::267.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::267.essence: True steadiness arises when you treat opposites like pain and pleasure as equal.
vishnu_gita::267.simple_meaning: You become steady when you treat pleasure and pain, praise and blame, as the same and don’t let them disturb your mind.
vishnu_gita::267.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing all experiences as equal, easing emotional highs and lows.
vishnu_gita::267.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a person who has mastered their senses and emotions so fully that external differences—like pain or pleasure, praise or blame, friends or enemies—no longer disturb their inner balance. This teaching encourages steady equanimity in the face of life's fluctuations.
vishnu_gita::267.modern_relevance: You receive a compliment and a criticism in the same day, but your heart stays calm, neither elated nor crushed.
vishnu_gita::267.insight: It teaches you to keep your inner state unaffected by external praise or blame, balancing your mind like an even scale.

vishnu_gita::268.verse_sanskrit:
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।
सर्वारम्भपरिसागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::268.verse_hindi: जो मान अपमान में समभाव रखता है, जो मित्र और शत्रु के विषय में समभाव रखता है और सब कर्मों के  आरम्भ का त्याग करने वाला है अर्थात् जो नवीन कर्म नहीं करता वह गुणातीत कहलाता है
vishnu_gita::268.english_translation: One who treats honor and dishonor equally, sees friend and enemy alike, and renounces all new actions is called beyond qualities.
vishnu_gita::268.translation_literal: मान (honor) / अपमानयोः (and dishonor) / तुल्यः (equal) / तुल्यः (equal) / मित्र (friend) / अरि (enemy) / पक्षयोः (towards both) / सर्व (all) / आरम्भ (beginnings) / परिसागी (renouncing) / गुणातीतः (beyond qualities) / स (he) / उच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::268.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::268.essence: Steady balance toward all people and outcomes marks freedom from inner qualities.
vishnu_gita::268.simple_meaning: You stay balanced whether praised or blamed, treat friends and enemies the same, and let go of starting new actions.
vishnu_gita::268.simple_insight: You find calm when you stop reacting differently to praise, blame, friend, or foe.
vishnu_gita::268.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the wise person does not get shaken by honor or insult, nor by friend or enemy. By refusing to start fresh actions driven by desire or aversion, they transcend all qualities.
vishnu_gita::268.modern_relevance: You receive a compliment or criticism at work and stay calm. You meet a loved one or rival and respond with the same steady heart.
vishnu_gita::268.insight: It teaches you to observe without preference or aversion, making your mind steady and free from new attachments.

vishnu_gita::269.verse_sanskrit:
माञ्च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते।
म गुणान् समतीत्यैतान ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
vishnu_gita::269.verse_hindi: और जो एकान्त भक्तियोग के द्वारा मेरी सेवा करता है वह इन गुणों को विशेष रूप से अतिक्रमण करके ब्रह्म भाव को प्राप्त होता है।
vishnu_gita::269.english_translation: One who serves me with exclusive devoted love transcends these qualities and attains the state of supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::269.translation_literal: माञ्च (me) योऽव्यभिचारेण (without deviation) भक्तियोगेन (by devoted love) सेवते (serves)। म (these) गुणान् (qualities) समतीत्य (transcending) एतान (these) ब्रह्मभूयाय (to supreme reality) कल्पते (becomes)।
vishnu_gita::269.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::269.essence: Exclusive devotion lets you transcend natural qualities and reach the supreme state.
vishnu_gita::269.simple_meaning: Serving with exclusive, unwavering devotion helps you go beyond ordinary qualities and reach the highest state of being.
vishnu_gita::269.simple_insight: There is freedom and elevation in serving with pure devotion beyond personal traits.
vishnu_gita::269.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a devotee who serves with unwavering, exclusive love goes beyond the three qualities that bind beings and attains the supreme state beyond nature.
vishnu_gita::269.modern_relevance: When you commit to a cause or person with full, undivided love, you move beyond your usual limits and find deeper meaning.
vishnu_gita::269.insight: It shifts your focus from personal traits and limitations to wholehearted devoted service, enabling spiritual transcendence.

vishnu_gita::270.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च ।
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखम्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥
vishnu_gita::270.verse_hindi: क्योंकि मैं नित्यस्थित और मोक्ष स्वरूप ब्रह्म के प्रतिष्ठा (स्थिति) का स्थान हूँ, मैं ही सनातनधर्म और ऐकान्तिक सुख का स्थान हूँ
vishnu_gita::270.english_translation: I am the foundation of Brahman, eternal and imperishable, the seat of eternal dharma and ultimate happiness.
vishnu_gita::270.translation_literal: ब्रह्मणो (of Brahman) हि (indeed) प्रतिष्ठा (foundation/seat) अहम् (I) अमृतस्य (of the immortal) अव्ययस्य (imperishable) च (and) शाश्वतस्य (eternal) च (and) धर्मस्य (of dharma) सुखम् (happiness) ऐकान्तिकस्य (exclusive/ultimate) च (and)
vishnu_gita::270.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::270.essence: You are the unchanging foundation of eternal truth, law, and lasting happiness.
vishnu_gita::270.simple_meaning: You are the unchanging foundation of the supreme reality, the eternal law, and pure lasting happiness.
vishnu_gita::270.simple_insight: There is deep comfort in knowing you embody timeless truth and joy beyond change.
vishnu_gita::270.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu declares himself as the unshakable foundation of Brahman, the supreme reality, embodying eternal dharma and ultimate bliss. This moment reveals his cosmic role as the source and seat of timeless spiritual truth and fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::270.modern_relevance: When everything feels fleeting or unstable, recognizing your inner source of lasting truth and happiness can steady you deeply.
vishnu_gita::270.insight: It invites you to identify with the eternal foundation beneath change rather than with temporary ups and downs.

vishnu_gita::271.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मस्य साम्प्रतं देवाः ! विशेषाणां ब्रवीम्यहम् ।
अङ्गानां त्रिविधं रूपं युष्माभिरवधार्यताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::271.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! अब मैं धर्म के विशेष विशेष अङ्गों का त्रिविध स्वरूप वर्णन करता हूँ आपलोग ध्यानपूर्वक सुनिये
vishnu_gita::271.english_translation: O divine beings! Now I will describe the threefold nature of the special aspects of dharma for you to carefully understand.
vishnu_gita::271.translation_literal: धर्मस्य (of dharma) / साम्प्रतं (now) / देवाः (O divine beings) / विशेषाणां (of special) / ब्रवीम्यहम् (I speak) / अङ्गानां (of parts) / त्रिविधं (threefold) / रूपं (form) / युष्माभिरवधार्यताम् (by you be understood).
vishnu_gita::271.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::271.essence: Dharma has three special parts that need careful understanding.
vishnu_gita::271.simple_meaning: The divine addresses the assembly to explain that he will now describe three special aspects of dharma.
vishnu_gita::271.simple_insight: Preparation and focus open the way to deeper understanding.
vishnu_gita::271.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine assembly, preparing to teach the threefold nature of dharma's special parts, setting the stage for the detailed philosophical discourse ahead.
vishnu_gita::271.insight: Recognize when a moment calls for full attention before learning something important.

vishnu_gita::272.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञो दानं तपस्त्रीणि धाङ्गानि प्रधानतः ।
तेष यज्ञः प्रधानं स्यात्तस्य भेदास्त्रिधा मताः ॥
vishnu_gita::272.verse_hindi: धर्म के प्रधान तीन अंग हैं, यज्ञ तप और दान। उनमें मुख्य अङ्ग जो यज्ञ है उसके तीन भेद हैं
vishnu_gita::272.english_translation: The three primary limbs of dharma are sacrifice, austerity, and charity; sacrifice is the chief among them and is classified into three types.
vishnu_gita::272.translation_literal: यज्ञो (sacrifice) / दानं (charity) / तपः (austerity) / त्रिणि (three) / धाङ्गानि (limbs) / प्रधानतः (chiefly) / तेष (of these) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / प्रधानं (chief) / स्यात् (is) / तस्य (its) / भेदाः (types) / त्रिधा (threefold) / मताः (are considered)
vishnu_gita::272.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::272.essence: True purpose is upheld by sacrifice, discipline, and giving, with sacrifice as the key.
vishnu_gita::272.simple_meaning: Dharma, your true purpose, has three main parts: sacrifice, discipline, and giving; sacrifice is the most important and has three kinds.
vishnu_gita::272.simple_insight: You can find your purpose by focusing on giving, discipline, and sacrifice together.
vishnu_gita::272.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that dharma—the right way to live—has three main limbs: sacrifice (yajna), austerity (tapas), and charity (dana). Among these, sacrifice is the chief and is further divided into three types, highlighting its central role in living rightly.
vishnu_gita::272.modern_relevance: When you balance self-discipline, generosity, and meaningful offerings, your actions align with a deeper purpose beyond daily routines.
vishnu_gita::272.insight: Recognize that your life's true purpose is supported by giving, disciplined effort, and self-offering; sacrifice holds a special place.

vishnu_gita::273.verse_hindi: ज्ञान , कर्म और उपासना, इस बात को सर्वशास्त्रनिष्णात तत्त्वज्ञानी पण्डितों ने कहा है।
vishnu_gita::273.english_translation: The wise scholars, experts in all scriptures, have declared that knowledge, action, and devotion are essential.
vishnu_gita::273.translation_literal: ज्ञानोपासनकर्माणि (knowledge, devotion, and actions) / यदुक्तानि (that have been said) / मनीषिभ: (by the wise) / सर्वशास्त्रेषु (in all scriptures) / निष्णान: (experts) / तत्त्वज्ञानाब्धिपारगै: (surpassing the ocean of true knowledge)
vishnu_gita::273.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::273.essence: True wisdom recognizes knowledge, action, and devotion as inseparable and essential together.
vishnu_gita::273.simple_meaning: Wise scholars who know all the scriptures say that knowledge, action, and devotion are interconnected essentials.
vishnu_gita::273.simple_insight: Knowing, acting, and loving are not separate but form a complete way to live.
vishnu_gita::273.detailed_meaning: Experts deeply versed in all sacred texts declare that knowledge, devoted practice, and action together form the foundation of spiritual life and understanding.
vishnu_gita::273.modern_relevance: When you face complex decisions, remember that learning, doing, and caring must all work together for balance.
vishnu_gita::273.insight: It teaches you to integrate your understanding, your efforts, and your heartfelt devotion into one seamless approach.

vishnu_gita::274.verse_sanskrit:
विशिष्टचेतनायुक्ता नराचा जीवजातयः।
स्वस्वाभाविकयोः सौख्यैश्वर्ययोस्त्यागतो ध्रुवम् ॥
vishnu_gita::274.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! विशिष्टचेतन मनुष्य आदि जीवगण अपने स्वाभाविक सुख और ऐश्वर्य के त्याग द्वारा
vishnu_gita::274.english_translation: Beings with distinct consciousness, like humans, attain certainty by renouncing their natural comforts and wealth.
vishnu_gita::274.translation_literal: विशिष्टचेतनायुक्ता (endowed with distinct consciousness) / नराचा (of humans) / जीवजातयः (living beings) / स्वस्वाभाविकयोः (their own natural) / सौख्यैश्वर्ययोः (comforts and wealth) / त्यागतो (by renunciation) / ध्रुवम् (certainly)
vishnu_gita::274.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::274.essence: Certainty arises when conscious beings renounce their natural pleasures and wealth.
vishnu_gita::274.simple_meaning: Distinct conscious beings like humans gain true certainty by giving up their natural pleasures and wealth.
vishnu_gita::274.simple_insight: Letting go of what feels naturally pleasant can bring deep inner certainty.
vishnu_gita::274.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that beings with unique consciousness, such as humans, achieve firm inner certainty only by renouncing their natural enjoyments and possessions. This moment points to the challenge of true renunciation beyond comfort.
vishnu_gita::274.modern_relevance: You might cling to familiar comforts and possessions, but real confidence grows when you step beyond them.
vishnu_gita::274.insight: It shifts you from identifying with comfort to embracing certainty through renunciation.

vishnu_gita::275.verse_sanskrit:
अदृष्टशक्तिं परमां यां लभ्यन्ते सुरर्षभा:।
नमव यज्ञं संपाहुः सर्वे नत्त्वविवेचकाः ॥
vishnu_gita::275.verse_hindi: जो परम अदृश्य शक्ति अवश्य प्राप्त करते हैं उसी को तत्त्वविवेचक लोग यज्ञ कहते हैं।
vishnu_gita::275.english_translation: The supreme unseen power attained by the highest beings is called sacrifice by the discerning.
vishnu_gita::275.translation_literal: अदृष्टशक्तिं (unseen power) परमां (supreme) यां (which) लभ्यन्ते (are attained) सुरर्षभा: (the best of devas) । नमव (offering) यज्ञं (sacrifice) संपाहुः (call) सर्वे (all) नत्त्वविवेचकाः (discerning persons) ॥
vishnu_gita::275.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::275.essence: True sacrifice is the attainment of a supreme unseen power by the highest beings.
vishnu_gita::275.simple_meaning: The greatest unseen power attained by noble beings is called sacrifice by those who understand its true nature.
vishnu_gita::275.simple_insight: There's awe in realizing sacrifice is about connecting with a supreme unseen power, not just rituals.
vishnu_gita::275.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the supreme power which cannot be seen but is attained by the highest divine beings is what true wisdom calls sacrifice. This shifts the idea of sacrifice from mere ritual to a profound cosmic principle.
vishnu_gita::275.modern_relevance: When you push beyond what you see or control, you tap into a force that wise people recognize as true offering or sacrifice.
vishnu_gita::275.insight: It teaches you to see sacrifice not as external ritual but as connecting with an inner, unseen power.

vishnu_gita::276.verse_sanskrit:
एतेषामेव सर्वेषामङ्गानां क्रमशः सुराः।
शृणु्दध्वं त्रिविधान भेदान् वाम्यहं गुणभेदतः ॥
vishnu_gita::276.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! इन्हीं सब अङ्गों के त्रिविध भेदों को क्रमशः बतलाता है, आपलोग शांत चित्त होकर ध्यान से सुनिए
vishnu_gita::276.english_translation: O radiant beings! Listen carefully as I explain the threefold distinctions of all these parts in order.
vishnu_gita::276.translation_literal: एतेषामेव (of these very) सर्वेषाम् (all) अङ्गानाम् (parts) क्रमशः (in order) सुराः (radiant beings) शृणु दध्वं (listen carefully) त्रिविधान (threefold) भेदान् (distinctions) वाम्यहम् (I, the speaker) गुणभेदतः (due to the division of qualities)
vishnu_gita::276.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::276.essence: Calm attention prepares you to understand the threefold distinctions among all parts.
vishnu_gita::276.simple_meaning: You are asked to listen carefully as the speaker explains the three types of distinctions among all parts.
vishnu_gita::276.simple_insight: The moment before learning holds quiet attention and readiness to understand deeply.
vishnu_gita::276.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the radiant beings, requesting calm and focused attention to explain the threefold distinctions among all elements based on qualities. This sets the stage for a detailed teaching ahead.
vishnu_gita::276.modern_relevance: You pause and quiet your mind just before an important explanation that will clarify complex ideas.
vishnu_gita::276.insight: It teaches the value of calm attention before receiving knowledge that unfolds in stages.

vishnu_gita::277.verse_sanskrit:
दातव्यामिति यहानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तदानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::277.verse_hindi: "दान करना उचित है" इस विचार से देश काल और पात्र की विवेचना करके प्रत्युपकार करने में असमर्थ व्यक्ति को जो दान किया जाता है वह सात्त्विक दान कहा गया है।
vishnu_gita::277.english_translation: Giving charity with consideration of place, time, and recipient, even to one unable to reciprocate, is called pure (sattvic) charity.
vishnu_gita::277.translation_literal: दातव्यामिति (to be given) यहानं (this) दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे (is given to one who cannot repay) । देशे (in place) काले (at time) च (and) पात्रे (to recipient) च (also) तदानं (that gift) सात्त्विकं (pure) स्मृतम् (is remembered/called) ॥
vishnu_gita::277.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::277.essence: Pure giving happens when you consider place, time, and recipient without expecting return.
vishnu_gita::277.simple_meaning: Giving charity thoughtfully by checking the right place, time, and recipient, even if they cannot return the favor, is considered pure giving.
vishnu_gita::277.simple_insight: Giving with awareness brings a quiet pride beyond expecting anything back.
vishnu_gita::277.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that charity should not be random. It must consider the right place, the right time, and the deserving recipient. Even if the recipient cannot repay, this thoughtful giving is called pure or sattvic charity.
vishnu_gita::277.modern_relevance: You decide to help a friend who can’t repay you right now, choosing the moment and way carefully—it feels right and meaningful.
vishnu_gita::277.insight: It teaches you to give with care and timing rather than impulsively, valuing the act over the return.

vishnu_gita::278.verse_sanskrit:
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थ फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::278.verse_hindi: किन्तु जो दान प्रत्युपकार के लिये अथवा फल की कामना करके कष्टपूर्वक दिया जाता है उस दान को राजस दान कहते हैं।
vishnu_gita::278.english_translation: But a gift given with the intention of return or desire for fruit, and given with difficulty, is called rajasic gift.
vishnu_gita::278.translation_literal: यत्तु (but) प्रत्युपकारार्थ (for return favor) फलमुद्दिश्य (desiring fruit) वा (or) पुनः (again). दीयते (is given) च (and) परिक्लिष्टं (with difficulty) तद् (that) राजसम् (rajasic) उदाहृतम् (called).
vishnu_gita::278.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::278.essence: Giving with expectation creates inner struggle and is not true generosity.
vishnu_gita::278.simple_meaning: Giving with expectation or wanting something in return creates tension and is called rajasic giving.
vishnu_gita::278.simple_insight: You feel the strain when your generosity is mixed with desire for gain.
vishnu_gita::278.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that gifts given with the hope of getting something back, or expecting a reward, cause inner struggle. This kind of giving is called rajasic because it is driven by personal desire and attachment.
vishnu_gita::278.modern_relevance: You offer help or gifts hoping for thanks or favors, but that hope makes you anxious and less free.
vishnu_gita::278.insight: It teaches you to notice when giving is motivated by desire, making your actions less pure and more stressful.

vishnu_gita::279.verse_hindi: देश और काल की विवेचना न करके, सत्कारशून्य और तिरस्कारपूर्वक अपात्रों को जो दान दिया जाता है वह तामस दान कहलाता है
vishnu_gita::279.english_translation: Giving gifts to unworthy recipients without considering place and time, done with disrespect, is called tamasic giving.
vishnu_gita::279.translation_literal: अदेशकाले (without place and time) यदा (when) अनपात्रेभ्यः (to unworthy recipients) च (and) दीयते (is given) असत्कृतम् (disrespectful) अवज्ञातम् (neglected) तत् (that) तामसम् (tamasic) उदाहृतम् (called)
vishnu_gita::279.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::279.essence: Giving without respect for time, place, and recipient is harmful and dark in quality.
vishnu_gita::279.simple_meaning: Giving without considering the right place, time, or worthy recipients, and done disrespectfully, is improper giving called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::279.simple_insight: You realize that how and when you give matters as much as what you give.
vishnu_gita::279.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that giving without proper thought—ignoring the right place, moment, or recipient—and with disrespect, creates negative energy and is called tamasic giving.
vishnu_gita::279.modern_relevance: You offer help or gifts impulsively, ignoring whether the timing or the person is right, making your efforts less meaningful or even harmful.
vishnu_gita::279.insight: It teaches you to pause and consider timing, recipient, and attitude before giving to keep your action pure.

vishnu_gita::280.verse_sanskrit:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्रिविधं सुराः।
अफलाकालिंक्षभिर्ययुक्तैः सात्विकं परिचक्षते ॥
vishnu_gita::280.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! आत्मा में अवस्थित व्यक्तियों के द्वारा परम श्रद्धापूर्वक और फल-कामना रहित होकर अनुष्ठित शारीरिक वाचनिक और मानसिक तप को सात्त्विक कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::280.english_translation: O divine beings! The supreme austerity performed with utmost faith by those established in the true self, without desire for results, through body, speech, and mind, is called sattvic.
vishnu_gita::280.translation_literal: श्रद्धया (with faith) / परया (supreme) / तप्तं (performed austerity) / तपस्तत्रिविधं (austerity threefold) / सुराः (divine beings) / अफलाकालिंक्षभिर्ययुक्तैः (without expectation of results) / सात्विकं (sattvic) / परिचक्षते (describe)
vishnu_gita::280.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::280.essence: Discipline rooted in faith and free from desire purifies body, speech, and mind.
vishnu_gita::280.simple_meaning: Discipline done with deep faith, without wanting rewards, using body, speech, and mind, is called pure or sattvic discipline.
vishnu_gita::280.simple_insight: You can fully commit to effort with trust, freeing yourself from the stress of outcomes.
vishnu_gita::280.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that true austerity is a threefold discipline of body, speech, and mind, performed with deep faith and without craving rewards. This sattvic discipline purifies and steadies the practitioner.
vishnu_gita::280.modern_relevance: You push yourself hard in your daily routine but stay calm because your effort isn't tied to praise or results.
vishnu_gita::280.insight: It teaches you to focus fully on your actions with faith, releasing attachment to what follows.

vishnu_gita::281.verse_sanskrit:
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
vishnu_gita::281.verse_hindi: संस्कार मान और पूजा के लिये एवं दम्भपूर्वक जो तपस्या की जाती है इस लोक में अनित्य और क्षणिक वह तपस्या राजस कही जाती है
vishnu_gita::281.english_translation: Any austerity performed here for respect, honor, or show is described as rajasic—unstable and fleeting.
vishnu_gita::281.translation_literal: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं (for respect, honor, and worship) / तपो (austerity) / दम्भेन (with hypocrisy) / चैव (also) / यत् (that which) / क्रियते (is performed) / तदिह (here) / प्रोक्तं (said) / राजसं (rajasic) / चलम् (unstable) / अध्रुवम् (fleeting)
vishnu_gita::281.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::281.essence: Effort done for show is unstable and quickly fades away.
vishnu_gita::281.simple_meaning: Doing spiritual practices only to gain respect or praise is unstable and temporary.
vishnu_gita::281.simple_insight: You feel the emptiness when your actions are only for others' approval.
vishnu_gita::281.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when austerity or spiritual discipline is done merely for social recognition or to appear pious, it is called rajasic—marked by instability and impermanence. Such efforts lack true depth and do not endure.
vishnu_gita::281.modern_relevance: You work hard just to impress others, but the feeling of emptiness remains once the applause fades.
vishnu_gita::281.insight: It teaches you to examine your motivation, shifting from seeking approval to authentic inner commitment.

vishnu_gita::282.verse_sanskrit:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत् पीड़या क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थम्वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम ॥
vishnu_gita::282.verse_hindi: अविवेक के वश होकर दूसरों के नाश के वा आत्मपीड़ा के द्वारा जो तपस्या की जाती है उसको तामस कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::282.english_translation: When suffering or austerity is performed out of ignorance or to harm others, it is called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::282.translation_literal: मूढग्राहेण (by ignorance) आत्मनो (of the self) यत् (that) पीड़या (by suffering) क्रियते (is done) तपः (austerity) परस्योत्सादनार्थम्वा (or for causing harm to others) तत्तामसमुदाहृतम (that is called tamasic)
vishnu_gita::282.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::282.essence: Discipline that arises from ignorance or harm to others is false and dark.
vishnu_gita::282.simple_meaning: Discipline or austerity done in ignorance or to hurt others is harmful and considered tamasic.
vishnu_gita::282.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that true effort respects both yourself and others.
vishnu_gita::282.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that austerity performed either ignorantly or to cause harm to others is tamasic, meaning it is rooted in darkness and confusion rather than true inner strength or clarity.
vishnu_gita::282.modern_relevance: Trying to push yourself through pain or to hurt others never leads to true growth or peace.
vishnu_gita::282.insight: It shifts your practice from harmful self-punishment to respectful, conscious effort that supports all beings.

vishnu_gita::283.verse_sanskrit:
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् ।
अफलपेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::283.verse_hindi: निष्काम व्यक्तियों के द्वारा नियमितरूप से विहित, आसक्तिशून्य और रागद्वेषरहित होकर जो कर्म किया जाता है उसे सात्त्विक कर्म कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::283.english_translation: Action performed regularly by selfless persons, free from attachment, desire, and hatred, is called pure (sattvic) action.
vishnu_gita::283.translation_literal: नियतं (regularly) / सङ्गरहित (without attachment) / मरागद्वेषतः (without desire and hatred) / कृतम् (done) / अफलपेप्सुना (without craving fruit) / कर्म (action) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / सात्त्विकम् (pure) / उच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::283.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::283.essence: Pure action is steady, selfless, and free from craving and hatred.
vishnu_gita::283.simple_meaning: Regular actions done without attachment, desire, or hatred, and without expecting results, are pure and good.
vishnu_gita::283.simple_insight: You can find peace in acting steadily without clinging to outcomes or feelings.
vishnu_gita::283.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that actions performed regularly by people who are free from attachment, desire, and hatred, and who do not expect rewards, are considered pure actions. This steadiness defines the best kind of action.
vishnu_gita::283.modern_relevance: You keep doing your tasks each day without obsessing over praise or blame, finding calm in steady effort.
vishnu_gita::283.insight: It shifts your focus from craving outcomes to steady, balanced action without emotional disturbance.

vishnu_gita::284.verse_sanskrit:
यत्तु कामेपमुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।
क्रियते वहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::284.verse_hindi: फलाकांक्षी अथवा अहंकारयुक्त व्यक्तियों के द्वारा बहुत प्रयास से जो कर्म किया जाता है उसको राजस कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::284.english_translation: Actions done with desire or ego-driven effort are called rajasic.
vishnu_gita::284.translation_literal: यत् (that which) / तु (indeed) / कामे (with desire) / अपि (also) / मुना (by) / कर्म (action) / साहङ्कारेण (with ego) / वा (or) / पुनः (again) / क्रियते (is done) / वहुलायासं (with much effort) / तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् (that is called rajasic)
vishnu_gita::284.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::284.essence: Effort driven by desire or ego creates restless, rajasic action.
vishnu_gita::284.simple_meaning: Actions performed with craving or ego involve intense effort and are called rajasic nature.
vishnu_gita::284.simple_insight: You can feel how desire or ego unsettles your efforts and makes them heavy.
vishnu_gita::284.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when a person acts motivated by craving or a sense of ego, their actions require much effort and are labeled rajasic, reflecting a restless and agitated nature.
vishnu_gita::284.modern_relevance: You push hard on projects because you want praise or to prove yourself, making your work feel heavy and restless.
vishnu_gita::284.insight: It teaches you to notice when desire or ego drives your effort, so you can shift toward calmer action.

vishnu_gita::285.verse_sanskrit:
अनुबन्ध भयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::285.verse_hindi: परिणाम में बन्धन, नाश, हिंसा और सामर्थ्य इन सबकी उपेक्षा करके मोहवश जो कर्म प्रारम्भ किया जाता है उसको तामस कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::285.english_translation: Actions begun out of delusion, ignoring bondage, destruction, violence, and strength, are called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::285.translation_literal: अनुबन्ध (bondage) / भयं (fear) / हिंसा (violence) / अनपेक्ष्य (ignoring) / च (and) / पौरुषम् (strength) / मोहात् (out of delusion) / आरभ्यते (is begun) / कर्म (action) / यत् (that) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (tamasic) / उच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::285.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::285.essence: Actions begun in delusion, ignoring harm or strength, are tamasic in nature.
vishnu_gita::285.simple_meaning: When you act out of confusion, ignoring harm, consequences, or your strength, your actions are called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::285.simple_insight: It feels unsettling to realize some actions come from confusion, not clear purpose.
vishnu_gita::285.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that actions started from delusion without regard for harm, destruction, or one's own power are tamasic, reflecting confused motivation that leads away from wise conduct.
vishnu_gita::285.modern_relevance: You might rush into decisions ignoring risks or your true capacity, acting from confusion rather than clarity.
vishnu_gita::285.insight: Recognize when confusion drives your actions and choose clarity to avoid harm.

vishnu_gita::286.verse_sanskrit:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहवाडी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः।
सिद्भयसिद्धयोनिर्विकारः कर्त्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::286.verse_hindi: आसक्तिशून्य, "अहं" इस अभिमान से शून्य धैर्य और उत्साहयुक्त, सिद्धि और असिद्धि में विकारशून्य कर्ता सात्त्विक कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::286.english_translation: A detached doer, free from the pride of 'I', with steady patience and enthusiasm, untainted by success or failure, is called sattvic.
vishnu_gita::286.translation_literal: मुक्तसङ्गो (detached) / अनहवाडी (without ego-pride) / धृति (patience) / उत्साह (enthusiasm) / समन्वितः (endowed with) / सिद्भय (success and failure) / सिद्ध (success) / अयोनिः (source) / विकारः (disturbance) / कर्त्ता (doer) / सात्त्विक (sattvic) / उच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::286.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::286.essence: A true doer acts with calm patience and joy, free of ego and outcome.
vishnu_gita::286.simple_meaning: You are steady and enthusiastic without pride or attachment, unaffected by success or failure. This balanced doer is called sattvic.
vishnu_gita::286.simple_insight: There's peace in acting without ego or worry about winning or losing.
vishnu_gita::286.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a person who acts without ego or pride, maintaining patience and enthusiasm. This person is not disturbed by success or failure, embodying the sattvic nature of balanced action.
vishnu_gita::286.modern_relevance: You face a challenge with calm patience and energy, not obsessed with winning or losing, simply doing your best.
vishnu_gita::286.insight: It shifts your focus from ego and outcomes to steady, joyful effort in the present moment.

vishnu_gita::287.verse_sanskrit:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुलुब्धो हिमात्मकोऽशुचिः।
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्त्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
vishnu_gita::287.verse_hindi: विषयानुरागी, कर्म फलाकांक्षी, लोभी, हिंसाशील, अशुचि, लाभा लाभ में आनन्द और विषादयुक्त कर्ता राजस कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::287.english_translation: One who is attached to sense objects, desires the fruits of actions, is greedy, violent, impure, and experiences joy and sorrow as the doer is called rajasic.
vishnu_gita::287.translation_literal: रागी (attached) / कर्मफलप्रेप्सु (desiring the fruits of actions) / लुब्धः (greedy) / हिमात्मकः (violent) / अशुचिः (impure) / हर्षशोकान्वितः (endowed with joy and sorrow) / कर्त्ता (doer) / राजसः (rajasic) / परिकीर्तितः (called)
vishnu_gita::287.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::287.essence: Desire and craving make you a restless doer caught in emotional extremes.
vishnu_gita::287.simple_meaning: If you are attached to things, want rewards, act greedily or violently, and feel happiness and sadness as the doer, you are driven by rajasic energy.
vishnu_gita::287.simple_insight: Recognize how desire pulls you between pleasure and pain, keeping you restless in action.
vishnu_gita::287.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a person caught in desire for outcomes who acts with greed and violence. Such a person is impure and experiences emotional highs and lows, labeled rajasic, reflecting restless and reactive nature.
vishnu_gita::287.modern_relevance: You find yourself chasing rewards, swinging between excitement and disappointment as you act with craving and impatience.
vishnu_gita::287.insight: See how craving creates emotional ups and downs and fuels restless, impure actions.

vishnu_gita::288.verse_sanskrit:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठोऽनष्कृतिकोऽलसः।
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::288.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियासक्त, विवेकहीन, उद्धत; शठ, निष्कृति-शून्य, आलस्य युक्त, विषाद युक्त और दीर्घसूत्री का तामस कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::288.english_translation: The one who is unprepared, natural in ignorance, motionless, deceitful, without initiative, lazy, full of despair and long-winded is called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::288.translation_literal: अयुक्तः (unprepared) / प्राकृतः (natural) / स्तब्धः (motionless) / शठः (deceitful) / अनष्कृतिको (without initiative) / अलसः (lazy) / विषादी (full of despair) / दीर्घसूत्री (long-winded) / च (and) / कर्ता (doer) / तामस (tamasic) / उच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::288.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::288.essence: Inertia, despair, and laziness together create a state that clouds clear action and knowing.
vishnu_gita::288.simple_meaning: When you are inactive, confused, lazy, and full of despair, these qualities reflect a tamasic nature.
vishnu_gita::288.simple_insight: Recognize how laziness and despair cloud your mind and stop you from moving forward.
vishnu_gita::288.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the tamasic state: a person trapped in confusion, inactivity, and despair, lacking drive and clarity. This state blocks progress on the path and clouds the mind.
vishnu_gita::288.modern_relevance: You sit frozen, overwhelmed by negative thoughts and apathy, unable to start the work you care about.
vishnu_gita::288.insight: It teaches you to identify and move beyond inertia and despair, which block your natural energy.

vishnu_gita::289.verse_sanskrit:
उपास्तेः प्राणरूपा या भक्तिः प्रोक्ता दिवौकसः !।
गुणत्रयानुसारेण सा त्रिधा वर्तते ननु ॥
vishnu_gita::289.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! उपासना की जो प्राणरूपा भक्ति कही गई है वह भक्ति तीन गुणों के अनुसार निश्चय तीन प्रकार की है
vishnu_gita::289.english_translation: O divine beings! The devotion that is the life force of worship is indeed threefold, according to the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::289.translation_literal: उपास्तेः (of worship) प्राणरूपा (life-form) या (which) भक्तिः (devotion) प्रोक्ता (is said) दिवौकसः (O divine beings) ! / गुणत्रयानुसारेण (according to three qualities) सा (that) त्रिधा (threefold) वर्तते (exists) ननु (indeed) ॥
vishnu_gita::289.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::289.essence: Devotion naturally expresses itself in three distinct forms shaped by fundamental qualities.
vishnu_gita::289.simple_meaning: Devotion, the vital energy of worship, naturally appears in three forms based on different qualities.
vishnu_gita::289.simple_insight: Knowing your devotion can take different natural forms opens your heart to its true diversity.
vishnu_gita::289.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses divine beings explaining that devotion—the essential force behind worship—manifests in three distinct types, each linked to one of the three fundamental qualities (gunas) of nature. This sets the stage for understanding diverse expressions of true love.
vishnu_gita::289.modern_relevance: When you notice how your feelings of devotion or care change with your mood or environment, you glimpse these three natural forms at work within you.
vishnu_gita::289.insight: Recognize that devotion is not one fixed feeling but varies naturally with your inner qualities and circumstances.

vishnu_gita::290.verse_sanskrit:
आर्त्तनां तामसी सा स्याजिज्ञामूनाञ्च राजसी।
सात्त्विक्यार्थिनां ज्ञेया उत्तमा सोत्तरोत्तरा ॥
vishnu_gita::290.verse_hindi: आर्तभक्तों की भक्ति तामसी, जिज्ञासु भक्तों की भक्ति राजसी और अर्थार्थी भक्तों की भक्ति सात्त्विकी जानना चाहिये। इन तीन प्रकार की भक्तियों मे उत्तरोतर श्रेष्ठ है
vishnu_gita::290.english_translation: Devotion of the distressed is tamasic, of the curious is rajasic, and of those seeking meaning is sattvic; the latter is progressively superior.
vishnu_gita::290.translation_literal: आर्तनां (of the distressed) तामसी (tamasic) सा (that) स्याजिज्ञामूनाञ्च (and of the curious) राजसी (rajasic) सात्त्विक्यार्थिनां (of those seeking meaning, sattvic) ज्ञेया (should be known) उत्तमा (excellent) सोत्तरोत्तरा (and progressively superior)
vishnu_gita::290.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::290.essence: Devotion evolves from confusion and restlessness toward a clear, meaningful, and superior form.
vishnu_gita::290.simple_meaning: There are three kinds of devotion: arising from suffering (dark and confusing), from restless curiosity (active but unsettled), and from seeking true meaning (clear and pure). The last is the highest form.
vishnu_gita::290.simple_insight: You can feel your devotion deepen as it moves from pain or restlessness toward clear purpose.
vishnu_gita::290.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains three qualities of devotion: tamasic devotion comes from suffering and confusion, rajasic from restless questioning, and sattvic from sincere seeking of deeper meaning. Among these, devotion driven by true understanding is the most elevated.
vishnu_gita::290.modern_relevance: When your feelings push you to seek support out of pain or curiosity, your devotion feels unstable. But when you find deeper purpose, your commitment calms and strengthens.
vishnu_gita::290.insight: It teaches you to recognize your devotion’s quality and gently guide it from restlessness or pain toward meaningful clarity.

vishnu_gita::291.verse_sanskrit:
भूतप्रेतपिशाचादीनासुरं भावमाश्रितान् ।
अर्चन्ति तामसा भक्ता नित्यं तद्गावभाविताः ॥
vishnu_gita::291.verse_hindi: तामसिक भक्त आसुरीसंपत्ति युक्त भूत प्रेत पिशाचादि की उपासना तत्तद्भावों में भावित होकर नित्य करते हैं
vishnu_gita::291.english_translation: Devotees influenced by darkness constantly worship beings like ghosts, spirits, and shadowy forces, absorbed in their own states.
vishnu_gita::291.translation_literal: भूतप्रेतपिशाचादीनासुरं (ghosts-spirits-demons-like) भावमाश्रितान् (relying on mood) । अर्चन्ति (worship) तामसा (by darkness) भक्ता (devotees) नित्यं (always) तद्गावभाविताः (absorbed in that mood) ॥
vishnu_gita::291.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::291.essence: Your inner mood shapes the objects of your devotion and worship.
vishnu_gita::291.simple_meaning: Your feelings and inner state determine what you devote yourself to and what you worship.
vishnu_gita::291.simple_insight: Your devotion reflects your inner moods, shaping what you focus your love and attention on.
vishnu_gita::291.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that devotees influenced by darkness (tamas) worship shadowy, fearsome beings, reflecting their inner states rather than pure devotion. Their worship arises from their absorbed moods, not clarity or higher vision.
vishnu_gita::291.modern_relevance: When your mind is clouded with fear or confusion, you might find yourself drawn to harmful habits or negative influences without realizing it.
vishnu_gita::291.insight: Recognize how your emotional state directs your focus and devotion, and choose to cultivate clarity to uplift your attention.

vishnu_gita::292.verse_sanskrit:
सकामा राजसा ये म्युः ऋषीन पितृश्च देवताः।
वह्वीदैवदेवीश्च मे शक्तीः पूजयन्तीह ते सदा ॥
vishnu_gita::292.verse_hindi: सकाम राजसिक भक्त ऋषि देवता और पितर एवं मेरी बहुत सी दैवी शक्तियों की उपासना सदा करते हैं
vishnu_gita::292.english_translation: Desiring and passionate devotees like sages, deities, ancestors, and many divine energies always worship me.
vishnu_gita::292.translation_literal: सकामा (with desire) राजसा (passionate) ये (those) म्युः (like) ऋषीन (sages) पितृश्च (and ancestors) देवताः (deities) वह्वीदैवदेवीश्च (and many divine energies) मे (my) शक्तीः (powers) पूजयन्तीह (always worship) ते (they)
vishnu_gita::292.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::292.essence: Passionate longing draws many beings to devotedly honor the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::292.simple_meaning: Many beings filled with desire and passion, including sages, ancestors, and divine forces, always worship the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::292.simple_insight: You are deeply loved and sought after by many who long for connection.
vishnu_gita::292.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that beings driven by desire and passion—sages, deities, ancestors, and divine powers—consistently direct their worship toward him, showing the natural pull of devoted love.
vishnu_gita::292.modern_relevance: When you feel drawn to someone or something deeply, you are joining a long tradition of devoted attention flowing toward what moves the heart.
vishnu_gita::292.insight: It teaches you that devotion naturally arises from longing and passion, connecting you to the larger flow of dedicated love.

vishnu_gita::293.verse_sanskrit:
केवलं सात्त्विका ये स्युर्मद्भक्ताः साधका इह।
त एवं ज्ञात्वा मद्रूपं मम भक्तौ सदा रताः॥
vishnu_gita::293.verse_hindi: इस संसार में केवल जो साधक मेरे सात्त्विक भक्त है वह ही मेरे रूप को जानकर सदा मेरी भक्ति में तत्पर रहते हैं
vishnu_gita::293.english_translation: Only those devotees who are pure and sattvic can truly know my form and remain always devoted to me.
vishnu_gita::293.translation_literal: केवलं (only) सात्त्विका (pure/sattvic) ये (those who) स्यु: (are) मद्भक्ताः (my devotees) साधका (practitioners) इह (here). त (that) एवं (thus) ज्ञात्वा (knowing) मद्रूपं (my form) मम (my) भक्तौ (in devotion) सदा (always) रताः (engaged).
vishnu_gita::293.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::293.essence: Pure, sattvic devotion is the key that reveals and sustains connection with the divine form.
vishnu_gita::293.simple_meaning: Only pure and sincere devotees can truly recognize the divine form and remain devoted continuously.
vishnu_gita::293.simple_insight: You feel steady and close when your devotion is pure and clear.
vishnu_gita::293.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that among all seekers, only those whose devotion is pure and sattvic truly perceive his divine form and stay constantly engaged in loving devotion. This highlights the importance of inner purity in spiritual connection.
vishnu_gita::293.modern_relevance: When your intentions are pure and your heart open, you naturally connect deeply with what matters most.
vishnu_gita::293.insight: It teaches you that sincere, pure devotion is what reveals deeper spiritual realities and keeps your commitment alive.

vishnu_gita::294.verse_sanskrit:
पंचाना सगुणानां ते मद्रूपाणा स्माश्रयात ।
मद्धयानमग्नास्तिष्टन्ति निर्गुणं हाथवा मम ॥
vishnu_gita::294.verse_hindi: वह मेरे मेरे पांच सगुण रूपों के आश्रय से मेरे ध्यान में मग्न रहते हैं अथवा मेरे निर्गण परमभावरूप
vishnu_gita::294.english_translation: The five with attributes take refuge in my forms, and the rest, without attributes, remain absorbed in my essence.
vishnu_gita::294.translation_literal: पञ्चाना (five) सगुणानां (with attributes) ते (they) मद्रूपाणा (my-forms) स्माश्रयात (take refuge) । मद्धयानम् (in my meditation) अग्नास्तिष्टन्ति (remain absorbed) निर्गुणं (without attributes) हाथवा (others) मम (my) ॥
vishnu_gita::294.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::294.essence: Connection to the divine happens through either form with qualities or formlessness without them.
vishnu_gita::294.simple_meaning: Some beings focus on the divine with qualities, while others are absorbed in the divine without qualities.
vishnu_gita::294.simple_insight: You can connect with the divine through form or formlessness, both are valid paths.
vishnu_gita::294.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that some beings take refuge in his five forms that have qualities, while others remain absorbed in his formless, attribute-free essence. This highlights different approaches to experiencing the divine reality.
vishnu_gita::294.modern_relevance: Sometimes you relate to a clear image or idea of what matters; other times, you connect through silence and openness beyond form.
vishnu_gita::294.insight: It teaches you to accept diverse ways of relating to the divine—through concrete forms or abstract essence.

vishnu_gita::295.verse_sanskrit:
सच्चिदानन्दभावं तं भावं परममाश्रिताः।
मम ध्यानाम्बुधौ मग्ना नन्दन्ति नितरां सुराः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::295.verse_hindi: उस सच्चिदानन्द भावका आश्रय करके मेरे ध्यानरूप समुद्र मे मग्न होकर हे देवगण! अंत्यंत आनंद उपभोग करते हैं
vishnu_gita::295.english_translation: Those who take refuge in that supreme state of truth, consciousness, and bliss, immersed in the ocean of my meditation, delight immensely, O celestial beings!
vishnu_gita::295.translation_literal: सच्चिदानन्दभावं (truth-consciousness-bliss-state) / तं (that) / भावं (state) / परममाश्रिताः (supreme refuge) / मम (my) / ध्यानाम्बुधौ (meditation-ocean) / मग्ना (immersed) / नन्दन्ति (rejoice) / नितरां (greatly) / सुराः (celestial beings)
vishnu_gita::295.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::295.essence: Deep immersion in the supreme meditation brings boundless joy to those who seek refuge.
vishnu_gita::295.simple_meaning: When you take refuge in the supreme state of truth, consciousness, and bliss and immerse yourself deeply in meditation on the divine, you experience great joy.
vishnu_gita::295.simple_insight: There is profound happiness when you lose yourself in deep meditation on the divine.
vishnu_gita::295.detailed_meaning: Vishnu tells celestial beings that those who take refuge in the supreme state of pure truth, consciousness, and bliss and immerse themselves in his meditation experience immense joy. This moment highlights the blissful reward of devoted meditation.
vishnu_gita::295.modern_relevance: You sit quietly, fully focused, and suddenly feel a wave of deep joy that nothing else can bring.
vishnu_gita::295.insight: It teaches you that surrendering fully to meditation opens the way to profound joy beyond ordinary pleasure.

vishnu_gita::296.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानी भक्तस्तु भगवद्र्प एव मतो यतः।
गुणातीतस्य तस्यात्र न निवेशो विधीयते ॥
vishnu_gita::296.verse_hindi: और चतुर्थ ज्ञानी भक्त तो भगवद्रपही है क्योंकि वह गुणातीत है अतः उसका यहां विचार नहीं किया गया है
vishnu_gita::296.english_translation: A wise devotee is truly like the supreme being because they transcend qualities and are not considered here.
vishnu_gita::296.translation_literal: ज्ञानी (wise) भक्तस्तु (devotee indeed) भगवद्र्प (like the supreme being) एव (indeed) मतो (considered) यतः (because) गुणातीतस्य (of one beyond qualities) तस्यात्र (here) न (not) निवेशो (consideration) विधीयते (is made)
vishnu_gita::296.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::296.essence: Transcending qualities makes a devotee indistinguishable from the supreme being.
vishnu_gita::296.simple_meaning: A wise devotee transcends all qualities and is seen as one with the supreme being.
vishnu_gita::296.simple_insight: You feel connected to the highest reality when you go beyond your traits and limitations.
vishnu_gita::296.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a devotee who has transcended the three qualities is regarded as identical to the supreme being, so such a person is beyond ordinary consideration in this context.
vishnu_gita::296.modern_relevance: When you stop identifying with your moods and habits, you experience a deep connection to something greater than yourself.
vishnu_gita::296.insight: It teaches you to recognize that transcending personal qualities aligns you with the highest essence beyond change.

vishnu_gita::297.verse_sanskrit:
श्रद्धावान् साधको यश्च भोगमैहिकमेव हि ।
विशेषतः समीहेत दम्भाहकारसंयुतः ॥
vishnu_gita::297.verse_hindi: जो श्रद्धावान् साधक ऐहलौकिक भोग की ही विशेषरूप से इच्छा करे, दम्भ और अहङ्कार से युक्त हो
vishnu_gita::297.english_translation: A sincere practitioner who especially desires worldly pleasures is bound by deceit and ego.
vishnu_gita::297.translation_literal: श्रद्धावान् (faithful) / साधको (practitioner) / यश्च (who) / भोगमैहिकमेव (worldly pleasures only) / हि (indeed) / विशेषतः (especially) / समीहेत (desires) / दम्भाहकारसंयुतः (attached to deceit and ego)
vishnu_gita::297.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::297.essence: Focusing faith on worldly pleasure binds you to ego and deceit.
vishnu_gita::297.simple_meaning: If you focus your faith on seeking only worldly pleasures, you become attached to ego and falsehood.
vishnu_gita::297.simple_insight: You feel trapped when craving earthly rewards because ego and deceit cling tightly.
vishnu_gita::297.detailed_meaning: Vishnu warns that a sincere spiritual seeker who desires only temporary worldly pleasures becomes entangled in ego and deceit, which obstruct true progress on the path of renunciation and self-realization.
vishnu_gita::297.modern_relevance: You might find yourself chasing status or material things, not noticing how pride and illusion quietly grow inside you.
vishnu_gita::297.insight: It shifts your focus from deeper purpose to surface desires, strengthening ego and false appearances.

vishnu_gita::298.verse_sanskrit:
इष्टं वेदविधि हित्वा मदुपासनतत्परः ।
विज्ञेयो लक्षणादस्मात् तामसः स उपासकः ॥
vishnu_gita::298.verse_hindi: और उपयुक्त वेदविधि का त्याग करके मेरी उपासना में तत्पर हो, इन लक्षणों से उस उपासक को तामसिक उपासक जानना चाहिये
vishnu_gita::298.english_translation: One who abandons the prescribed Vedic rituals and eagerly devotes themselves to my worship is known by these signs as a tamasic devotee.
vishnu_gita::298.translation_literal:
इष्टं (desired) वेदविधि (Vedic rituals) हित्वा (abandoning) मदुपासनतत्परः (eager for my worship) ।
विज्ञेयो (is to be known) लक्षणात् (by signs) अस्मात् (from this) तामसः (tamasic) स (that) उपासकः (worshipper) ॥
vishnu_gita::298.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::298.essence: True devotion includes respecting proper practice, not just eager worship alone.
vishnu_gita::298.simple_meaning: Giving up correct rituals yet focusing only on worship without understanding is a sign of a tamasic (ignorant or dull) devotee.
vishnu_gita::298.simple_insight: Devotion without clear practice can hide confusion, not true connection.
vishnu_gita::298.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a devotee who ignores the proper Vedic methods but focuses solely on worship with attachment shows tamasic qualities. This warns against blind devotion lacking wisdom or discipline.
vishnu_gita::298.modern_relevance: You might focus on passion or desire in your practice but miss the essential habits and understanding that give it true power.
vishnu_gita::298.insight: It teaches you to balance heartfelt devotion with disciplined, wise practice to avoid falling into confusion.

vishnu_gita::299.verse_sanskrit:
यः श्रद्धालुर्विशेषेण पारलौकिकमेव हि।
सुखमिच्छंस्तथा शीलगुणराशियुतो यदि ॥
vishnu_gita::299.verse_hindi: जो श्रद्धालु साधक पारलौकिक सुख को ही विशेषरूप से चाहता हुआ यदि शीलगुणों से युक्त होकर
vishnu_gita::299.english_translation: If a devoted practitioner especially desires only worldly happiness and is attached to qualities of character,
vishnu_gita::299.translation_literal: यः (who) श्रद्धालुर्विशेषेण (devoted especially) पारलौकिकमेव (only worldly) हि (indeed) सुखमिच्छंस्तथा (desires happiness also) शीलगुणराशियुतो (endowed with qualities of character) यदि (if)
vishnu_gita::299.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::299.essence: Devotion can begin with sincere desire for worldly happiness combined with virtuous qualities.
vishnu_gita::299.simple_meaning: A sincere person who mainly wants worldly happiness but has good qualities is still devoted.
vishnu_gita::299.simple_insight: It's okay to begin with simple desires; devotion can start there.
vishnu_gita::299.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a sincere seeker who, though focused on worldly happiness and possessing virtues, is still on the path of devotion, showing that devotion can begin from everyday desires.
vishnu_gita::299.modern_relevance: You care deeply about success and good character; this natural start is a doorway to deeper devotion.
vishnu_gita::299.insight: Recognize that devotion begins with honest, even worldly, desires combined with good character.

vishnu_gita::300.verse_sanskrit:
वेदानुसारतः सक्तो मदुपास्तौ हि साधकः।
राजसः स हि विज्ञेय उपासक इति स्मृतिः ॥
vishnu_gita::300.verse_hindi: वेदविधि के अनुसार मेरी उपासना में आसक्त रहता है तो उसको राजसिक उपासक जानना चाहिये, ऐसा स्मृतिकारों का मत है
vishnu_gita::300.english_translation: According to the Vedas, one who is attached to worshiping me is to be known as a rajasic worshiper, say the scriptures.
vishnu_gita::300.translation_literal: वेदानुसारतः (according to the Vedas) सक्तो (attached) मदुपास्तौ (to me worshiping) हि (indeed) साधकः (practitioner) । राजसः (rajasic) स (he) हि (indeed) विज्ञेय (to be known) उपासक (worshiper) इति (thus) स्मृतिः (scripture) ॥
vishnu_gita::300.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::300.essence: Attachment in worship reveals a restless, desire-driven devotion, not true surrender.
vishnu_gita::300.simple_meaning: When someone worships with attachment, scriptures say that person follows rajasic devotion, driven by desire and restlessness.
vishnu_gita::300.simple_insight: Knowing your worship style helps you move toward freer, deeper devotion.
vishnu_gita::300.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that according to Vedic tradition, if a devotee clings to their worship with attachment, they are classified as rajasic—motivated by desire and restlessness rather than pure devotion. This distinction guides seekers toward more sincere spiritual practice.
vishnu_gita::300.modern_relevance: You might find yourself clinging to how your efforts are recognized or rewarded, which shows rajasic tendencies in your devotion or work.
vishnu_gita::300.insight: Recognize attachment in your devotion or efforts as a sign to shift from desire-driven actions to freer, selfless practice.

vishnu_gita::301.verse_sanskrit:
सात्त्विक्या श्रद्धया युक्तो भाग्यवान विबुधर्षभाः ।
वितृष्णो लोकिकादागात्तद्द्वै पारलौकिकात् ॥
vishnu_gita::301.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्टों ! जो भाग्यवान् साधक सात्त्विकी श्रद्धा से युक्त होकर ऐहलौकिक और पारलौकिक भोगों की तृष्णा से रहित होता हुआ
vishnu_gita::301.english_translation: O best of the divine beings! The fortunate practitioner with pure faith is free from craving both worldly and beyond-worldly pleasures.
vishnu_gita::301.translation_literal: सात्त्विक्या (with pure) श्रद्धया (faith) युक्तो (joined) भाग्यवान (fortunate) विबुधर्षभाः (best of divine beings) । वितृष्णो (free from craving) लोकिक (worldly) आद (and) आगत्त (beyond) द्वै (both) पारलौकिकात् (beyond-worldly) ॥
vishnu_gita::301.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::301.essence: Pure faith frees you from craving both worldly and spiritual pleasures.
vishnu_gita::301.simple_meaning: Having pure and sincere trust helps you let go of desires for both worldly and spiritual pleasures.
vishnu_gita::301.simple_insight: Trusting fully brings relief from wanting and craving everything around you.
vishnu_gita::301.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the highest divine beings, teaching that those who cultivate pure faith become free from desires tied to both material and spiritual enjoyments, marking a key step on the devotional path.
vishnu_gita::301.modern_relevance: You feel stuck wanting success or recognition, but pure trust can free you from chasing every reward.
vishnu_gita::301.insight: It shifts your focus from craving outcomes to resting in steady trust, calming restless desires.

vishnu_gita::302.verse_sanskrit:
साधकोऽनन्यया वृत्या ज्ञानतो निरतः सदा ।
मदुपास्तौ स विज्ञेयः सात्त्विकोपासको वरः॥
vishnu_gita::302.verse_hindi: ज्ञानपूर्वक अनन्यवृत्ति से मेरी उपासना में सदा तत्पर रहता है उसको श्रेष्ठ सात्त्विक उपासक जानना चाहिये
vishnu_gita::302.english_translation: One who is devoted to me with exclusive focus and always absorbed in knowledge is to be known as the best sattvic devotee.
vishnu_gita::302.translation_literal: साधकोऽनन्यया (the seeker with exclusive) / वृत्या (conduct) / ज्ञानतो (from knowledge) / निरतः (engaged) / सदा (always) / मदुपास्तौ (in my worship) / स (that one) / विज्ञेयः (should be known) / सात्त्विकोपासको (sattvic devotee) / वरः (best)
vishnu_gita::302.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::302.essence: Exclusive focus combined with knowledge defines the highest form of devotion.
vishnu_gita::302.simple_meaning: The best devotee is one who worships with full, exclusive focus and is always absorbed in knowledge.
vishnu_gita::302.simple_insight: There is strength and clarity in combining deep focus with understanding in devotion.
vishnu_gita::302.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the ideal devotee as someone who dedicates themselves to worship with undivided attention and is always engaged in knowledge, showing that devotion combined with wisdom is supreme.
vishnu_gita::302.modern_relevance: When you dedicate yourself fully to a passion or belief, grounding it in clear understanding, you become truly exceptional.
vishnu_gita::302.insight: Shift your devotion from scattered attention to focused knowledge, deepening your connection profoundly.

vishnu_gita::303.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।
अविभक्तं विभक्तेपु तज़ज्ञानं वित्त सात्त्विकम् ॥
vishnu_gita::303.verse_hindi: जिस ज्ञान के द्वारा विभक्त रूप सब भूतों में अविभक्त, एक और विकारहीन भाव ज्ञानी देखता है उस ज्ञान को सात्त्विक ज्ञान जानना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::303.english_translation: The knowledge by which a knower sees the undivided, one, and unchanging essence in all beings, beyond their divided forms and faults, is called sattvic knowledge.
vishnu_gita::303.translation_literal: सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) येनैकं (by which one) भावम् (essence) अव्ययम् (unchanging) ईक्षते (sees) । अविभक्तं (undivided) विभक्ते (divided) अपि (even) तज्ज्ञानं (that knowledge) सात्त्विकम् (pure) ॥
vishnu_gita::303.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::303.essence: True knowledge is seeing one pure essence beyond all divided forms and faults.
vishnu_gita::303.simple_meaning: You can know a pure kind of wisdom when you see the same unchanging essence in every being, beyond their many forms and faults.
vishnu_gita::303.simple_insight: There is comfort in realizing all beings share a single, pure essence beneath appearances.
vishnu_gita::303.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that true wisdom is seeing the undivided, unchanging essence that underlies all beings, regardless of their diverse forms or flaws. This pure vision is called sattvic knowledge, reflecting clarity beyond surface differences.
vishnu_gita::303.modern_relevance: When you stop judging others by their flaws and see the shared essence in everyone, relationships and understanding deepen.
vishnu_gita::303.insight: This verse teaches you to shift your perception from external differences to the unified essence beneath.

vishnu_gita::304.verse_sanskrit:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान् पृवविधान् ।
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पञ्च तत्तामममुदाहृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::304.verse_hindi: जो ज्ञान पृथक रूप से सभी प्राणियों मे पृथक पृथक अनेकों प्रकार के भाव जानता है उस ज्ञान को राजसिक ज्ञान जानना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::304.english_translation: Knowledge that separately perceives many different qualities in all beings is called rajasic knowledge.
vishnu_gita::304.translation_literal: पृथक्त्वेन (separately) / तु (but) / यत् (that) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / नानाभावान् (many different qualities) / पृवविधान् (in beings) / अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पञ्च (and also a little of the true meaning) / तत्तामममुदाहृतम् (that alone is called supreme)
vishnu_gita::304.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::304.essence: Knowing many separate qualities is incomplete knowledge, lacking deeper unity.
vishnu_gita::304.simple_meaning: Knowing many things as separate and different is a kind of knowledge, but it doesn’t see the whole truth.
vishnu_gita::304.simple_insight: You might know many details but still miss the deeper reality beneath them all.
vishnu_gita::304.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when knowledge focuses only on many separate qualities in beings, it is incomplete and called rajasic knowledge. This moment contrasts surface knowledge with deeper insight into the true nature of reality.
vishnu_gita::304.modern_relevance: When you focus on differences and categories in people or situations, you might miss the full, connected picture underneath.
vishnu_gita::304.insight: It teaches you to see beyond separate appearances to grasp deeper unity.

vishnu_gita::305.verse_sanskrit:
यत्तु कृत्सनवदेकास्मिन कार्य सक्तमहैतुकम ।
अत्त्तार्वथवादाल्पन्च्य तत्तामसमुदाहृतं ॥
vishnu_gita::305.verse_hindi: जो एक कार्य में परिपूर्णवत् आसक्त, हेतुशून्य, परमार्थरहित और अल्प अर्थात् तुच्छ ज्ञान है उसको तामस ज्ञान कहते है
vishnu_gita::305.english_translation: The knowledge that is completely attached to a single action, without reason, lacking true purpose, and is small or insignificant is called tamasic knowledge.
vishnu_gita::305.translation_literal: यत् (that which) तु (indeed) कृत्सनवत् (completely/fully) एकस्मिन् (in one) कार्य (action) सक्तम् (attached) अहैतुकम् (without cause/reason) अत्त (and) तात्थव (true/reality) वाद (speech/knowledge) अल्पञ्च (and small) य (is) तत्तामसमुदाहृतं (called tamasic)
vishnu_gita::305.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::305.essence: Clinging blindly to one action without reason is shallow, tamasic knowledge.
vishnu_gita::305.simple_meaning: When your knowledge is fixed on just one action, without reason or deeper purpose, and is very limited, it is called tamasic knowledge.
vishnu_gita::305.simple_insight: It feels frustrating when your understanding feels stuck and narrow, blocking growth.
vishnu_gita::305.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains a kind of flawed knowledge that is entirely focused on a single action without understanding why, lacking deeper insight or purpose. This narrow, reasonless attachment is called tamasic knowledge, representing confusion and limitation in wisdom.
vishnu_gita::305.modern_relevance: When you insist on doing one thing your way without questioning or understanding why, your perspective shrinks and your growth stalls.
vishnu_gita::305.insight: It teaches you to notice when your focus is too narrow and encourages seeking broader, reasoned understanding.

vishnu_gita::306.verse_sanskrit:
सूरा: ! श्रुनुध्वमधुना सम्बन्धत्रिगुणस्य ह । 
अन्यान्यपि रहस्यानि कानिचिद्वर्णयाम्यहम् ॥
vishnu_gita::306.verse_hindi: हे देवगण! अब मैं त्रिगुणसम्बन्ध से सम्बंधित कुछ अन्य रहस्यों का कुछ वर्णन करता हूँ वह सुनिए
vishnu_gita::306.english_translation: O radiant beings! Now I will describe some other secrets related to the three qualities. Listen.
vishnu_gita::306.translation_literal: सूरा: (O radiant beings) / श्रुनुध्वमधुना (listen now) / सम्बन्धत्रिगुणस्य (of the relation of the three qualities) / ह (indeed) / अन्यान्यपि (some other) / रहस्यानि (secrets) / कानिचिद् (some) / वर्णयाम्यहम् (I describe)
vishnu_gita::306.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::306.essence: There are deeper secrets about the three qualities yet to be revealed.
vishnu_gita::306.simple_meaning: The speaker invites listeners to hear more secrets about the three qualities that govern nature and life.
vishnu_gita::306.simple_insight: There is always more to learn beyond what is already known.
vishnu_gita::306.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu addresses the radiant beings, preparing to reveal further mysteries about the three fundamental qualities (gunas) that influence all existence.
vishnu_gita::306.insight: It reminds you to stay open to deeper layers of understanding beyond initial knowledge.

vishnu_gita::307.verse_sanskrit:
सत्त्वावलम्बिनो यूयं शृण्वन्तो भवतादरात्।
सत्त्वं क्रमावर्द्धयदि स्त्रैगुण्ये च यत्यताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::307.verse_hindi: और आप उसको आदरपूर्वक सुनते हुए सत्वगुण अवलंबी होइए और क्रमशः सत्वगुण की वृद्धि करते हुए गुणातीत पद के लिये प्रयत्न करिये
vishnu_gita::307.english_translation: And you, respectfully listening, become devoted to the quality of goodness, gradually increasing it while striving for the state beyond the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::307.translation_literal: सत्त्वावलम्बिनो (devoted to goodness) / यूयं (you all) / शृण्वन्तो (listening) / भवतादरात् (with respect) / सत्त्वं (goodness) / क्रमावर्द्धयदि (gradually increase) / स्त्रैगुण्ये (in the three qualities) / च (and) / यत्यताम् (strive)
vishnu_gita::307.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::307.essence: You can steadily grow goodness while striving to transcend all qualities.
vishnu_gita::307.simple_meaning: Respectfully listen and embrace the quality of goodness. Gradually increase it by effort, aiming to move beyond all three qualities.
vishnu_gita::307.simple_insight: You can honor what is good in yourself and still keep reaching higher.
vishnu_gita::307.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs sincere listeners to adopt the quality of goodness (sattva) with respect and to steadily grow it, while also striving to transcend the three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas), pointing toward spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::307.modern_relevance: You recognize positive habits growing inside you and decide to nurture them while aiming for a deeper transformation beyond just good or bad traits.
vishnu_gita::307.insight: It teaches you to honor your current goodness while actively striving to surpass all limiting qualities.

vishnu_gita::308.verse_sanskrit:
अफलाकाङ्गिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते ।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥
vishnu_gita::308.verse_hindi: फल आकांशा रहित व्यक्ति "यज्ञानुष्ठान अवश्य कर्तव्य कर्म है। ऐसा विचार कर और मन को शांत करके जिस विधि विहित यज्ञ को करते हैं उसको सात्त्विक कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::308.english_translation: A person who performs the prescribed sacrifice without desire for results, with a calm and focused mind, is called sattvic.
vishnu_gita::308.translation_literal: अफलाकाङ्गिभिः (without desire for results) यज्ञः (sacrifice) विधिदृष्टः (prescribed by law) य (who) इज्यते (is performed) । यष्टव्यम् एव इति (must be performed indeed) मनः (mind) समाधाय (with calm focus) स (that) सात्त्विकः (pure/sattvic) ॥
vishnu_gita::308.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::308.essence: Act without desire for results; calm focus makes your action pure.
vishnu_gita::308.simple_meaning: You should perform your duties calmly and without wanting any reward; this kind of action is pure and right.
vishnu_gita::308.simple_insight: Peace grows when you act without craving the outcome, freeing your heart from restlessness.
vishnu_gita::308.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that sacrifices or duties must be performed as prescribed, but without expecting rewards. The mind focused calmly on the action, free from desire, makes the act pure or sattvic. This teaching guides Arjuna toward disciplined, selfless action.
vishnu_gita::308.modern_relevance: You finish a tough task without checking your phone for praise or results, simply focused on doing it well.
vishnu_gita::308.insight: It shifts your attention from chasing outcomes to holding steady focus on the action itself.

vishnu_gita::309.verse_sanskrit:
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते विबुधश्रेष्ठाः ! तं यज्ञ वित्त राजसम्  ॥
vishnu_gita::309.verse_hindi: किन्तु हे देवश्रेष्ठो ! फल मिलने के उद्देश्य से अथवा केवल अपने महत्त्व के प्रकट करने के अर्थ जो यज्ञ किया जाता है उस यज्ञ को राजस मानना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::309.english_translation: But O best of the radiant beings, a sacrifice performed with the intention of gaining a result or merely to show off should be considered of the rajasic nature.
