vishnu_gita::309.translation_literal: अभिसन्धाय (with intention) / तु (but) / फलं (fruit/result) / दम्भार्थमपि (even for showing off) / चैव (also) / यत् (that) / इज्यते (is performed) / विबुधश्रेष्ठाः (O best of the radiant beings) / तं (that) / यज्ञ (sacrifice) / वित्त (wealth) / राजसम् (rajasic/natured)
vishnu_gita::309.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::309.essence: Acting with desire or pride makes your action restless and attached.
vishnu_gita::309.simple_meaning: When you act only to get something or to appear important, your action is driven by restlessness and attachment.
vishnu_gita::309.simple_insight: You feel the weight of craving and pride clouding your true purpose.
vishnu_gita::309.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses a radiant being, teaching that sacrifices or actions done just to gain a result or to display importance belong to rajasic nature, marked by desire and ego rather than selfless purpose.
vishnu_gita::309.modern_relevance: You work hard to impress others or chase rewards, but that restless energy makes your efforts feel heavy and unsatisfying.
vishnu_gita::309.insight: Recognize when your motivation is desire or pride and shift towards acting for its own sake, freeing your effort from restlessness.

vishnu_gita::310.verse_sanskrit:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्ने मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥
vishnu_gita::310.verse_hindi: अन्नदानशून्य, मन्त्रहीन, दक्षिणाहीन और श्रद्धा रहित यज्ञ को तामस यज्ञ कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::310.english_translation: A sacrifice without food offering, without mantra, without gift, and without faith is called a tamasic sacrifice.
vishnu_gita::310.translation_literal: विधिहीनम् (without method) / असृष्टान् (without offering) / न (not) / मन्त्रहीनम् (without mantra) / अदक्षिणम् (without gift) / श्रद्धाविरहितम् (without faith) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / तामसम् (dark, tamasic) / परिचक्षते (is called)
vishnu_gita::310.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::310.essence: Actions without intention, support, or faith become empty and lifeless.
vishnu_gita::310.simple_meaning: A ritual without food, mantra, gift, or faith is empty and called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::310.simple_insight: Rituals without care or meaning feel hollow and ineffective.
vishnu_gita::310.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a sacrifice lacking essential elements: no food offering, no chanting, no gift, and no faith. Such a ritual is called tamasic, meaning it is done without energy or true purpose.
vishnu_gita::310.modern_relevance: You might go through motions at work or with loved ones without genuine care, making efforts feel empty and lifeless.
vishnu_gita::310.insight: Recognize that actions without wholehearted intention and support lose their power and meaning.

vishnu_gita::311.verse_sanskrit:
प्रवृत्तिञ्च निवृत्तिञ्च कार्याकायें भयाभये ।
बन्धं मोक्षञ्च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा सात्त्विकी सुगः ॥
vishnu_gita::311.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! प्रवृत्ति निवृत्ति, कार्य्य अकार्य, भय अभय और बन्ध मोक्ष जो जानती है वह सात्त्विकी बुद्धि है
vishnu_gita::311.english_translation: The intellect that understands action and inaction, fear and fearlessness, bondage and freedom is the pure intellect.
vishnu_gita::311.translation_literal: प्रवृत्तिं (action) च (and) निवृत्तिं (inaction) च (and) कार्याकायें (what should be done and what should not be) भयाभये (fear and fearlessness) । बन्धं (bondage) मोक्षञ्च (freedom) या (which) वेत्ति (knows) बुद्धिः (intellect) सा (that) सात्त्विकी (pure) सुगः (good) ॥
vishnu_gita::311.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::311.essence: True intellect clearly perceives what to act on and what to avoid without fear.
vishnu_gita::311.simple_meaning: True clarity arises when the mind can distinguish what actions to take or avoid, what causes fear or fearlessness, and what leads to bondage or freedom.
vishnu_gita::311.simple_insight: You can feel calm and steady when your mind clearly sees what matters and what doesn't.
vishnu_gita::311.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the intellect which can discern between action and inaction, what should or shouldn’t be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and freedom, is a sign of pure mind. This clarity helps the seeker navigate life without confusion.
vishnu_gita::311.modern_relevance: When you face tough choices, your mind feels calm if it can clearly tell what’s worth acting on and what to let go.
vishnu_gita::311.insight: It shifts your thinking to carefully distinguish between necessary actions and distractions, reducing anxiety about outcomes.

vishnu_gita::312.verse_sanskrit:
यया धर्ममधर्मञ्च कार्यञ्चाकार्यमेव च ।
अयथावत प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा राजसी मता ॥
vishnu_gita::312.verse_hindi: जिसके द्वारा धर्म अधर्म और कार्य अकार्य यथावत् परिज्ञात न हो उसको राजसी बुद्धि कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::312.english_translation: The intellect that cannot properly distinguish between right and wrong, and what should or should not be done, is called rajasic intellect.
vishnu_gita::312.translation_literal: यया (by which) धर्ममधर्मञ्च (right and wrong) कार्यञ्चाकार्यमेव (what should be done and what should not) च (and) अयथावत् (properly) प्रजानाति (knows) बुद्धिः (intellect) सा (that) राजसी (rajasic) मता (is considered)
vishnu_gita::312.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::312.essence: Confused intellect that can't distinguish right from wrong is ruled by rajasic nature.
vishnu_gita::312.simple_meaning: An intellect that fails to clearly understand what is right or wrong, and what should or should not be done, is influenced by rajasic qualities.
vishnu_gita::312.simple_insight: You feel stuck when your mind can't clearly distinguish what actions serve your true purpose.
vishnu_gita::312.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains that a person whose intellect cannot properly distinguish right from wrong or action from inaction is dominated by rajasic nature, which causes confusion and leads to misguided choices.
vishnu_gita::312.modern_relevance: You hesitate at work or in life because your mind can't clearly tell which choice aligns with your values and which doesn't.
vishnu_gita::312.insight: It teaches you to recognize when confusion clouds your decisions and to seek clarity beyond restless impulses.

vishnu_gita::313.verse_sanskrit:
अधर्म धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता।
सर्वार्थान् विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा तामसी मता ॥
vishnu_gita::313.verse_hindi: जो बुद्धि अधर्म को धर्म मानती है और सब विषयों को विपरीत मानती है उस तमोगुणाच्छन्न बुद्धि को तामसी बुद्धि कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::313.english_translation: The intellect that mistakes unrighteousness for righteousness and sees all things in reverse is called the intellect covered by darkness (Tamas).
vishnu_gita::313.translation_literal: अधर्म (unrighteousness) / धर्ममिति (as righteousness) / या (which) / मन्यते (believes) / तमसावृता (covered by darkness) / सर्वार्थान् (all meanings/things) / विपरीतांश्च (and opposite) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / सा (that) / तामसी (darkness-related) / मता (is considered)
vishnu_gita::313.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::313.essence: Confusing wrong for right reveals a mind clouded by darkness and distorted perception.
vishnu_gita::313.simple_meaning: When your understanding mistakes what is wrong for what is right and sees everything backward, that mind is clouded by darkness.
vishnu_gita::313.simple_insight: It feels unsettling to realize your mind can flip truth and falsehood without you noticing.
vishnu_gita::313.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when the intellect is veiled by tamas (darkness), it wrongly judges unrighteousness as righteousness and reverses all meanings. This distorted perception traps the mind in confusion and error.
vishnu_gita::313.modern_relevance: You catch yourself defending decisions or beliefs that deep down feel wrong, realizing your perspective is clouded and needs clearing.
vishnu_gita::313.insight: This verse teaches you to recognize when your mind reverses reality, prompting you to seek clearer understanding.

vishnu_gita::314.verse_sanskrit:
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःमाणेन्द्रियक्रियाः।
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या देवाः ! सा सात्त्विकी धृतिः ॥
vishnu_gita::314.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! योग के द्वारा विषयान्तर धारणा न करनेवाली जिस धृति से मन प्राण और इन्द्रियों की क्रिया धारण की जाती है अर्थात् नियमन होती है वह धृति सात्त्विकी धृति है।
vishnu_gita::314.english_translation: O divine beings! The steadfastness by which the mind, life force, and senses are controlled without distraction through yoga is called sattvic steadfastness.
vishnu_gita::314.translation_literal: धृत्या (by steadfastness) / यया (by which) / धारयते (are controlled) / मनःमाणेन्द्रियक्रियाः (mind, life force, senses actions) / योगेन (by yoga) / अव्यभिचारिण्या (without distraction) / देवाः (O divine beings) / सा (that) / सात्त्विकी (sattvic) / धृतिः (steadfastness)
vishnu_gita::314.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::314.essence: True steadiness means controlling mind and senses without distraction through yoga.
vishnu_gita::314.simple_meaning: Steadfastness means controlling your mind, life force, and senses without distraction through yoga.
vishnu_gita::314.simple_insight: You can feel calm and steady when your mind and senses are firmly held by focused practice.
vishnu_gita::314.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that true steadiness is a focused control of mind, life force, and senses through yoga, without wavering or distraction. This steadiness is called sattvic, the pure and balanced quality needed for spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::314.modern_relevance: When your attention drifts during work or conversation, steadying your mind helps you stay present and effective.
vishnu_gita::314.insight: It teaches you to steady your mind and senses through unwavering yoga practice, strengthening inner control.

vishnu_gita::315.verse_sanskrit:
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽमराः।
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकांक्षी धृतिः सा राजसी मता ॥
vishnu_gita::315.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! जिस धृति के द्वारा (जीव) धर्म अर्थ और कामको धारण करता है एवं प्रसङ्गवश फलाकांक्षी होता है उस धृति को राजसी कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::315.english_translation: The steadfastness by which beings uphold duty, wealth, and desire, yet cling to results, is called rajasic steadfastness.
vishnu_gita::315.translation_literal: यया (by which) तु (indeed) धर्मकामार्थान् (duty, desire, wealth) धृत्या (by steadfastness) धारयतेऽमराः (beings uphold) । प्रसङ्गेन (by circumstance) फलाकांक्षी (result-seeking) धृतिः (steadfastness) सा (that) राजसी (rajasic) मता (is considered) ॥
vishnu_gita::315.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::315.essence: Steadfastness tied to craving results is rajasic, even when it upholds duty and desire.
vishnu_gita::315.simple_meaning: Some people hold onto their duties, desires, and wealth but still want the rewards from them. This way of holding on with craving is called rajasic steadfastness.
vishnu_gita::315.simple_insight: You can feel the tension of doing while still wanting the outcome to be yours.
vishnu_gita::315.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to the divine beings that there is a kind of steadfastness where beings maintain their duties, desires, and wealth but remain attached to the results. This attachment driven by circumstance is known as rajasic steadfastness, reflecting a restless craving.
vishnu_gita::315.modern_relevance: You finish a task but keep checking for praise or reward, feeling restless until you get it.
vishnu_gita::315.insight: It teaches you to notice when your steady efforts are still motivated by wanting something back, not just by the action itself.

vishnu_gita::316.verse_sanskrit:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा तामसी सुराः । ॥
vishnu_gita::316.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! विवेकहीन व्यक्ति जिसके द्वारा निद्रा, भय, शोक,विषाद और अहंकार का त्याग नहीं करता है वही तामसी धृति है
vishnu_gita::316.english_translation: O divine beings, that dull determination which does not abandon sleep, fear, sorrow, grief, and ego is the tamasic resolve.
vishnu_gita::316.translation_literal: यया (by which) स्वप्नं (sleep) भयं (fear) शोकं (sorrow) विषादं (grief) मदमेव (and ego itself) च (also) । न (not) विमुञ्चति (abandons) दुर्मेधा (foolish) धृतिः (determination) सा (that) तामसी (tamasic) सुराः (O divine beings) ।
vishnu_gita::316.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::316.essence: Clinging to fear and ego is a dull resolve that blocks true clarity and freedom.
vishnu_gita::316.simple_meaning: Holding on to sleepiness, fear, sorrow, grief, and ego without letting go is a dull and confused kind of determination called tamasic resolve.
vishnu_gita::316.simple_insight: You feel the heaviness of clinging to old fears and sorrow that block your growth.
vishnu_gita::316.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that a stubborn mind which refuses to give up ignorance, sleep, fear, sorrow, and ego is a tamasic (dark) form of resolve that traps one in confusion.
vishnu_gita::316.modern_relevance: You find yourself stuck in old fears and negative moods, unable to shake off tired patterns that drain your energy.
vishnu_gita::316.insight: It teaches you to recognize when your determination is actually resistance to growth, rooted in fear and confusion.

vishnu_gita::317.verse_sanskrit:
स्मृति व्यतीत विषयां मतिमागामि गोचाराम
प्रज्ञा नवनवोन्मेषशालिनी प्रतिभा विदुः ॥
vishnu_gita::317.verse_hindi: अतीत विषयों से सम्बन्ध रखनेवाली प्रज्ञा को स्मृति, आगामि विषयों से सम्बन्ध रखनेवाली प्रज्ञा को बुद्धि और नवीन  ज्ञान विज्ञानों का उद्भव करने वाली प्रज्ञा को प्रतिभा कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::317.english_translation: Pragya connected to past objects is memory; to future objects is intellect; that which creates new knowledge is insight.
vishnu_gita::317.translation_literal: स्मृति (memory) / व्यतीत (past) / विषयां (objects) / मतिमा (pragya) / गॊचाराम् (connected) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / नवनवोन्मेषशालिनी (creating new) / प्रतिभा (insight) / विदुः (know)
vishnu_gita::317.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::317.essence: Wisdom divides into memory of past, intellect of future, and insight creating new knowledge.
vishnu_gita::317.simple_meaning: Wisdom works in three ways: memory recalls the past, intellect plans the future, and insight creates new understanding.
vishnu_gita::317.simple_insight: You can trust that your mind not only remembers and plans but also invents fresh ideas.
vishnu_gita::317.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how the mind's wisdom divides into memory, intellect, and insight, showing how we relate to past experiences, anticipate what is to come, and innovate new knowledge.
vishnu_gita::317.modern_relevance: Your mind replays yesterday's events, worries about tomorrow's tasks, and suddenly sparks new solutions in the present moment.
vishnu_gita::317.insight: Recognize these three mental modes so you can balance recalling, planning, and creating without being overwhelmed by any one.

vishnu_gita::318.verse_sanskrit:
द्रष्टुर्दश्यस्योपलब्धौ क्षमा चत् प्रतिभा तदा।
सात्त्विकी सा समाख्याता सर्वलोकहिते रता ॥
vishnu_gita::318.verse_hindi: जब द्रष्टा और दृश्य की उपलब्धि प्रतिभा समर्थ होती है तब सभी लोकों के हित में तत्पर वह प्रतिभा सात्त्विकी कही जाती है।
vishnu_gita::318.english_translation: When the seer and the seen are truly realized, that clarity is called sattvika, devoted to the welfare of all worlds.
vishnu_gita::318.translation_literal: द्रष्टुः (seer) दश्यस्य (of the seen) उपलब्धौ (in realization) क्षमा (forgiveness) चत् (and) प्रतिभा (clarity) तदा (then) सात्त्विकी (sattvika) सा (that) समाख्याता (called) सर्वलोकहिते (for the welfare of all worlds) रता (devoted)
vishnu_gita::318.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::318.essence: Clarity arises when you realize both the observer and the observed, devoted to universal welfare.
vishnu_gita::318.simple_meaning: When you truly perceive yourself and what you observe clearly, that wisdom is pure and seeks the good of all.
vishnu_gita::318.simple_insight: There is peace in clear seeing that connects you with all around you.
vishnu_gita::318.detailed_meaning: In the teaching, Vishnu explains that when the observer (the seer) and the observed (the seen) are both fully understood, the resulting clarity is called sattvika wisdom. This clarity is not selfish but dedicated to the welfare of all beings across all worlds.
vishnu_gita::318.modern_relevance: You notice a moment when your judgments soften and understanding deepens, opening your heart to others' needs beyond yourself.
vishnu_gita::318.insight: It shifts your view from separation to unity, inspiring actions that serve the greater good.

vishnu_gita::319.verse_sanskrit:
यदा शिल्पकलायां सा पदार्थालोचन तथा।
प्रसरेदराजसी ज्ञेया तदा सा प्रतिभा बुधैः ॥
vishnu_gita::319.verse_hindi: जब वह शिल्पकला और पदार्थीको आलोचना में प्रसार को प्राप्त होती है तब उस प्रतिभा को बुधगण राजसी प्रतिभा जानते हैं
vishnu_gita::319.english_translation: When skill expands into the analysis of form and substance, that brilliance is known by the wise as rajasic intellect.
vishnu_gita::319.translation_literal: यदा (when) शिल्पकलायां (in craft/art) सा (that) पदार्थालोचन (analysis of substance) तथा (also) प्रसरेदराजसी (expands as rajasic) ज्ञेया (to be known) तदा (then) सा (that) प्रतिभा (intellect/brilliance) बुधैः (by the wise)
vishnu_gita::319.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::319.essence: Deep analysis transforms skill into bright, active intelligence recognized by the wise.
vishnu_gita::319.simple_meaning: When your skill extends into examining the details of form and substance, this focused intelligence is recognized by the wise as a vibrant, active mind.
vishnu_gita::319.simple_insight: There's energy and brightness in a mind that deeply explores what it works with.
vishnu_gita::319.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how a person's skill or talent develops when it moves beyond surface effort into detailed examination of form and substance. This quality of sharp, active intelligence is called rajasic by wise people, highlighting a vibrant, engaged mind.
vishnu_gita::319.modern_relevance: You notice your focus sharpen when you stop rushing and start really understanding the details of a project or problem.
vishnu_gita::319.insight: It teaches you to value the moment when your effort becomes focused inquiry, turning doing into knowing.

vishnu_gita::320.verse_sanskrit:
साधारणं लौकिकञ्चेत् सदसद्रिमृशेत्तदा ।
तामसी सा समाख्याता प्रत्युत्पन्नमतिश्च सा ॥
vishnu_gita::320.verse_hindi: जब वह साधारण लौकिक सत् असत का विचार करे तो उसको तामसी प्रतिभा कहते हैं और उसको प्रत्युत्पन्नमति भी कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::320.english_translation: When the mind contemplates the ordinary worldly distinction between existence and non-existence, that is called tamasic intellect, also known as reactive thinking.
vishnu_gita::320.translation_literal: साधारणं (ordinary) लौकिकञ्चेत् (worldly if) सदसद्रिमृशेत्तदा (distinguishes between existence and non-existence then) तामसी (tamasic) सा (that) समाख्याता (called) प्रत्युत्पन्नमतिश्च (also reactive or arising mind) सा (that)
vishnu_gita::320.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::320.essence: Ordinary dualistic thinking is tamasic, a reactive mind state.
vishnu_gita::320.simple_meaning: When your mind judges things only as simply true or false in the ordinary world, that thinking is called tamasic, a dull and reactive way of understanding.
vishnu_gita::320.simple_insight: You can feel how limiting and dull it is to see only black and white.
vishnu_gita::320.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when the mind views the world in a simple dualistic way—just true or false, existence or non-existence—this is called tamasic intellect. This reactive thinking is clouded by dullness and confusion, limiting deeper understanding.
vishnu_gita::320.modern_relevance: You catch yourself judging events or people as simply right or wrong, stuck in a dull, reactive mindset.
vishnu_gita::320.insight: It encourages you to notice when your mind reacts habitually, limiting your ability to see complexity.

vishnu_gita::321.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिमकातिभेदतः।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी च बुभुत्सवः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::321.verse_hindi: हे जिज्ञासुओं! प्राणियों की प्रकृति के अनुसार श्रद्धा तीन प्रकार की होती है, सात्त्विकी राजसी और तामसी
vishnu_gita::321.english_translation: O seekers! The faith of beings is of three kinds according to their nature: sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic.
vishnu_gita::321.translation_literal: त्रिविधा (threefold) भवति (is) श्रद्धा (faith) देहिमकातिभेदतः (according to the differences in beings) । सात्त्विकी (sattvic) राजसी (rajasic) चैव (and also) तामसी (tamasic) च (also) बुभुत्सवः (are).
vishnu_gita::321.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::321.essence: Faith naturally arises in three distinct forms reflecting the nature of each being.
vishnu_gita::321.simple_meaning: Faith in beings appears in three forms based on their nature: pure (sattvic), passionate (rajasic), and dull (tamasic).
vishnu_gita::321.simple_insight: You can recognize your own faith by seeing which nature guides your beliefs and actions.
vishnu_gita::321.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to seekers that all living beings have faith that arises from their inner nature. This faith divides into three types—sattvic (pure and harmonious), rajasic (active and restless), and tamasic (dull and ignorant)—shaping how they engage with life.
vishnu_gita::321.modern_relevance: When you feel inspired, restless, or stuck, it reflects the kind of faith driving your thoughts and choices.
vishnu_gita::321.insight: It teaches you to identify the quality of your faith to better understand your motivations and responses.

vishnu_gita::322.verse_sanskrit:
तासान्तु लक्षणं देवाः ! शृणुध्वं भक्तिभावतः ।
श्रद्धा सा सात्त्विकी ज्ञेया विशुद्धज्ञानमूलिका ॥
vishnu_gita::322.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! अब उनके लक्षण भक्ति भाव से सुनो। जो विशुद्ध ज्ञान मूलक श्रद्धा है उसको सात्त्विकी जानो
vishnu_gita::322.english_translation: O divine beings! Now listen to their characteristics born of devotion. That faith, rooted in pure knowledge, is called sattvic.
vishnu_gita::322.translation_literal: तासान्तु (now listen) लक्षणं (characteristics) देवाः (O divine beings) ! शृणुध्वं (listen) भक्तिभावतः (born of devotion) । श्रद्धा (faith) सा (that) सात्त्विकी (sattvic) ज्ञेया (to be known) विशुद्धज्ञानमूलिका (rooted in pure knowledge) ॥
vishnu_gita::322.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::322.essence: Faith grounded in devotion and pure knowledge is steady and true.
vishnu_gita::322.simple_meaning: Faith that arises from devotion and is based on pure knowledge is considered pure and balanced.
vishnu_gita::322.simple_insight: You can trust deeply when your faith is grounded in clear understanding and devotion.
vishnu_gita::322.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine assembly, explaining that the kind of faith they should listen for is one born from devotion and rooted in pure, sattvic knowledge. This faith is steady and free from confusion.
vishnu_gita::322.modern_relevance: When you commit to something because you truly understand and feel connected, your trust becomes strong and clear.
vishnu_gita::322.insight: It shifts your trust from blind belief to faith grounded in clear, discerning knowledge combined with heartfelt devotion.

vishnu_gita::323.verse_sanskrit:
प्रवृतिमूलिका चैव जिज्ञासामूलिका परा।
विचारहीनसंस्कारमूलिका त्वन्तिमा मता ॥
vishnu_gita::323.verse_hindi: प्रवृत्ति और जिज्ञासामूलक श्रद्धा राजसी है और विचारहीन संस्कारमूलक श्रद्धा तामसी कही गई है
vishnu_gita::323.english_translation: Faith rooted in action and inquiry is of the nature of passion, while faith born of thoughtless habits is considered of inertia.
vishnu_gita::323.translation_literal: प्रवृतिमूलिका (rooted in action) / चैव (and also) / जिज्ञासामूलिका (rooted in inquiry) / परा (supreme/passionate) / विचारहीनसंस्कारमूलिका (rooted in thoughtless habits) / त्वन्तिमा (utterly inert) / मता (considered)
vishnu_gita::323.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::323.essence: Faith rooted in conscious action and inquiry energizes; faith from thoughtless habit dulls.
vishnu_gita::323.simple_meaning: Faith that arises from active effort and sincere questioning is lively and passionate, while faith based on unthinking habits is dull and inactive.
vishnu_gita::323.simple_insight: You experience richer trust when it comes from your curiosity and actions, not from empty routine.
vishnu_gita::323.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that faith can arise in different ways: when it comes from deliberate action or genuine inquiry, it is energized and radiant (rajasic). But when it comes from blind, unexamined habits, it is inert and dull (tamasic). This distinction helps Arjuna understand the quality of true trust.
vishnu_gita::323.modern_relevance: When you follow routines without thinking or question, your trust feels flat. But when you engage your mind and heart, faith becomes alive and motivating.
vishnu_gita::323.insight: Recognize the source of your faith and nurture the kind that grows from conscious engagement rather than mindless repetition.

vishnu_gita::324.verse_sanskrit:
वेदेष्वथ पुराणेषु तन्त्रेऽपि श्रुतिसम्मते ।
भयानक रोचकं हि यथार्थमिति भेदतः ॥
vishnu_gita::324.verse_hindi: वेद, पुराण और श्रुतिसम्मत तन्त्रों में भयानक रोचक और यथार्थ इन भेदों से
vishnu_gita::324.english_translation: In the Vedas, Puranas, and accepted scriptures, these distinctions are indeed terrifying, fascinating, and true.
vishnu_gita::324.translation_literal: वेदेषु (in the Vedas) / अथ (and) / पुराणेषु (in the Puranas) / तन्त्रेऽपि (also in the Tantras) / श्रुतिसम्मते (accepted by the revealed scriptures) / भयानक (terrifying) / रोचकं (fascinating) / हि (indeed) / यथार्थमिति (true) / भेदतः (in distinctions)
vishnu_gita::324.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::324.essence: Ancient scriptures acknowledge profound and unsettling distinctions as true.
vishnu_gita::324.simple_meaning: These scriptures recognize that distinctions can be frightening, interesting, and real.
vishnu_gita::324.simple_insight: Recognizing complexity can feel both unsettling and captivating.
vishnu_gita::324.detailed_meaning: This verse states that many sacred texts acknowledge the reality of profound and sometimes frightening distinctions or differences, highlighting their importance and impact.
vishnu_gita::324.insight: It invites acceptance of complex truths that challenge simple understanding.

vishnu_gita::325.verse_sanskrit:
वाक्यानि त्रिविधान्याहुस्तद्विदो मद्विभावकाः।
श्रूयतां दत्तचित्तैर्हि तत्राऽस्त्येवं व्यवस्थितिः ॥
vishnu_gita::325.verse_hindi: तीन प्रकार के वाक्य मेरे भावों से भावित तत्त्ववेत्ताओ ने कहे हैं । इस विषय में निम्नलिखित प्रकार से ही व्यवस्था है सो चित्त लगाकर सुनिये
vishnu_gita::325.english_translation: The wise who understand me have spoken of three kinds of expressions; listen carefully, for this is the established order.
vishnu_gita::325.translation_literal: वाक्यानि (expressions) त्रिविधानि (three types) आहु: (are said) तद्विद: (those who know that) मद्विभावकाः (my different aspects). श्रूयतां (let be heard) दत्तचित्तैः (with focused mind) हि (indeed) तत्र (there) अस्ति (is) एवम् (thus) व्यवस्था (arrangement).
vishnu_gita::325.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::325.essence: The divine truth is revealed through three kinds of expressions known by the wise.
vishnu_gita::325.simple_meaning: There are three kinds of statements revealing my nature, known by the wise; listen with focus as this is the proper order.
vishnu_gita::325.simple_insight: You feel invited to listen deeply because the teaching has a precise structure.
vishnu_gita::325.detailed_meaning: Vishnu tells that the wise who understand his essence have categorized his teachings into three kinds of expressions. He asks the listener to pay close attention, indicating a structured and important teaching is about to unfold.
vishnu_gita::325.insight: It prepares you to receive teachings in a structured way, highlighting the importance of focused attention.

vishnu_gita::326.verse_hindi: पाप से और अज्ञानसम्भूत विषय से डर दिखाने वाले जो वचन हैं तत्त्वदर्शी ज्ञानिगण उनको भयानक कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::326.english_translation: The wise who see the truth call fearful those words born of sin and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::326.translation_literal: पपच्चाऽज्ञानसम्भूताद्विषयादभीतीकृद्धचः (from sin and ignorance-born subject-fearful) / भयानकमिति (fearful, thus) / प्राहुर्जानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः (say the wise who see truth)
vishnu_gita::326.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::326.essence: Fearful words come from ignorance, not from clear understanding of truth.
vishnu_gita::326.simple_meaning: Words that cause fear arise from ignorance and misunderstanding, not from truth.
vishnu_gita::326.simple_insight: You can feel safe knowing fearful thoughts come from confusion, not reality.
vishnu_gita::326.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that fearful words or ideas arise from sin and ignorance. Those who truly see the nature of reality recognize such words as false and frightening, not as ultimate truth.
vishnu_gita::326.modern_relevance: When worries or fearful messages arise, it's often your mind's confusion, not actual danger.
vishnu_gita::326.insight: It teaches you to question fearful thoughts as products of ignorance rather than facts.

vishnu_gita::327.verse_sanskrit:
मुकृतेऽध्यात्मलक्ष्ये च रूचिकृवचनं मुराः ।
रोचकं तद्धि विज्ञेयं श्रुतो तन्त्रपुराणयोः ॥
vishnu_gita::327.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! पुण्य में और अध्यात्म लक्ष्य में रुचि उत्पन्न करने वाले जो वचन वेद तन्त्र और पुराणों में हैं उनको रोचक जानना चाहिये।
vishnu_gita::327.english_translation: O divine beings! Words that inspire interest in virtue and spiritual goals, found in the Vedas, Tantras, and Puranas, should be considered fascinating.
vishnu_gita::327.translation_literal: मुकृतेऽध्यात्मलक्ष्ये (in spiritual goal) / च (and) / रूचिकृवचनं (words that create interest) / मुराः (O sages) / रोचकं (interesting) / तद्धि (that indeed) / विज्ञेयं (should be known) / श्रुतो (heard) / तन्त्रपुराणयोः (in Tantra and Purana)
vishnu_gita::327.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::327.essence: Teachings that inspire interest in virtue and spirituality are meant to be engaging.
vishnu_gita::327.simple_meaning: Words that spark interest in virtue and spiritual goals, found in sacred scriptures, should be seen as engaging.
vishnu_gita::327.simple_insight: Interest in spiritual teachings makes learning feel alive and meaningful.
vishnu_gita::327.detailed_meaning: Addressing the divine beings or sages, the verse highlights that teachings from the Vedas, Tantras, and Puranas that encourage interest in virtue and spiritual goals are meant to be engaging and appealing.
vishnu_gita::327.insight: It shows the importance of engaging language to make spiritual teachings attractive and accessible.

vishnu_gita::328.verse_sanskrit:
आध्यात्मतत्त्वसंलिष्ट तत्वज्ञानोपदेशकम ।
वचो यथार्थ सम्प्रोक्तं यूयं जानीत निर्जराः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::328.verse_hindi: अध्यात्म तत्त्व से युक्त और तत्व ज्ञान का उपदेश देने वाले वचन को हे देवगण ! यथार्थ वचन कहते हैं ऐसा आप जानिये
vishnu_gita::328.english_translation: O divine beings, know that these words, grounded in spiritual truth and teaching essence, are truly accurate.
vishnu_gita::328.translation_literal: आध्यात्मतत्त्वसंलिष्ट (spiritual-truth-joined) / तत्वज्ञानोपदेशकम (essence-knowledge-teaching) / वचो (words) / यथार्थ (true) / सम्प्रोक्तं (spoken) / यूयं (you) / जानीत (know) / निर्जराः (divine beings) !
vishnu_gita::328.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::328.essence: Words grounded in spiritual truth convey true and reliable knowledge.
vishnu_gita::328.simple_meaning: These words teach deep spiritual truth and wisdom. You should know they are true and reliable.
vishnu_gita::328.simple_insight: There is confidence and trust in knowing profound teachings come from true understanding.
vishnu_gita::328.detailed_meaning: The narrator addresses the sages, urging them to recognize that the forthcoming teachings are not ordinary but rooted in profound spiritual knowledge and truth, preparing them for important wisdom.
vishnu_gita::328.insight: It encourages you to receive teachings with openness, trusting their foundation in deep spiritual understanding.

vishnu_gita::329.verse_sanskrit:
भयानकं वचो नित्यं तामसायाधिकारिणे।
रोचकं राजसायैव यथार्थ सात्त्विकाय वै ॥
vishnu_gita::329.verse_hindi: हे विभुत्तमो! भयानक वचन सदा ही तामसिक अधिकारी के लिये, रोचक वचन राजसिक अधिकारी के ही लिये और यथार्थ वचन सात्त्विक अधिकारी के लिये ही
vishnu_gita::329.english_translation: Fearful words always belong to those attached to inertia; enticing words belong to those driven by passion; truthful words belong only to those of pure nature.
vishnu_gita::329.translation_literal: भयानकं (fearful) / वचो (words) / नित्यं (always) / तामसयाधिकरिणे (to those attached to inertia) / रोचकं (enticing) / राजसायैव (to those driven by passion) / यथार्थ (truthful) / सात्त्विकाय (to those of pure nature) / वै (indeed)
vishnu_gita::329.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::329.essence: Words always reveal the speaker’s dominant inner nature: fear, passion, or purity.
vishnu_gita::329.simple_meaning: People speak differently based on their inner nature: fearful words come from inertia, tempting words from passion, and truthful words from purity.
vishnu_gita::329.simple_insight: You sense what kind of words truly reflect your inner nature and mindset.
vishnu_gita::329.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how speech reveals a person's dominant nature—those stuck in inertia speak fearful words, the passionate speak tempting words, and the pure speak truthful words, highlighting different inner states.
vishnu_gita::329.modern_relevance: When someone speaks harshly, you recognize their fear; when they entice, their passion shows; only pure words resonate deeply.
vishnu_gita::329.insight: It teaches you to listen beyond words to the speaker’s inner nature, discerning truth from shadow.

vishnu_gita::330.verse_sanskrit:
विशेषतो हितकर विज्ञेयं विबुधोत्तमाः। 
अतोऽधिकारभेदेन वचनं व्याहृतं मुराः ॥
vishnu_gita::330.verse_hindi: विशेषरूप से हितकर हैं ऐसा जानना चाहिये, इसलिये हे देवतागण ! शास्त्रों में अधिकारभेद से वचन कहे गये हैं
vishnu_gita::330.english_translation: It is especially beneficial to understand this, O best of the wise! Therefore, the scriptures speak differently according to the qualifications of the listener.
vishnu_gita::330.translation_literal: विशेषतो (especially) हितकर (beneficial) विज्ञेयं (to be known) विबुधोत्तमाः (best of the wise) । अतोऽधिकारभेदेन (therefore by qualifications-difference) वचनं (speech) व्याहृतं (has been declared) मुराः (fools) ॥
vishnu_gita::330.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::330.essence: Teachings change according to the listener's readiness and understanding.
vishnu_gita::330.simple_meaning: The scriptures teach differently depending on the listener's qualifications, because understanding varies among people.
vishnu_gita::330.simple_insight: Knowing teachings suit different people helps you accept varied guidance without frustration.
vishnu_gita::330.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that sacred teachings are given in different ways depending on who receives them, respecting their capacity to understand; this prevents confusion and makes wisdom accessible.
vishnu_gita::330.modern_relevance: You notice how advice changes when talking to different friends, because each understands differently and needs tailored guidance.
vishnu_gita::330.insight: Recognize that teachings adapt to your readiness and background, so be patient with variations.

vishnu_gita::331.verse_sanskrit:
श्रुतौ पुराणे तन्त्रे च त्रिधा वर्णनरीतयः।
दृश्यन्ते क्रमशः सर्वास्ता वच्मि भवतां पुरः ॥
vishnu_gita::331.verse_hindi: वेद पुराण और तंत्रों में तीन प्रकार को वर्णन शैलियां देखी जाती हैं उन सब को आप लोगों के सामने मैं क्रमश कहता हूँ
vishnu_gita::331.english_translation: In the Vedas, Puranas, and Tantras, three types of explanation methods appear; I will describe them to you in order.
vishnu_gita::331.translation_literal: श्रुतौ (in the Vedas) / पुराणे (in the Puranas) / तन्त्रे (in the Tantras) / च (and) / त्रिधा (threefold) / वर्णनरीतयः (methods of explanation) / दृश्यन्ते (are seen) / क्रमशः (in order) / सर्वा (all) / ताः (those) / वच्मि (I speak) / भवतां (to you) / पुरः (before).
vishnu_gita::331.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::331.essence: Ancient teachings use three different ways to explain knowledge, all worth understanding.
vishnu_gita::331.simple_meaning: There are three ways to explain things in the Vedas, Puranas, and Tantras. I will tell you all of them step by step.
vishnu_gita::331.simple_insight: Understanding different ways to explain can help you follow teachings more clearly.
vishnu_gita::331.detailed_meaning: Vishnu introduces that sacred texts like the Vedas, Puranas, and Tantras contain three distinct explanation styles. He promises to explain these methods one after another to his listeners, preparing them for deeper knowledge.
vishnu_gita::331.insight: Recognize that knowledge can come in different forms and methods; being open helps learning.

vishnu_gita::332.verse_sanskrit:
समाधिभाषा प्रथमा लौकिकी च तथाऽपरा ।
तृतीया परकीयेति शास्त्रभाषा त्रिधा स्मृता ॥
vishnu_gita::332.verse_hindi: पहली समाधिभाषा, दूसरी लौकिकभाषा और तीसरी परकीयभाषा, इस प्रकार से शास्त्र की भाषा तीन प्रकार की कही गई है।
vishnu_gita::332.english_translation: The scripture states that language is threefold: first, the language of absorption; second, the worldly language; and third, the language beyond this world.
vishnu_gita::332.translation_literal: समाधिभाषा (language of absorption) / प्रथमा (first) / लौकिकी (worldly) / च (and) / तथाऽपरा (also second) / तृतीया (third) / परकीयेति (beyond this world) / शास्त्रभाषा (scripture language) / त्रिधा (threefold) / स्मृता (remembered)
vishnu_gita::332.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::332.essence: Sacred teachings use three language types: absorption, worldly, and beyond-world.
vishnu_gita::332.simple_meaning: The scripture describes three types of language used: one for deep absorption, one for everyday life, and one for transcending the world.
vishnu_gita::332.simple_insight: Language can express different levels of experience, from ordinary to transcendent.
vishnu_gita::332.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that the sacred text uses three distinct types of language: one for describing absorbed states of consciousness, one for common worldly communication, and one for concepts beyond the ordinary world. It sets the stage for understanding different modes of teaching.
vishnu_gita::332.modern_relevance: Sometimes conversations shift between everyday talk, deep reflection, and abstract ideas beyond normal experience.
vishnu_gita::332.insight: Recognize that teachings may come in different forms—practical, philosophical, or transcendent—each suited to different understanding.

vishnu_gita::333.verse_hindi: जिसमें निरन्तर इतिहास आए, जो निर्मल और श्रुतिमधुर हो, जो मन को लुभाने वाली और इसी तरह चित्त के आह्लाद को बढ़ानेवाली हो
vishnu_gita::333.english_translation: Which contains continuous history, is pure and melodious to hear, captivates the mind, and thus increases the joy of the inner state.
vishnu_gita::333.translation_literal: इतिहासमयी (containing history) / शश्वत् (continuous) / कर्णयोः (to the ears) / मधु (sweet) / अमला (pure) / मनो (of the mind) / मुग्धकरी (captivating) / तद् (that) / वञ्चिता (deceived) / आह्लाद (joy) / अविवर्धिनी (increasing not)
vishnu_gita::333.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::333.essence: Pure, sweet teachings captivate the mind and increase inner joy continuously.
vishnu_gita::333.simple_meaning: The verse describes something that contains ongoing history, is pure and sweet to listen to, attracts the mind, and increases the joy of the inner state.
vishnu_gita::333.simple_insight: Joy grows when what you listen to is pure and captivating to your mind.
vishnu_gita::333.detailed_meaning: This verse praises a text or teaching that is filled with continuous history, is pure and sweet to the ears, and enchants the mind, thereby enhancing the pleasure and happiness of the inner state. It sets the tone for a text that is both informative and uplifting.
vishnu_gita::333.insight: It shows how pure, engaging knowledge nourishes the mind and uplifts inner joy.

vishnu_gita::334.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मसिद्धांत संयुक्ता समासबहुला न हि ।
ज्ञेया सा परकीयेति शास्त्रवर्णनपद्धतिः ॥
vishnu_gita::334.verse_hindi: जो धर्म सिद्धान्तों से युक्त हो और जिसमें जटिलता न हो उस शास्त्रवर्णन की पद्धति को परकीय जानना चाहिये
vishnu_gita::334.english_translation: A scripture that is united with established principles of dharma and free from complexity should not be regarded as foreign.
vishnu_gita::334.translation_literal: धर्मसिद्धांत (dharma principles) संयुक्ता (united) समासबहुला (full of compounds/complexity) न (not) हि (indeed) ज्ञेया (to be known) सा (that) परकीयेति (foreign) शास्त्रवर्णनपद्धतिः (scripture description method)
vishnu_gita::334.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::334.essence: Clear, principle-based teachings are never foreign or disconnected from you.
vishnu_gita::334.simple_meaning: A teaching that aligns with established principles of right conduct and is easy to understand should not be seen as strange or foreign.
vishnu_gita::334.simple_insight: You can trust teachings that feel clear and connected, not confusing or distant.
vishnu_gita::334.detailed_meaning: This verse explains how scriptures grounded in well-known principles of dharma and presented clearly should be accepted as trustworthy, not dismissed as unfamiliar or alien. It highlights the value of clarity and connection in teachings.
vishnu_gita::334.modern_relevance: When you find advice that fits your core values and is easy to grasp, you feel drawn to it, not alienated.
vishnu_gita::334.insight: It encourages you to recognize authentic wisdom by its clarity and coherence, avoiding confusion or rejection of true guidance.

vishnu_gita::335.verse_hindi: इस पद्धति के तत्त्वदर्शीगण इसको अज्ञानी के लिये और इसी तरह तामसिक अधिकारी के लिये विशेष हितकरी कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::335.english_translation: Those who see the truth say this path is especially beneficial for the ignorant and those bound by darkness.
vishnu_gita::335.translation_literal: इमामज्ञानिने (this to the ignorant) तद्वत्तामसायाऽधिकारिणे (and similarly to those of tamasic nature) विशेषतो (especially) हितकरी (beneficial) प्राहुः (say) तत्तत्त्वदर्शिनः (the seers of truth)
vishnu_gita::335.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::335.essence: Certain wisdoms serve best those burdened by confusion and darkness.
vishnu_gita::335.simple_meaning: This teaching is especially helpful for people who feel confused or stuck in negativity.
vishnu_gita::335.simple_insight: You can trust that this wisdom meets you where you are, especially in hard times.
vishnu_gita::335.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that this path of knowledge is particularly good for those who are ignorant or overwhelmed by tamasic qualities like inertia or darkness. It offers special help to those needing clarity and uplift.
vishnu_gita::335.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by confusion or stuck in negative moods, this teaching offers clear guidance and relief.
vishnu_gita::335.insight: Recognize that some teachings are especially designed to help when your mind is clouded or heavy.

vishnu_gita::336.verse_sanskrit:
अतीन्द्रियाध्यात्मराज्यस्थितं विषयगह्वरम्।
लौकिकी रीतिमाश्रित्य वर्णयेद् याऽतिसंस्फुटम् ॥
vishnu_gita::336.verse_hindi: अतीन्द्रिय अध्यात्म राज्य में स्थित गूढ़ विषय को लौकिक रीति का आश्रय लेकर जो अच्छी तरह वर्णन करे
vishnu_gita::336.english_translation: One who clearly describes the profound subject residing in the spiritual realm by relying on worldly methods.
vishnu_gita::336.translation_literal: अतीन्द्रिय (beyond the senses) / अध्यात्म (spiritual) / राज्यस्थितं (situated in the realm) / विषयगह्वरम् (the profound subject) / लौकिकी (worldly) / रीतिम् (method) / आश्रित्य (relying on) / वर्णयेत् (should describe) / याऽतिसंस्फुटम् (very clearly)
vishnu_gita::336.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::336.essence: Deep spiritual truths become clear through relatable worldly explanation.
vishnu_gita::336.simple_meaning: Someone who explains deep spiritual truths clearly by using familiar worldly ways.
vishnu_gita::336.simple_insight: Understanding deep spiritual topics becomes easier when linked to everyday experience.
vishnu_gita::336.detailed_meaning: This verse advises that profound spiritual topics, which exist beyond normal senses, can be best conveyed by using understandable worldly methods, making them clearer for the listener.
vishnu_gita::336.modern_relevance: You find complex ideas easier to grasp when someone explains them using examples from daily life.
vishnu_gita::336.insight: It shifts teaching from abstract to relatable, making spiritual truths accessible through familiar language.

vishnu_gita::337.verse_sanskrit:
नथा समाधिगम्यानां भावानां प्रतिपादिका ।
सा पूर्णा लौकिकैस्तद्रद्रसैर्भापाऽस्ति लौकिकी ॥
vishnu_gita::337.verse_hindi: तथा समाधिगम्य भावों की प्रतिपादि का हो और इसी तरह लौकिक रसों से भी पूर्ण हो वह भाषा लौकिकी भाषा है
vishnu_gita::337.english_translation: Language that conveys states attained through absorbed presence and is also full of worldly feelings is called worldly language.
vishnu_gita::337.translation_literal: नथा (and also) समाधिगम्यानां (of those who have attained samadhi) भावानां (states) प्रतिपादिका (the one that conveys) । सा (that) पूर्णा (full) लौकिकैः (by worldly) तद्रद्रसैः (with their distinct essences) भापाऽस्ति (has flavor) लौकिकी (worldly) ॥
vishnu_gita::337.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::337.essence: Worldly language fully expresses both deep states and everyday feelings together.
vishnu_gita::337.simple_meaning: Worldly language expresses both deep spiritual states and everyday emotions richly.
vishnu_gita::337.simple_insight: Language can carry both profound inner states and familiar feelings together.
vishnu_gita::337.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the nature of worldly language as one that can express deep states of absorbed presence (samadhi) alongside ordinary worldly emotions, highlighting the richness and fullness of such expression.
vishnu_gita::337.insight: It teaches that communication can bridge profound inner experience and common human feelings seamlessly.

vishnu_gita::338.verse_sanskrit:
इयं राजसिकायैव साधकायाधिकारिणे ।
सूतेऽधिकं सदा भव्यं सत्यं सत्यं दिवौकसः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::338.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! यह भाषा राजसिक अधिकार वाले ही साधक के लिये सदा अधिक कल्याण पैदा करती है, यह सत्य है सत्य है ।
vishnu_gita::338.english_translation: O beings of the higher and lower realms! This speech always brings more welfare to those qualified in the mode of passion; this is true, indeed true.
vishnu_gita::338.translation_literal: इयं (this) राजसिकायैव (to the one in mode of passion only) साधकायाधिकारिणे (qualified practitioner) । सूतेऽधिकं (more than Suta) सदा (always) भव्यं (auspicious/welfare) सत्यं (true) सत्यं (true) दिवौकसः (beings of the higher and lower realms) !
vishnu_gita::338.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::338.essence: Speech in passion touches those qualified in that mode most and brings them welfare.
vishnu_gita::338.simple_meaning: Speech influenced by passion benefits those ready to act in that mode more than others; this is absolutely true.
vishnu_gita::338.simple_insight: Some teachings suit certain temperaments better, bringing more welfare to those prepared for them.
vishnu_gita::338.detailed_meaning: The narrator Suta addresses beings of all realms, stating that speech aligned with the mode of passion benefits practitioners qualified in that mode more than others, affirming this as an undeniable truth.
vishnu_gita::338.insight: Recognize that the effectiveness of guidance depends on the listener's readiness and nature.

vishnu_gita::339.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकाशयति या ज्ञानं कार्यकारणब्रह्मणोः।
समाधिसिद्धभावैर्या सम्पूर्णा सर्वतस्तथा ॥
vishnu_gita::339.verse_hindi: जो भाषा कार्य ब्रह्म और कारण ब्रह्म के ज्ञान को प्रकाशित कर देती है तथा जो भाषा सर्वत्र समाधि सिद्ध भावों से पूर्ण हो
vishnu_gita::339.english_translation: That speech which reveals the knowledge of the effect Brahman and the cause Brahman, and which is everywhere filled with the qualities of perfected absorption.
vishnu_gita::339.translation_literal: प्रकाशयति (reveals) / या (which) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / कार्यकारणब्रह्मणोः (of effect and cause Brahman) / समाधिसिद्धभावैः (with qualities of perfected absorption) / या (which) / सम्पूर्णा (complete) / सर्वतस्तथा (everywhere thus)
vishnu_gita::339.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::339.essence: True speech reveals the deep unity of cause and effect filled with meditative presence.
vishnu_gita::339.simple_meaning: Speech that reveals the deep knowledge of cause and effect Brahman is always full of qualities of deep inner absorption.
vishnu_gita::339.simple_insight: You can recognize truth by the calm, complete presence behind words.
vishnu_gita::339.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a kind of speech that doesn't just communicate words but reveals the profound knowledge of the supreme cause and effect. This speech is completely infused with the qualities of deep meditative absorption, showing a union of wisdom and presence.
vishnu_gita::339.modern_relevance: When you speak with full presence and deep understanding, your words carry calmness and clarity that others can feel clearly.
vishnu_gita::339.insight: It teaches you to bring your full inner calm and understanding into your speech, making communication a reflection of wisdom.

vishnu_gita::340.verse_sanskrit:
तत्वज्ञानमयी तद्वद्या ही वर्णन पद्धति: ।
ज्ञेया समाधिभाषा या सात्विकायोपकारिका ॥
vishnu_gita::340.verse_hindi: और इसी तरह जो वर्णनपद्धति तत्त्व ज्ञानमयी हो उसको समाधि भाषा जानना चाहिये। वह सात्त्विक अधिकारी के लिये हितकरी है
vishnu_gita::340.english_translation: Similarly, the method of explanation that is filled with knowledge of the true nature should be understood as the language of absorbed presence, beneficial for the discerning mind.
vishnu_gita::340.translation_literal: तत्वज्ञानमयी (knowledge of true nature) तद्वद्या (like that is to be known) ही (indeed) वर्णन (explanation) पद्धति: (method) । ज्ञेया (to be known) समाधिभाषा (language of absorbed presence) या (which) सात्विकाय (for the discerning) उपकारिका (beneficial) ॥
vishnu_gita::340.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::340.essence: True knowledge is best expressed through calm, absorbed presence that benefits a clear mind.
vishnu_gita::340.simple_meaning: The best way to explain deep truth is through the language of absorbed presence, which helps a clear and discerning mind.
vishnu_gita::340.simple_insight: You feel calm and clear when truth is shared in a way that quiets the restless mind.
vishnu_gita::340.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that to communicate profound truths effectively, one must speak in the language of samadhi, a state of absorbed presence, which benefits those with a clear and discerning mind (sattvika). This highlights the connection between deep knowledge and calm awareness.
vishnu_gita::340.modern_relevance: When someone explains complex ideas calmly and clearly, your mind settles and you understand better without confusion or overwhelm.
vishnu_gita::340.insight: It teaches you to value calm clarity over noisy explanation when seeking or sharing deep understanding.

vishnu_gita::341.verse_sanskrit:
श्रवणं मननं तद्विन्नीदिध्यासनमेव च ।
एतात्रितयरूपो य: पुरुषार्थ इहोच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::341.verse_hindi: श्रवण मनन और निदिध्यासन, यह जो त्रितयरूप पुरुषार्थ जगत में कहा जाता है वह सब त्रितयरूप पुरुषार्थ
vishnu_gita::341.english_translation: Hearing, reflection, and deep meditation—these three forms of effort are called the triple practice in this world.
vishnu_gita::341.translation_literal: श्रवणं (hearing) / मननं (reflection) / तद्विन्नीदिध्यासनमेव (and that deep meditation) / एतात्रितयरूपो (these three forms) / य: (which) / पुरुषार्थ (effort) / इहोच्यते (is called in this world)
vishnu_gita::341.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::341.essence: True effort integrates hearing, thoughtful reflection, and deep meditation as one process.
vishnu_gita::341.simple_meaning: Growth comes through three stages: listening carefully, thinking deeply, and meditating profoundly.
vishnu_gita::341.simple_insight: True understanding unfolds when you first hear, then reflect, and finally settle into deep meditation.
vishnu_gita::341.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the path to inner progress involves three key steps: first, listening or receiving wisdom; second, reflecting on what was heard; and third, meditating deeply to internalize it. This triple practice is essential for meaningful effort.
vishnu_gita::341.modern_relevance: You read advice, mull it over during your day, then sit quietly to let it truly settle and transform you.
vishnu_gita::341.insight: It teaches you to move from passive reception to active reflection and then to deep absorption.

vishnu_gita::342.verse_sanskrit:
निर्वृतिमूलकं भूत्वा सक्तं ब्रह्मनिरूपणे
यदा चेत् त्रितयं सर्वं तदा तत् साविकं मतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::342.verse_hindi: जब निवृत्ति मूलक होकर ब्रह्मके निरूपण में  लगता है तब वह सात्त्विक माना जाता है।
vishnu_gita::342.english_translation: When the mind, becoming rooted in renunciation, is firmly established in the supreme reality, then it is considered pure and sattvic.
vishnu_gita::342.translation_literal: निर्वृतिमूलकं (rooted in renunciation) / भूत्वा (being) / सक्तं (attached) / ब्रह्मनिरूपणे (in the realization of Brahman) / यदा (when) / चेत् (mind) / त्रितयं (the three qualities) / सर्वं (all) / तदा (then) / तत् (that) / साविकं (pure, sattvic) / मतम् (is the view)
vishnu_gita::342.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::342.essence: A mind rooted in renunciation and clear understanding becomes pure and balanced.
vishnu_gita::342.simple_meaning: When your mind is deeply settled in letting go and focused on the true reality, it becomes pure and balanced.
vishnu_gita::342.simple_insight: There is clarity and calmness when you let go and connect with what truly is.
vishnu_gita::342.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when the mind becomes deeply grounded in renunciation and understands the supreme reality beyond the three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas), it is then regarded as pure (sattvic). This marks a turning point in spiritual clarity.
vishnu_gita::342.modern_relevance: You find calm and balance when you stop chasing distractions and focus on what truly matters.
vishnu_gita::342.insight: It teaches you to stabilize your mind by letting go of attachments and embracing clear understanding.

vishnu_gita::343.verse_sanskrit:
यदा तत्त्रयमुत्पत्तिस्थिसत्ययस्वरूपिणि।
भावे भावं समासाद्य द्वैतरूपं निषेवते ॥
vishnu_gita::343.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण! जब वह उत्पत्ति स्थिति लय. स्वरूप भाव में भावित होकर द्वैतरूप को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::343.english_translation: O divine beings! When the three qualities of creation, preservation, and destruction unite in their true form, the manifested and the unmanifested coexist in duality.
vishnu_gita::343.translation_literal: यदा (when) तत्त्रयम् (those three) उत्पत्ति (creation) स्थिति (preservation) लय (destruction) सत्य (true) स्वरूपिणि (nature) भावे (in the state) भावं (manifestation) समासाद्य (having attained) द्वैतरूपं (dual form) निषेवते (exists)
vishnu_gita::343.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::343.essence: The true nature unites creation, preservation, and destruction in simultaneous duality.
vishnu_gita::343.simple_meaning: The three fundamental states of existence—creation, preservation, and destruction—combine in their true essence, where the seen and unseen coexist as dual aspects.
vishnu_gita::343.simple_insight: Reality holds both unity and duality together in its deepest nature.
vishnu_gita::343.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the cosmic process where the three fundamental forces—creation, preservation, and destruction—merge in their true nature, resulting in the simultaneous presence of both manifest and unmanifest dual forms, revealing profound cosmic unity and diversity.
vishnu_gita::343.insight: It invites you to see beyond appearances and recognize the unity underlying all change and difference.

vishnu_gita::344.verse_sanskrit:
तदा तं राजसं देवाः ! पुरुषार्थ प्रचक्षते।
यो हि नास्तिकतामूलः स तामस उदाहृतः ॥
vishnu_gita::344.verse_hindi: तब उस त्रितयरूप पुरुषार्थ को राजसिक कहते हैं और जो नास्तिकता. मूलक त्रितयरूप पुरुषार्थ है वह तामसिक कहा गया है
vishnu_gita::344.english_translation: Then the gods call that threefold purpose rajasic; one rooted in disbelief is called tamasic.
vishnu_gita::344.translation_literal: तदा (then) तं (that) राजसं (rajasic) देवाः (the gods) पुरुषार्थ (purpose) प्रचक्षते (declare). यो (who) हि (indeed) नास्तिकतामूलः (rooted in disbelief) स (that) तामस (tamasic) उदाहृतः (called).
vishnu_gita::344.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::344.essence: Motivations rooted in passion or disbelief shape the nature of your purpose.
vishnu_gita::344.simple_meaning: The gods describe purposes motivated by passion as rajasic, and those rooted in disbelief as tamasic.
vishnu_gita::344.simple_insight: Knowing the nature of your motivations helps you understand your actions more clearly.
vishnu_gita::344.detailed_meaning: In this passage, the gods explain the classification of human motives based on the three gunas. Purposes driven by passion and activity are called rajasic, while those based on disbelief or ignorance are tamasic. This sets the stage for understanding different qualities of action.
vishnu_gita::344.modern_relevance: When you feel driven by restless ambition or doubt, noticing these motives can guide you toward clearer choices.
vishnu_gita::344.insight: It shifts your view to notice whether your actions come from clarity or confusion, affecting how you choose to act.

vishnu_gita::345.verse_sanskrit:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यमुखप्रीतिविवर्द्धनाः ।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः॥
vishnu_gita::345.verse_hindi: आयु, सात्त्विकभाव, शक्ति, आरोग्य, चित्तप्रसाद और रुचि के बढानेवाले, रसयुक्त एवं स्नेहयुक्त, जिनका सारांश देह में स्थायी रूप से रहे और चित्त को परितोष करने वाले आहार सात्विक पुरुषों के प्रिय होते हैं
vishnu_gita::345.english_translation: Foods that increase lifespan, vitality, strength, health, and joyful disposition, rich in essence and nourishing, staying steady in the body and pleasing to the mind are loved by those with a pure nature.
vishnu_gita::345.translation_literal: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यमुखप्रीतिविवर्द्धनाः (lifespan-vitality-strength-health-joy increasing) / रस्याः (juicy) / स्निग्धाः (nourishing) / स्थिरा (steady) / हृद्या (pleasing to the heart) / आहाराः (foods) / सात्त्विकप्रियाः (liked by pure-natured)
vishnu_gita::345.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::345.essence: Steady, nourishing foods build lasting strength and calm favored by pure minds.
vishnu_gita::345.simple_meaning: Certain foods help increase your lifespan, strength, health, and happiness by nourishing your body and mind steadily.
vishnu_gita::345.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing what you eat can support your well-being and steady your mind.
vishnu_gita::345.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes foods that promote long life, vitality, and mental contentment. These steady, nourishing foods are favored by those who cultivate a pure and calm nature, highlighting the connection between diet and inner wellbeing.
vishnu_gita::345.modern_relevance: After a long day, choosing a wholesome meal that steadies your energy and calms your mind can transform your evening.
vishnu_gita::345.insight: It teaches you to select foods that benefit both your physical strength and your mental peace.

vishnu_gita::346.verse_hindi: कटु, अम्ल, लवण (क्षार) अत्युष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, रूक्ष, विदाही, यह सब दुःख सन्ताप और रोगप्रद आहार राजसिक व्यक्तियों के प्रिय हैं।
vishnu_gita::346.english_translation: Sharp, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, rough, and burning foods are dear to rajasic people and cause pain, sorrow, and disease.
vishnu_gita::346.translation_literal: कटु (sharp) / अम्ल (sour) / लवण (salty) / अत्युष्ण (very hot) / तीक्ष्ण (pungent) / रूक्ष (rough) / विदाही (burning) / आहारा (foods) / राजसस्य (of the rajasic) / एष्टा (dear) / दुःख (pain) / शोक (sorrow) / अमय (disease) / प्रदाः (causing)
vishnu_gita::346.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::346.essence: Certain foods that excite the senses also bring pain and sorrow to body and mind.
vishnu_gita::346.simple_meaning: Certain kinds of sharp, hot, and spicy foods attract restless energy but bring pain, sorrow, and illness.
vishnu_gita::346.simple_insight: You feel the effects of food not just in your body but also in your mood and wellbeing.
vishnu_gita::346.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes foods favored by rajasic nature—sharp, hot, and pungent—that increase pain and sorrow, highlighting how diet influences both physical and emotional health.
vishnu_gita::346.modern_relevance: After a late night binge on spicy snacks, you wake up feeling restless and uneasy, realizing what you ate affects more than just your stomach.
vishnu_gita::346.insight: Notice how your food choices affect your mind's restlessness and your body's health, guiding you to choose with awareness.

vishnu_gita::347.verse_sanskrit:
यातयामं गतरसं पृति पर्युषितञ्च यत् ।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥
vishnu_gita::347.verse_hindi: एक पहर पहले बना हुआ (ठंडा) विरस, दुर्गन्धयुक्त, बासी, झूठा और अपवित्र जो आहार है वह तामसिक व्यक्तियों को प्रिय होता है।
vishnu_gita::347.english_translation: Stale, foul-smelling, leftover, and impure food is liked by tamasic people.
vishnu_gita::347.translation_literal: यातयामं (old/stale) / गतरसं (having lost flavor) / पृति (foul smell) / पर्युषितञ्च (rotten) / यत् (which) / उच्छिष्टम् (leftover) / अपि (also) / चामेध्यं (impure) / भोजनं (food) / तामसप्रियम् (liked by tamasic).
vishnu_gita::347.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::347.essence: Impure, stale food dulls your body and mind, fostering inertia and confusion.
vishnu_gita::347.simple_meaning: Eating old, smelly, leftover, or impure food reflects a dull, heavy state of being.
vishnu_gita::347.simple_insight: What you consume affects your energy and mindset more than you realize.
vishnu_gita::347.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the qualities of tamasic food—stale and impure—highlighting how such food dulls the senses and mind, encouraging Arjuna to choose purity and freshness to support discipline on the path.
vishnu_gita::347.modern_relevance: You grab leftover fast food late at night and wake feeling sluggish, foggy, and unmotivated.
vishnu_gita::347.insight: It teaches you to be mindful of what you consume, seeing food as a foundation for clear action and discipline.

vishnu_gita::348.verse_sanskrit:
सुखं त्विदानी त्रिविध शृणुतामृतभोजिनः।
अभ्यासादरमते यत्र दुःखान्तञ्च निगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::348.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! अब सुनो सुख भी तीन प्रकार का है। जिस सुख में अभ्यास से अर्थात् स्वतः ही परमानन्द लाभ करता है और दुःख का अन्त प्राप्त करता है,
vishnu_gita::348.english_translation: O divine beings! Listen: happiness is of three kinds. The happiness that arises naturally through practice leads to supreme bliss and an end to suffering.
vishnu_gita::348.translation_literal: सुखं (happiness) त्विदानी (now) त्रिविध (threefold) शृणुतामृतभोजिनः (listen, O enjoyers of nectar). अभ्यासादरमते (through practice, naturally delights) यत्र (where) दुःखान्तञ्च (the end of suffering) निगच्छति (is attained).
vishnu_gita::348.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::348.essence: Steady practice naturally brings deep happiness that ends suffering.
vishnu_gita::348.simple_meaning: Happiness can be of three types, but the kind that comes naturally from steady practice leads to lasting bliss and frees you from suffering.
vishnu_gita::348.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing consistent effort naturally brings deep joy and relief.
vishnu_gita::348.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that happiness has three forms. He highlights the highest type, which arises effortlessly through disciplined practice, leading to supreme bliss and the cessation of pain.
vishnu_gita::348.modern_relevance: After weeks of rehearsing a skill, you suddenly feel confident and joyful without effort or anxiety about failure.
vishnu_gita::348.insight: It teaches you to trust that steady practice transforms your experience from struggle to ease and joy.

vishnu_gita::349.verse_sanskrit:
यत्तदग्रे विपमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
vishnu_gita::349.verse_hindi: वह आदि में विषवत् किन्तु परिणाम मे अमृततुल्य और आत्मबुद्धि के प्रसाद से उत्पन्न सुख सात्त्विक कहा जाता है।
vishnu_gita::349.english_translation: That which at first seems bitter but ultimately results in nectar-like bliss born from clarity of the true self is called sattvic happiness.
vishnu_gita::349.translation_literal: यत् (that) तत् (it) अग्रे (at first) विपमिव (like bitterness) परिणामे (in result) अमृतोपमम् (like nectar) तत् (that) सुखं (happiness) सात्त्विकं (pure, sattvic) प्रोक्तम् (is said) आत्मबुद्धि (true self's clarity) प्रसादजम् (born of grace).
vishnu_gita::349.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::349.essence: Bitterness at first can become pure happiness through clarity of the true self.
vishnu_gita::349.simple_meaning: Sometimes what feels bitter at first leads to deep, clear happiness that comes from understanding your true self.
vishnu_gita::349.simple_insight: You can trust difficult beginnings because they may lead to pure joy rooted in self-understanding.
vishnu_gita::349.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that experiences initially unpleasant or bitter can, through the clarity of the true self, transform into profound and pure happiness. This teaching highlights how the initial struggle is a step toward lasting joy that arises from inner clarity.
vishnu_gita::349.modern_relevance: You start a challenging project or relationship feeling discomfort, but as you gain insight and clarity, it becomes deeply rewarding and joyful.
vishnu_gita::349.insight: It teaches you to see initial difficulty as a necessary phase that clears the way for authentic happiness.

vishnu_gita::350.verse_sanskrit:
विश्येंद्रियसंयोगादयत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम ।
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::350.verse_hindi: विषय और इन्द्रियों के संयोग से आदि में अमृततुल्य किन्तु परिणाम में विपतुल्य सुख राजस कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::350.english_translation: The pleasure arising from contact with sense objects is initially like nectar but eventually turns into painful poison; this is called rajasic pleasure.
vishnu_gita::350.translation_literal: विश्येंद्रियसंयोगादयत् (from contact of sense objects and senses) तद् (that) अग्रे (at the beginning) अमृतोपमम् (like nectar) / परिणामे (in the result) विषमिव (like poison) तत् (that) सुखं (pleasure) राजसं (rajasic) स्मृतम् (is called)
vishnu_gita::350.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::350.essence: Pleasure from senses starts sweet but inevitably turns painful and trapping.
vishnu_gita::350.simple_meaning: Pleasure from sense contact feels like nectar at first but eventually becomes painful, showing its rajasic nature.
vishnu_gita::350.simple_insight: You can feel fooled by pleasures that start sweet but end in suffering.
vishnu_gita::350.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that pleasures arising from sense contact seem delightful initially, like nectar, but their results are harmful, like poison. This rajasic pleasure traps people in cycles of craving and pain.
vishnu_gita::350.modern_relevance: You binge on sweets or social media; the first moments are joyful, but later regret or discomfort follows.
vishnu_gita::350.insight: Recognize the temporary sweetness of sensory pleasures and choose not to be trapped by their harmful outcomes.

vishnu_gita::351.verse_sanskrit:
यदने चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।
निद्रालस्यामादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::351.verse_hindi: निद्रा आलस्य और प्रमाद से उत्पन्न एवं आदि और अन्त में चित्त मोह उत्पन्न करने वाला जो सुख है उसे तामस कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::351.english_translation: The pleasure born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, which arises at the beginning and end and causes confusion of the mind, is called tamas.
vishnu_gita::351.translation_literal: यदने (born of sleep) च (and) अनुबन्धे (attachment) च (and) सुखं (pleasure) मोहनम् (confusing) आत्मनः (of the self) । निद्रा (sleep) आलस्य (laziness) आमादोत्थं (arising from negligence) तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् (that is called tamas) ॥
vishnu_gita::351.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::351.essence: Pleasure born of laziness and negligence clouds the mind with confusion.
vishnu_gita::351.simple_meaning: Pleasure that comes from sleep, laziness, or carelessness confuses your mind and is called tamas.
vishnu_gita::351.simple_insight: You can notice when your enjoyment dulls your awareness and causes confusion.
vishnu_gita::351.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that pleasure arising from states like sleep, laziness, and negligence clouds the mind's clarity, causing confusion. This kind of pleasure is called tamas and blocks clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::351.modern_relevance: After a night of poor rest or procrastination, you might feel a foggy pleasure that dulls your focus and confuses your thoughts.
vishnu_gita::351.insight: It teaches you to recognize pleasures that reduce mental clarity and avoid them for clear perception.

vishnu_gita::352.verse_sanskrit:
नियतस्य तु संन्यास: कर्मणो नोपपद्यते
मोहात्तस्य परिसागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः॥
vishnu_gita::352.verse_hindi: नित्यकर्म का त्याग नहीं हो सकता, मोहवश जो नित्यकर्म का त्याग होता है उसे तामस त्याग कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::352.english_translation: The renunciation of prescribed duties is never attained; abandoning them out of delusion is called tamasic renunciation.
vishnu_gita::352.translation_literal: नियतस्य (prescribed) तु (but) संन्यास: (renunciation) कर्मणो (of action) नोपपद्यते (is not attained) मोहात्तस्य (due to delusion) परिसाग: (abandonment) तामस: (tamasic) परिकीर्तित: (is declared)
vishnu_gita::352.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::352.essence: Giving up your rightful duties from confusion is false renunciation.
vishnu_gita::352.simple_meaning: You cannot truly give up your rightful duties. Leaving them due to confusion is a wrong kind of renunciation.
vishnu_gita::352.simple_insight: There is clarity in knowing that true renunciation does not mean avoiding what you must do.
vishnu_gita::352.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that abandoning the duties assigned to you, out of confusion or delusion, is not real renunciation but a tamasic mistake. True renunciation involves fulfilling your prescribed actions without attachment.
vishnu_gita::352.modern_relevance: You feel tempted to skip important responsibilities when overwhelmed, but true letting go means acting without craving, not avoiding your role.
vishnu_gita::352.insight: This verse shifts your mindset from avoidance to responsible action, showing renunciation as disciplined engagement, not escape.

vishnu_gita::353.verse_sanskrit:
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
vishnu_gita::353.verse_hindi: जो व्यक्ति दुःख होता है ऐसा जानकर दैहिक क्लेश के भय से कर्म त्याग करता है वह राजस त्याग करके त्याग का फल नहीं प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::353.english_translation: One who abandons action out of fear of bodily pain, thinking it is sorrow, does not gain the fruit of renunciation despite giving up rajasic activity.
vishnu_gita::353.translation_literal: दुःखमिति (sorrow-thought) एव (only) यत् (that) कर्म (action) कायक्लेशभयात् (from bodily-pain-fear) त्यजेत् (abandons). स (he) कृत्वा (having done) राजसं (rajasic) त्यागं (renunciation) नैव (not) त्यागफलं (fruit-of-renunciation) लभेत् (obtains).
vishnu_gita::353.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::353.essence: Giving up action from fear is not true renunciation and yields no real benefit.
vishnu_gita::353.simple_meaning: If you stop acting just because you fear pain or sorrow, that isn't true renunciation and you won't get its benefits.
vishnu_gita::353.simple_insight: Fear can trick you into quitting before real freedom begins.
vishnu_gita::353.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that abandoning actions due to fear of bodily suffering is mistaken renunciation. The person thinks they're wise by giving up rajasic (passionate) actions, but without understanding, they gain no true benefit.
vishnu_gita::353.modern_relevance: You hesitate to take on challenges fearing discomfort, but avoiding effort this way blocks growth and meaningful change.
vishnu_gita::353.insight: Recognize that true renunciation requires acting beyond fear, not just quitting when it hurts.

vishnu_gita::354.verse_sanskrit:
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽमराः।
सङ्गं त्यकत्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
vishnu_gita::354.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! इन्द्रियसंग और फल का त्याग करके “ कर्त्तव्य " जानकर जो नियमपूर्वक कर्म किया जाता है वह न्याग सात्त्विक त्याग माना गया है
vishnu_gita::354.english_translation: O divine beings, actions performed regularly as duty, without attachment or desire for results, constitute true renunciation.
vishnu_gita::354.translation_literal: कार्य (action) एव (only) यत् (that which) कर्म (action) नियतं (regularly) क्रियते (is done) अमराः (divine beings) संगं (attachment) त्यकत्वा (giving up) फलम् (result) च (also) एव (indeed) स (that) त्यागः (renunciation) सात्त्विको (pure) मतः (considered)
vishnu_gita::354.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::354.essence: True renunciation is acting on duty without attachment to results or desires.
vishnu_gita::354.simple_meaning: Act regularly with clear understanding of your duty, giving up attachment to results and desires. This is true renunciation.
vishnu_gita::354.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting without craving the outcome; your effort alone matters.
vishnu_gita::354.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, teaching that performing one's duties consistently without attachment or desire for results is the highest form of pure renunciation, freeing one from distraction and craving.
vishnu_gita::354.modern_relevance: You finish a task fully but stay calm when the outcome is uncertain or out of your hands.
vishnu_gita::354.insight: Shift focus from wanting results to steady, disciplined action; this purifies your intention.

vishnu_gita::355.verse_sanskrit:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि युष्मासु वा पुनः ।
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यानिभिर्गुणः ॥
vishnu_gita::355.verse_hindi: पृथिवी में स्वर्ग मे अथवा आप लोगों में ऐसा जीव नहीं है जो प्रकृति से उत्पन्न इन तीन गुणों से सम्मलित न हो
vishnu_gita::355.english_translation: There is no being on earth, in the higher realm, or among you that is not bound by the three qualities born of nature.
vishnu_gita::355.translation_literal: न (not) तदस्ति (there is) पृथिव्यां (on earth) वा (or) दिवि (in the higher realm) युष्मासु (among you) वा (or) पुनः (again) । सत्त्वं (essence) प्रकृतिजैः (born of nature) मुक्तं (free) यदेभिः (by which) स्यानि (are) भिर्गुणः (qualities) ॥
vishnu_gita::355.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::355.essence: No being exists without the influence of nature’s three fundamental qualities.
vishnu_gita::355.simple_meaning: Everything alive, everywhere, is influenced by three fundamental qualities that arise from nature.
vishnu_gita::355.simple_insight: You belong to the vast web shaped by three basic forces of nature.
vishnu_gita::355.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that no living being on earth, in the higher realm, or among the listeners is free from the three inherent qualities that arise from nature. This sets the foundation for understanding how these qualities influence behavior and perception.
vishnu_gita::355.modern_relevance: When you meet anyone, remember they are shaped by fundamental forces beyond their control, just like you.
vishnu_gita::355.insight: Recognizing the universal influence of these three qualities shifts your judgment from personal to compassionate understanding.

vishnu_gita::356.verse_sanskrit:
त्रैगुणयविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुणया: स्त निर्जर्रा
निर्द्वन्दा नित्यसत्त्वस्था निर्योगक्षेमकात्मकाः ॥
vishnu_gita::356.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! सब वेदों में तीनों गुणों का ही विषय है, तुम तीनों गुणों से रहित हो जाओ, सुख दुःखादि द्वन्द्वों से रहित हो जाओ, नित्य सत्त्वगुण में रहो, अलब्ध वस्तु के लाभ में और लब्ध वस्तु की रक्षा में यत्नशून्य हो जाओ एवं आत्मवान् अर्थात् अप्रमत्त हो जाओ
vishnu_gita::356.english_translation: O divine beings! All the Vedas deal with the three qualities, but you transcend them, free from dualities like pleasure and pain, established in eternal goodness, unattached to gain or protection, and ever vigilant as the true self.
vishnu_gita::356.translation_literal: त्रैगुणयविषया (three qualities subject) / वेदा (the Vedas) / निस्त्रैगुणया: (free from three qualities) / स्त (are) / निर्जर्रा (without old age) / निर्द्वन्दा (without dualities) / नित्यसत्त्वस्था (eternally established in goodness) / निर्योगक्षेमकात्मकाः (not striving for gain or protection)
vishnu_gita::356.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::356.essence: You can live beyond all changing qualities and dualities, steady in eternal goodness.
vishnu_gita::356.simple_meaning: Everything in the Vedas relates to three qualities, but you can go beyond them and their opposites, staying forever steady in goodness without clinging to gain or loss.
vishnu_gita::356.simple_insight: You can feel steady and free by not getting caught in life's ups and downs.
vishnu_gita::356.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that all sacred knowledge focuses on three qualities (gunas). He instructs them to transcend these qualities and the dualities of pleasure and pain, to be eternally established in goodness, unattached to gains or protection, and to remain fully conscious as the true self.
vishnu_gita::356.modern_relevance: When emotions swing wildly between success and failure, you can find balance by not letting those states define you.
vishnu_gita::356.insight: It teaches you to see beyond shifting qualities and outcomes, anchoring in unchanging goodness and awareness.

vishnu_gita::357.verse_sanskrit:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके ।
तावान् सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजाननः॥
vishnu_gita::357.verse_hindi: सब स्थान जलमें डूब जाने पर क्षुद्र जलाशय से जितना प्रयोजन रहता है, ब्रह्मनिष्ठ ब्रह्मज्ञ को सब वेदों से उतना ही प्रयोजन रहता है
vishnu_gita::357.english_translation: Just as a small pond is enough when the entire land is flooded, a Brahman devoted to Brahman gains all he needs from all the Vedas.
vishnu_gita::357.translation_literal: यावान् (as much as) अर्थ (purpose) उदपाने (in a small pond) सर्वतः (everywhere) सम्प्लुतोदके (in flooded water) तावान् (that much) सर्वेषु (in all) वेदेषु (Vedas) ब्राह्मणस्य (of the Brahman) विजाननः (knowing)
vishnu_gita::357.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::357.essence: Deep understanding makes vast knowledge feel small and fully satisfying.
vishnu_gita::357.simple_meaning: When someone truly understands the highest truth, even a small part of sacred knowledge is enough to satisfy them.
vishnu_gita::357.simple_insight: You can feel complete with little when your understanding is deep and steady.
vishnu_gita::357.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that just as a small pond suffices during a flood covering the land, a Brahman deeply rooted in Brahman finds full purpose in all the Vedas through a small portion of their knowledge. This highlights the sufficiency of deep insight over broad but shallow knowledge.
vishnu_gita::357.modern_relevance: You might have access to endless information online yet find peace and clarity in just a few trusted sources that truly resonate with you.
vishnu_gita::357.insight: It shifts the mind from seeking more knowledge to appreciating depth over breadth, trusting that true understanding is concise.

vishnu_gita::358.verse_sanskrit:
चातुर्वण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां वित्ताकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
vishnu_gita::358.verse_hindi: मैंने गुण और कर्मों के विभाग द्वारा चारों वर्णों की सृष्टि की है, उनका कर्ता होने पर भी अव्यय होने के कारण मुझको अकर्ता जानो
vishnu_gita::358.english_translation: I created the four classes based on qualities and actions; though their doer, know me as the immutable non-doer.
