vishnu_gita::358.translation_literal: चातुर्वण्यं (four classes) मया (by me) सृष्टं (created) गुणकर्मविभागशः (according to quality and action division) । तस्य (of that) कर्तारमपि (even as doer) मां (me) वित्ताकर्तारमव्ययम् (immutable non-doer) ॥
vishnu_gita::358.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::358.essence: You act in roles shaped by qualities, but your true self remains unchanging and detached.
vishnu_gita::358.simple_meaning: The world’s social classes arise from qualities and actions, yet the creator behind them remains unchanged and not truly the doer.
vishnu_gita::358.simple_insight: Even when you perform your role, your true self remains steady and untouched.
vishnu_gita::358.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the four social classes arise from natural qualities and actions. Though he is the creator, he remains unaffected and does not act through ego, showing the difference between acting and being.
vishnu_gita::358.modern_relevance: You may play many roles in life—parent, worker, friend—but your true self is deeper than any role or action.
vishnu_gita::358.insight: It teaches you to see your actions as roles shaped by qualities, not as your unchanging true self.

vishnu_gita::359.verse_sanskrit:
ये चैव सात्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये।
मन एवेति तान वित्त न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
vishnu_gita::359.verse_hindi: जो सब सात्त्विकभाव, राजसिकभाव एवं तामसिकभाव हैं, वह सब मुझसे ही उत्पन्न हुए हैं ऐसा उनको जानो। मैं उन सब में नहीं हूँ परन्तु वह मुझमें हैं ।
vishnu_gita::359.english_translation: Know that all the sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic qualities arise from me; I am not in them, but they are in me.
vishnu_gita::359.translation_literal: ये (these) / चैव (indeed) / सात्विका (sattvic) / भावा (qualities) / राजसास्तामसाश्च (rajasic and tamasic) / ये (these) / मन (mind) / एवेति (only) / तान (them) / वित्त (know) / न (not) / त्वहं (I) / तेषु (in them) / ते (they) / मयि (in me)
vishnu_gita::359.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::359.essence: Qualities arise from the divine, but the divine transcends all qualities.
vishnu_gita::359.simple_meaning: All qualities of nature—pure, active, and dull—originate from the divine. The divine is not limited by these qualities but contains them all.
vishnu_gita::359.simple_insight: It feels freeing to know your true self is beyond the moods and traits you experience.
vishnu_gita::359.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the three fundamental qualities shaping nature and mind—purity (sattva), activity (rajas), and inertia (tamas)—all come from the divine source. Though these qualities appear to define existence, the divine itself is transcendent and untouched by them.
vishnu_gita::359.modern_relevance: When moods or traits overwhelm you, remember they come from a source greater than them—and you are not limited to them.
vishnu_gita::359.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with temporary qualities to recognizing a deeper, unchanging essence.

vishnu_gita::360.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयभावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥
vishnu_gita::360.verse_hindi: इन तीन गुणमय भावो से मोहित यह सब जगत् इन सब भावों से अतीत एवं निर्विकारस्वरूप मुझको नहीं जानता है ।
vishnu_gita::360.english_translation: This entire world is deluded by the three qualities and does not recognize me, the supreme imperishable, beyond them.
vishnu_gita::360.translation_literal: त्रिभिः (by three) गुणमयभावैः (qualities-made states) एभिः (by these) सर्वम् (all) इदं (this) जगत् (world) । मोहितं (deluded) न (not) अभिजानाति (knows) माम् (me) एभ्यः (from) परम (supreme) अव्ययम् (imperishable) ॥
vishnu_gita::360.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::360.essence: The true self is beyond all changing qualities that cloud perception.
vishnu_gita::360.simple_meaning: The world is trapped in three qualities that cause confusion and do not see the supreme, unchanging reality beyond them.
vishnu_gita::360.simple_insight: There’s freedom in realizing that your true self is untouched by changing qualities around you.
vishnu_gita::360.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that everything in the world appears influenced by three qualities, creating confusion. People fail to recognize the supreme, unchanging reality that lies beyond these qualities, obscured by this delusion.
vishnu_gita::360.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by moods or personality traits, forgetting your deeper, steady self beyond shifting feelings and thoughts.
vishnu_gita::360.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with fluctuating qualities to recognizing your unchanging inner reality.

vishnu_gita::361.verse_sanskrit:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
vishnu_gita::361.verse_hindi: यह मेरी सत्व आदि गुणमयी अलौकिक माया निश्चय ही दुस्तरा है, जो मुझको प्राप्त होते है वही इस मायाको अतिक्रमण कर सक्ते हैं
vishnu_gita::361.english_translation: This divine, composed of the three qualities, my supreme illusion is very difficult to cross; only those who surrender to me can transcend this illusion.
vishnu_gita::361.translation_literal: दैवी (divine) हि (indeed) एषा (this) गुणमयी (composed-of-gunas) मम (my) माया (illusion) दुरत्यया (very difficult) । मम (me) एव (only) ये (those who) प्रपद्यन्ते (surrender) मायामेतां (this illusion) तरन्ति (cross) ते (they) ॥
vishnu_gita::361.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::361.essence: Only surrender to the divine can overcome the most difficult cosmic illusion.
vishnu_gita::361.simple_meaning: The divine illusion made of the three qualities is very hard to cross, but those who fully surrender to the divine can overcome it.
vishnu_gita::361.simple_insight: You feel hope knowing surrender can break even the toughest illusions.
vishnu_gita::361.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that his cosmic illusion, made up of the qualities of nature, is very difficult to overcome. But those who seek refuge in him alone can cross beyond this powerful veil.
vishnu_gita::361.modern_relevance: When you face overwhelming confusion or obstacles, complete surrender to your inner guidance can help you break through.
vishnu_gita::361.insight: It teaches you that surrendering to the divine is the key to transcending deep confusion and limitation.

vishnu_gita::362.verse_sanskrit:
गुणत्रयस्य विज्ञानं गुरो ! तब मुखाम्बुजात् ।
कृतकृत्या वयं जाताः श्रुत्वा तन्महदद्भुतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::362.verse_hindi: हे गुरो ! हमलोग उस अत्यन्त अद्भुत गुणत्रय के विज्ञान को आपके मुखकमल से सुनकर कृतकृत्य हुए
vishnu_gita::362.english_translation: O teacher, having heard the profound knowledge of the three qualities from your lotus mouth, we feel deeply grateful.
vishnu_gita::362.translation_literal: गुणत्रयस्य (of the three qualities) / विज्ञानं (knowledge) / गुरो (O teacher) / तब (then) / मुखाम्बुजात् (from the lotus mouth) / कृतकृत्या (deeply grateful) / वयं (we) / जाताः (became) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / तन्महदद्भुतम् (that greatly wondrous)
vishnu_gita::362.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::362.essence: Gratitude arises from receiving profound knowledge directly from a teacher.
vishnu_gita::362.simple_meaning: We are deeply grateful after hearing the wonderful knowledge about the three qualities from the teacher.
vishnu_gita::362.simple_insight: Gratitude grows when profound truths are heard directly from a trusted guide.
vishnu_gita::362.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the disciples express heartfelt gratitude to their teacher after learning about the three fundamental qualities that shape existence, marking a pivotal moment of understanding.
vishnu_gita::362.insight: It shows the importance of gratitude and openness when receiving deep knowledge from a trusted source.

vishnu_gita::363.verse_sanskrit:
इदानीच वयं सर्वे भवतः कृपया विभो !।
रजस्तमोऽभिसंसक्ता नाऽधःपातं व्रजेम हि ॥
vishnu_gita::363.verse_hindi: हे विभो ! अब हम सब आपकी कृपा से रजोगुण तमोगुण में फंसकर अपने अवनति नहीं करेंगे
vishnu_gita::363.english_translation: Now, by your grace, O Lord, we all shall not sink into decline, caught in passion and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::363.translation_literal: इदानीच (now) वयं (we) सर्वे (all) भवतः (your) कृपया (by grace) विभो (O Lord) । रजस्तमोऽभिसंसक्ता (entangled in passion and ignorance) नाऽधःपातं (not downward fall) व्रजेम (may we go) हि (indeed) ॥
vishnu_gita::363.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::363.essence: Divine grace prevents falling into confusion and harmful passions.
vishnu_gita::363.simple_meaning: With the divine's kindness, we will avoid slipping into harmful states caused by passion and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::363.simple_insight: You can feel protected from decline by trusting in the divine's grace.
vishnu_gita::363.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the assembled speak to Vishnu, seeking his mercy to prevent them from falling into harmful states dominated by passion (rajas) and ignorance (tamas). They express hope that his grace will keep them steady and uplifted.
vishnu_gita::363.modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelming and confusion pulls you down, trusting a higher support can help you stay steady.
vishnu_gita::363.insight: It teaches you to rely on the divine's grace to stay clear from harmful, reactive impulses.

vishnu_gita::364.verse_sanskrit:
कृपासिन्धो ! वयं येन ज्ञानेन त्रिगुणस्य वै।
रहस्यं द्रष्टुमर्हाः स्मः प्रत्यक्षं सर्वदैव हि ॥
vishnu_gita::364.verse_hindi: हे कृपानिधे ! हमें वह ज्ञान बताइये कि जिस ज्ञान से हम त्रिगुण के रहस्य को प्रत्यक्ष करने में सदा ही समर्थ हो
vishnu_gita::364.english_translation: O ocean of compassion, please reveal the knowledge by which we can always perceive the secret of the three qualities directly.
vishnu_gita::364.translation_literal: कृपासिन्धो (ocean of compassion) / वयं (we) / येन (by which) / ज्ञानेन (knowledge) / त्रिगुणस्य (of the three qualities) / वै (indeed) / रहस्यं (secret) / द्रष्टुमर्हाः (worthy to see) / स्मः (we are) / प्रत्यक्षं (directly) / सर्वदैव (always) / हि (indeed)
vishnu_gita::364.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::364.essence: With the right knowledge, you can always directly perceive the hidden truth of the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::364.simple_meaning: You can gain knowledge that lets you directly perceive the secret behind the three qualities that shape everything.
vishnu_gita::364.simple_insight: There's hope in knowing you can uncover hidden truths anytime with the right understanding.
vishnu_gita::364.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker appeals to the compassionate one to reveal the knowledge that makes the hidden nature of the three qualities always visible and clear.
vishnu_gita::364.modern_relevance: You want to understand the patterns and forces shaping your behavior, not just guess but see clearly what's behind them.
vishnu_gita::364.insight: It encourages active seeking of knowledge that reveals underlying truths rather than accepting surface appearances.

vishnu_gita::365.verse_sanskrit:
तथैव सर्वदाऽस्मासु शक्तिस्त्रिगुणदर्शिनी ।
विशेषतोऽनिशं तिष्ठत्तजज्ञानं नः समादिश ॥
vishnu_gita::365.verse_hindi: और त्रिगुण को विशेष रूप से निरन्तर देखने की शक्ति हम लोगों में सदा बनी रहे
vishnu_gita::365.english_translation: May the power to continually perceive the three qualities clearly always remain within us.
vishnu_gita::365.translation_literal: तथैव (in the same way) / सर्वदाऽस्मासु (always in us all) / शक्तिस्त्रिगुणदर्शिनी (the power to see the three qualities) / विशेषतोऽनिशं (especially continuously) / तिष्ठत् (remain) / अजज्ञानं (ignorance) / नः (our) / समादिश (may it be removed)
vishnu_gita::365.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::365.essence: Sustained power to clearly perceive the three qualities frees us from ignorance.
vishnu_gita::365.simple_meaning: You can maintain the ability to clearly see the three qualities of nature without losing focus.
vishnu_gita::365.simple_insight: You feel empowered by a steady clear vision that cuts through confusion.
vishnu_gita::365.detailed_meaning: Vishnu encourages sustaining the power to observe the three gunas—sattva, rajas, and tamas—without interruption, to overcome ignorance and understand reality better.
vishnu_gita::365.modern_relevance: When emotions and thoughts pull you every which way, steady clarity helps you keep your balance and see what really drives you.
vishnu_gita::365.insight: It teaches you to cultivate continuous clear awareness of your inner tendencies, reducing confusion.

vishnu_gita::366.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिदशा:! त्रिगुणैनिर्त्यम सृष्टिस्थित्तिलाया इमे ।
प्रपञ्चात्मकदृश्यस्य भवन्तीत्यवधार्यताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::366.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! त्रिगुण के द्वारा दृश्य प्रपंच के यह सृष्टि स्थिति लय नित्य होते हैं, वह जानो
vishnu_gita::366.english_translation: O divine beings, know that the visible world arises, exists, and dissolves eternally through the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::366.translation_literal: त्रिदशा: (three states) / त्रिगुणैः (by three qualities) / नित्यं (eternally) / सृष्टि (creation) / स्थिति (existence) / लय (dissolution) / इमे (these) / प्रपञ्चात्मक (manifested world) / दृश्यस्य (visible) / भवन्ति (are) / इति (thus) / अवधार्यताम् (should be understood)
vishnu_gita::366.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::366.essence: The visible world continuously cycles through creation, existence, and dissolution by three fundamental qualities.
vishnu_gita::366.simple_meaning: Everything you see in the world is created, maintained, and dissolved continuously by three fundamental qualities.
vishnu_gita::366.simple_insight: Understanding the world's constant change helps you see beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::366.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings explaining that the entire manifested world undergoes continuous cycles of creation, preservation, and destruction. These processes happen eternally through three fundamental qualities, revealing the nature of reality beyond surface appearances.
vishnu_gita::366.modern_relevance: When your plans shift or life feels unstable, remember everything you experience flows through cycles shaped by underlying forces beyond your control.
vishnu_gita::366.insight: It teaches you to recognize that change and impermanence are natural expressions of deeper qualities governing existence.

vishnu_gita::367.verse_sanskrit:
त्रिभावेनैव ते सर्वे ज्ञायन्ते च विशेषतः।
त्रिभावव्यक्षिका चाऽस्ति तत्त्वज्ञानोन्नतिः किल ॥
vishnu_gita::367.verse_hindi: और त्रिभाव के द्वारा ही वह सब विशेष रूप से जाने जाते हैं और तत्त्वज्ञान की उन्नति ही त्रिभावव्यंजिका है
vishnu_gita::367.english_translation: All things are known distinctly through the three modes; the highest wisdom reveals these three modes clearly.
vishnu_gita::367.translation_literal: त्रिभावेनैव (by the three modes alone) / ते (they) / सर्वे (all) / ज्ञायन्ते (are known) / च (and) / विशेषतः (distinctly). / त्रिभावव्यक्षिका (that which reveals the three modes) / चाऽस्ति (is indeed) / तत्त्वज्ञानोन्नतिः (the elevation of true knowledge) / किल (indeed).
vishnu_gita::367.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::367.essence: Clear understanding arises by distinctly seeing the three fundamental modes behind all things.
vishnu_gita::367.simple_meaning: Everything is understood clearly through the three modes that shape reality. True knowledge comes from seeing these modes distinctly.
vishnu_gita::367.simple_insight: Clarity comes from recognizing the patterns behind all things, bringing calm understanding.
vishnu_gita::367.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the three fundamental modes (gunas) underlie all phenomena. Understanding these modes distinctly is the sign of advanced wisdom, revealing the true nature behind appearances.
vishnu_gita::367.modern_relevance: When you notice the patterns behind your moods or choices, your insight deepens and confusion fades.
vishnu_gita::367.insight: It teaches you to focus on seeing the underlying modes shaping experience, not just surface events.

vishnu_gita::368.verse_sanskrit:
मयि यत् सच्चिदानन्दरूपेणाऽस्ति दिवौकसः!।
मूलमध्यात्मभावस्याधिदेवस्य तथैव च ॥
vishnu_gita::368.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! मुझमें जो सत् चित् और आनन्दरूप से अध्यात्मभाव अधिदैवभाव और
vishnu_gita::368.english_translation: O radiant beings! That which exists in me is of the nature of truth, consciousness, and bliss; it is the essential spiritual nature and the supreme divine.
vishnu_gita::368.translation_literal: मयि (in me) यत् (that which) सच्चिदानन्दरूपेण (truth-consciousness-bliss form) अस्ती (exists) दिवौकसः (radiant beings)! मूलमध्यात्मभावस्य (root-middle spiritual nature) अधिदेवस्य (supreme divine) तथैव च (and likewise).
vishnu_gita::368.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::368.essence: The true self is unchanging truth, consciousness, and bliss within all beings.
vishnu_gita::368.simple_meaning: The divine within is the true self, made of truth, awareness, and bliss; it is the essential spiritual nature and highest divine power.
vishnu_gita::368.simple_insight: There is a radiant, blissful truth at the core of all existence, including you.
vishnu_gita::368.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses luminous beings, revealing that the essence within him is the unchanging reality of truth, consciousness, and bliss, representing both the spiritual core and the supreme divine power.
vishnu_gita::368.insight: It invites you to recognize your inner being as pure awareness and joy beyond change.

vishnu_gita::369.verse_sanskrit:
अधिभूतस्य भावस्य ज्ञापकन्तु तदेव हि ।
तटस्थज्ञानसाहाय्यात्रिगुणस्य मतं बुधाः ॥
vishnu_gita::369.verse_hindi: अधिभूतभाव का मूल विद्यमान है, वही हे विशो ! तटस्थज्ञान की सहायता से त्रिगुण का ज्ञापक माना गया है
vishnu_gita::369.english_translation: The fundamental nature of the material world is known through detached knowledge, which helps the wise perceive the three qualities.
vishnu_gita::369.translation_literal: अधिभूतस्य (of the material nature) भावस्य (essence) ज्ञापकन्तु (knowing) तदेव (that alone) हि (indeed) । तटस्थज्ञानसाहाय्यात्रि (with the help of detached knowledge) गुणस्य (of the three qualities) मतं (opinion) बुधाः (the wise) ॥
vishnu_gita::369.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::369.essence: Detached knowledge reveals the true nature of the material world and its qualities.
vishnu_gita::369.simple_meaning: You grasp the true nature of the material world by using detached, unbiased knowledge to see beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::369.simple_insight: There’s freedom in stepping back from your feelings and seeing things clearly without bias.
vishnu_gita::369.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the essence of the changing natural world is understood by wise people through detached knowledge. This helps them perceive the three qualities—sattva, rajas, and tamas—without getting caught in their influence.
vishnu_gita::369.modern_relevance: When emotions cloud your judgment, stepping back and observing without attachment lets you see what’s really happening beneath the surface.
vishnu_gita::369.insight: It teaches you to cultivate an observer’s mind that watches without reacting, revealing the true nature of what you face.

vishnu_gita::370.verse_sanskrit:
अविद्याऽऽवरिका ज्ञेया मत्स्वरूपस्य निश्चितम् ।
पुष्टिस्तस्याश्च रजसा तमसैव विजायते ॥
vishnu_gita::370.verse_hindi: मेरे स्वरूपज्ञान को आवरण करने वाली अविद्या को ही जानो। रज और तमोगुण के द्वारा ही विद्या की पुष्टि होती है
vishnu_gita::370.english_translation: Ignorance is the veil that hides the true nature of the self; the qualities of passion and darkness support this ignorance.
vishnu_gita::370.translation_literal: अविद्या (ignorance) / आवरिका (veil/covering) / ज्ञेया (to be known) / मत् (my) / स्वरूपस्य (true nature) / निश्चितम् (certain) / पुष्टिः (support) / तस्याः (of that) / अश्च (and) / रजसा (by passion) / तमसैव (indeed by darkness) / विजायते (is born/arises)
vishnu_gita::370.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::370.essence: Ignorance veils the true self and is sustained by passion and darkness.
vishnu_gita::370.simple_meaning: Ignorance is like a veil covering the true self. It is sustained by the qualities of passion and darkness within us.
vishnu_gita::370.simple_insight: It’s comforting to know that confusion about who you are comes from known forces, not from you.
vishnu_gita::370.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the true self is hidden by ignorance, which acts like a veil. This ignorance is not random but arises from the qualities of passion and darkness, which cloud clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::370.modern_relevance: When emotions like restlessness or depression overwhelm you, it’s often the inner forces of passion and darkness veiling your true nature.
vishnu_gita::370.insight: Recognizing ignorance as a veil supported by inner qualities helps shift focus from self-blame to understanding the source of confusion.

vishnu_gita::371.verse_sanskrit:
सत्त्वात्प्रकाशो विद्याया भवतीति विभाव्यनाम।
अविद्याऽऽवियते लोके यथा तच्छ्यतां सुगः ॥
vishnu_gita::371.verse_hindi: सत्त्वगुण के द्वारा विद्या का प्रकाश होता है वह जानो। हे देवतागण ! संसार में अविद्या जिस प्रकार से आवरण करती है वह सुनो
vishnu_gita::371.english_translation: Know that knowledge shines through the quality of goodness. Just as ignorance covers the world, listen to this truth.
vishnu_gita::371.translation_literal: सत्त्वात्प्रकाशो (from goodness shines) / विद्याया (of knowledge) / भवतीति (becomes) / विभाव्यनाम (to those who understand) / अविद्याऽऽवियते (ignorance covers) / लोके (in the world) / यथा (just as) / तच्छ्यतां (let that be heard) / सुगः (O devas)
vishnu_gita::371.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::371.essence: Goodness makes knowledge shine clearly, even though ignorance tries to hide it.
vishnu_gita::371.simple_meaning: Goodness (sattva) allows knowledge to shine clearly, even though ignorance tries to cover it in the world.
vishnu_gita::371.simple_insight: You can feel hope knowing goodness reveals truth despite confusion around you.
vishnu_gita::371.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains to celestial beings that the quality of goodness (sattva) makes knowledge visible and clear, while ignorance (avidya) acts like a veil that hides truth from the world.
vishnu_gita::371.modern_relevance: When confusion and misinformation cloud your mind, the inner quality of goodness helps your true understanding shine through.
vishnu_gita::371.insight: It teaches you to trust the presence of goodness within as the source of clear knowledge amid confusion.

vishnu_gita::372.verse_sanskrit:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाशनो महापाप्मा वित्तनमिह वैरिणम ॥
vishnu_gita::372.verse_hindi: रजोगुणसम्भूत अत्युग्र और दुष्पूरणीय काम और क्रोध को इस संसार में शत्रु समझो
vishnu_gita::372.english_translation: Desire and anger, born of the quality of passion, are fierce and difficult to satisfy; consider wealth in this world your enemy.
vishnu_gita::372.translation_literal: काम (desire) एष (this) क्रोध (anger) एष (this) रजोगुणसमुद्भवः (born of passion quality) । महाशनो (great eater) महापाप्मा (great evil) वित्तनमिह (wealth here) वैरिणम (enemy) ॥
vishnu_gita::372.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::372.essence: Desire, anger, and worldly wealth fiercely oppose your inner peace and true purpose.
vishnu_gita::372.simple_meaning: Desire and anger arise from passion and are hard to satisfy. Wealth in this world often opposes your wellbeing.
vishnu_gita::372.simple_insight: Recognizing desire, anger, and attachment to wealth as obstacles brings clarity and peace.
vishnu_gita::372.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that desire and anger grow from the passionate quality (rajas), making them intense and insatiable. He warns that attachment to wealth in the world acts like an enemy, disrupting inner balance and distracting from true purpose.
vishnu_gita::372.modern_relevance: You may chase money or react in anger, but these urges often drain your energy and cloud your judgment.
vishnu_gita::372.insight: It teaches you to see desire, anger, and wealth attachment as barriers to calm and wise action.

vishnu_gita::373.verse_sanskrit:
धूमेनावियते वह्निर्यथादशों मलेन च ।
यथोल्वेनाटतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::373.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार अग्नि धूम्रके द्वारा, शीशा धूल के द्वारा और गर्भ जरायु के द्वारा आवृत रहता है उसी प्रकार आत्मज्ञान काम के द्वारा आवृत रहता है।
vishnu_gita::373.english_translation: Just as fire is covered by smoke, glass by dust, and a fetus by a womb, similarly self-knowledge is covered by desire.
vishnu_gita::373.translation_literal: धूमेन (by smoke) / अवियते (is covered) / वह्नि (fire) / यथा (just as) / अडशों (glass) / मलेन (by dust) / च (and) / यथा (just as) / उल्ल्वेन (by womb) / अटतो (fetus) / गर्भस्तथा (womb similarly) / तेन (by that) / एदम् (this) / आवृतम् (covered)
vishnu_gita::373.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::373.essence: Desire only covers self-knowledge; it does not destroy it.
vishnu_gita::373.simple_meaning: Self-knowledge is hidden by desire just as fire is hidden by smoke or glass by dust.
vishnu_gita::373.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing desire only hides your true self, not destroys it.
vishnu_gita::373.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that self-knowledge is not lost but obscured by desire, like fire covered by smoke or a fetus hidden in the womb. This teaches that the true self remains, waiting beyond these coverings.
vishnu_gita::373.modern_relevance: When your mind is clouded by cravings or distractions, your inner clarity feels lost, though it remains beneath it all.
vishnu_gita::373.insight: It shifts your view from believing desire blocks your true self permanently to seeing it as a temporary veil.

vishnu_gita::374.verse_sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।
कामरूपेण भो देवाः ! दुष्प्ररेणानलेन च ॥
vishnu_gita::374.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! ज्ञानी के नित्य वैरी इस दुष्पूरणीय कामरूप अग्नि के द्वारा ज्ञान आच्छन्न है
vishnu_gita::374.english_translation: O radiant beings, knowledge is always veiled by the relentless fire of desire, the eternal enemy of the wise.
vishnu_gita::374.translation_literal: आवृतं (covered) ज्ञानम् (knowledge) एतेन (by this) ज्ञानिनः (of the wise) नित्यवैरिणा (by the eternal enemy) कामरूपेण (in the form of desire) भो (O) देवाः (radiant beings) दुष्प्ररेणानलेन (by the hard-to-extinguish) च (and) अनलेन (fire)
vishnu_gita::374.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::374.essence: Desire’s relentless fire always veils the clear knowing of the wise.
vishnu_gita::374.simple_meaning: Your natural wisdom is hidden by desire, which acts like a persistent, burning fire blocking clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::374.simple_insight: You feel the frustration of wanting blocking your inner clarity and peace.
vishnu_gita::374.detailed_meaning: Vishnu speaks to celestial beings, explaining that even the wisest have their knowledge obscured by a relentless force: desire. This desire burns like an unquenchable fire, preventing clear insight and freedom of mind.
vishnu_gita::374.modern_relevance: You find it hard to focus or think clearly when craving or wanting pulls your attention away like a distracting flame.
vishnu_gita::374.insight: Recognize how desire clouds your discernment and begin to see it as a barrier to clear wisdom.

vishnu_gita::375.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिर्स्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।
एतर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
vishnu_gita::375.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियां, मन और बुद्धि, इस काम के अधिष्ठान कहे जाते हैं, इन्हीं के द्वारा यह ज्ञान को प्राच्छन्न करके देही को मोहित किया करता है
vishnu_gita::375.english_translation: The senses, mind, and intellect are called the seat of action; they veil knowledge and delude the embodied self.
vishnu_gita::375.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणि (senses) / मनः (mind) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / स्यात् (are) / अस्थानम् (seat) / उच्यते (called) / एतः (these) / विमोहयति (deludes) / एषः (this) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / आवृत्य (covering) / देहिनम् (the embodied self)
vishnu_gita::375.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::375.essence: The senses, mind, and intellect veil true knowledge and confuse the embodied self.
vishnu_gita::375.simple_meaning: Your senses, mind, and intellect form the basis of your actions and create confusion by hiding clear understanding from your true self.
vishnu_gita::375.simple_insight: It's unsettling but freeing to realize your mind and senses can trick you away from your true clarity.
vishnu_gita::375.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the senses, mind, and intellect are like a foundation where actions arise. Yet they veil true knowledge and cause confusion for the embodied self, making it unaware of its deeper reality.
vishnu_gita::375.modern_relevance: When your emotions and thoughts overwhelm you, it feels like your true clarity is lost behind noise and distraction.
vishnu_gita::375.insight: Recognize that your perceptions and reasoning can cloud your awareness, encouraging you to look beyond them for truth.

vishnu_gita::376.verse_sanskrit:
यूयं तदिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य विबुधर्षभाः।
पाप्मानं प्रहतैनं हि ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
vishnu_gita::376.verse_hindi: इस कारण हे देवश्रेष्ठो! तुम पहले इन्द्रियों का संयम करके इस ज्ञान विज्ञाननाशक पापी काम को नाश करो
vishnu_gita::376.english_translation: Therefore, O best of the divine beings, first control the senses to destroy this sinful desire that destroys knowledge and wisdom.
vishnu_gita::376.translation_literal: यूयं (you all) / तद् (that) / इन्द्रियाणि (senses) / आदौ (first) / नियम्य (controlling) / विद्धर्षभाः (best of the wise) / पाप्मानं (sinful) / प्रहतै (destroying) / एतं (this) / हि (indeed) / ज्ञान-विज्ञान-नाशनम् (destroyer of knowledge and wisdom)
vishnu_gita::376.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::376.essence: Controlling your senses first is key to destroying desire that destroys wisdom.
vishnu_gita::376.simple_meaning: You must first control your senses to overcome desire that destroys your knowledge and wisdom.
vishnu_gita::376.simple_insight: You can protect your clarity by mastering your impulses before they lead you astray.
vishnu_gita::376.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu instructs the listener to first restrain the senses, which are the gateways for desires that harm knowledge and wisdom. By controlling these impulses, one prevents the loss of insight and clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::376.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by impulses—like scrolling endlessly or reacting emotionally—gaining control helps protect your focus and clarity.
vishnu_gita::376.insight: It teaches you to redirect your attention from reactive impulses to disciplined sense control, preserving clear understanding.

vishnu_gita::377.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
vishnu_gita::377.verse_hindi: देह की अपेक्षा इन्द्रियाँ श्रेष्ठ हैं इन्द्रियों की अपेक्षा मन श्रेष्ठ है, मन की अपेक्षा बुद्धि श्रेष्ठ है और जो बुद्धि से श्रेष्ठ है वही आत्मा है
vishnu_gita::377.english_translation: The organs are said to be superior to the body; the mind is superior to the organs; the intellect is superior to the mind; and the true self is superior to the intellect.
vishnu_gita::377.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / पराणि (greater) / आहुः (are said) / इन्द्रियेभ्यः (than the organs) / परं (beyond) / मनः (mind) / मनसः (of the mind) / तु (but) / परा (higher) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / यो (who) / बुद्धेः (than the intellect) / परतः (above) / तु (but) / सः (that)
vishnu_gita::377.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::377.essence: You exist beyond body, senses, mind, and intellect as the true self.
vishnu_gita::377.simple_meaning: There is a hierarchy: senses are above the body, mind above senses, intellect above mind, and beyond intellect lies the true self.
vishnu_gita::377.simple_insight: You can feel yourself beyond your thoughts, senses, and body as something deeper and unchanging.
vishnu_gita::377.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains the inner hierarchy from the physical body to the true self. He shows how sense organs are higher than the body, the restless mind is higher than senses, the discerning intellect surpasses the mind, and beyond intellect is the true self, untouched by change.
vishnu_gita::377.modern_relevance: When your thoughts overwhelm you, remember you are not just your mind or senses but something deeper that observes all.
vishnu_gita::377.insight: It shifts your attention inward from external sensations and mental processes to the unchanging true self beyond intellect.

vishnu_gita::378.verse_sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धे परं बुद्धवा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।
हत शत्रु सुरश्रेष्ठा: ! कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
vishnu_gita::378.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्ठो ! इस प्रकार बुद्धि की अपेक्षा श्रेष्ठ आत्मा को जानकर और बुद्धि के द्वारा मन को संयत करके काम रूप दुर्निवार शत्रु का नाश करो
vishnu_gita::378.english_translation: O best of gods! Knowing the supreme true self beyond the intellect, restrain your mind by that intellect and destroy the insurmountable enemy called desire.
vishnu_gita::378.translation_literal: एवं (thus) बुद्धे (than intellect) परं (supreme) बुद्धवा (knowing) संस्तभ्यात्मानम् (restraining the self) आत्मना (by the self) । हत (destroyed) शत्रु (enemy) सुरश्रेष्ठाः (best of gods) ! कामरूपं (form of desire) दुरासदम् (hard to overcome) ॥
vishnu_gita::378.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::378.essence: Knowing your highest self empowers you to control the mind and defeat desire.
vishnu_gita::378.simple_meaning: By recognizing the highest true self beyond intellect and using intellect to control the mind, you can conquer the powerful enemy called desire.
vishnu_gita::378.simple_insight: You gain strength when your mind follows your highest self, not fleeting wants.
vishnu_gita::378.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs that understanding the supreme true self beyond mere intellect allows one to use that intellect to restrain the restless mind. This control defeats desire, seen as a relentless enemy obstructing spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::378.modern_relevance: When cravings pull you away, knowing your deeper self helps you steady your focus and resist temptation.
vishnu_gita::378.insight: It teaches you to apply your intellect as a tool to discipline your restless mind and weaken desire’s hold.

vishnu_gita::379.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः ।
मूढ़ोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम्
vishnu_gita::379.verse_hindi: महामायाके द्वारा आवृत होने के कारण मुझे सब नहीं देख सकते हैं। यह मूढ़ संसार मुझे अजन्मा और अविनाशी नहीं जानता है
vishnu_gita::379.english_translation: I am not the light of all because I am veiled by the yoga-maya; the deluded world does not know me as unborn and imperishable.
vishnu_gita::379.translation_literal: नाहं (I am not) प्रकाशः (light) सर्वस्य (of all) योगमायासमावृतः (covered by yoga-maya) । मूढ़ः (the deluded) अयं (this) न (not) अभिजानाति (knows) लोको (the world) माम् (me) अजम् (unborn) अव्ययम् (imperishable)
vishnu_gita::379.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::379.essence: The true self is hidden by illusion and misunderstood by the confused world.
vishnu_gita::379.simple_meaning: The divine presence is hidden by a powerful illusion, so most people fail to see it as eternal and unchanging.
vishnu_gita::379.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing your true nature is beyond the confusion around you.
vishnu_gita::379.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that although he is the supreme reality, a powerful cosmic illusion called yoga-maya hides him from most beings, who mistakenly see the world and themselves as born and perishable.
vishnu_gita::379.modern_relevance: At times, you feel lost in confusion and fail to recognize the steady presence inside yourself that never changes.
vishnu_gita::379.insight: This shifts your view from identifying with the fleeting world to recognizing the unchanging essence beneath appearances.

vishnu_gita::380.verse_sanskrit:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्त्तमानानि चामरा: !।
भविष्याणि च भूतानि मान्तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
vishnu_gita::380.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! मैं भूत भविष्यत् और वर्तमान काल में स्थित समस्त स्थावर जंगम प्राणियों को जानता हूँ परन्तु मुझको कोई नहीं जानता है
vishnu_gita::380.english_translation: O radiant beings! I know all beings past, present, and future, but no one knows me.
vishnu_gita::380.translation_literal: वेदाहं (I know) समतीतानि (past) वर्त्तमानानि (present) चामरा: (and future) । भविष्याणि (future) च (and) भूतानि (beings) मान्तु (but) वेद (knows) न (not) कश्चन (anyone)
vishnu_gita::380.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::380.essence: Knowing everything does not mean being known by anything.
vishnu_gita::380.simple_meaning: The speaker knows all beings across time but remains unknown to anyone else.
vishnu_gita::380.simple_insight: There is a solitude in being the source that knows all yet is not known.
vishnu_gita::380.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, claiming complete knowledge of all beings—past, present, and future—but reveals that no being truly knows him. This highlights the mystery of the supreme reality's hiddenness despite its omniscience.
vishnu_gita::380.modern_relevance: You might understand everyone around you deeply, yet feel that no one truly understands you.
vishnu_gita::380.insight: It shifts your mind to recognize that knowing others does not guarantee being known yourself.

vishnu_gita::381.verse_sanskrit:
इच्छोद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन निर्जराः।
सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्त्यसुरारयः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::381.verse_hindi: हे असुरशत्रु देवतागण ! इच्छा और द्वेष से सम्भूत द्वन्द्व के मोह से सृष्टिकाल में सब जीव सम्मोह को प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::381.english_translation: O enemies of the Asuras and hosts of the Devas! At creation, all beings fall into delusion born from conflict of desire and aversion.
vishnu_gita::381.translation_literal: इच्छोद्वेषसमुत्थेन (from desire-aversion arising) / द्वन्द्वमोहेन (from conflict-delusion) / निर्जराः (ageless) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / सम्मोहं (delusion) / सर्गे (at creation) / यान्ति (go) / असुरारयः (enemies of the Asuras and their hosts)
vishnu_gita::381.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::381.essence: All beings begin with confusion born from conflicting desires and aversions.
vishnu_gita::381.simple_meaning: All living beings begin their existence confused because of the inner conflict caused by wanting some things and rejecting others.
vishnu_gita::381.simple_insight: You can feel how wanting and rejecting cloud your mind and create confusion.
vishnu_gita::381.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the cosmic enemies, describing how at the moment of creation, all beings become caught in confusion caused by inner conflicts of desire and aversion, which leads them into a state of delusion.
vishnu_gita::381.modern_relevance: You notice how often your mind flips between craving something and pushing something away, trapping you in confusion that feels like it has been there since the beginning.
vishnu_gita::381.insight: Recognize that the root of confusion is the conflict between wanting and rejecting, which distorts your perception of reality.

vishnu_gita::382.verse_sanskrit:
येपान्त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।
ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥
vishnu_gita::382.verse_hindi: किन्तु जिन पुण्यात्मा व्यक्तियों का पाप नष्ट हो गया है वे इन्द्रजनित मोह से रहित होकर दृढ़वत होते हुए मेरी भक्ति में रत रहते हैं
vishnu_gita::382.english_translation: But those virtuous people whose sins have been destroyed, free from the delusion of the senses born of Indra, remain steadfast and devoted to me.
vishnu_gita::382.translation_literal: ये (those) पान्त्वन्तगतं (destroyed) पापं (sin) जनानां (of people) पुण्यकर्मणाम् (virtuous deeds) । ते (they) द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मक्ता (free from duality-delusion) भजन्ते (worship) मां (me) दृढव्रताः (steadfast) ॥
vishnu_gita::382.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::382.essence: True devotion blossoms when inner faults and sensory illusions are overcome.
vishnu_gita::382.simple_meaning: People who have overcome their wrong actions and freed themselves from confusing desires remain firmly devoted to the divine.
vishnu_gita::382.simple_insight: Steadiness in devotion grows when you release inner faults and illusions.
vishnu_gita::382.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that those who have purified themselves by overcoming sinful actions and sensory delusions become firmly committed in their love and service to the divine, showing the power of inner transformation.
vishnu_gita::382.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in cycles of regret and distraction, but when you let go of those burdens, your connection to what truly matters becomes steady and clear.
vishnu_gita::382.insight: It shows how shedding inner confusion and past mistakes helps you develop unwavering devotion.

vishnu_gita::383.verse_sanskrit:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये।
ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्म कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
vishnu_gita::383.verse_hindi: जरा और मरण से बचने के लिये मेरा आश्रय करके जो प्रयत्न करते हैं वह उस ब्रह्म को, समस्त अध्यात्म को और समस्त कर्म को जानते हैं
vishnu_gita::383.english_translation: Those who seek refuge in me striving to transcend old age and death know that supreme reality, all spirituality, and all action completely.
vishnu_gita::383.translation_literal: जरामरणमोक्षाय (old age-death-freedom-for) / मामाश्रित्य (me-as refuge-taking) / यतन्ति (strive) / ये (those) / ते (they) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / तद्विदुः (that-know) / कृत्स्नम् (complete) / अध्यात्म (spirituality) / कर्म (action) / च (and) / अखिलम् (all)
vishnu_gita::383.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::383.essence: Seeking refuge in the divine reveals complete knowledge of reality, spirituality, and action.
vishnu_gita::383.simple_meaning: Those who turn to the divine to overcome aging and death understand the supreme reality, complete spirituality, and all action fully.
vishnu_gita::383.simple_insight: There is deep assurance in knowing that surrendering to the divine connects you to everything truly lasting.
vishnu_gita::383.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that those who seek refuge in him to overcome old age and death truly grasp the supreme reality, the full spiritual path, and all actions. This moment reveals how devotion leads to comprehensive understanding and freedom.
vishnu_gita::383.modern_relevance: When facing fears of aging or loss, turning to your inner refuge opens awareness beyond these limits to deeper wholeness.
vishnu_gita::383.insight: It shifts your focus from fearing decay to embracing the divine as the source of all existence and action.

vishnu_gita::384.verse_sanskrit:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च य विदु:।
प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
vishnu_gita::384.verse_hindi: जो मुझको अधिदैव अधिभूत और अधियज्ञ के सहित जानते हैं मुझमें आसक्तचित्त वह मरणकाल में भी मुझको जानते हैं
vishnu_gita::384.english_translation: Those who understand me as the inner deity, the essence of all beings, and the supreme sacrificial principle, know me even at the time of death with a devoted mind.
vishnu_gita::384.translation_literal: साधि (accomplished) भूत (beings) अधि (above) देवं (deity) मां (me) साधि (accomplished) यज्ञं (sacrifice) च (and) य (who) विदु: (know) प्रयाणकाले (at the time of departure) अपि (also) च (and) मां (me) ते (they) विदु: (know) युक्तचेतसः (with joined/devoted mind)
vishnu_gita::384.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::384.essence: True devotion perceives the divine within and endures beyond death.
vishnu_gita::384.simple_meaning: Those who recognize the divine as the inner force in all beings and the ultimate sacred principle, keep that devotion even at death.
vishnu_gita::384.simple_insight: You can carry steady devotion that stays strong even when facing death.
vishnu_gita::384.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that those who perceive him not just as a distant deity but as the inner divine in all beings and the essence behind sacred sacrifice maintain devoted awareness even when leaving the body.
vishnu_gita::384.modern_relevance: When facing life’s hardest moments, like loss or endings, your steady devotion can be a source of inner strength and clarity.
vishnu_gita::384.insight: It teaches you to cultivate a devoted mind that remains connected to the divine beyond life’s transitions.

vishnu_gita::385.verse_sanskrit:
किं तब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म परमेश्वर ।
अधिभूतञ्च किं मोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::385.verse_hindi: हे परमेश्वर ! वह ब्रह्म क्या है, अध्यात्म क्या है, कर्म क्या है, अधिभूत किसको कहा गया है, अधिदैव किसको कहते हैं,
vishnu_gita::385.english_translation: O supreme being! What is Brahman? What is the inner self? What is action? What is called the physical realm? What is called the divine realm?
vishnu_gita::385.translation_literal: किं (what) तब् (then) ब्रह्म (Brahman) किं (what) अध्यात्मं (inner self) किं (what) कर्म (action) परमेश्वर (supreme being) । अधिभूतञ्च (physical realm and) किं (what) मोक्त (liberated) अधिदैवं (divine realm) किमुच्यते (called) ॥
vishnu_gita::385.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::385.essence: Deep questions about reality and self open the path to true understanding.
vishnu_gita::385.simple_meaning: This verse asks fundamental questions about the supreme reality, the true self, action, and the different levels of existence.
vishnu_gita::385.simple_insight: It invites you to open your mind and question the nature of reality beyond surface appearances.
vishnu_gita::385.detailed_meaning: In this moment, a seeker addresses the supreme being, seeking clarity about core concepts: Brahman (the supreme reality), Atman (inner self), Karma (action), and the realms of existence, setting the stage for deep inquiry.
vishnu_gita::385.modern_relevance: When confusion clouds your mind, asking clear questions about your true nature and the world can open new perspectives.
vishnu_gita::385.insight: It encourages shifting from assumptions to active inquiry about existence and the self.

vishnu_gita::386.verse_sanskrit:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन् दैत्यमूदन।
प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥
vishnu_gita::386.verse_hindi: इस देह में  अधियज्ञ कौन है और कैसे वह इस देह में स्थित है और हे दैत्य सूदन ! आप मरणकाल में संयतात्मा व्यक्तियों के द्वारा कैसे जाने जाते हैं
vishnu_gita::386.english_translation: Who is the supreme sacrificer in this body, and how does he reside here? O Daityamudana, how is he known by those with self-control at the time of death?
vishnu_gita::386.translation_literal: अधियज्ञः (supreme sacrificer) कथं (how) कोऽत्र (who here) देहेऽस्मिन् (in this body) दैत्यमूदन (O Daityamudana) । प्रयाणकाले (at the time of death) च (and) कथं (how) ज्ञेयोऽसि (are you known) नियतात्मभिः (by self-controlled persons) ॥
vishnu_gita::386.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::386.essence: The supreme presence within the body is recognized by the disciplined at life's final moment.
vishnu_gita::386.simple_meaning: There is a supreme presence within your body, known by disciplined people especially when life ends.
vishnu_gita::386.simple_insight: You are not just your body; something profound shows itself when life is ending.
vishnu_gita::386.detailed_meaning: Vishnu asks Daityamudana who the supreme sacrificer is inside the body and how disciplined people recognize this presence at death, highlighting a key moment for spiritual insight.
vishnu_gita::386.modern_relevance: When facing loss or watching a loved one near death, you sense something deeper beyond the physical body.
vishnu_gita::386.insight: It teaches you to look beyond the physical and recognize a deeper presence especially in critical moments.

vishnu_gita::387.verse_sanskrit:
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥
vishnu_gita::387.verse_hindi: परम अक्षर जिसका क्षय नहीं है अर्थात् जगत का मूल कारण वही ब्रह्म है, स्वभाव ही अर्थात आत्मभाव ही  अध्यात्म कहा जाता है, भूतभावोद्भवकर अर्थात् सकल प्राणिमात्र की उत्पत्ति और स्थिति करने वाला जो विसर्ग अर्थात् त्याग है वहीं कर्म है
vishnu_gita::387.english_translation: The imperishable supreme reality is called the true self; the source and sustainer of all beings is the act known as karma.
vishnu_gita::387.translation_literal: अक्षरं (imperishable) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / परमं (supreme) / स्वभावः (nature) / अध्यात्मम् (true self) / उच्यते (is called) / भूतभावोद्भवकरः (source of beings) / विसर्गः (act of release) / कर्मसंज्ञितः (called karma)
vishnu_gita::387.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::387.essence: The unchanging true self is the source from which all beings and their actions arise.
vishnu_gita::387.simple_meaning: The true self is the imperishable essence behind everything. The natural origin and source of all beings and their actions is the process called karma.
vishnu_gita::387.simple_insight: You can rest in knowing your true self never changes, even as life unfolds around you.
vishnu_gita::387.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the supreme reality, which never decays, is the true self within everyone. This self is the natural source of all living beings and the origin of all actions, which are expressions of this underlying nature.
vishnu_gita::387.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic, remembering your unchanging true self can bring calm and clarity amidst constant change.
vishnu_gita::387.insight: It shifts the mind to see karma not just as actions but as natural expressions arising from your true self.

vishnu_gita::388.verse_sanskrit:
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम्।
अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृताम्बराः !॥
vishnu_gita::388.verse_hindi: हे देहधारियों में श्रेष्ठो! नाशवान् भाव देहादि अधिभूत हैं पुरुष स्वांशभूत सब दैवी शक्तियों का अधिपति अधिदैव है और इन शरीरों में मैं ही अधियज्ञ कूटस्थ चैतन्य हूँ
vishnu_gita::388.english_translation: O best among those who bear bodies! The perishable nature of the body is the physical realm; the true self is the lord of all divine powers; I am the inner controller and consciousness within these bodies.
vishnu_gita::388.translation_literal: अधिभूतं (the physical realm) क्षरो (perishable) भावः (nature) पुरुषः (true self) च (and) अधिदैवतम् (lord of divine powers) अधियज्ञः (inner controller) अहम् (I) एव (indeed) अत्र (here) देहे (in the body) देहभृत (bearers of bodies) अम्बराः (all)
vishnu_gita::388.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::388.essence: Your true self is the eternal inner controller beyond the perishable body.
vishnu_gita::388.simple_meaning: The body is perishable and part of the physical world, but the true self inside is the supreme controller and source of divine power within.
vishnu_gita::388.simple_insight: You are not just your changing body; a powerful inner presence guides you always.
vishnu_gita::388.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses those embodied beings, explaining that the body and its nature are perishable and belong to the physical realm. Beyond this, the true self (Purusha) is the master of all divine forces and the inner conscious controller present in every body.
vishnu_gita::388.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your changing emotions and physical limits, remembering that your true self is beyond these can bring calm and clarity.
vishnu_gita::388.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with the body to recognizing your inner conscious presence as the true source of control.

vishnu_gita::389.verse_sanskrit:
ओंतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥
vishnu_gita::389.verse_hindi: ॐ तत सत्, यह तीन ब्रह्म के नाम हैं, इन तीनों के द्वारा पूर्वकाल में ब्राह्मण, वेद और यज्ञो की सृष्टि हुई थी।
vishnu_gita::389.english_translation: Om Tat Sat are three names of Brahman; through these three, Brahmins, Vedas, and sacrifices were created in ancient times.
vishnu_gita::389.translation_literal: ओंतत्सदिति (Om Tat Sat are) / निर्देशः (instruction) / ब्रह्मणः (of Brahman) / त्रिविधः (threefold) / स्मृतः (remembered) / ब्राह्मणाः (Brahmins) / तेन (by that) / वेदाः (Vedas) / च (and) / यज्ञाः (sacrifices) / च (and) / विहिताः (established) / पुरा (in ancient times)
vishnu_gita::389.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::389.essence: Three sacred sounds embody the origin of sacred knowledge, priests, and rituals.
vishnu_gita::389.simple_meaning: The sacred syllables Om, Tat, and Sat represent the supreme reality and have given rise to priests, scriptures, and rituals since ancient times.
vishnu_gita::389.simple_insight: You are connected to a timeless source that shaped knowledge and sacred practice.
vishnu_gita::389.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the three sacred terms Om, Tat, and Sat symbolize the supreme reality. These three formed the foundation from which priests (Brahmins), sacred texts (Vedas), and rituals (Yajnas) originated long ago.
vishnu_gita::389.modern_relevance: When you chant or reflect on Om Tat Sat, you tap into the deep roots of spiritual knowledge and practice that shaped culture.
vishnu_gita::389.insight: It teaches you to recognize the power of foundational spiritual sounds that shape tradition and inner understanding.

vishnu_gita::390.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।
प्रवर्त्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम ॥
vishnu_gita::390.verse_hindi: इसी कारण ओम, यह शब्द उच्चारण करके ब्रह्मवादियों के  शास्त्रोक्त यज्ञ दान और तप कर्म निरन्तर सम्पन्न हुआ करते हैं
vishnu_gita::390.english_translation: Therefore, by uttering the syllable Om, the scripture-prescribed acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity are continuously performed by the followers of Brahman.
vishnu_gita::390.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) ओमिति (Om - thus called) उद्धृत्य (having been uttered) यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः (sacrifice, charity, austerity acts) प्रवर्तन्ते (are performed) विधानोक्ताः (as prescribed by scriptures) सततं (continuously) ब्रह्मवादिनाम् (of the followers of Brahman)
vishnu_gita::390.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::390.essence: The utterance of Om sustains continuous sacred action by those devoted to Brahman.
vishnu_gita::390.simple_meaning: Uttering the sound Om supports continuous sacred actions like sacrifice, charity, and austerity as prescribed by scripture.
vishnu_gita::390.simple_insight: There is strength in a simple, consistent spiritual practice rooted in a sacred sound.
vishnu_gita::390.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the sacred syllable Om is the foundation for the continuous performance of important spiritual acts like sacrifice, charity, and austerity by those who follow the teachings of Brahman. This moment reveals how a simple sound connects to sustained discipline.
vishnu_gita::390.modern_relevance: You repeat a simple mantra or habit daily, and it becomes the steady engine for your deeper, disciplined practice.
vishnu_gita::390.insight: It teaches you to anchor your spiritual effort in a simple, steady practice that sustains long-term discipline.

vishnu_gita::391.verse_sanskrit:
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञ तपः क्रियाः।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकांक्षिभिः ॥
vishnu_gita::391.verse_hindi: मुमुक्षगण फलाकांक्षा त्याग करके और तत् इस शब्द को उच्चारण करके विविध प्रकार के यज्ञ तप और दान कर्म करते हैं
vishnu_gita::391.english_translation: Those seeking freedom perform various sacrifices, austerities, and acts of giving without desire for results, uttering the word 'That'.
vishnu_gita::391.translation_literal: तदिति (that - this) अनभिसन्धाय (without craving) फलं (result) यज्ञ (sacrifice) तपः (austerity) क्रियाः (actions) दानक्रियाश्च (and acts of giving) विविधाः (various) क्रियन्ते (are done) मोक्षकांक्षिभिः (by those desiring liberation)
vishnu_gita::391.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::391.essence: True seekers act with pure intent, free from desire for results.
vishnu_gita::391.simple_meaning: People seeking inner freedom perform sacrifices, austerities, and giving without expecting rewards, focusing instead on pure intent.
vishnu_gita::391.simple_insight: Relief comes when you let go of expecting outcomes from your efforts.
vishnu_gita::391.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that those who truly seek liberation perform various spiritual practices like sacrifices, austerities, and charity without craving results, focusing on the pure practice itself.
vishnu_gita::391.modern_relevance: You work hard on a project but keep your focus on doing your best, not on the praise or reward it might bring.
vishnu_gita::391.insight: Shift your focus from wanting results to committing fully to the action itself.

vishnu_gita::392.verse_sanskrit:
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत् प्रयुज्यते।
प्रशस्ते कर्माणि तथा सच्छब्दो युज्यतेऽमराः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::392.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! सद्भाव में (अस्तित्व में) और साधुभाव में (साधुत्व में) सत् इस शब्द का प्रयोग होता है एवं श्रेष्ठ कर्म में भी सत् शब्द प्रयुक्त होता है
vishnu_gita::392.english_translation: O divine beings! The word 'sat' is used for true existence, virtuous nature, and excellent actions.
vishnu_gita::392.translation_literal: सद्भावे (in true existence) / साधुभावे (in virtuous nature) / च (and) / सदित्येतत् (this word 'sat') / प्रयुज्यते (is used). / प्रशस्ते (excellent) / कर्माणि (actions) / तथा (also) / सच्छब्दो (the word 'sat') / युज्यतेऽमराः (is used by immortal beings)!
vishnu_gita::392.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::392.essence: The word 'sat' unifies true existence, virtue, and noble action as one reality.
vishnu_gita::392.simple_meaning: The word ‘sat’ is used to describe true existence, virtuous nature, and the highest quality of actions.
vishnu_gita::392.simple_insight: The word 'sat' connects being, goodness, and action as expressions of truth.
vishnu_gita::392.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that the term 'sat' is applied to true existence (being), virtuous character, and excellent actions, highlighting the unity of truth across states and deeds.
vishnu_gita::392.modern_relevance: When you call something 'real' or 'good'—whether a person, their nature, or their work—you are using the same deep standard of truth.
vishnu_gita::392.insight: It guides you to see that truth is not separate in existence, character, or action but unified under one word.

vishnu_gita::393.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥
vishnu_gita::393.verse_hindi: यज्ञ, तपस्या और दान कर्मों में लगे रहने को भी सत् कहा जाता है और तदर्थीय कर्म को भी सत ही कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::393.english_translation: Being engaged in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is called existence; action done for their sake is also called existence.
vishnu_gita::393.translation_literal: यज्ञे (in sacrifice) / तपसि (in austerity) / दाने (in charity) / च (and) / स्थितिः (being engaged) / सदिति (existence is) / चोच्यते (said) / कर्म (action) / चैव (indeed) / तदर्थीयं (for their purpose) / सदित्येवाभिधीयते (also called existence)
vishnu_gita::393.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::393.essence: True existence is steady commitment to selfless, purposeful action.
vishnu_gita::393.simple_meaning: Being consistently involved in acts like sacrifice, discipline, and giving is true existence, as is acting with that purpose.
vishnu_gita::393.simple_insight: There is strength and truth in steady, purposeful action beyond fleeting results.
vishnu_gita::393.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that true existence arises when a person remains dedicated to practices like sacrifice, austerity, and charity. These acts, and the commitment behind them, define meaningful action beyond just outcomes.
vishnu_gita::393.modern_relevance: You commit daily to causes or habits that feel right, and in that steady devotion, you find your true presence.
vishnu_gita::393.insight: It shifts focus from chasing results to valuing consistent engagement in right actions.

vishnu_gita::394.verse_sanskrit:
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतञ्च यत् ।
अमदित्युच्यते देवाः ! न च तत् प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
vishnu_gita::394.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! अश्रद्धापूर्वक होम करना, दान करना, तपस्या करना एवं जो कुछ भी करना, असत् कहा जाता है, वह न परलोक में और न इहलोक में फलदायक होता है
vishnu_gita::394.english_translation: O radiant beings! Actions like offerings, giving, and austerities performed without faith are called unreal; they bear no fruit here or beyond.
vishnu_gita::394.translation_literal: अश्रद्धया (without faith) / हुतं (offered) / दत्तं (given) / तपस्तप्तं (austerity-performed) / कृतञ्च (done) / यत् (that) / अमदित्युच्यते (called unreal) / देवाः (O radiant beings) / न (not) / च (and) / तत् (that) / प्रेत्य (after death) / नो (to us) / इह (here)
vishnu_gita::394.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::394.essence: Actions without faith are empty and bear no lasting fruit.
vishnu_gita::394.simple_meaning: Actions like offerings, donations, or austerities done without faith are ineffective and do not bring results here or after death.
vishnu_gita::394.simple_insight: You feel the importance of trust as the foundation for meaningful action.
vishnu_gita::394.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that rituals and deeds performed without faith lack power. Without inner conviction, these acts are empty, offering no benefit in this life or beyond.
vishnu_gita::394.modern_relevance: You might complete a task or help someone but feel disconnected or doubtful, making your effort feel hollow and unrewarding.
vishnu_gita::394.insight: It teaches you to root your actions in genuine trust to make them effective and meaningful.

vishnu_gita::395.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्वज्ञानस्य यन्मूलं संक्षेपाच्छृणुतामराः ! ॥
अवश्यमेव विजेयमित्येतावत् सुरर्षभाः ॥
vishnu_gita::395.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! मैं संक्षेप से तत्त्वज्ञान का मूल कहता हूँ सुनो। इतना अवश्य ही आपलोगों को जानना उचित है
vishnu_gita::395.english_translation: O divine beings! I will briefly explain the root of true knowledge. This much you must certainly know.
vishnu_gita::395.translation_literal: तत्त्वज्ञानस्य (of true knowledge) यन्मूलं (the root) संक्षेपात् (briefly) श्रुणुताम् (listen) अमराः (O immortals) ! अवश्यमेव (certainly) विजेयमिति (victory/should be known) एतावत् (this much) सुरर्षभाः (best of the gods) ॥
vishnu_gita::395.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::395.essence: True knowledge has a simple root everyone must understand.
vishnu_gita::395.simple_meaning: You are about to hear the essential core of true knowledge in brief. This is important and certain for you to understand.
vishnu_gita::395.simple_insight: There is clarity and relief in knowing the true knowledge’s core can be grasped simply.
vishnu_gita::395.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, promising to summarize the fundamental essence of true knowledge. This moment sets the stage to reveal the most essential wisdom that the celestial beings must understand.
vishnu_gita::395.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by complex ideas, you can find relief in focusing on the core truth that matters most.
vishnu_gita::395.insight: It encourages focusing on the essential core rather than getting lost in details, making wisdom accessible.

vishnu_gita::396.verse_sanskrit:
प्रपञ्चमयदृश्येऽस्मिन नास्ति किञ्चित्रिभावतः।
रहितं वस्तु भावो हि कारणं गुणदर्शने ॥
vishnu_gita::396.verse_hindi: कि इस प्रपञ्चमय दृश्य में कोई पदार्थ भी त्रिभाव से रहित नहीं है; क्योंकि भाव ही गुणदर्शन का कारण है
vishnu_gita::396.english_translation: In this world of appearances, nothing exists without the three qualities; because feeling is the cause of perceiving qualities.
vishnu_gita::396.translation_literal: प्रपञ्चमयदृश्येऽस्मिन (in this world of appearances) / नास्ति (there is not) / किञ्चित्रिभावतः (without the three qualities) / रहितं (free) / वस्तु (object) / भावो (feeling) / हि (indeed) / कारणं (cause) / गुणदर्शने (of perceiving qualities)
vishnu_gita::396.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::396.essence: Feelings cause you to perceive qualities; nothing appears without them.
vishnu_gita::396.simple_meaning: Everything you see is influenced by three qualities because your feelings shape how you perceive them.
vishnu_gita::396.simple_insight: You feel how your inner mood colors every experience and perception.
vishnu_gita::396.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that in the world of appearances, no object is free from the three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas). Your feelings cause you to perceive these qualities, revealing how your inner state shapes experience.
vishnu_gita::396.modern_relevance: When you react emotionally to a person or situation, you realize your feelings tint your perception, not just the facts.
vishnu_gita::396.insight: This verse teaches you to notice how your feelings influence what qualities you see in everything around you.

vishnu_gita::397.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतिस्त्रिगुणा या मे प्रथमं त्रीन गुणान् स्वकान्।
स्वस्मिन् सम्यक् विलय्यैव तदा सा मयि लीयते ॥
vishnu_gita::397.verse_hindi: त्रिगुणमयी मेरी प्रकृति पहले तीनों अपने गुणों को अपने में सम्यक् लय करके ही तब वह मुझ में विलीन होती है
vishnu_gita::397.english_translation: My nature is composed of three qualities; when it fully dissolves its own qualities into itself, then it merges into me.
vishnu_gita::397.translation_literal: प्रकृतिस्त्रिगुणा (nature composed of three qualities) / या (which) / मे (my) / प्रथमं (first) / त्रीन (three) / गुणान् (qualities) / स्वकान् (its own) / स्वस्मिन् (in itself) / सम्यक् (completely) / विलय्यैव (having dissolved) / तदा (then) / सा (it) / मयि (in me) / लीयते (is merged).
vishnu_gita::397.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::397.essence: The three qualities of nature dissolve only when fully absorbed into the true self.
vishnu_gita::397.simple_meaning: Your natural makeup has three qualities that vanish only when they fully merge back into you.
vishnu_gita::397.simple_insight: There is a quiet power in letting your changing nature dissolve into your true self.
vishnu_gita::397.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the natural world, made of three qualities, only merges into the supreme self when these qualities dissolve completely into it, revealing the deeper reality beyond change.
vishnu_gita::397.modern_relevance: You experience moods and traits that seem fixed until you realize they can dissolve when you deeply connect with your true self.
vishnu_gita::397.insight: It teaches you to see qualities as temporary and to focus on the unchanging presence beneath them.

vishnu_gita::398.verse_sanskrit:
आदौ देवाः ! त्रयो भावाः स्थिताः स्वस्वस्वरूपतः।
पश्चादद्वैतरूपत्वमाश्रयन्तीति सम्मतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::398.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! प्रथम तीनों भाव अपने अपने स्वरूप से प्रकट रहकर पीछे अद्वैत रूप को  आश्रय करते हैं, यह निश्चय है
vishnu_gita::398.english_translation: O divine beings! Initially, the three states exist in their own forms and later rest in the non-dual reality; this is certain.
vishnu_gita::398.translation_literal: आदौ (in the beginning) देवाः (divine beings) ! त्रयो (three) भावाः (states) स्थिताः (are established) स्वस्वस्वरूपतः (in their own forms) । पश्चाद् (after) अद्वैत (non-dual) रूपत्वम् (form/nature) आश्रयन्तीति (resting) सम्मतम् (certain) ॥
vishnu_gita::398.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::398.essence: Apparent separate states arise but ultimately rest in one non-dual reality.
vishnu_gita::398.simple_meaning: Three states appear in their own forms first, then they rest in the one non-dual reality; this is certain.
vishnu_gita::398.simple_insight: There is a deeper unity behind all apparent differences, even if they seem separate at first.
vishnu_gita::398.detailed_meaning: Addressing divine beings, this verse explains that the three states (likely waking, dreaming, deep sleep) appear separately in their own nature initially but ultimately rest in the singular non-dual reality. This sets the foundation for understanding unity beyond multiplicity.
vishnu_gita::398.insight: It shifts the view from seeing separate experiences to recognizing their shared root in non-duality.

vishnu_gita::399.verse_sanskrit:
गुणदर्शनहेतुर्हि तस्माद्भावः प्रकीर्तितः।
साधकानां मुराः ! भावो हवलम्बनमन्तिमम् ॥
vishnu_gita::399.verse_hindi: इस कारण से भाव गुण दर्शन का हेतु कहा गया है। हे देवतागण ! साधकों का अन्तिम अवलम्बन भाव है
vishnu_gita::399.english_translation: Because of this, the inner attitude is called the cause for perceiving qualities; O radiant beings, the ultimate support for seekers is the inner attitude.
vishnu_gita::399.translation_literal: गुणदर्शनहेतुर्हि (qualities-perception-cause) / तस्माद्भावः (therefore-attitude) / प्रकीर्तितः (is-called) / साधकानां (of seekers) / मुराः (O sages) / भावो (attitude) / हवलम्बनमन्तिमम् (ultimate-support).
vishnu_gita::399.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::399.essence: Your inner attitude shapes what qualities you perceive and is your ultimate support.
vishnu_gita::399.simple_meaning: The way you feel inside is why you notice certain qualities. For seekers, this inner attitude is their final support.
vishnu_gita::399.simple_insight: Trusting your inner attitude brings steady support on your journey.
vishnu_gita::399.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to sages that inner attitude (bhava) is the reason one perceives qualities in the world. For seekers on the path, this attitude becomes their ultimate foundation and support.
vishnu_gita::399.modern_relevance: Before deciding or judging, you realize your mood and attitude shape what you notice and trust.
vishnu_gita::399.insight: It shifts your view to see that perception depends on your inner state, not just external facts.

vishnu_gita::400.verse_sanskrit:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।
मन:षष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
vishnu_gita::400.verse_hindi: मेरा ही अंश सनातन अर्थात् माया के कारण सदा संसारी रूप से प्रसिद्ध जीव, प्रकृति में स्थित मन और पञ्चेन्द्रियों को जीवलोक में आकर्षण करता है
vishnu_gita::400.english_translation: The eternal living being in the world is a part of me; it draws the mind and five senses, situated in nature, into the realm of living beings.
vishnu_gita::400.translation_literal: मम (my) एवांशः (part) जीव-लोके (in the world of living beings) जीव-भूतः (living being) सनातनः (eternal) । मनः (mind) षष्ठानि (six) इन्द्रियाणि (senses) प्रकृति-स्थानि (situated in nature) कर्षति (draws) ॥
vishnu_gita::400.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::400.essence: An eternal part within you draws the mind and senses into the natural world.
vishnu_gita::400.simple_meaning: You are an eternal living presence that draws your mind and senses into the changing world around you.
vishnu_gita::400.simple_insight: You are more than your restless mind and senses pulled by nature.
vishnu_gita::400.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that each living being contains an eternal part of himself. This eternal presence attracts the mind and senses, which are rooted in the natural world, drawing the being into the cycle of living.
vishnu_gita::400.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed as your senses and thoughts pull you into distractions around you, unaware of the timeless presence within you.
vishnu_gita::400.insight: Recognize the difference between your eternal true self and the natural mind-sense complex that pulls you into reactivity.

vishnu_gita::401.verse_sanskrit:
शरीरं यद्वाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्ताम्तीश्वर:।
गर्हीत्वैतानि संयति वायुर्गंधानिवाशयात ॥
vishnu_gita::401.verse_hindi: ईश्वर अर्थात् देही जिस शरीर को प्राप्त होता है और जिस शरीर को परित्याग करता है, जिस प्रकार वायु आशय अर्थात् कुसुमादि से गन्धयुक्त सूक्ष्मांश ग्रहण करके जाता है उसी प्रकार प्राप्त शरीर में पूर्वपरित्यक्त शरीर से  इन सब इन्द्रियादि को लेकर जाता है
vishnu_gita::401.english_translation: The inner being takes possession of the body it attains and leaves it like wind carrying scents from flowers; it carries subtle elements from the previous body to the new one.
vishnu_gita::401.translation_literal: शरीरं (body) यत् (which) वा (also) अप्नोति (attains) यच्च (and which) अपि (also) उत्क्तम् (said) ईश्वरः (the inner being) । गर्हीत्व (carrying) एतानि (these) संयति (goes) वायुर्गन्ध (like wind carrying scent) अनिवाशयात् (from the abode) ॥
vishnu_gita::401.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::401.essence: The true self moves through bodies like wind carries fragrance, beyond physical form.
vishnu_gita::401.simple_meaning: Your true self receives a body, lives in it, then leaves it like wind carries fragrance from flowers to flowers.
vishnu_gita::401.simple_insight: You are not limited to your present form; your essence moves beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::401.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the inner being (the true self) inhabits a body temporarily and departs it like the wind carries scents from one place to another, carrying subtle impressions from the previous body to the new one.
vishnu_gita::401.modern_relevance: You feel restless leaving behind old habits or identities, knowing something deeper moves with you beyond your current self.
vishnu_gita::401.insight: Recognize your inner self as a traveler beyond physical form, carrying subtle impressions forward.

vishnu_gita::402.verse_sanskrit:
श्रोतं चक्षु: स्पर्श्नच्य रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चाय विष्यानुप सेवते ॥
vishnu_gita::402.verse_hindi: यह देही श्रोत्र चक्षु त्वक रसना और घ्राण इन बाह्येन्द्रियों पर और अन्तःकरण पर अधिष्ठान करके विषयों का उपभोग करता है।
vishnu_gita::402.english_translation: The embodied self uses the external senses of hearing, sight, touch, taste, and smell, and the inner mind to enjoy objects.
vishnu_gita::402.translation_literal: श्रोतं (hearing) / चक्षु: (eye/sight) / स्पर्श्नच्य (touch) / रसनं (taste) / घ्राणमेव (smell) / च (and) / अधिष्ठाय (establishing) / मनश्चाय (and mind) / विष्यानुप (objects) / सेवते (enjoys/serves)
vishnu_gita::402.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::402.essence: Your senses and mind together serve to experience the world of objects.
vishnu_gita::402.simple_meaning: You use your five senses and your mind to experience and enjoy things around you.
vishnu_gita::402.simple_insight: Your experience is shaped by both your senses and your inner mind working together.
vishnu_gita::402.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the living being uses both the external senses—hearing, sight, touch, taste, smell—and the inner mind to interact with and enjoy the world of objects, highlighting the complexity of perception.
vishnu_gita::402.modern_relevance: You notice how your phone, music, taste, and thoughts all combine to create what feels real to you right now.
vishnu_gita::402.insight: It teaches you that perception is not just through senses but also shaped by the mind’s engagement with what the senses detect.

vishnu_gita::403.verse_sanskrit:
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितम्वापि भुजानम्वा गुणान्वितम्।
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
vishnu_gita::403.verse_hindi: एक देह से देहान्तर मे जाने वाले देह में स्थित विषयभोगकारी और इन्द्रियादि से युक्त देही को विमूढ़ व्यक्ति नहीं देखते हैं किन्तु प्रात्मज्ञानी देखते हैं
vishnu_gita::403.english_translation: People lost in delusion do not see the true self that moves through different bodies with qualities; only those with the eye of wisdom perceive it.
vishnu_gita::403.translation_literal: उत्क्रामन्तं (going out) / स्थितम् (remaining) / वापि (also) / भुजानम् (enjoying) / वा (or) / गुणान्वितम् (endowed with qualities) / विमूढा (deluded) / न (not) / अनु पश्यन्ति (observe) / पश्यन्ति (see) / ज्ञानचक्षुषः (with knowledge-eye)
vishnu_gita::403.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::403.essence: Only wisdom reveals the true self moving beyond changing bodies and qualities.
vishnu_gita::403.simple_meaning: Only those with clear understanding see the true self that moves through different bodies and experiences qualities. Confused people cannot perceive this reality.
vishnu_gita::403.simple_insight: There is clarity and peace in seeing beyond appearances to the true self within all forms.
vishnu_gita::403.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the true self is distinct from the body and its qualities, moving through different lives. People caught in confusion fail to see this, but the one with wisdom perceives the deeper reality.
vishnu_gita::403.modern_relevance: When you identify only with your changing moods or roles, you miss the unchanging core that truly is you.
vishnu_gita::403.insight: It teaches you to shift attention from surface changes to the unchanging observer within.

vishnu_gita::404.verse_sanskrit:
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ।
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥
vishnu_gita::404.verse_hindi: संयतचित्त योगिगण इस देही को देह में अवस्थित देखते हैं और शास्त्रादि पाठ द्वारा यत्नशील होने पर भी आत्म तत्त्वानभिज्ञ मन्दमति इसको देख नहीं सकते
vishnu_gita::404.english_translation: Disciplined yogis see the inner being dwelling within the body, but those undisciplined in mind do not perceive it.
vishnu_gita::404.translation_literal: यतन्तो (striving) / योगिनः (yogis) / च (and) / ऐनम् (this) / पश्यन्ति (see) / आत्मनि (in the self) / अवस्थितम् (established) / यतन्तः (striving) / अपि (even) / अकृतात्मानः (undisciplined in mind) / न (not) / ऐनम् (this) / पश्यन्ति (see) / अचेतसः (foolish)
vishnu_gita::404.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::404.essence: Only a disciplined mind can perceive the true self within the body.
vishnu_gita::404.simple_meaning: Those who discipline their mind through practice can perceive their true self inside, while the undisciplined cannot.
vishnu_gita::404.simple_insight: Knowing your true self requires steadying the restless mind, not just effort.
vishnu_gita::404.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that yogis who have disciplined their minds see the true self residing within the body. Others, even if they try, fail because their minds are unsettled and unaware.
vishnu_gita::404.modern_relevance: When your mind is restless and distracted, you struggle to see who you truly are beneath the noise and chaos.
vishnu_gita::404.insight: It teaches you to cultivate mental discipline to witness your true self clearly.

vishnu_gita::405.verse_sanskrit:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।
क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::405.verse_hindi: क्षर और अक्षर नामक ये दो पुरुष लोक में प्रसिद्ध हैं उनमे से सब भूतगण क्षर पुरुष और कूटस्थ चैतन्य अक्षर पुरुष कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::405.english_translation: In the world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All creatures are perishable, but the unchanging consciousness is called the imperishable.
vishnu_gita::405.translation_literal: द्वाविमौ (two) पुरुषौ (beings) लोके (in the world) क्षरश्चाक्षर (perishable and imperishable) एव (indeed) च (and) । क्षरः (perishable) सर्वाणि (all) भूतानि (creatures) कूटस्थः (unmoving) अक्षर (imperishable) उच्यते (is called) ॥
vishnu_gita::405.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::405.essence: Among all beings, the unchanging consciousness alone is truly imperishable.
vishnu_gita::405.simple_meaning: Everything in the world changes and passes away, but the inner consciousness remains constant and unchanging.
vishnu_gita::405.simple_insight: You can find calm by realizing your deepest self never fades or changes.
vishnu_gita::405.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the world contains two types of beings: those that change and perish, and the unchanging pure consciousness that remains steady. This teaching helps Arjuna recognize the difference between temporary forms and the eternal self beneath.
vishnu_gita::405.modern_relevance: In moments of stress, when everything around you feels unstable, remember your true self is steady and beyond change.
vishnu_gita::405.insight: Shift attention from fleeting events to the unchanging witness within, grounding your identity in permanence not flux.

vishnu_gita::406.verse_sanskrit:
उत्तम: पुरुषस्त्वन्य: परमात्मेत्युदाहृत।
यो लोकत्रयमाविशय विभर्त्तयव्यय  ईश्वर: ॥
vishnu_gita::406.verse_hindi: इन क्षर और अक्षर से अन्य उत्तम पुरुष परमात्मा कहे गये हैं जो ईश्वर और निर्विकार हैं एवं लोकत्रय में प्रविष्ट होकर पालन करते हैं
vishnu_gita::406.english_translation: The supreme being, distinct from the perishable and imperishable, is called the highest self who pervades and sustains the three worlds without change.
vishnu_gita::406.translation_literal: उत्तम: (supreme) पुरुष: (being) तु (but) अन्य: (other) परमात्मा (highest self) इति (thus) उदाहृत (declared) । यो (who) लोक (world) त्रयम् (three) आविशय (enters) विभर्त्तय (sustains) अव्यय (imperishable) ईश्वर: (lord) ॥
vishnu_gita::406.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::406.essence: An unchanging supreme presence pervades and sustains all three worlds.
vishnu_gita::406.simple_meaning: There is a supreme being beyond what changes and what does not, who enters and upholds the three worlds without alteration.
vishnu_gita::406.simple_insight: Recognizing an unchanging presence beyond all worlds brings a vast sense of grounding.
