vishnu_gita::406.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the existence of a supreme being, distinct from both the perishable and imperishable, who sustains the three realms. It introduces a foundational cosmological concept in Vishnu Gita without specific narrative context.
vishnu_gita::406.insight: It shifts focus from transient things to the enduring presence behind all existence.

vishnu_gita::407.verse_sanskrit:
यस्मात् क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
vishnu_gita::407.verse_hindi: क्योंकि मैं क्षर से अतीत हूँ, और अक्षर की अपेक्षा भी उत्तम हूँ इसी कारण लोक में और वेद में पुरुषोत्तम प्रसिद्ध हैं
vishnu_gita::407.english_translation: Because I transcend the perishable and am even superior to the imperishable, I am known as the Supreme Being in the world and the Vedas.
vishnu_gita::407.translation_literal: यस्मात् (because) क्षर (perishable) मतीतः (gone beyond) अहम् (I) अक्षरात् (than imperishable) अपि (also) उत्तमः (superior) अतोऽस्मि (therefore I am) लोके (in the world) वेदे (in the Vedas) च (also) प्रथितः (famous) पुरुषोत्तमः (Supreme Being)
vishnu_gita::407.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::407.essence: Your true self is beyond all change and is known as the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::407.simple_meaning: The true self goes beyond everything that changes and is even higher than what never changes. That is why it is known as supreme everywhere.
vishnu_gita::407.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self is beyond all change and limitations.
vishnu_gita::407.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu explains that the true self surpasses both the changing world and the unchanging reality, revealing a supreme nature recognized universally and in sacred texts.
vishnu_gita::407.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels unstable, you can find a part of yourself untouched by change and truly supreme.
vishnu_gita::407.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with temporary things to recognizing your unchanging, highest nature.

vishnu_gita::408.verse_sanskrit:
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन निर्जराः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::408.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! इस प्रकार निश्चित बुद्धि होकर जो मुझको पुरुषोत्तम समझता है वह सर्वज्ञ व्यक्ति मुझको ही सर्वभाव से पूजता है
vishnu_gita::408.english_translation: Anyone who truly knows me as the supreme being worships me with complete devotion and understanding.
vishnu_gita::408.translation_literal: यो (who) माम् (me) एवम् (thus) असम्मूढः (undeluded) जानाति (knows) पुरुषोत्तमम् (the supreme being) । स (he) सर्वविद् (omniscient) भजति (worships) माम् (me) सर्वभावेन (with all feelings) निर्जराः (unfailing) !
vishnu_gita::408.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::408.essence: True knowledge of the supreme being naturally creates complete, steadfast devotion.
vishnu_gita::408.simple_meaning: When someone fully understands the supreme being without confusion, they worship with complete and unwavering devotion.
vishnu_gita::408.simple_insight: Knowing the supreme being deeply opens your heart to pure, steady devotion.
vishnu_gita::408.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that a person who clearly recognizes him as the supreme being worships with full understanding and heartfelt devotion. This moment reveals the power of true knowledge to inspire devoted love.
vishnu_gita::408.modern_relevance: You recognize someone’s true value clearly, and your respect and care for them naturally deepen without doubt.
vishnu_gita::408.insight: It teaches you that clear understanding removes confusion and naturally leads to wholehearted devotion.

vishnu_gita::409.verse_sanskrit:
इति गुह्यतम शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघाः ।
एतबुवा बुद्धिमान् स्यात् कृतकृत्यश्च देवताः ॥
vishnu_gita::409.verse_hindi: हे निर्दोष देवता गण ! यह परमगुहा शास्त्र मैंने कहा है इसको समझकर साधक सम्यक शानी और कृतकृत्य होता है
vishnu_gita::409.english_translation: O pure radiant beings! I have spoken this most secret teaching; understanding it, the seeker becomes wise and fulfilled.
vishnu_gita::409.translation_literal: इति (thus) / गुह्यतम (most secret) / शास्त्रमिदम् (this scripture) / उक्तं (spoken) / मया (by me) / अनघाः (pure radiant beings) । एतबुवा (thus) / बुद्धिमान् (wise) / स्यात् (becomes) / कृतकृत्यश्च (fulfilled) / देवताः (divine beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::409.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::409.essence: Understanding the deepest teaching brings wisdom and fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::409.simple_meaning: I have shared the deepest teaching. Those who understand it become wise and feel complete.
vishnu_gita::409.simple_insight: Knowing this secret brings clarity and a sense of true accomplishment.
vishnu_gita::409.detailed_meaning: After delivering his profound teaching, Vishnu addresses the pure radiant beings, declaring that grasping this secret knowledge leads to wisdom and fulfillment for the seeker.
vishnu_gita::409.insight: Recognizing and internalizing profound teachings transforms the seeker into a wise and fulfilled person.

vishnu_gita::410.verse_sanskrit:
जगद्गुरो! देवदेव: करुणावरुणालय !।
निर्भयाः स्मो वयं जाता उपदेशन ते विभो ! ॥
vishnu_gita::410.verse_hindi: हे देवादिदेव ! हे जगद्गुरो ! हे करुणावरुणालय ! हे विभो ! आपके उपदेश द्वारा हम निर्भय हुए हैं
vishnu_gita::410.english_translation: O world teacher! O Deva of Devas! O abode of compassion! By your instruction, we have become fearless, O Vibhō!
vishnu_gita::410.translation_literal: जगद्गुरो (world teacher) / देवदेवः (deva of devas) / करुणावरुणालय (abode of compassion) / निर्भयाः (fearless) / स्मः (we are) / जाता (become) / उपदेशन (by instruction) / ते (your) / विभो (O Vibhō)
vishnu_gita::410.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::410.essence: Fear fades when wise guidance from a compassionate teacher is received.
vishnu_gita::410.simple_meaning: By the teachings of this compassionate world teacher, we have become free from fear.
vishnu_gita::410.simple_insight: There is strength and courage that comes from receiving wise guidance.
vishnu_gita::410.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the speaker praises the divine teacher with many exalted titles and expresses that through the teacher's guidance, all fear has been removed. It captures a moment of gratitude and confidence inspired by the teacher's words.
vishnu_gita::410.insight: It highlights how guidance from a trusted source can dissolve fear and build inner confidence.

vishnu_gita::411.verse_hindi: संसार की सृष्टि का रहस्य, त्रिगुणजनित सृष्टि का विभाग और उसके यथावत् ज्ञान को प्राप्त करने के लिये
vishnu_gita::411.english_translation: The secret of the world's creation, the division of the world born of the three qualities, and how to truly understand it.
vishnu_gita::411.translation_literal: रहस्यं (secret) / जगत:सृष्टे: (of the world's creation) / त्रिगुणैजनितं (born of the three qualities) / तथा (also) / सृष्टे (creation) / विभागमेतस्याः (division of this) / यथा (how) / अवज्ञानलब्धये (to obtain true knowledge)
vishnu_gita::411.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::411.essence: True understanding reveals the secret divisions born from the three fundamental qualities.
vishnu_gita::411.simple_meaning: The verse introduces the mystery behind creation linked to the three qualities and how to gain true understanding of it.
vishnu_gita::411.simple_insight: Curiosity about the hidden workings behind everything invites deeper learning.
vishnu_gita::411.detailed_meaning: Vishnu begins to explain the hidden mystery behind the creation of the world, which arises from the three qualities (gunas), and how to gain accurate knowledge about this division.
vishnu_gita::411.insight: It encourages seeking clear understanding of the forces shaping reality rather than accepting appearances.

vishnu_gita::412.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञात्वा भावरहस्यं च कृतकृत्यत्वमागताः।
अतस्ते कृपया काऽपि पतिप्यामो भये न हि ॥
vishnu_gita::412.verse_hindi: भाव का रहस्य समझकर हम कृतकृत्य हुए। अतः आपकी कृपा से हम किसी भी भय में पतित नहीं होंगे
vishnu_gita::412.english_translation: Having understood the secret of emotions and our debts, we will not fall into any fear by your grace.
vishnu_gita::412.translation_literal: ज्ञात्वा (having known) भावरहस्यं (the secret of emotions) च (and) कृतकृत्यत्वमागताः (our indebtedness arrived). अतस्ते (therefore by your) कृपया (grace) काऽपि (any) पतिप्यामो (falling) भये (into fear) न (not) हि (indeed).
vishnu_gita::412.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::412.essence: Understanding emotional debts and grace removes all fear.
vishnu_gita::412.simple_meaning: When you understand the true nature of your emotions and debts, your trust in the divine protects you from fear.
vishnu_gita::412.simple_insight: You feel peaceful knowing grace shields you from fear's power.
vishnu_gita::412.detailed_meaning: This verse reveals a turning point where those understanding their emotional burdens and debts feel assured by divine grace, freeing them from fear. It shows how trust in the divine support transforms vulnerability into courage.
vishnu_gita::412.modern_relevance: You’ve faced emotional challenges and mistakes, but knowing you’re supported helps you stop fearing what might come next.
vishnu_gita::412.insight: It shifts your mind from fearing consequences to trusting in protective grace and acceptance.

vishnu_gita::413.verse_sanskrit:
स्वासीमकृपयेदानीमस्मानुपदिश प्रभो !।
सृष्टनिंदानं किं देव ! तदुत्पत्तिः किमर्थिका ॥
vishnu_gita::413.verse_hindi: हे देव! हे प्रभो! अब अपनी असीम कृपा द्वारा हमको उपदेश दीजिये कि सृष्टि का मूल कारण क्या है? क्यों सृष्टि उत्पन्न हुई है?
vishnu_gita::413.english_translation: O Lord! Please now bless us with your boundless grace and teach us: What is the original cause of creation? Why did creation arise?
vishnu_gita::413.translation_literal: स्वासीमकृपयेदानीम (now with boundless grace) अस्मानुपदिश (teach us) प्रभो (O Lord) ! / सृष्टनिंदानं (origin of creation) किं (what) देव (O divine) ! / तदुत्पत्तिः (its origin) किमर्थिका (for what reason) ॥
vishnu_gita::413.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::413.essence: A heartfelt plea to understand why and how the universe began.
vishnu_gita::413.simple_meaning: A humble request is made to the divine being to kindly explain the origin and reason for the creation of the universe.
vishnu_gita::413.simple_insight: There is a deep yearning to understand the source and purpose behind existence.
vishnu_gita::413.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker respectfully appeals to the divine for guidance, seeking to comprehend the fundamental reason behind the universe's existence and its origin.
vishnu_gita::413.modern_relevance: When life feels confusing and overwhelming, you might long for a clear explanation of why everything exists as it does.
vishnu_gita::413.insight: It encourages honest questioning and openness to receiving wisdom about existence's root cause.

vishnu_gita::414.verse_sanskrit:
तस्याः प्रवर्तकः कोऽस्ति मूलनिर्मूलने स्फुटः।
उपायः कश्च तब्रूहि भवव्याधिनिवृत्तये ॥
vishnu_gita::414.verse_hindi: उस सृष्टि का प्रवर्तक कौन है? और इसके मूल को निर्मूल करने का स्पष्ट उपाय क्या है? भवरोग की निवृत्ति के लिये कृपया कर यह सब कहें
vishnu_gita::414.english_translation: Who is the originator of that creation? And what is the clear method to uproot its root? Please explain this for the cessation of the disease of existence.
vishnu_gita::414.translation_literal: तस्याः (of that) / प्रवर्तकः (originator) / कोऽस्ति (who is) / मूलनिर्मूलने (in uprooting the root) / स्फुटः (clear) / उपायः (method) / कश्च (who) / तब्रूहि (please tell) / भवव्याधिनिवृत्तये (for cessation of the disease of existence)
vishnu_gita::414.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::414.essence: Understanding the origin and remedy of existence's suffering is key to freedom.
vishnu_gita::414.simple_meaning: A question is asked about who started the creation and how to remove the root cause of worldly suffering.
vishnu_gita::414.simple_insight: Wondering about the source and cure of existence's suffering shows a deep search for freedom.
vishnu_gita::414.detailed_meaning: A seeker questions who initiated the cosmic creation and asks for a clear way to eliminate the root cause of continued suffering in existence, seeking liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
vishnu_gita::414.modern_relevance: You might find yourself asking what started your current struggles and how to truly end them, seeking a clear path beyond confusion.
vishnu_gita::414.insight: It encourages moving beyond surface problems to identify and address the deepest cause of suffering.

vishnu_gita::415.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! अनादि अनन्त और जिसके विस्तार की अवधि नहीं है ऐसा सृष्टि प्रवाह मेरी इच्छा से प्रवाहित रहता है।
vishnu_gita::415.english_translation: O divine beings! The endless flow of creation moves by my will, without beginning or end, and beyond measure.
vishnu_gita::415.translation_literal: सृष्टिप्रवाहो (creation flow) / विबुधाः (divine beings) / मदिच्छातः (by my desire) / प्रवर्त्तते (moves) / आधन्तरहितः (without beginning or end) / तद् (that) / अविस्तार (expanse) / अवधि (limit) / वर्जितः (free from)
vishnu_gita::415.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::415.essence: Creation flows endlessly and limitlessly from the divine will.
vishnu_gita::415.simple_meaning: The endless flow of creation happens because of the divine will, without any limit or starting point.
vishnu_gita::415.simple_insight: Creation is vast and timeless, flowing naturally from the divine will beyond our grasp.
vishnu_gita::415.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, explaining that the continuous, limitless process of creation flows solely by his will, emphasizing its eternal and boundless nature.
vishnu_gita::415.insight: It invites you to see creation as a vast, ongoing movement beyond beginnings or ends, shaped by a profound inner will.

vishnu_gita::416.verse_sanskrit:
निजानन्दप्रकाशाय साहाय्यात् सचितोः स्वयोः।
स्वीयां शक्ति महामायां स्वतः प्रकटयाम्यहम् ॥
vishnu_gita::416.verse_hindi: मैं अपने आनन्द को प्रकाशित करने के लिये अपने सत् और चिद्भाव की सहायता से अपने मे से अपनी शक्ति महामाया को प्रकट करता हूँ
vishnu_gita::416.english_translation: I manifest my great power, the supreme illusion, through my own truth and consciousness to illuminate my own bliss.
vishnu_gita::416.translation_literal: निजानन्दप्रकाशाय (for own bliss's illumination) / साहाय्यात् (with the help) / सचितोः (of truth and consciousness) / स्वयोः (of myself) / स्वीयां (own) / शक्ति (power) / महामायां (great illusion) / स्वतः (by myself) / प्रकटयामि (I manifest) / अहम् (I)
vishnu_gita::416.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::416.essence: Your own truth and awareness manifest your greatest creative power and joy.
vishnu_gita::416.simple_meaning: You can reveal your deepest joy by manifesting your own truth and consciousness through your innate great power.
vishnu_gita::416.simple_insight: There is empowerment in knowing your bliss arises from your own inner truth and strength.
vishnu_gita::416.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that through his own essence of truth and consciousness, he manifests his great power called the supreme illusion to illuminate his bliss, showing the divine source of joy is self-originated.
vishnu_gita::416.modern_relevance: When you face moments of doubt, remember your ability to create joy comes from your own inner strength and clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::416.insight: It teaches you to trust your own consciousness as the source of creative power and joy.

vishnu_gita::417.verse_sanskrit:
सैव शक्तिश्च मे देवाः ! जगतो जननी मता।
किन्तु सर्वस्य जगतः स्थित्युत्पत्तिलयेष्वपि ॥
vishnu_gita::417.verse_hindi: और हे देवगण ! वही मेरी शक्ति जगत को उत्पन्न करती है, परन्तु सम्पूर्ण जगत की उत्पत्ति स्थिति और लयों में भी
vishnu_gita::417.english_translation: O divine beings! That same power of mine creates the world, and also sustains and dissolves the entire universe.
vishnu_gita::417.translation_literal: सैव (that same) शक्तिश्च (power also) मे (of mine) देवाः (O gods) ! जगतो (of the world) जननी (mother) मता (is considered). किन्तु (but) सर्वस्य (of all) जगतः (world) स्थितिउत्पत्तिलयेषु (in sustenance, creation, and dissolution) अपि (also).
vishnu_gita::417.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::417.essence: One power creates, sustains, and dissolves all that exists.
vishnu_gita::417.simple_meaning: The divine power that creates the world also governs its maintenance and destruction.
vishnu_gita::417.simple_insight: Everything that happens in the universe flows from one single divine power.
vishnu_gita::417.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, explaining that his power is the source behind the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of everything, highlighting his all-encompassing cosmic role.
vishnu_gita::417.insight: It shifts your perspective to see all changes in life as expressions of one continuous power, reducing fear of loss or change.

vishnu_gita::418.verse_sanskrit:
केवलं कारणं कर्म विज्ञेयं मुरसत्तमाः ।
जड़चेतनभेदेन मदीया प्रकृतिद्विधा ॥
vishnu_gita::418.verse_hindi: एकमात्र कारण कर्म ही है ऐसा जानना चाहिये। जड़ और चेतन भेद से मेरी प्रकृति दो प्रकार की है
vishnu_gita::418.english_translation: Action alone is the sole cause; know this well. My nature is twofold, distinguished as inert and conscious.
vishnu_gita::418.translation_literal: केवलं (only) कारणं (cause) कर्म (action) विज्ञेयं (should be known) मुरसत्तमाः (O best of fools) । जड़चेतनभेदेन (by distinction of inert and conscious) मदीया (my) प्रकृतिद्विधा (nature twofold) ॥
vishnu_gita::418.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::418.essence: Action alone causes results; the divine nature is both inert and conscious.
vishnu_gita::418.simple_meaning: The root cause of everything is action. The divine nature has two parts: one that is inert and one that is conscious.
vishnu_gita::418.simple_insight: Knowing that action is the only cause frees you from blaming others or fate.
vishnu_gita::418.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to the listener that all effects arise solely from action. He reveals his nature as dual: inert (matter) and conscious (awareness), establishing a foundational view of cause and effect.
vishnu_gita::418.modern_relevance: When you face outcomes beyond your control, recognize that your actions are the true cause, not external circumstances or blame.
vishnu_gita::418.insight: It teaches you to focus on your actions as the true cause, not external factors or excuses.

vishnu_gita::419.verse_sanskrit:
विद्या तु चेतना ज्ञेया जडाऽविद्या प्रकीर्तिता।
त्रिगुणा सा समाख्याता तत एव च हेतुतः ॥
vishnu_gita::419.verse_hindi: चेतनमयी विद्या कहलाती है और जड़ अविद्या कहलाती है। वह त्रिगुणमयी है और त्रिगुणमयी होने से
vishnu_gita::419.english_translation: Knowledge is understood as consciousness, while ignorance is called inertness. Both are characterized by the three qualities, and this is the cause.
vishnu_gita::419.translation_literal: विद्या (knowledge) तु (indeed) चेतना (consciousness) ज्ञेया (to be known) जडाऽविद्या (inert ignorance) प्रकीर्तिता (called) । त्रिगुणा (three qualities) सा (she/it) समाख्याता (classified) तत (that) एव (indeed) च (and) हेतुतः (cause) ॥
vishnu_gita::419.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::419.essence: Knowledge is conscious awareness; ignorance is inertness shaped by three qualities.
vishnu_gita::419.simple_meaning: Knowledge is consciousness, alive and aware. Ignorance is lifeless and defined by three qualities that bind it.
vishnu_gita::419.simple_insight: You can feel the difference between what wakes you up and what keeps you stuck.
vishnu_gita::419.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that true knowledge is a form of consciousness, alive and aware, while ignorance is inert and lifeless. Both are shaped by the three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas), and this distinction is the foundation of understanding reality.
vishnu_gita::419.modern_relevance: You notice moments when clarity lights up your mind versus times you feel stuck in dull confusion — that contrast is the difference between knowledge and ignorance.
vishnu_gita::419.insight: It teaches you to see knowledge as vibrant awareness and ignorance as passive inertia shaped by three forces.

vishnu_gita::420.verse_sanskrit:
कम्मोत्पत्तर्हि सा हेतुर्भवतीयवधार्यताम्।
परिणामात्तदुत्पत्तिस्त्रिगुणस्य मता सुराः ॥
vishnu_gita::420.verse_hindi: कर्म की उत्पत्ति का कारण बन जाती है, सो जानो। हे देवगण ! त्रिगुण परिणाम से ही कर्मों की उत्पत्ति मानी गई है
vishnu_gita::420.english_translation: Know that the cause of action’s origin is the effect of the three qualities, O devas.
vishnu_gita::420.translation_literal: कर्म (action) / उत्पत्तर्हि (indeed origin) / सा (that) / हेतुः (cause) / भवती (becomes) / अवधार्यताम् (to be understood) । / परिणामात् (from effect) / तद् (that) / उत्पत्तिः (origin) / त्रिगुणस्य (of the three qualities) / मता (considered) / सुराः (the devas) ॥
vishnu_gita::420.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::420.essence: Actions arise as effects of the three fundamental qualities within nature.
vishnu_gita::420.simple_meaning: Actions come into being because of the three fundamental qualities affecting everything.
vishnu_gita::420.simple_insight: Understanding your actions come from these qualities helps you see they are not random.
vishnu_gita::420.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains to the devas that all actions arise from the interplay of the three fundamental qualities (gunas) inherent in nature, revealing why actions occur as effects of these traits.
vishnu_gita::420.modern_relevance: When you notice your habits or reactions, they stem from deep qualities inside you shaping your behavior.
vishnu_gita::420.insight: It shifts your view to see actions as effects of natural qualities, not isolated events.

vishnu_gita::421.verse_sanskrit:
जैवैशसहजा भेदा: कर्मणस्तस्य कीर्तिता: ।
कर्मणा सहजेन स्युर्ब्रह्माण्डानां त्रयः सदा ॥
vishnu_gita::421.verse_hindi: कर्म के तीन भेद है, उनको जैव, सहज और ऐश कहते हैं । हे विपुल बलशाली देवगण! सहज कर्म द्वारा ब्रह्माण्डो के
vishnu_gita::421.english_translation: There are three kinds of action: natural, innate, and divine; through innate action, the three worlds are always sustained.
vishnu_gita::421.translation_literal: जैवैशसहजा (natural, innate, divine) / भेदा: (differences) / कर्मण: (of actions) / तस्य (of that) / कीर्तिता: (are named) / कर्मणा (by actions) / सहजेन (innate) / स्यु: (are) / ब्रह्माण्डानां (of the universes) / त्रय: (three) / सदा (always)
vishnu_gita::421.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::421.essence: Three types of actions exist; spontaneous action sustains the cosmos continuously.
vishnu_gita::421.simple_meaning: Actions are of three kinds: those done naturally, those done spontaneously, and those done with divine purpose; the spontaneous actions keep the universe functioning.
vishnu_gita::421.simple_insight: Understanding that some actions flow naturally brings ease and trust in life’s order.
vishnu_gita::421.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to the devas that all actions fall into three categories: natural (biological), innate (spontaneous), and divine (higher purpose). Among these, innate actions maintain the balance of the three cosmic realms, showing the interconnectedness of all beings.
vishnu_gita::421.modern_relevance: When you perform daily habits without forcing them, you contribute effortlessly to the world’s flow, like breathing or walking naturally.
vishnu_gita::421.insight: Recognize which actions arise effortlessly and trust their role in sustaining your life and environment.

vishnu_gita::422.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिस्थितिलया एते क्रमशो ह्यमितौजसः ।
विशिष्टचेतना  जीवा: सम्बद्धा जैवकर्मणा ॥
vishnu_gita::422.verse_hindi: उत्पत्ति स्थिति और लय क्रम से हुआ करते हैं, जैव कर्म के साथ विशिष्ट चेतन जीवों का सम्बन्ध है
vishnu_gita::422.english_translation: Creation, preservation, and dissolution happen in order; distinct conscious beings are connected through biological actions.
vishnu_gita::422.translation_literal: सृष्टिस्थितिलया (by creation, preservation, and dissolution) / एते (these) / क्रमशः (in order) / हि (indeed) / अमितौजसः (limitless potency) / विशिष्टचेतना (distinct consciousness) / जीवाः (beings) / सम्बद्धाः (connected) / जैवकर्मणा (by biological actions)
vishnu_gita::422.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::422.essence: Life cycles endlessly connect distinct consciousness through ordered creation and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::422.simple_meaning: The universe follows a cycle of creation, maintenance, and destruction, where distinct conscious beings connect through their life actions.
vishnu_gita::422.simple_insight: You are part of a continuous cycle that links all living beings through action.
vishnu_gita::422.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the cosmic process where creation, preservation, and dissolution occur sequentially. Distinct conscious beings exist uniquely yet remain connected through their biological activities, showing life’s interdependence.
vishnu_gita::422.modern_relevance: You notice how your daily choices affect others, part of a wider cycle of growth and change you can’t fully control.
vishnu_gita::422.insight: Recognize your actions connect you to a larger living system cycling through birth, upkeep, and transformation.

vishnu_gita::423.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मणैशेन सम्बन्धः पितृणां भवतां नथा।
ऋषीणां चावताराणां सर्वेषां मे दिवौकसः ॥
vishnu_gita::423.verse_hindi: और मेरे सब अवतारों के साथ तथा पितृ ऋषि और आपलोगों के साथ ऐश कर्म का सम्बन्ध है
vishnu_gita::423.english_translation: I am connected by action with the ancestors, the sages, and all my incarnations.
vishnu_gita::423.translation_literal: कर्मणैशेन (by action alone) / सम्बन्धः (connection) / पितृणां (of ancestors) / भवतां (of you all) / नथा (and) / ऋषीणां (of sages) / चावताराणां (and incarnations) / सर्वेषां (all) / मे (my) / दिवौकसः (the divine being)
vishnu_gita::423.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::423.essence: Your actions connect you intimately with all beings across time.
vishnu_gita::423.simple_meaning: You are connected to your ancestors, sages, and past incarnations through your actions.
vishnu_gita::423.simple_insight: Your actions create bonds that reach across time and beings.
vishnu_gita::423.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that action forms the link connecting him with all ancestors, sages, and his incarnations, showing the importance of karma as a unifying force across time and beings.
vishnu_gita::423.modern_relevance: You realize that what you do today affects not just you but also connects you with those who came before and those yet to come.
vishnu_gita::423.insight: It teaches you to see your actions as threads weaving you into a timeless community.

vishnu_gita::424.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मणी ऐशसहजे शुद्ध एव सदा मते ।
शुद्धाशुद्धविभेदस्तु जैवकर्मसु विद्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::424.verse_hindi: ऐश कर्म और सहज कर्म सदा शुद्ध ही होते हैं। जैव कर्म के दो भेद हैं, एक शुद्ध और एक अशुद्ध
vishnu_gita::424.english_translation: Natural desire-driven actions and spontaneous actions are always pure; biological actions have both pure and impure types.
vishnu_gita::424.translation_literal: कर्मणी (in actions) / ऐशसहजे (desire-driven and spontaneous) / शुद्ध (pure) / एव (indeed) / सदा (always) / मते (are considered) / शुद्धाशुद्धविभेदस्तु (the distinction of pure and impure) / जैवकर्मसु (in biological actions) / विद्यते (exists)
vishnu_gita::424.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::424.essence: Actions from natural desire or spontaneity are always pure; biological actions can be mixed.
vishnu_gita::424.simple_meaning: Actions done out of natural desire or spontaneously are always pure. But actions driven by biological impulses can be pure or impure.
vishnu_gita::424.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing some actions are naturally pure, free from confusion or blame.
vishnu_gita::424.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that actions motivated by natural desire or that happen spontaneously are inherently pure. However, biological actions, influenced by bodily impulses, can be either pure or impure, showing a layered view of action quality.
vishnu_gita::424.modern_relevance: You sometimes act naturally or follow your desires without overthinking, and those moments are free from guilt. Other times, your impulses may lead to mixed results.
vishnu_gita::424.insight: It teaches you to recognize which actions arise naturally and are pure, versus those influenced by conflicting impulses.

vishnu_gita::425.verse_sanskrit:
उभे एते समाख्याते कारणं पुण्यपापयोः ।
कामनाजनितावेतौ भेदौ हि परिकीर्तितो ॥
vishnu_gita::425.verse_hindi: यह दोनों कर्म पुण्य और पाप के कारण होते हैं। ये दोनों भेद कामना जनित कहे गये हैं
vishnu_gita::425.english_translation: Both these actions arise from desire and are the causes of merit and demerit.
vishnu_gita::425.translation_literal: उभे (both) एते (these) समाख्याते (are declared) कारणं (cause) पुण्यपापयोः (of merit and demerit) । कामनाजनितावेतौ (arisen from desire) भेदौ (differences) हि (indeed) परिकीर्तितो (have been described) ॥
vishnu_gita::425.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::425.essence: Desire underlies actions that create merit and demerit.
vishnu_gita::425.simple_meaning: Actions motivated by desire lead to good or bad consequences.
vishnu_gita::425.simple_insight: Knowing that desire causes consequences helps you see your choices clearly.
vishnu_gita::425.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that actions rooted in desire produce either merit or demerit, highlighting how craving shapes the moral quality of deeds.
vishnu_gita::425.modern_relevance: When you act driven by wants, you risk getting tangled in rewards or regrets that follow.
vishnu_gita::425.insight: It teaches you to notice how desire fuels your actions and their effects.

vishnu_gita::426.verse_sanskrit:
अनाधन्तो वासनायाः प्रवाहो ह्येव कारणम् ।
सृष्टेरनाद्यनन्तायाः प्रवाहस्य सुरर्षभाः ॥
vishnu_gita::426.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! अनादि अनन्त वासनाप्रवाह ही अनादि अनन्त सृष्टिप्रवाह का कारण है
vishnu_gita::426.english_translation: O divine beings! The endless flow of desire is indeed the cause of the endless flow of creation from eternity.
vishnu_gita::426.translation_literal: अनाधन्तो (endless) / वासनायाः (of desire) / प्रवाहो (flow) / हि (indeed) / एव (certainly) / कारणम् (cause) / सृष्टेः (of creation) / अनाद्य (from eternity) / अनन्तायाः (endless) / प्रवाहस्य (of flow) / सुरर्षभाः (O best of divine beings)
vishnu_gita::426.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::426.essence: Endless desire is the root cause behind the endless flow of creation.
vishnu_gita::426.simple_meaning: The endless desires within beings cause the never-ending creation and change in the universe.
vishnu_gita::426.simple_insight: You feel how your desires ripple outward, shaping everything without end.
vishnu_gita::426.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that from timeless eternity the continuous flow of desires is the root cause behind the infinite cycle of creation and existence itself.
vishnu_gita::426.modern_relevance: You notice how your persistent wants keep your mind restless and life in constant motion.
vishnu_gita::426.insight: It teaches you to see desire as the originating force behind ongoing change and creation.

vishnu_gita::427.verse_sanskrit:
वासनानाशमात्रेण कर्मणोः सहजैशयो।
जैवस्य परिणामः स्यादृशेयं कर्मयोगिनी ॥
vishnu_gita::427.verse_hindi: वासना के नाश होते ही जैवकर्म भी सहज कर्म और ऐश कर्मों में परिणत हो जाता है। इस दशा को कर्मयोग कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::427.english_translation: When desires are destroyed, the natural and instinctive actions become effortless, marking the state called karma yoga.
vishnu_gita::427.translation_literal: वासना (desires) / नाश (destruction) / मात्रेण (by the mere) / कर्मणः (of action) / सहजैः (natural) / ऐशयः (instinctive) / जैवस्य (of the living being) / परिणामः (result) / स्यात् (becomes) / ऋशेयं (this) / कर्मयोगिनी (karma yoga state)
vishnu_gita::427.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::427.essence: Destroy desire and action becomes effortless natural flow—this is karma yoga.
vishnu_gita::427.simple_meaning: When your desires disappear, your actions become natural and effortless. This effortless action is called karma yoga.
vishnu_gita::427.simple_insight: There's peace in seeing actions flow without inner craving or resistance.
vishnu_gita::427.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when a living being's desires are destroyed, their actions arise spontaneously without conflict. This effortless state of acting naturally is known as karma yoga, the yoga of selfless action.
vishnu_gita::427.modern_relevance: After frustration fades, your daily tasks feel lighter and more natural, as if they flow without force.
vishnu_gita::427.insight: It teaches you to let go of craving, allowing your actions to arise spontaneously and naturally without inner struggle.

vishnu_gita::428.verse_sanskrit:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
vishnu_gita::428.verse_hindi: इस निष्काम कर्मयोग में प्रारम्भ की विफलता नहीं है, प्रत्यवाय अर्थात् विध्न भी नहीं है, इस धर्म का अल्प आचरण भी महाभय से रक्षा करता है
vishnu_gita::428.english_translation: There is no failure or reversal in selfless action; even a small part of this practice protects from great fear.
vishnu_gita::428.translation_literal: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति (in this selfless action no failure is) / प्रत्यवायो (reversal) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists) / स्वल्पमप्यस्य (even a small part of this) / धर्मस्य (of the duty) / त्रायते (protects) / महतो (from great) / भयात् (fear).
vishnu_gita::428.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::428.essence: Even the smallest selfless action never fails and guards you from great fear.
vishnu_gita::428.simple_meaning: Any selfless action you take will never fail or reverse. Even a small effort in this way protects you from great fear.
vishnu_gita::428.simple_insight: You can feel safe knowing even small selfless steps matter deeply and protect you.
vishnu_gita::428.detailed_meaning: In the midst of teaching selfless action, Vishnu reassures Arjuna that no effort in this path is ever lost or undone. Even doing a little of this duty safeguards against huge dangers, encouraging start and persistence.
vishnu_gita::428.modern_relevance: You stayed up late trying to help someone without expecting a reward. Even that small effort builds your courage and peace.
vishnu_gita::428.insight: It shifts your mind to value every selfless act, no matter how small, as truly protective and never wasted.

vishnu_gita::429.verse_sanskrit:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह यज्ञभुग्वराः !।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
vishnu_gita::429.verse_hindi: हे यज्ञभाग-भोग करने वालों में श्रेष्ट देवगण ! इस कर्मयोग, व्यवसायात्मिका अर्थात् निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धि एक होती है किन्तु अव्यवसायी अर्थात् सकाम कर्म करने वालों की बुद्धियाँ बहुशाखाओ से युक्त और अनन्त होती हैं
vishnu_gita::429.english_translation: Among those who enjoy the sacred ritual, the highest have a focused, steady wisdom; others have many scattered, endless thoughts.
vishnu_gita::429.translation_literal: व्यवसायात्मिका (focused/steadied) बुद्धि (wisdom) एकेह (one) यज्ञभुग्वराः (enjoyers of the sacrifice) बहुशाखा (many branches) हि (indeed) अनन्ताश्च (endless) बुद्धयः (wisdoms) अव्यवसायिनाम् (of the unfocused ones)
vishnu_gita::429.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::429.essence: Focused effort produces clear wisdom; scattered effort creates endless confusion.
vishnu_gita::429.simple_meaning: A focused and steady mind brings the highest wisdom in action, while a distracted mind multiplies endless confused thoughts.
vishnu_gita::429.simple_insight: You can feel calm and sure when your mind settles, instead of spinning in many directions.
vishnu_gita::429.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses those partaking in sacred action, explaining that a single, steady wisdom guides the best practitioners, unlike distracted actors whose minds scatter endlessly.
vishnu_gita::429.modern_relevance: When you try to juggle too many tasks or ideas, your mind feels chaotic; focusing on one purpose brings clarity and calm.
vishnu_gita::429.insight: It teaches you to cultivate steady attention and discipline to unify your mental energy for effective action.

vishnu_gita::430.verse_sanskrit:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।
वेदवादरता देवाः ! नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
vishnu_gita::430.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! वेद के अर्थवाद में तत्पर, "जगत के अतिरिक्त ईश्वरतत्त्व और कोई नहीं है" इस प्रकार कहने वाले,
vishnu_gita::430.english_translation: O divine beings! The wise who speak this flourishing teaching of the Vedas say: there is nothing beyond the supreme reality in the world.
vishnu_gita::430.translation_literal: यामिमां (this) पुष्पितां (flourishing) वाचं (speech) प्रवदन्ति (speak) अविपश्चितः (wise ones) । वेदवादरता (attached to Vedic arguments) देवाः (divine beings) ! नान्यदस्तीति (there is nothing else) वादिनः (those who argue) ॥
vishnu_gita::430.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::430.essence: Only the supreme reality exists beyond all else in the universe.
vishnu_gita::430.simple_meaning: The wise say that beyond everything in the universe, there is only the supreme reality and nothing else.
vishnu_gita::430.simple_insight: You can find peace in knowing there is nothing beyond the ultimate reality.
vishnu_gita::430.detailed_meaning: Addressing divine beings, Vishnu explains how the wise, deeply devoted to the Vedas, teach that the universe contains no reality beyond the supreme reality itself.
vishnu_gita::430.modern_relevance: When you feel lost in complexity, remember that at the core, only one true reality exists beyond all distractions.
vishnu_gita::430.insight: It shifts your view to see that all appearances point to a single ultimate reality, simplifying confusion.

vishnu_gita::431.verse_sanskrit:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलपदाम् ।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगति प्रति ॥
vishnu_gita::431.verse_hindi: कामात्मा और स्वर्ग सुख की इच्छा करने वाले जो अज्ञानी जीव हैं, वह जन्मकर्म फलप्रद, भोगैश्वर्य प्राप्ति के साधनभूत और यज्ञादि क्रिया विशेषप्राय पुष्पित वाक्य कहते रहते हैं
vishnu_gita::431.english_translation: Those driven by desire and craving for heavenly pleasures get caught in birth and karmic results, endlessly speaking of rituals and enjoyment as means to wealth and power.
vishnu_gita::431.translation_literal: कामात्मानः (desire-driven) स्वर्गपरा (seeking heaven) जन्मकर्मफलपदाम् (birth and fruit of action) क्रियाविशेषबहुलां (many special rituals) भोगैश्वर्यगति (path to enjoyment and power) प्रति (towards)
vishnu_gita::431.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::431.essence: Desire-driven actions trap you in endless cycles chasing fleeting pleasures and power.
vishnu_gita::431.simple_meaning: When you act driven by desire for pleasure or status, you stay stuck in a cycle of birth and karmic results, focusing on rituals and enjoyment as the goal.
vishnu_gita::431.simple_insight: There’s a fatigue in chasing pleasures that never truly satisfy or free you.
vishnu_gita::431.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes those who are driven by desire for heavenly pleasures. Such people get trapped in the cycle of birth and karma. They keep performing many rituals and seek enjoyment and power, believing these will bring lasting happiness, but remain caught in endless craving.
vishnu_gita::431.modern_relevance: You keep busy with habits and routines hoping to gain status or comfort, yet feel stuck in repeating cycles without true satisfaction.
vishnu_gita::431.insight: Recognize how desire-driven actions keep you tied to outcomes and prevent freedom from endless craving.

vishnu_gita::432.verse_sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
vishnu_gita::432.verse_hindi: उन पुष्पित वाक्यों से विचलित चित्त और भोगैश्वर्य में आसक्त व्यक्तियों की व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि समाधिक योग्य नहीं है
vishnu_gita::432.english_translation: For those distracted by pleasant words and attached to enjoyment and power, a focused intellect cannot settle into absorbed presence.
vishnu_gita::432.translation_literal: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां (of those attached to enjoyment and power) / तयापहृतचेतसाम् (whose minds are taken away by these) / व्यवसायात्मिका (a focused, persistent) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / समाधौ (in absorbed presence) / न (not) / विधीयते (is established)
vishnu_gita::432.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::432.essence: Attachment to enjoyment and power prevents focused intellect from reaching deep stillness.
vishnu_gita::432.simple_meaning: When your mind is distracted by pleasures and power, it can't focus deeply or find quiet inner stillness.
vishnu_gita::432.simple_insight: You feel restless until you release clinging to temporary enjoyments and control.
vishnu_gita::432.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that people attracted to pleasure and power have restless minds. Their intellect, scattered by desire, cannot achieve the deep concentration needed for absorbed presence or true inner calm.
vishnu_gita::432.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with endless notifications. Enjoying them feels good, but your focus breaks and inner quiet fades.
vishnu_gita::432.insight: This verse teaches you to recognize how attachment to fleeting rewards fragments your focus and blocks deep concentration.

vishnu_gita::433.verse_sanskrit:
यत्र काले ह्यनात्तिमात्तिश्चैव योगिनः।
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि विबुधर्षभाः ॥
vishnu_gita::433.verse_hindi: हे देवता गण ! जिस काल में अर्थात् कालरूप मार्ग में मरण के पश्चात् जाकर योगिगण अनावृत्ति (मोक्ष) और आवृत्ति (संसार में पुनः आगमन) को प्राप्त होते हैं उस कालरूप मार्ग का वर्णन करता हूँ
vishnu_gita::433.english_translation: O divine ones, I will describe the path of time where yogis, after death, attain liberation or return to the cycle of rebirth.
vishnu_gita::433.translation_literal: यत्र (where) / काले (in time) / हि (indeed) / अनात्ति (do not perish) / मात्ति (return) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / योगिनः (yogis) / प्रयाता (having departed) / यान्ति (go) / तं (that) / कालं (time) / वक्ष्यामि (I will describe) / विबुधर्षभाः (O best of the wise)
vishnu_gita::433.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::433.essence: After death, yogis follow a time-path leading either to freedom or return to rebirth.
vishnu_gita::433.simple_meaning: There is a path related to time where yogis, after death, either achieve freedom from rebirth or return again into the cycle.
vishnu_gita::433.simple_insight: The journey after death is not random but follows a path where freedom or return is possible.
vishnu_gita::433.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining he will reveal the nature of the time-path where yogis, after their physical death, either reach freedom (moksha) or return to worldly existence (samsara). This sets the stage for understanding life, death, and rebirth.
vishnu_gita::433.insight: It invites seeing death as a transition governed by deeper cosmic laws, not an end or random event.

vishnu_gita::434.verse_sanskrit:
अग्निज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
vishnu_gita::434.verse_hindi: अग्निज्योति अर्थात् अर्चि (तेज) की सकल अधिष्ठातृ देवताएँ, अहः अर्थात् दिवसाधिष्ठातृ देवता, शुक्लः अर्थात् शुक्ल पक्षाधिष्ठातृ देवता, उत्तरायण रूप छ:मास अर्थात् उत्तरायणाविष्ठातृ देवता, इन देवता गण का जो मार्ग है उसमें मृत्यु के बाद जाने वाले ब्रह्मवेत्तागण ब्रह्म को प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::434.english_translation: After death, those who know Brahman follow the path of the six months of the northern course—fire, light, day, bright fortnight, and the six-month ascending sun.
vishnu_gita::434.translation_literal: अग्निज्योतिरहः (fire light day) / शुक्लः (bright) / षण्मासा (six months) / उत्तरायणम् (northern course) / तत्र (there) / प्रयाता (going) / गच्छन्ति (go) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / ब्रह्मविदो (knowers of Brahman) / जनाः (people)
vishnu_gita::434.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::434.essence: Enlightened beings follow a sacred cosmic path after death to reach supreme understanding.
vishnu_gita::434.simple_meaning: Those who understand the supreme reality after death follow a sacred path aligned with natural cycles and reach union with that reality.
vishnu_gita::434.simple_insight: There is a path beyond death that leads to deep understanding and peace for those who seek truth.
vishnu_gita::434.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains a spiritual journey after death where enlightened beings follow the six-month northern path linked to cosmic cycles, symbolizing progress towards ultimate knowledge and union with the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::434.insight: It highlights a symbolic path of transformation aligned with natural rhythms leading to higher understanding beyond physical life.

vishnu_gita::435.verse_sanskrit:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् ।
तत्र चान्द्रमस ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्त्तते ॥
vishnu_gita::435.verse_hindi: कर्मयोगी (मरण के पश्चात् ) धूम, रात्रि, कृष्णपक्ष और दक्षिणायन छःमास इन सबके अधिष्ठातृ देवताओ के पास उत्तरोत्तर जाकर क्रम से चन्द्रलोक को प्राप्त करके भोगावसान में पुनः वहां से संसार में आता है
vishnu_gita::435.english_translation: After death, the karma yogi passes through smoke, night, the dark lunar fortnight, and the six months of the southern solstice, reaching the moon's realm and then returning to the cycle of existence.
vishnu_gita::435.translation_literal: धूमो (smoke) / रात्रिस्तथा (and night) / कृष्णः (dark/dark lunar fortnight) / षण्मासा (six months) / दक्षिणायनम् (southern solstice) / तत्र (there) / चान्द्रमस (moon) / ज्योतिः (light/realm) / योगी (the practitioner) / प्राप्य (attaining) / निवर्त्तते (returns)
vishnu_gita::435.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::435.essence: The committed actor moves through dark phases before returning to act again.
vishnu_gita::435.simple_meaning: After death, the person who acts with commitment passes through stages of darkness and time before returning to the world of life.
vishnu_gita::435.simple_insight: There is a cycle of transition after death before new beginnings unfold.
vishnu_gita::435.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how a karma yogi’s journey after death involves passing through symbolic phases like smoke, night, and lunar cycles, reaching a higher realm before returning to the world, emphasizing the ongoing cycle of action and rebirth.
vishnu_gita::435.modern_relevance: You’ve faced dark, confusing phases in life that felt like endings but led to new beginnings and growth.
vishnu_gita::435.insight: Recognize that difficult endings are part of a cycle leading to fresh starts and renewed effort.

vishnu_gita::436.verse_sanskrit:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती होते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।
एकया यात्यनादृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्त्तते पुनः ॥
vishnu_gita::436.verse_hindi: प्रकाशमय अचिरादि शुक्ला गति एवं तमोमय धूमादि कृष्णा गति, जगत् के ये दो मार्ग अनादि. रूप से प्रसिद्ध हैं, इन दोनों से एक के द्वारा मोक्ष प्राप्त होता है और दूसरे के द्वारा पुनः संसार में प्रत्यावृत्ति होती है
vishnu_gita::436.english_translation: The world moves in two eternal ways: the bright path leads to freedom, the dark path returns to the cycle again.
vishnu_gita::436.translation_literal: शुक्लकृष्णे (bright and dark) / गती (paths) / होते (exist) / जगतः (of the world) / शाश्वते (eternal) / मते (according to opinion) । / एकया (by one) / याति (goes) / अनादृत्तिम् (without return) / अन्यया (by the other) / आवर्त्तते (returns) / पुनः (again) ॥
vishnu_gita::436.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::436.essence: The world follows two eternal paths: one leads to liberation, the other to repeated return.
vishnu_gita::436.simple_meaning: The world follows two eternal paths: one bright leading to freedom without return, another dark leading back to repeated cycles.
vishnu_gita::436.simple_insight: There is a path that leads beyond repeating cycles, and another that keeps you returning.
vishnu_gita::436.detailed_meaning: This verse describes two eternal paths of the world: a bright, radiant path that leads to liberation without returning, and a dark, smoky path that causes repeated return to the cycle of life. It sets up the cosmic framework of duality and liberation.
vishnu_gita::436.insight: It shifts your understanding from seeing life as random to seeing two fundamental directions: ongoing return or final freedom.

vishnu_gita::437.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मेव कारणं शुक्लकृष्णगत्योर्न संशयः ।
स्वर्लोक निरयम्वाऽपि पितृलोकमथापि वा ॥
vishnu_gita::437.verse_hindi: कर्म ही शुक्ल और कृष्ण दोनों गति का निःसन्देह कारण है। हे देवगण ! जीवों को स्वर्गलोक प्राप्ति, नरकलोक प्राप्ति, पितृलोक प्राप्ति अथवा
vishnu_gita::437.english_translation: There is no doubt that karma is the cause of both the white and black paths, leading beings to heaven, the mortal world, or the realm of ancestors.
vishnu_gita::437.translation_literal: कर्मेव (karma alone) कारणं (cause) शुक्लकृष्णगत्योर्न (of the white and black paths) संशयः (doubt) । स्वर्लोक (heaven) निरयम् (hell) वा (or) अपि (also) पितृलोकम् (ancestor realm) अथापि (or even) वा (or) ।
vishnu_gita::437.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::437.essence: Every path you take results directly from the actions you perform.
vishnu_gita::437.simple_meaning: The results of your actions determine the path your life follows, whether toward higher or lower realms.
vishnu_gita::437.simple_insight: Knowing your actions shape your future brings responsibility and clarity to every moment.
vishnu_gita::437.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that karma—the sum of actions—is the undeniable reason beings move to different realms like heaven, earth, or ancestors' world, emphasizing the universal law of cause and effect.
vishnu_gita::437.modern_relevance: After a day of choices, you realize how every decision nudges your life’s direction, shaping your experience beyond your control.
vishnu_gita::437.insight: Recognize that your current state is shaped by past actions, empowering you to act wisely now.

vishnu_gita::438.verse_sanskrit:
आसाद्य प्रेतलोकम्बा जीवा यान्ति पुनः पुनः ।
मर्त्यलोके जनि देवाः ! कृष्णगत्या न संशयः ॥
vishnu_gita::438.verse_hindi: प्रेतलोक प्राप्ति करा कर  वारंवार मृत्युलोक में जन्मप्राप्ति कराना कृष्णगति का कार्य है इसमें सन्देह नहीं
vishnu_gita::438.english_translation: Beings repeatedly go to the realm of spirits and return to mortal life; birth in the mortal world is surely the path of Krishna.
vishnu_gita::438.translation_literal: आसाद्य (having reached) प्रेतलोकम्बा (the realm of spirits) जीवा (beings) यान्ति (go) पुनः (again) पुनः (again) । मर्त्यलोके (in the mortal world) जनि (are born) देवाः (beings) कृष्णगत्या (the path of Krishna) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
vishnu_gita::438.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::438.essence: Existence cycles between spirit realms and mortal life without interruption.
vishnu_gita::438.simple_meaning: Beings repeatedly die and are born again, moving between the spirit realm and mortal world, following the cycle known as Krishna's path.
vishnu_gita::438.simple_insight: Life and death cycle without end, moving through realms beyond our sight.
vishnu_gita::438.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that souls repeatedly pass through the realm of spirits and are reborn into mortal life, emphasizing the cyclical nature of existence and the certainty of this process as the path associated with Krishna.
vishnu_gita::438.insight: Recognize life as a cycle of recurring births and deaths beyond what we immediately perceive.

vishnu_gita::439.verse_sanskrit:
सत्यलोकन्तु सम्प्राप्य शुक्लगत्या समुन्नतम् ।
तत्र कर्मबलेनैव कैवल्यं लभ्यते ध्रुवम् ॥
vishnu_gita::439.verse_hindi: शुक्लगति के द्वारा समुन्नत सत्य लोक में पहुंचकर कर्म के बल से ही वहां निश्चय मुक्ति प्राप्त की जाती है
vishnu_gita::439.english_translation: By reaching the exalted realm of truth through the pure path, unwavering liberation is attained solely by the power of action.
vishnu_gita::439.translation_literal: सत्यलोकन्तु (to the realm of truth) / सम्प्राप्य (having reached) / शुक्लगत्या (by the pure path) / समुन्नतम् (exalted) / तत्र (there) / कर्मबलेनैव (only by the power of action) / कैवल्यं (liberation) / लभ्यते (is attained) / ध्रुवम् (unwavering)
vishnu_gita::439.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::439.essence: True freedom comes only through steadfast, pure action in the highest realm of truth.
vishnu_gita::439.simple_meaning: You can reach a high realm of truth by following a pure path, and only through your actions can you gain lasting freedom.
vishnu_gita::439.simple_insight: There's power in your actions; they alone can secure your true freedom.
vishnu_gita::439.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that by following a pure, dedicated path (shuklagati), one can reach the exalted realm of truth. But the key to steady liberation is not chance or knowledge alone—it is the power of your own action that secures lasting freedom.
vishnu_gita::439.modern_relevance: After you commit fully to a challenging goal with integrity, you realize that only your genuine efforts lead to lasting success, not shortcuts or waiting.
vishnu_gita::439.insight: It shifts focus from waiting for external help to trusting that your sincere actions create true freedom.

vishnu_gita::440.verse_sanskrit:
कृष्णगत्यां प्रधानाऽस्ति प्रवृत्तिवि बुधर्षभाः!।
शुक्लगत्यां निहत्तेस्तु प्राधान्यं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
vishnu_gita::440.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! कृष्ण गति में प्रवृत्ति प्रधान है और शुक्लगति में निवृत्ति प्रधान कही गई है
vishnu_gita::440.english_translation: O divine beings! In the dark path, action dominates, and in the bright path, renunciation prevails.
vishnu_gita::440.translation_literal: कृष्णगत्यां (in the dark path) प्रधानाऽस्ति (dominates) प्रवृत्तिवि (action indeed) बुधर्षभाः (O best among the wise)! शुक्लगत्यां (in the bright path) निहत्तेस्तु (is renunciation) प्राधान्यं (dominance) परिकीर्तितम् (declared).
vishnu_gita::440.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::440.essence: Movement through life balances between acting and renouncing depending on the path you choose.
vishnu_gita::440.simple_meaning: There are two ways of moving through life: the dark way focuses on action, the bright way focuses on renunciation or stopping.
vishnu_gita::440.simple_insight: You sense relief knowing sometimes moving forward means acting; sometimes it means stepping back.
vishnu_gita::440.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings explaining two main paths: the 'dark' path emphasizes active doing, while the 'bright' path emphasizes renouncing action, highlighting a core duality in how beings pursue progress.
vishnu_gita::440.modern_relevance: You juggle times when pushing hard feels right and times when stepping back and releasing feels wiser.
vishnu_gita::440.insight: It shifts your view to recognize both action and renunciation as valid paths depending on your inner state.

vishnu_gita::441.verse_sanskrit:
आभ्यां भिन्ना गतिश्चान्या गतिभ्यां समुदाहृता ।
सहजाख्या च वो देवाः ! याऽधिकाराद्वहिर्गता॥
vishnu_gita::441.verse_hindi: इन दोनों गतियों के अतिरिक्त एक तीसरी गति और कही गई है जिसको सहज गति कहते हैं जो सहजगति हे देवतागण ! आपलोगों के अधिकार से बाहर है
vishnu_gita::441.english_translation: Besides these two paths, there is a third called the natural path, which lies beyond your control, O deities.
vishnu_gita::441.translation_literal: आभ्यां (from these two) भिन्ना (different) गति: (paths) अन्याः (other) गति: (paths) समुदाहृता (declared) सहजाख्या (called natural) च (and) वः (your) देवाः (O deities)! याऽधिकारात् (from authority) वहिर्गता (beyond gone).
vishnu_gita::441.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::441.essence: A third natural course exists beyond any control or authority you hold.
vishnu_gita::441.simple_meaning: Besides two known paths, there is a third called the natural path that exists beyond your control or authority.
vishnu_gita::441.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing some processes flow freely beyond your influence.
vishnu_gita::441.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes to celestial beings that beyond the two known paths of action or wisdom, a third natural path exists. This path is spontaneous and outside their control, indicating some truths or flows are beyond even divine command.
vishnu_gita::441.modern_relevance: You plan and prepare, but sometimes life unfolds in ways you cannot steer or control.
vishnu_gita::441.insight: It invites you to recognize and accept what unfolds naturally beyond your influence without resistance.

vishnu_gita::442.verse_sanskrit:
मद्भक्ता धर्मतत्त्वज्ञा आत्मज्ञानरताश्च ये।
त एवैतां महात्मानो  लभ्यन्ते सहजां गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::442.verse_hindi: जो धर्मतत्त्व के जानने वाले, आत्मज्ञान में तत्पर, मेरे भक्त महापुरुष गण हैं, वे ही इस तीसरी गति को प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::442.english_translation: Those who know the essence of dharma, are eager in self-knowledge, and are my devoted noble ones alone attain this natural state.
vishnu_gita::442.translation_literal: मद्भक्ता (my devoted) / धर्मतत्त्वज्ञा (knowers of the essence of dharma) / आत्मज्ञानरताश्च (and eager in self-knowledge) / ये (those who) / त एव (only they) / एतां (this) / महात्मानो (noble ones) / लभ्यन्ते (attain) / सहजां (natural) / गतिम् (state).
vishnu_gita::442.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::442.essence: Devoted love and self-knowledge together bring a natural, effortless state.
vishnu_gita::442.simple_meaning: Only those who sincerely love the divine, understand true dharma, and seek self-knowledge reach an effortless, natural state.
vishnu_gita::442.simple_insight: You feel seen and steady when devotion blends with deep knowing.
vishnu_gita::442.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that among many, only those who combine devoted love for the divine, understanding of dharma’s essence, and active pursuit of self-knowledge truly reach a natural, stable state beyond struggle.
vishnu_gita::442.modern_relevance: When your passion for what’s right meets a sincere desire to understand yourself, your life feels more naturally aligned and peaceful.
vishnu_gita::442.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing external results to cultivating inner devotion and wisdom together.

vishnu_gita::443.verse_sanskrit:
तत्वज्ञास्य लाभे ये वासनया: क्षये तथा ।
कर्मयोगे रता यन्ति जीन्मुक्तास्तु तां गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::443.verse_hindi: जो वासना का नाश, तत्त्वज्ञान लाभ और कर्मयोग में रत हैं, वे जीवन्मुक्तगण इस गति को प्राप्त करते हैं
vishnu_gita::443.english_translation: Those who destroy desires, attain knowledge of reality, and delight in the yoga of action reach the state of liberation while alive.
vishnu_gita::443.translation_literal: तत्वज्ञास्य (of knowledge of reality) / लाभे (in attainment) / ये (those who) / वासनया: (by desires) / क्षये (by destruction) / तथा (also) / कर्मयोगे (in the yoga of action) / रता (delighted) / यन्ति (attain) / जीव-मुक्ताः (liberated while alive) / तां (that) / गतिम् (state).
vishnu_gita::443.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::443.essence: Freedom arises when desire ends and action is embraced with clarity and joy.
vishnu_gita::443.simple_meaning: You reach true freedom alive by ending desires, gaining clear understanding, and fully engaging in selfless action.
vishnu_gita::443.simple_insight: There is freedom in releasing cravings and finding joy in your actions themselves.
vishnu_gita::443.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that those who overcome their inner cravings, gain true knowledge of what is real, and dedicate themselves to the path of selfless action become liberated while still living.
vishnu_gita::443.modern_relevance: After endless scrolling, you realize that letting go of wants and focusing on meaningful work brings a calm freedom alive.
vishnu_gita::443.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing outcomes to embracing pure action, opening the possibility of freedom now.

vishnu_gita::444.verse_sanskrit:
अतीवास्ति सुदुज्ञेया गतिर्देवा: ! हि कर्मण: ।
तत्रोदाहरण ह्योकं विषदं शृणुतामरा:! ॥
vishnu_gita::444.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! कर्म की गति अत्यन्त ही दुर्ज्ञेय है। हे देवगण ! इसमें एक स्पष्ट उदाहरण सुनो
vishnu_gita::444.english_translation: O radiant beings! The course of action is extremely difficult to understand. O radiant beings! Listen to a clear example of it.
vishnu_gita::444.translation_literal: अतीवास्ति (extremely is) सुदुज्ञेया (difficult to understand) गति: (course) देवा: (O radiant beings) हि (indeed) कर्मण: (of action) तत्र (there) उदाहरण (example) हि (indeed) ॉकम् (one) विषदं (clear) शृणुताम (listen) अराः (O radiant beings)
vishnu_gita::444.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::444.essence: The course of action is extremely complex and hard to understand.
vishnu_gita::444.simple_meaning: The path of action is very hard to fully grasp. Here is a clear example to help understand it.
vishnu_gita::444.simple_insight: You feel how confusing action can be without clear guidance.
vishnu_gita::444.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the radiant beings (devas), stating that understanding the nature and course of action is extremely difficult. He prepares to explain a clear example to clarify this complex topic.
vishnu_gita::444.insight: It shows that action and its consequences are not always straightforward, inviting patience and careful study.

vishnu_gita::445.verse_sanskrit:
ग्रंथीना बन्धनं कर्म ग्रंथिमोचनमित्यपि ।
तुल्यं कर्मद्वयं देवा उदर्के त्वन्तरं महत् ॥
vishnu_gita::445.verse_hindi: गांठ का बांधना भी कर्म है और गांठ का खोलना भी कर्म,  हे देवगण ! दोनों कर्म तुल्य हैं किन्तु अन्तिम परिणाम में बड़ा भेद है
vishnu_gita::445.english_translation: Tying a knot is action, and untying a knot is also action; both actions are equal, O deities, but the final result differs greatly.
vishnu_gita::445.translation_literal: ग्रंथीना (by knots) / बन्धनं (tying) / कर्म (action) / ग्रंथिमोचनमिति (knot untying) / अपि (also) / तुल्यं (equal) / कर्मद्वयं (two actions) / देवा (O deities) / उदर्के (in result) / त्वन्तरं (difference) / महत् (great)
vishnu_gita::445.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::445.essence: Two equal actions can produce very different results depending on their nature.
vishnu_gita::445.simple_meaning: Both tying and untying a knot are actions, but while the actions seem equal, their outcomes are very different.
vishnu_gita::445.simple_insight: You can do similar actions that feel equal, yet their true impact can be very different.
vishnu_gita::445.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that both binding and unbinding are actions with equal effort, but their consequences are significantly different, teaching Arjuna that the quality and outcome of actions matter deeply.
vishnu_gita::445.modern_relevance: You might work hard either to create or to undo a situation; although both require effort, the lasting effects can be very different.
vishnu_gita::445.insight: It teaches you to recognize that the apparent similarity of actions hides very different consequences and to act with awareness of outcome.

vishnu_gita::446.verse_sanskrit:
मोचनान्मुच्यते वस्तु बन्धनाचनियम्यते ।
तथा सकामनिष्कामौ देवा जानीत कर्मणी ॥
vishnu_gita::446.verse_hindi: गांठ के बांधने रूपी कर्म द्वारा जैसे पदार्थ बांधा जाता है वैसे गांठ के खोलने रूपी कर्मा द्वारा पदार्थ खुल जाता है । इसी उदाहरण के अनुसार हे देवगण ! सकाम और निष्काम कर्म जो जानो
vishnu_gita::446.english_translation: Just as an object tied by binding knots is freed by untying those knots, similarly, O radiant beings, understand that both desire-driven and desireless actions are performed.
vishnu_gita::446.translation_literal: मोचनान्मुच्यते (by untying, is freed) / वस्तु (object) / बन्धनाचनियम्यते (by binding knots, is tied) / तथा (thus) / सकामनिष्कामौ (desireful and desireless) / देवा (O radiant beings) / जानीत (know) / कर्मणी (in actions)
vishnu_gita::446.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::446.essence: Both desireful and desireless actions can free you from bondage.
vishnu_gita::446.simple_meaning: Just like untying knots frees what was tied, you can free yourself by performing both desire-driven and selfless actions.
vishnu_gita::446.simple_insight: There's hope in knowing that both kinds of action help you break free from what holds you back.
vishnu_gita::446.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that actions tied like knots can also be untied through action itself. He addresses radiant beings, teaching that both acting with desire and without desire are valid ways to release bondage.
vishnu_gita::446.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in habits or problems, but taking action—whether motivated by want or by selflessness—can help you break free.
vishnu_gita::446.insight: It teaches you to see all action as a tool for liberation, not just selfless acts.

vishnu_gita::447.verse_sanskrit:
हैमी लौहमयी वापि शङ्खला किम्विधापि चेत् ।
पाणिनां बन्धनायैव कल्पते नात्र संशयः ॥
vishnu_gita::447.verse_hindi: लौह निर्मित अथवा स्वर्ण निर्मित किसी प्रकार की भी शृंखला हो वह जीवों को बांधती ही है इसमें सन्देह नहीं
vishnu_gita::447.english_translation: Whether made of iron or gold, any chain binds living beings without doubt.
vishnu_gita::447.translation_literal: हैमी (iron) / लौहमयी (made of metal) / वापि (or) / शङ्खला (chain) / किम्विधापि (of any kind) / चेत् (if) / पाणिनां (of beings) / बन्धनायैव (for binding) / कल्पते (is made) / नात्र (there is no) / संशयः (doubt)
vishnu_gita::447.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::447.essence: All attachments, regardless of their appearance, bind living beings without exception.
vishnu_gita::447.simple_meaning: Chains made of any material, like iron or gold, bind living beings without exception.
vishnu_gita::447.simple_insight: You feel how all attachments, regardless of their form, hold you firmly.
vishnu_gita::447.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that whether a chain is made of iron or gold, it serves to bind living beings. This metaphor shows that external differences don’t change the binding nature of attachments or limitations.
vishnu_gita::447.modern_relevance: You might cling to comforts or achievements, but no matter their nature, they can still limit your freedom.
vishnu_gita::447.insight: It teaches you to see that the form of what binds you doesn’t matter; the binding itself is what limits.

vishnu_gita::448.verse_sanskrit:
तथा सकामकर्माऽपि शुभं वाप्यशुभं भवेत् ।
बनाति मुदृढ़ जीवानिति जानीत निर्जराः ॥
vishnu_gita::448.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार सकाम कर्म चाहे शुभ या अशुभ हो वह जीवों को अच्छी तरह बाँधता ही है, हे देवगण ! सो जानो
vishnu_gita::448.english_translation: Similarly, even desire-driven actions, whether good or bad, firmly bind living beings, O radiant ones, know this well.
vishnu_gita::448.translation_literal:
तथा (similarly) सकामकर्माऽपि (desire-driven actions even) शुभं (good) वापि (or) अशुभं (bad) भवेत् (becomes) ।
बनाति (binds) मुदृढ़ (firmly) जीवानिति (living beings) जानीत (know) निर्जराः (O radiant ones) ॥
vishnu_gita::448.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::448.essence: Desire-driven actions bind living beings firmly, regardless of being good or bad.
vishnu_gita::448.simple_meaning: Actions done with desire, whether positive or negative, strongly bind living beings to consequences.
vishnu_gita::448.simple_insight: Realizing desire binds you helps ease blame and clarifies the cause of your entanglement.
vishnu_gita::448.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that any action motivated by desire, regardless of its moral value, creates firm bonds for living beings, highlighting the trap of attachment that transcends good or bad outcomes.
vishnu_gita::448.modern_relevance: You chase a promotion or avoid conflict, but your craving keeps you tied, whether the result feels good or bad.
vishnu_gita::448.insight: It shifts your view to see desire itself as the binding force, not just the action’s outcome.

vishnu_gita::449.verse_sanskrit:
वासनाया: क्षये जाते तत्त्वज्ञानेन सर्वथा ।
कर्तव्यबुद्धया यत्कर्म निष्कामं क्रियतेऽमराः ॥
vishnu_gita::449.verse_hindi: तत्त्वज्ञान के द्वारा वासना के सर्वथा नाश होने पर कर्तव्य बुद्धि के अनुसार जो कर्म निष्काम भाव से किया जाता है हे देवगण !
vishnu_gita::449.english_translation: When desires are completely destroyed by true knowledge, actions performed with the intellect of duty become selfless.
vishnu_gita::449.translation_literal: वासनाया: (of desires) क्षये (in destruction) जाते (going away) तत्त्वज्ञानेन (by true knowledge) सर्वथा (completely) । कर्तव्यबुद्धया (with the intellect of duty) यत्कर्म (which action) निष्कामं (selfless) क्रियतेऽमराः (is done by the immortal beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::449.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::449.essence: True knowledge ends desire, enabling selfless action driven solely by duty.
vishnu_gita::449.simple_meaning: When your desires vanish through clear understanding, you naturally act without wanting any results, guided only by your sense of duty.
vishnu_gita::449.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful acting without craving, grounded in what truly needs doing.
vishnu_gita::449.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches here that when someone gains true knowledge that destroys all desires, their mind becomes free. Then, actions arise purely from their clear sense of duty, without selfish motives. This is the state of immortality and freedom from reaction.
vishnu_gita::449.modern_relevance: You finish a tough task without hoping for praise or reward, simply because it needs to be done—and that calms your restless mind.
vishnu_gita::449.insight: It teaches you to shift from acting for outcomes to acting because the action itself is right and necessary.

vishnu_gita::450.verse_sanskrit:
कैवल्यकारणं भूत्वा जीवेभ्यस्ताद्धि निश्चितम्।
यस्या न पुनराशत्तिस्तां दत्ते सहजां गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::450.verse_hindi: वही निश्चय मुक्ति का कारण होकर जिससे पुनरावृत्ति नहीं होती उस सहजगति को जीवों को देता है
vishnu_gita::450.english_translation: The supreme cause of freedom, which prevents rebirth, grants living beings their natural way.
vishnu_gita::450.translation_literal: कैवल्यकारणं (cause of liberation) / भूत्वा (having become) / जीवेभ्यः (to living beings) / ताद्धि (that) / निश्चितम् (certain) / यस्या (by which) / न (not) / पुनराशत्ति (again falls) / तां (that) / दत्ते (gives) / सहजां (natural) / गतिम् (way)
vishnu_gita::450.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::450.essence: True freedom arises from a cause that ends repeated returning and grants natural flow.
vishnu_gita::450.simple_meaning: There is a true cause of inner freedom that stops the cycle of returning and grants beings their natural course.
vishnu_gita::450.simple_insight: You can trust that freedom is a natural state that ends repeated cycles.
vishnu_gita::450.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the ultimate cause of liberation creates a natural flow for living beings, preventing their return to repeated cycles. This teaching reveals the source of true freedom beyond repeated existence.
vishnu_gita::450.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck repeating the same patterns, this reminds you there is a cause that can naturally free you.
vishnu_gita::450.insight: It teaches to recognize and align with the natural cause that ends repetitive cycles, not just temporary fixes.

vishnu_gita::451.verse_sanskrit:
जीवन्मुक्तोऽथ सम्प्राप्तः सहजां गतिमुत्तमाम् ।
मरुस्थलेऽथवा जह्याच्छरीरं जाह्नवीतटे ॥
vishnu_gita::451.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! उत्तम  सहजगति को प्राप्त जीवन्मुक्त चाहे मरुस्थल मे शरीरत्याग करे चाहे गंगातीर में शरीरत्याग करे,
vishnu_gita::451.english_translation: O divine beings! A liberated being who has attained the highest natural state may leave the body either in a desert or on the banks of the Ganges.
vishnu_gita::451.translation_literal: जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated being) / अथ (then) / सम्प्राप्तः (attained) / सहजां (natural, effortless) / गतिम् (state) / उत्तमाम् (highest) । / मरुस्थले (in desert) / अथवा (or) / जह्यत् (abandons) / शरीरं (body) / जाह्नवीतटे (on banks of the Ganges) ॥
vishnu_gita::451.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::451.essence: True liberation means the place of leaving the body no longer matters.
vishnu_gita::451.simple_meaning: A liberated person who has reached the highest natural state can leave the body anywhere without concern for place.
vishnu_gita::451.simple_insight: Freedom means the true self is not tied to any place or body at death.
vishnu_gita::451.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that one who has achieved liberation and the supreme natural state of being is free to depart from the body at any place, whether harsh like a desert or sacred like the Ganges bank. This shows liberation transcends external conditions.
vishnu_gita::451.insight: It shifts your view from attachment to place or circumstances at death to freedom of the inner being.

vishnu_gita::452.verse_sanskrit:
अथवा कृतकृत्योऽसौ  मुक्तात्मा स्वात्मवित्सुरा ।
अन्तिमश्वासपर्यन्तं वसेचाण्डालवेश्मनि ॥
vishnu_gita::452.verse_hindi: चाहे वह कृतकृत्य आत्मज्ञानी मुक्तात्मा चांडाल के गृह में अपने अन्तिम श्वास तक वास करे,
vishnu_gita::452.english_translation: Even if a liberated true self, knowledgeable of itself, lives until its last breath in the home of an outcast,
vishnu_gita::452.translation_literal: अथवा (or) कृतकृत्योऽसौ (that one, who has fulfilled all duties) मुक्तात्मा (liberated self) स्वात्मवित्सुरा (knowing own true self) अन्तिमश्वासपर्यन्तं (until last breath) वसे (resides) चाण्डालवेश्मनि (in an outcast’s home)
vishnu_gita::452.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::452.essence: Inner freedom remains intact regardless of external environment or social status.
vishnu_gita::452.simple_meaning: A truly liberated person remains free inside, no matter where they live or what their surroundings are.
vishnu_gita::452.simple_insight: Your freedom is not tied to your outer conditions but to your inner knowing.
vishnu_gita::452.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that even if a person who has realized their true self lives in the harshest environment, like the home of an outcast, they remain free and untouched inside until their last breath.
vishnu_gita::452.modern_relevance: You might feel stuck in a difficult place or situation, yet your inner being can remain free and unshaken no matter what.
vishnu_gita::452.insight: It teaches you to separate your inner state from external circumstances, preserving freedom despite harsh surroundings.

vishnu_gita::453.verse_sanskrit:
प्राणायाम प्रकुर्वत वां देहं देवालये त्यजेत ।
सर्वत्र सर्वदा तस्य मुक्तावस्थाऽवतिष्ठते ॥
vishnu_gita::453.verse_hindi: चाहे देवमन्दिर में प्राणायाम करता हुआ देहत्याग करे, उसकी मुक्तदशा सब स्थानों में हर समय बनी रहती है
vishnu_gita::453.english_translation: If someone leaves their body practicing breath control in a divine temple, their state of freedom remains everywhere and always.
vishnu_gita::453.translation_literal: प्राणायाम (breath control) / प्रकुर्वत (performing) / वां (or) / देहं (body) / देवालये (in divine temple) / त्यजेत (should leave) / । / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / सर्वदा (always) / तस्य (of that one) / मुक्तावस्थाऽवतिष्ठते (state of freedom remains) / ॥
vishnu_gita::453.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::453.essence: Freedom gained through focused practice transcends time and place.
vishnu_gita::453.simple_meaning: When someone dies while practicing breath control in a sacred place, their state of freedom continues everywhere at all times.
vishnu_gita::453.simple_insight: Freedom achieved in sincere practice is not bound by place or moment.
vishnu_gita::453.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that if a person leaves their body while engaged in prānāyāma (breath control) within a temple, their liberated state persists universally and permanently, showing the power of disciplined spiritual practice.
vishnu_gita::453.modern_relevance: You might feel peaceful after a deep meditation session in a quiet room, and that calm stays with you beyond the moment and place.
vishnu_gita::453.insight: Recognize that disciplined spiritual effort creates lasting inner freedom beyond physical limits.

vishnu_gita::454.verse_sanskrit:
जलबिन्दुर्यथाऽऽकाशपतितो यति वारिधिम ।
तथैव स हि मुक्तात्मा लभते मामसंशयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::454.verse_hindi: वह मुक्तारमा आकाश पतित वारिबिन्दु के समुद्र में पतित होने के समान मुझको निस्सन्देह प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::454.english_translation: The liberated soul surely attains me just as a water drop falling from the sky merges into the ocean.
vishnu_gita::454.translation_literal: जल (water) बिन्दु (drop) यथा (just as) आकाश (sky)पतित (fallen) यति (goes) वारिधिम (to ocean) । तथा (thus) एव (indeed) स (he) हि (surely) मुक्तात्मा (liberated soul) लभते (attains) माम् (me) असंशयम् (without doubt) ॥
vishnu_gita::454.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::454.essence: Freedom is merging completely with the true self like a drop joining the ocean.
vishnu_gita::454.simple_meaning: A person freed from all bondage naturally unites with the true self, just as a water drop falls into and becomes one with the ocean.
vishnu_gita::454.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true nature cannot be lost; it always returns to the whole.
vishnu_gita::454.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a liberated soul, free from confusion and attachment, inevitably merges with the supreme reality, like a water drop falling from the sky joining the ocean, symbolizing complete union and dissolution of separateness.
vishnu_gita::454.modern_relevance: When you let go of your fears and identities, you naturally reconnect with your deepest sense of belonging and peace, like a drop falling back into the vast ocean.
vishnu_gita::454.insight: It teaches you that freedom means dissolving the illusion of separateness and embracing your essential unity.

vishnu_gita::455.verse_sanskrit:
युष्माभिरपि भो देवाः ! कर्मयोगरतात्म्भि:।
कर्तव्यबुद्धया सततं कार्य कर्म विधीयताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::455.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! आपको कर्मयोग में रत होकर कर्तव्य बुद्धि से सर्वदा कर्त्तव्य कर्म को करना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::455.english_translation: O radiant beings! You should always perform your duty with steady wisdom, engaged in the yoga of action.
vishnu_gita::455.translation_literal: युष्माभि (by you all) अपि (also) भो (O) देवाः (radiant beings) ! कर्मयोगरतात्म्भि: (engaged in the yoga of action with steady mind) । कर्तव्यबुद्धया (with the wisdom of duty) सततं (always) कार्य (to be done) कर्म (action) विधीयताम् (should be performed) ॥
vishnu_gita::455.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::455.essence: Steady wisdom and commitment guide you to perform your duties well.
vishnu_gita::455.simple_meaning: You should always perform your duties with steady wisdom while being fully engaged in your actions.
vishnu_gita::455.simple_insight: There is strength in steady focus and clarity when doing what must be done.
vishnu_gita::455.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu addresses radiant beings, urging them to embrace steady wisdom and consistently perform their duties through dedicated action. It's a call to maintain clarity and commitment in fulfilling one's responsibilities.
vishnu_gita::455.modern_relevance: You face a demanding project that requires consistent effort and clear thinking; staying steady and focused helps you meet your responsibilities well.
vishnu_gita::455.insight: Focus your mind steadily on your duty, letting wisdom guide your actions without distraction.

vishnu_gita::456.verse_sanskrit:
देवाः : कुरुत कम्माणि योगस्थाः सङ्गवर्जिताः।
सिद्धयसिद्धयोः समा भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::456.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! इन्द्रियसङ्ग का त्याग करके, सिद्धि और असिद्धि में समभावापन्न होकर और योग में अवस्थित होकर कर्म करना ,समत्व ही, योग कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::456.english_translation: O radiant beings, perform actions established in yoga, free from attachment; being equal in success and failure, that equality is called yoga.
vishnu_gita::456.translation_literal: देवाः (O radiant beings) : कुरुत (perform) कम्माणि (actions) योगस्थाः (established in yoga) सङ्गवर्जिताः (free from attachment). सिद्धयसिद्धयोः (of success and failure) समा (equal) भूत्वा (being) समत्वं (equality) योग (yoga) उच्यते (is called).
vishnu_gita::456.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::456.essence: Act fully without attachment, remaining steady through success and failure.
vishnu_gita::456.simple_meaning: You should act without clinging to your senses or the outcomes, staying calm whether you succeed or fail. This balanced state is called yoga.
vishnu_gita::456.simple_insight: You find peace when you stop chasing results and treat success and failure the same.
vishnu_gita::456.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, advising them to perform their duties without attachment to the senses or craving. He teaches that true yoga is maintaining equal calmness in both success and failure, embodying steady action.
