vishnu_gita::456.modern_relevance: You sent an important email but didn’t obsess over the reply. You did your best and stayed calm no matter what happened next.
vishnu_gita::456.insight: Shift focus from craving outcomes to steady action without attachment, equalizing success and failure.

vishnu_gita::457.verse_sanskrit:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्मादयोगाय युज्यध्वं योगः कर्म सुकौशलम् ॥
vishnu_gita::457.verse_hindi: बुद्धि द्वारा ब्रह्म में युक्त व्यक्ति इस लोक में सुकृत दुष्कृत (पुण्य पाप ) दोनों को ही त्याग करता है इस कारण आपलोग कर्मयोग में नियुक्त हुए, सुकौशल पूर्ण कर्म ही योगपद वाच्य हैं
vishnu_gita::457.english_translation: A person united with the discerning mind abandons both good and bad deeds here; therefore, engage in yoga, for yoga is skillful action.
vishnu_gita::457.translation_literal: बुद्धियुक्तो (with discerning mind) / जहातीह (abandons here) / उभे (both) / सुकृतदुष्कृते (good deeds and bad deeds)। तस्मात् (therefore) / योगाय (for yoga) / युज्यध्वं (engage) / योगः (yoga) / कर्म (action) / सुकौशलम् (skillful).
vishnu_gita::457.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::457.essence: Wise action frees you from attachment to both praise and blame.
vishnu_gita::457.simple_meaning: When you act with a discerning mind, you give up attachment to good or bad outcomes. Yoga means skillful action without craving results.
vishnu_gita::457.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting wisely without clinging to rewards or blame.
vishnu_gita::457.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains to Arjuna that a person who acts with clear understanding lets go of both positive and negative results. This moment shifts Arjuna from confusion to clarity about performing action as yoga—skillful and unattached.
vishnu_gita::457.modern_relevance: You finish a project knowing your effort was good, yet you don’t obsess over praise or criticism that follows.
vishnu_gita::457.insight: It shifts your focus from outcomes to the quality of your effort, making your action pure and present.

vishnu_gita::458.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मजै बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
vishnu_gita::458.verse_hindi: बुद्धियुक्त पंडित गण निश्चय ही कर्मजनित फल को त्याग करके जन्मरूप बन्धन से मुक्त होकर सर्वोपद्र वशुन्य मोक्षपद को प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::458.english_translation: Wise people united with discernment renounce the fruits of actions and become free from the bondage of birth, attaining the spotless state of liberation.
vishnu_gita::458.translation_literal: कर्मजै (from actions) / बुद्धियुक्ता (united with discernment) / हि (indeed) / फलं (the fruit) / त्यक्त्वा (having renounced) / मनीषिणः (wise people) / जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः (free from birth bondage) / पदं (the state) / गच्छन्ति (go) / अनामयम् (spotless, free from disease)
vishnu_gita::458.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::458.essence: Acting with discernment and releasing attachment to results leads to true freedom.
vishnu_gita::458.simple_meaning: You can act with clear understanding and give up expecting results, freeing yourself from the cycle of rebirth and reaching liberation.
vishnu_gita::458.simple_insight: Letting go of craving results brings a deep sense of freedom and peace.
vishnu_gita::458.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains that wise people who act with clear discernment do not cling to the outcomes of their deeds. By doing so, they free themselves from the binding cycle of birth and death and attain a pure, liberated state.
vishnu_gita::458.modern_relevance: You finish a project and accept whatever happens next, freeing yourself from stress over results beyond your control.
vishnu_gita::458.insight: Shift focus from expecting outcomes to performing actions with wisdom and detachment.

vishnu_gita::459.verse_sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यदवत् ।
तद्वत कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
vishnu_gita::459.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार ( नाना नदियों के द्वारा) आपूर्यमाण और अचञ्चल समुद्र में (अन्य ) जलप्रवेश करते हैं अर्थात् उसमें मिल जाते हैं। उसी प्रकार जिसमें सकल कामनाएं प्रवेश करती हैं अर्थात् लीन होती हैं वह शान्ति को प्राप्त होता है किन्तु भोगकामनाशील व्यक्ति शान्ति को नहीं प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::459.english_translation: Just as countless rivers enter the ever-full and steady ocean, all desires that merge within bring peace; but those who cling to desires do not find peace.
vishnu_gita::459.translation_literal: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं (ever-full and steady) / समुद्रमापः (ocean) / प्रविशन्ति (enter) / यदवत् (just as) । तद्वत (in the same way) / कामा (desires) / यं (which) / प्रविशन्ति (enter) / सर्वे (all) / स (that) / शान्तिमाप्नोति (attain peace) / न (not) / कामकामी (desire-clinging) ॥
vishnu_gita::459.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::459.essence: True peace arises when all desires merge and settle within like rivers in the ocean.
vishnu_gita::459.simple_meaning: When all your desires come together and settle calmly within you, you find peace. But if you cling to desires, peace stays distant.
vishnu_gita::459.simple_insight: Peace feels possible when you stop chasing desires and let them settle inside you.
vishnu_gita::459.detailed_meaning: Vishnu compares the vast ocean, always full and steady, to the mind where desires flow like rivers. When all desires enter and dissolve calmly, peace arises. But those who keep wanting more remain restless and unsettled.
vishnu_gita::459.modern_relevance: You’ve felt scattered, pulled by endless wants—peace arrives only when you let these desires settle, like rivers joining the ocean.
vishnu_gita::459.insight: It teaches you to allow desires to merge and quiet rather than resist or chase them, opening the way to inner peace.

vishnu_gita::460.verse_sanskrit:
विहाय कामान् यः सर्वान् प्राणी चरति निःस्पृहः।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::460.verse_hindi: जो प्राणी सकल काम्य वस्तुओं की उपेक्षा करके नि:स्पृह निरहङ्कार और विषयों में ममताशून्य होकर यत्र तत्र भ्रमण करता है वह शान्ति को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::460.english_translation: One who gives up all desires, moves without craving, without attachment or ego, attains peace.
vishnu_gita::460.translation_literal: विहाय (giving up) कामान् (desires) यः (who) सर्वान् (all) प्राणी (being) चरति (moves) निःस्पृहः (without craving) निर्ममो (without attachment) निरहङ्कारः (without ego) स (that one) शान्तिमधिगच्छति (attains peace)
vishnu_gita::460.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::460.essence: Peace arises when you move without craving, attachment, or ego.
vishnu_gita::460.simple_meaning: You find peace when you let go of all desires, attachments, and ego, moving through life without craving.
vishnu_gita::460.simple_insight: Freedom from craving and ego brings a deep calm you can carry anywhere.
vishnu_gita::460.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a being who abandons all desires and acts without craving or ego moves freely and attains peace. This moment reveals the power of renouncing attachments to find calm amidst life's movement.
vishnu_gita::460.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly, chasing wants and comparisons, feeling restless. Letting go of craving opens space for calm, no matter where you are.
vishnu_gita::460.insight: This teaches you to act without chasing outcomes or owning your identity and thus discover inner peace.

vishnu_gita::461.verse_sanskrit:
लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयाऽनघाः !।
ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्ययानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम ॥
vishnu_gita::461.verse_hindi: हे निष्पापो ! इस लोक में दो प्रकार की निष्ठा मैंने पहले कही है, यथाः- ज्ञानयोग द्वारा सांख्यों की और कर्म योग द्वारा योगियों की
vishnu_gita::461.english_translation: O sinless one, in this world I have previously taught two kinds of devotion: the path of wisdom for the contemplatives and the path of action for the yogis.
vishnu_gita::461.translation_literal: लोकेऽस्मिन् (in the world) / द्विविधा (two kinds) / निष्ठा (devotion/steadiness) / पुरा (before) / प्रोक्ता (taught) / मयाऽनघाः (by me, O sinless one) / ज्ञानयोगेन (by the path of wisdom) / सांख्ययानां (of the contemplatives) / कर्मयोगेन (by the path of action) / योगिनाम् (of the yogis)
vishnu_gita::461.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::461.essence: Steadiness in life arises through either knowledge or selfless action.
vishnu_gita::461.simple_meaning: There are two main ways to steady your devotion: through knowledge or through selfless action.
vishnu_gita::461.simple_insight: You don’t have to choose only one path—both wisdom and action connect you to the true self.
vishnu_gita::461.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses a listener as 'sinless one,' explaining that he has taught two main paths of devotion: the contemplative path of wisdom followed by the thoughtful, and the active path of selfless action followed by the yogis.
vishnu_gita::461.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by choices, remember you can deepen your connection by learning deeply or by acting selflessly—both are valid.
vishnu_gita::461.insight: Recognize that steady devotion can arise either through clear understanding or through engaged action.

vishnu_gita::462.verse_sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भानप्कम्य साधकोऽश्नुते ।
न च सन्न्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::462.verse_hindi: कोई साधक कर्म का अनुष्ठान न करके नैष्कर्म्य अवस्था को प्राप्त नहीं कर सकता है एवं आसक्ति त्याग के बिना  केवल सन्न्यास कर्म त्याग से ही सिद्धि को प्राप्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::462.english_translation: No practitioner attains the state of non-action by not starting actions, nor does one achieve perfection merely by renouncing attachment through renunciation.
vishnu_gita::462.translation_literal: न (not) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / अनारम्भान् (not beginning) / अप् (negative particle) / कम्य (desired) / साधकः (practitioner) / अश्नुते (attains) । / न (not) / च (also) / सन्न्यास-एव (only by renunciation) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / समधिगच्छति (attains) ॥
vishnu_gita::462.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::462.essence: True freedom isn’t gained by avoiding action or mere renunciation alone.
vishnu_gita::462.simple_meaning: You cannot achieve a state of true non-action simply by avoiding all actions, nor by only renouncing attachments without effort.
vishnu_gita::462.simple_insight: Freedom requires more than just quitting actions or attachments; there’s a deeper practice involved.
vishnu_gita::462.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that simply not acting or giving up duties does not bring the true state of freedom. Nor does merely renouncing attachments without engaging in disciplined effort lead to perfection.
vishnu_gita::462.modern_relevance: You might stop reacting to situations or quit old habits, but real growth demands more than just stopping—it needs active inner work.
vishnu_gita::462.insight: It teaches you that true freedom requires disciplined engagement beyond mere avoidance or renunciation.

vishnu_gita::463.verse_sanskrit:
न हि कश्चित् क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत।
कार्यते ह्यवश: कर्मा सर्वै: प्रकृतिजैर्गुणै: ॥
vishnu_gita::463.verse_hindi: किसी भी अवस्था में क्षणमात्र भी कोई कर्म न करके नहीं ही रह सक्ता है, प्रकृतिजनित ( सत्त्वादि) सब गुण ही अवश करके कर्म कराते हैं।
vishnu_gita::463.english_translation: No one can remain without action even for a moment; all actions are inevitably caused by the qualities born of nature.
vishnu_gita::463.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / कश्चित् (anyone) / क्षणम् (moment) / अपि (even) / जातु (ever) / तिष्ठति (remains) / अकर्मकृत (without doing action) / कार्यते (is done) / हि (indeed) / अवशः (inevitably) / कर्मा (actions) / सर्वैः (all) / प्रकृतिजैः (born of nature) / गुणैः (qualities)
vishnu_gita::463.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::463.essence: Action is unavoidable because natural qualities constantly drive all doing.
vishnu_gita::463.simple_meaning: You cannot avoid acting even for a moment; your natural qualities compel you to act.
vishnu_gita::463.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing action is natural, not a failure or choice.
vishnu_gita::463.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that no one can ever completely stop acting because the qualities of nature constantly drive all actions. This reveals the inevitability of engagement with life’s tasks.
vishnu_gita::463.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or guilty for not doing enough, remember your nature is always prompting you to move and act.
vishnu_gita::463.insight: It shifts your perspective from resisting action to understanding it as a natural, continuous flow.

vishnu_gita::464.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन
इन्द्रियार्थान् विमुढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::464.verse_hindi: जो व्यक्ति कर्मेन्द्रियों को संयत करके मन में इन्द्रियों के सकल विषयों को स्मरण करता रहता है उस विमूढात्मा को कपटाचारी कहते हैं।
vishnu_gita::464.english_translation: One who controls the organs of action and constantly remembers the objects of the senses with the mind, but is deluded, is called a hypocrite.
vishnu_gita::464.translation_literal: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि (organs of action) / संयम्य (controlling) / य (who) / आस्ते (is) / मनसा (with mind) / स्मरन (remembering) / इन्द्रियार्थान् (objects of the senses) / विमुढात्मा (deluded soul) / मिथ्याचारः (hypocrite) / स (that one) / उच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::464.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::464.essence: Discipline of action without control of the mind is self-deception.
vishnu_gita::464.simple_meaning: Controlling your actions alone isn't enough; if your mind keeps craving sense objects, you remain confused and self-deceiving.
vishnu_gita::464.simple_insight: You can seem disciplined outwardly while being inwardly lost and confused.
vishnu_gita::464.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that merely restraining physical actions without mastering the mind's focus on sensory desires leads to hypocrisy and confusion. True discipline requires both body and mind to be aligned.
vishnu_gita::464.modern_relevance: You may follow rules and routines perfectly but still feel unsettled if your mind chases distractions and cravings.
vishnu_gita::464.insight: It shifts your focus from external control to inner clarity and mindful presence.

vishnu_gita::465.verse_sanskrit:
यस्त्विान्द्रयाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽमराः ।
कम्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगममक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::465.verse_hindi: किन्तु हे देवतागण! जो मन द्वारा इन्द्रियों को संयत करके कर्मेन्द्रियों से कर्मयोग का अनुष्ठान करता है फल कामनाहीन वह व्यक्ति विशिष्ट है अर्थात् प्रशंसायोग्य है
vishnu_gita::465.english_translation: But those immortals who control their senses with the mind and perform the yoga of action without craving the results are truly distinguished.
vishnu_gita::465.translation_literal: यत् (who) त्वि-इन्द्रयाणि (the senses) मनसा (with mind) नियम्यारभते (control/bind) अमराः (immortals) । कम्मेन्द्रियैः (with action-senses) कर्मयोगम् (yoga of action) अमक्तः (without desire) स (that) विशिष्यते (is distinguished) ॥
vishnu_gita::465.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::465.essence: Acting with controlled senses and no craving for results sets you apart.
vishnu_gita::465.simple_meaning: You become special when you control your senses with your mind and act without wanting the outcome.
vishnu_gita::465.simple_insight: There's strength and respect in acting calmly, free from craving or attachment to results.
vishnu_gita::465.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses celestial beings, teaching that those who manage their senses through the mind and engage in action without desire for its fruits are truly admirable and set apart from others.
vishnu_gita::465.modern_relevance: You stay focused in a noisy, distracting world, doing your work without obsessing over praise or reward.
vishnu_gita::465.insight: It teaches you to focus your mind on controlling impulses and to perform your duties without attachment to outcomes.

vishnu_gita::466.verse_sanskrit:
नियतं क्रियतां कर्म कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
शरीरयात्राऽपि च वो न प्रसिद्धयेदकर्मणाम् ॥
vishnu_gita::466.verse_hindi: आप लोग अवश्य कर्तव्य कर्म करो क्योंकि कर्म न करने से कर्म करना श्रेष्ट है। कर्मों का, त्याग करने से आप लोगों का शरीर यात्रा निर्वाह भी नहीं होगा
vishnu_gita::466.english_translation: You must perform your prescribed duties, for action is better than inaction; without action, even bodily survival is not possible.
vishnu_gita::466.translation_literal: नियतं (prescribed) / क्रियतां (should be done) / कर्म (action) / कर्म (action) / ज्यायः (better) / हि (indeed) / अकर्मणः (than inaction) / शरीरयात्रा (bodily journey) / अपि (also) / च (and) / वः (your) / न (not) / प्रसिद्धयेत् (sustains) / अकर्मणाम् (of those who do not act)
vishnu_gita::466.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::466.essence: Doing your duty is necessary; inaction endangers your very existence.
vishnu_gita::466.simple_meaning: You should always do your prescribed duties because taking no action is worse; without action, even your body cannot be maintained.
vishnu_gita::466.simple_insight: You feel the importance of doing your part to keep your life and responsibilities steady.
vishnu_gita::466.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu instructs that every person must perform their rightful duties. Avoiding action is harmful because it threatens not only progress but also the very survival of the body during life’s journey.
vishnu_gita::466.modern_relevance: You face a day when avoiding tasks seems easier, but skipping them risks your wellbeing and progress.
vishnu_gita::466.insight: It teaches you to recognize that fulfilling your responsibilities is essential for sustaining your life and growth.

vishnu_gita::467.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात् कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कम्मबन्धनः ।
तदर्थ कर्म देवौघाः : मुक्तसंङ्गा विधत्त भोः ॥
vishnu_gita::467.verse_hindi: हे देवता गण ! यज्ञार्थ कर्मों के अतिरिक्त कर्म करने पर इस लोक में कर्म बन्धन होता है अतएव यज्ञके लक्ष्य से निष्काम होकर कर्मों को करो
vishnu_gita::467.english_translation: O divine beings! Actions done for any purpose other than the sacred offering bind one to the cycle of karma; therefore, act selflessly with the goal of the offering.
vishnu_gita::467.translation_literal: यज्ञार्थात् (for the purpose of sacred offering) कर्मणोऽन्यत्र (actions otherwise) लोकोऽयं (this world) कम्मबन्धनः (is karma bondage) । तदर्थ (for that purpose) कर्म (actions) देवौघाः (are divine vehicles) : मुक्तसंङ्गा (free from attachment) विधत्त (establish) भोः (O!) ॥
vishnu_gita::467.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::467.essence: Actions aimed at personal gain bind you; selfless action frees you.
vishnu_gita::467.simple_meaning: Only actions done selfishly bind you to consequences; acting without craving for results frees you.
vishnu_gita::467.simple_insight: You can find freedom by focusing on the purpose, not on rewards or consequences.
vishnu_gita::467.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that actions done for personal gain cause bondage in the cycle of reactions. Actions performed as offerings to the divine, without craving, are vehicles of freedom. This teaching guides how to act without being trapped by karma.
vishnu_gita::467.modern_relevance: You put time and energy into tasks beyond your main goals; knowing to focus on purpose helps avoid burnout and regret.
vishnu_gita::467.insight: Shift your focus from personal results to the value of your actions themselves, dissolving attachment.

vishnu_gita::468.verse_sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च साधकः ।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्य न विद्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::468.verse_hindi: किन्तु जो साधक आत्मा में ही रत है, आत्मा में ही तृप्त है एवं आत्मा में ही सन्तुष्ट रहता है उसके लिये कुछ भी कर्त्तव्य नहीं है
vishnu_gita::468.english_translation: But the practitioner who delights in the true self, is fulfilled in the true self, and content in the true self has no further duties to perform.
vishnu_gita::468.translation_literal: यत् (who) / त्व् (indeed) / आत्मरतिरेव (delights only in the true self) / स्यात् (is) / आत्मतृप्तश्च (and fulfilled in the true self) / साधकः (the practitioner) / आत्मन्येव (in the true self alone) / च (and) / सन्तुष्टः (content) / तस्य (for him) / कार्य (duty) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists).
vishnu_gita::468.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::468.essence: Complete inner contentment removes the need for any further action or duty.
vishnu_gita::468.simple_meaning: When you find full delight, fulfillment, and contentment in your true self, you have no further obligations to fulfill.
vishnu_gita::468.simple_insight: There is peace in realizing you need not chase anything beyond your own inner fulfillment.
vishnu_gita::468.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a practitioner who is fully satisfied in the true self and finds joy within transcends all external duties. This marks the culmination of spiritual practice where all action and obligation dissolve.
vishnu_gita::468.modern_relevance: After finishing a long journey of self-discovery, you feel calm inside and realize there’s nothing more you must prove or do.
vishnu_gita::468.insight: It shifts your focus from external achievement to inner fulfillment as the true measure of completion.

vishnu_gita::469.verse_sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाऽकृतेनेह कश्चन ।
नचास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
vishnu_gita::469.verse_hindi: इस लोक में किये हुए कर्मद्वारा उसको पुण्य भी नहीं होता है और न करने से कोई पाय भी नहीं होता है एवं सकल भूतों में स्थित ऐहिक या पारत्रिक कोई भी विषय उसके लिये आश्रयनीय नहीं है
vishnu_gita::469.english_translation: In this world, no merit comes from doing or not doing, and no worldly or other support exists for it among all beings.
vishnu_gita::469.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) तस्य (his) कृतेन (by doing) अर्थः (gain) न (not) अक्रतेन (by not doing) इह (here) कश्चन (anyone) न (nor) च (and) अस्य (his) सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) कश्चिद् (any) अर्थव्यपाश्रयः (support for gain) ।
vishnu_gita::469.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::469.essence: Neither doing nor not doing guarantees merit or support in this world.
vishnu_gita::469.simple_meaning: Neither doing something nor avoiding it brings true reward or lasting support in this world or among beings.
vishnu_gita::469.simple_insight: You can feel freed knowing that merit isn’t tied to your actions or inactions.
vishnu_gita::469.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that neither performing actions nor refraining from them leads to real merit or lasting benefit. Among all beings and worldly matters, no reliable support exists for such outcomes. This teaching uproots attachment to results.
vishnu_gita::469.modern_relevance: You might feel pressured to constantly do or avoid things to earn approval, but realizing no action alone guarantees reward can ease that burden.
vishnu_gita::469.insight: It shifts your focus from expecting rewards to acting without craving outcomes, freeing your motivation.

vishnu_gita::470.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तैः सततं काय्य कर्म विधीयताम् ।
असक्ताः कर्म कुर्वन्तो लभन्ते पूरुषं परम्  ॥
vishnu_gita::470.verse_hindi: अत: आपलोग फलासक्ति शून्य होकर सर्वदा आवश्यक कर्तव्य कर्मों के अनुसार अनुष्ठान करो क्योंकि अनासक्त होकर कर्म करने से साधक मोक्ष को प्राप्त होते हैं।
vishnu_gita::470.english_translation: Therefore, always perform your necessary duties with no attachment, for those who act without attachment attain the supreme being.
vishnu_gita::470.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) असक्तैः (without attachment) सततं (always) काय्य (body) कर्म (action) विधीयताम् (should be performed) । असक्ताः (without attachment) कर्म (action) कुर्वन्तः (doing) लभन्ते (attain) पूरुषं (the supreme being) परम् (highest) ॥
vishnu_gita::470.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::470.essence: You can act fully without attachment and still reach the highest goal.
vishnu_gita::470.simple_meaning: You should always perform your necessary duties without attachment to the results. Acting without craving leads to the highest attainment.
vishnu_gita::470.simple_insight: You can find freedom by focusing on your action, not on its outcome.
vishnu_gita::470.detailed_meaning: In a crucial teaching, Vishnu instructs that one must consistently perform their bodily duties without attachment to the results. This teaching comes as guidance to act rightly while freeing oneself from the bondage of craving outcomes.
vishnu_gita::470.modern_relevance: You completed a task and wonder if it will be recognized. Freedom comes by doing your best without needing approval.
vishnu_gita::470.insight: Shift your focus from outcomes to the actions you can control, freeing your effort from expectation.

vishnu_gita::471.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धि मास्थिता साधका: सुरा: ! ।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि पश्यन्तः कर्तुमर्हथ ॥
vishnu_gita::471.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! साधकगण कर्म के द्वारा ही संसिद्धि अर्थात ज्ञान प्राप्त करते हैं। सब लोगों को अपने अपने धर्म में प्रवर्तित करने के विषय का लक्ष्य रखकर भी कर्म करना उचित है।
vishnu_gita::471.english_translation: O radiant beings! Practitioners achieve perfection through action alone. Seeing the goal as the welfare of the world, they should act accordingly.
vishnu_gita::471.translation_literal: कर्मणैव (by action alone) हि (indeed) संसिद्धि (perfection) मास्थिता (achieved) साधका: (practitioners) सुरा: (radiant beings) ! / लोकसंग्रहमेवापि (even the welfare of the world) पश्यन्तः (seeing) कर्तुमर्हथ (should act)
vishnu_gita::471.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::471.essence: True mastery comes from acting with the welfare of all as your aim.
vishnu_gita::471.simple_meaning: True progress comes through committed action focused on the welfare of all, not by inaction or selfishness.
vishnu_gita::471.simple_insight: You gain confidence knowing your efforts serve a larger purpose beyond yourself.
vishnu_gita::471.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings and practitioners, urging them that only through dedicated action can they attain true perfection. Acting with the goal of benefiting the whole world is the proper focus for their efforts.
vishnu_gita::471.modern_relevance: You put your heart into a project that helps others, feeling motivated because your work supports more than just your own success.
vishnu_gita::471.insight: It teaches you to focus your energy on actions that benefit the greater good, making your efforts meaningful and complete.

vishnu_gita::472.verse_sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरः खलु।
म यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्त्तते ॥
vishnu_gita::472.verse_hindi: क्योंकि श्रेष्ठ व्यक्ति जो कर्मा करते हैं अन्यान्य लोग भी  वही कर्म करते हैं, वह जिसको कर्तव्य समझते हैं उसी का अनुवर्तन अन्य लोग करते हैं
vishnu_gita::472.english_translation: Whatever actions a great person performs, others follow that example; whatever standard they set, the world adheres to it.
vishnu_gita::472.translation_literal: यद्यत् (whatever) आचरति (performs) श्रेष्ठः (great person) तत् (that) एव (indeed) अन्यः (others) खलु (certainly)। म (whatever) यत् (that) प्रमाणम् (standard) कुरुते (does) लोकः (people) तत् (that) अनु वर्तते (follow)॥
vishnu_gita::472.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::472.essence: Your conduct becomes the standard others naturally follow.
vishnu_gita::472.simple_meaning: When someone acts with integrity and excellence, others naturally imitate their behavior and follow their example.
vishnu_gita::472.simple_insight: You hold quiet power every time you choose what to do — others notice and reflect it.
vishnu_gita::472.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person who acts with higher standards influences society; Arjuna learns that his duty and conduct affect the whole world around him.
vishnu_gita::472.modern_relevance: In your team or family, your way of handling challenges quietly shapes how others respond and behave.
vishnu_gita::472.insight: Recognize your role as a model; your choices ripple beyond your immediate actions.

vishnu_gita::473.verse_sanskrit:
देवाः! मेऽस्ति न कर्त्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन !
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
vishnu_gita::473.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! मेरा कर्तव्य कुछ नहीं है क्योंकि त्रिलोकी में मेरे लिये अप्राप्त वा प्राप्तव्य कुछ नहीं है तथापि मैं कर्म में प्रवृत्त ही रहता हूँ
vishnu_gita::473.english_translation: O radiant beings! I have no duty because there is nothing left to gain or lose in the three worlds, yet I remain engaged in action.
vishnu_gita::473.translation_literal: देवाः (divine beings) ! मेऽस्ति (for me is) न (not) कर्त्तव्यं (duty) त्रिषु (in three) लोकेषु (worlds) किञ्चन (anything) ! न (not) अनवाप्तम् (unattained) अवाप्तव्यं (to be attained) वर्त्त (exists) एव (indeed) च (also) कर्मणि (in action) ॥
vishnu_gita::473.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::473.essence: You can act fully even when nothing is left to gain or lose.
vishnu_gita::473.simple_meaning: There is nothing left for the divine to gain or lose in all worlds, so no duty binds him, yet he continues to act.
vishnu_gita::473.simple_insight: You can act freely without being bound by outcomes or duties.
vishnu_gita::473.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the radiant beings, explaining that in the vast cosmos there is nothing more for him to gain or lose. Despite this freedom from obligation, he remains active, showing action beyond attachment or duty.
vishnu_gita::473.modern_relevance: You might feel stuck waiting for rewards or clear purpose, but this shows you can keep acting even when nothing seems owed or expected.
vishnu_gita::473.insight: It teaches you to act from presence and commitment, not from expectation or obligation.

vishnu_gita::474.verse_sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्लयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
मम वानुवर्त्तन्ते प्राणिनः सर्वशोऽमराः ॥
vishnu_gita::474.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! कभी यदि मैं आलस्यरहित होकर कर्मानुष्ठान न करूँ तो निश्चय ही जीवधारी मेरे मार्ग सभी प्रकार से अनुसरण करेंगे
vishnu_gita::474.english_translation: O divine beings! If I were ever to cease acting without laziness, all living beings would surely follow my path in every way.
vishnu_gita::474.translation_literal: यदि (if) हि (indeed) अहं (I) न (not) वर्लयं (cease) जातु (ever) कर्मणि (in action) अतन्द्रितः (without laziness)। मम (my) वानु (followers) वर्त्तन्ते (are) प्राणिनः (living beings) सर्वशः (completely) अमराः (immortal) ॥
vishnu_gita::474.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::474.essence: Consistent, earnest action inspires all beings to follow naturally.
vishnu_gita::474.simple_meaning: If you perform your duties without laziness or delay, others will naturally follow your example.
vishnu_gita::474.simple_insight: You feel the quiet power of consistent effort that draws others to follow.
vishnu_gita::474.detailed_meaning: Vishnu tells divine beings that if he were ever to stop acting with full commitment, all living beings would imitate him, highlighting the power of devoted action as a guiding force.
vishnu_gita::474.modern_relevance: You start a project without procrastination, and soon colleagues adopt your focused approach without being told.
vishnu_gita::474.insight: It teaches you that steadfast, energetic action naturally influences others to follow your path.

vishnu_gita::475.verse_sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुटयाँ कर्म चेदहम् ।
सङ्करस्य च कर्त्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
vishnu_gita::475.verse_hindi: यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ तो यह सभी लोग धर्म का लोप होने से विनष्ट हो जायँगे और मैं वर्णसंकर का कर्ता हो जाऊँगा, इस प्रकार मैं ही इन प्रजाओ के नाश का कारण बनूँगा
vishnu_gita::475.english_translation: If I do not act, all these people will perish due to the loss of dharma, and I will become the cause of their destruction through mixing of classes.
vishnu_gita::475.translation_literal: उत्सीदेयुः (would cease) इमे (these) लोका (people) न (not) कुटयाँ (mixing of classes) कर्म (action) च (and) अहम् (I) सङ्करस्य (of mixing) च (also) कर्त्ता (doer) स्याम् (would become) उपहन्याम् (destruction) इमाः (these) प्रजाः (people)
vishnu_gita::475.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::475.essence: Avoiding your duty causes harm and makes you responsible for destruction.
vishnu_gita::475.simple_meaning: You must act to protect the social order and prevent chaos; inaction will cause harm to others and yourself.
vishnu_gita::475.simple_insight: You feel the weight of responsibility when inaction risks harm beyond yourself.
vishnu_gita::475.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that if he refrains from action, the world will suffer the loss of dharma and social order. His inaction would cause mixing of classes and destruction, making him responsible for widespread ruin.
vishnu_gita::475.modern_relevance: You hesitate to step up, fearing failure, but avoiding action can cause bigger problems for those who depend on you.
vishnu_gita::475.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your choices affect not just you but the broader community.

vishnu_gita::476.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! कर्म में आसक्त अज्ञानी लोग जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं उसी प्रकार कर्म में अनासक्त ज्ञानी लोग भी लोगो को स्वधर्म में प्रवर्तित करने के लिये इच्छुक होकर कर्म करते हैं।
vishnu_gita::476.english_translation: Just as ignorant people act attached to their actions, the wise act without attachment but still perform actions to uphold the world's order.
vishnu_gita::476.translation_literal: सक्त्ता: (attached) कर्मण्यविद्वांसो (to actions, the wise) यथा (just as) कुर्वन्ति (they do) निर्जरा: (without decay/attachment) । (punctuation) कुर्याद् (should do) विध्वां: (the wise) तथा (thus) असक्त: (unattached) चिकीर्षु: (desiring) लोकसंग्रहम् (the world's welfare) ॥
vishnu_gita::476.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::476.essence: You can act fully without attachment while still desiring the world's welfare.
vishnu_gita::476.simple_meaning: You can act without being attached to your actions, yet still care deeply about supporting others and the world.
vishnu_gita::476.simple_insight: There’s freedom in acting without craving while still wanting to do good for others.
vishnu_gita::476.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu explains how the wise differ from the ignorant—not in action, but in attachment. Both act, but the wise do so without clinging, motivated by the welfare of all.
vishnu_gita::476.modern_relevance: You finish a project without obsessing over praise, yet still hope it makes a difference for your team.
vishnu_gita::476.insight: It shifts your focus from personal gain to selfless contribution while maintaining full engagement.

vishnu_gita::477.verse_sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् ।
योजयेत् सर्वकम्माणि विद्वान युक्तः समाचरन्  ॥
vishnu_gita::477.verse_hindi: कर्मासक्त अज्ञ लोगों का बुद्धिभेद नहीं करना चाहिये, प्रत्युतन्तु ब्रह्मज्ञ पण्डित व्यक्ति को स्वयं सब कर्मों का अनुष्ठान करके अज्ञ लोगों को कर्म में नियुक्त करना चाहिये
vishnu_gita::477.english_translation: A wise person devoted to the divine should not confuse the ignorant attached to action but engage in all deeds themselves and involve the ignorant in action.
vishnu_gita::477.translation_literal: न (not) / बुद्धि (intellect) / भेदं (division, confusion) / जनयेत् (should create) / अजज्ञानाम् (of the ignorant) / कर्मसङ्गिनाम् (attached to action) / योजयेत् (should join) / सर्वकम्माणि (all actions) / विद्वान् (the wise) / युक्तः (united, engaged) / समाचरन् (performing properly)
vishnu_gita::477.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::477.essence: Wise people act fully and guide the attached without creating confusion.
vishnu_gita::477.simple_meaning: You should not confuse people attached to actions because of ignorance. Instead, a wise person acts fully and guides others by example.
vishnu_gita::477.simple_insight: There's strength in steady example rather than confusing others with complicated ideas.
vishnu_gita::477.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when people are attached to their actions out of ignorance, it's unhelpful to create confusion. Instead, a wise person should engage in all duties themselves and gently involve others through their own example.
vishnu_gita::477.modern_relevance: You see coworkers overwhelmed and stuck in busywork; instead of arguing, you focus on doing your work well and help them learn by your steady example.
vishnu_gita::477.insight: It teaches you to avoid confusing others and instead show the way through your own engaged action.

vishnu_gita::478.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कम्माणि सर्वशः।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::478.verse_hindi: सब कर्म प्रकृति के गुणों द्वारा सर्वतोभावेन निष्पादित होते हैं किन्तु अहङ्कार से विमूढ चित्त व्यक्ति "मैं कर्ता हूँ, ऐसा समझता है
vishnu_gita::478.english_translation: All actions arise from the qualities of the natural world everywhere, but the confused mind, deluded by the sense of separate self, thinks 'I am the doer.'
vishnu_gita::478.translation_literal: प्रकृतेः (of nature) क्रियमाणानि (being done) गुणैः (by qualities) कम्माणि (actions) सर्वशः (everywhere) । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा (mind deluded by ego) कर्ता (doer) अहम् (I) इति (thus) मन्यते (thinks) ॥
vishnu_gita::478.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::478.essence: All actions arise naturally, but the ego falsely claims sole authorship.
vishnu_gita::478.simple_meaning: All actions happen because of nature's qualities, but the confused mind wrongly believes it alone causes them.
vishnu_gita::478.simple_insight: It's freeing to see that you are not the sole doer behind every action.
vishnu_gita::478.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that all activities arise from the three qualities of the natural world (sattva, rajas, tamas). Yet, the mind, clouded by ego (ahankara), mistakenly claims personal authorship of these actions, causing confusion.
vishnu_gita::478.modern_relevance: When your plans go wrong, you may blame yourself, but many forces beyond your control shape outcomes.
vishnu_gita::478.insight: Shift from identifying as the sole doer to witnessing actions as arising naturally; this eases pressure and blame.

vishnu_gita::479.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु सुपर्वाणः ! गुणकर्मविभागयोः।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न मज्जते ॥
vishnu_gita::479.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे देवतागण ! गुण और कर्मों के विभाग के तत्व को जानने वाला व्यक्ति “इन्द्रियाँ विषयों में प्रवृत्त होती हैं। ऐसा समझकर कर्तापन का अभिमान नहीं करता है
vishnu_gita::479.english_translation: But, O divine beings! One who knows the essence of qualities and actions understands that qualities act within qualities and does not fall into the pride of doership.
vishnu_gita::479.translation_literal: तत्त्ववित्तु (essence-knower) / सुपर्वाणः (O supreme beings) / गुणकर्मविभागयोः (of qualities and actions division) / गुणा (qualities) / गुणेषु (within qualities) / वर्तन्त (exist) / इति (thus) / मत्वा (considering) / न (not) / मज्जते (drowns/falls).
vishnu_gita::479.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::479.essence: Qualities act within qualities; knowing this dissolves the pride of doership.
vishnu_gita::479.simple_meaning: Understanding that qualities operate within other qualities helps you avoid getting caught in the illusion of being the doer.
vishnu_gita::479.simple_insight: You can feel relieved that your sense of control does not define your true self.
vishnu_gita::479.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that qualities (gunas) act within themselves and within actions, so one who understands this does not get attached to the false ego of doership during the battle.
vishnu_gita::479.modern_relevance: You realize that your personality traits and habits influence your actions deeply, so blaming yourself or others for outcomes feels less urgent.
vishnu_gita::479.insight: It teaches you to see actions as expressions of qualities, not as something you personally own or control fully.

vishnu_gita::480.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।
नानकृत्स्नाविदो मन्दान् कृत्स्नविन विचालयेत् ॥
vishnu_gita::480.verse_hindi: प्रकृति के सत्त्वादि त्रिगुणों से मोहित होकर जो इन्द्रियों में और इन्द्रियों के कार्यों में आसक्त होते हैं, सर्वज्ञ व्यक्ति को उन मन्दमति अज्ञ लोगों को विचलित नहीं करना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::480.english_translation: Those deluded by the three qualities of nature become attached to the senses and their actions; the wise should not disturb these dull-minded ones.
vishnu_gita::480.translation_literal: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः (by nature’s qualities deluded) / सज्जन्ते (are attached) / गुणकर्मसु (to qualities and actions) / नानकृत्स्नाविदो (the omniscient) / मन्दान् (dull-minded) / कृत्स्नविन (not completely) / विचालयेत् (should disturb)
vishnu_gita::480.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::480.essence: The wise hold steady without disturbing those confused by nature’s qualities.
vishnu_gita::480.simple_meaning: People attached to their senses and actions are confused by nature’s qualities. The wise shouldn’t disturb them.
vishnu_gita::480.simple_insight: There’s calm in not forcing clarity on those still lost in their distractions.
vishnu_gita::480.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that many are caught in attachment to the senses and their activities because of nature’s three qualities. The fully wise recognize this confusion and avoid disturbing those not yet ready to see clearly.
vishnu_gita::480.modern_relevance: You notice friends stuck in habits and distractions. Trying to shake them often backfires; patience is wiser.
vishnu_gita::480.insight: It teaches you to hold compassion and restraint when others remain unaware and attached.

vishnu_gita::481.verse_sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि सन्न्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा ।
निराशिषो निर्ममाश्च यतवं विगतज्वराः ॥
vishnu_gita::481.verse_hindi: मुझमें समस्त कर्म अर्पण करके आत्मा में चित्त को रखते हुए निष्काम और ममता शून्य होकर शोक त्यागपूर्वक कर्म करना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::481.english_translation: By dedicating all your actions to me with a spiritual mind, acting without desire or attachment, and free from sorrow, you should perform your duties.
vishnu_gita::481.translation_literal: मयि (in me) / सर्वाणि (all) / कर्माणि (actions) / सन्न्यस्य (dedicating) / अध्यात्मचेतसा (with spiritual mind) / निराशिषः (without desire) / निर्ममाश्च (without attachment) / यतवं (should perform) / विगतज्वराः (free from sorrow)
vishnu_gita::481.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::481.essence: You can fully act while letting go of desire and sorrow.
vishnu_gita::481.simple_meaning: You should dedicate all your actions to the divine with a focused mind, acting without desire, attachment, or sorrow.
vishnu_gita::481.simple_insight: Relief comes when you act fully but let go of wanting and grieving over results.
vishnu_gita::481.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs to give all actions to the divine, maintaining spiritual focus. Acting without craving or attachment, and free from sorrow, supports steady and pure action, vital for Arjuna as he faces his moral crisis.
vishnu_gita::481.modern_relevance: You finish a hard task and release the urge to control what happens next, freeing yourself from stress and disappointment.
vishnu_gita::481.insight: Shift your focus from outcomes to wholehearted action, freeing yourself from emotional burdens.

vishnu_gita::482.verse_sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति साधकाः ।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
vishnu_gita::482.verse_hindi: जो साधक मेरे इस सिद्धान्त के अनुसार श्रद्धावान् और दोषदृष्टि विहीन होते हुए कर्मों को नित्य करते रहते हैं वे कर्म करनेवाले होने पर भी कर्मों से मुक्त रहते हैं।
vishnu_gita::482.english_translation: Those practitioners who constantly act with trust in my teaching and without envy are freed from the bondage of actions despite acting.
vishnu_gita::482.translation_literal: ये (these) / मे (my) / मतम् (teaching) / इदं (this) / नित्यम् (constantly) / अनुतिष्ठन्ति (do not stop) / साधकाः (practitioners) / श्रद्धावन्तः (trusting) / अनसूयन्तः (without envy) / मुच्यन्ते (are freed) / तेऽपि (they also) / कर्मभिः (by actions)
vishnu_gita::482.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::482.essence: You can act faithfully without envy and still be free from your actions' bondage.
vishnu_gita::482.simple_meaning: You can keep doing your actions regularly with trust and without jealousy, and still be free from being tied down by those actions.
vishnu_gita::482.simple_insight: There’s peace in knowing your faithful actions don’t trap you, even while you keep acting.
vishnu_gita::482.detailed_meaning: Vishnu tells seekers that those who consistently follow his teaching with trust and without jealousy remain free from the binding effects of their actions, even as they act. This teaches how to live actively without becoming trapped by consequences.
vishnu_gita::482.modern_relevance: You keep working hard and honestly without comparing or resenting others, freeing yourself from stress over outcomes.
vishnu_gita::482.insight: It teaches you to act with trust and without envy, which liberates your mind from attachment to results.

vishnu_gita::483.verse_sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्वित्त नष्टानचेतसः ॥
vishnu_gita::483.verse_hindi: किन्तु जो केवल दोष. दर्शन करते हुए मेरे इस सिद्धान्त के अनुसार कर्मानुष्ठान नहीं करते हैं उन विवेकहीनों को सर्वज्ञान विमूढ़ और नष्ट जानना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::483.english_translation: But those who only criticize and do not follow my teaching are bewildered and lost in false knowledge.
vishnu_gita::483.translation_literal: ये (those who) त्वेतद्-अभ्यसूयन्तः (criticize this) न (not) अनुतिष्ठन्ति (stand firm) मे (my) मतम् (teaching) । सर्वज्ञान-विमूढान् (completely knowledge-confused) तान् (them) विद्धि (know) नष्टान् (lost) अचेतसः (mindless)
vishnu_gita::483.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::483.essence: Criticism without practice leads to confusion and lost understanding.
vishnu_gita::483.simple_meaning: People who just criticize this teaching and don't practice it are confused and lost in false knowledge.
vishnu_gita::483.simple_insight: There is clarity and relief when you move from judgment to genuine practice.
vishnu_gita::483.detailed_meaning: Vishnu warns that those who only find faults in his teaching and refuse to apply it become confused and lose clear understanding, stuck in ignorance despite apparent knowledge.
vishnu_gita::483.modern_relevance: You might find yourself endlessly doubting advice or wisdom but never applying it, leaving you frustrated and stuck.
vishnu_gita::483.insight: It teaches you to move beyond criticism and engage sincerely with what guides growth.

vishnu_gita::484.verse_sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्शानवानपि ।
प्रकृति यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::484.verse_hindi: ज्ञानवान् भी अपनी प्रकृति के अनुसार कर्म करता है और प्राणि मात्र ही अपनी प्रकृति का अनुसरण करते हैं अतः इन्द्रियों का निग्रह क्या करेगा?
vishnu_gita::484.english_translation: A wise person acts according to their nature, and all beings follow their nature; what can controlling the senses accomplish?
vishnu_gita::484.translation_literal: सदृशं (similar) / चेष्टते (acts) / स्वस्याः (of one's own) / प्रकृतेः (nature) / शानवानपि (even the wise) / प्रकृति (nature) / यान्ति (go/follow) / भूतानि (beings) / निग्रहः (control) / किं (what) / करिष्यति (will do)
vishnu_gita::484.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::484.essence: Your natural tendencies shape your actions more than trying to control your senses.
vishnu_gita::484.simple_meaning: Everyone acts according to their own nature. Even wise people do this, so simply trying to control your senses won't stop natural behaviors.
vishnu_gita::484.simple_insight: There is a gentle acceptance in realizing your true nature shapes your actions more than effortful control.
vishnu_gita::484.detailed_meaning: In a teaching moment, Vishnu explains that even the wise act according to their natural tendencies. Since all beings follow their nature, merely trying to restrain the senses is ineffective in changing the course of action.
vishnu_gita::484.modern_relevance: You try to force yourself to resist old habits, but deep down your natural tendencies keep pulling you back.
vishnu_gita::484.insight: Shift focus from strict control of impulses to understanding and aligning with your true nature for lasting change.

vishnu_gita::485.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियम्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
vishnu_gita::485.verse_hindi: प्रत्येक इन्द्रिय का अपने अपने अनुकूल विषय में अनुराग और प्रतिकूल विषय में द्वेष अवश्य होता है अतएव इन दोनों के वश में नहीं होना चाहिये क्योंकि ये दोनों मुमुक्ष के प्रतिपक्षी हैं
vishnu_gita::485.english_translation: Every sense has attachment for its own objects and aversion for the opposite; one should not be controlled by either because they oppose the seeker of freedom.
vishnu_gita::485.translation_literal: इन्द्रियम् (sense) इन्द्रियस्य (of the sense) अर्थे (object) राग (attachment) द्वेषौ (aversion) व्यवस्थितौ (established) तयोः (of these two) न (not) वशम् (control) आगच्छेत् (should come) तौ (these two) हि (indeed) अस्य (of this one) परिपन्थिनौ (enemies)
vishnu_gita::485.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::485.essence: Refusing to be controlled by attraction or aversion frees your movement and choice.
vishnu_gita::485.simple_meaning: Your senses naturally attract you to some things and repel you from others, but you shouldn’t let this pull you around because it stops your progress.
vishnu_gita::485.simple_insight: There’s freedom in stepping back from your cravings and dislikes.
vishnu_gita::485.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that each sense draws you toward what it likes and away from what it dislikes. For someone seeking freedom, being controlled by these pulls blocks the path, so they must learn to not be ruled by attachment or aversion.
vishnu_gita::485.modern_relevance: You find yourself wanting certain notifications and avoiding others, but letting these cravings and avoidances dictate your mood keeps you stuck.
vishnu_gita::485.insight: It teaches you to notice your attractions and aversions without letting them decide your actions or peace.

vishnu_gita::486.verse_sanskrit:
श्रेयान स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
vishnu_gita::486.verse_hindi: सुचारुरूप से अनुष्ठित परधर्म की अपेक्षा दोषसहित स्वधर्म श्रेष्ठ है, अपने धर्म में स्थित रहते हुए मरना भी अच्छा है किन्तु परधर्म भयोत्पादक है।
vishnu_gita::486.english_translation: Performing your own duty, even if imperfect, is better than performing another's duty perfectly; dying in your own duty is preferable, while another's duty causes fear.
vishnu_gita::486.translation_literal: श्रेयान (better) / स्वधर्मो (own duty) / विगुणः (imperfect) / परधर्मात् (than another's duty) / स्वनुष्ठितात् (performed) । / स्वधर्मे (in own duty) / निधनं (death) / श्रेयः (better) / परधर्मो (another's duty) / भयावहः (fearful) ॥
vishnu_gita::486.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::486.essence: Following your own imperfect duty is safer and better than perfectly doing another’s.
vishnu_gita::486.simple_meaning: It’s better to follow your own duty, even if not perfectly, than to perform another’s duty flawlessly. Staying true to your own role is safer and more honorable.
vishnu_gita::486.simple_insight: You can trust yourself and your path, even when it feels imperfect.
vishnu_gita::486.detailed_meaning: Vishnu advises that Arjuna should embrace his own role despite imperfections rather than imitate another’s duty perfectly. This teaching comes when Arjuna doubts fighting his kin, highlighting the importance of following one's true purpose.
vishnu_gita::486.modern_relevance: When you face pressure to do what others expect, remember it’s better to act on your own values even if imperfect.
vishnu_gita::486.insight: It teaches you to prioritize your authentic responsibilities over trying to be perfect in roles not meant for you.

vishnu_gita::487.verse_sanskrit:
न मां कम्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::487.verse_hindi: “मुझको सकल कर्म शासक्त नहीं कर सकते एवं कर्मफल में मेरी स्पृहा नहीं है" इस प्रकार जो मुझको जानता है वह कर्म में बद्ध नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::487.english_translation: "My actions do not bind me, nor do I desire their results. Whoever understands me this way is not bound by actions."
vishnu_gita::487.translation_literal: न (not) मां (me) कम्माणि (actions) लिम्पन्ति (bind) न (nor) मे (my) कर्मफले (fruits of actions) स्पृहा (desire) । इति (thus) मां (me) योऽभिजानाति (who knows) कर्मभिः (by actions) न (not) स (he) बध्यते (is bound) ॥
vishnu_gita::487.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::487.essence: You can act fully without being bound by your actions or their results.
vishnu_gita::487.simple_meaning: You do actions, but they do not trap you. You do not crave the results. Knowing this frees you from being bound by actions.
vishnu_gita::487.simple_insight: You can feel free even while doing your duties, without craving or aversion.
vishnu_gita::487.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains to Arjuna that even though he performs many actions, he remains free because he does not cling to their outcomes. This shifts the understanding of karma from bondage to liberation by detachment.
vishnu_gita::487.modern_relevance: You finish a demanding task but don’t obsess over the outcome or recognition. You stay steady, unshaken by success or failure.
vishnu_gita::487.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with the action or result to recognizing your freedom beyond them.

vishnu_gita::488.verse_sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।
तस्माद्विधत्त कम्मैव पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::488.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार जानकर पूर्वकालीन मुमुक्षुओं ने भी कर्म किया है अतः आपलोग भी पुरातन काल के मुमुक्षुओं द्वारा पूर्वकाल में किए हुए कर्म को ही करो
vishnu_gita::488.english_translation: Knowing this, seekers of freedom performed actions; therefore, you should perform actions like those done by earlier seekers.
vishnu_gita::488.translation_literal: एवं (thus) ज्ञात्वा (having known) कृतं (done) कर्म (action) पूर्वैः (by earlier) अपि (also) मुमुक्षुभिः (seekers of freedom) । तस्मात् (therefore) विधत्त (perform) कम्मैव (only action) पूर्वैः (by earlier) पूर्वतरं (earlier) कृतम् (done) ॥
vishnu_gita::488.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::488.essence: Following the actions of past seekers guides your own path toward freedom.
vishnu_gita::488.simple_meaning: Those who seek freedom have acted before you; following their example helps you act rightly now.
vishnu_gita::488.simple_insight: You’re not alone in seeking freedom; others have paved the way with their actions.
vishnu_gita::488.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs that seekers aiming for freedom have always acted within their abilities. You too should follow their example, performing your duties responsibly as they did in ancient times.
vishnu_gita::488.modern_relevance: You face a challenge that others have met before. Trust in their experience as a guide for your own efforts.
vishnu_gita::488.insight: Embracing the example of past seekers shifts your focus from uncertainty to confident action.

vishnu_gita::489.verse_sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्ममेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः।
तद्वः कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यथाशुभात् ॥
vishnu_gita::489.verse_hindi: कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है इस विषय में विवेकी लोग भी मोहित होते हैं अतएव जिसके जानने से आपलोग अशुभ अर्थात् कर्मासक्ति से मुक्त होगे मैं उस कर्म को कहता हूँ
vishnu_gita::489.english_translation: What is action and what is inaction, even the wise are confused about this; I will explain the action that, when known, frees you from harmful attachment.
vishnu_gita::489.translation_literal: किं (what) / कर्म (action) / किम्-अकर्म (what is inaction) / इति (thus) / कवयः (the wise) / अपि (also) / अत्र (here) / मोहिताः (are confused) / तद्वः (that) / कर्म (action) / प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will explain) / यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (knowing) / मोक्ष्यथ (you will be freed) / अशुभात् (from harm or unwholesome) ।
vishnu_gita::489.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::489.essence: Knowing which action frees you dissolves confusion about what truly counts as acting or not.
vishnu_gita::489.simple_meaning: Even wise people get confused about what counts as action and inaction. Knowing the right kind of action frees you from harmful attachments.
vishnu_gita::489.simple_insight: There’s relief in realizing not all action binds you; some actions set you free.
vishnu_gita::489.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu addresses Arjuna's confusion about what truly counts as action or inaction. Even wise people struggle with this distinction. Vishnu promises to explain the specific kind of action that when understood, liberates from harmful attachments and suffering.
vishnu_gita::489.modern_relevance: When you hesitate, unsure if acting or waiting is right, this helps you see which actions truly help you move beyond harmful patterns.
vishnu_gita::489.insight: It teaches you to distinguish binding actions from freeing ones, guiding your choices wisely.

vishnu_gita::490.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
vishnu_gita::490.verse_hindi: कर्म अर्थात् निष्काम कर्म का रहस्य भी जानने योग्य है, विकर्म अर्थात् सकाम कर्म का रहस्य भी जानने योग्य है और अकर्म अर्थात् कर्म भाव का भी रहस्य जानने योग्य है क्योंकि कर्म की गति अतिगहन है
vishnu_gita::490.english_translation: You must understand the mystery of action, the mystery of wrong action, and the mystery of inaction, because the path of action is profound.
vishnu_gita::490.translation_literal: कर्मणो (of action) हि (indeed) अपि (also) बोद्धव्यं (must be known) बोद्धव्यं (must be known) च (and) विकर्मणः (of wrong action) अकर्मणश्च (and of inaction also) बोद्धव्यं (must be known) गहना (profound) कर्मणः (of action) गतिः (the path)
vishnu_gita::490.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::490.essence: The mysteries of right action, wrong action, and inaction all must be understood—they shape your path deeply.
vishnu_gita::490.simple_meaning: You should understand three aspects: action done rightly, wrong action, and inaction, because the way of action is complex and deep.
vishnu_gita::490.simple_insight: There’s more to doing, not doing, and their effects than meets the eye—action’s nature is profound.
vishnu_gita::490.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to seekers that understanding only good action isn’t enough; one must also grasp wrong action and inaction. Each affects the cycle of cause and effect deeply, so grasping all three reveals the true nature of how actions shape life.
vishnu_gita::490.modern_relevance: You’re caught in choices: doing what’s right, what feels wrong, or doing nothing at all. Each choice carries hidden depth and consequences you might not see.
vishnu_gita::490.insight: It teaches you to explore not just your actions, but also your inactions and mistakes, seeing how all shape your journey.

vishnu_gita::491.verse_sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्माणि च कर्म यः।
स बुद्धिमान साधकेषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
vishnu_gita::491.verse_hindi: जो निष्काम कर्म में कर्म भाव देखता है और कर्म रहित अवस्था में जो कर्म का होना देखता है वह साधकों में बुद्धिमान है और वह सभी कर्म करते रहने पर भी मुझमें युक्त है
vishnu_gita::491.english_translation: The one who sees action in inaction and inaction in action is wise among practitioners and remains united with me while performing all actions.
vishnu_gita::491.translation_literal: कर्मण्यकर्म (in action, in inaction) / यः (who) / पश्येत (sees) / अकर्माणि (inactions) / च (and) / कर्म (action) / यः (who) / स (that one) / बुद्धिमान (wise) / साधकेषु (among practitioners) / स (that one) / युक्तः (united) / कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् (performing all actions)
vishnu_gita::491.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::491.essence: True wisdom is seeing action and inaction as intertwined without losing your inner balance.
vishnu_gita::491.simple_meaning: You are wise when you recognize that even in doing nothing there is action, and in doing something there can be stillness. Staying connected to your deeper self lets you act without losing balance.
vishnu_gita::491.simple_insight: You can feel steady and wise even when life pulls you in opposite ways.
vishnu_gita::491.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that true wisdom is seeing the paradox of life: sometimes doing nothing is itself an action, and sometimes acting can feel like doing nothing. This helps Arjuna understand how to be involved in the world while rooted in deeper awareness.
vishnu_gita::491.modern_relevance: When your mind races between tasks and moments of rest, you can learn to see both as part of your flow, not chaos or failure.
vishnu_gita::491.insight: It teaches you to hold steady awareness amid all activity, seeing rest and action as connected.

vishnu_gita::492.verse_sanskrit:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः।
जानानिदग्धकमणिं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥
vishnu_gita::492.verse_hindi: जिसके सब कर्म कामना और सङ्कल्प से रहित हैं ज्ञानीलोग उस ज्ञान अग्नि के द्वारा दग्ध्कर्मा व्यक्ति को पंडित कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::492.english_translation: One whose every action is free from desire and intention is called wise by those enlightened through the fire of knowledge.
vishnu_gita::492.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / सर्वे (all) / समारम्भाः (actions) / कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः (without desire and intention) / जानानि (by the wise) / दग्धकमणिं (burnt by knowledge's fire) / तम् (that) / आहुः (say) / पण्डितं (wise) / बुधाः (the wise)
vishnu_gita::492.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::492.essence: True wisdom is acting without desire or personal intention behind any action.
vishnu_gita::492.simple_meaning: You are wise when you do all your actions without wanting anything or planning outcomes.
vishnu_gita::492.simple_insight: There is peace in acting without craving or personal intentions behind your deeds.
vishnu_gita::492.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person whose every act is free from selfish desire and personal planning is recognized by the wise as truly knowledgeable, having been purified by the fire of understanding.
vishnu_gita::492.modern_relevance: You deliver your work fully without obsessing over praise or reward, feeling calm because your focus is on the task itself.
vishnu_gita::492.insight: It teaches you to shift focus from achieving results to performing actions for their own sake, clearing mental clutter.

vishnu_gita::493.verse_sanskrit:
त्यकत्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित् करोति सः ॥
vishnu_gita::493.verse_hindi: वह कर्म और कर्मफल पर आसक्तिरहित होकर नित्यानंद मे तृप्त और निरवलंबन होकर कर्म मे प्रवृत रहने पर भी कुछ भी नहीं करता है
vishnu_gita::493.english_translation: Abandoning attachment to the results of action, always content and independent, one engaged in action indeed does nothing at all.
vishnu_gita::493.translation_literal: त्यकत्वा (abandoning) कर्मफलासङ्गं (attachment to the fruits of action) नित्यतृप्तो (always content) निराश्रयः (without dependence) । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तः (engaged in action) अपि (even) नैव (indeed not) किञ्चित् (anything) करोति (does) सः (he)
vishnu_gita::493.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::493.essence: You can act fully without craving results and still remain untouched by outcomes.
vishnu_gita::493.simple_meaning: You can engage in your work without clinging to its results, staying content and independent inside. Even while acting, you remain as if doing nothing.
vishnu_gita::493.simple_insight: You can be fully active while feeling free from the pressure of results.
vishnu_gita::493.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person can perform their duties without attachment to outcomes. Even while active, they remain content and independent, untouched by success or failure. This frees the mind from anxiety and preserves inner peace.
vishnu_gita::493.modern_relevance: You give your best at work without obsessing over promotions or praise, feeling steady regardless of what happens next.
vishnu_gita::493.insight: It shifts your focus from seeking rewards to simply doing your part, freeing you from stress.

vishnu_gita::494.verse_sanskrit:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्व परिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्विषम् ॥
vishnu_gita::494.verse_hindi: जो शरीर के द्वारा केवल नाममात्र के लिये कर्म करता है वह निष्काम, यतचित्त आत्मा और त्यक्त सर्व परिग्रह होने के कारण पाप को प्राप्त नहीं होता है।
vishnu_gita::494.english_translation: One who acts through the body merely in name, with a disciplined mind and renouncing all attachments, does not incur wrongdoing.
vishnu_gita::494.translation_literal: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा (without desire, with disciplined mind, self) / त्यक्तसर्व (having abandoned all) / परिग्रहः (attachments) / शारीरं (body) / केवलं (only, merely) / कर्म (action) / कुर्वन् (doing) / आप्नोति (obtains) / किल्विषम् (wrongdoing)
vishnu_gita::494.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::494.essence: Acting without desire or attachment frees you from wrongdoing despite bodily action.
vishnu_gita::494.simple_meaning: You can perform actions through your body without desire, with a disciplined mind, and by giving up all attachments, thus avoiding wrongdoing.
vishnu_gita::494.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting without desire or attachment—no blame follows your effort.
vishnu_gita::494.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when someone acts bodily with a calm, disciplined mind and has renounced all possessions and attachments, their actions do not bring blame or negative consequences. This teaching comes during a moment of instruction on selfless action.
vishnu_gita::494.modern_relevance: You finish a task at work without obsessing over praise or reward, feeling clear and free despite others' opinions.
vishnu_gita::494.insight: It teaches you to focus on performing your duties without craving results or holding on to outcomes.

vishnu_gita::495.verse_sanskrit:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्राततिो विमत्सरः।
ममः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वाऽपि न निबध्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::495.verse_hindi: एवं वह इच्छा लाभ में सन्तुष्ट, द्वन्द्वातीत, शत्रुताशून्य और सिद्धि और असिद्धि में हर्ष विषादशून्य होने के कारण कर्म करने पर भी बद्ध नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::495.english_translation: Being content with whatever comes by chance, beyond dualities, free from envy, and unaffected by success or failure, one remains unbound by actions.
vishnu_gita::495.translation_literal: यदृच्छा (by chance) / लाभ (gain) / सन्तुष्टो (content) / द्वन्द्रातिो (beyond dualities) / विमत्सरः (without envy) / ममः (ego) / सिद्धा (success) / अवसिद्धौ (failure) / च (and) / कृत्वा (doing) / अपि (even) / न (not) / निबध्यते (is bound)
vishnu_gita::495.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::495.essence: Contentment and freedom from envy keep your actions from binding you, regardless of results.
vishnu_gita::495.simple_meaning: If you are satisfied with whatever you get without craving, free from envy and unaffected by wins or losses, your actions won't bind you.
vishnu_gita::495.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful knowing that contentment and freedom from envy protect you from being trapped by outcomes.
vishnu_gita::495.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches how being content with accidental gains, beyond opposing emotions like envy, and unaffected by success or failure frees one from the binding effects of action.
vishnu_gita::495.modern_relevance: You finish a project and feel no jealousy or craving over others' results, freeing your mind from stress and regret.
vishnu_gita::495.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing rewards to accepting whatever happens without envy, freeing your choices.

vishnu_gita::496.verse_sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं पविलीयते ॥
vishnu_gita::496.verse_hindi: निष्काम, सर्वबन्धनमुक्त, ज्ञान में अवस्थितचित्त और यज्ञ के लक्ष्य से कर्म करने वाले व्यक्ति के समस्त कर्म विलय को प्राप्त हो जाते हैं
vishnu_gita::496.english_translation: For one who is free from craving, with a mind established in wisdom, and who performs actions aimed at sacrifice, all their actions dissolve completely.
vishnu_gita::496.translation_literal: गतसङ्गस्य (free from attachment) / मुक्तस्य (free) / ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः (mind established in wisdom) / यज्ञायाचरतः (performing actions for sacrifice) / कर्म (actions) / समग्रं (entire) / पविलीयते (dissolve)
vishnu_gita::496.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::496.essence: Acting selflessly with wisdom dissolves the binding power of all your actions.
vishnu_gita::496.simple_meaning: If you act without craving, with a mind rooted in wisdom and focused on selfless purpose, your actions no longer bind you.
vishnu_gita::496.simple_insight: You can feel free from the burden of your actions by acting without desire and with clear wisdom.
vishnu_gita::496.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when someone acts without personal desire, with a mind steady in wisdom, and dedicates actions to a higher purpose like sacrifice, their actions lose binding effect, freeing them from consequences.
vishnu_gita::496.modern_relevance: You deliver your work with clarity and no expectation of reward, finding peace even when outcomes are uncertain.
vishnu_gita::496.insight: It teaches you to shift from craving results to dedicating effort to a greater purpose, freeing your mind from bondage.

vishnu_gita::497.verse_sanskrit:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि ।
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये ॥
vishnu_gita::497.verse_hindi: शरीरद्वारा, मनद्वारा, बुद्धिद्वारा और कर्माभिनिवेश शून्य इन्द्रियगण द्वारा योगिगण कर्मफलासक्ति को परित्याग करके आत्मशुद्धि के लिये कर्म किया करते हैं
vishnu_gita::497.english_translation: Yogis perform actions with body, mind, intellect, and senses without attachment, aiming for purification of the self.
vishnu_gita::497.translation_literal: कायेन (by body) / मनसा (by mind) / बुद्ध्या (by intellect) / केवलैः (only) / इन्द्रियैः (senses) / अपि (also) / योगिनः (yogis) / कर्म (action) / कुर्वन्ति (perform) / सङ्गं (attachment) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / आत्मशुद्धये (for self-purification)
vishnu_gita::497.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::497.essence: You can fully engage in action through all faculties while releasing attachment to results.
vishnu_gita::497.simple_meaning: You act using your body, mind, intellect, and senses, but without clinging to the results, to purify your true self.
vishnu_gita::497.simple_insight: There’s freedom in giving your full effort without needing the outcome to belong to you.
vishnu_gita::497.detailed_meaning: As Vishnu instructs, yogis engage every part of themselves—body, mind, intellect, and senses—in action. Yet they abandon attachment to results. This teaching guides Arjuna to act purely to purify his inner being, not for rewards or losses.
vishnu_gita::497.modern_relevance: You throw yourself into a project, use all your skills and focus, yet you don’t obsess over how others will judge or reward you.
vishnu_gita::497.insight: Shift your focus from outcome ownership to wholehearted engagement in the process, cleansing your inner state.

vishnu_gita::498.verse_sanskrit:
युक्त: कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम ।
अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::498.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म मे युक्त व्यक्ति कर्मफल का त्याग करके कर्म करने पर भी ब्रह्मनिष्ठा से उत्पन्न शांति को प्राप्त होता है और अयुक्त व्यक्ति कामना में प्रवृत्त होनेके कारण कर्मफल में आसक्त होकर बद्ध होता है
vishnu_gita::498.english_translation: A person united with the supreme being attains unwavering peace by renouncing the fruit of actions, while one not united is bound by attachment to results driven by desire.
vishnu_gita::498.translation_literal: युक्तः (united) / कर्मफलं (fruit of action) / त्यक्त्वा (renouncing) / शान्तिम् (peace) / आप्नोति (attains) / नैष्ठिकीम् (steady, unwavering) / अयुक्तः (not united) / कामकारेण (by desire and action) / फले (in the fruit) / सक्तः (attached) / निबध्यते (is bound)
vishnu_gita::498.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::498.essence: You can act fully and want nothing — these are not opposites.
vishnu_gita::498.simple_meaning: You can act and still keep steady peace by letting go of craving what your actions bring. Without this, desire traps you in attachment to results.
vishnu_gita::498.simple_insight: There's relief in knowing peace comes from releasing attachment to outcomes, not from controlling them.
vishnu_gita::498.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a person aligned with the supreme being acts without craving the results and so attains steady peace. In contrast, one driven by desire becomes trapped by attachment to outcomes. This teaching guides Arjuna on how to perform duty with calmness.
vishnu_gita::498.modern_relevance: You finished a big project but anxiety about recognition or reward lingers. This shows peace happens when you stop chasing approval.
vishnu_gita::498.insight: It teaches you to focus on your actions themselves, shifting attention away from outcomes that cause stress and binding attachment.

vishnu_gita::499.verse_sanskrit:
यं सन्न्यासमिति प्राहुर्योग जानीत तं सुराः।
न ह्यसन्न्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥
vishnu_gita::499.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जिसको सन्यास कहते हैं उसीको योग जानो क्योंकि फलकामना का त्याग किये बिना कोई योगी नहीं हो सक्ता है
vishnu_gita::499.english_translation: O deities, know that true yoga is renunciation; no yogi exists without giving up desire for results.
vishnu_gita::499.translation_literal: यं (which) / सन्न्यासमिति (renunciation-called) / प्राहुः (say) / योग (yoga) / जानीत (know) / तं (that) / सुराः (deities) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / असन्न्यस्त (not renounced) / सङ्कल्पः (desire/resolve) / योगी (yogi) / भवति (becomes) / कश्चन (anyone)
vishnu_gita::499.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::499.essence: No one can truly be a yogi without giving up desire for results.
vishnu_gita::499.simple_meaning: True yoga means giving up all craving for results; without this renunciation, no one can be a yogi.
vishnu_gita::499.simple_insight: There is peace in releasing the need to control outcomes to be truly free.
vishnu_gita::499.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, explaining that renunciation—giving up attachment to outcomes—is the essence of yoga. Without this, no practitioner can truly embody yogic discipline or reach inner freedom.
vishnu_gita::499.modern_relevance: You worked hard on a project but feel anxious hoping for praise. Real peace comes when you stop chasing rewards.
vishnu_gita::499.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing outcomes to practicing self-mastery through renunciation of desires.

vishnu_gita::500.verse_sanskrit:
आरुरुक्षोसुनेर्योग कर्म कारणमुच्यते ।
योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::500.verse_hindi: कर्मयोग मार्ग पर चलने वाले की इच्छा करने वाले योगी के लिए कर्म ही ही कारणरूप (साधनरूप) कहा जाता है, परन्तु कर्मयोग पद पर आरूढ़ व्यक्ति के लिये समाधि ही कारणरूप (साधनरूप ) कही गई है
vishnu_gita::500.english_translation: For one who desires to follow the path of Karma Yoga, action is called the cause; but for the person established in Karma Yoga, stillness is called the cause.
vishnu_gita::500.translation_literal: आरुरुः (desires) असुनेर् (for the one who) योग (yoga) कर्म (action) कारणम् (cause) उच्यते (is called) । योगारूढस्य (of the one established in yoga) तस्यैव (the same) शमः (stillness) कारणम् (cause) उच्यते (is called) ॥
vishnu_gita::500.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::500.essence: Starting with action is natural, but true progress depends on finding stillness within.
vishnu_gita::500.simple_meaning: At first, action is the tool for those wanting to practice Karma Yoga, but when they reach mastery, inner stillness becomes the true cause or support.
vishnu_gita::500.simple_insight: You feel the shift from doing to being as your practice deepens and matures.
vishnu_gita::500.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to seekers that when someone begins the path of Karma Yoga, their actions are the main focus and means for progress. But once established firmly in Karma Yoga, the person's calm inner stillness sustains their progress more than external action.
vishnu_gita::500.modern_relevance: You push hard at the start of a new project, but as you gain skill, quiet confidence and calm focus become your real strength.
vishnu_gita::500.insight: It teaches you to recognize when effort must shift from external doing to internal calm as your practice matures.

vishnu_gita::501.verse_sanskrit:
यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते ।
सर्वसङ्कल्पसन्न्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::501.verse_hindi: साधक जब इन्द्रियों के भोग्य विषयों पर और उनके साधनभूत कर्मों पर आसक्ति नहीं रखता है तब वह सर्व संकल्प त्यागी व्यक्ति योगारूढ़ कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::501.english_translation: When a practitioner is no longer attached to sensory objects or the actions that sustain them, they are called a renouncer of all desires and said to have ascended yoga.
vishnu_gita::501.translation_literal: यदा (when) हि (indeed) नेन्द्रियार्थेषु (to sensory objects) न (not) कर्मस्वनुषज्जते (is attached to actions) । सर्वसङ्कल्पसन्न्यासी (renouncer of all desires) योगारूढः (ascended yoga) तदा (then) उच्यते (is said) ॥
vishnu_gita::501.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::501.essence: You ascend yoga by renouncing all attachment to senses and their actions.
vishnu_gita::501.simple_meaning: You become established in yoga when you stop being attached to sensory pleasures and the actions that support them.
vishnu_gita::501.simple_insight: Letting go of craving brings steady peace and deeper connection to your practice.
vishnu_gita::501.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when a seeker stops clinging to sense objects and the actions linked to them, they renounce all desires and attain a higher state of yoga, marking progress on the spiritual path.
vishnu_gita::501.modern_relevance: You scroll past distractions but your mind still clings to desires; this verse invites you to release that grip and find steadiness.
vishnu_gita::501.insight: It teaches shifting focus from chasing sensory rewards to steady practice free from grasping.

vishnu_gita::502.verse_sanskrit:
देवाः ! नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते ।
न हि कल्याणकृत् कश्चित् क्वापि दुर्गतिमृच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::502.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! इस लोक में वा परलोक में उसका विनाश नहीं है क्योंकि कोई भी शुभकर्मकारी कहीं भी दुर्गति को प्राप्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::502.english_translation: O divine beings! There is no destruction for him in this world or the higher realm, for no one who performs auspicious actions ever meets with misfortune anywhere.
vishnu_gita::502.translation_literal: देवाः (divine beings) ! नैवेह (not here nor) नामुत्र (there) विनाशः (destruction) तस्य (of him) विद्यते (exists) । न (not) हि (indeed) कल्याणकृत् (one who does auspicious actions) कश्चित् (anyone) क्वापि (anywhere) दुर्गतिम् (misfortune) ऋच्छति (attains) ॥
vishnu_gita::502.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::502.essence: Rightful action guarantees safety from destruction across all realms.
vishnu_gita::502.simple_meaning: If you perform good and rightful actions, you will not face destruction or misfortune anywhere, in this world or beyond.
vishnu_gita::502.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing that right actions create lasting safety and protection.
vishnu_gita::502.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, assuring them that anyone who follows a path of righteous action will not suffer destruction or fall into misfortune, whether in this life or beyond. This verse encourages steady commitment to virtuous deeds.
vishnu_gita::502.modern_relevance: You did the right thing today, even if no one noticed. That choice protects your path forward, no matter what happens next.
vishnu_gita::502.insight: It shifts your focus from fearing outcomes to trusting that good actions build lasting security.

vishnu_gita::503.verse_sanskrit:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः।
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥
vishnu_gita::503.verse_hindi: योगभ्रष्ट व्यक्ति पुण्यात्माओं के लोकों को प्राप्त होकर और वहां बहुत वर्षों तक सुखभोग करके पवित्रात्मा श्रीमानों के घर में जन्म ग्रहण करता है
vishnu_gita::503.english_translation: A person who falls from yoga attains the worlds of the virtuous and, after enjoying there for many years, is born in a pure and prosperous family.
vishnu_gita::503.translation_literal: प्राप्य (obtaining) पुण्यकृतां (of virtuous) लोकानुषित्वा (living in the worlds) शाश्वतीः (for many years) समाः (equal) शुचीनां (of pure) श्रीमतां (prosperous) गेहे (in the house) योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते (the one fallen from yoga is born)
vishnu_gita::503.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::503.essence: Falling from yoga leads to rebirth in purity and prosperity after enjoying virtuous realms.
