vishnu_gita::648.translation_literal: असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः (unattached, not clinging) पुत्रदारगृहादिषु (to sons, wives, homes, etc.) । नित्यश्च (always) समचित्तत्वम् (equanimity of mind) इष्टानिष्टोपपतिषु (in gain and loss) ॥
vishnu_gita::648.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::648.essence: Steady your mind by letting go of attachment to family and possessions.
vishnu_gita::648.simple_meaning: You should not cling to family or possessions and keep your mind steady through good and bad experiences.
vishnu_gita::648.simple_insight: You feel peaceful when you don't get swept away by pleasure or pain.
vishnu_gita::648.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that attachment to family and home causes disturbance. Whether facing joy or sorrow, gain or loss, the mind should remain balanced and steady.
vishnu_gita::648.modern_relevance: You face social pressures to cling to relationships or status, but true calm comes from not letting these define your peace.
vishnu_gita::648.insight: It teaches you to practice emotional balance by releasing attachment to external people and things.

vishnu_gita::649.verse_hindi: मुझमें अनन्य योग (सर्वत्र समष्टि ) द्वारा अव्यभिचारिणी (अनन्य) भक्ति निर्जन स्थान में रहना, लोकसमाज में वैराग्य,
vishnu_gita::649.english_translation: Devotion to me without deviation, practicing exclusive yoga, dwelling in solitude, and detachment from worldly society.
vishnu_gita::649.translation_literal: मयि (in me) च (and) अन्य (other) योगेन (by yoga) भक्तिः (devotion) अव्यभिचारिणी (without deviation) । विविक्त (solitary) देश (place) सेवेत्व (serving) अरति (dislike) जन (people) संसदि (assembly) ॥
vishnu_gita::649.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::649.essence: Steady devotion grows in quiet solitude, free from social distractions.
vishnu_gita::649.simple_meaning: Devotion that focuses exclusively on the divine and remains steady grows by spending time alone and avoiding the distractions of society.
vishnu_gita::649.simple_insight: You can feel calm and steady in your devotion by embracing solitude and detachment from social distractions.
vishnu_gita::649.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that pure, unwavering devotion thrives through exclusive connection with the divine, practiced in quiet solitude, and by turning away from the restless distractions of social life.
vishnu_gita::649.modern_relevance: You find your deepest focus and love when you step away from constant social noise and distractions, creating space for steady connection.
vishnu_gita::649.insight: It encourages you to cultivate focused devotion by seeking quiet and limiting social distractions that pull your attention away.

vishnu_gita::650.verse_hindi: आत्मज्ञानपरायणता और तत्त्वज्ञान के फल (मोक्ष) का दर्शन, ये ज्ञान के लक्षण कहे जाते हैं इनसे विपरीत जो लक्षण हैं, वह सभी अज्ञान के लक्षण हैं
vishnu_gita::650.english_translation: Self-knowledge is eternal and truth-realizing; these are the marks of true wisdom. Anything opposite to these are marks of ignorance.
vishnu_gita::650.translation_literal: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं (self-knowledge eternal) / तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् (truth-realization for the sake of understanding) / एतज्ज्ञानमिति (this is called knowledge) / प्रोक्तमज्ञानं (opposite is ignorance) / यदतोऽन्यथा (whatever is otherwise)
vishnu_gita::650.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::650.essence: True wisdom is recognizing the eternal nature of your self and reality.
vishnu_gita::650.simple_meaning: True knowledge is realizing your self is eternal and recognizing the true nature of reality. Anything that denies this is ignorance.
vishnu_gita::650.simple_insight: You can feel secure knowing your true self is unchanging and real beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::650.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains that real wisdom means knowing the self is eternal and seeing the true nature of reality. This knowledge leads to freedom. Anything contradicting this understanding is ignorance, keeping beings trapped in confusion.
vishnu_gita::650.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by change or uncertainty, remembering your true self is eternal brings calm and clarity.
vishnu_gita::650.insight: It shifts your focus from fleeting experiences to the unchanging truth of your self, fostering lasting clarity.

vishnu_gita::651.verse_sanskrit:
निश्चितं वच्मि वो देवाः ! श्रीगुरोर्दयया विना ।
किञ्चित् कदापि कुत्रापि कथञ्चिन्नैव लभ्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::651.verse_hindi: हे देवतागण ! मैं आप लोगों को निश्चय करके कहता हूँ कि बिना श्रीगुरुकृपा के कभी भी कहीं भी किसी प्रकार से भी कुछ भी प्राप्त नहीं होता है।
vishnu_gita::651.english_translation: O divine beings! I firmly say nothing is ever attained anywhere without the grace of the revered teacher.
vishnu_gita::651.translation_literal: निश्चितं (certainly) वच्मि (I speak) वो (to you) देवाः (divine beings) ! श्रीगुरोः (of the revered teacher) दयया (grace) विना (without) । किञ्चित् (anything) कदापि (ever) कुत्रापि (anywhere) कथञ्चिन् (in any way) नैव (not at all) लभ्यते (is attained) ॥
vishnu_gita::651.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::651.essence: Nothing is ever truly attained without the grace of a sincere teacher.
vishnu_gita::651.simple_meaning: Nothing can truly be gained without the kindness and guidance of a sincere teacher.
vishnu_gita::651.simple_insight: You feel the importance of trusting a teacher’s support before success unfolds.
vishnu_gita::651.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, emphasizing that no achievement or knowledge is possible without the compassionate support of the revered teacher. This moment stresses the essential role of guidance on the spiritual path.
vishnu_gita::651.modern_relevance: Before mastering a skill or making a big change, you recall how much a mentor’s support shaped your progress.
vishnu_gita::651.insight: It shifts your perspective to value trust in guidance as the foundation for all growth and attainment.

vishnu_gita::652.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मज्ञानोपलब्धौ हि हेतुरस्ति गुरोः कृपा ।
आत्मज्ञानन्तु मत्माप्तौ कारणं नात्र संशयः ॥
vishnu_gita::652.verse_hindi: आत्मज्ञान प्राप्ति का कारण गुरु कृपा ही है और मुझे प्राप्त करने का कारण आत्मज्ञान है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं
vishnu_gita::652.english_translation: The cause for the attainment of self-knowledge is the grace of the guru, and the reason for attaining me is self-knowledge; there is no doubt about this.
vishnu_gita::652.translation_literal: आत्मज्ञानोपलब्धौ (for attainment of self-knowledge) / हि (indeed) / हेतुरस्ति (is the cause) / गुरोः (of the guru) / कृपा (grace) । / आत्मज्ञानन्तु (self-knowledge indeed) / मत्माप्तौ (for attaining me) / कारणं (the reason) / नात्र (there is not) / संशयः (doubt) ॥
vishnu_gita::652.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::652.essence: Self-knowledge arises through the grace of a teacher and leads to knowing the true self without doubt.
vishnu_gita::652.simple_meaning: The grace of a teacher is what makes self-knowledge possible, and gaining self-knowledge is what leads to knowing the true self without doubt.
vishnu_gita::652.simple_insight: You can trust that the care and guidance of a teacher open the door to your true self.
vishnu_gita::652.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that realizing the true self depends on the loving grace of a teacher. Without this grace, self-knowledge cannot arise. This verse emphasizes the essential role of the guru in leading one to the highest understanding.
vishnu_gita::652.modern_relevance: When you struggle to understand yourself, a trusted guide or mentor can help you see what was hidden and open your eyes to your deeper nature.
vishnu_gita::652.insight: It teaches you to recognize that self-understanding arises not just from effort but from receiving guidance and openness from a trusted source.

vishnu_gita::653.verse_sanskrit:
तद्वित्त मणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्निबो ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्वदर्शिनः ॥
vishnu_gita::653.verse_hindi: प्रणिपात, जिज्ञासा और गुरुसेवा के द्वारा उस ज्ञान का लाभ करोतत्त्वदर्शी ज्ञानिगण तुमको ज्ञान का उपदेश देंगे
vishnu_gita::653.english_translation: By bowing down, questioning, and serving the teacher, those who see the truth will teach you knowledge.
vishnu_gita::653.translation_literal: तद्वित्त (that knowledgeable) मणिपातेन (by bowing down) परिप्रश्नेन (by questioning) सेवया (by service) । उपदेक्ष्यन् (teaching) निबो (those who know) ज्ञानं (knowledge) ज्ञानिनः (wise ones) तत्त्वदर्शिनः (who perceive the truth) ॥
vishnu_gita::653.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::653.essence: True wisdom comes through humble respect, sincere inquiry, and devoted service to the teacher.
vishnu_gita::653.simple_meaning: You gain true understanding by showing respect, asking sincere questions, and serving your teacher.
vishnu_gita::653.simple_insight: Openness and humility in learning create space for deeper wisdom to enter.
vishnu_gita::653.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that seekers should approach their teachers with reverence, curiosity, and selfless service. These attitudes invite wise teachers who truly see the essence of things to share knowledge effectively.
vishnu_gita::653.modern_relevance: Before a mentor session, you prepare thoughtful questions and listen carefully, knowing respect and effort open the door to real learning.
vishnu_gita::653.insight: It teaches you to actively engage with your teacher through respectful questioning and service, which deepens your understanding.

vishnu_gita::654.verse_sanskrit:
यजज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यथ निर्जराः ।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यथात्मन्यथो मयि ॥
vishnu_gita::654.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जिस ज्ञान के जान लेने से पुनः इस प्रकार के मोह को नहीं प्राप्त होगे। और जिसके द्वारा भूतगण को आत्मा में और अनन्तर मुझमें सब कुछ देख सकोगे
vishnu_gita::654.english_translation: O divine beings, by knowing this knowledge, you will no longer be deluded and will see all beings in the true self and afterwards see everything in me.
vishnu_gita::654.translation_literal: यजज्ञात्वा (having known this knowledge) / न (not) / पुनः (again) / मोह (delusion) / एवं (thus) / यास्यथ (will go) / निर्जराः (without decay) / येन (by which) / भूतानि (beings) / अशेषेण (completely) / द्रक्ष्यथ (you will see) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / अथ (and then) / मयि (in me)
vishnu_gita::654.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::654.essence: Complete knowledge ends delusion and reveals unity of self and all existence.
vishnu_gita::654.simple_meaning: Knowing this knowledge removes delusion forever and lets you see all beings as part of your true self and then see everything reflected in the divine.
vishnu_gita::654.simple_insight: There is peace in realizing you and all life are connected beyond confusion.
vishnu_gita::654.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that once they fully understand this knowledge, they will no longer fall into confusion. They will perceive every being as the true self and then see all existence as a reflection of the divine presence in Vishnu.
vishnu_gita::654.modern_relevance: When your doubts vanish, you suddenly see people and situations as connected parts of a greater whole.
vishnu_gita::654.insight: It shifts your mind from separation and confusion to unified awareness of self and all beings.

vishnu_gita::655.verse_sanskrit:
अपि स्थ यदि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमाः।
सर्व ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यथ ॥
vishnu_gita::655.verse_hindi: यदि सकल पापियों से भी तुम अधिक पापी हो तो भी सम्पूर्ण पापरूप समुद्र को ज्ञान रूपी जहाज द्वारा सम्यक रूप से पार कर सकोगे
vishnu_gita::655.english_translation: Even if you are the most sinful among all sinners, you can cross the entire ocean of sin by the boat of knowledge.
vishnu_gita::655.translation_literal: अपि (even) / स्थ (if) / यदि (if) / पापेभ्यः (from sins) / सर्वेभ्यः (all) / पापकृत्तमाः (most sinful) / सर्व (entire) / ज्ञानप्लवेनैव (by the boat of knowledge indeed) / वृजिनं (the shore) / सन्तरिष्यथ (you will cross)
vishnu_gita::655.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::655.essence: Deep knowledge can completely overcome even the greatest wrongdoing.
vishnu_gita::655.simple_meaning: Even if you have done many wrong things, deep understanding can help you overcome all of them completely.
vishnu_gita::655.simple_insight: You can feel hope knowing that knowledge can help you overcome even your worst mistakes.
vishnu_gita::655.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu teaches that no matter how great someone's faults or mistakes are, gaining true knowledge can help them completely overcome all wrongdoing and reach a safe state beyond it.
vishnu_gita::655.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your past mistakes or regrets, remember that learning and understanding can help you move beyond them fully.
vishnu_gita::655.insight: It shifts your mindset from being trapped by past faults to using knowledge as a tool for complete transformation.

vishnu_gita::656.verse_sanskrit:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निभस्मसात्कुरुतेऽमराः ! ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
vishnu_gita::656.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जिस प्रकार प्रज्वलित अग्नि काष्ठ समूह को भस्मसात् करती है उसी प्रकार ज्ञानरूप अग्नि सकल कर्मों को भस्मसात् कर देती है
vishnu_gita::656.english_translation: Just as blazing fire turns wood to ashes, the fire of knowledge burns all actions to ashes.
vishnu_gita::656.translation_literal: यथा (just as) इधांसि (wood pieces) समिद्धः (blazing) अग्नि (fire) भस्मसात् (to ashes) कुरुते (makes) अमराः (immortals) । ज्ञानाग्निः (fire of knowledge) सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) भस्मसात् (to ashes) कुरुते (makes) तथा (likewise) ॥
vishnu_gita::656.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::656.essence: The fire of knowledge can completely burn away all actions and their effects.
vishnu_gita::656.simple_meaning: Knowledge acts like fire that completely destroys all your actions and their effects.
vishnu_gita::656.simple_insight: You can find freedom by letting knowledge dissolve what your actions leave behind.
vishnu_gita::656.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, comparing how a blazing fire burns wood to ashes with how the fire of knowledge completely consumes all actions, freeing one from their binding effects.
vishnu_gita::656.modern_relevance: You face regrets and consequences from past choices that feel like heavy burdens—knowledge can help you release them fully.
vishnu_gita::656.insight: It teaches you to use wisdom to dissolve attachment to your actions and their outcomes.

vishnu_gita::657.verse_sanskrit:
नहि ज्ञानेन सद्रशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धाः कालेनाऽऽत्मनि विन्दथ ॥
vishnu_gita::657.verse_hindi: क्योंकि इस लोक में ज्ञान के समान पवित्र और कोई नहीं है, योगद्वारा सिद्धि प्राप्त होने पर उस आत्म ज्ञान को यथासमय अपने में स्वयं प्राप्त करोगे
vishnu_gita::657.english_translation: There is nothing as pure in this world as true knowledge; those perfected in yoga eventually find that self-knowledge within themselves in time.
vishnu_gita::657.translation_literal: नहि (not) ज्ञानेन (by knowledge) सदृशं (equal) पवित्रम् (pure) इह (here/in this world) विद्यते (exists) । तत् (that) स्वयम् (by itself) योगसंसिद्धाः (those perfected in yoga) कालेन (in time) आत्मनि (in the self) विन्दतः (find) ॥
vishnu_gita::657.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::657.essence: True knowledge is uniquely pure and unfolds naturally within those devoted to yoga.
vishnu_gita::657.simple_meaning: True knowledge is the purest thing in this world, and those who master yoga will gradually realize this self-knowledge inside themselves.
vishnu_gita::657.simple_insight: There is a deep purity in knowing yourself that grows quietly over time.
vishnu_gita::657.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains that knowledge is the most sacred quality in the world. Those who sincerely practice yoga will, in due time, experience this pure self-knowledge within themselves, marking a key step in their spiritual journey.
vishnu_gita::657.modern_relevance: When you commit to a practice like meditation or self-inquiry, clarity and deep understanding arise naturally, even if not immediately visible.
vishnu_gita::657.insight: It shifts focus from rushing results to patiently trusting that deep understanding will emerge through steady practice.

vishnu_gita::658.verse_sanskrit:
श्रद्धावान् लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाऽधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::658.verse_hindi: श्रद्धावान् तत्परायण और जितेन्द्रिय व्यक्ति ज्ञान प्राप्त करता है और ज्ञान को प्राप्त करके अतिशीघ्र परमशान्ति (मोक्ष) को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::658.english_translation: A person with trust, focused and with controlled senses, attains knowledge; having gained knowledge, they quickly reach supreme peace.
vishnu_gita::658.translation_literal: श्रद्धावान् (trusting) / लभते (obtains) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / तत्परः (focused) / संयतेन्द्रियः (with controlled senses) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / लब्ध्वा (having obtained) / परां (supreme) / शान्तिम् (peace) / अचिरेण (quickly) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
vishnu_gita::658.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::658.essence: Trust combined with focused self-control quickly leads to true knowledge and deep peace.
vishnu_gita::658.simple_meaning: When you trust deeply, stay focused, and control your senses, you gain true knowledge that leads you quickly to profound peace.
vishnu_gita::658.simple_insight: You can feel hopeful knowing steady trust and focus bring inner calm faster than you think.
vishnu_gita::658.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person who has sincere trust (shraddha), is fully devoted, and controls their senses gains true wisdom. This wisdom then leads them rapidly to supreme peace, or inner freedom, highlighting the power of faith and discipline together.
vishnu_gita::658.modern_relevance: You start a new practice or habit unsure if it will work. With trust and steady focus, you soon gain clarity and calm you didn’t expect.
vishnu_gita::658.insight: This verse shifts your mind to hold faith as a real power that, combined with focus and self-control, accelerates your inner growth.

vishnu_gita::659.verse_sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नाऽयं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयान्मनः ॥
vishnu_gita::659.verse_hindi: अश्रद्धालु संशयात्मा और मूढ़ व्यक्ति नाश को प्राप्त होता है। संशयात्मा व्यक्ति के लिये इहलोक और परलोक दोनों कष्टप्रद होते हैं और उसको सुख प्राप्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::659.english_translation: A person without faith and full of doubt perishes; for them, neither this world nor the higher realm is pleasant.
vishnu_gita::659.translation_literal: अज्ञश्चाश्रधानश्च (ignorant and without faith) / संशयात्मा (one whose mind is doubtful) / विनश्यति (perishes) / नाऽयं (not this) / लोकोऽस्ति (world exists) / न (nor) / परो (other/higher) / न (nor) / सुखं (happiness) / संशयान्मनः (for the doubtful mind)
vishnu_gita::659.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::659.essence: Doubt destroys peace; only trust lets happiness flourish across all realms.
vishnu_gita::659.simple_meaning: Without trust in the divine or your path, your mind suffers doubt that brings destruction and blocks happiness in any realm.
vishnu_gita::659.simple_insight: Trust feels like a quiet anchor amid uncertainty, letting you find peace inside and outside.
vishnu_gita::659.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a person who lacks faith and whose mind is full of doubt cannot find happiness or peace in this world or beyond. Such uncertainty leads to inner ruin, showing why trust is essential for spiritual well-being.
vishnu_gita::659.modern_relevance: You hesitate before a big decision, torn by uncertainty. That doubt makes even good options feel heavy and joyless.
vishnu_gita::659.insight: It teaches you to replace indecision with trust, freeing your mind to experience peace and joy fully.

vishnu_gita::660.verse_sanskrit:
योगसन्नस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयानम ।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति दिवौकसः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::660.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जिस व्यक्ति ने योग द्वारा सकल कर्मों को आत्मा में अर्पण किया है और जिसने आत्मज्ञान द्वारा सकल संशय छिन्न कर दिये हैं ऐसे आत्म ज्ञान सम्पन्न व्यक्ति को कर्म बन्धन नहीं कर सकते हैं
vishnu_gita::660.english_translation: O divine beings! One who, through yoga, has surrendered all actions to the true self and whose doubts have been destroyed by self-knowledge is not bound by the consequences of actions.
vishnu_gita::660.translation_literal: योगसन्नस्तकर्माणं (yoga-surrendered actions) / ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयानम (knowledge-destroyed doubts) / आत्मवन्तं (possessing the true self) / न (not) / कर्माणि (actions) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / दिवौकसः (divine beings / gods)
vishnu_gita::660.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::660.essence: Clear inner knowing and surrendered action together free you from all binding consequences.
vishnu_gita::660.simple_meaning: You become free from being bound by results when you surrender your actions through yoga and remove all doubts through true knowledge.
vishnu_gita::660.simple_insight: There is deep relief in knowing that surrender and clarity free you from bondage.
vishnu_gita::660.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, teaching that a person who practices yoga by surrendering all actions to the true self and whose self-knowledge removes all doubts is no longer bound by the consequences of actions. This is a pivotal moment teaching liberation through wisdom and surrender.
vishnu_gita::660.modern_relevance: You’ve wrestled with uncertainty and tried to control outcomes, but peace comes when you trust your clear inner knowing and release your grip on results.
vishnu_gita::660.insight: It teaches you to dissolve doubt through knowledge and surrender your actions, freeing yourself from attachment to consequences.

vishnu_gita::661.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः ।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठत बुभुत्सवः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::661.verse_hindi: अत: हे जिज्ञासु देवगण ! अपने अज्ञान से उत्पन्न हृदयस्थ संशय को ज्ञानरूप खड्ग द्वारा छेदन करके इस योग का अवलम्बन करो
vishnu_gita::661.english_translation: Therefore, O seekers among the divine beings, cut through the doubt born of ignorance in your heart with the sword of knowledge and firmly hold on to this yoga.
vishnu_gita::661.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / अज्ञानसंभूतं (born of ignorance) / हृत्स्थं (in the heart) / ज्ञानासिनात्मनः (by the sword of knowledge) / छित्त्वै (cutting) / ऐनं (this) / संशयं (doubt) / योगम (yoga) / आतिष्ठत (firmly hold) / बुभुत्सवः (O abominable ones, here addressed respectfully as seekers)!
vishnu_gita::661.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::661.essence: Doubt born from ignorance can be cut by knowledge and steadiness in yoga.
vishnu_gita::661.simple_meaning: You can overcome the doubt that comes from ignorance by using clear understanding and firmly practicing this yoga.
vishnu_gita::661.simple_insight: There is strength and clarity when you face doubt with knowledge and hold steady.
vishnu_gita::661.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine seekers, urging them to overcome the inner doubt born from ignorance. He advises using the sharpness of knowledge to cut through this uncertainty and to hold tightly to the practice of yoga as their foundation.
vishnu_gita::661.modern_relevance: When your mind is clouded with uncertainty about your path, rely on clear understanding and steady practice to move forward.
vishnu_gita::661.insight: It teaches you to confront inner doubts actively with knowledge and maintain firm commitment to your practice.

vishnu_gita::662.verse_sanskrit:
नादत्ते कस्याचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।
आज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥
vishnu_gita::662.verse_hindi: ईश्वर किसी का भी पाप ग्रहण नहीं करते हैं और पुण्य भी ग्रहण नहीं करते हैं। अज्ञानके द्वारा ज्ञान आच्छन्न है इसी कारण जीवधारी मोहित होते हैं अर्थात् इन्द्रियासक्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::662.english_translation: The supreme being accepts neither sin nor merit from anyone; knowledge is hidden by ignorance, causing beings to be deluded and attached to the senses.
vishnu_gita::662.translation_literal:
नादत्ते (does not accept) कस्याचित्पापं (anyone's sin) न (nor) चैव (also not) सुकृतं (merit) विभुः (the supreme being)।
आज्ञानेनावृतं (covered by ignorance) ज्ञानं (knowledge) तेन (by that) मुह्यन्ति (are deluded) जन्तवः (beings) ॥
vishnu_gita::662.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::662.essence: Your true value is beyond actions; ignorance alone clouds your knowing.
vishnu_gita::662.simple_meaning: The supreme being does not take on anyone’s bad or good actions. Ignorance hides true knowledge, making beings confused and attached to their senses.
vishnu_gita::662.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing that your true self is beyond right or wrong actions.
vishnu_gita::662.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the supreme being neither accepts blame nor credit for anyone’s actions. Because ignorance obscures true knowledge, beings remain deluded and caught in sensory attachment. This moment reveals why clarity about self is needed.
vishnu_gita::662.modern_relevance: You felt judged for a mistake or praised for success, yet the deeper truth is your worth isn’t defined by outcomes but by your clarity of mind.
vishnu_gita::662.insight: It shifts the focus from external approval to recognizing how ignorance distorts your self-view and blocks true understanding.

vishnu_gita::663.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः ।
तेपामादियवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥
vishnu_gita::663.verse_hindi: किन्तु आत्म ज्ञान के द्वारा जिनका वह अज्ञान नष्ट होजाता है, सूर्य जिस प्रकार अन्धकार को नाश करके सकल वस्तुओं को प्रकाशित कर देता है। उसी प्रकार उनका वह ज्ञान परमात्मा को प्रकाशित कर देता है
vishnu_gita::663.english_translation: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by true knowledge, that knowledge reveals the supreme being as the sun dispels darkness and lights all things.
vishnu_gita::663.translation_literal: ज्ञानेन (by knowledge) / तु (but) / तदज्ञानं (that ignorance) / येषां (of those) / नाशितमात्मनः (destroyed in the self) / ते (they) / पामादियवज्ज्ञानं (knowledge like the sun) / प्रकाशयति (illuminates) / तत्परम् (the supreme)
vishnu_gita::663.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::663.essence: True knowledge removes ignorance and reveals the supreme as sunlight reveals all.
vishnu_gita::663.simple_meaning: When your ignorance is removed by true knowledge, that knowledge reveals the supreme being clearly, just as the sun removes darkness and lights everything.
vishnu_gita::663.simple_insight: There is hope in knowing that clarity can dispel the confusion hiding the highest truth.
vishnu_gita::663.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how true knowledge dispels ignorance inside a person. Like the sun that clears darkness to show everything, this knowledge reveals the supreme being, lifting the veil of confusion that hides it.
vishnu_gita::663.modern_relevance: When confusion clouds your mind, gaining clear knowledge can suddenly reveal what was always there, like morning light after a long night.
vishnu_gita::663.insight: It teaches you to trust that gaining understanding clears away deep confusion and opens you to the supreme reality.

vishnu_gita::664.verse_sanskrit:
विद्याविनयसम्पने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
vishnu_gita::664.verse_hindi: विद्या और विनयसम्पन्न ब्राह्मणपर और चाण्डाल पर एवं गौ हाथी और कुत्ते पर ज्ञानीगण समदर्शी हुआ करते है
vishnu_gita::664.english_translation: The wise see equally the learned Brahmin, the cow, the elephant, the dog, and even the outcast.
vishnu_gita::664.translation_literal: विद्या (knowledge) / विनयसम्पने (humble-endowed) / ब्राह्मणे (to Brahmin) / गवि (cow) / हस्तिनि (elephant) / शुनि (dog) / चैव (and also) / श्वपाके (outcast) / च (and) / पण्डिताः (wise people) / समदर्शिनः (equal-seeing)
vishnu_gita::664.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::664.essence: Wisdom is seeing all beings with equal respect, beyond social distinctions.
vishnu_gita::664.simple_meaning: True wisdom means seeing all beings—learned or lowly—without discrimination or prejudice.
vishnu_gita::664.simple_insight: You feel calm when you treat everyone with equal respect and kindness.
vishnu_gita::664.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a wise person treats the learned Brahmin, animals like cows and elephants, and even outcasts with equal vision, free from social or caste bias.
vishnu_gita::664.modern_relevance: When you meet people from different backgrounds or walks of life, this teaching invites you to honor each one without judgment.
vishnu_gita::664.insight: It shifts your mind to recognize the shared value in everyone, removing barriers of status or identity.

vishnu_gita::665.verse_sanskrit:
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्मादब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः॥
vishnu_gita::665.verse_hindi: जिनका मन समभाव में स्थित है, संसार में रहकर ही उन्होंने संसार को जीत लिया है क्योंकि समान और निर्दोषरूप से ब्रह्म व्यापक हैं अतः वह ब्रह्म भाव में स्थित रहते हैं
vishnu_gita::665.english_translation: Those whose minds remain steady in equanimity have conquered the world while living in it, because Brahman is equal and faultless everywhere; thus they abide in the state of Brahman.
vishnu_gita::665.translation_literal:
इहैव (right here) तैर्जितः (conquered by them) सर्गो (world) येषां (whose) साम्ये (in equanimity) स्थितं (situated) मनः (mind) ।
निर्दोषं (faultless) हि (indeed) समं (equal) ब्रह्म (Brahman) तस्मात् (therefore) अब्रह्मणि (in non-Brahman) ते (they) स्थिताः (abide)॥
vishnu_gita::665.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::665.essence: A mind steady in equal vision conquers the world by abiding in faultless reality.
vishnu_gita::665.simple_meaning: You master the world by maintaining a steady, balanced mind that sees everything equally and without fault.
vishnu_gita::665.simple_insight: Peace grows when your mind stays calm and undisturbed by life's ups and downs.
vishnu_gita::665.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that those who keep their minds steady and balanced amid the world's changes have truly overcome it. Because Brahman—the supreme reality—is equal and flawless everywhere, such people remain established in that unchanging state.
vishnu_gita::665.modern_relevance: You face a stressful day with conflicting demands, yet your quiet, balanced mind keeps you steady and unshaken.
vishnu_gita::665.insight: Shift your focus from external chaos to steady inner balance to experience true mastery of your life.

vishnu_gita::666.verse_sanskrit:
न प्रहृप्येत् प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्याप्य चाऽप्रियम् ।
स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविदब्रह्मणि  स्थितः ॥
vishnu_gita::666.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मभाव में अवस्थित, स्थिरबुद्धि और मोहहीन ब्रह्मवेत्ता व्यक्ति प्रियवस्तु पाकर हर्षित नहीं होता है और अप्रिय वस्तु पाकर विषादयुक्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::666.english_translation: One established in the state of Brahman, with steady mind and free from delusion, does not rejoice on getting what is liked nor grieve on getting what is disliked.
vishnu_gita::666.translation_literal: न (not) / प्रहृप्येत् (rejoices) / प्रियं (what is liked) / प्राप्य (obtaining) / न (not) / उद्विजेत्यापि (disturbed even) / च (and) / अप्रियं (what is disliked) / स्थिरबुद्धि (steady mind) / असम्मूढः (not deluded) / ब्रह्मविद् (knower of Brahman) / ब्रह्मणि (in Brahman) / स्थितः (established)
vishnu_gita::666.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::666.essence: True wisdom is steady calm beyond liking or disliking.
vishnu_gita::666.simple_meaning: A person rooted in the supreme reality remains calm and steady, not reacting with joy or sorrow to what they like or dislike.
vishnu_gita::666.simple_insight: There’s peace in not letting desires or dislikes sway your inner calm.
vishnu_gita::666.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the state of a person who knows the supreme reality and is free from confusion. Such a person remains mentally steady, unaffected by favorable or unfavorable experiences, embodying perfect balance.
vishnu_gita::666.modern_relevance: You face unexpected news at work and feel neither elated nor crushed, simply steady and clear inside.
vishnu_gita::666.insight: It shifts your mindset from emotional reactivity to balanced observation, freeing you from being tossed by external events.

vishnu_gita::667.verse_sanskrit:
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथाज्योर्तिरेव यः।
स योगी ब्रह्म निर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::667.verse_hindi: आत्मभाव ही जिसको सुखबोध होता है आत्मभाव में ही जिसको आमोद होता है और आत्मभाव की ओर ही जिसकी दृष्टि है वह योगी ब्रह्मभाव में स्थित होकर ब्रह्मनिर्धाण अर्थात् मोक्ष को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::667.english_translation: A yogi who finds joy and delight within their true self, and whose vision is fixed on the true self, attains liberation by becoming one with the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::667.translation_literal: योऽन्तःसुखः (who inner-joy) / अन्तःआरामः (inner-pleasure) / तथा (thus) / ज्योर्तिः (light) / एव (indeed) / यः (who) / स (that) / योगी (yogi) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / निर्वाणं (liberation) / ब्रह्मभूतः (become supreme reality) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
vishnu_gita::667.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::667.essence: True joy arises from resting your vision fully on your true self, leading to liberation.
vishnu_gita::667.simple_meaning: True happiness and delight come from connecting deeply with your true self; focusing your awareness there leads to inner freedom.
vishnu_gita::667.simple_insight: You can feel peace by turning your attention fully inward to your true self.
vishnu_gita::667.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu describes a yogi who experiences inner joy and delight by focusing entirely on their true self. This inner state, like pure light, leads the yogi to union with the supreme reality and ultimate liberation.
vishnu_gita::667.modern_relevance: When stress floods your mind, turning your attention inward can uncover a quiet joy untouched by external chaos.
vishnu_gita::667.insight: It teaches you to redirect your awareness from outer distractions to the inner true self, opening a path to freedom.

vishnu_gita::668.verse_sanskrit:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।
छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
vishnu_gita::668.verse_hindi: पाप जिनके क्षीण हो गये हैं, संशय जिनके छिन्न हो गये हैं, जिनका अन्तःकरण संयमशील है और सकल प्राणिमात्र का हित करने में जो तत्पर हैं ऐसे ऋषिगण ब्रह्मनिर्वाण अर्थात् मोक्ष को प्राप्त करते हैं
vishnu_gita::668.english_translation: Sages who have eradicated faults, whose doubts are dispelled, whose inner selves are disciplined, and who delight in the welfare of all beings attain liberation in the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::668.translation_literal: लभन्ते (attain) ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम् (liberation in supreme reality) ऋषयः (sages) क्षीणकल्मषाः (whose faults are diminished) । छिन्नद्वैधा (whose doubts are cut) यतात्मानः (whose inner selves are disciplined) सर्वभूतहिते (in the welfare of all beings) रताः (delighting) ॥
vishnu_gita::668.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::668.essence: Freedom arises when doubt is gone, faults are cleansed, and care extends to all beings.
vishnu_gita::668.simple_meaning: Those who have removed their inner faults and doubts, control their inner selves, and focus on helping all beings, achieve ultimate freedom.
vishnu_gita::668.simple_insight: There is peace in being free from doubt and devoted to the well-being of everyone.
vishnu_gita::668.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes sages who have purified themselves from faults and doubts, disciplined their inner selves, and joyfully work for the good of all beings. These qualities lead them to attain liberation, the supreme freedom beyond worldly bonds.
vishnu_gita::668.modern_relevance: You feel lighter when your worries clear, your doubts settle, and you care genuinely for others around you.
vishnu_gita::668.insight: It teaches you to cleanse mental obstacles and widen your concern beyond yourself to experience true liberation.

vishnu_gita::669.verse_sanskrit:
काम क्रोध वियुक्ताना यतीनां यातचेतसाम ।
अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥
vishnu_gita::669.verse_hindi: कामक्रोधरहित संयमी और आत्मतत्वज्ञ यातिगण के लिए सर्वत्र ही मोक्ष है, अर्थात वह देहांत होने पर ही मुक्त होते हैं ऐसा नहीं है, देह रहते हुए भी वे मुक्त ही हैं
vishnu_gita::669.english_translation: For those restrained from desire and anger, whose minds are steady and who know the true self, liberation is present everywhere; they are free even while living in the body.
vishnu_gita::669.translation_literal: काम (desire) क्रोध (anger) वियुक्ताना (free from) यतीनां (of the disciplined ascetics) यातचेतसाम (whose minds are steady) अभितो (everywhere) ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं (liberation in the supreme reality) वर्तते (exists) विदितात्मनाम् (of those who know the true self)
vishnu_gita::669.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::669.essence: Freedom is present now when desire and anger no longer bind your mind.
vishnu_gita::669.simple_meaning: When you let go of desire and anger and steady your mind knowing your true self, freedom is present everywhere, even while alive.
vishnu_gita::669.simple_insight: Freedom is not a distant goal but a present reality when you master your mind.
vishnu_gita::669.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that ascetics who overcome desire and anger and have steady minds, aware of their true self, experience liberation right now—not only after death. This teaching shifts the idea of freedom from a future event to a present possibility.
vishnu_gita::669.modern_relevance: After calming anger during a heated argument, you realize peace and freedom are available now, not only after some distant change.
vishnu_gita::669.insight: This verse shifts your focus from waiting for freedom after death to recognizing it in your current mental steadiness.

vishnu_gita::670.verse_sanskrit:
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानाषमानयोः ॥
vishnu_gita::670.verse_hindi: केवल जितेन्द्रिय और प्रशांत अर्थात रागादिशून्य व्यक्ति का आत्मा अर्थात अंत:करण शीत उष्ण, सुख दुःख, और मान अपमान में अचल रह सकता है
vishnu_gita::670.english_translation: The supreme self is established in the mind of the self-controlled and peaceful person, remaining steady amid heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor.
vishnu_gita::670.translation_literal: जितात्मनः (self-controlled person) / प्रशान्तस्य (peaceful) / परमात्मा (supreme self) / समाहितः (established) / शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु (in cold, heat, pleasure, pain) / तथा (also) / मानाषमानयोः (in honor and dishonor)
vishnu_gita::670.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::670.essence: True calm holds steady through all life's ups and downs.
vishnu_gita::670.simple_meaning: If your mind is peaceful and your senses controlled, you remain steady through all changes and challenges.
vishnu_gita::670.simple_insight: You feel safe knowing your calm isn’t shaken by ups or downs.
vishnu_gita::670.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when a person masters their senses and calms the mind, their inner self stays balanced despite external hardships like temperature changes or social approval and rejection.
vishnu_gita::670.modern_relevance: You face unexpected feedback at work or shifting moods in relationships but remain grounded and unshaken inside.
vishnu_gita::670.insight: It teaches you to keep your inner state unmoved by external fluctuations, creating mental balance.

vishnu_gita::671.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः।
मुक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
vishnu_gita::671.verse_hindi: जिसका चित्त ज्ञान और विज्ञान द्वारा आकांक्षाहीन है जो कूटस्थ अर्थात् निर्विकार है, वह जितेन्द्रिय है और जिसकी मिटटी के ढेले में, पत्थर में और सुवर्ण में समदृष्टि है ऐसा योगी मुक्त कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::671.english_translation: A yogi whose mind is fulfilled with knowledge and wisdom, steady and unaffected, who has conquered the senses, and who sees clay, stones, and gold alike is called free.
vishnu_gita::671.translation_literal: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा (mind fulfilled with knowledge and wisdom) / कूटस्थो (steady, unaffected) / विजितेन्द्रियः (conquered senses) / मुक्त (free) / इत्युच्यते (is called) / योगी (yogi) / समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः (seeing clay, stones, and gold alike)
vishnu_gita::671.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::671.essence: True freedom comes from steady wisdom and equal vision beyond the senses.
vishnu_gita::671.simple_meaning: You are free when your mind is calm from clear understanding, you control your senses, and see all things without preference.
vishnu_gita::671.simple_insight: There's peace in seeing everything without favor, beyond restless desires or distractions.
vishnu_gita::671.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the yogi whose mind is satisfied by knowledge and wisdom, who remains steady and unchanged, having conquered the senses. This yogi sees all things—clay, stones, gold—as equal and is called free at this moment of teaching.
vishnu_gita::671.modern_relevance: You encounter situations where your mind races with desires or judgments. Finding calm and equal regard for all things brings true freedom.
vishnu_gita::671.insight: It teaches you to steady your mind through wisdom and resist sensory distractions, seeing beyond surface value.

vishnu_gita::672.verse_hindi: सुहृत् ( स्वभावतः हितैषी) मित्र ( स्नेहवशतः हितैषी ) अरि (धातुक) उदासीन (विवाद करने वाले दोनों पक्षों की उपेक्षा करने वाला) मध्यस्थ (विवाद करने वाले दोनों पक्षों का हितैषी) द्वेष्य (द्वेष करने योग्य व्यक्ति) बन्धु (सम्बन्ध युक्त व्यक्ति) साधु और यहां तक कि पापियों पर भी जो समबुद्धि रखने वाला है वही योगियों में  प्रधान है
vishnu_gita::672.english_translation: Among friends, well-wishers, neutrals, enemies, relatives, saints, and even sinners, the yogi who has equal wisdom stands supreme.
vishnu_gita::672.translation_literal: सुहृत् (well-wisher) / मित्र (friend) / अरि (enemy) / उदासीन (indifferent) / मध्यस्थ (mediator) / द्वेष्य (one deserving hatred) / बन्धु (relative) / साधु (saint) / पापि (sinner) / समबुद्धिः (equal-mindedness) / विशिष्यते (stands superior)
vishnu_gita::672.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::672.essence: True wisdom treats friend and foe alike without preference or aversion.
vishnu_gita::672.simple_meaning: A yogi who sees friends, enemies, relatives, saints, and sinners with equal wisdom is the highest among them.
vishnu_gita::672.simple_insight: You feel peace when you treat everyone with the same steady mind.
vishnu_gita::672.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a yogi who maintains equal vision towards all—friends, enemies, neutrals, and even sinners—is the one who truly excels, demonstrating the power of unbiased wisdom in the midst of conflict.
vishnu_gita::672.modern_relevance: When a colleague, friend, or stranger acts against you, your calm and equal mind keeps you steady and respected.
vishnu_gita::672.insight: It teaches you to hold your mind steady and unbiased toward all people, regardless of their relation to you.

vishnu_gita::673.verse_sanskrit:
मय्यासक्तमनस्का हि युजाना योगमाश्रिताः ।
यथा ज्ञास्यथ पूर्ण मां तथा शृणुत निश्चितम् ॥
vishnu_gita::673.verse_hindi: मुझमे आस्क्तिचित्त होकर, योग के आश्रय से अभ्यास करते हुए जिस प्रकार से मुझे पूर्णरूप से निश्चयपूर्वक जान सकोगे उनको सुनो
vishnu_gita::673.english_translation: By dedicating your mind to me and practicing yoga, you will surely come to know me fully; listen carefully.
vishnu_gita::673.translation_literal: मय्या (by me) आसक्त (attached) मनस्का (minded) हि (indeed) युजाना (practicing) योगम् (yoga) आश्रिताः (relying) । यथा (just as) ज्ञास्यथ (you will know) पूर्ण (fully) मां (me) तथा (thus) शृणुत (listen) निश्चितम् (certainly) ॥
vishnu_gita::673.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::673.essence: Focused devotion combined with yoga practice guarantees full knowing of the divine.
vishnu_gita::673.simple_meaning: When you focus your mind on the divine and practice devotion with yoga, you will come to fully know the true self. Listen carefully to this promise.
vishnu_gita::673.simple_insight: There is hope and certainty that sincere devotion reveals deep knowing.
vishnu_gita::673.detailed_meaning: Vishnu encourages the devotee to dedicate their mind and heart fully to him through yoga. This verse promises that such committed practice leads to complete knowledge of the divine, inviting careful attention to this assured outcome.
vishnu_gita::673.modern_relevance: You keep returning to a daily meditation or prayer, unsure if it works—this promises that steady focus will bring deep understanding.
vishnu_gita::673.insight: It teaches you to trust that steady heartfelt devotion naturally leads to clear knowledge of the true self.

vishnu_gita::674.verse_sanskrit:
जानं वोऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।
यज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::674.verse_hindi: मैं आपलोगों को विज्ञानसहित इस ज्ञान को सम्पूर्ण रूप से कहूँगा जिसके  जान लेने से जगत में फिर कुछ जानने का विषय अवशेष नहीं रहता है
vishnu_gita::674.english_translation: I will fully explain this knowledge with all its understanding, knowing which nothing else remains to be known in the world.
vishnu_gita::674.translation_literal: जानं (knowledge) वोऽहं (I) सविज्ञानमिदं (with all understanding, this) वक्ष्यामि (will speak) अशेषतः (completely) । यज्ञात्वा (knowing) नेह (here) भूयः (again) अन्यत् (other) ज्ञातव्यम् (to be known) अवशिष्यते (remains) ॥
vishnu_gita::674.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::674.essence: Complete understanding of this knowledge ends all further seeking.
vishnu_gita::674.simple_meaning: You can fully understand this knowledge with complete insight, after which nothing else is left to learn.
vishnu_gita::674.simple_insight: You feel a deep relief knowing this teaching covers all that truly matters.
vishnu_gita::674.detailed_meaning: Vishnu promises to explain a complete, perfect knowledge that, once understood, leaves no question unanswered in the world, inviting readiness for full wisdom.
vishnu_gita::674.modern_relevance: You find a guide who offers the one clear answer that resolves your restless search for meaning.
vishnu_gita::674.insight: It shifts your mind from partial knowledge to seeking the complete, unshakable truth.

vishnu_gita::675.verse_sanskrit:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये ।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥
vishnu_gita::675.verse_hindi: हजारों मनुष्यों में कोई एक सिद्धि के लिये यत्न करता है और अनेक यत्न  करने वाले सिद्धों मेले भी कोई एक वास्तवतः मेरे स्वरूप को जानता है
vishnu_gita::675.english_translation: Among thousands of humans, one strives for perfection, and among many who strive, only one truly knows my real nature.
vishnu_gita::675.translation_literal: मनुष्याणां (of humans) / सहस्रेषु (among thousands) / कश्चित् (someone) / यतति (strives) / सिद्धये (for perfection) / यतताम् अपि (even of those who strive) / सिद्धानाम् (of the perfected) / कश्चित् (someone) / माम् (me) / वेत्ति (knows) / तत्त्वतः (truly, in essence)
vishnu_gita::675.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::675.essence: Deep spiritual understanding is extremely rare, even among those who strive for it.
vishnu_gita::675.simple_meaning: Many try to reach perfection, but only a very few truly understand the divine nature deeply.
vishnu_gita::675.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that true understanding is rare and precious.
vishnu_gita::675.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that among countless people, only one genuinely strives for spiritual perfection, and among those who do, only one truly understands the divine essence. This highlights the rarity of deep spiritual insight during a vast human search.
vishnu_gita::675.modern_relevance: In a world full of advice and self-improvement, very few truly grasp the deeper essence behind their efforts.
vishnu_gita::675.insight: It teaches you to value genuine understanding over mere effort and to recognize true wisdom as rare.

vishnu_gita::676.verse_sanskrit:
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च ।
अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टया ॥
vishnu_gita::676.verse_hindi: पृथिवी जल तेज वायु आकाश मन बुद्धि और अहङ्कार इन आठ प्रकार के भेदों से युक्त मेरी प्रकृति है
vishnu_gita::676.english_translation: My nature is composed of eight distinct types: earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego.
vishnu_gita::676.translation_literal: भूमिरापोऽनलो (earth water fire) / वायुः (air) / खं (ether) / मनो (mind) / बुद्धिरेव (intellect indeed) / च (and) / अहङ्कार (ego) / इतीयं (these) / मे (my) / भिन्ना (divided) / प्रकृतिरष्टया (nature eightfold)
vishnu_gita::676.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::676.essence: Your nature is a composite of eight changing elements and faculties.
vishnu_gita::676.simple_meaning: Everything that makes up your nature includes five elements plus mind, intellect, and ego.
vishnu_gita::676.simple_insight: Understanding your makeup can help you see yourself beyond surface appearances.
vishnu_gita::676.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that his nature is composed of eight fundamental parts: the five physical elements plus the three inner faculties: mind (manas), intellect (buddhi), and ego (ahamkara). This explains the composite reality of beings and the natural world.
vishnu_gita::676.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed, remembering that your being includes shifting elements and thoughts can help you find perspective.
vishnu_gita::676.insight: This verse teaches you to recognize that your sense of self includes changing physical and mental components, not a fixed essence.

vishnu_gita::677.verse_sanskrit:
अपग्यमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृति वित मे पराम् ।
जीवभूतां मुपर्वाणो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥
vishnu_gita::677.verse_hindi: यह अपरानाम्नी है। हे देवगण ! इस अपरा प्रकृति से भिन्न मेरी परानाम्नी जीवस्वरूपा एक प्रकृति है ऐसा जानो, जिसके द्वारा यह जगत् धारण किया जाता है अर्थात् जो जगद्धारिका है
vishnu_gita::677.english_translation: This is the supreme subtle nature, distinct from the other nature, the living being, by which this world is sustained.
vishnu_gita::677.translation_literal: अपग्यमितः (subtle, supreme) तु (but) अन्यां (other) प्रकृति (nature) वित (distinct) मे (my) पराम् (supreme). जीवभूतां (living beings) मुपर्वाणः (supporter, sustainer) ययेत् (which supports) ध(by) धार्यते (is sustained) जगत् (the world).
vishnu_gita::677.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::677.essence: A subtle living essence distinct from nature sustains the entire world.
vishnu_gita::677.simple_meaning: Beyond the natural world, there is a living essence that supports and sustains everything you see.
vishnu_gita::677.simple_insight: You can trust that a living essence quietly holds everything steady beneath change.
vishnu_gita::677.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains two realities: the manifest natural world and a subtle living essence distinct from it. This living essence is the foundation that supports all beings and the universe itself, revealing a deeper sustaining force behind apparent change.
vishnu_gita::677.modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelming and unpredictable, this verse reminds you that beneath all chaos, a steady living essence supports everything you experience.
vishnu_gita::677.insight: It shifts your view from seeing only surface change to recognizing a deeper sustaining presence behind all life.

vishnu_gita::678.verse_sanskrit:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधार्यताम ।
अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः मलयस्तथा ॥
vishnu_gita::678.verse_hindi: इन्हीं दो प्रकार की मेरी प्रकृतियो से पंचभूतमय सकल जगत की उत्पत्ति हुई है ऐसा जानो, मैं सकल जगत का परमकारण स्वरूप और प्रलय स्थान हूँ
vishnu_gita::678.english_translation: Know that all beings arise from these two types of my natural energies; I am the origin and dissolution of the entire world.
vishnu_gita::678.translation_literal: एतद्योनिनि (from these origins) / भूतानि (beings) / सर्वाणीत्युपधार्यताम (all, thus understand) / अहं (I) / कृत्स्नस्य (of the entire) / जगतः (world) / प्रभवः (origin) / मलयस्तथा (and dissolution)
vishnu_gita::678.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::678.essence: All existence flows from and returns to the divine's two natural energies.
vishnu_gita::678.simple_meaning: Everything in the world comes from two energies of the divine, who is both the cause of creation and the place of dissolution.
vishnu_gita::678.simple_insight: You are part of a vast cycle, beginning and ending in the divine's energies.
vishnu_gita::678.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the entire world of five elements arises from two of his natural energies. He is both the source from which everything emerges and the place where everything dissolves, revealing his cosmic role beyond just creation.
vishnu_gita::678.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by change, remember that all things start and end in the same deeper energy within you.
vishnu_gita::678.insight: Recognize your life’s changes as part of a continuous flow from and back to the divine's energy.

vishnu_gita::679.verse_sanskrit:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत् किश्चिदस्ति दिवौकसः।।
माय सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
vishnu_gita::679.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! मुझसे परे और कुछ नहीं है। सूत्रमें मणियों के समान मुझमें यह समस्त जगत् आश्रित है।
vishnu_gita::679.english_translation: There is nothing beyond me, O divine beings. All this universe is woven in me like jewels on a thread.
vishnu_gita::679.translation_literal: मत्तः (from me) / परतरं (beyond) / नान्यत् (nothing else) / किश्चिदस्ति (exists) / दिवौकसः (O divine beings) / माय (in me) / सर्वमिदं (all this) / प्रोतं (woven) / सूत्रे (on a thread) / मणिगणा (jewels) / इव (like)
vishnu_gita::679.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::679.essence: Nothing exists beyond the divine presence that holds all things together like jewels on a thread.
vishnu_gita::679.simple_meaning: Nothing exists beyond the divine presence. The entire universe depends on this presence like jewels strung on a thread.
vishnu_gita::679.simple_insight: You are part of a divine whole where everything is connected and supported.
vishnu_gita::679.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, declaring that nothing surpasses his presence. The universe depends on him like precious jewels strung on a thread, emphasizing his all-encompassing nature and the interconnectedness of all things.
vishnu_gita::679.modern_relevance: When life feels fragmented or overwhelming, remember that everything you see and feel is connected and supported by a single unifying presence.
vishnu_gita::679.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing your inseparable connection with the whole.

vishnu_gita::680.verse_sanskrit:
इदं गुह्यतमं वश्चाऽनुसूयुभ्यो वेऽधुना ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज़ज्ञान्वा मोक्ष्यथाशुभात् ॥
vishnu_gita::680.verse_hindi: अब मैं यह परमगुप्त विज्ञान सहित ज्ञान भी तुम दोषदृष्टि हीनों को कहता हूँ जिसको जानकर तुमलोग सकल पापों से मुक्त हो जाओगे
vishnu_gita::680.english_translation: Now I reveal this most secret knowledge combined with clear understanding to you free from envy, by knowing which you will be freed from all wrongdoing.
vishnu_gita::680.translation_literal: इदं (this) / गुह्यतमं (most secret) / वश्चाऽनुसूयुभ्यो (and to those free from envy) / वेऽधुना (now) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / विज्ञानसहितं (combined with clear understanding) / यज़ज्ञान्वा (by knowing) / मोक्ष्यथाशुभात् (you will be freed from wrongdoing).
vishnu_gita::680.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::680.essence: Knowing secret wisdom with clear understanding frees you from all harmful actions.
vishnu_gita::680.simple_meaning: You are given the deepest secret knowledge combined with clear understanding, which frees you from all harmful actions.
vishnu_gita::680.simple_insight: You feel hopeful knowing that understanding this knowledge can protect you from harm.
vishnu_gita::680.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses those who are free from envy, offering them the most secret wisdom combined with clear understanding. This knowledge promises liberation from all harmful actions, marking a turning point in the teaching.
vishnu_gita::680.modern_relevance: You discover a hidden insight that clears confusion and stops you from repeating harmful mistakes.
vishnu_gita::680.insight: It encourages you to embrace clear understanding as the key to freeing yourself from harmful patterns.

vishnu_gita::681.verse_sanskrit:
इदं शरीरं भो देवाः! क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।
एतद्यो वेत्ति तं पाहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
vishnu_gita::681.verse_hindi: हे देवगण यह शरीर क्षेत्र नाम से अभिहित होता है और इस क्षेत्र को जो जानता है उसको तत्त्वज्ञानी क्षेत्रज्ञ कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::681.english_translation: O divine beings, this body is called the field, and the one who knows this field is called the knower of the field.
vishnu_gita::681.translation_literal: इदं (this) शरीरं (body) भो (O) देवाः (divine beings)! क्षेत्रमिति (field-called) अभिधीयते (is named). एतद् (this) यः (who) वेत्ति (knows) तं (that) पाहुः (is called) क्षेत्रज्ञ (knower of field) इति (thus) तद्विदः (wise).
vishnu_gita::681.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::681.essence: You are the conscious knower distinct from your physical body.
vishnu_gita::681.simple_meaning: Your body is like a field, and the true self is the one who observes and knows this field.
vishnu_gita::681.simple_insight: You are not just your body; you are the conscious observer within it.
vishnu_gita::681.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that the body is called the field, and the wise are those who know the body as separate from the observer, the knower of the field. This sets the stage for understanding self and body as distinct.
vishnu_gita::681.modern_relevance: When you pause and notice your body, you realize that you are the awareness behind the sensations, not just the physical form.
vishnu_gita::681.insight: It teaches you to shift your identity from the body to the conscious awareness that observes it.

vishnu_gita::682.verse_sanskrit:
क्षेत्रज्ञं चाऽपि मां वित्त सर्वक्षेत्रेषु निर्जगः।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज़ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥
vishnu_gita::682.verse_hindi: और हे देवगण ! सब क्षेत्रों में भी मुझको क्षेत्रज्ञ जानो । क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ का जो ज्ञान है वह ज्ञान मेरा अभिमत है
vishnu_gita::682.english_translation: And O divine beings! Know Me as the knower of all fields. The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field is considered My wisdom.
vishnu_gita::682.translation_literal: क्षेत्रज्ञं (knower of the field) / चाऽपि (also) / मां (Me) / वित्त (know) / सर्वक्षेत्रेषु (in all fields) / निर्जगः (O divine beings) । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोः (of field and knower of the field) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / यत् (which) / तज्ज्ञानं (that knowledge) / मतं (opinion) / मम (Mine) ॥
vishnu_gita::682.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::682.essence: You are the observer behind all experiences; that knowing is true wisdom.
vishnu_gita::682.simple_meaning: You are the observer of every aspect of life. Recognizing this is true wisdom.
vishnu_gita::682.simple_insight: You can find peace by realizing you witness all experiences without being caught in them.
vishnu_gita::682.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu addresses divine beings, explaining that he is the knower behind every domain of experience—the field and its knower. This teaching reveals the inner observer that perceives the body and mind, emphasizing wisdom as knowing this distinction.
vishnu_gita::682.modern_relevance: When you pause and watch your thoughts and feelings without getting swept away, you connect with the part of you that observes everything calmly.
vishnu_gita::682.insight: This verse shifts your perspective to seeing yourself as the observer, not just the doer or experiencer.

vishnu_gita::683.verse_sanskrit:
तत् क्षेत्रं यच्च याहक च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।
स च यो यत्मभावश्च तच्छृणुध्वं समासतः ॥
vishnu_gita::683.verse_hindi: जो क्षेत्र है वह जो है जैसा है जिन जिन विकारों से युक्त है और जिससे उत्पन्न है एवं वह क्षेत्र भी जो है और जिस प्रभाव का है वह संक्षेप से सुनो
vishnu_gita::683.english_translation: Listen briefly to the field, what it is, its qualities, and its transformations.
vishnu_gita::683.translation_literal: तत् (that) / क्षेत्रं (field) / यच्च (and what) / याहक (qualities) / च (also) / यद्विकारि (transformations) / यतश्च (and from which) / यत् (what) / । (.) / स (that) / च (also) / यो (whose) / यत्मभावश्च (influence/state) / तच्छृणुध्वं (listen) / समासतः (briefly)
vishnu_gita::683.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::683.essence: Understanding the nature and changes of the field is the foundation for wisdom.
vishnu_gita::683.simple_meaning: The verse invites you to understand the nature of the field, its qualities, and how it changes, including what it comes from and what influences it.
vishnu_gita::683.simple_insight: Understanding the environment and its changes helps prepare you for deeper teachings ahead.
vishnu_gita::683.detailed_meaning: This verse serves as an introduction to the explanation of 'the field'—the body, mind, and nature—its qualities, changes, and origin. It sets the stage for deeper philosophical discussion by asking the listener to pay close attention.
vishnu_gita::683.insight: It prepares your mind to observe and reflect on the nature and changes of your own experience.

vishnu_gita::684.verse_sanskrit:
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक ।
ब्रह्मसूत्र पदैश्चैव हेतुमाद्भिर्विनिश्चितै: ॥
vishnu_gita::684.verse_hindi: जो ऋषियों से ब्रह्मसूत्र के पदों से और युक्तियुक्त तथा विनिश्चित पृथक् पृथक विविध वैदिक मन्त्रों से अनेक  प्रकार से निरूपित है (उसको संक्षेप से कहता हूँ )
vishnu_gita::684.english_translation: The teaching is presented many ways by sages, through varied Vedic hymns and clear, reasoned Brahmasutra passages.
vishnu_gita::684.translation_literal: ऋषिभिः (by sages) बहुधा (in many ways) गीतं (taught) छन्दोभिः (by hymns) विविधैः (varied) पृथक् (separately) ब्रह्मसूत्र (Brahmasutra) पदैः (passages) च (and) ऐव (indeed) हेतुमाद्भिः (by reasoned arguments) विनिश्चितैः (certain/definite)
vishnu_gita::684.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::684.essence: Timeless wisdom appears in many forms but can be clearly summarized.
vishnu_gita::684.simple_meaning: The teachings have been explained by sages in many ways, using different Vedic hymns and clear logical Brahmasutra arguments.
vishnu_gita::684.simple_insight: Wisdom is vast and varied, yet can be summarized clearly.
vishnu_gita::684.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that the wisdom about the supreme reality has been taught by many sages through diverse Vedic hymns and confirmed by the precise, reasoned statements in the Brahmasutras. This verse introduces a summary of that vast knowledge.
vishnu_gita::684.insight: Recognize that deep truths can be expressed through many methods yet point to one essence.

vishnu_gita::685.verse_sanskrit:
महाभूतान्यहंकारो बुद्धिरव्यक्त मेंव च ।
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकञ्च पञ्च चन्द्रियगोचराः ॥
vishnu_gita::685.verse_hindi: पंच पृथिव्यादि महाभूत, अहङ्कार, बुद्धि, मूल प्रकृति, दश इन्द्रियां एक मन और इन्द्रियों के विषय (शब्दस्पर्शादि ) पंच तन्मात्रा
vishnu_gita::685.english_translation: The five great elements, the ego, the intellect, the unmanifest root nature, the ten senses, the one mind, and the five objects of the senses.
vishnu_gita::685.translation_literal: महाभूतानि (five great elements) / अहंकारः (ego) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / अव्यक्तः (unmanifest) / में च (and also) / इन्द्रियाणि (senses) / दशैकञ्च (ten and one) / पञ्च (five) / चन्द्रियगोचराः (objects of senses)
vishnu_gita::685.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::685.essence: Your existence is a union of elements, mind, ego, and senses forming a complex whole.
vishnu_gita::685.simple_meaning: Your true self includes the five elements, ego, intellect, root nature, mind, senses, and their objects.
vishnu_gita::685.simple_insight: You are not just a mind or body but a vast combination of nature and awareness.
vishnu_gita::685.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the components that form the manifest and subtle universe: elements, ego, intellect, root nature, mind, senses, and sensory objects, outlining the complex makeup of existence to Arjuna.
vishnu_gita::685.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your thoughts and surroundings, remember you are composed of many layers beyond just your mind and body.
vishnu_gita::685.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as more than immediate experiences, understanding the layered composition of your being.

vishnu_gita::686.verse_sanskrit:
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं संघातश्चेतना धृतिः ।
एतत् क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::686.verse_hindi: इच्छा, द्वेष, सुख, दुःख, संघात (शरीर), चेतना (मनोवृत्ति) और धैर्य यह विकारयुक्त क्षेत्र संक्षेप से  कहा गया है
vishnu_gita::686.english_translation: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, bodily union, consciousness, and perseverance together briefly define the field of change.
vishnu_gita::686.translation_literal: इच्छा (desire) / द्वेषः (aversion) / सुखं (pleasure) / दुःखं (pain) / संघातः (union) / चेतना (consciousness) / धृतिः (steadiness) / एतत् (this) / क्षेत्रं (field) / समासेन (by compound) / सविकारम् (with modifications) / उद्धृतम् (declared)
vishnu_gita::686.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::686.essence: Your experience is a field shaped by desire, pain, and steady awareness.
vishnu_gita::686.simple_meaning: The body and mind together form a field marked by desires, aversions, joys, pains, and steady effort.
vishnu_gita::686.simple_insight: Recognizing these changing feelings helps you see your experience as a shifting field, not a fixed self.
vishnu_gita::686.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the body and mind create a field of experience defined by desires, dislikes, happiness, sorrow, bodily union, consciousness, and perseverance. This moment introduces the complex nature of changing mental and physical states in living beings.
vishnu_gita::686.modern_relevance: You notice how your moods, wants, and pains make your day feel unstable, like a field always shifting beneath your feet.
vishnu_gita::686.insight: It teaches you to observe desires and feelings as parts of a changing field, reducing identification with them.

vishnu_gita::687.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञेयं यत्ततप्रवक्ष्यामि यजज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते ।
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::687.verse_hindi: जो ज्ञेय है उसको कहूँगा जिसको जानकर (साधक) मोक्ष प्राप्त करता है। वह  अनादि परब्रह्म सत् भी नहीं कहे गये हैं और असत् भी नहीं कहे गये हैं
vishnu_gita::687.english_translation: I will explain what must be known, by knowing which the seeker attains freedom. It is the eternal supreme reality, neither called existence nor non-existence.
vishnu_gita::687.translation_literal: ज्ञेयं (to be known) यत् (that) तत् (that) प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will explain) यज (by which) अज्ञात्वा (knowing) अमृतम् (immortality) अश्नुते (attains) । अनादिमत् (without beginning) परम् (supreme) ब्रह्म (ultimate reality) न (not) सत्त् (existence) न (nor) आसत् (non-existence) उच्यते (called) ॥
vishnu_gita::687.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::687.essence: Ultimate reality transcends all labels of existence and non-existence.
vishnu_gita::687.simple_meaning: There is a supreme truth to know that leads to freedom. It is eternal and cannot be described simply as existence or non-existence.
vishnu_gita::687.simple_insight: Freedom comes from knowing a truth beyond ordinary categories of existence.
vishnu_gita::687.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the highest truth, the supreme reality, is beyond all dual labels like existence and non-existence. Knowing this truth leads the seeker to ultimate freedom.
vishnu_gita::687.modern_relevance: When you face impossible questions about what is real, you can find peace knowing some truths are beyond simple labels.
vishnu_gita::687.insight: It shifts your mind beyond limited categories to embrace a boundless reality.

vishnu_gita::688.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत् सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ।
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
vishnu_gita::688.verse_hindi: वह ( ब्रह्म) सर्वत्र पाणि, पाद, नेत्र, मस्तक, मुख और कर्ण विशिष्ट होकर संसार में सबको आवृत करके ठहरे हुए है
vishnu_gita::688.english_translation: The supreme reality pervades everywhere with hands, feet, eyes, head, mouth, and ears, covering and sustaining all in the world.
vishnu_gita::688.translation_literal: सर्वतः (everywhere) पाणिपादं (hands and feet) तत् (that) सर्वतः (everywhere) अक्षि-शिरो-मुखम् (eyes, head, mouth) सर्वतः (everywhere) श्रुतिम् (ears/hearing) अल्लोके (in the world) सर्वम् (all) आवृत्य (covering) तिष्ठति (stands/remains)
vishnu_gita::688.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::688.essence: The supreme reality pervades everything, sustaining all through every part.
vishnu_gita::688.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is present everywhere through all limbs and senses, covering and sustaining the entire world.
vishnu_gita::688.simple_insight: Everything you see and hear is touched and held by the supreme presence everywhere.
vishnu_gita::688.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu describes the supreme reality as present everywhere through all limbs and senses, indicating how the divine pervades the entire world, sustaining and enveloping all beings within creation.
vishnu_gita::688.insight: This verse shifts your view to see the divine presence as intimately involved in every part of existence, not distant or separate.

vishnu_gita::689.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं  सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम ।
असक्तं सबभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्त च ॥
vishnu_gita::689.verse_hindi: वह सभी  इन्द्रियों के गुणों के आभास से विशिष्ट, सब इन्द्रियों से रहित, संगशून्य, सभी के आधारभूत, गुणो से रहित और गुणों के भोक्ता हैं
vishnu_gita::689.english_translation: He is distinct from all qualities perceived by the senses, devoid of all senses, unattached, the foundation of all, beyond qualities, and the experiencer of qualities.
vishnu_gita::689.translation_literal: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं (all-senses-qualities-appearance) / सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम (all-senses-devoid) / असक्तं (unattached) / सबभृच्चैव (all-basis-only) / निर्गुणं (without-quality) / गुणभोक्त (qualities-experiencer) / च (and)
vishnu_gita::689.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::689.essence: The true self is beyond qualities yet witnesses and experiences them without attachment.
vishnu_gita::689.simple_meaning: You are separate from the qualities sensed by the body and mind. You do not cling to anything but are the foundation that experiences all qualities.
vishnu_gita::689.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing you are not defined by changing qualities but still aware of them.
vishnu_gita::689.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the true self as beyond all senses and their qualities. This self is unattached and serves as the underlying support that experiences qualities without being affected by them. It teaches the difference between the changing world and the stable observer.
vishnu_gita::689.modern_relevance: When you're overwhelmed by your emotions or thoughts, this reminds you that your true self is beyond those shifting states yet aware of them.
vishnu_gita::689.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with passing qualities to recognizing yourself as the steady experiencer behind them.

vishnu_gita::690.verse_sanskrit:
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च ।
मूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च यता॥
vishnu_gita::690.verse_hindi: जो जीवों के बाहर और भीतर है, चर भी हैं और अचर भी हैं, सूक्ष्म होने के कारण अविज्ञेय हैं तथा जो दूर भी हैं और समीप भी हैं
vishnu_gita::690.english_translation: What exists outside and inside beings, both moving and unmoving, is subtle and beyond perception; it is both distant and near.
vishnu_gita::690.translation_literal: बहिरन्तश्च (outside beings) भूतानाम् (of beings) अचरं (unmoving) चरमेव (and moving indeed) च (and) । मूक्ष्मत्वात् (due to subtlety) तद् (that) अविज्ञेयं (unperceivable) दूरस्थं (distant) च (and) अन्तिके (near) च (and) यता (because).
vishnu_gita::690.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::690.essence: You are part of a subtle, unperceivable reality that is both near and far.
vishnu_gita::690.simple_meaning: Everything that exists inside and outside living beings, whether moving or still, is subtle and cannot be directly perceived. It is present both near and far.
vishnu_gita::690.simple_insight: There is a comforting vastness in knowing you share a connection with all that exists, seen and unseen.
vishnu_gita::690.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that all beings encompass what is moving and unmoving, both inside and outside themselves. This reality is so subtle it cannot be grasped by normal perception, yet it is both distant and close, revealing a profound unity.
vishnu_gita::690.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated or separate, remember that what you truly are is connected to everything subtle and vast, near and far.
vishnu_gita::690.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing a subtle, inseparable connection with all existence.

vishnu_gita::691.verse_sanskrit:
अविभक्तञ्च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
vishnu_gita::691.verse_hindi: जो भूतों में अविभक्त होने पर भी विभक्त की भांति अवस्थित हैं और वह प्राणियों के पालक, संहारक तथा उत्पादक भी हैं ऐसा जानना चाहिए
vishnu_gita::691.english_translation: The divine is indivisible within beings yet appears divided; it is the sustainer, destroyer, and creator of all beings.
vishnu_gita::691.translation_literal: अविभक्तञ्च (undivided) भूतेषु (in beings) विभक्तमिव (as if divided) च (also) स्थितम् (exists) । भूतभर्तृ (beings' sustainer) च (and) तज्ज्ञेयं (that should be known) ग्रसिष्णु (destroyer) प्रभविष्णु (creator) च (also) ॥
vishnu_gita::691.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::691.essence: The true self is indivisible yet appears as many in the world.
vishnu_gita::691.simple_meaning: The divine presence is both indivisible and appears divided in all beings; it sustains, destroys, and creates all life.
vishnu_gita::691.simple_insight: You are part of a unity that seems separate, yet is truly whole and connected.
vishnu_gita::691.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that although the divine presence appears divided among all beings, it is actually undivided and unified. This presence sustains, destroys, and creates life, showing its all-encompassing nature beyond appearances.
vishnu_gita::691.modern_relevance: In moments of conflict or division, you can remember that beneath appearances, everything is connected and whole.
vishnu_gita::691.insight: It shifts perception from seeing separation to recognizing underlying unity in all forms.

vishnu_gita::692.verse_sanskrit:
ज्योतिपामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते ।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हदि सर्वस्य धिष्ठितम् ॥
vishnu_gita::692.verse_hindi: वह ज्योतियों की भी ज्योति है और अज्ञान से परे स्थित कहे जाते हैं तथा वे ज्ञान, ज्ञेय, ज्ञान से  प्राप्त करने योग्य और सबके हृदय में अवस्थित हैं
vishnu_gita::692.english_translation: That is the light beyond all lights and beyond darkness; it is knowledge, the object of knowledge, attainable by knowledge, and dwells in every heart.
vishnu_gita::692.translation_literal: ज्योतिपामपि (even than many lights) तज्ज्योतिः (that light) तमसः (of darkness) परम् (supreme) उच्यते (is called) । ज्ञानं (knowledge) ज्ञेयं (object of knowledge) ज्ञानगम्यं (attainable by knowledge) हदि (in the heart) सर्वस्य (of all) धिष्ठितम् (resides) ॥
vishnu_gita::692.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::692.essence: The highest knowledge shines beyond all darkness and dwells within every heart.
vishnu_gita::692.simple_meaning: There is a supreme light beyond all ordinary lights and darkness. This light is true knowledge, the goal and means of understanding, and it lives in every heart.
vishnu_gita::692.simple_insight: You can find the highest knowledge already present within yourself, beyond all confusion and darkness.
vishnu_gita::692.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a supreme light that surpasses all others and darkness itself. This light symbolizes the highest knowledge, which is both the object to be known and the means to know it, residing in every being’s heart.
vishnu_gita::692.modern_relevance: When you feel lost in confusion or overwhelmed by information, remember the deepest clarity is already within you, waiting to be recognized.
vishnu_gita::692.insight: It shifts your focus from seeking knowledge outside to realizing knowledge is present inside, making inner exploration the true path.

vishnu_gita::693.verse_sanskrit:
इति क्षेत्र तथा ज्ञानं शेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मदावायोपपद्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::693.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार से क्षेत्र, ज्ञान और ज्ञेय संक्षेप से कहे गये । मेरा भक्त इनको जानकर ब्रह्मत्व प्राप्ति के योग्य होता है
vishnu_gita::693.english_translation: Thus, the field, the knower, and the known have been briefly explained; my devotee, knowing these, attains the state of supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::693.translation_literal: इति (thus) क्षेत्र (field) तथा (and) ज्ञानं (knowledge) शेयं (knower) च (and) उक्तं (spoken) समासतः (briefly) । मद्भक्त (my devotee) एतद्विज्ञाय (knowing this) मदावायोपपद्यते (attains the supreme reality) ॥
vishnu_gita::693.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::693.essence: Knowing the relationship of self, world, and awareness leads to supreme realization.
vishnu_gita::693.simple_meaning: Three key concepts — the field, the knower, and the known — have been summarized. Knowing them helps you reach the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::693.simple_insight: There is confidence in knowing that grasping these three reveals your highest nature.
vishnu_gita::693.detailed_meaning: Vishnu concludes a teaching by summarizing the three fundamental concepts in understanding existence: the field (body and world), the knower (the inner being), and the known (objects of perception). He tells his devotee that knowing these leads to realization of the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::693.modern_relevance: When faced with confusion about yourself and your experience, grasping these three simple ideas can bring clarity and peace.
vishnu_gita::693.insight: It shifts the mind to see reality as a relationship between self, experience, and awareness, opening the door to deeper understanding.

vishnu_gita::694.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृति पुरुषं चैव वित्तानादी उभावपि ।
विकाराँश्च गुणाँश्चैव वित्त प्रकृतिसम्भवान ॥
vishnu_gita::694.verse_hindi: प्रकृति और पुरुष इन दोनों को ही अनादि जानो और (देह इन्द्रिय आदि) विकार एवं ( सत्त्व आदि) गुणो को प्रकृति से उत्पन्न समझो।
vishnu_gita::694.english_translation: Know that both Purusha and Prakriti are without beginning; the modifications and qualities arise from Prakriti.
vishnu_gita::694.translation_literal: प्रकृति (nature) / पुरुषं (pure awareness) / चैव (also) / वित्तानादी (without beginning) / उभावपि (both) / विकाराँश्च (modifications) / गुणाँश्चैव (qualities also) / वित्त (without beginning) / प्रकृतिसम्भवान (originating from Prakriti)
vishnu_gita::694.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::694.essence: Pure awareness and nature are both eternal; change arises only from nature.
vishnu_gita::694.simple_meaning: Pure awareness and nature have no starting point. All changes and qualities come from nature alone.
vishnu_gita::694.simple_insight: You can feel stable knowing some things, like awareness, never began or change.
vishnu_gita::694.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the foundational metaphysics: Purusha is pure awareness, eternal without origin; Prakriti is nature, also without beginning. But all changes and qualities arise only from Prakriti. This sets the stage for understanding the eternal self versus the changing world.
vishnu_gita::694.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic or uncertain, knowing that your true awareness has no beginning or end can bring deep calm amid constant change.
vishnu_gita::694.insight: It shifts your view to see awareness as timeless and stable, separate from the ever-changing qualities around you.

vishnu_gita::695.verse_sanskrit:
कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिमच्यते।
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते !! ॥
vishnu_gita::695.verse_hindi: कार्य और कारण के कर्तृत्व में प्रकृति हेतु कही गई है और पुरुष सुख दुःखों के भोक्तृत्व में हेतु कहा गया है
vishnu_gita::695.english_translation: In the doership of action and cause, nature is called the cause; in experiencing pleasure and pain, the true self is called the cause.
vishnu_gita::695.translation_literal: कार्य (action) / कारण (cause) / कर्तृत्वे (in doership) / हेतुः (cause) / प्रकृतिम् (nature) / अच्यते (is said) । / पुरुषः (the true self) / सुखदुःखानां (of pleasure and pain) / भोक्तृत्वे (in experiencing) / हेतुः (cause) / उच्यते (is called) ॥
vishnu_gita::695.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::695.essence: Nature acts as cause, while your true self simply experiences pleasure and pain.
