vishnu_gita::695.simple_meaning: Nature causes your actions, but your true self experiences their effects like pleasure and pain.
vishnu_gita::695.simple_insight: You can see yourself as the experiencer, not the doer, which eases self-blame and attachment.
vishnu_gita::695.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the natural world (Prakriti) performs all actions and causes, while the true self (Purusha) is the one who experiences the results of pleasure and pain. This distinction helps Arjuna understand his role as a witness rather than a doer.
vishnu_gita::695.modern_relevance: When you face success or failure, realize your efforts were part of conditions beyond you; you simply experience the results.
vishnu_gita::695.insight: It shifts your view from blaming yourself for outcomes to recognizing your role as the receiver of experience.

vishnu_gita::696.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुष: प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुन्ज्य्ते प्रकृतिजान गुणान ।
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु  ॥
vishnu_gita::696.verse_hindi: क्योंकि पुरुष प्रकृतिस्थ होकर प्रकृति से उत्पन्न सब गुणों को भोगता है किन्तु इस पुरुष के सत् एवं असत् योनियो में जन्म होने का कारण गुणों (सत्त्व आदि) का सङ्ग है
vishnu_gita::696.english_translation: The true self dwells in the natural world and experiences its qualities; the cause of births in the realms of existence and non-existence is attachment to these qualities.
vishnu_gita::696.translation_literal: पुरुष: (the true self) प्रकृतिस्थो (situated in nature) हि (indeed) भुन्ज्य्ते (enjoys/experiences) प्रकृतिजान (nature-born) गुणान (qualities) । कारणं (cause) गुणसङ्गोऽस्य (attachment to qualities of this) सदसद्योनिजन्मसु (in births of existence and non-existence) ॥
vishnu_gita::696.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::696.essence: Attachment to nature’s qualities causes repeated births of being and non-being.
vishnu_gita::696.simple_meaning: The true self lives within the natural world and experiences its qualities, but being attached to these qualities leads to repeated births in different realms.
vishnu_gita::696.simple_insight: Knowing that attachment to changing qualities causes ongoing cycles of birth brings clarity and relief.
vishnu_gita::696.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that the true self (Purusha) resides within the natural world (Prakriti) and experiences its qualities like sattva, rajas, and tamas. However, birth into existence or non-existence arises because of attachment to these qualities, causing the cycle of rebirth.
vishnu_gita::696.modern_relevance: You notice how clinging to moods, habits, or roles keeps pulling you back into old patterns and restless cycles.
vishnu_gita::696.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with qualities to seeing attachment as the root cause of repeated reactivity.

vishnu_gita::697.verse_sanskrit:
उपद्रष्टानुऽमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन् पुरुषः परः ॥
vishnu_gita::697.verse_hindi: इस देह में (वर्तमान भी) पुरुष (इससे) परे अर्थात् पृथक् हैं क्योंकि वह साक्षिमात्र, अनुग्रहकर्ता, पोषणकर्ता, प्रतिपालक और महेश्वर हैं
vishnu_gita::697.english_translation: In this body, the true self is distinct and beyond, as the mere witness, guide, sustainer, protector, and supreme controller.
vishnu_gita::697.translation_literal: उपद्रष्टान् (the mere witness) / अमन्ता (the guide) / च (and) / भर्ता (the sustainer) / भोक्ता (the experiencer) / महेश्वरः (the supreme controller) / परमात्मेति (called the supreme self) / च अपि (also) / उक्तः (said) / देहे (in the body) / अस्मिन् (this) / पुरुषः (the true self) / परः (beyond, distinct)
vishnu_gita::697.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::697.essence: Your true self is the silent witness beyond your body and its experiences.
vishnu_gita::697.simple_meaning: You are not the body but the true self inside who watches, guides, and sustains all experience.
vishnu_gita::697.simple_insight: You can feel the calm of being a silent observer beyond physical form.
vishnu_gita::697.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu explains that the true self within is separate from the body; it is the witness and protector beyond physical experience, establishing the foundation for understanding inner being.
vishnu_gita::697.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by stress or identity struggles, remember you are more than your body or roles—you are the calm observer inside.
vishnu_gita::697.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with the body to recognizing your presence as the silent witness and guide.

vishnu_gita::698.verse_sanskrit:
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुष प्रकृतिञ्च गुणैः सह ।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
vishnu_gita::698.verse_hindi: जो इस प्रकार से पुरुष को और गुणों के साथ प्रकृति को जानता है वह किसी प्रकार से अथवा किसी अवस्था में वर्तमान रहने पर भी पुनर्जन्म ग्रहण नहीं करता है।
vishnu_gita::698.english_translation: One who thus knows the true self and the natural world with its qualities, though present in all states, is never reborn again.
vishnu_gita::698.translation_literal: य (who) / एवं (thus) / वेत्ति (knows) / पुरुष (the true self) / प्रकृतिं च (and natural world) / गुणैः सह (with qualities) / सर्वथा (in all ways) / वर्तमानः अपि (though present) / न (not) / स (that one) / भूयोऽभिजायते (is reborn again)
vishnu_gita::698.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::698.essence: Knowing the true self along with nature frees you from being born again.
vishnu_gita::698.simple_meaning: If you understand the true self and the natural world together, even while living in any state, you will not be born again.
vishnu_gita::698.simple_insight: There is freedom in truly knowing yourself beyond all changing conditions.
vishnu_gita::698.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that recognizing the distinction and relationship between the eternal true self and the changing natural world enables one to remain free from the cycle of rebirth despite being present in all life states.
vishnu_gita::698.modern_relevance: You can face every part of your life fully aware, yet not be trapped by repeated patterns or old identities.
vishnu_gita::698.insight: It teaches you to see your true self beyond all changing qualities and conditions, ending repeated rebirth.

vishnu_gita::699.verse_sanskrit:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना ।
अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरं ॥
vishnu_gita::699.verse_hindi: कोई कोई ध्यानयोग से आत्मा को बुद्धि के द्वारा देह में देखते हैं, अन्य कोई ज्ञानयोग के द्वारा और कोई (निष्काम) कर्मयोग के द्वारा आत्मा को देखते हैं।
vishnu_gita::699.english_translation: Some see the true self within the body through meditation, others through wisdom, and some through selfless action.
vishnu_gita::699.translation_literal: ध्यानेन (by meditation) आत्मनि (in the self) पश्यन्ति (see) केचिद (some) आत्मानम् (the true self) आत्मना (by the self) । अन्ये (others) सांख्येन (by wisdom) योगेन (by yoga) कर्मयोगेन (by selfless action) च (and) अपरं (different) ॥
vishnu_gita::699.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::699.essence: Your true self can be known through meditation, wisdom, or selfless action.
vishnu_gita::699.simple_meaning: You can realize your true self in different ways: through focused meditation, clear wisdom, or by acting without desire for results.
vishnu_gita::699.simple_insight: There is no single way to see your true self; many paths lead there.
vishnu_gita::699.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to seekers that the true self can be experienced through different yogas—some use meditation to quiet the mind, others use wisdom to understand the self, and some engage in selfless action to realize it.
vishnu_gita::699.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by choices, remember that quiet reflection, clear understanding, or dedicated service can all help you connect with who you really are.
vishnu_gita::699.insight: It opens your mind to accept multiple valid approaches for inner realization, encouraging flexibility in practice.

vishnu_gita::700.verse_sanskrit:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते ।
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्यु श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
vishnu_gita::700.verse_hindi: किन्तु अन्य कोई कोई इस प्रकार से अर्थात सांख्ययोग आदि के द्वारा आत्मा को नहीं जानते हुए अन्य अर्थात् गुरु आचार्य आदि से सुनकर उपासना करते हैं वह भी श्रुतिपरायण होकर मृत्यु को अतिक्रमण करते ही हैं
vishnu_gita::700.english_translation: Others, not knowing the true self through direct experience, worship based on what they have heard from teachers; even they overcome death by faithfully following the scripture.
vishnu_gita::700.translation_literal: अन्ये (others) त्व (indeed) एव (only) अमजानन्तः (not knowing) श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य (upon hearing from others) उपासते (worship) । तेऽपि (they also) च (indeed) अतितरन्ति (surpass) एव (certainly) मृत्यु (death) श्रुतिपरायणाः (devoted to scripture) ॥
vishnu_gita::700.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::700.essence: Trusting and practicing teachings heard from others can still lead beyond death.
vishnu_gita::700.simple_meaning: Some people don’t directly realize their true self but follow teachings they’ve heard from teachers. Even this devotion helps them overcome death.
vishnu_gita::700.simple_insight: Faith in teachings, even without direct experience, can still bring profound transformation.
vishnu_gita::700.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that not everyone attains self-knowledge through direct insight like Sankhya yoga. Many worship based on what they've heard from teachers or scriptures. Despite lacking direct experience, their sincere devotion to the teachings helps them transcend death’s finality.
vishnu_gita::700.modern_relevance: You might not fully understand a spiritual truth yourself but following trusted guidance with faith can still transform your life deeply.
vishnu_gita::700.insight: It teaches you to value sincere devotion to teachings, even without full direct understanding.

vishnu_gita::701.verse_sanskrit:
यावत्संजायते किञ्चित् सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात् तद्वित्त विबुधर्षभाः !॥
vishnu_gita::701.verse_hindi: हे देवश्रेष्ठों ! जो कुछ स्थावर या जंगम जीव उत्पन्न होते हैं वे सब क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ के संयोग से त्पन्न होते हैं सो जानो
vishnu_gita::701.english_translation: O best of the divine beings, all that arises—whether immovable or moving life—comes from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
vishnu_gita::701.translation_literal: यावत्संजायते (all that arises) / किञ्चित् (anything) / सत्त्वं (being) / स्थावरजङ्गमम् (immovable and movable) / क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात् (from the union of field and knower of the field) / तद्वित्त (know that) / विबुधर्षभाः (best of the wise)
vishnu_gita::701.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::701.essence: All existence arises from the union of the physical and the conscious knower.
vishnu_gita::701.simple_meaning: All living and non-living things come into being because of the connection between the physical body and the consciousness that knows it.
vishnu_gita::701.simple_insight: You are not just your body; life arises from the meeting of body and awareness.
vishnu_gita::701.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to the divine assembly that everything—whether fixed or moving—comes from the interaction of the physical field (body) and the conscious knower. This foundational idea reveals the source of existence as a relationship, not a single entity.
vishnu_gita::701.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or limited by your body or thoughts, remember that life arises from their union, not just from one part alone.
vishnu_gita::701.insight: This verse shifts focus from identifying as only the body or mind to recognizing the dynamic relationship that creates experience.

vishnu_gita::702.verse_sanskrit:
समं सर्चषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::702.verse_hindi: सब जीवों में संभाव से अवस्थित और सब जीवों के विनाश होते रहने पर भी अविनाशी जो परमात्मा हैं उनको जो देखता है वही देखता है।
vishnu_gita::702.english_translation: One who sees the supreme being as equal in all beings, existing permanently yet witnessing their destruction, truly sees.
vishnu_gita::702.translation_literal: समं (equal) सर्चषु (in all beings) भूतेषु (beings) तिष्ठन्तं (standing/existing) परमेश्वरम् (supreme being) । विनश्यत् (perishing) स्वविनश्यन्तं (yet not perishing) यः (who) पश्यति (sees) स (that one) पश्यति (sees) ॥
vishnu_gita::702.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::702.essence: True seeing is recognizing the unchanging divine equally present in all beings despite their changes.
vishnu_gita::702.simple_meaning: The supreme being exists equally in every being, unchanged despite their birth and death. Seeing this is true vision.
vishnu_gita::702.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing the divine you see never truly fades or changes.
vishnu_gita::702.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that the supreme being is present equally in all living beings. Though living beings undergo birth and death, the supreme being remains undestroyed. Recognizing this truth is the highest vision.
vishnu_gita::702.modern_relevance: When you see everyone as equally connected to something unchanging, judgments soften and compassion grows naturally.
vishnu_gita::702.insight: It shifts your vision from seeing only change and loss to perceiving an unchanging presence in all.

vishnu_gita::703.verse_sanskrit:
सम पश्च्यन ही सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम   
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
vishnu_gita::703.verse_hindi: क्योंकि सब भूतों में समभाव से अवस्थित परमात्मा को देखता हुआ साधक अपने से अपने को हनन नहीं करता है इसलिये वह परागति अर्थात् मुक्ति को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::703.english_translation: Seeing the supreme being equally present in all beings, the practitioner does not harm the self, and thus attains the highest freedom.
vishnu_gita::703.translation_literal: सम (equally) / पश्च्यन् (seeing) / हि (indeed) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / समवस्थित (equally established) / ईश्वरम् (the supreme being) / न (not) / हिनस्ति (kills/hurts) / आत्मनात्मानं (self by self) / ततो (thereafter) / याति (attains) / परां (supreme) / गतिम् (state/destination)
vishnu_gita::703.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::703.essence: Seeing the divine equally in all stops inner harm and leads to supreme freedom.
vishnu_gita::703.simple_meaning: When you recognize the divine equally in everyone, you stop hurting yourself and reach the highest freedom.
vishnu_gita::703.simple_insight: Feeling connected to all life frees you from self-damage and inner conflict.
vishnu_gita::703.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that seeing the supreme being equally present in every creature prevents self-harm. The practitioner who holds this vision avoids actions that damage their own true self and thus attains liberation.
vishnu_gita::703.modern_relevance: In moments of conflict, realizing others share your true nature can stop you from self-destructive reactions.
vishnu_gita::703.insight: This verse guides you to view all beings as one, shifting behavior from self-harm to self-care.

vishnu_gita::704.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::704.verse_hindi: प्रकृति ही सब प्रकार के कार्यों को करती है और आत्मा अकर्ता है, इस प्रकार जो देखता है वही देखता है
vishnu_gita::704.english_translation: All actions are performed by the natural world; the true self sees itself as not the doer.
vishnu_gita::704.translation_literal: प्रकृत्यैव (by nature itself) / च (and) / कर्माणि (actions) / क्रियमाणानि (being done) / सर्वशः (completely) / यः (who) / पश्यति (sees) / तत् (that) / आत्मानम् (the true self) / अकर्तारं (non-doer) / स (that) / पश्यति (sees)
vishnu_gita::704.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::704.essence: The true self is the silent witness while nature performs all actions.
vishnu_gita::704.simple_meaning: All actions happen through the natural world, while your true self remains detached as the observer, not the doer.
vishnu_gita::704.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing your true self is not responsible for every action.
vishnu_gita::704.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that every action is driven by the natural world (Prakriti), while the true self (Atman) remains uninvolved as the doer. Recognizing this helps Arjuna see beyond personal identification with actions.
vishnu_gita::704.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by responsibilities, remember that many forces beyond your control shape outcomes; your core self remains untouched.
vishnu_gita::704.insight: Shift your mind from identifying as the doer to observing actions as natural processes beyond personal control.

vishnu_gita::705.verse_sanskrit:
यदा भूतपृथगभावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति ।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
vishnu_gita::705.verse_hindi: जब भूतो के पृथक भाव को एकस्थ अर्थात् एक हीं ब्रह्म में अवस्थित देखता है और उसी एक से भूतों का विस्तार देखता है तब वह ब्रह्म हो जाता है
vishnu_gita::705.english_translation: When someone sees the separate existence of beings as one and the vastness of all beings in that one, then they become the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::705.translation_literal: यदा (when) / भूत (beings) / पृथकभावम् (separate existence) / एकस्थ (in one place) / अनुपश्यति (sees) / तत् (that) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / विस्तारं (expanse) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सम्पद्यते (becomes) / तदा (then)
vishnu_gita::705.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::705.essence: True self-realization comes from seeing all beings as one unified whole.
vishnu_gita::705.simple_meaning: You realize the supreme reality when you see that all beings are expressions of one unity.
vishnu_gita::705.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing everything as connected and arising from one source.
vishnu_gita::705.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when someone perceives the separate beings as a unified presence and simultaneously perceives the vast diversity as arising from that unity, they attain union with the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::705.modern_relevance: When you stop seeing others as separate and instead recognize your shared essence, conflicts and loneliness soften.
vishnu_gita::705.insight: Shift your perception from separation to unity; this changes your sense of self and connection.

vishnu_gita::706.verse_sanskrit:
अनादित्वानिर्गुणत्वात् परमात्मायमव्ययः।
शरीरस्थोऽपि भो देवाः ! न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::706.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! यह परमात्मा अनादि और निर्गुण होने के कारण अविकारी हैं इसलिये शरीर में रहने पर भी न करते हैं और न फलों से लिप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::706.english_translation: O radiant beings, the supreme reality is beginningless and without qualities; residing in the body, it neither acts nor is attached to the results.
vishnu_gita::706.translation_literal: अनादित्वात् (from beginninglessness) निर्गुणत्वात् (from absence of qualities) परमात्माय (to the supreme reality) अमव्ययः (indestructible) शरीरस्थः अपि (though residing in the body) भो (O) देवाः (radiant beings) न (not) करोति (acts) न (not) लिप्यते (is attached)
vishnu_gita::706.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::706.essence: The eternal self within you acts not and is never attached to outcomes.
vishnu_gita::706.simple_meaning: The supreme reality inside your body is eternal, without qualities, does not act, nor does it get attached to outcomes.
vishnu_gita::706.simple_insight: You are more than your actions or their results; a part remains untouched and free.
vishnu_gita::706.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that the supreme reality is beginningless and beyond qualities. Though it dwells in the body, it does not perform actions nor becomes bound by their results, revealing a fundamental distinction between the eternal self and the changing body-mind.
vishnu_gita::706.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your roles and results, remember there is a part of you untouched and free inside.
vishnu_gita::706.insight: Recognize the difference between your eternal true self and the temporary actions and attachments of your body.

vishnu_gita::707.verse_sanskrit:
यथा सर्वगतं सौम्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते ।
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::707.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार सभी मे विद्यमान आकाश सूक्ष्म होने के कारण लिप्त नहीं होता है उसी प्रकार देह में सर्वत्र अवस्थित परमात्मा (देह धर्म से) लिप्त नहीं होते हैं
vishnu_gita::707.english_translation: Just as the all-pervading sky remains untouched by anything subtle, the true self present throughout the body is not tainted by the body.
vishnu_gita::707.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / सर्वगतं (all-pervading) / सौम्यादाकाशं (gentle sky) / नोपलिप्यते (is not tainted) / सर्वत्रावस्थितो (present everywhere) / देहे (in the body) / तथात्मा (thus the self) / नोपलिप्यते (is not tainted)
vishnu_gita::707.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::707.essence: Your true self pervades your body but remains untouched by it.
vishnu_gita::707.simple_meaning: Your true self is everywhere in your body but remains pure and unaffected by it.
vishnu_gita::707.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your essence stays clear despite all physical changes.
vishnu_gita::707.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that just as the sky, though everywhere, remains untouched by anything subtle, similarly the true self within the body exists everywhere but is not affected or stained by the body's nature or changes.
vishnu_gita::707.modern_relevance: You notice your thoughts and feelings arise and pass, yet the core of who you are feels steady and untouched.
vishnu_gita::707.insight: It teaches you to see your inner being as separate from the body’s fluctuations and remain unaffected by them.

vishnu_gita::708.verse_sanskrit:
यथा प्रकाशयत्येक: कृत्सनं लोकमिम रवि: ।
क्षेत्र क्षेत्री तथा कृत्सनं प्रकाशयति निर्जरा ! ॥
vishnu_gita::708.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! जिस प्रकार एक सूर्य इस सम्पूर्ण लोक को प्रकाशित करता है उसी प्रकार क्षेत्री अर्थात् क्षेत्र आत्मा सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्र अर्थात् महाभूतादि विशिष्ट शरीरों को प्रकाशित करता है
vishnu_gita::708.english_translation: Just as one sun illuminates the entire world, similarly the knower of the field illuminates all bodies composed of elements.
vishnu_gita::708.translation_literal: यथा (just as) प्रकाशयति (illuminates) एक: (one) कृत्सनं (entire) लोकमिम (this world) रवि: (sun) । क्षेत्र (field) क्षेत्री (knower of field) तथा (similarly) कृत्सनं (entire) प्रकाशयति (illuminates) निर्जरा (bodies without decay) ।
vishnu_gita::708.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::708.essence: Your true self lights up your entire being just as one sun lights the world.
vishnu_gita::708.simple_meaning: The true self within you shines through your body just as the sun lights the whole world.
vishnu_gita::708.simple_insight: You can feel the relief that your inner being is the light behind all your experiences.
vishnu_gita::708.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu explains how the true self (the knower of the field) illuminates all the bodies made of elements, just like a single sun lights the entire world. This moment teaches that your inner being is the source of awareness.
vishnu_gita::708.modern_relevance: When you feel scattered or lost, remembering that your true self shines through all your experience can steady your mind.
vishnu_gita::708.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with the body to recognizing the true self as the illuminator within.

vishnu_gita::709.verse_sanskrit:
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमंतरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षश्च ये विर्दुयान्ति ते परम ॥
vishnu_gita::709.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार से जो क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ का प्रभेद एवं जीवों की प्रकृति से मुक्ति ज्ञान नेत्र से जानते हैं वह परमपद को प्राप्त होते हैं
vishnu_gita::709.english_translation: Those who clearly distinguish the field and the knower of the field with the eye of knowledge, and who understand freedom from the nature of beings, attain the supreme state.
vishnu_gita::709.translation_literal: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोः (field and knower of field) एवम् (thus) अंतरं (difference) ज्ञानचक्षुषा (with knowledge-eye) भूतप्रकृतिम् (nature of beings) मोक्षः (freedom) च (and) ये (those who) वि-र्दुयान्ति (discern) ते (they) परम (supreme)
vishnu_gita::709.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::709.essence: True freedom arises from seeing the difference between the observer and the observed.
vishnu_gita::709.simple_meaning: You become free when you understand the difference between the changing world and the one who observes it.
vishnu_gita::709.simple_insight: There’s peace in realizing you are the observer, not the changing things around you.
vishnu_gita::709.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that understanding the distinction between the physical world (the field) and the conscious observer (the knower) leads to liberation from the cycle of change and confusion.
vishnu_gita::709.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by emotions or thoughts, recognizing you are the observer—not the feelings—can bring calm and freedom.
vishnu_gita::709.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with change to resting as the witness, reducing reactivity.

vishnu_gita::710.verse_sanskrit:
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥
vishnu_gita::710.verse_hindi: मैं पुनः सब ज्ञानों में उत्तम परम ज्ञान अर्थात् परमात्म सम्बन्धी ज्ञान कहूँगा जिसको जानकर सब मुनिगण इस देह बन्धन से (मुक्त होकर) परा सिद्धि अर्थात् मोक्ष को प्राप्त हुए हैं।
vishnu_gita::710.english_translation: I will now declare the supreme knowledge beyond all knowledge, which, when known by sages, leads them beyond the body’s bondage to the highest accomplishment.
vishnu_gita::710.translation_literal: परं (supreme) भूयः (again) प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will declare) ज्ञानानां (of knowledges) ज्ञानमुत्तमम् (the highest knowledge) । यज्ज्ञात्वा (knowing which) मुनयः (sages) सर्वे (all) परां (supreme) सिद्धिमितो (to the utmost accomplishment) गताः (have gone) ॥
vishnu_gita::710.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::710.essence: Knowing the supreme knowledge frees you beyond bodily limitation to highest accomplishment.
vishnu_gita::710.simple_meaning: There is a supreme knowledge beyond all others. Knowing it frees sages from the body and grants the highest achievement.
vishnu_gita::710.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of being free beyond your physical self and limits.
vishnu_gita::710.detailed_meaning: Vishnu prepares to reveal a profound teaching—an ultimate knowledge that surpasses all other knowledge. He explains that sages who understand this truth transcend their bodily limitations and reach the highest spiritual goal.
vishnu_gita::710.modern_relevance: When you discover a truth that changes how you see yourself, it can free you from the limits you feel every day.
vishnu_gita::710.insight: It shifts your view from limited identity to a limitless state beyond the body and mind.

vishnu_gita::711.verse_sanskrit:
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः।
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
vishnu_gita::711.verse_hindi: इस ज्ञान को पाकर मेरे स्वरूपत्व को प्राप्त होते हुए वह  मुनिगण सृष्टिकाल में भी उत्पन्न नहीं होते और न प्रलयकाल में प्रलय का  दुःख अनुभव करते हैं
vishnu_gita::711.english_translation: Those who take refuge in this knowledge and attain likeness to me are not born at creation nor distressed at dissolution.
vishnu_gita::711.translation_literal: इदं (this) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / उपाश्रित्य (taking refuge in) / मम (my) / साधर्म्यमागताः (attaining likeness) / सर्गेऽपि (even at creation) / न (not) / उपजायन्ते (are born) / प्रलये (at dissolution) / न (not) / व्यथन्ति (are distressed) / च (also)
vishnu_gita::711.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::711.essence: True knowledge aligns you with the divine, freeing you from birth and death.
vishnu_gita::711.simple_meaning: Those who deeply grasp this knowledge and become like the divine are not reborn nor shaken by destruction.
vishnu_gita::711.simple_insight: Knowing your true nature brings calm beyond birth and death's cycles.
vishnu_gita::711.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that those who fully embrace his knowledge and align with his nature transcend the usual cycles of rebirth and decay, remaining untroubled during creation and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::711.modern_relevance: You face endings and new beginnings in life, but understanding your true self can keep you steady through all transitions.
vishnu_gita::711.insight: It shifts your view from fearing change to seeing yourself as beyond birth and loss.

vishnu_gita::712.verse_sanskrit:
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भ दधाम्यहं ।
सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवाति निन्जर्राः ! ॥
vishnu_gita::712.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! महद्ब्रह्म अर्थात् मूलप्रकृति मेरी योनि अर्थात गर्भाधान का स्थान  है, उसी में मैं गर्भाधान करता हूँ उससे सब भूतों की अर्थात् ब्रह्मा आदि की उत्पत्ति होती है।
vishnu_gita::712.english_translation: O divine beings, the great Brahman is my source; in it I place the seed, from which all beings arise and then dissolve.
vishnu_gita::712.translation_literal: मम (my) योनिः (source/womb) महत्-ब्रह्म (great Brahman) तस्मिन् (in that) गर्भ (seed/embryo) दधामि (I place) अहं (I). सम्भवः (origin) सर्व-भूतानाम् (of all beings) ततः (from that) भवाति (arises) निन्जराः (then dissolve).
vishnu_gita::712.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::712.essence: All beings arise and dissolve from one supreme source where creation begins.
vishnu_gita::712.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is the source where I place the seed of creation, from which all beings come and later dissolve.
vishnu_gita::712.simple_insight: Creation and dissolution emerge naturally from one original source beyond form.
vishnu_gita::712.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses divine beings explaining that the supreme reality is the primal source where he plants the seed of all creation, from which every being arises and ultimately returns.
vishnu_gita::712.insight: It shifts understanding from separate beings to a single source that births and absorbs all existence.

vishnu_gita::713.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वयोनिषु भो देवाः ! मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥
vishnu_gita::713.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! सब योनियों में जो स्थावर जङ्गम रूपी मूर्तियां उत्पन्न होती हैं महद्ब्रह्म अर्थात् मूलप्रकृति उनकी योनि अर्थात् मातृस्थानीय है और मैं बीजप्रद गर्भाधान कर्ता पिता हूँ
vishnu_gita::713.english_translation: O radiant beings, all forms that arise in every source come from the great Brahman, the primal nature, and I am the seed-giving father.
vishnu_gita::713.translation_literal: सर्वयोनिषु (in all sources) भो (O) देवाः (radiant beings) ! मूर्तयः (forms) सम्भवन्ति (arise) याः (which)। तासां (of those) ब्रह्म (Brahman) महद् (great) योनि (source) अहं (I) बीजप्रदः (seed-giving) पिता (father) ॥
vishnu_gita::713.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::713.essence: All forms arise from the primal nature; I am the seed-giving originator.
vishnu_gita::713.simple_meaning: All forms in the world come from the great primal nature, and I am the source that initiates their creation.
vishnu_gita::713.simple_insight: There is a deep origin from which all forms arise, and a source that begins it all.
vishnu_gita::713.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, explaining that every form in existence—whether fixed or moving—springs from the great Brahman, the primal nature. He declares himself the seed-giving originator who initiates their coming into being.
vishnu_gita::713.insight: Recognize that all diverse forms have a common origin and a source that initiates manifestation.

vishnu_gita::714.verse_sanskrit:
पंचैतानि सुरश्रेष्ठा ! कारणानि निबोधत ।
सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥
vishnu_gita::714.verse_hindi: हे सुरश्रेष्ठो! सभी कर्मों की सिद्धि के लिये ज्ञान प्रतिपादक शास्त्र में कहे हुए वक्ष्यमाण पांच कारणों को जानो
vishnu_gita::714.english_translation: O best of the Devas! Understand the five causes explained in the wisdom teachings that lead to the perfection of all actions.
vishnu_gita::714.translation_literal: पंचैतानि (these five) / सुरश्रेष्ठा (O best of the Devas) / कारणानि (causes) / निबोधत (understand) / सांख्ये (in the Sankhya wisdom) / कृतान्ते (at the end or conclusion) / प्रोक्तानि (explained) / सिद्धये (for the perfection) / सर्वकर्मणाम् (of all actions)
vishnu_gita::714.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::714.essence: Understanding five fundamental causes unlocks the perfection of all actions.
vishnu_gita::714.simple_meaning: There are five important causes explained in wisdom teachings that lead to success in all actions.
vishnu_gita::714.simple_insight: Knowing key causes gives you confidence to act without confusion.
vishnu_gita::714.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the best of the Devas about five fundamental causes described in Sankhya philosophy that explain how all actions reach their achievement. This sets the stage for understanding the roots of karma perfection.
vishnu_gita::714.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by choices, knowing the core reasons behind your actions can clear confusion and point you forward.
vishnu_gita::714.insight: It teaches you to look deeper at fundamental causes behind your actions rather than just their effects.

vishnu_gita::715.verse_sanskrit:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणञ्च पृथग्विधम् ।
विविधाश्च पृथक चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
vishnu_gita::715.verse_hindi: इस संसार में अधिष्ठान शरीर कर्ता अहङ्कार अनेक प्रकार के करण चक्षुरादि इन्द्रियां नानाविध चेष्टा अर्थात् प्राण अपान आदि की क्रियाएँ और देव पाचवां है
vishnu_gita::715.english_translation: In this world, the foundation is the body; the doer is the sense of ego; the instruments are various; the senses are many kinds of activities; and the divine is the fifth.
vishnu_gita::715.translation_literal: अधिष्ठानं (foundation) तथा (also) कर्ता (doer) करणञ्च (instrument) पृथग्विधम् (different kinds) । विविधाश्च (various) पृथक (separate) चेष्टा (activities) दैवं (divine) चैवात्र (also here) पञ्चमम् (the fifth) ॥
vishnu_gita::715.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::715.essence: You are body, ego, senses, and beyond them, the divine support.
vishnu_gita::715.simple_meaning: The body is the base where action happens; the sense of ego feels like the doer; many instruments and senses perform different activities; beyond all these is the divine presence.
vishnu_gita::715.simple_insight: You can see yourself as body, ego, senses, and also as the divine that supports everything.
vishnu_gita::715.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains the layered nature of existence: the body is the foundation, ego (I-ness) is the doer, various organs and senses carry out actions, and beyond them all is the divine, which is the ultimate support.
vishnu_gita::715.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your thoughts, feelings, and actions, remember there is a deeper presence supporting you beyond your body and ego.
vishnu_gita::715.insight: Recognize your experience as multiple layers and shift attention from the ego-doer to the divine support behind all action.

vishnu_gita::716.verse_sanskrit:
शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत् कर्म प्रारभ्यते खलु ।
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चेते तस्य हेतवः ॥
vishnu_gita::716.verse_hindi: शरीर, वाक और मन द्वारा जो धर्म अथवा अधर्म कर्म किया जाता है, पूर्वोक्त ये ही पांच उसके हेतु हैं
vishnu_gita::716.english_translation: Action begins through body, speech, and mind; its cause is always one of five reasons, whether right or wrong.
vishnu_gita::716.translation_literal: शरीर (body) / वाङ् (speech) / मनोभिः (by mind) / यत् (that) / कर्म (action) / प्रारभ्यते (begins) / खलु (indeed) / न्याय्यं (right) / वा (or) / विपरीतं (wrong) / वा (or) / पञ्च (five) / एते (these) / तस्य (its) / हेतवः (causes)
vishnu_gita::716.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::716.essence: Every action arises through body, speech, or mind driven by five causes, right or wrong.
vishnu_gita::716.simple_meaning: All actions start through the body, speech, or mind and arise from five possible causes, whether right or wrong.
vishnu_gita::716.simple_insight: Understanding that your actions have clear sources helps you see their nature more clearly.
vishnu_gita::716.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that every action originates from one of three faculties—body, speech, or mind—and each action has one of five possible causes, either proper or improper, shaping its nature and consequences.
vishnu_gita::716.modern_relevance: You notice how your choices come from what you say, do, or think, influenced by clear reasons behind them.
vishnu_gita::716.insight: It helps you recognize which faculty—body, speech, or mind—is driving your actions and what motivates them.

vishnu_gita::717.verse_sanskrit:
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलन्तु यः।
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्याति दुर्मतिः ॥
vishnu_gita::717.verse_hindi: ऐसा होने पर उक्त विषय में जो व्यक्ति केवल (निःसङ्ग) आत्मा को कर्ता समझता है, अनिर्मल बुद्धि होने के कारण वह दुर्मति देख नहीं सकता है अर्थात् यथार्थदर्शी नहीं है
vishnu_gita::717.english_translation: When someone sees only the self as the doer in that situation, their impure mind prevents them from seeing the truth; such a person lacks clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::717.translation_literal: तत्रैवं (there thus) सति (being) कर्तारम् (doer) आत्मानं (self) केवलन्तु (only) यः (who) पश्यति (sees) अकृतबुद्धित्वान् (impure mind) न (not) स (he) पश्याति (sees) दुर्मतिः (wrong-mindedness/foolishness)
vishnu_gita::717.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::717.essence: Seeing only yourself as doer blocks clear understanding of reality.
vishnu_gita::717.simple_meaning: If you consider only your separate self as the doer, your mind becomes unclear and you fail to see the whole truth.
vishnu_gita::717.simple_insight: There is clarity when you recognize forces beyond just your personal doership.
vishnu_gita::717.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains that a person who sees only their self as the agent of action, ignoring other influences, has an impure mind. This blocks true understanding and causes flawed perception of reality.
vishnu_gita::717.modern_relevance: When you take full credit for events without seeing the bigger picture, you limit your understanding and cause frustration.
vishnu_gita::717.insight: It teaches you to broaden your view beyond personal ego as the sole doer to gain clear perception.

vishnu_gita::718.verse_sanskrit:
यस्य नाऽहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य लिप्यते।
हत्वाऽपि स न इमान् लोकान् न हन्ति न निवध्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::718.verse_hindi: जिसको “ मैं कर्ता हूँ" यह भाव नहीं है और  जिसकी बुद्धि (इष्टानिष्ट कर्म में ) लिप्त नहीं होती है वह इन सब लोको को नाश करके भी नहीं नाश करता है और बन्धन को प्राप्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::718.english_translation: One who has no sense of 'I am the doer' and whose mind is not attached to desired or undesired actions does not destroy these worlds even by killing, nor is bound.
vishnu_gita::718.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) न (not) अहंकृतः (egoistic-doer) भावः (feeling) बुद्धिः (intellect) यस्य (whose) लिप्यते (is attached)। हत्वा (having killed) अपि (even) सः (he) न (not) इमान् (these) लोकान् (worlds) न (not) हन्ति (destroys) न (not) निवध्यते (is bound) ॥
vishnu_gita::718.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::718.essence: Acting without ego or attachment means your deeds neither bind nor harm you.
vishnu_gita::718.simple_meaning: If you do not feel that you are the doer and your mind is not attached to outcomes, your actions do not bind or destroy you.
vishnu_gita::718.simple_insight: Freedom comes when you act without claiming ownership of your actions.
vishnu_gita::718.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when a person acts without ego—the feeling 'I am the doer'—and without attachment to the results, even acts like killing do not cause harm or bondage. This lesson comes as Arjuna struggles with the morality of battle, showing that detached action transcends binding consequences.
vishnu_gita::718.modern_relevance: You finished a difficult task without boasting or clinging to praise. You realize your effort is your own, not your identity.
vishnu_gita::718.insight: It shifts your mind from ownership of action to pure engagement without ego, freeing you from bondage to results.

vishnu_gita::719.verse_sanskrit:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगादिवौकसः।
अन्विच्छताश्रयं बुद्धौ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
vishnu_gita::719.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! ज्ञानयोग की अपेक्षा कर्मयोग अत्यंत ही निकृष्ट है इसलिये आपको ज्ञानयोग के आश्रय की इच्छा करनी चाहिए, फलके चाहने वाले व्यक्ति कृपण अर्थात् निकृष्ट होते हैं
vishnu_gita::719.english_translation: Action without wisdom is far inferior; those who desire only results are miserly and low.
vishnu_gita::719.translation_literal: दूरेण (far) हि (indeed) अवरं (inferior) कर्म (action) बुद्धियोगात् (from wisdom yoga) इव (like) औकसः (low persons) । अन्विच्छताः (desiring) आश्रयं (support) बुद्धौ (in wisdom) कृपणाः (miserly) फलहेतवः (motivated by fruit) ॥
vishnu_gita::719.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::719.essence: Acting only for outcomes is shallow; wisdom gives true depth to action.
vishnu_gita::719.simple_meaning: Actions done without wisdom are weak and lower; wanting only the reward shows smallness.
vishnu_gita::719.simple_insight: You gain freedom by valuing wisdom over chasing outcomes.
vishnu_gita::719.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine beings, teaching that action done without the guiding light of wisdom is inferior. Those who act only for outcomes lack generosity and depth. This moment urges turning toward wisdom yoga for true strength.
vishnu_gita::719.modern_relevance: You push hard to finish a task just for praise or bonus, but feel empty inside because the deeper meaning is missing.
vishnu_gita::719.insight: It shifts your focus from craving results to seeking understanding, enriching your actions.

vishnu_gita::720.verse_sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागृति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः॥
vishnu_gita::720.verse_hindi: अज्ञानाच्छन्न समस्त प्राणियों के लिये जो रात्रि है अर्थात् वह वे आत्मा को नहीं देख सकते हैं उस रात्रि में जितेन्द्रिय व्यक्ति जागता है अर्थात् आत्म साक्षात्कार करता है और जिस (विषयबुद्धि) में जीवगण जागते हैं अर्थात् जगत को सत्य अनुभव करते हैं वह आत्मतत्त्व दर्शी मुनि के लिये रात्रि के समान है अर्थात् उसकी विषयों की ओर दृष्टि नहीं रहती है
vishnu_gita::720.english_translation: For all beings, that which is ignorance is night; for the self-controlled, that same is awakening. Where beings are awake, that is night for the seer who perceives the true self.
vishnu_gita::720.translation_literal: या (which) निशा (night) सर्वभूतानां (of all beings) तस्यां (in that) जागृति (awakening) संयमी (self-controlled) यस्यां (in which) जाग्रति (are awake) भूतानि (beings) सा (that) निशा (night) पश्यतो (of the seer) मुनेः (sage)
vishnu_gita::720.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::720.essence: Your true awareness feels like awakening while others remain lost in ignorance.
vishnu_gita::720.simple_meaning: What feels like ignorance and darkness to most is awakening and clear seeing for the self-controlled seer.
vishnu_gita::720.simple_insight: You can find clarity when others are lost in confusion and darkness.
vishnu_gita::720.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that ignorance is like night for most beings, who cannot see the true self. But for the disciplined sage, this ignorance is replaced by awakening. Where others are active in worldly desires, the sage sees the truth and remains unaffected.
vishnu_gita::720.modern_relevance: When everyone around you seems confused or caught up in distractions, you can remain clear and aware of what truly matters.
vishnu_gita::720.insight: It shifts your perspective to recognize that your awareness may differ from the crowd’s perception, highlighting the value of self-control.

vishnu_gita::721.verse_sanskrit:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान् देवाः ! सर्वान् मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्ट: स्थितप्रज्ञस्यदोच्य्ते ॥
vishnu_gita::721.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! परमानन्द स्वरुप आत्मा में ही स्वयं तुष्ट होकर जब (योगी) मनोगत सम्पूर्ण कामनाओं का त्याग करता है तब वह स्थितप्रज्ञ कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::721.english_translation: When a yogi renounces all desires born in the mind and is satisfied in the true self alone, he is called a person of steady wisdom.
vishnu_gita::721.translation_literal: प्रजहाति (gives up) यदा (when) कामान् (desires) देवाः (gods) सर्वान् (all) मनोगतान् (arising in the mind) आत्मन्येव (in the self alone) आत्मना (by the self) तुष्ट: (satisfied) स्थितप्रज्ञस्य (of the steady wise) दोच्यते (is called)
vishnu_gita::721.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::721.essence: Steady wisdom arises when inner fulfillment replaces all desires.
vishnu_gita::721.simple_meaning: You become steady and wise when you let go of all desires and feel satisfied within your true self.
vishnu_gita::721.simple_insight: There is peace in being content inside without chasing every desire.
vishnu_gita::721.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when a yogi renounces all mental desires and rests happily in the true self, they attain the state of steady wisdom called 'sthitaprajna'. This teaching comes as guidance on cultivating detachment and inner contentment.
vishnu_gita::721.modern_relevance: After scrolling endlessly through wants and distractions, you pause and realize your calm center is enough.
vishnu_gita::721.insight: It teaches you to shift focus from chasing desires to embracing inner satisfaction as true strength.

vishnu_gita::722.verse_hindi: जिसका मन दुःखों में उद्विग्न नहीं होता है, सुखों में जिसकी स्पृहा नहीं है और जिसके राग, भय एवं क्रोध दूर होग ये हैं वह मुनि ‘स्थितधी' कहा जाता है
vishnu_gita::722.english_translation: A sage whose mind is undisturbed by pain, without craving in pleasure, free from attachment, fear, and anger is called steady-minded.
vishnu_gita::722.translation_literal: दु:खेषु (in sufferings) अनुद्विग्नमना: (mind not agitated) सुखेषु (in pleasures) विगतस्पृह: (craving gone) । वीतरागभयक्रोध: (free from attachment, fear, anger) स्थितधीर्मुनीरुच्यते (is called steady-minded) ॥
vishnu_gita::722.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::722.essence: True steadiness comes from freedom from craving, fear, and anger amid life's fluctuations.
vishnu_gita::722.simple_meaning: A person who does not get upset by pain, does not crave pleasure, and has let go of attachment, fear, and anger is steady-minded.
vishnu_gita::722.simple_insight: You can feel calm and balanced even when life brings ups and downs.
vishnu_gita::722.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu describes the ideal sage who remains mentally balanced despite pain or pleasure. Such a person has overcome emotional reactivity like attachment, fear, and anger, embodying steady wisdom.
vishnu_gita::722.modern_relevance: You face criticism or praise at work but your peace stays firm, untouched by external highs or lows.
vishnu_gita::722.insight: It teaches you to observe experiences without being pulled into craving or aversion, stabilizing your inner state.

vishnu_gita::723.verse_sanskrit:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत् प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।
नाभिनन्दात न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
vishnu_gita::723.verse_hindi: जो सब विषयों में ममता शून्य होकर उस उस शुभ और अशुभ को प्राप्त करके न आनन्दित होता है और न विषादयुक्त होता है उसकी प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठित होती है अर्थात् प्रकृष्टरूप से ब्रह्म में स्थित रहती है
vishnu_gita::723.english_translation: One whose wisdom is established neither clings to nor rejects good or bad experiences everywhere.
vishnu_gita::723.translation_literal: यः (who) सर्वत्र (everywhere) अनभिस्नेहः (without attachment) तत् (that) तत् (that) प्राप्य (having obtained) शुभाशुभम् (good and bad) न (not) अभिनन्दात (rejoices) न (nor) द्वेष्टि (hates) तस्य (his) प्रज्ञा (wisdom) प्रतिष्ठिता (established)
vishnu_gita::723.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::723.essence: True wisdom is steady in all experiences, neither drawn nor repelled.
vishnu_gita::723.simple_meaning: You can face every experience, good or bad, without clinging or pushing it away. This steady mind shows true wisdom.
vishnu_gita::723.simple_insight: There’s freedom in not needing to celebrate or reject what life brings.
vishnu_gita::723.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that true wisdom means being free from emotional attachment to any experience, good or bad. This steadiness means the mind is rooted beyond fleeting feelings and remains balanced in all situations.
vishnu_gita::723.modern_relevance: You receive praise or criticism at work but stay calm inside, neither overly proud nor upset.
vishnu_gita::723.insight: It teaches you to hold your attention steady, not pulled by attraction or aversion toward events.

vishnu_gita::724.verse_sanskrit:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभयस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठता ॥
vishnu_gita::724.verse_hindi: जब यह (योगी) इन्द्रियों के सभी विषयों से इन्द्रियों को, कछुपा जैसे अङ्गो को खींच लेता है उसी प्रकार सर्वथा खींच लेता है तब उसकी प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठित होती है।
vishnu_gita::724.english_translation: When a yogi withdraws the senses from their objects, just as a tortoise pulls its limbs inside, then his wisdom is firmly established.
vishnu_gita::724.translation_literal: यदा (when) संहरते (withdraws) च (also) आयं (these) कूर्मः (tortoise) अङ्गानि (limbs) इव (like) सर्वशः (completely) इन्द्रियाणि (senses) इन्द्रियार्थेभः (sense-objects) अस्य (his) प्रज्ञा (wisdom) प्रतिष्ठता (established)
vishnu_gita::724.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::724.essence: Withdrawing your senses from distractions stabilizes your wisdom like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs.
vishnu_gita::724.simple_meaning: When you consciously withdraw your senses from their distractions, your wisdom becomes steady and clear like a tortoise pulling its limbs inside.
vishnu_gita::724.simple_insight: There is calm and strength in retreating from distractions to your inner clarity.
vishnu_gita::724.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu compares a yogi’s control over senses to a tortoise withdrawing its limbs for safety. The yogi stops chasing sensory objects, which steadies his wisdom and mind amid distractions.
vishnu_gita::724.modern_relevance: When you stop checking your phone or social media and pull back from constant input, you create space for clear insight.
vishnu_gita::724.insight: It teaches you to redirect attention inward, away from external distractions, stabilizing your mind for wiser action.

vishnu_gita::725.verse_sanskrit:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।
रसवर्ज रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्त्तते ॥
vishnu_gita::725.verse_hindi: जो इन्द्रिय द्वारा विषय ग्रहण नहीं करता है ऐसे देहधारी व्यक्ति के विषय निवृत्त हो जाते हैं किन्तु भोगाभिलाषा निवृत्त नहीं होती है; परन्तु परमात्मा के साक्षात्कार होने पर उसकी वह विषयभोग की अभिलाषा भी निवृत्त हो जाती है
vishnu_gita::725.english_translation: Objects of sense withdraw from the embodied one who does not grasp them; yet desire for enjoyment remains; but upon realizing the supreme reality, even that desire subsides.
vishnu_gita::725.translation_literal: विषया (objects of senses) / विनिवर्तन्ते (withdraw) / निराहारस्य (without nourishment) / देहिनः (of the embodied one) / रसवर्ज (devoid of taste) / रसोऽप्यस्य (even the taste of that) / परं (the supreme) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / निवर्त्तते (ceases)
vishnu_gita::725.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::725.essence: You can resist pleasures but desire ends only by recognizing the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::725.simple_meaning: When you don’t seek sense pleasures, their pull lessens, but desire may still stay until you realize a deeper truth beyond them.
vishnu_gita::725.simple_insight: There’s relief in knowing that desire’s root fades only with higher understanding.
vishnu_gita::725.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a person who stops feeding senses with external objects experiences a fading of those objects’ allure. However, the deeper craving for enjoyment remains until one perceives the supreme reality, which finally ends all desire.
vishnu_gita::725.modern_relevance: You may avoid distractions like social media or junk food, yet still feel restless until you connect with something deeper within.
vishnu_gita::725.insight: It teaches you to distinguish between sensory avoidance and the deeper shift that ends desire through realization.

vishnu_gita::726.verse_sanskrit:
यततो ह्यपि हे देवाः ! साधकस्य विपश्चितः।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः॥
vishnu_gita::726.verse_hindi: क्योंकि हे देवगण ! यत्न करते हुए विद्वान् साधक के भी मन को प्रमाथी अर्थात् क्षोभ उत्पन्न करने वाले इन्द्रियगण हठात् खींच लेते हैं
vishnu_gita::726.english_translation: Even the wise practitioner struggles as restless senses suddenly pull the mind away.
vishnu_gita::726.translation_literal: यततो (striving) हि (indeed) अपि (even) हे (O) देवाः (gods) साधकस्य (of the practitioner) विपश्चितः (wise) इन्द्रियाणि (senses) प्रमाथीनि (restless) हरन्ति (carry away) प्रसभं (the mind) मनः (mind)
vishnu_gita::726.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::726.essence: Striving alone doesn’t stop restless senses from pulling your mind away.
vishnu_gita::726.simple_meaning: Even a wise person who strives can have their mind disturbed by restless senses.
vishnu_gita::726.simple_insight: You’re not alone when your focus breaks; this struggle is part of the path.
vishnu_gita::726.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that even a thoughtful practitioner faces sudden disruptions by the senses that pull the mind off course. This moment reveals the challenge in cultivating steady focus during spiritual practice.
vishnu_gita::726.modern_relevance: You sit to meditate, determined to focus, but distractions keep pulling your attention away unexpectedly.
vishnu_gita::726.insight: Recognize that restless senses will challenge your discipline; persistence is essential despite interruptions.

vishnu_gita::727.verse_sanskrit:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
vishnu_gita::727.verse_hindi: योगी को उन सभी इन्द्रियों को संयत करके आत्मपरायण होकर रहना चाहिए क्योंकि जिसकी इन्द्रियां वश में हैं उसकी प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठित है
vishnu_gita::727.english_translation: The yogi should control all the senses and be devoted to the inner being, for whose senses are controlled, wisdom is established.
vishnu_gita::727.translation_literal: तानि (those) / सर्वाणि (all) / संयम्य (controlling) / युक्त (joined) / आसीत (should be) / मत्परः (devoted to me) / वशे (under control) / हि (indeed) / यस्य (whose) / इन्द्रियाणि (senses) / तस्य (his) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / प्रतिष्ठिता (established)
vishnu_gita::727.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::727.essence: True wisdom arises when your senses are controlled and your focus is devoted inward.
vishnu_gita::727.simple_meaning: You should control all your senses and stay devoted to your true self; when your senses are under control, your wisdom becomes steady.
vishnu_gita::727.simple_insight: Feeling in control of your senses brings a calm inner confidence and clarity.
vishnu_gita::727.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a yogi must restrain all senses and focus devotion inward, because only when senses are disciplined does wisdom become firmly established. This teaching guides the seeker toward stable understanding amid distractions.
vishnu_gita::727.modern_relevance: You notice how distractions pull your attention in every direction—when you regain control, your clarity and confidence return.
vishnu_gita::727.insight: It teaches you to practice self-discipline over your senses so your discerning mind can stabilize and guide you.

vishnu_gita::728.verse_sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयानस्य सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्संजायते कामः कामात् क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
vishnu_gita::728.verse_hindi: विषयों की चिन्ता करने वाले  योगी की आसक्ति विषयों में होजाती है और आसक्ति से काम उत्पन्न होता है एवं काम से क्रोध उत्पन्न होता है
vishnu_gita::728.english_translation: Fixing the mind on objects causes attachment; attachment leads to desire; desire breeds anger.
vishnu_gita::728.translation_literal: ध्यायतो (fixing mind) विषयानस्य (on objects) सङ्गः (attachment) तेषु (in them) उपजायते (arises) । सङ्गात् (from attachment) संजायते (is born) कामः (desire) कामात् (from desire) क्रोधः (anger) अभिजायते (is born) ॥
vishnu_gita::728.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::728.essence: Focusing on objects triggers attachment, which leads to desire and then anger.
vishnu_gita::728.simple_meaning: When you focus your mind on external things, attachment grows. That attachment creates desire, which then leads to anger.
vishnu_gita::728.simple_insight: Recognizing how your focus leads from attachment to anger offers a chance to break the cycle.
vishnu_gita::728.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when a person constantly thinks about external objects, their mind becomes attached. This attachment naturally produces desire, and unchecked desire soon turns into anger, revealing a chain of emotional reactions.
vishnu_gita::728.modern_relevance: You scroll social media, obsessing over likes and comments; that fixation sparks craving and frustration when things don't go your way.
vishnu_gita::728.insight: It teaches you to notice how your mental focus creates emotional chains and to redirect your attention before attachment forms.

vishnu_gita::729.verse_sanskrit:
क्रोधात् भवति संमोहः संमोहात स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृति भ्रन्शादबुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात प्रणश्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::729.verse_hindi: क्रोध से सम्मोह होता है, सम्मोह से स्मृतिविभ्रम, स्मृति करे भ्रष्ट होने से बुद्धि का नाश और बुद्धि के नाश से जीव नष्ट हो जाता है अर्थात अत्यंत रूप से पतित हो जाता है
vishnu_gita::729.english_translation: Anger leads to confusion, confusion causes memory loss, memory loss destroys discernment, and without discernment, the being is lost.
vishnu_gita::729.translation_literal: क्रोधात् (from anger) भवति (arises) संमोहः (confusion) संमोहात् (from confusion) स्मृतिविभ्रमः (memory loss) स्मृति (memory) भ्रन्शाद् (from decay) बुद्धिनाशः (destruction of discernment) बुद्धिनाशात् (from destruction of discernment) प्रणश्यति (is destroyed)
vishnu_gita::729.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::729.essence: Anger initiates a chain that destroys mental clarity and leads to self-loss.
vishnu_gita::729.simple_meaning: Anger causes confusion, which leads to memory mistakes, destroying clear thinking, and ultimately causes loss of self-awareness.
vishnu_gita::729.simple_insight: You feel how anger can cloud your mind and let you lose yourself step by step.
vishnu_gita::729.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains how starting from anger, a chain reaction unfolds: confusion clouds the mind, memory falters, discernment breaks down, and finally the true self is lost.
vishnu_gita::729.modern_relevance: When you lose your temper during a stressful day, your thoughts scatter, making it hard to remember or decide clearly.
vishnu_gita::729.insight: It teaches you to recognize anger’s ripple effect that gradually erodes your mental clarity and self-control.

vishnu_gita::730.verse_hindi: किन्तु राग द्वेष से रहित आत्म वशीभूत इन्द्रियों क्र द्वारा विषयभोग करने पर जिसका मन वशीभूत है, ऐसा व्यक्ति आत्मप्रसाद अर्थात शान्तिलाभ करता है
vishnu_gita::730.english_translation: But one who, free from attachment and aversion, controls the senses and acts with a disciplined mind attains inner calm.
vishnu_gita::730.translation_literal: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैः (free from attachment and aversion) / तु (but) / विषयान् (objects) / इन्द्रियैः (with senses) / च (also) / रजन (acting) / आत्मवशयैव (with mind controlled by the self) / इधेयात्मा (obedient mind) / प्रसादम् (calmness) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
vishnu_gita::730.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::730.essence: Calm arises when you master senses free from craving and aversion.
vishnu_gita::730.simple_meaning: When you act without craving or dislike and keep your senses under control, your mind becomes calm and peaceful.
vishnu_gita::730.simple_insight: You can feel peace by mastering your desires and not reacting to what you like or dislike.
vishnu_gita::730.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person who has freed their mind from attachment (craving) and aversion (dislike), and who controls the senses instead of being controlled by them, achieves inner calm and clarity.
vishnu_gita::730.modern_relevance: You notice how peace slips away when your emotions pull you toward what you want or push you away from what you dislike. Learning to steady your mind brings lasting calm.
vishnu_gita::730.insight: It shifts your focus from being ruled by likes and dislikes to steady control over your senses, creating inner calm.

vishnu_gita::731.verse_sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्व्दु:खानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
vishnu_gita::731.verse_hindi: आत्मप्रसाद प्राप्त करने पर योगी के सब दुःख नष्ट हो जाते हैं क्योंकि प्रसन्नचित्त व्यक्ति की बुद्धि शीघ्र प्रतिष्ठित अर्थात् आत्मनिष्ठ हो जाती है
vishnu_gita::731.english_translation: When the inner being is delighted, all suffering fades; a serene mind quickly gains steady wisdom.
vishnu_gita::731.translation_literal: प्रसादे (in delight) / सर्व्दु:खानां (of all sufferings) / हानिरस्योपजायते (their loss arises) । / प्रसन्नचेतसो (of the serene mind) / ह्याशु (indeed quickly) / बुद्धिः (wisdom) / पर्यवतिष्ठते (is firmly established) ॥
vishnu_gita::731.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::731.essence: Inner delight dissolves suffering and quickly grounds steady wisdom in the mind.
vishnu_gita::731.simple_meaning: When your inner being is joyful and calm, all your suffering disappears because your mind settles into clear wisdom.
vishnu_gita::731.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing joy within can quiet pain and steady your mind.
vishnu_gita::731.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that when a yogi's inner being is delighted, their troubles vanish. This moment comes when the mind is serene, allowing wisdom to quickly settle deeply inside.
vishnu_gita::731.modern_relevance: You find a quiet moment of true joy, and suddenly your worries lose their grip, leaving your mind clear and steady.
vishnu_gita::731.insight: It teaches you to cultivate inner delight to dissolve suffering and stabilize your understanding.

vishnu_gita::732.verse_sanskrit:
नास्ति बुद्धि युक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
vishnu_gita::732.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म में अयुक्त व्यक्ति की आत्म विषयिणी बुद्धि नहीं होती है, अयुक्त व्यक्ति को भावना अर्थात् आत्मविषयक ध्यान भी नहीं होता है, आत्मध्यानविहीन व्यक्ति को शान्ति नहीं मिलती और शान्तिहीन व्यक्ति के लिये मोक्षानन्द रूप सुख कहाँ ?
vishnu_gita::732.english_translation: One without discerning mind lacks focused attention on the true self; without such attention, there is no peace; without peace, how can there be lasting happiness?
vishnu_gita::732.translation_literal: नास्ति (is not) बुद्धि (discerning mind) युक्तस्य (with) न (nor) च (and) आयुक्तस्य (without attachment) भावना (focused attention) । न (nor) चाभावयतः (without attention) शान्ति (peace) रशान्तस्य (of the unpeaceful) कुतः (where) सुखम् (happiness) ॥
vishnu_gita::732.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::732.essence: Without clear inner focus, peace and lasting happiness cannot arise.
vishnu_gita::732.simple_meaning: Without a clear, discerning mind focused on your true self, you cannot find peace, and without peace, lasting happiness is impossible.
vishnu_gita::732.simple_insight: You feel unsettled until your mind settles on your true self with steady attention.
vishnu_gita::732.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a person who lacks a discerning mind focused on their true self does not develop steady inner attention. Without this attention, peace cannot arise, and without peace, lasting happiness or freedom remains unattainable.
vishnu_gita::732.modern_relevance: When your mind is scattered and restless, no matter how hard you try, true calm or joy feels out of reach.
vishnu_gita::732.insight: It teaches you to cultivate steady attention on your true self as the foundation for inner peace and happiness.

vishnu_gita::733.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणा ही चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञा वायु वमिवाम्भसि ॥
vishnu_gita::733.verse_hindi: क्योंकि जिस प्रकार वायु असावधानी वश  कर्णधार वाली नौका को जल में डुबा देता है उसी प्रकार इन्द्रियां जिस ओर जाती हैं उसी ओर जो मन चला जाता है वह मन योगी की प्रज्ञा को (विषय में ) खींच लेता है
vishnu_gita::733.english_translation: Just as the wind carelessly overturns a boat with a helmsman, so the mind follows the senses, pulling the yogi's wisdom into worldly objects.
vishnu_gita::733.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणा (by the senses) / ही (only) / चरतां (moving) / यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते (where the mind follows) / तदस्य (of that) / हरति (carries away) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / वायु (wind) / वमिवाम्भसि (like a boat overturned by the wind)
vishnu_gita::733.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::733.essence: The mind blindly follows the senses, risking loss of steady wisdom like a boat overturned by wind.
vishnu_gita::733.simple_meaning: The mind follows the senses like a boat pushed by the wind, pulling your wisdom away from its steady course.
vishnu_gita::733.simple_insight: You feel how easily your focus can be swept away by distractions beyond your control.
vishnu_gita::733.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how the senses move outward, and the mind follows them without control, just like a boat overturned by the wind, risking the loss of steady wisdom for the yogi.
vishnu_gita::733.modern_relevance: You notice your attention slipping toward notifications, pulling you away from your calm focus and inner clarity.
vishnu_gita::733.insight: It teaches you to recognize the mind’s tendency to chase senses and to cultivate steady awareness despite distractions.

vishnu_gita::734.verse_sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य सुरश्रेष्ठाः : निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
vishnu_gita::734.verse_hindi: इसलिये हे सुरश्रेष्ठों ! जिसकी इन्द्रियां इन्द्रियों के विषयों से सब प्रकार से निगृहीत हैं उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित होती है
vishnu_gita::734.english_translation: Therefore, O best of the gods, one whose senses are fully restrained from sense objects has established wisdom.
vishnu_gita::734.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) यस्य (whose) सुरश्रेष्ठाः (best of gods) निगृहीतानि (restrained) सर्वशः (completely) इन्द्रियाणि (senses) इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः (from sense objects) तस्य (of that one) प्रज्ञा (wisdom) प्रतिष्ठिता (established)
vishnu_gita::734.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::734.essence: True wisdom arises when your senses no longer chase after external things.
vishnu_gita::734.simple_meaning: Your wisdom becomes steady when you completely control your senses and do not chase after their objects.
vishnu_gita::734.simple_insight: You feel more grounded and clear when your senses stop pulling you outward.
vishnu_gita::734.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the best gods, teaching that true wisdom comes when the senses no longer chase after external objects. This restraint stabilizes the mind, enabling clear understanding.
vishnu_gita::734.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes, notifications flood in; wisdom grows when you resist these distractions and keep your focus steady.
vishnu_gita::734.insight: It teaches you to restrain sensory impulses, redirecting energy inward to establish steady wisdom.

vishnu_gita::735.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानाधार ! दयागार ! विश्वात्मन् ! विश्वभावन !।
रहस्यं ज्ञानकाण्डस्य वैदिकस्य तदद्भुतम् ॥
vishnu_gita::735.verse_hindi: हे ज्ञानाधार ! हे दयासिन्धो ! हे विश्वात्मन् ! हे विश्वभावन ! वैदिक ज्ञानकाण्ड के इस अद्भुत रहस्य को
vishnu_gita::735.english_translation: O foundation of knowledge, ocean of compassion, universal self, creator of the universe, this is the wondrous secret of the Vedic knowledge section.
vishnu_gita::735.translation_literal: ज्ञानाधार (foundation of knowledge) / दयागार (ocean of compassion) / विश्वात्मन् (universal self) / विश्वभावन (creator of the universe) / रहस्यं (secret) / ज्ञानकाण्डस्य (of the knowledge section) / वैदिकस्य (of the Vedic) / तदद्भुतम् (that wondrous)
vishnu_gita::735.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::735.essence: Profound wisdom arises from the compassionate universal source behind all knowledge.
vishnu_gita::735.simple_meaning: This verse calls out to the divine by many names, introducing a wondrous secret from the Vedic knowledge section.
vishnu_gita::735.simple_insight: There is reverence and awe toward the source of profound wisdom and compassion.
vishnu_gita::735.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses the divine with multiple respectful titles, highlighting its vast qualities before revealing a secret from the Vedic knowledge. It sets a tone of wonder but does not teach a standalone principle here.
vishnu_gita::735.insight: It prepares the mind to receive deep wisdom by honoring its source, opening the heart for learning.

vishnu_gita::736.verse_sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा साम्प्रतमज्ञानान्मुक्ता जाता वयं विभो ।
किन्तु संश्रूयते नाथ ! कश्चिज्जीवो न चाहति ॥
vishnu_gita::736.verse_hindi: सुनकर हे विभो! हम इस समय प्रज्ञानमुक्त हुए हैं परन्तु हे नाथ! सुना है कि कोई जीव कभी
vishnu_gita::736.english_translation: Having heard this, O Vibhava, we have now become freed from ignorance, but O Lord, it is heard that no living being ever truly desires freedom.
vishnu_gita::736.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (having heard) साम्प्रतम (now) अज्ञानान् (ignorance) मुक्ताः (freed) जाताः (became) वयम् (we) विभो (O Vibhava) किन्तु (but) संश्रूयते (is heard) नाथ (O Lord) कश्चित् (someone) जीवः (living being) न (not) चाहति (desires)
vishnu_gita::736.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::736.essence: Many understand freedom but few truly desire to embrace it fully.
vishnu_gita::736.simple_meaning: We have become free from ignorance by hearing, but it is said that no living being truly wants freedom.
vishnu_gita::736.simple_insight: Freedom can be recognized but often remains undesired deep within.
vishnu_gita::736.detailed_meaning: After listening to teachings, the speakers claim to have freed themselves from ignorance, yet they express doubt because they have heard that living beings may not genuinely desire true freedom, reflecting the paradox of spiritual aspiration.
vishnu_gita::736.modern_relevance: You might understand a concept clearly but still feel resistance or doubt about truly embracing freedom or change.
vishnu_gita::736.insight: It reveals the gap between intellectual understanding and heartfelt desire for inner freedom.

vishnu_gita::737.verse_sanskrit:
सन्न्यासेन विना मुक्तिमधिगन्तुं कदाचन ।
सन्यासलक्षणंचातद्रहस्यंच हे प्रभो ॥
vishnu_gita::737.verse_hindi: बिना संन्यास के मुक्त नहीं हो सकता इसलिए हे प्रभो ! सन्यास क्या है और इसका रहस्य क्या है
vishnu_gita::737.english_translation: Without renunciation, liberation can never be attained; explain, O Lord, the nature and secret of renunciation.
vishnu_gita::737.translation_literal: सन्न्यासेन (by renunciation) / विना (without) / मुक्तिम् (liberation) / अधिगन्तुम् (to attain) / कदाचन (ever) / । / सन्यासलक्षणं (the nature of renunciation) / च (and) / अतद् (its) / रहस्यं (secret) / च (and) / हे (O) / प्रभो (Lord) / ॥
vishnu_gita::737.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::737.essence: Liberation requires true renunciation and understanding its hidden meaning.
vishnu_gita::737.simple_meaning: You cannot attain liberation without renunciation; understanding what renunciation truly means is essential.
vishnu_gita::737.simple_insight: Freedom feels distant until you grasp the deeper meaning of letting go.
vishnu_gita::737.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the speaker asks for an explanation of renunciation, emphasizing that liberation cannot be reached without it. It highlights the crucial role of renunciation as a gateway to freedom.
vishnu_gita::737.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by attachments, you sense freedom is impossible until you learn to let go deeply and truly.
vishnu_gita::737.insight: This verse shifts your focus from seeking freedom externally to starting with inner renunciation and understanding its nature.

vishnu_gita::738.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रूहि यह कृतार्था हि भवामसत्वरितं वयं ।
प्राप्नुम: परमात्मानं भवंत चैव मुक्तिदम ॥
vishnu_gita::738.verse_hindi: वह कहिये जिससे हम शीघ्र कृतकृत्य होवें तथा परमात्मा और मुक्तिदाता, स्वयं आपको प्राप्त कर सकें
vishnu_gita::738.english_translation: Speak of that through which we quickly become fulfilled and attain the supreme being and the giver of liberation.
vishnu_gita::738.translation_literal: ब्रूहि (Speak) / यह (this) / कृतार्था (fulfilled) / हि (indeed) / भवाम (we become) / असत्वरितं (quickly) / वयं (we) / प्राप्नुम: (attain) / परमात्मानं (the supreme being) / भवंत (you are) / चैव (and also) / मुक्तिदम (giver of liberation)
vishnu_gita::738.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::738.essence: Knowing what leads quickly to true fulfillment brings freedom and connection to the supreme being.
vishnu_gita::738.simple_meaning: You are asked to explain what helps us quickly feel complete and reach the supreme being who grants freedom.
vishnu_gita::738.simple_insight: There's hope in discovering a way to become truly fulfilled and free without delay.
vishnu_gita::738.detailed_meaning: The speaker requests knowledge about the means to quickly become fulfilled and reach the supreme being who grants liberation, setting the stage for the teaching ahead.
vishnu_gita::738.modern_relevance: You want a clear answer that helps you feel truly satisfied and free, without wasting time wandering.
vishnu_gita::738.insight: It shifts the focus from vague searching to learning the direct path to fulfillment and freedom.

vishnu_gita::739.verse_sanskrit:
सन्न्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसन्यासात् कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::739.verse_hindi: कर्मत्याग और कर्मयोग दोनों मोक्षदायक हैं किन्तु उनमें कर्म सन्यास से कर्मयोग श्रेष्ठ है
vishnu_gita::739.english_translation: Renunciation of action and the yoga of action both lead to inner freedom, but the yoga of action is superior to renunciation of action.
vishnu_gita::739.translation_literal: सन्न्यासः (renunciation) कर्मयोगश्च (and action-yoga) निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ (both lead to highest good) । तयोस्तु (but between them) कर्मसन्यासात् (from renunciation of action) कर्मयोगो (the yoga of action) विशिष्यते (is superior) ॥
vishnu_gita::739.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::739.essence: Mindful action frees you more than simply giving up action.
vishnu_gita::739.simple_meaning: Both giving up action and acting with detached awareness can bring freedom, but acting mindfully leads to a higher freedom.
vishnu_gita::739.simple_insight: You can find more liberation by engaging fully than by withdrawing from life.
vishnu_gita::739.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that both renouncing action and performing action with yoga lead to freedom. Yet, acting with selfless awareness is a deeper path than just renouncing duties, guiding Arjuna toward engaged living.
vishnu_gita::739.modern_relevance: You might feel tempted to avoid challenges, but facing them with mindful effort often brings deeper growth and freedom.
vishnu_gita::739.insight: It shifts your approach from avoidance to conscious engagement, encouraging active participation without attachment.

vishnu_gita::740.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसन्न्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि सुपर्वाणः ! मुखं बन्धाद्विमुच्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::740.verse_hindi: जो न द्वेष करता है और न आकांषा करता है उसको नित्य सन्यासी अर्थात् कर्म के अनुष्ठान काल में भी सन्यासी जानना उचित है क्योंकि हे देवगण ! राग द्वेषादि द्वन्द्व से रहित व्यक्ति अनायास बन्धन से छूट जाता  है
vishnu_gita::740.english_translation: One who neither hates nor desires is known as a true renunciate, free from all dualities and easily liberated from bondage.
vishnu_gita::740.translation_literal: ज्ञेयः (to be known) / स (he) / नित्यसन्न्यासी (eternal renunciate) / यो (who) / न (not) / द्वेष्टि (hates) / न (not) / काङ्क्षति (desires) / । / निर्द्वन्द्वो (without duality) / हि (indeed) / सुपर्वाणः (supremely disciplined) / ! / मुखं (face) / बन्धात् (from bondage) / विमुच्यते (is liberated) / ॥
vishnu_gita::740.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::740.essence: Freedom arises naturally when you act without hatred or desire.
vishnu_gita::740.simple_meaning: A true renunciate is someone who neither hates nor desires, remaining free from all inner conflicts and easily released from bondage.
vishnu_gita::740.simple_insight: There is peace in not holding onto hatred or craving; that peace is freedom.
vishnu_gita::740.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that a person who acts without hatred or desire is a true renunciate. Such a person transcends inner conflicts of attachment and aversion, naturally freeing themselves from bondage even while performing actions.
vishnu_gita::740.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in resentment or longing, but real freedom begins when you stop fueling those feelings.
vishnu_gita::740.insight: Shift your focus from resisting or craving outcomes to simply being present without inner turmoil.

vishnu_gita::741.verse_sanskrit:
सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥
vishnu_gita::741.verse_hindi: साङ्ख्य और योग अर्थात् ज्ञानयोग और कर्मयोग पृथक् हैं इस बात को अज्ञानी कहते हैं,  पण्डित ऐसा नहीं कहते क्योंकि एक का सम्यक् आश्रय करने वाला भी दोनों का फल प्राप्त करता है
vishnu_gita::741.english_translation: Ignorant people say that knowledge yoga and action yoga are separate, but the wise know that one who fully embraces either attains the fruit of both.
vishnu_gita::741.translation_literal: सांख्ययोगौ (knowledge yoga and action yoga) पृथग्बालाः (separately, ignorant) प्रवदन्ति (say) न (not) पण्डिताः (wise) । एकमपि (even one) आस्थितः (established) सम्यग् (properly) उभयोर् (of both) विंदते (obtains) फलम् (fruit) ॥
vishnu_gita::741.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::741.essence: Fully embracing either knowledge or action brings the fruits of both together.
vishnu_gita::741.simple_meaning: People who don't understand say knowledge and action yoga are separate. But the wise see that fully embracing either leads to the rewards of both.
vishnu_gita::741.simple_insight: It feels freeing to know you can gain wisdom and right action through one dedicated path.
vishnu_gita::741.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that ignorant people think knowledge yoga (jnana) and action yoga (karma) are different and separate paths. But a wise person knows that fully committing to either will bring the benefits of both, showing their essential unity.
vishnu_gita::741.modern_relevance: You might feel torn between learning and doing. This verse reminds you that fully committing to either learning or action can bring the results of both.
vishnu_gita::741.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing paths as isolated to recognizing their deep interconnectedness through full engagement.

vishnu_gita::742.verse_sanskrit:
यत्सान्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते ।
एकं सांख्यञ्च योगच यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
vishnu_gita::742.verse_hindi: जो स्थान साङ्ख्य से प्राप्त होता है वह योग से भी प्राप्त होता है, जो साङ्ख्य और योग को एक देखता है वह देखता है अर्थात् वह यथार्थ दर्शी है
vishnu_gita::742.english_translation: The state reached by wisdom (Jnana) is also attained by yoga (union); one who sees both as one truly sees reality.
vishnu_gita::742.translation_literal: यत् (that) साङ्खैः (by wisdom) प्राप्यते (is attained) स्थानं (state) तद्योगैः (by yoga) अपि (also) गम्यते (is reached) । एकं (one) सांख्यञ्च (wisdom and) योगच (and yoga) यः (who) पश्यति (sees) स (he) पश्यति (sees) ॥
vishnu_gita::742.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::742.essence: True vision comes from seeing wisdom and yoga as one unified path.
vishnu_gita::742.simple_meaning: The state of deep understanding reached by wisdom can also be reached through yoga. Recognizing them as the same is true seeing.
vishnu_gita::742.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing that different paths lead to the same truth.
vishnu_gita::742.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that both the path of wisdom (Jnana) and the path of yoga lead to the same ultimate state. Seeing these as separate limits understanding; true insight comes from uniting them.
vishnu_gita::742.modern_relevance: When you feel torn between study and practice, remember they both guide you to the same clarity and peace.
vishnu_gita::742.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing paths as opposed to seeing them as complementary ways to the same goal.

vishnu_gita::743.verse_sanskrit:
सन्न्यासस्तु मुरश्रेष्ठाः ! दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः ।
योगयुक्तो मुनिब्रह्म नचिरेणाऽधिगच्छति ॥
vishnu_gita::743.verse_hindi: हे सुरश्रेष्ठो ! कर्मयोग के बिना सन्यास का प्राप्त करना दुःसाध्य है किन्तु योगयुक्त मुनि शीघ्र ही ब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है
