vishnu_gita::743.english_translation: O best of sages! Without Karma Yoga, renunciation is hard to attain, but a yogi quickly attains Brahman.
vishnu_gita::743.translation_literal: सन्न्यासः (renunciation) तु (but) मुरश्रेष्ठाः (best of sages) दुःखम् (difficulty) आप्तुम् (to attain) अयोगतः (without yoga) । योगयुक्तः (united with yoga) मुनि (sage) ब्रह्म (Brahman) न चिरेण (not long) अधिगच्छति (attains) ॥
vishnu_gita::743.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::743.essence: True renunciation requires yoga-infused action; without it, renunciation is unreachable.
vishnu_gita::743.simple_meaning: Renunciation is difficult to reach without acting with yoga, but a sage practicing yoga quickly attains the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::743.simple_insight: You feel encouraged knowing that sincere action with yoga leads swiftly to freedom.
vishnu_gita::743.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses a great sage, explaining that simply abandoning action (renunciation) without yoga is very difficult, but a wise person who acts with yoga attains the supreme reality quickly.
vishnu_gita::743.modern_relevance: You struggle to quit old habits by avoidance alone, but when you engage fully with mindful effort, real transformation happens faster.
vishnu_gita::743.insight: It shifts your approach from mere withdrawal to active, mindful engagement as the path to true renunciation.

vishnu_gita::744.verse_sanskrit:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्ध आत्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रिय: ।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वनपि न लिप्यते ॥
vishnu_gita::744.verse_hindi: विशुद्धचित्त, विजितमन, जितेन्द्रिय और सब भूतो की आत्मा ही जिसकी आत्मा है ऐसा योगयुक्त व्यक्ति कर्म करता हुआ भी कर्म में बद्ध नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::744.english_translation: A person united in yoga, pure in mind, victorious over the self and senses, and the inner being of all beings acts without being bound by action.
vishnu_gita::744.translation_literal: योगयुक्तो (united in yoga) / विशुद्ध (pure) / आत्मा (self) / विजितात्मा (victorious self) / जितेन्द्रिय: (conqueror of senses) / सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा (inner being of all beings) / कुर्वन् (doing) / अपि (even) / न (not) / लिप्यते (is bound)
vishnu_gita::744.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::744.essence: You can act fully and remain free by mastering your mind and senses.
vishnu_gita::744.simple_meaning: A person who is steady in yoga, pure in mind, and has conquered their senses can act without becoming attached or bound by the results.
vishnu_gita::744.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting with clarity and self-control, even amid all activity.
vishnu_gita::744.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that someone who has united with yoga, purified their mind, overcome selfish impulses, and controls their senses acts without being caught by karma. This shows how mastery over self and mind leads to freedom even while acting.
vishnu_gita::744.modern_relevance: You face constant pressure to act and achieve, yet when you stay centered and calm, your efforts don’t trap or overwhelm you.
vishnu_gita::744.insight: It teaches you to act with awareness and self-mastery, preventing your actions from creating bondage.

vishnu_gita::745.verse_sanskrit:
नैव किञ्चित् करोमीति युक्तो प्रन्येत तत्ववित् ।
पश्यन् शृग्वन्स्पृशन जिघनश्नन् गच्छन्स्वपन श्वसन ॥
vishnu_gita::745.verse_hindi: मैं कुछ भी नहीं करता हूँ ऐसा समझता है ब्रह्म में युक्त तत्त्ववित् व्यक्ति दर्शन, श्रवण, स्पर्श, घ्राण, भोजन, गमन, निद्रा, श्वास,
vishnu_gita::745.english_translation: A person established in the supreme reality knows: “I do nothing.” They see, hear, touch, eat, walk, sleep, and breathe without identifying as doer.
vishnu_gita::745.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) किञ्चित् (anything) करोमीति (I do) युक्तो (established) प्रन्येत (knows) तत्ववित् (the knower of truth) । पश्यन् (seeing) शृग्वन् (hearing) स्पृशन (touching) जिघनश्नन् (eating) गच्छन् (walking) स्वपन (sleeping) श्वसन (breathing) ॥
vishnu_gita::745.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::745.essence: You can experience life’s actions without being attached to doing them yourself.
vishnu_gita::745.simple_meaning: You can live fully—seeing, hearing, eating, and breathing—without feeling like you are the one doing it.
vishnu_gita::745.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are not the one who truly acts.
vishnu_gita::745.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains to the listener that a person who understands the supreme reality sees all actions as happening without personal doership. Even normal activities like seeing and breathing are witnessed, not owned.
vishnu_gita::745.modern_relevance: You rush through your day feeling responsible for every little thing, unaware that some parts of life simply happen through you.
vishnu_gita::745.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying as the doer to recognizing your role as the witness of action.

vishnu_gita::746.verse_sanskrit:
प्रलपन् विसृजन गृहन्नुन्मिपन्निमिषन्नपि ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥
vishnu_gita::746.verse_hindi: भाषण, त्याग, ग्रहण, उन्मेष और निमेष करता हुआ भी, इन्द्रियगण इन्द्रिय के विषयों में प्रवृत्त होते हैं ऐसी धारणा करता हुआ
vishnu_gita::746.english_translation: Even while speaking, renouncing, taking, opening, and blinking, the senses remain engaged with their objects, one believes.
vishnu_gita::746.translation_literal: प्रलपन् (speaking) / विसृजन (renouncing) / गृहन् (taking) / उन्मिपन् (opening) / निमिषन् (blinking) / अपि (even) / इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु (senses in objects of senses) / वर्तन्त (are engaged) / इति (thus) / धारयन् (believing)
vishnu_gita::746.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::746.essence: Senses often remain engaged even when the mind tries to withdraw from them.
vishnu_gita::746.simple_meaning: Even when you speak or try to let go, your senses keep following their objects, as if unaware.
vishnu_gita::746.simple_insight: You might try to stop, but your senses often keep pulling you back to what they want.
vishnu_gita::746.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how the senses remain engaged with their objects—speaking, letting go, or moving—even while the mind believes it is detached. This reveals the restless nature of the senses and the difficulty of true detachment.
vishnu_gita::746.modern_relevance: You decide to stop scrolling, but your eyes dart back to the screen, drawn by notifications and images.
vishnu_gita::746.insight: Recognize that detachment is a process; senses often continue their habits despite your conscious will.

vishnu_gita::747.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
vishnu_gita::747.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार पनपत्र जल में लिप्त नहीं होता है उसी प्रकार कर्मों को ब्रह्म में समर्पित और फलासक्ति त्याग करके जो कर्म करता है वह पाप अर्थात् बन्धन करने वाले कर्मों से लिप्त नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::747.english_translation: Just as a lotus leaf remains untouched by water, one who performs actions dedicated to the supreme reality without attachment to results is not bound by harmful consequences.
vishnu_gita::747.translation_literal: ब्रह्मण्याधाय (dedicated to the supreme reality) कर्माणि (actions) सङ्गं (attachment) त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) करोति (performs) यः (who) । लिप्यते (is stained) न (not) स (he) पापेन (by harmful consequences) पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा (like a lotus leaf by water) ॥
vishnu_gita::747.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::747.essence: Act fully with dedication but without attachment; then harmful bonds cannot touch you.
vishnu_gita::747.simple_meaning: You can perform your duties fully if you dedicate your actions to the supreme reality and give up attachment to their results. Then, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, you are not affected by harmful consequences.
vishnu_gita::747.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting without craving results, like being untouched by what surrounds you.
vishnu_gita::747.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that when you dedicate your actions to the supreme reality and let go of attachment to the results, you remain unstained by negative consequences. Like the lotus leaf that water cannot cling to, your actions do not create harmful bonds.
vishnu_gita::747.modern_relevance: You finish a difficult task without obsessing over praise or failure, and find peace regardless of the outcome.
vishnu_gita::747.insight: It teaches you to dedicate effort to a greater purpose and release fixation on the outcomes, freeing your mind.

vishnu_gita::748.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा सन्न्यस्यास्ते मुखं वशी।
नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन न कारयन् ॥
vishnu_gita::748.verse_hindi: जितेन्द्रिय देही विवेक युक्त मन के द्वारा सब कर्मों का त्याग करके नव द्वारों से युक्त पुर में अर्थात् स्थूल शरीर में नहीं कुछ करता हुआ और नहीं कुछ कराता हुआ सुखपूर्वक रहता है
vishnu_gita::748.english_translation: With controlled senses and a discerning mind, the true self renounces all actions mentally, dwelling peacefully in the body without doing or causing anything.
vishnu_gita::748.translation_literal: सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) मनसा (by mind) सन्न्यस्यास्ते (renouncing) मुखं (mouth) वशी (controlled). नवद्वारे (nine gates) पुरे (in the city/body) देही (the embodied self) नैव (neither) कुर्वन (doing) न (nor) कारयन् (causing).
vishnu_gita::748.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::748.essence: You can fully withdraw from action internally while living in the body.
vishnu_gita::748.simple_meaning: You can mentally let go of all actions by controlling your senses and mind, living peacefully without doing or causing anything physically.
vishnu_gita::748.simple_insight: There's calm in knowing you can withdraw from action without leaving your body.
vishnu_gita::748.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains how the embodied self, with senses subdued and a discerning mind, can renounce all action mentally. Though residing in the body with its nine gates, it neither acts nor causes action, embodying true renunciation.
vishnu_gita::748.modern_relevance: You sit quietly, letting your restless mind and impulses settle, feeling peaceful without needing to act or control the world around you.
vishnu_gita::748.insight: It shifts the mind from feeling compelled to act outwardly to resting as the observer within.

vishnu_gita::749.verse_sanskrit:
अनाश्रितः कुर्मफलं कार्य कर्म करोति यः ।
स सन्न्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाऽक्रियः॥
vishnu_gita::749.verse_hindi: जो कर्मफल का आश्रय नहीं करके कर्तव्य कर्म करता है वही सन्यासी है और वही योगी है। निरग्नि अर्थात् अग्निसाध्य ईष्टादि कर्म त्यागी और अक्रिय (पूर्त्यदिकर्म रहित) व्यक्ति सन्यासी नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::749.english_translation: One who performs their duty without attachment to the result is both a renunciate and a yogi; one who abandons sacred rites and remains inactive is not a renunciate.
vishnu_gita::749.translation_literal: अनाश्रितः (without dependence) कुर्म (does) फलम् (fruit/result) कार्य (of action) कर्म (action) करोति (performs) यः (who) । स (that one) सन्न्यासी (renunciate) च (and) योगी (yogi) च (also) न (not) निरग्निः (without sacred fire) न (nor) चाऽक्रियः (inactive) ॥
vishnu_gita::749.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::749.essence: You can perform your duties fully without clinging to their results; that is true renunciation.
vishnu_gita::749.simple_meaning: You become a true renunciate and yogi by doing your duty without expecting any reward or result.
vishnu_gita::749.simple_insight: You can feel freedom in acting fully while releasing attachment to what follows.
vishnu_gita::749.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains to the listener that true renunciation is about performing one's duties without attachment to the fruits of action. Simply abandoning sacred rituals or becoming inactive does not make one a renunciate. The moment calls for acting with inner freedom, not withdrawal.
vishnu_gita::749.modern_relevance: You stayed up late finishing a project, not for praise but because it was your responsibility—and that is true dedication.
vishnu_gita::749.insight: It teaches you to focus on your action itself, not on what you might gain or lose afterward.

vishnu_gita::750.verse_sanskrit:
यत्कुरुध्वे यद्श्नीथ यज्जूहुध्वे छ दत्थ यत ।
यत्तपस्यथ भो देवाः! तत्कुरुध्वं मदर्पणम् ॥
vishnu_gita::750.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! आपलोग जो कर्म करते हैं, जो भोजन करते हैं, जो होम करते हैं, जो दान देते हैं और जो तपस्या करते हैं उसको मुझमें अर्पण करें
vishnu_gita::750.english_translation: O divine beings, whatever actions you perform, whatever you eat, offer, give, or practice as austerity, dedicate all to me.
vishnu_gita::750.translation_literal: यत्कुरुध्वे (whatever you do) / यद्श्नीथ (whatever you eat) / यज्जूहुध्वे (whatever you offer in sacrifice) / छ (also) / दत्थ (whatever you give) / यत (whatever) / यत्तपस्यथ (whatever austerity you perform) / भो देवाः (O divine beings!) / तत्कुरुध्वं (that do) / मदर्पणम् (as an offering to me)
vishnu_gita::750.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::750.essence: All actions become sacred when offered as a gift to the divine.
vishnu_gita::750.simple_meaning: Whatever you do—work, eat, offer, give, or practice austerity—offer it as a gift to the divine.
vishnu_gita::750.simple_insight: You can transform everyday acts into expressions of devoted connection.
vishnu_gita::750.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs divine beings to dedicate every action and ritual—whether work, eating, sacrifice, giving, or austerity—as an offering to him, teaching that devotion is present in all acts when offered mindfully.
vishnu_gita::750.modern_relevance: You prepare a meal, send a gift, or work hard—offering these acts as devotion makes them meaningful beyond routine.
vishnu_gita::750.insight: It teaches you to see each daily action as a chance to connect deeply through offering.

vishnu_gita::751.verse_sanskrit:
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यध्वे कर्मबन्धनैः ।
सन्न्यासयोगयुक्ता हि विमुक्ता मामुपैष्यथ ॥
vishnu_gita::751.verse_hindi: ऐसा करने से शुभ और अशुभ फल देने वाले कर्मबन्धनों से आप छूट जाओगे क्योंकि आप लोग मुझ में फल समर्पण रूपी संन्यास योग मे युक्त होने के कारण विमुक्त होकर मुझको प्राप्त करोगे
vishnu_gita::751.english_translation: By practicing renunciation yoga with dedication to me, you will be freed from bonds of good and bad karmic results and attain liberation.
vishnu_gita::751.translation_literal: शुभाशुभफलैः (good and bad results) / एवं (thus) / मोक्ष्यध्वे (you will be liberated) / कर्मबन्धनैः (from bonds of karma) / सन्न्यासयोगयुक्ता (joined in renunciation yoga) / हि (indeed) / विमुक्ता (freed) / मामुपैष्यथ (you will reach me)
vishnu_gita::751.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::751.essence: You free yourself from karmic bonds by acting with surrender to the divine.
vishnu_gita::751.simple_meaning: You become free from binding consequences of good and bad actions by practicing renunciation through dedicating your work to the divine.
vishnu_gita::751.simple_insight: There’s relief in knowing that giving your best with surrender frees you from burdensome results.
vishnu_gita::751.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains how dedicating actions to him through renunciation yoga frees Arjuna from bondage caused by all karmic results, good or bad. This promise offers liberation by changing how one relates to action and its outcomes.
vishnu_gita::751.modern_relevance: You finished a difficult project without obsessing over praise or blame, feeling lighter because you didn’t cling to results.
vishnu_gita::751.insight: This verse shifts focus from craving outcomes to dedicating effort, which breaks the cycle of binding consequences.

vishnu_gita::752.verse_sanskrit:
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं सन्न्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥
vishnu_gita::752.verse_hindi: दूरदर्शी पण्डितलोग काम्यकर्मों के त्याग को सन्यास कहते हैं और सभी कर्मों के फलों के त्याग को त्याग कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::752.english_translation: Wise thinkers say that giving up actions done for desire is renunciation, and giving up attachment to the fruits of all actions is true renunciation.
vishnu_gita::752.translation_literal: काम्यानां (of desired) / कर्मणां (actions) / न्यासं (giving up) / सन्न्यासं (renunciation) / कवयो (wise ones) / विदुः (know) । / सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं (giving up all action-fruits) / प्राहुः (say) / त्यागं (renunciation) / विचक्षणाः (discerning) ॥
vishnu_gita::752.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::752.essence: Renouncing desire for results is true renunciation, not just giving up actions.
vishnu_gita::752.simple_meaning: Giving up only actions done to satisfy desires is called renunciation. But real renunciation is giving up attachment to the results of all actions.
vishnu_gita::752.simple_insight: There's freedom in releasing your grip on outcomes, even while acting.
vishnu_gita::752.detailed_meaning: Wise thinkers distinguish between stopping desire-driven actions and truly letting go of attachment to all results. This teaching guides how to act with freedom amid life’s demands.
vishnu_gita::752.modern_relevance: You might stop chasing certain goals but still feel trapped by results. True freedom comes from releasing your hold on outcomes, not just actions.
vishnu_gita::752.insight: It shifts your focus from abandoning actions to abandoning craving for their results, enabling balanced engagement.

vishnu_gita::753.verse_sanskrit:
त्याज्यं दोषवादत्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः।
यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥
vishnu_gita::753.verse_hindi: कोई कोई पण्डितलोग दोषयुक्त कर्म को त्याज्य कहते हैं और कोई यज्ञ, तप और दान त्याज्य नहीं है ऐसा कहते हैं
vishnu_gita::753.english_translation: Some wise ones say that actions with faults should be abandoned, while others say that acts of sacrifice, charity, and discipline should never be abandoned.
vishnu_gita::753.translation_literal: त्याज्यं (to be abandoned) दोषवादत्येके (fault-involving alone) कर्म (actions) प्राहुर्मनीषिणः (say the wise ones) यज्ञदानतपः (sacrifice, charity, discipline) कर्म (actions) न (not) त्याज्यमिति (to be abandoned) चापरे (and others)
vishnu_gita::753.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::753.essence: Not all flawed actions must be abandoned; some sacred acts must be sustained.
vishnu_gita::753.simple_meaning: Some say all faulty actions should be stopped, but others say acts like sacrifice, charity, and disciplined effort should never be stopped.
vishnu_gita::753.simple_insight: You can learn to recognize which actions to release and which to cherish, freeing your practice from confusion.
vishnu_gita::753.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that among wise people, opinions differ: some think any action with faults should be abandoned; others believe that actions done as sacrifice, charity, or disciplined practice should always be maintained. This verse highlights the need to discern which actions align with true purpose.
vishnu_gita::753.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by guilt over past mistakes, you might wonder whether to quit or keep trying; this helps you see some efforts are worth continuing despite flaws.
vishnu_gita::753.insight: It teaches you to evaluate actions by their nature and purpose, not just their imperfections, so you don't give up on meaningful practices.

vishnu_gita::754.verse_sanskrit:
श्रूयतां निश्चयस्तत्र त्यागे मेऽमृतभोजिनः!।
त्यागो हि विबुधश्रेष्ठाः ! त्रिविधः परिकीर्तितः ॥
vishnu_gita::754.verse_hindi: हे अमृतभोजी देवश्रेष्ठो ! उस त्याग के विषय में मेरा निश्चय सुनो। त्याग तीन प्रकार का कहा गया है
vishnu_gita::754.english_translation: Listen closely, O supreme among the divine, to my determination about renunciation. Renunciation is described in three forms.
vishnu_gita::754.translation_literal: श्रूयतां (let be heard) / निश्चयः (determination) / तत्र (there) / त्यागे (in renunciation) / मेऽमृतभोजिनः (my O immortal eater) ! / त्यागः (renunciation) / हि (indeed) / विबुधश्रेष्ठाः (the best among the wise) ! / त्रिविधः (threefold) / परिकीर्तितः (declared) ॥
vishnu_gita::754.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::754.essence: Renunciation is not singular but has three distinct, recognized forms.
vishnu_gita::754.simple_meaning: There are three kinds of renunciation, and this verse introduces a clear determination to explain them.
vishnu_gita::754.simple_insight: Knowing renunciation has distinct forms helps you see how letting go can take different shapes.
vishnu_gita::754.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the divine, stating he has a firm resolve to explain renunciation, which is divided into three types, setting the stage for deeper understanding.
vishnu_gita::754.modern_relevance: You’ve felt the urge to let go but wondered how — this verse points to three ways to release what no longer serves.
vishnu_gita::754.insight: It teaches you to recognize that giving up attachments isn’t one-size-fits-all but has distinct approaches.

vishnu_gita::755.verse_sanskrit:
यज्ञदानतपाकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् ।
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥
vishnu_gita::755.verse_hindi: यज्ञ, तप और दान ये तीन कर्म त्याग करने के योग्य नहीं हैं, यह निश्चय ही कर्तव्य हैं, यज्ञ तप और दान विवेकियों को भी पवित्र करनेवाले हैं
vishnu_gita::755.english_translation: Sacrifices, charity, and disciplined acts are never to be abandoned; these duties purify even the wise.
vishnu_gita::755.translation_literal: यज्ञ (sacrifice) / दान (charity) / तप (disciplined effort) / कर्म (actions) / न (not) / त्याज्यं (to be abandoned) / कार्यमेव (indeed duties) / तत् (that) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / दानं (charity) / तपश्चैव (and disciplined effort too) / पावनानि (purifying) / मनीषिणाम् (of the wise)
vishnu_gita::755.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::755.essence: Certain selfless actions are essential duties that purify all practitioners.
vishnu_gita::755.simple_meaning: Actions like sacrifice, charity, and disciplined effort are essential duties that should never be abandoned because they purify everyone, including the wise.
vishnu_gita::755.simple_insight: There is value and purity in certain actions that remain vital no matter who you are.
vishnu_gita::755.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs that even the wise must not abandon the practices of sacrifice, charity, and disciplined effort. These actions are foundational duties that cleanse and elevate the practitioner, reinforcing the importance of consistent righteous action.
vishnu_gita::755.modern_relevance: When you hesitate to give time, money, or effort because you doubt their impact, remember these acts purify and strengthen your character.
vishnu_gita::755.insight: Recognize some actions as essential duties that purify, regardless of outcome or recognition.

vishnu_gita::756.verse_sanskrit:
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
कर्तव्यानीति मे देवाः ! निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम ॥
vishnu_gita::756.verse_hindi: किन्तु हे देवगण ! ये कर्म भी आसक्ति और फल का त्याग करने योग्य हैं यह मेरा निश्चित ही उत्तम मत है
vishnu_gita::756.english_translation: But, O divine beings, these actions too should be performed by abandoning attachment and the fruits; this is certainly my highest teaching.
vishnu_gita::756.translation_literal: एतानि (these) अपि (also) तु (indeed) कर्माणि (actions) सङ्गं (attachment) त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) फलानि (fruits/results) च (and) कर्तव्यानीति (should be done) मे (my) देवाः (O divine beings) निश्चितं (certainly) मतम् (opinion) उत्तमम् (best)
vishnu_gita::756.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::756.essence: You can act without craving results; that is the highest way to act.
vishnu_gita::756.simple_meaning: You should perform actions without attachment to them or their outcomes; this is the best teaching.
vishnu_gita::756.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting without needing to control the results of what you do.
vishnu_gita::756.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs the divine beings that all actions must be done without attachment to the action itself or the results. This teaching emphasizes detachment and dedicates the practice of action to a higher ideal beyond craving outcomes.
vishnu_gita::756.modern_relevance: You finish a task completely but feel anxious about the outcome. This teaching reminds you to release that anxiety and trust the process.
vishnu_gita::756.insight: It shifts your focus from expecting rewards to fully engaging in the work itself, cleaning the motivation behind your actions.

vishnu_gita::757.verse_sanskrit:
न द्वेष्टयकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥
vishnu_gita::757.verse_hindi: सत्त्वगुण शाली मेधावी संशयरहित त्यागी व्यक्ति अकुशल (दुःखजनक) कर्म में द्वेष नहीं करता है और न कुशल (सुखकर) कर्म में आसक्त होता है
vishnu_gita::757.english_translation: A person endowed with sattva, wise and free from doubt, does not hate unskillful actions nor cling to skillful ones; such a renouncer is steady and clear-minded.
vishnu_gita::757.translation_literal: न (not) द्वेष्टय (hates) अकुशलं (unskillful) कर्म (action) कुशले (skillful) न (nor) अनुशज्जते (clings) । त्यागी (renouncer) सत्त्वसमाविष्टः (endowed with sattva) मेधावी (wise) छिन्नसंशयः (free from doubt) ॥
vishnu_gita::757.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::757.essence: True steadiness comes from neither hating hardship nor clinging to comfort.
vishnu_gita::757.simple_meaning: You can be steady and clear by neither hating difficult actions nor clinging to easy ones.
vishnu_gita::757.simple_insight: There's calm in letting go of both dislike and attachment toward your actions.
vishnu_gita::757.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that a person filled with the quality of sattva, who is wise and free of doubt, remains balanced by not resenting difficult tasks nor clinging to easy or enjoyable ones. This steadiness marks a true renouncer.
vishnu_gita::757.modern_relevance: You face tasks you dislike and tasks you enjoy. Staying balanced means not resisting the tough ones or clinging to the easy ones.
vishnu_gita::757.insight: It teaches you to act without emotional swings—neither aversion nor craving colors your effort.

vishnu_gita::758.verse_sanskrit:
नहि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं काण्यशेषतः।
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥
vishnu_gita::758.verse_hindi: क्योंकि देहधारी विशेषरूप से कर्मों का त्याग नहीं कर सकता है किन्तु जो कर्म के फलको त्याग करता है वह त्यागी कहलाता है
vishnu_gita::758.english_translation: Because a being with a body cannot completely abandon actions, but one who renounces the fruits of actions is called a renunciant.
vishnu_gita::758.translation_literal: नहि (not) / देहभृता (body-holder) / शक्यं (possible) / त्यक्तुं (to abandon) / काणि (actions) / अषेषतः (completely) / यः (who) / तु (but) / कर्मफल (fruits of actions) / त्यागी (renunciant) / स (he) / त्यागीति (renounces) / अभिधीयते (is called)
vishnu_gita::758.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::758.essence: Renunciation means letting go of attachment to results, not ceasing all action.
vishnu_gita::758.simple_meaning: You cannot stop doing all actions because of your body, but you can give up attachment to the results of your actions.
vishnu_gita::758.simple_insight: There is freedom in releasing the need to control what happens after you act.
vishnu_gita::758.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Vishnu explains that living beings embodied in a body cannot cease all activity, but true renunciation means surrendering attachment to the results, not the actions themselves. This helps Arjuna understand how to act without bondage.
vishnu_gita::758.modern_relevance: You keep working hard, but often stress over outcomes beyond your control. Letting go of this worry lightens your daily load.
vishnu_gita::758.insight: It shifts your focus from stopping action to stopping craving results, freeing your effort from anxiety.

vishnu_gita::759.verse_sanskrit:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रञ्च त्रिविध कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु सन्न्यासिनां कचित् ॥
vishnu_gita::759.verse_hindi: इष्ट, अनिष्ट और मिश्र अर्थात् इष्टानिष्ट, यह कर्म का त्रिविध फल सकाम व्यक्तियों को परलोक में होता है किन्तु सन्यासियों को कहीं भी नहीं होता है
vishnu_gita::759.english_translation: The threefold fruits of action—desirable, undesirable, and mixed—affect those attached to outcomes after death, but never the renunciates.
vishnu_gita::759.translation_literal: अनिष्टमिष्टं (undesirable and desirable) / मिश्रञ्च (mixed also) / त्रिविध (threefold) / कर्मणः (of action) / फलम् (fruit) / भवत्य (becomes) / त्यागिनां (of renunciates) / प्रेत्य (after death) / न (not) / तु (but) / सन्न्यासिनां (of renunciates) / कचित् (anywhere)
vishnu_gita::759.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::759.essence: Desire binds you to action’s results; renunciation frees you from them entirely.
vishnu_gita::759.simple_meaning: Actions produce good, bad, or mixed results for those who want outcomes, but renunciates are free from these results.
vishnu_gita::759.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing desire for results is what binds you, not the action itself.
vishnu_gita::759.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that after death, those attached to the fruits of their actions experience good, bad, or mixed consequences. But renunciates, who have released craving, are not affected by these outcomes anywhere.
vishnu_gita::759.modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard on a project and worried about the outcome; this shows how releasing attachment frees you from that stress.
vishnu_gita::759.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing results to releasing desire, freeing your mind from outcome anxiety.

vishnu_gita::760.verse_sanskrit:
सिद्धि प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निवोधत ।
समासेनैव भो देवाः ! निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
vishnu_gita::760.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धि-प्राप्त व्यक्ति जिस प्रकार ब्रह्म को प्राप्त होता है और जो चरम ज्ञान है उसको संक्षेप से ही सुनो
vishnu_gita::760.english_translation: O radiant beings! Just as a person who attains mastery in action reaches the supreme reality, hear briefly about the highest steadfastness in wisdom.
vishnu_gita::760.translation_literal: सिद्धि (mastery) / प्राप्तो (obtained) / यथा (just as) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / तथाप्नोति (thus attains) / निवोधत (hear) / समासेनैव (briefly) / भो (O) / देवाः (radiant beings) / निष्ठा (steadfastness) / ज्ञानस्य (of wisdom) / या (which) / परा (highest)
vishnu_gita::760.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::760.essence: Mastery in action and highest wisdom share a deep, connected steadfastness.
vishnu_gita::760.simple_meaning: Mastery in selfless action leads you to the supreme reality, and now hear the essence of highest wisdom briefly.
vishnu_gita::760.simple_insight: There is a deep connection between mastery in action and the highest wisdom that grounds you fully.
vishnu_gita::760.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses radiant beings, comparing the attainment of perfect mastery in action to reaching the supreme reality, preparing them to hear shortly about the ultimate steadfastness in wisdom.
vishnu_gita::760.modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard to master your craft or practice; now it’s time to understand the deeper wisdom that grounds your success.
vishnu_gita::760.insight: It teaches you to see mastery in action as a gateway to deeper wisdom and steadfastness.

vishnu_gita::761.verse_sanskrit:
बुद्धया विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।
शब्दादीन विषयाँस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥
vishnu_gita::761.verse_hindi: विशुद्ध-बुद्धियुक्त होकर धैर्य के द्वारा बुद्धि को संयत करके शब्दादि विषयो का त्याग करके और राग द्वेष को दूर करके
vishnu_gita::761.english_translation: With purified intellect, controlled mind by patience, renouncing sense objects like sounds, and abandoning attachment and aversion.
vishnu_gita::761.translation_literal: बुद्धया (with intellect) / विशुद्धया (purified) / युक्तो (joined/engaged) / धृत्यात्मानं (with patience controlling the self) / नियम्य (restraining) / च (and) / शब्दादीन (sounds and others) / विषयाँस्त्यक्त्वा (renouncing objects) / रागद्वेषौ (attachment and aversion) / व्युदस्य (abandoning) / च (and)
vishnu_gita::761.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::761.essence: Steady patience and a purified intellect free you from craving and aversion.
vishnu_gita::761.simple_meaning: You purify your intellect, control yourself with patience, let go of sensory distractions, and abandon likes and dislikes.
vishnu_gita::761.simple_insight: You feel calm and steady when you stop chasing or rejecting things.
vishnu_gita::761.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches how to govern the mind by purifying intellect and practicing patience to control impulses. Letting go of distractions like sounds and avoiding emotional extremes of attachment and aversion helps steady the self for disciplined action.
vishnu_gita::761.modern_relevance: When your mind jumps at every notification or distraction, steadying yourself with calm patience helps you focus and stay balanced.
vishnu_gita::761.insight: It teaches you to use patience to restrain restless impulses and release emotional extremes.

vishnu_gita::762.verse_sanskrit:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः।
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥
vishnu_gita::762.verse_hindi: निर्जनस्थान वासी एवं मितभोजी होकर शरीर वाणी और मन को संयत करके सदाशान योग में तत्पर होता हुआ वैराग्य का भलीभांति आश्रय करके
vishnu_gita::762.english_translation: Living in solitude, moderate in eating, controlling body, speech, and mind, always devoted to meditation yoga and firmly relying on dispassion.
vishnu_gita::762.translation_literal: विविक्तसेवी (living in solitude) / लघ्वाशी (moderate eater) / यतवाक्कायमानसः (controlling speech, body, mind) / ध्यानयोगपरो (always devoted to meditation yoga) / नित्यं (constantly) / वैराग्यं (dispassion) / समुपाश्रितः (firmly relying)
vishnu_gita::762.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::762.essence: Living simply with self-control and steady meditation anchored in dispassion leads to spiritual progress.
vishnu_gita::762.simple_meaning: You live alone in a quiet place, eat moderately, control your body, speech, and mind, and constantly focus on meditation while relying on detachment.
vishnu_gita::762.simple_insight: There is strength in simplicity and steady self-control supported by inner detachment.
vishnu_gita::762.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a person who chooses solitude, eats little, and disciplines their body, speech, and mind. This person stays devoted to meditation yoga and firmly embraces dispassion to progress on the spiritual path.
vishnu_gita::762.modern_relevance: You choose quiet moments alone, eat lightly, and calm your restless mind to stay focused on what truly matters.
vishnu_gita::762.insight: It teaches you to build habits of moderation and steady focus supported by detachment from distractions.

vishnu_gita::763.verse_sanskrit:
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्प कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
vishnu_gita::763.verse_hindi: अहङ्कार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रह का त्याग करके ममता शून्य होकर शनी व्यक्ति ब्रह्म ही हो जाता है
vishnu_gita::763.english_translation: By renouncing ego, strength, pride, desire, anger, and possession, becoming free of attachment and peaceful, a person is established in the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::763.translation_literal: अहङ्कारं (ego) / बलं (strength) / दर्प (pride) / कामं (desire) / क्रोधं (anger) / परिग्रहम् (possession) / विमुच्य (having renounced) / निर्ममः (without attachment) / शान्तो (peaceful) / ब्रह्मभूयाय (to become of the supreme reality) / कल्पते (is established)
vishnu_gita::763.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::763.essence: Peace and true being arise by releasing ego, desire, anger, and attachment.
vishnu_gita::763.simple_meaning: Let go of ego, pride, desire, anger, and attachment to become peaceful and realize your true nature beyond the self.
vishnu_gita::763.simple_insight: Relief comes when you stop clinging to ego and desires and find peace within.
vishnu_gita::763.detailed_meaning: Vishnu teaches that abandoning ego, strength, pride, desire, anger, and possessions frees a person from attachments. This freedom creates peace and reveals their true nature as part of the supreme reality.
vishnu_gita::763.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by your rising pride, anger, and wanting more, but peace comes only when you release those burdens.
vishnu_gita::763.insight: This verse shifts your focus from grasping to letting go, cultivating peaceful detachment and connection to something deeper than the restless self.

vishnu_gita::764.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मभृतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु सन्न्यासं लभते परम् ॥
vishnu_gita::764.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मभूत और प्रसन्नचित्त व्यक्ति नष्ट वस्तुओं के लिये आकांशा नहीं करता है, सब भूतों में समभावापन्न होकर श्रेष्ठ सन्न्यास को प्राप्त होता है
vishnu_gita::764.english_translation: One who is established in the supreme reality and whose mind is serene neither grieves nor desires; being equal to all beings, they attain the highest renunciation.
vishnu_gita::764.translation_literal: ब्रह्मभृतः (established in Brahman) / प्रसन्नात्मा (serene mind) / न (not) / शोचति (grieves) / न (nor) / काङ्क्षति (desires) / समः (equal) / सर्वेषु (in all) / भूतेषु (beings) / सन्न्यासं (renunciation) / लभते (attains) / परम् (supreme)
vishnu_gita::764.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::764.essence: Calmness and equal regard free you from grief and craving, revealing supreme renunciation.
vishnu_gita::764.simple_meaning: A person whose mind is calm and established in the supreme reality does not grieve or crave. They see all beings equally and reach the highest renunciation.
vishnu_gita::764.simple_insight: You can find peace by letting go of wants and seeing everyone with equal regard.
vishnu_gita::764.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a person rooted in the supreme reality with a joyful, steady mind. Such a person neither grieves over what is lost nor desires what is unavailable. By embracing equality toward all beings, they achieve the supreme state of renunciation.
vishnu_gita::764.modern_relevance: After a tough loss, you stop chasing what’s gone and see others with kindness, freeing yourself from endless craving.
vishnu_gita::764.insight: It teaches you to balance your mind with calm acceptance and equal regard, dissolving restless desires.

vishnu_gita::765.verse_sanskrit:
मां सन्न्यासेन जानाति यावान् यश्चाऽस्मि तत्त्वतः ।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
vishnu_gita::765.verse_hindi: मैं जिस प्रकार का और जो हूँ सो यथार्थरूप से सन्यास के द्वारा वह जानता है और मुझको यथार्थरूप से जानकर अनन्तर मुझमें प्रवेश कर जाता है।
vishnu_gita::765.english_translation: One who truly knows what I am through renunciation then enters me without delay.
vishnu_gita::765.translation_literal: माम् (me) सन्न्यासेन (by renunciation) जानाति (knows) यावान् (what) यः (who) च (also) अस्मि (I am) तत्त्वतः (truly) । ततः (then) माम् (me) तत्त्वतः (truly) ज्ञात्वा (knowing) विशते (enters) तद् (that) अनन्तरम् (immediately) ॥
vishnu_gita::765.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::765.essence: True renunciation leads to direct knowledge and immediate union with the divine.
vishnu_gita::765.simple_meaning: When you sincerely renounce attachment, you come to truly understand the divine and unite with that reality.
vishnu_gita::765.simple_insight: There is a deep transformation when letting go leads to true knowing and connection.
vishnu_gita::765.detailed_meaning: Vishnu explains that through sincere renunciation—letting go of attachments—a person gains true knowledge of his nature and immediately unites with that divine reality.
vishnu_gita::765.modern_relevance: When you stop clinging to outcomes or identities, you can discover a deeper truth and connect fully with your inner being.
vishnu_gita::765.insight: It teaches you that renouncing attachments sharpens your understanding and opens the way to deep union.

vishnu_gita::766.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वकर्माणयपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रय: ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
vishnu_gita::766.verse_hindi: सर्वदा सब प्रकार का कर्म करता हुआ भी मत्परायण व्यक्ति मेरे अनुग्रह से सनातन नित्यपद को प्राप्त होता है ।
vishnu_gita::766.english_translation: One who always performs all kinds of actions while relying on me attains by my grace the eternal imperishable state.
vishnu_gita::766.translation_literal: सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) अपि (also) सदा (always) कुर्वाणः (doing) मद्व्यपाश्रयः (relying on me) मत्प्रसादात् (by my grace) अवाप्नोति (attains) शाश्वतं (eternal) पदम् (state) अव्ययम् (imperishable)
vishnu_gita::766.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::766.essence: Trusting the divine while acting leads to eternal, unchanging peace.
vishnu_gita::766.simple_meaning: You can keep doing all kinds of actions but if you rely on the divine with trust, you reach the eternal, unchanging state by divine grace.
vishnu_gita::766.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that steady trust in the divine guides your actions to lasting freedom.
vishnu_gita::766.detailed_meaning: In the midst of constant action, Vishnu teaches that relying on the divine with full trust leads to attaining an eternal, imperishable state beyond change and decay.
vishnu_gita::766.modern_relevance: You keep juggling tasks and roles, but when you take a moment to trust that your efforts are supported by something greater, you move toward lasting peace.
vishnu_gita::766.insight: This verse teaches you to keep acting while shifting trust from outcomes to inner reliance on the divine's grace.

vishnu_gita::767.verse_sanskrit:
चेतसा सर्व्वकर्माणि मयि सन्न्यस्य मत्पराः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मञ्चित्ताः स्यात सर्वथा ॥
vishnu_gita::767.verse_hindi: आप लोग चित्त से सब कर्मों को मुझमें अर्पण करके मत्परायण होकर बुद्धियोग का आश्रय लेकर सर्वथा अपने चित्त को मुझमें लीन कर लीजिये।
vishnu_gita::767.english_translation: Surrender all your actions mentally to me, devoted to me; relying on the yoga of discernment, fully merge your mind in me.
vishnu_gita::767.translation_literal: चेतसा (with the mind) / सर्व्वकर्माणि (all actions) / मयि (in me) / सन्न्यस्य (surrender) / मत्पराः (devoted to me) / बुद्धियोगम् (the yoga of discernment) / उपाश्रित्य (taking refuge) / मञ्चित्ताः (mind) / स्यात् (become) / सर्वथा (completely)
vishnu_gita::767.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::767.essence: Complete mental surrender of all actions, supported by discernment, merges your mind with the divine.
vishnu_gita::767.simple_meaning: Mentally give all your actions to the divine, stay devoted, and rely on clear understanding to fully merge your mind in that devotion.
vishnu_gita::767.simple_insight: You feel peace when your mind is fully devoted and trusting clear wisdom.
vishnu_gita::767.detailed_meaning: Vishnu instructs devotees to mentally dedicate every action to him with full devotion and to rely on the yoga of discernment (buddhiyoga). This teaching guides followers to merge their mind completely with the divine presence, cultivating spiritual focus and surrender.
vishnu_gita::767.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by daily choices, mentally offering your efforts to a trusted higher purpose helps calm the mind and steady your focus.
vishnu_gita::767.insight: It teaches you to shift your mental focus from personal gain to devoted surrender supported by clear wisdom.

vishnu_gita::768.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वलोकाश्रयश्रेष्ठ ! परमात्मन् ! जगद्गुरो !।
त्वत्प्राप्तिमुख्यहेतोहि ज्ञानकाण्डस्य हे प्रभो !॥
vishnu_gita::768.verse_hindi: हे सर्वलोकाश्रयश्रेष्ठ ! हे प्रभो ! हे परमात्मन् ! हे जगद्गुरो! आपकी प्राप्ति के प्रधान कारण रूप ज्ञानकाण्ड का
vishnu_gita::768.english_translation: O best refuge of all worlds! O supreme being! O world teacher! You are the chief cause for attaining the knowledge section, O Lord!
vishnu_gita::768.translation_literal: सर्वलोकाश्रयश्रेष्ठ (best refuge of all worlds) / परमात्मन् (supreme being) / जगद्गुरो (world teacher) / त्वत्प्राप्तिमुख्यहेतोहि (for your attainment, chief cause) / ज्ञानकाण्डस्य (of the knowledge section) / हे प्रभो (O Lord)
vishnu_gita::768.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::768.essence: The supreme being is the chief cause and refuge for attaining true knowledge.
vishnu_gita::768.simple_meaning: This verse praises the supreme being as the greatest refuge and teacher, the main cause for attaining knowledge.
vishnu_gita::768.simple_insight: There is reassurance in recognizing a guiding presence behind gaining true understanding.
vishnu_gita::768.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the narrator addresses Vishnu with reverence, acknowledging him as the supreme refuge and teacher. It highlights Vishnu as the main cause behind receiving the teachings of knowledge, setting the stage for the discourse.
vishnu_gita::768.insight: It reminds you that true understanding comes through connection with a guiding source beyond yourself.

vishnu_gita::769.verse_sanskrit:
रहस्यं मुक्तिदं जाता गृण्वतां नः कृतार्थता ।
भूयोऽपि श्रोतुमिच्छामो मधुरां ते गिरं हिताम् ॥
vishnu_gita::769.verse_hindi: मुक्तिप्रद रहस्य सुनकर हमलोग कृतार्थ हुए। हम फिर भी आपकी मधुर और हितकरी वाणी को सुनना चाहते हैं
vishnu_gita::769.english_translation: Hearing this secret that grants freedom, we feel fulfilled. Yet we still wish to hear your sweet and beneficial words.
vishnu_gita::769.translation_literal: रहस्यं (secret) मुक्तिदं (giving freedom) जाता (having come) गृण्वतां (hearing) नः (to us) कृतार्थता (fulfillment). भूयोऽपि (again also) श्रोतुमिच्छामो (wish to hear) मधुरां (sweet) ते (your) गिरं (speech) हिताम् (beneficial).
vishnu_gita::769.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::769.essence: Fulfillment from truth awakens a longing for more wisdom.
vishnu_gita::769.simple_meaning: We have heard a secret that grants freedom and feel fulfilled, yet we want to hear more of your sweet and helpful words.
vishnu_gita::769.simple_insight: There is a natural desire to keep learning even after feeling satisfied.
vishnu_gita::769.detailed_meaning: After hearing a profound teaching about freedom, the listeners express their gratitude but still long to hear more from the speaker, showing deep respect and eagerness to learn.
vishnu_gita::769.modern_relevance: After finishing a meaningful conversation, you still want to hear more wisdom from that trusted voice.
vishnu_gita::769.insight: It reminds you to stay open and eager for wisdom, even after feeling fulfilled.

vishnu_gita::770.verse_sanskrit:
कस्मिन रूपे भवन्त हि चिन्तयन्तो वयं विभो ।
शक्नुमोऽनुपलं लब्धं भवन्तं ज्ञानदायिनम् ॥
vishnu_gita::770.verse_hindi: हे विभो ! किस रूप में आप ज्ञानदाता को चिन्तन करने से हम लोग हर समय आपको प्राप्त करने में समर्थ होंगे
vishnu_gita::770.english_translation: O Lord, in which form should we always contemplate you to be able to attain you, the giver of wisdom?
vishnu_gita::770.translation_literal: कस्मिन (in which) / रूपे (form) / भवन्त (you are) / हि (indeed) / चिन्तयन्तो (contemplating) / वयं (we) / विभो (O Lord) / शक्नुमः (are able) / अनुपलं (always) / लब्धं (attained) / भवन्तं (you) / ज्ञानदायिनम् (giver of wisdom)
vishnu_gita::770.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::770.essence: Asking how to focus on the true source unlocks steady wisdom.
vishnu_gita::770.simple_meaning: You wonder in what way to focus your mind so that you can always connect with the one who gives wisdom.
vishnu_gita::770.simple_insight: Wondering how to keep your mind steady opens the door to lasting clarity.
vishnu_gita::770.detailed_meaning: In a moment of seeking, the speaker asks the divine how to contemplate the form that will allow constant connection with the giver of wisdom, highlighting the quest for steady insight.
vishnu_gita::770.modern_relevance: You pause, wondering how to hold your attention on what truly matters amid constant distractions.
vishnu_gita::770.insight: It teaches you to ask clearly how to maintain steady focus on wisdom rather than drifting.

vishnu_gita::771.verse_sanskrit:
अशेषं वर्णयित्वेदमस्मानाश्वासय प्रभो ।
भवता साम्प्रतं नाथ ! कृपयाऽसीमया यतः ॥
vishnu_gita::771.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो ! इस विषय को पूर्णतया वर्णन करके हमें आश्वासन दीजिये क्योंकि हे नाथ! इस समय आपने जो असीम कृपा करके
vishnu_gita::771.english_translation: O Lord! Please fully explain this subject and assure us, for now you have shown boundless compassion.
vishnu_gita::771.translation_literal: अशेषं (completely) वर्णयित्वे (explaining) अस्मान् (us) आश्वासय (assure) प्रभो (O Lord) । भवता (by you) साम्प्रतं (now) नाथ (O master) ! कृपया (with compassion) असीमया (boundless) यतः (because) ॥
vishnu_gita::771.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::771.essence: True assurance comes from complete understanding given with deep compassion.
vishnu_gita::771.simple_meaning: Please explain this topic completely and give us assurance because you have shown great compassion now.
vishnu_gita::771.simple_insight: There is hope when guidance comes from a place of deep care and openness.
vishnu_gita::771.detailed_meaning: The narrator requests the Lord to fully explain the topic and provide assurance, emphasizing the divine's immense compassion at this moment in the discourse.
vishnu_gita::771.insight: It highlights the importance of clear guidance and reassurance when facing complex or difficult subjects.

vishnu_gita::772.verse_sanskrit:
नानाज्ञानमयैर्वाक्यैः कृतकृया वयं कृताः।
अतो न विरहं सोढुं शक्ष्यामः क्षणमप्युत ॥
vishnu_gita::772.verse_hindi: अनेक ज्ञानमय उपदेशों  हम लोगों को कृतकृत्य किया है इसलिये हम लोग आपके विरह को क्षणभर भी सहन नहीं कर सकेंगे
vishnu_gita::772.english_translation: Many teachings full of knowledge have made us indebted; therefore, we cannot endure separation from you even for a moment.
vishnu_gita::772.translation_literal: नानाज्ञानमयैः (by many knowledge-filled) / वाक्यैः (words) / कृतकृया (by debt) / वयं (we) / कृताः (have become). / अतो (therefore) / न (not) / विरहं (separation) / सोढुं (to endure) / शक्ष्यामः (can) / क्षणमपि (even a moment) / उत (also).
vishnu_gita::772.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::772.essence: Deep gratitude to wisdom makes even brief separation unbearable.
vishnu_gita::772.simple_meaning: We have received so much guidance that we feel deeply connected and cannot bear being apart, even briefly.
vishnu_gita::772.simple_insight: You feel a heartfelt bond that makes absence feel like a heavy loss.
vishnu_gita::772.detailed_meaning: After receiving many profound teachings filled with knowledge, these listeners feel deeply indebted and connected, making the thought of separation unbearable even for a brief moment.
vishnu_gita::772.modern_relevance: When you've learned so much from someone, even a short time apart feels like a painful distance you don't want.
vishnu_gita::772.insight: It shows how deep trust and connection create a sense of belonging that resists any separation.

vishnu_gita::773.verse_sanskrit:
अपि वः श्रद्धया भक्त्या प्रसन्नोऽस्मि दिवौकसः ।
भवद्यः साम्प्रतं दिव्यं ज्ञाननेत्रं ददाम्यहम् ॥
vishnu_gita::773.verse_hindi: हे देवगण ! आप लोगों की श्रद्धा और भक्ति से मैं प्रसन्न हूँ, अब मैं आप लोगों को दिव्य ज्ञान नेत्र प्रदान करता हूँ
vishnu_gita::773.english_translation: O radiant beings! I am pleased by your trust and devotion; now I grant you the divine eye of wisdom.
vishnu_gita::773.translation_literal: अपि (also) वः (your) श्रद्धया (with trust) भक्त्या (with devotion) प्रसन्नः अस्मि (I am pleased) दिवौकसः (O radiant beings) भवद्यः (you all) साम्प्रतं (now) दिव्यं (divine) ज्ञाननेत्रं (eye of wisdom) ददामि अहम् (I give)
vishnu_gita::773.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::773.essence: Trust and devoted love open the door to receiving divine wisdom.
vishnu_gita::773.simple_meaning: Your trust and devoted love please the divine, and now you are granted a divine vision of wisdom.
vishnu_gita::773.simple_insight: Feeling your faith welcomed brings a quiet confidence that deeper understanding is near.
vishnu_gita::773.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the radiant beings, expressing joy at their sincere trust and devotion. In response, he offers them a divine eye—symbolizing clear wisdom—to see beyond ordinary perception.
vishnu_gita::773.modern_relevance: When you fully trust and open your heart in any pursuit, new insights and clarity naturally arise.
vishnu_gita::773.insight: It teaches you to recognize that sincere trust and devotion are the keys to unlocking higher understanding.

vishnu_gita::774.verse_sanskrit:
यूयं यज्ज्ञाननेत्रेण स्थातुं शक्ताः सुरर्षभाः ।
चेद्विज्ञानमये कोषे तदा भवितुमर्हथ ॥
vishnu_gita::774.verse_hindi: जिसके द्वारा हे सुरश्रेष्ठों ! आप यदि विज्ञानमय कोष में स्थित रह सकोगे तो मेरे इस
vishnu_gita::774.english_translation: O best of the devas! If you can stand firm in the treasury of true understanding, then you will be worthy indeed.
vishnu_gita::774.translation_literal: यूयं (you) / यत् (which) / ज्ञाननेत्रेण (through the eye of knowledge) / स्थातुं (to stand) / शक्ताः (able) / सुरर्षभाः (best of devas) / चेद् (if) / विज्ञानमये (in the treasury of wisdom) / कोषे (in the repository) / तदा (then) / भवितुमर्हथ (you deserve to be)
vishnu_gita::774.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::774.essence: True worth comes from standing steady in deep understanding.
vishnu_gita::774.simple_meaning: You become worthy when you can remain steady in deep understanding and clear insight.
vishnu_gita::774.simple_insight: There is power and dignity in holding steady to true understanding, even under pressure.
vishnu_gita::774.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the best devas, encouraging them to stand firm within the treasury of wisdom. This moment challenges them to maintain clear insight as their foundation to prove their worthiness.
vishnu_gita::774.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by confusion or pressure, you find strength by grounding yourself in clear understanding and steady insight.
vishnu_gita::774.insight: It teaches you to anchor your confidence in steady knowledge rather than fleeting feelings or doubts.

vishnu_gita::775.verse_sanskrit:
कृतकृत्या अनाद्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा नित्यस्थितं विभुम् ।
रूपं स्थूलादपि स्थूलं ममैतद्धि प्रतिक्षणम् ॥
vishnu_gita::775.verse_hindi: अनादी अनंत नित्यस्थित विभु स्थूलतीस्थूल रूप को हर समय दर्शन करके कृतकृत्य हो सकोगे
vishnu_gita::775.english_translation: Seeing the infinite, eternal, all-pervading form, even the gross form appears gross to me every moment.
vishnu_gita::775.translation_literal: कृतकृत्या (being fulfilled) / अनाद्यन्तं (without beginning or end) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / नित्यस्थितं (eternally established) / विभुम् (all-pervading) / रूपं (form) / स्थूलादपि (even grosser than gross) / स्थूलं (gross) / मम (to me) / एतत् (this) / इहि (here) / प्रतिक्षणम् (every moment)
vishnu_gita::775.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::775.essence: Seeing the eternal vastness makes all gross forms seem small and insignificant.
vishnu_gita::775.simple_meaning: When you perceive the eternal and all-pervading form, even the gross physical form seems insignificant every moment.
vishnu_gita::775.simple_insight: You feel the vastness of the eternal softening how you experience the physical world.
vishnu_gita::775.detailed_meaning: Vishnu reveals that by seeing his infinite, eternal, and all-pervading form, even the grossest physical forms lose their weight and significance for the observer, showing a profound shift in perception.
vishnu_gita::775.modern_relevance: When you recognize the vastness beyond everyday appearances, the challenges and distractions around you feel less overwhelming.
vishnu_gita::775.insight: It changes your perspective from fixating on surface appearances to recognizing deeper, boundless reality beneath.

vishnu_gita::776.verse_sanskrit:
ततो ज्ञान निधिर्मान्यो  महाविष्णुर्दयाणव ।
दिव्यं ज्ञानमयं चक्षुर्देवेभ्यो दत्तवान् प्रभुः ॥
vishnu_gita::776.verse_hindi: तब करुणासागर ज्ञाननिधि और मान्य प्रभु महाविष्णु ने देवताओं को ज्ञानमय दिव्य चक्षु प्रदान किया
vishnu_gita::776.english_translation: Then the compassionate great Vishnu, the treasure of wisdom, granted the gods a divine eye full of knowledge.
vishnu_gita::776.translation_literal: ततो (then) ज्ञान (knowledge) निधिः (treasure) मान्य (respected) महा-विष्णुः (great Vishnu) दयाणव (compassionate) । दिव्यं (divine) ज्ञानमयं (full of knowledge) चक्षुः (eye) देवेभ्यः (to the gods) दत्तवान् (gave) प्रभुः (lord) ॥
vishnu_gita::776.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::776.essence: Compassionate wisdom grants the power to perceive divine knowledge clearly.
vishnu_gita::776.simple_meaning: The compassionate Vishnu gave the gods a special divine eye full of knowledge.
vishnu_gita::776.simple_insight: Compassion can open new ways to see beyond ordinary limits.
vishnu_gita::776.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Vishnu, known for his compassion and wisdom, blesses the gods with a divine eye that reveals true knowledge, empowering them to perceive deeper truths beyond normal vision.
vishnu_gita::776.insight: It shows that true wisdom can transform perception, allowing you to see what was hidden before.

vishnu_gita::777.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वे देवास्तदानीम्बै स्थिराङ्गाः स्थिरलोचनाः।
स्माधिस्था भवन्तो ही विस्मिर्ताश्च विशेषत: ॥
vishnu_gita::777.verse_hindi: तब वे सब देवगण स्थिर गात्र और स्थिर नेत्र होकर समाधिस्थ और विशेष विस्मित होते हुए
vishnu_gita::777.english_translation: Then all the radiant beings became steady in body and steady in eyes, established in absorbed presence, yet especially astonished.
vishnu_gita::777.translation_literal: सर्वे (all) / देवाः (divine beings) / तदानीम् (at that moment) / बै (then) / स्थिराङ्गाः (steady-bodied) / स्थिरलोचनाः (steady-eyed) / स्माधिस्था (established in samadhi) / भवन्तः (became) / हि (indeed) / विस्मृताः (astonished) / च (and) / विशेषतः (especially)
vishnu_gita::777.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::777.essence: Complete stillness can accompany deep wonder and astonishment.
vishnu_gita::777.simple_meaning: All the radiant beings became still in body and eyes, deeply absorbed, yet notably astonished.
vishnu_gita::777.simple_insight: Stillness and absorption can coexist with surprise or wonder.
vishnu_gita::777.detailed_meaning: The radiant beings present became completely still and absorbed in meditation, their bodies and eyes unmoving, yet they showed clear signs of astonishment at what they witnessed.
vishnu_gita::777.insight: Stillness of body and mind does not exclude being open to new, surprising experiences.

vishnu_gita::778.verse_hindi: जीवों के मन वचन और बुद्धि से अतीत उस अद्भुत विराटरूप का दर्शन करते हुए स्तुति करने लगे
vishnu_gita::778.english_translation: Living beings, transcending mind, speech, and intellect, behold the wondrous cosmic form and praise it.
vishnu_gita::778.translation_literal: बुद्धरतीतं (beyond mind and intellect) / जीवानाम (of living beings) / अवाङ्मनसगोचरम् (beyond speech, mind, and intellect) / विरारूपञ्च (and the cosmic form) / पश्यन्तः (seeing) / तुष्टुवुस्ते (praised) / तदद्भुतम् (that wondrous)
vishnu_gita::778.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::778.essence: Living beings praise the wondrous cosmic form beyond mind and speech.
vishnu_gita::778.simple_meaning: Living beings see and praise the wondrous cosmic form beyond ordinary mind and speech.
vishnu_gita::778.simple_insight: There is awe in witnessing something beyond words or thought.
vishnu_gita::778.detailed_meaning: In this moment, living beings perceive a wondrous cosmic form that transcends normal mind, speech, and intellect, inspiring them to offer praise. It shows encountering the divine beyond ordinary faculties.
vishnu_gita::778.insight: It shifts perspective from ordinary understanding to reverence for what exceeds mental grasp.

vishnu_gita::779.verse_sanskrit:
देवादिदेव ! त्वदचिन्त्यदेहे आद्यन्तशून्ये प्रसमीक्ष्य नूनम् ।
देवानृषीन् पितृगणाननन्तान पृथक स्थितान् विस्मयमावहामः ॥
vishnu_gita::779.verse_hindi: हे देवादिदेव ! हम लोग आपके अनादि अनन्त और अचिन्त्य देह में अनन्त देवसमूह, ऋषिसमूह और पितृसमूह को पृथक पृथक् स्थित देखकर अवश्य ही विस्मित हो रहे हैं
vishnu_gita::779.english_translation: O Deva-adideva, seeing the infinite gods, sages, and ancestors separately established in your inconceivable, eternal body, we are indeed amazed.
vishnu_gita::779.translation_literal: देवादिदेव (O Deva-adideva) / त्वद्-अचिन्त्य-देहे (in your inconceivable body) / आद्यन्त-शून्ये (without beginning and end) / प्रसमीक्ष्य (seeing clearly) / नूनम् (indeed) / देवान् (gods) / ऋषीन् (sages) / पितृगणान् (ancestors) / अनन्तान् (infinite) / पृथक् (separately) / स्थितान् (established) / विस्मयम् (amazement) / आवहामः (we experience)
vishnu_gita::779.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::779.essence: The infinite divine contains countless beings distinctly within its inconceivable form.
vishnu_gita::779.simple_meaning: Seeing countless gods, sages, and ancestors distinctly present within the infinite and unthinkable body amazes us deeply.
vishnu_gita::779.simple_insight: There is wonder in perceiving vast, infinite presences beyond ordinary understanding.
vishnu_gita::779.detailed_meaning: The narrator Suta expresses amazement at witnessing the countless divine beings, sages, and ancestors distinctly existing within Vishnu's infinite, timeless, and inconceivable cosmic form, highlighting the vastness and mystery of the divine body.
vishnu_gita::779.insight: It invites you to recognize the immense, mysterious presence that supports all existence beyond what you can easily grasp.

vishnu_gita::780.verse_sanskrit:
तवैव देहादभुवनानि देव ! चतुर्दशैतेषु निवासिनो हि ।
देवाश्च दैत्याश्च मनुष्यसङ्का उचतुर्विधा भूतगणाश्च सर्वे ॥
vishnu_gita::780.verse_hindi: हे देव ! आपके ही देह से चतुर्दश भुवन और इनके निवासी देव, दैत्य, मनुष्यसमूह और सब चतुर्विध भूतसङ्घ उत्पन्न हुए हैं,
vishnu_gita::780.english_translation: O divine one! From your body arose the fourteen worlds and their inhabitants: Devas, Asuras, humans, and all four kinds of beings.
vishnu_gita::780.translation_literal: तवैव (from you only) देहादभुवनानि (bodies/worlds arose) देव (divine one) ! चतुर्दशैतेषु (in these fourteen) निवासिनो (residents) हि (indeed) । देवाश्च (Devas also) दैत्याश्च (Asuras also) मनुष्यसङ्का (groups of humans) उचतुर्विधा (four kinds) भूतगणाश्च (groups of beings also) सर्वे (all) ॥
vishnu_gita::780.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::780.essence: All worlds and beings arise from the divine's body and presence.
vishnu_gita::780.simple_meaning: All fourteen worlds and their residents—divine beings, shadow beings, humans, and all four types of creatures—came from your body.
vishnu_gita::780.simple_insight: Everything and everyone around us arises from the divine presence that sustains all existence.
vishnu_gita::780.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the speaker addresses the divine, explaining that from the divine's body arose the fourteen worlds along with their inhabitants—gods, shadow beings, humans, and all categories of living creatures—showing the cosmic origin of all existence.
vishnu_gita::780.insight: It reveals that everything you see and experience is interconnected through a single origin, inviting respect and reverence for all life.

vishnu_gita::781.verse_sanskrit:
जाताः पृथक सन्ति चतुर्दशस्त्रहो यान्न्यत्र नाशं भुवनैनिःसमम्।
संपश्यतामीदृशमद्भुतं प्रभो ! बुद्धिम॑मे मजति नः समाकुला ॥
vishnu_gita::781.verse_hindi: चतुर्दश भुवनों में पृथक पृथक हैं और अहो! अपने लोकों के साथ इसी (आपके देह में) नाश को प्राप्त होते हैं। हे प्रभो ! इस प्रकार आश्चर्य को देखते हुए हम लोगो की बुद्धि व्याकुल होकर भ्रम में मग्न होती है
vishnu_gita::781.english_translation: The fourteen worlds exist separately and perish along with their beings; witnessing this marvel, our minds grow confused and restless, O Lord!
vishnu_gita::781.translation_literal: जाताः (born) पृथक (separately) सन्ति (are) चतुर्दशः (fourteen) त्रहो (worlds) यान् (which) न (not) अन्यत्र (elsewhere) नाशं (destruction) भुवनैः (worlds) निःसमम् (along with) । संपश्यताम् (seeing) ईदृशम् (such) अद्भुतम् (wonderful) प्रभो (O Lord) ! बुद्धिम् (mind) अमे (our) मजति (becomes) नः (our) समाकुला (confused) ॥
vishnu_gita::781.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::781.essence: Seeing all separate worlds perish naturally unsettles the mind, but deeper steadiness is possible.
vishnu_gita::781.simple_meaning: All fourteen worlds exist separately and end with their beings, which confuses and unsettles the mind when witnessed.
vishnu_gita::781.simple_insight: It’s natural to feel shaken when seeing everything you know fall apart.
vishnu_gita::781.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how the fourteen cosmic worlds exist apart and each faces destruction. Witnessing this grand cosmic cycle causes the mind to become restless and confused, highlighting the challenge of grasping impermanence.
vishnu_gita::781.modern_relevance: You watch a beloved project or relationship end, and your mind spins in disbelief and unrest.
vishnu_gita::781.insight: Recognize that confusion at loss is natural, but the true self remains steady beyond endings.

vishnu_gita::782.verse_sanskrit:
देवाश्च ये स्थूलशरीरमानिनो विशन्ति ते सूक्ष्मशरीरमानिषु ।
देवास्तु ये मूक्ष्मशरीरमानिनो विशन्त्यहो कारणकायमानिषु ॥
vishnu_gita::782.verse_hindi: अहो ! जो स्थूल देहाभिमानी देवतागण हैं वे सूक्ष्म देहाभिमानी देवताओं में प्रवेश करते हैं और जो सूक्ष्म देहाभिमानी देवतागण हैं वे कारण देहाभिमानी देवताओ में प्रवेश करते हैं
vishnu_gita::782.english_translation: Those who identify with the gross body among the deva beings enter the subtle-bodied devas, and those who identify with the subtle body enter the causal-bodied devas.
vishnu_gita::782.translation_literal: देवाश्च (devas and) ये (who) स्थूलशरीरमानिनो (identify with the gross body) विशन्ति (enter) ते (those) सूक्ष्मशरीरमानिषु (into the subtle-bodied) । देवास्तु (devas but) ये (who) मूक्ष्मशरीरमानिनो (identify with the subtle body) विशन्त्य (enter) अहो (ah!) कारणकायमानिषु (into the causal-bodied) ॥
vishnu_gita::782.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::782.essence: Your sense of self deepens by passing from gross to subtle and then causal layers of being.
vishnu_gita::782.simple_meaning: Your sense of self changes as you move from identifying with the physical body to subtler levels of existence beyond it.
vishnu_gita::782.simple_insight: There’s freedom in realizing your identity is not fixed to one form or layer of being.
vishnu_gita::782.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes how beings who identify with their physical (gross) body move into subtler forms after death, and those identifying with subtler bodies move further into causal forms. It shows a progression of consciousness beyond the material.
vishnu_gita::782.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck in your physical or emotional identity, this reminds you that your sense of self can evolve beyond immediate appearances.
vishnu_gita::782.insight: Shift your view of yourself from a fixed body to a flowing presence spanning multiple layers of existence.

vishnu_gita::783.verse_sanskrit:
इमे तु सर्वे प्रविशन्त्यचिन्त्ये महामभावे कच तन्न विद्मः।
दृष्ट्वेदृशं तेऽद्भुतकार्यमीश ! वयं विमुग्धाः खलु ते प्रभावात् ॥
vishnu_gita::783.verse_hindi: किन्तु ये सब किस अचिन्त्य महाप्रभाववान् में प्रवेश करते हैं सो हमलोग नहीं समझ रहे हैं। हे ईश ! इस प्रकार आपका अद्भुत कार्य देखकर आपके प्रभाव से हम लोग विमुग्ध हो रहे हैं
vishnu_gita::783.english_translation: But we do not understand how all enter the inconceivable supreme power. O Lord, seeing your wondrous work, we are amazed by your influence.
vishnu_gita::783.translation_literal: इमे (these) / तु (but) / सर्वे (all) / प्रविशन्ति (enter) / अचिन्त्ये (inconceivable) / महामभावे (supreme power) / कच (not at all) / तन्न (that) / विद्मः (we know) / दृष्ट्वे (having seen) / दृष्टं (seen) / ते (your) / अद्भुतकार्यम् (wondrous work) / ईश (O Lord) / वयम् (we) / विमुग्धाः (amazed) / खलु (indeed) / ते (your) / प्रभावात् (by the influence)
vishnu_gita::783.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::783.essence: The supreme power's workings are wondrous and beyond our understanding.
vishnu_gita::783.simple_meaning: We do not understand how all beings enter the inconceivable supreme power. Seeing this wondrous work, we are amazed by its influence.
vishnu_gita::783.simple_insight: There is awe and wonder at the mystery of the divine power beyond understanding.
vishnu_gita::783.detailed_meaning: Suta speaks with sages who witness the vast, inconceivable supreme power. They struggle to grasp how all beings enter this power, overwhelmed by the divine's wondrous influence.
vishnu_gita::783.insight: It reveals how some truths remain beyond full understanding, inviting humble amazement.

vishnu_gita::784.verse_sanskrit:
साचिन्त्यशक्तिर्भवतो धुवा किम ? या वांगमनो बुद्धिभीर प्रमेया।
त्वत्तो जनित्वा निजगर्भमध्ये लोकान् धरत्येव चतुर्दशालम ॥
vishnu_gita::784.verse_hindi: क्या वह नित्या अचिन्त्य शक्ति आपकी है? वाणी मन और बुद्धि से अगोचर जो शक्ति आप से ही उत्पन्न होकर चतुर्दश लोकों को अपने गर्भ में भलीभांति धारण करती है
vishnu_gita::784.english_translation: Is that eternal, inconceivable power yours? The power born from you, invisible to speech, mind, and intellect, which perfectly sustains the fourteen worlds within its womb.
vishnu_gita::784.translation_literal: साचिन्त्यशक्तिः (eternal inconceivable power) भवतः (of you) धुवा (is it?) किम (what?) या (which) वांग् (speech) मनो (mind) बुद्धिभीः (by intellects) प्रमेया (to be understood) । त्वत्तः (from you) जनित्वा (having been born) निजगर्भमध्ये (within its own womb) लोकान् (worlds) धरति एव (indeed sustains) चतुर्दशालम् (the fourteen worlds) ॥
vishnu_gita::784.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::784.essence: An eternal power beyond mind and speech perfectly sustains all worlds.
vishnu_gita::784.simple_meaning: There is an eternal, unimaginable power born from the divine that holds and supports all the fourteen worlds perfectly within itself.
vishnu_gita::784.simple_insight: The vast power behind everything is beyond mind or speech, yet it sustains all existence calmly.
vishnu_gita::784.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes a supreme power that is beyond human thought or speech, born from him, which holds all fourteen worlds safely within itself. This moment reveals the cosmic scale and mystery beyond ordinary understanding.
vishnu_gita::784.insight: It invites you to sense the unseen power supporting all life, beyond your usual thinking and senses.

vishnu_gita::785.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्माण्डयप्येवमनन्तपिण्डमयश्च सर्ग धरते सदा सा।
सर्व प्रसूते पुनरन्तकाले लीन तु तत् सा कुरुते स्वगर्भे ॥
vishnu_gita::785.verse_hindi: इसी प्रकार वह शक्ति अनन्त ब्रह्माण्ड और पिण्डमय सृष्टि को भी सदा स्थित रखती है, सबको उत्पन्न करती है और पुनः अन्तकाल में वह उन सभी को अपने गर्भ में लीन कर लेती है
vishnu_gita::785.english_translation: In the same way, that power eternally sustains the infinite cosmic and embodied creation, always generating all beings and at the end absorbing them back into itself.
vishnu_gita::785.translation_literal: ब्रह्माण्डयपि (even the cosmos) एव (indeed) अमनत (infinite) पिण्डमयश्च (embodied) सर्ग (creation) धरते (sustains) सदा (always) सा (she/that). सर्व (all) प्रसूते (produced) पुनरन्तकाले (at the end time) लीन (absorbed) तु (indeed) तत् (that) सा (she) कुरुते (does) स्वगर्भे (in her own womb).
vishnu_gita::785.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::785.essence: The infinite power creates, sustains, and ultimately reabsorbs all existence.
vishnu_gita::785.simple_meaning: A powerful force continuously maintains the vast universe and all forms of life, creating them and eventually reabsorbing them back into itself at the end.
vishnu_gita::785.simple_insight: Everything that arises is held and returned by the same infinite power.
vishnu_gita::785.detailed_meaning: Vishnu describes the cosmic power that eternally supports the infinite universe and all embodied beings. This power creates all life and, at the end of time, draws everything back into its own essence, showing the cycle of creation and dissolution.
vishnu_gita::785.insight: Recognize the endless cycle where creation and dissolution are unified by a sustaining power beyond individual existence.

vishnu_gita::786.verse_sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा चमत्कारामिमं न विद्यः कथं भवत्यद्भुतमेतदीश !। 
किं कारणञ्चास्य पुनः क आदिरस्य प्रवाहस्य तथाऽस्ति कोऽन्तः ॥
vishnu_gita::786.verse_hindi: हे ईश ! इस चमत्कार को देखकर हम नहीं समझ रहे हैं कि यह चमत्कार कैसे हो रहा है, इसका कारण क्या है और इस प्रवाह का आदि क्या है तथा अन्त क्या है
vishnu_gita::786.english_translation: O Lord! Seeing this wonder, I do not understand how this miracle happens, what causes it, and what the beginning and end of this flow are.
vishnu_gita::786.translation_literal: दृष्ट्वा (seeing) चमत्कारम् (wonder/miracle) इमं (this) न (not) विद्यः (knowledge) कथं (how) भवति (happens) अद्भुतम् (wonderful) एतत् (this) ईश (lord) ! किं (what) कारणं (cause) च (and) अस्य (of this) पुनः (again) क (who) आदिः (beginning) अस्य (of this) प्रवाहस्य (flow) तथा (also) अस्ति (is) कोऽन्तः (what end) ॥
vishnu_gita::786.speaker: Unknown
vishnu_gita::786.essence: Witnessing wonder can inspire deep curiosity about its cause and limits.
vishnu_gita::786.simple_meaning: Someone is amazed and confused by a great wonder and is asking what causes it and where its beginning and end lie.
vishnu_gita::786.simple_insight: Sometimes, witnessing something extraordinary leaves us puzzled and seeking deeper understanding.
vishnu_gita::786.detailed_meaning: A character addresses the divine, overwhelmed by an incredible event or phenomenon, expressing confusion about its origin, cause, and ultimate boundaries, revealing human curiosity and the limits of understanding.
vishnu_gita::786.modern_relevance: You encounter a situation so surprising it leaves you questioning how it works and where it all began or will end.
vishnu_gita::786.insight: It encourages embracing honest questioning when faced with mysteries beyond immediate understanding.

vishnu_gita::787.verse_sanskrit:
अनन्त ! सर्वेऽनुभवाम आदरात त्वामीश ! जन्मस्थितिनाशवर्जितम् ।
अनन्तवत्रं बहुधा स्तुतं मुरै गन्धर्वयक्षर्विविधैश्च सूरिभिः ॥
vishnu_gita::787.verse_hindi: हे अनन्त ! हे ईश ! हम सब भलीभांति अनुभव करते हैं कि आप उत्पत्ति, स्थिति और विनाश से रहित हो, अनन्तमुख हो और अनेक देवता गन्धर्व यक्ष और विद्वानों के द्वारा अनेक प्रकार से स्तुत हो
vishnu_gita::787.english_translation: O Infinite One! We all deeply experience that you are beyond birth, existence, and destruction, with infinite faces, praised in many ways by gods, gandharvas, and sages.
vishnu_gita::787.translation_literal: अनन्त (Infinite) / सर्वेऽनुभवाम (all experience) / आदरात (with respect) / त्वाम (you) / ईश (lord) / जन्मस्थितिनाशवर्जितम् (free from birth, existence, destruction) / अनन्तवत्रं (infinite faces) / बहुधा (in many ways) / स्तुतं (praised) / मुरै (sages) / गन्धर्वयक्षर्विविधैश्च (gandharvas, yakshas, various) / सूरिभिः (gods)
vishnu_gita::787.speaker: Suta
vishnu_gita::787.essence: The divine transcends all change and is revered by countless beings.
vishnu_gita::787.simple_meaning: Everyone recognizes the divine as eternal, without birth or death, with countless forms, praised by many celestial beings.
vishnu_gita::787.simple_insight: The divine is timeless and beyond all change, honored by all beings of wisdom and power.
vishnu_gita::787.detailed_meaning: Suta, narrating to sages, describes the infinite divine as beyond birth, existence, and destruction, worshiped by many celestial beings like gandharvas and yakshas, highlighting its vast, timeless nature.
vishnu_gita::787.insight: It invites seeing the divine as beyond all cycles and forms, expanding awareness beyond ordinary limits.

vishnu_gita::788.verse_sanskrit:
अमितशक्तियुतोऽपि भवन भवा नमितबाहुरसि त्वमनन्तपात् ।
अमितसूर्य मृगाङ्क-शिखिग्रहा-दमितनेत्रघरस्त्वामिहेक्षसे ॥
vishnu_gita::788.verse_hindi: आप हम लोगों को यहां अमित शक्ति युक्त होते हुए भी अनन्त बाहु एवं अनन्त पादविशिष्ट और अनन्त सूर्य चन्द्र तथा अग्नि को ग्रहण करने वाले होने के कारण अनन्त नेत्रधारी दृष्टि गोचर हो रहे हैं
vishnu_gita::788.english_translation: You appear here with infinite power, countless arms and feet, and countless eyes that behold the infinite sun, moon, and fire.
vishnu_gita::788.translation_literal: अमितशक्तियुतोऽपि (though endowed with infinite power) / भवन (being) / भवा (O you) / नमितबाहुरसि (with countless arms) / त्वम् (you) / अनन्तपात् (of infinite feet) / अमितसूर्य (infinite sun) / मृगाङ्क-शिखिग्रहा-दमितनेत्र (moon-mountain-planet-tamed eyes) / घरः (house) / त्वाम् (you) / इह (here) / एक्षसे (see).
vishnu_gita::788.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::788.essence: Infinite power and perception manifest in countless forms reveal the vastness of the divine.
vishnu_gita::788.simple_meaning: You are described as having limitless power, many arms and feet, and countless eyes that see the endless sun, moon, and fire.
vishnu_gita::788.simple_insight: The divine presence is vast beyond ordinary limits, visible in countless forms and powers.
vishnu_gita::788.detailed_meaning: Vishnu, the cosmic preserver, is depicted here with infinite strength, multiple limbs, and eyes that perceive all cosmic lights. This verse paints a grand image of divine omnipresence and power, evoking awe and reverence.
vishnu_gita::788.insight: It helps you feel the magnitude of the divine beyond human scale, expanding your view of presence and power.

vishnu_gita::789.verse_sanskrit:
त्वं तह्सां तह इहासि चेतने चैतन्यरूऽसि ददासि शक्तये ।
शक्तिं प्रभो ! प्रेरयसे मति तथा त्वत्सत्तया सर्वमिदं हि सत्त्ववत् ॥
vishnu_gita::789.verse_hindi: आप तेजों के भी तेज हैं, चेतन में चैतन्यरूप हैं, हे प्रभो ! आप शक्ति को शक्ति देते हैं और बुद्धि को सत्कर्मों में प्रेरित करते हैं क्योंकि आपकी सत्ता से यह समस्त विश्व यहां सत्तावान् हो रहा है
vishnu_gita::789.english_translation: You are the brilliance beyond all brilliance, the conscious consciousness; O Lord, you empower strength and inspire the mind towards good deeds, for by your existence all this world becomes vibrant.
vishnu_gita::789.translation_literal: त्वं (you) तह्सां (than them) तह (then) इहासि (are here) चेतने (in consciousness) चैतन्यरूऽसि (are consciousness itself) ददासि (give) शक्तये (to strength) । शक्तिं (strength) प्रभो (O lord) ! प्रेरयसे (you inspire) मति (mind) तथा (thus) त्वत्सत्तया (by your existence) सर्वमिदं (all this) हि (indeed) सत्त्ववत् (alive/vibrant) ॥
vishnu_gita::789.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::789.essence: Your true source empowers your strength and inspires your mind toward good.
vishnu_gita::789.simple_meaning: You are the highest source of power and consciousness, inspiring strength and guiding the mind toward good actions.
vishnu_gita::789.simple_insight: You can feel supported by a power that energizes your strength and encourages your best intentions.
vishnu_gita::789.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Vishnu speaks as the supreme source of all power and awareness. He explains that all strength and mental inspiration come from his presence, making the entire world vibrant and alive.
vishnu_gita::789.modern_relevance: When your energy feels low or your mind confused, remember a greater source fuels your strength and guides your thoughts toward kindness.
vishnu_gita::789.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your inner strength and clear thinking arise from a deeper source beyond yourself.

vishnu_gita::790.verse_sanskrit:
विभो ! त्वयैकेन हि मध्यलोक अङ्घ तथाऽधश्च दिशां समूहः ।
अनाद्यनन्तः समयस्तथासौ व्याप्तोऽस्ति धीर्येन विमोहिता नः ॥
vishnu_gita::790.verse_hindi: हे विभो ! एक आप से ही ऊर्ध्वलोक,अधोलोक, मध्यलोक, अनादि अनन्त यह दिकसमूह और अनादि अनन्त यह काल व्याप्त हैं जिससे हमारी बुद्धि विमुग्ध हो रही है
vishnu_gita::790.english_translation: O Sovereign! By you alone, the middle world, the upper and lower worlds, the directions, and endless time are pervaded; this overwhelms our discerning mind.
vishnu_gita::790.translation_literal: विभो (O Sovereign) / त्वयैकेन (by you alone) / हि (indeed) / मध्यलोक (middle world) / अङ्घ (and) / तथाऽधश्च (also below) / दिशां (directions) / समूहः (group) / अनाद्यनन्तः (beginningless and endless) / समयः (time) / तथासौ (and also that) / व्याप्तोऽस्ति (is pervaded) / धीर्येन (by the discerning mind) / विमोहिता (bewildered) / नः (our).
vishnu_gita::790.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita::790.essence: The true self permeates all space and time, beyond the mind's comprehension.
vishnu_gita::790.simple_meaning: The divine pervades all realms and infinite time, overwhelming our discerning mind with its vastness.
vishnu_gita::790.simple_insight: There is humility in realizing your true self is beyond all limits the mind can see.
vishnu_gita::790.detailed_meaning: Vishnu addresses the vastness of the cosmos, explaining that all worlds—upper, middle, and lower—along with all directions and limitless time, are filled by the divine. This vastness confuses even the wise mind, showing how immense the true self is.
vishnu_gita::790.modern_relevance: You try to hold on to control but realize the forces shaping your life are vast and beyond your grasp.
